I was assured that Karina's technique is unique and long lasting, that said the services by Karina here are second to none, and organic and in a GREEN environment.  Meanwhile a simple polish change (called a Mimos) was heavenly in there one and only high-end "Sound therapy" chair - quite possibly the best pedi chair I have ever sat in.  You can tell Karina and her fiance have spent a bundle on equipment, products (Rich Hippe/Nature Girl is pricey stuff!) and renovating the space (Clay walls!!).  They have done a great  (and green) job.   Now for the bad news...  The icy-cold receptionist made me feel as though I was not trustworthy and she followed me around the salon, fearful that I would rip off a bottle of polish.  This tainted my experience in an extremely negative way.  I may or may not return.  Next time for a complete ritual.  perhaps now the receptionist won't be so nervous that I might steal products.  That really hurt.  Note: The day after my Mimos we went for our vacation in Cape Cod - the sun, salt & surf turned my sheer pink pedi - YELLOW within 48 hours. Sickly, ugly yellow.  Another example of how inferior the water-based top coats are.  I miss my CND and OPI.  I wonder if Karina would let me bring my own products and have her apply them?   Mama ain't too happy with the end results of this polish change!

Thankfully they restored my childhood theater, the County, in Doylestown, to its former glory.  Now they show alot of art-flicks and culturally sensitive  and independant films.  They have a great series of films each season and also show some "blockbuster" type films, too.  Best part?  I can walk here from my childhood home and graba yummy treat at Coffee 'n Cream afterward.

Probably more of a 2 star review - but I am feeling generous - and since this IHOP is one I am likely to re-visit I will try to be kind.  IHOP is the kind of chain that can vary greatly in cleanliness - but the food is EXACTLY the same in each and every location, as it is cooked via formula by disinterested underpaid teens and young adults.  Surprisingly enough we have never come here during the mad breakfast rush - but rather on Sundays after 4 PM when it is dead empty - and thus our service is usually good and food hot.  My hubby likes the flavored pancakes - and I really enjoy the crepes. Not a Holy Grail by any means - but it is cheap and good in a pinch.

Recently changed owners and slowly making improvements. They still have the BEST La Colombe coffee beverages including lattes, cappuccino, mocha and breve.  Gelato, pastries and a few sandwich options.  Love it here.

I truly think SEPTA has improved over the past 5 years - yes there are still problems.  The schedule on weekends, nights and mid-day (non rush hour) is awful (you can wait 60 - 75 minutes between trains), but if you are a "simple" 9 - 5 or 8 - 4 commuter and live on a shorter line (NOT Doylestown - the "slow boat to China") like Media/Elwyn - it's fairly painless.  Yes, the fares have increased.  So what?  Deal with it - try paying for gas and parking and dealing with the stress of driving every day?  No thanks.  I love public transportation - and just which there were more of it.

I am THIS CLOSE to giving Ursula's 5 stars.  I went back again for a bacial (Back facial) with Elina - who is a STAR esthetician.  I can't say enough good things about how well she treated the skin on my back.  WOWZA!!!  If you get a chance to try Ursula's "Pause" spa - you MUST try it.
Wow - this place is enormous.  They have all the department's you'd expect at a grocery store - plus a sushi counter and a pizza oven area.  No issues - I got in and out relatively quickly.
Stopped in Around 9 PM on a random Tuesday night and got a Gyro to go and it was terrific.  Honestly, great.  Will come back to try more items. Good service too - since the place was dead-empty.

An enormous space that is sparsely populated with hockey gear, skates and accessories (Sadly, no goalie gear).  Also no figure skating gear.    They will skarpen skates for $7.  Service was icy cold - maybe because I came in alone? Not in any hurry to return as I have a figure skater - not a hockey player.

I am NOT an Outback fan - and this location is no exception.  I was dragged along for a family birthday celebration - and the person who's birthday it was is on Atkins and can only eat big hunks of meat.  So here we go - we had a party of 7 - and were seated right away because we can at 4:40 PM - otherwise I can only image how long a wait would have been on a busy Saturday night.  Service was absolutely fine - but the ladies room was HORRIBLE.  I told a guy in the bar area about the trash on the floor and they cleaned it up right away.  As for the "formulaic" food - it was edible.  Not good but not inedible. I had a rib-eye steak (asked for it without the salt-lick seasoning they usually use - I have learned my lesson from past salt-lick-steak experiences). Added a grilled lobster tail for $11.95.  Seriously?  This this was barely 2.5 ounce.  I could have had a bunch of shrimp for a fraction of the cost.  Anyhow - I also got a naked sweet potato as a side (not brown sugar - and the giant lump of butter came along side.)  Our 11 year old got a salad topped with grilled shrimp (again sans seasoning - as it is just too salty for our family's tastes).  She said - and I quote she felt, "unsatisfied".  Unsatisfied - that is just about the perfect way to describe our experience.  Blargh!

Awful today!!!!  Lettuce was wilted, nasty  and gross, avocados (which I paid extra for) were rotten.  I spent nearly $10 on a custom-created salad and I had to throw half of it out.  I was already back at my office or else I would have brought it back to the counter.  This is the location in Liberty Place and I used to come here about 2 years ago all the time with my daughter who loved it here.  I never "loved it" but now I shall not return for quite a long while.  FOUL BALL, Saladworks!

Eh.  I was not thrilled by Banana Leaf - the service was pretty spotty.  Very little english spoken by our server in particular.  Manager Lady spoke well, but seemed pissed off.  The food?  Aside from the Roti appetizer (which was 5 star, fresh and tasty), it was less than stellar.  Fried shrimp with Yuca were HEAVY as lead, greasy and over-filling. Green Curry in a Clay pot was fragrant - but just is not my bag, baby. I tried the Ginger Duck Lo Mee - too much greasy sauce and I asked for it "dry".  Oh well.  Live and experiment.  Not horrible but not orgasmic.  I won't be coming back soon.  I think I like Thai and Viet Namese food better.

OK, now that I have been going here for a while (Please, Jeff Prall - my old instructor - don't be mad if you are reading this but they are cheaper than you and I am broke right now) I can give it a true solid 4 stars.  Why not 5?  The space is just too small for all the equipment they have crammed in there.  And the studio for mat classes, while adequate for 5 or fewer students (which is usually the case) is way too packed for the 10 people max they will except.  I also wish you could get a package of 5 Privates or 5 Semi-Privates instead of 10.  Even with a price break $700 is just too much to shell out at once - for me anyway.  Karen Pecarsky, the owner, runs a good business and has good client service skills.  Her instructors, especially Danielle and Lucia (Lucia's Tower classes will kick your a$$) are terrific.  The online reservation system is a little problematic, but so far I have purchased 2 packages from here.  (Thanks for giving my friend her free mat class for refering me!)  I will buy another package, barring no unfortunate occurences.  So far I am liking it here.  Alot.  Wish Jeff Prall taught here.  He is my favorite Philly Pilates instructor.  Oh - and did I mention that I am so glad to find a Power Pilates (brand) studiio?  That's the kind I took from Allisa Stein and Susan Moran when I lived in NYC.  To me Power Pilates is a strong, solid modaility.  Lucia, girl - in my mind you are the mini-Romana.  You keep going with your training.  You rock!  (5 stars to you!)

We have been here 3 times now - the first was the best and was for a friends birthday party and her (rich) parents got the top-of-the-line $23 per kid package so the kids could basically do anything they wanted.  Mama on her own is a bit more, shall we say, frugal, so we usually get the middle-of-the-road pass which includes $5.00 on a refillable card for games.  Our 8 year old LOVES it here and it is much nicer than the crap-ola purgatory that is Chuck-E-Cheese (especially the nasty Chuck E. we were stuck with on Columbus Blvd.). She especially loves the "rock wall".  The games are often $1.00 or $2.00 per play (ouch) so watch your money!  Weonly have one kid, but I could easily see how a family with 2 or 3 (or more) kids would NOT want to come here.  Fun?  Yes. Better if someone else is paying?  Yes!

I thought the food here was surprisingly good for the quick-service and the fact that there is a full bar.  I had 1 brisket taco (very good - could have used more veggies - it was simple - Pico & Beef).  Also tried a Chicken Enchilada with a sinfully rich lemon cream sauce (not very authentic for Mexican - but tasty and fattening nonetheless.).  Decent fresh-made guac & lots of chips.  Lunch was under $11. Not bad.

Underwhelmed by lackluster fish quality (not bad but not great - had hamachi and sake sashimi) and too many sauces on the Salmon Tar Tar masking "meh"minced fish.  Tom Kha Gai which I normally adore was cold and "gloopy" and had to be sent back.  The best bite?  The kiddo's chocolate fondue ($10).  Expensive to pay for average meal at best. This is our 4th visit and it has gone down a bit each time. Sad - as I loved it here at first and we all enjoy the ambience.

We had a lovely 30-35 minute "medium" horse drawn carriage ride with Cynthia (a Philly native and a tough broad!) and her horse "Rex" a tall, handsome, well-trained draft horse.  My little one and I thoroughly enjoyed the good weather (perfect day - not too hot, not cold, no rain) and quiet streets in Society Hill.  I am hopeful that the horses are well fed and kept better than those AWFUL stables we drive by on 13th Street.  I am concerned for all those carriage horses being out in the heat and little fresh water around.

This is our go-to Wawa when we need "cheap Jersey gas" on our way from PA to or from NYC.  Decently clean ladies room and my 9 year old can get a chicken strip shortie with lettuce, tomato and cucumber (her "usual"),  Snacks, drinks, coffee and all the usual Wawa staples.  And in Jersey the gas is all full-serve (such a novelty).

This is a really good place - a bit pricier than I'd like - but worth it.  BIG margarita's and a good selection of entrees.  And yes, as said below, it is nice that they use MANCHEGO cheese and not some generic American alternative.  This is as close as you can get to authentic Mex in Bucks County.

Urbanfront is a decent sized Pilates studio CRAMMED with state-of the art equipment (4 reformers, 2 or 3 Towers, a few chairs and a Cadillac).  There is also a large room for mat classes that about 12 people can be in for a class.  The owner, Karen, is a Certified Power Pilates partner - which is good news for me, as I study this method of Pilates.  There are 2 changing rooms and 2 restrooms in the hall near the studio.  Fees are competitive.  Private, Duo, Semi Private and Group classes are all offered.  I came here for a mat class and returned for a private session with Theresa which was excellent.  I plan to return again as I purchased a small introductory package of Private sessions and mat classes which was a good value.

After a 6 year hiatus (I was not working in Philly) I am back and I guess I did not read my own review because I needed some sushi (sashimi, actually) and for $9.99 I got 2 pieces each of Salmon (not that great), tuna (good) and Yellowtail (surprisingly good and not fishy tasting).  I also got a $2.99 side of cucumber salad.  I may be back - especially when I am in the Comcast Center, as Sook Hee's has sadly, closed.

We attended a corporate dinner/dance event in the Christina Ballroom. This venue is easy to get to for us and free parking is great, however the event was a bit "sterile" and "cookie cutter" for me and there is no way I would have a wedding here.  Trade show?  Perfect.  Wedding?  Not so much.  Meanwhile the staff was wonderful especially servers Nicole and Latavia.  (Not sure if they came from the venue or from a catering company.)  This venue is a great asset for the Wilmington area and I hope they will keep it well maintained (bathrooms were spacious and clean - hooray!).  Please support business in Wilmington, DE - they need your support.

Iron Hill redeemed themselves tonight with truly stellar service from Bob and Ashley who gave my 8 year old an impromptu brewery tour in the middle of a Sunday Night dinner service.  French onion soup was SPLENDID and not a bit too salty.  Wonderful and worth the close to $7.  Nacho platters are huge but one suggestion - cheese is needed throughout - not just on the top layer of chips (The end is naked chips)..  DD loved the pasta carbonara with shrimp added ($4 more) and had her sauce on the side so she could decide if she liked it or not.  She did.  A real winner tonight.  We'll be back again.

The Pineville Tavern has changed hands several time over the past 35 years.  In its current incarnation (apparently since 1989 - dayamn I am shoing my age), the food is much improved and it is more of a "real" restaurant - or perhaps a "Gastropub" than a bar.  You can still get sandwiches and burgers and brews, but now you get get real meals as well.  Sit in the back and it feels less like a bar (the bar's out front.)  Update: Oh - and no, I had no idea when I wrote this review that Pineville tavern was gonna be on Diners, Drive-ins and Dives tomorrow night!  ACK!  I bet they'll get real busy!

I'm sorry - but this is just not the place for me.    And to say the least - NOT a place to have your firms HOLIDAY party (What are we - 11 year old boys?).    Yes, really, we had our 2007 Xmas dinner here which included pitchers of soda, a mediocre hot food bar with pasta.  No desserts - they were extra.  They also gave us all token cards.  (I confess, i did play a few games of Deal or No Deal) and amid the noise and chaos, we had a scavenger hunt.  I can't even tell you what the wnners got.  I was so NOT into it.

Well, at least Philly HAS a SEPTA.  After living in SF, DC and NY it is so disappointing to have such limited schedules and services as in SEPTAS Regional Rail (could they PLEASE add more departures from Doylestown on the R5 during rush hour??).  I also take the Trolleys, Market El and Broad Street Line - and the stink is just horrible.    I am willing to pay more for better service.  Philly needs it.

We buy liquor here on occaision because it is convenient. I think the PA liquor laws are really strange and generally nonsensical. They did have some chilled prosecco, though and that was great as I was on my way to a BYO.  Not a GREAT store - but OK in a pinch.

This store has GORGEOUS merchandise and even offers a bridal registry.  Too bad it's out of my price range.  The owner has a friendlt dog - who is not always there.  It's a really neat place to look around and get ideas - but to actually purchase here?  Just not gonna work for me.  Sorry.

My 13 year old is a lover of (Honeydew) Bubble tea and has tried it at a bunch of places.  Boba Tiki (cute little thatched hut motif) in Media is super convenient for us but not the best Bubble tea - but "very good" nonetheless - per el kiddo.  $5.10 for a large.  Very, very hot inside due to the refrigerators and freezers.

It is truly a blessing to have Capogiro right here in Philly.  This gelato/sorbetto is some of the best in the world!  The WORLD!  Better than places in Italy, NY, LA and many others.  LOVE!!!  Run, don;t walk, here to try some. We return again and again.

I like Havana's.  I don't LOVE it. I could easily give it 4 stars on a good (read: not packed with a zillion NY tourists) day.  OK - so it's a 3.5 star place.  Decent food and live music on weekends and it the summer.  Although, frankly I avoid places like this during peak season.  It's been around forever and is not too overpriced.  We had a great birthday party here a few years back for a friend of mine and they accomodated our group of 16 with ease.  (And got all our food orders right - the first time.)  Not sure if it's still on the menu - but the "Day after Thanksgiving" sandwich (Cold turkey, stuffing, cranberry sauce and other things) was a big hit and so yummy.

This is a review for one of the many Nina's waffles & ice cream trucks.  Our company paid for the truck to come out to our facility in Plymouth Meeting, PA for about 2 hours on a hot summer afternoon.  Each employee had a choice of a waffle and/or ice cream or a waffle cone with ice cream.  Many toppings were available.  I chose the waffle (fresh, hot, liege style) with home-made espresso crunch ice cream and a drizzle of chocolate ganache.  The man who made them (fresh - to order) was lovely as well.  WONDERFUL and indulgent treat.  A great idea for a corporate event or large party - rent the waffle truck!

The bakeries in Bucks County have not been that great, but Crossroads is surprisingly good - anbd busy as a beehive on Saturday mornings.  My daughter's itty-bitty (.95 cents) chocolate cupcake was the perfect size of deliciousness and I enjoyed a flaky buttery croissant.  I was very impressed with what we tried and would definitely come back again.

We had a lovely 30-35 minute "medium" horse drawn carriage ride with Cynthia (a Philly native and a tough broad!) and her horse "Rex" a tall, handsome, well-trained draft horse.  My little one and I thoroughly enjoyed the good weather (perfect day - not too hot, not cold, no rain) and qiet streets in Society Hill.  I am hopeful that the horses are well fed and kept better than those AWFUL stables we drive by on 13th Street.
Back again - this time for lunch - kale salad is my fave and the tuna tartare on toast (with zesty tonnato sauce) hit the spot!  Patient kind service - they now know me! LOVE LOVE LOVE it here!

Went to Ben & Irv's during Covid (sat inside - everyone wore a mask when no seated) and Michelle, our server, was beyond wonderful.  Half Sour Pickles are always a good thing. Classic Deli food with HUGE sandwiches (and prices to match).  Sadly, not as good as some other places - the chopped liver was just OK and the kreplach soup was good but not amazing (next time, Matzoh ball - a better choice).  Plus:  You can order your take out while you eat so it will be ready when you are ready to leave.  Excellent service and good but not orgasmic food.
7 Stones is the perfect blend of hippie and hipster. Iced La Colombe Coffee, Sandwiches, Salads and a friendly (cute) young barista.  A lovely place for a REAL cuppa.

Back in the early '90's this place was truly innovative - and it still has many, admirable programs and activities.  We nicknamed the White Dog the "Adjective cafe".  A simple dish of corn frittersmight be labeled as:  "Warm fresh sweet corn and roasted red pepper fritters"  The entire menu was so loaded with adjectives that it was hard to find was the noun was!  Anyhow - the food was/is, indeed, very good and many of the ingredients are local or at least regional and organic whenever possible.  I really admire the work that White Dog has done and the viable business they have built.  Go, dog, go!

It's a target - but not the best one.  It's got alot of pick-over merchandise, but all in all we can usually get what we need.  We shop here 1-2 times per month and never fail to drop at least $100 on household products, toddler gear and assorrted crap we don't really need EVERY time we walk thru the door.

We came on a sale day (25% off just about everything in the store) and managed to battle the choking throngs of people to get bras & shapewear.  The shoe department was so overcrowded that shopping was just not possible.  Great values (on sale day) but be prepared to power-shop!
Fan-frikkin-tastic. Super fresh foods for meat eaters and vegetarians.  4 kinds of Tabbouleh - one with Quinoa. Lentils.  Eggplant.  Labni.  Dolmas.  Schwarma.  I'm in heaven!
Nice, small, independently run pharmacy - which I always love to see. Picked up a few sundries here. A bit pricey - but so convenient.  And it's NOT a CVS!    HA!  Glad to have you in the nabe!

Not bad - for a deli/hot food buffet.  Especially oif you get here at 11:30 or so when the food is still fresh and has not yet been picked over by the lunch crowd.  Nice guys behind the counter/grill for breakfast, too.  Reminds me alot of my deli in New Yawk.  I like it, OK for a cheap, quick fix.

Where would we be without Uber and Lyft? I check both and see which will get to me quicker out in the 'burbs.  Sometimes it's not about $$ for me but time. Time is money.  LOL. I wish more reliable Lyft drivers were in my area (Media, PA). One of my friends is a Lyft driver but she is in "Souffily".  Anyhow - so far only good experiences.

So sad - just called to book a lunch-time banquet and was told they no longer offer banquets on the weekends.  (And now that they are renovating part of the building they may not offer them at all for a while.)  Boo.  Wanted to have an event here.

This location is in the Gallery - so it gets downgraded from the 3 stars I would normally give to an ON by default. The dis-interested, underpaid staff has a distinctly "ghetto" vibe here - but all in all you can still get mass-produced, el-cheapo disposable clothing here.  I very rarely get anything for myself at ON - the snooty law firm folks I work with could sniff that out in a minute.  Instead, I lavish my pre-schooler with $5.00 sneakers and 2 for ten jammy sets.  Oh and socks - love the cheap socks.

I was part of a large party (about 33 people) with a set meal and it was good but not great - I have a feeling ordering off the "regular" menu would have yielded better results.  Meanwhile, service was good - especially by Will & Anna - and the lady at the reception desk is very kind also.  Tofu & Veggie soup was good. Salad was your basic iceberg with ONE slice of cucumber and one small wedge of pale tomato.  Kinda blah. (Got the overly sweet ginger dressing on the side).  Sushi was the best part and the tuna avocado and salmon avocado maki were both good (4 star for that).  Salmon teriyaki dinner was a bit too well done for me - but again it was part of a "set" meal and if I ever went back i would have ordered it more on the rare side.    I dither between 3 & 4 stars but dated decor and food improvements that are needed prevent me from giving a higher review.  In the mean time for a cost effective group party they can accommodate about 30 -35 people in the back dining area.

A beautiful, gilded Catholic church but absolutely nowhere to park. Celebrated a funeral mass here and parking in this neighborhood is chaos.  Singer had a beautiful voice and the organ is amazing.   Roman catholicism in all its old school glory.  Hallelujah. Lord, hear our prayer.

I'd skip Geno's and walk around the corner to Pat's - or better yet - go to Jim's. Or Tony Luke's. Or Pastificio's for the real deal.  Let me just add that I am NOT a cheessteak eater - I get a Chicken Cheesesteak 'wit Provolone and 'shrooms once or twice a year.  Geno's is filthy and to quote below - the owner is a racially prejudiced "ass clown".

We had a far better experience at the Ardmore location of NYAJ than we ever did at the Glen Mills one.  First of all the layout, crowd and vibe are a bit different. We arrived in stages - 7 women in total - and our delightful, albeit overworked server, Melvin, came right away with bread and "dipping oil".  Since we arrived in time for happy hour (must order by 7 PM) we were treated to $5 Sangria, Margarita or Pineapple Pain Killers.  The Sangria, to me, was the tastiest of the 3.    $6 apps included sliders in 3 varieties (any combination you choose), cheeseburger, mini crab cake (great) or buffalo chicken.  We also tied the waffle fries and lettuce wraps (from the regular menu) and carrot cake for dessert.  We had a great time socializing and listening to the (loud) 80's and 90's background music.   Shout out to MELVIN for top-tier service.

We went here - believe it or not- for our neighbor'd 5 year old daughter's birthday party. Um - OK - a 5 year old.  FIVE.  F.I.V.E.  OK.  We brought our 3 year old.  There were about 14 kids from ages 3 - 12 and their assorted parents.  It was a Saturday during the afternoon.  This place is really neat - but it's more like a club-slash-bowling alley.  It is NOT where I would have a kids party - but surprisingly it all worked.  The adults had drinks and lots of fried-bad-for-you apps. The kids ate a grocery-store cake that they brought and Lucky Strikes made little cheese pizzas for each kid.  They did not have any milk for my 3 year old so she got all sugared up on a big glass of OJ.  Dudes, this is not a kids place.  A sweet sixteen (like Rumer Willis - allegedly had at the Lucky Stikes in LA) maybe - but not a freakin' five year old.

A good place for take out - they do have a room with card tables & chairs next door for eat-in, but the decor just screams - take out.   An old-school staff of pizza makers crammed into the busy kitchen turns out terrific FRESHly baked pies.  The cheese, pepperoni/sausage and veggie combo we ordered were terrific.  2 large pies fed 6 adults and 3 yound children.  The veggie pie was my fave - with roasted red & green peppers, broccoli and spincah - so tasty.  I recommend the pizza here.
The crepe cakse are a work of beauty and art - $55 - $65 each and so worth it. Delicious crepes.  So excited by this place.

Raw at Boyd's is owned by Raw on 13 & Sansom. The sushi is excellent - and this is a neat place to have a quiet, casual or business lunch.  The lunch bentos are tasty and plenty of food. We enjoyed having lunch here numerous times in 2008 & 9. Have not been back since I changed jobs.

Neither a spa, nor relaxing. My daughter and her sister booked appointments for 60 minute massages and were deeply disappointed.  The male therapist (I doubt some how any of these folks are licensed), had shaky hands and was so bad my daughter's sister requested another therapist mid massage.  The other (female) therapist left a room several times to "get things" throughout the half-assed treatment.  No way we will ever come back here. You get what you pay for - and here that's not much.

We had great service (yes, really) from Ariel at Hildago - and the place was nearly empty (so maybe that helped).  My shrimp quesadilla (simple) was excellent and the Sopa Azteca was great, too.   Not cheap - and the $7.95 guacamole, while fresh, was not nearly as good as Dos Gringos nor my 12 year old kid's version.  Meanwhile, the food here is way, way better than at Diego's.  We are so glad to have them here in Media.  A little pricey for what it is...

What?  I coulda sworn I already reviewed Pietro's.  I have been here several times but will base this 3 star review on my last visit which included a terrific basket of hot pizza dough rolls (and Olive oil for dipping) and a special salad with Poached chicken, avocado and eggs over delicious, crisp romaine.  Huge - and FRESH.  A winner.  Very affordable and good in a pinch when you are in the Rittenhouse area and don't have time/money for the swankier joints.

It's ginormous - but it really has suffered in recent years.  This crappy economy can't be helping.  Droves of bored teens roam the mall.  Be sure you remember where you parked - people have LOST there cars (or had them stolen) from the enormous parking lots.  The outlets can be a bargain but yo9u MUST shop carefully.  Some of the prices are standard retail.  Do your research before you go.

Olive Garden is Faux-talian-American and is really not that great. My inlaws insist on going to chain restaurants like this, Buca di Beppo, Romano's Macaroni' Grill (how the heck do you grill Macaroni??) and other sub-par poser-Talian chains.  Meanwhile, my 3 year old loves it here - so there's no accounting for taste. And it used to be cheap - but no longer.  I had a so-so shrimp scampi (angel hair here is a definite AVOID - ads it is always overcooked and mushy.) and it was $16.95.  The unlimited iceberg & white-bread (Oh, sorry, I meant salad & grease-sticks) are a big turn on to college kids and cheap in-laws alike.  For my time & money - there are FAR better places to go (even in the spectra of Faux-talian chains.) [See my review of Bensi's]

We have always enjoyed the food at the Polish Festival - but you can also get some of the basics (Pierogies, Cabbage Rolls/Gulabki, Coffee and Babka) year-round in the rec-room/cafeteria area under the shrine.  Not particularly inexpensive though - so bring a bit more cash than you might think.  Brings me back to those Polish-fest days!

Have not been here for quite a while due to working "up north" and shopping for dog food and supplments at DelChester Feed (Love that little old place!).  Now I work 2 minutes away so this PetSmart and the nearby other "big box" stores come in handy.  Stopped in at 12 noon on a random Tuesday for a tick collar and some supplments.  Get your dog on Glucosamine/MSM at a young age! It makes a real difference in their elder years.  Happy they are here.

What problems!  What hassle - the cecutiry lines are miles long. Better allow for lots of extra time.  The parking costs a bundle (as with all airports) and once inside the shopping is mediocre and over-priced. ($3.00 for bottled water???) They have you TRAPPED.  Supposedly an airport "spa" is set to open.  Maybe that will help.  The bathrooms also need more frequent cleaning.  And don't even get me started about holiday travel.  Ugh!!!!!

What a difference 2 years makes.  Still need more dining and after 6 PM this place is DEAD - but during the work day we need LUNCH - and breakfast.  And another Starbucks (There is one in the hotel) - or better a La Colombe or Old City Coffee.  Keep it coming.  This area has such great potential. More shopping would be good. A spa?
One of the best La Colombe cafe au laits that I have ever had. Puts Starbucks to shame!  Lovely!

I am updating my review to give a GREAT recommendation.  Go see Mai and ask for CND Shellac - the relatively new no-chip gel lacquer.  It claims to last 2 weeks (mine lasted 9 days cip-free, 11 days with some edgewear - by day 14 it was cashed).  I just had a spa pedi, eybrow wax and a Shellac Mani (in a rich red shade) all for $67 ($77 with a $10 tip).  I am re-thinking Chau's.  I will be back.

Walked in and waited. And waited. And waited.  12:30pm  on a Wednesday.  Busy dining room. Not a hostess in sight.  Got a head nod from a busy waiter in the back but was unsure what it meant. Waited some more.   Walked out.  WTF???  This review is based on service.  I had no chance to be greeted, seated or "eated".  Sad.

OK, so instead of a dollar store - we now have a fiver store. 5 below sells lots of cheap crap - some of it useful and seasonal - like we got a booogie board for our 5 year old here, and some silly bandz. Now that she's 8 she can buy her nail polish and bath & body colorful items here.  My kids loves it here. The CEO used to run Zany Brainy and went to Friends Select.  (He's a smart guy!)  I am not a huge fan of cheap crap - but hey - if it keeps her happy - so be it.  Oh - and you can get Good Humor and other ice cream treats for 1-2 dollars in the front freezer (cheaper than most Wawa's and far cheaper than the rip-off ice cream truck at the beach.)

OK, I went to Ursula's spa "Pause" which is a single treatment room inside her make-up studio.  The facialist Elina was excellent.  the facial itself was also very good - and the home-made vegetable based (cucumbers and parsley) mask was the best part of the "Seasonal Phacial" that I got.  They are running a deal thru 5/2/09 where you can get one of 4 different PHacials (cute - huh?) for $60 - instead of the list price of $110 - which nobody pays.  I say that because she also has a discounted series price and cut me a deal to get a series of 3 more phacials - so I did.  If you are a client of UrbanFront Pilates - next door - she will definitely work with you.  For $60 I had a great facial and Elina did an extensive arm, neck and back massage, too.  The products are all cheap private label - sorry - but they are.  The just have Ursula's label on them.  The cleanser and toner were good - but very standard.  I am a product junkie and didn't buy any products.  Thankfully, neither Ursula nor Elina tried to push any on me - they were both sweet as sugar.  I can't wait to go back for my $50 back treatment nerxt week.  So for $60 it's a 5 star facial - but for $110 - no way - maybe 3 stars.  I will compromise and give them 4.  They are definitely worth checking out.  Also Ursula charges a very, very high price for lash application.  I'll be doing them myself.  Oh well.  Oh, and they offer REAL sugaring (not wax mixed with a little sugar, sugaring.).  Elina is really the star of the show, so I hope Ursula treats her well.  She is a good facialist and I know one when I feel one!

Friends don't let friends drink Charbucks.  (Ok, Ok, I still drink it sometimes...) But not when 7 Stones is so conventient and wonderful.  Between the La Colombe coffee drinks and a huge selection of teas, fine pastries, quiche and even ice cream, this place is a WINNER in every way.  Love. Love. Love it here.

No. Just No.  Came here for Dining Under the Stars because we knew they'd have a table (and here's why). Food is Meh and service is confused and chaotic.  Forgot to write down our order on a check thus we never got a check and had to TELL them what we got.  Then it took a while to actually pay.  Meanwhile people are waiting for our (now coveted outdoor) table.  Pad Thai (Chicken) was good - yes, it was. Tom Kha was average.  Bathroom is gross.  They need to step up their game or they won;t be around many more years.

I am writing thuis review kinda sorta on behalf of my dad (who might even give them 5 stars - he loves it here.).  I have only been here twice and both times (with my parents, of course - who LOVE the fresh mozzarella salad and prime-rib (or is it filet) beef sandwiches.  The first time we went my daughter was a wee 6 or 7 months old and I was in a post-partum haze.  The experience was a drag from soup to nuts.  (Nevermind that we did not order any soup nor nuts).  Mom ordered and raved about her fresh (and milky white) mozzarella and tomato salad.  Dad was in red-meat heaven.  Strangely enough we never actually get any beer here.  (The 'rents don't drink it.)  Then little angel-pie decided to pee in her diaper.  So I had to change her diaper.  And things got ugly.  There was NO WHERE - and I mean no where to change her.  The ladies room was a one-person operation with NO changing tabel and no area.  The floow in there seems icky.  So I whipped out my portable changing pad (waterproof) and tried to subtley and quickly change her on a tabletop in the back hallway.  I was immediately yelled at by a (male) manager to stop.  I basically ignored him - as I was nearly done anyway) and finished wiping the babies butt, threw the dirty things in a plastic baggie, threw the baggie backinto my diaper bag and went back to the table.  I was so ticked off.  I mean, what was I supppsoed to do - there was NO WHERE to change this kid.  A 6 month old baby.  Whatever.  So anhow - thety have great food and a terrific selection of salads - but don't bring a non-potty trained kid here.  (In our case an infant.)  Rant over.
Just  OK.  Good baked good.  Mediocre produce.  Sorry - but the peaches were sold out and the green pepper was old.  Not impressed, Tabora!

Ok - I'll give it 1 star - maybe 1 and a half. The staff (what staff?  One disgruntled lady at the front counter?) are inattentive, underpaid and look bored.  The prices are city prices - so I bought my much-needed box of Kleenex and got outta there.  Glad it's here, as this end of town NEEDS such services, but please - could you re-stock your shelves, lower your prices and get some people who CARE - even a tad bit - in there to work?  Rant over.

I was lucky - I came here right at 8 AM when the pharmacy opened and the place was empty - thus no waiting (lines here can be ridiculous.).  Plus I got a bottle of "SmartWater" for $1.  Score!  Wish they had more cashiers.  (They also have 4 self check outs that sometimes don;t always work.)  A necessary evil.

This farm-stand is on my regular route so I stop here in season for locally grown peaches, tomatoes, sweet summer corn and freshly cut flowers (mind the bugs!).  Driving by their sunflower field is just so uplifting.  Nice young (teen) gals running the front register.  Support our local farms!

Surprisingly wonderful.  This opld-school diner has friendly "career" waitresses and serves a terrific french onion soup. (Not too salty - and just the right amount of golden brown bubbling chees on top.)  Don't miss the home-made pierogies - a plate of 3 (large) one sauteed in ample amounts of butter and sweet onions.  BLISS (and calories) on a plate.  We really enjoyed stopping in here while house-hunting in the Media area and plan to return.

Every summer/fall I stock up on Billy's fantastic poultry-based (he makes pork based also) sausages which he sells at the Media Farmer's market.  I can't wait to get to his (new location) place in Wilmington.  The chicken/broccoli rabe and chicken/spinach/provolne sausages are delectable.

Grotty digs and no A/C, but even so, friendly staff and a family-run jawn.   An extensive menu of wraps, salads, hoagies, steaks and fried goodies. The food itself was just OK.  I had a wrap and the bacon tasted a wee bit sour.  (Odd) Plus it was drowning in ranch dressing.  Next time (if there is a next time) I will get less dressing or ask for it on the side.  I want to support and love local businesses - and Sleepy Hollow is a neighborhood fave, but for me it was just OK.

I am not and have never been a 7-11 person, however, I was desperate. Stopped in on a Saturday morning before 9 AM and the place was empty.  Bought a few low carb snack items, paid the friendly (owner? Manager?) cashier and left.  No issues.

Have been back 3 more times and I need to just stick to the items I like.  (Salmon Spring rolls - a greasy but tasty indulgence)  Love the Quinoa salad - dressing (sugar-fest) and puree on the side.  Pizza is AWFUL.  (We tried the whole grain crust and it was weird tasting.) Pasta dish was swimming in a greasy sauce.  (Never again.) No substitutions on specials.  (Oh, well.)  It's formula cooking and for a bar - 4 stars but as a restaurant it's more like 3.  Service is sporadic and server-dependent.  We've had it great and not-so-great.

As aforementioned, parking is inadequate here - but if you go on a Sunday morning you can park at a metered spot in the street and walk across.  A bit pricey - especially for produce - but staples like milk and eggs are on par with Acme or Giant.  Lots of gourmet items and prepared foods.  A nice "chi-chi" market in yuppified D-town.

A great selection of molded chocolate confections and other candies and goodies. Conveniently located in the RTM.  Bark, non-pareils, peanut butter cups, chocolate covered pretzels, rats, bats and Halloween and Christmas chocolates, too.  Fun!

So disappointed and a I fall for it time and time again. Well, this is the LAST time.  I came here when Comcast Center first opened and it was more like a 3 star place. This last time?  The tuna was NOT fresh, slices of fish were puny-small and thin, rice was dry and overly vinegary.  Just Plain Bad.  Oh - and it was $11.95 (plus tax) for a 4 piece nigiri and 4 pieces of a (gross) salmon avocado roll.  That's that. I am through here.  Sook Hee's, here I come.

For technician skills (love you, Mai!) this is the BEST I have found in Media so far. Plus they treat my little one so well (cute pedicure chairs for kids with DVD players in them.)  I had a mani and spa pedi ($45 - but they are offering a discount through 11/17 for their 10th anniversary). Oh - and a mani is regualrly $12, Pedi $25 (mani plus pedi is $30 I think??  They give a small discount).  Spa pedi is usually $35 (Mani and spa pedi ran me $45 - actually $41 after the 10% disc. - not including the tip I left.)  Very nice people running the place. I'll be back for sure!

Panchero's is akin to Qdoba/Chipotle and other fast-food Mex in that you move down "the line" and select your items.  Panchero's schtik is that they press your tortilla to order (The pull out a blob of dough from a proofing box and flatten it in a press).  Even though I usually get a low-carb option - I had to try the tortilla, I mean, come on, it's why you go to Panchero's.  Verdict?  Very fresh tasting and the quesadilla I got was tasty.    Slightly cheaper than Chipotle - and I think I like it better.  Need a fast-casual Mex?  Stop in to Panchero's. Plus it's right next door to the Media, Starbucks, so you can get a $5 coffee to go with it.

Just OK service and decent sashimi for a Saturday lunch. The place was deserted around 2 PM.  Salmon and tuna were fresh.  Escolar (Mock white tuna) was not.  All that said, I have now been here twice and I would come back, if in the area.

Absolute perfection (and you pay for that!).  I attended a corporate holiday soiree complete with 2 bands, a DJ, a photo booth, Open bar, lavish cocktail hour and a "stationed" dinner with Carving station, sushi, sliders, Italian/Pasta station and more desserts than any diabetic has a right to enjoy.  The coat check, restrooms, bartenders, food service folks and management were all TOP notch.  Wow.  Like a frikkin' wedding. Or Bar Mitzvah.  Amazing!

This is a review for the meeting space and public areas of this newly opened and sorely needed hotel in Media, PA - great location for business travelers who need access to the Delaware County Courthouse.  I attended a meeting in a meeting room (rented for a fee) on the first floor.   Since this hotel is brand new, everything was super clean.  The very young man at reception was friendly and helpful and said that rack rates vary from $125 - $200 for a single room or a "King Suite" with a pull-out  couch.  There is a teeny tiny indoor pool and several kids were enjoying it. They also include breakfast and the crowded breakfast area (at around 9:15 AM on a Saturday) seemed good.  We need this Hampton Inn very much so I pray they will keep it clean and well maintained.

UGH!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!  If I could give them Zero stars, I would.  We just got back from dinner with our 5 year old daughter who really, really, really wanted to go to a Burger King so that she could get the "Cats & Dogs" Plastic toys they are promoting on TV with their kids meals.  We obliged her - and I figured that even though I loathe fast food, I'd get a side salad or something.  Well, when we arrived I insisted that DD & I go to the ladies room to wash hands.  The bathroom was soooooooo disgusting (seriously, it made Penn Stations Bathroom in NYC look clean.) that I immediately attempted to tell someone.  That's where the real fun began...  My kind & patient husband was waiting in the order line and for us to come out of the bathroom.  (When we first arrive there was noone in the line - and the dining room was nearly empty - Monday night around 7 PM)  So buy now there are 2 people in front of us.  One guy gets his order fulfilled and leaves.  The next guy is having a problem swiping his credit card.  It won't take.  So we wait.  And wait.  And wait.  We placate DD with a Burger King crown.  And we wait.  Meanwhile 2 BK staffers are dealing with credit card man and another slack-jawed employee (in front of the fry machine) stands there looking on.  Noone takes our order.  Finally...  The guy comes over to take our order.  I tell him about the ladies room (We'll fix it, he says - and to their credit they did.)m he takes our order and we sit down.  Did you know that BK offers Kraft mac 'n cheese as a kids meal choice?  Well they do - and DD got the last order of the day.  Anyhow, may $1.00 dollar menu side salad (which was loaded with fake-cheese-topping - eew) was barely edible.  I watched kiddo eat the mac 'n cheese.  Drink her apple juice box, dip 3 fries in ketchup and play with the prized "Cats 'n Dogs" toys.  Aye yi yi.  Mama needs a cocktail And some real food...

Now I gotta be honest - I havenb't visited B&I in YEARS, but back in the day it was a go too breakfast/lunch/brunch spot.  Bagels, eggs, the works.  My parents liked it - and had it been closer to Doylestown we woulda gone there much more.  Glad to hear they are still around.

Pleasantly surprisedby the quality of the food.  Small Plate option of a single Salmon Spring Roll ($5.50) was perfect.  Quinoa Salad was nice but thank goodness I got the cloyingly sweet dressing on the side.  Loaded with sugary fruit puree too.  It's close by - so we'll be back.
Still great - and nice new digs. Taco Salad is great with (small, but plentiful) grilled shrimp.  Corn Tacos al Pastor are always a tasty winner.  Friendly service and quick, too!
I only like Saladworks if the lettuce is fresh - and sometimes at this one - it's not.  It's also like $7.000 for a salad.  Eek.

John, the owner is such a nice man. He gave my daughter 2 pretzels and a pretzel dog (with or without cheese).  The pretzels were cooked evenly and not too gooey nor burnt, however there was alot of salt which she picked off.  Good pretzels and located near our house.

This is a pretty sub-par Rite Aid - but at least it exists.  I was pretty close to giving it 1 star, but decided to be kind.  Disinterested staff, high urban prices.  Needs help, but I am glad they are around in a pinch.
New owners have made things better but hours are still insufficient and sporadic.  Now that Kung Fu tea has opened up about a block away, Boba Tiki needs to up their game.

We came back to Hildago with another couple who are regulars and they directed me to order the pork tenderloin special, served in a delicious chiorizo sauce and stuffed with Jamon and cheese,   It was amazing. I likened it to a Mexican riff on Pork Saltimboca,  Amazing!  Ariel (The owner's daughter) is lovely as always and the fresh pico, guacamole ($8) an chips are a must.  We love you, Hildago!

My 12 year old is obsessed with PINK and Adidas and other "name-brand" casual clothes.  Plato's closet is a hit-or-miss source for used, low cost clothing.  Be prepared to get your hands dirty (eew) and dig through the racks - but if you do find what you like it is a great value.  Plato's has many locations and this one seems grungier than the Paoli location or the Philly location.  Step it up, please! We need you.

Very impressed with the service and food for our group of 8 (supposed to be 12 but 4 people bailed) on a busy Saturday night.  French Onion Soup was perfect - not too salty and not too greasy.  Others enjoyed burgers, veggie quesadilla (loaded with 'shrooms) and guacamole (very good). Fried calamari is not my thing but the table enjoyed it.  Prices seem to have risen a bit - but it was never "cheap" here. A great selection of beers of all sorts.  Decent (but pricey) cocktails  ($9 - $13).

Massimo's pizza is located in Booth's Corner's Farmers Market and thus has limited hours. I got 2 slices and 3 (rather large) garlic knots to go for my 14 year old. She ate one of the slices (plain) and 2 of the $1 a piece knots right away and seems to really love it.  Later for a second meal she ate the other knot and the remaining slice of "upside-down" pizza - just like plain cheese pizza but cheese is under the sauce.  She liked them both but prefers the classic Neapolitan pie to the "upside down" pie.  All in all?  At $2.50 a slice this is a good way to get pizza by the slice - they have a ton of choices including "square" Sicilian, tomato pie, Hawaiian and many more.  And the garlic knots are, indeed, yummy.

Just OK - I had a salad bowl and the cucumber salad and baba ghanouj were fine - the rest (hummus, limp romaine, dry chicken and tough-mediocre "steak") was edible but blah.  Do not get the steak.  Not at all juicy.  I love this type of food and have tried 2 other local mini chains Naya and Cava and they were both better than Naf Naf.  I wanted to love it but it is just Meh.  That said they staff greeted me upon entrance (I came in early before the long-ass line)  and the cashier was very friendly and polite.  Might try it again but might now.
This used to be Genuardi's, now it's a Weis.  It's fine.  Not the worst and not the greatest - still better than Acme and not as good as Giant.
I love coming here - and have been coming here since about the age of 10 - I kid you not.  Asian art and decorations for the home.  Quintessentially New Hopian.

I have come here a few times and on 2 occasion now they have gotten my drink order wrong. Both times they fixed it right away though.  One time they gave me regular when I asked for decaf and I could feel it right away - wow.  What a jolt!  The 'Bux in Paoli is way better.
If you've been to one CVS you've seen 'em all.  Pros:  small parking lot Has everything you need  Cons:  Small parking lot - you better watch out! Inept staff High urban prices

5 stars for service from Emily (and the male manager and a pink-haired server who's name I did not catch).  Emily served our group of 9 ladies for a long-awaited and long-planned Happy Hour.  We got a large table (a few tables pushed together) in the back and ordered apps to share (delicious fried Brussel's sprouts and thick-cut sweet potato fries with 2 delectable dipping sauces - try the vanilla sauce).  Folks ordered their own drinks and dinners - but 4 of us had the pan-seared scallops with a creamy risotto.  DIVINE.  Our only complaint?  The $15 nachos (close to $20 if you want chicken) used to be an enormous platter - not anymore.   The nachos are still wonderful but you get much less - plenty for 3 people - but not for 9.  The 5 stars goes for the tremendous service including separate checks and rushing in a happy hour order (Iron Hill's Happy Hour drink specials end at 6 PM!!!!) for us.  So glad I planned my Ladies Night Happy Hour here.

I hosted a party for a group of 20 at Iron Hill and things went WAY better than ever expected or imagined.  We enjoyed delicious nachos, wings, guacamole, crab quesadilla, cheesesteak egg rolls and a few folks ordered dinners.  There were Salmon, Scallops  - and my 9 year-old demolished a big plate of fettuccine carbonara (Ah to be 9 again and to be able to eat like that). Desserts like cheesecake and the Chocolate Brownie Sundae (it has a special name) were show stoppers. (And many pints of Raspberry Wheat were consumed as well).  We are so pleased and grateful to our server, Megan and all the expediters, servers, bussers and hosts/greeters for a wonderful and fun evening.  I would not hesitate to recommend Iron Hill to friends and colleagues when planning their holiday parties or other group events.  What a great experience.  Brava!

Went to the "unofficial" yelp event last night at ten stone. Even though I am old and farty and not much of a bar-chick, we had a great time.  It was a lovely evening and we were able to snag a nice table outside.  My husband and a friend of mine ordered beers and I had a vodka cranberry.  (Made with the house vodka - it was pretty bad - I should asked for Grey Goose - Oh, WELL.).  A bit later we got hungry so we ordered a spinach and apple/goat cheese/candied cashews salad (YUM!), a chipotle chicken wrap, a big mug of spicy chicken chili, and another big mug of edamame.  Reaqlly quite good for "bar food".  I will definitely be back!

I dream of El Limon's Al Pastor - it's so good. The guacaomle/Salsa/chips combo for $5 is a great value. My kid devoured her huge $9.95 shrimp burrito.  (Dry - but you can also have it with one of 3 terrific sauces).  Even DH enjoyed his salad with Asada.  Love this place - and a free margarita if you simply ask.

Brand spankin' new Chipotle in Media/Lima, PA near the old Granite Run Mall (that has been demolished for brand new stores like this).  We are so glad you are here.  Love those burrito bowls. Please stop charging over $2 extra for guac.  At Qdoba guac is free (price is built in to base price though.)  Love the kids meals - enough for a grown up.

Surprisingly impressed by the "group dining" experience our school group (70 fifth graders are about 50 parents/teachers) has every year here. Carb-heavy el-cheapo menu of Bread & Butter, Chicken with Mashed potatoes (buttery) and Veggies (Squash/Zucchini) - super buttery.  For Dessert?  BREAD pudding.  Meanwhile that was a kid friendly and safe choice.  They greeted, seated and got us fed in under an hour.  WOW!

We had an amazingly great time - food and service (by the lovely Maria) with our party of 6. It was the first day of the "new" OctoberFest menu and we surely enjoyed it.  Mustard Crusted Salmon, Caesar Salad, Chicken and Pork Schnitzel and of course, great beer and beverages.  The only thing preventing a 5 star rating?  Deafeningly loud - as it was quite crowded (Saturday at 1 PM_ and we sat right near the open kitchen.  Service was quick and attentive.  Lovely!

I am not a big cheese-steak lover - in fact - I don't like them - but for Jim's I make an exception.  You can forgo Pat's and Geno's (and the rude "'Wiz 'Witout, fast-paced steak-nazi ordering techniques) and get me to Jim's after a night of partying.  Love the chicken cheese steak wityh provolone and 'shrooms.  Once or twice a year is MORE than I can handle.

I dunno - we come here about once a week and never have had an issue - my kid is a vegan so her "bowl" is rice, beans, pico and guac.  Never a problem.  Young staff but they are always fine to us.  Not sure why others have so many problems?   But yes, they do need to clean more.  Run by teens. Fast food. Not expecting the "Ritz".

I see Dr. Brian Feeney (Dr. Steve is often way overbooked) as does my teen daughter, my ex husband and my daughter's figure-skating coach.  He is wonderful and has helped me to manage occipital, neck and shoulder pain.  Can't say enough great things about his work.  Limited hours and days so book early.
A great dining area with casual places like the crepe place, a juice bar, Buddy's Burgers, Noodle Bowls and an OPlive Oil/Balsamic Vinegar place.  Fun to browse around and eat lunch here.

Just ordered a sofa and loveseat from Ashley - will update this review when it arrives (3 - 8 weeks from now.).   Fingers crossed.  So far the sales team has been great - and we are on track to receive the furniture in mid March.

What a beautiful community resource!   The library has a children's department, lots of space for adults to read and do research, computers and group activities.  They offer story time for little ones and Japanese Anime for teens. There is a conversational French group, too.

Oh, Zama - you truly rock my sushi lovin' world. Tonight I dined alone but was still treated well (thank you!) as I sat at the 8 chair sushi bar and watched the chefs work their magic.  A single negi-chu-toro hand roll was buttery perfection. A $28 (7 piece nigiri) of market specials was delicious and 5 of the 7 fish I had never tried or never even heard of.  All delicious.  Perfectly marinated ikura (salmon roe) - although for $5.00 a piece - the portion was very tiny.  (Like 18 eggs or so.  Come on, guys!)  And for "dessert" 2 perfect slices of house-made tamago (none of that frozen garbage here!).  Domo! Domo!  I am infatuated (once again) with Zama.  Decor is Zen, sleek & lovely.  (Look up to see the giant Koi above you.)  $60 including tax 'n tip (no alcohol) is pretty steep though.  My husband may freak out on me.  It also underscores what a GREAT value Doma is and how high-priced Morimoto is.  (Zama is right in between.)

I am vacillating between 3 and 4 stars - here's why...  I drove in (easy to get in - but hard to drive out - you must exit onto Route 1 and it is a divided highway there - so you have to go down to the next traffic light and then turn around to go the other way.  Located on a busy corner of Route 1 and 452, this place has been here 11 years!  It is freshly painted and bright and cheery inside.  WALK INS ONLY.  They do not take appointments.  NEVER.  (Really?  Yes, really.)  Meanwhile, It was not crowded on a Tuesday evening, but I bet there's a big wait on Saturdays.  Anyhow they offer many "tiers" of service from a basic $11 mani, to a cheapie $20 no-frills pedi to the $55 Delux spa pedi.  I went for the $36 spa pedi - a regular pedi with 10 minutes of extra massage (Ti-Kim - my technician - set a TIMER.).  So far, so good.  However, the polish selection are all no-name brands - with a few scattered bottles of OPI.  My suggestion - bring your own polish (and possibly your own base and top coat.)  The real test will be when I get a mani here. Oh - and they do gels for $25.    It's OK - but I have been spoiled by high quality/low cost NYC nail care (and more recently 4 sisters in Center City - the newer location).  Ti-Kim is  a lovely lady - so see if she is there if you go.  I will be back - this place is leaps and bounds ABOVE the other spots I've seen in Media/Aston.

Affectionately known as Charbucks or Fourbucks - we have adopted the slogan of:  "Friends don't let friends drink starbucks."  Save money by brewing at home with Peregrine Coffee (the BEST) or go to La Colombe or Caffeination.
Hit or miss - but when you hit, you can hit it big. Good deals on hostess gifts/housewares too - but you need to be patient and pick through.

O.M.Goodness. The hangover burger could easily be called the Heart Attack burger.  If you are ravenously hungry and have lipitor on hand, then try it. I ate 1/2 (and a side salad instead of fries) and I need a nap.\  Perfectly cooked burger on a brioche bun with bacon, cheddar cheese and a fried egg.  My diet has been calorie bombed!  Took the other half home. So good.  So bad.  So good.

I loathe fast food - so when my fast-food eating spouse (and newly indoctrinated child) demand frosties - we stopped here.  My bad.  Meanwhile, the food was (the usual unhealthy) edible. This place is very "old school" in decor and could use a makeover.  Do not try the "new" homestyle mac 'n cheese - swimming in velveeta-like goo. YUCK.  Salad greens were not so fresh.  Hamberger was fine (the same ole, same ole). Oh - and I asked said 7-year-old if the chicken sandwich was better here or at Chik-Fil-A she empatically declared Chik-Fil-A the winner.  But she loves those darned frosties.  For less than $15 for 3 people to eat?  CHEAP. But - you get what you pay for.  I never recommend eating fast food. UGGH!

I did not find evelvation burger to be particularly "elevated" - in fact, the burger had no seasoning.  (At least it wasn't over seasoned).  I ordered a "create your own" single patty burger (I don't need 2 patties) with Lettuce (iceberg) tomato, caramelized onions (greasy but good) and guac ($1.50 extra) - came to about $6.  No fries, no drink.  Not bad but not great - Five guys is about the same, Smashburger is better.  Meanwhile, if you need a burger (or fried chicken sandwich) and you are at the dying Plymouth Meeting Mall, go for it.  Spacious, clean seating, icy-cold a/c system - the place was nearly empty at 12:15 PM on a Monday.  Not a great sign.  Bertucci's next door was hoppin'.  Kid friendly.

I am rating this based on the swimming pool and programs for children/toddlers.  The teachers were/are lovely but the facilities (locker rooms & pool) are just Meh.  Meanwhile, I am thankful that my (then) 3 year old (now 5) had 2 great sessions of lessons here for a decent ( a bit high but not horrible) price.  She loved it here!

I stopped in after seeing the takeout food a coworker got at my new job - 2 minutes away.  It seems like a typical strip-mall take out spot with about 5 green-jade plastic tables.  The whole family runs the place and my pint of Beef & Broccoli (6.75) was just fine - asked for light sauce but still was not so light. The grandson (son?) was there and he is so cute - about 4 years old.  Nice younger lady running the front counter.  You can also get a lunch special from $5 - $7 which includes pork fried rice or white rice.  I will be back - but I don't do Chinese too often. Maybe in 2 weeks...  Strip mall is easy to get in but hard to drive out of (202 and another busy , divided highway).  Note:  They do not provide water nor ice so you HAVE to purchase a bottle of water (or a soda) or else go without if you are dining in.  I caved and bought a diet coke, but next time I am bringing my own water.

A great source for poultry - whol and parts (and eggs!) right in the Reading Terminal Market.  Ground Turkey, turkey and chicken cutlets, boneless skinless chicken thighs and whole fryers are some of the GREAT things I have bought here.  Great place!

I gotta say, for $3.71 I got a perfectly crafted (yes, that hot, hot barrista CRAFTED it) iced latte served with a smile and it tasted Deeeee-licious.  Maybe it was because it was 5:15 PM? Maybe it's because I asked for it with "whip" Maybe it's because the barrista was so hot (I did mention that, right?)  But whatever it was that latte was MAGIC!  Nice place.

Decent Chinese/American food.  Square on Square is better 0 in my opinion, but the decor here is a titch nicer.  They serve all the standards like egg rolls, chicken & brocolli and pepper steak.  I have had lunch here a few times - never dinner- and I always got in and out quickly.  Convenient Walnut Street location.

Coffee shop - only open in the mornings and early afternoon (thus never whenI am there.)  Parking lot is big but fills up EARLY with commuters.  A few benches outside to wait for the train when the station is closed. It's OK.  Just Meh.

Young & Bowman have been our family's plumber for years and years. They are trustworthy and know their stuff - and they come relatively quickly when its an emergency (and when ISN'T it an emergency when your toilet seriously malfunctions?)  Nice folks.  A bit pricey, but great customer service - and they come in the dead of winter to fix those leaky pipes.
You can get really nice stones from Blue Nile instead and have your own jeweler set them.  Yes, Tiff's has quality - but you PAY (dearly) and overly for it.  It's kinda like McDiamonds.

A new-year's day feast with my 12 year-old salmon-loving kid and great sushi. We actually tried to come at 2:40 PM - they are CLOSED from 2:30 - 5 PM (no "linner").  Lunch is a MUCH better value than dinner, but we love the spicy tuna ball appetizer and salmon plate.  (Ask if they have toro and/or salmon belly - as both are terrific.) The Tropicana roll ($7.95) is a tasty also.  Friendly service and not crowded.

My friend lives in Kennett Square and I just HAD to get an iced coffee - so off to the trusty Dunkin' we went.  Average prices, place was dead-empty at 4 PM (so speedy service) and all the "usual" DD suspects.  America may run on Dunkin - but Dunkin runs on me!  Long live the iced latte light!

Not very good.  My daughter ordered take out from here twice - she liked the wings - but now we prefer the Vine Street branch of Wings to Go.  The salads are not fresh here.  Sorry.  Oh - and get to-go (take out) it's depressing to eat here and small.

Juicy - long the purveyour of pricey velour tracksuits - has opened a boutique at 17 & Walnut where the Bath & Body Work used to be.  Very nice things, but kinda young for me and not corporate enuf for work.  Good "knock around" weekend clothes and party dresses - but way too pricey for the junky fabrics they use.  Also the sales staff (range in age from 18 - 24) are very snotty.  Not  a fave for me.

Since my last update, we have been to Doma 3 or 4 times including New Year's Eve (amazing) and last night just me and my 6 year old.  She ate 2 orders of Shrimp Shumai. and a bunch of edamame. And then she said, "Mommy, I don;t want any chocolate lava cake this time".  Smart kid.  I had the Naked Salmon roll (sans jalapenos) and it was so good, I ordered a second one.  And that was it.  2 rounds of Shumai 'n salmon.  And we were stuffed.  Dan & the guys are so great with my little one.  She loves to sit at the high-top tables in the back.  (I prefer the regular tables, but I was out voted.)  Oh - and if you go to DOMA - save room for dessert (if you can).  The mochi-coated strawberries dipped in fudge and chocolate lava cake (sounds trite - but they make a good one) are amazing.
This Dunkin has a drive thru - but in the morning coffee rush (7:30 ish) I usually park and go in -it's faster.  I come here on my way to work. decent service and clean dining area.

I have gotten breakfast here once and lunch 3 times so far - and it's right in my building complex - where the old Marathon used to be.  The meatballs are the real deal - fresh and homehade.  I also have tried the CHicken Cutlet with spinach and provolone - and it was delicious - although not diet friendly. (The cutlet is fried - but they do offer a grilled version.)  They also have a nice salad bar with a few hot foods on it. I got it today.  I also had a large ($9.99) spaghetti and meatball platter.  The meatballs were tasty and authentic. (Only 2 though - wish there were more.) Pricey for what it is - but so much better than Au Bon Blech across the courtyard.  The lines are long though and they need better crowd management.
Super-friendly service - and a good selection of papers and poster board.  I needed some in a pinch - and there it was.  Nice to have an art supply place around.

They have remodeled but the service is still pretty abysmal. Not to mention the low quality, artery clogging food.  My 13 year old likes to get the four for $4 deal about twice a month - You get a tiny sandwich (chicken or a mini burger), fries, a few chicken nuggets (more fried food) and a drink.  El kiddo like the chocolate frosty.  I am trying ever so hard not to be a food Nazi, but I would never eat this garbage.  I try to not take el kiddo here too often.  There is one guy who works here and has for a LONG time who live in our neighborhood.  Otherwise, I never get great service and the drive through line can back up in a hurry.  People, apparently, love Wendy's and this location is doing just fine.
Keeps getting better - and much improved from 2010. Christmas market (back every year), small ice rink in winter, music and food trucks in summer.  Nice!

5 stars for Zori and Tanya - the dynamic duo of nail technicians.  Yes $73 for a mani/pedi is way too rich for my blood (plus they charged an extra $10 to soak of gel - my salon charges $5 for a soak off - and I only had it on 7 fingers).   But the results are amazing. For a special treat (I had a gift certificate for a mani/pedi that I won in a charity auction)- I would not hesitate.  A regular mani alone is $23.  Youch!!!

Swanky indeed.  I loves me some good bubbly - so I was very excited to come here - and have been here thrice total.  The large & small plates are great for sharing.  Sushi is good - but not high-brow.  (Not Shiroi Hana Quality).  The Asian/Fusion fried rice and other dishes were good.  Pricey - but not mind-blowingly so.  Great service all 3 times - and not crowded - but all 3 times we went early.  Good date place.  I'll be back!

We have seen a frew films here at the Franklin Institute's Tuttleman Imax theatre - ,ostly because we are members and have a 4 year old.  She loves it and would probably give it 4-5 stars. We thought it was OK, but it can be crowded.  Luckily we got centrally located seats fairly high up and the views were great.  I miss the old days with Pink Floyd and Laser light shows.

I have had a couple of pairs of shoes shined here and one needed new heels/soles. No issues from me.  I wish Philly had MORE shoe shine/shoe repair places. They are a dying breed.  Bring money to pay the deposit.

Simply stunning!  George Baker provided all the floral arrangements for my former law firm - and also sent arrangements to all new hires (nice touch!).  The floral choices were always high-end and fresh.  No carnation and babies breath here.    Fresh Delphinium, Alliums, Bells of Ireland, Lilies, Rare Orchids - the works.  I love George Baker.  Pricey - but so worth it.  Elegance in a glass container!

Doma!!!! What a treat to be able to dine here again.  Tonight re-affirmed that Doma is one of the best restaurants in the city. It's my fave and my 9 year kid (who has been coming here since age 3 or 4) loves it too and scarfs down salmon sushi, edamame and her favorite - BIG shrimp shumai.  I had a delectable Kalbi dinner with 9 large pieces of tender, juicy short-ribs. DH had a variety of sushi including our love - the Naked Salmon.  (try this!!)  Thank you DOMA (and Pat and staff) for wonderful food and service for all these years - and hopefully many more.  We love you!! (And we miss you - now that we are out in the 'burbs.)

I work in Plymouth Meeting/E. Norriton now and we had Izzie's cater a lunch for 30 people.  The sandwich trays were very good - much better than many other places - as the sandwiches were served on mini challah rolls that were very fresh and delicious.  Chicken and Tuna Salad were great and not overly mayo-laden.  Meats looked good too - corned beef, turkey and roast beet.  1/2 sour and full dill pickles, coleslaw and pickled tomatoes were decent (I am not a coleslaw fan).  Very well done - and we will order again.

Just got back from IHOP in warrington (down 611) for an early (8:30 AM) breakfast on Labor Day.  Thus they are getting a nice, pleasant, non-mobbed 4 fat beautiful stars from me.  There were 5 in our party and (miracle of miracles) we were seated promptly and cheerfully greeted by a smilling late-teen server "Kelsey".  We ordered pancakes, crepes, eggs and omelettes all around and everything was hot, freshly made and served the way we specified.  I  much prefer IHOPs pancakes to Perkins - but my 3 year old has never met a pancake she did not like.  I also love the crepes - I omit the giant wad of butter-like spread they plop in the middle.  Who needs to eat THAT much fat?  2 for 2!  Now the best part - the check came quickly and was accurate, too boot.  In the past this IHOP has been a crazed 2-3 star mass of strollers and screaming children.  But today's miracle breakfast was just a J.O.Y.  Stay tuned for an update.  (Don't go here during peak times - it's a frikkin' zoo.)

We don't "do" fast food - but - we will on occaision take our little one (now 7 - went there more when she was 4,5 or 6) to play there and eat chicken and fruit cup.  It's fried.  It's not that great for you - but it's way better than McDonald's or BK. Plus the kids just love that play area.  So we love Chik-Fil-A - on special occaisions.

Super-yum and a super value. I also forget its here because I usually don't go that far down Arch Street, which is a shame because I love Aya's.  I have only been at lunch time - but the prices have been reasonable and the food is excellent.  Nice yellow/earth toned decor, too.  Delicious baba ghanoush and pita bread.  (Very thin, hot pita - so yummy.) They also serve some Italian-Greek ish food - sort af a Medditerranean hybrid.    I agree with Caroline about the Aya's taster - what a great way to start the meal.  The Chicken gyro is enormous and very nicely seasoned.  Not greasy, too, which is a plus.  LOVE Aya's! Can't wait to go here again.

I love crepes - and had walked by this place many times. So I finally went in (even though I had not before due to the high-ish prices). It was $4.95 for a plain crepe with butter and sugar (drizzled with chocolate or grand marnier had I desired.  I did not.  I wanted fresh lemon).  They had none. Do basically I had a plain butter/sugar crepe for $5.  Whipped cream is also a free option.  For $4.95 this was too miuch for a plain crepe. That said, it was tasty - and the service was friendly.  I will go back once more for the $6.95 crepe bearnaise.  I hope its more substantial.  Tip:  Eat there - or only take out if you are right nearby.  I work 5 blocks away and it was too far to take it out and have it still be hot and fresh.  I wish Passero's was still here.

Very good for grilled cheese, a few soups and salads to go with it (and a neat TV watching area - like a mini movie theatre - in the back).  I tried a sample of the roasted tomato soup (VERY good) but settled on a 1/2 & 1/2 - where you pick 2 different grilled sandwiches to try.  I got 1/2 shortribs and 1/2 Baja Chicken.  I really enjoyed the Ribs and Mashed potatoes (Not too much). Next time I will add tomato to it.  Avocado Ranch dipping sauce as tasty, too.  I wish they'd offer an alternative to potato chips (A green veggie?  Cucumber slices?).  I would definitely come here again - but not too often. Plain grilled cheese I can get at home.  Oh - the parking lot in this "strip" is awful.  Outback Steakhouse is there and take up a big chunk of the lot.

Hit or miss and you must be patient and willing to "pick through". As Marshalls go - this one is average at best.  Disinterested staffers gabbing up front.  Not a great experience but - when you find a good deal you can hit big!

Absolutely no issues - we came at 7:15 PM on a Wednesday night in the summer - so no line and thankfully, no dried-out old food.  My kid got a steak burrito to go and I did not have to cook.  Seriously.  No issues.

Decent enough service - and a selection of papers and poster board.  I also got some crayola (yes, really) art supplies here in a pinch for my (then) 4 year old.  Convenient location.  Nice to have an art supply place around.

Kinda pricey for potted plants, hanging baskets, garden supplies - but it has been there for years & years.  Always a good place to get my mom a hanging New Guinea Impatiens - in a pinch.  Also potting soil, pruning shears, the odd supply that I forgot to get at (dare I say) Kmart.  Oh - and Kmart is way, way cheaper.  BUT - and this is the big but - Buckmans will give you free gardening advice (try getting that from the zit-faced, disinterested 16 year old at Kmart!) and that my dear, is priceless.

5 stars for $1 (mini) canolli day!  We stocked up on 12 canolli and they were gone in a flash. Happy husband, happy kid and kid's friends. (We got 6 ricotta and 6 vaniall Italian cream.)  YUM!!!  We are so lucky to have Viso's right in our own back yard.

A welcome addition to State Street and a good place to take the kids for a cup or cone of house-made ice cream.  Flavors change periodically but the always have chocolate, cookies and cream, vanilla and at least a few fruit flavors. (Sorbetto?)
Love the Media Theatre.  Love the location, the history behind it, the shows, the fact that Wanda Sykes is involved (part owner?).  Love the camp in the summer.  Support your local theatre!

Well, I may be biased because friends of the family run this place, but Suzi's is the "best little topless bar" in Line Lexington.    No really - it's a good place for a bachelor party or just to chill.  Not MY scene, mind you - but yes, I have actually been here on a few occaisions.    Say Hi to Joel at the bar - and Suzy is still alive and well - but she does not run the bar any longer - her kids do.  We love you, Suzy!

Soft fresh white bread (rolls) and decent cold-cut based sandwiches. A decent value and yes, very fast service.  This location was clean and convenient when my kid & I needed a quick lunch. Tuna is very good - for chunk light - not too mayonnaise-y.  Cucumber and tomatoe slices were fresh.  No issues.
A neccessary evil - especially living in the "hub" pf Philadelphia. I try to take Southwest whenever I can - but sometimes I gotta do US Air.  Coach is, indeed, horrendous.
Update:  I just found out a friend of mine works here.  5 stars for Danny - about 3 for the food.

This is my 7 year olds FAVORITE store for cheap makeup (lipsticks), accessories, floral hair bows, ribbons, sunglasses and funky boots.  We love to browse here - and occaisionally buy, too.  Very kind staff.

Took my little one here for the $12 haircut. We usually go to the SuperCuts in Philly - different owner/franchise.  This one the lady did not cut the hair short enough.  I asked for the bangs to be shorter. She told me not to go any shorter because it would be shorter when it dried and would look too short.  So I trusted her.  I was wrong.  Kid looks like she barely got a haircut. Now we gotta go back 2 weeks later.  FAIL.  Thank god it only cost $12.

Delicious fresh fish, but pricey. Lunch (Just a special) was $15.95 - so $20 after tax and tip with no beverage.  5 pieces of nigiri and a delightful spicy tuna roll. The sushi chef (there were 3 or 4 when I went at lunchtime) was de-scaling a huge and beautiful snapper.  Wow.  I still wanted more - LOL. Friendly server and dark, but elegant digs.  A strange smell when we entered though - not awful or I would have left.  Meanwhile, I can't afford to have lunch here on a regular basis.  The full/dinner menu looks amazing - so maybe I will try a dinner here.

I ate here one time about 18 months ago.  Service was great and the Thai ladies who served me were very cordial and friendly.  Food was only so-so - and now the Thai Chef is in business there is really no reason for me to go to My Thai,  However, I will say that Thai food is not as abundant in Philly - so I am glad they are here as they do meet a need - but I am still on a quest for truly awesome Thai in Center City - there is some great Thai in the Suberbs.  Maybe I should have given them 4 stars?  But that really is pushing it.

Severino supplies fresh and frozen pasta to restaurants and gourmet stores all over the area. Good stuff!  And a great selection.  The basic linguine and fettucine are staples for us. Stuff pastas like cheese ravioli and tortellini are also excellent.

Sorry @Michael - but I disagree.  Yes, Stutz is an area landmark - they've been around for DECADES - but the candiesare just MEH.  (Better than Russell Stover - but not great.)  They are a fresher version of drugstore "assortment" chocolates.  ICK.  Once you've had fine chocolates (Michel Cluizel, Teuscher, Leonidas) you can't eat this dreck any longer.

I had already reserved a spot in this convenient garage (19 near Market/Chestnut) for an evening event in Philly and then I read the (scathing) reviews.  I feared the worst but was very, pleasantly surprised. Drop off at about 4 PM on a Summer Thursday was easy-peasy and Antoine was friendly and let me rummage around my car for a bit to make sure I took everything I needed with me (You can't easily get back to your vehicle once they valet park it).  Pickup is where most garages in cities fail, long waits, damage to vehicle, horror stories.  Thank goodness - I had NONE of that.  I presented my pre-paid parking pass and my ticket and in about 15-20 minutes (yes that's long but not horrible) My vehicle arrived.  I would definitely park here again but not during the business day (too much money) and not on a Friday Night (Center City is insane on Friday nights).
No issues.  Got in and out quickly. Took kiddo ext door to Yogurtland for fro yo.  Parking lot sucks - always a chaotic, crowded cluster.
