The salad was just OK - not the best Caesar and not bad by any means - a bit over-dressed and heavily sprinkled with parm (which some may enjoy.)  I am in no hurry to rush back here, but if I did I would bring more money and go for dinner and get the "full experience".  The $10 cheapie lunch is just "Meh". (Serves me right!)  Oh - my server, Erin was a doll - giver her a raise.  She could use it!

Even post-renovation, Wilmington station is pretty sad.  The good part?  Less crowded and smaller that NYC or Philly.  You can get Amtrak or SEPTA here.  The building itself is historic and architecturally significant.  Restrooms are nasty - but much improved post-rennovation.

I am a huge supporter of Philabundance as well as other food-related charitable organizations in Philadelphia and NYC.  Philabundance works with schools, businesses, corporations and community groups to gather and distribute non-perishable food for those who need it.  Learn more - and support Philabundance!

Location, location, location - and this is a good one. EVerything you need - for the most part from stationery to toner to computer stuff.  Nice to have it in Center City.  Customer service is meh and prices are high (you gotta pay that Center CIty rent!).

I had been to Oggi for hair (with the aforementioned and sublime Cynthia - she rocks!) but never for spa treatments.  I actually did not realize they offer so many great things. So when I heard about the mid-week (Tues, Wed or Thurs) 3 treatments for $99 special, I just had to indulge.  I had a "relaxation massage" (30 minutes of swedish) and 30 minutes of hot stone with Jenna.  She is a very nice gal and a talented therapist.  After that I had a marvelous paraffin manicure with (can't rember her name - Yelena??) a very excellent nail tech.  (Russian lady who's been there for years.) I loved it!  Seriously - the mani lasted about 6 days chip free.  Great products and flawless technique.  If I were able to - I'd come here all the time.

A little better post-rennovation (2015), bathrooms are still marginal at best.  ONE cashier at the Amtrak ticket counter.  ONE.  They need 2 for sure.  Few amenities - but thank goodness the a/c was working on that hot July afternoon I traveled from Wilmington to NYC.  Trains were packed and oversold.

My husband had a basic Lube/Oil/Filter done here about a year ago because we happened to be nearby.  They were very quick and seemed to do an OK job (but what the heck do I know about cars?  I write the checks, baby.).  They did recommend alot of un-needed extras (did we want new wiper blades?  Did we want an upgraded this or that?)  but we did not take the bait.  Thus we escaped with our wallets (and hopefully our Hyundai) intact.

I had dinner here at about 7:30 PM on a Friday night and the place was DEAD empty - I was the only person there.  The 2 people working (Owner's Mom who does alot of the cooking) and man at the sushi bar, speak NO english.   Very, very nice people and I want them to succeed but they can barely communicate.  Aside from that, the place is new and clean and the fish was fresh. I had the Tuna Tartar ($12) app and the Sashimi app ($12).  Fresh miso soup with LARGE chunks of tofu was great (complimentary?) and a small iceberg salad was fresh with what appeared to be ranch dressing?  (a creamy white dressing, not the typical orange colored ginger dressing).  They offer Sushi - as you'd expect but next time I will try the Chinese food menu as the owners are CHINESE!  Porkchop and Chicken Legs over rice looked great.  And home-made shrimp wonton soup.  I will be back.

What a great l'il (not so little, actually) space.  You can tell that atrsy-theatre types have made this space what it is - and it is a GREAT multi-purpose "Black box" theatre with a great array of gigs/shows & films that can be showcased here.  GOOD JOB!!!  I'm sold on 941!

Local dance school used Gertrude Hawk as a fundraiser around Easter time and the Chocolate bunnies (Big - but hollow) are delicious and worth the extra money.  The chocolate covered pretzels - packages in an elegant gift tin are terrific too.  Pricey - but that extra cash goes to the fundraising organization.  Pretty good, I say!

A little pricey - if it was $25 I would come every week - but for $35 ($42 with tip) it's better for important things.  I had a nice blow-out with Hope but I did not like it at first - not straight enough and it was a humid day - so I asked her to use the flat iron, which she did an then I loved it.  My hair is fine and slippery so the style only held for about 7 hours - but that was good enough.  Cute salon - like sitting inside a pink cupcake with sprinkles. Fun.  I will be back and I enjoyed Hope's witty banter.  One note:  Receptionist has a "cold" vibe - but it was 47:45 Am so maybe she hadn't had coffee yet?  Also - I LOVE that you are open at 7 AM so I can get a 'do for a business meeting. AWESOME!!!

3 Cheers and 4 stars to Fran (our fabulous server) and the Silver Diner.  Yes, it's faux.  Yes it's a bit kitschy - but when we went (for a lovely lunch on a weekday at 2 PM) it was clean, nearly empty (great service) and the food was GREAT.  My dining companion had a decadent platter of 4 Challah-French toast slices drizzled in (not too much - just right) caramel sauce.  Served with 2 eggs and CRISPY long bacon strips.  It was the picture of perfection and - according to my friend - tasted great as well.  My unique dish was the crab-cakes benedict.  (luckily I asked for the sauce on the side - as I did not need the extra glop/calories).  The 2 crab cakes (one atop each english muffin half) were VERY good.  Lots of crab and not too much filler.  I was even able to get broccoli in lieu of home fries.  We each ordered soft drinks which were served in large "vats" (free refills) and Fran got us to-go cups, which was a nice extra touch.  We'll return for sure!  A great alternative to the mall restaurants.

really good, solid, pies - delivered fresh and hot - and ACCURATELY (Whoo-hoo).  Decent chicken-cheese steaks too.  Reasonably priced, ample dining space (albeit not glamorous - and packed at peak lunch hours).  Note:  If you work for a big firm - like we do - they wil do BREAKFAST pizzas 0 wth bacon and eggs and ham on them - they are slammin' good - but by special order only.  (Normally there's nobody there during the breakfast hours.)

Get here early or you may be disappointed. We arrived at 6:45 pm on a busy Saturday and they were sold out of burnt ends, chicken and ribs. Luckily we enjoyed pulled pork, chopped brisket and wings.  Sides of cucumber salad, Mac 'n cheese and garlic mashed potatoes were satisfying.  Reasonably priced and super casual.

Perhaps one of the WORST Wendy's ever by sheer fact that the staff working here are illiterate, innumerate and just plain rude.  I came in here Friday evening to buy a kids meal for my 4 year old (the only reason I'd even venture in - as I don't "do" much fast food.)  We ordered a chicken sandwich, mandarin oranges (instead of fries) and a lowfat milk.  They left out the milk!  (Grrrr.)  So I went trudging back and was given the milk - what a pain.Unless your 4 year old MAKES you come here - don't bother!

Cute, needed and pricey coffee spot on Bridge Street in "downtown" Lambertville.  Bought 2 brownies ($2.75 each - YOWZA) and they really weren't that great.  Nice counter staff, though and the place was hoppin' on a Sunday afternoon.

Zero Stars - if possible. Awful food, dis-engaged service, loud outdated decor and just plain BAD.  My inlaws insisted on going here because they had a coupon. Oh the horror.  You can make better spaghetti at home.  The sauce came straight from a 55 gallon drum. Anyone can.

Honestly, the service and food here are always top-notch.  And, yes, it's a chain but it does not feel like one.  we had a private party for 12 (in the back small room) and it was lovely.  Lobster Salad (I love it here) never disappoints. Wonderful!  Tastes even better on an expense account,  (Alas, I was paying.)

Super slow service on a Wednesday morning at 8:15 am. One lady just plain left, but I stuck it out and got my $4.50 iced half-caff latte.    The good news? Close to my office. The bad news?  Don't come here if you are in a hurry.   Clean restrooms.
A Shiseido store that also carries Quiora (from Japan) and other lines.  Mostly catering to the Chinatown crowd, nice ladies selling products & accessories.

Great and conveniently located kitchenware shop.  They have cook and bakeware, bar ware and even coffee beans they grind (or not) to order.  A vast selection of peppermills.  GREAT for the novice or pro-Am cook.  Helpful staff and "decent" (not cheap but not overpriced) prices.  Many of the items here are high end and thus are pricey by nature.

Food is fine, service from Mandy is always terrific.  Stick with chinese dishes and skip the sushi.  Spare ribs, house special wonton soup and candied walnut shrimp are my parent's go-to meal.  The place is never crowded. I guess they survive on take out business.   A good choice for Chinese.

While I am not a 5 guys fan, I gotta give props to the attentive and friendly staff at this relatively new Media outpost.  I ordered a burger - which is 2 patties in a lettuce wrap.  $2.09 for a Dasani (shudder).  If your kid has a peanut allergy don;t go here - they serve peanuts-in-the-shell while you wait.  Typical 5 guys - not healthy, limited menu, but what they do, they do well.  And wow that cashier was great.  (Anitra??)  Big shout out to her.

Kudos to Justin and the team for a lovely lunch of Bun with Sugarcane Shrimp and a Spring roll.  A $4 Hot Espresso with Condensed milk served both as a beverage and a dessert!  I love Vietnamese food and Pho Street is a good place that is sorely needed in the 'burbs.  Prices are moderate and service today was wonderful.  Can't wait to come back!

It's just too darned expensive.  Yes, they have nice clothes for babies and kids.  Yes, they have cute gift ideas and upscale toys.  No I will not spend $256 on a wooden rocking horse nor will I spend $54 reduced from $180 on a bikini for a 2 year old.  Sorry.

It's in the Gallery and while it's decent - ,any of the pastries are too "gloppy" for me.  It is, indeed, cheaper than DiBruno's - but it is not nearly as good as Termini Bros.  The cookies have brightly colored sprinkles and thus, My 4 year old just adores it here - but she's a kid and would eat cookies just about anywhere.  Birthday cakes here are moist and tasty - a good option if you work in the area and need an office cake in a pinch.
Ate lunch here again and this time had the Pho and it was very good.  Even better? The summer roll appetizer with peanut sauce.  Sooo good.  Can't wait to come again. Great for a winter warm-up.

No issues with this location of Giant - and fortunately I shopped at a non-peak time - a weekday at 5 PM.  Place was dead empty - just the way I like it.  Prices match my go-to Aston Giant location and selection here is a tad more limited and also a few more ethnic (Hispanic and Asian) and high-end items.  (Welcome to Newtown $quare).  Ah, Giant.  You put Acme to shame!

Met a fellow yelper here for dinner and we both sprang for the $26 lobster rolls.  Big, meaty and the real deal!  Excellent - and the toasted, buttered top-split NE-Style bun was just right.  I subbed tender green beans ($2 up-charge, dang it!) for the fries.  My Arnold Palmer was quite tasty, too, with 1/2 iced tea and 1/2 "rosemary" lemonade.  Herbaceous yet refreshing.  I would come back - but for the price (a bit too high) I won't be running back.
Keystone concierge provides valuable and helpful services.  They found me a great dog walker.  I recommend them (and the owner Lori) highly.

Nothing for ambience - GET TAKE OUT - but for fast and tasty pizza with a medium thick (not thin and not thick) crisp crust - this is a great place.  Our law firm had a few lunches catered with NUMEROUS pies brought in including Plain, White. Veggie (so great), Sausage (pellets), and Pepperoni.    The attorneys feasted with gusto.  A decent nay-bor-hood joint.  Jewknowamsayin'?

A perfectly average Wawa (old school, no gas) with a star deducted for the super-hectic parking lot. Be careful!  A zillion people coming and going is an accident waiting to happen.   Meanwhile I got my $2 iced latte and got in and out.  Unscathed.

Wow - there are still a few Happy Harry's left in business.  Just the name makes me a little nostalgic.  Basically this is like a Rite-Aid or Thrift Drug - sundries, magazines, cosmetics and a pharmacy counter.  Not bad!  Very good for cheap school supplies, too.
Yuck!  Now that there's Bolt Bus (a division of Grey hound) I will NEVER use Greyhound.  So dirty.  Yick.

Had a very good Cafe Au Lait here this morning on my way to a SATURDAY training session.  (Oy!)  Service was fast and friendly - even on a Saturday.  The only downer?  The aggressive homeless lady who asked me twice for change and then followed me around to the coffee condiment bar and hovered while I put Splenda in my au lait.  Not Saxby's fault - but not a great way to start the day.

Happy hour is what you want here, not dinner. Service by Vinnie at the (crowded) bar and $1 buck a shuck oysters and shrimp on Wednesday nights are a good deal. And half of Philly was there to take part.  The $7 lemon drop martinis are well made, easy to drink and also a good bang for the buck.   One of the best happy hours in Center City.   Skip the dining room, hang by the bar!

After YEARS of walking by and not stopping in (even after reading great - and not so great reviews on yel) I popped in for a quick take out Iced Ethiopian Yrgecheffe coffee.  Soooooo delicious and a roasty-toasty (but not burnt tasting) flavor.  Friends truly don;t let friends drink Charbucks.  Well worth the $2.40 including tax.  Can't wait to come back for a proper Ethiopian meal.

TCT. (TCCT) Typical Chinese (cheap) Takeout.  greasy, fast, inexpensive - especially for lunch specials - I had Tofu w/ Mix. Veg. - light on the sauce which was a smart move.  2 Spring rolls (grease fest) for $1.85.  Desparate times called for quick lunch. This place looks like it has been here for years - and could use a new menu board (pictures are ancient) and a good cleaning.  Take out only - or eat on one of the 2 greasy tables..

Have not been back in a while and quality and cleanliness have slipped. So has service.  Very inexpensive and tasty Viet specialties - complete with V-Pop videos playing on a flat-screen.  Bun Hoi was OK - a little greasy (I was surprised). Crispy pancake was SOGGY - but it was loaded with shrimp, pork and crunchy bean sprouts. Spicy chicken over broken rice was very simple and good.  Took home an order ($4.95) of summer rolls for el kiddo.

This funeral home handled my late grandmother's cremation (they have an onsite crematory) and transported the remains to her final resting place over 20 years ago.  A few weeks ago I contacted them to ask about pre-planning and costs for other family members and they were so great over the phone at explaining everything.  When the time comes, we'll be calling Huff & Lakjer. Just hopefully, not too soon...

This branch of Old Nelson is located in 30th Street station - so you are a "captive audience" - and thus pay the higher prices for snacks, coffee, cold drinks, decent sandwiched and salad items (they have a full deli).  A decent choice when waiting for a train - and better than fast food.

Wow!  We got a Wegman's - right on my way to Whole Paycheck and just past the Fresh Market.  Love Weggie's - but very crowded and you can easily over buy/over spend here.  Don't shop hungry!.  The cheese department is terrific.  Also a "Pub" and dine-in prepared foods (and mediocre sushi).  Cute little coffee bar in the front of the store, too.

This is our go-to spot for take out Chinese in Doylestown (and seeing that I worked at the now de-funct Chong's Garden for 5 years - I know what I'm talking about.).  Jack is a great guy - he used to have a place in New Hope, too - but now it's only D-town.  The steamed dumplings are a little doughy - but my 4 year old loves them.  The 10 ingredient fried rice is cooked to order and is DELICIOUS every time.  Full of chicken, shrimp, scrambled egg, peas and other goodies.  We also enjoy Chicken & snow peas and peppersteak.  The peppersteak is loaded with onions - so know this - you can ask for it without or with less onion.  The chicken is all white meat and delicious.  They will make you just about any and every old school Cantonese or Mandarin sih you could want.  Oh - and get it for take out - the dining room needs a re-hab.

This place is kind-of a tourist trap and part business-yuppie lunch spot. They do have decent food, cutesy decor (with swinging chairs at some tables) and over-priced cutesy-named drinks.  They also recently starting hawking 2-bite teeny-weeny desserts served tapas-style.  Whatever.  The "Green Submarine" is a veggie sandwich that I'll get in a pinch at lunch time when I am forced to eat here by co-workers who have no originiality and are too scared to try Matyson.
This was sorely needed and now, thankfully, is well used and seems to be well maintained.  Lovely.

Kudos to Deb, Bob and the rest of the staff who run the Cafe and watch over the "VIP" club level seats.  What a treat to have a private box. Food is just OK (Tough "steamship round of beef" and oddly salty chicken marsala). Baked Ziti and salad were fine.  Popcorn and soft pretzels were a hit with the kids - and of course, having Rocky Bluewinkle visit the box is a BIG hit.  We love the Blue Rocks. The seats during the week are empty - so come out and take your kids.  Inexpensive family fun!

I had wanted to try Fat Salmon for quite some time and yesterday I got a chance to have lunch there.  For $13.50 they were offering a special holiday lunch.  You got a choice of soup or salad (I had the iceberg salad with tasty ginger dressing), and either 2 maki, 1 maki and 1 cooked item or 2 cooked items.  I chose 2 of the specialty maki which normally are $7.50 - 9.50 on their own - so this lunch was a good value.  Ask for sauces on the side - alot of the special rolls are loaded up with semi-spicy mayo and tempura crunch.  The regular lunch menu is also a great price point. Dinner prices are a little high but not crazy.  Cool, icy-blue decor made it feel like Christmas.  Service was quick and efficient.  I can't wait to go back. I will try the sashimi and then render a TRUE verdict. For now though, I still stand that DOMA is the best sushi spot goin' in Philly these days.  (Save for Morimoto which is cost prohibitive.)

A very important monument.  Took my kid here at age 5 and again at 6 & 7 to play and learn simultaneously.  Plus there is a cool dog park next to it.  A painless way to teach your kids about the concepts of immigration/emmigration, famine and Irish history.

It is rare for a jaded ex-New Yorker like me to give a 5 star - especially out in the 'burbs, but Nectar really lived up to the hype last night. Aside from the gorgeous decor and scrumptious Pan-Asian cuisine, the exceptional and personalized service we received from Bruce & Laura (??) was truly top-notch.  In truth, this is probably a 4 star place, but it is a very, very strong 4 stars. Terrific for a date night.  Wonderful for making healthier choices.  LOVE and can't wait to return.
Stick with Chinese dishes here. The salmon teriyaki was overcooked and the sushi was not great.  Not in a hurry to come back.

Mediocre food and truly awful management. There was a private event upstairs and we were told TWICE that all ages were welcomed - but it is a BAR and 21 and under are not allowed upstairs.  We wound up dining in a booth downstairs and our server Cindy was the best part of the night - she was terrific, but the manager?  Just awful. So rude.  In the mean time the $8 chicken fingers and $5 side salad were fine. Nothing to write home about,

Absolutely just OK. Pleasant service, acceptable decor - and do NOT get the over-sauced Pad Thai.  (A dud.)  But some good things?  A very good wonton soup with light, delicate wontons and a non-greasy broth, (Winner) and decent shrimp with Grand Marnier (read: Mayonnaise) sauce and sweet candied walnuts.  Like I said - decent but not great.

Took my (now) 6 year old to a double header tonight and it was such fun. read Steven B.'s review - he has it right on!  If you have kids - minor league ball (Blue Rocks and Camden Riversharks) is a great way to get them into America's favorite pastime.).  Hy husband even caught a fly ball and gave it to our kid which was a big thrill.

Nope.  Tried again as my 13 year old loves it here and loves Poke and Sashimi in general.  Fish is just not fresh enough and the $8.95 "regular" sized bowl has so little fish anyway.  She got salmon and added avocado ($1 extra). The greens are not my favorite - I like romaine over spring mix, but most people disagree.  Anyhow, I will not return for me but if kiddo wants it, I will get it.  Unsatisfied.  Also - it was so LOUD in there I could barely hear myself think.  Get takeout.

Meh. Smells like faint cigarette smoke with artificial rose air freshener sprayed over top in the hallways (fortunately room smelled ok).  Very dark, dated looking rooms with dark brown furniture and fixture. Clean bathroom.  No major issues.  Cheap. Hard to access (on a busy divided highway) but close to Longwood Gardens, Brandywine Museum and other area attractions.  Meh.  Not horrible but not great.

The people who work here are so kind and the food is very good - the shrimp salad now has larger shrimp (YAY) but the lamb chops were over cooked.  (Mine at home are better).  Spanakopita is always a great choice. They even gave us free rice pudding for dessert.  Salads are super fresh and tasty. I am sticking with salads from now on.

World's apart from the vile, horrid Chuck E. Cheese's in South Philly. This Chuck E.'s is actually, barely, mildly tolerable.  Less crowded, more games than work, shorter lines to get food and redeem tickets for cheap plastic "prizes". Better clientele.  My 5 year old is in Heaven here.  My husband and I?  Not so much.

Just OK - we've had better and worse teppanyaki meals in the past.  My husband and I were squeezed in at 5:45 (the last seating for the "early bird" prices with 8 other local-yokels including a well behaved 5 year old.  The room was already steamin' hot from the other teppanyaki table that had 3 kids - one of whom (maybe age 2) screamed every time a fire was lit.  That sucked - because that was almost our entire meal.  Meanwhile the act is pretty typical with the onion volcano (if and when we come back our 8 year old will love it) a big pile of so-so fried rice and OVERCOOKED steaks and shrimp.  The shrimp were nearly rubbery and my "rare (I always ask for rare at a teppanyaki and it always comes out over done) steak cubes were medium to medium well.  Oh well.  It was an experience. Oh and the guy ext tome ordered a sushi meal with pale tuna and blah looking fish.  No way I'll get sushi here.  Not thrilling - but it's an option in the land of suburban chain restaurants. And kiddos LOVE the show.

Incredibly mediocre. I have never been an Uno fan - but recent visits (dragged there by my chain-loving in-laws) were surprisingly good, at the Warrington, PA location.  Today's early lunch with a co-worker was a last minute decisions and the place was nearly empty when we arrived at 11:40 AM.  Even still service was painfully slow.  We both ordered off the "super fast" (10 minutes or less) lunch menu and both ordered nearly the same thing - salads with 2 sliders. After about 13 minutes we got fidgety, and finally EVERYTHING came out at once.  Salad was on rusty lettuce (I opted for the Garden Salad as I feared the Caesar would be only romaine and croutons) with ONE tomato wedge and ONE Slice of cucumber.  Oy.  Sliders were OK but VERY salty (due to the cheddar cheese).  Would NOT order this $7.99 deal ever again. Server admitted to us she was exhausted from the night before.  Sorry, UNO, today's lunch was a fail.

They have a gorgeous Olive Bar and delicious fresh-made ravioli.  I need to compare yet to see if they are beter, worse or on par with Superior.  Service was attentive and pleassant.  Veal ravioli were 7.79 per pound.

OK, Ok!  I have been won over by LOMA - the barristas, the terrific lattes (I dream about the next one I can get - and for $3.60 I can get a medium) and now that I tried a (pricey but egg-cellent) breakfast sandwich - I am hooked.  Just about a 5 star place - but prices for food are, indeed, high.

This is the Wawa in Ambler.  I stop here for gas and often coffee or other beverages as it is on my route that I drive (over an hour) regularly.  Friendly Staff (even during COVID19 era) and great coffee.

I agree with Gourmet G.  The building is an historic place - and while the quality of the productions can vary greatly from "What was THAT?" to "Broadway Quality", I have seen many a show here under many incarnations of this great play house.

I am so pleased at how GOOD Diane's Deli really is. Classic sandwiches - breakfast and lunch items.  Huge deli-style sandwiches, chicken and tuna melts.  The decor is dated - but comfortable and clean - and the service is great.    We love it here for office-related lunches. The closest thing to a REAL deli you will find near here - and the sign simply says "DELI".

Please note that firm is now called Berner, Klaw & Watson, LLP. I am a retained client of Megan Watson who is an excellent, dilligent and results-oreinted family attorney.  She has been invaluable to me during my child custody and child support cases.  I recommend her and this firm.

Great for pedestrians - not so great for traffic flow and parked cars blocking Mount Alverno Road.  We needed this trail so I can't complain too much - but the parked cars along the road were not anticipated.  Meanwhile, on a nice sunny day - this is a great place to walk, jog, run, bike or walk your dog (Please keep your pooch leashed and pick up after them!).

Our company catered a "social" reception complete with a beer/wine (iced tea and lemonade) bar with an excellent and attentive server.  She was just great.  Out crowd of 50-60 people devoured the delectable cold sandwiches and salmon mousse and LAYERED CRAB DIP - man that crab dip was tasty stuff!  I highly recommend le Petit Chef if you need a catered event in the Radnor/Wayne/King of Prussia area.

This is the Panera closest to my work (at the moment - LOL) and as long as you go before 12 noon (like 11:50 or so) or after 1:15 PM, you're fine.  Otherwise there is a line and it's hard to find dine-in seating. Salads are good here - I especially like the "seasonal" Cobb Salad with chicken and the bistro onion soup. (I get it without croutons to save a few carbs.)  They are somewhat famous for the pick 2 combination - soup or 1/2 sandwich or smaller salad.  It's fast food - but way better for you than Burger King or McDonald's.  There is also a honeygrow (better tasting but more money) and a Qdoba in this same strip mall/shopping area.
Totally average.  Not clean, not dirty. Not good, not bad. Not tasty, not yucky.  Just  Plain MEH.

Took DD & DH to Pho Street in Springfield. She had a Summer Roll (Shrimp) and Shrimp Tempura (NOT anything like the Japanese one) and a Mamoth Mango Smoothie (drank about 1/3 of it).   I had luscious Iced Vietnamese Espresso with Condensed Milk and Bun. I loves me some Bun. Just like Mama made (not!).   So glad to see el kiddo enjoying foods from around the globe. DH had Broken Rice with Lemongrass Beef.  Fabulous food & service.

I had not been back to Erawan in years - but I remember why. It's just OK.  Better than 2 stars and not quite 3.  We went out as a group of 6 and eveyone had one of the lunch specials ($7.95 - $11.95 depending on what meat you pick.) It's a good value as you also get a small salad and a choice of app or soup.  I had the Tom Kha (my very favorite soup) and Erawan's version is good but not orgasmic.  The salad is iceberg with a few veggies and a yummy peanut dressing (standard Thai-American restaurant fare).    The entree is where things went south today. I got Masaman curry (which I love) and asked for tofu. The order came out with NO TOFU - none at all. They forgot to add it. They were sorry.  Nice man brought cubes of hot steamed (naked) tofu in a bowl and I threw it in.  Rice was over cooked to the point of tasting like congee.  Meanwhile - the staff is kind and attentive. Prices are cheap.  Food is just OK.  We need a more up-scale Thai joint in this part of the city.

Was dragged here by a rich coworker who "just loves" it here. Blargh. My $14 salad was just ok at best and they have no creamy dressings, only 1001 vinaigrettes. Yes, they are house made, but I wanted a non vinaigrette.  The lettuce mix was very cabbage-heavy.   My lunch turned out to be $22 including tax and tip and it was unsatisfactory and unsatisfying.   So upset.

This place is so cutesy - and faux-euro-feeling. I popped in for a quick take-out salade nicoise ($11) and will stop in for coffee one day soon.  I had good service - there was no line at the café at 1 PM on a Thursday.  The seating areas, however were full of people camped out there all day or for hours at a clip, so I could not have sat down even if I wanted to.  Very urban-chic bookstore. Love the book machine.

This is the FiveBucks in the lobby of the big Marriott in Center City and it. gets. busy. And crowded.  And messy at the sugar/creamer station.  And attracts a few vagrants who are quickly ushered away from tourist eyes,  Meanwhile, I NEEDED a latte and I latte I obtained.  What a rush.  Try not to come here from 7:30 - 9 AM on a weekday.  Mob Scene.

OK - I am rounding up to 5 stars.  Is this truly "as good as it gets"?  Maybe, maybe not - but service wise and considering where you ARE? (A remodeled residential duplex in LANSDALE of all places?).  The London Broil and Egplant Schwarma sandwiches are terrific. Baba Ganoush was a bit lemony for my taste, but freshly made and delicious.   Best of all?  Many dessert choices and some to TAKE HOME including pistachio Baklava and REAL birdsnests.  YUM.  Can't wait to go back. (CASH ONLY) And the owner is a lovely man!  He made us feel so welcome. Best Lebanese/Mideastern joint this side of Beirut.

I will try again - but - for now 1 star and here is why:  I walked in at about 7:30/35 PM on a Tuesday night. I wanted dinner and a quiet place to eat and take an 8 PM conference call.  Was told "sit anywhere you want" - so I did (looked at the salad bar on the way in and it looked just fine). An elderly couple was leaving and a few more older folks were finishing up their meals.  Server was seated at another table chatting with friends and promptly came over. I tolder her about my 8 PM call - she said, "Oh, we close at 8:00."  So I replied, "Well, that won't work" and walked out.  Who closes a diner at 8 PM? Don't people in the burbs eat dinner? Please consider staying open until 9 at keast.  I wonder what they do on Friday and Saturday nights??  So if you want to eat dinner here - come early. Even if I had ordered - what if I had not finished by 8?  Would she have kicked me out?  Sheesh.  I have been told this diner is very good and even better than Tom Jones (up the road) but i was forced out and guess where I wound up goin'?  Tom Jones.  I will be back and I hope I have better luck next time.

3.5 really - our kid did not like her chicken salad sandwich on croissant nor the Boylan's Diet Soda (She wanted a true Diet Coke) but we (6 adults) all enjoyed our food very much.  Outstanding French Onion Soup and lovely salads and entrees. Crabcake (either on a "snowflake" roll or addedto a salad) isvery good. BlackPepper linguine is drowning in a too-rich sauce with 3 shrimp (small poriton). Clams in Lemongrass broth were good but broth way very salty.  Too full for dessert - but we'll be back!

Wow - are they still in business?  This restaurant - right on the corner of 2 major roads, has been a landmark for decades.  The median age of the patrons (and servers) is about 60.  They offer a great choice of old fashioned home-style platters such as welsh rarebit and chicken croquettes.  It was fun to eat here as a child and even then, felt like a nostalgic throwback to another era.  I hope they are still in business, as I have not personally eaten here in many years - but I gave 3 stars in anticipation that by now they MUST need a cosmetic overhaul.  Back in "the day" we even saw fashion shows here sponsored by the Chamber of Commerce and other groups.  And we ate fattening food and iceberg based salads.  What fun!

A total dive - with decent (mediocre) greassy, fairly thick-crusted, Neapolitan-style pie. It was one of the FIRST original pizza joints from "back in the day",  Believe me - back then they were awesome - simply because the choices were so very limited.  So anyhow, I am glad they are still in business - but somehow I can't believe that they are.  A MAKEOVER is needed. Stat.

Brand-new Petco in the "Promenade at Granite Run". Very clean (new) and stocked well.  No issues.  Prices on Eukenuba are a tad higher - so I will stick with my seed-feed store.  Comparable to PetSmart but cleaner and seems better run - we'll check again in 6 months.  Keep it groomed, people!

Stick to the Chinese/Cooked dishes and you will have a better experience (in my opinion).  Mandy, the server, is just lovely and treats my elderly parents - who are dine-in regulars - like royalty.  She even knows what they usually order.  (Creatures of habit).  The "special" house wonton soup is truly delicious and the meaty spare-ribs are so much better than "that other place" in Doylestown.  I like to get the Chicken with string beans, light on the sauce (to cut the grease factor). My parents love (but I am not a big fan) the Honey Walnut shrimp. It is fried so too rich for me.  If you like fried shrimp and sweet sauces you might like this.  The dining room at lunch on weekends is always nearly empty. Take-out does a decent business.  Give Jade Island a try - it's really quite good. For Chinese.

I was thrilled to see my local Giant (in Aston, PA) carried Talluto's frozen beef ravioli and I caved and bought a dozen (1 box) for $7.99.  They were so salty (570 mg of sodium per 4 rav serving) the filling was nearly inedible.  I ate the pasta (tender yet firm and so good) but de-filled them.  Sad.

Ate here out of desparation and a lack of knowledge. Mediocre at best.  Overly salt and fat laden garbage. Hey, it's inexpensive and very filling - and many people love it here - but I just don't.  Nope.  Never again.

Very disappointed in the flavorless, dry black quinoa salad that set me back $10 for lunch.  Also had an OK $3.00 Arnold Palmer.  The quinoa salad at Pure Fare (and even the frozen Quinoa Bowls I get at Whole Foods) are far superior and cheaper.  Not a fan of this place any more. Over-priced and not that good.  I should have stuck with the green submarine (glad it's still on the menu). Skip this place and go elsewhere for a better lunch for less money.

5 stars for food but 3 for the overworked bartender - DeeAnne - who tried her best.  There were 2 huge parties on a busy Saturday lunch so we sat in a booth in the bar area instead of the sunny garden room (perfect for parties).  My dad's ribs and my pork schnitzel were just terrific.  DeeAnne is a lovely lady, too but she had to make drink orders, tend bar AND serve about 5 tables.  Just too much.  Meanwhile, if you come during a quieter time, the Plumsteadville inn is just so nice.  We love it here.  Don't miss the crab cakes.  Out of this world!

We visit the Doylestown Saladworks about every 2-3 months when my DD wants "her usual" (She's 6) - a salade nicoise with shrimp instead of tuna, extra pasta, russian dressing mixed-in.  This may not be the healthiest choice - but if i can get my kid to eat vegetables, I'll take it.  This Saladworks is nice and clean and the lettuce and veggies are MUCH fresher than the scary saladworks in Phila.  We like it here.

A good choice for a TAKE OUT (there's no where to sit really) sandwhich or some Boar's Head Cold Cuts, yougurt, cold beverages etc.  It's 1 step above a Wawa in my book.  They also sell cigarettes -especially handy if you are having a nic fit.  Glad they are around.  This area of the nabe needs all the retail help it can get.

The era of the American shopping mall is slowly grinding to a halt - with the demise of the Granite run mall and slow decline of Concord and Springfield Malls (Concord has many empty stores.)  The good part?  Plenty of parking - and at lunch there is a Chick Fil-A and a grub burger bar (have not tried), a Sbarro, Auntie Anne's Pretzels and more.  There is also a Bath & Body works and a Victoria's Secret for when I need one nearby.  Glad it's here but I bet in 10 years it won't be.

This place gets 5 store for the nostalgia factor - although in reality it's a 3 or 4 star operation.  What I remember most are those big - and I mean HUGE - ginormous-honkin'  ice cream cones.  The ice cream tastes so creamy and rich because it's made from milk produced right on the farm.  I hope they can stay around for 50 more years.  AMerica is losing the family farms like these and it's a real shame.    SUPPORT YOUR LOCAL FARMS and FARM MARKETS!!!

I don't really like or claim to "know" BBQ - but for a chain restaurant this place is good enuf for me.  I usually get the lunch size BBQ chicken.  The cornbread/muffins are like cupcakes - so sweet and good.  The spicey green beans are too hot for me - and the beans are mushy.  I do like the  place for my 3 year old - there is alot of "flair" all over the walls - camping, hunting and fishing.  The bathrooms are labelled setters and pointers.  (Bah-duhm-bump...)  It's very, very inexpensive and makes for a good gift-card gift.  I gave Famous Dave's gift cards to my cleaning lady and babysitter last Xmas and they loved that!  They also served 4 or 5 kinds of BBQ sauce.  The original is my fave - and the sweet one is also nice - but it is quite sugary.  Try it once - but this is not a pit-masters haven.  It is a TGI Fridays with a BBQ theme.

I'm sorry but I hate shopping at this Acme, and Acme in general. This branch is near the old Granite Run Mall - now a construction site for a new shopping center.  While I am happy to see that Acme employs disabled people, the check out lines are painfully, painfully slow.  Freindly, but slow.  Selection is average. Cleanliness just average.  Not my go to.

Disappointed with our last 2 visits.  We have come to the Doylestown Saladworks for about a decade - maybe longer - and since Covid hit it is just not great.  Prices are up to around $10.49 - $10.99 for a salad.  Last time - no pasta and NO ROMAINE.  Only crappy iceburg that was turning brown.  Oh - and some other ingredient we like was out too, I forget what. Oh - and no more shrimp.    Very disappointed.  Please step up your game, Saladworks.

Gotta give it 5 stars (even though it's really more like a 4) 'cuz D-town is my HOME town, y'all.  This Museum was built in the ORIGINAL Doylestown Prison - in fact up until the early "80's - you could see inmates playing B-Ball in the yard if you peered into it from the top floor of the nearby Mercer Museum.

We have eaten many meals here - including Brunch and "special occaision" meals.  I also stayed at the B & B in the late '90's - and it was fine back then - not sure how it is these days.  The restaurant offers classic American fare and decent prices.  It screams "Mother's Day" to me - and we often do go here for that day.  Nice appetizers, as DJ M. has said - and a friendly bartender.  Years ago they had a pianist on Friday (and/or) Saturday at dinner.

After reading these reviews before my stay (I could not change locations due to an event I was attending at the Crowne Plaza) I prepared for the worst.  It was not nearly as awful as I feared BUT  (there is a big butt!)... While the room was clean-ish (I brought my own pillow and case) and did not skeeve me out too badly, the communal restroom on the lobby level is awful.  The entire foyer of the "Grand" ballroom (it ain't so grand) smelled like sewage.  When we complained a commercial grade air-freshener was sprayed make it smell like...  Sewage and Air Freshener.  I was astounded at the number of high school proms, weddings and corporate events that are held here.  The place is truly bad. No way I would book my own event here.  And no WAY I would get married here.
Yum Yum is a real donut shop.  Good coffee, cheap prices, greasy fresh donuts.  Been there for YEARS.  Love it!

Always crowded and definitely not my favorite place to shop but when I am in this area, this is where we go for all the essentials.  Opens at 7 AM - and if you go around 7:15 on a week day (Tuesday - Friday) it is less crowded.  I have never used the full services areas like the deli nor the seafood counter - I just grab dairy, produce and shelf stable items and go.  Mid-priced - decent sales.  The worse part? Crowded. Lines for checking out and crowded aisles.

Absolutely top notch food - with the freshest and finest ingredients, plated and sublimely served by an attentive waitstaff in an ornately decorated "old school" formal dining room.  Anniversary? Bridal Shower? Special Occaision? Planning to propose? Chistmas Feast? Easter Brunch?  Do. It. Big. Do. It. Here.
The Plumsteadville Inn is open and even has rooms available once again. A good choice for lunch or dinner - with good salads (Caesar topped with steak i
I was just informed by a FB friend that Plumsteadville Inn closed in December 2009.  What a shame.

Got a cheapie ($6.00 - and a $2.00 tip) polish change here yesterday by "Jenny".    It was quick and easy - which was what I needed.  Not a place I would ever consider going to for a pedicure.  (They have 2 pedi-chairs crammed against the back wall.  But for a Philly nail salon this was typical.  Not too clean, but not filthy. A mani is $10, Pedi is $20 - get both for $25.  Just OK.   They carry Limited OPI, Essie and "VS" an off brand.  They used industry grade, cheap base & top coats.  You can have the good stuff on request - but they will charge $1.00 extra.  You get what you pay for, ladies.  They also offer brow waxing.

I am gonna be generous and give them 4 stars as they cater 9and in a timely manner, I might add) many of our office functions.  The pizza is 3 star but the salads are chock full of goodies (eggs, olives, tomatoes, cucumbers, etc.)  They also served a unique hot sandwich platter at one of our meetings.  Very nice change from pizza.

As salad works go (they are a local chain of custom-tossed salad and panini shops) this Doylestown location of Saladworks (near the K-Mart) really isn't bad.  My little one & I order the same salad every time - and she loves it.   It's about $9.00 after tax but is way big enough for an adult anbd a child to share.  As with all the saladworks, they also have sandwiches (panini) but I don't care for them.  At least at the D-town store the lettuce is usually fresh and crisp (and NOT brown) and the ingredients are in good, cold, condition.  The high school gals (and a few guys) who work here are well mannered and friendly.  NOT like the crappy ones in Center City.  I am happy that Saladworks exist as I do not eat traditional fast food like burgers or subs.  Home of the $8.00 salad (or $9.00 for the one we get).  Do you want white or wheat (roll) with that?

OK, my husband (back then fiance) and I went here ONCE about 3-4 years ago and i will try to remember what I can.  I know that I loved it and he hated it, so I am splitting the difference at 3 stars.  (I'd probably give it a 4 for the Chicken Francese entree I had, and for chatting with the chefs in the semi-open kitchen.)  Service was good, but DH did not like his pizza (margarita) at all.  Too thin, too burnt tasting, too expensive.  he went on and on.  Meanwhile, i had a great time and (being fresh outta Manhattan at the time) thought the prices seemed pretty "normal".  I would like to go back and try this place again.

I have studied Pilates for a long time - but recently (January 2008) started working with Jeff Prall, who is a great Pilates instructor.  He works out of a spacious studio on 13th & Locust.  The studio is owned by Karen Carlson - also a great instructor.  The studio has nice equipment - 3 reformers, 2 cadillacs, 2 chairs (No towers - they use the low cadillac as a tower) and 4 elevated mats for mat work.  There is a men's room and a ladies room for changing.  There is also a lady who practices the Alexander Technique onsite.  Jeff is a great trainer and I enjoy working with him.

This is the Dry Cleaners in the gateway Shopping Center (on the far end - around the corner from Staples).  I needed 2 items cleaned and they were done well before i needed them.  Prices are exactly the same as 2 or 3 other cleaners in the area.  Cheerful service.  No issues.  Will use the again when I need to.

I had not been to Oyster house in years and we were thrilled at the top-tier service and delicious food our work-group of 7 received.  Everything from booking our reservation (Only for large parties), to requesting separate checks for each of the 7 diners (so convenient) to attentive and friendly service from Joey.  Shout out to Joey - he was "workin' it" and was just amazing.  The ladies at the hostess desk were terrific too. And the "shuckers" at the raw bar were shucking at top speed.  Food was swimmingly fresh - I had the pan-sauteed flounder with delectable lemon-butter green beans that were perfectly crisp yet tender. Our group enjoyed a plethora of raw-bar apps, soups (Chowdah) and lunch entrees and everything was out of this world.  My only wish?  That you could sub something for fries with the lobster roll. (I am a low-carber and can't have the roll or the fries.)  I would have LOVED to have some lobster.  One person ordered the lobster roll and it looked soooooo good.  It get's super, super crowded and noisy in here so be forewarned - but Oyster House is still doing a brisk and healthy business years later.  Wonderful!

Bad. Bad. Bad.  In fact, I have been to (another) Champps before - and I knew it would likely be bad - but a co-worker wanted to come here so I reluctantly agreed.  We were "greeted" (sighed at) by 2 very surly hostesses.  The place was nearly empty at 4:50 PM on a Wednesday night.   One of the hostesses led us to a "high top" in the noisy bar area (Noisy from TV's blaring - very few customers).  We asked to be moved to a "regular" table in the dining area and she shot us a dirty look and then led us over there.  Horrible service by the hostesses.  Meanwhile, our "jolly" male server was quite good.  We ordered lunch portions (even at dinner time!) of the cobb salad and iced teas.  Salads were fresh but "blah".  Not great and not bad - but very low on the protein (Chicken, Shrimp or Salmon).  I upgraded to shrimp for $2 and got about 5 medium sized shrimp.  I wished there were more.  The lunch portion is, indeed, small.  I left hungry, unsatisfied and felt the entire place could use a good cleaning (Carpets are grungy, bathroom was filthy and toilets do not flush properly.)  The teenagers running the place do. not. care.  Uninspired.  Uninspiring.  Avoid.

My 8 year old avid crafter loves Michael's, AC Moore and JoAnnes Fabrics - and we visit various locations of each.  This one has Deplorable service.  (Average for cleanliness and variety/price of items - but Non-existent service).  The manager had no idea what "washi tape" (crafting/scrapbooking tape even was and said that they did not carry any "colorful" tape for scrapbooking - only clear tape - but she said we could "try in aisle 3 A" - so we did and there was a HUGE display of tons of the stuff - so we snapped up a few rolls.  Odd, odd, odd place.  But they're near our home - so w'll be back.

This is our go-to Saladworks - and is far better (fresher veggies and lettuce, cleaner dining and restrooms than Philly locations or mall locations.  The staff is friendly and the prices ar $7.99 - $8.49 for salads (plus more if you add extras.)  My 7 year old loves saladworks - and if it gets her to eat more veggies - I am all for it.  (granted she loves her salad to have pasta in it - but she does eat veggies, also.)

While some of the good food is quite good, there are too many things that went wrong for me to rate this higher than 2 or 3 stars.  Service needs work. Stat! We were one of 2 parties dining at 5 pm on an empty Monday night and had problems getting a fork, getting water, getting anything.  I literally had to get up and find somebody. Twice. No bueno!  Also our original table had not one but at least 3 tiny flies buzzing about. So we asked to moved tables, the flies followed.  Not pleasant.  The good itself was hit or miss. Simple dry-fried string beans were tasty. Cabbage in a pumpkin soupy sauce was not.  Shrimp fried rice was very basic, not orgasmic, but good.  The pork belly bun appetizer is worth a try.  Buns are fresh and the pork belly was delectable.   Contains peanuts so beware, my allergic diners!  I would come back, but I am in no rush to do so, which is a shame because the decor is lovely and everything on the menu sounds better than it is.

So glad to have FINALLY gotten to go here and meet and chat with "Mom" who has run this "dead-head" institution for over 33 years.  She also has 2 great cats who manage the shop.  So many great gift ideas for music lovers and bead aficionados. Classes, workshops, music and guests.  Wonderful!

Fantastic food and good service from Kate I the Chandelier room on a busy Saturday lunch.  Our party of 3 feasted on decadent chicken pot pie, fall-off-the-bone BBQ ribs and a classic Wedge salad. Best of all? Added a crabcake to the Wedge salad and it, quite honestly, was one of the best all-crab, no-filler crab cakes that I have ever eaten. Seriously.  That good.   I can't wait to have another! $9 a pop but so worth it. My dad pronounced it the "best crabcake outside of Maryland".  Lovely food. Such a treat.

Horrible service, filthy bathrooms, mediocre food and just not worth it in any way.  Perhaps I should give them 1 star but the side order of brussels sprouts was good.  That ladies room was so nasty - they floors were awful and 2 toilets were clogged.  Yick.  I have lost my appetitie.

Okura catered the sushi bar at my husband's party at Hotel DuPont. Nigiri were super fresh and included yellowtail, salmon, tuna and shrimp (all equally delicious).  Maki cut to order included basics like Cali Roll and Salmon/Avo as well as Spider (Softshell Crab) and Shrimp Tempura rolls with fresh veggies.  Wasabi and Ginger were artfully displayed like flowers.  I could have skipped dinner altogether (but it was also divine) and blissfully grazed for hours (6:30 - 9 PM) on Okura Sushi.  They cater!  Have them cater your next party.  Special!

Went to DuRoss & Langel again last night as a special shopping-spree trip for my 5 year old daughter who literally RUNS into the tub whenever we use a D&L Bath Bomb.  Steve, you have saved bathtime for us!  Tub-time has never been more fun that when you have a Koi-Toy ($12) ducky soaps ($5 each - we got 4 of 'em) Bath Bombs ($8) and fizzies ($2.5 each -we got a bunch - my fave it the pomegranate one).  Oh, and you gotta buy a Koi-Toy (a light-up plastic koi that changes colors and swims all around the tub).  Such fun!  Lots of fun home-made (on premises - Steve was pouring soy candles that very day) bath & body products.  I LOVE THIS PLACE!  (Who wouldn't?)  Steve - you have RESCUED bath time for us!

This is a brand-new Royal Farms right on 452 in Aston (South Aston?). My kid loves the fried chicken - though we are both not keen on their fries - which are BIG slabs of skin-on spuds.  Just not our thing.  But for gas, Chicken and Krispy Kreme? (Must get them in the AM or they get stale super fast.) Here's your spot.

It's still bad.  Service is so slow. Prices are better at Giant. Better meats at Acme though - but the produce is pricey and "meh".  I shop at Giant in Aston, Trader Joe's, Whole Paycheck and Gentile's for Produce.  Acme is a last resort and everytime I shop here it's out of desparation (Acme is the closest grocery store to my house.)  That said, when my kid was little they let her girl scout troop sell cookies here and Giant wouldn't.  They employ great people with diabilities but my inner-Manhattanite can't handle the slow, slow pace.  Not a fan of Acme.

We have eaten here twice - and the first time was a 4 or 5 star experience - that Brian roll is AMAZING.  But...  There's always a big but...  The second time we went - a busy Saturday night - the fish was just not fresh.  It was kinda icky, actually.  The restroom also was dirty and gross.  We will not return.  What a shame.

Hoorah and Huzzah - at long last REAL juice (not smoothies from WAWA) - a high-tech OJ machine, Mom-Pops.  (Try Red, White and Blueberry or Pineapple Chipotle)  Veggie Juice.  Brand spankin' new and clean.  Fresh Wheatgrass Ginger Lime Shots And quite possibly the world's best fresh made low-sugar lemonades.  (Pure Fare around the corner also has good juices, but Yellow is a much, much appreciated addition.)  I wish you much success and you will be seeing alot of me. I LOVE IT HERE SO MUCH!

Back again for a wonderful $11.50 Honey Fried Chicken Tossed Salad lunch with that exquisite buttermilk dressing.  LOVE it!  Service is always great - and the Fish of the Day was Trout served with a delicious roasted asparagus and quinoa salad.  Kudos to Wendy, Jackie and the wonderful team at Day by Day. We love it!

Very friendlies service but my chicken gyro was woefully dry.  Pit was not "fluffy" either - kinda stale-ish tasting.   If there is a next time, I will try a "regular" gyro or a tuna melt.  Running out of options for lunch around here. They serve breakfast here and I may try that.  Inexpensive - $6.75 (or $6.95 as a lunch special with fries.)  Update:  My office got 3 pizzas from Mystic (Mistic) for a company lunch - 2 plain and 1 pepperoni and they were quite good, actually.  Maybe Pizza is what I should stick to here?

I think I am too old to even be allowed entry to H & M.   This is the epitome of disposable fashion.  Cheaply made, inexpensive clothes for YOUNG, thin gals who need to change outfits often. My fat size 8 (or 10 on a bad day) is a rarity here.  So if you are a stick you may have better luck.  Good for club gear - not so good for my corporate America lifestyle.  The shoes are truly awful  (Felt flats??  eew.)
Nice green space - a welcome respite within the City of Brotherly Love.  Especially nice during the late spring.

The male manager who has been there for the past 2 years or so is very helpful. I recently tried and love the smooth infusion conditioner.  I also (still) am hooked on the Green Science skin care line - even though it is IMO obscenely expensive.  Decent products - some are great others suck - be choosy and you just might find a few keepers at Aveda.

4 stars for the fabulous service by Shaun 2 stars for the mediocre food that may have made my 9 year old sick.  We stopped in - famished - and wear from a long day, at about 9 PM on a Thursday night.  The place was nearly empty so we got bright, cheerful service from Shaun - who is a lovely lady.  She even decorated my kids hot cocoa with whipped cream.  The restroom appeared clean but smelled horribly of old urine (Eew.). Normally this would be enough to give a place 1 or 2 stars - but Shaun's service is carrying my 3 star overall rating.  Stick to coffee and breakfast foods and you'll be OK. Skip the greasy chicken strips (kids menu - a steal at $2.99 - but not if they make you sick), and also skip the pasta dishes.  (Overuse of dried oregano.)  My husband had a grilled chicken sandwhich which looked very good.  If you ever read my other reviews, you may already know that I am not a fan of chain restaurants - but in a pinch this Bob Eveans will do.  And hopefully Shaun won't be there long - she's studying nursing and is well suited for a care giving profession.  She's terrific!

Ook. Went here about 3 years ago for a "Happy Hour" sponsored by the Temple Law Association.  This place was on par with Public House aka "the Pube".  Icky.  Bad crowd, watery drinks, mediocre bar snacks and a sort of a "I miss being a frat boy" vibe.  Not goin' back.  Nope.

No issues here - except the restroom which was in need of service. Theatre itself was clean and comfortable and no lines.  The one in Glen Mills is still nicer but this beats the crappy AMC Granite Run.  (But that one is soooo cheap with $3.99 matinees.)  AMC has taken over the county.  Food is was over priced and sucky.  We skip it.
A National (International) art treasure right in my own front yard. Love it!

As many in the yelp community know, I am not a big fan of Charbucks (aka fourbucks) BUT- and this location deserved the big but... considering that this shopping area (near the Target on City Ave.) is the only walkable place near my new office, I come here for an occaisional Ice Green Tea Lemonade.  This Starbucks is clean and (aside from morning rush) not crowded.  A pleasant surprise.  My goodness - I may start (gasp) liking Starbucks again.

With all the great international cuisine in Philly, I almost never consider Chinese (my first love from Childhood) anymore, but when I am sick I NEED soup.  Wonton, Subgum Wponton or Hot & Sour.  Well, Square on Square came through for us last night.  Delivery took about 40 minutes on a BUSY, Rainy Friday night - which isn't horrible considering those conditions.  My husband enjoyed his sweet-yet-spicy General Tso's (The call it something else) Chicken.  I ordered a Quart of THE BEST HOT 'n SOUR (For real.  I love their version.  Chicken and tofu and just enough black pepper, red pepper and vinegar).  I also got a quart of the "special" wonton soup which had a tasty broth and was loaded with chicken, pork, bok coy and mushrooms.  My only complaint?  Only 4 of the DELICIOUS, petit wontons in one quart.  Next time I'll ask for extra wontons - and gladly pay for them, too.    I ate a small bit of each soup and had plenty left for the next day.  You saved me, Square on Square.  Those soups are the BEST.

My father in law pretty much LIVES at grocery stores.  He's use $1.50 worth of gas to go to a store to save 50 cents on a dozen eggs.  You get the idea...  But we all can agree on Wegman's.  It is a pleasure to shop here and the selection is great.  If you are a comparisson shopper (and in our family - you are!), you can also nab some good bargains here.  We got some terrific imported cheeses and yummy prepared foods here and made a gourmet picnic for a fraction of the cost of having it catered.  Wegman's also does a fairly good job of appetizing/catering of their own - but we prefer to just buy the componenets and assemble them ourselves on trays.  Wegman's is great.  Wish there was one in Center City Philly!

I respectfully disagree with Ellen R.  Penzey's herbs are fresher and in many cases more reasonable than the Spice terminal at Reading Terminal Market - and both have a loved place in my heart.  As a dedicated Penzey's catalog shopper - I have to say that I just LOVE Penzey's.  With the exception of the California Basil and crystallized ginger - that I can find better elsewhere.

The BEST Chinese around - and its not even in Chinatown. We got delivery today - a day-after-the-snowstorm order takeout kinda day.  A QUART of the fabulous hot & sour soup always cures what ails me. Delicious chicken & snow peas. Pan fried dumplings are average - not mind blowing.  Service was friendly on the phone and lightening fast (They showed up in 17 minutes!)

Yes, it is pricey here - as in $13 - $15 for tricked-out burgers and sandwiches. The best deal going - if you happen to like the day's picks - are the pick 3 which is a boring salad, a soup and a 1/2 a sandwich or wrap.  Today's picks happened to be great - a turkey club wrap with Turkey bacon and the soups (both sounded awesome) were tomato veggie or butternut squash.  I had the butternut squash soup and the salad and took the wrap HOME. Two lunches in one for $12!  Plenty!  Good service and we sat outside as the weather was just perfect. Got here at 11:50 AM just before the rush. Do not come here at 12:10 or 12:15 PM.  Come early or late for better service.

OMG - so overpriced for what it is. I just had the $14 triple - an open-faced grilled cheese, French onion soup and a small salad, plus an iced tea.  My friend had an $18 burger and a beer.  Lunch was $52 after tax & tip.  Very nice food - but not THAT nice. Sheesh.

Best fresh juices (veggie, fruit, smoothies, banana twirl and now SALADS) in the city. Love it here.  Fresh Lemonade - some of the best ever. Delicious Fresh Wheatgrass shots  I love it so much and hope they prosper for years!

I strongly disagree with Veruca - this is "Mall Chinese" and just OK. My 9 year old loves the orange chicken and teriyaki (sweet) chicken so if we are in the Mall and she is hungry I will indulge her.  I don't eat here.  Ick.  The good part?  The lady behind the counter is very kind.

Oh boy.  Where do I start? Lots of things have changed at Fork.  Some for the better - but most are not.  Before I dive in - let me just say - or scream - this:  NOT GOOD FOR KIDS!!!!  Our fussy party of 4 included my not-so-fussy 8 year old - who has dined at many Philadelphia spots.  Before we went I saw "Crispy Chicken Nuggets" on the "Bites" menu - so I knew that was what we would get for her.  BOMB!  Dark meat chicken chunks in very pale (nearly white) tempura batter made the young lady frown almost instantly.  So we asked if the "Spaghetti al chitarra" (Homemade spaghetti with butter, scallions and crab) could be made as just spaghetti with butter?  What a fuss ensued - and after negotiations, yes - they brought her a small plate of home-made spaghetti DROWNED in butter.  And tried to charge $18 for it (which is the normal price when it comes with crabmeat.).  So disappointed.  OK - so "kids meal fiasco" aside - how were the grown-up dishes? Not bad.  Salads were the stand out - my kale salad was terrific (Matyson's is better - as Fork's is a bit too vinegary in my opinion), and my friends split the "Roots" - a unique preparation of seasonal root veggies.  Appetizer pastas were SMALL and $15 - $16 each.  Yikes.  Our server is a great guy - and I just knew I had seen him before! But the whole "not sure if we can make pasta with butter" thing just sat with me very poorly.  Even Ellen herself (the owner) cam out to chat with us - and I pretty much told her all of this.  I don't think it will matter one bit in the long run. 4 star food and 2 star (maybe even 1 star) service.  I won't be back. And there is no way I will deign to bring a kid in here.  (They made it very clear she was not welcome.

While I agree this is THE practice to take your kids (what choices do we have) our doctor, Cynthia Hill, has always been wonderful - once we actually get to see her.  The office is not well run.  Lots of waiting - not only for appointments, but also to get paperwork (forms cost $10 ) filled out and also waiting to PAY your copay.  Meanwhile, our 4 year old has gotten excellent care and I have received good ad vice from Dr. Hill and Advocare/Society Hill Pediatrics.

A lady at my office used to call this place $h1tty Gardens and the name stuck.  I just have never had a great meal here.  Usually we've had take-out (they deliver) and I ate in the restaurant (which was loud, crowded and cefeteria like) one time.  NEVER will I return.  If you want GOOD cheap CHinese - go to A Mandarin Restaurant or Square on Square.  The dumplings were thick and doughy with greasy meat inside.  (Blech).  The Chicken & Brocolli was OK - not bad, actually.  The fried rice just seems old and over-soyed to me.  Not a fan.

Just wanted you all to know that we ordered 2 dozen macaroons (Phenomenal) and 3 pies (Pumpin, Apple Crumb and a heavenly chocolate cream) for thanksgiving.  They are sooooooo delicious we will never bake again!  Seriously - try Hotel DuPont for your holiday baked goods - WOW!

This was our long-time home-town wawa, somplete with smokes, drinks and snacks.  The parking lot can get crowded so be careful pulling in & out.  Over the years Wawa has really expanded it's brand and reach.  This wawa was pretty much the first one I ever was in.

I had passed by La Pina (on Route 202 - on a divided part of the highway where the Firebird's is) but never got a chance to try it (It opened in February 2018) until today with a group of 5 ladies (all from work).  Our server Luckee was accommodating and wonderful.  She split our check and even split the cost of the $11 table-side guac - which Luckee herself whipped up for us in a huge stone molcajete.  I was overall very impressed with the menu, decor and service.  The tuna ceviche was excellent and the house salad (I know, what could possibly be so great?) was Amazing - with jicama, heirloom tomatoes and avocado.  A small sprinkle of cotija cheese, too.  Very, very fresh tasting food.  Can't wait to return for the $5 Happy Hour (Monday - Friday 5 - 7 PM.)

2 star food but surprisingly 4 star service - we sat at a table in the bar area. 11.95 for an Italian Hoagie?  Really?  I had a classic wedge salad which was fine but I asked to top it with a grilled salmon filet ($8.95 additional) and it was bone dry and flavorless.  Blargh.  The good news?  Super close to where I am working and quick service at lunch time. Have a drink but eat elsewhere.

Alas, the pop shop may be fizzling.  I would love to be able to give this place a 4 or 5 star - as it is just so preciously cute and the food is great, but the decibel level and service leave much to be desired.  Three of us, including my 4 year old, had lunch here today and the place was jammed.  The servers were so over worked, they just couldn't handle it.  For now the frenetic pace has made me too pooped to pop.  And the noise level was deafening.  That said, DD enjoyed her "Captain Underpants" sundae (basically a cone-clown a la Friendly's) and my vegetarian friend (a different one) had a seitan cheesesteak.  I had a VAT of Cobb salad - so huge it was not finishable.  There were about 4 chopped whole eggs in it.  We took it home.  I would like to come back here again when it is NOT busy (is that ever??).  I bet it'd get higher marks.

Our company ordered bulk take out for about a dozen people and everything was accurate and fairly good food.  About $15 per person.  The caprese salad was just fair as the (Roma) tomatoes were squishy. The fresh Mozzarella really was fresh and delicious as were the added (4.99) grilled shrimp.  Greens were gritty.  Not fun.  Wings here are surprisingly wonderful.   Can't wait to try dine-in.  I shall return.   Thank you for providing my company with a good alternative for lunch.  If I eat one more Panera-catered lunch... blah!

Friendly staff - a few of which have been there for years, and also a few who appear to be "mentally challenged".  Kudos to Acme for that.  Meanwhile, the prices are fine (cheaper than Giant) but also they do not carry certain items like Hint Water (I have to trek to Giant or the new Whole Foods for that) and other organic goodies.  They carry Reed's Ginger Brew - but want 6.89 for a 4 pack.  Ee-gads!  Anyhow, I do shop here and will continue to do soas it is on my way home from work. But for major weekend shopping it's Giant or Whole Paycheck for me.  P.S.  Your Newman's  lemonade was nearly 3 weeks out of date in the Dairy Case.

We had a great experience here - so much so that I made my 9 year old a VIP (unlimited session fees for $50 for a year).  No, it's not cheap, but you can easily spend 90 - 120 minutes at a clip here and it's a great rainy-day activity for artistically inclined kids.  Might even be fun for a Girls Night Out party with the grown folks!  We even came back the next day (Sunday - when one adult pays the $10 session fee - up to 2 kids under 12 pain free!).  We're in!

One night a week they serve - of all things - tacos - and they are pretty darned good.  I had shrimp tacos and gelato for dessert.  This is still not my favorite place - I want to love it but I just don't.  The guitarist in the background (again only on Mondays or Tuesdays - I forget which night) is terrific.  talented guy!  Great service, nice decor - but the food is just OK. If you plan ahead you can also have a larger party here - maybe 15 - 20 tops.  Above that and they really can't accommodate you. Try to go for tacos - not Italian (how weird!!!!).

Very good sushi (better than Temaki in my opinion) and decent chinese (kinda pricey for what it is.).  I actually liked the Granite Run Mall location better for chinese (did not have sushi there.).  Specialty Rolls are expensive - $16 for the Eagle Roll - topped with chunky lobster salad.  Rainbow Roll ($12) was good, but stuffed with fake kani stick.  Good deal for lunch - higher for dinner. Full bar.  Nice!  Will be back soon.

Fantastic decor and attentive device from Chris made up for a few minor problems with the food.   Pizza are fresh tasting and there are so many varieties. The 7 inch mini is quite small, so get a salad to go with it.  Seafood salad was very good, however the beef on the land 'n sea salad was way too over cooked.  Pricey, but you are paying the rent on the swanky digs.  I enjoyed it here but next time I will modify my order.

Yes, a guy does own this place - and he treats my 5 year old DD so very well.  She has had 2 manicures (polish changes actually) here over the past year and one time "jiji" (Not sure of her name) painted cute little lady bugs on her nails.  She was tickled!!!  I have never, personally, had any nail services performed here - but we like it as a place for my daughter.  They do very nice nail art and the polish lasted on her busy little paws.

OMG - Thank the LORD I did not go to use the bathroom at LP's until AFTER we had already eaten (and enjoyed) or dinner.  To get to the bathroom you walk through the kitchen and it is so GROSS.  I could not even go in there.  The stentch of the "disinfectant" mixed with urine was too much to bear.  Before this, however I should mention that I had eaten at LP's about 3 prior times and all were fine.  The food was decent, cheap, typical diner grub.  I was even impressed that the iceberg-based tossed salad was fresh and crisp.  Nice servers, too.  But that bathroom downgraded a 3 star experience to a disgusting big fat ZERO.

It's probably only really worth 4 stars but my brother is good friends with the owner - so I gotta give 'em 5.  They treat us like mini-celebrity's whenever we see shows there.  Finally - a decent music venue inb D-town!  GO PUCK!!  P.S.  Bring money.

I don't even like hoagies and I so love Primo. We stopped by the "quant" Claymont location today for lunch where my co-worker frequents and is known by name.  The 2 ladies who man the counter at lunchtime are very nice and funny.  I got a (basic) Turkey wrap and he got a Sharp Italian wrap. I love that they offer wraps now, because the bread is very heavy and chewy - yummy - but filling.  Also - if they happent o be hot and fresh (which they were today) grab a cookie - I got white chocolate macadamia - and oh, wow!

This is a cute little comedy club and they get some funny, funny people in here to perform.  The 2 drink minimum (you can get food in lieu of drinks) kinda sucks as it forces you to spend MORE money - but hey, that's kinda how it is.  Nicely run - we had fun and will return.  It's great to laugh!

3 stars is pretty generous - it's more live 2 or 2 and a quarter. The dumplings are crispy and FRIED and the prices seem a mite high for essential fast food noodles.  The lady at the counter was icy cold toward me - and the place was essentially empty.  I would only go back here in a pinch as Bill M. has said.

We are giving Bertucci's a strong 4 star review after last nights early dinner (We arrived at 4:50 PM and by 6:30 when we left the place it was mobbed with a long line of hungry families and a brisk take-out biz.  DD who is now 6, loved her penne & cheese off the kids menu. I enjoyed the chicken marsala.  The meal was very nice (especially for a chain) and the brought out a slice of tiramisu with a candle in it for FIL's birthday.  Jonas, our server, was effifient and pleasant.  DD spent a LONG time watching the pizza guys (and gals) roll out the dough.  She loves it here - which is mostly why we come here.  VERY family friendly.

A typical diner menu with variety and reasonable prices. We went with a party of 3 including a hungry 7 year old who enjoyed her French Toast.  Service was Ok - but at the end of the meal when i handed her my debit card - after a quick glance at the check, she rang it up and returned me the slip to sign.  No tip line?  So I asked her - "Where do I put the tip?", and she says, "Oh, we do it beforehand". I had very little cash on me so I left her the $5 I had and we left.  She basically deprived herself of the full tip  (Should have been $6 or $7.)  They need to explain this before the present the check,  Just dumb.  Meanwhile if I am in the area and need a diner - I would return.

It's fast(ish) food style Mexican - and you can get a decent taco platter for $6.99 ($7.99 if you want shrimp or fish).  I opted for 1 pork & 1 carne asada.  Both were good - but the asada had lots of onion on top - next time I will know to get it on the side.  Rice, beans & chips.  Quick service, big portions, no issues.  Gets CROWDED during the weekday lunch rush.
Yes - they really do deserve 4 stars.  Great catering - fresh salad, good pizza (and stellar tomato pie) and COOKIES!!!!!  A great value for a crowd.

A beautiful building with 2 restaurants (And plenty of room to host a private event) inside and engaging architecture.  Service is friendly and warm. A nice seleciton of fine teas.  Casual yet elegant - and a decent "date place".

This homegoods is pretty disorganized - as many of them are - and we could not find anything we were looking for (magnets and guest towels).  We also came on the Saturday after Xmas so the place was crammed with bargain hunters and gift return-ers.  Will not be back so quickly.

Oooh - I am first to review this place - now I guess I better be careful lest I let out my secret and they become so crowded that you can't get in...  But wait a second - you already CAN'T GET IN on a busy weekend morning.  The Bread Crumb is what I would classify as an "elegant greasy spoon".  It's a Breakfast & Lunch place (no dinners) it's really, really cheap and has sassy yet sweet waitresses who make you feel like family.  And the breakfast basics (Pancakes, eggs, omelettes) and all really cheap, large portions, and well prepared.  It's a treat to come here.  My parents like it, too.  (And they are next door to the Larder so you can shop after you eat.)  CASH ONLY!!!

Feast Your Eyes has catered our corporate event for the last 2 years (maybe longer).  The food is always great - and there are even tasty vegetarian options.  Hot food is kept hot and cold foods and chilled.  Friendly efficient staff - our set up was a buffet so no "servers" really - but they kept it stocked.  Delicious roast chicken - i know it sounds so simple - but theres was lemony and garlicky and terrific (even with the bones in.)  The owner, Lynn, is a doll.  Love working with Feast your eyes!

Ok - I am being nice and giving 3 stars, but I really want to give them 2. Don't get me started on UO.  We have a long post collegiate, complex relationship.  When they first opened and had only a few stores and seemed so cool.  It was the height of the grunge era back then.  And hot chicks and "hip" dudes worked there.  Now it's more than a bit played out and man, they jacked up the prices.  I mostly get accessories and socks here now - the pants fall apart.  (And for 60 bux??)  Oh I miss the good old days.  It seemed better back then."

Took my little one (now 6) here for an emergency sore-throat-that -might-be-strep (it was).  And had a great experience with Dr. Cynthia Hill.  We just love her.  Points off for the long wait though.  Fortunately the on-call nurse service is EXCELLENT.  They will call you back right away if your kid ever has a medical problem.  So wonderful.

I stopped by unexpectedly while walking by "The Porch" at 30th Street station at about 9:30 AM on my way to work.  I ordered a "Cali"  (BLT with avocado and a deicious lemon/lime mayo that really added a pleasant brightness).  Menu said $4.50 but she only asked me for $3.50.  Sweet gal on the truck!  So very pleased. I can't wait to try their burgers.
This is the Starbucks right near the Whole foods and it's fine.  Gets crowded during peak hours and the staff is pleasant enough.  Smaller floorplan.

Can't say enough good things about the staff and owner of CMM. My 10 year old kid and I are both VIP members and we have now brought 2 of y kids friends here who both loved it.  Very please with the products and service.  Made an $80 Christmas Tree (ouch) - but we will have it for years.  Our latest project was a 14 tile mirror that my kid custom made and hopes to take with her to college one day.  Very therapeutic.

Salon Royal Court really is a high-end salon in a unique and goreous building.  (The owners - a couple - live on the top floor.  Nearly everything in the multi-level salon is an antique and much of it is for sale.  I come here, oddly enough, for nail services. (I have never had my hair done here - as frankly, i can't afford the prices, but a friend has her cuts and highlights done here.)  I used to see Donna for FANTASTIC spa pedicures.  (They have a regular and a spa pedicure.  The only difference is $10 and an extra mask application.)  She was great - but she left, so now I see their long-term uber-manicurist, Ginny.  She is really loud and talks alot - so if you want a quient technician - she may not be the gal for you - but from a technical perspective she knows her craft.  I am still on the quest for the perfect pedi - and Cheryl Lee (spa elysium) has that title in the bag so far.  But, I sure miss Donna.  She gave me a great pedi.  Oh - and they used to sell Kerastase here but now they carry another line. (Which is a shame because I would buy my Kerastase here.)

Parking here is a nightmare - and often there are no spaces - except for 2 resevred for the empty "We Buy Gold" store next door.  I often park in the shopping center (acme) next door) and walk across the busy street to get my four dollar latte fix.  Meanwhile - the service here once inside is actually good.  The afternoon female barista (3-5 ish PM) is terrific.  Can't remember her name.  Oh - and please clean the bathrooms more.  Blargh!

I really like Ong's.  (Just stay out of the bathroom and don't look around the kitchen area too hard.  I have had some Pho and other noodle dishes here.  Prices are reasonable and it's a GREAT place to bring my little daughter who has been here about 3 times from ages 1.5 - 4.  I also happened to stop in during the Chinese New year and the dragon parade and fire-cracker festivities stopped in.  What fun!  We enjoy it here. (And it's very affordable.)

Carversville Inn has gone through numerous chefs and menu re-vamps over the years.  It is a great, historic structure and feels so homey and comfortable (yet elegant - in a countrified way).
