It's a convenient stop after school for us.  We have bought custom-made (pricey) stockings, doy toys and several treats.  She loves the German run candy shop stand with the chocolate covered fruit.  They even had 1/2 chocolate covered apples available one day - which was great because the whole apple is ginormous and far to much for her.  We also tried a crepe from teeh crepe and waffle making lady. Nice lady - mediocre crepe.  Oh well.  Perhaps next time a waffle?  There are also musical acts playing - mostly in the evening. Such a fun place. - Oh and don't miss the Nutcracker tent (it's heated!!!) filled with ornaments and (pricey) nutcracker themed items.

Support your local Dairy.  Yes, Rosenberger's Milk costs a few cents more than the store brand - but it is so worth it.  A great family business that supports our local agriculture.  I prefer the 2% myself...

5 star service from Sally and Ronnie (a 24 year veteran server - she is amazing) and 4 or 5 star food - but the noise level was deafening - and we dined at 5:30 PM (by 6:15 the place was packed).  Elegant (albeit pricey) cocktails at the bar (I had a Strawberry Basil martini that was delicious) followed by an elegant dinner, complete with an enormous ($130) chilled seafood display that was a meal in itself.  Crab Cocktail here is a treat!  Dinners included filet mignon, ribeye (overly sauced, for my taste - but the guys liked it), lobster roll (very good but not better than Cape Cod) and crab/lobster stuffed "sachetti" pasta.  Enjoyable desserts like fried donuts, creme brulee (yum) and buttermilk ice cream (very good).  Kudos to the chef and servers.

Not a ton of variety and no sushi for lunch time but for $7, you just can't beat it.  The lunch special is a bowl with your choice of protein.  Also you can get good coffee/espresso drinks here and even  breakfast   There are more choices for dinner time, so I will need to come back then.  Lunch was a good value.

OMG - this is the real deal, Jewish (not Kosher - you can get meat and dairy here) style deli including lox, knish, blitzes, great latkes, and thinly sliced amazingly lean corned beef.  Sooooooo good.  Don't miss that Matzoh ball soup - I got mine with noodles added. The hit of dill in that broth is just like Bubbe's.  Service was great (COVID complaint), too.  Can't wait to come here again.  P.S.  I got 1/2 a lb of Nova Lox and 1/4 lb of sliced corned beef to go - the Lox was silky, fresh, thinly sliced and decadent (ACME from Brooklyn).  So. Darn Good.  I am loving this place.

3rd year in a row - and it's even better this year (name contraversy and all). REAL German merchants at a few of the booths (not all) selling chocolate covered fruit, nuts, Nutcrackers, ornaments, plush animals and everything.  And this year there is a $2 a ride carousel that my 6 year old can't get enough of.  And she got to see Santa - with way less of a line than at Macy's (aka Wanamakers).  We will be back again and again from now thru Xmas day.  LOVE IT!

Stopped at this Wawa at 10 or 11 PM on our way home from Hershey with a sleeping kid in the car.  Ran in and out.  No issues.  Snacks, drinks, smoke and coffee. Well - no smokes in front of the kiddo.  Ever.  Wawa.  There when u need them. Grateful.
Your basic, big and well-stocked Pet Smart with everything our cat (and dog) need,  We get food, toys, treats and supplements here.  No issues.

For excellent customer service and everything from wedding jewelry to watch repair, you just can't beat Carroll's Jewelers.  They've been in the D-town shopping Center for EONS and are still family owned.  Jeweler Joel Robinson will give you an honest, no bull-S$$t appraisal of your stone - whether you bought it from them or not.  I trust them.    And of course, they have just plain gorgeous jewelry from reputable lines at the best prices.  You can also count on them to tell you honestly what the prices for gold and platinum are - which can help you greatly when you shop.

A decade later and Suburban station has improved a wee bit. A few more restaurants to choose from and better lighting on the track level.  Still a bunch of creepy characters and the restroom is awful.  We need to invest in our public transportation in America. So grateful from SEPTA, AMTRAK, MTA, LIRR and the worst of the lot?  NJ Transit.  You think SEPTA is bad?  It is terrific compared to NJT.
Excellent and free - and they have a horse farm in the center.  Lovely.
Clean, large and great for walking, biking, dog walking and especially with the kids at CHRISTMAS when they have a ton of lights and lit trees.  Fun.

OMG - what have I been waiting for? This place is amazing. The 1/2 rack platter (2 sides and 2 slices of white bread) is $16 and huge. Can't wait to try the brisket and chicken.  Go early - they do sell out.  My office-mates adore the burnt ends.  (They sell out quicker). Terrific!!!

Fantastic!  I love and support REAL Butchers whenever possible as they are a dying breed and we NEED them.  Steaks?  (T-Bones for 9.99 per lb, Ribeyes for 13.99 perlb) Chicken?  Lamb?  Veal?  Sausages?  Even Dog Food (scraps??)!  Love this place and can't wait to become more of a regular.

Wow! Blown away by the quality, variety and freshness of my sashimi lunch special at Qu.  $14 plus tax and tip was money well spent, and served by the delightful Miss Yvonne.   This place is brand-new, so new that the liquor license isn't even here yet (Gotta love those PA "blue laws")!  Nevermind, this place is gonna catch on fast.  I only hope that they maintain this level of opening-month quality. Everyone is clearly on their best behavior.  Keep it up, guys! I'll be back and I'll be watching.

Even though I am NOT a cheese steak lover (I rarley eat them - maybe 1-2 times a year), and I like Jim's better than Pat's, I prefer Pat's to Geno's.  I am also friends with a member of the Olivieri family - so I have to like Pat's better,  I order (quickly) a chicken cheessteak 'wit provolone and 'shrooms.  Too bad it's always so packed there's nowhere to eat. What a greasy mess!

Stopped in with my almost 8 year old and my MIL for flower cutting ($6 per 1/2 pound - our bunch was about $4.00) and blackberry picking.  (The berries were not quite ready that week - wait ONE more week.)  Cider donuts and NEW Cider Ice are a tasty treat.  Such a great place!  (Closed Mon, Tues, Wed).  Love it.
Delectable donuts holes - laden with sugar and oil.  Caloric BOMBS of goodness (or badness). So melt-in-your-mouth crack-dictive.

Food is great - margaritas (at least the $2.99 house special Lime Marg on Wednesdays ) are awful.  Great nopalitas salad (Marinated cactus leaves) - fresh veggies and a light dressing. Shrimp Ceviche was HUGE and tasty.  Serive at the beginning was great - but the server messed something up with my dining pal's credit card and we waited, and waited, and waited to pay our bill.  Nevertheless, we'll be back.  Muy delicioso!

Got some rare (springtime only) petit baby turnips today.  You can eat them raw or lightly steamed.  Delicious - slightly radishy - and highly nutritious.  Also locally grown straberries that are actually red all the way thru.  And heavenly japanese eggplant and pure, clean Belgian Endive.  I am in heaven in this cramped, tiny, NYC-style market.

I passed by this place in Suburban Station on my way to work so I tried the breakfast scrambler (no tots) and for $4 (and change) it was fine - nothing orgasmic - but the bacon was nice and crispy.  Not enough tomato, even though I asked for extra tomato in lieu of the tots.  Would not rush back here.  Service was medium (not fast, not slow - a few minutes to make it fresh - do not come if you are rushing).  Guy behind the counter was very nice.

I just have to review Doug's Place. Doug has been cutting my brother's hair since he was 5 years old - and he's over 30 now.  His home-like setting in Doylestown is a great place. I hope he never retires.
My 9 year old has come here about once a year since the age of 3 and takes a cute picture next to the Rocky Statue.  A fun yet touristy stop.

This place is carverous and huge.  That said they had a limited amount of cashiers at the main entrance so be prepared, there may be aline if you dd not pre-purchase your tickets.  Theater itself (we were in Theatre 3) was actually clean and comfortable and a bit on the smaller side.  Loud audio and reclining chairs.  No issues.

I have nicknamed Walmart, "Wal-nuts" because the people who shop there are truly on the brink of insanity.  Shopping only based on price.  Yes, it's cheap - but also chaotic, crowded (the check out experience is not pleasant) and for a few bucks more, I'd rather go elsewhere.  That said, Walnuts has saved my a$$ on numerous occasions when I needed groceries (This one is a a SUPER-Walnuts - with groceries, dairy and produce) or household supplies.  Yup - it's cheap.  Be patient.  This ain't no party. This ain't no disco This ain't no foolin' around...

Still going strong and now it is bigger and bigger and blends in with the other Christmas Market across the street.  Lots to see and browsing around was fun (and cold) but there was nothing I felt compelled to purchase.  A big plus - the heated tent where you can thaw out with a glass of wine or cup of (mediocre) coffee.  Very loud and crowded in there on a Thursday before Xmas.

This is a BIG, clean, super Wawa - with a gas station and tons of convenience food items, smokes, cold drinks, magazines, a deli counter with touch-screen sandwich ordering and lots of things now common to most Wawas.  It's convenient for the guys at the office, so we come here often. I usually get a Jr. or Shorti Hoagie.  Whoop-dee-doo!

It's fun to poke around a REAL bookstore (not Barnes & Noble or Boring's ahem - I mean, Border's).  The people here are very nice - family owned and run - and they can recommend a great book or 3.  It's tight and cramped - but if you are here without your kids and NOT in the tourist-packed summer or Xmas season, It's a great place to just meander around and read.  And they have a cat!

We love you, Doug - my father has gotten his hair cut here for over 40 years and my "little" brother who is now all grown up went here throughout his younger days.  We love you Doug.  Please, please, please don't retire.  The Flams.

A great source for nuts, candies, spices, teas and roasted coffees.  A fantastic find in Ardmore.  Walnuts, pecans, macadamia, almonds, all types of flavored/shelled pistachios.   So great.  Um, but not if you have a nut allergy.   Love.
Fantastic - chock full of free events. Just wish the restrooms were open and accessible during non-event days.

Hit or miss - but when you hit, you can hit BIG.  As in designer boots for $18 big.  Or Like-new catalog clothing for $7 big.  Come prepared to slowly route through racks and racks of "no"to find the good stuff. And - drop off your lightly-worn goodies for CASH here too!
Gorgeous park - and a horse farm with pony rides in the middle. Riding trails, hiking, biking, nature.  Paved pathways, a few benches.  Great for the entire family.
Awful excuse for a strip mall. Run-down K mart and a few struggling stores.  YUCK.

It OK.  A welcome D-town neighborhood edition - and on Spring and Summer weekend mornings, the joint is jumpin'!  They offer bagels in a variety of flavors and a selection of cream cheeses and spreads.    Your basic bagel type fare.  Good - but not mind-blowing.

I have had one massage and one chiropractice adjustment here. The massage was fine.  I did not like the adjustment at all.  The Dr. was totally different than the woman I used to see in New York.  I wll not likely return.  They also offerr yoga classes - which sounds intriguing.

I was dragged here yet again, and the food and service were decidedly sucky.  (Sorry "Amanda" - sweet yet clueless high-school aged server).  Mistake 1.  (Our bad) Come on a Saturday night at 6:30 Mistake 2.  Patiently wait for table with5 year old Mistake 3. Ask for "a few minutes" when said server asks "Ready to order?"  My kid nearly had a melt down while waiting for her $3.99 Kraft Mac 'n Cheese and my $9.99 burger - asked for medium- was charred and tasteless.  Yick.  Hope my inlaws enjoyed the teeny tiny overly salted steaks. If it were not for their generosity, I would never, ever come here.  (They paid, they picked. And, yes, I am grateful to them - but please - there are so many better places to go.)

DH & DD, a friend and I were trapped in the convention center during a freezing cold Flower Show and since Hard Rock was packed (35 minute wait) we snagged a table at the Field-Hole.    Lunch was unsurprisingly unremarkable. My Cobb Salad (regularly $14 with chicken) was jacked up to $20 when I asked to sub steak.  4 oz maybe of just OK steak.  5 cherry tomatoes cut in half, a few chunks of avocado and some over-cooked bacon chunks/chips.  I have had better and worse Cobbs.  The best part?  Our server Dana was an over-worked sweetheart.  She did her very best in a dining room packed with kids and families weary from the Flower Show.  Prices are a bit too high for the sub-par "formula" bar food that is served.

No Bueno. My father's crab cake platter (which sounded great on the menu - served with a mushroom risotto and asparagus) was nearly all filler.  Yes, this is a diner - but he was sorely disappointed.  Won't be back.

Lotus is cost prohibitive for my family - but it is also another example of "you get what you pay for" in that the quality of ingredients and execution of preparation is spot-on!  (Especially in Summer and fall when the harvest locally is in abundance).  If someone else is paying?  I am all-in.  But with entrees from $16 (burger) to $30, after you add a $5 - $20 small plate or snack - it is pricey.  Also it is BYOB but they have an amazing selection of teas and infusions. My $3 Genmaicha (Japanese Barley tea) was perfection,  Yes, I love it here but no, I can't come often.
Brand new (ok - a few years old) in venue terms and clean, spacious and plenty of seats.  Expensive.  We have seen numerous concerts here.

While the food (I get the breakfast scrambler - no tots) is just OK, Austin behind the counter is a gem.  He has personality to spare and is so charming.  A big shout out to Austin.  Also - if they offered soup (tomato soup here is good) in the AM (yes, really) I would get it.

Another fabulous outpost of El Limon (I have also been to the Conshy and Fraser locations) and it is just great.  BIG-a$$ burritos (wet or dry or in a bowl), delicious Al Pastor, free margaritas if you dine in, friendly service, fresh guac.  LOVE me some El Limon.  Do not miss their Al Pastor - just enough pineapple and succulent pork. So good.
Green Top - right next to red top - is a "touristy" landscaping/floral/plant place.  Fun to browse around but also tourist prices.

Interesting and strange combination of menu items.  Italian and "dinerish" and then sushi.  Whatever.  Meanwhile if you stick to the salads (huge and excellent) and sandwiches, byou'll be OK.  I did not care for the sushi here.   We ordered salads to go one time when we really needed food right before my wedding.  2 chicken caesars and 2 diet cokes were promptly delivered to a nearby hair salon and were we EVER grateful.  So thanks to Cafe Allesio for filling a need and serving up decent Italian fare (mediocre sushi) and AWESOME salads.

I was in this area for an 8 AM appointment and desperately needed coffee. Target (Starbucks) does not open until 8, but Ruby's is open at 7 AM and does a VERY nice breakfast.  I had coffee and a very nice "veggie" eggs Benedict with spinach, tomato and avocado.  The hollandaise likely came from a mix - but i asked for it on the side and it was pretty good anyway.  So after tax and tip - I blew $15 on breakfast but it was delicious and a welcome respite.  Excellent service - the place was nearly empty - just me and one other table at 7:05 AM!

Needed watch bands pronto and Joel and the team at Carroll's delivered!  This store is one of the foundational stores in D-town and it is still in the shopping center (near the Acme) today.  We love Carroll's Jewelers.
Returned in 2013 for the Pompeii exhibit which was - ok - kinda small. Just OK for me. Our 9 year old enjoyed the day.  Many Exhibits were broken.  I think they need a boost,

My 17 year old and I were both here for different things over the last few months - Xrays, CT scans, MRIs - they offer it all.  Basic Xrays are walk-in.  Very nice technicians.  The front desk ladies were very nice to me - but you must be polite to them - they are super busy and over worked. They all need a big raise.  I am so grateful to MMI for providing much needed diagnostics for me and my kid.

Yum!  What a great idea.  Wish I had thought of it. Jules has terrific gourmet-topped, thin crust pies. I love the pie with Artichoke hearts, arugula and chopped fresh tomatoes.  They offer gluten free alternatives and its a SUPERB place for families with small children.  My only complaint?  No "white" milk - only chocolate.

Had a 5 star experience tonight dining out with a gal-pal. We started off with delectable cocktails - I had a classic mojito with a few pieces of fresh pineapple muddled in.  Delicious and refreshing.  She had a purple concoction garnished with an orchid.  It had Chambord and Vanilla Vodka and other things in it.  So good!  We shared nearly everything.  The Horiatiki Salad was terrific (Though $15 for a plate of mostly tomatoes in olive oil and lemon juice is a bit steep.)  The trio of dips and spanakopita (which seemed a bit borekish) were great.  Entrees of Moussaka and (again? ) Dorado (Because it's cheap - they offer Dorado aka Mahi-Mahi as a fish du jour often.) were tasty and filling.  Dessert and tasty La Colombe coffee rounded out a teriffic meal. Kanella (Cypriot, not Greek)  is still my fave - but the service from Mark, a prime window-side table and a groovy mood (Thanks, Bacardi!) made this a 5 star Etsia night for me.

We had never been in here before but we have supported A Woman's place in the past.  My 15 year old snagged a REAL fox-fur jacket for $45!!!!  And for jusy $7 more a Jean Jacket, a top and 2 pairs of paints.  7 items for $52.  WOW.  We hit it big!!!
The flowers my friend sent me for the holidays were awful - nearly dead upon arrival, so they sent a replacement which was much fresher.  Not a great florist.

This is a large, clean, well-run starbuck on the corner of Marsh & Silverside roads in Wilmington.  We usually stop by in the morning - and even at the height of the AM rush, the lines move quickly.  Fourbucks, Charbucks, whatever yoiu call it - it's nice tohave one around when you need it.  Especially in the Culinary wasteland of North Wilmington.

Faux-juice bar.  The smoothies are loaded with calories. I only get one thing here and that is fresh wheatgrass juice. And sometimes - it ain't all that fresh.  It's the closest to my old office - but unless you want a milkshake (Like the Mocha Blast) or another caloric treat - this is not a true juice bar.  Oh - the blond lady with the LONG colorful nails - who has worked here a long while - is a doll and very efficient.  She deserves a raise.

Great for a quick lunch to go (or eat in at high bar stools or on a summer day at one of 3 small outdoor tables.  Sushi is made daily in a refriogerated case, but they will make fresh maki and nigiri to order if you are willing to wait.  (It's worth the wait for fresh hamachi scallion maki or the "Honeymoon Roll" - a delish concoction of Shrimp Tempura inside and Salmon and Avo outside.  They cook Yalitori bowls, Bi-bim-bap, Udon, Teriyaki Boxes and Gyoza/Shumai (frozen) at the hot food station, too.  Good prices and great for a quick fix.  Tip:  Don't just grab the pre-packed sushi - have them roll your maki to order.  Much better that way!

This is THE Starbucks - smack dab in the middle of New Hope's tourist district.  Right over the bridge from Lambertville.  And while, I tuly believe that "friends don let friends drink Charbucks" (or "Fourbucks") this one is not bad.  Nice customer service and the line (if there is one) moves quickly.  As Fourbucks goes - this is one of the better locations.

An older Library with a helpful staff including "Ginger" at the front counter. Restrooms are NASTY.  Truly awful, but the meeting room is spacious and the different areas of the library (Teens, Little kids Adults, Music, Computers) are just fine.  Support our libraries!!!!  They are sorely needed.

While I did not wind up purchasing my frames here (too $$$), I was very impressed with the high level of customer service.  (Drat - I can't remember the name of the nice lady who helpeed me.)  It's a great place - too bad I can't afford it at the moment.

Not just gyros!  In fact, when we walked in late (8:45 ish) on a Wednesday night we did not even order Gyros.  The Avgolemono soup (one of my favorite soups of all time) was good and the Horiatiki Salad was fresh and fabulous.  It reminded me of the Horiatiki at Kanella (Cypriot) in Center City and that is a GOOD THING.  Service with a smile was stellar and the pastitsio and stuffed eggplant (with bechamel, baby!) were very filling but also very, very well made.  Classics. Decor could use a refresh (thus no 5th star). Also front entrance is NOT compliant for elderly/physically challenged.  Just like Ya ya would have wanted it.  Can't wait to return.

We come in about once a month - this last time for wings & pizza for me and my 10 year old and her 10 year old friend.  The owner is terrific and treats us so nicely.  Kids love the cane-sugar-based sodas (Watermelon and Huckleberry).  Pizza is quite good here.  A great value, too.  They also cater many meals for our elementary school and the teachers love the food.

It seems like they should have decent food here - but alas, no.  Service is pretty disinterested, and the prices are more than the quality demands.  I did get a nice side of steamed broccoli in lieu of the fries - so that was good.  I don't come here unless co-workers force me to.

The place is under construction/outdoor removation and it looks just awful, but inside Kiersten treated us well and the basic food was about the best I havve ever had at an Outback (I am not a fan).  Salad was fresh (Iceberg, 1/2'ed grape tomatoes, a few cubes of cucuumber and croutons).  steak was a bit overcooked (asked for medium Rare got medium).  El kiddo inhaled a 7 oz. salmon filet and broccoli.

When my 12 year old finished hunting through the carnage at Plato's Closet we stopped here to check out the shoes and active wear.  TJ Maxx can be "hit or miss" but when you hit, you can hit BIG.    Snagged 2 pairs of sporty shorts and a pair of sandals just in time for summer for $46.  Yay!  This location is not as nice as some and yet much nicer thatn, say, the South Philly one. 3 stars.  Middle of the road.

4 stars for the food and 5 for the entertainment.  Maria herself - who had a cooking show on PBS for years - was in the kitchen when we came here for Mew year's Eve 2006.  (I was wondering why it took me so long to yelp her.)  We had a very enjoyable evening.  The best part were the home-made meatballs and the (keep it on the d.l.) tray of limoncello and cordials passed after the meal.  My only regret is that we have not yet returned. We will!

Nope.  I take it back. I was excited to have Chipotle as a quick lunch option.  Not quick.  The line can wind around for miles - you must get here before 11:55 AM or you are stuck. They then ran out of chicken and the line screeched to a halt.  Nasty attitude from the girls behind the line, too.  (Not the cashier lady - she was nice.)  My bowl of rice and veggies got cold during the wait so I literally had to walk out.  I will not be back until my coworkers drag me here again.  I certainly will not come bnack on my own and not from 12 - 1 PM.  No frikkin' way.  Get it together, Chipotle.

This brand-spankin' new Chick Fil-A (on a busy corner of Route 1 & Pennell Road (452) has a double drive-thru, a play room and GREAT customer service.  So far we love it for our 7 year old who can play and eat (And we usually get out of there for around $20 for the 3 of us).  Not the healthiest choice - but the side salad (skip the cheese, croutons, sunflower seeds and dressing) is good - and we enjoy the occaisional fried chicken sammy with diet lemonade.  There is also a Chick Fil A inside the (nearly dead) Granite Run Mall.  This is not it.  This is the NEW Chick Fil near the CVS.  They also do fundraisers for schools and community groups.  (I'll definitely be looking into this!)  Stop by!

Please note:  I came back here a second time on June 16 and had a mani & pedi for just $25.00.  Anthony himself did it and it was very good.  4 solid stars!  I had a good experience yesterday at 5 PM at Nails by Anthony.  A man (who I presume is Anthony) greeting me nicely when I arrived (walk-in) and a lovely lady, "Mimi" agreed to do my manicure.  I told her I wanted a "regular" manicure and 10 minutes of chair massage while my nails dried.  She said "Massage 10 minutes? OK?"  OK.  So the manicure progresses nicely - she does a good job and then she does a fabulous hand and arm massage.  For a really long time. Evidently she thought I wanted the "spa manicure" which includes everything from the $12 "regular" manicure and adds 10 minutes of hand & arm massage.  So at the end while my polish is drying - she reluctantly gave me a bout 3-4 minutes of a lackluster b.s. back rub.  OK.  No big deal.  I kind of expect b.s. massages at nail joints. Next time - honestly, skip any kind of extra massage - not worth the $8-$10.  I will however, be back for manicures - at $12 it was worth it.  The place is new and clean with 6 mani tables and 5 huge NEW pedi thrones.  I wonder, however, as is so often the case, if this place will be just as nice 6-12 months from now.  I kinda doubt it.  Expect to see a 1-2 star downgrade in a year. They are new and trying to get your business - so take advantage while you can.  Also - they have ONE GOOD package deal (Most of their "packages" offfer no discount) - for $55.00 you get a regular mani, regular pedi, eye brow wax, lip wax and 10 minutes of b.s. massage.  Please note - I did not try the waxing here - I only trust my eyebrows to Jennae or Cara at bodyrest - but if you feel like taking a chance on a cheapie brow wax - this may just be the place.  This is a good alternative to Rittenhouse nails or the dreaded Gomo. Again - try it NOW while they are still new (open for 3 months so far.).

I would give them 4 stars but they are closed in the afternoons/evening rush - so if you HAPPEN to be there in the morning this is a cute spot to grab a cup of coffee (or a latte or tea, etc.) before you get on the SEPTA train to Philly.  I sure wish they stayed open later.

I have come in and out of this store so many, many. many times. And always empty handed.  And so much BLACK and white.  Don't you people know about color?  The service is kinda snotty and prices are just too high.  It's a shame.
You can get them now at the Media farmers market!  Whoo-hoo.  REAL Canele!

Wendy's is never our top choice for dining - but el kiddo wanted something chicken-y so we stopped in (dine in) and she got her "value menu" chicken sandwich with lettuce, mayo and bacon added (30 cents extra).  Hubby got a few burgers that he ate sans bun.  We all got 99 cent frosties.  I tried the "new" bacon cheeseburger on a pretzel bun.  What a horrific waste of calories.  Bun was overbaked (dark brown and nearly black).  Loaded with both sliced cheese and a nasty fake-cheese whiz-like sauce.  Never again.  Batherroms were moderately clean. Service was poor - order was worng the first time  but corrected the second.  Please was dead empty at 5:30 PM on a Sunday. Drive through had a line though.  Creepy!

You're KIDDING me?  4 & 5 star reviews for this place?  Really?  OK, it's better than La Tolteca - but it is not great. It's MEH.  MEHxican. It looks like an old Wawa or 7-11. In fact - I am leaning more toward 2 stars - and here's why...  A good friend and I had lunch here - he had a "special" burrito stuffed with shrimp & chicken, covered in a cheese sauce and a green tomatillo salsa - not bad.  I had a mediocre "soft" chimicanga stuffed with beef tips. Not horrible - but not great.  But what really got us were the chips 'n ketchup, I mean salsa. This was NOT fresh salsa.  It was most definitely bottled and really tasted of canned tomatoes and vinegar.  It seemed like ketchup.  Weird.  Our server was a nice gal, but disappeared around "may we have the check, please" time.  If you are on a "lunch hour" don't come here.  It took us 70 minutes to have lunch.  Or at least tell them you are in a hurry.  So - if you want Mexican - avoid La Tolteca and only come to El Tapatio if you have no other alternatives.  And in this part of Delaware?  The MEH-xican American pickin's are slim.  Note:  Went back again.  Still 3 stars.  The chlicken flautas are good - but greasy.  Beef flauta was pretty bad.  Decent guac.  We'll probably be back again soon.

OK, so it's still MEHxican - and the salsa and chips taste like tostios and old el paso, but the servers now know us - and we now know EXACTLY what to order.  The servers and cooks here work HARD and are very gracious to us.  I always get the #75 burrito with chicken instead of beef (I don't like the shredded beef here for whatever reason), guac on the side.  Fresh brewed iced tea.  I'm set for my "usual" business lunch - and most days we can get in, out and back to work in an hour.  We'll be back - because we have few other choices.

Sing it Black Crowes Style...  If I had a RE-ME-DY...  ...anyhow - enough singing.  But remedy is a reason to sing.  I am so glad I can get a nice hot cup of greem gunpowder or an iced Jasmine in Summertime.  I love fine teas - and Remedy is a cute place to get some.

I am contually surprised and delighted by QVC (and I do not fit the profile of your typical at-home shopper).  I do not shop with them often but the jewelry, clothing and cookware items I have purchased over the years have all been high quality items and for good (to great) prices.  The Studio Park office complex is interesting to tour, and it's right in my own back yard!
Still very pricey - but great new digs and dining options. We'll be back!

The Pizza Wagon comes to my office in Chestrbrook, PA about once a month or so.  (Kinda wish it was more as it is a culinary wasteland around these parts).  For $10 you can pick from 5-6 pies and for one person they are huge.  I think the $10 also includes a drink - can of soda or bottle of water).  I like the Spinach pie (it is supposed to be white but i asked for sauce and they did it!).

Wow - a beaders paradise right in our own (new) Media back yard. Classes for kids and adults and a VAST selection of beads and beading supplies (books, wire, fishing line, clasps)/  Can't wait to take my artsy 7 year old here.

This is a BIG CVS right near the Uno Pizzeria in newtown Square. I usually shop at CVS or Walgreen's for cosmetic and OTC medications.  This one has ample parking and is much nicer than the one in Paoli near my office.  It is also a but nicer than the Aston location but not as good as the Lima/Media location which i now consider my go-to CVS.  Not sure how late the pharmacy is open - many close earlier than I would prefer - especially when you have a sick kid in the middle of the night.  Break out your little red ExtraCare card and get to shoppin'!
Very good jewish-style deli food - and they even have half-sour pickles.  YAY!  Not cheap - but nt horribly expensive either.  So glad they are here.

Thank you! Thank you! Thank you ! Yelp for introducing me to DnA. They are a great find - and if I lived in NoLibs I certainly would be a regular client of Rich.  He did a great color for me - single process and a decent cut. I have to say that my jury is still out of the cut - as I need to let it be for a few days.  I think it may make my face look fat.  UPDATE:  OK - I am officially not happy with the cut.  But I love the color. I am scared to call them and tell them?  I don't want to downgrade them to 3 stars - as they really are a 4-5 star establishment.  I just don't like this cut at ALL.  (Still lovin' the color though.)  The spa is clean and gorgeous - and although it is nearly 2 years old - it looks BRAND spankin' new.  Excellent choices in color scheme (blue & white) and good design elements.  My only reason for not giving it 5 stars was the weird (somewhat icy) vibe I got from the assistant (It feels demeaning to say shampoo girl - as I am certain she does MUCH more than that.).    The receptionist was cute and friendly and had GREAT HAIR. I got some serious hair envy from pretty much everyone who works there.  I will return.  (So I hope the assistant won't totally hate me if she reads this review.)  I would DEFINITELY go here for color.  Rich knows his stuff!  (And his mom - who just happened to be in that day for highlights) is a sweetie.

I attended and spoke at a conference here but did not stay overnight in the hotel part.  The conference facilities were very nice, well-equipped and comfortable.  The breakfast and breaks had an abundance of well-stocked beverages and treats.  I would definitely consider having a conference here.
This is our go-to Wawa all summer long whenever we are at the Ridley Park Swim Club - you can walk there!  My kid and assorted friends load up on snacks, candy and cold beverages.  A g-d-send,

I love whole paycheck, er, i mean Whole Foods. I stopped in when the store was very empty (YAY!) and the breakfast buffet was still up - so no hot foods for me.  I got a thing of Whole Foods Guacamole ($4.99 for a small) - so delicious, a $7 tub of mixed berries (yikes) and a $12.95 genji sushi salmon plate.    Funny how just a few tasty snacks add up here.  All were terrific.

Glad it's here.  Seems to have a more limited selection?  No Quesadillas?  Or at least not on the streamlined menu.  No matter... I wanted a naked burrito and they had it.  Fast service.  $9 no tax (it's DE!)

Yeah, baby!  They now are open for dinner!!!!!  Those blintzes rock.  Took my 5 year old here for Shavuos.  Wow!!!  Try the sidekick sampler!!!!!  Oh - and the kugel is better now than when I went before. LOVE IT HERE!

After we get our pet supplies at Tobin's (Feed Store), it's so tempting to stop for a breakfast sandwich or lunchtime feast.  Classic food served by friendly(mostly female) staff. Cute place and good, simple, "safe" food.

In the heart of the Gayborhood is Cafe Twelve. Plenty of comfy chairs, cafe tables - big windows that open in warmer weather and most importanly - top quality coffee drinks.  I had a cafe au lait (made with brewed coffee - not espresso) and it was smooth and delicious.  Super nice guys running the place, too. - And 2 fairly clean restrooms.  I'll be back!
Prices are WAY too high to justify buying fancy-schmancy sandwiches and "gourmet picnic" type fare.  Just OK.  Not a fave.

Stunning!  A treasure!  Not to be missed!  Especially in springtime when the azaleas and rhododendrons bloom, this place is just GORGeous!  Great for kids, adults, older folks - everyone. And - if you join the Pennsylvania Horticultural Society you can visit for free!

Just OK today.  I had not been here in quite some time and while the hot foods/cooked foods seem to have expanded the sushi was just not fresh.  I ordered a side order of ("new") grilled tofu - at $4.50 which was tasty and safe to eat.  The $10.95 (pricey) Valentine roll had very questional salmon inside.  So questionable that I still don;t know if it was supposed to be raw fresh salmon, smoked salmon or just old, nasty salmon.  Very disappointed - and I spent over $16 on a carry out lunch. I will not be back in a hurry, if ever.

This used to be "The Barn" and it had screens named Silo, Paddock and Hayloft - and other barn-like names.  Now it has greatly expanded to service the ever increasing amount of movie-goers.  It's a nice theatre with fairly clean environs.  I have great nostalgic memories of this theatre from when my friends used to work here in Jr. High & High School.  We took our 5 y.o. here on an un-crowded HOT summer Sunday at 2 PM and the a/c felt great.  Plus she sat still for the entire show.

This updated and upgraded review is based on the HAIR SALON (not the spa services.)  I received a coupon for a free haircut - and figured - for Free?  You bet I'll try it.  I was able to get a receptionist on the phone and she politely booked me for a 10 AM cut with Rudy - who is a doll.  Linda who shampooed my hair was really sweet, too.  I am happy with my cut (would have cost $55) and left a nice tip.  I may very well return!!!  Rudy is a sweet guy.

I love Beans (it's a chain) and the newish D-town location is a great addition to an already cutesy and affluent town.  You can snag dermalogica, OPI, Essie, Fekkai and many other well-known (and a few lesser known) beauty brands here.  A teeny salon-ette is in the back but it needs some tweaking to get it up and running.  Can't wait to come here for a quick wax.  Friendly staff so far. Lovin' it!

Stopped in here to do a small shop (about $50 worth) because it was on the way home and I really loathe the local Acme.  This Giant is pretty nice - I vacillate between 3 and 4 stars.  Giant - for me - is my go-to for non organic food and select household goods.  I usually like Whole Paycheck (aka Whole Foods) and Trader Joes - but for low cost staples - I gotta trust Giant.  We'll be back.

Ercolino Leather & Shoe Repair was our go-to place for YEARS.  (And they were just about the only game in town for years as well.).  Mr. Ercolino could fix just anout anything.  Shoes, boots, handbags, leather jackets/pants.  They were a needed service and a mainstay of the Doylestown community.

I dither back and forth between 3 & 4 stars based on each experience.  This time a gal-pal and I dined in and shared Chips & Pico (Not enough pico for that big pile of chips) for $7 and 2 orders of 2 tacos.  2 shrimp and 2 pork.  The tacos were fresh tasting and the pork ones were LOADED with pork and avocado spread.  The shrimp tacos were very skimpy with 2 small shrimp in each taco.  Delicious crema and radishes.  Next time?  I am getting extra pcio and skipping the shrimp tacos.

I prefer Qdoba to Chipotle - but in a pinch this newly opened location (next door to a Starbucks, and down the strip from Trader Joe's) is OK for a quick bowl of carbs & fat.  The chicken was over cooked, so maybe next time I will try the steak.  Guacamole is good.

I am not a Cosi fan but I was genuinely STARVING one morning and popped in here for a cup of soup - which came with apiece of their"Cosi bread".  Inarticulate, disinterested staff and watery "Lobster & Butternut Squash" soup which had little to zero lobster and an oddly fishy note.  I won't be ordering THAT ever again.

I am contually surprised and delighted by QVC (and I do not fit the profile of your typical at-home shopper).  I do not chop with them often but the jewelry, clothing and cookware items I have purchased over the years have all been high quality items and for good (to great) prices.  The Studio Park office complex is interesting to tour, and it's right in my own back yard!
Totally average Dunkin. When I went there was no line as it was about 2:30 PM on a weekday.  Got an iced coffee - got in and got out quick.
Ettore is closed.  Larissa is now at Tommi on 7 & Chestnut.

Better than expected and save for the milipede infestation (saw 3 of them in a one night stay) room was fine.  (Furniture in "living room" part of suite was a bit dated.  Bedroom was fine.  Food service is mediocre (banquet style catering) but the staff was friendly and helpful.  Came here for a conference - would not stay here otherwise.

This is now my go-to Strarbucks and is nearest on my way to my new job.  It's a 4 star place but I am knocking a star off gfor the horrendous parking situation.  It is located next to the Paoli train station which is jam-packed night and day and clearly there is just not enough parking for ommuters and locals alike.  I parked in a seafood restaurant next door and walked over.  Meanwhile, my Grande Nonfat Caramel macchiato (at $4.82) was pricey but delicious.  Nice gals running the show. I wonder where they park???  Excellent Service, Crappy Parking

Having been to the original shake shack and a satellite NYC location before, I knew what I was getting when I walked in (and out) of the Philly Shake Shack a few weeks back.  12:30 is NOT the time to go.  So today I was wiser and went at 11:40 AM. Perfect.  No line.  2 minute wait for a single burger with lettuce and tomato (no Shack-mayo for me) and a Half 'n Half made with STRAWBERRY lemonade.  I also got a taste of the Red Velvet Custard.  It was uber-rich and loaded with cake pieces and cream cheese icing.  The taste was enough - I did not need to get a cup of that caloric-disaster.  Meanwhile, my burger was great (I also enjoy the burgers at 500 degrees and when I've got cash to burn, Village Whiskey).  And they don't call me the "Empress of the Arnold Palmer" for nothin'.  That half 'n half was just what I needed.  Counter lady (I can't remember her name) was lovely and the guy cleaning the tables on the floor was a doll.  Execllent service (prior to the thundering herd that arrives at noon).  Do not come here during peak times. It's night and day.  Oh - and they were selling a $9 (NINE Dollar!!!) artisinal Brooklyn chocolate bar at the front counter.  Come ON!  It can't be THAT good????
Super fast response to an emergency heating call. Courteous and professional.  A bit expensive (emergency) but cheaper than Horizon.

I have been a big fan of Sushi Nami's Paoli location for lunches (and the occasional dinner) for a while so I was eager to try the Wayne Location on Route 30 not far from my office.  Yumi was there (she is usually in Paoli) and  the place is new - but has the exact same menu.  Lunch specials are still there and still great at $14.00 for the salmon lunch.  The pork dumpling soup is a great winter treat - hot and fresh with 3 pork gyoza and a bunch of veggies.  Love it here. Will be back!

Oversized and Overpriced - as Lori H. so succinctly said. My DD and I went here for Shavuos/Shavuot and shared a single blintz ($5.00) which was overly stuffed with "meh" sweet cheese filling and served with "blueberry glop".  DD was upset - she wanted real fruit.  She's 6 - she knows what good is.  She told me later that she liked "last year's place" (Delicatessen - they no longer do dinner) better.  We always have jewish-style food and blintzes on Shavuot.  (google it.)  The latkes (1/2 order is 5 latkes - PLENTY) were delish and the Dr. Browns and Fresh OJ worked, but the fried kreplach (they very same ones that I love in the soup) are deep-fried.  Yuck. So disappointed - I wanted pan-fried.  Never again.  The came topped with a mountain of greasy fried, sweet onions (OK - but a grease fest).  Our server Claudine was accomodating and we like her!  But to get that 4th Star back, I guess I'll just have to stick to the soup.  (I get the Chicken soup with Matzoh balls and Kreplach (I like both and will pay the extra charge.)  It comes in a vat and I take nearly everything home.  It was $27 (plus tip) for 3 appetizers, 2 drinks and 1 enormous (and woefully dry) $3.75 sugar cookie with sprinkles.  We have enough for lunch the next day.  Oh - and per our server - don't get the giant black & whites.  They're dry.  So sad to have to downgrade - but the truth's the truth.  All that said - I'll be back for soup soon with my gal pals. And "new" pickles (half sours).  Love those.  And I will try the Kasha.  Hope it's better than Herschel's.

It's a Wawa, but it happens to be the closest one on my route from office to home (or vice versa) so I am glad it's there.  Grab some coffee, cigs, a junky snack, a banana or a meh sub.  (Sorry - that's "hoagie" to you.)  We need more supermarkets (not Wawa's) and dry cleaners in Center City so I am glad they are here - but still wishin' for more grocery choices.

Moved to 2040 Market and is now called Fine Wines & Good Spirits. Much nicer - huge brand-new store.  Clean and gorgeous.  Lots of wines - less in the spirit realm (but Total Wine & Liquor in Delaware has spoled me forever).  Convenient to my work.  (Yay.)

We took our 5 year old daughter to a Camden Riversharks game at Campbell's field on a perfect evening.  She enjoyed herself immensely - and we did too.  The weather was perfect.  No rain, not too hot, not cold.  She posed for a picture with one of the mascots (Blooper), the other shark (Finley) was unavailable.  We waited 50 minuted (and spent $5) for her to get on that darned "bouncy castle" but she claims it was worth it for the 4.5 minutes she spent inside.  (Note to self:   skip that next time.)   Seats were comfortable and had cup holders.  Food is pricey (and basic ballpark fare) as we anticipated.  Parking was $5.00  A great alternative to a Phillies game and GREAT for kids.  Next time we'll ride the (small) $1 per ride carousel.  NOTE:  Most concessions and atttractions shut down at the 7th inning.

Hey - one man's trash is another's treasure. I have come here since I was a tween - when my granmother was still alive - and boy did she have a gift for scoring at a flea market.  You can find loads of jewelry, furniture, household goods (china and flatware, planters, etc.) old chothing and shoes (yech!!!) and much more.  It's a bit disheveld - but it's a FLEA MARKET a la Mary Fisher's of the old days.  Hours vary seasonally, so check before you trek. (They are not open every day - usually weekends and 1 week day - at the time of this review it was Wednesdays 6 AM - 4 PM).  Lots of vendors pack up by 2 or 3 PM though. Bruing cash - many do not accept plastic but more and more do.  Also you can graba cuppa joe at the diner next door.

Delicious food - great crocks of French Onion and BIG salads (even the side salad) chock full of goodies.  Service from Nicole was wonderful and my half coffee-half cocoa topped with a mountainous plume of whip was marvelous.  A decent selection of brews on tap from dark, chocolatey stouts to pale lagers and everything in between.  Moderate prices. Historic architecture and a beautiful bar.  Lovely lunch. Can't wait to come back.
For a chair massage (in a throne-type chair), this is fine - albeit pricey - and a decent way to kill time in the Philly airport.  It's usually not  that crowded.  Glad it's here.

We love and support Greensgrow.  My 5 year old's class took a wonderful field trip here - and kids need to know about farming and Urban farming.  It is very important that we support locavore ventures and sustainable agriculture.  Go, Grennsgrow!

For 3 years this was our go-to ice rink (the only game in town, really) but now that we live in the 'burb's we go to the one out in Aston which is bigger, cleaner and nicer (and offers a full service bar/snackbar).  Meanwhile, this rink is a much needed outlet for kids who want to learn to ice skate in Philly. They offer lessons and also hockey.  My (then 5-7, now 8) kid loved going here. So glad we took her to the public skating sessions. A good birthday party option as well.  It's cold inside - bring a jacket!!!

A good place to see live music.  Yes, the restrooms are pretty bad - but not the worst I've seen, by far.  And yes, there are copius amounts of drunk people - which increases based on the bands that are playing.  A nice big bar.

A single ice surface facility with a few USFSA - figure skating (minor) competitions each year. A decent place to practice.  Limited ice times due to single surface.  Lockers room, small snack bar.  Public skate times vary so check before you go.  They also have a pro shop with mostly hockey gear for sale, but the best part is Frank.  Frank gets 5 stars for sharpening my figure skaters Edeas over the past 4 years. We love him and pray he never retires.

This is a fun artisan gallery.  Great for gift ideas and just poking around and gawking.  Colorful glass, bright pieces, jewelry, wearable art, I love it here.  Bring money.  And avoid the high tourist season when it's packed.  And please, don't bring a very small child who might break something.

Unlike, my good friend "Fish", who evidently had a bad experience here - I never did.  Back in the '90's we'd go here after work (I worked at Accents & Images when the original owner, Joe, was still alive.  Or we'd get coffee at Granpa Hicks - which was also great.  Meanwhile, when the throngs of NY tourists get you down, take a break with a slightly overpriced, but very tasty coffee drink here at house of coffee.  They have snacks, too - and good iced tea choices during the summer.  A welcome respite from the rest of Peddler's Village.
Changed location and owners, and so pricey - and not worth it anymore.  I am sad. I liked the old Gross'.  RIP.

This bar has not changed in the last 25 years. Mostly biker-type regulars from Q-town or Souderton and a few D-town long-timers. Nice people in a dark and smoky bar (Hooray - you actually still smoke here).  Cheap drinks and easy access to the rest of town.  Not my thing - but OK in a pinch.  The bartender Susie is a doll.

Next time we'll make an appointment.  A friend & I showed up on an extremely busy Thursday before the July 4th holiday weekend. They were PACKED.  At least a 40 minute wait for the 2 of us to be seen.  (She for a mani, i for a gel mani.)  Gals were friendly enough - but they were multitasking for sure!  We'll stop back another time.  (We decided to try Gateway nails and wound up leaving there also - what a mistake.  Gateway Nails manager was soooooo rude).  At least the ladies are friendly here.

Just OK.  Stopped here for a needed sundry and got side-tracked in their (strange and centrally located) photo department.    Service was fine.  No major issues - but I like my "regular" Walgreen's in Aston better.

Our brand-new (2 days on the job) waitress seemed overwhelmed - but somehow got us through a decent enough lunch.  I had my usual - Matzoh Ball Soup (served in a vat) with Kreplach added.  (And a Diet Dr. Brown's Cream Soda).  Classic , heavy, jewish-deli-insipred fare served in HUGE portions with prices to match,  Whatever you are getting - soup, salad or sandwich - SPLIT IT with a friend. (Or take 1/2 home).  Gut-busting, not mind-blowing but good. Oh - and the smaller sized cookies the give you with the bill?  I wish they sold that size - perfect!

Chick-Fil-A Lima has sponsored 2 school fundraising events now for my child's elementary school.  They do a thing where on a certain day during certain hours (for us it was a Tuesday night from 5 - 7:30 PM) for everyone who mentions XYZ school they give the school 15% of the sales.  We packed the place with hundreds of families and it was a win-win for all involved.  The kids loved seeing some of the faculty and staff running the counter (and the principal bussing tables!) and the restaurant (and school) makes money.  Great job, Chick-Fil-A!

This is my 11 year old's go-to 5 below for pollyanan gifts, girl scout projects, last minute birthday party gifts and cheapie electronics (Like a selfie stick for $4.99) and accessories.  Is it my favorite store?  No.  But it is nicer (and more expensive) than a dollar store - it's a FIVE dollar store.  Great for tweens & teens - and even a few things for the parents.

4 stars for the food.  I try to ignore the surroundings.  Great Duck.  And hands-down best steamed dumplings.  LOVE 'em.  Wonton Duck Soup can be a little greasy - but man, it's a tasty indulgence.  Oh - and watching my 4 year old scarf down 3 different types of dumplings was precious.  She sat at the counter like a pro.  She tried the shrimpdumplings, wonton (sans soup they are very tasty) and the steamed chicken dumplings.  Can't wait to take her back here.

While waiting for Jewelers Row to open this morning, I strolled by DELICATESSEN - at the site of the former Kibitz in the City at 7th & Chestnut.  Now under new (and friendly) management, Delicatessen offers Jewish-Deli style food with a twist.  I ordered the Side Kick Sampler ($12) to get a taste of 4 popular items.  All were excellent but the real standout was the home-made cheese blintz.  Jill was a great server and I can't wait to go back and try "Bubby's Kitchen Sink Pho".  Check this place out - it sure ain't Kibbitz any more.  It's way better.

3 star food - maybe 4 star if you order selectively. I had a very nice salad (sans calorie bomb of fried tortilla bowl) with Avocado and shrimp.  Lovely.  Elote served on or off the cob with Chipotle mayo and Cotija cheese.  Friendly service, colorful decor and kid friendly.  Next time I am getting a margarita for sure! (And there WILL be a next time.)

My little girl and I are big fans of the Nicoise (we get it with shrimp instead of canned tuna) at Saladworks.  It's one of the best ways i get overtly get her to eat veggies.  Now, grant it, many Saladworks are kinda, well, rusty & gross. If the lettuce looks bad - don't bother.  But at the Montgomeryville location (technically North Wales, I guess) the Salad's good!  The eatin's good, too.  SCORE!  Plus there is a Baja Fresh nearbu for hubby.

I have eaten here twice and briefly considered it for a rehearsal dinner location (based on its location - near Doylestown & Warrington).  They could not accomodate our large group, so we opted to go elsewhere.  That said, Via Barolo has some decent food - you have to know what to order (do not get fish here!) and ask them to go light on the salt.  In my opinion, the food here runs on the saltier side.  Pasta was cooked al dente - and very good.  If I ever go back I will stick to salads and pasta dishes.

It's OK.  We went to Ted's because the line for PF Changs was "not worth the wait" long.  Had some burgers (Bison is offered,of course) and I had a decent salad.  Nothing to write home about.  Some of my family and friends love it - but I just think it's OK.  We have also been to the one in Philly where my little girl likes the mac 'n cheese.  Pleasant service and decor.  And not nearly as mobbed as PF Changs.

Thank god they are here!  Philadelphia is a holistic wasteland (or should I say "waist-land - people here are FAT!) and we veggie types need places like this.  I gotta have my grass - wheat or otherwise. I also get mixed green veggies (no carrot- they charge me more but I don't care - I want it GREEN!).  I need them and they have a reliable fresh product.  Gotta have my juice!

Not sure I can impart anything better or different than the other reviewers. I liked but did not LOVE the soup I picked (should have tried a few more samples first). I chose Crab & Corn (mostly corn) Chowder,  and it was OK.  The salad (1/2 is plenty big for me) a Cobb was fresh and good.  Weird ordering lines.  Saladworks with a yuppie vibe. About $11 - with NO DRINK.

The hubby and I stopped in on a Saturday around 1PM and there was nobody ahead of us, so we got a basic oil change for $39.95 (plus tax was 40-some-odd).  Friendly quick service and we were in and out.  No issues.

Chain pseudo-Brooklyn-Italian (Immigrant cuisine circa 1954) in whopping huge portions.  (Only recently has Buca Mio - for one - become an option.)  They make a passable Chicken Marsala and decent pizza.  It is, indeed, carby goodness!  I have my ordering down to a science - especially when dining alone. I get a side of fettucine alfredo with the alfredo sauce on the side (so I can control the amount of glop).  A side order is HUGE.  Then I order ONE SINGLE (yummy) meatball - which is the size of a small baby's head.  (*ouch, the imagery*).  I then slice up the meatball and put the red sauce ("It's Gravy if you're from soufilly") and a bit of the alfreddo over the pasta.  A tasty heart attack on a plate.  The decor is loud and so are the clients.  This is the only restaurant I've been to where the table in the kitchen (it's a hoot) is QUITER than the tables in the dining rooms.  Check out the "pope room" and the ladies room while your there.  What a hoot!  Gourmet - mais, non - but fun?  Why, yes!
I agree with manyof the valid points that DJ makes.  Valley Square is by far the newest, hippest, coolest Shopping Center around.  Good shopping, restaurants and plenty of free parking.

Might very well be a five star place - but I have not seen enough of it yet. We visited today (and did NOT have enough time to explore it all).  The grounds are just wonderful - and post Hurricane Irene with the normally meandering Brandywine River now a raging mass of muddy water - WOW!.  We saw a great blue Heron and a couple of Cormorants, too.  Can't wait to go back and actually take the tour.

The Body shop is good - but not what it was in the old days when Anita Roddick was more involved.  I do like many of the products and the prices are moderate.  The body butters (gee whiz, there are now about 16 types of body butter to choose from) are good - I like the Mango and Shea - both for VERY dry skin.  The new Lemon one is lighter and nice.  I also love the Satsuma fragrance in things like body wash and lotion.  Fun to shop and the Body Shop.

We attended a 7 year old child's birthday party here - 26 kids and about 20 grownups in 2 separate dining areas.  Service was amazingly smooth for a party that large and chaotic.  All had salad (caesar or classic), bread and baked rigatoni.  Kids got to "make their own" pizza" in shifts at the chef's table in the kitchen.  Bucca is not the greatest food - but for a 7 year old's luncheon party it's a neat choice.  The kids had a ball.  The adults took excedrin.  Sasa and Kyle and our other serves were amazingly patient. Thank you!

We had a splendid late-summer/early fall meal "just the gals" at T's next door (The European Side - not the Italian side).  My duck salad which contained delicious macerated cherries and a slab (yes a huge slice/slab) of honey chevre (the "gateway drug" to all soft cheeses) was perfect.  An $8 side of Brussels sprouts was large enough for 3 to share and contained more bacon than should be legal.  Mussels (Moules Frite) come with fries (Frites) and 7 different sauces to choose from.  A classic Provencale was ordered.  The booze selections are many and varied.  Pick your fave.

We attended a party here yesterday for the daughters of a local celebrity.    Really.  And let me just say that Pump it Up is like a chaotic wonderland for kids. It's filled with giant bouncy inflatables, an obstacle curse, a giant slide, a slippery-slope tower, air hockey and more.  For kids aged 5 - 10 it's great!  The also have 2 private party rooms for the cake and pizza eating.  They reserve parking spots for the birthday child and also place all the presents into a cart and help you wheel it to your car (nice touch).  If we lived closer, we would definitely drop in for the "Pop-in play"  sessions.  Fun times!

Wow - nobody's yelped Poor Richards yet?  There is also one on Easton road - but this one is the priginal and has expanded much in it's 35-40 plus years as a Doylestown staple.  Poor Richards is a unique shop.  Is it a gift shop?  An antique shop?  A craft lovers place?  It's abit of all of these things.  A great place for tourists and locals alike to poke around and make discoveries.

This McDonalds was the first fast food restaurant in D-town and it is still there today.  As McDonald's go it is well run and fairly clean.  It is, however, a McDonald's after all and I just can't stand their food.  Maybe the fries are OK, but I am not a fast food lover.

Toppers has been around for-eh-ver.  They were the first to popularize the day spa to Philadelphia back in the early '80's.  Back then Toppers was in the Bourse and was pure luxury.  They'd even pick you up in a limo for your "queen for a day" of beauty.  Nowadays - a lot of the shine has been diminished.  The rude (and disorganized) reservation system and lines at check in and check out really take away from the over-priced just OK massages and pedicures that I have gotten.  I can't speak to the salon (hair/make-up) services - but for spa treatments - there are better places to go.  That said I got a gift certificate for $100 here and I gave it away to the receptionist in my building who was absolutely thrilled and delighted with her first-time ever massage.  But for a jaded, ex-NYC day spa owner, toppers needs to re-tool it's customer service and therapies in order to continue its legacy.  Try Terme di Aroma, Spa Elysium in Chestnut Hill - or even the pricey Phoenix, instead.

Had a nice evening here - but had to beg for veggies instead of chips (trying to watch carbs) for the $7 pico 'n chips.  They eventually oblidges with delicious cucumber, celery and carrot sticks.  PERFECT!  I wish you'd offer veggies on the menu as a sub for chips - I'd be willing to pay $2 - $3 extra for it.  But man, that pico (avocado chunks in pico de gallo) is terrific.  Great service.

This review is for event services and catering - not for staying at the hotel. I attended a catered dinner meeting held in a lovely mid-sized room at the radnor Hotel.  Our event included a cash bar with complimentary soft drinks and a choice of chicken, fish or vegetarian meal.  Rolls and butter were fine, salad was pre-plated but fresh and crisp with a delicious sweet dressing.   I had the veggie entree which looked to be the best choice by far - a bed of cous-cous with pesto and a stack of grilled veggies on top.  Service was attentive (3 servers - one who also tended bar) for our group of 35 women) including coffee and dessert,  This was a nice event and a fine space.  Incidentally room rates seema bit high ($249 per night on a Saturday).  Not sure if I ever would need to stay here - and not sure if it is big enough for a large wedding - but a small wedding or anniversary party would be nice here, I think.

Finally had a chance to dine in at the (not so) new location in Media and my issue is NOT about price - the prices seem pretty fair, actually.  I ordered Pico & Chips (I have had their delicious pico several times before - as a take out item - they add chunks of avocado to their pico making it super yummy). and for $5 they should have called it CHIPS and pico.  there was a 4 oz paper cup of pico - so I ordered another ($2.00 more) so my friend and I could share.  Also it took a long time to sit and wait for it - i think somebody goofed as I sat and sat and sat (and took a few phone calls) and eventually had to ask at the counter where it was.  Finally my friend & I ordered salads (we both opted for small "side" salads - fairly priced at $6.) She had the Caesar and I had the beet salad.  They should have called this KALE salad as it was basically a plate of balsamic vinegar-dressed kale with a glob of beets on top (best part) and 3 balls of goat cheese.  There was no mention of kale nor goat cheese on the menu - and I am not a big goat cheese fan. Not ordering that again!  So for $13 I ate 1/3 of a side salad and some chips & pico.  Hardly the greatest dinner ever.  Also - I wanted to get a single (fish?) taco as advertised on the website but now you must order 2 or 3 tacos - no more single taco orders.  I hope they will reconsider this and bring it back.  They need to update the website menu. Also there are inconsistencies on their printed menu at the restaurant (Cheese plate pricing on page 1 does not agree was cheese plate pricing on cheese list (page 3).  I will be back and we love the owner - they are a terrific member of our small Media community, but I honestly, have had better meals. Next time I will order a real "plate" and see what transpires.  Oh - and the eggplant parm (I thought about ordering that - when I saw it on the website menu) is no longer on the paper menu.  Many small things "wrong" added up to a lower rating than I had hoped to give.  The place is very nice, and I hope my next experience will be better.

For ice rink food - this is pretty darned good. The Pub is between ricks 3 & 4 - there is also a snack bar between rinks 1 & 2 with a more casual feel.  Both have great views of the rinks (ntach) and chicken parm, meatball subs and hogies, salads and decent drinks.  Very impressed - and glad to be able to get food when we are at the rink ALL DAY watching our kid.
It CLOSED!!!!!

What's not to love? Come hungry and enjoy all the lovely Greek specialties just like Yiayia made - maybe even better.  Moussaka, Pastitsio, Lamb Shanks (expensive), Gyros, Spanakopita and skads of greek pastries.  Aside from the food there are a few rides and carnival games for the kiddies ($3 -$4 per ride) and a flea market/shopping for the grown ups.  Tours of the church - and on Friday/Saturday night DANCING and music.  A terrific event.  We love it!

Had a perfectly lovely lunch here with a girlfriend.  I played it safe and got the amazing matzoh ball soup with kreplach.  For $8.95 - it's served in a large vat.  I took over half of it home.  The new pickles are also delish.  Service was good - but the tiny tables and lunch crowds causedmy friend to have her soda spilled - fortunately it spilled all over the table and not much got one her.  Come for dinner - or after 2 PM when the lunch rush dies down.

I go here for lunch - have never been for dinner. Just wanted to get that out of the way.  Meanwhile, for lunch they have a reasonbly priced "bento-like" special.  I have tried the Kalbi (YUM) and Bulgoki boxes.  That Kalbi is truly tasty - Korean Short-ribs in a tasty BBQ sauce.  Served with 2 shumai (or sometimes another type of dumpling) some green salad and rice.  I have also have some clay pot dishes with tofu - but I am a wimp and found them spicy.  Miran is a needed addition to the neighborhood.  It is well worth a try.

Fantastic experience today - on a Monday at lunch. Got some hot (prepared) foods and a pack of Genji Sushi for a quick take-out lunch.  Pricey (over $20) but worth it. Got in & out fast and ate well instead of pre-processed junk from the office.

I agree with Chrissy R.  The food is very, very good and high quality -but it's just not worth the price.  However, they do carry a startling assortment of gourmet chocolates and snacks.    The salad bar option allows you to try a small bit of the items that appeal to you.  They used to have a slew of designer cupcakes, too.  Not sure if they still do.

A lovely meal at Teresa's (not Next-Door - but we shall try that next - LOL). All the pastas can be made with spaghetti squash - so I had Spag. Squash in a beet sauce with a blob of goat cheese/mascarpone.  So decadent.  Basic - but just about the BEST Caesar salad I have ever tasted  5 stars for the romaine, baby!  Too full for dessert but the coffee and iced teas were great - and wow, what a list of WHISKEYS!

I agree with Eveline - and I too am writing this review based on grease-laden memories of my post-collegiate Chinese Truck experience.  I don't understand the love.  Food is (as said before) full of oil, onions and MSG.  Yech!  Oh - but it's really, really cheap.

I prefer to shop at the CVS or Walgreen's nearby, but in a pinch I have shopped at this Rite Aid.  I will also check here if for whatever reason CVS or Walgreen's does not have the item I am looking for.  It's OK but not my favorite and I never get prescriptions filled here.  Good in a pinch though.
Stopped in today at 7:40 AM and there was NO LINE. Do not come here over lunchtime (11:30 - 2 PM) or you will wait and wait on the line.  Got in and out quickly. No issues today.

This is a staple for us - as we can take our 3 year old daughter there and the plac is never that crowded.  She likes the fried chicken dumplings and we like the Tom Kha Gai soup.  As for the regular chinese style dishes - they are good but not outstanding.  The prices are reasonable - although they did go up last time we went in.  The Shu Mai are huge with lots of meat (pork, shrimp and fake-crab) filling - but I would not get that again.  I did enjoy the chicken with sugar snap peas.

Their donation policies seem more restrictive and inconvenient (when and what they will accept donations) than other SA or Goodwill stores.  I come here mostly to donate items - not to purchase.  Glad they are here, though.  Update:  The building was destroyed in a tragic Collapse in June 2013 - killing 6 people and injurying many more.  So sad.

El Vez gets 4 stars for the GUAC - not for the rest of the menu - which would get 3.  The guacamole hear really is tasty - although if you've tried the guac at Xochitl - which is made tableside with cotilja cheese fresh-ground to taste - WOWZA - but that's another review (check out Xochitl and Tequila's in Philly - regional Mex fare.)  Anyhow, back to El Vez which is filled-to-the-brim with Starr-kitsch.  Kitschy or not, this is a good place to get an over-priced fruity drink and schmooze with the yupsters.  I better go again before I turn 40 and get permanently banned from the joint!

This is my go-to Taxi service, and the dispatchers are lovely. (A woman on the weekend mornings, another woman during the week and a guy "Joel"? some evenings).  I did have an issue over 2 years ago with unreliability, but recently they've been great.  Just call 215-744-7777 and press 1 to reserve a cab.  Prompt, courteous service in the "Yellow & White" taxis.

I have watched it on TV and live in the freezing cold. Both are great fun - and this is one heck of a LONG parade.  It takes the whole day.  Nothing like watching Sou-filly plummers and electricians wear feathered headdresses and shake their butts to the beat.  My little girl ADORES them.  Fancy Brigades are my faves - and she loves the comics especially Froggie Carr's crew. Also Fralinger's and the South Philly Vikings!  Oh and the string bands are fun, too.

Huge portions of old-skool Jewish-style (not Kosher - they have shrimp salad and meat and dairy) deli food.  I had the Matzoh Ball Soup with Kreplach ($6.75 plus $ extra) and a Dr. Browns Cream Soda (diet) and was in retro heaven.  The clean, BRIGHTLY lit dining area was pleasant enough (when I went it was not crowded - dinner time)  and Claudine, my server was a doll.  Can't wait to go back.
They carry good quality products but the staff are space cadets.  (Sorry - you are nice but flakey).  I have never liked shopping in here and only came here due to its close proximity to the office.

A nice green space - which is sorely needed - in Center Ciyt.  It may not be as well known as Rittenhouse Square - but it is a fine park and lots of cool stores and restaurants are in the surrounding area.
Cheap gas.  Full Serve.  Center of Town.  WINNER!

This Acme (a larger one) is on my way to work so today I literally ran in and out at 7:20 AM for a quart of milk and box of instant oatmeal packets.  The place was nearly empty at that hour so it was no biggie. Friendly cashier, too.  No issues and I know I'll be back.

This is the Starbucks attached to Macy's. We really needed a "fix" so we stopped here on Black Friday and the place was crazed.  Meanwhile we got through the line and were duly caffeinated.  Glad it was there.

This is a nicely maintained dog park good for small, medium or large dogs.  If only my 13 year old pug could handle the walk - but he just can't make it that far.  We'll have to drive him over one day.
Tiny outpost (no seating/standing room) of Dunkin. Got an iced coffee here with no issues.  (Went during the summer at 8:20 AM)
Best in the City.  For real. Best Valet, door personel, securit, rooms, cleanliness, service and food.  GREATEST frikkin' food.  If you can stay here - or play here - DO IT!

Walked in, walked out. Crowded, poor service, mediocre food.  But it is convenient when you just NEED to sit down in RTM.  Asked for water several times. Tripped over strollers.  Not a fun experience at all. (Which is a shame because I LOVE Jack McDavid - not sure if he still has a hand in this biz,)

Kitchen gadget central.  Love it here - and great for wedding and shower gifts.  Kinda expensive - but many of these things just ARE expensive (like espresso machines and a sno-cone makers).  Fun place to shop and knowledgeable staff.

It's worth a visit here for the decor and architecture alone. Ring the bell and a nice gal will let you in.  Super-trendy fashions for men & women - and all made in the USA. I picked up a $135 top (Ouch) but 3 dots for $70 (Less painful but still high). Very cute stuff here.

Went for lunch with my 11 year old and we actually enjoyed it - but still there are flaws. Rice is not the right texture. Too hard and crumbly. Hwever, the salmon sushi (nigiri) we ordered was fresh and tast.  The "rich man" roll ($13) is basically a souped-up spicy salmon roll topped with MORE salmon.  I got the 2 sauces (A sweet mango syrup/sauce and eel sauce) on the side which was a good move.  Kiddo got a rainbow roll sans "fake crab" kani stick.  She hates fake crab.  Smart kid.  $11.  "Regular" rolls are $5.25 - and for that I'd just as soon get 2 Alaskan rolls for less that the cost of the "rich man".  Dessert ($4.50) was an overly greasy tempura banana.  El kiddo devoured it.  A decent place but there are better places closer to Media and even better in Philly.

The owners of the Wayside Market (and their 10 (yes, ten) children and staff are amazing people.  Great food - and a few staples like milk and drinks - plus a deli counter - oh and they make pizzas and calzones. And wings!  Catering - great. Eat-in area - so cute.  A very pleasant place and terrific customer service. Family friendly, too.

I'm not much for updates - especially if nothing has changed- but a friend & I had a nice lunch at Asia on the Parkway today.  It was exactly as it always has been.  Good vegetable dumplings.  Good Tom Kha soup.  Efficient service got us outta there in time for my friend to go back to "the foim".  Also - during the snow of 2010 we ordered delivery from Asia - and it was very good - and a life saver inour snow-bound state.  SKIP the shumai.  Get the chicken or veggie dumplings instead.

Sorry.  I am getting less and less impressed each time I go.  I have been thrice.  The first time (the best of the 3 - so I returned) I had some delicious and fresh rolls at lunchtime.  It was not crowded and service was good.    The second time I came I had a platter of sushi and it was not as fresh as it should be.  The last time I went - and I will not return, the service was just awful.  The $17.95 maki I ordered, while HUGE and containing ingredients I like, was dripping in 3 kinds of gloppy sauces.  Go easy on the sauce, guys.  Use fresher fish and pare down to basics.  Some things don't need tempura crunch AND eel sauce AND spicy mayo AND whatever that other glop was.

Went for lunch here with a friend today and the place was EMPTY save for the 2 of us.  We were treated extra-well due to this, I think.  We both had lunch specials - a very good value - and my sushi platter was super fresh and delicious.  The ramen here is good, too!  And we split vanilla mochi ice cream for dessert.  YUM!  I will definitely be back to try the specialty rolls.  (My sushi lunch was a yellowtail scallion roll - 8 bite size pieces and 5 nigiri.)

I am consistently underwhelmed by Pietros and thuis do not eat here often,.  There are much better places IMHO to get Italian-American food. They do make a decent pizza (but Rustica in Northern Liberties is much better) and serve large plated entrees of decent - not memorable - chicken, fish & veal.  The pasta was, indeed, al dente - which was a plus.  Service was fine - but it was crowded and very loud.  I don't like to sit outside - the whiff of auto exhaust from Walnut Street is not my idea of a fine dining al fresco experience, so we were trapped inside with the hoardes.  Don't go on a Friday night, is all I can advise. Maybe don't go - try Le Castagne instead.  (19 & Chestnut)

Oh, I really wish I could give this place higher marks - but I just can't. Meanwhile I have been here now a bunch of time - always for a weekday lunch because they have relatively quick service and are located near my office.  Meanhwile - try #75 & #81 (both burritos) off the lunch menu.  I get the #75 made with chicken instead of the beef tips, and I like it much better. Avoid the beef here - not great,  It seems to be coated with Cheese-whiz.  Weird - but oddly good.  The chips & salsa still kinda suck.  The chips tasted like bagged ones (slightly stale tasting) and the Salsa it kinda like jarred Old El Paso.  Disappointing, but yet we return again and again.  And it's still way better than La Tolteca.  And the service is friendly (and as I just said - quick.) Selene is very sweet.

Great diner food at a reasonable price served by lifer staff in a neighborhood institution.  Can get SLAMMIN' crowded on weekends at brunch time.  I like to go for dinner and have breakfast for dinner at Zoto's.  Fun stuff!

I have been here twice - the first time was when they first opened and it was great - maybe 4 stars.  We had $1.70 sliders and fabulous ginger & pineapple cocktails.  We sat on a sofa in a corner of the bar and had great service.  A few months later we went back - this time for Center City Sips.  The place was PACKED, the menu (food and drinks) had changed and the service was just awful. A 1 star experience.  Thus, I am giving them 2 stars and I will not return.

Sorry - but I have to pan the Body Klinic.  I would have given it 2 - or maybe even 3 stars when I had just been there for a pedicure - a guy named Michael did it and he was pretty good.  (Even though you have to sit on an uncomfortable wood block elevated and covered with throw pillows, posing as a couch.  The owner (receptionist or owner - I couldn't tell) was not nice to me at all.  Still, a gluuton for punishment I came back for a cheapie massage - I mean who can resist that price?  Resist.  Trust me.  It was a mediocre "fluff & fold".  Sorry - but I will not be back.

2 stars on a bad day - 3 on a good day? This one is way better than the FILTHY friendly's down 611.  Meanwhile, my 4 year old daughter simply MUST have the cone-head sundae, so my DH and I gave in and had lunch here.  It wasn't AWFUL - but it was very slow service and mediocre food that is really not good for you.  (Fried chicken fingers & burgers.)  Not a fan.  Sorry.

This is, indeed, a small outpost of Ann Taylor - but I did have good luck here on a few occaisions.  One - during a sale - i snagged alot of cute knit tops & sweaters at insanely cheap prices.  I also came here last week with a holiday gift card I received - and lo & behold - everything in the store was 40% off - so i got a nice petitie sized (thus no shortening or hemming required) "interview" suit.  Ann Taylor is a decent place to get work-a-day clothing.
Great buy 3 get free sale - scored 6 $6.00 items for less than $17.00 (I have a 10% off card also.)  If you buy smart and buy on sale - you can get some nice bath & body gifts here.

Another successful (yet a bit pricey) meeting at the Hub - this time in a smaller room.  Sandwiches and salad for lunch (thanks steven starr) were great and a nice selection of beverages throughout the day.  Comfortable, professional, business-y digs.  Clean restrooms.  If you have to suffer through another boring meeting or training class - try to do it here.

I discovered AOS back in like 2003 on Madison Avenue in NYC. Meanwhile, they have one in Philly so, back in 2008 when my then fiance (now husband) and I were in pre-wedding mode, I got him a gift certificate.
