He wound up getting a "Royal" shave and said it was great, but both he and I know he NEVER in a million years would spend that kinda money on himself.  So last year I got him another gift card. And I'll probably give him one next year, too.  We like it here.

4 -5 stars for the view alone.  They could serve old shoe leather (which some steaks kinda resemble) and it would still be a great ambience.  Meanwhile, as hard to believe as it is, Chart house is a CHAIN.  It is a such a nice place, though - and a great "special occaision" restaurant.  Just don't have a steak.  The salmon was excellent when I had it years ago. Come to think of it the steaks I also had quite a long while ago - perhaps they have a better beef supplier now.  But anyhow, yes I do recommend the Chart House - especially for Mother's Day (Father's Day) and birthdays.  It is just a joy in Spring and Summer.
I heart Sephora - I liked it even better when they first started in the '90's and had even more brands (probably too many) and harder to find items.  Love it.

I just went here on a RAINY horrid day for lunch and wound up getting it to go.  I had the Chicken Parm over linguine special.  (8.95)  It is delicious and HUGE, plus it came with a fresh hot garlic breadstick.  I can't wait to go back and try the pizza.

I absolutely agree with Zach.  I enter or exit this station several times per week and you have to use the Vine Street side.  Plus - what is the point of that token booth attendant if you can't buy tokens?  There is a change machine - but only for change - no tokens.  Meanwhile I am glad to live so close to a BSL stop, but some changes need to be made.
A fun place to poke around - neat clothing and accessories - but kinda snooty service and high prices kept me from actually buying anything.  Cute just the same.

I have attened numerous events here - mostly associated with Square 1682 - the restaurant, but also some in the hotel lobby (They have wine for the guests!).  Rooms are small - and not cheap - but it's a great location and a nice place to stay. Slick decor.  Note:  Check in is at 4 and your room may not be ready any earlier.

I am a GINORMOUS fan of Sugarfoot and eat here for lunch whenever I visit my firm's WIlmington office.  The tuna melts, chicken salad sandwich, salads (with goat cheese) and soup (Chicken & dumplings) are all top notch.  Eat in or take out.  It's all SOOOOOOO good.  Too bad they only do AM and lunch.  (No dinners.) Wilmington rolls up the sidewalks at 4:55 PM.  Great for in-office catering, too.

Absolute mediocrity - but at a very cheap price. (A typical case of "you get what you pay for".)  My 7 year old and I stopped in - for a polish change ($5) and a manicure for me ($10).  Since she got fidgety we both ended up getting polish changes.  Mine chipped right away - even though I coulda sworn she used CND basecoat (which is a great product).  DD chipped hers too - but that was her fault.  Not very clean (I would NOT get a $20 pedi here EVER.).  Not coming back.  Cheap and would do in a desparate pinch.

Such deliciousness!  We even contemplated having our wedding here.  (THey have a gorgeous private room for multi-course traditional (or modern) Chinese banquets.  A good selection of fresh sushi, too.  Tasty dumplings and soups.  WE LOVE IT HERE!  Gorgeous decor and attentive service. We'll return!

3.5 stars. - A decent breakfast place for the Diner Classics - and Eggs benedict with "hollandaise from a mix".  Big portions and OK prices. Surprisingly decent hot coffee - maybe I lucked out with a fresh pot?  Overly made-up servers (can you say black eye liner at 10 AM)? wearing support hosiery.  Nostalgic - and a darn sight better than Country Squire (Blech.)

I am optimistic about Gavin's - an Argentine-owned Euro-style cafe, right near Taney Park and sorely needed.  The original Irish Bar (from years ago now serves as the coffee bar.  We had some cold drinks here yesterday and I got a home-made beef empanada that was so delicious.  The salad menu sounds great, too.  This is sorely needed in this area and I hope they will be successful.  Go, Gavin's!

This is now my go-to Saladworks near my job. The ladies who run the lunch rush are so kind and friendly.  The salad is consistently good (fresh lettuce is a must for me) and I sometimes add on a cup of lobster bisque or Turkey Sausage/Kale soup on a cold day.  I come in about twice a month.

Really?  I am not impressed. And I am not easy to impress, so you may want to take that into account, but my late lunch on an EMPTY Saturday at 2:30 PM was just OK.  I had the sushi/sashimi combo (served with a california roll) and 1 piece of ikura.  The tuna sashimi was not as fresh as it should be. Tamago is frozen Rice was hard.  Absolutely unimpressed.  Sushi Nami in Paoli or Azie in Media are better (not to mention Doma and Zama in Center City).
We buy liquor here on occaision because it is convenient. I think the PA liquor laws are really strange and generally nonsensical.

Yes, it's both - a dine and a dive bar (in the back) complete with Sassy waitresses (I love "Sugar") and a great manager, Vi.  The place is grungy - and up until recently you could smoke there and nobody would hassle you.  Dem Daze R gone, Alas.  I really like coming here - breakfast is great, lunch specials and even for dinner.  The Chicken Cacciatore - if they have it as a special - is a must.  I love my Midtown.

I give much respect to our over-worked, over-stressed police department. They have alot of idiots to deal with - not to mention violent and non violent criminals - on a daily basis.  The police around 30th Street Station have been very helpful to me.  I support our law enforcement and fire fighters.

Yay!  Hooray! I got green juice today (paid extra for it though)!  I got a medium (16 oz) juice of Kale, Celery, Cucumber, Lemon, Green Apple and a bit of ginger for like $7 or so.  Plus I got wheatgrass on the side (2.95).  Ten bucks for juice.  Oy vey! But my body is so thanking me.

So. darned. expensive.  But I fall for it more and more now that my 5 foot 7 and still growing amazonian 13 year old figure skater has grown out of ivivva and wanta "higher performance" fabrice than VS's PINK.  Luxe. Pretty. Fun. A bit elistist.  And did I mentioned to bring some money? Even on sale it's pricey for workout togs.  But we love them anyway.

People have complained about my old review, so now i will simply say they make decent burgers & shakes.  Is it akin to Shake Shack in NYC?  I don't think it's nearly as good and the burgers are smaller.  Want more deets?  See grubstreet's write up.  It was perfect!
I came here for alterations - so I can't really comment on their cleaning services - but the lady who did my dress fitting was so friendly and nice.  Great workmanship. I will return.

This review is for the Print & Marketing center and Cory, in particular at the Glen Mills location.  I needed - of all things - a document to be laminated (people still do that??) and thank goodness for Cory and his help and advice.  We have also shopped at this Staples location for "back to school" supplies.  Glad it's here!

This is a review for the banquet room and facilities. We attended an event in a large room and there was an open bar area in the "lobby" which was also nice.  Area was clean and service was excellent from porters, servers, bar staff and more.  The catering manager was on hand and additional trash cans were brought right away when they were needed.  The renovations look very nice and continue - so there is still scaffolding in front of the hotel.  When it is done it will be better.  Very good service for a large (200 people) event.

Worse and worse every time we come. The firt time we had a great 4 star experience.  This last time?  Not so much.  And do NOT get take out here.  No beverages to go (other than sugar-laden Mexican Sodas).  No Diet Coke.  No take out cups.  Bottled water (IF they have it) is $2.25 per bottle.  Plus they got my order wrong - and I called 45 minutes before I needed it.  They are clearly not well equipped for take out.

Pretty much the only fast food place I will let my kid eat at. The kids meal with 4 nuggets, fresh fruit and lowfat milk is a pretty safe option.  You can get a grilled chicken sandwich (they charge extra for a whole wheat roll).  You can get a side salad but it's loaded with shredded cheese which I try to pick off.  I sometimes get a diet lemonade.  Not too bad.  But it's still fast food.

Kovacs doesn't look impressive from the outside, but the man who runs it is terrific and was very, very kind to my friend who used to walk here almost daily from his Media Station apartment.  A great place to grab snacks or a sandwich before catching a SEPTA train into Philly.  They also have grocery items, lottery tickets and COFFEE!  Kovacs' is a neighborhood institution.

Raw - the sushi & sake lunge from 12 & Sansom - opened a 2nd branch inside Boyd's Department store on the mezzanine level.  I just had lunch there today and for $13 it very well may be the only thing I can afford at Boyds!  Less of the snotty attitude, too.  Much quiter and more refined. I had a yellowtail bento box and the sushi and all of the elements (miso, salad, gyoza, and spicy tuna tartare) were all top-notch.  I'll be back soon!

Wowie Wow!!!  5 star food for sure and 4 for the service, value and decor.  Especially for lunch - the $7.50 - $850 pita sandwiches are so tasty and the gyro is made with reall meat - not "mystery meat from a spit".  The avgolemono souyp is delectable, piping hot and comforting.  The filet mignon souvlaki (small lunch portion) is the real deal with tasty chunks of filet.  Just wish there were a FEW more.  They also have outdoor seating on a covered deck for when the weather is nice.  GREAT FIND - thanks to my parents who have been coming here for years - but somehow I never had!  I sure will be back.

Chick-Fil-A Lima is very well run and has worked with my kid's elementary school many years now to organise fundraisers and family events.  There is a play area for the little ones, and even though I can not STAND the political views of the company's CEO, I was not able to boycott them, because they are the only fast food I will allow my child to consume.  The chicken sandwich (whole wheat bun available) is pretty good for a fast food option - and you can get fresh fruit instead of fries.  El kiddo also loves the mini cones (not so mini!) of "Ice Dream".

What a terrific store for jewelry and accessories.  Friendly service (not pushy) and oodles of beaded, silver and hand-crafted jewelry.  Purses/Back packs, scarves, hats, gloves and winter wear.  Headbands, bows and hair accessories.  Funny how I have never notice it before - it's only been here for 28 years! Right next to Fellini's on State Street.  Can't wait to do more gift shopping here - and pick up some things for myself and my daughter.  Bliss.

This is a review of the Ann Taylor LOFT location in Liberty Place.  (There is also an Ann Taylor - non loft - on Walnut street a few blocks down.  LOFT is a the lower-end "casual" line put out by Ann Taylor - and for me it's better in the spring & summer than in the winter.  Moderately priced "corporate casual" duds that are moderate quality.  It's hit or miss for me - for whatever reason I do better at the "regular" (and higher priced - but not during a sale)  Ann Taylor.

I don't listen often - but the weather and traffic are repeated often and in a predictable fashion. Yes, I agree with below that the ads are LOUD and annoying. Methinks I shall never shop at the DUMP just on principle.  (They also advertise on WMKJ - 102.9 - which is my favorite station.  (Especially in HD.)  Anyhow - Philly needs you, KYW - so keep on keepin' on.  Oh - and in winter - please repeat the school closing numbers more often.

So glad we finally got to try La Porta - and especially the 5 star Caprese - one of the best I have had in a long, long while.  Home-made Mozz - so creamy; A drizzle of "the good stuff" - aged balsamic; red, ripe, roma tomatoes; basil chiffonade.  SUPERB.  The lasagna was so rich I almost could not eat it.  (Although others I know would swoon over this.)  An excellent meaty bolognese - but the creamy sauce on top was just too much.  Delicate house-made pasta sheets.  Topped with a fried egg that was, alas, oddly cooked (Thus precluding me from awarding LaPorta the fifth star).  The egg was, indeed, fried = the bottom was actually crispy and brown - the top?  Raw.  Not runny (which I like) but raw albumin over the yolk.  Slimy.  Not good.  Meanwhile the 2 pizzas our  table tried (Malfatta - neat! and a classic Margarita) were excellent.  Lots of love and care goes into this food and it shows.  LOVE IT and will return soon.  But I'll try other things (like the salads which sound great) that are not quite so rich and heavy.  Gorgeous bar area and a rustic older dining room, too. Lizzy - our server - and a brand-spankin'-new bus boy were pleasant and friendly.  Good job, Peter!!!!! Welcome to suburbia.

Fabulous service at the bar during Happy Hour from Paul and later Hailey.  $5 White Cosmos were terrific.  $7 mini tuna tartare was a tasty treat.   Skip the deviled eggs, the ones at Paramour are better.  A nice change of pace from my usual. I will be back!

I stopped at this Starbucks in a state of latte-emergency. I desperately needed a caffeine pick me up and this location at 5:30 PM on a Friday was nearly empty so I got in and out quickly.  Staff was friendly and restrooms were clean (enough).  No issues. Thankful they are here.

We had a marvelous first-time experience for lunch on a Wednesday at the Metro Diner on Concord Pike - just South of the PA state line. Our server Eddie was terrific and later the manager, Isaac, came over to see how things were.  (Everything was great - believe it or not.)  One of us is vegetarian (not vegan so eggs are OK, this is not a vegan place - lots of eggs and dairy) and she had a veggie wrap (huge - took 1/2 home) with Avocado and the "usual" suspects but also with FRIED JALAPENOS - inside the wrap.  Wow.  I had a "trying to cut carbs" eggs Benedict so - no English muffin and plain steamed spinach instead of potatoes.  $13.29 (no tax, baby, we're in DE).  I am sorry others did not have a good experience, but honestly, we had a great lunch and I can't wait to return.  (That divided highway, though...)

2 to 2.5 stars at best.  What a disappointment. A close friend and I had been planning dinner here for over 2 months. We finally got to go and the food just isn't up to par (or the high prices - $22 - $45 for entrees!).  We started our meal with delicious fresh bread and garlic-infused oil.  (That and the after-dinner coffee were the best bites of the night!)  I love a good caprese salad and was thrilled when "Fresh tomato and buffalo mozz" was a featured special ($12).  My friend and I split it - and the tomatoes were HARD - deli-quality slicing tomatoes.  This - in the middle of August when tomatoes are plentiful - is a sacrilege!  Also - who serves this over iceberg lettuce?  ICEBERG?  On a Caprese?  Blah!!!  Our server Leo tried to please us - but the entrees fell flat. My entree was OK (albeit very over-salted) - al dente linguine with about a doze steamed littlenecks in a garlicky, salt-bath of oil.  My friends "veal saute" was a joke.  While the veal was tender, the sauce was a bland concoction of greasy-oily floury blandness.  It was supposed to be a "light white wine sauce" and no wine or flavor was detectable.  We skipped dessert and had 2 very nice cups of $3 coffee.  I would not go back here. "Founded in 1990" - looks like they have not renovated since 2002.  FAIL!  Such a shame.

Not the greatest service - and the place is, indeed, packed with stuff - Hockey Skates galore. I was able to consign a $404 pair of figure skates in excellent condition.  I asked $200, got offered $100 - which I reluctantly accepted.  I just wanted to get rid of them.  So after the 50%/50% comission I pocketed exactly $50.  Better than nothing. And better than the $22 they offered to buy them from me outright.

I received good service at Watch Co. when having my husband's watch band and battery replaced.  Mattie (sp?) the lady at the front was very kind and I got in and out of there quickly and the watch works great.  A nice selection of Citizens Eco-Drive, too.

I have always supported food coops, CSA's farmers markets, Natural food stores and the like, so I was delighted to find Weaver's way.  In amongst the crowded, cramped, narrow aisles - along with farm-fresh local produce (much in season - less in the winter) are other treats.  Honey.  Peanut Butter.  Fresh Eggs (with round deep yellow yolks), and a nice selection of snacks and prepared foods.  If I lived in the neighbordhood I'd be joining for sure!

Without Whole Foods and Trader Joe's I'd be sunk. So, Whole Foods - I am be-whole-den to you.  High prices and all - what choice do I have?  My child must have chemical-free, persticide-free, herbicide-free non Genetically Modified organisms on which to feed.  That meat case is impressive!  As are the baked desserts.  The juice bar is a saviour - and sushi never hurts!  O, Whole Foods - how I love thee - though parking really sucks. A least they'll validate the lot and save me a few bux.

I love CVS - but this branch is RIDICULOUS.  The line is always long, clerks unfriendly (better at the pharmacy - but the "front line" is atrocious.   I consider it a neccessary evil, as this is the only CVS near my office. (ANd they do have everything I need - usually higher priced  but, Oh well.
This station is far more disgusting than the one at Race/Vine. It reeks - especially in the summer (I don't wanna know).  Definitely scary!
Very good ice cream - not withstanding the long lines that are par for the course at the RTM - my 4 y.o. dd loves Bassett's and as an occaisional special treat we get her a small cone.
A-may-zing. So good.  For $3.75 I got an excellent iced decaf latte.  Perfect. Gorgeous setting, great service and smooth, rich-tasting coffee drinks.  YUM!

The spa itself should be a 4 star place, but there are too many cracks showing in the proverbial armor.  Firstly, I should mention that my facialist, Amanda, was very nice and knew her stuff when it came to basic skincare and Aveda products.  Because they are an Aveda spa - they are forced to use this line - and while many of the products are good, a few are just not worth it.  Amanda "played it straight" and did not try to sell me un-needed products.  The massage therapist, Tracy, seemed great, too.  I did not have a massage today - but may come back to work with Tracy.  Locker room was clean and nice.  There was NO WATER in the glass-windowed wiating room.  It does seem a little weird to be waiting around in your robe and people in the pool can see you.  Also, nobody even mentioned to me that there was a pool and hot tub - ort else I woulda brought my suit and planned to arrive early or stay afterward.  DRAT.  Oh well.  Maybe next time.    4 stars for Amanda.  3 for the way the place is run.  Get it together, ladies!

Not sure why - but the Philly outpost of crumbs seems a bit... ...Stale?  Maybe it's because nothing is baked on premises.  It's all trucked in from NYC.  Walked in - excited to see a Crumbs (like those in NYC) here in Philly. The large cupcakes are way too much for one person - and many have an overload of toppings. I tend to stay with the "Squiggle" or simpler versions.  Meanwhile - the cake pops on display (push up pops?) looks so artificially colored it was off putting.  Stick with the mini cupcakes.  A better size and price point.  And the front of the store is EMPTY - you have to walk in and THEN you see the counter.  A plus? You can get your favorite over-priced fourbucks aka Starbucks latte or mocha.

Returned to La Porta for 5 star food and service but oh  - so many flies!!!! You need to do something about the black fly population inside and out on the patio (which is lovely, otherwise).  Tracey our server is terrific and the Caprese Salad (with August-ripened Heirloom tomatoes) was perfection and the house-made spinach gnocchi were terrific.  Can't wait to come back - but please get a bug zapper!

This has been my go-to Whole Foods for a while now - sometime I will trek to Glen Mills or Plymouth Meeting.  I know the layout of this WF better than others so I can get in, get what I want, and leave relatively quickly.   Also if you go after 7:30 PM or before 8 AM it is much less crowded. Avoid lunch hour and the after-work rush.  (Although - lots of these yoga-pants ladies look like they don't work.  Must be nice.)  Chi-Chi Devon location with prices and attitudes to match.  (Attitudes from the patrons - not the hipster staffers.)

Got a large group that likes to drink? Need some "safe" food choices? Want a private room?  Then, G. A. P. is your place.  I came here with a group of 27 people and we were easily accomodated in a private room (with our own bar and buffet area) and service by Michele was excellent.  The drinks during happy hour are cheap enough - 1 beer and 1 well-tequila margarita ran me $7.  The food is fine.  Chicken or Eggplant parm, penne marinara, veggies and over-cooked roast beef with rolls and horseradish.  Not great but not awful either.  Very "safe" and everyone enjoyed the dessert tray with brownies, pound cake (looked like Sara Lee) and mini canolli.  We had a great meeting and would definitely have events here again.  There is even an old-fashioned ballroom (seats up to 150, I think) huge with it's own dance floor and restrooms - suitable for a down-scale wedding or a bir rehearsal dinner or graduation party.  This place is HUGE and has many configurations for groups large, small and massive.

A beautiful new store next to the Whole Foods in Wayne - with a good amount of sparkling wines and vodkas (That's what I needed on the day I shopped).  Decent prices (But face it, this is PA - if you want good prices on Liquor you go to NJ or DE and sneak it back in your trunk.  Happy to have a nice place to buy booze.

This Acme (a larger one) is on my way to work so today I literally ran in and out at 7:20 AM for a quart of milk and box of instant oatmeal packets.  The place was nearly empty at that hour so it was no biggie. Friendly cashier, too.  No issues and I know I'll be back. This is the Acme on Rt. 252 near Rt. 30 in Paoli.

I was treated to lunch here today by a coworker and had the salmon lovers ($13) special.  6 pieces of sashimi (I asked for all sashimi as I am trying to cut carbs and they complied.) and a [mild] spicy salmon roll.  Also came with choice of miso soup or iceberg salad.  I got the salad with the ginger/sweet (carb) dressing on the side.  Service from Rebecca was excellent and the place was not crowded on a random Tuesday at 12:15 PM.  I will return when my sushi/Asian craving hits next.

Friends don't let friends drink Charbucks. Try Caffe Maida for some first-class real-deal Italian Espresso drinks, and delicious gelato and pastries (mostly Bindi - but still fine).  I had an iced coffee (pretty basic, I know) and it was terrific.  Clean digs (including the restroom) and Viceland on TV.   I was so pleased.
They are CLOSED!!!!

2.5 stars - I am giving them the benefit of the doubt. I stopped in here early one morning because it is across the Street from Penn Medicine where I had an appt.  Good a simple bagel with cream cheese.  Nothing special, nothing horrific either.  Glad they were around.

I do not get the appeal of Outback.  My parents and inlaws love it. I do not find it worth "the wait" (and on weekends there is always a wait) and the food is very "blah".  I had a ribeye and a baked sweet potato (told them not to put the butter and brown sugar glop on it) and it was OK but sertainly not on par with a fine steakhouse.  The wedge salad was covered in 2 dressings (balsamic glaze AND blue cheese) - thank goodness I had them on the side.  Plus it comes with bacon, blue cheese crumbles and onions which I omited.  A big old hunk of FAT on top of a wedge of iceberg.  Yick.  That said, our 7 year old ate evey one of her 4 kiddie-meal BBQ ribs plus ate every last bite of the (well-buttered) broccoli. They also make a surprisingly good mac-a-roo and cheese (penne in a creamy cheese sauce).  I am not a big fan - but for family dinners - it beats Applebee's.

If you need to plan a business event or function - the hub is a good place to know about - they can accomodate the business and social components with A/V and wireless computer capability plus catering by Starr.  Between the giant screens, the configurable tables and chairs and the enormous cookie and brownie trays i would say all in all that the hub is a pretty sweet place for meetings. (Even boring CLE classes.)  Pretty Sweet!
Dee M.  said it best - and I agree. Cheap gas just over the DE border, plus all the Wawa usuals.

This section of the city is a great mix of old, historic Americana and new, hip trendy boutiques, galleries and restaurants.  It's lots of fun on First Friday - and good for families in the spring & summer, too.  A nice place to visit and live.

OMG - I'm gonna do it.  I'm gonna go all out and give Fri. Sat. Sun 5 well deserved stars.  Tonight was my innaugural experience here - and (even with no reservation - on a Sunday night) we got a great table.  We had 2 lovely female servers and everything my friend (a fellow yelper) and I ate was just wonderful.  We both started with salads.  She had the Goat cheese, walnut and mixed greens, I had the beet and fresh fennel salad - and subbed goat for bleu cheese.   My salad was truly dreamy - and almost like eating 3 salads in one.  It was artfully presented ring-mold style with the top layer (salad No. 1) being a mache mix in a light and PERFECTLY balanced vinaigrette (just the right blend of acid and oil).  Under the mache layer was salad #2 - a crunchy, cold layer of shaved fresh fennel with (again) the perfect dressing ratio.  Now - you must understand that I am the quintessential "on the side" kind of gal.  I almost always ask for dressings and sauces "on the side" - but here I did not - and I am glad.  The salad was PERFECTLY dressed.  Around the edge of the plate was sub-salad number 3 - sliced, sweet, red beets and toasted pine nuts.  This salad was worth every blessed penny of the $12.  For an entree I chose a "small plate" (which was not small -more like medium size) of 8 butternut squash filled ravioli in a delectable brown butter and sage sauce.  (Not diet friendly - but I asked for light on the sauce and it was not too heavy).  The pasta was tender and perfectly cooked and every bite was delicious.  For dessert we shared a (dated, I know - but this one was awesome) molten lava cake, served with 2 generous blobs of home-made whipped cream - each topped with a strawberry fan.  2 cups of coffee later (the house blend is custom roasted for Fri. Sat. Sun. and it is yummy) we were so darned happy!  What a wonderful evening.  The ambience (this is a GREAT date place, dimly lit, romantic vibe), music (mellow '60's), service and food were all TOP NOTCH.  This ain't no Garces/Starr/Industrial place.  It's not slick.  It's an urban townhouse rest-o and as Arnold Schwartzenager might say...  "I'l be baaack..."  I can't WAIT to go back.

I was STARVIN' like marvin after a fabulous pedicure at Spa Elysium (see my yelp review of that, too.) and needed sustainance.  I considered a few other plkaces - including the French Cafe which was so packed and disorganized that I had to bail out.  (Will yelp that soon.) So I cautiously entered this PACKED pizza spot (1 PM on a gorgeous Spring Saturday) and ordered a single slice of silician pizza topped with eggplant.  YUM CITY!  So delicious.  I would like to come back and try more things - just not on a Saturday at lunch time.

OK - I am upgrading corner bakery cafe for their excellent work with catering. No, the food isn't all that wonderful - but it's better than lots of others we've had.  The cavatappi pasta salad (side) is great and the breads for the sandwiches are fresh and not sogged-out.  Nice presentation and better yet - they arrive on time and don't cost alot.  (Hot pasta meal for 8-10 is $90.)

For whatever reason the food seemed better this time as we watched our child's figure skating competition. We had lunch AND dinner here - including a decent cheesesteak quesadilla.  Wings were overcooked and dried out. French Onion Soup is not tasty - had a weird acidic component.  But - the Fish Sandwich ($8) with fries was good.  Counter service and a full bar. Friendly staff.
OK, I am upgrading the Liberty Place Ruby Schmoozeday's.  The new mini burgers are edible and my husband digs the Cheddar Burger here.  But again - I never eat here on my own volition.

I have known rebecca Michaels since she got her start as a pastry artist in NYC - and I knew her ex husband, too.  How wonderful that we both relocated to Philly just a few months apart.  Her Vermont Cheddar Apple Cake was served way back when at my party on the Upper East side - and now I can just walk over to RTM (Reading Terminal Market) for a blondie or a cupcake whenever I want.  (Diet permitting.)  I wish Rebecca and Flying Monkey all the success in the world!  Keep on baking, ladies (and gent.).  Oh - she used to make great chocolate truffles, too.  Don't know if they are offered these days.  Don't miss the specialty cupcakes.  WOW!!!  She gives Buttercup and Magnolia (bakeshops in NYC) a run for their money.  Go, Monkey, go!!!!

This is a review for Rastelli Direct (rastellidirect.com) a direct marketing website where you can purchase "restaurant quality" frozen meats and foods.  The good - everything is beautifully packaged and individually flash-frozen and vacuum packed.  I enjoyed my veal-leg slices and could cook just ONE at a time which was great.  The also ship right to your door with plenty of dry ice.  The website is easy to use and your friend (whoever refers you) gets 5% credit from your purchase.  The bad - in order to get the prices to drop from ridiculously expensive to insanely high, you either have to join as a Rastelli Consultant (minimum monthly order requirement) or join the "Smart Shopper" program - which drops the price 20%.  Still too damned high.  And they try to lock you in to a monthly auto-ship feature.  Oh and the $19.00 (about $16 after the discount) Steamazing frozen entrees (2 for 16 is ridiculous still) were glorified lean cuisines.  No thanks, Rastelli.  The quality just does not justify the price.  (They have to build in comissions for your upline.)  I will order again - but not every month.  No way. My steaks are gonna continue to come from Omaha.

My high review is because of Larisa, the lovely russian nail tech who did my spa pedi and mani at Ettore.  I succumbed to th temptation of "spa week" and got the spa pedi and regular mani - usually 52 + 17 - for $50.  That's a good deal!  The salon has 2 pedi thrones in tiny roomettes, plus 3 mani tables.  The place was bustling-crowded as it was a Saturday AM and the hotel had alot of weddings.  The salon itself seems OK - the front desk needs to be more attentive and friendly - when I arrived a man was at one counter (on the phone) and a lady was at the "payment" counter with another person.  Neither acknowledged me for several minutes - until I waved at the guy on the phone.  He gave me the "just a 'sec" look.  Oh well.  Other than that it's clean, hotel prices (tourist spot) and I will be back to see Larisa for sure.  Great pedi!

It's been YEARS since my kid - now a teen - has begged for fro-yo but we found an ancient Sweet Frog gift card and it still is valid so - YAY. Cookies and Cream for me and my vegan teen (They had 3 vegan options) had the dole-whip Pineapple (no dairy).  A plethora of candy toppings and fruits.  $6 for both of us (small cups).

Epic Fail and so incredibly scary. I literally walked in - was greeted by an Asian woman who was reading a newspaper and the cases had only canned and frozen product.  Many cases are empty.  The place is clearly failing and there is a sign that says "No Eating".  So clearly, they don;t want you eating here.  take out only.  Dirty. Abandonned. Icky.  Just. Plain. Bad.  Thankfully, no relation (at least not in decades) to the fabualour Lobster Claw in Doylestown.  That place rocks.  This place?  Rock-bottom.

Oh the Bon ton!  (In my mind it still is Hess's)  An all-purpose old-style department store right in the D-town shopping center.  You can get women's, men's and kids clothes and shoes here.  Accessories, hats, household goods and of course - cosmetics.  There is a Clinique counter, Estee Lauder - the works.  And if you read the Daily Mistake (I mean, the Daily Intelligencer, you can get coupons and come during one of their fabulous sales.)  Recently I bought a party dress for my 3 year old daughter here - a top designer in children's clithing - marked down from $110 to $59 - but I came with a sale coupon and walk out with it for $36.00  Gotta LOVE the Bon Ton.

Delicious 5 star hoagies - so good (and I don;t even like hoagies). Chicken Suprimo, Bada-Bing, Nonna's Veggie and the new Meatball Sub are all winners.  Alas, one star off for the super-high price.  My wrap  was 8.99 plus $1 extra for subbing eggplant for red peppers.  2 subs and a small mac salad was almost $20.  Ee-gads!  Meanwhile, our kid likes it here, too.

A lovely - albeit pricey - lunch at La Porta.  Anything they make with their house-made mozzarella (or scamorzza or burratta) is amazing.  If you are a fan of fresh mozz - you must try it here.  We had the special salad of the day - a summery mix of lettuce, fresh burratta (decadent) red and golden beets and sliced peaches.  LOVELY.  The blackberry balsamic was perfect for it.  I added shrimp to mine (which made the $13 salad go to $20).  I really do enjoy the food here.

The best diner in my area. A bit pricey - my salmon salad was $15.95 - ouch.  Breakfasts come in around $10 for omelettes or pancakes with toppings/fillings/sides.  My kid had a gyro platter with onion rings subbed in (upcharge!) for fries.  Soda was $2.45.  Bill for 4 people for lunch was $70.  Yikes.

5 star food and 3 or 4 star service for this update on Peter Mac's delightful La Porta on route 352 in Media.  Ate here for the first time in over a year and the late spring/summer menu is wonderful with crisp salads, pizzas, pasta and rich, flavorful entrees.  My pork cutlet stack with fresh mozz, spinach and peppers was so delicious and a generous portion.  I took about 1/3 home and enjoyed it the next day.  The bar was hoppin' on a Monday night and my Cranberry Moscow Mule was served icy-cold in the requisite copper mug.  Deeeee-licious.  Can't wait to come back.

OK, 3 strikes and I'm OUT!  Outta Tavern 17.  The weird (slightly older, short, surly) bartender treated me very strangely - kinda like I have a stick up my a$$ or something.  Anyhow - I hemmed and hawed a bit as to whether or not to even order alcohol (And bartenders don;t care for this), and ordered an iced tea.  (No, not a long island one - a regular brewed one).  It was nearly BLACK.  Overbrewed.  He nearly went ballaistic when I dained to ask for Splenda and mocked me a bit.  I guess I deserved it.  I also ordered two of the $1 sliders.  For a buck - they are well worth it and 2 (or 3 if I am absolutely starving) is perfect.  The best part of the night?  Tish (Leticia) the lovely hostess who got us extra chairs and gave me the ladies room key twice (I pee freely.),  Note ladies:  It's a long trek to the ladies room.  Also note: it's been recently renovated (The loo, that is).  All in all, had my friends not picked this place (I swear, twas not my idea) I woulda never set foot in the joint.  Sorry, Mickey or Mikey or whatever your name is...  Tish - you rock.  You deserve a BIG raise!

Wow!  Swanky renovations in 2017 include a REAl in-store Starbucks (Yes, you can use your Starbucks app or card) and re-done ladies room (THANK YOU).  Nice new floors in the deli and prepared food areas.  Still a great spot to get some cheap sushi for lunch. I come in a few times each week on my way to work.

OK - they are probably only worth 4 stars but nostalgia and YEARS of knowing the Gross family (Harry Gross is long dead - RIP) and many people who worked here - when D-town was a much, much smaller town.  The fried and oven roasted chicken are mouth-wateringly delicious.  They also make very heavy (but I think tasty) potato salad and cole slaw.  YUMMY all-white meat Chicken salad, too.  VERY expensive for what it is - picnic food - but we love to get take out meals from Gross'.  Years ago you could get the most amazing frozen meat (and cheese - but I liked the meat better) ravioli here, too - but alas, no longer.  Want a neat idea for a quick picnic?  Don't feel like cooking?  Like tasty chicken?  Try Gross'.  It's NOT at all gross.

Tim and Bob at the bar gave my friend and I top-tier service during Thursday night happy hour - and happy, indeed, we were.  The $7 wedge salad was so good we ordered 3 of them between us. Burrata (also $7) was rich and served with what appeared to be a whole tomato.  Once cut open, the tomato had been cored and stuffed with a delicious pesto.  Interesting presentation.  The tuna tartar is still on the bar menu ($10) but has been re-vamped and is better than ever.  Drinks are just $5 for the delicious sweet-tea-like Daly Pear and the always tasty William B. Pitt Mule (A Szuszhed-up Moscow Mule with Cinnamon and other spices) were terrific.    Can't wait to come back. The decor and great, great music (pop, rock, classic and hits) make this place just about "As good as it gets".

Just AWFUL.  I mean it. Zero stars if it were possible. We have come here exactly twice in the 4 years we've lived in Philly (we usually make a bi-monthly pilgimage to Target nearby.).  The first time we came - we didn't know any better.  Shopped for our "usual" stash of baby supplies and paper goods and got the hell outta dodge.  It was like shiopping in the hood.  So "ghetto" and very piggy patrons screaming at each other and tearing up the merchandise.  The 2nd time we went only becuase I wanted to by a Max Factor products supposedly carried only at Wal-Mart. They did have the product - and I bought 2 and vowed to never return.  Sooooooo bad. Make the "ghetto Kmart" look great and makes Target look like Bloomies.

Sashimi is the true litmus test for a sushi spot and Jasmine is just fair. Red Snapper was obviously a previously frozen fish (still had ice crystals).  Escolar?  really?  Ick.  The tuna and salmon were fine.  Good service and decent maki, but for a true sushi connoisseur, this is not your spot.  But hey - you're in DELAWARE.  So for that it's still pretty darned good.  Next time I stick to the basics.  I come here about once a month.

Super-fast, cheap take out lunches - you can't really eat here comfortably.  There are a few stools and a counter, but the place gets crowded (line out the door) at lunch.  Love tha Tom Kha Gai (Chicken Coconut Soup). Red Curry is fairly spicy (to my taste).  Tofu is fried - but delish! $6 combo plates to go are good but the fresh-cooked entrees are even better.  You get your choice of pad thai or fried rice with 1 to 2 entrees on top (from the steam table).  I tried a unique deep-fried egg half with tamarind sauce.  Neat.  Tip:  For better quality food than the $6 steamtable, call in your order - today I got $2.50 Tom Kha with soft tofu and a fresh order of pineapple fried rice $6.95.  Cost more than the $6 special but fresh, hot and cooked to order.  MUCH better.

Returned to Teresa's on a balmy, busy, summer Thursday night for a delightful plate of eggplant, spinach and cheese.  So good.  I always like the food here - both sides are good but different. Lots of alcoholic choices, too!

I had a fine experience my first time at this Saladworks.  There were 3 women working the counter during the lunch rush on a random Thursday.  There was a short-to-medium line and it moved quickly.   They offered about 8 soups (my old Saladworks offers only 3 or 4) and I got a Cobb Salad with Turkey instead of chicken and Brussels Sprouts instead of Bleu Cheese.    No issues.  Dining room was medium-crowded (we got a table and were not packed in).    Did not use rest room. Plenty of parking.  I will be back.

Yes, it's cheap (especially if you get the $6 steam table - and especially if you show up at 11:30 or so when everything is fresh), but it's not that great somehow.  I ordered the Coconut Soiup (with Tofu instead of Chicken or Shrimp) and today is was bland.  One-note coconut milk.  So disappointing.  I also got Pad-See-Yew (wide noodles with chinese brocolli and dark soy with scrembled egg and tofu (I got soft tofu instead of a meat or fried tofu.)  Good but also bland.  Next time I will come on a Friday - the only day they serve Masaman Curry - and stick to the $6 steam table.  The $10 I blew on a (huge) lunch today wasn't worth it.  But at least I won't need to cook dinner.

Beautiful furniture - and a huge variety of desks (need a corporate or lawyer-type desk?  Or a conference table/dining table - come here!).  Decent prices - and a few leather sofas and sectional.  BIG bedroom sets (ornate - and not our style - but beautiful wood.)  Need WOOD furniture that looks terrific and is well finished?  Head over here.  Neat place. We were pleasantly greeted and allowed to browse on our own - which was perfect! (Not too pushy.)

While the Midtown IV is my fave, the Midtown III (Different owners) is a few bloacks way and is a bit less grungy and good for a cheap quick breakfast or lunch.  The waitresses here just aren't as sassy as at the IV, but it is still the "diner" experience.  God Bless the American Diner.  We need it, we love it!

This is the Cosi by Barclays and well, it's THERE. So that gives it a star by default.  This area is a "trapped" for lunch scenario. You need coffee?  An overpriced faux-puccio?  That weird bread they serve?  Never been a Cosi lover but this one is a necessary evil. And in a pinch - you can interview here too.

I can't believe I have NEVER been to a Bonefish Grill before, but I have not. And I will be back.  A little pricey for what it is (Chain - owned by Outback), but very tasty. Nice atmosphere. Great for my daughter's friend's 12th birthday dinner.

For happy hour (4 - 6 PM) the $5 drinks are a great value. The blueberry lemon drop martini is like candy in a glass.  Lovely.  Also enjoyed the Cobb salad with shrimp.  Good service from Jess.  We'll be back!

I was turned off after my last lunch here so I did not return for a while but now, I am glad I did.  The Thai Basil stir fry (I chose chicken but you can get beef, shrimp or veggie or tofu) is delicious and inexpensive as a lunch special (back page of menu).  I also had some sashimi but stuck to salmon and tuna which were fine.  The escolar, snapper and hamachi here taste slightly "fishy" to me - and hamachi especially can taste "off" if it is not uber-fresh.  Lots of pre-frozen product in that sushi case, but hey, it's Wilmington, DE - not NYC or LA or Tokyo.  This is a good option for pan-Asian near my office.

Ten or eleven years later and nothing has changed - save for the prices which are a tad higher.  Old-school Greek-Owned and operated diner with American Classics (good for eggs and bacon - even for lunch) and old-pro waitress that say "What'll it be, hon?".  The food is exactly what you might expect and the décor is straight outta 1974.  "Gimme a whiskey down,  two on a raft, Mac."

I just don't know WHY so many people in opur office love this place?  They rave about the ham on pretzel bread (MEH).  They rave about the salads (MEH).  They even rave about the Cinnamon cream cake - and while it does taste awesome - a "serving" is over 1100 calories.  No thanks.  I'll walk across the Street to the snob-cast center instead for some local (NOT!) goodies from La Scala.  It's OK - but it's just MEH.

My first experience at Yummy sushi was actually quite, well, yummy.  It was a busy lunch rush, so I sat at the sushi bar and ordered the $13 sashimi lunch special with a choice of salad or miso soup.  Sashimi, to me, is the litmus test for any sushi bar.  Yummy passed!  My plate had 3 slices of 4 fish and all were fresh and good, no fishy odor. Tuna, salmon, and 2 white fish I am guessing were sea bass or fluke. It was not yellowtail. It was not escolar (fake white tuna).  Salad was the standard iceberg with ginger dressing that many places serves. Also fresh, crispy and good.    I will be back as this place is steps away from my office and relatively cheap.  Yay!

It seems much like the Vic's in Philly - but different owners.  Similar menu - and best of all TUNA DUMPLINGS - you gotta try these - so delicious.  I also got a sashimi sampler (app) with 2 pieces of tuna, salmon and yellowtail.  All were fresh and delicious.  $12 minimum for credit cards.

Huge!  Massive! And relatively clean.  We were fortunate to visit on a realtively non-crowded day and time (2 PM on a Sunday).  The A/C felt wonderful and our 5 y.o. enjoyed the movie and sat still for the entire show.  Yay!

Why on earth suburbanites PACK this place (with kids, also) is beyond me. We came here when we were out of other ideas and the wait at Grand Rodeo was 45 minutes.  Well, the wait here was 45 minutes also (even though we were told it'd be 20-25 minutes.)  Literally THRONGS of people.  Avoid on a Saturday night at all cost. Mediocrity served in enormous portions with a side of bovine growth hormone.  I'll pass.  But I bet somebody will drag me back here.

It will be hard to write a captivating review without re-stating many of the sentiments already expressed below, but I shall try...  Last night we went to Buddakan Philadelphia (there are now 3 locations) which is celebrating 11 years in operation.  Surprisingly, even after living in Philly for nearly 4 years and trying tons of restaurants, this was our first visit.  Years back we visited and peeked inside to see the amazing Golden Buddha and the waterfall wall fountain. I had read the menu many times on the website - so I felt like I knew what to expect.  (N.B. they will be CHANGING the drink menu and dinner menu in a few weeks - finally.)  Decor and Service were easily 5 star, but there are too many small details overlooked for me to give Buddakan that elusive fifth star.  (As Starr restaurants go, this is pretty typical in that there is some over-hyping going on - but for a restaurant like this to survive and thrive for 11 years - an eternity for a restaurant - they are doing alot of things right!)  We started with $11 - $13 drinks at the nearly empty  bar (from 5:30 - 6:10 on a recession summer Thursday - it got crowded around 8).  The enlightenment was too strong with tequila for me to drink, so I sent it back and tried the tickled pink which was cloyingly sweet and the Malibu rum was not a great idea.  Oh well.  Meanwhile the ASIAN MOJITO was well-balanced, with freshly muddled mint, a hint of ginger and delicious.  (NOTE:  THey are changing the drink menu in a few weeks - many of these cocktails have been on the menu for years and it's all gonna change.)  Next the 3 of us sat at a great table on the main level (there is also a cute bar upstairs and more tables.).  One of us is a vegan and there are very few vegetarian options (and NO vegan apps! The edamame ravioli uses chicken stock)  He had vegetable fried rice (or could have had noodle dishes or the house salad.)  If you are a vegan - this is not a great place for you - unless you just want some drinks.  Everything is served family style with sharing plate s- which for us is great as we all like to share (execpt my vegan friend who, natch, would not eat the fish or duck).  Chicken Dumplings were a step up from the frozen gyoza we get at our favorite sushi joints.  Tasty for sure - but not worth $9.  A scallion pancake topped with shredded shortrib meat was enjoyed by DH but way too salty for my tastes.  A miss at $12.  Entrees were much better.  The miso black cod, that was so famous, lived up to most of the hype.  Perfectly cooked.  I subbed a DELICIOUS eggplant in lieu of the wasabi mashed potatoes.  That eggplant was GREAT - reminiscent of Kung Pao - it was studded with Pine Nuts.  YUM!  DH ordered the thinly sliced duck breast - a bit too well done for me - but I like my duck with a bit more QUACK left in it.  The accompanying Corn Spoon Bread was AWESOME.  Desserts were by far worth the extra calories.  3 people shared the chocolate Bento box ($14 with chocolatey-good 6 selections - easily feeds 3 by itself).  We also got the hot, fried, five-spice & sugar donuts.  Now this is how I wished the churros at Xochitl could be!  WOW!  Five slightly greasy, hot donuts with 3 delectable dipping sauces (well - the cream cheese was too thick to really be called a sauce) including a rich ganache.  A cup of green tea and a Millenum Cocktail (rimmed with Tang - what is with Starr and his obsession with Tang in cocktails???) capped off a lovely early summer dinner.  Great for special occaisions - and the tab was $180 or so including tip which really isn't bad.  Expensive but not obscene (we spent more on dinner for 2 at Morimoto!!).  I will be back - but maybe just for drinks and dessert!  (HA, HA!) \ Oh - and I must mention our bartender Adele (She's there Thursdays thru Sundays) and our 5 year veteran server Meg who was charming and spot-on with our orders.  Oh - and if you want to (we didn't) they will valet park your car for $18.00).  So close to 5 stars - but not quite.

I echo Monique's review below in that this is a reasonably price zoo that is good for small kids (6 & under) but you need to bring your own food and water, and avoid the cafe.  Staff are friendly and easy to talk to. Giraffe feeding is $3.00 to feed them 2 pieces of romaine lettuce.  Totally worth it! They have 2 adorable giraffes.  Not a great zoo - very small - but good.

Very good service from a friendly Covid-19 compliant staff and tasty burgers - 2 thinly-smashed patties.  I had a lettuce wrapped cheese burger with fried mushrooms, lettuce and tomato and wee bit of M2O sauce (Ketchup plus mayo).  The owners were from Kosovo - interesting.  I would definitely come here again. Better than Smashburger comparable to 5 guys with more choices (salads, smoothies and shakes).  Loving M2O so far.
This is the Panera in the Lawrence Park Shopping Center and it is just like every other Panera - maybe a tad grottier.  Not great and not bad.  Sandwiches, Salads, Soups and Breads/Pastries.
A new fro-yo place (akin to those in Philly - pay per ounce). Lots of toppings.  My 8 year old loved the pink and green decor.  Christian-owned FROG - Firmly Rely on G-d.  Whatever.

Where would we be without Uber and Lyft? I check both and see which will get to me quicker out in the 'burbs.  Sometimes it's not about $$ for me but time. Time is money.  LOL.  Anyhow - so far only good experiences.

We have a great experience at Elmwood Park zoo and became members. It is best for families with young kids - and you can still feed the giraffes (They now have 3 males) and American Bison (we saw 2).  Due to Covid the little "choo choo train" and a few other exhibits are closed. Bring a mask.  They have sanitizer at many of the playground and attractions.  A cute little zoo - you only need 2.5 - 3 hours to see it all and bring your own food/beverages.  Way less crowded than the Philly zoo but, of course, not as many types of animals.  A great place for local school trips.

My sister in law (and her mom) get their T-giving turkeys here (and Easter and any time the need a turkey) here.  How they raise a 22 lb bird without growth hormones is beyond me - but that was a big and tasty bird!  (Not dry or tough or stringy at all).  Delicious!

My 11 year old dim sum loving daughter and I enjoyed an inexpensive and satisfying lunch at Tom's.  We were treated well and even though they do not yet have Moon Cake (nor egg tarts, nor Bubble tea - please consider serving Bubble Tea!), we ate to our hearts content.  The mammoth triple steamed bao ($1.95) is big enough to share and stuffed with mustard greens, eggs and shrimp paste.  (Next time we'll try the meat bun).  For dim sum we had the superb Shanghai Pork Soup Dumplings.  #Bliss. The har gao (crystal shrimp dumplings) were tasty (kiddo's fave) but my favorite were the pan fried beef dumplings.  Wow.  I am sold and can't wait to return.  Next time we shall try the scallion pancake and 2 kinds of Shu Mai.  Never met a dumpling I didn't like - but these are terrific. Chinatown (a cleaner, more yuppified version) has come to "downtown" Media!  Update:  We went again on 8/15 and who did we see working there?  SABRINA!  We love her.  She introduced us to the fabulous sweet potato cake for dessert.  We also tried the Shanghai Shumai (very good), more har gao (LOVE THEM) and an order of the pork & chive dumplings.   One of the best bites?  The cold, marinated sliced pork.  Soooooo good.

Typical Irish-style local bar - with live music and a great outdoor "alley-space" to sit outside on a warm evening.  Parking is tough.  Food is decent enough - with all the pub-grub staples. I had the Cobb salad - and my mates had classic burgers with fries. Kim - our server - is a tough cookie who is fantastic with the regulars.  Good times - and lots and lots of booooooooze!
Still lovin' it.  Brought a crowd of 5 here for bao, har gow, noodles and more. Try the stir-fried green beans. - So good.  Inexpensive and fun.

As her website states, Celeste serves up the finest cheesecake in town.  Specializing in classic pinup and burleque photography, Celeste and her team of make-up and hair stylists can transform even an ordinary house-wife into a vampy vixen or pinup.  She offers a variety of packages in her private studio in overbrook.  I did a pin-up photo shoot and it was a blast.  Can't wait to do it again some day!  Celeste is one in a million and I just love her work.

Meh - 1.5 stars.  food was 2 and service was 1 or zero.  My husband asked them to cut our kid's slice into squares and they could not figure out how to do this.  Odd.  We cut it ourselves.  I had a chicken cheese steak. It was pretty awful.  We won't go again.

OK.  I am now officially hooked on Zushi - I tried the "signature" zushi which is fish on top on "butter toasted rice" - not healthy but so tasty.  Smeared with avocado mash and sprinkled with tobiko and shredded scallions.  YUM.  $10 for just a Zushi or $15 for a combo meal (better deal - you get the Zushi, a California roll and a small seaweed salad.)  Super-easy touch screen ordering.  I am liking this place more and more.

A fantastic breakfast - real banana pancakes with both bananas on top and IN THE BATTER which is what i like.  Alas, fake syrup - I would gladly pay an upcharge for REAL maple syrup.  Yes, we know how much it costs!  Very nice service from our old-school server and the male host was efficient.  The "Springfield Benedict" (get the faux-hollandaise on the side) is delicious with spinach and bacon instead of canadian bacon.  HUGE and filling.

Just had my 3rd photo shoot with Celeste (and Jessica - the makeup/hair artist). It was soooooooo much fun.  Can't wait to see the proofs.  And...  They are amazing. I love working with Celeste for the "best cheesecake in town".

This large Wawa is nearly always hoppin' - especially the morning, lunch and after-work rushes (avoid).  The coffee lines in the AM are almost comical - you'd think they were giving it away. Service is quick, efficient and depending on the gal or guy you get - can be friendly and funny (The young man I saw last night when I stopped in for a quart of milk - $1.59 - was so funny.).  Wawa is a very convenient thing!!!
NPR - we were FORCED to listen to it as kids - my parents just love it - things like "Fresh Air" with Terry Gross and other shows.  I remember thinking how BORING it was.  Still kinda do.

New owners are taking over and good things are happening at Play It Again.  Thank goodness that Ellen (the manager) is staying.  Love her.  I have sold or consigned 3 pairs of high-end figure skates here. My kid is a competitive figure skater and when she was younger would grow out of thr $200, $300 and $500 boots so quickly.  Now, her stuff costs even more but she now needs new skates from wear, not growth,  Have a young skater (figure or hockey)?  Soccer kid?  Tennis?  You gotta check out PIAS to sell your old gear. Hey, $20, $30 or $50 in my pocket is more than ZERO dollars in my closet.

Wow. Very impressed. Generous slices of sashimi. Tuna, salmon and yellowtail were all fresh.  Enormous $5 tempura veggie app.  Next time I am getting the sashimi app - you get 2 pieces each of Tuna, Salon and Yellowtail for $12 instead of $18 if ordered a la carte.  So happy.  Got my protein fix. Definitely better than Yummy Sushi around the corner and much quicker.  You can eat there but it is really a take out kinda place. Super easy touch-screen ordering.  I will be back.  Hopefully soon.

Love the food here - burritos, quesadillas (traditional or Tex-Mex) and the Camarones Platter ($14.95) with Mojo de Ajo is a garlicky dream.  Service is down to earth and you may need to be a bit patient with the staff to get what you want.  Don't miss the house-made salsa verde - with fresh tomatillos.  Can't wait to try their Al Pastor next.

Bring money and patience and a book or e-book to read and enjoy. The food is fairly good for breakfast/brunchtime or a snack (coffee and pastry).  Not great for a true lunch or dinner.  I enjoyed my croissant and coffee and lingered over a magazine.

OMG - what is this? A diner?  On Chestnut Street? - below is an excerpt from 2/6/2020 in the Inquirer:  "Center City's flagging diner scene got a boost this week with the opening of the Chestnut Diner, a snazzy, two-story affair across from Liberty Place at 1614 Chestnut St. It occupies the former 4 Seasons Food Court, which closed last year.  The Chestnut, open 24 hours on weekends for now, joins the 24-hour Midtown III, that wood-paneled vestige of the 1970s two blocks away on 18th Street, and the more modern City Diner at Broad and South Streets, which also runs 24 hours on weekends."  Our party of 4 had lunch there and server, Jen, a bubbly blond was terrific. The food had some hits and misses.  (Breakfast is served all day)  The Cobb Salad was fresh and HUGE for $10.95 - came with a cup of soup. Burgers are served with fries and a cup of soup.  (A great value at $7.99 or 8.99).  Soft Drinks are $2.00 and come with refills.  The hot roast beef sandwich was a hot, gloppy mess.  PASS.  Also you pay "up front" which during a busy Friday lunch rush took quite a bit of time.  Come hungry!  All the classic Diner Faves are here. No more 4 season's salad bar.  Much nicer than Little Pete's (remember that??).  I wish them much success.

Back 10 years later for yet another "special" birthday and Celeste and her hair and makeup team (Raina was not there - I had Jessica who was also great) are world-class. Her overbrook studio is comfortable, clean and so very retro.  LOVE LOVE LOVE.  I chose one set with a $75 upgrade for a beach theme. My goal?  To make it not look like 10 years went by. I get the proofs in 2 weeks.  Can't wait.  If you have ever, ever, ever wanted to do this - run to your phone and call Celeste (or book online).  It's well worth the money and I can't wait to come back again in 5 or 10 years.  Seriously. Can't say enough great things about Celeste as a person and as a professional photographer.

Hosted a "Ladies Night" Happy hour with 6 of my friends.  Service from Allan was terrific and the drinks ($5 specialty cocktails and wines) and food (mostly we got small plates) was very good.  A great choice for a fun night out.

We had amazingly good service from Alexa (and a shout out to Jeff the manager) at my ladies night Happy Hour (6 of us) at the bar area.  While Happy Hour prices (which are a great value - $5 drinks and $6 apps) only last from 4 - 6 PM we stayed until after 8:30 and a few of us enjoyed (Shrimp) Cobb salads (always terrific), Bang Bang Shrimp, Shrimp Tacos and Lobster bisque from the "regular" menu.  There is also a lovely server named Sara who treats me so well any time I come in with family or friends.  Yes, Bonefish is a chain, but I really like this location of it. Don't miss the brunch menu - very good also.
Attended a graveside service here. Man, this place is big and complicated. Funeral home organized everything well. The cemetery itself seemed fine.  Expensive to be buried here.

I'm sorry but the food here truly sucks. We came as part of a large group party (I would never dine here of my own accord - I men, El Limon, Chiang Mai and Black Fish are all on the same street!) and they provided a cash bar (luckily sodas were free) and 5 hot appetizers in chafing dishes.  Thank g-d for the vegetable tray - it was fresh and fine.  Wings?  Mediocre - kinda dry. Mozz. Sticks - cold Scaliop pieces (or was in a shrimp, or a piece of cheap fish) wrapped in flabby bacon - ICKY. Fried Gyoza/Potstickers - clearly frozen but at least edible. And one other item I forget - as I clearly did not eat it.  Not a fan.  Gross food.

It's 2021 and boy, how the world has changed. My kid is 16 - and a vegan  But We still enjoy Tom's Dim Sum (Delicious steamed broccoli, vegetable dumplings)  I am not a vegan so I get Har Gao (Crystal Shrimp Dumplings) and dip them into the delicious sweet soy/vinegar sauce.  So satisfying.  Love it here.

It's just OK.  Way passed it's prime - but the cute location is fun and they now offer some strange "game meat" choices on the menu.  Back in the '90's we'd come here for brunches and celebratory dinners.  It was good for graduations and such.  Today?  I might not choose it.  Note:  We also investigated the Inn (across the parking lot) for a potential wedding venue - but it was not what we were looking for.

Very friendly and helpful young guys running the place. tasty selection of pre-cooked (softshell crabs, crab cakes) fried items that you can reheat.  Good for takeout (they have 2-3 small tables if you want to eat there.).  Lots of frozen seafood soups (Chowders and Bisques).  I'll be back to try the Salmon Teriyaki Rice Bowl. ($8.99).

My 13 year old still adores the Shrimp (Har Gao) Dumplings, Soup Dumplings, Meat Bun (big and fluffy and $1.75) and Shanghai-style Shiu Mai at Tom's.  Also faves include the cold, marinated roast pork (Chinese Salumeria at its finest), and believe it or not excellent Chicken & Broccoli and Pork Fried Rice. If you LOVE garlic - try the thinly sliced roast roast with garlic (appetizer).  So tasty!  We just love it here - and lunch for 2 is never more than $30/$35.
Dana R.'s review is accurate.  Sarku has never been a favorite of mine - too oily and carb-heavy.  Chicken is just OK - very greasy.

We stopped here on a slow July 5th and had a surprisingly good experience - even though it was clear that the manager is a jerk and most of the waitresses hate their jobs.  My french onion soup was actually good - not overly salted and full of beef stock and roasted onions - melted cheese and crisp crouton.  No issues.  DH ordered a short stack (3 pancakes) and they were fluffy and hot (not leaden!) and served with cheap-a$$ syrup.  Not a holy grail but we were pleasantly surprised.  Steven B. is an accurate source of info., though - so next time we'll head to a different place. We stopped here when very hungry and the place was nearly empty.

This Maggiano's (Cherry Hill Mall) is much better than the one in Philly. Cleaner, better service and for whatever reason the food tasted better to me. (Even though it's the SAME menu.)  Pasta dishes are a great value at lunch - but I ask them to go lightly on the sauce(s) - the garlic load is pretty intense.  A good place for a "family meal" - no, it's not earth-shattering - and it can feel a bit "cafeteria-like" as it gets loud and the acoustics are pretty awful, but we take the 5 year old here and she loves it.

Pretty Mediocre.  The family stopped in here while house hunting in this area. Clean but GRAY and cafeteria-like dining area.  DD had a meatball sub (my meatballs are better - these were bready and tasteless), DH had a cheesesteak which he hated and I actually like my (Kronos pre-packed, obviously frozen) Gyro sandwich on Pita.  The gents behind the counter were friendly and very nice. I was leaning toward 3 stars until I tasted DD's sub.  Blech!  Bathroom was clean and decent.  The place needs a facelift for the dining room and a re-vamp of the "classic" Greek-owned Pizzeria menu.  I wish I could have liked it better - but we will NOT be back.

Chima is the kind of dining where you much have a clearly mapped-out strategy before dropping $60 plus on lunch (or $80 ish for dinner).  Two words... Meat. Sweats.  Two more words... Food. Coma.  Some rookie mistakes to avoid: 1.  Skip the little cheese/bread - yes, they are delicious but they will fll you up. 2.  Go very, very easy on the salad bar - BE SELECTIVE.   3.  Ask, ask, ask your server to bring you the cuts you most want.  Once they do get 2 slices of those you love the most (for me the Lamb (chops not leg) and Angus Beef (Classic) were the best picks. 4.  Allow adequate time - at least 2 hours.  This is not a place to go if you are in a time crunch.  Yes, I would go back here - especially for a celebratory meal, but I will also ask for a side of LIPITOR.  P.S.  NOT vegan friendly (Um, duh!).

What a great place!  This historic tower has a nature preserve and wildflower tours for kids and parents.  A great place for bird watching, too. Climb to the top of the Tower for a fabulous view of the surrounding countryside.  Don't miss a visit to Bowman's Tower and Wild Flower preserve.  (And if you have kids - bring 'em.)

Believe it or not, I had NEVER been to a MP before last night (Mother's Day) but I had read the menu, reviews and my brother and his wife love it there - so I kinda knew what to expect.  I completely agree that this is the kind of meal you can only have a few times per year.  Great for kids (they love to dip) and if you are younger and not as jaded makes a good "date night" or special occasion place.  They try to make it dimly lit and faux-mantic in there!  (LOL.)  It was PERFECT for Mother's Day - and our server, Amanda (who has been at this location for 11 years) was terrific.  For $40 per person ($20 for el kiddo) we got the "whole shebang" and even upgraded our dessert dippers ($4.95) to include a slice of (mediocre) cheesecake and frozen cream puffs.  not sure we'd do that again.  Also the salad (Caesar) was unimpressive.  The cheese and chocolate fondues were the best parts of the meal (would ike to see better veggies for dipping - we only got celery, carrot and cauliflower - would love to see broccoli, sugar snap peas, bell peppers.)  Court Boullion was very salty - but tasted OK - definitely imparted flavor to the potatoes and mushrooms.  Meats varied from delicious (Shrimp & Filet Mignon) to boring (Chicken) to not very good ("Ahi" Tuna - who BOILS tuna?)..  We'll return - but not right away.  I would go back just for dessert - or they now have (but not all the time) a $20 deal for Cheese, salad (yawn) and dessert. Or maybe just dessert?  Oh - and the "Parmesan crusted pine nuts" in the Caesar salad were NOT parm crusted - they were downright candied.  Tasty - but not what i was expecting.

They opened a brand-new ALDI on 352 near the Wawa, where the old Giant (now across 352) used to be.  I had a pretty crappy first experience, and I was excited to try Aldi as friends have said it is "really cheap".  Well, sometimes you get what you pay for...  In this case my experience sucked before it even began.  In the parking lot.  I walked up to get a cart and you need to put a Quarter in to release a cart.  Feh.  I had no quarters.  So I figured I'd "wing it" and only buy what I could carry (which was about  5 items). There are no shopping baskets inside the store, either.  What is this? Grays Ferry?  So I browse and I shop, and yes the prices are super low, but - BUT - no-name brands or brands I have NEVER heard of and no sourcing info.  (Fresh grated Parmesan-type cheese for $1.99 - distributed by ALDI in IL but WHERE is it from?  US?  Italy (no way)?)  Too scared to buy meat here. Bought my kid a cookies & cream type candy bar from Germany (interesting).  I approach the checkout line and there is ONE lady working (everyone else has scattered) who desperately wants to go on break.  The lady ahead of me is being served and I remarked (out loud - my BIG mistake) Oh, they have no plastic bags?  And the eco-conscious lady ahead of me gave me a HUGE earful about how all stores should do this and how "You need to bring your own bags" and how it's better for the environment and on and on.  And, honestly, she is correct - but her snappy, bitchy-toned delivery needed much improvement.  She left and I paid for my $11 worth of stuff (which would have cost about $15 at Giant) and hand-carried it out to my car.  (Admittedly, I looked around in the parking lot to make sure that lady was gone.  She was really pissed off for some reason.)   Next time I will remember to bring a quarter and my own bags.  If there is a next time.  I am in absolutely no rush to ever return to ALDI.
My teen is a competitive skater so the Public Skate is not her thing but she enjoys the River Rink from time to time each winter.  Lots of special events here too.  Gets crowded.

We attended a low-scale (no catering - we brought in pizza, chips and brownies), minimally decorated, no booze school function here.  We were VERY lucky to have a member of our school community who knows the owner. This is a very nice (and importantly - large) ballroom which easily accomodated our group of 175 (with plenty of room to spare and a large dancefloor).  Would I have my own wedding here?  Probably not.  But for other events - family reunions, etc, it's a good pick.  I can't speak to their in-house catering as we brought in our own food. (Again - someone knew the owners, you normally have to use their food.)

We had an excellent time at a corporate luncheon held at the Doubletree on 202 just North of Wilmington.  Over 150 people, cash bar, plated lunch.  Everyone could see the presentation and hear the audio.  (Microphones worked well).  Waitstaff was attentive and efficient. No issues.

Meh.  I had the Cobb Salad here and substituted "roasted Shrimp" for turkey which proved to be a pricey and needless mistake.  The Shrimp were over cooked and rubbery.  The salad itself would have been just fine (Next time, IF there is a next time sticking to Turkey - I pray it is not dry.)  Avocado Ranch on the side was tasty.  $13 salad.  Blargh.  Oh - one bright spot - Service at the front counter from Natalie (sp?) was great and she ubbly, sassy, smiling personality.  They kind lady (Keysha?) who brought us our dine-in order was great, too.  They get packed during the lunch rush - location, location, location.

Pag's is, indeed, pricey - but hey - you're in DOYLESTOWN.  They serve decent pizza with yuppy ingredients like pancetta or prosciutto.  The main restaurant has great pasta dishes. (This is the Cafe next door.)
Parking lot is usually very crowded so use caution, otherwise - this is my go-to branch of TD bank.  Here or Aston, occasionally Newtown Square.  No issues.

Still love TJ's - the prepared Medditerranean Pasta salad makes a great lunch (and for $3.49 - whoo-hoo!). Also for $1.99 the frozen bowties with spinach and 4 cheeses is great (rich though and 390 cals.).  To say nothing of the divinely fattening shells with asparagus and brie ($3.49).  I come in very frequently now that I am working 1 block away.

the gyros are the best thing they make ($7 - and 4 stars).  The spanakopita is not that good.  Greek salad was OK - but not mind blowing.  With all the fabulous choices in RTM (and trust me - I love greek food) I usually find myself drawn to Thai or some other place over Olympic.  A big plus - they have their own seating so at least you know if you get a (tasty) gyro there that you will usually be able to get a stool to sit and eat it on.

I got takeout (delivered, actually) when I needed a quick lunch one day at my firm's Cherry Hill office.  It was really very good.  Cindy's is located in a nearby strip mall,  They have "the usual" Chinese food and a few Japanese selections as well.  I would definitely order again.  I never got a chance to dine-in so I can't speak to the decor or service.

2 stars is plenty generous for this chain of BLAH seafood (all pre-frozen) and bisquick (Cheddar Bay) biscuits.  It's the Olive Garden of the sea.  And my brother in law and his wife both worked here when they were just out of high school, met and fewll in love here and now are married.  Best thing to come out of a Red Lobster in my opinion.  Certainly the food is not "gourmet".

Wow - that Riverfront Market just gets better & better.  Today I stopped in with business colleagues for a quick lunch meeting and while they were off getting cheesesteaks, Thai & Sushi - I got myself a FAB-U-LOUS Salade Nicoise from Harry's.  This huge and fresh salade can be make with freshly grilled Ahi Tuna or Shrimp.  I opted for Shrimp and got 5 big ones atop a mound of fresh crisp greens, grape tomatoes, nicoise olives, cooked potatoes, blached naricot vert (yum!) and a luscious side of vinaigrette.  I also sprung for a fresh-blended Arnold Palmer.  This place rocks!  Yes, I spent about $12 on lunch - but there was more than enough to take back to the office to eat tomorrow!  Hooray for Harry's as a fresh, quick seafood-lunch (they also do great burgers & fries with unique dipping sauces).
Picked up my stuff and paid $85 by personal check (Whatevah!). Lady is very nice and clothing seems to be OK and does not smell bad.  Still, I will NOT go back here.

I've had some great meals at Pag's (the main restaurant has the best food of the 3 - wine bar, pizza cafe and restaurant.).  We shared a delightful Mozzarella di Buffula (the REAL McCOy - and priced to match) with red ripe summer tomatoes.  The garden area outside is a great summer night's treat.  In winter - try the (a bit heavy) house made pastas.  Tagliatelle was perfectly al dente hear and served in asugo di burro (Butter sauce - I think I spelled that wrong - sorry.).  Fresh shaved parmesan over the top.  Yes, the prices are steep - and a bit "too -too" for people like my parents - we prefere Luberto's which is more "homey" and alot cheaper - but for a romantic date or a birthday celebration?  In D-town I love Pag's.  Oh - and I came here with my daughter when she was just under 2 years old and they treated her really well - spaghetti and everything.

So, against my better judgement, I walked in on a whim to see if I could get a (cheap) blow-out. I had a special event on a Saturday night and - by some miracle - the place was dead-empty.  Danielle (a 22 year-ish, fresh outta High School stylist) did a simple and decent blow-out (not flat itron - as that would have added $15 - Feh.)  So my TOTAL was $15 - with tip was $21.    Still not mad about this place, but at least the high staff turnover has brought in some better people.  Wait 6 months - they'll all change again.  (The owner of this franchise owns OVER 50 LOCATIONS.  Wow!)  Globs of hair by front door - needed sweeping.  I would NEVER get color, highlights or any complex chemical service here. It's basically a training ground for stylists right outta school. Lots of MEN and kids come here in search of a cheap cut.  You get what u pay for!

Less crowded than the CVS at 19 & Chestnut - and it's on my way to work so I stop at the Walgreens on JFK from time to time to fill a prescription, pick up sundries or (twice) get photo processing.  No major complaints and no major praise - glad its there.

Well - I guess I am writing this review a little too late. Lily Orlando's frozen Italian Foods is CLOSING in 2 weeks (Nov. 2012). Currently, Lily Orlando's is a line of home-made frozen take-out meals that you buy in the BP station.  Yup.  That's right. Gas station. With food. In freezers.  Prices are $8.00 (cheese ravioli) to $16 (REAL veal parm) and each container feeds one big hungry guy or 2 normal people.  LOVE the food - and so surprise to find it. And so sad to hear they are closing. (They may reopen elsewhere in Media once the dust settles - the BP is turning into a Wawa soon.)  Tried the Chicken Parm, Shrimp Scampi, Veal Parm and Cheese Ravioli.

Back again and lovin' it! Got a case of Blackberry Hint Water (10% of a case of anything), some $18 maple syrup, a pair of duck legs and tons of boutique yuppified frozen meals. Plus crispy-fresh bean sprouts, mini bell peppers and a $2.17 single humongous mandarin orange called a Sumo.  Lady at check out was a doll - Kenishon??  I know I got that wrong.  I'm stocked up!

La Prima catered a conference I attended held at the PECO Building in Center City Philadelphia. The theme of the conference was "Green Technology" so the caterer had to also be "green" - and La Prima is.  They use compostable plates, cutlery, paper goods etc and use foods from local CSAs and farms.  Meanwhile - how was the food? It was Good to Great!  Pasta was served hot (not lukewarm) and chicken was delcious and not dried out.  (Food was a buffet in chafing dishes which can be hit or miss).  Servers were friendly and helpful.  Very well run catering with tasty food that is locally (when possible) produced and prepared well.  Yay!

This is a nice outpost for Teuscher - there is another (tiny) shop at 16 & Walnut.  Teuscher has a good assortment of filled dark & milk chocolates. The truffles at Leonidas are somehow better - in my opinion. And for packaging and presentation - I'm all about Neuhaus.   But for top-quality chocolates, Teuscher is a safe bet for corporate or special occasion gift giving.  The flower boxes are beautiful - but very pricey.

I will be writing another - more detailed - update once I get my facial and my (groupon) massage - but for now I must give credit to Nikki for her excellent customer service (at least to me - she's always been great) and also to Christy (Christine??) who did my ($75) spa pedicure.  The pedicure itself was excellent.  CND and OPI products, included an exfolliating scrub, a massage and a wrap with a chocolate/peppermint clay masque.  Pollish application was very good as well - so far no chipping (it's only been 2 days though.).  What made it less-than-five star was the (gorgeous but) uncomfortable banquette that you sit on.  There are 6 pedi stations and they are just BEAUTIFUL to look at - but after a while my lower back pain started kicking in.  They do provide bolsters - but they were too wide for me.  It's a shame because you can tell alot of time and money went into the design of this spa and the nail area.  It is elegant, spotless and lovely.  But not very comfy.  Meanwile - I can't wait to return and  get another pedi from Christine (Christy??).  And I have a wondeful facial to look forward to in a few weeks.  This place is improving every time I go.

Had lunch here with Pat D. (what a sweetie she is!  and a great yelper, too.) and it was terrific.  Note:  If you are from Thailand or a true hot & spicy Thai lover you'll likely have to ask them to "kick it up a notch" but for people like me who like "wimpy" Thai - this place is great.
