Decor is freshly painted with brand new everything (red wodd chairs) and a big blue sea-scape mural painted on the walls.  Service was quick and quiet - just great.  My 3 course lunch special (if you eat in it's 7.95 - 11.95) included a soup (I got the "ravioli" aka  wonton soup - clear broth and light, yummy wontons -2), appetizer (I got the Tom Sum - Thai salad made with cabbage instead of the usual - and more pricey green papaya), and entree (I had Masaman Curry with Tofu which was coconutty and mild - which I love - and I ate every bit.)  I will DEFINITELY be back.  YAY for close-by Thai!!!

This is now my go-to (near work) Starbucks - as it is closest.  Can get crazy-crowded during peak times. Some of the baristas are terrific and others not so much.  There is a young guy with dark hair who is super funny and bright - and been there a long while.  He is great.  (Can't remember his name.)  If you can snag seating in the back it can be a decent place to get work done.  Parking in this shopping center has always been and still is a nightmare. (Lunch rush, Holiday time etc.)  Try to come at odd hours and you'll have a better experience.

Well, at long last, I can scratch Le Bec Fin off my to-do list.  Finally, I was able to justify the expense...  My husband & I celebrated his birthday by attending Chef Georges Perrier's Chef's table last night.  The main dining room is amazingly gorgeous.  What a place for a wedding or party!  We were seated in a slightly less glam area at the front of the house at a long table for 20.  (17 in all)  Perrier is running a special all summer Mon. - Thurs.  (20 seats per night) a "pay what you wish" 5 course set menu.  If you can, ACT FAST and get in on it before August is over.  The first course was the chilled pea soup from the regular menu.  Very good - but no way I would have ordered this in real life.  It was pluched with a dollop of almond ice cream which was heavenly.  (Made up for the fact that it's pea soup.)  2nd course was a single seared scallop.  DH & I are not scallop lovers - in fact, DH won't touch 'em so he had a salade ennui (boring salad) in its place.  I forced myself to eat the scalop and it was, indeed, perfectly cooked and surprisingly good (for a scallop fan I bet they'd LOVE it.).  3rd course was a slightly overcooked white fish called Limon (like a fluke or flounder).  I was looking so forward to this course and it was sauced with a lemon foam and plated over a few fava beans (yummy), chanterelles (a bit salty to my taste) and a tasteless hazlenut puree - the consistency and color of putty.  4th course was the best (save for dessert which was REALLY the best.) - a rare hanger steak.  3 -4 morsels in a decadent bordelaise (or was it a red wine/demi glace reduction?).  The sauce was lick-the-plate worthy.  And for dessert one of the BEST classic creme brulee.  Lightly laced with Gran Marnier and a crispy top.  Service was very attentive UNTIL the end when we needed our check.  At about 9:45 PM nearly everyone (there were several waitstaff) disappeared.  The Chef came out to our table prior to and during service and was collegial and utterly charming.  (Really.)  It helped that I speak un peu de francais and was seating next to a lovely, fluent, Belgian woman.  (Merci, Madame!)  Will I return?  Oh yes - but not in a hurry.  I would simply like to sit in the bar downstairs and have desserts off that AMAZING dessert cart (not part of our meal, alas).  That opera cake has my name on it!  Bien Fait!  Oh - and don't laugh but I actually drank (again don't laugh) a Mojito with my meal (I know, I know - in a French restaurant) and it was GREAT.  And it was $10.  My husbands manhattan was $12.  They do not serve Veuve Cliquot - which was what I was jonesin' for.

The best sushi I have found in this area - and so far I have only been there once for lunch - but man, it was good.  I tried the sushi "pizza" (sauces on the side - wasabi mayo & spicy mayo) based on a fresh-cooked scallion pancake.  Soooo tasty!  Plus this is a JAPANESE restaurant (Japanese/American) not Asian-Fusion - which I appreciate.  Heck, they even had Kampachi as a special.  Yee-Haw! And they DELIVER!  Wow.  Can't wait to return.
Ulta is kinda like Sephora meets Duane Reade. Beauty supplies galore (at full retail), includingnails, hair and skincare.

Took my 10 year old here at her request for dinner.  (We ended up getting take out as it was nearly 9 PM)  Wonderful, friendly service - and now they greet me by name.  El kiddo loves the Doner platter and I got Koobideh this time. Plenty of leftovers for lunch the next day.  Super-fresh pita. I am now hooked!
Great idea in concept but 3 stars in execution.  The would NOT take my couch because it had a small tear in it.  Oh well.  I free-cycled it away.

Kremp - and Leslie Kremp is my go-to source for local flowers. I have placed orders for Mother's Day (2012 and 2013), friend's birthday's, baby showers and many other things.  They even did my wedding back in 2008 and I have loved them ever since.  And no visit to the PHS Flower Show is complete without a bunch of Irises and Roses and uber-cheap prices from the PHS Marketplace at the flower show every year.  WE LOVE KREMPS!

Oh, my!!! A cigar bar in Media?  Yes!  And a brand-new and nicely appointed one at that - complete with $70 lighters and $50 cutters and (of course) a great selection of fine (and moderate) cigars.  Best of all?  The bartenders are terrific - especially Melissa - who mixes a great cocktail with high-end tequilas (or vodka - they have a blood orange one).    Food selections are limited but the cheese plate sounds great. I will be back - and next time I am eating!!!  What an addition to the State Street scene!

The Manhattan Bagel in the Chesterbrook Shopping Center is my go-to these days for coffee on my way to my new job.  Service is quick and friendly and they all know my boss there - she is there every morning.  There are usually 5 pre-brewed selections - Decaf, House Blend, Hazelnut and 2 others (today is was Dark Roast and Pumpkin Spice).  Bagels are good too - but I need to lay off of those for a while. This is a much cleaner location than the one in Center City.

Ya for Siren - it saved our asses in Jr. High and High school for sure.  It was a hang out and a place of employment for some of my friends.  Great selection of music and they can order you anything you'd ever want.

Back in the day Rice's was the shizzle!  We went almost every Tuesday in the Summer at the CRACK of dawn to score cheap socks, tee-shirts, back to school gear and fresh produce - simultaneously.  The place is HUMUNGOUS - but many of the vendors are lifers who are there week after week, year after year.  It's great fun for a bargain (but buyer beware, of course) antique (junk) shopping or just browsing around.  Great place to bring kids, too.

We don't "do" fast food - but when you have a 2-4 year old and need a play-room this is a great choice.  Our daughter gets a 4 nugget kids meal with fruit (instead of fries) and lowfat milk.  Then she plays - sometimes for a whole HOUR in the play room.  A great break for mom & dad.  Cheap.  Not too nutritionally horrible.  (But we don't come more than every 2 weeks.)  However, recently our daughter discovered that they serve Lemonade.  Our lowfat Milk days are numbered.  NOTE:  Recently (May 2009) the play area has gotten stickier and dirtier.  It needs a good floor to ceiling cleaning.

I had not been back here in years once I discovered Vic's and other places. A good friend really wanted to come here for lunch and we both split an order of 8 steamed frozen) gyoza (They offer chicken, pork, veggie, shrimp or beef - wow!) and we each got the $8.95 lunch special.  It includes miso soup (good - but tastes like a kikkoman restaurant-mix) and your choice of 4 half-makis (4 pieces).  I got spicy yellowtail (OK), yellowtail scallion (very good), albacore cucumber (real Albacore - not Escolar - yay extra star for that), and Tempura Salmon.  Very inexpensive for lunch and quite filling due to all the rice.  The owner/manager from years ago seemed to remember me, too - which was nice but also made me feel bad that I had not been coming for a long time.  So my faith has been restored in Mizu - and although Vic is still better quality sushi, it is much more pleasant to dine here - at a table and not elbow to elbow with the other 7 seats at Vic.  I'll be back - and sooner than I had planned.
This is a nice, typical VS store - but it is not the closest one to my house.  I came here to redeem my "free panties" coupon - and basically went in and out - no issues.  Seems fine to me.

So Steven Starr kinda-sorta redid the bar at the back of the old Midtown 2 Diner and now it's the "Ranstead Room" - a pricey , dimly-lit speakeasy with fresh ingredients and $12 drinks.  Think Candied Ginger and Granny Smith Apples.  Fun.  Still got the old tufted red booths - just polished up a bit with the cracks repaired.  Grab dinner at El Rey and then walk ALL THE WAY AROUND (Darn it, just open the door!) to Ranstead.  Oh - and they don't even open until 7 PM - so NO happy hour here.

I have been going to Tommi on and off for over 2 years - and they do offer groupons from time to time - which are a great value.  This time I had a facial with Liana and she is terrific. My skin looked and felt amazing afterward (I never judge a facial until at least 24 hours have ellapsed ) with no breakouts.  She also did a lip and eyebrow wax for me and they were great, too.  Tommi is a relaxing beautiful spa and I love to come here.  So glad Tierra is still here - she is a great massage therapist.

I grew up going to PVP alot - I even was "baptized" into my brownie troop - or brownie-ized or whatever that little ceremony they have is called, back when I was in 2nd grade.  We rode bikes here, and fished for sunnies, and have oodles of picnics and BBQs here in the summertime.  Lots of fond memories of Peace Valley Park and Lake Galena.
What a fun boutique with cute clothes, sparkly accessories and even BLISS spa products.  The owner and his daughter who works there are helpful and not pushy.  I'll be back for sure!

OK - again I vacillate between 4 & 5 stars.  Decor and Service were top-notch. Cocktails are delicious - albeit pricey - with freshly "crafted" ingredents like smoked cinnamon and house-made bitters.  For "healthy" food - many of the dishes were oily or had fried components or incorporated bread.  The cauliflower was fried and oily.  Potatoes and root veggies?  Fried.  The best bite of the night?  Parsnip spread - on white toast (odd that so many things are served on bread??  Come here in the summer for fresher better choices.  Winter veggie fans, rejoice - you can get parsnips, turnips, potatoes, radishes and a plethora of beet varieties.  I wish I could remember our french female servers name - she was patient and kind. The "bus folks" were workin' it, too!  Love it here.

This is for the Halal Cart with Green & Yellow Signage parked on the corner of 20 & Market (South East - not the Falafel Man on the NE Corner).  $5 got me a huge rice platter with 1/2 chicken cubes and 1/2 gyro (salty but not horribly so) meat cubes, iceberg "salad" with 2 slivers of tomato and a pile of rice.  "White" or "Hot" sauce (or both).  INCLUDED a soda or water - not bad for $5!
Ok, it does suck here - but what choice do we have?  I am a mother of one of those crying toddlers - and this is where we go to see such classics as Madagascar and Wall-e.  Oh, G-d.  Make it stop.
We had a good first experience with the service department here when we took our 2006 Sonata for inspection.  $407 later we passed.  Hmmmmn...

I have had good luck with Nikes at this location (near the Walmart & PetSmart in Springfield). No issues so far - prices are on par with Famous Footwear and higher prices than crappy payless (I hate that store!).  I tend to come to chain stores for my kids shoes (my kid wears ladies sizes). This DSW location is just fine for now.

Pate's and porc-loving products which i discovered at the Rittenhouse Square Farmers market on Saturday AMs - but their main place is in RTM.  Pricey - but delicious. If you don;t eat pork - try the lamb pate.  DIVINE!  Oh - and they sell pre-cooked/pre-seasoned carnitas.  Neat-o!

Much less chaotic than the one on Chestnut Street - I guess it depends on when you go (lunch time and the holidays are mobbed just about anywhere.)  Yesterday I popped in around 6:45 (they close at 7) toget my "free cotton panty".  When I got to the registers there was a HUGE line - about 8 people and 1 cashier.  Straight away - 2 more ladies jumped onto the registeres and saved the day.  I swear, you'd think they were giving it away!  (Oh wait, they are...)  Anyhow VS must HATE me because I am a coupon minimalist - I only buy the item covered by the coupon and nothing else.  I took my 1 free panty and left.  I had to chuckle at the 2 ladies in front of me who were busily sorting through their stack of cards and coupons.  We're all they same - just looking for some free panties and cheap bras.

We had a delightful lunch for 5 that far surpassed my expectations for in-mall Chinese.  Edamame and Gyoza apps were tasty.  Lunch entrees were reasonably priced and perfectly sized.  Some of the best (basic) Chicken and brocolli - tender white meat and not gloppy.  Outstanding shrimp lo mein with thinner than usual noodles - not overloaded with onion.  NOT GREASY.  A pleasure.  Rainbow shrimp was great, too- and not skimpy on the shrimpy. Friendly, efficient service and lovely decor.  Full bar and sushi (did not try it yet.).  We can't wait to return.

No major issues with Olde City Taxi.  I usually call a few hours before I need a cab and it is usually there on time.  Some of the cabs are pretty shoddy - it's on a car by car basis.  Some are 1 star - others 4 or 5.  Cabs in Philly cost even MORE than in NYC.  Who knew?

Please note that I am NOT an Indian food lvoer - in fact - I generally don't eat it.  I can't deal with all the cardamom and curry and fenugreek and such.  I will be generous and give it 4 stars - but my conscious is screaming "3 stars".  I reall would like to see them succeed.  The Callohwhill area needs new businesses.  But 3 of us had a very lovely dinner there last week.  The place was nearly empty - but you can see that the decor (which is lovely) is brand new.  The ladies room was clean and marble-ized and nice.  Service was very attentive - some might argue a bit much - as he asked my husband if he'd like to order any bread 3 times.  (I ordered a poori - with Shrimp as an appetizer which was fabulous in all its deep-fried glory).  My husband did not want any bread.  Really.  Our friend who dined with us is FROM India - and he ordered a Chana (can't remember) appetizer which we all enjoyed but it was served on a bed of shredded ice berg lettuce - which would NEVER happen in India.  The Lamb Curry was tender and mildly spiced. The rice was excellent - as well cooked basmati can be.  I would go back - but again - I am just not an Indian Food lover.  For Philly - this seems like the best of the lot.  For betetr Indo-Pak food try Queens NY or North Jersey.  Oh - our dessert (Galub - can't spell it) fried cheese balls, was syrupy and friend and just as I rememberfrom the Dipavali festivals I used to attend.  Yum-my.  Oh - it's BYOB - so BRING something. (We didn't and wished that we had.)   Dinner for the 3 of us was $60 even including tax & tip.  Really not bad.

It's the hood of all malls.  There is nothing here to speak of.  on a very rare occaision i will go to the Old Navy (which is nearly always picked over and dis-shelveled.)  I also once dained to get my nails done at the Korean-run nails salon on the lower level.  NEVER AGAIN.  This is a really low-end mall - which is a shame because when it was built it was a shining star and an attraction for Philadelphia.

I agree 100% with Steve S. this is a Chipotle-esque pizza spot - and I got the mini ($4.97) loaded with veggies.  Not bad!  A thin crisp crust (bordering on burnt - so they need to be careful) and lots of goodies.  No issues. Quick and cheap.
Stopped in to get razor blades and a few cosmetic necessities for my teen daughter.  Easy in and out, ample parking.  No issues.  Did NOT get prescriptions filled here.

Quality has been slipping over the years.  I have gone to Mizu since it first opened (now there are 3 of them in Philly),  Back then it was dirt-cheap (which always makes me suspicious when dealing with raw, fresh fish) and very, very good.  Today, Mizu offers a limited selection of fish - the basics like tuna, salmon and yellowtail and also standard rolls.  Prices are low to moderate and they give you BIG portions.  A roll is really 1.5 rolls - 12 pieces.  Mike, the owner, is rarely ever at the Original 20th Street location - and the sushi bar chefs I used to know well are not there anymore.  I am hopeful they can recapture the service and freshness level they had when they first opened.  Incidentally - they make an excellent Hwe Dup Bop and tasty Gyoza and Shumai are cheap (frozen - not home made).

It's a 3 star place but I am giving 4 stars for the extremely well-executed holiday party we threw here for our party of 9.  Granted, the food was family style - which meant it all came out promptly - but it was actually good (Chicken Parm, Chicken Marsala and a baked ziti with meat in it).  Best of all were the huge platters of (very good) tira-misu.  Chrissy our server brought cappuccino and beverages right away.  Considering how busy and crowded the restaurant was (and the place is huge) with every holiday party under the sun - groups from 6 to 36 at long tables - the service was AMAZINGLY good.  For a faux-talian chain.

Horrifying.  I walked in at 4:45 PM (they closed at 6 that day) with my 10 year old for a cut and "dip dye" color.  We brought our own color but were told we could not use it and were assured they had the cobalt blue shade she wanted.  Well, we never even got that far because the 4 gals - 2 coming on shift and 1 or 2 leaving - were having a huge in-staff fight.  2 of the gals tried to stay out of it but the other 2 looked ready to kill each other.  They marched to the back and screamed at each other.  We left.  I don't need an amateur, unprofessional, angry hairstylist working on my kids head.  Soooooooo unprofessional. And they lost a potential client as well.  At least el kiddo snagged a lollipop before we left.  DO NOT RECOMMEND! (We had a far better experience at the Supercuts on South Street in Philly and of course we LOVE Shear Blliss in Brookhaven)
Stopped in on a DEAD Sunday night at 30th Street Station and needed good coffee.  Old Nelson Hooked me up with a REAL La Colombe Latte for under $2.00.  SCORE!!!!

This ShopRite is pretty nasty.  If you happen to come on a weekday, just after the shelves (and produce) are stocked - it's passable, but the weekends are hellish chaos.  Customer Service?  Slim to none.  At least the prices are lower than Whole Foods (as is quality) and sometimes lower then SuperFresh.  Oh - and when we shop with our child we always disinfect the nasty shopping carts.  Eeew.  Sticky & Gross.  I really loathe taking her there.  the slow moving lines make her antsy.  Not a fave for me, but - since our choices for grocery shopping are so limited in Philly (Where ARE you Fresh Direct?  PeaPod?), I am glad they exist.

My 4 year old can't get enough of the big wooden slide at Smith Playground.  The house is also great - but many of the toys are old and dirty - so bring Purell!  The outdoor playground areas are terrific on a sunny day - and all this is FREE.  For a small fee you can rent a space to have your child's birthday party here, too.

Wow - I can't even believe I am writing this.  My 4 year old daughter and I were in China Town yesterday - and we walked into Angel Beauty - a Shiseido Store - when we asked if they do nails - the lead us into a back room - which was GORGEOUS and clean and wonderful.  For 5 bux, dd had a polish change.  There was a lady there having reflexology done, and they had 3-4 pedi-chairs.  Definitely will return.  Not scary at all - just completely unexpected.
We have not yet decided which phone to purchase and where but I was impressed by "George from Ridley Park" and his knowledge of the products and plans.  Very nice!

Well, it doesn't feel "New" And the hoagies are NOT "Tiny" But the 6 inch Chicken Cheese Steak I got was great - and the friendly young lad at the counter was personable AND good looking.  I don;t eat hoagies often - but when I want one I'll be skipping Wawa and heading straight here!  Plus they deliver (even out my way in the boonies) for $1.50 charge - $10 minimum.  I will try the pizza soon and let you know... So far great for steaks/hoagies.  Take out ONLY (not where to sit - not even a card table).

I had walked passed this place but never cared to go in - so for whatever reason i stopped in yesterday for a manicure and (yes, really) a pedicure.  It looked clean - but I can not say what the sanitation situation is until I wait a while.  Meanwhile, Kim (who is pregnant) did the mani and pedi and did a nice job.  Not mindblowing - but acceptable.  Not sure if I'll be back but $30 for a mani/pedi is very reasonable.  I would probably NOT ever get eyelash extensions here (or anywhere, really.).  They take credit cards but tip must be in cash.

I had a good 4 star and a lousy 2 star experience at the Old Nelson inside 30th Street Station (used to be a Saxby Coffee a few years ago).  The first time I cam I bought packaged goods (A cup of Haagen Dazs, actually) - paid and left.  No problem.  It was a 4 star day and nice to see the wide variety of products.  But TODAY I decided to order a breakfast sandwich.  FAIL.  For $2.49 (You order at the counter - she writes it on a colored post-it note and then you go pay a la manual Wawa) I chose egg & cheese on a bagel.  Sounds simple, right?  So they make it (and I swear I saw a microwave was involved and I immediately knew this would not be pretty), wrap it, bag it and I march off to my office.  5 minutes later I unwrap this steming hot MESS of wax paper (microwaved-glued to the bagel).  I spent a good 2 minutes trying to pick off pieces of soggy wax paper from the bagel.  Threw half out - it was unsalvageable.  Ate the egg and cheese insides with a kinife and fork - eggs were nuked and horrible.  NEVER again for an egg sandwich - but yes for a quick stop for "packaged" goods - and they have an expansive cold beverage selection.  Cashier and counter folks were friendly - but please, take heed - NO MORE NUKING the egg sammies, OK?

Cute place with good - but not overwhelmingly good - sushi. I had one order of yellowtail sashimi (for $7.00) and a Polar Bear roll - which was basically an alaskan roll topped with white tuna. ($13.00)  That's it.  I didn't have much - and I was still kinda hungry - but cash has been tight.  Service was great because the place was dead empty on a Wednesday night at 7:45 PM.  Again - it's good - and worth a second visit - but by no means a holy grail.

Friendly service and BIG portions of very good food. However the prices are too high.  I'd gladly come more often to get a lower priced platter (I like platters better than sandwiches) and a smaller portion.  That said, for $11.95 I took 1/2 my meal (lots of great rice, Doner and roasted tomato plus lavash) home.  And it came with a fountain drink (again - knock $1.50 off and I'd gladly skip that - I like water.)  Super-friendly ladies offered us samples of the savory beef stew.  (My friend ordered that).  Lovely!

In the Old Days (Before the folks who own HomeGoods and Marshalls or whatever big chains they own - bought Christmas Tree Shops), CTS was only in Massachussets - mostly on Cape Cod and sold Holiday Decor.  Those days are looooooooong gone.  Now it's more like a 5 and 10 - random cheap home goods, food items, paper products, children's toys, lawn furniture and seasonal decorations (Halloween and Christmans come to mind).  This location is not one of the best - but I will  be kind agive it 3 stars - but it's more like 2.5.  CTS is becoming more and more like a Dollar store - but things cost more than a dollar.  I miss the old fashioned, quaint, New England CTS of old. But, those days, alas, are gone.

Rice's has been around for years and years and it ebbs and flows, expands and contracts basedon the seasons and the economy.  It's now $1.00 for parking (get there AT 7 AM when they open - by 9:30 AM the place is packed.  We scored some American Girl clothing (hand made), a tutu for our 8 year old, hair ribbons and sparkly no-name nail polish for $2 a pop.  A few produce people - but more "stuff" than food this year.  Once a summer is more than enough for me.  It's part street fair, part farmers market, part flea market, part mart.  A classic experience.

I feel a little silly updating my Tommi review so many times - so this will be my last update for a while - since now I am going here regularly.  Tommi has become my new "spa of choice".  I had a delightful massage with Tierra, and I can't wait to get another pedicure here. Massages and pedis - I will go to Tommi!

I just don't dig the Coffee Bar.  It's OK in a pinch - but ING Direct has bette, cheaper coffee.  This place is EXPENSIVE - you are paying hotel prices.  The decor is still nicer - nicer than back in the Capriccio Days - and it ain't Starbucks. (Which is a good thing in my book.)  Nice place to sit & rest   - I usually buy one cheap beverage and nurse it a while.

We ate here on July 2 - during the BIG crowds of the 4th of July weekend pre-fireworks mayhem.  We needed a place to kill 2 hours and eat.  I went with DH & 6 year old DD who was pretty well behaved, considering. We each ordered the $24.95 3 course pre-fixe and DD picked off my plate - Shrimp risotto (which was awful - gloppy and in some sort of weird "brown gravy")  Odd.  The soup - Clam Chowder - was watery and just Meh.  Service was bad, too.  The hostess is a doll and our server was fine - but the bus lady took alot of our stuff away before we were ready (I got up to use the ladies room and when I got back my napkin and water glass were gone. - I mean, who clears away the WATER glasses - you wait until the meal is over for that.)  Anyhow, at least they waived the $5 plate sharing charge.  Would NOT rush back - even though I still have dreams about the pierogies (only at lunchtime).

Had my rings cleaned and polished here just prior to Xmas. Such lovely people and great service.  Ray Feldman, sadly, has passed away and he will be missed. So glad we bought a platinum wedding band here.  We love and trust Barsky's.

This is not the one on Germantown Ave.  This one is in Old(e) City on N. 3rd Street.  Bone Appetite sells doggie (and kittie) gear, treats, pet food, supplies and custom-made (expensvie) bakery treats.  Akin to "Doggie Style", but a smaller feel & vibe.  The dog treat my daughter selected was $3.25 and was super-small.  (Not cool, but I'm a sucker and bought it anyway.)  They also have a PAWS cat (or 2) up for adoption at any given time.  Friendly front-desk lady - knew her products. Surprisingly GOOD prices on ZEKE's hip-action treats.  I shoulda got some - it might have made up for the over priced doggie baked goods.

It's been 2 years since we last visited 4 dogs but some things remain the same - lovely dining under the big green tent, and a vast array of fine cheeses in all forms all over the menu.  (The chef is apparently a "cheese head").  If available do not miss the $16.50 Caprese salad with sweet heirloom tomatoes and creamy, rich buratta.  Wow.  If you do not like cheese or are dairy averse - this may not be the best restaurant for you.  Ironically, nachos here are a disappointment - although plated on a cedar plank (cute) - but not enough toppings to justify $13 nachos.  French onion soup was good - but also pricey at $11.  Lunch for 3 with NO ALCOHOL was around $80 - ouch. Far too pricey for what you get.  On the plus side?  Dogs are so welcome - and there are many cute dogs to pet while you vist. On the minus side?  ONE tiny ladies room and always a line.

Friends don't let friends drink fourbucks.  This particular location is crowded fduring the AM rush especially.  I also call it CHARbucks as the coffee drinks usually are roastde too dark for me.  The espresso drinks are passable - but be careful as they are loaded with sugar and often with fat if you get them made with whole milk.  Not a big fan of Starbucks in general.  We grind and brew our own at home using peregrine coffee beans for a fraction of the price.

Run but teenagers and extremely slow service - bordering on ridiculously slow.  Meanwhile our 8 year old loves it here and we hosted a "sundae party" here for she and 5 of her little friends last September.  We have been back a few times to eat - and prefer this location to the SPringfield Mall one - but you have to tell them you are in a hurry (maybe even if you're not!) to get your food in a timely fashion.  Avoid the iceberg-blah salads. Burgers are OK - a bit greasy. Ice cream is the main reason to come at all.  Got kids?  They'll like Friendly's. Got tastebuds?  You may not like it so much!

I am torn - the food is 4 stars but there are too many other things that need attention - mostly decor-wise - like dust-covered bread plates and a dining room that needs a makeover, stat.  The business has been around for 11 years and is clearly family run. Shrimp scampi was very basic - but good.  I asked for it light on the sauce (oil/garlic) so that was a good move.  Frittata for lunch is a good and tasty value.  Bread was cold and dry (and sitting on the table waiting for us). Not great.  I can cook alot of these things at home just as well. I would return but won;t be rushing back.

I am vacillating bewteen a 2 and a 3. Grabbed a quick sushi (4 pieces of nigiri and 1/2 a california roll) and it was $12.00 and change after tax.  Yikes.  The Salmon was fine - but the tuna tasted a bit old. Mall Sushi.  Serves me right, I should know better.  I will not be back in a hurry and if I return I will try the "cooked" food instead.  The hot food looked OK but there were alot of fried items.

Stopped in last night (walked in did not use drive thru) and the place was empty at 8 PM. I actually thought they were closing, but they were just cleaning.  Very nice shift manager and 2 female baristas.  Got my kid a Peach Iced Green tea Lemonade and I got a Grande Caramel Macchiatto. Both were just perfect.  No issues.
Really?  So old school and no wraps.  It's wheat, white, rye or a roll. Limited choices.  Not my scene at all.  Terrific little old ladies behind the counter though and very inexpensive.

I just had a spa pedicure with...  ...None other than Larisa (formerly of the now closed Ettore).  She remembered me - before I came to my senses and remembered her.  And yes, she is still a wonderfully talented nail technician.  Nikki and Tom were kind to me as always.  Cliff and Tierra (my go-to massage therapists) are there and all is right with the world. Vera still does facials on Saturdays.  Let's hope that Tommi can iron out their staff and management kinks and build a good spa.  I know they can do it!  Meanwhile - definitely go have a massage or spa pedi here - it's now $65 for the spa pedi - which is pretty fair.  Good products too.  Sweet!
This is a fun place to browse around.  Great T-s, clothes & accessories all with the Sailor Jerry "tattoo" motif.  Thanks to McThrill for the wikipedia history lesson.

Philadelphia's answer to NYC's Gracious Home, Fosters offers upscale, classy bath, kitchen and home decor.  They also have cooking classes and other home-related workshops here.  It is pricey - but if you need a certain something - they can get it for you. A great place for unique house-warming gifts, too.  Glad it's here!

3,5 stars - for deli-style sandwiches, cheese-steaks, hoagies and iceberg based salads.  Long lines that move quickly during the lunch rush.  Bren - who has worked here for years - is a doll.  I'll be back!
Old City and Passero's have some of the BEST coffee drinks in Philly. I had a delicious Cafe au lait here for under $3.00.  Remember - "Friends don't let Friends drink Charbucks!"

Don't get me started. It was the Time Warner mega-monopoly when I lived in NYC and now this.  The Comcast monopoly.  A neccessary evil in which my family pays just over $100 bucks a month to have the priviledge of watching frikkin' TV.  The bill is always wrong, always too high and I am ALWAYS put on hold for between 12 and 22 minutes each and every time I call to threaten to leave unless they lower my bill - which they occaisionally, reluctantly will.  I was on a 6 month "promotion" that ran out and for whatever reason they just couldn't find another "promotion code" that would work.  And on and on and on it goes.  "May I speak to your supervisor?" -No!!!!  I was put on hold AGAIN!!!!  Alas, my apartment building has Comcast for their carrier and no satellite TV is permitted, so we are SOL.  In addition, each day I get to walk past the shrine to Comcast - yes, oh yes, the GORGEOUS Comcast Center with it's multi-million dollar screen in the lobby and over-priced chi-chi food court and programable fountains out front.  This hommage to COMCAST turns my stomach when I think of my $100 a month  (for cable and internet - sheesh there's no way in holy hell I'm gonna give them ny phone bill, too - you'll have to read my rant on verizon which also blows.) and all the other citizen's of Philadelphia who wait ON HOLD for the priviledge of paying over $100 a month so our kids can watch PBS Sprout.  I hope this yelp review will not preclude me from future employment. I could have cursed alot more and said some truly evil things - all of which are true - but you NEVER KNOW when Comcast will need a kick-ass technology trainer.  (That'd be moi.)
Came back a second time for a "regular" $14 mani. Yu is a real pro and I love her!  I also like Tina who did my pedi last time and gives a great massage.  I will be a regular at 4 sisters for sure!

It is rare for me to give a 1 star review but, frankly, I am aggravated. A good friend of mine & I decided to go for manicures on July 3 (The Thursday before a BIG holiday weekend.)  After deciding not to go to another neaby salon which was packed (overbooked) and could not see us for about 40 minutes, we took a gamble and came into Gateway Nails.  "Oh, this looks nice!" I exclaimed as we entered.  A tall blond receptionist hastily asked what we wanted and brusquely informed us that they were very busy (as we expected - and as we could see)  We decided to wait, and I took my time browsing the Gel, Vinylux and traditional polish colors.  Since a manicure is $14 plus there is a $5 soak-off fee, i figured i'd just get a gel - since that is what I usually get.  Gel mani's are $30 here.   I wanted to ask about the Vinyluxx - but the lady was so hurried and rude and barked at me to "Wait a minute".  She really was unpleasant.  So my friend and I left.  i really don't think I'll ever go back. We were prepared to spend good money there, too. It's a shame.  She lost 2 potential clients.

Sterling Pig is yet another creation by the same guy who brought Media Diego's (OK), Belle Epoque (Can be great can also be so-so) and Picasso (Not good - and shares the SAME KITCHEN as Belle).  Decor is Rustic at SPB and my husband enjoyed a specialty IPA.  ($6). The food is way, way over priced especially for the meh quality.  My Flank Steak salad had a small portion of delicious sliced steak over a bed of boring mixed greens with 3 (no kidding, 3) tiny cubes of diced tomato.  I asked for more tomatoes and they were brought.  No cucumbers were  available.  For $16 that is kinda steep.  DH also had flank steak - his was also a small portion (too small in his opinion) served with grilled zucchini, red and yellow peppers.  $22.  (Whoa.)  Our kid had the pulled pork sandwich ($14) sans coleslaw.  It was very smoky and kinda dry.  She added BBQ sauce to it.  Brioche bun was tasty.    The fries that came with the sandwich could be a memoir all their own.  They literally glistened with grease and were so oil-soaked it was almost comical.  They were presented in a cute "mini fry-basket" lined with paper that el kiddo said "was (clearly) not doing it's job". No way for $6 I would have ordered a separate side of these oil-slick fries.  Unless I am dragged here by fellow Media-ites, I am in absolutely no hurry to return to SPB.  Stick to the beer and you'll be fine.
Convenient and easy to get in & out. I have never come here for prescriptions - only to pick up a few items here & there.\ No issues for me.

Lots of fun to poke around the old-time-feeling Booth's Corner's Farmers Market.  Not as much produce and food as I expected - and alot more gift and knick-knack shops - even a LAWYER has a stall here.  I especially like Esh's Eggs and Stoltfuz meats and produce.  Only open Friday - Sunday. Wish they had more days open.

Had GREAT service when refilling a prescription here early today at 7:55 AM. Pharmacy Manager (female) is very sweet and entered my new insurance information and got me my medication promptly.  No issues.

Christmas Tree Shops were soooo great when they were a Cape Cod original.  They are now owned by the conglomerate that owns Home Goods & Marshalls.  So yes, you can still get great deals here on home decor and knick knacks - but it also has more of a "Dollar Store" feel to it.  Meanwhile if you are planning a party, wedding, event or Holiday-themed get together - you really should check out the DIY items and paper goods available here.  Also a good deal on certain PET SUPPLIES and random summer items.  Changes seasonally so check back often.

Love Kremp's!  They did 2 mother's day orders (my mom and MIL) as well as an Easter order for me this year.  Less than $150 for all 3 orders and just the flowers I wanted.  (No filler, no cheap glass vase.)  So pleased!  We love Kremp's and a shout out to Leslie Kremp!

Located in a Shopping Center in Plumsteadville - of all places - this place has decent NY style Neapolitan pies.  Get one fresh made - as the pre-made slices can vary in quality depending on when they were made - but you CAN'T go wrong with a fresh baked pie from here.  Cheesy and not too greasy.  Good stuff.

I have no issues here - I never dine in - I stop in for breakfast usually a Whole wheat "Bagel-Thin" with low-fat veggie cream cheese, tomatoes & cukes.  The spinach & cheese "specialty" bagel looks great but i can't seem to justify the calories.  I never get coffee here - I don't love it.  I prefer Charbucks or Dunkin'.

A nice array of whole and fileted fish, frozen crustaceans, battered ready-to-fry items and smoked salmons.  You can also have a seafood meal prepared to eat at the market - but I have never done this.  I have bought shrimp and Halibut here both were fine. (Fresh and not fishy smelling.)
We get loaves of sourdough through our company's CSA through Philly bread - big, perfect loaves that smeel and taste so good.  Eat them when they're fresh.  Carb-a-licious!

Had an amazing experience - and impeccable service from Michael - at White Dog for an Early (5 PM) Friday night.  The seafood platter for two is expensive but amazing.  4 oysters, 4 perfect shrimp, Tuna Tartar ($16 on its own for a larger serving) (delicious) and delectable lump lumps of crabmeat.  The famous mushroom soup is a rich treat. Try the Cauliflower with parmesan, too. Crab rolls (like a lobster roll) were sweetened with honey (odd but great) ad served on a hot dog bun.  (Decidedly un-white-dog).  $18.  A strawberry bellini ($10) was so good I could have downed 3 of them. The cheese plate for dessert ($16 for 3 selections) was terrific, too.  Try the red leaf goat cheese.  Quince, Honey, Apples. Dried Cherries and MARCONA Almonds, baby!  I am in my happy place.

Billy sells his home-made salami, sausages and charcuterie (sp??) at the Media Farmers Market on Thursday from 3-7.  Nice guy and best of all - a top-quality product.  (Uses some D'Artagnan and other more local sources.)  The porkette with broccoli rabe and provolone is terrific. As is the Chicken sausage with spinach and sharp provolone (a bit salty).  Can't wait to get some more.

My 9 year old loved it here but I think Yogurtissimo (on State Stree) is better. There is no free water - luckily we brought some or we'd have had to buy 2 bottles.  The yogurt itself seemed fine but the toppings were not as fresh (fruit looked mushy) and more candy-based.  (Of course the kid loved that) Also the cute orange & green decor while fun to look at - the chairs are not comfortable.  At all.  Lady at the front was nice - and ran the place single-handedly.  We'll return if my kid wants to - but I would not go here again on my own volition.
Well run store with helpful staff. No issues.  Got in & out quickly - even the weekend before Xmas.

Fail. While the service from our young, tattooed and under-educated server was good.  Attentive and pleasant, the food is just awful.  DO NOT order the Chicken Francese - a gloppy, gloopy over-sauced mess served over a bed of mushy overcooked pasta.  Salad bar was just OK.  Broiled Seafood platter (all frozen) was a bland JOKE and a waste of $20.  Not goin' back.

For whatever reason it was busy in here on a Thursday "after work" - around 5 PM. I had the famous "free panty" coupon - but I also needed some 5 for $26 cotton undies and was in DIRE need of hosiery - as mine had a run.  The pantyhose I selected?  $16.  No sale! Yikes.  Meanwhile the line was pretty long to check out but they got another lady to open a second register and that helped.  The usual Icky Vicky experience.

Not bad.  A homey little place for pizza and sandwiches. Beverly, the sassy waitress will bring you your order and a sunny smile.  The Red veggie pie (no sauce) was delicious and at $8.50 for a small was perfect for 2 of us to share.  Once time for lunch I had a tasty tuna melt.   The dining room can get very crowded (and loud) at lunch time so come right at or before 12 noon to get a seat.  Oh - and that home-made Lemon Crunch cake looked mighty tempting.  Maybe next time...

OK, first of all, I am not gay - I am a straight, married, corporate chick with a young kid and a pug dog - and I LOVE WOODY's.  I come by myself on Wednesday Nights for the best cheap Italian food around - and an Arnold Palmer.  The gay community is alive & well at Woody's and the DJs have the tunes pumpin' - but I go early and have a quiet little dinner.  Usually I get the fabulous Chicken Francese or Marsala.  They serve the meals with fresh bread, a plate of Olive Oil and a roasted long-hot pepper.  The crabmeat salad - appetizer or entree size (I get the small one and it's still huge) is fresh and tasty.  The pasta is al dente.  And... the eye candy is a bonus - even for a straight-chick like me.
5 stars for a great massage with Tierra (who is still there thank goodness). Go see her now!  I love coming to Tommi - they treat me very well.
Needed a drug test (aka Pee in a Cup) for a new job. Got in & out as a walk-in although there was a LONG line at opening.  No issues.

They are going out of business in late August so get there NOW to pick through the last of their gorgeous dresses, separates  and prom-worthy Formal gowns all for 40% off.  We will miss it here. Sorella's always carried beautiful clothes.

Old-school toy stores are getting harder and harder to find (Thanks a lot, Toyz-R-Hell!) so Pun's really saved us a few years back when our then 4 year old needed a hard to find plush Gund toy.  Pun's found it for us!  Excellent.

So very pleased with the food & service here.  The ladies at the counter are terrific! I am now a semi-regular and get both eat-in and take out lunches here.  A little pricey *(I spent close to $13 today) but I get nearly 2 meals out of it.  (Or a meal and a snack).  And now - my 10 year old kid is hooked.  She loves the food here.  The Doner and Barg are my faves (as a platter).
A very good hospital but extremely long waits in the ER for triage and care.  Unacceptable to wait 75 minutes with a 9 year old.

This Starbucks just moved "down the street" from the Paoli train Station (where there was NO PARKING) to here - where the old Burger King used to be.    I have not yet gone into the store, but I used the convenient drive-thru today and got in & out quickly.  Glad there is parking!

This is a GREAT restaurant and it's more American than Italian.  Quiche and sammies for lunch and yummy pierogies.  (Yes, really.)  We love coming here to de-compress after Peddler's Village madness.  Good service and good homey food.
It's OK.  Not great (and certainly not 5 star), but it's passable for an urban supermarket.  Big pluses - home delivery and Italian products.

Somewhere between Meh and OK.  We bought a laptop from Best Buy yesterday and waived all their extra charges for geek squad and useless warranties.  Now if anything goes wrong, we're on our own.   Oh - and we waived the $99 installaion fee - so we are installing MS Office ourselves (this isn't rocket science, people).   The 17 year old high school student who helped us (Nick) was reasonably intelligent and put up with my husband and I agruing while our 7 year old was bored as hell and getting whiny.  What a drag...  Meanwhile - still a decent value for laptops and big-screen TVs.
Great cupcakes - in particular the straberry shortcake - which doeesn't even contain any chocolate.  They serve 4-5 kinds of hot chocolate.  It's such a fun and SWEET place.  Alas, no nudity.

This Domino's is located right next door to where my 9 year old gets her hair cut, so one day she was famished so I ordered her a small plain pie (plenty left to take home) and it was ready in 12 minutes.  Do I like dominos?  No. Has their quality improved lately?  Yes.  And the staff here are friendly and attentive.  Grease-laden, high caloric and NOT my thing - but in a pinch - it's OK.  Take out only.  Large delivery radius.

Things are getting better & better every time I visit Tommi. Today I was up at the CRACK of dawn (on a Saturday anyway) to snag a 9 AM appointment with Vera - a russian facialist/esthetician with 20 years of experience.  I am a former esthetician myself and extremely picky about facials and who I let go near my face.  Vera is terrific.  the products (she used primarily anti-oxidant/anti-aging stuff on me - it's nearly winter and my skin gets dry) are gentle and hydrating. The facial lasted exactly 60 minutes (I was seen at 9:05 and got out at 10:05 AM). I wish I could remember the name of the product line - it starts with an "H" and I had never seen it before.  The grapeseed scrub and anti-oxidant mask were nice - and I may purchase.  I respect her opinions and trust Vera.  I will definitely come see her again (but probably not for a while since I tend to do alot of my own skincare.)  Next up - I am due for a massage and booked an appointment for December.  I will let you all know!

I give Smoke's 5 stars for one reason.  Kenn Kweder.  Yes.  I love this man. Really.  But not in a sick, stalker, psycho kinda way.  Anyhow I spent many a late night in the early nineties watching Kenn and drinking watered down gin & tonics and eating greasy chicken wings.  Back then you could even SMOKE inside Smokes.  Ah the good old days.  Jammed with Penn Kids - but the nostalgia factor runs high for me here.

Quick cheap and good for college students.  Let me just say that the last time I was in Beijing was 1995.  Really. I am amazed it's still here.  It's becoming a Penn institution.  Back in the day I'd get the lunch specials. CHicken & Brocolli or Steamed Shrimp & Veggies.  More than a few orders of thick doughy dumplings, too.  (Not the greatest by any stretch.)  Quick and cheap.  Not superb - but a good value.

Excellent choice for a casual lunch, and on a nice day you can sit outside.  I got the "Breeders combo" (The restaurant is dog themed) with a 1/2 size Cobb Salad and a cup of delicious lobster bisque (not much lobster in it, but still tasty).  Next time I will try the mushroom bisque.  They have alotta bisques - and chicken noodle.  The sandwich my friend got look great, too.  Can't wait to come back. Hannah (Cashier and later in dining area) was a doll.
CUtesy doggie boutique with EXPENSIVE treats and toys.  Cute outfits, leashes, collars and everything your pooch could want.  But you'll pay for it!

Yumi (Server/hostess) is a doll and always treats us so well whether I come alone for lunch or with a friend or my 10 year old (who, incidentally, loves it here).   Today I tried the Pork Dumpling soup and was so pleasantly surprised by how wonderful it was.  3 gyoza (likely frozen - but so tasty) and a savory broth - but best of all?  Chock full of veggies - napa Cabbage, Carrots, Shredded Snow Peas (so sweet) and Mushroom slivers.  I LOVED IT.  The $13.95 Chirashi lunch is a steal - a la cart there is a good $20 worth of tuna, salmon, yellowtail, fluke (or some other white fish) and snapper on the plate.  No 5th star?  Frozen tamago. How I long for good home-made tamago!  Meanwhile, I enjoy the food here very much - and now they know me!

You get what you pay for - yeah it's cheap to fly Southwest but everything costs extra. Want to board first (so that you have a snowball's chance in hell of getting overhead space for your luggage)?  Pay for it. I absolutely loathe their "cattle call" approach to seating.  Need a snack?  Pay for it.  Want to be able to change your ticket or G-d forbid refund it?  Pay more for it again.  Yikes.  Flying in this country sucks in general and Southwest can suck a little less (or alittle more depending on your viewpoint).  Bon frikkin' Voyage!

Came here again (and again) and it's still greta and still a great value at $8/95 for a 3 course sit down lunch.  Masaman Curry or Pad-See_Ew are my faves here.  Soooo tasty.  And Pookie - one of the servers - is a doll.

We had already discovered Darlings as a great spot to take our 3 year old for Mac 'n Cheese (there's is so yummy) before we decided to plan a playdate at the Please Touch Museum.  After the playdate we pre-arranged with Darlings (they are so very small) to have all 6 kids and about 9 parents drop by for lunch at 1 PM.  Darlings was great about us taking over the joint.  The kids had PB & J and of course plently of mac 'n cheese.  The parents had lots of cheesecake and mexi-bowls (can't remember the excact name) but it's like a bowl of rice, beans, taco meat and Mexican fisings.  Very yummy.  No a/c (ugh) and they take CASH ONLY so be forewarned.  A great place to eat after going to the Please Touch or Franklin Institute.

Meh.  It's really small - and has a coffee bar, a bar and ONE (lame menu) burger-bar food based restaurant.  Lots of slots and a few table games.  Not my bag, baby.  Honestly?  Were it not for proximity - I would NEVER come to Sugarhouse - I'd sooner go to AC or even Bethlehem, PA.  Philly fought long & hard to get a casino - and THIS is what they get?  Sorry - Unimpressed.

They re-modeled.  Looks much cleaner now.  I am not a big DD fan - but the coffee is fine.  I don't eat the donuts (which are not freshly baked - and usually taste stale to me) and NEVER eat the 400 PLUS calorie breakfast grease-wiches.  It's a good place to get a Vanilla Iced Decaf or a quick cup of joe when it's cold out.  And they sell gift cards - a good $5.00 "I don't know what the hell to get the mailroom guy" gift.  But that's all.

A cute men's tie store in the bottom of Liberty Place.  Too expensive unless you get a sale item.  Ties are colorful and nicely displayed. Medium quality (not high end, not cheapies.).  Need a tie badly?  Pick one up here. Or an ascot or pocket square.  Or a lame father's day gift.

Vitamin Shop is a huge chain and offers nearly every supplement you can imagine.  Just be careful as some are animal derived (if you are a vegan - you gotta be really careful at TVS) and many come from lab created sources.  A good place to pick up some Co-Q 10.  (I'm a big fan of my Co-Q.)  They are a huge chain - and if you get the membership card - there can be some good deals.
Some of the best popcorn, bulk-roasted in-shell peanuts and chocolate covered treats (pretzels, graham crackers) in Philly.  Such a fun little place crammed with snackies.

Yuck.  I really loather chain restaurants and Chili's is no exception.  The one nice this about this Chili's is it's proximity to the Penn Campus and the universally cheap and greasy burgers and other fried foods are the same at any Chili's nation wide.  It's kinda dirty in here - and the place is run by teenagers.  I guess it beats TGI Friday's - but not by much.

I am back in the area - and now the owners know me - and they REMEMBERED me. I just love the lunch specials here (huge portions - I take about 40-50% home) and so delicious. Fresh, hot pita.  Delicious sides and sauces, and fluffy long-grain rice (Persian Style).  Chicken, Beef, LAMB - so juicy and savory and wonderful.  I have missed it here - and now I will be back - at least until early 2-17.  Don't forget they serve a terrific dinner, too - for take out or dine in.  (Very casual for dine in.)  Much love to the crew at Kabab Café.  Keep doing what you are doing.

Excellent service from Brett. I had been avoiding coming here for years as it never appealed from the outside and I was certain it would be "just a bar" on the inside.  And I am partially right.  However - when surrounded by good friends and great conversation - we had great food and service as well. Maybe the stars were properly aligned?  Or maybe I am de-volving into a Delco chick?  I had a BLT with Avocado with sweet potato fries and it was perfect.  For $5.25 my "well drink" of cheap vodka, cranberry juice and a splash of seltzer was just F.I.N.E. fine.  Live (loud) music - even on a Tuesday night at 10 PM.  I do believe I shall return. Pleasantly - even shockingly surprised.

Yes, Tom A.  everyone IS right.  Total mediocrity and a neccessary evil.  Philadelphia has a piss-poor number of grocery stores and supermarkets.  The Superfresh kinda sucks, the Pathmark is ghetto and this ACME is barely passable.  We come here when we don't wanna deal with Superfresh's picked-over produce.  And then we'll come here and it'll be just as bad with a  picked over dairy case.  CHECK YOUR FRESHNESS DATES on meat and dairy products especially.  We found yogurt that was 2 weeks past it's date.  (We told the manager who promptly pulled it off the shelves.)  Be careful.  Like Superfresh and Pathmark (which are also filthy), ACME could use a good cleaning.  The floors are just nasty.

4 stars for $6.99 Taco Tuesdays - I usually get the fish tacos (You get 2 tacos and a side of Beans).  You have to get it to go.  I also get a (pricey) $2.50 Strawberry Ginger Iced Tea (They Used Premium Steap teas and I love them).  Fast service - especially if you call your order in and then go pick it up.

A centrally located, convenient Walgreens.  I have had a few prescriptions filled here and the lines are better than the CRAZY CVS on 19 & Chestnut.    Happy it's here.  Photo processing is decent, too.
Stopped in once while in 30th Street - looked around and left. I'm not a big fan of Au Bon Pain.
OK - they did it!  They got the 5th Star (but I also do love Salumeria for my grating cheeses).  What a great place.

I have known Michael Colabelli (I just KNOW I spelled that wrong) for years - since the '80's - and his father before him who owned the shop (It's now it the 3rd and 4th generation.    They are a well-run business that has stood the test of time and provide affordable cuts and GREAT colors to the Penn campus and beyond.  I love them.

Panera is one of those "chain" pseudo-fast food places that seems like it would be great - but the calorie and sodium counts on most dishes (except salads) are super high.  The 1/2 order of pasta whas over 500 cals! That said, my 9 year old likes the mac & (gloppy white cheddar) cheese here. I had a shrimp salad that had 4 smal shrimp it it.  Lunch for 2 was over $20 with NO DRINKS. Yikes! Kinda high for fast food, don't ya think?  This place is new - only about 6 months old - so it is still very clean and seemingly well-run.

I had a much, much better experience a few years later at the Victoria's secret in Glen Mills (Brinton Lake Shopping Center).  I came in November early for holiday shoppig and was able to get some leggings and a pre-boxed (yeah, I am a sucka for cute packaging) loungewear PINK set for my 13 year old.  She will be happy and I got my one, lonely free panty.  She gets $115 worth of stuff and I get one. lonely. panty.  Gotta love motherhood.  The new store manager is terrific - I sure wish i could remember her name - she told me but I forgot.  She is friendly and great.
Go take your kids to a BlueRocks game - it's such fun - the seats are all good ones - and it's affordable, family fun.  We love coming here for BlueRocks games.  And don't forget Mr. Celery!
I have known Jay Sand & his wife since High School and this is a truly wonderful program.  He has always been a talented guy - and this proves it.  Kids just thrive here.

I was excited to try this place - but also bummed when I found out that Ong's Noodle House (the former restaruant in this sapce) had closed.  But the gorgeous fresh coat of green paint and renovated bathrroms and dining area - along with a Half Chinese/Half Sushi Bar menu had me!  So last Friday me, my husband and our active 4 year old daughter dropped in for a quick dinner.  DD's gyoza were the best part of the meal - freshly cooked and perfect. (Even if frozen.)  DH had a greasy, heavy chicken lo mein, and a spicy tuna roll that he enjoyed. I tried a specialty roll - at $11.95 I expected better.  It was stuffed with Shrimp Tempura and Cucumber and coated with spicy tuna (not the best I've had but OK).    What killed it was they literally DUMPED a load of Tempura Flakes all over it.  Now don't get me wrong - I like tempura "crunch" but this was over kill.  I also ordered a green salad.  I should have known better and ordered the ultra-sweet orangey-ginger dressing (again - I've had better) on the side.  The iceberg lettuce and sigle slice of tomato were fresh and crisp.  Not gourmet - but good.  It's a solid 3 star joint.

I am torn between 3 and 4 stars.  The prices are high for what you get.  My husband and I came here on a weeknight - and the bar area was PACKED.  We found out later that there are 2 for 1 roll specials at the bar.  Sure wish we had known that before we sat in the dining area.  Oh well.  Our server was friendly and attentive - and had GORGEOUS hair. (Irrelevant - but fun to know).  We ordered drinks ($7.25 for a White Cape Codder - essentially vodka and white cranberry juice) and perused the menu.  I walked over to the sushi bar to stare at the fish.  Looked good - but the tuna looked not-so-fresh.  Meanwhile we ordered some rolls - the "Crystal Palace" topped with chunks of lobster - was a stand out.  The "Wilmington (aka Fattening) Roll" was deep fried salmon and mayo and onion.  Not for me!  The $10 order of 4 "lobster" shumai came in a rich, delicious cream sauce - but the dumplings themselves contained very little lobster (nearly all filler) and were not worth the money.  We did not have dessert.  I liked it here - and it has a sexy "bar-type" vibe.  Good for a date place. Would i rush back here?  Nope.  Doma or Shiroi in Center City Philly are more my thing.  That said, this is probably the best sushi you can hope for in Wilmington.

Closing for good on April 30.  (Final open mic and party on April 27 & 28). I will miss Thursday night Musical Quizzo with DJ Big Mike M. I will miss Brett H., the best server I have ever known.  I will not miss the grotty digs that were sorely in need of a renovation nor the overpriced and average bar food.  Thanks for many years of service to the Media area. You shall be missed.

Kennedy Fried Chicken serves all the typical fried foods and burgers as well as a few "halal-style" (Gyro over rice, Chicken over rice or salad) platters.  It is not $4- $6 - more like $7 - $9 - I got a gyro platter over rice with a drink for $8.99. Nicer than NY Fried Chicken down the street - and better service but you pay a buck or two more.  The grilled shrimp is way, way over seasoned.  They also sell about 8 flavors of ice cream.  Super fast.

I had a mediocre at best experience here.  I would NEVER get a pedicure here.  I came here once to try it out (on just a mani) and I won't return.  First of all, it's very cramped in there - and if you don't have an appointment, you could be waiting a while.  The techs are mostly Asian and don't speak alot of english.  The lady I had seemed very rushed to get me done and get onto the next client.  They do not offer massage.  Whatever.  El-Cheapo rushed, basic mani.  I won't be back.
I needed keys made - and even though the place was mobbed (the Sunday of Thanksgiving weekend) I zipped in and out and the lady made my 2 keys and they WORKED.  Yay!

Decent rates, smallish but clean rooms. In-house Starbucks and a small mediocre restaurant - and Chili's for room service (What-ehv).  VERY convenient location though - you can walk to everything and you are steps away from the Broad Street Line.  Added bonus:  watch the "Parade of Lawyer" and jurors march into court on weekday mornings.  Added risk:  MANY homeless panhandlers abound.

I am torn between 4 and 5 stars.  I love to get fresh dairy cheeses here and also Grana Padano and other Grating cheeses.  The line can get lengthy as they serve each person as an individual (which is nice.)  Worth the wait for yummy cheese!!!!

My husband ran in here today for an EMERGENCY pie to take to his brother who is stuck at HUP and craving Pizza.  He ordered a calzone and a Quattro (pick 4 toppings - one per 1/4 of the pie).  He said everything was fine.  Thin crust, decent toppings and since the pie was made fresh to order it was tasty and good. (Not stale).

I am NOT a temple student.  I got a take out menu from here in my building and stared at it for weeks before taking the plunge.  Last night I justs DID NOT want to cook, so I ordered food for myself, 5 year old DD and DH (who decided not to eat any).  The order took 45 minutes to arrive and was wrong when it got here, plus I was charged for 2 $4.99 orders of items I never ordered.  "Ron " on the phone has said he will be refunding my credit card, so I am on the lookout for that refund.  Meanwhile the food we did order was good.  Fried dumplings ($4.99 for tem) were crisp and tasty.  $1.00 each for spring rolls (also fried - it was a fried food fiesta) were good too.  Tempura shrimp was stuffed with a SPICY sauce.  Won;t be ordering that again.  The main dish - Bul gogi was very good, but a bit scant on the meat (but wha'dya want for $7.99).  In my opinion Goji is much better food, but for take-out this Korean/Japanese hybrid is a great alternative to Chines or Pizza.  We will order again - next time from "The Line".  Or maybe a Bibim Bap.  I loves me a good bap!  If you are a student and live on take-out - we suggest you give Koja a try.  Just read your receipt!!!!

Talluto's, Caludio's , DiBruno's, Spice Corner, Superior Ravioil...  The stuff of culinary dreams. I am loving the Italian Market soooooo much. What a treasure to Philadelphia.  Fresh fruit & veggies - and all the great Italian meats, cheeses and olives - plus fresh pasta and ravioli from 2 great sources.  I'm in love.

This is NOT closed - in fact, it recently opened to the public in Nov. 2010 and is GORGEOUS.  A content-rich (spend 2-3 hours there easily, 90 minutes is too little) 4 story museum that chronicles American Jewish life since the mid 1600's.  I became a member (just $54 for 1 person, $72 for a couple) which gets you free admission for an entire year.  I can't wait to go back, as I did not get to see (or rather read - there's alot to read) everything I wanted to.  Oh - and they have a Kosher-Dairy cafe with Matzo Ball soup, Kugel, tuna & egg salad and other tasty looking food!

I've had Old City iced coffee many, many times at the RTM location.  I like that they keep the milk IN THE FRIDGE (not sitting out in pitchers) and pour you as much or as little as you wish (soy, skim, whole or half 'n half).  Thanks for NOT being a Charbucks.  Great coffee and a fun place to just hang out. And a pleasant older gentleman and a nice young lady barrista to boot!  I love the coffee at Old City Coffee.  I will continue to come here.

Not bad for a chain.  My 3 year old daughter likes to watch the "pizza man" make pizza - so she, of course, loves it here.  It's better than Olive Garden - but not as good as Bensi's - in the "Scheme of mock-Italian chains".  It is also less noisy in atmosphere and decor than the obnoxious Buca di Beppo.  I'd go here if it was nearby - but would NOT go out of my way to eat here. At least it's not too expensive.

Went here for an eat-in lunch for the first time ever!  (I come here alot for breakfast but it's always grab 'n go.)  Was it ever good.  We were seating promptly by Tony - the sassy waitress, and offered water (or whatever we'd like to drink) right away.  Both I and my dining companion ordered the "Greek Chicken" special.  A grilled (or breaded if you like) chicken breast topped with melted provolone and FRESH, green spinach leaves.  Mnnn!  So great.  In lieu of fries (I don't do fried), I got green beans - and I expected diner-esque.  They were anything but!  The grean beans were bright, green, crisp and perfectly seasoned with a bit of garlic salt.  TASTY STUFF.  The meal was served with a roll & butter - and for whatever reason, when Tony asked "You wanna roll & butter?" I said yes.   Another pleasant surprise!  A braided, yellow egg roll (like a mini challah bun) appeared, quartered and perfectly buttered.  Alas, my thighs, I ate the carbs!  A delightful inexpensive lunch, served on paper plates, eaten with plastic silverware, in the company of local cops and working folk.  Oh - lunch costs $10 bucks exact including tax 'n tip.  Pay up front!  I heart Yonni's.

Catered hoagie trays for a corporate lunch - and it was fine.  Ham, turkey and roastbeef on seeded rolls, lettuce, tomatoes and cheap white American cheese.  (Mayo pre-spread on the turkey hoagie-piece I ate.)  Served with may small bags of Herr's chips.  No issues.

This City Nails is not owned by the same people as the $hi*ty  nails on South 17th Street.  This place is marginally cleaner and better run - but it's still a far cry from clean, sleek & luxurious.  What it is is cheap and, for some, convenient.  The ladies will shout "Peek-collah" at you when you arrive.  I usually bring my own base & top coats as I do not care for the no-name  base coat they use.  I would NEVER get a pedi here.  I am uber-picky about pedis and only get them at Spa Elysium from Cheryl Lee.
This Wawa is always PACKED and people are coming & going. Decent restrooms and a reliable place to get coffee, food etc.  No issues.

Solid.  A good choice for salads - and even noodle bowls.  You pick the ingredients and can control calories and fat.  Pleasant "green" sleek decor.  I tend to stick with the salads - but a few of the bowls and soups look (more carb-heavy) good.

How in the world do you rate a stop on the MFL?  Relative to others?  This one, as many are, is dirty and gross.  It is convenient to Penn and Drexel and other University City areas.  As David mentioned you can't buy tokens here - but I use a pass anyway.  Be careful at night - as is common sense in any major city.

I hadn't been back here for years - but I needed a masage in the worst way so I booked 30 minutes with Gabby (she's terrific, by the way) and was so pleasantly surprised by the renovations to thelobby floor, the privacy of the rooms (They have DOORS now - not just fabric panels.  I will be back - at $45 for 30 minutes ($80 for an hour) it's great in a pinch.

5 star service from Vera and 3.5 star (heavy, carbo-loaded, caloric) food. A gal-pal and I shared the whopping-huge "Marco's Meal" and took home most of it.  With the $42.95 (We paid $52.95 - as we each opted for upgraded entrée choices) you get EITHER an appetizer (we got the $10.95 stuffed mushrooms - very good.) OR 2 small side salads.  Then you pick 2 entrees (Classic pastas only.  If you want "special pastas" or a chicken dish - pay $5 more).    Then you get 2 "classic" pastas (cold and pre-prepared/wrapped that morning) to take home.  And ANY dessert you want to share (we got the $7.95 hunk-o'-cheesecake).  But VERA (serving here for about a decade!) is the best part of all.  She is hilarious and warm and wonderful.  Is the food "haute"?  "Fine cuisine"?  Heck, no.  This is a chain. The digs are cafeteria-meets-checkered table cloth "Faux-talian".  But we had fun - and left with enough for 2 more meals.  Easily!  P.S.  The pricey cappuccinos here are actually GREAT.  Get a cappuccino in lieu of dessert.  Good stuff!

I had a surprisingly delightful (yes, delightful) lunch at Champps - and my expectations were not high (I have dined at another Champps and am not a big fan).  Someone else paid (add a star right there). Lunch special of pasta (any kind you wished) and a 1/2 size greek salad were very good.  HUGE portions of run-of-the-mill formula cooking - but if you choose wisely you can get a decent meal here.  Tip:  Come after the lunch rush (we were here around 1:30 PM) during the week when the place is much less crowded.  So surprised I liked it as much as I did.
Consistently good. Had a 3-roll maki combo lunch for $11.95 which is a great value (comes with salad only for take out, sould and salad when you eat in).  Try the crispy eggplant app - so good!

A great find!  A wee bit more expensive (mani is $14, gel mani 424, Pedi $25, spa pedi $47 - mani-pedi combo is $35) than the usual - but a better service.  Tina did a great mani-pedi for me and got me out the door in time for an imprtant meeting.  I will definitely be back.  Cash for tip - but credit card is OK.
Cute shops, restaurants, a hair salon and outdoor events in the spring & summer.  I fun place for sure!  Parking can be a trick though - so I take a bus and walk a few blocks.

Had another FABULOUS facial (this time no Groupon so the full price is $90 - but still worth it in my opinion - if you get Larissa or Liana.  Lan is gone.)  I also love massages with Tierra (as Cliff has also left).  They treat me so well here now that I really can't think about going ayywhere else. (Except for the occaisional jaunt to Ursula's).  Beautiful spa with great staff. An now that the receptionist downstairs is actually friendly, I am sold on Tommi.  I just wish they'd put a little more effort into the esthetics "backbar" and use better known products. (Or at least products where clients can purchase the retail equivalent.)  A plus:  Tommi carries (a little bit of) the Hylunia line - which is little known but very good.  (The grapeseed scrub is awesome.

Yay!  I am the first to review!  Oh, I have such sentimentality for Borghi's - so perhpas my 4 stars should not be 4 - but merely 3?  But my (now husband then) boyfriend and I had our first ROMANTIC (third real) date at Borghi's back in 2005 and the meal was great (and dessert was even better - hubba, hubba).  We attempted to have our wedding rehearsal dinner here in 2008 but it was just cost prohibitive for our large group.  Dino, the owner, was very nice to work with and I am sure this would be a great place to have an anniversary or birthday (special occiasion) meal or party.  We enjoyed the veal chicken and pasta dishes we had (both back in 2005 and more recently.).  My parents don't really like it - they think it's too expensive - but I say for a special occaision - Borghi's is a great place.  And it's in the historic Chalfont Inn Building - which is easy to find.  (Right on 202.)  Please leave your young children at home.
I had no issues - and decent service when I popped in on a Sunday afternoon to get a dozen donuts (for 7 hungry kids) and an iced latte (for me).  In and out quickly.

Always crowded at peak lunch times - especially when its raining.  Loaded with lawyers and other corporate types, the $16 grilled fish is wonderful for a healthier choice.  They also have burgers and a wonderful veggie burger wrap.  Nice addition to the area - and way more upscale than the Saladworks that used to be in this space.
This is a pretty "chi chi/shi shi" store for second hand womens fashion.You can actually find some great items here.  Not cheap, though - but way nicer than most consignment places.

We had PHENOMENAL service at Aloha (Happy) hour at Roy's last night. It started off rather rocky - my DD & I walked in (SHE wanted to go.  So I humoured her.)  The hostess seated us (reluctantly) at high tables overlooking the kitchen, but wecould not get the $5.00 bar specials there.  So we moved to the bar, but legally, DD can't sit there.  So we got a HIGH bar table at the edge ot the bar and ate some (decent not great) shumai, lobster potsticker (the best thing we had - very good buttery sauce) plate and lobster california roll. (Good - and comped by the manager).  The manager, Edward was terrific and even brought a BIG box of toys for DD to play with.  After our meal he gave us a tour of their private party rooms.  GREAT!  Hannan (spelling??) our servers was terrific as well.  OK food - and great service.  For $5.00 - a great deal.  Still have trouble believing this is a CHAIN.
Glad it's here - but it is expensive - you are paying for convenience.  Also the deli (Dietz & Watson) looked nice - but just didn't appeal.

My childhood classmate, Kim's parents own this and are accomplished musicians and music teachers.  Its a great (and long time) Bucks COunty resource for instruments, music lessons and all things folk.  Love it!

OK, I am updating my review and giving Jake's an extra star due to the wonderful customer service we received.  The man behind the counter recognixed us from yelp and automatically knew to cut my little daughter's slice in half and gave her a generous side of black olives, gratis.  They also now (sometimes) carry milk.  The pizza that night, also, was fresh and wonderful.  try to get pies when they are just coming out of the oven - or order a whole pie (we get a small, which is still way too much for the 2 of us) and that way it is guaranteed to be oven-fresh.  Yay, Jake's.  Our neighborhood pizza spot keeps getting better.

Cheap, decent, low-budget sushi (and bubble tea) tale out.  2 complaints?  No Hamachi (yellowtail) and all the "crab" is fake crabstick.  A plus?  Tasty "summer rolls".  Prices are moderate and it's a good place for take-out or a working lunch.  Glad they are around.  Curiously enough they also supply sushi to Friends Select school a few days a week.  Not a holy grail - but a great, quick sushi alternative - and right near Jefferson and the Gallery.

My mom (who's in her 60's) gets her hair set here every 1-2 weeks.  She used to see a great lady named Venus - but I think Venus is long gone.  For a quick, cheap blow-out or wash & set it's a good choice.

Uh Oh.  I should have trusted my instincts. I dropped off $85 worth of clothes today and she told me it would be cash or check only and I was like "What???" Plus it smelled just AWFUL in there.  (She wanted to charge me $13 for each dress - but I talked her down to $11 which is what my other cleaner charges.)  So against my better judgement I left my clothing there.  They are due to come back Thursday.  I pray they smell OK.  Wish I would have read these reviews first.  Lady was very nice but also pushy and I felt guilty not leaving my stuff there even though many red flags went up even before the whole "no credit card" thing.  It just smells HORRID in there.  I hope I do not get burned, I have a sneaking suspicion i may nee to take the clothes somewhere else and re-do them.  Fingers crossed. If I can please get my stuff back unscathed I highly doubt i will ever fall for this again.

A decent place to drop off shoes for a shine or minor repairs like new heels or soles.  I have had several pairs of leather loafers, 1/2 boots (ankle boots) and dress pumps shined here.  Decent prices and they have never lost anything.  That's a big plus.
This is a great (small) asset to the neighborhood.  Selling cases of beer, soda and ice.  Believe me - when you need it -it's great to have someone who sells ice.  Bring cash.

This review is for the pre-made sushi (in a refrigerated case at lunch time) only. The Salmon Avocado Roll (Alaskan) was excellent but the Phoenix roll (Tuna outside was fine, inside - not so fresh) was not as fresh as it should be.  In the mean time, so far, so good and I may return to try some cooked items.  $3.50 for the Alaskan Roll (It's $5 on the menu) and $6.75 for the Phoenix - which I will not order again.

I became a founding member and am so glad I did.  I have now been 5 times - and twice with my 7 year old who really enjoyed alot of the exhibits.  Great use of video and audio elements (and computers).  Great special events for members - and a nice gift shop and cafe.  The shop has great Hannukah and Passover gift items.  The "Members Night" is great - they open the museum from 6 - 8 PM and only members  and their guests can visit then.  It's quiet and peaceful.  We love it here.
A big Gold Crown Hallmark store in the Shopping Center at 252 & Rt. 3. Friendly staff and I went during a sale and got some good gifts very inexpensively.

Um - for this part of Philly it's not so bad - but compared to a "normal" Pier one?  It's kinda hectic in here at times and the displays get knocked around and messed up due to the crowds of Phjilly folk that rush on through.  A decent place for home decor, furniture and table ware. (Candles on sale are a good deal.)  Not a big fan though, due to the disheveled feeling of the store.

What choice have we got?  We live at Broad 'n Vine - and Jakes is 1 block away.  My little daughter LOVES it here and gets 1 slice with black olives.   She also loves to look at "the Mummer on the wall" - they have a pretty colorful mural of Philly-stuff all over the walls.  I have tried the pizza - which when fresh - is pretty decent.  The pastas are not worth the money - I can make this at home.  The Chicken Chees-steaks and Chicken Parm sandwiches are both good - and large.  My dad & I split a chicken parm last time we were there and It was plenty.  Note to moms:  They do not carry MILK - so bring your own.

I attended the NWCT (Network of Women in Computer Technology) annual conference in Center City and La Prima did the catered (hot) lunch.  The chicken francese, salad, rice pilaf, rolls & butter, and assorted dessert trays were all delicious and well presented in a buffet style.  Service by at least 5-6 uniformed serves was great also.  My one complaint?  The vegetarian option - penne pasta (Cold and swimming in oil) served with a caponata (way too vinegary) was not to my taste - but others enjoyed it.  I was glad they offered some veg-friendly fare.  Best of all - they use recycled materials wherever possible and are about as "green" as a caterer can be!
Still open!!!!  Thank goodness. Just got me some veal and chicken parm to stock the freezer for those nights when I just don't wanna cook.
