I like how it works here: you fill out your card with what you want and what you want in it, give it to the folks, pay, and they make it for you and bring it your table. I got my sushiritto with tuna and salmon and other stuff such as sweet onions, scallions and edamame. It took a while, but when it was finally delivered it was beautiful. It also came with two sauces on the side, but I decided to keep it simple and just add a little soy sauce.  The food was DELICIOUS. It was fresh and tasty and the flavors in my concoction blended together perfectly. Some of it fell apart as I ate, but that was no problem, I just went after those bits with my fork. I love eating things like this, because it's a healthier alternative to eating a burger or taking my weekly trip to the nearest Mexican restaurant. I like that they use "washable" dishes to cut down on waste, just be sure to put your dishes in the right place when you're finished.  The atmosphere of the restaurant is great and while it was pretty dead on the cold, rainy afternoon I was here, I can see that it's built to handle a crowd.  If you're a poke fan, or if you're curious about sushirittos, this spot is a must. The location is great, the staff is friendly and the food is delectable.

I wanted to update, because since I last reviewed I have gotten both mashed potatoes and red beans and rice here.  The mashed potatoes are good and they come with gravy.  I'm sure they are "instant", but who cares?  Other fast food places serve instant potatoes.  It's a convenience store and it's just as good as Popeyes, especially if you take them home and add some Crystal to them.  And yes, Brother's has red beans and rice!  Who knew?  I was really surprised at how good it was!  I'm actually going to "go there" and say that I prefer them over Popeyes!  They are more like actual homemade red beans and not the canned stuff that Popeyes is serving up these days.  Like I said before, pick some up and spice to flavor with some Crystal sauce and you are good to go.  When I get food here, I get the two piece white with a small mashed potato and it costs about $4.75, which is cheap and on top of that, they are open late.  Just sayin...  ;)

Decent fast food pizza.  Not as good as an actual pizza place like Rotolo's or even Papa John's, but it gets the job done.  The best thing about this place is the large pepperoni pizza for $5 and the really cheap bread sticks.  Not worth going out of your way for, but worth checking out, if you are in the mood for a quick bite.

I'm not a huge cook, so I don't make it here nearly as often as some people do. HKM has a nice assortment of Asian goodies of all types, including different fancy noodles, soy sauces, meat and fish. If you are looking to make anything Asian from pho to sushi, this is going to be your one stop shop.  I really liked that they sell fresh Spring rolls. You can get four really good sized ones for about $3, which can't be beat. On the day I went, they had pork and shrimp.  I'll definitely be back, HKM is an interesting place and you are bound to find something here that you will enjoy.

My boyfriend and I were here for date night after he said he had a craving for lobster and I can always go for oysters.  They don't take reservations, so we just stopped in a little before 7 on a Saturday night, and hoped for the best. It was pretty packed but, success: we were seated immediately! As I was looking over the menu I spotted shrimp and grits, and since I hadn't had that in while, I decided to go with that. We also ordered a dozen char broiled oysters.  As always, the oysters were out of this world. Char broiled oysters is one of my all time favorites and Drago's does theirs right with lots of butter and French bread so that you can sop up all of the buttery goodness once the oysters are gone. Then came the shrimp and grits and I loved their version! Big, fat peeled shrimp served with creamy grits, tasso (ham) and a sauce that is out of this world. I'm not sure exactly what was in the sauce, but it was rich and delicious. Talk about a dream come true! The grits were nice and creamy and they were topped with rosemary, which was a very nice touch. My boyfriend had a stuffed lobster which looked delicious and he enjoyed. I couldn't have been happier with all of the food.  Caleb was our waiter and he was excellent. Even though he was waiting on many tables, he was fast about taking our order, checked in on us regularly and had a friendly demeanor, which is always appreciated. I will absolutely go back for more of the goodies I had here.

I have a problem with Texas Roadhouse and I can maybe never go back as a result.    Hi. My name is Marielle and I'm addicted to fried pickles.  Yes, it's true.  I have a major problem saying saying "no" to the salty, fried little things and this place gives you a huge basket of them for only 4 bucks.  A major problem indeed.  I mean, I'm eating them and I know that they must be somewhat healthy...I mean, pickles are cucumbers and cucumbers are vegetables, right?  Yeah, I'm just gonna go with that.  Along with the fried pickles from God, I also got a pulled pork sandwich that came with steak fries.  I swear, this was so much food that I didn't know what to do with myself and I ended up taking most of it home.  The sandwich was ok.  I've had better, but this is a chain and you get chain food at a chain.  Kinda weird how that works out.  They also give you a basket of free bread with cinnamon butter when you order, so you will definitely leave this place satisfied.  Honestly, I'll be back for the fried pickles alone.  I'm not enough of a bbq fanatic to go back for any other reason, but those fried pickles got this place to 4 stars in my book.  Just a note: I sat at the bar area and the girl who served me (I wanna say her name was Kali) was super attentive and nice.  You could tell she knew what she doing and she was really good about making sure that everyone sitting at the bar was taken care of.

This is a review of the iced coffee.  This is a cute little restaurant that just opened and they serve various sandwiches and soups. In addition to the food they have an extensive juice and coffee menu. Because I love Vietnamese coffee, but I feel weird going into most places and just asking for it "to go", this seemed like the perfect place for me because "to go" is one of their specialties. I got an iced coffee and it was 12 ounces for $4. At first I thought that this was a bit overpriced, but the coffee was really rich and I enjoyed it. I think next time I am going to ask for less ice only because they packed the cup and I hate when I finish a drink and I still have a full cup of ice.  The place itself is small with a few booths and there is seating outside, if you happen to be there on a cooler day. I am eager to return and try the food and will post a review update when I do.

Awesome!  A fantastic thrift store close to home.  I stopped by here today, because the sign had been up awhile and I was anxiously awaiting it's opening.  The store is HUGE (as are all Red White and Blue thrift stores) and it was nice because it's new and everything is neat and clean.  There also weren't a TON of people, because not a lot of people know about it yet.  I guess that's about to change.  Ha.    They are cash only, and if I had more cash on me today, I would have definitely left the store with a lot of stuff.  I was most impressed that none of the stuff looked raggedy or used.  A lot of the things here still had tags and some of the dresses were the same style that I would find at upper hand consignment stores.  I saw a cute dress, that still had tags on it, that was marked as $5.95 and it was originally $20 at a retail store!  You can't beat that.  Don't be put off that this is a "thrift" store.  Go in and look around, and I think you'll be surprised at what you see.

Bastante deliciosa! 4 estrellas!  This restaurant has been open for a while and I finally made my way to the place that was once a Byblos which was once a Nacho Mama's.  It was a pretty slow night and we were eating early, so it was a light crowd. I was looking over the menu and I found myself in the mood for a margarita. Since the "house" margarita seemed to call to me, that was the first one I ordered. I got it and- I don't know. Something about it was a bit off. It was a little too sweet. I like a sweet cocktail, but I like my margaritas to lean more towards the tangy side. I decided to try another one, so I got their "top shelf" margarita. It was a little better, but it didn't blow my socks off. Well, I wasn't wearing socks but if I had been they would have remained on. Next time I just might add more lime to it. Maybe it's me and my weird palate.   Ok, enough of the drinks. For our appetizer we got the guacamole and it was fresh and perfect. I'm a big fan of when the guac has chunks of avocado in it and that's how this was, so it was an immediate win. For my entree, I got the burrito con pastor. I loved this! The meat was spiced to perfection and the entire burrito had tons of flavor. My dining companion (he had the tacos), who has been to Mexico many times, remarked that this is the most authentic tasting Mexican meal he has had in the city. I really love it and I am anxious to go back and try more of the menu.

I know what you are thinking, and yes I am giving Applebee's 5 stars.  When the boyfriend and I started discussing our mutual love for burgers, I lamented that there just isn't a good burger place on the Westbank. That's when he suggested Applebee's. At first I was skeptical. I mean, come on, how good can an Applebee's burger be? But, he has proven to be a "tough sell" when it comes to food, so I figured that he must know what he's talking about.  We stopped in and of course, immediately knew that we wanted burgers. We both decided on the bacon cheddar cheeseburger. I really like that the waitress asked how we wanted it cooked and when we said "medium" she asked if we wanted pink in the middle, which we did. I feel like a lot of burger places are afraid to cook a burger a little less than medium. When the burger came out, it was perfect. It was perfectly pink in the middle and topped with three thick strips of bacon and thick cheese and the best part is that it was actually delicious! The meat had a lot of flavor and the bacon added a nice touch to it and it all tasted very fresh. I ended up eating the entire thing along with most of the fries that accompanied it.  For dessert, we split the chocolate mousse shooter which was the perfect end to the meal and a real deal for $2.99.  Until the Westbank decides to get a really good burger joint, it looks like Applebee's will be my "go to" for a burger on the Westbank. I will definitely be going back for the bacon cheddar cheeseburger.

I love Bunny Bread Warehouse, and not just because it's pretty much right down the street from where I live.  This store is pretty "no frills" and it's fairly small, but it's packed with goodies. I usually stop in here to get hamburger buns or Italian bread, because it's really fresh and it's a little bit cheaper than what you can get at the grocery store. When I come I usually like to pick up some of the small snack pies they have- I really like to get the individually wrapped pumpkin pies and pecan pies that make for a perfect dessert when you don't want to buy a whole pie. I'll occasionally pick up one of those "snoball" treats that come wrapped. Whenever I have been here the people working are usually teenagers, but they do their best to help you if you are looking for something specific.

In my best Jeff Foxworthy voice: You might be a Westbanker if... you're excited about the new Wal Mart.  Okay, so I won't say I am excited per se, but I am pretty happy that there is a Wal Mart in the 'hood that is an actual grocery store and not a super gigantic "if you need it, we got it" Wal Mart that they all seem to be these days. If you remember the Wal Marts of yesteryear- when life was a little simpler and you couldn't buy a gun in aisle 6, then this is the place for you.  Today was the opening day, so you know I had to be first in line. Not really, but I was there at 11 to beat the impending crowd. There was still a crowd, mind you, but it was manageable. They have a nice selection of things here and it's new and clean, so I enjoyed that while it lasted. I was most impressed with the bakery section, as they had a nice selection of breakfast pastries that were well priced. I scooped up some rolls, just to say I helped the cause (does Wal Mart need my help? Nah.) The beer section isn't anything to write home about, but they do have a pretty impressive wine selection.  The lines were short, even though there was a bit of a crowd and all of the employees were working fast to get everyone in and out. Ample parking and a big parking lot made navigating the parking area a breeze. It's everything that you would expect from a typical grocery store, and while it's no Rouses, it's a nice addition to the area.

I was on the hunt for some gifts for a Harry Potter loving friend of mine when I was told that this place was worth checking out.  Nestled in a converted house on N. Carrollton Avenue, this cute book shop seems to have a little something for everyone. They have a nice selection of really cute magnets and toys all relating to book characters. I loved the Jane Austen action figures and temporary tattoos- that is such a cute way to get kids interested in reading!   As promised, they had a nice selection of Harry Potter toys and other fun little things. I ended up getting a massive book about the Harry Potter houses as well as a couple of little toys that my friend is sure to like.  Things that I really liked about this shop: the small, but effective "local books" section that had a nice selection of local interest books, the really cool floating book shelf (how did they do that?), a whole upstairs section of children's books and a reading area for kids.  Basically, this little shop is everything you want a book shop to be and I will return.

I went here for lunch the other day and this place was awesome!  When you walk into this small place, you are immediately struck by the fact that it is "dining room" style.  You walk in and order at the register and pay, then you find a seat and wait for your order.  We went a little after regular lunch time and there were still a lot of people in there, but we had no problem finding a seat at a picnic table.  Yeah, some of the seating is at picnic tables.  This means you will be eating with total strangers, so if that weirds you out, you may want to get your order to go.  We were sitting across from these two gentlemen who were explaining to two other people at the table exactly what a mirliton is.  It was pretty cool.  Everyone was talking like they were old friends.  As for the food, I ordered an oyster poboy dressed and it was amazing.  The bread was super soft and not all crumbly and over toasted, which I liked. Between the time and ordered and when my food was ready it was about 10 minutes.  They have a whole huge selection of things you can get.  I heard the fried chicken is awesome, but I was in a sandwich mood.  I will definitely be checking this place out again and trying some of their other poboys and New Orleans based treats.

WHAT A VIEW!  When I heard about the reopening of the Bayou Bar and the Caribbean Room at the Pontchartrain Hotel, a tiny part of me wondered if they were going to open up the penthouse to the public. I was in this penthouse years ago for a private event and the best part of the space is the gorgeous view of the city.  I am happy to report that the penthouse has been converted into a cool bar/club type of space. There are sofas and chairs for lounging inside and there are tables and chairs out on the balcony, so that you can soak in the entire city. Getting up here feels very VIP- you have to get in line and wait for the doorman to let you up. This is for safety reasons, but really makes the experience feel that much more exclusive. The bar feels as if you are in someone's living room at a fancy party.  The balcony area is small, so you have to wait for some space to open up before you can make it out there. On the night I was there it was pretty packed, even though it was late in the evening. I think some people just like to take over the tables and "camp out" for the night.  I definitely want to go back a little earlier in the evening, so that I can watch the sunset from this gorgeous spot. My sad little picture definitely doesn't do this place justice.

I love a thrift store! There is no shame in my game and I would rather buy second hand over retail any day of the week. Something about getting a super deal on something awesome just makes me happy.  This Goodwill makes me happy. First of all, the place is huge. Although there are sections with used books, housewares and records, the real deals are with the clothing. Look, I'm not one of these people who is bothered if something has been previously owned. I live for a deal and I don't care if a grandma used to wear something: if I like it, I'm buying it.  The dress section here is incredible. The short dresses are $5 and the long dresses are $10. They have a HUGE selection and so many things are new with tags! I was able to score a gorgeous sun dress that was actually on display. The dress was new with tags (originally $20) and I was able to grab it for $5. I got it home and it fit PERFECTLY! Ah, I'm so excited to wear it and I love a steal!  I will definitely return. Dare I say that this Goodwill almost blows my beloved Red, White and Blue out of the water as far as savings and selection. You are bound to find something worth buying.

This is a review of an art show.  I think I came on a good night, because I attended an art show here. I feel that this is what this space is best suited for. I really can't imagine it being much else. Anyway, the art was all spread out and there was a lot of space for mingling with others. The bartenders did well keeping up with the crowd, and I enjoyed my house cabernet. There was nice performance art here and I liked that there was plenty of seating right next to the stage,  I really can't imagine anything but an art show happening here. I feel like it's too small for any kind of club, unless they move a lot of stuff. I probably wouldn't go back for a "club" night, but I'd be happy to come back for another art show!

Here's a fun fact about me: I absolutely love Cuban sandwiches. Unfortunately, I never really know where to find them (and if they aren't pressed, then they don't count!). When I heard that Down the Hatch had a pressed Cuban on French Bread, I knew that I had to try it.  So, the thing about Down the Hatch is that it is basically a bar that serves food. But they have a full menu, plenty of seating and table service, so it's not like when you order food at some dive bar.   Anyway, I went in and ordered my Cuban with a side salad. When it came, they accidentally brought it with onion rings, so I ended up with a side salad and an order of onion rings. First of all, the side salad was HUGE and it wasn't just a little lettuce and tomato salad. It had carrots, mushrooms and cucumbers in it. I could have seriously just eaten the salad and been fine. The Cuban was really good. There was something missing on it, maybe mustard, but that was no big deal. I only ended up eating half of it and I packed up the other half (and onion rings) as leftovers.  I would definitely go back. The waitress was really nice and was good about making sure we had enough drinks and that everything was taken care of.

Joi's review of the iced coffee here was part of my motivation in getting myself over to St. Roch Market and I am so glad that I made the trip.  I am an iced coffee addict and I have become somewhat picky in what I like and expect from a tasty brew. I stepped into St. Roch and as soon as I saw the line for Coast Roast, I knew that Joi's review was dead on. I ordered a large iced coffee which came to a reasonable $4.25 or so. I like that their large is actually LARGE. Give me something that is going to last me a while. I added some half and half and what I had was one of the best iced coffees I have ever enjoyed. Nice and rich, strong without making me jittery and bonus points for the ice lasting a long time as I sipped the drink. Seriously- I drove uptown and left it in my car while I went shopping and it was still icey cold when I returned, as if by some sort of iced coffee magic.  I really hope Coast Roast adds a few more locations as I would love to enjoy their offering regularly.

I was able to check out this Rotolo's as soon as it opened.  Having been a fan of Rotolo's for years, I was excited to see that one was opening so close to where I live.  I got my usual: a medium pepperoni pizza with extra cheese, and of course it was fantastic.  It was big enough to split with my friend and we were both satisfied.  My friend also decided to try a bowl of their tomato basil soup.  While I was unable to try it, my friend told me that it was really good, so I will be sure to get it the next time I go back.

Well, no one likes having to bring their car to the shop and the dealership can be an extra pain because they always seem to take a little longer.  I had to bring my car in because GMC had a recall so I had to get my key worked on. It's a whole thing. Anyway, I dropped the car off in the morning and they told me it would be a few hours. About an hour after the drop off, I got a call from the dealership. It seems they went nosing around under my hood and found that my belt and brake pads needed to be replaced. Well, how dare they go looking for trouble in some odd effort to keep me safe!  Anyway, they quoted a price and after giving the "go ahead" they told me my car would be ready after lunch. Then the craziest thing happened: my car was ready after lunch! They actually stuck to their word and got the job done in a timely manner. Car issues can be stressful, so it's nice that Don Bohn made the experience as painless and fast as possible.

This gorgeous shop is any glamour girls dream!  What caught my eye and got me into this shop were the lovely tiaras in the window. Honestly, I really want one, but I sometimes wonder if that's a level of "the most" that I'm not ready to approach just yet. Walking in, there are all kinds of high end sparklies that any woman would love. This is really high end costume jewelry, not the cheapo stuff that you might find at the mall (not that I have any issue with the cheapo stuff).  They have an entire table full of different rhinestone tiaras and another table full of rhinestone masks. If you're looking for something for a ball or a costume party, this is definitely the place. They even have a case full of rhinestone crowns, if you are really feeling regal and want to add some fancy head gear to your collection.  The shop owner was very sweet and asked if I needed help and informed me of the items that were for sale. I didn't purchase anything this time, but I do really want a fancy tiara, so I will eventually be back.

Today I popped in here for the first time since my last review, which was 4 years ago, so I figured it was time for an update.  We got there and the woman working the front was so nice and friendly. She immediately asked us if we wanted to sit at her favorite spot in the restaurant. We said "sure", and she lead us to a nice and cozy corner booth. It was delightful.  We weren't super hungry, so we got the vegetarian special and a rainbow roll. The vegetarian special comes with three vegetarian rolls, one of which is an avocado roll, so I was a happy camper. The rainbow roll was super good and between the veg special and the rainbow roll we had more than enough for lunch.  The waiter was very attentive and friendly throughout  the entire meal and all in all we had a perfect lunch.

I love little coffee shops like this one. This is one of those little New Orleans coffee shops that really makes the space their own by adding art and different posters to the walls. It makes the place a little bit more unique and cozy and creates a good vibe.  I stopped in here for my usual iced coffee to go. The barista was super friendly and helpful and the coffee was tasty with a lot of flavor. There are table and chairs so that you can sit and do work or just waste time. Ask the barista for the wifi password- it changes daily.

This is a super convenient Rouses right off of Poydras.  If you live in the area, and want to stock up for goods for a Saints game, it's the "go to" spot.  There is always plenty of parking and it's never overly packed with people, so you can check out pretty fast.  Just like any other Rouses there is a huge selection of goods and hard to find items.

Whoa. I finally remembered to check into this Walgreens, even though I go here all the time (seriously. I'm here at least once a week!).   This is my favorite Walgreens in my area. They seem to always have exactly what I'm looking for. The usual stuff I get here is makeup or something along those lines. They always have a nice selection of "holiday" oriented items. When I went yesterday, they had a whole aisle full of cool Valentine's Day goodies! They also have a neat little "gift" aisle full of toys for kids. I'm always pretty satisfied with what I find here.

This shop has some gorgeous jewelry. It makes me wish I had money to burn on diamond fleur de lis pendants.  This is a small shop, but it packs a lot in. Beautiful diamonds glisten in the lights and you imagine yourself being draped in luxury while attending some fancy event at someplace interesting. They have a good deal of New Orleans themed jewelry- gators and fleur de lis in every fashion, but they also have a nice selection of vintage jewelry and charms. I loved the selection of antique charms for charm bracelets, and they had so many that I'm tempted to start my own charm collection.  The owner of the shop was very nice and offered to take anything out of a case, so that we might have a closer look. For the average shopper, many of the items here will be out of price range, but they have a few items that you might like for a special occasion.

Woo hoo! Another great Magazine St. find!  I loved this store as soon as I walked in. First of all, I knew I was in a good place because when I walked in and looked to my right, I saw a "$30" rack and a "$40" rack. Now you know me, I am a fashionista on a budget. You don't have to spend a lot to look good. They have so many cute things here for great prices. The owner told me that she likes to keep most things between $20 and $60 dollars. You can't beat that and that makes this the perfect place to pick up a cute dress for a party or just hanging around town.  What's best about this place is that if you "like" them on facebook you can stay up to date with everything they have in the store because the owner posts pictures of clothes as they come in. Amazing!

I thought I had seen every type of Ulta there is, but this is a super fancy Ulta with a salon in the store! Oooh fancy!  I have mentioned in past Ulta reviews how much I love this store because some of the things they sell are better priced than what you would find at a drug store and everything is neatly organized by brand. On this particular day, I was in the market for a curling iron and I knew that Ulta would have a large selection, so that I could find what I needed. I ended up getting the perfect 1 1/2 inch barrel curler that I was looking for for a little under $40.  While this Ulta isn't necessarily worth going out of my way, it's great for beauty needs if you are in the area.

There's really not much you can say about a Metairie dive bar. I guess I'm spoiled since the NOLA smoking ban but yeah, this place is pretty smoky. I didn't have any of the food but one thing I can report is that they have Lagunitas IPA on tap, so that made me happy. On the night I was here, the crowd was pretty mellow and service was prompt. I wouldn't go out of my way to come here, but it's a decent choice if you're in the area.

I really hate to give St. Lawrence 3 stars, because the staff was super nice, but I was still left disappointed.  First of all, we ended up here because this is one of the few places that has a pretty decent menu and serves food after 10. We were STARVING (at least I was starving), so I was expecting to be blown away by whatever I ended up getting here.  The first thing we ordered was the Irish stout cheese dip. Whoa! This is super good and it comes with kettle chips for dipping! Everything else on the menu sounded so amazing. Shrimp and grits, a Cuban sandwich and the bacon cheddar burger had me torn. I decided to go for the burger.  So, we ordered, and although they didn't seem super busy, the food took a while. Then the waitress comes out to tell me that they accidentally made my burger "well done" (I wanted medium), so they had to redo it. The other food order was ready, so they brought that out, so my dining companion could eat. I'm still waiting and I'm still starving and the burger is taking forever.  When the burger finally made it out, I was excited. It looked AMAZING and well worth my 30 minutes-total wait. I cut into it and immediately knew that it was cooked medium-well to well done. I wasn't about to send it back, so I just dealt with it. The fries were cold, as I'm sure they were made when my first burger was on the grill. I didn't bother mentioning this to the waitress, because honestly, I didn't want to wait another 15 minutes for a burger that MIGHT be cooked the way I want.  I ended up eating half of the burger, about 3 fries and just taking the rest of it home. For our trouble, my one ($6) beer was comped. Um...yay? It was basically a total rip off for the price.  My friend got the Cuban sandwich, and mentioned that it was really good, so if I go back I guess I'll get that. Honestly, I probably won't return. They are getting three stars because the atmosphere is nice and the staff was attentive and apologetic about their blunder.

Accessories is really the name of the game here. I was hopping down Maple Street when I came across this cute boutique. They have really cute clothes, but the jewelry and sunglasses were out of this world! With the help of the awesome employees, I was able to find the perfect gift for a friend- a pair of mirrored sunglasses that are both stylish and useful. The clothes here are light and perfect for the impending warmer weather and they come in lots of bright colors. Prices are a little steep, but the sunglasses I found were reasonable and seemed worth the money.

Good not great. "A-OK pretty much sums it up.  Stopped in here for lunch around 1 pm. The place wasn't packed at all. We got our menus, decided what we wanted pretty quickly and then waited. And waited. And waited. About 35 minutes later our food finally came out. Now, before you go thinking that I must have ordered something complicated, let me break it down. I ordered a croissant club sandwich with a side salad and my lunch companion ordered a wrap with fries. Nothing about either one of those things takes 35 minutes.  After the wait, the food wasn't too bad. I ate half of my sandwich and took the other half to go. My side salad was basically lettuce and cheese, but that's not too bad I guess.  I would probably go back if I wasn't in any type of hurry, but if I had to be somewhere by a certain time I would probably choose another lunch spot.

I've parked in this lot a bunch and I've never had an issue. One of the better priced lots in the area at 3 hours for $11. The attendant is always around and easily accessible, if you need help with something. I dealt with a malfunctioning machine once and the attendant was quick to help me. Keep an eye on your time because the meter maid ticket people come around every ten minutes.

This delightful little shop is right up my alley! Not only do they carry gorgeous hats, but they have all kinds of fancy wraps and dresses as well.  I stopped in here while strolling down Royal Street and was so excited about the amazing selection of hats this store has. They have some from every day to fancy hats for special occasions. I think that they might even make hats to order, but you would have to check with someone about that. Another thing that I loved is that the have a whole case of sparkly, crystalized hand bags. They have everything from a basketball and a Saints helmet to a heart shaped bag and even a dog. They also have a selection of sparkly pill boxes and compacts. I will definitely have to go back and treat myself to one of these lovely conversation pieces.  The store is really big and they have a lot packed in here, but it wasn't so much that I felt overwhelmed. The woman working immediately greeted me and asked if I was looking for anything specific. If you are looking for something for a special occasion, especially a hat, this should be your first stop.

After years of lamenting that the only decent coffee place on the Westbank is PJ's and after quite a few people told me about J'aime Le Cafe', I finally decided to give this place a shot.  Whoa. Okay, I don't know what they put in their coffee but I think that I'm already addicted. I got the 16oz iced latte and I seriously drank it so quickly that I wanted to turn around and go back and grab another one. It was packed with flavor, super tasty and just perfect for the warm day.  I do love that J'aime Le Cafe' has a drive thru and, even though there were a couple of cars in front of me, the line moved quickly. I will absolutely return.

Okay, some of y'all who are giving Esplanade such low ratings have obviously never been to Oakwood on the Wank.  I visited Esplanade Mall today for EASILY the first time in 15 years. I wasn't expecting much, because some of the reviews were ROUGH. I was actually pleasantly surprised with what I found here. Look, no one is ever going to accuse Esplanade Mall of being cool or trendy- they have a lot of empty stores and the stores they do have are a bit out of date (there's a Spencers AND a Hot Topic), but for what it is, it isn't terrible. There are a few cute little clothing shops here and even though it's limited, the food court has a selection of a few different eateries.  I think that the biggest problem with this mall is the fact that it's too big, too spread out and it's two stories. This mall suffers from the same design problem as the long forgotten Belle Promenade mall that was in Marrero- there are too many stores hidden around corners and off to the side. There's nothing that can be done about that at this point, but that's my theory.  When I was here the mall was pretty empty and there were a lot of store workers waiting outside their stores hoping that someone would stop in. Esplanade EASILY needs a makeover and badly. In this day and age of internet shopping, you have to offer something that is going to draw people in. I'm no mall manager, I'm just throwing my two cents out there.  This is not a terrible mall to visit if you live or work in the area, but it's not worth going out of your way. The biggest selling point is that they have a Macy's.

FINALLY!  After years of hearing about how fantastic Yo Mama's food is, I got to check it out for myself!    I was super hungry when I checked out what Yo Mama's had to offer.  I kept it simple and ordered the "Yo Mama" burger with a side salad (yes, a salad.  Shutty!).  It was incredible and I finished it in about ten minutes.  It was easily one of the best burgers I have had in the city.    My only complaint was that I ordered it medium and it was cooked medium well.  That's not a huge thing.  I still ate it and it was still good.  Also, be prepared, this place tends to get really packed and you may be waiting about 30 minutes for food, but that's a small price to pay for such a good burger.  I want to go back and try their famed "peanut butter" burger.  I just wanted to try something basic my first time in there.

Home decor galore!  This would be the first place I would stop if I had one of those trendy Garden District shotguns and I had the money to decorate it however I wanted. All of the items here seem to be vintage inspired, and that's right up my alley. I love the bright colors and I love that the first room you see when you walk in is decorated to look like a cozy living room- it really gives you an idea of what YOUR space could look like.  My favorites were the gorgeous antique chairs that were finished with beautiful pops of color. They also have smaller items, just in case you don't have the nerve to pull the trigger on a large piece of furniture. The woman working was very friendly and I liked that there was a lot packed into the space.

I gotta be honest when it comes to Rock n Sake: people rave about this place, the restaurant gets packed and I just don't get it.  The atmosphere is really odd.  The place is small.  There's a restaurant area and a "dance" area.  Yeah, the place is kind of like a nightclub that serves sushi.  The music is super loud, so it's hard to have a conversation and there is a sea of drunk people that you have to wade through in order to get to the bathroom.  As for the food: on a friend's suggestion, I got the "Atomic Tuna" special roll.  It was good, but nothing great.  My date got the "LSU" special roll and it was fantastic.  If I were to go back here, I would definitely get this roll instead.  We also had an order of shrimp wontons which were amazing.  All in all, this place isn't terrible.  It's within walking distance to Harrah's and a lot of other "party" spots, so I get that this is mainly a "starter" place, if you are going out for the evening.  My suggestion would be to try a place a little quieter if you aren't in "party mode", but it's not bad for what it is.

Man, I almost don't even want to let the secret out on this amazing place but I want a lot of people to go so that it stays open, so here we are. Let me start at the beginning- Big EZ Seafood is fairly new and not only offers boiled seafood such as crawfish, shrimp and crabs, but they also offer a variety of platters and poboys. They even have yakamein!  I have been here twice. The first time I got the boiled crawfish. This is an early crawfish season, so the bugs were a bit on the small side, but I really enjoyed them. I happened to get a really spicy batch, and even though I love spicy food, they were a bit too much for me. They weren't so spicy that it would keep me from getting them again though, and that's all that matters.  The second time I got a 12 inch fried shrimp poboy for $10. Yeah, you read that right, and not only was a 12 inch poboy $10, but it was PACKED with huge fried shrimp! These things were fat, y'all! I was so pleasantly surprised that I didn't even know what to do with myself. So many other Westbank poboy places charge an arm and a leg and then don't fill the sandwich up, but Big EZ's poboy exceeded my expectations.  The two times I got food here I got take out, but they also have tables if you want to sit and eat in the store itself. They have a wide variety of things on the menu and I won't bore you with the details, since their menu has been posted on here. They also sell live crawfish, if boiling your own is your thing.  I will definitely be back, probably for another amazing poboy.

My favorite Metairie sushi place!  I love to sit at the sushi bar and chat with the personable staff.  I usually get sashimi and a few rolls.  Kind of small, but I like the cozy atmosphere.  My favorite thing about this place is that it's open late on the weekends (12:30), so if you find yourself in Metairie late, for some reason, there is another option other than just fast food.

Oooh, I'm a sucker for Seersucker!  I finally managed to get here for lunch, after a friend of mine RAVED about it and called it one of the best lunch spots on the Westbank. He is bi-coastal (Northshore and Southshore), so he definitely knows his food.  This is a pretty simple little place that serves up good food. You walk up to the counter and place your order, you are given a number then you pick a table and wait for your food. The food here is typical lunch fare- poboys and platters are the star of the show. I decided to get the oyster and catfish platter with fries and potato salad. The food came out, after a short wait, and WOW- this is a ton of food. The oysters were small but very nicely fried and a bit crispy. The piece of catfish was HUGE and I ended up just eating the oysters for lunch and saving the fish for dinner. The fries were amazing! I don't know what they do to the fries here, but they were a little bit crispy and very tasty without being too salty. I didn't get to my potato salad until later that night, but it was packed with big chunks of potato and had celery finely chopped into it, which is my favorite in potato salad.  When you are finished eating, clear your own spot and grab a box at the counter, if you have leftovers. The owners here are extremely friendly and I could tell that they get a nice crowd of regulars because quite a few people stopped in and the owners knew them by name. I will definitely be eating at Seersucker again!

Since it has been nearly 6 whole years since I last reviewed this LC, I figured it was time for a re-review.  I still stand by the fact that the pizza here is "decent". We stopped in the other night and got one of the $5 pepperoni hot 'n ready pizzas. First of all, I'm pretty impressed that after 6 years, the price is still $5. Second of all, the pizza was really good and satisfied my pepperoni pizza craving perfectly. I also have to add that while $5 pizza is still not as good as Rotolo's, it is better than Papa John's, in my opinion. This isn't the place to say it, but I gave up on PJ's a long time ago, because quality has just gone down hill. I blame Peyton Manning.  Anyway, if you have a pepperoni pizza craving, this place will nip it in the bud.

I stopped into this tiny cafe for an early brunch and I was lucky that I was able to grab a table just as someone else was leaving.  Going in, you should know that this place is pretty small. If you have to wait for a table, please wait outside so as not to take up too much space. I was pretty hungry, so I decided to get the pork grillades Benedict and a small bowl of the full blast grits.  The pork grillades benedict is huge chunks of pork and gravy served with eggs Benedict on top with sliced potatoes on the side. It was delicious! The pork was so tender and the gravy was delicious. This honestly felt like more of a dinner than a breakfast, but I loved it.   The full blast grits is grits topped with bacon and cheese and it's as decadent as you can imagine. A large bowl of this would easily be enough for a full meal, even though it's offered as a side. There's just something magical about melty cheese and bacon on top of savory grits. Needless to say, I had plenty of food to take home.  The waiter was attentive and the staff was great. My only complaint is how small the place is and I kept getting bumped because I was seated right by the door. Next time I'm going to request a table more in the back, even if I have to wait. The food was fantastic and I'll be back.

Coyote Ugly is not only a downtown bar, it's a chain bar and that might be the worst of the worst.  Look, I get it, a place like this isn't interested in appealing to the local crowd. They are just hoping to attract enough tourist foot traffic to keep the doors open. I totally get it. The people who work here are super nice and welcoming. If you think your experience here is going to be anything like the movie that shares it's name, you are going to be sorely disappointed.  Not once did anyone say to me, "Hell no, H2O!" Pfft!

Ugh.  Is there anything appealing about the Gold Mine once you leave the cloud of college?    First of all, why is there a cover?  Why are they charging 3 bucks to go into a bar that is a smidge larger than a one bedroom apartment, hot as I don't know what, in the summer and has an actual line to get their signature drink...a flaming dr. pepper, is it?  Uhh...yeah.  I can't remember the last time I set foot in this joint, but what I always tell people is that it's not that type of place you set out to go to, it's the kind of place at which you just end up, for whatever reason.  If you are in college or out at 2 am in the quarter, go for it.  Otherwise, just cut your losses and call it a night.  This is a rare "unlisted" review.  It doesn't even deserve one of my cool lists!!

Maïs Arepas was so amazing! Possibly the perfect lunch spot.  I had actually never had an arepas before. It's basically a sandwich on a type of flat bread. I had the cerda with plantain chips which was basically a pork sandwich with freshly cooked plantains on it. It was delicious! It was packed with flavor and made for a fantastic sandwich.  Maïs Arepas also has a "juice of the day". I decided to try the strawberry limeade which was out of this world and super fresh and full of flavor.  I like the atmosphere here and it seems like this would be a really good place for groups. I can't wait to go back!

I've been putting off reviewing TJ's for a long time now. Too long, I suppose. I guess my whole issue is; I never know what to rate this place. I could give it 5 stars for what it is: a divey college bar with drinks that are pretty cheap. Or I could give it 1 star because of some of the people who tend to hang out here and the "vibe" you get when you walk in.  Finally, I decided to give it a middle of the road 3 stars. TJ's (it won't be called The Annex for much longer) is a cool place that recently went under a much needed renovation. A lot of people think it lost something, but those are probably the people living in the past. It still has a pool table and it's the same as it used to be, just a bit cleaner. The staff is always really nice and the crowd is young, but not terrible.  This isn't a place that I would go out of my way to visit, unless there is something drawing me here, but it is not yet on my "avoid at all costs" list.

Stopped in with a coworker friend of mine to look around for a birthday gift for her son. This comics shop is pretty expansive with books and toys galore. On the day that we were here, my friend was looking for something specific, and although they didn't have what she was looking for in store, they offered to order it for her.  Of course, they have some rare books that you can buy as well as some collectors items. I'm not really into comic books, but the woman working was super friendly and helpful and showed me around a bit and gave me an idea of what they have. I want to go back and bring David because he loves comic books and I know that he'd appreciate this spot.

This is the perfect shop for the fashionista in you, especially if you're looking for a dress or outfit for a special occasion.   This shop has cute little party dresses that sparkle and shine and fancier long gowns, if you need something for a wedding or party. The long gowns that they have here are out-of-this-world and look like they belong on a red carpet somewhere. They seriously look like couture designer gowns. The staff is extremely helpful and, as I looked around, I didn't feel pressured at all to purchase anything- they just let me look and ask questions, if necessary.  I didn't purchase anything on this trip, but I will definitely be back at the end of the year, and hopefully I will have an excuse (or a fancy New Year's Eve party) to wear one of these beautiful dresses.

It seems that everywhere I go, I see some work by Simon. These are nifty art pieces and signs with cute little sayings on them with a New Orleans twist. I actually stumbled into this place on accident one day after stopping into District Donuts. I had no idea that Simon even had a studio! Something else I didn't know- you can actually commission a custom piece! If you are looking for a unique "New Orleans" style gift or even if you just want something artsy to hang over your front door, this is the place for you.  Simon definitely adds a little something to the culture and magic of New Orleans.

This is such a fun time!  I hadn't been to an arcade/ticket type place since my days of running around Chuck E. Cheese as a kid. This seems to be a more sophisticated version of that. Yes, this place is kid and teen friendly, but you don't feel weird if you are just a couple of adults playing some games for tickets.  They have fun arcade games and other classics such as air hockey and skee ball and basketballs games and stuff like that. Almost all the games "pay out" tickets/points onto a card that you can cash in for prizes. Some of the games are pretty easy but others are challenging, so it's a nice mix for all age groups. We played a game of laser tag, but it was the last game of the day and there weren't a ton of people playing, so we will have to play earlier next time.  I like that the place is big and you don't run into people and there aren't lines waiting for games- there is a lot for people to do. They have a little cafe area where you can get pizza and drinks and other snacks. This seems like it would be a good spot for a party, no matter what your age.

This is a pretty good Goodwill that is packed with everything you can imagine. It's organized pretty well, by size and style of clothing. A lot of what they have here is out of date- very out of date, but I guess that's to be expected because they have a lot of things for sale. Aisles are narrow and can be hard to navigate when it's busy.  You are going to find things for really cheap here ($1 and $2 t shirts), but it's not as good of quality as you will find at other thrift stores. Much of what they have here has been well worn.

I was today years old when I discovered the glory that is Tower Beauty.  I was on the hunt for some gold stockings to wear with my Mardi Gras outfit (it's never too early to start planning). Normally I would just hop onto Amazon and be done with it, but I'm no longer online shopping, because I want to keep local businesses alive- a suggestion on Facebook brought me here.  For some reason, I always assumed this was just a hair care store, but I was so wrong. Y'ALL, if you're in the market for inexpensive makeup, leggings, stockings, jewelry or undergarments, this is the place!  I found the gold stockings that I was looking for and they were on sale for $2! Boom! Sure, they aren't the highest quality, but so what? They're enough to last me at least one day and that's good enough for me. They also have a wide assortment of fishnets that are good for costumes as well. I didn't buy any makeup, but they have really affordable name brands like Nyx and a big selection of perfumes and body sprays too.   This place is a treasure trove of cheap supplies and I will definitely be back.
This is a really great and generous parade.  It's a great precursor to Bacchus and really gets the crowd going.  The riders seemed to be having a good time and made the experience fun for everyone.

Galaxie is the hot new taco place on the Bywater block and I was pretty excited to check it out. The restaurant is actually a former gas station that's been totally redone and made into a taco sanctuary, if you will.  Ordering is pretty basic: you order at the counter, they give you a number and you go into, what I assume was maybe a garage or something, at some point, and sit down. There's also a bar and you can eat there. On my visit, I got an order of the grilled queso, black beans and an al pastor quesadilla.  The grilled queso was good but, I'm gonna be honest, it was basically just melted cheese. I'm not mad at that at all, but I would have loved to have a tortilla to wrap it in. The black beans were AMAZING. They had good flavor and they were topped with some sort of cheese that put them right over the top. My quesadilla was interesting- the tortilla was hard, but I liked that it was piled high with yummy al pastor. There was a lot of good flavor here and I was wishing I would have ordered another one.  A few drawbacks: I was here at night and the place was super dark. I could barely see what I was eating and I was wishing there was a little more light in the seating area. Also, my food and my friend's food came out at two different times. We got our beans together, but our entrees came out a few minutes apart. This is kind of a pet peeve of mine and seems to be happening at more restaurants lately. Whatever happened to bringing everyone's food out together?   I wish the portions were a little bigger, but now I know to order more when I go back. As much as I enjoyed my quesadilla, I was wishing that it was a little bit bigger.

Fantastic!  This place is amazing! Not only do they have comic books and graphic novels (I stopped in to see what they had to offer- Walking Dead wise) but they have tons of comic book related action figures, toys and gifts. The store is set up in such a way that everything is extremely easy to find. The staff was friendly and asked immediately upon my arrival if I needed help with anything.  Whatever you are in the mood for, you are bound to find it here. I will definitely return.

So, for those of you not in the "know", tulips have a pretty brief life. I learned this the hard way last year when I went to see the tulips at City Park and they were all dead. Womp womp.  This year I didn't make it as early as I would have liked, but I did make a special trip out there today to go and take my pictures and finally experience the tulip field. It was as lovely as social media told me it would be. The tulips are right next to Big Lake and are in all of the pretty colors of the rainbow. There's a little rope separating you from them, so please do not tiptoe through the tulips.  Believe it or not, they are already dying so get out there asap if you want to catch them this year. I wonder if the location is poor because they are in direct sunlight. When I went today they were baking in the heat. I have no idea- a plant expert I am not and I do not posses a green thumb. I'm just here for the flowery eye candy.  The tulips usually pop up around mid February each year.

I don't know what it is about this PJs.  Whenever I'm in mid city (which is pretty rare these days) I usually find myself here and I am usually left disappointed.  It seems as if they are consistently out of 2% and whole milk (shouldn't whole milk be a staple in a coffee shop?  Kinda like...cups?) and they only offer half and half or soy milk, instead.  Soy milk?  In iced coffee?  Yeah, I'll take your word for it.  I get the half and half, and it usually dilutes the whole flavor of the coffee, even if I just get a little.  I do like the croissants, as they are usually pretty fresh, but compared to other PJs, the iced coffee here just isn't to my liking.

I was having one of my burrito cravings when I realized I had never been to the newest Mexican restaurant on the Westbank, so I headed over to Los Compadres at about 11 am. Hey, when the burrito monster asks to be fed, it doesn't matter what time it is.  There was no one else in the place, probably because they had just opened for the day, so I was seated in a booth and tended to immediately. I liked that chips and salsa was dropped on the table and the salsa was kind of thick and actually pretty good. I was impressed. I decided to get the burrito supreme with chicken and it came topped with all the goods- lettuce, tomato, guac and sour cream. I also got some rice and beans on the side; more on that later.  The burrito was great! It was HUGE and packed with chicken, rice, cheese, beans and had a lot of flavor. In the future I'm going to get all of the "toppings" on the side. The waitress asked me if I wanted all of it on the burrito, but it's a lot to get through when you really only want the burrito itself. The rice and beans were okay, but for $2 each, I expected more. The rice was pretty dry and flavorless and the beans seemed like they came from a can. I felt like $4 was a bit of a rip off for what I got, but now I know.  Service was excellent and I like what they've done with the place. OG Westbankers will remember this location as the former Cuco's and it pretty much has the same vibe and feel as it always has. They packed a pretty good burrito, so I'd probably go back.

When it comes to Drago's, I really feel that it's one of those Oyster places you check out for the ambiance and the experience.  Honestly, you can get oysters a lot of places and they are probably just as good, but there is something about Drago's. It's one of those places where you dress a little nicer and have a nice night out downtown.  Their charbroiled oysters are fantastic and they aren't super expensive, considering you are in downtown New Orleans. They have a lot of other good seafood, too but I think that I've only ever had the oysters when I have been.

Gorgeous! A visit to the Lakefront Airport is like stepping back in time- I only wish I had been wearing my favorite vintage dress on the day I visited.  My dad and I had lunch at Messina's, so we decided to walk around after looking at all of the renovations at the airport. If you walk up the stone stairs, you get to see the murals that are being restored. They look so perfect that it's hard to believe that they were painted so many years ago. The Walnut Room is huge, if you are looking for a place to hold an elegant reception and there is even a flight school here. Here's a secret: I have always wanted to learn to fly, but I've never had the guts to look into lessons. Now that I know that there is a flight school at this airport, I might just have to give it some real thought.  Be sure to look down at the floor to see how many miles away from New Orleans different cities are (this will make more sense when you see it in person). The Lakefront Airport is a must visit for everyone.

If you read my review for the Westbank Panera location, than you already know that I'm a Panera fan.  I met a friend here for lunch and I was impressed- the employees were getting people quickly through the line on a busy Saturday and we were taken care of immediately. I ordered the half and half with a half of a roasted turkey and avocado sandwich and a cup of the broccoli cheddar soup (my favorite). They scanned my Panera card, I went into the dining room with my buzzer and after a minimal wait my food was ready  The roasted turkey and avocado sandwich was great! I had never had it before and I was happy to see that the turkey was freshly sliced and the avocado was perfect and ripe. Of course, the broccoli and cheddar soup was perfect as always and came with bread on the side, in case you want to dip.  As far as I can tell, this Panera doesn't have a drive thru like the Westbank location does, so if you are in a hurry you might want to call and order ahead for pick up.

I was in the downtown area and I had been craving Mediterranean, so what do you know, I found myself here.  I was here on a rainy day, so the place was completely dead around lunch, which was fine by me. I knew exactly what I wanted. I started with an order of Turkish coffee, some grape leaves and some kibbeh. The Turkish coffee was tasty and potent. The grape leaves were perfection. I think that Mona's grape leaves are some of my favorites in the city. I had the meat kibbeh and it was good as well. Both the grape leaves and the kibbeh were served with the tasty yogurt-like stuff that comes with this type of food and it was all perfect.  For my entree, I got the beef shawarma platter which comes with shawarma, salad, hummus and pita. This is SO MUCH FOOD for the price! Wow. The hummus and salad were generous and the meat was PILED HIGH on my plate. Perfect. The hummus was smooth and tasty and the shawarma was seasoned perfectly. It was nice and peppery and juicy, just the way I like it. If you have never had the shawarma at Mona's, it's a "must try".  I like that this Mona's is consistent with the other locations, as far as food quality goes. Service was super fast (probably because it was a slow afternoon, but still) and the experience was excellent. Also, don't be put off that it's in a busy area- I was able to find parking right out front!

What a gorgeous place! The New Orleans Botanical Garden is a gorgeous wonderland tucked away in City Park. I had always heard about it, but never visited because I figured it wasn't much different than the rest of the park. I was wrong!  When you walk in, it feels like you're walking into a secret garden. You're greeted by a unique water feature and beautiful archways. Follow the path and you will see all kinds of different landscaping including a fruit and vegetable garden, a butterfly garden and a toy train through a model of the different neighborhoods of New Orleans. If you go on a weekday it's quite quiet and a great place to relax. Although you're in the middle of the city, it feels as if you're in a different world and I like that there are different places to sit if you just want to relax.  The garden is free entry on Wednesday, so you have no excuse to not drop in and relax by the gorgeous fountain on a nice afternoon or take a leisurely stroll through the beautiful grounds. Pretend that the gardens are a part of your luxurious estate- that's what I did! This is a real treasure in New Orleans and must see for every local and visitor.

I have been wanting to try Red's FOREVER. Seriously, when did they open? This spot has been on my radar for a while.  I finally got my chance to enjoy some Red's goodness. When we got here the crowd was thin and we were seated immediately. I knew exactly what I wanted. We started with an order of the pork belly bun sliders and the craw rangoon (crab rangoon, minus crab plus crawfish).  The pork bun sliders were delicious and two orders would have made for the perfect meal. The craw rangoon was really tasty- fried to perfection in a yummy sauce. I could have made an entire meal of appetizers, if I'm being honest.  For my entree I got the large order of the General's chicken. Okay, so no one warned me that a whole order includes a HUGE breast, leg, wing and thigh. Yeah, this was made for two people and I kind of wish the waitress had given me a heads up. The chicken was good, but there was so much garlic! Big chunks of it! I mean, there was so much garlic that my eyes were watering and I had to stop eating because it was too much for me. I don't know what was going on in that kitchen, but there must have been a garlic explosion or something. The sauce on the chicken was good and had that nice salty/sweet taste of General Tsao's chicken that I've enjoyed elsewhere. I ate half of the serving and took the other half home where I could scrape off all of the garlic and it was good after that.   I'll go back, but I might just get the fried rice or munch down on a few appetizers.

Walking into Luna Libre feels as if you're walking into a friendly living room; the seating is as unconventional as the menu, which changes daily. On this visit, I started with an order of Stewart's cheese dip-  a combination of smooth melted cheese, meat, tomatoes, and guacamole that owner Rhonda Findley grew up on. She promised that it would be a "bowl-licker" and, when paired with warm tortilla chips, she wasn't kidding.  Next, I dug into the chicken enchilada verde ($12), a cheesy enchilada topped with crema. The flavors were incredible, and if the goal is classic American-Mexican comfort food, then this dish didn't disappoint. Next up was tacos -- now, I love tacos, so this part had me especially excited. I dug into a sampler of the Ahi-jerk taco with mango relish; the Ark-Americana taco- a crunchy taco served with meat, lettuce, tomato, onion, and crema; a carnitas taco; and a chicken-tinga taco. The Ahi-jerk taco is perfect if you like a little spice. This taco definitely packed a bit of a punch, but the spice was cut nicely with the addition of the mango relish.  The Ark-Americana taco was a nice twist on the classic crunchy taco- flavorful meat, fresh veggies and a shell that didn't get soggy under the weight of all of its contents. The carnitas taco might have been my favorite- house-made carnitas made from pork shoulder and cooked slowly. The meat was juicy and flavorful and didn't need any "extras" to make it special. The chicken tinga taco was crafted with Halal chicken and had a smoky, sweet flavor that was very distinct. Although I didn't have a chance to sample it, Findley also offers vegetarian taco options with mirliton and cauliflower.  If you're looking for a tasty cocktail, Luna Libre's flaming margarita is a must; handcrafted and made with all fresh ingredients, you can taste the freshness, and it isn't the overwhelming sugar bomb that you get from margaritas at some other restaurants.  This place is soon going to be a New Orleans hot spot, so be sure to check it out before the word gets out.

Woo hoo! A Bud's Broiler on the Westbank!  What's not to love about Bud's? Flame broiled burgers that are cooked to order with thick layers of cheese and onions. Sure, they serve chicken sandwiches too, but you have to go for the classic when you are eating here.  This Bud's is pretty much like all the rest of them. I think if you have been in one of these places, you have been in all of them.

This is an interesting place. They call themselves a "bakery", but it's more a small grocery that offers a whole array of things.  Me and some friends we starving and having been here before, they said this was a good place to get some Mexican Food.   Walking in, I honestly had no idea what was going on. We walked to the back where there was a menu taped up and food being prepared. A lot of people didn't speak English, so I was a little intimidated. Looking over the menu, I thought that the beef quesadilla sounded good and for $7, it seemed like a good deal for lunch. I ordered and waited. When you get your food, it comes with a ticket and you pay at the register in front of the store. Just a FYI.  The quesadilla was HUGE and although a bit greasy, really good. It definitely hit the spot and I liked that there was a lot of cheese on it. They have a few seats for dining in, but I would probably suggest just getting your food to go.  There is a bakery section with an assortment of Latin pastries and desserts. I didn't try any this time, but I will when I return.

There are a few things you need to know before seeing a show at the Sugar Mill: the whole place is basically outdoors, there will be lines for everything from food and beer to bathrooms,  and there is no where to sit so wear comfortable footwear.  We were here seeing a few bands here on a warm but not terribly uncomfortable Friday evening. I had never been here before, so I went in totally blind. Outside of the main concert area there were different stations for beer and mixed drinks and there was also a nice selection of food trucks serving up grub. There was also a whole line of port o pottys to accommodate the crowd.  The venue itself isn't terrible. The place is really big and, considering how many people were here, they did a good job at utilizing the space well. My biggest complaint was lack of seating- it's a small complaint, but I was there for hours and would have been happy with a bar stool. Lines for food and drinks were long, but moved fairly quickly. Bring cash- the drink stands don't take cards.  I would attend another event here, especially now that I know what to expect but I would hesitate to come here during the summer's hottest days.

Like all of you, I've been laying low the last few months and I've certainly missed sitting down and eating in a real-life restaurant. My feeble attempts at home cooking were enough to sustain me, but there comes a point when you just have to see other people and taste something that's cooked by someone who actually knows what they're doing.   On one of my first restaurant adventures, I decided that I needed good fried chicken. Like, good homemade fried chicken. Anyone who knows me knows of my love of fried chicken and Frazier's Connection in Marrero is rumored to have some of the best.   I knew I was going to be making a mini-celebration of my visit here, so I got a little generous with my ordering.  I got ¼ chicken (breast and wing) with macaroni and cheese and, what the heck, let's throw in an order of red beans and rice for good measure. I'd be remiss if I didn't try two of the dishes that Frazier's is known for.  All chicken is fried to order, so there's a bit of a wait, but I was in no rush. Out came two large pieces of chicken, mac and cheese and my full serving of red beans and rice. Right about now you might be thinking, "She can't eat all that." Look, please don't challenge me. I'm hungry.  The chicken was crispy and delicious, fried to perfection with steam wafting out as soon as I tore into it. The meat was juicy and the flavor was perfect! I got the "spicy" version and I found it to be impeccable and not over-spiced in any way. The seasoning enhanced the natural flavor and taste of the chicken, which is always what you want. I never enjoy something when I taste more spice than actual food.  The mac and cheese was made with "long" noodles, almost Rocky & Carlos style. The noodles were coated in delicious cheese and each bite had that ooey-gooey cheese pull that you really want in homemade mac and cheese. As someone who can only make box mac and cheese, I will never not be in awe of people who can make it so rich and creamy.  The red beans and rice was unparalleled. WOW! Perfectly spiced, just like the chicken, with pieces of pork and sausage. The portion was more than generous for $6 and, if I was here any other day, this would have been more than enough for lunch.  Next time you're in the mood for some good food, think local. All these people want to do is provide a good meal for the people in the neighborhood. They want to feed your soul and I'm happy to oblige.  *Portions of this review was originally written, by me, for Offbeat Magazine. Read the full story here: https://www.offbeat.com/news/fraziers-connection/

Bro, in the year of our Lord 2019, there is ZERO reason to allow smoking in a place that serves food. That's just gross.  We were here to see a band on a Saturday night and naturally the place was packed. They have a kitchen area, a stage area and a decent tap list. They also allow smoking. Not only do they allow smoking but the place reeks of cigarette smoke. I think everyone was smoking when we were here- even the bartender was smoking while she was working. Good Lord. That's not even the craziest part. The craziest part is the cigarette machine at the door, so you can buy cigarettes to smoke! It was insane.  We were here maybe 45 minutes and left stinking of smoke, so I doubt I'll be back. Jefferson Parish smoking ban soon come.

Ooh Barracuda!   When I first heard that Algiers point was getting a Barracuda Taco stand, I was pretty excited. Barracuda is one of the more popular taco places in New Orleans. This location is an old Gulf station, which is an icon of the neighborhood.  David and I stopped in to see what it was all about. First of all, all of the seating is outside, so if you have an issue with the heat, you might want to get your tacos and margaritas to go. I got a couple of pork tacos, and David got the chicken taco. The pork taco was excellent. It was a bit spicy, with big chunks of spicy, juicy pork. It was a bit messy, but I really enjoyed it.  I didn't get to try any of the Margaritas this time, but they are definitely on my list. I have heard they are amazing. In fact, I know that they are fresh made with none of the artificial stuff, so that makes me even more anxious to try them.  The atmosphere here is fun and funky and, because it's mostly neighborhood people, the vibe is very friendly. Be sure to clean up your mess and don't leave scraps of food on the tables, because it attracts flies.  David and I loved it and we will be back.  I interviewed the owner of Barracuda for my Offbeat Eats column here: https://www.offbeat.com/articles/dining-out-barracuda/

What's that smell? Oh, it's Kirkland's.  Okay, so as others have mentioned there is a very STRONG scent of candles and perfumes in this place. I won't lie- I liked it for the first few minutes. Then I hated it. Then I didn't notice it.  Aside from the smell, Kirkland's is pretty awesome! I don't even think I have set foot in a Kirkland's since there was one at Oakwood mall in the pre-Katrina days. This store is packed with all kinds of decor for the home from lamps to wall hangs and really cool stuff for the kitchen. They had these really cute measuring cups (see my photo) with cupcakes on the handle! That stuff is right up my alley and in my wheelhouse.  Fair warning: being in this place will make you want to redecorate asap. I want a portrait of a French cafe on MY wall, is all I'm going to say. I found a really cute hand painted tea cup that is large enough for a lot of green tea for about $7, so I was more than happy to pick that up.  I liked it here and I'll be back.

Jen L's review reminded me that I had never reviewed this bar built on bad decisions and broken dreams.  Most dive bars aren't too bad. Most dive bars have their selling points. Brothers 3 has two good jukeboxes. Henry's has a surprisingly good beer selection. Snake and Jake's has...a dark dank bar and a sofa that might give you ebola.  Maybe it's because I wasn't a Tulane or Loyola kid, but I didn't discover Snake and Jake's until my late 20's. By then, my eyes had opened onto the reality of what this place really is and any charm that I would have found here was long gone.  The people are nice enough but it's so dark. I like a dark bar, but it's so dark here that I feel uncomfortable. Is that part of the charm? Hey, whatever floats your boat. And the bathrooms. Ohhhhh the bathrooms. They are pretty much pitch dark, which can only be a blessing. God only knows what it looks like in the light.  The biggest problem that I've encountered here is by the time people get here, the night is over. It's done. You don't need to be drinking anymore, you need to be at home sleeping. People tend to be obnoxious and start waving their cigarettes around in tight quarters. That's another thing- the smoke. The point is nearly moot, but the ventilation in this joint is non existent. Really, the smoking ban will only help this place.   It's one of those places you want to visit at least once, just to say you did. Go once. Have a beer, watch out for flailing cigarettes, don't use the bathroom and, for the love of God, do NOT sit on that sofa.

I attended a home brewer's beer tasting here.  I hadn't been to Deutsche Haus since it was moved from it's previous location to this new spot, so even though I knew what to expect, the experience was still pretty new. The beer tasting itself was outside in the parking lot area and inside there is a full bar and lots of tables with "family style" seating. The place got crowded fast, and when the food came out there was a pretty long line, but it moved quickly.  When it was time for the food, I was delighted. They were serving three different types of sausage as well as sauerkraut, German potato salad, bread and even pretzels. All of the food was amazing! I really enjoyed my bratwurst and the other type of sausage was a spicy sausage that was fantastic. I could tell that the sauerkraut and potato salad were homemade and it was some of the best I have had. I'm happy to report that even though Deustche Haus is in a new spot, the quality hasn't changed.  I am considering becoming a member because I am part German (6% is better than nothing!) and I had a good time here. As Emily said, this spot is temporary and they are planning to move, so be sure to support them in this location while you can.

The few times I've been here, I've been left wondering how the place really stays in business. I mean, it's not a bad place, but there is never really anyone in here. The staff is nice enough and there are always one or two "regulars" at the bar, but you would expect more on a Friday or Saturday night.  While I wouldn't go out of my way to visit this place, it's not bad if you are looking for a quiet place to have a beer and hang out.

From start to finish, saffron was a class act. I stopped in here on a Friday night on a work venture. I didn't have reservations, so the hostess kindly asked me if I would be okay it's sitting at the bar and I was more than okay with that. I sat at the bar and the bartender was friendly and jovial. He gave me my menu and I looked it over with the light. I started with the gumbo and I had the pork vindaloo, as my entree.  I also treated myself to some coffee and dessert. All of the food and service was out of this world. I had such a wonderful time, that I actually wished that I lived in the neighborhood so that this restaurant would be within walking distance.   I had always wanted to visit saffron when it was in Gretna, but I never had the opportunity. Everything here was picture perfect and I couldn't have been happier. I will definitely return. This is perfect for a date night or just the night out with friends.  I made a guide to Indian food! Check it out here https://nola.verylocal.com/heres-your-guide-to-indian-food-in-new-orleans/188741/

We stopped in here after another New Year's Eve party was kind of dull and we were happy to find a good crowd, a good beer selection and generous seating.  This is more a sports bar than an Irish pub, but the folks are really friendly and they have some of my favorite beers on tap, so I was happy. There are plenty of tvs, so it would be a good place to watch a game and the drinks are reasonably priced, considering the location. The bartender was nice and the place is pretty clean.

Deep below the streets of New Orleans, the city's newest bar is hidden. Double Dealer, an homage to the speakeasy type of bar of the Prohibition Era, is tucked under the famed Orpheum Theater at 129 Roosevelt Way. Here you will find a different kind of drinking and socialization experience. Named after a New Orleans literary journal from the 1920s, Double Dealer keeps a respect for history, while creating a social space for the modern era.  Walking down the stairs and down the long ramp to the bar itself, you first think you might be in the wrong place. Once your trust your instincts, you are greeted with the wall of "house rules" reminding performers to return house props and costumes, and to raise a toast to Barry, the ghost said to haunt this space.  Upon entering the place itself, you're welcomed with warm lighting and colors. The gorgeous bar is a nod to the art-deco period and a waitress brings you drink menus as soon as you sit down. On either side of the bar are "snugs"- booths where patrons can sit and drink, unbothered, away from the fray of the crowd. The velvet curtains, which can be pulled for more privacy, are actually repurposed vintage stage curtains, adding a touch of authenticity, as well as a nod of respect to the theater above. When in the snugs, a switch can be flipped that illuminates a red light, indicating to the bartender that you're ready for another round.  The cocktails at Double Dealer are in a class by themselves. I was fortunate enough to sample a few and one of my favorites was Cables of Cobweb, a refreshing rum cocktail that was crisp and subtle.
