Another drink I found to be delicious was Blind Viking; made with Mezcal, Aperol, sweet vermouth and bitters, it had a smoky after taste and just enough bite. If classic cocktails are more your thing, Double Dealer offers tasty favorites such as the Old Fashioned, the Sidecar and the old standby the Daiquiri. Drinks are wonderfully priced and no cocktail is more than $12. Considering how well-crafted these drinks are (and how easily they go down), that's quite the steal!  This is a lovely new spot and I'll definitely be back.  *Portions of this review was written, by me, for Offbeat Magazine. Read the full write up here: http://www.offbeat.com/news/double-dealer/

Meat. MEEEEEEEEEEEEAT. Seriously they call this place a meatery for a reason and good Lord they do not skimp on the good stuff.  First of all, can we talk about how fantastic it is that you can order drinks by the pitcher? Super convenient. We got the pineapple basil margarita and it was delicious. It was a different kind of margarita, but I really enjoyed it.  Now for the food. Fair warning: if you are going to eat here you have to know what to expect. If you are going for dinner, DO NOT eat lunch that day. That lunch is just going to be taking up valuable stomach real estate when it's time to chow down on meat.  We started with the meatery board which is as fantastic as it sounds. Oh, what's that? A board with a ton of different meats? Yeah. IN. You get a lot on the board: boudin balls, hogs head cheese, pate', sausage and a lot of other stuff I can't even remember because I think I blacked out from meat joy half way through.  For my entree' I got the pork shoulder which comes in it's own gravy on top of a nice grit cake. It is pretty much a pork brick. It's a slab of pork that is smothered in the best gravy you will probably ever taste. You better go in and get it now because the waitress told me that the chef switches up his pork dish every few months. Did I beat the pork shoulder or did it beat me? I can't say, but I will say that if the pork shoulder was Mayweather and I was Ortiz, I would have gone down in the 4th round. TKO!  Yes, I got dessert. They have a bacon and peanut butter Doberge cake by Debby does Doberge and I didn't have the strength to resist it. Lucky for me I had someone to split it with, so I didn't have to be rolled out of the door.  Would I go back to Toups? Oh yes. Would I order the meat board AND the pork brick in the same sitting? Probably not. I would have to force myself to choose one or the other, but either way it's a win.

If you're in the mood for soul food this is the PLACE!  Look, I had already heard about the long lines at Chicken's, so I stopped in as soon as they opened on a Monday. You know I had to hook it up with some red beans and rice and fried chicken.  The food here is served hot, fresh off the line. They have daily specials, so be sure to check the website to see what is being offered. The red beans and rice I had was perfect and the fried chicken was juicy and packed with flavor.  The staff here was super friendly and helped me figure out exactly what I wanted. Even though I was here early, the crowd was starting to build as I ate, so if you're on a time restriction, get here early!

Buzz has been surrounding Blue Giant for months and I already had a plan of action going in. I find with these hot-spots it's best to try and go at lunch, so I headed over around 1 p.m. on a Saturday. There was a bit of a wait, but we quickly settled into a booth in the cozy dining room.   I love the atmosphere of this spot. It's small inside, but not cramped, and the open kitchen provides thrills as you wait for your food. There are a few booths and more seating at the bar space, overlooking the kitchen. Peking ducks hang in the kitchen's window, tempting those dining to try one out for taste.  Onto the food! I started with an order of egg rolls ($3 each) and an order of the shrimp and pork dumplings. I was so excited about this egg roll; it came out so fresh that it was steaming when I cracked it open. There is a nice crust on the outside, and it has that nice "crunch" when you bite into it. It's packed with a generous amount of pork and shrimp and the flavors are exotic and familiar. I love a good egg roll and Blue Giant's immediately jumped to the top of my "must order" list. The dumplings are another star; they are pan fried and come with a nice lacy crust on the outside, almost akin to edible art. The dumplings themselves are soft and flavorful and filled with tender pork and shrimp. They have a very light crunch on the outside, while the inside is soft and melts in your mouth.  For my entrée I got the Salt and Pepper Catfish. This is piece of catfish sliced, battered and fried, almost tempura style, and served with sautéed onions and peppers, which added some spice. The catfish itself was light and it was a dish that would have easily paired well with some of the other offerings on the menu, especially if you're visiting for dinner and you're looking to go "all out."  Don't go into Blue Giant expecting an authentic trip through the Orient or typical greasy American-Chinese take-out. The dishes here err more on the side of Chinese-inspired, but if you like Chinese with an American twist, as I do, then this will be the place for you.   *Portions of this review was written, by me, for Offbeat Magazine. Read the full write up here: http://www.offbeat.com/news/american-chinese-eatery-blue-giant-is-a-new-star-on-the-dining-scene/

Who doesn't love good books? If you are looking for a picture perfect bookshop, Faulkner House books is the place for you. This spot is known throughout the country for their impeccable collection of Southern books and classics.   Walking in you feel like you're in the library of someone who has been collecting books for years. There's a cozy feel to the place that will make you want to lurk and linger for hours. You'll want to thumb through the stacks to find that perfect book that speaks to you.  You'll see signatures of authors on the wall, so you will be inspired by greatness. The bookstore is under new ownership and they are doing right by the place. Every book is perfection and fits into the City and the store with ease. They even have a subscription service where someone working at the store will pick out some books that will be sure to set your soul on fire and bring a smile to your face.   Located in a cozy alley, Faulkner House books feels like a secret. Well the secrets out. This store is a must visit for any bibliophile.  I wrote about this shop for Very Local New Orleans here: https://nola.verylocal.com/faulkner-house-books-new-orleans-bookstore/182301/

This is a review of the bar area.  While I have yet to experience the food here, I have been through for a Bloody Mary quite a few times, and I have to say that they make one of the best I have ever had. This place has a nice casual local vibe and I think most of the people who stop in here are locals. Staff is friendly and they pour generously.

Delicious pastries and Mojo coffee on the westbank! Yes, please. The owner of this spot makes all of her pastries by hand such as croissants, cheesecake, and scones. Not to mention mojo coffee, which is one of my favorites. I'm so excited to have it right down the street.  The cafe itself is super cozy and welcoming, and the prices are really good, especially considering everything is handmade. I'm really excited that we have another coffee and pastry option here on the West Bank, that isn't Starbucks or PJ's.  I wrote about this spot for Big Easy Magazine. Read all about it here: https://www.bigeasymagazine.com/2021/05/02/local-pastry-chef-serves-up-delicious-treats-at-newly-opened-le-cafe-eblouir-coffee-pastry-boutique/

I completely fell in love with this whimsical little gallery.  The art here looks like something you would find in a child's bedroom, but it has that grown-up feel that let's you know that there's no shame in enjoying the art here, no matter your age. Whimsical fairy tale characters, New Orleans and Mardi Gras themed art and painting of animals of all types is what you'll see here.   They have small prints which are extremely affordable and really, the only reason I didn't buy something when I was here was because I couldn't decide exactly what I wanted. I know what I do want: a print of the kittens in the king cake, for obvious reasons.  The artist is very talented and I love the "carefree" feel of her work.

I was craving Italian and when I heard about this spot in Kenner, I decided to take a trip.  I had been told that the meatballs are a must, and for $5, I couldn't pass them up. When the waitress brought out these meatballs, Y'ALL! Talk about a work of art. I knew they were going to be big, but these meatballs are huge and coated in Mozzarella cheese. It's the type of cheese that has that nice cheesy pull that you usually only see in pizza commercials. It's the kind of cheese that you have to twirl around the fork like pasta. The meatballs themselves can't be described -- spiced and flavored perfectly and made from, what I can only assume, is an old family recipe. The sauce is out-of-this-world. Like I said, I was not fortunate enough to be born Italian, but food like this makes me want to look into some sort of conversion program. I need a Sicilian grandma to teach me her ways, just so I can make sauce like this.  With all this meatball love, I had totally forgotten about my entrée. I ordered the eggplant Parmesan, because we're trying to keep it healthy over here. Yes, it comes with angel hair pasta topped with the angel sauce, but it also comes with a salad. It's called the "pair it with a salad" diet and it's going to sweep the nation. Anyway, the eggplant was pretty perfect and, let's be honest, everything is kicked up a notch or 12 when it's topped with red gravy and Mozzarella cheese. The angel hair pasta was the perfect balance to everything and, believe it or not, I left the meal feeling satisfied and not heavy. Yes, I did leave with three containers worth of leftovers, which I'll be munching on for days, but it's all about pacing yourself. Right?  I should really mention how reasonable this spot actually is. Nothing is over $20 and the portions are huge. The food is delicious and you will most likely leave with leftovers. Like any true Italian family, the Gendusas aren't going to let you walk away hungry.   *Portions of this review was originally written, by me, for Offbeat Magazine. Read the full story here: http://www.offbeat.com/news/gendusas-serves-up-old-school-italian-in-kenner-its-worth-the-trip/

Gracious Cafe on S. Jefferson Davis has been a favorite of mine for a while and I always stop in for iced coffee whenever I'm in the area. When I saw that they were adding a location to St. Charles, I was pretty pleased, even though I think the original might be "easier access" for me.  Anyway, I decided to stop in here during my work runs and grab an iced coffee. This place is cute and has a little bit of everything: coffee, pastries, sandwiches, salads, beer, and wine. Oh yeah, this place serves booze, but you can't drink it on premises. I'm pretty "no frills" with these types of things, so I just got my normal iced coffee to go. It was okay. For some reason, it seemed to be lacking a little something, which is odd because it's always really good and rich when I get it at the other place. This time it just seemed a bit watered down. It was still good and I did enjoy it, so I'm not really complaining, but it seemed different. Maybe it was just an off day.  The atmosphere in here is really nice and gives off a nice little "cafe" type vibe. I think this shop fits well into the area.

It's pretty surprising that I had never been here, since I have lived on the Westbank my entire life.  I think I may have gone one other time when I was a kid, but I remembered nothing about the place.  A friend and I had lunch here, and after I figured out exactly how to get to the place (it's located at the edge of Narnia), I went in and enjoyed a really good meal.  I got the catfish and white beans, which was the lunch special and one of my favorites.  It was amazing and so good!  It was a generous serving and cooked perfectly.  The atmosphere of this place is really nice and I could see myself going here on a dinner date.  It has an "upscale" feel. but I didn't feel underdressed in my jeans and sweater.  I definitely want to go back and try some other things on the menu.

I'm going to just lay it on the line: the bar is cool, but the drinks are overpriced. Way overpriced. $8 for a beer you can get for $5 elsewhere overpriced. Look, I'm not a dope. It's the Quarter. You're gonna charge what dumb tourists are gonna pay. Can I show you my Louisiana ID and get a discount? Even if it's just a buck off? Seriously, we are on the same team here. We're all friends. $15 for two beers is a little much. It's water and barley...don't get arrogant.  Other than that, this place is cool. Cool people and cool staff. Just don't rob me.

More like 3.75 stars. I had been wanting to try this place for a while, so when I had a photo shoot in the area a few weeks ago, it was my perfect opportunity to stop in for lunch.  I was here on a Saturday afternoon and the place was packed. I knew what I wanted- the brat burger and a side of sauerkraut, so I ordered and sat over by the side wall. While I waited, one thing I noticed was how warm the place is. I guess summer + small space + kitchen heat= warmth, but I wished they at least had a fan going for air movement.  My food came out pretty quickly and I was excited because it all looked delicious. First of all, the sauerkraut was great! It had that nice tang to it that I like and I really enjoyed it. The brat burger was okay. The meat itself was delicious; the only problem was the bun. The sausage came on a thick pretzel bun that almost overwhelmed the rest of the sandwich. I really liked the sausage though, so if I go back I will opt for a regular brat bun.  I also want to go back and try some beer and pretzels!

I am so excited that something has moved into this building and I couldn't be more excited about this locally owned spot.  I had lunch at Southern Charm Bistreaux and Bar on the second day it was open and I was delighted to see the staff was busy serving a packed house. I was greeted with a smile at the door and when I was seated, was treated to some complimentary jalapeño cornbread. It was delicious and made for a nice treat and got my appetite going. Looking over the menu, I was happy to see on Monday through Friday from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. they have an "Express Lunch Menu" that includes such offerings as Blackened Chicken Alfredo, a Classic Burger topped with your choice of cheese, Smothered Catfish, Mom's Pot Roast and more.  I decided to get the smothered catfish, which is pan-fried catfish with Cajun crawfish sauce over dirty rice and sautéed vegetables. The serving was generous for lunch, the fish was tender and cooked to perfection, and the crawfish sauce was a nice touch and very tasty. I also greatly enjoyed the sautéed vegetables and they acted as a nice accent to the fish.  Other selections on the main menu include barbecue shrimp, charbroiled oysters, a variety of salads, a selection of po-boys, burgers and other favorites such as pecan roasted redfish, seafood feast pasta, a pork porterhouse and a smoked duck leg quarter. The team also plans to serve brunch on Sundays.  Hospitality was certainly not on short hand during my visit here; I was repeatedly asked if everything was to my liking and co-owner Kendall Bussey came over and encouraged me to tell him if I had any suggestions on what could be improved. The staffers never stopped as they ran food out to tables quickly and made sure that no one who came through the door had to wait to be seated. Considering this was only their second day of operation, I was impressed with how well everything flowed.  Cross was our waitress and she couldn't have been nicer and my whole experience was wonderful. I can definitely see myself coming back and having a drink at the bar while enjoying some tasty apps.

Such a great place! Stopped in here on a Friday night and I was surprised that there was no one else dining here (this seems to be some kind of trend with me). We were immediately seated and began looking over the menu.  Everything sounded so good. I liked that they had different pictures of their special rolls to give you an idea of what you are ordering. We both started by ordering some iced green tea and edamame. I was delighted when the green tea came bottled. None of the mix stuff you get at other places. I could tell that this stuff was freshly brewed.  We ordered salmon sashimi which came in a generous portion and was fresh and delicious. For our rolls, we decided on the Tiger Eye roll which is Smoked Salmon, Cream Cheese, Jalapeno, with Soybean Wrap and  topped with eel sauce, the Nemo roll which is Spicy Tuna, Snow Crab, Avocado, topped with Fresh Salmon, Chili Oil and creamy sauce, and Snow Crab Naruto which is thin Sliced Cucumber wrapped with Snow Crab, Crab Stick, Avocado, Masago, with a creamy sauce. It was all so good! I think my favorite was the Nemo roll, because I am a huge salmon lover.  The service was great and all in all the meal was amazing. I will definitely be back. I think that the reason the place wasn't packed was because there is a bar right next door that shares the parking lot. The parking lot was full of bar people, so I think that passers by assumed that the restaurant was full. I guarantee you probably won't have to wait for a table, so be sure to stop in and check this place out.

Lakeside Shopping Center is definitely the nicest mall in the area and easily blows Oakwood, Esplanade, and Clearview Mall out of the water. The good thing about Lakeside is that they seem to keep up with the times. The stores are all very current and trendy and the mall is renovated pretty regularly and has a nice fresh look.  Whenever I have to take a trip to Lakeside I try to go during the week because it's not as packed with young people (get off my lawn) and really the only people you have to deal with are retirees and mall walkers. They have nice shops that you aren't going to find at other malls and I'm a fan of the MAC store, Athleta, Macy's and Sephora. They also have MULTIPLE bra stores that aren't Victoria's Secret and I can't express enough how important something like that is, because sometimes you like to have options.  The food court has a nice selection of eateries, although most are not-so-healthy fast food and if you're looking to eat healthy, Byblos Express is pretty much your only option. Outside of the mall itself they have P.F. Chang's, which has been there since I was in high school, and The Cheesecake Factory. The mall also regularly holds fun events here such as little performances during the holiday season and bridal shows.  I don't get to the mall much, but if you're looking to do a day of indoor shopping, this is definitely the spot.

It had been a long White Linen Night by the time I found myself at Geisha. I had done way too much walking, I had been to a boring art show (even by boring art show standards) and I was starving because I hadn't eaten since breakfast because of a busy day. It was late and I was craving sushi. Horinoya was closed, so the cab driver suggested Geisha. Due to all of these factors, my review may be a bit skewed.  Walking in, I was immediately impressed by the size of this place. It was really big and had a nice atmosphere. We were immediately seated and looking over the menu, everything sounded like heaven. I can't remember everything I ordered but this is what I do remember: salmon sashimi, salmon sushi, salmon roe, tuna roll, Philly roll and two specialty rolls. I can't remember the exact name of the speciality rolls, but one was flash fried with cream cheese, and it's hard to mess up what is basically fried cheese.  The salmon sashimi was incredible and I liked that the slices were thick. All of the other rolls and sushi were on point and everything was incredible. We finished everything with no problem. I probably could have eaten more.  Now, I don't know if it's because of the time of night, but I loved this place. The food was fresh and delicious and I like that they are open a bit later. I might have to go back when I'm not on the verge of starving to death, in order to make a full assessment, but as it stands now I will definitely go back.

It's been almost a whole month since I ate at Emeril's and the reason this review has taken to long to piece together is because I'm expected to fit 25 years of history and a delicious food experience into one single review. I'll try my best.  A friend of mine had a business meeting at Emeril's and being the awesome friend he is, he asked me if I wanted to tag along. Not only am I being considered for new business ventures, but I get a fantastic meal out of the deal? Ok, I'm in.  Walking in, I immediately loved the feel of Emeril's. It was upscale, yet intimate and cozy. It wasn't too bright and the large dining room had a nice feel about it. I sat down with my dining companions and was served 3 types of bread as soon as I was seated. I can't remember the exact description of each type of bread, but I do remember that the corn bread was amazing.  The menu made ordering difficult. Everything sounded amazing. I decided to start with the soup of the day which was crawfish flourintine. This was a tomato based soup filled with delicious crawfish. It was flavored to perfection and a delectable start to an incredible meal.  For my entree, I decided to try the Andouille crusted drumfish, which the waiter informed me is one of the dishes that Emeril's is known for. I was excited that I got to try this "famous" dish for myself. When the fish came, I was blown away. It was fried to perfection and sat atop some fried shoestring potatoes.  The fish itself was topped with glazed pecans and a nice sauce. The entire dish was delicious and had tons of flavor. I can see why this is one of the dishes that Emeril's is famous for.  The entire meal was exquisite from start to finish. The staff was attentive and perfect and went out of their way to make sure that we had everything that we needed. Emeril's is one of the finest restaurants in New Orleans, and a "must" for locals and visitors alike.

Well, I didn't even know this lake had a name, much less that it was reviewable.  This is a beautiful spot located right by the New Orleans Museum of Art at City Park. It's a spot where people come to relax and take in the scenery or paddle around on a kayak. I most recently found myself here when I came to check out the tulips, which are planted annually next to the lake. You can sit on the side and enjoy and a nice day and watch people boat around in the water and watch the ducks waddle back and forth.

We got some catering from this place and it was delicious!  We ordered big trays of pasta, jambalaya, salad, finger sandwiches and brownies. I personally tried the pasta, salad and finger sandwiches. The pasta was penne pasta that was nice and cheesy and had tons of flavor. My favorite was definitely the salad because it was packed with goodies- it had spinach, avocado, walnuts, feta, dried cranberries and it was topped with a yummy vinaigrette. It was one of the best salads I have ever had and it made me want to go to Cafe Royale and have more. The finger sandwiches were pretty good, but didn't really blow me away and I've had better elsewhere.  If you need something catered, I would chose Cafe Royale because I was more than pleased with the food.

This CVS earns bonus points because it was open on Christmas! I think they are all open on Christmas, but this was is convenient for me, because it's near me.  This CVS is WAY better organized than other ones that I have been to and everything is really easy to find. The staff was super friendly, even though they were working on Christmas and I was able to get in, find what I needed and get out in a timely manner.

I was so glad that I found myself in the neighborhood since I had heard that this is one of the better Ideal Markets.  This is a small market, but they have the good stuff- namely sweet breads made fresh. After looking around, I got a sweet bread (it had a fancy name in Spanish, but I forgot to make a note of it) and it was delightful! I could tell that it was made in store and I enjoyed it later that evening.  If you're in the mood for something hot, they have a hot bar where they are serving up delicious looking authentic food, that must be good because there was a pretty sizable line for it. The staff is always working to keep everything fresh, and when I was here they were adding fresh pastries to the pasty case, so you can bet that no matter what time you get here you're sure to enjoy something that is tasty and fresh.  Like any convenience store, they have basic groceries and a nice selection of cheeses, fruits and other produce so you should be able to find whatever you might be looking for as far as that goes.

NOW SMOKE FREE!!  St Joe's is one of those weird little New Orleans places that I love.  It's a total dive, but it has a few redeeming qualities:  1) The place is decorated like a rejected church.  The crosses hanging from the ceilings and the dim lighting was enough to creep out this Catholic girl the first time I set foot in the place.  Just sitting at the bar makes you think you are doing something wrong.  2) A good jukebox.  Great tunes and although the place can get cramped, there is bound to be something in there that the crowd will love.    3) A signature drink.  Here, it's the mojito.  They have the regular one and the blueberry one.  Don't ask me about either, as I don't drink liquor.  I've heard they are good.  I think I had one once, but I wasn't impressed, but trust me, I'm not the one to judge.  4) The patio.  You can sit outside when the weather is nice and you'll feel like you are in a tropical paradise.  The patio is decorated with banana trees and there is an outside bar, which is always packed (get there early) when it isn't in the 90s.  5) Everything else.  A pool table, awesome atmosphere, nice people, and they allow dogs.  What more could you want?  Did I mention that the place is smoke free now??

This Taco Bell is pretty good. I just wish that it was closer to my house.  Taco Bell is pretty much the only fast food I eat, since I eat fast food so rarely. I stopped in here and I was happy that the line was not only short, but it moved quickly. I ordered a nacho supreme, which is my "usual" and is basically chips with cheese sauce, meat, and sour cream. I have found that some Taco Bells kind of haphazardly throw all of the ingredients together and call it a day. Not only did this Taco Bell actually make the nachos correctly, but they were generous with the "fixings". Hey, I know it sounds silly, but it's a Taco Bell review, so that's what you get.  In conclusion: pretty much as good as you can expect from a Taco Bell. Oh, and when I ask for "a lot" of sauce packets, they actually give me a lot of sauce packets.

I'll be the first to admit that this was a TOTAL experiment on my part. This was my first time ever trying Ethiopian food and I had no idea what to expect.  The menu has a little bit of everything from poultry to fish and lamb. We decided to order the lamb and whole fish. Everything is served at once on one plate with a side of soft bread and you are meant to pick up the food with it. All of the food was really good. The whole fish came with all of the bones intact, so eating it was a bit of a challenge, but after a few bites I got the hang of it. The lamb had a lot of flavor and the bread was porous and picked up a lot of flavor of whatever was wrapped in it, In addition to the meal, we had a yummy hot tea that was a perfect end to the experience.  I'll be totally honest- this food is going to take some getting used to, but I can appreciate that this is good food. Does that make sense? In other words- it's not up my *immediate* alley, but everything was perfectly cooked and had a lot of flavor. Out waiter was extremely nice, and although the restaurant was full, we were seated and served in a timely manner.  I definitely want to go back and try some more dishes. I know that if I try Ethiopian food a few more times it is something I will definitely love, so I'm excited to try more.

While ice cream will always have a place in my heart, there's just something special about gelato- ice cream's lighter cousin.  David and I were having a dessert craving, and this place had been on my list for a while, so we popped in. It was pretty busy for after 8 on a Saturday night, but we were served quickly. I had the raspberry gelato and it was delicious with lots of flavor and the lightness that I expect from gelato. If it hadn't been so late, I probably would have tried some of the coffee, so that's a good excuse to go back.  Aside from gelato, they have a great selection of sweet and savory crepes and with plenty of seating inside and outside, it's the perfect place for a bite to eat any time of day.

I'll be the first to admit that I am not really outdoorsy. I can go outside and have a good time, but when it comes to nature, the relationship is strictly platonic- there's no romance happening.  I didn't even know this place in Belle Chasse even existed until I was sent here for work purposes. This is basically a trail through some woods. If there's a park, I sure didn't see it. The trail itself varies between mud and grass and there are definitely some mushy areas, so wear appropriate footwear (I didn't). I do like that there are a lot of trees to shade you nicely from the sun on warmer days. I didn't find out until after I had gotten fairly deep into the woods that this is rattlesnake territory. I was walking through and I decided I wanted to get a closer look at a really cool tree. I just happened to look down and OH THERE'S A SNAKE and it was probably a rattlesnake, although I didn't stick around long enough to make pleasantries.  OH YEAH. And here's me with flat shoes on that barely cover my feet. I coulda died- that's all I'm saying.  If you are looking for basically untouched woods in the middle of Belle Chasse, this is the spot. They do give tours on certain days and they have "breakfast with the birds" events, that sound like they are worth checking out.

This Ulta is okay, but it's not the best one in the area.   The staff has always been really friendly. My complaint about this store is that it's pretty small compared to other Ultas I've been to and there is a limited selection of products. The samples that they have for people to swatch the more high end products are DISGUSTING and look old and like kids (or messy adults) have slammed their fingers into them. I would never put my hands anywhere near that stuff. Also, they should have tissue next to the samples so that if I do decide to swatch it on my hand, I can wipe it off when I'm done.  I do like that they have a pretty extensive designer perfume selection, as well as a wide variety of hair products. I go to this Ulta pretty regularly out of necessity, but it's not worth an extra trip.

I could have sworn that I had reviewed Wit's Inn, but here we are. Anyway, I love this place! Not only is it a fantastic place to watch a Saints game, but they make delicious bloody Marys and have fantastic pizza.  The crowd is more of a neighborhood krewe, but I have always found people here super friendly and fun. Whenever I go I usually sit at the bar, but they have plenty of tables and chairs if that isn't your thing. The crowd gets rowdy during Saints games, so come with your game face on.

I had never had Pho before (believe it or not), when my b/f decided that we had to go here for lunch.  I was hesitant at first and it was all really different, but I was in for a treat.  The serving of the noodles and broth was HUGE and delicious.  I wasn't feeling too adventurous, so I just got the kind with beef in it.  It all sounded so good that I know I will be back.

Wanted to update my review, adding a star.  When I first came here, I had never had Pho before. Now that I consider myself pretty seasoned on the stuff, I have come to appreciate how fantastic Tan Dinh's Pho is. I got the Pho Tai Nam, which is rare flank and brisket and an order of pork Spring rolls. It was all amazing. The broth had a ton of flavor and I love that you get a HUGE serving of it. The rolls were delicious as well.

I just discovered this place by chance and apparently it's only been open a month or two. Unless you're familiar with the area, you're going to have trouble finding Pho 99. Pro tip: it's in the strip mall near Auto Zone.  I was in the mood for something quick and cheap, so I stopped in here for lunch. They have a really extensive menu of all of the Vietnamese faves, but as always, I was in the mood for Pho. I got the large #10 with rare steak and brisket. The portion was HUGE and I was hoping that it was all as good as it looked. Lucky me, it was delicious. The meat was perfect and the broth was full of flavor without being overpowering. I'll admit that I don't have most sophisticated palate when it comes to Pho, but I know when a bowl is bland and this one definitely wasn't.  Take it from someone who actually ate here- this is a good bowl and if you're in the mood for Pho you won't be disappointed. I'll be back!

Even though Barcadia is a chain and brand new, I'm going to go ahead a give it four stars. Although, side note, I think this is probably where Shamrock got their business idea.  First of all, the place is huge and has a lot going on. In the front room, you have seating, a bar with a pretty decent beer selection and arcade games. Yeah, you heard that right, it has old school arcade games. The middle room is cool too with it's own bar and even more seating.   And then there's the back room. Ah, the back room. You go through a magical portal into the back room and magic happens. You gotta see it for yourself. It's the room in the back. Just go through the back door and you're in.  I really dug the atmosphere of the place, even though I saw a few people who would probably be better suited at Metro, but whatever. Of course, I dug the old school pinup calendars and magazine covers that adorned the walls. Barcadia, you totally stole my future bar/restaurant/antique store (patent pending) decorating idea!  Word on the street (and when I say street, I mean that little pathway you walk up to get into Barcadia) is that they will be serving burgers and other food soon, so I will definitely have to go back and write a review of the food.

Rue is one of my favorite places for coffee, and since the one on Magazine is now closed (boo) this is the one you gotta go to.  I'll be honest, I'm not the biggest fan of this location.  Oak in general tends to be kind of a mess, and I'm the type who doesn't like to drive around looking for a place to park.  Enough with the complaints!  I love the coffee here.  This place has huge windows and has a great light, and the cool thing about this Rue is the fact that it has an upstairs, so if you have to study and get away from the crowd, you can sneak up there and get some work done.  I'll probably re-review after I visit a few times and let the shop grow on me.

I don't get to Old Point very often.  Although it's conveniently located on the Westbank, it's just a place I find myself in very often.  When I do find myself here, it's a really cool experience.   Unless you live in the area, there's no real reason to go here, unless there is a band playing.  The venue is small, but they have bands playing here regularly and it's a cool place to have a drink and check out some local favorites.  I've never been here for a Saints game, but they have tvs, so I assume it's a good place to check one out.  I'll have to swing by next football season.  Fun fact: Scenes from the movie "Ray" were filmed here.  Wifi password: 1234567890

Let me start by saying that I am not a huge BBQ expert, so take this review for what it's worth.  While this place does have the moniker of "saloon", it is pretty big and spacious and has plenty of tables and chairs for dining. I stopped in here with a friend for lunch not really knowing what to expect. Looking over the menu, it seemed like typical faire. I had a pulled pork sandwich with potato salad. It was good, but it was lacking a good amount of sauce and I found it somewhat dry.  I didn't try any of the beer or spirits whilst I was here, so I can't comment on that, but they seemed to have a good number of local beers on tap.

This is a really nice bar with super friendly people.  We stopped in here after hanging out at Mimi's for a while. The bartender couldn't have been friendlier and the patrons were happy to chat. It's obviously a neighborhood bar full of regulars, but everyone was nice and inclusive.  The atmosphere is pretty dark and murky- it seems like a good place to go if you want to get lost for a few hours.

There is just something special about eating a meal in the heart of the French Quarter. The staff of places like this are always eager to show you a good time and make sure you experience the best of New Orleans.  I had just finished a photo shoot in the upstairs area of the place, when my companions and I decided to get lunch here as well. It was a rainy, miserable day, but it was nice because the doors were open and we could enjoy the rain from the safety of the restaurant.  We were seated in the downstairs area and greeted by a friendly woman who was eager to take our drink order. As I ordered my iced tea, I looked over to the bar area to see a man shucking fresh oysters. I love watching people shuck oysters. I guess because I love oysters, but there's also something really neat about watching someone who is really good at popping open those shells do his work. Maybe I'm odd.  Okay, onto the food. I decided on a chicken Caesar salad, thinking that this would be a good choice for a small, simple lunch. Well, the salad was HUGE and for the price I was not disappointed at all. The dressing came on the side, which I really liked and the chicken was tender and juicy. I guess I was hungrier than I thought, because I ended up eating the entire thing. It was fantastic!  I love Royal House and I will definitely be back. I feel like it's the perfect NOLA casual dining experience for local and tourist alike. They have everything on the menu from salads and sandwiches to shrimp and oysters platters, so you are sure to find something that you will enjoy.

I have had the opportunity to go to the Ogden a lot lately.  We have seen films and exhibits here and it was fabulous on White Linen Night in August.  A great place to check out on a Sunday afternoon when you want to look at lovely art and just "get away" for a bit.  There is always something going on and memberships aren't expensive at all.  Go go go!

It's been three long years (nearly four) since my last review of this place, so this is long overdue.  I went to Commander's for my birthday dinner last night and it was as amazing as to be expected.  Our main waitress was Evelyn and she was amazing and attentive. She made sure that we were taken care of and had everything that we could possibly need. The entire staff was on point and everything was perfect.  Looking over the menu, everything sounded so amazing and decadent. I decided to start with the turtle soup. Commander's is famous for their turtle soup and I have never had better in the city. It was full of amazing flavor and topped with sherry to add a little more kick. For my entree, I enjoyed the pecan crusted Gulf fish. This fish was cooked to perfection and topped with tender crab meat. It was served in a delectable cream sauce which complimented the flavors of the fish perfectly. For a side, I got the goat cheese stone ground grits, since I am on a tad of a grits kick. They were delicious, but I had to add a little more salt to them. I totally understand why they weren't salted and this wasn't a big deal. The grits were tasty and I really enjoyed them.  For dessert, I decided on the pecan pie- one of my favorites, topped with home spun vanilla ice cream. This sugary treat was the perfect end to this memorable meal.  At the beginning of the meal, I was asked if I was celebrating anything and when I told them it was my birthday, they added balloons to the table and brought me a chef's hat to wear. It was a nice touch and a lot of fun. They even put a candle in my pecan pie as part of the celebration.  There's a reason Commander's Palace is considered one of the best restaurants in New Orleans. From start to finish, you are made to feel special and you are given beyond the five star treatment. I will always return.

It's definitely time for a re-review, especially because the store has moved since my last review.  Retro Active is a great shop and I love the place on Oak. It's SO much bigger than the place on Magazine was and everything is setup perfectly. Here you will find a lovely collection of everything from vintage hats to bags to dresses to jewelry and even some men's pieces (which are located upstairs).  If you aren't really familiar with vintage clothing or if you aren't sure what you are looking for or what will look good on you, Leslie will be happy to help. She owns the store and is an EXPERT in all things vintage. You can seriously show her anything from any era and she will be able to tell you all about it. That's exactly what you want when you are vintage shopping.  All of the items are super reasonably priced and this isn't one of those stores where everything will be out of your price range. While you will find more expensive items here, you are sure to find some gorgeous affordable pieces as well. All items are fairly priced and in good, clean condition.

Call Nancy Drew. Call The Hardy Boys. We have a case of another missing review on our hands. Madigan's, I have definitely reviewed you before; I would not have checked in this many times without writing a proper review. Oh well, here we are again.  Madigan's is known mainly as a college hang out, and I guess that's true to a certain extent. On weekend nights you will find a younger crowd here, but it doesn't get as crazy as other college bars in the area. As of late, I have been meeting friends here in the late afternoon/early evening for post-work drinks. The bar gets gorgeous light at this hour and the big windows allow you to look out on Carrollton Avenue and watch the street cars go by.  The bar itself is big, so you never feel cramped and they have an internet jukebox so that you can play whatever you want to hear as you unwind from a long day. There's a pool table in the back, if that's your thing, and you can order food from GB's if you are looking for something to munch on.  Madigan's isn't really a regular destination for me, but I always enjoy my time here.

I was in the area, so I decided to stop in for a quick lunch after I checked Yelp and I saw that they had a pretty good lunch special.  Walking in, there was no one else here at 2. I get it- it's a little late for lunch. I knew what I wanted, so I ordered immediately. I got the beef shawarma lunch special which comes with rice, hummus and pita bread. It was just okay. The rice was pretty good, so I had so complaints there and the hummus was good as well. The meat, while spiced well with a nice flavor, was really tough. I don't know if it was a poor cut of meat or overcooked, but it was hard to get through it. Also, the pita was a bit stale and not warm, which was disappointing.  The waiter was very nice and attentive and my food came out shortly after I ordered it. Before tip, my lunch was a bit over $10 and I do think that it is well worth the price for what you get. It sure beats going to a chain for lunch. While I wouldn't rush back, I wouldn't hesitate to give them another shot if I am in the area for lunch.

Ross!  I went into the store today to check on your progress since my last review!  I was shocked to discover that you have actually learned something!  I walked in, and I immediately noticed that the clothing was more organized on the racks, there were no messes or clothes on the floor and things were grouped together by size!  The second thing I noticed was 4 (count 'em) FOUR registers were open, as opposed to the previous count of one total open register!  There was still a line, but it moved quickly and there wasn't a long wait to check out.  It was fantastic!  I rewarded your efforts today, by not only purchasing a dress (I was able to find it easily, because the racks were organized by size and the fast moving line gave me no excuse to not get it), but by coming on here and boosting you up a star.  Why not a boost of 2 stars?  I want to make sure that this isn't a fluke, Ross.  Don't get lazy as the summer goes on.  Keep up the good work and that fourth star will be yours, and I will visit your place more often.

Kinda mediocre.  I usually find myself here when I am heading somewhere else on Magazine and I get hungry.  The margaritas aren't bad, but the food is nothing great.  One plus is that you can sit outside on nice days.

It feels weird to review a "chain" bookstore in New Orleans, when there are so many awesome "homegrown" bookstores in the city, but this is the one I go to, so there it is.  I find myself in B&N at least once or twice a month.  They are always having fantastic sales and the staff has always been incredibly friendly and eager to help me find anything I may be looking for.  I like that they have a lot of art books (and some really obscure ones) and they have a huge section dedicated to books by local authors and about the city.   I would love for a local bookstore to pop up in my neck of the woods, but until that happens, I am happy to call this place a favorite.

Oh, Ross, you are an enigma wrapped in a riddle wrapped in a mess.  Let's start with the good.  You carry all kind of clothes, but specifically, the dresses you carry are great.  I can find anything here, from casual to dressy and for a really great price.  There are dresses here from the same brand as dresses I have seen at Dillard's (for a lot more money).  I love to come here and look for a nice sundress, when I need one for a summer party and the ones I have have become boring.  Now, the bad.  Oh, Ross.  Why do you have only one register open out of seven?  Don't you see the super long line this creates?  Don't you realize that most times I don't visit you, because the length of time I stand in line isn't worth the money I will be saving by patronizing you?  I mean, there are TWO greeters at the door.  Couldn't one of those ladies be working another register?  Certainly they have more skill than just saying, "Welcome to Ross!" when I walk in.   Also, your aisles are super narrow and your shopping carts are super wide.  I understand that you are pressed for space, but a few inches would make a world of difference.  Also, wouldn't it make sense for customers to NOT push their wide carts down the aisles, thus blocking anyone else who would like to shop in said aisle, but can't, because it would be a squeeze?  I thought this was common sense, but here we are.   Last but not least, all of the sizes are mixed up.  You have 2's mingling with 12's and 6's cavorting with 10's.  There's no rhyme or reason to this.  That's one thing if I'm at a thrift store, but Ross, you aren't a thrift store.  Don't sell yourself short.  Get organized!  Let's be honest, Ross, I am being very generous with my two stars.  You know it.  I know it.  So many simple changes could be made in order to make this store great.  PLEASE start with opening more registers.  There are people who would LOVE a job right now.  Hire more people.    In conclusion, Ross, you have an assignment: 1) Hire more people and open more registers. 2) Expand the aisles.  More space means more shoppers! 3) Organize your selections by size!  2,4,6,8,10,12...etc.  In that order, Ross!  Don't get creative!
Got a couple of po boys here a few weeks ago.  Really good, and the oyster po boy is as expensive as you would expect.  ;) I'd go back.

This is a delightful spot right in the middle of the avenue. They have pastries, fruits, smoothies, coffee drinks, tea and the like.  On the night I stopped in, it was kind of late and I was craving some carrot and beet juice (who doesn't?!) and I was majorly bummed when the woman behind the counter told me that they had just begun breaking down the juice machine. Really made me blue, especially since they were an hour from closing. I decided to get an iced green tea. It was okay, and I really have no complaints. It didn't knock my socks off, but it's tea.  I like the atmosphere here. A lot of tables and chairs for people to study (many were) and a lot of space to spread out. There's a nice seating area by the window, so you can look out onto the avenue as you enjoy your breakfast, lunch or coffee.  I definitely want to return and actually try their fruit juice. I'll be happy to re-review upon a future visit.

Just in time for Christmas, this toy store would make any kid's (or kid at heart's) toy dreams come true.  We passed through here because I had been past this shop a few times without ever going in. Upon entering, you're swept away to a toy wonderland. They have everything from stuffed animals and baby dolls to collectible figurines and books. One thing I really liked about this store is the fact that it's focused mainly on actual toys rather than electronics. As much as I love the modern games and such, there's something to be said about sitting down and actually playing "hands on" with something.  They had a nice assortment of local kids books, which I thought was awesome and they had some gorgeous chess sets that any chess player would love. I especially liked the cool superhero figurines that they had here that would be at home on any collector's shelf.  Even though we were here just before closing, the woman working was very friendly and made sure that we weren't looking for anything specific that she could help find. I wish there were more toy stores like this around, because I really feel like they are slowly fading away.

Wow. I had no idea that this gem was here and I had no idea that it was so big!  Walking in, I was immediately taken with the huge selection of fresh produce. They have a wide variety of everything you would want- and a large variety of peppers for all of your cooking needs. They have a fantastic bakery case full of Latin American goodies. One thing that stood out to me was stuffed cheese bread. Talk about a must have!  I also liked that they had a wide selection of neat looking cookies and snacks that I had never heard of, but looked delicious. They had this one thing that was a cookie sandwich filled with strawberry marshmallow. Although I was tempted, I didn't cave in, but I might have to go back and pick these up. As others have said, the meat section is incredible. If you are a fan of beef tongue, they have a whole pile of it. Go nuts. haha.  One section of this market that I will definitely be trying in the future is the cafeteria. Here you can get Latin American hot dishes of all types and there is a nice area where you can sit and eat. Everything seemed well priced and the tables looked nice and clean.  While this market isn't as lush with goodies as Ideal, I would definitely say that it's worth checking out, if you're in the area.

I don't know.  On a scale of "Sucky" to "Awesome", I think that I would rate this place a solid "Meh".  First, let me start by saying that I'm not a HUGE fan of Greek food and gyros, so if you are, you may be a better judge then me.  This place pegs itself as a coffee shop that also serves food.  I went and I got some pita and hummus as an app and a chicken gyro as my dinner.  It was ok.  Nothing special.  The hummus wasn't bad, but it's hard to screw that stuff up.  I would try it again, only because I like to try a place twice before I declare that I hate it.  Decent enough if you are on the Westbank and want a gyro.  If you have the time, just head over to Byblos.

Whenever I have sushi on the Westbank, I go to Tennou.  I know what I like, and that's it.  So when some friends suggested that we try Sakura, I was skeptical.  First of all, I walked in, and the place smelled like fish.  Now, yes, I know they serve fish, but is a place supposed to reek of it?  We got regular sushi (not the Hibachi) and I wasn't impressed at all.  There wasn't anything overly terrible about it, it just didn't blow me away.  Best described: it was what it was.  I guess I would go back for the Hibachi, since I don't know of any other Hibachi places in the area, but if I just wanted regular sushi, I would head down the street to Tennou.

I went to this restaurant weeks ago, and this review is so overdue, because I wanted it to be perfect.  The entire experience here was definitely memorable, from the time I walked in the door until the time I left.  I arrived with a friend and I was immediately impressed by the fact that there was a valet.  It was a cold night and we definitely didn't feel like doing the "park and walk", so valet was perfect.  We walked in and sat at the bar as we waited for our table to be ready.  There was a piano player/singer in the bar area and we had a good time sitting and listening to him sing classic Christmas songs.  The music could also be heard throughout our meal.  For an appetizer we decided to have the gumbo, which was a special that night and for my meal I had the pan fried drum which was amazing.  I was tempted to try a steak, since they are dry aged in house.  I guess now I just have an excuse to one day go back and try one.  While I was here I got to try Bananas Foster for the first time and it was amazing.  They make it right in front of you, which turns out to be an amazing show.  Everyone here is so professional and nice and helpful.  At one point, I wanted to go to the restroom to freshen up and the waiter actually let me take his arm and led me there.  The wait staff was extremely attentive and knowledgeable and really went out of their way to make sure that we had a memorable experience.  I would definitely go back to Delmonico and I would absolutely bring someone here who is visiting from out of town.  It's definitely the "old, classic" New Orleans that people want to experience whether they are just visiting or they have lived here their entire lives.

This is my favorite beauty supply store and I have been going here for years.  They sell the best of the best at low prices.  I was able to find my now "signature" red nail polish here, "Ruby Pumps" by China Glaze.  They also carry an excellent array of liquid eyeliners in various colors including black and even dark blue.  This is also the only place that I will buy bobby pins.  I have really thick hair, so the cheapo "Goody" brand can't stay in place.  They have heavy duty pins that stay put in my hair all day and night.  Their selection of hair care products is out of this world and it is where I discovered what I call my "magic wand", my Helen of Troy hot air brush, that gives my hair a pretty wave, without having to roll it.  Join the Sally Club for discounts and specials!

Wonderful flower shop with a wonderful owner. Pamela went out of her way to accommodate our needs over a difficult two weeks. She went in early and made special trips to complete our order and make sure that everything was perfect and delivered on time. Such a sweet woman and such a nice shop.

WOW. For such a small shop, this place sure does pack a lot into it.  I don't think I had ever even heard of this shop before I spotted it on Magazine St. the other day. They have so many cool things. Miss Claudia's carries a lot of vintage things from suits to gloves to costumes. Not only that but they have all kinds of different hats and wigs and shoes. I seriously wish that I hadn't been in a rush on the day I stopped in, because I really can see myself spending an hour or two here just going through everything that they have.  They have a perfect selection of sparkly things for Mardi Gras and I will definitely be going here the next time that I need stockings for a specific outfit or costume. Miss Claudia's had a ton of them!  I will definitely be back and I will be ready to spend more of my time here.

I'm not sure how long this place has been open, I think just a few months, because I am only just now hearing about it!  So, I heard of this restaurant only because I got some coupons in the mail, one of which was for $7 for a large one topping pizza. An excuse to not eat Papa John's or some other chain pizza (because that's all the Westbank has except for Mo's)? Count me in!  I called in and pre-ordered and went in to pick up my pie. The store itself is very no frills. There are a few booths and tables, if you want to dine in, but you can tell that take out is the name of the game around here. I was immediately impressed that my large pizza was HUGE and they weren't trying to pass off a medium pizza as a large.  Once I got it home and dug in, I was pretty impressed. The pizza had a lot of flavor and the cheese and pepperoni was more than generous. DEFINITELY a better alternative to bad chain pizza. If you are comparing it to other Westbank pizza, it isn't as good as Mo's, but I liked it. They have other things on their menu such as pasta dishes and chicken wings and salad, but I am probably going to just stick with the pizza when I return.

I barely even know where to begin with Fausto's. There was so much going on and everything was so delicious, it's hard to put it into words.  We were in a big group, so we ordered a few appetizers for the table. We decided on the fried eggplant and the calamari. The eggplant was lightly fried and cut into "sticks". There was marinara sauce for dipping and it was beyond good. The calamari was out of this world. I'm pretty picky when it comes to calamari, because some places overcook it or serve you pieces that are way too chewy. This calamari was just perfect with a nice flaky crust that just melted in my mouth.  For my entree I got the Fettuccine Carciofo. This was a pile of delicious fettuccine mixed with olives, artichoke hearts, and large shrimp in a tasty olive oil based sauce. The sauce was garlicky and perfect and was dripping off of every bite. The shrimp were fat and juicy and cooked perfectly and the serving was so large that I took home probably half of it. This dish was so full of flavor that it made the entire meal an experience.   I was wishing that I had room for desert, but it wasn't meant to be on this particular day. Our waitress was Mindy and she was a total pro in getting everyone's orders in a timely manner. She was really sweet and patient with our large group and she made sure that our water and teas stayed full and that everyone was happy. She was a gem and made our experience perfect.  I will absolutely be returning to Fausto's for delicious food and an all star experience.

I recently was able to attend the Saints vs. Falcons game at the new Mercedes Benz Superdome.  I can't remember the last time I had been in the dome, but I had such an amazing time.  The dome has been beautifully redone and it's just a great venue.  They have everything here that a sports fan could want, as far as food an drinks go.  The people who work here are professional and helpful and go out of there way to make sure you have a good experience here.  If you have the opportunity to see a Saints game here, don't skip it.  It will be one of the best times you will ever have.

I really like this Mojo. I'm happy to see Freret St. expanding a little more all the time.  The atmosphere in here is cozy and the coffee is good. It's pretty much exactly like the Mojo on Magazine St. It was a little crowded on the day that I went, but I suppose that's probably because it's new. I just got an iced coffee to go, so I didn't stay long, but I can see how this could me a neat little place to study or do a little work.

I'm giving this Walgreens 5 stars because they actually saved me some money and they didn't have to.  I was in the area, so I stopped in because I had to pick up some nail polish and Walgreens is the only one that carries it. I got the name brand nail polish and the Walgreens brand clear coat. When I went to pay,  the beauty counter lady told me that the name brand nail polish was 2 for1. So, I was able to get the name brand clear polish instead of the Walgreens brand. Yeah, not a huge deal, but she didn't have to point it out to me.  Tip: don't park in the parking lot overnight. You will probably be towed.

I have to say, that I have been here twice, and I am already a fan of Publiq house.  Located on Freret St., Publiq house is a brand new bar/music venue. When you first walk in, you are greeted by a long bar with a lot of drink selections. They have a few beers on tap and they also have a huge selection of bottles beers. They have a menu you can look at and decide what you want. They also have a fancy cocktail menu.  All of the drinks are served very uniquely in different types of jars. It sounds odd, but it's actually really cool.  Throughout the entire place there are tables that seat about 5-6 people each. There is also a huge stage for music performances. I would imagine that the tables are moved aside if there is a performance, but I have yet to see a band here.  I think that my favorite thing was an old army Jeep that was going to be used during the Korean war and that now contains the bar's sound system.  I will definitely be back here, hopefully sooner rather than later. The entire place has a cool vibe and I can see this place really taking off over the next few months.

Don't ask me what any of the food looked like. I couldn't see anything. I've never before dined in complete darkness/by cell phone glow, but here I am and you're gonna pay $30+ to make it happen.  I had never been to the Theaters at Canal Place (said in a proper snooty tone), so my boyfriend got us tickets to see Beauty and the Beast. I thought it was neat that there is assigned seating and I was glad that we got a pretty good seat. Sadly, due to traffic, we sat down right when the movie started, so it was a bit hard seeing the menu. We decided to get the prixe fixe menu for $30. For our starter we got the spinach-artichoke dip. It was pretty good, but we both agreed that it would have been a bit better if it had been warm. For our entree we got the margherita pizza and the sliders. The pizza was okay- it had big pieces of tomato on it and I liked it, but if tomatoes aren't your thing, avoid it. The sliders were great! I think there was bacon on there- I had to go by taste for all of this stuff. I seriously couldn't see anything, but I think I tasted bacon.  The one thing that bugged me is: I know that it's a laid back atmosphere, but can you please hustle if you're walking past the screen? At one point a server stopped right in front of me to fiddle with her iPad order thing and completely blocked my view of Belle and the Beast. I'll admit, I am really easily distracted, but that was annoying.  All in all, I liked my experience here, but I wouldn't see movies here exclusively. For Beauty and the Beast it was perfect because I knew the plot of the movie, so if I got distracted by a server coming or going, it wasn't the end of the world. The sound and picture were great and the seats were really comfortable, so no complaints there. It's a nice novelty, I'm glad I got the experience and it's nice that New Orleans has a place like this.

I was in the mood for quick Chinese food and Wok to Go hit the spot.  I'm not overly picky when it comes to Chinese food: I really never expect it to be really great, all I expect is for it to taste somewhat like what I'm expecting. Wok to Go fit the bill. I stopped in and I got pork fried rice, an order of spring rolls and an order of dumplings. The pork fried rice was great with a lot of flavor and nice pieces of pork. The spring rolls were pretty good as well. They were veggie spring rolls and I enjoyed them. The dumplings were a deal for as many as I got for the price, but sadly they had a "plastic" after taste. I know that this stuff comes from a bag and isn't hand made, but two dumplings in and I was done.  I would probably go back and just get the fried rice- it was cooked to order and delicious.

What can I say about a place that hasn't been said in 353 reviews before this one?  Commander's is the best of the best.  It's where you want to go when you have a little extra money to spend and you want to not just have dinner, but have an EXPERIENCE.  Here the gourmet food is prepared by Chef's who were trained in their craft.  The waitstaff does this as a career, and isn't just a bunch of 20-somethings working their way through college.  This is a place where memories are made, laughs are had, and friends come together.  Engagements happen here.  Birthdays, graduations and promotions are celebrated here.  You are treated as if you are royalty, because from the time you walk into the door to the time you leave, that's exactly what you are, at this restaurant.  Sure, the place would be considered pricey by most standards but  you aren't just paying for the food.  You are paying for the privilege of dining here.

Yay!  I finally got to try Hoshun.  It's appropriate that this is my 200th review, because I love sushi so much and have been wanting to try this place forever.  So, last night, the sushi craving hit, and my friend suggested we go to Hoshun, since they are open a little later, and sometimes you don't always want a burger.  I loved that the Miso soup comes with those little crunchy things with it.  I know there must be a technical term for them (wonton?), but to me they are "crunchy things".  It's just a nice little change of pace, from the typical bowl of soup.  We just ordered rolls and we got a crunchy roll, a tuna roll, a philly roll and a special roll, that I can't remember that name of, but it came out in foil that was lit on fire.  Impressive.  I really liked the rolls.  I think it would be pretty hard to mess up a tuna roll, but you never know.  I would love to go back and try the sashimi, since that's my favorite.  I loved the atmosphere of the place.  Like Hana, you can tell they really put thought into the decor and wanted the restuarant  to have a certain feel.  Mission: Accomplished.  I would definitely go back, but I think my late night spot for sushi is still Little Tokyo on Carrolton, just because the prices are a little less expensive.

As promised, I am bumping Second Line up star because they now have working bathrooms and they are pouring into glass!  I stopped by on a Sunday afternoon, just to check the place out again and see if anything had changed since my last visit. Sure enough, they are now pouring their beers into glass and they have added a few more brews since my last visit. I loved the Chocolate Spice Stout that had just enough "kick" to it, without being too overwhelming. I also tried the Trans-Siberian Coconut which definitely had that coconut flavor. It almost reminded me of a "Mounds" bar.  There was a decent crowd for a Sunday and the bartenders were nice and helpful. I'm excited to come back and try more of their beer. I heard they are going to start bottling and canning after Mardi Gras, so that'll be a cool expansion for the company. I'll be eagerly awaiting what the future holds for this brewery.

Let me start by saying that I didn't do Fiorella's, probably the way it's supposed to be done.  In other words, I didn't get the fried chicken, or a main entree.  With that said, I ordered the chicken caesar salad and a side order of baked macaroni (mac and cheese).  It was good, not great.  The salad was huge, and was definitely big enough for a meal.  The lettuce was kind of mushy, but the chicken was tender and juicy.  The mac and cheese was ok.  It wasn't overly creamy or anything.  It was more mac and cheese with just a hint of cheese.  It wasn't terrible, but it wasn't the best, either.  The place is known for their famous fried chicken, so I would probably go back and give that a try.  The atmosphere was really nice, with kind of a "diner" feel.  The waitress couldn't have been sweeter, and was even nice enough to recommend some music acts that we should check out.

I'm going to start by saying that this is NOT the same as Buffalo Exchange.  While Buffalo Exchange has some high end stuff, Plato's closet is geared more towards teenagers and girls in their early 20's (20-22 or so).    A LOT of tshirts, short shorts and baby doll dresses.  I went in hoping to find a cheap pair of jeans just to hang around in for the summer.  If you were wondering what ever happened to low rise jeans, it turns out that every pair that was ever made, worn, and tossed aside, ended up here.    It's a good place if you have a teenager and want to pick up some tshirts or cute dresses.  If you have a more sophisticated taste, stick to Buffalo Exchange.

I love Sucre and I have been going since it opened.  When I go, I usually get the cookies and cream gelato, but the last time I went, I was talked into getting one of their small chocolate cake "treats" and it was amazing!  The small cakes tend to be a little on the expensive side, but it's good for a special occasion or a treat.

I hadn't been to Trolley Stop since before Katrina, when I decided to stop in here for a bite to eat.  The atmosphere is very "old".  It's not bad, but you can tell that this place was decorated in the 70's and hasn't been touched since.  The place gets really packed, so if there is a seat at the bar, take it.  My friend and I sat at the bar because there were about 3 groups of people waiting for tables, when we arrived.  The only thing that I had ever previously gotten here was breakfast, so I was eager to try something else.  I got a club sandwich that came with a side of fries.  I was pretty impressed.  You would think that it would be hard to mess up a simple club, but trust me when I say, I am disappointed a lot in the way some of these places make their clubs.  Anyway, this one was fantastic, even though they may have been a little heavy handed with the mayo.  For $8, you really can't beat it.  Trolley Stop is open late (maybe 24 hours, but I'd have to check), so it's the perfect place to stop if you are looking for a late dinner.

I am no fan of parking anywhere downtown. With that being said, this parking lot isn't too bad. You pay at a machine but be warned, the lot is really small. I was lucky to get a parking spot in the middle of the day when some friends and I decided to do some shopping. I managed to make it in and out the lot without my car sustaining any mystery dings, dents or scratches, so I consider the whole parking event a victory.

Tableau is a tough review for me for a few reasons.  First of all, I really like the decor here. They really did a great job with the place. When we arrived, we were lead upstairs to a fairly large room with other diners. Although the room was a good size, almost every table was filled with people, so when we were seated, it made conversation somewhat difficult. I feel if they removed one of the tables and spread things out a little bit, it would be a little better.  We got the wine list, decided on a wine and ordered. It seemed like the wine took a while, but it was a Saturday night, so I won't be too critical of that part.  For our appetizer we decided on the bacon wrapped oysters. They were delicious. The oysters were semi-raw and wrapped in cooked bacon. The bacon added a lot of flavor to the oysters themselves making it the perfect appetizer.  I decided on a soup for my second course, which was French Onion. It came in a small bowl with a THICK layer of cheese and bread on top of it. It was amazing and perfect. I probably could have eaten three bowls and called it a meal.  For my entree' I decided on the red fish in some kind of butter sauce. While it was good, it wasn't amazing and it didn't blow me away. At places like this, I usually order a steak because you usually can't go wrong with a steak, and I found myself wishing I had made that decision here. It was a major disappointment.  Finally, for dessert, we ordered bread pudding. It was pretty typical bread pudding and nothing overly special.  The staff was super nice and attentive and although the service was somewhat slow, the staff was really good about checking on us and making sure that all of our needs were met.   I know that people say that you should wait a while before trying a new place. Under normal circumstances, I would probably give my experience here three stars. Because we dined here within two weeks of their opening, I decided to bump them up to four stars because they are still working out the kinks. I would go back, but I think I would wait until they are a little more settled into their routine.

This Pho Bang is good. Really good. As much as I liked this one, I really miss the one on Manhattan, but I digress.  I went in and got my usual beef brisket and rare flank Pho. It was really good and had a lot of flavor. Honestly, if you read my review for the other Pho Bang, it was pretty much exactly like that. Oh! And I also really love their pork Spring rolls!  For whatever reason, this Pho Bang was really packed when I went in and it took a little while for me to be seated. That's not a huge deal, as I wasn't in any kind of major rush. I am hoping that the Pho Bang on Manhattan reopens soon (their sign says that they are TEMPORARILY closed),  but in the meantime this one will have to do.

I attended a wedding here and the experience was top notch from beginning to end. This is a lovely mansion on St. Charles Avenue and I just love the idea of being able to hear the rumbling of the streetcar during any event you have here. I think that it adds a nice New Orleans touch to the festivities.  The wedding and reception were both in the Elms Garden, which was beautifully decorated. The wedding itself was lovely with the bride and groom exchanging vows under a gazebo. Chairs were arranged nicely, so that the guests didn't feel piled on top of each other and after  the ceremony ended, the bar was open and the garden was transformed into a lovely reception area. As if by magic, the chairs were whisked away and replaced by multiple tables. I was impressed that the food was setup and ready to go immediately after the ceremony, and there was no wait.  Speaking of the food, it was all amazing. We enjoyed turkey and stuffing with gravy, assorted cheeses, grape leaves, brussel sprouts, salmon and passed food such as crab, frogs legs, meat pies, pâté, escargot, sausage and much more. The food seemed to never stop and it was all excellent. I also liked that when the cake was cut, they passed around cake to all the guests so that we didn't have to worry about going and looking for it. They also had other desserts such as cheesecake and chocolate covered strawberries. Yum!  I loved the lighting on the dance floor area and there was a lot of space so that people could move around and have a good time. The staff was fantastic at clearing plates and glasses as soon as we were finished and keeping everything neat.  I had a fantastic time at the wedding and Elms Mansion was a wonderful venue for it, especially on a mild Autumn night.

While I'm sure that Glue would appeal to some people, it's just not one of the "nicer" vintage stores in the city.  A lot of the stuff in this store I wouldn't even consider vintage.  I mean, sure, I like a ratty looking AC/DC shirt as much as the next gal, but I doubt that I would rush out to buy one for 30 bucks and call it vintage.  The place is packed with what I guess some people would call "hipster" clothes (I HATE that term, btw.) but if you are looking for something a little fancier, you would probably be better off going next door to On the Other Hand.

I recently shot with a photographer from Texas who wanted to capture the "essence" of New Orleans, so of course he wanted to shoot at Cafe Du Monde.  Cafe Du Monde is more than cafe au lait and those beignets we all love so much, it's a New Orleans "must".  It's one of the first things people want to go when they are visiting the city and rightfully so.    When I go, I personally like to sit inside, but I know that most people prefer the experience of the patio.  The patio gets extremely packed, especially at night when tourists are walking around, but it is still worh the experience.  I think that one of my favorites is their frozen Cafe Au Lait.  I love it so much, I'll even go to the Cafe Du Monde located at the mall just to get my hands on it.  It's soo good.

While wandering around the area, we happened to stumble upon this quaint little bar.  It wasn't too late, but we were the only people in the place. That was fine by me- there were some extra credits on the jukebox so I requested a few songs and we sat and had a few drinks. The feel of the place is divey and laid back and the bartender was super nice and friendly. I'm normally not a fan of places with internet jukeboxes, but it worked well here, maybe because it was only my songs playing. Ha.  We weren't here long, but it was an enjoyable evening and I would come back for another visit.

Yay! I got to try another food truck.  I was STARVING when I ran into this truck outside of Rendezvous on Magazine. I'm always excited to try new things, so I walked up and looked over the menu. I decided to get the lechon (braised pork) in a white corn tortilla with chipotle crema and avocado. It didn't take long before my food was ready, even though there were a good number of people there.  I would say the food here is good if you have nothing to compare it to. I compared it to taceaux loceaux, which is my usual "go to" food truck for Mexican food. The pork had a lot of flavor, but the meal itself was missing something. I did enjoy it, and I would go back, but taceaux loceaux is still my first choice.

I was first introduced to this Blaze location through a Yelp gathering and David and I recently returned for dinner.  I'm sure you know how Blaze works, so I won't bore you with the details, but it's basically a "build your own" pizza place. We were here on a Friday evening and while it wasn't too crazy, service was a bit slow because the workers were taking dine-in orders as well as trying to make pizzas that were ordered over the phone and via their app. The process took a little longer than usual, but that's okay. Once the lady took my order I was moved through the line quickly, the pizza was cooked fast and I was enjoying my pie in no time.  This is a great spot if you're in the mood for a quick pizza fix that's a bit on the healthier side (thin crust and you can put whatever you want on it). This isn't the place to come if you dislike kids- there are a lot of them running around at any given time. It's also, understandably, a big college hangout so get your food to go if you don't want to be surrounded by folks under 20.

Yay! I made it here and they were open and not sold out!  Ok, well I'm not a HUGE barbecue person. I like the stuff, but it's not really something that I ever seek out. After hearing that NOLA Smokehouse is now officially the best barbecue in the city, I knew that I had to see for myself.  First of all, finding this place is a trick.
