From what I could see, it had no signage, and the only thing indicating that this old store front was serving food was the huge "open" flag in the front. Once I finally tracked this place down, I was eager for my lunch.  Upon entering, I looked over the menu of the day and decided on the pulled pork sandwich. I'm the type of person to likes to ease into a new place and not jump right in. The nice woman took my order and I sat and waited. The place is pretty small, so I can imagine that during peak hours it can get pretty nuts.  My sandwich came, and first of all, it was huge. It was just packed with so much pulled pork. One thing I really liked was that it didn't come with sauce on it. They let you add your own, so that you can pick your flavor- spicy or sweet, and add as much or as little as you want. I found that my best plan of action was adding the sauce to one side at a time, so that the bread didn't get soggy.  The pork was tender and delicious. I honestly took a few bites of the sandwich without any sauce on it, and I could have eaten it just like that. The different sauces did a good job of bringing out the flavor of the meat and enhanced the flavor of the pork without masking it.  The super nice staff and the amazing food guarantees that I will most definitely return. One thing I noticed when I was here: I was the only girl! Almost every spot in the place was filled with all guys. Girls, head over here and get you some barbecue! Show the guys that we like smoked meat, too!

I stopped in here for breakfast, eager to see what this lovely restaurant had to offer. I was immediately excited to see that ordering is really easy. The menu is on the wall and you just walk up and tell them what you would like. When I went, I was immediately greeted with a welcoming smile and I instantly felt right at home. I decided on the #1 breakfast which is eggs cooked to order, bacon or sausage, hash browns or grits and a biscuit or toast. I got my eggs over easy with bacon, hash browns and toast. I really liked that the coffee is readily available on the main floor, so that you can get it yourself and refill at will. After I ordered, I sat at one of the nice tables and waited for my meal. The restaurant is decorated with kitschy items from times gone by and the cloth table cloths add a nice "old school" feel to the entire experience.  My food came quickly via a nice waitress who made sure that I had everything that I needed. Now, I'm one of those people who can tell whether or not I will like a place by what kind of breakfast they serve and LeBlanc's did not disappoint. First of all, the servings here are huge! My eggs were cooked to perfection and the bacon was crispy and plentiful. My favorite was probably the hash browns. They were Brabant style (diced) and there were so much of them that I could barely finish it all! Just a note: the toast is on the lighter side, so if you like your toast a little more on the "toasty", you might want to tell them so when you order.  A place like LeBlanc's is a wonderful addition to Gretna. With good food and a friendly staff, they are sure to go far. I'm excited to stop in again for breakfast or try one of their delicious lunch offerings.

Ok, so don't get nervous. No, I am not getting married. I am however going to be playing bride in an upcoming photo shoot and every bride (real or otherwise) needs the perfect dress. I met the photographer here and we immediately started going through the huge selection of dresses that they have. We really didn't know what we were doing. We knew that we wanted something with a vintage feel and that was about it.  After pulling 3 or 4 dresses, we asked a consultant for some help. We described what we wanted and she immediately pulled a dress that she thought would be perfect. I tried on the first dress we had chosen and it wasn't for me at all. Then I tried on the dress the consultant had suggested. Well, let's just say she knew what she was doing. I tried on the other dresses that we had pulled, but we both knew that I had found "the one". Just like that! Granted, this was just for a photo shoot and I probably would have taken more time if it was for a real wedding, but the dress is amazing and exactly what we had in mind.  I would suggest any bride add this place to their list of dress shops (every bride has more than one!). You may surprise yourself and find what you are looking for here.

One of the best lunch deals on the Westbank? I think so!  Mimi's has been making headlines lately for their Viet-Cajun crawfish and, while I did see some platters being served up while I was here, that wasn't the reason for my visit. After seeing Tony H's delicious banh mi photos, I knew I had to head over to this place ASAP.  The restaurant is super casual- you order at the counter and they bring you your food when you're ready. They have a variety of Vietnamese goodies, including a variety of tea, boiled seafood and sandwiches, but the star of the show (in my opinion) is the banh mi. I got B2, which is the BBQ pork banh mi and a side of fries. After tax and before tip, my total was about $8.50.  I had seen photos of the banh mi here, but looks can often be deceiving. I was pleasantly surprised when a good size sandwich PACKED with pork and a generous side of fries was placed in front of me. The sandwich was perfect- crispy bread and flavorful tasty pork. It was everything I expect from a good banh mi. The fries were good too- nice and crispy.  To top it all off, the staff here is beyond friendly. They checked on me multiple times to make sure that I was enjoying everything and that I had everything I needed. The food was the perfect amount for lunch and, in my opinion, it's hard to beat the price.

As good as other places in the city that serve gelato are, there is no topping Brocato's.  Brocato's is a classic Italian dessert place.  They serve gelato, Italian cookies, Cannolis, and more.  You can go in after a nice dinner and get a sweet treat with some coffee on the side.  I have never been in this place where it hasn't had a nice crowd.  This is a New Orleans institution and the people who go here are serious about it.  Really.  I've met people who have gone to this place their entire lives and are now bringing their grandchildren.  A definite New Orleans "don't miss".

This place is brutal with a capital "B".  Err...Brutal!  I went here a while back with the friend of a friend who was visiting town and wanted to check it out.  First of all, it's on Bourbon St., so that right there is gonna tell you that it's geared towards tourists, which is fine.  That's not my complaint.  My complaint isn't even the fact that it is always packed no matter what time you go.  No, my main complaint is if you actually want to sing here, you gotta be ready for a wait.   Now, that makes sense, because of the crowd.  The only problem with waiting is the fact that you have to listen to drunk tourists sing 80's hair band songs at the top of their lungs, and that's almost too much to handle.  To top it all off, drinks are out of this world expensive.  Beer is about 6 bucks without the tip.  I know it's the quarter and I know it's Bourbon, but come on.  When will one of these places on Bourbon realize, "Hey, let's charge a smidge less for our drinks and then we will be known as the 'cool' bar on Bourbon!"?  Just askin'...

Ugh.  What it has: A pool table that is used more for dancing on than actual pool. An upstairs that you probably didn't know about. A patio that you probably didn't know about (other than the name of the place). A hiding place under the stairs. Cheese fries that taste better after a long night. College kids  What it doesn't have: A clean bathroom A real reason for anyone over 25 to rightfully go here A sense of decor "Mr/Mrs Right" A proper dance floor  I would like to state, that in the last 5 years I have never gone here on my own volition. I have always been BROUGHT here.

I've decided to update this review because my view of the Old Point has changed considerably.  I was wrong when I said that unless you live in the area there is no reason to go here. There are a lot of reasons to go here, not the least of which is seeing a variety of different bands and enjoying the New Orleans atmosphere at a neighborhood bar just outside of New Orleans proper.  The staff is always friendly and the crowd is a bit older and respectful. My only complaint is the cigarette smoke. I don't know if it's a ventilation issue or what, but even if just one person is smoking in there, the entire place fills with smoke. I would love it if they went smoke free or installed some better smoke eaters.

It was post-Thanksgiving and I was tired of leftovers, so I wanted a fried seafood platter.I had passed this place a few times, and all of the reviews were great, so I called ahead and stopped in.  They have a little bit of everything here- shrimp, oysters, different types of fried fish, but I decided on the oyster platter just because I like to try them out everywhere I can. The man working (I think he was the owner) was really friendly and nice when I came to pick up the food.  As for the platter itself: the oysters were pretty small, but there were nicely fried and tasty. I subbed my fries for onion rings and I think that I was upcharged for that. I'm not positive, but the small oyster platter was $10 and my final total was over $13. The breakdown on the receipt had "tax" listed twice so I think one charge was the upcharge for the sub. Not a huge deal, I just wish they would have mentioned that subbing is extra. I know for next time.  The onion rings were okay, but I'm afraid a few of them were over cooked and inedible. Also, the batter was a bit sweet and I really didn't like that. I think next time I will probably just keep it simple an get the catfish and fries. This is a great place if you want fried seafood fast and I'll be back.

Hmmm... why is Hubig's marked as closed? Down but not out, people! Hubig's is coming back!  If you grew up in New Orleans then you grew up on Hubig's. Those yummy little fried iced pies that you know are terrible for you but you didn't care because they were AMAZING.  When I was a kid, I remember enjoying mine at Kmart of all places. Trust me, I have no idea why I had them I Kmart. Maybe they were by the register? I don't know. Anyway, I think that my favorites are apple and lemon.  I know that non-locals will insist that Hubig's aren't as great as we make them out to be, but Adam Richman (host of Man vs. Food on Travel Channel) RAVED about them when he was down here, so there's that.

I want to start by saying that the location for The Blue Crab is golden. It's right on the lake and there is a gorgeous view of all of the boats.  So, we stopped in here for lunch on a Friday. My dad had heard about this place and wanted to try it. Looking over the menu, it was your typical seafood faire. I was pretty hungry, so I decided to start with the corn and crab bisque and for my entree I got the stuffed crabs (2 to an order) which came with some bread and fries.  The corn and crab bisque was really good. I added a little hot sauce to it and it was pretty perfect. The stuffed crabs were also really good (served in shell) after I added a little "kick" to them. I liked the fries, but I should mention that they were a bit burnt. Now, I like my fries super crispy, but I know that a lot of people don't, so this might have been cause for complaint for some. One of my main issues was the bread. It was super dry, so I asked for some butter. The waitress brought some back from the kitchen that was rock hard and impossible to spread. My suggestion would be to have a stick or two out, in case someone asks for some. Or better yet, have a few packets of butter on the table. It makes sense that if you are serving bread, someone might want to butter it.  My dad also had the suggestion that water be on the table, since there was none and we only had the drinks that we ordered. Other than all of that, it was a good experience. I can imagine that this place does fantastic business when the weather isn't too hot or cold. There is even outside seating!   I want to go back and try their fried soft shell crab, since I understand that it comes into season in mid March.

As far as Taco Bells go, this one is okay.  A few things you measure a fast food place on: speed of getting customers through, order "correctness" and quality of food. We stopped in here at around 10 on a Saturday, and of course there was a line. Despite this, the staff did get us through pretty quickly. It didn't feel like there were any major delays that could have been handled on their end. Once we ordered, the food order was right and it was pretty good. I'm glad we didn't have to deal with any of the issues that past reviewers had to deal with.   This isn't my "go to" Taco Bell, but it's just as good as any of the other ones I've been to.

I went here this past weekend, and I was going to sit on this review until they made some improvements, but I decided to just review now and re-review when improvements are made, so that you know what you are getting when you stop in here.  I visited on Saturday night and there was a good crowd on an unseasonably cool evening. The setup here is similar to other breweries in that it's mostly outdoors with a small indoor area where beers are poured. There is a nice selection of tables and chairs and tvs were showing the LSU game and there was a food truck parked out front.  Second Line has a good selection of their own beers on tap. I'm not sure if they plan on offering guest brews in the future, but their selection seemed to keep the crowd happy. The beers were nothing overly spectacular, but I did enjoy the IPA..  A few complaints: they served their beer in plastic cups. I'm not trying to sound like a beer snob, but if I'm going to pay for craft beer, I want to drink it out of glass. They had glasses on display in their display case, so I had no idea why they didn't choose to use them. Maybe they were afraid of people walking off with them or they save the glass for a smaller crowd? I don't know. It just immediately put me off. The second issue is: at the moment the only bathrooms they have are port o potties. Again- I'm not trying to sound uppity, but unless I'm at a parade, this is a "no go" for me. I think someone mentioned they are going to have bathrooms and they are still being constructed, but still.  Like I said, the place just opened and I know they are still working out the "kinks". I will definitely return and I'll be happy to re-review and rate them higher, if things are different.

I was really impressed with Los Panchos. I eat at my fair share of Mexican restaurants and Los Panchos was up there with some of the best.  I ordered a chicken burrito that came topped with cheese sauce. It was amazing and so good. It was really big and I took my leftovers home and got a second meal out of it. Also, it's worth noting that the free chips and salsa are also really good. The salsa here has flavor and a little bit of spice, which makes it delicious. I have found that other places have salsa that is really bland. I guess they are afraid to give you the spicy stuff, because not everyone likes it, but Los Panchos didn't hold back. They also have yummy Mexican coke with real sugar. It can't be beat!  I will definitely go back! Their food is good, the prices are reasonable and they have a ton of different dishes to try.

I love a really cute shop with well priced jewelry.  I just happened to find this place while I was out and about and it's wonderful! They have earrings, necklaces and other pieces of costume jewelry and most are priced around $20. They have a board in the back of items that are 75% off and I was able to get two pairs of cute earrings for $10 total! They also have other "girly" type accessories, that you or the lady in your life are sure to love.  This is a great place to pick up a stocking-stuffer for the holidays or treat yourself to a little something special.

I had been patiently waiting for this Lush location to open when I came across Emily M.'s review! I am so excited that there is a Lush uptown!  This place is on point in every way possible. The good smells hit you as soon as you walk in the door and all of the bath goodies are out on display so that you can pick them up and smell them. The employees here are extremely attentive and eager to help. I stopped in on a weekday afternoon, and since I was the only customer in the store, all eyes were on me.  The first employee told me all about their newest bath bombs and bubble bars and explained what was in some of them as I sniffed around. I headed over to the soap and exfoliation section and an employee was super nice about demonstrating an exfoliant, toner and moisturizer, that was made with all natural ingredients, including violet buds, on my hand . I wasn't really in the market for that type of stuff on this particular day, but I LOVED the products she demonstrated and I will be back to get some of it soon. Along with bath and shower goodies, Lush sells all kinds of different makeup that is meant to be gentle on your skin and that is basically a dream come true.  I decided to get a few of the smaller bath bombs, but I know that I will definitely be back for much more soon. The store itself is HUGE and has everything that you could ever want as far as beauty goes- they even have shampoo and conditioner, if you are looking for something gentle to put on your hair.  This is a fantastic addition to the area and I really look forward to shopping here again and getting some bath treats for some friends of mine. Note: avoid the temptation of just grabbing one of the glittery bubble bars. My hand was covered in gold glitter for the rest of the afternoon, even after a wash!

Really nice PJ's, It almost feels like it belongs Uptown. It's really big with sofas and a few tables for sitting. I did however, find it a bit dark, There wasn't a lot of light coming in and the lights were kind of dim. That's awesome if you are looking for place with mood lighting, but if you are trying to get some work done it might be a bit difficult,  The coffee was typical PJ's coffee. I kind of wish this PJ's was closer to me because I really dig how big it is, even if it is a little dim in here.

We decided to get a drink here while we waited for our reservation at a place across the street.  This is a neat little bar that mainly attracts foot traffic off the street- I don't know if anyone really sets out to spend an evening here. I had a tap beer and my friend had a vodka and cranberry. My beer was good, but my friend's vodka and cran was pretty weak. The main focus here is "drunk food"- they are open late and serve pizza, burgers and the like, and I am sure that's how they get most of their business. The bar was pretty dead at 7 on a Saturday, but we enjoyed hanging out here and chatting while other patrons started their evening.

This seems to be one of those New Orleans staples that I had always wanted to try, but never had the opportunity.  A friend and I stopped in here one night for a bite to eat.  I had never been, but had always wondered about the place.  First of all, I was really impressed by the diverse menu.  Not only do they serve burgers and salad, but they serve breakfast food AND one of my faves, spinach artichoke dip!  We got an order of dip and I had two eggs over easy with bacon and hash browns (which were pretty much just sliced up potatoes).  The food was really good and the eggs were perfectly cooked.  The dip wasn't the best I had ever had, but it did the job and it was served with chips.  I would definitely go back here.  I am a huge fan of any place that serves breakfast food all day (IHOP, Waffle House), so it's always nice to know where to go, if I'm ever in the mood for that kind of thing.

This is a pretty good spot, if you are in the mood for some quick Mexican-ish food.  I came here for lunch at around 1 and it was pretty empty. After looking over the menu, I decided to get the burrito lunch special with pork. This is a pretty basic burrito packed with pork, rice, beans and cheese and a side of "fixins"- sour cream, guacamole, lettuce and tomato. The burrito was pretty good, but nothing earth shattering. It was somewhat bland, so I added some of the salsa from the complimentary chips and salsa and that added a little kick to it.  It's had to really judge a place on a simple lunch, so I will return and get a full dinner and re-review, if appropriate.

I was pretty disappointed in this stop on the Westbank snowball tour.  First of all, like Jess mentioned, they are really slow. You order at one window and they give you your snowball at another window. We only had two people ahead of us and there was still a bit of a wait to get our snowballs.  I got the pink bubblegum. There wasn't a lot of "juice" in it at all and I think you can even tell in my picture that the ice wasn't really soaked. The flavor was weird and tasted like medicine with a weird aftertaste. David tasted mine and he said the same thing. They do have a wide selection of hamburgers and poboys, if you aren't in the mood for a snowball, but you want to munch on something. I probably won't be back.

I used to come to this Walgreens fairly regularly back when I had friends who lived near it. I recently visited this Walgreens for the first time in a long time.  This is a pretty typical Walgreens- they carry all of the usual Walgreens stuff. The staff at this location was pretty friendly when I dropped in and helped me find what I was looking for. I happened to be looking for a certain kind of vitamin for joint pain (not for me, btw) and the pharmacist pointed me in the right direction right away. Also, on the day I was here, they were having a pretty nice little sale on some makeup products, so I stocked up.  The store and the pharmacy here are both open 24/7, so make note of that if you are in need in the late night/early morning hours.

Such a cute shop! This place is a candy lovers dream and offers all types of yummy candy gifts such as giant Reese's cups, giant Hershey bars, extra long Twizzlers, giant gummy bears and pocky along with tons more.  The shop is small and they do have some candy that you can pile into bags and buy, but the main attraction here is all of the unique candy themed gifts and things like that. Some really cute things that I had to resist purchasing was the plush ketchup and french fries that had smiley faces, a plush ice cream cone and pillows that were made to look like candy. One thing I loved was the assortment of candy scented candles that I will definitely be going back to get.  Since we are in the Halloween season there is a nice assortment of Halloween themed treats, so be sure to stock up if that's your thing.

I had always seen Dr. Bob's art all over New Orleans, but it wasn't until a friend and I did a post lunch pop in, that I knew that he had an actual studio.  If you are looking for New Orleans folk art, Dr. Bob is pretty much the "go to". In this small studio you can find paintings and signs of all types. In fact, until Simon came along, you would see Dr. Bob's art in every restaurant and bar in the area.  You can find art for pretty cheap here (under $50) and he has bigger, more expensive pieces, if you are looking for something like that. He also does custom work, so if there is something that you have in mind, sit down with him and he will be happy to collaborate with you.  Dr. Bob also works Jazz Fest every year and sells his work there, if you don't want to venture to Chartres.

I am so excited!  Owners Lindsay and Scott have been working SO HARD on opening their own brewery and tap room. The day has finally come and I am so excited that I got to be a part of it!  First of all, the brewery is small, but it's gorgeous. There are 12 taps  of all different types of beer that are all reasonably priced and Russell is the fantastic bartender who is serving them to you.  Not only are they going to be serving "visiting" beers, but they are also going to be brewing and serving their own beer, which is beyond exciting. This city doesn't have enough breweries serving up really good craft beer. Courtyard Brewery is helping to solve that problem.   When you are hanging out here, you really feel as if you are among friends. I met a bunch of people that I had never met before and we all got along great because we are all beer lovers.  Courtyard Brewery is a welcome addition to the New Orleans beer scene. I am so excited to experience it and I am so excited to go back!

Hansen's is a New Orleans institution and who doesn't love a snowball on a hot day?  I stopped here on a not-too-hot day and was intimidated by the line out the door, onto the sidewalk and nearly into the street. Luckily, the line moved at a steady pace and before I knew it, I was inside placing my order.  They have the basic flavors here and don't really have anything super exotic. I decided on a bubblegum snowball (one of my faves). I liked that the ice was really finely shaved giving it a velvet like consistency. They were super generous with the syrup and the snowball itself was delicious.  I can't wait to go back to Hansen's.

If you ever travel from New Orleans to Slidell, chances are you're familiar with Fisherman's Castle on the Irish Bayou. When I was a kid I was convinced that real royalty lived here after being banished from their kingdom for reasons unknown.  It was originally built over 30 years ago for the World's Fair and thanks to new ownership, it has undergone a complete renovation which is easy to tell from the outside.  We are talking full renovation- from what I've heard they gutted the entire place and completely restored it.   I have no idea if they hold events here or not, but I do know that it's a private residence so I would discourage anyone from knocking on the door and asking for a tour. According to Facebook, the owners are restoring the grounds and will be opening the space up for photo shoots, so I guess we'll see. I would love to get a look at the inside, if it's at all possible. This is one of the most noted landmarks on the NOLA to Slidell drive, and is worth looking out for as it's something a bit different on the landscape.

So, the name "Woldenberg Park" is kind of misleading. It's not really a park at all. Well, not by typical New Orleans standards.   I like that the French Quarter fest is here and that it's right on the river. It gives you a nice view of the bridge. It's always nice to go here on a nice day and enjoy the sights.

A nice little "blink and you'll miss it" wine shop in the middle of the Bywater.  I am rarely in the Bywater and I passed this place a few times and just assumed it was nothing more than a wine shop. It wasn't until I was brought here on a date that I realized that not only is it a wine shop, you can also sample wine by the glass here as well. Walking in, the place is packed with wines of all types that you can buy by the bottle and take with you or drink on premises. I decided to try a nice glass of $5 red wine. I'm no wine connoisseur, so this was perfect for me. There are seats where you can sit and chat and they have a tapas menu, if you want something to munch on.  I really liked the atmosphere, and while I wouldn't call it the most romantic place in the world, it's a nice spot to sit and sample wine, if that's your thing.

I'm not usually a Starbucks fan at all but, after hoofing it around the Quarter for French Quarter Fest, I decided to stop in here for an iced coffee to get my energy up. It worked like a charm and I went from dozing to having a pep in my step in no time.  The set up of this store is nice enough and they woman who made my coffee for me was good at her job, in the sense that she didn't mess up my order. Other than that, yeah it's a Starbucks.

I was in the mood for Chinese food, but I didn't feel like spending money at my usual "go to" Empress of China, and I wasn't in the mood for anything super fancy anyway. I am normally super hesitant to try "hole in the wall" Chinese places. A lot of times, they cater to mostly take out and delivery orders, so the kitchen may not be as clean as in regular sit down places. I remember coming here once, but they were closed for some reason. When I looked up the reviews and saw that they were mainly good, I decided to give this place a try.  I didn't get anything too crazy. I ordered some spring rolls, fried wontons and some steamed dumplings. It was probably stuff that they got out of a bag, but that's not a big deal. I called and ordered and was told my order would be ready in 5 minutes. I got there in about that time and my food was hot and ready to go. I was pleased that it was also super cheap. This is a pretty large place with lots of tables, in case you are interested in actually eating here (there was a couple eating dinner when I went).  The food was good and what I expected. Not as great as a sit down place but really good for take out. Plenty of food for what you spend. My order cost $9 and could have easily fed two people.  All in all I was pleased and I'll be back.

I have recently become familiar with the JPAS because one of my beloved cats went missing and I have been searching for him here (among other places). Although I have not yet located him, the staff here is extremely helpful and nice. They agreed to let me put up a flyer with his picture and my contact info and one of the women working here even agreed to be on the "lookout" for him.  I'm basically writing this review in order to remind people who are looking to adopt to check the shelters first. At this shelter they have a TON of animals, especially kittens. Some of them are so teeny tiny they look as if they could fit in a pocket. They even have a room where kittens are free to walk around and you can go in and mingle with them, if you are looking to adopt. It was SO HARD for me to not leave there with a kitten. They are sooo cute.  They also have puppies. They had one that looked like maybe a beagle mix and he was so small and shaky, I just wanted to pick him up and take him home. I'll admit it, I'm not exactly a tough sell.  Whether you are searching for a lost pet, or you are hoping to add to your family, the JPAS is a good place to start. There are always a lot of animals who are looking for a home and would love to be a companion for years to come.

My experience here was SO disappointing.  I had been waiting for months to go to Kyoto.  I had never been and I had always heard how fabulous it was.  I was pretty excited when I was finally able to make it here for dinner after the St. Patrick's Day parade.  First of all, when we walked in, the first table at which we were seated was located under some stairs.  It was so dark I could barely see my menu and I was with my friend who is 6'5" and he could barely fit.  I would have totally understood if there were no other tables available, but there were, so to be seated under the stairs was not only ridiculous, it was insulting.  In fact, never seat  anyone under there.  EVER.  Remove that table completely.  It's insulting, when you have two dining areas, to ask a paying customer to sit in the "connection" between the two rooms.  When we were reseated in the actual dining room, we ordered some soup, the salmon sashimi, the stella roll and the funky margarita roll, which we had heard were the best special rolls that they had.  The soup was pretty good and it's hard to mess up raw salmon.  The two special rolls, unfortunately, were nothing special.  Sure, they were good, but they didn't seem much bigger than the regular rolls that you would get at any other restaurant.  My friend noted that the rolls were expensive for what you got and the tables were really close together.  The latter I can understand, because the place is small, but when I order a special roll and I pay "special roll" prices, I expect it to be a good size and something, well...special.  I might go back to Kyoto and give it another try, but I think I will stick to my favorite sushi place, Hana, where the special rolls are huge and good and definitely worth the money.

This is a cool place to check out, if you want to get off of the beaten path of Bourbon Street.  There is always a good crowd in here and the staff is really nice.  The bar is decorated with old New Orleans memorabilia and has a kind of "old, gritty" New Orleans feel.  They do serve food, although I've never eaten here and the food looks a little shady and boring.  The bar has a back area, but I'm not experienced enough with the place to vouch for all that.

Although this isn't the best Popeyes in the area, this is the one I go to most often. Their drive thru is always fast and they actually fill the mashed potato and red beans and rice containers up to the top. Also, the staff has always been friendly. So, while it's still fast food and it take A LOT for me to give fast food more than three stars, this is a decent stop for some chicken and sides.

Baker's Dozen donuts seem to be everywhere lately, and that is definitely not a complaint!  These delicious donuts are fluffy, light and delicious and whenever I go to a party or event and see that they are serving Baker's Dozen donuts, I know that I am definitely in for a treat. Yes, their store is located all the way out in Jefferson, but it is definitely worth the trip. Not only are the donuts delicious but the staff is amazingly friendly. Brandi, one of the owners, is super personable and is always open to a chat.  I look forward to another delicious bite of Baker's Dozen.

I don't know.  Maybe I'm a snob when it comes to oysters and seafood in general, but I was left underwhelmed by my experience here.  My friends ordered a dozen oysters; half raw and half char broiled.  I ordered the seafood etouffee.  I tried the oysters, but I immediately noticed that they weren't very big.  The char broiled oysters were good and had a nice buttery flavor.  My etouffee was ok, but not really anything special.  The prices here seem a little bit steep for what seems to be just a casual dining place.  I will say that one of my friends ordered the seafood platter, which came with fried crab, catfish, oysters and fries.  It was huge, looked really good, and can definitely be split between two people.  The service was good and we were seated quickly, with only about a ten minute wait.  Given the choice, I would probably go somewhere else for my oyster needs.  I'd be more inclined to support a small local business, rather than this chain.

This is a really nice bohemian-chic kind of spot.  They have a nice selection of long flowy dresses and coverups, jumpsuits, lounge pants and tops that are probably meant to be worn without a bra. Real free living type of clothes.  The woman working when I came in was really friendly and I did find a few things that I was interested in trying on. I like the style of some of the things here, but I did find some things to be a little pricey. For example: there was a long, blue thin material "kaftan" (as it was labeled) that was over $200. Basically this store is great if you want to live the free beach life and you don't mind spending a few bucks.  I'm giving four stars because the staff was beyond helpful and I do like some of the clothing here. I just wish it was a bit more affordable for the every day boho queen.

I am so confused by the mixed reviews of this place, I really liked it.  When I stopped in on a Tuesday night I was the only one in here and the DNC was on- perfect. I sat at a nice little table in the back and I enjoyed the solitude as I looked over the menu. I started with my usual- noodle salad and got the tuna roll, Philly roll and a rainbow roll. The noodle salad was perfection, as were the rolls. Everything tasted really fresh and tasted the way I expected it to taste, so I was pleased.  I love the atmosphere of this restaurant. The inside feels like a restaurant you would find Uptown and it's actually pretty "fancy" for a Westbank place. The waitress was attentive, probably because I was the only customer, but she was good about getting everything to me in a timely manner.  I liked everything here and I'll be back.

Les Bon Temps is a cool place to check out live shows or just go and hang out with friends.  It's a small place, so if you want access to the pool table, you have to get there early.  Brass bands and other bands put on shows in the back, which is always a lot of fun.    Be aware: the floor in the back is brick and uneven, which makes dancing difficult, especially if you are in heels.

Okay, this is one of those places where I loved the idea but not quite the execution.  I attended a happy hour here with a few friends. While we were there there was a shift change. The first waitress got some people's orders who were there before myself and then it all turned over to another waitress. As nice as the second waitress was, she was just slow. There weren't a lot of people there and it took forever for her to come and get drink orders and then come and get food orders. We were seated outside, so maybe that had something to do with it, but like I said, the place wasn't packed.  I decided to get an order of the appetizer tuna tartine as well as an order of the queso fundido. Appetizers are half off during happy hour, so I was happy to take advantage of that. The tuna tartine was delicious! It was raw tuna mixed with peppers and spices and I loved it. The queso fundido was okay, but it didn't knock my socks off. It went from melty to "stiff" pretty quickly and didn't have a ton of flavor to it. Some places add spices and peppers to theirs, but this just seemed to be melted cheese.  I had one frozen margarita which was delicious! I was planning on having more than one, but after tasting the strength of my first, I decided one was probably enough. I liked the outside seating area, as the weather was fairly nice and we were in a nice shady spot.  I want to go back for dinner to get a better idea of how the service normally is here.

I love this shop! Walking in, you immediately discover that Idea Factory is going to bring you back to simpler times. The times before modern technology when toys were built to last.  Everything here is hand made out of wood, and it's a sight to behold. Tops, puzzles, train whistles, secret boxes and much more are on display and available for purchase for the kid (or big kid) in your life. They have a fantastic selection of unique gifts that are sure to capture the imagination. The staff is very friendly and is more than happy to explain how everything works and you are sure to find something that you'll enjoy. I want to go back and buy one of the slide boxes to keep my rings in, so I'm sure I'll be making a trip back to this delightful spot.

Pretty good, but don't expect anything spectacular.  We popped in here pretty late and I'm pretty sure it's the only late night diner type place in the area. I ordered 2 eggs over easy, grits, toast, and bacon- you know this by now. Well, the eggs were definitely over medium, but that wasn't earth shattering. Two things that put me off were the slice of American cheese on the grits and the "butter" that didn't soak into my toast. I don't mind the cheese thing so much, it just would have been nice if they had mixed it in. Other than that, the grits were pretty good, As for the toast- I took a bite and couldn't bring myself to eat any more of it; something just wasn't right.   The staff is nice enough and the food came quickly. It's a good spot for greasy spoon type food if you have a hankering.

I guess I am pretty lucky. I have only caught the Lapalco Bridge when it's been up a few times in my life, and I've traveled on it a lot. I think it's cool that when they do construction on it, they are pretty fast about it. Although, last summer it was a closed for 4 or 5 days and it took me forever to get from Marrero to Gretna, but whatever. That wasn't a huge deal.

This place was a nice little surprise while we were out and about looking for some Halloween fun that wasn't too crazy.  We were here for a few drinks at the upstairs bar. I love the view from the balcony area and the nice breeze coming off of the river was really pleasant. I couldn't stay out there long because, even though it was a warm-ish night, the breeze from the river made it quite cool.  They have a pretty decent selection of local beers on draft. I didn't see anything that really blew me away or anything that was that unusual or hard to come by at other spots, but I appreciated that they had so many local taps. There are a few big screens, which makes me think that this is probably a hot spot during football games.  This place feels a lot like Happy's with a more local vibe. I didn't have any food, but they have a full menu of sandwiches and other hot dishes.

I pass Frosty's practically every day and I always see reviews popping up on my feed, so I finally decided to stop in.  I didn't know much about Frosty's except that the serve fresh juices, tea and different types of coffee and espresso. They also serve food, but this review isn't about the food. When I was here, the first thing that struck me were the prices- they seemed a little steep for coffee and juice, but hey, maybe it's really good so I held off judgement.  I decided to get the strawberry jasmine green tea without the tapioca balls in it. The nice man working rang me up and when the total came to nearly $6 I was a little shocked. That seemed a little pricey just for some flavored tea, but in for a penny in for a pound, I paid and gave it a shot.  Well...okay...I get why their tea is a little more expensive. This tea is obviously made with super fresh strawberries and not a mix. I was excited about the fresh fruit flavor and the little chunks of strawberry in my tea. Talk about refreshing! It was almost like drinking strawberry juice. Also, the drink was really sweet (a good thing), so I was able to sip on it and stay cool for the rest of the afternoon. I enjoyed my drink so much, that I think I will have to start coming here fairly regularly.  If you are looking for a refreshing and real fruit drink, and you aren't in the mood for a smoothie, this is definitely your place.

I had been wracking my brain for DAYS trying to remember what this place was called, when someone reviewed it, I finally remembered...McHardy's!  The first time I ever went to this place, I had just wrapped a photo shoot  and the photographer asked me if I wanted to have lunch.  When he mentioned that we were going to take a ride and get McHardy's, I had no idea what he was talking about.  Let me tell you, I LOVE me some Popeyes, but if I had to choose, I would definitely choose McHardy's.  I think that it's probably the closest you can get to homemade chicken without making chicken at home.  It's crispy, juicy and spicy.  It's delicious.  Also, this place has any other chicken place beat, as far as the price goes.  You can get a whole dinner for a super reasonable price.  There used to be a McHardy's on the Westbank, but I never made it to that one.  It might still be there, so be sure you check that out, if you are on the Westbank.

Not a bad little bar.  They have their signature drink: the hand grenade.  Word of advice: don't chug those things and don't have more than one.  They are stronger than you think.    Tropical Isle is one of those typical touristy kind of spots.  They have bands every now and then. If you are visiting, go just to say you went, but seek out nicer places once you try the drinks here.

Whee!  This is always a fun and unique way to see the city and get from point A to point B.  I have never lived near the streetcar, so I have never actually used the it for it's designated purpose (actual transportation).  I've only hopped on with friends for a ride on a nice day.   Actually, that's not true!  A guy I dated a few years back lived within walking distance of the line and I remember we rode the streetcar down Canal to downtown on the 4th of July, in order to see the fireworks.  I remember it being really packed and hot, but hey, it was a huge Summer holiday, so I can't fault anyone for that.  Anyway, the streetcar is definitely one of the most "New Orleans" parts of the city and something you have to do at least once, even if it's just for a fun, cheap ride.

I just LOVE people who knock off a few stars for a long wait at a place that just opened. Good Lord. Pro tip: if a place is new, expect a bit of a wait.  Like Katie A., I have never been to the original Willie Mae's. I just never find myself in the 5th ward when I am craving fried chicken. When I heard that there was going to be an Uptown location, I though to myself, "Hey, you're Uptown all the time! Now you can go get chicken there!" and today I did just that.  I stopped in at about 2:30, and although the large lunch crowd had moved on, there was still a nice gang of people in there. I was still able to walk up to the counter and order pretty quickly. I decided on the three piece fried chicken with mac and cheese and peas. I also got a sweet tea.  The wait was maybe a little over ten minutes, but I could tell that they had just pulled the chicken out of the fryer, because when they brought it to me, it was literally sizzling! Definitely worth a wait for chicken that fresh.  I let the chicken cool a bit and I dug into the mac and cheese. It was so good, creamy and delicious with a lot of flavor. Finally it was time to try the chicken. I could tell that it was different because the crust on the chicken was golden brown and crispy. It must be that wet batter they use. So much steam came off of the meat when I pulled off the skin. I love it when you can tell that fried chicken is super fresh and hasn't been sitting under a lamp. The meat was tender and delicious and was falling off of the bone- I couldn't get enough of it. Three pieces (breast, wing, and leg) proved to be a lot, so I was happy to take the leg home to snack on later.  Although I thought the meal was a little pricey- $14, I definitely found it to be worth it, as I left the place full and satisfied. The staff was really friendly and nice and gave me everything I needed with a smile and I liked that a lot. I can't wait to go back and get more of the delectable chicken.

I have been on the "hunt" for an avocado smoothie for a while now. I have heard they are the hot new thing because avocados are super good for you and rather than take the time to buy avocados and make my own, I just wanted to buy one somewhere. Seems reasonable? Anyway, when Joi B. posted a picture of hers on instagram and mentioned that she got it at Superfood Bar, I knew I had to check this place out.  I wasn't disappointed at all. The place is small, but was easy to find. They have a lot of "raw" foods, and as you would expect, everything is super healthy. I got my "simple" avocado smoothie which comes in one size- 16oz.  It was fantastic! First of all, it is basically a cup of pureed avocado with a little coconut in it. It is perfect if you are as much of an avocado lover as I am. Second of all, I was surprised at how filling the smoothie was! I had some cheese with it and that was basically my lunch. Finally, it is WAY cheaper than a place like Smoothie King and doesn't taste like it is loaded with sugar. It seems like whatever I get at Smoothie King just tastes overly sweet. All I got from my smoothie here was the flavor that I was looking for.  I will definitely be back. I want to try more of their menu and see what else they have to offer.

This was my first time ever at the track for Thanksgiving!  Since I had never been here, I really had no idea what to expect. Now I am about sound a little childish, but here we go. I don't gamble. I'm not good at it, I always lose, and I prefer to spend my money on clothes or yummy food than try my luck. With that said, YAY HORSIES! I really liked getting to watch the horses race and get to see them line up and all that. I'm sure there is a more technical term than that, but I'm new at all this.  It was cold. Luckily the area where you place bets/get snack and drinks is enclosed, so that made for a nice place to stay warm. It gets boring in between races, so don't be shy about chatting it up with other people who are waiting for the race to start. Everyone seemed pretty friendly.  I want to go back and watch the ostrich races one of these days!

Ooh! This is another local favorite of mine!  Although Aunt Sally's sells all different types of pralines (triple chocolate, cafe du lait, bananas foster) my absolute favorite go to is the original creamy. Now, what is a praline? Well, it's basically cream and sugar mixed with nuts and made into a delicious candy. The original creamy melts in your mouth and is so sweet and good. They are perfect as a desert or even in the morning with a nice cup of coffee.  Here at Aunt Sally's you can buy them in boxes or 6 or 12, so they are extremely easy to take back home with you or even give as gifts. They also have a nice assortment of different gift baskets that are perfect for any occasion.

I had a meeting, so naturally I suggested this place because meetings are always better with cake. This is a really cute idea- the concept of mixing sweets with fancy cocktails is pretty genius, and I'm surprised it has never been done in New Orleans before (wait, does Sucre serve liquor?).  We stopped in around noon and the place was empty except for us. I decided to get an iced coffee (which you can add REAL cream to!) and a couple of the doberge bites. I have been a fan of Debbie Does Doberge for years, so it's awesome that she finally has a brick and mortar shop where you can drop in a pick up a few sweets, when you are in the mood. The "real" food on the menu sounded great, but the kitchen doesn't open until 4. That's a little confusing, considering they serve breakfast style food. Is it different on Sundays or is the kitchen closed until 4 every day? Is this going to change? So many questions!  I would definitely kick this place up to 5 stars if their kitchen was open all day. They just opened, so maybe that's in the future plans. I loved my doberge bites and iced coffee. Both complimented each other really well and made for a delicious experience. The space itself is lovely with plenty of light flowing in through the large windows, plenty of seating, and books and games to keep people entertained.  I want to go back "after hours" and gauge the vibe of the place then. This is a cute little spot to check out, whether it is at the beginning of your evening or the end.

This was a tough one for me. I think I'm going to go with 3.5 stars. One of the big selling points of this place is that it's open late (until midnight), even during the week. In a city that likes to brag that it's all about the night life. that's hard to come by.  Me and a friend had gone to an event earlier in the evening when we realized we hadn't eaten. I jumped onto my Yelp app, did a quick search and saw that this was one of the few places still open in the area, after nine- perfect.  We started with the truffle chips, which was kettle cooked chips topped with truffle oil and cheese. I think this must be the new trend in apps as this is the third time I have had this somewhere. I don't know why I always expect it to be more spectacular than it really is. For my pizza I got the pepperoni pizza which came topped with a really generous serving of pepperoni. I liked it and although the pizza is cooked in a wood oven, it was evenly cooked and not charred on the bottom. Was it the best pizza in the world? No, but I was really hungry so it definitely hit the spot.  The staff here is friendly, and although the pizza takes a while to come out, I would say that it's worth the wait. This wouldn't be my first choice when looking for a good pie, but I would eat here again.

This seems to be a popular little gas station because it's located right off of an exit. I stopped in to load up on some snacks for a mini road trip. The store is small and the selection of goodies is somewhat limited. They have a lot of "Golden Flake" brand chips and jerky and stuff, but nothing really beyond that.  I found it strange that they don't sell sunglasses. I had forgotten my sunglasses, so I had planned to just pick up a cheap pair and nope, they don't sell them. I found it pretty odd, because I'm sure a lot of people stop in for little things like that. Oh well.  They have a nice selection of Mad Dog 2020 and malt liquor, if that's your thing.

This cute little shop is located in one of the best parts of Mid City- the American Can, not far from the bayou. Here you will not only find a nice selection of wines, but I was delighted to discover that they have a really great beer selection as well. They have wine tastings on Thursdays and Fridays, as well as other little events throughout the month. I enjoyed a Friday tasting and the staff is happy to tell you a little bit about the wine and find a wine that you would enjoy.  I love the little seating area right inside, so you can buy a bottle on wine and sit and sip with friends on a nice afternoon. Everything here is well priced and the staff is eager to help you find whatever you may be looking for.

Not a terrible bar. I only go here because some friends of mine live about 2 minutes from the place.  Okay crowd, but it gets super packed with young people who are just there to get ripped. Ridiculously smokey and since I am being drawn more and more to places that lack smoke completely, this is a turn off.  They do have a few little bar games here that are pretty fun. Like Morgan mentioned, the skee ball is one of the selling points. All in all not a bad place if you are in the area, but not worth the trip if you aren't.

I can't believe I have never reviewed this place!  No trip to mid city is complete without a trip to Parkway.  In my opinion, they make some of the most perfect po boys in the city.  Whenever I go, I usually get a shrimp po boy, fully dressed.  I usually eat at the bar, when I go, because I find the service to be faster.  Or, I will order at the bar and take my food outside when I get it.  Also a great place to get a good poboy, a beer, and watch the game.

Okay, so the first time we were here they were out of food. Seriously. 7 on a Saturday night- OUT OF FOOD. What? Chalk it up to not being prepared for the large crowd during their first month of business.  Cut to this past weekend and we were here for dinner. It was a 20 minute wait for a table, but we decided to sit at the bar and this was a great choice. I had looked (and drooled) over the menu, so I already knew what I was going to get: the pulled pork platter with potato salad and cole slaw and bacon mac and cheese. Oh yeah, they have 4 kinds of mac and cheese. Hey Frey, my wheelhouse: you're in it.  After a bit of a wait, out came the food and...yeah this looks amazing. No complaints about the pulled pork: it was tasty and juicy and, even though it had a lot of flavor and it didn't need it, I added their delicious sauce to kick it up a notch and made my mouth happy. The cole slaw was...um...salad with mayo on it? I get it, that's basically what cole slaw is, but this was straight up lettuce and mayo. It was a side salad. Just call it a side salad. The potato salad: siiiiigh. I should have switched my side choice when the woman next to us didn't touch her potato salad. It was potatoes and mayo. No frills. No flavor. I'll admit that I am really picky about my potato salad, but this was a disappointment.  Last but not least was the bacon mac and cheese. This was my favorite thing, besides the meat. It was tangy, creamy and perfect and it had pieces of bacon in it. It was heaven in a bowl. Hey Frey, since you serve 4 kinds of mac and cheese, why not make a mac and cheese sampler with a few bites of each kind? That would be amazing.  All in all, my experience here was good and I would return. The bartenders were fast about getting drink and food orders out and I like that there are TVs in the bar are to keep the crowd entertained.

A very strong 3.75 stars.  I used to go to The Camellia Grill location on South Carrollton all the time. Then I discovered St. Charles Tavern and I never looked back.  I was super hungry after a show downtown and fortunately for me, Camellia Grill is located right across the street. I walked in, and I was seated immediately at the counter. First of all, it's chaos in there. The chef working the grill (and everything else) is shouting at people asking them what they want. He definitely stays busy. The man behind the counter who got my coffee and made sure I was taken care of (Jack) was SUPER nice.  I decided on a cup of coffee, 2 eggs over easy, hash browns and toast (I'm a big breakfast for dinner type of person when I am out and about). Everything was cooked well and came pretty fast. The hash browns were okay, but not fantastic. The food definitely got the job done. Everything I had was ridiculously cheap (I would have spent more had I decided on Taco Bell or something) and pretty good.  They also have burgers, sandwiches and other food options if you aren't in the mood for any kind of breakfast.  The only drawback of the whole experience was that I felt kind of rushed. No one working there made me feel that way, but I feel bad sitting and sipping coffee when there is a line of people starting to form. Whenever I am back in this area, I will most likely return.

I'm always appreciative of any reason to have lunch at St. Roch Market, because it's always an excuse to try something I've never had before or revisit an old fave.  Good Bird has been on my list for a while, mainly because I love any kind of chicken sandwich, so I was eager to see what they had to offer. Upon a friend's suggestion I got the Larry Bird. With chicken, lettuce, tomato, avocado, and bacon all on ciabatta bread, it's hard to go wrong. The sandwich didn't disappoint- it's really big and served wrapped in paper with a side of their homemade chips. The chicken is nice and juicy and the avocado and bacon was the perfect touch. This sandwich was delicious! It was go-out-of-your-way good.  They have a pretty vast menu of other chicken sandwiches, but honestly I would just stick with the Larry Bird because, bacon. They also have wraps available, if you're not in the mood for a lot of bread. They have a Freret location that I'm eager to check out, mainly because it's closer to me than St. Roch.  Good Bird isn't just good; it's great! I'll be back.

I first stopped here for drinks during the Gretna Food Truck Fest, so I decided to stop back in and try the food.  We were here on a Friday afternoon for lunch and there wasn't much of a crowd, so we were seated quickly. We decided to take a seat in the bar area, but if I return I will definitely opt for the dining room instead. I got their classic burger which came with a nice pile of fries. I ordered the burger medium, but of course it came closer to well done. One of these days I am going to learn my lesson and just order the burger medium-rare and tell them to make sure that it's more on the "rare" side. Despite all of that, the burger was tasty and it had a lot of flavor. I liked that it was really big, so I had leftovers.   Although we didn't partake, they have a lot of drink special here such as "Trainwreck Tuesdays" and "Fireball Fridays", if that's your thing. I can see how this is probably a fun little night spot. The reason I mentioned I will sit in the dining room in the future is because the bar area is "high traffic" (of course), so I felt like I was in the middle of everything. The food is good, so I'll be back.

I'm always such a huge fan of Bath & Body Works aka "The Works" and this one is no different.  We stopped in here while we were doing some gift shopping and we were immediately greeted by Allison. She was super nice and helpful, told us about some specials that they were having and even hooked us up with some coupons. Right now The Works is having a "buy 2, get one free" sale, so while that's not on the same level as the Semi-annual sale, it's still worth checking out if you're in the market for some fall scents.  They're always having cool sales and great deals, so keep an eye out if candles, body sprays, shower gels and lotions are your thing.

Yum! This place really hit the spot in the middle of French Quarter Fest when I was craving something delicious, but didn't feel like waiting in a line.  One thing that I really love about this place is the atmosphere.  They have outdoor and indoor seating.  We sat inside and it was very cozy and almost felt like we were in a Parisian cafe (not that I would know. Ha.).  The tables are small and the dining room has a huge window that looks out onto the street so that you can watch people as they walk by.  As an appetizer, my friend and I started with the alligator sausage.  It came with a yummy dipping sauce, which really brought out the flavor of the meat.  I LOVE alligator and the sausage didn't disappoint. For our entree', we both got the red beans and rice and sausage. It came with bread and after we added some hot sauce to it, it was delicious. The sausage was smokey and full of flavor.  It was definitely what we needed after a long afternoon of walking around and looking for something to do.   I would definitely go back and bring out of towners here, as well.

This is a typical Party City. They have a lot of party decorations and things like that. During the Halloween season they have a really good selection of costumes. During the off season, you can find some costume pieces like wigs and gloves and stuff, but if you really need a costume worth something, you are going to have to look elsewhere.  I really like the huge candy section that they have now. You can go in and fill up a bag. Every 15 pieces of wrapped candy is a dollar, so it's a really good deal and can be a lot of fun to bring the kids for a treat.

I have to update this review because I'm addicted to Sucre cupcakes. I totally blame David.  If you have never had the cupcakes here, you need to know that you're going to get addicted. My faves are the strawberry ones and the vanilla ones. You get a HUGE cupcake that is soft and moist (sorry...damp? Is that better? Not dry.) and then you top it with the lightest, fluffiest icing that has even been created. I'm not even an icing person, but I could eat this icing by the tub.  Last time we were here I got a confetti cake gelato and a strawberry cupcake to go, because sometimes you want to eat a cupcake with glitter icing in bed and that's okay. They also have a wide assortment of chocolates and other fancy desserts and yums.  You're not going to be disappointed with anything you get here and all of it is well worth the price.

Wow.  This place has majorly improved in the year since my last review.  I have been here a few more times since I last reviewed and I have pretty much enjoyed it every single time.  I usually get a burrito, which comes with a side of chips.  I like the queso, but if you want just salsa, they will charge you for it.  Chips and salsa are not free here as they are at other places.    This is a pretty good place to eat on major holidays.  I remember eating here on the 4th of July when other places were packed and I had a really good time.  While Nacho Mama's will never rank as high as "Felipe's" in my book, I would definitely not hesitate to eat here if I was in the area.

Well, I'm apparently the last person to hear about this place because it was packed when I happened to stop in here for lunch. I knew it was opening but when I walked in, I saw a huge well established restaurant offering soups, sandwiches, salads and other treats.  Ordering here is simple- you go up to the counter, tell them what you want and they give you a number a bring it to you when you're ready. This place has all kinds of stuff: muffalettas, wraps and sandwiches, pasta, soups and even a salad bar. Think of it as Panera Bread on steroids.  For my lunch I decided to get a turkey wrap with steamed veggies and a cup of the tomato basil soup. The turkey wrap was perfection and I loved that it was low calorie. It was generous slices of turkey with some fresh spinach and tomato to round it out. It was light and good. The steamed veggies were good- I enjoyed the carrots and broccoli, but there was too much cucumber for my liking, but that's not a terrible thing, just my personal taste. The tomato basil soup was EXCELLENT! It came out nice and hot and topped with cheese that melted into it. I'm a sucker for good tomato basil soup and, while La Madeline is still my favorite, this version is sure to satisfy the craving.  The staff was super friendly and polite and they checked on me throughout the meal to make sure that everything was to my satisfaction. The dining room is huge and there were a lot of people here for lunch, but there was no line and the food came quickly. Oh, and they have free soft serve ice cream, if that's your thing.  This is a great little lunch spot on the Westbank, it was tasty and it wasn't as pricey as Panera, so I can definitely see myself coming back.

What better place to review for my grand finale of 2015 than the legendary Brennan's! Even though this is a frequent tourist destination, I would suggest making reservations; we made reservations and were seated as soon as we walked in.  It was so hard deciding what to start with on this amazing menu- everything sounded incredible. I was torn between the gumbo, the turtle soup and the roasted oysters, but ultimately I decided to go with the oysters. Out came six large oysters topped with buttery bread crumbs and roasted to perfection. The oysters were nice and juicy and the bread crumbs added an amazing touch to the dish that couldn't be topped. I was so glad that I made this appetizer choice.  For my entree I decided to get the Mahi Mahi amadine, which is a large piece of fish cooked with Marcona almonds, haricot verts and lemon butter. This fish was perfect. First of all, I loved the way it was cooked- flaky and smooth with tons of flavor (getting super technical here. ha). It was a perfect portion that left me satisfied, but not overly full. The almonds were a fantastic touch, and when they mixed with the butter they were a delicious addition to the fish. I had never had this type of fish before, so this was a real culinary adventure for me.  Finally, because we were at the place where it was born, we had to get the Bananas Foster. Of course, they do the whole show here: they wheel the hot plate out to your table and prepare it right in front of you, all while giving you the history of Bananas Foster. The dessert itself is incredible. My experience with it here made me realize that I have never really had Bananas Foster before, even though I have enjoyed it at other restaurants. There is just something about the way that it is prepared here that just pushes it over the edge. The yummy, buttery caramel goodness poured over ice cream and served with slices of banana just can't be beat and I am eager to return and have it again.  The wait staff here is incredible. They are beyond attentive and in addition to our waiter Reggie, another man came over regularly to make sure that we were satisfied with everything and that we were having a good time. We were seated in the main dining room and I thought that was the perfect spot, but I would love to see the other rooms as well.  I am so glad that Brennan's is back and I would love to return to this New Orleans institution. I feel like this is one of the New Orleans staples that everyone should visit at least once in their life.

No go cups and rude staff makes for a sad Marielle.   Seriously the muscle men at this place were gross and the staff was beyond rude. I asked for a go cup and I was told that they weren't allowed on this block. This is the same block as Lucy's and Vic's. I can't take my drink to go? Come on.    The music is what I would I imagine my suicide soundtrack would be. Seriously. It's boom boom boom with no end. Good Lawd.  If I had to pick an afterlife torture for my enemies, it would be Ohm. In conclusion, this place sucks and the people know it because I told them. I said, "Hey, do you know what Yelp is?" The dude at the door said, "Yep!" and I smiled. Here's the review you deserve.   Good morning. Good afternoon. And Good Night! Oy.

This is always a fun parade, if not a little slow moving. I have to agree with Bobby, there are always huge gaps in the parade where you feel like it's over.  Honestly, for me the best part of Barkus isn't really Barkus at all. I like going down to the Quarter on the day of and walking around and seeing all of the people out there with their dogs. On this day, everywhere in the Quarter is "dog friendly", people dress up their dogs and it's a lot of fun to see.  I do always enjoy seeing the parade dogs in their various costumes- some are very extravagant.

I loved this neat little vintage store.  It seems that they have a little bit of everything from clothing to jewelry to picture frames. Oh, and I loved the hats! I saw a cute little travel box with all kinds of goodies in it and I guess I should have asked if it was for sale. Now I'm kicking myself. Oh well.  I was admiring a rack of dresses when I noticed a lovely stuffed dog curled up on the sofa. Well, I admired it until it opened it's eyes and curiously looked at me. I asked him for some assistance but he explained that I was interrupting his nap, so I went about shopping on my own.  I was wondering if they buy vintage things. I couldn't really figure out if the owner herself is a collector and just finds things online to sell, or if she would be open to buying from someone off the street.  I will definitely go back whenever I have vintage needs. I agree with Joi. The smell of this shop is really nice and it's quiet. You feel like you are in an elder's old home full of antiques.

This place had been on my "bar-dar" (radar for bars) since they opened and, after trying one of their cocktails at the Yelp Salutes Our Troops event, we decided to stop in the day after to see what this spot was all about.  We were here late afternoon (about 4:30) and the place was empty. That's no problem- we make our own fun around here. We looked over the drink menu and David and I both decided to get the "Faux Rita". This is a frozen vodka drink with some cayenne pepper in it to give it a bit of a kick. They should call it a "Cajun Rita", in my opinion, but I digress. It was really tasty and had a nice flavor to it. Pro tip: wait for it to melt a little because I really liked when it got a bit liquidy.   We chatted a little with the bartender and he told us that vodka is "phase one" of what NOLA distilling has planned. They are going to be rolling out a lot of other liquors as the year progresses so when that happens, I'm sure that a lot more people will be spending time here enjoying some tasty drinks.

This should definitely be your first stop if you're looking for some art that's a little "different". There's a lot of different things here, but all of it has a spooky edge, that I just love.  I was here for Dirty Linen Night and I was able to walk around and really get a feel of the work here. The art is gorgeous and ranges from the strange to the macabre. There was even a diorama of a creepy murder scene, in case that's something that you might want to add to your collection. Anything that you end up purchasing here is sure to be a conversation starter. There is a sweetness to some of the more creepy works, which I can really appreciate.  I'm not sure if I'll be purchasing any of the works here for my own home, but I do like what they have going here.

My visit to Beachbum Berry's Latitude 29 was about 5 or 6 months in the making. I wanted to visit this place as soon as I first heard about it and after hearing all the raves, my excitement had reached it's peak by the time I finally set foot here. Something you may or may not know about me: I LOVE tiki drinks. Come on, how can you go wrong with fruit, sugar and spices? Sadly, it seemed like every time I had plans to visit LAT 29, something came up. I finally made it here and my experience did not disappoint.  We stopped into this cute restaurant and bar located in the Bienville House Hotel. Oh yeah, they serve food too! I didn't know either until about a month or two ago. I'm going to get to the drink reviews in a bit, but let's start with the food. We were seated and because I had already scoped out the menu online, I knew exactly what I wanted. We started with the pork and beef dumplings. We got them steamed and they were delicious. Each one was wrapped in a differently flavored "wrapper" and I wish I could remember the exact details because they were incredible.   For my entree, I got the Hawaiian Cuban Sandwich which is pork belly, ham, creole mustard, cream cheese, coronations, on buttered pineapple bread. It was RIDICULOUS. I mean it was insane how good it was. Before you ask; yes, it was a pressed sandwich! Don't you hate when you order a Cuban sandwich and it isn't pressed? One of my major food pet peeves. I got the fries as my side and they came with kimchi Ketchup & sriracha mayo. Yeah, they have a sriracha mayo and it's as delectable as you can imagine. The sandwich was so rich and delicious that there was no way I could finish it all. Soooo good.  Now for the drink reviews. We tried a bunch, so I'm just going to go ahead and list them with my thoughts.  Kea Colada: My first drink. Their version of a piña colada. Delicious, especially since I wanted to start slow with something that I knew I would like. Sweet and perfect in every way. Probably my favorite drink of the night.  Hawaii 504: My companion's first drink. Spicy with a lot of kick. This one packs a punch. For my taste, good for a few sips, but I might have some trouble drinking a whole one.  Zombie: My second drink. One of my Tiki "go to's". Rich and delicious with a bit of a kick, but not so much of a kick that you will want to call it quits while drinking it. Let it grow on you.  Navy Grog: My companion's second drink. This thing is no joke. Very strong and tastes like straight liquor. Has a spicy and fruity under taste, but it's definitely a "sipper".  Espresso Bongo: My third drink and second favorite of the night. Coffee and rum and fruit? Yes, please! SO good. It's sounds like a weird combination that shouldn't work, but what you end up with is a drink with a lot of flavor and a lot of kick without being overpowering. I can see myself getting this if I were to ever stop in for lunch. A nice pick me up.  Pontchartrain Pearl Diver: My companion's third drink. Sweet and spicy with a lot to offer. Over all really yummy and easy to drink. I definitely wouldn't hesitate to order this one for myself in the future.  As you can probably tell, I loved this place and I really can't wait to return. The decor is perfect and I like that it has a nice Tiki feel without being "in your face" about it. They have expanded their hours, so there's really no excuse to not check this place out, especially for a night cap. Word on the street is that they stop taking food orders at 10, so stop in early if you are looking for some grub.  I can't wait to go back and try more of the cocktails and food. This place is an absolute winner in every way. I should probably stop here because I'm starting to gush.

This seems to be the new food truck on the block and ooh baby is it a good one!  Ok, so I'm going to admit that I was one of people saying "$7 for a banh mi? Seriously?" But after tasting it's deliciousness, I was put it my place. This banh mi was PACKED with pork and provided a culinary experience that was out of this world. It had so much flavor that I enjoyed every bite and I was excited to share the experience with my insta-foodies.  While I'm being totally honest, I'm going to admit that the Cajun Spring Rolls were less than spectacular on my end. I think that they could use a bit more spice. Hey, add a little kick to those rolls and I will be all over them!  Saigon Slim's is going to go far and I am so excited that I was able to experience them tonight. I can't wait to try the rest of their faire!

I know that i have reviewed Commander's Palace two times before, but my opinion hasn't changed and each time the experience is top notch.  David took me here for our anniversary dinner. We knew we wanted to the evening to be special, so he chose this spot to make it a night that we wouldn't forget. As you do, he called ahead and made reservations. We arrived about 20 minutes before our reservation and we were seated upstairs at a lovely table by a window.  Lorenzo was our waiter, and since he knew it was our anniversary, he made sure that our experience was special. When I told him that I wanted to drink a cabernet, he picked one out specifically and it just happened to be a wine that is made in France just for Commander's Palace- it was delicious.  For my appetizer, of course I got the turtle soup. The turtle soup at Commander's Palace is probably the best in the city and it never disappoints. For my entree, I got the redfish topped with crawfish tails. This was great! It was a nice portion of fish perfectly cooked and topped with crawfish tails in a sauce that was a little spicy. It was perfect without being too heavy or overly filling. David had the filet and mashed potatoes, which looked incredible. If I return, I just might have to get the steak.  For dessert, I ordered the pecan pie ala mode that David and I had planned to share, but Lorenzo was so sweet, he brought out some extra ice cream, since it was a special night. He was also kind enough to send some complimentary shots over to the table- I think they were made with champagne and they were really good.  Our experience was perfection and Lorenzo made sure that we had a wonderful dinner. From beginning to end, we felt really special and I am excited to return.

"Treat yo self!"  Ok, so this isn't an every day store where you would shop, but every now and then a little splurge is nice.  I just inherited a bit of money and since I don't have any children or dependents, I decided to head over to Saks and treat myself to a little something special Why not? I deserve it. First of all, this place is fantastic and just being in here makes you feel special. They have designer clothing, handbags and jewelry, but on this particular day, I was interested in shoes.  As soon as I walked into the shoe section, I was greeted by a nice lady who asked me exactly what I was looking for and if I needed help finding anything. She helped me pick out some nice pumps that I had been eyeing and fetched my size so that I could try them on. When I say that I could have spent the ENTIRE day here trying on shoes, I'm not even lying. I found an adorable pair of pumps that weren't INSANELY expensive (but way more than I have ever paid for shoes) and I felt like I had stumbled upon a treasure. Then, I decided to swoop over to the makeup department and pick up a gorgeous shade of red lipstick, courtesy of Yves St.Laurent, just for good measure.  I think everyone (or at least every woman) should head over to Saks at least once and treat yourself to something special, even if it is makeup. The staff is super nice and helpful and not "uppity" at all (some people might be worried about that). Will I return? YES!
