When you are in the middle of summer and your air conditioning has died and you are ready to kill your fellow cohabitants due to being out of your mind hot, you want to call someone who knows how to fix the ac. That's when you have to call Keefe's.  We have been using Keefe's for as long as I can remember and they are always friendly, quick and know exactly how to solve whatever air conditioner problem that you may have. On more than one occasion, they have come to the house past 7 o'clock at night in order to take a look at things. Also, they don't overcharge you. If it's a small repair that has to be done, they charge a small price. They are extremely fair and efficient.

This is definitely my favorite French Quarter bar.  It is the oldest bar in the country and I love the dark and cozy atmosphere and the unique clientele that frequent this place.  Since it's located at the very end of Bourbon St., I've found that it doesn't get overly "touristy".  I rarely go on the weekends, but it's a great place to check out during the week, maybe after a date when you just want to get a drink in a cozy place with someone and chat.  I don't know if they still have this, but the few times I have been here on a Saturday night, they had a man in there playing piano and singing, which is always a good time.

I was here for a Pelicans game after David got some suite tickets and man was it fun!  I had been to a Pelicans game one other time, but I had never viewed it from the comfort of a suite and, let me tell you, there is simply no other way to watch an event here. The suite is gorgeous with a great view, super comfy seats and a menu that you can order goodies from. The Pelicans game was a blast and I love that they do interactive activities with the audience during "breaks" and the half-time performance was fantastic.   The Smoothie King Center isn't so big that you feel as if you're miles away from the action and, although I watched most of the game on the big screens, I had no problem seeing all of the action on the court.  The staff was excellent and we found our seats with no issues. The only hiccup came when we were leaving getting out of the garage took and while was a bit of a pain, but that's to be expected at a place like this.

Here's a little about me: about 8 years ago whenever some friends and I would hit the town we would always end the night at Waffle House. It was never good, I always regretted it and I have secretly judged Waffle House lovers ever since.  Fast forward to present day. David and I were hungry after I night out and, for some reason, I suggested Waffle House. I hadn't been in years, I wanted breakfast food and I figured anything was better than IHOP. We wandered into Waffle House and sat in a booth. We both decided on the "All Star" breakfast that I got with two eggs over easy, toast, grits, bacon and a waffle. Go big or go home, right?  First of all, I was immediately impressed at how fast the food came out- we're talking less than 10 minutes for the both of us to be served. The eggs were cooked perfectly, the grits were great and the bacon was crispy. I had never actually had a Waffle House waffle before and it was perfect- nice and fluffy, the way a waffle should be. Could it be that I actually enjoyed something I got at Waffle House?  I'm not sure if it's because our experience at Huddle House was bad, but David and I were both impressed by the service and food here. Maybe you have to go to Huddle House first to really experience the professionalism at Waffle House. Who knows? All I know is that our check was $20 and our food was delicious and we'll definitely be back.

This is one of my favorite places to check out live music on Frenchmen street.  Although it's not as fancy as Snug Harbor or even dba, it has a certain "New Orleans" charm about it and there are always cool bands playing here.  Spotted Cat doesn't seem to have become as overrun with "Treme" fans as other Frenchmen street places and the crowd is more local.  The staff is always friendly, even when the place is packed.  A definite "must" for any local or visitor.

I had been here a few times in the past and I was left pretty underwhelmed. While my experience today was better, it's still not going to be my favorite Westbank sushi stop anytime soon.  My friend and I were in the mood for some pre Christmas sushi, so we stopped in here for lunch. I knew exactly what I was going to get, as I am fairly easy to please when it comes to sushi. Since the sashimi here is only served in 2 piece increments, I decided to just focus on rolls.  We got two tuna rolls, a rainbow roll and a tornado roll. The tuna rolls weren't bad and the rainbow roll was fantastic. The tornado roll was good and a nice size, and although I usually think that fried sushi is gross (doesn't frying it kind of defeat the purpose?), I found the tornado roll interesting. It's really big, so I didn't feel any shame when I had to forgo my chopsticks and just pick it up with my fingers.  One complaint that I have is- I ordered iced green tea, which came with ice. Every time it was refilled, she would refill it from a pitcher with no ice in it. I was left with room temperature green tea, which was just weird.  Tennou is still my favorite Westbank sushi place, but Cafe Zen would do in a pinch.

Just wanted to update this to say that I have been LOVING their rainbow roll as of late!  You can get a half order, so you don't have to worry about having to eat 8 really big roll pieces.  Also, I have taken to getting their iced green tea with my meals, which is fabulous and refreshing, especially on hot summer days.  I really wish I could bottle the stuff, because it has more flavor than the iced green tea I've had at other places.  Just a note: others have complained about the service, but I've never had any issue and I've been here A LOT for both lunch and dinner.

Yikes. It's a split here between really good and really bad.  The really good: they were having a big sale on home decor, which I happened to be in the market for. They also had my hair products that i buy here because they are super cheap salon-like brands and I get to save a lot of money.  The really bad- disorganization, this place is a mess. I couldn't find anyone to help me get something specific that was on a high shelf, so they lost out on a $40 sale. Once I went to check out, the price of some hair products I bought rang up more than what it was marked. The cashier went to go check it out and came back and told me it had been labeled wrong and the higher price was the correct one. At that point i just bought it, because I had been in line for at least 10 minutes. I know I should have walked out, but I didn't want to think I had completely wasted my time.   All in all this frustrating experience guaranteed that I will shop elsewhere next time.

I usually hate doing a "pros and cons" list for reviews, because I feel like it's too simple, but it's going to be the easiest way to sum this place up. Red, White and Blue is my usual thrift stop on the Westbank, so naturally I am going to compare this store to my "go to".  Pros: They accept credit cards They have fitting rooms The store is really well organized. Not only are things organized by gender, but they are organized by size and style with big signs (noted improvement since Jennifer B's visit). No long lines Cheap cheap cheap: they had some decent looking tops for as low as $2 Great selection of kid's clothes for low prices. Considering how quickly little kids grow out of things, why waste your money paying retail?  Cons:  Abysmal electronics selection and a lot of what they do have is broken. A lot of the things they have are stained or torn, so be sure to check each item carefully. Quality of merchandise is less than other thrift stores, but there is much more of it. Housewares are piled on top of each other and completely unorganized I HATE the area where this store is located and there are pan handlers in the parking lot that store owners do nothing about.  There you have it- a solid three star rating. This spot is worth checking out, but don't expect to find anything spectacular.

I just got a fancy new Samsung Galaxy smart phone (subtle brag) and the folks at T Mobile were more then helpful in helping me figure out exactly what would work best for me and getting me all set up.  They helped me take my old, sad smart phone and transfer all of my info to my fancy new phone, with no trouble at all. Service was fast and there was zero wait, even though there were a few other people in the store.

No, you're eyes aren't deceiving you. Ruby Red's is BACK in their original location!!  It's been two long years (maybe more), but today I was able to have one of Ruby's delicious steak cheddar burgers that I missed so much. Now, they have only been open for about 5 days and they are currently only serving burgers, so if you are craving a chicken sandwich, you might have to wait a week before you are able to sink your teeth into one.  Walking in, it was as if nothing had changed. The peanuts were on the floor, the checkered table cloths were in place and I was a happy camper. I got my burger medium rare and it came with steak fries. It was all as good as I remembered.  I can't wait to go back again and again. FINALLY a good burger place on the Westbank!

Eh, it was okay but I've had better.  A group of us stopped in here for dinner after the last elite event. I suggested this place, mainly because it was a few doors down from our event venue and I figured they would have something for everyone. There was no one really here on a Sunday night, except for a few parties and it was a nice evening, so we were seated on the balcony area upstairs.  I want to start by saying that our waiter was Mike and he couldn't have been any better. He was good about getting us our drinks and anything else that we needed and he didn't complain when we asked if we could split the check seven ways.  For my entree, I ordered the shrimp and grits and I think everyone else got a burger and one person got chicken fingers. When my food came out it was warm on top and cooler in the center. I think that the kitchen probably made mine first, stuck it under the heat lamps and then made everyone else's burgers. It wasn't a huge deal- the dish was still pretty good and I was hungry so I ate most of it. It wasn't the best shrimp and grits I've ever eaten, but it hit the spot. Next time I'm here with a big group, I think I'm going to just order a burger like everyone else and not throw the kitchen any curve balls.  The balcony area was really nice and spacious and I liked the "New Orleans-y" feel it had while we all sat, chatted and ate, so I would probably return for that experience.

Well, it's been a month since I have tried Johnny Sanchez and since it's doesn't look like I will be making it back anytime soon, this review is going to have to stand as is, for now.  It was a Saturday night and the place was packed. Thankfully we had made reservations for a slot they had open at 10. Yeah, pretty late for dinner, but no biggie. The first thing that struck me upon walking in was the interesting mural on the wall. The second thing that struck me was how loud the restaurant was.   We were lead to our seats and given a menu. First of all, it was so loud that I couldn't even hear my dining companion over the din of the dining room. Also, there was a football game on in the bar area and the crowd SCREAMED every time some team scored. Seems like a little much for a restaurant, much less one that is trying to consider itself "fine dining".  Looking over the menu, everything sounded pretty good. The thing that stuck out to me was the "whole fish". I was pretty hungry and I like fish, so I told the waiter that that was what I wanted. Well, he immediately talked me out of it, telling me that it's more suitable for two people and there's no way I could finish it on my own. That sounds like a challenge, but okay...after a quick glance over the menu, I decided on the lamb enchiladas  My enchiladas came and while I am not a huge fan of lamb, they were well prepared and had a lot of flavor. I wasn't really blown away by the meal and I left not really seeing what all the fuss was about.  After talking about my experience with some friends they ALL recommended the whole fish. D'oh! Maybe if I hadn't been swayed into not getting what I wanted in the first place, this would be a 4 star review. Serves me right for not sticking to my guns. Oh well. If I ever make it back, whole fish it is.

This is a nice little bar off of Bourbon St. It's not so bad, as it has a nice mix of locals and tourists. I've always found that the bartenders here are nice and friendly.  There is a really nice patio in the back where you can socialize on nice days. You can also host private parties on the patio, as I have been to a couple. I have always had a good time here and I would return.

Man, this should have been my 200th review!  Oh well, a bit over #200 will do.  I would like to start by saying that I am a PROUD alum of The University of New Orleans.  I not only received my Bachelor of Science in Psychology here (as did my father), but I also came away with a well rounded education that included classes, not only in Psychology, but in Geology, Biology, Arts, Anthropology, Art history, English, Foreign Language, Computer Science and three different Maths (one of which nearly killed me.  Trig is the devil.).  Am I bragging?  You bet your bow tie I am!  That was a lot of hard work, man!  You can take classes online, which makes it really easy to work around your schedule.  UNO offers a huge and gorgeous campus with buildings for classes, student housing (apartments and dorms), a student center (in which a student bookstore and eating area is held), a library, a performing arts center, a gym and an arena where sports events and concerts are held.  Did you know that UNO has a children's center that caters to children of faculty and students ages 1-5 years?  They are called the petite Privateers!  How cute is that?  Parking at UNO is really convenient.  Buy a parking pass at the beginning of the semester and park in the parking lot closest to your classes (planning classes by day that are all in close proximity to one another is an art all it's own).  If you are interested in social activities at UNO, they offer everything from Basketball to Football (for 2 years now) to Greek life.  There are a lot of organizations that you can get involved in, in the arts as well.  When I go for my Master's degree, my plan is definitely to return to UNO.    UNO alums be heard!  Review today!

I stopped in here because I found myself in the 'hood and I needed to stock up on some Mardi Gras supplies. This place was STOCKED for Mardi Gras and I was so excited to get some holiday stuff here.  I got a few tshirts and a king cake scented candle (yum!). This is a cool shop and while I don't think it has as much as other Fleurty Girl shops, they have a nice selection here. The girls working here did a good job at managing the customers and helping with whatever was needed. As always, FG is a great gift shop and a great place to pick up a cute top or gift for your favorite NOLA lover.

This TJ Maxx won my heart immediately for the simple fact that their shoe section is organized and not all over the floor.  I found some cute pumps that were on sale for $5 and fit me perfectly. They also had a nice selection of flats, although I was not really in the market for them on the day I was here. The checkout went fast and the staff is friendly enough. Honestly, I knew what I was looking for, so I didn't venture into the rest of the store, but I was happy with what I found.

I kind of dragged my feet in visiting this Dairy Queen. I think that it's been open for a few months and I was really looking forward to it. I have just been avoiding it, because I knew that having a Dairy Queen this close to my house would be big trouble. The one in Marrero was far enough away to not be a temptation. I can get to this one in 3 minutes. Uh oh.  I finally stopped in (well, drove through) because I had a craving for a Strawberry Cheesequake Blizzard and I had a "buy one, get one" coupon for my birthday. The Strawberry Cheesequake is my ultimate favorite. I think it's the fresh strawberries and cheesecake chunks. You can't really go wrong with that.  I went through the drive through and there was pretty much zero wait in the middle of the afternoon. I got my Blizzard in record time with no hassle at all. I should mention that I don't eat DQ food, only because I don't think you get your bang for your buck, but the blizzard was on point, as per usual. I found the girl at the window especially friendly and my blizzard came with a few coupons to be used at a later date: uh oh (again).

Hallelujah! I think we finally have a good Vietnamese restaurant located at the Hong Kong Market!  Rice Paper newly opened and is operated by a former chef from Pho Tau Bay, so when a friend told me all about this place, I was excited and my expectations were quite high.  We stopped in for lunch and I was immediately impressed because there were a good number of people here. You might be thinking "Wow, you are easily impressed!" but hey, the last restaurant that was here never had any customers when I ate there, so there's that. They have quite an extensive menu of spring rolls, pho, banh mi, vermicelli bowls and the like and the menu isn't lacking a lot of options (filet mignon pho, anyone?).   I decided to get a small bowl of the pho with round steak and brisket and because it's a new place and we were first timers, we also decided to get an order of egg rolls and and an order of spring rolls. I also got a Vietnamese coffee.  The pho was amazing and the broth was full of flavor and yummy. You can definitely taste the link between Rice Paper and Pho Tau Bay. The egg rolls were also really good. I like that they were lighty fried and the "main show" was the inside, which you could tell was all fresh ingredients. The pork spring rolls were delicious, and easily measure up to my favorite pork spring rolls at Pho Bang.  I am so excited that the Westbank has another really good Vietnamese restaurant and one more delectable option when a craving for Pho hits. I can't wait to return and give these wonderful people my business.

Okay, am I going to lose all credibility if I say that I kind of really liked Voodoo BBQ?  Let me start by saying that I am not as much as a barbecue "expert" as some other folks, but I do know what I like. We were here for dinner on a Friday night. This is one of those "order at the counter" type places and after looking over the menu, I decided to get the brisket platter with cole slaw, mac and cheese and corn bread.  I really liked it! The brisket was tender and juicy with a lot of flavor and the cole slaw was obviously fresh made. The mac and cheese was okay, but I could tell it had been made way earlier in the day and just warmed up when I ordered it. This will probably be the only thing that I skip next time. The corn bread was soft and very good. I was surprised how much I enjoyed the platter, and overall I think it's a good deal for $10.  If you are looking for fancier barbecue, then head over to Blue Oak, but if you are in the area, Voodoo will satisfy your craving

The oyster fest is nice mainly because it's one of the smaller fests in the area.  There are all kinds of awesome oyster based foods from all around the city. My favorite, the oyster po boy, never disappoints. There are also bands and live music so you can have a good time while you eat. The fest is held at Woldenberg park, so you can watch the river as you eat and relax.  The only complaint is that it happens right at the cusp of Spring and Summer, so the heat can be pretty intense. Don't forget your sunscreen!

I think that it's probably impossible to put my experience here into words, but I'm going to try. After years of wanting to visit Le Crepe Nanou, I finally had the opportunity, and I may never be the same.  I'll start at the beginning. I knew it was going to be a good evening when I was greeted at the door by a red cat sitting on a stool.  Seriously. I think he works there. He was greeting people.  I walked in and was immediately taken by the atmosphere. The inside is small and dark, but cozy and nice. We were lead to a small table and given a menu. In the dim lighting it was difficult to read, but I was able to make out the basics and I knew exactly what I wanted.  First and foremost, I knew that I wanted to try the cheese plate. They brought out a board of assorted French cheeses. I can't remember the exact names and I know that they switch them up a lot, so I will just say that they were delicious and just as you would expect in a nice French restaurant. They came with a side of some fruits, which I feel really brought out their flavor and added a nice touch.  For my entrée, I decided on the filet mignon. It came medium rare and cooked to perfection. I asked for it topped with a béarnaise  sauce and it was decadent and rich and delicious. The meal also came with a side of grilled vegetables and pommes frites.  Throughout the meal, I enjoyed delicious red wine, which complemented my entrée wonderfully and delicious fresh French bread and butter added a nice touch to the entire meal.  I will absolutely go back to La Crepe, hopefully sooner rather than later. The entire meal was an experience that I won't soon forget.

I like Parasol's although admittedly, I don't go here as nearly often as I used to since Tracey's moved in and I really never eat here.   This is a nice little neighborhood joint that serves up a good poboy. I'll usually stop in with friends at the end of the night to get a beer. It's on a dimly lit corner, so I would never go by myself and the place itself is really small, so it's not the first place I seek out when I am looking for a place to hang out. It serves it's purpose, but as I said before, I prefer Tracey's.

After our awesome Yelp event here, I couldn't wait to get back to Belle's Diner.  We stopped in on a rainy Saturday and we were immediately seated. Joe was our waiter and he couldn't have been more fantastic. The first thing I did was order a milk shake and he suggested I try their brand new pecan pie shake- a man after my own heart. I gave him the green light as I looked over the menu.  I went into Belle's thinking I was going to get some breakfast, but after I saw a club sandwich on the menu, I decided to go with that. This huge sandwich came topped with more fries than I could ever eat in one sitting. While the sandwich was definitely good, I wouldn't say it was the best I have ever had. The pecan pie shake, however, was AMAZING! It tasted just like pie and was topped with whipped cream and caramel and I will be getting it again when I return!  Joe was fantastic. It was a busy Saturday and he never stopped. He took the order, made the shake and split his time between many different tables and always checked to make sure that we had everything that we needed. He was the waiter from heaven.  The decor of Belle's is SO me: pinup and WWII everything! You feel like you have been transported back to the 50's and the oldies playing on the radio are a nice touch. My only complaint is that the ac isn't that great and the place gets warm when the doors are closed. I don't think that can be helped- it's a small place, but I wanted to mention it in case you are someone who "overheats" easily.  Belle's is a perfect spot if you are spending the day Quarter hopping or just shopping around at the French Market and need a good bite to eat for a reasonable price. They serve breakfast all day, so I am going to try some French Toast when I go back.

Surprisingly clean and friendly, considering it's in the French Quarter!  Stopped in here during French Quarter fest for a water break. Being out in the hot sun all day can start to drain you after a while. Even though the place was pretty packed, the staff did a good job of keeping up with the crowd and getting people in and out of the door in a timely manner. CVS turned out being a lifesaver during the fest.

Yay! I feel like this little spot on Decatur has finally found the bar that it's supposed to be. Other bars that have moved into 1135 Decatur haven't seemed to last, but I love Spitfire.  First of all, the bar itself is really cool. There's a propeller behind the bar that actually spins! Second of all, the staff is friendly and the music is good, with various tunes from the 80's and 90's. It doesn't have the "dirty" feel that other bars on Decatur seem to have, and although it's dark, you don't feel like you are going to run into a bad element here. There are pool tables in the back, if that's your thing and you are bound to have a good time.
Reviewing this one, since it's the one I go to.    The best iced coffee anywhere.  Better prices than Starbucks.  Why go anywhere else?

This is a neat shop that has a lot of fun little treats.  As the name suggests, they have pralines. I didn't try any, so I can't vouch for them, but I've discovered that if you've had one praline you've had them all. They also carry a variety of cooking supplies such as utensils as well as spices and hot sauces and things like that. The woman working was sure to ask if I needed any help or if I was looking for anything specific. This was nice, especially considering I had stopped in on a pretty busy night.  Magnolia probably isn't worth going out of your way, but if you find yourself in the area, it's worth a look.

I'm giving this Cafe Du Monde 4 stars, for the main reason that it's convenient for me.  It's a Cafe Du Monde just like any other.  You're gonna get cafe au lait and beignets.  When I go to this one, I usually just get a frozen cafe au lait, which is just fabulous!  This location is in the mall, so it's never packed.  They also have their classic little green tables and chairs for sitting.  Nice view of the mall fountain from the seats.

Yvonne Lafleur is known as the poster woman for fashion in the New Orleans area.  Not only is this shop located in one of my FAVORITE parts of uptown, but it carries some of the most gorgeous dresses I have ever laid eyes on.  If you need a dress for a special occasion (and you have a few bucks) this should be the first place you look.  Now that it's the season for Carnival balls, their window is dressed with gorgeous sparkly treats that I can only dream of being able to afford and having somewhere special enough to wear.  They also carry lingerie, which I would call "special occasion" lingerie for a honeymoon or anniversary.

Whenever a place has just opened, I am always hesitant to give it a shot. There are usually kinks to be worked out and everyone is just getting the hang of the restaurant biz.  Baie Rouge is the exception to that rule. When we went in, we were told we could sit anywhere, so we did. The dining room is huge and has a separate sitting area with sofas, if you just want to go in, order an app and relax with friends. Baie Rouge has applied for their liquor license and is waiting for it to come through, so it is BYOB (for now) but they are happy to open your wine for you.  All kind of things on the menu from soup and salad to steak. For our appetizer we decided on the pomme frites topped with Brie. I thought this was going to be typical fries with some Brie sprinkled on them. Boy was I wrong! The cheese was melted onto thin cut fries and there also seemed to be some kind of sauce in there too. It was ridiculously good. I love fancy pants cheese fries!  For my meal I decided on the Magazine Club with a side of cole slaw. The sandwich came on bread that was toasted to perfection with delicious ham and bacon making up the sandwich itself. It was so good! Check out my picture of it. Doesn't that look amazing? I loved that the cole slaw was kind of different. It didn't have any mayo in it, which was a different experience for me, but I liked it because it felt like a healthy little salad treat. I know that sounds odd, but it worked.  Our waitress, Jordan, was super attentive and friendly and made the experience perfect. I will absolutely be returning to Baie Rouge. Great food that isn't too expensive is always my idea of a good time!

I have since gone back a few times since my last review and I really love this place.  Not only are the cookies fantastic, but the mega-fours (extra large petit fours) are AMAZING! They are almost like slices of wedding cake. They also have regular sized petit fours as well as slices of cake and cake balls. I also like that they decorate the sugar cookies according to the season. Also, the woman working here is always super nice and friendly and will help with whatever you may need.  Check out the picture of my festive Christmas cookies!

Oh my God! I am way overdue for an Avenue Pub update!  Since my last review, I have become a bit of a beer connoisseur and I know a good beer when I taste one. Not only does Ave Pub have revolving taps, but the owner Polly  is always sure to have an abundance of delicious brews in bottles for her patrons to sample. I love the Pub because the bartenders are always super friendly, even if you are a beer novice and you need a little help figuring out what you like.  I love this place not only for the beer, but the balcony and the fact that it is open 24 hours. It also doesn't hurt that one of my bestest friends, Liam works the graveyard shift a lot of nights. If you are service industry, head in here after work and you will be treated right.  Oh and it helps that Ave Pub has a kitchen. Not sure what time it closes, so you might want to do your research before you plan on munching here. Just a note: the dump truck fries are legendary.  Will I go back? Uh...yeah. Always.

I had always passed this place, whilst driving down St. Charles and would think to myself "eek, what a dive!"  So, when my boyfriend suggested that we meet his friend and her husband here, one afternoon for a beer, I was less than thrilled.  Whatever, I'll give it a shot.  So, I went and it really wasn't that bad.  They have a huge beer selection, which is a huge plus.  This place didn't really start to grow on me, until a few months later when we celebrated a friend's birthday here.  We went to the upstairs area and sat in a big group on the balcony.  You have a great view of St. Charles Ave and the atmosphere is nice and not too loud.  They also serve food.  This night, we got a few snacks.  We also went back and got burgers, which were really good.  I took off one star because it's really smoky, so sitting inside isn't as nice as sitting outside.  Despite that, I would definitely go back.

Every now and then I get a major craving for pasta and since it had been years since I had been to Olive Branch, we decided that this would be a great place to get dinner.  We got here at around 7 on a Tuesday and we were seated immediately, but I already knew there was going to be an issue because there was a big table full of kids that were screaming and running around and...no, just...no.  We decided to start with an order of cheese sticks while we looked over the menu. There was some type of "2 for $22" special going on where if you ordered two pasta entrees you got them for $22, total and free garlic cheese bread, so we went with that. The garlic cheese bread was basically a mini cheese pizza, but it got the job done.  For my entree I got the Cajun trio pasta which is penne pasta with crawfish, sausage and chicken topped with plenty of sauce and cheese. This dish was out-of-this-world good! There was a lot of it, I loved how cheesy it was and how generous they were with the sausage, chicken and crawfish and it had a nice little spice to it. I had plenty of leftovers and I will definitely be getting this dish again.  Our waitress was super sweet and attentive and she was good about getting everything to us quickly and even gave me a "go cup" for my iced tea. I'm sorry to knock off a star, but I have to because the table of kids that were screaming at the top of their lungs and running around the restaurant, like it was a playground, definitely detracted from the experience. I was wishing the waitress would have gone over and asked the parents to get the kids to chill out, but I guess that's frowned upon in today's society where kids are basically allowed to do whatever they want and never hear the word "no".  I would be back for the delicious food and the great service.

Now, I'm sure that some would consider this Asian food, but I would respectfully call it "Asian light".  I don't think I've ever eaten anything overly Thai here.  Not unless putting a sauce on a piece of salmon is Thai food.  Not that I'm complaining.  I have never had anything here that I didn't like.  In fact, I like this place a lot.  Whenever I go I feel like I'm eating dinner in the middle of a nightclub.  They have many delicious signature drinks.  I had one, but I can't remember what it was called.  I think it was some kind of daiquiri.    They have a lot of social events here, and I can see this being a cool little "after work" place to stop and get a drink.

This is a SUPER cute gift shop in Metairie.  The sell New Orleans "centric" gifts, jewelry and home decor that is in the same vein as Fleurty Girl. I stopped in here looking for a New Orleans charm bracelet and I was excited to discover that MJ'S carries them and has plenty of really cute New Orleans charms for under $15 each. Some of my favorites included a shot gun house, Roman candy cart, K&B sign and the Rosenberg's girl. Really unique stuff that any local is sure to love.  They also sell a lot of things to do with the Saints and pretty much Fleur de Lis anything. If you are looking for a cute gift, this is a fabulous place to start.

I was here when I was having my Roux Carre adventure and after hearing raves, I knew Splendid Pig was going to be my lunch choice.  I got the Pork-a-mein, which is their version of Yakamein. This is hot a dish with an egg, noodles, and meat all served in a broth. The pork was flavorful and the egg was a nice touch. It was cooked over easy, so it oozed into the rest of the dish, which I liked. While it wasn't the greatest version of this dish I have had in my life, I enjoyed it and I wouldn't hesitate to order again (although, I really want to try their Banh Mi).

Honestly, it's a daiquiri shop on Bourbon and all that entails.  We stopped in here one night during/after French Quarter fest and it was pretty dead, all things considered. The bartender was really nice and I think that we just had beer or something.  They do, of course, have their famous frozen daiquiris, if that's your thing. Of course this is the type of place that caters to 90% tourists, so it is what it is.

Judge me all you want, but I had a really good time here.  This is a cute little piano bar that does a good job of getting the crowd going. We stopped in here after the Yelp awards looking for some good music and to have fun. There was a "washboard" player who pulled me on stage so I could dance around like a dope and play his washboard. They play a lot of classic piano type songs like Billy Joel and some music you can dance to as well. I know that this place is more of a tourist hang, but I had a blast here and I wouldn't hesitate to return if I was in the mood for something a little bit different. I almost prefer it over Pat O's piano bar because this spot encourages dancing.

I was in Lakeview and craving a burrito big time when a friend suggested we head to El Gato Negro.  It was lunchtime, and although it was about one there was no crowd and we were seated immediately. First of all, this menu is amazing. They have a wide variety of choices (including fajitas!) but I had my mind set on that burrito and I decided to get my burrito with pork.  As we waited, I dug into the bowl of chips and salsa that were given to us as a free munch. The chips were amazing and tasted warm and fresh. The salsa was pretty light with not too much spice to it, although there are a couple of hot sauces on the table, if you want to spice things up.  My burrito came out and WOW. Not only was it huge, but it was topped with salsa, guacamole and sour cream. Along with generous amounts of pork, this beauty was stuffed with onions, beans, rice and cheese. The burrito had a lot of flavor and was beyond delicious. You could really taste all of the fresh ingredients that went into making this meal. I must have been really hungry, because I finished all but about 2 bites of this thing. It was out of this world.  I will definitely return to El Gato Negro. Between the food, the friendly waiter and the atmosphere, I am a fan.

For review 1800, what better place to review than a restaurant I have driven past my entire life and always wondered about until recently? Beef Connection has always intrigued me- it's a windowless building and I never see any people over there. What's the situation?  My dad and I decided to try Beef Connection for lunch, since I had never been, and we were in the mood for steak. We had no problem just walking in and getting a table on a Friday afternoon. To our surprise, there were a few people here and they were all regulars- the waitresses knew them by name. For the lunch special you can get a cut of steak and your choice of any two sides. I decided to get the petit filet with potatoes au gratin and spinach au gratin.  The petit filet was perfection. I got mine cooked medium and it was juicy and tasty and everything I want in a steak. The potatoes au gratin was great! A MASSIVE serving a potatoes covered in a thick crust of cheese with cheese mixed in throughout. This could easily be shared, if you're the sharing type. The spinach au gratin was excellent as well. Let's just be honest- a thick coat of cheese makes everything delicious. Once again, the portion was massive and the taste was out of this world.  Service was excellent and our waitress checked on us regularly even though she was juggling a lot of tables. There's absolutely no natural light in the place and the dining room tends to be dark, so be aware of that if you are claustrophobic. Not seeing daylight was a little odd after a while, especially since it was around noon on a sunny day when we were here. I thoroughly enjoyed my experience here and I will absolutely return.

This place was okay, but nothing really to write home about.  We stopped in here before a show at the Civic. Convenience is really the only thing that attracted me to this restaurant. I am a HUGE fan of the Magazine St. location, and for me this location just couldn't hold a candle.  First of all, we came in and the woman seating people first seated us at a small table right next to the kitchen. There were plenty of other available tables that weren't next to the busy, noisy kitchen, but we were seated here. I'm usually not one of *those people* who asks to be re-seated, but in this case, I asked the waiter if we could move and we moved to a larger table on the other side of the room.  Happily seated, we decided to order some margaritas and some queso to start. The margaritas were good, as always, but the queso was lacking something. I'm not sure what it was exactly, but it had no flavor to me. It was...odd.  I decided to get my usual which is the Al Pastor burrito- wet. It came out and it wasn't wet (which means salsa, sour cream, and other goodies on top). He swept it off to the kitchen for a fix and quickly brought it back. It had all of the stuff on top, but by the time I got to the middle it was room temperature and not warm. All in all, it was decent and if I didn't know how it was supposed to taste I wouldn't be complaining, but knowing how good it is on Magazine St.- I was pretty bummed.  The atmosphere in this location is also super loud to the point where it's hard to have any kind of conversation. Long story short: good place for takeout, don't order anything "wet", and don't let them seat you next to the kitchen.

Actually not terrible for fast food in the middle of a casino.  We were in Harrah's enjoying the sights and the smoke free air, when we decided that we could definitely eat. Where else but Fudrucker's, open 24/7? I got a bacon cheeseburger and onion rings and maybe I was just hungry, but I found it to be really good for fast food! The service was super fast (and yes, there was a line!)   If I was hungry at the casino, I would definitely swoop into this place again. At least it's not a buffet!

If anyone ever questions my dedication to good food, I will probably just tell them about the time I got in line at 10:30am for grilled cheese. Hey, I was 6th in line and I got to order as soon as they opened, so who's the fool now? I was here for The Big Cheezy grand opening and you really haven't questioned your life until you have rushed over to a grilled cheese restaurant at 10:30am so that you can eat delicious grilled cheese and then get back to work.  The line moved quickly and when it was my turn to order I got the crawgator, which is alligator and crawfish sausage with cheddar and pepperjack cheese, onions and peppers. I don't think I had ever had this sandwich before and it was SO GOOD! If it's your first time and you are looking for something really cheesy, I would go with this one. It's all packed between two buttery slices of sour dough bread and it's just perfect. For my side I got the bacon mac and cheese, which was beyond rich and delicious. I was happy they had "to go" boxes, because there was no way I could have finished all of this in one sitting.  The service was fast and the food was delicious. Also, they are connected to Henry's bar, if you happen to be in the mood for a cocktail with your cheese. I'll be back.

I recently needed two tires replaced on my car and the first place I decided to go to get them was firestone.  They are always extremely helpful and friendly.  Not only were my tires replaced with ease, but they gave me a warranty on them, in case I get a flat or have a blowout and need a tire replacement.  They make the stressful situation of needing new tires a lot less stressful with their knowledge and the ease of which everything is handled.  Highly recommended and I would definitely return for future help.

This neat market has always been a favorite of mine, especially since it is open on weekend evenings and is only a few steps from the best music clubs on the block.It's the perfect spot for local artists and designers to sell their wares and I have known quite a few people who have had sale tables here.  The vendors here sell all types of things from jewelry to hair accessories to housewares. About a year ago, I was excited to find a small handmade hat here that is a perfect costume accessory once parades and festivals roll around.  Please note: a lot of the vendors do not want pictures of their wares taken, so be sure to ask if you want to send a picture to someone with a gift idea. I spotted some hand painted coasters here, that I thought a friend would like, but the vendor didn't want me taking pictures. Totally understood and worth noting.

Really good lunch specials. I usually get the fried chicken and corn grits. The serving is usually way more than a lunch portion and I always have left overs. Although Zea is a chain, it's still a good place to stop for lunch.  I feel bad for writing such a short review, but there really is nothing more to say about the place!

I have been a Fleurty shopper for years and I am always impressed with the products and service at this shop.  I was recently in the market to pick up some NOLA themed gifts for an out of town friend, so of course Fleurty Girl was my first stop. I wasn't in the market for t shirts, because buying clothes for other people can sometimes be tricky, so the girl working helped me on finding some other gifts that my friend would like. I got a few New Orleans themed candles, a tumbler and some stationary that my friend is sure to love. I was able to construct an entire New Orleans gift basket with the goodies I found here.  Fleurty Girl is your "one stop shop" for all things New Orleans and you are sure to find something that the New Orleans lover in your life will like.

"Some girl came in here and now we're on Yelp!"  That's what the bartender said to me when I told her that I had recently heard about this dive through a friend of mine. That friend and the girl who put Pete's on Yelp are one in the same. I have Holly G. to thank for this latest discovery.  What an awesome place! Totally unassuming bar located in the middle of a neighborhood. So unassuming, in fact, that one of the people I went with once lived 2 blocks away on the same street and had no idea it was there. It's like a secret clubhouse! It doesn't even have a sign!  Really cool people and the bartender is really nice and friendly. Loved the jukebox. Got in there and played a little Beatles and Elvis. Yeah, it was that kind of night. There weren't a lot of people in there and it wasn't super smoky so that's also a big plus.  Hours vary depending on the crowd. The bartender said sometimes they will close at midnight and sometimes they will close later depending on how many people are in there. I will definitely be back!

I had a date here once!  Sorry Scott S.  But, seriously!  I danced and everything!  This place is amazing.  How is it I had forgotten about it until now?  It's along the lines of Irvin Mayfield's as far as music and ambiance goes.  Never been there?  Allow me to explain.  The atmosphere is fantastic.  Really upscale and nice. Comfy seats, a good crowd and good music. You don't feel out of place in nice jeans, but trust me, dress up.    Jeremy Davenport plays here every Thursday, Friday and Saturday.  His shows start at 5:30 on Thursdays and 9 on Fridays and Saturdays and it's always a good time.  Sure, the drinks aren't cheap, but it's almost as if they were it would bring the place down, you know?  Like... if you take a girl out to dinner and she orders a salad, it's almost like, "What's the point?".  Ok, I'm rambling.  Do you like cool music, like The Rat Pack and big band stuff?  Do you like to dance?  Well, then get to the Davenport!

I am not exaggerating when I say that Vacherie might not only be my winner for best Coolinary experience 2016, but it might be one of my favorite places of all time. Of all of the places I went to for Coolinary, Vacherie did everything perfectly. For starters, the atmosphere was romantic with it's dimly lit dining room and cozy feel. It's the perfect spot for a date.  We made reservations, but this turned to be unnecessary and there were plenty of places to sit when we got here at 7:30. Our waiter was extremely friendly and took our drink orders right away as we looked over the menu. I knew exactly what I was getting from the Coolinary menu, so I was excited to get started.  We did go off menu and start with some blackened gator bites. I am a sucker for gator and these were good. They had a little spice to them and they melted in my mouth. They even had a little sauce on the side for dipping- I'm not sure what the sauce was, but I liked it.   For my starter I got the house salad with balsamic dressing. This was a large salad that was packed with tomatoes, cucumbers, carrots and other goodies. I love that they put the dressing on the side so that I could add as much or as little as I wanted. Everything was fresh and tasty and I was already impressed.  For my entree, I (naturally) got the shrimp and grits. Shrimp and grits is my favorite dish and this version was incredible. First of all, the serving was huge! Vacherie was beyond generous with this portion and if the Coolinary serving was even half of this I would have been happy. Fat tail-on shrimp in delicious , creamy grits served with French bread rounds. There were SO MANY shrimp- at least 10 and maybe 12. The sauce was perfection and the dish was full of flavor. For the first time in a long time I couldn't finish it all. That's right, there was so much food I was struggling. Just when you thought Vacherie was done, they also had pork smothered collard greens on the side. I love greens and adding pork just brought it all to another level. This wasn't just some puny portion, this was a generous serving of greens. I was in heaven.  I must have managed to save a little bit of room because when my final course of pecan pie came out, I was all over it. Pecan pie is my favorite pie and I have it so rarely, but I decided to just dive in and really enjoy myself. This was a generous slice served with whipped cream on top. I think this pie must have been made from scratch because the pecans were whole and the crust was nice and flaky.  I loved Vacherie so much that I think that I'm going to have to go back and get this special again during restaurant week. Everything was perfect from beginning to end. Our waiter checked on us regularly to make sure that we were enjoying everything and that we liked our drinks. This might be one of my new favorite places and not only will I be returning, I will be telling EVERYONE about this restaurant.

Considering that I live literally down the street from this place, it's amazing I have never been here until today. I always passed it and I guess I assumed that it was just a little dinky cafe. Uh...I was wrong.  I stopped in today for lunch. There was no wait and I was quickly seated. I had sneaked a peek of the menu online, and to my amazement, I saw that they have a Cuban sandwich! I have been searching for a freaking Cuban sandwich on the Westbank for YEARS! I decided to get the Cubano and I had the jalapeño cheese grits as my side. I thought I would go a little exotic and a little Southern for lunch today. The sandwich was so good and did not disappoint. It was the right kind of bread and pressed to perfection. It could have used a BIT more mustard (I'm a freak for the stuff), but other than that it was a winner. The grits were good as well. Nice and creamy and not spicy at all with a lot of flavor. I also liked that I got a big portion of them and I had enough leftovers for a nice munch later on.  Another thing I noticed that this place has margaritas that aren't made from a mix- something else I have been scouring the Westbank for! I didn't get one today, but I will definitely go back and try one, as they are only $5- "all day, every day" is what it says on the menu. Also, on Wednesday nights bottled wine is 20% off.  What a little gem of a place this turned out to be! I will absolutely go back and explore more of the menu.

I do not make it to this fantastic music hot spot nearly enough. That's a real crime considering that I have never had a bad time here.  Most of the time there is a cover because there is an awesome band playing, but this is one of the few places where I actually don't mind paying a cover. The drinks are pretty cheap and the crowd is so fun. When I was in here there was a band playing that was a nice mix of all kinds of characters. The crowd had a good time dancing along to the music and the atmosphere was just happy.   I can't wait to go back!

After reading all of the fantastic reviews of Hong Minh, I knew I had to try it.  We stopped in for lunch on a Saturday. There was no one else here and we were seated immediately. They have lunch specials, which is an entree that comes with pork fried rice or steamed rice, but sadly they don't do the pork fried rice on the weekends. I decided to go with a bowl of the wonton noodle soup. The soup was a good portion and for $7 it was perfect for lunch. It had SO MUCH flavor and I was thrilled that the wontons were large and the noodles were plentiful. This might be the best wonton soup I have had since Pho Tau Bay- it's a definite must. My dining companion got the shrimp fried rice and it was a really large portion and plenty enough to take home for later.  The staff here is obviously all family and they are really kind and attentive. The place itself is very much "no frills", but the food more than makes up for that. Don't be intimidated that the place is located in a sketchy looking strip mall, it's some of the best Chinese food in the area. I will be back.

4 stars bumped up to 5 because of one word: hospitality.  Decided to stop here on date night. We had been craving raw oysters, and you really can't beat the price of the ones here.   As soon as we walked in, we were immediately greeted and told to sit anywhere. The waiter was quick to come over with food and drink menus, took our drink orders and left us to look at the menu. We started with a dozen raw oysters which came out quickly. They were fat and juicy and really good. They definitely hit the spot.  For my entree, I decided to try the Cuban sandwich on French with a side of cheese grits. We also got a side of alligator hash to try. Alligator hash is hash browns with alligator sausage in it. It was good, but truthfully it could have used a bit more sausage. My sandwich was really good and huge. It was basically a sandwich and a half and I was happy to have some left over. The grits were also very well prepared and hit the spot.  Now, the sandwich was good, but it was probably 4 stars. The reason I'm giving 5 stars is because the waiter was super attentive and regularly stopped by to make sure that we had everything we needed. Also, the manager (or maybe the owner) came over to our table, thanked us for coming in and asked if we were enjoying our meal and made sure that we didn't need anything. The same man also told us goodbye when we were walking out of the door. Hospitality goes a long way in my book. So often I have been to places and had a decent dining experience, but the waiter is no where to be seen and I am left needing a drink refill or an extra knife. I was not left wanting for anything and I felt extremely welcome.   I will definitely return to Blind Pelican, not only for the food, but for the friendly atmosphere.

I had a photo shoot here and this is a review of the aesthetics of the place.  I'd always passed this hotel whenever I was driving down Poydras, and I always thought that it looked so rich and regal. I just love the European feel of the outside with the statues and the door man.  Upon arriving, parking was a bit of a trick. The photographer, who was staying here, told me that valet and parking over night was costing him $40. Since I never stay at hotels in New Orleans, I really don't know if this is typical or not, but if it is- whoa. I ended up paying a meter and parking on a side street.  Walking in, the hotel is just as gorgeous inside as it is outside. It feels as if you are on a European vacation. There are gorgeous chairs and sofas in the lobby and I noticed that some people are just sitting and reading, which speaks well to how comfortable the place is.  On my way to the elevator, a hotel employee was quick to run ahead of me and press the button for me. I thought that that was a nice touch. The room was small, but not anything overly spectacular. We decided to head up to the 9th floor and do our photo shoot in the pool/spa area.  The pool area is lovely. There's a nice covered cabana, if you just want to lay out. There's a hot tub and although the pool is small, it's a rooftop pool, so the view of the city makes up for it. Also, I liked that towels are provided poolside. All in all the whole area is gorgeous. There's also a gym, if you would like to work out while you are staying there.

I mean...ok. Yeah. Um...sure.  Miracle on Fulton doesn't really do it for me. Am I missing something? It's basically Celebration in the Oaks with a lot less celebrating. It's free, so that's good but it's nothing overly special. It's nice for what it is, but a little cheesy. I'm not a "fake snow/colored tree" kinda girl. This is Louisiana. Give me a fake green tree with zero snow and that' fine. It's a nice place to visit, but if you have seen this attraction one year, you have basically seen it every year.

The crazy thing is that I come to this Winn Dixie fairly regularly, but I always forget to check in! Hence my belated review.  This store is okay. It's not really my first choice when I am looking for something  grocery wise in the area. Some of the stuff here can be a bit overpriced and they often don't have what I am looking for. If you are looking for fancy beer or cheese, skip this place and head over to Rouses.  I have found the staff pretty friendly, but during the day they don't keep a ton of registers open during the day because the crowd that comes in is smaller.

Time for an update and I'm bumping them up a star.  The place is still packed, but it's not OVERLY packed as I remember. Everything is neatly organized and I loved the extensive selection of vintage hats in the back. The staff is super friendly and nice and very welcoming. Here you will find dresses and clothes from every era- 40's and 50's to 90's. You are sure to find something that will suit you here.  Be sure to check in the back for wedding and prom dresses.

Compared to some of the other cemeteries in the area, this cemetery seems pretty "low key" and unassuming. It doesn't have a lot of fancy monuments. It doesn't have tourists walking through and taking pictures to bring home. It's just a nice cemetery to walk through and admire on a nice day.  The one or two times I have been here the big gate hasn't been open and you have to work your way in through a small rusted gate that's on the side. A lot of the graves here are pretty old and while some are falling apart, a lot of them are kept up nicely.  It's not a "destination" spot, but it's definitely worth a look.

I've driven across this bridge by accident a few times. I'm not super familiar with the area and I figure my intended destination is on the other side of this bridge and it rarely is.  On the occasions that I have crossed this bridge on purpose, it hasn't been all that bad, even though sometimes people drive like maniacs and I'm convinced that I am going to go off the side, even though that's impossible. The bridge definitely does need some work. Teneha hit the nail on the head when she called it "rickety" and whenever I cross it, I half expect the whole thing to come tumbling down. I mean- if there is a big truck on the bridge, the whole structure shakes and shifts. Yikes!  This isn't a bad bridge, but I'm glad I don't have to cross it regularly.

This was the perfect place for a quick iced coffee stop when I was running around in the area and in need of caffeine.  The shop is small and located behind New Orleans Hamburger and Seafood and can be tricky to find if it's your first time. The barista was friendly and the coffee was really good. A large cost a little over $3, which is a good price point for the area. I'm not usually a big beignet person, but chocolate beignets intrigue me, so I will probably be back.

I wish I had come early enough to get a picture of the gorgeous view of the city, but I was here just as the sun was setting.  New Orleans has been really knocking it out of the park with rooftop hang outs as of late. Between Alto and Hot Tin, you can get some really good views on both sides of town. This is a nice spot- there is a bar area that has a tropical type feel, a pool (that might be just for people staying at the Ace Hotel), a kitchen that serves food and plenty of space for lounging.  I was here with some friends for a post-work cocktail and I was delighted because I didn't even know this place was here. The bar was pretty crowded, but luckily there were some waitresses who were taking orders, so we didn't have to wait in line. I ended up getting a frozen Mai Tai that was really good and had a nice kick to it. A "large" was still pretty small, but the drink didn't taste like a mix, so I was happy. I didn't have any food, but the food my friends had- a skirt steak and a burger looked really good, so I will have to dine in next time.  This is really going to be a great spot to hang out, especially when the weather gets a little cooler. I can't wait to sip a fancy cocktail under the stars once fall arrives.

With time comes wisdom and not only do I "do" Wal Mart now (I love a deal), but this Wal Mart is pretty good. The staff is always friendly and helpful, they have good deals on household items and beauty things and the check out line moves quickly, especially if you keep your item number low.  I was most recently in here eyeing up the bicycles because I want to start riding. I didn't need anything fancy- just something nice to get me from point A to point B. The man working in the bike department was extremely helpful and let me look at the bike I wanted to buy and "try it out", so that I knew it would be right for me. He was so friendly and helpful and he made the process a breeze. I purchased my bike here and I love it!  I've also noticed that makeup products are about $2 to $3 cheaper than you would pay at a drugstore, so this is where I get my makeup basics like pressed powder and things like that. The only recent frustrating experience I had was when I was buying a whole cart full of items and the cashier came to one item that had apparently been discontinued and her register locked and I couldn't complete my purchase because the manager was at lunch and she's the only one with the key to fix the machine. That was a mess, but that's the only issue I've had here.  Tip: if you can, do the Wal Mart thing in the afternoon on a weekday- there are a lot fewer people and you'll be in and out in no time. I don't come to Wal Mart super often, but when I do I'm pleased with the experience.

H&M is really nothing special. It's cheap clothing at a cheap price. I don't know why so many locals got so excited about this place. I guess it's just because it's new. Meanwhile, if you wanted to, you could just go shopping on the H&M website. But uh...I guess people didn't realize that.  H&M is located in a prime spot in downtown New Orleans, and to me, it just seems out of place. If I was a tourist, I wouldn't want to waste my time shopping at a huge national chain store, but I guess that's me.  The clothing style is basically modern casual tops, bottoms and dresses for girls. They have stuff for men and kids, but I honestly didn't check that stuff out when I went. Honestly, you can find clothing that is just as nice or nicer at one of the little shops on Magazine St., and by shopping there you are supporting local business.

I like this Tuesday Morning a lot. It's big and they offer the typical home decor type of stuff.  On this day, I was here looking for a housewarming gift for a relative and the woman working was able to help me locate some bar stools that will be perfect for the new place. I like that everything here is neatly organized- it made it very simple to find what I want. Also, because we are heading into the fall season, they have a nice selection of fall items and even some stuff out for Christmas. I will definitely return to pick up some more house stuff, especially when my kitchen remodeling is done.

I stopped in here for a lunch meeting and this is actually one of the few Vietnamese places, on the Westbank, that I had never visited before!  First things first- parking is just dumb around here because the place is right by the courthouse. "Is there not a lot of parking?", you might be asking. Oh no, there are TONS of empty spaces, but you better be prepared to feed a meter. "I don't pay to park on the Westbank!", says I! I ended up parking a few blocks away for free and enjoyed a lovely 2 block walk from where I parked to the restaurant.  When I arrived, I was struck at how large the place is. There are some big rooms in the back, if they ever get super packed or if someone decides to have a party here. While it was filled with a good crowd of jurors, I had no problem quickly finding where my dining companions were seated.  Looking over the menu, I noticed that they had a good variety of both Vietnamese dishes and more basic dishes like tomato and avocado salad and grilled chicken. I had actually read some reviews of this place before I came in, and after reading Bobby B's review of the Pho, I decided to stick with a Vermicelli salad bowl with pork.  This was a good sized salad with a lot of nice grilled pork, carrots, cucumbers and Vermicelli noodles on top of lettuce with fish sauce on the side. It was simple, but really good and had a lot of flavor. The pork had a really nice glaze on it that I enjoyed.  All in all Thanh Thanh was fine by me. I would definitely go back if I found myself in the neighborhood.

This is a cool hotel. When I got here it took me forever to find the room where I was to have a photo shoot. I had to ask the maid exactly where the room was. I ended up going to the floor, and then I had to walk through an outdoor patio, through another set of doors and there I found the room. Apparently it was some sort of suite and the suites are by a courtyard.  The room was really big. I was impressed. The sitting area was huge and felt like a living room with a lot of sofas and a big tv. There are slide doors separating the bedroom area from the rest of the suite which is convenient if you are ready to go to bed and the person you are traveling with isn't.  Minus one star because the room was a trick to find and minus another HUGE star because I was there for three hours, parking cost me $20 and they only take CASH! What a pain! I had to have the photographer spot me $20 and then pay him back because I only had a credit card on me (Dumb. I always have cash on me now.). What type of French Quarter hotel doesn't take a card? Really odd.

What have I been doing with myself? This restaurant is practically in my neighborhood and has been for years and I am only just now trying it. I guess don't eat on the Westbank nearly enough.  So, I get these weird food obsessions. At the moment one of them happens to be Mediterranean food and all that entails. I came here for lunch to check it out and started with my basic hummus and pita appetizer. The hummus came in a very generous serving mixed with olive oil and the pita was warm and perfect.  For my main meal I got my usual beef shawarma plate. The servings here are HUGE and prices are more than reasonable. For $11 you get a huge serving of beef, a nice sized salad and, of course, hummus. By the way, am I the only one who mixes the hummus into the beef? Is that just me or is that a thing? On this particular day I was starving, so I all but finished the plate in one sitting. Thank God I run three miles a day or I would have serious problems.  The guy who was working here was fantastic and really attentive. He made sure that we had everything we needed and that I liked everything. When I ordered the hummus appetizer and then the schwarma, the waiter offered to sub the hummus on the schwarma plate for rice. Super nice but I'm a hummus freak, so the more the merrier. I will absolutely return and I'm so excited this place is so close to me.

I love Baskin Robbins when I want a specific treat.  I don't really go for the ice cream, itself.  Honestly, it's a smidge overpriced and blue bell is just as good and cheaper.  I love to get the cappuccino drinks here.  Get them without the whipped cream, if you are interested in cutting out a few calories.  That's just a good life rule...always go "no whip".  Anyway, they also have awesome ice cream cakes.  I had one for my birthday (chocolate chip) and it was great!  If you sign up for the birthday club, you get a free scoop of ice cream on your birthday and a discount on an ice cream cake for your birthday, too!  I've been a member since I was a kid.

A friend and I were Uptown and avoiding parades, during the Mardi Gras season, when we decided that we really needed to eat. Since all of the good restaurants on St. Charles were blocked by dumb floats (ha), we ventured off the beaten path in search of sustenance. In other words, we went to Magazine Street.  Restaurants on Magazine have this annoying habit of closing at a reasonable hour- 10pm, so we were hoping to find something that was open a little later. That's when we noticed the glowing "open" sign in the window of Pita Pit. I'm not usually a fast food person (unless it's Taco Bell, don't judge me), but we were super hungry so we stopped in.  Pita Pit is basically a Subway for pitas instead of sandwiches. I am obsessed with comparing places to Subway, but here we are. You walk up and tell them what kind of pita you want, and they add whatever "fixins" you want to it. I got the cheeseburger pita with lettuce and tomato with a side of chips and a drink.  The pita was actually really good. I think that pitas are supposed to be healthy, but I nipped that in the bud with my cheese/meat combo of DOOM! There was a good mix of veggies and cheeseburger in it, so I liked it.  Pita Pit is what it is. It's a fast food place, but it's pretty good in pinch. I can see the appeal of it, especially since they deliver all over uptown and they are open until 1am, so I'm sure they do a good late night business.

At a Yelp elite event earlier this year I was lucky enough to win a $100 gift card to Mila, so we decided to have a date night here recently.  I made reservations through Open Table, but this proved to be completely unnecessary because we walked in at 7:30 and there wasn't a soul in the place. We were seated in a really cool booth and we looked over the menu. We had $100 to spend, and the menu wasn't that expensive, so we decided to go all out.  For my starter I got the charcuterie board which came with assorted cheeses, venison pâté and some fancy mustards. This was such a yummy board and it was plenty enough for two. I don't know what the cheeses were, but they were really good and the mustard was a perfect addition to the venison.  Next I had the bouquet of organic greens salad. This was a salad that came with assorted greens, radishes, sesame seeds, feta cheese and topped with a light dressing. This was delicious. It was fresh and refreshing and was a nice balance the the charcuterie board I had just enjoyed.  For my entree I got the Parmesan Salmon Blue Crab and Brie Pearl Pasta. This was an interesting dish. The salmon was nicely cooked and it was flaky with good flavor. The pearl pasta was unlike anything I had ever had before- it was almost like rice in pasta form. I didn't taste much of the blue crab, but I still enjoyed the dish.  Finally, we got an order of bread pudding to go. I liked that the put the "sauces" on the side, so that it wouldn't get soggy. While it wasn't the best bread pudding I've ever had, it was really good reheated and we enjoyed it.  I liked Mila a lot, and even though I believe they are closing soon, I enjoyed my time here.

I had been wanting to check this place out for a while, but I never really knew what it was. Then when I asked on facebook where I could get plantain chips, I was tipped off to this place.  As soon as I walked in, I was pleasantly surprised. It's a Latin American grocery store! Not only do they carry the things that a normal market would carry, but they also carry a bunch of Latin American treats! I saw all kind of things from different candies and snacks to soft drinks. They had coconut water and juice and, of course, that really good Coca Cola with the real sugar in it! I picked up a bag of plaintain chips and it only cost $2.  In the back, they have a section where you can get hot food to go, so I will definitely have to try that. They also have a huge butcher section with a HUGE meat selection, including whole pigs! Now, I don't really have a current need for a whole pig, but they are there if you need them.  The store is just packed with stuff and I will definitely be going back and picking up some goodies that aren't as easy to come by at a Winn Dixie or Rouse's.

Oooh wee! It was hot out there, y'all and I ain't talking about the shrimp and jalapeño cheese grits I had. That sun was shining. There was nothing but open space. I was glad I wore sunblock. I was mad I wore jeans (serious rookie mistake!).  This was my first time checking out the Seafood Fest and it didn't disappoint. My only real complaint is that it was in an area with no tree coverage in the middle of the summer. I think having it in the fall would be better, but what do I know? I was able to sample a few things, so I'm going to review each one by one.  PJ's: 5/5 stars- This was our first stop. I got a nice iced coffee for $5 and if you saved the cup, you get could get a refill for $3. Considering this was one of the few booths with a huge fan and tables, this spot ended up being a lifesaver. Bonus points for the free coffee coupons they were handing out.  Lüke: 5/5- I got the shrimp and jalapeño cheese grits and they were amazing! For $8 they gave a nice size serving and it was served nice and hot. My favorite dish of the day.  Saltwater grill: I can't rate it because I wasn't the one who ate it, but for $5 you get a really big alligator sausage stick. It looked tasty and you can't beat that deal with a sausage stick.  Drago's: 3/5- We got the half- dozen charbroiled oysters and they were just okay. The oysters themselves were TINY. I know this is supposed to just be a sample, but I was underwhelmed and for $9 it didn't feel like it was worth it.  Dirty Dishes: 5/5- We had the dirty mac which was smoked gouda mac and cheese with crawfish and tasso. I have written a separate review for Dirty Dishes and this dish before- I am definitely a fan. They gave a huge serving and the cheese was nicely melted over the whole dish and it was quite tasty. For $8, this might be one of the better deals at the fest.  I also stopped by the Barefoot wine tent for a few samples and I really enjoyed them. Also, the misting tent was a total lifesaver. It's amazing how good semi-cool water can feel when you have been standing under the boiling sun for 45 minutes. We didn't stop to listen to the bands, but I liked what I heard and they sounded great.  All in all it was a good time. Next year I will remember to wear a sun hat and shorts and a tank top, so that I can stay cool. It would be nice if they moved this fest to the fall or at least under the trees where Brunch Fest was, but I know beggars can't be choosers when there is a festival nearly every weekend.

I seem to always pass this place on weekends and hear fantastic music flowing from this bar but it is usually so packed (lucky them!) that fighting a crowd just doesn't appeal to me when there are so many other options.  I was able to stop in here when a friend and I decided we were in the mood for sake. I really liked it here. There was a small band (a singer and her accompaniment) playing when we sat down and looked over the drink menu. They have a HUGE selection of cold sake. I'm not usually a fan, but I tried one that was a little sweet and fruity and I was pleasantly surprised by it. They have such an extensive collection of sake and Japanese beer that you are bound to find something to enjoy, no matter what your tastes.

First of all, they sell the same balls here that you find in ball pits at Chucky Cheese and places like that. YOU CAN CREATE YOUR OWN BALL PIT! I want to buy bags and bags of them and fill a whole room with them and have my own ball pit. I think this is also how 5 year old's think.  I stopped in here looking for kid stuff. I hadn't set foot in a Toys R Us since I was a kid myself, so it was interesting to see it from the "other side" as it were. The place is huge and carries pretty much everything your little rugrat could ever want. I really like that everything is organized by section. There's a section for little kids (Playskool, Fisher Price), a section with Barbie stuff, another with Star Wars stuff, Hello Kitty stuff, WWE, Iron Man, etc. You get the point.  I went on a weekday afternoon, so the place was pretty much abandoned. I saw maybe 2 kids the entire time I was there and I didn't see anyone working the floor. Everything was pretty easy to find and well priced.  I can imagine that this place gets ridiculous on the weekends and during holidays, so if you need to venture into this place, plan accordingly.

After reading so many great reviews about the deli here, I knew that I had to stop in and check this place out. I think it was Charles H.'s picture of that amazing Lindy that finally pushed me over the edge.  First of all, there are two huge parking lots, which for a business in this area is appreciated. It's nice being able to just park next to a place and walk in. It's a small luxury, but an important one. Walking in, I was so blown away at how gorgeous this space is. In the front, there is a nice selection of wine and other liquors. Further towards the back there is a refrigerator with beer.  I headed toward the back where there is a large deli area with tons of seating. You walk up and order and then they call you when your food is ready. They have lunch specials, but I knew I wanted that Lindy- a sandwich  loaded with oven-roasted turkey, Swiss, housemade coleslaw, tomato and Russian dressing on 7-grain bread. I also got a side of Zapp's, but who cares? The sandwich came out after a brief wait and WOW. Let me just say- that this sandwich exceeded all expectations. It had a ton of yummy turkey and cole slaw on it. The dressing was amazing and the bread was fresh. Also, the sandwich was huge. I took a picture, but I'm not even sure I did it justice. If I hadn't been starving, I would have taken half of it home, but all bets were off once I took a bite of this thing. It was so good and the dressing really put this sandwich over the top. For $11, I could have probably gotten two meals out of it, which is how I judge a place and it's pricing. What an amazing lunch!  I will definitely return to Martin's and if you find yourself hungry and ANYWHERE near this place stop in!

This place takes the headache out of banking. Always in and out really quickly. Knowledgeable staff will take care of whatever you need. When making transactions, I've never had to wait in line longer than 5 minutes.

Storyland is a really cool addition to City Park.  It's all of the fairy tales comes to life! There is a pirate ship, Cinderella's carriage, a princess castle and much more. I loved going here as a kid and I still have my special "key" that I was given so that I could hear the story of each special character.   Be sure to call ahead and see if they are open before you go, because the hours seem to be odd and I think that on certain days they close earlier than on other days and they close for inclement weather, etc.

Uh...ordering drinks took forever because the two bartenders can't handle the crowd and someone's dog peed on the floor RIGHT IN FRONT OF ME.  The owner of the dog made no move to clean it up.  Disgusting.  If you are going to bring your dog out, please make sure the thing is properly trained.

Suzette's calls itself a "romantic boutique" and you will definitely find all that that phrase would entail here.  This is a great place that sells everything a woman would need to feel her best and sexiest.  They carry lingerie, including fantastic honeymoon lingerie (white robes, slips and nighties).  They also carry various "fun" outfits, stockings, makeup and the like.    I was amazed by the amount of Halloween costumes this place has!  Everything from the "sexy" looks to the more elaborate.  They carry all sizes and they have a fantastic selection.
