The staff is really helpful with anything you may need, and will help with fittings, if you would like a second opinion on a certain outfit.  They also carry what I will refer to as "personal" items.  Just head to the back and go behind the curtain.

This isn't a bad place.  They serve salads, burgers and cheese fries.  It's pretty much a few steps up from bar food, but that's not a bad thing.  The staff is very efficient and attentive.  When I went, I got a burger.  It wasn't anything overly special, but I liked it.  This would be a good place to come before you head out for a night out, as the place is right next to a bar (and also HAS a bar) and the food is well priced.

Well, after years of trying I finally made it to Horinoya. I had been here a few times in the past but they were either packed or just about to close. Thankfully, I was extremely pleased with my experience after I ate.  We decided to check this place out on possibly the best night ever: a night when the Pelicans were in the playoffs. It was 8 and the place was dead. Perfect!  We were seated in the front dining room and I was immediately excited because the decor and atmosphere made me feel like I was in Japan (not that I have ever been, but I've seen movies. ;)). Looking over the menu, it was hard to decide exactly what to start with.  We decided to get the sashimi appetizer to start. It came with a delicious assortment of super fresh cuts of salmon, tuna and white fish. Trust me when I say that this is some of the freshest sashimi that I think that I have ever had. The flavors were amazing. After that, we got the wasabi shumai which was pork wrapped in a wasabi wrapper. It was great and had a fantastic kick to it. I like a little spice, so this was right up my alley.  For our entree we went a little nuts and not only got the tuna tataki, but we also got the  dynamite roll, squid, rainbow roll and Philly roll. Out of all of these rolls, I would have to say that the dynamite roll and the rainbow roll were my favorites. Once again, the freshness of the fish added something special to this dish and made the entire experience special. The tuna tataki was yummy as well and I liked that the portion was small and made for a nice little "taste".  All in all, I loved Horinoya and I can't wait to return. The wait staff was attentive, the food was delectable and the entire experience was great. Now I know what people mean when they say that this is the best sushi in New Orleans. After my experience here, I might have to agree.

Oh my God! I had seriously forgotten about my experience with American Taxi until John's review!  During YSB we decided to take a cab to the event on St. Claude in order to be safe. Well, driving might have been a better idea. The driver we had was INSANE! He was speeding and running red lights and swerving in and out of lanes. It was seriously scary. They are getting two stars because I made it to my destination in one unharmed piece.  From now on, I will ONLY cab with United. Every other cab company I have ever experienced has been sub par.

First of all, I want to start by saying I don't know why I do this to myself. I once again ended up at a bar on Bourbon St. Gee, I wonder how it went.  Well, it sucked. It was Razzoo's without the charm. The music was pretty good and the shot girl was super nice, but the guy on stage who was pumping up the crowd needs to work on his act. It wasn't really entertaining. Of course, in places like this, you gotta take what you can get.  So, why the two stars?? Uh... $6.75 for a beer is the reason. It was Abita Amber, not some fancy import. I know it's the quarter, but come on.

Stopped in here for a bit during French Quarter Fest. The bartender was really nice and I liked that all of the doors were open letting fresh air into the place.  I didn't stay long, but they do seem to have a nice selection of absinthe and the bartender sounded like she knew what she was talking about when someone asked about them. The decor is a little grimy, but it's not terrible for a FQ spot.

This is such a cool hangout for beer lovers.  Not only can you get delicious beer that is super fresh, but you can get NOLA brews that are only available in the tap room. It's a great excuse to spend an evening "taste testing" some of the best beers around.  The staff is super friendly and knowledgeable, and although the tap room itself it small, there are plenty of seats at picnic style tables. When I stopped in on Friday I tried the Pineapple Habanero IPA, which is a beer with a little spice to it (and a tap room exclusive) and I also had the Prytania Porter, which was dark and delicious.  The beers are constantly rotating, so I will definitely be back to see what they are going to brew next.

I guess I'm old fashioned when it comes to banking, but I like to deal with humans. I am not a fan of dealing with a machine when I have to make a deposit. I know, I'm weird and I'm living in the stone age.  As a result, I rate banks on how fast the lines move and how quickly and I can get in and out of the bank. The lines here move quickly and the tellers are great. I was here on an weekday afternoon and there weren't a lot of people in line and the two tellers who were working did a great job at getting everyone through in a timely manner. I was just here to make a deposit, so I wasn't doing anything earth shattering, but my needs were handled with ease and I can't ask for much better than that.

This was more of a 3.5 star experience.  A friend and I stopped in here 2 days after Christmas for a quick lunch. The place was dead, except for one or two other tables. We were here for the sushi, so we looked over things as we waited on our drinks. That's one strange thing about this restaurant: they serve burgers and sandwiches and they serve sushi. It's like the owners weren't sure what they wanted the place to be.  Anyway, we ordered the Philly roll, the Metry roll and the Rainbow roll. After we ordered we had to wait a really long time. Normally this wouldn't be a big deal, but there was no one here and we felt that the wait was way too long considering the place was dead. When the food finally came, it was pretty good. My favorite was the Metry roll because it had a bit of spice to it which gave it a nice kick. The other two rolls were pretty good, but nothing spectacular.  I might come back, but I am going to skip the sushi next time. There are better places in Metairie with more sushi selection and tastier rolls.

I'm not sure how to feel about this place. On one hand, the clothing is gorgeous. On the other hand, I felt less than welcome when I shopped here.  I was in here looking around and hoping to find some new clothes for my New Year wardrobe. I was dressed down, having spent the entire day running errands and finishing Christmas shopping. Upon walking in, the woman working kind of looked me over and didn't say "hi" or anything. However, I did notice that she greeted other customers. I didn't think much of it and I just looked around as I normally do, but I did find it kind of weird.  The clothing here is lovely and they have a wide selection of things from casual to dressy. I saw a lovely red dress that I am actually considering purchasing just so I have it for any fancy event that might come up. The clothes are a little pricier, but I can tell that they're worth it because the quality is outstanding.  Because they're located in old Metairie, I would recommend dressing up a little when shopping here. Otherwise, you're on your own as far as help is concerned.

I stopped in here while doing some last minute Christmas shopping and I just love the vibe!  This is a shop that features gifts by local artists. A lot of it has a "New Orleans" theme, but nothing is gaudy or tacky like some other shops. While browsing, I happened to find some oysters and a voodoo doll toothpick holder made by Yelp's very own Re! It's always cool finding her art out in the world. Although I didn't buy anything on this go round, I did see a lot of things that will make fantastic gifts and I will be returning to spend my money. The owner was really friendly and asked if I needed help finding anything, which I always appreciate.

Who doesn't love a little bling?  This place is heaven for anyone who loves something shiny and loves to match their necklace to their top. As others have said, everything here is organized by color and while they have purses and clothing, I always go for the jewelry. One of my favorite spots for costume jewelry is So Good, but Charming Charlie is a close second.  I stopped in here with the intention of just looking around, but of course that never happens and I ended up getting some cute pink earrings that will go great with any summer ensemble. Another thing I love about CC is you can get hair accessories here as well- they have a nice little selection of tiaras for your wedding or everyday tiara needs.  True, the jewelry isn't the greatest quality in the world, but if it falls apart or you lose something you won't feel terrible about it, because it's all pretty cheap.

We were in the area when we decided to stop in here and grab a bite to eat. The setup here is pretty simple: you order what you want at the counter and you wait at a table. I like that they have dishes to choose from or you can just build your own, if you desire. I decided to keep it simple and I got a salad that was big and packed with olives, cucumbers, tomatoes, feta and onions. It was great and was filling without being heavy and I especially liked the vinaigrette that it was topped with. David had the spaghetti and meatballs, which he said was delicious.  This restaurant also has a really nice beer selection, so I was pleased that I was able to enjoy a nice IPA with my meal. The dishes are well priced, the food is good and the staff is friendly. I'll be back.

I loooove this place. I think this might be my new favorite coffee in the city.  I recently discovered this cute little "sip and go" (as I'm calling it) after hanging out at Courtyard Brewery. I had heard people rave about the yummy coffee that is just around the block, so I knew I had to check it out. I had never had the opportunity to try French Truck before they opened this store front, so I was excited to go on a coffee adventure.  The store itself is pretty basic. There are a couple of tables and chairs, but the idea is to come and get what you need and go. Since I am a fan of iced coffee, that's what I've gotten both times that I have been here. I am such a fan of this velvety coffee. First of all, not only is the coffee itself ridiculously good and packed with flavor, but they serve it over crushed ice, which just adds to the magic of the brew.  I don't claim to be a coffee connoisseur by any means, but this coffee is nice and smooth and doesn't have any bitter under taste that I have found in other coffees. French Truck roasts everything super fresh, and the care really shows in the flavor. I also liked that the coffee is potent without being overly strong.  I will return to French Truck. This place might actually get me to try espresso!

We stopped in here to see one of the cover bands that frequently play the Metairie bar scene. It's not a bad place. Legends is pretty big and gets pretty packed when a band is playing. The bartenders are quick to get drinks distributed, even with a large crowd. The sound for the music isn't all that wonderful, but for a bar it's pretty good.  I wouldn't mind checking this place out on a "slower" kind of night.

What do you get when you cross a bike shop with an art gallery? Apparently you get Lil Deb's Snow World.  I had zero clue that this place existed until David's aunt suggested we check it out. It's literally located in the back of a bike shop/art gallery right on Lafayette. We walked through and ordered, which was easy enough. I got the strawberry cheesecake snowball, just to mix it up a bit. I really liked it- the ice was nice and fine and they were really generous with the juice.  There are a few seats inside and there is a picnic table outside, so that you can eat your treat on site. They also have other snowball stand basics such as nachos, pickles and things like that.

Ok, so just before I start you should know that I have been to this place twice in one week because it is THAT good.  Driving up to this Cafe, it almost feels as if you are in a storybook and you happened upon a wondrous cottage that serves delicious food. The restaurant is actually a small house located in the middle of a neighborhood. It's surrounded by a picket fence and has a nice porch. You almost feel weird walking in, because it feels like you are walking into someone's home.  Upon entering the first time, I was greeted by a kind woman named Betty and told to sit anywhere. Looking over the menu, I realized that this place has everything from poboys to fried catfish to stuffed chicken. I decided on the club and I was delighted when it came because it was HUGE and was accompanied by a large pile of fries. I then went back today and got the corn and crawfish bisque and the Friday special: catfish, toast, fries (or potato salad) and a side salad all for about $9. Both times the food was AMAZING and well priced. I liked that the corn and crawfish bisque had A LOT of crawfish in it, making it a very filling treat. The servings were huge and I had plenty of leftovers both times.  The owner, Darryl Ballard, introduced himself and thanked me for coming. I thought it was really nice of him to take the time and check to make sure that I was enjoying everything.  10th Street Cafe is my new favorite place and I plan on becoming a regular. They have great lunch deals (and the serve dinner Wednesday through Saturday) and they have food that will please every palate. Can you tell that I am excited about this place?

I walked by this place tonight and I remembered that it's been my "to review" pile for awhile now. Famous Door is pretty cool- they have nicely priced drinks, they usually have a band playing and the majority of the place is well-behaved tourists. The few times I've been in here I've gotten the house drink which is a sugary concoction of which I can't remember the name. I do remember that there is plenty of seating near the door if you want to people watch or make a quick escape. I would hang out here again.

I usually don't review parking lots, because if you've been to one you've been to all of them. I'm reviewing this one mainly to say that if you park here and you are going to GW Fins (and other surrounding "nice" restaurants, I'm sure) you can get your parking validated and park here for free.  The staff here was all women on the night that I went, and I thought that was pretty cool. They were extremely fast and efficient, and while it wasn't the busiest night of the week, I appreciated it because I have been in situations where I feel like I am waiting forever for them to get my car for me and there is no one else there.  The lot is in an area that is relatively safe and it wasn't a far walk from the lot to GW Fins.

It's a Wal Mart, so if you've been in one, you've been in most.  I don't "do" Wal Mart. I can take the crowd. I can't take the chaos. There is too much going on all at once and it gives me anxiety. But alas, sometimes you must venture into the deepest depths of the scariest places on earth to get something that you need to live.  They have good deals on groceries and they have just about anything you could ever want here. The only drawback in the super long lines and the slow cashiers. I mean, seriously. Wasn't there a time where cashiers put a little hustle into the checkout? Oh well.

Finally something has moved into this building that has sat empty for two years since Cuco's closed!  This is the second Las Cazuelas location on the Westbank. Apparently I have been to the Harvey location, since I reviewed it, but I have no memory of it. I was here for lunch and there was a nice crowd and I was seated in a booth right away. The decor is all new and really nice.   My waitress came over, took my order, and dropped off some chips and salsa for munching. The menu here is really extensive, but I got M5- the burrito supreme with chicken. This was a burrito that came topped with sauce, sour cream, guacamole, lettuce and tomato. I could tell that the chicken was fresh and I liked that it had flavor to it before being added to the dish. In other words, it was seasoned and cooked in actual spice before the burrito was put together. For the price I wish it had been a little bigger, but that's okay.  My waitress was amazing and I wish I had gotten her name because she was really sweet and friendly and stayed on top of everything I needed. I'm glad that there's a new restaurant in this space and I'm sure it will do well.

I didn't even know that this spot was check in-able until I saw someone review it. I guess I should have known.  I have spent so much time at Latrobe Park and I find it to be one of the hidden gems in the city. Located right outside the French Market, it's the perfect spot to sit and enjoy a nice day or munch on beignets. I like the the area is "sunken" (for lack of a better term), so you are kind of hidden away when you are sitting on the benches under the trees.  I kind of think the term "park" is generous when describing this little spot. It's more of a sanctuary where you can sit and enjoy the day away from the rest of the crowd of the Quarter.

Good Lord. Parking in this area on a Saturday is a beast!  Pretty cool little place. The large ice coffee is really large. I like that they have a "bar" area where you can sit and hang out. The only real con about this place is it's SUPER busy and the line is pretty long when you are waiting to get coffee. They do have a lot of beverage and pastry choices, so that makes up for it.

Leslie Knope: "Why would anybody ever eat anything besides breakfast food?"  Ron Swanson: "People are idiots, Leslie."  Truer words have never been spoken and breakfast is life even when it's lunch, so when I saw that The Flying Pig was having a $13 for $25 worth of food deal on Groupon, I jumped on it.  It was after a photo shoot and I was starving because I don't eat before those things, so I knew that it was Flying Pig time. I stopped in shortly after lunch time on a Saturday and it was pretty dead, which I was happy about because more food for me. I had been eyeing the menu online and I decided on the Prytania on the pictures alone. This is poached eggs, tasso cream sauce on top of fried chicken. Uh...yeah. You get a side and I got the grits because I love grits and for my bread I got corn bread because #South.  "Oh you went to a place called The Flying Pig and got chicken?" Aw yeah. This poached egg/chicken combo was amazing. The eggs were perfect and runny and the chicken was crispy and juicy. Once you get past the whole "cradle to the grave" thing with the egg/chicken combo, you're good to go. Seriously, this was a fantastic dish. The grits were fantastic as well. I almost messed around and got an order of shrimp and grits as my "side", but I decided to not go crazy. The corn bread was excellent, as corn bread mostly is, and it wasn't dry at all.  We also got an order of fried green tomatoes that were fantastic. They were lightly fried and topped with a delicious sauce.   Because The Flying Pig knows what's up, they serve their full menu all day. You can get breakfast for dinner if you want. It's like a neighborhood diner, but fancy. I wish I had gotten the waiter's name because he was so sweet and was on top of things and made sure that my corn bread was nice and warm when it got to me. Food came really fast, I'm sure because no one else was there and I loved all of it. Believe me, I'll be keeping an eye out for another Groupon and I'll be eating at The Flying Pig again, no matter what.

Oh my gaaaaah! Talk about retro dress heaven!!  I stopped in here with a friend, after he mentioned that this place is a "must" for any retro lover. They carry a wide selection of "Stop Staring!" dresses, which are all  amazing. If you are into the whole 50's retro look, this is the place for you.   There is a wide selection of retro dresses in a lot of different sizes. They vary from what I would call casual swing dresses to fancier form fitting wiggle dresses, in both solids and prints. I am only knocking off a star because the dresses are a little steep, though I understand this is the dress manufacturer price.  I kind of wonder if past reviewers. went into the store, or just went by what they saw in the window, because if you are a guy, they also carry a wide selection of suits of all kinds at very good prices. In fact, I would say that they have more men's suits than ladies dresses! You are sure to find something amazing.  Bonus points: they are open late every night of the week (close at 11pm!).

The Kingpin is a cool place to catch the Saints game, or catch a band when they have one.  They have an extensive beer selection and the crowd is always nice and friendly.  The place does tend to get crowded on weekends.  One huge complaint: the smoke in this place is insane, even if there aren't a lot of people in here.

I'm actually kind of honored to be the first to review this awesome store! In a world of Home Depots and Lowes, this nice family owned store will make you feel good about shopping local.  I recently had to stop in here because my dad was working on something that he needed a certain part for. We have always gone here for our hardware needs, so he called ahead and had them set it aside, so I just had to go and pick it up. The owner is always sure to give me a really personal experience whenever I go in and he will usually ask what I'm working on or what I have planned for the part I'm buying.  The store itself is nicely organized and the prices here are just as good, if not better than the big name stores. Also, this is where I go whenever I need a brake tag. Just pull your car around to the side and you will be in and out in no time. I have never had to wait in any kind of long line and I have never had any problems getting a tag here.

Smoothie King is a must. It's now a national chain but did you know that it all started in Kenner, of all places? Pretty neat piece of trivia.  My favorite thing to get here is the angel food. I swear, I have been getting these things since I was a kid and I don't think I have ever gotten anything else. It's a yummy blend of strawberries, bananas and other fruits. It's super sweet and makes for a great treat every now and then.  Smoothie King also has assorted supplements, power bars and drink mixes for all of you health freaks out there.

It's pretty insane that it's taken me this long to get to O'Briens. This lovely restaurant is, after all, practically located in my back yard. Nevertheless, it wasn't until recently that I was able to sit down and enjoy a meal here.  We stopped in for a Friday for lunch at around one. Even though it was a bit after the typical "lunch rush' there was a good crowd in the medium sized dining room, but we were still seated quickly. Just a heads up: if you are looking to have dinner here, you are going to have to make a reservation. The place is pretty small and I would bet that they get packed at dinner time.  Everything on the menu sounded just amazing. Duck quesadillas? Whoa. Prime Rib sandwich? Irish Dip? Everything just sounds incredible. I decided to go with the Panko crusted gulf shrimp on a bed of truffle mac and cheese. Yeah, you read that right: truffle mac and cheese. You should know by now that I love mac and cheese and I adore fancy mac and cheese. As soon as I saw that mac and cheese was on the menu at this fancy pants restaurant, I was in.  After a short wait out came the shrimp and mac and cheese. WHOA. This food is amazing! The shrimp is perfectly battered and fried and the mac and cheese is creamy, rich and ridiculously good. Not only that, but the portion is more than generous. Before my entree came, I was regretting not getting an appetizer, but as soon as this magic was put in front of me that regret vanished.  The staff was super attentive and was really good at refilling my iced tea and coffee as soon as it was needed. They made sure that we were enjoying everything and had everything that we needed.   Be aware: yes, this is the Westbank, but this is a fine dining establishment; please dress accordingly. As Morgan said, there are white table cloths on the tables and the service is top notch, so leave the short shorts and tank tops at home.  I can't wait to go back and try more of this amazing menu! I definitely hope to return sooner rather than later, especially since the restaurant is so close to me.

Carmo has been on my list of "must trys" for a while now, so i was pretty excited when we stopped in for dinner on a Friday night. There was a bit of a wait for a table, so we decided to make things easier on everyone and we sat at the bar.  We started with some sashimi- we chose the sashimi creole which is fish that is lightly dusted with creole seasoning and then torched. This isn't what I think of when I hear "sashimi", but it was different and really good. The middle of the fish was still a bit raw and the outside was lightly cooked and I enjoyed it.  Next I had a small Broken Noodle Salad. This is basically Carmo's version of a vermicelli salad. The small is a really good size and this probably could have been my entire meal. The salad was nice and fresh with rice noodles, bean sprouts and cabbage with tofu, cucumber, peas, carrots, mushrooms, peppers, scallions, cilantro & peanuts all tossed with citrus ginger chili vinaigrette. It was an interesting combination and I especially enjoyed the peanuts, which added a nice crunch to the whole thing. This is a definite "must order".  Finally, I had the Rico which is a breadless pulled pork sandwich served open faced on a grilled plantain patty. So many people had recommended this, when I mentioned that I was going to be eating at Carmo, and it didn't disappoint. Once again, the serving was large, the pork was tender, and the plantain added an interesting touch the entire dish, almost making it "guilt free".  I enjoyed Carmo immensely and I am excited to return. The staff was attentive and parking was pretty easy- we were able to grab a spot right in front of the place on a Friday night.

This was such a fantastic parade!  First of all, they are super generous with throws and the floats are GORGEOUS.  The highlight this year for me was definitely seeing Harry Connick Jr. and Cindy Lauper.  I was also excited to catch beads from the mayor himself: Mitch Landrieu!  I think I was more excited to see him than the actual "celebrities".  Ha.  I guess I'm a nerd.  Orpheus is definitely joining Muses, Tucks, and d'Etat as my "must see" parades of the season.

After passing this place for years, I FINALLY decided to stop in and check the place out. One Smart Cookie is a small bakery that sells different sugar cookies, petit fours and cakes. I just stopped in to look around and decided on one of the sugar cookies. It was really good with a lot of flavor and kind of reminded me of wedding cake, flavor wise (I think it was the almond).  I think that you can order specific cookies and cakes for special occasions. I'll definitely be back.

I had been trying to figure out what review #600 would be, and when I decided to go to Stein's, I knew that this was going to be it.  I had been wanting to try Stein's for so long, but it seems like something always put me off. Either I didn't have time to head over that way or I was intimidated when I heard that the lunch crowd was pretty big. So, finally on a Sunday afternoon, it was decided that this was the perfect time to check out Stein's and I was right!  When I walked into the small deli, I was immediately overcome by the delicious smells of whatever was cooking. There was a smoky haze in the air and I knew that these folks meant business. I already knew what I wanted (yes, I asked seasoned Stein's-goers for their opinion), so I walked right up and ordered. I got a Foxy which is roast beef, avocado, cheddar, red onion with horseradish on rye bread. They have a small seating area, and I was pretty lucky that there was no one else in there at the time. I sat down and I waited.  When my sandwich came, I was blown away just by the look of it (see picture) it looked amazing and I was delighted that it came with two pickles on the side. I love pickles! I was excited that the sandwich was even better than it looked. I am not exaggerating here...I finished the entire thing in probably 5 minutes. That's how good it was. I liked that they didn't skimp when it came to the cheese and there were nice thick pieces of avocado on it. It was so delicious.  Stein's also has a nice little market of different things you can purchase and they even have a selection of fancy bottled beers, but to be honest with you, I was so focused on this awesome sandwich that I didn't pay attention to much else.  Will I return to Stein's? Absolutely. I think I am going to try and get a different sandwich each time, until I have tried the entire menu. Living the dream!

Metairie cemetery is probably the most beautiful of it's kind in the city.  There are gorgeous statues and structures and the graves themselves are really works of art.  A description just won't do it justice.  You must see it for yourself.  The cemetery is extremely well kempt and almost looks like a park with beautiful statues when you are visiting.  I encourage everyone to visit and see it in person.

A very strong 3.5 stars.  Me and some other models used a suite here as a "prep" space for a fashion show that we were participating in across the street. The suite was pretty perfect. There was a good sized "sitting" area complete with a sofa, a nice sized table for meals and a full kitchenette with fridge, microwave and sink. The bedroom was actually a good size and the whole area really felt like a small apartment. The hotel itself is also pretty nice and looks modern, but still has a nice "old school" feel.  I knocked off a couple of stars, because it isn't located in the greatest area. In fact, the parking garage for the hotel is basically in one of the worst parts of New Orleans, and I would be worried about my safety at night. They do have a valet, but when your car is a short walking distance from the hotel, sometimes you don't want to wait for a valet. Also, we were taking "pre fashion show" pictures in the hotel, out of the way of other customers (near the suite room) and the security guard made a fuss about that and said we couldn't do that. I think that's probably more of a Wyndham rule.  All in all, not a bad place, but there are better options on St. Charles Avenue alone.

When it's early morning (11am) and you are about to get into a full day of festing, you are gonna need a jump start. Enter Starbucks. We grabbed some coffee here on the way to French Quarter fest, and even though they were busy, the staff got our coffee to us quickly- and with a smile! The iced coffee is as good as any Starbucks. This spot is pretty small, and we were in and out so fast I didn't notice if there are places to sit, but if you are downtown for festing or shopping, this is a good place to get some brew.

OMG! This might be the cutest shop in the Quarter and maybe even the city!  I was strolling down Royal when my eye caught some really adorable collectibles in the window. Limoges! Limoges of all types! My mom used to love Limoges and she had quite a few and I had never seen so many in one spot, so of course I stopped in. They pretty much have any type of Limgoes box that you could ever imagine- they also had small ones in the shape of red beans and bigger ones in the shape of bananas and alligators. If you are a collector, this is your dream shop.  I picked up a couple "New Orleans" themed boxes to ship to some friends out of town, as they are always on the hunt for unusual New Orleans souvenirs. The staff is helpful and will help you track down the perfect gift. Seriously, if you are visiting, skip the tacky tshirt shops and stop in here instead.  They also sell chocolate and other fun things here, but for me, it was all about those neat little boxes.  Note: There's a review on this business listing that is not for this business. I flagged it and nothing happened, I just wanted to mention that this store is an antique shop that doesn't serve food, so that one star is unwarranted.

I'm gonna be frank.  The only real reason to ever go to Vinnie's is if you want a burger, because they are actually really good.  I'd say it's probably a step up from usual bar food quality.  The burgers are always really big and cooked to order.  They actually serve a few different sandwiches, but in a place like this, a burger is probably your best bet.  I came here years ago and actually "hung out", but as of late, I only get take out from here, so I can't really speak to the quality of the place itself.  I do remember that they have a few pool tables, as well as tables and chairs, if you want to sit down and eat something.  Not a bad place to check out, if you are in the mood for some late night grub on the Westbank.

Over the years, I've had a few dealings with Ochsner Medical Center.  Things usually go smoothly (all things considered) and the staff and nurses are really nice and do their best to make your comfortable and make your stay enjoyable. Years ago I had to go to the ER with stomach issues and then my dad had to go with a cut and the wait wasn't long either time. They do their best to get to you as quickly as possible and make your stay as enjoyable as they can, under the circumstances.

This is a pretty good Wal Mart. You might be asking yourself "what qualifies a pretty good Wal Mart?" Well, for me it's a few things: I find what I need quickly and easily, the check out lines move fast and...that's about it.  This Wal Mart met all of my Wal Mart expectations. I stopped in on an afternoon that I happened to be passing by and needed some stuff. Walking through this place I realized that this Wal Mart is way bigger than the one in Harvey, which means they have more stuff to choose from. I didn't need much on this trip, just some basic makeup and some ear buds. I found both without hassle and without having to deal with too many other people (don't you hate when people block an entire aisle with their cart?). Believe it or not, I was in and out in less than 10 minutes. I was even super impressed when the check out woman in my line had to go price check something for another customer and another worker saw me waiting, waved me over to her line and checked me out WITHOUT PROMPTING. Pretty good, Wal Mart.

I HAD A PHOTO SHOOT HERE.  This is a pretty basic road side motel. I called ahead to make a reservation and they said, "Uh, wat? We're a roadside motel. Just come on by, check in and you're good." COOL. You check in at the service window that's behind glass. (I'm pretty sure it's bulletproof glass. You can't miss it. It's right next to the last working pay phone in New Orleans that always has someone on it- true story). Once you pay for your dirty little stay (you sinner), they give you the goods. The goods is the key to your room and your TV remote. You MUST return the remote when you check out or you will be charged a fine. Get it? Good. They should probably also include a packet of Purell, but I'm not gonna tell them how to run a business. I didn't need a remote, but the sketchers were circling, so I took it and kept my trap shut.  The room is basic af. You get a ratty old bed and...uh...that's about it. BUT the bathroom is surprisingly clean. Like, no mildew or anything and all the soap you could want. If I was staying the night I would legit sleep in the tub. Who's the cleaning person at this place? They're killing it. If you want bathroom things like towels and toilet paper, you have to go down the hall to the service room and get it your own damn self. Thankfully, I wasn't here long enough to need any of that stuff.  The room was pretty clean and it made me itchy, but that's more of my own OCD issues, and not so much the motel's fault. If you're staying here, bring your own pillow because the pillows they have are sad as hell and the cases look like they've been Febrezed- tops.  Anyway, when check out time came I turned in my key and my remote like a good little customer and I went on my way. The guy working here was SUPER nice and didn't ask any questions so take note, you weirdos.

I'm going to keep this pretty short and sweet, because it's a delicate thing to review, yet I need people to know what kind of place this is.  My grandmother recently passed away at 95 years and she had made all of her arrangements through Lake Lawn, thanks to a long standing relationship with them. Thanks to those arrangements and our funeral director, this whole process was made much easier than it could have been. Jean (sp?) was SO sweet and wonderful throughout the entire thing and she made sure that all of our needs were met. The priest (Fr. Meyer) who performed my grandmother's funeral mass was perfect and we couldn't have asked for anyone better during this difficult time.  Lake Lawn made a really unfortunate process a lot more comfortable through their professionalism and gentility. We couldn't have asked for anything better and I would recommend them to anyone faced with a sudden (or not so sudden) death.

I've been back to Pho Tau Bay many times since my last review.  I've also tried other pho places.  Pho Tau Bay is definitely the best I have been to.  I can look past the lackluster decor and focus on the food and it really is amazing.   When I first reviewed, I was completely inexperienced when it came to pho.  I now realize that Pho Tau Bay is pretty fantastic and you really do get  A LOT for the (little) money you spend.  There is a reason that people will travel across that big scary bridge to get a taste of this wonderful food.

Time for another review update because I wrote my first review when I was a new Yelper and didn't know what I was doing.  I like this PJ's. I go here usually once a week and get a large iced coffee. Sometimes I'll go crazy and get a mocha granita. Both are always good. The place is small, but has a good amount of tables and chairs if you need to study and there are also a few tables and chairs out front, if you want to sit there. Keep in mind that this PJ's is in a strip mall, so you are sitting outside of a strip mall. It's not super glamorous, but it gets the job done.  Ownership of this PJ's has recently changed, and I don't know if it's related, but they no longer carry the Gambit or Where Y'at papers. That's a shame because I used to like to stop in here and pick one up with my coffee, so I don't know if they are gone for good or what. I also don't understand why every PJ's seems to price their coffee differently. Ok, I'm starting to sound like Andy Rooney, so I'll end here.  Cliffs: I go here all the time and the coffee is awesome.

Here's the situation: when you get invited to fancy brunch, you go. When David's cousin asked us if we wanted to join her and a few other people for fancy Sunday jazz brunch at Arnaud's, I couldn't say "yes!" fast enough.  I had never been to Arnaud's for brunch, but I knew that I was in for a memorable experience. We were seated in the big dining room and a small jazz band was making the rounds moving from table to table playing old favorites. The brunch menu is a prix fixe menu, and you get four courses. The price of your entree is the price you pay for everything.  I started with the turtle soup. I LOVE turtle soup au sherry and Arnaud's version didn't disappoint at all. It was full of meat and quite tasty. This was a perfect way to start the meal. Next was the salad. This was a simple side salad that was a nice palate cleanser between meals. My entree was the Eggs Adrienne. This was poached eggs, grilled Louisiana country sausage on English muffins with Creole sauce. This dish was GREAT! The eggs were cooked perfectly and the sausage and sauce were to die for. This is the way a Creole breakfast should taste and I liked that I got a nice taste of Louisiana at brunch. The final course was dessert and I had the bread pudding. As someone who has gone most of her life avoiding bread pudding, I certainly have found myself sampling a lot of it lately. Arnaud's version is fantastic made with rum soaked raisins and served in a Bourbon sauce. It's really hard to go wrong with that.  It was David's cousins birthday and the band made her feel special by coming over and singing Happy Birthday to her. I love special touches like that. The atmosphere was very laid back and it was a lot of fun. I enjoyed a couple of mimosas and the brunch lasted for about 3 hours and the time just flew. The staff here really does a fantastic job of making sure that you have a memorable experience and we certainly did. Put this on your "must" list, whether you live in New Orleans or you are just visiting.

I hadn't been to the Carousel Gardens since I was a little kid, when we came here for Jingle Bells and Beer last week. I really need to make more of a point to come to this part of the park!  The park itself is large and there are a lot of rides geared mainly towards small kids, tweens and teenagers. Some rides are the train around the park, ladybug rollercoaster, a few rides that spin you until you die, bumper cars, a fun house and, of course, a carousel.  On this particular night we decided to check out the train, the bumper cars, the funhouse and the carousel. My favorites were the train and the carousel- what can it say, I like things a little more low key. The train is really neat because it takes you throughout the entire park and I can see how small kids would really love it. I loved riding the carousel and the whole experience brought back a lot of memories. There's just something magical about doing something like that.  I think that the park is closed for the season, but I will definitely be back once winter is over and the weather is really nice.

"Your girl is lovely, Hubbell..."  This is a lovely historic library in old Algiers that has actually been around since 1907. When you step into this building, you are becoming a part of New Orleans history. On the day I stopped in, I actually got to speak with George Hubbell and he told me a little history of his wife, Cita Dennis Hubbell, who fronted a campaign to restore and reopen the library in the 60's. I also got to meet librarian Seale Paterson who was fantastic and told me about all of the "ins and outs" of this divine little library.  They hold monthly events such as "meet the author" every second Tuesday of the month, story time for kids every month and even drag queen story time when a drag queen comes in and reads stories to the kids and a lot of other activities. It all sounds like a lot of fun!  The library is small, but they have plenty of books for adults and children, movies, and computers. This is the main library for the International School of Louisiana, so don't be surprised if you stop in and run into a child or 30.  Mr. George is at the library every day, so if you happen to see him, tell him "hi" and he will be happy to chat with you and give you a little history of the library and the neighborhood as well.

I was doing some work at the Jung Hotel over the course of two days, and I hit this coffee shop, located therein, 3 times.  I like this place, even if the coffee is a bit pricey. I can't complain as I know why it's pricey: 1) It's a coffee shop located in a brand new hotel. 2) It's located on Canal street and the foot traffic is off the walls.  The staff here is really great and they have all the fancy stuff as well as teas and I think they also have smoothies. Like any good coffee shop they have a nice variety of pastries and sandwiches and they have Abita Amber in their cold case, if you're looking to party.  I got their iced coffee which was VERY good- it was nice and rich and it had a lot of flavor. The space is small, but there are plenty of tables if you want to work and the nice big windows give you a good view of the world passing by outside.  If you're in the area this is a good place to stop for your caffeine fix.

This is a cool place, but WHY do you allow smoking??   I was told that I had to try the barbecue here, so we decided to stop in so I could get a taste. We sat at the bar, looked over the menu and started with some yummy fried pickles. I decided to get the pulled pork sandwich and mac and cheese (my barbecue favorites). Full disclosure: they did screw up my order at first, bringing out a brisket sandwich, but they quickly corrected the problem and I was well on my way.  The sandwich was really good- the pork was tender and smoky and had a lot of flavor without needing sauce. The mac and cheese was out of this world! It might be some of the best mac and cheese I have ever had; it's definitely up there.  Honestly, I wouldn't dine in again mainly because of the cigarette smoke. There weren't a lot of people in here, but it was a little overwhelming and took away from the entire experience for me. I wouldn't hesitate to drop in and get an order to go, however.

For review 2100, I knew I wanted it to be special and what's more special than a place I got to try for my birthday?  I was so excited about eating at Gabrielle. I hadn't been fortunate enough to dine here when it was open pre-Katrina, so I was determined to visit for a special occasion, especially after I had heard to many raves about the place.  I made my reservations a month in advance and mentioned that I was going to be celebrating my birthday. When I arrived, I was seated immediately at a table that was decorated with a "Happy Birthday" streamer and some confetti. I love special touches and I was already excited about this experience. I had looked over the menu ahead of time, so I already knew what I was getting.  She-crab bisque- This bisque was delicious without being too thick and filing. There were huge pieces of crab in it and the bisque itself was creamy, smooth and full of flavor. This was a perfect starter.  Traiteur Fish- This was a seared fish filet served on top of a crab cake with preserved lemon and chili aoli. It doesn't get much better than that! The fish was cooked and seasoned perfectly and was nice and light. The crab cake was pure crab meat and very filling. It was a nice balance with the lightness of the fish.  Chocolate Pecan Pie- I am a huge fan of any kind of pecan pie and Gabrielle's chocolate pecan pie knocked it out of the park. The pie is made in-house and I ordered mine served with vanilla ice cream on the side, for good measure. What I really like about the pie is that you can actually taste the chocolate in it. Talk about decadent! Since it was my birthday, they put a candle in it and decorated the pie plate. I was also served a complimentary glass of champagne, which I thought was a super nice touch and made me feel really special.  Our waiter for the evening was Victor and he was great! You can tell that he really knows his stuff and that he wants to make your meal as special as possible. He really did his part to make my birthday evening feel special. If you can, sit in Victor's section and he'll take good care of you.   I love the ambiance at Gabrielle. It's a neighborhood place and it's small without feeling like tables are crammed into a space in which they don't fit. The restaurant has a cozy feel, as if you're dining in a far away cafe somewhere. Although we were here on a slow night, because a Saints game was on, I was happy that I made reservations ahead of time.  I will absolutely go back to Gabrielle, and now that they are serving lunch on Friday's, I'm going to have to add them to my lunch rotation.

We were leaving Roulaison Distillery when Andrew mentioned something about a chocolatier right next door, and before I knew it I was at Piety and Desire Chocolate. It's next to a distillery and brewery, which is perfect!  The shop is really small, but their case is packed with the most beautiful little handmade bon bons you ever did see in your life. They come in interesting shapes like tombs and dragon's eggs and they even have shiny little king cake chocolates, that are just adorable. I decided to get a couple of the cute little king cakes and I couldn't wait- I snarfed one down in the car. This particular chocolate had a gooey filling and I felt quite fancy eating a gourmet chocolate on this rainy afternoon.  You can buy the chocolate individually or by the box and you can mix and match whichever ones you please. They also have real king cake, but the owner told us to call ahead and make sure that they have it because it's only on certain days. If you're looking for a fancy gift, especially something with a New Orleans flair and a touch of uniqueness, this is an excellent place to start.

It's always interesting reviewing car washes. I mean, as long as it shoots soap and water on your car and then sucks it off, it's all good right? Well this car wash does just that. It shoots soap and water on your car and then vacuums it off like nobody's business! Boy oh boy was that car clean!  It's unfortunate that the day after I got my car washed the trees decided to explode their pollen all over the place like "whoa". Now my car is covered in tree aftermath. Figures.

This is a review of the bar.  It was a cold night in December and David and I had decided to go see the lights at the Roosevelt Hotel. As everyone knows, it gets pretty packed over there come Christmastime and this night was no different. On top of that, the Sazerac Bar was at full capacity and drinks were outrageously priced for the season. We got one drink there, took our pictures and headed out. That's when I spotted Moxy.  We popped in and immediately liked the look of the place: a wide open bar area, plenty of comfy seating and games made us feel right at home. We ordered a couple of cocktails (and we didn't have to mortgage the house) and we decided to play some games. We played a round of foosball and a few rounds of Connect Four. Look, it doesn't matter who won. We had a great time and I hadn't played either games in years and I have a bad knee. Anyway, the staff was really friendly and the drinks were good, so we were happy. We especially liked the "living room" style seating area where we could just sit and people watch.  If you're in the area, this hotel bar is worth checking out.

This place was nice, but I expected more.  Filmore in the Oaks is the City Park golf course country club and my dad and I came here for Coolinary lunch. Upon walking in, there were a few people eating at tables in a huge room and no one to tell us if we seat ourselves. Finally, the bartender told us to just sit anywhere, so we did. We waited about ten minutes before someone came around to bring us menus and take our drink order. I'm not sure what the hold up was, as we were here before noon and they weren't busy.  So, I ordered off of the Coolinary menu and I got corn and crab bisque as my starter and I got the fish almondine was my entree. The bisque was great with a lot of flavor- I really enjoyed it. The fish was okay and the waitress admitted that they don't use local seafood. It was served with greens that I actually enjoyed more than the fish itself.   For my dessert I got the bread pudding and my dad and I told the waitress that we wanted coffee, as well. Well, the waitress brought the bread pudding and said she would be "right back" with the coffee. She then proceeded to bring food out to 2 other tables, with no acknowledgement to us. I understand that you want to get people their food as soon as it's ready, but a quick "didn't forget about your coffee!", as you walk past us twice, goes a long way. Also, after she dropped off the food to the other tables, she disappeared for another 5 minutes.   At this point I have finished my bread pudding and here she comes with the coffee in paper "go" cups and barely an apology. Obviously she wanted us out of there because you would think in a "country club" type setting, they would serve coffee in actual cups. During the entire meal my dad and I both agreed that we felt like an afterthought and the people they were hustling to serve must be members or, at least, regulars.  I'm glad I got to try their Coolinary menu, but I wouldn't go out of my way to eat here again. The three stars is actually more for the setting and the bread pudding than anything else.

I happened to be in the area after a photo shoot one night, so we stopped in for dinner. It was a Wednesday night, so there was no crowd at all, even though the bar across the street was pretty packed for 7 in the evening.  I started with the calamari, which was very tasty and a nice start to the meal. We got a few rolls: salmon and avocado roll, tuna roll, crunchy dynamite roll, Royal roll and a rainbow roll. The salmon and avocado roll and tuna roll were perfect. The fish was super fresh and they had a lot of flavor. The rainbow roll was a typical rainbow roll and very tasty and fresh.  The Royal roll came was spicy tuna, snow crab, asparagus, fresh salmon, tuna, with ponzu sauce and spicy mayo. It was good, but if I ordered it again I would tell them to not include the spicy mayo. In fact, most of their specialty rolls are made with spicy mayo and that's just not something I need in a sushi roll. I dare say that if they didn't include it, no one would even notice and the roll would be a smidge healthier.   I like that even though the special rolls are large, they are cut in such a way that makes them easier to handle and eat. There's nothing more frustrating than gracefully trying to fit a huge roll in your mouth.  All in all I liked my dinner. I've heard the ramen is excellent, so I might try it next time I'm in the area. The rolls are a little pricier than you can find elsewhere, but that's to be expected since it's near the Quarter.

Nope, I'm not even going to TRY to top Harry T's review, because he was probably the first person to ever set foot inside this establishment and he described the whole place perfectly and there is no way my Yelp review will ever do the place justice. I will, however, take you on a tour of my meal and hopefully it will float your boat.  It was a rainy night when I visited, but that didn't deter the crowd. For whatever reason the light was not on the front gate and I had to feel my way in. After navigating through the rainy patio, I found my way into the bar. I was told there would be a 30 minute wait, which was expected, so I sat down with my dining companion and we ordered a bottle of red. As we were eyeing the menu, two women walked in and were seated immediately in the back. Kudos to our bartender for informing the waitress that we were there first and hustling up a table for us as well.  Once seated, we knew what we wanted: pomme frites and aioli, olives, eels in olive oil, habanero oysters (my pick) and squid pâté. Needless to say, this was definitely an adventure for my taste buds. The pomme frites and aioli came out first and it was just perfect. The aioli was nice and garlicky and the frites were crispy. Yum!  Next came the tray of squid pâté, oysters and eels. You should know that all of this comes in a can- this is the European way. The tray also came with a nice amount of bread, so that you could spread the seafood on it. I started with the oysters, because that was my order. They were yummy and spicy and a had a fantastic flavor- this was probably my favorite. I had the pâté next, and although my date thought it was bland, I really liked it. It was smooth and reminded me of potted meat with a bit of a kick (That's a terrible description, but I like potted meat). Next I tried the baby eels. My date said he learned somewhere that these eels live in rice patties. Erm...okay.  Honestly, it tasted like salty noodles. If you don't think of it as being eels, you'll be fine. This was my first time eating it and I was excited to try something new, even it was a bit weird. But, then again, I like being adventurous.  Finally was the olives- salty and perfect and served in their own juice- I loved them. Be aware that they have pits, so chomp with caution.  What is better for dessert than some cheese? The cheese platter came complete with cow, sheep, and goat cheese and also with a bit of strawberry and pear all served with crispy bread. It was absolutely perfect and a great end to a fantastic meal. I got to a point where I was so full that I ditched the bread and ate the cheese straight- thank God for my fast metabolism.  Our waitress was amazing throughout the entire experience. She was extremely attentive and got us water and extra bread and butter when we asked for it and she was really sweet about making sure that we had everything else that we needed.   The atmosphere of the place itself is pretty cozy. The dimly lit bar area and the decor make you feel like you are tucked into a European cafe. There are a few tables in the front and some tables in the back. The music is a bit loud, but not intrusive.  If you'd like, you can eat at the bar. We chose to sit at a small table in the back. (Note: it was raining the night we were here and water was leaking through the wall and puddling onto the floor. This is going to be something that has to be fixed- I'm thinking wood rot and eventually termites- it could get funky. Just a seal on the outside will fix that issue- my two cents.) The bathroom is outside on the left and around the side.  N7 is the type of place you have to go into with an open mind. Don't go here and just order meat and salad. You HAVE TO try at least one of the canned goods, or you haven't gotten the full experience. Personally, I want to go back and get the sardines, squid in ink and the meat, just to try it. Yes, I will be back!

If you're looking for a quick Mexican lunch, and you don't feel like fighting the crowd at Juan's, than La Carreta is the place for you.  I stopped in here for lunch mid-day on a weekday and the place was pretty empty. Free chips and salsa was dropped on the table and I looked over the menu. I was in a burrito kind of mood so I decided to get the build-it-yourself burrito with carnitas. It also comes with your choice of salad or tortilla soup, so I got the soup.  First of all, the soup was fantastic. I never think to order soup at Mexican restaurants, but this one didn't disappoint. The burrito was great as well, it was packed with carnitas and other things and it had a nice kick to it. I also had it topped with a green sauce that has just enough spice. The burrito and soup came to $12 and I took half of the burrito home, so I consider this a complete lunch success!  This spot is great and satisfies the Mexican craving. It's not super authentic, but if you're looking for a burrito fix, this is the spot.

You know those Disney Halloween movies you used to watch as a kid where all of the neighborhood houses were perfectly decorated for Halloween with pumpkins, skeletons and lights? Well, Ghost Manor was exactly like that, only better.  I first heard about this house last year and I was determined to check it out this year, especially since they added a few things. Every year the family that lives in his house brings it to life with singing skeletons, shadows of ghosts and skeletons dancing in the windows, lights that move with the music and pumpkins that flash in time with the tunes.  Ghost Manor is "open" from sundown to 10pm the last two weeks of October and the "show" plays every 15 minutes or so and from beginning to end it's really cool. The owner of the house builds and creates everything himself, so this isn't just some store bought decorations hooked up to music.  We were here on Halloween night and, of course, the whole area in front of the house was packed and there were people handing out candy and trinkets to trick or treaters. Ghost Manor is a cool piece of New Orleans "local flavor" and a fun alternative if you don't want to bring your child to an actual haunted house.

I was actually pretty surprised by Cheesecake Factory. When someone mentioned we were eating here for dinner, I wasn't super excited. I didn't really know what to expect from a national chain, but I kept an open mind.  We came on a Thursday evening and the place was PACKED. Seriously, there was a 20 minute wait and I was pretty surprised. I guess because it's attached to the mall it gets a lot of action. Anyway, after waiting for a bit we were seated and given the huge super long menu they have. It pretty much has everything on here you could want from burgers and fish to ribs and their version of Thai food- no kidding.  I decided to get the fried catfish which came with sides of mashed potatoes, corn and green beans. When the food came, I was immediately impressed by the portion- three good sized pieces of catfish and generous amounts of sides. The fish was cooked nicely with a thin crust and had a good flavor. The sides were okay- my favorite was the mashed potatoes but I could have done without the green beans as they were a bit under cooked for my liking. All in all, dinner was good and more than I expected from a chain.  Since we were at the Cheesecake Factory, naturally I had to try some of the good stuff. I got the Hershey's Cheesecake and not only were they generous with the portion, but it was delicious! It was basically a chocolate bomb and I had to stop myself from scarfing down the entire thing.  As for service- our waiter was a bit slow, but that was only because the dining room was full. The guy was still very sweet, so it wasn't a huge deal. While I wouldn't rush back to Cheesecake Bistro, I wouldn't balk if I ended up here for dinner again.

I've been a fan of the original outdoor art market on Frenchmen for a long time and they now have a second location on Decatur.  Packed with tons of local art, this is the perfect place to pass through if you are looking for a unique gift or art piece and you want to support a local artist. I really like that the artists are personally there with their booth so you can ask them questions about their art or see the process of it actually being made.

Not so much a "club" as it is a fancy casino bar.  I don't know what goes on during the week, but on Friday and Saturday night at 10, they turn the music up and have gogo dancers.  They also have a VIP section, which is just a little quartered off section of the club.  There's really no where to dance, so I think that calling this place a "club" is being generous, but it isn't a bad place to hang out if you have some friends in the casino and you just want to get a drink.

If you are into art that's a little strange, interesting, and different, than look no further than Funeral Gallery and, more specifically, Vinsantos' hand made art dolls.  There's a lot of different art by different artists here, but Vinsantos' dolls caught my eye. Like something out of a Tim Burton fantasy and completely hand made, these dolls are molded with big eyes, beautiful colors, gorgeous clothes and reside in a handmade case for display. The dolls aren't cheap, but the detail that has clearly gone into them really is something to behold. If you aren't ready to commit to an actual doll, they have small prints of different dolls that are available for $20 each.  Other art goes along with the "Halloween all year" type feel of the place. There are large portraits of Frankenstein, The Bride of Frankenstein, and Vampira among others. All of the art here is very different from other galleries and appeals to a certain type of person, namely the type of person who wishes to adorn their home with conversation pieces rather than the same old "picture on a wall".

This place is kind of a trip. I came here not really knowing what I was getting into: there is no menu online and I was just getting food here based on Yelp reviews. It was a Friday night and I wanted some take out, so I decided this was as good a night as any for an adventure.  So, I stopped in and they are blasting merengue/salsa music. I get it: it's Friday night- time to party. The waitress handed me a menu and I knew right then this place was legit- the menu is completely in Spanish. I noticed they had a Cuban sandwich, so I pointed to it (the waitress didn't speak English very well) and I gave her the signal for "to go" and I sat and waited. The food came out pretty quickly and I was on my way.  I got home and dug into the sandwich. WHOA! Okay, this is pretty delicious. This isn't what I would call a "classic" Cuban, but it was delicious shredded pork and cheese on pressed bread, so I was pretty happy. The sandwich was really big and came with a side a fries; it was a total steal at $9.  If I'm being honest, if I was dining in, the music would have been a little much for me. It's a small place and it was blasting, but hey- run your business how you want. I was really happy with my take out experience and I would absolutely stop back in and get that sandwich again.

Santos is the newest incarnation at this spot at 1135 Decatur. It seems there have been A LOT of different bars here over the years, but since this bar is owned and operated by the same people who run The Saint on St. Mary, hopefully it will stick.  We were here semi-early on a Saturday night and it was pretty quiet. I do like the vibe here- it's a little spooky and cool and there's a nice dance floor where I assume they will have music. They have some good local beers on tap, which is always a plus for me and the bartender was friendly. The bar seems a lot nicer than when other businesses were here- I'm not sure if they have done a full on renovation, but I like what they've done with the place. I'm excited to see what type of events they host here in the future.

I have a mission this year: track down all of the snow ball stands on the Westbank and try/review them. I'm no hero and you don't have to thank me. I'm doing the Lord's work.  Snow World was my first stop and this is a cute little stand that used to be called "Van's Snowballs" when I was a kid. We came around 7 and there was a nice little line. I ordered a 12oz strawberry cheesecake for a little over dollar. The ice was finely shaved like any good snowball and there was plenty of juice. The flavor itself wasn't overly strong with the "cheesecake" part of the flavor, but it was very sweet and I enjoyed it. Even though there was a long line and multiple orders, the folks in the stand got everyone through pretty quickly.  Bonus points: they have a "clear" bubblegum flavor for those of you who like bubblegum, but don't want to turn your teeth blue.

Ahh. Being in this place brought back a lot of memories. This used to be where the Westbank Bennigan's location was and I came here all the time as a kid. Oddly enough, not much has changed on the inside. Sure, all of the Bennigan's knick knacks are gone and replaced with Mexican decor, but the layout is exactly the same.  I have discovered that I am pretty easy to please when it comes to Tex-Mex type food: basically as long as it's cooked well and has cheese on it, I'm happy. I was here on a night that I happened to be craving a serious burrito, so that's what I got. The burrito platter comes with a good sized burrito topped with tomato sauce and cheese with rice and lettuce, tomato, guacamole and sour cream on the side. I was really impressed, especially considering this platter is under $10. Everything had a lot of flavor and although the rice could have been cooked a little longer, I still enjoyed it.  The staff was friendly enough and everything came out pretty quickly, especially considering we were here during the dinner rush. I will definitely be dining here again.

Time for a review update! Wisp has worked their magic yet again! My laptop (the same one from the last review) was having charging issues again and, sure enough, it needed a new charge port. Also, I had had a cracked screen for well over a year and had them fix that as well, just as long as they were going to be doing things with it. Well, in a day they fixed the port and the screen and my computer is back to work! Yay! They always do such a good job here and I would never bring my computer anywhere else. I use my laptop for my job, so downtime is a "no go" for me. Thankfully, they work fast at Wisp!  The staff is friendly, the work is exceptional and the prices are fair.

NOLA is a fantastic local brewery run by kind people who know their way around the hops. Really nice facility with a room full of all of the NOLA beer taps so that you can treat yourself to free samples every Friday at 2 during the brewery tour.

It's a bookstore. It gets the job done, doesn't it?  I really like B&N because they always seem to have whatever I am looking for, no matter how obscure it is. Really. You can be looking for a book that hasn't been in print since the 80's and it's very likely that this place will have at least one copy of it.   They also have a really big selection of magazines here. I was able to find Burlesque Bible, a magazine that is on the more expensive end and that I hadn't been able to locate anywhere else in town. I thought I was going to have to order it online and pay shipping when I spotted it here. Fantastic!  If you are looking for something specific, in the reading material department, this should definitely be your first stop.

This is a review of drinks at the bar.  We stopped in here for some pre-party drinks before the Yelp awards. I think I was here ages ago (over 10 years) for dinner, but I can't really remember. I digress. We sat at the bar and decided to get a beer and a cranberry and vodka. The draft was down, so I had to get a bottled beer, which wasn't really an issue. When it was time to get the check it came to $16 for just those two drinks. Now, keep in mind there was house vodka in the mixed drink and I had a local beer.  I get it- I'm in tourist country. These places are going to charge what they know they can get from out-of-towners. And I guess it wouldn't have left such a bad taste in my mouth if I had been able to get the draft beer I wanted in the first place. I wouldn't have even minded the price if the place was a little fancier (Galatoire's, Arnaud's, etc.), but it felt like a bit of a rip off considering this is a "walk in off the street" kind of establishment.  I'm not sure if they do a happy hour. If they don't, they should and cut us locals a break. Not a bad place, just know what you're getting when you visit.

It was a gorgeous Sunday when David suggested we take the ferry to the French Quarter, have lunch and sight see. It was the day of the Barkus parade and we knew there would be a lot of people out and about. I love this ferry. I don't utilize it all that much, but it's a great way to see the city and take some pictures (if that's your thing). On a clear day you can see St. Louis Cathedral as you ride across. As others have said, it costs $2 per person each way and they don't give change which is a bit shady. I get that it would take time to give everyone change, but it's still a little weird.  On a nice breezy day, a ferry ride is a great way to get to and from the city and you don't have to worry about driving, which is always a plus.

This is a really cute shop and if you're into the "old timey" kind of decor like I am, you are sure to love it.  Think back to the days of old metal signs, small gas stations, corner stores and soda shops and you will understand exactly what this store is all about. They offer a wide variety of "not so modern"-day items that are good conversation pieces and fun things to add to any collection. One thing that caught my eye was the hot air balloon mobile. I have no need for one, but I was tempted to get it just to add it to my home.  A few things are a little bit ridiculous and out there. I had to roll my eyes at the portraits of different generations of presidents playing poker- not exactly something I would want in my study. Other things are cool: they have some unique decanters, wall art, compasses, jewelry and much more.  If you're into things from "yesterday", this is a great place to visit.

I might have found my new uptown coffee house!    I was disappointed when Rue de la Course, on Magazine, closed and I was trying to figure out where I was supposed to get good coffee in the Uptown area, without having to drive all the way over to the Rue on Oak.  I found a new home at Mojo!  Not only does Mojo have a nice and cozy atmosphere, but their iced coffee is amazing.  I got a large and finished it in no time.  I wanted another, but I decided that I didn't want to be so caffeinated  that I could fly, so I opted against a second cup.  I will definitely be going back for this delicious coffee next time I am in the area.

This is a super-cool new interactive art experience that is just what the doctor ordered, for these pandemic times.  Around every corner is a pop of color or a bit of New Orleans magic and a reminder of what makes the city so great.  Whether you're a local New Orleanian, or you're just visiting The Big Easy, the experience will make you smile and you'll leave with a new appreciation for the city and its people.  One of my favorite rooms was Bling Bayou by Pompadour Productions. This glittery bayou shines under the moonlight as a sparkly alligator looks on. Look up and see a Spanish moss-covered light that seems to twinkle under the stars. Use your QR code to learn about 9 amazing hiking trails near New Orleans.  One of the best parts of the JAMNOLA experience is the personalized microsite. When you arrive at the experience, you scan a QR code on your phone, enter your email address and you're given a link to a custom site where you can learn more about each art room.  There are also ways to use your personalized QR code to interact with different exhibits. Click one link on your site and learn all about po-boys. Click another and learn about the cultural tradition of Spirit Trees. This is a fun way to learn more about the artists, and their vision for each space, long after you've left the building.  *Portions of this review was originally written, by me, for Very Local New Orleans. Read the full story here: https://nola.verylocal.com/jamnolas-permanent-art-pop-up-is-all-the-fun-youve-missed-during-quarantine/159123/

Great place for window shopping, especially if you are trying to waste a little time waiting for a movie to start at the theater. Fantastic stores that are really nice with an upscale feel. There are a little expensive, but not too bad.   One complaint-man oh man do I hate the parking garage attached to this place. It is super narrow and has one of those "roundabouts" that get you from one floor to the next. I am always so scared that I'm going to hit the wall. So yeah, I'm a chicken, so I just end up parking in the lot right across the street in order to save my sanity.

What a fantastic company!  Recently, I needed my 16 year old sofa partially reupholstered and I also needed the reclining function fixed on one side. The owner came to the house, looked at the sofa, assessed what needed to be done and made the arrangements for the sofa to be picked up so that they could work their "magic".  After a little over a week, my sofa was ready and in excellent, like-new condition! Not only did they reupholster two cushions and fix the recliner, but they also added necessary padding to certain cushions as well as the arm rest. The sofa has never looked better and I couldn't be happier with the results!  I would highly recommend this company for their great communication, excellent service and good pricing.

I just started going to Dr. Connell after my other dentist retired. t Dr. Connell and his staff are fantastic.  Extremely friendly and personable.  The dental assistant who worked on me was very nice and was quick to explain things to me.

Ooh tasty!  I had had Chez Pierre pastries before at bridal shows I've worked, so they were definitely on my list of places to visit. David brought me here when we were in the mood for something sweet and the spot didn't disappoint.  I got a strawberry Napoleon and David got a huge piece of red velvet cake. My Napoleon was delicious with thick cream inside and big piece of strawberry. It wasn't overly sweet and it satisfied my sweet tooth nicely. I only wish that the crust on top had been a little flakier and easier to pierce with my fork- I ended up having to pick it off and eat it like a cracker. David's cake was big and easily big enough for two people, if you're looking to share.  They also have a full menu of Vietnamese food here, so you can get lunch along with your dessert, if you wish.

What is the deal with this place? I'm starting to understand why Winn-Dixie is closing down. I rarely find myself here unless there's some kind of special going on. For whatever reason, they run out of their special items by noon on the day it starts.   Here are some examples: I was here during Mardi Gras to get one of their special creme king cakes. I got here early on the day the special started. The cakes they had out looked old and the creme was melting off. The lady working in the bakery department told me that she would make me a fresh one and set it aside for me the next day. She did so, but why not have fresh cakes out on the day of the special?  There was recently a special on steaks. I got here noon on the day the special started (Saturday). Steaks are gone. Really, I suspect they just didn't put them out and the guy working looked at me all confused when I asked if he had more steaks. He didn't know what was up.  I've been in here where the chicken is OBVIOUSLY not fresh. I've seen items in the butcher improperly wrapped and juice dripping out of the package. Boy, I tell you what- y'all better get it together. It's bad enough that Winn-Dixie is consistently over priced, but to try to pass off bad product is just a bad idea.

I can't believe that I have never reviewed this quaint little Magazine St. bakery. I believe the ownership changed hands a while ago, but I've always loved this place.  I was here today for quick work meeting and every meeting is better with yummy iced coffee and croissants. La Boulangerie has both along with cake, pastries, sandwiches, soups and much more.   There was a decent crowd for a Thursday lunch hour, but it wasn't terrible and everyone was masked up (pandemic-era review). My only complaint was that it was a bit warm inside, but I know how a.cs have trouble keeping up with the intense NOLA summers, so that wasn't a big deal.

Owner Jason Gonzalez has had his Gonzo's storefront for about a year, but his food has already amassed a loyal following of fans far and wide. He works all week getting his meat ready for the public and his selection is spectacular: brisket, beef ribs, pulled pork, burnt ends, turkey breast, chicken thighs and barbocoa boudin, all served by the half-pound or pound (or more!), and cut fresh when you order. They're only open on Fridays, so be sure to get there early before they sell-out. Even better, Gonzo's takes pre-orders (up to 50 a week), if you want to make sure that you will be in that tasty number.  I had the brisket plate ($12) with brisket mac ($4.50) and corn grits with Gouda cheese ($4.50). As soon as Jason sliced up this meat in front of me, I could see why this place has already made a name for itself.
