Big chunks of juicy, thick brisket cooked to perfection with a gorgeous crust that made my mouth water. Digging into it, I was not only blown away by the flavor, but how tender it was. It crumbled nicely under my fork and I was easily able to cut through it like butter. The brisket mac was THICK. That's the only way I can describe it- they were generous with the cheese and the bits of brisket mixed in pushed it to the next level. The corn grits with Gouda cheese is made with butter and the menu promised they would be creamy; I wasn't disappointed. The flavor of both of these sides was beyond rich and totally worth the drive.  As I was eating here, I was actually planning my next visit. I was making plans to order ahead, so that I could sample the boudin, pulled pork and turkey. I was contemplating getting another order of the brisket mac to-go. Needless to say: Gonzo's gave me everything I could want in a barbecue place; the food here is what I think of when I think of good barbecue.  I made a list of best hidden BBQ for Very Local New Orleans and this l restaurant was on it! Read it here: https://nola.verylocal.com/bbq-new-orleans/228292/

New Orleans is full of different burlesque shows, troupes and acts.  In a sea of traditional burlesque, the Dirty Dime Peepshow stands out. Bella Blue is the producer and she never disappoints.    Edgy and fun, the Dirty Dime features seasoned performers, as well as new talent.  It is so much fun, and if you are a Burlesque "virgin", you will definitely cut your teeth quickly here.

During the Yelp event at Pearl, I decided to duck into this neat little Farmer's Market and see what they had to offer. What I found was one more reason why Mid City is so great. This small market offers a whole variety of things such as fresh fruits and vegetables and fresh caught seafood. The woman working the seafood table mentioned that the shrimp and crabs she had were caught the day before- it doesn't get much better than that.  I didn't get anything this time, but I this is definitely a neat little addition to the area, especially when the weather is nice and you are headed to a wine tasting at Pearl on a Thursday. All of the vendors are local, so you are supporting local businesses by shopping here and I found them all to be friendly.

I was super impressed by this PJ's! I just stopped in for a quick coffee and a croissant, but considering it's in the Quarter, I was happy that it was only $6. Don't you hate places that upcharge, due to location?  This shop was following all proper Covid precautions and Julie (I think that was her name) was super nice. Stop in, if you're in the area!

This is easily one of the best Dollar Trees in the area.  I stop in here regularly to get cheap flowers for my mom's grave, which is right around the corner (the grave is outside, so super-nice silk flowers would be a waste). They always seem to have the cutest accessories for sale and the last time I was here I got some St. Patrick's Day socks (on sale the first week of January) and a gaudy Shamrock thing to stick on my Irish mother's grave, which I'm sure she appreciated.  The staff is always nice and I always find whatever I need. Big win!

WOW! What a fantastic find! We just happened to run into this place when we were on our way to a comedy show in the area and decided that it would be best to eat first. I knew nothing about Silk Road when I walked in the door, but after checking a few Yelp reviews, I figured it was worth a try.  First of all, upon entering, we were immediately greeted by one of the owners who mentioned that they were having a complimentary wine tasting and we should head to the back and help ourselves. After trying the wine, we looked over the menu. A vast array of options lay before us.  Upon the recommendation of fellow yelpers, I decided to start with the lemon grass crab bisque. It was incredible! It was full of flavor and tasted very earthy. It was different, but I loved it. For my entree, I decided to get three tacos- two beef and one chicken. They are served in soft tortillas with their house made salsa verde and pico de gallo. Look, I'm going to go ahead and be super honest with you here- no exaggeration, these are probably some of the best tacos that I have ever had in my entire life. They were PACKED with tons of flavor and so full of meat and pico that I had trouble getting them into my mouth to take a proper bite. If I had known they were so big I would have gotten two instead of three. No, scratch that. I'm glad I got three because I took one home and ate it for lunch the next day.  After dinner, the owner chatted with us for a bit and he was so nice and made us feel very welcome. They will even box up your leftovers for you. It's a small thing, but I love that extra touch. The overall atmosphere of this restaurant is extremely friendly and welcoming. There is a nice neighborhood vibe without the place feeling like a dive. They even sell beer and wine by the bottle, in case you are just in the mood to have a drink and relax.  I will definitely be returning to Silk Road sooner rather than later.

I like Metairie Cemetery so much that I did my 6th grade social studies project on it. There was a time where I could tell you about the specific types of tombs throughout the cemetery and some of the more notable people buried therein. Alas, that was a long time ago, so now I can only wax poetic about the beauty in the design of these gorgeous resting places.  I've been a regular visitor to Metairie Cemetery throughout my life. We have family buried here and my parents knew and worked with quite a few people who ended up here. The graves are gorgeous and beautifully designed and it seems that each one holds a different story. I think a few of my favorites are the one that is shaped like a pyramid complete with sphinx, the Angel of Grief which is in a locked enclosure, but can be viewed through a window and the grave with the statue of the woman knocking on the door with flowers in her hand. Some of the more notable folks buried here include local legends Mel Ott and Louis Prima.  If I'm being honest, there is something slightly creepy, if not beautiful, about this cemetery. If you are here around sunset you definitely get some chills, especially if you are near the graves with the statues with faces somewhat worn off due to time or other where the heads have been knocked off. It's always pretty quiet here and if you visit, remember that it is a cemetery so be respectful. The style of Metairie Cemetery is something that makes New Orleans unique. I'm glad that it is looked after and taken care of.

Well, this place just came out of nowhere!  We were waiting to get lunch at Blue Giant, so we popped in here for some coffee while waiting to be called. This is such a cute shop in a nice developed part of Magazine St.  The space is bright with big windows and there is plenty of space outside for sitting. The shop is right next door to a work out studio and right across from Claret, so you are going to have a lot of people to mingle with.  The coffee I had was great and I was delighted to see that they offer a full menu of snacks and sandwiches, that are sure to keep you satisfied. They also offer free wifi, if you're looking to get some work done.

Yakuza House is putting a twist on what you think sushi is. You aren't going to find typical rolls here. You're going to get hand rolls that are made right in front of you, sandos, and other delicious food made fresh by the chef.   The place is small, so you're going to need reservations, but it's definitely worth it. I sat at the bar, so that I could watch Chef work his magic. I had salmon belly nigiri, a sando, and the Nibbles hand roll set, which came with three kinds of hand rolls--salmon, bay scallop and blue crab, which were served fresh when I was ready for them.   If you sit at the bar, the chef will keep an eye on your plate and serve you the hand rolls as you need them. There are only four tables in the entire restaurant, so don't expect a huge place.   I really think Yakuza House is going to be the next hot restaurant on the scene, so get in while you can.  I wrote about this spot for Offbeat Magazine's Offbeat Eats column. Check it out here: https://www.offbeat.com/articles/dining-out-yakuza-house/

It's become a tradition among some NOLA Yelpers to make every 100th review a "milestone" review. It was tough trying to decide what my 2,000th review should be, but after much consideration, I settled on reviewing this local favorite for this very special review.   I have lived in New Orleans my entire life and I had never set foot in the original Willie Mae's. Oh sure, I had tried their chicken at their short-lived St. Charles Avenue location, but I had a feeling that I hadn't tasted Willie Mae's until I had it here. When I found myself in the neighborhood for work, we saw the line was short so we decided to pop in.  As I said, there was a line at about 11:00 am, but it was short and moved fast and we were inside and seated within about 10 minutes. Once we sat down, out waiter was on top of it- he came right over and handed us menus and took our drink orders. I already knew what I was getting: white meat fried chicken meal with mac and cheese and a side of fried okra. Once we ordered, the food came out fairly quickly. Not shocking, since it seems that they have perfected the fine art of getting people in and out as quickly as possible.  The food looked amazing: big pieces of crispy chicken with creamy mac and cheese and peas on the side. I started with a wing it was really good- nice and juicy with just enough "crunch". I then tore into the breast, which was equally juicy, but sadly, the wet batter was so thick that it wasn't quite cooked all the way through. The chicken was cooked perfectly, but the batter was cakey in some spots. They probably should have left this one in a little longer. The mac and cheese was excellent and the fried okra was plentiful and delicious.  The place itself is small, so that's why there's a line. Also, when we were here, I'm pretty sure that we were the only locals. This place has been Bourdain'd and Zimmern'd to death, which is great for them, but tends to keep some of the locals away and draw in the tourists. And yes Anthony, everyone knows what to order, but there IS a menu. Calm down.  All in all the food was good. Was it the best chicken I've ever had in my life? Am I going to be standing in that super long line at Fried Chicken Fest just to get my fix? Not quite, but there's a charm about this place and it's a definite New Orleans institution that everyone should visit at least once, if for no other reason than to say you tried it. It's a part of New Orleans culture and one of those places that makes our city so special.

Really, how can you give Jackson Square anything less than 5 stars?  When you talk Jackson Square, you are talking classic New Orleans. The majesty of St. Louis Cathedral and the statue of Andrew Jackson that are synonymous with New Orleans and the magic of the city. The artists selling their masterpieces, street musicians putting on a show and fortune tellers that will tell you what your future holds.   You know, when you get right down to it, the best parts of this city really are free. I love that you can just walk around and take it all in. Jackson Square is as good as it gets. It's the second thing that people think of when they think of New Orleans and we wouldn't have it any other way.

Bayou Beer Garden is a good place to go see some live music or comedy.  I agree with Shannon's comment that the main draw is the huge patio.  The bar itself is basically an old house that has been converted and the whole "backyard area" is where the deck and patio is.  This is where bands perform.  It's well lit and has Christmas style lights for atmosphere.  Admittedly, I haven't been here in a really long time, but the last time I was here, the inside was really smoky.  This probably isn't a place I would go unless a band I really wanted to see was playing.

Take out only, and they have some outdoor seating, but unless you want to sit in the hot sun, your best bet is probably just taking it to go.   On the day I was here, they had a boudin special, so that's what I got. I got it with a side of potato salad and mustard greens. The boudin was really good, although I think I would have enjoyed it more if it was a little spicier. I always like my boudin to be on the spicier side.   The potato salad and mustard greens were perfect and balance out the sausage well. The process is pretty easy, you go to the window and order, and the food comes out pretty quickly. All of my food cost $11, so I'm not complaining. I will definitely be back; the food was great.  I made a list of best hidden BBQ for Very Local New Orleans and this l restaurant was on it! Read it here: https://nola.verylocal.com/bbq-new-orleans/228292/

There's a new sweet shop on Magazine and this could get dangerous. I had been pretty much stalking the opening of this place since I heard it was happening. I love Haydel's pastries, but I never get out to Jefferson to have any. In fact, I think I have really only had them at events. Being able to pop in and get some yummies to go was an exciting prospect.  I stopped in today and the shop is adorable. They have some good treats such as full cakes, cake bars, petit fours, croissants, muffins, eclairs and a few other sweet indulgences. They also serve French Market coffee, so you can get some caffeine to really make all of the sugar pop. I got a blueberry muffin and a petit four. Both were obviously super fresh and delicious and I liked that the muffin was packed with blueberries. My iced coffee was tasty as well and paired perfectly with the pastries.  The staff was gracious and helped me decide exactly what I was in the mood for. The shop itself is small and there's no seating, so it's one of those "grab and go" type of places. I'm sure that they will start getting a nice little crowd as soon as word gets out and especially during the madness of carnival season. I'm excited to go back soon and try some more goodies.

Long overdue update!!  Since my last review, smoking has been "outlawed" in bars, so that isn't an issue. The outdoor patio has its own bar with TONS of beer on tap- local and otherwise.   The vibe is fun and I love that there's a lot of space out there. There are big TVs that are great for game watching and the staff is friendly and fun. There's still the indoor area if that's more your thing, but the draw is that awesome patio/bar situation.  This spot is a Mid-City gem and I will definitely be visiting more often.

Morning Call is back!  I was so excited to see that this new location of Morning Call has finally opened! The gorgeous new building has tons of outdoor seating and the staff is as fantastic as ever. If you have been missing Morning Call's delicious beignets and cafe au lait, this new venture won't disappoint. They have all the classic delicious on the menu, including other bites like red beans and rice.   I stopped in for some tasty cold cafe au lait and sit outside and watched the world go by on a lovely spring day. The weather couldn't have been nicer and the staff could not have been more efficient. I didn't partake in the beignets this time, but Morning Call beignets are some of my favorites.   I'm so glad that Morning Call has found a home in the City Park area. Judging by the crowd today, I predict that there's going to be a lot of people getting their beignet fix at this spot, in the future.  The only negative I see is the tight parking. It's very limited, and the lot is small, so be careful, especially when you are looping around the building trying to find a spot. Other than that, I have zero complaints.  I am definitely going to make this a regular stop.

This is a review of an outdoor event that Velvet Cactus put on for Cinco de Mayo.  So, usually I don't like reviewing a place based on an event experience, but I had food and drinks here, so here we are. I was here last week for the Velvet Cactus Cinco de Mayo celebration. This is a 3 day out door party that consisted of food, drinks and different bands.  On the day I went, it was packed. The Molly Ringwalds were set to play and they had a huge stage set up in their parking lot. There were different booths where you could get food, margaritas, beer, and soft drinks. The main reason I wanted to review was because of how they handled the crowd. The place was PACKED and the staff got people through the lines quickly with barely any wait.  While I was here I tried the frozen margaritas and the pork tacos. The margarita was delicious and the tacos were outstanding! For $9 you got three tacos that were PACKED with delicious pork that was spiced perfectly. I had never really had any desire to go here, but after trying these tacos, I know I will be back for more.  Another thing that impressed me was how clean they kept the indoor bathrooms. I don't use port-o-lets if I can avoid it and the staff was cool with people coming in and using the restrooms inside. They stayed on top of keeping the area clean and stocked with everything you might need- it was great.  I am definitely going to return to Velvet Cactus for more tacos and to sample more of their menu.

Because it took me SO LONG to check this place out, and because I am now well on my way to being a mega-fan, I thought it only appropriate to make review #1400 St. Roch Market.  Let me just start by saying I knew nothing of the old St. Roch Market and that disappoints me, because I know that before Katrina it was considered a New Orleans institution where locals could go and buy produce and food at an affordable price. With that said, I have to say that I love the new incarnation of the market.  I like that parking is fairly simple- the first time I was here I scored a spot right next to the building with no hassle and the second time I parked in the lot, which is a nice size and has plenty of space and is located on the right side of the building. The market itself is a delight: they have fresh produce, smoothies, desserts, coffee, sandwiches, crepes, and even a bar. They are open early, so you can come for breakfast or just stop in and grab your lunch to go.  The first time I was here I treated myself to iced coffee at Coast Roast and a taco salad at La Mezcla. The second time I was here I got another iced coffee and a yummy sandwich at Dirty Dishes. And if you are really feeling wild, you can mix and match different food from different places in the market.  All of the proprietors here are local, so when you spend your money here, you are spending it on local businesses. The staff is quick about getting plates and utensils out of your way when you are finished and the space itself is beyond clean and very well maintained. One suggestion: if you are planning to eat lunch here on a weekend, go a little earlier or later because it gets really packed around noon and it can be hard to find a place to sit. On my second visit I went to lunch at 12:30, on a weekday, and it wasn't packed at all. There is even seating outside, for those nice days when it isn't too hot.  Although I don't live in the area, I do think that this is a good addition to the neighborhood. I know that some people have called it "overpriced", but I didn't find that at all. Sure, I'm not going to spend $9 on lunch every single day, but every now and then it's nice to treat yourself. I am definitely going to make St. Roch Market a habit.

Computer problems: always a pain, right?  I was recently having an issue where I would plug my laptop in and it wouldn't charge. After exhausting my computer repair skills by replacing the charger and the battery and still not fixing the issue, I decided to pop into Wisp and see if they could help me. I brought in my laptop and, after explaining the issue, they said that I probably needed a new charge port and it would cost me $100 and take a few days. Okay, not terrible.   An hour or two later someone from Wisp called me and said that I could come get my laptop, as the issue had been fixed. It turns out I didn't need a new charge port at all; there was just a minor connection issue between my battery and laptop and it was an easy fix. It was such an easy fix, that they didn't even charge me anything to fix it. I thought that was really cool of them, because they could have asked for $20 and I would have happily given it to them.  The folks here are super honest and good at what they do. I hope I never need their services in the future, but if I do I know that my computer is in good hands.

Thanks to Dennis G, who reviewed the Metairie location for reminding me that I owe this place a review.  Wow.  I can't believe I have never reviewed this place!  I seriously eat here probably once a month.  Now, Piccadilly isn't one of those places that you go to for a fancy dining experience, but the food is like home cooking to me, probably because I have been coming here since I was a kid.  I always get the dilly plate, which is an entree', two sides and a piece of bread for under 8 bucks.  You really can't beat that.  I usually get the fried catfish, mashed potatoes and gravy and broccoli with a soft roll.  It's always good and fresh and it always leaves me satisfied.  Also, I don't often get dessert, but when I do I get the chocolate pudding.  This place is pretty awesome.  I know there are people who have never been and would never want to try it, but this place reminds me of my childhood when I would go with my grandmother to lunch.  They also have take out, if you don't want to sit down and eat!

WOW. Why would anyone ever go to Acme?  Stopped in here for lunch on a Sunday afternoon. The restaurant was pretty empty, and we were seated and served quickly. We started out with an order of a dozen raw oysters. OUT OF THIS WORLD. Fat and fresh. Amazing and soo good. I probably could have gotten another dozen and called it a day.  For my entree, I got a hot sausage po boy. This came topped with blue cheese cole slaw and had thin cut french fries on the side. I really liked that the sausage was "pattie style". It made it way easier to eat and handle. It was delicious and full of flavor. We also decided to split an order of onion rings. Not only did they bring out a lot of rings, but they were huge and perfectly fried.  So, seriously. Why would you wait in line at Acme when Felix's has everything you need? Mine is just one more positive review to add to the pile.

I grabbed some post-Yelp event drinks here with Steve, and although the place was on the slower side on this particular night, I had a good time. The bartender was really friendly and I was happy to see that they offer Not Your Father's Root Beer, which I happily sipped on. I like that the bar is a little dark and somewhat tucked away just enough to make it feel like a hide out. I want to come back on a night that there are a few more people here and I would love to see a drag show.

Went tonight for "industrial" night at my friend Travis' suggestion.  Good bar.  Good crowd.  Good music.  I have seen a burlesque show here in the past, and the place was packed.  From what I hear, it is a lot how "Krystal" and "Dervish" used to be.  I can't speak to that, it was before my time.  I went and had a good time.

Ooooh Coolinary! As soon as I saw Pascal's on the Coolinary list I knew that I had to finally make my way over there. We were here for a late lunch on a Friday and we pretty much had the place to ourselves. I already knew what I was going to be getting, so I just dove right in.  First, I started with some raw oysters. Since this is one of the things Pascal's is known for, I felt that it was a must. Oysters weren't on the Coolinary menu, but I made the executive decision to go off route in the name of oyster deliciousness. Also, it was National Oyster Day, so I pretty much had to. There were fat, salty and perfect and they satisfied my oyster craving immediately.  I also started off with their Caprese salad. This was yummy mozzarella served on a bed of fresh tomatoes with a balsamic vinaigrette. The flavors in this dish were out of this world and beyond anything that I expected. It was a perfectly refreshing start to the meal.  For my entree I got the alfredo ravioli which is stuffed ravioli in a cream sauce. This dish was HUGE. This was way more than I expected from a "special deal" type menu. The cream sauce was rich and the flavors of the ravioli mixed with the sauce was perfection. It was out of this world and what I would call a "must order".  For dessert I had the bread pudding. I am usually not a fan of bread pudding (texture) but this version was excellent. It was firm and not gooey as some are and the sauce it was served with was excellent- sweet with a bit of tartness.  Of course, service here was incredible and even though we were the only people here we didn't feel rushed at all. I know I have to go back and try their famous BBQ shrimp. After the memorable experience I had here, I am excited to return.

David and I wanted to try a new spot for our third anniversary, so after doing some research, I chose the much raved about Justine.  We were greeted by the friendly staff when we walked in and, because we had made reservations, we were seated immediately. We were seated in a booth area right across from the kitchen, which was nice and kind of tucked away. The atmosphere of the restaurant is very nice with a modern feel mixed with some older, classic touches.  The waiter brought us a glass of celebratory champagne as we looked over the menu. I decided to get the trout amandine on a bed of green beans and David got the prime rib au jus which came with a side of fries. I loved my trout! This is one of my favorite dishes and Justine's version was excellent. I loved that it was piled high with almond slivers for an extra crunch and the fish itself was cooked perfectly- buttery and melt-in-your-mouth texture. David loved his prime rib. It was a huge cut of meat and it looked yummy- nice and pink in the middle.  For dessert, we got a cake and I'm kicking myself because I can't quite recall the name of it. It was light and not too sweet and the perfect end to the meal.  All in all I liked it here. My one complaint was that the music was REALLY loud (it was a Saturday night and I think that there were trying to get the crowd pumped up for their evening), but other than that it was fantastic and I'd return.

Morbid curiosity is what brought me here. I had passed this place tons of times and constantly wondered what it was all about. I had definitely asked myself more than once, "Why would a bar choose to have a toilet theme?" Well, I still don't know the answer to that question, but I finally made it here.  The place is a lot bigger than I expected and on this particular night the place was packed. Even though there were a ton of people here, the bartender was fast and friendly. There's a large space so there were people dancing and others just sitting at the bar chatting.  This is a cool little chill spot. I don't know if I'll be back. I feel like my question has been answered about this place, but I'm glad that I went once.

This is a fancy little bar located in the Windsor Court. A friend and I stopped in here to get a drink before heading out to dinner. I really like the nice upscale decor. It feels as if you are in someone's really nice home. They have a whole array of fancy cocktails, but instead of a cocktail, I just decided to get a beer. I really liked that there was a pianist playing "background music" as we chatted on one of the many sofas.  I would definitely love to go back here on a date, as I think it would be the perfect spot to start a romantic evening.

This is such a great rentable space with lots of light and big windows and mirrors. Most people rent this spot to practice dancing, but I recently had a photo shoot here it was the perfect area to convert into a quick studio.  They let you rent the rooms by the hour and I love the open area of the room, the abundance of natural light and all of the space we had to work with. The staff here has always been nothing but kind to me whenever I have found myself here. There is a small kitchen space downstairs with a few snacks and coffee, if you plan on being here for a while.

"Why Marielle? Why do you do it to yourself? The Company Burger is a hop and a skip from here. You know it's your favorite. Why didn't you just go there? Frostop is right across the street. Felipe's is RIGHT THERE. Yet, you chose a place that you knew would suck. LOL U DUM."  That is what was going through my head during lunch today. I was bopping around this college neighborhood and stopped for coffee when I noticed a Bud's across the street. Since I was hungry and Bud's is mostly decent, I stopped in. Well, I should have listened to the elderly Greek man who was encouraging me to try Pyramids Cafe next door. "It's better than THAT.", he tried to convince me. But I had already decided I wanted a burger, so I ignored his pleas and headed into Bud's.  I was delighted that there was zero crowd during lunch. In hindsight, I should have taken it as a sign. I stepped up and ordered. The woman who took my order was very nice and friendly and I appreciated that. I got a #3: meat, cheddar, mustard, mayo and onions and an order of onion rings. As I waited, I noticed that I was the only non college kid in here. Another sign that I ignored.  Let me say this- Bud's needs to do something about their buns. There is NOTHING appetizing about a burger on an ice cold bun. In fact, it's down right off putting. Pop that thing in a toaster oven for 20 seconds. That should give it at least a little warmth. The burger was okay, but nothing great. The thing that bumped this from 2 stars to 3 were the onion rings. They were actually pretty fantastic, lightly battered and tasty.  Would I go back? Nah. I should have gone to Frostop or something, but you live and you learn.

Ooh! My friend took me to brunch here, and since I had never been, I was pretty excited.  Looking over the menu, everything looked amazing. First, warm cornbread was brought to the table. It was just like homemade and it was delicious. This was a great way to start the meal.  For our appetizer, we decided to try the bacon salad and the fried green tomatoes. The salad was amazing and came with a delicious mix of lettuce, apple slices and bacon. I feel that bacon really does make anything better, and this salad was no exception. The fried green tomatoes came out warm with crab on top and a creamed spinach topping. They too were amazing.  For my entree, I got the crabmeat and shrimp fritata. It was really good with tomatoes, cheese and mushrooms mixed in. I kind of wish it had a little more crab meat in it, but there was plenty of good sized shrimp, so that made up for it. My friend got the eggs Boudreaux, which was crabmeat and poached eggs topped with hollandaise and duck cracklins. I was able to try some of this dish, and as good as mine was, I was wishing that I had gotten this instead. The eggs were perfectly cooked and the sauce on top was delicious. When I go back, I will definitely be ordering this for myself.  I understand that brunch is fairly new here, and I loved it Our waitress, Melissa was really nice and attentive and made sure that we had everything that we needed. I can't wait to return.

Probably closer to a 3.5.  I really like that this is a nice neighborhood coffee shop with outside seating. I was shocked at how packed it was at 11am. Really. It took me about 15 minutes from the time I ordered to the time I finally got my drink. It was nuts.  I ordered a mocha chip Mochassippi, which is basically their version of a frappuccino (which everyone knows, I'm sure). It was okay. Not as sweet as I was expecting, but all in all not bad.  The place is pretty loud inside, especially when there are a lot of people around, but you can reserve private rooms in the back for designated periods of time.  I'd go back, but probably after the morning rush.

It was the second Friday of Lent, and when my dad suggested we have lunch somewhere, I was a good Catholic and suggested a seafood restaurant. Not that Station 6 doesn't have meat, but a good rule of thumb is stick to what the place specializes in.  We were here a little after the lunch rush and were seated inside immediately. They also have lovely outdoor seating, but it was fairly warm on this day, so I chose to sit in the a.c. Looking over the menu, everything looked incredible. I had heard raves about quite a few dishes here, and I decided to go with the trout almondine.  The trout was perfectly prepared and was topped with a nice butter sauce. It also came with a side of new potatoes and asparagus, which I only ever enjoy in restaurants, so I consider that a treat. My photo doesn't do this dish justice at all: the fish was tender, juicy and full of flavor. The potatoes and asparagus were nice and buttery and all of the flavors of the food blended together wonderfully. The portion was light and great for lunch.  My one complaint is the wait time for the food. Usually when I go to a restaurant for lunch I expected to be in and out within about 45 minutes, max. Well, from the time we ordered to the time the food hit the table, 30 minutes had passed. I guess that one could argue it's because the meal was made-to-order and it takes time, but with only a few other people eating I was kind of baffled why it took so long. It's not a a big deal, but it's worth noting if you have a limited lunch hour.  The service here was excellent, I enjoyed the atmosphere and the food was delectable. I'll be back.

Oh no bb, whatisyoudoin?  We were a bit hungry this morning, so David and I decided to hit up Huddle House- the bastard cousin of Waffle House. Actually, that's a lie; Waffle House doesn't claim Huddle House. Huddle House is not welcome at the family reunion. We got here at 11 and since this is a "seat yourself" kind of place, we did just that. The diner was packed with the post-church crowd, but a waitress came over immediately and took our drink order.  After a few minutes, she came back and we ordered. I got grits, toast, bacon, eggs and hash browns. Even though they were slammed, they only had one guy working the griddle- for a packed house of people. What? Why? Needless to say, it was 45 minutes before our food was ready and David got his a few minutes before me.  Grits- okay, once you add salt. I'm not overly picky about diner grits. David didn't care for them at all.  Bacon- crispy and good- easily the highlight of the meal. It's hard to mess up bacon, so they don't get any gold stars for not burning it.  Eggs- Ohhhhhh no. I ordered the eggs over easy and they were rubbery and stiff. Two of them were hard and maybe one was medium. How do you cook three different eggs at, I assume, the same time and make them different consistencies? What a talent.   Hash browns- too crispy and a pathetic serving size. I don't need a pound of hash browns, but give me more than just a few bites. They had zero flavor and I had to add salt to even make them decent.  Toast- super thin and stingy on the butter.  Also, it was really warm in here. I understand that they have an "open" kitchen and they are cooking non stop, but crank that AC down to 60 if you have to.  The experience was probably more like 2.5 stars, but I'm not rounding up for this one. The waitress at least kept my coffee filled and brought the check quickly. I MIGHT go back on a day that is not so busy.

Allow me to add to the pile of praise for this lovely establishment. As soon as I heard that a fancy grilled cheese restaurant was opening in New Orleans, I was immediately on board. As soon as I got as taste of the deliciousness that is The Big Cheezy, I knew that this would have to be my 1100th review.  It took me forever to get here and when I finally did it was on a Thursday at about 7. I was thrilled that there was no one else here, so we were able to order quickly with zero wait. I had looked over the menu before I came, so I knew exactly what I wanted. The Flying Dutchman was in my future. With ingredients like gouda, turkey and bacon, it seemed like a no brainer. My dining companion wasn't so sure, but after a few minutes he decided to get the Crazy Old Goat, which was packed with goat cheese, monterey jack, bacon, grilled peppers and red pepper jelly. That sounded pretty amazing as well. We also got some waffle fries to munch on the side.  Because we are smart, we decided that we would split our sandwiches so we both got to taste both. We sat down and we didn't have to wait long at all because there was literally no one else in the place. As soon as the sandwiches came out I was SO excited. Gooey cheese was oozing our of the sides of both of these sandwiches. I could tell that the bread had been buttered (the only way to do it) and the sandwiches looked simple but delicious.  First I bit into my Flying Dutchman. There was so much cheese on this thing and it was melted perfectly. The cheese mixed with the turkey and the bacon to create and amazing and delectable experience. After I finished my half, I couldn't wait to switch. The Crazy Old Goat was so different! I loved how the cheese and the bacon made for a savory experience, the peppers added a little kick and the red pepper jelly added a bit of spicy sweetness. There was a lot happening on this thing and I loved every bit of it.  Both sandwiches that I tried were incredible and I can't wait to go back and try some more of The Big Cheezy menu. I would definitely suggest going later in the day, if you are like me and have no time for a line.

Wow Carreta's, I'm actually kind of impressed.  We stopped into Carreta's on a Saturday for lunch and the crowd was pretty thin. The waitress took our drink order immediately and within just a few minutes of ordering our food (about 10 minutes) we had it in front of us. My first thought was, "Uh oh, we have a reheat situation on our hands.", but it wasn't reheated at all (at least from what I could tell.).  I decided to do the "create your own" with the shredded chicken quesadilla and the shredded chicken flautas (two per order). For a grand total of 8.20, this is probably one of the best lunch deals in the city. The quesadilla was perfect- plenty of cheese mixed in with the juicy chicken and seasoned perfectly. The flautas were out of this world. They were hot and fresh and I really enjoyed them and the shell had just enough crunch to it. The combination of both the quesadilla and the flautas made for the perfect lunch.  I would absolutely return and try more of what Carreta's has on the menu. I am eager to try their burrito plate!

You guys. This place. Wow.  Where did this restaurant come from? Was this always here? Why am I just now discovering it?!  This restaurant is incredible and completely New Orleans. There is an AMAZING view of the river and delicious food. We were just here for appetizers and the view and this place didn't disappoint in either department. We ordered the fried calamari and the bacon wrapped olives. The calamari was amazing and the serving was huge, plenty enough for two people. The bacon wrapped olives were different and good.  My only tiny complaint was that it took a while for a waiter to acknowledge us, but as soon as he did, he was quite attentive. This would be a fabulous place for a date night and I will definitely be back.

The Elks trucks parade is a classic and it's the perfect end to Mardi Gras. The crowds are always a lot more laid back at this parade than at other parades, the riders are always really generous with the throws, and while the "floats" aren't anything overly fancy, they get the job done.  I pretty much grew up on truck parades. The sounds of a truck's horn and the smell of exhaust will probably remind me of Mardi Gras for the rest of my life. For this particular parade, I like to just sit back and relax somewhere on St. Charles Avenue and just watch it pass as I enjoy the day.  The best part of this parade is that it seems to go on and on almost without end. It's really entertaining and it's one of the few parades where people aren't chomping at the bit to get some fancy throw- they just enjoy it for what it is.

I'm gonna start by saying that I am NOT crafty at all, so I can't really give a review from a "crafters" point of view.  Michaels is a really cool store that has everything (or close to it) that a creative type could ever want.  Paints, beads, markers, crayons, and clay are just a few things you can get here.  What I really like about this store is, if you have a kid, you could take them in here and let them pick out a fun activity for them to do.  They sell things that you can paint and decorate, like wooden cutouts.  They have coloring books and crafts of all types.  If you get a child started with this kind of thing early, they will be creative for life.  It's also a good idea to pick up colors and crafts for a kids party or rainy days when a child needs something to do.  Michael's also carries frames and things like that.  Like I said, I'm not a person who is really into crafts, but if I were, this would be my spot.

Wow, fancy!  This place is HUGE and is located right before the Causeway Bridge. Seriously. Don't accidentally cross the bridge.  I came here for a photo shoot and at first I was a little confused. I mean, the building itself isn't hard to miss, but there are a bunch of different parking garages and I wasn't sure which one to park in. I pretty much just picked one at random. It turned out that parking is super cheap (mine was free) so it all worked out.  The lobby is huge when you first walk in and you feel like you are in an expensive New Orleans hotel and not out in the 'burbs somewhere. It was pretty impressive. The room is small, but gets the job done. Nothing overly special, but clean and efficient.

It's no secret that I love Mediterranean food and I am slowly trying every Mediterranean restaurant in the New Orleans area.  I stopped into Babylon Cafe for dinner and it was a fairly slow night. This is a "no frills" type of place, hence the "cafe" title, but I like the murals on the wall and the staff is friendly. I got an order of the beef shawarma which came with a side salad and yellow jasmine rice. I got hummus on the side, because it doesn't come with the dish.  The dish was a bit expensive at $17, but the serving was huge- easily enough food for two people to share and I had a ton of leftovers. The shawarma was tender, well spiced and delicious. The salad was perfect and fresh. And then there was the rice- what was in this rice?? This rice might be the best yellow jasmine rice I have ever had. I'm usually not a big fan of rice in dishes like this, because I find it a bit dry, but I couldn't get enough of it here.   I was disappointed in the hummus- for some reason it just lacked flavor to me. I usually like to spread the hummus on my meat (am I the only one?) and I didn't do that here because I almost felt as if it would have taken away from the flavor of the meat. I was also disappointed that it cost $2 or $3 for a side of hummus when I felt it really should have been included with the meal, especially considering the meal was $17.   Service was fantastic and the waitress was great about refilling drinks and checking on us regularly. I would return, but Babylon wouldn't be my first stop for Mediterranean.

This coffee shop is a lot like the tv show "The Wire"; everyone is telling me how good it is and I just don't get it.  Best coffee shop in New Orleans? Calm down, people. Let's not get carried away. First of all, I would call this place more of a cafe that serves coffee than a coffee shop. That's not a bad thing, just saying. I ordered a large iced coffee which came to a little over $4. Kind of steep compared to other places. It was okay, but not "OMGTHISISTHEBESTCOFFEEIHAVEEVERHADEVER!!!!" good.  For me, the ambiance left a little to be desired. I like small, cozy coffee places. This place had a small restaurant feel. Again, not a bad thing, just not what I expect from a coffee shop. The music was pretty loud and if I was trying to get work done, I would have had to go elsewhere.  I saw that they have a pretty extensive menu. They serve vegan tomato soup. Isn't all tomato soup vegan? Are there beef tomatoes out there that I have been missing out on? That would be AMAZING.*  They have a green smoothie, so I will probably be back to try that, but for coffee I would stick to Mojo or Reservoir Cafe.      *The emails explaining what vegan tomato soup is can stop now. This was my attempt at a joke. A bunch of you thought I was serious about beef tomatoes. I wasn't.

What a gorgeous bar!  As soon as I walked into Vive, I knew it was high class.  The bar is beautifully lit with Vive's signature purple.  The bartenders were very friendly, as well.  I love that there is a nice lounge area on the inside part of the bar.  It would be a great place to enjoy happy hour.  Outside is lovely.  It's a hotel, so there is a small pool, as well as a patio with plenty of seating.  There is a beautiful garden surrounding the pool area that makes you feel as if you are on vacation in another city.  WIth the open patio you can enjoy the sun, or admire the night, after the sun goes down.  Vive is located just a few doors down from one of my favorite restaurants, Oceana, so I can definitely see myself getting a cocktail here before heading to dinner, one night.  A definite gem in the Quarter.

Truthfully, this place is A LOT more organized than I remember.  You go in, get in line, tell them what you need and they give you a number. Then you sit and wait until they call you. Everything moves pretty quickly and smoothly. Always remember to bring your insurance and car registration info. And the DMV only takes cash, so be aware of that. I suggest going early in the morning when everyone is still in a pretty good mood and the crowd isn't too thick.

I hadn't been to this theater in years when I decided to stop in to see The Amazing Spiderman.  It was just as I had remembered with one major difference: the seats are now made out of a fancy fake leather (or maybe real leather?  I couldn't tell.  It was dark,) instead of the typical cloth.  At first I thought it would be pretty nice to have seats like that, but I had worn shorts on this particular day, and after a while my thighs began to stick to the seat.  I had to keep shifting because it was pretty uncomfortable.  Also, I know it's summer, but the theater was FREEZING.  It was a good 65 degrees in there and maybe even colder!  Another reason I wish I hadn't worn shorts!  So, in conclusion, not a bad place to see a movie, if you are wearing pants.

Because I'm a weirdo, I popped into this Bath and Body works to check out the same sale that I just checked out at my other local Bath and Body works. Today's mission was: candles.  So, twice a year Bath and Body works has a major sale. They have one sale in the beginning of June and another right after Christmas. This is when I really stock up on my Bath and Body works goodies. I mean, when you can get a $14 body spray for $4, you make a point of planning your bath goods shopping around these sales. I already hauled some major finds from the Oakwood location, so I stopped in here to check out the candle selection. Um...three wick candles for $12?? Yes, please. This is the time of year that I stock up on stuff to give people for Christmas and birthdays. They had all season candles on sale, so I was sure to get a bunch and heads up pumpkin lovers: pumpkin scented everything is priced to move and fall is right around the corner.  A super helpful sales girl, who just happens to have my same name (minus one 'le'), was good about pointing me in the right direction of where I could find the best deals. I like that this store isn't stuck in the middle of a mall and it's easy in and out.

Here's a fun fact about me, that I'm not proud of, but I'm going to admit:  I don't see nearly enough plays.  Well, considering I live in a city that is always putting on fantastic productions, I really should find myself in a theatre more often.  With that said, it should be a surprise to no one that I had never had the opportunity to see a show at the Rivertown Repertory Theatre.  Located in the deep recesses of Kenner, the Rivertown Repertory Theatre is a fantastic theatre that features regular productions.  Last night, a friend brought me along to see a production of "A Chorus Line".  It had been years since I had seen a musical (I think that last one I saw was at the Saenger, pre Katrina), so this is territory that I hadn't covered in quite a few years.  Besides, the greatness of the place, the thing that I was most impressed by was the sound quality of the place.  The theatre is huge, and although we were sitting way in the back, the cast was mic'd to perfection, so that everything was crystal clear and there was zero feedback.  The performance itself was excellent, and it makes you proud to know that there is such musical acting talent, right here in our own backyard.  The next performance at Rivertown is going to be Chicago, and since it's one of my faves, I definitely plan on checking it out and even bringing a few friends.

This place is obviously family owned, which is fantastic.  The pizza isn't bad and they have beer on tap.  The staff is very attentive and eager to please.  My only complaint would be the prices.  I KNOW that it's a small place, so they have to make some profit, but the prices are a little steep and you feel like you are getting ripped off, unless you are ordering a large.   Definitely go, but know that you will be paying a little more for pizza than usual.

A friend of mine asked me if I had ever been to Adolfo's, and since I had never even heard of it, he insisted we check the place out. Well, when we got there, at 8:30, they weren't seating anymore. That was a major bummer, especially because the place smelled SO good.  Take two: we stopped in after Krewe du Vieux, of all nights. Suggestion: if you want to try a restaurant on Frenchmen, do so during a major parade. There was no wait.  This cute little restaurant is pretty small and located right above the Apple Barrel bar. My friend had been raving about the place, so I was eager to try it.  Looking over the menu, everything sounded amazing, but I was in the mood for fish. I decided to get the Fish Renee, which is fish topped with oysters, spinach and sherry. It also had an amazing "ocean" sauce, which sounds a little "iffy", but was actually amazing. The fish (I think it was grouper) had A LOT of flavor and the sauce was delicious. I love oysters, but I found them a little weird with the fish. I think it was a texture thing and was more of a "me" issue than an issue with the dish itself.  One complaint: I think the only bathroom is downstairs in the bar area (if there is one upstairs, please correct me). I went downstairs to the bathroom, and in that little bit of time, they locked the door going back upstairs and since I had left my phone on the table, I had to really finagle my way back up there. i mean, I had to really convince these people that I was indeed dining upstairs and not just trying to sneak into the dining room. Always an adventure.  This cozy little place is perfect for a date and what I would call "essential" New Orleans. I will definitely be back.

The same owners as the old Parasols.  HUGE place, delicious food and awesome atmosphere.  Great place to go see a game, because they have a huge projector screen.  I have only been twice, but both times I got a wonderful roast beef po boy.  You can even eat outside!   One star knocked off for not taking credit cards (although, I get why they don't...one less thing to worry about.).  I will definitely be going back!

I had never been to this place when my boyfriend took me to celebrate my birthday.  First of all, the atmosphere is wonderful and romantic.  The lighting isn't too bright or too dim, it's perfect for dates.  The food was exquisite.  I had no idea what to expect, but I got the salmon and I was blown away at how wonderful it was.  The wait staff was extremely attentive and helpful.  I would definitely love to go back someday.  The place isn't cheap, but it's worth spoiling yourself on a special occasion.

There are two things I love when it comes to coffee: PJ's iced coffee and not having to get out of my vehicle to obtain said iced coffee. This PJ's has both of those magical qualities.  So there I am, driving through the Da Metrys, when I decide that I could use a caffeine fix. Not only is there a shiny PJ's over yonder, but I drive up and discover that they have a drive thru. Bing! Oh, and it's 2 in the afternoon, so there's no line. Bing, again!  Not only does this PJ's serve up an icy cool treat on a warm day, but the staff is quick with your order AND bonus points because this PJ's has 2% milk. Who needs Starbucks?

Victory wasn't too bad, but after waiting a while to check this place out, I was left unimpressed.  Victory is really small and is really a bit of a dive in nice clothing.  I can picture coming here on a nice night out, but on the night I was here, it just felt like your average run of the mill bar.  When we received our drinks, the order was messed up not once but twice.  I understand that it was our waitresses first time ever waiting tables (that's what she told us), but on a busy Friday night, the wait staff should really know what they are doing and management should maybe not put the new girl on the floor.  Would I go back?  Yeah, if I was in the area, but I wouldn't really go out of my way.

This is a typical "greasy spoon" type of breakfast place.  The quality of the food here really depends on who happens to be working in the back when you get here. I usually get two eggs over easy, toast, bacon and hash browns. More often than not the eggs are cooked correctly, but there have been a few times where they have been under cooked and I've had to send them back to the kitchen.  They also have donuts and a few other pastries, but if you want them fresh you better get there in the morning.

We used this service Saturday night because the Uber app was being a pain and not working right. This is the exact same idea as Uber: tell them where you are and where you're going and they'll come get you. The wait is a bit longer because there aren't as many Lyft drivers in the city as Uber drivers, but the service is identical and you can tip on the app. Our driver was really nice and chatty, which made the ride through traffic from our hotel to our dinner destination a breeze. I would probably still opt for Uber, if given a choice, but Lyft is a good alternative.

Okay, so as someone who lived on the Westbank for most of my life, I have driven past this place probably a thousand times. Easily. I always thought it looked kind of sketchy, and as much as I loved Chinese/Vietnamese food, this was probably one of the few "big" places in the area that I had yet to try. A Facebook post from a friend of mine changed all that: she posted photo after photo of the most delicious looking food, so I decided to roll the dice and give this place a shot.  I stopped in for lunch and I was determined to try a few things. I could have gotten one dish and been satisfied, but what's the fun in that? I got the pork vermicelli bowl, Imperial rolls (Vietnamese egg rolls) and an order of Spring rolls.  Pork vermicelli bowl- While I wouldn't say it's the best pork vermicelli bowl I've ever had, it was really good with a generous portion of pork and noodles. There was plenty enough to just have this for lunch and I was happy to leave with leftovers.  Imperial rolls- YUM! These crispy fried rolls were my favorite out of all the things that I ordered. This was four rolls cut up into bite size pieces that were perfect for sharing. Not that I shared them- I didn't, but if sharing is your thing, these are perfect for that. I'm not even totally sure what was in them, but they were delicious.  Spring rolls- Ooh! These come four to an order too and they are packed with shrimp and pork. These were nice and fresh and as good as Spring rolls that I've had at other places.   Service here was super fast for lunch and while the waiter could have been a little more attentive, I had everything I needed and I was in and out in a little over 30 minutes. Kim Son really surprised me, because I wasn't really sure what to expect from this place. Now I can't wait to return.

Wow. I really like this place.  With any discount kind of store, you have to go in with certain expectations. No, you aren't going to find an Oscar De La Renta dress on sale for $49.99. In fact, just avoid the clothes here completely, because unless you are just looking for casual stuff to wear, it'll probably be off season and nothing you are really going to like.  What Marshall's does right is beauty products, home decor and underwear. I was able to find a few cute bra and panty sets that were marked down considerably. They even have Jessica Simpson brand sets which retail for $20+ marked down to $5. They also have a wide selection of beauty and bath products, including big "salon size" shampoo and conditioner, complete with pump. It's not something I really need, but if you have a big family, something like that could definitely come in handy and it helps that you can get it here for cheap.  They had some cute Halloween decorations out, including a really nice mug, bowl and plate set adorned with skulls. I ended up getting a big mug that only set me back $4. I was pretty pleased with my purchase and now I have a cool skull mug for my coffee.  Marshall's has a decent sized shoe section, but I didn't see anything that really caught my eye. The checkout line is long, but there are multiple cashiers and they work fast, so the line moves quickly.

This Reginelli's is conveniently located in the "social hub" (as I've begun calling it) of Poydras, where there is a nice selection of bars and different restaurants to choose from and the proximity to the Superdome can't be beat.  Some friends and I just wanted a quick snack, so we ordered a small pepperoni pizza (6) slices and it cost $9.33.  What I didn't understand was that a large pizza, which is 8 slices cost about $14.  A little over $4 for two more slices?  Seems odd, even if the slices are bigger than normal, but I digress.  The pizza was really good and the crust had a lot of flavor.  I will definitely be going back and trying some of their many specialty pizzas.

Last summer was the first time that I was able to make it back to Houston's since I had first eaten there, about a month before Katrina.  I was delighted to discover that it was better than ever.  When I first got there, I was told that there would be a 45 minute wait.  Instead, I ate with a friend at the bar and the mood was great.  Because we were sitting at the bar, we were served quickly and I already had my food when I was told that I could move to a table, if I wanted.  I went on a Friday night, and apparently this is a night that they have live music.  Or maybe it's every night.  My only complaint would be that the music was super loud for such a small place, so it was hard to talk.  Other than that, I would definitely go back.

I'll admit it.  I am a total bargain junkie/thrift store enthusiast.    This place is HUGE and packed with great deals.  Great place for new moms, because a lot of the baby clothes are brand new with tags (probably given as gifts and the baby outgrew them quickly).  I have found dresses, blouses, and tshirts here.    There is nothing wrong with shopping thrift, if you know what to look for.  The people who just see it as "second hand junk" don't have the "eye", as I like to call it.  I have found many awesome treasures here.

I think that this spot would have made more of an impression on me if I was more of a cocktail person.  We decided to grab a quick bite before heading over to a show. We sat at the bar and got a couple of drinks. We ordered the meat and cheese board to split. It was pretty good, but it didn't really do it for me. I think it was too simple, if that makes sense.  I think if I were to go back I would probably focus more on trying some fancy cocktails, rather than the food. The atmosphere is nice and the staff is friendly. I can see how it would be a cool spot to start the evening.

Mid City Yacht Club is a real gem of a place.  I had never been when a friend invited me here to check out the Mayweather fight.  I am so glad I discovered this place!  The people are really nice and it's a great sports bar.  They have 5 tv's behind the bar that are always showing 5 different games, whether it's football, baseball, or anything else you could possibly think of.  There is a big projection screen in the back of the place with plenty of seats and there is free food (meatballs, hotdogs, chips) on game days.  There is also a tv outside, if you don't feel like dealing with the smoke or huge crowds that like to gather here on game days.  I have to be honest, this is one of the friendliest places I've ever been to in the city.  I had never been here before and people seemed eager to introduce themselves and make me feel welcome.  A really great place to make friends and watch a Saints or LSU game.  WiFi password: yachtclub

The first time I went here, I was less than impressed.  It was packed, I couldn't find a seat and the people were kind of rude.    When my boyfriend suggested a few months ago that we check it out, I was hesitant.  It was kind of early, so we gave it a try.  We got to sit at the bar, which was a huge plus.  Then, it was time to order "munchies".  We got a yummy cheese plate and the "pomme fritas" (I think that's the spelling) with some Chimay from the tap.  It was fantastic!  I would definitely suggest going a little early, if you aren't into the crowded "bar" scene.  It's a really great little date place and a good place to start the night.

Just for the record: I'm not very adventurous when it comes to Chinese food. I usually get the cheap take out stuff and that's good enough for me.  Dustin suggested China Doll, mainly because of their Tiki bar, Yes, China Doll is  the only Tiki bar in New Orleans, at the moment (Tiki Tolteca is currently closed for renovations). So, we decided to check this place out. We sat in the bar area and looked over the drink menu. They have pretty much any classic Tiki drink for $5.75 each. I decided to start with a Fog Cutter and Dustin got a Mai Tai. My drink was really good, and of course it's sweet, which I liked. The next drink I got was a Piña colada, which was a nice blended drink and was a nice follow up to the strong Fog Cutter.  For actual food, we decided to split the Empress chow mein. This dish is a dice blend of chicken, shrimp and vegetables over crunchy noodles with a nice sauce. It was really good and it was A LOT of food and there was plenty left over to take home.  Everyone was so nice at China Doll and I will definitely be back. The Tiki Bar is definitely an experience and the food is good, too. Go early, if you are planning on eating in the dining room. While we were there a long line formed of people waiting to be seated.

This is a dream store for anyone who is decorating their house or yard. They have a little bit of everything from chairs to sofas to fountains for the yard and lawn furniture. They have adorable mid-century couches that make me want to re-decorate immediately.  When I stopped in, I was on the hunt for a new patio umbrella. They have a great selection of colorful umbrellas for a good price. The biggest that I found was a large umbrella for $79, which I found to be a pretty good deal. Something else I like is that they have two kinds: the stand alone umbrellas and the ones that go in the table.  Everything here is well organized and staff is everywhere on the floor, in case you need help with something. You can also visit their website and see what the store has in stock which makes it convenient, if you don't want to make the drive to Kenner.

Updating and bumping to five stars because not only do I now eat here once or twice a month, but it's my favorite place for Pho and I had the BEST PHO OF MY LIFE  yesterday!  So, let me start by telling you what I get. I go with #14 which is the eye of round and brisket. I have found that this combo has the most flavor and adds the most flavor to the broth. It's so amazingly good and for some reason, yesterday it was the best I have ever had. I mean, the best Pho I have ever had in my life! I have no idea what they did. It's always super good, but it was ultra good this time.  I also get the pork rolls, which I really like because they include a huge piece of pork and are ultra generous with the greens. An order of spring rolls and a small bowl of Pho is definitely more than enough for lunch.  Service here is always top notch and the staff is friendly and is always eager to make sure that everything was to your liking, I am here all the time, so of course I will be back over and over again.
If this place really closed, that makes me sad.  They had a great patio and their Cinco de Mayo parties were always fantastic.

Balcony Bar has improved greatly since my last review. The crowd is MUCH improved thanks to an awesome door guy. The place gets a good crowd without being TOO crowded. There is no smoking (I know that there is no smoking in every bar now, but Balcony Bar has been no smoking for two years). And the best part is the beer- the owners have really made an effort to add a lot of local beer on tap which I am always a fan of. As a result of there being better beer, the place isn't as "fratty" anymore and you can actually sit down and have a conversation and not feel weird.  While Balcony Bar still isn't my first stop if I am looking for a good time, it's not a bar that I avoid as I once did.

I thought I had reviewed WWOZ!  I love this station and I have found myself listening to it more and more as of late. It just seems like there is nothing else good on non-satellite radio! They are always playing good music, local and otherwise and the live wire music calendar is a must.  If you aren't in NOLA, don't fret, you can listen to WWOZ on their iPod and Android app! They play a lot of good stuff during Mardi Gras, too and that is probably my favorite time of year to tune in.

I'm going to give 3 stars to my dinner experience, but I think this is probably an awesome little lunch place.  I had been wanting to try Tal's as soon as I saw them move into the space that used to be McClure's BBQ. I love Middle Eastern food and rumor had it that the hummus here was amazing, so we came on a weeknight for dinner around 7:30. There was no one here, and we wasted no time walking to the front and placing our order.  We decided to start with an order of regular hummus and I got the chicken pita. The hummus was delicious and the pita was so unique- it was thick and fluffy! I had never had pita like that before and I loved it. It was really fresh and the hummus was perfect and lemony. The chicken pita was okay, but it didn't knock my socks off. The chicken itself was really good and it was packed with lettuce and other goodies, but I think it would have made a better lunch than dinner. I honestly found myself hungry again a few hours after eating, so that's what makes me say that.  I love the little bar of condiments they have and, as an olive lover, I have a deep appreciation for the fact that you can load up on as many olives as you want. Seriously, give me all of the olives.  I would definitely stop in here for lunch and maybe grab dinner somewhere else when I am in the mood for Mediterranean.

A friend and I got some take out from this place last night.  We got a couple of crunchy rolls, a Philly roll and a tuna and avocado roll.  The rolls were good, but not great, and the Philly roll had a distinct "fish" taste.  Not a fresh fish taste, but an overwhelming "not so fresh" fish taste.  Also, the rolls were super small.  You would think that 4 rolls would be plenty of food for two people, but we were both still hungry at the end of the meal.  I doubt I would go back here.  If I was in Metairie and wanted sushi take out, I would spend a few extra bucks and go to Little Tokyo which is always fantastic.

I had actually never eaten here when my boyfriend brought me to this place a few months back.  I got some kind of calzone that was really salty and cheesy.  The cheese wasn't bad, but it was a little too salty for my liking.  Also, we went on a Saturday night, and although they weren't insanely packed, it took them forever to get us our order.  I would go back again (my rule is to try a place twice, unless the food is horrible), but I would be more careful about what I order (when they call something "meaty", they mean it!).

Madame John's is a self guided tour through a classic French home that really isn't anything overly great. It's a gorgeous spot and the tour is free, so you really can't complain and it's worth checking out, as long as you aren't expecting anything over the top. Move from room to room and read about the history of the house and the pottery therein.   I really liked the space itself, but I'll be honest when I say that I found the "tour" kind of boring. There was no one there so I could ask questions and the building was basically a ghost town. I was happy to stop in and I did appreciate the history of the home, but I would have liked to have been able to ask a few questions.

Come on baby... Kick them daisies Look at them girls with the Daisy dukes on I want ya to Look at them girls with the Daisy dukes on Everybody Look at them girls with the Daisy dukes on  Anyone remember that song? Just me? Fair enough.  I stopped in here to sample the Bloody Mary because of Yelp's Bloody Mary challenge. I really love the Bloody here and I have since I first tried one at a Yelp event a few years ago. I love that this drink comes in a big glass mug and is garnished with lemon, lime, olives, a celery stalk and a crawfish. No, it's not crawfish season. No, I do not want to know where this single crawfish came from. Their Bloody is pretty classic with just enough spice and more tomato flavor than booze flavor (I don't like it when the ratio is off).  I didn't try the food on this stop, but people around me did and it looked fantastic, so I will definitely be back to try a yummy breakfast or burger!

I loved Brisbi's. I think I love any place where I can sit and look out on water. Considering I didn't grow up in Florida, the lake is the closest I can get to experiencing this.  Me and a group of other Yelpers met here on a lovely afternoon for happy hour. We all sat outside on the patio which allowed us to enjoy the view, breathe in the fresh air and mingle freely with one another. Some chose this spot because of their debris fries and I was pretty happy when I saw oysters and shrimp and grits on the menu. The raw oysters were yummy and obviously fresh and the shrimp and grits made me wish I had ordered the full entree and not just the appetizer. The grits were nice and creamy and the tail-off shrimp were nicely cooked and there was a generous portion of them.  Our waitress was Mary and although it was one of her first days on the job, she was fabulous at making sure our group of 13 was happy and had everything we needed. She also had no issue splitting our check, so she is basically an angel because I know that can be a pain.  I would love to return to Brisbi's, but only if I can sit outside again and be one with the sea.

I'll be honest- after reading some of the reviews of The Junction I was pretty hesitant about going here after a friend suggested this spot for dinner. He said he had been here before and that it was good, so I took his word for it.  We stopped in here around 9 on a Saturday night for some burgers and beers, since that is what they do here. First of all, you should know going in that you have to order at the bar. Yes, you can sit in a booth, but order at the bar. We decided to sit at the bar, mainly because I can't with the up-down every time I want something and the bar had plenty of seating.  They have a really incredible beer selection here and they give you a nice menu of beers that you can leaf through and make your decision. Even though it was a Saturday night, the place wasn't packed at all and we were served pretty quickly.  With drink in hand, I looked over the menu. My friend suggested the fried veggies to start so we went with that. I also decided to get the Central Vermont burger which is a burger topped with bacon, white cheddar, a grilled apple and maple sauce. Weird, right? Maple sauce on meat. There is a note on the menu that says that all of the burgers are cooked medium here, unless otherwise requested. They say it's because it's lean meat that comes from one single animal, so this is how it tastes best. Science! Sure, sign me up.  The food came really quickly. The fried veggies were really good and I could tell the veggies were fresh, even though they were coated in a layer of batter. Hey, fried vegetables are healthy, says I! The burger came and oooh man. This thing was packed with all kinds of goodies. The cheese did that thing that melted cheese is supposed to do when you cut through it. Like, it got all melty. I don't know the technicalities, but it did that. The burger was big and delicious and the maple sauce and apple were oddly perfect on it. The bacon was nice and crispy- just the way I like it. I really enjoyed the combination of the apple and the sauce, and the burger was just great. I couldn't even finish all of it, so I just took the other half to go. Oh yeah, I forgot to tell you that fries are a dollar extra.  All in all, my experience here was pretty tasty and I would definitely return. I wouldn't go so far as to say that The Junction has the best burger in the city, but they do have a pretty darn good one.

Dang Algiers Rouses, you fancy!  This Rouses feels a lot like the Rouses on Tchoupitoulas: a bit upscale and sophisticated with a lot to offer. Also, being in this Rouses makes me realize how much the one on Belle Chasse Highway needs an update. I don't even know if the one on Belle Chasse Highway can even be called a real Rouses because it lacks a lot of cool things that other Rouses have.  Anyway, Algiers Rouses has it all: a neat salad bar, an impressive seafood selection, sushi, a hot bar and a decent beer selection- all of my "go tos". Everything is organized nicely and the staff is really friendly and greeted me as soon as I walked in.  I like that they had multiple registers open, even though the place wasn't super busy, so I was in and out in no time. I might start going to this Rouses more often, mainly because it's nicer and it seems to have more of the "good stuff".

Ok, where do I start? Well, we stopped in for a late brunch and we were told there would be a bit of a wait. The person seating us suggested that we eat at the counter, because it's faster. I'm not usually a fan of counter eating, but considering that I was STARVING, I figured that I would suck it up in the name of fast service.  Well, we got our drinks quickly, ordered our food and waited. And waited and waited and waited. Finally, nearly an hour since we had first set foot inside the door, our food comes out. I ordered the broken yolk sandwich which is a fried egg, tomatoes, bacon and cheese on French-like bread. I also got a side order of grits. The sandwich was...okay. Nothing really special and it was pretty much something I could have made at home. The grits weren't bad, but were somewhat bland.  Let me point out that the staff was extremely apologetic about the wait. This brings me to another point: there was a couple sitting at a table that were clearly finished eating. They had paid and they had "go" boxes in front of them, yet they continued to chat and sip on their coffee as people waited. Now, I'm not usually one to tell people to hustle as soon as the check comes, but when you see people waiting- chug that brew and step. It's just common courtesy.  I would go back, but not for brunch.

Here comes another parking lot review.  I won't bore you with repeating that I'm not really a fan of the "pay ahead" lots they have downtown now, but this isn't a bad one. I have parked here a few times on my way to catch an event at House of Blues, or have dinner in that general area. The cost for 3 hours of parking is $18, which is a little steep, but it's still better than risking your car's integrity by parking on the street. There is always a lot of space in this lot and it's fairly easy to find a spot closer to the street and under the lights, which I like.  Pro tip: set an alarm on your phone and get back to your car before your time is up because they won't hesitate to boot/tow you. I see the truck out there just waiting for people to forget to come back.

Woo wee.  I love this place!  They have so many neat things, from furniture to beer (different departments ;)).  This is the place to go to if you are looking for Warsteiner Dunkel.  You know... that yummy German beer that you can only find once in a blue moon at a bar?  Well, they actually have it here!  In fact, they have a pretty awesome and diverse beer and wine selection.  Also, if you are adventurous, they have a pretty eclectic amount of international foods.  A lot of different pastas and things that would be great for side dishes.  If there is something that you always wanted to try that is kind of different, and you would prefer to try it at home and not in a restaurant, chances are that this place has it.

Generations Hall is a really cool venue for hosting events. I went to a fundraiser here and I was struck by how well everything was organized.  The staff was on point and were taking care of people quickly with no long lines. There was plenty of food that was organized into neat little stations. There were even a few silent auctions going on that went off without a hitch. I had never been to Generations Hall when it wasn't "Metro", but seeing how everything was done, I would definitely suggest this venue to anyone who is looking to host an event.

This place might have the same owners as El Mesquite, but if I am comparing the two, there is really no comparison.  I stopped in here for a quick lunch. I was on limited time so I was happy that I was seated and my order was taken right away. I like that the chips and salsa are free- it was nice to have something to munch on while I waited.  I got the chicken taquito lunch platter which came with four taquitos topped with cheese and sour cream. The platter was okay but I found the taquitos a bit too greasy for my liking. I would say it was definitely worth the $8 it cost and it was decent, but I don't know if I would order this dish again.  The waitress was attentive the entire time, probably because I was one of only two customers  here. Something weird happened when I went to pay the check. I paid in cash and my change came to $11.25. When the waitress brought me my change, she only brought me $11 and she kept the $.75. It's not a huge deal- it's only $.75, but I just found it strange that she took it upon herself to keep it. Maybe it was just an oversight, who knows? I would have mentioned something if I hadn't been in such a rush, and that's not why I rated them three stars, I just want future customers to be aware.
