It does get boring after a while, especially when you are waiting for lawyers and other involved people to show up, so bring a book or other form of entertainment and bring a sweater because the courtroom gets really cold and bring your own snacks if you have dietary issues.  When all is said and done you'll get a fancy certificate thanking you for your service, so feel free so show that to the jerk who you said you would never make anything of your life.

Goodness gracious! What a charming little find!  I have been up and down this street tons of times and I never noticed this little spot until a friend brought me here. I had just had a huge lunch, so I didn't partake in the amazing looking pastries. I am talking about HUGE danish that looked incredible. I just decided to get an iced coffee that was delicious and flavorful.  I also noticed that they have an array of sandwiches on the menu, so I will have to stop in one day for lunch and really see what this place is all about.

This is pretty cool neighborhood bar. I never would have even known it was here, if I wasn't looking for it- the front of it kind of blends into everything else on the street. The bartender was nice and the people drinking here were as well. It has a lot more space inside than you would ever imagine- if you head to the back there is a whole lounge area with a pool tables and sofas. There's also another sofa right outside the lounge area, which I enjoyed and that was actually clean. Not worth going out of your way, but nice if you are in the area.

It's always weird to review a bridge, because there's really nothing much to say about it, unless it's in terrible disrepair.  I passed over this bridge and I didn't even realize it was a bridge until I saw the sign. It's in good shape and doesn't seem like it's going to collapse and take me down with it, so that's a plus. I only ever cross this bridge when I'm heading to the Lakefront Airport, which is a rarity considering I don't own my own private plane, yet. I think I might have crossed this bridge a lot, back when I was going to UNO, but I'm not sure.  As others have said, the views of the lake are great, but eyes on the road unless you're the passenger.

It's always a good day when I can make it over to St. Roch Market to try something delicious. I had my eye on Fete au Fete for a while, more specifically on their shrimp and grits that I had heard raves about and I decided that this was the day I finally try them.  Well, you know what they say about best laid plans. I ordered as usual, but after a 30 minute wait I was called over and told that they were out of grits. This kind of confused me, considering it was only noon, but oh well. I was pretty bummed, but I decided to go with my second choice of the Cajun Cubano. This was a delicious Cuban sandwich cooked perfectly with melty cheese and pressed nicely, just as I like it. It was fantastic, full of flavor on flaky bread and made for the perfect lunch.  I'll be honest, if you're in a hurry, this isn't the place for you. They cook everything to order (of course) and after the 30 minute wait, just to be told they were out of grits, it was another 20 minutes before I got my sandwich. I was kind of forced to scarf it down because I had to go on with my day. For a place located in a cafeteria, I wish they were a little faster, but I will say that the food was super good. I understand that it's a popular place and I got there during the lunch rush, but next time I'm going to visit on a day when I have some time to spare. And I still have to try their shrimp and grits.

Such a cute boutique!  When House of Lounge closed, there was definitely a need for another "upscale" lingerie shop on Magazine St. Bonjour filled that need.  I stopped in here to browse around and I was immediately impressed. First of all, they carry a huge range of bra sizes, even for the bigger busted gals, and the bras are gorgeous. They have a nice selection of corsets and ruffle panties as well. I like that the boutique has a lot of space, so that you don't feel cramped as you are searching through all of their amazing merchandise. The whole place has a very fancy and Parisian feel and this would be a great place to shop either for yourself or a gift for a bride or girlfriend.

We stopped in here for David's birthday dinner.  I want to start by saying- the staff was amazing: everyone was masked, social distanced and contact tracing. All was excellent on that end.  I got the Trout Lafitte with corn grits and red beans and David got the full ribs with corn grits and red beans.  David's ribs looked GORGEOUS. The meat was falling off the bone and he said it was all great. Look at my photo: those ribs are a work of art and well worth the $26 price tag.  My dish, however, left me disappointed. The fish was GREAT, but the piece of fish was small and thin. I haven't gotten the Trout Lafitte in years, but I definitely remember it being a bigger cut of fish, especially for $22+. I believe at, one time, it was even two pieces of fish, but that was easily over 10 years ago. As good as the fish was, I just wanted more of it.  My sides were good, as always, and the waitress couldn't have been better. We also got the duck empanadas as our starter and we loved it.  I know things are *different* right now, but I hope, if I go back here, the trout is a bit bigger.

Man, I don't know what to say about this place. I love the concept, but the prices...good Lord.  Let me fill you in: I would never call myself an expert, but over the past year I have learned quickly what people are willing to pay for older oddities. My grandmother passed away and we had to clear out her house with two estate sales and a garage sale. Things we expected to get money for sold for barely anything. That's why this place confuses me.  Walking in, you feel like you are walking into your grandmothers junk room. There is a little bit of everything from days gone by: rotary phones, old magazines, old kid's books from the 50's, prints of different types and much more. They have a huge selection of stuff like that. My issue is the prices. For example: they have an old rotary phone that they are trying to sell for $45. My grandmother had two phones like that and we barely got $10/ each for them. I found one on eBay for $24, shipping included http://tinyurl.com/na6znhw Truthfully, you could go to a garage sale and get one for even less than that. And why are you selling books with broken spines for $10+? I get that they are from the 50's and probably out of print, but come on. Unless you are lucky enough to get a collector in there who is looking for that specific book, there is no way you are going to get someone to pay that.  Then there is the magazines. It's awesome that you have old fashion magazines from the 70's, but for $30?? Good Lord, that's a lotta money! Old prints are also about $45 which just seems excessive for what is basically a thrift store.  If you are looking for something specific (and you are willing to really pay for it), then you should definitely makes this your first stop. Otherwise, this store is a browser and not a buyer.

Really cute store with "rockabilly" and "retro" kind of styles.  I do agree that it's a little pricey, but for the French Quarter it really isn't that bad. Here you will find all kinds of "swing" dresses as well as different looks for men who are into the retro kind of look. They also have a wide assortment of cowboy boots, and if steam punk is your thing, they sell a few accessories in order to complete your costume.  The store is small, but has a really wide selection of clothing and shoes to choose from. Don't forget to look in the back for the shoe selection!

Full disclosure: I prefer CVS over Walgreens all day. CVS is never really packed and the service is always fast and friendly.  I was here today looking for my favorite hair serum, after not being able to find it at another CVS location. I found it here quickly and painlessly. While I was here I also picked up some Olay products, that were cheaper than I've seen at other places and some travel size mouthwash and hairspray. Checkout was simple and fast and I joined the CVS discount club to save money on future purchases. Win!

This is a divey little spot and, although it calls itself the Roosevelt Hotel Bar, it has nothing to do with the Roosevelt Hotel. I guess there's a history behind why they named it that.  There are only a few seats at the bar and the drinks are cheap. This is a nifty after dinner spot if you want a good cocktail, but don't expect anything fancy. The staff is friendly enough (although, when I was here they were experiencing post-Mardi Gras burn out) and they have a few decent beers.   I probably wouldn't choose this spot over The Sazerac Bar, in the Roosevelt Hotel, but it gets the job done.

My experience here couldn't have been any easier.  I was in the Quarter for a meeting and, lucky me, this shop was just a few doors down. Their counter is facing the street, so I ordered as soon as I walked in. My iced coffee came fast and it was perfect- definitely what I needed to deal with people in the French Quarter driving like dopes.

Anyone who knows anything about me knows I'm a Fleurty Girl fan and FG is always my go to for any gift giving occasion.  It's hard to believe what started out as just a t shirt shop has expanded into an entire empire of the coolest gifts in New Orleans. I stopped into this location to look around for a birthday gift. There was a wide assortment of all things New Orleans related such as ornaments, cups, mugs, shirts and things of that nature as well as a lot of other home decor.  The woman working was setting up for Christmas, but she took the time to show me a few of the new things that they had in store. I didn't find anything that really fit the bill for my friend's birthday, but I love that they always have new and unique items in the FG stores and I loved the plentiful parking at this shop. I know I'll be back, I always am.

Fantastic sweets, especially pralines!  I sampled some of Old Town's offerings at a recent event and I was blown away by how good their classic pralines are, as well as their chocolate pralines! Both were really fresh and tasted like homemade. I like that their classic praline is a little thicker than some others I've had. I also had some chocolates and candied nuts, which were tasty as well.  Their actual brick and mortar store is no more, but you can still order their products online and arrange a pick up. You can order sweets for them for yourself or for an event.

Look, whenever someone says they want breakfast I am always going to suggest The House. I used to think I was too good for The House, but I was very wrong. Now I am a faithful follower and I wish to convert everyone I meet to my delicious religion.  I had never been to this Waffle House and boy, it is ROWDY! I can tell that in order to work at this WaHo, you have to have a sense of humor and you can't be shy about singing along with the jukebox. I was here pretty late in the morning (pre-lunch) and there was a nice crowd, so we sat at the counter. The staff was on top of it coming over to take our order right away. As the cooks prepared breakfast, they sang and danced along to the jukebox and I had a great time watching them enjoy their job.  Instead of my usual all-star, I kept it simple with a two egg breakfast which comes with grits and a biscuit and I got a blueberry waffle because they still had the special going at that point. As always, the food was ready really fast, it was delicious and it satisfied my craving for deliciousness. And they seriously need to have blueberry waffles year round. They're so good and they taste like blueberry cake!  This WH is a little out of the way for me to visit regularly, but it's a solid member of the Westbank WH family.

I had heard about authentic Brazilian food, by way of Arabi, so I decided to take a drive.  This is a quaint, family-owned place complete with full bar and music on Fridays. The menu is packed, and I wasn't familiar with Brazilian food at all, so it took a few minutes for me to figure out exactly what I wanted.  The restaurant offers a variety of delicious, natural juices from the Amazon, so I started with the acerola juice, which was quite tasty and refreshing and not overly sweet. The owner had mentioned that two of her favorite items on her menu are bolinho de queijo  and picanha grelhada . Bolinho de queijo is a ball of cheese baked into a piece of bread -- basically a breaded cheese bite. Quitutes' version is amazing and light with flavorful cheese baked into soft bread. These bites were addicting and I was tempted to order more, but I wanted to save room for my entrée.   Picanha grelhada is prime top sirloin, grilled to your liking, served with rice, pinto beans and vinaigrette. When I took my first bite of this dish, I could tell it was something special. I liked that the meat was seasoned well, tender and lean; I didn't feel guilty eating this for lunch and the food wasn't heavy at all. My personal preference was to mix the rice and beans together and enjoy it with the meat; this was an amazing combination of flavors. The vinaigrette was a nice, fresh addition, as well. My lunch was so good that I'm going to add it to my list of recommended lunches in New Orleans.  This is a cool little addition to the area and they also have a drive through, if you aren't in the mood to dine in.

I've been a fan of Dirty Coast long before they had an actual store and they were just operating online and selling their wares at odd little venues around the city.  The shirts are definitely unique and if you are "NOLA-centric", as I am, you will quickly become a fan of these quirky tees.  I have a few of the "original" ones, that are kind of worn out from over wear, but I still rock with pride. "New Orleans: It sticks to you" and "NOLA: Made with soul" are personal favorites.    There are a lot of great t-shirt shops in the city (that I am also a fan of), but there is something special about Dirty Coast.  All you have to do is attend one of their fashion shows in order to see it.

Talk about a penny pincher's heaven! This is where Dillard's clothes go and get a second life.  I had never heard of this place when David took me and this is nothing like regular Dillard's. This is like a Dillard's warehouse full of discounted clothes that didn't sell in their main stores. There is rack after rack of all types of clothes for men and women including highly discounted dresses and gowns. Really- if you need a fancy gown for any event such as a Mardi Gras ball or New Years Eve, this is the place to come. I saw some dresses that were originally $300 marked down to $70!  This store is pretty "no frills" and you have to take the time to sift through the racks in order to find something you like. It's all organized by size, but that's about it. You could easily spend and entire afternoon looking through racks and picking out deals, and if I had been on the hunt for something, that's exactly what I would have done.  I didn't buy anything this time, but this store is definitely on my radar for the next time I need a fancy outfit at a low price.

David and I stopped in here tonight for little dessert and to see what this place is all about.  This is a new ice cream spot and of course, the "gimmick" is the ice cream is prepared on a cold surface and rolled instead of scooped. You pick your flavor and then you can mix in some other things and add toppings. I got a "kiddie" mint chocolate chip with chocolate sprinkles. It was cool watching them make it and they basically make the ice cream from scratch right in front of you. The flavor of the ice cream was pretty good, but I wish my cup had been filled a bit more. David got the regular size and his cup was PACKED with rolls. Oh well, it was enough for me.  The prices are a little high- my kids cup was $4.50 and the regular size is $7.50. I found that to be a little steep for this type of thing, but maybe it's typical. You can also get soft serve and they have milkshakes as well.  This wouldn't be my first dessert stop, but it's a good addition to an area that was lacking and the variety of ice cream flavors means you won't get bored with the selection.

Oooh baby!  David and I stopped in here before a burlesque show at House of Blues, thanks to my pre-show sleuthing. Everything on the menu looked pretty amazing, so I was excited to dig in.  We were seated upstairs, which was just perfect. It was a nice space and we had a nifty little view of the street outside. We started with some drinks and looked over the menu. I knew exactly what I wanted- the redfish Orleans. This is catfish topped with a generous helping of crawfish etouffee on a bed of white rice.  When it came out- WOW. Okay, this is definitely enough food for two people. I didn't know if I could get through the whole thing, but I am always up for a challenge. The etouffee had the perfect amount of spice and didn't need any extra hot sauce- yay! The fish underneath was tasty and cooked to perfection. The rice mixed well into the etouffee basically making for two meals in one. I failed at getting through all of it in one sitting, but I did have some yummy leftovers to enjoy later.  I was happy that Mr. Ed's had some decent beers on tap, which is always a bonus in my book. I had the Reasonably Corrupt which was a good pairing with my dish, actually. Our waitress was fast and on top of things, even though she never stopped running up and down those stairs. I was also happy with how fast the service was- we were in and out in less than an hour.  If you are seeing a show at HOB or wandering to other parts of the area, this is a great place to stop for a meal.

Here's the thing about me and my friends: we are food fanatics and we love our bbq. When we heard that Chef Rob was back with his newest venture, Crescent City BBQ, we knew we had to be the first in line. Sure enough at 11am, on opening day, we were walking through the door.   First of all: what a gorgeous space. I can see this spot becoming a hang out for Saints games. The dining room is huge, the bar area is gorgeous and has a wide selection of beer on tap, there's tons of seating and there are tvs so you can catch up on the scores. There are huge windows that open up onto the patio that let in a lot of air and light. I was able to go on a little tour of the entire place and there is so much more than meets the eye at first glance: picnic tables for outdoor dining, a huge space in the back for private events (or maybe a Yelp event *cough cough*), rows of smokers and a whole room dedicated to chicken and ribs. It's a BBQ lovers dream come true. Chef Rob has sure come a long way since his little spot on Jackson Avenue where you would have to fight to find a place to sit.  Enough about that- the food is where it's at. I started out slow and got the brisket platter with cole slaw and remoulade potato salad. I got a mix of both fatty and lean brisket and this was a fantastic choice.  I added a little sweet sauce to the meat and it was perfection. The potato salad had just enough kick to it and the cole slaw was crispy and refreshing. I wish there was mac and cheese on the menu, but what are you gonna do? People in my group also got the pulled pork and burnt ends that look just as amazing as they were back in the NOLA Smokehouse days.   I predict a lot of success at this spot. The staff is super friendly and quick to take orders and get them out, the atmosphere is welcoming and laid back and the place is gorgeous. I will be back again and again.

David and I stopped in here to celebrate my birthday and, since we had just gotten engaged, we were celebrating that too!  I just love the vibe of this place- it has a "high end" feel, but still maintains a nice laid back vibe. I already knew what I was going to get, so I ordered the blue crab risotto right away. We also got an order of the garlic bread. Now, let me tell you something about this garlic bread: it might be the best I've ever had. It's garlicky and cheesy and AMAZING. But, you have to ask for it by name- it isn't on the menu and they don't just bring it out. We only knew it existed because David saw a photo of it on Yelp.  My blue crab risotto was delicious and left me wanting more. Seriously. The portion was smaller and I really could have used a bit more, but I loved it. It was so creamy and nice.  They knew it was my birthday, so they brought out a free little cake for David and I to share and they put "Happy Birthday" up on the little screens in the restaurant. I love little touches like that and it really made me feel special.
A very generous krewe, especially to kids.  A lot of themed throws.  I got a lot of beads with "Hermes" on them.   Catch of the night:  Blinky winged shoe beads

Mister Mao is a fun restaurant with a vibe perfect for a night out or celebration!  The food at Mister Mao is eclectic, made with 80 percent fresh, local ingredients that change with the seasons.   The menu is divided into different sections, depending on what you're in the mood for and how much you want to eat. The "Drinking Snacks" section of the menu includes Pineapple Hawaiian Bread with grilled eggplant caviar, baharat (a middle-east spice blend) and saba (a syrupy condiment from Italy made from reduced unfermented grape juice); Yucatecan Sikil Pak pumpkin seed dip with habanero, Mexican and Indian wheat crackers, and crudité. Other "Food We Love to Share" is Escargot Wellington with preserved lemon cream, horseradish, and powder of stems and pork chorizo maque choux with cumin, corn, onion, and Jalapeño cream.  A crowd favorite is the Pani Puri. Made with chickpea and potato masala, pickled blueberry, and fiery mint water, it's unlike anything else served in New Orleans. On my visit I enjoyed the yellowfin tuna made with turmeric green beans, fenugreek, pickled chard, Fresno chili and grape relish. This unique dish was unlike anything I have ever had. The tuna was cooked perfectly and the chili added a nice kick of spice without overwhelming the flavors of the tuna and the greens.  Don't get too comfortable with anything on the menu here--it all changes regularly.  If you're in the mood for a cocktail, Mister Mao's bar has you covered. Co-owner William "Wildcat" Greenwell's bar, Naked Bill, is a cozy and casual spot where you can enjoy drinks that lean more on the tropical side, such as Uncle Butthead (made with mezcal, ciacaro, lime, and cane sugar) and Man Hands (gin, almond, lemon and rose water). There's also a tiki-inspired drink that I really enjoyed called John Secret Dragon Lady, made with Malort, Benedictine, velvet falernum, orange, and saline--it will keep your party going with its island flavors.  I wrote about Mister Mao for Offbeat Eats. Read the full write up here: https://www.offbeat.com/articles/dining-out-mister-mao/

Since my usual "go to" sushi place, Tennou, is doing take out only, I ended up here for the dine-in sushi experience.  I got the New Orleans roll, the salmon roll, the tuna roll and a Philly roll. All of the food was great. I've been here a few times and the service is pretty good and, although I wish the staff was better about wearing masks, I felt safe because the tables were distant from each other.  The restaurant itself is huge and gorgeous, and has been totally renovated from when it was Parrot Pete's. I'm not sure if this would be my first pick for Westbank sushi, but it did the job. I'd like to return and try their ramen!

I would definitely give Gambino's a solid three stars.  My main complaint is that if you want anything good, you have to go pretty early because they sell out of pastries quickly, and they won't get anymore in until the next morning.  When I get something here, it's usually a king cake.  Not a bad place to go, if you are in the area, but not worth going out of your way for.

I have seriously never reviewed THE Wally World?  Wow. Well, I've been here maybe twice. Once I was looking for a bathroom, so I don't know if you want to count that. They have everything that a regular Wal Mart has but it's quite...colorful. You might see someone get cursed out. You might see a baby draw a weapon. Anything can happen at this Wal Mart.  In all honesty, Wal Mart DOES serve a purpose and it's really a necessary evil. They have super cheap stuff that you need and you know you are going to end up here at least once in your life. Just go limp and let it happen. Wait. What?  Anyway, 1 million hits can't be wrong! This is THE Wally World. You better recanize! http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WF0tkdhtIDA

Moe's might be a chain, but this spot gets a nod for being super affordable. With a menu that includes well-priced sandwiches, platters, a kid's menu and catering options, there's no reason why Moe's shouldn't be an option when looking for something tasty and smoky. The fact that it won't cost you and arm and a leg is a huge bonus here.  I had the pulled pork sandwich with mac and cheese and potato salad ($9).  I'm a firm believer that good barbecue doesn't need sauce and Moe's proves that. The delicious pork speaks for itself, but I added some sauce, just for a little more "zing".  The mac and cheese and potato salad were perfection and I am happy to report that I left Moe's feeling more than satisfied. I especially loved how friendly the staff here was and how fast the food came out; when I'm hungry, I don't want to wait!  I made a list of best hidden BBQ for Very Local New Orleans and this l restaurant was on it! Read it here: https://nola.verylocal.com/bbq-new-orleans/228292/

Wow. I was in the area and searching for a lunch place when I just happened to walk past this spot. Apparently, it was one of their first days doing dine-in, so I popped right in and had a seat (after signing in).  This restaurant actually used to be a record store and I love the open vibe of the place. I got an order of the ramen, some lumpia and the dumplings. The way it works is your order at the counter and pay and they bring you your food, when it's ready.    The lumpia and the dumplings were incredible. The dumplings came in a tasty sauce that was just a perfect compliment and added even more flavor. The lumpia was delicate and tasty.  The ramen was great! It was packed with pork and the broth was flavorful. Of course, I picked an unseasonably warm October day to get ramen, but it was totally worth it. I loved every bite.  I really admire that this restaurant opened during the pandemic and the hard work really shows in the delicious food. This was a great spot for lunch and I'll be back.

Not my usual "go to" Brothers, but it gets the job done. This place is as reasonably priced as the other convenience stores in the area, but this one definitely isn't as clean and it has a certain "sketch" factor to it. There are always people just lurking around in the parking lot not really doing anything. I've never gotten hot food here (and I wouldn't), but their drink selection is as good as any other spot.

Hmmm...okay, here's the situation: this would be a pretty great place if it wasn't on Bourbon St.   We ended up here one night after a day of hanging out in the Quarter and we were pretty surprised- the staff is friendly, drinks aren't crazy expensive and there was a live band rocking out and actually playing listenable music and not TOP 40. The main problem is the crowd. Of course, you're on Bourbon, so everyone is rowdy and loud and drunk. The place is fairly small and it was crowded, so people were pushing each other out of the way to get to the bar. There are tables and chairs throughout the venue, that are almost in the way when there are a lot of people and a band is playing.  I think if this bar was a little more "off the beaten path" it would be more stars, but I'm sure the owners are making their money, so what do I know? Stop in to see a band, but brace for a Bourbon crowd.

"You'll never know what heaven means, until you've been down to New Orleans"- King Creole, 1958  For my 400th review: I present, in no particular order, the top 10 things I love about NOLA.  1) The food.  Where else in the U.S. can you find a delicious shrimp po-boy in a convenience store that is better than any other fast food out there?  New Orleans cuisine is world famous for being some of the best food in the world.  Lucky me, I can get it anytime I want.  Crawish etouffee, catfish Louisiane, shrimp gumbo, beignets...'nuff said.  2) The culture.  New Orleans is a city that was built from the gound up by many different cultures. The ancestors of those who built New Orleans remain here today.  Our culture is as diverse as our food and there are many different flavors.  Spanish, French, African, Irish, Italian- it's all here.  It is reflected in the architecture and music of the city and it is what makes New Orleans unique.  3) The music.  Walking through the French Quarter, you can hear the music flowing like the Mississippi River.  Musicians stand on street corners and entertain the passers by with their euphony.  Their accompaniment is tap dancers and singers.  These people don't do this for the few dollars they make, they do it because it is their passion.  It is their love.  They take pleasure in sharing a piece of New Orleans with the tourists and the locals alike.  They take pride in the flavor that they add to the city and we love them for it,  4) The French Quarter.  Only in New Orleans can you decide at 4 in the morning that you are tired of being home and you want to go out and party (or eat!) and places are actually open.  Make no mistake about it; New Orleans is truly the city that never sleeps.  We are up and at it 24/7.  You can walk around and listen to the music coursing out of the bars with a beer in your hand.  You can dance in the street and have a good time any day of the week and any time of the day.  5) Mardi Gras.  It is about more than beads.  It is about spending time with family.  It's about going out to a parade, with a packed lunch and a lawn chair and sitting on the neutral ground.  It is about that smell of 18 wheelers that reminds every New Orleanian about this special day.  It is about yelling at strangers to throw you a 10 cent pair of beads that is worth more than gold at this magical time.  Spending time with your friends and just forgetting about your worries and troubles for a few hours.  It's about getting a day off from school and work in order to just enjoy the day, rest, relax, and celebrate life.  Where else in the U.S. is an entire city given the day off just so that it's citizens can go and celebrate life, even if it means going to a parade and yelling at stangers?  6) The streetcars.  I love the streetcars.  Not only are the environmentally friendly, but they are a fun way to get to where you are going and a good way to see the city (especially if you don't like to walk).  I'll take a streetcar over a taxi cab any day of the week.  7) Faith.  Say whatever you want about New Orleans being a party town.  Just know that we know that there is a time and place for everything.  New Orleans is a city with deep religious roots.  One of our major landmarks is St. Louis Cathedral.  New Orleans is the home of many people who believe many different things.  We go to church, we have faith, and we believe in the goodness of people..  8) The architecture.  Unique to New Orleans and admired by many.  Most who visit the city are quick to notice our unique builidings and our beautiful balconies.  Many of them are as old as the city itself and when I walk down the street, I sometimes feel that I am in an old movie.  It's classic and it could never be duplicated.  Anyone who has ever lived here has driven down St. Charles Avenue and admired the beautiful homes that line the street.  Where in New York or LA could you find old, classic, beautful homes such as those?  9) Magazine St.  Our very own Rodeo Drive right here in the Big Easy.  Ok, not quite, but you can find whatever you need on Magazine, that's for sure.  It has antique stores and jewelry stores and vintage clothing boutiques and fine shoe stores.  It has bars and restaurants and groceries and chocolate shops and everything else you could possibly want.   10) The people.  The people in New Orleans definitely have flavor and are never boring.  The people are friendly.  They have their traditions and their rituals.  They are stubborn and strong.  They have seen the worst and lived through it.  They have seen the best and told you all about it and celebrated it.  They have been through hell and back and they have survived.  There is no stopping a true New Orleanian. And even if you weren't born here, they still consider you one of their own.  There are a lot of more things that make New Orleans a great place to live: City Park, the art of the cemetaries, etc.  You'll just have to pay us a visit and see for yourself!

Super cute spot, especially if you want a tasty treat and you're tired of the same old snowball.  Big O's pushes their pops all over town, but right now you can get one at the popsicle doorbell at 3510 Royal St. Just ring the bell most days between 2 pm and 8 pm and the awesome owner Jesse will take your order and bring your wrapped popsicle to you promptly. Pay with Venmo for a completely touch-free experience.  I got the blueberry mango cream and the watermelon basil lemonade. The cream pop was smooth and rich just like yummy ice cream and the watermelon basil lemonade was crisp and tasty. All of the pops are made with fresh ingredients and the taste proves it.  I'll definitely be visiting again soon!

This is a cute little shop that carries a nice mix and casual and "fancier" clothing. The prices are pretty reasonable and right now they have a nice selection of light cotton clothing for the warmer weather.   When I was here I was greeted by the owner and her sweet dog, Gus. They have a good selection of cotton dresses, but on this day I was on the hunt for some comfy shorts that I could wear all day and that were a little different from what I usually go for. I found some cute pink cotton shorts that are thin and perfect for the summer and will be great to wear to festivals.  This is a good place to shop if you are looking for something a little nicer than you would be able to find at a mall.

Finally, New Orleans has a proper pie shop!  I love pie! It's one of my favorite pastries, and perfectly crusted pie with delicious filling is my happy place. Enter Windowsill Pies. This yummy woman-owned business has been cranking out the tasty treats for years, and now they finally have a brick and mortar to call home.  Naturally, I couldn't wait to stop in and try the tasty treats for myself. I love that the shop offers both sweet and savory pies and you can get certain pies whole, by the slice, or in hand pie form.  When I stopped in, I treated myself to the croque madame hand pie and the strawberry chocolate hand pie. The savory was my lunch and the sweet was my dessert. The shop also offers one of my favorite local coffees, Coast Roast, so I got some cold brew to go with my treasures.  All of the pies are handmade by the two lovely owners, Nicole and Marielle, and you can taste their personal touch in every bite. The pie crust is flaky, buttery and perfect and the sweet pies aren't heavy, like certain local pies that so many seem to pine for. These are the light, delicious pies of your dreams.  The menu here is ever-changing, but they seem to be keeping a nice balance of sweet and savory options. And I'm THRILLED that you can now actually get a proper, homemade-style pie at a shop, rather than those boxed factory-made pies you find at the grocery store.  This shop is already a beautiful addition to Freret and I will absolutely be back, especially since we're coming up on the holidays. And they have online ordering, so you can order and pop in and get the pie that you crave.   If they start making cherry pies- I'm in big trouble.

Oh here we go. Good 'ol Cleopatra used to be a Westbank parade, until it decided to switch to the Uptown route. Well, for all intents and purposes it is still a Westbank parade. All of the Westbank high schools are represented as well as the Gretna police and the fact that people with "Westbank is the Bestbank" signs get a lot of beads, should tell you that this is a Westbank parade at it's finest. In fact, everything about this parade is Westbank, except for it's route.  Pretty decent throws to be had and the Krewe is generous. This years keepers were a Cleopatra koozie, a few light up throws and a bottle opener key chain with a light on it.

This seems to be one of the better music bars on Bourbon. On the night that we stopped in there was a pretty good band playing, a good crowd and everyone was having a good time. The drinks were a little pricey, but that's to be expected.  The reason for the three stars is this: my friend went to get some money out of the ATM and the ATM took the money out of his account, but didn't produce any cash. We took the issue to a manager who just told my friend to call his bank in the morning and tell them what happened. I guess the machine was out of cash, which is odd because we were here on a weeknight and not a busy weekend. The experience immediately soured us on the place and we left. I can only imagine if a tourist had experienced that- someone is on vacation, an ATM steals their money and they have to call their bank? What a pain.  My friend's money was refunded, but I would be nervous to return and use their ATM or even a credit card. It almost feels like some sort of weird scam (hoping drunk people won't notice/complain?). Who knows? The only reason I'm rating three stars and not two is because the band was good and we were having a fun time until the ATM incident.

This has become one of my favorite places in the city.  Since my review over 2 years ago, I have tried much of the food, a lot of the wine and some of the beer. Delachaise is the perfect little bistro when you want to enjoy a night out, but you don't want to get overly fancy.  My favorites on the food menu are the gourmet grilled cheese and the cheese plate. I have tried many cheeses on the cheese plate and I've always been delighted by my choices. The gourmet grilled cheese is to die for. It's so rich that you can pretty much split it with a friend.  I really like the seating area by the window, and it's always a perfect night when I am lucky enough to grab this limited spot. Sitting on the patio is perfect for early evening as the sun begins to set and the night winds down.  There is an extensive wine selection so you are sure to find something that suits your tastes.

Rouses is a pretty great market.  They are always having specials and have a great selection of deli items such as assorted cheeses and sandwiches.  You can go in and get a mini platter of finger sandwiches for around 5 bucks!  Who wouldn't like that?  They also have sushi rolls that are made fresh daily.  Don't be scared.  It's nothing too exotic.  They usually have crunchy rolls, rolls made with faux crab and veggie rolls.  I don't think any of them actually contain real raw fish and they are actually pretty good, if you want to pick one up for lunch.

Talk about a pleasant surprise! I'm always happy when I hear that a place is really good and worth the visit and then it turns out to be REALLY good and worth the visit.  I stopped in here for lunch, with not so high expectations. Nothing against Westwego, but it's not exactly a top food destination. So, I came to the Westbank Grill and I brought a craving for an oyster poboy with me. The awesome thing is one of their lunch specials is an oyster poboy with fries for $7. Don't mind if I do.  Well, I'm not lying when I say that this poboy was perfect. I am pretty picky when it comes to oyster poboys- the oysters have to be fried perfectly and the bread has to have that perfect combination of softness and chewiness for me to be happy. This sandwich was a win on all fronts. Not only was it really big and well worth the money, but it was delicious.  The staff here is so friendly and the waitress even turned the ac down after she saw me rubbing my arms because I was cold. I thought that was really sweet. Service was fast and they have great lunch specials, which pretty much guarantees that I will return.

I recently attended a fancy lady lunch with Re H., Katie A. and company and I was so excited to try Antoine's for the first time. This restaurant was actually Katie's sister's suggestion- they were in town visiting and she had heard about the prixe fixe lunch for $20.17. This sounded like too good of a deal to pass up.  We started with some of Antoine's famous puffed potatoes for the table as I looked over the menu trying to decide exactly what I wanted. I decided to start with an order of the charbroiled oysters. These yummy oysters were nice and fat and juicy and topped with garlic, herbs, butter and Romano cheese. There were some of the best oysters I have probably ever had.   For my entree, I had the fried chicken and macaroni and cheese. I know what you are thinking- you went to this fancy place and had fried chicken? YES! This wasn't just any fried chicken, this was fried chicken that was fried to crispy perfection and then topped with a tasty marmalade drizzle that brought out the flavors of the meat. The chicken was juicy perfection and perfect in every way. As for the macaroni and cheese, it was three cheese macaroni and cooked to gooey deliciousness. The serving was more than generous and it was all delightful.  Finally, for dessert, I had the pecan bread pudding. I know this is going to make me sound like a strange New Orleanian, but I'm not the biggest fan of bread pudding BUT I love pecans, so I decided to give this a try. Well...you know how some bread pudding can kind of be a mushy mess? This wasn't the case here at all. The bread pudding was firm and tasty like really good cake and the pecans were toasted to perfection.   Our amazing waiter was Paul. Not only did he have a great personality, but after our meal he gave us a tour of the restaurant. Antoine's is HUGE and gorgeous. I was so excited to take a walk through a piece of New Orleans history where presidents, movie stars and even the Pope had dined. Our waiter told us he had been working at Antoine's for 26 years and his expertise and professionalism absolutely showed- he made a great experience even better.  I would love to some day return to Antoine's for dinner and I will absolutely be back for lunch. I'm always excited for any excuse to dress up and be glamorous and the Antoine's experience encompasses the word in "elegance" at every turn.

I hate to give one of the few parks/green spaces in this area a paltry three stars, bit I feel like it's deserved.  This park is plagued with a few issues: not the least of it is there really isn't much going on here and there isn't much to look at. The grass is frequently overgrown, drainage isn't great, it's a mess after it rains, people litter and it isn't picked up regularly, and sometimes the place can be a bit of a mess. One of the few things this park has going for it is there are a few nice cypress trees and there is a lot of space. I used to come here frequently when I was a kid and fly my kite and it was perfect for that because there is room to run.  I have never been to the observatory, but I do think that that's a cool addition and I wouldn't mind checking that out.

This place really soothed my soul tonight.  So, as it happens, I've been waiting a year for this El Gato Negro to open. One of my favorite Mexican restaurants, El Gato announced their Gretna location over a year ago, but you know how a pandemic goes.  David and I went tonight because we are 3 days out from a Cat 3 hurricane hitting the city (Zeta) and we still don't have power. Peanut butter sandwiches and dry cereal only goes so far. In search of a good, warm meal, we headed to the very-powered old Gretna for some grub.  This spot is beautiful and my goodness, you can really see all the work they put into it. The inside has an upstairs and downstairs and every detail is perfect. They didn't just throw this place together, because it's on the Westbank. They put the work in.  We started with some amazing queso dip, which was out of this world. I had a pulled pork burrito and David had an enchilada platter. I also had a frozen margarita because...hurricane. All of the food and the drink were delicious. My burrito was packed with goodies and the pork was tender and flavorful. My margarita was great and I could tell it was made fresh. David loved his enchilada platter. It was a win on all angles.  One special touch I appreciated was the mention of "historic Gretna" on their signage and drink glasses. That makes for a nice touch and makes you feel like the restaurant is invested in the area.  We greatly enjoyed our meal here and we will absolutely be back.

Mr. Tequila on Freret Street is a Mexican restaurant that has tasty food and cocktails to satisfy your craving.  Some popular menu favorites include Traditional Fajitas ($11.50), a savory blend of grilled bell peppers, onions, and a choice of rice, refried beans, sour cream, lettuce, pico de gallo, guacamole, and tortillas; Freret Burrito ($14.25), a steak or grilled chicken burrito filled with rice, beans, pico de gallo, and guacamole with a side of fries; and Nacho Fries ($10.95) topped with steak, cheese, pico de gallo, guacamole and sour cream.  On my visit, I had the Black and Gold Burrito ($12.25), which the menu describes as a burrito filled with ground beef or shredded chicken, rice, beans, topped with chile con carne and white cheese dip. I got mine with shredded chicken and chile con carne on the side. It was a great size for the price; the chili con carne and cheese dip were the perfect touch.  With great food and great service, I will definitely be back!  I wrote about this spot for Uptown Messenger. Check it out here: https://uptownmessenger.com/2021/08/gonzalez-brothers-offer-authentic-mexican-flavors-at-mr-tequila/

Cheap and tasty lunch alert!   Someone told me about the delicious, cheap lunch at China Gate, and since I am currently on the hunt for GOOD Chinese food, I figured I had nothing to lose by eating here. I was here pretty late in the afternoon for lunch, around 2, and the place was empty except for me. The sweet waitress (and owner, I believe) greeted me with, "You've never been here before!" She was right and she happily showed me to my table.  Looking over the menu, this all seemed a little too good to be true. Not only are these prices beyond reasonable, but they have dishes I actually recognize. Okay, what's the rub? Small portions? Food from a bag? I was about to find out.  I ordered the sweet and sour chicken ($6.99) and it comes with an egg roll, shrimp fried rice and egg drop soup. The egg drop soup came out and it was the perfect "starter" portion. It was nice and thick and it was topped with crispy wantons. It was at this point that I started getting excited. Then out came the chicken. WHOA. This plate was PACKED with food. The chicken was lightly fried and sliced and the sauce was underneath. There was chicken on top of chicken and they weren't stingy with the portion at all. Not only that, but the sauce was perfect and not too sweet. The shrimp fried rice was great and the egg roll was fried to crispy perfection. The entire meal blew me away- really. It was so much food that I had leftovers! The best part is they do take out for lunch as well, in case you aren't in the mood to dine in.  My entire meal, including my iced tea, was $9 before tip. That's pretty incredible and is probably one of the best lunch deals in town. The owners are beyond sweet and I will be so happy to go back and eat here again! In fact, I plan on being a regular.

I was expecting more.  I'm a beer lover, so when I heard that a beer bar was opening on the Westbank (where I live), I was excited. When I walked in, my excitement faded fast.  For starters, it's Jefferson Parish, so they allow smoking. I just can't "do" smoking bars anymore. My sinuses have aged, I guess, and being around cig smoke leads to two days worth of congestion that I don't want to deal with. Why they don't have machines sucking out the smoke, I couldn't tell you, but it was so thick that it left a haze across the bar.  On top of that, they only have 6 beers on tap and the rest are bottles. Come on. You're going to call yourself a beer bar and not have a decent tap selection? Even Vinnie's has a respectable selection of beers on tap.   Between the smoke and the limited taps, I'll just head over to Avenue Pub on St. Charles for my craft beer fix. Maybe I'm a snob. If you want a big selection of bottled and canned beer, this is the spot.

This is a cute little shop with a little bit of everything. The name is quite appropriate because you do feel as if you are looking through your grandmother's old collectibles.  Grandmother's Buttons has a nice mix of everything from jewelry and house decor to Christmas decorations and clothes. This place is a few steps above your typical thrift store. On the day I was here, I found a pair of earrings that were perfect for a coworkers birthday and she just loved them. This is a nice spot to check out if you are looking for something a little different and unique or if you are looking for a gift for someone special.

This is such a weird review to write, but I have to be totally honest here.  A friend and I stopped in here at about 12:30 on a Friday for lunch. There was no crowd (two other tables with two people each) and the weather was nice, so we sat outside on the porch. It took a while for the waiter to come over, but at first it wasn't a big deal.  We started with an order of guacamole and chips. I was really delighted that the guacamole was obviously made fresh, as it had HUGE chunks of avocado in it. It was so good and I enjoyed it. After the waiter dropped off the guac, he totally disappeared. As he was walking by, I asked him if I could have an iced tea. He said "sure" and disappeared for another 10 minutes. Keep in mind, we haven't even ordered our entree yet.  He returns with my tea and is about to walk off again when we tell him that we are ready to order. For my entree, I got the Del Fuego burrito which is a burrito packed with rice, beans, cheese and shredded brisket. After we ordered we waited well over 20 minutes (closer to 30 minutes, if I'm being honest) for the food to come out. Normally this wouldn't be an issue, but it was lunch and I was kind of in a hurry, there was no crowd, and one of the other two tables had already received their food. When the food finally arrived, I loved it- the burrito was maybe one of the best I have had in a long time and it was a pretty perfect lunch.  I am giving three stars because as good as the food was, the service was just awful. I feel bad because there was only one guy working and I would be totally understanding if there was a big crowd or if it was the dinner rush, but from beginning to end our lunch took over an hour and there were only three tables of customers in the whole place. That's just not time that I can spare during the week for lunch, especially when I can go to Felipe's and be in and out in 30 minutes.  I should have listened to my fellow Yelpers who said the service was slow. If you have the time to sit there for an hour or so, the food is fantastic and well worth the price. If you are in any kind of hurry, skip it.  Food- 4 stars Service- 2 stars

I went to Del Fuego twice in a week. Really, I went twice in 3 days because it was that good and both times I was blown away.  Okay, so the first time I went was on a Saturday night. There was a bit of a wait, but after about 10 minutes we were seated on the front patio. It was a nice evening, so I was happy to sit outside. My only complaint, and it had NOTHING to do with Del Fuego, was that we were seated next to a large party of college guys who were loud and reacted with "OH!!!!" every time one of them said something. I could have done without that.  So, I ordered a house margarita and looked over the menu. The margarita came on the rocks and tasted fresh and had a lot of flavor. For the appetizer, we decided on the Queso Fundido con Chorizo Verde which is melted queso with meat and spinach served with small soft tortillas so that you can make little wraps. It was delicious and full of flavor with a nice mix of spices. For my entree, I decided on the Los Tres Hermanos Burrito (The Brothers Three) which came packed with pork, chicken, rice beans, guacamole and onions. The burrito was perfect and it was so good and a great deal at $9. We also had the chance to sample some tequilas, and while I am not a "drink tequila straight" type of person, I found it smooth with little to no "after burn".  When I went back, on a Tuesday, there was no wait at all and we were seated inside, which I think I prefer to sitting outside. We got the Ceviche which is gulf fish with tomatoes, jalapenos, lime, cilantro and tomatillos. It comes with hard chips for dipping. It was so good and so fresh. I honestly probably could have just eaten that and left happy. I liked the Tres Hermanos burrito so much the first time, that I got it on my second visit as well.   Shannon, one of the owners, was super accommodating  and made sure that we had everything we needed and that we were happy, the both times that I was there. I will definitely be back, especially now that I know that they have begun serving lunch.

I'm updating and giving taceaux loceaux 5 stars.  Consistently good food, fast service, and they let you know on twitter (@tlnola) what their menu is for the evening and where they will be serving.  They also take credit cards now.  In two months taceaux loceaux has become one of my favorite stops.

This is a review for the patio/bar/outside area.  We were wandering around the Saturday before Halloween kind of just looking for something to do, and after not finding much, when we found ourselves here. The place had a good crowd and there was a band and a place to sit, so we were all about it. The patio area is really nice, there's a lot of space and the bar is right there so you can get some drinks with no hassle and without having to push your way through the crowd. They do have a few local beers on tap, so I enjoyed that while we listened to the band and took in the space.  This seems like a cool place to just hang out, so we'll be back.

I am so bummed. I've been waiting for ages to try this place and I was left with one big disappointment.  Okay, so I was here with my dad on a Friday for lunch. We got here at about 1 and we were seated immediately- great! I was here for the restaurant week lunch special, but I think they might do the $20/3 course special all the time, I'm not sure.  For my three courses I decided on the thin cut fried pickles, the shrimp and grits and the bread pudding. The thin cut fried pickles were great! Lightly battered and not heavy or overly filling. This was a great starter. The shrimp and grits were okay. The grits were decent, but not the best I have ever had and on the somewhat bland side. The shrimp are tail-on, but they were cooked nicely and were a good size and juicy.  My main reason for the 3 stars is the fact that they were out of bread pudding and we weren't informed until the end of our meal. The reason we decided to even have lunch here was because we wanted the bread pudding. Honestly, I feel like they should have either put two bread puddings aside at the beginning of the meal when we ordered, or they should have come out and said that they were out of bread pudding. I just felt like I had been kind of tricked and I don't like that feeling. And how do you run out of bread pudding two hours into lunch? Instead of bread pudding we were given chocolate torte and it was okay, but I wasn't in the mood for chocolate at all.  Anyway, the owner was super sweet and the service was good. I just don't know if I'll be back or not.

This is an Old Metairie classic that was pretty packed on the night I was here, but thankfully the line moved fast.  This seems to be the "teenage hangout" and I think I was the oldest person here (who wasn't a parent) on the night that I stopped in. I decided to get the rainbow flavor, because I've been on a rainbow kick lately and rainbow is different at every stand. At this particular stand, the rainbow flavor was really good and tasted like melted ice cream. Their prices are a little more steep than Westbank stands, but by "steep" I mean 50 cents more...so not horrible. The ice isn't as fine as some other places, but I found it smooth and the syrup pour was generous.  Along with snowballs, they have an assortment of ice cream cones. The people in front of me got some swirl cones that looked delicious! I will be back if I find myself in the area.

This is an adorable bed and breakfast on Esplanade. The staff is super nice and helpful with any of your needs. I did a photo shoot here and the man working that day was extremely helpful and accommodating. He was really nice about letting us use one of the rooms as well as the living room for the shoot.  One of the best features of the room was the claw foot tub. It gave the room an extremely romantic feel and would be perfect for a weekend "away", even if you are a local. The entire house has that "old New Orleans" type of feel and the house has antique furniture throughout. This bed and breakfast would make a cozy getaway for tourists and locals alike.

I was wandering around Marrero when I had a burrito craving and I remembered that a new El Paso had just opened up, so I headed over.  I thought I was safe going to lunch during a Saints game, but I was wrong- the lot was packed making me immediately feel bad for La Hacienda De Leon, located right next door with their mostly empty parking lot. This El Paso building was built for the restaurant and it's just gorgeous. There's a HUGE patio that is perfect for happy hour and Cinco de Mayo celebrations and the inside is really big as well. As packed as the lot was, I was expecting to have to wait for a table, but I was seated immediately.   I already knew what I wanted, so I placed my order and the waitress came right over with warm chips and salsa and refried black beans for dipping. I was starving, so the chips, salsa and dip definitely hit the spot. I like El Paso because they have lunch specials 7 days a week, so I happily got the burrito supreme lunch platter which comes with a burrito stuffed with beef or chicken (I got chicken), rice and a little side salad with guac and sour cream. The food was delicious and it was a perfect serving for lunch and I could tell that all of the ingredients were fresh. I don't know what they put in the sauce at these places, but it's consistently good. I know that some food snobs hate on restaurants like this for not being more "authentic", but El Paso is locally family owned, so I'm happy to eat here.   The staff was very attentive and the waitress checked on me regularly and overall my experience was fantastic. I'm glad that they opened another Westbank location, so I don't have to go to Algiers to get my burrito fix. I love my Tex-Mex and I will definitely be eating here again.

I don't know why it has taken me so long to review my lovely dinner at Primitivo. I guess I was just trying to figure out how to put such an amazing experience into words (see what I did there?).  We stopped in fairly early on a Friday night, with zero reservations, and had no problem grabbing a table. I started with a cocktail that was named after me. Ok, not really, but the "Marie Louise" is awful close to "Marielle Louise", so let's just pretend, shall we? It was some kind of citrus soda that was really tasty and refreshing. I'm not even sure if it had alcohol in it, but I really liked it.  I knew exactly what I was going to order before I even got here: I had read nothing but raves about the braised pork cheeks, so that's what I got. They came with smoked pork butt and dumplings in Carbonara. WOW. This dish was delicious and really exceeded my expectations. The meat was extremely tender and cooked perfectly and the dumplings were amazing.  For dessert, my companion and I were able to split a sundae, even though I was pretty full from the delicious dinner. The waitress was extremely attentive and everyone made sure that we had everything we needed and were enjoying our meal. As the night progressed, and more people came in, we did notice that it started getting a little loud. Other than that, the experience was perfection and I would return.

Some places are probably best left as a part of a song. Margaritaville, for example. I spent the entire time I was here looking for my lost shaker of salt and never found it. That's a metaphor for something. I have no idea what, but I'll figure it out.  Honestly, it's not a bad place for a tourist to stop and get a cocktail, but this local girl just couldn't enjoy the place. The front bar (or is it the back bar?) had a band playing that was way too loud for the room. The lead singer must have thought he was playing Jackson Square or something. We seriously had to relocate to get away from it. It was that bad.  Margaritas aren't terrible, but tons of alcohol doesn't necessarily make a good drink. Their mixologist needs to know that. I didn't try the food, but I'm sure it's typical chain faire. Go in if you are in the neighborhood and need sustenance, but there are a lot of better places in the area.  Some people say that there's a woman to blame. I'm that woman. I went here and it was my own damn fault.

This is a really cool, upscale bar in the quarter. With it's cozy atmosphere and waiters in full attire you are made to feel special as soon as you walk in. I sat on a sofa and perused the list of fancy cocktails. Since I am not a big liquor drinker, I decided on a simple glass of red wine. It was, of course, delicious.  This is also a cigar bar, and although I don't smoke, they seemed to have a wide selection of stogies to choose from.

I have literally driven by Atchafalaya probably a few hundred times in my life. I always wondered about the small restaurant on Louisiana that I had always heard good things about, so when a friend suggested that we get dinner here, I jumped at the chance. Walking in, I was surprised at just how small the place is. There is a cozy bar area that leads into a dining room and a little more space upstairs. We had no reservations, but we were immediately seated. Maybe it was a slow night.  We started with a beef tartar app. I usually shy away from what is essentially raw beef, but I was feeling pretty adventurous, so I decided to give it a try. It came out and it was topped with a soft cooked quail egg. What you do is break the yolk and mix it into the meat. Ooohh...primitive! The meat was nicely spiced and the egg added something interesting to the dish. Honestly- I didn't hate it. AND I didn't get sick or anything, so all in all the experiment in raw meat was worth it. I actually would get this dish again without hesitation.  We also decided to get the soft shell crab app. I LOVE soft shell crab and I have taken to sampling it wherever I can. This app had a thick crust on the crab and I do prefer when the crust is a little lighter. However, the crab itself was delicious and perfectly cooked. I had no complaints about the dish at all.  Last but not least, I got the shrimp and grits as my entree. This was delicious! The shrimp came on the bed of grits and the whole dish was covered in an amazing sauce and served with andouille. My only complaint was that the shrimp came with heads and tails on. It's easy enough getting the heads off, but the tails were a struggle with the sauce. No matter, I couldn't get enough of it. I loved how buttery and smooth the grits were. When mixed with the sauce, they were the perfect consistency and really tasty.  I am SO excited about getting back over to Atchafalaya. I have heard such amazing things about the brunch that I know I will have to try it at some point.

This is a cute little shop that carries tshirts with a New Orleans and Louisiana theme in a city that seems to be full of shops that carry tshirts with a Louisiana theme.  Like Jen mentioned, they are from Laffy, so a lot of their shirts are Acadania-centric, but they have a good selection of NOLA themed shirts that are sure to satisfy anyone with local pride. Aside from shirts, they have baby onesies as well as themed coasters, magnets and post cards.  Their prices are fair and are shirts are only a few dollars more than certain shirts at other shops. Also, their shirts are unique- they don't "recycle" themes from other shirt shops and I appreciated that because it would be really easy to take a "known" phrase and put a new design to it.

This isn't a bad little place, if you happen to be on the Westbank and need some sports equipment.  They sell everything that you could probably need, from football pads to golf clubs.  My only complaint was that their "tailgate" selection of Saints and LSU shirts/jerseys etc was really kind of sad.  There wasn't a big selection at all and there were a limited number of sizes.  I don't know if it was just this particular location, or if I should be looking for game day gear at a specialty shop instead.  I would go here if I need sports equipment, but for other stuff I would go elsewhere.

I have been on a serious Middle Eastern food kick lately and when I told a friend of mine I had never been to Mona's, he insisted that I check it out.  We stopped in for dinner on a Saturday night and the place was empty except for just a few couples. I always have to get the hummus, so we started with some of that and we also got some fried kibby. I had no idea what kibby was, but apparently it's a meat pie type thing served with a type of sour cream sauce. Both the hummus and the kibby were great and the flat bread was plentiful.  For my entree I got the beef schwarma which came with a salad and more hummus (I really can't get enough). The beef schwarma was perfect, moist and tasty. I chose the beef mainly because the chicken tends to be dry at some places, but I might try the chicken next time after reading the favorable reviews. The salad was simple but nice and the hummus went perfectly with everything. I do wish that rice came with the dish, but that's just a preference.   Mona's was fantastic and I would definitely return to satiate another Middle Eastern food craving.

I think that I am quickly becoming a big fan of the coffee here.  I was in Metairie and in the mood for coffee when I spotted this place. Having first tried N.O.C&B for the first time just a few weeks ago, I was all about adding another iced coffee to my frequent buyer card. I got a "large" and it was as tasty as the coffee at the St. Charles location. This spot gets a few extra points because it has a drive thru, making it really convenient, since I was in a bit of a rush.  I do think that $4.10 is a little steep for a large iced coffee, but it has a lot of flavor and you get a lot of it. I wouldn't go out of my way to visit this particular location, but it was good in a pinch.
I stop in here once a week.  No crowd.  Good beer and wine selection.  Fresh produce and bread, always!

Thanks to Steve, I was finally able to try Pizza Delicious after hearing all of the raves about it.  Apparently, this is a pretty hot spot on a Friday night. When I first arrived, the line to order was nearly out the door. Once I made my way to the outdoor patio, and said my hellos, I headed back inside to tackle the long line and place my order.  I decided to get one slice of pepperoni pizza and a Caesar salad (I know, who gets salad at a pizza place?? I'm trying to eat a bit healthier these days. Blah). Once you order, they give you a number and bring your food out to you when it's ready. The first thing that came out was my slice of pizza. It was really big and looked delicious. I took a bite, and as good as it was, it was ALL GREASE. I mean, the grease was dripping out of it when I bit it. I know that pizza is naturally a greasy food, but this just seemed extreme. I was pretty happy that I only got one slice, otherwise I would have really felt gross. That sound you hear is my attempt at eating healthier soaring out of the window.  My salad then came out. I ordered my Caesar salad in a "go box", because I wanted the dressing on the side. Sometimes I tell these places that I want the dressing on the side and they don't remember. Restaurants ALWAYS remember when you ask for the salad "to go"; just a tip. ANYWAY, the salad was so good! It was big and packed with a generous amount of cheese and croutons, so I was really happy and it definitely made up for the greasy pizza. I would definitely recommend the salad.  Because we had a large group, we sat outside so we would have room. Even though it was a nice cool evening, the mosquitoes attacked me with a vengeance. I was chewed up, y'all! Not cute. Maybe they can put a citronella candle out there or something. Other than that, it was really nice to sit outside. Ha.  All in all, Pizza Delicious wasn't bad. I think if I go back, I'll get a pizza with more veggies on it, in order to cut down on the grease factor.

Every now and then a girl likes to treat herself and Trashy Diva has everything that you need in order to make the possible.  I love this place. For those not in the know: I am a sucker for retro fashion and anything a little bit fancy. Trashy Diva has it all. They have an amazing selection of dresses of all types that are perfect for summer. One of my favorite things about this brand is that they have the same color or print in a lot of different styles. This is perfect if you want different styles for yourself, or maybe you want to mix things up for bridesmaids dresses.  This particular store is great because it also has the lingerie section as well. Here you will find fancy underthings that are sure to please. I love the upscale feel of the entire store, but I like that the prices aren't out of this world expensive.  If accessories are more your thing, Trashy Diva has a full case of costume jewelry that will definitely complete your look. I can definitely see myself stopping back in here to get everything that I might need for a fancy night out on the town.  This location on Royal is probably a little more touristy than other locations, but the nice woman working greeted me with a smile when I walked in, and I felt relaxed while I browsed the racks.

Stopped in here on a Friday night after a movie. It was about 10pm, so I was happy to see that they were open. There was really no one else in here, so we sat down, looked over the menu and decided to order the Smokin' Chicken pizza which is chicken breast,  onions, pancetta and green onions.  I was pretty impressed by the pizza. It had a lot of favor and I am not usually the type of person to put chicken on a pizza. Usually if I'm eating pizza I like pepperoni and sausage on there, because if I'm gonna be bad I'm going to do it right. Anyway, a medium ended up being the perfect size for two people and we had no problem finishing it.  I would definitely return, if I found myself in the area. I think it's the perfect place to eat before or after a movie, since it's so close to the theater.

I was in the area, and in the mood for coffee, so The Bean Gallery was a natural pick.  Parking was easy on this particular day- plenty of street parking, and there was a good crowd in the place. I like the atmosphere here and there are plenty of tables and sofas where people can spread out and do work. WiFi is free with a password.  The man working was really nice. I got my usual large iced coffee and I found the coffee here to be good, without being too strong. While I would say the coffee should definitely be sipped, I didn't find it overwhelming at all.  There are some tables and chairs, if you want to sit outside on a nice day and they also serve an assortment of sandwiches if you want to stop in for lunch.

A downtown bar with an uptown feel.  I'm not giving it 5 stars, mainly because it IS downtown (not my scene) and parking is a nightmare.    But I digress...  I went to this place not knowing what to expect.  Tonique is small, cozy and intimate.  The people are friendly and they have a huge choice of cocktails.  Now, let me start by reiterating that I am not a liquor drinker, however, when in Rome...  I started with a "True Kick" which is Gin based.  It was smooth and really easy to drink.  A real "sip" kind of drink, which is always ok with me.  The next drink I tried was a "St Claude" which had a rum base and a cherry under taste.  I liked it a lot and although it wasn't as smooth as my first drink, it was definitely a good one.  The place didn't get too crowded and the people there were really nice.  I would LOVE if this place were smoke free, only because it's so small that the smoke gets thick really fast.  I would definitely go back to this place, maybe on a date.

Great food and they actually carry Kroenenbourg!  Can you believe it??  I have never had a dish here that I didn't like.  I usually get the muffaletta calzone!  Mmmm....so good!  The "Sweep the floor" breadsticks are another fave.  This location is HUGE, so if you have a big group, they can accomodate you and it is walking distance from good Quarter bars.

I went on a date here a while back and I loved this place!  They have a nice patio area, so my date and I decided to sit outside (it was summer).  We both had the salmon and we loved it.  It was perfectly prepared and it was served with a delicious sauce that was incredible.  We decided against wine, but they have a really impressive wine list.  I haven't been back yet, but I have to make that a priority, as I was extremely happy with the service, the food and the place itself.

I was pretty torn between giving this place three and four stars, but I think I'm gonna go with a strong three.  My dad and I came here for his birthday lunch. It was pretty packed when we dropped in around one, so we weren't quick to complain when a waitress guided us to a small table in a corner. The waiter was nice and although it was packed, he was fairly attentive most of the time. We sat at the cramped corner table for a while, and after the place cleared out, we were "allowed" to move to a bigger table. Yippee!  Looking over the menu, everything seemed like pretty "typical" New Orleans food that you would expect from a place like this. Since it seems that I am always getting the fried oyster platter, I decided to mix things up and get the red beans and rice with some hot sausage.   As I waited for my entree, I decided to try a pile of Liuzza's "famous" onion rings. These onion rings are supposed to be the best in the city. They weren't bad, but I wouldn't sit here and say they are the best. They needed a little salt and hot sauce to get them going, but they had a nice crunch to them. I do tend to prefer the rings at Felix's, however.  My red beans and hot sausage came out and it was pretty good. The dish had good flavor and I didn't have to add any additional spice to it. My dad got the fried pork chops, and although they looked big, he later mentioned that they were pretty thin and there was a lot of batter on them.  Liuzza's wasn't a bad experience. I don't know if I would rush back, but for lunch it's a decent choice.

Yay! I had always wanted to check out Grand Theater and I got my chance when we came to see Batman vs. Superman here. I love the comfy reclining seats that make you feel like you are basically at home in your living room (with a bunch of strangers, in the dark). Everything was clean and there wasn't popcorn or old candy wrappers strewn about, so that's a "W" in my book.   I'm usually not one to mention bathrooms in a review, but the ones here were perfect! Everything was neat, clean and well taken care of. This theater is definitely worth the drive if you are looking for an experience that is a little more special than your usual movie night.

I've been to the Big Top a few times, mainly for Burlesque shows. In all honesty, I usually forget about it because it's tucked into a street right off of St. Charles Ave away from the hustle and bustle of the city.  This is a cool little place. It is pretty small and tends to get really packed whenever there is any kind of show. The cash bar is tucked away in a corner, making it somewhat difficult to get a drink if there is a big crowd. I have always enjoyed looking at the art here (when it is bright enough to see it) and for the most part this is a cool little place. I really wish the bathrooms weren't combined, but I guess that's the only option when a place is super small.

Oh my goooooooosh. This is a great store!  So, anyone familiar with my "style" know that I love dresses with a little bit of a vintage/retro/pinup flair. I just happened to stumble into this fabulous shop which carries dresses in the style of "Trashy Diva", "Bettie Page Clothing" and other favorites.  I was in kind of a rush, so I didn't have time to try anything on, but I definitely need to have some kind of shopping spree here soon. I just wish I had discovered this place before the holidays. I would have sent EVERYONE here to purchase my gift.  The dresses here are amazing and you really can't go wrong with anything you find here. Even if you think it's not really your "style", just stop in and check them out. You are bound to find something you will like.

Dinga dong ding!  Only 1 review for Root?  Well, allow me to add the second!  I ate here last night with a friend of mine for one of my birthday dinners.  It was my first time, and it was amazing.  I had the gulf fish and my friend had the scallops.  My fish was amazing and I sampled the scallops, and they were great too!  They came in a cigar box because they are "smoked".  How cute is that??  Also, for the appetizer, we got the Aloo Gabi which is basically grilled cauliflower and potatoes in a yummy sauce.  It was a little spicy, but I loved it.  For dessert we had the "Yorkie" which is a frozen york peppermint pattie served with mint ice ceream, coco puffs (yes, the cereal) and milk.  It was like a fancy pants breakfast and it was awesome.  My friend has already been here about 5 times since they have opened, and I can see why.  The food is amazing, the atmosphere is nice and the staff is great!  Oh, and they are open until 2am on Fridays and Saturdays, so if you are in the mood for some good food at a late hour, this is the place.

Café Hope is such an amazing place. Not only is it a restaurant, but it's a program designed to train young people between ages 16 and 24 in the restaurant business. They are trained in every aspect of the restaurant from the garden to the kitchen to the dining room. They then go on to a job at another restaurant. It's a really incredible program.  I have been to Café Hope twice. The first time I sampled a little bit of the entire menu and the second time was a typical dining experience. This review is of the second time I went, but if you are curious about any of the other food I tried (see pictures) feel free to ask.  My dad and I stopped in here because, although I had been here for a sampling, I had yet to try the shrimp and grits, so that's what I got. I have been on a real grits kick lately and I have no idea why. If I go to a place and grits are on the menu, they are a "go" for me.
