Apparently, they do a good brunch here and people were knocking back the cocktails at 10:00 a.m. This is a cute place to hang out if you want drinks and something to munch on, especially around breakfast or lunch. It's casual but has a good vibe.  I've never had anything other than coffee here, but the flavored beignets are tempting, so I might try them when I find myself here again.

After reading all of the raves about this sushi spot, I was excited when I found myself in the area for lunch.  First of all, I'm going to be honest- I didn't even mess with the tiny parking lot they have. What is the deal with Metairie and those tiny "one way in, one way out" lots? No. Uh uh. I parked across the street and kept my sanity. Walking in, the restaurant is almost as small as the parking lot. There are a few tables scattered throughout and, of course, the sushi bar area. I was seated at a table in the corner by a very sweet waitress.  I decided to start with a miso soup as I looked over the menu. I was pretty hungry, so I got the  protein special roll which is salmon and tuna wrapped around spicy tuna, snow crab and avocado. Note: their special rolls contain no rice. I also got a Philly roll and a crawfish roll. All of the rolls were excellent. The protein roll was huge and well worth the money and, if I'm being honest, I could have gotten this roll and the miso soup and called it a day. The Philly roll was tasty and I especially loved the crawfish roll because it had a nice, spicy kick to it. I have been very into rolls with a little spice added, as of late.  The service was great. The waitress was friendly and fast to take my order and bring everything out, even though the place was full. My drinks were refilled regularly and the little chocolates at the end of the meal were a nice touch. While I wouldn't necessarily drive from the all the way to Metairie for their sushi, I would absolutely choose this spot over other sushi restaurants that I have tried in the area.

Alma is such a fantastic cafe for brunch and lunch! If you're a fan of coffee and delicious Hondura food, this is the place for you.  All-day breakfast includes highlights such as the Alma Breakfast: two eggs, refried beans, sweet plantains, avocado, queso fresco, and homemade crema; Louisa Toast: Louisiana lump blue crab, soft scrambled eggs, mushrooms, and herbs served on white rustic bread with chive cream cheese; Breakfast Tacos: three homemade corn tortillas, scrambled eggs, roasted poblano, pepper jack cheese, crispy potatoes, and avocado served with salsa; and Corned Beef Hash: Homemade corned beef hash, home potatoes served with two sunny-side-up eggs.  The lunch menu is sure to delight with Enchiladas Hondureñas: two enchiladas made with local Louisiana ground beef, green cabbage, sliced boiled egg, homemade red sauce, and queso cotija; Carne Asada: Louisiana-raised Wagyu ribeye, torched cherry tomatoes and encurtido served with four homemade corn tortillas; and Camarones a la Diabla: grilled local Louisiana jumbo shrimp topped with Calabrian chile butter and Japanese panko breadcrumbs.  I wrote about this spot for Offbeat. Read more here: https://www.offbeat.com/articles/dining-out-alma-cafe/

I walked into Coquette, and having made a reservation ahead of time (something that seems to be a luxury in NOLA these days), I was seated immediately by the door. I was taken in by the cozy decor and I definitely felt as if I was in "old" New Orleans. The dining room has a very classic and elegant feel and I felt right at home immediately.  My server was Alex, and since I had never been here before, I hung on his every word as he described everything. The first thing I asked for was a red wine recommendation. He suggested the Malbec, which I settled on. I am no wine expert, so I was happy for the guidance. I was impressed that he actually suggested the least expensive wine. I've noticed at other places they push you in the direction of the steeper priced glasses, but it was nice to see that he was concerned with me actually liking the wine, rather than driving up the bill. The wine was perfect and wasn't too acidic. I know very little about wine, so this was a perfect choice for someone like me.  When it was time to order, Alex was on top of it. Once again, I asked for his suggestions. For the small plate (appetizer) he mentioned how much he liked the fried oysters. He then went into detail about how this dish and others on the small plate list were prepared. For the main entree', Alex suggested I try the fish (I can't remember exactly what type and now I'm kicking myself) and a few other things on the menu. Once again, he wasn't quick to suggest the highest priced dishes on the menu and he went into great detail about how the food was prepared. It was amazing. He didn't stumble once. This man must have a mind like a steel trap!   I ultimately decided on the fried oysters and the fish. The oysters were amazing. They were very lightly fried and extremely juicy and delicious. I could tell that they were fresh, and I liked that I could taste more oyster than batter. The fish was grilled to perfection. It had a thin crust on the outside of it that protected the tender meat inside. Everything was eaten. There were no leftovers. It was incredibly good.  When it came time for dessert, I once again deferred to Alex, who had not yet lead me wrong, and he suggested the strawberries and cream. This light dessert consisted of a candy like shell of strawberry with delicious cream inside. It was topped with a whipped strawberry sorbet that was light and airy. It was the perfect ending to a perfect meal. I liked that it wasn't too heavy and I didn't feel overly full when I had finished my dinner.  I can't wait to return to Coquette. My food and experience were both amazing. If Alex is working on the night you go, be sure to sit in his section and he will take good care of you. I am not usually one to fawn over a waiter, but Alex single handedly ensured that I will return here, dine at Coquette again and recommend it to friends.

We all want to give back to our community, but a lot of times we don't know where to start. Enter the Algiers Point Lil Free Pantry. When I first read about this unique little box in the paper, I was excited about the idea and I knew I had to check it out for myself. Located in the Community Garden in Algiers Point, this little box of blessings works in the same way a Lil Free Library does: you put in what you can and you take out what you need. It's meant to serve those in the community who might be having a tough time and may need some extras to eat or even basic toiletries.  I headed out to the box and I was happy to add some cans of chicken noodle soup, baked beans and yams. I've made a commitment to add to the box weekly, to make sure that the pantry stays full. The box was started and is maintained by Becky Hicks who makes daily donations to the box. This is such an easy way to help others and do a little "feel good" type of thing. This is the first box of it's kind in New Orleans, but I'm hoping that the idea takes off because it's a simple way to take care of others in the community.   Join the movement: https://www.facebook.com/groups/254333225017443/

I have been to this place twice and both times it was fantastic.  The first time I went I got the pig ears (yeah...) and I think I got some kind of sandwich.  That was pretty good.  BUT, the second time I went I got the rabbit and dumplings.  Oh my gosh!  It was one of the most fantastic dishes I have ever eaten.  I had never had rabbit before, so I was hesitant, but it was so rich and delicious, I couldn't get enough.  Be sure to make reservations (if possible) or get there early in order to avoid the dinner rush, because the place does get crowded and getting a table can be a challenge.  Also, they are also the only place that I know that serves actual moonshine.  Do with that what you will.  ;)

When I heard Red Gravy was moving Uptown and serving dinner, I knew I had to get over there!  I was excited to visit Red Gravy on a recent date night with my fiance David. The quaint atmosphere transports you and the smell of delicious food is intoxicating.  We started with the Nanni -- miniature meatballs served with red gravy and fresh ricotta. These meatballs were anything but mini, and the red gravy and ricotta balanced the flavors of the meatballs well.  For an entree, we got Red Gravy's famous lasagna Bolognese, which is layers of ricotta, mozzarella and Bolognese layered delicately together and served fresh-baked from the oven. The lasagna is made fresh, so there's a 30-minute wait time when you order, but it's worth every bite. Our waitress described it as "a true lasagna, the way it's supposed to be."  We also got an order of the Bolognese -- hearty beef and pork ragu served with rigatoni. I loved how much meat was in this, and the flavorful sauce was delicate, yet bold, with the perfect amount of spice. The tastes were exactly what you would expect from any good Italian meal.  If you're a fan of Red Gravy's famous brunch, they still serve it up on Saturdays and Sundays and offer favorites such as shrimp and grits, served Tuscan style, brulee French toast, and breakfast spaghetti, which is served with sausage sugo, ricotta and sunny egg.  I wrote about this spot for Very Local New Orleans! Read my full write up here: https://nola.verylocal.com/red-gravy-restaurant-has-been-around-for-a-decade-but-youve-never-had-it-like-this/164161/

I don't understand why the French Market has such a low rating.    Sure, it's always packed with cheap stuff like sunglasses and lighters and purses, but there is something about it I love.  On a nice day, I like to take a trip down to the french market and go "treasure hunting".  There is no denying that it's a great place to find that perfect souvenir for an out of town friend.  I would much rather patronize this market rather than the dinky little souvenir shops that litter the downtown area and carry tshirts that say things like "I got Bourbon faced on S**t St." (although, that is a classic).  This place carries everything from purses to sunglasses to lighters and everything else in between.  They only accept cash, so be sure to hit the ATM before you go.

I have been so conflicted (oh yeah. CONFLICTED!) as to what to rate Angeline.  On one hand: this place is amazing, as far as atmosphere goes. It might be the perfect date place with the warm lighting and patio access. The wait staff is extremely helpful and attentive and the beer list is pretty impressive.  First of all, for our appetizer we got the roasted cauliflower which was out of this world. It was delicious and amazing and you must get it if you find yourself here. For my entree, I decided on the blue crab fettucine and my dining companion chose the braised pork cheeks and grits.  My dish was okay. The blue crab was delicious, but I found that the pasta was lacking something, but I'm not sure what. I tasted a bit of the braised cheeks and grits and immediate regret set in upon realizing that should have been my choice as well (don't you hate that?). The pork cheeks had SO MUCH flavor and the grits complimented it perfectly. If I had gotten that, this would easily be a four star review.  For now, I am going to go ahead and rate Angeline a strong 3.5 with room for improvement. I definitely hope to return and you better believe I will be getting those pork cheeks.

While this isn't my "go to" salon, I recently had a fancy pants photo shoot and I was sent here to have my "up do" and makeup done.  First, Ms. Jan took care of me and started on my hair. She worked with me to determine what kind of look I wanted, and then she went to work. You can tell that she is a pro, because she had me in a gorgeous up do in no time!  Next, it was time to get my make up done. I went over to Meg and she gave me a "natural" look for the bridal photo shoot that I had planned. Honestly, I don't wear makeup a lot, but when I do I like to put a little more on than she did. I guess when you are doing a bridal shoot, you want subtlety. All in all, I was satisfied with the look I was given.  I can't say I would go back to Salon Couvie, only because they are no where near me, but I will say that if you are in the area and you need hair or makeup done, the Salon Couvie staff does a great job.

A cool fest that would probably be a little cooler if there was more Jazz and heritage. That's not even a joke.  I think that the Jazz Fest definitely has it's place, but over the years I feel like it's just become this big mess of headline acts performing to people who are easily impressed. A little harsh? Yeah, I guess so.  Jazz fest just gets too packed for me and most of the acts that I am interested in seeing can most likely be seen on Frenchmen St on any given night. Immediately when I hear a "big name" band is going to be stopping here on their tour, it puts me off. I mean, why should I have to stand outside in the rain/heat/sweat with a huge crowd of worn down/sweaty/tired people in order to see Dave Matthews Band? Seriously. They have only played Jazz fest the last few times they have played in New Orleans. It isn't cool with me.  And also, I think it costs too much for what it is. Cut me a break on the tickets and I will be sure to eat A LOT of the awesome food that is offered here every year. Deal?

It's so cheesy that you appreciate how cheesy it is after a couple of cocktails.  Yeah, this is a super small *blink and you'll miss it* bar in Pirate's Alley. Yeah, the female bartenders are trussed up like wenches. Yeah, they serve Absinthe. Yeah. the whole place has a pretty "toursity" feel, but by the time you venture into this place none of that is going to bother you.  The place is small and cozy and tends to get packed, but there is seating outside, so what are you complaining about? They serve Absinthe and it comes with a whole fancy story that is intended for tourists but if you're a local, I'm sure you will appreciate it as well. I like it here because it feels like a secret hideout, since it's in alley. Cash only, sucka.

I had been to Cure once before, but since I'm not usually a cocktail drinker, I wasn't impressed.  I went on a Saturday, the place was packed and just seemed like an overpriced meet market.  I was determined to give this place another shot, and boy, am I glad I did!  When I decided to visit Cure again, I was with some friends.  We went early on a Friday evening and we decided to eat there.  I just thought they had little munchies, but they have full on dinner!    I got the short rib debris sandwich that was SO good I actually wrote down the name of it!  It was warm meat served on toast with a thin layer of cheese.  It almost reminded me of an upscale version of the pot roast sandwich from IHOP.  Yeah, I know that's a stretch, but that was really what it brought to mind for me.  Long story short, it was AWESOME!  If you are a fan of meat, as I am, then you have to try it!  For my cocktail, I had a margarita, which was really good and smooth.  It was definitely an "A" list margarita.  If you are looking to beat the crowds, be sure to go a little earlier (before 10).  We went around 8ish and it wasn't bad at all.  I can't wait to go back and get that sandwich or maybe the "breakfast" sandwich, with egg and ham, that they have.  Mmm...

Oh wow! Uber is pretty amazing. I don't understand what people have been complaining about.  We were heading to a fancy party at the zoo this past weekend, and we decided to order an Uber since we were going to be Uptown and the zoo is pretty much right down the street. My friend ordered the car on his phone and immediately we got a little "ding" that the car was on it's way. The coolest thing about it is you get to track where the car is, so you aren't left waiting around wondering if the car is coming.  Tyrone arrived promptly and picked us up and whisked us off to the zoo. His car was very nice with leather seats and the car was super clean. Not only did he bring us to the zoo for the event, but he actually helped us navigate exactly where it was. It was also nice that he was friendly and made nice conversation with us as we drove.  At the end of the night, we ordered yet another Uber to bring us back to our original destination and our car. Once again, the driver was very nice and polite and the car was clean.  I don't know if I would use Uber exclusively, but it's a nice option when you are having trouble getting a cab.

I never make it out to the East, so when I found out I was going to be in the area I hopped onto Yelp and started researching places where I could eat. Hey, I might as well eat some good food if I am going to be in the neighborhood.  Enter Two Sisters 'N Da East. People on Yelp raved about this place, so I decided to stop in and check it out for myself. I was here pretty early for lunch- about 11:30 and the restaurant was fairly empty. I was told to sit anywhere and the waitress brought me a complimentary garden salad, potato salad and corn bread. Well, I like this place already! The salads were delicious and the corn bread went nicely with my meal.  The menu changes daily, and one of the specials of the day was black eyed peas with hot sausage, so I got that. A HUGE portion of black eyed peas over rice came out and I couldn't have been more delighted. The dish was flavored with bits of ham and really delicious. The hot sausage was perfect and was obviously home made and it went wonderfully with the black eyed peas. This was a lot of lunch, so I ate half and enjoyed the rest later that night.  The staff here is so friendly and they make sure that you are happy with everything that you order and check on you regularly to see if you need anything else. I will definitely return to Two Sisters and I would say that the food is so good I would probably make a special trip just to eat here. They even do takeout, if you aren't in the mood to sit and eat. This is home cooking at it's finest and you won't be left disappointed.

Ahh! My sweetie was nice enough to surprise me with some goodies from Sucré and I couldn't have been more delighted. There's just something about a man who knows you have a thing for fancy cupcakes. We each had a vanilla cupcake and red velvet cupcake. The cupcakes are HUGE, soft and tasty. I preferred the vanilla one slightly more that the red velvet because it was a little more moist and it had GLITTER ICING! Who doesn't love edible glitter? It might be the best thing ever. These cupcakes are probably worth whatever you have to pay in order to get your hands on them- they are delicious and decadent and reminiscent of pieces of wedding cake. I can't wait to have more.

Raucous, rowdy and irreverent are all words I would use to describe Krewe Du Vieux.  Classically, the first parade of Carnival season, Krewe Du Vieux is always a good time.  The themes are very "adult" themed, so mom, leave little Timmy at home.  The throws vary from the usual (someone gave me a ceramic mask one year) to the ridiculous (condoms and tequila shots).  This parade is always a good time and is best enjoyed with a cold beer and a good group of friends.  Another Mardi Gras "must".

OH MY GOSH. I don't even know where to start talking about the deliciousness that is Kin.  Kin has been on my list of places to try since it first opened and I finally had my opportunity when my friend mentioned that we get some ramen for lunch. Y'all know I love Asian food of all types and ramen is no exception. If only there were more ramen places in this town. Seriously. I think we only have 2 or 3.  So, this isn't the place to go if you are looking for a super fancy spot to eat. Kin is a small restaurant that is more about food than atmosphere, as Alvin mentioned. The place was packed at lunch, so we sat at the bar area and looked over the menu. We started with an order of dumplings. I have no idea what was in the ones we ordered (pork, I think), but they were fried to delicious perfection and full of flavor.  The special of the day was the brisket ramen. Out came this HUGE bowl of delicious ramen full of different vegetables, an egg, and a pile of brisket. This brisket was so tender and juicy and there was so much of it! The broth was perfect and the noodles were cooked to tender perfection. All of the goodies in the bowl blended together to make for one delicious lunch. I even had leftovers and I love my leftovers. Good news: the leftovers held up and it was all just as good after a night of sitting in the fridge. We both told the owner that he needs to keep the brisket ramen on the menu- it was that good. I'm eager to go back and try the pork cheek ramen, which I have heard great things about.  I will absolutely be back for another bowl of this good stuff.

Yes!  This place is fantastic.  They have wonderful sandwiches and pastas.  One of my faves to get is actually the "vegetarian" sandwich, which is basically a veggie pizza between two pieces of flat bread, but it's really good.  I've also had their chicken pasta which was absolutely fantastic.  This place does great take out, if you are just in the mood to place an order and pick it up.

Pretty good, but I wasn't overly blown away. The iced coffee wasn't too bad but it really wasn't anything special. It was as good as PJ's (and about the same price) but if I'm going to a local coffee shop, I want something a little more special.  The place itself is small. Very small. And it seemed to be lacking something. It didn't feel very "warm" to me and the atmosphere seemed off. The porch was super nice and if it had been a cooler day I would have enjoyed my coffee there.  I would go back for the coffee, but I wouldn't stay.

Ole Saint is owned by Deuce McAllister and is the same idea as Walk Ons, with a New Orleans twist.  We stopped in here a few weeks ago before a LSU game just to get a few drinks and have some "quarter" time. Walking in, I was immediately impressed with the size of the place- the bar area is huge with a lot of space and there is an entirely different section for the restaurant.  We sat at the bar and I was pleased to see a lot of local beer on tap. I am so glad that bars are starting to embrace craft beer, especially local craft beer, and offer more than just Bud Light and Coors. The beer menu is pretty extensive, but if you are a regular craft beer drinker you aren't going to find anything here that you haven't had before. They also have a full bar, if beer isn't your thing, and the bartenders were fast and attentive.  They have quite a few big screen tvs, which makes Ole Saint the perfect place to watch a game and I like that they put a note on the tvs letting you know which game will be shown next. I didn't have any of the food this time, but I saw a few things coming out of the kitchen that looked really good, so I will have to get dinner when I go back.

Ok, I think I discovered the secret of Chiba: sit at the sushi bar and let the sushi chef create something special for you.  I stopped in here with a friend during their late night "happy hour" (funk and roll hour) and we sat at the sushi bar. First of all, their happy hour specials are pretty fantastic. They have a good selection of rolls for $3 as well as a nice assortment of discounted drinks. We decided to let the sushi chef work his magic and make us something amazing.  Nick was our sushi chef and he was super nice and friendly. We kind of just let him "do his thing". First he whipped up a roll with some kind of smoked fish and rice with a sauce on it. It was delicious. Then we decided on the short rib and sauteed duck steamed bun. I didn't have the short rib, but the duck was amazing and I'm not even a person who really likes duck!  Finally the chef made us another special roll that was a typical sushi roll, only instead of fish there was tender meat in it (beef) and it was topped with ginger flakes. I really should have had enough presence on mind to ask for a name, but I honestly just think that he was having fun and experimenting. It was fine with us, because it was fantastic!  I will definitely return for "funk and roll" hour. It's a really neat concept and makes for a more personal experience.

I have to give a special shout out to Christopher W. for my discovery of this spot. I have seen him check in here multiple times which lead me to looking at the menu which lead me to stopping in on a rainy Saturday night.  The rain did not keep the people away and the place was packed when we stopped in at around 8. We were given a 50 minute wait and sent to the bar to get some drinks. Lucky us, some people were getting up right as we got there, so we sat down and decided to eat at the bar.  The bartender was super sweet and she never stopped. She was taking orders at the bar, taking phone orders, serving drinks and getting to-go orders together. A smile never left her face and she never missed a beat. I wish I had gotten her name because she was a pro!  I decided to get the fried oysters with potato salad and mac and cheese. My food came quickly and I eagerly dug in. Okay, it's obvious why this place is so popular- this food is just like homemade. The mac and cheese was nice and gooey, the oysters were fried and  generous and the potato salad was amazing. I polished off the mac and cheese and potato salad in no time. I ate half of the oysters and boxed up the rest.  They also have a house drink called the Pow Wow. If you finish it, you get the next one half off, but don't be a hero. I didn't get one, but I saw the bartender making them and they are probably 90% liquor. It is seriously no joke. I wanted to try one, but I'm not crazy.  I will absolutely return to Neyow's! I loved the food and the staff is great.

When I heard that a new little ramen shop was coming to Magazine St., I was excited to try it. After an AMAZING experience at Kin, my expectations were sky high. They don't open until 4, so I stuck it out for a late lunch/early dinner and walked in as soon as they unlocked the doors.  The restaurant itself is SMALL and the menu is limited, but that just made it easier for me to decide exactly what I wanted. We started with the pork buns which were amazing. The pork was falling out of them and they were so good.   You have two choices when it comes to the ramen: Tonkotsu, which is a creamy pork broth and Geki-Kara, which is their "too-spicy" pork broth. Normally I would have gone with the spicy one, but I got the Tonkotsu this time. I tried a taste of my dining companion's "spicy" broth and it wasn't bad at all, so I might get that next time. For a few minute up-charges you can get an extra egg, seaweed, corn and other goodies added to the bowl, but I just went with the bowl without the add ons. I found the Tonkotsu really tasty- the pork was cooked perfectly and the broth was flavorful. I wished that there had been a little more food in the bowl (without having to pay extra), but I still enjoyed it.   A few notes: there are no refills on drinks which is...odd. I had the iced tea and it's just iced tea. It's not bottled or anything. Why can't I get a refill? For 3 bucks I should be able to get at least one refill. As others have mentioned they don't have a vegan option, so hopefully they will add that in the future. Last but not least, they don't let you take any leftovers with you. I had no leftovers because a friend of mine had already warned me about this weird little quirk. I'm really glad I was super hungry when I got here at 4!  Finally: Is Nomiya is good as Kin? Short answer: Not in my opinion. Long answer: Kin has a more diverse menu, their bowl has more flavor (and it's HUGE), they give you free drink refills and they let you take your leftovers home. And y'all, leftover ramen is the best!  I'd go back to Nomiya, if they made a few changes. Otherwise, head to Kin for your ramen fix.

I was introduced to this by my boyfriend.   I'm pretty picky when it comes to Chinese food, but this place is great.  My faves are the steamed dumplings, crab rangoon and fried rice.  Food is ready fast and it's always good!

Oh yes! I stopped in here for one reason and one reason only: their beautiful stock of all the Yves Saint Laurent makeup you can handle!  I was greeted when I entered the store, but I didn't need any help- I knew exactly where I was going. Yves Saint Laurent makes the most luxourious makeup that you can find and I think that this Sephora is the only place in our area that carries the full line (correct me if I'm wrong!).  I treated myself to some yummy red lipsticks and a few of the eye shadow palettes they have. This stuff isn't cheap: lipsticks are $36 each and the small palettes are $60 each. I decided to treat myself because I love this line so much and it wears beautifully.  Sephora is great because they offer a lot of different brands that range in price from cheap to a little more "spendy". They have a SPECTACULAR Christian Louboutin lipstick that I pretty much need, but I'm going to wait a bit before I go and drop $90 on a lipstick.  The women who work here are always friendly and eager to help, and if you are ignorant about makeup they will guide you in the right direction and find something that works well for you.

Didn't actually step into this place, but we did order delivery from here.  We had the grilled chicken pizza and it was so good. It's a veggie pizza topped with chunks of chicken. The best part is the HUGE pieces of roasted garlic. I LOVE garlic, so it was awesome finding yummy pieces of garlic buried under mounds of cheese and other toppings. Speaking of cheese, there was tons of it. Magazine Pizza does not skimp at all. I will definitely be trying other pies from this place!

Goorin Bros. is one of those places where I would definitely splurge on a regular basis, if I had the money and if I had the occasion to wear a lot of different fancy hats.  We stopped in here during French Quarter Fest and I think I was secretly hoping that I would stumble across the perfect sun hat, because I was baking in the sun. Alas, it wasn't meant to be, but they do have a nice selection of different fancy hats for special occasions. The selection of women's hats seems to be a bit more generous than other hat shops I've visited, and the staff seems to be pretty cool with people coming in and trying on hats to see what works best for them. Hats aren't cheap, but you can tell that they are made to last.  Goorin Bros. does frequently have sales, so I think the next time they have one of their sample sales I will have to treat myself.

The Rusty Nail is okay. I don't know if I understand the obsession that some people have with that place. They serve decent drinks and the staff is nice and friendly.  The real selling point of "The Nail" is the patio. It's large and gorgeous and on a nice night you can sit out there with friends and have a really nice evening under the stars.  There's pretty much nothing else for me to add that hasn't been said already. I'll return to The Rusty Nail, but I won't go out of my way.

If you're going on vacation, renting a car is the way to go.  David and I decided that renting a car would be the best idea for our trip to Pensacola and we were right. David booked a 4 door car on booking.com, made all the arrangements and the car was ready for pickup at 8am on the day of our trip. The car was the perfect size, super comfortable and had plenty of room for luggage and room to spread out. The car didn't have any funky smells and it was clean and ready to go when we picked it up. Not only that, but the car got fabulous gas mileage and got us safely to and from Pensacola with no issues at all.  You have to put down a $250 fee, with the regular fee, when you rent the car but you get that back when you return the car. We are definitely going to be renting from Enterprise again.

I felt pretty fancy going here for my first ever facial. I didn't even really know what to expect or what a facial entailed, so I went in completely blind.  When I met Sunny, the esthetician, she immediately seemed really nice and put me at ease. She lead me to a small room, and after a few questions and a minute to get comfortable, the facial began.  She started with some nice aroma therapy. She then proceeded to put all kinds of stuff on my face and upper body. I have no idea what it was, but it was really relaxing. My favorite part was definitely when she wrapped my face in hot towels and then massaged my arms and shoulders. I seriously could have fallen asleep. The towels completely blocked out everything else in the room and the heat relaxed all of the muscles in my face. In fact, I'm going to start wrapping my face in towels regularly- just for fun. I left with skin that felt amazing and fresh.  My experience was fantastic and I would absolutely go back for another facial. I got the 30 minute one this time, but they also have an hour one that I would love to try.

Like everyone else, I'm going to go ahead and call this store really cute. They have a great selection of shoes and they were even having a really nice sale when I was here. Whether you are looking for "night on the town" type shoes or just casual shoes, you will find some good deals here.  When I was here I was looking for some shoes to go with my Halloween costume. The woman working was very helpful and although I didn't find exactly what I was looking for, I saw enough to know that I will be returning whenever I am in the need for some stylish pumps. They also carry a nice selection of New Orleans themed t shirts that are made out of a really soft cotton, so check that out if it's your thing.

I think this is the third or fourth time I've reviewed a pho restaurant inside the Hong Kong market in this very same location. I really hope that this one sticks around.  I have described the atmosphere of this spot in past reviews and nothing has really changed- it's a seat yourself situation with a good number of tables and chairs and big tvs on the walls. We were here for an early dinner and we were the only ones dining, so we were served quickly.  To start, we got the charbroiled pork spring rolls and for my entree I got a large bowl of the round steak and brisket pho. You get two sizes of pho here: large and extra large, so I decided to go with the large just to see what we were working with as far as portions go. Since we were the only ones here, our spring rolls and pho came out together and within 5 minutes of our order. The spring rolls were pretty good. They aren't the best I have ever had, but I enjoyed them. I really enjoyed the pho. The large serving was actually really large and the broth had good flavor. My one complaint was that the concoction was lacking the usual onions and peppers that come in pho that i have had elsewhere. It was basically broth, meat and noodles. This isn't a huge deal, but I feel like it did change the flavor a bit.  Saigon Noodle House offers a solid bowl and, if you are in the area, they are definitely worth checking out. It's not the best pho I have ever had, but I wouldn't hesitate to eat here again.

What kind of weirdo goes to a Jamaican food truck and gets a veggie burger? Um...I do!  I guess I really wasn't in the mood for jerk chicken when I decided to mosey up to this truck for a bite to eat. The veggie burger wasn't bad. It certainly got the job done. I was starving when I noticed this truck! I would try it again and I would probably get the jerk chicken and not the veggie burger.

I was really bummed when the Vietnamese place that was here previously closed, but when I saw that a new place was moving right in, I was excited to give it a shot. After all, I love a good bowl of noodles and since today was rainy and cold, I figured this was as a good a day as any to drop in for lunch.  We stopped in at about 12:30 and the place had a nice little crowd of Vietnamese folks enjoying their lunches: I took this as a really good sign. My friend and I are both Vietnamese food fanatics, so we decided that we were going to sample a few things just to get a feel of the place.  I started by ordering a Vietnamese iced coffee. This came out in the traditional way, in the little brewer, with condensed milk at the bottom. I then poured it over ice in a glass and enjoyed. Don't you hate when it all come out already mixed? It was tasty and a great start to the experience.  We decided to start with an order of pork spring rolls and fried egg rolls. The egg rolls came out first. There were four of them, they were big and served with fish sauce. Talk about delicious! The rolls had a lot of flavor and were cooked nicely with a flaky crust on the outside and deliciousness on the inside.  The spring rolls came out next. The first thing I noticed was the peanut sauce: it was super thick and had some sriracha on top that we mixed in to add a little bit of a "kick" to it. I liked that the sauce was thick, but my dining companion didn't and would have liked it a little thinner. The spring rolls were good. My only tiny complaint would be less vermicelli noodles and maybe a little more pork. The pork was yummy, but there were a couple of bites where I got nothing but noodles.   Finally, I ordered a large bowl of eye of round and brisket pho for $8 (#20 on the menu). WOW. This might be the largest "large" bowl of pho I have ever encountered! I could have gone swimming in this thing. They are extremely generous with the portions here and the bowl was packed with meat! The broth had a nice rich flavor and I could tell that this pho had definitely been cooking over night. All of the flavors melded together perfectly and no one flavor was more overwhelming than the other. It all mixed together wonderfully and made for an excellent lunch.  My large bowl was so large that the waitress had to pack it up for me so that I could take it to go. Speaking of the waitress, she was super sweet and made sure that we had everything we needed. They were fast with getting the food out, but still gave us enough time so that we could enjoy each dish.  My experience here was fantastic and I can't wait to return. I am eager to see what some of the other pho lovers have to say about this spot. I know that I am not as "seasoned" as some people, so I am eager to hear what folks with better tuned palates have to say about this bowl. I am encouraged that this place has only been open since Monday and there is already a nice crowd. I will be back soon.

David and I stopped in here before seeing a movie and I was surprised how packed the place was. There was a 30 minute wait for a table, so we just decided to sit at the bar.  Cajun Cannon is a sports bar on steroids: the place is huge with multiple rooms, huge tvs (including tvs in the bathroom), sports memorabilia on every surface, and an extensive menu. We started with an order of the alligator balls, which came out fried to perfection, nice and crispy and hot with a tasty dipping sauce. They were really good and were a great start to the meal.  For my entree I got the cheese burger, topped with bacon and fries on the side. WOW. I tend to be pretty picky when it comes to burgers and this one was great! It was cooked to medium-perfection, it was super juicy and the bacon was nice and crispy. This might be one of the better burgers in the area, believe it or not. The burger was so big that I could barely manage to maneuver into it and I ended up taking half of it home for later. The fries were okay, but nothing overly special. The real star of the show was the burger.  I would go back to Cajun Cannon and get that burger again. for sure. I imagine this is a really fun place to watch the game. Maybe I'll find myself here when the Saints go back to the Super Bowl.

Honesty time: I am super boring when it comes to breakfast. I don't need anything fancy- just give me the basics. Of course, I went to a fancy brunch place today and got my usual basics. Of course I did. So, here's my basic review.  I've heard raves about Coulis for a while. I've been told they do breakfast and they do it well and I finally made my way over here to check it out. I'm easy to please when it comes to breakfast and I always get the same thing: two eggs over easy, toast, grits and bacon. That's exactly what I got here and it was pretty good. The bacon was crispy, the portion of grits was generous and the wheat toast was yummy.   I have two tiny complaints: the eggs were a bit under cooked and runny and I like them a bit stiffer and we were seated at a tight table in the back. In the grand scheme of things, this is not a huge deal.  I will go back mainly because they have a Cuban sandwich on the menu (not available on weekends) and I must try every Cuban sandwich in the greater New Orleans area. Nothing will beat El Libre, I'm sure, but I am willing to do all the research necessary to find the best of the best.

One word: Tomato Basil Soup  Really, that's all you need to know.  The soup...it is to die for.  Everything I have gotten here has been fabulous.  They have great desserts and bread, but that soup...WOW.  Let's just say this...they sell it by the jar.  That's how awesome it is.  Great prices and great food.  Who can hate that?

My boyfriend and I's favorite breakfast spot.  He usually gets the french toast, which looks delicious.  We have also gotten the big breakfast and the breakfast sandwich they have there.  The food is always awesome and if you like bacon, they don't "stiff" you on it.  Coffee isn't fabulous, but you can eat outside with your dog, if you want.  Great on Saturdays after the Gretna Farmers Market, which is just a few steps away.

I love finding places off the beaten path and then they turn out to be delicious!  I was in the mood for something of the Mediterranean variety, and Kebab had been on my list for a while, so I stopped in here while in the area. The setup is easy: order at the counter and wait for them to bring you your food. Everything on the menu sounded so amazing, but we decided to start with some Belgian fries and I got the portabello mushroom veggie sandwich.  The Belgian fries were great! I'm not sure what makes them different from regular old French fries, but they were salty and definitely a great start to the meal. Then out came my sandwich. Whoa! There's a lot to take in here. First of all, the sandwich is HUGE! It's packed to the brim with mushrooms, greens, beets, pickles, red onions and topped with feta, garlic and turmeric dressing. For $8.50, this might be one of the best sandwich deals in town. The sandwich was full of flavor and the turmeric dressing added a nice little touch to it. I can't put my finger on it what the taste reminded me of, but it was great. I also liked that they were super generous with the feta. The juices from the whole thing soaked nicely into the bread, but the bread is such that it's integrity stayed in tact.  The menu is pretty limited, but if the rest of their offerings are anything like this portabello sandwich, then I will definitely be trying some of their other stuff. This is one of those places that makes me wish I lived in the neighborhood. I would love to drive down and grab one of these sandwiches for lunch or dinner on a regular basis.

It's easy to see why they call it Burger King. This place is truly tops when it comes to a good burger. The burgers are flame broiled, so you can really taste the difference. Is it real meat? Who knows and who cares? When something tastes this good, you just want to eat it. I really like how the slice of American cheese that was haphazardly slapped onto my double cheeseburger was clearly done so with love. Was the cheese melted onto the burger? Of course it wasn't! It was still cold from the fridge, just how you like it. The bun was perfectly warmed to slightly above room temperature which added a nice touch to this meal that I scarfed down in my car, in under 3 minutes, while at a red light.  I actually was impressed that no one was here in the mid afternoon and I was served quickly without any fuss. Brava.

I really loved this bar. On a night where we were trying to avoid a huge crowd, it was a life saver. They have a jukebox in the back and it's nice and dark. I love a dark bar! A few street performers filtered in and out for drinks and it just seems like a really fun spot. The bartender was really friendly and welcoming and the beer was good.

Surprisingly, things are pretty well organized here. I've never been confused or gotten lost when I was trying to figure out where to go. Parking is fairly plentiful. People working here taking care of tickets are really nice and helpful.

A large gallery of bodypainted works located in the French Quarter.  Craig is a true artist and paints everything on the human body from landscapes to animal prints.  It's such a unique art.  You can buy pictures of his work at his gallery.  Craig takes his work very seriously and travels the world attending different body painting conventions and events.  He is known for bodypainting large groups on White Linen Night and Halloween night and sending them off to hypnotize all the people who are out and about for these events.  If you want, you can even contact Craig about possibly being a living canvas for his gorgeous work.

I can't really give a review of a "full on" dinner experience here, but we did stop in on the tail end of happy hour and sat at the bar and ate.  The bartender was friendly and took our order and brought our food out fairly quickly. I had the Caesar salad with chicken, which was nothing overly spectacular, but it hit the spot at the time.  I think their happy hour starts at some insane time like noon and goes until 7, so if you are looking for an early drink, this might be a good place to start.

Total lifesaver! We were out for Halloween fun when I started realizing I was pretty hungry. Being the good Yelper that I am, I had done my research ahead of time and bookmarked some quick and cheap food spots where we could grab a bite to eat.  We found ourselves at Copper Monkey fairly early, all things considered- 6:30. We sat at the bar and looked over the menu. I knew what I wanted immediately- the Copper club wrap with pasta salad sounded divine. Don't you just love a place that offers more than just fries on the side? The wrap came packed with ham, turkey, swiss cheese, cheddar cheese, bacon, avocado and mayo. WOW. They were super generous and I was more than happy with the serving size. The pasta salad was delicious as well and had tomato and artichoke in it. Artichoke is one of my faves, so I was really happy. For $11.50, this meal was not only a deal, but it hit the spot as well. My boyfriend got the burger and he raved about how good it was, so that's worth trying if you are in the mood for meat.  Copper Monkey is definitely worth checking out if you are in the area and want a quick bite to eat. They serve more than typical bar food and the atmosphere is friendly and welcoming.

I have been on the hunt for organic soap for a while now, so when someone suggest I check out the Herb Import company, I was a bit confused. I thought this place only sold incense and essential oils. I had no idea that there is so much more to this shop!  Not only was I able to find my amazing organic soap, but they had it in all kinds of yummy scents and it didn't break the bank. This shop also carries a wide variety of things such as Saints you can display in your car (holy Saints, not NFL Saints), assorted vitamins and supplements, organic teas, "good luck" candles and interesting gifts that are perfect for the more spiritual person in your life. Of course, they do also sell incense and essential oils, but you should go in knowing that they sell a little bit of everything.  Bonus points: this shop smells so good!

Wow. This drugstore has changed A LOT from the times I used to go here as a kid with my grandmother. A little back story about me: I used to really dig this place as a kid because it was so random. It was super small and nothing was really organized. You would find the cookies next to the cotton balls which was next to the face cream. I remember once being in here and finding a perm kit that looked like it was from the 70's. Seriously. There was no rhyme nor reason.   Well, when I stopped in here today it was like I was stepping into another world. Everything has been redone and it's more like a Walgreens than a little pharmacy down the block. They have all kind of things from snacks to vitamins to everything else you could probably want. They even have a refrigerated section so that you can pick up milk or juice while you wait on your prescriptions.  From what I could tell, everything was really well priced and although I didn't need any prescriptions filled, I did notice that they had a lot of people working the counter and they seemed to be getting people through quickly.

We had a major craving for crawfish when we we decided to check this place out. They have crawfish at $5/lb, so the prices aren't terrible right now.  This is a pretty basic place: they have a bar area, you sit at a table and you order whatever you want. We decided to get a few pounds of crawfish, potatoes and two big pieces of sausage. The crawfish was pretty good, and although I like it when it's a bit spicier, I enjoyed them. It's early in the season, so they were small and some were mealy, but that's not the fault of Perino's. The potatoes were delicious and the sausage was perfect.  Aside from crawfish, they have crabs, shrimp and oysters so they will satisfy any seafood desire that you just so happen to have.

I really never go to this Popeye's, even though it is the one closest to my house. Why? Because they are super slow and they are stingy with that you get for your money. I usually order a breast, a wing and a large mashed potato. The chicken breast is consistently lacking in the "meat" department (this is a problem at most Popeye's these days) and they NEVER fill my mashed potato container to the top. Never. They always leave about an inch and a half of space and I have to tell them to fill it to the top. What is the problem here? Are their managers telling them to leave an inch and a half of space? It's just really ridiculous, considering Popeye's is one of the more expensive fast food places around. At least give me what I am paying for and don't try to cheat me. I shudder to think about all of the people who DON'T check that kind of thing before leaving the store. This is why I never go through the drive through anymore.   Oh yeah, that's another thing. If you complain about the food in the drive through, they make you park and go inside to get any issue taken care of. Ridiculous.

It's a bar!  It's a theatre! One Eyed Jack's has everything.  This place has regular burlesque shows as well as comedy shows and live music.  They have 80's night on Thursdays starting at 10 and the it is by far one of the most popular weekly events in the city and the place gets packed.    The drinks are pretty cheap, by quarter standards, and the people here are always nice.  Great place to hang out if you are an "artsy" type, as you are sure to meet someone here that you have something in common with.

Okay, this is a really cute bed and breakfast type spot, but the cleaning situation seriously needs to be addressed.  The room that I was in was lovely: a four poster bed with nice bedding, a good size T.V., beautiful drapes adorned with flowers and flowery wallpaper to match. I LOVED the huge bathroom with the pedestal sink and large walk in shower. The room was cozy without feeling too small.  My issues are with the cleaning, or lack thereof. There were two mugs for coffee, one had a VERY OBVIOUS lipstick print on it. I learned a long time ago that they don't wash dishes all the time at these smaller places, but how did you miss that? You rinse the cup and don't wipe the rim? Did you even rinse the cup?? I was pretty grossed out thinking about it. And then, kind of easy to see, someone's gross (lipstick stained) cigarette had rolled right under the microwave. The cleaning person didn't see that, but I saw it as soon as I walked in. Also, this is a non smoking room, so I guess someone was incognito smoking in the room. Hmmm okay.  I'm giving three stars simply because the building itself is lovely with a winding staircase inside and a lovely porch and garden outside. As nice as the decor is, I would have trouble returning or recommending this spot since they can't manage to clean it properly.

This is a cute cafe located in the Roosevelt hotel and is a pretty perfect spot for lunch  This was a tough call, as far as a rating goes. On one hand, the Cuban sandwich I had wasn't the best I've ever had but I was starving when I ate it and it really hit the spot. The truffle fries were amazing. They came with aioli for dipping and I couldn't get enough. I could have had an entire meal of fries. They have a really cute case that is full of little chocolates to choose from and they also have coffee drinks.  They have a few sandwich and salad options here and while it isn't the cheapest lunch in the city, you get a good amount for what you pay for.  I'm marking the place three stars, but would probably lean more towards 3.5 stars, if this were Star Search.

I was excited to try Fellini's today because I had noticed that a lot of yelpers check in here and it sounded like a good location for lunch.    So, I went today for lunch and the place was pretty empty.  I ordered the ham and cheese sandwich which came with a side of pasta salad.  Ok, so the sandwich wasn't anything amazing and I've had better pasta salad, but for lunch it wasn't bad.  I'm giving this place four stars for a few other reasons.  There is outdoor seating on a lovely patio.  It seems like a great place to have lunch with girlfriends, sip wine and watch the world go by.  Another good thing about it, although the place is small, there is a nice size parking lot.  One of my biggest pet peeves of other "cafe" type places is lack of parking or super small lots.  Yeah, service was slow, but that's not a huge deal.  I sat at my table and read the latest issue of the "New Orleans Levee".

This is a tough call, but I am going to give the food 4 stars and the service 2 stars. This is going to be a long review, so grab a snack.  We made reservations here for a Friday night, because we were going to see a show at the Saenger and we wanted to eat somewhere close. We arrived a bit after our 7 o'clock reservation (the show was at 9:30) and were seated at a small table next to a wall. This wasn't a huge deal- at first. It kind of became a bit of an issue when a few minutes later a couple walked in with no reservation and were seated at a nice roomy table in the middle of the room. I get that they have to accommodate who comes in when and what's available, but it kind of bugged me because we were a little cramped.  When I was first seated I was given the menu along with a wine list. I then waited 10 minutes before I was asked if I wanted a drink. Our wine was brought out and a lump of butter on a plate was placed between us with zero explanation and zero bread. About 10 or 15 minutes later the waiter came back over and asked if we were ready to order. We ordered and I asked about bread. The waiter said, with a bit of attitude, "The bread is in the oven. It's coming." Well, thanks. Maybe mention that next time when you just abandon some butter on the table. The bread did eventually come and the one good thing about getting bread fresh from the oven- it's hot.  For our appetizer we got the Beggar's Purse, which is lump crab meat wrapped in a flaky pastry shell. It was nothing overly special, but I enjoyed it and it served as a nice start to the meal. For our entree we both got the Puppy Drum Pontchartrain which was drum topped with crab meat and served with mashed potatoes and asparagus. Again, this wasn't anything that blew my socks off, but the fish had a lot of flavor, the potatoes were creamy and the asparagus was crispy and added a nice touch. All in all I enjoyed the meal and I would recommend both of these dishes to anyone dining here.  After dinner, the waiter brought over a dessert menu and again disappeared for about 10 minutes. When he returned, he was going over the menu with us and explaining what was what when a large party walked in. The waiter literally stopped in the middle of his sentence, turned from us and walked over to the walk-in party and tended to them. He didn't give us an "Excuse me a moment" or a "I'll be right back" or anything. It was very strange. He walked off in the middle of the conversation. When he returned, we ordered the Bourbon Swamp Pop Martini Float and two Irish Coffees. After another long wait of probably 10 to 15 minutes, the float came out sans Irish Coffees. When we reminded the waiter of our order, he looked genuinely confused and said he would get them right away. "Right away" here is 5 minutes, so we were happy we didn't have to wait longer than that.   The entire meal lasted 1 hour and 50 minutes. Look, I'm not an impatient person. I would be totally understanding if the place was packed (it wasn't) or if we didn't have a reservation (we did) or if the food was held up because we were chatting rather than eating. I would love to recommend this place to friends, but the service needs to pick up a bit of urgency. To leave people sitting and waiting, or walking off in the middle of a conversation to serve walk-ins, just makes people feel a bit insulted.  Cliff's: good food, slow service, stop in if you aren't in a rush.

Question: why is the hot new trend things that are knitted? Dresses that are knitted. Shorts that are knitted. I don't get it, but if you like knitted things, H & M has tons of it!  I can't figure out how I feel about H & M. On one hand they have some cute things at good prices, on the other hand I feel like most of their clothes are geared towards 21 year old girls living in California. However, I am glad that this huge new store opened at Oakwood.  This store is pretty big and they have clothes for men, women and kids. They have a large selection of mainly casual clothes and they have a decent shoe and lingerie section. The shoes don't look like they would last that long, but they are only about $10, so it's still a deal.  When I visited this store, I was happy to see that the line was super long, so they seem to be doing good business already. The staff seemed capable and were getting people in and out fairly quickly.

Sometimes a girl needs something sexy- either for her own thrill, or the thrill of another. Enter Trashy Diva.  Don't let the name fool you- there is nothing "trashy" about this spot. Here you will find the best of the best when it comes to lingerie and other underthings. I scooped up a bra (and a few other frills) for a keen price and the staff was more than willing to help me figure out exactly what I needed.  If you are looking for a little bit of satin and lace to make you feel special, then this is the spot for you. Don't be shy about asking the staff for some help, they are here to make sure you find exactly what you are looking for.  I had NO IDEA you could hold events here and thanks to Emily M., I will be making a note of this and will probably have a party here in the future. What a brilliant idea!

Yes yes. Ba Chi did not disappoint.  I was delighted when I arrived here and I was seated on the enclosed patio on a nice (but rainy) evening. It made for a nice atmosphere, even though it was a little humid.  We started with a couple of pork spring rolls. While they weren't the best I have ever had, they were definitely tasty and the pork was cooked to perfection. For my meal I decided on the Pho with rare flank and brisket. It was out of this world. Not only was I served a huge bowl that was packed to the brim with meat and noodles, but the broth had a lot of flavor. It was so yum and the brisket was cooked to perfection and piled high in the Pho. It made for an amazing meal. I have to say that I really liked the prices. Some of these places feel that they need to mark the food up a bit because the restaurant is uptown. Here you get a good uptown meal at an excellent price.  Extra points because my friend requested that he take his leftover Pho to go. The waitress took it to box it up and accidentally dropped it, so she gave him an entire new order (complete with a baggie of bean sprouts!), even after he had told her not to worry about it. That's good business for you. Stop in. Eat. You won't be let down.

This is a pretty good PJ's with a friendly staff. I love the fact that it's big and the windows let in a lot of natural light. I ordered my regular large iced coffee and it was good, but I think that the half and half I added to it was off. It had an odd taste, so I blame the add-in.  There are plenty of big tables so that you can sit and do work and, of course, the wi-fi is free. This wouldn't be my first choice for a NOLA PJ's, mainly because there's a sketchy gas station across the street, but it gets the job done if you're in the area.

I had been anxiously awaiting the opening of this spot since I first heard about it. I stalked their Instagram. I pestered them on Facebook. I was ready for something delicious in the neighborhood. The day is finally here and I have been to the promised land.  Located in the old NOLA Smokehouse building, Turkey and the Wolf is a yummy neighborhood sandwich place that I predict is going to be the next big thing in the NOLA lunch scene. I was here today and I already knew what I wanted- I had to have the ham sandwich. Ham, cranberry sauce, cheese, herb mayo all on a roll is just what the doctor ordered. You order at the counter, they give you a table marker and then they bring the food out.  My sandwich was delicious. They were generous with the ham, the cranberry sauce was a perfect touch and that herb mayo was out of this world. Seriously, I wonder if they make the mayo in house or if it's by some fancy mayo company or something. My friend got the ham sandwich and the chicken skin deviled eggs and they looked SO GOOD. I will definitely be getting those next time along with one of their head cheese sandwiches.  Although the place has only been open two days, they are fast about taking orders and getting the food out. It wasn't crazy packed today, but I predict that will change once word gets out about how good the food is. One tiny suggestion: I wish there was an option to get a bag of chips with my sandwich. I would be willing to pay an extra dollar or two for that option.  I highly recommend Turkey and the Wolf and I will be back.

Stopped in here during French Quarter Fest to take a break from the heat and get a bite to eat. Considering it was a busy day, we were seated and served quickly.  We got to sit in a small table in the corner, which I really liked. It was nice to be away from the crowd for a while. We decided to order the muffaletta and split it. It was a little on the bready side, but after a long day on my feet it was delicious and hit the spot.  I loved the atmosphere of this place. All of the doors were open and people were sitting outside and inside eating and talking and enjoying each other and the nice day. It gave the afternoon a very quaint feel and I really appreciated it.  I'l definitely be back and I'm excited to try the other food that they offer.

To the locals, the Gambit might not be much, but I think it's an excellent resource for out of town visitors.  Available at many venues through the city, the Gambit offers information on events that are going on in the city such as live shows, fests and gallery showings.  The Gambit offers reviews of restaurants and has articles about little historic things that are going on the city.  For example, in the Mardi Gras issue, there was an article about the history of Rex.  It's not one of the greatest free publications in the city, but considering that it is probably geared more towards tourists, it gets the job done.

This is a neat little grocery store. It reminded me a little of Whole Foods, but not as snobby.  I came here looking for something specific and was helped right away. The staff is friendly and everything is really easy to find.

Anyone who knows me knows of my love of anything vintage/vintage inspired. For me, Bambi Deville's is a dream come true.  This gorgeous shop has room after room of delicate vintage pieces from many decades and you are sure to find something that suits you, whether you are looking for something to wear every day or you are shopping for a special night out. We stopped in during French Quarter Fest and we were greeted by the owner, who was on the porch taking in the sights.  This shop has a little bit of everything. I was most blown away by the vintage 50's prom dresses and I found myself wishing that I had an excuse to spend my money on one. Aside from the clothing, the selection of beautiful rhinestone vintage jewelry is to die for. Delicate bracelets and necklaces that were lovely, but a bit too pricey for me.  As others have mentioned, the best thing about this shop is the condition of the clothing. All of it looks barely worn/well taken care of. I could tell that the owner takes great pride in the pieces she decides to display in her shop.  I didn't buy anything on this visit, but I will absolutely be returning in the future, especially if there is a special occasion for which I would want to wear vintage.

Two new sushi places in a week!  Lucky me!  I had never been to Sushi Brothers, and I'm always eager to try new sushi places.  Seriously.  I think I want to review every single one in the city.  Anyway, we weren't super hungry when we ate here, so we only ended getting three rolls.  We got a crunchy dynamite roll, a cucumber roll and a special roll, the black and gold roll.  I won't bore you with the details of the crunchy dynamite and cucumber rolls.  They were good, and let's face it, that stuff is hard to screw up.  The black and gold roll was fantastic!  I can't remember what was in, except that it had cream cheese and it was topped with avocado and mango.  They said that it is their most popular specialty roll, and I can see why.  It is fantastic!  Don't be scared of the cream cheese, fish combo...it's really good!  I would definitely go back here.  I like that it has a more casual feel than a lot of other sushi places around town.

I was starving after a Yelp Gets Physical event when I popped onto Yelp to check my bookmarks and discovered that Le's was nearby. I decided to head over and get myself some dinner to go.  Finding the restaurant was super easy and parking was a breeze. As soon as I walked in one of the owners, Michael, shook my hand and greeted me. "You came to the right place!", he proclaimed and I was instantly happy that I had chosen this spot for dinner.  Ordering is simple: let them know what you want at the counter and sit and wait for your order to be ready. I decided to get the five spice bbq pork vermicelli bowl with an egg roll on the side. It was ready pretty fast and I was on my way within 10 minutes.  After I got my meal home and dug in, I was blown away. Not only was the portion HUGE, but it was packed with flavor. I liked that they put the sauce on the side in little cups, so that I can add it myself. The egg roll was great and was a perfect addition to the bowl. For $12 it was a great dinner and very filling. This wasn't some puny little salad- this was a meal.  I'm eager to go back and try their pho and some of their sandwiches. The staff is beyond friendly and welcoming and the food is great!

Because everyone needs goals in life, I am on a mission. That mission is to eat at all of the restaurants listed on the "38 Essential New Orleans Restaurants, January 2015": http://nola.eater.com/maps/the-38-essential-new-orleans-restaurants-january-2015  I had already eaten at 22 of the above establishments, when I found myself in the mood for Mexican. I rushed over to Casa Borrega to satisfy the craving.  First of all, the decor in this joint is choice. I love the Catholic/Mexican/Dia De Los Muertos feel of the entire place. I almost felt like I was having dinner in a fancy Mexican Church. Or maybe I felt like I was having dinner on a Dia De Los Muertos altar. Whichever it was, I liked it.  I hadn't had a margarita in way too long, so the first thing I did was order a "Margarita Borrega", which was muy delicioso. I might have had two, but who was counting?  The first thing they do after you order your drinks is bring you some chips and fresh guacamole. OH MY GOSH! This guacamole puts my homemade guac to shame. It's super fresh and it's nice and thick with tomatoes in it. I couldn't get enough. One complaint: the chips are way too thin for the thickocity of the guac, so they tend to break. As far as "issues" go, that's not a big one.  As for the menu, everything sounded incredible, especially the "Plato Mixo", which was basically a little sample of everything. You gotta really ask yourself, "Do you want to walk out of here or waddle?" I chose to walk, so I went with the Enchilada de Mole instead.  Let me tell you- these chicken enchiladas were delectable and they were not shy about smothering them in mole sauce. I'm not complaining! The sauce was AMAZING and the enchiladas were incredible. The dish came with a side of beans and rice, but honestly, I would have been happy with just the enchiladas. The beans and rice were a little bland, which I totally get, because not everyone likes spice.  I wish I had had room for dessert, but alas, there was no way that was going to happen. All in all, I loved my meal here and I can't wait to return. They also have a stage for live music, so that's something I will definitely have to check out!

Maybe it makes me a weirdo, but I was super-duper ridiculously excited when I discovered that we were finally getting a Reginelli's on the Westbank. It's my favorite local pizza place and the new location isn't far from my house: score!  I stopped in for lunch at around 2 on a Wednesday. First of all, this place is huge- perfect for groups and lots of space. I wasn't in the mood for pizza, so I decided to get the Downtowner sandwich which is turkey, salami, tomatoes, cheese and some other goodies on toasted garlic bread. The sandwich was fantastic and I really enjoyed it and it the perfect thing for lunch.  I'm also excited about this place because they have free delivery, so I will be taking advantage of that soon.

While I'm not as outraged as Charles H., I gotta be honest: the iced coffee here is sub par. I drink a lot of iced coffee around town and the brew here is two things I can't stand: super bitter with a tart under taste and so packed with caffeine that it made me feel jittery and weird.  I got the iced coffee with 2% milk, but I guess that wasn't enough to dilute the weird, bitter flavor of it. It just wasn't good. I got a large, took 2 sips and really wanted to throw the rest away. I forced myself to drink it, so as not to have totally wasted my money, and I was left a shaky, over-caffeinated mess by the time I finished the cup.  They are getting three stars because the woman in front of me ordered 4 or 5 cups of coffee and a ton of pastries and they were fast about it, so I didn't have to wait long to get my order in and get out of there. The atmosphere seems nice and would be a quiet place to do work or chat, but the coffee just wasn't for me.

I'm a longtime fan of La Madeline and, although I usually frequent the one on St. Charles, this is a good location as well.  I stopped in for my usual- a bowl of their delicious tomato basil soup which, paired with bread, is pretty much the perfect meal. It was as good as ever and I lucked out because there wasn't much of a crowd on the evening I was here.  My one complaint about this location is that the parking lot is awful. There is one way in and one way out, and if you miss your chance to turn in, you are pretty much screwed. In fact, all of the parking lots in this little area are bad, but I digress. Just have your wits about you, when you get here because if you miss your turn, you're done.

Jeez, I really wanted to like this place.  I went here with a friend, after we had hit St. Joe's across the street.  He got a pizza and I got the Aglio Olio (pasta dish).  Well, the pizza looked good, but I don't know why I was expecting my pasta to be something special...it wasn't.  It was linguine with some lemons in it and some garlic powder mixed in.  It was covered in a thin coating of olive oil.  In other words: it was nothing earth shattering.  It really didn't even have that much of a flavor and the only reason I ate so much of it was because I was starving.  Did I take the leftovers home?  Of course.  Why?  Because even mediocre leftovers are still worth eating for lunch!  I'm gonna blame some of this on myself.  I probably should have just ordered a pasta dish with a sauce or something on it (do they even have that kind of stuff here?).  I guess I would go back and just try the pizza or calzone, since the name of the place is "Slice" , so that would be considered their specialty.  If you are looking for genuine Italian, then this may not be the place for you.

I don't know, but Puccino's really thinks a lot of themselves.  I passed through, and I was just in the mood for an iced coffee. A medium iced coffee costs a bit over $3 and a large costs over $4. Uhh...what? I know that they peg it as "Italian" coffee, but it's not good enough to be charging these kind of prices. I didn't eat here, but they have a pretty extensive lunch menu with sandwiches and salads. I do like the atmosphere with the booths and little coffee things packed into every corner. There are too many coffee places in this area to waste your money here.

I went to Murphy's for the first time years ago.  I think I was on a date.  Considering it's a Westbank bar, it's really not a bad place.  They have a pretty diverse beer selection on tap, pool tables and dart boards.  They also have a really cool internet juke box, so you can play any kind of song that you like.  The bartenders are always friendly and the atmosphere is laid back.  My only complaint is that the smoke in here is out of this world, so it's not a place that I would frequent, because of that.

Some might say my first mistake was getting fish at a chicken joint.  Well, who asked?  So, I went and I was in the mood for catfish.  I got the catfish, and well...there was a good amount of it and the pieces were nice and thick.  The problem was...well...see, it's a chicken place.  They fry their chicken in the oil and then they fry their fish in the oil.  Then the fish tastes like chicken.  I guess if they called it "chicken fried fish" I would have given them three stars.  This is what I get for being adventurous.

Yeah. yeah.  I know.  Most people go here for breakfast.  Hey, I was one of those people too.  I always got the "quick two egg breakfast" whenever I happened to be here, no matter what time.  Getting anything else but pancakes or eggs at a place with "pancakes" in the title just seems...wrong.  Well, one day I was there for lunch  My boyfriend got his usual french toast, but I wanted something else.  I wanted to try actual lunch food.  So, I decided to try the pot roast melt, and oh, what the heck, I'll have some onion rings on the side.  Oh. My. Gah.  It was soooo good.  I haven't ordered anything else since I had this.  There is no going back for me.  I have even turned my boyfriend into a pot roast sandwich fan.  They are FANTASTIC!

Ah, newspaper, the dying medium.  My family has been a faithful subscriber to the Times Picayune for as long as I can remember.  Some may say that it's "bias", but really, what newspaper isn't?  Wherever you go, the newspaper is going to lean one way or the other and that's just the way it is.  I'll be honest.  Since I am a part of the "younger" generation, I do get most of my news online at nola.com (which is the same as the TP). because I find it more convenient to read throughout the day.  You get good info from this paper and I really think that it has a lot to offer.  My favorite part of the paper is probably the more local, bi weekly "break off"; Gretna Picayune, Marrero Picayune, etc.  It's full of local information about what is going on in the area and little local events.  Sure, this paper has flaws, but who doesn't save the first page when something significant happens in this town (Katrina, Super Bowl).

This is such a fabulous addition to this little area right off of Magazine St.!  I'll admit that I'm not huge in the crafts or sewing departments, but this store has a friendly staff that will show you around and help you with whatever you need. If you are the sewing type they do sell a lot of different fabrics for your to turn into something amazing.  I was most blown away by their embroidery. I got a beach bag embroidered with my name on it and it was lovely. It's the perfect thing to get me ready for the beach. They do embroidery on anything you like, so don't be shy about bringing something in for the staff to work on. They also offer sewing classes for kids, if you are looking to get them into a neat and useful hobby.

Well, I finally got to see what all the fuss what about when The Halal Guys opened today on the Westbank.  As you know, I am a big fan of Middle Eastern food. Give me all the shawarma! The Westbank already has two really good locally owned Halal places: Sahara Cafe and Cleopatra. While I usually avoid chains (and I have avoided the two other Halal Guys locations that have opened in NOLA), I decided to give this place a shot.  Like I said, it was opening day, but there was barely a crowd so I was in and out in 10 minutes. The staff is great and has everything organized and they move quickly- major bonus points. I got the combo platter (chicken and gyro), extra white sauce and a side of hummus. The large platter will run you $10 and it's A LOT of food and well worth the money. The taste was good, but not great. The platter had a lot of flavor and the hummus tasted homemade, so I was happy about that. I enjoyed it and it definitely satisfied my craving, but it wasn't the best Middle Eastern food I've ever had. However, I could say that about a lot of other locally owned places I've tried.  It's a really good lunch place and they have a few wraps I'm eager to try. I would always choose to eat local, first and foremost, but this spot is good in a pinch.

I see that this spot is listed as a "dive" bar, but with the atmosphere and an amazing beer list, I think this watering hole ranks a few notches above that. Yes, this bar is so much more than a dive bar. It's a treasure on North Rampart. Granted, this bar isn't located in the best area, but bring a buddy and you should be fine.  We stopped in here after a show at the Saenger. I had been wanting to try this place ever since some beer loving friends mentioned that Black Penny has a legit beer selection. I liked this bar as soon as I walked in- it was nice and dark with a seating area off to the side, if you didn't want to sit at the bar itself. We decided to sit at the bar and I was thrilled to see that their beer menu was out of control. So many craft bottles and cans- I was a happy camper.  I sampled a few beers and I enjoyed all of them. I love that they give you the can or bottle and then give you a nice glass that you can pour it into. Perfect!
