After sitting at the bar for a while, we decided to set up camp at one of the small table and chair areas that are on the side. This spot is a lot less hustle and bustle than the bar itself.  The overall atmosphere of the place is dark, cozy and a little mysterious. The bartenders were family and the patrons were all having a good time. I can't wait to return and see what else Black Penny has to offer.

This shop is a little weird. In fact, I think it might be one of the few year round Christmas shops in the country, so soak it in!  You walk in, and no matter what time of year it is outside, it is Christmas inside 24/7. Seriously. I could never work here. Maybe if I was a masochist. Side bar: can you imagine a world where Christmas never ends? Seriously. Like, people coming in year round asking about mundane things like ornaments and lights. I'm just saying it takes a special kind of person to tolerate that. I mean, it's only a matter of time before someone snaps because some customer asks about Santa Claus wrapping paper on January 2nd.  Anyway, whatever you need at any time of year for Christmas kind of stuff is here. I guess this is a really good place to shop if you want to avoid Christmas crowds and do your Christmas gift/decoration shopping in June. I suppose they must do good business, because this place has been around forever. It might have opened shortly after the very first Christmas. I don't know. Also, a neat place for people to visit if they are in the mood for something a little off the beaten path.

I used to go to this bar "back in the day" when it was called "Snooks".  I liked it then, and I like it even more now.  There are a few reasons to like this place.  First of all, it's at the end of Bourbon St. that is away from most of the drunken crowd.  Sure, you get some of it, because Tropical Isle is right across the street, but it's far enough away from the hip hop clubs to still be enjoyable.    Second of all, it's a hotel bar.  That means that you not only have access to a clean bathroom (on Bourbon St!), but the place is never going to get super, annoyingly packed and you're gonna be able to sit and have a conversation while enjoying a cocktail.  All in all, if I HAD to go Bourbon, I would probably try to stick to just going to this place, since it is nice for a Bourbon bar and the crowd isn't too rowdy.

The sculpture garden at the New Orleans Museum of Art is one of New Orleans' hidden treasures.  Located behind the museum, near city park, the garden is free to visit and the sculptures are ever changing and when you visit you almost feel as if you are in another world.  There is a body of water that goes through the garden and you can actually go on a gondola ride!  This is a great place to just come and relax and reflect and enjoy the scenery.  It's very quiet and peaceful and I think it would be fantastic to come here after a long day and just walk around or even on a date.

This is a good size Victoria's Secret with a really friendly staff.  Whenever I go here, I really can't walk from the entrance to the register without being asked if I need a bra fitting.  That's not a bad thing at all.  I don't need one, but they don't know that.  They have a nice selection of gorgeous lingerie, as well as perfumes, lotions, stockings and makeup.  There are obviously better places where you can buy higher quality lingerie, but if you are on the Westbank, don't hesitate to stop in.

I've been holding off on writing this review, because I don't exactly know how to put this place into words.  I guess we'll start with the word "exquisite" and go from there.  A friend of mine decided bring me here one night.  Actually, this was all my friend's idea, as I had honestly never heard of the place.  I know I know.  I should be ashamed.  The atmosphere has a very relaxed feel.  Although it is an "upscale" restaurant, it's not as formal as Commander's or Antoine's.  You could definitely go to this place for after work drinks or appetizers and not feel out of place.  They have an extensive cocktail menu and the wait staff is extremely helpful in choosing one that is right for you.  They have everything from whiskey mixers to cucumber martinis.  For a starter I decided to get the white truffle parmigiano toast with wild mushrooms.  It was amazing.  The toast was very lightly toasted and the mushrooms were in a veal glaze that was delicious.  For my entree I had the black drum which was served with cous cous.  It was cooked to perfection and it melted in my mouth.  It was light enough so that I didn't feel bad about enjoying every bite.   My dessert, which was amazing, consisted of a fresh baked brownie topped with a delicious vanilla ice cream.  It was more than just some run of the mill "brownie bottom pie", it was decadent and delicious.  I would love to go back to Lilette and I hope I have the opportunity to do so  sooner rather than later.

Precision Movers is fantastic! I needed movers and I had zero experience with this type of thing, so naturally I was a bit nervous. I didn't know the process and I was worried about my antiques getting scratched.  Well, first of all, Precision Movers showed up a bit early (after calling to confirm that we were ready for them) and quickly got to work. Everything was wrapped up in padding so that nothing would be damaged and everything was moved, loaded and unloaded with care.  The two men that came were extremely nice and friendly and more than capable of handling the job in front of them. Everything that I needed moved was moved in about 2 and a half hours (they were scheduled for three hours).  I was beyond pleased and happy with the entire experience and I would DEFINITELY call on Precision Movers again. Also, I called them about a week before I needed them and they had no problem scheduling me in.

I was in the area a few weeks ago and Juan's has always been a favorite, so I decided to stop in for lunch. I had never been to this newer location and I have to say, I love the decor. As charming as the other Magazine St. location is, it has always felt a bit grimy. This spot has been completely redone and it's gorgeous.  I was in a burrito mood, so I got the al pastor "wet". This is basically a pork burrito with all the fixins. Now, I know that it's been a while since I've eaten at Juan's, but I don't remember their burritos being this small. Whenever I have gotten this burrito at the other Juan's I remember it being so big that it took up the whole plate. Also, it was packed with everything it was supposed to be packed with, but it seemed like most of the meat was in the middle just leaving rice in the ends of the burrito- it wasn't evenly distributed. As good as it was, I'm just not sure it was worth $11 after tax and before tip.  The staff was super friendly and nice and the waiter checked in on me constantly, so that was a plus. I like Juan's, so I'll be back. This might have just been an "off" afternoon.

Popeyes doin' WORK!  If you read my last review, then you will understand why I hadn't returned to this Popeyes until tonight. I didn't feel like driving very far for dinner, so I thought I'd give this Popeyes another chance. After all, I was only ordering a couple of sides, so if they screw it up it's not a huge loss.  I popped in and I decided to just go inside rather than wait in the long drive through line. First of all, I was greeted immediately upon walking in. Then I gave my order- one large red beans and rice and one large mac and cheese. Service was fast and efficient and there was no wait. Here's the big news: they filled the sides all the way to the TOP, y'all! They topped them off! I'm talking a full container! Look, this is HUGE. Popeyes is always trying to hold back on the goods, but not tonight. TOPPED. OFF.   Maybe it was a fluke, but I'm kicking them up two stars for fast friendly service and delivering on the sides.

I've been to both this location and the uptown location.  Since the uptown one has nearly 100 reviews, I'll review this one.  Out of the two Juan's locations, this one is my definite favorite.  I have never had a to wait for a table here and the service is always fast and friendly.  I've found that at the other one, unless you sit at the bar you are in for a long wait for a table and then your food.  That's fine, if you aren't in a rush, but if you have places to be, then that doesn't work.  I go to the one in mid city and the staff is always friendly.  I get usually get the super burrito and end up taking half of it home.  I don't have to tell you how good the margaritas are.  They are excellent.  A good priced place with good food.  You can't go wrong.

I don't make it out to Lager's often, but when I find myself in Metairie, and the group I'm with wants something other than the same old, I usually suggest this place.  Not only does Lager's have a fantastic beer selection (in that sense, it is basically Metairie's answer to The Bulldog.  They even have some beer on tap that The Bulldog doesn't offer) but they have really good food.  I have gone here for dinner more than once and I would definitely call it a step up from typical "bar" food.  I like the "old pub" feel of the place.  They have a big screen for games days, but the place is small.  If you are planning on checking out your favorite team here, you might want to arrive early.

Not sure why so many people dislike this spot. I've been here a few times and the place is good for my purpose, which is- walk in, order coffee and leave. The store is pretty big with lots of seating, including booths which I think is cool if you are looking for a place to do a group project and you need space. The coffee has always been good for me and is on the same level as other PJ's. Parking can be a bit tricky on busier days.

Tivoli & Lee was a wonderful experience from beginning to end!  First of all, we pulled a HUGE no-no in the restaurant game by coming through the doors when the place was about to close. There was no one else in there at 9:45 and they were cleaning up. Some friends of mine are traveling cross country and were late in getting in and were staying at Hotel Modern for the night. The waitress was SO nice about seating us, when she could have been telling us to get the hell out. For this, we were greatly thankful.  I decided on the Des Allemands Catfish which was fried catfish that came topped with cabbage and over stone ground grits. The pieces of catfish were large and lightly battered and fried perfectly. The grits were creamy and offered a nice compliment to the fish. The entire dish was amazing. After our meal, we were sitting in the Bellocq courtyard and we got to meet Warren, the man who cooked our dinner. He was super nice and friendly and we were sure to tell him how great his food was.  I would love to return to Tivoli & Lee and I promise it will be at a decent hour and not when the poor waitress is ready to close up shop!

Mid City seems to be ever expanding and Mr. Ed's is the newest addition to the neighborhood.   I stopped in with a friend for lunch and we were both surprised that the place was pretty empty at noon. Everything looked really good and we decided to start with a plate of the fried calamari. Looking over the lunch specials, the only thing I could focus on was the fried chicken. I had heard amazing things about the chicken here and while I'm aware that this is a "fish house", three pieces for white meat chicken for $12 was too good to pass up.  The calamari was crispy and perfect. It was lightly battered and had a lot of flavor and came with a side of marinara sauce for dipping. When the chicken came out, I was blown away at the serving size- two huge breasts, a wing and potato salad was an incredible amount of food for lunch. I started munching on the first breast and I loved how crispy it was. The batter on this chicken is nice and thick (that's how I like it) and had some nice spice to it. One complaint- I did find the chicken a little bit greasy and really salty. I wasn't too upset, because I was able to get through one breast and I took the other two pieces home,  The potato salad was perfection and it might be some of the best potato salad I have eaten at a restaurant.  I enjoyed my food here, the service was pretty good and the atmosphere is casual. There are also big screen tvs in the bar area, if you want to get a beer and watch a game.

Maple Street Book Shop is a New Orleans institution and I am SO embarrassed that I am only just now stopping in here.  For such a small shop, Maple Street Books has quite the selection of everything from new and used to fiction, non fiction and local selections. As I walked up the quaint porch there was a rack of used books with a decent selection that I flipped through. After I made my way inside, I found myself in the "New Orleans" section that was full of books about the city we love. I picked up a copy of "Cast of Characters", a book about the different personalities that make New Orleans so unique.  There aren't enough book shops like this anymore and it feels like the "big names" have taken over, so it was nice to patronize this locally owned shop for a change. If I lived in the area, I would make it a point to come here more regularly.

The Standard is one of those new places that evokes old New Orleans as soon as you walk in the door. There's just something about this place that charms you.  I had brunch here on a Sunday and the crowd was light. The have basic NOLA brunch food on the menu such as french toast, eggs benedict and potato pancakes. I got the shrimp and grits, because whenever I see it on the menu I have to try it. Their version is really good. First of all, they give you A LOT of it and it is really rich- if you are able to finish an entire bowl in one sitting, I would be pretty impressed. The shrimp is tail-off and the grits are nice and creamy and topped with a cheese sauce. I wouldn't say there are the best in town, but they are up there. Note: menus floating around don't include the shrimp and grits on the brunch menu, but they ARE on the menu.  I also enjoyed a bloody Mary which was decent, but didn't really blow me away. I would get one again, if I were here, but I wouldn't make this a destination for JUST a bloody. I really liked the food and service and I would come back for brunch.

We came here Saturday night for a special event and before hand we decided to get dinner here.  I had been here before when it was another establishment. The place is very small, so I can imagine that if you don't get here pretty early for dinner, you are going to be looking at a wait. For our appetizer, we decided on the flash fried oysters. They were really good. I liked that the meat on the inside was a little under cooked, which left the oysters juicy and tasty.  For my entree' I decided on the fettucine with shrimp. Now honestly, I don't know if I am super picky or it was an off night, but my dish had absolutely no taste to me. I was so disappointed because our waitress had gone on and on about how fresh the seafood is and how it is fresh caught every other week. Well, the shrimp was good, but the fettucine was the definition of "bland". Maybe they do that so that tourists won't become overwhelmed with a lot of spices, but I think that you are going to be serving food in New Orleans, you should make it "New Orleans" style (for lack of a better term) and give tourists and locals alike the full experience.  The staff couldn't have been nicer and I do feel bad about the three stars. I will say that Evangeline has a lovely patio complete with fire pit for cold nights. I would definitely go back and get a drink and sit on the patio and enjoy the night, whenever I am in the area.

Not my first choice for gas, but my gas light was on and I found myself here. This isn't a bad neighborhood station, but it's a little scary if you're here by yourself (especially if you're a woman pumping gas alone). Lots of folks will want to engage in small talk and the parking lot gets packed with lurkers. Pumps are slow to...well...pump, so you're going to be stuck standing there forever as people lurk around and look you over wondering who you are and if you live "around here".  Keep your head on a swivel, and you'll be fine.

THIS is what I'm talking about!  The snowballs here are the kind that made the snowball famous- the ice is super fine like velvet and each bite melts in your mouth. I decided to get a rainbow snowball, which is a mix of 4 flavors I couldn't name, but it was delicious. They also have a nice selection of shakes, malts, funnel cakes and other sweet treats. For some reason they don't take cards, so be sure to have some cash on hand.
It's a Sonic. What can you say? I pulled in, ordered a cherry limeade and got a cherry limeade. Service was fast and it was happy hour so I got a large for a little over a dollar. Win.

Im giving the Dungeon four stars on music alone.  They have really "heavy" stuff, that you don't hear in a typical bar.  Slated as an "underground" bar, the Dungeon has been around forever.  In the light of day, the gargoyles on the wall and the "spooky" decorations would look cheesy, but for some reason, it works here.    I went recently and was kind of disappointed that the long haired metal heads, that usually work the place, are gone.  In their place now is typical bouncer looking guys, who look out of place, except for their black tshirts.  The place is now, for all intents and purposes, a tourist trap, as is every other bar in the quarter.  In other words, if you are going to go expecting to see leather clad women hanging from the ceilings and "head bangers" rocking out to the latest NIN release, then prepare to be disappointed. If you are in the mood to listen to some good metal, then you will have a good time.

I hope your have your fancy pants ready, because you will definitely want to have them on when you drop into Mélange.  Not that the place is overly fancy or snooty, but it feels like one of those bars where it is most appropriate to dress up.   A friend and I dropped in here one night to see what this place was all about and what we found was a delightful speakeasy.  The atmosphere is wonderful and the bartender will be happy to make you a fancy cocktail for you to sip as you watch the foot traffic on Frenchmen go by.

I stopped in here for lunch today, one of the few local pho places I had never visited.  I walked in and I decided to take a seat at the bar, even though it was mid-afternoon and the lunch crowd had passed. The nice man behind the counter took my order. I was pretty hungry, so I decided on an order of grilled pork spring rolls and small bowl of brisket pho.  The spring rolls came pretty quickly and were tasty. As good as they were, I'm not sure they were worth $5.50, but when I'm Uptown (ish) I don't mind paying Uptown prices.   The pho came out and it was a decent sized bowl. I gotta be honest- I compare every pho place to Pho Bang- my go to. I know that isn't fair, but it's the standard by which all other pho places are measured, in my book. For the price ($7.50) I was pretty underwhelmed. There were only a few pieces of meat and that was a disappointment. Also, the broth lacked flavor to me. It was okay, but it didn't knock my socks off. And why so stingy with the bean sprouts? I was given barely even a fistful.   All in total, my lunch was $16 (I also got an iced tea which was huge) and while it wasn't the best Vietnamese I have ever had, it did the job and satisfied my pho craving. I wouldn't rush back to Pho Bistreaux, but I wouldn't mind stopping in again if I found myself in the area.

I like sushi.  You know this.  I even have a lengthy sushi list.  Can I just hit the high points and not fancy pants this review up?  Great.  Appetizer: Edamame with black salt.   verdict: Awesome.  Pretty hard to screw up and the black salt added an exotic kick.  Rolls: tuna, Black and Gold (specialty), Gulf Coast (specialty) verdict: the tuna roll was a typical tuna roll.  The Black and Gold and Gulf Coast rolls were all fancy pants and topped with caviar of some sort.  Now, let me ask a question;  When you order a special roll, you kinda expect them to be BIG, right?  Well, these were normal size rolls, but instead of 6 pieces, you got 8 pieces... for 7 bucks more.  That's $3.50 per extra piece, for those of you playing at home.  Were they good??  Yeah, but not $12 a roll good!  I also had green tea which was pretty good and the whole place had a "sake cafe" feel.  Look, I'm sorry.  I like places that are a little less "trendy".  That's just me.  I prefer a "Hana" any day of the week: good food, no whistles.  I have yet to find a place that can compete.  Call me a snob.

This is a great dog park on the corner of Barracks and Dauphine St. in the French Quarter.  It's really big and takes up about half of a city block.    There is a large grass field for dogs to play in and get to know each other.  There are is also a cement spot where baby pools are filled with water, if your dog wants to take a dip on hot days.  There is also a fountain for water.  We brought a boxer here, and the other dog owners were really nice, even though he is a big dog that always wants to play.  The people seemed friendly, and there were nice shady spots to sit and escape from the heat as the dog wore himself out making new friends.

Heyyyy Heyyyyyy.  Ok, so first of all: I am starting to think that all of these New Orleans coffee shops get their coffee from the same place and the joke is on all of us for paying different prices.  I stopped in to grab an iced coffee. Yeah, I know that I'm boring and predictable. Whatever, I like what I like. The coffee was good and pretty cheap blah blah blah.  I really like the atmosphere of this place. It's right next door to Ms. Mae's which gives the places a bit of a "gritty" feel. It's small, but cozy with people doing work at the tables within. The door was open and I liked the welcome feel.  They have a lot of sandwiches and baked goods here, so it's a great place to stop in for a snack. It actually feels a lot like Mojo with the food and setup. I like it. I'll be back.

I've been to this place a few times.  I like it, for the most part.  I usually go with friends to play a few games or dance to the DJ.  However, lately this place has been slipping a bit.  The games are still fun and it's still a good place to go with friends, but more and more people are discovering the place and more and more people are smoking here.  It seems that the smoke eaters can't keep up with the crowd.  This past weekend, some friends and I were hanging out and as the night progressed the smoke got thicker and thicker until there was a haze hanging over the entire place.  This place is huge and I was standing on one side and I couldn't see all the way to the other side due to all of the smoke. I couldn't breathe very well and I coughed for a day and a half after.  I can only imagine if someone with asthma hung out here for too long.   I understand that making this place smoke free probably isn't a real option, but I think it would be great if they could install some more (or stronger) smoke eaters.  The music was still fun and I still had a good time.  I'll be back, but I won't stay too late due to all of the smoke.

This isn't a bad little bar. I like the "Australian" kind of theme. There is usually soccer or some international sport playing on one of the tvs. It isn't the biggest place in the world, but a lot of days it sure beats whatever is going on across the street at Lucy's, which tends to get overly packed.  I probably wouldn't go out of my way to hang out here, but it's a cool spot if I find myself in the area.

Gautreau's might be one of the nicest and coziest restaurants in the city. Yelp has not been letting me down lately, when it comes to restaurants and I have been having some pretty fantastic luck and discovering a lot of cool places.  We made reservations for Gautreau's early on a Wednesday evening. We decided to have an early dinner; it was even still light out when we arrived. We were seated immediately, and even though it was early, there was a good little crowd.  Fresh bread was brought to the table and everything on the menu sounded perfect. We started with a poached egg and asparagus appetizer that was served over pasta. When you broke the egg, the yolk ran all over the pasta making for a delicious experience.  For my entree, I decided to get the special of the day which was a lightly fried flounder served on a bed of vegetables. The fish itself was nice and thin and it was fried just enough to leave it crispy. It was a pretty fantastic dish. My dining companion got the veggie plate which came with an assortment of beets, turnips and carrots. I was able to sample a taste and that dish was tasty as well!  I really loved the atmosphere here. The tables are small, creating a nice intimate setting that would be perfect for a date night.

Lakeview is a quaint little New Orleans suburb. I think it's really nice because it is basically right on the lake, there are a good number of decent restaurants and it's a good place to raise the kids. It's the perfect neighborhood for people who want to live in New Orleans, but not really.  Before Katrina, a good amount of the people who lived in Lakeview were older and mainly retired. Since the rebuilding, more and more younger people and their families have moved in and have contributed to the revitalization of the area.   Lakeview is a great area to live in for the days that you just want to go out to the lakefront and hang out and relax. If you are looking for a quiet neighborhood to live, this is the place. Just pack up the family, move into a lakefront mansion and pray that the levee doesn't snap (again).

This is a friendly neighborhood place that has probably became a lot more friendly since it was featured on a T.V. show that I won't name.  On the night I came there was no band (I know!) and there were just some neighborhood folks sitting around and have a good time. The bartender had a lot of personality, and even though it was late, he didn't "shoo" us out of the bar when we stopped in. I liked the atmosphere and I do want to come back when they actually have a band playing.

I feel weird writing a review of this place, because all we had here are appetizers, but here we are.  Me and a friend went here just because we were in the mood for some appetizers and we had both heard a lot of good things about this place.  We sat in the bar area and decided to order the pork tacos.  They were small, but really good.  The atmosphere of this place is nice.  It's a Susan Spicer restaurant, so you know it's going to be good quality dining.  I didn't get a look at the actual menu, but I would love to go back and check this place out for an actual dinner.  Just an amusing note.  You can tell that this is one of those places that is "see and be seen".  It's located in Lakeview and between all of the tanned, blonde women, I felt like I was watching a live version of "The Real Housewives of New Orleans".  I literally overheard a woman talking about how her kids are away at camp for the summer.  I just thought that was a neat little observation.  :)

Oh, Fridays, why did you mess with a good thing, when you changed your Caesar salad dressing?  I LOVED the old dressing.  What the heck is this new Caesar vinaigrette dressing you have now??  It's no where near as good as the old creamy Caesar dressing was.  I FINALLY found a Caesar dressing that I LOVED and you change it!  I'm so let down.  I understand that you might want to offer a healthier option, when it comes to dressing, but could you offer both the vinaigrette and the creamy one?  When all I'm having for lunch is a salad and soup, I'm really not counting calories.  4 stars, still, because I do like the food and it is really super cheap.

This is a fantastic little bar to hang out in, if you aren't really in the mood for the hustle and bustle of the Sazerac Bar. The vibe here is extremely laid back and on the nights I have been, there has been a jazz band playing. Food is served here and they have an assortment of specialty cocktails. I enjoy the Bayou Swizzle, which is a yummy rum drink with juice.  For a really romantic feel: sit in one of the corner booths. It's the perfect spot to sit and enjoy the music and atmosphere with a date.

I love The Grocery!  I just wish they were open later.  I guess with food this good, you can close when you darn well please.  I have a friend who lives within walking distance of The Grocery, and when we are hanging at his house for the Uptown parades, The Grocery is a must.  They have the best pressed sandwiches ever and my favorite is the pressed ham.  There is always a line during parade season, so be patient.  I have never been inside, I have always just ordered at the window and taken out.  I will have to try eating there the next time I go.

When I heard a new, "fancier" Delachaise was opening on Maple, I was eager to try it.  I stopped in during happy hour literally as the place was opening one Tuesday. We sat at the bar, drank wine and took in the atmosphere on a lovely summer afternoon. The setup here is completely different from the *other* Delachaise- the emphasis here is very much on good food, cocktails and wine. They have a full menu and seating inside and outside for those who come for dinner.  On this day, we decided to get some $5 wine and the goose fat fries, just because I think you have to get these fries when you are at any Delachaise- it's the rule. Of course, they were as perfect as they always are and although I didn't try any other food, I was happy that the fries are as good as this location as the other one.  I almost wish I had stayed longer because I would love to do a full dinner here and try some of the cocktails. I think this is a great addition to the area and it's nice to have a bar on this street that isn't college oriented. I'll be back, probably to grab some drinks during happy hour again.

A little bit of Italy in our own backyard!   I didn't even know this place existed until a few years ago when a photographer suggested that we do a photo shoot here. I was blown away that something so cool was right in the middle of our city.  I love the different fountains and water scapes and at night it is just gorgeous when it is all lit up.  Taking pictures here is always fun, because someone will inevitably ask where the photo was taken and express shock when you tell them that it is right here in New Orleans.

The iced coffee proved to be a life saver during a particularly hot walk through the Quarter. The girl who took my order was nice and helpful and there wasn't a long line. I like that this location has two registers in order to keep up with any potential crowd, as I can imagine that in the morning this is extremely necessary. The coffee was tasty, cheap ($3 for a 24 oz) and definitely hit the spot.  They have an assortment of pastries and a nice area for seating. Everything is clean is well kempt, even after a busy French Quarter morning. The bathroom is also really clean and nicely taken care of.

The average rating of this place is three stars, and I would call that accurate.  This restaurant is located a few doors down from the House of Blues on Decatur.  Like a lot of French Quarter places, they depend mainly on foot traffic as their customer base, so they don't take reservations.  The place itself is somewhat dimly lit with a decor that has the feel as if it's straight out of the 70's.  That's not necessarily a bad thing, just an observation.  Our wait was about 10 minutes, which wasn't bad at all, considering it was the dinner rush and the place was pretty packed.  For my starter, I ordered the Caesar salad and my entree was the redfish Lafitte, which was grilled and topped with crab.  It came with a side of mashed potatoes, which was my choice "side".  All in all, it was okay.  The Caesar salad was good and the fish wasn't too bad.  Really, it was nothing special, but it was good for what it was.  Honestly, if I was a tourist just coming in off the street and was looking for some "New Orleans" food, then I would definitely give the place 5 stars.  It's only because I live down here and I know what else is out there that it's getting the three stars.  Now, I know what you are going to say.  "Uh...you went to a steak and lobster place and didn't get steak nor lobster.  Isn't your rating a little unfair?"  To that I say, if it's on the menu, then it better be good.  Right?  Right.    I will say this... my friend did get a New York strip steak which was ordered "medium well" and it was cooked to perfection.  So, if you want a really good steak, then this would be a place worth checking out.  If I go back, I will get the steak, just to see if that is, indeed, their "speciality".

NOMA is such a gorgeous museum.  This used to be one of my favorite places to go as a child.    First of all, NOMA is huge and has a lot of different works of art.  They always have "touring" exhibits.  I remember seeing a lot of different ones here, but I think my favorite was the Monet exhibit when I was about 12.  One of my favorite parts of NOMA is the sculpture garden, which is located just behind the museum itself.  It's a surreal garden with different sculptures that are always changing and it is just overall nice and relaxing.  When the weather is nice, NOMA also puts on plays in the sculpture garden and in the museum itself, so be sure to keep an eye out for that.

A fork in the road is to sandwiches what taceaux loceaux is to Mexican food: fast, convenient, good, and served fresh out of a truck.  I had been eager to try this place for a while.  Having been a huge fan of that other truck food place: taceaux loceaux, I couldn't wait to try "fork".  I decided to get their ham and cheese melt, which comes fully dressed and with or without tomatoes, mustard and mayo.  I loved it.  It was a cheesy sandwich, which was then pressed, so that the cheese would melt, and it would be nice and warm.  It almost reminded me of a Cuban sandwich.  It came with a small bag of chips, and for $6 (for 6 inches of sandiwich, or $8 for 8 inches), it's the perfect lunch or dinner.  The next one I'm going to try is going to be the pulled pork sandwich, which is not listed on their menu, but was good enough to get "fork" featured on the local news.  They serve lunch every day from 11am-2pm at Tulane University Square on the river, and some days they even serve breakfast.  They set up shop all over town, including outside of Dos Jefes, so be sure to follow them on www.twitter.com/forkdat to find out where they will be next.  I can't wait to go back and try more.  Get more info on their website at: http://www.aforkintheroadtruck.com/

My dad and I stopped in here for lunch during Coolinary.  First of all, I really like the feel of the place- it still maintains the warehouse vibe with tables, a bar and a kitchen added. We were greeted and seated right away and the place was pretty empty on a Friday around 1. Looking over the menu, it becomes clear very quickly that Toups South is completely different than Toups Meatery- the offerings are lighter and lean more towards sandwiches and small plates.  I already knew what I wanted, so I got the fried chicken sandwich as my Coolinary entree and the poppy cake for my dessert. The sandwich was OUTSTANDING. A huge piece of chicken, fried to perfection, came out on a bun and I was happy. The chicken was really juicy and it was battered and fried perfectly. My dad got a tuna melt sandwich but he wasn't really a fan of it. He gave me his leftovers to take home, I tried it later and loved it, so I guess it all just depends on what your tastes are. The poppy cake was delicious, as well. It was nice and light and topped with a nice creme. It was a perfect end to the meal.  Toups South seems like a good lunch place, but I would probably venture somewhere else for dinner and I wish the prices were a little more affordable for folks in the neighborhood.

Here's another one of those "starter" parades that kind of get you ready for the bigger parades.  It's nice, but short and really not all that memorable.  I had a good time watching it, but I probably wouldn't go out of my way to see it, as I might for some other Krewes.

I know for a FACT I have reviewed Still Perkin' before, because one of their employees emailed me about my experience the last time I was here. I guess my last review is hanging out somewhere with the Loch Ness monster and Bigfoot.  Anyway, Still Perkin' is a cute little Garden District shop with a friendly staff and a nice atmosphere. Walking in, it almost doesn't feel like you are in an actual coffee shop. The way the tables and chairs are setup, it almost feels a bit like a library. This isn't a bad thing at all as I found the shop fairly quiet, considering I stopped in on a busy morning. If I had had time to stay, I probably would have and I can see how this would be a nice spot to do some work or study.  I ordered an iced coffee (which I am still sipping as I type this) and it's not too bad. I probably wouldn't go out of my way to come here, but for what it is it's fairly good. I wish that the coffee had a bit more kick to it, as it tastes like all the other iced coffee that I seem to get at every other coffee place.

I just happened to stumble upon this new pho place nestled in a strip mall in Harvey. I was hungry and it was pouring rain, so I thought a bowl of pho would be perfect.  I want to start by saying that the place itself is nice and the staff is super friendly. My waiter couldn't have been nicer. I wasn't starving, so I just decided to keep it simple with a bowl of Pho Tai. When the bowl came, I noticed it wasn't really big (you can get a way bigger bowl elsewhere in the area for the same price), but that wasn't a huge deal. My issue was the broth- it had no flavor. None. It just tasted like water and I even had to add sriracha to it to give it some spice. The meat was prepared correctly and tasted pretty good, but that broth had no substance to it. It was very strange. I know they just opened, so maybe they are still getting the hang of how long they have to soak the bones and add spices to make the broth tasty, I'm not sure.  I am giving three stars because the place is new, growing pains happen in new restaurants and I am definitely going to visit again in a few months once they have gotten all of the kinks worked out. I know that this is an easily fixable issue, so I'm sure they will tweak their process and the food will improve.

How does one go about reviewing a Home Depot? I mean, it's a huge hardware outlet. They sell everything from ceiling fans (have you ever just stood in that section on a hot summer day? Refreshing!) to all kinds of rope and everything in between. On the rare occasion that I have found myself here, I have been able to find whatever it is that I was looking for.

This review is for the bar area.   I would tell you how the service was here, but we were never served.  The people seemed nice.  The atmosphere was fancy-esque (although there was a game of some sort on the t.v.).  But we never got any food or drinks here.  We waited, but it took forever for the waiter/bartender to notice us.  Even when he did, we were left with zilch.  And there you have it.

This is an adorable bed and breakfast on St. Charles that will make you feel like you own the entire house.  The process here is easy: you book a room, you make an appointment for check in, you are given a code so that you have access to the house and you go about your business. We were in a downstairs room that opened up to the porch. I liked this setup because the room got a lot of light and you could come and go without having to deal with other visitors.  The room was gorgeous- it was nice and big with two chairs by the windows so that you could look out onto the avenue. There was a bureau for clothing, a hardwood floor and the bathroom was a good size. I like that the room had a classic feel with modern amenities. In the house itself, there is a large living room that you can lounge in and relax that is stocked with plenty of books. There are basic "munchies" in the kitchen such as cereal, fruit, coffee, candy and things along that line.  The house is within walking distance of a coffee shop and a few restaurants and, as others have mentioned, it is just a few steps away from the streetcar.

After 5 years I hate to update with a lower rating, but I have to do it. I have given this place TOO many chances (check my number of check ins).  I visit this store multiple times a year and I am a regular customer. Honestly, I spend more money here than I care to admit. Over the past year, whenever I have shopped here, there is only one person checking people out and the line is long and takes forever to get through. I could understand if other workers in the store were helping customers (some are), but many of the employees are just standing at the front greeting people. Shouldn't they be working all of the registers to get people through the check out as quickly as possible? It doesn't matter what time of day I'm here, I wait in line for at least 10 to 15 minutes. I have actually put items down and left because I saw the length of the checkout line. I don't blame the staff, because I am sure they are doing whatever their manager instructs them to do, but something has to give.  Also, their AC "lost juice" a few months ago and they have been using a big industrial fan to keep the place cool.  I will continue to shop here, because I am not going to drive to Metairie for my VS needs, but something really should be done about getting customers in and out faster.

The Green Bridge connects Chalmette to the rest of the world. Depending on how you feel about Chalmette, this could either be seen as a good or bad thing.  This bridge kind of feels like it leads off into nowhere and David mentioned that he doesn't feel like it's in the best condition. I don't think it's going to crash down or anything, but I wouldn't want to drive on it during a major storm or other weather event. As Chris mentioned, it doesn't have any lights, so I wouldn't want to drive on it at night.  This rusty old bridge to Chalmette is a perfect metaphor for being in Chalmette itself: it's not quite as good as what you'd find in New Orleans and you're going to have to deal with some things that make you uneasy so just hit the gas and get through it as quickly as possible.

I never even knew this bar existed until I ended up here with the promise of a BBQ pop up.  This is a nice little cocktail bar located in a soon to be up and coming part of Tulane. I think they are trying to be a fancy pants cocktail bar, but I got more of a lounge type of feel from the place. They were having happy hour when I was here and although I didn't partake, they were offering half off on draft beers until 7. The only reason I didn't take them up on the offer is because I'm not really a fan of the 4 beers they have on tap- no biggie. I enjoyed an Urban South beer in a can and I was happy camper.  They have a small corner where I think they have an occasional band, and on the evening I was here they were showing the pre-season Saints game- minus the sound. The bar area itself is pretty small and there is one big sofa and some chairs for people to lounge on, but I can see this place being "standing room only" on busier nights.  This wouldn't be my first spot to grab a drink, but it's a nice little joint if you are in the neighborhood.

Dang, Mike! You surprised me, dude!  I stopped in here with fellow yelpers Joel M., Steve I., Re H,, and Shannon S. for a bite to eat, after our first choice was serving up nothing but a closed kitchen. This spot is as no frills as it gets: it's a bar with a few tables and chairs, if you want to eat. Oh yes, we wanted to eat.  They serve up a nice selection of "pressed" sandwiches including a Cuban, a Muffaletta and roast beef. I had to go for the Cuban, just because I am always on the hunt for the perfect Cuban (does such a thing even exist in NOLA)? My Cuban came out and my first impression was that it looked really good, but looks can be deceiving. Once I dug into it, I was really shocked. It was great and was packed with pork, cheese and had the perfect amount of mustard. The flavor was outstanding and I couldn't believe that I was eating something like this in a bar- this is so much better than your average bar food! Sure enough, I devoured the entire thing and was left with zero regrets. Did I mention that the sandwich is only $10? Oh, yeah. The only thing that would have made this experience more perfect would have been if I had thought to get fries.  The bar itself has Laguinitas IPA on tap, which was enjoyable and video poker and plenty of TVs round out the experience. Once again, it's places like this that make me glad that smoking is now banned in NOLA bars. I noticed that other reviews, from a year or so ago, mention how smoky the place is. That's not a problem anymore and my experience here was fantastic. I will definitely return.

I barely know where to even begin in describing how excellent Rue 127 is. We stopped in here on a whim, because our first choice (Ralph's on the Park) was booked to capacity. We didn't have a reservation here (they recommend one) so we had the choice of sitting outside on the patio or at a table in the bar area. We chose the bar.  We started with delicious fried okra and bone marrow. The fried okra was lightly battered and fried and came with tomatillo sauce for dipping. The okra spears were delicious and a perfect start to the experience. The bone marrow was roasted veal marrow bones filled with caramelized onions and chipotle salsa verde. Decadent is an understatement. The marrow was amazing and when it mixed with the onions and salsa verde it created an unbelievable taste experience. I couldn't get over how rich and delicious this appetizer was.  For my entree I got the pan seared salmon which was herb crusted salmon over white and green bean succotash with a bacon broth. I liked that the fish had a nice crust of herbs on it. The meat below the crust was tender and cooked to perfection. I loved how it just flaked off when I touched it with my fork. It spilled into the bacon broth and absorbed that juice, adding even more flavor to the experience. It was a perfect combination of fish and vegetables with a little something extra.  Throughout the meal the wait staff was extremely attentive, and even though we were kind of off to the side, they checked on us constantly. The place itself is pretty small, so I definitely would make reservations in the future. I can also see how this would be a fantastic little stop for lunch. I will gladly return.

This store is AWESOME!  Have you ever gotten one of those gift catalogs in the mail full of little odds and ends and stuff you really don't need, but you really want?  Well, Funrock'n has that stuff and more.  When you first walk in, don't be overwhelmed by the huge selection of goods.  There is so much stuff to look over, it will take you a while to absorb everything.  They have a huge selection of "retro inspired" items, such as Bettie Page and Marilyn Monroe lunchboxes, magnets coffee mugs, playing cards and other assorted gifts.  They also have cute little gift like hand held noise machines, and at Christmas I was tempted to get the stocking that was in the shape of the "major award" from "A Christmas Story" (they also had the night lite!).  Another thing I love about this place is the assortment of quirky greeting cards and magnets with nifty little sayings on them.  This is definitely a fantastic place to check out, if you are looking for a gift for someone in your life who is maybe a little quirky, fun, and has a sense of humor.

This is just a review of the bar.  We stopped in here on my birthday night because everywhere else in the area was pretty packed (one of the downsides of having a birthday that falls in that weird purgatory between Thanksgiving and Christmas). This is a pretty nice hotel bar and it was pretty quiet for a Saturday night. In fact, it was so quiet that David and I were the only couple in the place.  The bartender was really nice and they have a few decent beers on tap, for a reasonable price, so I had no complaints. The seating is really comfortable there are lots of sofas and chairs for lounging if that's your thing. Honestly, if you are having a night out in the Quarter, and you want to go a bit off of the beaten path, this is definitely the place for you. It still has the "New Orleans vibe" without the hassle of loud and obnoxious crowds.   It's a nice place to unwind at the end of a night out and I'd visit again.

My dad and I stopped in here for Coolinary lunch. First of all, I was excited that parking was super easy at the Marriot, so that was awesome.  We were here during a busy Friday lunch hour, but we were seated immediately. Fresh bread was dropped off at the table, as I looked over the menu. I was here for Coolinary, but there was one thing that wasn't on the Coolinary menu that I knew I had to try- Crabmeat Cheesecake. More about that in a minute. Along with the cheesecake, from the Coolinary menu I got the Werlein salad and the Shrimp Tchefuncte.  Crabmeat Cheesecake- When I read the reviews of Palace Cafe and saw the pictures if this dish, I knew that I had to get it. This might be one of the best things I have ever eaten in this city, and that's saying something. Imagine a delicious, buttery cheesecake stuffed with crab and then topped with crab claws and the yummiest sauce you have ever tasted. It was like a crab cake with cheese instead of breading. It was outstanding! I want to go back and have some more. Pair this with a salad and it's pretty much an entire meal. If you eat at Palace Cafe, you must get the Crabmeat Cheesecake- if you don't, you're doing yourself a disservice. It's so good that I looked up the recipe online and I'm going to attempt to make my own!  Werlein salad- This was basically a "deconstructed" Caesar salad with a few leaves of lettuce topped with dressing and a bit of cheese. I liked it, but my dad was underwhelmed. It was a good palate cleanser after the cheesecake, though.  Shrimp Tchefuncte- Delicious! The website says it's Gulf shrimp, Creole meunière, roasted mushrooms, popcorn rice and green onions. This dish was really tasty and had a lot of flavor. My one tiny complaint was that the shrimp were tail-on, but they were easy enough to pop off. Once again, the sauce in this dish was out of this world and made me want to track down the recipe.  For Coolinary, the salad and the entree was $20, which was a great deal considering the Shrimp Tchefuncte is $19 on the regular menu. Wes and Juan took care of us and they were fantastic! They took our orders quickly, checked on us regularly and made sure our drinks were filled. Service was really top notch, even for lunch, and I was left impressed.  I am definitely going to be dining at Palace Cafe again because I have to get David to try that cheesecake! From beginning to end, my experience here was a delight.

I was in the neighborhood, so I stopped in for a brunch lunch on Memorial Day. This is a cute little cafe and I was happy to be seated immediately.  I believe the owners were the servers on the day I was here and there was a decent crowd in the place. I already knew exactly what I wanted as soon as I looked over the menu: give the shrimp and grits with a side of bacon! The server suggested a poached egg on top, so I went with it.  The dish was great! I think I read that the sauce on it is made in a Bloody Mary type style and it was great. Just a warning: if you aren't a fan of tomatoes, it might not be the dish for you. The shrimp were tail-off and perfect and the poached egg was a perfect, gooey addition. Yes, I crumbled some of the bacon into the mix, because I was in a party mood. I loved the whole thing and I would definitely order it again.  One bonus is they have $10 bottomless mimosas here every day that they're open! Whaaaaaaat! I'm going to have to come back for a proper brunch on a weekend and partake. The table across from mine was full of ladies enjoying their Memorial Day mimosas and I was envious that I was driving and had other places to go that day. haha  This is a cute neighborhood cafe and definitely worth a visit.

4 stars for Fridays?!  Yeah, I can't believe it either.  While running around on the Westbank today, it was decided that we should get a cheap lunch somewhere.  Then someone said it, "Hey, they just opened a Friday's in Harvey!  Let's go there."  Now, let me start by saying that I LOVED the Chevy's that used to be in this location, so when I heard a Friday's was coming in it's place, I was a little bummed.  But, I decided to keep an open mind, and try it out, anyway.  First of all, the place has been totally redone (Friday-ized), so everything is brand new and clean and nice.  The staff is friendly and really eager to please and make a good first impression.  There weren't a ton of people in the place, so it wasn't too loud and we could actually hear ourselves talk.  We sat in the bar area, and although we didn't drink, I did notice that they had a huge assortment of different  drinks from margaritas to fruity drinks to beer to fancy "signature" cocktails.  It was pretty impressive for a little chain place, when others usually only offer beer.  I decided to get the lunch special, which is a soup, a salad, breadsticks and a drink (all unlimited) for about $7.  I was super excited to see French Onion Soup on the menu!  I don't think I have had a decent bowl of the stuff since those old Steak and Ale days!  It was really good and cheesy and perfect.  I was really impressed.  I got a Caesar salad with it and coupled with the breadsticks, it was just enough for lunch.  So, although I am a total snob when it comes to chains, I have to say  that I would go back to Friday's.  They have a HUGE menu and their food is really reasonably priced, and I would love an excuse to see how good their margaritas are.  You got me, Friday's!  You got me!!  Please note: The above info is wrong.  There IS outdoor seating, as well as wifi. Wifi password: fridayswifi

This is a really cool spot that I had no idea even existed!  This is basically different spaces that you can rent for whatever your needs, whether it be dance or photography. The space that we were in was $30 for an hour, which is really perfect if you are giving a quick dance lesson or if you need space for a photo shoot. The studio we used had really big windows that let in a lot of light and make the area perfect for photography. It also had a huge mirror that was fun to play around with.  So many artists in this town are looking for open spaces in which to work, and I think that Nola Spaces is perfect for just that. The staff is friendly and accommodating and will put you in the space that best fits your needs.

There was a time when Bourbon St. was a host to glittery Burlesque shows and jazz bands and culture.  Those days are long gone.    Now Bourbon St. is nothing more than tacky souvenir shops, strip clubs and cheap drink bars.  It's basically where any kind of New Orleans culture goes to die and end up slapped on a tshirt.  It gets way too packed with people who are just there for cheap beer specials and terrible cover bands.  I guess this is a "must" for any New Orleans first timer, but go during the day and only go once.  There is really nothing redeeming about the place.  Oh, and whenever you see moisture on the street, ask yourself, "Did it rain today?".

Decided on an oyster po boy for dinner on Ash Wednesday. It was AMAZING!   The thing I liked most about it (aside from the juicy oysters) was the bread. It was nice and soft. Now don't get me wrong, I like crunchy and crumby French bread on a po boy as much as the next person, but every once in a while you want to taste more of the goodies in the sandwich than the bread. I feel that some places have a weird bread:sandwich filling ratio and a lot of times the bread over powers the whole thing. That didn't happen here.  I also got some fries on the side, but they were just okay. The place is pretty well priced. I don't know what Steven S. was talking about because the foot long stuffed crab is only $8.49, but I digress. Along with the usual seafood po boys, they also have roast beef, sausage and more. I definitely have to go back and try their alligator sausage po boy. They also have different platters that come with fries.  I'm always happy to find a good place for a seafood po boy on the Westbank.

Woo hoo! I'm always happy when a new Vietnamese place opens up in my area because I love having different options for spring rolls, egg rolls and pho.  This spot is brand spanking new, located in the same shopping center where I used to hang out at Blockbuster back in the 90's. For starters, the place is HUGE. You can tell that it's not only a restaurant, but it plans on being an event space as well. There's a small stage in the corner that looks to be hooked up to a serious sound system, so I think it'll be a cool party spot.  Onto the food- it was a rainy and cold Thursday when I stopped in with a craving for egg rolls and pho. The menu here is extensive and I was so excited to see that they have banh mi! It's always nice to have a banh mi place nearby. I started with the pork and shrimp egg rolls, which were great. I love when the outside is nice and thin and crispy and the inside is nice and tender. These were exactly what I was craving.  As far as pho goes- Le Delat has a massive selection of all types including beef, chicken and vegetarian. I got P25 which was the eye of round steak and fatty brisket. I got the "large" size and I am very happy to report that their large size is actually large! The broth was flavorful and it was packed with a generous amount of meat. It definitely satisfied my pho craving and for $9, the size just can't be beat.  The staff was really friendly and checked on me multiple times throughout the meal and even kept me updated on the status of my food. I was also impressed that they had some nice vegetarian selections for those of us who don't eat meat, but still want to enjoy some good Vietnamese food. I can tell that these folks care a great deal about their business, their food and their customers and I'm excited to go back for more pho and a banh mi.

Namese was a really good experience. I arrived here at about 7:30, on a weekday, to meet a friend for dinner. I was lucky enough to quickly find a spot in the small lot, but be warned: the parking is limited here, but you can park in the lot next door. I walked in and was told there would be a bit of a wait. Since it was a nice night, I decided to wait outside in the front (there is seating and tables, if you want to eat outside on nice days) until my friend arrived.  After a few minutes, the gentleman seating us apologized for the wait and we were then seated. Looking over the menu, everything looked amazing. To start we decided on the shrimp and pork spring rolls. They were fresh and amazing.  For my entree, I decided to mix it up a bit, because I always seem to get Pho. I decided on the combination which was half banh mi and half brisket Pho. See, I told you I was mixing it up. When it came, I was amazed. For $10, I got a really nice sized banh mi and a bowl of Pho. It was so much food that I couldn't even finish it and sadly, a quarter of my delicious banh mi went uneaten. It was all so good and the staff was super friendly and nice.  After the meal, the man who seated me came over and asked how everything was. I really like when people do that, because it shows a really interest in the customer's experience. I will absolutely be back.

I stopped in here for lunch since I was in the area and I was eager to see the new place since the expansion. It was pretty packed at lunch, so me and a coworker had no choice but to order at the counter and sit/eat outside.  I got the original cheesesteak half with a side of fries. The sandwich itself was great- the meat was tender and the fries were really good too. The meat on my sandwich had really good flavor, the cheese went nicely with it and the "half" was the perfect portion for lunch. It was a fairly hot day so I was wishing that there was a bit of shade outside- an awning, an umbrella on the table, something. Other than the heat, my experience here was good.  Service is pretty fast, so I would probably come back again for lunch.

How do you review a bridge?  How do you rate a bridge?  5 stars because it's always done a good job of not collapsing whilst I was driving on it!  It is pretty cool to drive over, because it IS so long.  You get a nice view of the lake and I can imagine that driving over it at night can be a bit of an adventure.

It's always strange reviewing something like a hospital. Quite often, hospitals are personal places that people choose because their doctor works there or simply because it's close to home. In the last few months, I had two family members admitted here for two different reasons.  I'm not going to go into vivid detail about our experience with West Jeff. What I will say is that my loved ones ended up here because we were told that this is where they would receive the best treatment, and I didn't always find this to be the case. We've had experience with both West Jeff and Ochsner, and all the way around we preferred Ochsner. Things just seems to be run better over there.  I will say this- when a 95 year old woman is discharged at 6 pm, it is inexcusable for an ambulance to not become available until 9 pm and leave her waiting that entire time. That MIGHT be fine for a 30 year old who is admitted for a broken leg, but when a woman has been admitted for dehydration and just being 95, there is really no excuse. Elderly people depend on a schedule in order to keep them functioning. Meals and sleep must happen at a certain time, and when you feel like the hospital doesn't respect that, it's a little off putting.

This is a really cool little shop on Oak.  I had been wanting to check this place out for a while, after hearing raves about it and earlier this week, I finally had the chance.  I would classify the clothing here as "casual chic".  There were a lot of nice dresses, tank tops and thin tops for summer, which is perfect for the New Orleans climate.  The clothes here we colorful, modern and really fun. I was also impressed by the prices, as everything was really affordable without looking cheap.

Stopped in here while out with friends and we decided we needed a bite to eat. I probably never would have even know about this place if my friends hadn't been regulars here.  I got a big slice of pizza with chicken on it. It was really good, especially considering this is basically just one of those places and you order pizza and it's already made. The chicken had a lot of flavor and the slices are really big.   They are open late and this place is definitely a better choice than a lot of the other "fast food" options in the area.

This is basically the same idea as Pure Yogurt Culture, except it's located on the Westbank.  It has way more flavors than Pure (like red velvet cake and strawberry lemonade) and it goes by the same "self serve and pay by the ounce" system.  When I went, the place was packed, but the line moved quickly.  The girl took about 30 seconds to ring each person up.  I was pretty impressed.  The yogurt was really good and I got a good amount for the $3.43 that I spent.  Excited that there is a place like this on the Westbank.  A good, semi-healthy alternative to the same old thing.

I really don't understand the one star reviews of this place.     I am always looking for good Mexican food in my neck of the woods, and this place definitely qualifies.  I went for lunch and realized that I hadn't been to this place since I was a kid, and it was called Visko's.  The first thing that struck me is that inside, the restaurant is exactly the same as it was when I was a kid.  Just a bit of nostalgia.  I kind of thought that was neat.  Also, the place is huge and has a separate area, if you have a big group or you want to have a large get together here.  I sat down and the waitress brought out complimentary chips and salsa (why do some places charge for chips and salsa?  It always blows me away when you go to a place and you have to pay for the stuff.).  The chips were great and the salsa was really good.  I ordered the taquitos that came topped with cheese, sour cream and green sauce.  I also got a small  frozen margarita (that is more like a medium, I'd hate to see their large!).  The taquitos were great!  They have chicken in them, and although they were rich, I thought it was perfect for lunch.  The order comes with four of them (see my picture) and I finished all but one of them.  Super good stuff.  The margarita was closer to a margarita flavored daiquiri.  If I wanted another one, I would probably get it frozen or on the rocks.  I would definitely go back.  They have a HUGE menu, so there is definitely something for everyone here.  I can't wait to return and try and few more things.  Oh and they have a band on Wednesday nights!!

I know that today is only the third day that MANGÚ has been open, but if today is any indication, this restaurant is about to take off. I'm glad I got to try it before the word really got out.  I was so excited to hear about a new Dominican restaurant opening, that I immediately made plans to stop here for lunch. I was here today at exactly noon and there was a good crowd. The place is small, so on busier days there might be a bit of wait, but the staff was pretty good at getting everyone served as quickly as possible.  I had looked over the menu ahead of time and I decided to get the Mofongo: fried plantains with salt, garlic, olive oil and pork cracklins served with shrimp. After we ordered, there was a good 30 minute wait, but that was all forgotten when the food came out. WOW. This is a BIIIIIIIG lunch! I was more than happy to dig in and I was overwhelmed by the incredible flavors of the dish. The plantains were perfectly cooked and the pork cracklins were nice and soft. The tail-off shrimp were a perfect addition to the dish and I loved all of it. Did I have leftovers? You know I did. I have to say- for the prices, the servings are HUGE. It definitely makes me want to go back with a group, order a few different things and split it all up.  Our waiter (who I think is one of the owners) couldn't have been nicer. He mentioned up front that it's their third day open and they are still working out some kinks (we ordered an appetizer that never came. No worries, it just gives me an excuse to go back). One thing I'm excited to try is their fried plantains. I almost got some today, but decided to try a "big" dish first. I can see myself picking up an order of fried plantains "to go", sometime in the very near future.  As we were getting ready to leave, the place was starting to get packed, so if you're planning to go, prepare for a short wait. Trust me, it's totally worth it.

Not too bad for what it is.  This is the new Christmas tradition that has happened at the Convention Center for the past few years. It's pretty neat- you walk in and there are all kinds of differently decorated Christmas trees, there are rides, little snacks, an ice skating rink and inflatable things for kids to jump around on.  David and I liked walking through taking it all in. It's definitely geared more towards kids, but there's some cool stuff for adults to do. I really liked the carousel. David went on the snow mizer ride, which I avoided because it spins you around and I can't get down with that. The ice skating rink was really small and the line to ice skate was insane, so we decided to skip that. If we go again, we're going to go when they first open so that we can get on the ice when it's fresh and avoid standing in a long line.  I had a good time and going definitely put me in the Christmas spirit, so I think it was worth the time to go.

Stop what you are doing right now and make plans to get brunch here. Trust me on this one.  I had heard a lot of mixed things about Press Street Station. When I mentioned to a friend of mine that I was heading here for Monday brunch, she warned me that the service is terrible. I like to sometimes make my own judgement, and the Yelp pictures of the food told me I had to at least give it a shot.  One thing that I immediately loved about this place is that they have a parking lot. In this area, that's pretty much unheard of, so they scored a point right there. We got here at about 11:30 and the place was empty except for two other tables of customers. The waitress seated us, gave us menus and immediately took our beverage order. I was impressed by the prices, but I was expecting small portions. How much could you get for only $12?  I decided to get the Cochon d'Lait which was slow­-roasted pork shoulder au jus served over creamy grits, with sunny-side-up eggs. YOU GUYS. I am not exaggerating when I tell you that this is one of the best brunchy things I have ever had ever. The grits were delicious and the sauce from the pork mixed into the grits to make them even more yummy. The two eggs on top were cooked over-easy, so when you sliced them the gooey part of the yolk mixed into the rest of the dish making for a concoction of amazingness. This dish had so much flavor and there was SO MUCH of it that the $12 price tag felt like a down right steal! I also got a side of bacon, which was cooked to crispy perfection, but honestly the pork and grits was more than enough for me.  I also have to take a second to rave about the iced coffee. Not only is the coffee itself delicious, but they mix real cream (not half and half) into it to give it a nice rich flavor that I enjoyed immensely.  I loved my meal here, and I am making plans to go back sooner rather than later. Yes, I will be getting the Cochon d'Lait again. Service was fast when I went and the waitress was really nice and attentive. I would say that we were in and out in about 30 minutes or so- not bad for a weekday brunch or lunch.

I stopped in here for an oil change the day after the 4th of July, which was probably my first mistake. I figured there wouldn't be a big crowd and I was very wrong.  Tom was the man who took care of me and he was very nice. Nothing that happened was his fault, but a lot of people "called in" because it was the day after a holiday and they were understaffed. My simple oil change and tire rotation took over two hours. Again, Tom was lovely and very apologetic and the job was down well, so in the end, the length of time was my only main complaint.  I like that you can make your appointment online and they do take you car as soon as you come in. Next time, I plan on being the first appointment of the day.

This seafood place is owned by the same folks who own Big EZ seafood, so if you have been there, you won't be disappointed by the quality of food here.  I got my usual 12 inch shrimp poboy and it didn't disappoint. For $10 you get a poboy PACKED with large shrimp that are falling out of the bread. They are fried to perfection and delicious and you get a lot of "bang" for your buck, which is why I'm a big fan of this place. Just like Big EZ, they have boiled seafood, other types of poboys and platters and I have always been beyond pleased with what these owners have to offer. I am so glad to see them expanding and plan on adding Mr. Crabhouse to my regular seafood rotation.

I found an amazing dress for New Year's Eve here! Yes, I already got my New Year's Eve dress- I don't like waiting until the last minute.  Yes, the dresses here are a little fancier and more expensive than the average "run of the mill" dresses you might find at Dillard's, but they are better quality and for special occasions. I came in just thinking that I would look around and "window shop", but then I found an amazing dress for a pretty good price that I just had to have.  I was specifically looking for something with a little sparkle and pizzazz and the woman working here was quick to find me something that worked for me and in my price range. I would absolutely recommend this store to anyone looking for a fancy dress for a special evening or a night out on the town.

David and I had a craving during these *unprecedented times* and Company Burger wasn't open, so we decided to go on a burger hunt. Well, first it was a snowball hunt, but either way you look at it, we ended up here.  The place has been around for like 60 years and it's nothing spectacular, but they serve all kinds of classic foods like burgers, shakes, ice cream, hot dogs, etc. You walk up and pay and eat outside, or in your car (if the times you are in are unprecedented).   We got cheeseburgers and David got onion rings and I got fries. The burgers were great. Maybe I was just super hungry, but it hit the spot. The fries were aiight- they could have used some salt, but I'm not complaining.  For dessert, we got vanilla ice cream which comes soft serve style. WOW. OMG- it was delicious! I got a small and scarfed the whole thing- you know I can eat, y'all. They can make you a sundae, if you want to pay extra for a topping, but I was pleased with just the soft serve.  We will definitely be back and it's pretty silly that I had never been here, even though I'm a lifelong Westbanker.

There's no excuse why it has taken me so long to sing the praises of Schnell's.  Behind that glorious German name is some of the most delicious fried chicken you will ever put in your mouth, but I'm getting ahead of myself.  I stopped in here months ago for an easy dinner and I was the only person in here on a Friday night. I had a man's hunger, so I decided to tuck into their fried chicken and some onion rings.  In case you weren't aware: I'm an onion ring snob and only the best will do. Schnell's rings passed the "dip" test (the batter stays on when dipping into ketchup or other dip of your choosing). Crispy on the outside and soft on the inside- perfect.  The fried chicken is out-of-this-world. For $10 you get all the white meats fried to juicy perfection. Unless you are looking to break some sort of record, you are going to need a go-box.  The waitress couldn't have been nicer and she even apologized for the wait time for the fried chicken. Look, I don't mind waiting for fried chicken at all- I know the good stuff takes time.  If you didn't grow up on the Westbank, this place might not be on your radar, but it's definitely worth a visit.

We're getting into the warmer season here in New Orleans, so you know that it's time for snowballs. What's better than a regular old snowball? A designer snowball! A designer snowball is a creation by stand owner Stricen Carter and it's topped with candy cookies cheesecake and basically any goodies you can imagine. These Instagram worthy treats will have you coming back for more.  When I stopped in here, I got a strawberry cheesecake snowball that came complete with a wedge of cheesecake inside of it. It was outstanding! I love how fine the ice is here and as the snowball melted the cheesecake mixed in to make it a perfect treat. There's a lot of sugar here, so be sure to pace yourself. If you're looking for a unique dessert fit for Instagram, this is the spot.  I wrote about this spot for Very Local New Orleans. Read that article here: https://nola.verylocal.com/sweet-thangs-update-stricen-carters-designer-snoballs/180480/

For Review 1600, I chose to review the newest Emeril restaurant in town.  My dad and I came in for lunch and, because I had made reservations, we were seated immediately in the nicely packed dining room. Right away I loved the atmosphere- sunlight spilled into the dining room through large windows, the kitchen is open so you can see the hustle and bustle of the food being prepared and the tables are arranged nicely in the space and it didn't feel cramped. I had sneaked a peek at the menu online, so I already had in mind what I wanted to order.  For my starter, I got the fried calamari and for my entree I got the fettuccine nero. The calamari was delicious- small pieces were lightly battered and it literally melted in my mouth. The fettuccine was good, but I did have to add a bit of salt to it. It was black fettuccine served with a generous portion of crab meat and almond slivers- I really liked it. My dad had the shrimp dish and I think that he found it a bit underwhelming for the price.  For dessert, I treated myself to their peanut butter banana chocolate pie, which is as decadent as it sounds. It was good without being overwhelmingly sweet and I could tell that it was made in house. It was a nice touch that they put the whipped cream on the side of the pie, rather than on top, so that you can control how much you eat.  Meril has only been open about two weeks are there are a few growing pains they have to work out, We had two waiters (I think one was training) and they both forgot to bring us water when we first sat down. I ordered coffee, which came in a personal french press, and it jammed- twice. I did think that they were good at getting the food out in a timely manner, especially considering the crowd. Also, I do like the affordable price point, which makes it a perfect lunch spot. On my way out I even got a "Thanks for coming!" from Emeril himself, who was at the door chatting with customers. I really liked Meril and I'll be back.

I like Stein Mart. They have a little mix of everything at different prices and they seem to always be having some sort of sale.  I was here looking for a few vacation items and, as usual, I headed right to the sale section. Why pay full price when you can pay a sale price, says I. They had a great selection of sale stuff and I found a cute top that is great for summer. If sales aren't really your thing, they have a nice selection of "fancier" items that range from $100 to $200+, depending on what you are looking for. They also have a wide selection of work out clothes, which I wasn't in the market for, but I will be returning when I am looking for that type of thing.  This is a pretty typical department store that has a little bit of everything and you are bound to find something that suits you.

I've become a bit of a freak for Asian food lately. Sushi, Pho, fusion- I can't get enough. I think I eat Asian at least three times a week these days, so it's basically incomprehensible that I had never tried Noodle and Pie before, even though it's been open for well over a year.  Walking in, I thought to myself "what can you really do with ramen to make it stand out"? I mean...it's noodles and broth. Not quite Pho and maybe a little better than the stuff college kids live off of for four years. Well, I was wrong. I was so wrong.  They have a pretty small menu and a few different bowls of ramen with different things mixed in. Our waitress told us that the special of the day was a tomato based ramen with meat in it, so I decided to try that. I got the large bowl, which really wasn't all that large and I think would be easy for anyone to finish.  The tomato based ramen had so much flavor! I was really shocked at how good it was. It was a delightful tomato broth with ramen, meat and topped with a fine shredded cheese. I really enjoyed it. Their spoons are HUGE and make it super easy to get all of the goodies out of the bowl.   As for the the pie- yeah, the pie.
