First of all, considering they have the word "pie" in the name of their store, the pie menu isn't very extensive. I decided to try the pumpkin pie because I really like pumpkin pie. Honestly, it was just okay. I wasn't blown away by it and I've actually had pie that is just as good and cost $2 at a diner.  I would definitely go back for the noodles and get my dessert fix elsewhere.

I just got back from having lunch at Shaya, and I couldn't wait to rave about it.  First of all, when I first heard that an Israeli inspired restaurant was opening in NOLA, I was immediately "in". I didn't know much about Israeli food, but I'm a pretty adventurous person, so I was eager to check this place out.  A friend and I stopped in for lunch and sat at the bar. The restaurant is extremely nice with a typical John Besh "upscale" type of feel. Looking over the menu, I was happy to see that there are a lot of small plate options, so that you can sample a lot of different dishes.  You can get 3 small plates for the table for $9, so we decided to start with Baba Ganoush, Tabouleh and Lutenitsa. The Baba Ganoush was eggplant, slow roasted garlic and olive oil. It was yummy and had a lot of flavor. I had never had Tabouleh- parsley and bulgar wheat salad, red onion, toasted almond and preserved lemon or Lutenitsa- Bulgarian puree of roasted pepper, eggplant, garlic and tomato, before and both were good and were an interesting mix of tastes. All three were served with fresh pita bread on the side so that you could spread it on and really enjoy it.  For my main dish I had curried fried cauliflower hummus which was amazing. It didn't look like a lot, when it first came out, but after I had started eating it I realized that it was quite filling. It made for the perfect Lenten lunch, as there was no meat involved at all.  I would say that Shaya is a great place for lunch. They have a few more items on the menu for dinner, but if you go for dinner, I would say you should be prepared to order quite a few things, as the food is very light.   The place itself is nice, but it gets pretty loud in there. This seems to be the trend with Besh-involved restaurants, as of late, but it's not terrible.  I would definitely return to Shaya for a yummy lunch that doesn't break the bank.

Whoa! When did the Westbank get a Hardee's?  Dustin told me about this hidden "gem" in Marrero, so I decided to swing through and check it out. I'm not crazy adventurous so I just decided to get a burger and fries. I know, this place has burritos and tacos and stuff, but I wasn't in the mood for that. Well, the burger and fries were fine (better than McD's, not as good as Wendy's), but somehow they forgot to put my order in, so I had to pull up in the line and wait 10 extra minutes for my food. How does someone forget to put an order in?  I want to go back and try some of their breakfast stuff, as I hear it's pretty amazing.

What can I say that I haven't said before about this amazing place?  David and I stopped in here before the Saints game.  As usual, I got The Chicken St. Charles which is poached eggs on a piece of fried chicken atop a biscuit. If it sounds like I just described a piece of heaven, you aren't wrong. There's just something special about breaking a poached egg and the yolk drips all over a piece of fried chicken and onto a biscuit. There must be a word for it, but I'm not sure what it is. Let's just go with deliciousity. This deliciousity was off the charts and I had no idea how rich it was going to be- and that's not a complaint.  The side of grits and bacon were a perfect round off to the meal. The grits were delicious and the bacon might be some of the best bacon I've ever had at a sit down restaurant. The iced coffee was okay but, surprisingly, I actually preferred the hot coffee. They serve it in a huge mug and it's just great.  The waitress was really nice and got everything taken care of in record time. I love the vibe here and the food is out of this world, so I'll be back.

As far as bars on Bourbon Street go, this one wasn't too bad. The place is actually called "Prohibition: Huge Ass Beers", so make a note of that if you're looking for the place, for some reason.  Just like any bar like this, it's going to be a tourist trap and there were plenty on the night we were here. We were hanging out waiting for the Krewe of Boo parade to start and we decided to sit at the bar, have a few drinks and watch the LSU game. There was a band playing that was pretty good and the staff was friendly and fast. They have a "2 for 1" deal that basically applies to all of the crappy beer, so I skipped it and got myself a regular priced Lagunitas IPA that I was happy with.  I wouldn't plan an evening around hanging out here, but it isn't a bad choice if you're in the area.

When someone texted me and asked me if I was opening a chicken place I had no idea what they were talking about. No, Nola Chick is not my new chicken joint, even though it's been my online handle for years. But I love fried chicken, so I knew I had to check this spot out.  When I stopped in, I had the Hot Chick on a bun. It had the perfect level of tang from the chili sauce. I tried the Parish Chick on a biscuit, and the spicy-sweet honey complemented the tender chicken, and would make a perfect (late) breakfast sandwich. I especially loved the way the honey and juice from the chicken soaked into the biscuit.  I also had chicken tenders, which were tasty, and with choices of sticky Thai chili, satsuma barbecue, Cajun honey or ranch dipping sauce, you can't go wrong with mixing and matching your flavors. In my opinion, these juicy tenders give another popular chicken tender spot a run for their money.  I wrote about this spot for Mid City Messenger. Read more here: https://midcitymessenger.com/2021/02/12/nola-chick-drive-thru-opens-at-tulane-and-carrollton/

For some reason, I'm obnoxiously picky about Chinese food. Where do I get off? I can't cook it, but I consider myself the Guy Fieri of the stuff. Okay, not quite, but I know what I like when it comes to pretend Chinese cuisine.  I got Panda King takeout because I got a flyer in the mail, with the menu, and I realize I'd never been. I got a takeout of sweet and sour shrimp, veggie fried rice and it came with an egg roll and two crab rangoons.  The sweet and sour shrimp was okay, it was a little heavy on the batter, but I do like that the sauce came on the side. The veggie rice was flavorless and I had to add soy sauce to make it edible. The egg rolls and the crab rangoons were great! I'd probably order these on their own- I guess you can never go wrong with fried stuff.  Would I go back? Eh, maybe to dine in or to do dim sum. For takeout, there are better places around here.

I don't even know where to start. Maypop has been on my list for a while, so when I saw that I would be in the area, I made plans with a coworker to get lunch here. My entire experiences here was nothing short of amazing.  We got here a bit after typical lunch hour around 1 or so, and the place was pretty much empty which is always fine by me. We were seated and our drink orders were taken. After looking over the menu and deciding what we wanted, we settled on the fried oyster app and I got the pork belly, grillades and cheesy grits as my entree.  After we ordered, someone from the kitchen brought out a complimentary sample of the curry beignets. These little beignets were delicious and packed an amazing flavor. There were so good that they got me really excited for what was to come.  The fried oysters were next. Delicately fried and the perfect serving size, I loved them. They came topped with manchego cheese and spicy cucumber and they were served with a bourbon barrel soy mash aioli that brought the entire dish to the next level. These oysters are a "must" for any fried oyster lover.  My slow roasted pork belly, grillades and grits didn't disappoint. The dish was rich and full of flavor. There was a generous serving of tender pork belly that was nice and crispy on the outside and tender as you cut into it. The grillades mixed with the grits beautifully to create a flavor that was memorable and a perfect combination with the pork belly. I especially liked that there were tomato, shaved pepper and roasted garlic in the dish as well, as I thought it was a nice touch and really emphasized the freshness of the food. This dish was perfect for lunch.  At the end of the meal, we were given an after-meal treat of cocoa "candies" and I was given a fresh iced tea "to go" without having to ask, which really made an impression on me.  I was extremely impressed with the professionalism of the staff here- after we finished our appetizer, our flatware was cleared and replaced with fresh and our table was wiped down. As soon as we finished one dish, that dish was cleared. We were checked on regularly by many members of the staff, but especially our wonderful waiter Joey who went out of his way to make sure that we had everything that we needed.  Maypop was one of my favorite meals of 2017 and I'm adding it to my "favorites" list. From beginning to end, the experience was perfection- the food, the staff, the atmosphere- everything. I can't wait to go back for dinner and maybe even Dim Sum brunch one weekend.

Not bad for what is basically fast food pizza.  They have regular specials, so you can always find some kind of deal depending on what day you decide to go. The pizza itself is just "okay" but better than most other pizza chains. I find it a little "bready", if that makes any sense. My first choice is always something a little more "upscale", but if you need something in a pinch, don't hesitate to come here.

I've been trying to eat a bit healthier lately, but I allow myself the weekend to splurge on the good stuff, so I ended up at Lakeview Harbor for a cheeseburger and onion rings.  Truth me told: I never went to the old Lakeview Harbor. I had always heard raves about how good the burgers are, but I rarely eat burgers these days, and when I do, I go for Company Burger. This new spot is really nice and the inside is set up nicely and is quite welcoming. I was here right when they opened, so the crowd was thin and I was seated immediately.  As I mentioned, I got the cheeseburger with onion rings and also a side of potato salad because...salad is healthy. Duh. The cheeseburger comes cooked any way you want and you have your choice of a few cheeses. I went with cheddar cheese. The burger was great- it was cooked perfectly, it came dressed and the cheese was plentiful. While it wasn't as good as Company Burger (I think they cook their burgers in bacon fat or something), I enjoyed it. The potato salad was yummy and the star of the show was the onion rings. I love onion rings and these were golden brown and crispy. They were great and I'd order them again.  All in all my experience here was good and I'd return.

I have zero experience with casinos.  I don't gamble and I've only been to two casinos in my entire life.  Harrah's is one of them.  Really big and geared towards tourists with Fleur de Lis on everything and a brass band that does a second line through the casino every few hours.  There's a restaurant in the casino and I'm pretty sure it's a buffet.  I've never tried it, but it must be pretty good because there are always people in there.  The best section of the casino is probably the poker room.  It's huge and there's usually a waiting list to sit at one of the tables.  It's one of the regular locations for the "World Series of Poker", so everything in the poker room is top notch.  The cocktail waitresses are super attentive and the section has it's own bar, if you want to get your own drink.  I agree with Jeremy S, in that the restrooms are always super clean, and I don't think that I have ever been in there when there wasn't an attendant keeping things neat and tidy..

Fat Harry's isn't a bad little place.  We stopped in here on Lundi Gras after parades. They recently had a fire and redid the entire place, although it really doesn't look all that different to me. By the time we got here, it was pretty empty. I guess the usual crowd had better things to do after the parade. I did have a good time dancing around to the music that was playing.  This probably isn't a place I would seek out. From what I remember from years ago it's mostly a college hang out and these days I am just too old to hang out with people under 23 (hair flip). I do hear that their grill is reopening soon, so maybe I will stop in just to see what they offer.

The shoes here are weird for me.  Allow me to explain- I wear 3 different shoe sizes depending on the brand. Sometimes I wear a 7, sometimes it's a 7.5 and sometimes it's an 8. Most of the time, one of these sizes ends up being the perfect fit for me, so it's not usually an issue...until now. I came here to check out the sale they were having. I was in the market for sandals, so that's where my focus was. First I tried on the size 8s and they were all too big. Then I tried on the 7.5s but they were too narrow and smooshed my foot and all of my toesies didn't fit into the shoe. I felt like I was in a weird Goldilocks/Cinderella situation. If I were to buy shoes here, my only option would be to get the 8s and just deal with that fact that they are going to be loose. This is probably just a "me" issue and not the store's fault, but I have never left a store unable to fit comfortably in the shoes. It was a bummer, mainly because I was hoping to take advantage of the sale that they were having.  I might try again if I'm in the area, maybe I should try different styles.

I like Thai food, but I don't eat it nearly enough. I had heard so much good stuff about Secret Thai that I knew I had to make a point of eating here when I found myself in Chalmette.  The place itself is small and it was pretty empty when I went a few hours after noon on a Saturday. It was storming, so that might have had something to do with such a light crowd. After sitting a while, the waitress came over and explained the "process". So, this is legit Thai food and as the waitress explained- spicy means that it's spicy and it isn't "dumbed down" (my words) for Americans. They have different levels of spice for most of the dishes. We started with the shumai and Tom Yum Soup (level 2) and I got the chicken fried rice, which was just chicken fried rice with no spice added (fine by me).  Shumai- these cute little dumplings were tasty and had a bit of a kick, but weren't overwhelming. They definitely had some spice, but they were flavorful and really good.  Tom Yum Soup- Hey now! Okay, this was level 2 and it did have some bite to it. I could handle it- I like spice, but I couldn't have gone any higher than 2. It wasn't so much a "burn" kind of spice as it was that gradual kind of heat that builds and can be dangerous if you aren't used to it. It was great, though and a really big serving for the price.  Chicken Fried Rice- HUGE serving! Wow, this could easily feed two people. It was delicious and what I imagine authentic fried rice to be. It didn't have a kick- it was just savory and good with big pieces of juicy chicken. This is probably what kids order when they eat here, but I enjoyed it and I would absolutely get this dish again. I had plenty to take home, and that always makes me happy.  All in all the experience here was great. Just a warning: everything here is cooked to order, so don't go if you're in a rush. There was no crowd when I went and it took about an hour to get my entree. If you like Thai food, give this place a shot.

Smoked is a barbecue haven tucked into an unassuming strip right off of Jefferson Hwy.  The menu here has offerings of brisket, pulled pork, ribs, chicken and salmon, which is a unique choice for a barbecue place. Sides include potato salad, mac and cheese, coleslaw, baked beans and much more. They even have a breakfast menu and desserts!  I had the brisket with potato salad and mac and cheese ($18). Man, this brisket came out smoky and tender! There's amazing flavor to the meat and the restaurant's selection of sauces such as hickory, sweet and pineapple Bourbon, kick the tastes up to the next level. Potato salad is a favorite barbecue side for me and Smoked's is delicious- smooth and flavorful. The mac and cheese was excellent and had a bit of pimento flavor to it and a nice creamy texture.  The food was great, and so was the service. Owner Maureen came around to every table and made sure that everything was up to the restaurant's standards. And here's a secret- there's a bar next door and, if you want a beer with your barbecue, you are more than welcome to bring your food to the bar and enjoy it there.  I made a list of best hidden BBQ for Very Local New Orleans and this l restaurant was on it! Read it here: https://nola.verylocal.com/bbq-new-orleans/228292/

When I saw the new kid on the block moving into this prime spot on Gretna Blvd., I knew I had to get over there and taste test it for myself. It's a hard job, but someone has to do it.  It was lunchtime and I was starving, so I was happy to be seated immediately and presented with chips and salsa, which was delicious. They have a really big menu with ever Mexican-inspired dish you could imagine, but I decided to get a Burrito Supreme with chicken off of the lunch menu.  The burrito supreme is a calorie explosion that comes topped with lettuce, tomatoes, tomato salsa, guacamole and sour cream. The dish also comes with a side of rice. It was probably the perfect portion for lunch, even though I like when I have some leftovers to bring home. At $10 I thought it was a little small, especially compared to the burrito at El Patron for the same price, but I enjoyed it.  Staff was friendly and attentive and I like the vibe of this spot, so I would have lunch here again.

This is more like 3.5 stars. It was good, but I expected more.  This is one of those places that I have always heard is a "must try" NOLA institution type restaurant. We decided to stop in for lunch for a "pre-Father's Day" meal. After we sat down, the waitress came over and took our food and drink order in a timely manner. She brought out a bowl of small boiled potatoes (in lieu of bread) which we found a bit odd, but we went with it.  I got the double soft shell crab platter which came with cole slaw and french fries. The crabs were pretty good. They were lightly fried and crispy. My dad mentioned that his had kind of a "fishy" taste, but I didn't notice that at the time. It wasn't until later that night that i heated up the second one in the oven that I noticed a distinct "seafood" taste. The cole slaw was okay, as were the fries.  Our waitress was kind of a mess. She was slow in refilling drinks (she had maybe one other table), slow checking on us and just slow in general. Also, her attitude was as if we were inconveniencing her by being there. I searched some other reviews and I can tell that others had the same woman. I didn't get her name, and I wouldn't call her out if I had, but she just seemed miserable.  All in all, Deanie's wasn't terrible but I have had better food and service elsewhere. I might return, but I wouldn't recommend this place.

Not the worst, but they definitely need to work on some things.   This Starbucks is already located in a Target store, so I feel like it should lose points for that. I don't like having to wade through a sea of middle-aged, oblivious moms in yoga pants who would rather chit chat than let you get your coffee (this actually happened, I'm not stereotyping).   There was one woman working when I was here and she was being run ragged. She was hustling getting coffee, food and everything else that the MAMs were demanding of her. I seriously think she was thrilled when I just ordered a large iced coffee.  At other stores such a simple order comes out right away, but because there was only one person working, it took a while. Seriously Target, get that girl some help. The coffee was mediocre, as expected, and I only stopped here in the first place because someone gave me a gift card for Christmas because they obviously hate me or something.  Anyway, if you need coffee during your Target trip, then this is the spot. Otherwise, you should probably avoid.

Cooter Brown's is fantastic.  Not only is it a great place to watch a game (the place is huge, has two bars with a HUGE beer selection and lots of tvs) but they have FANTASTIC oysters.    Whenever I go here my friend and I usually split a dozen raw oysters and some fries.  The oysters are really BIG and juicy and full of flavor.  I've found at places like Acme, the oysters tend to be on the smaller side, but that wasn't an issue here.  The fries we ordered were topped with chili and cheese and we ate them with a fork.  So good!  If oysters aren't your thing, Cooter's also serves different kinds of sandwiches, burgers and po boys.  They also have different types of hot dogs and side orders such as chicken fingers and mozzarella sticks.   Whether you are stopping in for the game, a beer with friends or dinner, you are sure to find what you are looking for here.  Please note: the online menu is not up to date AT ALL, so be sure to look the bar menu over, before ordering.

This is a wonderful book shop, especially if you're looking for the local goods.  I ended up here for a book signing and I fell in love! I like that it's located at the Rink, which is a cool little center and I like the New Orleans and Louisiana representation on the shelves. They have autographed copies of books, if that's your thing, and if you're looking for a rare book, GDBS will help you track it down.  The shop is regularly holding cute events, so you can stop in, get a book and maybe a cocktail. You can't go wrong!

I'm usually not a liquor drinker at all. Beer and wine (sometimes) is more my thing, but my friend had his birthday party here, so it was the perfect opportunity to check the place out.  Seven Three has all of your liquor bases covered: they make vodka, gin, whiskey and even moonshine. They have an extensive cocktail menu, or you can just get them to whip you up one of your favorites. I had the Gentilly Gin Punch. I haven't had a lot of gin, but the punch went down really smoothly and I could barely taste the alcohol. I know this might not be everyone's thing, but I liked it.  The distillery and bar itself is huge, and was perfect for the event I was attending. There was a big room in the front with a bar and another bar in the back with plenty of seating, including booths, if you don't want to sit at the actual bar. My only small complaint was that the place doesn't have a lot of windows (it's basically a converted warehouse), so I imagine there isn't a lot of natural light coming in during the day.

This is a pretty laid back neighborhood bar. Like other bars in this area, everyone seems to know each other and the place is friendly. There are pool tables, if you like to play and there's a fairly decent beer selection. On the day I was here I was just grabbing a quick drink with some friends and we sat at the bar and chatted with the bartender for a bit. The service was good, but it wasn't really packed when I was here, so I don't know how service is when there's a crowd.

A lot of fluff for what is basically a typical hotel bar.  The only really redeeming quality of the place was the view of the city.  Drinks were overpriced and the over all attitude of the place wasn't very welcoming. The only reason to go here would be if you are a man who wants a beer while you wait for your date to finish getting ready up in the room.    I would have no reason to ever go back here.  If you're visiting New Orleans, venture out and go see the more friendly places that our city has to offer.

Fair warning: I was in starvation nation when I found myself here, so keep that in mind when you are reading this.  OH MY GOD THIS MIGHT BE THE BEST PIZZA I HAVE EVER EATEN!!!!!!  Okay, now that I got that out of my system- we stopped into this neighborhood convenience store on the hunt for a snack. This place has a little bit of everything, like others have said. It's a spot where you can "make groceries", if you are in a pinch.  They have a pretty good selection of fresh pizza and I decided to get the feta and spinach one, because it looked really good. You get a huge slice of pizza and mine was so big that I had to actually fold it and eat it sandwich style. It's not the very best pizza I have ever had, but it had been a long evening and I was thankful for it. It did have a lot of flavor and was really good, especially considering that this place is basically just a hole in the wall.  Would I return? Sure, why not?

This is one of the dark little bars that is located at the end of Lower Decatur.  Abbey isn't one of my favorite spots, but it's a nice haunt where you can stop and grab a beer or a mixed drink for pretty cheap. One thing I really do like about this spot are the booths where you can sit and chat away from the hustle and bustle of the bar itself. They have a jukebox with some pretty interesting tunes, and I like that's it not one of those internet jukeboxes so many places have these days.  In general, the crowd is friendly here, but I have encountered a few salty types once or twice. The bartender I have dealt with the last two times I've visited was really funny with a great personality and was open to providing some good conversation.  I wouldn't go out of my way to return, but I'd gladly duck in, if I find myself in the area.

Uh...well. Let's just say this: they are fast to show up, but you really better know how to get where you are going, because you are going to have to give your cabbie directions. At least, that was my experience.  A friend and I were going from Tchoupitoulas to Oak Street. I thought it was an easy enough job. Well, the cabbie had no idea where Oak Street was and we had to give him turn by turn directions: "left here, right here". I guess that's no big deal, but if I didn't know the exact way myself, I would have been up a creek without a paddle. Why would a cab company hire someone who doesn't know their way around?  Also, it was eerily quiet in the cab. Aside from us giving the guy directions, it was silent. No radio, no nothing.  I will avoid this company from here on out.

Not one of the nicer bed and breakfasts, but maybe it was just my room.  This bed and breakfast is located on Prytania and I was in the first room on the bottom floor. For starters, this happened to be one of the few cold days of the season and there was zero heat on in the place. No heat in the room, which is understandable, but also there was no heat in the rest of the house. I can understand if they don't want to crank the heat up to 90, but put a little something on to take the chill off of the house. If it had been colder that day, it would have been really uncomfortable.  The room itself was pretty basic. There was a ratty old vintage chair, a desk and a bed. It was as "no frills" as it gets. The desk was blocking the air conditioning/heating unit, and I could barely move it out of the way to let heat into the room. I wouldn't have even really known who to ask to help me at this time of day.  The bathroom was really small and nothing to write home about, but I know that in these old houses they have to fit the bathrooms in where they can but the size of it was worth noting.  The most off putting part of the room was the paint that was chipping off of the walls and the cracks in the walls that were lazily spackled and no one even bothered to try to paint over it or hide it or put the ugly chair in front of it.  They do have a nice dining room/kitchen area where you can have breakfast and coffee in the morning and the staff is nice enough. This would definitely be a good crash pad if you are just going to be out and about for Mardi Gras or on vacation. I'm sure the more expensive rooms are a little nicer than the one I was in.

Yeah, this is the kind of place that I will shop one day when I am a multi-millionaire.  Everything here is incredible and gorgeous. Not only that, but I happen to know the person who photographs all of this good stuff for the sale catalog, so I get to see all these wonderful things up close on instagram every now and then.  This is a fantastic antique shop that sells fancy, intricate clocks, gorgeous furniture and even statues. All of it looks like it belongs in one of those mansions on St. Charles Avenue.   Even if the stuff is out of your price range, it's worth stopping in and seeing what they have because everything here is just gorgeous and perfect.

Oooh. I had yummy croissants from here this morning. So good. Nice and fresh and I like how there is an outer thick "crust" with the soft inside. They are so delicious, no butter or anything else needed. They also sell danish and other pastries. Perfect little neighborhood breakfast spot, if you are looking to pick up something that isn't a doughnut or a bagel.

David and I decided to check out this new beer bar and we enjoyed it, even though the place was pretty dead and their beer was limited.  The space is lovely and they have their own parking lot, which is immediate bonus points. I sampled a couple of their ciders and enjoyed them- the Broad Street Belle stood out to me. When I went, they mainly had guest taps and cans that you can find just about anywhere. No complaints as I was happy to sip on my Founders All Day IPA which was only $3.  I'll definitely be back to sample more of their own offerings.

I adore this place on so many levels! They pull you in with their pink decor, zebra carpet bright lights and shiny sparkly jewelry. It's the ultimate girl trap.  I love anything that glitters in the light and this place has it by the truckload: There is shiny everything from earrings and bracelets to necklaces and keychains. Some of it is big and obnoxious (in a good way) and some of it is subtle and dainty. I swear, I would show you but you really aren't allowed to take pictures here, probably because it ruins the magic.  I wanted some "statement" rhinestone earrings, and fortunately I was in the area, so I found myself in So Good. I found exactly what I was looking for immediately. Staff will follow you around the store, especially if you come later in the evening. Don't take it personally, I am sure they have people trying to steal all the time.  This is your one stop shop for anyone who wants their costume jewelry to make a statement and get them noticed.

Review #1700 is going be all about my kitchen remodel. Yayyyy! Let's begin...  This is going to be a long one, folks. This is a review of the kitchen remodel that Lowe's was at the helm of in my house. Fix a drink. Get a snack.  I want to start by saying that I first went to Lowe's over the July 4th weekend to begin the process of building my dream kitchen. This process took way longer than expected- there was joy, there was pain, there was a kitchen. I'm going to cover everything step by step, so if you aren't interested, skip to the end for the cliffs.  Floors- So I got the floor tile from Lowe's. After gutting the entire old kitchen (I didn't even have a toaster in there), I call Lowe's (per their instruction) after the kitchen was gutted and they say, "Oh, we can come out in A MONTH and install it then." Sooo I'm supposed to go a month with NO progress being made on my kitchen (floor has to be installed before everything else)? I was freaking out. THANKFULLY my dad asked a friend of his to help me out. He was a total lifesaver and did a great job installing the floor. If Lowe's had told me they needed a month's notice before the floor install, this would have been a non-issue. All's well that end's well, but there could have been more communication. 2/5   Cabinets- I ordered the cabinets first, as per Lowe's instruction. All of the cabinets were delivered to my living room within a month. I had a living room full of kitchen cabinets for 3 months- no kidding. The hiccup came when the cabinet installer (Ron) came to look over the order and discovered nearly half of it was wrong. That was a BIG delay that put my kitchen construction off by about 6 weeks. Ron came back for the install and he was AWESOME. Super nice, personable and he works fast! He was quick to mention if something was damaged and it was nice to know someone was looking out for me. He is definitely a guy you want on your team. I had to order a new cabinet door, because one they sent me was warped, but that was easy enough to deal with. 3/5  Appliances- The microwave/vent was delivered and installed first, with no issues. The rest of the appliances were delivered about a week later, also with no issues. Yay! 5/5  Granite- The first time they came out to measure for the granite, they said that all of the appliances had to be installed first. No one told me this, so measuring was delayed a week. The guy came back out on December 8th and explained that I needed to get a special sink because the cabinet people didn't leave a big enough space for a sink the same size as the old sink...okay. Then they said the granite would take two weeks. They failed to mention that's in "business weeks" and the Christmas/New Years week didn't count, and I owed money that they didn't even tell me I owed so that held the process up. Delay delay delay. Also, getting someone to return a call is darn near impossible. Granite was finally installed on January 19th and if I said it wasn't worth the wait, I would be lying. It was worth the wait and then some: it's just plain gorgeous and perfect and MAKES the kitchen. 4/5  Back splash- purchased at Lowe's and installed by my contractor friend. No problems at all! 5/5  From start (tear out) to finish (back splash install) the whole process took 12 weeks. I must say that now that I am at the end of it, I am extremely satisfied. As upset as I can get about unreturned phone calls and having to hire outside help, I am more than pleased with my new kitchen, and as long as you are aware of the entire process going in, you will be happy with the results.  Cliffs: I needed to hire outside help for the floors because scheduling was an issue. Cabinets took a while, but were worth it in the long run. Appliances and back splash are perfect. Granite took a while, but was worth the wait. Follow up on everything and never assume.  Grand total: 2+3+5+4+5=19 19÷5=3.8  3.8 rounded up equals 4 stars.

I went here for the first time with some fellow yelpers to enjoy happy hour.  We all decided on cheese fondue and chocolate fondue.  It was good, but not great, but a nice little something to munch on while sipping wine and enjoying conversation with friends.  A couple of people that we were with decided to eat dinner here.  That was an adventure.  You basically cook your own food.  Do you like cooking your own food?  Awesome!  So, why are you going to go to a restaurant and pay to cook your own food?  I don't know.    I would go back for the fondue and maybe a salad, but the idea of cooking my food at the table just isn't appealing to me.  But hey, some people might love that.

When David told me that our favorite band, Nathaniel Rateliff and The Night Sweats, was coming to NOLA for the second time this year and playing Emeril Lagasse's Boudin, Bourbon and Beer fundraiser, I knew that we somehow had to get in. We've seen this band two other times and they always put on a fantastic show. I had no idea that unlimited food and alcohol was also a part of the party.  After a little luck, we were able to secure some passes and we were ready for action. First of all, the food at this event is incredible. This year it was 67 different chefs all offering their best boudin dish. We're talking empenadas, wraps, tamales, and anything else you can imagine packed with delicious boudin. It's all you can eat, so you get to sample as many different dishes as you'd like. Considering you have some of New Orleans best restaurants participating, I don't have to tell you how fantastic the food was.  The alcohol is free as well and there are full bars throughout the grounds. The staff is fast and there really weren't any lines and I like that they had the food and alcohol spread out all over the venue, so that people wouldn't cluster into one space.  Speaking of the venue, Champions Square is the perfect spot for this event and more festivals need to be hosted here. There's plenty of space so people aren't piled on top of each other, there were tables where you could set your food down while you ate, the bathrooms are clean and attended to and there's wifi! Not to mention a lovely view of the Superdome at night. Seriously, please host more events at Champions Square!  The music was incredible. After enjoying a few local bands on stage, it was time to rock out to Nathaniel, after a brief "thank you" from the man himself, Emeril. Sound was great and I was comfortable near the front and, because it's such a great space, I wasn't cramped in.   This was a fantastic time and absolutely one of the best events I have been to this year. If someone were to ask me if it's worth the $100 ticket price, I would give them a resounding "YES!". Ticket proceeds go to a good cause and you'll get to sample some dishes from a few of the best restaurants in town. It's a night you won't forget. I plan on going back next year, so hopefully I'll see you there.

Do you like great food by local restaurants and generous servings of it? Do you like live music outside? Do you like homemade crafts and art? Do you like amusement park rides? Do you like big fests that have a "small town" feel?  Well, then you need to get to Gretna fest!  Not only will you get all of the above, but you will get an awesome time with friends and something to do on a weekend, besides the same old.  I LOVE Gretna fest.  I know that most love it because of the music and the music is a definite selling point, but I go for one thing and one thing only:  the food.    Oh yes.  I use Gretna fest weekend as an excuse to eat myself stupid.  They have all kinds of offerings from different restaurants all around Gretna and also New Orleans!  And what I love most is that it's cheap and you get a serious bang for your buck.  I can't remember where it was from, but I got catfish smothered in a delicious sauce and it was only $5 and I could barely finish it because there was so much of it!  It was delicious and cheap...a total win.  The live music is fantastic and can be enjoyed on a selection of different stages.  With three days to choose from, there is bound to be a lot of different acts that you will enjoy.  Local artists and vendors also sell their wares on the grounds and a lot of the stuff is great for gifts and there are a lot of things to collect.  Great for families!  And with the ferry that goes from Canal St to Gretna, you New Orleans folks have no excuses to not check it out at least once!

I just got back from going to this place for lunch, so I am all fresh to review it.  Ok, let me start by saying that I am EXTREMELY picky when it comes to sushi.  I like the perfect amount of rice on my rolls and I like my sashimi a certain "thickness", so take that into consideration as you read this.  First of all, when I first walked in, I could immediately tell that they were modeling themselves after Westbank Sushi fave "Tennou".  From the small bar, to the booths, it all seemed really familiar.  The tables have paper "table covers" which I never like.  I know it makes cleaning up after a meal easy, but there is just something cheap about it.  They use paper napkins and not cloth and they use plastic chopsticks and not wood.  And they only offer low sodium soy sauce.  When you order, there is no sheet that you mark down what you want, you just tell the waiter.  And there is no warm towel before the meal.  Just mentioning all of this, because it's unusual for a sushi place.  I ordered the salmon sashimi, the tuna roll and the philly roll (my "usual").  When the food came, I immediately noticed that the rolls were really small and I only had two pieces of sashimi.  It turns out that you can order "2", "5", or "9" pieces of sashimi.  I didn't know that.  Since I didn't specify, he just brought the two piece.  Ok, no huge deal.  The food was pretty good, but not anything amazing.  There was only one other couple in there and the order took about 20 minutes.  If you are looking for cheap sushi, then you will like this place.  My rolls were $4 each and the sashimi 2 piece was $3.95.  All in all, I paid about 15 bucks for lunch, including tip.  I think when I go for sushi on the Westbank, again, I will just stick with Tennou.  There's a reason why that place is always packed when you go in at any time of day.

This is a really nice Walgreens in a good location. I was actually in Mid City and craving lemonade, of all things, so I stopped in here to pick one up. There weren't any long lines and the staff seemed efficient.  It's basically the same as any other Walgreens.

Musician's Village is another example of the good that is being since Hurricane Katrina.  This provides an area for the musician's of New Orleans to live. These are the people that contribute to the culture of our city and many of them were left homeless after the storm. Harry Connick Jr. and Branford Marsalis have lent their time to helping get this endeavor off the ground and funded.

How do you describe perfection? I have no idea, but I am sure going to try. As soon as I heard the Pontchartrain Hotel was reopening I was all about it. I was all about the rooms. I was all about the Bayou Bar. I was all about the Silver Whistle.   The hotel itself is heaven. It feels like an old style hotel and when you check in at the counter, you can just tell you are in for something special. One of the things I really like is that you get keys to the rooms. REAL KEYS and not cards! I hate the cards and this "old school" touch made me so happy. The room itself is lovely. The room I was in cost $100 for a night and it was gorgeous. The bed was huge and comfy, there was an honor bar, there were fancy robes and the bathroom- um, the bathroom is HUGE. A big giant shower that is all about luxury.  If you get tired of hanging in the room, you have a few options. Head downstairs to Bayou Bar where you can sip fancy cocktails, get a bite to eat and listen to the piano player singing old standards. Or you can head upstairs to Hot Tin for more fancy cocktails, a crowd that's a bit younger and the best view of the city this side of the Mississippi. If you are in the mood for caffeine and breakfast, the Silver Whistle will hook you right up. If you are craving dinner, put on your fancy dress and coat and head to The Caribbean Room for probably one of the fanciest dinners you will have in your life. I have done all of the above except for The Caribbean Room, so I am putting it on the list and it will be happening sooner rather than later.  If you want to venture out you are a short distance away from restaurants like Houston's, Cheesecake Bistro, Blind Pelican, Irish House and Hoshun. Avenue Pub and Eiffel are also on the street if you are in the mood for a little nightlife fun.   I have pretty much made Pontchartrain Hotel one of my weekly stops, so if you drop in you might see me hanging out at Bayou Bar or Hot Tin. This is the place for people who enjoy a bit of the past and fancy themselves a bit "modern old fashioned".

I was doing some work at the mall and I was pretty much forced to eat here, because it's the only relatively healthy restaurant in the food court at Lakeside Mall.  I'm going to start by saying the food was good. The system is simple: you let them know if you want a wrap or a bowl and then you pick your meat, veggies, and all the other stuff and it comes with a side. It's basically the "Subway" business model. I got a wrap with chicken and veggies and my side was a Greek salad. The wrap was great- the chicken and veggies were fresh and it had a lot of flavor. The salad left something to be desired. It was basically just lettuce with some vinaigrette dressing on it. That's their version of a Greek salad, I guess.   As good as the food was, I found it a little pricey. The meal itself was $9.50 and my water was another $3 (even though it said water is $2 on their menu board). I just wish that the healthy option at the mall wasn't the most expensive, but I guess that's just the way things go. I wouldn't have a problem paying $9.50 for a wrap and a side salad at an actual restaurant, but I did find that a little steep for mall food and $3 for water is just insane.  I'm giving four stars because the food was fresh and service was fast, especially considering there was a line. I liked my wrap, but I probably wouldn't get it again because paying over $12 for a wrap, a pile of lettuce and some water makes me feel pretty dumb.

Stopped in here, and if I'm being totally honest, I was left a bit disappointed. Let me explain. I had heard that although Elio's mainly deals in wine, they also have a pretty good beer selection. While the beer selection isn't anything out of this world, I will say that it's decent. The only problem is A LOT of the beers are old. Like, 6 months old. I understand that most people who come here are looking for wine, so that is the main focus, but if you are going to offer something, I feel that it should be pretty fresh.   I was able to pick up a couple of bottles, but I probably would have picked up a few more if there were more fresh selections. For my buck, I think that next time I'm going to skip this place when looking for beer, and just come for the wine.

As a long time fan of French Truck coffee on Magazine, I was eager to try their new cafe on Dryades. After reading Aaron's raves about the place, I knew I had to check it out.  Previous reviews do a great job at describing the atmosphere, so I'll get right to the goods. I stopped in for lunch, and while it took me a minute to find the place, there was no missing that signature orange building. There's a nice porch out front and folks were sitting with their dogs, drinking coffee, and enjoying the weather. I lucked out and there was no line, so I was able to walk up and order with no wait. I got a NOLA iced coffee and a pressed roasted turkey sandwich, which comes with a side of chips.  I was given a number, and after a short wait my food came out. This was a good size sandwich that was thick with turkey, cheese and lettuce. The bread was substantial and held it all together nicely. The turkey was obviously freshly sliced and the sandwich hit the spot. The chips were kettle chips, but I don't think they were Zapp's.  As always, the coffee was perfection- French Truck has some of the best coffee in the city and the NOLA iced coffee is tasty and rich without being overwhelming.  Overall this was a great lunch and I'll be back.

Tout De Suite Cafe serves both breakfast and lunch, but I am going to review the breakfast because that's the reason I visited,.  I stopped in on a Friday morning at about 10 and, while there was a good crowd, it wasn't overly packed. The way it works here is you order at the counter,  then find a table and wait for someone to bring you your food. The cafe is small, but it's a lovely atmosphere and a spot that seems to be full of neighborhood locals enjoying their breakfast and reading the paper.  I decided to get the Atchafalaya- crawfish etoufee poured over organic grits that comes with 2 eggs, which I decided to get on the side. After a short wait, the food came and wow- this is seriously a lot of food for this early in the morning! It was a large portion of delicious etouffee and buttery creamy grits. I loved that the etoufee had just enough spice to it, without being overwhelming and the eggs were cooked to perfection and I will gladly admit, that there was no way I was able to defeat this dish and I absolutely had leftovers. The meal was $13 and worth every penny.  I would love to return and maybe eat outside now that the weather is cooling down.

There are two things that I love: a deal and a good cause. You will find both at the No Fleas Market.  No Fleas is a thrift store with a twist. Not only are you going to find clothing, housewares and books here, but all of the proceeds of anything purchased here go directly to help animals!  They have a huge selection of clothing here. In fact, it's mostly clothing and a wide variety of it. The clothes are in good condition and are well priced, so you are sure to easily find something here that you will like. They also sell basic housewares such as glasses, household decorations and the like and they have a large book selection.  When I stopped in. I saw a gorgeous sequin black dress and if I had had an excuse to wear it, I would have snapped it up on the spot. The staff is friendly and knowledgeable and will help you find anything that you may be specifically looking for.

Hmmm this bar used to be a place. The bartender said "Round Up", but that didn't sound familiar to me. What was this place??  ANYWAY. We came here because I was in search of music and this bar...didn't have music. Womp. Oh well. They DID have All Day IPA, so I was pretty happy. You can sit at the bar or you can sit outside on the PATIO! Yeah, that's right, this place has a patio complete with a light up tree, tons of seating and a blow up pool. Did I get in the pool? NAH. But I did dig the patio and the vibe out there was fantastic. I just wish that it was a smidge cooler so that I can really hang out and soak up the atmosphere. This is definitely going to be a destination once fall arrives.

I have been a long time fan of the Pop City on Magazine and I recently stopped into the downtown location looking for some gifts.  This is a really cute store that has different types of gifts for people who appreciate things that are a little different. One thing I was looking for were some Elvis and Marilyn Monroe themed gifts and this places delivered in the form of coffee mugs, lunchboxes, figurines and other cool things to choose from.   They also carry any array of non-cheesy New Orleans souvenirs as well as t shirts and other fun gifts. I almost want to say think of it as a New Orleans version of Spencer's and you have Pop City, except that Pop City is better because it's locally owned.

What is going on in this strip mall? All of the stores here are terrible. Get it together, Algiers.  Okay, so this Ross is a mess. This Ross has the same issue that the Ross on Manhattan had before they got their stuff together. Nothing is organized, everything is thrown around and the shoe section looks like a bomb went off.  All I wanted was some cute flats at a low price. Did Ross have them? Maybe. Who's to say, considering nothing is organized by size and there are shoes missing their mate? It's sad, because I came in ready to spend money, but I was left frustrated that I couldn't figure out what was what.  I won't be back and I'll just stick to the more organized Ross in Harvey.

Ok, so my four stars is really a 4.5, but yelp doesn't have half stars like Star Search did, so here we are.  I stopped into A Girl is a Gun today after reading all of the awesome reviews.  I LOVE vintage and vintage inspired clothing and I was eager to see what this place had to offer.  I was not left disappointed.  Here you will find lovely dresses by Bettie Page clothing as well as Bernie Dexter.  There was a lovely dress here by Bernie Dexter called "Happy Valley" and the entire dress was like a beautiful painting.  It was a real work of art.  The only reason I give this place 4.5 stars is because of the prices.  It's not a bad thing, but most of the dresses are between $165-$200.  I could kind of understand that if the store was located in the quarter, but it seems out of place on a dingy little stretch of Magazine St. that is only a few doors down from a Circle K.  I would LOVE it if they kept the more expensive pieces, but also offered a few that were under $100 for the customer who doesn't have a ton of money to spend on a nice dress.  All in all, I would definitely recommend stopping into "Girl" and giving the place a look for yourself.

So this is what the Dungeon is now and I am not a fan.  The old dungeon had a certain appeal to it. Yeah, it was cheesy with the gargoyles and stuff, but there was a certain mysterious charm. Now it's just like any other tourist trap in the Quarter. The last time I went I was blown away by how different it is now. All of the kitschy decorations are gone and in it's place is a whole lot of nothing.   Also, there once was a time where taking a picture inside the Dungeon was grounds for immediate banishment into the streets. Now you are encouraged to take a souvenir picture in a stand up coffin that they have leaning against the wall. I took a picture in it to show how bad it is. And of course, the bookcase and all of the cages are gone, so really what are you even doing here?

Interesting.  I'm not usually a huge frozen yogurt fan.  I mean, I live in a city where there are awesome places like Sucre and Brocato's, so why do I want yogurt?  Because yogurt is better for me, you say?  Well, who asked?!  Ooh, sorry.  So, I went to this place after passing by it a few times, looking in, and getting weirded out by the chrome everything and the spaceship feel.  The first thing they tell you when you go in is that you can basically have as much yogurt and toppings as you want, but they weigh by the pound.  Did I ask how much it would cost if I were to fill the entire bowl they give you, with yogurt?  Uh yes, I am here to help... 9 bucks!  Anyway, they offer your basic flavors: chocolate, banana, watermelon and a few others.  They also have a "mystery" flavor called "Who Dat", which is the one I got.  Spoiler alert: the mystery flavor is kind of a sherbety flavor.  You can mix and match whatever flavors you want, and then add toppings, like chocolate chips, fruity pebbles (yeah, I don't know either), gummy bears, and a bunch of other choices.  I chose chocolate chips, because I like to keep it pretty simple.  The yogurt was really good and they say that it's actually good for you, which is always a plus.  It's a nice light treat for a hot day.  And just for the record, no, I didn't fill my ENTIRE bowl with yogurt.  My order only cost about $4.  :)

I had a meeting at this CC's recently and it turned out to be the perfect place to grab a coffee and have a chat. The coffee is typical Community Coffee, so I'll spare you my thoughts on that. This review is for the space.  This CC's is huge with plenty of tables and chairs and plenty of natural light flowing in through the windows that look out onto Magazine St. I love the whole "New Orleans" vibe of the place, right down to the New Orleans brass band music that was playing over the radio.  There's a nice selection of sweet treats, if you're in the mood and the staff was really friendly and service was fast, even though there was a bit of a line.

I think I am quickly discovering that Metairie has some really good places for fried seafood.  I stopped in here, with my father, for lunch because he was saying how good this place was. It's a pretty small place, but it has been around for over 20 years, so I assume that they know what they are doing. Looking over the menu, they have a little bit of everything, but their speciality is seafood. Because I am a huge fan of oysters, especially the fried variety, I decided on the fried oyster platter, which came with a good sized side salad, fried oysters, thin cut fries and toast.  The salad came out immediately, and my only complaint was that the dressing was on it (not on the side) and there was tons of it. Not a big deal- I only ate about half of the salad and I will get dressing on the side next time. Next up was the oyster platter and WHOA- not only were the oysters HUGE but there were tons of them. There were 13 or 14 giant oysters, fried to a light golden brown, on this plate! I was so excited! I cut them in half with my fork, and inside they were nice and juicy and delicious. These might seriously be some of the best fried oysters I have ever had and that's not an exaggeration. I had a ton of leftovers, mainly because I wanted to save some of the amazingness for dinner.  My dad got the Trout Carrie which was grilled trout topped with a TON of crab meat with mashed potatoes and peas on the side. I was able to take a taste of the mashed potatoes and they were delicious.  Jessica was our server and she was super sweet and attentive and made sure that we had everything that we needed. I will definitely go back to Fury's and I can't wait for more of those oysters.

After a busy day of Quarter hopping, my companion and I had to make a stop for some iced coffee. Lucky for us, this spot was right on our route.  First of all, what a cute place! It almost has a casual walk in diner type of feel. They not only offer coffee but they have beignets, obviously, as well as a few other cookies, tarts and sweet goodies as well as omelets and other savory yums. There was a bit of a line, but the staff here is great at getting peoples orders and moving folks through the line quickly. I had an iced coffee in my hand in no time and only for a little over $3- talk about great prices (considering you are in the Qwatas).  We took a seat at the table on the side and sipped our coffee for a bit. There's also a nice little outdoor seating area, if you would like some fresh air.

I know that I must have been to Vaso before, but maybe not.  Some friends and I were wandering down Frenchmen St. just looking for a place to listen to music where there was no cover. For some reason Apple Barrel was packed and charging a $5 cover. No thanks.  We saw that this place was way less crowded and a bress band was on stage, so we decided to stop in. I think that this place was the Hookah bar years and years ago. Anyway, I really liked the atmosphere in here. It was cozy and laid back with plenty of seating so that we could enjoy the show. The band was awesome and it was a really good time.  I'm excited to add this to the list of my "regular" music hang outs.

This is a nice part of the city and some green space in the middle of the concrete jungle of the French Quarter area.  I've attended a few events here, the most recent being the NOLA Mac and Cheese fest and it's always a good space for events and I always have a good time. The park is home to famed Congo Square, ponds, and sculptures honoring those who have helped make New Orleans great.  If you have the opportunity to attend a festival here, be sure to do so because it's a nice space worth spending some time in.

I love the Bulldog, because of their vast beer selection and pretty good food.  The Bulldog mid city is not my regular "home base", but it does have it's high points.  It's bigger than the Uptown location, which I know that some people would prefer.  It's much better for bigger groups, because if you have a big group at the other Bulldog, you pretty much have to either get there early and get a table or sit on the patio.  This Bulldog has a really nice patio area.  I like the way it's decorated with the lanterns and the lights.  This venue has more of a "lounge" feel to it.  It's definitely a different vibe than the other one.  I'm giving it 4 stars, only because my personal preference is a place that is a little more intimate, but that's just personal opinion.

I stopped into this new little clothing store on Magazine St after noticing the cute dresses in the store window.  Bella & Harlow has really cute vintage inspired dresses. When I was here, I was wishing that I had a few more dollars to spend. There is nothing cheap about the clothing here, that's for sure. I think I saw a dress here that was over $300. That's fine if it's going toward a fancy gown or something,  but I can't see spending that on a little day dress. I know what you're going to say... I have cheap taste. Ok, whatever you say!  But hey, they do have really cute dresses here and I would absolutely shop here and spend the money if I saw something I really liked.

I make fun of it a lot, but Whole Foods does serve a purpose. They have a lot of organic "high end" kind of food, and if that's your thing, then this place is heaven.  This Whole Foods is like any other grocery store, only a little more pretentious. Hey, they have the right to be. They sell gourmet nuts and have fresh made sushi in store. You walk in and the overwhelming sweet smell of the bakery and the fresh cut flowers combines to form an olfactory pleasing combination that you could probably bottle and sell, if you had the wherewithal. In their parking garage they (naturally) have a place where you can plug in your electric car and charge it while you shop. I didn't visit the butcher shop, but I can only imagine that Whole Foods' steaks are marinated in the (joyful) tears of angels until the meat practically slices itself.  One thing I will say is that this place has a pretty impressive beer and wine selection. If you are looking for rare spirits, start your search here.   I might return to Whole Foods, but don't tell the people that work here that I sometimes drink orange juice straight out of the container or that I have been known to fall asleep without brushing my teeth. I would surely be blacklisted.

Although Dimartino's serves a variety of sandwiches, I have only every gotten the muffalettas here.  It helps that this is the only place that I have ever found a muffaletta that I like (on the Westbank).  I usually get the "large" muffaletta, and although it's not as big as it used to be (back in the day, it was the size of a dinner plate, and half was plenty for a dinner!), they are still fantastic.  I like to get mine to go, bring it home, and put a little extra olive oil on it.  Mmm!  Also, did you know that you can order mini muffalettas for parties?  It's true!  They are as good as the big ones, just in a smaller form.  My family usually orders a bunch for New Year's Eve, and they are always a hit.  And they freeze really well, if you want to save a few for later.

Okay, so I don't even know if you can really consider this a Sephora. This is like the MAC store at Dillard's- it's a much smaller version, and while you will be able to find a few things you like, you need to go elsewhere to get the full experience.  I was here looking for some foundation- it seems that I always have to switch up my foundations because my skin gets irritated. The girl working here was helpful, but she wasn't successful in finding a foundation that matched my skin tone to my satisfaction.  They offer other makeup things here, but if you are looking for a big selection, you'll be better off going to the big store at Lakeside.

Am I old? You can tell me, it won't hurt my feelings.  I have no idea how I ended up at the newest incarnation of The Dungeon. A friend of mine suggested it and it sounded like a good idea at the time. Walking up to the place, I thought this might be a mistake. Going in, I was convinced it was a mistake.  Look, I used to like this place. It was a neat little metal bar with interesting characters. Now it just seems that this place has taken a turn for the "yikes". We were hanging upstairs and there's a big bar in the very back that people crowd around it gets super packed in that back section. You are forced to the front, where the other bar is, and where people are trying to dance. Back in the day, when I came here more than I do now, they had a guy working upstairs just to tell people NOT to jump on the floor. Now people jump and I am terrified that the floor is going to cave in or something. I got outta there quick, so as to avoid being on the news for dying in a washed up metal bar (what a way to go!).  It's not terrible for what it is, just go in knowing that the "cheese" factor is high. And stay downstairs. And sit near the door in case you have to make a quick escape. Just my suggestion.

A friend of mine eats here all the time and he told me they had a good Cuban, so I had to check it out.  Holly's is a convenience store with a kitchen in the back. The store itself just sells basic things- snack items and soft drinks, and the place isn't big at all. You order at the counter and then you wait as they make your food.  I decided to get the Cuban sandwich with a side of plantains. The sandwich was really good. I don't know if it's as a good as the one at El Libre, but it's pressed nicely, really cheesy and the bread is nice and crispy. The plantains were really good too and you get a good amount of them for about $3.  I'm going to go back and order ahead next time, because there is a bit of a wait while they make your food for you.

I am a huge fan of burritos and after seeing pictures of the "Big Ass Burrito", I knew that I had to make my way over here, at some point, and try it out for myself.  We were here on a Saturday evening, the crowd was thin and we were seated immediately. We decided to start out with some chips and queso- our favorite. I really liked their version and the queso had good flavor. I decided to get the "Big Ass Burrito" with pork and while it did live up to the name (it was huge and overwhelmed the plate), it was lacking something for me. I took a few bites and enjoyed it well enough, but I ended up boxing the rest and taking it home. After diving into it later, I realized the ingredients weren't evenly dispersed. There were big pockets and cheese and meat no where near each other. It was strange. I also got a frozen margarita which was okay, but clearly from a mix (it was neon green) and lacked the "limey/salt" flavor that I like in margaritas. It was closer to a margarita daiquiri.  Tacos and Beer is a good alternative to Taco Bell, but if you are looking for a really good burrito/margarita experience, for cheap, I would recommend Felipe's.

I got my braces from Dr. Devereux back in '99.  I remember that he PROMISED that they would be off in time for my senior prom and graduation and they were (2 years total)!  He totally made it happen!  Now I have a fabulous straight smile that I am always getting complimented on and I couldn't be happier with his work.  Dr. Devereux was always fabulous and really nice and efficient.  I would highly recommend him!

So first things first, yeah this cemetery is located in a pretty sketchy part of town so you have to be careful when you go. With that said, it really should be counted among the historic cemeteries of New Orleans.  It is not PERFECTLY well kept, so a lot of the tombs are falling apart, while others are in pretty good condition. This isn't as nice one of the fancier cemeteries like Metairie cemetery or something, but it still has it's own charm nonetheless.

Talk about your lifesavers, I am giving 4 stars mainly because they serve the caffeine that I so craved. I like the atmosphere of this place- it's located in a hotel. There is seating right by the windows, so people watching is breeze.   The reason I am giving four stars and not five stars is because of the bathroom. So, I go in the bathroom of the hotel lobby, which is also the PJ's bathroom and both toilets are clogged up. On top of that, the automatic sink didn't recognize me as a person. It wouldn't work. Am I a ghost? I am waving my hand in front of both faucets and nothing is happening. All in all it was a pretty gross experience. I guess it was a weird fluke, but for a bathroom to not work in the lobby of busy hotel is pretty odd.

I checked this truck out at Gretna Food Truck Fest and I am so glad I did!  First of all, the owners of this truck are beyond sweet and have a great personality, which is always a delight. I stepped up and decided to get the Southern Chicken. This is their version of the Chic-Fil-A sandwich (I'm saying that, not them)- a nice cut of fried chicken, topped with a pickle on a buttery bun. There are two sliders to an order and they are pretty big, so don't be afraid to share.   The slider is out of this world! The chicken is juicy and perfectly fried with a lot of flavor. They have mustard on the truck, if you want to add it, which I did. The mustard added the perfect kick to this tasty delight that was served fresh out of the fryer. I will definitely have to seek this truck out again. I think I'm addicted to that chicken!

I had lunch here today and I couldn't wait to hop on here and review this sweet little restaurant.  I decided to try this place after reading some of the great reviews they've been receiving. Looking over the menu, everything sounded fantastic: fried or grilled chicken, meat loaf, chicken wings, gumbo and much more. They seemed to have a little bit of everything, but I decided to go with the meat loaf with mashed potatoes and red beans and rice.   I wasn't expecting anything much, considering the meal is only $10, but I was very wrong. Out came two large slices of meatloaf with gravy on the side and a generous portion of mashed potatoes and gravy and red beans and rice. I am happy to report that the meat loaf is just like home made! This is seriously as good as anything I used to have as a kid and I could tell that the mashed potatoes were fresh and the gravy was perfect. The red beans were tasty and flavorful and had a bit of ham in them, which was great. I was so pleasantly surprised by the food here.  Justin was the waiter and he was super friendly and he got the food out fast and kept my tea filled. The place is really casual and seems to have a few regulars, and I'm happy to now be in that number. I will absolutely be back and I will definitely be ordering some take out in the future as well.

A friend and I decided to check out a comedy show here and when we walked in we immediately realized that we were both really hungry. Buffa's serves food! Perfect! I think that you can eat in the front bar, but the show we were seeing was in the dining area, so we just headed back there.  Looking over the menu, it really does seem like Buffa's has everything. Burgers, sandwiches, breakfast food and even alfredo are all on the menu. I was in the mood for a sandwich, so I decided on a club on rye bread. It came out pretty fast and it was huge! I was so hungry, I didn't even take a picture of it, I just jumped in. It was delicious with turkey, ham and bacon and I finished the entire thing.   The bartender, who took the order, was super nice and friendly. Although he was busy, he was attentive and was sure to ask how everything was. Buffa's is open 24 hours, so this is a really cool place to stop and eat after a wild night in the quarter. I also really like that the dining area is smoke free.  Now that I am familiar with Buffa's menu, I think I will definitely come back and eat here again.

Here's another one of those cool music clubs near Frenchmen street.  It seems that whenever I pass this place there is some wonderful music coming from it.  It seems that there is always some kind of fantastic band playing here.   The other night some friends and I stopped in here and there was an eclectic band playing some amazing music.  I don't know how to describe it, but the band consisted of a sax, a trumpet, a bass, a guitar, a drummer, a keyboard and the leader of the pack was a rapper/hype man.  It was a combination of hip hop and jazz and it was really amazing and unlike anything I had ever heard.  They did a good job at getting the crowd up and dancing and we had a fantastic time.  All kinds of musicians are welcome to play here, as the Balcony hosts an array of artists.  No matter when you stop in, you are bound to hear something that you will like.

I came to this Home Depot after my usual Home Depot in Gretna didn't have the industrial cleaning supplies I needed. A quick search showed that this HD had what I sought, so I headed this way.  I had trouble finding what I was looking for, but a sales person quickly pointed me in the right direction and turned out to be a major lifesaver. I have also done some shopping here for under cabinet lights that I am considering once my new kitchen is built. They have a nice selection of rope lights and "puck" lights that are surprisingly easy to install and priced well.  Home Depot is pretty good about having seasonal sales, so keep an eye out if you are looking for something specific.

What an amazing find this place is!  This is a small unique shop on Lower Decatur that kind of reminds me of someone's grandmothers house that is filled with antiques and treasures. Here you will find all kinds of unique things. Some items that stuck out to me were: TONS of vintage clothing, including old Navy uniforms, vintage hats, unique salt and pepper shakers, religious figurines, antique decorations, statues and bottles and much more! One thing I loved is that there are boxes of old black and white photos. If you are a collector of unique pictures, you must stop in here and check them out. Looking through the box you see people dressed up for Mardi Gras on Canal street, people enjoying themselves at wedding and much more. There is even a case with antique jewelry in it.  Some of the items here are a little expensive, but keep this in mind: these are unique items that will make great gifts and if you see something you really like, why would you want to hunt around for a better deal online when you are already in the shop? Also, the shop is pretty small and it's packed with things so you are bound to find something worthwhile in any price range.  If you are a collector of things that are a little dated, unique and a touch creepy, than this is definitely the shop for you.

Finally! A sports supply store other than Academy on the Westbank!  This store is HUGE and has everything you could possibly want. I came in to check out what they had as far as Saints apparel, and they had a ton of options. OTHER stores see fit with only offering a couple of pink jerseys and cutesy t shirts to their female football fans, but Dick's offers actual league apparel, which is nice.  They have anything sports related to could want here. They even have fancy frisbees for frisbee golf. I have no idea what frisbee golf even is, but you can get whatever size/weight frisbee you want for it here, so go nuts.  Anything you could need in the sports related field is here, so check this place out.

I've never gotten more than an appetizer here, but I really like the place.  It has an "old school" Westbank feel and could probably stand to be updated, but the staff is nice and it's a nice place to hang out if you just want an appetizer or a drink.    The front has more of a "loungey" feel with a jukebox, bar area, and video poker, but the back is huge and gorgeous.  I can definitely see having a party here or going here on a night out with friends.  The staff was really nice and attentive and made sure that we were taken care of and had everything that we needed.  I would definitely go back, maybe for lunch.

Look, I don't know who decided to open a Häagen-Dazs on the Westbank, but I'm not one to question small miracles. Also, whomever decided to open up a Häagen-Dazs next door to a Reginelli's is a damn genius and deserves multiple awards. Who doesn't crave something sweet after eating salty pizza?  This is the only Häagen-Dazs location on the Westbank, and I'm excited that it's so close to my house. It's dangerously close, y'all. I had been passing this place for weeks, waiting for them to open, and the day finally came and off me and David went.   The shop is pretty small with limited seating, but that's not a big deal. They can hold about as many people that usually lurk around at an ice cream shop. I decided to get a small (one scoop) pralines and cream in a waffle cone and David got a banana split caramel thing that came in a cup. I should mention that not only does Häagen-Dazs have the classic "strawberry, chocolate, vanilla" flavors, but they have fancy-pants flavors too. My pralines and cream was delicious and I MIGHT have finished it before we even got back to the house. Ooops.  On top of that. they have hot fudge and caramel on tap- like a beer tap for hot fudge. And get this- it's warm, y'all. They put some on David's banana split cup thing and he loved it. I stole a taste and the warm caramel is delicious with the cold ice cream. This might be the place where dreams are made.  If you're in the mood for something a little more simple, they have wrapped ice cream bars in a case. They also have ice cream cakes and milkshakes, because of course they do. They staff was super friendly and I know that this will likely be our new Westbank dessert spot. I'm so excited they're here!

If you are from the Westbank, this is the streetcar that you can hop on and travel to Mid City. Or, if you are in Mid City, this streetcar will take you downtown.  I don't have a ton of experience when it comes to riding the rails, but this streetcar line has always served me well. Of course, it gets packed on busier days- a few years back riding from Mid City to downtown on Halloween was cramped, to say the least. It usually runs on time with few delays and the cars are in good shape.  I like that the cars have ac, so you're not sweating to death on hotter days and it's a dependable alternative if you want to travel throughout the city and not have to worry about parking.

YAY! I never go on the ferry (because I honestly never have any reason to), but this was a really cool experience.   I went on the ferry to go from Algiers to downtown for the French Quarter Fest.  It wasn't overly packed, it was a great view and it was super convenient, because it dropped us off right where the fest was.  I can definitely see why people would use the ferry to travel, especially if they are on a bike.  I would love to go over on a bike and pedal around the quarter without having to worry about parking.  Oh!  And it is super fast, if you are in a rush, for some reason.

Amazing.  I had heard about this place over and over again and I don't think I realized that it was so close to me! I decided that I needed to go in and try one of their po boys right away. I decided to order the roast beef. I usually go for seafood, and I was delighted to see that they had fried oyster on the menu.  The roast beef po boy was amazing. I got the 8 inch which was plenty enough for a lunch and I had a little left over. As a side I got fried pickles ($2) that were crispy and fresh and so good. I was satisfied with the meal and it didn't cost an arm and a leg.  I will definitely be back because I am anxious to try the oyster po boy.

This is a pretty fantastic Breaux Mart. I wish the one by my house was this well stocked.  This is mainly going to be a review of the beer selection. It's pretty great. I stopped in here and they had a great selection of Stone Brewery beers, including the ever elusive Stone "Enjoy By". I was impressed by their diverse selection of brews. They even had Lazy Magnolia Jefferson Stout, which I had only ever had on tap and had never seen in a bottle. Well, I bought it and it wasn't as good as it is on tap, but that point is that they had it here. They also had a bunch of beers that I hadn't heard of, so if you are in the area, and you don't feel like going to Stein's or Whole Foods, this Breaux Mart is a decent place for beer.  As others have said, don't illegally park in the parking lot, because you will be towed.

I was able to finally make it back to The Joy last night, for the Ben Folds show, and it was a wonderful experience.
