It has been a while since I have been in Best Buy and Best Buy seems to be selling everything now.  We came here because we were looking for an X Box headset thing, but I ended up getting distracted by all of the other amazing tech goodies in this place. Big fancy hi def tvs, fit bits, hi tech refrigerators- it's all here. I know I must sound like a total newb, but I am so ignorant when it comes to the latest technology. The most technologically advanced thing I own is an iPod and a flat screen tv, so seeing 3D viewers for smart phones is pretty cool. And did you know you can get a watch that you can link to your phone to answer calls? Whoooooa. I don't need to be that connected to my phone, but Best Buy has it if you're looking for it.  Some of the prices for some things are a little high, so wait for a sale if you are trying to pinch pennies. We found what we were looking for and the staff was friendly when we were checking out.

FINALLY!! The Westbank has a Fleurty Girl!  I have been saying for years that the Westbank needed it's own little branch of this fun local shop, and owner Lauren finally made my wish come true. The newest Fleurty Girl shop is in Old Gretna and I couldn't be more excited!  After the madness of Gretna Fest died down, I was able to stop in and see FG's newest home. It's perfect- an old house that has been converted into a quaint little shop where you can find New Orleans themed t shirts and gifts. I have been a Fleurty fan for years and it's been so exciting watching this little company expand from a t shirt shop to a full blown "must" for any New Orleans gift giver.  On the day I was here, I was greeted with a friendly "Hello!" from the woman working and I was eager to look around and see exactly what this shop had to offer. FG-OG is a bit smaller than the other shops I've been in, but they pack a lot into a smaller space. They sell much more than just shirts- they also have a variety of jewelry, accessories, house decor and a lot of other fun things that you are sure to like. On this day, I found a pair of earrings that will be perfect to wear when watching a Saints game. I also saw a few t shirts that will definitely be going on my Christmas list. Oh yeah...if you want to buy me something, a Fleurty Girl gift card will do nicely.  I'm so happy that Fleurty Girl has found a home on the Westbank and I can't wait to make this place one of my regular shopping stops.

I love a yummy, fast, affordable lunch and Shahrazad Cafe fits the bill!  I popped in here after reading the reviews and seeing pictures of the delicious offerings here. I wanted something easy, so I decided to go for the beef shawarma sandwich. This is tender beef that is spiced perfectly and stuffed into a pocket of pita bread. It also comes with a side of fries. It was great! I like that there was some hummus on the meat that added a little more flavor to it. For just under $10, before tip, it might be one of the best lunch deals in town. I left feeling satisfied without having to break the bank.  I believe that it was the owner who waited on me, and he couldn't have been any nicer. He checked on me regularly and made sure that everything was to my satisfaction. It was a delight eating here and I will be returning for lunch again soon!

My boyfriend and I discovered this gem one night when we were looking for a new place to eat.  We were the only customers in the place (although, it was late), which makes me think that not a lot of people know about it.  The restaurant is actually an old house that has been converted and is a landmark.  The atmosphere is very cozy and romantic.  It's dim, so it's nice for dates.  The staff was also very personable.  I don't quite remember what I ate, but I remember it being excellent.  They even brought out a complimentary sweet treat after the meal.  I would definitely go back and I hope that more people try this little place.

This is a pretty cool snowball spot, even if the atmosphere is a little "plain Jane". David and I stopped in for a later-night (8 pm) snowball and we were the only people in the place. The staff was friendly and nice and I like that, unlike the Uptown location, there's seating inside. The only drawback was the weird club/techno music that was blasting into the seating area, but whatever.  I got the peanut butter pie stuffed snowball and it was a peanut butter lovers dream. It was a peanut butter snowball stuffed with peanut butter cheesecake. It was ALMOST too much peanut butter but, as someone who buys Reese's by the truckload, I approved.  Great spot to grab dessert in the area.

I had ordered the "perfect" dress for my birthday in the perfect shade of red. Two days before my birthday it still hadn't arrived so, I went to this Goodwill in the hope of scaring up a quickie "stand-in" at the last minute.  This Goodwill is like all the rest of them, as far as organization goes. They're organized by style and size. The store is pretty big with clothing items, households items, old records and cassettes and things of that nature.  I was perusing the dress section when I came upon a gorgeous dress in that perfect shade of red that I love. Not only did it fit perfectly, but it was only $6, so I was more than pleased. I wore it on my birthday and I might even wear it on Christmas.  This Goodwill isn't the best thrift store that I've been in, but they have a nice enough selection that the place is worth a visit.

I had heard raves about this spot from pizza lovers, so David and I decided to check it out for dinner.  The place is about as basic as a pizza parlor gets: it's located in a strip mall and it's a "seat yourself" place with tables and chairs and a window looking into the kitchen. The menu is pretty basic: you got pizza, salad and spaghetti. There's no bread or anything like that, which we found kind of odd and they also didn't have tea on the menu. How hard would it be to just have some canned tea in the fridge for people who want it?  We ordered the Tower Special, which came topped with sausage, pepperoni, onions, green peppers and mushrooms. The pizza was good, but was it $22 good? No. I didn't really like that the pepperoni was under the cheese, so it didn't have a chance to crisp up in the oven. They were generous with the cheese and I did like how big the mushrooms are.  This spot is a Metairie classic, but there are better options out there. For example, there's another local place- Theo's Pizza, right across the street and they have better prices and more options. I'm glad I got to try this place, but I doubt I'll be back.

This is a pretty basic little hole-in-the-wall that has been serving up lunch for about 51 years.  We stopped in a little after the lunch rush and there wasn't much of a crowd. This is an "order at the window" type of place, so I walked up and ordered the roast beef po boy. It doesn't come with any sides, so if you want something like fries, you have to pay extra. They give you a number, you seat yourself and they call you when your food is ready. Drinks are "serve yourself"- they give you a cup and you fill it up at their drink machine.  The roast beef po boy was great! While it's not on the same level as R&O, it's huge for the price and packed with meat. The whole thing was dressed perfectly and the gravy was yummy with a lot of flavor, but there wasn't so much on it that it made a huge mess- which is a plus, in my book. I ate half and took the other half home. Whenever I can get two meals out of one dish, I consider that a perfect lunch.  Service here is fast- the food took less than 10 minutes to come out and everyone working was friendly. I can see why this place has been around so long, and I'll return if I find myself in the area again.

I like Ike's! David and I are trying different snowball stands around town and he suggested this one that I had never heard of.  Ike's is right by the Burger King/MoPho strip mall by City Park and there was no crowd when we were here early on a Friday evening. There's a lot of seating area with tables and they have a nice selection of different snowball flavors and ice cream and also offer boudin, for some reason.  I got a wedding cake snowball and David got pralines and cream. I have to say, I really liked the fact that they flood the ice with syrup. It was practically spilling out of the cup, and when it comes to syrup, you can't over do it. The ice was nice and fine and the flavor was great.  The stand is right by a bus stop and a nice "New Orleans' highlight was when a bus driver parked the bus at the stop, hopped out and treated herself to some much earned ice cream. This stand wouldn't be my first pick for a snowball, but I wouldn't skip it if I was in the area when a craving hit.

I've been to this grocery store a few times, when I have been in the area. I have always found items here well priced and I like how they actually have a bunch of lines open at once, in order to get people in and out. I have never had to wait in a super long line here, which is awesome when you are in a rush.

I came here to see an acoustic show. Usually I would avoid any place that allows smoking, but you gotta do what you gotta do.  The staff is friendly and the bartender was super nice and the sound for the show I attended was pretty impressive, considering this is just a dive bar. There are pool tables in the back and darts if you are into that type of thing.  My biggest complaint is the smoke. I was only here about two and a half hours and I had to shower when I got home because I reeked of smoke and I had a headache because of the smoke. Maybe if they had better smoke eaters it would be tolerable, but I don't know. If you can tolerate cig smoke (it doesn't seem to bother a lot of people the way it bothers me), than this is definitely a cool spot to hang out and catch a show.

I had a hankering for a sizable oyster platter, and after seeing other check ins from my fellow Yelpers, I decided to head over to Seither's and see what they had to offer.  The parking lot was packed and the small restaurant was full, when I was here for lunch, but we were seated right away. Upon the recommendation of a food group I'm in, I started with the shrimp and corn bisque. WOW. I know that most people would say that all bisque is pretty good, but the shrimp and corn here is excellent. It's creamy, thick, flavorful and they are super generous with the shrimp. This was delicious and I know I'll be getting it again.  For my entree, I got the oyster platter and my dad got the shrimp platter. They are beyond generous with the seafood portions here. My plate was piled high with big, lightly fried, juicy oysters and sliced new potatoes underneath all the goodness. The oysters had a lot of flavor and I got that kick of just enough juice and salt when I bit into them. My dad's shrimp platter was equally generous and he had plenty to pack up and take home for later.  Our waitress Ashley was so sweet and attentive and, even though she had a lot of tables, she never let our drinks get low and she checked on us regularly to make sure that was had everything that we needed. Seither's was great and reasonably priced and I'll be back.

In September, I visited the zoo for the first time in about 10 years!  It was just as I remember.  I love how big the place is and of course the animals.  I have a lot of great memories of being a kid here.  I remember riding the elephant and even have a picture of me having a camel ride!  Remember the camel rides?  Yeah, they don't do them anymore.  We went on a Sunday, so it wasn't too crowded with kids.  Weekdays during the school year are the worst, because the zoo is a field trip staple.  I remember going at least once a year, when I was in grade school.  It's in expensive enough.  I even know people who go for an afternoon and bring lunch.  A great "something to do" in the city.

I never went to the Chalmette Battlefield as a kid. It was never a field trip destination or anything like that. The first time I went, I think I was in college and I just went because a friend of mine wanted to check it out.  I went again recently and man oh man. First of all, it was blazing hot. I know that it isn't SUPER smart to go to a vast field in the middle of the day in the middle of summer, but I never claimed to be the brightest bulb on the tree. The entire tour is pretty much self guided, at least on the weekdays. You can drive around and see the battlefield, a few cannons and a large plantation house. There is also a walking path that tells you different things about the battlefield. They also hold war reenactments every now and then and I actually wouldn't mind checking that part out.  And that's about it. I mean it's a battlefield. Men died here; pretty heavy stuff, but when you get right down to it, it's a quick visit. I wouldn't call it a "must see", if you are visiting the New Orleans area, but if you are in Chalmette, go for it. The gates are locked at 3:30.

The moment I walked into Hazelnut, I was swept away to a beautiful Christmas wonderland. They were in the process of decorating for the holidays and the decor definitely put me in the mood to do some holiday shopping. Ornaments, flatware, full service and much more are available here. They have everything to make your house or apartment feel like full luxury.  Whoever does the shopping for this store obviously has some serious taste. Everything feels high end without being overwhelmingly "fancy". The items are nice, and are still well priced and tasteful. I have a friend who collects unique ornaments, so I picked up a couple for her while I was here.  This is a great place to shop if you're looking for something a little "different"

The folks at Mobile One definitely know what they are doing when it comes to audio and other vehicle matters. They work fast, they are super clear in explaining what they will be doing and they don't charge you a crazy amount of money. I left here a happy customer.

Peewee's is a small spot, with to-go food, but it has a lot to offer. I had heard this was the spot to get good, home-cooked food, so I had to see for myself.  After hearing all the raves, I was excited to step up to the window and place my order. This is a true take-out spot: there's an order window and a few chairs for your wait. I ordered the stuffed catfish, which is fish stuffed with crabmeat, crawfish and shrimp. On Armstrong's suggestion, I got the seafood rice as my side. Of course, one of Peewee's famous crab cakes was included.  The first thing I tried was the seafood rice, which was delicious! It had shrimp and other seasonings throughout and it was spiced well. I really could have eaten an entire plate of just rice. The catfish was mouth-watering and topped with a creamy thick sauce, with a bit of spice, that was teeming with crawfish. The dish that was rich, but not overpowering. The crab cake was incredibly good. Armstrong wasn't lying when he said that he packs them with 98% crab meat -- it was hearty and almost a meal within itself. I've paid way more for crab cakes that have had way less crab and Peewee's version is the best I've had.  The owner is planning to add a patio, so that you can stay and eat, so I'm going to visit again soon.  *Portions of this review was originally written, by me, for Very Local New Orleans. Read the full story here: https://nola.verylocal.com/dont-let-the-takeout-window-fool-you-peewees-crab-cakes-are-worth-the-wait/120167/

This is the parking garage for the CBD area that also caters to a few hotels.   I've parked in here a few times and I've never had any issues. The way it works is: you park, take your ticket with you, pay on the machine downstairs upon your return, insert your ticket in the machine on the way out of the garage and you're released- in other words, you don't deal with an attendant.  I've never had any issues with this garage and paying has always been a breeze. The first 5 levels are reserved, so don't park there unless you are lucky enough to have a reserved spot. The price is good for the area and a lot of nice restaurants are within walking distance of the garage.

I stopped into Fam Bizz on a Monday after hearing raves about their red beans and rice special. It didn't disappoint. The special come with a hearty helping of red beans and rice, fried chicken, potato salad and toast.  The beans were delicious and flavorful and the fried chicken was perfect- tender and juicy. The food here is made to order, so you're going to have a wait if you didn't order ahead, but it's worth it.  I wrote more about this spot for Big Easy Magazine. Check it out here: https://www.bigeasymagazine.com/2021/07/22/1brothers-johnny-and-ronneil-williams-find-a-home-for-the-wildly-popular-food-with-new-brick-and-mortar-fam-bizz/

Wow. Okay, where to begin? Fharmacy is pretty amazing on multiple food levels.  We were here on a Monday for lunch and the place was empty except for us. I wasn't worried, I had heard glowing things about Fharmacy, so I knew I was in good hands. My friend had heard the mussels and frites were the "the bomb", so we started with that. You might be asking yourself "what's the big deal? It's mussels and french fries." Well, I'll tell you what the big deal is. First of all, the fries are the thin cut fries and they are nice and salty. The mussels are plentiful and perfectly cooked. They are generous with both portions and I could easily make a meal out of this if I wanted. Then, there's is the gravy. Yes, there is a delicious gravy that all of this goodness comes soaking in, so when you scoop out mussels and frites, you are scooping out a delicious gravy with it. I can't even explain how good it is.  I also got the Fharmacy Burger which is a burger topped with house Giardiniera, bacon jam, provolone, aioli, tomato and lettuce. You gotta look at my picture- this burger is STACKED. It was cooked perfectly and all of the yum was piled high on top of it. I could barely get all of it in my mouth in one bite. The bacon jam added a delicious layer to the burger that brought the whole sandwich to the next level.   We sat at the bar and made small talk with the owners and really enjoyed ourselves. They have a full bar, so they are a great spot for an after work drink and snack and the atmosphere was friendly. I'll be back.

I don't do fast food often, but of course, the one day I decided to go to BK there's an eternal wait. I was in the drive thru line for over 15 minutes- long enough for multiple levels of regret to seep in and wonder what I was doing with my life.  I finally got my whopper and fries and it was all okay. I hate to blame the staff, but they just didn't seem motivated to even be working.

Talk about a much overdue re-review!  I love Panera. I eat here fairly frequently and I have sampled a bit of everything from the pastries to the soups and salad. My usual "go to" order is the chicken Caesar salad. The salad is HUGE and it comes with the dressing on the side which is perfect because I never really need a lot of dressing anyway.   I'm also a really huge fan of their bagels and they have a pretty nice selection: chocolate chip, blueberry, everything, plain, asiago cheese, cherry and a few more. They also have a really good selection of pastries that are made fresh every day. It doesn't seem like a big deal that they have fresh croissants, but there are only so many places on the Westbank where you can get them.  If you sign up for their rewards program, you get all kinds of free treats like bagels and cookies.

This is a decent Dillard's, all things considered. Items are pretty well organized, they sell Michael Kors bags and sunglasses, and they have sales pretty regularly. Don't sleep on their shoe department because they have really nice things at pretty good prices. I also like that this store not only has a generous fragrance and beauty department but they have a decent MAC counter. While the MAC counter doesn't have as much as an actual MAC store, it's better than nothing.

Soooooo much fooooood. My dad and I decided to check this place out for Coolinary, because the deal they had was pretty fantastic. You get onion rings, wedge salad, your choice of a filet or NY strip steak, a side and a dessert for $40- definitely one of the better Coolinary deals in town.  First of all, they don't have menus here, the waiter just tells you what they have and you go ahead and order- very no frills. We told the waiter that we were here for the Coolinary menu, and that was all he needed to hear to get the ball rolling.  Onion rings- they brought out a ridiculously HUGE pile of onion rings that could have easily served four people. They were the thin kind, crispy and really good. This was a great start to the entire experience.  Wedge salad- the salad came out next and I decided to get mine with the house made bleu cheese dressing. They didn't hold back on this salad at all. Out came a huge wedge of lettuce, with big pieces of tomato and so much bleu cheese I was almost a little overwhelmed. I thought they were going to hold back because of the special "deal" menu, but they didn't at all. The dressing was delicious and the salad was fresh.  8oz filet- I decided to get the filet cooked medium rare. While I'm not going to sit here and tell you that this is the BEST steak I have ever had in my life, I enjoyed it. The steak came out sizzling on a metal plate, which was a nice touch. It was cooked perfectly, and although some parts of it were a little tough, I liked it enough and I wouldn't hesitate to order it again when I return.  Potatoes au gratin- this was my side. A more than generous serving of potatoes topped with mounds of melted cheese. There was so much cheese that I could barely get through it all to actually scoop out the potatoes. I ended up eating a little bit of this and taking the rest home. This was easily enough food to be shared between two people.  Spumoni- honestly, by the time I got to the spumoni, I was pretty full. Their version comes with an Italian cookie on the side. I liked the ice cream, but it didn't blow me out of the water and I found that it was pretty typical ice cream that you could get anywhere. Still, it was a nice was to close out the meal.  The waiter here was really attentive and everyone was fast about getting the food out during the busy dinner rush. The room we were in was pretty small, and when I left I smelled like smoke and steak, but that's more of an observation than a complaint. This isn't a really fancy place, so if you are in the mood for a steak don't hesitate to just drop in here and pull up a chair.

I was hungry out in Metairie and after a quick search of nearby restaurants, I decided to check out Bistro Orleans.  The place was decently filled with a "regular" type crowd on a weekday; I can tell that most of the people dining here live in the neighborhood and know the place well. I was really hungry, so I decided to get the catfish with angel hair pasta and crab meat. As I waited, some garlic bread was brought out to the table, which was a nice touch.  When my entree came out, I was blown away by how much food this is: the catfish was underneath a huge pile of pasta with a generous amount of sauce. As I dug into the food, there was so much crab meat that it was easy to spot. Sometimes you go to a place and they serve you a crab meat dish and you can barely find the meat- that wasn't the case here. The Alfredo sauce was creamy and delicious and the catfish was fried nicely and worked with the dish well.  Honestly, the catfish is almost an afterthought considering how much pasta there is, so if you're in the mood for a lot of catfish you might want to get another dish. I was really happy with the food- I thought it was a rich, hearty meal and I was starving so it was perfect for lunch (and I even skipped dinner later, because I was still full).  Bistro Orleans has a pretty extensive menu, so I'm sure I'll be back to try some of their other offerings.

Ah, Bayou St. John.  One of those little things that makes you feel as if you are in a different world.  I love the Bayou for a few reasons.  The neighborhoods that surround it are within walking distance, so if you live around there, a nice body of water is just a stroll away.  You can bring small boats or kayaks on the water.  A few years ago, I dated a guy who lived a few blocks from the Bayou and we would kayak along the Bayou on nice days.  Ok, he would kayak and I would sit there, in the kayak, like a diva, but you get what I'm saying.  It's just really nice and idyllic and really makes me want to live in Mid City someday.

This isn't a bad thrift store on St. Claude. It's pretty basic: you go in and there are just a few racks of clothes. The store is kind of strangely organized in the sense that the sizes seem to be mixed up on some of the racks. As I was looking through 4s and 6s I found random patches of 10s and 12s.   The interesting thing about this place are the prices- some of the things they carry are kind of cheap looking and they are marked $15 and up. No, that's not a lot of money, but at a thrift store I don't like to pay more than $10, unless it's something spectacular like a long dress or something. They have simple sundresses for $20 which just seems a little overpriced to me.  It's okay if you are in the area, but don't go out of your way.

Tucked away on Magazine St. is a nifty little hideaway that I had no idea even existed.  The Green House Inn is a mansion that has been converted into a lovely little "bed and breakfast" style hotel. The bottom floor has a large sitting room and leads to an outdoor patio and pool area. The upstairs is where the rooms are.  We had the Orchid room, and although it was a bit out of date- style wise, it was nice. For some reason, this room has two bathrooms, so that's worth noting if you are traveling with someone and you don't want to share a bathroom.  The biggest selling point of this place is definitely the pool. The gorgeous pool is large and comes complete with a hot tub. The pool and patio area is surrounded by greenery which really makes it feel like you are far away on an exotic vacation and the palm trees and banana trees made me feel like I was in Barbados or some far away place like that. I really enjoyed the entire atmosphere.  The staff is nice, but please note that photography is not allowed by the pool because the pool area is "clothing optional", so keep the camera phones turned off while you are relaxing.

WOOWWWWWW. How can I even describe this place? It's a snowball, but so much more.  David and I were in the mood for a snowball and he had seen this place online and it looked good, so we went on an adventure. The shop itself is really cute with an ice cream parlor type feel. The unique thing about these snowballs is that they are stuffed with cheesecake. Intrigued, I ordered the Tifffany's Blue Box because it's a wedding cake type flavor. David got the bananas foster.  My snowball was great. It was really sweet, but I like that. Buried deep inside was the cheesecake and that changed the entire snowball experience for me. Once you get a scoop of the creamy cheesecake with the icy snowball, you are sure that you're in heaven. It's the perfect combination of a little bit savory and sweet. I can't believe that more snowball stands haven't thought of this and I'm sure that I am completely spoiled for other stands from here on out.  This spot is a little pricier than your average snowball stand, but keep in mind you are getting more than just a cup of sugar ice here. Along with the cheesecake inside, you can get all kind of toppings, if that's your thing. It's more than a snowball- it's a legit dessert. I will absolutely come back and try more of their goodies.

I want to start by saying I am a complete gun novice, so this review is from the perspective of a "newbie".  A friend of mine carries a gun and, when I told him I had never even held a loaded gun, he suggested we go to the gun range for some practice. Hmm okay. Yikes. Let me start by saying I was really nervous and scared and I have a healthy fear/respect for guns. I am very aware that they are weapons that should be treated with respect.  We went in on a Saturday afternoon and there was a good number of people here. We told the guy I was new and he was super nice. I filled out all of my info in their computer, got my safety gear (ear muffs and eye protection) and headed to the range. It is LOUD in there and I jumped every time someone fired a gun, but lucky for me, I got used to the sound pretty quickly.  My friend went first, and I stood in the back and watched. Let me tell you what type of person I am: I feel better when I can observe how things work, especially if those things are new and kind of scary. Finally, it was my turn. I'll be honest- I only shot the gun once, BUT I got a head shot, so I was proud of myself (that is SO WEIRD to write). I was still a little nervous after I shot, so I decided to remain an observer for the rest of our time here.  Now that i know what to expect, I will go back and shoot more. I kind of just needed to go once and check it all out before I jumped right into shooting, you know? The staff was SO NICE and made me feel at ease. I am excited to learn more about how to properly shoot a gun and spend more time at The Shooter's Club.

Here at Très Bon, owner William "Billy" Newton is serving up all the Cajun meaty goodness you could ever crave and you're going to smell it as soon as you enter the parking lot. Très Bon's menu includes pulled pork, brisket, grit bowls, cracklins, and ribs- and that's just scratching the surface.   Their sandwiches include smoked brisket with pimento cheese, BBQ pork and slaw, and pulled pork with garlic mayo. If that's not enough for you, Très Bon offers deep fried Oreos and a Maple Bacon Sundae and they have a fridge full of sausage and other goodies packed up just waiting for you to take home- talk about "very good"!  I had the pulled pork platter with corn grits and andouille mac ($13). This platter was delicious. First of all, the portions were huge! The pulled pork was actual pulled pork and not a pile of pork shavings covered in barbecue sauce that you tend to get at some other spots. It was juicy and smoky perfection on a plate. I never think of corn grits as a barbecue side, but Très Bon is here to change all of that- creamy and rich, they were perfect with the pork. The andouille mac was in a league of its own- VERY cheesy and the andouille was a nice touch, but totally not necessary as the mac spoke for itself.  I loved the huge portions and cool atmosphere. Look around and you'll see old matchbooks on display, an extensive hot sauce collection and even vintage pinball machines. Really though, it's all about the delicious food at a great price.  I made a list of best hidden BBQ for Very Local New Orleans and this l restaurant was on it! Read it here:https://nola.verylocal.com/bbq-new-orleans/228292/

There is just something about Bustout Burlesque.  This isn't your typical burlesque. This is the show to check out if you are more interested in "classic" burlesque than "neo" burlesque. All of the dancers have gorgeous custom made glittering costumes and they perform to a live band. Watching them, you get the feeling that you are back on Bourbon St. in the 50's watching a world famous performer.  I would say that Bustout is a "must" for tourists and locals alike.

The West Bank finally has a dedicated taco spot! Paco's Tacos is here to make all of my taco dreams come true. I stopped in here on a Tuesday, and I think it was Taco Tuesday or something because when I ordered the five tacos for $10 deal, the woman who took my order through in an extra taco. Score!   I got the the Arrachera, Birria, Suadero and Chorizo tacos. It was all so good! The meat was sliced fresh and it's all made to order. They even have a salsa bar, so you can add your own fixins as you see fit. They have margaritas too, so I'm going to have to go back and try them. On Wednesdays, they have two for one margaritas, so you can get two margaritas for $12, which is pretty good.  I'm pretty excited that Paco's tacos is in the area, and I will definitely be visiting here regularly.  I wrote about this spot for Big Easy Magazine. Check it out here: https://www.bigeasymagazine.com/2021/04/28/pacos-tacos-brings-its-authentic-street-tacos-to-the-westbank/

This place is fantastic!  I am a huge fan of Mexican food and while my area has a lot of options, only a few really pique my interest. I can now add Taco Daddy's to that list. This is a small, no-frills kind of place but the food is really good.  They cover all of the bases here: they have free chips with really good salsa, they have fajitas, taco, and burritos and they have friendly service. When I went I got a burrito with pork that was fantastic! It was topped with sour cream and all of the other goodness. David got a fajita and LOVED it!  This spot is definitely going on the "regular" list and I'll be back.

It had been so long since I had eaten here, that I had forgotten what a wonderful place this is.  For starters, the atmosphere is wonderful and cozy and has a real Eastern feel.  There is a koi pond, right when you walk in, which adds a nice touch.  The food is amazing.  I got one of my faves: sweet and sour shrimp with a side of fried rice.  It was so amazing and good.  The glaze on the shrimp was the perfect combo of sweet and savory and really brought the flavor out of the lightly fried shrimp.  This isn't the place to go, if you are looking for a cheap Chinese food "take out" experience.  The reason to go here is to take your time, sit down, and enjoy your food.

This is such a fantastic shoe repair shop and the only one I would ever bring my shoes to.  I tend to buy... inexpensive shoes and they are great, but the only problem is that the tips of the heels on my high heels wear off so easily and are not made to last. Enter A B C Shoe Repair. Not only do they fix my heel tips, but they LAST. In fact, I don't think I have ever had to bring a pair of shoes in twice to be fixed.  I recently brought in some leather boots and not only were the heels fixed, but they were polished for me. Word to the wise: the first polish is done as a courtesy and kindness counts! If you don't thank them for the free polish, you won't get another one!

This store is a must if you're on any kind of budget.   You'll find highly discounted name brand and off-brand items from cereal to wine. The store is kind of just thrown together, so you might have to do a little hunting to find something specific, but if you walk through, you're sure to find something you need.  One of the best deals they have is ice cream- most boxes of ice cream bars are only about $2.00.

Gris-Gris, you have definitely cast a spell on me.  As soon as this spot opened and food groupies started raving about it, I knew I had to stop in. Lucky me, I happened to be working near Magazine during lunch and had an opportunity to try this spot.  It was early lunch on a Monday and we were seated upstairs on a pretty low key day. I immediately noticed the lovely decor and I fell in love with the hanging lights throughout the place. The mood was lovely with a classic feel. We ate upstairs, in the bar area, which was perfect because it wasn't crowded at all.  I had looked at the menu online, so I had an idea of what I wanted to eat. We started with the shrimp and fried green tomatoes and an order of complimentary red beans and rice, since we were here on a Monday. For my entree I got the shrimp and grits which comes with tail-off shrimp, smoked sausage, roasted red peppers and cherry tomatoes.  Red beans and rice: Delicious! This was a super generous portion, especially considering that it was free. If you're stopping in, pair this with an app and it makes a great lunch. Add a beer, if you're feeling squirrely. The beans were flavorful and there was even sausage in it. I was expecting sub-par red beans, only because they're free, but this was great!  Fried green tomatoes and shrimp: I love fried green tomatoes and this dish didn't disappoint. The tomatoes were nice and thick with a light batter and a yummy sauce. Again, I was really impressed with the portion size: the shrimp were huge and plentiful. I would order this again.  Shrimp and grits: Yum! Y'all know that I'm a huge fan of shrimp and grits, and this was one of the best versions that I've had. Creamy smooth grits topped with fat juicy shrimp, sausage and cherry tomatoes in a delectable sauce. Really, what kicks shrimp and grits up a notch? Sausage, always sausage. This was so rich I couldn't even finish all of it and I enjoyed the rest later. This is a "must" order- you won't regret it.  The staff was really friendly, and although the waiter was being pulled in different directions, our food came out quickly and he stayed on top of the drink refills. I want to go back for dinner and try the chicken and dumplings and get the full dinner experience because I feel that it's probably pretty special.

I had one of the most romantic dates of my life here and I am so excited to tell you all about my Irene's experience.  Okay, so we didn't make reservations, but I'm glad we didn't because I think it made the experience even better. When you arrive they send you to a back room so that they can put your name on the list for a table. The back room is full of magic with a piano player, small tables and drink service. Trust me, you want to go to the back room. After we put our name on the list, we sat, chatted and drank wine. After a while, we were lead to our table in the small dining room.  I loved how cozy this was and we were seated in a corner, so we were away from the hustle and bustle of the rest of the room. Everything on the menu sounded so amazing and we decided to start with a order of Oysters Irene, which is grilled oysters topped with cheese and tomato sauce. This dish was out of this world, full of flavor and a perfect start to the meal.  For my entree, I had the shrimp papardelle (on this evening, soft shell crab was replaced with shrimp). Five huge tail-on shrimp came out on a bed of delicious papardelle mixed into a yummy cream sauce. When I say that this dish blew my mind, I'm not lying. WOW. The flavor was just incredible and the entire meal warmed me right up. For dessert, we split an order of the pecan pie dessert which was dangerous with a side of ice cream. Again, this dish knocked my socks off. The freshness of the entire thing and the flavors made for a perfect end to this experience.  The wait staff here is, of course, extremely professional and on top of everything. They are attentive and are sure to keep an eye on drinks and check in as the evening progresses. Irene's is one of my new favorite spots in the city and I am putting it in my "top 10" of places to recommend to local and visitors alike, when looking for a nice place to dine. I will definitely return.

I love Bath and Body works because they have a lot of neat little beauty products that are really nice and not out of this world expensive.  I think that my favorite thing to get here is the Japanese Cherry Blossom perfume. It has been a favorite of mine for years, and about once a year they switch up the scent to keep it new and interesting. I'm not sure if they do that for other products, but as an avid Cherry Blossom fan for years, that is something that I've noticed.  They also have a lot of gift baskets and things like that that are perfect for birthdays, anniversaries and Christmas.

Wow. This is a really nice Rouses. I love the layout and it feels like a real fresh market. I stopped in here with a friend to pick up some things to make for dinner. Everything here is really fresh and seems to be well priced, just like any Rouses. They have a huge deli selection and a large cheese case, which you know I'm a fan of.  Pretty respectable beer selection. Found a few rare bottles here and a huge walk in fridge with 6 packs and cases. Super convenient for anyone who lives uptown.

Say you decide that you need a new door...and you only have $35.  Where do you go?  the Green Project.   Or you have a bunch of left over building supplies, random bits of lumber, some roofing materials, maybe even some paint?  Where can you bring it so it doesn't end up in a landfill?  Again, the Green Project.

I usually go to Superior because other people want to...like my brother and his kids.  It's a good place to bring children because it's so loud you don't have to worry about your noisy ones disturbing other folks' meals.  The cocktails are free flowing and the food's OK.

Yay a new ice cream shop...which has only been open a couple of weeks. The space is small but I like the sparkly booth seats.   The ice cream selection is small but there is definitely something for everyone. I had the peach vanilla and it was fresh and tasty. My only small point was that the peaches bits were large so they got a bit icy to the tooth. But that's probably me just being a weirdo. My friend loved her toasted coconut and it was yummy.   The business is cash only and supposedly also has snowballs but I didn't see anyone get those while I was there.

I had an our to kill before meeting some friends so I stopped in for a cup of tea and a snack. Unfortunately, they were out of the tea I wanted so I settled for another type. And the spinach-feta pastry that I had was yummy; I wish it could have been toasted rather than heated in the microwave.  The staff was nice and apologetic about the missing tea. The space indoors is cozy, but the tables are pretty well spaced. The front patio area is spacious...if sitting near Veterans Hwy is your sort of thing.  So let's discuss why this shop gets 3 not 4 stars. The parking lot SUCKS. Because the space has a drive through, parking spaces are almost non-existent. And all the nearby businesses have threatening signs about parking in their lots with dire consequences promised.

Oh my, when we said we were going to Franklin my friend's younger daughter asked us to stop by this candy shop for her favorite...  And they had some super tasty stuff. Loved the self serve jars. They had cute displays for Easter when I was there.  And I was able to buy bulk Spree (which I am NEVER allowed to do again) and some old school satellites (like communion wafers filled with candy) and some fancy chocolates.  Really cute addition to the area.

The other big french bread bakery in the city.  They don't get the press or the market share of Leidenheimer's but are still really good.  Again, this is the bakery, but they may have a retail store where you can actually purchase items...at least they did once upon a time.  Look for Binder's at your local grocery.

Since I was just chatting about this new bakery over on twitter, I guess I'll finish my review...  The space is small and they do have dine in tables (but no liquor license if you're here for brunch...but they do have mixers I'm told if you bring your own).  The staff was courteous and prompt.   But on to the important stuff. The $1 croissant bites are genius. They melt in your mouth with buttery deliciousness but still have a bit of a crunch on the edges. I hate a mushy croissant. I also tried the mixed berry and apple turnovers. They were perfectly sized and the mixed berry was clearly the winner being tart and not too sweet. The apple was good to but the berry was amazing.  As I'm not a coffee person I got a perfectly tasty iced tea and was out the door.  The one thing that is lacking is their signage. Maybe it's building rules or maybe they just haven't gotten there yet. But blink and you'l miss them. They are riverside on Magazine between General Pershing and Milan...so dangerously close to home.  I'll be back soon...

Y'know how you have that impossible person on your gift list and you really have no idea what to buy them. BUT lucky for you, they are obsessed with their pet.  This is the place to buy them a gift.  Yes, it is mostly doggie stuff but I have found items for the cat lovers in my life.    Plus you can bathe your own dog here in their self-service bathtub which is up on a platform which really could save your back.

Maple Street is not on my usual weekend path, but I've stopped by this bakery the last few times I've been over that way.  Delicious apple turnover, almond croissants, and cheese danish/turnover/thingy.  I even bought my Mom a Thanksgiving cupcake with plastic turkey on top - old school.    My only criticism is I wish they had a true vegetarian sandwich on their lunch menu.

I'm still a big fan of Il Posto (and the currrent duchess, thank you very much), but thought I would update my review based on my observations last night.  Tuesday & Wednesday nights from 5-8 and around 7 last night (a Tuesday) a small herd of cute 20-something gals all came strolling in. They weren't one big group either. So as my public service to single men of the appropriate age, go check it out.

Cute selection of upscale shoes (and even in my baby feet size!) and handbags. The sales person was helpful without being pushy and actually seemed occupied by store tasks rather than her cellphone!    The costume jewelry and other accessories were fun too.  Also, this one of the locations where you can check out Dominque Giordano's creations in person since her shop across the street is shut down.

Just bought a great box of fresh, organic produce: blood oranges, strawberries, frisee, lettuce, mushrooms, etc.  I love that they are trying to buy local and it's great service.  Wonderful use of the old Guilliot's nursery.  Check them out!   Open every Saturday from 10-2.

Yelp's own Andrea B wanted to have a UYE (unofficial yelp event) and this is where we ended up and we were treated (yes, treated, I say!) to our girl BELTING out Welcome to the Jungle.  Please do see the pic I posted, but really it doesn't do justice.    Best of all, there was a random drag queen bake sale going on & I scored an excellent apple pie.    No I wasn't brave enough to sing myself...maybe next time.  Being a native, St. Claude was the last place I expected to find such a great club, but it's an avenue that's turning around.  Seriously, a dragon (a real one not a costume) could walk into Kajun's and take turn on the stage and no one would bat an eye.  Minus 1 star for the billowing cigarette smoke.

Made it to Luke's for dinner and the crabmeat ravioli is AMAZING.  However I'm knocking off a star because the place was a zoo.    The next table was a 50th birthday party of 9 adults; one of the women was literally yelling at the top of her voice.  With tile/hardwood floors and tin ceilings, the volume in the restaurant almost ruined our meal.  It was exceedingly difficult to carry on a conversation at our table of 5 in between the shrieks next to us.    Other dishes at our table were the redfish (w/ the crabmeat), the vanilla duck, shrimp & grits, and the shrimp farci.  Everyone thought their food was lovely...if only the atmosphere had been as nice.

I was on a mission of mercy and picked up dog food (not in my neighborhood) for a friend.  The staff was really nice and repeatedly offered to carry the bag of food to the car. The prices seemed compatible with big box chains, but this is a locally owned store.  (The original is in my childhood neighborhood). PLUS you get the convenience of down the street, well y'know if you're my friend.  Nice selection of doggie items, collars, treats, food, etc. I didn't look at cat stuff.

Oh look it's been 3 years since I last reviewed Fairy...  You know a shop is great when you become friends with the owner. Elizabeth has many years of retail/clothing experience and it shows in the great eye she has for the styles and lines she carries. Not everything is to my taste (we will never agree about pre-ripped jeans), but there are always quite a few things to tempt me. The sale rack in the back is typically full of bargains. She carries GREAT and affordable accessories and I love the sunglasses she carries, so much so that I currently am rotating 3 pairs.   Love that she supports other small business owners via trunks shows for various local jewelry, hat, purse makers. And, of course, Toulouse is a great shop ambassador.   Hey Yelp - can I give Fairy 17million stars?

Looking for a treasure? Or a questionable collectible? Or maybe an Infant of Prague statue? Or even a vintage Mr. Bingle? This might be the store for you.   Yes, it's super cluttered and it's set up in individual booths and getting someone with the right key to the right case can be a bit challenging. But if you find the exact pitcher you used to use in your grandmother's kitchen for about $20, then it's worth it.  I hate that you have to check your bags...but browsers aren't always honest so I get it.  Although I would say this is not the place to go if you have major dust allergies, but you already knew that.

Santa Fe on Frenchmen has moved to Esplanade Ave. The cocktails were lovely as was the outdoor seating.  We only had appetizers but both were well plated an delicious.    Plus we were serenaded my fellow diners who were inspired by the 80s soundtrack playing on the sound system.  I think they may have had one too many of the margaritas.

And the veggie pho is delicious...in case you were wondering, as is the spicy tofu appetizer.    I've also tried their grilled shrimp items and YUMMY.  Love that the place is so low key and that you are greeted like you've just arrived at your favorite aunt's house.

Hmmm...to write a review of lucky dogs or to not. Full disclosure, I last ate a lucky dog in high school so maybe a couple of decades ago. But I am a big fan of the carts and love that they exist.  If you're a hot dog lover, you should definitely have one. Rumor has it that the stand closest to Jackson Square is always the cleanest. And if you are leaving NOLA without having indulged, there's a cart on at least one of the concourses.  If you haven't read Managing Ignatius by Jerry Strahan, add it to your New Orleans book list. It's a memoir not fiction, because who could make some of this stuff up.  I will warn you that if you read it, and you're from here, it'll make you really miss orange julius.  OMG! I just discovered their online shop. Lucky Dog gifts for everyone! http://www.luckydogs.us/shop/index.cfm

I'm so glad this is a restaurant space again. Pre-K I went to Christian's often and it was nice to back inside this churchy location.    The food was wonderful. I started with a lovely mixed green salad with a pungent & delicious blue cheese. And then had the stuffed baked shrimp withe hominy cakes. Seriously tasty. My dining companion had a very lemony/anchovy-y caesar salad (and I mean that in a good way) and then stuffed salmon with gnocchi and asparagus. Since I sampled her food too, I thought the gnocchi were a bit heavy, but still delicious.  Then for dessert? AMAZING dark chocolate creme brulee. Seriously y'all, I love fancy chocolate pudding and this was the fanciest (and tastiest).  Only off note was that our server was struggling. The restaurant was busy because of superbowl weekend, but we never did get to hear the specials and had to ask for more bread.  Not that big of a deal really, especially when you view it in light of AMAZING dark chocolate creme brulee.

This is a solid neighborhood bar that is spacious and has MLB season pass (if that's important to you). I would hang out here alot except y'know the smoking.   The liquor is well priced, the bartenders are on point, the clientele is diverse and welcoming. But dang do they smoke.  I've heard their trivia night is outstanding. And just as a note about the women's restrooms, they are spacious (not palatial) but you don't feel trapped and feature my all time dive bar favorite...plywood stalls. Love some industrious carpentry. PLUS they have old high school prom pictures to make you laugh.   OK I just changed my review rating from 3 (because of the smoke) to 4 (because of the prom pictures).  Sometimes it's the little things...

Love the curry fried rice. Seriously why isn't this a standard on every menu?  And my friend had the mango shrimp salad special; it was fresh and delicious.  And the lack of a liquor license has been confirmed.  I think the liquor behind the bar is just there to tease you.  Plus I have been corrected; the 2 Singhas are the same owners. So, yay, for expansion!

Yeah it's a chain but it's very special diet friendly. If you're a veggie or a vegan or gluten free, they have something for you.  The food is pretty good quality for a chain and I like being able to customize to my exact taste...although I'm sure the servers want to throw something at me. "I'd like 1 tablespoon of this and a smidge of that..." OK I'm really not that bad.  I like being able to refill my own beverage too.

Wow! The new sports areas are amazing! Went out last night to catch my niece's soccer game and I couldn't believe how that end of the park was transformed.  A great addition to an already good space.  Now if we just could do something about the extreme leash laws...my 13 yr old dog isn't wandering away or going to do anything besides collapse.

I used my Living Social deal to go visit Christine at Skin Studio yesterday.  Wow.  Her approach is much more clinical and scientific (rather than crunchy granola) compared to previous facials.  We discussed my skin issues, my care regime (such as it is), and my goals.  She gave me multiple options based on my stated goals from very basic to more advanced.    Basically, if I want my skin to be different than it is, I have to stop being lazy. HMMMM something to consider.  I can really see the difference in my skin today.

Ha! Christy L beat me on this review.    I take my Mom to shop here at least once a year, just so she can walk around and be astonished at the prices people pay for stuff she still has.  But really you could tell me you bought just about anything from this place and I would believe you.  My fave gift from here is an Infant of Prague religious statue.  My fave purchase was a decade old Mr. Bingle.

I finally got to try this food truck outside NOMA one evening with my Mom. We had the Bootz and the Rachel. The Rachel was the definite winner of the two; it had pesto, truffle aioli, provolone, smoked gouda and tomato. The Bootz was good too (colby, swiss & cheddar on sourdough) but it was just pale in comparison to the Rachel. Two sandwiches were the best of both worlds though so we could each have a half.   Price point was good and the sandwiches came up quickly. Will definitely hit them up again for cheesie goodness.

I stopped in for lunch here while shopping with my Mom on Magazine Street. And the staff was lovely and attentive. The space is really open and attractive.  The food was good and the prices were inexpensive compared to other Vietnamese places. And the food is more traditional than some of the other spots uptown/garden district.   I had veggie avocado spring rolls and they were perfect. My Mom had a small pho (which was huge for her) and she really enjoyed it. I also had the bun with tofu and it was OK.   There were definitely regulars who must be in all the time since they were greeted and asked if they wanted their usual dishes, which I would appreciate if I were a regular. The porch seating seemed to be dog friendly too.  The steps were a bit steep and my Mom did struggle with them a little but she had been walking all over the place for a few hours.

A friend randomly chose this restaurant since none of us had ever been before. The decor is...charming but odd. The faux french quarter balcony feels weird when you're just a few miles up river from the real deal, but it's well done and the starry sky is lovely.  We started with cocktails and the oysters rockefeller and the crab cakes meuniere. The oysters were amazing; the addition of brie is genius. The crab cakes were fine but I wasn't as blown away by them as my friends were.  I had a trout special, one friend had the trout long beach and the other steak with sauteed mushrooms. What isn't clear from the online menu, is that when you order an entree, you get a starter and a side. I had a salad which was ok and gratin potatoes. My fish was amazing and the best thing about my night. The salad and gratin potatoes were OK but nothing special. My friends loved both of their meals.  We got a couple of desserts (Yelp checkin deal!). I got what was advertised as a doberge cake...which it wasn't but was a delicious, rich, dense, delicious chocolate cake. And also bread pudding which was served beautifully but differently in slices, rather than in a square or a ramekin.   Service was good but no obtrusive. There was a preseason Saints game on so we knew when a big play was made, since you can hear Monkey Hill next door...if they're loud enough. Sadly, we only heard that once or twice on that evening. (Geaux Saints anyway...le sigh).

Hmm...I ended up here after a show at HoB since my friends really wanted to hang out with the band and they had given us passes. I'm not really a velvet rope kind of girl so that part kind of annoyed me. It's a bar that charges huge prices for drink and you have to be invited in (or you have to a member or something).   The decor is cool and there was a DJ with accompanying horn player spinning an eclectic selection of music. There's a couple of different spaces (including a VIP area) to escape the music and dancers.  Then there was the crowd. It was bizarre. There was a definite sugar daddy/much younger woman thing happening. Maybe it is the velvet rope thing...people seemed really stoked to be in the space. I don't know. I like weird spaces. But the crowd just didn't do it for me. My friend who got us in acted like she was in hell...until the band showed up and she got to geek out. Then all was right with the world.

It makes me sad to discover that this classic bar is now a daiquiri shop. The great thing about stopping at this old school narrow bar was that the drinks were well made, the clientele was reasonable and you were able to use the hotel's nice bathroom.    Now it's just a sad, sad, sad bastion of machines and neon and no access to the hotel that houses it. Blah.

Time for a re-review of this spot. While it still has all juice snoballs (current favorite is pineapple mint), they've expanded into smoothies and fancy juice mixes. As well as paninis (although I've never ordered one at the shop).  There is usually just one person working inside but they'll tell you if they are running any specials...like satsuma juice. The prices are affordable considering the quality.  My only annoyance is that I really can't tell if they are open from the street and they used to be less than consistent with their hours but that seems to be getting better.

I had not been on the Natchez for a cruise since grade school and guess what? It's as fun as I remember (even without the getting out of class/field trip aspect).    I didn't sign up for the YSB cruise since my oldest/dearest BFF was coming into town for a convention the next week for a conference. I had helped him decide on some of the social events, including one on the Natchez.  So I got to cruise the river at night with a bunch of engineers...and explain the food to some of them.  While there were many bars set up all over the boat for this event, the main bar had the best selection of liquor in case you're a brand snob AND for this event, the conference had booked Sunpie Barnes and the Louisiana Sunspots, so much fun!  The food was yummy! My BFF even compared their gumbo to his grandfather's! High praise. I enjoyed the caprese salad on a stick, the passed spanokopitas and the shrimp creole,  The mini-muffalatas and the bananas foster were big hits too!  So on the river, I loved watching the city glide by and the engineers were pretty impressed with boat turning around since the captain let the river handle part of it rather than using fuel to do so.  MUST DO! Stand at the very back and get splashed by the paddle wheel! Makes me feel like a kid again when we were allowed to file past (making sure none of us fell) to feel the water on my skin.

I usually pop in here when heading over to Elmwood for a movie or shopping.  For a sushi joint in a strip mall, they are really good.  They have items on their menu that the Magazine St. location has dropped (like their delicious inari).  Service can be sketchy because I think they hire local HS students, but it's OK.

So I'm not sure why this place has uptown in the name when it's clearly in the Garden District. But that's just me being picky.  I stopped in during the 1st weekend of carnival season and they were serving a limited menu and all orders were handled at the bar. No problem.  I ordered a couple of bahn mis for me & my family and they came out quickly. Both sandwiches (grilled shrimp and tofu) were delicious and huge!   Staff was very nice and gave me a huge glass of ice water which was much needed on that warm first Sunday.   4 stars for life-giving food during carnival. Now I'll just have to get back over there for a meal when they have regular service.

The DIS location that I had been using near Touro closed. So I wasn't thinking when I made my appointment and had to drive out to the Metrys.   The location is fine and efficient. The front office was crowded but they were hustling people through. Technician was quick and professional. Test results were communicated quickly.  My biggest problem is the parking lot. I don't know who designed this strip mall but the parking is a pain. Thank goodness my appointment was after lunch because finding a spot during prime meal times is impossible.

Il Posto is a great alternative to a typical heavy NOLA lunch.  Light sandwiches, soups, and salads are the main event.  Although the pastries are pretty tempting.  Breakfast items are limited to bagels, hard boiled eggs, and occasionally quiche.  GREAT environment.

I'm very torn about this restaurant. First it's BEAUTIFUL. Really the views from the window are stunning and the grounds are really lovely.  BUT my food was just OK and after making a point about saying no meat (especially in Catholic Louisiana on Good Friday), they served me dirty rice with my stuffed crab. The stuffed crab was OK; the dirty rice, I gave away and then there was a side vegetable, sweet cooked carrots which were again OK. But not enough food for the price. The garlic bread was yummy.   Our server was nice. I felt bad for the hostess who kept having to check the men's room for occupancy since the ladies' room was out of order. The inside of the restaurant is pleasant. I just wish the food had been as good as the views.

Because Dorothy Y wrote a review, I'm going to offer a differing opinion.  As someone who grew up in the shadow of the Huey P, I have a lingering affection for it.  Yes, it's old & sways, but rickety?  I'll trust a bridge built in the 30s over one built in the cost cutting 80s any day.    It was a right of passage to drive over the Huey P after getting your driver's license and be terrorized by 18-wheelers passing you on the narrow bridge.  You had to be sure not to hit them or the curb and once you survived, you felt like a real driver.

Wow. What a beautiful park! The landscaping is gorgeous and when everything grows in it will really be lovely. There are definitely sections that are still works in progress...the lawns that are still mostly rocks and dirt and of course the unfortunate burned wharf that was part of the original design until...yknow fire.  I was really glad that the city allowed the park to be open after dusk for the fireworks on the 4th. It was a great relaxed spot to watch.  Disadvantages would include that their only 2 entrances (3 by the end of the year) which makes for bottlenecks. And then their is the extreme steepness of the Piety Street entrance stairs...kind of brutal when you're carrying your picnic supplies. I felt bad for the folks with little kids/strollers.   Can't wait to see what happens next with this great new park.

My caveat is that I have never stayed in a room here, but I have attended meetings and used the facilities.   The staff is great.  I have never had a rude person and everyone is courteous and professional.  The meeting rooms are lovely and well appointed.

Love this little bridge that crosses Bayou St. John which is pedestrian only... But I have seen people bike across. It's the perfect spot to stop and contemplate the sky and the water or chat with a friend.  There have been various threats to tear it down but the community always rallies to stop the demolition. And it has been proven to be structurally sound for people.  Take a moment and walk around Bayou St. John and then stop on the bridge, perhaps with your favorite beverage and just be. You won't regret it.

After reading all my friends' 5 star reviews, I was expecting to be wowed, but the drinks I tasted (during Tales so maybe they were overworked?) were all way too sour. We had the classic Mai Tai, a Hurricane and ...something smokey tasting. The hurricane was actually the best of the drinks. The mai tai was so sour that it tasted more like a margarita, definitely not what I was expecting.   As for the atmosphere, it's very warehouse-y with a bunch of decorations slapped around. And while there was table service, they were a bit overwhelmed while I was there. The prices are good for the size of the drinks.  Maybe I just need to go back when it's not Tales.

Ummm YUM! These are the most delicious daiquiris I've ever had out of a machine. Yes the Jennifer B is correct the strawberry-chocolate (a mix) is delicious. My friend got the strawberry-margarita with an extra shot of tequila for a only a bit more.   I've never used the drive through...mostly because the building confuses me. And the space is clearly a neighborhood bar for lots of folks.  I just wish it wasn't so far away from my house...or maybe it's good that it's on the other side of town from me.

Wow! My lips just stop tingling from the spicy awesomeness that was the chili noodle.  Delish! We also had the Panang Curry and the fried spring rolls.  All the food was fresh and yummy.  The atmosphere was really light, airy and open.  I guess I haven't been inside this space since it was a coffee shop over a decade ago and it still had a house configuration back then.  So the renovation may not be new to this restaurant but I really like it.  The menu has a lot of variety without being too long. And they state that they will customize any dish even making stuff vegan.  The Chili Noodles normally have chicken or beef, but I got them with fried tofu, but I also could have picked soft.  It looks like they have a liquor license now since behind the bar they're was the biggest bottle of knob creek that I've ever seen. mmmm bourbon.  Also, the name is really Singha Song Thai so I'm guessing they aren't affiliated with the Singha downtown. I submitted the change to our Yelp overlords so I guess it will changed eventually.

I'm torn about the Howling Wolf...I remember it's origins out in Metairie and it's open mike nights. (WOOO Fat City!) And then it's second incarnation in the warehouse district. And now it's current location (which is really like 3 businesses in one), so I guess I feel it's a bit more fractured then it used to be.  There's the bar (ooh just checked the website... officially this is the Den) that serves food and is a great place to chill. There's the backroom where I've seen comedy and gone to random events. And there's the large music hall.   I do really enjoy the bar and if I lived nearby, this might be my hangout. They serve food (always a plus) but the menu is pretty meaty. They do sell Mrs. Wheat's meat pies but only the crawfish and beef ones. The atmosphere is right and the drinks are well poured.  The backroom is intimate and mostly just a big empty space so that's cool. I seem to remember an anti room too. Clearly I was paying lots of attention when I went to my friend's comedy show here.   Finally the big room...it's really big and the acoustics are pretty decent. There are some odd bits of decorations around the sidelines which are used when it's rented out as an event space I think. But they just add to the general chargm.

Cute clothes at much more reasonable prices than you would think for a boutique on magazine.  Bought a cocktail dress with only hours to spare and received complements on it all night.  The owner is super nice too.

mmmm...a choc-work orange, so good.  Flavors to please everyone in the family from the gourmand to the 6 year old.    This ice cream parlor does traditional bar service in the location of the original McKenzie's Bakery location (and they've left the old neon sign earning eternal love from many New Orleanians).

I still think the clothes at Fairy are really cute and, yes, Toulouse demonstrating his love for me is a draw.  Love the owner and while the stock is not necessarily my style all the time, I almost always find something cute that I need to buy.  My only issue is that some of the lines that the store carries are ridiculous about sizing. If a large equals a size 8 then that's a problem. So I just stick to other lines that are human sized.  Love the accessories too.

This has been E's go to tow truck company since the 80s (when he drove a 50s vintage car that needed a lot of towing). This morning they responded promptly to our houseguest who's car decided to give up the ghost last night.  The dispatcher was a bit confused, but the driver arrived promptly (within 20 minutes of the call). And was courteous.  Not sure if they take plastic or not.  My houseguest paid with a check.

When I lived in Old Jefferson, this was my go to independent repair shop and its where my parents still go.  I always found them to be honest and above board as well as getting me my car back when promised.  It's an old neighborhood gas station (the elderly man who owned it in my childhood fixed my bike on occasion for free) and you can't miss because they decorate with inflatables on the roof for every holiday.  I don't use them any longer because I tend to use a repair shop in my neighborhood.

I was wandering along Esplanade when I realized I was in dire need of hydration so I stopped in for a well-brewed and inexpensive iced tea.   The outdoor space is wonderful and the indoor seating looked very comfy. On this gorgeous Saturday afternoon the space was pretty full but seating could still be had.   The barista was friendly and looked grateful that I just wanted a simple iced tea. If I lived closer I would definitely be a regular.

It's funny that tee-niny little Surrey's has 189 reviews (yay #190).  The place is small so expect a wait, but the servers are efficient and the food comes out quick.  The menu is inventive and much of my breakfast was delicious.  What did they make those grits with? Crack? Yum.  The only low point was my biscuit.  I LOVE a good southern biscuit. Mine was more like hardtack.  The banana pancake (which I kept picking at off of E's plate) was amazing and bigger than my head.  Lots of vegetarian and vegan options along with supermeaty ones too.

A solid choice for ice cream or sherbet (if you're at this end of Magazine), but there isn't a huge selection...but maybe that's good for the indecisive? I had blueberry something and it was really tasty.  The staff seemed...friendly but indifferent.    Since I've seen a bunch of businesses come and go on this block, I admire how the current folks have dressed up this location.  The design aesthetic is clean and welcoming.  I'll have to try the shave ice to compare it to a snowball.    I'll leave y'all to the bubble teas; tapioca freaks me out.

I'm a big fan of Lafayette Square these days. It's actually being kept clean and is a welcome respite of green in the midst of a lot of concrete.  Plus it's the location of a number of events from the Wednesdays at the Square music series to the Seafood festival to the Blues & BBQ Fest.

Lunches coffee pastry & its in the library? Yes, please. I stopped in for a quick water and some yummy banana bread on my way to sit at a car repair place. But I'll definitely be back. The sandwich menu looked tasty. And the seating while not plentiful was well appointed. I also like that it is separate from the library (no drinks around the books!)

Bacchanal really is a lovely slightly bohemian place to share a bottle of wine and chat with friends. Yes the mosquitos are ridiculous and it is nice that there are bottles of bug spray scattered about...but how about hanging some sort of deterrent devices around the perimeter? I would love to see an old school purple bug zapper. (Do they even make those anymore?)  The wine selection is good and the food is tasty and diverse.  I'm also grateful for the diversity of non-alcoholic beverages that can be purchased for the non-drinker/underaged patron.  My only other bit advice is be careful with some of the chairs which are perhaps not as sturdy as one would like, even for the slightly built.

Still a great value and a GREAT place to donate used or unnecessary building supplies. Since my last review, I've dropped off paint, paint and more paint, light fixtures, ceiling fans, a bathtub, sinks, the entire contents of my parents' condemned garage.  The staff has always been great, helping us unload and asking questions about our donations. They were very impressed with my Dad's castoff collection of homemade tool boxes.    Watch for paint drop off locations at alternate locations too. I've dropped off paint and both Hollygrove Market and Whole Food Uptown.

I just love the new space, so much larger and airier than the tee-niny shop they had on Maple.  Love the expanded collection of vintage clothing and coats. And all the purses, oh my.  They are really good about buying vintage items from collectors (a friend has sold them jewelry, furs, purses and clothes). The owner does have a great eye and she's very easy to work with.  The staff member that was in the store when I stopped in a couple of weekends ago was lovely and the space is very conducive to browsing.  Great addition to Magazine Street.

Ultimately, I decided the Skin Studio wasn't for me. I think Christine does great work, but since my issue wasn't acne (which is her main focus), I ultimately wasn't sure where we were going.  I'm not one to get chemical peels or any injectable and so ultimately,  I think this spot was too medically oriented for me.  Maybe I do need the crunchy granola touch instead.

Parcels & post is an interesting retailer; yes you can rent mailboxes here and mail packages and buy stamps. But they also have a fairly eclectic (some would say random) selection of retail items as well.  And they always give me options on shipping my packages.  Almost forgot, most important, they have a parking lot behind the store that is accessible off of Nashville ave.

I realized that I never updated my review of this place. I never did go back for another cut.  The cut I was given was expensive and didn't really work with my hair texture.    So your mileage may be different, I was just underwhelmed and have moved on.

What a wide variety of stuff... Loved that they carried a lot of costume gear (new and used) before Halloween; really smart of them.  I've tried on some really wacky & some really practical stuff.  Just go in and be prepared to dig.  I probably won't try to go back on a Saturday though...what a madhouse.

When the big box home improvement don't have the wood you need, then this is the place to find the odd bits necessary to complete your NOLA home improvement project.  They, of course, do sell the general items like 2x4s or sheets of plywood, but the real draw is stuff like tongue & groove flooring to match the rotten bits in your 100+ year old house. Or picture molding, or base shoe of the correct diameter.  These tings matter. Staff is knowleadgeable and helpful.

Gorgeous renovation and the food is usually good and downhome. The space has been closed for 6 months (maybe more?) for a thorough renovation. When we went today, my chief problem with the restaurant was still not fixed...you come out smelling like food. I thought the issue was with the ventilation system but maybe they didn't upgrade that. Sometimes it's OK to smell like fried the rest of the day...and then again sometimes it's not.  The servers are all at risk youth so don't expect white glove fancy pants service. But they honestly are trying so that goes along way with me.  Since this was only their 1st or 2nd week back open since the renovation the service was bit disordered but the place was slammed. I

Well I guess I'll go ahead and write their last review. Only open a few years, but they're closing up shop at this location.   My facialist Nikki just landed here in the last few months and I know she enjoyed the space. I booked an appointment here a few weeks ago and when I arrived I was told it was their last week of services. Final day is tomorrow February 24.   The space is lovely and very relaxing. Nikki is always great. I'm sorry to see that they are closing.

I'm not big on this store BUT it's where you can recycle electronics. I dropped off my old CPU (minus the hard drive of course) and a damaned monitor and an old non-working DVD player. You can recycle it all here.  So that's AOK in my book.

The only pieces that I've purchased from Guthrie Rinard are his Barkus posters  (http://www.barkus.org/store/)   But I love those & I can't wait to learn this year's theme.  His pieces are fun & playful and his staff as always been courteous & professional.

Went with friends who ordered absinthe which is their other specialty besides vodka.  I, of course, had vodka instead...lime flavored vodka.    Once again it was great civilized place to cool your heels and have a cocktail in the FQ.  Although I did think the Rasputin painting was watching me the whole time...but I'm cool, so I pretended not to care.

So a car ran a stop sign... wait, no, she said she stopped at the stop sign and I wasn't there so she zoomed out and ran into me... who knew my car had the power to materialize out of thin air? And while it was minor accident... no injuries, my airbag didn't deploy, her child was in car seat, thank goodness. My poor car had a jacked bumper, hood, quarter panel & light kit. So I limped home and called my insurance and this location was one of the recommended State Farm body shops. OK. I saw that Harry was a fan and one of my car-guy coworkers likes them too. Sold.   Communication was excellent. I dropped my car over the weekend so called them Monday morning. They explained the insurance estimate process to me. And everything went smoothly. Seriously, I emailed them with questions and they answered promptly... I can't even get that sort of response time from other offices, much less a mechanic.  The car was ready when they told me and they washed and vacuumed it so it looks great!

It's conveniently located and I can get multiple services in one location, so that makes me a fan.  Oil change was done on a rainy day so I got a raincheck for the carwash...which was only valid for around 30 days.  Car wash was fine and the oil change was quick.  On a previous occasion, there were windshield repair folks on hand to patch the dinks in my glass...for an added fee, of course. Didn't see them this time.  I was entertained by the children who were being amused by the birds & lizards inside the lobby.  So bonus points for them.
