The guy who answered the phone seemed surprised to hear they had voicemail that he was maybe supposed to check.   I ordered the cupcakes and was told that I had to pay in advance. OK. Telling him my credit card number was another bit of ridiculousness since he couldn't remember the numbers long enough to write them down.  Fast forward to pickup. My dozen cupcakes are ready but the couple extra are nowhere. There is a box on top of mine, but it is empty. They are, of course, sold out of the flavor of the extra cupcakes...wedding cake because y'know anniversary party. The girl just stares at me and says she doesn't know what to do. After a couple of beats, I just ask for my money back. She brightens and says sure she can do that.  Next time I'll use a store that actually has employees who care. OTH, they clearly don't need my business because their display case was nearly empty at 5:15 on a Friday.

This is one of 6 parts of Jean Lafitte National Park.  It is a fabulous outdoor hiking space that is so close to downtown that tourists cannot believe they just left the city.  In the spring, you can go for the irises.  You can see wildlife all year.  Definitely worth the 20 minute drive.

Love the new menu!   Last night I had the crawfish lobster roll; as a NOLA native, I wasn't really sure what I was supposed to do with the serving of melted butter (after dipping my fries and bun in it). The crawfish were plump and delicious and the bun was nicely toasted. Also let's not underestimate the deliciousness of a well cooked fry. I love fresh cut fries with the skin still on; these were fried perfectly.    I also swiped a smidge of my friend's mac n cheese. mmmmmm....smoked gouda. And another friend got the fish and chips; the beer batter looked amazing all puffy, golden brown. I was too full to sample his though.  The price point is excellent, especially for the FQ. The drinks run to the sweet side but the bartenders are happy to adjust for individual taste. (I'll ask for an extra shot of bitters in my old fashioned next time.)  Love the atmosphere and the exposed brick walls. A really well designed space that is casual with elevated food. Definitely worth a visit or 7.

Yes this business is a spin-off/branch/non-profit venture from the District Donuts folks. And it is a non-profit: http://www.districtstreetcar.com/about   The Streatcar (that purposeful typo is hard to type) was near my work today so I my coworker and scarfed down some tasty treats. I had the tofu slider and she had the cheeseburger & fries (waffle style!).  The service was fast and my tofu slider was delicious...check my photo. My coworker's waffle fries were super tasty and well-fried because you know I had to help her with those. She said her burger was super tasty but was perhaps a little pink for her. And, of course, I had to get a cinnamon sugar donut which is yummy.   The streetcar is the sort that I remember as a tourist conveyance in the 80s so it's cool to see that style back on the street.

This is another great program to educate at risk youth that also servers some awesome food. It's been on my list to check out for some time and last week, I finally made it over there with a couple of coworkers.  Two of us had the shrimp and grits (each of us asked for an ingredient left out) and they were fine about that. The third got the chicken club...while it wasn't a traditional club, she loved it.  I was surprised at what a large dining room the cafe had. It's basically the entire basement of the double. Entrance is on the side (away from Tulane Ave) where there is a small parking lot.  The service is provided by the youth in the program and so it ranges from excellent to means well. I can't wait to go back and try something else...maybe the fish taco special on Fridays.  Bonus: Arrive between 11 & 11:15 for the early bird discount.  15%

I missed PoBoy Fest for a couple of years...some years I'm just not up for the crowds. But yesterday, my youngest brother convinced me to meet him out there for 11ish.  I do think the parking situation might be easier coming from the Jefferson Parish side...or maybe the streets are just wider.  They've moved a lot of the activity down to that end of Oak which is smart as there is more room. The use of side streets is smart too.  I wish more booths sold sample sized portions. I ate the super delish seafood au gratin poboy (on croissant) and was done because it was so rich.  It was fun to see so many friends randomly on the street. I knew if I staked out the poutine poboy stand that Jennifer B would show up eventually...poutine=catnip for Canadians, FYI.  This year there were only 2 big bottlenecks and both were closer to the Carrollton end of the street...including the one in front of the Maple Leaf since a brass band was taking up better than 50% of the road. Fun, but annoying when you're hustling to meet up with people.

While I'm on my credit union reviewing tear, I'll do one more.  I use the credit union's ATM all the time.  It's conveniently located (for me) at the corner of Louisiana and Prytania.  And since I'm a member of a different credit union, I don't pay ATM fees. Yay!  Not so yay, was when I tried to do other banking here.  No go.  They are not a service center.

I used to work with a woman who raved about Ulta; she was a huge fan and constantly complained that there was no location in the GNO. Fast forward a couple of years and we have a location in Elmwood.   I liked being able to buy inexpensive brands that are tried & true next to the higher end items. I did have a sales associate offer assistance on the high end side but she seemed stressed and so I said no thanks. There was no one offering help on the more crowded drugstore brand side.  I was disappointed by the messiness/empty shelves. Maybe this place has been slammed since opening a few months ago...oh wait, it's been almost 7 months, so they should have their act together.  Bonus star for finding a hairbrush that I'm actually liking...yes I'm super picky about that sort of thing.

So it's a post office with all the usual stuff and employees who range from surly to friendly. So why that 4th star? Because it's location is so pretty...  No not the semi-abandoned hospital behind it but the bayou in front. If I was a postal worker, I would love working here just to watch the bayou out front during lunches and down time.

When I need a quick gift, I find myself heading to this shop pretty often.   They really do have great accessories at an excellent price point.  Even my Mom has purchased gift items here, so that means they meet her price needs AND quality demands.  Unlike many shops on Magazine, they carry a variety of sizes up to 18 in some styles. So that's a great change pace too.  My 20-something executive trainee niece LOVED the necklace I picked up here for her birthday.   Definitely check the sale rack for out of season merchandise.

Y'all I am a sucker for candied orange peel and they had both orange and lemon dipped in white (blech), milk or dark chocolate. I got an assortment of the real chocolates with each fruit and they were delicious.  They had samples and were open late so my friend and I had dessert here after eating at 9 Roses around the corner.  The salesperson was helpful and polite and the store was really clean and well stocked.

So I'm not so big on Tastee donuts and never have been...well, except for maybe their cake donuts. That's pretty good.  But more importantly, Tastee is where you can get your old McKenzie's Bakery fix.  They sell the McKenzie's recipe sweet rolls, jelly roll, buttermilk drops, coffee cake (which I'll be sampling tomorrow) and KING CAKE!    I know, I know.  For the folks who didn't grow up here, they just don't understand the love that many of us have for this simpler, sans icing king cake.  But this is what King Cake was growing up, all that filling stuff was for fancy folks and probably didn't appear until the 80s.  So go get your McKenzie's fix today!

Sometimes you have to have your innards looked at by medical professionals. And as far as radiology centers go, this one is pretty nice. The waiting room is a clean airy space. There is plenty of parking; note that the parking lot is accessible from Napoleon Ave only, not Claiborne...which is probably safer.  The staff was pleasant and efficient. There were dressing rooms and a locker to place your valuables with keys so you felt safe. The imaging is unpleasant, easy, annoying, disconcerting, no big...depending on what you're having done.  Because of the location, I'll definitely be moving all my testing to this location.

This space is an historic home (built 1865) that is now used for special events. Since I was once involved with the opera guild, I used to attend meetings here. It is a beautiful home...that is not really handicapped accessible.   Normally this home is closed except for events, like when my college bestie got married here over 20 years ago. The house is only more beautiful now, having gone through a complete renovation post-K.   It looks like you no longer need to be related to someone to rent the house for special events, however be prepared to use their preferred caterer or service provider. The house is full of antiques and they want to make sure that whoever comes in respects and honors the house.   Supposedly home tours are given on Mondays, by the volunteer docents, but I would definitely call before just showing up. It might also still be on a commercial Garden District tour, but again, I would say that it isn't certain.

I've been a fan of the original location for years. And I was really happy to see that they were opening a branch location on South Broad & Eve St. The grand opening was Monday.  This location is looking to be a bit more than the original location, I think. While I just stopped in for pastries this morning (love their slices of banana bread), they also offer sandwiches and salads at lunch (see my photos) and I think a broader coffee service (says the non-coffee drinker).  The space is open and airy with a little bit of an industrial feel. There were plenty of cafe tables inside...not sure about wifi. Parking is on the street and there is a small parking lot in back but the gate was closed this morning (and it looked full) when I drove past this mroning.  I'll definitely be back by and can't wait to try the lunches!

I finally tried this truck that is usually near my work 2x per week. I had the salmon hibachi plate.  The salmon was perfectly cooked and they were out of my first choice, California roll, but I had edamame and really yummy mini serving of seaweed salad.  All the food was really tasty but the portion size was a bit small for the price. Maybe the meat portions are greater.  Would definitely try again

I have always loved Fluevogs but didn't own any until this year. All the local shops that carried the line didn't order baby feet sizes. FF to 2016 and I shopped the Toronto shop and found great shoes.  And then made it to my NOLA local store (open less than a year) for their big summer sale. Sales associates are great. Re was great company and I found 2 awesome pairs of shoes in my size. Love that they carry both men & women's shoes. Love the decor.  Shoes are great for comfort as well as style!

Time for a update...  I still don't really get the frenzy, but many of the dishes are solid. I was with a huge group for a friend's birthday and everyone seemed satisfied with their meals. I had the grilled mahi mahi (dolphin in local fisherman talk...but no not porpoise) with pistachios, grilled asparagus & shrimp. The fish was delish but the sauce was maybe ...not what I expected. I chose the beets and mashed potatoes for my sides. It was a lot of food, but $28 worth? I don't know.  The drinks were huge (which explains the WOO! party atmosphere and the folks who spill into the street when I'm trying to drive past) and my old fashioned was good. Many of the others ordered the special mojito of the night which was tasty (I heard) but also too sweet.  Since we were a large group, we were in the old Christina's seafood market next door to the main restaurant and this is the 2nd time I've been in that space. I actually prefer it to the main house, I think. It's not quite so cacophonous and the decorations are certainly fanciful.   I can't fault the owners. They have found a formula that works and the tourists keep flocking in. Yes. You will get a good meal here and yes, you can get a better one elsewhere for maybe less money.

Cute neighborhood joint with plate lunch specials. And I got to share my meal with Jennifer B so that's always awesome.  Of course, I was totally confused by the 2 business listings at the same location. One is for the diner and the other for the catering business. Why not just do it all together?  I had a tuna on wheat and it was substantial and tasty. I saw a guy at another table with one of the plate lunch specials and it was HUGE, like 3 meals for me large.  Service was fine. Order at the counter, find a table and someone brings you your food. It was pretty speedy for a random weekday.   Will definitely consider this spot again if I'm out in Rivertown when they're open.

Lovely little boutique with higher end lines . The layout is open and airy and the clothes are well displayed. The selection skews a bit young for me, but that's not an issue since I'm often buying gifts for the plethora of nieces.   What is the problem is the staff. Everytime I've been in, I've been ignored. On this last visit my modelesque niece tried asking a question about a sale item and got a deep sigh in response. Really...  Then I had the audacity to ask about an item on a counter display. Same deep sigh and the salesperson grudgingly acknowledged my question and answered me like I was an idiot.   Whatever. Because that's the attitude of the staff.

Carrollton is a solid day parade on the first weekend of carnival.  The riders throw a good amount and the floats are full, especially since this is a small organization.  The floats are pretty good, but nothing super fancy.  Most of the good high school bands march in this parade.

Funny that Kuang beat me to this review.  I made myself a note to create an entry for PoBoy Fest last night.  This is only its 3rd year but they have grown and improved each of those years.  They started with small ambitions which have exploded with enthusiastic city wide response.    Some of the poboys do suffer from sitting or from being in steam trays too long; but you have to overlook some small issues, to be able to eat so much fabulous food in such a small time/area.  Insiders tip?  Ask for 1/2 poboy (usually 1/2 the price) so that you can consume a greater variety before getting full.  Most vendors will hook you up.

City Park is so beautiful...and big.  If one section isn't to your fancy or is too crowded, wander to another and you'll find something to your liking.  It is 1300 acres after all.  Carousel Gardens, the train, boats, picnicking, the Botanical Gardens, Storyland, open fields, sports fields, an art deco arena, you name it and City Park has it.  I'm so glad that so many of the oak trees seemed to have survived despite their submersion 5 years ago.

I can't believe it's taken so long for me to get over to the new fancy Rouse's. It was Christmas Eve and I needed just a few last minute items to make both Christmas Eve and Christmas Day dishes. I drove over to my neighborhood Rouse's...and the humongous parking lot that is always 1/2 empty? It was full to the gills.   Luckily, I had seen a tweet from Anita M that the Baronne Rouse's was blessedly free of crowds. While that wasn't the case by mid-afternoon, it was considerably less crowded that the Tchop location.    Great selection; nicely laid out store; folks offered to help me AND I found everything I needed and was in and out within 30 minutes. Woo Hoo!

Most of the cupcakes are really tasty & creative.  I got a lemon rasberry filled recently that was probably my favorite.  The icing is good and not too sweet or too plastic-y (hate!) and the prices are OK.  There are 2 nearly identical listings for this business (both have reviews).  I hope Yelp! central merges them soon.

The Botanical Gardens are a section of City Park.  They include WPA buildings and sculpture.  The botanical gardens were particularly hard hit by Hurricane Katrina, losing most of their plants.  Volunteers are working steadily to rebuild the gardens so go spend some money there and give them some love.

I miss watching this parade where it belongs...on Carrollton avenue.  I know it's easier for the police to have most of the parades follow the same route, but I miss the neighborhood routes.    Anyway Carrollton is a solid first weekend parade that is still pretty vibrant considering the organization is over 80 years old.  The street tile krewe beads were really pretty today.  And they always have good bands.  Plus my niece caught superballs, her favorite.  All that plus fabulous weather? Definitely 4 stars.

So delicious! The menu was really inventive and the specials all sounded tasty.  I had some sort of delish gyozo style dumpling filled with shrimp & mirliton; my only criticism was that the spicy mustard/soy sauce was a bit too heavy handed and so it overwhelmed the delicate flavors a bit. I wish they were closer to my house and that they were in a non-smoking venue but I will definitely be back

This is my go to location for sports related gifts (how many Saints knick knacks exist anyway?) and jeans.    The store is always a bit disorganized and the clothes are pretty smashed together as if the racks were supposed to fit in a larger space.  Be prepared to dig around in the jeans section to find the right size/style/wash.  But the prices are pretty good if you wear levi's or lee's.  They also carry a fair amount of work clothing in the men's section (but not the women's).   My brother is a big shopper of the back row /out of season section.  He's found some major deals in that area.

DH saved my life during Endymion. They were open and for $5 for adults you could come and go, buy food and drink, and most importantly go to the bathroom. It made my 5 year old niece and 70 year old father much less cranky.  Oktoberfest is fun; everyone loves to chicken dance, right?  They also have film nights and a host of other activities.

Run do not walk to go sample the yummy foods at Milkfish. Seriously, everything I sampled was delicious. And do not worry if you're vegetarian or pescatarian, Chef Christine has your best interests in mind.  Loved the veggie lumpia and the lumpia shanghai, the veggie pancit, and OMG the garlic rice. And we ended with the super yummy fried banana dessert.  Quick note: be prepared for 2 bills to be paid separately if you have anything more to drink than water. All beverages are on A Mano.  Here's the tough news...Milkfish just popped up in A Mano recently and A Mano announced today that they are closing Labor Day weekend (before/after?). I hope Milkfish finds another spot quickly.  I know they are hoping for a full time non-wandering restaurant soon and I hope that happens.

Y'all I got to use a blowtorch!  I wasn't allowed to use it by myself, but still BLOWTORCH!  I went to a glassblowing class in May (I think classes will be happening again come fall) that a friend scheduled for a huge group of us on a Friday night. There was a party room for us to bring food and drinks and then we all took turns making pumpkins (other choices include ornaments and eggs...but maybe tumblers in the future).   I was semi-terrified that I was going to melt glass on myself or others but our instructor made sure we were safe...and y'know she let me handle the blowtorch so all the stars!  The selection of items for sale is diverse and beautiful and I love the old movie theater setting. Definitely a great time!

Another review for bars on Frenchman...most of which I was sure I had reviewed. I think Yelp tortures me by disappearing my reviews occasionally and no they aren't filtered. Or maybe I'm suffering from a huge hallucination...in which case I blame the sinus meds.  I like DBA because it's large and not smokey. The atmosphere is chill and for those who like it...there are LOTS of beers. But there is other liquor too for the non beer drinking (yay!)  The bartenders are on point and hussling.  The local music when it's happening is excellent and the sound is usually good to great.

Delicious food booth in the Nashville Farmers Market. We both had the supertasty grilled brie apple sammich and split some of the tomato soup...and we asked for some extra sliced bread to go with.   The counter folks were really helpful and I believe the menu selections are seasonal. I was really impressed that they were offering a charlotte russe as a special Christmas order and I really wanted to just get one because...this was not feasible because I was only in Nashville for a long weekend. Still. Next time...  Would go back for the bread any time.

Hmm...the girl who doesn't eat meat is going to all the meaty places.  There were choices on the menu for pescetarians but not a lot.    My group shared the fried green beans and the deviled eggs as appetizers. Seriously I would come back just for these dishes alone. And then I split the mixed green salad with a friend because it is HUGE! Small plate? I don't think so. And the tempura gouda in it is OMG good.  I had the drunken shrimp as my entree and it was tasty but the sauce was a little thin...maybe or just needed a bit more oomph. Also the sauce was with wine the night I was there not beer like on the website. I like a changing menu. Keeps things fresh.  My companions had a rib special, a bone marrow dish, meatballs and other assorted meatiness. They all thought their dishes were good to great.  Now I need to go back for that pickle plate that we didn't get this time.

So I'm a little torn about this small space in a strip mall off of Causeway Blvd...the food was OK. Sort of hit or miss. My friend asked for no sausage in her red beans but got two huge pieces of sausage which she wasn't going to eat. I had the shrimp and mango salad. The mango was great but the balance of the salad was just off...maybe too many toppings not enough lettuce, which is better than the inverse f'sure. The cup of seafood gumbo had sausage in it, even though I asked and the menu doesn't say it does. So I didn't eat it.  Our server was OK. The space is small. It seemed like most folks were doing take out rather than dining in.   I wouldn't be averse to returning but not someplace I'd go out of the way for.

I usually get the shrimp poboy not the hamburgers because it has longer hours and a drive through which most poboy joints don't.  If you go inside you do get dress your sammiches yourself.  The fries are big steak fries which I like.

What's up with the Metry bars that are split level? If you can't make it down the steps, you're too drunk to buy another drink? The regulars were super friendly and welcoming so that was nice. The drinks were cheap AND, y'all, there were inspirational quotes written in mirrored letters in the ladies room. Seriously, I felt inspired.  The karaoke DJ (only on Saturday night?) may have been insane...or he just thought he had skillz. So that was kind of annoying. HOWEVER, hearing Joel sing (thanks to Steve) I'm in Love with a Stripper will live in my memory for a long, long time. Seriously this was a classic moment and I'm sorry if you missed it. Pair of Dice gets a bonus star just for being the locale of that song...and y'know the mirror quotes.  The crowd was really eclectic which surprised me.
Excellent full service comic book shop.  They've special ordered both comics and graphic novels.  Great selection, friendly staff.

So this is your basic Bourbon Street bar, non-annoying division. What it doesn't have? No flashing lights, no screaming djs. What it does have? Solid basic drinks, some novelty drinks since it's the sister establishment to Tropical Isle (WOOOO handgrenades), a low key atmosphere. Here the focus is on the music.   The staff was great when I wandered in on a late Saturday night. The courtyard was lovely despite the heat and the restrooms were clean. My drink was a bourbon & coke and the pour was heavy and not rotgut level liquor.   +1 for having Big Al Carson play here most nights and he is awesome.

Solid old school bar in the FQ. Cash only.  Do not expect a fancy drink. Buy a beer or a straight pour.  I love the bartenders who have seen it all and do not want to put up with your nonsense. They remind of the folks who tended the bars that my Gramps brought me into as a kid (no my Mom didn't really know).   Low key (unless a Saints game is on). Prices are good for the FQ.

Wow! Still only open on Friday nights and lacking a liquor license, Saffron still has it going on.  What an amazing meal.    I had the crabmeat pudha which was sort of pancake with nice lumps of crabmeat and was made with chickpea batter, I think.  Since I was with Anita M I also got to taste the amazing curry gumbo.  What a perfect marriage of south Louisiana and India, subtle and delicious.  E gobbled up his tomato soup before I got to try it, so it must have been good.  For entrees, I had the seared scallops mumbai which was sweet and a little bit spicy with perfectly cooked scallops surrounding a mound of spiced veggie rice.  Fabulous.  Anita had the tamarind shrimp which were really good.  E got the vegetarian trio; you can select your own three from 7 sides, 3 of which are vegan.  He had the paneer lajawab, cauliflower & potatoes ludhiana & the dal makni (thank goodness for online menus).  All were tasty but we all tasted the paneer and LOVED it.    Since it would be rude to not at least look at the dessert menu, we did.  And there it was...my one true love: fried sweet dough with syrup no less.  So we had gulab jamun (the aforementioned fried dough...seriously I could have eaten a dozen of these without the syrup.  I think the syrup does enhance but it's also there to slow you down.) and the lychee and cherry ice cream.  Really, really good and definitely worth a trip to the Wank.

After seeing Charles' review it made me realize that I've never gone back and re-reviewed St. Lawrence. I'm not sure what's going on with the management here but the place is really inconsistent. I had good food here with chefs 1 & 2 but now? Not so much. Plus the bartenders can be great or completely ignore you which for me has always been a problem.   I just don't get it. The decor is great; the location is good. But this joint doesn't really want a local crowd with this level of foolishness.   So if you're lucky, you can have a fabulous experience and if you're not, you'll think all the multi-star yelpers are insane.

I remember going here is a child...and I don't think the exhibits have been altered one bit.  AND the scariest thing (in my child's mind) the breathing soldier at the Battle of New Orleans, didn't even work the last time I was there.  Most of the museum is dedicated to the history of New Orleans with a horror section thrown on at the end for good measure.
Best fish tacos in town.  The sangria is delish too.

WOW! This building is a gem. Love the restoration (some parts still being completed), the architecture, the views, and the location on the lake.  When I asked Lindsay A to meet me out here for lunch, I think she thought I had lost my mind. But then we ran around the airport like children...investigating all the nooks and crannies. I highly recommend closing yourself into the old telephone booths to see how well they dampen the outside noise. But the telephones are gone... they should hook up charging stations in the booths.  We happened to be there on a Saturday when there was a WWII airshow nearby so there were lots of people around but it also meant that we got to watch vintage planes flying around so bonus!  The Walnut Room was open rather than the Cafe (to accommodate the crowds) so we got to see the beautiful bar space too.   Just gorgeous. I wish air travel was still so elegant.

I do enjoy a jaunt out to HK Market. Some of the prices make the trip completely worth the gas spent.  Then there is the exoticism factor. Who doesn't love perusing the candies and cookies from other countries? And the condiments? I'm still curious about the crab sauce...but I chickened out.  I also like that they've added an entire Hispanic aisle...gotta give the customers what they want.

I think this is another of my reviews that Yelp ate. Someone should really feed it.  Crabby Jacks is a great grab-n-go place for plate lunches and poboys.  I've had both fried seafood (excellent) and grilled shrimp poboys (plan to get messy) as well as plate lunches (huge).  My only disappointments were their mac-n-cheese (kinda bland) and their fish tacos (which were delish but were served on blue tortilla shells which turned the fish a distressing shade of gray).  My Mom loves their brisket poboy.

I am cheap so I try to never park at the airport since all the parking options are too much money. BUT I had no choice on this recent trip, even with being gone for 6 days a cab to and from was going to be more expensive than parking. Plus I found online coupons for your first time parking...first time parking for that license plate that is. So I was good. I got to park for $4 per day instead of almost $7.   The parking spots are tight, so my poor car has a new ding which makes me sad and also consider that my fellow drivers are jerks.   The staff was great. The driver to the airport helped with our luggage. I only waited a few minutes for a bus when I got back. And I was offered a bottle of water as a I checked out.

They have always taken excellent care of our dogs.  And when our last baby had to be put down they were incredibly caring and sweet.  Our current girl loves to go there; she doesn't care about the shots because they give her enough treats to make up for it.

I kind of miss the seat of the pants atmosphere TC had back in the late 80s.  But the fact that they've been around since then shows their quality.  Excellent values on the dinner plates.  Will custom make non-menu items for picky children.  Fabulous Sangria.

Since John has been raving about this place since last summer, I finally stopped by and tried it. And, man, was it a welcome and delicious respite the night I went.  We ended up eating really late since I had to wait around my cold house waiting for Entergy to show up and get my heat working. So when I walked into Mais Arepas, I was so grateful for such a warm and inviting space.   I had a delicious glass of sangria and some roasted corn as an appetizer and then had the shrimp arepas as an entree. My cousin had the ajiaco. We both really enjoyed our food and the server/owner was really great about giving us advice on what to order.   Definitely need to go back and try more of the menu.

So many pretty, pretty things.  From full on home decor items, like 3d wall tiles to fancy dishes to make your table look pretty, this store has it going on.  I really liked the wool/rubber wall planter thingys.  Definitely on my list of places to hit up for an usual gift for shower or wedding.

So I had to write a mini-review to get this business to add from my phone the other day.  Full disclosure: my cousin owns/runs the joint.  Ridge Bistro is a solid lunch/casual dinner cafe which offers tasty & filling food.  The location is your basic no frills strip mall.  And the decor is simple and clean.  The menu has enough to interest most and includes at least one vegetarian entree.  My nieces loved the mac-n-cheese & grilled cheese sandwich (2 separate items on the kids menu).  My brother had the shrimp & grits and thought they were really tasty.  E had the pecan crusted fish and gobbled it up.  I had the shrimp remoulade poboy (featured at the poboy fest the last couple of years).    The daily specials are posted on their webpage.  Oh & his shrimp remoulade poboy just won an award at PoBoy Fest 2011.

From what I understand...the Bronx Bar doesn't really open until the adjacent New York Pizza closes...or maybe there is some overlap.  The important thing is that you can buy a slice late night. And scarf it down while drunkypants and give yourself a wicked pizza burn that sends you down the WtH memory trail the next morning.    On the particular night that I went, I was grateful to Lindsay A for buying me a slice and amused by Holly G when she stole it. And even more grateful for my 2nd non-molested slice.    Basic pizza slices came out quick. Selection of beverages is good, but as Joel M said...the bartender wasn't really interested in us.

Lee Circle is a pain to drive around because traffic circles confuse people. Lee Circle has a statue that you can't really see because it's so high in the air. But Marielle is correct...it is one of those landmarks and it is also a demarcation of the border between the LGD (Lower Garden District) and the CBD (Central Business District).    So a couple of reasons why I am a fan of Lee Circle, both are from the carnival season:   I was at the Circle, walking back to my car after the parades were long over, one Carnival light many years ago and I saw the most amazing sight ever...a car going around the circle in the correct direction, but in reverse at 40 miles per hour; I thought I was hallucinating. That driver should've gotten work in Hollywood as a stunt driver.  Used to be that really drunk dudes with death wishes used to try to climb up to hang out with the General.  When I was in junior high, I saw a guy fall while trying.  Luckily, he was so drunk that he walked away with no broken bones. Plus he only made it half way up the column.  The area is now fenced off to prevent folks from doing that anymore.

I wandered into this gallery during Dirty Linen Night and was really surprised to see lithographs by Chagall and Picasso and Warhol and Erte. I had no idea that a gallery in NOLA was selling these items.  As I suspected this gallery is part of a national chain...because really who locally would have the money to buy the rights to so many big name artists?  They had a local band playing and the space was welcoming and much larger than it appeared on the outside. Definitely a lovely space to browse and to dream about what I could buy should I win the lottery.

I heard about this new coffee shop while I was on jury duty last month. And then I read that they were serving Tandem teas (local distributor) so I guessed that they actually have a commitment to teas as well as fancy coffee drinks.   Well yum. They do a proper tea service with a cup and saucer and a steeping vessel and a strainer. Very very British. They only had 4 tea selections with a green, black, herbal and ? when I stopped by yesterday. I had the jasmine dragon pearls and a yummy croissant!  Love the style of this place with the retro uniforms and the precision in making you a cuppa. The backroom is gorgeous. What a lovely renovation. And the backyard is just waiting for more furniture; there are currently stools on the deck. I noticed people coming in from the backdoor as the rode their bikes to the back.   As Alvin said the music is a great mix (New Order) and just loud enough to cover up conversations but not too loud. Great addition to the area!

Interesting little shop with a definite aesthetic...if it meshes with your own, you'll love it; if not, you might find a present.  Lots & lots of blingy jewelry, some vintage & some new. I'm coveting a 1930s Christmas tree pin which is well priced at $180. But there are lots of new pieces as low as $20:  It is definitely not a hard sell place; the sales woman was much more interested in chatting than convincing me to purchase. Not a bad thing...

I used to go to a bar at this location, oh many moons ago, and once saw a professor passed out on the bar. So the location has that bit of nostalgia going for it.  I ordered an iced tea and a egg sandwich. One of the servers was great; the other one seemed to be off in her own universe. I had been seated for about 15-20 minutes when she finally noticed me. Luckily, the on-top-of-it server had already taken my order.   The space is great if the weather is good. You eat outside under the covering of a 1940s gas station...y'know where the pumps would be. And it's dog friendly which is nice.  But my food was pretty indifferent. I arrived poorly assembled and with inedible tomatoes  Would I stop in again? Maybe on a beautiful day but just don't expect great food.

Posting a whole slew of reviews for stores I hit with my Mom on Black Friday. Gogo jewelry has really different pieces of contemporary jewelry. Some of it is simply beautiful while other pieces are funny.  Despite it's hipsterish appearance, the store really does have something for most folks.  We gave my MIL (in her 70s) one of the necklaces a year or so ago.  I must admit that I could live with out the weird taxidermy displays though.  My Mom, on the other hand, was mesmerized by them.

MMMMM... they have dark chocolate covered candied orange peel by the pound.  Really I could just stop there and be done.  But they also have fun gift items, a variety of jelly bellys, sugar free items and are super nice.  They do wonderful gift baskets for showers or corporate events.
Yum! Promise this is just a placeholder

In honor of St. Joseph's Day, I wandered over to this huge hulking church on Tulane Ave. Their St. Joseph's Day altar is beautiful but behind the altar rail so you can't get too close. And they had the lamb cake which has always been my favorite; that & prominent placing of the stuffed artichokes makes this a great altar to me.  As for the church itself, it is often mislabeled a cathedral because it is so huge.  It is a gorgeous enormous church with beautiful windows, carvings and statues. Love that it is so well kept AND that it smells like years of incense. I also appreciated the samovar-looking thing full of holy water, so you can take some home.   Not sure how you'd make it up the huge front steps if you were physically challenged...maybe there's another entrance around back?  Definitely worth a visit.

This is a solid, slightly disheveled hotel bar. It makes a good cocktail and the prices are reasonable, unusual for a FQ hotel bar.  The ambiance is a mix of early 20th century brothel (which is their shtick) and weird 1970s era disco mirrors.  I would definitely go back here again. I do like that they cater to locals while still handling the tourists with grace.

I ate all the foods at Maurepas on a Friday night recently.   Seriously my friends and I ate a 4 course meal.  And with three people (and only 3 cocktails) and 11 plates, our bill was still around $120 which is a bargain, I think.  This was my second trip to Maurepas and so I was somewhat knowledgeable about their menu and plate sizes...which can be odd. The chicken & grits dish is HUGE but the fish entrees are quite petite. Sometimes their combos can be just odd (squash and blueberries?) but other times they are genius (butternut squash and pickled peanuts!).  The cocktails are inventive and tasty.  Service...can be odd but that just fits in with the quirky theme.  Bonus points for the old work sinks out front, repurposed as planters.

Super cute gift shop/stationery store. Love the variety of items and all her signature script items. Love the examples of custom work she has done, very inspirational/aspirational.   Liz was very helpful and even customized a makeup bag for me. Love it! She also offers classes if you're interested in upping (or y'know creating) some skills.   The shop is small but you might just find the perfect item for yourself or a friend.

DELICIOUS gelato, rich and flavorful.  The lime balanced tartness & creaminess perfectly.  The only downside is that it is pricey. One scoop for about $5. That's a lot.  I'm sure the ingredients are worth the cash, but still, a girl has to count her pennies.  I didn't find the staff rude so much as exhausted since it was Poboy Fest when I went.

So this is a brand new Sonic...and as I've stated before Sonic is my favorite fast food. This one is fancy, all clean and new, with the new style high arched canopy that Sonic is doing now.  Plus there were freaky looking ducks to dodge in the parking lot.  I think they were begging for fries & tots. Smart ducks.

While this goodwill is pretty big...I expected the shopping area to be larger. But I guess the other half of the building is offices and work spaces. I didn't find anything great here, but there did seem to be some OK clothes.  I agree with Rene that the housewares/furniture is really picked over.  The staff was nice and the place was clean and smelled OK.  C'mon you know you judge thrift stores by smell too.

A large brightly lit gas station at the corner of Veteran's & Causeway.  It's always clean; the lights work; the pumps work; and their is a pretty good carwash which starts at $5.  The gas prices are in line with other stations in the area and it feels a lot safer at night than most.

Everyone has been raving about this jumbo (for the GNO) super-target, but I was like well this alright. I wasn't super impressed with the stock and the one thing I needed from the grocery section (a lemon cake mix), they didn't have.   I found some of the things I needed but ultimately this location is just too far from home to be my regular store...but if I ever decide shop on the way home from the airport again, I'll definitely stop in.

Y'all know this is my cousin's joint so I try to go back when I'm in the area and support his efforts. Last night I had (for the 2nd or 3rd time) the yummy tuna salad which is sashimi grade tuna seared and served over greens. The tuna was melt in your mouth delicious. I'm also a fan of the shrimp wrap and the pecan crusted redfish.  The daily specials are inventive and all that I've tasted are delicious. He does have vegetarian items on the menu, like an eggplant sandwich and a portabello wrap, as well as many meaty items. The Saturday night special is usually prime rib.  They've just expanded to the space next door so they can use it as an overflow dining room on busy days and he's now booking holiday parties.  While lunch is order at the counter (which is great if you're with a group...no bill splitting), dinner does offer table service.

Sketchy gas station at the corner of Milan & Claiborne. It used to be a BP and then it was something else...and now it's a Fuel Express...and maybe sells fried chicken inside. But I haven't had that.  There are only 4 pumps at the space is small. Although it is conveniently located, I only go here during the day.  The gas is cheap though.

This is a small gallery & framing shop with an eclectic selection of items. Since I was just browsing, I did not use their framing services.  The selection of art was interesting and was not all one style or type like other shops.  LOVED the shop dog. The owner was courteous and left us to our browsing and made sure we were treating her pup well.

I've been hesitating to write this review...mostly because I'm on the fence about what rating to give. This establishment is so not my cup of tea BUT...  The staff was pleasant. When I turned down their kind offer to dance on the bar and then have the choice to purchase a t-shirt, they weren't pushy about it. The bartenders were quick (order a straight pour, simple mixed drink or beer). Security was courteous and advised that we might want to move as a dart board was being brought into action...or was it a wheel. The manager was nice...yes, I talked to just about the entire staff in the short time I was there. They really made an effort to make me feel welcome.  The restroom was clean (a huge plus in the FQ). The older women working out their same sex fantasies by taking body shots off the attractive bartender were amusing, but the whole body shots off a stranger triggers my cross-contamination issues.  In summation, not as bad as I feared.

Indian food isn't big in NOLA and that makes me sad.  I'm not sure if Taj Mahal deserves 4 stars but I drive across town to them when the other Indian restaurant is closer.    They are hard to find in a weird strip mall that is perpendicular to the street.  You just have to trust you will find them.

As I wandered on Magazine with friends yesterday, I discovered this new shop on a stretch of Magazine I thought I knew well. And it turns out that they have a location in the FQ. Where have I been?  There's a really cool art gallery in the back and the prints were very affordable. The staff was polite and attentive but let us browse in peace. The shop has a TON of merchandise and it's all really interesting.  My friend bought a couple of NOLA water meter trivets and I ended up with Frankenstein socks (because I have a brother how needs those). But they also had clothes and accessiories and NOLA stuff and you name it.

What a fun night last night in the Botanical Gardens with Jennifer B. Seriously the gardens look gorgeous! All the buildings are looking spot on and I love some of the new sections in the old buildings.    At the fundraiser last night, we were able to tour both the rainforest and the living fossil rooms and they were beautiful...especially by the light of my flashlight app...Maybe we weren't really supposed to be wandering around those sections in the dark. Oh well.  It is the perfect time to tour the gardens...everything is just beginning to bloom and the weather is gorgeous.

When I'm out in Metry (and it's not Saturday since they keep the Sabbath) I'll often stop at Casablanca.  I'm a big fan of their spinach & feta pie.  The menu is diverse enough to satisfy the average diner who is not as adventurous (that would be my brother) and the staff is polite and not hover-y.

Before the HoB this was the place to see live music.  Unfortunately HoB hired away their booker but they still get some great acts.   A great intimate setting to see any band.   As a truly bit of useless trivia, NKotB filmed the Right Stuff video here.  I snuck my adolescent cousin to see the place during the day so she could check it out and the bartenders were totally cool, since I didn't try to buy her a drink.

I wish I could say that I have stayed at the Roosevelt; instead I'm basing my update on my parents' stay in early September.  My parents are...let's say frugal.  But September 3rd was their 49th wedding anniversary and when they saw a local's special for the month, they were sold. They spent 2 nights at the hotel and couldn't stop raving.  The staff was courteous; the food was good (they ate at Domenica's which opened just for them and at Teddy's Cafe); and they were treated fabulously.

A beautiful space in a converted corner store/bar/house. The exposed wood walls are gorgeous and the space is very adaptable, I imagine. The website says it's available as studio space or as an art gallery or as event space.  I was there for a Mosquito Supper Club dinner (review to follow) and it was great space for that. One room was set up with two long tables and a sideboard. The other room held a bar and drink setup. I met a couple at the dinner who are planning their wedding in the space in the fall.  There was a note about a handicapped entrance through the backyard, if that was needed. And I was told the bathrooms were off the backporch but didn't actually use them.   Really a beautiful renovation that honors the history of the building.

I love pie and that is the one baked good that seems in shorter supply around NOLA. Enter the popup entrepreneur the NOLA Pie Guy. He sells pies at various locales, stalk him on FB or twitter or order a pie from his website.  I sampled his key lime & peach pie slices last month.  The key lime was a standout, tart and creamy and very satisfying. The peach was good but not as successful. I think maybe the peaches weren't perfectly ripe so the pie wasn't the super peach bomb that I wanted.  Definitely worth hunting down.

Recently I had planned a Friday night in AND then the power went out, so I gave Vicky a shout and we hightailed it to Mid-City in search of food & A/C. And this is where we ended up. I think this is the 3rd or 4th restaurant I've eaten at in this location since the building was constructed (including a Shoney's in HS).  The layout is odd since you have to choose the dining room or bar as you walk in. Maybe I would choose the bar next time.  We tried a couple of different rolls and some old standbys. The sushi and edamame were fine, The standout was the delish Louisiana roll, spicy crawfish with a pickled okra. Seriously GENIUS.  The meh was the blue crab mango roll. Like Kanno a couple of weeks before, the blue crab was dry and did not taste fresh. My guess is that it had been frozen...  I would definitely go back for the Louisiana Roll and sit in the other room (closer to Bienville) to see if that atmosphere is better.

Oh yum! LOVE the open and airy dining space at this location. And LOVE LOVE the HH pricing (4-7) for house pours (including bubbles) and a cheese plate. Yes please.  The staff is really friendly and makes up a nice varied board. Just let them know if you have any restrictions.   The sandwiches are delicious and they really do get you in and out quickly if you're here for a midday meal. Counter service means that if you're with a group, there's no pesky bill splitting and that the decisive can order while the indecisive or newbie can peruse the menu. Wins all around.

This is one of those businesses that I've used for years...I remember going inside with my Grampa about a million years ago.  A solid choice to buy a new battery for your car or whatever else you might need. They pro-rate if your battery does last it's promised lifetime...please see my brother's jeep which eats batteries.  They also recharged my FiL's generator battery that had issues post-K.  According to their website they sell all sorts of batteries (and you can pay with paypal which I find stunning for such an old school operation), including gear and marine. Cool

Really cute clothes and amazing accessories.  I scored a couple of Christmas gifts here for the teenage nieces.  And the super picky 14 yr old was actually wearing the handband I bought here, the NEXT day.  Amazing.  The staff is helpful without being over solicitous.  The store is small but the selection indicates a well edited eye.  As Leslie said, the sizing seems to be all over the map, but that's an issue with the brands rather than the store.

I was here for a community event and it's a lovely large space with good a/c on a really hot summer day.  It is very warehouse-y. But doesn't feel industrial, if that makes sense.   The room was packed the evening I was there so I didn't get a better sense of things.  But I do know it's a HUGE improvement of the nothingness that used to embody this block.

I have such fond memories of eating at Drago's. My HS banquets were held here.  In fact I had dinner in that same room on Saturday night...definitely not for private parties any more.    The pros:  The chargrilled oysters were tasty and fresh. I sampled the fish special that one of dining companions got and it was delicious. Lots of variety to the seafood dishes. They have a Chandon sparkling split for a glass or so of bubbly.  The cons: They do not take reservations, even for large parties. So my group arrived at 5 pm. We were seated immediately. By the time we left, the hordes has descended. It was craziness. The crabmeat au gratin dip tasted like velveeta.  The weird: Drago's is no longer an inexpensive restaurant and the server was very much...the jokester nephew of the owner style. I found an oyster shell under my chair....remember we were seated at 5; had it been there since lunch?  The verdict: My entree (an fine but not remarkable shrimp & pasta dish) fed me for 2 additional meals since Saturday. I would rather pay less and have an entree that doesn't feed 3.  I wish the meal had been better and that our waiter hadn't disappeared so we could pay the bill and escape the gathering hordes of people.

Met up with some folks for lunch on Saturday and I was the only one who had been to Crabby Jack's before.  And every other meal I've had has been fine.    Saturday I had a plate lunch special of seafood stuffed mirlitons which I love. Except at Crabby Jacks they felt the need to deep fry the mirliton (in breading) and then deep fry the stuffing (again with a weird crust of breading) then slap them together on the plate and cover with a cream sauce.  Weird.  Yes there were also fried shrimp under the mirliton which was a nice bit of lagniappe, but the whole deep fried thing was a bit much.  I removed all the breading and ate the mirliton without it and then ate some of the stuffing...and OK most of the fried shrimp.    I forgot that I was not a big fan of their mac-n-cheese and got it again (@ +50cents) and it is still dullsville.

Generally I'm a fan of Thoth.  I like that they take an extra long uptown route (which is allowed since the krewe was founded by medical professionals and parades past Children's Hospital and other facilities) and it's a really vibrant organization.  The riders were very generous and lots of throws were pelted at me & mine, but the parade just seemed too long, maybe something broke down.  Honestly, Sunday is a blur at this point.

I still sort of miss Taqueria circa 1990 when it was tinier, grittier & with a smaller menu. On the other hand, more choices and more tables and more drinks!  I still think their black bean burrito is yummy. And I like both the fish and shrimp tacos (two separate items). The taco salad is more meh. And I wish they offered specials sometimes just to change stuff up. They do offer some kid friendly items like a cheese quesadilla or American taco. My uncle is a huge fan of their tongue taco (not for me thanks). And, yeah, the sangria is delicious.  Service is usually speedy but you definitely aren't rushed. I like the open kitchen and that there is bar seating if you choose to eat alone.

I must admit I haven't been here since they reopened after Katrina.  The bookstore is in the basement (above ground naturally) of a large house just off Carrolton Avenue and across from Notre Dame Seminary.  Unlike the Pauline shop, this store does focus more on books and has fewer gift items.

Latest addiction? dark chocolate non-pareils and instead of white candy bits, they're purple, green and gold.  Seriously, Blue Frog is my go to shop for fancy chocolates or other yummy candies.  Love that they've added some tables & chairs so that you can sit and enjoy their goodies on site.  Love the assortment of seasonal items that they get for holidays.

Great place to hear eclectic music.  They mostly have jazz but really you can hear almost anything there.  The venue is oddly laid out but that doesn't really detract...unless you get one of the seats where you can't even see the stage.  As for food, I've only ever had appetizers but they were all tasty.

I wandered over to the Wank this evening to check out Daiwa as they are one of the Wednesday participants in Sushi for Sendai.  And I think we'll be making that trek again.  Every roll and each piece of sushi was beautifully presented.  The chef's knife skills were particularly noticeable on the vegetable roll with each piece of cucumber looking identical to the other. Amazing.  The crispy tofu was the lightest and freshest version of that dish that I've ever had.  The salmon mango roll was delicious and different; the rice paper roll was beautiful.  Plus they have inari which I LOVE and it's always on the menu.  The fish was all fresh and delicious.  And the service was attentive to the point of funny.  When the staff found out we lived uptown, they were amazed that we drove over the bridge.   The owner even recognized E from when he used to eat lunch weekly at Hana.  Crazy.

I ended up here after the Krewe of Halloween because my niece and her friends wanted to catch the World Series game.  I was not too impressed.  I would blame any service bobbles (1 plate out of 6 came 20 minutes late) on the crowds, but then the waiter charged one of the nieces' friends for the entire meal on her card after also receiving cash. Sketchy. He did apologize when called out.  I thought the garlic fries were bitter. And the crabmeat on my seafood cobb salad did not taste fresh.  I guess I should mention that I ate in the bar so maybe that makes a difference.

My review is for the gas station only.  As Roger said, the prices are good.  The pumps work.  This is a smaller location so I think they have 6 pumps max though so it can get backed up.  It is well lit at night.

Krewe D'Etat is a great satirical parade that maintains a slightly macabre sense of humor.  Love the blinky gargoyles and this years seizure inducing blinking rings were fun.  I wanted each float to stop in front of me so I could read/analyze all the stuff they were lampooning.  Good times.

This is an interesting addition to this commercial stretch of Prytania. The pastries are amazing...even day (or two) old. And the chocolates are divine.  I haven't had a beverage here yet, but plan too.  The decor is still sparse...because it's new? or because that's the design choice? I'm not sure.  But I kind of like it.  It is hard to tell what the business if from the window though.  On a random side note, I used to get my hair cut here a million years ago when it was Command Performance (c'mon sing the old TV commercial) and many years later I worked with a trainer when there was a gym here. So that's an interesting collection of businesses in one location.

Restoration review! You may have read in the news that vandals painted the Marie Laveau tomb pink...with latex paint which is seriously damaging to plaster since it can no longer breathe. Save our Cemeteries has worked with the Archdiocese of the New Orleans to remove the paint but that damaged the original plaster. (WTH is wrong with people.)  So they are doing a big campaign to raise money to restore the tomb. Even a few dollars will help.  Check out the SoS FB page for more info: https://www.facebook.com/photo.php?fbid=441225066009560&set=a.289440261188042.1073741826.288933097905425&type=1&stream_ref=10

First there's the building. LOVE the WPA post office that this once was. The attention to details (OMG the floors) is amazing and lovely.  Second there's the exhibits; while they do have a standing collection, the traveling exhibitions are exceptions. I saw the American Art from The Phillips Collection... and as I've been to that museum in DC as well, I can definitely say this is a well curated and informative exhibit.  Finally, the museum offers multiple amenities like an actual (pay) parking lot, a cafe, and a gift shop.    Highly recommended.

Man, I want a grilled shrimp sammich now.  Yes, there is a wait.  The owner is a bit of a perfectionist and makes most of the sandwiches himself and it's not the most organized place in the world.  But it does have some tasty poboys.

After a trip last year was cancelled by a deluge, I've been wanting to come back to the preserve and today seemed like the perfect day to finally get back.  The weather was gorgeous and with great friends, I couldn't have asked for a better morning. Because of all the recent rains, we stuck to the boardwalk/gravel paths of the visitor's center, palmetto, bayou coquille & marsh overlook trails which all feed into each other. We probably walked about 4 miles there and back.   We saw alligators, snakes, bugs galore, an owl, a swamp bunny, and a toddler almost get bit by a snake since he crouched down to look closely at it as it reared back to strike. Seriously parents what are you thinking.  The irises are just start to bloom so you have another couple of weeks to see them in their full glory. The smell of all the honeysuckle was intoxicating. Plus I noticed a ton of blackberry vines so in a few weeks you might be able to have a snack while you wander around.  Funniest thing was the clearly out of town folks who were fascinated by the little lizards that run all over my front porch and that's what they were sitting on a bench watching them run around. Oh and the girl who's swamp attire included fishnets, high heel boots and a mini-skirt.  Other funny thing, we ran into my uncle, the park ranger, while out there. He LOVES his retirement job.   I'll repeat that it's amazing to be out here and you're only 30 minutes away from the city. No power lines in sight, outside and you can just breathe the swampy air...which is home to me but may be cloying to others. Oh and brother 4 says that the twin canal trail (separate parking lot) is a good place to go fishing. And the highest of the non-boardwalked trails.  Also as a National Park, it's free.

Still loving the comic shop...though I am woefully ignorant on most of what they carry.   I've been hanging out here a bit more lately, since I joined one of their graphic novel bookclubs.  The Sandman bookclub on (usually) the 2nd Sunday evening of a month for the next year; next month is volume 3.  There is a huge selection of back issues taken in trade if you want to dig for a treasure and I always peruse the used graphic novel section to see if there is anything I need.

Cute boutique with very interesting sense of style. Lots of linen in the summer and spring available. I like that the clothes are sorted by color and level of dressiness.   They do carry a few shoe lines and have styles that I haven't seen anywhere else. A seriously large selection of hair do-dads and other accessories.  The sale stuff is all the way in the back near the dressing rooms.  My only frustration with shopping here is that I feel like the sizes are all over the map. But I guess that's more on the brands than the store.

Good old school Chinese.  I love that they have the paper Chinese zodiac place mats.  The entrees are large.  I had the veggie hot pot and it made 3 meals for me.  The veggie egg rolls were tasty, but a little greasy.  Plus I kind of love family run establishments that have multiple generations working together.

This shop is definitely an interesting concept and there are lots of folks who will appreciate the gluten free, healthy fare. I was interested in some of their veggie chips but didn't want to buy a whole bag at $7-8 without a taste which unfortunately they didn't have while I was there.  I did get a gluten-free chocolate chip cookie made with almond flour, since that's always a good tester item. The chocolate was organic and rich. The cookie was good but it tasted like cake and was really soft.   I'll have to remember them the next time I'm in the mood for a smoothie. It looks like they will be expanding in the future so I'll be interested to see where this shop goes.

I used to LOVE Juan's pre-K.  Since...it's gotten a little more corporate (if you can say that about a restaurant that only seems to hire by tattoo volume) and now charges for your 2nd basket of chips.  That said, they still make some excellent tacos.  The burritos are usually 2 meals for me.  I just wish they had sangria.

This is not a location to purchase bread. This is the commercial bakery. You have to go to a store who carries their bread.   That being said...oh yum. This is more European than much of the bread around NOLA with a thick heavier crust on their baguettes...which I say as someone who loves a crust. You may have already had their delicious bread as many restaurants around town use it.  Check out their website for their current retail partners which include wine shops and local groceries. PLUS you can take classes with them once a month! which I totally need to do!

Cars. Man. They can be annoying. I was having some issues getting my car to start...it was sluggish but it was really cold and then it just flat out wouldn't start, except a few hours later it did.  Ran out on Monday morning to Jefferson Battery my go to shop for decades. And they said one cell in my battery was faulty so a new battery was had and I made it to work and was only about 10 minutes late. Sweet.  They had what I needed and took care of everything quick quick. Easy credit card payment and I was on my way. Let's hope this one lasts the full 3 years.

Choctaw is another parade that originally paraded in another part of town but now is on the standard uptown route. As it is 80+ years old, no one thought about the name being controversial in the 1930s (Choctaws were in Louisiana). BUT the dudes need to stop painting their faces with red face. It seems a bit bizarre in 2014.   I do like that this parade has a ton of horse groups (cowboys, uniforms and "indian" dress); it's always fun to see all the pretty horses.  Throws are not super plentiful and the floats are the rented sort, but it's still a solid 1st weekend parade.

Let's review Katie A's favorite bar... Yes it's a real dive, although it's looking much better than when the front of the building fell off. The drug dealers on the far corner have mostly moved on. And you're in the university area so expect ridiculous fratty behavior. But then again I mostly hung out at Snake & Jake's in the late 90s so my measure of grunginess is a little different.  BUT, Katie is correct, if you either come here early (before 10) or in the summer (when the students are mostly gone) or very late (after 3), then you will have a good time.  Do not expect fanciness or premium liquors. Do expect cheap drinks and furniture that might collapse.   Depending on your company and the level of idiocy around you (on a scale from amusing to WTF), a good time can be had.

Umm...free skee ball and real cocktails and a good price?  Yeah, I'm there. Mostly if I want a good cocktail and I'm being poor, I drink at home. But sometimes you want to go out in the world and socialize and, y'know, play skeeball. And this spot is an excellent place to do all of the above.  The drinks are mostly well made...warm vodka? uh no. And I wouldn't ask for anything too fancy, but their premade punches (and Pimm's cups) are solid. The price point is good and it's very casual, although not pajamas casual.  There are board games and skeeball and that ring/hook game who's name I don't know.    Nice addition to the Freret corridor.   OH! And I get to add this to my list of slaphappy bars since I saw a girl slap her date here. It was pretty funny. I wonder what he did.

A friend was visiting over MG and she wanted a poboy! And luckily I remembered that Parran's opened near me last year, at the (sniff sniff) former location of Kyoto.   We went just after opening on the Friday before Mardi Gras and they were very busy but our poboys came out fast and were delicious. I asked for extra pickles (as usual) on my dressed fried shrimp and their were beaucoup. Yum. Also I had to ask for cocktail sauce as well. I would have liked more horseradish but I'm a weirdo.  My friends loved their poboys too, more shrimp and oyster. Plus we had fries (ok) and fried pickles (nice batter). They have fresh brewed tea. And beer and wine AND king cakes were available.   I need to remember that they are open until 8pm in case I get the dinnertime craving for a sammich.

For some reason, I just never made it over to this spot when it opened. But that was rectified late night on Wednesday after Nyx when my houseguests were starving and everything around us was closing at 10pm. I called to verify that their kitchen was still open. Yes! Until midnight. Whew  I had the gougeres, my friends had a pickle plate and fries (vegan items) and another the burger. My gougeres came out first and were a little flat, not as fluffy as other versions that I've had but satisfying. Then my friend's fries came out, then her pickled veg. Then finally after we were finished eating, the burger came out. Despite this kitchen bobble, service was good.   We had a couple of glasses of wine and one cocktail. Pours were good and the selection was interesting. It was a good people watching scene, from folks like us, straight from the parade to people in formalwear, to folks on dates and everything in between. Good times.

Running errands and I was starving + craving a poke bowl. Luckily Yelp helped me figure out that I wasn't that far from the Metry location of Poke Loa.   Even though this is a big shopping center, everyone was there so parking was a bit tight. This location is small and doesn't have much interior seating and only about 4 outside tables, luckily one freed up for me to eat. The staff was great. And the restaurant was clean just no as charming as the uptown location... but it's a strip mall.  So they were out of all the flavors of aqua fresca. Color me sad. I got a 3 scoop protein bowl with lettuce (to offset all the Christmas cookies). And here's where I got sad. The lettuce wasn't great, wilty and some pieces tasted off. And then some of the fish had an ammonia smell. Very offputting.   Because I was starving and paid $$ for my bowl, I took the risk and ate it anyway. And it was fine. I finished about 1/2 of it (so I wasn't a starving beast) and then got it home and added some balsamic vinegar to hide the smell. And ate the rest. I was fine so it definitely wasn't bad, just smelly.  Maybe it was time of year or just a bad day. Would stop in again, but would try to not be ravenous and more aware of the ingredients.

Tee-niny gay bar uptown. Love that there is a casual gathering place that caters to my LGBTQ friends.   I stopped in because it was late and I was starving. They kindly whipped up some veggie friendly potato skins. So 80s and so delicious.  Solid drinks and friendly environment. It is small but they also have tables outside if the weather permits.

I had popped into this location of Gracious Bakery once before but it was carnival time and they had a very limited menu. I finally stopped by again this past Saturday and it's a great small shop.  There's less seating than the other 2 locations but I find this space the homiest... maybe because it's in an older building. The staff were really friendly and helpful.   I bought a couple of pastries. (Is it health to want frangiopane at every meal?) And, of course, I bought a King Cake. They have 5 or 6 varieties and I went with the almond filled queen cake. Oh YUM! The filling was a really light almond paste that just made the cake supermoist and delicious.  I need to stop by and actually have a meal here sometime... but I'll wait until after Mardi Gras day for that.

Pandemic update: Still 5 stars and they are making it super easy to order and get your books, puzzles and games.  If they have whatever you need instock, then you can get contactless delivery to your car! If they don't there is an independent bookstore link and they get a good percentage of the sale proceeds.   They have a great selection of new and used books, many local.  And they have great gift selections too.

Weird. I feel like this is one of those disappearing review situations...  I've shopped at Good Feet for a while. They are a good local source of birkenstocks and other walking shoes, orthotics and shoes that are well-made and therefore cost more.  This shop is smaller than the Metairie one and seems more aimed for style. I feel like the Metairie location has more actual orthotic shoes. Or maybe it's just how the 2 shops are arranged.  Service is always great and I've been really happy with my purchases.

Poor Haus, I know they lost their space on Galvez, but their temporary (?) quarters off Airline is just sad...especially in comparison to their old building.   Now located in an old VFW hall, they still have a bar, food & various german knick knacks.  But not Oktoberfest, at least not at this location...  Oktoberfest will be in Kenner at Rivertown over 2 weekends next month. Not in the vfw hall location.  I hope the rumor of them buying space off Bayou St.John is true.  +1 star for hosting a benefit for my cousin.

Thoth is another unique carnival experience. It has the longest route of any uptown parade because it starts near children's hospital.  It was originated by physician's (Thoth being the Egyptian god of medicine) and so has been allowed to deviate from the standard route and pass a couple of hospitals.    The riders are generous and they always have some unique out of town bands.  Bonus points because this year I met friends outside of Boulangerie bakery to catch the parade and got to watch & eat fresh pastry. Yea!

Sometimes you just need a smoothie... I'm not as addicted as I once was to these delicious drinks. My go to is a Caribbean Way, no turbinado (trying to avoid the extra sugar... even though it's so delicious) add peaches.  So you get a big helping of fruit and juices. Yum.   This location was super busy on a weekday at lunch time. But the staff was hustling.   There is parking in the back but it's tight. And don't you dare park there if you're not in the Smoothie King.

It's another case of the disappearing review... I stopped in the other night because I really needed a chocolate chip cookie and discovered no review.  So here's what you need to know... the baked goods are amazing and delicious. The chocolate chip cookies are great. The biscuits are phenomenal.   The service at the restaurant? It's hit or miss. Last time I ate here... and the main content of my review... I asked questions about an item. The server said let me go ask and then disappeared for like 20 minutes and finally came back and had forgotten to get an answer. I gave up and ordered a salad. When our items finally came out, my salad was swimming in dressing and was almost inedible. My friend enjoyed her food but c'mon.   Poor service has been a problem the couple of times I've actually done table service. When I've sat at the bar or just picked up baked goods, no problem.

Oh yum! These bagels are the real deal. They are soft on the inside with a chewy crust. I've sampled the plain, poppy seed and the sesame seed. All were delicious AND the seeds don't pop off the bagel so that's awesome.  The last egg & cheese sandwich I got was so enormous that I ate it for 2 meals. Plus the strawberry cream cheese is perfect. Just fresh Louisiana strawberries cut into creamy cheese....mmmmmmmmmmmmmm.  My only complaints are the limited hours (at the moment Thursday - Sunday / 7-11 only). I can't wait for them expand days and to lunch!

My review is for dinner only... I scored seating on the porch on a Monday evening for a celebratory dinner with a friend mid-May.  It looked like the porch seating was only for tables for 2 since there still needs to be room to pass.  I was impressed with the menu and that there was a little something for everyone. My friend and I started with shrimp etouffee dumplings; these were delicious and that ginger sauce was amazing. I had the seafood salad and my friend had the duck mole dish. They were both very good and I was impressed with the seafood and size of my salad. I had also ordered the crawfish tortelli in case I as still hungry but I ended up taking that home to eat the next day.   For dessert we split the chocolate candy bar which was stunning. I mean delicious. I would go back just for it. Yummy. My friend got one of the signature cocktails and I had a refreshing glass of bubbles.   All staff was masked and social distancing was good.

I still miss the Blue Bird at this location... they had some hippie-ish egg dish that always set me right, but I am enjoying having Wakin Bakin in the neighborhood.  It's clean, affordable and quick!  They do have mimosas and the like if you want a boozy breakfast, but usually I'm in here and out pretty quickly. I am a fan of their biscuits so get those as an add on fsure. Last visit was just an OJ, scrambled eggs with swiss and a biscuit. Delicious and fast.  All the servers are friendly and efficient. Parking is on the street and don't neglect paying the meters!

Pandemic update: HB is open from 7-12 (or until they run out) Thursday- Sunday.   Last night I was really really craving a bagel with cream cheese so went over to HB's social media and discovered that they are open with social distancing. So I walked over this morning.  They've used their small tables as a barrier for their employees to keep them safe and distant. Everyone was wearing masks and they had markers on the floor to keep everyone apart.   I was tempted to get a sandwich... that veggie mix which looks delish (and is vegan) or the egg and spinach or ... or ... but I got my standard poppyseed bagel with strawberry cream cheese!   Easypeasy

I've been to the other locations in NOLA, but this is the original store and they have really cute clothes (some at OMG prices) and the staff is really nice.  The space is gorgeous with lots of exposed brick and really attractive displays of accessories.  The selection was good with a number of different styles and brands to appeal to a variety of customers and sizes.   Definitely a spot to find a casually elegant outfit to make you feel fabulous.

When I was hunting for a spot to go to lunch with the parents over in their neighborhood, this spot popped up. Since I had been to their new food truck recently (and Yelp deleted my new listing and collapsed it with the bricks and mortar spot on Carrollton, GRRRR). I thought why not.  They had good accessibility for my not so mobile Dad. And the staff was really sweet and helpful which I appreciate.  I had the veggie pho which was a huge amount and really tasty. My spring rolls with avocado and tofu were large and the tofu was fried really beautifully. Dad had the egg roll and grilled shrimp sliders (aka bacos) both of which he thoroughly enjoyed. Mom had the some of our apps and then had the grilled pork bun which she said was delicious and it was also a large portion. Mom is a bubble tea convert (gotta love the adventurous seniors) and got an avocado one with tapioca and said it was tasty. I got a strawberry lemonade and it was tart with big chunks of strawberries.   Definitely would pass back by for a meal. And I like that they have bar seating since I prefer that when dining alone.

Important things to know: They serve until 11 on weekends and the smoked tofu bun are life changing. I mean super delicious amazing and I want to go over there right now and get more.  Other things to know: service can be interesting. And the AC isn't the best at the moment because everything here is superhot. They are veggie/vegan friendly.   I enjoyed the crawgoons (or crawfish crab rangoons or whatever they're called). My General Tso's tofu was OK. And the seafood fried rice was fine.   And I still want that smoked tofu...

Arc does great work with the intellectually disabled in the greater New Orleans area.  They run a kitchen, a grounds keeping service, a garden and their carnival bead operation.  I was at this location on a recent Saturday (thanks @Shercole!) to volunteer to sell beads.  It was really fun and the paid workers were all extremely enthusiastic.  I loved working with some of the employed adults who were volunteering their time on the weekend.  The staff had king cake (made in house), soup samples and coffee for those who were volunteering AND those who were buying.    Donate your beads to the Arc after carnival is over & go buy the beads you need from them.  Sales are Saturdays from 9-1 until carnival weekend.

OMG! Now I know why I shouldn't be allowed in a restaurant supply house.  Why have I paid retail for much of this awesome kitchen stuff.
