I should clarify, I do not own a bar or restaurant, I just like kitchen stuff and Caire is open on Saturdays which worked out with a recent MacGyver like project we needed done ASAP.  (It involved ashtrays - 45 cents each here and rubberbands.)  I also perused their knives, bought some cartridges for my inherited soda thingy, and bought a giant food grade bucket with a lid.  PLUS they had a whole endcap of awesome oyster shucking stuff.  Good to know.  I'll be back

Pandemic update Quick update! They have limited their indoor seating with about half the tables taken out of service. They have floor markers at the queue to get you to space out. They also are asking for credit card/debit payment to limit contact. There is a nice patio out the back door which I always forget exists. PLUS they have a liquor license now.  I stopped in for lunch and my Mom LOVED her chicken salad sandwich. As always I wish there were more non-meat options but decided for a egg and cheese sandwich on a biscuit and it was tasty. PLUS amazing scones and a day old almond croissant.  Tasty and the staff was great.

I just noticed that my review from last year says no liquor license...they've had that since last summer so definitely in need of an update.  I have seriously never had a bad item here.  So worth a jaunt to the wank on a Friday night.  Reservations recommended.

I've used Dr. Ross as my gyn since 2006.  She's always been easy to talk to and makes sure you don't have any questions or issues.  The staff at her office has been efficient and professional.  So high marks all around. She is part of the Crescent City Physicians group.  Worst part about going? Getting weighed. Seriously. I just don't want to know.

Pandemic review: According to the counter person on Saturday (May 30th) this location has new owners and won't be Bevi any longer after crawfish season.  I was disappointed to be the only person in the place (customers and staff) to be wearing a mask. I was picking up take out for the elderly parents + crawfish for me. I had called in my order so at least I was in and out quickly.  My parents fried seafood dinner was plentiful and looked tasty. My crawfish were a nice size but OMG were they salty. Like I had to stop eating them salty. But don't you worry I pealed all the tails to use in a recipe where I'll eliminate the salt so it'll be OK.  It will be interesting to see what goes in this spot next. This location as Bevi was only open during crawfish season and seemed to have a lot of issues with hours... my parents had tried to go on multiple occasions only to find it closed.

Discoveries has those ridiculous late night ads with the catchy maybe- Bollywood tune and it's a local chain. I had passed the downtown store on several occasions but never stopped. Now there is one much closer to home.  The space feels like a well appointed warehouse more than a traditional furniture store but that works with their eclectic pieces. I was surprised to find so many housewares (especially local arts and crafts) in addition to the furniture. I may have to go back for those presidential glasses for my Dad's birthday.  Much of the furniture is big...so if you need to fill a large space this may be for you. They also had a metal closet/hanging rack that sort of looked like a wedding chuppah...if that makes sense. So if you need an insta-closet, it's pretty cool.  Definitely a great place to browse and find a quirky furniture piece or a great gift item.  This week (through 3/27) they were actually sponsoring a pop-up rug store from Togar Rugs out of North Carolina. And I fell in love with a Konya carpet and whim purchased a 5X7 rug. Yes, I have a problem.

Overdue review!  I've been to this location a few times since it opened. And I think it's a good replacement for the previous closed bakery. The staff is nice. The pastries are good and they are usually well stocked.  Plenty of seating and the light is wonderful. But for someone reason I almost never dine in. It's always pastries to go for me.   I need to suss out their beverage situation... I hate that the iced tea at the Jeff Davis location is made with concentrate so I'll have to ask about that. Plus the one time I ordered a hot chocolate here, I ended up with a mocha and I didn't realize until I was blocks away. Blech. (I know I'm a weirdo). Luckily I ran into a friend who was thrilled to be gifted a large mocha.

Now y'all know I love an independent bookstore and then couple that with this being in a two story Victorian? Charm galore. And the upstairs children's area with its murals is sure to inspire any child, or your inner child, whatever.   Plus it's a nerdist delight with tons of Dr. Who, Alice in Wonderland, and other fan-child swag on sale. The owner is knowledgeable and this is clearly her passion.   The selection is eclectic and they do host book signings. PLUS they also buy selected gently used books so you'll find those mixed in with the new stuff which I like.   I love that they are hosting a ton of book signings and author events as well as gaming events on Saturday nights.

Since this joint was rated best crawfish in some local publication in the spring, I had to check them out. And the crawfish they were solid. However, the potatoes and corn I purchased were inedible because they were soooo spicy. I actually had stopped in first thing when they opened and the crawfish weren't ready yet so I passed back by later in the day. So glad I made the effort.   I'm making myself sad typing this review up since crawfish are done until next spring...yes you can still buy them someplaces, but you will most likely be unhappy with the quality.  I need to get back over there to try their fried shrimp and gumbo.

Wow 12 years later for this review...  Octavia books is my go to local book store mostly. I like their local sections of cookbooks, fiction, history, whatnot. They also have a great section of staff recommendations.   I've always had great service from the staff here. I recently needed to order a few things as a gift and it was easy peasy and quick. I've also pre-ordered books with them to pick up as signed copies when they are released.   The store is large enough to for almost everyone to find something of interest and yet small enough to be very accessible.  Parking is mostly on the street. There is a very small parking lot on Laurel St and you can enter the store by the backdoor, but right now that space has some outdoor tables for the restaurant in the same building. Even in normal times I would not try the lot with a large vehicle.

So I was taking a visiting friend out to dinner and we settled on this spot. Honestly it really was meh.   The hardest part was that my friend is vegetarian and even the vegetable dishes here aren't. The beans are cooked with meat. And our server could not be bothered to assist us.   The tacos that I had (spinach & mushroom and fried shrimp) just didn't have much flavor.   The table and floor where we were seated were slightly grungy and really needed a good cleaning.   I'm sort of stunned at all the 5 star ratings. Maybe the drinks are really good?

I love a good Poke bowl and Kais offers some good selections. My friend said building her own bowl required too many decisions so she selected one of the chef's creations. I am too picky so I built my own. We were both very happy with our choices.  All the ingredients were fresh and tasty. The amount of food for the price was good. The bowls came up quickly. And you can pre-order online if you need to.  Also they have a vegan option with tempura and tofu!

In my frenzy to find a dress for my niece's wedding, I went into every dress shop I could think of. My sales person was very helpful and upbeat. She found a selection of dresses and understood what I was looking for. They didn't have a ton of items in my size. And I do think they do a lot of specialty ordering...which of course I was way too late to do.   They did have some really beautiful dresses and a variety of styles. PLUS what I saw was not the same items that I had seen in other shops around town. My sales person was great and not pushy. And didn't seem to mind that I showed up in a tshirt and tennis shoes.   Parking tip: there are only a few spots in the front but there is more parking around back and that parking lot exits to the sidestreet behind the shop.  Definitely a spot to check out for a special dress.

This specialty store on a side street off magazine is the perfect place to look for that vintage lighting fixture or lamp that will be the cherry on top for any room in your house.   They repair lamps and chandeliers, everything from replacing plugs to complete rewiring. They also carry a wide range of shades so if you need an off the wall shade for a vintage lamp, this is a good place to try.  They currently have a lamp that belonged to my grandparents for some minor repairs. I know it will come back working perfectly.

So SOS isn't just about giving tours to Cemeteries, they are a successful non-profit that has helped preserve the unique heritage of New Orleans cemeteries.  Many years ago cemeteries were being looted wholesale for their statuary and ornate bits; SOS made sure that these thefts made the news.  They also publish who is responsible for various small cemeteries on their website, so that if a neighbor wants to report an issue, they will actually know who to call.

Still a solid choice for Chinese in the Garden District and the owner is so very nice. I came in soaked to the skin on Bacchus Sunday and they were very kind about my wet foot prints and my wet butt on their, thankfully, vinyl chairs.   I was very grateful for their hot tea AND the vegetarian vegetable soup. Delicious and definitely restorative. My friend and I also shared crab ragoon, the green beans (on both the regular and traditional menu) and the shrimp with cashew (which was a little bland). All the food was tasty. And service was great.  Great now I want another cup of that soup.

So what's the person who doesn't eat pork doing reviewing this spot? I was in charge of ordering and acquiring a ham for an out of town relative.  Ordering online was super easy and you don't pay until you pick up. I was sort of concerned about the amount of time it would take to pick up, the day before Thanksgiving. But they were super organized and since I went around 9am, I was in and out in less 15 minutes.  The staff was hustling and it was easy. Bonus my family loved the ham.
I'm sorry folks.  I think it's over-rated.  I've had better elsewhere and it's insanely crowded.  The hype has taken over.

What a lovely whimsical little shop. I was charmed as were my nieces. Lots of original (and reprints) of animal themed art, as well as Alice in Wonderland and Bead Dogs. If you're looking for originals rather than reprints, consult with the sales person. All the pieces are the work of artist, Ally Burguieres.   We were also directed to a shop around the corner which prints some of the images on clothing. So if you fall in love with a sloth or a rubber duckie or a pig wearing a crown, you might be able to buy a print and a shirt.   I need to come back when not being tugged everywhich way by small people.

I had to stop by this downtown main branch of NOPL a week or two ago to pick up a misdelivered book. I had not been inside in over a decade. WOW have times changed.  I was impressed that a maintenance person was cleaning the exterior windows as we walked up and that there is a lobby with security guards (and a John Chase mural) who were there to make sure everyone behaved.  THEN we walked in and the public space is light and airy. LOVE the color coded endcaps to the shelving units. Blue, green and orange denoted fiction, non-fiction (I might have those switched) and other (like oversized). The staff was helpful and friendly.  We actually went into the staff area and could immediately tell that all the money went into the public spaces but again the back staff was super friendly and helpful.  We noticed a lot of comfy seating and computers in use. Parking is at meters on the street. But this location is at the intersection of two major bus lines and there are pay lots in the area. If you need parking, one of the more suburban locations may be for you.

Fish Fry Friday - pandemic edition I was scoping Fish Fry plates on the interwebs and saw that the Katie's plate came with a crabcake! Yes please.   I picked up 4 plates on Friday afternoon; I had called my order in and they were waiting when I arrived. They've set up the front of the store for good social distancing with everyone wearing masks and all the wipes downs on my card and pen for payment. Great job!  The food... the plates were delicious. The frips were yummy, crabcake was rich and the fried fish was crisp. Plus momma said they doctored those peas up good. We also got a side of fried okra which is always good here.  Definitely need to remember to cross town and order from them again soon.

In addtion to the standard Hallmark items, this store has lots (and lots) of local stuff, glassware, dish towels, decorative items, Saints, Pelicans, LSU, fleur di lis, you name it.   The staff is very accommodating and helpful. The store is spacious and full but not overwhelming. They have an anti-room with out of season gift items (in December this was Halloween & Carnival) in case you need it, plus lots of pet related gift items.  Love all their seasonal door hangers, in fact I received a giant king cake for my front door as a Christmas present.

Pandemic review: Since we're all cooking at home more AND I was in the neighborhood, I decided to stop in and stock up on a few things.  You can still peruse the shelves and they are limiting entrance (I think) but this wasn't an issue on the random Thursday afternoon that I was there. As always I was asked if I needed help and they directed me to the one item that I couldn't find. Loaded up on a bunch things: forks for work, baking mat, piping bag, paring knife, etc.  And checked out.   They've added a counter inside the warehouse to help with distancing and I was in and out pretty quickly even with my wandering and standing contemplating a variety of items before deciding what I really needed and where would I store that giant bowl, anyway...  Currently only open on weekdays.

Sometimes you just have to fight the parking lot at the suburban Whole Foods.  I think there is some sort of cosmic ray that makes most of the folks who park behave like imbeciles.  I don't have this problem with other suburban parking areas.  Still that's not a WF problem...unless they are sending the cosmic ray as part of some bizarro world experiment, hmmmm...  But I digress, I like the produce at this location, but seriously the displays in the middle make it almost impossible to pass even a small buggy through, especially when the store is crowded.  I agree with Andrea that there seems to be a whole lot less veggie stuff, but that's what their market wants, I guess.  I think their cheese & bulk food sections are top notch.

I had to rent a van to drive a bunch of coworkers to a meeting in rural Louisiana. The online booking process was easy and the staff was very nice when I arrived. (I picked this Metry location because it was close to the staff rendezvous location.)    BUT the van wasn't ready. Yes I know I was picking it up at 7:30 am but it was being cleaned until almost 8:15. The staff apologized but the van (while a fancy town & country) was still not clean. My coworkers ended up picking up trash from inside.  Also, while I didn't have an issue since I was booking on a corporate account, there seemed to be much drama regarding new rules for folks trying to rent a car with a debit card. So look into that if you don't have a credit card....

My cousin planned my uncle's 80th birthday party here and it was GREAT! We had the entire porch area for our group. My cousin said the staff was great to work with and everyone loved their food. We had boats full of boiled crabs and shrimp, along with sausage, potatoes, corn and brussel sprouts. There were trays of jambalaya and seafood pasta. We also had a couple of different appetizers. Everything was delicious. We had a cash bar and the staff was hopping to keep up with the demand of our group as well as everyone else.   My uncle was so surprised and had a great time. A+++ all the way around.

Updating to 4 stars because I got to watch the classy way a rando was booted tonight...after he fell on the floor from his barstool and his pants fell down around his ankles. Re explained to him (after the bartender told him to leave). "It's just not cool, man." Classic   Oh and then Re threw her beer to the ground in anger over the unripe RNA that Katie was discussing...or something like that. I can say definitely that beer hit the ground and that RNA was discussed because we're all sciencey like that.   Cheap drinks, dark as sin, and a good time until the college crowd or jerk tourists invade. Plus it's dog friendly so Chunky can hang out with us. Understandable why Katie is the reigning duchess.

Wow! A group from my work went to Francesca's yesterday and what a great meal! You order at the counter which prevents the horrors of splitting the bill after the meal.   Their menu is varied and had something to please all of us. Amongst the six of us we had sausage and peppers, cochon de lait + shrimp, fried grouper, lakeview (cheese and veggies), turkey panini, and a muffaletta. Oh and delicious fried okra and frips (fries cut into thin strips). Everyone really enjoyed their food. Service was quick (even during a busy lunch) and the space is clean!  There are a few parking spots out front and along the side (maybe in back?) but we parked on the street. I was racking my brain trying to remember what this spot used to be then a friend reminded me. This is the location of the pre-K Charlie's poboys and most recently Koz's. Great addition to the neighborhood!

So, of course, it's John's fault that I went here. I haven't stepped foot in this bar since High School and really another 20+ years will just be fine.  Same people just different bodies.  I've never understood the appeal of these cavernous spaces with bad acoustics and questionable liquor.  Thanks for reminding me that I'd rather drink at home then spend even $2 on a holla.  Also, there are all sorts of sketchy rules (mostly to comply with the neighborhood association who would love to shut them down): everyone had to have their IDs scanned, even though most of us ...are a bit older than 21, we all had to wear "drinking bracelets" and you weren't allowed to leave with your nasty drink.

So I had been hearing about Gerald's for a while and when I was leaving Chalmette National Cemetery on Friday, I passed by AND saw they were advertising fried shrimp sliders so I u-turned and headed back.  I bought shrimp sliders (sold as 1, 3, 6 or 12) dressed and 3 donuts (y'know for a representative sample) and a GIANT iced tea. The sliders were DELICIOUS; yes it was basically a fried shrimp poboy but on soft rolls with added onion. And yes I am a fan.   The donuts were fine to very good. I had ordered a glazed, chocolate glazed and a cake. The cake donut was the weakest and I still wolfed it down. The chocolate glazed was the best and tasted like cocoa.  Oh all this deliciousness + the life-giving giant tea? Just over $8.  Oh yeah I'll be driving back to Arabi soon.

We used the Bank to strip some shutters and doors at our old house and they did a great job.  I also spent hours one afternoon hunting for a matching doorknob to complete a set (Yes, I have OCD. Why do you ask?)  The random vintage salvage stuff that is available is just amazing.

I finally made it to RetroActive's new space on Oak Street and wow! The store looks great. The selection is much smaller than before but that just means you're not sorting through...lesser quality items.   The first floor is devoted to women's clothing and jewelry and the 2nd floor is devoted to men's items. That's right a whole floor for men's vintage, not just a rack...or y'know nothing.  Staff is helpful and courteous. The store is light, bright and airy.

Watcha gonna do. If you want lights/air/gas, you have to deal with Entergy.   But I will give them the benefit of a 3rd star because I was NOT one of the 7000 households uptown without power this afternoon.  And why did the power go out this afternoon? Because it rained...which never happens in New Orleans.

I stopped in while shopping with my Mom on Magazine Street. She had requested middle eastern food so Vida's fit the bill. When we arrived we were the only diners (around noon on a Friday) and we were a bit confused as to which door to enter. (The one all the way in the back). The menu is really interesting and has a lot of variety. All sandwiches can be made veggie so that's a plus.  I had lentil soup and the avocado bravo salad (which featured barberries...and they were tasty so that was a new food for me) and a Turkish spinach pie. All were delicious. My Mom had a Gyro Muffaletta (and she planned to bring 1/2 home to my Dad but she gobbled it up instead).   We also enjoyed some really yummy flan and Turkish tea which was beautifully presented.   Bonus in that there is off street parking at Jena and Magazine although the parking lot is a bit narrow.

Um so it can't be called Camellia Grill because of a contract dispute with the original owners, but the decor, the menu, the staff, it's all Camellia.  The food is the same as the original uptown location which is reliable diner food. In the past month, I've had a tuna salad sandwich (and stole fries from a friend) and then a late night pecan waffle...although they did break my heart by not having cane syrup to go with the waffle. C'mon people.  The chocolate freeze is still delicious and, yes, I gave myself a headache. Plus points for excellent ice in their ice teas & cokes.

Tiny storefront that sells salads, juice, smoothies, raw bars, and supplements.  I tried the superfood salad and it was really delicious.  I also went for a juice spritzer that was pretty tasty...and affordable.  Not my usual sort of spot but when you're in the mood, they hit the spot.

Bon Temps goes down a star for me since they closed their kitchen.  The band space is "intimate" so that can be amazing or awful depending on the band.   And maybe the crowd has changed or maybe I have, but this is no longer a place that I am comfortable hanging out for hours on end.  *I have been informed that their kitchen is open randomly...OK that's odd.

Five Happiness is the Chinese food of childhood...only a little fancier.  They've done a great renovation on the inside and it's really pretty, but you pay for the pretty in the prices.  Because of all the smaller rooms, it's a great place to bring a large group.  I'm a big fan of the shrimp toast and the moo shu.  My niece got the triple dragon and really liked it.    Plus they have all the ridiculous 1950s tiki style drinks.  And even the shirley temple comes with a fans & fruit.

Still my fave sushi place...maybe it's partially since I can walk there. And I feel like Norm! when I walk in.  Sometimes the fish is not cut as precisely as it should be but it's always fresh.  And the seaweed udon is E's comfort staple.   The table under the stairs is awful and the very back room is super loud so avoid those if you can.    If only they had inari then all would be right with the world...

I'm going with four stars because while the food was fine, the location and ambiance was definitely 5.   I had a salad with redfish...yes I know...what is my problem with getting salads in places that I shouldn't, but it was good with a yummy remoulade dressing and my piece of fish was delicious. I also tried the corn and crab soup...which was odd, really peppery but sort of thin. It was OK just not what I was expecting; maybe I should have known since the menu says soup rather than bisque.  Finally I had the onion rings which were perfect.  The restaurant is loud when full and the service was still working out a few bobbles when I was there. The most confusing part is the dual entrances. If you need to take the elevator to this highly elevated space, you end up at the back of the restaurant BUT this is where the hostess stand is. If you enter through the steps (closer to the lake) then you enter into the bar area and that's where the wait staff beverage station is. A bit confusing.  Really, I can't wait to go back at sunset and enjoy a cocktail and fried everything on the porch.
Just ate the pad cashew and it was delicious.  Super fresh veggies & the tofu was extra yummy.

This is one of those shops that I can't believe I haven't reviewed, as I've stopped in here for years. They have plenty of moderately price jewelry and housewares and doodads that make great gifts...if you have the girly sorts to purchase for.  Another I like about this shop, it's not packed to the roof with stock. You can actually peruse without being overwhelmed and move without fearing that you're going to take out a shelving unit of glassware. WHEW.  The staff has always been helpful without being push and there is often free wine while you shop (BONUS). Sometimes I hit the jackpot and sometimes not.   The upstairs (ok 3 steps) back room is a separate business so be prepared to use your card twice if you want merchandise from both spaces.
Solid gas station in the Garden District. It is well lit at night and the pumps always work. I've never used the minimart here. Gas prices reflect the scarcity of stations in the area.

Thimbelina is not my usual alterations place (only because of location) but I recently bought a pair of jeans that was almost 8 inches too long.  I was advised by fashionable type people that I had to get original hem and that Thimbelina was one of the top places to do that.  My drop  off & pick up were easy...although the shop was packed with ladies getting their last minute ball gown alterations for carnival.  My jeans were ready in 2 weeks and the original hem was only about a dollar more than regular pants (or maybe the dollar more was for jeans?)  They accept cash & checks only.

ummm...y'all, I may have a problem.  We went to Casamento's 2 Fridays in a row and now I want their gumbo every Friday.  I want to be one of those old ladies who dines at the same place every day and gets the exact same thing.  It has now been 2 weeks since I ate at Casamento's.  We'll see if I make it to a month without going back.  If you see me checkin, start planning the intervention.

I evidently reviewed the airport governing board last time oops.  So the Nashville airport is really clean and just about every time I've been in there has been live music somewhere.  Security and signage are good.  I do like that they have a by the minute chair massage place on the concourse.

I had a love/hate relationship with the old F&J restaurant. When it was good, it was great but when it was bad...hoo boy.  So I went in with high hopes and left a little disappointed. I thought the food was a little pricey for what it was. My grilled shrimp salad was meh. No grill flavor and I wasn't wowed...but yes I know that's my fault. Why do I insist on getting non-fried stuff and salad at places like this. My nieces fried shrimp poboys were better. But our fries were almost raw (and delivered after we were finished out meal) as were the yummier onion rings.  The place does seem cleaner and they've moved out the games in the front in favor of more booths. The clientele did seem to be skewing a bit older.  I will give them another try sometime when I'm craving fried seafood...or when boiled crawfish are in season.   BTW: Gambit says Happy Hour from 2-6pm Monday through Friday.  25% off liquor,  beer, wine and oysters

One of the two essential Elmer's in New Orleans.  This is the one who makes CheeWees, the local pre-cursor to the far inferior cheetos.  Elmer's was on hiatus for awhile after Katrina and I feared they were gone.  When I found them in stores again, I bought 6 bags and gobbled them up.  My favorite is BBQ.  They also make an excellent (and addictive) caramel corn.

This another one of those places that I can't believe I haven't reviewed. I've been going to this hardware store since I was a child.   It covers all the basic hardware stuff PLUS it has crawfish boiling setups, porch swings, crab nets, and a ton of pretty, pretty rocks.    The rocks are why you may not want to bring a child with you. I always begged for these pretty shinies back in the day. And the answer was always "but what are you going to do with it?"  Clearly I was going to name it my precious and love it for all of my days...except no one ever bought the shiny rocks for me...and they still tempt me to this day.  Anyway, it's a great hardware store.

Ah, Hubig's, you make a vegetarian eat lard and like it.  The quintessential bad for you NOLA snack food.  I've even sampled the elusive blackberry!  Peach and apple are my favorites.  My brother swore that strawberry in his work vending machine could turn an entire bad week around.  This address is the manufacturing plant; pies may be purchased at almost any grocery, convenience store or other sensible retailer.

So don't go into this museum expecting an enormous collection, despite it's outside appearance it's actually rather small in square footage, although it is pretty tall.   The collection originated with the personal collection of Roger Ogden. And obviously it focuses on Southern art. The special exhibits are always worth viewing; the recent Basquiat and the Bayou was particularly good.   Well curated and they offer lots of after hours programming to draw more folks into the museum. Follow Jen B's advice regarding zooming to the top then wandering down.

I was really excited to try Atomic Burger. Their philosophy of offering elevated fast food with different & healthier choices definitely appealed to me.  Tonight I drove through and got a regular edamame, a portabella burger and a chocolate shake...so that was kind of a lot of food for me. The regular edamame was equivalent to an appetizer order at a Japanese restaurant and was great. The portabella burger came with carmelized onions (yum) and good quality swiss cheese. I definitely should not have attempted to eat this in my car. Yummy & messy.  The chocolate shake was really good. It actually tasted like chocolate & milk and not chemicals.   I hope this idea succeeds.

I must not have gotten Rene's amazing tech. So my pedicure was fine. Nothing spectacular and it was done well. Maybe if I wanted a gel manicure....  I will say that the salon was really clean and yes, the instruments are autoclaved. The salon is also small. There were only 2 techs working on the afternoon that I went in..although I think a 3rd one came in as I was finishing up for the after work crowd.   It was a fine experience and I would go back but I probably wouldn't go out of my way.

Hmm... don't know where all the dislike is.  I've had a tire fixed here in 2006 (when I had tires fixed all over town) and they were fine.  I've gotten gas here and it is expensive because they are the only station in the area.  All Uptown gas is expensive.    AND they are the only Orleans parish brake tag station uptown. I must have hit it just right this afternoon because there was no line and I was in and out in 10 minutes.  The guy who helped me was business like and polite.

Another interesting used clothing store on Oak Street. The selection is a bit more curated than most shops with an emphasis on a boho style. There are equal amounts of men and women's clothes along with some accessories.  When I stopped in, the owner (I think) was actually in the shop and she was repricing winter coats at a discount. If her style is yours, you will rack up. If not, you might find an accessory to your liking.  Extra star for actually carrying men's clothing.

So I was just checking times/locations for brake tag/inspection sticker replacement and Uptown Shell is no longer on the list. Not sure if that's a city error or they're no longer offering the service.  http://new.nola.gov/brake-tags/

If I update this review from birth until I or Yelp is done on this earth, I can't believe I'll ever rate them less than 5 stars. If for some reason I had to, it would probably break my heart. I LOVE, LOVE, LOVE this place.  Yesterday, was St. Joseph's Day and when fellow yelper, Lindsay A and I were talking about dinner, we didn't know what we wanted but we knew we wanted dessert here. We wandered in (and there wasn't too much of a line!) and ordered mocha gelato and a blood orange ice plus we each got the special for San Giuseppe Sfinge, which was puff pastry with cannoli cream with a cherry and candied orange. So much goodness. We got to check out their altar (which is much smaller these days than I remember it in the 80s) and enjoy all the passersby.  At Jazz Fest, Brocato's has a booth at Food 1 and sells spumoni and few other items so I always try to stop by. Back when I was a little girl and fest was MUCH less crowded, I was allowed to cross the fairgrounds by myself to buy myself a wedge (for $1) and then I would gobble it up as I walked back so I wouldn't have to share it with my brothers.   In my family, the mango ice is one of the first real people foods that new babies are allowed to eat, ensuring that their taste buds are set for life.   When they reopened after K, I cried and cried because I was so happy they were back. See it's just true love.

I came here with my family last weekend...and none of us got the burgers. I know we're weird.  So take my review for all the non-burger options.  Nieces got the kid's grilled cheese and the non-picky one  loved it and crammed her fries on her bun to make a "cheese fry sandwich." Clearly she is a genius. The picky one ate a couple of fries and the ate 1/4 of her sandwich in exchange for playing on my phone.  However the non-picky kid would not eat/drink her root beer float because the ice cream had "pepper in it." The restaurant has recently switched to New Orleans ice cream (yay!) and are using a vanilla bean ice cream which weirds out 7 year olds.  E had the veggie burger which was kind of gross looking (really black bean paste w/ black beans in it?) and he said was pretty bland.  I had the sashimi tuna salad, rare.  Tuna was OK but not great and again the cheapest ingredient (the lettuce) was tired and kind of gross looking.  My brother had the grilled chicken salad and seemed to like it.  My SiL had a baked potato and fried pickles.  Both were OK.  The service was good and ice tea refills were plentiful.

Woldenberg park is a wonderful way to stroll along the river.  Hard to believe this idyllic park (and location for many an outdoor festival) was carved out of old warehouse/wharf space just 20-ish years ago.  Love the statue of Mr. Woldenberg on a bench.  -1 star because some of the infrastructure (stages, sidewalks, etc) are in serious need of rehabilitating.

There is not a great deal on the menu here for the non-meat eater...but that's kind of obvious with the name. However, their mac n cheese was AMAZING. Seriously, I think it was cooked in a mini cast iron skillet because it had delicious crispy cheesy bits that Anita M & I had to divy up exactly.  So so good. I think it was the muenster.  We also split a shrimp chop salad which was also really good. And a Marguerita pizza which was OK. I think it was just a little under-done because Lindsay A loves their pizza and raves about the crisp cracker crust...which we didn't get. So maybe next time.  Finally, we had the super chocolate dessert...the name was cute, but I can't remember it. It was again delicious. My only problem with the dessert menu is that it is printed in red ink on cream paper; in a comfotably lit room that's tough on the old peepers.  I had a glass of their sangria which was good...but maybe too much cinnamon for me. Will defintely be back.

Another gas station review...because I didn't go in the store so I cannot confirm Margaux's no ice cream lament. The gas is inexpensive, but the lanes are weirdly tight.  I would NEVER want to be at the middle pump on the inside...you'd never escape the place.  Several people drove up to the air pump and were disappointed by the big out of order sign. This is the last gas before the interstate entrance at the Orleans Parish end of Veteran's so plan accordingly.

Just went back because it was the 2 year old niece's birthday party.  And guess what?  It was the grand reopening of the grocery store sponsored by Winn Dixie.  My Mom looks at her watch and says "it's 11; I'll be back."  I guess all the festivities started at 11.  The 5 year old niece LOVED the freshly stocked grocery and had much fun with the mini-grocery cart.  The staff was great and super patient.  Plus some of the student volunteers started line dancing to the Radio Disney music that was blaring.  So I was sufficiently entertained.

I feel like I should love Publiq House more...it's in my neighborhood and the space is big and airy and I like the decor, but something is lacking...Despite the beautiful renovation of this building, it's just not welcoming, but that problem is more with the people than the space.  Maybe it was that during my interactions with multiple staff members, only one was actually pleasant. Sure some were busy but c'mon it wasn't so busy that you could have smiled or SOMETHING.  I was here most recently for the Gambit Y'at Speak awards (AKA twitter prom) and was trying to use their wifi on my tablet since my phone is sad and dying... I asked 3 or 4 people for the complicated password (sorry don't remember it) and only 1 would pause long enough to make sure I understood them.  I would stop by again if a band I wanted to hear was playing or if friends wanted to go, but this definitely wouldn't be my first choice to stop in for a drink.

Sunday night I wanted Vietnamese food and after checking Yelp, I discovered that my 1st, 2nd, and 3rd choices were all closed. Thwarted! With further investigation, I discovered that Tan Dinh was open. Yay!  The menu is huge! Almost worringly so, but I stuck with the one page veggie menu and we got tofu spring rolls which were fine.  I liked that the peanut sauce was bit spicier than usual.  Then I got tamarind tofu bun (next time I'll ask for extra sauce), which was seriously so huge that I couldn't finish it at lunch today.  E got the spicy tofu with fried rice cakes.  Everything was tasty and fast and super cheap.  While Tan Dinh may not be my first choice, they are definitely a spot I would visit again.

About a year ago, I went to the Fairgrounds for an actual race.  It was part of a fundraiser so we had a buffet lunch and were up in the top part of the grandstand (can't remember the name for the level...maybe clubhouse).  The food was really good but my group overwhelmed the bartenders and we ended up heading down to the next level to beat the crush.  I needed a cocktail to help decide on which color horse or silk to bet on; I am so scientific.  I was surprised at how into the racing I got.  Learning who the jockeys and the horses were and where they were from was really fun.  Prior to that trip, I've been to the Fairgrounds every spring since I was about 5 or 6 to attend Jazz Fest.  The grounds are an excellent setting.  I do miss the old grandstand though...stupid fires.

18 months later and I'm sticking with my 4 stars. I've been back several times with family, friends and work people. The food is consistent and the atmosphere is laid back. I got the stuffed crab for the 1st time and it was delicious.  Yesterday the downstairs was open with a limited menu, burgers, shrimp tacos, etc. But not the boiled seafood which seemed weird to me. I would have loved to sit outside but the menu was a bit too limited for my family group.  Parking can be tight especially on a beautiful Sunday afternoon but there is usually plenty of parking across the boulevard by the levee. My only criticism is the volume. It's a loud restaurant and wish they could get that under control. It made it hard to have a conversation with the group at my table.

The best ice in the city.  They have traditional flavors so if you're looking for something wacky this isn't the place for you.  They are only open from May to August.  Now I want a snowball even though it's January.

Barkus is a great time for a great cause.  Who doesn't like dogs in costumes?  That being said it's really crowded in sections the dogs seem stressed and the spectators who bring dogs don't practice enough leash control.

Way past time to update my review. I usually eat at this yummy food truck about once a week when they are parked neat my work.  Rachel & Benoit treat me like family even saving me special items that they think I'll like.  The food is always tasty & fresh.  They offer innovative vegetarian options abd even got me to enjoy roasted turnips today.  Their battles to get food truck legislation modernized in NOLA means that we will all reap the benefits.   Bonus check out Chef Benoit on Padma's Picks for TopChef New Orleans (http://www.bravotv.com/top-chef/season-11/videos/padmas-picks) episode 5: Food Truck Wars.

I've been a fan of Antoine's since before Katrina when they were located on the Old Freret Street (current location of High Hat). Post-K they were on the WB and now they've move to the Metrys.  The location is spacious, bright and smells delicious! The cases are brightly lit and sparkling (see my pics). The staff was nice and checkout was easy.  There was a small coffee station so I'm not sure if they sell coffee or were giving it away for the grand opening.  I sampled a piece of king cake (out of season I know all bad luck in the city of NOLA will be my fault for the next year but free pastry and I am powerless) which was delicious and bought a cinnamon roll which was light and fluffy and yummy. The other pastries were seriously tempting and they even have Russian cake which I'll have to bring to my mom.

I've eaten/snacked at the bar at least twice. And had dinner in the restaurant section twice AND had just cocktails. And I can definitely say I'm a fan.  The food is great which is what I expected from Chef Chris Shortall, formerly at the popup in 12 Mile. The cocktails are DELICOUS. But these are handcrafted beverages of love so expect to pay...and wait if the joint is busy. I'm a fan of the Missionary's Downfall, the Pina Colada, the Rum Old Fashioned (because of course) and the Pearl Diver...which is disturbingly buttery for a cold drink.   The staff has mostly been extremely friendly and polite. The decor is fun and inviting.   Definitely one of my new gotos in the FQ

I checked out Sterling Silvia just before Christmas while I was in a frenzy of last minute shopping.  While I didn't find any last minute gifts, I did find a gift for me!    Seriously, this shop does have something for just about everyone from skulls to fleurs.  In addition to jewelry there are some housewares and miscellaneous stuff.    Lots and lots of local items that were super cute.

I stopped by the Cork & Bottle at the same time as the Mid City Green Market.  They were having a wine tasting and the wines were mighty tasty.  I was impressed with their stock & the sales people were helpful but not pushy.    PLUS, they have their bourbon selection bottled by a company in Kentucky.  How cool is that?  And did I mention that it's a mighty tasty bourbon too.

This is a great little lunch/breakfast spot in a busy business corridor. I don't know that it's the best place for a quick coffee, but if you need eats.   The last time I stopped in everyone was pleasant, even though it was a weekend. And my only big issue was the customers in front of me...who were relaying an order via a phone call for a delayed companion. C'mon. Try to hustle it up.  I was between stops so got a breakfast biscuit to go and it was tasty. If I was in the area more often...

Again, I don't normally write reviews for national chains, but I make exceptions.  This is my go to CVS because I can walk to it from my house.  The staff is helpful to indifferent...like most places.    But the real reason I like this place is that it was one of the few places open when we snuck in to the city in September 2005.  And one of the only places that had alcohol.  Which you really needed after seeing everything that had happened, even in the sliver by the river.

This is a pretty small gas station which also has a garage. Gas prices are usually a bit high but it's the only pump around, so that's to be expected.  They get +1 star for the absurdity of Shell Fest...which is a party in the gas station parking lot during Jazz Fest. You can pay big bucks to park here and then party away the rest of the evening...in a gas station parking lot.  I must admit, I've only ever wandered by the party since I was usually hell bent for a shower by the time I left the fairgrounds.

Chill Out Café was named best Thai restaurant by New Orleans magazine late last year.  Best Thai?! And I hadn't eaten there? How could this be?  After scoping out the location on my shopping-palooza trip earlier this month, E & I went for dinner on a chilly, rainy Friday night.   The menu is eclectic to say the least.  Traditional American breakfast is served all day as well as Thai specialties and gumbo thrown in for good measure.  I stuck with the red curry (I have an obsessive devotion to Thai curries) and E was intrigued by green bean noodles (I think) - they turned out to be glass noodles with veggies though.  Both dishes were very good and service was quick, especially considering that the only server (who is also an owner, I think) was very pregnant.   It's a small restaurant with maybe 10 tables inside (and as many outside on the porch I think).  Outside was not an option that night.  The Thai menu is limited compared to other restaurants in town.  But what they have, they seem to make very well.  The prices are VERY good.

So delicious, but really formal.  You have to be ready for the stuffy and to be stuffed.  I had a poached pear salad once that I still dream about.  That said when I've been with friends with kids, the staff has been incredibly sweet to the children.

Another one of those how have I not reviewed this yet.  I love Casamento's.  The seafood is always good and fresh.  And I love that my grandmother went as a child.  Just remember to stay out of the servers way while you're in line and it's all good.

Canal Place will be closing for extensive renovations in about a month (October 2009).  They should reopen sometime next year with a new management company.  Goodbye Landmark; you've served us well.  I'm keeping my fingers crossed that the new company (Mississippi-based) will keep their promises and maintain Canal Place's Indy cred.

It's a Walgreens...but with a deceptively large parking lot so that's pretty helpful since this is a really crowded section of Magazine.    The staff seems competent and no one cursed me out so that's a plus. (Yes, this has happened at other Walgreens in the city)  The store is clean and well-stocked...  If it was closer, I'd probably stop in more often

Solid neighborhood bar with a good selection of beers and liquors.  As always if you're driving over to Algiers, I can get lost getting to the point. It is much easier to take the ferry.  On the gorgeous spring afternoon, I was last hear (Yay for the Party Bus Wank Bar tour) the windows were all open so any smoke was quickly dissipated.  Loved that the regulars were tolerant of our shenanigans.  Random fact: the first time I ever came here was the Bonerama CD release party since they recorded their first CD live here.

Let's start with the good, I really enjoyed my food. They start you with complementary roasted/fried chickpeas and some pickles which are both tasty and welcome.  I had the tuna nuevo tacos...which were really lettuce wraps since no tortilla but they were delicious! I enjoyed my salad, the aguacate, although the dressing was not really very garlicy. The queso fundido (say fundido repeatedly to your server...she will not be amused) was yummy too. Anita had the traditional shrimp tacos and really liked those (plus this was her 2nd or 3rd time dining).   And I enjoyed my cuba libre with mexican coke...which comes with a shot glass of rum and whole bottle coke so mix as needed.  The weird, the manager/host who sat us was a little too used car salesman-y and was sort of off-putting. He finally figured out that we didn't need the sales pitch and wandered away. The server takes your order and immediately inputs into a big tablet/iPad. Which looks really techy, but seems really awkward.   The annoying, I know this parking lot is really tiny and it makes sense to have a valet but I hate valeting my car. I would never survive in California. OTH the valets were extremely professional and polite and it's free and it does beat hunting for parking only to find an inept person has taken up 2 spots.  They've done a beautiful renovation of this building...it's light and airy and modern. A far cry from it's last 2 incarnations. Since these folks have successfully developed other local chain restaurants, I expect a Mizado Cocina will soon be opening in other locations.

I have a life long love affair with Angelo Brocato's and the spumoni is as good today as it was when I was 6.  Now though I also enjoy the cannoli, the mango ice...OK, I'm making myself hungry.    You just can't go wrong.

Looks like Mojo is going to break the jinx on this location as they are busy most times when I drive by. Love that they are open until midnight every night of the week in case I get a late night pastry hankering.   The space is airy and bright with lots of scattered tables and both studiers and people talking quietly.   And yay for having several iced tea choices!

Markey Park is a great neighborhood park/playground.  I noticed the new playground equipment for the kids when I was there on Saturday and it looked really fun & was COVERED in children, so that's a good sign.  I know the folks who live in the neighborhood appreciate the open space.  I've mostly come here for events, like the now defunct (?) arts market and last weekend the Mirliton Festival.

The weather was terrible and we were late so selection was limited by the time we arrived. Love that this space is so open and that there is a spot to buy all this fresh fruit and veg.  Great space to move around and enjoyed that there was some prepared food as well as all the fresh items.   Great clean restrooms and spacious parking lot.

How have I never eaten the gumbo at Casamento's?  Really it's just a crime.  E had the oyster stew in memory of his Dad. I had the gumbo and then we had some delicious fried oysters & shrimps.  So glad they have reopened this fall and that Mike is still the man shucking the oyster.  Dinner is much less crowded but they are only open on Thursday-Saturday nights and close @ 9, I think.

Last time I was there, I couldn't get my mother to leave.  Maybe she's just a retired child at heart.  Great fun exhibits and educational stuff.  And you can have a child's birthday party there too.  My niece loved that her chair was one that "a princess would sit in."

First this is a new, super-clean store with actual helpful employees who were not grumpy. So Yay for that.  Second, I hate the parking lot which isn't really WD's fault since they share it with lots of other businesses. Cars back up on Carrollton trying to get in and why not exits/entrances on N.Solomon. That would help so much.  We ran in quickly to buy a couple of items on our way to Jazz Fest so not a real grocery trip. Definitely would stop in if it were closer to my house.

If I ever went back to eating meat, it would be because of a Dom's roast beef & swiss.  The seafood is always fresh and the bread is good.  No I don't wait in the long lines, but will pop in when it's not too crowded.  As a bonus, if you eat in, you smell like fried for awhile, but that's a good thing, right?

So maybe it was the hour, but the evening started to decline. Physically this was the smallest bar space so getting to it to order a drink was tough. Another bar more karaoke (Saturday night only), which definitely had some regulars singing their favorites.  The welcome from the staff and patrons was...odd since it made you feel like strangers never walk into the bar. Or maybe I was just getting paranoid.

The only independent movie theater in NOLA.  It was definitely an afterthought when the building was designed.  The smaller theaters are so intimate you feel like you're in someone's living room.  They do have good snacks.

Interesting shop; it seems like it is a cleaner/neater version of something that belongs on magazine st. There are lot of different booths with a wide variety of items. Everything from re-purposed furniture to shabby chic furnishings to vintage Americana to original art.  I will definitely head back over come Christmas shopping time.  Things I was tempted to buy: a 1930s era photo of Grand Isle, an xray photograph of a flower by a retired MD, a vintage spice cabinet, and several gaudy costume broaches.   The store actually faces Focis, but you can't miss the round, former waterbed store in front of it.

I was running errands before work on a weekday and realized I was STARVING. I stopped in for a breakfast sammich and was very pleased. The space was bigger than I expected. The menu was pretty big, but I just got a bagel sandwich to go and a pastry out of the display. Both items were tasty and the iced tea was strong and not bitter.  The staff was lovely and helpful and the store was really clean. I didn't think service was slow as other folks have commented but I knew I was asking for a freshly cooked item.  I need to remember to stop in more often.

The ice is so perfect...and the flavors are still excellent with no taint of chemical aftertaste that you get with cheaper syrups.  It doesn't have as many flavors b/c the ones it does have are done right.

I went for lunch last week with a group of work peeps. Only 1 of us opted for the lunch buffet which was very meaty, if that's your thing. The rest of us ordered off the menu: 1 shrimp poboy, 2 ital plates, 1 jerk chicken and 1 mixed jerk plate. I loved my ital plate... callaloo, beans & rice, plantains and a veg...OK the veg that day was cooked cabbage which is not my favorite but it was a good value for the money and I actually ate the rest at a 2nd meal. My coworkers enjoyed their poboy and jerk chicken. The person who had the buffet loved the variety of meats (which are unlabeled so ask if there is something you don't/can't eat).   The service was really friendly and the decor was basic but clean. My iced tea was sweetened and I wish I had been warned, I would have gone with a Jamaican drink or water.   I'm glad I finally got to visit and I'll have to go back to sample more of the menu.

I was hunting for some place to have lunch on a Sunday afternoon around 2 p.m. Surprisingly what was open was crowded and lots of places were closed.   My friend suggested this restaurant because he liked the pad thai. I was really pleased with both the selection and the descriptions. Since I'm a curry fiend, I was excited to see a wide variety, offered with a choice of proteins. They also had a veggie page which was divided into true vegetarian items and those that include fish sauce. I had panang curry with veggies & tofu and it was delicious.    My friend decided to try dessert which was sticky sweet rice & custard. The dessert was ok, but not something I would need to order again.   Service was attentive and the price was good. Definitely a spot I'd try again.

I was excited for a new tea shop in town and who doesn't want to go sniff all the spices (in a non-creepy way of course). But I was disappointed in the tea selection which leaned more to fruity florals rather than actual varietals of green, black or white tea. And the prices were high for what they had too.  I did buy a few items and the spices were very fresh and you could buy a small amount which is nice and some of their mixes were innovative and tasty. But yeah this is a local franchise of a national chain and it didn't really have much to do with it's FQ location.  Also if you're in the store when the culinary tour stops in, prepare yourself for drunken folks standing around in the way. A nice departure from the usual tourist haunts but I won't go out of my way to get down here again.

Posting a whole slew of reviews for stores I hit with my Mom on Black Friday. My review is for their retail store rather than for their spa services.  Earthsavers carries a variety of upscale brands, like Kiehls, Jack Black (for men), and Bliss.  The prices are comparable to the mall stores.  They also carry baby lines, gift items, and few shoes.  My only real complaint is my fear that I will knock over an entire display in the very narrow store with my purse.

I've been wanting to make it to Boucherie since I read Christy's review in  February.  And it has been worth the wait.    The specialty cocktails were delicious as were the old favorites (the cougar, sazerac, and a mint julep).    The appetizers were tasty. Seriously the best french fries I've ever eaten.   The shrimp & grit cakes were as good as everyone said.  The only blah moment was a the salad which was OK but not really anything special.  The entrees were equally good; two of us got the smoked scallops which weren't super smokey but were very tasty with a nice bright herby sauce and spaetzle.  We also had the puppy drum which was really well cooked.  And then we had dessert (and my stomach still hurts).  We had the special apple gallette with ice cream (can't remember the flavor but it was spiced with cardomon, yum), the thai chili chocolate chess pie (not sure why it was a chess pie but it was like a super rich melty brownie with a kick of an aftertaste) and the krispy kreme bread pudding.  Seriously the bread pudding is insane.  And I didn't think the prices were that high.  5 cocktails, 3 courses for 3 people and the bill was around $135.

Lovely pre-fixe menu in a private room on the 3rd floor (yes there is an elevator) for a family event.  The staff was AMAZING and so kind when one of our more senior attendees knocked her diet coke over. They hustled to clean it up while making her feel better about the accident. They let me wander around a bit with the younger nieces to keep them entertained and since we weren't causing problems just smiled at us.  I had a lovely salad and great piece of fish (I think we had 2 choices for entree which had all been planned in advance by our hostesses). And then there was that pot of creme. OMG that was delicious.  I definitely need to get back over here, especially for those $5 French 75s at their happy hour!

Fleurty Girl's shirts have been available online & at Storyville until this weekend.  Just in time for Po-Boy Fest, she opened her retail store and it was packed on Sunday.  Fun different shirts.  LOVE my #WhoDat shirt!

How can you not be a fan of this place. It offers fancy cocktails at the mall....AND at the movies. And it has delicious food too.  I like that they offer a cocktail of the day. I must admit that I've only ever used their table service and not their theater service. I think it would be difficult for clumsy me to eat in the dark while watching a movie. I would wear most of my food.  I do think the food prices are a bit high, but their drinks are comparable to other upscale spots. My most recent purchase was a crabmeat & watermelon salad with a mojito. Perfect for a tough day of shopping on a hot day.

As this is one of my fave restaurants, it totally deserves an update almost 4 and half  years later. Boucherie has gotten so popular that it can be hard to get a dinner reservation, so I was really glad to stop in for a quick mid-Saturday lunch.  I started with a yummy dark & stormy that was lovely and gingery while my dining companion had a full salad with her bloody mary. Our service was on point with an attentive server (Hope) who also knew when to leave us be.   We shared 3 small plates and a large and could not finish our food. We had the grilled romaine salad (seriously I dream about this salad), fries (so many fries...), the shrimp & grits with regular, not bacon vinaigrette (for the non-pork people) and the smoked scallops. All the food was delicious and on-point.  I wish I had left room for dessert because, again, yum.  Will be back soon, I hope.
An excellent way to cruise the avenue, get downtown, and enjoy the city.  I was so excited when the line finally came back to my neighborhood.  I missed it rumbling by.

I like the Nashville airport; it's a lot like the city.  It's really clean; it's well laid out and it's kind of fancy but still trying to seem all country down home...but not in a fake way.  I like the live music in the food court when I arrived.  And the grand ole opry on big screen tvs as I left.  Also liked the quicky massage place & nail/brow salon on the concourse.  Signage was good and I was able to meet my friend with a minimum of fuss.
Some innovative dishes which blend NOLA & Thai cuisines.  But overpriced for what it is.

Upon the recommendation of many, I've made the jaunt out to Kenner a couple of times to sample the yumminess on the Little Chinatown menu. And I agree with Vicky's estimations completely (since we were together both times).   For lunch the service was quick and efficient, Jennifer B & I ordered off the lunch special menu but Vicky didn't and all our food came out quickly and deliciously. For dinner service was still good, but the food was a little more m'eh. I'm not sure if they are better at lunch or if were jut there on an off evening. I'm going to give them the 4th star and try again...probably at dinner since I'm no where near Kenner for lunch most days.

Despite being chilly, Carnival season 2010 gets high marks.  Crowds were big but folks were happy.  Everyone was still high from the Superbowl win and you saw as much black & gold as purple, green & gold.  I tried to see as many parades as possible and eat as much king cake as one person can stand.  Can't wait for Jan. 6-Mar.8, 2011.  See you there!

With a heavy heart, I have to drop Kyoto down to  3 stars. They have been my go to sushi place for over a decade but not anymore.  First it was poorly cut fish (on a couple of occasions) to the point that I could gnaw through a piece of tuna. Then on my last take out order, I opened up my box of sushi and the white fish stunk up my kitchen with the ammonia smell. Old fish is just not acceptable.   There are just too many good sushi spots around. If I crave seaweed udon, I'll still pop in but order with care.
Good homey Thai food.  They'll boost or reduce the heat to order (good when you're dining with dietarily challenged).  I LOVE the red curry.
This is one of those overwhelming holiday decoration stores.  The staff was super friendly & helpful. They carry Halloween & Mardi Gras decorations as well as Christmas.

I like that the space was big & airy...and even better when they opened the big garage doors on a nice night. And, of course, I like that it's smoking on the patio only.  The menu is limited but good; I had the seared tuna salad and it was tasty.  The table service was...attentive if distracted, y'know?  I wish the Dolly Parton pinball was better restored, but then again it was giving us free games. I just wanted all the lights & bells to work.  The giant jenga games were entertaining to watch, especially the person who turned beet red when he pulled the wrong block.

Acme on Vets is where I usually end up after shopping at the nearby mall on a weeknight.  They have good seafood gumbo and my brother loves the charbroiled oysters.  And you can't go wrong with the fried anything.

I recently discovered that this store is under new management...and has a new location since my last review.  The new store is still chock-full of merchandise, but it is better organized and you can actually make your way through the store now.  The sales person was helpful (and honest when she didn't know the answer to my question).    Still a great place for vintage and unique gifts AND the with better organization and better sales team/owners, oh yeah, I'm definitely a fan.

I asked our Yelp overlords to collapse the multiple convention center entries into one last month, but so far that hasn't happened.  Oh well... here's review #2 for the many entries.  It's a giant convention center. There are enormous rooms and tiny rooms, all are confusingly numbered.  The audio for packed auditorium with a national speaker was awful with lots of pops, buzzes and distortion. Have some pride in your work audio-tech.  The staff was all polite and the hired greeters/hospitality folks were great.  Be prepared (again depending on room) for every temperature imaginable.

La Concinita is NOT located at the address listed. It is a food truck and so goes where ever the city allows (which evidently was not at their first choice location on 1st Saturday of carnival...thank goodness they found private property across the street on Sunday).    I must say la Concinita may save my life this carnival season. They plan to be set up most parade days within a reasonable walk of where I usually catch the parades.  The 2 sauces I've tried were amazing (avocado lime & spicy mango).  The two veggie options were super tasty. Seriously, I'm so in love with the butternut squash/black bean combo that I may try to duplicate that at home.  My niece loved the chicken. And I noticed lots of families ordering just rice & beans or just fried plaintains for their picky eaters. Smart  Follow them on twitter or FB and track them down. You won't be sorry.

My favorite of all NOLA sushi places.  Last night I had the rainbow roll and the white fish was grouper, so good.  I love their cucumber salads with crab.  The fish is always super fresh and the staff is professional & friendly.  It is not necessarily the most "authentic" sushi place I've ever been.  But it's still my fave.

I have to be in the mood for Retroactive.  The ~abundance~ of stock can be completely overwhelming.  But it is the best place in the city to find one of a kind gifts.  There are cases and cases and cases of vintage jewelry, tons of clothes, shoes, Christmas ornaments, accessories, tchokes, and anything else you could imagine.  Yes the store owner (and his friends who occasionally work for him) can be touchy.  But I think it's because they don't really want to sell anything; or that they want to make sure before they sell anything to you that you value it as much as they do.

If Angelo Brocato's ice cream parlor was a man, I married it.  I love it sooo much.  They had blackberry ice on Saturday night and, of course, I had a mini cannoli.    And the people watching is excellent too.

This is a brand new gas station (Exxon at the moment) and convenience store.  The space is super clean (as it should be since it's brand new). The gas station portion is well lit.  Do not confuse this with the Original Brown Derby which is across Jeff Davis from this location and sells hot plates. I do wonder if they are affiliated or all appropriating a traditional name.

Great spot to find vintage items of a wide variety. Like a lot of these spots, there are a lot of different booths within the store and each booth has slightly different stock. The place is not so crowded that you're afraid to move, but it is pretty full...especially some of the display cases. Still I felt safe bringing my youngest nieces with me AND they didn't knock anything over.  The staff is polite and helpful but definitely let you browse until you need assistance.   You can definitely spot this location along River Road because it has metal animals outside in the fenced yard. Some how the baby goats really speak to me, but they also have chickens, a giraffe, flamingos, and a variety of others.

I'm really hesitant to write this review now...It was announced a few weeks ago that John Besh would not be continuing his relationship with the WWII Museum and so would not be providing the dinners before the shows at this venue. BUT the change over won't happen until August so...  The Stage Door Canteen is just what the name suggests, dinner & a show (or just a show if you like). When I went with my Mom, it was a prix fixe menu with 2 to 3 choices for each (a soup or salad, pork or seafood or chicken, bread pudding or chocolate torte) and 1 free glass of wine. (see my photo for the full menu that we were offered) You can order more wine or a cocktail from the adjoining American Sector and run a tab. I'm not sure if they can make accommodations to dietary needs or not.   Dinner service was well paced and I liked that our servers asked if we were ready for our next course to come out. The space is comfortable...until you've sat in the dining chairs all the way through the show, which was mostly a problem for my Mom.  My food was mostly OK. My salad was a bit underdressed, my Mom's soup a bit undersalted. She loved her pork entree which was easily twice the size of more lackluster seafood pasta dish. Seriously, why skimp on pasta it's the cheapest item in there. She loved her bread pudding and my chocolate torte was HUGE and delicious and way too much.  Then there was the performance (no clinking silverware as the meal was completely cleared, thank goodness). We saw the Rat Pack show and it was really entertaining. Much of the patter seems to have been based on the Live at the Sands album (which I own and know well) but the actors did a nice job of ad-libbing with the audience and customizing it to NOLA.   I would definitely come back for a show as those are done in house by the WWII museum. We'll see about dinners in the future with the new company in charge.

I think that Hoshun overreaches.  It is probably a little TOO pan-asian, but everything we had was OK.  Problem #1 the server never brought rice to go along with the vegetarian Chinese dish that one of my dinner companions ordered. Problem #2 the server told us that one of the sushi items we ordered was just too fishy...and then backpedaled.  It was weird.   And the sushi was fine (and not too fishy) but nothing to write home about.  I feel like I was in a fancified version of a strip mall place.  Two pluses (that equal one extra star), I had some variation on a cosmopolitan that was made with plum sake that was delicious and worth returning for AND they had a big basket of grab your own fortune cookies that had actual real fortunes and not just inscrutable aphorisms.

Delicious delicious ice cream. Rich and tasty.  My youngest niece was disappointed that they didn't have any supersweet kiddie type flavors, although they have plenty to satisfy, she was being a brat. The teen niece had a strawberry and was very happy and I had the dark chocolate, which was almost like coffee.   The space is light and airy and super clean. The owners are great and definitely evangelize the ice cream. Parking can be a challenge in the area thanks to all the new businesses but I often walk over.

I had a big bunch of limits from various family members for Easter Sunday lunch and the Peppermill fit the bill. We made reservations (a must for a busy day like Easter) a few days before and were seated promptly. Easter had a limited menu but there were easily enough selections to keep us all happy.   Sundays have the dinner menu at lunch time which is really appropriate since this is a *very* old school restaurant. Old but solid. All 5 of us were very pleased with our meals. I loved that the salad dressing are made in house. And we had the veal with seafood, the redfish almondine and the stuffed crabs. We didn't peruse the wine list or order drinks so not really sure about that.  This spot does offer 3 meals a day so that's unusual for an independent spot and my brother has been here for breakfast meetings and says the food is good.   We also sampled the desserts; a carrot cake - cheesecake, caramel custard and lemon meringue pie. All were delicious.  The server was on point. The food came out quickly and the tables turned over quickly, despite that we were in a room with a table set up for groups of 20.

My Dad worked on the construction crew that built the dome in the 70s.  When I was little I thought he built it all by himself.  I've seen sporting events, concerts, and conventions within.  And, yes, Saints fans do get loud.

I can't believe this space has had a new owner for a year. I'm sorry it's taken me so long to get here. I used to hang out here a lot when it was Clever. And then...not so much.  The new owner has really changed the space and the wine is well labeled and is really interesting in it's selection. They continue to cover liquor and accessories as well.    Plus now the bar is more integrated into the store which makes more sense. The cocktail program is no joke. I've had a couple of excellent old fashioneds here. The bar is very loungy and I noticed someone having snacks so I'll have to investigate that.  On Saturday night as we left Jazz Fest, we happened on a crawfish boil in the parking lot. $10 all you can eat. Yep I'll have that.   Will definitely try some of their other evening specials...like wine tastings and manicures!
Very traditional Italian New Orleans restaurant.  Some inventive dishes but still a place that you would be very comfortable bringing your grandmother.

I stopped in at lunchtime on Saturday. It wasn't really clear if people were ordering or waiting around for food and no direction was given by the staff. We figured out that others were waiting on food, so approached a register. Which was the correct thing to do!  There wasn't much left in the case so I tried a couple of the sweet kolaches. My friend got a breakfast taco and a fruit kolache. They were completely out of savory kolaches, empadas, and rancheros. I was not that impressed with kolaches. Maybe it was a construction issue? Giant blob of fruit or cheese in the center of a lot of dough which was a bit dry.  I was disappointed that they only had bottled tea and no fresh brewed. They did have a soft drink vending machine but my friend said it was so high that she couldn't tell when her drink was filled. #shortpeopleproblems   I was also disappointed that they had zero non-meat kolaches. Although their are 2 non-meat rancheros. Otherwise you're waiting on breakfast tacos....

This was my niece's choice for her birthday dinner and my first time at this new location. The restaurant is spacious and open (especially compared to the old location). The staff was good although it was slow weekday night. We sat at the sushi bar and the chef was engaging but left us to chat.  We had the Veggie Roll, the Burning Woman roll (sauce on the side) and the Mystery roll (also sauce on the side). So sauce is one of my pet peeves, I think it usually overpowers the sushi and hides fish that's past its prime. They were happy to accommodate my eccentricities. I asked about some items on the sushi menu (pompano! and another specific fish) but were informed they were out at the moment. Oh well. The sushi was well prepared and my niece and I ate until we were stuffed. The bill wasn't too bad either.  As for the parking lot, I found it crowded...especially considering the number of patrons inside. Or maybe it was just that the cars that were in the lot were parked poorly.  Definitely will stop back in when I'm in the Metrys.

It cracks me up that Mardi Gras is on here to review.  My disclaimer is that my family (except for Dad) is MG crazy!  I have brothers in a couple of different krewes.  And I go to every parade that I can.    I do miss the old neighborhood routes, but I understand why the police want everything more standard.    Go for the camaraderie, for the throws, for the people watching, for the excuse to publicly consume a ridiculous amount of food and drink.  Just GO!

Oh look it's one of sadly brief early reviews...time for an update. Somehow this former go to spot had fallen off my radar, but it's still a solid choice. I've eaten in this location (same name different owners over the years) for over a decade. It's always a good spot for a variety of dishes that will please most palates.   I had a their mango special last night and it was DELICIOUS. Big chunks of really ripe delicious mango with shrimp, scallops, pineapple and onions. YUMMM. My friends had the Pad Ginger with shrimp and the tofu red curry. All the dishes were super tasty and the veggies really fresh. Love the ginger in the pad ginger.  The restaurant was not too crowded on a Thursday night at dinner time but there were a steady stream of people stopping in for takeout.   The restaurant is small but well laid out and the staff is attentive without being pushy. I definitely need to place this spot back into regular rotation.

Say you need a religious gift of a Roman Catholic nature, like a religious statue or saint's medal for a child's christening or birth. This is the shop for you.  It is mostly run by nuns which I kind of like.  It does sell books, CDs, and DVDs of a faith based nature.  It is, of course, closed on Sunday.

OK, the best thing about this place is that it is no smoking...or maybe that's 2nd and the 1st is the amazing wine list.  Which would only make sense since it's the bar 1/2 of a wine store.  That said the bartender made me a tasty (and potent) old fashioned so Yay for variety.

Wow. This place had the nicest staff EVER the other night when I stopped in. I was all mopey and the staff here seriously brightened my day. It was my 1st time ordering with this spot and so it's a little different than other places with WAY more choices. WAY!  They offer over 10 protein choices including tofu and chicken, not just seafood! That's in addition to 7 base choices. I love black (aka forbidden) rice, so nutty! Plus there are so many choices for add ons. And the staff even told me that I could add more with my comes with price.  My bowl was delicious and fresh (once I got home where I could scarf it down without fear of judgement). And I like that if you dine in, they don't use takeout containers.   I will definitely be back!

I had visitors from out of town and as was traditional in my family, I took them out to the lake for dinner. Back when I was kid, we always headed out to Bucktown or WestEnd for seafood eats when we had out of town visitors. You got the freshest seafood AND you got lakefront breezes to keep you cool.  I knew my parents were a fan of this seafood joint and it was open on a Monday night so score. The newly renovated patio was perfect...especially since there was a huge, disorganized, loud family birthday party happening inside.  We all enjoyed our food and the company and atmosphere but our server was kind of a ditz. She was very sweet but forgot items (like additional drinks or more sauce).   The restaurant had enough variety that everyone was happy too.

A couple of weeks ago, it was unseasonably warm and I realized that I was going to have to wear a dress. Whoops my legs were not in shape for that. Knowing that this spot opened near my house, I made an appointment for the next morning for a lower leg wax and tossed in a free eyebrow wax as a first time customer.  Online booking was super easy. So was check in the next morning. The staff was professional and courteous. The tech started with my eyebrows and I explained that I was just looking for a cleanup and nothing dramatic.
