The final product was fine. She moved onto my legs and I noted where I have an old scar that can be sensitive. She was quick and methodical. Nary a stray hair was left.  I got the sales pitch for their products and then the pitch about booking a series of appointments. Nope and nope. Quick and easy and just what I needed.

My goto nail salon was sold and is still being renovated but is now Premier. I actually made an appointment via the Yelp app for a Sunday afternoon. And enjoyed a luxe pedicure. I had 2 different techs work on me while I was there. Both were lovely and professional.   The salon is still a little run down and my massage chair remote was held together with tape. But maybe that's part of the redo that will be forthcoming.  The luxe pedicure (see my photo of the menu) included a paraffin wax treatment that felt heavenly on my battered feet. And 10 days later my toes still look good despite my clumsiest attempts to destroy them.

OMG! A friend gifted me with a dozen macarons from this shop! I tried pandan (LOVE), raspberry, creme brule, birthday cake, and so many more. They were all delicious.   A friend reposted from their Insta a couple of months ago and the cookies look amazing. And I really need to make myself a note to stop by when I'm out in the Metrys. Meanwhile who doesn't love gift pastry?

Thank goodness Casamento's is open again! (They close every summer...which was the custom pre-refrigeration,)  Love, love, love their seafood gumbo. And they fry real good too.  E always gets the oyster stew since it was his father's favorite. When my Mom tried it, she said she it was like tasting part of her childhood, since it was similar to something her grandmother had made.  Yes, they are cash only, but there is an ATM in the restaurant now.

Y'all know I love a good bookstore and I hadn't been to Kitchen Witch since they moved out of the quarter. Yes all the random kitchen stuff is still there. And they have even more room to spread out and you can better go through their stock.  The owners are so sweet. And offered a variety of beverages while I was there. I also hear they have popups in the parking lot on specific nights.   They have definitely worked at becoming part of their new neighborhood and honestly N. Broad fits their desultory take on capitalism much better than the FQ these days.  Beware of all the dust but that's any good used bookstore.

The prices are great. And they carry brands and items that no other shops have. The pastries are BEYOND tempting and everyone I've sampled has been DEELICIOUS.  The store is chockful so it can get crowded. Parking is kind of a free for all, but there are spaces on the side street and in back.  Staff is friendly and has always been patient with this gringa.

Updating a 2009 review, over a decade later. I have to say Sucre was so different than anyplace else in NOLA when it opened over a decade ago that it was sort of stunning. And in the last 10 years, I've suggested it as a place for a 1st "maybe" date or to celebrate that great grade for a tween. Or just for something special.  My most recent trip was after having been soaked to the skin during parades. I really just needed a dark hot chocolate. And it was amazing, as always. This is the closest I get to drinking coffee.  Since I had eaten nothing but king cakes for weeks prior, I wasn't interested in pastry and was too cold for the gelato but both are a regular temptation.

I thought I had already reviewed Sucre but I guess not.  I've sampled the fancy chocolates, the gelato, and the pastries.  All are DELICIOUS!    I just bought a king cake from them today and can hardly wait until tonight to cut into it.  The only reason fro 4 stars instead of 5 is that I've been asked if I was finished with my plate because they were running low.

I wandered all the way around the Big Lake on Saturday at dusk with the wild junior nieces and am so glad I did. It was a gorgeous night for a walk and it was really wonderful to see the variety of folks out enjoying the weather, from multi-generational families to young lovers and all races all enjoying the same space.   The nieces were horrified by all the bird poop where the water fowl roost at night. Yay wildlife, I guess. They chatted with a boat rental person about the paddle boats...turns out the birds don't even try to climb in those. They performed on the ministage and just ran around like wild monkeys. And despite their lame efforts, no one was pushed into/ fell into the water.  Loved seeing the Wave sculpture again. Restored in 2014, the sculpture was originally at the 84 World's Fair and was just found again. It looks wonderful.   The tulips (see separate review) were gorgeous along the edge of the lake, closest to the museum. What a relaxing space...

When I heard the concept, I thought this is my ideal bar. Who doesn't want baked goods while sipping cocktails?!  A group of us wandered over on their first Saturday night open. We sampled their specialty cocktails, an old standby (a sazerac) and a glass of sparkling. All beverages were proclaimed delicious. Then we sampled their cheese board, shrimp tartine (see my pic) and a variety of cake bites. Re is correct that the cheese board was amazing...that bread, yum! My shrimp tartine was delicious and again the bread supporting the shrimp and veg was heavenly.  The cake bites were a little less successful, but only because some were mislabeled. The white chocolate fig turned out to be a wedding cake. And the salty ball was probably really almond something. I blame this bit of miscommunication on opening issues and the fact that they were pretty crowded for an opening weekend.  I'll definitely be back to sample more baked goods. I'm hoping for more variety and not just cake in the pastry case.  Also when I asked about cookies, I was told that if we had stayed until last call (midnight) we would have been sent on our way with milk & cookies. Next time!

I stop at this gas station pretty often because it is between home & work.  It's an interesting place because all the pumps are different, as if they were bought at the salvage yard.  If you go to the pump set closest to Toledano then those accept pay at the pump.

I'm over in Elmwood all the time but Friday night was the first time I remembered to stop in this location. It was after 8 and I was still running after work errands. I realized all the quick places would be closing soon. And then I saw their sign shining like a beacon.   I was really pleased that they still had savory options. I immediately ordered waffle fries and a iced tea when I noticed that they still had one potato kolache left. Since John is always raving about kolaches I had to try one.   I got my order to go and they warmed the kolache and I got fresh dropped fries. I must admit that only about 1/2 the order of fries made it home. I was too busy scarffing them down in my car. The kolache was delicious, potato, eggs and queso! The dough was just a tad sweet which I wasn't expecting. But seriously those waffle fries may have saved my life. And the tea was good too.  Quick service and more seating than I expected. I'm going to have to put this into rotation when I'm in the area.

It was 1 am and the place was packed...so why don't more non-bar type places stay open this late on the weekend?  As always, service was...curious. Although Re found the bellowing bartender (who was also our server) pretty funny.   Let this review serve as a reminder to me not to get sushi here. None of the sushi was great but it was all OK. PLUS they have inari (under bean curd on the sushi menu) which is difficult to find in NOLA.  So if it's late at night then give it a go...you might end up with a semi-belligerent drag queen show (from other patrons) and you might end up full or drunk, depending on your needs.

oh look... another disappearing review. I reviewed Cafe du Monde years ago... and I remember that I was review 900 at the time, I think it's funny that I'll be review 824 (maybe) on this listing. At what point do the Yelp overlords decide to start a business over? It's so weird.  So beignets... they are delicious. I mean who doesn't like big hunks of fluffy fried sweet dough? My standard order hasn't changed since I was a child: an order of 3 and a chocolate milk. Use the water that is supplied as a fingerbowl for washing the sugar off your fingers.   Pro tips: don't wait in line, just go back later when it's not so busy. It is cash only. Be nice to the people at the other tables and of course you servers.

Solid choice for neighborhood sushi. It's in a strip mall so ambiance isn't amazing but it's clean and the tables are well spaced. We had great service the night I was there.  The drink menu is interesting but I stuck to tea, but my friends enjoyed their cocktails. Many of their specialty rolls come with either eel sauce or spicy mayo. I'm not a fan of either so I just ask for no sauce and they were happy to accommodate. The fish was really good quality the night I was there. And the veggie roll was tasty (always my palate cleanser). I did not see any hibachi action happening the night I was there, so I can't  say anything about that.   Solid neighborhood choice and I'll be back when I'm out that way.

If anyone can turn this maybe jinxed location into a success, I think Milk Bar can. This location is much larger with more seating than the Delachaise location. And of course, if you're not a fan of parallel parking, this location has an honest to goodness parking lot.   The menu is the same as the Delachaise location although the two locations will run different specials, like soup of the day. Like other local restaurants with more than one location, don't expect identical sandwiches in both locations.  The sandwiches are tasty and offer an interesting alternative to poboys They are generally large enough that I can eat them for 2 meals. And yes the shakes and freezes are way too delicious.

Build your own salad spot inside the Place St Charles food court and it is delicious! I had the crunch Thai salad with tofu as my protein. The salad was really filling and all the ingredients were fresh and tasty.  I also had a small sampling of their soup of the day which was gazpacho. It was very tasty but I was so full that I ended up passing it to my friend who as less pleased with her selection.   Since I was feeling too healthy with my salad choice, I also got one of their chocolate chip cookies. Very tasty!  Definitely will come back if I'm in the area.

I've wandered past this spot many times and never stopped in. But a friend was having a party here on Friday night so away I went.  It's a great neighborhood bar. Not too fancy and drinks are affordable.   Everyone was super friendly... even when I knocked over a box of empty liquor bottles with my giant purse. Not sure why there were boxes of empties taking up floor space, but there you go.  There's a big projection tv that had sports and random TV showing, maybe by bartender preference/patron request.  Great spot to hang out and visit.

Of course, the location hasn't been on Canal in a while and they are rebranding themselves as Floor 13. I've been in this shop at its various locations and it definitely can have some interesting stock.  Mostly they get furniture when big businesses are refreshing. So the quality can be great to not so good. Earlier this year they got a ton of furniture from a local high end hotel and so they had a bajillion incidental chairs, beds and other furniture. They also get lamps and TVs.  It's a great spot to get some decent items at a lower cost. If it's hot outside, this is a metal warehouse so it will be hot inside. But there is a section of select items that is cooler. Since it's been chilly the last few days, I imagine the reverse is true right now.

Pandemic update: I was out near this delicious bakery on a week day morning and decided that I NEEDED pastry. NEEDED. Of course, I overpurchased but how could I resist all the delicious buttery pastry?   This is a small shop and so they have removed most of the dine in tables so that you have to leave to consume, but that was fine with me. The staff and the bakers are all masked as are customers (thanks for those rules, Louisiana Governor!)  I have never had a bad item here so you can't go wrong with anything on their menu.

As you drive down the I-10, east of New Orleans, you may have a WTH moment. There's a castle off in the distance (well on Hwy 11). It is a private home, for now, with aspirations for more that never quite materialize. Still the history of the place; it's recent vintage and it's singularity in the swamps of South Louisiana make it something special.  You have to love a man with a dream. In 1981, Simon Villemarette decided he wanted a castle. Was it supposed to be at tourist attraction? Or was it just going to be his home? Whichever he built it well. He passed and his family had to sell.   Yes it survived Katrina when most buildings did not. The official assessor's description says "concrete castle" so maybe even the K winds were intimidated.   Some folks from Virginia owned it from 1995 to 2014, maybe they planned to make an inn out of it (according to news stories at the time), but that never happened. Now the current owners post to the official FB page that they too want to make it an entertainment/photo shoot/bed & breakfast spot. BUT the FB has been saying be patient since 2016.   Still it's a fun spot to see. It is private property so don't be a creeper. And I decided this bit of unique architecture should be my review #2400. Enjoy!

Y'know Parkway, I loved your shrimp poboy and really who doesn't like cheese fries...and then I had the caprese poboy.  Beautiful tomatoes, fresh mozzarella, basil all on fresh french bread and then doused with a balsamic dressing.  Delicious and HUGE.  Which was good because my cousin (who is a scary ravenous nursing mother at the moment) attacked my sandwich too.  I must also complement my fellow diners.  A pigeon became trapped on the side porch and when I caught it (I know...I have hidden bird catching skills) they applauded.  Thank you.  No thank you.

I've been here a bunch of times... to meet up with friends, to attend charity events.  It's a huge bar... lots of seating and many TVs for the sports-watching. There's a covered patios if the weather is nice and you can stand the smokers. There are a few parking spots along Andrew Higgins Blvd.  The bar is great for a beer or a straight pour. They do mimosas and bloodies on weekends.   As for the food, I've never had any. Weird.

Pandemic review I woke up on Sunday morning, craving soft serve ice cream... and I tried to talk myself out of it. No where close was going to have any. I'd have to wash my face and put on clothes... all the things to go out into the world.  But once I searched Yelp and found that Aqua wasn't too far and they were right by the downtown Rouses AND I could actually buy groceries, my justification was done.  I had their seasonal special blood orange... which is vegan and amazing. I also bought a mini brownie to have at home which I've resisted so far.  I wish I had been able to consult the menu before I went in. But their doesn't seem to be one one their website and while there is good information about their seasonal flavors, there is less info on the ones that are always on hand.   Staff is all masked and gloved. Low contact payment and social distancing enforced!

I had bid on and won a gift basket at a fundraiser back in the spring and included was a GC to this restaurant. So last night I drove over and spent it all!  We had Mahi tacos and blackened shrimp tacos AND fried okra and fried  pickles. PLUS I got a fried shrimp plate to go. The grilled tuna tacos were perfect and it was a huge amount of food for $10. The blackened spices were a little strong for me when I tasted Katie's shrimp but she loved it. The baskets of fried okra & pickles were huge and definitely meant for sharing. And my fried shrimp & fries were delicious for lunch today.  They only have bottled drinks, but I heard them say you can get an adult beverage at Parlay's next door. And there is a bunch of outdoor seating, but only about 20 seats indoors. I bet they do a huge takeout business. I heard someone ask and they will have boiled crawfish soon so those outdoor tables will be perfect.  The burgers looked huge. The staff was lovely. I enjoyed my food and thought it was well priced. Plus they support the same wonderful group that I do so I'll definitely be back.

4 years later, I'm gonna add a star. I think the new owners took a few minutes to find their footing.  But this is my go to spot for neighborhood fried seafood when I have folks in from out of town. The spot is homey and the menu has a little bit of everything.   The service is usually swift and my food has been solid on my last few visits from fried to poboys to red beans & rice to gumbo. The beer variety on tap pleases most people and they even have bubbles by the glass. They also have a full bar for all your drinky needs.

The selection in house isn't huge, but they have a ton of catalogs to hunt through to find your perfect light fixture/lamp whatever.  I was a little disappointed in our sales associate.  "Why yes we would love to stand at the counter for 30 minutes and flip through catalogs rather than move to a seated area."  But really it may be our fault for showing up just before closing.

This may be a super convenient lot but it is pricey. I also purchase hours more than I need to avoid the boot. And I have the app on my phone so easy peasy and I don't have to wait in line with the folks at the kiosk.  This lot was $30 for 4 hours. I probably would have hunted for street parking further away but I had my old people with me.   Spaces are smallish so do your best to park between the lines.

Madigan's is a neighborhood mainstay. I went quite often way back when I was in college and have stopped in a couple of times in the last couple of months when I was in the area.  Bartenders are good to great. The atmosphere is homey with just a touch of decaying elegance (so very NOLA). When it's a lovely night and the windows are open, it's just glorious.  HH is great and you really do get a cross section of the neighborhood so you might run into almost anyone while here.

I sent them an email and they called me back with in an hour or so! And with 24 hours I had someone scheduled to come by the house and give me an estimate. A week later the work started! Now this timeline might not be the norm but for me it was great! I had called a half a dozen independent contractors over a period of months to look at various carpentry repairs and either got zero response or "let me get back to you when I'm less busy." Then my tenants moved out of the rental side of my house so work needed to be done ASAP.  Randy was prompt and made an early morning call so I could make it to work, almost on time. He wrote up a quote. Their automated system for quotes and acceptance is a tadbit clunky but I'll take technology where I can get it. Everything was typed out and readable. The man who did the carpentry was polite and meticulous! I'm sure the doors he repaired haven't looked so well in 100 years. Then the painter came in and took care of the rest.   Will definitely use them again. I do think their prices might be higher than hiring an independent. But they also show up and do the work when and how they promised. So definitely worth it.   Now to pay off this bill and to start thinking about the other rotten wood spots that need work...

I noticed this shop had opened when I was visiting the Ace Hardware across the street and made a note (in my brain) to bring a visiting friend here the next week.   And yep, she was in love! The shop is Gorgeous! with really beautiful details and attention to detail. Which is true of the garments as well. I've never been into corsetry because of my super short torso but the shop owner (I think) assured me that I would be able to find something that fit. They had a great selection of gloves and art work as well.  Definitely a great spot to browse and buy yourself something special!

Wow! 12 years later.  What a difference a decade makes. This local bookstore has established itself as a go to resource for folks around town. They keep both new and used items in stock. And they of course, have beaucoup local titles.  The staff is helpful and friendly. I've always had good service. When I stopped in over the weekend, everyone was masked and nerding out while perusing shelves in the best possible way.  My only regret is not re-reviewing and upgrading them years ago.

Y'all know I love a good cemetery and this cemetery is actually 3...over 3 city blocks. Which was tough for me because I was hunting for a friend's grandparents' crypt.  He had guessed right as to which of the 3 blocks it was on. But there are a lot of wall crypts...in all 3 cemeteries. If you're not sure where your loved one is...and you're not enamored of wandering around a cemetery... you can always call the Archdiocese of New Orleans and get an exact location. Luckily my visiting friend AB was with me and we scoured the cemetery, being charmed by the names, the decorations, the offerings (from plastic flowers to a  pint of rum).   The neighborhood is better than it once was and while it's definitely still working class and you should ALWAYS be wary when wandering by yourself in New Orleans, I did not feel concerned.   We did find my friend's grandparents and I could send him a photo. So he could see the condition of the wall tomb. So that was an achievement. Also when walking through graveyards, I like to say the names of the dead outloud (or mumble them to myself). I feel like the dead like it when they hear their names again.

Bakers Dozen is a solid old school donut shop. It's been in operation in the location since 1993 but the location has been a donut shop most of my life.   The donuts are always fresh and nice and yeasty. If the donuts are iced, they aren't usually glazed which I appreciate. Love their fun flavors and that they give back to the community. Their donut holes are completely addictive and if near me will be ravenously consumed in the style of cookie monster.  Even when the shop is busy the staff is on the hustle to get everyone moving.  Delish!

Molly's is a solid bar on the backside of the FQ.  While it's not a usual watering hole for me, I'm always happy to meet folks here.  The bartenders are efficient and personable.  The crowd is diverse (unless it's really late night).  I love day drinking here near the window.

Molly's is that rare beast in the FQ where it's mostly locals... depending on the time of day and year. The space hits that sweetspot of roomy enough for a group but still intimate. The bartenders are efficient with a little bit of sass. The drink prices are good. The space feels like a bar that's been around 100 years (in a good way) and not just since (looks it up) since 1974.  I'm not a coffee person, but one of my friends said she biked over the day they re-opened to grab a frozen irish coffee. So that's a pretty high recommendation.   The rest rooms are actually pretty clean at the moment. There is a courtyard out back but it's more storeroom than actual gathering space.   The AC was struggling to keep up with the group I met up with last night, but this is my own fault for wearing my work drag out in the FQ.

The great... the food. There is really something for everyone on the menu, vegans, keto, norms. Everyone and it's really tasty.  The good... the space is lovely and the tables are well spaced. The staff is attentive and helpful.  The oh dear... on a weekend the wait is ridiculous and then they end up in the weeds. The worst was when a dish was put on our table and then they attempted to take it away since it belonged to another order, but I had touched it. Oops. Also the same time that I didn't actually receive the correct entree but honestly by that time since it was something I would eat, I just did and said thank you.  I will definitely stop in on a random weekday. I no longer attempt Saturday or Sunday visits... maybe if I tried after 2pm? Also I've been in when a large party inside was so very loud that I could not hear my friend on the other side of the table. So it can get noisy. As for accessibility I *think* there's a ramp that takes you into the back of the building to access the restaurant. I have not attempted but it's a new build so there HAS to be an accommodation.

Excellent shrimp poboy; really fresh shrimp & bread.  Good atmosphere.  Staff was good...sarcastic & diner-ish, the way they are supposed to be.  Minus one star for my sandwich not being made with love. the extra pickles I ordered being in one giant clump.  Really who wants that.

I put this spot on my radar after a chef friend was raving about their pastries. First time I went it was around noon and they had a handful of cookies left. The cookies were tasty but...   So a couple of Saturdays ago I was in River Ridge by 10 am. Surely they would have pastries! I was able to sample a croissant (and my friend had the chocolate croissant) plus a brownie bite. Pastries were flying out the door. Get here early! Or order in advance... I NEED the kumquat croissant and also a morning bun.  The shop is small but there are a few tables to enjoy your pastries. I was offered water when I was there. I'm not sure if they sell beverages or not.   Adorable and delicious. Maybe it's good that it isn't closer to my house.

My review is for a private party and the use of this space as an event space.  As a venue this is top notch spot. There are a lot of different spaces and plenty of room. We were able to use the main room, the roof top and the loft area. It was fun to explore the building and use the different spaces. For any event this would be a great way to differentiate spaces.  And it looks like they have a fool catering kitchen.  Parking was easy on the street. Only limitation was I don't know how accessible this space is.

Lovely shop with lots of local art to fit all moods/decors.  I like to stop in this shop when I'm in the area to see what local artists they are carrying. Some items are originals and some are prints, but the prices reflect the difference.  The staff is always friendly but lets you browse. And the shop is chockfull of every sort of local art that might interest you.

I've been attending Southern Decadence since the 90s (maybe) and my favorite part is the parade. Because y'know it's a parade and it's interesting how it's changed over the years. I'm glad to see many of the regular marching groups walking in the parade now.  It's still a parade that celebrates...whatever you might be into, not just LGBTQ so be aware if you're bringing kids or your old people. Also shout out to any NOLA parade that makes me have awkward conversations with my Mom.  Don't expect to catch anything at the parade, just enjoy the pageantry. There are also a bunch of other things going on. Some official, some word of mouth, maybe you'll get invited to someplace fun!

I still love me some parkway and when I'm not in the mood for fried, I still enjoy the caprese, but my last time...the love just wasn't there.   The tomatoes were not ripe and were cut way too thick to be eaten in between french bread. Plus it felt like the whole joint needed a thorough scrubbing.  Next time I hope they show me the love.

Pandemic update: On the last work day of the year, the few of us who have had to be on site decided to celebrate the end of 2020 with some Parkway. Ordering online from their website was easy (dressed but on mayo, dressed + creole mustard, whatever).   For pickup, you show up at a little booth next to their parking lot and give your name. Then you park in a numbered spot and await the golf cart delivery person.   The menu is a little different too. The caprese isn't on there (permanently or just at the moment?) but they are now offering a beyond burger poboy for the vegetarians in the group. My fried shrimp was delicious as always. My coworkers got a variety of items and everyone seemed pleased.   All staff was masked and from now on I want all things delivered to me by a decorated golf cart!

Just before MG I saw that Happy Raptor was advertising a King Cake spiced rum so I had to have some.   They are open limited hours at the moment, of course. But I stopped by on a Friday evening and was the only person there. I was also able to sample their Bananas Foster Rum so I ended up buying both bottles and a to go cocktail, a painkiller.  The rum is delicious and flavorful. And my painkiller was amazing... although I thinned it out with a little club soda only because OJ (not rum never rum) kills my stomach.  Masks for everyone and payment was easy peasy.   I can't wait to go back and enjoy the space with friends

Minus 1 star for you. I was in recently and the staff in the retail store was BEYOND rude.  Forgive me & the other ladies in the store who actually wanted to purchase items.  I know it was the manager who was helping the other people in the store...who apologized for disturbing her while she stomped around and offered terrible service.  I just left.  They still have great products and I'm not going to let one ridiculous person totally get to me.  But it does make me consider shopping elsewhere.

This Rouse's is on the location of the giant Schweggman's that was our main grocery when I was a kid...so it will always pale in comparison to those memories.  This isn't my usual store but I end up stopping here when I need something on the run.  They have a great wine selection and really good takeout. I've also used the gift card rack for last minute gifts and the staff usually is very helpful and knows what they're about so that's good.  Solid choice if it's on your path..

TLDR; Great gay dive bar.   Longer version, I always enjoy a bar in the FQ with lots of locals and this one fits the bill. Bonus points for having jello shots... look sometimes you just want to eat your alcohol, OK? People love their bloody mary's and they have a variety of local beers if that's your thing. You can't go wrong with a basic pour. Would I order a craft cocktail here? Probably not.  Warning: if you are full of attitude to the the bartenders or the regulars, expect to be treated with the same disregard that you put out there.   I was really impressed last time that I visited that the bathrooms had been given a major upgrade.

I have to give Entergy some credit. My heat went out again on Sunday. And after the HVAC guy came out, he determined that there was something wrong with my gas feed. I called Entergy on a Sunday afternoon and the gas guy was at my house within 30 minutes. They diagnosed the issue together and my gas meter was swapped out and I have heat again.  PLUS I chatted with him about my gas issues on the other side of my rental and that problem should be resolved later this week.  Yay.

I've been to Cavan a couple of times. Once for a happy hour and once for dinner. It's a lovely space... and used to be a spa (which I never had the money to go to). The renovation to a restaurant is lovely.  First time, happy hour runs from 4 to 7 so that's great for me who doesn't leave work until after 5. Classic cocktails are half off? Yes please. There are snacks including $1 oysters. And everyone seemed to enjoy those but for some reason I didn't snack the night I was there.   Second time, the food was good, although not always what we expected. The antipasti plate was more dips than meat and the shrimp lettuce wraps were so juicy, we gave up on wrapping. I had the jerk rubbed fish which wasn't as spicy as the jerk name suggested, but was delicious. My friends seemed happy with their dishes too. The drinks were tasty.   Service was good and understanding since my reservation was for 5 or 6 then became 8. The tables are close to each other so I'm hoping our large group didn't disturb other diners.

I haven't had the service issues since my first visit to this cafe. But it still gets ridiculously crowded on weekends. So my solution has been to only stop in on weekdays. Problem solved!  Breakfast is served the entire time the cafe is open but lunch dishes are only served after 11am. Specials are also all day.   The food is tasty and there is something for everyone which can be difficult in New Orleans.   There biscuits are a solid choice as are the veggie specials.

Since I knew my girl Dorothy Y was a big fan AND that they carry local NOLA brand Jolie & Elizabeth AND I saw that they were having a seersucker sale for Labor Day weekend I knew I had to make the time to stop in.   The store is small but well laid out; the staff was chatty but not invasive. They offered assistance while I was in the dressing room which I always appreciate...who wants to get re-dressed to go find another size.   The clothes were cute but as with most boutique clothes, the sizes were all over the place. When a large is too small for me, I think there's a problem. The housewares were very cute; I noticed that they carried some Jonathan Adler stuff as well as locals.  Very cute gift items and I'll definitely stop back in when I'm thinking about the herd of nieces and their Christmas presents.

Ahh sweet review #700, it's only fitting that I review the spiritual heart of my city for this auspicious occasion.  St. Louis Cathedral is one of the most photographed buildings in New Orleans (along with the Bourbon Street sign) which is sort of perfect as it shows the dichotomy of our city.  We know how to have a party and yet we know the importance of spirituality (and repentance).  Whenever I'm in the area, I stop in for a moment or two and offer a prayer to my two very Roman Catholic grandmothers and light candles in their honor.  My Granny was convinced that a candle at the cathedral carried more weight than a candle from another church.  The church is a beautiful example of early architecture and it definitely deserves a tour and a donation!  But remember it is still a functioning church, so if you are visiting be respectful of those who are there to pray.  Check out the gift shop while you're there.

I went to Mirliton Fest the year of its inception (2006) and was so pleased this year to see how it's grown.  The crowds were great, the music tight, and the food booths were not the same old-same old.  Plus each featured a mirliton dish!  Yum.  Wish their had been more crafts to see but I think they are making excellent use of their space.

One of my HUGE pet peeves about Yelp is when they collapse two separate locations into one. And then my carefully (yeah right) crafted review makes no sense. Welp that happened earlier this year and ALL the Sculpture Garden reviews were folded into the ones for NOMA. Yes they are adjacent too each other. And the sculpture is curated by the museum staff, but one is outdoors/the other is not, one is free/the other is not.   Reasons I go to the Sculpture Garden: * I need to be someplace outdoors to sit and look at beauty, both art & trees. * I need to run my nieces until they are too tired to ask me what are we doing next * I want to walk and chat with a friend. * I want to visit some old friends (seriously some of these sculptures have been with the museum for my entire life). * I want to go to one of their many special events.  Hints: * Bring your own beverages. * Bathrooms are at the front of the property which faces towards Esplanade. * Sometimes the back gates near the Botanical Garden or Casino are open. * Don't litter. Seriously what is wrong with people.  My old photos were folded into the NOMA page but I'll try to dig up some new ones. And here's my original review from 2010:  What a great eclectic selection of sculptures in a beautifully landscaped environment.  There are some old favorites (the lipazaner & Hercules that we used to climb on when we were kids & they were in front of the museum). The giant tree stump that I got in trouble for trying to sit on when it was inside in the gallery.  Loved the ladder to nowhere when it was part of Prospect 1, but it had more power in the devastated lower 9.    Great place to wander.

Also known as the Greater New Orleans Bridge, the GNO and the CCC this is the largest span over the mighty Mississippi in the New Orleans area.  And it's a good bridge, lots of lanes, not too sway-ey scary.    It costs a buck to go from the westbank to the eastbank but not the other way.  You can buy a toll tag...whatever you do DO NOT get in a tolltag lane without a tag, mayhem and expensive tickets ensue.  Also stop & get change so you actually have a single on you, I hate waiting for the attendants to break a 20.  I am not a daily commuter and the 2 bridge system is so much better than the old single bridge.

Seriously, an outfitters store with all the gear (especially the clothes) that also carries Lily Pulitzer.  Alrighty, the selection was impressive and all the standard brands are represented, with Men & Women's clothes about evenly distributed.  The shoe selection was OK.  I was seriously tempted by some of the hammocks that they carried.

While I do think the overall quality of the clothes at the SMs in NOLA have gone down a bit in the last few years, I do occasionally hit a jackpot (the jeans I'm currently wearing).   But I'm re-reviewing specifically since the shoe department changed hands. No more checking out separately in shoes, and the sales (if they have something you like) are really good. I'm glad DSW is the new subcontract.   The housewares make good last minute gifts and again if you need a basic last minute then this is a good place to check.  The staff varies from extremely helpful to outright surly depending, which is about what I expect. My biggest let down? the dressing rooms which often seem to need a good cleaning.

Updating to include information on their King Cake offerings. I really appreciate a bakery that offers a small version and Fresh Market does...it's packaged in a pie plastic clamshell (if that gives you a size idea) and they do have a larger size too. The King Cake I sampled was moist and overly cinnamony (it was cinnamon filled...or plain to the natives) but with a good amount (not overwhelming amount of icing) and a lovely dusting of colored sugars.  The baby is a bright green so that's a bit different and the container included purple, green & gold beads and "doubloons" which I thought was overkill.  I like their selection of produce and teas. It's a well stocked store. I just wish their prepared food cases interested me more.

Seriously, Lu makes the best old fashioned ever. It was perfectly balanced. The atmosphere is lovely; you can sit at the bar (the bar chairs are comfy) or lounge about on the sofas or at the tables adjacent.  We had great service and though I was last there with a large group. They were able to keep our tabs straight and amazingly all our bills came out correctly.

Curious. I hadn't been inside Rendon Inn in over a decade and it's so fancy now!  I was really pleasantly surprised. Guess I'll have to make it over more often especially since it's pretty close to my house.  I'm gonna give them a pass on service last night. The entire Rising Tide crowd went for their after party.  And I don't think the bar understood what that meant. There was only one bartender working and only one person in the kitchen.  Both were pretty overwhelmed.  But they also were working their butts off to get everyone their drinks and food.

What a difference a decade (or so) makes...  I work a little less than a mile from the Superdome and have for...a long time. I could not believe the circus atmosphere that accompanied this year's game.  And the road closures that made getting to work a total pain.  Last time the game was here (2002), it was much lower key and sort of somber, post 9/11.  Still, it was a good game. It's just too bad it wasn't the Saints because, man, that would have been awesome.   Just thinking about it makes me blood tingle...

I was wandering the FQ last weekend and happened into this shoe store since I was trying to find information on a closed store across the street. The staff person couldn't help me with that and since that was my initial question, she didn't really seem interested in helping me in the store. Perhaps we just got off on the wrong foot. (How could I resist?)  The shoes are off beat and aren't terribly expensive and they do carry a variety of styles with heels and flats and spectators, etc. The store is really spacious and the decor adds to the funky vibe.

About time to update my review. I still enjoy the concert space. The drinks aren't the cheapest. But the concert space is good. It's tough to find a seat, so plan on standing for the whole evening and wear comfy shoes.  On this particular occasion, I stepped outside for a moment to warm up (the A/C works REALLY well). And as I was standing on the little entrance porch, the doors banged open and I got to see a malcontent tossed out onto the bricks below. A few moments later, his wife (girlfriend?) was tossed out after him, followed by her shoe. My friends had witnessed the two of them trying to pick fights with others in the crowd. So that was exciting.  The band sounded good and the crowd watching was entertaining...even after the couple was ejected.

I'm not really in the market for furniture at the moment but stopped into this store to see what they might have that was in the gift item/housewares category. They didn't have tons of gift items when I was there. But they did have some pretty amazing modern house decor.    As befits a store selling modern furnishings everything was clean and well laid out. The store was easy to move around in and everything was clearly marked.  The staff seemed to be in a meeting when I arrived (30 minutes before closing) but a salesperson did offer to help me and the one other customer in the store. She checked back in with me while I browsed but was definitely not pushy.   I really want/need the copper chair they had on display...but first I'd have to figure out where to put it.

I haven't been out to Siamese in years but as we were out this way on Sunday night, I thought it might be worth a stop.  I wonder if there are different owners to this restaurant from the last time I went (which may have been years ago).  The menu seemed really different.    We ordered the eggrolls which were really cabbage-y and not my favorite.  I had a noodle dish with veggies & tofu and E had a red curry dish.  Both were fine although his needed more heat.  The lack of heat is our fault since we ordered medium.  Since hot at some of the closer Thai places burns a hole in my stomach I've gotten wary.    Really it was OK. But we won't be driving out of our way to go here.

I was surprised the first time I stopped at this small cafe and how many items were on their menu. On my first visit I got a smoothie and it was tasty and fresh.  On my next visit I got the veggie panini deal which added a bag of chips and instead of a bottled soft drink, I chose a fresh brewed tea (sweet & unsweet available).   Service is pretty quick and there are a few tables to dine in, although I brought mine selection back to work. Yes the parking lot is kind of odd; the whole lot is a weird shape, but since I walk over from work it's not an issue.  Good alternative to the chain sandwich place next door.

After having major owie feet after tromping around at carnival over over 4 miles AND standing around and watching parades all day, I decided to ditch my old tennies and go on the hunt for something that didn't cause me pain.  I ended up at Varsity and am so glad. The sales person had me march around the store to check my gait and we talked about what I was looking for (general athletic shoes) and how much support I needed (lots).  AND they even carry baby feet sizes...well at least size 6 in women's shoes.  Turns out I was wearing the wrong size and although I normally wear a 5 1/2 or 6, for athletic shoes I should have been upsizing by a half or whole size. Who knew?!  Love my new shoes and that they were on sale. I also bought some size small technical socks which is another pet peeve of mine. I have little feet how can I wear the same size as every other woman?  Next time I'll definitely explore the athletic wear, especially since they carry TASC performance wear which is made out in the Metrys.

Solid neighborhood watering hole. The bartender was fine and the crowd was lively but I felt like I was crashing the party...not really sure why.  Drinks were affordable; there was a decent selection; it wasn't too smokey when I was here but then again it was more like 9ish than the wee super drunken smokerific hours.  Maybe if this was all my friends hung out...

Russell's is a solid diner with NOLA standards. It's where you can take your Granny (or in my case little niece's) and everyone is happy. Of course, the littlest niece wanted to eat fries and not her chicken strips but that was just contrariness.  I had a delicious shrimp wrap last time I was there. And the pancakes at the next table looked delicious. The fried shrimp that my niece had were tasty too.   The staff is good to great and the environs are pretty amazing since they look pretty much like it always has to me...and that's pretty impressive considering the damage in 2005.   After you finish your brunch/breakfast/lunch (but no dinner in post-K world), take a drive along the lakefront.

Ended up here after all my usual place had a long wait; and it had been recommended by a non yelpy friend. The strip mall is a bit sketch, but the staff was really nice and quick! Plus it's a good bit cheaper than my usual spot.    Chairs and decor could use a bit of freshening, but it all looks clean.

Poor Rivertown. This is a quaint little neighborhood that the city of Kenner reimagined as small museums and touristy shops...except the tourists didn't come and neither did the locals, or at least not much.  So now it's a few aging "museums" with a few shops and restaurants hanging on thanks to faithful clientele.    I was actually wandering in Rivertown for the first time in decades because the Deutches Haus Oktoberfest was relocated here temporarily.  If Kenner wants to keep Oktoberfest they really need to expand it beyond two weekends.  Great use of space though.

I've been to Salu twice. Once for a NOLA-Eats party (and I was late so didn't eat too much) and again on Saturday night with a party of 6.  Our server on Saturday night was personable but a bit odd.  One of the soups of the day was seafood gumbo, so I asked if it had sausage in it (which I don't eat...and you really don't want to know why).  She acted sort of put upon and said it was seafood gumbo so no.  After I ordered it and then reiterated that I didn't eat sausage, she did come back and say yes it did have sausage.  Anyway: Pros: Caesar salad, crabmeat cheese flatbread; flank steak was deemed tasty by my companions Cons: ceviche was inedible; gumbo came without rice (?!); service was odd  Overall: I felt like most of the items were sort of ho-hum.  Fine, but not that great.  I was also disappointed by the lack of non-salad vegetarian options.

I tried the southern comfortini this evening which is a TotC signature drink at the Carousel Bar.  I was a little hesitant as it sounded really sweet with Southern Comfort, blackberry and some other liqueurs.  And maybe it was sweet.  But after my super rich dinner, it was the perfect after dinner drink.

I've sampled many tasty tasty pastries from Maurice's over the years. This time I stopped in for a French style king cake and then was tempted by a king cake donut and Russian cake slice (for my parents).   The French king cake was flaky and the almond paste was rich. Although I was disappointed that my apparently porcelain lady (not baby) was plastic. The donut was a donut, a novelty that I enjoyed gluttonously. My Mom said the Russian cake slice was so rich and boozy that she and my Dad split it and still ate it over two meals.  Service is quick and they have a wide variety of items. I had to limit myself to just 3, but man did I want that Pontchatoula strawberry king cake...which isn't a king cake by my definition but it's really delicious nonetheless.

Oh my GOSH!  My first time here they had royal red shrimp as a special....and yes they were pricey but OMG WERE THEY DELICIOUS. Sorry got a little excited. They are more expensive for fisherman to catch so are pricier when you buy but they are so so so tasty. Sorry I'm getting a little weepy remembering.   Since that first time, I've had a variety of seafood and veg dishes and they were all delicious. I mean all. The veggie sides are particularly good.   Definitely chat with your server (service was excellent each time) about what's going on with the specials etc that night. And be sure to tell them if there is something you don't eat to make sure it's not in there... One of the items (fried bread / hushpuppies ?) was made with pork fat for instance.   Definitely a great place to dine.

As I am currently drinking a home version of their signature cocktail, I felt I should review the bar.  My only occasion to drink here was last year's Tale of the Cocktail and I had visited MANY free tasting rooms that day.  Yet the bartenders were kind and quick to supply me with more alcohol. They made sure I knew about drink specials and supplied us with snacks.  We felt well taken care of in addition to being well lubricated.

Tasty inexpensive Amercanized Vietnamese.  I do like the outdoor seating and that the BBQ pit out back is always going.  I do like the variety of dishes and there is something for everyone, vegetarian to meatarian.  Even my picky eater 8 year old niece liked the shrimp fried rice...which was fried rice with a handful of lovely grilled shrimp on top.  This place has been slammed since it opened and I get it. It is tasty and cheap.

Last week I got to tour the Rex Den as a fundraiser for the State Museum friends group. So I got a preview of the 2014 floats (see the most recent 3 photos). It was so fun to stroll around and check out all the details of the floats without worrying about being run over or dodging beads or other parade goers.   As usual they are going with a classical theme of gods & goddesses and some of the floats are just gorgeous. It was also fun to stand underneath the Boeuf Gras and imagine him snorting down on me.   As part of the tour, we were also able to view the robing room which features photos of Rex, gone by, and collections of archived scepters, crowns, costumes, etc.   I'm so glad that I was able to wander through and get a preview. Can't wait for March 4th.

Fast & inexpensive... with a full bar. Really what else do you want?  How about a self-serve bar with pickles & variety of salsas? Yeah that too.  Check out the daily drink specials for extra good deals.  Of course, you can customize your... burrito, tacos, tostada, whatever with the toppings of your choice.  And, yes, they still have really good ice.

I love the old school floats & themes. The royalty was actually pulled by 6 mules last night and all of them seemed pretty happy, except for one of the lead ones. But his handler calmed him down with some pets. The wagon wheels definitely change the way the floats sway over the streets. While the theme was a bit obscure (it paid tribute to a long time member...well member's wife who was active in their design process for over 50 years), the floats were beautiful as always.  The parade does zoom by superfast; these old guys don't play. They want to parade and get home, I guess. Not a ton of throws but enough to placate the crowds...more like the volume that I grew up with rather than the showers of stuff that come from some parades.   We felt like there were fewer brass bands this year which is usually their staple so minus 1 star.

I went on the last day of the old menu (two months ago) so I definitely need to pass back by to try the new one. But I'll probably have to wait until a day when I'm not working or have a long time for lunch; the service is on Caribbean time or maybe it's that our server was also the chef. Plan your time accordingly.  I'm not sure if it was even on the menu, but ended up with a rice curry with grilled shrimp. They were delicious. And the portion was so generous that I ate it for supper too.  I liked the basic, yet colorful decor and the staff (OK the one lady) was really nice and checked on us to make sure we were enjoying the food.  Don't let the strip mall corner dissuade you. And, yes, cash only.

Wow! This is a GORGEOUS space. The renovation of this old warehouse is amazing. Love that you can watch the bakers work through the window in the shop (or shoppe). There is another set of windows on Earhart so you might catch a glimpse if you're at the stop light.   Lots of donuts and cupcakes and croissants and muffins when I was there yesterday morning AND, of course, King Cakes (which could be filled while you waited by one of the bakers). The King Cake was light and yummy with a bit too much icing for me, but my cousin's kids seemed to love that part.  They advertise that they serve both breakfast and lunch but I didn't see a full menu. It looks like mostly pastries and a few sandwiches and that's about it.   Park in the lot for Ye Old College Inn (hmmm see the connection there) and Rock n Bowl.

Still one of my favorite places to stop and take a breath and have a cuppa (iced or hot) and maybe a snack.  The staff is efficient and polite. The sandwich (lunchtime) I had was tasty and my customization was handled perfectly. My iced tea hit the spot. And the space is relaxing and cool on a warm day.

Hmmm...How do you eat at a meat shop if you don't actually eat meat? Don't worry there are some sides that you can snack on while your friends consume their meats.  The brussel sprouts are delicious and worth a drop by just for them, even for folks who think they don't like them. The mac-n-cheese I was less impressed with. I didn't realize that it would have peppers as addition which I thought overpowered the cheesy goodness.   Service was great with lots of water refills. Ordering at the counter and hunting for a table was a bit tricky since the place was packed on the late night I was there.  This wouldn't be my first choice since options are limited for me, but good to know that there is something I can eat.

Since I'm not a beer girl, this was one of the few Freret Street spots that I hadn't been to. This was corrected when micro-brew loving family was in town last month.   I was impressed that the wine list was varied and while not huge, well selected. There were interesting food choices. I had a beet and hummus dish and the earthiness of the two items worked well together.  The grilled  broccoli with smoked fish was delicious. The cheese plate enjoyed by my uncle looked delicious. PLUS OMG chocolate pudding for dessert. Just remembering the tasty pudding, I would like to go back now please.  Service was good, even though we sat outside on a somewhat warm evening. But the breeze was good and the bugs stayed away.   I didn't see the plating or quality issues that others did. Maybe they've resolved some of their problems. Or maybe I hit them on a good night.

Our final stop on the Party Bus wank tour and really it's pretty sketchy. Loved the sign that said "don't hustle the paying customers." Did not love the drink I received. I have no idea what I ended up with but decided that it was a sign that I shouldn't drink.  A friend who lives nearby says the parking lot is packed between 5 and 8 am so that maybe the most interesting time to go.

I stopped in during parades yesterday and they were serving their full menu! I picked up a couple of jello shots (don't judge), grilled shrimp banh mi and tofu spring rolls.  The jello shots were tasty. The spring rolls were HUGE...and delicious. And the banh mi was good but a little light on the fillings for me.   Staff was really nice and the space has not altered since this was Pho Orchid. I liked that the TVs in the bar were showing 2 different food shows while I waited.

How is it possible that Champions Square has zero reviews? That's just weird.   This is the space created adjacent to the superdome for partying/concerts/what not before you wander into the superdome. It seems really big when it's empty...but then you're packed in with a bunch of other fans and it seems quite small.  Still it's a great space to enjoy before you head into the dome...or for a random concerts that sometimes occur.  I think my favorite thing is that it feels like a canyon (pretty rare in NOLA, y'know) so besides enjoying whatevers going on, I can also pretend I'm in an old western. Yes, I know that's odd, but there ya go.

The service was more college student indifferent then I expected...but we did arrive right after a couple of large parties, on a slow Tuesday night.  The house salad was indifferent iceberg lettuce a few mini tomatoes, decent croutons and sliced purple onion, but the dressing was good. Still iceberg, really? I expected more.  I had the AMAZING seafood au gratin. Seriously a perfect blend of really high quality crab meat (including obvious chunks of claw meat) and shrimp.  I was in high cholesterol heaven.  And my brother got a special of barbecue shrimp which was really delicious and highly spiced. Both dishes came with generous servings of really fresh french bread.  So I would definitely go back...and maybe just forgo the salad.

Bizarro world. When I stopped by this Rouses this afternoon. Yelp told me it was my 1st checkin at this location...more like my 20th or 50th or something. Then I noticed this was a "new & hot" location. Um what? Try it opened in 2011. So I guess I'm rereviewing. Why did the old listing suddenly disappear? Mysteries of Yelp  This grocery is great for folks who don't need bulk items, unless it's liquor. There's a lot of prepared food with lots of various selections of hot foods. The freezer section is good and there's an area to eat if you're grabbing a quick lunch on the go.  The adjacent parking lot is small but there's more parking on the roof...where the herb garden is and an elevator for quick access.  The staff is always friendly and the store is usually really clean. Just watch out for tourists overwhelmed by their choices for Louisiana foods.

From the street we saw the sign and thought this would be a craft market, instead it is a sewing store. When we stopped in there was a sewing class going on which is great!   We walked around looking at the fabric and the notions and the supplies. The staff was very nice and they seemed pretty used to folks wandering in erroneously.   Great shop for your sewing needs.
Good cheap food. And they have pellet ice.

I was lucky enough to score some food from this yummy food truck this evening....since the rally was WAY more crowded than they expected.  I got the superplato for $8 which was 2 empanadas, cole slaw, chimichurri and poblano cream mac-n-cheese. I chose the sasquash (squash, onions and cheddar) and the Bean Vista Social Club (black beans, plaintains, coconut rice and vegan). Both were delicious! And I was stuffed. Loved the chimichurri too.  Bonus points that I got to explain who Zac Morris & AC Slater (on the dueling tip jugs) were to the guy behind me.

Fabulous swamp exhibit and the penguins are back.  The jelly fish & seahorse exhibits are way cool.  And they let you touch some stuff...although that's probably supposed to be mostly for kids.  I wish the IMax was bigger but you can't have everything.

Such a great NOLA experience. Fancy mansion on the Ave that decorates for all the masses to see come Halloween. A must stop every October.   Love the topical skeletons and the nieces liked figuring out who was who. Although the 8 year old said that the Annie skeleton must be old because Annie has brown hair now not red. All knowing children, y'all.  Family legend says that my great grandfather helped build this house but we know how those legends are.

Since I'm flying 3 times in the next couple of months, I decided to bite the bullet and go through the TSA Pre-Check paperwork. You can submit your information online and then search in their system for the closest business to get fingerprinted and show your photo ID.   This new IdentoGO was the closest to uptown. I made my appointment online (hours are 8-3/M-F only) and then altered it later.   I showed up. Showed them my passport. Answered the questions. Got fingerprinted on their scanner. Paid my money. And my pre-check (which should be active in a week or so) will be good for 5 years. Domestic travel only...  They also do the background checks for federal jobs and a couple of other things. I think.  Easy peasy

Ahh...this is not the Bruno's of my youth, a place I spent MANY an hour (that would be the building where Rocco's is now), but it is big and airy so if the place was smoky I couldn't tell.  I liked that our server was quick to mention 1/2 price appetizers (maybe because the kitchen was about to close which would make sense since it was around 1 am).  The drinks were cheap and the dj was absurd.  There was line dancing and shot pouring from the stage.  I'll have to go back when remotely sober to see if any of my impressions hold true.

This isn't my favorite store; mostly the problem is with the other patrons. I've been hassled in the parking lot by panhandlers, cursed out by old people at the pharmacy counter for perceived slights, and harassed in the aisles by random dudes looking for a "date." So I only stop in when absolutely necessary.  The store alternates between acceptable and dirty; they did a big refurbishment right before the CVS opened across the street but it's already back to being slightly ratty.   The staff is OK in my opinion. But the store definitely needs better security

I went the 1st night they were open after Gustav and had good food and excellent service.  Even better an out of town family member was footing the bill.  My uncle felt that the chicory coffee creme brulee was a platonic dessert.

I am a fan of Stein Mart because they are the only department style store close to my house.  With the recent cold snap, I needed tights to wear with my dress...Stein Mart had some and even in the color I needed. Astonishing.    Like Christy L, I think you have to pick through a lot to find the cute stuff (like Michael Kors cords that I bought last year).  But it's a good place to buy basics or if you live nearby and need a last minute Dad gift...not that I've ever done that.  I also think the shoe department is a little better now that it's a DSW subcontract.  Now if we only had a real DSW nearby, I'd be a happy girl.

It's late and you need that last little pick me up to get you home in the wee hours. Enter the Morning Call Coffee Stand in City Park.   We arrived around 2:30 am. There were other people in the place; they seemed sober...maybe late night shift workers.   We got beignets and powdered sugar. All was right with the world.

My visiting friend wanted ice cream despite the cold temperature and so off to find this location of CC we went. It is smaller than the Uptown location. And I feel like they didn't have as many flavors but they had the ones that we needed.  I got the Chef's Perfect Chocolate which is my 2nd favorite chocolate flavor after a Chockwork Orange. My friend got gingerbread AND pistachio (her favorite). Plus a scoop of peppermint to go.   The counterperson was hustling because everyone including us, came in trying to beat the 10pm closing time.   Yes cash only. And there is a small number of parking spots in front of the shop.

I was starving in the Metrys and searched my Yelp app and found myself this location. As Jen B said they location is under new management recently (there's a big sign outside) but I'm not sure what's different.  My food came out quickly and was delicious. I had grilled shrimp bun, crab rangoon and a to go banh mi (lunch the next day). All the food was fresh and tasty. Since I was there at an odd time, it wasn't too busy...just me and 2 other tables. There was only a single server but he was making sure everyone was taken care of and was very quick on his feet.  Next time I'm out this way and STARVING, I'll definitely pass by.

So good that it's worth the drive over the bridge.  Some of the best croissant's I've ever eaten.  And their king cakes are divine...I once had one still hot from the oven ~OK, I'm better now.  The french bread comes in a variety of lengths, so perfect for whatever your needs!

I hadn't eaten here in a million years, but in an effort to find someplace on a Saturday during Jazz Fest for 5 people at 8:30 without a wait...we ventured out to the wilds of Metairie.  And we had a most excellent meal.    My first plate was a salad which was OK.  I didn't go with my 1st instinct (the brie & apple) because it was supposed to have leeks as was my 3rd plate.  As it turned out my 3rd plate didn't have the listed leeks either.  Oh well.  The artichokes with feta relish (my 2nd plate) were excellent.  And the diver scallops with butternut squash were AMAZING, leek or no leeks.    Everyone else enjoyed their food.  And the bits I tasted off their plates were good, except for the risotto (can't remember what else was with the dish, maybe fish).  The risotto was really salty and not much else.  My only other criticism is the whole tapas phenomenon.  I feel like I should pre-eat so that I don't break my budget.  All those small plates are expensive!

I hadn't stopped into Wise Buys in years...like maybe over a decade.  And the sales associates (2 in a tiny store) couldn't be bothered to say hello to me.  I always greet folks in small stores; it's only polite.  Prices were meh.  And I didn't see anything that really blew me away stockwise.  I guess it'll be another decade before I wander back in.

I agree with everyone that the spicing at this location is a bit out of control. If you order medium prepare to need lots of water. I ordered mild last time and it was perfect me, but would have been too spicy for others.  I don't understand why this is such an issue at this location and not the other.  Plus 1 star because I walked by over the weekend and they now have their liquor license.

I'm so torn... I LOVE the food. And the cocktails. The space is lovely (if loud). The location is super convenient for me.   BUT I hate the ordering process. As others have said, you walk in and order at the bar this includes drinks. Then you go find a table. Maybe this isn't a problem for most people, but each time I've been there (including at Jazz Fest when there was a wait for a table), you feel like you have to hurry up and order or lose a table to whoever is more organized.  Sitting and perusing a menu is so much more civilized. ESPECIALLY when I'm paying prices that normally would mean full table service.  Of course, you can order drinks (or more drinks) from your table and they'll run you a new tab...you can't leave an open one, which is still dumb.  AND then there's the water service. When I went after JF I apologized to our server and said, I'll need a constant flow of water because I've been out in the sun all day. Even with this heads up, I ended up with a dry glass a couple of times through dinner. The most recent time, we actually had to ask for glasses of water...really?  Again the food is yummy, but this won't be first choice for having a meal in house...maybe I'll try again with takeout.

Yum! I had the veggie Banh Mi & the person before me had the Bayou Banh Mi (chicken & boudin) and both were super tasty...not that I tasted hers. She was just raving.  Seriously, I want to drive back over the Hollygrove Market (where they are right now) and get another sandwich, not because I'm hungry or anything.  Nice guys and you can track where they are (and their specials) via their twitter feed: http://twitter.com/#!/GeauxPlates  Next time I'm gonna try the spoonbread...along with my Bahn Mi.

I was at supper next door and my friend decided he needed one of these shakes. And um wow. They are something. I watched the creation of shakes and thought I can't eat all that. And since there were several children and ahead of us who were getting all the things on their shakes, we had a while to wait. You can have sauce stuck to the side of your cup (which is decoration? do you eat it?) and then edible things stuck to the cup. And then ice cream and stuff and things and more things and I think I just died. I'm supposed to call the things garnishes by the way.   Anyway I had a basic shake which did not cost $10 but was still $6. It was tasty and I did not immediately lapse into a sugar coma.   I definitely see the appeal and this would be a great reward for something important of a child or a child at heart. The staff was nice. There were beaucoup choices and the store was mostly clean, except for the kid who was knocking the (looks at the menu) "trim garnish" on to the floor rather than eating it or ignoring it.

Since we were gadding about and shopping, my friend and I decided to stop in and check out this lovely design shop. While I think it's mostly a interior decorating business, they also have a very attractive multi-room show room with a selection of items for sale from accessories to books to furniture.  The staff asked if we needed assistance and then let us wander. The items for sale were very attractive and high end. Definitely a great place to check out if you need a special gift item or a bit of design help.

Not a store that I shop at often, but the staff is super knowledgeable and helpful.  They helped my grandmother who wanted to complete my aunt's out of production silver service and were genuinely kind to her.

Wooo! Love getting an FtR for an historical site. If you've been to sea lighthouses along the Atlantic coast....this is nothing like that. It's short and squat and built in 1838. It guided ships along the lake to the canal that accessed downtown NOLA.   For most of my life, it was just kind of there. According to the historical timeline on their website, the lighthouse was owned and in use by the Coast Guard until 1999....I'm not sure about that in use part.  But it was one of the many structures damaged in the aftermath of Katrina. It was actually knocked off it's base and landed at an angle. There was a huge fund raising effort to rebuild the lighthouse and the create the education center.  When I passed by today, the lighthouse was gated off and closed but it's still pretty to look at from the road...or from the Point. Now I'll just have to make it back to see the inside exhibit.

This is the only po-boy place that I will go to in the quarter. It can be uneven, but it has an excellent selection and decent prices.  The daily lunch specials are a good value.  In addition to the standards (roast beef, ham-n-cheese, fried shrimp/oyster/whatever) they have things like a pork chop poboy.  On the other hand I think the seafood muffaletta is just wrong.
I have found my dishes at Magasin and now I won't stray. LOVE the avocado spring rolls and the fried shrimp balls. BALLS, I say.

Still a good place to hear a band, but the food is sort of meh. Don't expect well executed cocktails so stick with the basics. The prices are corporate prices rather than NOLA ones so I just plan on staying soberish.  Random HoB story... I once ate dinner at the restaurant when Black Flag or Henry Rollins was performing. The volume pounded the whole place. It was awesome.

I've been saving my Saenger review for a special occasion...and here it is. Review #1700.  The newly (reopened 2014) theater is a joy. Yes it's almost 100 years old and the Rococo ornamentation reflects it's 1927 opening date. However, the sound system, the HVAC and the other mechanicals are definitely 21st century. Of course, they had 9 years to get it right.   The theater has wonderful acoustics and even the nosebleed seats offer a decent view (bring your opera glasses). The ushers are helpful and the theater does offer handicapped seating on the 1st floor.   There are bars on each floor so while one might be crowded the next one won't be...especially if you head down to the Grotto at the lowest level of the theater (which is always cool). Bonus this layer has the largest number of restrooms too.  My only kvetch is that while the starry sky is back, the cloud machine isn't. Even before theater was flooded in the aftermath of Katrina, the cloud machine had broken down. I miss the illusion of random clouds moving across the ceiling.

The Rivershack was indeed a grocery once upon a time, maybe in the 1940s.  But it's always been a bar in my lifetime.  It's a solid neighborhood bar with decent food (expanded beyond the typical bar menu).  They only get 3 stars because the decor is too self-conscious, with it's ashtray collection and funky barstools.  They just need to take a deep breath.

This place was stupid crowded on a Sunday morning but our group of 6 was told that the wait would be 15 minutes...uh, yeah, we shouldn't have believed them. As we were about to leave 75 minutes later, they finally find a table for our group. hmmmm  The porch is great. And our server was awesome. I enjoyed my bananas foster waffle (except that the bananas came out a good 10 minutes after the rest of my waffle) and I snuck potatoes off of one of my companions plate and they were yummy too.   I'm really glad we were seated on the porch because the inside was freezing with the a/c cranked pretty high. I get that the servers are running but no need to turn the patrons into icebergs.   The menu was varied and our group found something to make each of us happy. But between the delay and the price point (my waffle was $11 dollars with the foster sauce & bananas), I'm not sure how soon I'll be back.

I ended up here for the first time in awhile with a large group visiting from out of town.  We had planned to go another restaurant (which was closed for a private party with no info regarding that on their answering machine/webpage, grrr).  So Deanie's was a fallback since it was walkable from the friends' hotel.    Y'know it's not bad and it can accommodate large groups, but it's also not that good.  I was wooed by the crabmeat augratin on the menu; it was odd and tasted like it was made with sour cream.  E had a fish special and it came out the first time with the wrong side & on sauce.  When it came out the 2nd time, it was sauced and the correct side...which was cold.  The fried items that our group got were more successful.

This was probably my favorite bar on the Metry bar crawl. The decor reminded me of my aunt & uncle's rec room...all padded leather and wood paneling with big (heavy) captain's chairs. Unfortunately it was really smokey (maybe some scrubbers?)  The bartender seemed to be distracted so it was difficult to get a refill. The DJ (Saturday night only?) was playing an eclectic selection of music ...which didn't really go with the environment. I would have preferred some old school rat pack maybe.  Price point was pretty good. And I'm not sure what was going on with that meat roasting out front....
Great neighborhood bar with excellent fish n chips.  The Monday night pub quizzes are really fun.

NOLA's newest carnival organization and it's all female AND it already has a waiting list for next year!  The headpieces were great; the signature throws...might need a bit of work, but that just gives them something to aspire to next year.  Great new parade with awesome bands!

Since I reviewed where one set of grandparents were entombed, I need to do the same for the other set.  This is a modern cemetery with very few raised tombs, so not really what people come to NOLA for.  It is big but you can go to the office to get assistance in finding the grave you want.

I've never been the big comedy show fan... And the New Movement may just change that. I've been to a few of their shows (one in the old space at Howling Wolf and a couple at the great re-purposed space on Burgundy) and I giggle, I laugh, I wince. What more could you want from a comedy show?

Proteus was beautiful this year, as always.  The theme was obscure mythology and the interpretation was whimsical.  I love the use of the antique flambeaus.  The wagon wheels cause the floats to lurch and move in such a different way from modern tires.  Also, points for uniformity of throws, no purple, green & gold allowed.  Everything was red, white or silver.  Classy.

Wow! What a fun junk store... or maybe it's junque since some of the items are nicer. They have monthly garage sales which means longer hours on Saturday...check out their FB page for dates.   Random items I was tempted by... a 1990 handdrawn advertisement of a friend's store in Metairie (just remembered to text him), one of those weird 1950s lady vase heads, vintage hardsided luggage, old medicine cabinet, and candy (which was free).   The shop staff was very nice and happily supplied prices for items that were without. Most items were well-priced for the condition and the stock was definitely interesting.

Another locale that I can't believe I haven't reviewed before. Allways has a great stage (and theater outback) and is a fun venue to catch a band. Or just to hang out and have a drink. It's spacious enough to feel like you have room to dance and cozy enough to feel homey.  Great fun visiting again with my YSB buddies and I just wished I had more energy for the dancing!

Oh my. I was wandering along Magazine thinking about dinner and I saw that this shop was open. I've been wanting to try them.   And when I went inside they had a lump crabmeat mini quiche and it was OMG delicious. The chocolate silk pie is the stuff of dreams. I have a cherry pie too but I'm saving it for tomorrow. Yep this shop sells nothing but pies and quiches. And seriously their crusts are UHMAZING.  It's a small shop and while they sell some drinks, there is no where to eat inside. Like the entire building (the shop is located at the back of the Uptown Delivery Pharmacy), there seems to be renovations happening. There is a small parking lot adjacent to the building.   The staff was really friendly and a pleasure to chat with. And seriously they have a wonderful product.

Y'know sometimes a girl needs a sparkly purple, green & gold tie back (with tassels, of course) to complete her costume. Or a some giant king cake babies and plastic king cakes...the essentials.  Jen B is right. You can buy almost anything carnival here. Throws, tshirts, polos, costumes, beads, rubber chickens. Accent Annex has it all.   They also carry seasonal items at other holidays. So it's not a bad place to stock up on paper products regardless of the holiday.  The staff is courteous and do know where all  their stock is...which kind of amazes me.  Worth a trip for the visual overload alone.

Siberia is a solid neighborhood bar. I think it's too nice to really be called a dive bar, but maybe my standards are low. Even though I don't live in the neighborhood, I've always felt welcome..maybe it's because I order easy drinks like bourbon and water.  I have not heard a live music show here...and the one time I was here when one was setting up, I fled before it started. The huge Marshall bass amp in a cinderblock building and me with no earplugs was the frightening piece of equipment that scared me away..yipes! A little bit of knowledge about hearing loss is terrible thing.  Now if I could ever get over there when the Polish popup was open, I'd be a happy girl.
