Mignon Faget jewelry has been around since the 70s & this location has been in existence for about a decade. My service here has varied depending on the associate.  Popped in for the first time in a year or so with visiting family yesterday, the associated was solicitous but left us alone to browse.   This location also features art, books, housewares and accessories from MF and other local designers/artists so that's cool. Loved the oyster plates!  Prices are bit high for sterling, but folks (including myself on occasion) are willing to pay it.  There is a tiny 2 car lot on the side street (off magazine) behind the store if parallel parking on Mag seems to terrifying.

Since I was just typing about this place, I thought I would review it.  I am not a coffee drinker so let's get past that.  But I love this place.  The ambiance is great; you can sit outside in a courtyard.  The place sells a variety of teas (iced & hot) and snacks.    And I agree I mostly see locals.  Maybe the tourists are out looking for a starbucks?

The staff was really nice as I hustled in 10 minutes before closing in dire need of an iced tea and a muffin. My tea was smooth and perfectly brewed and my strawberries & cream muffin was sticky and delicious.  The coffee part of the shop is small but doesn't feel that way since it's open to the Herb store adjacent....which is where the rest room is located (and you have to get the key from the cashier). I did wander around the shop for a moment attracted by the large displays of teas.    So maybe my minor complaint is my own fault since I ventured from the coffee shop section... I smelled like a hippie when I left, not unwashed, but smelling like patchouli which makes me sneeze. Next time I'll stay on the beverage side than head outside to enjoy the views of Canal St and the cemeteries.

Didn't people make the runs on the grocery stores last week?  Why is the dairy case at this store still empty?  It looks like they haven't really restocked completely after the post-Isaac carnage.  The store is small but it carries some different brands and items than the other groceries in town, so that's a positive. Every one was raving about the produce and the cheeses, since these areas were a bit depleted, I'll have to go back and check again.  Four stars for now...I've really liked Fresh Markets in North Carolina. I am surprised at how tiny this store feels.

I'm a big fan of Chef Sue Zemanick and have been wanting to try this new spot since it opened. I finally took the opportunity this week.  The space is small but lovely. I was actually surprised that the layout was still very standard dinner since I expected something more wine bar in the space. The wine by the glass has interesting selections; I had a couple of glasses of a lovely sparkling rose since that's a perfect August refreshment. I was pleased to see they have a full bar too.  The small plates we sampled were delicious and perfect. We had: tuna tartare...bright and beautiful with the seaweed salad ceviche...very interesting and delicious but after the tuna a bit more mundane roasted root vegetables...for such a plainly named dish, this was a star and was arranged like abstract art gnocchi...also very good, the fresh pea shoots were lovely light touch cheese plate...by this point we were just out of control. this was huge and came with amazing fig bread & several of the cheeses were deliciously stinky blueberry & peach cobbler...also yummy although I probably should have stopped at the cheese.  The service was lovely but not intrusive. The tables are close together so that's a bit awkward when you have the newly engaged smooching a few inches away, especially after they order the wedding cake dessert.   The price point is high but the quality of everything I ate was spectacular.

I knew this spot had opened in Elmwood but I couldn't find it. I finally figured out that it was next to the Starbucks in the area adjacent to the Home Depot. Finding the place - Mission 1 accomplished.  Salads can be made into wraps with no upcharge so that's cool. They had a standard menu (which included tofu...in the suburbs!) and a seasonal menu. I went with the tuna & satsuma wrap from the Winter menu. Of course, since it's actually March, satsumas are pretty much done so they subbed in pears, with my permission. And said the menu would probably be changing this week. Points for seasonality and for a great staff.  Great (if a bit pricey...but y'know salad restaurant) health choice in Elmwood. Parking lot is kind of a pain, especially if their are beaucoup people at the 'bucks.  Bonus outdoor seating for a pretty day

I hadn't stepped inside since before Katrina. I mostly used this store as I ran to friend's house in the neighborhood. And the store is certainly different now. There are lots of takeout options and the grocery basics.  The staff was nice and offered assistance. And the store was clean. I was confused by the layout but that might be a personal problem.   +1 star for having Vernor's ginger ale which I haven't seen around NOLA before.

How is it possible that I don't have a review of Mandina's? That's just odd.  Mandina's is an old school neighborhood restaurant that offers New Orleans Italian influenced seafood dishes. It has daily specials and does offer non-seafood items, but I don't think I've ever had one.  The food is solid, if unremarkable. For a native, it's really comforting to get the same dishes prepared the same way for decades...like going to grandma's house.  But why three stars? The place feels really disheveled for having only been renovated post-K. I just want to give everything a good scrub down. The service can be everywhere from hey baby-casual to surly-indifference depending on the server and the night.

I was starving for lunch and down in the FQ with visiting friends.  I had read all these great reviews on here and I have say I was kind of 'meh'  The food was OK.  My friends enjoyed their screwdrivers.  But the prices were high (even for the FQ) and the food was just not that special.  Maybe it was my fault and I should have gone with my first instinct and had the pancakes with ice cream and cane syrup.

I love the carousel bar.  When you're sober it's fun to watch the drunks be confused by the spinning bar; when you're drunk it's fun to try not and fall over.  The drinks have always been well priced and well poured.  Plus this is a bar that I am perfectly comfortable hanging out by myself, until the rest of my krewe actually shows up.

This truck is usually somewhere around the corner of Gravier & S. Prieur near the University Hospital ER. It just depends on the parking/construction.  I've been watching this truck from my office window (which doesn't sound creepy at all) for a couple of weeks and it always seems to have a crowd. The folks from University Hospital, from LSUHSC and the nearby construction workers all grab their lunches from this truck.  I perused the menu last week and this today, I took the plunge. The menu is pretty big for a food truck with "fryed" wings, chicken and beef shwarma, kabobs, salads, po-boys and sandwiches and fried seafood platters. Whew.  I saw folks mostly ordering poboys, the fried chicken wing platter and seafood platters...which is what I got (see my photo) a shrimp platter for $10. There were plenty of crispy and well-fried shrimp and fries, along with 4 1/2 slices of white bread toast and a "salad" of shredded iceberg lettuce, some sliced tomatoes and pickles...so basically the dressed portion of a poboy. The salad was the only disappointing bit since I know they have tabouli on the menu elsewhere. The shrimp were really good and the amount was a lot for me; I'll eat the rest for dinner later.   If you're in a rush, calling in your order is definitely the way to go since I watched everything be made to order. As I stated in my tip, the truck has a website and twitter handle printed on it, but they don't actually work. So that's odd.
Mikimoto is not my go-to restaurant for sushi, but they are pretty good.  And very helpful.
Friend & company has excellent gemstones for good prices.  They also do exceptional repair work.  I have had them repair inherited fine jewelry pieces as well as costume pieces.

When I heard on the interwebs that the new location of Sukho Thai opened over the weekend, I was beside myself with glee.  While I LOVE their food, the Marigny location is not super-convenient for me.  And then I heard the glorious news that they would be opening a branch in my 'hood.  YAY!  The location is gorgeous with twice as many tables as the Marigny location.  Still no liquor license so BYOB.  And the drunken noodles were as delicious as the downtown location.  Our server even commended us for eating the pineapple under our veggie rolls.  Who sends back the pineapple?  Crazy.  I am still giddy from my tasty meal...or maybe that's the endorphins from the heat!

So this has become my go to big box home improvement store since my last review. I can almost always find someone to give me directions or answer my questions.   I've gotten used to how the store is organized (the HVAC filters are behind plumbing). And can pretty much find what I need.  I've purchased lumber, tools, curtains, plants and appliances here. I like that they carry longer curtains at this location which is what you need for vintage uptown houses.   I know others have had customer service complaints but I really haven't experienced that at all.

Funny how times change....this used to be my drycleaner in the early 90s. But it's been a yoga studio for over a decade...   I've practiced yoga off and on for awhile but I can never remember what anything is called. I've decided this is a mental block from having choreography screamed at me in dance class as a child. I'm trying to get better. So I know I do better when things are explained to me.  I've been taking a series of intro to yoga (4 weeks at a time) this year and it's really helping my stress levels and my breathing... why do I hold my breath so often? I've had a series of instructors as I've taken these classes and I find their different approaches helpful and how they focus on different things.  I expect some hippieness and as I really need to work on my breathing that's actually good for me. The facility is great, always clean. The staff is always friendly. And it's 5 minutes (by car) from my house.

Oh look a 2009 review! Time for an update.  If you can, plan early and come in before the crowds descend. I had the place to myself this past rainy Saturday morning. I pretty much knew what I was looking for so asked. They showed me a couple of selections for facepaint. Then for goggles.   There is a ton of stock, at a variety of price points, so don't hesitate to ask if they have something better quality or cheaper if that's what you're going for. You can browse if you're looking for inspiration but you will need to check larger bags (or leave them in your trunk if you're driving). The place is chockful at the moment waiting on the carnival onslaught.  Service was quick and chatty. I was in and out quick quick.

My first journey into Wayfare was just for drinks (and maybe a nibble of cheese) so I waited until I had eaten here to review.  Dorothy Y and I had great light meal here of many tasty dishes... I sampled two of the daily specials which were a seafood sausage slider (OMG GOOD) and assorted brushetta, also delicious.  I like the laid back service and that you order at the counter (yay for no annoying bill splitting). The environment is really welcoming too.  I will definitely be back.

This isn't generally our first choice for home improvement stores as it is a bit smaller than most of the others. BUT it is really close to home and I had a gift card!  I found what I needed and was tempted by various random items...loved all their Halloween decorations, but really where would I store this stuff?  I was a bit disappointed in the plant selection, many looked a bit tired and there wasn't much variety. But maybe that was just the practicality of October...not many folks buying much more than some quick porch color.

Iris is the oldest women's parade and it shows. They don't seem to be interested in new members. But they do have some nice homemade old lady throws (so plus one for that).  It's a fun daytime parade and they did seem to be throwing more this year than in years past.

I checked this new clothing store out during the chaos of PoBoy Fest. But made it back today to score some excellent local tshirts as Christmas gifts.  They have a couple of fun non-official saints shirts, one with wild things & another that says Jesus loves the Saints.  I did not really peruse the consignment clothes as I was on a mission but will definitely be back once the holiday budgeting is over.

The Museum of the American Cocktail is a separate room within the Southern Food & Beverage Museum.  It's an interesting look at our relationship with alcohol and it does have a small local slant.  What I find most fascinating is that it is mostly one person's obsessive collection.  Let that freak flag fly.

Wow. This space is really really beautiful. If you should ever attend a service here, wander about and take in the lovely relaxing spaces.  Evidently one of the Schoens knew my grandfather, so they have been taking care of family funerals since my great grandmother in 1971. They handle everything whether the service is at their parlor or at a church.   The staff is lovely and has the manner down perfectly.

OMG so popular! After a delicious breakfast of yummy biscuits (with assorted toppings...eggs, cheese, sausage), we tried to come back for baked goods to bring home after wandering and shopping in Franklin.  Our mistake was coming back at lunchtime. It was packed!  I wish they had a separate line for folks ordering food and folks who want baked goods from the cases. I guess if you're more experienced, you know to come at off-peak times.  Next time...

Some cute pieces and definitely some cute accessories at a lower price point then expected on this section of Magazine.  Unfortunately, it's definitely more of a juniors store, in style and sizing. Or maybe, fortunately, if that's what you're looking for.    The staff was courteous. And the shop is open on Sunday...again not as common with boutiques on Magazine. Which is smart since on a recent Sunday they were pretty crowded.

Super cute neighborhood pizza place... The first time I went I met my friends late and decided to just order a drink. I was pleased with the cocktail selection and the bartending skills.   Fast forward to last week and I finally got to eat their delicious food! I had a Caesar salad which was a solid version. And then I had the cacio e pepe pasta which was DELICIOUS, but I wouldn't really call it cacio e pepe since that's a much simpler dish. The crabmeat on it was fantastic though. My friend had the fungi pizza which she shared with me and it was delicious too. They did warn us that they were out of buratta for the evening but subbed in mozzarella instead on my friend's salad.  While she had dirty martinis, I had the Drunk Roy... that's not the name but it was essentially a Roy Rogers with Bourbon. It was really sweet which isn't usually my style but really drinkable.   Service was great and the space is homey. I'll definitely be back.

So I finally got to experience y'all's Costco obsession and I kind of get it. The prices were pretty amazing and yeah the gas was cheap.   But, man, I'm glad I don't have a card here. I went a month ago with a friend who has a card and bought WAY too much stuff. I will have bulk supplies of peanut butter, cereal, and almonds for some time to come. I used up the butter, cheese, asparagus, and various other items with my Christmas cooking/baking.  The store was well laid out but people were sort of oblivious with their buggies and it was a bit of a free for all. There were lots of samples to be had on a Sunday afternoon.   The staff was really nice and checking out was easy. I'll go back...in maybe a year or so...

Ahh the Jimani... it's probably been a couple of decades since I last stepped inside. It's just one of those corner bars that are just there in the FQ. Good spot to hang out and chat with your friends and chill for a bit.  Drinks are relatively cheap for the FQ and service can be hit or miss. But that's about what I expect from a dive.   I stopped in on Saturday night with a friend who was curious about the spot. It felt weird to be just in a bar but I guess we'll all be doing this again soon...   Disappointingly or maybe predictably mask wearing was spotty. The bartender wore her mask when my friend (maybe because he was wearing his as was I) ordered our drinks but wasn't doing so consistently. Other patrons were in varying degrees of unmasked to chin straps to masks on their wrists.   We stayed for a few and sipped our drinks and then moved on.

I'm going to boost Iris up a star this year.  The riders seemed livelier (and younger...sorry if I'm being ageist) and were throwing oodles, even after it started to rain.  I feel bad that they were on floats in all that terrible weather.  Iris also get's points for the little lace doilies around the masks that the riders wear.

I was so excited to see that this restaurant has tofu 2 ways, regular and lemon grass. I picked up regular tofu spring rolls and a lemongrass tofu banh mi to go on a recent visit.   I picked up takeout on a recent night of terrible weather and was worried about getting back across the bridge before the heavens opened but my order was up pretty quick so ordering to leaving was very efficient.   The restaurant is really cute and I'll definitely be back to dine in at some point. They've done a lot with the basic stripmall box. All staff were masked and everything was really clean.  First my spring rolls by the time I ate these fatties, I was done. Finished. FULL! They were delicious and the regular tofu was really yummy. The next day I ate my banh mi for lunch and the lemongrass tofu was even better (and really aren't banh mis often better on day 2? Good amount of veg along with the tofu and yummy yummy bread.  Now I'll need to go back and try more things!

If you need a wig for a costume or to be incognito or for some more legitimate reason, this is the place to shop.  The staff is funny, friendly, and helpful.  The wigs are good quality from staid to outrageous.  They carry interesting jewelry, fun make up lines, and are willing to give you advice and help.

One of those shops that I didn't even know existed... and then I attended an event next door and noticed the closed shop. When I was back in the FQ this past weekend, I made a point to drop in.   The variety of items is impressive from purses made of old cowboy boots to original paintings to sculpture to glass; there is something for everyone.  I was familiar with some of the artists but others were entirely new to me. This is a great location to purchase a truly unique souvenir or gift

Pandemic update: I picked up Theo's for a work lunch (socially distanced of course) a few weeks ago. The pizzas were very good. We got one for the meaty folks and one veggie for the non-meaty. We got a Margarita and Marilyn's POTA Supreme and everyone was happy.  Service was great. Staff was masked and precautions were being taken.

Oh wow! When my coworker brought in day old baked goods AND they were gone before I could even make it to our kitchen, I knew I was in for something special.  I made it by on Saturday midday and had their special strawberry-peach freeform tart and a deviled egg for my lunch. Delicious!   Then I bought another tart and a cinnamon roll (although that's not what they call it) to bring to my parents. (I snitched a piece of the roll and also VERY tasty). And a durham loaf for myself. Everything was really good and not too sweet.   I can't wait to try a shave ice with their homemade syrups.

Hmmm...it's another case of the disappearing review. I was sure I had reviewed Brigtsen's previously.   I ate lavishly on the Coolinary dinner menu here last week. And really, my only problem with any of the dishes here is that they make me lose all self-control. I eat until I think I'm going to explode like that dude in the Meaning of Life.  The Coolinary courses that I had were: a salad with guacamole and shrimp, gulf fish with crab and shrimp with a bordelaise sauce and lemon ice box creme brulee.  The salad was good but the fish was UHmazing. It was pompano on the night I was there and my first thought was how jealous my Mom would be since that's her favorite. It was prepared perfectly and the crab on top was luscious and plentiful so much so that the shrimp were almost an afterthought...don't worry I ate those too.  The creme brulee was lemony and creamy and I could not stop eating.  The last time I was in was at Christmas and I had a reveillion menu. I need to stop saving this spot for special occasions and put it in regular rotation.   The restaurant itself is a sidehall cottage so you feel like you're dining in an elegant home and their are 3 small dining rooms so if you have a bigger group, definitely get a reservation. The staff is lovely and accomodating, no snooty waitstaff here.   I definitely need to go back soon.

Great new spot in the LGD! Look for the new build building and they are in the back on the left as you face the courtyard. I say this because the door is inset a little. Thanks goodness for their triangle floor sign... that's not their name but you know what I'm talking about.  I've been 2x already and had an assortment of cocktails. On one of the preview nights, I had a lovely glass of bubbles and sampled a Boulevardier. The other night with the fabulous Shercole, I tried a Rosy Disposition, at first I though the Pernod might be too much for me, but that was just the first sip. Refreshing and delicious. Second I had the Wrong Way Home, so tasty and citrusy.   I also tried the pimento cheese on a saltine which is stupidly delicious and the carrot puree which pops with ginger.  Service was great. And the atmosphere is well designed and fun. The outdoor courtyard is great... when it's not 80bajillion degrees.

I love that as this area has gentrified that the Corporation is still standing. Once upon a time this was a working man's bar and I used to stop in when I was just out of college because a friend of a friend's Dad owned the joint.    Fast forward a *few* years and the atmosphere and the mood is exactly the same. I love these unchangeable places we have.  And I'm really not sure why we haven't stopped here on any of our bar crawls.  Since I've only ever been here at night, I've never tried the food. May have to remedy that....

Pandemic update Love this neighborhood theater and so when they reopened and were showing the latest Bill & Ted movie, I had to go. I mean I saw the first two in the movie theater...  I went on a weeknight for the last show and attendance was sparse. And about 1/2 the theater seats were blocked off.  They had signs everywhere reminding you to wear your mask and I purchased my ticket in advance so that was contactless, but I did pay cash for my cocktail while enjoying the movie.  Staff was great as always. And bonus there was a preview of Alex Winters and the director (I think) thanking the Broad for their hospitality while filming the movie.  Good times.

Man was this place dirty. The carpet is in serious need of replacing in the lobby and I'm pretty sure someone had hurled in the hallway and stained the floor...or maybe it had happened that day. Eww...  But the sound was good and the screens were clean even in small theaters. And the space didn't smell. Isn't that sad that I have to state that.  But judging from the amount of food thrown on the floor, it isn't a given. Really moviegoers? You can't throw away your own trash?  The staff was fine and the time was convenient, so there you go.

I know lots of folks who love this restaurant but it's never my first choice.  I've had good food here, but not every time.  And it's pricey for mediocre food.  Plus it's really really loud.  I guess I'm just not a "lively" restaurant person.  The funniest thing was the last time I was there, my uncle (yes same one from the last review, he likes the place) questioned the waiter about a beer that they had on draft.  The waiter started to describe it and my uncle just told him to stop and go ask the bartender.  Poor waiter was trying to make it up; little did he know my uncle is king of all beer.

Pandemic Review: This outdoor theater opened in October in response to the pandemic and movie theater restrictions. It's located next door (across the side street) from the Broad. And it's a wonderful (and safer) addition to the neighborhood. The theater has a wide variety of entertainment from sports to movies to live music to a theatrical review.   I took my Mom to see the le Petite production of NOLA Noel on December 23rd. And the weather was great... not too chilly for my Mom and a very clear night. The chairs were well spaced and since we had to purchase tickets in advance, the seating was arranged by ticket groups.   The seating were adirondack styles some low, some high. We brought a couple of blankets just in case and Mom was happy to have those. There are portolets for bathrooms. And there is a trailer serving snacks and cocktails (a hot apple cider for Mom and hot buttered rum for me). Plus there was a food truck in the parking lot before the show started.  The show was really fun and the theater company made great use of the space and some popup tents for costume changes.  All staff were wearing masks and patrons were expected to wear them too unless eating and drinking. We were spaced well and it was outdoors so Mom could enjoy some theater!

Wow. I had no idea Pub Quiz was so popular! While attending Lindsay A's fabulous birthday bash, I was once again exposed to the joys of Finn McCool's and except for the crush of people, I think pubquiz is even better than now than when I attended regularly a few years ago.  It was also fun to be there without my super competitive brother who got a little too hyped up over the whole quiz thing.  I'm happy to report that no one threatened to stab anyone else in the neck last night over a changed answer...at least while I was there.    Boo Koo BBQ was cranking out the eats and their soup special of the evening, corn & crawfish bisque was delicious, if a little thick.  The fried mac-n-cheese balls were tasty but maybe a bit much for me.  Perhaps if I had more to drink?  The bartenders here are top notch and even with the crowd, remembered what I was drinking.  Great folks!    My only problem is that this is a full-smoking bar.  I hate coming home so stinky.

Oh yum! The perfect casual noshing after a long day. We had the ceviche and cru, daily special and the crab claws. All the food was super fresh and delicious. Service was quick and each dish was placed before us as it was ready.  I love that this is in a food court so I could pretty much eat a progressive dinner by wandering from kiosk to kiosk... except I didn't. I just gorged myself on seafood.  The chef & shucker were hustling to get orders up. Next time I'm going after those charbroiled oysters.

Tucks is really fun because of the ridiculous floats and throws.  My Mom was excited that I caught the toilet seat sunglasses (yes they have a lid that flips down).  I also caught several of the coveted mini-plunger throws...are you seeing the theme?    Great marching clubs to accompany the krewe including dragons!

This was my FIL's favorite restaurant mostly I think because it was a throwback to the day's of his youth.  I still miss the pre-K more extensive menu, but I am enjoying their more contemporary specials (grilled tuna salad!)  The garlic bread is as flaky as ever and the stuffed mushrooms are to die for.

So while the friends were in Bud's getting take out next door, I went into Pyramid and got a most excellent falafel sandwich.  I love that it comes with a side and their falafel seems lighter than many of the other places around town.  And the side of hummus seemed to have a bit of jalapeno sprinkled on top.  Yum!  The wait staff seems a bit...frazzled, but that's not a deal breaker.

Y'know Rex is a really pretty parade with classical themes and great signature floats.  I love that the Boeuf Gras breathes smoke. I'm also a big fan of the Royal Calliope.  The bands are always great.  This is another parade that uses the traditional wagon wheels rather than modern tires.  It gives great movement and sway to the props tumbling from the floats.

Originally I this store sold remaindered items from various midrange catalogs (explains the name), but now it  seems to be more of a basic women's boutique.  I must admit it had been several years since I lsdt stopped by.  The clothes are mostly geared to college  aged  females.  The selection is very of the moment.  The store carries  workout wear, shoes, casual party dresses,  lots of jeggings, and beaucoup accessories. I ended up with a cute  skinny lapel tuxedo style jacket....even though I went in looking for  Christmas presents. Oops

Um. Can a lingerie store be life changing? Maybe so.   When I realized that every single bra I owned was causing me pain, I decided it was time to get remeasured and see what I was doing wrong. Yeah. I was wearing bras that were completely not my size. Mind blown.  Staff was lovely and patient while I had a slight meltdown when I discovered my new size. Why do numbers matter so much to our own self image? They brought a variety of styles and colors to try on and helped me understand why some fit better than others.   Seriously, this shop has EXCELLENT customer service. And Joi is right. It smell lovely too.

So here's my big tip about the high rise, do not try to cross over on a low tank of gas. People will hate you when your car breaks down and traffic gets gacked up for miles.  Angie is correct; the few from the top is pretty but only gaze at length if you're a passenger. If you're the driver then keep your eyes on the road. Seriously why are there so many accidents?  As an occasional passerby, I find the bridge perfectly acceptable. If I drove this everyday I would need a rocket launcher.

Y'know I never understand Yelp's modus operandi. Sometimes businesses just get updated addresses and sometimes they get new listings. I reviewed this "new" business back in October under it's old address and asked for it to be moved. Whatever.  Since it has a new listing, here's my review. The staff/owners are really nice.  I love their new space inside the Rink. The light is amazing...thanks to the skylights. And the shop is open and airy. They've added a variety of items from different designers so now they have tshirts and cards in addition to jewelry.  I stopped in last week and bought gifts for 3 nieces with fall birthdays. They are still setting the store up so I'll have to check back soon to see what they've added. .

I like Plum Street snoballs but I don't *love* it. It's a really solid neighborhood shop with a large variety of flavors and yep those great Chinese food takeout containers, but I never eat that much snoball so I just stick to the cups.  The service is brisk and you better know what flavor you want when it's your turn, if a line is piling up behind you. The benches/seats/umbrellas out front is nice.   While some stands have branched out into other summertime treats, Plum Street sticks with snoballs which I appreciated.  Protip: add a little liquor to the snoball for the ultimate summertime drink.

This is a great choice for a semi-quick lunch...especially when you and your coworkers cannot agree. Lots of choices from the various food booths. And there is ample seating.  My group selected items from the Jamaican spot, the poke bow place and the Louisiana food spot. Everyone enjoyed their food and we didn't have to argue!  It is obviously a retrofit, but I think that adds charm to the place. There are staff moving around picking up trash (really people bus your own table!) and keeping things neat.  There's a bar so that's good if you need an adult beverage and the coffee shop was about to open when I was last there.  Some tables have access to power and their is WiFi so that's good for working.

I believe I began one of the most surreal nights of my life in the Sazerac bar; it was one of those evenings with a random group of acquaintances that mere alcohol can't explain.  And I promise no other substances were ingested by me.  That was maybe in the mid-90s?  Fast forward to summer 2009, the Sazerac bar is revitalized as part of the amazing renovation to the Grunewald/Roosevelt/Fairmont/Roosevelt.  The atmosphere is dark & sexy and the cocktails are delish.  Again, the drinks might be a bit on the pricey side, but c'mon you're paying for atmosphere.

OK. I'm not sure who these faceless yelpers are with axes to grind. But yes, Southeast Veterinary Specialist is pricey...because they are SPECIALISTS.    Dr. Rose has done 2 different surgeries on my sweet baby girl.  The first when she was a pup and had a bone chip in her elbow that cause her to limp.  The 2nd about 4 years ago because she had blown her ACL; she had TPLO - had to go look the initials up.  Her leg was completely rebuilt; it was expensive and worth it so that Sienna has a good quality of life.  Even though almost 10 years had passed between surgeries, Dr. Rose recognized Sienna immediately and talked about what a sweet girl she was the 1st time.  I consulted with a friend who is a vet and lives in NC. She said she would always refer this type of surgery to a specialist since she hasn't done it since Vet School.

My review of this realty firm will be a little different from others. I own a double and last year I hired Jean-Paul as the leasing agent.   For a reasonable price (a percentage of the first month's rent), he listed the unit on YouTube and I had a short-term renter within a month at a premium rent. He fielded inquiries, handled the application and interview process. Then ran a credit check on the applicant. He communicated with me throughout the process.   I would definitely hire Jean-Paul and his firm again as both a leasing agent and as a property manager. The process was super easy and smooth.

I've not taken any classes here, so I'm just reviewing the gallery space. And let me tell you, the gallery space is gorgeous! And sort of terrifying to a clumsy person like me.    There are amazing glass sculptures as well as smaller ornament type items and handmade wine glasses and the like. There are also prints and paper art but that's maybe 10% of what's on display.  Gorgeous work and lovely place to find a special gift or piece of art.

What a difference a change in venue makes! I've attended the seafood festival for a few years and it used to be a street festival near the casino.  Moving it to Lafayette Square seems to have quadrupled the attendance.  We went late on Saturday and the lines for some items were ridiculously long, especially since we had the little nieces with us.    We got a few items from booths with shorter lines and everything was tasty.  The crowds were well behaved and security was keeping paths clear.  There seemed to be fewer vendors than last year, but maybe not as many applied.

I still haven't made it back to Borgne for dinner, but I did stop by for pre-game  cocktails. Solid old-fashioned that was potent enough to carry me through the 4th quarter (no super expensive dome drinks for me).   Everyone else seemed to be enjoying the complimentary pork rinds. I chose not to eat them.    The bartenders were hussling and keeping a large crowd happy. Minus one star because we weren't allowed to order any food in the bar area. What? Not sure if that was the pre-game business or always.  Next time? Food.

Review is for delivery only. BUT HOLY COW these are delicious! I first discovered empanola last year when Rouse's had them in their restaurant to go section. Shrimp & cheese empanadas, yes please!  Fast forward to this week... and some coworkers and I had received a delivery GC from a pandemic project we had worked on. So we ordered the munchies pack. Six empanadas were the perfect way to close out the project. Ordering was easy online and now that I know where they are I'll have to driver over and get some more! One of my coworkers loved hers so much (shrimp & cheese and crawfish ettouffe) that she order more today for a family event this evening.   Don't sleep on these delicious treats! No pandemic comments since I had them delivered by a 3rd party.

Pandemic update: Momma wanted a gyro plate for her birthday and when I was hunting around to order online, Pyramid popped up. And I'm so glad. She LOVED her gyro plate and said the lamb and beef were delicious. Dad had the chicken shwarma and gobbled it up. I got the veggie plate and my falafel and tabouleh were good and the hummus yummy. Mom was not a fan of the babaganous. The spinach pies were a star and 1 pie is 2 good sized triangles.   Ordering was through the grubhub app and I opted to pick up on my way to their house. Everything was ready when I got there and they gave us beaucoup pita.   Ridiculous historical note: when Mom asked where the restaraunt was I told her where Bud's Seafood used to be, next to Bud's Broiler on Calhoun. Bud's Seafood closed in the 1970s. But she knew exactly what I was talking about.

Here's the thing Pat O's is a staple. It's not great, except for the piano bar...that is. Do not get a hurricane here, they are yucky. Make yourself a fresh fruit juice one at home instead. The bathrooms are generally stocked and clean.  I mean my parents went on dates here 50 years ago, how can I not give it 4 stars.  Random facts about Pat O's from my life:  My SiL's step-grandmother was a piano bar performer in the 50s. So she has one of the original bar tables.  A friend from HS somehow got hooked up with Andy Gibb's entourage in the mid80s. The stories are pretty epic.  My youngest brother watched the superbowl hear and everytime the Saints did something awesome, a patron left the bar and sprinted up and down an empty Bourbon Street.

The first time I ever went to this neighborhood dive, the bartender told me a long involved story about his lost love who only had one arm and mean mama. C'mon how are you EVER gonna top that?  The bartenders aren't quite as colorful in my experience in our post-K landscape but the bar remains the same. Cheap drinks, random person passed out on the bar, a cross section of humanity wandering in and out.  Good times.

Pandemic review: Take out Italian was the decision for Father's Day this year. And I had picked a restaurant... but they were closed for vacation. Whoops. So I searched around and found that Cafe Roma as open on Sundays and put in my order.   I picked up 2 shrimp pasta dishes (alfredo and primavera), 2 chicken sandwiches (parm and caesar) as well as large salad and a meatball app. My Mom said the meatballs were divine and saved them to add to pasta to make another entire meal. My Dad LOVED the chicken parm sandwich and my Mom really liked her chicken caesar. AND they were both enormous, easily making 2 meals for my parents. The 2 shrimp dishes had almost the same sauce with the alfredo just having more cheese. They were both good and the portion size was good. The garlic bread (cheese bread, not much garlic) was tasty and the side salad was a good portion.  Ordering was easy (via grubhub) and pickup was right on time. There was a table barring entrance into the restaurant and the person who brought me my food was wearing a mask.  Will definitely be back in the future.

You know you have the olds when you want to start an Abe Simpson like story with... I remember when this park was first built but there you go. Back when I was in grade school this was just scrub AND a bird preserve because we drove past and I saw the sign and learned what a preserve was.  Now unlike most of the green spaces in JP which are playgrounds this is truly a park. And it has space for everyone. From running trails to dog areas to play areas to bbq spots to a soccer field to places to be chased by geese. The park really does have it all.  It's also the location for many JP festivals and fairs so prepare for not enough parking at those times. The main entrance is on West Napoleon but there is also a secondary entrance on Downs Blvd. There's also a pedestrian entrance where York dead ends into Judith but I'm not sure when that gate is unlocked.

I had an actual party to go to and I looked in my closet and did not want to wear anything I already owned. So I decided it was time to shop local and get me a new dress.  I'm short and I'm curvy so not all styles worked on me, but the lovely sales person worked with me until we found a style that looked cute and that I liked the pattern.   The sales person was great to work with and she was very helpful. All staff was masked and they asked that all customers be masked too.

I've been curious about this spot for awhile. So since my feet have just been aching lately (I blame every pair of shoes I own), I decided to stop by and ask for a foot massage.  My foot massage was great. First your feet are washed and then you can just lay back and enjoy. Eventually I was asked if I would like more time and/or a neck/should massage. Of course, since I was getting so relaxed I said yes. For my neck/shoulder massage I moved into one of the private rooms. But I stayed fully clothed. Also for those who are thinking pervy thoughts, there is a sign to keep your genitals covered because c'mon. Eww.   The space is kept semi-dark and restful. And I appreciate that the atmosphere makes everyone use quieter tones as they walk in because you can certainly hear everything that's said.   The price point was good. They do take walk-ins but you can also call in to reserve a time. Reserving is smart especially on the weekend if you want to come in with a group. They do take credit cards but there is a $2 surcharge to do so. There is an ATM as well but I bet it also has the charge.

I am a fan of this independent movie theater! They get small films and the blockbusters. They are engaged with their audiences and have a bar! With 4 screens they do offer something for everyone.  Some of the screens are smaller but the sound is good and the seaters are comfy. I can zoom over from my house pretty quickly and it's even quicker if I go straight from work.   If it's a busy night then tickets are sold a the ticket counter, if slower than they are sold a the concession stand... kids aren't really allowed at that counter because it's also the bar. Not really sure how that works if they're selling tickets from there and you're under 21. You can purchase tickets online which has been a lifesaver for a popular event or movie.  My only problem with the theater is the parking. The lot is small and people park willynilly so that's it's hard to get in and out of the spots that exist. And some spots are striped white and others yellow... only one color (and I forget which) belongs to Broad, the rest belong to the building adjacent. Otherwise street parking.  Great to have another first run theater in the city!

Pandemic swan song for one of my favorite shops... A&C has lost their lease so they will be closing in the next 10 days. And will shift to an online store while looking for a new space. I hope she finds one that suits her as well.  Not only does this shop feature Maria's beautiful jewelry but she also takes consignments from other designers and features a host of fun, funky, earth-friendly items.  I have bought gifts for myself and a host of family and friends here over the last 6 years. If you can get in before the doors are shut, almost everything is 15-30% off.   I hope the next chapter is great.

I finally got to taste the mythical Dong Phuong King Cake and it was delicious! I had always heard how could it was and now I know.  The pastry is somewhere between a brioche and a croissant and the cream cheese filling was light and well distributed.  Fighting the crowd in the bakery (who were mostly there for more traditional items) was a bit of a hassle, but the cake was worth it.  Wish I hadn't had to stuff my own baby.  Now I just need to go back and eat in the restaurant again.

So I'm in Brentwood and my niece was disappointed that she didn't get to take the driving test...something about too many people or something. So what's a good aunt to do?  Check her Yelp app and find a nearby bakery for deliciousness stat!  Being the awesome aunt, I spent over $30 on cookies and pastries for the whole family. We got gorgeous iced cookies (favorites were the dinosaur and the unicorn...we got into a fight over who got to eat the unicorn's butt & I won!), apple strudel, chocolate croissant, wedding cookies, chocolate chip cookies and the AMAZING chocolate bombe. Seriously it was so good.  The staff was friendly and helpful despite my haphazard ordering style. And everything was well packaged for the trip home.  I would definitely come back for lunch.

Stopped by this new spot on the rainy Sunday after being cooped up at home by TS/Hurricane Barry. They only had an abbreviated menu and were out of some options. But I get it.   Love the space and I had a couple of lovely pours of bubbles. The wine list is interesting and has some nice selections. And I can't wait to try some of their signature cocktails. We ordered a preservation plate and the pickled mirlitons were my favorite. My friend LOVED the hogshead cheese.   The staff is great and since it's near NOAC on Decatur, parking was easypeasy.   I can't wait to come back on a normal night and try the full menu. PLUS the kitchen is open until 1am on weeknights and 2 am on weekends. So great to have options.

Copeland's used to be OK.  But now... Huge plates of inferior food.  I also find some of their choices of sides or sauces sort of random.  Like let's just throw everything at the plate and see what sticks, random.  I used to like this original location (and one of my brothers worked in the kitchen in the 80s~maybe), but now I just think it's past its prime.

Pandemic Review: This is truly a warehouse with wide open doors on the Sunday that I visited so dress accordingly. Of course, that means that it feels a bit safer these days with the super tall ceiling and the feeling of being outdoors. Masks are required and hand sanitizer was supplied, FYI.  They've also been hosting art markets in their backyard on weekends in December which is great.  Some of the vendors were new to me and it's always fun to discover new work.  The furniture inside is mostly BIG pieces or maybe that's just what they have at the moment. And they have a custom furniture shop so if you need a specific piece for a weird nook, I'm sure they could hook you up.   Make sure to check out the crazy cactus garden in the yard!

Maybe it's good that Dong Phuong isn't closer to my house because y'all know I love the baked goods and Dong Phuong does it right.  Love their cream puffs, their eclairs, their king cakes (of course) and their bread. But what prompted the review today? Rouse's (at least the one on Tchoupitoulas) is carrying their cookies in the bakery department!!!  And the price is great. $4.99 for about 2 dozen bakery cookies is a bargain. We've had the almond, the champagne, and the butter cookies all delicious.  Now I just have to get my lazy self over the east and try these 3 dollar sandwiches that Jeff is talking about.

I must admit that I'm not much of a quarter rat these days, but Erin Rose is a solid, neighborhoody-type bar...despite it's location just off Bourbon. It's small enough to feel intimate but with high ceilings that make it seem more spacious than it is.   My most recent visit was with a bunch of our fellow yelpalistas.  When our bartender, Molly, heard who we were she told us about a review that named her specifically...to her detriment.  As we all wandered out into the night we promised to mention her in our reviews.  So I highly recommend you go see Molly & buy her a shot and if you're lucky, she'll call you a pussy...and she says that with love, of course.

They have a good selection of accessories, wigs, and package costumes (which you are allowed to try on).  Do not wait until the last minute because the store is PACKED in the days before Halloween & Mardi Gras.  My biggest gripe with them is that all customers crowding the counter and you just hope to catch a salespersons eye to have them pull some accessories and then find a cashier to ring up your purchases.  The rest of the year their main business comes from selling dancewear, shoes, leotards, and the like.

Attended an anniversary party at this venue this evening.  It was a little strange to get to as it's in an industrial corridor, but the space itself was attractive inside and the staff was nice and helpful.  The food was fine & the bartenders made decent drinks as long as you didn't ask for anything to complicated.

I stopped in at Tchoup Yard on Friday night for a birthday party... and this is a great spot for a gathering since it's HUGE! In fact it takes up an entire city block!  I like that there are so many different spaces to enjoy, from being indoors to being out in the open to the firepit area (it was a little chilly on Friday) to being on a covered porch. Something for everyone. AND the outdoor spaces are dog friendly so I made a couple of dog friends!  There's a huge selection of beer for the hop heads but there's also non-alcoholic and a full bar for the folks who prefer something else. There's also a food area. My friends were allowed to bring in cupcakes for the birthday fella. And remember this is a bar space so it's 21 and over and they card EVERYONE, even those of us who are more than 2x the age minimum.   I have been to one private event here where they took over a whole section (of the parking lot maybe) and set up a stage so that was fun!   There's a good sized parking lot along the 2nd street side of the property... although the address is on 3rd street, there is no entrance at that location.

When the owner of this classic lounge passed over the summer, I thought "that's it. Gone." I'm so glad I was wrong.  I saw a post that said the bar would reopen at 11am on December 26th and I was over there by 12:30pm. And it was the same old joint... but cleaner!  I was really worried about how it would smell after being closed up for months, but the new management had a cleaning crew in there who did a great job. Same old shabby everything and Danielle was a great returning bartender for the day shift.  At the moment it will not be 24/7 but they are planning on 11am to 4am (or later if the crowd is good). So I guess that will do.   It was fun to hang out and watch all the neighbors stop in and grab a beer and say hi. Lots of hugs and reminiscing going around.

Since I just reviewed the Elmwood location and the Uptown location is one of my go to places for pizza, I realized that I never reviewed the mid-city location.  Theo's is a solid thin crust American style pizza. The toppings are interesting and of good quality.   This location is spacious and comfortable. The staff is friendly and helpful.   The specials are usually yummy and the pricing for adult beverages is good.

Sometimes you need to turn on the radio & step back in time. WTIX was the station you listened to on your transitor AM radio (kids go look it up). Then they got all fancy & went FM in the mid70s.  They play oldies with a distinct New Orleans flair.  Plus it turns out it's now owned by one of the big 70s/80s era morning DJs.  Could for him.  Inspiration for this review? Fats Domino singing Jambalaya @ 8:15 this morning

Y'know it's fine. We've all changed shape slightly during this last year...  So I went and got re-measured before I started investing in new bras. And yep I had changed sizes slightly since I was measured over 6 years ago. It happens.  I was offered a host of options and ended up with a couple. And they are working fine. The sales person was helpful and listened to my concerns. No hard sell tactics here.  Masks all around and there were only a couple of people in the store when I was there. Hand sanitizer was available too.

There aren't a ton of places to eat near my work, but since this place has opened it's now our go to spot.  The plate lunches are a great value. (Friday special was 2 good sized pieces of des Allemands catfish - yes they specified - mac n cheese, fresh green beans and a large biscuit covered in honey & butter.)    I've had their small fried shrimp poboy and ate it for two meals. As I said in my tip, the cup of gumbo is normal bowl sized and their bowl of gumbo is a serving bowl. I haven't tried it but my coworker had the chicken & sausage and said it was good, just not as spicy as she prefers.  The fried pickles are delish.  Table service if you're dining in. Staff is courteous and fun. Definitely worth a trip to Tulane Ave.

I get so tired of throwing all my recyclable glass in the trash since it's not collected in curbside recycling. I used to bring it to a local big box store but then they stopped collecting. le sigh.  So when I heard of this business, I was excited. Of course by the time I had made my move to bring in a batch, they had moved out to Louisa but oh well.   Drop off is easy. There are bins with colors (clear, green, brown, and blue) over them and you drop your bottles inside... which is LOUD. They do have monthly curbside pickup but there have to be enough people in your neighborhood to make it feasible. Otherwise you go on a waiting list.   Best of all the glass is turned into sand which is then used in coastal erosion projects!  Pandemic notes: Everyone was masked and dropoff is outside of a warehouse so no indoor contact.

The newest Racetrac in town... RIP Picadilly... All shiny and new and the pumps are so fast! And there are so many of them, as befits this chain. Plus the gas was a few cents cheaper than other local spots.  As I was pumping gas, kids ran back to an SUV next to me saying they had gotten FOOD! and boy did they. It almost made me go inside and stock up on beaucoup snacks. Next time!

Oh my. This was the location of my niece's wedding on Saturday night and we had the whole space and it was GORGEOUS!  All the out of town guests were super impressed with the historic FQ charm and I was really impressed with the staff and the food.  All the items from the fancy crudite display to the passed appetizers to the crawfish ettouffe to the amazing mashed potatoes were yummy.   The staff was really accommodating to the various needs of my family, from finding an additional chair for older parents to pretending I wasn't sitting in a corner on the floor with a child crashed in my lap.   Of course, this being NOLA, I'm friends with a few of the management folks who run the joint but my brother wasn't aware of that connection until late in the game. But I did get to hear how helpful and responsive they were after the fact, especially with all the players involved in the wedding planning.  Thanks, Latrobe's for a wonderful night.

Solid little boutique in a strip mall across from Lakeside shopping Center. I was on a quest to find the PERFECT dress for a family wedding in July in the FQ. And this was one of my stops. And it was having it's grand opening!  The shop is not huge but the selections are really varied with dressy items along with more casual wear. The accessory selection was really cute too.  The dressing rooms were spacious and the staff person was really helpful and friendly without being pushy.  I liked the colorful selections and loved the really different styles that they had here. I didn't find my perfect dress at this location but I will be back.

Brunch review!  I headed over to Paladar with my friends on a rainy Sunday midday. We had reservations which is probably a good thing and were seated immediately.  My group was hyped over the food and we ordered family style and with 4 of us we had: lemon-ricotta pancakes (stunning), 2 orders of the eggs benedict (delish), yellowfish crudo (good), spicy breakfast pizza (good) and corn, tomato and burrata salad (delicious) and crab soup (delish). Plus a couple of Pimm's cups, mimosas and a bloody (nice & spicy).   Service was great. And the atmosphere is fun.

I've been hearing raves about this bar since it opened and finally made it over to have a beverage last weekend. And let me say upfront, the Ward 8 was perfection in a glass. Simple and delicious and just perfect.  My friends had two of the other fancy cocktails and said they were fine but not as good as mine. We didn't have anything to eat... nothing on the menu jumped out at us.  The space is gorgeous and our server was lovely (and hustling as it was HH). But but... I don't know. It was all a little forced fun, maybe because it was the first weekend of parades. I don't know.  I'll have to try again. And of course get the same drink on a night when it's not so crowded.

Pandemic update I was so happy when Brigtsen's reopened a couple of weeks ago for take out only. AND I was really impressed to hear that chef is giving his kitchen staff time to shine with dishes that they came up with.   On Wednesday I called in my order (10am to 3pm / Tuesday-Saturday) and arranged for a 5:30pm pick up. The menu is updated daily on their website. I had already discussed with my Mom what she wanted so we ordered: the gulf fish meuniere, blackened tuna, vegetable Thai curry, an app of shrimp remoulade AND creme brulee and brownies.  The meuniere was gorgeous and the tuna was delicious. They both came with sides of veg and mashed potatoes. My Mom who is not really a mashed potato fan said they were divine. And the portions were large enough that we both had 2nd meals from our servings. The shrimp remoulade was tasty and I love the sauce mixed with a bit of guacamole.  I saved my curry for my lunch today and it was amazing, rich and tasty. Finally my Mom did a happy dance for the lemon ice box creme brulee, so good. And the brownies were also really really good. And you get 4!!!  After your time slot, you drive up to the restaurant from River Road towards Maple. One person with a clip board gets your name and another person brings out your food. I pre-paid with my credit card (and didn't forget the tip) so super easy. They only take so many people per time slot so it works really well. All restaurant staff is masked and gloved.   Next time I'm getting the redfish!

Hmph. I'm almost certain that I've reviewed this spot before...but maybe that was undera a different name. This shop has a great selection of local crafts as well as national brands.  Need a wacky gift for a friend? Want to just find something superfun and not too expensive? This is your shop. Items purchased here over the years: fun plastic earrings for the grade school nieces, lego themed jewelry for a cousin, fancy bracelet for a special birthday for a friend, cat themed socks for a teen niece, locally made candles for an aunt... and so on and so on.  Definitely a great shop to browse because you never know what you'll find.

This is a great small makeup shop. That does makeup lessons/applications in store and by appointment on-location.  They sell various lines here, like my beloved Blinc mascara and locally made Kismet lipsticks. The staff is wonderful and will help you find the perfect shade for you. I love that they clearly want you to feel beautiful and not just upsell you whatever the latest product is.

My precious is back in my hands thanks to these guys.  I did experience a few communications bobbles with them...some were probably my fault but not all.  My phone is fixed and for the price that I expected.  And the southshore location is certainly convenient for me....I just would have had my phone faster if I would have driven myself over to Mandeville.  For the record I have an Android slider phone; the cable between the keyboard and the screen finally broke when I dropped it one too many times.  Makes me think that I may have to look into a different phone this summer when my new every 2 deal comes up.

Nice low key neighborhood coffee shop.  Good selection of teas and they offer bubble tea too which really isn't too common in NOLA.  But if you're offering a vegan coffee cake, why wouldn't you have a vegetarian sandwich offering?

Had a mini-shopping-palooza today and hit a few of the clothing consignment shops (Prima Donna, Swap, Encore, and On the Other Hand) uptown in search of a formal gown that would fit my short, curvy self.    On the Other Hand, located in the Carrolton Neighborhood, was the most overwhelming of the stores; it is CHOCK-FULL of merchandise.  The sales person who assisted me was very solicitous and helped me figure out the dressing room situation.  Seriously the store is going to explode from stock.  This store probably had the greatest number of formal gowns, but some of them seemed to date from 1984; so if I was drag queen, it would have been perfect.  The prices were very reasonable but I think I was losing my urge to rummage.  I also think they carry men's clothes so that also makes them unique.

As I walked in, I realized that I've been to this location several years ago for a rather indifferent massage. I'm sort of glad I didn't remember because my massage this time was AMAZING. Ashley was great and my 80 minute massage was the perfect length to make me feel like a puddle.  Love that you can do online booking so you can see what's available in advance. Including booking same day. AND you can choose a specific person or anyone or enter a preference for gender.   The space is very calming and depending on your service they do have a good locker area and I think showers.   Street parking only and make sure you pay the meters for the right amount of time since nothing ruins a relaxing spa experience like coming out to a parking ticket.

Confused about what to get a special child in your life, the staff at the Magic Box is amazingly helpful.  They have the best toys!  Great sections for crafty kids, musical kids, girly-girls, macho-boys, geeks, boardgame freaks, babies, toddlers, everyone.  OK the Madame Alexander doll section freaks me out a little.  I think they are staring into my SOUL.

If it weren't for my Yelpy friends, I wouldn't have known the name of this charming little oasis. I've parked my car adjacent to this park a bajillion times as I sampled the restaurants on Esplanade.   I've enjoyed the plantings, the art, the benches all supplied by local residents. I love that this park is allowed to be semi-wild with raucous plantings but never looks uncared for.   Truly a great spot to stop and take a breath.

Just bought champagne for a family party.  The staff was helpful and did not try to upsell me which I appreciated since I had to buy a bunch of bottles.  There prices are good, but don't expect any really cheap bottles here. They go for quality instead.  They also carry some hard liquor & mixers.  Buy a bottle & go next door to drink it with some cheese at St. James.

What a great festival!   We had gorgeous weather, really good music (mostly blues when I was there recently) which my friend who attends regularly said was bit out of the norm. There were food trucks and vendors. And activities for the kids and the pets.  Coming from NOLA, I thought it was nice that there was a beer garden but odd that you had to be fenced off from the populace in general. The beer must not escape the picket fence!  Loved that there were some mature trees to offer shade and that there was plenty of space. Did not love dog owners who cannot control their pets.

I've been to Bar Frances quite a few times since they opened. I've had dinner twice and brunch once and then just drinks...  I was actually surprised the first time I came in (opening night!) to see they had a full dinner menu. From the pre-opening information, I thought this was going to be a wine bar with a small selection of snacks. NOPE. Full restaurant. So I sat at the bar and ate...everything that first night and it was delicious! And it's remained delicious each time I've been back.   LOVE the mushroom toast. Love. It's on Bellegarde bread and is super luscious and savory. I've had a couple of different salads and each has been delicious as have the veg sides (those snap peas are amazing). Loved the avocado toast for brunch (again on the Bellegarde bread). The bartenders make a great old fashioned. I've also had some lovely glasses of bubbles at good prices.  The space is very industrial and they are slowly warming it up. They've added pursehooks at the bar (yay) and some acoustical panels on the ceiling which has helped the volume between my 2nd and 3rd visits.   Great spot to hang out with friends and enjoy a beverage and some yummy food.

So I saw this truck and was like, what? Of course the owner is named Jon and he's from Slidell, LA. But I didn't head to Nashville to get jambalaya.   My friend got the chicken and waffles (half mild & half spicy). I snitched a bit of waffle and it was really tasty. She knew from experience that all spicy was too much for her and the half and half was just perfect.  The items are made to order so it can take a bit of time. But definitely a truck with an inventive menu.

OK. Really it's a fine bakery. It's just... I miss the old shop. The one with rich but not too sweet pastries... now the tasted are sweeter and probably more in line with what the general American public wants.   I haven't seen the French style king cakes here. And the recipe for the NOLA style are the same ones from Cochon Butcher.   They've expanded their sandwich selection too AND added ice cream. Phew. There's a lot going on in this shop.  The decor is minimal and still lovely. Not much has changed from the previous owners. There's a small amount of seating but I mostly take out.   Solid bread selection.

I knew the reviews weren't great, but decided to give this place a try. And it was packed on a Thursday night...maybe it's because of their extensive outdoor seating and the gorgeous weather.  We ended up inside, but that' was OK since the enormous garage doors were open.  The chips were delicious, very fresh and tasty. The salsa was a bit meh, but OK.  We had a couple of different tacos..fried fish was deemed OK, the grilled shrimp were really tasty, the vegetarian tacos...were really weird and odd tasting.  And the baja quesadilla was gone so I'm guessing it was good.  The tres leches cake was served in a bowl of milk which may be off putting for some.  Big warning...the sangrias here are fortified. The white sangria has a lot of rum and the red has brandy.  So be prepared for that...I should have read the menu better.  Service was indifferent to odd.

Wow. This is one of those places that I sort of shutdown because it's so HUGE. This is the biggest used book/record/cd/dvd/game store I've ever been in.  I was impressed with the organization and that the staff seemed to be working diligently to get everything back on the shelves. The gamers corner was a really cool idea with not just games but controllers and consoles.  I bought a bunch of books (yea! heavier luggage going home) and my friends bought a bunch of LPs.  It's probably a good thing that I don't live any closer to this store.

Oh look. It's the other Dillard's around town (ignore the listing that says 70112 since there is not downtown store and it's actually a duplicate for this location...an update that I've submitted to Yelp HQ at least 3x). ANYWAY. It's a department store, you can buy everything from some undies to a sofa to pots and pans to holiday decor.   And really you know that the holiday decor is why I'm bothering to review this National store, because Dillard's bought out Maison Blanche which means they own the legal rights to produce Mr. Bingle, Santa's snowman helper. And y'all know how I love Mr. Bingle.

The Pontchartrain Center is on the other end of the earth to me, right off the lake on Williams Blvd.  It is Kenner's answer to the convention center.  It can be rearranged into a variety of configurations.  None have been to great.  The staff was surly, the bathrooms weren't very clean, the parking was nightmare AND I there were men in inappropriately short shorts b/c Back to the Beach was happening just across the levee and the casino.  Thank goodness my niece is quitting dancing school, so I won't have to go to another dance recital here next year.  I hope it will be another decade before I return.

I stopped in to this location last Sunday to look at their supercute seatbelt purses and it was pretty busy. The store isn't huge (go to the Metry one for big) but the staff was very nice and helpful.  I think it's  really interesting that this store is so successful in the FQ since I think many of it's shirts are uber-local. I have to explain the K&B crayon one to newbies pretty often. So high marks to Lauren that her shop attracts tourists as well as locals.  Great place to shop for local crafts, art & tshirts.

I like that this art market happens in the evening/at night so you can browse before dinner or whilst wandering with a drink. And I love that there is some space to move in the center (although walking down the alley to get to the larger space can feel like running a gauntlet).  Not all the art is to my taste, but there is something for everyone...photos, prints, jewelry, housewares, paintings, vintage ... you get the idea. Also this market occurs every week (Thursday-Sunday) rather than monthly like many others so it's easier to get too.  Sellers are personable to grumpy. The space can be a bit much when crowded. But other nights, it's a lovely spot to browse and find a perfect gift for yourself or someone else.

Tasty but OMG loud. There was a table of 50 year olds enjoying the free corkage repeatedly to the point that they were shrieking the entire time we were there.  But that's not really their fault so I'll give them the 4th star and hope it's better when I go back.  I had the yummy brie fries and the Catch sandwich; the sandwich was big enough that I ate it for 2 meals.    The space is sparse but in a clean way and they seem to still be adding elements as they can.  The staff was nice but spacey...maybe the shrieking olds had gotten to them too....

Lake Lawn is a large cemetery and it is very well kept.  I was here on Easter Sunday for their sunrise (7 am) ecumenical service with the Zion Harmonizers. It was a lovely ceremony out amongst the tombs...which I get may seem a bit weird to some.  I can also say that the staff here is professional and kind. We worked with them a couple of years ago when a family member died. They were helpful and made the process easier.

I'm a little torn about the 4 stars... Yes this is a solid neighborhood choice for sweet fried dough and if you're a coffee drinker, you're covered. There are ZERO tea options. The hot chocolate was meh. So as a non-coffee drinker, I can have water or overpriced bottled juice. OK.  But they still get the 4 stars for an amazing staff. Seriously, every time I've been in here, they are lovely and friendly. They clearly know the names of their regulars.   I think the Metairie location has more drink options and I wish this spot did too.

I only had cocktails here so I can't really comment on the food.  But the watermelon mojito that I had and the cucumber cosmo that my friend had were certainly worthy of a detour.   Will have to go back and actually have something to eat.

Le sigh I saw that friends liked this place and it was around the corner from where I was parked so I took a chance.  Our server (see Katie A's review) was...a little lost. Pretty much everything we said seemed to confuse him.  The space itself is lovely both inside the restaurant and the attractive patio I peeked into  I got a cup of the seafood gumbo and it was mediocre at best. I also had a special salad which was grilled romaine with shrimp. The salad was OK. Some of the romaine was overcooked and it just made me long for the superior version at Boucherie.  I sampled a couple of companions items. The ceviche wasn't...it was a cold seafood salad. The roasted okra was amazing. The rest, meh.  So maybe next time I'll try the bar instead

I decided to try someplace new and walked over for a fancy pedicure. I had checked them out from their website (which let me know that this place is a chain) and I found a first time user coupon which made any of their $45 pedicures $29. Yes please.  The reception area was inviting and the racks of polish were attractively arranged. We discussed which pedicures I could get for the coupon and I chose the Happy Feet. I was picked my color and headed to the pedicure area. There are 24 chairs...which are not massage chairs (in case that's your favorite thing). There were also maybe a dozen manicure stations as well in the same room.   My pedicure was very thorough and I realize thta the massage chairs usually distract me from the foot sanding, but I survived AND did not kick the technician. Whew. Part 2 of the HF pedicure was a neck/shoulder massage. A bench was slid over the foot bath and I simply reversed my seated position. The massage was by a different person than the pedicure. (Important to know if you like to tip in cash like me.) And it was somewhere between a traditional chair massage and an acupressure one. Then I sat back in the pedicure chair again for the intense leg foot massage. Wowsers. I would definitely pay the extra $ for that again.   A bit pricey to become my regular basic pedicure spot, but I'll definitely return for the extra pampering.

So how does a non-beer drinker rate a brewhouse?  There's a bunch of beer and that seems to make other people happy and I've even tried some of it but it all tastes like beer. They do have the deliciously addictive Mexican coke and other non-beer/non-alcohol drinks.  And the space is huge so I've seen dance rehearsals and craft fairs and all sorts of things happening here...so that's what keeps me coming back.  The staff is great and there's food and parking in the back. All the things most people need.

Petite Grocery was the locale for my birthday dinner this year and it was great selection.  The atmosphere is lovely; they've kept just enough details to remember the old grocery store (the tin ceiling, the flooring) along with some nice additions (the work station is a vintage looking sideboard).  Since my birthday is right after New Year's and was the middle of the week this year, the restaurant was pretty empty when we arrived, but the bar was full; evidently folks are taking advantage of the happy hour specials (drink and appetizer specials from 5:30-6:30).  Our cocktails were well made and we were given some brand choices.   We both had salads for our first course; I had the celery root & apple and E had the Caesar; bother were well balanced & very fresh.  For entrees, E had the evening's special which was fish and I had 2 appetizers (although one would have been plenty).  E's fish (can't remember the details) came out Napoleon style which I thought was silly since you had to break it down to be able to eat it.  My appetizers were a special of pasta with lobster cream sauce and the crab & brie "gratin."  I should have paid attention to the quotation marks as the gratin (which I had very much been looking forward too) was not at all what I thought it would be.  It was tasty but a little dry.  The lobster special was better with a yummy pasta & sauce (that's what bread is for, right?) and the lobster was very sweet.  For dessert (since it was my birthday) we had chocolate pudding (my favorite!) and creme brulee.  Both were good.

I've passed this gallery a million times but never stopped in until last month. And why did I stop in? This gallery carries Dr. Seuss art AND they had a traveling exhibit of Dr. Seuss' hat collection. Y'all have no idea how much I wanted to try on a hat, but they were behind plexi so no arrests were necessary.  The rest of the gallery is a whimsical mix of contemporary artists, like Peter Max. They have both small sculptures as well as paintings and limited edition prints. Oh how I wish I could afford a Theodore Geisel original.  Customer service was great and the owner even got a piece out of their storage area for me to look at.   I also appreciated that the gallery has a small bit of old signage on the brick highlighted in the corner window and framed by drywall. Art is where you find it after all.

Used to be the RC Bridge Lounge, but I guess they dropped the initials when they went all upscale.  Good selection of premium liquors at decent prices.  Yes the mojitos (and mint juleps) rock.  Love the dog portraits and that doggies are welcome.  Minus points for turning up the jukebox to 11 about 30 minutes after we arrived last night.

Cruising around the burbs and hunting for a pedicure place because it was necessary AND it's Sunday and Yay this shop is open.  The shop is clean an spacious. The techs were polite and not chatty. It was really busy on a Sunday afternoon but they took care of business.  My pedicure was fine and the price was OK. But it's not someplace I'd seek out otherwise.

I asked my brother where he's been purchasing his crawfish (live) this year and he said Michael's (which was formerly Gator's and before that an oil change place). I called them for a price on pre-boiled for a party and they were 20 cents cheaper (and day of even cheaper than that) than anywhere else.  I placed my order and gave them a time. Easy peasy.  The price was good, picking up and paying was easy. So why 3 stars? The pre-boiled just weren't that great. They were OK. And I was glad that I could get potatoes and corn sides. But the potatoes seemed like they were just boiled plain and then had spices dumped on them.  I would use them again but maybe just for live...

A solid choice for a basic drink in the French Quarter. Don't go expecting to order a fancy frou-frou cocktail and you'll be fine.  The bartenders are speedy and personable. The decor is minimal. The jukebox is great. The bathrooms are usually clean-ish and stocked.   I hadn't been in several years, but then I was wandering with Betty from Cali and we ran into Joi & her krewe AND we were right by Aunt Tiki's so it was fate, right? The company of course makes anyplace better or worse. And with these friends, it was all the fun.

Wow. I finally got to go to a Tales of the Cocktail Spirited Dinner because Bourbon House is offered a vegetarian option menu. AND it was a whiskey dinner, my favorite!!!  Ah, if only, my initial excitement had carried me through. The whiskey was, of course, excellent. The dishes (even some of the meaty ones) were not always well matched with the liquor...which was the whole point I thought.  Confusion abounded (from the reservations to the servers) regarding the veg.option. I tried to tell them when we reserved out spots; they said no need to let the house know when we checked in...at check in, they were dismayed to learn I wanted the alternate menu. The servers repeatedly served me meat dishes...although I must admit I kept the delicious scallop dish with the vanilla cream and I'm glad I did it was the best dish of the night (yes, I'm pescetarian really). BUT it didn't really go with the Irish Whisky it was served with.  My other dishes were a 2 salads and a red bean hummus dish that was more of appetizer.
