And there are a lot of fun touches (like the salt & pepper shakers clued to matchbox cars). There were beaucoup tourists there on the Saturday before Christmas so they were confused by parking and the queue, etc. I would like my little bubble of space to not be invaded, please.  Definitely a fun spot to take in breakfast/lunch.

I wandered into this pretty new nail shop a couple of weeks ago and they do "princess pedicures" for kids (cost $20). And my little nieces were begging for a treat.  That day, they only had time/people to do the two girls, but I went back today and had my toes did.   The shop is small but well appointed. The instruments used came out of a sealed package so I trust the cleanliness. I liked that someone compulsively sorts the nail polish by color and that the display is like an art piece on a wall rather than in spinny displays.  The price is good at $25 for a basic pedicure.  And the staff was nice...if perhaps a bit unpolished themselves.  This probably won't replace my go to nail spot, even at the cheaper price point.  But I would definitely stop by again, especially if I'm on aunt duty.

My breakfast was *really* greasy to the point that I really couldn't eat it. But everyone else seemed to enjoy their food.  Next time I'll get the ginormous pancake and have left overs for 3 days.  The server handled our drunken krewe really well and just rolled with our nonsense so high marks for that.  The food came out quickly and was hot.

I just took a class from an archivist at the Williams Research Center (part of the New Orleans Historic Collection) and was able to enjoy this specialty library.  Their collection of artwork is lovely as is the facility. The staff is accommodating and helpful.  And as Jude F said the collection really is something special.  Yes, the university libraries around town all have Louisiana collections, but the WRC is the only one located in the FQ and that makes it unique.

OMG truck floats...with the constantly blowing horns and the sound systems....  OK, I kind of like the sound systems otherwise the entire block wouldn't have been doing the wobble in the middle of the street...I think the wobble was the official dance of Carnival 2013.  This is the favorite of all children because they throw tons and tons of junk.  As a side note, parents inspect those stuffed animals before you let your baby/toddler play with them... some are soaked in beer and some are just dirty.  I caught some classic old school 1970s beads which are about the only throw I'm holding on to this year.
An excellent somewhat eccentric history museum. Eccentric because it began it's life as one couple's collection.  They create exhibits that are fascinating and thought provoking.

Oh, Buds.  A number 6 with sauce actually tempts me to eat beef again...  Friends were visiting from out of town over the weekend and hitting Buds was a MUST on one of their lists.  She said it was just as wonderful as she remembered.

I met a herd for friends here for a birthday celebration...and that may have been the problem. That we were a herd. We were polite and seated at the center long table ... and two of the servers got into an argument, twice, about who had to take care of our table.   Need a new drink? GRAB a server as they tried to scoot by us. Want to order food? Again, attempt to flag down someone, anyone.  The folks in the middle of the table had it the worst.  The food I had was tasty and I hear the cocktails were good. But if you're going to offer a yelp checkin/4square check in deal, make sure it's reflected on the final bill...which I hear took about 30 minutes to sort out.   I would give it another shot, just not with a big group.

Miss Linda is getting all fancy (in her dress not in her food, don't worry) since winning Chopped in 2012. She had a custom chef's jacket with her name embroidered the last time I saw her. And because of her fame (see also: Bourdain's shows), she's being asked to cater a lot of different events.   I don't see her at the Freret Market so much anymore, but that could change. I'm sure she'll be at Jazz Fest again this year, if you're hunting for her. Her food is soulful and delicious...but not very veggie friendly or for those who are watching their salt intake.  She does have veggie yakamein at Jazz Fest usually and I love her mac-n-cheese. When she's done fried fish, that has been awesome too.  Seriously, Miss Linda is a good person and a great cook and deserves all her success.

I had a delicious veggie burger from Ms. Beasley; I didn't read the entire listing so I was surprised by the tasty hummus on the burger and the fresh salad. All so good.   I also grabbed a cup of soup for my Mom but I didn't have any. She gobbled it up so it must have been good.   What sets this food truck apart from the others (besides the healthy vegan selections) is the fabulous demeanor of the owner. She radiates joy and positivity. That gets a 5th star fsure!

5 years later and Tartine is still great. I had a family lunch here today and everyone loved their food.  Dad had the corned beef hash special and threatened to lick his plate he enjoyed it so much. The accompanying sour cream/horseradish sauce was super tasty. Mom enjoyed her pork rillette and my brother really liked his shrimp salad,especially the variety of vegetables. I can't get passed the eggs in brioche, so very delicious.  I also love their king cakes but I am happy to report there were none for sale 2 days early.  Still have a cute courtyard and it's order/pay at the counter. Friendly staff and good prices

I recently had a business dinner at Sofia with some out of town colleagues. They were super impressed, even though on of them is currently not doing dairy or carbs.   We started with garlic bread, the whipped ricotta and the brassica. All were delicious. And I was glad there was an app that everyone could enjoy. We had the cacio de pepe, the crab risotto and the gulf snapper for entrees. Everyone enjoyed their food and service was on point.  The drinks were tasty and one of my colleagues LOVED the house amaro. I had a lovely class of prosseco and the other was happy to be able to partake of local draft beer.   Will definitely be back.

Love this old school space in the back of the quarter (location of the original Angelo Brocato's until the late 70s). If the weather is good there's a lovely courtyard, or you can admire the decor inside the shop.  The pastries are delicious and there is quite a variety. It's a wonderful spot to cool down or warm up while wandering the FQ.   Service ranges from extremely friendly and helpful to curt but that's pretty much expected.  And this is another case of the disappearing review. Hmph.

Wow! I passed by this bar one weekend and thought what is that? And didn't notice a sign. The next weekend, I met friends here and realized the Domino out front IS the sign. Gotcha.  What a great happy hour! And what a fun and spacious bar. First the HH: It runs 7 days a week! from 3-6. Yes please. I know I enjoyed $5 cocktails, but I remember beer and wine specials. OMG I love the giant wrap around bar. So many places to sit and the vintage booths are amazing.   They have all sorts of events and popups happening too. Definitely a spot to cross town for!

Still 4 stars for me. If you need random hardwood floor care items or a 16 x 16 mini-sheet of drywall for a patch or a 1/2 gallon ball canning jar, this is your place.  You cannot walk more that 2 feet into the store without being greeted and/or offered assistance. LOVE the personal touch.  Latest purchases: black wire ties, goo for a slow sink, ice cube trays, and the elusive tropical fruit life savers.  And yep, this was part of my annual Magazine-Street-Black-Friday-Shopping-Extravaganza with my Mom.

For my 500th review, I solicited advice as to what should I review.  Couple of people asked if I had reviewed my city and I hadn't so here I am.  I know lots of folks think of New Orleans as a drunken wanton woman, but to me she's always been a slightly besotted grandmother...and you never know what she's going to do or say.  And I love her for it.  I love our history, the food, the culture, the architecture, and the trees.  I'm not so fond of the continued corruption, institutional ignorance and hereditary poverty, but hope springs eternal that we can overcome our issues.  My roots go deep in the city.  I'm 5th in New Orleans (longer if we include the ancestors who emigrated from France to the Northshore).  I joke (well pretend to joke) that I should start a history of my family tour of the city.  I can show you where my parents got engaged, where my grandparents went on their first date, where my great grandfather's cobblers shop was.  I know what my grandmother's house was like as a little girl at Camp & Jena and how scared she was to live through the influenza epidemic of 1917.  And, of course, I was born at Touro Infirmary.

This is one of the those New Orleans locations that has been a number of restaurants over the years.  I confused my cousins this morning by telling E that we were headed to Bright Star...which I think was its name about 1991.  Luckily, he usually knows what I'm talking about when I leap back in time.  This morning I had eggs sardou and it was pretty tasty.  One of my cousins had the 2-3-2 (maybe) and her pancakes were delish.  Yes the servers are a bit indifferent; I've always assumed they were a never ending stream of hungover college kids.  But really it's a diner, do you expect white glove service?  The food is good, plentiful and inexpensive...now if they were only open for dinner...

First time at a hibachi place. That's right. I've never been to here (at least not since it was a pizza place in the 80s); my niece was stunned too.   I did not have the sushi but other people at my table did and it looked delicious. My group had an assortment of dinners. At first I thought the price was a bit high, but then I saw how much food you got. Seriously I ate my "dinner" for 3 additional meals. My shrimp were perfectly cooked and my dinner companions enjoyed their steak, lobster, scallops and chicken. My only criticism would be that I found the fried rice a bit greasy.   There was a veggie dinner option but the soup that comes with has a seafood broth and, of course, your veggies will be cooked adjacent to meat and seafood.   I did enjoy the hibachi antics... the egg split on the spatula, the onion volcano, the flipping knives, and corny jokes. I did decline the offer to catch shrimp bits in my mouth. I'm way to spazzy for that.

I was stalking a particular product that Breaux Mart was carrying so after they were sold out at the Magazine location, I tried the River Ridge one. I had not been inside this store in a few years but wow! It looks great.  I remember being in this shop pretty regularly way back in the day and so my memory was that it was a little run down. But not anymore! And this has to be the largest of the Breaux locations. Recently I've been to the Magazine and Severn locations and this one is maybe 2x the size!  The staff was friendly and checkout and pricing were easy/good. Of course, they were also sold out of the specialty item I was looking for... but that's on me for taking too long to get to the store.  The prepared foods are really good as are the baked goods!

I have been wanting to try Tartine for some time but since it's only open for breakfast and lunch and is on the other side of town from work... you know how it goes.  I finally got to partake of their deliciousness a few Fridays ago.  The weird: We couldn't find the restaurant...the sign isn't huge and was partially hidden by trees. I felt like I was about to walk into someone's house. The security door wasn't tied open so the place looked closed so don't let that deter you.   The delicious:  As Charles H said, the baked eggs in brioche is ridiculously delicious. Like I'm typing this and I want to get in my car and drive across town and go get some good. My friend loved her Salmon Rillete and it was a HUGE amount of food.  The meh: You order at a counter and our counter person did not tell us to server our own coffee and tea, one of the other diners did that.  The menu is small. The decor inside is rundown grandma's house...which isn't necessarily a bad thing but doesn't really go with the food. I was expecting more of an upscale shabby chic vibe and this is more downhome than that.  The good: The food, the patio, the price.
OK I may be obsessed with soup, but I dream about the spinach crawfish zucchini bisque from here.  Good food and they have belly dancers on Saturday night.

My brother had asked if I'd been to this restaurant a couple of months ago since it's near my work because he had heard it was really good. So last week I finally went. There were no English menus that I saw but between my HS Spanish and google translate, I managed to order something super tasty.  I think you're supposed to order at the counter but we had sat down to figure out the menu and someone actually came to us. I ordered the fried shrimp plate (big surprise) and I had my choice of corn or flour tortillas. My dish had fried shrimp, salad, pico, pinto beans, rice and corn tortillas. It was delicious and too much food for me. My friend got the Honduran tacos and said they were tasty and he even took some food back with him. We both had agua fresca. I had blackberry and he had passionfruit and both were amazing and not overly sweet.  I will definitely back to try more items.

Wow! This location of the local grocery chain is huge! I sort of had some deja vu when I walked in because I'm pretty sure I bought snacks here when it was a previous grocery... a few decades ago.  There is a great selection of prepared food and a hot bar line. I just needed a few things and was able to find all the things. Plus a crab and mushroom quiche. Delicious  Service was good and it was a spotless store with ample parking.

Pandemic update I ordered lunch for me and Mom and a couple of friends on a recent Saturday. Ordering online was easy through DoorDash.  We ordered a lot! We had beef kebab pitas and chicken shawarma and hummus and baba ganoush and carrots and Israeli salad. The pita is poofier than some of the other places in town, but that's a regional difference. My Mom loved her beef kebab and the baba ganoush. The hummus was yummy and so were the carrots (spicy!) and the salad.  I picked up and you can choose to go inside (where the specials are listed so you have FOMO about what's not on the app) or there is a window on the side street to be even more distant.  Everything was delicious and the staff is great.

So I don't usually get gas here because it's pricey...but that's uptown where gas stations are scarce. It does have a mechanic and a car wash. And this location often lets various clubs use it's space for fund raiser car washes...or at least it used to. Maybe that's passe now...  Anyway, 4th star for the lady who issued my brake tag yesterday. She was courteous, funny, efficient and charming. You heard me charming. I had all my paperwork and my cash and I knew I would owe them extra money for being a couple of months later getting my tag.  Be prepared and it's a breeze! In and out in 10 minutes with waiting for the car ahead of me...

Like the other 2 Felipe's the food comes out fast and is really well priced. The food is solid with lots of fresh ingredients and everything customized to your liking.  Loved my aqua fresca and I did try to order a drink at the bar but couldn't squeeze in. I had a quesadilla with shrimp and it was delicious and I even had some the next day.  This location is a little more open than the uptown location which means that it's a little more confusing since you have more space to wander in.  I almost want to take a star off for the parking lot which I hate. HATE. Why can't you enter from St. Louis St? That's just dumb parking lot planners.  But I won't penalize Felipe's for parking stupidity.

Pandemic review: This spot has been my parents go to for Vietnamese food for awhile and I had never been... since I thought they were only open Monday-Friday. But they added Saturday awhile back and I never knew!  Mom and I needed a break last Saturday from doing chores around her house. So I ordered up our food and took a drive over for pick up. They do have tables outside so you can definitely dine there. Not sure about dining inside since no one was doing so. Pickup was easy and the staff is very nice and friendly. Everyone was masked!  The food was so good. I got a shrimp banh mi which I only ate half of because I also gobbled up several crab rangoons. Yummy. Mom had grilled pork and shrimp bun. And it was a huge amount of food. As I said this is her favorite. And she does love the pho here but it was just too hot on Saturday for that.  Parking lot out front and they offer delivery through Waitr too.

Pandemic review: So I found a chair at their main showroom on Veterans. But this location is the Scratch/Dent showroom plus the warehouse for the main showroom.  I arrived and went inside and paid for the item I had ordered on Saturday. I had the order number but I'm sure they could have looked it up by name too.    My brother pulled his van around back and the boxed chair was loaded up within 15 minutes; please note signs at the loading dock said it could take as long as an hour to pull items but I guess because it was Tuesday, it was much speedier.  Lots of hand sanitizer everywhere. Masks were required and they could give you a disposable if you didn't have one!  Chair was just what my parents needed and all and all a good experience.

I finally made it over to the Pelican Club for a Coolinary this year. And Yum! I'm sorry it's taken me so long to get there.  I enjoyed a glass of bubbles at the bar while I waited for my group, refreshing and well-priced. This restaurant has the longest coolinary restaurant menu this year I think. There even vegetarian selections! Unheard of in NOLA!   I started with the seafood ravigote so fresh and delish. Then I had the crab pasta which was ridiculously rich and was such a large portion that I ate the rest of it the next night. And finally I had the coconut creme pie which was perfect.   Service was good if a bit harried. They were slammed for Coolinary which was good to see.  Will definitely be back.   Note: if you are driving in, depending on your map app, it might tell you to drive down the alley to get to the restaurant. This is pedestrian only. Do not attempt.

So I mostly end up at this Walgreens late at night and that's why it's getting a review...a 24 hours shop on St. Charles....excellent location for people watching. Drunk tourists, random local nuts (waves), and folks who just want to chat with you at 2 in the morning while you are in urgent need of...whatever.  AND the staff handles all this with aplomb and amusement.  This location does have a huge makeup selection. And some good local stuff, including souvenirs and then there is the random things like sundresses or scrubs. Weird.  In summation, I think it's probably a 3 star store, but the people make it worthy of 4.

It's time for my annual Magazine-Street-Black-Friday-Shopping-Extravaganza with my Mom. And while I stop into Dirty Coast all the time, my Mom doesn't.  The staff was really patient with all of her questions. And even pulled the last Makin' Groceries shopping tote off the wall to sell to her.    Bonus for the 10% off Yelp checkin deal!

Oh, look another random bridge review.  If you're driving over this bridge, you may not realize it because it feels like an overpass. But on windy days this bridge is often closed due to high water from the lake and you hear it's name all the time on the traffic reports, especially as an alternative to other routes.  The bridge really isn't much to look at, but if you're the passenger, enjoy that view of the lake as you cross over. So beautiful.

Over 10 years later and this cafe is still great! I love love love their spinach-zucchini crawfish bisque. LOVE!  I've had a variety of items here over the years. The Mediterranean shrimp is a favorite (watch out it's very splattery) as is the couscous vegetarian. Family members rave about their lamb. And I've also had some delicious salads here.  Service is wonderful. The owner greets you like a long lost friend and welcomes you with open arms. Even though the restaurant is small, you are never rushed to finish so they can turn the table. If you're deep in conversation, you won't even get the bill until you ask.

Family dinner on a Sunday night! With visiting family in town, I get to go to all the restaurants. We started with the Mamere's crabmeat casserole. It was petite but rich! And a great starter for 4 out of the 5 of us... the 5th decided that he wanted his own pot for his entree. Very crabby!  I had the seafood salad and chose the large because I was hungry... well that salad is so full of crabmeat and shrimp that the small would have fed me so I had leftovers for lunch yesterday. Still delicious. And that green goddess dressing was strong in the best sort of way. No wimpy goddesses around here.   My family had the shrimp sandwich and the pompano (my mom's fave fish) and the oyster pasta. Everyone really enjoyed their food and our server was good. The only misstep was that my iced tea tasted like coffee. ARGH. Why do places not pay attention to this? I like my tea to taste like tea. It's so sad.  I'll definitely be back.

With parades cancelled, many of us have decided that the only response is to turn our houses into floats.   MG Spot (aka Plush Appeal) has beaucoup materials for making your house look MGtastic. I've ordered some petal paper and I'm waiting for that to come in. But I've also purchased a variety of very important items, like purple, green and gold fringe, PGG lights, and glass beads and MG decor. Y'know the essentials.   Staff was super sweet and helpful. And there several parking spots out front so that's easy. At the moment, the streets are all torn up so it's a little like off-roading to get to the them. But totally worth it.  Pandemic notes: they had hand sanitizer and wipes AND disposable masks by the front door. All staff was masked and of course, customers are required to wear masks too.

I was on #auntduty and wanted to liven up the front porch with some flowers for fall so decided to head to this garden center so they could admire the staff animals.   I found excellent selections of flowering plants and herbs, perfect for my porch design, and affordable. The nieces enjoyed talking to the garden cat and petting various bunny rabbits. I enjoyed watching the geese and some ducks having an argument (they were in a pen so no need to fear being chased by geese). And then as we were admiring their billy goats, one of them got hold of my shirt. Luckily I got him to release before he chomped a hole. Goats are ridiculous.  There is a small parking lot, but I often end up parking on the street...be careful getting out of your car because of the folks who use Tchop as a speedway.   Staff is always helpful and prices are good. Plus you get to make some animal friends.

It's been a little while since I used Audubon and I did have a few issues but as they put new gutters on my house in 2006, I will cut all of us some slack.  My gutters were damaged slightly in the Katrina mess; then the temporary roof repair guys damaged the more (both times); then the real roofers trashed them.  So new gutters.  While it was a bit of an ordeal to get any workers at the time, the guy who came out to install the gutters gave us the heads up about some serious sill damage near our roof line and we had that repaired (by another contractor as it was too large of a job for them to do) then they came back and installed the final bits.  Good selection of styles and colors and they were good communicators throughout the process.

Grand opening this morning! My neighbors alerted me to this jew spot. They were invited to the preview and were raving about all the food.  I buzzed in this morning and picked up a small chicken potpie, a chocolate strawberry hand pie and mini pecan pies.   The chicken was for mom and she raved about the crust and the flavor of the filling. The mini pecans were the perfect 2 bite snack and the hand pie was tart, rich and delicious.   Pandemic wise, masks are required. Contactless payment is possible. Staff is all masked and their is outside seating.  Can't wait to go back

My restored (in 2004) clawfoot tub needed some refurbishment. A small plumbing accident in it's 1st year of life with me resulted in a divot (always put a towel down before changing shower heads) which was repaired but fast forward 5 years and some renters and I'm not sure what happened. The small divot had become a crater with a crack running away from it. AND then there was rust stain at the drain where they allowed water to drip.  I hunted around Yelp and the internet and the BBB for a tub refinisher. And then I thought to call the general contractor who redid the bathroom in the other half of my double and she highly recommended Southern Refinishing.   I called them and booked an appointment two weeks later and I wasn't really sure...was the guy just coming out to look at it or what. He arrived said he could take care of the problem right then or come back but that the bathtub would be unusable for 48 hours. They were done in less than an hour and it looks amazing (see my pictures).   They were really professional and neat.   *warning* the smell is potent. So you might want to complete this sort of project when you do NOT need to sleep in the next room. I think this would be the case for any company used.

I hadn't been to the dermatologist in years. And it was definitely time for a quick mole check, can't be too careful with the skin cancer, people!  Dr. Hickham has been my dermatologist for over a decade but I hadn't ever been to the Metry location (the only location left post-K). The office was comfortable and there is an elevator up to the 3rd floor.   The staff was efficient and I was in and out in no time. As I've only ever gone for medical issues, I've never gotten a hard sell on the cosmeceutical items that they do (botox, etc) and I appreciate that.   Best of all? No skin cancer. Woo Hoo!

Today I bought, redfish filets (really fresh), some medium raw shrimp, crawfish pies and boil potatoes & corn.  The place smelled fabulous and was a zoo because of all the folks buying their good Friday boiled crawfish.  But the staff was great and hustling.  Even with the line I was in and out in 20 minutes.

Solid middle eastern food.  The menu is not too different from the various locations of Mona's.  They do somethings better than Mona's (notably some of the salads), but others not as well (I love the falafel at Mona's the best).  The atmosphere is good and the wait staff seems to be a bit ditzy.

Pandemic update I stopped in to pick up a desired tshirt for one of my brothers. And high marks to DC for keeping people safe in a small store.  Obviously the merch is great. Locally made and inspired gifts as well as the great tshirts/bags. Sometimes I know exactly what I want from the online shop stalking but others times I'm browsing, especially if you decide you need a candle. I mean... what exactly does that satsuma snoball candle smell like?  I got what I needed and rolled on out. Masks were required and shopping felt safe.

Pandemic update: Thank goodness for e-resources from the public library over the last eleventy-bajillion months of this pandemic. And I was super grateful that they actually added in curbside pickup. I thought I would update since it had been 11 years since I last reviewed this space.   One of the great things about this location being a former mansion (donated in 1948 to commemorate Milton Latter who was killed during WWII) is the porch. The porch allows for distanced pickup and drop off while the Library is only open via appointment.   The staff of all the public libraries in the city is doing a great job during the pandemic; this branch just happens to be mine.  For more information on the mansion: http://nopl.s3.amazonaws.com/files/LatterLibraryHistory_2016-10-03-21-05-10.pdf

Peaches was bro1's go to record store in the 1970s... when it was on Causeway Blvd near the mall (I think). Same logo as back in the day so I'm guess the same folks.   This location is a great use of the former Woolworth's on Magazine Street. It's a huge space so they have beaucoup crates of albums, tapes and CDs. PLUS they have all sort of novelty gifts, tshirts and whatnot... and I do mean whatnot. From silly trinkets for the youngsters to naughtier trinkets for your friends, they probably have gag gift of your dreams.  They also seemed to have some of the Bayou Shirts HowAhYa stock that is sold at Jazz Fest.   Super friendly staff. And I love that the old lunch counter is intact, even if it's just for show.

Imagine my surprise when I saw that my previous review of WWOZ (from 2009) was listed under a business that was CLOSED. Uh, yeah, not really. While the office space/broadcast location may have moved, you can still find the DJs spinning at 90.7 and on the web. As they have since the mid 70s.  Yes, my Dad's friend was an early DJ and Jiving Gene retired earlier this year. But those who are gone have been replaced with equally passionate (occasionally kooky) DJs who love their music. If you don't like the genre that's playing at the moment, wait a couple of hours until someone else comes up.  Currently, love the Sunday morning Gospel show and the late night Kitchen Sink shows and, of course, DJ Soul Sister on Saturday nights. And I'm always a fan of the drivetime Jazz shows.  Now if I could only find one of those vintage Wizard of OZ t-shirts, I would be a very happy camper.

I love the King Gator t and have bought it as a gift for others...I think it may be time for my own.  Yes, many of the designs are semi-inside jokes but you know you want to be one of the cool kids.  I have a "making groceries" tote bag, a festivals t, a Grand Isle t and I'm sure some others I can't come up with right now.

Friday night in the French Quarter and I was with a pack of 6 friends who were starving and it was after 8pm. Where to go that would take us in various casual attire and be tasty and affordable?   Thank goodness for Mr Ed's! I've eaten at various other locations around town, some that don't exist any longer but I'd never tried the FQ location. And I'm glad we went.   We had a variety of cocktails and wine. And my friends had everything fro a dozen raw to full entrees to apps (like me with my crawfish bread). Everything was tasty. The oysters all looked great. And my crawfish bread was not like what you get at Jazz Fest (or the type I made last month) but was more like a dip stuffed inside a small loaf. It was tasty though! I also really liked my old fashioned.  Great service, fun staff. And they could accommodate our big table immediately.

They've pretty much eliminated the home organization store and now just offer services. Everyone I know who has used them (to help pack & move, to plan storage solutions, etc) has been very happy.   I'm sad that they don't have the store anymore...although I did stop in at that location yesterday because they were having a HUGE estate sale (another service).

Pandemic update: All store employees are masked and some were even wearing face shields. There are markers on the floor asking folks to stand 6 feet apart while waiting on cashiers.  You do still have to use the keypad/pen to sign for your credit card and I didn't notice it being wiped down between customers.   The store is well stocked, except for the same cleaning items that are out everywhere. And the staff is still very helpful.  Great for a quick run in to get light bulbs, batteries, and a flash light for Mom.

This was my first time at my dermatologist's fancy new digs on Bienville. The space is gorgeous! And it definitely feels more like a spa then a doctor's office.   I'm mostly low key when it comes to my skin and I like that when I come to this office (off and on) for nearly 20 years, the conversation is strictly my concerns and there are no upsells. Each time I've gone it's for a worrisome spot or mole or whatever.  The office staff is very professional and helpful. And since it's a medical office, all COVID19 precautions were in place.

I did not call pop-a-lock directly but they must have a service contract with my Subaru roadside assistance. Sadly last week one of my tires lost it's life to a pothole on St. Charles Ave. St. Charles is supposed to be a fancy street free of sidewall busting divots, but no.  I called my roadside assistance and they said someone would be out in 40 minutes. About 20 minutes later, a car pulled up behind mine. After laughing (good humoredly) at my offer of the pathetic jack that comes with my car, he pulled out a hydraulic jack and my car up and my tire swapped in less than 10 minutes. Because this was part of my assistance package (paid for when I purchased my car), there was no charge but I signed some paperwork so they get credit for the job.  Easy peasy and I was glad I didn't need to change a tire in the rain, in my work clothes.

Cute CBD spot with brunch on the weekends BUT they also serve their regular menu too! So while one of us was craving their yummy benedict, I went tacos and another friend tried one of their salads.  Service was great and they do have some outdoor seating. But it was noon and  OMG hot so we sat inside. We split the ahi tuna app and it was delicious. I had the 2 tacos, 2 sides plate with  one fish taco, one shrimp taco, cucumber salad and grits. The fish was great but the shrimp was a little sweet for me. The salad was perfect but the grits were a little solid. My friends enjoyed their food. We opted out of drinking on this particular afternoon but the groups around us were enjoying mimosas (maybe bottomless).  Which brings me to my main complaint. It was LOUD. I know I've spent a year indoors but the volume was a problem for me. Maybe it was the area I was sitting in? Will definitely give them another shot.

I worked for a suburban WD in HS and maybe that's why I prefer not to shop at any of them.  But this store always seems dirty.  They have greatly expanded their natural food selection in response to the Whole Food a few blocks away.

I've always liked this triangle shaped building.I remember going to a delicious restaurant in the 80s but it's been a coffee shop for a long time. I stopped in to grab a quick hot beverage on a chilly day.   Service was quick and polite and my hot chocolate was tasty. Reliably good hot beverages and baked goods. Yay.   But where this location is just a little bit better is the locale. I would love to sit at the table in the nose and read a book and feel like I'm in the prow of a ship. Seating isn't too jammed and folks were chilling and talking on this chilly morning. There is outside seating which would be lovely on a non-rainy not-cold day.

It had been a few since I last came to this theater. So yesterday I payed $11.50 for a movie and tried to find a seat in the theater that was intact. I was in theater 10 and most of the seats were cracked and broken, some were missing backs. The last time I remembered being horrified by the condition of the ladies room....multiple broken/out of order toilets, broken tile, just felt dirty, so I waited until I got home rather than brave those again.   The staff was pleasant and as usual I didn't hit the snack bar. But I did notice the upgrade of the fancy coke machines and multiple flavors of icee. There is still a bar in the lobby as well.  The whole place from parking lot to lobby to theaters just seems shabby. Definitely time for a makeover.

Go buy Louisiana seafood right now.  I stopped by Big Fisherman on Thursday and the owner thanked me for coming in.  He said either folks are scared to eat the seafood or they assume there is none to be had.  I bought gorgeous, huge boiled crabs and tasty boiled crawfish from them.  As well as crawfish pies for a family party that night.  Great quality and prices are competitive. Bonus because you know what you are getting.

Not sure how stuff ends up here instead of at the Green Project next door. But they do have some interesting and BIG architectural pieces. The last time I was over they had a bunch of desks, some weird half finished art projects, some random cabinets, columns, arches, and some in need of repair neon.  Wander around and see if they have what you need.

If I was just rating drinks and service this would probably be 4 starts. Both were good. I think I've had dinner 2x and HH at the bar at least once.  But the food is just not all that. The shrimp boil is just odd ... pouring a buttery sauce over (2 few) boiled shrimp so that the fries underneath end up mush? The crab and avocado dip is too much of a mish-mash and had me searching for the crab. The green salad was fine. And my favorite item is the corn on the cob.   The space is gorgeous. And it's a wonderful renovation from the old leather furniture store. I just wish they'd step up their food game.

I will let you in on a secret about me...I am a librarian, so I love libraries.  Latter is an interesting building.  Because it was once a private home, it doesn't really make a great library.  The collection ends up very chopped up and it takes awhile to figure out where everything is.  That said it is a beautiful building.  The family who donated it lost their only child in one of the World Wars.  Which is a beautiful way to remember a lost son, but the city has NEVER had the money to keep the building up.  It has beautiful grounds around the building taking up almost a 1/2 city block.  Bonus points for the book sale that takes place out of the garage every Saturday.

Delachaise has good food (although don't expect a full meal if you're a big eater) and a great selection of wines by the glass.  They also have good selections of hard liquors...except last time I went, they couldn't find bottles for the first 2 bourbons I requested.  And Mr. Euro bartender was tres annoyed with me.  Whatever.  But they stay at 4 stars for becoming non-smoking last year.  Honestly I had stopped going after the time I came out smelling like I had rolled in an ashtray.

Pandemic update: I was able to order online. My food was waiting for me at the counter. And I did pay once I was in house.   Staff was all wearing masks; half the tables have been removed but they do allow in house dining. Delivery is available.   And I got to have the eggs sardou that I was craving. It is not the classical preparation of the dish but it hit the spot. And I'm also very glad that I ordered biscuits to enjoy the next day.
Great local business.  I am now the proud owner of the coffee & beignets shirt.  And I hear the Fess shirt will be making a comeback once a small issue with his heirs is straightened out.

I ran over to Harold's with a couple of neighbors because they were having a plant sale. While the stock was a little picked over because of the sale, what they had was great and well priced.  Loved all the fun planters that were available. Staff was friendly and knowledgeable. Parking was easy-peasy even with the crowd.
I like Hermes...the old school floats and the pretty floats.  There theme is always interesting and this year's plush winged H's were an inspired throw.  A good start to carnival weekend.

Yknow when you put off car maintenance for way too long and then the universe gives you a sign... And it has to be now! That was me with an oil change. And stopped by this Valvoline and there was a coupon via Yelp! So yay for 20% off.  Of course, there is the up-sell but I also knew I had been neglecting things so sure change the air filter while you're at it. What my transmission fluid is low according to your computer? Um, sir, I drive a standard.   Staff was very nice. The process was really efficient. And it was all good. They even warned me that I had picked up a nail in my tire which at that moment was still sealed tight.  Entry is around the corner on Polymnia and exit is on St Charles, FYI

This wasn't my first trip to the Tasting Room but it was my first time there in almost 2 years. We were asked for proof of vaccination (or a negative PCR test) as we entered and Tomas checked us in.   Of course, I forgot the whole gift exchange part but that was OK. Snacks and cheese were delicious and loved our passed fries. I was in the mood for sparkling which wasn't included with the event drinks so I just went off book and payed for my bevvie. The bartenders were lovely and the entire staff was helpful.   Plus there were unexpected Yelpies!!! My obsessive documentation of all the home improvement folks I've used over the years paid off!  Thanks to the Tasting Room and the staff and Tomas for steering us out of 2021 and hopefully into a better 2022!

I was a bit hesitant when I met a big group and this new hotspot since I knew they had a focus on the meats, but I was pleasantly surprised at the number of straight up vegetarian/vegan options, plus you know plenty for the meat eaters & the pescetarians.  My group gobbled down the wings like they were the last food on earth and then I watched as folks used spoons to scoop up the rest of the sauce...I'd say that was a solid endorsement. I sampled both the shrimp and tofu spring rolls (tofu spring rolls are not on the menu but they are happy to make them). The shrimp was fried which added a really nice texture to the standard spring roll and the sauce that they came with (made in house) was SOOO yummy.   For an entree I had the black bean braised crab bowl with rice. The black beans which I'm guessing were the fermented variety had a strong flavor that almost overtopped the crab but not quite. It really was a delicate balance. The fried okra that was an accent to the dish was hit or miss; some bits were a tad overcooked.  I snitched a bit of my neighbors fried tofu and cauliflower rice bowl and it was AMAZING.   Others at the table ordered the pho which comes in a variety of broths with your choice of proteins. Everyone was raving about the broths, the meats, and the fancy soy sauce.   No desserts for our group and no cocktail for me this time. The boba teas with alcohol seemed a popular choice with the group and the cocktail list looked inventive.  Our server handled our large group (13) with ease and it was a lovely night to sit on the back deck (at picnic tables). There is parking in front of the restaurant and in the back (where you enter through the deck/backdoor). There are warnings everywhere that the Burger King will have you towed if you park in their lot, so be warned.  Will definitely be heading back soon.

Love the uptown location...which was a gym and a laundromat previously.  The space is light and airy and the food is fresh and delicious.  We had the green breakfast sandwich on a croissant, scrambled egg, cheese, arugula, avocado and tomato. Yum! And the roasted pear and brie melt on sourdough. Double Yum! As an appetizer, we had a ginger muffin and also a great watermelon lemonade and some strong ice tea.  Definitely will be back soon.  Order at the counter and receive a local musician tag to place at your table. Food and fancy juices will be delivered.

I'm not sure what the other reviewers had, but I ate dinner at this sushi joint on Friday night with a friend after it was highly recommended to us.  The service was on point with our server checking back if we needed drink refills and checking to make sure we enjoyed our food. The design of the restaurant is cozy and they must have some good sound blocking panels (or something) because we barely heard the child having a meltdown until he passed our table as his Dad hauled him outside for some quiet time/whatever.  I had a sake cosmo which was tasty but maybe at touch too sweet for me. We ordered WAY too much food with both rolls and sushi and some edamame and salads. Anita's favorite roll was the Sunset (which we got without the jalapenos); it was spicy and an good blend of flavors. I think the Sweetheart roll was my favorite. My cucumber salad was HUGE and could have been split between 2 people. The hamachi sushi was good quality and perfectly sliced. Anita got her standard salmon roe sushi and enjoyed it. And of course, we got a vegetable roll as a palate cleanser; it was pretty standard.  I enjoyed the food and the service here and would definitely go back.

Pandemic update:  Another year (or 2) and another brake tag/inspection sticker... now with social distancing!  I actually remembered to get my new tag on time (because I put a reminder in my online calendar 2 years ago) so that's a win. And this Shell station was doing inspections again. (I think they only stopped for a couple of months in the spring.) So I drove over on a weekday (key) when it wasn't raining (also key) and waited behind one other car.   We (my car and I) did the song and dance of hit the horn, turn on the wipers, left turn, right turn (signals) and reverse! and we got the choreography mostly correct. I really need to listen better.  I was masked the inspector was masked. Cash was handed over. New inspection sticker. Done!

Plus 1 star for having Murphy's on draft...right, I don't drink beer but it's E's favorite.  I've had the deep fried mushrooms (bar menu), a crab & tomato salad (dinner menu), the mussel tomato soup & ploughman's panini minus the bacon (lunch menu).  The food was all OK to good.  My lunch companion LOVED the Sheperd's Pie (wish they made a vegetarian version).  I feel like the servers are still working out their flow...but it's only been open a month or so.  At one point at lunch, there was not a single server or bartender on the floor.  I definitely saw the kitchen staff walking the floor getting feedback from diners, so I know they are working towards improvement.  I will say the dinner menu is much fancier/expensive then you would assume from the environment.

Pandemic update I was in the FQ recently and realized I was starving and after verifying that this shop was open, I wandered on over.  And I was the only person in the shop when I stopped in. I ordered a mini quiche, an orangina and splurged on some macarons. My quiche was perfect and the macarons were good. And who doesn't love an orangina. They are requiring masks and asking patrons to distance.   The case wasn't as full as it normally is; reflecting fewer patrons going in I guess. Staff was great as always.   Gorgeous spot with good pastries

Pandemic update Momma wanted to bake a whole fish for our very small Christmas dinner. Most people do not want a whole fish so I was supposed to order one. Guess who forgot? So I showed up at Big Fisherman first thing in the morning on Christmas Eve. Alleluia!  They had beautiful whole speckled trout and even cleaned them for me to Mom's specifications. They were hopping with folks picking up previously ordered crates of oysters and shrimp and what not.  I really appreciated them getting me out of a bind of my own creation.  Staff was all masked. Social distancing was good. Dinner was saved!

First off a breakfast/brunch spot that takes reservations! AND it opens at 7am for the early birds and stays open until 3 for the folks who can't make it out of bed or their house before noon.  We had a variety of dishes. I had the avocado toast and added an egg. OMG so tasty with toasted sunflower seeds and some orange oil, it was so bright and perfect. And my friends and I shared the bubble waffle which was perfect and delightful and may have put me in a carb coma... or maybe that was the side of biscuit and jam that I had to have. My biscuit was delicious and the strawberry jam was yummy.  I was really happy to see a bunch of vegetarian/vegan (?) options on the menu. I think this has been really missing from many of the local breakfast places.   We just had hot tea and coffee since we all had to actually be functional later in the day but the bar menu looked good and others were definitely enjoying the bottomless mimosas as we left.   Pandemic notes: they have outdoor seating under an a tent and everyone was well masked. There was OK distance between tables.

This was one of the restaurants that my Nashville friend wanted to share with me and we were in the neighborhood and they were open for lunch (a once a year occurrence thanks to Vandy's graduation). So yumminess ensued.  We started with a delicious cheese plate and they had interesting items to choose from.  And we had garlic, parmesan baked oysters (think charbroiled) and the oysters were from Louisiana...so my Nashville located but NOLA born friends were super excited.   Oh and we started our meals with a basil fashion (add basil bitters & a basil leaf to a standard old fashioned) and a perfect bellini. My only criticism was that my drink was a bit too sweet.  I would have preferred a heavier hand with the bitters, but that's just personal preference.   Then we had fish tacos, substituting pickled veg for the fries, and shrimp enchiladas and a fire roasted beet salad. All three dishes were very good.   Service was on point and very friendly.  We were well taken care of without being interrupted.  We ate in a bar booth but it felt really cosy and not like an afterthought.  The space is really attractive and I'm pretty sure is a repurposed vintage car dealership.

Fun new addition to Magazine street. I had the fried cheese pies which were delicious and too rich for me to eat both at one sitting. So I'm glad I had an order of the hummus with mushrooms to split with a friend. AND OMG that pita was amazing so fluffy (please read that like Agnes from Despicable Me). The hummus was good and for $11 it was a huge portion.  The place was noisy (lots of kids that night) and the free pickles and what not ended up being blocked by the people in line ordering. Will definitely be hitting them up for take out soon. I have to try the falafels!  Side note, you can order online (love) and they have "broccoli trees" on the menu which is what we called them as kids (2x love).

No one likes blood work but this spot is quick and makes the bloodletting relatively painless.  I showed up. Handed them the orders from my doctor's office. Waited, maybe 2 minutes and that was it.   The person drawing blood was friendly and did a good job of distraction while she found a vein with her sharp. Then a couple of vials later, done.  Only thing else I could really ask for was a lollipop because I didn't cry.

This is a great green space in the Marigny. It has play equipment for kids and benches for chilling out. The various people who seem to hangout in the park full-time will try to bum cigarettes, cash, whatever, but aren't too pushy. And it is dog friendly.  It can be annoying that the many, many gates into this park are locked and it seems arbitrary which ones are chained and which ones are open.   It's great that the park is just big enough to be the kickoff locale of various marches...most recently the Women's March.

I was last here for a private event and the space is lovely as always and the layout was perfect for the memorial service that I was attending.  The staff was great and the food was very good (although perhaps servers should actually know what they are passing). The space though...the space is so gorgeous with a beautiful porch and giant windows so you can appreciate the lovely oak trees and surrounding park.  Another bonus is that despite all the exercisers on a random weeknight, there is reserved parking for the clubhouse.

I really can't change my rating.  I love the setting so I always hope the food will be better.  I think they ran out of caesar dressing so made up for it by covering my greens in cheese.  Plus they were out of all but the boring beers.  Running out of Abita almost dropped them to 2 starts, but it was such a lovely night to sit outside...

Good tapas & a nice lunch menu.  Some inventive dishes & some that sound better on paper than they actually taste.  Love the corn item and the tuna was great.  The avocado/mushroom thing which I was really excited about was sort "meh."  Definitely worth a visit.

Wandered in with my Mom for a quick lunch on a pretty day a few months ago. Points for the (often full) on site parking lot. It is tight if you drive a big vehicle.   Yes, this is a national chain but it tries to incorporate local flair. Lovely outdoor area which is where we ate. My Mom got the club and declared it tasty. I got the veggie burger which was less successful. A bit too mushy in preparation for me. Service was a bit spotty for us but the locale made up for that.  Fine for dining outside on a pretty day if you're in the area.

Fun neighborhood joint with a varieties of tacos and good drink specials. The servers seem to be mostly neighborhood kids, so y'know they're easily distracted.  Loved the tots, my cocktails and my tacos (portabella and fish).  Great mid-afternoon meal.

So let's talk about the crabmeat au gratin.  Seriously, I love it's artery clogging deliciousness. My favorite version used to be a long closed restaurant on the lakefront. Not any more, this is now the platonic version by which all other versions shall be judged.  Y'know brother 4 warned me how good this place was (he gets to fancypants lunch on a work tab sometimes) and he was so right.  Don't tell him I said that, OK?  The decor is basic and the service is old school New Orleans, courteous, knowledgeable without putting on fancy airs.  I know I ate lots of other foods here which were all tasty, but honestly, when you find the platonic version of crabmeat au gratin in kind of eclipses all else.  And, oh, look, it's my 800th review.

Yang's is a solid neighborhood poboy shop.  I had a grilled shrimp poboy which was tasty and fresh.  The bread was very good and the shrimp were flavorful and well cooked.  I got it dressed and the lettuce, tomato, pickles, condiments were really well balanced.  What kicks them up to 4 stars for me, was the counter service was very friendly and helpful.  Plus they had really excellent fresh brewed unsweet tea.  I hate tea from the soft drink vending machine.

Good addition to a busy area of Harahan and a good choice for a family dinner.   I went over the first time just before Christmas with my parents and an assortment of nieces. Our server was great and the kids found things they enjoyed. The fried items were tasty and the portion sizes were good. There were a couple of bobbles...my Dad's meal came out a good 10 to 15 minutes after everyone else's but there were several very large tables that night so benefit of the doubt. The pre-teen niece gobbled up my side of creamed spinach, too velveeta-y for me, but she loved it. I LOVE their mashed potatoes.  Went again in early February with a couple of visiting family members. My cousin had the tomato cheese grits and YUM! We also had a 1/2 dozen charbroiled; very good oysters just wish they were a teeny big garlickier.   Their specialty cocktails are on the sweeter side but they do have about 10 wines by the glass plus an assortment of beers. Hopefully I'll be able to try a drink next time I'm there.   The staff is great. The space is made up nice, for a stripmall. There is a parking lot out front, although it gets pretty jammed up.

I was surprised to see that Diva Dawg didn't have a listing. They've been serving breakfast and lunch near my work for a couple of months. They make all their own sausages for their dogs, including the veggie dog with veggie chili that I tried today. My coworker got the red bean dog with fried chicken nuggets on top! That seems to be their signature item. The veggie dog was really tasty (with a red bean base); I advise adding creole mustard for some zing.  Love that they accept text message orders if you're short on time. Super friendly staff and quick turnaround.  Follow them on Instagram, FB or twitter to find them around the city.

Hitup WINO this weekend with an expiring Fetch Puppy deal.  So yay for having a limit.  Boo for having the wine vending machine feeling the Halloween vibe and fritzing out a bunch.  One of the machines finally went kaput BEFORE I could taste the Pink Floyd. Who doesn't want to taste a rose with that name?  We had 2! lovely cheese plates and then all the exhausted working people toddled off to bed with tummies & heads full of wine, cheese & baguette.  Perfect lowkey night.

Ummm...they advertise vegetarian dishes, but most of their Vietnamese items with tofu have chicken broth or pork... exception is the tofu appetizer.  Stick with the Thai specialties if you want to avoid the meat stuffs.    They do have 3 sizes of pho bowls so if you're feeling extra starving (or want to feed a family) get the large.

Pygmalion is a relatively new krewe (founded 2000). I like that it's co-ed and the folks did seem to be having a good time this year.  They had some decent bands this year. And, of course, the weather was gorgeous...which means that they either have weather control or are very lucky.  A fun way to kick off parade season.

King Arthur is a solid parade with a much older ridership it seemed. So don't expect too many folks to be able to throw to the back. The floats were fun (but are rented so you'll see them several more times) and the riders were enthusiastic.  The bands were trying on this rainy rainy day.   Minus points for their preponderance of blue beads bleeding blue all over my hands, my clothes, my house. I know the theme was King Arthur has the Blues, but did you have to give it to the rest of us?  And Danon, KA was never a Metairie parade...it used to be on the Westbank.

The Jean Lafitte National Park is divided up into 6 parts all over south Louisiana.  This the part that's in the FQ.  They offer walking tours and great information on the FQ and even have their Jr. Ranger program if you have kids.  They don't offer as many walking tours as they once did after the local for profit tour groups complained.  Well worth a stop...and not just because my uncle plays as a park ranger as his retirement job.

When Shercole suggested this place, I was intrigued. One of my family names is Munch and some of them do still live in Gentilly...of course, I think this place is more about the verb than the family name.  I enjoyed that the menu was a bit more varied than standard fried seafood. I loved the tuna tacos and the fish was really fresh and yummy. My shrimp boat was OK; the shrimp were delicious and perfectly cooked but there was too much bread and it was kind of hard so difficult to eat.    Our server was attentive and refills on ice tea and water happened quickly, which is a big deal considering they were slammed the night I was there.  My only complaint was that the restaurant needs a better exhaust system. I ended up smelling like fried seafood after I left.

So this place wasn't my favorite. While cigarette smoke isn't my favorite, I usually can ignore it. Maybe not so much in a place that says "Smoking Welcome." So there's that.  But really I think the vibe just wasn't doing it for me. Can we pick somewhere else next time?

When my plane finally arrived in NOLA after several delays, I was starving so I stopped in here for a quick brinner (breakfast for dinner). The menu is limited but covers the basics.   Nothing was great but it was solid and cheap. The space was clean but slow. This isn't someplace I'd go out of my way to find but it's a solid choice for the basics.

I know I've said it before...I used to love Nirvana but it's just so uneven these days.  After a long day of home improvements, we just wanted a simple meal and to crash.  We ordered a pakora and chat papri and both were fine.  But the saag paneer we ordered to share was borderline inedible.  And, of course, it made both us sick, so no sleep for us.  It will be a while before I give Nirvana another try.

I do love food trucks and I'm only sad that TLNOLA is not often where I am.  They do offer some delicious food. And the worker bees are always friendly, fast and helpful.  I just wish that they had more inventive non-meat selections.  Although when they have their fruit drinks (usually at day events) those are amazing.  Veggie choices on Saturday night were a sauteed swiss chard which they gladly gave me a sample of...it was tasty but not what I was wanting. So I went with the standard rice & beans.

This is a lovely an intimate wine bar...but don't worry, it carries the hard stuff too.  It's hard to classify this as a hotel bar since that engenders ideas of sterility and disillusionment.    The staff was efficient and pleasant even on a packed Halloween weekend night. The crowd here skews a bit older as befits the locale and the pricing. But really, you come here to escape the screaming around the corner, right?  My only criticism is that this place is in the French Quarter where I am not often these days. I wish it were closer to my house.

John reviewing Sun Ray made me realize that I didn't have a review...although I'm convinced I wrote one.  Oh well, Yelp! gets hungry on occasion.  This is a great place to go with a group who cannot agree on food style or genre. It has a very diverse menu which means something on it will come out mediocre.  But they usually do prepare most dishes well.  I know we ended up here on Father's Day in 2008 after our first choice was shut down by flooding...it was a crazy day.  My Dad really liked both his martini and the duck.  And I think I fought with one of my brothers over appetizers...but I can't remember any other details since my brothers & I fight over food fairly often.  But here's my BIG addendum to John's review.  Yes, there is a parking lot.  But for goodness sake, DO NOT TRY TO USE IT @ NIGHT.  It has no lights and is not safe.  I was headed over to Sun Ray one evening with friends and turned into the lot and...I'm still not certain what I saw going on in the back corner, maybe solicitation, maybe a drug deal, but whatever it was it was supremely sketchy and made me slam into reverse &  buzz out of the parking lot pretty darn quick.  When I mentioned it to the staff at the restaurant, their response was that they wished the parking lot had lights.  Yipes.

Up until now I had never had a disappointment at Dante's; it has always been one of my favorites.  I don't know if it was the early spring menu or that I went on a Monday night...or that the Monday night was the day after the Saints won the Superbowl (WhoDat!) but my meal was weak.    First problem was that two of the items I wanted to order had hidden pork in them that was either not specified on the menu or couldn't be altered for it to be removed.  (Really pork sausage in a fish stew? Is that really necessary?)  I had the scallops with grapefruit and radish sprouts and they were delicious.  As all the other small plates weren't of interest to me, I went ahead and ordered the seared fish (which seems to be halibut at the moment but was a gulf fish when I was there - as a side HALIBUT? in New Orleans, also disappointing).  I thought the dish was only OK and ended up giving my leftovers to my brother a few nights later.  I will definitely wait for the menu to change before going back and I hope that Dante redeems itself.

If you need to find some 80s black leather & chrome furniture, check here first.  And I mean that as a good thing, not that I'm in need of an 80s flashback.    Much of the used furniture here is on consignment, so you never know what you're going to find.  Each price tag has a date; if the item has been in the store for over 30 days, the price is lowered; if it's 60 days then lowered again.  Sorry I can't remember the actual percentages.    I bought a 1940s slipper chair for $25 from them several years ago...and then spent another couple of hundred on new fabric & reupholstering, but I love it. And you certainly can't buy anything new with it's style.  (PLUS it had Spanish moss in the arms as part of the cushioning.  How cool is that?)  You sort of have to walk in with an open mind and see what they have.  Couple of weeks ago, I was seriously tempted by Lucite chairs.

I was early for a book club meeting out in the metrys and stopped in for a cuppa and hopefully a slice of king cake.  The hot teas is mighty leaf brand. And it was fine. Y'know a basic cup of tea.  The king cake by the slice was from one of the Randazzo's...I'm not sure which one. But here's my pet peeve, if you're going to serve king cake by the slice make sure all slices are near the same width. Don't make me ask for the healthier slice when you try to give a scrawny one and they're both the same price.  The staff was courteous and quick and the location was pretty clean and had lots of tables with wall outlets.  I'm sure the regulars love the drive through option.

Hermes Bar is the newly created bar (from the old Hermes dining room) at Antoine's Restaurant, est.1840.  I think it's a long overdue move for this old line establishment to create a space for drinkers right off the street.    The bar is fancy looking, but welcoming and there are a many pub style tables as well as the bar itself.  The night I was there (with a dozen of my friends and friends of friends), fire was roaring in the fireplace (can't believe it actually functions!) which was very welcome on a chilly and damp NOLA night.  The drinks were well made (with 1 exception) and I was pleased to see you can order ANYTHING from the regular menu at the bar.  So some of my friends ordered cherries jubilee and we got to see the entire flaming dessert routine from our pub tables.  Fun!  The only issue of the evening seemed to be one server who had difficulty keeping the assortment of tabs open (we had at least 6 running from our group), but a more experienced person stepped in and the bills all worked out.  Definitely a great way to sample the traditional Antoine's fare without committing to the full meal.

I had Bar Tonique in my bookmarks to try for over a year. And I finally get there and they can't make any custom soda because their machine is broken. I did have a lovely old fashioned but the staff seemed over stressed and cranky. Maybe that was the broken machine?  I would definitely give this bar another shot on a less crowded & smokey evening.

Oohh lala. I know Bourbon gets all the press, but honestly Royal Street is the best window shopping/gallery hopping street in NOLA. First off it's pedestrian only during the day so you don't have to be worried about getting run over which is nice.*  Galleries feature art for every taste and just about every price point. There are clothing shops, accessory shops, antiques, housewares, restaurants, bars (of course), hotels and homes. The architecture is great. And on a hot summer day, there's usually enough shade that you won't melt into the sidewalk.  Definitely plan to stroll the 13 blocks of Royal in the FQ from Canal to Esplanade. Each one offers something different from tourist kitsch to fine art to a refreshing beverage.   *Side note to all the tourists in NOLA: the French Quarter is a functioning neighborhood. People drive in it. Please look before wandering out into the street.

This is not our preferred Home Depot (those would be the big one on Clio and the one out in Elmwood) but this one had the boxes of floor tiles we needed for our home renovation. Yay!    Really it's just a basic Home Depot although perhaps smaller than some other stores.  Nothing too exciting.

This was one of my FiL's favorite restaurants and every special occasion merited a trip.  Clancy's really is a five star restaurant, but a recent visit merited only 4 stars.  Why?  Because we were placed in an upstairs dining room that smelled like fresh paint.  Enough with the bad...  The good:  E & I split the crab salad and honestly, with that & bread I could have been done.  E got the special of the day, a beautiful piece of redfish (a bit on the small side) with crabmeat & capers. The sauce was delish.  I had the pineapple scallops which were good but the fritters (maybe plaintains?) mostly tasted like starch & fried.  The peppermint ice cream & lemon ice box pie remain classic desserts.  Really a lovely meal...except for that nagging paint smell.

This is a super convenient gas station in an area where they are scarce. The prices can be high, but considering the location...  There are 4 double sided pumps so not a huge station. The store is miniscule and I've never used it.   I like the new low fences so it's clearer where to drive in an out on Magazine & Jackson. The station is well lit and really busy so I feel pretty safe.

Honestly it's the only game in town, so the airport could totally suck and I'd still use it...at least until that private jet magically appears and then I could use the Lakefront airport.    Most of the concourses have been renovated (except for A; it's terrible). The food selection is often local companies rather than national so that's a +1.  Wifi is free!  Staff & security is on a continuum from friendly to surly just like most businesses.  So about average I think, plus local companies and free wifi make it a solid 4.

So I was STARVING and I was in the neighborhood and thought, when was the last time I ate at this Chinese restaurant? Maybe the 80s? So I took the chance and ordered *all the takeout*  I ordered moo shu vegetables, shrimp green beans and shrimp toast. And unlike my last disappointing take out adventure, everything was very tasty. The shrimp toast was fluffy and shrimpy. The moo shu came with the sauces and the yummy crepes. And the shrimp and green beans were delicious, easily the best dish.  I ordered at the front desk and my food came out quickly. Definitely need to remember to put them in rotation.

Once upon a time, this was Farhad Grotto (which I think has something to do with the Masons) and the location of the scariest haunted house that I ever attended. Seriously I freaked out and attacked one of the "monsters" and then dragged my brother out of the room.  Yes, I was 10, but this is why I don't go to haunted houses.  Anyway, before it was Southport, before it was the Grotto, it was an old gambling hall because it's just over the Jefferson parish line from Orleans parish where it was illegal.  So consider the history when you next go see a band or go drinking there.  The venue is good for music and the space is wide open with high ceilings.  I've never spent much time at the bar, so I can't really comment on that.  Minus 1 star because I contacted them about renting out the venue last summer and never heard a response.  If you really want to use them, I suggest going in person or calling (and pursuing them).

How did I miss writing a review of Muses in my post Mardi Gras frenzy?    Muses has great female centric floats and AMAZING throws.  I actually used my lightup "diamond" ring as a flashlight for the rest of the weekend.  The hand decorated shoes are the catch to get; right up there with the Zulu coconut.  The organization is INSANELY popular with a long waiting list of women who want to ride.  But you can still join the fun as a non-riding member.

A decent coffee/tea establishment in a convenient location.  The barista seemed a little confused by my friends iced cafe au lait order, but eventually they worked it out.  The wifi must work well judging by all the folks working there.

Loved the selection and that I was asked if I needed help and then left alone. The tag line is accurate in that there were unusual bottles here, that I haven't seen elsewhere. It is a small store but well stocked.  My only problem is with the parking lot. I feel like the pinkberry people want me to run them over and that if I left my car here while I picked up the one thing I needed from another store, I would get towed.

I'm not a coffee drinker and I have to admit that I don't really hangout in coffee shops but this place good change that. First off it's super deep so don't let that narrow storefront trick you. Second the staff is really nice. Third is has yummy iced tea and pastries.  Plus y'know board games and lots of areas to hang out and visit or y'know study if that's your sort of thing. I have to admit that when I walked in I almost had a Borsodi's flashback with the bohemian vibe...although a bit more grownup. (I realize this only makes sense if you were hanging out on Freret street in the 80s but so be it.)  Now that's it's cold I'll have to go check out their hot chocolate game.

I'm going to agree with Eileen that Cool Zoo is pretty cool.  We went on Good Friday and oh my goodness, was the zoo packed. But the out of town niece & nephew LOVED it.  There are lots of zoo staffers trying to keep a reign on the chaos and making sure the big kids don't plow over the little ones.  There seemed to be an area in back that was more sedate for little ones.  And many of the adults jumped in on the action.  I know my niece (who is 17 & works at the zoo) has gone to the cool zoo with her friends & siblings (all teens) so it's not just for kids.  I agree that you will get dampish just by sitting on the perimeter.

Formerly known as the Krewe of Boo (which I think is a much better name) this parade is generally the Saturday night before Halloween.  It has only been around since 2007 and is corporate sponsored...which may be the biggest problem I have with this parade.  I HATE seeing advertisements on floats.  I know that's normal everywhere else, but for Mardi Gras it's against the law.  The parade has had it's ups & downs in its 4 years of existence.  The 2010 parade was a bit...sparse.  But other years it's been really great, I guess it all depends on the economy.  Plus I love that Chris Owens sponsors a float.

Hmmm...this is tough. The staff was awesome. The bar was pleasant. I did not sample any food, but my ginger based cocktail was lovely.   So why 3 stars? The bathrooms. The restaurant/bar bathroom is shared by the pool facility. There was a mid-day party when I was there and the very drunk girls were wandering in and out barefoot (shudder) and so the bathroom floors were filthy and dangerlously wet.  If I was eating lunch while at work...I would not want to use them.  Is that a dealbreaker for me? Probably not and I'll give it another try and maybe this time use the pool...but probably not the workout room because y'know I'm lazy.

Cute new tshirt shop! Loved the old school vibe of their designs. The shop just opened in the last couple of weeks and is still getting established but it's fully stocked with shirts for men & women and babies. They also had screen print art and flags.  The themes are Louisiana specific with some NOLA stuff but they are Lafayette based so they definitely have a different perspective.  They share the space with another Lafayette based company, Red Arrow Workshop and there are 2 staff members and 2 cash registers.  The stock in both is interesting and the staff were friendly. I'll definitely be back.

My original review for Haydel's was the 2nd one I ever wrote. So 5 years later time to revisit.  The location is not the most welcoming with a solid brick building and only a glass door to peer through. (All the parking is behind and on the side of the store by the way.) But once you're inside, you're breathing in the beauty that is sugar and dough.  They make beautiful cakes (OMG try the doberge) here and have assorted other pastries (my Mom is a big fan of their Russian cake slices). But c'mon you know you're here for the King Cake.   Their cakes are deliciously consistent and the plain is anything but. I prefer the unfilled cakes because I feel the fillings are overkill but go crazy and do what makes you happy. I love that the baby is inside the cake when you get it...as it should be! And the porcelain collectables are a really cute lagniappe.  PLUS Haydel's is the place to ship a cake from. They do huge volume and the cakes arrive on-time and delicious.    Bonus for the Uptown folks, they have a popup at SnoWizard on Magazine for King Cake season in case the trek along Claiborne to Jeff Hwy is just too much for you.

Since I last went to Atchafalaya (October 2008) it has changed owners again. I swear I must have eaten at this location with substantively different menus and owners around a dozen times over the years.  I had been hearing good things about their food so took a chance on Saturday night.  We made reservations through open table, super easy-peasy.  And were seated promptly.  There were 7 of us so I can't remember what everyone ordered, but the food was universally enjoyed, as were the specialty cocktails.  Really appreciated the mix of small and large plates and though the saffron cream sauce was amazing.  Will go back again soon.

Massey's makes me wish I was more outdoorsy so I could justify spending money on all the supercool stuff they have in their store.    They carry clothes, gear, footwear, bags, camping/fishing/biking/you name it.  I may have to remember them next year for a Jazz Fest appropriate sundress.  Or when I need to replace my messenger bag.    It's a fave place to shop for my man (shoes).

This pretty random but my book group ended up meeting here. We were at Petroiska down the street and they cranked the music up too loud to chat. So we wandered in here.  Nice pour on my bourbon and they had a number of local beers so points for that.  I didn't have any food, but noticed that the kitchen was open.    I guess my only qualm with this joint is that it seems so corporate. Maybe my opinion will change if I go back for food.

One has been on my list of places to try for at least 3 years and I finally made it over there a couple of weeks ago.  We sat at the bar (in front of the open kitchen) so we had the food prep floorshow; it was like a live action food show.  The food was amazing. We started with the char-grilled oysters while we perused the menu...they were amazing. So glad I had bread to mop up the extra cheese & sauce.  I moved on to the butternut squash bisque with crabmeat and it was really yummy. THEN we split the roasted beet and celery root salad also delicious (and really I could have stopped). I also had the crab cakes with the mirliton fries. Both were amazing (and the leftovers complemented my scrambled eggs perfectly the next day).   Seriously delicious and I wonder why it took me so long to get here. I'll be back soon.

Taking a cruise on a paddlewheeler was part of my childhood field trips (and early concert experiences - RIP Riverboat President).  And it's a great way to relax and see the river.    Step back in time and take ride.  I've not eaten on this boat so I can't really comment on that.

My current favorite restaurant!  Emphasizes "localvore" items.  Delicious specialty cocktails, as well as a changing seasonal menu.  Plus the attire is casual so you don't have to wear your fancy clothes...that won't fit at the end of your yummy meal.

I'm sad to say that I think they're quality has declined. I've been to this location over the years and I'm afraid the attention to quality and detail is not there any more.  It's still an OK choice if you want rolls (and everything I ordered on my last visit was cooked...for the invalid I was delivering to/eating with). The snowcrab tasted mostly like mayo. the crunchy roll was blah. The veggie rolls were good though.  Bonus points for the staff at the bar who was very sweet to my niece while we waited for our takeout.
