It's the post office. This is a small branch with usually only 2 clerks (at most) working, but the line actually moves pretty quickly.  So it's never too awful.    I used to have to stop here all the time to pick up packages; my postal carrier never left them.  My current carrier just throws them over the fence and I find them sitting on my steps...in the rain.  Oh well, at least my dog has never gotten pepper sprayed.

Another of those places that I couldn't believe I hadn't reviewed. And then I considered how long it had been since I stepped inside....  Old school Sicilian-seafood restaurant which was a staple of my childhood in New Orleans. The menu has beaucoup fried seafood and many Italian staples.   I do have to ask why do I torture myself by ordering salads in places like this. But they were offering a roasted beet salad as a special. It was fine...just no special.  Although I bet the Caesar is solid and you can get it with or without anchovies. I also had fettuccine Alfredo, all garlic and delicious cheese. I had actually ordered a side but ended up with a full serving. I ate that fettuccine for 2 more meals! And we did start with onion rings which were perfectly fried. The group I was with ordered a variety of items from fried oysters to the eggplant to porkchops and pasta.   Solid old school NOLA place.

haha! Marielle scooping me on the FTR when I just created this listing tonight.  Vicky and I were cruising lakefront this evening and I almost wrecked my car when I saw that the fountain was lit up. Tonight was only the third night with lights. The grand opening won't happen until all the krewe tiles are restored and the landscaping is finished.   It's going to be phenomenal

Y'know most of the krewes that roll first weekend of carnival are fine.  Nothing spectacular but a good appetizer to get you in shape for the following week.  King Arthur follows that rule.  The parade was fine (but with gorgeous weather today) and my cousin's little boy was charmed by the Merlin float (an annual tradition).    It also gets bonus points for their custom foam sword (which says King Arthur instead of Excalibur since that's a different parade out in Metairie) and stuffed dragons.  So +1 for appropriately themed throws.
Good selection of pizza toppings, some little more unusual.  Good salads and calzones.

I was kind of surprised to discover that Academy is a Southern regional chain.  They've only had a website for about a year or so; what retail establishment with over 100 locations doesn't have a website until 2010 (OK, maybe late 2009).    Anyway, much of what I said about the Clearview location is duplicated for this one.  I shop here for jeans, local sports themed items, random sporting goods equipment, ice chests, gifts, y'know that sort of thing.  This store is pretty crammed with clothing, so much so that it's hard to make it through the aisles.  The sizing of a lot of their brands is pretty random.  I've purchased clothing with a spread of about 4 sizes. The sale racks do offer some deals.   They have a LOT of shoes, but again are somewhat haphazardly organized. Although  I do know that the cleats are usually in the back corner.  This is my go to location for sports related gifts (how many Saints knick knacks exist anyway?) and jeans.

I hadn't been to the Inn since they moved to the new building...for those counting at home, that means I hadn't been in almost a decade.  I do think the "new" space (when a restaurant has been around since 1933, then the 8 year old building is still new) is really airy and attractive and clean.   The menu is really different but that's a good thing. BUT I think they try to be fancy for fancy sake and miss there mark. I brought a couple of out of towners here on Saturday night and the wait was 45 minutes around 8 pm. Really I know better.   I started with a special appetizer, since our server was really soft spoken and the restaurant can be lively, I think I misunderstood. I thought I was getting a bruschetta type dish, but ended up with grilled cheese, sort of. It was brieoch bread and the brie and strawberries were not of a quantity to stand up to it. Plus I'm not really sure what the greens and egg were doing there. Although the egg was perfectly poached. My entree was the appetizer portion of the crawfish mac-n-cheese which would have been much better without the truffle oil which was a bit heavy handed.  My dining companions loved their dishes the redfish delacroix and the remoulade poboy. Plus the folks next to us raved about their porkchop and hamburger steak dinners.

hahahahaha, Shannon created a listing for the FQ and almost immediately a tourist from California complains about getting a ticket. That's just funny stuff.  As a local, I actually do love the FQ, the buildings, the streets, the history. Yes, I know we pronounce many of the names "wrong" but y'know that's how we can tell who's local.   Some of the best and oldest businesses in the city are located here. Be sure to check out the museums and historic sites like Madame John's Legacy and the Ursuline Convent.  My favorite time to be in the Quarter is before 10 am. Many of the drunks are still passed out; all the worker bees are out cleaning down the sidewalks and it's not so crowded.

Y'all know I love a good used bookstore and this one is like your grandparents' living room full of random stuff, including cookbooks.  There is an order to the books and some of them are not for sale (listed just inside the front cover same as the prices). Besides cookbooks they did have some other Louisiana/NOLA themed books for sale as well as a few food items and other tchochtkes.   The prices of the cookbooks reflect the locale within the french quarter so don't expect to find any bargains. BUT you just might find that cookbook you've been looking for...

A solid not too sketchy gas station (with a really small quicky mart) in a neighborhood where stations are scarce. Lighting is acceptable and it's very easy access from Tulane, Jeff Davis and d'Hemecourt.   The space is tight so watch out for folks in giant vehicles who have spatial issues.

When I realized where this new hotel bar was, I couldn't help but laugh. The last time I was in this space, the building was still the YMCA and I was picking up packets for the Corporate Cup race that they used sponsor.  And I have to say for a former cinderblock & concrete space, they have certainly made it feel cozy.  The room is spacious without feeling cavernous. The wait staff was attentive.    I didn't have any of the fancy new cocktails since I was on a bubbly kick that night, but the sips I took from others' drinks were good. (Yes, people I knew. Jeez)  I'll definitely head back over when I'm feeling moderately fancy-pants.
One of my 2 childhood bakeries.  They do a good job with all the bakery standards.  And their king cakes are delicious.

hmmm...where to start?  I grew up drinking fruit wines that were made in various rural areas of south Louisiana. My grandparents' had friends that served orange wine in their restaurant, somewhere down on the bayou.  And I've had strawberry wine many times.  Both of these were more sherry like than the wines @ Tropical Winery.  The wines here (and I tasted maybe 4 or 5) are all really sweet, like I need it cut with seltzer, sweet.  I didn't taste anything that inspired me to buy an entire drink.  I guess it's just not my thing.

K-Paul's is running a summer deli menu for lunch which means: no table service cheaper prices still delicious food plastic plates & utensils (-1 star -really how expensive good it be to hire a dishwasher)  I had a DELICIOUS piece of flounder with seafood stuffing - that seemed a bit soggy and a side for $13.95.  Can't beat that with a stick.  Yes, it was odd to have your name hollered out from the kitchen but I'm willing to sacrifice some class for cash.

Y'all know that I have a serious bread addiction, right? And the whole carb-free diet would require me having my jaw wired shut.  So obviously, I was excited to hear about a new bakery.  And then I saw Susan W post something online about stopping in today...AND I could drive past on my way to my parents. PLUS I was doing computer work for my parents so I was going to earn some baked goods.  Gira is right; the bakers are generous with their samples.  So much so that I ended up buying beau coup bread.  I bought their big pain au levain (maybe) loaf which is like a supercrusty sourdough. The baker said he could live on that & butter and yeah.  I also bought a sweet bread with almonds and grapes, again amazing.  E got a pineapple & coconut muffin which is light and not overly sweet and the fruit flavor really shines. Finally, I got a chocolate chip cooking which was rich and delicious and again not too sweet.  For the summer they are only open on Friday & Saturdays. I can't remember the opening time that was posted at the door (but not on their website) but I'm guessing they will close when they run out...and at 3 today they didn't have a lot of stock left.

Thanks to Yelp NOLA, I won free tickets to Tales of the Toddy this year. I've had friends who've tried to convince me to go each year...but something always conflicted.    The space was lovely and it was fun trying all the seasonal beverages and having restaurants snacks.  The lines for some tables were too long so I wandered over to the booths who needed some attention. I had some great drinks and some so-so drinks and some that just weren't my cup of tea...literally in once case I think.  The food was all tasty and everyone was wearing holiday finery so that was fun too.  The space was roomy and there were lots of cocktail tables but no seating (no wearing boots with heels next time) Plus I don't know what was up with the wandering trash cans.    But best of all, I got to catch up with a bunch of AWESOME peeps.

I've had this quaint small bar bookmarked for months and finally stopped in because I had an actual real live Englishman as a houseguest and wanted to get his take. He was gobsmacked with it's accuracy, the flower baskets, the couch...which is killing me that I can't remember what he called that cozy area, the beers.  It was a lovely night so we all sat outside and enjoyed watching the world go by. My friends were pleased with the beer selection. We were all pleased with the prices.   Definitely a spot to go get some authentic British flair to your drinking.

I would probably like this spot better if they offered a veggie burger option. Maybe I'll go back during Lent when I heard they offered a seafood option on Fridays.  For the non-meat eater there is a grilled cheese which is delicious but at $5.50 I thought it was a bit small.  I also nabbed the vegetable side of the day which didn't have meat (which was unusual according to the staff). It was a corn and crowder pea (maybe?) salad which was OK...the peas were a smidge under cooked.  My brother enjoyed his burger and fries. He thought the mayonnaise bar was a bit over the top. I ate all his pickles since he is not a fan of the bread & butter style.  Atmosphere on Sunday afternoon was low key and relaxed so that was definitely a plus.

Great new space in a pretty ordinary strip mall. The inside makes you think upscale tavern (even though they don't have a liquor license yet). The menu was broad enough to have a little something for everyone but small enough to do each item well.  I couldn't resist the fish of the day which was sheepshead with a succotash underneath and some citrus/fennel salad on top. DELICIOUS...but a bit pricey for lunch at $16. My coworkers each got a burger and fries and enjoyed them. We started with fried pickles which were OK but not great. I think the pickle to batter ratio was off.  The staff was lovely and the service was good. I'll definitely be back to sample that pimento grilled cheese.

Woo Hoo! That's a fancy pants makeover, pawpaw!  Seriously the furniture that has been in the airport since the 70s is gone. Concourse B looks all shiny & new and the security gates make more sense.  Loving the new food options and everything looks cleaner. There were even fresh flowers in the ladies' room and it's not even Superbowl week.   And I love the new Saints store!

I went to the VooDoo Mystere because a friend had a play running in their backroom.  I just found out that all theatrical productions stopped last month...disappointing.  It was a good intimate space.  The bar itself is on the edge of the quarter and seems to be a drop in spot for folks on their way home for the night, including some of the local performers.  Definitely a dive, but one with a very diverse clientele where everyone is welcomed.

Wow! Party Palace appears to be an actual bricks & mortar store.  I have never actually been there, but they sell they're very tasty King Cakes at local groceries around uptown.  I've found them at both Langenstein's & Zara's.  I've never gotten a stale one (occasionally the one I've ended up with has been sort of smushed, but that is probably the stores fault...although not anymore since this year I noticed boxes of king cake rather than bags.)  One of my friends insists that the Party Palace King Cake is the first she has each year because she loves them so.  Hunt one down, you won't be sorry.

Oshun is the first of the Uptown parades each season and it's not a very large parade.  But points to them for fighting it out and keeping their krewe together in tough economic times.  The floats actually seemed to be fully occupied this year...which is not always the case.  Extra points for having St. Mary's and Xavier Prep marching, they have great bands.

Great basic neighborhood bar where you see a cross section of the city. What's not to love about a heavy pour & cheap drinks type of bar?   Well...there's the cigarette smoke when too many smokers congregate in the low ceilinged establishment at once. And, of course, there is the difficulty on a crowded night of squeezing by to get to the restroom when wearing a cape.  OK so maybe you won't be wearing a cape and that won't be a problem for you.  Solid choice.

I decided to try a one day juice cleanse. And I bought the package of juices from Raw Republic. They had a bag ready to go out and the thoughtful counterperson, checked the expiration dates on them... because one was already expired so that was swapped out.  I had a tough time drinking the lemon cayenne first drink. And I wasn't really that big on the two smoothies. But all the juice drinks were great, very flavorful and I really wasn't hungry all day. Although the next day all I wanted to do was eat crunchy foods, almonds, crackers whatever.   The juice cleanse was a good excuse to hang around the house and read and do nothing else so that was a positive. Next I need to try some of their snacks.

Super cute shop with a variety of items... clothes, books, gifts, jewelry made from old buttons (hence the name). The jewelry is really fun and eclectic.   The shop is well laid out and it's easy to peruse. And the staff is helpful without being aggressive.   I ended up with a couple of cute gifts so perfect!

Wow. I don't think I've been in this coffee shop since I've been yelping, but it's a really cute old house conversion. With a painfully reminding (or astonishing if you weren't here at the time) Katrina line painted above the sugar & cream station in the back. (The line is also above my head btw.)   Stopped in for a quick iced tea while on the clock and was dismayed to discover that  9:30 on a week day morning seems to be the time to order your very complicated coffee beverage. What are these drinks with 4 pumps of this and 2 of that then throw the whole thing in a blender...OK that might have been 2 different orders. But the baristas were hustling and I was their 2nd favorite customer since all I wanted was a straight up drink. Of course, the favorite was the guy who just wanted a cup of coffee. My order required both tea and ice.   They also had a pastries, juice and a sandwich board. There were lots of folks camped out at the tables and the comfy chairs. But no one was shushing anyone else so that was good. The space on the porch is nice *if* no one is smoking.

Things I wanted on my last visit:  vintage metal cabinet from a 40s era doctors office WITH autoclave, green apothecary cabinet, vintage library book cart.   What I bought?  Nothing  The new location seems better laid out although the parking lot is still tight.

I thought this shop was closed since it was no longer located at the address listed in the Yelp database...but then I discovered it a few blocks upriver still on Magazine (address change submitted to Yelp HQ).    The shop had a great selection of fancy cards, stationary and art books. I loved all the fancy papers as well.   The staff member/owner was very nice and helpful as she prepared for a party later that night. Definitely a spot to find a gift for a special someone.

Nirvana...I used to dream about you...your navrattan korma, your saag paneer.  But then since the storm, you've been using frozen vegetables.  For the 1st year, I could forgive, but now?  Your cranky wait staff doesn't really help.  EXCEPT if the owner is in the house, then the waiters are suddenly actually helpful.

I grabbed some takeout here today. And it was fun to watch the hibachi action while I waited.   I ordered fried rice, a naruto roll and a veggie roll. The veggie roll included a bunch of lettuce, a small amount of cucumber & avocado and a little bit more of asparagus. No carrot, no radish. A little disappointing.  The naruto roll was tasty but the menu says sashimi naruto and maybe 1/4 of the filling is sashimi, the rest is snowcrab. Was hoping for more fish with the $14 price.  The fried rice had big beautiful shrimp and that plus the speed with which my order was prepared bumps them up to 4 stars.   My guess is that the hibachi menu outshines the sushi one.

Man the owners here are AWESOME. Seriously helpful but they also leave you be to browse and seek your inspiration.   The store includes legit art supplies for the talented like Re H and for me they include costume crafting items. They also have great art kits as gifts for kids or the kids at heart.  They also sell gift certificates if you need those.  The prices are bit higher than the big box stores, but the quality of many of their items are better and, of course, there's the neighborhood/local angle. Do yourself a favor and check them out.

Four and  half years later, Amy is still my go to masseuse. Damn, can she work the knots out. In case y'all haven't noticed, I can be a little type A and I hold a LOT of tension in my shoulders. Amy pounds (well y'know not literally) those knots into submission. She is thorough and you should prepare to feel like jelly when you leave her.  Her prices are competitive and she occasionally runs a special where you can purchase a block of massages at once for a discounted price. So definitely get on her mailing list  Seriously if I could give her 6 stars (because it's 1 more) I would.

So glad this parade changed it's name back to the Krewe of Boo from the shortlived Krewe of Halloween, rhyming is so much better.  Things I liked in the 2014 parade: * All the marching groups (from the Cherry Bombs to the Muffalettas to the 610 Stompers) who looked to be having a great time. * Cheewees as one of the signature throws * Parade on the edge of the French Quarter * Good looking, scary themed floats  Things I didn't like: * Corporate themed throws * Throw packages so there wasn't any variety to the throws  Still it was fun and I got to take my aunt & uncle and out of town friends, who were very entertained. Plus I impressed them with my ability to snatch a praline out of the air. Bonus points for the gorgeous weather this year.

I'm going to be cranky & "get off my lawn"-ish..but I miss the old Ms Mae's location (where St. Joe's) is now.  Yeah, it's 24/7 and the drinks are cheap.  But I don't know th vibe is just off for me.  However this bar affords AWESOME people watching, especially if you're headed someplace super early on a Saturday or Sunday morning and you're watching the drunks spilling out on to the sidewalk.

Why am I compelled to stop in at shoe stores?  I might have an illness.  This store has some of the same stock as the Magazine Street store but is about 1/4 the size.  The sales associates are helpful and they do have some different things than the uptown store, but mostly I stop in because of my shoe compulsion.

The French Quarter's response to the White Linen Night...which means all the art galleries stay open late and many have live music. Royal is shut down for the evening and there are food trucks and liquor tents set up on the street.  This year it was pretty rainy which actually made the event less hot and more entertaining...or maybe that was because Red Dress Run was earlier in the day and some folks through a white linen shirt over their red dresses and others were still drunk from running around all day.   We started out late so didn't get to go to all the galleries on Vicky's list...this was another evening in her farewell NOLA tour. But I really enjoyed the spots we did hit.   I do think that despite the rain this event was larger than it had been the last time I attended...which was a few years ago.

Sometimes you just feel fancy AND drinky and you just want to have a cocktail in a relaxed gorgeous environment. Yep this is your place. C'mon the place has monkey lamps!  Love the French 75 and whatever my friends bought for me. Drinks are always tasty and well made.  I've always found the service to be spot on and have even had servers track me down to give me my drink while I was being a social butterfly.  The prices are a bit higher but considering the locale (FQ) and the environment (again monkey lamps!) and the quality of drinks...really it's a bargain.  Also, I like that you get the same service if you show up in your shorts & t-shirt in the middle of an afternoon as you do dressed to the nine in the evening.

I am not an artsy or craftsy person. I wish I was but I know my limitations and those are that I have two left thumbs.  Despite that I do shop @ National Art & Hobby for gifts or stuff for E (who actually has artistic skills).  Service has always been good and I generally find what I'm looking for...unless I have no idea what that is which really isn't their fault.  It's a really solid locally owned store.

Stopped by Storyville today to pick up a birthday gift...and of course ended up buying myself a couple of shirts.  They really do have a ton of cute styles.  And I love their new online tshirt contests, if you win your tshirt gets produced and you win cash. And as fan, I can get notified if a design makes it to a shirt. Fun!

When I wrote my last review in 2011 I had this location confused with the closed location on Carrollton. This is the biggest HD in the area. It has a huge selection of plants and all the wood in the world.   The staff is generally nice and does offer to help, but I've never had the customer service that Larissa receives...but she is special.  I don't really understand why the address is on Claiborne since you have to enter the parking lot on Earhart. Confusing.  But definitely the 4th star for the great selection of lighting and fans alone.

This is the closest Sonic to my house which is both good (less eating of fries/tots) and sad (distant access to strawberry limeades).   It's not a great Sonic; the service can be slow and the whole place feels a bit rundown, but it does give me access to my preferred fast food choice so really it's always going to be OK with me....well except for that time they gave me a *cherry* limeade. Yuck.

So I'll add to the love fest.  What I love about the National WWII Museum (formerly the D-Day Museum) is that they strive to cover all aspects of the WW II experience, the soldiers, the workers at home, the families, everything.    It is a state of the art history museum with interactive exhibits as well as historical tableau.  Simply fascinating.

Did you know that today (8/4) is national champagne day? I read it on the internets, so it must be true. To celebrate, I stopped La Divina to enjoy (ENJOY) a cup of peaches & prosecco gelato.    Would it be bad if my review was just the word YUM typed about 20 times?  OK, I'll try to be reasonable.  The prices are good, the decor is fun and the servers were sweet. They let a little boy sample way more flavors than I would have allowed.  Luckily his Dad let me cut them in line. Props to the kid though, he was trying all the exotic flavors like avocado. I wouldn't have done that at age 10.  I have got to remember to check them out for sandwiches sometime soon.

So maybe my mistake was going here on a Sunday around lunch. But it was so crowded and so very loud. Eventually I was seated at a table in the back and still really loud.   The menu is interesting and has a lot of variety. I got the Southern Breakfast and passed both the bacon and eventually the fried green tomato over to my cousin. The green tomato was just too thick and too greasy for me. The grits were good and the eggs were meh. I did enjoy my biscuit.  Our server was friendly but not around too much... mostly because they seemed to be serving a billion tables at once. The table next to us were jonesing for a 2nd breakfast drink and had to flag someone down to order it.  I do like that you can be put on waiting list before you arrive so that's a plus. Maybe on a less hectic day, I would enjoy it more.

I love the Tchop location of this garden center but when I heard they had opened a location near my work, I had to pass by.  This is a much smaller spot, but they had some good looking plants and I was able to get some annuals and some potted plants to make my porch look festive.   As always the staff is super friendly and helfpul.

Good personalized service.  A variety of styles and price ranges, although nothing too modern.  They also sell mattresses.  The best thing about Doerr as compared to other furniture stores, is that they actually have furniture scaled to NOLA's old houses and their small rooms.  I bought a full-mattress sleeper sofa from Doerr when another local company told me those didn't even exist anymore.

I go to Oakwood b/c it is the closest mall to uptown, but the stores (except for Dillards) are mostly for adolescent hipsters.  They've done an amazing renovation post-K.  I just wish there were a better selection of stores.

SoFaB is an interesting space.  And I hope they grow into something greater than they are right now.  I thought the White House china exhibit was cool (but is it Southern?).  And they had a copy of my FAVe childhood cookbook in the kids section.  They get a +1 from me for ambition and potential.

I was early for an appointment down the block, so popped into La Boucherie...ahh what memories the building has.  There was a nightclub of the same name in this location in the mid 80s (I think).  Thankfully, no one tried to vomit on my shoes at the coffee house and the service was efficient & polite.  The barista was even kind to confused tourists.  Bonus the bathroom was really clean.

Amy is a genius. She employs multiple techniques to really knock the knots out. She discusses what your needs/expectations are on each visit and asks what you would like to work on.    I was really grateful to find her again after Green Day Spa closed.  Seriously she is amazing.

It's hot and I'm bored with all of my make up. I've gone to the mall superstore and have not found them superhelpful and the makeup counters at the department stores have been very hit or miss.  So I decided to seek new make up at a boutique store on Magazine.    Cindy helped me and she was awesome. She worked with to find colors that really worked with my skin tones and not just under their lights but in real sunlight too.  Loved the personal touch and the no hard sell attitude.    Plus they always seem to have colors on clearance somewhere in the store. Whim purchasing lipstick isn't so bad when it's $5.

I think the deal with the 2 Kyotos (Elmwood & Uptown) is that they were at one time owned by the same folks, but not any longer. Still they have very similar menus, but I found some of the rolls much blander at this location. The rainbow had a very mild snowcrab center versus the spicy one uptown. A nice addition to the Elmwood menu was the mango & seafood salad in ponzu sauce. I would definitely order that again...without squid (can't get over the texture).  Still the location was convenient and the service was excellent. My family rushed in 15 minutes before closing and ordered a ton of food and they were really nice about it and didn't hussle us out the door.  Even though it's in a strip mall, they have done a good job making it a more elegant space.

Great t-shirts from a variety of creative folks.  Definitely think there is something for everyone and it's not just another t-shirt store.  I bought a shirt for myself (#WhoDat), one for my 16 year old niece, one for my 21 year old niece, and one for my 70 year old Dad.  Now that's variety.

Let me preface by saying I am not a musician, nor do I play one on TV.  BUT I do live with one and he's a big fan of this shop.  So much so that he bought his first new guitar from them in over 20 years.  So now one person will get to rotate between 5 different guitars.

Bicycle World dropped Adam out of their name & moved to Jefferson Hwy just over the parish line in Jefferson Parish, post-Katrina.  I bought my current bike from them in spring of 2006 and was really happy with the service and assistance that they offered.  I had never bought a "real" bike before...just ones that you could pick up at K-Mart.  The bike that they sold me has held up the NOLA city streets just like they said it would.  I haven't had any service work done so I can't really speak to that service.

I needed a bunch of small gifts (both in cost and size) and remembered this lovely shop... Zoomed over and was in and out pretty quickly. They had pralines packaged in various sizes from a single praline in a sealed bag to multiples in other packaging. Perfect!  The staff was friendly and helpful. The space is roomy with an assortment of other gift type items to catch your eye.  The pralines were delicious and the perfect small gift that I needed.

Sometimes you just need the cheapest gas. And this was my go to spot for most of the 80s when it was Tenneco and my parents had given me a gas card. Yep dating myself with all the old-timey references.  It's a pretty sketchy location and mostly the guys hanging outside are just interested in drinking and don't cause any trouble...it is JP afterall.   Gas is cheap. It is not well lit and I only stop during daylight hours.

One of two subcontracts for city trash removal. If their number is on your city issued trashcan then they're your contract.  The garbageman takes all of our cans (and sometimes we have a lot) and don't leave trash in the street...such an improvement post-K.  And the one time they missed our entire block, I called and trash was picked up the next morning.

I was a little apprehensive about fruit in my poke bowl. But I was wrong. The kiwi, pineapple and orange with my ahi tuna was delicious. Plus I added cucumbers to my bowl and I'm glad I did; the bowl needed the crunch.  The counter folks were great. The food was tasty and fresh. And, of course, all the spots at AM are super clean and spiffy.   While I love the fishes, I'll probably check out the smoked tofu bowl because I love that too. Definitely a great option while you're in Auction House.

Finally made it to Café Adelaide for a Christmas lunch a couple of weeks ago, and the food was delicious.  The soup of the day was a butternut squash that was creamy & deeply satisfying.  My dining companions had the turtle soup & the gumbo and they both said they were excellent.  And being ladies at lunch we all had salads; two of us had the strawberry salad which was nicely balanced with all its various elements. Our third had the shrimp boil salad which (despite missing some punctuation on the menu and causing us to be confused) was boiled shrimp and boiled potatoes in a salad form.  She said it was super tasty & spicy.  The service was attentive without being officious.  And did I mention the 25 cent martinis?

+1 star for the fabulous outdoor setting.  -1 star for indifferent plating.  And by that I mean ending up with bits of someone else's meal on my plate.  They have a bunch of vegetarian selections.  And cover the gamut of salads, burgers, and hot dishes.  Maybe's it's just that they are trying to do too much to do any of it really well.

Another space where I've eaten at a variety of restaurants here. But never Patois until Easter brunch earlier this month.  I made a reservation for my family on OpenTable and they had space for 8 (which eventually became 6) at the right time on Easter. My family can be...difficult when it comes to holiday meals in restaurants. THERE ARE SO MANY RULES. But I digress.  We were seated promptly at our reservation time and we enjoyed some delicious cocktails and wine. The basket of brunch breads were tasty but the selection was on the sweet side for me. It was more a basket of muffins and we fought a bit over the brioche.  For appetizers, we mostly had the salads which are all delicious if my Mom stealing fried oyster from my Dad's was any indication. I had the heirloom tomato salad which was perfection.  For entrees, we had shrimp & grits which Daddy devoured, a Cuban Madame that my Mom really enjoyed, 2 of the omelettes of the day which featured crawfish, the rabbit biscuit which my brother said was tasty and I had the gulf fish of the day (flounder) which was again delicious.  The restaurant is small and gets really loud + they have piped in music. This was a bit challenging when 2 out of 6 people at your table wear hearing aids and a 3rd should probably have one. The space is beautiful however and my mom & uncle enjoyed reminiscing about the area when they were children...and the sandwich shop that used to be in this location in the 70s and 80s. Service was OK. I think our server was done in by the holiday crush.   The menu online is definitely not what you will find when you arrive. LOVE that they create the menu based on season ingredients.

Vincent's would be a good place to bring a date...maybe not a first date, too much pressure. Maybe like a third or fourth when you really want to wow them.  The food is rich and tasty...and garlicy (maybe you and your date will cancel each other out?)  The decor is kitschy Italian bistro but still cute.  The lighting is low and romantic to the point of my MiL pulling out a flashlight to read her menu.  (I didn't say I was on a date.)  The restaurant is small so reservations are a good idea.  I've never had a bad meal here even when we've come with a group over 10.  The corn & crab soup in the bread bowl is delish.  And last time I had the mirltons stuffed with shrimp, super tasty and way more garlicy than my grandmother made them.

John is correct... the old Bonnet Carre listing disappeared. I looks like I reviewed in back in 2015 and I could still get to the review, even though the listing was gone.   So here's a reprise: I'm really glad that I don't drive over the Spillway in rush hour very often. Because even though it's 2 lanes in each direction in a STRAIGHT LINE, people are dumb. And make a mess with traffic for zero reason.   But it can be a really pretty drive when the traffic is light and the weather is right.  Favorite spillway memories:  1. commuting to BR to get my graduate degree, and on the way home seeing the biggest brightest spring moon rise ever. It was like a blessing. 2. They opened the spillway for flood control when I was a little kid. My Mom decided we should go see so she loaded me, bro2 and bro3 in our old Volkswagen van. We're driving back and there are a bajillion crawfish crossing the highway so my Mom stops and we all run along the shoulder by headlight and scoop up crawfish into the van so we can boil them later. I don't really remember much about the spillway being open except rushing water. Kids. They're just unappreciative. Now the crawfish and the mosquito bites, that I remember.

Review 2200! Yes. I have a problem.  This review is for the newly opened (less than a week ago) space on Broad & Banks. I took my parents for lunch today because this address was the location of the Carpenters Union of which my Dad was a member for 25 years....where Dad & Gramps picked up their free turkeys the week of Thanksgiving!  The parking lot is off of Banks as is the entrance to the restaurant, despite the Broad address. There is an alley to walk around the back to get to the actual entrance.   The renovation of this former union hall is lovely. The space is open with great windows, even on a dreary day like today but still feels homey and comfortable. There is a good waiting area. And a worker was assembling the new patio furniture while I was there. My Mom was impressed with the parking lot. It's water permeable and the spaces are well marked.   The food is the same menu as other RS locations but my meal today was well executed which was not the case last time. My parents really enjoyed their food. Today I had the smoked salmon benedict which was a huge amount of food. Dad had the Chicken St. Charles and said the fried chicken was perfect. And Mom had the stuffed French toast of the day which she also enjoyed. No cocktails for us today but the full bar was happening... on a Thursday at lunchtime but it is almost New Years.   I just wish the menu had more vegetarian/vegan friendly options. Almost everything on the RS menu is very meat or seafood forward. I noticed the diner next to me was having toast with a side of avocado, fruit and home fries. That's probably all they had for her since she must not eat eggs.   This is definitely my new favorite RS location.

Pretty sure this is the original Mona's location. And it was closed for a few years after it caught on fire.  The renovations post-fire are pretty fancy...for Mona's.  But don't worry the prices are still ridiculously low.   Since I have a Mona's a half  mile from my house, I don't make it to the mid-city location to often.  But I came by on Mother's Day with the family before a concert in City Park.  The parents have always been big fans of middle eastern food (I remember going to a restaraunt called House of Mesopotamia with them in the late 70s/early 80s).  The menu is the same as the other locations.  And we all enjoyed the food, as a group we had lamb, beef, chicken, and veggie options.

Housed in a beautifully renovated craftsman shotgun, this neighborhood art gallery drew quite a packed house for their art opening tonight. How could I resist a show entitled, Whimsy?  Of course I found a piece that I really want & may have to come back after considering the piece a bit.  The crowd for the opening was substantial for such a small space...I thought all the parking was being taken up by folks at Happy Hour at Cure (almost next door) but I was wrong.  ALL of them were for the gallery, a great party scene but it made it a little difficult to view the art.  I'm going to have go back and check the pieces when it's a bit more subdued.
Really fresh seafood for sale and sandwiches too.  Good stuff.  No dine in service though.

I'd been to JE previously for HH (2-5 weekdays) which offers well priced drinks and pasta specials...HHs that end at 5 are normally just terrible for me. Besides a less than friendly bartender, I had a nice time.  FF to this week and I actually sat down in the restaurant and revisited one of those pasta dishes. I wolfed down an order of the canestri cacio e pepe, so little basket pasta with cheese and pepper. And OMG did it hit the spot. Just what I needed and then some.   Service was great and the server was on the spot with water refills and the bill so we could be on our way. Will definitely come back for a pasta fix.

Makings of a fun evening?  *Good bourbon selection - yep *Hanging out w/ childhood friends - yep *in a bar where you can actually hear each other speak - yep super low key & fun.  Glad my friend Dave lives around the corner. Although I do think it's cheating for him to pick a bar 30 feet from his house.

My neighborhood post office and I avoided if I can. But I thought I'd update with a funny story about NOLA and lines and old ladies...  I had to stop in to pick up a package and the line was moderate when I came in. As is usual with the post office, you see a little cross section of the city: old/young, working class/professional/borderline homeless, all races. You get the picture. This post office has wooden handrails rather than ropes or something flimsy to assist with the queuing up and they are super convenient for resting a package on while you're waiting your turn.   The last couple of people in line were all white and dressed professionally to semi-professionally...mostly folks like me who were stopping in on their way to work. Except the last 2 or 3 were all clumped up blocking the door instead of using the wooden "lanes" to line up in. Rather than stand in the doorway, I squeezed past and took my spot in the lane leaving room for the folks who should have been ahead of me. My action must have met with the approval of the a couple of older black ladies in line because they started tsking and fussing about "folks not knowing how to line up." And they eventually shamed the other people in following the unwritten rules.  It was a lovely bit of theater first thing in the morning.

This location is smaller than the Lakeview store and I'm not sure if carries the same merchandise or not but it does have some really cute locally themed gifts and kids stuff. It definitely has less women's clothing.  The staff was busy (it was the Saturday before Christmas) but I was offered assistance and everyone was nice.  The parking lot is bit frightening since you have to back out onto Metairie Road AND I was parked between 2 monster SUVs...luckily one of them wanted might spot. Phew.

Did you know that if you go to Dirty Coast wearing a Dirty Coast t-shirt that they give you 10% off? That's what I was told over the weekend at this location. So remember that if you're ready to purchase some gifts...  I usually shop at the uptown location but this is a great spot for local t's and gifts in the FQ. Love the decor that they use inside including items from parades and what not.  I forget how hyperlocal some of their stuff is until I'm explaining to a visitor what some of the items mean/are.  Great locally owned shop to find souvenirs and gifts and maybe something for yourself!

My review is for lunch only. While I was seated near the stage area, no music was happening on the weekday afternoon while I was there. And since I was in town visiting with one of my besties, I was really glad that we could chatter at each other rather than listening to what I'm sure is awesome music.   We chose a variety of small plates and gobble up everything with only a few leftovers for her family to sample. We ate the pimento cheese balls, skillet cornbread, grilled pear pizza, brussels sprouts, Gray's salad....and maybe a special. Everything was delicious. And our server was great. The cocktail menu looked amazing but we were behaving ourselves so next time.  The building is gorgeous. Love all the exposed brick and woodbeams. We were seated upstairs and it was very cozy.

Newcomb art museum is a small free museum on the Tulane Campus. If you're there during the day, make sure to park in visitor spots. Luckily my last visit was for a show opening, so parking was not an issue.  The museum has a variety of galleries in the same building as the art school. Some of these galleries are not well signed so if you don't know where you're going, you have to ask...or like we did last night for the opening, follow the noise.  I think there are special 4 exhibits happening at the moment in different rooms. And the permanent collection is not always on view. It's a good spot to check out a small installation or collection. Call before you go if you wish to see something specific.

The menu is interesting and has some items I haven't seen on other local menus. And I like how they've dressed up the decor...but left the doors from when it was Doors. Odd.  We had a variety of rolls, sushi, appetizers, and udon in my group. Everything was fine. BUT on the Sunday afternoon that I went, the whole place smelled like spoiling seafood.  I will try it again but the locale will not replace my regular sushi haunts.

One of my favorite memories of the Peristyle was dancing across it, just spinning and spinning...of course I was just a tot when I did that, although yes I would do that again...as soon as it gets a little cooler. Yesterday when I passed by the entire pavilion was full of tables and chairs as caterers were setting up for some sort of to do.   When it was built, in 1907 it was designed for open air dances with a band on one side and a dance floor on the other. I love the neo-classical colonnade and I miss the melty faced lions. Who knew our weather would be so brutal on their faces but those were "renovated" in 2012 and look more lion-y now.   You can rent the space for your event from City Park, hence the catered event yesterday, but if it's not booked you can have your own dance party/photo session/impromptu soiree in it's environs and backed by beautiful Bayou Metairie.

Went in October and the french bread tasted like freezer.  And they were out of 1/2 of their entrees.  I know times are tough, but c'mon.  The food they did have was pretty good.  But freezer burned bread?  You get a 2.

In relation to the reupholstery of our vintage chair, this is where we bought the fabulous retro fabric.  Fabrixx specializes in upholstery and curtain fabric; this is not where you will find cloth to whip up a dress, unless you are Scarlet O'Hara and want a green velvet drapery dress.  Finding someone to actually help you can be a challenge, but when you do they usually have good advice.  I believe the store offers some services (like making curtains, etc.) but I have never used those.  They really do have fabric for almost every taste + great sales on remnants.

Took the 7 year old niece shopping today for her birthday and checked out Swap for Kids.  The store is small but well stocked...if you're looking more for baby/toddler clothes.  My niece who is 7 but wears a size 12 (what are they feeding kids these days?) had a more limited selection.  But we still found her a skirt, dress, and jacket...all for under $30.  And if her Mom doesn't approve any one piece? I'm not so concerned since they were under $10 each.

I decided that I needed a photo of a cemetery for a professional poster that I presented at a meeting.  (Yes this seemed an excellent idea to me at the time...it was sort of zombie/Halloween themed.)  And I was looking for the perfect cemetery to use as my shadow on the title.    After taking photos various places in my fair cities of the dead, I decided that I needed to try Lafayette no.1.  Really it was silly that I had used them earlier since they were a lot closer to my house than others.  I guess I just feel like this cemetery is overexposed. Anne Rice used to use it to make grand entrances to book signings at the independent bookseller nearby (even being carried out in a coffin once).  And then it was featured in a local novel (Ruined by Paula Morris which is pretty good so don't let the YA designation dissuade you).  ANYWAY.  I found the perfect shot, so yay Lafayette no.1

I went to Serendipity on Thanksgiving eve with a small herd of friends and it was a nice juxtaposition with the uber-traditional dishes consumed the next day.    The menu is hyper-creative...almost too much so on some dishes and for some tastes. (Think the Salierie criticism of Mozart...too many notes.)   The menu changes a LOT! And that's what the chef is known for so don't expect the website to reflect the menu that will handed to you on any given night.  There are items here for the extreme carnivore and the vegetarian and most folks in between.  I had the shrimp in grass skirt and the Vietnamese style crepe with crab. Both were really tasty and filling.  One of my big appetite friends got the tasting menu which was 5 courses and was satisfied. Everyone else at the table got two plates and left full and many things were passed around for sampling...which is probably the best way to go.  The drinks menu is very creative but there were no bourbon based drinks the night I went so I just stuck with my standard old fashioned. And old fashioned it was and made perfectly.    We also shared 2 desserts among our big group.  The ice cream special of the evening ...which had absinthe & pistachio flavors and also the homage to hubig's pie. Both were delicious.  The service was good and personable and the chef stopped by our table twice so that was cool.  I was afraid the restaurant would be loud with it's concrete floors and modern ambiance...but they've done a good job with deadening the hard spaces so it was a really comfortable place to have a meal.
Good, fast work.  I haven't had anything complicated done here though.  Only hems in pants and sleeves.

Wow. Can I say the chef who runs this small spot in the Catahoula hotel is HUSTLING. He cooks in a tiny space and seems to do it all by himself! Kudos,sir.  The menu is small and vegan but the food is really flavorful and tasty. I had the chinese greens (these were OK and a little difficult to eat with plastic utensils...solution eat with your hands), the bao (tofu was super tasty) and the scallion pancake (the star). Everything was tasty & quick!   Ordering and payment was at the bar of the hotel (Pisco Bar) so that was easy. There is some space inside the hotel/bar to eat but we enjoyed the lovely courtyard which was somehow cool enough (after an earlier rain) on a Saturday night in August!  Will definitely be back to sample as the menu changes with the season.

I'm not sure how it happened that I haven't been to this spot since it reopened, post-K. But away a group of us went a couple of weeks ago. We knew it gets busy for lunch no matter what the day, so we arrived early to get a large table for the 5 of us. Most of us ordered off the regular menu and one person got the buffet.   My stuffed shrimp were delicious! And while pricey at $18 for a lunch, the portion was dinner sized and I had the leftovers for dinner. My coworkers had the shrimp clemenceau and the stewed chicken as well. We all really enjoyed our food. And service was great. They even separated our checks, whew.  I love the renovated dining room and the various rooms of the restaurant. I remember it being much darker 15 years ago. And it was very convenient for us that it has a parking lot.  Definitely will not wait so long to be back.

This is a large lot on Rampart and it is well lit. There is not an attendant on duty but be assured they have folks who circle looking for expired parking.  There is an app to pay for parking but I usually just add cash to the machine on site or swipe  a credit card. I've parked here pretty often without a problem.  Rate do vary depending on day of the week, time of day, time of year, etc. They do offer monthly contract parking if you live/work nearby. http://www2.premiumparking.com/park/locations-nola/420-n-rampart-st-338/  So my big issues are mostly with other users of this lot. Usually they cannot figure out the machine or park their gigantor vehicles too close to the lines and try to ding my car. Hmph

The first itme I stopped in was for lunch on a work day and Revel had just opened. My salad was delicious but with only one server working the restaurant portion and no drinking for me, it may not have been the quickest choice.  Finally made it back for a Happy Hour last week. Loved the wine and cocktail selection at HH and that they were supporting a charity that day. My sparkling wine was tasty and the snacks people got looked delicious.  Next stop...to actually eat dinner here.

While waiting for traffic so I could cross the street, I looked up a the golden shininess of this statue. It used to be located on the street between Harrah's and the river but was moved when Harrah's went under construction. She was a gift from France in the 1970s and is a replica of a statue in Paris.  She was moved to her current location in the tiny pocket park where N.Peters and Decatur split off in 1999ish. I like to think she's guarding the French Market against incursions from national retailers.  The Joan of Arc parade honors her on Epiphany which is also her birthday (and the start of the carnival season). Her feast day is May 20th and the day she was burned at the stake... maybe something should start happening in her honor then.

Y'know I used to love Bacchus with the BacchaGator and the BacchaWhopper and the Kong family (all are annual floats).  But this year the themed floats were LAME.  I think Bacchus is showing the age of it's krewe. C'mon "Saluting our WWII Veterans" may be a fine & noble theme, but it doesn't lend itself to exciting floats.  Yawn.  Props for the Bacchus foam football that looks like grapes.

I was surprised when I checked in here earlier today to see that the flag shop had such low score (2.5 stars) and now I see why...only 2 reviews.    I think this shop is a hoot.  The owners are very sweet and helpful.  The selection is huge.  I'm not a super home-decoratey person, but they carry such a variety here, that there truly is something for everyone.  We've purchased Saints & Jazz Fest flags here.  Today it was gifts for my Mom to give various folks.  She bought 3 different New Orleans themed flags and was very pleased with the prices.  Yes, walking into the shop is an experience as you are walking with flags brushing your shoulders (even short me).  If you're claustrophobic, it could be a problem.  Also the owners have a pet parrot in the store; I enjoyed talking to the bird, but my Mom is a bit phobic so she just pretended that it didn't exist.  You can't miss the store when it's open since they put so much of the stock on the street and it's really fun to see all the flags, windsocks and whirlygigs blowing in the wind.

I stopped in for an early Saturday morning breakfast with a friend.... And while it was good, it wasn't really what I was expecting. It's more a grab and go sort of place.  You order at the counter and folks were a mix of fancy coffee drinks and food. They seemed to be short staffed the day we were there, but that's just the way it is these days.  I got a breakfast biscuit with bacon on the side and an iced tea. My friend got the avocado toast and a coffee. My biscuit was good but the cheese was skimpy. My friend really enjoyed her toast.  The big plus is that if you want to have an adult beverage at 7am that's possible here.   It's in a big space with well spaced tables and outdoor dining so those are all pluses.

My only mistake at WINO was running an open tab on my card.  And after hitting the fun wine vending machines (it was like I was a little kid with unlimited change to hit the gumball machines), I quickly ran up a tab double what I thought I would.  Oh well, that's what happens when you taste lots & lots of wine.    I'm envious that @Seale P has eaten there a few times.  The night I went and wanted to eat, they were out of almost everything and my companion is gluten intolerant so that severely limited the few choices left.    I would happily go again...and give myself a credit limit the next time.

On a rainy Saturday we stopped in here because we were starving. I knew there wasn't too much on the menu for me (non-meat eater) but my friends eat all the meaty things so no big.  I had the caprese panini and my friends has a burger and a philly cheesesteak. They both really enjoyed their sandwiches and mine was fine but a little skimpy on the fillings. The crisps and fries were aces though. DELICOUS. They have coffee and tea and then a cooler of drinks. So there's a good selection for your beverage needs and a water area near the front.  Of course then we got ice cream and we all enjoyed our scoops. I had the hummingbird flavor (no actual birds, more the southern cake) and I can't remember what my friends had. Again delicious.  Staff was great and the space is really fun but with limited seating. I think most folks take their sammiches to go.

Please note that I have not used Zeus' Place for boarding or grooming as my big girl isn't with me anymore. BUT I have donated towels to their rescue efforts and occasionally played with their animals up for adoption through their rescue efforts.  Everyone is so nice and very into the welfare of the animals in their charge. And I love how committed they are to rescuing animals. Good job!

I stopped into Jaegers recently and picked up some to go plates for my parents and my dinner. It had been a while since I'd been over here.   Placing my order while sitting at the bar was super easy and the staff was friendly. And everything was well priced for the quality and the quantity. But let me tell you... my Dad's face when he saw those stuffed crabs, in the real shell not a little metal tin. He LOVED it. The friend shrimp were great and my Mom said the shrimp pasta was good too.   I wish the menu was a little more informative as to what is on a plate so I wouldn't have to ask so many questions.

Jaeger's was an institution on the lakefront until Katrina.  And I've always thought it was OK.  The advantage to the Lakefront location was that you ordered & paid at the counter and then a server brought your food.  This was ideal for large groups (no bill politics at the end).  The new location on Clearview is a basic NOLA seafood restaurant, lots of boiled (in season) and fried.  Good but not great.

Slowest Sonic ever. All I want is my strawberry limeade as a reward for running my errands. And it takes over 10 minutes to even take my order? Ridic...and not exactly fast food.  Otherwise food/drinks are the same as all Sonics.

Pandemic Review: I guess it's been a very long time since I've been in this shop if I don't have a review for it.   I am working on my house float and needed some exterior paint quarts to make it happen. SW was actually cheaper than other locations for some really basic paint. I walked in (masked of course) and they had hand sanitizer ready for me.  The sales associate was great to work with and she helped me find the least expensive options, knowing that I need the boards that I'm painting to last from Jan. 6 to Feb. 16.   The paint worked great and my project is looking wonderful.   Staff was all masked. There are plexi barriers at checkout. Hand sanitizer is supplied and there are clear social distancing markers on the floor.

Another solid Mr. Ed's. Y'know this local chain isn't fancy but is really solid, especially for fried foods. Like every location, the food was good and plentiful. The staff was great. The menu is the same as the other locations with the daily specials. I feel like the bar might be a little better. My old fashioned was perfect. And since fried shrimp has been my go to since I was a tyke... they do it right.   The location on St Charles is lovely and if you get a front window like we did you can watch the streetcar pass by. The bathroom is a bit of a wander so prepare for that.

I was hunting for an accessible lunch spot on a Saturday with the parents. Someplace that did plate lunches and not just sandwiches and this place was a great homey choice.  There is a ramp into the restaurant so it was easy for my seniors to access. The menu had enough variety to keep us all happy. Mom had the cochon de lait cuban and loved it. Dad had the hamburger steak and I had the fried shrimp plate. Our food was all tasty and well-prepared. The portion size was good and we had leftovers for them.   The server was great and she checked on us a couple of times and was very helpful. A good choice if you're in the area.

Once upon a time, I got a large portion of my wardrobe at the old UAL that was located on Vets. That store (and the shopping mall where it was located) is long gone but I remember it fondly when I pop into the FQ location.  This store is jammed with clothing...overly jammed. It's hard to move around and hard to get the clothes off the racks. So you have to have the energy to dig... The sizing is all over the map so definitely plan to try everything on. The staff is varied, but you sometimes find someone actually helpful.   I've mostly been successful with accessories in the last few years. Maybe because I no longer have the energy (after wandering the FQ) to do that much digging through the racks.

My review is for facial services. I have chased my favorite facialist around various locations in the GNO for the last decade. And now Nikki is affiliated with this salon. The location is new (and beautiful!) but the salon has been around for a bit (formerly located on Lapalco).  Nikki was running a special on infusion mini-facials for their grand opening. And while it wasn't relaxing as what she normally does, I definitely could see the difference in my skin. She is happy to consult with clients on whatever their skin needs are.   The facial room is very relaxing and well decorated with a very comfy bed and low lights. The whole salon is beautifully renovated. There is parking in back but you enter through the front door...unless you need to use the ramp.   Will definitely be back soon for Nikki's care.

This is such a lovely space and has been a variety of businesses over the last few years. I hope this iteration of the Tasting Room makes it!  My most recent visit was to a HH event planned by a friend on a Wednesday night in early January. There were $5 wines and $5 HH boards. They also have cocktails. But I was only doing club soda that evening but still had a great time.  The space is lovely and very conducive to intimate conversations or even some silliness with your friends. The bartender was friendly and the kitchen was quick.   In better weather there is a closed courtyard in back that is really pretty. I'll definitely have to stop back when I'm actually imbibing.

Pandemic Review: I was pretty sure I had previously reviewed this spot...  But since things have changed this year, I'll take another go. Most important thing to remember is that they are closed on Saturdays!  Right now, your minimum order is 4 cupcakes, so plan to either share or be a cupcake piggie. I split the difference by eating 2 and then giving the other 2 to my Mom.   One person inside the small shop at a time. You stand behind a table and everything is handled distantly; you can also call in an order and use one of several apps to have them delivered. And they even have shipping!  First choice: the blackout cupcake, just like the old McKenzie's cake but better. I also tasted the strawberry cupcake (the fruit flavors are delish) and the chocolate cupcake. My Mom raved about the sweet potato. Previously I've tried the lemon blueberry (seasonal flavor I think) and it was amazing too.  Putting on my GBBS hat, the sponge is light and moist and the icing is fluffy and not too sweet. Fillings are tasty too.
They sell pre-made Mardi Gras ladders, but you have to trick them out yourself.  Decent selection, incredibly helpful staff.

Pandemic update: Eleven years later (wow this was an FtR for me in 2009), this is still a solid choice for a neighborhood hardware store. I need various items for my housefloat and stopped in here while I was in the neighborhood to see what they had.  While one item was sold out, the others were available and at good prices. The workers are generally helpful and happy to give you ideas for your projects.  Everyone was masked and they had hand sanitizer so yay!

I was looking for a spot with outdoor drinks last week because I had cousins visiting. And I had forgotten that the Columns acquired new owners in 2019. (Yes the historic buildings here, acquire owners rather than the other way around). So I walked over and grabbed us a table in the garden. And yes they are still taking names for reservations for contact tracing so good them. Also the staff was masked at all times.   The garden is lovely as ever with an upgraded brick patio and a completely unnecessary (on a early June evening) fire pit. The porch still has a number of large tables like it always has had.   It looks like the bar isn't actually open to patron seating yet (pandemic rules) and the double parlor room had the doors closed. The front room is now their coffee/breakfast area for a grab and go experience if you're walking down the Avenue. The left side of the 1st floor which previously had been mostly unfurnished to facilitate it's use as a live music/reception space is now fully furnished with a variety of upholstered furniture.  Let's be honest the atmosphere has always been 10 stars at the Columns but now the whole experience has been upgraded. So far I've only had drinks but I'll definitely be back for their small but interesting food offerings.  One day maybe I'll stay in one of their 20 guest rooms... hopefully on someone else's tab.

I loved the auction house that used to be in this location. But this fancy food court is a great addition to the area. It's perfect for when you cannot agree with your friends on a type of food.   The renovation of the space is beautiful and it's bright and airy. The food booths are interesting and tasty. The private room is a great space, roomy enough to move around and still intimate.   Love that in addition to the yummy food there is also a bar in case you need a grown up beverage. I haven't tried all the booths, but I've eaten at about half.

I decided that I deserved a biscuit early Sunday morning after running around and taking care of some business for my family. I consulted my app to see who was open at 8am and had good biscuits. So I ended up at Blue Line.   So early on a Sunday there was plenty of seating choices but since I was alone, I sat at the bar. Order at the counter and boom my food was out quick-quick. I ordered the blue line breakfast with grits and a biscuit. They allowed me to sub avocado for the meat. (See my pic).   Staff was super friendly. Food was good and way too much so I took some home. Biscuit was just what I needed and their homemade jam was yummy.

I attended a family wedding at this old school reception hall in Elmwood. The hall is divided into 2 sections and we were actually in both. The wedding happened on one side and they set up a very nice space for the ceremony and then we proceeded to the other side (after second lining in the parking lot) for the reception.   The staff was uniformly great and very helpful. Like most receptions the food was a mixed bag. Some items were delicious and others were meh. However the passed pastries at the end of the event were delish and I was sad that I was almost full. The bartenders were hard working and kept up with the thirsty crowd.  The dance floor was spacious and the dj played a variety of music so that even my 70+ parents got up and danced.  Yes the area is more industrial but there are a couple of reception halls in the area. The parking is abundant.

I missed the Yelp party a year to two ago here. But when I was in the need of a casual boozy brunch spot and a friend suggested them I knew it was fate.   I stopped by on a Saturday morning alone to explore the brunch options before committing and the vibe was decidedly low key and sort of perfect for our group. I ordered a custom loaded biscuit and a mimosa. Both were delicious and while I was intrigued by the boozy floats, I thought ice cream & alcohol was a bad combo for me.  Fast forward to the next Saturday, and the menu was much more extensive and the place was a bit busier but still very manageable. (Maybe the 1st Saturday of the month is special brunch day?)  There was a frittata and french toast and options for building your biscuit OR burrito. Everyone loved the food and we gabbed away until the band showed up and started to play (around 12:30).  My only regret? Not sampling any of the Debbie does Doberge cake slices...maybe when I stop in just for a drink.  Brunch is each Saturday from 10-3 is what I was told. Enjoy! And the bar is non-smoking (maybe just for Lent...or maybe forever - fingers crossed).

My go-to-bar for when I have out of town guests.  If they have a teenager, you can sit outside.  If you have a member of the senior generation, they still love the locale.  Great ambiance, good drinks, amazing people-watching

Wow! My last review of this spot is from 8 years ago... when I was looking for spot to have a boozy brunch for Jenn B!  So many years so many checkins. I miss bar hangs so much!  I stopped by just before 12 Mile was shutdown for MG weekend and got some batched to go cocktails. My 12 Mile Limit was delicious as was my to go old fashioned. You can always count on an excellent drink from the bartenders.  When I went it was to go orders only, at the front door with a plexi guard between me and the bartender + masks. Easy peasy.   They are serving on their patio at the moment (I think). And food is definitely available. High marks to the management for doing everything they can to keep their people (employees and patrons) safe.

Saints Football re-starts on Sunday so I guess it's about time that I get around to reviewing this event space. On game days, it's a "private lounge" to get a drink before the game. I've been inside on those days, but I don't remember how or why... was I on a list? Did I just wander in and no one stopped me? Who knows?  I've also been here for a variety of charitable events and it's a nice large space so there's plenty of room to move around. The food has always been good (from the mashed potato bar to sushi to salad bar to carving stations) and the bartenders are top notch.  If you're paying for drinks they can be a bit pricey but consider the locale. Random thought... I think this used to be the lower level of the Macy's that was once in this location, so I think I've bought housewares in the same space. Maybe.

Are you in dire need of Saints/Pelicans/LSU/Tulane gear? Then this is the shop for you.  It's no frills but has shirts, hats, homegoods, whatever you might need. I've mostly been here for Saints stuff and they have a wide variety of items.  Staff is helpful and the store is full. The parking lot though... it can get very full and is very narrow.

Yum to the tasty drinks and the awesome mac-n-cheese.  Love hanging out on the veranda in gorgeous weather.  And then there's the pool. Yes, there are lots of naked people. Yes, everyone looks, but don't be a douche and stare.   Things I like about the pool area:  * spacious * tab can be run at both bars at once (genius!) * hot tub * lots of chairs * secret tattoos on the patrons  Things I don't like: * bare asses on the chairs  * rented towels are pretty chintzy (bring your own) * mosquitos  All and all a fun way to spend the late afternoon....

When I first noticed these coffee shops popping up around town, I thought they were a national chain. Upon stepping into this location on Sunday morning, I realized nope; this is definitely local. Wow that's a lot of stuff everywhere.  I met some family members and we had a variety of items. I liked that I could ask for my hot tea in ceramic and not in their go-cups. I think hot tea changes taste when served in those synthetic-y cups. My nieces got hot chocolate and it was OK. The one person who got iced coffee was happy.  The food was hit or miss. The grits were gummy and the cheese grits had unmelted squares of cheese on top. One of the croissant sandwiches was sort of burnt, but my biscuit sandwich was good but really small.  Definitely will do a in a pinch but not my first choice.

Had a mini-shopping-palooza today and hit a few of the clothing consignment shops (Prima Donna, Swap, Encore, and On the Other Hand) uptown in search of a formal gown that would fit my short, curvy self.  So I feel confident in my comparisons.  Prima Donna's Closet is located in the Garden District right on the streetcar line.  It is very organized and has a good selection of shoes (green patent leather Jimmy Choo boots - thank goodness they weren't my size), accessories and a variety of women's clothing.  Several of the gowns I tried on were actually new, so I didn't have to examine them as closely for stains or damage.  The quality of the merchandise is good, but the prices reflect that.  There is a clearance room in the back but you have push past the enormous wedding gowns.    Not sure why Plus sizes is in the name. They carried from size 2 to 3x.

I hadn't been in Vic's in years when I stopped in the other night. And while it's a huge open space with lots of tvs and seats, it's still not going to be on regular rotation because of the cigarette smoke. As Vicky said, even if you don't seen anyone smoking the place just smells.   The drinks are cheap. So maybe dash in to order, then sit outside in front of the bar if the weather is OK.  The regulars are generally welcoming. But the bathrooms are odd. The stalls do not have doors instead they have curtains...which seems really unhygienic.

Shh! Don't tell my dentist that I go in here OK.  This is the store that you wished were next to your house when you were 10 years old.  Seriously.  It has a variety of candy to fit every need...or want...or whatever.

Yum Brunch! My poached eggs St Louis were totally delish.  My friends got the poboy benedict...although the ham was in chunks not shaved like the menu said and a catfish poboy which was huge.  All the food was tasty; service was a bit odd.  It felt like maybe our server was in training and the floor manager kept asking us weird questions about her service, with her standing next to him. She was doing a fine job but still weird & uncomfortable.  My friend also hit up the bloody mary bar...which had the strangest selection that day. No spicy beans, no celery, no okra. Weird.  I went with a sangria that was really tasty.

This is not your standard shopping mall, instead it's a former factory converted into a variety of arty stores and restaurants.    My friend loves the antique mall here. And it's a nice space to wander in on a rainy day.    There is also a giant rocking chair which seems to be a photo op destination.

Hmmm....what is there for the non-meater? Surprisingly a choice of grilled cheese sandwiches, including one made with cheese wiz.  But what gives this joint the 4th star? The boil fries!  They were OMG delicious and spicy!  Plus the staff was working their tails off to make sure everyone was happy and fed. Good job!

OMG! They have Flatsies here...OK they aren't the ones from my youth, but one of the modern incarnations, but still cool.  The selection was really interesting and different. This would definitely be on my list for gift giving for the children in my life.  The store was also really well laid out and well lit.

As far as I can remember this was the first Rouse's in the greater New Orleans area. It's small and a bit rundown at this point, but it has a good selection of location items.  The staff was pleasant and helpful. But boy does the parking lot need work.

HUGE warehouse out near the Lakefront airport. Wow there was so much stuff in there, much of it dusty so dress accordingly.  I was given the heads up that they had a bunch of surplus wheelchairs in their warehouse so I called to verify and got a price of $50 and showed up on a Saturday morning. We made our way through the rabbit warren of furniture and lamps and housewares and stuff to the wheelchair graveyard. They only had a few left, so I picked the best of the lot and was able to pay with my credit card.   As I tried to get the wheelchair in my car, it wouldn't fold but one of the workers realized that it had an anti-theft bar on it and took some tools out of his vehicle and removed it for me.   Yay! The wheelchair rolls well and isn't the prettiest but it served my Mom well yesterday at parades, even though "she doesn't really need it."

Maybe I'm justing missing the Blue Bird, but I thought the menu at Coulis was a little sparse.  I almost never eat breakfast out so was looking for something....but whatever it was wasn't on the menu.  Which is more a personal problem, I know.  So I ordered the breakfast sandwich and I think they scrambled up 3 eggs to go on it which was bit much for the croissant.  And we had a service bobble (the server didn't think E had ordered anything), but it was remedied with appropriate apologies.   Maybe I'll try again for lunch...

I was surprised to see that I gave this go to spot 3 stars over 3 years ago, as I eat here pretty regularly.   I love their fried shrimp banh mi also their tofu banh mi which isn't on the menu but they'll totally make you one. Speaking of not on the menu, they've also made me a grilled shrimp banh mi when I just couldn't do fried.  I also like their bun and the curry (which states is a shrimp broth). The spring rolls are solid as well.  I do a lot of takeout since this is near work. But if I dine in, I always prefer the patio. The parking lot can be a bit of a disaster around lunchtime but you can usually find parking on the street nearby, especially now that street construction is wrapping up.

Fun neighborhood bar in the warehouse district; good selection of scotches (which I don't drink).    About 4 times a year, they host Opera on Tap which is a fabulous way to check out some highbrow stuff in a lowbrow setting.

This is a nice spacious location with a patio (yay outdoors, boo smokers) They had a good variety of pastries the last time I was in.  And the ginger peach iced tea hit the spot.  The staff was courteous and quick. A solid local choice.  BUT I hate the parking lot at this strip mall with a vengeance...it's weirdly layed out and then add old ladies in giant cars. Yipes!

Interesting place. It's not really a traditional sushi restaurant.  But more of an Asian restaurant that also sells sushi.  Very important items to note it has INARI which is really hard to comeby in NOLA and I love it.  It also has a vegetarian sushi or sashimi plate which is again rare.   We had the specialty strawberry something roll and while I was hesitant, it was delicious. Another standout was the dessert tempura blueberry something. So tasty  The specialty cocktail menu was interesting and they had a good selection of high end sakes.  The service is still uneven but it's a new restaurant. I did feel the staff was trying...just confused.

I came here with a group of 6 coworkers for lunch last month. And the space is amazing! So light and airy and as is only right filled with art.  The food was great. I loved my mushroom and gouda grilled cheese. Others had the frittata, the apple melt, and the pulled pork. Everyone loved their food and that mac-n-cheese was divine. No time for dessert but I look forward to having a more leisurely meal in the future.  When I know I'm going to a place that is training HS age students, I have more patience with service bobbles and really our only one was that no one was sure who was our server, but that was quickly handled. The iced tea and water refills were plentiful so Yay for that.

This is the original location of the Pho Orchid empire...ok maybe it's not an empire, but  it does have a couple of locations and at least one express location.
