The atmosphere is fancy asian and the staff is efficient and polite. It was *freezing* during my supper so I was definitely glad I brought a sweater.  The food was good but the menu isn't as veggie friendly as some other Vietnamese places, but maybe that doesn't sell in the Metrys. For instance when I asked if the vegetarian pho came with veggie broth, I was told no. So that would be not a vegetarian dish.  I got a shrimp dish and it was really tasty as were the spring rolls. My friend, who is a regular, enjoyed her more meaty dish.  It is a spacious restaurant with a couple of 8 tops so this would be a good choice for a larger group.

Obviously, I did not attend school here...but my Dad did...back when it was where you sent your son to get him to behave.  Add in an uncle, a bunch of cousins and now my nephew and I guess I do have a good family connection.    My reviews are for the chapel and the theater space...where I've spent the most time. The chapel is BEAUTIFUL. Love the domed stained glass...and I was sure I had a photo of it to post. Maybe later.  The theater space is good and really state of the art in many ways. The a/c can be spotty so if you're always hot, sit towards the outside walls and if you're usually cold than stay towards the middle.

I was on a quest for something very specific which is a terrible thing to look for in thrift shops, but y'know I'm stubborn.  This shop is really clean and well laid out. BUT if you're looking for clothes this may not be your best bet as it half the store is devoted to furniture. And the furniture is again in decent shape and clean. Some of the stuff looks new so I wonder if they get items from stores sometimes.  The parking lot is also clean and easy in and out from Jefferson Highway. I didn't find what I was looking for but it was clear that lots of other people were.

The best thing about this tiny little gas station? The price.  They consistently have cheaper gas prices then most of the stations around them (with the possible exception of the Discount Zone).    The worst thing? It is tiny so there is often a line for the pumps and it's ill planned in a corner of the Walmart parking lot, almost too close to the Highway.    Also, I feel bad for the person who has to work inside the tiny cube. Maybe it's secretly a government experiment?

As bright & shiny as the original on Magazine, but y'know in a strip mall. The staff was helpful and knew their product.  And the desserts were as delicious as ever. I do love the sense of playfulness that Chef Tariq brings to his dishes.    Minus 1 star for the disaster that is that corner of the Lakeside parking lot. Jeez.

You can sit out on the porch and pretend to be super fancy while admiring the Victorian/Queen Anne architecture of this lovely building.  Solid iced tea selection with normally 3 options...many more for hot. A very tasty and filling chocolate chip cookie is generally available as well as muffins and bagels.  The staff is usually pleasant and the indoor rooms are very cozy.

So mostly I just ditch shoes when they wear out, but I recently blew out both heel caps on a pair of vintage suede boots that I love.  So off to Joe's Cobbler.  The repairs are always stellar and the woman who works there (Josephine? or perhaps Joe's daughter?) has always been very helpful and kind.    Plus I love stores with shop dogs.  Hers is well trained and does not come down the stair into the store front without permission.

I am not a huge donut person, but when I stop by Freret to bring donuts to work? I am the hero.  These are tasty donuts, the glazed, chocolate glazed and the cake (which are considered fancy and cost a bit more).  I have not had a plate lunch here yet, but E did stop by to grab a breakfast sandwich to go.  Since he didn't want meat on his egg & cheese biscuit, the staff was a bit confused.  They didn't want him to pay the extra 25 cents (or whatever) for meat he didn't get.  Good folks.

Last night Midway was my perfect stop. I had been shopping all day, was cranky, and wanted seafood AND cheese. Lo & behold the King Creole pizza...  Seriously, this pie was a marvel. Plumb juicy beautiful shrimp that were clearly fresh  on top of a white sauce but then dabbled with a tomato basil bits  and, of course, lots of yummy cheese made for a lovely and delicious pizza.   I ordered my takeout at the bar and the lovely bartender made me an old fashioned while I waited. She even warned me that she had made it "a little strong." Clearly she recognized a road weary shopping warrior when she saw one.   The wait time was just enough for me to enjoy some of my cocktail and take a few deep breaths. Yay for go cups in NOLA (as always but it needs to be said).   I also had the tasty fresh house salad, but the pizza was the star of this show. 5 stars for being exactly what I needed.

If you're in the French Quarter and you need a New Orleans themed Christmas ornament in August, then this should be your destination.    Honestly the Christmas all year round freaks me out a bit.  C'mon let's keep the seasons in perspective.  However, my oldest brother helped renovate this place when it 1st opened. I think it was his first job (outside of working for family) when he was a teen...so maybe 1977?  I thought he was supercool to be working on a shop in the French Quarter.

Great little coffee and snack joint inside the Roosevelt Hotel. It's where the gingerbread houses are displayed in December.  It has a pretty dessert selection and PJs coffees & teas. Since I'm a fan of PJs teas, this is good for me They can also make a yummy hot chocolate.   It's convenient and affordable (especially considering the surroundings). The staff has always been pleasant and patient and the place is clean and beautiful.

Y'know when I've gone to this strip mall before, I've only had eyes for Hi Do bakery, so I never even noticed the bar down the way.  If it hadn't been for Joi & John and the Party Bus Wank tour, I would never have stopped here. But y'know it was a pretty cool place. The regulars were funny and tolerant of our nonsense. The bartender makes a good drink and was very nice.  Definitely worth a stop if you're in the area and looking for a homey (if your home is somewhere in the timewarp 70s) experience.

So I randomly ran into my aunt and uncle (and their friends) on Halloween as they were heading to one of my uncle's favorite bars in the FQ. Of course, they couldn't miss me as I was the one in the enormous Mad Hatter hat.  Who knew my Ohio (but Louisiana born) uncle loved this place? And why? Because he likes their absinthe service...which was a bit off (plastic cups) on Halloween night but still. I have no idea what sort of absinthe was served as I am not a fan. But if you're looking to drink the formerly forbidden drink in the shadow of the cathedral than this is the place for you.   It's a great location and off the beaten path a bit. Sitting outside and watching and commenting on everyone's costumes was a great end to my Halloween festivities. My favorite costume? A girl who was the travel gnome and her costume was mostly yarn and posterboard. Supercreative.  I think the last time I stopped in a this place, it was more of a restaurant...or maybe that was because it was during the day. Sometimes FQ memories can be a bit hazy, y'know.

I hadn't been to this spot in forever when we stopped in for a quick meal on a Saturday night. We must have missed the early dinner rush since the place was emptying by the time we were seated just before 8.   I ordered a salad with grilled shrimp and it was all soooo salty that i must have guzzled 2 or 3 iced teas.  My friend enjoyed her meal more than I did, but for the life of me I can't remember what it was.   The staff was attentive and friendly.  We were in the overflow room and our service didn't suffer but  think I would choose the main dining room on lighting alone.

What a great independent coffee shop. My iced tea was excellent which is great because so many coffee shops in town do tea poorly.   Shake sugary baked goods, my slice of morning glory bread was super tasty.   Views are great as are the outdoor seating area. Owners/staff are lovely.   Will definitely need to stop back in.

This is the big Lowe's..especially when compared to my little Jefferson Highway version anyday. Maybe it's because I was here on a Sunday evening, but while folks answered my questions (mostly about where stuff was located), no one was really helpful.   I stopped in this location because I thought there might be a better selection of certain items (closet storage and lamps) and while there was more overall stock, it still wasn't what I was looking for.  Oh well.  The hunt continues.  Pro tip: they shut down the air 30 minutes before the store closes, but don't actually make an announcement, until they start turning out the lights at 5 minutes till closing..or at least that's what happened at 8 pm on a Sunday.
Went last week for my birthday dinner (on a Monday!).  The menu is focused and delicious.  I had a fish special that included beets & jerusalem artichokes.  Highly recommended.

Painted Alive specializes in paintings on skin.  Don't be scared, no people or animals were flayed in the name of art.  The pieces that are for sale are photographs of the original artwork that was painted directly onto human flesh.  Some pieces celebrate the human form, where others are more in a trump d'oeil style so that you have to hunt to realize that you're actually looking at a person.  The gallery covers several body painting artists, but the majority of pieces are by the owner Craig Tracy.  (My disclaimer for the day - Craig & I grew up together.)

Not much to eat if you're with a vegetarian, but a very cute place.  The wait staff seemed way overworked the night I was there, like they weren't completely prepared for as many diners as were there that night.

I was on a Sunday afternoon bar crawl in the Quarters and was fading and there it was my caffeine godsend. Seriously, I'm not a coffee drinker but that go cup of iced tea saved my life.  The staff was helpful and polite. The space was clean  and there was space to move around. And my iced tea did not taste like coffee! So I was a happy girl. Oh and the chocolate chip cookie that I bought was life saving to another member of the group who was starving.   Of course, when I left the store, I had lost my group and had to go find them over on Bourbon. But totally worth the detour.

I was convinced I had already reviewed Performance...but clearly I was confused.  More confusing? While the shop is still open (and still called Performance), it is no longer a Subaru dealership.  I've used them for warranty work (now will have to go out to Bryan Subaru...oh wait, my car is out of warranty) and for general repairs.  The staff has been fine and the repairs have held.  But c'mon the car's a Subaru which means it's a tank (I give Subaru 5 stars btw)

Ummm... I've been here a bunch and never reviewed? Weird. Y'all know I love pizza so I'm all about the local pizza places. This spot has some interesting specialty pizzas that are tasty with fresh toppings. The crust is medium thickness but not too chewy. Love the grilled shrimp and the spinach artichoke. I'm also a big fan of the mango-cado salad.   I've always picked up my pizzas... I may be outside of their delivery area.... or maybe not. I figure if I'm getting a pizza at least I can go fetch it myself. The staff in the shop is personable but not necessarily your standard service industry interaction. I once got into a totally ridiculous (and fun) argument with the counter staff about Madonna... because a song of hers was playing. Good times.  The dine in portion of the restaurant is small but serviceable.   Great now I want pizza at 9:30am.

Y'know I like Krewe du Vieux and have attended most years that it's rolled.  (Shout to 1990 & King Al Scramuzza - My Mom & I sang his commercial to him when he stopped in front of us. Classy)  Since this parade is made up of subkrewes who are essentially independent, the parade seems a bit disjointed.  One group will have amazing costume or a great satirical theme and the next boring surprise pizza boxes. (I'm sorry I'm just over it after seeing them for the last decade.)    I do love the brass bands.  So points for fun satirical themes and keeping it old school in the French Quarter, minus points for some dude molesting me (on my back thank you) with a..."personal massager" and right after he did the same thing to my mother.  Sketch.

Sorry, Ryan, I'm going to disagree with you on this one.  I think Bourbon street is entertaining.  You get to watch tourists from all over the world have massive freak outs / bouts of complete drunkeness / whatever.  Yes it's filled with tourist nonsense, but that doesn't mean it can't be fun.

I went to Midway on their opening night, despite TS Lee.  They seemed a bit overwhelmed (but grateful) for the crowd that turned up.  Despite it being opening night, the staff seemed to be working well together with only minor issues.  We ended up eating at the bar.  We had a 2 salads & 2 small pizzas, but we should have split a single pizza. The crust is thick and very filling.  I really liked the flavor and the texture but E wasn't as enthused.  I think he's just a thin-crust person.  I liked it because it was different.  The toppings were good and his veggie pizza had really fresh big pieces.  The salads were tasty and the local beer selection was good.  I hope their menu expands a bit beyond just pizza & salads in the future.

Even in college, I never hung out at FH. Sure I'd stop in when other folks wanted to but it wasn't my regular spot.  But I have to give it to the owners. They are survivors.   The joint burns? They rebuild. The construction next door causes them damage? They fix it.  They're like the energizer bunny of bars. They just keep going.   To me the best time to stop by is for happy hour on a pretty day and sit outside with a beverage and some cheese fries.    +1 star for coming back from their latest setback and opening (bar only) in time for the carnival season.

As I was leaving City Hall on Saturday morning, I discovered this brand new car wash on Earhart. So new that they were offering all washes for $2. All the bells and whistles (normally $14) for that price? Yes please.  The wash did a great job on my car. And liked the blinking lights and multicolored  swirls for foam that poured over my car...very rave like. And the vacuum section was good and spacious and the brand new vacuums have major suckage...so much so that one tried to eat my sweater.   They don't offer a vending machine to purchase a shammy or other cleaning supplies which I've noticed at other car washes. And there was no floor mat machine. I'm not sure if this is because they are so new or they don't plan to get those.   The space was super clean and the staff was really nice. They do offer unlimited washes for $10 per month which is a really great deal if you're organized.   Will definitely stop back in.

I like Sparta because it has an old line feel despite being formed just in the latter half of the 20th century (that would be 1951).  They have flambeaux which is great. And I love that they keep one mule drawn float with the old wagon wheels.    The parade is not the longest (only 18 floats in 2012) but the throws were decent and it's a good start up on first weekend.

I'm not a coffee drinker but my SO is & he stops by Village Coffee daily. Prices are good; coffee is tasty and staff is friendly.  Definitely better than the abandoned bank building that once brought down this corner.

I swore I wrote a review of this little park, but it seems to have disappeared.   This is a great park to play on a swingset or a slide. Yes those are mostly for kids, but I tried to convince E that we should try the swings out while we were walking by this week...and then I realized what Jean-Paul put in his review...all the non-toddler swings are gone, which is sad.  There still open green space at the back of the park so that's something.

Solid (this is my adjective of the month, I guess) diner type spot.  I did not have the coffee since I don't drink the stuff but the iced tea was good and the breakfasts were all really tasty. They even added extra strawberries to the fruit cup for the nieces.  Good prices, courteous service, good choice in Old Gretna for diner food.

My review is for the weekend Dim Sum only. I've not eaten at the buffet next door.  Until Vicky brought me over to the dim sum world, I had only read about this lovely tradition or seen it on TV. And I can see why folk are fans.  You order beaucoup small plates of delicious and spin them to each other on a lazy susan. What's not to love?  Service is different and you sometimes have to ask for things, but all the servers have been polite and helpful. If you know about a dim sum dish that is usually offered, don't hesitate to ask. You may have missed it on a cart or it may not have been offered to you yet.  Standouts for me are the steamed dumplings, the Chinese broccoli, the noodle dishes (which are veggie), the gyoza, and the egg & rice cake dish that looked like hashbrowns.  Tip:  Leave the teapot lid open if you want another pot of tea...

Honestly they had me at fried okra when I read the online menu. I needed a spot closer to the airport that was open on a week night.  Once I saw that Steve I was a fan. I knew it would all be good. My aunt and cousins enjoyed their food thoroughly. One of my cousins DEMOLISHED some boiled crabs and we all enjoyed boiled crawfish (this was a couple of months ago). The plate dinners were good to OK. Don't try to go healthy here, just go ahead and get the fried food rather than the grilled. My stuffed crab wasn't my favorite but it was fine. The fried okra did not disappoint, but I would probably tell them to leave the whisper of grated parmesan off next time.  Service was great. Our server made sure our water glasses were full and that the beers were restocked at appropriate intervals. The decor is old school seafood joint so that was perfect.  My aunt was so impressed with the seafood that she bought a few pounds of boiled crawfish to bring  home to my parents.  Great spot if you're in the neighborhood.
Great full service book shop.  Lots of signed editions.  Great local selection.

My Mom and I got crepes for dinner from the truck while at the sculpture garden at City Park. They were slammed with orders but were hustling to get everyone's orders out.  I had the crepe Italian with mozzarella, tomatoes and basil. Tomatoes could have been riper but it was very satisfying. Mom had the SBT, spinach, bacon and tomato and gobbled it up so she must have been happy.  I couldn't find a separate listing for the crepe truck vs. the bricks and mortar. The big difference is obviously location and the truck has only a small selection of the full menu.

Posting a whole slew of reviews for stores I hit with my Mom on Black Friday. So while we were in our Black Friday shopping extravaganza, we stopped for lunch with friends at Slice.  AND I love the Garden District location.  But this one really needs to work on their service, it took over 90 minutes from start to finish which is ridiculous.  Multiple tables came in after us and were finished way before us, because it took so long for our food to come out.    I will give this location another chance if I'm in the area, but will stick with the original for now.

A friend recommended their veggie burger...which I had never seen on their menu so I asked the next time they were parked by work, as again it wasn't on the menu. And yes they had some!   Their veggie burger is beet based so it was a pretty purple and it was nicely spicy with a nutty crunch so definitely a tasty version. The burgers come with lettuce (nicely crisp), slice of tomato (really ripe) and homemade pickles (delish) then you can finish dressing with mayo, yellow mustard and ketchup at the counter. The bun was soft and not seeded (my preference).   I wish I knew consistently if they had the veg burger before I sought them out. Also since I ordered off their regular menu I had no idea of the cost beforehand ($8).

Was craving some soup but they don't have the vegetarian tofu soup on the menu with the new name and new menu.  I opted for tofu spring rolls and grilled shrimp bun. The rolls were fine just a bit heavy on the noodles and not so much with  the rest of the ingredients. The bun was huge! And there were lots of veggies in addition to the shrimp. Very very tasty.  The space is lovely and the service was spot on.
Great neighborhood pizza joint.  And they have pellet ice.

Still the same cute stuff with good selection of seasonal shoes and handbags. But across the street, from the original location. They are now located at 4122 Magazine Street which is stated on their FB page, but not on the website...yet.  It seems like they've eliminated some of the secondary merchandise but maybe I'm still confused by the new layout. It's gonna take me awhile to get used to it.  Their stock was a tad bit diminished today but that's because they had HUGE sales prior to moving. Smart girls.

Vietnamese restaurants are exploding all over the city and this one is in Mid City. I had dinner with some friends and we all said it was fine...but....  Between the 4 of us two had the combo pho and two had the vegan. The beef broth for the combo was deemed way too salty and the vegan broth was too bland. My companions did like that they could add their own rare beef to the broth ensuring that it didn't overcook and I liked the assortment of veggies in the vegan. The meat eaters did enjoy the wing appetizer and I really liked the veggie spring roll; the firm lettuce inside the rice paper gave it a really nice texture/crunch.   Because one of my friends decided to order a sandwich to go for the next day, I did too. My next day tofu banh mi was very tasty but a little dry...but it was a day old.  The parking lot is kind of a mess and yes the "lot" next door is a bit sketchy since it's mostly dirt/sand and people park willy-nilly in both. The restaurant space is kind of amazing considering that this was once an oil change joint before being a generic sandwich shop. Good job to the designer/architects. Our service was earnest but distracted.   I'll definitely try it again and maybe do a rice or noodle dish instead. I did like that they give you a snack/amuse bouche of shrimp crackers with some sauce

Outstanding atmosphere, yummy cocktails and great snacks.  But then again, I have a special affinity for Napoleon House.    In the 1930s there were apartments on the upper floors (the 1st floor was a grocery not a bar).  My grandparents lived on the 3rd floor when they were 1st married.  And if you give my mother a few sips of an adult beverage, she will giggle that she was conceived there.  It's her only dirty joke.

What? I don't have a review of this joint? Craziness  So, yeah, you can buy your throws here (beads, stuffed animals, spears, etc), but the real reason to hunt this joint down in a mixed residental/industrial area is for the costume supplies.  Gaudy satins, sparkly trim, appliques, tulle (for homemade tutus), hats, feathers, feathers, feathers. All of it is here. Caveats: check for cleanliness. Since this is all stored in a warehouse, the bottom of the pile fabrics can be dusty/dirty. Also make sure the checkout folks treat your feathers gently.   You can also buy tiaras, scepters and other royal accouterments here. I mean who doesn't need a Mother of the Queen pin?
Delicious fresh baked goods and my boyfriend (the coffee drinker) says they have his favorite coffee in town.  And you can buy king cake by the slice most days, during the season.

My meal was fine (I had the veggie quesadillas); the crawfish bruschetta were good. Two of my friends seemed to enjoy their meals (daily fish special and a salad), but our fourth said his pasta and seafood dish was inedible. That plus the extremely long wait for our entrees rates only 3 stars.  And it's a shame because it's a cute little restaurant in an interesting neighborhood.  Also, they had to find us a table that wasn't super wobbly.

Really cute boutique store in downtown Franklin.  They had a nice variety of accessories. The clothes were a good mix of special pieces and basics. I was lucky enough to hit up their sale rack and get some nice discounts.  My teen niece was in love with a couple of the purses here.  The sales clerk was helpful and not intrusive.

Another solid King Cake bakery.  I haven't been to the actual store. Their cakes are at various locations around the city.  A coworker brought this one today.  We had the pecan praline version which was more of a topping then a filling.  The pecan praline was tasty without being too sweet (emphasis on pecan rather than praline which I appreciated).  I did have to dump off some of the icing.  That was a little too sweet for me first thing in the morning.  Tasty.

Updating my review after a lovely father's day meal... I was expecting their standard brunch menu (which is good) but instead we were treated to a really extensive father's day menu (the same one they also used for mother's day).  We ordered the sampler appetizer tray for the table and it was quickly gobbled up: veggie eggrolls, yucca, softshell crab, shrimp, chicken croquets, and plantains.  It was definitely the way to go for our group of 5.  My parents split paella valencia  for 2 and proclaimed it delicious. The variety of seafood was really amazing and my Mom was impressed that the chicken wasn't the primary protein.  One brother ordered the breakfast burrito (which was huge) and the other brother ordered ropa viejas which he loved.  I had the scrambled eggs with seafood which was tasty but probably a little safe. I wish I had gotten something a bit more exotic.  We split a flan and a tres leches cake for dessert which were both excellent.  Round that out with some tasty sangria.  And it was a good day.

NOMA is a great regional art museum with good collections in Asian and African art.  They also have scored some excellent traveling exhibits.  I will always love NOMA because as a child, it really opened my eyes to art.  I climbed on their lipanzzer modern art sculpture.  And fell in love with a Georgia O'Keefe landscape.

Yum! Cake donuts for days. I love cake style donuts and they are hard to find.  Blue Dot has a multitude of flavors...an embarrassment of riches even.  Some were perfect, a couple were a bit too sweet, but I'm sure that's personal taste.  Staff was friendly & efficient.    Thank goodness I don't live too close.

hmmm...I forgot to review this place last summer. But maybe that's because I had a totally forgettable meal.  I think I enjoyed one of my tapas items...something with watermelon, can't remember.  Maybe if I knew I was heading to a bar scene with food, I wouldn't have minded. The place was loud, loud, loud (or lively in Open Table parlance) and that made it hard to chat with my friends visiting from out of town.

Oh my, another overlooked gem that I haven't reviewed yet.  If you need a hat (OK maybe not a befeathered 1890s lady's confection), this is the ONLY place to go. I know there are national upstarts in town, but you know you want to shop at a locally owned store that is staffed by a multi-generational family.  My uncle replaces his straw Panama hat here every few years (and invariably tells me the same Panama hat joke). I still have my grandfather's stetson (with his initials embossed inside) that he wore into the mid 70s. You can buy a safari helmet from them or a kangol or Greek fisherman's cap ...most anything.   My next purchase from them will be a top hat because y'know...I need one of those.  Stalker tip: Follow them on FB to see what celebrity has stopped in.

Not my usual cup of tea... When the Red Eye opened it was more of a diner, right? Or am I hallucinating that? And then it became a throw back dance club bar where you should NEVER where your good shoes since some drunky is going to pour a drink on you anyway.  My youngest brother told me tonight that you shouldn't even try to go here if you're over 30. Oops...messed that one up.  So the drinks are basic and the floor is sticky, but there was some awesome people watching. And I got to see a drunk girl try to pick a fight with a bouncer so that was amusing.    I guess if it's what you're into then wooooo!

As our only "alternative" paper (and I do use that term loosely), the Gambit offers a needed counterpoint to the mainstream Times Picayune.  And importantly, it is locally owned.  As others have noted, it is free and used to be the go to place for apartment classifieds...but I guess Craig's List has all that business now.  The writers go in-depth on local issues each and every week, with occasional breaks for highlighting important local happenings, Hello Jazz Fest issue!  They also host one of my favorite local news blogs, Blog of New Orleans (http://www.bestofneworleans.com/blogs/blogofneworleans/). The once a week twitter round up, on Mondays, is hysterical.
My least favorite of the local bookstores.  If you're not a regular don't expect good service.

First time I wandered into this gallery, I just couldn't help but laugh. Mostly because the little boy I grew up with has made good! Love his aesthetic and his creativity. His path to this gallery has been quite twisty & turny but that all influences his art.   He sells both original works, prints, limited editions and does commissions. His trompe l'oeil style is fascinating and is the most beautiful camouflage you've ever seen.   The gallery space is lovely and there are usually videos playing that demonstrate his process.   Definitely a must stop while you're wandering the quarter.

So maybe this just isn't my sort of place...although with the cheap prices for premium liquor, you would think it would be.  And it was good for people watching.  But with the booming sound system (my throat was hoarse the next day from yelling over it), the pervasive cigarette smoke (Yuck), and the subzero a/c (brrrr), I was not too comfortable.    Maybe if friends wanted to go back on a less crowded/smoky/noisy night, I would try again. Or maybe I'll just convince friends to try someplace else.

As I have small feet, I appreciate that they carry a wider variety of sizes.  Yes, some MawMaw (that's your grandma) shoes, but lots of cute and classic stuff too.  Recently scored cute Cole Haan orange casual shoes for $25.

Hmmmm... another review that disappeared. I'm still not sure why that happens.  Very delicious iced tea and I liked the frozen lemonade drink that they have here. I've found the pastries to be fine. They have them delivered from other local establishments and I remember them being labeled as such. Great for locals who have an affinity for certain bakeries. Love the shopping kiosk in the center and I've definitely bought fun little gifts here.   The line can be confusing if it's busy since many folks are first timers/tourists grabbing a beverage before their tour (that meets in the lobby of the Rink).  The outside deck is great and relaxing. And, of course, I love the Rink, the building that houses Still Perkin'. BTW the name refers to the fact that this independent coffee shop was once a franchise of a local change. When that relationship ended, they kept on going. Good for them!

It's hard for me to believe that this beautiful opened up space used to be the old Sazerac restaurant. It only makes sense to expand to another lounge...especially one that serves food. The space is spacious and airy although it does get loud depending on the crowd.  The evening I was there, the service was slow but they were slammed. My old fashioned was OK but not great. Next time I'll get a straight pour here and same the fancier drinks for the Sazerac Bar.  Benefit of this space...since it serves food, it is not exclusively 21 and over if you have younger family members with you.

The Theater of the Performing Arts was your typical 1970s era venue...until the Katrina floods.  It had its gala reopening last month (January 2009).  During the time it was closed it was entirely refurbished with all new sound and lighting systems.  I can't wait for the opera to return to the Theater in March.  And I'm off to see a symphony concert there tomorrow night.

Wait, what?! A chocolate shop that I didn't know about in the heart of the FQ? Where have I been?  But honestly it would be very easy to overlook this tiny little shop.   Yes, the space is small. And there were actually 2 staff members working (one for chocolate and one for gelato) in an area the size of a small living room. I was a bit stunned by the prices but the quality was good. I had a couple of chocolates and a sample of the king cake gelato that was on special.  I would probably stop in again, especially for the gelato. The prices would force me to have some portion control.

Again, I don't know how I haven't reviewed the Dungeon yet.  I used to spend a LOT of time here.  Almost got kicked out once with a friend b/c of our wild dancing.  Ha!  Has anyone mentioned that you can dance in a cage on the 2nd floor?  Or your friends can make out with supposedly gay boys in there?  A great place to people watch and just have a ridiculously silly good time.

Late on a Sunday night, I was hungry for sushi and several of my regular spots were either closed or I wasn't in the mood. And even though Sushi Bros has been in this location forever, I'd never tried it. So here's a run down of some of what we ate.  The good: the yellowtail roll was delicious and well balanced. The geisha girl roll was huge and really grew on me (but we asked for it without the eel sauce; I'm really not a fan of drowned in sauce.)  The OK; the Louisiana roll needed more pickled okra.  The bad: poorly cut red snapper sushi. Seriously how do you make red snapper that tough?  Pricing was good so I might go back but I would stick with rolls and not sushi in the future.  The staff was attentive and refilled our water/iced tea glasses several times. The ambiance is attractive.

I had lunch at Maya's last weekend and they were using their brunch menu.  I suspect that my entree is on their regular menu though I got the curried shrimp which was very tasty but maybe a little heavy on the cream sauce for a hot midday.  My friend got the breakfast sandwich on DELICIOUS coconut bread.  Really amazing.  There were also cocktails specials, so that definitely influences up to 4 stars for delish sangria & bloody marys for $5.  (Mimosas too but I didn't have one of those).   Definitely plan on going back.

My biggest problem with this location? It never seems too clean...the floors, the tables. Let's just hope the kitchen is OK.    I like their salads and love the tomato basil soup and their savory pastries are usually OK.  Yes the sweet pastries are tasty, but honestly I'd rather patronize a non-chain.  But that's just me being snobby (or shop locally or whatever).    This is a solid choice for quick (but not fast, y'know) lunch especially if you're alone.

I need to try this spot again...maybe earlier in the day. My food was yummy...but they had run out of ice for my tea. So I ended up with mostly warmish iced tea.  The baked goods were really tasty and my boxed biscuit was good...but I had to tell the counter clerk 3 times to leave off the bacon which she never wrote down. When she turned my order in to the back, I called out to the line chef that I needed the bacon left off. He looked at the ticket again and said thanks for letting him know since it wasn't written down. They did offer me extra fruit since I didn't want bacon. Now that's an awesome trade off for me.  The preserves were outstanding and homemade so that's a definite bonus.

I went for brunch and was so not impressed. The drinks were hit or miss. The food was OK, but not great. And it was crowded and super hot.  I did enjoy the 80s DJ and the videos projected on the wall.  I went back for lunch a week  or two later because it's someone's favorite lunch place and I wanted to give the lunch menu a shot.  And my experience was really much better.  The lunch items were tasty and well prepared. And while the place was still not well air conditioned, it was not nearly so warm.  But the problem for is that it's still inside the super sketchy St. Vincent's. And I don't know that I'm ever going to be comfortable wandering into that place.

Low key coffee shop but with fancy coffee...except I don't drink coffee.  So they have a nice selection of pellogrino here as well as other non-fancy canned drinks. They also have quality iced tea that does not taste like coffee.  Although the space is long and narrow, it's usually not packed and so you can find a space to stop and chat with friends. The one table out front affords excellent people watching. And the courtyard out back is very restful.  The staff has been uniformly polite and sometimes really friendly.

I'm not really sure how I don't have a review of this store; I think Yelp likes to keep me on my toes by gobbling up some reviews.   This store is chockablock full of novelty items. They do custom t-shirts; have gift items for whatever is the hip tv show of the moment...or classic show that people love (Dr. Who or I Love Lucy or Family Guy, etc, etc, etc).   Things I bought last week, a handsaw for cutting cakes, cat key caps, a batgirl keychain, novelty ice tray.   The staff can vary from out of it, to superhelpful, to hating life, so that's always a fun spin of the wheel. I will say the staff has always been really nice to my older Mom who asks way too many questions when she shops here.

This is the main post office for the City of New Orleans so it's usually crowded but it stays open later and usually has a bunch of windows open.  I've mostly gotten cranky but helpful employees. (I think if you're too cheerful or pleasant that you get delegated to other tasks.) But I've also seen them go out of their way for an honestly befuddled senior.   The vending machines for stamps and whatnot have always worked and there is plenty of parking.  They have longer hours than most branches, so it's all good.

I mean c'mon the name is awesome so my friend and I decided to stop in and check it out. They had some great furniture including a sideboard that might work in my friend's dining room. Lots of fun decor items.  The staff was helpful but left us to wander ...and the store is much larger on the inside than you would think. The prices were good for both the large furniture items and the smaller decor pieces.  Definitely a fun shop. Next time I had to Nashville, maybe I'll have to drive.

So I added photos to the wrong Sonic.  Once again, I am a smart...  So this Sonic is fine, but it can be slow.  Although the one time they were SUPER slow, I got a coupon for a free drink the next time I came.  Had to use that as the strawberry limeades are delish.

The space is beautiful and the staff seemed friendly, but we were just picking up takeout for a quick weekday lunch.  But oh dear. I really wanted to like this place...and maybe I might try their breakfast/brunch.  With the quality of food we received for lunch, I don't think I'll be trying their higher priced dinner options.  *the bad* If you say "lump crabmeat" on your menu, any good New Orleanian is going to expect blue crab. I'm not sure what was on my panini (which wasn't pressed so I'm not sure  what that was about) and I'm going to say maybe it was a different variety of crab (and not krab) that wasn't as tasty as the blues in the gulf.  If I had been dining in for lunch, I would have sent the sandwich back.   *the good* My coworker who got the curry chicken sandwich really liked her dish and she said the steak fries were yummy. Only error here, was that the menu says served on a croissant, but she got toast.  Also the side of corn was tasty.  The one person who got a juice (the ginger ale) from the bar really liked it.  *the meh* Other coworker's turkey club was dry and had no condiments at all included and that her potato salad side was a bit mayonnaise-y.  Also, my side salad was undressed so left me scrounging in the work fridge for dressing.

Thanks to Rene, I was able to check out the Mosquito Supper Club last week. AND the menu was even pescetarian friendly so I didn't have to abstain from a single course! Be warned that this is a limited seating dinner so buy your tickets in advance online  The environment was very homey and fun, although the tables were a bit crowded with last minute additions. Get there early/on-time to get a good spot, or y'know the chairs with backs. Everything is served family style so be prepared to pass around. And don't be shy about gobbling up seconds.  The staff was lovely and the food was tasty. My favorites were the cucumber & tomato salad (because, dang, those tomatoes were PERFECT), the stuffed crabs (being cooked in the crabshells added so much flavor and style), and the blackberry dumplings. I almost regret gobbling up all my Pop Rouge ice cream since I had no room left for more dumplings. But how could I resist ice cream that was bro2's favorite drink when we were kids.   The rose that was offered as the wine of the evening was a perfect accompaniment to the meal. There were also a variety of local beers (not for me) and a house made cocktail with mulberries...but I didn't have those. Water was self-serve after the first pour and was available on the table in recycled wine bottles.   Oh, wait, my OTHER favorite was the biscuits served with butter, mixed with cane syrup. Yummy!  At the end of the night we got to listen to audio clips of one of the owner's grandmother and I loved hearing her accent. And then, of course, there were Boudreaux jokes...and not the ones that my Parran told. And I forgot to mention at first that one of our cooks was Toby Rodriguez, who you may remember from the Bourdain Boucherie episode of his show.

Cute converted corner store that makes a lovely intimate theater space. I saw a moody multi-media theater piece here and the only distraction was that during the quieter spaces I could really hear the traffic on St. Claude.  The box office space was furnished like an eccentric aunt's living room (and I mean that as a compliment) and was a comfortable space to wait for the show to go on.  The seating in the theater was comfortable and felt sturdy. (That seems a weird thing to state until I mention that the last venue where I saw this theater company my chair lost a leg in the middle of the performance.)  And the staff was all really nice.
Where to start?  I've never had the correct order of food delivered.  Last time I was there my cousin's bill was 4x the amount it should have been and took over an hour to straighten out.   O

I've been to Mondo a couple of times and my food has always been delicious and the service has been fine. But I've hesitated to review because I feel like a crankypants, the place is just so darn loud, especially at night.  The food is inventive and interesting and it's difficult to pick what to order because it all sounds so good. PLUS it has items that even tempt the less adventurous eater so you can bring the picky folks along with you.  My faves: the deviled egg plate (I will not share next time) and the fish tacos. One of my dining companions was raving about the pimento & andouille grilled cheese.  So my problem is the volume. I've been here at night where I cannot hear my dinner companion who is speaking at a normal volume. C'mon it's a restaurant not a night club...not that the problem is music. It's the other patrons. The place is popular and jammed many evenings so the volume you hear is everyone having a good time.  And I'm still crankypants.  So 4 stars because all they really need is some sound deadening and I would be a much happier camper.
Yummy Hippie pizza tonight.  But what is up with parents bringing their kids to restaurants to let them run amok.  Made me want to trip the little angels.  Tonight was also $10 bottle of wine night.

Obviously the best thing about going out to eat with Vicky is her awesome company. But another advantage is that when we go to Chinese restaurants, they immediately offer her the traditional menu rather than the American one.  We had the seafood and bean curd soup (which may normally have meat in it too but  they customized it) and while the texture was really different for me, it was really delicious. The stir fried string bean was addictive. I WANT IT NOW. Seriously, it was green beans in sauce and yet it was so amazing. I think Vicky & I may have been crossing chopsticks to fight for the last few beans. I know we had another dish but I can't remember what. It was a stir fried vegetable and was good but not super memorable.   The service was very accommodating about making changes and they were superfast. The space is a bit tired but very clean.   Definitely a place I'm gong to be scurrying back to, especially for those green beans.

I feel like this corner restaurant spot always has issues... I really wanted to like this new spot more, but...  I thought it was pricey for what it is. And as a non-meat eater, it was hard to find something on the menu. I mean who opens a new spot without thinking about vegetarians or maybe event Lent in our extremely Roman Catholic city. The menu on the website is not the menu that I experience in the restaurant (just an FYI). I had verified that there was a shrimp dish that I would eat online. But it was not on the menu when I was on site. No big... there's a shrimp salad... that included burnt ends. No thanks. My friend got the hot fried chicken salad.   So both salads were good. My friends said that her chicken wasn't that spicy after the first bite. Mine had some nice kick to it. Both were a bit on the high side. We also ordered a starter of one of the cheeses of the day. The presentation was lovely but the amount of cheese on the plate for $7 was sort of sad. That was just a bit of a snack for me!  My old fashioned was tasty and my friend also had a lovely cocktail but I can't remember the name.   Service was good and they did a nice job sprucing it up since the last restaurant. But the prices are too high for it to last.

This review is for the gardens only. After several days of rain, I really wanted to spend sometime outdoors and the Cheekwood gardens were gorgeous!   I particularly liked the Japanese garden; it is definitely laid out for quiet contemplation and the plants are well maintained and so well thought out.  The herb garden was really cool too. Although many of those plants were still showing the signs of winter.  The lines of daffodils and tulips were just mesmerizing.  Highly recommended

John is such an inspiration. Yes, Bruning's has been closed for a long time. But since my grandmother loved it since her childhood, how can we not all miss it.  I remember running up and down the dock that accessed the restaurant and going sprawling when my foot slipped between the slats...which made my brothers laugh. I'm sure back then all I ate was fried shrimp because really what else did a little NOLA kid need?  My last trip was to the temporary location too. (Previously a bar name Federico's where I got epic-ly drunk in college but that's another story.) My aging grandmother wanted to go to the lake for seafood but as she was in congestive heart failure, we needed to find a spot that was handicap accessible...which the temp location was. My visiting aunt, cousin Beth, Mamere and I enjoyed a great lunch. I remember the server treating my grandmother like family. My grandmother asked to order the children's plate since her appetite wasn't that great and the server told her she looked like "a child at heart" and said sure.   I have no idea what I ate that day, except that we enjoyed ourselves. Thanks, John for making this memory spring into my head whole.

This is supposed to be the best sushi in the area and my friends who live there say they only get takeout at night because of the crowds. We stopped in for a late lunch and while it was full, it wasn't unpleasant.    The atmosphere is bright and there are the obligatory autographed photos of Nashville stars on the wall. The staff was on point with refills to water and hot tea.  We ordered an assortment of sushi, rolls, and appetizers. Everything was fresh and tasty. I really liked the Candy Roll which does not taste like candy but is pretty like sweets.  The tuna salad roll was also delish.

Props to Anna B for organizing one last night of snacks and drinks... At the bar next door but this is where we ended up.  FABULOUS cocktails made by the lovely bartender Hayley. I'll be back to hangout with her again on a Sunday night.  Plus we ate a variety of snacky items from the menu which were all DELICIOUS.  I can't wait to come back and actually eat dinner.  The environment is very welcoming and low key and does not feel like a typical hotel restaurant/bar.

The first thing you notice is the freakish number of taxidermied creatures. THERE'S A LOT!  The place is pretty bare bones... besides all the animals. You get real plates, but plastic utensils. There are rolls of papertowels on the table as only befits a seafood joint.  We had the gumbo which was 100% seafood with zero sausage, my favorite! And the cup is really a bowl and the bowl is enormous. My friends had raw oysters which looked plump and luscious. Then there was the 5 pounds of crawfish (price break for 5 pounds so $20 on Monday). And I also had the seafood salad. The seafood was tasty but the lettuce was blah. Why do I do this to myself?   My friends were happy with the food and the next time we need some boiled seafood, I may just head over the bridge.

Do not go into this store if you have claustrophobia because dang, this place is packed to the roof with stuff. And what is the cloying potpourri smell? I swear it adds to the trapped feeling.    So, yeah, I'm not too much of a fan. BUT stores like this are a necessary evil. I was hunting for home storage doodahs and after trying all my usual haunts, I found what I needed (and for good prices) here.    Just watch out trying to turn around or you might knock over a display.

Judy's offers a gifts in a few different categories. There is interesting jewelry, customizable somewhat preppy houseware items, serving pieces, New Orleans themed art and maybe a few purses.  It's an interesting selection. While you might not find anything to your taste/liking the first time you're in, the next time you may find the perfect wedding/graduation/birthday gift.  They do carry quite a few local artists so that's cool.

Color me confused because I did not realize Root squared and Square Root were two different establishments. Glad my friends finally got it through my thick head.  So, yes, this is the upstairs bar above the fancy restaurant. And the atmosphere is lovely and spacious. You can even eat bar snacks (which are pretty meat heavy) and make a meal of it. I did sample the enormous (and delicious) Big Cheese plate; it had interesting selections and a nice number of accompaniments, fruit, nuts, bread, etc. I also had the deviled eggs which included shrimp. They were tasty but not my favorite.   The old fashioneds though. Oh my those were good and at HH prices (5-7 pm), yes please.   The staff was lovely. The space is inviting. There is a wacky toilet paper art installation in the restrooms. Really great spot to be fancy while having some food and drinks.  Hard to believe I bought one of my favorite tables at this location just a few years ago. The transformation is amazing.

I finally made it over to Jack Rose for brunch on Sunday. The crowd was lively since it was hours before our heartbreaking Saints game and there was a band playing in the front room... and the piped in music was still being fed through the speakers in the back room, where we were. I mentioned it to our server after I couldn't take it anymore and he immediately shut down the piped in music. WHEW.  I started with a Bubbles & Butter cocktail. Yum bourbon and sparkling wine, 2 of my favorite things! My appetizer was the royal red shrimp with squid ink pasta. The shrimp were delicious and the pasta was earthy and rich. For my main, I had a scallop special with saffron risotto. It was gorgeous and very tasty but could have used a smidge of salt and pepper. For dessert we split the mile high pie, because how could I resist? It was gorgeous and lived up to the hype.  The place was packed (they moved our reservation back) because the restaurant was closing early because of the game. So the minor service bobbles were not a big deal. And for whatever reason, the back room was really cold, but it was in the low 40s outside. I was pretty impressed that they kept the folks who were doing bottomless veuve well supplied.  I would definitely be back to sample more delicious items, but hopefully on someone else's tab next time.

Cure is about a 1/2 mile from my house so I drive by all the time.  And the crowds of glitterati (or what attempts to pass for it in NOLA) made me think Cure wasn't my sort of establishment.  Well, it turns out I was wrong.  I know shocking.  I went on a weekday after work for a benefit for a New Orleans charter school.  The after work crowd was friendly and a good mix of ages.  I had a glass of their fall sangria (because I got a free glass) and it was really tasty and delicious.  My friends sampled a variety of cocktails and deemed them all well made.  Well, except for the unusual presentation of the Old Fashioned which should have been labeled a New Fashioned.  What no muddling?  And I LOVE the building and that it is no smoking indoors.

I know it's a National chain, but I love Tuesday Morning so I can't help myself.  This is the smaller (but closer to me) of the two stores I frequent.  While the store is often a churned mess, you can find discounted super cool European toys, linens, cookware, luggage, crystal, and just about anything else you can think of.

All the king cake! Looking for beaucop king cakes and don't want to drive all over town to pick up various types and flavors? Then KCH is your new bestie.  I stopped an hour before closing but they still had a great selection. Cakes from 6 or 7 different bakeries with a great selection of flavors. I went for a HiDo one but they had a special berry flavor from Cannatas that was this week only which turned my head.  There's a cooler for cakes that need to be refrigerated.  Staff is friendly and helpful. I was worried because I heard it was on the driveway of the Mortuary but it's well covered by a portico. Cash or credit card. And it's funny that all the scary mortuary statues are decorated for carnival.

Cooter's is a stop on the family tour of NOLA.  Why?  Because it's the location where my parents got engaged.  Of course, it wasn't Cooter Brown's in 1959/60.  But it was a "pub style restaurant" or maybe my Mom just doesn't want to admit she got engaged in a bar.  I miss the shabby haphazard Cooter's of the 80s. But it's reincarnation as a sports bar has its merits.  Another bar that kept me fed post-K.  And for that alone they get 4 stars.

This is my review for the south to north shore span since there seem to be two listings.  I was in grade school when the old bridge was finished and crossed the first time with my girl scout troop. One of the girls cried and hid under a blanket because she was convinced the bridge would collapse...or she was full of pre-adolescent drama. (Later that summer, same girl would explain what the song Afternoon Delight meant, so there you go.)    Anyway back to the bridge, this is the smoother span which means less sleepy time and you don't have to pay a toll to get to the northshore just to come back again.

Ummm wow. I think I found the dress if I ever want a costume as an ice dancer.    I've always meant to pop into this store and the prices did seem reasonable for the amount of details on the majority of the dresses. There were a few more daytime looks but the majority of the stock were for a BIG night...in a small dress...with feathers and sequins....which is totally not me.  But it might be you, right?

Service was slow but we were warned before we sat down that they were having a personnel emergency. And the staff that was there, was hustling.  The decor and atmosphere is fun and welcoming. I love lingering over all the different art pieces. There does seem to be a small elevator outside for those who cannot make it up the 5 steps.  The shrimp taco dinner was delicious with just the right amount of cumulative spice so that the delicate shrimp flavor was not overwhelmed. And the corn tortillas were yummy and fresh. The veggie beans (Caribbean style?) were a little watery but still tasty.    Definitely worth a return visit...maybe at night when I can partake in the specialty cocktails.

Yay! A new food truck by work! I was actually craving a tofu banh mi when I wandered out to see what food trucks might be parked near work today. And there one was and for only $7. It was delicious!  They have a really large menu for a food truck and of course they are affiliated with the bricks & mortar locations on Carrollton and in Elmwood. They were accepting cash or cards. They started out using names but as it got busier they switched over to numbers, easy-peasy.  My banh mi and spring rolls were delicious and my coworker was happy with her pork bun.   They post their locations on their Instagram (phobistreauxotg) where they are, infrequently. Looks like they are by my work on Fridays!

Sometimes I think Yelp eats my reviews to keep me humble.. Because I don't really think it's possible that I haven't reviewed the mid-city Juan's.   I like that the 2 Juan's do not make the same dishes in the exact same way. I guess because it feels less corporate. This is definitely a roomier and less noisy location. The food is good and the service is OK to very good.  Tasty drinks, good food (at a good price) and there's limited off street parking.  My go to order: house special veggie quesadilla on spinach tortilla with spinach, broccoli & mushrooms.

Do you need all the fancy glitter for your carnival crafting? Then this place has you covered. They also have all the varieties of adhesives and feathers and what not.   One of the owners was working the counter and was giving a new rider great advice while I was there. I was seeking inspiration for a costume so not exactly what I needed but I'll definitely be back.  I also liked that they had some original artwork for sale. And their list of classes/party options look fun too!  The store is in a former 2nd story home so that means steps. Not sure that they have an accommodation for folks who can't do stairs.

i waited for another visit and this place is OK. But I probably will only come back if I'm craving one of their bacos. The menu is very diverse and there are lots of vegetarian and meatitarian options But everything is just that OK.  The tofu pho was just  fried tofu cubes and broth and lacked flavor. I should have known when the waiter asked "are you sure?"  The baco are tasty and fun, steamed buns served taco style with a variety of fillings. The tamarind tofu with mango is really tasty.   Service is high school/college student random.

I stepped inside the Milan for the 1st time in years this past weekend and, right, it hasn't changed. Tiny hole in the wall bar that serves cheap drinks. Really who isn't a fan of that? Do not expect fanciness. Order a straight pour or regular mixed drink or a beer.  Cash only but there is an ATM inside  Since it's carnival season, the door was standing wide open and they had made containers of hurricanes and trays of jello shots (and, yes, I bought jello shots for my Mom but she said they were too vodka-y. My Mom, the gourmand of jello shots)  The bar is as smoky as ever (which is why I'm not a regular) so it will be interesting to see how it fairs after the smoking ban.   Also because it's carnival, there is a food truck parked outside everyday of parades. This year it's the Cluck Truck.

Wow. It's been 8 years since I reviewed this theater and I was an FTR back then! I must say the renovation is holding up. And they are keeping the theater looking spiffy and clean.   I really like the seating configuration now, as opposed to pre-K. The sound in the theater is great. And even though I was in the cheap seats, the view was good of the stage. And I can attest that the A/C works really well because I was freezing.  Will call and the ticket lobby is small, especially if folks are standing around chatting instead of taking care of business. Use a different entrance if you can. I didn't purchase any concessions this time, but the bartenders were hustling to get everyone served.  -1 star because the parking lots are pretty bad. They are not well kept up AND they wanted $15 for a Sunday matinee of the opera? Nope, I'll just park on the street and walk in. If I had been leaving late at night different story and I would have paid for the safety. But really the lots need some help.

Do you love old NOLA houses? Then PRC might be the non-profit to you. They sponsor tours and offer renovation workshops. And otherwise support neighborhood and historic preservation.  I've enjoyed their stained glass window tours, their shotgun tours, but I haven't been on the fancy mansion one...imagine that.  Yes, I think they can get a bit myopic but that comes with being passionate about historic architecture.

I hadn't been to Palace Cafe since my grandmother's 90th birthday party (in 1997) so I was glad to see that it was still very attractive inside with some of the old Werlein's store visible.  Our wait staff was attentive but not ridiculous.  The prices were good for lunch.  I had the seafood gumbo and thought it was a little thin.  Plus I like my rice to gumbo ratio to be 50/50 and this was 25/75.  But as my brother said, some people don't want filler.

What a fun little cafe! I was meeting a friend for brunch on a Saturday morning and this is the spot we settled on.   Our server was great, fun and friendly. I had the eggs florentine and bourbon milk punch. Super yummy and so filling. I didn't need to eat again for hours.   Love the decor and that they have a full bar. Great spot!

OK. I'd like to say super yum! This is the name of the business where we've been enjoying brunch (inside of 12 Mile Limit) for months. Delicious biscuits, amazing french toast, etc and so forth.  Tonight I actually tried their BBQ. OMG. They have veggie "sliders."  So sliders is a bit inaccurate for a thoroughly reasonable price, you get 2 burger size sammiches.  The veggie patty is comprised of black beans and beets and sweet potato and deliciousness. Seriously good. By skimming off of other's plates, I also sampled the mac n cheese and the tots AND the spinach & artichoke dip. All were really good.  Seriously, 12 Mile Limit has yummy cocktails but the food makes it a must.

This is a solid boutique with items that you won't find at the mall.  I loved the selection of art that is displayed (and for sale).  Kelly, the sales person who helped me, was available without being hover-y and offered good advice.    The selection of clothing feels curated rather than throwing everything against the wall to see what sticks. The accessories were super-cute.  I bought a pair of really cute jeans...which I will have about 10 inches cut off the bottom before I can where them, but they were on sale 50% off. How could I resist?  The Vera Bradley was was impressive...if you're into VB.  Parking is available behind the store.

I pass this locale almost every day but stopped in for the first time yesterday. It's your basic new model CVS. The makeup selection was good; the snack selection was meh.  So why 4 stars and why am I bothering to review a national chain.  Pre-K this corner house a bank and a Popeye's (then a Quizno's). Both buildings stood mostly abandoned and often broken into, until they tore them down to make way for the CVS.  While I do think it's silly that the CVS is across the street from the Walgreens, that's how this intersection has always been. The Walgreens was built across Napoleon from a K&B...later a CVS. That building was torn down to make way for the Touro Imaging Center...are you lost yet.  Anyway, a building that is actually maintained and used is better than abandonment so 4 stars.

This is the bigger of the two Steinmarts that I check out but I actually find this one less useful...except for maybe shoes. The shoe department is much larger than the uptown store.   Really the whole place is big and so has a better selection of sizes if you're buying gifts. My last trip in was Easter weekend and the checkout lines were so ridiculous that I left without shopping.  As befits a store that carries a variety of lines, the sizes are all over the map so be prepared to bring a variety in to try on. And don't expect to find anyone to actually help you.  Coupons are usually available in the paper or online for bigger discounts.  And, then there's the parking lot which is generally filthy. I'm not sure what's up with the management company but it's pretty gross.

So glad that Re recreated this venue. The original listing was hijacked by an "owner" of a different entity.  So I deleted my review from 2013 (it was even an RotD for me back then) over there and recreated it here:  I was in an office building near Canal & the cemeteries and I was trying to figure out what a business nearby was. So I used my Yelp app and it's nearby feature. So I identified the original building I was curious about (a coffee shop) but also showed this space. If I knew a Katrina memorial existed, I must have blocked it out. And it was just down the street...   Prior to being the Memorial, this was the cemetery for folks who donated their bodies to science and then were interred. Or for the folks whose bodies were never claimed at old Charity or were never identified. No markers, no headstones.   The new space is lovely and sad as is fitting. The curving lines suggest the traditional spiral shape of the hurricane symbol and the stark black marble monoliths are appropriate. I guess the banks of wall tombs are for future cadavers? Or maybe just a reminder? There are no markers on those.   The plantings were pretty barren in late January, even if it is warm. I'll have to go back and see the cypress trees and garden when it's spring or summer.   Like most things Katrina-related, just being in the space made me cry. It's been a tough 7+ years back. So I decided this somewhat somber review should be number 1000 for me. My city, my community, we don't let anything hold us back and we keep moving forward and we reach new milestones every day.

One last review update from my annual Magazine-Street-Black-Friday-Shopping-Extravaganza with my Mom.  I'm in and out of Feet First all the time.  They have cute stock and let's be honest...it's the closest shoe store to my house.  They have cute accessories and great sales.  And what made me stop in on black Friday?  Promises of mimosas and free chair massages (from the new spa that's opened across the street).  My Mom found some cute gifts for the nieces and I, of course, bought more shoes for me.

What a great eclectic selection of sculptures in a beautifully landscaped environment.  There are some old favorites (the lipazaner & Hercules that we used to climb on when we were kids & they were in front of the museum). The giant tree stump that I got in trouble for trying to sit on when it was inside in the gallery.  Loved the ladder to nowhere when it was part of Prospect 1, but it had more power in the devastated lower 9.    Great place to wander.
Best thing from JF 2009 - Pete Seeger interview at the Allison Miner music heritage stage.  Grossest thing - guy walking into a port-o-let barefoot.

The egg & cheese biscuit is solid. It must be 2 scramble eggs and the standard plasticy cheese and a yummy biscuit at a really affordable price point.  I still love their donuts and they make a solid apple fritter. Bonus points for having twisted donuts (twistahs) which are my favorite.    And, no, I still haven't had lunch there.

This is my least favorite of the HDs in my sphere of travel. The whole place is sketchy. The parking lot is kind of awful. The store is often out of stock and but at least it's cleaner than the parking lot...  The staff is helpful and so points for that. Last time I went, I walked out empty handed since they were sold out of the one thing I really needed.   HD HQ needs to rehab this store soon.

Seriously, I was here for maybe 45 minutes and scored maybe a dozen christmas presents, all under $20.  The prices were definitely comparable to what I've seen around town (including some of the big box stores).    The staff was very knowledgeable and patient.  Shout out to the young woman who was helping the set of grandparents pick out a remote controlled car for their grandson. How you dealt with their bickering was model of patience.   Plus I'm pretty sure they assemble many of the toys they sell, not just the bikes...but that might be for an added fee.

Hey look it's one of those NOLA spots that I can't believe I haven't reviewed yet.  So let's get the Farmer's Market part out of the way. I WISH. There hasn't been a real farmer's market here in decades. This is where we used to come by pumpkins at Halloween and get the super cheap produce from truck farms in Mississippi. No more. It's all groceries and tourist junk.  I was pleased to see that the infrastructure of the market was looking better. Working fans, bathrooms, tables and chairs are welcome. But all the produce and vegetable stalls have been replaced by outdoor cafes and stores.  It's a good place to people watch and y'know buy some cheap souvenirs. There are some people here making handcrafted items rather than all cheap imports though. Find the guy doing stained glass; I love his work.  In HS when we came here to buy cheap sunglasses we always differentiated between the Farmers Market and the Flea Market. I guess it's all flea now.

Let's get the real reason to stop and this small gas station... it regularly has the cheapest prices in the area. The pumps are tight and if you're driving a large vehicle be prepared to maneuver. The pumps are also fast. No waiting forever to fill up. As for safety, it's decently lit and it always has folks around, again, because it's cheap.   I've never actually been in the store. I just gas and go.

If you grew up along the gulf coast, fried shrimp can be your comfort food and after a long week last week, I needed some comfort... so I met up with a friend at this location of the local Mr. Ed's chain.  I hadn't been inside since this was a PeiWei and they did a beautiful renovation. The space doesn't feel like a chain and it's nicely decorated. Be warned the tables are close but more seating meant no wait for me on Friday so that's all good.   I had my fried shrimp platter with fries and an old fashioned. My friend had a cup of gumbo and a dinner special, smothered cabbage and a porkchop. My old fashioned was perfect and not too sweet. My dinner was enough for 2 meals. And my friend loved his meal too. I just wish they had a small salad so I could have pretended to be healthy. Oh well.  Service was prompt and the bartender was hustling with all the drink specials. Parking can be problematic since there are so many businesses using the same lot but spots turnover quickly.

I was in dire need of lunch and this truck came to my rescue. A veggie burger was just what I wanted. There version was interesting in that it was a bit... chunky, like whole edamame chunky. And really tasty. I could have lived without the plastic cheese but for $8 my combo included the burger, fries and a canned drink. Great deal!  The service was super quick too. I'll have to try the falafel next time.  LOVE their logo!

The staff was great, really. The space? It looked like it needed a good scrubbing.  The grilled shrimp bun had good shrimp but the lettuce was completely wilted and needed to be pitched rather than served.  They were quick and the food was filling but with so many other good choices around...

Claim to fame? I've attended just about every year since ~maybe~ 1974.    Some years I eat myself sick; some years I roast my flesh; every year I sit strategically  between 2 stages for an instant live mashup.

I am not a beer person BUT I attended a birthday party here. The space is great. Comfy and interesting... love the old car bench seats which made me feel like I was sitting on someone's porch.   There's beaucoup beer and other liquor items for sale as well as a cooler if you're in need of a cider instead of one of their dozen or so beers on draft.   Love that there is a parking lot in back that's well lit. Staff is great and helpful.

Decided to give the new place a try a month or so ago for a basic pedicure. I don't need fancy, just clean and attentive. So Jades gets high marks for both.  Since this was previously a dress shop, all the nail equipment is new and fresh. There are 4 steps up to the main part of the salon (and the original house that this was converted from) so don't let the sidewalk level front door fool you. I liked that the chairs are sort of in an alcove so it feels private.  The salon is very quiet which is a great break from the TVs and chatter and chaos at many other places. But maybe it was too quiet for me? I think I needed some low new age music or something.   Loved their color selection and the techs were great.

As a non-quarter denizen, you might wonder why I have occasion to go to Cabrini Park, but once a year the French Quarter Resident's association hosts a Mother's Day concert here with a big band that my Mom loves.  So off and on for the past bunch of years, we're there.  It is a big park (maybe 1/2 of a city block) and that gives the younger kids plenty of room to run around and play.  They've planted more trees in some sections in recent years so hopefully the shade quotient will be raised eventually.  The pavilion is spacious (but I've never sat under it as that's where the band plays).   Minus 1 star because of the owners who refuse to pickup after their dogs, even though their are bags provided by the park. Eww.

Still order at the counter (just like when it was Il Posto) which is great for not splitting a bill. The menu is an interesting mix of Vietnamese and breakfast foods and other sandwiches. The restaurant looks fresh and clean despite having purchased all the furnishings from its predecessor.   I ordered a tuna and avocado salad and tofu spring rolls. Unexpectedly the tuna was more like a traditional flaked tuna salad rather than tuna steak. It was very tasty and filling (especially for the price) but not what I thought I would be getting. The spring rolls were delicious with well seasoned tofu and the peanut sauce had a nice heat.  I do like that your food is brought to you (via a numbered flag system) which is an improvement. If you choose to sit in the back patio, they won't bring hot soup out there. Understandable.   Definitely a great new spot in the neighborhood.

I've been intrigued by this store since they opened and then they moved a few blocks from my house. I had been stalking some cast iron on their Etsy account and finally stopped by last rainy Saturday.  The shop is 1/2 a shotgun so there are steps and it is chockful of house decor and kitchenwares in addition to pots and pans. I think they may have the bamboo tray that my grandmother used to use to carry lunches out to her porch, as well as baking pans and utensils and whatnot.  I ended up purchasing a glass juicer and a cast iron sauce pot. And I was eyeing one of the giant magnalite pots...   One staff person and she was super nice. Great addition to the neighborhood!

Pandemic delivery review: I read about this new spot near work and since there were only a few of us on site on a slow Friday, I asked around about who wanted potatoes for lunch!   We ordered 3 baked potatoes, 2 orders of fries and 1 shrimp/fries via a delivery app. WOW! This was a ton of food. The shrimp and fries were plentiful for the price. The baked potatoes were HUGE! I got a seafood potato and a broccoli & cheese (to save for later). I must have gotten 4 or 5 meals out of these. The sauce was great... a mix of melted cheese and cheese sauce. The seafood one had a lot of fried shrimp and the other had tons of broccoli. The french fries were more meh. My coworker loved the bbq sauce but wished it was on the side and that there was more of it. Maybe that's something that would work out better on site?   Communication was good and the transaction was easypeasy.  Will definitely order again.

The daiquiris are good, as are the fries... I am not nor will ever be a wings person. So decide for yourself on that one, BUT during crawfish season they offer crawfish out front at picnic tables from noon until ???  The crawfish were tasty and affordable; you can purchase by the pound to stay or go and they come with the fixings, garlic, potatoes, corn and mushrooms. The crawfish are well spiced and flavorful. They are not super spicy but by the time I inhaled 3 pounds (that's a platter with veg), I definitely could feel the lip burn.  Staff is great and the space is small but gets the job done.

This is the most adorable coffee shop conversion ever. I mean the roof is pretty and the ceilings are awesome. The outside is adorable. The furniture is comfy. Oh yeah, and the tea and food is yummy.  I know you're supposed to go to coffee shops because of artisanal coffee or whatever, but I'm not a coffee drinker. So I appreciate that they pay some attention to tea. And the baked goods and food is very tasty.  If I lived in this neighborhood, I'd probably be here everyday.

If you are a tourist in New Orleans, this is the St. Louis cemetery that the busses drop you off at. No.1 is limited access now (it's the one by the FQ). No.2 is currently closed unless you are visiting a loved one or having a funeral because the tourist crowds were too much for the small space. No.3? It is huge. And it's where my Dad is.   My family bought a plot here in the 1880s. So when I go visit my Dad now, I can also say hello to a few generations of family. One of the benefits of this cemetery is that you are allowed to drive in which is really helpful when Mom wants to visit Dad. Luckily we are along one of the main roads near the front.    The grounds are well kept and there are trash cans and some faucets (aka hose pipes) scattered around if you need water for your flowers/vases. There are no bathrooms.   Fun fact: there is still space available if this is where you or a loved one would like to spend eternity. Plus I found out the open space next to my family's tomb was sold in the 1880s but never used so we will probably always have a nice grassy sideyard.  Tourists were mostly respectful since we were clearly family members.

Here's the thing about the TP. Everyone loves to pick on it but then I go read papers in other cities and I realize how lucky we are to have it.  It has it's issues (get it, Ha!) but I think it is still solid.  The online site (nola.com) is more likely to have typos and errors as they rush to get the news out, but most of these are corrected by the time they print.
