Pandemic Review: Orleans Shoe Company aka Good Feet has a new space on Magazine St. I tried to go to the old location (soon to be closing) around a month ago but found it closed; but maybe it should have been open? Anyway that location will be closed soon and this locations has 2x the space.  I can't even with normal shoes after this year so I was looking for baby feet size Birk clogs. And they actually had a pair! Yea. And the sales person was super nice and not pushy which is what I've always found with this shop.  Masks are worn by the staff and required of the shoppers and there is actually some room to move around so social distancing is actually possible.

I met some cousins for lunch here the week before Thanksgiving. Loved that it was counter service... no pesky dividing of the bill. And my falafel sammich was HUGE and tasty.   My cousins got gyro and a falafel plate (which doesn't seem to be included on the online menu). Everyone loved their food. Service was good and the bread was amazing. And they had good quality iced tea which is becoming a rarity these days.   Decor is minimal and make sure to park legally.

While some nail salons feel like chaos unleashed, Jade's feels like serenity. It is mostly quiet with some light music. The patrons mostly read, bliss out or look at their phones. The techs do chat with each other but in hushed tones and no hollering across the salon.  I've been for pedicures mostly but did recently get a basic manicure (buff nail only). I've always had excellent care with attention to detail.  The whole space is very clean and well kept up. The techs have been fully masked every time I've been since the pandemic and I've been masked as well. Although not everyone is. Grrrr.

I've been aware of this small but well curated grocery/sammich shop. But I'd never stopped in until last week. What tempted me? Their cannoli king cake, of course!  First let's talk about the king cake. It is a bit pricey, but so worth it. The dough is somewhere between pate de choux and brioche. And the cream... delicious and rich. So while the cake looks amazingly decadent, it isn't too sweet. The cake isn't huge but it's so rich that I shared it with my parents, their neighbors, and a couple of my brothers. UHmazing  I also purchased some fancy cheeses, bread and cookies while I was there. They have prepared foods in their freezers/coolers. And they make sandwiches (and advertise their muffulettas). I did get some yummy cheese spread (because I need all the cheeses) but did not order a sandwich.  Some shelves seemed sparse so maybe they only get some supplies in sporadically or in advance of St. Joseph's day.

It's been a while since I used Delta World, but I would go back to them for tires...which hopefully I won't need for a bit.  They've always treated me in a professional manner and my car has been ready as promised.  I ended up at the Veteran's store one time and I much prefer the downtown location.

Pandemic review: I've been watching pics from the gorgeous shop for over a year. And finally on Saturday, I stopped in.   OK. So I'm not a coffee person, and many coffee shops do not offer much in the way of tea. Drink Beauty does have a few tea selections as well as a matcha latte btw.   But since Drink Beauty is participating in a charity drop off and I had ordered some items that did not work for me but were on the wish list for Covenant House, I packaged said items up and dropped them off on Saturday morning. AND I scored a hot chocolate (surprise!) for my efforts. I thought the free beverage only applied to a small coffee. The hot chocolate was great and I will be back just for that!  Also they have a fun machine where you can make your own foam art and I am stupidly in love with it.  Staff was masked and of course I was too. You can pay with cash or card. Parking is on the street.

I've been helping brother #4 shop for furniture for his new condo and I suggested we stop in here. He was hesitant as he assumed that all the furniture was really high priced. But they do have excellent sales here and if you can find a good salesperson, you are good to go.  Liz M is right this store has the largest selection of anyplace else in the city and you can get really lost in the store (download a compass app to orient yourself). We walked the entire store to see the selection of sofas since our main limitation was size rather than style or color.   Our sales person was very patient and nice. But that is not always the case, I have had sales people who were neither. And sale weekends can be awful...but when you consider the volume of people in the store...  I've never had a problem with delivery but then again I usually just pick up from them at my convenience.

I first discovered this local designer at Jazz Fest many years ago when he only had a shop on the northshore. I was pleased to discover that he now has a shop on Magazine in addition to the one in the French Quarter.  His designs reflect a south Louisiana aesthetic and are super fun and affordable.   This shop is spacious and the jewelry is easy to view in the various cases. The person working over the weekend was fun to chat with and knew a lot about the items in the shop.

I have about 5 or 6 groceries in my monthly rotation and this is one of them. It is a small store but it has ALL the essentials. And I can find instant cream of wheat here which I don't see in other shops.  What brings this to 5 stars? The seafood market. It is not inexpensive but they are careful with their refrigeration and I consistently find good quality fish, crab and shrimp here. The manager is super nice and I've talked to her about specialty orders but haven't pulled that trigger yet.  The takeout food is good to great. And they usually have a variety of items. It can get pretty crazy just before a big holiday.   Their produce is good and the store is always well stocked.  There is plenty of parking too!

My favorite Langenstein's story:  I'm in line behind a little old lady who looked to be about 90.  The cashier starts hollering at her (deafness not rudeness), "Mrs. A you don't have to buy any cigarettes.  You bought them yesterday."  Now that is service.  Great prepared foods, some specialty items that can be hard to find (like almond paste).

Woo Office Products...OK they're kind of boring but necessary. This store is small but has the essentials. And sometimes you can find someone to help who may know what he or she is doing. Bonus that you can buy a book of stamps with no mark up. Although the stamps are locked up in safe (or something) so a manager has to come retrieve them for you.  There is a parking lot and also an NOPD officer since the bar/daiquiri shop around the corner has had...issues, let's say.  Office Depot opened up this tiny store so that it comes up as the closest delivery location to the convention center. They make most of their money delivering to out-of-towners so us stop by shoppers are not their bread & butter.

Pandemic review: I was leaving my job (yes actually onsite!) and realized I was starving an in no mood to prepare my own food. And I remembered I had seen a yummy sandwich on the Iacovone website. So I called it up on my phone and somehow ended up in Postmates (although they do Waitr) as well.   Ordered my items (and sides) and then drove over to their storefront. And it is just a storefront. This is a takeaway spot so they are setup to give you the goods. My food was ready and delicious. For some reason PM wouldn't let me tip on pickup (and that's not cool so I probably won't use them again... of course it could have been operator error). So I put some cash on the table.  I had the shrimp boil panini and the next day I ate my winter caprese. Both were delicious. And let me tell you, if you are a beets fan get that caprese. UH-mazing. I got the creole cole slaw and the quinoa salad as sides. The cole slaw was fine; really I'm not that into cabbage anyway. But the quinoa was great.   This yummy spot is definitely going into my rotation.

I ordered some material for my HouseFloat through the Mardi Gras Spot and pickup was through the Plush Appeal Warehouse. Which was a little confusing... you call a number on the front door of the warehouse side, but no one answered. So I went back across to the retail store and they got someone to come answer the front door. Then I wandered through the building with them and came out to the warehouse.   The warehouse is HUGE and essentially outside so some staff was not masked but they were mostly far away so not too concerning. I signed my papers and picked up my supplies and headed out.  I think they aren't really setup for an order as small as mine but 2021 carnival being what it is, they were happy to oblige.   Definitely would use them again.

Met some friends here after work one day a few weeks ago, and while I was sure I had been here before, maybe not. This is a great neighborhood bar that just happens to be at the edge of the FQ.   They have a bunch of beers available for the beer folks, then they have some fancy liquors for those folks, and then they just have regular old drinks for the rest of us. The bartender was friendly but also kept himself busy with bar things. There is an art to being both available but also keep working.  He handled the drunkypants tourists well and made sure folks were masking up as they entered the bar or moved around.  Good prices too!

Pandemic review: I was looking for some place open for takeout on Sunday morning on Mother's Day. A friend gets take out from La Madeleine pretty often and said that the contactless system was pretty good. Welp. Not on Sunday.   Ordering was easy and their website is very easy to use and customize what you want. And at the moment it also includes some basic groceries, like milk and fruit which is great.  When I arrived to pick up my order, the emailed instructions said just call from your car and someone would bring it out. I called 10x. Out of those 10, I was immediately disconnect 6 or 7 times. On the 3 or 4 times I was able to get into the menu to let them know I was outside, I was disconnect every time before I got to that point. So I went inside (defeating the whole contactless thing), and was told that their phone was acting up. Of course, the customer before me was unmasked and clueless. The staff was all wearing masks and were friendly.   My order was large and we were only missing a single side item which of course I didn't notice until I got to my parents' house.   An even bigger problem with this system (besides it breaking down), is that there was no way to tip while ordering. So the staff of the restaurant who are potentially exposing themselves could be doing so for the less than minimum wage that is legal here. And you know most folks do not even realize that a tip should be offered.

10 years later and a 3rd review. I've been getting my tires from DWT for my last 3 cars. They've also done some mechanic work for me. AND fixed so many stupid tires.  I've always found them to be professional and their prices comparable.  The waiting room is comfortable... until the old dude next to you decides to play candy crush (or whatever) at full volume. Luckily they are across the street from the Broad Whole Foods so you can always go wait over there.  Good product, good communication, fair prices. What else could I ask for?

This truck is in regular rotation downtown at the medical centers and I never even looked at the menu because Korean food is known to be super meaty. But what did I find? Tofu katsu (see my pic) and for $8 I got 3 nice slices of deep fried tofu (don't @ me and my love for the fried) + rice + 2 veggie dumplings + salad + small amount of kimchee. Delicious.  Definitely going to consider them again in the future. Find out where they'll be following their FB, but they are usually at LSUHSC or Tulane Med Wednesdays and Tuesdays.

Pandemic update: I was walking in my neighborhood recently and I was hungry so I decided to stop in for a banh mi.  Excellent decision on my part.   Masks are required, of course. (Thank goodness for our state mandate). And the staff was masked obviously. While the same number of tables were in the space, many were marked do not use to allow for social distancing. I was getting take out so no big.  My tofu banh mi was delicious and hit the spot. And was very inexpensive. Yummy all the way around.

The staff was a bit confused by our request...my Mom wanted a not-too-old-looking grandmother of the bride dress. Eventually we found a salesperson who seemed to get it...but mostly I pulled dresses that I thought my Mom would want to try on.   And we finally found the dress. It was really in the bridesmaid section I think, but it was a grecian style in a good color and in her size off the rack. Good thing to because when we asked about another color the turn around time was over 3 months. So no matching shrug that would come in sometime in August.  The price point was fine. The help was OK. The styling was all over the map. The parking lot was a pain...or maybe that was just all the jumbotron SUVs in the lot.

I've used Delta World on and off since I bought my very first new car in the early 90s.  This week they rebuilt the front end of our little Katrina truck.  It runs like a new car which is pretty good for a vehicle we bought used with 75K miles on it.  They communicate well and are reasonably priced.

I met up with a few friends on a recent Friday night for drinks and snacks in the lovely outdoor space that is used by the Bower, Claret and Birdy's. Claret has not yet reopened but my understanding is that it will reopen eventually.  Drinks were lovely. HH prices were great! Snacks were tasty and varied. Service was very good. Ambiance is amazing as always. BUT whew when that sun was setting, I thought I was going to boil. And there was a guy at a nearby table in jeans and cowboy boots. I felt bad for him.   There is a breeze but definitely dress for the hot and humid weather.

As a non-coffee drinker, I just want a decent cup of tea sometimes or if it's warm a giant iced tea to get me through the day. So imagine how disappointing it is when your iced tea tastes like coffee. C'mon. This is what you do. Brew coffee & tea and you can't even keep things separate. So completely annoying.  I should have taken a sip before I left the store and then handed it back to the counter guy.

The nieces and I passed by the first week it was open to sample some delicious pastries.   It felt like they were still pulling themselves together and the day I went there were not specials just the basics. We had creampuffs with chocolate creme and an almond crescent with vanilla creme. Both were delicious.   Can't wait to go back when they are more settled to sample more.

A hip looking (but CLEAN) coffee shop in the Marigny.  I'm not a coffee drinker but their tea selection was good and tasty.  Plus I got to try mochi (ice cream w/ rice something around it).  Very delicious  If it was in my 'hood I would be here at least once a week.

It had been years since I last ate here, so I was pleased when this was the choice for a working lunch earlier this week. The menu covers all the bases from paninis to flat bread pizza to salads, etc. The staff is lovely.  Order at the counter, take your number and wait for your food to be delivered which will be pretty darn quick. There is also some outside seating in a courtyard if the weather is agreeable.  And the views are stupendous, especially since we could see a water spout out over the lake from the huge plate glass windows. I was pleased to see there was an exterior door so that you don't have to go through the museum. It's over near the Big Lake side of the museum, or to the right as you face the front steps.  I got the spinach salad with blue cheese and grapes (1/2 size) and it was huge plus I got a cup of the daily soup which was curry cauliflower. Great curry flavor but the soup was really thin.   Definitely a great spot to get a quick beverage (I think they advertise beer & wine but I saw bottles of booze behind the counter) and a lovely light meal.

OK. So I am lame. I have been invited to house parties near the festival area for years, but I've never gone. This year with the Sunday closers being Pat Benatar followed by the B-52s. Yep I'm there.  Small pet peeve. There is no way to buy advance tickets locally without all the ticketmaster fees so my $20 advance ticket instantly became a $31 & change one.  Wait to pay the $25 in cash a the door and risk a line...  Lots of food options and drink options. I enjoyed my frozen sangria and I should have made it back to whatever bar/restaurant was offering spooky batched cocktails.   My favorite moment outside of the headliners was the Chee Weez singing Don't Stop Believing... and changing the lyric from "born in South Detroit" to "born in Westwego" which doesn't really scan but was funny.   The shuttle from Oakwood was super easy and the staff was really nice!

Had a mini-shopping-palooza today and hit a few of the clothing consignment shops (Prima Donna, Swap, Encore, and On the Other Hand) uptown in search of a formal gown that would fit my short, curvy self.  So I feel confident in my comparisons.  Swap is a newer store in the University Section and seems to cater mostly to the college crowd. That said there were some cute shoes, jackets, etc in mostly nicer mall brands (J. Crew, Banana Republic, Jessica Simpson).  The prices were good and the shop was well organized.  It was also the smallest of the four stores I went to, but that was OK since I was getting overwhelmed by volume, so it was nice to have some actual breathing room.

The best place to buy fresh fruit & vegetables, artisan prepared foods, seafood, and all sorts of other stuff (depending on the season).  I never get to the Tuesday mid-day market at Uptown Square (curse work and my need for a paycheck).  I mostly hit the Saturday market on Girod.  There is also a Thursday evening market at the American Can Company.  Good stuff!

Cute clothes with a definite vintage flair. The store also has great locally made jewelry pieces and accessories.   This another well curated collection of items in a small store. The stock rotates often and the sales are very good. Since the clothes are not really my style, I stop in more often to peruse their accessories and jewelry which are well-priced and unique.  The staff has always been extremely helpful and offer really good suggestions.

Gallier Hall used to be city hall and it's a lovely building. I've been to a private party here and to a performance in a small theater that is on site.  The architecture is impressive and the building is surprisingly well kept up.  Out front on St. Charles Avenue is where city officials greet the carnival monarchs. So it's a pretty great place to be during the season.

Yes I'm the dummy who shows up at the airport hungry, every SINGLE time. I'm rushing around too much and don't get hungry until I get through security and can breathe. Then I'm waiting for my flight and grumbly grumbly tummy.  I was excited to see a new option on the SW concourse AND it didn't have a line on this very busy Saturday morning. I got a HUGE and yummy breakfast burrito. Yes it was airport prices but what are you gonna do.  The staff was quick and friendly and I was able to nosh on my burrito through lunch it was so big.   I'll have to try their non-morning offerings but so far I'm a fan.

Orient Expressed is one of those places that I hit up every few months for gift ideas. You never know what sort of wacky items you might find (reusable ice cubes shaped like high heels or a big banana leaf serving plate).  Make sure to check out (the very messy) clearance room in the back of building two.  On a recent visit, I had the most helpful sales person ever.  She pointed out sales on the kids' clothes that weren't marked yet.  And pulled items for me and everything, so plus 1 star for them.  Still I would say about 1 in 3 times I am totally ignored by the sales people (and they are definitely not busy with other customers.)

This is still my go to salon.  I cheat & go to other spots but always end up returning. The prices are a bit higher then some other places but the quality and location make it worth it.  The staff always remembers my name and asks after the family that I've brought in over the years. Good selection of colors and styles. And the decor is restful too.  Tipping is cash only.

I was sorry to see that the tea place didn't make it, but this spot also has a good tea selection PLUS y'know biscuits.  I had the delicious waffles with brie & blueberries and they were yummy. But seriously the standout was the side of fruit salad. It was really the best fruit salad I've ever had at restaurant; it had apples and berries and all sorts of fresh items.  I can't wait to get back over there.

hmmm where to start...  The space is beautiful and light and clean. The bar is inviting and the space includes sound dampening panels so actual conversation is possible. The music (bartender's choice I think) is eclectic and fun.   The upstairs art gallery is spacious and the balconies are a great traditional addition. The side yard is like an upscale picnic area...in really good way. All interior spaces are no smoking!  The food is yummy. I've sampled a variety of things and found everything a good value and delicious.   The drinks. Oh my. The drinks. Um Bulleit Old fashioneds for $7 that are perfectly mixed. Yes please. I will unfortunately drink them all.  Friday nights after work seem to be the busiest time...although I hear lunches are popular too.   The neighborhood is in transition so be careful, but you already knew that I'm sure.

I've been putting off writing this review.  I really want to like Cafe Granada more than I do.  I've been a few times over the last couple of years and have never had a great meal.    My dinner on Sunday was probably the best food I've had there but the service was...odd.  Again, having a hard time explaining w/o getting myself in hot water.  Part of the oddity was caused by confusion generated by my dining companions (who may or may not be older family members), they found the menu & the tapas concept difficult.  But the waitress did nothing to help ease their minds.  And got several items wrong by not asking for clarifications or being oblivious.  White & red sangria are not easily confused, right?    So because the food was good and we were a slightly difficult table, I might have still given them 4 stars, except.  The last time I ate at here I ordered the vegetarian paella and it was nothing but mushrooms and what appeared to be a bag of frozen mixed vegetables.  Sigh.  I won't say no the next time folks want to eat here.  And I will hope for better.

I'm surprised that this only has 1 review and it's bad. We had a storage unit here for almost 6 years.  E stored many of his tools and work stuff in one of their air conditioned units (bonus that it's in a pre-civil war warehouse).  The internal structure they created for individual units kept everything nice & safe.  Like most storage units, the lighting isn't optimum, so bring a flashlight to hunt in the corners.  The folks were always nice and accommodating...although if you were 1 day late with the rent check, they did pad lock your unit, but I can't really fault them for that.  We only stopped using them when we moved & built the garage.

Oh look more festival food.  The fry bar makes french fries...super yummy french fries (with the skin still on - yum) and they add interesting flavors.   Check them out at festivals about town (like the Freret Street fest & the Arts Market where I have sampled their wares).  Now, some of the flavors are not really up my alley...the garlic fries will keep the vampires away for you for days, for instance, but that might really appeal to someone who is a super-garlic person.  They use really good quality ingredients plus who doesn't like to eat fancy fries.

Since I'm not generally in this store's demographic, the staff mostly just ignores me. But that's OK with me. I'm usually in this shop to peruse the accessories and selection of local tshirts.  I haven't shopped for actual jeans here in years since that didn't go well the last time I tried.   On the other hand, they do have lots of the jean brands that folks in the know want to buy. (I mostly just want jeans that actually fit and aren't overly embellished.) So for a large selection of styles take a gander. And maybe you'll hit the jackpot of style and fit.

I've never worn glasses, but I've reached the age where eye wear is becoming a necessity.  And thus begins my saga...  I saw an ophthalmologist and he wrote me a prescription which I brought to St. Charles Vision  The woman who helped me pick my glasses was really nice, stayed within my price point and helped me find cute frames.  The lens were OMG expensive, but my friends who have worn glasses for years said that the price was within acceptable limits.    Then I picked up my glasses and they made me nauseous and my computer screen was blurry...so back I went.  They were really nice and the tech said that she thought my prescription must be wrong by my description.  For no additional charge, they retested my eyes. Gave me a new prescription. I ordered new lenses (same frames).  When I picked those up, they weren't what the optometrist and I had discussed so I left them with the staff.  There seemed to have been a data entry-type error when they were ordered.  The next day the store manager (Chris who is great) called and I went back in for a few measurements and we ordered a 3rd set of lenses.  And yesterday, low and behold I have glasses. While getting the glasses right took awhile, the staff was really helpful and friendly and I paid no additional charges after the initial one.  Let's hope for fewer headaches and a greater ability to read comic books.

Seriously, I hate all the parking lots along 17th street. You can pull into the post office parking lot, but if you want to drop a letter in the mailbox? Pull back out on to 17th and then go to the next cut through.  So annoying.  Oh and the area floods. So when I dropped off my taxes at 8:30 pm tonight, the cut through with the mailboxes? Still flooded from the rains this morning.  Bleh.

Sorry to be the crankypants person. But their black iced tea was completely undrinkable. I paid $2.50 for concentrate that tasted AWFUL. Why can't shops just brew a good tea? BLAH. I was annoyed all day on Saturday. Also when they called out my order they said Southern Tea unsweetened...which I guessed was me. Maybe this concentrate was designed to be hidden behind a copious amount of sugar/   For my sandwich I got the croissant with egg and cheese...and tomato jam? I nixed the bacon and asked for avocado instead. Nope. No substitutions. OK fine. But I barely got any cheese and I have tomato jam in my fridge... if there was any on this sandwich it was a thin smear that I couldn't taste. AND my fluffy croissant was panini pressed. Isn't the whole point of a croissant sandwich is to enjoy the airy pastry? Denied.   The space is gorgeous. Since I used to live around the corner, I know what this shotgun home used to look like. The transformation is astonishing. The outdoor space is lovely. The staff was moving quickly as the crowds increased on a Saturday morning. I just won't be one of them again.
Catch was sort of "meh" when I went back around Easter.  But really it's pointless to go on since it's CLOSED.

Chaos is a fun parade with lots of local satire. The floats are fun but often zip by to quickly to allow you to fully read/digest the joke. So look out for card decks to explain all the floats. My mom was gleeful to get a pack last night.  I do feel bad for Chaos sometimes. While it's satirical, it's considered second to Krewe D'Etat. It's sandwiched between the traditional Babylon and the mad-popular Muses and so I think they get short changed.  It's a good parade with good bands and, last night, in my area, they were generous with throws.

I appreciate that I can drink in the back and because that's technically the dining room...no smoking! But I do love the atmosphere of the front bar.  Drinks are fine, just don't expect fancy pants ones.  Staff is friendly and snarky (a personal favorite combination).  LOVE the fried green bean snack as an alternative to straight up fries.

This is one of those places that I've heard about for years, but never actually stepped foot in. So I wasn't sure what I was expecting.  Yep, it's creepy with so many vintage mannequins looking like they want to come alive and zombify you to join them. (Maybe that's just me though.) The costumes are fabulous and the photos are amazing.  BUT the entire collection is starting to crumble. Long term the heavier beaded dresses should not be hanging on mannequins and you can see where the fabric is starting to give. I hope it gets some attention before it's too late.  Also shout out to Lindsay for her commentary while we were touring the space and to Michelle who just giggled the whole time at whatever we said.  Good times.

What a beautiful space! I attended a wedding here over the weekend and it was really lovely.  My friends went ahead and rented all the rooms available (according to the website: the Fulton, Lafayette & Orleans + the balcony).  The out of town guests were amazed by the space. Even though it was on the 2nd floor there was an elevator.  The entranceway is a lovely wide staircase with marble floors.  This the space above Ernst Cafe and if there is a band downstairs, you can hear them...so make sure your music is louder.

I stopped in for drinks for my birthday twin in January. I LOVED their menu. And my choice of bourbon + their old fashioned was delish! The bartender was personable and checked back to make sure my drink was too my liking. May I reiterate that their brown liquor list is awesome. I  The only food I tried was their popcorn and, yes, it was really crack-like.  Definitely a space I hope to return to soon and sample some of their yummy eats.

Cafe Granada was Mom's choice for a Mother's Day lunch. And it was lovely. The staff was on point with fresh bread and waters and offering suggestions and descriptions of the dishes. My family shared a large assortment of tapas (and we polished off almost all of it!)  Highlights were the ceviche of the day: Redfish with Mango & Mint, the grapefruit salad, and the brie with fig marmalade.   Also yummy were the fabada, the potatoes, the salmon salad with anchovies (my Mom loved it), the mussels and the shrimp and garlic sauce.   Definitely much improved since my last visit. I won't wait so long until next time.

In only in its 2nd year, the Roadfood festival gets high marks for organization and, of course, great food!  I enjoyed local favorites (shrimp remoluade poboy & crawfish enchiladas) but also got to sample Maine seafood chowder - those Maine folks were LOVING the weather this weekend.  I was disappointed in the shrimp uggie (2 shrimp & some mini-bits of potato?); I know Ugelisich's is closed but c'mon charge more & don't be so stingy.  Most items were anywhere from a dollar (Rouse's mini-muffalettas) to around $7 (Dunbar's fried fish & fries).   You have until 6 tonight...or you have to wait until next year.  Get out there!

Ah, Galatoire's.  If anything ever changed here, I think I would cry.  I hadn't been for awhile, so I don't have a regular waiter.  But that was OK.  We arrived early enough on a Sunday evening to be seated right away. Dinner was lovely with nothing rushed.    I forwent the crabmeat sardou for the crabmeat au gratin.  yum, yum, yum.  I was even good & ordered a salad.  Cocktails were lovely & the caramel custard dessert may be better than my mother's.  Please don't let her know I said that.

Love the patio (especially the swings) and it's usually a bit less smokey than the inside bar. I know...I know...don't complain about smoking at a cigar bar.  On the other hand, the inside bar has some awesome exhaust fans so that unless someone is stogie-ing it up right next to you, it's really not too bad.  I've always had  quick, friendly and courteous service.  And the fact that Taceaux Loceaux parks out front on Saturday nights. Bonus!

Just had a lovely lunch at the new location on Prytania near Touro.  Because the weather is gorgeous, we sat on the porch. There is also deck seating and a parking lot on the side street...including a spot for folks picking up to go orders.  The menu seems a little broader than most locations, about a dozen pasta dishes and dessert shots (mmm key lime mousse).  But seriously the inside is like eating in a fancy pants restaurant and the bar looks gorgeous.  I may have to hit this place up again for happy hour.

I've been to the joy for a variety of events... movies, parties with stage shows, live music. It's a fun venue that's been restored attractively.  Sometimes the floor is open; sometimes they have seating setup. And one time, it was bring your own chair... that was odd.  The staff is friendly and bathrooms are mostly clean.  There are a couple of bars around and the prices and quality of drinks have varied depending on the event and who was at the bar.   Great place to see a show in a more intimate setting and if the floor is standing only, you can always rest your feet by heading upstairs, if it's open. Also there's often a food truck parked outside for your snacking needs.

Belladonna has a fabulous gift shop and selection of retail items.  For spa treatments though it's OK.  I understand other reviewers' criticisms.    The rooms do not have enough privacy so you feel like someone is going to bust in the door at any moment.  But for the biggest problem is the turnover rate of their masseuses.  If you get a good person and you try to see them again in a month or two, they are never still employed by Belladonna.    I've not done a pedicure here, only a manicure that was included in the price of a spa day.  And my manicurist was grumpy, so no points there.  Lastly I had my makeup done once (again as part of a spa day GC).  My makeup was done around noon on a weekday but the makeup artist gave me an evening super heavy look that I would never wear, even after I told her I go for a more natural look.  I just went home and wiped it all off.

I shop hear a lot....really y'all too often. It has a nice selection of stores: Home Depot to Ulta. It has some decent spots to eat, the new Theo's to Nacho Mama's and a bunch of chains. It has a daiquiri shop so you can drink & shop if necessary.  It's close to my parents' house so I'm in the neighborhood pretty often. So convenient for me (and really most of Uptown NOLA since it's just upriver).   The parking lot is sort of a jigsaw puzzle but it has multiple entrances/exits with lights so you don't have to fight Clearview too hard. The fitness center is INSANELY popular so parking near it can be a pain.   I just wish the owners kept up the space better. On rainy days, you'll see plastic bins collecting rain water inside the stores. The parking lot & sidewalks are often dirty/littered. Maintenance, it's important.

Solid neighborhood bar. I like that I can usually find a table in the back (by the food) to avoid the cigarette smoke.  Drinks are well priced and basic, but the wine selection is actually pretty good and the bottles that are on special are particularly well priced.

I'm just going to go ahead and say, yes, to this new sushi joint. The staff was great (I got takeout) and the atmosphere is small but inviting. The menu has some basics and some more unusual items... bro4 wants to try the jellyfish salad but they were out last time he was there; that might be too adventurous for me.  The tuna was great and I wish I had noticed that they have a pickled radish roll on the veggie roll menu. I love those. My crab naruto was a little heavy on the mayo for me but that might mean it's perfect for you.  I will definitely be back to dine in and try to drag the parents along.

I stopped in for lunch one Saturday while running around in #themetrys because one of my friends LOVES this place. Do not let the location adjacent to a gas station deter you. The food is tasty. I got a grilled shrimp banh mi which was delicious with perfectly cooked shrimp. I am the weirdo that loves tofu but they don't carry it. Their veggie sandwich is a portobello banh mi which I'll have to give a try on another day. I saw a man enjoying one while I waited for a take out and it looked delicious. I also splurged on some crab rangoon which were very good, a little bit spicy, and a huge order for the price. I dropped off some with my parents so they could share the goodness.   The seating is outside on the patio or a few counter seats so the space is really for a quick meal or takeout. The staff was super friendly and patient.   You know that this spot has a good local rep, if even my mom has passed by for lunch! Although she was sure to tell me that it was gas station adjacent and not IN the gas station. This is a very important distinction to her.   Definitely will pass back by to try more of the menu.

I checked out this sushi joint because it was the 2nd closest to my brother's house (the closest served me fish the wrong color last time) and because Naomi P recommended it.  Naomi did not steer me wrong. The location is a bit difficult but they do have 2 reserved parking spots in front of the restaurant.  I tried a variety of rolls and everything was top notch.  The little nieces enjoyed the shrimp fried rice and I even got them to eat some of the cooked rolls.  My cucumber salad was delish and the noodle salad was also tasty...and not as mayonaissey as it is other places.  The server was also great to the little ones, even making them custom starter chopsticks.  The rainbow roll was smaller (and didn't use spicy crab) then I've had in other places, but the fish was beautifully interwoven.  Definitely worth checking out.

Pontchartrain is another small krewe which runs the first weekend of Mardi Gras.  I like that they often have the folks on the street guess the title of the floats...not that most folks notice.  And I like their fishy mascot.  Unfortunately, I missed most of the parade this year because of a small incident between my bike and some dude with a ladder.  It is not cool to bleed on folks at the parade.

Wow still 5 stars from me. My aunt & uncle were in town with friends and I got to dine with them on a Thursday evening after the Halloween parade. Which meant that I handed out Elmer's Cheewees to most of the staff, because that's how I do.  I had requested a table in Imre's section because he had been the waiter for my parents' 40th anniversary dinner many years ago. And I knew that his level of service and charm would appeal to my family. And he did right by us completely...as one would expect for someone who is been on the job for 40+ years.  We started with lovely cocktails and delicious hot bread. This was followed by salads, escargot and sweetbreads for most of the table; everyone was pleased with their selections. Then came the entrees and this time I had to switch back to the crabmeat sardou which was perfection. Others at the table had the softshell crab (with lump crabmeat of course), shrimp ettouffe (which was amazing) and crabmeat yvonne.  It goes without saying that if the waiter tells you not to order something (for instance the only pompano left by the time we ordered were small, so he recommended the red snapper instead).   Wine, desserts, hilarity, more cheewees. Really it was a perfect evening.

Hemline is a really cute boutique.  And their seemed to be a good variety of items...skirts, blouses, dresses, sweaters, jeans, jewelry, etc.  Unfortunately it was all just a little too girly for me.  I'll have to go back again and see if that's their aesthetic in general or just at the moment.    Meanwhile the space itself is AMAZING, with beautiful super high ceilings, exposed beams, open brick work.  Just lovely.  I know some movie scout is going to want to use the space for some sort of pivotal scene down here in Hollywood South.

I was definitely surprised when I stopped in here. I expected upscale gardening items and yard furniture (which can be seen from the street) but that the shop inside carries a variety of items including home decor, clothes, jewelry, art and children's items...I definitely wasn't expecting that.  First the gardening section, I was specifically looking for lighter weight (but still attractive) planters but they didn't stock those. I was greeted and offered assistance withing a minute or so of entering the garden. I was allowed to browse on my own and then checked back with as I had finished my turn in the garden. I really liked the selection of outdoor furniture and they had plenty of items to fit a more small scale city yard. There were was an area for plants, but that section was mostly empty considering the recent freeze.   I entered the shop from the backdoor and the backroom is more garden oriented with vases and smaller planters. But as you move to the front of the store, there is a large variety of items. There were cases devoted to individual artists like India Stewart or walls for an individual artist. Definitely wish I had stopped in while I was Christmas shopping. The prices were reasonable too.  Bonus: I heard that they sell Christmas trees every year AND you can pick out your tree and it can be stored until you're ready for it in their cool house (off site, I think). So that's pretty cool too.

I had really been looking forward to trying the Green Goddess, but was sort of disappointed with my food.  The premium ingredients in my crab & mango salad were tasty (including the avocado) but the salad greens should have been pitched rather than served.  Also disappointing was that the food menu was a single page & the drink menu was 5 pages.  C'mon I had to go back to work.  And to quote a cranky elderly relative (about many restaurants) "they need an exhaust fan in this place."  I don't think I could have eaten indoors; it was so smoky.

I hadn't been to 9 Roses in years...and I"m not really sure why. I always enjoy it and I like that the menu has both American-Chinese items as well as Vietnamese dishes.   The menu had changed substantially since I'd last been there and I was excited to see veggie steamed dumplings on the new menu...except they ended up not being Chinese steamed dumplings, but more like gyoza (Japanese) instead. They were still tasty but not what I wanted.  On the other hand, I LOVED my tofu with coconut curry. And the portion was so substantial that I enjoyed a couple of extra meals out of it.  I definitely need to remember to stop by again soon.

One of the few fabric/notions stores left in the GNO. The fabric selections are not awesome...mostly poly-cotton blends in bright colors. If you're working on a kids project then you'll do OK.    They do have a lot of other crafting supplies though.  Stuff I have bought here? Mostly notions, a pack of throw pillows in assorted sizes, foam, and most recently cording to make curtain tie backs.  The staff was surprisingly helpful so +1 star. Double bonus? Two ladies pouring over the pattern books and discussing what they were planning to make. Nice throwback to my Granny.

Now starts a series of reviews for bars on Frenchman...most of which I was sure I had reviewed. I think Yelp tortures me by disappearing my reviews occasionally and no they aren't filtered. Or maybe I'm suffering from a huge hallucination...in which case I blame the sinus meds.  I like the bar. I love the food (tachos!!!!) and they're open late, yay! So why three stars? Because WTF is up with the service?  Seriously, 4 or 5 tables got all of their food before my friends got anything. I understand that some dishes take longer but c'mon it was ridiculous. You can put out at least a dozen dishes before theirs?  Also, on my most recent visit the bartender wouldn't even look at his customers. It was so weird. It became a game for me to try to see if he looked at anyone or if I could make him look up at me...Nope. Guess he won that round.
OK I draw the line at eating bugs.  And they get 4 stars because bugs kind of creep me out, but kids LOVE this place.

A solid choice for middle eastern food. Yes the service can be a bit odd...think distracted college student, but really we had no problems yesterday. The food is quick and always tasty.  The space is light and airy which makes eating in comfortable.  I love their spinach pie and their hummus. I just wish I would remember that as much as I love their falafel sandwich that it ends up sitting in my stomach like a lead weight for the next 4 hours....but that's a personal problem. This was our lunch stop during my annual Magazine-Street-Black-Friday-Shopping-Extravaganza with my Mom.  Why didn't I pick a place with a liquor license?

Funny...I just realized I've already reviewed this market under the Crescent City Farmer's Market name.  Oh well, duplicate submitted to Yelp! intergalactic headquarters.  I love the Saturday market...now if I could just make it out of the house to get there before everything is gone.  On any given week, you can find a selection of fresh herbs (in pots), fruit, veggies, honey, wine, canned goods, cheeses/dairy, meat, seafood, baked goods, prepared foods, and flowers.  All really fresh and beautiful.    If the weather is poor, the market moves inside the adjacent parking structure.

Why replace a lock when you can rekey?    I called the store for a locksmith to come out to my house & re-key all three exterior doors. Two of my locks are "vintage" and the third is only a couple of years old. I was concerned that the older locks might only be able to be re-keyed so many times, but the locksmith assured me that the old solid metal locks can be re-done many times.  I now have all the locks on the same key (Yay!) and he made me multiple copies so I didn't have to make a trip to the hardware store.  The person who answered the phone was professional and pleasant. They were able to schedule someone quickly and on the day & time that worked for me. (I did call a couple days in advance of when I knew I'd be home on a workday.) The locksmith who came to my house was great. He did his work quickly and cleanly. Love a no muss, no fuss contractor experience.

I've wanted to try Restaurant August for quite some time and kept hoping to find someone else to pay for the pleasure...  Unfortunately that never happened, but E decided it's where he wanted to celebrate his birthday earlier this week.    Reservations were easy to get on a Tuesday night and we were seated promptly.  First up was hot sourdough rolls and cocktails.  I love bread and the room temperature butter was welcome.  Then came an amuse bouche that looked like a soft-boiled egg.  Presentation was excellent but the flavor was a little flat to me.  E is not a big egg fan so he had a couple of bites & was done.  For our 1st course we each had a salad, his came from the VEGETARIAN TASTING MENU.  (As an aside I was stunned that this was published alongside the meatier tasting menu.  Yay John Besh for being diverse compared to most NOLA fancy restaurants!)  Mine was more standard the blue cheese & greens.  E's grilled melon & heirloom tomatoes was the much more exciting choice.  For our 2nd choice we each got a fish dish off the standard menu.  E got the redfish "courtbouillion" and I got the trout. E's dish was definitely not my Daddy's courtbouillion (pronounced COO-bee-yon in Louisiana).  It was a piece of redfish pan seared with an herb persillade crust plus crabmeat and shrimp.  The sauce was a bourride and poured over the seafood like a stew.  The sauce was so rich that it was not something either of us could eat with a spoon although one was provided.  Guess we're wimps.  My dish was a beautifully cooked piece of trout with lump crabmeat and chanterelle mushrooms with the best hollandaise sauce I've ever eaten.  Dessert was the nougatine napoleon which was a wee bit too salty for me, but E loved it.  PLUS we were given some peanut butter brittle & fancy chocolates as a parting shot.  Final tally:  Amazing food, -1 star initially because there was a large LOUD table in the same room with us who were very disruptive, +1 star for having a vegetarian tasting menu (although it was definitely not vegan) = 5 stars.  Now I just need someone else to pick up the tab next time...

I'm a big fan of WWNO.  I get most of my news from them (NPR affiliate) or from Twitter. I know that's weird.  I also like the classical music, opera, and jazz shows.  And, of course, there is my small obsession with Wait Wait Don't Tell Me.  Good stuff all the way around.

Y'all. How can I be the first person to review this shop?! Lovely small French food specialty shop. We bought tea, cookies, sauces, all sorts of fanciness.  The lady who owns the shop was wonderful and could describe or tell us about all the items we asked about. She has an online shop which may be dangerous because some of those French Kusmi teas are $$$ and so delicious... She also does some lovely gift baskets.  There were some tables and chairs to enjoy some of the goods in the store if that's your preference.

Oh, yum! I love doberge cake and I've even made one...ONCE. (It was chocolate in case you're wondering and tasted delicious but wasn't so pretty.)  And, man, this is a genius business.  Seriously, go stalk some cake immediately!  As others have said, you have to stalk her cakes. I've seen slices for sale at WINO, 12 Mile Limit and over the weekend at Toups Meatery.  So so tasty.  Friday night we had a slice of pistachio (the favorite) and thin mint (freakishly cookie-like); both were gobbled up and rated highly by our entire table.  Right now, the business only has a FB page, but is launching a real live webpage "soon." Evidently they had a hacking incident a year ago...so soon is relative.

I don't usually eat at this location because it's off my beaten path.  But after Katrina, I was helping some friends salvage what they could from their house in Lakeview.  We drove out to this location and they were a godsend.  Under those circumstances, I think it was the best food we ever ate.

Both times I've been to Sugar Park, I've sat outside on the patio which is lovely. The atmosphere is relaxing and conducive to enjoying yourself and your friends.    The drinks are inexpensive and delicious. The servers/bartender are the owners, I think and they will make every effort to make sure that you are enjoying your food and drinks.  I've had some of the small plates/bar items (can't remember what they call them) like banh mi sliders and really enjoyed them. Their fries are delish.  My only disappointment was that my grilled tuna special had extremely overcooked tuna. So I wouldn't order that again.  Seriously a great place for a low key meal that fits within your budget.

This isn't my favorite PJs. I feel like the whole place, indoors and out could use a good scrubbing. The service is usually bored college students and if it's finals prepare to be shushed by the studying fanatics as you try to chat with your friends in a low voice.  The outdoor patio is a nice option when the weather permits with ceiling fans that do a good job of moving the air.

The Prytania gets 5 stars for 2 reasons: 1.  I can walk here from our new house & 2. It's a survivor.  In the last 20 years it has closed 2 or 3 times and each time it was going to be torn down for condos, or a school expansion, or whatever.  Each time the community rallied an new management stepped in.  I wish they still played old movies and art house fare, but it is the last stand alone theater in the city.

Y'know when you feel dumb for showing up at the airport hungry? Because you know the food will be terrible and expensive...WELL, on concourse B you have a tasty (if expensive choice).    I made a yummy meal out of two sides, collard greens (cooked with out meat) and mac-n-cheese. The collards were nice and spicy, although I added Crystal anyway.  The mac-n-cheese was fine and had some crunchy bits which made me happy.    Bonus points for fresh brewed yummy iced tea (unsweet, of course). Price was high but you're at the airport so what are you going to do.
Great store in a small old fashioned location.  Good for all your basics.  AND if you're having a party they deliver and will take back some stuff that wasn't consumed (or opened, of course).

I'm leaning more to 3 1/2 but will round up to a 4 because my food was really good.  Had 2 special tacos and the mango guac.  The guacamole was tasty but the mango was a tad under-ripe. Then again they were slammed so maybe I was sampling tomorrows mangoes.  The special tacos (one shrimp and one flaked drum) were tasty & cheap.  Plus it was mojito madness so NOLA Rum mojitos were only $4.  Delish.   PLUS we got the rum cake, very good.  My only real problem with the restaurant was that it was deafeningly loud, like my ears were ringing after I left loud.  Not the place to go for a quiet restful meal

So say you're trying to do an event on a budget and you want to purchase bulk flowers (especially roses) that are inexpensive but pretty.  This is where you want to go.  I really don't know how Federico's can sell their stuff so inexpensively.    We ended up not being able to use them for our event because they were closed over Thanksgiving weekend, but seriously the staff is good to work with and the prices are great.

I was really excited to see this suburban branch of my favorite FQ coffee shop. Since it's in a strip mall (OK a fancy strip mall), there was plenty of parking.   The menu looked really enticing but I opted for a tasty chocolate chip cooking and a large iced tea. Both were just what I needed and I was off in no time.  The space was roomy with lots of tables for the lunch/breakfast crowd. The staff was nice. Definitely will stop back by when I'm cruising Metairie Road.

E & I had to play the trading ownership of vehicles game.  It's a fun activity we engage in every decade or so...  And it requires a notary so off we went.  This time the locale was the Notary Shoppe.  The woman who helped us was harried but competent.  I did like getting my license plate immediately rather than waiting for it to come in the mail...but maybe that's a change in state rules/processes rather than this location.

What is up with delicious restaurants taking over old Popeye's locations? Yep this little Vietnamese joint is in a former fast food establishment on Airline HWY. OK I'll let that go.  Once you're inside, you won't believe the renovation. It's really spacious and modern. Order at the counter, get your own drink and wait...but not for long. Your choice of dine in or carry out. The menu is a bit brief (hence the Express) but their was plenty to satisfy everyone, veggie or meat eater.  I had a noodle bowl (bun) with tofu and it was delicious and refreshing on a boiling hot day. I will have to go back and try their vegetarian pho and see how it stacks up against my favorite...just not when there is a heat advisory.

I hadn't been to Mona Lisa in over 10 years.  And the food is just as good as I remember.  And it does have good Italian & pizza. The building is interesting and their wine list is even pretty decent these days.  BUT (and you knew it was coming) I have several good pizza joints in my neighborhood so I'm not usually heading to the FQ for pizza.

Um yum! When you're hungry but you want to be healthy, this is the perfect spot.   It's an assembly line and you decide exactly what you want in your bowl. Hate cilantro, skip it. Love macadamia nuts, yep you can have those. Just beware that a few ingredients are an extra cost, avocado, crab salad and, of course and extra scoop of your protein.  I wasn't big on the spicy tuna (but then again I never am) and I thought the tofu could have more flavor. That's right, tofu so you can definitely have a vegetarian meal here.   The space is light and airy but I usually get my bowl to go. Staff is friendly and efficient. And OMG the watermelon agua fresca is delicious!

I was finally able to stalk Nikki my all time favorite esthetician at this location. It had been years since I had last seen her and yet she remembered my skin and was able to take care of me like no time had passed. She is the best for facials.  As for the space, it's interesting. It's in a slightly rundown 1950s era building that is "features an open courtyard, with abundant parking in the back. Haven is through the archway and is the 2nd door on the left. The space is intimate and serene. They've done a nice job in small space. And the rooms are well appointed with everything you might need for your service.  They do not have a receptionist so if you're too early for your appointment, you may have to wait in your car. The door is locked when everyone is with clients. 5 stars for Nikki; she is definitely worth my jaunt to the westbank. The space is more like a 3. So averaged out to a 4 stars.

I don't know. It's been open since May and still seems to be finding it's footing. Our server was sweet but had to go ask a manager to verify before answering our questions. At least then I was confident in the answers.   I had the DELICIOUS tuna tartar which was the best dish of the night from all that the 3 of us ordered. The crab salad  was good also.  But everything is so pricey. Gumbo was a cup size poured into a bowl for over $10. The flavor was good, but the price point vs the serving were just too high.  I want this restaurant to succeed but I'm not sure it will. It's kind of a mish-mash of too many ideas maybe.

Moving sucks, right?  I have to say that this location made it a less painful process.  I needed a ton of boxes and decided to just buy some instead of scavenging them. They were really helpful and even loaded everything into my car. AND I was in an out in like 10 minutes. Scavenging would have taken hours.  Then I go back and rent a 10 foot truck and the process was super easy and the weekend staff was once again really nice and helpful.  Definitely worth every penny

While throwing down for the super awesome Linday's birthday spectacular at Finn McCool's, I ate some dinner from BooKoo.  I had the fried mac-n-cheese and the soup of the day...wait, serious dejavu. I think I wrote this up in my Finn McCool's review. Oh well.  Anyway, the mac-n-cheese wasn't my thing. But if I had been drunk, it would have been perfect to soak up all the alcohol in my tummy.  The soup on the other hand was delicious, a very non-traditional bisque that I thoroughly enjoyed.

Jean-Paul is correct. It's a quicky mart. But y'know it's a convenient one with good hours.  So if you live nearby and need toothpaste...or other personal hygiene items, they will probably have it.  Really though, we usually just stop for beer (and maybe snacks) on the way to parties.

I finally visited this spot...I had been given a gift card for my birthday back in January and my oldest brother raved about how delicious it was. Plus I went during coolinary so 3 courses prix fixe? Yes please!  The peach salad was light and flavorful. The catfish and greens, tasty, but OH MY the mirliton chowchow was AMAZING. Now I do love me some mirlitons in all forms (that's chayote for much of the world) and this dish let them shine while putting a new spin. Yum!  I had the Rail to drink...I mean bourbon and lemonade in August is a no brainer. And an ice cream sandwich for dessert which was tasty.  The restaurant was crowded when we arrived, despite the difficulty in getting to it thanks to road closures. And, was it loud, there was a drinking party at the bar and when they left, it was such a relief. While I don't want a restaurant to be library-quiet, I don't really expect the people adjacent to be hollering.

Things I have bought a Jefferson Feed:   a curry brush for a horse (as a gift)  chickens, ducks feed for my hamsters, gerbils, dog, chickens, ducks, and rabbits soil plants sod. And probably some other stuff that I forgot since I grew up around the corner from the store.  Really, they have all sorts of stuff that you never knew you needed.  The best thing is that the store is located in the old Jefferson Movie Theater where my Dad used to see the Saturday morning serials in the 1940s-50s.

While part of me still pines for the neighborhood restaurant that was here pre-Martinique, I have to admit that comparison would be apples to oranges.  Martinique is a lovely but small french inspired spot.  I have never tried brunch here (and don't think I'm really a brunch person) so my review is strictly for dinner.  I've had delicious cocktails here and the seasonal menus are lovely.  I've had excellent fish, vegetarian dishes and desserts.  I honestly can't remember a plate that I didn't enjoy.    My only complaints are that the dining room is a bit tight and if you end up at a table in the middle of the room it's a bit hustley.  And if you're near the bar, you can feel the waitstaff frenzy on occasion...which just makes me antsy I must admit.  The garden space is lovely when weather permits.  As for the previous restaurant in this location: RIP Mais Ouis...know that I still long for your crawfish ettouffe, and your cornbread, and your chocolate pudding.  OK I'm done now.

Interesting little shop on Magazine with a very different selection of items that other stores. Yes they have jewelry, art, tchotchkes but the style/flavor is very different from what I've seen elsewhere in town.    Yes, they do have stuff made of bones and nails so the name doesn't disappoint. It's not a huge store but there is still a ton of stuff to see. The staff has been polite and not pushy.  The store is a vintage shotgun so the steps were a little steep for my 70+ Mom.

Pitot house is a beautifully preserved Creole home. It is nicely furnished with period furniture and has been fabulously restored.  So why 4 stars instead of 5?  Like most period homes, it's really small so touring it takes maybe 30-40 minutes. Definitely worth a drop in when you're in the area, but maybe not a special trip.

Le Petit fsure. This small theater (seats just over 300 people) is an intimate venue with often ambition programming. Yes it can get crowded and now that patrons can get full strength drinks at Tableau...through the archway... watch out for drunks on the stairs!  The theater seats in the balcony are tight so consider that when booking. The acoustics are good and every seat has a great view of the stage.   I miss the even smaller theater (called the Children's theater when I was a child)... last play I saw there was the Complete Works of Wm Shakespeare Abridged.   I saw the Tabasco Opera this past weekend in the theater and it sounded and looked great. I wonder how the orchestra fit in the pit?!  Looks like your next opportunity to see something staged here, is Tennessee William Fest and Streetcar.

Oh wow. I finally made it to dinner here and I wonder what took me so long. While technically we were here for a Coolinary meal, it turns out the Grill Room's 3 course tasting menu is an all year long thing.  And if you wanted to upgrade, you could have a 4 course or 5 course and even add lobster or foie gras for an upcharge.   I went for an all sea menu... crawfish rangoon, seared tuna, and poached snapper. I appreciated that our waiter mentioned which dishes were smaller and which were larger. And his service was on point! He was ready for drink orders and gave good advice and really made my group's meal special.  Of my 3 dishes, the rangoon was good, the tuna was AMAZING and the snapper was delicious. I was pleased with all 3 and I would order the second two again, but maybe start with a salad next time.   The wine and cocktail list looked amazing and I'll have to sample some of those next time.   And, yes, I need to get over for that $19.84 plate lunch sometime... maybe on a weekday off so I can fully enjoy the $2 martinis!

Brand new nail salon that is in my neighborhood. It's beautiful inside with really upscale pedicure chairs. The whole place is really clean and my instruments were taken out of a freshly sealed package.   They also offer hot stone massage with their mani/pedis (for an extra fee of course) and waxing services. We'll see how my toes hold up and if. This will become my new go to spot.    Oh & they're having a 25% off special...until August maybe?

This was a super fun party that benefited Southern Food and Beverage Museum and The Museum of the American Cocktail. The drinks were definitely free flowing and most tables did not have a line...or if there was a back up it was only a couple of two people and you could watch the alchemist bartenders concoct their wares.  I even tasted 2 gin drinks that I liked! Me & gin...thought it would never happen.  I was a little disappointed in the quantity of the food but these events often run out so I had pre-eaten a snack. What food there was, was delicious.  Of course, the company was awesome. I met some random people who were lovely and one even thanked me for being a librarian. So there's that.   High marks!

So when I was hunting in cemeteries a couple of years ago, I finally toured St. Louis #1.  Growing up here, you know all about Marie Laveau (although my understanding is that it's her daughter who is interred here not the actual VooDoo Queen herself) and so it was really interesting to see her tomb and all the offerings that were before it.  I also think it's amusing that the former mayor of New Orleans tomb is just a few steps away.  This was not my favorite place to photograph though.  I guess I like the cemeteries that actually have some greenspace in them (see my reviews for the Valence Street Cemetery & Lafayette #1).    Negative points for the homeless dude sleeping in the back of the yard who scared the bejeebus out of me.  But plus points again because I then scared the bejeebus out of my brother.    Warning: do not come here alone and mind your surroundings.  You do not want to be easy pickings for zombies or our local criminal element.
Great, free, fun time.    -1 star because so many of the folks there have absolutely no interest in the music.  Talk, talk, talk, talk.  They could at least go to the other side of the square.

Once again, I am writing a review for my partner.  He had his acoustic guitar "repaired" by another shop in town and they...let's say, overcorrected, and the saddle snapped.  After asking around for the best luthier in town, he was steered to Todd.  Not only did he repair the guitar to its former glorious sound, it turns out that he probably sold the guitar to E back in the early 80s when he worked for a now defunct music store.  Great prices, friendly staff, walls full of instruments and a floor full of vintage amps.  Fun for the whole family.

Solid intimate (but not too small) hotel bar. The decor was welcoming and fancy which is a difficult combination to pull off, I think.  The bartenders weren't super personable but did a good job handling the deluge of yelpers that descended on them on Saturday night.  The prices were high, even for a hotel bar.

The multi seed bread is divine as are the danishes (so not the American version).  I do enjoy the king cakes (both NOLA & French versions) and the croissants as well.  They supply the bread to many of the fine dining restaurants all over the city.

Definitely an intimate little theater. I've been here for a couple of events, but never for a comedy show.   The venue can be noisy (because of the A/C) and it's really hard to be anonymous since it seats maybe 40 people. But the chairs are good (which isn't a given since I disrupted a performance in a different tiny theater in the FQ when a chair leg fell off in the middle of act 2), and the location is really convenient to me.  It does seem like the folks who rent out the space struggle with the mechanicals a bit. Perhaps more direction is needed on how to get the sound system, lighting and a/c to work properly.

I've never actually eaten a beignet here, but y'know it's fried sweet dough so as long as they fry well...I'd probably be a fan.  I actually ate here 2x in a week this summer. Cash flow as a bit tight and I could get a good basic sandwich and iced tea for under $10. The staff was really friendly. My iced tea was well brewed and they offered free refills.  The space is charming and seems to be an old carriage house. The curved ceiling is really lovely. Plus outside dining in the courtyard of the police station...yep, the police station which is inside an old mansion. (You've actually seen these buildings beaucoup times on tv shows and movies).   Bonus? the audacious little sparrows who steal crumbs from tables and chairs...or maybe not if you're my bird fearing Mom.

I finally popped in to the newly remodeled Riverwalk last week late on a Wednesday. It was dead, deader, deadest...so if you need to get some shopping done without a crowd. Go after dinner.    I wasn't super impressed with the store selection but I am highly suspicious of *outlet* clothes anyway. However, the one store my friend needed to run to was Nordstrom Rack and them I was impressed with. I'll definitely come back to shop there.  I didn't hit up the food court so can't discuss the selection and I'm kicking myself for forgetting to validate my parking since just over an hour was $10. Ridiculous.

The staff was really nice. The shuttle arrived quickly and the driver helped with my bag. The parking spaces are tight...which generally means more dings.  Make life easy and reserve a spot online and prepay, much easier. Especially when you're on the state contract and have to enter the secret code.   If no spots are available, you can leave your keys with them and they'll park the car after you're gone, at least for the state contract folks. This idea is not one I'm a fan of.

Solid choice for a quick breakfast or coffee/tea stop. Prices are FQ high but the food is usually good. My 2 pet peeves: the breakfast menu ends too early. AND they have those tiny beverage napkins only. C'mon. Get some real napkins.  The staff is mercurial; one day you may get sweetness and light and the next is all storm clouds. The space is lovely and airy.

Sigh. So my go to spot isn't any longer. After my last couple of trips, I've decide to downgrade them a star.   On my last visit, my tech was on her phone a lot...she was checking her work email at her other job and then commenting and cursing the entire time. When I tried to engage her in conversation, y'know to draw her focus back on me, the paying customer, she either ignored me or made a couple of disparaging comments.  While some of the same people are there from the beginning, I think the owners have changed and the manner of the space has become much more abrupt and less welcoming.  The brochure of services is heavily marked up with strikeouts for all the items they no longer offer. Despite fewer services and more utilitarian atmosphere, the prices are still premium.

I stopped in while I was on Metairie Road because I had heard a report of Bingles in this shop... No Bingles but lots of other Christmas decorations.   Yes this is the high end Goodwill so you don't have to pick through a million stretched out/faded tshirts. I'm not sure who does the sorting, but there did seem to be a donation space in the back.   The clothing is really well laid out and the store is SPACIOUS...really spacious as in the may need more stock. Prices were good on many things but I saw an interesting Phaidon Press book (very high end art books) and they're price was $95...that seemed like a new/retail price, not a 2nd hand one.   Lots of silver housewares and some art. Good spot to stop and browse.

The place to buy smocked children's clothing.  If that's not your thing, then they have jewelry, housewares, gift items, seasonal stuff, linens, and interesting antiques.  Really a little bit of everything.  They don't get 4 stars because the staff can be snooty.

Beckham's is an old school used book store.  They have both reading and collectible copies of a wide variety of items.  As the previous reviewer stated they also have music so they are the perfect stop for the group that includes obsessive collectors in both areas.

So the Dungeon has new owners and the music has definitely shifted again. I wish they would bring the by request DJ back. I'm not sure who was picking the music.  The space is lovely and the staff works hard. The cage is still there and now there's weird bench seating across from it that doesn't really fit adult knees. We decided it should be called the cuddle pile.   Depending on your night the bar might be filled with idiots...I was very adult and resisted punching the dude who smacked me on the ass, but I did warn the bouncer that if this random guy touched me again then I was going to take a physical stand...he said he would try to look the other way.  On the other hand, I was there with fabulous Jeannie from Portland (with her family entourage) and our own Joi and Danny so a fun time was had by all.   Solid drinks, with some froufy frozen concoction at the downstairs bar that will probably put you out after a couple.   Protip: No photographs and they will come after you for taking them...

You have to love a neighborhood hardware store. You walk in and a counter person usually asks within a few moments what I need. Then they actually walk me to the corner of the store where the item is located.   This isn't the biggest store in the world but if you need a couple of keys made, a ladder, some other basic hardware type stuff, then you can be in and out of this location quick-quick.  They also have stock here that I definitely don't see at the big box stores or even Harry's Ace. Most recent purchase? Picture hangers that can go directly into brick. They were so easy to use too.  One caveat? With the doors wide open and minimal a/c (maybe just an attic fan?), this place gets hot in summer, but then again it's pretty chilly in winter too.
Service is definitely indifferent at this location; on the other hand the food is good and CHEAP.  They're hummus is my favorite.  And I love the falafel sandwich.
Reasons I go to Riverwalk: 1. One of the only malls in the city limits. 2. A couple of stores that I would have to drive to the suburbs for otherwise. 3. Biggest Gap in the area & the only Gap Body

What do NOLA folks do in the evenings when they're home and bored? Argue about food on twitter... So Sam B (see his review) stated that this was the best NY style pizza to be found in NOLA. I do love pizza but I have been told my NY natives that my tastes do not coincide with theirs. Still I put this on my list to try.  About a week later, I was at a party in the area and the food & drink lines were just too long so Anita & I ducked into this spot to freshen our drinks and get some eats. We sat at the bar since the place was pretty full thanks to our party and the convention center being busy.  Both the owner of the business and the owner of the building (I think) were there that night, with the business owner subbing in as our bartender/waiter. So our service was a bit over the top.  The food was good and we shared a spinach/ricotta pizza. Mad props for the delicious ricotta. We also tried their yummy garlic knots. I really need to go back and try their pasta with vodka sauce since I do love that.  The space was still a work in progress when I was there last month (with empty fish tanks waiting to be filled) so I look forward to the completed space. Definitely a nice addition to the Italian restaurants in town.

Dang. I didn't know that there was still a fabric store in the GNO that was so huge. And the craft section was pretty big too. The staff was polite and helpful.   Prices are good especially if you sign up for the emails or mailers for coupons...or if you have a friend who does and knows that you are planning on working an insane costume and need supplies.  So 4 stars and definitely worth a jaunt to almost Kenner.

Hand crafted in Tennesee? I'm there. And while some of the items were really cute. Others were old school craft fair. So if you're looking for that sort of thing, then this is your place.  I liked that the prices were reasonable, but nothing really jumped out at me.  And the staff member who was there, was on a personal phone call the entire time we browsed.

I was looking for costume inspiration and had a few minutes so I buzzed into this shop.  It has some standard beads and plastic stuff that gets thrown from carnival floats, but it also had tchotchkes, clothes, boas, masks, dried out alligator heads... You get the idea. Basically any  stuff made in southeast Asia.  The prices on some items seemed a little higher than other stores, but if you're looking for some different items it might be worth a pass by.

I've been hearing about the amazing MG Zone for years. And I finally stopped in last month. I can see why the neighborhood folks love it. This shop really does sell a little bit of everything. Fancy canned goods, basic dog food, prepared foods, veg-friendly stuff, it's all there.   Yes I can see that some stuff may age out on the shelf, but really what grocery exists where you don't have to check the expiration dates.   I enjoyed my perusal and I did feel like a tourist in a strange land... And then I headed back to my part of town which evidently hoards all the grocery stores so the rest of the city can't have any.

Wow! I stopped by late on a weekday to this cozy spot and grabbed one of the few seats a the bar.   I wish I still had room for food but it was not to be. However the drinks were stunning. One of our group was not feeling so great after an earlier misstep with some extremely salty food. So our lovely bartender fixed him up with a non-booze stomach soothing option.  The drinks were amazing and the staff here is great! Sitting at the bar, I had a great view of the kitchen and they were hustling!  Definitely need to stop back and get dinner next time.

Wow! The new renovation makes the shop look much fancier...we'll see if it improves functionality.  I can't believe they've added gelato (or whatever the french word is).    I stopped by this morning to buy bread for a party at the line was 30 people deep. I wish there was an express lane to grab a couple of loaves and begone.

I'm with Rene. I reviewed fg's original store on Oak St. This location is 3 (maybe 4) times the square footage of the old store.  Besides t-shirts it carries a ton of New Orleans themed items, and some original art with NOLA themes.  The staff is friendly and will even explain some of the tshirt phrases is you're not sure what the local joke is.  Love that they have carried shirts that support local charities (like the Audubon Institute or a local man rebuilding his house in the Treme).

I don't know who Kristie dealt with, but the store owner was in the shop on Saturday morning and she was super nice. My friend found a ton of jewelry that she loved...and maybe a couple of pieces of clothing. I bought a shirt. Yeah I'm boring.  The shop has an eclectic vibe and the pieces were different from what I've seen in other shops. Definitely a spot I'll check back to see what new stock is in.   Bonus parking is available in the Dominique's lot during the day.

I hadn't been to this location since it was a Straya. And I ended up here with a large family group after a dance recital. I should have just ordered some of the ridiculous drinks.
