Instead I ordered dessert like everyone else. AND every dessert was enormous and off...   That's my problem with Copeland's, they sacrifice quality for huge portions. Our server was overwhelmed and not super professional. The table next us started screaming profanities...guess they were drunk?  And I hate that they have maybe 4 non-valet parking spots. And those are reserved for take out or some nonsense.

The decor is nice; it's really spacious; the price is comparable to other spots uptown, but this won't become my go to spot.  I gave them 2 attempts and both times (and 2 different techs) they were just too rough. Once I got the deluxe pedicure and was exfoliated within an inch of my life, even after I asked that they be gentle around a scar on my leg. The second time I got the basic pedicure and the tech clipped skin twice while trying to get my nails.   They do autoclave their instruments but I everyone scoops out of the same jars (with their hands) for the deluxe pedicure.   This would be a good spot to go if you have a large group who all wants to have services together.

I always miss this parade for one reason or another... working, out of town, etc. So I finally put it on my list of things to do this past weekend. And... yknow it was OK.   First I am so very grateful that Carnival krewe floats MUST (by law) remain ad free. The sponsored floats are kind of sad to me. OTH, if I won the lottery I would totally sponsor a Jen's Friends float in all these ridic parades and have a moving party.   So yeah. 10 floats (yawn) and beaucoup marching groups, which I really enjoyed how the different groups jazzed up their outfits with Holiday flair. Also I'm going to push this review up to a 4 for the McMain band which reminded me why I miss catching parades downtown. That drumline echoing between the buildings is the BEST!  So if you're around, go check it out but don't make a special trip in for it. But as always, any parade is better than no parade!
Another great way to see the city.  This line was closed in the 1960s and the reopened in the last decade.

Wow! Do yourself a favor and get over to Vom Fass.  This is a local franchise of a European specialty foods retailer (one of only 3 locations in the US).  They sell cask stored oils, vinegars, and liquor.   I am OMG-obsessed with the avocado oil. Weird, right? Wait until you taste it.  They offer tastings of all their items so you can try before you buy.  You do have to purchase bottles to store your liquids though and the bottles are a range of prices depending on size and fanciness.  You can bring the bottles back for a re-fill.

I like Gretna, especially old Gretna. It's like a step back in time with all the 1930s houses etc.   It is the Parish seat for Jefferson Parish which is weird since most of the parish is on the Eastbank. So if you get called for jury duty this is where you go.  Gretna does have some good shopping and restaurants (both local and chain).   And it even has it's own local t-shirt...Greatna!

I guess if I want to review parade I have to add them. I accidentally added my photos to the Block Party link but this for the actual parade.  Please note that while this parade does not have a really long route, it takes forever because drunken men (mostly) are marching around handing out flowers, beads and sloppy kisses.  There are traditional bands and floats and you can expect to catch a variety of food items from the parade, from cabbages to carrots to peanut butter crackers (Yay for me on that one). Plus I also caught a bar of Irish Spring and a little ziploc bag of random candy.  The paraders are extra drunk and the crowd is happy and if the weather i great than it's an awesome parade.  The most crowded areas are by bars on Magazine Street and not on St. Charles for this one.

Oh look FG moved again into what used to be a furniture store so it has a lot more room. So lots of stock to sift through. Still plenty of NOLA/Louisiana stuff but some National lines too.   They have some of their original shirts but a lot of new stock too. I ended up buying another Saints shirt because you need to be able to wear black & gold for 2 weeks without a repeat, right?  There are multiple platforms and steps up in the shop, in case you're with the mobility challenged.

I agree with Allison M; you never know what kind of service you're going to get at this neighborhood mail place.  If you need to rent a mailbox or bike over a package than they are a decent neighborhood alternative to the post office.

Still my go to market for a quick trip. When I just need a couple of things, I can be in and out of the store in 10 minutes. And really isn't that worth 4 stars?  You have to check the produce carefully but the dairy cases seem to work better these days.  They still have butchers on site for shifts during the day but not all the hours that the store is open. Call if you need something special,  Their prepared food are good but are more downhome than fancy. A good place to stop for quick sandwich or hot lunch.

The people at this branch were amazing. I found an older savings bond that my grandmother purchased for me... a very long time ago. While they can cash an EE bond issued to you, the older E bonds now require a bunch of hoops. These hoops have nothing to do with Chase and are federal requirements.  Since my matured bond was over $100, you know I wasn't letting that money go. I had downloaded the forms from the treasury website and then brought them into Chase (where I am an account holder) to have them stamp it with a seal. I should have made an appointment to do this but they were kind enough to take me as a walk in. After figuring out exactly what was needed, I signed the document in their presence and it was stamped. I mailed off the documents and a week later a direct deposit was in my account!  There is parking behind the building which is tight but manageable.   Whew!

I haven't been to original Acropolis in Metairie in years, so I was really pleased to see that they were opening another location in the old Wayfare spot. I went over with my uncle for dinner last week and he reminisced about going to the original in Metairie when in first opened.  I opted for a four course special for $20.95 and it was a great deal for the amount of food. I had cauliflower bisque to start then a Caesar salad and then grilled pompano and finally baklava for dessert. The soup was rich and delicious. The Caesar was fine and the grilled pompano was delicious plus I had pilaf and veg of the day to take home. My uncle and I split the baklava which was good. He had lamb kebabs because "he always has the lamb when going to Greek restaurants."  Service was good and the space hasn't changed much from when it was Wayfare. Great addition to Freret Street.

My biggest wish for Armstrong Park is that it was kept up better. It's such a lovely (and historical) space and if it would stop being a political boondoggle we'd all be better off.  I was in the area a couple of weeks ago to see a matinee at the Performing Arts Center. It was lovely to be able to go stand outside during the intermission... and because it was a Sunday afternoon, the drum circle was happening in a different section of the park, but resonating through out. The park did look clean and well groomed so perhaps there is a contract for that at the moment.   The park is large, most of a city block or 2. This includes multiple buildings and parking lots (which are in terrible condition) and lots of different spaces to explore. As always be aware of your surroundings and be safe.  And could someone please please please get our city admin to bring the Municipal Auditorium back into service. It's been sitting there rotting since Katrina.

Personable staff, interesting selection, but dang those prices. I have to admit that I have paid the prices that they list for jeans but I also got free alterations at that price.  If I was desperate for a new pair of jeans and couldn't find anything that worked, I would probably hit them up again. And I did buy a really cute dress, so there's that.  My only other complaint is that the dressing rooms were really warm. Trying on jeans in August is hot enough and the warm dressing room was making me a bit dizzy.

This is the distribution location of Mrs. Wheat's Meat Pies....I remember eating these for the 1st time at the World's Fair in 1984.  And they are delicious.   The pies are deep fried so they must be good, right?  Back then they had 2 kinds of meat (spicy & blah) and broccoli & cheese.  They have been at Jazz Fest every weekend for decades.  And now have dropped the non-spicy meat and added crawfish (really more like a crawfish dressing because it has rice too).  I cannot tell you how much I love the broccoli & cheese pie.

How can it be that I don't have a review for this coffee shop? Seriously, I think Yelp eats my review. It's not like I say Scott's forbidden word in any of mine...Jeez  Stuff I like about this CCs: it's a local company; they offer some tasty baked goods; they offer a nice selection of teas (y'all know I'm not a coffee person); and it's pretty inside.  Stuff I don't like: it's really popular and the "regulars" can be cranky if you want to sit inside and have a conversation.   As a random note, I remember sitting outside this CC's after closing (which was pretty early) in late 2005, cadging their Wi-Fi and a car screeched to halt and asked if they were open. That guy was seriously jonesing for some caffeine.

Potsalot is a great local pottery place with some innovative designs.  They do a bread bowl...which you bake in. And now have a wine bowl (doubt that's the real name) that allows you to ice down 3 bottles and the niches in the bowl keep them upright.  It appeared in a Treme episode according to in-store press.  They also do vessel sinks...or as my MiL's plumber called them birdbath sinks.  She has one from here and loves it.    They are doing some really interesting things with pressed clay that I really like.

Maybe it was because we came at night and not for lunch. But I wasn't super impressed with the fish here.  And I get that you treat your regulars well, but I felt like that there was almost a class system in the works...and I was definitely amongst the plebes.  We tried sushi of the specials that day, a gulf tuna (delicious) and sea urchin (good but I couldn't get past the texture).  We also tried an assortment of rolls including the Elvis. I liked that you could order large rolls as halves so you were able to sample more. I ordered the blue crab roll and both the texture and taste were off so I didn't finish that.  I had a salad that I enjoyed but now I can't remember what it was.  While I enjoyed much of my food, I don't know that I will make the jaunt out to this location on a  regular basis.

I discovered that I never finished this review when I ate at the Runway again yesterday. Love the renovated airport, love the art deco diner. But both time I've eaten here, it was in the Walnut Room since that seems to be the thing on weekends.   The menu selection is elevated diner and I've had omelets on both occassions. The first time the Lindberg (mmmm brie) and this time the Wright Brothers (although what they have to do with crawfish ettouffe...). The Ettouffee was a little tomato-ey for my taste but was still yummy. And I remember the Lindberg being delish. My nieces got a kid's pancake (huge!) and the shrimp & grits. Both were very happy.  Service is very personable and attentive. And the views of the planes and the runways are great. Definitely worth the drive across town for me.

Y'know some mornings you wake up and you just need pancakes and not just any pancakes...I needed pancakes that I once had from a restaurant in Tannersville, NY.  Well that wasn't going to happen, so I went to Surrey's Uptown.  And while their single jumbotron of a banana pancake (w/ pecans added) was not exactly what I wanted, it sure hit the spot.    Also the glass of fresh orange mango juice was super tasty and went perfectly with my pancake.

Tiny PJs but a HUGE pastry case...which sadly was mostly empty when I stopped by.  I was hoping for a single slice of king cake. It wasn't to be.  I know it was late on a Sunday but the shop was kind of trashed. Maybe everybody else was jonesing for king cake too and so they threw all their trash on the ground?  And, not that this has anything to do with this coffee shop, but what right minded parents buys their under 12 child a sugary coffee drink at night? That just seems a road to madness to me.

I had been meaning to try RioMar for months and since we were downtown and starving a few weeks ago, we decided it was time.  The food was delicious.  Chef Adolfo came out to chat with us...and thanks to my friend the Traveling Buddha we even scored a free dessert tray!  My friend & I shared the ceviche platter and each had a salad.  The ceviche was wonderful (although the one with fish & habanero cause me some delicious pain).  And both salads were super tasty.  Hers had a fried oysters; the oysters were battered in cornmeal and MELTED in your mouth.  Yum...  And did I mention Anthony Bourdain was there?  It was a very fun and somewhat odd night.

I am not super vintage girl, but my friend who was in town yesterday is.  She LOVED this store.  They have clothes and accessories (hats, shoes, purses, and jewelry).  Expert friend said the prices on the jewelry were great.  I found a really cute Bakelite purse that I was tempted by.  They used to be further down on Magazine (close to Napoleon) but have recently moved over toward Louisiana.

The last time the locksmith came to my house? I hugged him. That's how much I love their service.   My house is old; they are doing beaucoup construction work in my neighborhood causing my house to shift on it's foundations. Locks don't like shifting foundations, so sometimes they spaz out. Or you discover that there's a button lock on the front door that gets accidentally pushed and how do you get OUT?! So I just call up the office and someone comes out usually with 24 hours (weekdays).   I have had a variety of locksmiths come out but my favorite is the older man because he reminds me of my grandfather. (He's also the one I hugged last time. Yes I think he thought I was crazy.) Everyone has been very professional and really helpful, giving me hints on how to prevent future problems.  I know they have gift items in their store and really should get over there and shop.

How good is Cowbell?  I had to go twice in one week!  Of course, I want to be supportive as it was opened by friends of a friend (Hi Anita M!).  But the food is tasty and at a price point that makes it easy to return, again and again.    So far I've sampled the mac-n-cheese, fish tacos, shrimp quesadillas, veggie burger, a special grilled cheese (brie & asparagus & avocado) the apple pie (really a compete tart), and the chocolate something dessert.  All really good in a casual environment.  Now they just need city hall to let go and give them a liquor license.  Seriously, I might have to go for mac-n-cheese & a salad tomorrow.

Once upon a time one of the uptown PJs was my go to spot for hanging with friends, studying, having a tea, whatnot. But then the business was sold and all the PJs lost their 70s hippiesh roots and became corporate. This PJs is a perfect example of a strip mall corporate shop.   The good - it's really spacious. There is plenty of parking. I've never had discourteous service. It has outdoor seating.  The OK - the tea selection is just OK, mostly because I remember what it used to be. It always seems to need a good scrub. The smokers who use the outdoor seating don't clean up after themselves, yuck.  So if you're needing to feed the caffeine jones, this is a fine place to stop. I guess ultimately I'd give them a 3.5?

Somehow I had never stopped into this old school CBD costume shop. I was surprised to see that it also carries party goods, as well as packaged costumes plus pieces made in house.   The stairs up to the costume area might be a bit difficult for some (like my Mom) but that's where all the good stuff is. I was looking for some pretty specific pieces and I felt like if I had more time than they could have made them for me.  The staff was helpful and the place is HUGE...not that all the space is well used, especially on the first floor.  This will definitely be included in future costume shop excursions.

Oh WOW! I've been wanting to check out Alon Shaya's new restaurant and over MG week, I finally did. My visitor was surprised to get a reservation on a Friday night but she didn't realize that night's parades were starting just blocks away. Zero problems being dropped off by a rideshare.   Food was delicious. We had the beets, feta, and the roasted apple, along with brussel sprouts hummus. Everything was amazing, delicious, rich, interesting, well prepared, all the superlatives. Neither of us was starving since we had each had a large lunch but we wished we had room for more food. The apple was interesting in that it was roasted with tahini but was so gorgeous, we hesitated in demolishing it...until we tasted it then all bets were off. And of course, the pita was delish and was whole wheat the night I went so a little more substantial then the usual white wheat.  I had a yummy old fashioned while I was there. There drink menu is super inventive but I just needed an old standby. And of course the wine list is good too.  Service was attentive without being pushy. The atmosphere is lovely and airy. Definitely will be back soon.

I love me a bagel sandwich so I can't believe it's taken me so long to get over to Artz.  Love! the decor. Seriously I think it's really smart and airy (although loud) and I like watching the bagel makers do their thing.  The bagels were tasty and while I'm not an expert on authentic, I do know good bread.  Try the blueberry cream cheese, rich, delicious and not too sweet. Yum.

A bajillion years ago, I shopped at this store (in a different location) all the time. They have always had interesting clothes that you didn't see in other shops.  So I discovered that they had reopened a shop in Metairie and stopped in last month. Loved that it was well organized and well labeled. And while no clothes jumped out at me on that visit, I definitely saw some jewelry that was really lovely.  The sales person was helpful without being pushy. Will definitely be back when I'm looking for something unique.

My most recent visit to this lovely courtyard was for brunch... in June. And our large group was outside. I thought one of my colleagues makeup was going to melt off. I don't think she realized that we would be dining outside when she made the reservation.  As always the food was delicious. We sampled the baked oysters and I had the Amelie salad which was perfect. For my entree I got the breakfast sandwich without the ham and it was huge and filling. I had an orange blossom cocktail with brunch and it was lovely. Service was great service. And they were on it for our large group. But OMG was it hot since it was after 1 when we left. Whew...

Until last night, I had not stepped foot in Deja Vu since...maybe high school (so the 80s) and either I'm remember a different bar or the place has changed considerably.  Let's just go with I was probably really drunk back then.  *I checked with a friend who went to Deja Vu back in the day. Yes it was a dance club back then, so I wasn't totally drunk.*  We ended up here on a Monday with a large group of semi-drunken visitors.  The kitchen & wait staff handled our influx with aplomb.  Everyone raved about their food (and I sampled the fried pickles & the fried green beans...both really tasty).  The drinks were well priced and the room was spacious.  My only issue is the same one I have with lots of bars, the smoking. But seriously, the out of town visitors LOVED lighting up indoors.  How decadent.

Oh look. It's time for more parades. But this is a totally different experience than most carnival parades. There are tons of walkers who are handing out flowers (for kisses...or not), many of whom are so drunk that it is amazing that they can still stand. This leads to many large gaps in the parade which gives parade goers time to get more drinks or chat with their friends or dance in the streets, y'know, whatever.  When the floats come along the riders are pelt you with many of the standard throws, but also cabbages, potatoes, carrots, and ramen noodles. Yeah. So watch your head.  Funniest moment of the parade? A man handed a maybe 9 year old girl a flower then asked if she would kiss him. She looked skeptical and then said nope, I don't know you. The man high-fived her instead.

This has always been the weirdest spot. The building is so large that every space in here has ended up feeling a bit like a warehouse.   Good things: Bar staff was great. It's open until 11 on weeknights and some food (maybe the whole menu) is available at the bar until then.   Meh: Food (that my friend ordered) was OK not great. Drinks were OK.  Weird: The entire place was deserted until my group rolled in. And the staff seemed surprised (and happy) that anyone was there.  Probably not my first choice but I would stop by again if I was in the area.

A really clean, well laid out thrift store. The selection wasn't huge but there is a pet section which is appropriate considering the cause.  They mostly have household items and clothes. As others have said, there is no room for furniture.  My only curiosity is how to do they afford a Magazine street rent and still donate the proceeds to animal shelters. Maybe the building owner is an animal lover.

I was looking for a REALLY specific piece of furniture (and felt like Goldilocks while hunting...this piece is too wide; this one is too short; this one is just right...oops, look at the price).    And Dop actually had something that was sort of perfect...except that it was a real antique (they also sell reproductions) and was ebonized wood AND was inlaid with real ivory. So even if I had been tempted (not at that price point), the ivory might have been a deal breaker because it kind of creeps me out.  This is a hot warehouse and it's dusty so be prepared. And a staff member was there to help me within moments of entering their space.  They have a constantly rotating selection of interesting items. I will be back again.

Pandemic review: Who shops for furniture during a pandemic? The good daughter does because Dad's recliner is broken and he almost lives in it.  Mom decided it was time to upgrade to a lift chair in addition to the recliner. So I looked a couple of places. At Comeaux, I was helped immediately by the wonderful CC. She understood the situation and showed me what they had available. I knew the decision was between 2 chairs. Some of the ones out there have really flimsy remotes and I feel like they would break instantly. CC let me know that both the chairs, I was interested in were in stock and we could pick up the chair on Tuesday from their warehouse in MidCity and save the $99 delivery charge.  They also offer a protection plan which covers a number of things including the motor for 5 years. Considering Dad's last recliner lasted 3 years and 5 months, I think it's worth it.  BTW, you purchase a lift chair based on height and weight so consider that should you ever need to get one, if the chair is too large then your feet dangle as it lifts you up which could be dangerous. And if the motor isn't robust enough for the weight of the person using it, then you'll burn out the motor.   I sent pictures of the 2 options to my Mom and we made a decision and I called CC to actually place the order. I paid once I got into the warehouse store (the scratch and dent showroom).   Chair was easy to set up and Mom and Dad's and Dad was super happy with it. And Mom said it looked even better in person.  Yay!

I'm not super fond of this location since I've been hassled by the loiterers here. But I thought it would be safe to stop in the middle of the day in the bright sunshine.  Of course, I had the nieces in the car who started a slapfight with each other and I had to intervene. THAT's when I discovered the auto-shutoff on the gas pump did NOT work.   I blame the gas station and the children.
The stinkiest cheese store in town.  Super knowledgeable staff and great selection.  Plus lunch! and you can buy wine next door.

Oh yum. I'm glad Re suggested this is as our family dinner last night. Because it was very tasty. We were a big group so we got a variety of items. I really liked my tuna sandwich (cooked rare); my piece of tuna was lovely and really big ... I'm eating the last 1/3 for my lunch today and it came with a small salad so yum! Katie loved her burger so much that it was GONE. I got to sit next to John (and watching a 14 year old inhale pepperoni pizza like a machine was an impressive sight) and his pizza and his dad's looked delish.  Others got a meatball sandwich, a steak sandwich and a calzone. Everyone enjoyed their food and had zero room for dessert. Did I mention that the menu is HUGE!   I was impressed by the size and cleanliness of the restaurant. And our server was very sweet and it was her first day! I felt bad that she had to put up with our silliness. She did a great job and asked about refills and boxes and whatnot. They do not have a liquor license but you can bring your own. And my iced tea was fresh brewed and tasty because y'all know I'm a tea snob.  I'll have to go back and try the spinach calzone after hearing Re rave about it... oh and that cranberry salad. Yes I see that in my future.

A group of friends was looking for breakfast on a Sunday morning in Algiers and found this super cute spot. We shared coffee and tea and dined on delicious food and there was something for everyone from vegetarian to eat all the meats. The biscuits are A+  Order at the counter and food is delivered to your table. Prices are very affordable and their is a staff person who is refilling waters and bussing the tables for you. There was even a musician playing quietly in a corner with a tip box out, adding to the ambiance.  There are a few outdoor tables but it was a bit chilly and there were 4 of us. The only thing that could make it better is if they offered Cane syrup in addition to maple.   Will definitely be back.

Reasons to go to Ricca's:  You're trying to match an historic door in your house because the bozos who renovated it have one door mismatched from the rest.  You're looking to replace 19th century hardware to make your transoms actually work.    You really need some pocket doors, columns, mantle, or other random piece.  Have fun & wear closed toe shoes.
They have everything you need (but maybe not the brand you want) and you can be in and out in 15 minutes.  What's not to love.  Oh, and they make yummy sandwiches.

The best thing about the Uptown Whole Foods is that it used to be the bus barn for the city and the architectural transformation is nothing short of miraculous.  But it is small compared to other stores.  The prices are high, but it's also the only location for many go to items. They have some of the best produce in the city.

Pandemic Review: I drive past this space almost every day on my way to work. And I've been really impressed with how Zony has expanded over the last few years. But y'know I don't drink beer so I haven't made visiting a priority.  Fast forward to this week, and there was a small event for Give NOLA Day at this location and I knew a bunch of people who were going. So I went on over not expecting there to be much for me. Boy was I wrong! They had 3 different hard seltzers for me to try, plus a food truck and a band!  Love that it was outside and socially distanced. And while there were portalets outside, you could also go inside (masked of course) to use a real bathroom. Social distancing was good and the employees were great.  And I really liked my hard seltzer! Good job all the way around.

I've always enjoyed the original EatWell on Canal so when I was searching for lunch at Pythian Market, I was excited to see a booth from them!   I had a huge delicious fried tofu banh mi and some shrimp spring rolls. Both took a few minutes to come up which allowed me to wander and see about dessert. My food was delicious and I had enough for another meal.  Counter staff was helpful and efficient.

So the dmv is a fact of life. There are other options sometimes but I needed to renew my driver's license and get a Louisiana real ID. Of course it's always a zoo in the month leading up to my birthday so I planned for an hours long stay.  Step 1: the sorting hat. You go to the front desk and let the person there know why you're there. You get sorted into groups. Handicapped tags, renewals, new plates, whatever.  Step 2: wait for your number I was actually called up pretty quickly. First thing I was asked was if I actually had the proper documents. And I did! Two official documents proving who you are (social security card, birth certificate, passport) and 2 documents proving your address (utility bill and my old driver's license since it has my correct address).  Step 3: have a picture made Go wait for your name to be called and then have your picture made. Then wait for your license to be printed. The printing actually took the bulk of my time as the printer was being repaired as they took my photo and there were 30+ people waiting.  The staff was all pleasant and no nonsense. The new building is really spacious compared to the one in replaced.

Over 3 years later, this is still a favorite. The perfect spot to order a cheese plate for a party or to find a cheese to complement your latest culinary creation  But if you don't believe me that the staff is really knowledgeable? Then check this out: http://www.nola.com/food/index.ssf/2013/07/new_orleanian_is_new_national.html The store manager, Justin Trosclair, is the current supreme cheesemonger in the US. Or y'know a champion of something.  They serve amazing food, sandwiches & salads, and you can order a glass (or bottle) of wine. It does get ridiculously crowded sometimes though.  Last father's day, I went in and asked the staff for the stinkiest/funkiest cheese that they carried as a gift for my Dad. Hoo boy, it was stinky. No I didn't try it and yes, my Dad loved it

I am a fan of a local grocery store that offers good pricing and Breaux Mart fits the bill. The sale prices on Steen's syrup this weekend were great as were pricing on many other holiday baking essentials.   Love the fresh squeezed orange juice machine (near produce by the front door) and this past weekend it had Louisiana satsumas. YUM. Satsuma juice is much more delicate and spoils quicker than regular OJ.   The staff is usually friendly and helpful. Although I got to help the teenage staff in produce on Saturday since he didn't know what a particular vegetable looked like. Adorable and sort of scary.   The parking lot usually has spots available because they police it pretty heavily to keep folks from the nearby restaurants and bars from grabbing all the spaces.  Ran into a colleague in the catering/prepared foods area and he swears by some of their catering items. I know he was picking up sandwiches...and ??? I think he was trying to make sure I didn't follow him home for his party. Please. I was totally not dressed for a party.

I was so done with my own cooking last week and then I happened across Cowbell's Friday special... the Lawrence Fishburger and I just couldn't resist.   I ordered mid afternoon for a dinner time delivery (via Waitr) and because I was getting delivery... I ordered there delish mac-n-cheese and an apple tart too.   All my food was hot when it arrived right on time. And I may have not taken a breath as I wolfed down the 1st half of my tasty sammich. And potatoes are my go to restorative for these crazy times... so you know I ate all the fries too.  The tart was perfect with the sauces packaged separately and I ate half on Friday and half yesterday.  Mac-n-cheese is my lunch today (although of course I sampled a taste already... yummy as always).  PLUS they are doing little #LagniappeTakeoutArt pieces to brighten your day!

Yelp is so weird. I wrote a review of this location at it's grand opening... And my photos are still there but the review poof!  The treats that I bought were delicious. The plum tart (which doesn't appear to be on her regular menu) was particularly amazing and beautiful. And y'all know I am a sucker for iced cookies. Yummy.  The space is lovely and super sparkling white but not sterile. How do places accomplish that?  I need to stop back in and sample more.

New addition to the local tshirt wars. Weirdly the shop is uptown on Magazine just upriver from Napoleon Avenue and not in the Bywater at all. The store is on the small side but they actually have a fair amount of stock for the size.   As their centerpiece is their NOLA Girl line, the shirts do skew a bit more on the feminine side.  The shirt selection is interesting though and I love that they have filled the rest of the small store with items from local artists. The metal signs and voodoo dolls are great.  A great spot if you're looking something for yourself or a gift.

12 years later... guess I'll re-review. I got an FtR for this business in 2009 and I'm still going back.   If you need architectural salvage this is a must stop. And you may need to return on several occasions to get just what you need. I've purchased a window, hardware, trim and a cabinet from Ricca's over the years. When I bought my house I was probably over there monthly.  It can sometimes be a challenge to find someone to assist you but the folks who work there really really know their stuff.   Be careful as you wander the back of the store and handle doors/shutters/windows what not. My recommendation for closed toe shoes still stand. And it's mostly a warehouse so don't expect A/C... or heat if it ever stops being hot.

Pandemic review: Breaux Mart has been my go to grocery for the current insanity. It's small enough to get in and get out quickly and big enough to have almost everything you need.  They were on the front edge of requiring masks and putting up distancing marks and plexi for their checkout people. They even had signs to tell folks to stop fondling the fruit and veg.  The prepared foods are consistently good and y'know I deserve a little container of fried shrimp when I brave the grocery!

I don't know why it took me so long to stop by this yummy spot. I needed donuts for work and passed by and picked up a couple of dozen. They had a great assortment, including a large variety of cake donuts (my favorite).   I was in and out quickly. The donuts were fresh and delicious. Service was courteous and friendly. And I loved my tiger twist, half regular/half chocolate twist glazed donut!  Now if they have apple fritters next time.... I'll be in real trouble.

What a bargain! The lunch prix fixe for $20.12 was a great deal for 3 courses at a super fancy restaurant. Dress was mostly business casual...with a few casual/casual people (yes, I was judging).  There were of course selections not on the prix fixe price and though there were only 2 choices for each course, I was more than happy with what I selected.  The 3 courses last week were a lovely gazpacho blanco with poached shrimp, a gorgeous piece of fish with a light and tasty corn souffle and then for dessert was a really fancy chocolate pudding.  Delicious and a great way to get over the Isaac blahs.  Thanks for the great idea @John LH.  My 15 year old niece was worried that the food would be too fancy but she loved it all.

Short version: Great to work with. They gave good advice and the turn around was fast and affordable.  Long version: Phew. 2021 has not been off to the best start. My Dad passed away and I needed to get a program printed for his service.   I emailed them on a Wednesday morning and discussed what I needed. They gave me some advice on how to improve my program booklet (that I created and saved as a pdf). And quoted a price AND they could have it for me by end of business that day.   Program looks great. The paper was a nice weight and communication was excellent. I forgot to send some details and they were quick to clarify while also being kind.   Price point was great and they were very affordable.  I picked up from their warehouse... the door is not so obvious, FYI. Staff person was masked and payment was quick.

Ummm why haven't I been here before?! This was a friend's choice for her recent birthday lunch and WOW!  We were a group of 6 and they were super accommodating to our group. We had a wide variety of food and drink but I ordered the ceviche Nikkei, the papas a la huancaina, and the special gazpacho of the day (OMG made with avocado and cucumbers with shrimp - just heaven). Oh, and their local sangria (which packs a bit of a punch). All the food was simply delicious. I would like to go back right now and eat it all again.  Service was outstanding. And the space is lovely as ever.

Pandemic update:  My last review was when the business still went by another name and it's still a supercute shop. They carry a bunch of local artists/crafters and have a great selection of souveniers/NOLA themed gifts. The folks who work in the shop are always friendly and helpful.  I was here a couple of months ago to pick up MG themed signs so my Mom could have a virtual parade in her front yard for Yardi Gras. I had ordered online so pickup was easy.  Staff was wearing masks; customers were required to wear masks too. Hand sanitizer was available. Great experience all the way around.

Wow! So my previous shop closed it's doors spring 2020 and so far the person who had been cutting my hair for almost a decade has still not gotten back in the biz. Hunting for a new stylist is the WORST.  It had been 16 months without a cut and my hair was trying to murder me. I wanted a space that felt safe (with all COVID precautions) and had online booking and after hunting around. Then looking at reviews in various places, I decided that I would give Jen a shot.   First of all... great name! And all appointments are done with online booking and her Covid protocols were clear and precise. I like that she's a one person shop so I won't have to worry about some other client's behavior.   And my cut? I love it! I feel like she gave me great shape and understood what I was looking for. Plus the pricing was great!   The location is in an old warehouse but she's made her space really lovely and cozy. Plus bonus dog kisses while you are there!  Next stop? Professionally dyed blue hair!

It's been over a decade since I last updated my WF review. And the entire chain has been purchased by new owners...   Some things are the same. The quality of the produce is still great. As is the cheese selection and the bulk aisle. The staff is always helpful and really nice.  I feel like the items in the hot bar have gone a bit downhill (all locations).   The parking lot can be a bit insane, especially with the small spaces and giant vehicle issue. Also people don't pay attention to the posted signage. OTH I saw an honest to goodness Delorean in the parking lot AND saw the driver open the gull wing doors, so that's the best thing ever.

Whew. I had Russell's clean my favorite rug and it looks beautiful.  It came back to me in perfect condition...minus dog urine so Yay! (hazards of an elderly canine companion).  Let me clarify this is not really the rug location; you're supposed to head out to Metairie, but because of confusion on my part and that my rug wasn't too big (about 5x5) and that I was already there, they took it. It was ready sooner than I was promised and was delivered back to the Tulane location, saving me a trip to Metry.  The confusion was that I was looking for Klein's which used to be down the block (and I had used them previously, pre-K) and when I called the Klein's number (found on the internets), I just asked what time they closed.  Turns out Russell's bought Klein's and that I wasn't paying attention to the name when they answered.  Hilarity ensued...OK, not hilarity but y'know life isn't a sit-com.  Price was reasonable and I'm a happy camper and so is my dog as she is currently lounging on the newly cleaned rug.

So I needed beaucoup crab for a family party a couple of weekends ago and I called around and it was $$ no matter where I looked. I asked over on the twitters for suggestions and someone said try the Shrimp Lot. So I decided a westbank adventure was just what I needed...  The directions from Google maps are junk. You're looking for the corner of Louisiana and Westbank Expressway. If you see the big Westwego carved sign on the neutral ground...the shrimp lot is on the other side.  The lot is comprised of individual businesses set up in lean-tos, sheds, and buildings. Each person has a different selection and different prices. When I was there on a Friday afternoon about half the businesses were occupied. There were a few wholesalers mixed in with the fresh catch items.   Prices for shrimp and crabs were excellent and this would be a great choice to buy for your next big boil. The already picked crab? It was only about a $1 less than my go to spot in Old Jefferson.   But y'know westbank adventure!

Pandemic update: I was looking for outdoor dining that took reservations on Easter Sunday and Sala was open and had space on their front patio. The tables outside were nicely distanced from each other. Which was great since even post-vaccination, I worry about all the things. The staff was lovely.  The three of us enjoyed our brunch items, and we opted for a carafe of mimosas rather than bottomless which worked well for the driver (me), a senior (mom) and a friend. I had eggs sardou which were good, mom really enjoyed her eggs pontchartrain and my friend liked her Kentucky hot brown, plus we ordered fruit cups and a biscuit. The fruit cups were more like finger food for children but otherwise OK.  Staff was masked and the tables were well spread. Indoor dining was happening, including as large groups.

The little grocery that could...  I've been shopping with Zara's for decades. They are a solid choice for a quick shopping trip or some tasty takeout.  They have a good selection of all the basics and often do boiled crawfish or BBQ as well.   These days they are also offering curbside/delivery of groceries via email/phone call. And have prepared foods on a couple of the other apps.  It is hard to be 6 feet away from anyone else in such a small store. But you can also get in and out quick quick.

How anyone has given them more than one star I don't know.  (Sorry Allison) Seriously, they are one confused agency.  I so wish the efforts to privatize them had worked a couple of years ago.  Not that I'm normally for privatization of public entities but anything would be better.  My favorite example of their insanity is that their was a leak (pre-K) at Napoleon & Loyola for a good 3 months.  The water was bubbling up into the street.  When did the crew show up to repair the leak?  On July 4th. Can you say triple overtime?

I've spent many good meals inside this former church when it was Christian's and the last time I ate here was when it was Redemption. So I was happy to see what was up with the newest incarnation for a late lunch on a Friday.  We wandered in without a reservation but that wasn't a problem. Since it was a gorgeous April day, the outside dining was hopping but inside there were only 2 other tables so we chose to sit inside at one of the communal high top tables.   We each had a cocktail and shared a cheese plate which was gorgeous! Then my friend had a burger and I had the chopped salad with grilled shrimp. The shrimp were delicious and the salad was fresh. My friend enjoyed her burger and I might have stolen a fry or two from the huge pile!  Cocktails were on point. I of course had an old fashioned and she had a punch. They both tasted like more, but we both needed to stay functional for the rest of our Friday.  Service was good but there only seemed to be 2 people working FoH and they were slammed. Everyone was masked and felt safe.  Will definitely be back for their happy hour so we can glow in that gorgeous light!

Pandemic update: Last night I took a chocolate and cheese class online from St James. The ordering for the class was super easy and since I was going to pick up...  I bought myself lunch as well.  Their website is very easy to use. And they prefer all orders to happen on there but they will also do a custom cheese selection (some cheeses are on the website too) as they have time; don't call during the lunch rush!  First yesterday's lunch... the manchego salad was delicious with fresh crisp pears and savory manchego cheese plus the dressing... yum! I also bought a Creole tomato sandwich for today's lunch... which is a seasonal special.  The cheese and chocolate class (St James and Piety & Desire) was super fun and interesting and actually a great value for all the cheese and chocolate you get (more cheese than chocolate of course). The bleu cheese with a warm spice chocolate was a revelation! And I love how super nerdy/knowledgeable both our cheesemonger Molly and choclatier Chris were about their specialties.   Check out their events page for future fun!  Pandemic notes: You cannot even go in the courtyard of the building. Everything is handed over from the balcony seating at the moment. There is a sign up asking you to order from the website (where you can specify a time for pick up and square will text you - if you wish- when your order is ready.) Good use of masks and gloves and appropriate distancing!

Wow! Since Harahan is part of my old stomping grounds, I kidnapped Lindsay and we stopped in for dinner to celebrate St. Joseph's day.  And I ordered all the foods because the menu looked so amazing.  I started with the caesar salad which was yummy and very garlicy, in a good way. Then had a seafood antipasto dish which was also delicious but small for the $11...but I get it because the seafood was amazing. THEN the verdure pizza and after the first bite I was all "this olive oil is amazing" and Lindsay thought I had lost my mind until she took a bite and said the same thing. THEN I had the pasta parpardelle  (I'm sure I'm spelling that wrong) which was also delicious and now I need to learn to make homemade past because...oh so good.    Yep, it's an old Popeye's where one of my HS besties worked. And the space is small but they've done a good job making it clean and elegant. The night I was there it wasn't too noisy but I could see how it could get loud. Our service was fine...attentive to distracted depending on the tables around us. I'll definitely be trekking out here again and am recommending it to all my friends in the area.

I'm on the prowl for a pretty specific tile for my bathroom floor. Since this is the local big box store for flooring (that isn't general home improvement store) AND it's open on weekends/after office hours, this was one of my first stops.  The layout is actually pretty easy to use. And the tiles are well marked as floor or wall or whatever. There are a LOT to choose from but I knew pretty much what I was looking for.  I wandered through snapped some pics to consider later and was in/out pretty quick. They do have good sales on short stock in various locations around the store.  Ultimately I didn't find exactly what I want so back to the drawing board.

Almost 5 years later, this is still one of my favorite local markets. It has live music and puppies (rescue groups with adoptables) and lunch (lots to choose from) and crafts. It's just a great way to spend an afternoon.   Last weekend I had a watermelon lemonade, crawfish pasta for lunch, petted a few rescue pups, AND watched the band and a toddler interpretive dance to their music. I perused the crafts and the costume sale they were having in the back.  So much fun and you never know who you'll run into. And what you might be able to take home with you.

Great spot for very unique (hey it's in the name) housewares, clothing, jewelry or gifts. They have lots of recycled/upcycled items, as well as some of the clothing lines that Big Life Toys carried when it was in this location. Plus Adorn & Conquer is in their loft space (but is a separate business).   The staff was courteous but let you browse; the store can be a little jammed with stock which makes it a bit difficult if there are a bunch of people shopping, especially on the weekend before Christmas.   Definitely a place to stop and buy a present that will make your recipient ask "where did you get that?!"

Do you see how many checkins I have? This spot has my go to soup when I'm sick, the tamarind tofu, my picky youngest niece's favorite soup, the kid's chicken noodle (which has broth, chicken and rice noodles and that's it). And enough variety to feed whomever else I'm with.  The lunch banh mi and soup deal is a good one. And the tofu/avocado bowl is still a favorite. I got the seared tuna the other day and it was delicious with really good quality fish.  The staff is polite and friendly and the whole place is speedy in its turnarounds.

I should finish this long languishing review of the SoBou bar now, since the lovely Abigail will no longer be running their program.   I always plan to eat at the restaurant and somehow it never happens. I just end up hanging out at the bar and having snacks. The cone with tuna and avocado ice cream is delicious.  They make an *EXCELLENT* old fashioned and this includes the special carnival one that had a king cake baby encased in ice...king cake baby Han Solo!  The space is inviting and modern while honoring the exposed brick and history one expects in the FQ. The staff has always been wonderful to me. The happy hour is a great deal from 3 to 6 every day of the week with food and cava for $4.  Now I just need to unpark my caboose from a bar stool and actually eat dinner here.

Pretty & pricey. I saw a gorgeous silk & velvet "personal" quilt and then saw the price tag. Whew. But then I was pleasantly surprised that there were some affordable items.  The bedding, especially the canopy up front, is like a fantasy world...or a movie set, very inspiring.  I regret that I didn't buy any of the ant sculptures that I saw there...

Really this spot (which has poor exterior lighting and signage at night) is probably a 3. It's pretty bare bones Vietnamese. ACCEPT I had the curried tofu bun this evening and it was super tasty.  As this is a spin on the dish that I haven't had elsewhere and I really liked it, they get a plus 1 star. My dining companion loved her crispy fried egg rolls (and they looked really meaty) and her pork banh mi.  Y'know they may have gotten that star anyway for being open on a Sunday evening.  The servers were brisk and the menu is limited. The space is pretty stark and can be loud when full, but it's clean. And they take credit cards.   In conclusion, not my first choice, but I can see craving the curried tofu again.

I love their new space inside the Rink. The light is amazing...thanks to the skylights. And the shop is open and airy. They've added a variety of items from different designers so now they have tshirts and cards in addition to jewelry.  I stopped in last week and bought gifts for 3 nieces with fall birthdays. They are still setting the store up so I'll have to check back soon to see what they've added. They are having a grand opening party for the new space on the evening of November 5th.

I was wondering how the Roman Candy Man had less then 5 stars and then I realized that the FTR has a fundamental misunderstanding of how he works.    First, ignore the address and phone number listed. I'm not sure what that's about.  2nd, stalk the cart via it's twitter feed: https://twitter.com/RomanCandy   3rd, if the mule is working then be prepared to find the cart since the mule wanders where he (she?) likes.  4th, enjoy some tasty old school taffy and watch out for your fillings.  5th, if they are selling cotton candy, buy some. It is delicious and freshly made.

Took the out of town niece & nephew to the new splash park at the zoo (+$5) and they had a ball.  It's a great addition to the park.  Plus we got to feed turtles and oggle the animals.  Why do I love the smell of the rhinoceros area?  Maybe it's the combo of rhino, zebra & wildebeast/gnu.    I also noticed the zoo is featuring the oak trees a bit more. Glad to see these elder statesmen getting the attention they deserve.

OK. It's a sushi place that has a roll called the Sexiest Man. C'mon you know you want to try it. (see my pic)  I've been here for dinner/takeout a couple of times. And the sushi is really fresh. The staff is nice and helpful, attentive without hovering.   The restaurant is a bit dark but that might make it a good date place. The fish prices are a bit high but then again the quality has always been good and I'm suspicious of discount fish. I need to remember the non-sushi items on the list and try some of those sometime.  And I definitely need to try get over there for their lunch specials.

Tasty fancy hot dogs. They're everywhere these days. Dreamy weenies has both super meaty & vegan options (which you can make unvegan by adding cheese) and lots of fancy toppings. The staff is helpful and can help you make choices.  Yes the dogs are a bit pricey but they're really big so I felt like I got my money's worth...and I feel like I'm supposed to make some sort of double entendre at this point...but disappointingly nothing comes to mind.   Definitely a spot I'll go again for a quick & filling meal in the FQ.

So I was meeting friends here, and when I finally figured out which building they were talking about (in the dark), then I couldn't figure out which door was the entrance...turns out there are two. So confusing.   Once I found myself inside, I enjoyed the clean but clubby atmosphere. I enjoyed my time at the bar and will have to put this sot on my list of places to try for dinner when I'm in this part of town.   Since I was early, I was at the bar by myself for a bit and was made welcome which is a plus in any establishment.

I thought I was all burned out on parades and then I run across a 1980ish documentary on our local PBS station recounting that year's carnival season and it was AWESOME. Bacchus still went into the Rivergate (RIP) and Krewe of Clones was still parading.  Seriously WYES does some great local programming, including the bizarrety that is the Meeting of the Courts on Mardi Gras night.  Ooh! And John Besh cooking on Justin Wilson's old set. Love!  AND they bring me the national PBS shows like Antiques Roadshow, Nature, and Sesame Street...because sometimes you just want to hang out with Grover.

I was only going to give this gas station my standard 3 stars because y'know it has gas & is brightly lit. But seriously, these were the fastest pumps ever.  So yay for that.  The store seemed really busy on Friday night, but I didn't need any stuff.  Only negative (or was it...since it was talking to me) was that the TV screen on my pump was stuck/broken.  Telling me that it was 40 degrees on Friday night just made me laugh.

I think the re-signing of Deuce McCallister today has sent the city into pure insanity.  I cannot explain the level of excitement that his return is generating.  Through all the years of the Aints & the rumors of Superdome curses, we have stayed true to our boys.    My youngest brother still talks about the Return to the Dome game in Fall of 06 as a highpoint in his life. The streets around the Dome were certainly insane that's true.

Palmer Park has a brand new jungle gym for the kiddies and it's pretty impressive.  Lots of fun interactive parts as well as traditional slides and swings.  And the park is kept so clean by the neighbors (and the Arts Market folks).  Really a lovely spot.

It saddens me to change my review for this place from 4 to 2 stars.  I've been going here for over 2 years.  And I was pretty sure the owners changed late last year.  And the place has just gone down hill.    The attention to detail isn't there.  They are no longer autoclaving their tools that I can tell (cleanliness is #1 on my list) and the place just seems to be a bit of a mess.  I have felt like I'm in someone's living room with kids eating pizza & lounging around.  Guess I'm shopping around again...

Oops I clearly didn't keep my promise in 2012. Guess it's time for an update.  So Druids has an identity crisis. I really like their tree themed floats. And they're satirical so normally that would be a yay...but their *satire* is really pretty dumb/mean spirited. Every year a float fighting with/insulting the women's krewes. Yawn.  They also like to pretend that they are an old line krewe but they are a youngster having not even paraded for 20 years...consider the oldest krewes are well over 100 years old then you'll see why this is an upstart.  I'm always enthusiastic for this parade because it does kick off the marathon. I just wish they were a bit stronger...in theme and in branded throws.

Over the years, I have had some really fun WLN and some really boring ones but there are two threads that run through all of them. 1. It's mind numbingly hot. 2. Most people are about the scene and not the art.   So if you know an artist and/or gallery owner and hang out in their space most of the night, WLN is pretty awesome. But if you're wandering the streets in search of water or food, maybe not.

Freret Street Market happens on the first Saturday of every month from noon until 5.  Vendors include crafters, caterers, junk sellers, and produce vendors.  Every month is different.  It's a great market and has a really funky feel in comparison to a lot of the other neighborhood markets.  I'm walking over in a few minutes.  See you there!

Once upon a time this was the portage from the Lake to the Mississippi. Now it's a great place to kayak, walk your dog, play some volleyball, etc.  Definitely a neighborhood and area to take visiting tourists to give them a different view of the city.  It's a great neighborhood waterway...sort of like all of our neighborhood graveyards.

She must be doing something right since they were sold out of the chicken cordon bleu when we walked up. I opted for the Bbq shrimp sliders which were really tasty & well balanced. The shrimp might have been too spicy without the bread. Bonus that you get a choice between chips & creamy potato salad.   I will definitely start stalking this truck around NOLA

I honestly can't remember when I lost saw Zulu in person... It's difficult to make it out of bed so early on carnival morning and walk over to the parade; Zulu follows it's own route...which is a couple of miles from my house. But this year my niece and I made it!  LOVED the walking Zulu warriors, one of whom handed me a coconut so score!  Love the costumes. Also the fire truck krewe was great with unique throws to their little group.  But many of the folks on the floats seemed disinterested in being in a parade. Maybe it was the cold but lots of riders were on their phones or drinking and not really paying attention to the adoring crowds at their sides.   I'm definitely going to make it back down to see them next year...I hope in better weather.

I went on the grand opening weekend so there were a bajillion employees in the store and I was offered help almost that many times. Everyone on staff was really nice and if they didn't know the answer to my question, then they found someone who did.  The store is clean and shiny as befits a brand new location. The signage was clear and while some areas were understocked...like the shipments hadn't made it in for opening day, in general I found the selection to be great.  Yes, this is a chain store, but a national chain in Orleans Parish is a reason to celebrate. This new location is walkable from my house rather than a drive out to the suburbs.

Since I'm the duchess here and I love my stylist, I guess it's time to update.  Nicole has been cutting/coloring my hair for a few years now. I always get complements on both. Despite the fact that my hair still has a mind of its own, Nicole is able to work with it and make me look presentable.  The space is open and airy (although on the 2nd floor so if you have issues with stairs then this place isn't for you). The salon staff is lovely and I love getting my confirmation text messages in advance.

Much smaller menu than the original westbank location with about 1/4 the seating as well. But they also offer solid Vietnamese in the FQ for a good price. So basically heaven!  They offer many basic Vietnamese dishes and some vegetarian fare. Like with most places, ask about fish sauce so you won't get a surprise. I had the lemongrass tofu bun and it was delicious and just the right amount of food for me.  Service was quick and courteous and the space is small but airy. I was surprised to see they had a liquor license, maybe only beer and wine. But they didn't complain when folks wandered in with drinks in hand. I also noticed several police officers (station is a couple of doors down) picking up takeout and enjoying the cuisine.

Wow. This was my first time in this thrift store since they moved from the strip mall across the street. Their space has doubled; it's HUGE.  The clothes are sorted by gender and then by color (which is a little weird but works).    Today there were men trying on dresses for the Buddy D dress parade happening tomorrow in honor of the Saints in the superbowl so that was pretty entertaining.  The store was so crowded that I actually wasn't too successful, but perhaps another time without the pushy grandmas & screaming babies.

So Yelp will not allow me to add a different address for this company because Google maps does not believe it exists, but MapQuest does. Weird.  Doesn't really matter since they will probably come to you & the phone number is the same.  We used these folks (who do seem to have 2 names which is a little confusing..the other is Harmon Auto Glass) to put in out brand new fantastic looking frameless glass shower surround.  It looks marvelous.  Justin was really professional and seemed to know his stuff. They came out once and measured and then came back for the installation once the wall/door was fabricated.  I'll edit after I take my first shower in there tomorrow morning.  Can't wait!

I want to like Funky Monkey more and their NOLA (and hipster) themed tshirts would normally ensure that I would, but...  I don't know what's up with the staff attitude. It's difficult to get someone to assist you...in a create your own tshirt shop - sketch. And the last time I was in there with my 70+ year old Mom, they acted like she was a shoplifter. Because my Mom is a highly suspicious looking grandma.  As for the vintage stuff, I've never really shopped it.

After being wowed by this new restaurant at a Yelp event, I went back for an early dinner on a Monday night... and by the time we left the place was pretty crowded...on a Monday in July!  I shared a bunch of small plates with my friend and they were all delicious and then I thought I might explode. I had the Fogerty cocktail with bourbon and peaches, very tasty and tart! My friend had the brown butter old fashioned (which I had sampled the last time) and thought it was as delicious as I did.  We shared the oyster gratin, the pickled shrimp (and they offered bread in addition to the pork rinds...or even crudite), roasted asparagus, and the cucumber salad. The cucumber salad was summer in a bowl, simple and delicious and the cucumbers were perfectly cut to absorb maximum dressing. The pickled shrimp were amazing and the white bean hummus was great. Honestly it was all good.  AND then we were stuffed and the server told us that the dessert special (now on the regular menu) was a pots de creme made with cane syrup. Oh yummmy  Service was great and the location is lovely.

I stopped in for an exhibit of old newspapers during Tales. All the vintage NOLA papers had to do with prohibition and were super fun to read. And if it hadn't been for this exhibit, I wouldn't have known this place existed.  There was a Old New Orleans Rum tasting and I sampled their 300th anniversary rum (again), so tasty. But let's discuss the bar's candied old fashioned. Phew. It was no joke with a bit of candied orange peel to top it off, well-balanced and potent. The pecan syrup was a nice addition.  There were some snacks associated with the exhibit but after a couple of cocktails we decided that a "bread & spread" was necessary AND 1/2 price during HH. So we tried the art & spin...artichoke and spinach. Super tasty and it came out quickly.   Our bartender was on point and my friend and I had a great time.

As many times as I've been to the Hilton, I've never actually stayed here. My review is exclusively for their meeting rooms.  The Hilton does have a variety of sized rooms to accommodate many groups. Unfortunately, many of them give the feeling of being in a dungeon thanks to the low ceilings and the lack of windows.   The staff ranges from incredibly helpful to indifferent, depending. The lobby does offer many seating areas for informal gathering but as others have said, it is dated and could use some sprucing.

I love how this strip of a park has developed over the years. It's now a lush green space with a fountain where you often find children playing and dogs frolicing.   Since many of the people who live in the area do not have a ton of yardspace, many make this their defacto front yard which is fun to observe and not crash (unless invited of course).   Love that the trees are lush and beautiful right now despite the cold winter...or maybe because of it. Now I just wish some neighbor with a green thumb would plant some flower beds to enhance the beauty.

Maybe the blush of new love is over. Yes, I'm still a fan of this Target, but not as enamored as I once was.   It's common to find entire sections devoid of stock. And some areas look like a tornado has just swept through and everything is a jumble. On my last visit the store was the dirtiest I've ever seen it and it wasn't even a big sale weekend or anything.  The staff is generally helpful. I still like the basket escalators (when they work) and I still go when I need to stock up on housewares and groceries and cleaning products. But I wish this store would get a little bit of TLC.   3.5 stars.

I journeyed to this place for Pho with a bunch of friends and I was apprehensive since I had heard it was a very meaty place.  Since I do eat seafood I was able to find something to eat. The staff was really nice about making something custom with noodles and shrimp and no beef or chicken broth. But that meant no pho for me.  It is a cafeteria like space, so very no frills.    This is probably more like a 3 star joint but they get bumped up a star for being accommodating to my food demands AND because the crab rangoon was delicious. Seriously, not overthick with cream cheese and the crab was present and tasty plus it was just a little spicy.  Seriously, I might stop back by just for a to go order of crab ragoon.

Plum offers electic gifts, tshirts, and jewelry many with NOLA themes. I have a ring from them that started life as a starlight mint.  I have been tempted by the Peeps jewelry a few times, but have always decided I would rather eat Peeps than wear them.

This is a weird PJs. Why are there so many things for sale?  The counters are littered with jewelry and touristy displays.    My iced tea was fine. But my cookie? It tasted pre-packaged and  yucky.  Staff is courteous to indifferent like most coffee shops. Not my first choice unless I'm hitting up another spot in the strip mall.

We came in for lunch on their first Sunday.  E got the vegetable plate and the server was really careful to discuss with him which items contained meat and what didn't.  He ended up with okra & tomatoes, slaw, and green beans.  All three were tasty; the green beans were super buttery and garlicy and cooked to retain yummy crispness.  The okra & tomatoes were heavier opposite my perfect ratio (2:1 okra but that made them the perfect ratio for E...takes all kinds).  The corn bread was def not NOLA but was still yummy but not at all sweet.    I had the crab & corn bisque which was delicious; the crab quality was first rate but the soup was maybe a bit too thick.  I also tried the chop salad which was really nice and fresh.  I REALLY wanted to try their dessert special of the day but will have to go there another time.  The wine list looked interesting and I hope to make it back for cocktails soon.    Seriously though, a brand new restaurant that doesn't have a webpage? That's just crazy talk. I'm so glad I found the hours of operation on the Gambit blog.

I feel like I should hurry up and finish this long overdue review since Feelings is up for sale!  First OMG this spot is gorgeous, the perfect blend of casual elegance and exposed brick. The staff was uniformly lovely and went out of their way to take care of my group.   My old fashioned, my fish dish, my salad (seasonal so probably not on the menu now) were all perfect and delicious. Seriously why was 2015 my first time eating here?!  I can see why this restaurant was named most romantic and my group of friends were certainly feeling the love...platonic naturally.

People LOVE this joint, but it's not my favorite. Yes it's kind of awesome to do your laundry and drink ...BUT your wet clothes will absorb all the stinky smoke in the bar like a sponge...or at least that's what my friends who've done laundry there report to me.  If there is a band playing it's LOUD. The crowd can be interesting....the other night there was a person full on passed out on the sidewalk outside the bar which isn't that uncommon.   I think I prefer day drinking here. And I must admit I don't think I've eaten here ever...in over a decade?

Loved the stations of the cross and the new and weathered tombs, but the gem of this cemetery is the chapel. Loved the ceiling...I wish I knew the architectural term. I'll have to bring Vicky L with me next time. And the alcove with the "milagri" (ha! I know the Spanish term but not the English) was really moving.   Not so good? tourists cutting up and acting the fool. Look I get that you're on vacation and WOOHOO drinkypants, but show some respect.
Essential for local music.  Great selection of used CDs and vinyl.

The food here was OK to pretty good, but I thought the prices were high for what they were offering.  The cocktails were fine.  AND I love that this corner is no longer a rotting hulk.  But here's my issue, I find the inside a bit schizo. The tile & wood work are gorgeous and scream fancy-pants restaurant (as do the prices). But then you realize there are big screen tvs all over the place on random channels (it's not like there was a Saints game on) and piped in music. C'mon.  Decide on who you want to be.  For these prices, turn off the tv and the music.  Service-wise our waiter was struggling but was making a clear effort so I was kudos for that.  Even though it's in my hood, I don't know that I'll head back anytime soon...maybe if I need to seat a big group since there aren't that many spacious restaurants in this part of town.

While others have had huge issues with Cox, I've been a mostly satisfied customer. Maybe it's that I get a discount for my internet throught my work (Yay!) or that it was such a monopoly for so long that I don't expect much. Yes, it's too expensive, but sometimes I'm a lazy couch potato who wants to laze and stare at the tv for hours on end.  This retail location was completely painless. I picked up my new HD box and was in and out of the store in 10 minutes. The folks on the phone to setup my tv & internet (didn't want to pay someone else, thank you very much) were all professional and helpful.    Maybe my experience atypical but everything went fine.

I've had this spot bookmarked forever as a to try place. Sadly the GNO is not overflowing with great Indian food and now this place is included. I stopped in too hungry so ordered WAY too much food.   I ordered navrattan korma, bhindi masala, vegetable pakoras and naan. The Pakoras were tasty. The korma was OK. The bhindi was pretty much inedible...canned tomatoes and so much oil...okra cooked to mush. And the naan was ok. What's sad is the bhindi was recommended by a staff member as a 2nd vegetarian dish.   So I won't be going out of my way to go there again. Perhaps the buffet is more successful.

Well lit and the pumps mostly work.  Do watch out for the shady characters that John mentions.  I've been hit up for change at this gas station more than any other.  The store has the most random stuff, but that's a good thing.

I love the Endymion fiberoptics and that they parade AWAY from my house. I was able to catch the parade across from Warren Easton HS this year and it was a great spot. Lots of alums were out to cheer on the band as it marched in the parade. Love seeing the local pride. The bands were great and, of course, the riders were super generous with their throws.   This year was extra awesome, I brought my niece to see her Daddy ride AND I got to bring awesome PDX Yelpers Melvin & Merilou to their very 1st carnival parade. It was really fun to see the parade through their eyes and my niece  had a ton of fun and the crowd was not too aggressive or pushy.  Plus I love the esoteric themes, so Endymion goes to the opera was right up my alley. Definitely a great parade...to see away from Orleans Ave.

Still a solid choice especially for the beer drinker, although they can make a basic cocktail here. The patio is awesome ...until it rains on you or when you decide to sit outside to avoid the smoke on one of NOLA's rare freezing evenings. Thank goodness for heaters and the bar supplied blankets.   The staff is usually good and if you can catch the kitchen when it's open, the snacks are tasty.
I love the tamarind soup here.  And the tofu & avocado salad is really light and different.  No liquor license but you can get something from the Shell next door if you're in need.

Posting a whole slew of reviews for stores I hit with my Mom on Black Friday. I have never ordered stationery with this store so I can't comment on their service or selection.  BUT they do have a lovely gift ideas, pens, fancy notebooks, NOLA themed Christmas cards.

I used Singer last summer to put custom cabinets in my kitchen.  Despite having to switch sales people in the middle of the job, I was really pleased with the service.  They helped me design the layout, choose materials, and make decisions based on time constraints.  And the kitchen is gorgeous.  They even replaced a drawer front & cabinet door with no problem.  (Drawer front was missing a spot of finish and cabinet door was slightly warped).

My FIL used to get half of all his meals here.  They have a variety of NOLA specialty items (shrimp creole, stuffed bell peppers, etc) both fresh and frozen.  They also do catering for events.  My only criticism is that since much of their takeout clientele are seniors, everything needs salt.  But that's easy to add.

This is one of my friends' go to restaurants. Consistent and delicious, it is a great neighborhood restaurant.  All dishes can be customized to ingredients and to heat.    Their curries are very good and the steamed mussel appetizer is amazing.  I'm also a big fan of their cucumber salad.

So I don't really get why folks are disappointed with Charlie's. It was EXACTLY what I expected.  Old school decor (or lack thereof), basic delicious food, and an overall great experience, even for someone who doesn't eat beef.  We were the first to arrive for a friend's birthday dinner here.  So we had cocktails at the bar.  And while service was perfect, my old fashioned was really heavy on the bitters...like I should have sent it back heavy.  But I will definitely go back to give it another try.  We were seated in the downstairs dining room and no there aren't any menus.  I missed part of the ordering process but I know the bday friend had asked in advance about the availability of....TUNA!  That's right, the super secret menu item is tuna steaks, sometimes.  You can even call in advance and ask.  I would have been content with the potatoes and the salad and the onion rings, but, dang, they cook a mighty fine tuna steak too.  And mine came out a perfect red rare.  The service was efficient and helpful without being officious.  And dessert was a selection of ice creams from Angelo Brocato's. Oh, spumoni, my childhood fave, how I still love you.

Posting a whole slew of reviews for stores I hit with my Mom on Black Friday. Hazelnut is owned by local Broadway/TV celeb, Brian Batt and it's biggest claim to fame is the New Orleans themed toile.  The store carries a variety of upscale & trendy home decor items.  It's a small store with a lot of stock (especially during the Christmas shopping season) so be careful.  Yes, another store where I'm afraid of knocking everything over.

I stopped going to this salon a while back.  I liked my stylist but the salon itself was never my fave.  Love the old building that used to be a jail.  But it never seemed super clean to me.  And there were always dirty coffee cups everywhere. Yay for not using disposable, but boo for never washing them...until the receptionist did at the next shampoo station one day.  Yuck

When you see this tree, you can't help but be stunned.  It is so beautiful and welcoming and stately.   Growing up,  we called this tree the grandfather oak but I have heard the Tree of Life for many years.   I spent some of my last hours with my dog Bosco under this tree. We knew it was time since his kidneys were failing. One last romp under this tree with a tennis ball...  The location is in the part of Audubon Park known as Laurel Street,  near to where they installed a labyrinth.

Yay! My precious is like new again. After reading online the shenanigans needed to change the battery on my Nexus 6p (removing the camera glass? Nope). I started searching for a local place to have it done. And I ended up here.  I ordered and paid for a new battery on September 2nd and a swift 8 days later (1 day delay because of the Monday holiday), my battery had arrived. I rearranged my Sunday and dropped off my phone. I wandered around shopping (and feeling bereft without my precious).  Wait time was supposed to be 2 hours but it was done quicker.   Techs were good at explaining and communicating and I'm loving the restored battery life. Would definitely return.

I should start by saying that I am not a beer drinker, but I can appreciate  that the Bulldog offers a plethora of beers to choose from for the aficionado.  The Bulldog was one of the locations of weekly meetings that I had with my coworkers post-K while we were all working from home and displaced from our building.  It was the perfect location to sit outside and enjoy a Monday afternoon in the early spring.

It's time once again for my annual Magazine-Street-Black-Friday-Shopping-Extravaganza with my Mom.  This shop has t-shirts, locally themed barware, fun gift items and jewelry.  Purchases yesterday included pilsner glasses and really cute cuff bracelet.    The owner is very helpful and really the stock in this shop is so varied, you have to check back often to see what's new.
