The real Keller Branch is a gorgeous historic home (built 1918) and was only converted to a public library in the mid 90s.  That building is still under going extensive renovations.  I think the plan is to shore up/stabilize the original structure and then put a major addition on to the back which will more than double the size of the library.  Great...when it ever happens.  For now the library is a portable unit in the side yard.  It is conducting basic business... you can have materials shipped here from other branches who have collections; there are children's books and computers.    Supposedly the renovation will be complete this year; let's hope.

I hadn't actually been in the store in it's "new" location...yes I know they moved 2 years ago.  Can I just say I LOVE the new space! Spacious and airy and bright!!! And when I had to run in to purchase a couple of last minute Christmas presents, I found parking around the corner and was in and out in less than 30 minutes!  The staff is still top-notch. They are knowledgeable and friendly and offer amazing service. Love that their is a Swamp Shop to support WWOZ inside the store.  Definitely the place to stop to get your local music fix.

The menu is slim for vegetarians, but the couscous that accompanied the scallops I had were   veggie/vegan friendly I think (not sure about butter) AND OMG it was good. My entire group loved their dishes from burgers to sides. Loved the salad of the day which featured tomatoes and radishes.  Dining outside is quieter if you can stand the heat. We did have some other patrons who were... a bit overindulged/never eaten anywhere beyond fast food/IDK. The clued in person apologized to my table as they left. I thought it was funny but not everyone I was with did.  SOLID cocktails (delicious old fashioned) and a good beer list.

C'mon folks it's the GOVERNMENT. Do you really expect efficiency?  Maybe I'm just jaded.  I had to get a new driver's license for the first time in 8 years since I moved (no, I won't tell you my address).  I verified what I needed from the DMV website (old license, proof of insurance, cash) and waited.    The first line is definitely the more annoying.  You file around like a robot until the receptionist can sort you into your respective section (new license, handicap tag, insurance issue, reinstatement, whatever).  That took about an hour and the line was out the door, but the movement was pretty steady.  So I mostly just felt bad for the old people who were wearing out; maybe they should bring a pinch line stander.  The second line was quick-quick.  I went and sat in the the chairs until my number was called.  That took maybe 20 minutes, I gave my new address, signed my life away.  Waited in a quick line to pay the cashier and then took my took picture (my hair looks terrible) and was out the door.  Honestly, I expected to be there for hours so less than 90 minutes seemed quick, especially considering the volume of people.

One assessor. Wow what a difference.  If you're a homeowner in New Orleans, you've dealt with the assessor's office. Honestly every experience I've had with them has been professional and easy. I KNOW a government office, who knew.  When I bought my house, we were still under the old 7 assessor thing...which honestly was mostly confusing. Everything was paper based and staff scoffed when I asked about submitting anything via email or even fax.  I let my homestead exemption go when I stopped living in the house I owned for a few years and when I needed it restored, it couldn't have been easier. I called the one assessor and they mailed me some documents and I sent them back. Easypeasy.  FF to now, the housing prices in my 'hood have gone bezerk so my reassessment, which I knew was coming, was harsh. So I went in (open enrollment is July 15-August 15) spoke to a staff person with paperwork in hand and 30 minutes later had a small adjustment and they had the correct dimensions for my house. Whew.  Also, I love that the database is all online, so I can find out who actually owns the houses around me.   Good job!

After our first experience, we went to High Hat maybe another handful of times.  And the food was always OK to good to pretty good, until the last time.  The special of the day was shrimp creole, Yum! right? And the sauce was pretty good, but the shrimp which should have been mighty tasty were inedible.  Why? Because they hadn't been cleaned properly.  Since they hadn't been purged or deveined, they were so gritty as to ruin the dish.  And, I guess, that's why we won't be back anytime soon.  The attention to detail just doesn't seem to be there.  From past their prime veggies, to inconsistent seasoning, to not properly cleaning their seafood, I just don't trust their product.

Neutral Ground is an old school type coffee shop (anybody else remember Barsodi's?).  It is more about the atmosphere and the camaraderie.  I just walked past and they had 3 different people playing tonight, plus poetry, plus books, plus games, plus coffee & tea.

This is a brand new DMV office. I just needed an address change on my driver's license (which is free) and I was in and out in less than 45 minutes. So yes I am a fan.  The office is small and on the Thursday morning I was there, only 3 workers were assisting but it moved fast.  They don't do driving tests here though.   The space is a bit odd since it used to be the Mardi Gras museum. I wanted the person calling for numbers to stand on the wrought iron balcony and call out our turns. No TVs, exposed brick and great windows in the space.  Parking is across Williams. There is no signage if you're coming from Jefferson Highway.

I actually ate at Jazmine for the first time in a while (instead of just picking up take out) and was pleasantly surprised by the renovations to the space.  \  They've added a spring roll bar (not sushi as we thought) and I had a mango based roll which was delish.  They've also expanded their salad noodle bowl selection; E got the seared tuna and added tofu and I was jealous.  His Mom found something pork based that worked with her dietary needs. And I tried the mushroom glass noodle pho.  Everything was tasty and service was fine.  Again, I know this isn't the most authentic but it is tasty and really what else do I need?

Yes, the Bluebird is standard diner fare, but y'know that's hard to find in NOLA.  Go while you can.  The owner is retiring at the end of May. And the diner will be closing.  Had silver dollar pancakes (wish I had silver dollars that size) and scrambled eggs.  They even had green tea for the this non-coffee drinker.  And, yes, CASH only.

I hadn't eaten at Doson since it moved from Oak st. And it's still pretty darn tasty.  I went in for lunch last week and service was quick.  My noodle bowl of tofu & veggies was delish and I really liked how they put the sauce on the side in case fish sauce is a no go for you.  Very basic but good.

Located inside the Royal Sonesta, I usually end up at this PJs when I'm early for an event at the hotel. This location isn't my favorite, but it's usually pretty clean.   There's plenty of seating for the small space and access to outlets. The wifi is kind of terrible, even when the location isn't crowded.   I've had acceptable sandwiches and pastries here. And the iced tea is good. The price point is higher than other PJs but considering the location on Bourbon Street, it's not too bad.

Old school news stands are hard to find these days. But if you need an exotic magazine or are looking for something new, this is the spot.  They carry newspapers from all over the country. They have postcards. They have beacoup magazines on whatever your area of interest is. Plus they carry some tourist oriented books too. (The clerk told me that my Uncle's humor book was their best seller the summer it came out, so Yay!)   The staff is nice; the place is brightly lit and appropriately musty.  $10 minimum on credit card purchases, FYI

This is my preferred location to see a band at HoB. It's the smaller upstairs venue.  The space reminds me of some of the clubs that used to be around NOLA in the 80s. So I guess I'm saying it feels much less corporate than downstairs.    Same drink prices, same smoke but a bit more intimate.  Again don't expect fancy drinks nor apparently draft beer (I'm not a beer drinker so I'm kind of oblivious).
The kick off to 7 straight days of parades. Promise to expand after the parade tomorrow night.

Oh, the Camellia Grill...how I wish you were still open 24 hours.  Doesn't everyone need a pecan waffle at 3 a.m. on occassion?  Well too bad if you do since they actually close these days.  So sad.  The chocolate freeze is amazing.  E always craves their pecan pie.  And I am a sucker for their pecan waffle anytime of day. Last time my brother got the turkey club and was really pleased to see it was actual sliced turkey.  That said, I won't wait in ridiculous lines to eat here.  The last couple of times I've been, I've walked right in and then within 15 minutes the line is out the door.

Flashback! When I met Joi & Danny here last month, I hadn't been inside Carrollton Station in a few years. But for the part it remains the same. It's still a great building that's for certain.  The dart boards are still in the back. (Do not try to play if a band is on stage.) The gorgeous wood Brunswick bar is still there. The drinks are still solid and not too pricey.   What's changed? The old school games are gone, although the bowling one was kind of broken. I miss that bear shooting one. Random Story Alert: I brought some French visitors (friends of friends) here in the 90s and one of them was totally enamored of the bear shooting game. He proceeded to demonstrate his marksman skills for quite awhile. Turns out he had been in the French army.   In place of the vintage coin op games? Video poker. Sigh.  The management has changed in the last few years. But that doesn't seem to have affected the bar much.   Great place to see a band in an intimate venue.

So the best thing about driving by the Brown's Dairy as I take back streets to downtown? The Giant cow! Who doesn't love a larger than life farm animal?  I'm glad that Brown's still has a distribution center in the heart of the city and that you can buy their dairy products in groceries around the city.  Right now I have milk, cream and eggnog from them in my fridge. Go Brown's.   Yes you can buy milk from all over but c'mon bring your buy local sentiments to the dairy case.

Finally got to stop back in and see the new/old cafe at the Keller Library. LOVE that this is a Liberty Kitchen project so at risk students are learning job skills and making money.  My iced tea was perfect. My blueberry scone was more muffin-y than scone-y but delicious nonetheless. The cafe space was clean and airy.  The parking lot was full at 10 am on Thursday so yay for library users...since the cafe was not. But I found parking on the street, under a shadetree so it was all good.   Just wish their hours were a bit longer so I could go more often. 10 to 5 is tough for me. Now I need to find a day to go get one of their sandwiches.

I've only had hair services here.  And my color has always been great (Thanks! Andy).    A visiting friend did get a massage from them and said it was amazing.  And she seemed plenty relaxed afterward.

Have purchased McKenzie's & Schweggmann's logo pint glasses from Plum.  The stock is always changing so you have to check back often.  Plus I noticed they were putting in a chocolate case, so I'm looking forward to that.

I think I've decide that High Hat is just that OK. I still go here when friends want to give it a try.  But I still find it get be hit or miss.   My friend was thrilled with his short ribs over potato hash. I had the same hash under a beautifully cooked piece of drum. While his hash was made tastier by the au jus from his hunks of meat. Mine were dry and blah...even with the random addition of a few shrimp.  I like that they have actually added a few vegetarian vegetables (ha! oxymoronic) so that vegetarians can have a veggie plate in peace.  My friend also really liked the chicken & andouille gumbo so points for that. The soup I had sampled a couple of times (crab & corn?) is no longer on the menu.  The special of fried okra was delish too.

Be prepared to think skinny while shopping in Hazelnut.  It is a small store chock full of lots of decorator item like Jonathan Adler vases, serving pieces and lots of cute Christmas ornaments at this time of year.  And you will feel like you are going to knock something over...or maybe that's just clumsy me.  Of course, the NOLA toile is still a big seller but it seems like they have scaled back the variety of items made with it...for instance I didn't see the umbrellas. But they do have it in a variety of colors (red, blue, green, black and brown).  The shop also has purses and other random objects d'arte.  And, yep, this visit was party of my annual Magazine-Street-Black-Friday-Shopping-Extravaganza with my Mom.

Cafe Degas is like a dependable family member; if you don't visit often, you always think "why haven't I been here lately?"  And if they drop off your radar for a few months, they are just as accommodating & tasty when you return.    I went recently with 4 friends and had a fabulous meal.  Great appetizers, salads, entrees, desserts, wine.  It is traditional French cuisine so if you have diners with special dietary needs you might be out of luck.  I can't remember a vegetarian dish (besides a salad) on the menu.  But I suspect they would try if asked.  My family often does the Easter brunch at Cafe Degas & it is a delicious if not altogether relaxing experience...but maybe that's just holiday brunches in general.

I went to my second fancypants high tea over the weekend and it was great fun. I would definitely recommend reservations. My 2 adventures in tea parties were really different. But Carmen was awesome both times.  1st time was a random Sunday in June and my group and one other were the only ones there. It was relaxing and a great way to catch up and chat with my friends. The 2nd time was this past Sunday and it was a special Mad Hatter's tea. The place was packed! And there were tons of kids...who were mostly well behaved.  I was tad bit disappointed that they didn't carry the Mad Hatter theme into the food. The only special items were eat me/drink me notes on the sugar and creamer. Plus an actor who played the Hatter, but when my Mom quoted the book to him, he was confused. Oh well. He was mostly there for the kids.  For your prix fixe menu/price, you get a cocktail, a pot of tea (beaucoup selections), and three courses: seasonal tea sandwiches, scones and desserts (tea cakes, chocolate covered strawberries, etc).  The menu was the same in both June and August, but it is supposed to change seasonally. They do offer a number of themed teas throughout the year, some are more child oriented (Princess) and others are definitely for adults (Prohibition).   I definitely want to go back in the fall.

I've had this shop bookmarked for years. It's inside Up/Unique gifts in the loft. And the space isn't huge, but what's there is pretty awesome. All locally made jewelry with prices points from $5 to a couple of hundred. You do pay separately from the store downstairs.  The work is varied since several artists are represented, as are different materials. My niece loved the laser cut acrylic rings that I gave her. And I have my eye on a really cool pelican necklace...AND part of the purchase price for that benefits gulf coast oil spill charities. So maybe I'll get that as a HB2Me.

If you have a writer in your life, this is the place to stop. Fancy pens, fancy notepaper, choice gift items and Nola themed note cards/pads and Christmas cards (at this time of year). I found a perfect German style paper craft for a friend who misses her home country most of all at this time of year.  I think their main business is personalized stationery.  And this was part my annual Magazine-Street-Black-Friday-Shopping-Extravaganza with my Mom.

My little nieces (OK so the 11 year old is taller than me, whatever) and I stopped by Gallier House for a tour a few Mondays ago. (Yes open on Monday!) Our tourguide gave us a great tour of the house which is currently wearing it's summer style. The rugs have been picked up in favor of strawmats and the chandeliers, pictures and furniture is draped as if the windows were open to save them from bugs and sweaty people. But don't worry they have all the modern A/C for us wimpy folks. This is an historical house so expect stairs. Tours are at 10, 12 & 2 Monday-Tuesday and Thursday-Friday and 12, 1 & 2 on Saturday. And there is online booking: http://www.hgghh.org/exhibit/gallier-house/  I was surprised at how interested both the 8 and 11 year olds were to learn about the house. They were sort of intrigued/horrified to learn about chamberpots and from then on they were hooked. The tour does include old slave rooms and the guide did discuss slavery with the girls after being certain that they had learned about it in school.   The tour includes the living room, kitchen, a peek into the pantry, the dining room, sitting rooms, bedrooms, bathroom (inside!). The building has been restored beautifully and I can't wait to go back to see the mourning style (for Halloween) or dressed for the holidays.   Definitely a great historical house. They typical tour (depending on group size) only lasts about 60 to 90 minutes, I think.

Interesting that everyone is reviewing Bobby's as a sammich joint.  I've only ever used them as a fishmonger.  (Why, yes, I do like saying fishmonger, why do you ask?)  My family has ordered everything from pre-boiled shrimp to live crawfish to fresh oysters.  The seafood is always first rate.  C'mon they have to be good since they're housed in a former gas station.

I get that this is not the most authentic Vietnamese around. But I still find their dishes tasty & fresh.  I dine in or get take out here at least once a month.  I was surprised to note on my last trip in that they now have a full bar.  Yea for a liquor license!  No more trips down to O'Henry's to get a beer (or 2) for my brother in law.

This is a pretty large antique mall so there is a good bit of diversity to the stuff that is carried. Most of the prices seemed reasonable and there are signs everywhere stating that you need to bring your own labor for heavy/large furniture items.    The jewelry cases were well lit and not jam-packed so you could actually peruse them easily.  Some items were appropriately marked as reproductions but not everything...so the usual.

My first stop at their new space in the building with the Whole Food on Broad...what a huge change from their old small space closer to the courthouse. The new space is light and airy and there is so much room! Plus outside seating.  The menu is still small but offers a little something for everyone. The items are tasty, healthy and well prepared. I had the grilled veggie and cheese sandwich and it was delicious and big enough with the side salad (+1) for me to eat it for lunch and dinner.  The staff is the real reason to come. This is still a great work program to teach young people job skills. And folks working front of house were personable and enthusiastic.   Can't wait to go back.

Love the zoo.  Love the swamp exhibit, the African Savannah, the monkeys, the bird house, the reptile house, the butterfly habitat.  The gardens are usually beautifully planted and the animals seem happy in their habitats.

I hadn't been to Ernst in a few years, when I met up with a bunch of fellow yelpers a week or two ago. I was late to the party and cranky. In no time I had a glass of bourbon (not my preferred brand but they did have a decent selection) and had ordered an ultimately delicious fried shrimp plate.   (As a side note, when I tipped the member of the kitchen staff who delivered my plate, I got a hug...which was nice and with the shrimp/fries/bourbon completely erased the crankies.)  Ernst has solid food since it's a popular spot with the service industry crowd (I think the kitchen is 24 hours). The shrimp batter was nice and spicy and the shrimp were a really good quality and c'mon tasty french fries...which are excellent for shoving in the maw of your too drunk friends. That's the stuff.  Yeah the tile floor is odd...but seriously it was installed 100 years ago. I don't know about a symbol for piece but before it was co-opted by an insecure Austrian, it was a symbol for national identity for Germanic peoples...since they didn't even have a flag. Too bad the man with the 'stache had to ruin things.

I have not actually been to the shoppe, but I purchased a donated apple pie at a bake sale last night.    OM good.  The apples are perfectly cut and the filling is well spice without being too sweet.  The crust is just perfect.  Will definitely have to hunt down the actual store after eating this pie.

I think it's got another new name...maybe Prytania Bar...yep I just found their website: http://www.prytaniabar.com/ I swear this bar changes names at least once a year.  Anyway...I stopped in for a drink during the parades 1st weekend after discovering that the Milk Bar was closed so no sandwich for me...boo hoo.  I walked in to one patron at the bar and no one behind the bar. And I waited and I waited.  Finally the bartender came from the back and served us a well poured drink at a good price.  But c'mon, I could have run away with several bottles if so inclined.  One staff member (even if it was late morning/mid-day) with parades a block away seems foolish.

My 1st choice for auto parts for the last couple of decades. Sometimes women aren't treated that great at autopart stores, but that's never been my experience here.  That being said, you do have to know what you need when you arrive, like most places.  Not the most organized place, but all the most important parts are in the back and fetched by the employees anyway.  There are 2 listings for this location, and I've sent the duplicate to our Yelp overlords, but it doesn't seem to have been corrected yet.

Wow. It's been a long time since I've eaten here...like pre-yelp, pre-K long.  But this is where my aunt and family decided on dinner the week of Thanksgiving. So I tried to make a reservation, but if you want more than 4 people, you have to call. Now this is not a small space and I knew that but whatever. IF you want a reservation for a larger party, you have to give them a CC number and if you end up cancelling with less than 24 hours to spare than you are charged $20 per person for the no show. Wow. That seem excessive to me but then again, people are really inconsiderate.   So we make our Monday night reservation, and we're seated next to a party of 10 so that was a bit loud, but our service was on point with those delicious, stupid good biscuits and drinks. I had the royal red shrimp as my app and my family had a special salad, the firecracker tuna tacos, and the shrimp remoulade. Everyone seemed to enjoy their apps, and I thought my shrimp were tasty.  For entrees, we had a variety of fish dishes from the red snapper to the drum to the sheepshead (my granny favorite fish). Again they were well cooked and enjoyed by all.   My only real complaint was the "liveliness" of the restaurant. It's a big space and if you're with older folks who are quiet speakers, it's a challenge.  They do validate parking at 911 Iberville for up to 3 hours, but I found street parking closer to the restaurant so that was super easy.

Another cute women's clothing boutique on Magazine. Azby's definitely skews a bit more expensive than other stores on the street, but the clothes do seem to be of a bit better quality.  Yes, the service can be snooty.  And I have yet to actually purchase anything there, but I have tried on some adorable dresses that just didn't work out for one reason or another (too precious, too young, too much skin for me, yikes that color looks terrible next to my skin, the usual).

Posting a whole slew of reviews for stores I hit with my Mom on Black Friday. Life has something gift items as well as practical exercise wear.  The folks who work there have always been friendly although my purchases have always been small ones.    I guess I just can't commit to spending $ on exercise wear when I can't make myself get off the couch most days.

Solid neighborhood bar. It's pretty spacious so it's a good place to hangout with friends or watch a game. Bartenders have always been good to acceptable for me. They serve food in the back so that's always a plus for me. Go for a beer or a basic cocktail, nothing frou-frou.  This establishment was hit hard in the SM wars a couple of years ago so take any negative reviews with a grain of salt, many were obviously written by someone who has never been there.   Parking is on the street. And make sure you're parked legally and not blocking anyone's driveway.

Ooohh fancy new suburban style car wash, right by my house! The cheapest wash is $6 and it gets the oak pollen off. Plus then you get to use the free vacuums. The vacuums aren't quite as powerful as some of the other car washes I've been to but they do get the job done with some extra effort on your party.   I do wish they had the floor mat machines and more vending machines for supplies...instead I brought my own and had my the people around me try to mooch.   Weirdly, if you go to the Pelican Pointe website to check hours or prices, this location is not listed. Maybe they just haven't gotten to that yet.  As a side note, I uploaded a short video of the disco lights and sloshy carwash action for your amusement, and while it's available on the app, it's not on the desktop version of Yelp. #whatupwiththat

The permanent library is getting closer!  The new space looks like it's going to be amazing! I just hope the city actually funds furniture & materials for this branch.  Meanwhile the portable unit has moved to: Rosa Keller Branch TEMPORARY LOCATION during construction Andrew H. Wilson Charter School 3617 General Pershing (enter on S. Miro) 4:30 pm - 8:30 pm, Mon. - Thurs. 10 am - 5 pm, Sat. 504 596-2660 according to the NOPL website.

I went to this MM location for a Christmas dinner for 10. The staff was very accommodating and our server was great.  I really enjoyed the Southern man cocktail and others were impressed with the beer selection. The spinach dip appetizer was good (get it with pita instead of bread). And the pies I sampled were tasty, the Holy Shitake & the Bayou Bleu (although I didn't really taste any spicy blue cheese in it).  A great spot to go with a big group.

What a gorgeous space! LOVE the renovation of this historic home. Seriously the buidling is beautiful. But that's not all! The art on display is incredibly varied and really impressive/moving/inspiring/calming depending on the piece. I'm a big fan of highly curated collections like these. It really helps you see the collector/curators vision.   I was lucky enough to visit because of fellow yelper Teneha had rented this space for her birthday extravaganza! So much fun and it was wonderful seeing all her friends & family celebrating her awesomeness.   Their special exhibitions are interesting and diverse. I just wish they were keeping regular hours, despite the hours posted on their website, the front page says "open by appointment only."

This gallery primarily represents Bill Hemmerling with originals of his works and giclees and other items. It does have paintings by a couple of other artists who paint in a similar folk art style.  The original Hemmerlings are pricey but since he has passed their are only so many pieces left. But there are more modestly priced prints.  The person running the shop was really friendly and we ended up chatting about home renovation projects. Because that's what people who own old houses do.

While I miss Michael's Mid-City Grill, Minh Cafe is a welcome addition to mid-city.  The menu is sort of pan-asian, but I like to think of it as a kitchen sink menu with asian flare.  I had the red shrimp curry on angel air.  Curry with pasta.. OK that's different but good.  My dinner companions had the short ribs (my dog is loving the bones) and the lacquered duck both said they were phenomenal.  My partner had the veggie tofu stir fry and was very satisfied.    Plus delicious cocktails (mine was a LARGE mint julep so thank goodness for spell check).  So Yum all the way around.

How is it possible that I am the 1st to review Palm Court?  What is the world coming to...  This is THE place to see traditional jazz in a comfortable setting.  I mean I love Preservation and all, but it's hot & you have to stand to see anything.  Palm Court is much more civilized.  It's the sort of place you can imagine in a 1940s movie.    Must admit I've never eaten here only listened to music & had cocktails.

Circle Bar is a good time if you like dive bars and people watching.  The drinks are pretty cheap and as in most of NOLA are on a heavy pour.  This is the place that Anthony Bourdain hung out until 3 or 4 a.m. when he was in town shooting.  So that should give you some idea of what it's like.

When Re said there was a new art marketplace on Magazine, I knew I had to go check it out. Located in the space where Dombourian rugs used to be, this brand new building makes great use of the space.  They had a variety of artists, crafts people, and interesting items to look at. The space is airy and comfortable and the booths are well spaced. There is a central counter to check out.   As always with these spaces, the booths are varied and there is a good variety of work from turned wood to paintings to sculpture to lamps to gift items.  A space I'll be keeping my eye on for the future.

Don't let the word craft in their name fool you.  Rhino is an artist consortium retail shop.  You can find jewelry, pottery, furniture, sculpture, paintings, hats and scarves here.  The artist members do change and the stock at the two stores can be very different, so check them both out!  This is the one in Canal Place shopping mall.  It's on the 3rd floor.

Remember when Monky Hill was just a hill and it wasn't inside the zoo and you could just roll down it with your siblings.  And your uncle told you it was the highest point in New Orleans and you believed him?  Well I do.  Now it's all super fancy with water for you (or y'know kids) to play in and for once something from childhood actually seems bigger than your memory.  BUT you do have pay to go inside the zoo.  And it has concrete paths, so don't try rolling down.  Maybe I should just get a waxed chunk of cardboard and sled on the levee instead.  Psst...also this is review #950 for me!

They have beef, turkey & veggie burgers! However, they are pretty much cooked on the flattop right next to each others, so if that bothers you....Maybe you could ask for them to clean a section and segregate?   I got the au Naturale veggie burger with a side of curly fries. The smashed avocado was more like guacamole but I'm OK with that. The bun and veggie patty were both put on the grill and you can taste it. Very yummy. The curly fries were lightly battered and delicious. Ketchup and mustard were available at the truck to add yourself.   Service was quick and I was back at my desk in no time, sigh.

I'm not a big department sure shopper, but I always make sure to hit up Dillard's between October & early January because they are the official merchandiser of Mr. Bingle.  Mr. Bingle is a New Orleans icon and Dillard's owns the rights since they ate the old Maison Blanche department store.  Maybe I should create a listing just for Santa's little helper...  Anyway, it's a Dillard's, otherwise.

Yay for a separate listing for the Library book sale! This is a great spot to find recent hardback best sellers as well as children's books and vintage items. It was the actual carriage house when Latter Library was a private home. Recent renovations have made it a great spot to browse.  It is run by the Friends of the Library and your cash helps fund the Public Library so win win! It is only open 2 days a week for 4 hours each day, Wednesdays and Saturdays from 10-2. Usually they put a sign out on St Charles when they are open.

I missed having a pair of birkenstocks in my life and my go to shop for those had closed years ago. So when I was out in Metairie, I passed by this shop.   My sales person was lovely and very helpful. My feet are petite so many birks don't really fit me correctly but we found a pair that I was happy with.  Easy peasy. And, why was my sales person looking at me funny? When I gave her my name of their computer system, she said are you related to bro1 and nieces? And of course, I was. I wear my name on my face.

Weird. I know I typed up an update to my review from last year a couple of months ago. And I was pretty sure I posted it...maybe I never actually hit save/publish/whatever.  My very large family hit Lola's for father's day in June.  It wasn't everyone so we only needed a table for 10.  My Dad LOVES Spanish food so he was very happy.  He still pines for Espana (which used to be on Jeff Hwy and hasn't been around in over 20 years).  He was really excited to find Fabada on the menu as this is a dish loves.  Everyone was happy with their food, even my picky teenage nieces & nephew who all ordered Caesar salads with grilled shrimp or chicken.  The sangria is still yummy.  And, of course, as we discovered they now take credit cards. Woo Hoo!

Unlike everyone else this year, I was bummed that Endymion took the Uptown route.  It just made Sunday too long (but that's what I get for being nice & delivering coffee to the route at 8 am).  But forget about the schedule, the floats were beautiful.  Some of the figureheads were a little boring (but not as boring as whole floats in Bacchus) but the themes were carried across the floats (unlike Orpheus & all their flowers).  The riders were generous, literally dumping beads on the crowd.  And as always my brothers who ride had a great time.

Really. No one has reviewed the great city of Kenner? I find this hard to believe.  After all, we all go to Kenner to go to the airport.   Otherwise Kenner is just a suburb of New Orleans which is really too bad because it' has a really long history. Did you know that there used to be a street car all the way from the city to Williams & Jefferson Highway? It ceased in 1931.

I was a little disappointed in Sylvain's menu...so few vegetarian items. Luckily, I wasn't super hungry so I just snacked. I guess if I had been starving, I could have filled up on desserts.  I ordered a cheese tray for our table; it came with 3 cheeses (all tasty), toasted baguette rounds (yum), almonds, and macerated dried cherries (delish).  I also had the shaved brussel sprout salad which was really good...bright and slightly sharp and really good.    Sylvain gets a solid 4 for inventive cocktails and their mixologist. She handled the specialty requests from my table with aplomb.

Oh, Target, I do love thee.  I went last night (avoiding parades times both uptown & in Metairie) and bought most of the items on my list.  And a purple dress and gold sweater for my MG costume.  I really think Target has the best cereal prices of any store in the GNO area.  I love that Target used to be Maison Blanche and I like the basket escalators.

After seeing some recent excellent scores from a friend on Instagram, I made a note to myself to check this Goodwill out. And I'm glad I did. It's smaller than the one on Tulane Ave which is good for me so I'm not overwhelmed.   The stock is definitely a bit fancier, consider the neighborhood, and I scored a brand new (with tags) silk skirt for $3.50. AND an odd but excellent 2nd skirt that will be a good addition to my costume box. But yes like all thrift stores, exam the clothes carefully and consider the brand vs the price.   The staff was nice. The store was clean as were the dressing rooms. And it was easy in and out.

This is an interesting location...sort of open air cafe, but inside the Factory space. So you feel like you should be outdoors...but you're not. That was very good for us as we stopped by when it was pouring rain outside.  The menu is mostly soups, salads and some southern dishes. I had the fall/winter salad and it was tasty, but I didn't expect full on sugared pecans (I know the menu says candied.) and I wanted more beets. My friend really liked her chicken salad.  Bonus points for the incredibly random conversation with our waiter. His response to the Beatles / Stones debate? The Grateful Dead. Interesting.

As I was leaving the quarter, we popped in here because we needed beverages and what did I spy? A lovely looking tray of donuts.  Before I bought, I asked who made them and when the cashier told me Gerald's. I knew they would be a solid choice. We gobbled up a couple of donuts and a delicious apple fritter and they were as fresh as promised.  Otherwise it's a wee shop that sells the basics. Solid choice for a quick bottle of something...

Of the stores in this stretch of Magazine, I'd say this place is on the medium pricey side. But the quality of the clothes reflects that. The selection is good and reflects a range of styles rather than just one type of look.  When I was there last weekend, they were having an excellent sale with many of their winter shoes clearanced at $50 per pair. And with racks of clothing divided by price. I tried on a handful of dresses that ranged in price from $250 to $75. And score! My favorite was a half priced item.   The sales people were OK. but clearly it would pay to be a regular here. The accessories did look interesting but I was trying to keep the spending to a minimum so I didn't browse.   Definitely worth a perusal when you're looking for something new.

I hadn't been in this consignment shop in years. And it has way more stock than I remember. It isn't a huge store so it's a bit crowded. The clothes (all women's) is organized by size and color. There are jewelry cases and shoes and purses.  The clothes mostly skew a bit older and the ladies in the shop are polite. Definitely a spot to find some work oriented clothes. The prices were good for better quality used items.  There are a few parking spaces in front of the store but there is a larger parking lot across the street and down half a block if those are full.

I've been here twice. Once for a party in one of the karaoke rooms and most recently on Friday in the main dining room.    The karaoke room was totally fun and I couldn't believe the selection of songs to sing from.  The food was good, but I honestly can't remember what I ordered.  On Friday, a friend and I ordered 6 small plates/salads: a fried oyster dish, a cucumber seafood salad, okra skewers (Kushi Yaki), burning man roll (spicy tuna inside/pepper tuna outside) w/o the eel sauce, baked scallops and a special shrimp gyoza.  The roll was good and I loved the okra skewers and salad.  The shrimp gyoza and the baked scallops were not that good.  The fried oysters mostly tasted like fried.  BUT, the music was cranked pretty loud so it was difficult to actually have a conversation with my friend.  I think the "lively" atmosphere was why so many families with were kids there; no one could here them cut up. So maybe that's a plus.  My ears were ringing by the time we left.  What made up for the noise?  Tasty specialty cocktails.

Y'all they have this veggie wrap that is AMAZING. Filling and delicious and the mushrooms are sauteed with something nice and fire-y so there's some heat.  I've dined in once and then picked up takeout another time (lunchtime). And both times the food was speedy both times. By the way their french fries are addictive. The only problem with calling in my order is that I don't know what the daily special is and they often sound delicious. My fellow diners have had the burger and the lemongrass chicken wrap which also got raves.   I need to pass by after work for a cocktail and some dinner soon. And I need to try their tots. Definitely in the regular work rotation.

While this was my first time at this location, I have used Bedding Plus previously to purchase mattresses (in my pre-Yelp days). This local chain (spin off from Doerr Furniture) carries Sealy, Beauty Rest and Stearns & Foster. Most of the mattresses are from the higher end lines but generally these are also mattresses that last. Yesterday I was helping a family member pick out a new mattress set.  The sales person was knowledgeable about his stock and discussed the pros & cons of various types of mattresses depending on what kind of sleeper you were (back, side, stomach). He also made good suggestions about how to extend the life of your mattress. And respected the price point that we needed to stay under.  Delivery is free and can be changed with 24 hours notice. Very easy-peasy. And you know you're getting a good quality product. I'll be back again when I need to replace my mattress.

Smaller market but in December it's an old school craft market! I purchased mustard greens, a piece of art and some ornaments when I was there on Saturday. There were also prepared foods and wooden toys and all sorts of things available.  I was also tempted to buy an afghan, custom cutting boards, pork skins (for my parents), and spiced nuts.   I was able to find street parking nearby without a problem. Some vendors were cash only and others accepted e-payments. My guess is some might accept checks as well.

Pre-K, I thought about checking out Twisted when it was on Magazine because I liked the signage.  But I thought perhaps I wasn't cool enough to go there since they advertise themselves as stylists who do some avant garde kinda stuff.  Flash forward to earlier this year and I am still searching for a stylist that I click with and on a friend's recommendation when to see Nicole here.  She was personable and professional.  We discussed my hair issues (like extreme stubborness...hair not me, or not just me) and what we could do with the extreme layering that I was growing out.  My hair cut was so good that I didn't go back for months and my hair still looked cute.  Once my bangs were long enough to chew on, I decided to go back.  Another great haircut and no fuss no muss I'm back to looking non-shaggy.

All I really knew about this place was that John LOVES it. So since my car needed a bath AND I had errands to run on the Westbank, I figured I'd check it out.   It was definitely not what I expected. I liked that you use a touchscreen to select your carwash and can then just pay with a card or cash at the machine. Then you sit in your car while it runs through the wash, an attendant is on hand to make sure you're in the right position.   Then you can pull around and use the free vacuums and mat cleaner yourself. Yep you do the labor. No gathering up your valuables out of the car in case of sticky fingers. No complaining that "someone" missed a spot because that someone is you. I even bought a sponge from the vending machine (for $1) to wipe down the doors and dash.   And while the place was busy, I still felt like it was money and time well spent. Minus 1 star because I think I was too close to the car in front so my bumper wasn't grime free.

Jut realized that I never reviewed this tree service.   My family still owns my grandmother's house and in the back yard was (sniff sniff) a glorious giant oak tree. An arborist told one of my brother's that he had never seen such a short wide live oak. But unfortunately over a year ago it split almost in half. Luckily it didn't land on the house. Phew.  We called around to a number of companies and because of the size of the oak, the prices were $$$. But J & W came in at the best price. And to help us with costs (and because the house was empty at that point), they cut back the oak over several trips, fitting it in around other jobs.  The final product is no more oak tree (which makes me sad) but also no more danger to the house or to the neighbors.  One of my brothers was the main communicator with them and he and my Mom were pleased with the outcome.

I was having lunch next door at MoPho and my out of town dining companions asked about Ike's. I explained the VAST superiority of a New Orleans snoball to the mundane widely available snocone. And of course, then I had to have one.  I was super excited to see cucumber lime as a flavor so that's what I got, after I was allowed a small sample to check it out. It was just tart enough and with a nice subtle cucumber flavor. Speedy service, good-soft ice, and it hit the spot.  Now I need another snoball.

I hadn't been to Lola's in about 10 years until tonight.  And I am thrilled to see they got a liquor license sometime in the last decade.  The sangria was delicious.  But the are still CASH or check only.  Luckily there is an ATM down the street.  The crabmeat tropicale was an amazing appetizer as was the cold almond soup and we all loved our entrees (2 pasta dishes - 1 vegetarian and a trout dish).  The only complaint was that one of the pasta dishes was really salty.  I'm going to have make it over to the Esplanade Ridge more often.    Also love that all veggie items were printed in green ink.

Had my toes done on Good Friday and they were still looking good...until I ran over my foot with one of our giant garbage cans and cracked my toenail & the polish.  Luckily that was my only injury.  They just opened this month and still seem to be getting their staffing under control.  And I really like that they sterilize their clippers, etc before using them on my feet.

Pandemic update: I've been craving some sushi and since I was feeding one of my nieces after she helped all day with a project around the house, I owed her! Ordering from the app on their website is really easy and more $ stays with them that way.   We got a crab salad, a cucumber tuna salad, edamame, veggie gyoza, miso, and a couple of rolls. Everything was packaged really well and it was all delicious. The gyoza was new to my niece and she really liked them. The cucumber tuna salad was just what I needed.  While I did takeout but they are dining in on their patio and probably inside. They have hand sanitizer as you walk in and pickups at are the front, in the bar area so you're not in the actual eating area which I like. They have signage which makes it clear which way to go.  Staff was all masked and since I paid online there was very little contact when I picked up.

I stopped in here late on a weekday after missing lunch and I was STARVING. I had my fingers crossed that the sushi would be good and I was rewarded! Everything I had was very tasty and the fish was really good quality.   Since I was starting I ate a tuna cucumber salad, Hawaiian roll (sauce on the side & I was really glad because I wasn't big on it & the roll didn't need it), fresh salmon sushi and by request inari!  The tuna and cucumber were delicious and it was a huge portion and normally this might have been enough for a meal for me. Not this day. I loved the Hawaiian roll...mango and coconut fried shrimp with spicy tuna in a soy wrapper, YUM! The salmon was tasty, fresh and well cut. I had ordered a veggie roll...maybe asparagus and they were out so we were discussing a substitution and I mentioned that I loved inari and the sushi chef said that while they didn't have it on the menu, they had some in the freezer. Um OK. And it was tasty.   I was the only person in the restaurant at 4pm on a Thursday so my service was excellent. Prices were on par with the quality of the fish. Parking can be a pain on this part of Magazine especially with all the Napoleon construction. Do NOT use the lot next door (which is super awkwardly laid out and has many signs telling you who is allowed to park there).   Will definitely be back.

Perseverance I tell you. Sometimes you have to just keep trying to go to a restaurant and eventually it will be open when you're hungry.  Since this is mostly a lunch spot and I'm not often in the neighborhood until evening, I thought I was star crossed with Sarita's. Yes, they have evening hours, but I can never remember them so inevitably go on the closed nights.  I had their delicious flounder tacos out on the street at Freret Fest last year and I've been craving them. So the other day, I realized I had less than 30 minutes until their closing time and so I zoomed over. I was able to grab my amazing tacos (1 fish and 1 shrimp) to go. Add an iced tea and it totaled less than $10.  YUM.  I noticed that they do have a liquor license. I'm going to have to fix into my brain when they're open for dinner and get over there again soon.

When the eastbank solid wood furniture store closed, I switched my allegiance to this shop. I haven't been in for a while... since they're old location in fact so I guess that's where my old review went.  Pieces in my house from this shop: bookshelves, desk, kitchen table, liquor cabinet... and soon to be...  I went in this weekend to look at a free standing pantry cabinet for my kitchen. We looked around at what was available and I made a decision. Yes I could finish it myself but it's really a cost savings to have them white wash the piece for me. Who knows when I would get to it.  Pricing is competitive for solid wood furniture. Yes you might be surprised at the price tag but that's what wood goes for these days.   The staff is great and really helpful. My new cabinet should be ready in 2 weeks. They do deliver for a fee but I'll just use my Dad's truck instead.

This is a Sprint store and I guess it's a subcontract so that's why the name isn't...y'know...Sprint store.   I switched carriers and REALLY wanted my new phone immediately so rather than wait for a phone to be shipped out to me, I made an online appointment to sign up at this location. (Just a note, Tchoupitoulas is mis-spelled on the Sprint website which makes me laugh.) I arrived on time for my appointment and was helped immediately which may have been luck on my part rather than a scheduling thing.  Thanks to a couple of computer snafus and the time it took my number to port from one carrier to the next, I was there for about 90 minutes. The sales person I worked with was great and patient...I think I have her name somewhere, if so I'll edit and add it. LOVE my new GS4 phone.  And walletwise am happy that I switched carriers.

The staff was really nice and really we just needed some brochures or maybe a postcard (which are getting harder to find) to send off with a flat Stanley my friend was responsible for. In addition to information, they had tshirts and postcards for sale.   Great spot for quick information.

I was pretty sure that I reviewed Cane & Table a couple of years ago after having dinner there with friends... I guess the disappearing review bug hit me again.  Last time I reviewed my meal which was OK. And wrote about how eating late in the courtyard was difficult since it was so dark and my fish had bones.   This time, I wandered in on Saturday evening with a group of friends for an after dinner drink. We were seated in the courtyard which was lovely on a balmy December evening. I had an old fashioned and my friends had a specialty cocktail and a couple of hurricanes. All the drinks were delicious.   We had said at the host station that we were drinking only, and that was OK for a 4/5 top but when friends tried to join us, we were told that we have to move to a bigger table AND order food. But we could move to the bar, except maybe that wasn't allowed either because there weren't enough seats.  I get that this place is striving for elegance (and maybe there are fire code restrictions) but at some point you're just chasing off customers. I am a craft cocktail fan but I also like to feel welcomed.

Chalmette Battlefield is another of the 6 parks within the Jean Lafitte National Park.  I remember going to it often as a child with the cub scouts (right-I wasn't a member, but I have lots of brothers, OK?)    I remember my Mom explaining to me that all the crosses represented soldiers who died in battle.  I was maybe 6; it was really overwhelming but those crosses made me realize the cost of war.  Or maybe I was just a really overwrought child.

Great to people watch and sample a variety of bar action/cuisine.  Strangely, enough my first exposure to this stretch of street was back when Snug Harbor was the only club and there was a Catholic Elder car facility around the corner. I would drive my grandmother over to pick up one of her nun friends...my have times changed.  Anyway, there are a number of great bars and music clubs, good restaurants, and just about anything else you could want.  On busy nights, there are often food vendors set up around so you can do walk up food.    Just remember that this street does get just as crowded as Bourbon so don't show up on say Halloween if crowds make you freak out.  Also, this is NOT a closed street, so do watch for cars.

These days I'm not often out this way to buy groceries. But this grocery was one of my Granny's favorites, especially the butcher department. I used to drive her out this way once I had a license.   I was in the neighborhood on Saturday afternoon and noticed a bright shiny new Zuppardo's building right next to the old one but it isn't open yet. I'm glad I was able to stop in the old school one... I doubt the new one will have wood paneling. But I hope they still have a lunch counter!  I was mostly in the store for prepared foods for my parents. (This is my SiL's favorite chicken salad btw.) And they did not disappoint. I picked up some beef stew and some crawfish Monica along with carrot salad and a few other things. Prices were good and the staff was friendly.  I did notice people in line at the butcher counter so it looks like they are still doing custom cuts which is hard to find at most groceries these days.   Now I'll just need to check out the new store after it opens.

Oh, Sid-Mars.  What can I say. I've been planning to go to the new location since it opened.  And while the food was good, but different. The new location makes me sad.    It's sort of like going to visit a family member after a bad accident.  They aren't the same (to a startling degree) but you're still grateful that they made it through.  The carpeting and fancy decor just don't say Sid-Mar's.  And I'm not sure if it's the oil spill or the new location, but their was no boiled seafood on the menu last night.  I'll definitely go back, especially when I have a craving for their stuffed crab.  Also, it was nice that our server (I think the wife of the owner) treated us like long lost family.

Y'know I'm not a "lively" environment person & this place is lively to loud. I think they weren't prepared for their instant popularity, so service seems a bit chaotic...like they haven't found their groove.  But the food is delish. We had the daily market salad which was a caprese this evening and the heirloom tomatoes were AMAZING.  We ordered 2 pizzas...whose names I can't even remember b/c I am braindead. But they were both excellent.    Cocktails were an interesting twist to an old-fashioned (no orange but satsuma cello instead...may account for my current zombie state) and NOLA brewing wheat bear.  Tasty.

Ha! I forgot that I checked in at this statue whilst wandering on Canal Street with John & Ronnie.   So here's my confession, I am not a Confederacy of Dunces fan. I've tried to wade through it a couple of times and never finished. My problem is that it doesn't really speak to my version of NOLA and that's OK. (Additional confession, I also don't get many other "classics" in modern literature and we can debate those any time.)  On the other hand, I love public art in general and this statue in particular. It's a great representation and very accessible in both location and form. Even if you're not familiar with the character, you know who he is through the artist's work.  Thanks to the Wyndham Hotel folks for letting him stand in front of the old DH Holmes Department Store in perpetuity.

A New Orleans institution; Adler's has been around since 1898.  They are the go to fancy jewelry store for many New Orleanians.  I wish that I could say that I shop here all the time.  But finances don't allow it, plus I'm just not they type to be dripping in gemstones.  But I love the New Orleans themed "boutique" jewelry as well as Chesley Adler's pieces.  They also do repair work.

Pandemic update: For December 2020, the Market has moved to City Park on the Great Lawn across from the Peristyle. It is much smaller than the usual December markets at Palmer Park but it is well spread out. It is happening every Saturday until Christmas.   You enter from the Dreyfous Dr side of the Great Lawn, where you leave your info for contact tracing and they have hand sanitizer. The whole area is taped off and we are trusted to be adults and comply; but in case you aren't a good citizen, there is a security guard nearby.   There were 20-30 vendors selling their wares. Everyone was masked and I was glad to see more and more vendors were excepting e-payments.   Great way to support local artists and get some amazing presents for your loved one  or you!

I hadn't worn either of my watches in awhile because the batteries were dead. I had been carrying them around in my purse for a few weeks, meaning to get to a watch shop. And then I stumbled across this spot. They said they could do both batteries in about 20 minutes if I had time to wait. Yep.  AND they promised if it wasn't the battery then it would be no charge for attempting the change. Yes both were batteries and I have a 1 year guarantee on the watch batteries.   Quick and precise and only about $20 per watch. Easy peasy.

Jackson Brewery gets a +1 because I worked in a jewelry store there over 15 years ago.  But really the shops are mostly tourist traps with a few exceptions.  It's a good place to duck in out of the weather and it does have a cool history as a brewery.

This was my 2nd choice on a rainy Sunday... our first stop had over an hour wait and I didn't have time for that. As I was headed to Mississippi, I used my handy Yelp app to see what was available as I headed out. And found this cute little spot on Yelp.  LOVED the family feel and that it was clear most of the people were regulars. Did not love that they were out of so much that morning. My friend wanted the meatball sandwich but they were out. They were also out of fries. I think he ended up with a burger and I had fried shrimp.  The Sunday brunch menu was not in effect that day and I'm not sure why because it looks amazing. Would try it again if I was in the area.

OK.  I have to admit, I was not a fan of the Save-a-Center and only went under duress or great need.  But Rouse's has definitely improved the space and the selection of fresh produce and Louisiana products.  They are slowly working to improve this store and it is appreciated.

Pandemic update I deserved some gnocchi for my recent pandemic birthday! So I ordered some to go... along with a specialty pizza and an old fashioned. You can call or order online from their website.... but I just stopped in, ordered and waited.  They are doing limited dine in service but that isn't for me at the moment.  My gnocchi was heaven. They are doing it as cacio y pepe and it was divine, like I want to drink the sauce divine... but instead I dipped my pizza crusts in it. Perfection! My pizza was a special with shaved garlic and fresh mozzarella and other deliciousness. But you can't really go wrong with any of their pizzas. As always my old fashioned was delicious.  Social distancing is being enforced. Masks are required. Hand sanitizer is available. Staff is great as always.

Umm...how is it possible that I haven't reviewed Audubon Park?  I've spent so much time here over the years.    I was once pulled into the lagoon by my dog; it was a really bad idea to try to "walk" him while wearing rollerskates when ducks were nearby.  They were just too exciting.   Besides rollerskating mishaps, I've walked the park to chat with friends, biked the edges in a semblance of exercise, lounged on a blanket while snoozing and reading, played on the kid's equipment with nieces, and just enjoyed the beautiful trees.

I just realized that I reviewed this Rouse's as one of my very first reviews and the store has improved so much in the last couple of years.  Love the produce area and the wine/booze selection.  Love all the local products, especially the Dong Phuong bakery cookies.  So why not 5 stars? The same issues as when this was a Save-a-Center. The parking lot needs better drainage. After one of our lovely NOLA thunderbursts today, I walked to my car in shin deep water. My car almost flooded...but that was really due to the jerk in an SUV and his wake. I really do wish my eyes were death rays sometimes.

Not my usual Rouses but I was making groceries for Mom and Dad and this was close. I was impressed by the produce department and that there was a lot of variety and it was huge!  I wasn't as impressed with the prepared foods area; it was much smaller than in my usual locations. Maybe that doesn't sell as well here. They had good selections of most everything else I needed.   Otherwise it was laid out very similarly to other Rouses. I was able to find what my parents needed and check out quickly.

When I ate lunch here recently, I couldn't believe it had been decades since I'd last stepped foot in here. I was running around on a weekday with one of the college-age nieces and we stopped here because we were both starving and she really wanted breakfast, even though it was noon.  Welp, breakfast went out the window when we discovered that one of the $7.75 lunch special that day was fried shrimp on a bun with soup or salad, tea, and dessert + French bread and butter. Yes please! The salad was mostly iceberg but that's OK with me. And the dessert was either a slice of cake or canned peaches. I LOVE canned peaches and am not too fancy to admit that. The sammich was huge and came with fries. So I ended up taking 1/2 of it home and eating it for dinner.  The table next to us order the white beans with a *giant* ham hock which was another special and that dude was digging in. I think my niece was freaked out by the ham hock but whatever.  Pay at the counter. Tip your server well because they are hustling. Their is a parking lot on the side street if street parking isn't your thing.  I need to put this in regular work rotation.

So like a silly girl, I started drinking at 3 pm and ate a few snacks and was STARVING. My time was limited and I had to pick up the lovely Lindsay A. I started yelping for a nearby foodtruck and instead saw Kukhnya which I've been wanting to go to for months. Last time I stopped by they were closed. So I crossed my fingers and prayed to the Slavic Mary and YAY!  I ordered the pierogies and an asparagus polboy (for me and Miss Lindsay). OMG delicious. Seriously those pickled onions on the sammich were AMAZING, sliced thin  and piled on... It ended up being so much food that Joi was gifted 1/2 of our polboy.    Definitely will be back soon.I can't wait to have my Polish co-worker experience the yumminess...plus there's the entertainment in seeing her inside Siberia.

Pandemic review: I took a drive through the FQ on Friday afternoon just to see the spaces that I miss and see what was open.  I had heard that VM never closed... because it is a corner store and that was definitely in evidence as the owner helped an older quarterite who trying to find the essentials of cleaners and TP.   I headed to the back and ordered a grilled shrimp on bun, dressed. And let me tell you. It gave me life. Delicious.  Honestly it's been years since I ate at VM. It's often just too crowded when I'm in the FQ.   I'm so glad that VM is around and supplying its community with groceries and sustenance

Pandemic update: Rouses is my usual go to big grocery. I popped in midday yesterday to do my parents' shopping and pick up a few things for me too.  There as a staff person outside wiping down baskets. All employees were masked and the checkout stations have plexiglass.  Most of the shoppers were wearing masks. And the store was well-stocked, I got almost everything on Mom's list. They even had paper towels! (OK, one brand and they were the small rolls.)   Since this is a large store, I felt like I could keep my space away from people more easily and people maintained distance at the checkout.

The Arts Council of New Orleans sponsors this monthly market, corner of Claiborne & Carrollton.  It features a variety of local artists from painters to sculptors to photographers to fiber artists to metalsmiths and jewelers.  Plus there is always food for sale as well as live music and crafts for kids.  It is by far the largest art market in town.   Next market is Saturday, December 19 and Sunday December 20.  Check out the news page from the Arts Council:  http://www.artscouncilofneworleans.org/index.php?topic=artsmarket  My only problem this weekend was that I was supposed to be looking for presents for others & mostly found stuff for me.

I am not a coffee drinker but I do enjoy a good cup of tea. And Cherry did me right in the tea department. I do love a proper cup.  BUT of course what I really love about this shop is the building! What a wonderful reuse of the space! The high ceilings make everything airy. And even with all the hard surfaces it wasn't loud... were people being considerate? or was it magic?   I just had a yummy pastry when I last stopped in but I need to remember to try an actual meal here.  Gorgeous! And I hear the coffee is delish too.

Pandemic update: I think I have a million check ins here (OK I checked it's only 64). When in doubt I stop by for tacos.  Seriously this spot has fed most of my family in friends, from my Mom "who doesn't like Mexican food" and now loves their rice bowls (both the superbowl and the MexiBowl) to the pickiest niece when she was a little who only wanted a single chicken taco with sour cream for dipping.   For pandemic times, I've gotten take out a few times, including bringing big plates to my parents. Dad loves the plantains.   You can call in an order or stop at the counter. They are doing curbside delivery if you ask. You can also get a sangria or margarita to go.   I love that you can mix and match tacos based on your mood. The fish is flounder and delish. I also love a no meat taco with all the veggies, beans & rice. Plus the shrimp quesadilla is a fave.   When I last reviewed 7 years ago they were still busiest at lunch but that hasn't been the case for awhile.   They are really good at accommodating dietary issues. I brought a friend who is gluten and dairy free do to allergies and she loved it!

I haven't been to this spot in so long that I didn't realize that it was owned by the Riccobano's now, like since Katrina now. Clearly I am not paying attention.  I met a couple of friends there for lunch recently and had a great meal. My cup of shrimp and corn bisque to start was warm and yummy with just a hint of spice to offset the richness. I had the spinach artichoke panini with a bag of chips and it was just what you think, like dip on bread. Delicious. I ended up having half the sandwich to go. My friends got yummy and bountiful fries as their sides and one had the same sandwich as me and the other had the turkey bacon and said it was really good.  Good to know they have heaters for their outdoor seating during this chilly time of year. And that they have a boozy brunch on weekends.   I definitely need to go back and try more items.

Seriously since the gnocchi were added to the menu, I crave/Crave/CRAVE them. Perfection. Last night's iteration a simple & simply amazing beurre fondue. I am warning you that the gnocchi may be laced with crack.  Still love the pizzas, and the daily specials are uniformly tasty and/or interesting variations for local produce.     And I always get their delish old fashioned. Bonus points that you can eat at the bar if the place is crowded or you're by yourself.

As many times as I went to the old thrift store in this spot, I can't believe how much stuff is crammed into the new Rouses.  To be clear, this is not a full grocery but it is a great spot to pick up a couple of essentials or some party food... which is what I did. Prepared foods are definitely the focus.   I had some family come town and we had a last minute cookout and I was in charge of apps. Stopping in the new Rouses was perfect, I picked up deviled eggs and chips, salsa & guac and crawfish pies. And of course beer and cookies.   Since it was the first weekend open, they were more than fully staffed and there were tons of staff around greeting customers and offering assistance. The parking lot was turning over pretty quick but it is small. So don't be surprised if you can't find a spot.   There's a covered outdoor area if you're grabbing a quick lunch.   Only about 25% of the staff is masked and probably the same for the patrons going in.

Just finished a State Street Kitchen, Grilled Chicken, Spinach, Swiss and Honey Mustard Sub.  To kick it up a notch I stuffed in Jalapeno Chips for a spicy crunch.  It was great on an afternoon when autumn is starting to assert itself with bluster.    This excellent local establishment continues to turn out first rate creative dishes thanks to the ever-present Micha, and her friendly staff.  It has become my most constant breakfast companion, and often my lunch date, as well.    If you have not been in for a taste of home cooking with a Korean flare, you don't know what you are missing.   Find a way to get there.  Sit down and become part of the family.
Surprising good bagels from this unassuming shop on the north end of Lambertville.  Very friendly owner.  Decent coffee.   Definitely a keeper.

Asian Taste Inn in the Huntingdon Valley Marketplace on County Line Road, is a primarily Chinese house owned by a Guangdong Province family, that has been turning out pretty good semi-authentic dishes for a while.  The space is well maintained with many booths and tables, and an amiable server corps dressed in tan and green that actually seems to enjoy interacting with their customers.    True to its cultural roots, the cuisine tends toward sweetness, and even their spicy dishes maintain a hint of sugar just behind the chili flavors.  Our Orange Beef and General Tso Shrimp came either drowned in heavy sweet amber, or had it on the side.  Both were framed in Broccoli Florets, the much overused non-Chinese veggie. Their tastes were fine, but we all commented on the unexpected sugariness of the platters.  The Spicy Shrimp, Scallop & Squid with Pepper Corn Salt, was a relief from the cane, and would have been completely on target had it all been crisper.  Finally, my sushi sample of an Eel & Avocado Roll was average, with much more Avo than Eel, and artificially colored Wasabe and Ginger.    Bottom Line - The suburbs has taken the edge off the kitchen here.  Everything was accommodating to the local market.  Too much broccoli, and not enough real heat. Not bad if this is what you are looking for.

Came down to 40th Street to meet a good friend, and parked right in front of Tandoor India.  When he arrived, I asked where he wanted to go, and he pointed to the doorway right behind me.  Auspicious beginnings... First impression was of an old establishment somewhat in need of refurbishment, but with inviting scents of curry and coriander drawing us in.  I checked the buffet as we walked past to our table and saw an extensive collection of yellow, red, brown and rusty sauces, all looking fresh and inviting on a cold Sunday night.  The place was not crowded.  Settling in, I decided to take a look at the menu because I was not in the mood for a cascade of flavors and tastes, but wanted to relax with only a few.  We were given copies of the take out menu, which somewhat surprised me.  On the cover it said: "We believe that the joy of eating lies in the art of fine cooking." I'll drink to that. We ordered Tikka Masala (with Chicken), which came out in a fine pink sauce of tomato and ginger, and was quite good. The Baigan Bharta was tasty, but was chopped fine rather than with the chunky eggplant I expected.  They cheated a bit on the Garlic Naan by bringing us regular Naan painted with garlic butter.  It didn't work, as it was not integrated into the bread, but sat on the surface, and lacked the baked garlic pieces I love in true Garlic Naan.  A disappointing way to pay an extra buck. The Mango Lassi was pretty good,  but a little thin from using milk rather than yogurt.  A nice plate of rice came with the meal.   This was a meal in which we were more engrossed in the conversation than attentive to our food.  The strong brotherhood carried the day, and the meal became background.  For the overall experience, I was quite satisfied. We didn't solve any world problems, but agreed we would get together soon, and try again.

Tough crowd!  Coffee depends on the quality of the water.  Here, you might want to have it tested. Definitely has an unusual aftertaste.  Still, it was potable and left no lingering aftereffects.    Can't speak to the sweets, but the bathroom was tidy.

Returned today for lunch at 12:30.    The small dining area was crowded, but I found a deuce in the corner nearest the work area and settled in after ordering their Apple Sausage Special.    It arrived about 10 minutes later, a small, but tasty Apple Pork Sausage with Maple Chipotle BBQ Sauce, Grilled Onions, and a boatload of fries.  While it was a very good lunch, a couple of observations need be made.  First, the roll of a potato hot dog roll, which was not as good as a crusty French or Italian alternative would have been.  Second, there were a lot more fries than sausage.  They were good fries, but made the sandwich seem even smaller by comparison.   Still, I liked the ambiance, service, and overall brightness of the place, and did not mind that they made some presentation decisions that detracted from what could have been an exceptional lunch.    Certainly worth many returns.

Rolling in from Westmoreland County on the Pa Pike, my stomach started growling after almost four hours on the road.  I was near exit 312.  I pulled out my trusty sidekick Mobile Yelp and dialed in "Thai Restaurant."  It came back with two choices in the vicinity, so I opted for the one nearer my location.  Thai Place has an unassuming name, but under its self deprecating identity lurks a very fine Thai kitchen and comfortable dining space turning out very good authentic grub. Where many other restos of this genre approach the atmospherics with dark wood and musty scents, this shop is bright, light, and airy.  The owner works the front of the house enthusiastically, while the single server on the floor managed a warm smile and genuine concern for all the patrons.   I ordered the Tom Yum Soup (Vegetables) and Drunken Noodles (Chicken).  Both were excellent.  They asked my preferred spice level between 1 and 3, and I asked for max spice.  That's the way I got it, right at the point where my sinuses start to run. Love it!  There were plenty of Veggies and Tofu in the soup, and even more in the Drunken Noodles.  There was enough for dinner the next night.    The only reason Thai Place did not reach the apex was that my Jasmine Tea arrived in a lovely lime green mug with a teabag, rather than a pot of brewing boiling water and loose tea leaves.  That is the best way to achieve full bodied flavor, and requires fewer return visits to refill the mug with hot water.  I get that good tea is expensive and often unappreciated, but for me it sets apart the very good from the superlative.

Mandarin Garden in Willow Grove, Pa., is a throwback type of Chinese restaurant, the kind I went to with family as a kid in New York. Larger space.  Silk wall hangings. Jade sculptures.  Large menu covering most things from Cantonese through Hunan and Szechuan delicacies.  Seniors taking advantage of the Early Bird specials.  My nostalgia surprised me.   Most important, the food was very good.  We were celebrating a first birthday in the USA (Chinese national), and were hoping for something a little extraordinary.  Judging from the approving smiles as each dish was devoured, we got what we came for.    Hot Green Tea arrived immediately along with the dry crisp noodles duck sauce and hot mustard so ubiquitous in Chinese/American houses.  I don't indulge in this table snack, but my friends did in large quantities.  I was selected to do all the ordering, and came up with the following choices: DanDan Noodles (Spicy), Gunpowder Chicken (moderate spice), Jumbo Walnut Shrimp (mild spicy), Crispy Beef with House Made Toffee Cashews (mild spice), Cumin Lamb (spicy), and Tsingtao Beer for all the birthday toasts throughout dinner.    Realizing that management was Fuzhounese, we did not have high expectations in the spice department.  Their cuisine tends toward sweetness, but there was no harm in asking for some heat.  The kitchen handled each dish in their own fashion.    The DanDan Noodles were topped with ground pork and a chili sauce mix that was warm, but not what I was hoping for.  Still, our server anticipated this and had given the table a small dish of chili sauce to upgrade the burn.  I used some of it, but my guests did not.  They were content with what was presented, and not as accustomed to heavy spice as me (Good to know).    The Gunpowder Chicken was also on the mildly sweet side, with a trace of chili on the bird breading, but with the sauce sweetened by an apple.  Unusual, and enjoyable, even if not packing heat.    The Cumin Lamb was the strongest dish, with plenty of tender meat and cumin, that brought a light sweat to the upper lip.  Not the killer dose of cumin piled on lamb chops in some shops, but strong enough to know they were trying to appease us.    The Crispy Beef with Toffee Cashews, was also tending toward sweetness, but they had candied the nuts very well, and when eaten with the copious slices of lightly crisped beef, was fun to eat.    Finally, the Jumbo Shrimp with Walnuts reinforced the theme that the house interpretation of spice and heat began from the perspective that food from this part of China was always degrees of sweetness or sourness, but not really chili pepper fire breathing dragons.    Again, my friends were fine with all of this and genuinely enjoyed their meals.  It was my own blinders about Szechuan flames that was the issue, not the kitchen attempt to move their dial in my direction.  Once I realized that I was making myself too critical of the platters because I wanted my friends to be happy; and that they were already there and praising me for finding such a nice place to celebrate, that I was able to let go, and just roll with the food, and accept that it was really very good.    Good lesson to learn.  Better to let the house do what it does well, than to ask them to conform to my unrealistic expectations.

As a facility to hold a large luncheon meeting for about 150 lawyers, this Wyndham Garden Hotel in the heart of Trenton, NJ, is reasonably decent. Walking distance from the courthouses, and parking deck next door, it is easily accessible for most who want to attend to get a good meal while listening to a quality presentation on the latest issues in internet discovery requirements and security. These Bench Bar lunches are always a good place to catch up with friends and hobnob with the judges in this vicinage.
