She seemed to take a proprietary interest in the operation.   Glad I returned and was able to write a more positive review. It also provides me with another good joint to eat when in the vicinity.

Way back in 2009 when I attended my friend Jessica M's wedding, I was so blown away by the DJ she hired that I sang their praises to anyone who would listen. A year or so later, at my girl Karen B's wedding, we tore up the dance floor all night. Once again, No Macarena was responsible. I knew - KNEW - that they would one day DJ my wedding, and they were one of the first vendors I booked once my man and I set a date.   Kim, the owner, hooked us up with Jonas, who was amazing to work with. We had some venue changes a couple months out and he worked with our venue contact on logistics. I sent over the music request sheet a couple weeks out and we spoke on the phone to go over everything, including how to pronounce the names of everyone in our wedding party. I thought this was great and so thoughtful.   We were stuck on a final song and I told Jonas the song we wanted, but thought would be awkward because of a talking interlude. He sent me a version without the talking part, which is what we ended up going with - it was the perfect choice (Home, by Edward Sharpe and the Magnetic Zeros, in case anyone is curious)! Also, I asked Jonas to play my grandparents' song, and he checked with me first to make sure they were ready and available for their dance. He really thought of everything.     My only advice would be to provide all of your song requests up front. Including songs that aren't part of the reception but that you still want to hear on the dance floor. This will save you many trips to the DJ booth and will probably make the night easier for your DJ (sorry, Jonas, but thank you for being so great about all of my last minute requests!).

It took some time, but I finally made it in to FedNuts today. And while I didn't partake in the donuts or chicken (both of which were tempting and delicious-looking), I did have a large cup of smooth coffee while enjoying conversation with the revolving door of industry peeps and neighborhood loyalists.  Felicia and Blake make the ordering process look seamless, even as the small space filled with eager chicken-lovin' hopefuls right before noon. Arrive well before that to enjoy counter seating and some of the non-fancy donuts, which are only available early in the day. Next time, that chicken is mine.

Tippling Place was the third cocktail bar I walked into on Saturday night around 8pm but it was the first with an available seat. I think this place flies just below the radar, which is great when all you want is a place to sit and enjoy a beverage. The bartenders are friendly and there isn't any attitude. Just a cool, comfy setting and great drinks.   The cocktail menu is pretty extensive but I was disappointed that there weren't any hot beverages listed. So I went with a different seasonal delight, which was a pumpkin egg nog of sorts. It wasn't as heavy as a traditional spiked nog though it had all the right flavors. My second drink was made with rye and it was boozy. I loved the pretty cocktail glass it was served in - very vintage.  Drink prices are steep; right in line with other cocktail bars in this city.

C'est vrai: J'aime French Bakery!   The third time was the charm for me with this adorable new bakery. On my first attempt, I tried to meet Alisha S on a Monday, only to find that the shop is closed on Mondays. Alisha had arrived before me and walked in through the open doors. Though she was informed that they are not open on Mondays, the employees sent her away with some complimentary pastries - so nice!   My second attempt was for a savory breakfast. Alas, there was no quiche left by the time I arrived, and I needed something substantial before my long day.   Finally, another meeting with Alisha was scheduled and the bakery was both open and stocked with several quiche options! I ordered the quiche lorraine which came with a small side salad. It was absolutely perfect - decadent and just the right size for lunch. I haven't tried the sweet pastries yet, but there will be many more visits in the future.   I'd love to see an enhanced menu of savory items (perhaps some baguette sandwiches?). Also, I'd REALLY love some wifi (but understand if they don't want to be the type of place where people like me stick around too long). In any case, looking forward to my next visit! À la prochaine!

So far, so good. I had my first experience with ECO Cleaners a couple weeks ago. I dropped my clothes off on a Monday or Tuesday in hopes that I could have them by Friday, which was not a problem. My usual spot always takes at least a week.   On Friday morning, I received a text message from the cleaners informing me that my clothes were ready for pick-up. I haven't done an Inspector Gadget-style study of my threads but they seemed appropriately cleaned and pressed. Also, this place was a lot less expensive than my usual dry cleaner.   Today I dropped off a second batch, which will again be ready by Friday. If all continues to go well, ECO may become my go-to dry cleaner. Super happy to have this business so close and convenient to my home.

Just wanted to give a gigantic shout out to the crispy bacon & feta salad I had for lunch today. It was so damn good, I may need to go back tomorrow for another. Ants Pants is legit. Just wish they accepted cards!

I've been taking Platoon's free classes at the Comcast Center for the past four weeks and I absolutely love them. The trainers, Michelle and Malik, are awesome and inspirational.   I'll admit, I begrudgingly went to the second class dreading the various cycles we had gone through the week before. I assumed that because the classes were free, they would be exactly the same. Wrong! Every single class has been different. Each has been painful in its own special way, but for me, not knowing what's next makes it easier to push through. This has kept me going back for more week after week.   Although I already have a gym membership and pay for another boot camp in NJ, I am seriously considering looking into Platoon's programs.

Super solid delivery experience from Southgate last weekend! Though my husband and I have been to the restaurant plenty of times, it was our first time trying delivery. The restaurant did an incredible job wrapping everything securely, and the time between placing our order and receiving it was really quick!   We started with the KFC (spicy) and the pork dumplings. My husband loves dumplings and I was lucky to snag one. Southgate's were very tasty and I really liked the dipping sauce. The KFC was delicious, as always.   I stayed consistent with my main and got the Seoul hot chicken sandwich, with fries. It was delicious and definitely spicy. My husband had the pork ssam - I didn't try it but it looked great. Can't wait until we can enjoy a meal at the restaurant again but, in the meantime, I'm happy to know we can enjoy the same delicious food at home.

When a double date was scheduled with one of my favorite couples, I needed to select a restaurant with good food and a fairly laid-back atmosphere.  One in which we would not offend our neighboring diners, once the wine was flowing and our inappropriate "remember when" stories were unleashed for the billionth time.    I had only been to West Side Gravy once before but I knew it would meet my requirements while being wallet-friendly to boot.  We arrived to find the restaurant mostly full and very loud.  The background music I had enjoyed during my quiet lunch was completely drowned out.  Fortunately, we were able to snag a table in the rear corner of the dining room, and many of the families with younger kids left soon after our arrival (coincidence?).  We ordered all the fat kid appetizers: crispy cheesesteak eggrolls with horseradish cream sauce and frizzled onions, cheddar and bacon-topped potato skins and West Side fries, topped with bacon and melted cheese, with wine gravy for dipping.  Everything was as delicious as it sounds and we tried to convince ourselves that it wasn't really that bad since we didn't each order an appetizer.  Ah, denial.  My dinner of (now I'm cringing) fried chicken left a little to be desired.  All of the pieces were dark meat, which was disappointing.  The potato salad served alongside was tasty, but the mayo-laden coleslaw was overkill.  My companions all seemed happy with their dishes.  The spicy bacon-wrapped meatloaf over mashed potatoes was devoured, as was the seared ahi tuna special.    Health fanatics that we are, we passed on dessert and decided to finish up our wine and continue on with our night.  I wouldn't mind returning again soon, and I may even try something that doesn't get prepared in a fryer!

I wasn't sure what to expect with Suraya but I absolutely loved everything about it! I'm a fan of the order at the counter, get your number and find your own seat style of dining. Maybe not for every meal, but for lunch or brunch, I'm totally down.   Suraya was incredibly beautiful, as expected. I love Root and Cafe La Maude so was not surprised that these two wonderful businesses combined to make for one lovely offspring.   In our haste to try a medley of items, I completely dropped the ball and forgot to order a side of fries. Who even am I? Next time, for sure. Things we did try: crispy chickpea hummous (perfection), cheese/tomato/onion/long hot/parsley man'oush (very good but I'd recommend sharing along with other items so you have a wider variety of flavors), and the kafta kabab (my partner hogged it and I only got a small bite but it was awesome!).   My man loved his clementine ginger soda and my orange blossom iced tea was nice as well.   The only thing that bums me out is that Suraya is all the way across town from where I live. How come Fishtown gets all the nice things?! I am looking forward to making the trek again when dinner is added to the mix. Suraya is worth the trip.

I probably (definitely) made some mistakes with my first Buena Onda experience. For starters, I didn't actually check them out in-person; I ordered delivery from a service. Second, I didn't order tacos. What was I honestly thinking?!   So while this review is strictly for my delivery experience, I'm confident that I'll stop in for the real deal experience soon.  That said, my meal was solid. I ordered tortilla soup and a chop salad with chicken. The soup serving was pretty small. But, with a thick broth that was chock full of chicken and avocado, it was actually pretty filling. The salad presented really well - the veggies were super fresh and there was a very nice sized serving of sliced, grilled, seasoned chicken. The chicken was a little bit dry, and I definitely was not crazy about the sweet taste of the cotija lime dressing. Also, the tortilla strips that topped both the soup and salad were quite hard/chewy - I had to be cautious because of my sensitive teeth.   Clearly, Buena Onda is all about the taco experience, and I definitely went way off the grid with my order. Next time, I'm in it for the tacos and I'll surely update my review once that experience takes place.

Kanella was the latest installment in my BYO girls' night-outs.  I had bailed on the ladies a few days prior due to a hectic schedule, but after having a pretty rough day, my friends convinced me to cross the bridge and join them.  Always better to sulk in the company of good friends than on one's own, no?    The service was great--our server was full of character and didn't seem to mind explaining menu items we weren't familiar with.  He was on-point with refilling wine and water glasses alike.    We started with a trio of dips and some pita bread.  There was easily enough garlic in said dips to take out all the vampires in Nintendo's Castlevania (I, II and III), so be warned.  The entrée selections were very heavy on meats and whole fish.  Since I'm not very adventurous when it comes to protein, and I wasn't very hungry to begin with, I opted for a Horia Tiki salad (basically a Greek salad) and the Garides Saganaki appetizer, which was a small serving of roasted shrimp in a feta-tomato sauce.  The salad was fantastic--the dressing was more acidic than oily, which I prefer.  The shrimp were good, but they came with their heads attached which is not my favorite presentation.  My friends dined on the octopus app, the pork entrée and the goat stew entrée.  Everyone seemed happy although I did not taste any of them for myself.    Dinner was finished with an assortment of Cypriot pastries and a thick and buttery date tart that had a cinnamon-tasting ice cream.  I had French-press coffee for the first time, which was a presentation in itself and a nice end to the meal.

I was out for a long walk yesterday when I came up to Hale & True, and immediately noticed the signage outside. They are currently offering cider to-go through their window. How could I resist? The employee was friendly and informative about the different types of cider. They had two different bottled ciders, another in cans, and everything on tap was available for growler fills.   The employee put on gloves for the transaction and it was quick and easy. I went with the Lil' Sunshine, which is made with honey and orange peel. I'm saving my cider for the weekend and can't wait to pop it open for a little taste of sunshine!

Xochitl is one of my favorite places to go for a drink in Philly. I hope that doesn't change anytime soon. The margaritas are the best and I do believe they are a bit larger than they used to be. But several staff changes (including the chef) over the past year lead me to this review update.   I'm going to shoot straight: this new version of Xochitl is overpriced. Not for the drinks, which I feel are worth their tag, but for the food, which is sadly not as good as it was in the past. Wanting to share a few small plates for dinner on Saturday night, we ordered a red snapper ceviche for $14. The fish was more like sashimi with some red onion and orange pieces thrown in. There was absolutely no citrus taste to the fish itself, which is a staple in ceviche. It really lacked any kind of taste other than the snapper, which could have used a little salt as well.   Two types of tacos were better in show. The steak tacos were juicy and very flavorful, and the chicken tacos with a nice, healthy slice of avocado were great... with the exception of a small bone in one of mine. The accompanying sides of black beans were slightly warmer than room temp and not so great.   These three plates plus two margaritas each came close to $100, including a generous tip (we received a couple new drinks on the house in exchange for our thoughts on them so we wanted to make sure our server Michelle was covered). Happy hour will probably be the way to go for me in the future, because I cannot live without those amazing margs. Sadly, the late night happy hour I used to love on Thursday nights is no longer, but I'll happily pull up a seat from 5-7 on weekdays.

I met up with a friend for lunch outside on a gorgeous afternoon a few weeks ago. There were plenty of outdoor tables which were covered by a tent that was open along one side. Because it was so sunny, it actually felt quite warm but I bet the tent would be great at blocking some wind on a chillier day.   I was happy to see some booze free options on the beverage list, and ordered a Don't Call Me Shirley, which was a simple club soda with housemade grenadine - fantastic!   We shared the arugula salad, margherita and mushroom pizzas. I specifically requested the salad first but everything was brought out at the same time. Nonetheless, every single item was delicious! So delicious, that my husband and I ordered dinner from the Pizzeria Vetri in Rittenhouse that same night.  I feel like Philadelphia has gone from pizza desert to pizza wonderland in a pretty short time. I don't always think of Vetri when I think of pizza, but it's a consistently solid spot that shouldn't be overlooked.

I've been on the receiving end of André's emails for several months now. The salon always seems to have great specials, but I don't typically require any services outside of my usual cut and color every eight weeks. I'm very loyal to my regular stylist and don't feel the need to experiment outside of our monogamous relationship.  However, the day came when I had a fancy event to host (helloooo Yelpy Awards!) and I wanted to step up my game with some sexified hair. Since my regular salon is located in Vineland, NJ and is not open on Mondays, I had to improvise. Enter André Richard Salon.   The blow out bar was something that I'd heard about through emails and on Twitter, and when I found out that all services on Mondays are 20% off, I was sold. I made a quick and easy appointment online with LB, and the salon called to confirm.   LB was super sweet and definitely seemed to know her way around hair. She expertly blew out my tresses and managed to work some serious body into my locks. I felt like a straight up diva walking out of my appointment, and my hair is still holding onto some volume a day later. Next time I have a fancy event and I can't get out of the city, I know where I'm going.

I ordered delivery from Poke Bowl recently and was pretty happy with my order. I got the Ahi on Fire bowl, regular size. I did ask for the sriracha aioli on the side, which was a solid decision. I'm a little picky about aioli so having the ability to control the amount was perfect.   The bowl came with sticky rice, fresh tuna, jalapeños, scallions, spicy shoyu and a couple other ingredients. I have to agree with Megan Y that there was more heat than actual flavor. Next time, I think I'll create my own bowl and add some seaweed and cucumber to enhance.   Overall, solid poke delivery and I'll be ordering again in the near future.

Thanks to the care instructions I received at Pure, my white orchid has been thriving. So well, in fact, that it grew so top-heavy with blooms that the simple base it came in could no longer anchor the plant down - even with a weight thrown in! After watching my lovely take a flying leap from the windowsill one day, I finally got the hint and off to Pure we went.   One of the florists helped me pick out an appropriate base, and then she transported the plant and added some taller stems to keep the branch upright. I am so pleased with the results and how much prettier the orchid looks in a proper flower pot.   I do not believe the orchid will attempt any more dives.

I really wish I hadn't waited to write this review as the details aren't as fresh in my memory. But, I'd be remiss if I didn't still pop up to give my five star seal of approval!   My husband and I had reservations for an early dinner on a Saturday in October. We tried a lot from the menu: date truffles, garlic yogurt, baked cheese, croquettes, chili chicken kebab, and whole roasted fish. Honestly, I think there was more but, like I said, it's a little hazy over a month later. All I know for sure is that our table was covered with gorgeous food!   Every dish packed a ton of flavor but there was a lot of variety between each plate. Extra props for the fish, which was sea bass on our visit. If you know anything about Jen Carroll, it's that she knows her way around a fish-you'd be kind of silly not to order one at her restaurant! The sea bass was absolutely perfect.    I was partaking in a sober October, and was thrilled to try the N/A Groni, which I had read about prior to our dinner. Basically, it's a booze-free take on a negroni. I absolutely love bitter cocktails and this version was delicious and made me feel really excited to sip on something interesting.   Unfortunately, we had to rush through our desserts as we were running behind for another commitment. Our own fault as we really took our time during dinner. I won't make that mistake again; next time, Spice Finch is the main event! Looking forward to trying the breakfast and brunch menus as well.

I may be having a little too much fun at Juniper Commons. What? There's no such thing? Okay then. We'll just settle on lots of fun being had during my two visits so far. Not to mention, great food and drinks.   There's a lot about the 80s that should probably be left in the past, but the folks at Sbraga Dining managed to pull out all the best parts and incorporate them into their new restaurant. The music selection is on point. I'm talking dance in your chair, sing all the words magical.   The decor is most definitely 80s-esque without being cheesy. I am in love with the lounge area, with its great furniture and throwback culinary magazines. The shirtless Tom Selleck photo on the wall in the ladies room is the cherry on top.   The food that I've tried has been great. I enjoy salads more than the average person and the tableside Caesar and wedge are both awesome. I've had the crab cake on both visits and it was even better on night two. The baked potato is perfection. I've also had bites of the clam chowder, manicotti, eggplant parmesan, fettuccine alfredo, and creamed spinach. All great choices.   The cocktails are mostly gin-based with a couple other fun options like house-made wine coolers. The Flying Caucasian, a gin and coffee concoction, went down really, really easy. My next reservation has already been made and I am looking forward to many more visits!

After almost giving up on finding really good sushi near my apartment, I conducted a little yelp research and came across Oh Yoko.  Not only did they have great reviews, but a few yelpers noted that the owners are huge fans of the Beatles and play only Beatles music in the restaurant.  I quickly realized this place had the potential to both satisfy my sushi craving and provide a solution for what to get my step-dad for Christmas (he's into sushi and also happens to be John Lennon's number one fan!).   I went to check the place out myself for lunch on Saturday.  In Mi, one of the owners, kept me company as I was dining solo and they were not too busy at the time.  I learned that Oh Yoko has been open for three years and all of the fish comes from Hawaii.  The menu was large and had plenty of delicious-sounding options.  There was a huge list of special rolls that made choosing only one very difficult.  I opted for a volcano roll, which came with spicy tuna, mango, avocado, masago and crunch.  True to its name, the dish arrived in the shape of a volcano, with wedges of mango and avocado in the center.  It was phenomenal.  So good, that I decided to order another roll~ this time with shrimp tempura and spicy tuna on top.  Meanwhile, In Mi brought me a bowl of their clear soup, which was a perfect complement to the sushi.    I left feeling very full but with a new favorite sushi spot and a gift card for my parents.  Success!

Excuse me, have you had the mac and cheese? It comes in a piping hot cup which keeps the cheese gooey until the last mouthful, and is topped with buttery breadcrumbs that provide a perfect little crunch.   I shared one side of mac with two other ladies during dinner last night, but it just wasn't enough. So I went back for a midnight feeding and ordered another... which I ate all by myself. I'll spend the day in self-loathing mode but damn that mac was good.

After closing down a nearby restaurant, it was decided that Tria was the closest spot for a drink in a quiet atmosphere.  At around midnight, the bar was surprisingly quiet for a Saturday and there were only a few tables still occupied.  I loved the dark, sexy vibe, flickering candles and the music selection, which was loud enough to hear but not so much that we had to shout over it.    Since I had already enjoyed several beverages throughout the late afternoon and evening, I asked the bartender for a light beer of his choice.  He suggested one of their newest beers, Avril, which turned out to be a refreshing Belgian Ale.  It was a lovely evening and I plan to return soon for another relaxing night, perhaps with wine and cheese next time.

I've been to this Sephora only twice, but both experiences were very positive. My first time was for a makeup application. I didn't make an appointment in advance because it was a weekday morning and I figured there wouldn't be a wait. Wrong! I quickly found out that the makeup counter is always slamming. Fortunately, there was a spot available and I was able to slide in - I don't know what I would have done if they hadn't been able to accommodate!   There is a $50 minimum purchase for the makeup application, but you can buy whatever you want. It's a good excuse to stock up on the essentials. I picked up two of my old standbys which needed replacing, and I also bought the lip color that was used on me that day. My makeup artist was great, and fun to talk to, but I do wish I would have spoken up a bit more about what I wanted.   Unfortunately, I returned a few days later after deciding that the lip color was way too bright for my day to day. It was returned with no questions asked, and the woman at the counter even gave my friend and I some free samples while she was at it. Meanwhile, after signing up for Sephora's insider card, I received an email that my birthday sample pack is waiting for pick-up. Happy bday to me!

While in NJ this week with some time to spare, I did a Yelp search for nail salons and Tara's was among the highest-rated in the vicinity. Several people mentioned calling first and that was solid advice - this is a small operation and only two people were working. I gave them a ring around 3 and they asked me to come in at 4, which worked for my schedule.   There was a short wait time and then I was up for my pedicure. Unfortunately, the chair was wonky and I couldn't move the seat back or recline it at all. Not ideal since I'm fairly tall, but the massage function made up for that a bit.   The woman who did my nails was friendly and, very importantly, gentle. I do not like for my cuticles to be cut on my hands at all and my request was honored. My services were very relaxing!   I gave my nails a good twenty minutes to dry, but one of my nails smudged about ten minutes after I left. Two days later, I have also seen some chipping. I'm hoping the top coat I applied today can fend off any more.   Overall, for the price, which was very reasonable, I'd consider booking there again if in the area. I'll just be prepared with my top coat!

This review is of the private spaces at Hotel Monaco. I have not actually stayed there or seen any of their guest rooms, but I did swing by recently for a site visit and I was completely blown away by the gorgeous decor and fabulous layout. The lobby area is filled with unique chairs, tables and decorative pieces, all of which are bright, colorful and patterned, all of which still manage to exist in harmony despite the craziness.   The large event space fits up to 350 with the adjoining area across the hall, and the space manages a personality that is both classy and modern. It's a refreshing change from your standard hotel ballrooms. For smaller meetings, there are several board rooms on the lower level, plus a gorgeous private dining room that would be perfect for a swanky bachelor or bachelorette party. Or a fancy business lunch, I suppose.   The rooftop lounge, Stratus, is also incredible. There is great indoor and outdoor space, separated by funky glass garage doors. Plus, there are two private rooms on each side of the outdoor area that are just really cool. I am really looking forward to checking out this space when the weather gets warmer.   In summary, I'd like to plan every private party at the Hotel Monaco.

There isn't too much to say that hasn't already been said.  This particular location is clean, nice-looking and always packed with fun-loving people.  Once in a while, you will run into people from the local sports scene, which is always fun.    My most recent visit was on Friday night, after the Flyers' disappointing overtime loss to the Montreal Canadiens.  When my friends and I arrived shortly after the game, Riley Cote and Arron Asham were already seated and drinking beers with a group of people.  How these guys showered and got over there so quickly remains a mystery.  Is there an underground tunnel that leads from the Flyers' locker room to Chickie's main bar?  In addition to the lively crowd and local sports figures, there were also Amstel Light girls giving out free beer.  Score!

At the eleventh hour while getting ready for Feastival last night, I decided it would be fun to have an updo for the event. Since I definitely didn't want to pay $50-75 like the last two I had (bridesmaid problems), I yelped "cheap updo" and Jean Madeline popped up in the results. I scoped out the reviews and their website, and within an hour I was at the salon reading the latest issue of Glamour.   My stylist was Gia and she was only three weeks away from graduation, so I knew I was in good hands. I don't know how the students get anything done with their instructors pacing the floors, but props to all of them!   I requested a modernized bun. Not one of those goofy things women are wearing on the tops of their heads these days, but something a bit classic just with some volume. Gia the miracle worker got down to teasing and pinning. The end result was a fabulous 'do - possibly my favorite updo in my hair's history, even!   Of course, I tipped on the price of a normal updo and the entire thing cost me $35. Still a total steal, considering. I will absolutely think of Jean Madeline for my next special occasion!

Kermit's is overdue for an update from me. I'm there about once a week but could easily be there more because of my addiction to carbs. Fortunately, they do carry other, less carb-forward items! Soups and salads, for one. Their soups vary but I'm a fan of the potato leek. The salads are always delicious!    Obviously, my favorite items are the pizza, bagels and a few of the sweets. I'm not crazy about the icing used for the cakes (it's got that whipped cream taste - I prefer sugary frostings) but I love their brownies and cheesecake bars. They also have great hot and iced coffee and there are rumors of soft serve for the summer. That's a rumor I can get behind.

For the organizational freak in me, The Container Store fulfills my every wish. I got so excited by the potential of the merchandise on my last visit that I had to force myself to focus and stick with the tasks at hand. Which were: airtight mason jars for my flour, sugar, etc., a vertical wrapping paper container and a box for Christmas decorations.   So maybe I got a little sidetracked by all the after-holiday sales. At least I have mini cards to attach to next year's gifts!  Frugal shoppers beware, gettin' tidy comes at a price. Set limits and try not to get bamboozled by the aisles and aisles of promised structure to your chaotic life.

I was pleasantly surprised by my dinner at Olly on Tuesday night! I'd heard some good things, and was expecting a nice meal, but dinner absolutely exceeded my expectations. The space is really cozy and inviting; there aren't too many tables so be sure to make a reservation if you want to eat in the dining room!  My friend and I shared a bottle of sparking water which was fine, but I would love to see some inventive non-alcoholic options on the menu (currently they have iced tea and soda).   The food was awesome, and our server was fantastic. We started with buffalo cauliflower which was much lighter than what I was expecting. Here, you could actually taste the cauliflower, and the sprinkling of blue cheese was a nice addition. Next, we had the mushroom carpaccio, which was delicious! It was spread over the plate with some mixed greens and had a hearty sprinkling of parmesan.   My friend chose the gnudi for her main (really nice!) while I went with the special of the day, a cod and clam chowder. This dish was hearty and loaded with delicious veggies and tons of flavor. Such a perfect cold weather meal!   We couldn't resist dessert and had the chocolate tart and apple crisp. The tart was definitely my favorite; it was super rich and came with the most fantastic whipped cream and a caramel sauce that was phenoms. Loved it!   Scrolling through my insta last night, I saw a photo of some really bomb-looking margherita pizza. Turns out, also from the folks behind Olly! They just opened a concept called Gigi Pizza, which you can access through Olly or a separate door on Bainbridge. Planning my visit!

My first experience at Heads & Tails was on Friday, and it will not be my last. The boutique salon was recommended from a business owner friend who always looks amazing. I booked my blow out with Dana and hoped for the best.   I was a bundle of nerves when I arrived to my appointment - that night I would be hosting a large event and I wanted everything to go smoothly while simultaneously looking cute, calm and collected. Dana hooked it up with a glass of red while she got to work on my tresses. We chatted easily and my nerves started to calm.   My hair is that weird length between short and long so I wasn't sure how a blow out would look, but Dana knew exactly what she was doing. In the end, I had a great style that I felt comfortable with and that even boosted my confidence. To my utter amazement, my hair still looked great after a heavy night's sleep and I was able to rock the look for an extra day. Already looking forward to my next visit!

My first visit to Tbar was almost a year ago, while I was training with my then-manager Kevin L. It was our third and final day together before I would be unleashed to my own devices and we needed a place to settle in for some calls. Tbar fit the bill on that cold day, and aside from accidentally dripping some hot tea on my brand new Mac and nearly having panic attacks over it, it was a good experience.   My second visit occurred yesterday with my now-manager Colleen C. The place was pretty quiet early in the afternoon, and we scored seats on the extremely comfy couches. I confessed to never having bubble tea before, and it was pretty much decided that I had to try it. I ordered an almond flavored tea with skim milk and just a touch of sugar. The tea was delicious, and I was curious about the wide straw and unsure of what was to come. Then, the bubbles started popping up through the straw and I'm pretty sure the look on my face was priceless. It was interesting. I liked it, for something different, although it's probably something I would go for only once in a while.   While we were there, a pressed sandwich was made for another customer and it smelled absolutely heavenly. I'll probably head back and set up shop for a day sometime soon.

I've been back to Osteria twice for happy hour and both times have been solid. If you arrive early you can have your choice of seats at the bar; the crowds don't start rolling in until after 6.   Glasses of prosecco, a red wine and a white wine are all $5. Pretty solid! There is also a beer and cocktail on the happy hour list as well. I'm a fan of the prosecco.  All pizzas are half off and there is a variety of small plates - I tried the trentino and parma pizzas and both were great. The wings were also very good. They are small and cooked perfectly and have a slightly sweet glaze and some seasonings.   Pro-tip: you can get from Osteria to Distrito on the inside if you need to avoid the elements!

If you haven't had brunch at Xochitl yet, get thee a reservation. It won't be long before Sunday's little secret gets out.   I've now been for breakfast on two separate occasions, and on both visits, everything has gone beyond my expectations. Full disclosure: My second visit was comped because my boyfriend and I were invited to come in and sample the menu. But our first visit was on us, and we arrived on the very first Sunday they started offering the brunch menu.  Starting with the drinks, the coffee has an ever so slight cinnamon taste that really goes well with the bold flavors of the food. Mimosas are served cold and taste fresh-squeezed. Bloody Marias are a bold take on traditional BMs, served with tequila and a chili-salt rim. Waters are filled regularly without having to make requests.   Xochitl's ceviche remains one of my favorite preparations in the city. So light, so flavorful, no matter what variation they are serving it is always delicious. Skip the usual guacamole and share this light starter instead.  On both visits the boy and I ordered the same exact thing. For him, huevos con chorizo: Two sunny-side eggs baked in a dish with kale, potatoes and loads of chorizo. Just as good as it sounds. For me, huevos revueltos: Eggs scrambled with thick-cut, almost pancetta-like bacon pieces and spicy peppers, topped with queso fresco and spicy salsa and served with corn tortillas. Every bit as good with egg whites substituted for whole eggs, which I requested on my second visit.   We also tried the cornmeal and black bean pancakes, topped with fresh whipped cream, seasonal berries and the most delicious syrup I've ever had the pleasure of eating. These pancakes were nothing like any I've ever known before and yet they ranked among the very best. Highly recommended.   The sun-lit room with happy music made me actually feel like I was on a mini-vacation. This is how brunch is supposed to be.

Shout out to Ed and crew!   After scratching up my car pretty solidly in a tight driveway earlier this year, plus more love taps than any car should endure, my vehicle was looking pretty beat up.   I pass Philadelphia Auto Body regularly and noticed their signs to check them out on Yelp. I was impressed by the reviews and before/after photos, so brought my car in for an estimate. Admittedly, it was a little more than I wanted to spend, but Ed walked through every step and I realized I had underestimated the amount of work needed. At the end of the day, I feel like the price was well worth the result.   My car looks beautiful! There is zero evidence of the driveway incident, and my bumper was also touched up quite a bit (anything more would have required a new bumper so I am thrilled with the results of the touch up). Additionally, Ed recommended a bumper license plate protector for the front of my car - a genius suggestion that looks great and will hopefully help keep the front from getting too banged up in the future. Last but not least, the team identified some shoddy repair work from a previous incident that was handled by another shop in the city. They fixed these mistakes as part of my service, which I greatly appreciate.   But wait, there's more! My car was returned with a full detail. Goodbye, Jersey shore sand and grime.   I feel like my car is new again. I'm so happy! Highly recommend these guys and wouldn't hesitate to bring my car there again.

I've had takeout from Izumi a couple times now and I really love it. The food is always packaged very nicely and everything tastes great. I love that they label the sushi on the clear lid so you know which rolls are which! The gyoza are huge, delicious and come with an awesome cucumber salad. Probably my favorite gyoza in the city. I've still never dined in but I would love to do that sooner than later!

If you read my recent review for Tria Rittenhouse, this one is essentially going to be pretty similar. We once again ordered the Cheesy Package for 2 from Tria's current takeout menu. This time, we went with pickup instead of delivery because we also wanted some wine.   Again, everything was packaged so nicely though I will say Rittenhouse had a slight edge because they packaged their side salads separately (not a big deal). This time, we went with two sandwiches, one turkey and one tuna. I asked for aioli on the side for the turkey sandwich but didn't think to ask for no mayo on the tuna since our sandwich the week before didn't have any. Turns out, the tuna sandwich does come with mayo and it was on there pretty thick, so it's something I'll keep in mind for next time.   We also switched up our dessert from the flourless chocolate torte the week before to the ricotta cheesecake. I didn't think the chocolate could be topped but the cheesecake was incredible! Next time, we might have to add on the extra dessert because it will be tough to decide between the two.   Can't wait to enjoy Tria in person again but I'm loving their current to-go offerings!

Sea salt honey tart, you make me want to write a country song.   Last night, I hosted my book club and one of our fabulous members brought over the sea salt honey tart from Cake Life. Hmm, Cake Life? "It's where Beyoncé got her birthday cake." 'Nuff said!   I'm not a huge dessert person but I know when a good thing's in front of me, so of course I helped myself to a sliver. Wow. The rich, sweet, buttery-goodness with just the tiniest hint of sea salt to round out the flavors was truly magic. The tart reminded me of St. Louis gooey butter cake - but better.   Waking up this morning to a leftover slice really made my day!

I only stopped by RBC for a single round with some friends but had a great time! There's a huge lot with tons of parking, and plenty of seating both indoors and outside on a patio. I was really impressed by the selection of brews and thrilled that there were a couple cider options.   Upon looking at their website, I realize now there are also some wine, cocktail and a few NA options as well. Good job, Rockwell!   I wasn't feeling beer so opted for the chile guava cider, which tasted like a typical apple cider but with a fantastic spicy kick at the end. The sweetness was just right for me. Not too dry but definitely not too sweet. I really loved this cider!   There's a small shop where you can pick up beer to go and I thought the packaging was really gorgeous. I would have loved to pick up some beer for my husband but didn't want to chance packing them in my bag before flying home. If you're hungry, there's also a food window and I saw some delish looking cheese fries - next time!

I had a very positive experience with Wilensky's. Our front door lock had been getting tougher and tougher to open over the course of a few weeks - to the point where we realized we couldn't leave the house without getting it fixed because we feared we wouldn't be able to get back in!   I found Wilensky's on Yelp, gave them a ring in the morning and spoke with a friendly guy who said he would have their locksmith give me a call as soon as he was in. I received a call maybe an hour later and the locksmith said he could be over around noon, and he was.   Turned out, something in our lock had broken and needed to be replaced. This was remedied in about fifteen or twenty minutes and now our lock works perfectly. The total charge was $140 - eighty or ninety of that was the visit alone and the rest was for the fix. Yowza. Hopefully my locks will be good to go for a long time!

After dinner at ZoT with a large crew of yelpers, several of us were in the mood for a change of scenery.  I had never been to The Irish Pol before, so had no expectations whatsoever.  This is what I encountered:  - 30 or so beers on tap, including Blanche de Bruxelles, the first beer I requested at ZoT and seemingly the only beer that they did not have  - Awesome jukebox that consistently defaulted to Beastie Boys tunes between requested songs  - My newest addiction, Photo Hunt, which apparently cannot be mastered (even with a team of five people)   - AWESOME bar food.  Does The Irish Pol cater?  They should.  My brother will be so impressed when I introduce him to this most wonderful dive bar.  It is sure to become a staple.

I love this bar. Last night was my second visit and I enjoyed it just as much as round one. The cocktails are well-balanced and delicious; the bartenders really know what they are doing.   Happy hour is a total steal, featuring a really nice red and wine selection and a handful of cocktails, plus some of the regular bar snacks at way reduced prices. I won't tell you how many orders of the puffed pork chips with wild onion sour cream dip I ordered, but it was more than one.

I am way overdue on an upgrade to Buena Onda. We order lunch or dinner from them pretty regularly, and it's rare that I receive an order that I'm not happy with, though it does occasionally happen. Thankfully, our orders are on point more often than not.  One thing Buena Onda does better than most of its competitors is packaging. Tacos arrive in grooved cardboard containers that keep the tacos from spilling all over. We enjoy the fish and shrimp tacos but have tried many of the others as well.   Recently, buena bowls have been added to the menu, and they are great! So far, I've tried one with tofu chorizo and one with shrimp. Both were excellent and kept me full all day, which is what I want out of a healthy(ish) lunch.   I have been pretty disappointed by the serving sizes of the guacamole and salsa, which come at standard restaurant prices but really small portions. Nonetheless, I love Buena Onda for quick and easy Mexican food, delivered to my front door.

Went to the Hut on Wednesday night with two of my girlfriends.  We sat on the outside deck which was nice, although a combination of the overhead lights and fan caused a blacklight effect that was giving me an intense headache.  Luckily, someone turned off the fan and the Jamaican rave experience ceased.  Other yelpers mentioned very slow service and I would say that they were partially right~ our server was very attentive (as were the other staff members who consistently refilled our chips and mango salsa basket) but the food took a long time to come out.  Not such a big deal for my group of friends that night because we talk for hours anyway, but I could see how it would be annoying if you were hungry and didn't want to be there for three hours.    The coconut shrimp app was DELISH.  I wish we had ordered two since the plate had four shrimp and there were three of us.  Two of us got the jerk chicken breast platters and the other had the mango chicken platter.  The chicken was tender and very flavorful but perhaps a bit too spicy on the jerk plates.  The mango chicken was really good also but my friend kept coming across a lot of small bones throughout her dish-- I think it might have been harder to see them in the mango sauce versus the jerk sauce where you could see them more clearly.    I'm glad we got to check it out but I don't see myself dining here often with so many other options that I prefer in the city.  Also, the $4 corking fee for EACH bottle of wine or six pack was pretty ridic.

I love Shibe! My husband picked up a couple gifts there for Christmas, including something I needed for a pollyanna gift for my brother in law. I was very happy with the items he picked out - the styles are cool and have a throwback look, totally different from other Philadelphia sports wear I've seen.   The shirt for my brother in law was too small, so I swung by the store one day to swap out, after calling first to confirm that there was a larger size. While there I also picked up a gift for my grandfather, a long-sleeved gray Eagles shirt made of the softest cotton. The shirt is nice enough to wear out for a casual dinner and doesn't have gigantic logos or anything too loud.   I also happened to notice the nice selection of female attire, and I have my eye on a throwback Eagles sweatshirt. Prices are very reasonable and the selection is vast for such a small store. I'm impressed!

My nails were having an emergency situation (aka, looking like a frightful mess) and I had to take action. Normally, I would have booked an appointment at my regular day spa in Jersey, but a couple things prevented me from doing that. First, they aren't open on Mondays and second, I was car-less as I had just dropped off my wheels for some much-needed TLC. Time was of the essence as I only had one day before leaving on a week-long work trip. A quick call to Rescue Rittenhouse Spa at the eleventh hour and I was delighted to not only receive an appointment, but in a desirable time slot, no less!   The elevator doors opened and I faced a large sunny room with wood floors, white walls and pretty everything (staff included). I selected my polish (Chanel's newest, Black Pearl) and had a seat near the pedi station, where I chatted with another client who told me I would quickly become a Rescue devotee just as she had. Soon after, the lovely Jean swiftly erased the signs of flaky old polish and shaped and buffed my nails back to their natural state. Then, she expertly painted. After the top coat, I was taken to a waiting area and instructed to wait at least ten minutes before making a move. I checked my tendency to fidget and did as told.   When I looked down at my hands hours later, they appeared wet with shine and resembled nothing of the morning's talons. While I still plan to remain loyal to my usual place, I don't see any problem with having a fabulous alternate for the days when convenience matters more.

My experience with Pacifico Hyundai was not a positive one. I was working with a negotiator who I hired to help me through the buying process. My negotiator set up an appointment for me through the manager of this location. I was supposed to go there for a test drive, plus an assessment of my current car's value. Easy in, easy out, and with intentions of buying a car if everything went smoothly.   When I arrived and asked for the manager, he immediately passed me off to a sales rep and I knew things were not going to go as planned. When I sat down with the rep, she asked for my phone and email address, which I did not wish to give as I would not be doing any of the negotiation for the sale. This did not go over well. My test drive was pretty awkward and very short - I was reminded more than once that it was the last day of the month which made feel uncomfortable. I brought up the fact that my car was also supposed to be assessed and that was quickly shut down.   After leaving, I immediately called my negotiator and asked that he find my car at another dealer; I simply did not feel comfortable there. One week later, I've got the car I want at the best price possible (spoiler alert: not from Pacifico).

I checked out Brodo on day two and while there are definitely some kinks that need to be worked out, I anticipate that this will be a solid spot for lunch in center city. I knew I wanted a salad but I also wanted a taste of one of the delicious-sounding soups. Fortunately, they have a combo option where you can do a half sandwich or salad and a cup of soup. I did the salad/soup and with a largish bottle of diet Snapple, the total setback was just over ten bucks. Not too shabby!  My lunch partner and I had arrived just after noon, right before the rush. As we collected our utensils and parked ourselves at a table, it was clear that there was going to be some major back up with regards to the amount of customers and the time it was taking to get orders out. We didn't have to wait too long but there was a large crowd of people waiting for the rest of our lunch. As we waited, I noticed the Boylan's soda fountain. Nice!     The half and half combo is the perfect size for lunch. The Maryland crab soup was average but did the trick (admittedly, I chose it specifically for the "LF" insignia, meaning low fat, but there are plenty of richer options), and the cobb salad had crisp romaine lettuce and just the right amount of toppings and dressing - not too much but not lacking.   It seemed like table wipe-downs were being overlooked in the rush, but other than that and the small wait for our lunch, my experience was solid. Hopefully in a few weeks, Brodo will be running like a well-oiled machine.

As far as my care at this office goes, I feel pretty confident. But that's once I'm in the exam room. Everything before and after that point is why this facility gets an average rating. The receptionists are hit and miss... mostly miss. I've gotten attitude and short attention spans on almost every call I've placed to the office. God forbid you ask whether your insurance covers something and they have to open a file or place a call to find out.   The doctors are solid. I used to see Dr. Hyder but after seeing Dr. Prasad once I ended up continuing with her. She's no longer in the Cinnaminson office but on my visit last week I saw Dr. Kessler and she was great, too.

Okay, Smiths.  To be fair, your establishment is pretty swank for a sports bar and my brain did start chanting "sau-sage par-ty, sau-sage par-ty!" upon entering.  However, $26 for two slightly-dirty Ketel One martinis?  For realz?!  Not to mention, the martini I specifically requested was listed on the board as having blue-cheese stuffed olives and yet the olives in my drink, while indeed plump and delicious, were hollow and... empty inside.  Sad.    I'll be back to check out a game and some of those delicious-looking apps, but I definitely won't be hitting the hard stuff.

The fall wedding season rolled on for me last Saturday with the reception of my newly married friends, Shannon and Ed, at Citizens Bank Park.  Everyone was totally stoked about this one because it was so different from the norm.  Parking was a cinch in the special events section, and there were plenty of staffers to direct everyone to the appropriate places once we were inside.  Cocktail hour was held in the Hall of Fame section, which I was familiar with already.  The passed hors d'oeuvres and cheese boards were perfect for taking the edge off.  Everyone was then instructed to take the elevators to the Diamond Club, where dinner and dancing would take place.  The fun level of this room was out of control.  A huge dancefloor was situated to the left, with high-top tables and a large bar in the back, and all the guest tables were to the right, with food stations on both sides of the room.  The newlyweds took Philly pride to a whole other level when, instead of clinking champagne glasses to initiate a kiss, guests were instead asked to wave their Phillies rally towels, which were placed at every setting.  I'm pleased to report that only one towel caught on fire and it was stomped out quickly.  The food was a highlight for many, with one side of the room offering traditional wedding fare such as pasta and chicken, and the other side of the room offering ballpark style food like hot dogs, sausage and peppers and, of course, a build your own cheesesteak station.  Always the classy one, I opted for a whiz wit, extra ketchup, and a Flying Fish which was on tap along with many other selections.  After dinner, we danced nonstop for the remainder of the night and had a great time.  The staff was abundant and mostly everyone seemed friendly and helpful.  I would love to attend a special event at Citizens Bank Park again.

One of my girlfriends and I decided to get together to gab over pedis instead of our usual cocktails, and Rescue was one of the few nicer salons with evening hours. Unfortunately, my friend was unable to make it at the last minute, but that wasn't going to change my plans. I called Rescue and ended up moving my appointment up by an hour, which was more convenient for me.   My last visit to Rescue was about a year and a half ago, and at the time I felt they could not match my favorite salon. Unfortunately for me, that salon closed, and since then I've been a nail care wanderer, checking out all types of salons around the city. I've found a few places I like, but I'm not fully committed to any of them. It had been a while since my last Rescue experience, so it was time for another try.   My pedi with Anna Marie last night was pretty wonderful. I'm still not a huge fan of the bench seating, but it was more comfortable than I remembered. Maybe those yoga classes are paying off. Even though the pedi was only a half hour, it still felt really thorough and my nails and skin were properly filed, buffed, scrubbed and polished. Like an idiot, I wore socks and pointy boots to the appointment (it was cold and rainy!) so I stuck around for a good 35 minutes after to let the polish dry. No one made me feel like I was wearing out my welcome as I waited, either. I was offered tea or coffee and told to relax as long as I wanted, which was so nice. My toes were then slathered in oil and wrapped with plastic wrap to protect the pedi from my boots. There was still a very slight smudge by the time I got home but it's practically miniscule and certainly not the fault of Rescue. Stupid pointy boots.  I also noticed there is now a check-in offer for a $100 massage and manicure package. It's so tempting. I may return sooner than later.

Wild child notwithstanding,* I do like having La Va as a local coffee option. Last night, I went to meet a friend for a cup and catch-up. My sweet tooth was kicking, and I had every intention of trying one of the chocolate desserts I had ogled in the case during visits past. I asked the barista about them, and he told me there were three different varieties and his favorite was the chocolate mousse. I paid for my large latte and took my chocolate mousse bomb to a table.  Holy chocolate heaven, Batman. I'm surprised I was able to put the spoon down after a single bite and save the rest for when my friend arrived. I could have easily scarfed and destroyed the evidence, but I'm glad I shared, because sharing is nice, and all girls love chocolate. I will definitely consider a sweet treat from La Va again (just not if I've already indulged in one of their oozy fresh mozzarella, tomato and olive tapenade panini - that would be going overboard).     *The moment I walked in, I noticed a toddler running rampant. The parents clearly did not care that there were meetings taking place, people doing work, etc. Their kid was just booking around the store, running into people's stuff, touching things, etc.   If it was annoying for me within the first 30 seconds of my arrival, surely it must have been annoying for the other customers. I wish I could review the parents, but this sidebar will have to do.

I got Prime Rib'd, y'all.  I was warned that the happy hour at Prime Rib was so magnificent, so unbelievably dealtastic, that it had actually overpowered some of the most seasoned drinkers I know. I had heard about the battles fought, the stories that have become legends, and yet I went in blind, became instantly mesmerized by the old money and botox, and ordered my half-priced Kettle martini with blue cheese stuffed olives, up. And then I ordered another. And then I ordered a cosmo (that tasted more like a gimlet). And it was only after my third drink that I thought it wise to order some food for my empty-besides-the-vodka stomach.   I think you know where this story is going.  After a few tasty clams casino and some potato skin crisps, some renegade in our group insisted we order yet another drink. I got a glass of sauvignon blanc. What I needed was a large water and two advil, plus a full night's sleep.   Onward into the night we went. I can only hope the other people we encountered throughout the evening were as intoxicated as our crew/me. It may be a while before I'm able to face a martini again. And that is really saying something.

Starbucks in my home town! The future is now!   Like Yelper Steve P, I too was very skeptical when I saw the Starbucks sign outside of the building that once was a mom and pop pancake house way back in the day. But I was pleasantly surprised by the large, inviting space when I walked through the doors. This would be a great spot to get some work done or have a casual meeting.   I ordered an Americano and asked if they had the egg white breakfast sandwich, since I didn't see it on display. The employee at the register looked through the refrigerator but, unfortunately, they didn't have my go-to. I opted instead for the bacon, gouda and egg sandwich which was tasty if not as light as the egg white option. My Americano was HOT - I couldn't drink it for a good twenty minutes.   Overall, glad to see this new location so close to home. No more driving to Delran for my Starbucks fix!

Guys, this place is dangerous. In fact, my stomach is rumbling at the mere thought of all those rum drinks I put down during my recent trip to New Orleans.   There's some good news. While the sickeningly sweet grenade drinks are poured straight from a bar gun, there are some drinks on the menu that are a little less suspect. The Pirate's Passion is made of 151 rum, Malibu and pineapple juice. No added syrups or sugars or anything. Drink one so you can get the whole Bourbon Street thing out of your system and then switch to something lighter. Don't drink several. Trust me.   Love that they feature bands and especially love the request system, which is one of those bank tube thingies that suctions your container of requests (and your tip for the band, of course) over the bar and to the band.   Last but not least, props to the bartenders, who pour the same drinks over and over and who maintain the same high level of theatrics every time someone orders a Shark Attack.

It has been about a year since I first joined City Fitness and I still think they deserve four stars. I love the variety of classes and have gotten myself hooked on spinning and yoga - never thought I'd say that! My favorite yoga instructors are Abby, Carmencita and Tesh, while my favorite spinning instructors are Nicki and Timaree. But everyone's teaching style is different, so if you're new I'd suggest bouncing around until you find your favorite.   Also, after a year of going to the same classes consistently, only twice did I show up to find out that a class was cancelled. That's not too bad considering I take anywhere from two to four classes every week. It seems like they do their best to find a sub in the event that an instructor can't make a class.  My membership includes WeFit but I've only gone once. It was really intense, and the "Who's Fit - We Fit!" shout is totally corny. It's a great workout, but I feel like I'd enjoy it more with a friend. I cannot seem to motivate myself to go alone. But the classes are always really packed so people are definitely hooked  Really, the only disadvantages to the gym from my point of view are that towels sometimes run out at night when it's most crowded. Also, the lockers are limited and at night it's really hard to find one that is available at all. That's annoying as is but it also causes people to bring their belongings to class which can get in the way. I'm lucky that my schedule is flexible enough to come during the day - by far the most peaceful time at the gym. Regardless of the time of day, the staff members are all still very friendly. I'm still very happy with my decision to join City Fitness!

Crazy Sushi remains my go-to for an inexpensive sushi lunch delivery during the week. Their lunch specials are great; I always get three rolls with soup and rarely deviate from that order. By the time tax and gratuity are added, my total is still less than twenty bucks! Delivery is usually super quick, often within a half hour of placing an order. I usually see the same delivery man who is always very friendly. Love this place!

What's not to love about this gorgeous example of architecture? Traveling can be hectic and sometimes stressful, but whenever I find myself inside 30th Street Station I feel calm. There's usually a pretty chill vibe about the place, which puts me in a good traveling mood. Whenever I return from a trip, I feel welcomed back by a beautiful building that reminds me I'm home.   There are plenty of coffee options for the morning, and from what I hear some of the restaurant selections aren't half bad, though I don't believe I've ever taken advantage myself. The book store is pretty decent, and there's usually somewhere to sit if necessary.

Fried. Cheese.   But not just any cheese - these curds are pressed in Wisconsin and sent straight to the folks at The Cow and The Curd, where they are prepped and served within days of arrival. Bite into one of these little nuggets and expect some of the ooziest cheese around. Definitely try them with the chipotle dipping sauce, which only makes them tastier.   I highly recommend splitting an order with a friend or two - much as you'll want that little bucket all to yourself, it's probably in your best interest to share.

This was the go-to movie theatre during my teenage and college years. And apparently, it still is since Loews' parking lot is always full and the theatre remains relatively nice. The one thing I don't love about the place is that the crowds can be unruly depending on the movie and time of day (usually a night or weekend, which is becoming less and less likely a time that I'll go to the movies nowadays). That's probably not something most movie theatres have control over but it is a reason that I'll typically opt for the former Ritz in Voorhees or the Ritz locations in the city. That said, it's the perfect theatre for a weekday flick and very convenient to the area's shopping and restaurants.

I've been here twice now, the first time for a manicure and the second for a pedicure. For a manicure, it's a very nice place and you'll certainly get your money's worth. But for pedicure services, no one can match my regular guy Thom from the salon I frequent in NJ.  The pedicure chairs are not comfortable. Basically, you are sitting on a cushioned bench against a wall. From this angle, lifting your leg for certain parts of the service feels more like exercise. For the cost of a pedi at Rescue, I want to relax and zone out, not pull a muscle trying keep from sliding off the bench as I hold my leg in a 90 degree angle.   I would certainly return to Rescue for another manicure or some of the services they are better known for, but for pedis I'll stick to my usual spot.

Every time we sit at one of the pub tables at Southwark, I admire the beautiful orchids in the windows. The thick, sturdy leaves of the plants are deceiving; they give way to long, thin branches too weak to support their own stunning flowers without assistance from supports. I'm fascinated by them.   Needless to say, I was touched when my boyfriend presented me with my own white orchid for Valentine's Day. It was one of the most thoughtful, lovely gifts I've ever received.   Since it was purchased from Pure, I decided to pop in to get some tips for how to take care of my new beauty. The store had several interesting flowers and not the typical bouquets one would expect from a flower shop.   The woman I spoke with was super helpful, and I'm so happy I stopped in. Apparently, orchids draw most of their moisture from the air, so it's really only necessary to water them about once a month with a half cup of hot water. I shudder to think what would have happened had I not known this info. Hopefully my plant will continue to thrive and flourish for many moons to come.

After getting home late from an event recently and realizing I'd skipped dinner, I opened my various delivery apps to see what was available after 10pm on a weekday. I had a craving for Chinese and Red Kings 2 was one of the very few places that was still accepting orders. So I crossed my fingers while placing an order for general tso's, fried rice and wonton soup.   Not only did Red Kings come through with some very solid eats, the window of time between my order and delivery was only about 30 minutes, give or take. The food was nicely packaged and there was plenty of it; I got several meals out of my order. Adding this one to the delivery rotation for sure!

Another great option in St. Louis! I went to Grace Meat + Three with some girls for brunch, and we scored the beautiful farm table by the front window.   We ordered everything at the front counter and took numbers back to where we were sitting. I really couldn't decide what I wanted and ended up with an everything but the kitchen sink salad (got some of their Nashville hot sauce on the side for the chicken!), plus sides of grits and mac and cheese. The mac was all right but the grits were super good.   My salad was nice, the ingredients were very fresh, but I felt like it was missing something. I realized after I finished that the salad was supposed to have cheddar and cornbread crumbs -- both items were definitely missing and would have added a lot of flavor.   Later, I wanted to grab an iced coffee but realized I'd have to get in line again to order. I'm not sure if you can head over to the bar side for additional drinks but I just waited for the line to die down.  All of the staff we encountered were so friendly and it was a comfortable place for a leisurely meal! Great spot for a group and I'd happily return.

Not awesome.   That's how I'd describe my experience at Five Guys tonight. I was so pumped for a Five Guys burger, since they are Whole30-compliant. The young lady who took our order was friendly and seemed to understand exactly what I wanted - a burger in a lettuce wrap, with grilled onions, tomato and pickles.   When our number was called, my mom and I grabbed the bag and went back to her house to dig in. I opened up my container and couldn't believe it: two grossly overcooked patties, no lettuce whatsoever, a couple slices of pale tomato, a couple pickles and a small pile of grilled onions. Where was the g-d $&*# lettuce wrap?! In that moment I was Nancy Kerrigan. Whyyyyyyyyy?   My stepdad said the Cajun fries were really good, but his burger, and my mom's, were also majorly overcooked. The fries I couldn't have, because, Whole30. Nine more days. French fries of the world, you're on notice.

My first experience with Kermit's was last week, and it was not nearly as rave-worthy as I expected. I wasn't feeling well so I ordered the chicken spaetzle soup, which comes with mustard bread. At home, I discovered absolutely no chicken in the soup and the spaetzle-like remnants were sparse. The soup mostly consisted of broth and some slighly crunchy carrot and celery pieces. The broth was salty and had a heavy rye taste. Not really my thing but it did have a lot of flavor. The bread was easily the best part of the meal. So not really off to a great start.   A few nights later, I came home to discover half of Kermit's sausage and peppers pizza on the counter. I had half a slice at room temp and thought it was pretty good. The next day, I heated some up for lunch and was really impressed. The spicy peppers were really awesome and the caramelized onions gave a hint of sweetness. Things were looking up.   Last night we ordered a selection of things to try. I had some of the antipasta salad, which was delicious, although the dressing was not. I ended up using some of my own from the fridge. The salad's ingredients were all sliced and scattered over the lettuce. I loved the slivers of pepperoncini and artichokes. I had half a slice of the BBQ pizza just to taste, and it was absolutely delish.   This morning, I had a chunk of the salted caramel brownie with my coffee. Heaven!   Based on my experiences so far, there are things that Kermit's does really, really well, and others that need some fine tuning. I'm happy to test out the waters, and I'm very happy to have them right in my neighborhood.

My girlfriends and I had a wonderful dinner at Heirloom last week. Our server was new so she had a more experienced server with her at most times, but she did a great job and everything came out as requested. The bread basket to kick off the meal was impossible to resist -anyone who can turn down a biscuit is not human, in my opinion. The restaurant is warm and inviting.   My first course was a chopped salad with crab and shrimp. The salad was supposed to feature blue cheese, but there was just a small amount on a tiny crouton. It was a good salad, but I'd recommend the mozzarella and tomato salad over the chop, which is what my friend ordered. Also, the crab cake small plate was excellent.   My entree was the bouillabaisse, which was a great option for someone looking to eat light. There was a nice piece of fish, some shellfish and root vegetables in the sauce... but I did pick out a few bones. My friends seemed happy with their entrees, also.   For dessert, we shared some sort of cake with ice cream which was a nice end to the meal.  Although this review may not come off glowing, I truly enjoyed my dinner at Heirloom and think it is well worth a trip from the city. I look forward to returning!

I definitely like this location of Foodery more than the other. Even though it's smaller and cramped, I feel like I can find what I'm looking for quickly. The prices are still astronomical. A mixed six pack and a bag of Doritos set us back somewhere around $26 on Saturday. And before you go thinking we picked a bunch of fancy stuff, consider the following. The beers in our sixer were: Dogfish Head 60 Minute, Harpoon IPA, Ballast Point Sculpin, Victory Weizen Bock, Cerberus something or other (looks slightly fancy with a foil topper) and Great Lakes Edmund Fitzgerald. Come on.

I did a three month trial at Benjamin's Desk in the spring, in an effort to get out of my work from home (sometimes in my pajamas until 5pm) routine. My plan got me something like five days at Benjamin's Desk per month, plus several hours of conference room time per month. I thought the price was reasonable at something around $99/month but I believe that may have been a limited-time offer.   The set-up is spread across two very unique floors. The first floor is a quiet space with lots of desks, a nice-sized conference room, some offices and several phone rooms which were available to reserve (perfect for interviews or phone calls). While I noticed some socializing on this floor, it was mostly done in whispers. This is the put your head down and work type of space.   Upstairs is a much more vibrant floor. It reminded me of Yelp's offices, actually. It's an open floor plan with desks and chairs but also some couches and counter seating around the outskirts of the room. The vibe on this floor is a lot more casual and the conversation flowed. I made some buds and felt energized by the company.   At the end of my three months, I ultimately decided that I wasn't utilizing my membership to the fullest. I truly enjoy working primarily from my home and bouncing around the city to different coffee shops as necessary. But I can absolutely see how Benjamin's Desk could work (and does work) for creative, work-from-home professionals. Check them out if you've got a flexible work schedule and you'd like a change of scenery.

Three of my girlfriends and I picked Pizzeria Vetri for this month's GNO, and we were not disappointed. The restaurant was actually a bit smaller than I expected but fortunately there was no wait for us to sit on a Tuesday evening. Seating is community-style at long tables. I loved that they already had the hot red pepper flakes and parmesan shakers on the tables.   We started with salads, the wood oven and the arugula. I stuck mostly to the arugula (though I stole a slice of prosciutto from the wood oven salad - wise move), which was absolutely delish. It's topped with roasted potatoes, pesto and olives. So pretty much some of my favorite things on a plate right there.   We reasoned that four girls should have four pizzas so we ordered the margherita (the best version I've had in a while), the quattro formaggi which may have been my least favorite though certainly tasty, the sausage and roasted fennel pizza which was very nice, and finally the melanzana with eggplant and stracciatella cheese, my hands-down favorite. Is it shameful that we had only one or two slices left when all was said and done? Maybe, but I have no regrets.   Vetri does it again!

At around 12:45 a.m. on a recent night out, it was decided that one more drink was necessary, along with some bar food.  Since I was the driver that evening (cue shock and awe), our fate was in my hands.  I tried to think of a location that would have both ample street parking and a quick and easy route to the bridge.  Prohibition Taproom came to mind.  The bar and furnishings were dark and mostly made of wood.  A string of old-fashioned looking lights hung above the bar, and they would dim a little on occasion, which I loved.  A DJ played some serious jams that were heavy on the gangsta rap.  It had been a while since I'd heard Easy E, Dre and Ice Cube and I was digging it wholeheartedly.  Everything flowed perfectly with the old school, moody vibe.    We sat down at the bar and asked if the kitchen was still open.  It was maybe five after 1 at this point, and the bartender took a look at the clock and told us that everything in the kitchen gets turned off at 1.  There were no ifs, ands or buts, and no offers to see if there was anything that could be done.  For a new bar trying to make it in a recession, I found this response to be pretty off-putting.  I got over it when I looked at the beer list, though.  One glance at the words Blanche de Bruxelles, and I knew that Prohibition Taproom would soon become one my spots.  Next time, I'm coming earlier so I don't miss the kitchen cut-off.

Being in the Market & Shops at Comcast Center reminds me all too much of my former life in the corporate world. Shudder.  That said, if I did work in the Comcast Center, I'd be pleased with the options for lunch that I'd be able to take advantage of without even leaving the building. Percy Street Barbecue and DiBruno Bros., most notably.   The "Shops" would leave me wanting. There isn't much to get excited about. A lady who wants to flex some plastic on her lunch break is better off at Liberty Place or Walnut Street.

"It was a cold and rainy day in March.  I went to Kristoff's where I usually get my hair done.  But Kristoff wasn't there. He had mysteriously disappeared.  In his place was a stranger named... Rinaldo.  I'll never forget him.  His eyes were steely gray.  His hands were like ICE.  He said 'I'll streak your hair and I'll give you a body wave.'  He worked very fast and then, as he turned my chair around to face the mirror... I saw it... HE PERMED ME!"  I'm sure many of you remember this story from the oh-so-campy eighties movie, Troop Beverly Hills.  Well, it was the exact scene that came to mind after a recent hair misfortune.  My story goes a little something like this:  It was a hot and sticky day in July.  I was in Boca Raton, where I never get my hair done.  Luckily, I had my Paul Mitchell products, the hotel hair dryer, and my straightener named... Chi.  I'll never forget it.  The cord was long and black.  The hot plates had always made my hair look nice.  I plugged the bad boy in and then got to work with the dryer.  Then, with a lion's mane of fully-dried, poofy hair, I picked up the Chi.  That's when I noticed... MY STRAIGHTENER HAD DIED ON ME!  AHHHHHHHHHHHHH!!!!!!!!!!!!! (blood curdling screams) ______________________________________________________   You don't even want to know what my hair looked like that day!  Luckily, I flew home that night and set my alarm for the following morning, a Sunday, so that I could go to Bed, Bath and Beyond first thing and replace my most valuable hair tool.    At five til 10, I stood outside the BBB like a crazed animal waiting for a feeding.  Finally, the manager unlocked the doors and I stalked to the beauty section, a woman possessed.  A nice (scared?) employee unlocked the case containing the pricier beauty appliances and retrieved my Chi.  Moments later, the manager graciously approved a price match, based on a picture from Ulta's website that I conjured up on my iPhone, as I could not produce a hard-copy flier since Ulta was not yet open for the day.
