Even better, the good people at the register accepted my 20% off coupon.  96 dollars later, I raced back home with my wonderful new replacement, purchased significantly lower than the suggested retail price.

My sister and I hit Franklin's for an early dinner, not knowing what to expect. The layout is what you would see in a big sports bar. The main dining room with bar is huge and then there is a smaller bar room with games and a jukebox towards the back. A big wraparound deck is off the back. At just after 4pm, the place was nearly empty so we took seats at the back bar where the only other customer was sitting.   The bartender was friendly and everything we ordered came out fast. I noticed a solid beer selection though I stuck with light beer. We ordered the fried pickle chips to start, and they were really solid. Cornmeal crusted and served with a really great aioli. We both had buffalo chicken salads and found them to be very tasty. I would have preferred a bed of romaine lettuce instead of plain old iceberg, and a little more buffalo sauce would have been great. Next time I'll ask for some on the side.   Franklin's seems like a fun place for an after work happy hour (assuming they get more of a crowd after 5 or 6). Sis and I are definitely planning to return.

I recently noticed Giorgio on one of the apps I use regularly for delivery. My go-to pizza spots are Kermit's and Santucci's, but I was in the mood for something different and gave Giorgio Pizza a try. It's worth noting that the prices at Giorgio are a lot lower than these other spots.  We ordered a sausage pizza and some arancini. Delivery was fast and the food was just the right temp. While the sausage on the pizza was average, I found the pizza overall to be pretty solid. The arancini was cooked nicely but it was sitting in sauce so the parts facing the sauce became soggy. I'd recommend serving the sauce separately for take-out or delivery.  I would definitely consider Giorgio again for fast pizza delivery when I'm not looking for anything extra fancy.

After loads of visits in the past year, I'm actually shocked that I haven't already updated my rating for Pub & Kitchen. I adore the place. First of all, the staff is amazing, genuinely friendly, and gorgeous. That's a rare combo. They're also all fabulous dressers, but that's just a bonus.   The space is inviting, comfortable and lovely. It always smells nice, like freshly finished wood, and the flower arrangements (particularly the recent Christmas-y ones) are gorgeous.  But the food is what gets me, hook, line and sinker. I'm going to say it: Jonny Mac is my favorite chef in all of Philadelphia (and the Jersey Shore, for that matter).   Basic pub grub like fish and chips and spicy pulled pork are favorites, and breakfast is always on point, but entrees and specials are out of this world. On New Year's Eve, we enjoyed several courses, two of which included beets and raw oysters; items that aren't favorites of mine. A beet salad was citrusy and the beets were shaved so thinly that the flavor didn't overwhelm. I ate the entire thing. Next up was an oyster ceviche. I am not a fan of raw oysters but I give them a try now and then because I do enjoy the briny taste of the ocean. The oysters we were served on NYE were so unbelievably amazing, I'm still thinking of them fondly three days later. That ceviche marinade came straight from the gods.     Other courses included gnocchi with poached lobster, perfectly seared scallops, mahi mahi and brussels sprouts, pork belly wrapped pork loin and the most amazing cast iron seared steak. If there is one thing that is guaranteed to come out tasting incredible every single time, it's the steak. Any steak. With a lightly seared crust on the outside and tender, juicy meat on the inside, one cannot go wrong. Desserts are inventive while still remaining classic, and will not disappoint.  I am so very happy to be living just a few blocks away.

Solid eats, Golden Triangle. And thank you, Yelpers, for the solid reviews which led to my trying this place for takeout while in the neighborhood. I placed an order through Eat24 and the food was ready fifteen minutes later.   My order was just some basic shrimp pad Thai but it was easily one of the better pad Thais I've had in Philly. My husband started with the roti, which came with a cup of potato curry soup. This four dollar starter is absolutely delicious and a must-get, if you're carbing out on a Sunday (or any day, really). His pineapple rice was nicely balanced with crunchy veggies and great flavor. The price was right as our total came to about $25.   If it weren't for the $4 delivery fee I'd probably order from here on the reg. For now, I'll stick to pick-up when I'm in the area.

Czerw's is a no-frills shop for all your Polish needs. There's a fridge filled with pierogi and a meat counter with several varieties of Polish sausage. The guy who works the counter has to be one of the nicest butchers around. He welcomed me and my fiancé like we were regulars for years. We picked up a couple pounds of kielbasa and grilled it for the game - it was a huge hit and couldn't have been easier. Five stars!

Compared with other Starbucks locations, this one seemed fairly new. There were several comfy-looking chairs and the entire place was spotless.   The staff seemed a bit amateur. I asked about the ingredients in a pumpkin latte and got a bewildered look from a staffer, like I had just asked a question about quantum physics. After I explained ("You know, is there sweetened syrup? Just spices? What exactly gives the latte it's pumpkin flavor?"), she relaxed and ran through the ingredients list, which seemed too sugary for what I wanted (and there's no sugar-free version of the pumpkin latte). I went with a regular latte and the boyfriend ordered a mocha.   There were several staffers but the process wasn't as seamless as other locations. Still, this is one of the few coffee shops in the area that I could find on my Yelp app, so it did the trick.

I have finally experienced the awesomeness that is Xochitl.  Reluctantly, after several seasons of passing up on Restaurant Week, I decided to give the promotion another shot.  Xochitl has made me a believer again.  My friend and I arrived slightly early for our 7 p.m. resie but we were escorted to a table immediately.  Our water glasses were filled and bread was dropped off with two buttery spreads.  Our server, whose name escapes me, was wonderful throughout the experience.  When she asked to take our drink order and I handed over the recipe for a "Skinnygirl Margarita," she didn't bat an eye although she did let me know that their regular margaritas are made only with tequila, fresh lime juice and a little bit of simple syrup.  No sour mix, no triple sec, no hidden agendas; just honest ingredients, served over ice, with a rim of salt.  I ended up taking her word for it.  (For the record, one Skinnygirl plus two positively delicious Xochitl margs equals three sheets to the wind, minus any trace of a stomachache, which I almost always get when I drink margaritas anywhere else.  Hallelujah!)    The food was glorious.  For our first course, we both chose the tortilla soup.  Large bowls containing cubes of cheese, slices of avocado, tortilla strips and dried peppers were presented to both of us.  The broth was poured on top, tableside.  I really enjoyed this dish, although my friend and I agreed that the dried peppers had a curious taste.  She didn't like them, I was intrigued by them.  Next, we both ordered the octopus, mackerel and shrimp ceviche trio.  Each was served atop a little fried tortilla round.  I have been daydreaming about the octopus ceviche since I awoke this morning.  It was easily the most tender, well flavored octopus I have had (sorry, Mr. Garces).  For my entrée, I chose the squid hot pot, which was another win.  When the lid was removed from the pot, tender rings of squid in a spicy tomato sauce appeared before us.  I have to say, the dramatic presentations really made the dining experience special.  The woman seated next to me ordered a stuffed pepper that was so beautiful it could have easily been pictured in a food magazine.  Meanwhile, at our table, my friend had food envy as she was experiencing mixed feelings about her skirt steak (which I thought was good, although it was served lukewarm).    For dessert, my friend had the churros, which came with three dipping sauces.  One of my favorite things in life is the right to choose several condiments to go with a meal and this presentation was right up my alley.  Fortunately, I had my own dessert to tackle; an appropriately sized mini chocolate soufflé with a mini scoop of cajeta ice cream alongside.  Perfection.  Our experience last night wasn't just great by Restaurant Week standards; it was great by any night's standards.  What a truly fantastic meal.  When our bill was dropped, along with a plate of mini biscotti (delish, by the way), we were also each given a $10 card to use any time before November 31.  My dining companion and I are already discussing what we will order on our return visit!

On more than one occasion, I've found myself so frustrated by this particular Acme that I vowed to never return.  Nevertheless, its close proximity to my apartment has lent itself to repeat trips for the sake of convenience.  I can't think of a trip to this store where the experience has not been flawed in some way.  Basic grocery items are often out of stock.  There are hardly any workers so the lines are always long and there inevitably ends up being a problem at some point that requires the involvement of a manager.  Worst of all, the produce department is horrendous, and it just so happens to be the straw that broke this camel's back.  Last week I bought a bag of baby carrots.  When I got home and opened the bag, they were slimy.    Yesterday, I bought some pre-husked and packaged corn on the cob.  Naturally, it was twice as expensive as the unhusked fresh corn, but I was in a hurry and I wanted a healthy snack (corn on the cob + spray butter + Frank's buffalo hot sauce + seasoned salt = food of the gods).  I also bought a large container of watermelon chunks, to bring to a pool party.  When I got to my apartment, I threw a pot of water on the stove and tore open the corn.  I was immediately met with a weird smell, which seemed to coincide with the slime that was now on my hand from a piece of the corn I had just picked up.  A whole lotta' cursing started going on at this point in time, as I disgustedly threw the cobs into the trash and frantically washed my hands with pink grapefruit soap, hoping to erase the association of Elmer's glue with my favorite summertime produce.  The watermelon was sufficient later that evening, but the damage had already been done.  I will not be returning for any reason in the future.

When my husband and I got home around midnight on a recent Friday, we realized we were hungry and had no food in the house. We were super excited to see that Oregon Steaks was still taking delivery orders, and we placed an order for a chicken cheese steak for him and a turkey hoagie for me.   The delivery was fast - maybe thirty minutes tops? Awesome. The sandwiches were huge. I thought the quality of the turkey was just okay - and I also pulled about half of it off because there was so much. My husband enjoyed his chicken cheesesteak.   Though I might not pick Oregon Steaks as my first choice when other options are available, it was more than solid for an impromptu late night meal delivered right to our door.

Spending a Saturday night at my sister's house often comes with some late night eating, and Domino's has come through for us on more than one occasion with fast, reliable delivery and accurate orders.   After trying but failing to find a local pizza shop that was still open and making deliveries around midnight, we had to default to Domino's. While I wasn't involved in the ordering process, my phone was used to download the Domino's app and place the order. Apparently, there were lots of helpful notifications about our order being received, our pizza being prepared, and at what time we could expect delivery. Just like our previous experience, delivery was surprisingly quick and our pizza was hot and actually quite tasty.   This may have been our only option for late night eating, but it wasn't a bad option at all.

My boyfriend and I popped into Rittenhouse Hardware this morning to pick up a few supplies. Compared to the home improvement giants, the store was minuscule, but every square inch of space was taken up by gadgets and tools.   As one employee worked on making us key copies, another was available to tell us exactly where to find everything on our list. Both knew the merchandise inside and out, and we received helpful tips whenever we were stuck deciding between items.   The experience was quick, painless and dare I say, fun? I absolutely plan to visit this little shop on the regular for all my household ish.

At first, I defended this store because it's the only affordable grocery option for anyone south of South/north of Broad. But after several visits, I've realized it's okay for picking up a few items, but not a replacement for my regular stores (Shop Rite in South Philly/Jersey or Wegmans in Jersey). Yes, I still make regular grocery runs to Jersey, because the quality of the stores is so much better. I digress.   The guy who works the seafood area seems to hate life and he takes it out on the crustaceans he haphazardly throws around. My first and only encounter with him was when he made me feel as if he was doing me a favor by using the same gloved hands he used to slop around a bunch of fish guts to handle the cooked shrimp I requested. (I ended up not purchasing them.)  Panhandlers set up camp outside the store and though there are security guards just inside the doors, no one does anything.   On the bright side, mostly everything is priced competitively and I can generally find what I need (though it takes some searching since I never remember the layout of the store). The rotisserie chickens are tasty as well. I'll return if I'm too lazy to drive all the way down to Shop Rite, but I'll try my hardest not to be that lazy.

Numa has taken over one of my old favorites (Moshi Moshi) from the days when I worked in the evil world of legal marketing. I was happy to see a trendy overhaul had taken place with regards to decor, since its former self was pretty dated.   I found prices to be on the high side for lunch. My tuna set which consisted of a miso soup starter and two pieces of tuna sushi, a tuna avocado roll and a spicy tuna roll set me back $14. This is definitely higher than typical sushi roll combos at most places, but I did think the sushi was better than average. It was quite delicious, actually.   I'm happy to know that this is still are reliable spot for quality sushi and I'll likely return.

My crew returned to Smith's for happy hour on Friday night.  Both bar areas were packed with people who were happy to be out of work and starting the weekend on an unusually warm March evening.  A table opened up and we sat down to order some apps.  The boneless buffalo chicken and bacon mac and cheese* were both pretty awesome.  Our server was friendly and fairly quick, although she forgot special requests like sauce on the side, etc.  Overall, it was a solid happy hour and everyone around us seemed to share that sentiment.  *Several hours later, I returned home and tried to recreate the culinary delight that is bacon mac and cheese.  My findings?  Microwave bacon and Annie's whole wheat shells and cheddar do not a gourmet bacon mac and cheese make.

Since giving up meat and poultry for the month of February, I've often found myself lusting over memories of my meal at The Fat Ham last month. I really don't think I was cut out to be a vegetarian.   My favorite bites:  Ricotta cheese Oyster sliders Baked mac and cheese Hot chicken Chocolate chip cookie skillet  So, to sum it up: cheese, fried things, and carbs. Fantastic.   My dining companions and I had several more dishes, including the mustard greens, ham and eggs, grilled trout, shrimp and grits and Carolina gold rice, amongst others. While these didn't make it into my faves (and I'm starting to realize why - because they were not fried and were possibly healthy), it was nice to try a little bit of everything. Knowing now what Kevin and the team can do with a chicken, I'm also very much looking forward to testing out the country fried lobster tail.  On a brief second visit for drinks, delicious cocktails and a light and bright red wine on tap were enjoyed.        Anxiously awaiting my next visit.

This store has all of your costume needs covered. The best part is that it is open year round, as opposed to many of the pop-up Halloween stores that come in and out of the area. I stop by every few months to pick up props for events and they always have what I'm looking for. The prices are a little more expensive than I'd typically expect for cheaply-made, plastic doodads. But honestly, the fact that I can get in and get out with exactly what I need makes it worthwhile. Just be sure to purchase only what you want - the store does not take returns, which can be an inconvenience.

My friend Kory introduced me to BItar's today, and I feel like I need to send him a thank you card. This was probably the best Greek/Mediterranean food I've ever had, and conveniently also the least expensive. Currently only open until 7pm, this is the perfect spot for lunch, or an early dinner if you can get over there and grab some take out.   My chicken kabob combo platter came with delicious grilled chicken sliced over lettuce and tomatoes. I requested a tatziki sauce instead of the sesame sauce. On the side was a generous serving of tabouli salad, a heaping pile of hommus, and a grilled pita served in foil. The portion size was huge. I had enough left over to eat for dinner.   While there I also had a few bites of the Bitar gyro, which has lamb, marinated onions and peppers, french fries and a sriracha aioli. Also delicious, if a bit heavy for my usual lunch preferences. Definitely a solid hangover meal, however.   Of course, I couldn't leave without a little bite from the pastry case. I tried a pistachio and honey selection that was wrapped in a shell which reminded me of shredded wheat (only more delicious). I knew I should have written down what it was called, but I did take a photo of the full tray.  I will be happy to jump in my ride and head down to South Philly for lunch at Bitar's. It surely will not be long before my next visit.

They have a wedge salad on the menu! Happy day!  Only problem is, I cut into it during this morning's brunch without realizing one of the herbs sprinkled on top is something my palette is vehemently against. The freshly diced herb served as a salad shrapnel, which unfortunately turned me off. Otherwise, this would have been one of the best wedge salads I've come across in recent memory, since all other components were perfect. Next time, I'll order without the extra greenery.

I'm not really a Starbucks fan but sometimes, it works. The employees at this location were all super friendly and engaging. You know when you have a bunch of questions about something and you can tell when the person behind the counter is losing patience? Not this crew. They were happy to answer the surprising array of questions I had about their iced teas.   Speaking of which, I ordered some type of berry concoction that was bright pink and fruity but very, very tart. Walk the extra block to Cafe Ole for their amazing raspberry iced tea if that's what you're jonesin' for (sorry, Starbucks). The only reason I didn't do that was because I had already been there just an hour earlier and didn't want to be that weirdo going back twice in an hour.

Monica's previous review was all I needed to assure me that Preferred Party Rentals would be more than capable to assist me with rentals for Yelp's Backstage Pass Party. From my first phone call to my last (the day of, when my point of contact Kristin called just to make sure everything was going smoothly), the service I received was stellar.   I made multiple changes to my order and Kristin handled it like a total professional, even though I was convinced she probably wanted to strangle me after my many additional requests. But hey, it was a learning experience for me and the next time will hopefully be a little more seamless with regards to the ordering process.   PPR had everything I needed, from tables to linens to chairs to coolers to a helium tank and more. The delivery guys were fast and I didn't have to tell them twice where everything went; they were on it.   My only misstep was sending an email a couple days before the event to request some additional chairs, when I should have just called. Somehow, the message was lost in translation and I didn't get the extra chairs. It wasn't a big deal, but in the future, I'll definitely be sure to call with any changes or add-ons. I'd highly recommend this company to anyone needing a large amount of party supplies, and I will definitely call them again.

I haven't been hitting too many new businesses lately so I'm making sure to give extra love to the ones that have been getting me through this year. Every single time I'm in Old City, I figure out a way to swing by Cafe Square One. Their salads are still just as awesome as they were when I first tried them a couple years ago, and the employees are always friendly and welcoming.   One day I'll deviate from my beloved southwest salad to try one of the wraps or sandwiches... one day.

Kanella has skyrocketed into a comfortable place among my favorite restaurants in Philadelphia. I absolutely love Greek/Mediterranean food and Kanella does it best. I'm definitely a little sad that they have outgrown their cozy little BYO on Spruce and are moving further east to a larger location with a liquor license... but that won't stop me from going the extra distance, either.   At dinner or brunch, we always start with the trio of spreads. This is the only time I have ever eaten beets and enjoyed them (pureed with who knows what but this spread is delicious). The pumpkin feta spread is wonderful as well, and I'll always love the potato and onion spread. While I love the pita, I have been trying to cut back on carbs and I was able to get a side of veggies on my Friday night visit, which was awesome.   Lately when we go for dinner, my fiancé and I order a handful of small plates and just share everything over a couple courses. The octopus with white beans is excellent, as well as the grilled halloumi with tomato and fig salad. We recently tried some lamb dumplings which were super flavorful and a little spicy. If mussels are on the menu, I highly recommend those as well.   Basically, you can't go wrong with whatever you order at Kanella. I'm hoping for one more visit at their current location but I'm looking forward to seeing what the future brings as well!

If you haven't had happy hour at Xochitl yet, you are missing out. From 5-7, get $3 drafts and $5 margs (the best in Philly, in my opinion). Late night Thursdays add half off to the bar menu. I suggest the guacamole, queso fundido, torta sliders, calamar, tacos de suadero and ceviche.  So basically, everything is awesome.

Wow. Collingswood keeps making me miss it more and more, and Zeppoli is no exception. Located in the former IndeBlue space, the difference in decor is night and day. The minimalistic look has been replaced by dark wood tables and chairs, lace curtains that go high enough to block out the street view while still giving a peek at the night sky, and flickering candles on each table.   Our server was excellent, and very helpful in guiding us through the tough decisions between one dish or another throughout the night. Freshly baked bread was delivered to our table along with olives and olive oil. I can honestly say my starter was the only thing I was underwhelmed by - a salad filled mostly with bitter radicchio that seemed like an afterthought once I experienced an evening filled with amazing tastes.   Taking a cue from Drew Lazor's Twitter feed, I opted for a half order of tagliatelle al limone, only with prosciutto. Heavenly. The light pasta was bursting with lemony flavor and just the right amount of salty prosciutto. Rigatoni with eggplant and ricotta salata was also delicious, and very hearty for a half portion. I may just order pasta as my main course next time.  But on this evening, I had the Sicilian fisherman's stew, a flavorful broth with cous cous pearls and a selection of tender calamari, mussels, cockles and nice-sized pieces of fish.   For dessert, we shared a cannoli and a trio of gelatos including nougat, caramel and pistachio. Capo... Capo? What was that place I used to get my gelato? Doesn't matter. Zeppoli served me the best gelato I've ever tasted, no contest.   The teeny asterisk besides this five star gem of a dinner? My boyfriend was being treated to it as a member of the press and I was his guest. So if that's the kind of thing that turns you off a review, okay. But the bottom line is that Zeppoli is Osteria-grade dining at a fraction of the cost. Plus, it's a BYO. And I won't stop thinking about the tagliatelle and gelato until I have them again.

Really? I've never written a review for this Capogiro? Okay, well we all know that their gelato is deserving of five bright and shiny stars, so that's out of the way. The super special thing about this location is that they also have booze. And, their staff is more than capable with putting together delicously boozy concoctions featuring said gelato and sorbetto.   This is probably their largest location, with outdoor seating in a roped off area. And they have free wifi. So why only four stars? Well, it's something so simple and easily fixable but, to me, comes off like nails on a chalkboard. In fact, I'm not even sure how their employees stand it. I'm talking about the chairs. And not their functionality or comfort level, but the fact that when they move across the floor, they screech like a million tortured demons in the seventh circle of hell. It's a terrifying sound, one that makes my blood run cold, and ultimately the reason why I had to pack up my bags and head out earlier than I intended while working at their cafe yesterday afternoon. Hey, maybe that's their tactic for getting people to leave. Probably not, though. Please, Capogiro, I beg - put something on the bottom of those chair legs!

Maybe Top Tomato does some menu items right, but my turkey and cheese hoagie was pretty weak yesterday. They didn't have American cheese listed on their menu when we ordered online, so I had to get provolone. No big deal. But the turkey definitely wasn't high quality deli turkey and the tomatoes were a tad mealy. If you're going to have the word "tomato" in your name, at least get some tasty hothouse varieties.   My sandwich was sliced at a really weird angle and not all the way through, so when I tried to pull the sandwich apart the bread ended up ripping at the wrong place. I realize this is the whiniest of all complaints, and I probably sound like a total brat, but if I'm going to order a sandwich from one place over dozens of others in this city, at least try to sell me on it.   My friends seemed pretty happy with all of their selections (cheesesteaks, some type of chicken sandwich and an eggplant parm). I'll admit, there was some food envy. But I'm not sure that I'll be giving Top Tomato a second look the next time I want a sammie.

I had a hankering for Thai and Jasmine Rice was very close to where I was when said cravings occurred. After checking out the reviews and deciding to go for curry rather than a noodle dish, I placed an order for the green curry with shrimp. The food was done quickly and I was on my way.   The portion size was generous and there were five or so very large shrimp and lots of crisp, fresh veggies. The curry was flavorful, with a little heat, and not too heavy. The rice was perfectly sticky and delicious. I was very pleasantly surprised by Jasmine Rice (based on some of the reviews I read), but I will definitely think of them next time I have a curry craving.

Thanks, Jay's, for helping me out with my diet today. How did you know I don't like salmon sushi? You must have had some idea since you replaced my California roll with a spicy salmon roll in my take-out. Clearly, my eyes were bigger than my stomach (yet again) when I ordered the three roll combo instead of the two roll. However, in the future, I'd like to make that decision on my own. Because you still got me for the cost of three rolls even though I only ended up receiving two out of the three that I ordered.   Who knows what that poor guy who walked in after me ended up with. Five minutes after placing his order, he was asked for his order... again.   For average-at-best sushi, awkward service and the California/salmon roll switcheroo, I bestow two stars.

Sbraga was the restaurant my boyfriend selected for his birthday dinner. I had been anxious to get back since our first visit in December, and when I checked out the current menu I was even more stoked. We went all out and opted for the beverage pairing, but I started things off with a glass of sangria, which was super fruity and flavorful.   The first course really set the bar high. Housemade mozzarella with local tomatoes and fried clams appealed to all my Jersey girl senses. This was the perfect summer dish.   Next up was parsley risotto with escargot and prosciutto. I love Sbraga's risotto. Art raved over his scallop and pork belly, but the plate that got the most attention was the tempura fried lobster tail that was sent out from the kitchen. Lobster has never been more tender.   At this point we were feeling pretty full and it was only halfway through the meal. Fortunately, the third course was presented in a smaller portion. My plate consisted of barbecue chicken confit, pickles, cole slaw and onion rings. Tasty and fun.   The dessert course at Sbraga is not an afterthought, but a vital part of the meal. I wasn't walking out of there without the mascarpone/coffee granita dessert from my previous visit, which was thankfully still on the menu. The boyfriend opted for a cherry coke dessert that was totally unique and really well executed. The kitchen sent out the strawberry rhubarb streusal, which was served hot with a scoop of vanilla ice cream on top. So delish.   Our second Sbraga visit was really pretty flawless. Service was excellent and everyone seemed to be working in harmony. The restaurant was also packed, which was awesome to see. I'm looking forward to our next visit, most likely after the menu changes up yet again!

We had a nice meal with friends at Osteria in Jersey, though I have to admit I like the Philly location more. At 10pm on a Saturday, we were one of the only tables still in the restaurant. The bar had a small crowd, but it was definitely pretty quiet.  We started with the vegetable board for the table, which was great. Also, the mozzarella in carrozza which is basically the fanciest take on a mozzarella stick that you could possibly imagine. Awesome.   My friend and I each ordered the pork milanese which came with a lightly dressed arugula salad. It was very good. The fish dish my other friend ordered look great as well. For sides, we shared the olive oil smashed potatoes, which I believe also had pancetta, and the roasted potatoes, which were the clear favorite. Another person in our party ordered pizza and an additional pie was sent from the kitchen. Everything that featured pancetta or some type of pork product (aside form the milanese) seemed overly fatty. I normally love pancetta but I did not enjoy anything it appeared on or in that night.   We finished things off with a couple items from the dessert menu which were hits. With a couple rounds of drinks, the evening made for a fun but expensive night out.

I've always been a fan of Jones, and I'm clearly not alone since this restaurant has been around for quite a while. I swung by after tonight's Yelp Elite Event for a bite and was not disappointed. The menu offers something for everyone.   Since our threesome was all in agreement that the "cheese hold the meat burger" sounded great, we decided to share it as an app. This pseudo-burger consisted of a soft and buttery roll with a giant slab of haloumi cheese, lemon aioli, lettuce and tomato. We hacked it into threes and I was instantly wishing there was more to go around. Our server told us it's a new addition to the menu, and to that I say: "Well played, Jones. Well played."  I also had the ahi tuna tacos, which were good, but not as good as the non-burger burger. Everything in the tacos is served cold; essentially ahi tuna in taco shells, with lettuce, cilantro and a spicy aioli.  I'll be back for that haloumi burger.

Burger Up was one of the spots I had bookmarked before my trip to Nashville. Several of my colleagues had given high praise, and I was staying in the neighborhood, so it was a solid lunch destination for Sunday of my trip.   I was very pleased to see a Bloody Mary listed on the chalkboard, because I was HURTING with a capital H upon arrival. I sucked down two and started to feel like life was worth living again. They were also quite delicious.   Our little blonde server was a peach and asked us where we were from and how we liked our trip when she realized we weren't locals.   We started with the fried pickles which were good. I especially liked the dipping sauce. All of the burgers sounded awesome but I was drawn to the bison burger with white cheddar, lettuce, tomato, fried red onion and fried jalapeños. I also subbed in a side of the truffle fries. The burger was served a perfect medium, as requested. Totally awesome, and my only regret is that I got full really quickly and could only eat about half of what was on my plate.   Most of the seating is communal, and I do wish I would have requested an individual table as there was very little space between us and our neighboring diners. It would have been perfect had we been with a larger group. I would likely return if I found myself in Nashville again.

In one of the more random moves ever, some friends and I ended a weeknight out at Ariana. There were several tables filled with people who appeared to be regulars, and I got that fun feeling like I had stepped into a cool, secret spot. That doesn't happen often. I liked it!  I had enjoyed a peach hookah once before at another establishment and no one seemed to protest at my suggestion, so that's what we ordered. It took a few rounds to really get going but once it did - hiyooo! Some felt the buzz more than others (that would be me, the lightweight), but it was pleasant and brief, without any weird side effects.  We thought the place was open pretty late but the check was dropped at our table shortly after midnight and we got the vibe that it was time to go. Next time, I'll make sure we have enough of a time cushion to finish up before feeling like we have to split.

Woe is me to give any government-run service more than three stars. Like Dan F, it was the third time that was the charm for me with PennDOT.   After 14 months of living in Philly, I decided it was finally time to commit to being a Pennsylvanian. So on Monday I got all dolled up (license photo, of course!) and had my hand on the door when it occurred to me that I should double check the business hours. Closed. Slightly miffed, but not as much as I would have been had I made the trek, I went about my day.   On attempt two I actually made it to the office. I had every document ready to go, but when the woman behind the counter took an extra long time studying my birth certificate, I knew something was wrong. Turns out, my birth registration certificate - the same one I've been using my entire life for all matters of importance - was no longer acceptable because it wasn't an actual birth certificate. Huh? Turns out, you need to apply for a birth certificate because your birth registration certificate isn't actually the real thing. (And yes, that's going to cost ya - $20 to the state!) Luckily, a passport can be used as a document in lieu of a birth certificate. Too bad I didn't have that with me. Imagine my crankiness.  Third visit, chip on shoulder, I returned. I had a full bladder just in case they added urine sample to the proof of identity requirements (kidding). This visit was quick, relatively painless, and I was out the door with my temporary license in less than an hour. Next up: registration and license plates.

You know how every town has an Italian restaurant that consistently churns out awesome food and is your go-to staple?  That's Bruno's.  There are three main parts to this establishment; a BYO restaurant where you can have a nice dinner, a take-out type section where you can also enjoy a quick slice and a liquor store.    Take-out is probably my favorite option.  You can call ahead to place your order, run into the liquor store to grab the perfect bottle of red or white, then pick up your dinner.  Dinners come with a roll and a pretty large side salad, and the entrees are huge (without compromising on quality) and delicious.  I highly recommend the pasta with clams and red sauce.  The red sauce is homemade with plum tomatoes and fresh garlic.  Soooooo good!

Every time I bit into the snappy dog of my Cincinnati Skyline on Saturday, I couldn't help but think that it was the best hot dog I'd ever eaten. I probably said it at least three times. The experience reminded me of a fond hot dog memory of my childhood. Christine B was the lucky recipient of that tale, and if she was bored to death hearing the story of my favorite hot dog, she was a good sport and didn't show it.   This particular link was nestled in a soft bun which held up to the ingredients: chili, chopped onions, creamy nacho cheese and fresh diced green onions. The entire thing was delicious. Adding to the experience were the thick cut French fries. I felt they needed a tad more salt, but they were great otherwise. We opted for garlic aioli and peppercorn ranch dipping sauces, but I tried the honey mustard also and liked it best out of the three.   Not sure why it took me so long to give in to the temptations of Hot Diggity, but it definitely won't be long until my next visit.

For anyone who has been dying to know the answer to the age-old question, "How are those pretzel-dogs at Philly Soft Pretzel Factory?"  I have stepped up to the challenge of taste testing one.  The results:  Not that great.  Kind of gross, actually.    The regular pretzels are bangin', though.  Especially when they're fresh out of the oven.  In tomorrow's edition of Questions People Ponder:  Wawa chocolate milk: moo or don't?

Craft Hall is really interesting. It's a gigantic, family-friendly brewery with a pretty complex restaurant concept. All of the bread and desserts are baked onsite via Lost Bread Co. The menu features a lot of great snacks and sandwiches, though not many healthy options. I've tried the cheese curds, wings, fries and italian market panini. All were absolutely delicious!    The beverages menu offers a lot to drinkers but not much for non-drinkers. I've personally tried their ginger beer, which is on tap (it's great!) and virgin bloody marys (their mix is made in-house and it's delicious!). I'd really love to see some creative NA cocktails, though! For the drinkers, there's a ton of beer, plus some wines, hard seltzers and cocktails. Only a few of the cocktails are made with local spirits (shout out to Philadelphia Distilling and Manatawny Still Works) and it would be cool to see more Philly representation on that list.   For someone like me, aka, not a kid person, Craft Hall is kind of a hard sell. This place was without a doubt made for families. It's truly a genius concept! On my two visits (so far), there were multiple children's birthday parties. That said, the space is so large that even adults-only groups can likely find some kid-free space near the front bar.   This is my spot for hanging with friends who have kids and my go-to recommendation to parents who want to get out with the little people for a while.

Love La Colombe, don't necessarily love this location.   The baristas are all friendly enough, but the bustling energy makes me want to grab my cup and peace out rather than pull up a chair. I'm a much bigger fan of the location on Penn Square.

I am picking up what you are putting down, Southgate! My friend and I had a catch up dinner on Tuesday and it was perfect!   First off, I can't even believe the space was formerly Tangier. It has been completely transformed and looks very modern and sleek. While we passed on drinks, there is a full bar and it looks like a great spot to perch for drinks or a solo dinner.   After reading the rave reviews of the KFC we had to share some to start, and I have to say it was incredible. We both liked the spicy version more but the garlic soy were also delicious.   For my entree I went with the bibimbap with beef in a hot stone bowl. It was great, if perhaps a questionable choice on a hot summer night. I will save the sizzling bibimbap for cooler weather in the future. There are lots of other options I'd like to try in the meantime.   Our server was pleasant and on top of keeping our water glasses full. My only gripe was that it was at times hard to hear him and even my friend over the din of the restaurant. Nothing that will keep me from going back, next time with some drinks thrown in!

I can't tell you how happy I am to finally have a great Italian restaurant in the neighborhood! While I loved Fitler Dining Room, it was more of a once in a while restaurant for us. I can see Trattoria Carina popping up on the rotation far more often.   The restaurant was buzzing on Saturday night - we lucked into one of the last open tables outside and it wasn't long before people were placed on a wait. At this time, reservations are not accepted. I kind of like it - there aren't many places that offer first come first served, so Carina is perfect for a night when you didn't plan ahead but still want a nice dinner.  There is a short list of cocktails and also red, white, rosé and sparkling wine, which you can get by the glass or bottle. The menu is broken into starters, salads, pastas, mains and sides. We wanted to try a little of everything so we ordered the meatballs, pumpkin salad, tagliatelle with bolognese, shells with crab, branzino and broccoli.   I thought all of the food was nicely prepared and presented and tasted great. I love a good plate of pasta and neither of our pasta dishes let me down. The shells may have won out by a small margin - the tomato sauce was just spicy enough and I loved the toasted breadcrumbs for some texture. The branzino was perfectly cooked and I really enjoyed the citrusy tomato salad underneath. Also, those meatballs! If Carina ever opens for lunch, I really hope they put a meatball sandwich on the menu.   I'm looking forward to many more meals at this neighborhood gem!

My first trip to Mac's was solid. A server set us up at a table for six right away and he was on top of his serving game for our visit. When I wasn't sure what I wanted to drink, he brought over a few different samples for me to try. Still kicking myself for not ordering the high ABV coffee IPA that was available.   A friend seemed to enjoy a hummus plate so I ordered one to snack on. I liked that there were a lot of vegetables and not just pita. For the most part the plate was okay, but the first red pepper strip I picked up was slimy, so I avoided those. The cucumber slices were good but they were layered with some sad looking tomato slices. The garlicky hummus had some random red onion slices sticking straight out of it.   Don't go to Mac's for the hummus plate. Do go for the beer and friendly service. (And maybe some french fries - those looked really good!)

I was very pleasantly surprised by my lunch at Red Owl Tavern today. I always sort of thought of the place as a tourist spot since it's located in a hotel. The lunch crowd did seem like a mix of tourists but also regulars who work in the area. I heard more than one table order the cheesesteak, and my server, Liam, said it's one of his recommendations whenever people ask what's good.   I went with the cobb salad, dressing on the side, no onions, add grilled shrimp. The salad came out just as I requested, was perfectly sized and so fresh! The shrimp were huge and there were four - I feel like this salad will actually carry me to dinner. The homemade ranch dressing was perfection. I loved everything about my lunch! I drank water and was happy that my server left the bottle on the table.   Everyone from the hostess to my server to the GM was very friendly. Great experience and I would certainly return without hesitation when in the neighborhood.

Motherhood.   Apple pie.   Weekend brunch.   If these aren't things you can get behind, what are you doing in America, fool?!   Okay, perhaps brunch doesn't top everyone else's list of feel-good national freedoms, but my love for this weekend staple knows no bounds. Case in point, I shamelessly agreed to brekkie at Ant's Pants over the weekend despite my unfortunate pajama-outfit: sweatpants, galoshes and a long sleeved tee straight out of my guy's wardrobe. My car was parked on South and we decided that if the café looked table-ready when we walked past we would go for it and, if not, we would head back to Jersey, where sweatpants are considered acceptable attire in all diners.   We walked into the adorable café and the wait was four deep. A server tried to talk up two available stools at the window bar to the couples before us, but they declined and we happily took them. The same server hooked us up with water and coffee and gave us time as I decided between five or so items that all sounded great, including the famous bacon stack. I went with an omelette from the standard menu - goat cheese, caramelized onions and spinach. It hit the spot and was just the right size. I especially enjoyed that it was served with a side of fruit salad, a welcome change from the norm. The bacon and toast sides I shared with my guy were nice add-ons. The bacon was perfectly crisp and the wheat toast was thick and satisfying.   The price was reasonable considering the tasty fare, and it was a great meal to kick off the weekend.

I used The Gourmet Vendor for an event and it worked out great. I found out about them from a friend who has hired them for family parties on several occasions. What's more fun than an old-school hot dog stand at your party?!    Brad, the owner of the company, was very easy to get in touch with and the cart arrived on time for set-up at my event. The guy who operated the cart was great and I saw lots of happy hot dog lovers. Definitely a great move for a party!

Wow, I had no idea Doylestown had such a shopping scene! I happened to park across from this business on Friday afternoon, and when I saw the Free People sign I had to pop in for a look.   Since I was with my husband I tried to make it quick, but I could have easily spent a half hour or more combing through everything in the store. They stock a variety of recognizable brands and I thought everything was priced fairly. I ended up with a pair of cute, lightweight pants that I can't wait to break out in warmer months!   I look forward to future Doylestown visits and more shopping at this awesome boutique!

On Monday night, for the first time probably ever, I had to tap out of my dinner before even tasting some of the dishes on my table. I was that full. Granted, we went a little overboard while ordering. We ordered: pimento cheese (a special), cornbread with ham and jalapeño butter (a special), pickled shrimp, oyster sliders, mac and cheese, collard greens, fried whitefish and hot chicken. On top of this feast fit for more than just our two, the kitchen graciously sent out: the mustard greens salad, charred cabbage and shrimp and grits.   I had tried the mustard greens salad and shrimp and grits on my previous visit. Since then, both have gotten tastier. The salad seemed less bitter than I remembered, and the shrimp and grits were just phenomenal. I really like that the shrimp are now served completely free of shells.   The charred cabbage is something I wouldn't have ordered but am glad I got to try; it had a lot of nice flavors from the char of the grill, tomatoes and a sprinkling of feta.   Of course, the stars of the show for me were the hot chicken, mac and cheese and collard greens. Better than I remembered and rivaling anything I've had in Nashville. Unfortunately, I was far too stuffed to even attempt a bite of the cornbread or fried whitefish.   I'll be spending the rest of this week trying to work off that meal but it was totally worth it. The Fat Ham has really found their Southern groove.

I've hit up Village Whiskey twice in the past couple of months and it's still a great spot for a bite. Both visits were on Sundays, and we've been lucky to get seated right away both times even though the restaurant is small and seating is tight.   On the first visit, three of us shared a bunch of plates: pickled cherry tomatoes, village burger, bbq pork sammy, and duck fat fries with Sly Fox cheddar sauce. Everything was delicious! I was also happy to see a couple solid non-alcoholic options as well; the lavender fields was a hit!   Last Sunday, I tried the veggie burger and my sister had the bbq pork sammy. Again, we ordered the fries with cheddar sauce. I do think the cheddar sauce could have a bit more flavor, but the fries themselves are really great regardless.    Honestly, Village Whiskey is a spot I didn't think about much because I always just assumed it would be too crowded. Now that I've found the sweet spot, it's becoming part of my weekend rotation!

It's pretty bad when, a short time after "checking in" to a bar via the yelp app, you get a text that says, "What the heck are you doing at Paddy Whacks?"   Trust that you better have a good answer lined up, in the interest of saving any remaining street cred. My reason for being in this self-titled Irish bar last night was for one thing and one thing only: cheap beer. Paddy Whacks is an official sponsor of the Philadelphia Sports Network and, more specifically, the Wednesday night coed floor hockey league which I participate in. This means our team gets 10% off our total bill, half price appetizers and three dollar drafts.   The decision to take this offer up was met with a collective groan amongst teammates, but we decided to scope out the sitch anyway. We entered to the pulsating bass of hip hop. The DJ spun to a room of about ten uninterested people. Poor guy. We grabbed a table on the opposite side of the room and struggled to hear each other over Nelly lyrics. Do the sentences, "Andele andele mami E I E I uh ohhhhhh! What's poppin' tonight?" mean anything to you? Spend one Wednesday evening at Paddy Whacks and I guarantee you they will play on a repeat track in your head the entire next day.   I love some hip hop, but only at the right place at the right time and in the right mood. What kind of responsible person shakes it like a salt shaker on a Wednesday night, anyway?   One beer (Victory pale ale - props for that) was all I could handle before turning in for the night. A couple teammates shared some boneless chicken wings that looked and smelled pretty tasty, but it's unlikely I will be back to try them for myself. The unanimous decision to find a new team bar was made in silent acknowledgment.

Summer has only just begun, but I've already made several trips to John's for their delicious water ice. My favorite is a pineapple and cherry combo. Both flavors are perfection and just the right amount of sweet. The prices are great; it's two bucks for a small which is perfect for an every day sort of treat. I look forward to many visits as the weather heats up!

My friend and I spent much of Bastille Day at the bar at London Grill. The bartenders were friendly and in jovial moods. There were some liquor promo girls giving out free samples of product, which was cool.   Once we decided we were hungry, I ordered a burger and my friend ordered parmesan truffle fries. The burger was curiously served on an English muffin-type roll, but it was pretty tasty. The fries that came with, along with my friend's fries, were room temp and not delish. She sent hers back but I had my burger so I was okay. A new batch came out approximately one minute later and they were definitely hotter but still just so-so.   It's not often that I'm in Fairmount so I'm not sure I would go out of my way just to hit up London Grille. But if I found myself in the area, I wouldn't be opposed to stopping by, either.

Because of all the negative reviews we had read on Yelp, my friend and I almost changed our dinner plans at the last minute.  We are both really glad we decided to form our own opinions instead.  We arrived at Pearl slightly early for our 7 p.m. reservation, and the entire restaurant/bar area was empty except for one couple~ never a good sign.  The bartender made me a great martini and we were off and running.  Once seated, our server was very attentive, almost to the point of being overly so, but I guess that happens when you have a grand total of 1 table to look after.  We started off with the duck spring rolls and tuna tartar~ great choices.  I couldn't get enough of the spring rolls, which came with a spicy mustard sauce, and my friend loved the tartar.  For dinner, I ordered the crabcake entree and my friend ordered the yellowfin tuna entree, rare.  The crabcakes came standard with rice and I was told by our server that they would not substitute the bok choy instead.  Fine, whatever.  We also ordered the potato pancake side.    Dinner came out pretty soon after the appetizers were cleared, and my crabcakes were really good.  My friend felt that her tuna was on the small side, and cooked a little longer than she wanted.  The potato pancakes were nowhere in sight.  I don't know if our server forgot to put the order in or what, but they didn't come out until we were more than halfway through the meal.  They were all right but definitely not worth the extended wait.    Overall, we were happy with our meal and the service we received.  Judging from the other reviews, I'm not sure how it would have worked out had we been there on a busier night.  Either way, I wouldn't mind going back for round 2, and I definitely want to check out the upstairs club sometime on a weekend.

I returned to Prohibition Taproom for some pre-concert eats and drinks.  Happy hour was from 5 - 7 but since everyone in my group was drinking bottled beer, we did not benefit from the specials.  Still, the beer selection is very fairly priced.  The bartender was friendly and effortlessly handled the entire bar on her own, which was no small feat as mostly all of the stools were taken.    Between four of us, we had the hummus plate, deep fried green beans and onion rings.  There was more than enough food and we didn't even come close to finishing everything.  The hummus was very good, as were the green beans, which came with some sort of garlic dipping sauce.  I highly suggest investing in some Altoids if you plan to order either of these plates.  The onion rings were really thick-cut and almost a little too onion-y.  The dipping sauce seemed like a cross between ranch dressing and vinegar.  It was pretty potent and I'd probably lean towards ketchup in the future, but that's just me.    I shall return.

I purposely avoided joining City Fitness prior to their opening and immediately after because I knew there would likely be some hurdles to overcome. Judging by the early reviews, I was right in my decision. But now that they are in their third month, things seem to be flowing smoothly. I've been a member for two weeks now and I'm very happy with my decision to make the switch from my old gym to this one.   For starters, the facility is brand new. That means everything is clean, machines are new, nice locker rooms, etc. The two-story layout is interesting and the hallway downstairs is a little tight but after a few trips to the locker rooms after using the back staircase, I feel like I know where everything is located.   Everyone on the staff is super friendly. That's important. You don't want to join a gym and feel awkward. I've been greeted with friendly hellos or goodbyes every time I've gone so far. The towel service is great, and there are always plenty of fluffy hand towels available.    I purchased the highest tier membership, which includes all classes and access to the We Fit classes. This membership was only five dollars more than my previous gym, and now I'm getting access to the circuit training classes I used to seek outside of my old gym (an extra expense I'll no longer have to worry about). I took advantage of my free personal training session and liked it enough that I have signed up to train with David once a week. Since I'm currently training for Broad Street, I'll probably stick to the treadmills and my PT for the next couple months, but I look forward to trying the classes and We Fit after the run.   Bottom line, I'm really happy City Fitness finally made it to the neighborhood!

I'll admit. I was super bummed when I heard the news that Johnny Mac would be stepping down as head chef at Pub & Kitchen. He was easily my favorite chef in the city, and no matter what I ordered at P&K, I was always impressed. I wondered how things would change and if I would still think of Pub & Kitchen as my go-to spot for a great but casual dinner.   There were some big changes to the menu, most notably, the burger selection, which has been pared down to a basic burger with American cheese, shredded lettuce and thin slices of pickle. Sounds simple, but one bite and I was absolutely hooked. I spend significant amounts of time thinking about it (sad but true). I don't know what makes it so delicious, but I've practically forgotten about the Churchill I used to love. When I ordered the burger at dinner with my girlfriends, I had already raved so much that they had to try it. My one friend even asked for a second bite, and the thick-cut, perfectly crisp fries were devoured.   The rest of the menu is equally impressive. I loved a simple but flavorful pappardelle with fresh summer vegetables and thin parmesan shavings. And the brunch offerings are still awesome. I even ate rabbit (which I will not typically do) when it was crumbled over their famous breakfast poutine. Chef Eli Collins is killing it, and I'm happy that my favorite neighborhood spot is still my favorite neighborhood spot.

Like David B, my first introduction to Cucina Zapata was also at the Vendy Awards. Curried chicken over rice hooked me in while mini tacos with chicken and short rib sealed the deal. It was one of the few trucks that day that kept the line moving quickly and was also prepared for the crowds. Even when an L&I inspector jumped aboard in the beginning of the event, causing everything to grind to a halt, the food truck peeps kept their cool and business was back up and running in no time.   I'll definitely make a point to seek out Cucina Zapata for lunch in the near future!

SUPER BOWL LII CHAMPIONS!!!  Thank you to this incredible team of players and coaches for making the dreams of an entire region come true. What an amazing story of perseverance, hard work and camaraderie!   See you at the parade! #FlyEaglesFly

The awesome reviews of In Riva that are constantly in my Friends feed are what first got my attention. I knew it was only a matter of time before we took a trip down Kelly Drive. With an open Sunday afternoon ahead of us, we decided to take a ride and check out In Riva for ourselves. I made a reservation since I wasn't sure how crowded the place would be, but at 6pm it actually wasn't too crowded. Since it was super hot, we decided to sit at one of the tables inside by the bar. The restaurant is cute and has big open windows facing the river, plush a nice deck with a separate bar. We also learned that the second floor is used for private parties and fits up to 100.   There is a nice selection of wine, beer and cocktails, many with Italian leanings. I opted for a drink made with gin, aperol and prosecco and was not disappointed. To start, we had the burrata which was served with some pickled baby tomatoes, balsamic, croutons and black olive fragments. The burrata was excellent; firm on the outside but creamy on the inside. All of the supporting flavors worked in harmony. Next, we shared the seared octopus, which was served over a puree of black olives along with pieces of fried lemon rind and some pickled watermelon. Each component had strong flavors and I wasn't entirely sure if I liked the dish. It may be something that could grow on me but in all honesty I'd probably try something else before going back to it.   We ended our meal with a spicy ham pizza that was up there among my favorite pizza in Philly. I hate bringing other restaurant names into my reviews and try to avoid it, but this pizza gave my usual go-to pizzeria (hint hint) a run for its money. The crust was perfect: slightly crisp and just the right amount of char. It wasn't so chewy that it gave me a headache. The ham had the right kick of spice and it went along perfectly with the flavorful mozzarella and tomato sauce.   The next time I have a pizza craving, I may need to pull straws. This place is legit.

I've been wanting to try pierogi from Mom Mom's for ages and finally had the opportunity at this year's Bloktoberfest. A friend and I decided to share an order which was a good move since you get several pierogi.   I grew up on my grandmom's pierogi so I have my preferences as to what I look for and enjoy. Mom Mom's pierogi have come the closest to the bull's eye, even if they were slightly different than my Gram's version. I liked that the potato and cheese filling wasn't completely pureed - there was a little texture which makes a huge difference. I also liked that they were topped with sauteed onion and served with sour cream and chives. In my family we sauté our pierogi in some butter and call it a day but this was a nice twist.   Mom Mom may not be MY grandmom, but she's still throwing it down in the pierogi gauntlet.

Somehow I missed the fact that this place even existed. It's a bizarre part ice cream shop part café. I agree with Tom M that the decor is dated. It's what I'd expect a restaurant in Harrisburg to look like. To-go is the way to go at this place. For me anyway.   The dessert case was interesting. I think I saw the biggest apple pie crust ever. How they get it to rise so high I have no idea. A peanut butter pie looked absolutely delicious. But last night, it was all about the ice cream.  I tried samples of two different flavors before making my decision. I eventually settled on a waffle cone with rocky road on the bottom and birthday cake ice cream on top. The birthday cake ice cream was so sweet and delicious. Probably a little too sweet for some people, but I was loving it. By the time I reached the rocky road, it tasted bland in comparison. Art finished off the second half of my cone, having already devoured his cone with mint chocolate chip and cookie dough.   Both cones came to eight bucks, which seems like a really good price when compared to the likes of Franklin Fountain and Capogiro. It's not as good as either place, but it's still an option.

After a draining experience at the Nissan service department across the street, I decided to treat myself to a little pity party lunch for one at Nordstrom Cafe. Menus are on a table just outside, so you place and pay for your order first, then choose a table. At that point, a server picks up your receipt and everything proceeds like a normal restaurant experience. The only thing I didn't like about this set-up was that you have to know exactly what you want at the time of ordering. So if you suddenly feel like dessert, I guess you'd have to go back to the front. No big.  I ordered an iced tea and chicken Caesar salad. My server was very sweet and made sure I was all set with everything I needed. She also refilled my tea, which was great. The salad was pretty good and everything I saw at other tables looked great, too. The best part of all was that I enjoyed a relatively cheap lunch in a quiet setting which was worlds above the mall food court. I'll definitely return when I need a little shopping break.

I finally made it to The Blue Duck, and it was worth the car ride to the northeast. The restaurant is situated in a shopping center with very uniform looking signage for all of its stores. Inside, the restaurant is bright and sweetly decorated with cool lighting fixtures and pretty wall art.   It was around 2pm on a Saturday but there were still several tables full for lunch. We ordered the blue duck fries and a couple sandwiches. The fries arrived before the sandwiches - a good thing because we were super hungry. Said fries were covered in melted cheese sauce and shredded duck. Somehow, they were also still crunchy. Best fries I've had in a while.   There was quite a bit of time before our sandwiches arrived, which is fine, but this is when I started wishing we had brought some beer along. Mental note for next time! I opted for the fried chicken sandwich but requested a wheat wrap. It was delicious! The ranch dressing from the coleslaw had a slightly sweeter flavor than I was expecting but it was very tasty. The chicken was excellent. My fiancé's grilled chicken sandwich with pimento cheese and bacon was also great.   Already looking forward to my next visit, definitely with some brews in tow!

Every time I walk into the Foodery, I'm excited by the well stocked beer selection, which I am confident has been handled with care to avoid any possibility of spoiling.      Every time I walk out of the Foodery, I feel like I've been robbed in broad daylight in front of a police station.  Why did two bottles of Stillwater Ale cost almost TEN DOLLARS more at Foodery than at a competitor (ahem, Food & Friends) across town?  I get the convenience factor of the location, and the fact that Foodery started the trend, but come on.  Maybe the price gouging works on the clueless but I'll mix my six elsewhere.

There's something very cozy about La Va, and I like that in a coffee shop. Comfy chairs intermingle with standard table and chair set-ups, where people come in droves to work or study.   Lattes are served in giant mugs and the pretty barista with curly hair will even craft a design in the foam, if she's not too busy. That automatically makes her my favorite.    Weekend afternoons at La Va are a little too crowded for my liking, but weeknights are usually quiet enough to sit down and relax a bit. I expect to visit quite often once I'm in my new 'hood!

I loooooove me some Nordstrom but found this particular location to be a little less cared-for than others. Sales racks weren't very well organized and no one came up to ask if I needed help with anything, which is unusual for Nordstrom. When I helped myself to a dressing room (again, no one to be found), the open rooms had piles of clothes and the room I ended up in wasn't super clean, either (I'm talking dried spills on the tables - ick).    All that said, this location is the largest in the area and has a really great selection of clothes. The woman who rang me up was also very sweet. I am not a fan of driving out to KOP but when I am in the area for business I always make Nordstrom a stop.

Cute cafe in the Francisville/Fairmount area that provided an awesome place for me to hole up for several hours and have lunch, take a couple meetings, and get some work done. Seating is outside or downstairs, and on a Monday afternoon, I had my choice of tables as there was only one gentleman in the entire place (nice to meet you, Andre!).   My café au lait was perfect, and I love the help-yourself water station with large glasses. I was excited to see crêpes on the menu and went for the goat bacon with goat cheese, bacon, mushrooms, and tomatoes. The crêpe was good but I would have enjoyed it a lot more if the bacon inside was crunchy. My dining companion's pesto sandwich looked incredible and I had a bit of lunch envy. I'm definitely going to try a sandwich or omelet next time.   The staff was really friendly and the wifi was complimentary. Definitely adding Vineyards to my rotation of spots to get some work done, and looking forward to trying more from the menu.

I think you'd have to royally screw up water ice for it to receive less than five stars. To be completely honest, Italiano's wasn't so different than any other ice I've had. The fact that the place is located deep in the heart of South Philly and reminds me of carefree summer nights as a kid (a kid in Jersey, anyway) was a bonus.   I loved that they serve so many different flavors. I tried my hand at a makeshift Shirley Temple, with cherry ice on the bottom and ginger ale ice on top. The ginger ale ice was overpowered when mixed with the cherry but it was delicious on its own.   The somewhat passive-aggressive sign about being the originators of the gelati is pretty hilarious. I don't think my friend really cared about that as he was too busy enjoying his pineapple ice with vanilla ice cream.   I want to go on a South Philly water ice tour so it may be a few more stops at other places before I return, but I will return.

During my 2+ years working at a Center City law firm, I spent many a lunch break trying to escape from the madness at the Liberty Place shops and food court.  The stores are limited, but most are higher-end and provide enough options for those times when your heel breaks and you need a new pair of shoes or you just got paid and want something cute to wear for the weekend.    Bonus points for all the eye candy at lunch time.

After getting totally lost via crappy directions from Google, my mom and I finally arrived at Sam's for a bridal shower - a half hour late. Fortunately, the bride was even later, and we didn't ruin the surprise.   Sam's needs a major update, stat. The air smelled of old carpet and everything had kind of a sticky feel. The room we were in for the shower was decent enough, and a bartender kept soft drink pitchers filled, with plenty of glassware and ice available.   We had a choice between chicken parm and crabcakes. Chicken seemed like the safer option, which is what I ordered. To start, a round of garden salads with just about the palest iceberg I've encountered. The dressing was tasty though, and there were black olives (bonus points there). Entrees were better than expected, although not super flavorful. The crab cakes were more filler than crab, but my mom liked the veggies served alongside. My side of pasta was weak, but the tomato sauce was decent and the chicken itself was fine.   I most likely will not return to Sam's on my own volition, but I'm not super familiar with the area to know how it compares with other spots. I'd recommend using the Yelp app to find alternates if I had to offer advice to someone passing through.

Public House: A Users Guide for the Ladies  Your experience at Public House will depend solely on when you go.    If you don't mind hobnobbing with married men who pretend they are still single (think "oops, I forgot my wedding band" types), definitely hit up Friday nights.  You'll get a mix of suits who are still out from the happy hour that should have ended three hours ago, along with some younger gentlemen who look like they missed the stop for Mad River.  Expect the place to be jam packed, expect to run into at least one of the accidents you dated back in your naïve years and expect your dirty martini to be spilled all over your arm when you are bumped by one of the many drunks.  Good times.    And now a look at the brighter side.  During the week, Public House can be a decent place to grab a drink and socialize.  It's far less crowded and the service is less spread thin.  Sometimes Bryen from Mr. Greengenes plays an acoustic set on Wednesday nights, and you know you love some Third Eye Blind throwbacks mid-week.    Public House isn't a bad place, it just depends on the day you go and your tolerance level for others.

I passed by Sbraga many times while it was under construction, and I couldn't wait to check it out for myself when it opened. My excitement heightened after reading several reviews that sang big praises. I had high expectations.   From the moment our party of four arrived on Tuesday evening, the level of service we received was exceptional. The hostesses were welcoming, our water glasses were refreshed all night, and every question about the menu had a thoughtful answer.   The puffed bread, infused with truffle oil and cheddar, was massive. People have been raving over this bread but I personally prefer something a little more traditional. I'm probably in the minority here. The amuse bouche was a celery flan with lobster salad, indicating the creativeness of the menu.   To start, I went with a Caesar salad with poached egg. The salad was nice, but I definitely played it safe here and probably would have been rewarded had I branched out to try something different. Next up was the risotto, with white truffle and hen of the woods. I am not a huge fan of mushrooms but I took a chance and am so glad that I did. The risotto was incredibly rich and absolutely delicious. I also tried my boyfriend's clams with bacon, which was unbelievably incredible. The crunchy texture of whatever sort of breadcrumbs were in the sauce was just awesome. I had major food envy even though I loved my risotto.   For my third course, I ordered the meatloaf with potato puree. The potatoes were so smooth and buttery; I just wish there had been a little more of them. As for the meatloaf, I can certainly see why people like it. Its got tons of flavor and the bacon marmalade on top makes it super rich. There was a flavor going on that was a little overpowering for me, but everyone else at our table enjoyed it.   Last and definitely not least was our dessert course. Something about the mascarpone/chocolate/coffee granita jumped out at me from the menu, and when I took that first bite I was in absolute heaven. My exact words were, "I love this dessert so hard." It was sweet, crunchy, icy, a little salty and all the other things I want to taste at the end of a meal. My coffee could have been hotter but I was too busy with my granita to really care. Baby, please don't go (off the menu).    I'm looking forward to seeing how the menu changes over time but I also hope to enjoy some of the same things again. Sbraga is a definite gem in the Philadelphia dining scene.

We finally made it to Vetri, a first for both my fiancé and me (with the exception of a preview night for their fabulous upstairs renovations). Of course, the entire evening was absolutely wonderful.   I'm the kind of person who checks out a menu before I go to a restaurant, and I typically know exactly what I'm going to order. At Vetri, you are presented with a menu of possibilities and asked simply to mention anything that you definitely do not want, or even that you definitely do want. Despite my Type A tendencies, I absolutely loved sitting back and letting the kitchen run the show.   We opted for the lesser of the two wine pairings, which was still very pricey. The pairings were spot on and every wine was terrific. I was impressed. I'm sure the higher-end pairing is mind blowing.   Course after course arrived during the evening, and everything was perfectly paced. I can't recall every single thing that I ate but every course was exciting. My favorites were the pastas, and there were lots of them. Another big standout for me was the antelope. I had no idea what to expect but I was really pumped to try something new. The meat was absolutely delicious - tender and lean and super flavorful. I was pretty full by the dessert course, and I'm not a huge sweets person anyway, so I mostly focused on my dessert wine, which was great.   As for a return visit, of course, I'd absolutely love one. However, with the cost for two topping out around the neighborhood of $600, it's going to be a while (or an unexpected financial windfall!) before it will happen again. Until then, I've got my memories!

Solid standard Chinese. And they deliver. I ordered chicken and broccoli one weekend when I had the craving but didn't want to eat anything too heavy. Lots of tasty white meat (nothing scary), and lots of slightly crunchy broccoli (just the way I like it). The sauce wasn't too heavy and the rice was perfectly cooked. I also liked the wonton soup. Definitely interested in giving this place another shot sometime soon!

A large group of ladies hit Victoria's for manis and pedis a couple days before my sister's wedding (it was a Thursday at noon). My sister scheduled the appointment a week or two in advance and the staff at Victoria's was totally ready for our arrival, with plenty of employees and open stations. In fact, there was only one other young lady at the salon when we arrived, so we had the whole place to ourselves for practically the entire time we were there!  My pedicure was wonderful. I forgot how much I miss those massaging chairs - they really are awesome! My nail tech was super gentle and the entire experience was great. I felt completely relaxed when it was over. A week later, my toes still look great.   Victoria's has a huge array of polishes, including some selections from Vinylux, though I'm not sure their techs know the proper way to apply this polish. My go-to salon has been using Vinylux for a while and they never use a base coat. My tech at Victoria's applied an OPI base. My nails were still fairly chip free for days so I guess that didn't really have a negative effect, but it was an extra unnecessary step.   Overall, solid experience for a group and everyone's nails looked great.

The words "ice cream" and "water ice" usually fill me with happy thoughts, but when combined with the word "Cabana," my mood sours.  One night last summer I had a craving for vanilla custard (that's "soft serve" for those of you who don't speak South Jersey) so off to Cabana I went.  Now, I get that "soft serve" is supposed to be softer than hard ice cream.  But is it supposed to be so soft that it starts melting all over your hand as you pay?  No.  Is it then supposed to implode into a hidden ice cream cavern before falling off the cone and onto the asphalt before you even reach the car?  No.  Vowing to boycott Cabana, a full year passed before I found myself giving them another chance when out with a group of friends the other night.  Had we not been pressed for time, I would have happily driven us all to Maple Shade Custard Stand, one of my favorite places on Earth.  However, Cabana was on the way and it had been a while since the mishap so I figured, why not?  This is why not.  My friend stepped up and ordered her hot fudge sundae.  They were out of hot fudge.  At 7 p.m. on a Friday night.  Two minutes later, a guy came in requesting blue raspberry water ice.  They were out (natch), and when the guy left, one of the Bratz dolls behind the counter remarked that water ice is artificially flavored anyway so it all tastes the same.  Awesome.
