The concept is very similar to Agno in that you can build your own bowl, only the flavors are Asian as opposed to Mediterranean.   I went with the jasmine rice with scallions as my base, ginger beef for my protein, pickled red onion, shredded carrots and snap peas for my toppings, and peanut Thai basil sauce. I also added a lemon ginger turmeric water in hopes that some vitamins and minerals will help cure me of the never-ending seasonal cold I've been suffering.  I was very impressed and happy with the bowl and the flavors of all the ingredients. Often when I deviate from the house suggestions to 'create my own' I do a disastrous job of choosing items that taste delicious when put together. This time, the planets aligned and everything was just right. Definitely adding Yoku to the healthy eats rotation.

My husband and I are on a mission to support some of our favorite local businesses during this very trying time, while also finding a balance with cooking at home and keeping our diets relatively healthy. Weekends are when we've been treating ourselves to time off from cooking and cleaning, and we chose to end our weekend with a massive takeout order from IndeBlue.   We saw on social media that IndeBlue was offering 25% off for takeout orders placed directly with them over the phone. I called and spoke with the nicest employee who gave feedback on our choices and even threw in some complimentary rice pudding!   My husband swung by on his bike for the pick up, and I was very impressed by how nice everything looked when he got home. We ordered: crispy cauliflower, vegetable samosas, crispy spinach chaat (a longtime favorite!), sea bass entree, shrimp moilee, paneer tikka masala, and a double order of naan. Our intention was to have enough for at least two meals and we definitely accomplished that.   Everything was delicious, as always. I can't wait to enjoy our leftovers (and another night off from cooking and cleaning!) for dinner tonight. Definitely think of IndeBlue if you're craving really fantastic Indian food!

After a mediocre experience at another repair shop, I was on the hunt for a different shop to get my Frye bag repaired. My friend said the place on 15th & Spruce was recommended to her by a mutual friend and she said the business earned her loyalty, so off I went.   My broken-in bag needed a lot of love: some work on the strap, which constantly frayed, and a complete sew job on the clasp, which had completely torn off from the interior leather flap.   For just $25 and only a few days' time, my bag is looking great. Not brand new, that would take a miracle, but good enough that I can get through a couple more seasons before spending the dough on a new bag.

My sister and I were shopping around Collingswood and Haddonfield a few days after Christmas. Our plan was to get some lunch to-go, but when we noticed the setup at The Bistro, we amended our plans. They have a lovely outdoor seating situation with lots of heaters. Even though it was a pretty cold day, we felt completely comfortable eating outside. We lucked out with a table against the front window of the restaurant. The sun was shining right on us and there was a heater overhead. It was great!   There were breakfast and lunch menus to choose from and we both went with lunch. We each ordered chicken wraps or sandwiches and added on the French onion soup to start. The soup was really great - tons of flavor and everything you'd want from a French onion soup.  We both thought our sandwiches (the chicken caesar wrap for me, the chicken milano for little sis) were weighed down by the boursin cheese. I also thought the chicken was so-so. I'm incredibly picky about meats so I'd probably opt for something different next time. The chip fries served alongside the sandwiches were bomb!  Our server was great and came by at all the right times. Also, the meal was incredibly wallet-friendly. This was an excellent outdoor dining option, even in winter, and I'd happily return.

Three girlfriends from college and I set out for Chifa on a Thursday night.  I specifically requested a table in the back room when making my reservation on Open Table, as I wanted to experience what Monica S. described as the "Eyes Wide Shut" room.  After a short wait in the bar, we were seated in a large corner booth with a view of the kitchen (where, to my utter delight, I noticed Jose Garces hanging out and chatting it up with a chef - very cool).  The sides of the booth had some crazy chain curtains and while the lights were dim, the room was illuminated by the crimson walls.  The whole effect was rather kinky.    Our server, who could have easily been a Diesel model with her faux-hawk haircut and bad-ass tattoo snaking up her leg (fem crush alert), took our drink orders and explained the menu.  She recommended three plates per person, so we went with her advice.  We placed our order and the feast began shortly after with the delicious buns o' goodness that mostly everyone has already mentioned.  Our never-ending feeding frenzy then went a little something like this:  The Beginning ("We're hungry!"):  * Medai ceviche - This was presented with corn chips and corn nuts, which went over well, despite a few "you go first" looks shooting across the table.  * Shellfish ceviche - I personally liked the flavors of this ceviche but my friends thought it was a little bland.  More Substantial ("Tapas is fun!"):   * Empanadas (2 orders) - Stuffed with shredded crab, these were a highlight of the meal, and two orders was the perfect amount for four people. * Anticuchos - I enjoyed the shrimp and a piece of the cilantro chicken, but my friends were turned off by the (justifiably) fatty pork belly.  * Pork Belly Buns - The pork was less fatty here than in the anticuchos and the flavors were great. * Pulpo - This was a nice surprise that was brought out as a gift from the chef.  The octopus was tender and seasoned well.   * BBQ Ribs - I was slightly disappointed by these as they were not as lean as I had hoped they would be (just my personal preference, not to take away from how the ribs were served).  The flavors were delicious. * Chaufa - This was a surprisingly large portion of fried rice with scallops and was definitely in my top three favorites. * Lomo Saltado - The beef in this dish was so tender we could pull it apart with a fork.  High praise all around!  The Finale ("We are so full; please roll us out of here."):  * Chupe - This spicy bisque came loaded with seafood and, to our surprise, a poached egg (which no one really wanted anything to do with at this point in the game). * Duck wonton soup with sliced duck - I was really looking forward to this dish but there was a very strong flavor of clove or some other intense seasoning that I didn't care for. * Lobster noodles - It was a shame this dish came last although if it had come out sooner the whole thing would have been devoured in seconds.  The lobster was plentiful and the bacon somehow remained crunchy despite being smothered in an alfredo-like sauce.  Delish.  As far as I'm concerned, the service was excellent and the food was very interesting and unlike other restaurants I've been to in Philly.  Chifa's serving sizes are definitely larger than most tapas places.  I would strongly suggest trying to narrow down selections to two plates per person, as we were not able to finish many of the dishes due to an overabundance of food.  This was not my favorite Garces restaurant but a great experience nonetheless.

With a little time to kill before an event in the area, my friend and I decided to check out Wine-O.  We arrived around 6:30, which still put us in the happy hour range.  I had a glass of the house white for $3, a total steal for any bar in Philly.    The bar and restaurant area had a very cozy feel, and the bartender was extremely nice and welcoming.  This is a place I would want to come with one or two people to catch up and have a relaxing night.

After dinner at Mama Palma's, my girlfriends and I set out in search of a byo with a dessert menu.  One friend knew of this place, so we made a quick call to make sure it would be okay that we stopped in for dessert & coffee only.  The owners/staff were very welcoming and eager to please... perhaps a little too much, although it's hard to be turned off by the attention of Italian men.    We ordered three desserts to share- tiramisu, a chocolate mousse something-or-other and a cannoli.  All three were good, but the cannoli was out of this world amazing.  The shell was slightly different from others I've had; it was thicker and coated in dark chocolate.  The ricotta filling was rich, smooth and very delish.    I can't speak for the food but based on the desserts I would love to give it a try!

Who knew such a lovely park existed on the Delaware Banks in Fishtown? I certainly didn't - at least, not until I attended the Fishtown RiverCity Festival on Saturday. That festival enabled me to see more of this section of the city than ever before, thanks to the 5K fun run that kicked off the event. An awesome beer tent and loads of food vendors provided sustenance as our group of yelpers chilled in the sun, chatting and laughing it up and making new friends along the way.   The large expanse of freshly mowed grass and a clear view of the river felt far from Center City. I'm so happy every time I discover a new park within Philadelphia, and this was no exception.

You cannot go wrong with Restaurant Week lunch at Butcher & Singer. I returned once again for the three course meal during week 2 of RW, and everything from the greeting at the front door to the water glasses that were constantly being refilled was great. I enjoyed a mozzarella and tomato salad with chopped pistachios and olive tapenade followed by a cobb salad with a generious portion of juicy sliced chicken alongside.   I was somehow able to turn down the dessert course, although the spiced pear sorbet was sweetly calling my name. I can't believe I've never been for dinner but it's something I continue to look forward to!

Yards Brewing Company is one of those places I do not get to often enough. I've visited the tasting room on one or two occasions and it's always a scene. Bachelor parties and groups of friends or family seem to dominate and the result is a fun, lively environment.  The brews are great, of course, and the bartenders are fast and friendly. I'd love to swing by on a night when it's not as crowded as the weekend rush and have dinner and some suds.

Fitzwater Street Bagels is always solid, in my experience. In pre-pandemic times, I'd occasionally swing by for a turkey sandwich, customized to my liking. Nowadays, customizing gets a bit trickier through an online delivery app, so I've had to modify a bit in order to get what I want.   My go-to bagel breakfast sandwich is an everything bagel with bacon, veggie cream cheese, tomato and cucumber. This is obviously not a combo that's offered online (or anywhere, probably, because it's super random!) so over the weekend I instead ordered a BLT, hold the L, plus some extra bagels and cream cheese to have on hand. I was able to add my desired cream cheese to my BT bagel, and now I have bagels in my freezer for whenever I want one.     I've never had an issue with my order, and I love having a bagel shop in the neighborhood that's both walkable and available for delivery on a lazy Sunday morning.

Wow, nine years since my last review of Pizzeria Stella - it's time for an update! Luckily, I'm very much still picking up what Stella's putting down. I went for dinner on a drizzly night but the seating under the Headhouse Shambles kept me and my friend dry and comfortable. Our server (I forget her name but it was her first night back to work) was fantastic and so sweet!   I was a bit pizza'd out and was happy that my friend was down for ordering pastas, instead. We shared the tomato salad with burrata which was a special that evening. This super fresh and delicious salad was summer in a bowl! For entrees, my friend had the blue crab bucatini while I went with the rock shrimp paccheri. I loved my dish and ate every last bite!   Pizzeria Stella is a classic that's still going strong. I'm planning to return ASAP for more outdoor dining!

At a recent girls' night, Jessica T. became my enabler.  MY CUPCAKE ENABLER!  She brought no less than three varieties of cupcakes from FOUR different bakeries.  By far, my favorites of the bunch were from Brown Betty.  The gargantuan confections were way larger than your standard cupcakes.  The cake itself was heavy and moist, and the icing was the exact way icing should be - appropriately thick, sugary sweet and full of flavor.  Because of their size, Brown Betty's cupcakes are perfect for sharing with a friend.  I would definitely feel way too guilty eating a whole one by myself (although I'm sure I'd do a bang-up job).

My mom is a member of this location, and I've been wanting to check out Orangetheory for ages. On Sunday, I took advantage of the "first class for free" offer and my mom and I went together to get our sweat on.   The staff was very friendly and did a nice job explaining how Orangetheory works. James, the instructor, showed me and another newbie the ropes before class, and he also went over our results after class. I thought the use of heart rate monitors would be kind of distracting, but I didn't even notice the monitor when I was working out. I loved getting the personalized info from the monitor, especially the total calories burned (633, FYI).   The workout for our session was apparently a bit different than a regular class, with a series of steps. I started on the treadmill side of the gym and went between jogging on varying inclines for varying distances and rowing a corresponding number of meters. It was a challenge for sure. Halfway through the class, cardio people switched with strength training people. The second half of my class was a series of strength training exercises which worked the whole body. The lighting is dim and the music is pumping, which definitely helps for getting in the zone for this workout.   Two days later, I am still pretty sore and feel that I had a great workout. I do think if you are a highly motivated person, you could do this type of circuit on your own, but there's no denying the rush you get from great music and a positive and motivating instructor. I also love that you can go at your own pace without the worry of comparing yourself to anyone else. I currently work out with a trainer several times a week and don't see myself making a switch, but I am thinking about purchasing some type of package so I can take a class here and there.

I enjoyed a couple coffee meet ups and lunches at Bloomsday in pre-pandemic times, but didn't have my first dinner experience until last week. Their outdoor seating is under the Headhouse Shambles, making Bloomsday one of the few places in Philly where you can sit outside for an enjoyable meal even in drizzly weather.   The menu is small but there were still multiple things that caught my eye. My husband ordered the heritage farm salad to start so I snagged a few bites and it was really tasty! My beer battered fish sandwich was massive and came with a heaping pile of dill slaw and a fresh side salad. My husband had the spaghetti, shrimp and mussels and our friends had the chicken under a brick and adult happy meal. Everyone was happy with their food and I really liked the draft wine selections as well.   While I look forward to the day when things are safe enough to dine inside again (if you haven't been, Bloomsday Cafe is probably one of the prettiest restaurants in the city), I'm excited for more meals al fresco in the meantime!

I was craving Indian food and hadn't ordered from Tiffin in a while. Placed the order via Yelp (which was somehow way less expensive than placing the order directly with a delivery app!) and patiently waited the hour plus I was quoted.  Overall, my experience was solid. The food arrived hot and correct as-ordered. That said, some things were better than others. The vegetable samosas were hot and crispy - a nice start. The garlic naan was also spot on. Of the three heartier dishes we ordered, the tandoori shrimp was easily my favorite.   We also got the saag paneer and chicken tikka masala. I thought the saag paneer was nice, but also very rich. The chicken tikka masala was my least favorite. The sauce was really sweet and the chicken was rubbery.   I'd consider ordering from Tiffin again, but would likely spend a little more to order from one of my preferred spots, instead.

I've had some great experiences at the Wachovia Center.  Billy Joel, The Rolling Stones, Sixers games, Flyers games (including Ron Hextall's induction to the Flyers' Hall of Fame!) and March Madness games, to name a few.  My favorite experience of all?  Sitting two rows behind the home bench at last night's Flyers v. Ottawa game with my Mom.  The tickets were costly, but neither of us wanted to pass up an opportunity to sit so close to the action, and the chances of a blow-out were high.  Unfortunately, with Briere's groin still on the mend and Richards and Upshall still feeling weak from their recent bouts with the flu, the Senators looked more like the Sharks and the Flyers more like... well, the Senators.  As for Nitty?  I don't know what his deal was, but his impersonation of a sieve was not appreciated by the crowd.  We saw a blow-out all right; it just wasn't the one we expected.  Alas, this review isn't about the Flyers (who, despite a weak performance, still get five stars in my book); it's about the Wachovia Center.  As far as concerts go, I prefer an outdoor venue, but since we live in the northeast it's nice to have an indoor option when a big act comes to Philly in the colder months.  As a previous poster mentioned, for such a huge space the sound quality is decent.    I personally prefer to see sporting events at the Wachovia Center.  You can't beat this place for a game.  Every seat, whether close to the action, in a luxury club box or in the nosebleeds, provides a great view.  There are tons of bathrooms and concession stands throughout the complex.  The main concourse is always buzzing with excitement, and I'm sure it doesn't hurt that there are so many bar areas scattered around.  Never will you have to settle for Coors Light if you really want Bass, because the next bar area is always a short walk away.    I can't finish out a review of this place without a quick mention of the hotness that fills the building every time a Flyers game takes place--and I'm not just talking about the guys on the bench.  There must be a four to one ratio of guys to girls here on any given game night.  I'm no Vegas Vic or anything, but I like those odds!

I happy hour'd at Blue2o over the holidays with my mom and a friend. Their HH specials are solid and include dollar oysters, five dollar select apps and wines by the glass, six dollar Stoli cocktails and four dollar beers. On Fridays, bottles of wine are half-off all night. Deals!  We arrived just after 6 and the bar and lounge area was packed. It would have been great to sit in the lounge but we did score seats at the raw bar and the happy hour was honored there as well. I inquired about the oysters and was told they were a medium size, so we ordered four. They were definitely on the larger side of medium so I took one of the smaller ones and opted for the other apps. The slider duo is a great choice, but I far preferred the crab cake slider over the beef. I'd double up on the crab cakes on a future visit.   The clams casino were okay; not even close to my Gram's, but decent. The sriracha shrimp are a better bet, and they were quick to go at our table. We also received a bread basket before our apps, and I couldn't stop eating the delicious warm rolls. Carbs. My Achilles' heel.   Our server (tall guy, deep voice - can't recall his name!) was great and always arrived just when we were thinking about another drink.  I was skeptical going in to Blue2o for some reason, but I enjoyed my visit and would return again.

Seeing Carrie's recent South Moon Under review update reminded me that I had to make a long overdue update myself.  If you recall, my last trip to SMU was to pick up a Christmas gift.  While there, I spotted THE CUTEST black fitted Flyers t.  Since it was the season of giving to others, I reluctantly decided to hold off until after the holidays.  I suppose with all the hustle and bustle (and post-Christmas credit card payments), I forgot about the coveted t... until one day in March when it suddenly popped back into my mind.  After a website search, the item was nowhere to be found.  I crossed my fingers and sent an email to the customer service department, to inquire about whether the shirt still existed.  Within a few hours, I had a response from Emily, who promptly located my "Retro Sport Flyers T" in one of their stores.  She expedited the payment process and even applied a 20% off birthday coupon, which had been sitting in my purse since August.  The UPS tracking numbers were emailed to me as soon as my purchase left the warehouse, and I had my brand spanking new shirt soon after.

We swung by Brauhaus on a whim after watching the Flyers kick some Buffalo butt on Thursday. Little did we know, we'd be joining in on the Karneval celebration.   Bags of hot, sugary fastnachts made their way around the table and paired surprisingly well with my Erdinger. A shared plate of chicken jägerschnitzel with sides of potatoes and potato pancakes (again, we were several beers deep at this point - double potatoes were necessary) plus an order of delicious sauerkraut balls and I was in heaven. German heaven.  I've decided that Brauhaus is well deserving of the full five stars. They're the place for great German beer and food in this city. And I am pretty stoked for their upcoming expansion as well.

I've been to this LeBus location twice for lunches in the past month and I thoroughly enjoy it! Parking is usually not too hard to find during the week, but remember to bring quarters for those stupid, outdated meters! It's not always easy to find a business that will make change, either. (Parking situation has nothing to do with my rating for this restaurant, by the way, this is just a public service announcement for anyone who drives!)  The restaurant is quite large and I've had no problems getting a table, even during busy hours. On both visits I had the Blue Colorado salad which comes with some absolutely delicious glazed chicken, tomatoes, asparagus and corn. I always add avocado because avocado. There are two different types of iced tea: a regular and another version which I believe rotates. I've had the raspberry tea twice and it was great.   Solid spot in Manayunk!

I've taken two classes at this location and really like the studio. There are fewer stations than my home studio (UCity) but the layout is great, offering plenty of space between stations. Speaking of space, I love the layout of the lockers which gives ample room for everyone to get to their stuff without having to be right on top of each other. Bathrooms are clean and well-stocked with necessities. The front desk staff have been very friendly and welcoming.   My recent class with Anna was awesome. I loved her style of coaching which was clear and positive. Sometimes I have a hard time hearing the instructions over the music but that wasn't the case here at all. Anna was extremely encouraging, calling people out by name and cheering us on along the way. Also, the playlist was just right.   I don't get to this studio too often since it's out of the way for me, but I look forward to my next visit nonetheless!

Lucien's Manor could also be called "Lucien's Wedding Factory" or "Lucien's Taj Mahal of Weddings," because receptions are pumped out from all angles.  Friends and I walked into the lobby and were faced with a woman wearing an earpiece and holding a walkie talkie.  We were instructed to use a set of stairs on the left and turn left once we reached the top.  When attending a reception at a place like this, there is always a moment of panic before walking into a hall that you might accidentally walk in on some other newly married couple's first dance or something.  Luckily, our directions were solid and we saw familiar faces right away.  Whew!  We made our way to the bar and the 'tenders seemed harried.  Despite its availability, I noticed that the Grey Goose was kept hidden from plain view, unless it was specifically requested.  Tsk, tsk!  The pours were weak and martinis were in no danger of spilling as they only filled about half the glass.  I also heard a couple people lamenting over the no shots policy.  Regardless, people did not seem to have problems getting socially lubricated enough to bust some moves on the dance floor.    I liked the room we were in because it offered some privacy from the other weddings taking place.  It was cozy, with a fireplace in the corner behind the newlywed table.  There were adjoining bathrooms, which kept us completely secluded from the other partygoers in the building.  Dinner was above average as far as wedding fare goes.  Italian wedding soup, Caesar salad and a choice of stuffed shrimp or filet made for a filling and flavorful meal.  As others have mentioned, servers walk around with trays to offer extras.  Later in the evening, a huge dessert table was unveiled, along with a flambé station and gourmet coffee station.  The attendant probably thought he was doing me a favor by pouring about three ounces of Jameson into my Irish coffee, but unfortunately I had to abort mission after a sip or two so that I would be sober enough to drive home.    All in all, the wedding was lovely and the staff at Lucien's did a nice job keeping the night flowing and guests happy.

I can't believe I haven't reviewed Greene Street! I've been consigning my clothing, bags and accessories with them for years and have always been pretty happy with my experiences. Their employees are very friendly and the location on South Street always looks nice.   Greene Street has changed their consignment model a couple times over the years. Recently, they've reverted to their former model which is when they email a contract within a couple weeks of the drop-off. The contract lists each item they plan to re-sell and the price. After the consignment window (45 days, reduced from the previous 60), you receive a payment for any items that were sold, minus a $4.99 handling fee. The payment is a percentage of the sale price, which fluctuates depending on the value of the item. Anything they don't want to put on the floor and anything that doesn't sell in that 45 day window can be donated, unless you want to pay a fee to pick up the unsold items.   It sounds complicated but really, it's a great service. I don't like holding onto things I don't need or no longer wear so this gives me an opportunity to clean out my closet a couple times a year while making a few bucks in the process (for me, typically anywhere from $50 to occasionally $100+ for each haul). I also love that they simply donate items that they decide not to sell. Wins all around!

Really enjoyed my experience at Cinder on Saturday night! My party of two was seated at a high top table towards the rear of the bar. I was happy with this because there was a crowd towards the front of the bar and it was extremely loud. It doesn't seem like there is any soundproofing built in, but that would be really helpful since it seems like they are going for a bar/restaurant vibe and not just a bar scene.  We started with the Juniper Looks Bright cocktail, featuring Manatawny Still Works barrel aged gin. It was boozy and smooth.   I had heard that pizzas are what Cinder does best, so we decided to skip the apps and order two pizzas to share. The sausage and peppers pizza had a really delicious marinara, and the pancetta pizza featured a white sauce and loads of thick and crispy pancetta. If you're feeling pretty hungry like we were, two pizzas are perfect for sharing between two people. I opted for the pinot noir to go with my 'za, and I liked it a lot. The rosé that is currently on their menu is fairly dry and also went really well with the pizza.   Our server was very sweet and always right on top of filling waters and taking new drink orders. I also love that they accept reservations. Great experience and I'd definitely return!

Just popping in a little update to say: Oishii Poké is officially my favorite poke spot in Philly. This year, poké has become one of our go-to, healthy-enough takeout meals. We've tried and re-tried a handful of different spots around Philly, but Oishii tops them all. The bowls are always loaded and packed very nicely, and the ingredients are super fresh and flavorful. Last but definitely not least, our orders are accurate every time. Looking forward to continuing to support this great local biz this winter!

El Merkury has been back on my radar since the pandemic hit; I knew I was way overdue to give them another chance. Also, they are one of several woman-owned businesses that have been stepping up to the plate to feed local healthcare workers and hospital staff. In a time where all small businesses are struggling, that says a lot.   My husband and I were out for a bike ride last weekend and wanted to grab a healthy lunch. I suggested El Merkury since we had been talking about ordering from there and I knew they had some fresh salads. We each picked a salad and also shared an order of cheese and bean pupusas. I topped my salad with shredded chicken which was a smart choice; otherwise, I think the salad would have been too plain. I really liked the taste of the mustard dressing, however.   I think where El Merkury really shines (and where I missed the boat the first time) is with their street food options, which is the majority of the menu. Though I only had a single pupusa, it was delicious and left me wanting more. In addition to their regular takeout menu, El Merkury is offering family meal options as well. Think pupusas and taquitos by the dozen, proteins by the pound and sides by the quart. This would be so great for a family or even just to have a couple meals spread out through the week. I am definitely looking forward to putting a larger order together in the coming weeks with this option. I'll also have to try some of their famous churros, once I do!

My sister and I popped in to Flying Pig Saloon on a Friday night when we happened to be in Malvern. The place was totally packed but we were able to score the last available two top table. There didn't seem to be more than a couple servers but there were also a couple bussers running around.   That said, service was still on the slow side, and our orders were inaccurate so we had to keep asking for things which was annoying for us and our server.   We had a round of Moscow Mules which were served in copper mugs, but without lime. My sister ordered a taco salad which was on special, but it didn't come with dressing, which we had to request. I had a buffalo chicken wrap with fries. It was delicious, but served with the dressing in the wrap, which I would have preferred on the side, as requested. We also had to ask for silverware and napkins after receiving our food.   Would I go back? Probably, if I'm ever in the area again. Maybe I'd choose to sit at the bar or at a pub table near the bar, if the option was available.

I returned to SPTR after a long hiatus for Memorial Day brunch. Or lunch. We saw a tweet by the restaurant linking to the brunch menu, but when we arrived it was the regular menu plus a small handful of brunch specials. I was disappointed because I had been looking forward to the brunch burger, but I ended up going with the regular menu burger instead, with salad instead of fries.   The burger was okay; not super juicy and probably a bit more on the med-well side than medium. I had a couple bites of the fried clams which were awesome and the perfect summer menu item. Service was solid.   Going back to four stars for SPTR but it's still a reliable neighborhood spot.

There's really something to be said about the hospitality you receive at any given establishment. A little kindness goes a long way and, in this case, has pushed a four star review update to five. Charlie and Heather at The Institute are masters at making people feel comfortable and accommodating special events.   Last night, several yelpers and friends gathered for the inaugural meeting of the Yelp Film Club. The second floor was opened up specifically for the screening, and an Ithaca Brewing Co. promotion was held simultaneously, boasting $3.50 pints. THREE DOLLAR AND FIFTY CENT PINTS! This may very well have been one of my cheaper nights out in the past month, and I ate dinner.   Speaking of dinner, the new menu had me eeny-meeny-miny-moing between at least five items. I eventually settled on the pork tacos, which were delicious and very generously portioned for a mere $7. My only gripe is that they were a tad greasy, and I had to place a napkin on the plate to sop up the juices so they wouldn't run onto the other taco shells. It was a small miracle that I kept my white sweater spotless, but I wasn't about to miss my mouth with the delicious tortilla vehicles of shredded pork and mango salsa goodness.   Later in the night, I took a bite of Blake F's pumpkin mac and simply could not stop myself - it was probably the best mac and cheese I've ever tasted in my life. I had her side of fries transferred to my check to (hopefully) make up for some of the damage.   My only regret is that I waited so long to get back to The Institute. I'm very much looking forward to hanging out there again soon!

My beau and I swung by Fish on Thursday night on a whim, and it turned out to be a very fortuitous decision. We were seated at a comfy two top against the window. A note to the ladies: the window is drafty; dress accordingly.   The meal started off with a nice, crunchy roll and some butter scented with nori. The butter was deliciously briny - the perfect prelude to a seafood meal. Our starters were the hiramasa crudo and the king crab. Both were nice, light introductions to the menu. A course of the Maine shrimp with hazelnuts, gnudi and orange was a lovely surprise from the kitchen. It was absolutely delicious and definitely something I'd order in the future.   My entree was the skate wing with spaetzle, parmesan broth and melted leeks. Flakes of black truffle decorated the fish, which was perfectly cooked and easily one of the best skate dishes I've had. The spaetzle had a delicious taste and awesomely crunchy (in all the right places) texture. My boyfriend was also very happy with his pastrami-crusted mahi mahi.   Desserts by Monica Glass are not to be missed. We settled on the bombolini, which was a set of sugar-dusted doughnuts with dulce de leche sauce and crumbled pistachios. A gingery grapefruit sorbet was served alongside. At the end of the meal, mini green tea macaroons were a delightful little treat. It should also be mentioned that our server was excellent, staying on top of drink refills and anything else we needed.   I love this new incarnation of Fish and look forward to returning.

I was pleasantly surprised by my brunch experience at The Strip Joint. Cheeky name for a steak restaurant, by the way. I like it. That said, I really hate that they took it a step further and labeled the menu with sections called "something wet" and "happy endings" - ick.   Now that I got that out of the way; four dollar bloody marys and mimosas! That's pretty sweet. For a deal like that I didn't bat an eye at my $16 brunch selection, which ended up being totally worth the price tag. The crab cake benedict is served over a risotto cake and has a large serving of breakfast potatoes. The sriracha hollandaise, which I requested on the side, was absolutely delish. My fiancé didn't seem blown away by his peppers and eggs sandwich, but the bacon on the side was pretty great. It was thick cut and perfectly cooked.   Our server was nice and helpful. The bloody marys were very tasty. I'd go back for brunch again sometime.

Wow, the AMC Marlton has changed since my last visit, eons ago! I love the reserve ahead system, the comfy chairs with plenty of cup holders, the space between rows (and your neighbor), the wide aisles!   My only two gripes, and I know one of them isn't changing: the inability to use gift passes online, and refreshments prices. I had four movie pass tickets and went to book my seats online, only to find out that I had to go in-person to redeem. Come on, AMC! Give those passes a code, update your online reservations system, and we can all avoid the unnecessary advance visit to the theater.   A small popcorn and small soda costs $11 and change?! SMH, indeed!

A very hectic day came to a slow and peaceful halt the moment I walked through Biba's doors on Saturday evening. We went with the intention of learning something during Drink. Think. but ended up staying for dinner and several more glasses of delicious red wines.   The place is darkly outfitted but has a huge window which allows for both natural light and people watching. We chose to sit at the bar, complete with always-necessary hooks for coats, purses and, on that night, umbrellas.   We learned about Old World and New World Syrah, and we paired our tasting with a crunchy cheddar, smoky speck with the most delicious honey mustard and roasted garlic scented olives. This was just enough to whet our appetite for heartier bites of a vinaigrette-dressed salad with figs, blue cheese and hazelnuts, as well as a smoked chicken panino which was super tasty but not too heavy.   As always with any Tria establishment, we ended up spending more dough than we intended, but the fact that I was able to exchange some stress for sanity was well worth the price. I look forward to my next visit!

My friend treated me to a spa day a few weeks before my wedding (I have amazing friends). We had a package that included a facial and massage. My massage was with Kim, and it was wonderful. She guaranteed that I would fall asleep by the time she was done, and I thought there was no way because I was pretty wound up with so much going on in my head. Despite this, Kim had to wake me out of a gentle sleep as she finished!   My facial was nice and I really enjoyed chatting with my facialist, who was hilarious. I do have to admit that I didn't really care for the scent of the products that were used.   I have a go-to salon in the burbs that I really love already, so it's not too likely that I'll switch. But I did really enjoy my spa day here and would recommend it to anyone looking for some relaxation in the city.

Capogiro's locations are some of my favorite places to grab a cup of coffee and get some work done. The music is always great and the employees are always pleasant. And the wifi passwords are always hilarious. Today's password was: grapefruitcampari. That made me happy.  I don't know how I turn off my attraction to their gelato on the days that I visit solely for work, but I do. Knowing I'll get a delicious latte out of the trip definitely helps. And if I ever did want a treat, there are loads of confections on the counter... and about a million flavors of said gelato.

I ordered a buffalo chicken cheesesteak and a soda from Talk of the Town for lunch today via GrubHub. The delivery was quoted at about an hour, which was accurate. The sandwich was actually pretty good, if a bit small for more than eight bucks. It was the right amount of food for lunch, just on the expensive side.   The soda arrived in a to-go cup with a lid. I thought that was kind of strange since I was expecting a can. Then I noticed that the cup itself reeked of cigarette smoke. As did the napkins and the bag that contained my sandwich. Gross. There are few things I find more offensive than a big whiff of cigarette smoke, and the last thing I want is for my lunch to be permeated with the stuff. Needless to say, I won't be ordering takeout from Talk of the Town again, though I wouldn't rule out a visit to the actual storefront.

Big fan of Rizzieri's new location in the Moorestown Mall, which is super close to my parents' house and therefore, very convenient. I booked a facial with Christina, who is the only person I have ever gone to for a facial at Rizzieri. As usual, my service was five stars and I left feeling fresh and relaxed.   The facility is a little odd with regards to the set-up. The space for the beauty salon is enormous (and so loud when several hair dryers are going at once - some sound absorbing panels would be really helpful), while the spa areas are small and even a bit cramped with regards to the lounge and locker rooms. The locker area is super tiny - more than two women would not fit comfortably in the tight space. And the lockers themselves are very small. A winter coat, purse and clothing could barely fit, and only when the coat was folded over and shoved in.   Alas, I don't go to a spa for the locker rooms so the above comments are just little pet peeves that won't deter me from Rizzieri. I just wish they dedicated a little more room to the spa since there is an abundance of it in the salon.

My experience at Schlafly over the weekend was a little strange, to be honest. I sat down and ordered a club soda and some fish tacos. The tacos were brought over in less than five minutes which was a little suspect, but I was truly hungry and took my chances. They were actually edible and I was happy to have a somewhat healthy meal before flying home.   I asked for the check and my server offered to give me a refill of my club soda in a to-go cup, which was very nice. My bill came to nineteen dollars and some change; I put thirty on the table. My server came by and picked up the check and cash, said she appreciated me, and was off. I started to realize after a few minutes that she wasn't coming back. I don't mean to sound cheap, but I wasn't about to leave a fifty percent tip, either! I basically had to hunt down said server by the kitchen to ask for some change. It was awkward! Next time, I'm eating before I get to the airport.

I was somehow given the unofficial charge of organizing an after party to the Supper elite event.  After polling most of the remaining yelpers, the votes between Varga Bar and Mom's were pretty much split down the middle and we seemed to be in a deadlock.  As my immediate crew walked down the steps from the lovely private room, through the main floor and out the double doors at the entryway, it hit me: why go anywhere else?  Luckily, a few other people were in agreement and our small group retreated and took over the bar.  Kyle, our charming bartender, made my friend a chocolate martini with an elixir that brought me right back to the chocolate factory ride at Hershey by smell alone.  I opted for a vodka martini, to go with the small plates we ordered: warm pretzel bites with a cheesy dip, lightly fried squid in a creamy sauce flavored by thin strips of raw peppers and onions, a grilled flatbread with clams and a small cheese board.  While I found each item to be interesting, the cheese board was the most satisfying for me.  I can't remember the exact selections but they were all wonderful.    I am very much looking forward to enjoying a relaxing dinner at Supper in the near future.

I can now state confidently for the record that I am an Orangetheory fangirl. Since my first review, I was gifted a four pack of classes and then purchased a 10-pack on my own. I go once every week or two and love how the class complements my other workouts.   Classes are always challenging and every class is different. Some days there is a lot of rowing, other days there are incline runs, sometimes it's two long blocks of cardio and strength, while other days bring more back and forth between the two.   I love Wendy's classes but I took Raymond's class for the first time last week and really loved it. His instruction was so clear and his playlist was on point! He announced to the class that the Moorestown and Cherry Hill locations would be merging, which means a bigger variety of instructors, which I enjoy. Everyone runs the class differently so it's fun to mix things up.   The front desk staff is always so friendly and helpful; this location truly feels like a community, even though I only get there every so often. For me, it's worth crossing the bridge for a workout that will kick my butt and get my endorphins pumping!

Tiffin is not my favorite Indian, but it is far less expensive than my favorite, so it wins out when it comes to delivery.   After reviewing a previous order, I again ordered the chili chicken and garlic naan, plus chicken tikka masala and onion bhaji, a new-to-me app.   The chili chicken was completely different from what I remembered, and my fiancé and I were not fans and will not order it again. I actually loved the onion bhaji for an inexpensive and slightly guilty app (they are fried) and the chicken tikka masala was very good but contained only 7-8 pieces of chicken. For the price, it's still a good deal and I'll likely choose Tiffin next time I'm craving Indian food at home.

I'm not very good with change so I was pretty sad when I heard Kanella on Spruce was closing up shop to move to a bigger space with a bar. Despite the fact that Kanella South is no longer the cozy BYO I loved, I think I can get on board with Kanella 2.0.   The bar is in a separate room entirely from the dining room. The space is dark and sexy - the perfect spot to have a quiet dinner alone or a drink and light bite with a date. The cocktail list is inventive, and there is a nice selection of wine as well.   The dining room is more of an open space and has a clean, modern look. Three of us were seated in a booth that felt a little bit tight to me, with various layers of jackets and bags. I'm not sure if they have a coat check but I'll definitely ask next time when I undoubtedly have an even bulkier winter coat.   I was happy to see many of my favorite items still on the menu: trio of dips, octopus with white beans, village salad, saganaki, etc. All of them were just as delicious as always, and filling, too. We opted to share two of the entrees: kofta kebabs with bulgur wheat pilaf and pork shoulder with veggies. I loved all of the vegetables that came with the pork shoulder, and though I'm not a huge fan of lamb, I thought the kofta kebabs were delicious.   We were all in the mood for something sweet and my chocolate tart with caramel ice cream hit the spot! It was very rich - the kind of dessert where I could be satisfied after a few bites.   For a rainy Wednesday night, the restaurant was nearly full. Happy to see Kanella getting the love and looking forward to my next visit!

My stepdad has long drilled it into my head that jury duty is a civic responsibility, and I have to say I agree with him. As much as I still dread to see the jury duty slip come through the mail slot, I accept the call to action.   Maybe it's my easygoing attitude that keeps landing me in the jury box! I just completed my second stint as a juror on a criminal case (first time in Philly - the other case was when I was a NJ resident). I have to say, I found the whole thing fascinating, if a bit time consuming.   There are inconveniences involved for sure. The expense of getting to and from, not to mention lunches out each day. But probably the worst is giving up your cell phone the moment you get into the court room. They take this so seriously, even though they send you home with all the Internet access in the world each night. I don't understand it and I suspect it has more to do with not trusting people to have their phone on airplane mode or off in the courtroom, than it does with having Internet access.   Pro-tips for potential jurors: serving on jury duty even for just a day will get you discounts at nearby restaurants and some Reading Terminal Market vendors. Be sure to ask about the discount! Also, you can bring coffee or other beverages into the building, but not in glass or aluminum containers. We had a laid-back judge who also allowed us to bring beverages into the courtroom. Trust me, you're gonna need a steady infusion of coffee if you get selected.   Overall, my experience was interesting and fairly pleasant, but I'm off the hook for the next three years and not sad about it. I'm sure I'll be back at some point, hopefully in the distant future.

My friend and I found ourselves here on Sunday night in hopes that we could get seated.  As luck would have it, there were two seats available at the chef's counter.  Since neither of us was starving, we ordered 4 plates to share~ a serrano ham and fig salad, two different flatbreads and parmesan artichokes.  Everything was really nicely presented and full of flavor.  Our server was very attentive and pleasant.       The seasonal peach sangria was delicious and probably one of the best I've had.  Our only gripe was that it was SO HOT in the restaurant.  And not just where we were seated, but everywhere.  We suspected the managers were probably trying to conjure the actual temperature of Spain to provide the full experience.  As we watched the desserts being prepared in front of us, the ice cream scooped on top started melting instantly.  I felt kind of sad for the people who had ordered them.  Overall, I'd love to try Amada again, but probably not until summer is over.  I loathe melty ice cream!

It had been years since my last visit to the Electric Factory - er, Franklin Music Hall. It's hard to distinguish between the two because, aside from the name change, I didn't notice many big differences. But again, my last visit was likely 10+ years ago!   Last night I found myself in line with a sea of people for the Rüfüs du Sol show. The line snaked out of the building, through the parking lot and all the way out to the sidewalk. A parking lot attendant kept yelling at people to keep the line away from the lot entrance, but the only alternative was the street/wrapping the line in a really unorganized way which is what happened. I think Franklin could do a much better job organizing this line.   Once inside, I grabbed a $4 bottle of water and made may way pretty easily towards the stage on the left hand side of the room. It did get a lot more crowded just before the main act took the stage but, overall, the (young) crowd was really respectful about space which was refreshing!   For this particular show, the musicians were all on risers/platforms which gave everyone a clear view. I thought the sound was really good, and the lighting was spectacular. These things may have more to do with a given act than the venue itself but I was really impressed with the show.   Once it ended, we quickly exited out a side door into the parking lot, which was easy peasy. I never used the restroom or bought other concessions so have no comments there. I do think the a/c could have been better as it got pretty hot a couple times. Overall, a good experience!

I had my first and definitely not my last experience at Crème Brûlée bistro a couple weeks ago. I had no idea the place existed until a friend posted some delicious looking photos on his instagram account. I made it my mission to try the french onion soup as soon as possible.   Sadly, the soup was sold out on the day of my visit! L'horreur! Instead, I opted for a tomato, mozzarella and pesto baguette (hold the truffle oil) with a side salad. It was very satisfying but I still have my soup craving and will need to return sooner than later to satisfy it! Also looking forward to trying some of their beautiful pastries.

I went to Le Viet for dinner with a group of seven. I had been interested in trying this place for a while but never got around to it, so was excited to finally try it. Service started out okay - drinks arrived quickly and our orders were taken. We received one of the appetizers very fast... but then the other apps we ordered didn't come out. Another server came over to ask if we had ever gotten the remaining apps and she made sure we received them.   I think the delay in apps also caused a delay in entrees. I kept seeing other tables receive their food super quickly but it seemed like our table in the corner was forgotten. When dishes did come out, they were extremely staggered. I got my dish first and it sat in front of me for at least five minutes before anyone else got their entrees.   My dish was fried shrimp in a ginger sauce with a side of rice. It was pretty tasty though I wish it had more vegetables involved aside from just onions. Everyone else seemed happy with their entree choices, which were mostly noodle dishes.   I liked Le Viet but the service left a lot to be desired. It makes for an inexpensive night out so I'd give it another shot sometime, maybe with a smaller group.

I had a pretty solid first experience at Poké-Man. I popped in on a Friday evening and placed an order for two poké bowls. One of the employees helped me out with the menu and some questions I had. I decided to get a bubble tea at the last minute and asked for the black tea but made less sweet. The end result was a delicious bubble tea made exactly to my request.   At home, the bowls were also as-requested. I thought some of the toppings were a little skimpy but, overall, still a pretty packed bowl that kept me full for the rest of the night. I'm looking forward to more visits and am happy they use frequent customer cards as well!

I've had the Cherry Hill Sammy Chon's bookmarked on Yelp for ages. So long in fact, that they've since put an express location in my hometown, along with a full-sized restaurant in Chinatown, which we checked out last night.  I dropped the ball and forgot our beer at home, so we had to ask where to get some in the area. A six pack of Tsingtao from David's later, we were back at Sammy's and seated at a two top in the center of the restaurant. A baby cried nearby. This is going to be a family friendly kind of spot.   For the duration of our meal, service was great and very sweet. We started with Korean fried chicken, spicy style. I'd never had this oft-talked about dish before, and when it was set before us I told my boyfriend he might need to order his own. There were four wings, each with the most crunchy coating and smothered in sticky, sweet and spicy sauce. This could become dangerous.   I had just finished the last bites when my spicy pork bibimbap dolsot arrived, snapping and crackling in a hot stone bowl. I tossed the sunnyside egg towards the side to cook a little longer and got to work on mixing up the rice to get maximum crunchiness. It should be noted that brown rice is an option, but when I asked whether it gets just as crunchy, our server kind of smiled and said it doesn't even come close. That was all I needed to hear. White rice it was.   The food was so hot that even on my last few bites, I still managed to burn my mouth a bit. I'm not complaining - I like food hot and I'm used to scalding my mouth several times a week from my own impatience. The flavors were great. The pork was a little fatty but I was able to find some leaner pieces. The egg yolk definitely added something to the mixture as well.   Super excited for some great Korean in the city. It won't be long before my next visit, and I can't wait to check out the Cinnaminson spot soon.

Upon hearing that some of our go-to South Philly Christmas tree locations were not operating this year, my husband got to work on finding a new spot. Not only was picking out our tree at Giordano fast and easy, we also spent less than any other year in recent memory.   I pulled up curbside on Washington Ave and nervously turned on my flashers. Yep, I was that girl, but thankfully didn't get any angry honks. Within five minutes, we selected a great-looking tree with a pleasant bluish hue (a blue spruce, I'm told). We paid just $45 plus a nice tip for the young guy who eagerly helped us out. Our tree was loaded onto the car and we were off.   The tree is absorbing water quickly and it smells fantastic. The needles are definitely sharper than other trees we've had in the past, but I don't plan on bumping into it too often! Great experience and we'll definitely consider them again next year!

Mid City took care of my whip, and they did so honestly and at a reasonable price.   The back-story: About a month ago, I took my car to the dealership for an oil change. I suppose I was setting myself up there - that oil change cost me over two hundred dollars when I was pressured to purchase a new battery that day. Worse, I was told that my front wheels were unsafe and needed replacing immediately, along with a laundry list of other things that would have surely cost me well into the high hundreds, at least. When I told the guy I couldn't afford the $350 he quoted me, he was suddenly able to drop down to $250. I told him I'd be in touch.   And then I took my car to Mid City.   My tires ended up costing something like $280, including tax. I know it would have cost me the same at the dealership after that second quote, but now I know that Mid City will give me the fair price first, without question. I appreciate that.   When I went to pick up my car, I described the other problems to Mike, and I agreed to bring my car back so they could take a look. A few minutes later, Ernie, Mike's father and the owner, told me that he'd like to take a look himself, so he can let me know what needs to be updated and how soon, what can wait a bit longer, etc.   I feel like I can trust these guys, and by the looks of the other reviews, many of my peers feel the same. No more dealership drama for this girl.

A South Jersey gem! Donkey's Place makes a killer cheesesteak that's slightly different from your typical sub shop steak. They use a round, poppy seed roll, and they stack that roll with layers of meat, American cheese and perfectly fried onions. It is a heavy sandwich. And it is delicious.   Call me crazy, but I think the sandwich is even better if you let it marinate for a little while before diving right in. It also tastes great reheated in an air fryer. No matter how you like your cheesesteaks, Donkey's makes a great one!

Nomad Roman is my preferred Nomad location. Although I do think the Nomad just off of South Street is nicer, decor-wise, Nomad Roman on Locust Street has two things going for it that the other doesn't: less children and better pizza. Of course, pizza style is definitely a matter of preference. For me, the super thin and slightly charred crust at Nomad Roman is worlds better than the slightly thicker and much more chewy crust at Nomad.   The salad with mixed greens, pears, dried cranberries, blue cheese and pecans is a perfect start to a meal. Meatballs with broccoli rabe and a dusting of parmesan are also really great. You can't go wrong in the pizza department but the Trenton pie is pretty close to perfect. It's also just five bucks at their amazing happy hour, which also features five dollar glasses of house red and white.

My first experience at Via Locusta was very good, and I'm looking forward to returning so I can try even more of the menu. My dining companion and I were on a little bit of a time crunch because we had theatre tickets, so we let our server (Richard) know up front and he did a great job pacing our meal and making sure we had plenty of time to get to the show.   My friend and I were both looking for something non-alcoholic, but there weren't any options on the menu. We took our server's suggestion to leave it up to the bartender, which resulted in two okay tasting sweet drinks. I'd much rather choose something for myself from a list to satisfy my own tastes.   For food, we started with snapper crudo and romanesco fritto. Both were great. The crudo was fresh and bright while the romenesco had a great kick of heat.   For our mains, we shared four pasta dishes which, in hindsight, could have (and probably should have) been knocked down to three simply because they were so filling. We had: quadretti ravioli, agnolotti, fusilli and garganelli. All of these were delicious and only made me want to return sooner to try the others that we left out.   We sadly did not have time for dessert but I've seen photos of the chocolate tart which I would really like to try. That said, we still received a couple hazelnut and chocolate cookies to end on a sweet note. Looking forward to getting back to Via Locusta sooner than later!

Mummies, Roman statues, the third largest sphinx in the world: The Museum of Archaeology and Anthropology is fantastic!    I loved this museum when I first toured it almost ten years ago for a business event, and I loved it just as much on my second visit during Fair Food Philly's Brewer's Plate event. Exploring ancient history with a beer in hand is definitely an awesome experience.   The architecture of the building (especially the rotunda) is breathtaking and the grounds are lovely. This is a great museum and should not be overlooked by visitors or long-time residents.

We ordered poke bowls for delivery from Red Poke last night for the first time. The ordering platform we used (Uber Eats) required a selection of two proteins. I would have preferred to stick with just one but went with the big eye tuna and yellowtail.   The bowl was large and the ingredients were fresh, but every so often something in the bowl had a mild chemically taste. I couldn't tell if it was the cucumbers or the onion crisps but I narrowed it down to those two things, which I'd probably avoid in the future. The cucumbers were sliced a little too thick for my liking, anyway. I'd just try other toppings next time.   This wasn't my favorite poke spot but I'd be open to trying again in the future.
Grounds in my cuppa, with increasing frequency? No thank you, Grooveground.  Surprise! "Regular" had cinnamon undertones. Morning just got worse.

My experience at Salon Soha yesterday was so not five-star worthy. And it had nothing to do with my services, but rather, customer service.  I started seeing Thom last July, and after one pedi with him, I knew he was the one... for helping me with my girly upkeep, that is. From manis and pedis to facials and eyebrow waxing - the man does it all and does it well. So, despite my move to Philly, I've continued to book appointments at Salon Soha and have happily traveled out of my way for Thom's care.   When I arrived for my 12pm appointment on the Friday before Easter, I was told that Thom had called out sick and I would be seeing Sherrie instead. A call with this information beforehand would have been helpful, as I had booked the more expensive pedi with the knowledge that Thom would be performing my services. In all honestly, I most likely would have rescheduled if given the opportunity. But by this point, I was already there so I agreed to wait "15 minutes" since they were running behind, and I downgraded to the express pedi since I was seeing someone new.   One hour after my appointment time, I was still seated in the waiting area, no doubt looking somewhat peeved. The thought of getting up and leaving occurred to me several times over that hour, but I was not about to waste my time and be pedi-less. Finally, I was taken over to the station, where I proceeded to soak for about 15 minutes before - finally - it was my turn.   Sherrie did a great job, was fun to talk to and put me in much better spirits by the time she finished her last stroke of "Guy Meets Gal-veston." I don't hold her accountable at all for what happened. But that doesn't change the fact that I should have received a call.

I feel kind of bad writing this review, since I belonged to this gym for a number of years, but a little constructive criticism is exactly what this place needs.  Before I get into any of that, I just want to state the positive~ I have always felt very comfortable going here, and for a small gym, there didn't seem to be anything missing with respect to cardio and resistance machines.  The price is right and fresh towels are provided, which is a great feature.  Also, I love the look of the gym~ tons of brick and wood with exposed ceilings.  They had the industrial look going before every other place had it too.  Over the past year or so, there have definitely been some regressions.  At least one or two treadmills are out of order at any given time, and of the ones that do work, some of the buttons do not--specifically, the one that slows the belt ("Jane, stop this crazy thing!")!  Also, about half the time, one of the treadmills is occupied by the person who is supposed to be working the desk, and not just when the gym is empty.  On numerous occasions, there were people waiting for a treadmill while one or two sat out of order and another was taken up by a gym employee.  Are you kidding me?  One of the resistance machines has a rope attachment that has been worn down to its last few threads for quite some time, one or two of the TVs have been broken for months, etc.      These things could all be easily taken care of and should be.  It's understandable that not everything is going to be perfect all the time, but after a few of these things started adding up with seemingly no change, I reluctantly decided to move on.  In the past, I would have given this gym four stars, but now I can't see giving it more than two with all things considered.

My mom and I set out for Q BBQ & Tequila on a rainy weeknight, ready to indulge in some southern style cooking.  Although I had never been to the restaurant in its prior life, I loved that the large Philadelphia Fish & Company sign was still present, displayed proudly above the bar.  The rest of the interior was very nice, with wood floors and flat screen TVs visible from every angle.       The menu consisted of a nice selection of barbecue and tex-mex style items on one side, and a gigantic list of tequilas on the other.  The beer selection was located on a chalkboard on the far wall of the restaurant, and our server told us about the three specialty margaritas.  I opted for the strawberry basil, and my mom ordered one of the tequilas.  This particular spirit was previously only known to me in two forms: mixed in a margarita or slammed down with some lime and salt (acts of idiocy following soon after).  I was surprised when the tequila arrived looking classy in a champagne flute.  I tried a small sip and, expecting to cringe, found that I enjoyed the flavor and lightness.  The tequila seemed to evaporate as soon as it hit my mouth.  The margarita was excellent, and the strawberry flavor came from actual fruit, which was nice.  It was similar to a mojito, only with tequila.      We started our meal with salsa roja, salsa verde and guacamole.  All three had great flavors, and though I usually prefer my guacamole on the chunky side, I still enjoyed Q's smoother version.  For dinner, we got the combination platter with ribs, pulled chicken, pulled pork and a side of baked beans, the street tacos with pork and a side of fried green tomatoes.    When the feast arrived at our table, it was almost a little embarrassing.  We went for the tacos first.  The pork inside was shredded and topped with chopped onions and cilantro.  They were very good, especially with a squirt of lime.  My mom really enjoyed the ribs, and we later found out that one of the restaurant's partners used to sell them from a cart in Old City.  When he told us this, my mom and I both instantly realized that we were speaking with the famous "Rib Guy," whom my brother had raved about on many occasions after late nights out.     The pulled pork and chicken were both very good.  They weren't drenched in sauces when they arrived, because Q puts the flavor outcome in the hands of its diners by providing three different sauces on the table.  Carolina vinegar, sweet barbecue and Q sauce, a slightly spicier version of sweet barbecue sauce, are offered.  While all three had nice flavors, we felt that there could have been a little more spice or maybe even a little hot sauce in the Q for a bigger kick.     My mom and I really enjoyed ourselves at Q, and we both plan to return.  Tequila flights are going to be added to the menu in the near future, and I have every intention of checking them out while sitting on the outdoor patio on a warm, sunny day.

I had a major craving for one of those Thanksgiving sandwiches and this Primo was close to my location when said craving occurred. The store was clean and employees were all business but friendly. As I waited for my order, I perused the chips - they have every variety you could possibly want.   I wanted my sandwich hot but was informed that it might not travel well and was encouraged to opt for the cold turkey on the sandwich and a side of gravy. A generous side of gravy was provided in a separate paper bag, and I agree that this was the best option.   All of the ingredients of the sandwich were good and my craving was satisfied, but I think the Thanksgiving sandwich is better in my imagination than it is on my tastebuds. I think I'll stick with regular hoagies for the most part, but if the craving strikes once a year I'll definitely hit Primo for the fix.

Rittenhouse Square? Too crowded, too expected. Washington Square? Too far, not enough character. Fitler Square? Juuuuust right!  This unassuming little park just across from Dmitri's charmed me when I first discovered it a year or so ago, and it has remained my favorite in Philly. It's well-maintained, with a few cute animal statues, brick walkways and lots of soft green grass for picnicking. The park is never overcrowded, and there is always a bench available, even on weekends. What a perfect oasis near my home!

Definitely a huge fan of The PokéSpot! I've ordered for delivery and stopped in for takeout for the first time yesterday. I'm fairly certain I ordered the same thing each time; a rice base with one scoop of ahi tuna and one scoop of spicy tuna. I topped with seaweed salad, avocado and cucumber, though it's kind of hard to narrow down because there are so many delicious fresh options! Crispy onions add some texture and wasabi shoyu sauce on the side is perfect for an extra flavor kick.   There was a line when I visited in-person but it moved quickly and the employees were friendly. The bowls make for a hearty lunch and tide me over until dinner. Nothing but praise from this girl!

A beautiful, classy dining room, impeccable service and delicious food are all what makes Fountain Restaurant one of the finest restaurants in Philadelphia. We enjoyed a leisurely two-hour-plus dinner on a quiet Thursday night; everything about our experience was just perfect.   I started out with a glass of prosecco. The wine and cocktail list is all kept on an iPad which is pretty cool. Cocktails are all made with local ingredients and spirits. Later, we discussed how the iPad concept would work amazingly with the cheese selection. It's a fun experience to choose directly from the display, but having descriptions of the cheeses to peruse through (without having to ask our server about every single one) would be even better.   A bread basket with a nice array of freshly-baked breads was brought around not once but twice. It was hard resisting that second piece but I knew I had several courses ahead of me. To start, I had a sweet potato soup with apple and bacon. Perfect in every way. My beau had a chilled lobster salad that was excellent. For my main course, a perfect filet served in a thick sauce with shredded Brussels sprouts and bacon. The filet was topped with a cheese pierogi, which was fun and also delicious.   We skipped dessert in favor of the aforementioned cheese. The selection was incredible and the presentation gorgeous. We shared around five cheeses and I found a new favorite - Stilton blue.   Coffee service is like an experience in itself, presented with a selection of what I assume are housemade candies, each one fantastic. I especially loved the ramekin of raw sugar for the coffee, which reminded me of rock candy. The kid in me was delighted!  Through our visit, every staff member we came into contact with was supremely professional. The service at this restaurant is truly unmatched by most restaurants anywhere. The Four Seasons staff are experts at making you feel like a guest.   I'd go back in a heartbeat. Anyone feeling particularly spendy?

I enjoyed this cute local theater that shows only a few feature flicks at a time. Though clearly an older building, the theater was clean and comfortable. We saw Silver Linings Playbook and the picture was very clear and, just as important, the movie audience was respectful. Before the movie, an employee came in to announce a raffle the theater was running, and also talk about their upcoming Oscars party, which sounded like fun. I'd happily trek out to Ambler for dinner and a movie again.

I really liked my first lunch at Mission Taqueria, and am excited to go back for dinner and margaritas. We started with the guacamole, which was a healthy portion and served up a nice kick with chunks of jalapeño. The tortilla chips were thin and crispy. We asked for a side of salsa and were later charged $6 unexpectedly - this was removed from our check but I have noticed in the meantime that there is a salsa section on the menu that I somehow missed. To me, guac without salsa is peanut butter without jelly so this combo will sadly set me back mucho dolares in the future.   My salad choice was the romaine and bean, to which I made a couple modifications (no cheese, vinaigrette instead of creamy dressing). I also added shrimp. This salad was filling and delicious and the shrimp were really nicely seasoned. Would order again. My dining companion's kale salad looked solid.   We were treated to a couple fresh juices on the house and I loved the light and refreshing red pepper drink I received. It was just a touch sweet which was perfect for me. Our server, Zareen, was a doll.   Can't wait for the visit numero dos!

Caffe Maida provided two much-needed espressos on a recent evening in Ambler. But let's be real. If there was any competition at all this place would probably be in a little bit of trouble. I can't give less than three stars since they seemed to be the only coffee-slinging game in town, however. Glad they had the beans when I needed them.

I'm pretty sure Lowe's was the first store I physically set foot inside since the Covid-19 pandemic took over in mid-March. Last weekend, I decided it was time to get my roofdeck summer-ready and I felt comfortable enough to visit the store while donning a mask and bringing my own Lysol wipes.   This particular location has an exit only situation coming from the garden center, with entry taking place through the main doors. Everyone there including customers had masks on which was great. I didn't see any wipes available but I also didn't look super hard. I grabbed a cart from the parking lot so I could sweep through the outdoor plants by the curb before entering the store itself.    The plants and flower selection was poppin' and I picked up a couple geraniums and a gorgeous yellow calla lily that I am hoping I can keep alive for as long as possible. I would definitely return to this Lowe's if I needed more home or garden supplies.

Dig came in with the healthy lunch option this week, delivered right to my door with no contact. For whatever reason, lunch seems to be the hardest meal for me to figure out while social distancing. I've always been a big breakfast person, so that's easy. Cooking dinner mostly every night is a pain, but I've got that too. It's this lunch business that has me stumped! I didn't realize how often I grabbed my lunch on the go before the pandemic hit.   Thankfully, there are still tons of businesses offering delivery or takeout during the lunch hours, so people like me can avoid putting together random struggle lunches from odds and ends in the fridge.   I was so happy to splurge a little on my bowl from Dig earlier this week. I've long wanted to try their Jasper Hill mac and cheese and decided it was as good a time as any. I really enjoyed it, even though it was more dry than creamy. I was disappointed to see that my requested carrots had been subbed with sweet potatoes. I already had rice as a base so this made for three starchy inclusions. The sweet potatoes were very basic; not much going on there. I miss the brussel sprouts from the winter menu - they are amazing! The salmon portion was generously sized, however, and I always love the tarragon mustard.   Definitely keep Dig in mind if you're sick of leftovers and need a (mostly) healthy, hearty meal!

This Ritz is a step below the one around the corner closer to Chestnut Street. But it's still a solid spot to catch a flick.   On weekday afternoons, the cost for a movie is just $6.50, which is practically unheard of these days. Concessions are still on the pricey side - some things never change.   Bathrooms were relatively clean on my recent visit. Ever notice how Ritz bathrooms smell like orange Fruit Loops?

One of my favorite girls and I decided to catch up over dinner at Chew Man Chu.  She had already been once before and enjoyed her experience enough to return.  At 6 p.m. on a Monday, there were plenty of tables available and we sat right away.  The décor was bright and fun but somewhat reminiscent of a chain.  Tables were very close together and it was difficult trying to ignore the conversations around us in order to focus on our own.  One thing I did like about the tables was the fact that they were long and offered plenty of room for the various plates we shared.  An array of sauces lined one side.  I'm a condiment lover so this was right up my alley.  Our server was friendly and helpful throughout our stay.  Despite not appearing on the drink menu, I was still able to get a lychee martini, my fav when eating any kind of Asian cuisine (authentic or Americanized).    We started off with steamed shrimp dumplings, which were large but otherwise standard.  Next was the crispy Chinese salad, which was enormous and surrounded by slices of chicken spring rolls.  I'm torn because I enjoyed the salad in theory, but there were too many slivers of ginger throughout and I found the taste to be very overpowering.  I'm a fan of ginger flavor and shredded ginger in sauces or marinades but I've never liked whole pieces so maybe it's a matter of preference.  Regardless, the same heavy hand was used in adding the cilantro, and we picked our way around that as well.    Next we split the salt and pepper crusted shrimp and a side of brown rice.  There were four shrimp on the plate, each the size of a baby's fist and encased in a cloak of delicious fried goodness.  This was by far the best part of the meal.    If our meal had ended there, I might have gone with four stars.  Unfortunately, we decided to try the gelato.  Along with sorbet, this is the only dessert offering at the restaurant.  My friend had the bananas foster flavor, which she enjoyed, and I had half pistachio and half chocolate.  I found the taste of my selections to be slightly freezer burnt and a little mealy.  Miniature donuts are served with the check and had I known this ahead of time, I probably would have passed on dessert (or headed down to Capogiro!).

I'm new to the frozen yogurt game and don't have a ton of experience with what's great and what's not so great. But Kiwi was bright, clean, had plenty of choices and a friendly staff. What's not to like?
