To expand my frozen yogurt portfolio, I tried dollops of the red velvet flavor with graham cracker crumbles, peanut butter flavor with super mini chocolate chips and original tart flavor with Cinnamon Toast Crunch. You get your own and then pay by the ounce, which is great for trying as much or as little as you'd like. It was a nice treat, and I may just be intrigued enough to develop a habit.

I've landed at this Continental quite a few times recently. It's a super convenient location for a pre-River Rink meal and I've taken advantage of that twice in the past month. Service is always friendly and fast - you place that order and food starts arriving at your table within five minutes, it seems.   Our go-to starters are usually the French onion soup dumplings, the Szechuan shoestring fries, BBQ chicken quesadilla or the Korean tacos.   I generally follow up with something much healthier. The Continental salad is my go-to on four out of five visits. Last night I ordered it with shrimp, which came with something around a seven dollar up-charge. But I really wanted shrimp! The salad was delish, as usual. There is a lot of flavor but it's still pretty light overall (even though they give you a mountain of salad). Although I haven't had it in ages, the seared tuna with mushroom risotto has always been a fav.   The desserts are small but perfect for sharing if you only want a few bites of something sweet. Our go-to has been The Grasshopper, which is a very fudgy brownie, scoop of mint chocolate chip ice cream, chocolate sauce, whipped cream, and chocolate candy topping.   Continental's prices aren't too bad for each individual dish, but when you start adding up plate after plate it can get expensive.

Wow, Rowan has really changed since I was an undergrad. There's a full on shopping center with multiple restaurants. Back in my day, (insert long, winding speech about terrible food options and walking uphill both ways).   The Chickie's & Pete's wasn't too crowded on a Wednesday night. We were seated near a huge screen, which made hockey watching lots of fun. I cannot go to a C&P and not get crab fries, so we ordered those as soon as we sat down. I was happy this location had Heineken 0.0, since I was driving but love beer with bar food.   The fries were delish, and then we moved on to the lobster pizza, which had a lot more flavor than I expected! It was very garlicky and had loads of cheese and some really nice chunks of lobster tail.   Our server was friendly but didn't come around super often, which was really the only negative part of the experience. Overall, a solid night out before heading home!

When the winter months set in, my cravings for hot chocolate begin to skyrocket. After attending a Sixers game one cold night a few weeks ago, we decided to hit Broad Street Diner after the game. We sat at the counter and I had hot chocolate with whipped cream while my husband had a black and white milkshake. Both hit the spot, and the milkshake was huge.   Our server was sweet and overall the experience was good. This may become a tradition for post-game celebrations!

Hands down, Maple Shade Custard Stand has THE BEST soft serve in this area.  I say this as a former employee (summer job in college) and a lifelong customer.  My sister worked one or two summers there during college as well and shares my opinion.  Sundaes, milk shakes, flurries (soft ice cream blended with toppings of your choice), water ice, homemade chocolate covered bananas, chipwiches and ice cream sandwiches are just some of the things you can get every day of the week and any time of year.  I always leave happy and with exactly what I came for-- they are well prepared and well stocked for business.  Probably one of the reasons why they have been around for decades!

While I have yet to dine at this particular Le Pain Quotidien, I do have to give their staff five giant stars for helping me out the other day. I was running late to a personal training session at Platoon's new facility and I realized as I got to the corner of 8th and Walnut that I actually wasn't sure about the exact address. Panicked and without my iPhone, I popped into Le Pain Quotidien to see if, by chance, one of the employees would know where the place was located.   After explaining my predicament, the friendly young lady behind the counter popped out her smart phone and checked her Yelp app for me. I got to my appointment with a few minutes to spare and a smile of relief. I'll be sure to update once I return for a paid experience!

I've only been to Falls Taproom twice, but I really like the place. My husband and I stopped in for dinner on Friday night before heading over to an event at Laurel Hill Cemetery. We are so lucky we walked in when we did (just after 7), because even though there weren't any tables available, a handful of groups walked in right after us. We were already pretty tight on time so we would have had to go somewhere else if we weren't up next. I was super stoked to be seated after just a few minutes of waiting even though we sort of had to rush through our dinner a little.   The draft list is awesome and the bottle list is just as solid. I was excited to see my new fave, Austin Eastcider, on the menu. We started with cornmeal-dusted fried pickles, which were really delicious. I was feeling the meatloaf until the mussels went by and promptly changed my plans. The mussels in red sauce were delish and plentiful. My husband was disappointed that they were out of pierogi since he had his heart set on the kielbasa and pierogi platter. The kitchen wouldn't substitute hush puppies in for the pierogi so he had to pick something else entirely. Still, he seemed happy with his pulled pork sandwich and fries.   I really dig the vibes in this place! Everyone seemed pretty darn happy that it was Friday night, and the music was on point - tons of great classic rock cranked up yet not loud enough that you couldn't enjoy your conversation. Definitely looking forward to next time!

If you're looking for an upscale cocktail bar without the riff raff while in New Orleans, this is your place. In fact, they close at 11pm on weeknights and midnight on Fridays and Saturdays.   A group of us popped in for a nightcap after the place was recommended to me by a Yelp bud (thanks, Kyle!). Perusing the menu of tiki drinks, I went straight for the mai tai and it was absolutely delicious. So good, that my cocktail was passed around to everyone in my group for a taste. When we heard the gong (yes, gong!) signaling last call, everyone placed their order for a mai tai. Solid spot!

I checked this place out for lunch earlier this week. The menu is massive and curiously runs the gamut from traditional pizza shop offerings to Mediterranean style dishes.   I placed my order online, but when I tried to punch in the promotion code for a 10% discount, nothing happened. The ordering process was easy and even offered options for customization. I removed the onions from my chicken Caesar wrap and entered a note that I wanted the dressing served on the side.   When I arrived less than ten minutes later, my order was ready, but the dressing was mixed in the wrap. (So if you plan to order a sauce on the side, I'd recommend calling over using the online ordering process.)  The wrap was decent, but the chicken was more in the style of a chicken cheesesteak than regular grilled chicken. It was served with a bag of chips and a pickle. For less than $8, it wasn't a bad lunch option, but it's not about to become a regular in the rotation, either.

Our group of six ducked into The Corner Foodery for some pre-gaming action before the Flyers game on Saturday. The set up is half bottle shop, half sit-down eatery. You can pick out bottles to drink there and just pay as you go and enjoy the seating. There are still and bubbly water taps and several TVs scattered around. I was surprised at the ample amount of seating and even more surprised at the lack of people. I think this place is still under the radar, but I can't imagine that it will be for very long. It's not often you can go to a restaurant and drink a beer at the bottle price.     The menu is a mix of sandwiches, salads and snacks that sounds delicious. I'm eager to get back for lunch or dinner sometime soon.

Our normal sushi delivery spot wasn't open so we tried Koto on a whim, and our delivery experience was pretty great. We ordered the vegetable gyoza, which had a perfect chew and flavorful filling. For rolls, my husband had the spicy tuna and salmon avocado, while I had the spicy tuna and tuna avocado. We shared an angel roll, as well. Everything was packaged nicely and the prices were fair. I'd try them again!

My feelings about this location of Good Karma somewhat echo my feelings of the other; decent but not my fave. This particular spot is very close to where I live, so I'm sure it will go into the rotation of places to grab a cup, as I've yet to find the cafe that will become my steady.   The other day I stopped by for an impromptu latte. I was sure I would end up liking this second version of GK better than the first. The cafe was smaller than I expected, but it was bright and full of the same good vibes that fill the front part of the Pine Street shop.   I walked outside and pulled my first sip - it was warm, not even close to hot. Frustrating, since coffee comes at a premium nowadays.   I'll return, but I make no promises once I find my go-to establishment.

Cute coffee shop with excellent iced coffee and great pastries. I enjoyed a ham and cheese croissant which was flaky, buttery deliciousness.   I read something on their website about how tables can be reserved for $10/hour. Since I was meeting with one of my team members I decided to reserve a table for two hours. When I arrived on that weekday morning, the coffee shop was empty save for one or two other people. So, I most likely wouldn't formally reserve a table again unless I was going at a peak time - seemed like kind of a waste of money. Although, your reservation does get you a 20% discount on all food and drink orders. And I suppose if you really needed to guarantee a table for a work meeting, it's good to know that Rally offers this, since I can't think of a single other place that does. So there's pros and cons to that.   I am looking forward to returning!

I am a regular at the Lacquer Lounge in Queen Village but the Rittenhouse location proved to be more convenient this week so I decided to make my appointment there. The space is larger than the other location but just as cute and girly. Everyone working was laid-back and friendly, which is one of the things I have always loved about Lacquer Lounge.   Both my classic pedi with Lina and my power hour mani with Nicole were great. These gals really made my nails look fantastic. Even though the Queen Village location will always have a slight edge for me, I'm really excited about this second location which is closer to where I live and also convenient for whenever I'm running around Rittenhouse. Best of both worlds!

My boyfriend suggested that we swing by the new Farm & Fisherman Tavern while in Jersey for a party, and I was all too happy to oblige. I love the Lawler's restaurant on Pine Street so I was excited to check out their more casual Jersey location.   When you walk in, there is a small market and deli section to the right of the bar area. The bar is in the center and features some high top tables, and the dining room is a bit more sectioned off on its own to the right. We were seated in the dining room in sort of a semi-booth that faces out to the room. It's hard to explain, but these booths are a little awkward because it feels like you are staring at the people seated in the booth directly across from you. But on the plus side, these quasi-booths are quite roomy for two. A little tight for a family of four, though, from what we could see.   We started with a couple beers from the solid selection of draughts and bottles. The chips and onion dip went along perfectly. We continued the tour of taters with the "crushed and crispy NJ spuds" appetizer. This featured a medley of potatoes, a sour cream sauce, some sort of earthy green sauce and pieces of bacon. Tasty, not life-changing.   My tavern steak with salsa verde, Kennett Square mushrooms, crispy onion straws and au gratin potatoes was excellent. It came exactly medium rare as requested and paired awesomely with a Dogfish Head 60 Minute. With zero room left for dessert, we opted for some strong coffees to get us through our second party of the night.   Service was solid and the dining room was full by the time we left. I text messaged a friend who lives nearby to let her know I found the location for our next double date. Looking forward to next time!

After staring longingly at the "Coming Soon" sign that hung in the doorway for months on end, Woksabi finally opened and I was able to check out the eats.    Yesterday being my birthday (shameless plug~ I'm a Leo, what do you expect?!), I decided it was as good a time as any to treat myself to a little take-out.  I tried the "tuna madness" roll, which the previous reviewer recommended.  It was a crunchy spicy tuna roll topped with seared tuna, scallions and tobiko.  I figured at $12, the roll would be pretty substantial, but I threw in a cucumber roll just in case.    I got home and tore into my bag-- and was a little disappointed.  The tuna madness roll was no larger than an average, run of the mill tuna roll, with small pieces of seared tuna on top.  I wondered, "Where exactly is the madness?" It was good for sure, but definitely not worth $12.    I'll be back, but next time will opt for the regular spicy tuna rolls that cost half the price.

Does someone mind explaining why the apocalypse hit this Walmart location a long time ago?   Walking in, I'm like a deer in headlights with the absence of neck tattoos, tight polyester clothing and loud, screaming children. I quickly scurry past the masses at customer service and Subway, trying to avoid eye contact while planning my attack. The faster I get to the items I need, the faster I can just get out of there already.   Problem is, the items I need never seem to be in stock, or available at all. Something as basic as plastic cups was too much to ask on my recent visit. I secured small cups but, other than the giant red Solo cups, there were no other options for something in between.   The only redeeming thing about the place is the body shop, which unfortunately means I have had to endure many an hour walking around the store while my car received an oil change. There aren't even any decent stores in the strip mall that shares the parking lot to escape to.   I do believe I made my final exit through this Walmart's doors the other day.

Today was my second experience with Stock. The first time, we ordered pho and the delivery arrived with a cracked soup container and broth everywhere. I knew that was on the delivery service and didn't bother with a review.   This time, everything arrived intact. I tried the Lao curry soup with grilled shrimp. It's mandatory to choose tofu or poached chicken but I really only wanted the shrimp and made a note on my order, which was honored. Why not just give all the options and adjust pricing accordingly?   Anyway, I was surprised that the broth was cold and came with instructions to boil in a pot. I order delivery so I don't have to cook or clean! Only joking (sort of). I do think it's worth the extra step because warming the broth at home really made the soup that much more delicious. I followed the instructions and microwaved the noodles in a big bowl, then added the other ingredients and poured the steaming broth on top. I actually liked having control over how many fresh herbs I put in my dish since I don't really care for too many. My only complaint is that the shrimp had a slightly mushy texture, though they tasted fine. The soup itself was spicy and soothing - exactly what I was after.   Solid experience and I'd order this dish again when the craving strikes!

Recently, I wrote about the disappointing search for good pad Thai in my area.  I had surrendered my efforts and had given up hope, when I suddenly recalled seeing some random hot entrees on a take out menu from nearby Woksabi.  Thinking the chances of finding Thai items at a Japanese restaurant were slim, I quickly scanned the menu when, out of nowhere, I saw it: Pad Thai with chicken, shrimp or beef: $10.  I promptly placed my order and was told it would be ready in 20 minutes.    A half hour later, I pulled a huge container of steaming hot goodness from the brown paper bag.  The noodles did not appear oily at all, which meant the dish was created by Thailand standards as opposed to most Americanized versions which are made with oil (yeah, I looked it up- Wikipedia rocks!).  My request to 86 the tofu was honored.  Not only was the serving size large enough for two lunches, it was also light, flavorful and just all-around awesome.  Pad Thai victory!!!

Airport food is so hit or miss (mostly miss) but Balducci's is a solid option. They have a large variety of snacks including some heartier stuff that actually passes off as healthy, too.   There is a pretty solid selection of grab and go meals, including sandwiches, salads and vegetarian entrees. There is also a counter where you can get some of the sandwiches warmed up. That's where I ordered my bacon, egg and cheese on an english muffin while grabbing a caprese baguette to go. (In my opinion, caprese is the most inoffensive sandwich one can eat on a plane.)  The breakfast sandwich was actually quite tasty. Their coffee is also acceptable. But the best part of Balducci's is that you can get in and out relatively quickly. The Starbucks and La Colombe located in the main hallway outside of terminals B and C always have the longest lines! This is my new go-to.

It's been a while since I've eaten in the restaurant, but every time I have whether for dinner, brunch or a small party, it is always a great experience.    Recently, my mom ordered dinner from Due Amici for my sister's graduation party.  There was plenty of food and everything was delicious.  Even better was knowing that my mom would have one less thing to stress about so she could enjoy herself along with everyone else.

I love Career Wardrobe and everything they stand for - bettering the community by helping unemployed women to find jobs and look the part.   Donating is easy, especially at The Wardrobe Boutique location on Spring Garden. The building is located on the corner and there is a sizeable loading zone on 19th Street where you can pull up to unload. The boutique itself is cute and well-organized, and the women who work at this location are always so friendly. Tax forms are available, if you need/want them.   Great community service!

This place is so solid, I have to update my review to five stars. We order delivery from The Foodery pretty regularly, and we are always very happy with our orders. The half sandwich plus a side of soup or salad is a great deal at $11. You get the heartiness of the sandwich without feeling like you went overboard on the carbs. Favorite sandwiches are the olive oil poached tuna, the godfather, and the roasted turkey (served warm).    Sandwiches are very consistent - I know what I'm going to get every single time. Ingredients are tasty and high quality. I definitely think The Foodery is a level above other comparable sandwich shops.

I've experienced better is right. Of all Saladworks locations I've patronized, this was one of the worst. The workers were friendly but the restaurant wasn't a place I'd like to sit down and eat a meal.   The salad I did get was totally fine, but the salads on display looked sad and gross. They aren't trying very hard, and it shows.

First Person Arts is a first class organization. Their events are meaningful, well-run, well-staffed and always a great time. I attended my first Story Slam last week and it happened to be a Grand Slam - pretty much a guarantee for great narratives and funny deliveries.   Before the Slam was an optional pre-party barbecue catered by Sweet Lucy's and Victory Brewing Company. I cannot say enough great things about Sweet Lucy's and their delicious smoked meats and hearty sides. Experiencing them once again only reminded me that I need to return to the mothership soon, likely with a sixer of Victory brew.  The Slam took place in a large, air-conditioned theater with better than average folding chairs and the right amount of leg room. Every participant followed the rules and the time guidelines, and the event moved along seamlessly, with a short but necessary break for intermission.   If you haven't yet seen or participated in a Story Slam, they take place about once a month and they provide a fun, different kind of night out.

My sister and I wandered over to Falls Taproom for an after dinner drink on Friday night. The downstairs bar was packed but we grabbed two newly opened seats at the bar upstairs. I love the dark wood and old timey light bulbs. Didn't really love/understand the TVs with black and white movies, which were on silent. I say sports or nothing!   The cocktail menu is interesting and I was immediately drawn to the hot apple cider with rum. My sister opted for another boozy concoction but she switched over to the apple cider for her second round. I loved the cracked clove on top; it made the drink very fragrant. This is the perfect beverage for a chilly fall night.   Our bartender was nice and we enjoyed chatting with him. We're already talking about our next visit!

Stella Pizza is pretty darn good.  It's my second choice when I order pizza because I do prefer the pies at another Haddon Ave. establishment, but the thing about Stella is that their other items are reliable as well.  Salads are great (especially the Caesar salad and the buffalo chicken salad), and they come with a garlicky roll.    AND, Stella was my great-grandmom's name.  What's not to like about that?!

My friend and I arrived at Melograno at 8 p.m. to find the rest of our "BYO girls" already waiting.  We were promptly seated at a roomy table near the open kitchen, which was cool.  Our waitress arrived and ran through the specials, which included a pepper stuffed with crab something-or-other, a salad and two lamb entrees.  Then she was gone... for a long time.  Unremarkable bread was dropped at our table with a little bowl of olive oil that looked to be seasoned with pepper.  As it was 8 p.m., we were all pretty hungry so the bread was gone in no time while we waited for our server to return and take our order.  When she eventually came back, the rest of the evening went pretty smoothly.  We started with the salad special, which had roasted grape tomatoes, slices of mushroom (not sure what kind as I don't really eat mushrooms), shaved parmesan, walnuts and a lemon dressing.  It was an interesting mix of ingredients and they came together well.  We also enjoyed the antipasto plate, which had some nice pieces of prosciutto and mozzarella, olives, roasted vegetables and toasted bread slices with various spreads.  My entrée was definitely the highlight of the meal.  I had the mixed seafood grill, which came with a nice sized piece of salmon, a few shrimp and several calamari rings, all served over buttery mashed potatoes.  It was heaven on a plate.  The calamari was tender and grilled perfectly, with a touch of coarse salt in the seasoning which made this my favorite part of the dish, especially when combined with the potatoes.  Everyone else seemed happy with their selections as well, evidenced by the fact that we probably set a record with how fast everything was eaten.    For dessert, we tried the crème brulee, spiced chocolate cake with vanilla gelato and the tiramisu.  I enjoyed the tiramisu most, followed by the crème brulee.  The cake did nothing for me, but I generally like my desserts straightforward and uncomplicated (apparently for me, spicy chocolate = complication), so this particular offering could easily be someone else's favorite.    I definitely agree with the other reviewers who mentioned the noisiness of the restaurant.  It was incredibly loud, so much so that it was impossible to have a conversation across the table without shouting.  This was definitely a drawback but not enough so that I would not return.  However, I wouldn't recommend the place for a quiet, intimate dinner for two.  For purposes of group get-togethers and girls' night out, count me in!

Volvér is a little hit or miss for me. My first experience for dinner after they first opened was pretty exceptional. Since then, I've returned for drinks on several occasions and dinner at the bar about a month ago.   The happy hour menu offers some deals, but bites are on the very small side. The paella maki roll sounded awesome but wasn't really all that special, in my opinion.   Moving on to dinner, the grass fed beef tenderloin with potatoes and broccolini was excellent. But, again, small. There were two nice slices of beef, three tiny potatoes and two stems of broccolini. The size of the plate compared with what was on it was laughable, quite honestly. But every bite was delicious and I also didn't feel guilty so there's that.   My husband ordered the fried chicken sandwich, which looked delicious. For just $13 (or $16, with bacon), you actually do get a ton of food so maybe consider that or the burger if you are really hungry. Unfortunately, the chicken was reportedly "chewy", which was obviously a surprise considering the caliber of the restaurant.   I feel like this review reads more like a three star account, but I'm going with four because I love the female bartender who works there - she's always friendly and fun. Considering the prices and inconsistency with the food, I probably won't be rushing back to eat but would drop in for a drink or two.

Prior to attending Opening Tap for Philly Beer Week on Friday, it was absolutely imperative to get a solid base going with an early dinner. After talking about the usual spots, my boyfriend and I decided to go outside the box and meet at Nodding Head.   I've never been a huge fan of Nodding Head's beers, but considering the fact that it had been about two years since my last visit, I was willing to try again. There were five or six beers priced at $4 for happy hour (which went until 7) and I opted for the Zephyr, a mild, slightly hoppy brew that was pleasant enough for repeat orders. There were some food specials as well, so we ordered a $4 plate of mussels to start.   The mussels, steeped in a delicious broth with bacon, were every bit as good as Monk's and we polished them off very quickly. For dinner, I pulled a wild card and went with the vegetarian chili after seeing it delivered to a nearby table. The rice base was perfectly cooked and flavorful, and the medley of spicy beans and squash was awesome. Cheddar topped off the hearty plate, and a side of sour cream was served with the dish.   I'll definitely consider Nodding Head again for happy hour and a bite.

I woke up today still thinking about last night's meal at Modo Mio. For that reason, I'm going with five stars rather than four. Our server, Michelle, was very nice and checked in with us at all the right times even though she was quite busy with every table in the place full. We of course opted for the turista menu, a prix fixe that cannot be beat.   To start, I opted for the mozzarella antipasti, which was like a mozzarella grilled cheese sitting in caper brown butter. It was quite rich but so delicious, especially when dipped in spicy marinara sauce from the mussels across the table.  Next up for me was the lasagna. Thick, creamy and topped with a perfectly crisped-around-the-edges fried egg, this was one take on lasagna I'd never encountered before but definitely want to meet again. Again, it was extremely rich but so delicious. I traded plates often with my boyfriend, who at this point had a plate of hollowed spaghetti with tomato sauce flavored with pancetta and pecorino. We were warned that this dish was a little "salt forward" but I would say that most of the dishes at Modo Mio were a tad heavy on the salt. It didn't turn me off because the heaviness of the food seemed to warrant the salt, but I did drink a lot of water. Not that it mattered, because our glasses were refreshed before ever having to ask.   Soldiering on, we greeted our entrees. For me, a red snapper filet that was crisped on the outside but moist on the inside. It sat over crushed tomatoes with green olives, capers, potatoes and onions. This is probably one of the lighter offerings on the menu and at that point I was grateful. But it didn't stop me from asking for bites of the pounded pork cutlet, blanketed in prosciutto and provolone and resting in a buttery caper sauce. I'm not even a big fan of pork but this was incredible.   By the time we were offered dessert, I can honestly say that nothing really appealed to me because I was so full. I ordered the lightest-sounding option, honey semifreddo, which was indeed delicious although I could only take one bite. The caramel pudding, however, was devoured in a flash.   While the restaurant was loud and bustling and not exactly romantic for our date night, we chatted with neighboring diners and even exchanged contact info with some folks from LA who make Modo Mio a part of every visit to Philly. I can't wait for my next visit to this fun, comfort food-filled BYO.

What a fabulous building! I had been to the College of Physicians once before, but only to walk through the lobby so I could get to the Mütter Museum, which is housed inside, off the main lobby. On Saturday, I went to attend the wedding reception of a wonderful friend.  Cocktail hour took place in said lobby, in front of the giant marble staircase. A side room resembled a fancy, old-fashioned library. Eventually, the party was led upstairs, to a huge wood-adorned room decorated with huge portraits of doctors from back in the day. This room was set up for dinner and dancing.   Another large side-room was accessible, with dessert and coffee stations... and a photo booth!!! We may or may not have borrowed a bust off one of the nearby bookshelves, to use as a prop during our booth session. Said bust was returned to his rightful shelf (although we think it's been quite a while since he's had so much fun).   I'm not sure if the catering company is the regular house caterer or not, but in any case, they did a really nice job and the food was great. The only issue was with the bartending area. There seemed to be a lack of glassware and shakers, and one of the bartenders was very frenzied for most of the night. We all still managed to get our drink on, and I do not believe there was a sober person in the house that night.

After a long car ride home from North Jersey, the last thing I wanted to do was go back out in search of dinner. We placed an order with Slice, and within 45 minutes dinner arrived. One small signature salad and one large margherita pizza came to around $25, with free delivery.   The dressing for the salad came in a side cup, which was great because there were no soggy bits. Just fresh arugula, dried cranberries, gorgonzola and pine nuts. The pie, on the other hand, was definitely soggy. Some time in the oven helped significantly, but shouldn't delivery pizza be ready to enjoy when it arrives?   Nonetheless, I do like Slice and I'll give some of their other pies a try the next time we order.

When I learned that the pastry chef who made my wedding cake was taking over a local bakery in Wayne, I immediately marked my calendar for a visit! Marqessa Gesualdi is not only extremely talented, she's also lovely to work with and truly cares about creating the best experience possible for her clients.   Alisha S and I popped into Aux Petits Delices for some morning sugar. We shared the flaky napoleon and the ultra rich delice - both were incredible! The delice put me into a near sugar coma, but the combination of dark chocolate and hazelnut were irresistible.   The bakery also sells baguettes, croissants and chocolates. They have some seating, and serve La Colombe coffee, so you can enjoy a sweet treat right in the shop. I am so happy Marqessa has landed in her very own bakery and cannot wait to commission her for a (smaller) replica of my amazing wedding cake sometime in the future!

I don't know if I'm being stingy or if all this economy business has me paying more attention to financial matters, but lately I'm feeling like quality is declining and yet prices are crazy high!  Hang on.  Wait just a minute.  I think my micro and macro economics professors just got their wings!  Finally, five-plus years later, I get it!    Joking aside, 2007's Best of Philly happy hour winner leaves A LOT to be desired.  They boast $5 wines by the glass-- but that's only for two selections, one red and one white.  The Cabernet they had on special was pretty beat, and since we didn't want to take a chance on the white, my friend and I ordered a bottle of chardonnay off the regular menu that was actually really good.  After a couple drinks, we ordered the tomato & mozzarella pizza and a wedge salad to share.  The pizza was good for sure but there was no substance.  A saltine is thicker than the crust used in this pizza, no joke.  As for the wedge salad?  I had to ask the bartender if he brought the right one-- it was a hunk of iceberg with some really random vegetables leaned up against it, and an unidentifiable gray substance on the side.  When the bartender confirmed that this was indeed the wedge salad, I asked where the Gorgonzola came in-- oh the gray stuff, of course!  The menu didn't mention that it would be presented in a baby poop-inspired way so that's probably why I didn't realize.  My bad!    Rae is a cool-looking spot for sure, but I think they take advantage of the fact that they are the only real restaurant in the 30th Street Station/Cira Centre vicinity.  They miss the mark on "creative, complex and imaginative" because they try too hard to get overly fancy, which is just annoying and unnecessary (much like the 5 star reviews that are clearly written by Rae staff).  I can see why it's a popular spot, and the complimentary valet is definitely a bonus, but I don't think I'll be going out of my way to grab a drink or bite to eat there again.

I'd give 3 stars for the food and 4 for the ambiance.  Since I'm feeling nice today, I'll round up to 4 stars total.    I was meeting a friend for dinner and knew we were going to get into some deep conversations.  I wanted a place with a relaxed atmosphere and chill vibe, so we went to Positano Coast.    The bar area on a Tuesday was really dead, which was fine with us.  I'm not crazy about the happy hour specials ~ $4 for a 3 ounce glass of wine didn't really feel like a deal, but whatev.  Our dinner reservations were for 7:30, and we were led to the dining room, which was filled with an older crowd and some business types.  I asked if there was anywhere else to sit, and we were taken to the lounge area which was perfect.  Little nooks with comfy chairs and pillows were sectioned off by gauzy curtains, which made for a really intimate setting.  We had the antipasto to start, which was a great match to the fresh bread and olive oil that was brought to the table.  For dinner we ordered the branzino and chicken rollatini entrees, plus a side of gnocchi gorgonzola.  The food was good but entrees were on the smaller side so I'd recommend getting a couple side items for every two people.   I'll definitely be back next time I want to unwind and feel like I'm on a mini vacation!

It's no secret that I love PJ's. What born-and-bred South Jersian doesn't? My family decided to check out the Medford Lakes location on Saturday night for a change of scenery from the Moorestown and Cherry Hill locations that we frequent. We were given a 25-30 minute wait time but it was more like 15 minutes which was great. Alysa was our server and she was fantastic - always swinging by to check on us and making sure we had everything we needed.   We started with the cheesesteak nachos which are awesome. Possibly better than the regular nachos because the distribution of toppings was on point. We also had wings, of course. I normally love PJ's wings but they missed the mark for me on this visit. Their wings are usually pretty sizable which is why we always ask for them extra crispy, but these wings were almost too big so they didn't reach the desired crispiness (I realize how ridiculous this sentence sounds, but I'm picky about my wings). My mom and I shared the Sriracha chicken tacos special but they weren't very special. I tasted no trace of Sriracha and we both thought the dish was sort of lame. Should have went with my usual, the buffalo chicken salad, which my sister said was delish.   Menu misses on this visit aside, this PJs was running like a well oiled machine and that definitely counts for something. I'm sure we'll be back soon since this location isn't far from my sister's house.

I hit up Blue Belly BBQ on a whim with some peeps yesterday afternoon. The menu is small but interesting. This isn't your typical order a quarter pound of smoked meat and a side type of place. Sure, you can do that, but you can also order a sandwich made with really unique ingredients. Sammies that aren't your standard pulled pork on a potato roll.   I opted for the jerk chicken sandwich, which came with pickled onions, some sort of aioli and fried okra. I personally hate okra, but I was willing to just pull those bits off. When I realized after ordering that the sandwiches come with cole slaw and fries, I asked if I could sub out the fries with collard greens. After a brief hesitation, my request was granted. But it seems like this may be something they are still unsure about. I'm hopeful that they'll change "served with cole slaw and fries" to "served with cole slaw and your choice of side." I'm sure I won't be the only one who asks for another option.   My sandwich was awesome. The chicken was well seasoned and tender. I did come across a bone at one point, which was obviously unpleasant since I was nomming down a sandwich and didn't expect it. The collards were very tasty and the slaw had just the right crunch and vinegar-y taste.    BBBBQ is cash-only, and they aren't open on Monday and Tuesday (at the time of this review).

Dig is pretty similar in concept to another nearby healthy, fast-casual concept. However, Dig's execution is much better. I'd seen tons of recent positive reviews on Yelp so I made a mental note to check them out next time I was in the area.   Fast forward to my visit, I probably looked like a deer in headlights when I got in line. Thankfully, the staff could not have been nicer and even helped me along with some suggestions to keep me moving. I opted for a rice base, salmon protein, roasted brussel sprouts, and roasted carrots (there may have been some other root veggies in there as well). An employee suggested I try the mustard sauce and she was spot on because that sauce went perfectly with this combo! Everything had so much flavor and I was really impressed with my experience overall.   I'm dying to try some of the macaroni and cheese but that will have to be on a day when I'm feeling splurgey. Otherwise, I'm super grateful for another healthy and quick to-go option in Center City!

I'm really wavering between three and four stars for this place, but I've decided to go for three with hopes for an upgrade after my next visit. We were greeted and shown to a table for four even without a reservation on a Friday night. The restaurant was still relatively empty around 7, but quickly filled up within the hour.   Drinks are ridiculously cheap. As in $3-5, including top shelf. So needless to say, we ended up staying for three hours and drinking like we just turned 21.   The food is where this review reaches its three star ceiling. Apps were all nice, including falafel with creamy hummus (but no pita?), phyllo and feta cigars and a tzatziki-like dill and yogurt sauce (again, no pita?). We did receive some really tasty bread with deliciously olive-y olive oil.   I ordered a shrimp, mushroom and tomato casserole topped with mozzarella cheese. It was nice, and I'd probably order it again. Maybe with a side of rice or a vegetable or something if I was really hungry. I didn't love the lamb dish to my left, but I'm not a big lamb-eater. That said, I did enjoy the lamb dumplings, which were flavorful and very nicely prepared. The ground chicken kabob didn't do much for me, either, but I'd consider giving it another shot.   A creme caramel dessert was lackluster and overly gelatin-loaded, but the baklava was awesome.  My first impression was mixed but I'm definitely looking forward to giving Divan a second look, and I'd definitely encourage others to give it a shot as well.

I was craving some basic comfort food recently and decided to order a grilled cheese and tomato soup from The Foodery. The order came with a pickle slice and bag of chips. Though I did need to reheat the grilled cheese in my air fryer upon arrival, it was still great and the tomato soup was perfect (and topped with a big, cheesy crouton thing!).   I've always liked this spot and am glad to see they are still offering quality eats!

A group of girls from my field hockey team headed to Sage after the final game of our first-place season this morning.  We were seated right away, and our server was quick with drinks and always refilling coffee without us having to ask.  My challah French toast was similar to our earlier victory-- sweet and satisfying!

Jackass Burrito is a welcome addition to my delivery lineup. The burritos are a bit of a departure from the usual options. We ordered the K-Town (korean beef, kimchi, etc.), baja shrimp (crispy shrimp, cabbage, baja sauce, etc.) and all day breakfast burritos, plus an order of guac and the salsa trio.   The burritos were large, wrapped very well, and delivered in super cute boxes. We enjoyed all of them, though I'd consider these burritos to be more on the splurgey side of the burrito spectrum (it's possible to eat a semi-healthy burrito, I swear!). The shrimp had a distinct buffalo tang, which I loved but my husband wasn't crazy about. Of all three options, I think the breakfast burrito was my favorite. Guac and salsas were all great, too. Will definitely order again!

Our threesome hit Lucas Park for a late dinner after working an event for hours. The reason behind the decision was that it was one of the few places nearby still serving food.  I was surprised that, for a pretty clubby environment, the menu consisted mostly of fancy entrees and apps. We started with the arugula and artichoke dip, which was solid. I ordered the smoked chicken breast sandwich. Don't get me wrong, I polished it off, but the taste and ingredients were just okay. I also tried a piece of the chicken flatbread. This was not food that stood out in any way or that I'd feel the need to go back for again.  My biggest issue was the service. Our server was nice and apologetic when she was around, but she was pretty absent overall. It took forever to get drinks, forever to get our orders in, forever for our food to come out, forever to pay the check. All the while, we were treated to the pounding house beats of the DJ.    Should Lucas Park and I ever meet again, it would likely be for happy hour or a drink at the end of the night or something, but that would be it.

(said in a NeNe Leakes voice) You have done me wrrronnng, Yelp!   With a four star average, I thought I was in store for a pretty great slice of pie. Not so. The first bite of the plain slice was promising, but subsequent nibbles were dry and lacking flavor. The bbq chicken slice had an off-putting flavor from the barbecue sauce. Ick.  Perhaps a whole hot pie would work out better than a single slice from behind the counter... but it's unlikely I'll be back to find out.

I am way late in my review of Cook, which is one of Philadelphia's best offerings in the food and beverage world. Every month, a schedule of events is announced, along with a date when tickets go on sale. Tickets go very quickly, and they are pricey. But totally worth the splurge.  I've attended a dinner put together by sushi chef Hiroyuki Tanaka (of Zama restaurant), which was beautiful and incredible. Wine pairings were poured for every course. More recently, I attended a rum class by Sara Justice from Franklin Mortgage that was fun and boozy. Some small bites were served.  Seating wraps around the large kitchen island in the center, providing a great view for all and accessibility to ask questions. Looking forward to my next class!

This gorgeous store is packed to the gills with team memorabilia. Unfortunately, the selection of merch for the hometown teams is a bit limited. But if you're a fan of another team and you live in Philly, this is certainly your best bet for finding gear. But it's definitely going to cost ya. I picked up a Sixers tee for my dad today and it was not cheap. It's a very nice shirt, though, one that he'll hopefully have for many years due to the high quality.

I had a very positive experience at OCF yesterday. It had been a while since my last visit. I'm not sure why; this place is in my neighborhood and there always seems to be plenty of seating available. They have free wifi and the music is great, ranging from indie rock to jazz during my visit.   The baristas were so nice and I really enjoyed chatting with them. And these guys make an absolutely delicious (and pretty!) chai tea latte with real tea. I noticed some really tasty-looking pastries and cookies, but didn't partake. Next time! I won't wait so long before my next visit, either.

My brunch threesome spent three very leisurely hours at Kennett on Sunday. The space was homey, the staff super-cool, and the soundtrack a calming mix of Simon & Garfunkel and Rolling Stones.   We started with a round of bloody Marys, which had been built up to great expectations. The drink tasted like a spicy vegetable garden, clean and healthy (minus the vodka part). It was nice, but not one of my favorite BMs.   We started with the salumeria pizza, which was a traditional pie topped with halved olives and freshly sliced salami. I know it was freshly sliced because I watched the chef shave that meat stick with my own eyes just a few feet away.   Having tasted most of the brick oven pizza in this city, I'll go out there and say that Kennett gets it right. Even the center crust had a crunch, without a trace of a burn towards the outer crust. I liked it so much, I ordered the breakfast pizza, with over easy eggs, perfect slices of bacon and a sharp, tangy cheese as my main. My only gripe was that the toppings on both pizzas didn't extend far enough to the outskirts of the pie. The crust was a good inch or more wide around the good stuff.   We were all shocked that the restaurant didn't fill up during the hours we were there. Besides our table and a few people at the bar, it was quiet. With sweet service and fresh, local ingredients, it's only a matter of time before we'll be waiting for our table along with everyone else.

While this wasn't the most seamless rental car experience, it was still fairly solid. My car was sideswiped by a city trash truck so my insurance hooked me up with Enterprise for a rental while my car was in the shop. My husband and I dropped in on a rainy Saturday and we were maybe third in line. There were a couple people working but the process to get people in and out was taking longer than anticipated.   When it was my turn, we went through the paperwork then went out to look at car options. Once I selected my car I thought I'd sign off and get the keys, but we had to go back inside and the car was brought around to the front (only about 30 feet from where it was originally parked), where we then went over more paperwork. It seemed to me like this process could have been streamlined a bit.   As for the car itself, a Hyundai Veloster, I absolutely loved it! It was in great condition and I enjoyed driving the car so much I started thinking about how I'd go about trading in my own Hyundai Elantra for the zippy, simple-to-park-on-city-streets, Veloster!   Alas, my car was finally ready for pick up after 3+ weeks in the shop, and I (somewhat reluctantly) returned my rental this morning. One of the agents walked me out to the car, did a brief inspection and then I was able to sign off on an iPad and head out. Far easier and faster than my first visit.   This particular office is closed on Sundays and has limited Saturday hours, but it's convenient to my neighborhood and especially the auto body shop where I took my car just two blocks away. Hopefully I won't be requiring their services again but if I do I'd be fine with using this Enterprise location.

I still have love for Lolita, but my feelings have waned after experiencing the restaurant on a busy Saturday night. After checking out the menu online, I was so excited to see that my salmon dish from over a year ago was still being featured. When we got to the restaurant, however, the salmon was there but the pureed hearts of palm and grilled corn salad were replaced by other sides. I opted for the short rib entree instead, while my date went with the filet.   We started off with a pitcher of margs, some guacamole and the queso fundido. There isn't much to dislike about any of these things, and they were all a great start to the meal.   Entrees came out pretty quickly after our apps were cleared. Probably a bit too quickly. The restaurant was packed, with a constant rotation of walk-ins, and I got the distinct sense that turning tables as fast as possible was the name of the game. Nonetheless, I dug into my short rib, which was tender and well-flavored, although not nearly as exciting taste-wise as the salmon dish from my previous visit.  We debated on whether or not to share a dessert or simply finish up the margaritas. I opted for the dessert not because I was dead-set on something sweet, but because I felt awkward lingering over our drinks with so many people waiting for tables by the door. Turned out, the chocolate bread pudding was a dry, crumbly disappointment (the coffee was great). After chatting with several people since Saturday night, the tiramisu has been recommended more than once.    The check came, marking the end of a somewhat lackluster night... and it was only then that we realized Lolita is a cash-only establishment. My boyfriend had to dart across the street to take out cash at a pizza shop.  Lessons learned: Bring cash, only go on a weeknight and tiramisu or bust.

I found myself craving that baja shrimp burrito again so we placed another order with Jackass Burrito. This time, we also tried the frito pie burrito and also a more traditional al pastor burrito (I don't believe this was an option last time so it was nice to see a new menu item). We again ordered the guac and salsa trio. This was more than enough food for two meals - one very hefty dinner followed by a slightly less hefty dinner the next day.   I'm a fan!

A friend of mine (what's up, Kylie!) told me about Geisha House when we got together for coffee last week. Since it was in the area and I had some free time, I took a stroll on over to check it out for myself.   First impression: super cute shop! I started chatting with the woman working who I quickly found out was filling in for her daughter (the owner of the store) that morning. She could not have been nicer and it was really nice to chat with her as I shopped.   I wasn't looking for anything in particular but ended up trying on four different pieces. There were two that I really liked but I ultimately went for a dress for just under fifty bucks. As I was paying I also took note of the many great accessories and small gifts. I had to hold myself back from impulse purchasing several more items.   I was beyond bummed when my favorite Old City boutique recently closed, but I'm thrilled to have found a new store that I like just as much!

Welcome to the neighborhood, OCF! My first trip was fairly solid. Four styles of coffee were offered and served in a French press, yielding multiple cups for my friend (who unfortunately didn't love the brew she selected). The barista asked if I wanted my latte flat, which I can honestly say I've never been asked before in my history of ordering lattes. Apparently it has to do with the thickness of the foam.   The café has an Elixr meets Noble meets office building vibe. There is a lot of lime green, wood, funky chairs, and some more practical-looking chairs as well. I personally hope OCF will be a more mature alternative to La Va, where people will be able to have meetings or get some work done in a calmer setting. Time will tell.   Cakes, croissants and other baked goods looked delicious, and come from The Sweet Life Bakeshop. I'll be returning soon for a slice of that lemon cake to go along with my coffee.

Perhaps I'm becoming more high maintenance as I mature, but when I realized last week that I was in dire need of a pedicure, the thought of going to one of the usual cheap-o nail factories was more than I could bear. I took to yelp's "Sales & Offers Near You" page to see if, by some miracle, there was a salon offering a pedicure special in the area.   Christmas come early!   To my delight, I noticed a Tuesday pedicure special that was being offered at a salon I had never even heard of in nearby Haddon Township. I checked out the website and the salon looked stylish and modern. A quick phone call later and I had an appointment set for my Tuesday lunch break.   Fast forward to noon today. I couldn't remember the last time I was actually excited for a pedi. Usually, I see them as sometimes-enjoyable/sometimes-painful necessities (for me, anyway). I knew from experience though, that salon-quality treatments are (usually) far superior to those offered at the express places on every corner.   My pedicure with Thom not only met but exceeded my every expectation.   Thom was thorough but delicate, and he even managed to make the steps that sometimes make me squirm uncomfortably just another pleasant part of what was a totally blissful experience overall.   The search for a fab pedicure in an upscale but friendly environment is finally over! I look forward to treating myself well at Salon Soha again soon.

Sometimes, all it takes is hearing a word before I abandon all other thoughts and lust after said item. For example, bubble baths, shoes, wine, eyelash extensions and, most recently, hoagies.   My mom said the word to me on Saturday morning and for the remainder of the weekend, all I could think about was sinking my teeth into turkey, cheese and fresh veggies on a delicious roll. I've been trying to watch what I eat so I came up with a game plan and allowed myself to indulge - but only if I saved half of whatever sandwich awaited for dinner.   I wanted to try a place that was new-to-me, and with a variety of factors to take into consideration, I eventually landed at Jake's. The menu was filled with mostly hot and very pork-heavy offerings, and there were only two choices for cold sandwiches, but both had turkey. I opted for the schmeer: roasted turkey, sharp provolone, baby spinach, red onion, roasted peppers and garlic spread (i.e. mayo) on a long roll. I say I hate mayo but at this point I think I'm just kidding myself. If a mayo-based sauce is called spread or aioli, I'm all in.  I got that bad boy home and, true to my word, wrapped up half and tossed it in the fridge for later. The next ten or so minutes were spent in heaven, if heaven were a sandwich. It was soclose to my favorite turkey sandwich from Paesano's. More field testing is in order.    A note to the owners: the menu on the website is impossible to read! I thought it was just on the iPhone but looking at the site from my laptop yields the same straining, unless you click on the pdf.   Also, for those with extremely large appetites, Jake's has this crazy challenge where if you eat a dump truck's worth of food in less than 45 minutes, you get your food for free (and the indigestion I can only assume comes with) and your picture on the website. If that's your kind of thing.

I really love Gran Caffe L'Aquila. It's sort of become my low-key coffee meeting spot. The vibes are super relaxed in the morning - it feels more like a market in the early hours of the day than a restaurant. You can order coffee at the counter and sit anywhere.   Around lunchtime is when things start picking up and table service kicks off. Last week I had a coffee meeting around 11, but I decided to stick around a little while longer to get some work done and enjoy lunch. I had the chitarra pasta which was tossed with a bright, zesty tomato sauce, guanciale and pecorino cheese. It was perfectly sized and absolutely delicious.   The sandwiches also looked incredible and I would love to try them sometime. But first, I need to make my way through the rest of the pasta menu.

So I've never written a Sweet Lucy's review. Say whaaaa? From my first visit, after a football UYE with yelpers Jim H, Bill M, Dan C, Akshay M and Caroline L, to my experiences with their catering at First Person Arts events, one thing is for certain: Lucy is one smooth southern lady.   Pulled pork, mac and cheese, spicy collards and corn bread - that's all you need to know. If you're planning to eat at the restaurant, bring a crew, bring some brew and grab one of the picnic tables. You're guaranteed to have a great meal and a great time.

A nice restaurant near my hometown has been needed for a long time, and I'm glad the folks from District 611 settled in Riverton. My meal there last night was my last before starting a ten-day detox and I'm happy to report that it was a worthy final supper.   Our server explained the menu and told us that everything was prepared to order, unless we wanted things coursed. Naturally, our small plates arrived first (soft pretzels with cheese sauce and báhn mi spring rolls), but a pizza was dropped almost immediately after. There are two kitchens, the open pizza kitchen and the regular one, but there should be some communication so that pizzas aren't arriving at the same time as small plates. That was my only gripe with the pacing.   Though I wasn't crazy about the cheese sauce with the pretzels, I really liked the pork báhn mi spring rolls, made with shredded Berkshire pork and pickled veggies and served with a cilantro sauce. These were very tasty.   The pepperoni pizza was covered in delicious mozzarella, pepperoni and dollops of ricotta. The crust was definitely soft in the middle, making it more of a fork and knife kind of pizza. I didn't mind because I thought the flavors were really delicious. Brick oven pizza often has a softer crust than traditional pie. As long as it tastes good, I don't mind. This pizza tasted great to me.   We also tried the steak frites, which came out after we had some time to try everything else on the table already. We were between medium and med-rare when ordering and eventually went med-rare. It's a good thing, because the steak arrived closer to a medium to med-well. But, it was still really nice, with pickled red onion and a really inventive watercress sauce. The fries were tasty but would have been better if they were hotter.   District 611 also has some really fun soda options. My skinny cola was very tasty and my boyfriend enjoyed a ginger soda followed by a huckleberry soda. We passed on dessert after our feast but I was more than satisfied at that point. I'm looking forward to returning with my family and am optimistic that it will get even better.

For what it is (cheap and quick), Le Chic Nails is all right.   But I'm a big girl now, and I've moved on to greener pastures, in the form of nicer salons.  Should you choose to make Le Chic Nails a part of your girly upkeep, ask for Pheng. She's a sweetheart and she does a nice job.  (FYI: Cam, the woman from my visits back in '09, no longer works there.)

This local farmers' market is a great place for flowers and fresh produce. The flower selection is vast and includes flats for planting, larger buckets for doorsteps and hanging baskets. I picked up two beautiful hanging baskets this week, one of which contained bright orangey begonias. They also carry seasonal flowers, like tulips and lilies for Easter.   The market always seems to be open during daytime from spring through the fall and prices can't be beat. Well, unless you hit a place like Produce Junction, but I'd rather spend a couple more bucks and shop local.

Gotta give some more love to one of my favorite spots for a quick sandwich and a great place to stock up on some grocery staples! Though I don't get there as often as I'd like simply due to distance from my house, Palm Tree is a must stop anytime I'm in the area.  The chicken salad is still a favorite though I've been opting for tuna lately which is always great. I love that there is always a loaf or two of fresh bread available so I can grab a pint of tuna salad to make lunches at home. Their day-old bags of rolls, bagels and croissants for half price also come in handy. I bring them home, slice them up and throw them in the freezer for whenever I need them.   The snack selection is amazing - I don't know how they manage to pack so many things into such a small store, but Palm Tree carries all of my go-tos, like Pop Chips, Smart Sweets, Tate's and more. Add in the always-friendly service, plus the recent addition of plexiglass barriers between employees and staff, and you've got a five star biz!

For a late Monday morning, this restaurant was surprisingly busy and the staff seemed very frantic. I sat at an open table which I soon realized was sticky from the previous guest and was never wiped down. There were also a lot of flies in the restaurant which was pretty annoying.   My omelet arrived quickly and was just okay - definitely not something I would go out of my way for again. I find my experiences at the other LPQ higher up on Walnut to be pretty consistently solid, and that is my preferred location for sure.

Huge Zoës Kitchen fangirl here! I used to frequent the Cherry Hill location, but now that the Moorestown location has opened it's become my new-go to as I am in the area often.   Everything at this location is just as clean, fresh and delicious as I've come to expect from Zoës. My go-to is the salmon kebabs with tzatziki, side salad and white beans. My husband loves the chicken piadina. I've often ordered the fresh fruit side and it is always a great mix of really delicious fruit. I so appreciate businesses that make it easy to eat healthy  yet heartily, and that is accomplished here.   Last but not least, the staff at this location has been great, particularly the young gent who works weeknights.

Seasons 52 has the best happy hour for a health-conscious person who wants to go up on a Tuesday (or any weekday, for that matter). My friend and I arrived shortly after 5pm and the bar was already packed - we nabbed two of the last remaining seats and promptly ordered some vinho verde. The pours are generous at Seasons 52, and this seems to be the case regardless of the location. I like it.   After trying nearly all of their happy hour bites on previous visits, I know that I'm not super crazy about any of them. So my friend and I ordered a couple flatbreads to share, which are tasty and still pretty low in cals. The pepperoni with pesto was very flavorful while the artichoke and goat cheese was nice and light but still tasty. Will return next time I want some happy hour action before a shopping trip!

Marsha Brown's was recommended by several Yelpers as a solid spot for lunch and I'm really glad we checked it out. As much as I wanted a burger, I opted for the chopped salad. I never imagined I'd crave a salad as much as I have since I finished it yesterday.   The chopped salad contained asparagus, artichoke, broccoli, olives, bacon and blue cheese. It was all mixed together and formed into a mold of sorts. I ordered it with grilled shrimp and the dressing (ranch) on the side. I don't know what made that salad so delicious but all the ingredients together were awesome. And the dressing was absolutely perfect, though I hardly needed any since the salad itself was so flavorful.   We sat at the bar since all tables were booked. The bartender was very friendly but he also had to take care of the nearby tables, so things like place settings and drink refills had to be requested. No big, though. We were taken care of and we really enjoyed ourselves. I will be making plans to return, and hopefully not too far into the future - I need that salad in my life!

Last night, my girlfriends and I enjoyed a very carb-heavy meal at Little Nonna's, and I loved every bite. We had an 8pm reservation and were seated just a few minutes later, after a table was cleared. There's not a whole lot of space going on, so I was happy to be seated in the aisle as opposed to trying to squeeze between tables into the banquette side.   I started with a sgroppino (vodka, prosecco and a scoop of blood orange basil sorbet) - absolutely delightful! Later in the meal I switched to a glass of white wine. It was then that I noticed that all beverages are a flat ten dollars. Good stuff.   Food-wise, we started with the shaved salad. But let's be real. If you're eating at Little Nonna's you aren't looking to be diet-conscious. Don't kid yourself. Skip the salad and save that room for the good stuff. Like the garlic bread, with spreadable roasted garlic. It's even more delicious when dipped into the sauce left over from the pepperoni marinara mussels. In fact, we shamelessly ordered a second round of that delicious bread. The arancini were also a hit at my table, though I thought the insides were a tad dry.   For the main course, we shared three pasta dishes: spaghetti and meatballs (so good, though I typically like a little more sauce on my pasta), fusilli di pretti (surprisingly yet delightfully spicy!), and gnocchi (loved the sear on these little nuggets). Having stuffed ourselves silly with the starters, we ended up with leftovers. Which I got to take home. Happy day!   Dessert was not an option, though I probably would have opted for another sgroppino to finish out the meal if there was just a bit more room (probably for the best that there wasn't). Many thanks to our lovely server, Oren, for putting up with our many questions throughout the meal (I'm still trying to figure out where I know you from!). Can't wait to get back for round two.

Bomb Bomb is every bit the stereotypical South Philly restaurant. Ancient reservations book? Check. Loud, perhaps a-little-too-friendly service? Check. Red sauce? Check. Wine in jugs? Check check.   I passed on the jug wine but gave an enthusiastic hell yes to a lot of the food menu during my visit with friends a few months back. We ordered a bunch of stuff to share, though they were also out of some of the items we requested. Like salad. Weird, right? Nonetheless, our veggie-free meal was still delicious and there were plenty of laughs thanks to the laid back style of the servers and other patrons.   Looking forward to my next visit!

I was a little skeptical when my parents wanted to go to Uno for dinner on Saturday, but who was I to complain while they were footing the bill? I'm glad I kept my mouth shut because we actually had a great experience. We wanted to sit in the bar area which the hostess said we could do, but we had to wait a bit for a table to be cleared. Because of this, I thought that our service would be lackluster once we were seated but we were taken care of completely.   The beer list is great and they offer flights so you can try several types. Troegs bottles are only four bucks during Flyers games, so my stepdad and I took advantage of that. There are several really nice, big TVs in the bar area that were perfect for game-watching. I did wish there was sound on in the bar area, however.   My mom and stepdad both had the steak tips dinner while I went with the honey crisp chicken salad, which was really good. The salad was huge and filled with fresh veggies, crunchy chicken and served with honey mustard dressing on the side as I requested. I was pleasantly surprised by our experience and I'd go back for sure while looking for a brew and bite in the area.

I've always been a fan of the Pistola's restaurants and Pistola's Del Sur is no exception. We popped in after a killer Eagles win with some friends from out of town - San Diego, to be exact. These folks know their tacos.   We shared an order of nachos with beef and the freedom tacos. I think these might be my favorite nachos in Philly. The toppings were adequately dispersed across the chips, and the taste was great. I'm also a huge fan of those freedom tacos and they did not disappoint. The San Diegans were impressed.   Our server, Becca, was incredibly sweet and went out of her way to make us happy. After receiving our order of wings, she recognized right away that the wings were not well-done as we had requested. She swooped them away and we received a plate of well-done wings a few minutes later.   I do agree with Jaime S that the margs are on the sweet side. For this reason, I'll remind myself to stick with beer. They always have a well-balanced menu of crafts and even a couple light options for when you just can't do another heavy brew.   Super pumped about this addition to East Passyunk Ave and looking forward to many more visits.

Just here to add yet another five star review to Philadelphia Distilling's Yelp listing! My husband and I stopped by for pre-concert cocktails and this place did not disappoint! It was my first time there but his millionth (or so). I need to start taking up his invites more often because I've clearly been missing out on some of the city's best spots!   The space is incredibly beautiful and we were lucky to grab the last two open seats at the bar on our visit. The bartenders really know their stuff and the woman who helped us out could not have been more on point. She asked what kind of drinks we like, flavor profiles, etc. and then mixed us up some very tasty concoctions.   Very much looking forward to my next visit!

Ugh, our Philadelphia state liquor stores, am I right? This one was close to where I spent my afternoon working, so I headed in with high hopes of a decent bubbles selection for celebrating my first wedding anniversary. To my surprise, there were several inexpensive but nice enough bottles to choose from. I went with a bottle of Chandon and also a cheap Sauvignon Blanc to go along with our dinner.  This store is one of the old, ugly ones that hasn't yet been remodeled. Where the names of countries on the walls has absolutely nothing to do with the organization of the wines underneath.   Oh, and as other reviewers have mentioned, there was a panhandler. Not outside of the store, IN the actual store. No idea how this happened as there was a security guy at the entrance when I walked in.   Good luck and godspeed.

As most probably know, I tend to dine out more than I dine in. But on the rare occasions that I do feel like holding it down in the kitch, I want to cook with the freshest ingredients possible. Headhouse Farmers Market appeals to both sides of my culinary conundrum.   On the days I want to get crafty, there are loads of fresh produce available. Some veggies I wouldn't even know what to do with. More often than not, I just want to fork over some cash for a prepared product. Luckily for me, Market Day Canele, Renaissance Sausage, Los Taquitos de Puebla and the expensive-but-delicious lemonade stand are there to satisfy. Look for me on the nearby steps, with all the others who go to the Farmers Market just to eat!

I've only been twice, but I really like Lucky 13. My first visit was several years ago for some drinks. Not sure why it took me so long to return but it was selected as our meeting place for Saturday night's shenanigans and it was just right. The bartender was friendly and fast with slinging our drinks. Several rounds ended up costing far less than I anticipated, a welcome respite in this world of fourteen dollar cocktails in which we live.   The music was on point and just loud enough. The TVs were programmed to whatever games were taking place. The bathroom was clean and I especially liked the cool throwback photos adorning the walls (Bridget Bardot - meow!). I've heard the food is surprisingly delicious and I'm looking forward to seeing for myself next time.

I had always heard mixed reviews about Kitchen 233, so even though I've lived in the area for almost three years, I never went out of my way to test the waters.  When my date last Friday suggested the bar there as our backdrop for drinks, I was excited for the opportunity to finally check the place out for myself.    The hostesses were friendly and informed me that there are two bar areas.  Unfortunately, the more open-air bar towards the back was reserved for a private party midway through the evening, so I went directly to the main bar.  I loved the set-up of the entire restaurant, which is very open, yet darkly decorated.  It's unlike any other restaurant in the area and was a chic change.  The happy hour specials included some half priced appetizers and reduced wines by the glass, but we both opted for the Blue Russian, which was a vodka martini with blue cheese stuffed olives.  The glasses were small but the mini shakers were served alongside for another half-pour.  Very nice.  We ordered the sesame seared ahi tuna, spicy rock shrimp and calamari appetizers.  All three were good, not the best ever.  If I were to pick only one of the three to have again it would be the tuna.  Two large flat screen TVs displayed that never-ending, extra-innings Phillies game, which was still a lot less painful to watch than Sidney Crosby holding the Stanley Cup while allegedly blowing off the end-of-game handshake.  (I'm not bitter.  Nope, not me!)  My final drink of the night was the Kitchen Cosmo, which was deliciously light and a perfect summer drink.  Sadly, my head did not agree the following morning when I had to wake up for a 5K race.   I will definitely return for drinks, hopefully on the patio area next time.  The jury is still out on whether I would be up for a dinner experience.

It was well worth the rainy drive to Turnersville to receive the kind of friendly, straightforward service that I was not afforded at another Hyundai dealer closer to where I live.  I worked with a negotiator (who I hired) to handle the details of the purchase of my new car and the trade-in of my old one. He arranged everything with Dave at Hyundai, who was very nice to work with, patiently answering all of my questions and showing me every last detail of my new car. I also received more than I expected for the trade-in of my old vehicle, which was awesome.   The paperwork was pretty straightforward and quick, and there were no surprises. I am thrilled with my new car and with my experience at Hyundai of Turnersville!

This is my new go-to nail place.  I randomly stopped in a few weeks ago on a Monday night and was able to get a pedicure without an appointment.  The employees were all very friendly and welcoming, and my nail tech, Cam, did a great job.  When my service was complete, the owner gave me a card for $5 off on my next visit.  Two weeks later, I returned for a mani and pedi, again with Cam and this time with an appointment.  She again did an excellent job and I was in an out in about an hour.  The salon itself is great because the pedicure chairs all have awesome massage functions and the manicure chairs are comfortable and have wheels (i.e., you don't have to risk ruining your nails by touching the chair).  The decor is cute and very beachy.

After two visits in the past week alone, I am convinced; Triumph Brewery is a magical place where good things happen.  Take last Saturday night, for starters.  My sister decided she had done enough 23rd birthday-celebrating at Mad River (thank god), so we went across the street to Triumph.  I got my pumpkin ale and started people watching when all of a sudden I noticed someone very familiar at the far end of the bar... my favorite Flyer, Mike Richards, and BONUS, Jeff Carter and some other studs from the team!!!  I attempted a discussion with Richards but I'm pretty sure he was questioning my sanity and basic motor skills because I had lost all ability to stay calm and collected.  Still, he was gracious enough to pose for a couple pictures, making my night and possibly my year.  Last night, my guy (the real-life one, not Richards) and I were walking around, trying to find a bar to watch the Phils game, and hopefully one that wouldn't be too crowded.  It seemed highly unlikely that we would be able to do this, but when we arrived at Triumph, two recently vacated bar stools were calling our names.  Again, a pumpkin ale for me and something with a really long name for him.  We also ordered the pizza and truffle fries.  The pizza was bangin' and so were the fries, although I'm not sure what "truffle" had to do with it.  They seemed like plain fries to me, and at only $4, I doubt we were getting any truffle action.  Still, they were piping hot and perfectly salted.    Two cold, crisp honey wheats later, we celebrated the Phillies World Championship.  I'm convinced this is a place of good luck.  I might buy some lottery tickets and go hang out there again this weekend just to see what happens.

I was on the hunt for "saucy" traditional pizza yesterday, and a friend recommended Francoluigi's. I was pumped to see the special - two medium pies for $15 (good on Wednesday, Thursday and Sunday). I ordered the special, plus a caesar salad and a side of marinara for crust-dipping. I was able to pay by card over the phone and was told delivery would be within the hour.   True to their word, my delivery arrived about 45 minutes later. The medium pizzas are on the small side, but perfect for two people to share. While I wouldn't say the pizza was especially saucy, the extra side of marinara I ordered made up for it. If you can wait an extra ten minutes, I'd strongly suggest re-heating slices in the oven for a much-needed crisp. Props to the caesar, which was large and had the most delicious homemade dressing.   We have a second pizza on deck for tonight's dinner and I couldn't be happier about it. Francoluigi's is officially in the rotation for delivery that won't break the bank.

It's Party City, so you pretty much know what to expect walking in. Five stars for being one of the only party supplies stores in the entire city. Minus one star for the check-out process, which always seems to take far longer than it should. God forbid someone in front of you has a return. That's an all hands on deck situation.   There is a great selection of trinkets for every possible occasion or theme. They even carry those tacky cake-toppers where the bride is dragging the groom down the aisle. So there's that. For elaborate or even unique costumes, go elsewhere. Party City carries the same costumes they always have, back since the days you scoured the Halloween circular when you were 12.

Planter's House is a gem in St. Louis. My friend and I went for drinks and dinner and were not disappointed.
