There is a front room that has slightly more of a restaurant feel while the back room is darker and more intimate - it would be an awesome spot to bring a date.    We both started with cocktails which were made with care and heavy on the booze. I switched to wine once the food started to arrive - the bartender gave a very nice pour. We had the marinated olives and a cheese plate to start and I would highly recommend both. I opted for the cioppino for my main and it was very nice - the toast that was lathered in aioli was perfect for broth dipping. I was powerless against those carbs.   We passed on dessert though a quick look at the menu would suggest maybe that was a mistake. A homemade "twicks" bar? Someone please get that and report back.

First time home buying is scary! Luckily, we were hooked up with an amazing agent who walked us through every single step of the process. I cannot say enough good things about Bryan Capone.   At our first meeting, Bryan sat down with us for well over an hour to discuss what we were looking for and describe the home-buying process. From there, we worked with the folks from Trident Mortgage, who share the office, for our pre-approval.   Once pre-approved we started receiving listings from Bryan on the daily. We spent the better part of a couple Saturday afternoons driving around with Bryan to look at properties in which we were interested. We revisited properties, talked about their pros and cons to death, asked a million questions and, through it all, Bryan was extremely patient, always honest and helpful and never pushy. He asked smart questions that often helped us find our own answers.   After we found our home and reached an agreement on price, the mortgage process with Trident began. I'm an extremely organized person so even though the list of required documents was daunting, I was able to quickly PDF everything, throw it in a zip file and send it along.   Everyone told me to expect a frustrating experience with the mortgage process, but our experience with Trident was at times very frustrating. We worked with a handful of people, which probably contributed to some of the confusion: lost paperwork that we had mailed in using their pre-addressed, postage-paid envelopes (the envelope was later found, thankfully), repeated requests for documents we had already sent, and general disorganization. It's amazing that people can actually hold down their jobs while trying to secure a mortgage - everyone who warned me that it would be a huge headache and very stressful process was not kidding.  Finally, closing day came. Signing boatloads of papers was actually a joy because it meant the whole long process was coming to an end! Getting the keys to our new home was one of the best moments of my life.   There are still some minor things with our home that have to be taken care of by the seller, and Bryan has been great about keeping in touch and keeping us in the loop. After all is said and done, I'd definitely recommend Bryan to anyone in the market for a new home. Since this review is technically for the real estate side and not the mortgage side, I'm going with five stars. However, if you have a recommended mortgage broker, perhaps you'd like to shop around instead of defaulting to the in-house.

My first experience at Triumph was for a networking event over a year ago.  We were situated in the upstairs area, which got extremely crowded considering the size of the group, but the staff handled the event really well from what I remember.  I always wanted to go back but sort of forgot about the place.  A few nights ago I found myself back at Triumph for an after dinner drink.  The bar area was somewhat crowded, but we managed to get two bar stools at the far end of the bar.  Now, me being 5'10" and my companion being 6'3", I'm fairly certain the bartender noticed us.  It's hard to miss two giraffes.  Yet, I could have fit a nap in during the time we waited for him to come over.  When he finally did get to us, his attitude was pretty beat and I was afraid it was going to rub off on me.  I quickly ordered a raspberry beer and was told that the menu I was referring to was old.  Ooookay.  I was handed a new menu and chose the pumpkin ale (which was absolutely delicious, by the way).  When my beer runneth over -- literally, all over the bar-- upon being placed in front of me, I watched as a small river made it's way slowly but surely towards my body.  It was impossible to miss but the bartender peaced out.  With not a napkin in sight, my companion gracefully took the clean-up rag from the bar area and saved the day.    I will definitely be back soon for some more of that pumpkin ale, and I hope for a better experience so I can bump up my rating, because I do really like the place.

I had the best day at Linvilla with my mom and grandmom! My sister has been raving about her fall and winter trips to Linvilla for the past couple of years, so we decided to see what the fuss was about. We didn't really go in with many expectations, which worked in our favor. I was really impressed by the grocery selection and also the craft market.   A local wine and cider company was there doing tastings, so we tried a few things and decided to purchase a bottle of dry cider - delicious! We ended up grabbing a couple more bottles on our way out to go with Thanksgiving dinner. We did the hayride, which was fun, though once was probably enough for me. It was a cute tour and I was very impressed by the large array of fruits and vegetables available at this farm!   After that, we enjoyed some snacks from the grocery store, before heading over to check out the animals. There are deer, goats, sheep, and tons of different birds. Very fun to see and kids would love it. We ended our day by swinging through the craft market. All Halloween items were marked down to either 50% or 75% off, so I grabbed some decorations at a total steal.   I may have to tag along on my sister's winter visit!

I liked everything about this coffee shop, to be quite honest. There was plenty of available seating on a weekday morning, the ac was kicking on what was an unseasonably hot day, and I had a pretty view of 13th and Pine. The cherry on top? La Colombe is the house brew. I was quite content during my almost two hour visit.   The baristas were nice, and I was able to start a tab since I was expecting someone to meet me a bit later. They also take credit cards! Before leaving I ended up ordering a chicken salad sandwich on ciabatta to go. If that wasn't the best chicken salad I've had in a long time. It was awesome! I'll definitely add The Last Drop to my rotation for those days when I need to get out of the house to work or take a meeting.

I used to be charmed by La Viola, but as Catherine L. points out, it is a "BYOB for beginners."   Last month, I arrived early to a 7 p.m. reservation on a Saturday night. The reservation was in one of my girlfriend's names, but the hostess searched in vain to find it. Eventually, I was told "that's okay" and I was seated at a tiny four top by the window. I was happy that our placement by said window meant that we would only be sitting on top of each other, versus the other diners, but I hated feeling like I had gotten the second degree as though we didn't really have a reservation.   When my friends arrived, servers bustled around us to open wine bottles and drop warm bread. For starters, we ordered mussels in the two different ways they were being offered, as well as an antipasto salad. I skipped the mussels and stuck with the salad, which was nicely sized and served over a tangy vinaigrette.   By the time our mains came along, I'll admit I was pretty hopped up on wine. I had ordered a chicken and shrimp dish, which came with veggies and potatoes. Perhaps it was a bit gauche, but when one of the servers came over to offer fresh Parmesan, I accepted. "You want cheese... on your chicken?" the waiter smirked. I tried to reverse my decision, but the waiter gave me my cheese, as I sat there feeling admonished.   I thought the food was good, but it certainly wasn't anything to rave about. There wasn't anything about the experience that made me feel like La Viola should come up in the rotation more frequently, if at all. The most redeeming part of the meal was the price. We got out of there for less than $25 per person, including tax and tip, although we skipped dessert.   This is the place you send your college-aged cousin who wants a dinner in the city experience on a budget.

Kraftwork is Sidecar's Northern sibling. The beer list is great, and you can see what's on deck after any particular keg is kicked. The look of the bar is industrial and a lot of the materials were salvaged and re-used, which makes for a cool space.   We stopped by for some beers and a bite on a Sunday afternoon. The bartender was nice enough to let us sample a couple different beers while we made our decisions. We shared the beer can chicken sandwich, which was pretty tasty. The bun is really big and it's easier to just eat the thing open-faced. The fries that came with were delish and especially good with the mustard dipping sauce. The parmesan truffle popcorn was a bit of a let-down. Definitely not as good as the version at Royal. But probably a lot healthier.   I wouldn't go out of my way for Kraftwork, and that's probably because I'm lucky enough to have Sidecar around the corner from my apartment. But when in Fishtown, it's a solid choice.

My friend suggested M Restaurant for happy hour. I had never been and was interested in checking out somewhere new-to-me. The bar was pretty full on a Wednesday evening but we managed to snag a high top. There was also live music which was a nice touch, though at times it got a little loud in the small space.   There are a few different options for happy hour food and drinks. We stuck with glasses of wine, which were four dollars. We also ordered a charcuterie plate, which came with five or six different types of salami, and a cheese plate with three different types of cheese. Both plates were generously portioned and came with the appropriate accoutrements. Best of all, each offering was delicious! We had several glasses of wine and our total at the end of the night was just over fifty bucks. What a steal!    There was a single bartender who handled everyone in the bar with a little bit of help from a server. She was spread a little thin at times but we still received everything we ordered in a reasonable amount of time. My friend says happy hour in the garden outside during the warmer months is must-do, and I'll absolutely check that out if I'm not back there sooner for another trip to the bar.

Very very solid Thai delivery last night via Yelp! This was our first time ordering from Ratchada and the only thing that was disappointing was the delivery itself. We received our order about a half hour after the original hour that it was promised, and only after contacting Eat24 for an update.  Aside from the long delivery wait, everything else was on point. We ordered a Thai beef salad, which was really nice. The veggies were crisp, the beef was tender and nicely seasoned, and there was a spicy kick. I ordered the pad si-ew with shrimp, which was delicious. There was enough to split into two meals! My husband had the pork jungle - great flavors, though he said the pork was a little tough. He also had a lot of leftover veggies, which I tossed into my pad si-ew leftovers for lunch today. Possibly even better on day two! We'll be ordering from Ratchada again.

Paging Blake F, paging Blake F!   Satellite Café screamed "hippy" from the moment I walked up the path to the front door to the moment I walked out.   Needing a little caffeine boost after dinner at Dock Street, I meandered over to the establishment next door. The entrance was set back, so we had to walk through a cute little garden/patio area.   The café had dim lighting and lots of random decorations (think free trade coffee bean sacks hanging from the rafters, etc.) I ordered a latte and the dude at the counter looked at me and said "soy milk?" I shook my head and asked for skim, which they did have.   As my drink was being prepared, I noticed that many, if not most, of the sweets in the pastry case were vegan. They looked really good!  I knew better than to expect any Sweet'N Low or other artificial sweeteners, and there seemed to be just white sugar or honey to choose from (I was surprised that I didn't see any raw sugar). I did squeal at the pretty flower in the foam as I popped on the lid, so that I could take my latte home and doctor it up with my fake sugar.   I'd like to go back to check out the food sometime, and I'm willing to bet that I'll be with Blake when I do.

While I'm keeping my rating for Misconduct at three stars, I can now say they are three very robust, shiny stars when compared with the three hesitant stars from my previous review.   After a very late night on the town, I was in need of food in my belly and a little hair of the dog action. My lunch buddy and I were ushered past Misconduct's long bar, its seats full with construction workers who looked but kept their traps shut. Clearly, lunching indoors as opposed to on a wall somewhere has a different set of decorum.   My bloody Mary served as the life raft in my hangover sea, and my grilled chicken Caesar salad was perfectly dressed, with tender, grilled chicken and a thrilling excess of croutons. It was just what I needed to right my ship.

I like Green Line Cafe so much more than I liked Lovers and Madmen (sorry, fans of L&M). The entire space looks like it had a face-lift. The café feels cleaner and updated and it's now a great place for a business meeting or just a quiet place to get some work done. There aren't too many food options so maybe don't go there hungry or expecting much variety, but the coffee does the trick.

These guys are open late for all your drunken (food) desires. After my sister's bachelorette party shenanigans, it was pretty unanimous that everyone wanted/needed something greasy to sop up the cocktails. I gave our limo driver the address for Sonny's and we were whisked to cheesesteak heaven.   We must have arrived just before the bars closed because there were only a couple other people there. I'm sure this place gets slammed at 2am. Everyone received their orders pretty quickly. Back in the limo, I immediately regretted not adding some fries to my order. I nabbed a few from my sister's friend and they were some of the hottest, crispiest, tastiest spuds around. From what I recall, my whiz wit was pretty solid as well.   We were pretty tuned up when we arrived and the guys behind the counter were so nice. They must have the patience of saints, because I can only imagine what they deal with every weekend.

Let's talk about the awesome experience I had at Zahav last night.   It may have been Restaurant Week, but it was still business as usual at Zahav. Everything was seamless, from our party of six being seated as soon as everyone arrived, to our service, to the drinks and the food.   I've dined at Zahav before, but after dining with a group of friends, I can easily say the experience is heightened when you have more to share. Our table was covered with food at all times, but these are the bites I tried for myself:   -salatim and hummus with laffa (Delicious. I even enjoyed beets and fennel. Impossible!) -fried cauliflower  -fried potatoes with shishito peppers -figs with feta and crispy eggplant -crispy haloumi -grape leaves -kofte (ground beef and lamb meatballs) -branzino served over rice and tzatziki (Fantastic!) -chocolate konafi  I would order any and all of these items again. The food was spectacular! My server was also able to suggest a wine that would pair well with everything I ordered (a dry riesling).   After everything, we were given ten dollars off cards for a future visit to either Zahav or Percy Street Barbecue. I can't wait for my next Zahav tasting. With friends.

My family hosted an event here over the weekend in the private wine cellar downstairs. I'll preface this review by saying that not everyone (my parents, who were paying the check) was happy with how things went. My parents felt that our service was too slow and they were annoyed that there was only one server working our entire party of twenty-something people. We did have a table full of kids with us so I can see how they might have had a different perspective.   But from my table with my brother, sister and our significant others, things were great. We don't all get together as often as we'd like so there's always a lot to talk about and time flies. Which is probably why we never noticed or were bothered by the length of time our dinner took (more than three hours). I felt that drinks were refreshed in a timely manner and our server never seemed to forget anything. There was a little bit of a wait between salad and the main course, and the time it took to cut and serve the cake at the end of the meal was definitely way too long.   That said, the drinks were solid. Nice wine pours and a great selection of beers. When we sat down, trays of Italian meats and cheeses were available for snacking. The bread course, with awesome tomato bread, made everyone happy. Salads were a little salty, but main courses were really great. I had chicken parmesan but my boyfriend's red snapper was awesome. Aside from the cake we brought, we were also served trays of miniature desserts, which were better than expected.   I'm surprised I never had dinner at Lamberti when I still lived in Jersey. The place is huge and was totally packed. I wouldn't hesitate to go back again with friends, but I'd definitely make a reservation pretty far in advance.

Last night, I dreamt I went to a crazy, no-holds-barred, Jersey shore-themed party... only it took place in one of Philly's classiest, most heralded restaurants, Zahav. The large, bright space was cleared of its tables, and all of the staff members were transported from a late 80s Def Leppard concert, with big hair and stonewashed denim as far as the eye could see. When I glanced into the open kitchen area, I almost pinched myself (but didn't because then I would have had to wake up). There stood some of Philadelphia's most notorious chefs, elbow to elbow, preparing delicious renditions of Jersey shore staples such as juicy hamburgers, spicy pizza turnovers, garlicky fried clams and savory crab boils. To wash it all down? Miller Lite and Miller High Life pounders, sold straight out of a wheeled ice bucket, natch. The pièce de résistance? A Journey cover band that also dedicated plenty of play time to Jersey boys Jon Bon Jovi and Bruuuuuuce.   This morning, after turning off the alarm and sleepily sitting up in bed, I noticed the blue stamp on my hand. The epic party from my dreams was real!!!

The availability of solid coffee options from the adjoined Milkboy and a really nice selection of snacks are just the icing on the cake at Bryn Mawr Film Institute. What really sets the place apart from other theaters is the small, hometown vibe and interesting selections.  Last night, I attended a preview screening of Race to the Bottom of the Earth, which starred Todd Carmichael of La Colombe. The screening was presented by First Person Arts, and after the movie, there was a Q&A with Todd which brought a very personal touch to an intense documentary.   Regarding the aesthetics of the theater itself, everything appeared clean and well-maintained, but seats were ancient and a bit uncomfortable. A minor detail but one that will sneak up after two plus hours of sitting.   It isn't often that I get out to the burbs of PA, but I would definitely go out of my way to see a film at Bryn Mawr Film Institute again.

Mainland Inn is a gem in Harleysville, PA. My fiancé and I were fortunate enough to enjoy a complimentary dinner on a beautiful Friday night just before their head chef, Ezra, left the restaurant to pursue other adventures. Based on what we witnessed from our seats at the chef's counter, the restaurant is being left in good hands. The kitchen was firing on all cylinders during our nearly three hour meal. Also, I've never seen a kitchen so organized and tidy, which greatly appealed to my Type A sensibilities.   We were informed at arrival that we would be treated to the chef's tasting. To be completely honest, I'm iffy on chef's tastings because I'm somewhat picky, mostly about proteins. I mentioned a few of my aversions to our server, who was fantastic throughout our meal. She was also spot on with her wine recommendations.     The tasting is several hearty courses and we were each served different plates for each course so it was fun to share. Standouts for me were the bluefish and caviar (one of three relishes that were presented), garlic vichyssoise which was simply excellent, the agnolotti and gnocchi dishes, and the salmon and halibut dishes. Also, the desserts were extraordinary. One was a spin on an affogato and the other was a spring pea soufflé that was creative and fun.   It's rare that we get out to the 'burbs for a meal since we live in the city, but every so often it's fun to go on a little adventure. Mainland Inn is worth the journey.

Still very much enamored with Francoluigi's. Since my last review, I've had a couple slices at the restaurant, and another delivery experience. I loved that I was able to enjoy a Peroni with my slices at the tables by the front counter. I'd like to have a meal in the dining room sometime.   Recently, I was craving baked ziti so we placed a delivery order. Again, you can't beat delivery for a dollar and the ability to pay by card over the phone, including your driver's tip in your payment.   Their caesar salad was still incredible, and I loved the garlic knots that were included. Two orders of baked ziti for two is more than enough for two meals. I stuck one of the ziti trays in the freezer for another day. Francoluigi's uses more of a rosé sauce in their ziti, while I would have preferred a more acidic red sauce. I was glad I once again asked for a side of marinara. When I heat my extra ziti, I'll be adding some tomato sauce to the top for a little more bite.

What's that? You've waited until the last minute and you still don't have a costume for Halloween?   I can hardly judge. I was in the same boat until Wednesday, and the only reason I'm giving you all a heads-up about Pierre's is because I've got my awesome costume safely hanging on my closet door.   I arrived on a Wednesday evening and the store was surprisingly quiet considering Halloween was just a week away. After chatting with my consultant (I cannot remember her name but she was so sweet and helpful), I met the owner, Rich, and we got to talking. The next thing you know, we were exchanging business cards and I was getting a full tour of the warehouse. Oh yes, the warehouse. What you see when you step into Pierre's is like a drop in the bucket compared to what's going on "in the back." I'm talking rows of clothing from floor to very-tall ceiling. No costume request is too obscure.   Back at the dressing rooms, I tried on a handful of costumes but I knew I hadn't found the one. My consultant went back to the warehouse for a bit and when she came back, she had something totally unique. With her help, I zipped, snapped and secured myself into the perfect Halloween costume for Yelp's Night By The Nile (shameless plug!).   Pro tip: Pierre's is open until 8pm in the days leading up to Halloween. Do yourself a favor and go on a weeknight, if possible, because the weekends are bound to be totally cray.

I loved swinging by this cute beer garden in Fishtown over the weekend! There were a variety of beers on tap and a couple kombuchas by Baba's Brew that were made specifically for Tired Hands. I tried the purple one and, unfortunately, found it a little too tart/vinegary for my tastebuds. I'm fairly choosy about the kombuchas I like so don't let that dissuade you if you're a fan!   There's lots of seating all around the perimeter of the garden and the space is really cute overall. The bouncer was hilarious and the staff working the beer trailer were very nice. Definitely a great summer stop if you're in the area!

Sometimes I dismiss Lord & Taylor as sort of a mom store but I have to say that they really came through for me before my recent trip to Mexico. I went to Nordstrom to check out the swimsuits and was wildly disappointed in the selection. I called my mom in despair and she told me she had seen a pretty big variety at Lord & Taylor and she offered to meet me there (Moms. They are the best!).   Before long, I had an armful of swimwear and was headed to the dressing rooms. There were also loads of cute cover-ups as well. I left the store a little poorer but a whole lot happier. Definitely going to give Lord & Taylor another look next time the occasion arises!

Stuck in jury duty and with the Flower Show in town, Reading Terminal Market was no place to be at lunch time. I hightailed it to Maggiano's, where I hoped I could grab a seat at the bar and a reasonably healthy lunch.   As luck would have it, there was one open bar stool. I ordered an iced tea and the chopped salad with chicken. In the meantime, I received a bread basket with olive oil and spices - this helped take the edge off.   My salad arrived soon after and I have to say, it really hit the spot. This salad was huge but I ate every last bite. The dressing was delicious and not too heavy-handed. The chicken was tender. My only complaint would be that the tomatoes were hard. I wish restaurants would omit tomatoes when they aren't in season because, more often than not, they're just sad.   Lunch was pretty steep at nearly $23 plus tip, but it was worth it since I avoided the insane crowds at RTM.

I saw Kevin's review and couldn't pass up the chance to throw my two cents in also.  My family has had many dinners here for special occasions such as milestone birthdays and high school and college graduations.  Despite always having a reservation, we usually have to wait a little while for our table.  Understandable, since the place is always packed on weekends.  My grandfather usually just leads everyone in a round of drinks at the bar.    Once seated, the service ranges from pretty good to great.  As mostly everyone has mentioned, the chicken parm is huge and delicious.  We always have leftovers.  Somehow, after the rounds of bread, salad and entrees, we soldier on for the best part of the meal--strawberry and vanilla ice cream crepes.  Two or three orders will easily feed a group of 10.    Georgine's definitely isn't a spot I would think to go normally, but for an affordable family dinner, it's a great choice.

We've had our eye on Alma del Mar ever since watching their story on Queer Eye a few months back. Finally made it in for a late breakfast this morning and had a great experience!   The outdoor patio is really cute and tables are very spaced out. There aren't too many places to sit and eat in the Italian Market but Alma del Mar is right in the middle of all the action, while still being tucked away from the street. There are signs at the front of the patio with all of the Covid precautions the restaurant is taking and requesting of their customers. There was hand sanitizer on our table and everyone we encountered was wearing masks properly.   After checking out our menus, my husband and I both decided on huevos rancheros. Plus a trifecta of water, coffee and OJ. The OJ was fresh squeezed and tasted great. The coffee was awesome, too.   We were presented with enormous servings of huevos rancheros and we each left about half of the dish behind. On a future visit, we'd probably order one to share plus something else from the menu. Looking forward to next time!

Did you know you can get six packs to go at David's? Well, you can. Nothing fancy, but they do have Tsingtao, which kind of works for whatever it is you're doing in Chinatown.   I haven't tried the food, but after witnessing the take-out orders and hearing the phone blow up, I'm looking forward to a visit. Of course, I'll update my review accordingly at that time.

So happy to see the former Kanella space back in action as Kanella Grill. This iteration is casual and has a short menu with kebab and shawarma pitas and platters, plus a few side items.   My friend brought a bottle of rosé, which was promptly put on ice, and we received a cup of flavorful olives. We started with the chips and tzanziki - a huge bowl of seasoned, hot and crispy fries that is an absolute steal at four bucks.   My entree was the chicken kebab platter with rice and extra tomato salad in place of pita. It was great, and I loved the little cup of tahini that was served with the dish.  We were too full for dessert but I will be partaking in the baklava at some point in the future!

Until last Wednesday evening, I had never been to Swift Half, let alone the Piazza, despite being a Good Dog fanatic.  The bar was quiet, with only the booths occupied when I arrived.  I selected a high top near the jukebox and surveyed the surroundings.  The square room had high ceilings, dark wood paneling, a bar on one side, flat screen TVs, a row of booths and some regular and high top tables.  Some generic art decorated the walls and modern light fixtures hung from the rafters.  Despite the accents, the bar seemed a little sterile, but that was my overall vibe of the Piazza in general.    The lackluster décor was eclipsed by the friendly staff and great eats.  I was famished, so I ordered a Bells Two Hearted and fried pickles, a $2 special.  They arrived in no time and, I'm not going to lie; the thought of polishing them off and hiding the evidence before my friend joined me crossed my mind.  I somehow managed to save her a couple, as I sat on my hands in the meantime.  When Blake F. showed her lovely face, she agreed that the pickles were delish.  We went on to order a cheeseboard, which was nicely presented and very fairly priced.  For dinner, I had the pounded curry chicken sandwich, topped with sautéed spinach, plum tomatoes and goat cheese.  I should have taken a cue from Blake and boxed up my second half but I just couldn't bring myself to stop.  A glutton for punishment, I tell you.  Fortunately, with my tummy stuffed, I couldn't do too much damage on the heaping pile of fries that came with my sandwich.    The quiet refuge of Swift Half ended up being the perfect locale for our night of girl talk and world domination planning.  I'll certainly return, but I look forward to the warmer months which will surely bring out more of a crowd.

After weeks of bridesmaid dieting, the day after my friend's wedding all I wanted was margaritas and nachos. Loco Pez was the perfect setting for this indulgent affair. The bar is bright and fun. The holographic Jesus picture and various random decorations are great.   Margaritas are solid and the nachos are huge and loaded with toppings. Apparently the happy hour is pretty sweet so we'll definitely return for that. Be sure to bring cash or your debit card to hit the ATM!

I am thrilled to have a large Lou Lou boutique in Philadelphia! I've been a fan since a friend introduced me to this place years ago in DC. There are several locations in that area and I am always sure to stop by at least one when I'm in town. When I saw the signage pop up right here on 13th Street a few months back, I was stoked!  My recent visit was for a specific reason, but of course I left with way more than I planned. I wanted a placeholder ring for an upcoming vacation so that I don't run the risk of losing my good bling while participating in water sports and such. Call me paranoid, but I'd rather be safe than sorry! There were several options and I am happy with the simple but classy band I purchased for a cool $18.   In addition, I grabbed novelty sunglasses, a scarf, and a cover-up/kaftan that I'm absolutely loving. It's a good thing they have a loyalty card - my purchases are going to add up quickly!

I had plans to spend the better part of a day in KOP, and I didn't have to think too long or hard about where I'd have lunch. I arrived around 1:30 and the restaurant was pretty emptied out from the lunch crowds by that point. I ordered a salad with chicken (half and half on the dressings, which were served on the side) and a side of chickpea masala, since I was extra hungry.   I had just enough time to get my beverage (love that big Coke machine because sparkling Dasani is my jam) and all the little side sauces before my order was up. The salad plus side was plenty for a super hearty lunch and kept me full until dinner. The Choolaah salad has so much going on, flavor-wise, that not much dressing is even needed. I love the unique flavors and textures; there's a ton going on in this dish! The chicken was plentiful, super tender and delicious.   For a fast casual restaurant, the food at Choolaah exceeds every expectation. Great concept and I can't wait for my next visit!

I took a chance and ordered some delivery from Mole Poblano, a restaurant unfamiliar to me until I came across it on Eat24 and saw the really high rating. Normally, Mexican food does not travel well, but I was dying for something different from my usual sushi/Mediterranean/rice bowl lineup.   I ordered the chicken enchiladas in red sauce, no cheese or sour cream (in an attempt to keep the meal semi-healthy). Since I didn't hit the minimum required for ordering, I also got some guacamole.   The delivery arrived within the promised window and by a friendly delivery guy. Not only was the food packaged well, it looked fresh and appetizing and came exactly as I requested. The portion was enormous and more than enough for one full meal and another smaller meal. Everything tasted great and not at all heavy or oily. The guac was some of the best I've had in Philly. Definitely a fan and looking forward to trying more!

I'd give them an extra half-star, but since that's not possible I tend to round down when making my final decision.  Service is hit or miss-- our guy last night rocked it out and didn't hesitate to switch my beer when I wasn't crazy about my first choice.    The food is your typical bar fare.  I've had a jerk chicken sandwich here that was the bomb, and hummus that tasted like it came out of a plastic container from Acme.     Since the jalapeno poppers don't come with a warning, heed mine: give those little bitches time to cool, or you WILL burn your mouth upon taking your first bite.  The pain will be so severe that it will likely cause uncontrollable drooling and possible God sightings.

Just thinking back on my limited experiences at this establishment gives me the creeps.  At the time, I worked at a nearby law firm and this was a favorite for support staff members and alcoholic attorneys alike (sorry for blowing up anyone's spot).  It is one of those places that you sneak off to for lunch to have a beer or four, and if you see anyone from work, you silently acknowledge them and immediately forget that you saw them there.  So I guess it's cool that this unspoken code exists.    However, the place is downright nasty.  Cobwebs hang in the corners and every surface has that sticky feel to it.  You know what I'm talking about.  Mace's Crossing is as close to a dungeon as you can possibly get in the middle of Center City.

Great experience at Pokeworks last week! I was in the area for meetings and this came as a suggestion for a healthy lunch. I selected the spicy ahi bowl but customized my order with a bunch of add-ons. The employees were so friendly and patient while I made my selections. I also received 10% off my order, I think because I was a first timer. I'd definitely return when in the area.

Good things come to those who wait. And wait. And wait some more. I was thrilled when rumors of an opening started swirling last week, but I avoided opening weekend like the plague. Living right around the corner combined with the luxury of working from home, I knew there would be plenty of opportunities to eat at Honey's on the reg.   My friend and I stopped in for lunch today, and the first thing I noticed was how much larger and more spacious this new location is compared with the original. I love the bright, open layout.   Within seconds, I had water and a cup of coffee. Our server was on his game the entire time, and he was also super patient when it took about three rounds of him stopping by before we finally made up our minds with what to order. I tried the turkey burger with cheddar and it was delicious. I struggled to finish every last bite (must. not. waste. food. -button pop-) and I didn't even order an extra side or anything. That was one helluva sandwich. I loved the coleslaw that came alongside - it was more tangy than mayo-ish.   I've always ordered the same two or three things at Honey's since I get over there so rarely. But now, with a Honey's in the 'hood, I'm about to work my way through the whole damn menu. Fat kids unite!

Misconduct isn't my bar of choice, but when the group decides to roll there I don't put up a fight, either.  Truth be told, it's a very solid choice for sports fans.  I have enjoyed several Flyers games at the bar, one of which was during the snowpocolypse last winter.  Last night I watched the Phils sweep the Reds, with lots of other excited fans.  There are loads of TVs and each has a sign that states which station/game will be showing.  The boat interior decor is a little strange, and I hate that the bathrooms are downstairs.  The good thing is, the bar doesn't tend to overcrowd so it isn't too difficult to get seating.    The food is hit or miss for me.  A grilled veggie plate on one visit was surprisingly great, while an order of chicken tenders were totally boring.  Said tenders had hardly any breading and bordered on the undercooked side, plus the serving was skimpy.  Fries are good if they arrive hot (not entirely likely) and I've heard good things about the onion rings although I can't attest to this myself.  Some people rave about the burger but the bite I tried last night didn't impress me.  It was very salty and too charred.    The Phils game specials were a little weak: $3 Kenzinger drafts or Sly Fox cans.  I was in more of a martini mood so I went with the double chocolate, off the menu.  It was fantastic, but the unlisted price came as a shock once we got the bill - two of those bad boys came to $21.  Come on.  We're drinking in a faux boat here!  Happy hour has them for half off, so I'll have to get my fix from 5 - 7, M - F in the future... but only if a game is scheduled because this isn't the place I'm hanging for any other reason.

I was referred to this practice by a friend and had a positive experience overall during my first visit in February. The waiting room was clean and inviting, and there were plenty of current magazines.   My cleaning was very thorough and I liked the dental hygienist - I wish I could remember her name! She did a great job and my teeth felt shiny and new after she was through. She also gave me a couple tips for how to care for my sensitive teeth, which was appreciated.   The dentist was fairly quick as most dentists are, but I had a positive experience with her as well. I'm so happy to have found a new dental practice in my area that takes my insurance and makes me feel comfortable!

West Elm is responsible for furnishing and decorating several areas of my house. Even when we shop around for certain pieces, my man and I usually return to West Elm for the final purchase. We love the place so much we registered there (super pumped over that, by the way)! Setting up said registry could not have been easier; you download an app and start scanning right from your phone!    This particular location is gorgeous and I've heard it's one of their biggest showrooms. There are always a lot of employees and it's pretty easy to find someone to help when you have a question. I have also had employees go out of their way to make sure I had a good experience. I once had a discount card I wanted to apply towards an expensive rug, but I didn't read the fine print, which included some extra hoops to go through before receiving the discount. West Elm still honored the offer anyway, no hoop jumping required. Happy, loyal customer here!

Wow, fancy schmancy. My very first visit (and definitely not my last) to Le Bar Lyonnais was a great one. Although I was only there for one drink with a business contact, I left with a very positive impression.   Walking up to Le Bec Fin's door, I hesitated. I wasn't sure if I should try for the door or ring the bell, as I had heard in the past that the door was kept locked and ringing was required. I went for the door and it turned out to be open. A hostess led me down a flight of stairs into the bar area. My boots sunk into the plush carpet and my inner diva swooned.   My slightly dirty martini tasted like mermaid tears, even after Georges walked through the empty bar area, glanced over and made a flagrant remark about our selections. I wasn't sure if he was referring to my martini, my companion's diet coke, or both. I was actually just happy to be acknowledged by a Philadelphia icon (he was actually quite gracious when we were introduced, although I delighted in seeing his famous personality come to life as he paced back and forth through the room).   I eagerly look forward to my next visit.

Based on my fellow yelper's reviews, I may have visited Tastebuds on an off day. In a desperate hunt for coffee this morning, I emerged from my lair and made my way down the street. All of the nearby establishments were closed (Mondays made worse!), and I eventually stumbled upon Tastebuds.   As I had zero dollars in my wallet, I was happy to see the credit card sign on the door. Then I found out about the $10 minimum. It was close enough to lunch time, so I decided to grab a wrap and call it a day. When my order rang up about .40 under $10, I added a chocolate chip blondie to the growing pile.   At home, the coffee was kickin' and I powered through the rest of the morning. But when I unwrapped my wrap for lunch, I was met with some seriously dry chicken. Half remains in my fridge for when I reach afternoon hangriness, in which case anything edible will suffice.  A few bites of the blondie were not much better - it was probably a lot tastier several days ago.   Hopefully this was just a bad day, because I love supporting the cute local markets that are scattered all over the city. I did notice an ice cream counter while there, so at the very least I'll be returning to hit that up on a warm day!

Exhausted and in search of additional sustenance, Mexican comfort food seemed to be calling after the epic dance party I had just been part of. Our group of three walked through El Rey's doors and were greeted with the overwhelming aroma of coffee; perfectly fitting for the space formerly known as Midtown Diner IV.   We started with a round of drinks; margaritas for the ladies and a Yakima Glory served in a miniature boot for the guy. The margs were tasty, but it was already late in the game for me and I ended up leaving about half behind. It was good eats I was mainly after.  We started with guacamole and salsa, which came to a grand total of $13.50 all together. (Sidebar: I simply cannot have guacamole without salsa, so ordering both was a no-brainer, even though I felt a bit swindled. Just because all the high-end Mexican spots are charging this much doesn't make it right.) The chips served alongside are the super thick kind similar to ones I've had in Mexico.   Modest prices on all other menu items made the guacamole inflation an afterthought. I ordered chicken quesadillas and was quite pleased. They arrived quickly and tasted great; not super heavy but totally satisfying. My amigos were more than happy with their tamales and mushroom quesadillas. Portions weren't huge but that's just fine with me. On a super hungry night, I'd probably order the same and maybe throw in another dish to share or an app.  The brunch menu intrigues; I will return for another showdown.

Last night I attended Brat Productions' double feature at Underground Arts. It was kick-off night of the Philly Fringe Festival, a first for me. We saw Popsicle's Departure, 1989 and Eternal Glamnation (both were awesome, by the way).   But since this review is about Underground Arts, I'll try to stay focused. I'd only passed by the place in my car before, usually after a stop at the nearby Trestle Inn. I knew next to nothing about the venue, and I arrived a few minutes before showtime wondering if there would be a bar. There was, and (even better!) I actually had some cash in my wallet (the bar is cash-only). I was surprised to discover that all beers, including bottles and a small-yet-tight list of drafts, were only five bucks. Mixed drinks were six. Even more surprising? There was also a small food menu -and the stuff I saw people eating looked decent.   People milled around the bar which is actually in the main stage area before the first show, which took place in a smaller, more intimate studio. The second show was back in the more casual main room. I liked that the audience was encouraged to grab drinks during the show and that it wouldn't disrupt the actors. It turned out, parts of the show actually took place at the bar.   To top it all off, the bathrooms were clean.    I look forward to my next visit, and I'm going to make an effort to add more alternative live arts programs to my life!

I finally made it to North Bowl for a happy hour that extended well into the evening on St. Patty's Day. We hung out at the bar upstairs, which was relatively quiet until around 7 or 8pm. Our bartender was fantastic and I was an instant fan of her blackberry bourbon smash cocktail. Woooo, that was some potent sipping!   Eventually, it was time to grab some food and I loved the buffalo chicken salad, which I requested with ranch dressing instead of the balsamic and thousand island dressings that come standard. The chips with salsa and queso are a great snack, and the long tots with longhots and cheese are completely delicious.    Best of all were the vibes - kind of island-y, plus a super amazing playlist that was later replaced by a DJ who was fantastic. I also loved the local artwork, which became a topic of discussion between almost everyone seated at the bar at one point. We called it a night around 10:30 but I could have partied all night in that atmosphere. Can't wait to return (and I don't even love bowling)!

Cafe L'Aube is an excellent option for weekend (or weekday!) brunch in Graduate Hospital. On the day we went, there was absolutely no wait, and there were several tables available. Ever since L'Aube left their South Street location, I've been seriously missing their delicious lattes. I'm so glad they are back in the area and even closer to my apartment so I can have the lattes any time I want! I even think the crêpes are better at this new location. The ham, egg and cheese version I had was enormous and so delicious.   I'm overdue for another visit.

The Pickled Heron has been on my list of bookmarked restaurants for a long time, and I finally got to check it out with two girlfriends on Friday. We arrived armed with three bottles of vino. Though the restaurant was featuring some type of restaurant week deal, they still had their full menu available, which was our preference. Unfortunately, the menu didn't exactly match the one online, and my friend was disappointed to see that the scallops were no longer being offered. Luckily, there were still a handful of other seafood options.   I started with the moules frites. The mussels were served in a light, saffron-scented broth and they were fantastic. The fries were piping hot and served in a cone with a mild dipping sauce. Next up was a steak with bone marrow stuffing, mushrooms and onion. The steak was a perfect medium rare as requested.   We passed on dessert but said yes to French pressed coffee. I'm glad I finally got a chance to try The Pickled Heron and I'd be down for a return trip sometime.

In my early twenties, Pizzicato was THE place to kick off a girls' night out in Old City. Somehow, as the years have passed, the spot has slipped off my radar. But due to a recent pizza kick, my boyfriend and I decided to pay a visit and see how things were holding up.   Not much has changed - the decor remains the same, the menu remains the same, and they were still getting their fair share of Friday night clientele. We walked in just as the last table was given away in the front dining room, so we were led to the back room, curiously known as Bijou, where we dined in solitude with the exception of appearances from the staff.   It was kind of nice having an entire room to ourselves - we just hoped that we wouldn't be forgotten. We weren't; Ross took great care of us. Salad starters were very solid - fresh ingredients and just the right amount of dressing. My Caesar hit the spot.   Margherita and prosciutto pies both had light, crisp crusts and zesty, well-flavored sauce. They weren't on the same level as Pizzeria Stella, but they weren't bad, either.   Coffee was pretty awful, however, and was served with milk instead of cream. I got my energy jolt but my tastebuds weren't happy about it.   I wouldn't go out of my way for Pizzicato, but it's still a decent option in Old City after all these years.

Maggiano's is an Italian chain with pretty good food and fair prices.  Most times, I have eaten here with just a couple other people, so we all order our own meals and take home leftovers.  However, if food comas are more your thing, gather up some friends and go "family-style."    If your experience is anything like the one I had with a group of about 20 on Friday night, you will be seated about 30 - 45 minutes after your reservation time.  Just as you start to ponder cannibalism, massive appetizer plates and bowls of salad will be delivered.  You'll be stuffed before the main course yet you will continue eating, because by now there are huge dishes of pasta and plates of chicken.  By the time dessert comes around, you consider calling a wide-load crane instead of a taxi.  Diets, beware.

I popped into Kei for lunch yesterday and it was solid. Everyone working was super nice and I loved that our server was on top of refilling water glasses through the entire meal.   To start, I had the yellowtail and jalapeño. I was expecting thin slivers of fish like I've had in other restaurants, but I received a small plate with two very large slices of fish. In all honesty, I would have preferred smaller slivers because these were a huge pieces of fish that were difficult to eat in one bite. I typically like this starter a lot but might not order it again at Kei for that reason. My dining partner had shrimp shumai which looked really tasty.   The lunch special comes with two rolls and soup or salad. I opted for soup which was nice but the salad across from me looked delicious - Kei went above and beyond a simple bowl of iceberg and offered what appeared to be a beautiful starter salad.   The avocado tuna and crunchy spicy tuna rolls I ordered were massive! Two was more than enough after the soup and yellowtail starter. Next time, I'll skip the starter and go straight to the lunch special. I'll definitely return for lunch, hopefully soon!

I had lunch at Marathon on the Square for the first time this week because it was a convenient meeting place for myself and my dining partner, both of us short on time and coming from other meetings in the vicinity. I arrived first and was seated inside. When my companion said he'd be late, I planned to order for the both of us but it was really hard trying to get my server's attention. I didn't catch her until my friend arrived.   I started with the matzo ball soup because I was really hungry and needed something ASAP. It's a Best of Philly winner so I thought it would be great but it was pretty plain. I did like the al dente vegetables in the broth but the chicken was intensely dry (how is that possible in soup?!) and the matzo ball itself seemed like a waste of carbs.  We both had blackened chicken caesar salads. I thought mine was too lightly dressed and asked for additional dressing - something I rarely do. The salad was fine. My friend really liked his. I had a bangin' caese the day before at another establishment and it was hard not to compare.   Lunch came to $42 with tip which seems really steep for two salads, a soup and no beverages aside from water. I'll probably look a little harder next time I need a lunch spot.

It's time to upgrade my review for the PFS Roxy! My husband and I went to the Saturday, 6pm showing of Beauty and the Beast (which was amazing, and the theater was filled with mostly adults so don't be shy if you want to see it and you don't have any kiddos to take!). I called in advance to ask about available seats for the earlier show, and was told that the theater had been bought out for a party. My husband quickly purchased tickets to the 6pm so we wouldn't miss out.   We arrived about 30 minutes early so we could queue up. The theaters are very small so if you want to choose a seat, you better get there in advance. We went to purchase popcorn, and the  friendly guy at concessions offered us small, pre-filled bags on the house because they were left over from the earlier party. So nice!   The screen in the theater was comically tiny compared with other mainstream theaters, but once the movie started I really didn't notice! Everyone in the theater was respectful of others and there was nary a cell phone buzz to be heard.   I love that they have BYO Wednesdays. It's a $3 corkage fee/person but they provide the glassware. You are also limited to one regular-sized bottle of wine or a six pack of beer. Looking forward to checking that out sometime.

Ela has a lot going for it: a beautiful, sexy space with a nice, long bar; attractive and engaging servers who know the menu; a young, enterprising chef with fresh ideas. Ela has great potential, but on my first visit I wasn't really wowed.   Our starters of kale salad, scallop noodles and gnocchi were all nice but not anything I'll crave again, with the exception of the kale salad, which had a very tasty, mustard-y vinaigrette. The scallop dish seemed a bit gimicky - I far prefer the nice sear and texture of a regular scallop to this manipulated version. The gnocchi was a teeny tiny portion - maybe I didn't get the full array of flavors after sharing the dish with two friends.   The cocktail list, meanwhile, had some gems. I started with Last Chance to Lose Your Keys, a tequila mixture served straight up. It was a bit on the sweet side but still enjoyable for someone like myself, who prefers a basic drink over something special. The beer list was decent and had something for everyone.   While all of the entree options were unique, I had a hard time narrowing in on one that appealed to me. Eventually, I ordered the veal skirt steak, which was fine but again, not overly memorable. I was also able to try a piece of the skate wing, and I was not a fan of the preparation. It was very similar to a version I had at Blackfish last summer, with the outer parts folded under, resulting in a taste and texture that seemed undercooked.   Desserts were probably the best part of the meal, although the hot chocolate chip cookie dough did nothing for me. It was a bowl of warm, caramelized bananas with kind of a dulce de leche-type sauce. I was quite content to pass that up in favor of the red wine poached stawberries with white chocolate whipped cream and shortbread crumbles. That, friends, was the star of the night for me. The manjari chocolate was pretty awesome as well - definitely worth ordering if you're really in the mood for chocolate.   I'll be honest. Parting with more than eighty dollars for my share of the bill (three shared apps, three entrees, three desserts and two drinks per girl) wasn't easy. But the bright side of all of this is that restaurants like Ela have the freedom to change dishes with the seasons and available ingredients. Maybe there will be a future menu that appeals to me more. In the meantime, I'll happily settle for the strawberry dessert at the bar.

I cheated on my regular nail salon because they are not open on Mondays and I really needed a mani/pedi before an event on Tuesday. I searched Yelp and Coco Blue was one of the best-reviewed nail salons. I called and scheduled an appointment at my desired time that same day.   At my appointment time, I walked in and they were ready for me. There is a nice selection of colors by all the usual brands. They also have a great selection of current rag mags. My pedi was very relaxing. My nail tech took her time and I feel she did a very good job. Hot stones were involved!   Sadly, all it took was one spin class the following day for the polish on my toes to chip. I get pedicures regularly and also spin regularly and this never happens after services at my other salon. I'm not sure why this happened but needless to say I wasn't pleased. Luckily, I was able to do a little emergency repair at home.   In the meantime, My manicure still looks really great, although I noticed after leaving the salon that the polish didn't start as close to the cuticle as I would like. My nails grow very quickly and I hate seeing a large gap between my skin and the polish after one day!   I realize I'm very picky when it comes to my services so please take this with a grain of salt if you aren't as particular. I would probably go to Coco Blue again in a pinch but I'll continue spending a little more for better results at my usual spot.

It's rare that I purchase an offer from a deal site, but I was in desperate need of a last minute mani/pedi on a day that my usual nail salon was closed, so I took the plunge when I noticed an offer for B2. The deal was a mani/pedi for $25. I had an enjoyable service with Carole, who is very sweet and has been in the industry for quite a while.   When I paid, I was given a coupon to return for the very same deal on another occasion. Nice! Once again, I made an appointment at the eleventh hour before a holiday weekend and the place was packed. It was understandable that appointments were running a few minutes behind, though I ended up soaking in lukewarm water for ten minutes or so, with no magazines in sight. I do appreciate that B2 uses tub liners for pedicures. That's something I've grown accustomed to at my usual nail salon and it makes the service much more sanitary.  The color selection leaves a lot to be desired. Many of the polishes look old or like they haven't been used for a while. I didn't see a lot of full bottles and some of the polishes were separating. That said, my mani lasted several days without chips (though I did apply an extra top coat at home after a couple days).   I won't be leaving my normal salon but it's nice to have a back-up. I would consider purchasing a deal for B2 again though I don't think I'd be willing to pay full price for their services.

Wow~ I don't know what some of the posters from '06 are talking about, but it's definitely not the same place I've been hitting up...  I love coffee, but Grooveground's is a bit strong and takes some getting used to~ they will happily throw a shot of hot water in there if you ask though... I've since worked up a tolerance and take my fix strong the way they serve it!  The people who work here are so friendly; many of them remember what you drink and most are always willing to chat about whatever random bullshit you talk about before you get your first cup of the day.    I've never gotten food here, but they have a nice variety for such a tiny place.  Also, there are only one or two people working at one time, but it's not normally crowded enough to warrant more.  This is a neighborhood joint~ if you don't like it, there are at least 3 other options for coffee within two blocks!

My husband and I popped into Fiore for a late lunch on Sunday afternoon. Since it was a holiday weekend, the restaurant was on the quiet side, save for a few occupied tables.  The brunch/lunch menu is pretty small but there were a few things that jumped out right away. In terms of beverages, I was very happy to see multiple non-alcoholic options available, including San Pellegrino sodas and Baba's Brew kombucha. They had Purple Rain and Flower Power, which are my two favorites.   We decided to share the chopped salad, 'nduja toast, and chorizo pizzette. Everything was fresh and tasty, though each plate was pretty small so be prepared for a tapas-style meal, at least during brunch.   Solid experience and I'd be interested in returning to try more!

This is a cute place and much-needed for the area it is in.  The beer selection is decent but the food... needs work.  The menu is very small and the way things are presented make it seem like they are trying too hard to be upscale.  The nachos in particular were a huge disappointment.  I didn't know it was possible to screw up a standard plate of bar nachos until the other night at Devil's Den.  After seeing a couple plates go by, we decided to order them.  We hadn't noticed an abundance of salsa, so we specifically asked for some on the side.  This is how the conversation went:  me: we'll have the nachos with a side of salsa server: (weird look)...okay...  two minutes later  server: we don't have salsa... is fresh pico okay? me: that would be great!  two minutes later  server: um, we can't do pico either.  How about a free side of guacamole? me: um, okay  Who serves nachos without salsa or anything resembling salsa?    Devil's Den does.  P.S.  For the record, ketchup is not really good on nachos...

From my first set of fangs to present-day maintenance, Dr. Dickey has always been my go-to guy for dentistry. His staff members are all welcoming, gentle (especially in matters concerning my sensitive gums!) and genuine.   To this day, I have never had a cavity, and I credit the many torturous minutes of flouride treatments during my childhood. The good news for kids of this generation is that the office no longer uses the tray and gel methods of yesteryear; now kids can simply swish around some rinse and be on their way!  Bonus points for current magazines and Wi-Fi!

After working up a sweat at Maha nearby, Melissa P and I decided to reward ourselves with a semi-splurge lunch at Luke's Lobster. The lobster roll combo comes with chips and a drink for $17, which is a deal when you consider the fact that you are eating lobster, just a bit pricier than I would normally spend on lunch. Totally worth it for a special treat.   The roll was pleasantly stuffed with big chunks of lobster meat, and just the right amount of butter and a bit of seasoning. If I could think of one thing that would make it even better it would be a slice of lemon to squirt on top. The pickle was great, and the chips were the delish kettle-cooked kind. I thought the seating inside was really cute and a lot more plentiful than I expected for such a small place.   I've been thinking about the lobster roll ever since I ate it nearly a week ago, so if that doesn't say five stars, I don't know what does.

We hired First Class for my sister's wedding and also the bachelorette party. Since my family had already booked them for the wedding, First Class hooked us up with discounted pricing for the bachelorette party which was great.   For both occasions, the drivers were pretty well-versed with all of the stops we wanted to make. I'm sure providing all of this info ahead of time helped. I thought the driver on the day of the wedding was particularly awesome. He not only knew each stop in two different states without needing help from anyone in the bridal party but he also handled the gigantic limo bus really well and always found a convenient place to park.   The limo bus we had for the wedding was pretty incredible. We fit sixteen people easily and could have fit more. There was tons of space, plenty of handrails and even a stripper pole. Yup. Bridal party gone wild!

It took me more than three years to hit up Palm Tree Market but, since my first visit a few weeks ago, I've returned or ordered delivery a handful of times. There is a large variety of sandwiches and lunch meat is carved fresh for each one. I love the paninis because they aren't super heavy. They are just the right amount of toasted to where the cheese is melty.   There is a small refrigerated section with dips and a few other essentials, and a nice variety of chips. They also have every type of cold beverage you could possibly want.   The store is super clean and nice-looking. The employees are friendly. Super happy I finally checked this place out!

I really have nothing bad to say about my experience at Laughlin. In fact, it was probably the easiest of all the steps in the transformation of a NJ-licensed vehicle to a PA one. I went on a weekday around noon and was in and out in a matter of ten minutes. Steve was a pretty funny guy, and he was nice enough to remove my old NJ plates and put my new plate on for me. I'd definitely recommend this place to anyone in need of title transfer, registration and plates.

A couple weekends ago, I enjoyed a lovely date night at Hoof & Fin. We arrived for our reservation and the dining room was hectic, but we were seated right away. Things got off to a slow start with receiving water and having our wine opened, but after we gave our order to our funny, engaging server, the rest of the evening was pretty close to flawless.  We started with beef empanadas and provoleta fundida. The empanadas were incredible; we immediately started discussing which version we would order on our next visit. The fundida was comparable to the queso fundido at Xochitl: although the latter has the slight edge for me. Still, a great selection nonetheless.  For his main course, my boyfriend had a rice and shellfish special, very similar to the arroz a la gallega which is on Hoof + Fin's regular menu, only this was made with coconut milk and spinach, I believe. It was excellent, and I stole forkfuls at every opportunity. My dish, skate wing with truffle potato gratin and a side salad, was fantastic, except for one thing: too much salt. It wasn't at the point where I couldn't still enjoy it, but I did drink a lot of water with that meal.   We somehow managed to save a small corner of room for dessert, so we went with the churros and dipping chocolate. Unreal. They were especially awesome with a cup of La Colombe coffee.  My boyfriend loved the meal so much he went back the following week with his mom and loved it all over again. I'm looking forward to my next visit as well!

This is a review of my Covid-19 testing experience; I never set foot inside the hospital as all testing is taking place outside, in the driveway off of Sansom Street, just past 10th.   I recently returned from a trip to Mexico. Despite taking proper precautions during my travels, I wanted to get tested for my own peace of mind and to ensure that I would not unknowingly expose anyone if I was an asymptomatic virus carrier. Jefferson's testing site is by appointment only. I had a brief televisit with my primary care doctor, who wrote me a script and recommended that I book my appointment for three days after my return home. I called Jefferson and had no problems booking my desired day and time.   I arrived for my appointment about fifteen minutes early. I was admittedly pretty nervous after watching far too many videos on the Internet! After a few paperwork formalities, a medical professional came over to my car, explained the test and asked if I was ready. I nodded, closed my eyes, and braced myself for torture. Much to my surprise, there was no torture! While I definitely felt the swab inside my nasal canal, it wasn't painful at all, just a little strange. The medic counted down - 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 - and it was over! I couldn't believe how simple it was and would have no hesitation taking the test again in the future, if needed.   Thanks to the medical staff at Jefferson, who were friendly and professional and made this experience as easy as possible!

I have been loving this Chipotle for healthy, fast lunches. Yep, I said healthy. Because if you forgo the wrap, cheese and heavy meats, you really can have your Chipotle and eat it too. Ask for a burrito bowl, and then use a lettuce base with just a little bit of brown rice and black beans, plus onions and peppers. I've noticed that Chipotle workers across the board are super generous with toppings, which is awesome, but also dangerous if you are trying to watch what you're eating.   I finish off my burrito bowl with pico and both of the tomato-based salsas, plus some guacamole for some rich flavor and healthy fat. Their guac is super fresh and tasty. No dressing needed!   The employees are always fast and friendly. Once their diet coke dispenser shot out clear liquid which was a bummer, but besides that, this location rocks.

If you're in the South Jersey area and looking to load up on seasonal flowers, Lowe's in Delran has you covered. I stopped by and was super impressed by the amazing array of hanging baskets and planters of all shapes and sizes. I do find them to be a little on the pricey side, but the selection was truly incredible. Hopefully I don't kill off my new buds (lolz) in record time.

I swung by LA Nail Bar on a whim to get a quick mani before the weekend. My experience was positive; I popped in before lunch and there was an opening. The woman who did my nails was nice and gentle. She worked on my nails quickly but efficiently, and they looked great when they were done. I took extra time to dry them and was given a great neck massage.   My nails looked awesome, but that only lasted for one day. By Saturday, my nails were already chipping a lot. I think some more buffing would have prevented this, and probably a better quality top coat too.   I'd consider trying LA Nail Bar again if I was in the area and in dire need of a mani, but I wouldn't go out of my way.

When my sister told me that our Saturday night plans had to do with a bar just off of South Street, I rolled my eyes and figured I was in for a long night.  We arrived at Get Happy just as the Villanova game was ending, so there was a pretty large crowd in the upstairs bar where we were hanging out.  The game ended and the majority of the crowd took off, leaving plenty of space at the bar for us to get drinks and maneuver around comfortably.  A DJ started his shift, and our group of about 8 decided it was a good night for an old fashioned dance party.    In between rounds of cheap beer and shots, we danced the night away to classic tunes, including the majority of Michael Jackson's Thriller album, A-Ha's "Take on Me" (by request!) and various others.  By the end of the night, our rowdy crew was using anything that wasn't nailed down as props for our dance routines.  The staff, miraculously, put up with our shenanigans all night long and continued to serve us.  I had low expectations going into the night but ended up having one of the best times I've had in months.

I always thought Las Vegas Lounge would be every bit as seedy as it sounds.  While I had never looked for a reason to prove this theory, a friend and I decided that any old joint with booze would make a better alternative to Chifa's overcrowded downstairs bar, where we stood packed like sardines in a sea of d-bags while taking part in the final CC Sips of the summer.  We hurried our way across the street and I have to admit, I was quite relieved by the lack of crowds and lack of pretentiousness that welcomed us when we entered the dimly-lit bar.  The abundance of a/c didn't hurt, either.  As we hovered over the other patrons in an effort to read the specials, the bartender told us we could get the same deals at the tables as well.  We made our way to the nearest high top, which was tucked into an even darker corner.  For the next hour and a half, our friendly server kept our drinks coming and graciously offered a last call for Sips when 7:00 rolled around.    I highly recommend this place for anyone who needs a break from the 'tudes that oftentimes go hand in hand with swankier places.  We all need a good dive bar in life every now and then.

"Very good."  This was my response almost every time our server asked about our dinner on Friday night. I became aware of this after the second or third time saying it, and then later my boyfriend pointed out that there was one time that I simply said, "good." It was during the main course. More on that later.  We were seated at a cozy two top in the second room, and service was near perfect throughout the night. To start, a choice between focaccia or sourdough, with olive oil. The focaccia was delicious. An amuse bouche of chilled soup was forgettable - in fact, I don't remember the flavors at all.  Our first course was a yellowtail tuna sashimi and gazpacho. Both were incredibly light and had bright flavors. The tuna had a slight spicy kick and the components of the dish were spot on. A second course had us enjoying short-rib stuffed ravioli in brown butter sauce and seared scallops with salsa verde. For me, the scallops won out ever so slightly but my date felt the same way about the ravioli. It was a win-win course.   At this point we were both very excited about the entrees, but I was sadly a bit disappointed with mine. The skate wing was presented with a crispy exterior, but the outskirts were rolled under and had a really undercooked appearance and lacked the texture of the exposed area. The peas and country ham bits underneath were a little boring. I left a large piece of the fish untouched. The grilled yellowtail tuna was significantly better, with a nicely seasoned crust and a delicious tomato salad served alongside.   Next, we shared a cheese course with Morbier, a French blue and a mild brie. The temperature was just warm enough to bring out the flavors, which were enhanced by accompanying spreads and served with crusty sourdough slices.   Finally, a round of warm, sugary beignets which were served with a raspberry sauce and a creamy creme anglaise. These were delightful if a bit unnecessary at that point in the meal. But date nights are special and a shared dessert is par for the course.   Overall, the meal was very good.

Finally tried Wrap Shack after hearing good things for years! I ordered a chicken caesar wrap even though they only have it on the menu as a salad option. The wrap was super dense and I ended up enjoying it for lunch on back to back days. That said, the wrap barely had any lettuce; it was mostly just chopped chicken and dressing. So I would love to see some lettuce and even tomato, but I also understand that I ordered off the menu. Would try again for sure!

Popped over to Zavino for happy hour last night and was pretty impressed. I can't believe it but that was only my second visit since they opened. I certainly won't wait so long to get back again.   I didn't eat anything (except for the garnishes in my martini) but the combination cheese and charcuterie board that my friends ordered looked beautiful and delicious. Happy hour wines are five dollars but the options were pinot noir and chardonnay. I'd rather walk on hot coals in bare feet than drink chardonnay (okay fine, I'd pick the chardonnay between the two but I wouldn't be happy about it) so I instead opted for a glass of prosecco. Nine dollars seemed reasonable and the bubbles were tasty!   Then, I spotted a martini with prosciutto-wrapped blue cheese stuffed olives on the menu. I had to have it. When I found out the house vodka is Gordon's, I had to upgrade to Grey Goose, their only other vodka. This drink was amazing. A meal in a glass!   So while I did fail miserably at the whole save money at happy hour thing, I did have a very positive experience and am looking forward to next time.

My boyfriend's parents took us to Monsu for one last supper before they left town on a ten day trip to Europe (luckieees!). I wasn't sure how I'd feel walking into the former Paesano's location - I had some good sandwich memories from that place. Fortunately, the Sicilian fare Peter McAndrews is sending out of the kitchen at Monsu is no joke, either.  I started with the scallop app, which was served over pearl pasta with dried cherries and a red wine glaze. The scallop was seared perfectly, but I could probably take or leave the accompaniments. Next up was half an order of gnocchi. Unreal. Served in a salty tomato sauce with just a hint of cream, and topped with shavings of ricotta salata, I would absolutely order this as my main course at a future visit.   Unless of course, I wanted the eggplant parm again. Layer upon lightly crisped layer of eggplant melded with fresh, oozy mozzarella, red sauce and more of that delicious ricotta salata. It was rich and satisfying.   For dessert, my boyfriend and I shared a cannoli which was just so-so. The bar is definitely raised for cannoli any time one enters the Italian Market, so I think this particular offering could be improved.  Otherwise, stellar meal. I'd also love to check them out for brunch.

In an email conversation the other day about plans for that evening, my heart skipped a beat as I read these words: "BYO at Lolita then watch hockey?"  Score for a case of Tastykakes!  Not only would we be watching the boys kick some Toronto butt, we'd also be hitting up one of the restaurants that has been on my places-to-try list for ages.  I grabbed a bottle of tequila and jumped on the train.    The restaurant was just as I imagined it would be; dim lighting with dark furniture and exposed brick walls.  My date and I were seated at a two top near the door.  I had a nice view of 13th Street, but there was a major draft whenever people walked in or out, despite the curtains in the doorway.  Fortunately, the margaritas helped to numb the chilly sensation.  Said margs were light and without a hint of stomach-churning sour mix.  Our pitcher went down easy throughout the meal.  We started with a spicy guacamole with diced mango.  I usually don't mess with the classic recipe but I'm glad we branched out because it was fantastic.  I would easily order this version again on a return visit.  I flip-flopped between the salmon and the boneless short rib entrees, but ultimately ended up choosing the salmon.  My fear was that the dish would be somewhat plain and I'd regret my decision.  Happily, this was not the case at all.  The salmon arrived, a generous cut that sat majestically over pureed hearts of palm, all topped with a grilled corn salsa and surrounded by a smoky sauce.  Stars aligned on my first flavor-punched bite.  I was so content with the dish in front of me that I actually passed on the offer to try the beef tips, a special that night.    We skipped dessert in the interest of having more time for hockey watching, but I'll be sure to check the offerings out on a future visit.  I look forward to dining at Lolita again.

My boyfriend and I trekked all the way to NoLibs for brunch at the much-talked-about Jerry's Bar on Saturday. We had a late start and arrived around 2, so there wasn't a wait for a table which was great as I was getting pretty hungry by that point. The bar is really pretty. Lots of very cool touches with regards to decor and a beautiful outdoor patio adjacent to the dining room.   We started with a round of bloody marys and coffee.
