For our main course we tried a margherita pizza, which was anything but ordinary because of the quality of ingredients used.  The flavors of fresh basil on top of slightly-salty mozzarella melding with just-right tomato sauce made for the perfect bite.  Our other pizza selection was the trentino, which featured (appropriately) salty cheeses, hunks of grilled fig and a type of prosciutto.  We saved this one for last but everyone agreed that the margherita had it beat.    We ended the evening with a baked fig strudel, a heavenly caramelized apple cake (which our server described as jewel-like in appearance - sold!) and an order of gelato, half mascarpone and half pistachio, which came complete with a candle for the birthday girl.  The desserts were great but the gelato was other-worldly.  The impeccable service, comfortable surroundings and memorable food made for a really nice evening.  I'd most recommend Osteria for small groups, so plates can be shared, but it would be a great date spot as well.  So... anyone who feels so inclined to take me there can just let me know, k?  K.  Good talk.

COVID-19 update: I visited Ringpfeil for my annual skin check and felt extremely comfortable with how everything was handled during my visit. Check-in was on the first floor, as usual. After settling my co-pay, I was directed to the second floor and given a specific exam room. There were signs everywhere pointing to the numbered exam rooms, and signs inside the room with instructions.   My appointment was just as thorough as always and, as usual, I received excellent care from my dermatologist. There is always an additional staff member in the room to take notes and I felt very comfortable at all times. Everyone, including me, was masked up and my dermatologist was also wearing gloves.   Get your skin checked and don't forget your SPF daily!

Swung by the new Cambridge last night and it was bumpin'! So much so that the wait for a table was almost a half hour. Normally, this wouldn't be a problem and we'd just grab a drink and wait, but I was already well into hangry territory so we opted to grab a bite elsewhere. Afterwards, we returned and were seated at a table right away. We had several drinks and our server was great. The food at the surrounding tables looked awesome, and I was a little regretful that we hadn't just waited before. But I'm sure we'll be back in no time.   My only gripe, and I see that it is a common theme in the reviews so far, is the noise. We broke out a decibel measuring app for fun and the reading was very high. But our ears already knew that. I did enjoy the music selection, but I'm hanging on to hope that some sound muffling will take effect soon. Aside from that, the bar/restaurant is gorgeous and I'm really looking forward to hanging out there!

I was looking for a birthday gift for my brother so wandered into this store the other day.  Right away I found something he would like, which was awesome.  The store had a lot of great stuff but the prices were a bit ridic for things like basic t-shirts.  Like the previous poster said, there is definitely a hipster-type vibe here~ but nothing wins a hipster over faster than when you compliment the music selection (especially when it's coming direct from his ipod- bonus points!!!).    I'm just kidding~ the guy who worked there was super nice and even wrote down the name of the cd for me (Different Class by Pulp).  That little act of kindness made my day, and my bro loved his new hat!

This review is a tad belated, but I still wanted to swing by Neuf's Yelp page and tell y'all about the amazing brunch I had late last year. First off, the Bloody Marys are the jam. They feature a nice, smokey flavor and spices that give them a Moroccan flair. I shared the endive salad, which curiously seemed to lack endive, but was nonetheless very tasty. The blue cheese crumbles were perfection.   Shakshuka. This is one of my favorite dishes and I love that they have several different options to try. I kept it simple and went with the traditional, which was great. I told myself I wouldn't eat the bread, but it looked too delicious to pass up. I showed restraint by leaving one small bite behind. My husband's ratatouille omelet was absolutely incredible - quite possibly delicious enough to choose over the shakshuka next time!   The chef surprised us with the Paris brest for dessert, piled high with rose-scented whipped cream, candied cherries and shaved almonds. I took a bite or two, but I was pretty stuffed from brunch already and don't have much of a sweet tooth except for rare occasions. If you love dessert you should definitely try it!   I'm dying to go back for dinner and may even make it an official New Year's resolution to do so.

This pizza place has been around for ages and is still kicking.  There is definitely a ton of nostalgic appeal for me here since I grew up in Cinnaminson; pizza in my grade school classrooms was ALWAYS from Brother's, I had my first kiss after a group dinner here, my field hockey and lacrosse teams in high school always convened here and now my sister and I hit it up for hangover food when we're so inclined.  Years have gone by but one thing remains the same-- the pizza.  And it's freaking gooooooooood.

Several weeks before Thanksgiving, I took to Twitter to find out which local businesses were taking orders for pecan pies. I received several recommendations, but Wedge & Fig stuck out since I had been wanting to get back in the wake of an awesome YEE in October.   When I called to order my pie, I quickly discovered that W&F was not taking orders for pecan, but they were doing two other varieties. After explaining the mix-up of info I had received on Twitter, they generously agreed to bake a pecan pie especially for me. Floored and touched, I promised I would not reveal this information to the masses. Now that Thanksgiving is over, I think it's safe to let the cat out of the bag.   For the record, the pie was absolutely delicious. Everyone in my family had a slice and all agreed that the rich, buttery flavor and crunchy, sticky texture was spot on. Out of the three pies we had, the pecan yielded the least amount of leftovers. I enjoyed a coveted second slice this morning, and it was every bit as good as last night.   My mom told me I am now officially on pie duty for Thanksgiving. I know where I'll be ordering my pie from next year, and I can only hope that the pecan will be offered as one of the selections.

As far as fast food restaurants go, Chick-fil-A is all right in my book.  The chicken strips and nuggets are always tender on the inside, with a crunchy, slightly salty coating of goodness on the outside.  The fries are of the waffle variety, but you won't see Aunt Jemima around this neck of the woods.  Barbecue sauce, honey mustard or ketchup will do just fine.  Yum.

I'm embarrassed to admit that I stepped foot in this place over the age of 25.  Alas, it was a friend's 24th birthday and the decision was not my own.    There are two parts to this establishment.  The downstairs is a sports bar/restaurant and the upstairs is a club.  After hanging out downstairs for a while, a few of the girls decided to check out the upstairs.  Two bouncers made a huge production of searching purses and patting down all guys.  A sign that read "NY Style Dress Code" was posted nearby.  This should have been my signal to turn around but curiosity won out and I paid the five bucks to get in (it's ten for guys).  We proceeded up the steps... and straight into a code-red situation: popped collars, wannabe platform dancers and more hair gel than a mid-nineties LA Looks campaign.   A few girls wanted to stick it out and dance but I made my way back downstairs to watch the Flyers' game.  My experience was severely hindered by the constant opening of a side door that let in a very cold and smoky draft.  Apparently, the patio area that is open in the summer also doubles as a smokers' lounge.  While the building itself certainly holds many memories of my past (under 18 dance parties back in the day at The Iguana, my first real bar experience after my 21st birthday at Top Dog, etc.), the ship has sailed.

What a cute little spot in the heart of Old City! A gorgeous square wood communal table is the first thing that drew my eye when I first walked into Fork Etc. late in the afternoon on Friday.   My companion and I were just swinging by for a quick beverage - bottles of Victory's Fists of Feury. We took our beers over to the super cushy and comfy banquet close to the giant window, perfect for people-watching.   I am very much looking forward to returning for lunch or a quiet meal in the evening, where I'll watch the world pass me by.

Walking out of Hop Sing in the wee hours on Sunday morning, we asked Lee for a recommendation for late-night Chinese and he rattled off a couple places. We walked past the line at David's and into the nearly-empty Shiao Lan Kung.   My klutzy self had suffered a minor incident on the one block walk (heels are dangerous and even moreseo after several drinks) and when we arrived my left knee was looking a bit questionable. A lady who worked there came over right away with some first aid stuff, which was much appreciated.   If you want to continue your drinking, you'll have to BYO as Shiao Lan Kung does not serve alcohol. We saw several late-night parties walk in after us with beer. That said, leave the bar before last call and secure your table. The place got a lot busier as the night went on.     We started with fried dumplings which arrived in a soy sauce with fresh chopped scallions. They were booze-soakingly delicious. Next up was some perfectly sticky white rice and chicken in black bean sauce and pork in garlic sauce. Both were awesome.   I'm still impressed that my motor vehicle skills allowed me to use my chopsticks successfully. I definitely owe this place a more sober visit so I can properly assess the food.

As much as I totally loathe taking my car to Cherry Hill Nissan, I will say that I always feel like it has been well taken care of after all is said and done.   Or maybe I just need to tell myself that as I part with hundreds of dollars every time my ride needs fixing. Everything is beyond expensive, and should you decide not to have an issue fixed right away (because there are other, more pressing car issues to handle first), you will still be charged a fee just because someone looked at the source of the noise, light, etc. In addition to paying whatever fee you are already paying to have other problems resolved.   Having a car while living in the city is definitely a luxury, but it's an expensive one. Regardless, I need my wheels to work like a well-oiled machine whenever I want to get out of town. After 7+ years, my car is still treating me well, and I probably have CH Nissan to thank for part of that.

I had a $20 Rum Bucks coupon from an event I went to last year that I finally put to use last Saturday. The rum list was huge, but I flipped to the cocktail section of the menu to make my decision. Right away I noticed a skinny mojito, made with Splenda syrup instead of simple syrup. Unfortunately, there was no Splenda syrup made. Did I mention it was a Saturday, just after opening? I sucked it up and went with a regular mojito instead. The drink was tasty, I even had two, but I don't see myself dropping $12/drink there regularly.   The decor feels dated but it's still a nice looking place. But the tacky pirate in the lounge area up front has got to go.   If you aren't in the mood for a fancy drink, the happy hour specials are pretty recession-friendly and are offered seven days a week. Also, the bartender was nice, which certainly isn't a given these days. I don't know that I'd go out of my way for Rum Bar, but if I were in the area and the mood hit, I wouldn't object to going back.

I've been dying (har har har) to get to Laurel Hill Cemetery for years, and a spooky evening of "Tales from the Tombs" enticed me to finally get over to East Falls for some Halloween fun. I highly recommend buying tickets in advance if there's a particular event you want to attend. I checked-in on Yelp and a friend commented that tickets were sold out by the time she went to purchase.   Parking is available for free in the lots across the street, which are cemetery property. Our tour started right on time and we were guided by flashlight to several tombs where actors told us the real-life stories of some incredibly interesting Philadelphians. We did experience a small hiccup when our group was left without a guide after the last story, and we all sort of stood around for ten minutes before making our way back to the entrance. There was a table where you could buy refreshments and my husband and I enjoyed some spiked cider by one of the firepits.   Bathrooms are available on site and they were clean and well-stocked. I loved this fun and different night out and would definitely go back for another event sometime.

I'm definitely a fan of Cafe L'Aube, and I was super bummed to discover a couple weeks ago that their Washington Ave location is no longer open on weekends. But when the craving for L'Aube coffee and a crêpe strikes, you have to answer the call, even if it requires a little more distance to travel.   L'Aube's Rittenhouse location is cute and very French (or at least, how I imagine very French to be). Baguettes, pastries and juices line the counters and the short but sweet menu has something for everyone. I went with my standard order, the Complete, with Emmentaler cheese, ham and egg, in a buckwheat crêpe. Sometimes, this crêpe is perfect, and other times, it can be a bit dry. To avoid this, the Le Fromager crêpe is probably a better option because the chevre has a wonderful creaminess that pairs really well with the egg, bacon and grape tomatoes.  One of the best things about L'Aube is their coffee. It's absolutely delicious and right up there with La Colombe, my other favorite. Their lattes are better than anywhere else, and served in gigantic mugs. Je t'aime, L'Aube!

I've always been a fan of Tria but my delivery experience this past weekend was especially great. I've had my eye on Tria's to-go menu for a while and we finally decided to try their "Cheesy Package for 2" which costs $50 before tax and tip. The package includes: a three cheese board (you select the cheeses from a list), burrata and tomato conserva toast, fennel-roasted almonds, marinated olives, two choices of salad or sandwich (there are six options to choose from), and a dessert to share (two options to choose from).   We opted for cheddar, blue and goat cheeses for our board. They were packaged so nicely and labeled, along with the spreads or jams that accompanied each cheese. In fact, everything was packaged perfectly, arriving just like it would had it been served in the restaurant. I was extremely impressed. We chose the artichoke and asparagus salad and spanish white tuna sandwich for the mains, and the flourless chocolate cake for dessert (so rich and simply perfect!).   The food was all fresh and delicious and I felt like this was one of our better delivery experiences since the pandemic shut down dining-in at restaurants. I have a feeling it won't be long before we order this package again. It would also be perfect for a picnic!

In the span of a 15 minute train ride, PATCO made me vow to start saying my prayers again every night, and possibly even start hitting Sunday mass again. Let me explain.   Last Friday evening around 5:30, I boarded a westbound train with two other people. The train car was surprisingly empty, but I made a mad dash for the only seat that had a sports page sitting on it. Just as I started to get into the Flyers' injury updates, the lights went out. This seemed odd, but the train was still moving so I didn't think much of it.   We went underground in Camden, and the darkness in the tunnels was quite spooky. As we approached the first underground station, the train slowed, but did not stop. Same with the second. So the lights were out, we weren't making stops and no announcements were being made. As we made our way out of the tunnel and onto the Ben Franklin Bridge, I text-messaged my sister about the situation and said that I was a little freaked.   As we went back underground in Philly, I thought we would surely stop at 8th and Market, where I was supposed to get off the train. Again, the train slowed but did not stop. At this point, it is safe to say-- I WAS LOSING MY SHIT!!! Worst-case scenarios featuring gunmen and hostage situations filled my head.   I abandoned the sports section and made my way closer to the other passengers. A lovely woman by the name of Susan comforted me when I expressed my concern for our safety. For that, I am eternally grateful.   When the train started slowing to what appeared to be a stop as we got to the 12th/13th & Locust station, I stood up and announced that I was going to pry the doors open with my bare hands if I had to. Which is exactly what I tried to do-- only, the doors were locked. I felt like I was in a horror movie when suddenly, the lights went on and we could see the conductor walking towards us from the car in front of us, a confused look on his face. He opened the door and said, "this train is out of service!" To which all three of us replied (i.e., screamed) something along the lines of "well then why were we let on to begin with?!" peppered with many expletives (mostly mine).   I shakily made my way above ground, grateful to be alive, grateful for the kindness of strangers and grateful that some taxi drivers don't mind driving drunk girls home to Jersey at the end of the night when they decide to pass on the train.

I've been to CTH several times, but my experience on Saturday night was one for the books and definitely worthy of five stars. My friend was back in her hometown for a visit and we wanted to go somewhere with a lively atmosphere to watch the March Madness games and grab a bite.   We walked in around 7:30 and the bar was predictably packed. Worse, the hostess told us that all of their tables were committed to reservations. But then she pointed out an open bar stool at the end of the smaller satellite bar, and she said she might be able to wrangle up a second stool for us, if we didn't mind squeezing a bit. We went over to stand by the bar and the hostess returned moments later with a second bar stool. Win!   Our bartender Erica was amazing - with an extensive knowledge of the beer list, super friendly attitude and uncanny ability to top off waters before we ever had to ask. I was pumped to discover a beer that I absolutely loved because of her recommendation - Captain Lawrence 6th Borough Pils. It was light and just the right amount of hoppy but didn't leave me feeling weighed down like so many craft beers tend to do. I had several.   My friend and I shared the corn and crab hushpuppies to start, which were great. My friend had the burger, which she claimed was cooked perfectly to her request (medium rare). The fries that came with were hot and crispy and everything french fries should be. I had the salumi pizza which was spicy, saucy and delicious. The second half came in handy later that night back in my kitchen.   I was expecting a fun evening but I have to say my expectations were exceeded. I'll definitely be thinking of City Tap House next time I want to get out for a game.

I've been living in Philly for nearly six years, but have held on to a lot of my South Jersey doctors just because I felt comfortable and had good relationships. A long drive and even longer wait times at my former dermatologist finally convinced me to search for a new one in Philly for my annual body scan. I'm so glad I found Ringpfeil Dermatology through Yelp!   Making my appointment was easy and the office is conveniently located in the Rittenhouse area. The office is clean, bright and modern, and I was seen right at my scheduled appointment time. Dr. Bird was awesome. I liked her the moment we started talking and knew I had made the right decision. She took her time with my scan and called out notations for her assistant to record on my medical file. I had a couple small biopsies which were practically painless and handled very quickly.   I feel so good about my decision to move my dermatology care to Ringpfeil and Dr. Bird and look forward to years of healthy skin with their help!

Gennaro's Tomato Pie is not only an awesome new addition to the pizza scene in Philly, it's also the lucky biz to be my 1,000th review on Yelp. Tell them what they've won, Johnny!  Gennaro's exists in a totally unlikely neighborhood, but you are transformed into a 1940s-style pizzeria when you walk through the lace-covered door and past the curtain. Posters and advertisements from long ago adorn the walls, and every detail about the place brings to mind an old-timey business from a time when life was simpler. Even the waitresses, with their red headbands and cute demeanor, fit right in. Our server could not have been sweeter during our visit.   We kept things pretty basic and ordered one small tomato pie with half pepperoni and one small white pie with half garlic spinach. Both were very, very good and more than enough food for two. We brought almost an entire pizza home. The tomato pie had a slight edge for me. I loved everything from the tangy sauce to the stringy mozzarella. The crust was just right, and Gennaro's mastered the one thing that many other thin-crust pizzerias in this city have not - a crust that doesn't completely flop toward the middle of the pie.   I'm glad I stopped eating when I did because our waitress brought over a sampling of their three desserts on the house. My favorites were the cookies and cream dessert and the chocolate mousse cake, but we were informed that a new dessert will be on the menu soon, some type of delicious-sounding chocolate pie with graham cracker crust.   The biz is cash only and delivery service will be starting soon. Other menu items like sandwiches will also be added in time. In hindsight, I'm glad Gennaro's picked South Philly as their location. If this place were closer to Center City, there would be lines just to grab a table!

On its opening weekend, Nomad Pizza made a pretty good impression, but there is room for improvements in the future. We were seated on the second floor, and it was pretty evident that they'll be doing movie nights, with a projector faced towards a large white-walled canvas. Nice!  Our server was great, and helped us order the appropriate amount of food for three people. We started with a round of drinks: the house white for me and Victory root beer for the guys. The root beer came out in frosty mugs and I was a little jealous, despite my nice glass of white. That root beer is worth every delicious calorie.   We shared the blue cheese salad, with mixed greens and sweet pecans. It was nice! Personally, I think it would have really took off with some pears or even halved grapes in lieu of grape tomatoes. But either way, I'd definitely order it again.   Three pizzas were delivered one after the other to our table. The margherita arrived first. When it was dropped off, I asked the runner if they had forgotten to cut the pie, and he said something about how they are serving pizzas in the authentic Italian style, meaning we are meant to cut our own. We each took to cutting up a pie with the knives that we had used for our salads. Hopefully, Nomad reconsiders this decision at some point.   Out of the three pies, the margherita was surprisingly our least favorite. It was okay, but I think the basic concept of this pizza showed the flaws more than our fancier versions. The crust became soggy quickly and was exhaustively chewy. This was true for all of the pies, but the spicy sausage and the tartufo had so many great flavors in the toppings that it was less noticeable.   Desserts were limited to a couple sorbets and a banana nutella pizza, which none of us were interested in at that point. I think some gelato or ice cream would be awesome.   Again, this review was written on the third day of opening weekend. Nomad is a really nice spot for a first date, casual night out or cool place to grab a seat at the bar. I'm looking forward to seeing how they develop.

Yelp came through big time for dinner in Plymouth Meeting! With a meeting at the Plymouth Meeting Mall, dinner options looked pretty basic for me and my team. Yelp app to the rescue! Just a couple miles down the road is WOOJUNG, nestled in an unassuming strip mall. I made a reservation in advance and was happy I did - even on a freezing Wednesday night, the restaurant was near capacity!   Our server was one of the owners and she was hilarious and awesome. She also provided some great feedback when we had questions about particular dishes.   To start, we had the shrimp shumai, wasabi shumai and tuna munchkins. All were delicious. Highly recommend the latter two for fun twists on some classics.   For mains, everyone ordered a different specialty roll and it was so fun to see the creativity from the kitchen! I wanted to keep things simple and went with the new rainbow roll, which was just a spicy tuna roll topped with a rainbow of sashimi and avocado. Fresh and delicious! The standout roll at the table was the kiss of death, which was a shrimp tempura roll topped with baked fish tossed with chili peppers. You can order this roll on a heat scale of 1-5, and we were advised that things start getting really steamy around a 3. Alisha S bravely accepted the challenge and opted for a 3. I got to try a bite and it was indeed very spicy. I might go for a 2 myself if I were to order this on a future visit.  At the end of our meal, everyone was stuffed and the price wasn't bad at all. I'd even say it's worth a drive out of the city. Definitely hoping to return sooner than later!

This particular Iron Hill Brewery comes as a runner up to my preferred locations in Maple Shade and West Chester. On a quiet Saturday afternoon, the place was fairly empty and yet service wasn't as on-point as it could have been.   I find some of the menu items (at all locations) to be on the high side for the quantity received. A fish taco appetizer which contained a single taco was about eight bucks. The cheesesteak egg rolls are also bling-blingin' at eleven dollars for two rolls, each cut in half. (For the record, I can get cheesesteak eggrolls that are every bit as good at Woody's for half the price.) My Mediterranean wrap was fairly priced at $9.50, with a $2.50 upcharge for sweet potato fries swapped out for regular.   I do enjoy Iron Hill Brewery and I dig their beer especially, but as far as food is concerned, there are better finds.

This review comes more from a customer feedback standpoint as opposed to an intent to answer the question, "What is Saladworks?"   You all know what to expect, unless you've been living in the rainforest and growing your own vegetation for the past fifteen or so years.  I've been patronizing the chain for ages, since the very first location opened in Cherry Hill Mall.     Unfortunately, the ginormous salads I enjoyed during my teenage hangouts at the food court have been whittled away over time.  Remember when the container was that gigantic seafoam green styrofoam thingy?  Now it's a square plastic bowl that contains about half the salad.  Veggies and other toppings are usually very fresh but protein options are questionable.  I avoid the chicken at all costs.  Dressings are abundant and there are plenty of low fat or fat free options for the health conscious.    The salads cost anywhere from seven to almost ten bucks, if you throw on an extra vedg or even some croutons.  It's a salad monopoly!  Lettuce highway robbery, I tell you!    At this particular location, the employees are all friendly, the place is clean and it is a hop, skip and a jump from my office, which is why I keep going back (and forking over my Hamiltons like a cucumber junkie).  It's nice to have a healthy lunch option but the quantity to cost ratio is kind of ridic, which is why I can only part with three stars.

I can't believe I'm saying this but I had my very first experience at Isgro's yesterday. I'm sure I've had their pastries before as they're a Philly institution, but yesterday marked my first visit to the store for my own order.   I placed an order by phone on Friday for a mini desserts tray that would serve 10-15 people for an event on Monday. I said I would stop by in the afternoon to pick it up, but I was out a bit earlier than expected, and got there around 1:30. The tray was nearly finished but the mini cannolis still needed to be stuffed. To me, this was a good sign because cannolis definitely have a shelf life.   The tray was gorgeous and had really nice variety: cannoli, cream puffs, pumpkin cheesecake, coconut brownies, eclairs, and more. The mini sizes were great so you could try a couple at a time. My first pick was a cannoli and it was phenomenal. I'm not typically a big cannoli person but Isgro's may have converted me - their shell was crispy crunchy and the filling had that light ricotta taste with enough sweetness to give it depth. The chocolate chips capping each side were just right.   I will definitely think of Isgro's the next time I'm having a party and need some sweets!

I have never had a bad meal here~ although I tend to order one of the same three things every time: the Mediterranean salad which has the most amazing homemade salad dressing, the pasta with vodka sauce (I usually substitute their whole wheat fettuccini for the penne that comes standard) and of course, pizza.  The food is always great; everything is homemade and very fresh.  I could probably eat here several times a week and never tire of it~ in fact, I was here on Friday night for dinner and went back again for lunch the next day.  The service was good both times this past weekend but it can get really crazy at lunch time during the week.  In my opinion though, the quality of the food and the prices are worth it!    My only gripe is that they serve their martinis with crappy little salad bar olives instead of the nice big ones~ you've gotta have the big ones for martinis!

I do declare, that Percy Street Barbecue has the best mac and cheese I have ever stuffed in my gullet.  Thick, rich, cheesy sauce and perfect noodles (not quite al dente but not the least bit soggy) are nestled under a layer of buttery breadcrumbs and served in a piping hot dish. Unreal.   Also of note is the warm German potato salad (and you KNOW I love some GPS) and the collard greens. The jalapeno cheddar corn muffin is tasty for sure, although I agree with Dan F that it leans on the too-much-butter side. Yes, that side does exist, although it's a hard one to admit.  On my recent visit I ordered pulled pork as my protein, and found it to be nicely smoked but with too many fatty bits throughout. Another BBQ spot owns my heart when it comes to pulled pork, and Percy's was good, just not as good.   The restaurant was extremely quiet during lunch hours on a weekday. Not that I'm suggesting it would be an ideal spot for corporate workers to escape Big Brother and enjoy a liquid lunch. Nope, not at all.

I have to give credit where credit is due and I can definitely say my initial feelings about Dock Street South have changed. When Covid came rolling into our lives, Dock Street started offering bake-at-home pizza kits. We ordered one in those early shelter in place days and thought the pizza was delicious. Recently, we ordered another as part of the Yelp KIT, which resulted in another great pizza night at home.   Additionally, this location has recently hired a new chef, and they were also seen rolling a pizza oven into the building recently. Happy day! I guess 2020 isn't a total bust, afterall.

I popped into Paper On Pine today to pick up a little something for my love. I ended up with little somethings for four people I love. The cards are absolutely perfect. The selection at first appears small, but when every card says exactly the right thing, you don't need aisles to choose from.   While I didn't have time to peruse the rest of the store, I have a feeling I'd love every inch of it. At check out, the (very nice) woman working there gave me a card for frequent visits. Buy ten cards and get the eleventh free. I'm already halfway there. What a great shop!

When I checked-in to PF Chang's last week, I admit that I laughed at my buddy Brian L's five star review (sorry, Bri). Admittedly, it was several years old, but five stars for a chain restaurant?  I happily ate my words after experiencing excellent service courtesy of our bartender (John) and a terrific happy hour featuring majorly discounted food and drink specials. The specials run from 3-6, an awkward happy hour time for sure, but the deals are aplenty. There's an array of discounted beer, wine and cocktails (not just one or two from each category). Food ranges from $3-7, and the portions are regular-size.   We enjoyed a couple drinks each and four happy hour plates (tuna tataki, chicken lettuce wraps, crab wontons and pork dumplings). The total was just over forty bucks. That's a mid-week dinner out that I can get behind.

I had a hankering for some sushi and always heard positive things about Fuji, so I decided to give it a try.  The restaurant is located in one of the miniature mall-type buildings on Kings Highway in Haddonfield.  The sign out front makes it relatively easy to find, and there is free parking on nights and weekends in the back.    My meal was basic, but exactly what I wanted.  Clear soup, edamame, two pieces each of yellowtail and tuna sushi plus a spicy tuna hand roll.  And a salt lick.  Just kidding.  Luckily, my salt-a-thon was followed shortly thereafter by a boot camp class.   I found some items to be a little on the pricey side when compared with other restaurants of similar caliber in the area.  Still, everything was prepared well and was of a high quality.  I would certainly recommend this restaurant to anyone in the Haddonfield area who wants great, uncomplicated sushi without having to travel very far to get it.

I hate giving only two stars to a relatively new local business, but I honestly can't bring myself to say that my brunch was "A-OK" the other day because, frankly, it wasn't.  Two seems rather low though, considering the cozy, inviting décor and the extreme friendliness of the staff.  I think two and a half would be more appropriate.    We arrived to a mostly empty restaurant at around noon on a Saturday.  A friendly gentleman (the owner?) seated us by the fireplace, which was lovely as we had just walked through freezing winds to get there.  The prix fixe brunch is $14.99 and includes coffee and orange juice, a starter course consisting of fruit with mint yogurt dressing and a homemade muffin and finally, a choice of about eight or so main dishes.    The fruit salad was mostly melons with a couple strawberry halves.  My first bite of melon was slightly prickly, but I decided to try another piece in hopes that my first was a fluke.  Unfortunately, I was met with the same results.  Moving on to the (apple chocolate chip) muffin, I took a couple bites and decided to save my calories.  Except for the very center, the muffin was extremely dry.    I was hopeful that the main course would somehow rectify the situation and make our freezing trek through the Collingswood tundra worthwhile.  My chicken crepes arrived as did my dining companion's quiche du jour, which contained lobster, spinach, mushrooms and cheese.  Both dishes looked promising but fell flat in taste.  I did enjoy the consistency of the crepe itself, which was perfect, but the tiny cubes of chicken inside left much to be desired and the overall taste was very bland.  The most noticeable flavor was the red sauce ladled on top of the crepes, which completely took over the rest of the ingredients.  The quiche was somewhat better, although my bite allegedly came from the "tastier quadrant."  Brunch was disappointing but I would like to give Bistro AmericanA another try sometime nonetheless.

I purchased the Yelp KIT from Aurora Grace and it was fantastic, as expected. Included in the $25 kit is some "ball park bark" - thin, dark chocolate speckled with popcorn and peanuts - plus a pint of vanilla bean ice cream (creamy and delicious!) and, finally, an adorable Philly Phanatic bar which has so far proven to be too cute to eat.   I placed my order online for next day pick-up and received a notification that it was ready earlier than anticipated. My husband picked up the order when he was out running errands, easy peasy. I love fancy chocolates and ice cream so I'll be keeping Aurora Grace in mind for gifts for friends (or myself) in the future!

I'm very picky when it comes to salons and nail services because I feel like you really get what you pay for. I'm willing to spend a bit more to avoid the torture of a cheap-o nail spot that has you in and out like a drive through, oftentimes with a sub-par mani or pedi and sometimes with more pain than pleasure involved. So despite the great Yelp rating, I still sent a text to Jessica T before booking my appointment with Salon Ba Si just to make sure they were all that. Although she hadn't been there in a while, she assured me it was a great spot. (Later on, when asked how I found them, I mentioned Yelp and my friend Jess. The owner perked up and described my friend to see if it was the same person. Great memory!)  I arrived to a tiny salon with only two mani stations and two pedi stations. Nice. My view of 19th Street from above was as relaxing as the next hour and a half that followed. Danin took her time and was super thorough with my service, and the stress in my world was lifted and replaced with smooth, soft skin and perfectly painted toes in a robin's egg blue. I will absolutely return.

Macy's Cherry Hill is on one helluva downward spiral. It's almost like Nordstrom arrived and the whole place just gave up and waved the white flag of defeat. The only area of the store that doesn't make me want to pull my hair out is the downstairs home area.  I'm sure it's in Macy's best interest to at least keep the bed, bath and kitchen departments up to snuff - they'd be reduced to nothing without their bridal registry business.  The shoe department is always a zoo, the lingerie/pajama department is stocked with items I'd imagine could be found in a Kmart (cheap- and tacky-looking) and the women's department is a minefield littered with detonated clothes explosions: articles falling off of hangers, draped over racks or just on the floor. Dressing rooms are outdated and just kind of gross.   It would really take a miracle to get this place back on track.

I wish I could give a separate review for the bartender (his name is escaping me), because I would give him five stars for his amazing service, great memory and the ability to keep it together while singlehandedly serving the entire restaurant and bar area.    Alas, this review is based on my entire ZoT experience, which was closer to a 2.5 but I'm rounding up.  Our very large party was somewhat urged into a $35 tasting menu, with no one really knowing what exactly that entailed.  I insisted on being a pain in the ass and requested a separate check so I could order my mussels and frites and steer clear of Jiminy Cricket.    I ordered the Bruxelles mussels, which I had read about in LaBan's review.  I was underwhelmed and expected a lot more flavor.  I tried one of the mussels from the tasting menu and liked their spiciness a lot more.    The frites were seasoned well but I would have preferred something crispier... ZoT's variety had the consistency of limp noodles.  The blue cheese dipping sauce I ordered on the side was great, though.    When the communal bill arrived at the table, shock and awe transpired over the total cost of dinner and drinks.  I was thankful to remain out of the loop.  ZoT didn't leave me with any warm and fuzzies, other than the amazing service by the aforementioned bartender.  The yelpers I kept company with, however, were pretty awesome.  Five stars to McThrill for organizing such a well attended soiree!

My friend/colleague Cara and I enjoyed a leisurely lunch at Strangelove's this week. We arrived past the usual lunch hour and there were just a few people eating at the bar. The bartender, Jill, took care of us at a nearby table.   We started with a glass of vinho verde which was slightly effervescent and went very well with the delicious pimento cheese we ordered. Next up was a round of gazpacho, which came in an enormous bowl. We both did not finish since we had salads on the way. My arugula salad was dressed in a tangy vinaigrette with a handful of grilled shrimp and pickled veggies. It was light but high on taste; I'd order it again. Looking forward to returning for dinner!

Give it up for PATCO.  In the past year, there have been drastic improvements in areas that count.  Out with the old-school magnetic tickets and arcade-like change machines, in with paper tickets from a machine that accepts ones, fives, tens and twenties.   Gone are the days when you must brandish your mace like a deranged lunatic while waiting at the stations (many of them underground) after dark; now there are security people at every stop.  Keep that mace handy while in the train though... the freaks really do come out at night.  The trains might be reminiscent of 1980, the year they were last updated, but so what?  PATCO is still a reliable, quick and affordable way for people to travel across the bridge.

The beer menu definitely has personality but besides that?  Eh.      Chips and salsa cost 7 or 8 dollars, which is crazy considering they come standard at most Mexican restaurants.  The chips bore a strong resemblance to Tostitos Gold.  Remember them?  They were the super thick yellowy chips.  I suspect you can't find them in stores anymore because Jose Pistolas probably bought them all out.      My boyfriend had a pork and pineapple burrito, which was... different, and I had the tuna tacos which were good but not memorable.    Everything is pretty much a la carte~ so if you want rice and beans with your entree you better fork over $4.  We passed.    I would go back if I was with people who wanted to go, but probably wouldn't choose to go there again myself.

I was in the neighborhood for a meeting and swung by GSpa afterwards for a mani-pedi. The sign outside suggested that they were offering $10 off this combo but when I got inside I found out that was only for the more costly mani-pedis. I decided to stay regardless, and I'm glad I did. There were tons of OPI and Essie polishes to choose from, and I had the place all to myself which was very nice. This is definitely a much nicer salon than most nail places in the city. The decor is better (more spa-like) and there's a fountain or two with trickling water.   My pedi was so relaxing and, just as importantly, not painful. The nail tech took her time and didn't rush through any part of the process. The massage she gave was absolutely wonderful, and the products used were better quality than your average spot.   My mani was just as great and I had a blast chatting with the young woman who performed my service (if you're reading this, I didn't get a ticket!). I'm adding GSpa to my list of acceptable nail salons and I will be back.

While on my way to one of my usual spots for coffee in Rittenhouse, I took a sharp left and detoured to Saxbys, since I had never been. The first thing I noticed was the expansive menu of coffee beverages. They sounded great but I know these types of drinks usually taste too sweet for me so I went with a regular coffee and requested a single shot of chocolate syrup. For $2.05, I don't know if I got that little kick of suga' for free or if Saxbys prices are just that low. Nonetheless, it made me happy. And happy people tip better.   The fixins station was a bit of a mess and in a crowded area. I think it would be better for everyone over by the ledge near the door. The staff all seemed nice. Not bad, Saxbys.

Swinging back over to the Sprouts page to share more love. This has become my go-to grocery store and I have been placing weekly orders through Instacart since the beginning of the pandemic. We do pick-up because it's super easy; just pull in to the designated spots, let the shoppers know you're there via the app, pop your trunk and you're out of there in no time.   The best thing about Sprouts is that the products are comparable to what you'll find at Whole Foods, only better priced. Cons are that their pantry and household items are limited to a couple different brands. Some products I do like, but I often have to do a Target run for things where I have a brand preference. In terms of the basics, Sprouts covers us pretty well and I am so happy to have them nearby.

I love the Stage for its large main stage and the artists that appear on it. Also, I've heard of surprise visits by some big names which has got to be an amazing thing to see when you're just there hanging out.   The place is always pretty crowded and it's difficult to get to the bar. That would be the biggest negative about The Stage. But the quality of live music and - this is important after all those beers - the gigantic bathrooms which can accommodate lots of ladies are clutch. Definitely a must-visit while in Nashville.

New Brakes, Part 2  After wasting a perfectly good lunch break on a trip to another mechanic, I returned to work, annoyed with my experience but happy that I had read my yelp friends' reviews that morning.  Brian L. had written about his recent experience at Jafstram, an auto shop within walking distance to both my apartment and job.  Brian L's car had also needed a brake job, and he had called around to other shops in search of price quotes so he knew that Jafstram was fair with their pricing.  Another established yelper had also written a stellar review for the place, so I felt like I would likely be in good hands.  I called and spoke with Brian (too many Brians in this story), who said I could bring my car in first thing on Monday morning for an estimate.    On Monday, I arrived at the garage and left my car in Brian's care.  A couple hours later, he called with an estimate and then proceeded with the brake job.  I was able to pick up the ride on my way home from work that same day.    Apparently, it's a good idea to have brakes replaced every four years, and not every five and a half.  I learned the hard way that the longer you wait, the more expensive things get, when you have to start replacing rotars and other thingamabobs that make the car run.  I'm officially on house arrest for the next few weeks or so do to EWS (empty wallet syndrome), but my ride is safer and the brakes are no longer screechy.

Elixr is one of my favorite coffee shops for meetings and brainstorming. The energy is high, the music is pumping (which sometimes makes it hard to have a conversation so I generally keep said meetings to three people max) and the caffeine is a-kickin'. Pretty sure I'm never falling asleep tonight after two afternoon coffee drinks. Also, the baristas are friendly and they always do that cute heart thing in the latte foam. I love cute hearts in latte foam!   The turnover for tables and especially the more comfy couch seating is pretty high, or maybe I've just been lucky on my past couple of visits. The people watching is prime.

My life was made easier because of Fireball Printing. With a short time frame and limited budget, I turned to the fabulous Felicia D for a recommendation that would fit my needs. She sent me Fireball's website, which was both easy to navigate and understand. I uploaded my file, gave my contact info and received a call within a couple hours.   After discussing my options, I made my decisions and gave my credit card info over the phone. One week later, 5000 postcards were delivered to my front door at no additional charge. Not only did my cards look exactly the way I wanted, but a few Atomic FireBall candies had been thrown in to boot!

I'm pretty sure I now know the true meaning of "everybody wang chung tonight."  A limo bus packed with 20 girls on a bachelorette party was my destiny on a wintry Saturday night.  Upstairs at Risque was our first stop.  No sooner had the door of the bus opened, that a beefcake jumped aboard and got acquainted with our bachelorette.  High pitched squealing ensued.  After being escorted inside and to our table, we were waited on and entertained throughout the night.  My memory remains extremely hazy about all the goings-on, but one thing remains firmly intact in my temporal lobe: DayGlo orange banana hammock.  While I don't think any of the girls plan to start frequenting Upstairs at Risque on regular weekends, I'm sure we'll all keep it in mind while planning future bachelorette parties.  Minus one star for letting people smoke inside!

Peet's coffee with a side of financial planning? Yes, please.   If you've never been to ING Café, give it a whirl for your morning cup. The beverages are cheaper than most coffee shops, and the baristas/bankers are friendly. No one will talk your ear off about a savings account or anything. If you have a question, they're happy to help, but if you don't, just get your drink and be on your way, no hassle.

I love the drive through at this Starbucks. I realize that sentence makes me sound like the laziest person alive, but I'm typically on my way to a friend's house whenever I swing by this location and the drive through is just too convenient to pass up. Everyone who works there is super friendly from my experiences and the line moves quickly. They even plug your drinks with those little green plastic things so there's no spillage. I just wish there was a more convenient way to get out of the parking lot, instead of having to drive back through the strip mall lot.

My man brought home dinner last night, in the form of a half chicken and two sides from Rotisseur. A hot and healthy meal with no kitchen prep? Sign me up!   The chicken was super juicy, tender and very flavorful. Even the pieces well below the crackling skin. Our sides were roasted potatoes and pickled veggies. While the pickled veggies were snappy and fun, I would have preferred some collard greens, spinach, green beans or basically any type of healthy, hot vegetable option. Most of the sides currently offered are starchy and heavy, like mac and cheese and corn bread. Which is totally great, but some lighter options would be most welcome.   I'm sure it won't be long before we pick up dinner again - hopefully with a heaping side of veggies to go alongside!

The building alone is worthy of five stars. Decked out with enormous windows and incredible views of both Independence Mall and the city skyline, it's a breathtaking vantage point.  My recent visit to check out the Spies, Traitors and Saboteurs exhibition, created by the International Spy Museum, was an informative and interesting one. The exhibition chronicles deviants of American history, from when the British invaded in 1812, to the rise of the KKK in the 60s, to present-day tragedies like 9/11. Seeing a mangled sign from the 76th floor of one of the Twin Towers brought tears to my eyes.   I think Tom D sums up my feelings on the Constitution Center best in saying that it is a place "that makes you really proud to be an American."

While the Midtown Tria has always been my favorite, Rittenhouse Tria has really started to grow on me as of late.  The walking proximity to my guy's place makes it the obvious choice when we want a nice glass of wine and a little bite.    The big snowstorm of Winter 2010 is when Rittenhouse Tria really warmed the cockles of my heart.  Despite the weather, the beer, wine and cheese bar was business as usual, with an abundance of pleasant servers who were up to the task of keeping guests fed and quenched.  For $5, we enjoyed glasses of 18% Dogfish Head World Wide Stout.  If that doesn't get the blood pumping on a wintry day, nothing will.  We people watched from our high-top at the back of the bar, amazed by the fact that the nail salon across the street was open, and laughing about how funny it would be if we ran off with some poor woman's snow boots as she enjoyed her pedicure.        Gotta love snow days.

I do like Plenty Cafe, but I also think that they are a bit overpriced and that there could be some improvements. My caprese sandwich yesterday clocked in at $11, before tax and a tip for the gentleman who took my order.   I got home and opened the box to find a sloppily-constructed sandwich, with balsamic soaking through the bread (almost as if it had been poured on top!), which made for a mess. I will admit, I substituted multigrain for the standard ciabatta, but it seemed like the balsamic should have been put on the side since it would have clearly soaked through (and did). Not to mention, I took it to go, and when I got home it was just a scattered mess in a box. Toothpicks to hold each half together would be really helpful here! I know this isn't the first time I've received a sandwich like that from Plenty. You'd think I'd learn my lesson!   This particular location is really cute and felt like a place I could settle in for a while on a quiet weekday. I think dining-in is the way to go with Plenty, and I'll update accordingly when I return to this location.

I just returned from lunch at Rotisseur and was thoroughly impressed. I had a craving for chicken salad, and when my boyfriend mentioned that it was served at Rotisseur, our lunch date was set. I hadn't planned on ordering any sides, but the tray of mac and cheese looked too good to resist. Also, another dish filled with something equally awesome-looking was just pulled from the oven. When we asked what it was, the guy behind the counter told us it was a new recipe and it was the first batch. It was a casserole of bread, butter and garlic. We decided to give that a shot, too.   We sat down and I admired how cute the restaurant is. It's small, but there's a decent amount of seats and even a few counter stools. The tables weren't on top of each other, either, which is nice.   A few minutes later our sides were dropped off, followed by a curried chicken salad sandwich with apricot chutney and a chicken banh mi. We split the sandwiches and shared the sides. That bread casserole thing I mentioned? Delicious. And the mac and cheese, while different from the gooey versions we all love from some of the other spots around town, held its own. I loved the cheese - gruyere, maybe? It was thick and had a bite to it. I wasn't crazy about the bread crumb pieces but that's probably because I was already on a carb overload.   The chicken salad sandwich was stuffed with chicken and huge leaves of bright green lettuce. It was really pretty. The banh mi was colorful as well, and really snappy in taste from the pickled veggies.   One thing I noticed while looking at the menu is that there are now collard greens and sauteed vegetables available as sides. I think the veggies are served only at dinner-time, but nonetheless I am really impressed that the owners decided to add these to the other offerings. Good stuff!

I am thrilled to say my crew of college friends and I escaped the room with four minutes to spare on Saturday night! We were a small group so we were placed in a room with two couples. I am pretty sure the entire group except for one of my friends was pretty tipsy, and yet we somehow still managed to get it together enough to play the game successfully.   I can't help but compare Philly's Escape The Room to my experience at Escape Room Live in DC. Escape Room Live had really nice sitting areas where you could hang out before the game and even host small parties for your group. This would not have applied for our visit the other night but it would be a nice option. Also, the game rooms were nicer in DC. Escape the Room Philly is no-frills. It is basically a section of an office building and the room we were in had the obligatory props but it was pretty bare-bones and not all that creative (although I did think some of the puzzles to figure out the clues were pretty clever). I know there is one other game room and they will soon be opening a third room in an old bank vault, but overall, the entire venue could use a little more imagination.  Would I do it again? Hell yes. My fiancé is dying to get a group together so I expect to return with a group large enough that we can have a room to ourselves. Hopefully by then there will be a few improvements to make the entire experience from start to finish more exciting.

I visited this year's PHS Pop Up Garden yesterday and left a lot less impressed than I was last year. Drinks are now cash-only which is inconvenient. Also, the beer seemed to be pouring very slowly which was causing a major back-up in the line. The move from bottled beer to draft beer somehow also came with a one dollar mark-up over last year's prices.    Food is available through the Jamaican Jerk Hut and rotating food carts. I really liked the offerings from last year's Garces Catering truck - there were some healthy items available, which was great.     Unfortunately, the bathrooms were lacking both soap and paper towels on my visit.   I'm sure I'll be back at some point this summer, but with the plethora of other outdoor beer gardens this year, I'm not rushing back.

Funny that Brian L compared Fleming's to Capital Grille in his review, because that's sort of what I was doing on my second visit there last night. My first visit was just a couple weeks ago for a charity event, so I didn't really get a good idea about the food or drinks. The private room was nice, though!  Last night, I returned with my mom and a family friend for happy hour before hitting up Rizzieri for spa services (yep, we were spoiling ourselves right before Christmas). They have a "five for $6" special that includes select wines, cocktails and appetizers. Since the house vodka is Smirnoff, we skipped the special in favor of Kettle martinis. But we did order calamari, ahi tuna and a garlicky shrimp dish from the happy hour menu.   The food was pretty great. The shrimp came in a ramekin filled with a spicy garlic butter sauce. There was a small piece of bread so we asked for more and received a warm parmesan baguette with two different whipped butters. The calamari was tossed in a slightly sweet sauce with bell and banana peppers.   For our next couple rounds of drinks we decided to try some of the wines from the special. I had a pinot grigio followed by a shiraz and both were nice. We decided to end on a sweet note, so we shared the caramel walnut turtle cake, which came with fresh whipped cream. It was absolutely awesome.   Our server was nice but I felt like I had to flag her down whenever we needed something. When our friend pulled out a card she had for a discount the server told us it wasn't good for happy hour. Then our friend pulled out another card for a comped dessert, and the server's response was just kind of awkward.  For the amount of money we plunked down on happy hour, I did think the prices were a bit high. But we enjoyed ourselves and I liked the food. I'd go back if we made plans there again but I wouldn't go out of my way.

It was a random twist of fate that brought me back to Jose Pistola's doorstep once again.  The original plan was to meet up with some fellow yelpers at The Good Dog for libations.  When I arrived at the GD however, the second and third floors were reserved for a private party and the main bar was packed.  I quickly decided that Jose Pistola's had the makings for a really solid Plan B.  Despite not loving the place the first time I was there, I knew they had a very solid beer selection and ample space for my crew.    When I walked through the doors and heard G-Love's voice oozing "my baby's got sauce," I knew it was going to be a good night.  I took my saucy self to the upstairs bar and set up shop.  Buddy the bartender was my instant amigo.  First of all, the man was setting a timer for the upcoming Flyers game and he was wearing an Eagles' shirt.  I knew this was someone I could trust with the big decisions in life, and I put my beer drinking fate in his hands.  Throughout the evening, Buddy introduced me to Triple Karmeliet, Buffalo Bill's Pumpkin Ale, Bells Two Hearted Ale and best of all, Blanche de Bruxelles.  He also gave our little group a heads-up on the good eats.  I went for the chicken quesadilla with a side of guac and it was seriously awesome.  Have I mentioned that I'm not only a member of the clean plate club, I'm also the president?    A great night was had and I am now a big fan of Jose Pistola's.  Yay for second chances!

I literally just walked in the door from my coconut manicure at Tierra Mia and I feel positively blissful. As if that didn't justify my visit enough, my nails look flawless. That's no easy feat, especially when the shade is dark. And speaking of which, one of the things I love about this salon is that you are guided through the polishes and encouraged to check them out on your nail first before committing to a color. What I originally thought I wanted turned out to be too dark but a second polish was just what I was looking for.   Treat yourself, ladies.

We popped into Green Line Cafe on Sunday for a quick iced coffee to go and, I have to say, that coffee was delicious! Smooth and flavorful; it was everything I wanted in an iced coffee!   The baristas were so friendly and we were in and out quickly. I also noticed lots of good looking baked goods as well.

I was in the mood to try something new and different, so I ordered a lunch delivery from this spot yesterday. I kept it simple and went with just the lemongrass chicken entree.   My delivery arrived quickly, but as soon as I got the bag into my house I realized the sauce from the chicken had leaked out all over the inside of the bag. The food was packed in styrofoam containers which don't exactly travel well if they're being jostled around by a delivery guy on a bike. It was a mess to clean up and the chicken container didn't have much sauce left inside.   Once I got everything onto a plate, I can honestly say the food was just all right, nothing special. I did contact the delivery service about my experience and was given a credit for a future order. Unfortunately, it won't be with Huong Tram.

I can't imagine giving the PHS Pop Up Garden any less than five stars. PHS took a vacant lot and turned it into a gorgeous urban oasis. There are picnic tables everywhere and some other casual seating areas.   The food by Garces Catering Co. is limited but everyone should be able to find something they like. I had the turkey sandwich for lunch and enjoyed it so much I had it again when I found myself hungry for dinner about four hours later! Ten bucks for a turkey sandwich is a little cray, but the minced onion jam and avocado aioli took it up a notch, and the kettle chips alongside were great. Beers are five bucks and I enjoyed several icy cold Summer Loves throughout the day.   Bathrooms were better than I expected! Probably cleaner than a lot of the bars I've visited. Can't understand why I waited so long to check this place out, but I'll take advantage as much as possible for the rest of summer!

I'm definitely a fan of Lolita's new look and the switch from BYO to boozy. I love a good margarita and the bartenders there serve them up every which way - salty, spicy, skinny, sweet - the choice is yours.   Every Mexican meal should start with some guac. I'll probably skip the charred shishito for the traditional on my next visit; I wasn't really picking up much pepper and the peas weren't doing it for me. I think I'm just a traditionalist when it comes to the green stuff. The tuna tostaditas are a total win; I was far more into those than the citrus marinated shrimp and scallops.   The cholula fried chicken tacos are fun but I think the carnitas tacos have the edge. Do not miss the fried plantains. Trust me on this one. They are fantastic!   When it comes to Mexican food, I definitely prefer the savory over the sweet. On our visit there was absolutely no room to even consider dessert.   Rumor has it late night happy hour is a go. It won't be long before the tequila calls me back.

Five stars for Hawthorne Painting! I was driving near my neighborhood when I spotted a sign for this company, and I pulled it up on Yelp as soon as I got home. I sent a request a quote message and ended up chatting with John, the owner, the same day. He stopped by to see my project, sent me a quote, and within days he and his crew were at my house!   We needed our front railing, front door, and roof deck railings to be sanded down and re-painted. Our house is only four years old but, as we've discovered, new construction doesn't always equal the best quality. John and his crew showed up bright and early around 8:30am, and worked tirelessly in the sun until the project was finished around 4pm.   John explained the differences in the types of paint he needed to use for the railings and door. Everyone in the crew was friendly and careful about their work space - by the time they left, you wouldn't have known they were even here, aside from their gorgeous handiwork! My husband and I think the railings and door look even better now than they did when we bought our house.   My only regret? Not taking before and after photos! These guys made a world of difference and I'm so happy every time I look at my front door. I highly recommend Hawthorne Painting and wouldn't hesitate to hire them again for another project.

In a word: disappointing.   I was so excited for Dock Street to open in my neighborhood but it's a struggle to continue to put my money into this lackluster business.   The positives are that the space is huge and beautiful, the people are (usually) very nice, they have a great beer program and they are open as a coffee bar during the week. I do enjoy working there with a coffee from time to time.   The food program is terrible. I had dinner there soon after they opened and didn't enjoy anything. The shrimp salad was boring and barely dressed, the potato salad was nothing special and the chicken was so dry it was a choking hazard.   Today my husband went out in the rain to grab a couple of their newly added breakfast sandwiches: one sausage and one broccoli rabe. At home (less than a five minute walk and that's being generous) we opened the boxes to find: untoasted English muffins, unmelted slices of cheese, and cold - not room temp, not lukewarm, but cold - eggs and toppings. The sausage didn't even look completely cooked and the broccoli rabe was possibly steamed but had no detectable seasoning or oil of any kind. We heated them up in our air fryer which made them edible though not necessarily good.   I won't be taking chances on the new lunch specials or any other meal for that matter unless multiple friends and neighbors tell me they've had a great experience.

I finally made it over to Stargazy today! My husband and I ordered a medley of items to-go, since we were bringing lunch to his parents' house. We ordered a beef and onion pie, the special pie of the week by Chris Kearse from Will, a cheese/caramelized onion/potato pasty, two sausage rolls, mashed potatoes with parsley liquor and a banoffee tart. This was just the right amount of food to try everything without totally over-stuffing ourselves.  Everything was absolutely delicious, as I knew it would be. I'm quite familiar with Chef Sam's cooking as I worked as a server at Sycamore back in the day. His banoffee was great then but it's even better now, served in a petite pie crust with the most perfect whipped cream ever. I still can't say the word "banoffee" correctly but at least I can say "Tottenham".   I think one of the things I have always liked about Sam's food is that it is hearty, stick-to-your-ribs fare that reminds me of the kind of stuff my Grandmom would (and still does!) make. Sam knows when to keep things simple (the mashed potatoes, for example) and also how to elevate with a little something extra (parsley liquor - genius!).   Stargazy is comfort food at its finest and I can't think of a better fit for the upcoming winter months.

Small, quirky spot that provided a solid weekday lunch and a lot of entertainment. I went one day during the summer and the Olympics were on the TV. The owner was all over the restaurant, commenting on the Olympians, chatting with the other occupied table who seemed to be regulars, dropping off coffee, etc. We chatted for a while about pierogi and I definitely want to get in there to try her version sometime.   I had either an omelet or scramble (I forget which at this point) but I do know it was delicious and there was a ton of food on my plate. They also serve their own hot sauces from mild to very hot - nice touch! Tables are small and, as I mentioned, so is the restaurant, so go expecting a solid, hearty meal and probably some very entertaining conversation then be on your way.

After a wine-filled dinner out with two girlfriends, we decided to pass on dessert and instead continue our night with an after-dinner drink.  Someone suggested L2 since it was nearby so off we went.    It felt like fate when we walked into the bar and three front and center bar stools were available.  I proceeded to order a chocolate martini from Liz, the friendly tattooed bartender who was positively jamming to the Prince CD playing in the background.  The martini was so good and seemed perfectly matched with the Goldfish crackers that were in glass milk jugs on the bar.  The combination reminded me of my youth, which was awesome.    DISCLAIMER: Next time I want to re-create a childhood snack, I'm going to stick with good old-fashioned chocolate milk, because three chocolate milks will not cause the side-splitting headache effect that three chocolate martinis (and many glasses of wine) will the next morning.  However, if I'm ever again jonesin' for ONE really good chocolate martini, L2 is my place!

This is becoming my favorite coffee shop, even though it's not in my neighborhood. The baristas are nice, and they take credit cards. I am in love with the Earl Gray tea with some steamed milk. Also, their pressed mozzarella tomato sandwich is great! I go out of my way to work at this cafe, and I don't mind a bit.

With a trunk full of soiled linens from the recent Yelper Party, I searched Yelp to find a place to get them cleaned. Maytag came up with great reviews and weekend hours. Plus, it's in my neighborhood, so extremely convenient.  I swung by on Saturday with two huge trash bags filled with linens, and the woman who worked there weighed them and gave me a receipt, saying I could pick them up later. Same day service! I ended up getting them the next day, but for more than forty pounds of linens, my charge was less than $35. Crazy! After the sheets were folded up, they all fit neatly into just one of the bags. It's cash only, but such a deal. Strongly recommended.

Three stars seems appropriate for Joe's. My husband and I were out running errands all day, when we realized it was time for dinner. In the mood for seafood, we thought it might be fun and a little bit random to try Joe's Crab Shack. The restaurant was poppin' so we decided to take seats at the bar.   The bartender who was our server was friendly, but didn't check in with us very often. The other bartender actually went out of her way to make sure we had the proper utensils, napkins, etc.   I wanted something simple and healthy so I got the cedar salmon. It was indeed simple but the fish was flavorful and the portion was pretty generous. The veggies and rice alongside were boring but, again, I was going for healthy. My husband had a steam bucket with crab legs and a medley of seafood, corn and potatoes. He was happy with his choice.   Overall, I'd say our experience was fine but probably a one and done.

Love The Lodge at the RiverRink! My husband's former company threw his farewell party there, and we had a private area catered with huge trays of Chickie's crab fries. Amazing.   I was back again for a family fun night on Saturday and we had a blast. The ice was pretty crowded for the 5pm skate but not enough that you couldn't get around without knocking into people, if you can skate somewhat strategically. I did see quite a few spills.   Our crew ice skated for probably 25 minutes tops before we decided to warm up in The Lodge. I love the selection of beers, wine and hot spiked beverages. There are also food offerings from Chickie & Pete's, Garces and Franklin Fountain. We grabbed a bunch of food to share and I have to admit the cheesesteak from C&P's hit the spot.   Why not five stars? The bathroom situation is dire. It's one of those trailer bathrooms that are often just fine, but looked absolutely gross on the night we visited. I took one look and turned right back around. The bathrooms inside the rink are a much safer bet.

Pat O'Brien's was the first stop of the day on a day that quickly went downhill due to many, many rum concoctions and little food. Of course, we went to try the Hurricanes, which come to you in all their Hawaiian Punch-red glory through a serving device that fills several glasses at the same time from a seemingly endless trough. PRO TIP: There are several bars throughout the property and, if you can believe it, they all charge different prices for their drinks. The least expensive by a quarter or two can be found at the inside bars.   The outside patio area is very pretty but also very hot (because, New Orleans). We opted for the cool temps of the inside bar, which had the smells and feels of just about every old school Irish bar out there. This is when we discovered the differing price structure of the beverages. Said Hurricanes were sweet. God only knows what possessed me to order a second after finishing that first.   I think Pat O's is a one and done type of experience for me personally, but don't let that stop you from doing as the tourists do on your own trip!

Tattooed Mom has never been my favorite spot (my last visit was probably about five years ago), but I definitely get why people dig it. On my recent visit, I discovered the upstairs for the first time. Interesting. I enjoyed finding Doggystyle in the jukebox and played almost the entire album. I also played pool (terribly) alongside Vinny P, who amazingly kept me as his partner for more than one game. Speaking of my pool partner, he graciously shared his basket of tots and I found them to be quite delicious.   Until we meet again, T-Mom's.

Jury duty: sequestered at lunch edition.   If you're ever performing your civic duty in Philadelphia and lunch is brought in from Tootsie's, you are in good hands.   Though the menu is brief and pretty basic, there was something for everyone. My turkey and cheese on wheat hit the spot, came with the correct side (chips) and a decent fruit cup for dessert. There were a solid array of choices of sides and desserts.   I'm fairly certain everyone got exactly what they asked for, so this would be a good spot when you need to order lunch for a group, or are just in need of a simple, brown bag lunch.

I desperately needed a pedi, but not anything too fabulous/expensive. Just one that would get me through the two weeks before my friend's wedding when, as one of the bridesmaids, I'll be primped and prettied up and my nails will be taken care of all over again. When I read the reviews for Boutique Nails and Hair, I saw mostly positive things from some trusted Yelpy cohorts.   The woman who took care of me was sweet, and when I mentioned that I'm training for a run she was especially careful not to go overboard on the scrubbing.   It's rare that I'll give more than 3 stars to a quickie nail salon, because I'm too spoiled by nice salons at this point. The difference in quality of products, attention to detail and overall relaxation is huge. But for a walk-in spot that smoothed over the rough edges and painted my toes a shiny candy apple red, I'm pleased with my experience.

I breezed through this store for the first time on Sunday, after seeing a cute dress on a sale rack outside the front door. As I busied myself with a rack of clothing, my boyfriend came over and whispered in my ear, "Did you see who's here?" One quick glance at the back of a curly-headed man was all I needed to see: Scott Hartnell!   Turns out, even athletes don't get out of shopping with their ladies.  The merchandise was on the slimmer side, compared with some of the larger stores on the street, but there were a few interesting pieces. I tried on a couple cute dresses that ended up fitting like a potato sack and a muumuu, in that order.   I would probably swing through the store again while in the area, but I wouldn't go out of my way for it, either.

After a long and stressful day, I typically like to finish out with a couple drinks and a bite at a quiet bar. On a recent stressful day, all I wanted was to go home and go to bed, but my man was not going to let that happen. He gently reminded me that I hadn't eaten since lunch time and that we should at least pick up something to bring home. When I relented and revealed that I had been craving a cheesesteak all week, we were off to the legendary Philip's Steaks.   I waited in the car watching for the nearest PPA agent to jump from the shadows while my fiancé went to retrieve our food. He was back to the car in moments, bags in hand. At home, we shared an "Old Fashioned" steak, topped with provolone, tomatoes and super hot peppers. For me, they were actually a touch too hot and I had to do some work to pull off a bunch of those little seeds so that I could get through my half. But damn, was that steak tasty. I really enjoyed it, fire-in-mouth notwithstanding. The cheese fries were also delish - tons of cheez whiz on those suckers. I would have preferred a touch more salt on the fries, however. We shared this meal in near silence over our kitchen counter and it could not have been a more perfect or appropriate way to end the night.   If you haven't been to Philip's, add it to your cheesesteak rotation pronto.

Last night I checked out Vie for the second time after being invited to the John DeBella Comfort Food Fest. My first visit was for the PhillyMag party last summer, and the place was just barely in functioning order. It was more of a swanky warehouse than an event venue at that point. Several months later, it looks like Vie is almost ready. I say almost because while the interior was complete, the outside patio area is still under construction. But that patio will really make the venue, and it will certainly make for a huge advantage over most of the city's other event spaces.      I do wish the decor was just a little more modern. While it shies away from the traditional ballroom style for the most part, some elements remain. The chandeliers are mismatched and the larger ones in the center of the room come off looking a bit tacky (in my opinion).   The bar area is nice and big and I like how the one bar functions to serve both the reception area and the event room. Although, the black bar has a barely visible ledge that probably sees many spilled drinks each night. Bartenders at this particular event gave off that very busy vibe even though the crowd at the bar was fairly minimal.
