If you've read my reviews of other event spaces, you'll know that I am not a traditionalist and so this space, while newer and nicer than some others, probably wouldn't be my first choice when planning a personal event. I'm looking forward to seeing the finished patio, which could change my mind completely.

I'm a fan of Veda. In fact, I find their food very comparable to my favorite Indian restaurant (IndeBlue), only slightly less expensive. I've dined in for dinner and have also done delivery, which was my most recent experience. It's the delivery experience that brings this rating down to three star territory.    After reading some of the reviews, we knew to order rice, because people mentioned that they did not receive rice with entrees. Well, it seems Veda has since changed, because we received double the rice. I really think the online ordering system should indicate that rice comes with entrees, so people don't spend an extra few dollars for no reason. At the very least, the business could have called us to confirm that we wanted two orders of rice instead of just the one that comes with the entree.  My other gripe is that we ordered the tandoori chicken and thought we were receiving boneless kabobs, since the dish is listed under the kabobs section. However, the chicken was served on the bone. This would have been useful information because we would have ordered something else. Again, it comes down to the lack of description in the online ordering system.    The vegetable samosas, garlic naan and chicken tikka makhani were all delicious. Veda, please make your online ordering a bit more user friendly!

I've been to Founding Fathers three times. The first was during an Eagles game, and it was so crowded that our group left right away, knowing it would be very difficult to even get up to the bar. So, I probably won't be going back during any major sporting events, despite the plethora of large TVs on every wall.   My next two visits were for a late dinner. Bianca was our server on both occasions and she was friendly and did a great job. It seems like this bar hosts a lot of loud twenty-somethings and I'm sure that doesn't always make for an easy night.   The food is fairly average, maybe a little above, but I've also only tried some of the small plates. Flatbreads are good but could use a couple more minutes in the oven, and the chicken fingers are great but you get four for nine dollars which is crazy. The beer selection is solid. I also like that the high tops along the wall have lots of room and feel a bit further from the crowd than the high tops closer to the bar area. Overall, solid spot for a casual meal.

What can be said that hasn't been said already? The Philadelphia Museum of Art is a landmark in Philadelphia and a beautiful place to spend an afternoon while taking in some culture.   I attended the Van Gogh exhibit recently with a friend and though the lines were long and the museum was crowded, I thought the staff did a nice job keeping things moving. The audio tour was just great. You could view pieces and listen to the narration at your own pace. While the narrators were a bit stuffy, it was nice to learn something about the art and the artist, and it definitely beat listening to certain self-important guests who were loudly voicing their own opinions.   Last summer I enjoyed taking some bootcamp classes right on the famous steps of the museum. As I squated, sprinted and lunged my way around the courtyard, the experience was made somewhat bearable with the distraction of beauty and the occasional mist of the fountain.   I'm dying to check out Art After 5, a live music and art reception held on Friday evenings. Snacks and cocktails are available for purchase, which is really fun.  We're lucky to have such a great home for art in Philadelphia!

I was making homemade crunchwraps and needed tostadas. Harder to find than you might think, even at the giant grocery stores I occasionally visit in the 'burbs. That said, I knew exactly where I'd find them in Philly, so I sent my husband on a mission to Tortilleria San Roman, where he secured a fat stack.   The tostadas are perfectly crunchy and ideal for recipes, or breaking apart and dipping into every last queso/salsa/hot sauce you've accumulated during this crazy year. The bonus was getting to support a local business, even whilst cooking my own dinner for a change.

Just off the plane from Philly to St. Louis, I was in desperate need of some caffeine and a bite. To Kaldi's we went, where an oasis of coffee beverages and healthy food options awaited.   The baristas were friendly and funny - love that. I ordered an iced coffee and a chickpea wrap which came stuffed with quinoa and kalamata olives and came with a choice of side. I picked the chips, which were super thin, perfectly crunchy and just a little salty. The wrap was filling and delicious but didn't make me feel super weighed down.   I noticed some outdoor seating which would be great on a nice day. This is a great spot for a solo working lunch, coffee meeting or gabfest with a friend.

I've come to like honeygrow a bit more over the past year or so. The machines can still be a little finicky at times but nothing like they were when I wrote my last review. I love being able to customize my salad to my exact needs without annoying anyone in the process. The ingredients are always fresh and I love the dressing options (I usually opt for one of the vinaigrettes). This is one of my go-to spots for a healthy salad. The juices are solid as well.  I do hate the bowls they use, because if you cut your salad, the bowl will topple over and your ingredients will go flying and you will rage. You. Will. Rage. For this reason, I usually transfer my salad to a sturdier bowl at home.   Fresh. Healthy. Friendly employees. Worthy of an upgrade to four stars.

I really loved this adorable bagel shop my sister brought me to when I stayed at her house a couple weekends ago. If I lived in the area, it would undoubtedly be the place where I would set up shop a couple times a week. It's cozy, with the brick oven cooking bagels and lots of comfy seating and coffee tables. Looks like they have lunch options in addition to breakfast.  Love that they serve La Colombe, and loved even more that they had bags of beans for sale as well, since I needed to stock up. While I didn't get my own bagel that day, I did try a bite or two of my sister's, which was delicious. Can't wait to go back next time I visit and eat all the carbs.

I put off trying Zama for far too long. I'm not sure why, but it was a foolish decision in hindsight after two fantastic meals at the hands of this very talented chef. My first experience took place a couple weeks ago at a Cook class. The several course meal was impressive, and I quickly requested a venue change for my upcoming birthday dinner with my boyfriend.   Saturday was the big night. I entered the new (to me) incarnation of my former stomping grounds (Loie, RIP). The lighting was dim and the blonde slats adorning the walls made for an attractive atmosphere. I requested a martini with olives and stressed that I wanted it just the teeniest bit dirty. It seems that every time I ask for this, my drink comes back too salty ninety percent of the time. But our server was listening and, more importantly, the bartender was listening, and the two martinis I ordered during our evening were perfect.   We started off with pan fried dumplings, which were great. What's not to love about a dumpling? These were better than average. Next, Kirin braised short ribs over crunchy noodles. Damn this dish was good. Things were off to a great start. The hamachi tataki had been a feature at our Cook class, and it was just as delicious a second time.   My favorite of the night, a dish that I will lust over until the next time I have it, was the king crab oshizushi. Words fail me in trying to describe this buttery, delectable delight. Just trust me. After that, the maki paled in comparison but it was still very good. The surfer roll and the wasabi tuna roll were both very tasty and I'd order either again.   We passed on dessert and went off into the night. In the days since, I've had Zama on my mind like a new crush. I'm thinking threesome.

My husband and I went out for a long stroll around the city on Labor Day, and one of our first stops was Cira Green. To be honest, I didn't really know what to expect, but I was very pleasantly surprised by the beautiful, well-maintained space. There was hardly anyone around on such a gorgeous day, so the park felt like a fun secret between the few people who were enjoying some time there.   The views of the city are absolutely beautiful. Because of the building's proximity to the Schuylkill River, you get the river views as well as the skyline views in all directions.   I hope to get back soon and I plan to bring a picnic along!

At the eleventh hour leading up to my mom's birthday get-together, there was only one place that I felt confident would provide a suitable gift. Funny thing is, I had never even set foot in Verde. But I had been on the receiving end of a beautiful pair of earrings for Christmas last year (thanks, Art!), plus I had read enough positive reviews from trusted friends.  I immediately took in all the gorgeous handbags, scarves and jewelry... and their corresponding price tags. Some were way out of my price range but there were enough items that fell safely in the comfort zone. After touching just about every scarf in the store and scrutinizing every piece of jewelry, I eventually settled on a pink scarf and a lighter pink bracelet, with heavy stones. I was even able to nab a birthday card by the register, and the bag with tissue paper was nice enough to forgo a more formal wrap job.  My mom loved the bracelet. Loved. The scarf, on the other hand, wasn't really her style. Back to the store I went just two days later, receipt at the ready. I was able to exchange the scarf, no questions asked, for another item (which was slightly more expensive, natch). And if Mom doesn't like the replacement, I'm keeping it for myself.

If we were voting on decor alone, I'd give the place 5 stars, hands-down.  The place is so cute inside and I did not run out of things to look at the entire 2+ hours I was there for brunch on Sunday.  The crabcake sandwich I had was really good and served with a nice fruit salad on the side.    My only gripe is that it was extremely warm in the restaurant~ I was sweating the entire time I sat at the bar while waiting for my friends.  Other than that, fantastic place and I'd be inclined to bump my review up to 5 stars if I go back and have another great, less hot-flashy, experience.

In case you haven't heard, Sidecar's upstairs bar/dining room is open for service! We swung by last night with friends to check it out and everyone agreed that the exposed brick, retro banquettes and tables and large windows with a pretty view of the skyline were on point. It's a totally different vibe and yet somehow the same old Sidecar. Great servers, awesome beer. Two thumbs up.

This is pretty much the nicest public library I've ever been to. It's enormous. More like something you'd find on a college campus. Now I know where Cherry Hill taxpayer dollars are going.   My little cousin held a film premiere (yes, really) in one of the rooms on the lower level. I think my aunt said it was around $150 to rent and it fit ~100 people. So on a meeting space standpoint, that's not too shabby.

Oops!  I was wrong in my previous review when I said that Severino pastas only come frozen or dried. Some varieties are also available fresh. I know this because I have a pound of whole wheat fettuccine packaged neatly in a little box, ready for dinner tonight.   Another thing I noticed while in the store today is that the cheese selection is no joke. I literally swooned when I saw a big block of etorki, which I previously thought was only available at DiBruno Brothers (in this area, anyway). If summer wasn't just around the corner I'd be serving a cheese course tonight as well. Le sigh.

I have only great things to say about Rittenhouse Women's Wellness Center. I had long been thinking about the fact that my last well-visit physical was back when I went to a pediatrician. A friend sent around an email last fall about her great experience at this office, and I saved the email in my inbox, where it sat for months. A few weeks ago, I received a pamphlet from RWWC in my mailbox, and I took it as a sign that I should make an appointment. I noticed all of the positive reviews from my Yelp friends and felt confident in my decision.   The receptionists were great, the waiting area wasn't congested, and the office is very nice in general. My scheduled visit started right on time. My appointment was with Dr. Rowbotham, and she was professional, knowledgeable and thorough. We talked about my lifestyle and history for a good twenty minutes before the exam.   I feel great that I've taken steps to be proactive about my health. I received some really helpful advice that I've been applying, and soon I'll be hearing back about my basic bloodwork. I'd recommend this office to any woman who needs a general practitioner.

My sister and I both ended up buying our wedding dresses at Bridal Garden, about a year apart from each other. I felt that my experience was very solid. On my first visit, I had no expectations of finding a dress. I was paired with Donna, who was a perfect match because she listened to what I wanted in a style, and didn't overwhelm me with options. I tried on five dresses and the moment number five was zipped, I just knew that I found the dress. Before committing, I still went to one other store just to be sure, but I couldn't stop thinking about the dress I had tried on at Bridal Garden, and I scheduled another appointment to try it on once more. After that, a deposit was put down for the dress!   I got a call right around May or June that the dress was in, and I scheduled my first fitting. The woman who does all of the alterations is wonderful. She's a no nonsense lady who knows all the right things to say during the many fittings leading up to the final, while keeping things moving. Fittings were at the top of my list of most stressful moments leading up to my wedding, so five stars for her! My dress didn't need many alterations and it was just right on wedding day.   The reason I can't give five stars across the board is because of the bridesmaid dress situation. Most of my bridesmaids were from out of state and had to order dresses over the phone by providing their measurements. Nearly all of my bridesmaids were told to order sizes that were way too big and everyone with the exception of one 'maid (who ordered the size she thought she needed, rather than the size that was recommended to her by the woman at BG) needed expensive alterations. I'm sure Bridal Garden wants to cover their butt so no one gets a dress that is too tight, but when a size 8 girl is told to order a size 14 dress, something is wrong. I've heard from lots of people who have had this experience at Bridal Garden so I know it wasn't just a fluke. Bridesmaids from afar, find a store that carries the collection in your area and try on the styles so you know what size you should order.

I'm picking up what you're putting down, Bardot. The dark and sexy bar is perfect for a date or small group. And the tiny, tucked-away parlor with curtain would be perfect for a scandalous liaison.   The staff was sweet but not entirely up to speed on menu items. The buttery shrimp were served head-on, though when I asked before ordering I was told that they were served only with the tails still attached. Minor, but enough of a turnoff for me that I probably would have opted for a different plate. The octopus dish was a win amongst our table of three, and I simply could not get enough of the spaetzle with purple cauliflower. It was perfect.   Our server recommended cocktails for my friends while I tried the Côtes du Rhône Blanc, which I deeply enjoyed. I can't wait to go back for another glass, some more French pop, and that delicious-looking burger that accidentally almost made its way to our table.

I'm going to update my rating to three stars, because I enjoyed my lunch on Saturday. But, I still feel pretty strongly that some of the sides could be tweaked a bit for better taste. My German potato salad and sauerkraut were both served ice cold. I don't get it! German potato salad is delicious at room temp, and who eats sauerkraut cold?! To be honest, I order these sides because they aren't as heavy as some of the other options. I really wish a little more care was put into the way they are presented.   My quarter pound of pulled pork was smokey, full of flavor and delicious! And my husband's burnt end beans were equally awesome.   I really do like Fette Sau, but I still don't love it.

My visit to Lemon Hill started off at their media night party, but after having such a good time chatting with the staff and enjoying a few cocktails, a few of us decided to get a table when the party ended and the restaurant opened to the public for dinner.   We ordered a round of drinks and a few apps to share. I had already enjoyed an old fashioned and two Blues Explosion cocktails, so I opted for a beer to avoid getting completely blotto on a Tuesday.   Bites included roasted tomato soup with blue cheese popovers, pastrami chicken wings and beer cheese fondue. We also got to try a couple different items during the party, which included a chicken flatbread with pickled yellow tomatoes that was insanely tasty. The pickled tomatoes popped with flavor against the heavier components.   The tomato soup was nice; the popovers provided a good texture and nice bite. I wasn't a fan of the pastrami chicken wings but everyone else seemed to really like them. A matter of taste, I guess! The beer cheese was delicious. What's not to like about a melted crock of cheese with pickled red onion and peppadews, plus toasted bread for dipping?   Event though I only sampled a few different bites and some fab cocktails, I really enjoyed the warm vibe Lemon Hill exuded. I can't wait to return the next time I want to get out of my own neighborhood and into somewhere cozy.

This PJs has definitely made some major improvements since my last review more than five years ago. At the time, Iron Hill had rolled in around the corner and seemed like a shinier, better option. But over time, my loyalties have remained with PJs. They definitely went through a rough patch but my handful of visits over the past few years have all been solid.   The beer program has improved from a selection of domestics to an array of craft brews for every taste. Their wings are awesome and I love that they have so many different types of buffalo-style choices like wraps, salads and sandwiches. Big fan.

I randomly parked my car right next to Tela's when I was running to the nearby state store. As I got out of my car and looked at the window, I couldn't believe my luck with landing smack in front of a local grocery, since picking up a few items for dinner was next on my list.   Walking in, I was so impressed by the stock - it's a small but very well-curated selection. They had every single thing I needed, from minced garlic to zucchini and yellow squash to prepared items and more. I picked up all of the ingredients for a veggie recipe, plus some twice baked potatoes to go with my dinner, and a pre-made chicken wrap for lunch the following day.   The employees were super friendly and knew where everything was located. All of the produce was very fresh and high quality.   The honey mustard chicken wrap I had for lunch today was gigantic. In my opinion it was a little heavy on the honey mustard sauce - I wish they went a little lighter on that and maybe put some extra sauce on the side, instead. But all in all, a filling lunch for less than ten bucks (and the chicken itself was delicious).   The prices were probably in line with what I'd pay at Whole Foods, minus the crowds, headaches, or crappy produce I've come to expect from that store. I don't mind paying a little more to support a local grocery with great products. I wish there was a Tela's in my neighborhood!*   *Graduate Hospital, in case you Tela's folks get any ideas!

Super cute boutique on Pine that I never even knew existed until Friday. I popped into Hello Home thinking they sold baby gear, and was told that only their location in Rittenhouse has a baby section. The woman working also told me that Industry just down the street stocked a small amount of baby merchandise.   I had ten minutes on my meter and no more quarters so I needed to make things snappy. It's probably a good thing, because I saw a lot of cute stuff as I rushed my way to the back of Industry. I could have easily done way more damage with some more time. The baby selection was small but there were some really cute Philly-centric onesies, which was exactly what I was hoping to find. The gentleman at the counter took off the price tag and wrapped the onesie in a cute box with a twine bow. I love when I don't have to wrap gifts! I'll definitely return, perhaps for my own perusal.

Solid experience from The Original Turkey yesterday. Options are fairly limited, which is actually great because it helps to keep the line moving. The line was maybe ten people deep when I jumped on and it moved pretty quickly.   I ordered the turkey sandwich with lettuce, tomato and choice of cheese. I opted for rye and asked for one slice of swiss - no mayo. I also asked for toasted bread. Turns out, if you want toasted, they just pop your sandwich onto a press. I like that! I also got a small side of coleslaw and some pickles. The coleslaw was a bit mayo-heavy for my liking but I did enjoy the sweet taste with the saltiness of the pickles. All together I think my order was in the neighborhood of nine dollars and I can definitely get on board with that.

After reading a few reviews the other day, I decided to pop over to El Fuego for some cheap margaritas and a bite. My first discovery was that the place was more fast foodish than I was expecting. My second discovery was that the margaritas only come frozen, which basically equates to about a zillion calories each. I got my cheap frozen margarita and some chips and guacamole and settled in to watch some March Madness hoops while waiting for my friend.  I actually loved the guacamole, which had a ton of citrusy lime flavor. I always like a little bite to my guac, though. The chips were decent enough, but the hot salsa was more like a hot taco sauce - I should have asked for some pico instead. My margarita seemed pretty weak, but it was hard to tell through all the sugary sweetness.  About twenty minutes in, a homeless man wandered in, sat down at the table next to me, and proceeded to yell at the TV for a solid ten minutes or so. No one did anything. In fact, no one seemed the slightest bit fazed, which I thought was really strange.  Clearly, my expectations of El Fuego were something far above what the place actually is: A fast food burrito joint along the likes of Chipotle, only with a liquor license. Bottom line, skip the alchy and take your order to-go.

Surprises like Pentridge Station Beer Garden are why I love Philly. My husband and I were checking out the new Dock Street Cannery when we overheard our bartender talking with another couple about a new beer garden a few blocks away. After dinner at Dock Street Brewery, we decided to check it out.   We walked over to Pentridge and gave each other a look: this street has a beer garden?! The street is filled with a bunch of car garages and there were a lot of people hanging out. We kept walking and could make out an umbrella with a beer logo, and then, a big open lot filled with wood chips, some makeshift tables, chairs, games like giant Jenga and bean bag toss, and some stuff for kids. I think it was only night two so I would imagine they will add more to the space as time goes on.   The garden was cash-only on our visit but we were told that credit cards will be accepted soon. The boozy mint lemonades with Jim Beam were tasty but tiny for $5. I really liked that they have hookah available - something fun that you don't see at other beer gardens! There was also a guy playing the guitar and singing and he was really great!    The only option for bathrooms is a couple port-a-potties, which is ultimately why we only stayed for a couple drinks before calling it a night. Also, I don't think they serve food in the garden itself, but there was a street cart just outside and if we hadn't just had dinner we would have hit that up for sure.   This beer garden doesn't have the bells and whistles of most others, but I dig what they are doing and could see myself coming back again this summer.

My husband has been raving about Burg's forever, and I'm so glad I finally took his recommendation and tried it for dinner with a friend. The decor is super cute; think relaxed surf shack vibes. The menu of drinks and food is short but sweet. What they do in the food department, they do very well.   My friend ordered the lone cocktail on the menu, which was some sort of fresh watermelon punch, served in a fun tiki glass with a fistful of fresh mint. It was delicious! I was feeling super basic so was happy to see Coors Light among the list of much tastier yet heavier craft brews.  We ordered a bunch of plates from the menu - they are so affordable, how could you not?! We had edamame, mushroom and kimchi spring rolls, miso cod, tuna poke, cucumber salad, and also a surprise from the kitchen - mixed olives which I believe were lightly dusted with fennel pollen and served with some orange rind. Everything was delicious and light - even the spring rolls had a very thin wrapper and didn't seem greasy.   In short: I loved Burg's and can't wait to return!

This gated storage facility is clean, easy to get in and out of, and not too scary. Well, it's a little scary when the light timer runs out and you get stuck in the dark, but other than that, not too bad.   The rental fee for a very small closet is edging ever closer to $100 per month, but I have to say, I'm happy to have a place that isn't my own apartment to store all my schwag.   I also hope to one day become friends with the VitaminWater rep.

On a cold night before Christmas, we stopped by Sassafras for drinks that were magnificent and bordering on magical. It was a Friday, and the bar was packed, but my man and I nabbed a high top and enjoyed some Great Lakes Christmas Ales and spiked hot ciders while taking in the very festive holiday decor. Nearby, a couple dined on the most delicious smelling burger. I knew I had to get back and try the food.   Last week, a friend/business contact suggested Sassafras for our lunch meeting, and I didn't have to think twice. It turned out to be a great decision. Sassafras got sassy all up on my taste buds when I bit into the bison burger with cheddar and sauteed onions. Absolutely delicious. The patty was perfectly seasoned and so flavorful, but it was much leaner than a beef burger so it didn't feel like a lead weight in my stomach all afternoon.   Our side of sweet potato fries was an excellent move as well. These were the best sweet potato fries I've ever had, and I had no problem saying it over and over. Surely I sounded like a parrot. The fries were crispy and crunchy (that almost never happens with sweet potatoes!) and the spicy ketchup and garlic aioli dipping sauces just added to the awesomeness.   Totally looking forward to my next visit.

I'm still very much a fan of Garces Trading Company. Armed with a pretty hefty gift card, my husband and I had a fantastic dinner on a recent Saturday night. The place was packed, so reservations are clearly a must for the weekend.   Our server was very knowledgeable about the wine list and made great suggestions. We shared a bunch of starters including some cheese and charcuterie, housemade mozzarella and olives. Olives are on so many menus as a small plate and don't differ much from place to place. Not at GTC: their olives were addictive. There were three types including a green sort that had a rich, almost cheesy flavor. I feel like our server said they were Castelvetranos but I can't be positive. Maybe it was just a super fresh batch, but they were incredible.   For dinner, I had to go with the steak frites. I couldn't decide on the sauce so our server suggested a sampling of all three, which was music to my ears! As always, this dish was a home run. My husband had the trout, which is always delicious as well.   We skipped dessert in favor of more wine and some espresso to finish. Looking forward to our next visit!

Sometimes you don't appreciate the things you have until you see them from someone else's point of view. Morgan's Pier, for example. I bumped into a friend from Manhattan there a few weeks ago and he was really impressed with the space and the mixed crowd. That wasn't exactly how I would have described Morgan's Pier prior to that moment, but when I actually looked around at the crowd that night, it truly was varied. And everyone seemed to be having a great time doing their own thing, whether it was dancing, drinking, eating or just hanging out.    I've gone with large groups twice so far this year and both were mostly positive experiences. There will always be extremely drunk people in a sizable place like this, and I had a drink spilled all over me on the first night, which was obviously annoying. I do think the security staff does a pretty good job keeping an eye on people but things happen.     We ate dinner the second time and the food was great. Props to George Sabatino for holding it down. We shared the scallop crudo, a cheeseburger and fries and the whole fish of the day. The crudo was nice, the cheeseburger and fries were both solid, and the fish was incredible. On that night it was served with a chopped tomato salsa with some avocado, and the fish was cooked with fennel and orange stuffed inside. It was excellent. We also rarely came across any bones.   Getting a drink can be a challenge but the smaller bar to the back left seems to be less crowded. I'm looking forward to spending a bit more time at Morgan's Pier this summer!

I attended a showing of the play Bachelorette with a couple friends last night. Before then, I had never heard of the Adrienne Theater, and I was surprised when we arrived to a multi-purpose building that seemed to have a lot of different theater spaces within. Bachelorette was in the Sky Box, all the way up the staircase.   The stage was small but the set was cool, and every seat in the small theater was filled. Even from my position in the last row on the end, I could still see and hear everything just fine. I'd definitely attend a show there again.

My husband and I celebrated our first wedding anniversary at Le Chéri, and it turned out to be an excellent choice. I had previously only been there for drinks in the amazing garden outside. Though a cool, drizzly fall night kept us indoors for our dinner, the dining room is beautiful and romantic. I love, love, love the French pop playing in the background.   The wine list is insane and the servers are excellent with providing suggestions for pairing with courses. I started with the French onion soup - this version was more sweet than salty and very well balanced. The escargot was also delicious. Next up, my husband and I shared a middle course of butternut squash ravioli with mushrooms and pumpkin seeds (I think those were the ingredients, anyway!). This was great but I had to keep it to just a few bites since I was already getting full (blaming the bread basket!).   My main course, filet mignon with au poivre sauce and darphin potatoes, was perfection. My husband's whole fish special was expertly filleted tableside and was also very delicious.   I was far too full for dessert but happily partook in an after-dinner cocktail. J'adore le Chéri! À la prochaine!

The last time I wrote something about Tinto was almost seven years ago. I didn't think it was a five star restaurant. Silly youngin'!    A few weeks ago, my husband and I returned for dinner. The decision to head to Tinto was made in the late afternoon but reservations were still available so we made one to secure our spot. We were seated right away in a comfortable, cozy booth towards the back of the restaurant.   We shared several plates including the arugula salad, pulpo, prawns, brussels sprouts, mushrooms and paella. The pacing of the courses was absolutely perfect - we were able to enjoy each dish without becoming overly stuffed. In fact, we had about half of our food boxed up and enjoyed the same meal at home the following night! Our server was knowledgeable about both the food and wine list - he made some great recommendations and we really enjoyed the many wines we tried throughout the meal.   This dinner was a bit of a splurge for a random weeknight, but considering we had dinner for the next night too, it wasn't really so bad. I loved our meal and am looking forward to a return visit sooner than later!

Located on what is probably one of the most beautiful, majestic streets in Philadelphia is the Rosenbach Museum & Library. I stopped by for a tour recently and was really taken by some of the beautiful pieces and the stories behind them. My docent of the day, Elyse, knew everything there was to know about each item and the museum itself. Truth be told, I felt like a royal dum dum, knowing next to nothing about art history, but I was assured that most people aren't overly familiar with many of the works. That, or Elyse was trying to make me feel better. It worked!  My favorite piece was a Thomas Sully portrait of Rebecca Gratz, a well-known Philadelphia socialite in the 1800s. The tale behind the woman is a truly fascinating one, and I was inspired enough to do my own research.   I'd encourage anyone with a little extra time to spare to go and find his or her own muse within the walls of the Rosenbach.

How I love this place! Georgetti's is the quintessential neighborhood prepared foods grocery. It's a one stop shop for a delicious meal for one or ten (or more - they cater!).   I'm honestly not a big fan of cooking, so any ally that assists in getting a delicious meal on the table is a huge plus. From fresh breads to homemade soups, dressings, pastas, sauces and more, I generally pick up anywhere from two to five meals' worth of groceries whenever I make a stop.   Georgetti's pumpkin bisque kicks off my family's Thanksgiving dinner and their lobster bisque is a staple in our annual feast of seven fishes for Christmas Eve. This business is truly one of the best and I'm so grateful it exists!

I was totally stoked to check out the Philly version of Fette Sau. Hate to say it, but I was really disappointed. The meats are smoked and not saucy; you can add your own sauce once you are at the table. We had a few different meats and they were okay but I do prefer a saucier style of BBQ.   The real disappointment was in the sides. The sauerkraut was served cold. It was crunchy. Let me repeat: crunchy, cold, sauerkraut. Who likes that? The German potato salad was also cold. GPS is often served at room temperature which is just fine, but this was refrigerator cold and lacking in any tangy, delicious flavor. It was so weak. The only side I really enjoyed was the baked beans.   Fette Sau doesn't come cheap, either. For that reason, I guess I can look at the bright side and be grateful that I'm not a fan.

I went to The Mann on Saturday night for Jaws with the Philadelphia Orchestra. I had first seen an advertisement on a billboard, and thought it sounded fun. When I got a promotional email about it a couple weeks later, I took it as a sign and bought tickets. There is a lot of language about how the shows are rain or shine and not all seats are covered. This scared me into spending over $50/each for covered seats.   We arrived and I was really impressed with the cleanliness of the venue, variety of food and beverage options, and helpfulness of the staff. Our seats were in a balcony box which an usher helped us locate. It started out as a beautiful night, so when we needed a drink refill, we decided to relocate to the grassy area which is perfect for a picnic. Tip for lawn seaters: bring bug spray! We probably would have been fine had we stayed in our seats, but once we moved to the open air we were eaten alive.   We made it almost to the end of the movie before the skies opened up, forcing us under cover. There were a lot of empty seats so we actually just grabbed the first ones we saw in a covered area. Ushers didn't seem to stop anyone from doing this though I'm sure it would be a different story with a more crowded event.    My only complaint about the entire evening is that we had a hell of a time trying to access an Uber. There was traffic everywhere after the show and we had to walk in pouring rain across a soaked field to get to the main street where we'd have an easier time getting a car. Not sure if there's much that can be done about this but it's worth mentioning for anyone who plans to use a ride sharing app.   I would definitely love to visit The Mann again for another casual event like the one we attended, but I'd likely chance it with the less expensive lawn seats. There's nothing like sitting outside on a beautiful summer night while enjoying some entertainment!

My last experience with the M.P. was in college.  It was great fun at the time but that was five years ago and my palate has matured to bigger, better, less chain-oriented cuisines... or so I thought.  For whatever reason, my sister was hell-bent on going here for her graduation dinner, and that's exactly what we did last night as a family.    The six of us piled into a table that had 3 burners; which meant that the people who sat across from each other got to choose their cheese, broth and chocolate together; instead of all six people trying to agree on only one of each for the entire table.  I believe this significantly cut down on any possible family bickering - awesome.  My sis and I were partnered up and we went for the cheddar fondue for our cheese course.  It was predictable but delish.  Even better was the spinach & artichoke cheese that my Dad and brother were sharing next to us.    The salad course was very good; there were about five or six choices and everyone seemed happy.  Things got rather tricky when the cooking broth arrived in a contraption that looked like it was straight off of the "Deal or No Deal" set.  Our server, while polite, didn't really explain things completely to those people at the table who had never dined there before.  So naturally, as soon as the plates of raw meat were set down, my dad picked his up and proceeded to dump half of the contents directly into the broth.  Hilarious!  My brother (who was paying a little more attention) declared that the pieces still on the plate were his, and my dad could fend for himself with the search and rescue spoon that was provided.  Overall, the meat and veggie portion of the evening was good but everyone was ready to move on to dessert--  WHICH WAS FUCKING PHENOMENAL.  My sis and I chose the "Flaming Turtle" (milk chocolate & caramel, flambeed and mixed with chopped pecans), Dad and bro got the "Chocolate S'Mores" (milk chocolate & marshmallow cream, flambeed and mixed with graham cracker pieces) and my stepmom and 7 year old bro got... something else.  They were too far away for me to hit up their pot for a sample and so I didn't really pay attention.  The dippers included cheesecake, pound cake, brownies, rice crispy treats, graham-covered marshmallows, chocolate graham-covered marshmallows, bananas and strawberries.  Never in my wildest dreams did I ever expect the highlight of my week to happen on a Monday night; yet I say with confidence that nothing this week could possibly top the goodness that was dessert fondue at the Melting Pot.      Bravo, The Melting Pot Restaurants Inc., for making me a believer in chains once again!

I'm really not a big casino person, but I thought Parx was pretty solid!   Driving into the massive complex, I thought the parking lot was pretty confusing; it wasn't really clear to me even with the signage where anything inside the casino was located. I finally spotted my destination (the beer garden) via signage on the building, and ended up parking in a lot that seemed kind of close but was still located pretty far from an entrance.   I left my coat in the car and opted to walk college-style into the building because I did not want my coat to smell like cigarette smoke from the casino. Turns out, that probably would not have been a problem, since the beer garden was located beyond another restaurant which prevented any detectable smoke from seeping into the vicinity.    The beer garden itself was awesome! The TVs were the largest I have ever seen outside of an actual sports arena. I loved watching the Sixers and my husband had fun with the sports betting machines, where he won a few bucks betting on who would score next in a hockey game. We sampled a few snacks and I was very impressed with everything I tried. My only suggestion would be to add some non-alcoholic beverage options to the menu (a beer garden should probably have at least one NA beer - even Chickie & Pete's had Heineken 0.0!).   Later, we moved onto Chickie & Pete's for a late night bite, and we had a good experience there as well, though it was a much louder, music pumping type of vibe.   The casino floor was quite crowded but it was so smokey I don't know that I'd want to spend any time there playing games. That said, I'd be happy to return just to hang in the beer garden and watch some sports!

After perusing the Yelp reviews on Foo Truck, I decided the green curry quinoa foo'wich sounded like a winner. The contents were secured in a perfectly folded tortilla, which looked like it had been pressed for extra measure and a little crunch. The delicious pocket stayed intact even through the last few bites -impressive!  The sandwich itself was nicely flavored with coconut milk and some serious heat. A small side of Sriracha added an extra kick, though I had to take turns guzzling water between bites. I was also able to nab a bite of the meatball 'wich, and I definitely liked the flavors there, too. I expect more visits to the Foo Truck in my future!

What took me so long to get to Square Pie?! We arrived at 5pm for an early dinner on Saturday night. The restaurant had just opened but already a couple tables were occupied. By the time we left a little over an hour later, every table was seated and a line was forming.   Our server was awesome and kept it real with advising us on how much to order. We felt (over) confident about how much we would eat so we ordered a caesar salad, arancini, and two large pies for four people.   Square Pie is BYO and we were provided with glassware for all of our beverages. Shortly after ordering, the salad arrived. It was large enough for everyone to have a decent sized serving. The salad was delicious, exactly what I want in a caesar: well dressed but not overly so, lots of parmesan and lots of croutons. The arancini were also great.   The pies were ordered were the porchetta from the menu and a red sauce special with soppressata and pepperoncini. Both pies were absolutely delicious and we did a pretty solid job though we still walked with two leftover slices.   This was one of the best pizza experiences I've had in Philadelphia so I look forward to many more visits and takeout as well!

Damn you, Scott L. from Belmont, CA, for thinking to review Georgetti's before me!    I grew up on the pasta, sauces, soups and bread from Georgetti's.  Everything is homemade and takes very little time to prepare at home.  This is a one-stop shop for pulling together an Italian dinner for two or ten, without the hassle of actually cooking.

At the urging of my sister, I am lowering my rating for this particular PJ's location.  The two of us, along with our step-dad, decided to hit the Maple Shade PJ's for game 1 of the Flyers/Penguins playoff race.  We were seated at a prime table with no less than 6 televisions within ten feet.  The evening looked promising.  I ordered a Bass and was told that they were out, a typical response when ordering beer at this location.  I settled for Smithwick's.  We started off with chicken nachos, which arrived at our table curiously smothered in long strips of lettuce.  Was it to hide the very minimal amount of toppings underneath?  Was it to hide the strange, almost undercooked consistency of the chicken?  I didn't know but I didn't like it.  And neither did Kate, who at that point, started voicing her displeasure over the restaurant's recent descent.    My step-dad and I had "wicked chicken" sandwiches for dinner.  These sandwiches used to come with nice, big chunks of grilled chicken with buffalo sauce on a long roll.  Now, they use some type of shredded chicken that is reminiscent of a chicken steak, only not fried.  The sandwiches were okay but not "wicked" great.  Meanwhile, Kate was angsty over her Cajun chicken wrap, which was falling apart all over the place.  It was decided that dessert could save the meal so we ordered peanut butter cup pie and a hot fudge brownie a la mode to share.  The pie hit the spot but the brownie was a failure.  Normally, this dessert is our favorite on the menu, but the brownie had a light, cake-like consistency, and Kate claimed the ice cream tasted freezer burnt (I have a cold so my taste buds cannot be trusted).  For the most part, I love my PJ's, but the Maple Shade location is definitely a buzzkill.  In addition to the food quality going down, the environment is devoid of any energy or excitement.  Iron Hill Brewery is set to open shop around the corner on Kings Highway in the very near future.  Things are going to get really interesting if improvements aren't made soon.

Despite not being able to locate a single employee during my hour+ visit on Sunday, I was definitely feeling this branch of Sweat. I walked in, took one look at that giant ramp to the second floor, and kept right on walking towards the back, thinking (hoping?) that the treadmills would be on the first floor. Nice try. I found an approachable looking dude who, between gulps of air, informed me that the cardio equipment was on level two. Up the incline I went.   It turned out to be a good thing, because I got to scope out the gym in its entirety and without much distraction, as pleasant Sunday afternoons are the deadest time in the life of a gym. The huge open areas really worked for me, and everything was new-looking. The treadmills faced a large open window, providing a nice distraction during commercials of the Phillies game, which I watched on the TV that was attached to my machine. I had an excellent workout, and I'd happily visit this location again.

A little slice of peace and tranquility right in Philadelphia! I'm so glad I got to -finally- check out Shofuso Japanese House & Garden. Shofuso is located in Fairmount Park, and there is a small parking lot onsite. You must leave your shoes on a rack before entering the house (don't forget to bring socks!).   The gardens are small but lovely, and I especially enjoyed the koi fish in the pond, which were enormous! The house is very interesting; some rooms you can walk through while others you can only look into from outside, but each room has a sheet with information so you can learn more about the function of the room. The docents were all tied up with leading other people around the house but I overheard some of the information which was quite interesting. If you can snag a docent to lead you around, do it!   The wraparound porch overlooking the pond was a great place to sit and relax after the tour. I could see myself going back on a nice day simply to enjoy a refreshing mental break. Philadelphians: add this to your summer to-do list!

Love the new Whole Foods so much I've been there three times already in the ten or so days since it opened. My first visit was just a quick walk-through to get the lay of the land, while my next two trips were for grocery shopping.   Since the store is so large, everything seems really well stocked. I've only come across one item that was totally out and that was on a Sunday night trip. I suspect the store gets re-stocked early in the week which is why I missed out.   When I couldn't find a couple items on my list, I asked for some help from one of the friendly employees. He immediately led me to the first item, but I stumped him on the second. We both sort of shrugged and then went our separate ways. A few minutes later, a bag came soaring through the air and landed in my cart - this guy tracked down what I was looking for and then tracked me down to make sure I had it. Amazing!   In addition to the handful of local restaurants and plethora of grab-and-go food options, another great thing about this store is the bar and bottle shop area. Prices seemed a lot more reasonable than what I've seen in state stores. I also like the idea of grabbing a bite and sitting at one of the the long tables with a beverage. This definitely makes trips to the grocery store a hell of a lot more fun.   If there's a drawback to this store, it's the crowds, which I know isn't Whole Foods' fault. I've yet to find the sweet hour or so where crowds are at a minimum, but if and when I do I won't be sharing that information (sorry).

I found Philly Custom DJ through a Yelp search and it was a total win! Adam responded to my message within minutes and was able to work with my budget for a two-hour event. When the party was still rocking, he had no problem adding an extra half hour (paid, of course), which I greatly appreciated.   From our first communication, Adam was always available and he even created a shared playlist doc so that we could work together on the music for my event. Working with Adam was above all else easy - I can't tell you how many times I've had difficulty getting in touch with DJs in the past. That was not the case here at all. I'm looking forward to booking Philly Custom DJ for other events in the future!

I have passed by this fairly new-to-the-neighborhood coffee shop often and have wanted to check it out.  Friday morning presented the perfect opportunity to do so as I had the day off and was running errands around town.  I stopped in for a coffee and something sweet, I wasn't sure what yet.  The friendly woman behind the counter said that the pumpkin scones had been freshly baked that morning, and I was sold.    The shop was super cute; stylish and fun but relaxed.  I prayed that the coffee would be good so I could start making this place a regular stop--it was!  I got home and tore into my scone which was filled with nuts, raisins and cranberries.  Yum.    I really hope the owners do well here and I will be doing my part to make sure they do!

Burg's was a favorite of mine, so I was pumped when Community opened up in its place. The opening menu didn't thrill me but, recently, the menu has changed quite a bit and I finally got around to trying Community for takeout this week.   I had the chicken shawarma sandwich with zataar fries. My husband had the chickpea veggie burger which was basically the same thing that I ordered but with a meatless protein (love that this is an option!). I also added on a side salad.   Everything was packaged nicely and the portions were generous. I really loved my side salad and the homemade dressing that came with - delish! The sandwich was also solid, though I would have preferred it without beets but didn't see a way to modify or make a note anywhere. Also, I would have ordered the sandwich with salad instead of fries, but there wasn't an option to swap (salad instead of fries was an option for the chickpea sandwich, however, so this may have just been an oversight or glitch).    Overall, a solid first experience and I look forward to trying more from the menu!

It's been a minute since my last visit to La Calaca Feliz. My husband happened to be in the neighborhood and I was jonesing for tacos so he suggested takeout from La Calaca. Excellent choice!   We ordered the shrimp tacos, blackened mahi mahi tacos and a side of refried beans all to share. I had some leftover guac and chips at home; otherwise, we probably would have ordered another side or app.   The tacos were absolutely delicious. There were two flour tacos in the mahi order and three, smaller corn tacos in the shrimp order. Both had entirely different toppings, which I loved. I think the shrimp tacos had a slight edge for my favorite but the mahi was great as well. The beans were solid, too.   Glad we revisited La Calaca Feliz and I'll be thinking of them for takeout more often in the future!

I've loved Vault + Vine since before I ever stepped foot in the store. My sister lives nearby and she picks up a lot of her gifts there. Most recently, a pair of earrings for my birthday in August!   Last Sunday we stopped by together and I was really impressed by the array of jewelry, candles, cards and other gifts that they are able to pack in to such a petite space. The greenery is particularly impressive, and they have a really beautiful selection. I'm in the beginning stages of making some changes to my home office and would like to incorporate a large plant. We spoke with one of the employees (Kay, I think!) who was very knowledgeable. When I'm ready to make a purchase, I'll definitely consider returning to Vault + Vine since they were already so helpful.   Also, love the cafe area and they make a great, not-too-sweet chai. What a cute spot!

Update! Café Ynez is my go-to neighborhood spot for a working breakfast. There are always seats on weekday mornings and everyone is so friendly. I love the food (the vegetarian enchiladas and breakfast burrito are my faves) but I enjoy chatting with Qamara, the manager, just as much! The prices are more than fair which gives me an excuse to go pretty regularly. One of these days I'll go for dinner with a bottle of tequila in tow so I can try their margs.

We checked out Flying Fish's tasting room on a recent Friday before heading to dinner nearby. The location isn't super desirable as it's way down 295 without much else to visit nearby, but Flying Fish may soon become a destination in itself with the addition of some outdoor elements, on deck for later this summer.  State law requires tasting room visitors to receive an education about the beer before consumption, so we quickly learned a bit about each beer style Flying Fish creates. We wanted to try all the beers available during our visit so our group of four shared a tasting of all nine on tap. I'm pretty familiar with the regulars: Hopfish, Red Fish, Extra Pale Ale and the Exit series. The NJ 350 Anniversary Ale is available now and it's awesome.   There is no food served in the tasting room (again, blame the state laws) but it's still worth a trip to try the suds. I'm looking forward to going back when the outdoor area is complete.

I owe Veda an upgrade. My husband and I went recently with my in-laws and had a really fantastic meal!   We shared a bunch of starters which were all delicious and everyone was pleased with their entrees as well. Our server (I can't remember her name but she's so sweet and I remembered her from when she worked at Sidecar) was great and very knowledgeable about the menu and the wine list. I enjoyed several glasses of crisp white along with my meal.   I've always considered Veda to be a pretty close tie with my other favorite Indian restaurant in town, but Veda might have a slight edge. I'm looking forward to my next meal, either in-house or via delivery.

Dinner at La Calaca Feliz was a great way to end the holiday weekend on a high note. I was happy we made reservations; the dining room was packed the entire time we were there. We were seated in the back left corner by the fireplace. The restaurant is really pretty and has some great little touches, like the high tin ceiling with star chandeliers, the beautiful outdoor seating and the mural on the side wall.   We started with margs and guac. The reposado margarita was recommended but for a few dollars less, the house margarita was really delicious. The guacamole was awesome - plenty for two and with a little bit of heat. I enjoyed the tortilla soup but the watermelon gazpacho gave it a run for its money; perfect for summer.   We were treated to a dish from the kitchen that was a special. I can't recall the name but it consisted of noodles, fish sauce, yellowtail, peas, green peppers and mushrooms. It was very Thai-reminiscent, not what I would have expected but absolutely delicious. By the time entrees arrived we were already really full. I had a few bites of the skirt steak and beans from my arrachera dish, but had most of it boxed to go (yay leftovers!). Same with the delicious plantains. I couldn't even fathom a peek of the dessert menu, but I do know that I cannot wait to go back for another meal. It's definitely a strong birthday dinner contender.

We checked out this theatre to see Life of Pi late on Friday evening, and I was surprised to see that there were hardly any people there at all. There were maybe three groups in our theater which made for a quiet, relaxing viewing.   Everything from the hallways to the bathrooms was clean and well kept. I was a little disappointed in the film selection (Jack the Giant Slayer in both regular and 3D? Really?), but I ended up really enjoying Life of Pi so there were no regrets there. Would I go out of my way for this theatre? No. But if you live in the area, it's a solid option.

My favorite part of a cupcake, or any cake, for that matter, is the icing. Oddly enough, Pamcakes' cupcakes proved to me that there can be too much of a good thing. There was more icing than cake! However, the cake itself was one of the moistest I've encountered - the day after it was purchased!  Our two cupcakes were adorably packaged in a to-go box and tied with a white and red string. Just opening that box made me happy today. I'll definitely check out Pamcakes again, but I'll be crossing my fingers for just a bit more cake to even out all that icing.

If you're looking for high quality, delicious chocolates in Philadelphia, Lore's is your place. My mother-in-law has been giving us boxes of buttercreams for some time. Recently, she threw in a box of dark chocolate covered caramels sprinkled with sea salt. They are so fresh and so delicious!   The store itself has all the nostalgia of an old school candy shop. I stopped by during the Christmas season to pick up a box of chocolates for my grandmom. Lore's is now my go-to for nice chocolates!

One of my goals is to become more familiar with Chinatown this year, so I started with Chinatown Square this week. Basically, this is sort of a modern food court with a nice-sized handful of restaurants. The space was clean and had a nice, sleek appearance, plus good music pumping in the background! Some of the restaurants had counter tops only and you'd have to take your food to the seating area in the back, while others had bar seating in front and looked to serve alcoholic beverages.   I was happy to see one of my favorites, Halal Guys, as well as discover a new favorite in Philly Poké. I also can't wait to check out the new Korean restaurant upstairs, and the Mexican-Korean fusion spot towards the back. I'll be returning ASAP!

First of all, I LOVE the bar.  It's so swanky and there is always at least one bartender who is super attractive.  I don't know about you but that equals points in my book.  The cocktails are good, and the happy hour specials are the jam, but the drinks aren't always consistent.  Take last night.  My first blueberry gimlet had lots of blueberries and was a bit on the syrupy side.  My second was only slightly blueberry tasting but the vodka taste was way offensive.  I suspect a brand switch came into play because that concoction could have cleaned an engine from '76.  But, it was Center City Sips night, so I get that they were crazier than usual and that's why.  The food is consistent and very high-quality every single time.  Sometimes the service can be a tad slow, and that includes times when there are only four or so tables taken in the entire restaurant.  I also feel that the dinner menu could be slightly less hoity-toity, for those people who don't want to branch out to frog legs and bison.  I don't need a roast chicken, but a bigger selection of seafood or even a pasta dish would be nice.  Those things aside, dining here really does make me pretty happy because the ambiance is so nice, the service (while sometimes slow) is generally excellent and the food is very good.  Having brunch here with my mom last year is probably one of my favorite Philly memories to date, and that's pretty cool.

Giorgio's on Pine is a cute BYO with an extremely hospitable owner, friendly staff and, as Jim H. mentioned, a very easy-on-the-eyes chef.  Highlights for me were the service, hospitality, décor and desserts.  Our group had several bottles of wine on the table, and we never had to wait for our server to open another bottle--she was all over it.  We started off with baskets of delicious bread and garlicky olive oil, and a plate of bruschetta was dropped off at our table, gratis.    I had the grilled calamari appetizer and wasn't crazy about it.  I've been spoiled by the delicious calamari at Dmitri's and have not met a matching squid since.  I felt more optimistic about my entrée selection, gnocchi with a braised beef ragout.  I was hoping for a similar dish to the one served at Mercato, which is absolutely fantastic.  Unfortunately, the two were not at all comparable.  The gnocchi didn't do anything for me and the ragout was entirely too bitter.  The beef was few and far between and tasted like plain old ground meat.  I ditched my entrée and went back to my old standby, the bread basket.  Giorgio's hit a much higher note with desserts.  While I didn't agree that the tiramisu was "the best in the city," I did enjoy it.  The other desserts I tried were all appealing as well--bread pudding that had a crunchy texture to some of the outside pieces (mmm), chocolate mousse and another very rich chocolate cake type thing, which was another complimentary addition to our meal.    Despite not being crazy over my own dinner, others at my table seemed happy with their selections.  I'd be willing to give Giorgio's another shot, and plan to do so in the near future.

Lord knows we needed an alternative to McFadden's at the Ballpark down by the stadiums. Thank goodness for the multi-bar megaplex, albeit poorly-named, Xfinity Live! (Hey Comcast: we get it, this is your brainchild. No need to be a whore about it, though.)  From the outside, X-Live just looks like a big gray building with some nice patio space. But inside is a mini-mall of bar-restaurants, with an absolutely gigantic screen taking center stage in the main crossroads.   As others have said, the passageways between different areas are tight. There's a very large, unavoidable VIP area that taunts the commoners with its comfy chairs, ample space and barely-covered cocktail waitresses. What one must do to gain access to this cushy space, I'm not sure. It probably isn't cheap. There's also an upstairs area that hosts some of the sports shows, along with the upper echelon of the Philly sports world. Upon first walking into Xfinity, I immediately spotted Bernie Parent hanging out by the balcony above. Awesome.   I'm not sure if the crazy crowds are due to the dire need of a hang like this, or if it's just opening curiosity getting the best of everyone. I suspect the former, though. On my two visits, I breezed through the Victory pub and the Broad Street Bullies bar. It seemed like every individual bar had their own entertainment, and it was less crowded in the bars than in the central space (though not by much). The best part of all are the outdoor areas which lend themselves to day-drinking in the sun.   I envision hanging at this complex even when I don't have tickets to the games, because I like being surrounded by people who are into sports as much as I am. Let's go Flyers!

I'm with Angela J - Penguin Cleaners is ridiculously expensive. However, every item I've ever dropped off comes back looking like I just pulled it off the rack. The kind folks who own this place have restored dresses that I swore would never look the same again after accidental wine spillage.  Now that I live in the city, I am going to look for a place nearby for my regular dry cleaning needs. But when it comes to my favorite, most delicate pieces, I'll continue to travel across the bridge for reliable care.

Wow. Four plus years of living in Collingswood and I had yet to step foot into the Collingswood Ballroom until this past weekend when one of my besties got married. The main events coordinator seemed really organized and, more importantly, calm. The ceremony was set to take place outside and that's how we rehearsed it, but when rain threatened on the big day and everything had to be moved inside, no one panicked and everything went off beautifully and without a hitch.   The Ballroom itself is very pretty and fits a ton of people. I love that there is only one ballroom so your special event feels special and not like one of many as it does at a lot of wedding-focused venues. The balcony provides the perfect setting for pre-reception cocktails. Bathrooms were very clean throughout the night.   I'm not sure if you can hire your own catering or if the catering is contracted to a specific house caterer, so I'll reserve my comments on food and service. Speaking just from a venue standpoint, I was impressed and I'd recommend the Collingswood Ballroom for weddings or other large-scale events.

Last night we hit up Race Street for some brews after ice skating. The lighting was dim, the fireplace was kicking, and Radiohead was the soundtrack. It was a very comfy place to kick back for a couple hours with friends.   We ordered a few dishes and I remain skeptical of the offerings. Buffalo shrimp were a disappointment as they arrived completely naked - no batter or any sort of crunchy coating - and just sort of marinating in buffalo sauce. At least it was a healthy snack! Waters were requested but never brought over to the table, even after a server mentioned he would be back with waters after we asked.   Great spot for a beer with friends while in the area, maybe a bite if you know what to order, but probably not a destination.

I ordered delivery from Amalia's last week for the first time. When ordering Mediterranean, I usually keep it pretty simple and stick with the chicken kebabs. These were served over rice with a side of salad (several choices - I went with the classic Mediterranean) and some mezza which included olives and pickled veggies. The platter also comes with pita which I asked them to leave out since I try to avoid delicious gluten during the week.   I was bummed that there wasn't an option to add a side of hummus as part of the meal. Instead, I had to order a small side which cost five dollars for a teeny tiny portion. I was grateful that they were willing to sub fresh veggies for pita, however. All of the food was quite good!   My lunch total came out to over twenty bucks which was quite steep, but I was also paying for the convenience of delivery. I really liked Amalia's but will probably keep it as a once-in-a-while treat instead of a regular in my delivery lineup.

A friend and I set out to the Taproom one night last week for a couple drinks.  Despite living in the area for almost three years, I had never actually gone to this particular bar, which was formerly known as R Mac's.  The parking lot was completely packed, and the outdoor deck was crowded with a mix of people in all age groups.  There are two bars on the deck, the larger of which held flat screen TVs that were easy to see from all sides of the bar area.  I was pleasantly surprised that my martini was served in a real martini glass (the cute stemless kind!) as opposed to a plastic version since we were outside.   When it started to get cooler, we moved inside.  The restaurant and bar area was very nice, and looked like a great place to hang out, grab a bite or watch a game.  They also have live music on Thursday nights.    It's nice to have an alternative to PJ's, and the outdoor deck gives the Taproom an edge with the warmer months coming.

I'm not really a prophet of Restaurant Week or anything. I can take it or leave it. Mostly leave it, since I feel like I can have a better experience for the same price (sometimes less, sometimes more if we're all being honest here) any other night of the year. That said, I do dig RW for one thing - lunch. Because if you can score a table at one of the few gems on the list that runs like a well-oiled machine, you are all but guaranteed a fantastic meal at a price that can't be beat. Barbuzzo is one of those gems.   I entered the restaurant at 12:45, my reservation time, and my lunch date and I were taken to our table right away. No waiting! If our server was unhappy to be working this shift, he certainly didn't show it. He took care of us for the duration of the meal and offered helpful suggestions when we asked for his opinion. I started with a crisp glass of white wine which went perfectly with my meal.   To start, the vegetable board, which had a piece of buttery oven-grilled bread, roasted peppers, brussels lightly scented with truffle, glazed carrots and some broccoli rabe. It wasn't rocket science but it was a healthy and satisfying start to the meal. The sheep's milk ricotta across from me was wiped clean from the plate. Next up for me was a chicken dish, with two thin cutlets topped with parmesan and a little prosciutto. This was served over some braised greens and mashed potatoes with a little bit of gravy around the bottom. It was very nice, not too heavy and packed lots of flavor. My companion had the pizza. Folks, if you haven't had Barbuzzo's pizza, get on it, because it's some of the best in the city. Last but not least, the caramel budino. I somehow managed to restrain myself to only half, which is honestly plenty for me since the flavors are so rich and sweet.   Surprisingly, this was probably the quietest meal I've ever enjoyed at Barbuzzo. Everyone around us seemed to be seated on time and there were no waits at the door. I guess when a restaurant is used to having a full house on the regular, Restaurant Week is no different from any other day.

If Georgetti's ever closed, I'd be totally screwed, because I buy all of my meals for special occasions celebrated at home from this place! Please don't ever, ever close, Georgetti's!  My last review sums it up but to get into a bit more detail, my favorites are:   Soup - lobster bisque, escarole, chicken chili   Pasta - I'm a fan of either the plain white pasta or the wheat, cut into fettuccine thickness. In my opinion, it's better than any other fresh pasta you can buy in this area.  Sauce - marinara, meat sauce, pesto, alfredo  Salad dressing - traditional vinaigrette  Prepared foods - lasagna, any of the stuffed breads, chicken parmesan cutlets  These are my standard go-tos but you could get anything in that store and not go wrong. I've happily trekked over the bridge and back just to grab dinner. The people who work there are always the nicest, and there's always something different to sample while you're there. One of my favorite local businesses, and I'll go back again and again.

Really loved this pretty coffee shop in Old City. It's bright and spacious, with a nice seating area by the window up front, and plenty of tables throughout the space. I chose a table towards the back near the awesome desert mural. Props for having coat hooks prominently placed along the higher counters. Five stars to their music selection, also.  The baristas were all really nice. I opted for a basic cup of coffee which tasted great. My coffee companion went for a breakfast sandwich that looked really delicious.   Going to Menagerie just to enjoy a coffee while I work would mean going out of my way, but I can honestly see myself doing that because I liked the place so much. Looking forward to my next visit!

Love this pretty boutique in Old City! I dropped by with a friend to browse and ended up with a lacy tank perfect for layering. The tank itself was very affordable but I did notice some higher-priced items as well. Like many of the other boutiques in Old City, it's a mix which is good for everyone.   The ladies working were super friendly and it was an overall pleasant experience. I'll return next time I'm strolling the shops.

Maybe I went on an off day but I felt like So Crepe was so average. There were only a few occupied tables but it took forever to order drinks, order food, receive food, etc. It was just a slow operation.   As for the menu, I was surprised by some of the weird savory options (hot dogs?!) and lack of more classic offerings. I ordered the So French crêpe and found the crêpe itself to be rather dry, and I also wasn't crazy about the ham used in the dish.   Ever since L'Aube closed its doors I have been unable to find crêpes I enjoy as much in Philly. The quest continues.

It's official: I love this spot.   My very first experience with soup dumplings actually took place at Bing Bing on the tail end of a girls night out a couple months ago. I thought they were delicious, along with a few other things I was able to try (that bubble tea cocktail - love!), and I couldn't wait to go back.   Saturday, my fiancé and I decided to swing by for Bing Bing's first lunch service. Apparently the masses had not yet been informed so we were seated right away. The servers were all so friendly and knowledgeable about the menu. They recommend ordering 2-3 plates per person. We ordered: kimchi pork soup dumplings, turnip cake, rice noodle rolls, pan fried bao (mushroom and cheddar), xo chicken wings. We were also treated to the green beans, which are really delicious.   The soup dumplings were so awesome. I may need my own order next time. Though I certainly wouldn't have room for anything else - the food is very filling and we took enough home for a hefty snack. The bao are pretty large; I loved the taste of the mushroom and cheddar. The turnip cake is super unique and fun to eat. I'd probably pass on the rice noodle rolls in the future only because I enjoyed everything else so much more. Looking forward to my next visit!

Sidecar is great. The beer list is awesome, the food is always on point, if a bit heavy handed on the hot spices sometimes (Appetizer Formerly Known As, I'm looking at you). Happy hour runs from 3 - 7 pm. That's four whole hours of happy!!!   People freak over the nachos, and I say I don't really love them, but I always end up woofing half the plate when they're ordered. When I do the choosing, I like the carnitas or mahi mahi tacos (when they're offered). Mostly everything comes out with a really nice side salad.  Brunch is also very solid. I usually opt for a beermosa over a Bloody Mary with my huevos at Sidecar. For the uninitiated, a beermosa is 50% wheat beer, 50% OJ and 100% awesome.  Alas, I have one gripe, and it's kind of a big one, although it doesn't stop me from returning. When the sun goes down, it is way too dark in there. No joke, I had to download a flashlight iPhone app to read the menu on my last visit. Forget about seeing anything on the plate. Just spear blindly and eat. It drives me crazy! For the love of beer, turn up the lights before 10 so people can see their dinner!

I just came onto this page to write a review update and realized: I have never written a review at all! How could I have forgotten to write about one of the city's best places for brunch, beer and great service?   Every time I go to Hawthornes I remind myself that I need to go more often. Their brunch is seriously awesome, and offered every day. The cream chipped beef is the best I have ever had, including my dad's.   Last night, we made a last-minute decision to swing by for dinner since we were in the neighborhood. Unbeknownst to us, they were hosting a Philly Beer Week event with an Oscar Blues lineup and an awesome blues band. The large windows in front were wide open, and with all the pretty plants and flowers around, we could still enjoy the beautiful spring evening, despite being inside.   Our server was great, very attentive. I wanted something light but still flavorful and she guided me towards the tilapia soft tacos. They were awesome, especially with a few shakes of Frank's. Homemade tortilla chips with pico and sour cream were served alongside and provided just the right amount of crunch.   The best part about Hawthornes is the bottle shop, and the option to grab a beverage from the case to enjoy with your meal. The prices are still bottle shop prices, which puts most beers around the three dollar mark, which cannot be beat when dining out.   In the winter months, the fireplace and seating nearby makes for a cozy place to hang with friends. In fact, I always thought of Hawthornes as more of a winter hang, but now that I've seen how lovely it is on a breezy spring night, I'm thinking this is just a great place to go year-round. Looking forward to my next visit, hopefully soon!

We hit Knead Bagels a few weeks ago and I liked my breakfast very much. I always order the same thing at bagel shops - everything toasted, with veggie cream cheese, bacon, tomato and cucumber. This is what I ordered at Knead but was told they don't serve tomatoes off-season. Fair-enough! I opted for their roasted tomato cream cheese to give the flavor I wanted.   With coffee and a bottle of water, the price rang in less than what I'd spend at Spread but more than South Street Bagels, which is fine. Everything was very tasty and I'll definitely go back when I'm in the area at breakfast time again.

I've probably been watching too many episodes of Say Yes to the Dress. That must be the reason why walking into David's Bridal felt like walking into a time warp back to the 80s. The cheesy music, the terrible decor. Kleinfeld's twas not.   My visit was specifically for bridesmaid dress shopping for my friend's wedding. Our sales rep was somewhat helpful. I'm not sure if she had other appointments at the same time or what, but my friend's mom actually did a better job retrieving the correct dresses and the appropriate sizes for the bridal party.   The common area in the dressing room was a bit tight, with only one large mirrored area for everyone in the fitting room to share. The individual rooms were quite roomy, however.   I felt like the bridesmaid dress selection was a little weak, but they did have tons and tons of wedding gowns. Erin F's experience as a bride-to-be was quite positive, and I'm kind of a novice when it comes to these matters. I'm curious to see how this store would compare with others in the area.

My mom and sister always rave about Marshalls (attached to HomeGoods) but I can't ever figure out what gets them so excited. 95% of the time I go into this hybrid of a store, I'm going to the HomeGoods side. I've scored everything from white plates and a pretty wicker basket for Dîner en Blanc to luxurious Calvin Klein pillows at big markdowns.
