I'm always intrigued by the majorly discounted accent furniture, and I can't wait to decorate my future home with fun pieces, provided it is bigger than the tiny pad in which I currently reside. Oh yes, HomeGoods, we're going to have some fun.

Knock fills the much-needed niche of the classy gay bar in town. It seems worlds away from Woody's, Tabu and Q Lounge, which is precisely why it felt just a bit out of place as a stop along last night's Gay Bar Crawl.     No matter, the bartenders there treated us kindly with discounted drinks that were creative and enormous. In the line chart that was my drunkenness last night, I'm pretty sure this is where the line started to take a sharp descent.   It seemed like the kitchen was turning out some really awesome eats, because mostly everyone there was having dinner. Also, the Flyers game was on several TVs around the bar, which pleased me greatly.

It had been years since my last Farmicia visit, and with a friend staying at a nearby hotel I thought it would be a solid place for us to grab lunch. We started with the butternut squash soup, and it wasn't long before we both realized that there were awkward chunks of spice within the soup that were impossible to chew. I gave up on my soup about halfway through and mentioned something to our server when she stopped by to check in.   Next up for me were the steak fajitas which were fine but not very memorable. I was happy with my option to sub corn tortillas for flour, however. My friend's salad also looked fine but not very special.  For somewhere in the neighborhood of fifty bucks including tip, I expected a lot more than partly inedible soup and lackluster main courses.

Swift Half* and Whiskey Dix* had a baby, and its name is Gunners Run!   My boyfriend and I stopped by last night to check the place out and grab a beer, and that was my first impression. The music had a hard rock tilt and the art was strange and edgy. We found two available seats at the bar and surveyed the crowd. It looked like everyone there had been at the Phillies game earlier in the day. We perused the menu. Short and not interesting enough to grab a snack (although what did go past looked good). We ordered our beers and watched the end of the Flyers game, which was conveniently showing on the TV in front of us.   Then, a very drunk man tapped my boyfriend on the shoulder, which he ignored. The guy started giving me a weird look, which I also ignored. He moved past me, further down the bar, and as he started making his way back, he smacked my ass on his way by.   Internal monologue: "OH NO HE DIDN'T!!!"  Ponytail swingin' and mouth a-movin', it's safe to say my Jersey was showing. My man stood up and things could have gotten very ugly, but I came to my senses and got the attention of a bartender. Within a few seconds, a bouncer made his way over and the situation was handled swiftly and quietly. The staff was extremely apologetic, and they bought us our next round, which was very sweet.   I really don't know what the future holds for this place. I do miss my Swift Half and it felt weird being there for another business. I'd consider going back, but I wouldn't go out of my way, either.    *RIP

My first experience with Snap Kitchen yesterday was truly as good as it gets, as the five stars indicate. I was immediately welcomed by Kerry, who explained how all of the products are arranged, how they are labeled, etc. I'm currently embarking on a meatless month, and was happy to see a nice array of choices containing seafood, plus vegetarian and vegan options.  I picked out a few meals for the week, and by the time I got to the counter to pay, Kerry met me there with a couple of his favorite meals, which he kindly included in my order on the house.   I have to admit, I was dubious about the ginger glazed salmon, but heated in the oven it made for a fantastic, healthy dinner. I also really enjoyed the Greek salad with shrimp. The grilled kale hoppin' john was a solid and hearty mini-meal, and vegan too.   Overall, I'm so on board with healthy, flavorful meals that I don't even have to think about, since the ingredients and nutritional info are provided. Prices are a little spendy, but no more so than a takeout meal from anywhere else, plus you don't have to guesstimate what you're eating. If Snap were to open a location in the southwest side of the city, I'd be pretty pumped.

Mangia Macaroni had been on my radar for a while. Their IG page always features some delicious-looking pasta or Italian side. We decided to give them a try on Saturday night for delivery.   We ordered shrimp scampi, crab ravioli and garlic bread. All of the entrees come with a side salad and a hunk of bread with garlic butter.   Presentation-wise, everything was packaged well and was intact upon arrival. The food was probably about three stars for me; the fact that the prices were great and the entrees came with side salads and bread definitely elevated the experience to four star level. This is affordable takeout perfect for a night when you don't feel like cooking.

My friend and I were out on Friday night watching March Madness hoops at a Rittenhouse-area bar when we made a couple new friends.  When the games ended, the guys insisted on a late night trip to nearby Byblos.  I will be the first to admit that I never would have walked into Byblos on my own accord, but since I wasn't buying and we were having a pretty good time, I went along for the ride.    The place was packed and a table was out of the question.  As luck would have it, a group at the bar got up and left just as we made our way over.  Other yelpers have stated that the crowd is an interesting mix of attractive people and I have to agree.    Our ringleader ordered a round of beers and a hookah.  The smoke was peach flavored, and the effects were much stronger than I had anticipated.  For a place I had always turned up my nose at, I was really digging it.    While this was probably a one-time-only visit for me, I enjoyed the experience a lot and would recommend an evening at Byblos to anyone looking for something totally different from the regular scene.

Upgrading Race Street because my experience last night was solid. My friend and I had just finished dinner at Tuna Bar but we weren't ready to go home. I suggested hot toddies at Race Street and across the street we went.   With only a few more nights until Christmas, this place was bumpin'! We grabbed a table but just a few minutes later, every seat was taken. The servers seemed to be rotating and everyone who stopped by our table at one point or another was super friendly.   The hot toddies were delish (they also do a hot spiked cider) and didn't cost a fortune, which was nice. I also love the fireplace, which is always crackling away on a cold winter's night. It might even be time to try the food again. Hopefully I'll be back sooner than later for a revisit.

My girls and I got together for an afternoon flick followed by dinner at Distrito.  We had a 6:15 reservation on a Sunday night, but the first floor was practically deserted when we walked in, save for a family who was seated in the car table.  The upstairs was a bit livelier but not by much.  We were seated in a large booth and my friend immediately traded in her plate, which was dirty, and her glass of water, which contained an insect.  Things were pretty smooth after that, though.  The decorations and atmosphere are very colorful and fun, but didn't really do anything for me.  Also, it was a very cold night and the thermostat was not adjusted accordingly.  We were all a little chilly at our table by the window.  Our server looked like he was straight out of Miami in those unfortunate white pants.  They were very distracting but did make for a memorable uniform.  He was quick with taking our drink and dinner orders, but we didn't see much of him after that, until we were ready for dessert.  He might have gotten another round out of us had he stopped by mid-meal.    As for the food, favorites were the encarnacion nachos, the guisados huaraches and the quesadilla.  The guacamole was good, but not as good as the guac at El Vez and the chilango chop salad was tasty, but the pecans and green olives in the salad seemed like an odd combination to me.  We also tried the enchilada de cangrejo, which was okay but not something I would order again.    The coffee at the end of my meal was very good, but the churros with coffee ice cream and Mexican hot chocolate did not even come close to the ones served at Café Apamate on South St.    I'm hovering between three and four stars.  The location of Distrito would keep me from returning more than anything else, because I did like the food and the servers were all very nice.  Four it is!

I was back again last Friday with a "buy one dinner, get one free" birthday postcard in hand.  I brought my sister since she had never been.  We started out with the guacamole, which was good but would have been better with a little jalapeno or something to give it a kick.  The pico and black bean salsa that comes standard with dinner was tasty as usual.    By the time the entrees rolled out, we were each two deep with Corona Light and feeling a little full from all the chips, salsa and guac.  We found a way to soldier on and really enjoyed our meals.  Mine was a shrimp and scallop burrito with a side of grilled veggies, and Kate's was the chicken fajita plate, which she ate less than half of before giving up.  Everything was really, really good.  Service was consistent throughout our stay and the manager was pretty entertaining and even let us keep his bottle opener on our table.  Tortilla Press, you get another star this time!

Our search for a stylish bar cart led us to Cella Luxuria, a fairly large furniture store on Chestnut Street that houses some truly beautiful and unique pieces. If you're not in the market for furniture, there are also great prints and accessories that you won't find anywhere else. We were thrilled when we inquired about a bar cart and were given an option that would look perfect in the space we had in mind.   The piece was expensive and we had to sleep on it before making a final decision. Ultimately, we decided to make the splurge because the look and functionality of the piece were unmatched by anything else we had come across. I called and placed my order with Hayley, who was easy to work with and told me my piece would be ready for delivery in two to three weeks.   Just before we hit the third week mark, I called the store for a status check. The person who answered the phone asked for my number and said they would call me back with info. That never happened. The next day, I called again, was asked for my number, and never received a call. The next day (yes, third day in a row), I called again, and explained what had happened the previous two days and was assured by someone that I would receive a call back. NOPE. At this point, we were past the three week window and I was starting to get extremely frustrated that I had not heard from the store at all, especially since I had paid in full when placing the order. It wasn't until I emailed the store with my experience that I received a call from the store's owner, who let me know that the piece would take a little longer and that I would receive a call when it came in.   A couple weeks went by and I received a call that my piece was in and I scheduled a delivery. The delivery guys assembled the piece and I noticed that one of the doors on the cart had a scratch. They were able to take back the door and switch it out with another they had in their inventory, all within the hour. I received a call from the store a week or so later and was asked if I was happy with the piece - nice.   I am extremely happy with my bar cart, as a matter of fact. It's gorgeous! But I have to admit, my negative experience when trying to get a simple question answered has left me a little salty overall. I would recommend Cella for their products but I would also warn folks that they may have a hard time reaching anyone for questions after the purchase but prior to delivery.

I've been wanting to try Ambrosia for ages, since it's close to where I live and their outdoor seating is really nice. I made a reservation for a late Easter brunch for four people about two weeks in advance and specifically requested the covered outdoor seating in my reservation. Unfortunately, when we arrived, all of the little rooms were filled with no signs of anyone leaving, so we were seated at another outdoor four top. It was a beautiful day so it was fine, but our table was on a slant and there was less space than if we'd had one of the booths. The manager (owner?) was really nice and he did swing by several times to make sure we were happy. It was a busy holiday so I understand things don't always go according to plan.   Our server was great and efficient. We had waters as soon as we sat down and all of our bottles were opened. Our group started with some shared plates: arugula salad, frisee salad, burrata and artichokes on toast. A nice start to the meal, but the mains came out before our apps were cleared so it definitely felt like we were being rushed a little bit. I had the gnocchi for my main which was tasty and filling; I brought about half home. My husband had the squid ink pasta and it was gone before I could ask for a bite! My friends seemed happy with their orders as well, and I enjoyed a bite of my friend's pesto pasta.   Too stuffed for dessert, we all ordered cappuccinos or espressos while polishing off the rest of our wine. Our experience wasn't flawless but it was still really nice and considering the busyness of the holiday, the staff did a nice job. I'd like to go back for dinner sometime, maybe on a weeknight when the pace is more relaxed.

I see that I gave this store three stars on a previous visit, but I feel that was probably too generous. Yes, the employees are friendly. And yes, the store is close to where I live, but convenience doesn't make a solid wine store.   This particular branch of PA Wine & Spirits is small. There are maybe three aisles and wine accounts for about half of the store. Half of the wine is cheap crap. So in the end, you are left with about a half an aisle of drinkable vino.   It's super rare that anyone will offer assistance in selecting a bottle, but you're probably better off busting out an app or doing some Internet research as you walk through the aisles.

When I saw Tinto on the list of participating restaurants in the Dining Out for Life event, I was thrilled and made a reservation.  My friend and I had talked about going for months, and this seemed like the perfect opportunity.  The reservation was made two weeks in advance on Open Table, when there were still plenty of time slots available.  When we arrived at the restaurant, we were seated at the four top closest to the front door.  Looking around the small room, I figured it was better to be by the door and in a comfortable booth than seated at the banquette along the other wall, with very little space between tables.  It wasn't until I got up to use the ladies' that I saw the many tables in the next room with the bar, plus all the cozy seating downstairs.  I had table envy.  One person in our party was running a bit late, so we started with a round of drinks.  The red sangria was pretty awesome.  When our group was eventually complete, the dining room was in full swing and our server was definitely not as available.  A drink was spilled on our table and another server came to help clean up.  Eventually, our guy came back to take our order.  We had some picky eaters at our table (not recommended when dining with a group at a tapas restaurant, BTW), so between the four of us, we ordered a few lighter items to share and then each person picked one or two more substantial plates for themselves.  In the meantime, another round of drinks was ordered, and the unusually long wait had some wondering if grapes were being stomped out back.      A complimentary plate of cheese crisps started the meal.  Everyone enjoyed these with the accompanying dipping sauce.  Soon after, we received a double order of Serrano wrapped figs.  They were good, but we all agreed that the coarse sea salt sprinkled on top was unnecessary.  Several minutes later, we received a dish of olives.  They were small and very garlicky, and at this point in the meal, I was ready for something more substantial.  As plates were dropped one by one, nothing that I ordered was appearing.  Now, I've eaten in tapas restaurants many times (including Garces' own Amada and Distrito), but the timing between each dish was so long that when our server asked how we were doing, my sangria got the best of me and I could only think to reply, "Hungry."  Eek.  Not very ladylike!  Eventually, we received the rest of our plates, each one spread out over more time than was necessary.  My friend's tuna tartare sandwich looked amazing, as did a crab dish that another member of our group enjoyed.  Despite reading mixed reviews on the organic chicken, I ordered it anyway and found it to be just okay, nothing extraordinary.  The highlight for me was most definitely the mussels, which came shelled and served in a tiny pot with the most delicious tasting sauce and a side of perfectly seasoned frites with a lemon aioli at the bottom of the cup.  This dish single-handedly salvaged my opinion of Tinto, which was not a high one before this point in the meal.  Someone in our group remarked that there is always one table that gets the short end of the stick on a busy night, and it was unanimously decided that we were that table.  When our server asked about dessert and coffee, it was a no-brainer that we cut our losses and move on.  I do plan to return, maybe with just one other person next time, to give Tinto another shot.  Despite our not so great experience, it was still wonderful to see so many people out to support an important cause.

My first experience at honeygrow was okay. As a first timer, I wasn't sure if I needed to wait in line to use the order machines, if I could go right up to one, or what. It's a tight space with a lot of people during the lunch hour. When I got up to the machine, something was off and I had to touch the screen a hundred times every time I made a choice. The process was slow and frustrating. Maybe I just picked the wonky machine that day. I certainly hope so, otherwise I'd be a lot less likely to go through this process again.   My salad was good but I honestly would have customized it more if the machine had not been so slow. I wasn't super crazy about the soy ginger dressing; it was just like the ginger dressing you would get at a Japanese restaurant; thick and not really good for coating the ingredients. But I loved the list of fresh ingredients, and some of the other dressings sounded pretty tasty. I'll give them another shot sometime.

I am so thrilled to see Hawthornes back up and running after their fire last year. I've been back twice for brunch since they re-opened and, dare I say, I think it may be even better than before?!   There is now wine by the bottle plus Bloody Marys and mimosas! This girl is happy. On my first visit back I ordered the SOS - cream chipped beef on toast. Looks terrifying to the unfamiliar, tastes amazing to anyone who grew up eating it! The second time I ordered Juan's Big Burrito, minus the tortilla. So basically I chose my ingredients (cheddar, onions and bell peppers) and had some scrambled eggs with all of the extras from the burrito on the side (sour cream, avocado, salsa). This came with a heaping side of homefries. It was awesome!  I've checked out their dinner menu and I'm excited to give that a whirl. Welcome back!

I absolutely loved Wonderspaces! For those who are familiar with Artechouse in Washington, DC (or Miami or NYC), it's somewhat similar but, in my humble opinion, waaaaay cooler.   This is Wonderspaces' second permanent location, so new art installations will swap out every few months. That said, do not sleep on the first round of installations! I was truly impressed by so many of them, and they ranged from more traditional art pieces to interactive exhibits, including some virtual reality works (my favorite overall was one of the VRs, titled: Transition).    There's a bar in case you want to grab a drink, though you'll have to leave said drink at drop tables for many of the exhibits.   To be honest, I first thought Wonderspaces was a temporary exhibition and am thrilled that it's permanent! I will definitely plan more visits in the future and can't wait to see how the installations change over time!

Some reviews can't wait until the morning. Y'all, Sidecar is back!!!  I have to admit, my last few visits to Sidecar had gone from so-so to bad. After our last visit, it sort of became this unspoken rule in our house that we weren't going back. Yet, I didn't have the heart to downgrade my review. Sidecar has been a neighborhood staple - the first neighborhood staple, actually - for more than a decade. I definitely wasn't cheering for its demise.   Then, news came of how the crew behind Mike's BBQ and Stockyard Sandwich had taken over Sidecar. The photos of new menu items looked extremely promising. Finally, after late nights at work, my husband and I met up in our neighborhood and hit Sidecar for a late bite. The place was packed, like it used to be.   We sat upstairs and perused the menu. I was thrilled to see Heineken 0.0 on the beer list! This is my go-to NA beer and I am so so happy to see it in my hood!   We tried to order a pizza after seeing so many photos of it on the 'gram, but our late arrival meant they were already out. So I ordered a hot chicken sandwich with a side of fries, instead. You guyyyys. They did Nashville proud! Easily one of the best takes on Nashville hot chicken I've had outside of Nashville. And the fries were bomb, too!   We didn't have room for dessert but I've got my eye on the carrot cake. So stoked we have our neighborhood bar back and wishing the new owners all the best!

I'm a little wishy washy about my feelings towards Garces Trading Company. On my first visit, I was with my mom and our cousin and we ordered a cheese plate to enjoy with a bottle of wine we purchased there. The entire time, we felt pressured to either order more food or hurry up and get out so the table would be free for people who were planning to eat a meal. It was a Friday afternoon, hours after the lunch rush.    I've also had sandwiches and some take-home meal options and just wasn't really blown away by anything. I do love the concept and the beautiful, yet pricey, grocery area with fancy spreads, cheeses and meats. I would like to return sometime for a full meal and see how it goes. I've had their brunch prix fixe bookmarked for what feels like ages, but $12 bellinis make me hesitate.

Solid ice cream shop in the Marlton area. This place is close to my sister's house and serves a large assortment of homemade ice creams and frozen custard. I had mint chocolate chip with hot fudge and it was so big I could only eat about half. Prices were reasonable and I will definitely want to hit this place again the next time I am in the neighborhood.

Though I tend to gravitate towards local shops for bath and beauty products, I still think Lush is great. You can usually find one in any major city, which works when you need something in a pinch and prefer natural products. The packaging is fun and loud, and the names and descriptions are always creative.   I find employees to be a bit pushy sometimes, however, I had an easy in and out experience this week when I recycled some old containers for a brand new face mask - brazened honey. I can't wait to try it! Because the products are natural, they often have a shelf life (some have to be refrigerated!), which is understandable but can be preventative when it comes to committing to a full-sized purchase.   Finally, some of their bath bombs have left color behind on my tub. It's always removable, but that doesn't happen with the bombs from my local spot. Nonetheless, I'm still a fan and enjoy a lot of their products!

Square Pie is still bomb as ever. We arrived at 4pm on the dot to place a takeout order to bring to my brother's house for his birthday. We started a tradition of birthday pizza parties and, let me just tell you, it's proven to be a great decision.   We ordered a pepperoni pizza and spinach pizza, and a Caesar salad. But after chatting it over with the chef and hostess, I added a second salad which was smart. One would not have been enough for four people but two was just right. Their caesar is great!   The pizzas were perfection. I don't know how they make those giant, thick slices somehow feel light but the crust is flaky, flavorful and just amazing. The toppings are just right without going overboard. I had a slice of each pie which was the perfect amount. Can't wait for the next visit or takeout order!

Edit: After receiving a response from the GM, I found out the caesar salad has Asian pears, not apples. Whoops! Original review still posted below.   I really liked my first experience at Rooster Soup last week! I arrived a little after 1pm on Friday to a long line snaking down the block. Fortunately, that line was for Goldie, the falafel shop above Rooster Soup. I went downstairs to find my husband already seated at a table by the counter - score!   Never in my life had I tried matzo ball soup (I know, right?), so I knew I had to upgrade my lunch to include a cup. The broth itself was perfect and I loved the taste of the fresh dill. The matzo ball? Eh. I don't feel that I've missed out on anything by not trying this soup until now.  My chicken caesar salad was unique. I loved the dressing, the croutons and the parmesan cheese, but was very surprised by the bits of apple throughout. Not in a bad way, not in a good way - I honestly couldn't tell you if I loved it or could leave it. I do think they should list apple as an ingredient to the salad on the menu, though. In any case, I would order this salad again - to be determined if I'll ask for it without apple.   There are so many other menu items I'm interested in trying (milkshakes! brunch!), and I'm looking forward to a return visit soon.

This place is the jam. I've never been but my boyfriend has brought home the goods on several occasions. The chips are great and stay fresh for a long time. The salsas are awesome but the red one is hotter than the blazes of hell. So get the green which brings just a hint of heat if you're sensitive to that sort of thing.

I blame my self-loathing this morning on last night's adventure to Adsum, where, despite having just housed a burrito, I was still tempted enough to try the poutine. I ordered it without the foie gras, and still found it to be delicious. The fries were perfectly crispy and salty, the gravy was spot on, and the cheese curds were just starting to melt. Delish.  I washed it down with a Dogfish Head 60 Minute IPA, followed by an old fashioned, which was made to perfection.   The tunes that played in the background could have been from my own Pandora station, so I was definitely happy there. Beakers and test tubes behind the bar made my inner science geek absolutely giddy. I'd like to venture back sometime soon, when I have a legitimate hunger going. Then I'll really do some damage.

I had a great experience with this Canal's on Saturday. I was craving 21st Amendment's Hell or High Watermelon and wasn't sure where to find it by the case. Since I was in NJ, I gave Canal's a call and they not only had it in stock, but were willing to put a case aside for me as long as I planned to stop by that day. Since there were only two cases left, this was a great favor and made my life pretty easy. Not to mention, the case was around $32 before tax, which seemed really reasonable.  I walked up and down their beer aisles while there and was surprised at the great selection. Since this place is just a few miles from my parents' house, it's safe to say there will be plenty more visits in my future.

The Capogiro on Passyunk has a distinct vibe that differs from the other locations. The front is reminiscent of an old-fashioned ice cream shop, while the back seating area feels like a fancy living room in South Philly.   There didn't seem to be as many flavors to choose from at this location, and the gelato isn't displayed in the same tantalizing way as it is elsewhere.   Regardless, I'm always happy to have a Capogiro option around for when the mood strikes.

One thing I definitely didn't have while living in the burbs? Delivery sushi. And not just sushi that defaults to acceptable because it saves me a trip off the couch. Vic Sushi is pretty decent stuff.   I did think the fancy rolls were overpriced. Paying well over ten bucks because a roll involves two types of fish and some eel sauce does not justify that cost (although the rolls with mango intrigue). Next time, I'll go for one of the three roll dealies, which comes to a much more wallet-friendly $10.95.

The first time I sat down in Sassafras a few months ago, I thought I had stumbled upon Old City's answer to Chick's Café & Wine Bar.  I had been vaguely aware of the café's existence for years yet never thought to stop in.  I was instantly charmed by the tin ceilings, tiled floors and old-timey surroundings, including the bartenders, who were dressed in starchy whites with black ties.    The cocktail menu looked promising.  Absinthe, ROOT, and other interesting spirits were listed as ingredients.  After two or three visits, however, I've found the consistency of the drinks to be staggeringly different depending on the 'tender.  I've had great drinks at Sassafras but I've also had several disappointing ones.  I once ordered a bloody Mary, a featured drink on the menu, and the result was something akin to what I can mix myself on an airplane using only two ingredients.    All things considered, I still think this bar is one of the gems of Old City, and rumor has it that the food is pretty good, too.  I'll definitely return but I'll be choosy with my beverage selection.

My second visit to Distrito was a solid 4 star experience.  My friend and I had early dinner reservations and I had requested a table upstairs.  When the hostess tried to seat us next to one of the only occupied tables, I asked that we instead be seated in one of the many open booths for two.  Instead of simply walking us over, she asked us to wait at the table while she called down to the front desk.  We stood there awkwardly in the middle of the dining area while she did this.  Having been a hostess, I realize there is a server rotation and the tables are numbered and in sections.  However, there is no reason for people to be seated on top of each other in an otherwise empty dining room.  We were granted access to the booth and all went smoothly after that.   Our server was great with answering questions and making recommendations.  We started with margaritas but they didn't really do anything for me so I switched to beer after one, although my friend stayed on with them.  We ordered guacamole and salsa, which were both very good, if overpriced (a pretty common theme in the restaurant, actually).  For dinner, I absolutely had to order the guisados that I had tried a couple weeks prior, as well as the carnitas tacos, with pulled pork, black beans and pineapple salsa.  The tacos were presented really nicely and were absolutely fantastic.  My friend had the hamachi tacos, which were so pretty that I wanted to take a picture.  Jose Garces really hits the nail on the head with creating dishes that are as visually pleasing as they are delicious.   Throughout the meal, our water glasses were never empty, because there was always someone swinging by to fill them up and clear plates.  We were visited several times by our server as well as other waitstaff to see how things were going and if we needed anything.  Despite really enjoying the food, service and overall experience, something is still keeping me from bumping to five stars.  Still, I look forward to my next visit!

You guys know what to expect at Panera. This one is clean, has all the things I need and in the right places and provides an acceptable quick meal when necessary.   When I ordered my bagel the other day, I asked for it to be toasted. The girl at the counter even said, "you wanted it toasted, right?" So that was two confirmations that I wanted that bagel toasted. Guess what wasn't toasted?   The moral of this story is, don't go asking for anything above and beyond the status quo at this Panera, and you should be satisfied.

My very first experience at La Locanda del Ghiottone was on a first date, almost a year ago.  The guy I went out with had dined there several times and the owner and staff welcomed him with open arms.  In fact, they showed us to the "engagement table," where they claimed many first dates occurred in which the couple later got engaged.  Mmm-hmm.  Probably one of the more awkward moments of the date...  Luckily, the food (and wine that I was now guzzling at warp-speed) made up for any weirdness.  My date asked if I liked mushrooms, and when I said no, he insisted on ordering the mushroom appetizer anyway and promised I would like it.  Ooohkay.    I had to hand it to the guy, the "crepe con funghi" was good.  Points.  He also recommended the homemade gnocchi, which I believe is a special and made from cheese instead of potatoes.  Of course, being the stubborn girl that I am, I went for the ravioli instead.  Which were good, but not as good as the gnocchi, which I stole from my dining companion's plate at every opportunity.      The tiramisu that was given to us "on the house" was to-die.    There was a love connection made that night, only it wasn't with my date.  But I will be forever grateful to him for introducing me to this charming little Italian BYO.  Swoon.

I like Panera.  It's quick, convenient and tasty.    Unfortunately, many of the items are a caloric death trap, so I tend to stay away from the following 90% of the time: sandwiches, paninis, frozen/blended drinks, breakfast selections and bakery items.  If I'm hungover, it's a different story and I'll eat anything that isn't nailed down.  For the other days of the week, there are still some viable options that won't send you straight to diet hell.  Today, the chicken and rice soup with a hunk of multi-grain baguette made me a pretty happy girl.  It remains to be seen if this will actually get me through to dinner, or if I'll be gnawing my own arm off for survival at some point later in the day.  I'm going to go with 4 p.m. on the over/under.

I am giving three stars but I feel I am being pretty generous here, because I most likely would not seek out a meal from this place again. On a total whim, we decided to grab pizza and a salad to go on our way back to Philly today. The employees were friendly but it seemed like everyone was in training or something - there were more than enough people but no one really seemed to know what they were supposed to do or where things were located. For what was billed as a quick serve pizza place, I feel we waited nearly as long as any other pizza place from the time of placing our order to receiving it.   At home, we dug in. The pizza was still hot and looked nice, but it was extremely doughy and not the brick oven pie I was expecting. I did really enjoy the sauce on the Trenton tomato. The ingredients were flavorful, but the pie itself wasn't my fave.  As for the salad, don't even bother. The chicken had those fake grill marks on it and the salad was akin to something you'd get from a drive through - complete with a packet of Ken's dressing and baggies of croutons. We tossed half of it which is saying something because I always finish the salad!   Apparently 1000 Degrees is the next big fast casual concept, but I'm not really buying.

I got my birthday brunch on at Green Eggs last week and I was a pretty happy camper. There were so many amazing-sounding things on the menu that I had a difficult time choosing just one. Since it was a special day, we went a little crazy and started the meal with a muffin topped with walnuts and crème anglaise that was featured that morning. It was delicious, and a perfectly sweet way to start our brunch.   When I saw two gigantic griddles of the "kitchen sink" delivered to a neighboring table, I almost changed my order. But I ultimately went with the breakfast burrito, with egg whites instead of whole eggs. Because you know, it's so much healthier that way.   Stuffed with eggs, potatoes, peppers and cheese and topped with black beans, pico, avocado and sour cream, it was one hefty burrito. I was so engrossed in my own meal that I barely glanced at my boyfriend's smoked salmon benedict.   Servers were all friendly and chatty, and the café had a really pleasant, comfortable feel. I have no idea why it has taken me so long to try this place, but it's sure to become a staple.

I'm way overdue on this review, but I was scrolling through businesses and was reminded of a really great day last summer that included Dahlak. My husband and I spent a beautiful summer day bouncing around the city with family, then we all went our separate ways and he and I ended up at Dahlak to smoke some shisha. We'd never been to the restaurant before, so it took some directions from the friendly staff for us to find our way past the dining room to the back bar area.   We posted up at the bar and I had a fresh juice while my husband had a beer. And some shisha, of course. There was an electronic jukebox and we quickly bonded with another couple over our music selections. It was just one of those perfect summer Sundays.   Dahlak is closed for renovations at the moment and I'm looking forward to checking those out once we can all get out to enjoy restaurants again.

I hate, hate, HATE to do this to one of my favorite local businesses, but I have not been happy with my recent experiences at Penguin Cleaners. This was my go-to dry cleaning place for 6+ years. Even after my move to the city, I continued to take my clothes to Penguin because I always felt that they were returned to me looking brand spanking new. And for that reason, I didn't mind that the prices are on the high side.   A month or so ago, I brought in a nice dress that I had worn once before getting a grease spot on the front (no more sherry bone marrow shots when I'm dressed all classy-like). I specifically pointed it out to the gentleman who works there and picked up the dress a week or so later without taking a look. Once home, I got the dress out of the bag and the spot was still there. So I brought the dress back during the day, along with two others, and I asked if there was anything that could be done. The lovely woman (whose name is escaping me!) who often helps me out said that she thought they could probably get the stain out and it was possibly just overlooked the first time. She marked the spot with a sticker.   Today I returned to pick up my dresses. Miracle of miracles, the dress is spotless. I'm so relieved. But I also paid to have that dress dry cleaned twice. Once home, I looked at my other dresses. One still has a couple marks on it towards the bottom. I knew they were there when I dropped off my dresses but I didn't think I needed to point out every mark. Now, I have another dress that needs to be dry cleaned yet again.  Like I said, I have always had great service from Penguin and I really like the people who work there, but I'm super frustrated with the quality of services lately. I think it's finally time for me to look for a new dry cleaner closer to where I live.

To say I am a fan of anything Four Seasons would be a total understatement. I'm not shy about my love of the finer things in life and the Four Seasons brand certainly caters to that sentiment.   My beau and I enjoyed a day at The Spa right before Christmas and it was pretty fantastic. The services are very costly. I do have a go-to spa already that is just as nice (though doesn't include the perks of an indoor pool/whirlpool and gym) and far easier on the wallet. However, there is currently a Weekday Reset package (offered Mon-Thurs from 9-5) that makes a trip to The Spa at Four Seasons Philly within reason. At $100 for two twenty-five minute sessions, it's still spendy but doable.   First, you pick from a selection of massages and facials. I went with the deep tissue massage. Then, you choose from another list of services. I chose the scalp treatment. I expected my treatments to be separate, but my massage therapist worked them both into one fifty minute session, which was absolutely incredible. I really felt like I was getting away with something, since a fifty minute massage service normally costs around $150. It was wonderful!   After the treatment, I was given a light snack which I enjoyed while relaxing by the pool for the rest of the afternoon. Weekday Reset, we shall rendezvous again.

A box of six of the most delicious sticky buns you ever did taste (with nuts or raisins - your choice!) will set you back only $5.50. That's less than a dollar per sweet, sticky, gooey bun!   The donuts and cakes also looked incredible but we were on a mission for buns only. I'd definitely make the trip to deep South Philly again for more sweet treats!

On a recent cold and rainy night, I decided to go the delivery route for dinner. Yellowtail was new to me, so I checked out the reviews which were fairly positive. The delivery fee is $1 but the minimum order is just $10 so this worked out well. I ordered the three roll combo for $10.95 and my delivery arrived well within the promised time of 30-45 minutes. Probably less than that, actually.   I ordered a tuna avocado roll, tuna cucumber roll and a California roll. I loved that the rolls weren't too weighed down with rice. Each bite was the perfect size and everything tasted great. I asked for extra wasabi and received enough for a family of four. I will definitely order from Yellowtail again.

Super cute dog and cat -stuffs. My sister and I swung by one afternoon and she was very impressed with the array of merchandise. Particularly the doggie outfits, which she is always buying for her own pup. She says he likes it.   They always have a cute pooch or two up for adoption, and seeing their little faces through the window on the street melts my heart every time (and I'm not even a "dog person").   Doggie Style also offers grooming services, but I've heard mixed reviews from friends who have taken their dogs there. But for pet necessities or even items for pet-lovers, this is a great spot.

When I went to this FedEx location to pick up a shipment my colleague re-routed for me, I happened to mention to the employee looking for my box that the shipment had just been re-routed the previous night. She immediately went into auto FedEx employee mode, reciting something about how re-routed packages never arrive the next day, blah blah blah, call 1-800 blah blah blah. My colleague had guaranteed that I would be able to pick up that shipment, but I knew I wasn't going to get anywhere trying to argue my case so I left and contacted my colleague for the scoop.   A few hours later, low and behold, my packages arrived! I was helped by another employee who was really friendly and who even offered to help me out with my packages. I declined because how else am I going to get the arms of a WWE Total Diva?   So all in all, not a total fail but certainly not my favorite customer service experience.

I enjoyed my meal at Luna, but I'm going with three stars which feels accurate of my experience overall. Our server was friendly and poured us waters as soon as we sat. I ordered the buffalo chicken salad with dressing on the side.   My salad arrived and was super tasty, but I did need some more buffalo sauce because I like things saucy. There was no avocado on the salad, which had been listed on the menu. So that was a bummer. My dining partner ordered a sandwich, which she later told me was really kind of boring. Mental note for next time.   No one really checked in with us after we got our food and I had to flag a server down for more water. Our check was dropped without an ask if we needed anything else. And, as others have mentioned, it's cash only.   Again, I liked my salad a lot so would get that again if I were to return. I wouldn't go out of my way, though.

Bella Bridesmaids to the rescue! My beautiful friend Aimee K is getting married this fall, and she graciously allowed her bridal party to select their own dresses with a few parameters. I first went to the go-to bridal chain, where I was met with the same dresses from nearly every wedding I've been in over the past decade. I left without a dress and did a bit of research, which is how I found out about Bella Bridesmaids.   Because the bridal party members were able to select their own dresses, I was a little worried that I wouldn't be able to get an appointment with Bella as a solo bridesmaid. Happily, they were more than accommodating and I set up an appointment within a week or two of reaching out.   At my appointment, I had a dedicated rep who listened to my style preferences and made recommendations. There were so many dresses that I mostly just had the rep (I wish I remembered her name - she was so sweet!) bring me whatever she thought would work. I had a dressing room filled with beautiful options in a matter of minutes, and it didn't take long before I selected the dress. I'll admit, my selection was a bit pricier than the dresses at that other bridal shop, but it was worth every penny. It's worth noting that there were still options that were a good amount less than the dress I selected.     I picked up my dress this week (just about 2.5 months after placing the order) and tried it on at home right away. The fit is perfect. The dress is beautiful. And, best of all, I am confident that I will wear it again. No, really, I mean that. The dress is chic enough for a black tie event. If I am ever fortunate enough to have the option to pick out my own bridesmaid dress again in the future, I will immediately reach out to Bella Bridesmaids.

I was invited to an event at the Delaware Art Museum tonight and I really enjoyed myself. The main foyer served as our gathering area, and I found the space to be clean and modern. The adjoining galleries that we had access to had some nice pieces of art, although nothing really stood out in a major way to me.   As a former event planner, I have a critical eye when it comes to details for large parties. The bartender was wonderful, and did well under pressure, but the set-up was in a corner of the room that was prone to overcrowding.   The food was excellent and passed hors d 'oeuvres were abundant. The stations were spread out, but nothing was labeled, which left everyone guessing about each dish. I personally was able to sample the wares with gusto, although I imagine it may have been difficult for anyone with food limitations. The Caribbean station was my favorite, with spicy jerk chicken, plantains and collard greens that were full of flavor and not at all bitter.  All in all, it was a nice event and the service seemed to move along without any noticeable snafus. I would recommend the venue for any special occasion.

I don't know, y'all. I know the 'Vous is a staple but I'm just not that into it. I swung by for a quick beverage on a recent Saturday because my guy was there with his friends. There are specials even on Saturday, which is cool, but High Life and the other beer they were featuring on tap just did not appeal. When my girl Aaliyah P arrived, we hung around for one very quick drink and were on our way.   On a positive note, I do remember good bar food from a previous visit. I wouldn't be opposed to swinging by sometime to check that out again, but it probably wouldn't be my own suggestion.

I've found my new Chinese takeout/delivery spot! We decided to try Dim Sum House the night before Christmas Eve, when we were in the thick of gift wrapping and recipe making. I was looking for comfort food and received it in abundance.   We started with scallion pancakes (always a must) and pork soup dumplings. The scallion pancakes were perfect. Sadly, the soup dumplings were oddly placed at the bottom of the bag in a styrofoam container, which resulted in most of the dumplings arriving crushed, as pictured. However, each dumpling was in its own tiny container, so the dumplings were still somewhat intact, if less soupy than desired.   Our entrees were general tso's and dry pepper chicken. Both were generous portions and each dish was great. My only complaint with the entrees is that we received only one side of white rice, when we definitely could have used two.   Overall, the food was delicious and we were happy despite the small flaws. Definitely ordering from Dim Sum House again next time I have a Chinese food craving!

Our crew of friends had a really good time pre-gaming for a wedding at Cooperage. (Wow, reading that last sentence back makes me feel like this might be a problem. But we had time to kill between the ceremony and the reception! Insert other excuses here.)  I haaaaate the smell of bleach and it was the first thing I noticed when we sat at some high top tables near the bar. I think they were using it in a solution to clean the chalkboards. Maybe if they could do this before opening the smell would dissipate before patrons arrive.   The guys ordered up brews but I wanted to stick with something lighter. Lighter in consistency but certainly not alcohol was the pineapple jalapeño margarita. It had just a touch of sweetness and a kick of heat. My kind of margarita. However, when the bartenders changed, so did my drink. The same beverage was served to me in a different style glass and, also, the balance wasn't quite right.   We ordered some snacks to tide us over and the chicken quesadilla was huge and delicious. The spinach artichoke dip was okay, but lacking some flavor. A little salt or hot sauce might help here. Overall, we were all happy with our pre-gaming choice and I'd like to get back to check out more of the menu sometime.

Louie is the spot in St. Louis! I've been twice - once with a group for my best girl's bachelorette dinner and again last weekend with the same friend. We loved having Jordy as our server for the group dinner but our server on Saturday, Chloe, was also awesome!   Do not sleep on the small plates as they are all delicious! I can't remember all the details from our group dinner but I do know we basically ordered the entire small plates section. On Saturday, my friend and I narrowed down to the olives, hummus, and cauliflower. Still thinking about that cauliflower two days later. It's battered (and possibly lightly pickled prior to battering?) and served with an aioli. Increds.   Because we're carb monsters, we ordered two pizzas to share: the pomodoro fresco and broccolini, ricotta and lemon. Both were delicious! My only regret was eating all of the amazing fresh bread when we first sat down because we had no room for dessert.   Love this spot and can't wait to return on my next visit to St. Louis!

This restaurant is close to where I work and the only Thai place in town so I decided to give it a shot.  Last week, I ordered the chicken pad Thai to-go at lunch time.  The dish was all right but nothing to write home about.    Why I returned for seconds after not being impressed the first time, I'm not sure.  It was kind of like one of those first dates that go okay, but the cocktails make you think you enjoyed the evening more than you really did and you agree to go out again.  You then spend the whole second date wondering why you didn't trust your instincts while simultaneously planning your exit strategy.    Such was the same with my vegetable pad Thai at lunch today.  As soon as I took my first bite I knew I just wasn't that into it.  To its credit, the veggie pad Thai spared me from corny jokes and emergency phone calls to friends from the bathroom.  I suffered through the meal in silence and when it was over, I tossed the Thai Basil phone number into the nearest trash can.

Despite a frustrating experience at Tinto back in May, I knew I wanted to return for another round to see if I had judged too harshly.  Turns out, the dining experience is a lot better when the service is exceptional and you are in the company of someone who understands the tapas concept.    We were seated at one of the two tops against the left wall.  The tables are positioned so close together that it was difficult getting into the banquette side without giving a partial lap dance to my neighbor while trying to swing my booty behind the table and onto the bench.  I've got a little cushion for the pushin' but it's not like I'm packing.  I can't imagine the awkward moments that must take place when more full figured people are seated there.  Would it kill them to take out one two top and create a few more inches of space to make the guests more comfortable?  (The answer is no.)  Besides that one issue, I enjoyed everything else about our dining adventure.  We started with the Serrano wrapped figs, which were great, and the sopa de castano.  The soup was presented beautifully.  A duck and mushroom stack topped with a fried quail egg sat in a bowl, while the thick and velvety broth was poured around the stack, leaving only the egg visible.  I had reservations about the soup because I'm not much of a truffle fan, but gave it a try and was immediately won over.    Next up was the revuelto de cangrejo, which was like a fancy breakfast dish containing scrambled eggs, peas, lump crab, bacon and herbed toast points.  This offering might be better suited for a brunch menu, but I was digging it nonetheless.    After reading Monica's review, I wanted to try the shortrib sandwich.  This would have been difficult to cut in half, so we decided to go with an open-face method.  My guy graciously took the top half of the bread, which contained a dollop of mayo-heavy sauce, while I took the bottom, which was soaked through with juices.  The beef was tender and went perfectly with the slivers of asparagus and other accompaniments.  My love for the shortribs was matched only by the moules basquaise, which were every bit as wonderful as I remembered.  The duck canapés were another very good dish.  Duck confit wrapped in Serrano ham may sound a bit overboard, but the flavors melded together and really worked.    My least favorite dish of the night was the pulpo, which I wanted to try after reading rave reviews.  I just wasn't into it.  The presentation was a little dramatic for my liking, with a long smear of... something, and a pile of pulpo at the end of the plate.  The textures of the potato and octopus together didn't really work for me.  I'm bumping to four stars because the meal was very good overall and the service was great.  I don't think Tinto will ever become a five star spot for me, but it was a nice step up from my last experience and I would definitely be willing to return again.

As far as state stores go, this one's not too bad. It's super close to where I live and convenience is always a factor. Also, the employees at this particular store go out of their way to be friendly, which you know is not the case for all state stores if you've been to the one around 12th and Chestnut.   I do wish the refrigerated section extended beyond a few bottles of chardonnay, pinot grigio and cheap white zinfandel. If you want anything decent and you want it cold, make sure to purchase early and refrigerate yourself.

700.   The number of course makes me think of Veteran's Stadium, which makes me think of football, which makes me think of Philadelphia sports, which makes me think of hockey, which makes me think of hockey players, which makes me think of Race Street Cafe (Flyers players are rumored to hang there), which will now make me think of my 700th review! Full circle. Don't you love it?   Think that over for a second while I tell you what I most definitely love: Race Street Cafe's garden salad with buffalo chicken. Fresh mixed greens, shredded carrots, cherry tomatoes, blue cheese and two perfectly-crunchy strips of chicken in delectable wing sauce. Skip the standard balsamic dressing that comes with in exchange for homemade ranch, which had delightful flavors of fresh herbs.   Yelp-tern Allison's special salad of the day had beets, halved hard-boiled eggs, red onion and fried goat cheese. I'm not a beet lover, but if that salad didn't look good...    There were plenty of other things on the menu that I had ruled out in favor of the salad. I can't wait to go back again and again to tick them all off my list!

It's a good thing I don't work in the Comcast Center. I'd probably spend all my money at DiBruno and eat cheese and bread for lunch every day, rendering me into one of those people who wears the matching separates that barely pass as acceptable out-of-the-house clothes. You know the ones.  While I didn't peruse the cheese and charcuterie section on my short visit yesterday, I did have a bangin' iced coffee with a shot of chocolate syrup. Delish!

Hot dayamn I'm getting my culture on lately!   Last night, I hit the Academy of Music for some more Tchaikovsky action. This time, for The Pennsylvania Ballet's performance of Swan Lake. The performance itself was beautiful, and the orchestra was fantastic, melding seamlessly into the show.   The theater was pretty in a way I would imagine old-school theaters to be, although the areas outside reminded me of a grade school building. The hallways and bathrooms were just too sterile for a structure that holds such grand events.    Seats were tiny, and there were some sections with obstructed views because of columns. I was dangerously close to one of those seats, and I would not have been happy had I been seated there. Nonetheless, we still had a pretty good view even from our location up high.   I would definitely return for another ballet or musical, but I'd probably try to get seats on a lower level.

I returned to Race Street Cafe for brunch recently and was not disappointed. Service was friendly and there were quite a few brunch selections that sounded great. In the end, I went with the feta and spinach omelet, which came with tater tots, choice of breakfast meat and toast, and a side of fruit. Everything was delicious!   Tables are packed together pretty tightly and my chair was constantly bumping against the person seated behind me. It's a tight squeeze when all the tables are seated.  I was glad we decided to check out Race Street for brunch. I don't get there too often but am always happy with my experience.

I had the unfortunate need to visit this Urgent Care location after injuring my ankle while traveling over the weekend. I arrived around 9:30am on Monday morning and was super pleased to find an empty, clean waiting room. I was told this location is newer so they are still in the growth stage which means I lucked out.   Everyone I encountered was pleasant. I received x-rays and a diagnosis, plus an air cast and crutches. However, it was recommended that I see a specialist as well, just to be sure. It's a good thing I took this advice because it turned out that my injury was worse than what the doctor at Urgent Care could see. I don't hold this against the doctor - he told me it was a possibility since the technology at the center wasn't as strong as what would be in a specialist's office. That said, the specialist at the follow up needed new x-rays because the ones from Urgent Care didn't have me positioned properly for the type of injury I had.   Hopefully there won't be a next time, but if I do injure myself again, I would likely try to get in with a specialist from the start, if possible. However, for basic colds and flu-like stuff, I'd definitely hit this place again if I couldn't get in with my regular docs.

I've been to High Street on Market on several occasions for lunch. It's generally pretty crowded on weekends but I have lucked out and scored seating every time. My go-to is the turkey sandwich, no mayo. It is absolutely delicious and so flavorful! I like that they have potatoes as a side but would love if they added chips to their menu as well!   The real reason I'm busting out this review today is because I finally made it to HSOM for dinner last night! I normally avoid Restaurant Week but my friend/colleague is in town and she has celiac so I needed to find a restaurant that would have some options for her. I was thrilled that High Street not only had options but they also make their own gluten-free pasta!   We were seated promptly when we arrived for our 7pm reservation and our server, Maggie, was incredible. We lobbed tons of questions at her and she was really great about providing info or getting answers from the kitchen if she wasn't sure. Excellent service all around!   My friend opted for wine while I inquired about alcohol-free options. My server and I discussed flavors and some magician managed to whip up an AF moscow mule that rivaled the best ones out there. Seriously, it was delicious.   The RW menu offers a lot of really great choices and I could happily go back and order totally differently on another visit. Although, my choices last night would be hard to stray from, they were so on point. I had the crab rangoon, steak, and chocolate hazelnut cake. My friend had the crispy vegetables, gluten free pasta with lamb ragu, and buckwheat-honey ice cream. We finished with a pot of fragrant peppermint tea from Rival Brothers.   We both loved our meals from start to finish and I couldn't even wait to get home to tell my husband how amazing our experience had been. High Street is definitely a top contender for my next night out.

I went to Severino in hopes of finding homemade soup.  Unfortunately, there was no soup to be found but that was only a minor setback once I saw the many different pastas and homemade sauces displayed.  The pastas come frozen or dried, depending on the type, and I believe everything is made on the premises.  Pasta in every shape and variety is available.  I settled on whole wheat fettuccine, which came in a nice sized bundle.    Picking a sauce was a bit trickier.  They had every flavor imaginable, either homemade in the freezers or in gourmet bottled varieties.  The homemade red clam sauce jumped out at me so I went with it.  Meanwhile, I practically needed a straitjacket to avoid throwing any of the cheeses, breads (focaccia!!!), crackers, dips (dirty martini dip?!?!?), olives or veggies on the counter along my otherwise healthy meal.    For $11, I had at least two nights worth of said pasta and sauce (which was DELISH, by the way), plus tons of leftover dry pasta for the next time I want to get all Italian with myself.  And speaking of the next time, I'm totally planning to break down and try that dirty martini dip!

Solid experience at this FedEx location today. I walked in and was instantly welcomed by at least one employee, and a manager came over to ask what I needed help with and directed me to the right place.   I had to overnight a document and the woman who helped me was friendly and thorough - she had me double check all of the info she entered for accuracy. I was in and out in a matter of minutes and that's worthy of five stars in my book!

Yelpers of the greater Philadelphia area, I challenge you to find a better soft pretzel than the ones that are served at this fine establishment.    If any of you are familiar with the late, (not-so) great Pennsauken Mart, then you will surely remember the delicious, piping-hot and perfectly salted pretzels that were served to lines of people on the days the Mart was open.  Many people thought the demise of the Mart meant the death of our beloved pretzels.  Well friends, that was not the case.  The magical twists of dough you fondly remember still exist to this day, and they are right down the street in Cinnaminson.    Just like finding the perfect cheesesteak, sometimes you have to travel a little to reach the pinnacles of pretzel satisfaction.  If you are the type of person who is down with Pat's or Geno's when getting your cheesesteak fix, by all means, hit up the nearest shopping cart for your soft pretzel.  But, if you are looking for the creme de la creme of soft pretzels, the pretzel-equivalent to Tony Luke's or Jim's or Chink's (or whichever spot you prefer), then you will get into your car and travel a little outside of your comfort zone... to the Jerz.  Don't be afraid, city dwellers.  The pretzels are THAT good.

Admittedly, South Square has not always been my favorite grocery store, however, I am definitely a fan of how they are handling safety and sanitation during the COVID-19 pandemic. From the very beginning, this store had a sanitation station set up outside for their shopping carts. Inside, there are wipes and also barriers between customers and employees at the check-out lines. These steps are greatly appreciated!   In addition, South Square was stocked on several household items that we haven't been able to find elsewhere for weeks. We were able to secure our preferred laundry detergent, along with a large container of Lysol wipes, among a handful of other items.   I also have to admit, when I can't find a basic household item at the newer nearby grocery store, I have almost always been able to track it down at South Square. They can be pricey, and I don't love all of the departments, but this neighborhood staple definitely serves a purpose.

Loved my dinner at Doma last night. We made last-minute reservations on a whim and the minute I walked into the restaurant I knew it was the right decision. There was a really calm and peaceful vibe. The soft tunes on the speakers overhead were just right; well-known but chill songs. Everyone on the staff was pleasant.   The menu is pretty extensive and there's definitely plenty to choose from even for non-sushi lovers. We stuck with the raw side for our meal. I started with the hamachi crudo - thinly sliced yellowtail with jalapeño and cilantro in a yuzu sauce. The taste was clean, with a hint of heat and totally delicious. Art was happy with his choice, an assortment of sashimi in citrus vinaigrette.   I went basic for my main and ordered a snow crab california roll and a spicy crunchy tuna roll. I could have used a little more spice in the tuna roll and I thought the rice was a bit thick on both, but that may also be due to the fact that I had forsaken carbs all week until this meal. The specialty roll across from me and on the tables around me all looked, well, pretty special. I'd like to try something from that part of the menu on my next visit. And I don't think it will be long before that time comes.

We swung by GTC for a quick snack on Sunday afternoon. I really love the switch to a bar in exchange for the shopping area that previously occupied the left side of the restaurant. There are lots of interesting sounding cocktails and, of course, a very solid wine list.   There are two versions of Bloody Marys - one is fairly traditional and one is made with green tomatillos and garnished with cheese-stuffed olives and a pepper. In my opinion, the traditional bloody could use a bit of salt or worcestershire or a salted rim, but it was solid. The green BM was interesting and tasty but the standard red is still my preference.   We shared a bowl of pasta e fagioli and the house made mozzarella. Both were excellent and really hit the spot. Said mozz is available for just five bucks during the weekday happy hour which runs from 4-7. My fiancé and I were in agreement that we need to get back for that happy hour ASAP.

As my stomach starts its predictable pre-lunch growling, I can't stop thinking about the delicious meal I had last night at My Thai. Dinner kicked off with a shared plate of steamed dumplings in three varieties: veggie, shrimp and pork. The dumplings were all topped with some crunchy fried garlic, a nice touch.   My date and I were under the impression that the place was a BYO, but we were quickly informed that there was indeed a liquor license. We made our bottle of brew disappear and ordered some Sapporos instead. I'm almost positive that's Japanese for Coors Light. No matter; a light beer went just fine with the spicy flavors of our main courses. For me, that included a heaping plate of chicken and shrimp with baby corn, onions, peppers and cashews in a mildly spicy brown sauce (him-ma-pan shrimp and chicken). White rice was served on the side, as well as some steamed veggies which included broccoli, carrots and cabbage. The extra veggies were a nice touch and a welcome alternative to the rice, which my boyfriend gladly accepted. His pot of chicken and veggies in a lemongrass scented broth was far hotter and more complex in flavor. While I am personally not a big fan of lemongrass, he enjoyed the dish and said he would order it again. I was more than pleased with my choice, which I polished off without much help.   The cost of dinner was in line with and probably even less than many of the gastropubs we frequent. After our lovely meal, we agreed to make more of an effort to step outside the box when choosing a weeknight dining destination.

GTC has become one of my favorite dinner destinations. The menu is reasonable enough for a weeknight meal but also a great option for a weekend dinner with friends. You can BYO wine with no corkage fee, even though there is a full bar.   As far as the menu goes, the house specialty frites is always a great choice. The butcher's steak option comes with 7 ounces of delicious, perfectly cooked steak, topped with butter and served with a choice of three sauces. Duck fat fries come standard but I haven't had any problems subbing a salad instead. The salsa verde is basically a chimichurri sauce and it is perfection.     On my most recent visit, I opted for the trout almondine, which was incredible. I only wish that it was served with a side salad since it was basically just the fish, with a whole lot of fresh parsley on top. GTC should consider adding a section of sides since many of their entrees are served a la carte, like the trout.   Of the smaller plates, you can't go wrong with the house made mozzarella or the French onion soup. I look forward to my next visit!

I'm bummed to say that my second visit to Race Street Cafe was a bust. On Saturday of Memorial Day weekend, the bar was understaffed and overwhelmed. Our server was nice but clearly spread too thin between the many occupied tables in and outside. Our food took forever and drinks were almost as long.   The food was good for bar food but there was no reason why we should have waited as long as we did. Needless to say, I won't be recommending the place on a weekend though I'm sure I'll return for lunch sometime.

Delivery via Eat24 from Hummus Grill was solid. I ordered the grilled chicken platter with rice, cucumber and tomato salad, tabbouleh and hummus. It came with a side of wheat pita, as well as some delicious homemade hot sauce.   The delivery travel caused the ingredients in the container to shift around a bit, but nothing was spilling or too messy, which I appreciated.   I skipped the pita in an effort to keep the carb count down so no comments on that. The rest of the food was definitely enough for two filling meals. Though the chicken wasn't all white meat, which I prefer, it was completely boneless and had a really nice grilled taste. All other sides complemented the chicken nicely and tasted very fresh.   Hopefully meal two out of this order will taste just as good for lunch tomorrow. Glad to have another solid delivery spot that doesn't break the bank.

Scoop DeVille and I go way back, to my early career days when I worked at a law firm. One of the (very few) highlights was when we'd order ice cream delivery for the department. Scoop DeVille was the only place doing sweet treat delivery at the time and we were oh-so-grateful. I hadn't had their treats since that time and was thrilled to be reunited when I spotted them at The Bourse at their November opening.   Since then, Scoop DeVille has become my go-to for all my ice cream needs. They are known for their blends, but I'm more of a hard ice cream girl and theirs is fantastic! The constantly-rotating selection always offers something unique and delicious, and the friendly employees are happy to oblige sample requests. Recently, I've had the Cookie Monster ice cream, the Nick Foles ice cream (loved this one!), and another with peanut butter cups and Reese's pieces. All of their ice creams are rich and flavorful; I think Scoop DeVille easily beats out everything at the grocery store.   I've yet to try the chipwiches or other desserts but plan to make my way through all of them, eventually. I love this place and have a hard time walking through The Bourse and not stopping for a pint to take home!

Update! It has been years since my last Sidecar review! Nearly four, to be exact. Meanwhile, Sidecar is my go-to neighborhood bar, I practically know the menu by heart, I have consistently great experiences with servers and bartenders there, they always play great music... the list goes on!   Something I'm really loving that they didn't have the last time I wrote a review is the addition of a few really nicely done cocktails. I've been drinking less beer and more wine and cocktails lately, and I absolutely love the raspberry cooler, with fresh raspberry iced tea, vodka, simple syrup and fresh lemon and mint. It's a simple drink that isn't overly sweet, which is just perfect for me.    The food is consistent, whether you go for brunch or dinner, and I love that the kitchen is open late. My go-tos are the pretzel chicken bites, carnitas, salads and, when I'm feeling extra splurge-y, the Super Mario burger. Delish. Anything on their brunch menu is a hit with me. Thanks for holding it down in the 'hood, Sidecar.

Just a reminder that Frangelli's is still the South Philly bakery you want, need and deserve. I picked up cannoli donuts and sticky buns for a recent tailgate party (this was a serious tailgate party!) and they were, of course, a huge hit. The donuts were so fresh and the sticky buns were just incredible. Their prices have increased since my last visit but still remain very affordable. Totally worth that deep South Philly drive and questionable park job for sure!

I met my sister for lunch at Le Bus on a day off. It was fairly quiet but we were there on the earlier side. I've been opting for meatless meals lately so I was limited to a handful of options like the salads, grilled cheese, and fritatta.   I opted for the fritatta which was a great choice as it was filled with veggies and both ricotta and cheddar cheeses. The bread basket we had at our table was the perfect accompaniment. I actually was able to take some of my fritatta home as well.   My sister had a Caesar salad which was super basic; it was just romaine with dressing and some grilled shrimp on top. I think she was expecting croutons but since she said she didn't want the French bread that came with perhaps they didn't put any on... but I bet Le Bus could do some great croutons.   Our server was nice but not super attentive; luckily it was easy to flag him down when I needed a coffee refill.   My sister goes to Le Bus for dinner once in a while and she said the menu is more expansive at night so I would be interested in checking that out sometime.

I have to admit, I was super bummed when I heard about Resurrection Ale House's closing. RAH was one of my favorite neighborhood bars and I really loved the staff. Luckily, Devil's Pocket is a suitable replacement.   The food and beer menus are definitely more basic than some of RAH's offerings, but I'm okay with that. In a city where craft beer reigns supreme, it was nice to see a light beer on tap. I love craft beer but, sometimes, I just want an easy drinking, low-calorie brew. Stop judging, beer snobs!   Not low in calories but well worth the splurge are the Hell in a Hand Basket fries: thin-cut spuds topped with whiz, chili, pickled jalapeños and scallions. YES. The mac and cheese was okay - I'm not crazy about rye and the mac is topped with rye croutons. You can also add bacon. I was definitely a fan of the turkey pot pie and have to agree with Stephen H - a side of cranberry sauce would take this dish from good to great.     My fiancé introduced me to Marcus, one of two owners, who was super sweet and seemed very excited about his new place. Wishing them the best and looking forward to many more visits!

When I attended the Barre Om class at Sculpere during Yelp's Fit Club, I knew I would be returning on my own as soon as the month was over. Cristina was a fantastic instructor for our class of Sculpere newbs and I left feeling like I had a great workout but without feeling like I had been tortured through the class. I couldn't wait to try more.   I was a little nervous about the yoga sculpt class, which is essentially yoga with hand weights. It had been a while since my last yoga session and I was nervous about the added weight component, but my friend Melissa P and I decided to give it a shot. So glad we did, because I absolutely loved that class as well! It was definitely challenging but every time I felt like I couldn't do one more lift/squat/etc, the set was over. I liked the class more than traditional yoga, which I tend to get bored with easily. I left with the relaxed feeling of attending a yoga class, and two days later I'm a bit sore in some areas which means I had a great workout as well.  Can't wait for my next session!

This PJ's is very close to where I grew up so it's probably the one I've been to most, although I prefer the Westmont/Haddonfield location.  Maple Shade PJ's has the same good bar food and beer specials, but the service is usually slower and not as accurate.  For example, while lunching with my sister today, I asked for my salad dressing on the side.  The salad came out with the dressing on top.  It was easy to push some aside so it wasn't a big deal (it was a wedge salad, just to give you a visual image).  Had the dressing been mixed in (chopped salad style), I would have gone a little Chuck Norris because a) I hate overly dressed salads and refuse to eat a plate of dressing with some lettuce and, b) sending it back would have only added more time to my already maxed out lunch break.     Now when you have me over for salad you know what not to do.

I want to love this place.  There are definitely things I love about it~ the guacamole, the black bean and salsa dip, the decor, the churro dessert... but the experience as a whole?  Eh.    It's hit or miss.  I've been there and have ordered things that came out perfect (quesadillas, fajitas, fish tacos); and I've been there and ordered things that sound awesome in theory (honey lime scallops, chicken mole, chicken and sweet potato burrito) and they just taste bland.  An average place gets an average 3 stars.  Also, don't be the last party in there... or the remaining uncut staff will give you the hairy eyeball and you'll be lucky if they don't start turning off the lights!

These four stars are for the happy hour, which is positively awesome, especially considering the location. A handful of us had plans to meet up at one of Rittenhouse's bar/restaurants, only to discover the place was closed for a private party.
