We scoured our brains to come up with an appropriate Plan B, and Alma de Cuba saved the day.  Happy hour runs every weeknight from 5-7 and features six dollar sangria and two types of mojitos. Small plates are half off, which is a total bargain. Everything ordered looked delish, though I only tried the toasted hazelnut guacamole since I had plans for dinner.   While I wasn't crazy about the sweet sangria, the traditional mojito did the trick. It was boozy but light; perfect for summer sipping. It had been years since my last trip to Alma de Cuba, but they are now on the short list of happy hour spots.

Our group stopped in Reds Bar for a quick beverage while making our way down the Pacific Coast Highway in November. First thoughts: Santa Barbara is a cool town! We all would like to go back sometime. First thoughts of Reds Bar: cute, and a little divey. I dig.   We were the first patrons to arrive and the only patrons during our brief stay. Despite this, service was pretty laid-back. We had to walk up to the bar to order our drinks and, even though there were only four, one of the drinks was incorrect. It was mine, of course, but I went with it and the drink I received was pretty tasty. Not sure how the low-key service would fare with a larger crowd but it was fine for just our little crew. That bathroom could probably use a scrub down, though.

This is a quickie review for anyone considering Tinto for Restaurant Week. I just returned from my dinner and both my friend and I were thrilled with the food, service and price of our meal.   The Restaurant Week menu is fairly expansive and very generous - we shared eight plates plus a dessert course which was just the right size, as we were stuffed by that point. Also, I'm not drinking this month, and our server said the bartender would be able to whip something up for me. I had an alcohol-free sangria which was light and fun. Having a mocktail option really helps me get past the no-wine-for-me sads at the beginning of the meal.   Another thing that I should mention is that the pacing was perfect. We were not rushed at all and spent a leisurely two hours at dinner. If you're considering Tinto for Restaurant Week, or anytime really, just make your reservation already!

Looking good, Cafe Ynez! We stopped in for breakfast on opening day and it appeared the staff were firing on all cylinders. Of course, I asked for the one thing they don't have yet, fresh juice, but I was informed that they will be getting their juice machine later in the week. All three of us opted for coffee - we were asked if we wanted cream and I can definitely say I would have preferred to have that on the side so I could add it in myself, but my cup had just the right amount for my tastes so I was happy.   The decor looks great. It's like a cute little Mexican-themed diner - I love it. The menu of all-day items isn't super extensive but everything on it sounds awesome. There is also a smaller menu with brunch options. I opted for the vegetarian enchiladas which contained beans, avocado and some fresh veggies, all topped with queso fresco, sour cream and a fried egg. It hit the spot! While we waited, we were served fresh tortilla chips and some salsa verde. Nice! My boyfriend housed his breakfast burrito and our friend's plate of chilaquiles looked great. We're pumped to have this new option in the neighborhood and it won't be long before we're back again.

After reading Marcello D.'s very solid review of Tony's, I swung by one day last week while running errands on my lunch break.    The door was held open for me by a friendly gentleman on his way out, and I entered to hear the husband and wife duo behind the counter speaking to each other in Italian.  Swoon!  I ordered two slices to go, one plain and one veggie.  Fifteen minutes later I was back at my desk, inhaling the pizza as fast as humanly possible.  The slices were nicely sized and with a thin crust.  The toppings on the veggie pizza made me feel downright healthy about my lunch choice.  I felt like I gave into my pizza craving without going way overboard in the calorie department.  Whether or not that was true... is irrelevant at this point.  I have had better pizza, but for a quick takeout slice, Tony's wasn't a bad option.  I'll check them out again sometime soon.

Today was my first trip to Yokohama, post-renovations, and I can't believe it is the same place.  Walking in, you almost forget that you are in the middle of a Jersey strip mall and not a trendy new spot in Philly.  The interior has been completely upgraded and now features a bar, a waterfall wall and a hibachi room.  I love that they kept this separate from the rest of the dining area, as I wouldn't want to smell like a hibachi chicken after a sushi meal.    Speaking of which, the sushi at Yokohama is top notch.  As others have mentioned, the rolls come with an above average amount of fish and minimal rice, so you can actually taste the flavors.  The lunch menu is a total steal, and even more so when your dining companion picks up the tab (domo arigato, Mom!).    I was feeling pretty hungry today so I decided on a three roll combo, which came with soup or salad.  I selected a spicy tuna roll, California roll and tuna avocado roll.  I asked our server if they would make the last roll crunchy and it was not a problem.  As always, the rolls were delicious, nicely sized and I was absolutely stuffed after our meal.  I used to think of this place as a great spot for lunch but now I will also keep it in mind for a nice dinner option on this side of the bridge.

My first trip to Little Spoon Cafe was good. At noon, there were plenty of tables available and no wait to order. Water glasses were brought over to the table and I went to the counter to place an order for myself and my dining companion, Simone A.   I love that the tables have everything you could possibly need - flatware, napkins, salt, pepper, ketchup and Cholula. All my usual staples!   Simone ordered the grilled cheese of the day and some tomato soup, which she said were both very good. I opted for the BLT, no mayo, add avocado. We also shared a side of the baked parmesan fries. Both sandwiches came with awesome dill pickles.   I was really surprised that the bread for the BLT was not toasted - I would have asked if I had known. Otherwise, the sandwich was nice, but I did have a little regret for not going with my other choice, the Cuban. The fries definitely had that distinct baked texture - not a lot of crispiness to them - but they came with a lot less residual guilt than if they had been fried! No one came around to refill waters so we had to take our cups back to the then-busy counter to ask. Maybe some carafes on the ledge by the window for people to self-serve would be helpful!  Definitely looking forward to round two and trying that Cuban.

Overall, I'm very pleased with the care I received from Rothman. I fractured my ankle in July and it has been a long, slow recovery process. I saw Dr. Karanjia who was awesome and a perfect fit for me, personality-wise. He's super funny and personable. He has a way of making bad news seem not so bad, and he's really great at explaining the process.   I was put into a boot up to my knee for five weeks. Normally, it would be six, but I really wanted to downgrade before my brother's wedding. I went to see Dr. Karanjia at the five week mark and, after an x-ray, he confirmed that my bone was healed and I was ready to move into a much smaller brace. After four weeks of wearing the brace, I went back this morning and got clearance to start physical therapy. Sadly, I'm still in the brace until I get the clear from a therapist, but it's been beaten into my head at this point that a slow healing process is necessary if I don't want to risk re-injuring myself.   Everyone I encountered at this office was very friendly and professional. Wait times were never more than a few minutes, which was fantastic. Highly recommended if you are able to get into this practice - I've heard it can be hard to get an appointment, but that was (thankfully) not my experience.

I am definitely loving Seasons 52, a diet-friendly restaurant that serves nothing over 475 calories.  All items are made with fresh ingredients and cooked over a grill or with olive oil, when necessary.  On my first excursion, I enjoyed the steak and gorgonzola flatbread, which I requested sans mushrooms.  The flatbread was filling enough for lunch and felt like a splurge.  My second visit was this afternoon.  My mom and I split the garlic chicken flatbread and the buffalo burger.  The flatbread was okay, definitely not as good as the one I had on my prior visit.  The chicken resembled the stuff from Lean Cuisine flatbreads, which I usually try to avoid.  Fortunately, it tasted better, but I couldn't shake the unappetizing resemblance.  The burger arrived split in half, which was nice because our server must have special requested that when we indicated that we were sharing the dishes.  It was predictably on the small side, but I enjoyed every juicy bite.  I would absolutely order this again in the future.   The selection of wines is excellent, although they were out of the sauvignon blanc that my mom requested.  Fortunately, our server was able to make a suggestion for something comparable, which is always appreciated.    I'm going back later this week with girlfriends and am looking forward to another bikini-friendly meal.

Excellent experience at this Square One location this morning! I love the 13th Street shop and was surprised to discover that there is another right on JFK Blvd. The aesthetic is similar - it's a really attractive coffee shop with clear signage and nice people.   There isn't as much seating in this shop as there is on 13th Street, but I was able to grab a couple chairs at a community table, which served my purposes well since I had multiple meetings.   I'm battling a winter cold which is making me feel groggy and tired, so I really needed a pick-me-up upon arrival. Their Americano comes with four shots of espresso and you'd better believe that woke me up. The barista was super friendly and very enjoyable to chat with; he recommended that I try one of the immune booster shots that they carry in their cold case. I selected the one with turmeric, vitamin C and some other ish I can't remember. The taste wasn't super pleasant but I'm down to try anything if it will help kick this cold.   Definitely putting this Square One into the meetings rotation.

For the most part, I get by with a little help from my friends. However, during a stressful time in my life, a close friend suggested I give therapy a whirl. I got to work researching local therapists who take insurance. Easier said than done, because many therapists run private practices and do not take insurance. I'm still not exactly sure how I came across Delaware County Professional Services, but I'm so glad I did because they were like hitting the therapy jackpot.   First, you call for the initial appointment. At this appointment, you meet with the captain of the therapist team and have a little chat about what's going on in your life, etc. He chooses a therapist that he feels will be a good fit going forward. I really like this step and feel that it was a crucial one in finding the right person for me as an individual.   I can't say enough about the therapist I saw once a week for several months' time [I'm purposely omitting that person's name because what worked for me may not be the best fit for someone else (see second paragraph)]. Being able to share your deepest thoughts with someone you can trust while receiving their unbiased feedback is so, so helpful.   I'm generally a private person when it comes to my personal life, and I'm putting my pride aside to write this review, because I genuinely hope it helps someone. When I started my research, it took hours before I finally narrowed down to DCPS and a lot of nerve to pick up the phone and dial. The difference in how I felt before therapy compared with after was night and day. I had a much better understanding of my feelings and a whole lot more clarity. And there's absolutely no shame in that. I wouldn't hesitate to use DCPS' services again and would absolutely recommend the practice to anyone looking to lift some emotional weight off their shoulders.

Our return to Rex was just days after our first visit, we liked it so much. I had logged an extra long run that day and I was jonesin' for something a little richer. I ordered a salad to start and it was nice, but barely touched by dressing and pretty light on the toppings. No big, I had a burger coming my way.   My medium burger arrived looking super tasty. I sliced it in half as I normally do and as I picked up half I noticed that it was extremely red inside. On closer inspection, it was actually still raw. I notified the bartender and they took it back to the kitchen. Not very long after, a new burger appeared, but again, it was really undercooked on the inside when I sliced it. The staff agreed and it was taken back to the kitchen. The third time, the burger was brought out to me and the manager said they had sliced it in the kitchen to make sure it was cooked. I kind of thought that maybe it was my previously-sliced burger thrown back on the grill, but I honestly didn't really care at that point as long as it was edible. Of course, the center of the burger looked fine because of the cut but the center of each half was definitely still too red for medium. I kind of ate around the innermost parts. Honestly, the burger was very nice and it would have been great had it been properly cooked.   What ultimately left a bad taste in my mouth was that the burger was on our check, after having sent it back twice. I feel weird saying it but I suppose my expectation was that it would have been comped since it went back and forth to the kitchen as my boyfriend struggled between waiting for me to eat or letting his food get cold.  This doesn't change my feelings about Rex, and I'm still really happy that they are in the neighborhood. I had one bad experience but it's not going to stop me from going back, and hopefully adding back some stars in the process!

Why does Collingswood get all the cool things AFTER I move? Luckily, my sister now lives in the area so I get to visit my old stomping grounds on the reg. And Devil's Creek Brewery, conveniently located in the middle of town in the Lumberyard complex, is going to be a regular stop.   The tasting room was packed on Friday night and we even ran into friends from the city when we walked in. This place is definitely a destination. Laws prevent the brewery from serving food but you can BYO or order delivery if you're so inclined.   I really enjoyed the pilsner and also the IPA on nitro (Nitro Man). There were six or seven beers of different styles, so most likely something for everyone. The business owners and other staff were all super fun and nice and we had a great time socializing. I look forward to many more visits!

One of my close friends introduced me to Cherry St. Tavern because her fiance lives around the corner and it's their go-to spot for beer in a laid-back environment.  Something about the place reminds me of my grandparents' basement, but in a good way.  It's just a comfortable place to be.    Pitchers are available, food is basic but pretty darn good (especially while trying to soak up the alcohol), there's a juke box filled with classics and last but not least, there is a super cute bartender.  What else could a girl need?

My mom had discounted tickets for the Philly Sightseeing Tour so we took my grandmom out for a day of sightseeing. This tour can really be made or broken by the tour guide. For the first half of our day (start point at The Bourse to the Art Museum), our guide mumbled and wasn't very enthusiastic.   We decided to walk around the Art Museum for a bit, so by the time we got back on the bus, we had a new tour guide. He was friendly, enthusiastic and knew a lot about the city. I was a bit disappointed that he promoted Pat's and Geno's, however. There was one other local on the bus as well and we sort of gave each other the eye like, "Really? Really?!" Friends, there are far better cheesesteaks out there!   While I didn't learn anything new about the city, from a local's point of view, I thought the tour did a very nice job showcasing Philadelphia to visitors.

I loved my weekday brunch at The Dutch. Everything from the food to service was great. The interior is nice but there are also several tables outside, which is where we decided to dine.   The menu is short and sweet but very well-rounded. I loved that there were several options for breakfast meats. I ordered the eggs, meat, bread, potato plate and asked to sub a side salad for bread, which was not a problem. I selected the turkey bacon as my meat and it had great flavor. I loved the seasoned potatoes as well. My dining companion had the banana pancakes which looked heavenly.   Our servers kept our coffee and water glasses full and were very sweet. Great experience and I'm looking forward to my next visit.

My husband and I were in the mood for something different over the weekend so we decided to treat ourselves to delivery from Oyster House. Two entrees, plus all the associated delivery fees, came close to $70, but we enjoyed our entrees and were happy to have a night off from cooking.   I had the pan roasted flounder with broccoli, chickpeas and tahini. I wasn't crazy about the tahini and would likely ask for that on the side next time. The fish was cooked perfectly, however, and the dish was overall a nice, healthy meal. My husband had the fisherman's stew which had great flavor.   I'd love if Oyster House offered some healthy sides like roasted vegetables or baked potatoes. We weren't feeling fries or salads so we ended up making a side at home to complement our entrees. Solid experience overall, though, and we'd definitely order from them again!

Of all the Philly Fine Wine & Good Spirits stores, this one is definitely up there among the nicest and most organized. Occasionally I have had some luck with getting decent recommendations from staff members, but more often than not I have to do some iphone research from the aisles.   The woman who was sampling wines from CA on my recent visit was knowledgeable not just about the wines she was pouring but also other wines in the store. The cashiers are fast and friendly.   It's still not as good as the stores in New Jersey but it's an improvement over other FW&GS locations.

Love, love, love this gelato and coffee shop! I was headed to West Chester to host an event and decided to get there a couple hours early to beat any rush hour traffic. I had some studying to catch up on for my French class so I needed a quiet spot with wifi and great coffee. Gemelli came up in a Yelp search and it proved to be the perfect spot.   The gelato and desserts looked amazing. It was all I could do to not order something splurge-y and call it a day. Instead, I ordered a latte with fresh whipped cream. I also tried a sample of the cannoli gelato which was heaven. I immediately texted my sister to say I'd be willing to drive to West Chester anytime so she could visit her old college stomping grounds... and get gelato.   I'm sure this cafe gets packed with families and college kids in the evening, but it provided the perfect, quiet place for me to hunker down and crack the books during the afternoon. Can't wait to return for that amazing gelato!

I attended a baby shower at Brio on Sunday and it was so-so. Honestly, the food was pretty good. The service, particularly my table's server, was not very helpful and came across as unfriendly at times. She practically threw plates onto the table - I'm surprised the sauce in my pasta didn't splash. Water glasses sat for a while until another server came to fill them. We also had to ask for coffee while other tables were offered.   Onto the food. We had a choice of soup or salad followed by a few entree choices. I had the Caesar salad which was lightly dressed and had nice, crisp lettuce. My entree selection was ricotta-filled pasta in vodka sauce. Pretty rich but also really tasty.   My biggest complaint about the shower was that it was an absolutely beautiful day and we were stuck in two small back rooms with a half wall between the two. Meanwhile, there was a nice-sized, covered patio nearby that probably could have fit everyone and it would have been much nicer.   The main area of the restaurant was just a giant room that didn't really have a lot of personality. While I've never had a sit-down dinner at Brio, I do like their happy hour though I prefer the Marlton location because I like the bright bar/lounge space.

Clearly, I am in the minority, but I was underwhelmed by Fuji Mountain.  The meal started with a plate of complimentary edamame.  No complaints there but I don't know that it's possible to have strong feelings one way or the other about steamed soy beans with salt.  Next up was the house salad with ginger sesame dressing.  It's one thing to eat a salad with chopsticks, and do so gracefully.  It's another to eat large leaves of dressing-covered lettuce with chopsticks.  The salad was good, but due to the awkwardness of it all, I quit midway through.    For me, the pinnacle of Fuji Mountain was their clear soup.  It was served in a large bowl and had a huge scallop at the bottom.    Our rolls arrived soon after the soup.  There were five total: a California, tuna, spicy tuna, spicy yellowtail, and one other tuna variation.  I tried one bite of each, and had a really hard time deciding which roll, if any, I liked enough for a second round.  The rice was perfectly sticky but completely took over.  The fish itself was a little too room temperature for my liking and comparable in quality to the stuff at Wegman's.  Don't get me wrong, I love the Weg's but when I'm at a Japanese restaurant I expect something a little better.      The mochi that ended our meal was great but tiny.  I'm talking "the body of Christ, Amen" size.    On the plus side, our service was great, and I adore any Japanese restaurant that makes a practice of shouting out a greeting to clientele.  Fuji Mountain wasn't my cup of green tea, but they certainly have many loyal fans who love the place so I wish them well.

I'm going with four stars after two experiences. The first was a couple weeks ago. We arrived in time for happy hour and enjoyed several delicious and well-balanced margaritas. We ordered chips and salsa and, since we couldn't decide between the two, guac and black bean hummus. All three of these starters came with the same tortilla chips, dusted in a salty (albeit tasty) seasoning. I would love to see different chips (plantain, yuca, etc.) served with the guac to shake things up. I'd order the guac again but probably not the salsa, unless they switched it to more of a pico. The salsa was very similar (if not the same?) as what is served with the tacos. I'd also really love to see a lighter starter offered, like a shrimp ceviche.  Tacos are definitely the star of the show, and we especially loved the carne asada with black bean puree. The fish taco was nice, and the shrimp taco was very good. Our dinner rang in around $100 - pretty steep on a weeknight. The happy hour takes out some of the sting but cheap Mexican this is not.   Fast forward a couple weeks later to when I was home and craving tacos. I noticed Tio Flores on a delivery service and decided to go for it. Delivery can be a tricky beast but I was pleasantly surprised when my shrimp tacos arrived in immaculate condition. They were excellent and the corn tortillas held up well. I was happy that there were a couple sides of salsa included.   I can't finish this off without mentioning how much I hated the chairs in the dining room. They are extremely uncomfortable! Next time, I'm going for bar seating or a booth, if possible.

My experience at Marigold Kitchen on Saturday night was definitely a memorable one. I'm currently challenging myself to a month of no meat/poultry. I didn't want to make a big deal of this so I was prepared to go into my meal at Marigold with the intention of ordering fish for my entree and then just passing anything with meat or poultry to my boyfriend. But the restaurant called a day or so in advance to confirm our reservation, and they specifically asked if there were any dietary restrictions. My boyfriend mentioned that one of us is following a pescetarian diet and they said that was no problem at all. In hindsight, it was the best thing that could have happened because I was able to enjoy the entire meal without having to sacrifice any of the courses. So the takeaway from this situation is that accommodations can be made with advance notice and the experience will not be compromised. Super!  Everyone on the staff from the moment we walked in the door to the moment we left was just wonderful. The restaurant is in a lovely converted house so there are a few different dining rooms. I liked that the tables were spaced out enough that it felt like a private dining experience.    We started with some crazy awesome truffle-flavored, liquid nitrogen-treated popcorn. From there, the bites started to flow from the kitchen. Since the beginning courses were amuse bouches and small plates, each course was quickly followed by the next. Once the plates started getting a bit larger, the pacing slowed down a bit which was just perfect. Some of my favorite bites of the night were the popcorn, a cheese puff, butternut squash soup with cinnamon foam, lobster pot pie, the cheese course and the most amazing dessert which featured both frozen and hot components. I've been thinking about it every day since.  Dining at Marigold Kitchen was an awesome experience and I'd be delighted to go back again. This one is going on the short list for special occasions.

A group of friends and I hit up Talula's Daily last week for their January dinner tasting. It was a meal I had been looking forward to for a while, and everything about the experience exceeded my expectations. In particular, our service. I could not say enough about our amazing server, Erin. She went above and beyond to accommodate some special requests at our table and she was just incredible throughout our meal, which lasted several hours.   Our group of eight were seated at the long table, which was beautifully set. I had heard a lot of hoopla about some overselling of the Anthropologie-brand tableware, but we experienced none of that during our visit. Honestly, the products sell themselves; I would happily set a table with anything used during our visit.   From the warm bean dip to the smoked trout salad to the delicious chicken and dumplings to the whimsical cheese plate to the grand finale of assorted cookies and pastries, dinner was FANTASTIC. I wasn't drinking but those who opted in to the beverage pairing seemed very happy with their decision. As if we hadn't been completely spoiled already, we were all given a parting gift of delicious homemade granola with dark chocolate. It was the perfect treat the next day and a great reminder of our meal. Can't wait for my next dinner at Talula's!

Met a friend for lunch at Soup Kitchen and enjoyed my experience. The space was larger than expected, with plenty of tables for what is probably a light lunch crowd, given the less-busy neighborhood. While I'd love to try the meatloaf sandwich sometime, both of us opted for the shakshuka. It's basically a vegetarian chili with two over easy eggs and some feta cheese. It's spicy and delicious, served with a piece of toasted French bread.   Service was really relaxed; we had to sort of grab someone from time to time if we needed anything, but it wasn't a big deal. I will definitely come back sometime... and I may even go out of my way for another bowl of that shakshuka!

Although I've never set foot in the store, I have been the lucky recipient of some gifts from Duross & Langel. I am a huge fan of bubble baths, and while there is indeed a time and place for Mr. Bubble, a girl likes to luxuriate every now and again. D&L's vanilla bubble bath has a pleasant scent without overpowering. Just a tiny teaspoonful was more than enough to produce tons-o-suds once I turned on the jets in my tub. Best of all, after soaking for over a half hour, my skin didn't feel the least bit dry.  Also in my arsenal is a container of brand new lavender-scented relaxation bathing salts that will undoubtedly leave my bathroom smelling like a Rittenhouse day spa. Serenity is mine!

Yesterday, I attended the annual oyster shucking competition at Oyster House, where professionals and amateurs battle it out to see who can schuck the best.   The five dollar cover charge to watch the competition was completely tacky. Yes, oysters were passed around to guests after they were shucked, but they were donated to begin with. The bar was full and mostly everyone had a drink in hand; money was being made. So that's how I felt about that.  Otherwise, the crowd was great, the event was a good time, and the bloody Marys were on-point.

Since my first visit to Farmers' Cabinet last week, I've already been back twice. This review is regarding my experience at the bar only, since I've yet to eat there. When Phoebe is on the roster, you know you're in good hands. I've sampled several of the cocktails, including the beer-inspired selections, and there really is something for everyone on the list. Well, except for that guy who foolishly asked for a bloody Mary the other night. Maybe not him.   Bar snacks make a triumphant and interesting return in the form of sometimes sweet, sometimes spicy (sometimes a little of both!) popcorn and roasted barley. My digestive system thanks Farmers' Cabinet for the unexpected fiber supplement with my liquor.  The old-timey decor is stellar, and I've noticed more and more people dressing the part of Prohibition-era rebels. Best of all, though, is the band, Drew Nugent and the Midnight Society. The dapper outfits, the old-school microphone, the horns and the lead singer's Eddie Cantor-like vocals are just perfect. Even a song called "My girl's p***y" had people grinning ear to ear and singing along during a Friday night performance.   I adore this place.

Hello, new favorite food truck! I was pumped to learn of the Fry Truck's existence and its appearance at the Wheat Beer Fest in Point Breeze was serendipitous. The menu is quite extensive - several types of fry options, loads of different topping combinations - these guys thought of everything!  In the end, we decided to try the waffle fries, Vicki N' Pete style, which came with Old Bay and melted American cheese. As we waited for the order, I helped myself to a large cup of ketchup and lots of napkins from the counter.   The serving size of our order of fries was enormous! The spuds were perfectly cooked and very tasty. They were possibly a little too salty which only caused my beer to go down faster (festival problems). Later, I had a bite from a friend's order which had waffle fries (no added seasoning) and steak, and they were awesome, too. Can't wait to bump into this truck at another festival soon!

My husband and I were in the area (I recently discovered Suburban Square and let's just say I'm obsessed) and looking for something new-to-us for dinner. Biga popped up on a search for pizza and had great reviews, so the decision was easy!   We were greeted warmly by the hostesses and seated. I loved the interesting non-alcoholic beverage options and ordered a grapefruit concoction called nautical nonsense, which was reminiscent of a paloma. It was refreshing and a great cocktail substitute.   We started with the farro salad which was super tasty. I don't think my husband has ever been so into kale! Next, we shared a classic margherita and da bomb, with soppressata and chilis. The latter packed a punch in both flavor and heat. We loved both pies and they were sizable enough to enjoy several slices from each and still take a few home.   Great experience all around and I will definitely think of Biga again next time I'm in the area!

Machi Sushi is one of the few sushi restaurants that delivers during the afternoon on a weekday, so I gave it a whirl. There is a delivery minimum (but no delivery charge), and the three roll combo didn't get me there so I added on a seaweed salad. With tip, this made my lunch a little on the pricy side at $20, but it was worth it.   The delivery arrived quickly, and the sushi rolls were pretty good and just how I requested. I had a shrimp tempura roll, a spicy tuna roll and a regular tuna roll with crunchy flakes added. There were eight small-sized pieces to each roll, and I was happy with the portion size. The seaweed salad was average if a little too oily. I had a few bites but mostly stuck to the rolls. I'll probably opt for a house salad or soup to get to that minimum next time.

It's always a little awkward returning to a business after giving a not-so-stellar review. Fortunately, the staff at Rex 1516 were total class acts when I showed up for lunch today, welcoming me back and immediately apologizing for the previous snafu. Much as I wanted to give that burger another try, the thought of something so heavy in my stomach before my run this afternoon swayed me into ordering the fish tacos instead.  This turned out to be a wise choice. The blackened fish was perfectly cooked and heaped into two doubled-up flour tortillas, with lettuce, tomato, red onion and what (I am pretty certain) was a goat cheese cream sauce. They were absolutely delicious and satisfied my hunger without making me feel like I needed a nap.  My dining companion, Allison B, tried her hardest to finish her hefty brie and bacon sandwich, but she had to throw in the towel with a few bites left. She put in a good effort, though. Our check was dropped and my tacos had been comped, which was extremely nice. Even nicer for Allison, as she graciously offered to pick up the tab (folks, she's now loaded with this new job of hers).   Lunch in an hour may be a tight squeeze, but for those days when the boss is out, Rex is the perfect spot for a leisurely meal.

My mom and I got into a little happy hour action at Harvest a couple weeks ago and it was a pretty solid experience overall. The bar area is bright and sunny and the bar is quite large, with lots of tables around as well.   The happy hour deals are pretty sweet, but the best bang for your buck is in the food offerings. Flatbreads are large and offered for just five bucks. They are much more substantial than the flatbreads at a similar restaurant chain and a lot tastier, too.   The happy hour wines were a steal but the wines themselves were not great. My mom and I both switched to full price glasses after our first round. All in all, it was an inexpensive night out and I always love having healthier alternatives to happy hour snacks.

A full upgrade to five stars is long overdue for this Philly staple. I've been back time and again and, while most visits are for drinks only, I have a great time every time. Last Saturday night we stopped in twice, for pre-dinner and post-dinner drinks. Their earl grey hot toddy is perfect for a chilly night, and the wine list has something for everyone and at reasonable price points to boot. Bartenders are friendly. The music selection is always a fun mix - loved the 70s disco jams on our recent visit!   My previous review nearly nine years ago reflects the opinions of a different, must less mature person. I'm older now, I'm wiser now.

Davio's Galleria is one of the few (if not the only) coffee shops around the KOP Town Center. It's big and roomy, quiet, never crowded (I often go at random times, like mid-late afternoon), has free wifi, big tables and access to outlets. What more could a girl ask for?   Coffee. They have it.   Food. They have that, too, but they are often out of ingredients. Again, I usually pop in later in the day, so it's probably on me if certain items aren't available any longer.   I love this place for what it is and have always had a good experience.

Monday night at the newest Thai joint in town only proved that we are in desperate need of more good Thai food in this city. We scored a table for two around 6:45. By 7:15, every table was full.   The small BYO makes use of its space by fitting as many tables as possible onto the dining floor. It's not too tight for diners once everyone is seated, but I noticed that it was difficult for the staff to get around at times. The walls really are as lime green as they look in the pictures, and the large windows have pretty green leaf patterns along the top panels, creating a tree effect.   Throughout our dinner, our server seemed a bit swamped, but everything we ordered came out correctly. I did have to ask a couple times before I received a soda, and the same thing happened again when I needed a refill. In a few weeks, service should be smooth sailing.  We started with the dumplings, which were lightly fried and very flavorful. My boyfriend had a noodle dish that was phenomenal. The noodles were wide and flat and there were onions in the broth. I couldn't stop swiping bites. I had a chicken dish with bamboo shoots and bell peppers in garlic sauce. The dish was colorful and just what I wanted out of a Thai meal.   The thing we liked most about our food was that the sauces and broths were very light and not at all syrupy. The flavors of the chicken and vegetables weren't cloaked in overly sweet or pungent sauces, so everything tasted bright and fresh.   Lunch is a steal with three courses for under ten dollars. I looking forward to my next visit.

I've recently found myself popping into Lucky more and more whenever I'm in the area. The employees at the Walnut Street location are always very friendly and helpful, which makes shopping more enjoyable. Also, they run some amazing sales! It's pretty unlikely that I will swing in and not find something to purchase. While I haven't tried their jeans in a while, the sales have been enticing me to check them out. To be continued!

I really loved the power yoga class I took with Ang yesterday! My friend Erin, a long-time student at Sol, organized a private class for a group of ladies.   When I walked into the space, I realized instantly that it was heated - ruh roh! It had been a long time since I last took a heated yoga class and I was a little bit nervous. Then, we were told we would be experiencing a 60-minute power yoga. Power yoga?! Now I was really sweating and not just because of the heat! In hindsight, I'm glad these two elements were a surprise because I may have been too intimidated to sign-up had I known.   Happily, Ang's laid-back attitude and casual conversation at the beginning and throughout class really helped me relax and get into it. I really liked the background music as well. It was a mix of folky, new age-y meditation music and it was just perfect for setting the tone of a non-judgemental and fun practice.   An hour flew by and I was sweating like crazy but I enjoyed every second! Sometimes my mind wanders in yoga classes and I find myself thinking, "When will this be over?" That never happened during Ang's class. I think the hour length was just right. Though Conshohocken is a bit of a hike for me, I'd strongly recommend this studio to anyone nearby who is looking for a relaxed and fun setting for their yoga practice.

Duross & Langel has long been a fixture in my house, especially in terms of bath time essentials. I've loved on their bubble bath, bath bombs, bath soaks and bath salts for years.   Steve, Sarah, and the rest of the crew are always coming up with amazing new products. More recently, I've gifted friends with some of the aromatherapy rollers, and I also have a couple bottles of their pure essential oils, which are great for a thirty second meditation break. The balms and salves have been wonderful, too (bug off saved me and my husband on our trip to Bali earlier this year!). Believe it or not, there are still some products I've yet to try, but I'd undoubtedly love them all. I've been a totally satisfied customer through and through.   As we've been nearing the end of some of our national-brand hand soaps, I decided to hit up D&L's website for supplies. I always try to support local whenever possible, but the current pandemic has me finding new ways to swap big name brands in all areas of my home.   According to their social channels, Duross & Langel is shipping once a week. I placed my order on a Monday and it arrived by Wednesday! There were even a couple fun surprises thrown in, which was so thoughtful and very fun. Please think of the little guys when you're replacing items around your home, or even if you're just looking to treat yourself with something nice while we all social distance. I can't wait to shop the shelves in person again!

Every time we decide to order Chinese, we end up spending loads of time on research, because we simply haven't come across a go-to place. Usually, one of us will enjoy their food while the other thinks theirs is just all right. Spicy Memory may have changed the game on Saturday night.  We ordered a quart of wonton soup ($8.95), a scallion pancake ($4.50) and two chicken entrees (general tso's and garlic sauce, $14.95/each). I included prices here because I do think Spicy Memory is more expensive than its competitors. However, I felt the quality was better, as was the quantity. The soup was delicious and came with 10 dumplings. Both containers of chicken were loaded and provided us with plenty of food for a second meal.   Spicy Memory, you have my attention! This is definitely my spot the next time I'm craving Chinese.

I'm so happy to see Occasionette growing with a Collingswood location! I frequent the East Passyunk shop, but my sister lives about three blocks away from the new location, so I've already stopped in a handful of times over the past month or so. Every single time, I end up with a card, gift for a friend or family member, or little present for myself. I absolutely love this store and the interesting selection!   From tea towels to candles to kitchen gadgets to spices (my husband and I are fans of the popcorn enhancers, and my sister loved the spiced wine/cider kit I tossed into her birthday gift) to jewelry to adorable cards and more, I could just go cray cray at this place (and often do). Best of all, prices are very reasonable!   Please support this amazing local shop - you'll be a fan for life just like me!

Garage lived up to its name in that it was about as hot as a garage during our visit last Saturday. It was truly sweltering. Not sure if the AC just isn't up to snuff with the size of the place, but eventually, they gave up and opened the large garage door in front. That was when we decided to move on.   But aside from the heat, I did like the place. The can selection is pretty sizable, though they did run out of my beer of choice during my visit. There are a lot of fun arcade-style games. And the bathrooms are nice and clean. The acoustics are very loud. Put money in the juke and you won't hear your songs unless you listen very closely. A bunch of people had BYO food from nearby restaurants; not sure if that policy will continue after the built-in food truck is running, but I thought it was cool nonetheless. I think I'll probably prefer Garage in the cooler months, and it's definitely a good place for groups.

This Michaels is my go-to spot whenever I need something crafty for work or life. Most recently, I hit them up for wedding supplies. I was very impressed by the range in products. I always thought of Michael's strictly for craft supplies but found entire sections of wedding necessities, including a really nice variety of bulk thank you cards.   My mom always tells me you should never buy anything at Michael's without a coupon, and she's right. All you have to do is go to their website to see their weekly coupons, and you can present them at the counter right on your phone. I had a 50% off any item coupon that I used on a box of thank you cards. My husband was in line behind me with box number two, and as he tried to pull the coupon up on his phone, the employee helping me out said he could just use the coupon that was already on my phone - excellent!   I'd rather drive across state lines to visit this store than visit the AC Moore in South Philly. It is worth the trip!

This particular Lulu location was smaller than some that I've been to, but they had a nice selection of merchandise. The ladies who were working at the changing rooms were super nice and helpful.   I ended up with a cute pair of running shorts which made their debut yesterday. They were comfortable through my run and stayed put the entire time. There's nothing worse than clothing getting in the way of a workout. That's something I never have to worry about with Lululemon's apparel. My friend got some really adorable pants that I keep thinking I may need to buy for myself. If only they had sales!

I always heard good things about this place but I rarely venture to the Fairmount neighborhood. For shame! I was really missing out - until last night, when my BYO girls convened for the last time before two of our foursome move to other cities. Sniff. (Not to worry, they'll both be located within driving distance, or accessible via train. Just in case anyone was really stressing over it. Pass the Kleenex, please.)  With wine poured, we scoured Umai Umai's online menu and made our selections. Two of the girls set off to collect our meal. The seaweed salad, two calamari salads, spirited away roll, spartan roll, yellowtail roll and eel roll set us back $22/lady. Oh was it worth it.   The girls returned with a huge bag. I wondered what could possibly be taking up so much space, since it didn't really seem like we ordered all that much. Turns out, they wrapped each component of every dish separately. The calamari was in a different container than the actual salad, which had its dressing on the side. The sauce for the spirited away roll came in a little container. It was such a thoughtful takeaway. There were even enough chopsticks, wasabi and soy sauce for everyone.   The spirited away roll was filled with peppery tuna deliciousness, while the spartan roll, with beef and shrimp tempura was bananas. I'm already craving that calamari salad, and it surely won't be long before I'm calling Umai Umai and trekking across town for some of the best sushi in this city.

My mom and stepdad offered to treat me to a drink on Saturday night after helping with some little projects around my apartment.  Free help AND free drinks?  My parents are the bomb.  We were all curious about Treno, the new restaurant that recently took over Kitchen 233's spot on Haddon Ave.    I had only been to Kitchen 233 once, and while I loved the setting I was not crazy about the menu.  I think the P.J.W. Group made an excellent call with changing the concept to an upscale brick oven pizza and pasta restaurant.  It seems that most people these days are gravitating towards less expensive comfort food, and Treno delivers just that.    When we arrived, there were a few people waiting for tables and the dining area appeared full.  Fortunately, we scored the last high top in the back bar area (the chic one with the huge windows and slate everywhere).  I was pleased to see that not much had changed with regards to the décor.  Our server dropped off drink menus and filled our water glasses, leaving the water carafe on the table, which I loved.  I'm constantly looking for water refills when I'm out and having extra right on the table was great.  The drink menu was extremely reasonable, with wines by the glass at $5, $7 and $9 price points.  Cocktails were $8 and beers were reasonably priced as well, with a few surprise selections.  My stepdad opted for a glass of red while my mom and I ordered the Treno Locale, a spinoff from a traditional cosmo that tasted like a lighter gimlet.  Delish!    We split a roasted vegetable pizza, white style (although red was an option as well).  The pizza was great, with carmelized peppers and onions, spinach and fresh mozz.    Another round of drinks and we called it a night.  This spot will be added to the rotation of local establishments to visit when I'm not feeling a city night.

Finally made it to Jamonera and really enjoyed my experience. I was with a group of four and we went specifically for the Spanish fish fry for Wine Week. That was $25 per person and included fried cod, patatas bravas and a glass of Mallorcan white. More on that later.   We were seated shortly after our reservation time, which was good, because there isn't much room for standing in this tiny establishment (though the restaurant is still substantially more comfortable than Barbuzzo, in my opinion). We started with a pitcher of sangria and a trio of tapas - the veggie board, mushroom coca and a crisp and tasty salad with asparagus, pickled chorizo, croutons and a light vinaigrette. All three were great but we especially loved the mushroom coca, and ordered another round...  Which turned out to be completely unnecessary, once we saw the gargantuan plates containing the fried cod and patatas bravas. Wow. I don't know how we did it but we managed to put a hurting on this course, though there were still some leftover potatoes that we just couldn't finish. Total Wine Week win for us. If Jamonera ever features this dinner again, I'll be making my reservations immediately. The fish was perfect, the potatoes were crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, and the dry wine cut right through all the heaviness of the food. We enjoyed the wine so much we ordered another bottle to share, in lieu of dessert.   Our server (whose name I forget - she is blonde and very friendly!) was fantastic. She appeared at all the right times and had great suggestions. Really looking forward to my next meal there, which is already in the books for April!

We attended a wedding at HollyHedge Estate on Saturday and it was absolutely beautiful. The estate is laid back a bit from the street, and there are several different structures on the property.   The ceremony was held outside on a very nice patio. Immediately following was a cocktail hour on the same patio. I've never seen staff move so quickly to transform a space!   The reception took place in a space that had a warm and cozy feel, but that still managed to fit somewhere in the neighborhood of 180 - 200 people, with a smallish dance floor.   The food was definitely above average compared with most weddings, and the bartenders were great. I would definitely recommend HollyHedge as a great place to host a special event.

After taking too much time to decide what I wanted for dinner at the Night Market, the lines were beyond long and my hungry levels were on code red. I ditched my boyfriend in a line that wasn't moving and stalked down the street like a deranged lunatic. The wait at Earth, Bread & Brewery was about a half hour, so I moved on to Wine Thief, where I had picked up a glass of wine from their Night Market table earlier in the evening.   As luck would have it, a high top in the bar was available, so I sat down and proceeded to have a nice dinner for one, not knowing if my boyfriend would get to the end of his line in time to join me (for the record, he didn't). The bar was dimly lit with candles throughout. It was crowded, so the din of the crowd was palpable, but not bothersome. As I sipped my glass of sauvignon blanc, I felt pretty peaceful - except for the occasional clanging of the bartenders at the ice machine, which was obnoxiously loud.   For dinner, a big bowl of mussels in marinara sauce, with a few slices of toasted sourdough bread. It was heavenly. I felt positively blissful by the time I paid the check and rejoined the crowd. I'd love to check out Wine Thief for dinner on a night with less activity to see how the other menu items compare.

I can't believe my first review of Silk City took place almost three years ago. Time flies. Interestingly enough, I still find the three star rating to be consistent with my experiences there over the years. At this point, I've now had meals on a couple different occasions, sat in the beer garden several times, and even hit up the dance floor again.   The food is average at best. Some things are better than others, like the fresh cut fries with cheese sauce and scallions (unbelievably delicious) or the Thai chili glazed wings. Other items completely underwhelm: A buffalo chicken salad that I could have made at home with some iceberg, baked chicken strips and Frank's hot sauce; the fried chicken with smothered chorizo green beans. I'd recommend sticking to apps and sandwiches for best results.   The beer garden is cute and fun; screaming kids and their obnoxious parents who ignore them are not. I dig family friendly places when children behave, but there should be a no-running policy or something. Yes, I sound like Mr. Wilson. No, I do not care. Get off my lawn.   Silk City's dance floor remains one of the few places in the city where it's fun to dance. Even though I find the DJs to be hit or miss, and erring on the top 40 side, I still like having the option.   Everything said, I'll take the good with the bad for an occasional trip to Spring Garden's iconic diner.

On a Friday afternoon during lunch, Oyster House was bumpin'. I was drawn in by the fact that it was National New England Clam Chowder Day. In hindsight, I wish I ordered a bowl of the stuff as my lunch, but I ended up getting the Judi salad with a cup of chowder on the side. The soup was lighter than I expected and had a really nice, fresh taste. I loved the smattering of diced fresh chives on top.   Service was on point. It seemed every time I stuffed another oyster cracker into my mouth, someone was there to refill drinks or check on us. I did notice another nearby table that didn't seem to share in this, though. They waited a while to get their food, while our soup came and went and our entrees arrived soon after.   The Judi salad came already-dressed with a nice pile of mixed lettuces, some feta cheese and a generous helping of shrimp salad. I personally found the salad to be a touch too salty, and would probably rectify this next time by ordering the dressing on the side. It was a great salad nonetheless, and certainly filling enough to carry me through the day. I spotted a plate of fried oysters on my way out and resolved to try them next time.   The decor is all white tiles and wood, with oyster plates adorning the walls and other classic touches. The look is simple and spot on for what the place is. High top tables in front are somewhat tight and the stools were a bit uncomfortable, especially after tucking my coat underneath me. Also, the front door allowed gusts of cold air to wash over the room every time it was opened. A temporary winter vestibule would do wonders.  Late night happy hour on Saturday nights from 9-11 seems like a great deal, with dollar oysters, a featured beer and oyster shooters at a nice price.

I stopped in Society Hill Society with my partner in crime Aaliyah P on a sunny Sunday afternoon.   First off, love what you did with the place, SHS! There's still a great rustic vibe but the space has gotten a lot cozier. This bar is the ideal setting for a chilly fall or winter night.   We were only in for one quick drink and we both opted for The Mind-Killer, which involved a brûlée torch to finish it off. Fancy! Said cocktail was fun and tasty and pretty to boot!  Looking forward to my next visit and trying some of the food menu!

I'm amazed at the positive reviews for this dentist because my experience was anything but positive. I reluctantly started searching for a new dental practice when my go-to for the past several years reached out to say they were no longer accepting my insurance. Due to the great reviews and proximity to where I live, I made an appointment quickly and easily with this office. I received texts leading up to the appointment which prompted me to confirm.   I arrived a few minutes before my 1pm appointment. The waiting room is very small and you can basically hear all of the procedures as they are taking place a few steps away. I filled out some forms on a computer and waited about twenty minutes or so before being called back. I was seated in the first patient area closest to the waiting room. The only thing separating me from the patient right next to me was a small half wall - there was no privacy and I could see my neighbor's procedure as it was happening. I know dentist offices are always kind of open (which I think is incredibly strange) but this was really open and made me pretty uncomfortable.   A dental hygienist came over to give me a dental bib and some protective glasses and I thought we were about to begin, but then she walked away and I just sat there, waiting. The sounds of Christmas carols and dental work filled my ears while a TV played some sort of dental demonstration, adding to my unease. As an entire hour of waiting came to a close, I removed my bib, grabbed my belongings and made my way to the door. The receptionist was apologetic but, truthfully, I was happy to leave. The search for a new dentist continues.

My sister and I were walking around Haddonfield after Christmas and we came across William Heritage. Things have really changed since I lived in nearby Collingswood ten years ago! Both towns used to be dry and now there are breweries and even wine tasting rooms. I would have loved this when I lived in the area!   We walked inside to check it out and I asked about tastings and was told that they were fully booked that day. I was mostly just curious; my sister is pregnant and I wasn't planning on tasting alone. I didn't receive the warmest welcome from their employee and when I asked about a particular wine I was told it was good. The entire exchange was honestly a bit awkward until I made it clear that I wasn't planning on sticking around for long. I asked if I could taste before purchasing a bottle and the other employee who was helping a customer turned around and said absolutely. I asked about two different reds. One was a blend of CA and NJ grapes. I haven't had much luck with NJ wines in the past and since I didn't want to take up too much time, I sipped just that wine, thought it was solid and purchased a bottle.   The tasting room itself was really cute; up there with some of the prettier ones in Healdsburg and Napa. Will I be returning? TBD.

Last night I had dinner at a.kitchen with my husband and in-laws. I think it's safe to say that we were all super happy to be reunited with Chef Eli Collins' cooking. Eli's food is always seasonal, innovative and delicious (he was formerly the head chef at Pub & Kitchen, one of our go-tos).  The squash and fig dish was out of this world! From the crunch of the pumpkin seeds and rye crisps to the sweetness of the figs, this plate was bursting with fall flavor. I absolutely loved it! The octopus and sausage/shishito peppers starters were great as well, but the squash stole the show.   For dinner, I had the steak with mushrooms and bernaise butter. The steak was perfectly cooked and very flavorful. Our server was incredibly professional and kind, knew the menu inside and out, and had a great wine suggestion every time we asked.   Dessert was nice but probably not a must. I wasn't crazy about the pecan cake but I did enjoy the chocolate tart, which is ideal for dark chocolate lovers as it's not overly sweet but still very flavorful, with raspberry sauce complementing the chocolate (my favorite combo!).   The only negative we experienced was when my mother-in-law requested a black russian with a side of ice. The drink the bartender sent over was not a black russian, but some type of coffee martini. She wasn't crazy about it, and it was removed from our check (very nice and much appreciated!) but I just wish the bartender would have sent our server back to say that they couldn't make the drink/didn't have the correct ingredients/etc. We had this exact same issue years ago when we last dined at a.kitchen together - we even mentioned it to our server when we placed our drink order! It was a small snafu, but kind of strange that a restaurant with a full bar next door wouldn't have Kahlua.   a.kitchen is one of those spots I don't get to very often, but after last night's fantastic dinner, I'll be keeping it in mind for future nights out!

Everyone in my family refers to this place as "The Bread Basket," which I believe was the original name.  I'm not sure when they changed their moniker to the oh-so-creative "Bread and Bagels."   Despite the identity crisis, the little shop has been churning out the same delicious breads for years.  They have several varieties, but the pepperoni bread remains the favorite at our family gatherings.  It is especially delish when heated in the oven for a little crunch, and served with marinara.  Yum.  In addition to the stuffed breads, they also have, you guessed it, bagels!  Never had one but they look and smell delicious, as do all of their other baked goods, which include: pastries, muffins, gargantuan cupcakes, etc.  Prices are low ($6 for a loaf of pepperoni bread) and they always seem to be open whenever I need to pick something up last-minute before a party.

Upgrade! It was after 9pm and I was in the area and craving some Vietnamese takeout. Vietnam Palace still had some people dining inside, though they looked to be at the end of their night. Thankfully, the gentleman who was managing the restaurant (he may have been the owner), said that I could still place an order.   I was craving comfort food and really wanted to try a Vietnamese soup. The manager/owner recommended the beef soup which sounded good to me. Since I only had a credit card and the limit was $15, I also ordered the lemongrass shrimp entree for the following day.   I took a somewhat spastic Uber ride home but my eats were packaged up well with no spillage. The soup was indeed comforting and delicious, and enough for two light meals. The lemongrass shrimp entree was also great and enough for two small meals.   After re-reading my former review, I see that I enjoyed some lychee martinis here back in the day. I'm going to have to dine in next time. Lychee me!

I popped into Ten Six Club for their media night, so the place was packed to the gills with PYTs trying to get their free drink on. Around 10pm, the club officially opened to the public and the crowd became considerably less dense. So it's hard to give my full opinion since I haven't been there yet on a totally normal night, but I will certainly update once that happens.   That said, the last time I went to Walnut Room it desperately needed an update, and that's going back at least a few years. Ten Six Club has that wood varnish smell of newness. The main room features a bar, a tight dance floor, some high top tables and the bathrooms, which are waaaaaaay in the back, past the dance floor and DJ. If you've gotta go, best to account for the walk past/through/around the dancing bodies. Said bathrooms are dim and not at all updated, from what I could see.   The DJ was great, and there is another small room with a bar to the left where you walk in, which is helpful. I'm definitely planning to return for a night of dancing with friends at some point in the near future.

I returned to Sawatdee for dinner on Monday night. It was night two of my Thai cravings and I had to satisfy the beast. The hype of Sawatdee's opening has definitely waned and we were able to score a table with no problem. Service was notably better than my previous two experiences at lunch and dinner. Water glasses were kept filled and everything was cooked just the way we asked.   For a starter, we shared the grilled chicken skewers with peanut sauce and cucumber relish. A nice little bite before the meal and not too heavy, either. I ordered chicken pad Thai sans tofu for my main, and I opted for a two star level of spiciness out of three. At first, the dish didn't seem spicy, but it was a deceptively slow burn. By the time I was three quarters of the way through, I was chugging water and had to tap out. Next time, I'll go with one star of heat. Truth be told, I'm kind of a heat pansy. But my meal was damn good nonetheless. I don't know what they do at Sawatdee that is different from other Thai places, but the noodles are just so much better. They easily swirl around a fork and are never stuck together. And the flavors of all the ingredients really pop. That was especially true for my dining partner's dish, the pad kee mao gai. Wow, was that good.   I'm not positive that my cravings for Thai have truly been satisfied at this point. It probably won't be long before I'm back for another fix.

Per usual, it was the eleventh hour before leaving for vacation and I still needed a pair of heels, a manicure and an eyebrow wax. I found the desired heels in record time and dashed to Nail Trix, the only nail salon in the entire mall, with about 45 minutes to closing time.   There were two employees and one was just finishing with another customer so she was ready for me when I selected my color. When I asked to have my nails trimmed, she clipped them so fast I was a little afraid she would accidentally get my nail bed, too. She flew through the manicure in record time, and I tried to remind myself that you get what you pay for and it was my own fault for waiting until the last minute. Not even 48 hours later, most of my nails are starting to chip. Glad I picked a light color.  The eyebrow wax, also quite fast, got the job done although I had to do a little extra plucking at home. I'd say two stars is actually pretty generous, all things considered. Next time, I will definitely plan ahead and go to a nicer salon.

I've passed The Sample Rack countless times while driving down Pine Street. There are always gorgeous dresses in the window and they rotate constantly. I called to book an appointment and spoke with Carlene, who explained the unique nature of the shop (samples only; designer dresses offered at a discount, etc.).   The shop is open by appointment only and you receive the undivided attention of the staff. Carlene and her colleague (whose name I forget - she was so sweet!) pulled a really lovely array of dresses according to my preferences. I tried on an incredible gown that was discounted by several thousand dollars. It wasn't quite what I was looking for but I'm sure the woman who purchases said gown will be absolutely thrilled with the find.    Leading up to my appointment, I booked an appointment at another store just to get an idea of the styles that I would like. I wasn't expecting to find something that I loved at the first store, but that's exactly what happened. I kept an open mind for my appointment at The Sample Rack, and even found a couple strong contenders for runner-up, but ultimately decided on the dress at the first store. I called Carlene after I made up my mind to let her know and she was so sweet and genuinely happy that I had found my dress. I wouldn't hesitate to send a friend to The Sample Rack and will continue to sing their praises!

Update! I got to sink my fangs into the matcha chocolate cake, thanks to my manager, who sent two pieces to my house in celebration of my ten year work anniversary. The cake is super rich; half a slice was more than enough to calm my sweet tooth this afternoon. I look forward to enjoying the other half, and can't wait to try more from this adorable café!

I love Thai Square so much and am so happy they are open again for delivery and takeout. This is one of our favorite neighborhood businesses, but we also think it's some of the best Thai the city has to offer.   I almost always start my meal with the tom yum soup, which is vibrant, flavorful, and just the right punch of spicy (when you order mild or medium). Other starters we like are the golden spring rolls and chicken skewers with peanut sauce.   As for entrees, I've liked everything I've tried but the crabmeat pad thai has become a favorite, along with the pad kra pow with shrimp.   The restaurant is small but really cute and we've enjoyed dinner there with a bottle of wine on a few occasions. That said, our go-to is delivery and it's always fast and accurate.

Rex 1516 has only been open for a week or so but they are bringing their A-game already! It is so nice having another option south of South/west of Broad. We walked in without reservations on Thursday and were lucky enough to score a table. The ambiance is Prohibition-esque, with custom boxed speakers projecting swinging sounds, a gorgeous bar, studded tables and other accents adding to the atmosphere.   The wine, beer and cocktail list is nicely developed and priced well. I tried two different whites which were interesting and different from the typical offerings. To start, the mussels in a bacon-y beer broth with white beans were large, tender and full of flavor. The three toast points that came with soaked up the juices and the dish was a fantastic start to the meal. Since I was keeping it light, I opted for the chopped salad with cheddar, ham, croutons and red onion for my main. I didn't take offense to the balsamic dressing even though our server assured me that they are moving to a white balsamic so that the greens didn't look wilted. It didn't matter to me - the veggies were snappy and fresh.   My boyfriend's crawfish pot pie starter and his entree, roasted chicken with mashed potatoes and root vegetables, received rave reviews. I sampled the potatoes and they passed my test. We cannot wait to return and we wish them tons of luck!

Perhaps Dolce Carini's pizza is decent (according to my fellow Yelpers), but their wraps are not. I ordered delivery via Eat24 yesterday, and I can honestly say it was my first bad experience with that service and one of their participating restaurants. First off, someone called me to ask my address (which you confirm at the time of ordering) because the delivery guy was lost. I live on a corner in a pretty easy-to-navigate neighborhood so I don't know what the problem was. I had to wait by the door for over ten minutes as I took calls from this guy while attempting to navigate him closer to my place.   So the food arrives, and my turkey club wrap is just falling apart. It looked like the wrap was placed down, the ingredients were put inside, and the sides of the wrap folded over. The under-side was wet. I literally had to get a plate and deconstruct and then reconstruct the wrap. Doing so enabled me to remove most of the turkey, which was low-quality deli slices. Sorry to say, but that was my first and last experience with Dolce Carini.

I love Occasionette! I make it a point to make this adorable store one of my first stops every year before Christmas. It's where I find all of my husband's stocking stuffers, plus a few unique and local gifts for friends.   I was thrilled to see Sugarfina's rosé gummy bears in stock - those things were sold out with waitlists for months when they came out over the summer! My husband was stoked that I had tracked them down (#brosé #summerofbrosé).   While at the store I also bought myself the most amazing, wood wick candle called Christmas Past. At $18 this was definitely a splurge but the scent is incredible and I love the crackle sound the wick makes (#basic).   This is by far one of the best local shops for gifts in Philly.

I'm trying to think of something nice to say... At least there's a parking lot?   The woman who called and left a message about my package repeated the info three times, which I liked. Okay, so we'll go with two stars for said woman and the parking lot. The customer service I received during my brief visit was non-existent. I asked two or three questions and each was met with the same "I dunno" from the dimwitted, robotic employee.   Lesson learned: dealing with the Philly UPS employees in person is just as frustrating as when you have to call and wade your way through the automated prompts.

Three dollars for an ice pop seems a little steep. But I guess when you compare that to, say, the desserts at Franklin Fountain or Capogiro, it's a bargain. Though I do enjoy those other two quite a bit more. Perhaps I'm comparing apples to oranges?   Nonetheless, this shop is adorable, with their popsicle puzzle toys for kids, bright colors and mini trays for serving the pops. There is an extensive list of pops containing dairy or not, and all of the flavors are interesting combinations. I went with a pineapple basil which was very nice for a hot summer night.

I had a very solid experience with Springboard Media yesterday. I heard they were offering an iPhone trade-in deal for the 4 and 4s so I took my flailing 4 and traded it in for a 5. The cost of the 5 is $199 but I received a $50 discount by trading-in. And when I checked-in on Yelp, I received a check-in offer for $20 off any iPhone case with the purchase of a phone. Cha-ching! Since I was in the market for one of those anyway, this was an unexpected bonus.   The process of backing up my phone took some time but store manager Jamie took care of it for me - all of my apps and info were saved and promptly loaded onto my new phone. I am clueless with technology and have lost data in the past when upgrading, so I was very grateful for this and didn't mind the extra time. In the meantime, I perused the iPhone cases and settled on one for twenty-five bucks, which seems to be the low end of the going rate. Jamie gave me her card and told me to let her know if I had any problems. She was great to work with and I would definitely recommend this store to anyone looking to upgrade their phone.

Tasty food. Dainty food. Expensive food.   My feelings about A.kitchen are mostly positive, but damn are they expensive when you consider the portions. Even for the Square. Now I know how all the celebrities can eat there and get away with keeping their figures.   Fortunately, the food is pretty good. My table of ladies ordered the arugula salad, octopus with watermelon, blue crab salad and beets to share. The salad was okay, but the octopus and crab dishes were both excellent. I didn't try the beets but my friends seemed to like them.  We each chose our own main and I ordered the fettucine with bottarga. It was very rich, and this is where the smaller serving size actually worked to my advantage. The bottarga flavor was subtle which I preferred when compared with a similar dish I had at another restaurant. A couple of my noodles were slightly more firm than al dente, but overall I was very happy with my choice.   My friends ordered a puff pastry filled with white chocolate and rhubarb and a pineapple upside down cake for dessert. I had a teeny bite of each and neither really wowed me, but I'm not super big on sweets. Both were cleared out so my friends definitely liked them.   Would I go back to A.kitchen? Yes, but most likely if the check is being picked up by someone else. I liked the food and the service but there are other restaurants with similar dishes at more reasonable prices.

Picking up tickets to yesterday's afternoon showing of The King's Speech left me, well, speechless. A pair of tickets were more expensive at this mall theater than at the Ritz in Old City!   Also more expensive were the concessions. A small soda (oddly enough, the same size as a small kiddie pool) cost $4.50. I realize there is a huge mark-up on food and drink at the movies, but I could get four or five 2 liters for that price!   The saving grace was the theater itself. The room was clean, floors didn't seem sticky and the quality of the film seemed flawless to my eye. This spot is miles above Loews in Cherry Hill, but not quite Voorhees status.

My husband and I have been talking about grabbing roast beef sandwiches at Cherry Street Tavern for the longest time, and we finally made it over on Sunday night with a friend. We started with a plate of nachos which didn't stand a chance. The 'chos were super basic - hearty round chips out of the bag with some cheese sauce, chili, sour cream and pickled jalapeños. They were simple yet hit the spot, which led to a lengthy conversation about the bastardization of nachos in recent times. Really enlightening stuff.   Next up were our roast beef sandwiches, which you can top with American, Swiss or Provolone. For .50 more, top your 'wich with sharp provolone and a side of hot peppers. Washed down with a couple beers, this meal hit the spot. The bartender was a friendly gent who both wrangled drinks and put together meals for everyone in the place. My next craving for a hot roast beef sandwich will have me heading straight to Cherry Street.

For some crazy, still unbeknownst to me reason, I thought hitting the very first Curiosity Doughnuts pop-up at ITV would be a good idea. The pop-up started at 8am, on one of the very first really cold days of the year. My husband and I arrived around 8:15 to a line that snaked down the block. We took our place in line and hoped we wore warm enough clothing (spoiler alert: we didn't).   We waited in line for well over an hour. I am not that girl who waits in line for specialty food products; I still don't know what possessed me to that day... Though I suspect my alcohol-free November had something to do with it. My sweet tooth rages when I'm on dry island and doughnuts are a weakness. Okay, now we know.   As we got close to the door, it was pretty evident through the window that pickings were getting very slim. Once inside, we didn't have much of a choice; we ended up with a box of six doughnuts, most of them flavors that I wouldn't have picked had I had more options. That said, I was thrilled to have any doughnuts at all; they were completely sold out after one or two more customers went in after us. I would have been crushed if I had been in that line still!   At home, the doughnuts were incredible. The insides remind me of a Market Day Canelé (this is a very good thing - Philadelphians, get after it if you haven't had one before!). The exterior had a perfect crunch. Some of the fruity glazes weren't my thing, but the doughnut itself was a work of art.   Now that Curiosity Doughnuts is more of a fixed thing and not a pop-up, I've heard the wait times have improved. Great news for me, as my days of waiting in long lines for food are now officially over. Can't wait to try more flavors!

A boozy brunch is the perfect way to kick off a Saturday, if you ask me. And The Scottish Arms does it right, with a make-your-own Bloody Mary bar complete with several types of mixers, hot sauces and other add-ins.   Their brunch menu is filled with hearty options, and my Seamus MacBenedict (available with ham instead of salmon, if you choose) was delicious. My only little gripe, and this seems to happen often when it comes to eggs benedict, was that the egg white was not fully cooked. No worries, because I had a lovely little cast iron pot of home fries which were on point.  The French press coffee was smooth and our service was lovely. This is the kind of pub where I could easily pass a day (or night) hanging out.

These five stars go out to DiBartolo Bakery's chocolate-frosted, cream-filled donuts, with a special shout-out to the intoxicating aroma that wafts out of the corner building and into the neighborhood.
