I can't speak for any of the cakes, cookies or other pastries in the store, though they are all beautiful.  When I walk into Dibartolo, there's only one thing I'm after.

Vietnam Cafe was a last minute dinner destination after spending Sunday afternoon in West Philly. My husband and I arrived feeling pretty hungry so we started off with two apps: veggie fried spring rolls and shrimp papaya salad. We also ordered the coconut drink and the Vietnamese limeade. Both were delicious but the coconut drink was extra refreshing and complementary with the food.   The starters were really great. The spring rolls were hot and perfectly crunchy while the papaya salad was light but full of flavor. These went together really well.   For mains, I tried the Mongolian beef while my husband had the lemongrass chicken. The flavors in each dish were really complex and intense. My only suggestion for the beef dish would be for the chefs to cut the meat into smaller, bite-sized pieces. Also, the servings were large enough to bring home leftovers for dinner the next night.   I can easily see this review getting upgraded to five stars if future visits continue to impress. I'll definitely try to get back sooner than later!

I checked out The Bling Pig with some yelpers after the CMYE shopping crawl in Northern Liberties. The restaurant was cozy and cute, definitely different from other bars in the city. The list of beers on tap was limited but there was still enough of a variety for everyone and all from solid breweries. There is also a very large list of beer available by the can.  We ordered poutine, chorizo quesadillas and the Thanksgiving balls, since everyone seems to rave about them. The quesadilla was okay, not great but not bad. The balls were kind of bland. They seemed like more of a gimmick than a great appetizer. It was a whole lot of breading that didn't feel worth the calories. And mostly everyone in our group felt the same. The poutine, however, was great. The fries were crunchy, the gravy tasted spot on and so did the cheese curds. We woofed down the plate and put in an order for the "dirty fries" which had shortrib gravy. They were good too but the poutine is where it's at.   I didn't really check out too much else on the menu but I would definitely like to go back and do so. I could see myself back there again with a group for a chill night out.

We've been ordering takeout every weekend during the pandemic, but last weekend set the bar much higher. We'd been keeping an eye on Pumpkin's social media, just waiting for a menu that really jumped out for us. Friday was the day! We called around 1:30 to place our order for a 6:30pm pick-up. I was relieved that everything we had our eye on was still available. There was a small swap with one of the ingredients in an entree that I actually preferred over the original dish.   My husband biked over to pick up our food and he reported that there were several people waiting for takeout when he arrived. Pumpkin has clearly been making a great effort to bring restaurant-quality meals to people in their homes for a reasonable price. Three courses for $35 was very reasonable for the experience we had on Friday!   Unpacking the bag, I noticed that everything was packaged very nicely. I replated everything to elevate the experience. Our first course of shrimp escabeche and a crab cake was excellent; we didn't know if the main course could keep up but were happy to find that it did! My husband loved the halibut while I really enjoyed the flank steak (with potato salad instead of the original polenta). The desserts, panna cotta and rhubarb cake, were a perfect ending to what felt like a really special meal. We appreciate all the hard work from Pumpkin and will definitely order from them again! They'll also be at the top of our list for when it's safe to dine out again.

Yeah... no. The first thing I noticed upon arrival to Tootsie's Orchid Lounge, airport version, was the distinct and slightly unpleasant smell. The second thing I noticed upon sitting at the bar was the disgustingly dirty floor. Why did we stay? I guess the live music had something to do with it. That was the only redeeming quality about this place.   It's a shame that a place as iconic as Tootsie's would put their name on this extremely sub-par restaurant, even if it is in an airport. The rest of the airport seemed very clean and well-kept, so I'm not sure why the ball was so majorly dropped here.   Service was extremely slow and you really had to speak up to get someone's attention. The food was pretty awful. I also witnessed a bartender pouring a drink with one of those liquor measuring devices, but he would pull the bottle away before the pour was complete which amounted to spilled liquor around the drink. I would veer towards fast food or eating before the airport when given the choice again.

Very solid first experience with BLO/OUT! My hair was just two days from my regular cut and color, but I had an event to attend plus my anniversary dinner, so decided to treat myself to a blowout to ensure a good hair day. I booked my blowout, and added on a ten minute scalp massage, online.   As luck would have it, I was paired up with Alessandra, who was amazing. I don't feel like I gave very good direction on what I wanted and yet she read my mind anyway and worked out a look that was bouncy and fun. The scalp massage was relaxing and just what I needed.   I have been spoiled by my regular salon with super comfortable hair washing stations, and I found the stations at BLO/OUT to be a bit hard on the neck. I also thought the salon could use a little bit of an update, but I read in another review that this might be currently happening, so I'm interested to see how it goes. I'd be happy to see Alessandra again and will book with her for my next visit!

I checked out Acme Feed & Seed last year on a hardhat tour when construction was still underway. I couldn't wait to return on my next visit to see the finished product, and that's exactly what I did with a couple other ladies on the last day of my bachelorette trip.   On a Sunday afternoon, Acme was surprisingly not very busy. There seemed to be plenty of tables available for brunch with live music. The band was more jazz and blues than country, which was a nice change from everything else on Broadway.   The second floor has more of a lounge vibe, while the third floor is for private events. We ended up spending most of our time on the roofdeck, which had amazing views of the city plus a stellar DJ. Shoot for a shaded seat if you can because it gets super hot in the sun. A couple misting machines were placed around the deck and the occasional misty breeze was a welcome respite from the sun's rays. Moscow mules were my drink of choice and they were excellently made. I look forward to returning for more good vibes on my next visit.

Solid experience at the Deptford Five Guys last weekend! My husband and I were on our way to a wedding in deep South Jersey, and we needed something quick and easy for lunch. I hadn't been to Five Guys in ages so we decided to grab some burgers.   We walked in right before a crush of local athletes so our timing was great. I didn't really get a chance to take in the menu before the cashier asked us what we wanted to order. I felt a little rushed so just went with a bacon cheeseburger and order of fries to share. It was only after we placed our order that we carefully read the sign and realized that our burgers wouldn't come with any toppings. My husband ran over to the counter to see if we could add lettuce and tomato. The staff took care of that for us which was greatly appreciated!   Everything is cooked to order so we waited around five minutes or so before our number was called. Again, in a rush to order, I didn't realize that my burger came with two patties. The burger was massive but delicious and I housed it! The fries came overflowing into the brown paper bag and there were so many we actually didn't even finish them.   The space for eating isn't really comfortable (uncomfortable chairs that screech loudly when moved across the floor) so I think there could be some improvements there. Otherwise, this was a positive experience and I'd return if I was in the area and craving something on the opposite end of healthy.

I worked with DJs Available for DJ services and special effect lighting for a large scale event. Leading up to the big day, Tina was my contact and she was wonderful to work with. Super helpful and very quick to reply to email.   A day or two prior to the event, I received a call from Paul the DJ to confirm details. He was friendly and seemed genuinely excited for the event, and was just as lovely in person and a ball of energy at the party. I didn't give too much guidance for the playlist simply because I ran out of time while I was busy planning. I simply suggested that he play all fast songs, which he did, with lots of variety in genres.   My only minor disappointment was the special effect lighting. I paid to have a logo light (called a Gobo) specifically created for the event, in addition to some mood lighting. All together, lighting cost as much as the DJ services. Since my venue was a bit on the brighter side, much of the lighting effect was lost, though I do think it would have really popped in a darker venue. My only suggestion would be to bring this up during the consultation process if the customer seems to be on the fence. Otherwise, great company to work with and I'd hire them again.

For anyone looking for a unique gift, or just a treat for yourself during some trying times, Occasionette has got you! Though their stores are currently closed for in-person shopping, they have an online shop and orders over $45 ship free.   Of course, it would be impossible to list every single item sold in these fabulous stores online, so if you know of something they sell but don't see it on their website, you can reach out via DM on Instagram or through email. This is exactly what I did earlier this week when I realized I was running low on my favorite non-alcoholic spirit, Seedlip.* I knew Occasionette stocked all three flavors so I reached out to Sara, Occasionette's owner, with my request. Sara sent me a link for payment and she's going to ship the bottle right to my house!   In addition, Sara and the team are thinking of crafty ways to bring the shopping experience to their customers. Today, they're hosting a virtual shopping party via Instagram Live so people can see the merch in its entirety and place orders. Genius!    *For a delicious cocktail sans booze, pour two ounces of Seedlip Spice over ice and top with Fever Tree ginger beer and a lime wedge. Serve in a copper mug with a sprig of rosemary. Spicy and satisfying!

I'm with Lia B - Thai Square is definitely the best and most affordable Thai in the Graduate Hospital area. Not only is it a cute, BYO restaurant right in the neighborhood, but they also have delivery for those nights when you just don't feel like leaving the house.   I've tried a lot of the menu at this point, and favorites are the vegetable spring rolls, curry chicken dumplings, chicken skewers, coconut shrimp, curry entrees, shrimp pad Thai and tom yum soup. Actually, I don't think I've had anything I didn't like from Thai Square. Also, their spice levels mean business. I generally order medium which can occasionally be almost a little too hot for me (in a good way - please don't change this, Thai Square!).   The folks who own the place are very friendly, and I'm happy to have such a solid spot so close to home.

My main squeeze surprised me with a bouquet of flowers last Wednesday, and that same bouquet is still rockin' out with its blossoms out a full week later. The flowers were wrapped nicely in paper with a straw bow, which matched the theme of the fall blooms inside.   While not a huge fan of lilies myself (I find their fragrance to be a little overpowering), anyone who does enjoy them will absolutely love the selection from Flowers & Company. They are gargantuan! Truly, I've never seen a flower so big, and especially not in a home arrangement. Give this place a shot the next time you are looking to brighten someone's day!

So glad I came across The Quick Fixx during my Yelp search for delivery on Friday night, when I was looking for something hot, healthy, and reasonably-priced. It's worth noting that The Quick Fixx has no delivery fee and only a ten dollar minimum. That's a better deal than all my other regular delivery spots.   The create-your-own option is legit. I went with whole wheat penne, broccoli, fresh mozzarella and tomato garlic sauce. And guess what? There's now a side salad option! So I got myself a side salad with lemon vinaigrette because I'm a baller like that. The total was $14 plus tip.   Imagine my surprise when my doorbell rang and I was greeted by the owner himself, Matt. This is a guy who really cares about his business, his customers and the neighborhood.   Dinner was bangin' and exactly what I wanted. I even had leftovers for lunch the next day. After perusing the website and finding out about their "Ten Spot" lunch menu, I'll be hitting those up in the near future as well.

The drinks are good (although I once asked for a bellini at the indoor bar and received champagne mixed with peach schnapps-- I don't think so!), the food is consistent and tasty, but the rooftop deck has several issues that this cupcake does not love.   First, the glassware. Or shall I say, plasticware. When I order a ten dollar martini, I do not want to drink it out of room temperature plastic in a martini glass shape. I'm sure the reason behind this decision is so knucklehead drunks don't go throwing things over the ledge... but at the very least, they could serve real glasses to the patrons seated at the bar or at tables having dinner, or save the plastic for after 10 p.m.   Second, although there were no pools in sight, the entire deck area curiously smelled like one. Musty, chlorine-filled air combining with the scent of prepared foods was not at all appetizing. A rooftop bar in the middle of Philadelphia should not smell like low tide under the boardwalk. Please, Mr. Starr, give this place a good scrub down and replace the flooring with something that doesn't absorb spills.   I'm sure this wasn't my last visit to the deck at Continental Midtown... but with more bars and restaurants opening outdoor patios and setting up street-side tables, this place won't be topping my list for drinks al fresco.

Very cute coffee and specialty candy and gift shop in Lambertville. My husband and I stopped in for a cup of something warm on a cold night. I noticed the delicious-sounding hot chocolate sign which mentioned several spices. It sounded wonderful but I opted for a mocha latte since I was looking for some caffeine.   Our drinks were prepared and we sat at the stools by the window. My drink was absolutely delicious, but it definitely was not a mocha latte. I'm fairly certain I actually got a cup of the hot chocolate afterall, based on the description I read and the flavors I tasted. It was great, just not what I ordered. Regardless, cute spot and I would return!

Five.   Five dollar.   Five dollar footloooonnnngs!!!!   Not only is Subway convenient and diet-friendly, it's also cheap! I go through stages where I'll get a foot-long and eat half for lunch and half for dinner all week. Please tell me where else you can get two meals for $5.35 (including tax)?!   This location is great because it is conveniently located near both my office and apartment. The restaurant is always clean and the employees are friendly. In other words, they never make me feel awkward about loading my turkey and cheese with lettuce, tomatoes, onions, black olives, green peppers, sweet peppers, banana peppers, pickles and red wine vinaigrette.  I probably owe them money by the time I leave...

After a day at Longwood Gardens with my mom and grandmom, we decided to hit Victory for a late lunch. Our server was super sweet and helpful. My grandmom wanted a lighter brew while my mom was feeling something hoppier; our server made some recs and both were very pleased with their selections. In fact, my grandmom said she loved her beer, which made me really happy since she's more of a domestic light kinda gal. I was cruising with water but I can't wait to get back sometime to try some of the fresh suds.   The menu was really well rounded with something for everyone, and the prices were quite honestly a steal. At our server's recommendation, I went with the salmon entree, which was a mere $14. The salmon was served over sauteed spinach and sun-dried tomatoes in a buttery, lemony, garlicky broth. It was so delicious and felt like a splurge even though it was one of the lighter menu options. My mom loved her blt wrap with fries (I can confirm the fries were awesome!). My grandmom had some of the boneless wings which were also very good. Those came with a healthy side of fresh carrots and celery and some of the best blue cheese dressing I've ever tasted.   I've only been to Kennett Square once or twice but I'm now dying to get back for a longer visit, and Victory will definitely be on the list!

They definitely have the "quick" part down. Our order was delivered in about twenty minutes on a Saturday night. But as for the "fixx," I'm sort of in need of another, and I finished dinner only a half hour ago. What I mean is, the portion sizes are small. That's not to say that they aren't perfectly fine. In fact, if you're on a diet or you just like single-serving portions, this is actually a great option so you won't go crazy and eat five times the amount of pasta you should eat.   My boyfriend had the cheese ravioli with spicy red sauce, while I had a makeshift Caesar with romaine, tomatoes, grilled chicken and Caesar dressing on the side. I requested croutons, but only received two slices of grilled baguette. Not sure if that was supposed to be the actual croutons or what, but either way, I'd prefer regular croutons. Know what I mean?   Our food was tasty for sure, but for $18, we were left looking at each other and asking "what's next?" I'll definitely give them another shot but if I've got a full appetite I'll probably need salad AND pasta.

Welcome to the neighborhood, Green Aisle! I must say, I was super excited when I heard news that Green Aisle would be occupying the former Betty's Speakeasy (and short-lived ¡Juice!) space. What I didn't factor in was the additional hit to my checking account. It's true, items at this grocery are at a premium, but that's because they're of the highest quality. Specialty items are just that - special. Ya dig?   Owners Adam and Andrew are some of my favorite Philadelphians. They embody all that is great about small, local businesses - friendly service, an interest in the neighborhood and its residents, and a true passion for their products.   From homemade butterscotch sauce from Brooklyn (the best ice cream topper I have ever had outside of an old fashioned ice cream shop), to house-made pickles and preserves, to the fabulous array of cocktail accoutrements, Green Aisle has every last thing on your pantry wish list. They also have hand-dipped ice cream!

What a cute, deceivingly large, market! I ran into Sassafras for a hot second before Thursday night's Elite Event to grab some ice and was shocked at the spread in what I thought would be a tiny corner store. The place was clean, well-stocked and had a friendly staff. I wish I had a cute market like this in my neck of the woods.   Ten dollar credit card limit but you probably aren't spending less than that in a market anyway.  Also, since this is neither 100% gourmet market or grocery store, I'm going to tow the line and list it in both.

I love restaurants like Bar Bombón and others that have opened the door for lifetime meat eaters like myself to tiptoe into the world of vegetarian and vegan food. My husband and I have switched to a pescetarian diet during the week, so we're always looking for new and delicious meals that will keep us full and satisfied.   We ordered delivery for lunch this week through Caviar, and I was really excited to see that that Bar Bombón is currently offering some grocery items in addition to their regular menu. I scored some fragrant cilantro and mint, lemons and a pound of roma tomatoes. Yes!   In terms of the prepared food, my husband chose the blackened "chicken" fajita tacos while I went for the latin chop. We got the peruvian yucca fries to share. I'm a little wary of substitute meats (fully aware of the irony here) and I'm trying to get more adventurous. I tried a bite of the taco and was pleased to find: it tasted just like chicken! I'd try these myself in the future. My salad was fresh and tasty, but I was glad to have the yucca fries because the salad alone wouldn't hold me over. The yucca was delish, topped with a substitute cheese, sliced green olives and fried capers. I was sad I had to share.   The reason for four stars and not five is because the portions are pretty tiny and the prices are not. Two tacos were $13, and the yucca was $8.50 but we each only had about four pieces. Our weekday lunch was pricier than I'd like but I'm happy I got to try some new things!

From our first visits to Frida Cantina for watching Eagles games with friends at the bar, to our recent deliveries during Covid, we remain big fans!   Delivery is always a solid experience and everything is packaged well. I've been digging the al pastor tacos and we almost always get an order of guac and chips, which is pretty substantial. The restaurant always throws in some homemade salsas - the green salsa is absolutely delicious!

I'm shocked at the bad reviews for Terminal F, which is easily my favorite terminal to fly out of at PHL. I get super excited when I find out my flight is leaving from Terminal F. The dining options and brighter space are worlds better than the other terminals.   If you're getting dropped off, you don't have to go through the main terminals and take the shuttle to F - you can just get dropped off right at F! Just check your gate before you get to the airport. It is that easy.   As for the food, I'm partial to Local, the sit-down restaurant with iPad ordering where you pay right after you order so that when you are finished you can leave at any time. For fast food there are some solid offerings, like Chipotle, Le Bus, Philly Pretzel Factory, Smashburger, etc.

I've had two really great meals at Kidari so far. Once with my girl Angela J over the summer and again with my man on Friday for lunch. Both times I had the spicy tuna tartar which is delicious. It is served with some fried potato straws and two different types of sauce. I also really enjoy their miso soup, which has a bit more flavor than some of their competitors' versions.   Normally, I'm not a fan of raw salmon but Kidari's fish is so fresh and clean tasting that I really enjoyed their spicy salmon roll. Maybe even more than my usual go-to, the spicy tuna roll. Their rolls are plump and filling; after the soup and shared app, two was more than enough.   During the summer there was an awesome half-priced sushi happy hour. Not sure if they are still offering this deal but if so, it's a total steal for some really quality sushi.

I love that there's a new Pure Fare relatively close to my neighborhood. This one is much smaller than the location on 21st, but the size is just right for the area. There are a few tables up front and a small refrigerated case with a selection of sandwiches, salads and snacks.   There are only about five sandwich and five salad choices, so go in with an open mind as to what you'd like to eat. I selected one of my faves, the turkey and cheddar sandwich with spicy honey mustard, yesterday. I also grabbed a banana cookie and coffee. Total cost was over twelve dollars, which is a bit steep, but I always appreciate knowing what is in my food and exactly how many calories it's going to cost me. I'll pay a premium for that anytime.   Since the closing of my go-to lunch spot (Healthy Bites To Go), I haven't really found a suitable replacement as far as healthy lunches are concerned. Pure Fare is a welcome addition to the neighborhood, and I'll likely become a regular fairly quickly.

How am I the first to review this magical wonderland of jeans???  This is my tried and true, go-to place for the perfect pair.  There are tons of different styles for every body type and loads of size options.  Best of all, the jeans come in long and extra long, for those of us who've got legs and know how to use 'em.    Now, there may be some skeptics out there who can't rationalize dropping a Benjamin or more on a pair of jeans.  Rest assured, ladies (and gents), these are not your Grandma's dungarees.  Once you enter the store, a helpful staffer will guide you through the confusing process of finding your style and size.  What's that?  You already know your size?  Fine, learn the hard way that your regular size is going to quickly transform into a baggy version of what you now see in the mirror.  Unfortunately, I know this from experience.  On the other hand, if you heed the wise advice of the Lucky staff and buy the pair that feels slightly tight but possibly doable, I promise you will look and feel like a vixen.  Those jeans will fit you snugly without being too tight, and they will never lose their shape (please wash in cold water, inside-out and line-dry).  Now work it!

Allison B and I had a delightful sushi lunch today at Machi. I had only tried them for delivery in the past, and it was apparent to me today that most of their business is of the take-out variety.  We were the only table in the small restaurant, which was just fine by us.   The lunch special comes with either soup or salad and a two or three roll combo. I had just come from spinning class so my hungry self was all about three rolls (which I of course couldn't finish). The salads were quite large with delicious ginger dressing. My sushi rolls were very tasty and the fish was very fresh. The wasabi was delightfully strong. I'll return (or order) again!

Every time I go to the P&P, I wake up the next morning enveloped in regret. I should probably stop going, huh?   It had been a long while since I set foot in the place. So long, in fact, that I was told the ground floor bar had been closed for renovations for some time and the bar action was now upstairs.   The upstairs bar area looked like part of a sad comedy club from the early 80s. The only brightness in the room came from a small television, and the creepy monitor from the video camera trained on the front door. Absolutely no music played, and I didn't see or smell any hot water dogs. Downgrade.  My three stars are for the daydreams I have, thinking about what characters have sat at the bar over the years and wondering if they shared the same melancholic feelings as me while doing so.   I hope not to return, but at some point I probably will.

We stopped into Talula's Daily a couple times over the weekend. The first time, we were looking for a quick breakfast. There were croissants stuffed with turkey and Swiss for under four dollars, so we opted for those along with a couple cups of La Colombe coffee. I asked for extra room in my cup after noticing that the coffee was filled to the brim. My boyfriend, unfortunately, did not. When he picked up his cup, it started to buckle causing hot coffee to spill all over his hands. So unless Talula's decides to upgrade their cups, do yourself a favor and ask for room so you don't suffer the same fate.   Aside from that unfortunate mishap, I have mostly positive things to say about this place. The dining area is very cute, though shared tables are a concept that not everyone seems to grasp. Sharing is caring, folks!    There's currently a check-in offer for a free cookie, which I am looking forward to claiming. The aforementioned turkey and Swiss croissants were quite delicious. A second visit yielded tomato focaccia that was absolutely fantastic. Their mushroom soup was too heavy for my taste, but if you love mushrooms and are looking for a soup that will stick to the ribs, you'll probably want to try it.   I'd really love to check out one of the dinners sometime. Until I do, I'll be swinging by for more food to go or a quick bite in.

Prime Stache was an awesome choice for a girls night out over the weekend. I made a reservation in advance and we were seated right when we arrived. We were all in the mood for martinis and I asked for my usual - slightly dirty with olives. Prime Stache serves only American products so my choices were Tito's Vodka and Penn 1681. I'm down with Tito's so I went with that and my drinks were perfect all night; never too dirty, just right.   One of my friends is gluten-free but she was able to find a few menu items that worked. We started with the house salad which is all veggies and vinaigrette, and my other friend and I ordered the edamame and sweet pea ravioli, which we both loved. The kitchen sent out a second round of the ravioli and an order of fish tacos; two of us had already ordered the tacos for our mains but our gluten-free friend was able to eat the fish which was great, since she couldn't have the ravioli. I personally thought the tacos could use a little bit of sauce; some type of spicy aioli or sour cream would elevate these tacos from good to great.   What I did like is that a lot of the food we ordered was fairly healthy and didn't feel too heavy. There are more decadent menu items for sure, but it's really nice to have a lighter option for once when dining out. Something for everyone.   We skipped dessert in favor of another round of drinks, and when all was said and done, our bill was reasonable for a girls night out.

19 Degrees is a solid step up from the market that was previously in this space. It still serves a similar purpose (deli/market), but the feel is much nicer. I'd be just as comfortable sitting down for a bite as I do taking my sammies to go. The counter staff is friendly and they also seem to have regulars at lunch time.   That said, my sandwich was slightly off from what I requested when I stopped in last week. It was still tasty, just lacking all the components I wanted (which I actually had to repeat while ordering). I definitely like that they use quality deli meats and everything tastes super fresh. I'll keep 19 Degrees in the rotation for quick and inexpensive lunches during the week.

Tom's is solid. We order delivery from time to time. Our orders are always accurate and fairly fast, so that's definitely a positive.   In terms of food, their soup dumplings are great and they have the best scallion pancakes around. As for entrees, my husband likes the garlic chicken while I lean towards the sesame chicken. I've really enjoyed it in the past but my order last weekend seemed overly syrupy sweet. Maybe next time I'll go with the ol' general for more of a balance.

Wow.    That was my first impression when walking into Union Trust.  Beautiful architecture, and what were probably some crazy-expensive renovations, stretched from marble floor to richly adorned ceiling.  The main level bar was still swinging after 10 on a weeknight, but there were plenty of available chairs at the upstairs bar for an after dinner cocktail.  As my mom and I sat there chatting, I had a hard time focusing on the conversation as my eyes were wandering all over the room.  For me, this restaurant instantly became the most glamorous in the city, and has shot to the top of my "places to dine" list.  Therefore, my stars are all based on my cocktail experience alone (said cocktail was a tasty gin, strawberry and basil combination made by a friendly bartender).  I hope they can be matched when I come back for dinner, so I can love on this place even more!

Tired from a long day of travel woes, we arrived in Nashville hungry and weary. Urban Grub was our first dining destination. Though fairly hungry, I didn't want to eat anything super heavy since it was pretty late in the evening for dinner. I took our bartender's recommendation and ordered the trout, which came topped with delicious spices, arugula and bacon vinaigrette. It was served piping hot in a cast iron skillet.   My friend opted for the shrimp and grits and, despite not wanting anything heavy, I could not stop stealing bites. This dish stole the show. What I loved most was that the grits had lots of peppers, onions and tomatoes, which added a ton of flavor and texture.   The beer list was solid and I was able to try a couple local brews: a pale ale by Jackalope (great) and a hefeweizen by Yazoo (far too banana-y for my taste though I drank it down anyway).   This place would probably be a lot more fun with a group since there wasn't really any socializing going on even on a Friday night. I probably wouldn't go just for drinks unless I was in a group. But for a nice dinner, it's a solid option.

M2O is an interesting concept but definitely one I can get behind. Of course, I always love a good burger and fries, but I'm much more likely to order a salad, especially for a weekday lunch. M2O (short for made-to-order) has something for a splurge or a healthy meal!   I met the lovely Alisha S for lunch earlier this week and we were both M2O newbies. She opted for a burger while I went with a caesar salad with grilled chicken. It's typical fast-casual service where you pay at the counter, take a number on a stand, and find a table. We sat outside which seemed like a great idea, but I'd probably sit inside next time to avoid bugs, which descended as soon as our food arrived.   Our food was delivered without any napkins or utensils, so be sure to swing by one of the counters inside to grab everything you need. As far as my salad was concerned, it was delicious. The chicken was perfectly grilled while still tender and the dressing was just right. Alisha's burger looked incredible so I definitely want to get back for one of those sometime, too.   With all the protein options for salads, I was surprised that there weren't more sandwich options outside of just a regular burger or veggie burger. Maybe that will come in the future. I look forward to my next visit!

Yesterday I had what was one of the best customer service experiences in recent memory. While putting on my coat to go forage for a late lunch somewhere in the GradHo 'hood, The Quick Fixx popped into my mind. I took off my coat (who really wants to go out in the rainy cold, anyway?), perused the menu and gave them a ring.   The owner, Matt, answered the phone and, once I gave him my digits, told me that he had planned to call me this week so we could discuss my recent experience. It was pretty obvious that he had read my Yelp review, so we talked about the restaurant, their products, etc. It was clear that he valued the feedback and wanted to make sure his customers were happy. This pretty much cemented me as a repeat customer.   I ended up ordering a salad off the menu, the Di Carlo, which is a Caesar with grilled haloumi cheese. I added chicken and also ordered some of the tomato bruschetta, just in case. With a can of Diet Coke, the order came to around $15, but Matt gave me a five dollar discount for the fact that I was willing to chat for a few minutes. Totally unnecessary but definitely a nice gesture.   My order arrived in the quoted twenty minutes and I was happy with everything. Their Caesar dressing is seriously tasty (and by the way, the toasted bread is how they do their croutons - Matt and I discussed that also). I do think the salad and a side of bruschetta was just the right amount of food for lunch. Until next time!

YUM! I loved my dinner at Agno Grill last night. My boyfriend has been bugging me to try this place and telling me that I would love it. I'm already a big fan of Pure Fare and, honestly, I might like the Agno Grill concept even more. There are so many choices for what you can put into your bowl or wrap that you could probably go twenty times and have something different each time.   Last night I opted for a (step 1) black rice bowl with (step 2) veggies, (step 3) roasted cauliflower, olives, and white bean, spinach and parmesan spread plus (step 4) tzatziki and the special sauce of the day, green peppers and olive tapenade. And no, I didn't order a single thing extra - you really get that many different toppings in your bowl or wrap! Having so many things in a bowl was kind of crazy but it was fun trying different flavor combinations. I loved every bite and will definitely be hitting up Agno again soon. The more healthy-yet-interesting options in this city, the better.

I'm smack in the middle of my French for Travelers class, and I am truly loving it. Before signing up for my course at Alliance Francaise de Philadelphie, I did some research to decide where I should take my classes. Very happy with my decision to go with the Alliance, since it's not just a place to take classes but also a community of folks who are either from France or speak French or are attempting to learn. Though I have yet to take part, there are community events each month that seem interesting and fun.   I'm a total beginner, and could not have asked for a better instructor in Yann. He moved to Philadelphia from France just four months ago and he's a wonderful teacher. He's very encouraging and patient and has a great teaching style. We learn at a pace that is challenging but not too fast. He assigns homework and sends materials that help me with at-home study.   It's going to take a long time to really understand this language, but I feel like I've found the place that will give me the tools and knowledge to do so.

Bakersfield was conveniently located right near our hotel for my bachelorette party weekend in Nashville. On Saturday afternoon, we had nine hungry girls and no reservations, which made Bakersfield the perfect option since they take walk-ins only. We didn't have to wait long for a table large enough to fit our group to open up, but we did have to wait until our whole party was there to even put our name in for a table. In the meantime, the hostess kept pushing these standing-only tables on us, but we held out because we weren't interested in standing while eating a full meal.    Once our name was in, we migrated to the nearby bar to get drinks. The hostess was on us every ten seconds to move out of the way, which we gladly did, once we received our drinks. It was a little weird and made ordering kind of awkward since we knew this woman just wanted us to get out of the way. But how else would we have ordered drinks?   Seated at the table, things ran much smoother. Our server was awesome and made some great recommendations. The queso and guac were both delicious and came out seconds after we ordered them. The tacos were also great and I found two to be more than enough after the chip bonanza. Also, the margaritas were on point. Prices are very reasonable, and our server was willing to split our checks without a second thought.   I'd definitely hit this place up again though I'd be wary of where I stood to order a cocktail.

Still a fan of Seasons 52 although sometimes I think their food could use a bit more... seasoning. Today I had a cup of clam and shrimp cioppino, which was light and tasty. For my main course I had fish tacos. They were presented very nicely, and the flavors were good, but the lettuce mix seemed like something that came right out of a bag. I'm pretty sure that it was, with little strips of carrots and everything. A vinegary slaw in its place would have made a huge difference, and would have kept the tacos from being a touch too dry. Nonetheless, it was a guilt-free meal and filling lunch.

I like Stogie Joe's. It's South Philadelphia to a T and I enjoy the laid back, friendly neighborhood vibes. You get the sense that everyone knows each other.   My husband and I were in the neighborhood and looking for a casual spot to watch the Sixers game. I was dying for wings and beer and a friend suggested Stogie Joe's. We lucked out with a four top facing the TVs at the bar so we were both able watch the game while having dinner.   Our server was friendly, and I think a little impressed by my appetite. We ordered buffalo wings (fried, well done) and potato wedges to start. The wings were great! One order wasn't enough so we asked for another round and our server suggested we try the grilled wings, well done. It was a great suggestion because these were also awesome. We also shared a chicken parm sandwich, which was great. As I said, I was extra hungry!   We had several rounds of draft beers and everything including tip came to under a hundred bucks. Considering we spent a good part of our evening there, that wasn't so bad. Cash-only which is pretty annoying in this day and age, but they have an ATM on site which helps. I'm looking forward to our next visit!

I finally made it in to Eviama for a service (though I have been there several times to make purchases or host events), on New Year's Eve no less! My neck and shoulders had been feeling super tight for weeks so I finally decided to give my fiancé a break and get a professional massage. I could not believe my luck that there was an available appointment with Cooper in the early afternoon.   When I arrived, I filled out a quick form and then Cooper took me to the treatment room, where we talked about some of my problem areas. The massage was fantastic. My shoulders and upper back felt a lot less stiff and I had that euphoric feeling that only the best massages bring on when I walked outside into the cold winter air. I would definitely recommend Cooper and Eviama to anyone looking to escape the city and the craziness of life for an hour of relaxation.

Not updating this review sooner has been a complete oversight.  I've actually been back four or five times since my first visit, and Amis has become one of my favorite destinations for dining and/or drinks.  There are several things on the menu that I have come to absolutely adore, starting with the strozzaprete alla vongole, its buttery flavors I have talked up to just about anyone who will listen.  Another favorite is the bufala ricotta; rich and creamy and drizzled with olive oil, it is the perfect spread for the accompanying toasted bread.    I was once offered a bite of the turkey cutlet by a distinguished gentleman sitting next to me at the bar.  Normally, I'd pass without thinking twice, but this man insisted that the preparation changed his previous contempt for turkey to pure lust, at least, for this particular dish.  Who could pass that up?  I have to hand it to the guy, he was right on.  It sounds crazy to order something so plain-sounding, but trust Vetri and his crew to turn a plain old turkey into a Cinderella story.  A turkerella, if you will.  Make your reservations far in advance, dolls.  The tables don't come easy!

I like Lo Spiedo even though I don't get there very often due to the location. Because they are a bit off the beaten path, I appreciate that they offer free parking on-site.   My recent visit was for the Summer of Brosé happy hour. I loved the lineup of rosés, even if I didn't think their special was all that... special. Only one of the wines was discounted and it was still an eight dollar glass, which made for a pricey night when all was said and done.   The food is always great, but I was so bummed to see some of the grilled/skewered protein options removed from the menu since my last visit. The menu is now primarily composed of small plates, sandwiches, pastas and pricey entrees. I really dig the grilled chicken wings and bbq popcorn (amazing!). I'm hoping they bring the shaved pumpkin salad back in the fall, which is one of my favorite seasonal dishes, and something for which I'd go out of my way.

Pumpkin has been the MVP of our dining experiences during the pandemic. We've had two exceptional takeout meals at home, and this week we booked a table outside for my husband's birthday. We arrived right on time for our 6pm weekday reservation. The parklet set up in front of Pumpkin is super cute, with string lights and little flower pots.   In addition to the three course menu for $35, there was also a menu of a la carte items. Those really appealed to us so we went to town and ordered: Lost Bread tavola, grilled olives, fluke crudo, hot tomatoes, salt potatoes, NJ hake, and flank steak. Everything was coursed out and the food was excellent. We ordered the chocolate cake with banana caramel for dessert, and it was brought out with a candle, which was so sweet.   Our table was appropriately spaced from the one behind us, and servers were always wearing masks. There was also a bottle of hand sanitizer at the door in case you needed to enter (I did, to use the restroom), and a sign asking that you wait for assistance before entering, presumably since the space is small and they want to keep everyone distanced.   We really lucked out with a nice summer night that wasn't too humid, and our celebratory dinner felt special and -almost- normal. We look forward to our next meal!

Thank you, Andrea F, for leading the way to Plaza Garibaldi! I'd had this spot bookmarked for a while based on Andrea's review, and I finally placed an order for delivery one night earlier this week.   I went with the chicken enchipocladas which was a tasty and hearty choice. There were three corn torillas stuffed with shredded chicken and topped with chipotle sauce, sliced avocado and a light sprinkling of queso fresco, plus a swizzle of sour cream. This was a nice, lighter alternative to enchiladas.   On the side, I received a container with pico de gallo, rice and refried beans, plus a small bag of tortilla chips and two salsas. The meal itself was only twelve bucks but delivery plus tip put the total slightly above $20. Considering I got two meals out of it, that was fine with me.   I might deviate to other menu items next time as I felt like I was missing a bit of texture. Overall, excited to have a new option for Mexican delivery!

If only I had options like the ones at Franklin's Table back when I was in college! This food hall is pretty legit. It brings together some of Philadelphia's best known restaurants and makes them a lot more accessible. Perhaps Franklin's Table is a little pricier than other food halls, but I'd argue that you're also getting really high quality food at a fraction of the regular restaurant cost.    I'd imagine this place must be pretty crazy at peak hours. I've only stopped by during random afternoon hours and have had positive experiences. Even the bathrooms are clean and nice. My main suggestion would be to add a composting bin in addition to the regular trash and recycling. So many restaurants are using compostable utensils/containers now and it's a shame to not dispose of them correctly.

Wow, the happy hour. I popped in for a drink and bite one weeknight and was pleasantly surprised. The bar features a red, a white and one cocktail for half off. They also offer a complimentary flatbread. I chose the goat cheese and artichoke flatbread and a small Greek salad. Both were awesome and substantial enough for dinner. With my glass of white, the total bill was just over eleven dollars. What a steal! And even though I was dining solo, I had live piano music to keep me company. I may need to make happy hour at Seasons a weekly thing!

Erawan deserves an upgrade from me. They are definitely in the running for my go-to Thai delivery. They aren't open on Mondays and their delivery fee via GrubHub is $3, which is kind of a bummer. But the food is solid.   I enjoy their tom yum soup and I also recently tried their version of wonton soup. It's totally different from the Chinese version, almost reminding me of a chicken noodle soup, but with light wontons instead of noodles. It was a nice alternative to the tom yum, although that's still my preference.   The chicken with pineapple sauce is always on point, though the portions can sometimes be a bit small compared with the price. The rice is sticky every single time; it even holds up in the fridge better than most rice.

I'm tempted to give four stars, because I've never had a bad experience (besides the standard wait time for a table, of course), but something is holding me back... most likely, the extra weight I put on after my meal on Saturday evening.  Picture this: three relatively health-conscious girls out to dinner.  Nobody was trying to get all South Beach or anything, but it was clear that we wanted healthy meals so we could splurge a little on dessert.  Two orders of wasabi tuna and an order of miso salmon seemed like a safe enough bet.  Not so much.  My friends' wasabi tuna entrees were really delish, but the wasabi crust had a fried consistency to it-- good for sure, but totally not necessary.  My salmon dish had an absolute river of thick creamy sauce going around the plate.  Luckily, the salmon itself was on dry land, located on top of an island of rice.    I just don't understand why the people behind the menu at Cheesecake Factory think that healthy food has to be bombarded with fat before people will order it.  The salmon was fantastic with just the miso glaze-- and the tuna didn't need such a thick, greasy crust.      Oh, the CF does have healthier selections on the menu.  You'll know what they are because they are listed with the words "Weight Management" before each item.  What genius came up with this idea?!  Can I take his or her place on the marketing team when he or she gets fired?

While I'm definitely more skeptical than my fellow Yelpers when it comes to trying the prepared foods at this market, I will agree that the place is stocked to the brim with absolutely everything. I've never made it all the way down the aisles; the couple of visits I've made have been for milk or OJ. But it's clear that this place probably covers every household need.   Maybe I'll give the breakfast sandwiches a shot sometime. Maybe.

My girlfriends and I hit Heritage about a month or so ago for dinner and drinks. I loved everything about my experience and have been hankering to get back. The space is gorgeous. There's a very large dining room and bar area plus a lounge area and seating outside on a cute patio. We chose to sit outside for our meal which was a good call on a nice summer night.  There was a rosé from NJ that was so amazing (I know, crazy!), we ordered several bottles throughout the night! Favorite dishes were the kale salad, heirloom tomatoes, corn cakes, egg noodles and roasted chicken. Oh wow that chicken. Our least favorite dish was the mussels. They sounded nice but we should have read between the lines when our server described them as "on the large side." They were grossly large and the only thing we didn't finish!   We skipped dessert in favor of a nightcap in the lounge area. Our dinner server stuck with us for serving our drinks as well and he was awesome all night. Really excited for the next visit!

I've had two really solid experiences at Hi Kori. Tucked away at the far end of Chinatown Square, the bar is a hidden gem offering a break from the rest of bustling Chinatown.   Each visit was for drinks only. I found them to be well balanced and crafted by really friendly bartenders. Certainly a worthy place to spend your dollars and relax for a bit while in the area!

I was never a fan of the Standard Tap.  My ill-will towards the place started many moons ago, when my then bf promised Old City's Mexican Post (I was a youngin', go easy) but his friend insisted we go to Standard Tap.  It was there that I was met with blackboard ordering, a forgettable burger and the curious 80s hairstyle of the friend's date.  Our dinner put me in a pissy mood that started a downhill spiral of our night, culminating in a massive blowup over who-knows-what at the G-Love concert.  Ah, memories.  Over the years, I've held my contempt in check while swinging by just for beers.  They have a decent selection, after all, and there has always been seating available in a dark corner somewhere.  Actually, it seems like everywhere is a dark corner, come to think of it.  I highly recommend the place for hobbits and vigilantes.  When the Standard was selected as the brunch location last weekend, I wasn't thrilled but knew it was about time I gave them another shot for food.  Seated in a dark booth (natch), six of us squinted to see the blackboard.  I almost always opt for savory over sweet while brunching, so I was a little disconcerted at the lack of options.  As my coffee mug was filled, I requested sweet n low and was asked if Equal was okay.  Anyone who knows me will tell you that I have a penchant for little pink packets and a strong animosity towards blue and yellow varietals.  Still, coffee is coffee and when you really need some, exceptions are made.  Our orders came out quickly, and I'd be lying if I said I didn't clean my plate.  My breakfast, though basic, hit the spot.  Two eggs over easy, a homemade biscuit, home fries and a heaping pile of thick cut bacon made this girl very happy.  I took a bite of my guy's biscuits and gravy dish and had to admit that the Standard's version was even better than North Third's, which I didn't think possible.  Bloody Marys were spicy and kickin'; the perfect beverage to accompany the meal.  I'm going to go with a very solid "A-OK" for Standard Tap.  It's been a tumultuous ride over the years but it appears we may have weathered the storm.

My last experience at Little Spoon left a lot to be desired. My friend and I, having really enjoyed our previous visit a couple months ago, decided to return for lunch and some catching up. We both ordered the exact same things we had on the previous visit - the omelet with cheddar, apples and sausage for me, the meatloaf sandwich for him.   We ordered and paid separately, which was probably a mistake. My omelet was dropped off about two minutes after we sat down, while my friend waited a good 5-10 minutes more for his sandwich. My omelet had no sausage whatsoever. They simply forgot to add it in, even though it's a staple on their menu. There was hardly any cheese and the very sweet apples overpowered the eggs. The breakfast potatoes were bland and undercooked. Also, they were out of multigrain bread so I had a choice of sourdough or white. I went with the sourdough which was very good but I would have preferred multi or wheat.   Eventually, my friend received his sandwich; the ingredients were completely engulfed by the bread. The meatloaf inside looked dry and unappetizing - my friend said it tasted completely different from the last time we were there.   This wasn't the first time I visited Little Spoon and left underwhelmed. I'm officially taking it out of the lunch rotation.

Loving this new DiBruno location in Market East. They carry a healthy array of to-go items, packaged foods and snacks, have a nice selection of cheeses and meats, and there are loads of helpful and friendly employees all over the store.   Very nice touch giving customers free flowers with a purchase the day before Thanksgiving. They were beautiful and lasted at least a week!

I absolutely love that there is a Tuesday Farmers Market that runs all afternoon and into the evening right in my neighborhood. Julian Abele is a really pretty plot of land and I really hope the market continues through the year (well, as long as possible once the weather starts getting cold - hopefully in the very distant future). It seems like there are usually only one or two vendors so there isn't a huge selection, but there is always a nice array of local produce, some canned goods and some baked items available.

Last Saturday morning, my friend and I visited the new Bruegger's for a grab and go breakfast that would remedy our stomachs from a late night out.  I ordered an everything bagel "softwich" with turkey, lettuce, tomato and pickles on the side as well as a cup of coffee.  When this rang up somewhere around the $9 mark, I was momentarily stupefied.  Talk about over-inflation.  After parting with my final skinny jeans-crumpled Hamilton, we were off.  Back at the couch, I discovered that my softwich, while slammin', was missing its side of pickles.  Bummer.  Still, this would not keep me from returning to Bruegger's in the future.  Then, I took my first sip of coffee.  It was quite possibly the worst ever, right alongside the crap they serve in the Philly airport (refer to my review for details on THAT).  Yuck.  Bad coffee just ruins the breakfast experience.    I'd come back for bagels, but who really wants to make two stops in the morning for bagels and coffee?  Madness, I tell you.

After two experiences at Urban Farmer, I think three stars is more than fair, and possibly a little generous. My first was lunch with a friend shortly after the opening. I didn't have reservations, and asked the host if I could have a table for two. He said he could seat me at the bar. I assumed the available tables must have been on hold for reservations, but when I settled in at the bar and pulled up Open Table, there were still openings. Needless to say this was not the best start.   On my second lunch visit, the hostess was busy with calls and another person waiting to be seated. When she was free, I gave her my name and she told me my dining companion had already arrived. I was basically pointed to the direction of the table and I sat myself (Four Seasons, you are missed).    The most reasonable options for lunch are the sandwiches, which are generously portioned and come with a side. The turkey sandwich is solid and I very much enjoyed the side salad during visit number one. Entree salads get very expensive very quickly, as I can attest after my second lunch, in which a modest-sized Caesar salad with (four) shrimp added-on set me back $23. Ouch.   The most redeeming thing about each experience has been the service. The blonde female bartender from my first visit was an absolute doll, and the brunette female server who took care of my table on visit two was also very nice and really on top of making sure our drinks were constantly refreshed.   There are so many great dining options in the Rittenhouse area, and while I love the Logan Hotel's vibes, a girl can't get her kicks on decor alone. Undecided as to when I will return.

I hadn't been to this deli in quite some time, but I wanted some beer for the game last weekend so decided to swing by for a six pack. This place is weird. It appears to be owned or run by a bunch of young guys. One guy, not sure if he was part of the crew or what, was passed out at a table.   There are definitely better places to grab a sandwich or six pack in the area, and I probably won't be back.

Want to know how to ruin a good thing? Throw some mediocre dishes on a prix fixe menu and call it Restaurant Week. I already boycotted Philly's version this year after too many disappointments in the past. Unfortunately, the promise of four courses for $35 got the best of me when the SJ Restaurant Week ads came out. When I saw the ChopHouse on the list, I booked right away. This is normally one of my favorites, but not one I get to very often considering the price and location.   My friend and I got to the bar early for happy hour. Since our reservation was not until 7:45, we were hoping to get something small to tide us over. Unfortunately, they were only offering the Restaurant Week menu and nothing else, so ordering an appetizer was not possible. No big deal. The blue cheese-stuffed olives in our Effen Blue martinis did the trick.   Once seated, our server and supporting staff were all attentive and provided great service. The manager, Patrick, stopped by several times to chat with us, which was nice. For the first course, we had the tuna tartare and calamari. The tuna tartare was pretty good, if Barbie-sized, and the calamari was okay but not the greatest. The second course was our favorite (which says a lot about the evening)-- a wedge salad and lobster bisque. Both were really, really good. In fact, we should have requested these as our main courses as well. My friend's penne and vodka sauce with shrimp and scallops was basically boxed pasta with a red cream sauce (i.e., not vodka sauce) and my crabcakes were just okay. Definitely not what one would expect from the ChopHouse under normal circumstances. We thought dessert would redeem the meal, but my friend's pumpkin creme brulee lacked the usual sugary hardness on top and my brownie sundae would have been beaten in a throw-down challenge from Friendly's.   My four stars are generous based on last night's dinner. I've been to the ChopHouse a number of times though, and all my other experiences were five star worthy, which is why I can't justify anything lower. The bottom line is, even great restaurants fail to impress during Restaurant Week.

This review reflects my first of what will probably be many experiences at Amis, especially if my guy has anything to do with it. We stopped in for drinks and some light bites after our recent class at Tria's Fermentation School. At 8:30 on a weeknight, mostly all the tables were full so we opted for one of the high tops near the bar. The environment of Amis is the antithesis to that of Osteria. Amis is cozier, darker and sexier.   A basket of soft focaccia was dropped at our table. Later, it was replaced by a different type of bread. I love, love, love bread and I enjoyed the variety.   We started with the pecorino trio, a salami (I can't recall the exact name) and the ricotta. One of the selections on the pecorino plate seemed a bit dry, as if it had been stored incorrectly, but we really enjoyed the others, particularly the softest of the three. The salami was studded with pieces of peppercorn and had a nice consistency, but the flavors were not as abundant as I expected. The ricotta was the clear winner in this first round; a heaping pile of the snow white cheese glistened with olive oil and was specked with black pepper. It was heavenly, and will certainly be ordered again on our next visit and should be a mandatory part of everyone's first visit.   We also ordered the stuffed clams and oxtail gnocchi. The clams were very good - almost as good as my grandmother's but not quite. They had an interesting flavor which made me wonder what exactly went into the preparation. The gnocchi was delicious and extremely rich. A few delectable bites was all I could handle on top of the other splurges of the evening.   We didn't have room for dessert but I definitely look forward to checking those options out soon. I'm going with three stars for my first experience but am looking forward to trying more of the menu.

I popped into Kildare's for lunch with Akshay M on a Sunday afternoon. Akshay was in it for a bite and some soccer, I was in it for just a bite. "I've experienced better" really sums it up, but the reasons are as follows: stale beer smell upon walking in (which I could get past only because of the big open windows), forgetful bartender (had to ask for sugar for my iced tea twice, no cutlery presented after ordering, etc.), lame presentation of food.   I ordered a steak salad with dressing on the side and this thing was lame, lame, lame. The kitchen forgot the bacon crumbles on the salad. The steak portion was pretty small and not super flavorful. The red onions that came on the salad were thankfully served on the side. I had one bite and I could tell they were not super fresh; there was no sweetness, just that really potent onion flavor that you do not want lingering around.   I should have known when all the other restaurants on the street were bumping that Kildare's was empty for a reason. If there's a next time, I'll go with a sandwich, which looked like a decent option. But there probably won't be a next time.

I was shocked - SHOCKED - I tell you, when I arrived at FedEx Ship Center on the Saturday before Christmas and became just the second person in line. Had everyone really beat me at the Christmas game this year or were the employees at this location just that good at expediting packages to and from customers?   Honestly, it was probably just a fluke that I walked in to no crowd when I did. The employees didn't seem particularly speedy but I still received my package in one piece with little fuss.

I popped into Writer's Block Rehab last Saturday after attending a play nearby, and was super excited to see two open seats at the bar downstairs. Now, looking at the photos on the biz listing, I'm wishing I had gone upstairs to snag a spot. The upstairs seating area looks so fun, like a library! Next time.   The downstairs bar did have its perks. With just a handful of seats, my companion and I had lots of face time with the bartender and we were able to ask questions about different drinks. I started with a pisco sour featuring turmeric. It was like drinking a healthy juice with booze. My next drink had gin, egg whites and a couple other ingredients I don't remember. It was pink, yet surprisingly light in taste. I really loved that not one cocktail tasted too sweet. I like my drinks boozy with just a hint of sweetness and I felt the bartender really hit the mark.   Last, we finished with a round of espresso martinis. These were topped with some chocolate shavings and were very nicely presented.   I'd love to return for drinks upstairs on a date with my husband or to catch up with a friend or two.

Dear Friends and Family,  The holidays are fast approaching! Don't you hate it when, once the pressure is on, you suddenly forget all those great ideas you had for gifts all year long? I do, too. So I thought I'd make myself useful and remind you all of my love of Duross & Langel's bath products. I'm still obsessed with the bubble bath, and my vanilla is running dangerously low. I'm also a big fan of the eucalyptus scent. I'd also LOVE some of their soy wax candles. These items will set you back less than $25 a pop (you could actually get TWO bottles of bubble bath for less than $25!). See? One person off your Christmas list already. Always happy to help.  Love,  Michelle      PS, I'm currently loving the stress relief bubble bath, but I'm pretty well-stocked on that one.

I'm going with three stars for my first visit, though I could easily see Dim Sum House earning another star with some small tweaks. Two friends and I stopped in for an early dinner on a Sunday, and we were seated right away at a table near the bar. It was only when I made a trip to the restroom later on that I noticed the much larger dining room - this is a nicer area though the more informal bar area was fine for our visit.   I was in the mood for a cocktail, so I went with the What's in the Flask? Magic Potion?, which is a bourbon base with grilled peach syrup, oolong, mint and lemon. It was excellent. One of the best cocktails I've had in recent memory. The second one I ordered was just as good. That drink alone is enough to get me back in the door.   We ordered a ton of plates to share; perhaps this is why servers kept bringing dishes to our table that we actually didn't order? We repeatedly had to tell servers, no, that order of... isn't ours, but we are still waiting on the...   Another note about service: our server, while friendly, was also seen chomping away on food at the bar in between taking orders and serving drinks. Not exactly polished.   As for the food itself, I thought it was really solid. Soup dumplings, scallion pancakes, honey walnut shrimp, noodles, veggies and more were all tasty and perfect for sharing.   I'd like to return, and I'd love to see some improvements on the service since they are clearly going for a more refined vibe than some of the dim sum restaurants in Chinatown.

Chick's is our date night closer bar, and I absolutely love it.   We usually swing by on Thursdays when Jesse is working (but we've experienced great cocktails under the care of George as well). Just one drink always turns into several, and how could it not with great conversation amongst staff who have become friends.   The bar is typically quiet later in the evening and there's never any trouble getting a seat. There's usually a character or two which adds to the laughs. If you haven't checked this place out, hit your bookmark button and give them a look next time you want a nightcap.

I popped into A La Mousse in hopes of a bubble tea, but was informed they only have them certain days of the week. So I decided to try one of their many hot beverages, instead. I ordered a matcha latte with almond milk and asked that it only be made a little bit sweet.   As I was waiting, I perused the desserts. They really have some gorgeous cakes and other confections. I will definitely have to return to try the matcha chocolate cake, which looked incredible.   The store was super clean and bright, a very inviting space. My drink was made to perfection and warmed me up for the rest of my walk home. I look forward to returning!

Located in an inconspicuous strip of office buildings, right across the street from Cooper River, is the best kept secret in Camden County... and it took a born-and-raised Philadelphian to tell me about it!  Moore Brothers imports wines from small distributors.  Every bottle is kept in a temperature-controlled setting.  The staff members are not only excellent at pairing wines with whatever food combination you throw at them, but they are also well-versed with menus from restaurants all over the Delaware Valley.  Last week, I was on my way to a friend's house for a dinner featuring grilled chicken, corn on the cob and Caprese salad.  The gentleman assisting me asked if I knew what marinade was being used on the chicken.  When I wasn't sure, he pulled several options for me, but he used the salad as the determining factor, which led to a pinot grigio that perfectly complemented the meal later that evening.  On every visit, I've been helped the moment I walk through the door, and I've never once been made to feel foolish asking a question about the wine.  The staff members seem to appreciate people who want to learn, and they are always happy to assist.

What's not to love about this Di Bruno Bros.? Its location in the Italian Market dates back 75 years. Though small, this may be my favorite location of all - the curated selection is top quality and allows you to get in and get out with everything you need. The cheesemongers are the best. I could walk through that store and not even look at the cheese and they will still offer a slice of whatever is being featured that day. (Note: When in Di Bruno, I always purchase cheese.)  Last year my fiancé and I took our families to Di Bruno After Hours, which is when the shop closes and you have the entire place to yourselves. You bring the wine and beer, Di Bruno hooks it up with cheese galore and various snacks. Even my stepdad, a man whose personal constitution involves something about pledging allegiance only to American cheese, found things to enjoy.   Here's to 75 more years!

While I've never stepped foot inside Pretty Sweet Bakery, I've often admired the robin's egg blue-and-white shop from the street or car.  It's probably high time I check out the store firsthand, as I've already tried their delicious chocolate chip scones, purchased at local coffee shops, as well as their cupcakes.  Oh the cupcakes!  Last week, my stepmom surprised me with cupcakes in lieu of regular cake for my birthday.  There were three different versions, but I made a beeline for one of the red velvets, my favorite.  The cake was dense and moist, the frosting whipped and sweet.      Cupcakes make me sooooo happy, and Pretty Sweet Bakery's are no exception!

We ordered some solid Thai from Erawan last night. Delivery was fast compared with other Thai spots with delivery. They definitely get some points there. We ordered fried pork dumplings which were incredibly greasy, but still tasty. On the healthier end of the spectrum, my pad broccoli with chicken was light and flavorful. The rice was perfectly sticky. My boyfriend had chicken in pineapple sauce which was lighter than I expected and had a really nice sweet but spicy flavor. Last week he ordered chicken in some sort of spicy pepper sauce which was also really great.   As far as my favorite Thai delivery goes, I still have one other place that leads the pack, but because of the fast delivery, Erawan will definitely see some repeat business from me.

I'm ashamed to admit that I was a Chinatown virgin before my very first Jewish-Christmas.  Upon hearing this, Blake and Yuri, my hosts of the evening, made the experience special.  Blake donned red and green threads and Yuri somehow fixed my stubborn blinking lights necklace, which I received in my Christmas stocking that morning.  Neither seemed to mind that I wore it for the duration of the evening.    My hosts were torn between Vietnam and Vietnam Palace, but the shorter wait time at Vietnam Palace made the decision an easy one.  We lingered for about five minutes before we were seated.  I was surprised to see such an expansive cocktail list and immediately decided on a lychee martini.  It was so delish, I ended up having two (shocking, I know).  We ordered charbroiled lemongrass shrimp, beef short ribs and tofu rolls to start.  I'm not a tofu girl so I passed on those, but they were presented well and the peanut dipping sauce was met with much fanfare.  The shrimp were lightly flavored and well prepared, but perhaps could have used a dipping sauce themselves.  The short ribs had an excellent marinade but were far too fatty in my opinion.  I understand it is the nature of the beast, but actual meat was hard to come by.    For my main, I tried vermicelli with charbroiled chicken.  The chicken was seasoned well and I liked the sauce that accompanied the dish, but overall, I found the concept to be kind of boring.  Yuri offered a bite of his chicken and veggies in curry sauce, and while I wasn't crazy about the flavor, I liked the presentation.  I'd probably order something similar in the future, except in either the lemongrass or ginger variation.  We finished our meal with Vietnamese coffee, also new to me.  When I questioned the whereabouts of cream and sweetener, Yuri instructed us to simply stir.  A thick, sweet cream at the bottom of the cup mixed with the hot coffee on top.  A couple sips were nice, but the sweetness was too overpowering for my liking.  Our experience was a pleasant one and the staff did an excellent job.  I may return in the future but I'd like to try other Vietnamese spots first, to get a better idea of the cuisine in general.

After several visits to Farmers' Cabinet and never eating anything other than the popcorn and barley, I have finally tried some of the grub. And it just so happened to be from their new chef. The verdict? Yum.  We arrived with a crew of wild ones after the Yelp Elite Event at Lucky Strike. As our group grew in numbers, we moved from a small parlor-looking area in the formal dining room to the gigantic long table in the dining room off the beer bar. Our server Amy was sweet, helpful and on her A-game, despite our surely unexpected, slightly raucous crowd later on a Monday night.  Cocktails were distributed, menus floated around. Honestly, the regular menu at Farmers' Cabinet really doesn't do it for me (too eclectic), and I asked about the availability of a bar menu and inquired about the cheese fondue that I had seen during past visits. Unfortch, new chefs mean new menus so the fondue is sadly no longer, but I was presented with a sneak peak of the late night menu (available after 11) that had some interesting sandwich options. While my boyfriend munched on a buttery glazed pretzel, my carnal desires opted to wait it out and order something fleshier instead.   The chicken sandwich with bacon and jalapeno mayo was well worth the wait. The mix of thin and thick cut fries were an awesome partner. I was rude, I didn't offer any to my neighbors. My late night self is such a brat sometimes! At least I gave half the sandwich to Art, who agreed on its tastiness, though he barely had enough room for it.   Although I'll likely continue to think of Farmers' Cabinet as more of a place to get a great cocktail, I'm happy to know the option of a tasty late night snack exists as well.

Saturday night at Pumpkin had all the trappings of a great dinner for two. The intimate space was lit by candlelight and the heavy curtains by the doorway kept out any chill.   The seasonal menu had some variety, but there were only one or two selections from both the starters and main courses that appealed to me. I ultimately chose the celery root soup followed by pan roasted monkfish.   Warm, crusty bread was delivered to our table alongside roasted garlic olive oil. It was a delicious start to the meal. Starters came out quickly, and my soup turned out to be heavenly. The bowl was presented with some sauteed shallots and small rounds of apple, and the broth was poured tableside. I couldn't get enough of the velvety broth and incredible flavors, but luckily the portion size was generous. My boyfriend very much enjoyed his appetizer, which had tender pieces of octopus and squid.   After the soup, I couldn't wait to taste the entrees. They were delivered shortly after our apps were cleared and were nicely sized. Unfortunately, they didn't live up to the starters. My monkfish was slightly too salty and came served along a river of capers. Next to that was a gelatinous square of pork belly that lacked meatier bits. Across the table, a ridiculously large piece of beef cheek was tender like a short rib, only not as moist, and much fattier. Our favorite part of this course was the side, the name of which escapes me. It was grainy like brown rice and served in the style of risotto, with some minced vegetables throughout and a sprinkling of parmesan on top.   Even though we didn't love our entrees, the things we did enjoy were truly special. Service was also attentive and very informed. I absolutely see the potential here and I already have plans to return for an upcoming special event.

I hate to downgrade a restaurant that I've really loved in the past, but my recent brunch experience at Amis was not at all worth the high price tag that came along with it.   My friend and I were seated against the wall in the upper left area. Our server was polite but possibly a bit spread thin as we often had to wait longer than usual to order drinks. Speaking of drinks: the bellini is a spiced peach version that's high on flavor but low on champs. I had nary a buzz after I finished so I switched to the spicy bloody mary which was fine but didn't seem all that different from a regular bloody mary.    For food, I opted for the san marzano tomatoes with eggs and basil. This teeny tiny portion tasted fine but, again, nothing special. The roasted potatoes were under-seasoned and Lo Spiedo's homemade smoked bacon tasted no different from store bought bacon.   After hearing so many positive things about Amis' brunch I can honestly say I was disappointed, especially since brunch for two with tip came to somewhere around $100, give or take. I'll stick with dinner at Amis from here on out.

In all honesty, I really do like Continental Midtown. There are just a few things about it that irk the nerves sometimes. Like the issues I have with their rooftop bar that I pointed out in my previous review.   The premise is slightly upscale continental dining, but every time I eat there I feel like I've spent significantly more money than I intended. That said, I'm always thoroughly happy with the food.
