The Continental salad, just a basic Greek salad chopped up with some wonton wrappers thrown in for extra flavor, has always been a favorite. Same with the seared ahi tuna with sprouts over mushroom risotto and a small puddle of soy sauce. Recently, I tried the french onion soup dumplings and found them to be quite delicious.   The decor for me is starting to get a little outdated, and in certain areas it feels a bit cheap. Seated on the second floor a couple weeks ago, I leaned back in my quasi-booth and found it tipping backward. Huh? Also, I dislike the bathroom, with black toilets and a two-way mirror that any (Peeping) Tom, Dick or Harry can peer through on his way to the John. A covert teeth-check becomes impossible.    Another peeve is the seating policy. Even when the place was empty on a random weeknight, the hostesses were hesitant to seat me without my dining companion. They did, but what was there to think about? Understandable on a busy weekend, weekday lunch or with a larger party, but not one solitary woman weighted down with the bags of her Walnut Street revelry.  Will I return? You bet. The food, service, and swingy basket chairs outweigh my minor grievances in the scale of Starr.

Lots of TVs for sports fanatics?  Check.  Good bar food and decent drink specials?  Check.  Home to one of the more awkward dates of my life?  Check.  A fabulous server who knows to keep those drinks coming?  Double check.

The absolute best. While I adore all of the restaurants in Philly that are currently offering wine to-go during Covid-19, I really appreciate that I can order bottles from Moore Brothers at very reasonable prices and pick them up contact-free within a 24-hour window.  The website is easy to use and each wine has a lot of info so you could really spend some time being selective. My husband and I ordered a medley of rosés and whites, plus a couple lighter reds. We placed the order on Sunday morning and our pick-up was ready later that day. We arrived shortly before closing and called the store - the woman who answered told us to pop the trunk and they would be right out. So easy!   One of the nicest parts of the experience is that Moore Brothers packs in some slips which give details about each wine. I love that because I always try my best to pair our wines with the food we're eating. If you've never been to this great local biz, it's most certainly worth the trip!

As guests of my girl Karen B's wedding at the College of Physicians on Saturday, it was our understanding that we would be able to tour the Mütter Museum throughout the evening. So when my guy and I decided to take a break from dancing and get some science on around 9pm, we were surprised to find the entire museum area devoid of any staffing personnel. We entered through the gift shop (again, no staff = no sense of direction). The only light came from the iridescent glow of the exhibits in the exhibition beyond the shopping area. When we tried the heavy doors that presumably led to the museum - they were locked. A few minutes passed*, and we walked back out to the main corridor and through the next set of doors, which led to the main area of the museum, where all lights were on.   We only got to peer over the balcony for a moment, where I was able to point out the giant colon to my Mütter neophyte boyfriend, before the lights clicked off.   To be clear: lights off in the gift shop - no problem. Lights off in a room featuring skeletons - not okay! We yelled and a janitor came in and told us the museum was closed. How 'bout locking the door next time?!      *In which we may or may not have taken advantage of the unexpected alone time in a museum to make out.

My sister and I had planned to hit up Silk City for some time to get our dance on and check out the scene.  Last Friday we finally made that happen.  We got there around 10:30 or so and the lounge area was pretty dead, so we went to the bar in the diner.  The two bartenders were more interested in chatting with friends than they were with mixing drinks, but eventually we were deemed worthy and got to place our orders.  Many times when I order a "slightly dirty" martini, my drink will still end up tasting like a salt lick was plopped into my glass.  Much to my delight, the girls behind the bar knew what they were doing and rocked my world with a couple perfect drinks.  My sister had some sort of Lemonade and Popov concoction.  She's fresh out of college so she can still get down with some Popov.      After seeing a girl throw up on the bar near the bathrooms (PS, it wasn't even midnight yet), my sister was a little creeped out.  We decided to finish our drinks and head to the lounge.  As we were settling our tab, we noticed a bunch of people in the vicinity wearing fake mustaches.  Strange.  Walking into the lounge, we did a simultaneous double take--EVERYONE was wearing fake mustaches.  I looked at my sister and asked if we were dreaming.  Little sis and I were a tad out of our element at Silk City but we had a good time dancing and it was a fun night.  We probably won't be back for the nightlife, but I'd definitely be open to checking out dinner sometime... far away from the bar area near the bathroom, of course.

A friend in the neighborhood told me she prefers Thai Square over another nearby Thai restaurant, so my man and I decided to check it out on Saturday night. We walked up with a six pack on ice, expecting a wait, but there was only one other seated table. After being a very loyal Healthy Bites To Go customer, I was surprised by how roomy the dining room was - I think they can seat about 20.   We started with the fried pork dumplings, chicken skewers and coconut shrimp. I thought the dumplings were a bit too doughy (I prefer the ones in a thinner wrapper) but I really liked the shrimp and chicken skewers and their accompanying sauces.   For my main, I talked it over with our server and took her suggestion to try the exotic spiced pork. I ordered a medium spice level which was borderline hot for me, which is to say it was just right. The pork was lean and tender and the veggies were crisp. My fiancé's pad kra pow with chicken was very flavorful as well. Service was very pleasant. We look forward to trying more from Thai Square.

I still have a lot of love for Heritage, but my last dinner experience was not five stars. My husband and I made a last minute reservation on a snowy December Saturday. The restaurant was fairly empty and we arrived right before the live jazz duo started up.   Our server seemed a little green. He didn't know much about the wine - when I asked about a selection his response was that a lot of people like it. Fortunately, I too was one of those people after opting to order it, but a bit of a description would have been nice.   We started with a vegetable board which was excellent. So creative and a really fresh way to start off our meal. We moved straight to entrees from there. However, the side of jerked broccolini that we ordered with our entrees arrived unexpectedly as a mid-course. We decided to save it for the mains but it just sat there getting cold in the meantime.  I believe my husband had a seafood stew, while I went with the chicken. Folks, this was not your run-of-the-mill, boring chicken. It was Lancaster chicken, cooked perfectly, and served with the most delicious gnocchi and red cabbage. Wow. It's been almost a month since my visit and I can recall this dish perfectly.    I'd say the only thing that was really lacking from our visit was the excellent service I've received in the past. Otherwise, Heritage is still bringing their A game in the kitchen. I look forward to returning.

I'm on a review update kick and Tio Flores is up! I popped in for happy hour on a Monday and was pleased to see so many great HH specials and menu changes. The menu seems much more approachable and wallet-friendly than what I remembered from my last visits several years ago.   Happy hour is a bargain with house margs at five bucks. You can upgrade to a flavored marg or one with a smoked salt rim and mezcal float for just $1.50 more. There are several bites offered at great prices, and we did a mix of happy hour choices and some stuff from the regular menu. The house guacamole is really fresh and I enjoyed the bits of jalapeño throughout. Same with the chips and salsa, which comes with salsa verde and pico. I love options!   I tried the bacon and garlic shrimp tacos and found them to be overly salty and really messy. My husband went with the happy hour beef tacos which looked delicious.   I love the open and airy feel of the restaurant, especially with regards to our seats at the bar by the open windows. That said, a trip to the bathrooms revealed some pretty questionable cleanliness standards. I actually used both bathrooms and they were equally gross - like they had gone through the whole weekend without being cleaned.   Bathrooms aside, it was a mostly pleasant experience at Tio Flores and I'd gladly hit them up for happy hour again in the near future.

I really enjoyed lunch at CO-OP this week. The restaurant is incredibly beautiful. My friend and I were hoping to sit outside, and when we mentioned this to the hostess, she hit a button and the walls started to fold up into the building!   There were a lot of tasty-sounding dishes available for lunch, but I wanted to keep things relatively light with a salad. I ordered the kale salad with the dressing and blue cheese on the side. I also added avocado and grilled shrimp. The salad was quite large and very pretty. There was an entire half of perfectly-ripe avocado, which I loved! I wasn't so crazy about the green goddess dressing; it didn't really have much flavor. I'd order this salad again for sure, but perhaps with a vinaigrette, instead.   I told my husband last night that I really want to return for dinner sometime. And I'd be very interested to know whether or not they offer a happy hour. That's one I'd be willing to go out of my way for, mos def.

My husband and I decided to finally use a Starr gift card we had been sitting on for ages at Morimoto on Friday night. That was our first great decision, which was followed by many more.   We arrived and were led to a cozy little booth for two on the left wall. Our server came by with water and I mentioned that I wanted to start with something bubbly and described my preferences. He recommended the blanc de blancs which was perfection.   We started with the kumamoto and seasonal oysters, which came with six to the plate. The oysters were topped with three different sauces. The sauces were all nice, but I think I prefer a more traditional oyster plate with just some lemon and mignonette.   Next up was the hamachi with ponzu and jalapeño. Simple and delicious, this is always one of my favorite dishes at a Japanese restaurant. Next was the toro tartare. It is pricey. It is tiny. It is incredible! Nestled inside the small cup of an overly large plate is the tartare, flecked with crunchy tempura flakes and topped with caviar. The fresh wasabi used sparingly only enhanced the flavors.   For our mains, my husband opted for the soft shell crab special while I went for the Chilean sea bass. I can't comment on the special since I didn't try it, but my sea bass was increds. Served in a light broth with bright, crisp, seasonal vegetables and herbs, the fish was seared perfectly and the flavor was intensely buttery. The dish was super light yet felt completely satisfying because of the naturally rich flavors of the fish. The domaine de seailles sauvignon blanc that my server recommended was once again a perfect match.   In the end, our gift card only covered about half of our meal, but it was worth every penny. Well worth the splurge and a most excellent date night was had by both of us.

I just returned from lunch with Allison B at Milkboy and I'm already a fan. From the sweet servers, great and sometimes random (in a good way - Cornershop, anyone?) tunes and solid eats, what's not to like?  I arrived just before 12:30 and had my choice of available tables. Where was everyone? I selected a booth away from the busy open windows but still with a view of the street and got my coffee on. As I decided between a turkey wrap and a burrito, our server told us about the special, a roasted pork sandwich with tomatoes, sauteed spinach and a creole spread. I was sold. I requested a side salad in place of fries for two dollars more.   Our food arrived and the fries managed to sneak onto my plate, but after a quick mention to our server a side salad arrived shortly after. Allison's pickled veggie tempura was awesome, and her tomato bisque with croutons and cheese looked super tasty. My sandwich was great and although the fries looked tempting, I stuck to my guns and ate only the side salad, which was worth the upcharge. Allison confirmed that the fries were indeed delish. I'm definitely looking forward to return visits and checking out the upstairs area for live music.

It has long been lamented that we don't take advantage of our waterfront property, with the exception of maybe Festival Pier. The gorgeous remodeling of Pier 11 is a welcome sight. Hopefully this new addition will start a revival.   Walking towards the water on the upper level, you get the sensation that you are walking towards an edge with no barrier. On closer inspection, a row of steep steps/seats come into view, along with a smaller staircase on the left. Railings surrounding the pier are all angled, providing a comfortable place to stand and reflect.   Several benches and a few picnic tables are available, but alcohol may only be consumed with the use of a permit... so either conceal wisely or just bring some Ssips iced teas.   Very much looking forward to seeing this park in full swing during the hot summer months, and hoping it is only the beginning to a more beautiful waterfront experience.

My friend has been raving about The Couch Tomato for ages, so we met there for lunch last week. I love the various salad offerings or the option to create-your-own. We placed our order at the counter then grabbed a table outside.   I selected the salad with barbecue chicken, tomatoes, corn, black beans and cheddar. I got ranch dressing on the side. The salad was big, super-fresh, and really delicious. Since the chicken had a decent amount of sauce, I didn't need as much dressing, which I liked. My friend created his own salad but the toppings were a little skimpy, especially the quinoa - he ended up paying extra to get some more on the side.   Overall, very solid spot for a healthy lunch and I've heard the pizza is delicious as well. I'll definitely return when I'm lunching in Manayunk!

Great first experience with Body Restoration Spa! I called on a Friday night with low expectations of scoring a Saturday appointment, but I lucked out and was able to book a 75-minute aromatherapy session for 12:30pm.   I was surprised that Body Restoration's rates are higher on weekends. Also, all forms of massage are the same price, even deep tissue and sports massage. Definitely things to consider since I have a flexible schedule and could easily book a weekday appointment next time.       I arrived a bit early and had plenty of time to change into a soft robe and relax in the peaceful waiting area. The changing rooms are private which is really nice. At my appointment time I was greeted by my therapist, Denise, and taken to the room.   My massage was very relaxing. Sometimes it takes me a bit to fully ease into it, but before I knew it I was in a twilight sleep state and feeling great. The aromatherapy oils used were not as strong as what I have become accustomed to at my usual place. I think next time I might opt for a massage with more pressure, but for what I was going for on this visit, everything was just right.

I've been loving on this store from afar for quite some time, following their Instagram and plotting my purchases. I finally made it in and picked up the perfect Christmas gift for a friend. Meanwhile, my husband was taking notes, as he got me the most beautiful pair of earrings. Seriously, I'm obsessed.   The store has a great selection of new age-y crystals and stones, tarot cards, candles, and other assorted energy enhancers. There's also a ton of really beautiful jewelry, including some incredible vintage pieces.   I've recently subscribed to the newsletter and am very excited about the store's monthly horoscope and tarot reading sessions!

My husband and I met up with our friends at Frida Cantina for a quick drink before our dinner reservations at another nearby establishment. What a gem! The decor is bright, festive and inviting. Though we weren't there for very long, I was really impressed and can't wait to go back for a meal sometime soon!   We sat at the bar and the list of cocktails looked delicious. I wasn't drinking alcohol, so asked the bartender if I could possibly get something off the menu. He didn't hesitate and within a few seconds, I had a gorgeous hibiscus drink of my own, complete with a very tasty rim!   If the food is anything like the drinks, I will be very happy. Can't wait to return soon!

You would think that in our age of advanced technology, upgrading a phone would be a piece of cake. Unfortunately, this process always seems to take hours. I'll never understand it.   The bright side to my visit to this location on Saturday was the woman who helped me through, Yezenia. She calmly explained my options and answered my questions. I also felt that she really took the time to explore what packages would be best for me personally, based on my usage history. Not only did I leave with a new phone which I had to shell out $0 to receive after my trade-in, but my bill will also be less than what I was paying before because of the new plan offerings.   While the entire process did take over an hour to complete, Yezenia made it as painless as possible. Also, I'd like to give a shout out to the gentleman who helped me when I first walked in - I don't remember his name but he came across as honest and informed, which was appreciated.

I love this place! It's dark, it's cool, it's a welcome addition to a growing list of great businesses in the area.   Both of my visits to Second District have been at the end of my night after several libations. At that point I am usually nursing a pale ale or two and several glasses of water as I go in for the bites.   The chicken sandwich is fantastic and so are all of the snacks I've tried, particularly the pork rinds, wings and pickles.   Table service has been great - I had the same friendly server on both visits. Excellent addition to the Philly food and beverage scene!

My experience at Breakaway Bikes was brief but solid. My boyfriend bought me indoor cycling shoes for my bday but they were a tad small and also needed clips installed. They were quickly exchanged for the correct size and then they were fitted appropriately with the clips. I was told that if I have any problems with my ride, I can bring the shoes back and have the clips adjusted at any time. Sweet! Employees were friendly and helpful. Solid spot.

If the La Colombe in Rittenhouse and the one by City Hall were men, I'd choose the latter without a shred of uncertainty. Polar opposites, the City Hall location is newer, cleaner, brighter, cooler.   Despite less seating, the turnover was pretty fast during my afternoon visit on Thursday. Pastries looked decadent, and their coffee is my absolute fave. A water station with cold, sparkling and room temp options with real glasses was just perfect. I may plan all my meetings there.

I used to work at a custard stand when I was young, so I know better than to try any of the 20 flavors the sign on Kayla's Kustard Corner boasts. Those things are definitely a gimmick for kids.  That said, I went with one of my tried and true favorites the other night- vanilla and chocolate twist with chocolate jimmies. The cone was supposed to be the regular size, but it was enormous and I didn't even make leeway on the cone itself before throwing in the towel. With that said, I don't complain about being served too much ice cream. Nope, not this girl.  I have to agree with the other reviewer in that the chocolate was a bit texturized... It looked like little flecks of chocolate, which didn't bother me, but I liked the vanilla better, nonetheless. Next time I'll go with my true favorite, vanilla with rainbow jimmies.  It's not the best custard around, but it's not a bad option, either.    PS, For anyone wondering about the future of the garden center that was run by the same owner, I asked the other evening and, to my chagrin, they will only be offering mums on Easter and Mother's day.  Guess this means I'll be schlepping to Home Depot for my hanging basket gifts...

In all my years of drunk eating, I had never been to Lorenzo's before Saturday.  After a long night out, our crew ordered a pie which, to my shock and drunken delight, was so large it required TWO boxes!  Noticing the condiments on the counter, I opened the top box and started liberally sprinkling the pie with... something.  We discovered soon after that the something was garlic powder.  Oops!  We enjoyed a very garlicky pizza that tasted like the food of the gods at the time, if a tad potent.    Sober reflection tells me that the pizza was tasty but undercooked.  The one remaining slice in my fridge will be reheated in the oven for lunch today, providing some much-needed crunchiness.  It should be noted, this is probably the first time in history that I have ever had leftovers from late-night eating.  Lorenzo's, I salute you!

I looooove Plenty on East Passyunk Avenue, so I was absolutely stoked when their new location on Spruce Street finally opened last week. I parked the car illegally and stood watch while my partner in crime ran inside for breakfast sandwiches.   My choice was the pancetta hash, with two fried eggs, pancetta, breakfast potatoes, and fontina. We got home and tore open our packages. Mine came in a cardboard to-go box, and when I opened the lid the first thing I noticed was the pool of egg yolk covering the entire bottom of the box, leaving the whole underside of my sandwich completely soaked and really messy. Meanwhile, the roll was really tough and also very large, and it overpowered (what was left of) the ingredients in the sandwich. If you do feel compelled to order the pancetta hash to go after reading this, be sure to order it with scrambled eggs.   This was my first time ordering breakfast at Plenty; normally I have sandwiches and almost always the tasso ham panini, which is incredible. I'm looking forward to swinging by again soon, and hopefully updating my review once that happens.

Normally, cocktails and dessert wouldn't bring me to five-star territory, or even review territory, but my experience at Stateside tonight was just that good. We nabbed two seats at the bar before the restaurant got crowded. Over the next couple hours, free seats were sparse, and people came and went when there was nothing available, with a few that got lucky at the right time.   As we watched the bartender (Jen) whisk drinks together, the smells were simply intoxicating. The Hot Butter Rye was too aromatic to pass up, so the boyfriend went for it. Literally made with butter, brown sugar, rye, whipped cream and other delicious ingredients,  I stole sips whenever possible, praying the calories per sip weren't too horrendous. Meanwhile, my Gasparilla was like a wintry version of a rum-infused creamsicle. Delicious.   We also tried the smoked chocolate ganache dessert, topped with sea salt and served over creamy marshmallow and graham crackers. The warm sugared doughnut with maple bacon syrup was equally fantastic. La Colombe coffee is served at Stateside.  We couldn't bring ourselves to call it quits, so we went for one more round. Clover Clubs had just the right bite of gin but enough other flavors to round out the sharpness. Drinks are very reasonably priced, and I'd even go so far to say one of the best deals on quality cocktails in the city. And with pleasant, smart service like Jen's, a trip to Stateside's bar will be a no-brainer in the future.   My only regret? Calling it a night and asking for our check moments before David Ansill sat down next to us. Surely that would have made the evening even more interesting.

Never had a sit-down dinner here, but I remember the bar food being good from a happy hour I went to a year or so ago.  Went last night and threw back a pretty delish sangria like nobody's business.  The server told me what was in it but after the second or third alcohol he mentioned, I lost track.  There was definitely burgundy wine in there somewhere and at least one type of brandy.    The upstairs bar area is super cute but tiny~ so get there early after work if you want a table near the kick-ass windows that overlook Chestnut.

I took the Yin Yoga class with Barbara on a cold Friday night in December. Yoga is one of those things I have a love/hate relationship with; I'm not very flexible, so poses don't come easily for me. In fact, I'm often so tight that it's hard for me to even get into or hold poses. This gentle yoga class is perfect for runners and weight lifters who need to loosen up and stretch those muscles.   The thing I loved most about this class in particular is that it is a candlelit class, so the room is dark and only lit by flickering candles. It made me feel less self conscious as I was struggling through poses. I really enjoyed how Barbara walked around and offered corrections and soothing words. Also, the studio has everything you need, from blankets to straps and blocks. I brought my own mat but it was nice to have everything else available.   Looking forward to getting back for another class when my schedule allows!

I love this place for a healthy lunch! The employees are very efficient to the point of making me feel super rushed - be sure to know exactly what you want when it's your turn in line! That said, even when the line is long you know you won't have much of a wait, so that is the plus side.   It's taken me a few visits to figure out the lay of the land, but my go-to is usually a greens and lentils bowl with chicken, topped with hummus, tzatziki, and harissa, plus an assortment of fresh veggie toppings and kalamata olives. I usually get a sauce on the side but often don't need it because everything in the bowl is flavorful enough on its own.

My grandmom has been talking up this diner for a while, so I had to take her out for lunch to see what the fuss was about. We went on a Friday and the restaurant was pretty busy.   The menu stands up to any other Jersey diner. It's several pages long and loaded with options. How do they do it? I'll never know. I decided to go basic and had a bacon, cheddar and tomato omelet with hashbrowns and toast. It was a huge plate of food and the hashbrowns were perfectly crispy! My grandmom had a turkey club which came with soup and dessert, so that was also a massive meal. She swapped onion rings for fries and they were quite delish.   My only suggestion would be for the servers to stop by the table a few minutes after food is delivered, just to make sure everything is correct, drinks are filled, etc.   Naturally, Gram had coupons so the meal total before tip was under $25. Such a steal! I think this is our new go-to for lunches out together.

I am hooked. Since my last review, not only did I lower my regular gym membership, but I actually decided to terminate my membership completely. Nothing came close the to the workouts I receive at Flywheel. The classes and instructors, quality of the bikes, wide variety of class times, and themed rides at Flywheel are unmatched.   If you had told me a year ago that I would regularly spend $20-$25 on single spin classes, I would have said you were crazy. But that was before my introduction to Flywheel. And now, for us frequent fly-ers, there's a $180/month membership option which entitles members to unlimited classes. In my first month alone, I hit twelve, which works out to $15 per class, making my membership completely worthwhile. While still pricey, I've decided that I can make some cutbacks to my other expensive habits (food, drinks, nails, shopping, etc.) in order to fit Flywheel into my life. I'm more than willing to sacrifice a few cocktails each week in exchange for a toned, fit body.

The diner-style seating and Greek grandma-ladies behind the counter kicked things off to a promising start during stop three of an Old City pizza crawl. Homemade desserts called from behind a display window, but it was the pies we were after. Pizza pies.   A slice of cheese and a slice with crumbled sausage were placed on our table, hot from the oven. This pizza had so much potential, with a nice crunch to the entire crust and the delicious crumbled sausage. Alas, the cheese had no oozy stretch. As my boyfriend later recounted to friends, "government cheese laughed at this cheese."

Yesterday I popped in to try on some jeans since I'd heard about Madewell's denim exchange program. It's a promotion going on through the end of the year where you can bring in any pair of old jeans to donate (jeans are used for housing insulation for those in need) and receive $20 off a new pair from Madewell. Their jeans are pretty pricey so I was all about this deal, especially after hearing rave reviews about Madewell's denim.   I gathered tons of clothes to try on and was helped by Sophia, who pulled other items that were similar to things I was already trying on, which I loved. She also gave honest feedback - I wasn't pressured into anything I knew was not right. I ended up with just one pair of jeans and one sale tee, but I loved both pieces. And I cleaned out five pairs of old jeans from my closet in the process, so there's that. Love this store!

Let it be known: I love brunch.  If I could shout it from the rooftops, I would.  However, my reluctance to try new places because of the fear of being disappointed has led me to the same handful of spots over and over.  On a beautiful Sunday morning, the cycle was broken when my brekkie qualifiers included: the need for ample street parking, a liquor license and possible outdoor seating.  North Third fit the bill, but would it deliver where it counted the most (in my tummy)?  Answer: Hells to the yes!  It was just early enough that there was still plenty of available real estate both inside and out.  My party of two was seated at one of the sidewalk tables on the less-chaotic Brown side, which was perfect as Third Street had some real claustrophobia potential, with so many people out and about on such an uncharacteristically warm morning.    Waters were dropped off immediately and our request for coffee and bloody marys was met soon after.  The BMs were spicy and flavorful, and came with an array of garnishes that included celery, cucumber, dill pickle, cherry tomato, olive and lemon.  The many choices on both the regular and special menus had me deciding between three or four plates that each sounded fantastic.  In the end, I opted for my original craving, huevos rancheros.    In what was probably the fastest turnaround time ever, our dishes arrived.  The plates were loaded with picture perfect breakfasts.  My huevos were spot on and nailed my craving, and my dining companion's homemade cheddar biscuits with sausage gravy were realllllly good.  I resisted the urge to pull the old, "hey, what's that?!" while swiping half a biscuit off the plate.    North Third has officially been inducted to the brunch rotation, and I look forward to checking out the scene during the wee hours as well.

Someone - anyone - tell me what I should be ordering here. Because I want to love this place. The grocery section is just perfect for any last minute picnic or dinner party item (or even just something quick for lunch), the workers are always very friendly, and the ingredients are always so fresh.   But every time I try Pumpkin Market, I end up disappointed. After my initial visit back in December, I stopped by again for a breakfast burrito. I found it to be a bit bland and on the small side for the price. Today I returned and the pork bánh mi caught my attention. I asked for the aioli on the side so I could go sparingly. Back home, I tore open the foil to reveal a very pretty sandwich, quite large, and with tons of veggies poking out from all sides.   Then I took a bite into the fattiest piece of pork I've encountered in quite some time. Thinking it was a fluke, I separated the sandwich so I could pull off any other fatty pieces... and ended up taking off more than half of the meat. Straight fat. Isn't roast pork usually pretty lean or am I crazy (or worse, am I that girl who takes all the nice lean bits at a party, leaving the fat for everyone else?)?   The abundance of veggies was nice, but there wasn't much pickled flavor. The actual pickle that came alongside helped. And the aioli was very tasty. But I'm pretty sure what was supposed to be cilantro on the sammie was actually mint. Scratch that, I'm positive it was mint.  As I said, I want to love this place. It's one of the few spots in the area that does quick lunch to go. But for the love of God, someone tell me what to order already!

Cheers to Little Fish for offering a few unique options for take out that are vastly different from a lot of other restaurants. Obviously, we're a bit limited at the moment, so trying something new and exciting was a treat. My husband and I splurged and ordered two of the hamachi rice bowls - I managed to get the last two of the day! The guy who took my order over the phone was very nice. Once I arrived to the restaurant, I called and the bag was brought out right away.   The bowls were put together nicely and everything was fresh. I think next time I might opt for one of the bento boxes for more variety.   It had been ages since my last visit to Little Fish and I look forward to going back for a full meal when possible.

Sugared + Bronzed is my new go-to. I had tried a sugaring service in Manhattan earlier this year, and liked it so much more than waxing. But I wasn't aware of any reputable places in Philly and, to be honest, I never really looked. It was by chance that I came across S+B - I was actually looking up the phone number for another salon I occasionally visit. That's when I noticed the listing for this business and the amazing reviews. I booked my appointment on the spot.   I'm a huge baby when it comes to anything that might be painful, so I took advil an hour before my appointment. The woman at the front desk was so sweet and we chatted while I filled out paperwork and waited for my turn in the torture chamber.   The appointment rooms are very clean and actually comfortable. I love love love that they use more of a fabric cover for the table, instead of a paper one. So much nicer!   The esthetician who did my service was Brittany and I loved her. She calmed my nerves and we chatted away and, before I knew it, the whole thing was over. The pain, while still there, was minimal compared with waxing.  The best part of all is that new clients get a buy one get one free deal. You pay the first time and then you can book your second visit on the spot. Great way for the biz to earn loyal customers and great on my wallet. So happy I found this place!

What started as love at first sight went slowly downhill into lukewarm feelings territory. I arrived at Audrey Claire before my BYO girls and had a seat at the table while my wine was opened and water glass filled. The first thing I noticed was that the table was slightly higher than most, meaning there was plenty of room for me to comfortably cross my legs. It may sound silly but I can't sit down without crossing my legs, which happen to take up a lot of me, so this was a huge plus.   When my friends arrived, we enlisted the help of our server to guide us towards the right menu choices. We started with the grilled octopus salad and the arugula and goat cheese salad. The first salad was nice, but the arugula and goat cheese salad was simply heaven. I need this salad in my life, and I do plan to return soon, if only for that salad.   I was torn between the potato crusted tuna and the crispy chive crusted sole, but I eventually chose the sole. As did a friend. Our other friend was smart and got something different - a pork chop, served with bacon-topped asparagus and mashed potatoes. The plate was cleaned except for the bone. The sole dish was disappointing. While seasoned well, the fish was absolutely drowning in butter or oil (or both? I couldn't tell which). As were the green beans alongside, which were otherwise very plain. Then there was the side of pearl pasta that lacked anything resembling flavor. My friend and I both decided it wasn't worth the calories... and it's rare that I leave something on my plate.   I was underwhelmed by the entrees but optimistic that a fantastic dessert could really bring back some points. Alas, the check was dropped and we were never asked if we wanted dessert. Bummer.

Sorry, Cava, but it's time for a downgrade. I visit this location every so often and the quality has gone down over my past few stops. The food station area is always very messy. The employees, while efficient, aren't very friendly. It's clear that you are expected to do your part in ordering quickly to move things along, and yet, nothing is labeled so how would a first timer (or even an occasional customer) know what anything is without asking a hundred questions?   I often order the grilled chicken which isn't always lean and/or trimmed, which can be gross. Other than that, the other ingredients are always fresh and tasty. I also really like the option of lentils for something different, and I dig the lentil and supergreens mix as a base.   Hopefully, some improvements will be made to the customer service and also the tidiness of the food station.

Vegan chocolate frozen yogurt that tastes just like chocolate soft serve... and is 220 calories for quite a large cup. What's up.   (Skip the swirl - the vanilla cashew is really grainy. But maybe that's your thing. If so, keep on keepin' on you grainy ice cream lover, you.)

This Staples was surprisingly crowded when I stopped in for a print job last week. There was one person working the printing center and several people waiting on projects. Once I made it to the front of the line, my printing was handled quickly and I was happy with the results.   Then I moved over to the registers where two employees were handling customers very slowly. Mid-afternoon Staples runs should not be so time consuming!

Welcome to the 'hood, Tria! After the super sad news that Dmitri's would be leaving their Fitler Square home, the only thing that numbed the pain was the announcement of Tria moving in.   I've swung by twice now and both nights were poppin'. Of course, the wine program is on point and the servers are super hospitable and very well-versed in their knowledge of the grapes (and everything else).   On the food menu, I loved seeing some of my Tria favorites (warm bean dip, asparagus and white bean salad) plus some new, heartier fare thanks to the full kitchen. My bae Aaliyah P and I split the aforementioned salad and some mushroom tagliatelle and that pasta was to-die. It was actually a very nice portion to split after the salad (I could totally clean house on that pasta myself on a hungrier night, however). I can't wait to try everything else on the dinner menu!

My two friends and I started our girls' night at Figs on Friday evening.  The small byo was packing them in, including a large party of very loud college kids, armed with wine in a jug.  Since it was so crowded, the room was pretty warm, but the only source of fresh air came from the open front door.  Last time I checked, open doors are usually an invitation to bugs, and unfortunately there was no exception at Figs.  It wasn't so bad, but it could have been avoided with a simple ac wall unit.  Times are tough and all, but come on.  Other than that, the experience was good.  Our appetizers were tasty (spinach and feta phyllo triangles and a mozzarella and tomato salad with fig vinaigrette).  I really liked my dinner, a salmon and shrimp special in a roasted red pepper sauce with spinach and garlic mash, but my friends didn't seem crazy about theirs.  My completely empty plate and their slightly picked over plates was proof of this.  We were all in agreement that dessert was the best part of the meal.  We shared a chocolate mousse, baklava and an apple tart.  Each was fantastic.    We agreed to return sometime for dessert, but unfortunately I don't think we'll be back for dinner.

I've been loving Bakeshop on 20th for quick and healthy breakfast delivery every now and then. I love the egg white wrap with feta, tomatoes and spinach. So tasty! I also tried the avocado toast recently, which was absolutely delish as well.   I'm not as big of a fan of going in to the shop. It's so tiny and gets super crowded. I also find them rather expensive. An avocado toast, salmon avocado toast special, and four largish pastries somehow set me back to the tune of fifty dollars last weekend (plus tip, for the super sweet gentleman working that Sunday). I'm still scratching my head over that one, and I'm clearly not over it.   I'll be sticking with the breakfast bites, but will be purchasing bulk pastries elsewhere in the future!

Okay DaMò, I see you!   This place has been on my radar for a while, but we don't order Italian for takeout super often. After a long and chilly day, I was craving comfort food. My husband suggested DaMò which sounded just right.   We each ordered small pastas (mine was the casarecce arrabbiata and his was a custom creation with tonnarelli and bolognese sauce). We also ordered the caprese salad and a piece of focaccia. The caprese was small and the tomatoes were just okay. For $14, we'll pass on this dish in the future. The focaccia, however, was fantastic. Going to have to double that order next time!   Both pastas were great and exactly what we were expecting. The small portion size was perfect for both of us; I even had a little bit left over for the next day. Adding DaMò to our takeout/delivery rotation for sure!

Walk into this bar and walk back in time to when dark lounges with kitschy decor ruled all. There wasn't enough time during my stay to take in all the fabulous sculptures, trinkets, paintings and more.  While there was a nice selection of cocktails, my crew of ladies kept things simple with a few rounds of beer. We also sampled a couple items from the menu - the mac and cheese which was unreal and the potato and celery root latkes which were very tasty as well. I ordered a chicken parm sandwich to go for my man and the takeout bag must have weighed about five pounds.   And how about that bar staff?! What a bunch of crafty, fine-looking individuals!   Franky Bradley's is about to become my spot, and I'm not the only one. Mayor Nutter and his posse rolled in during my visit and word is, that wasn't his first time, either. I look forward to my upcoming dance-off with the mayor once the upstairs opens up.

While I'm tempted to click 2 stars for "I've experienced better," I can't, because that would be a lie. The bánh mi I ate for lunch yesterday was, in fact, my first bánh mi ever, so I have nothing to compare it to.   Perhaps my expectations were too high? I don't know. I walked in and immediately confessed that I had never tried a bánh mi before, and so I wanted to know my options. Barbecue pork sounded best to me, so I went with that. I asked the woman if they put paté on their rolls (because if they did I would have asked for it without), and she told me they use butter. I thought that sounded weird but what did I know?  I got my sammie home and inspected. The meat looked so-so... not the sliced pork I anticipated but more like quick fried pork you would see in Chinese take-out. The veggies looked fresh and crisp, but they were sparse. The roll was crispy on the outside as I expected, but the butter oozed on the inside, which was kinda gross. I cut the roll in half and transferred all the ingredients onto one half.   I was starving by the time I ate, so the sandwich provided sustenance. I love the concept, but I didn't love my lunch. I will go forth and try other bánh mi, but I'll probably check out some other places.

I'll start with the good: the staff. While our group brunch was a pretty big fail (more on that in a moment), I can say our server did his best to keep us as happy as possible. Also, after we closed out our checks and moved to the outside area, the bartenders outside were super friendly and fun and just awesome overall.   Back to the brunch. My friend made reservations for about twelve people several weeks ago. We were pumped about a rosé brunch with DJs, and the menu looked awesome. Once our group was seated with drinks, we decided to order. This was around 3:15. The first dish to arrive was a random side plate with two eggs. Those eggs sat by themselves on the table for quite some time before the first complete dishes started to trickle out. And I do mean trickle. It was around 4 when the first plates started arriving. Unfortunately, there would be 5-10 minute lapses between the arrival of dishes. The people who had food started eating because the lag time was ridiculous. The last plates arrived around 4:25. Not acceptable.   On top of this, the food just wasn't good. My friend ordered a benedict which first arrived with a bursting yolk which had cooked itself into scrambled eggs. Frankly, it was gross. She sent it back and received a second benny which was still a bit overcooked though the eggs were intact.   A girl two seats down passed me what we thought was my dish, a seafood omelet. It looked more like an overcooked scramble but I started to eat it anyway. That's when our server arrived with an actual omelet. He said what I had was actually the huevos rancheros, which was impossible because it had all of the ingredients of the seafood omelet and none of the ingredients of huevos rancheros. But, I took the omelet, anyway, because it looked a lot more appetizing. The dish was not great by any means but it wasn't awful either, so I ate most of it. My husband was one of the last to receive a dish - the infamous huevos rancheros. There were two overcooked eggs, no tortilla, no avocado (just a side of sad, brownish guacamole), and his "bacon hash" was actually just breakfast potatoes with a piece of bacon on top.   I haven't had a food experience this bad in Philly in I don't know how long. The fact that it was the experience of everyone at our table, across the board, is really telling about whatever is happening in the kitchen.  The DJ was pretty great and the rosé specials were very solid. But that's not enough to get me back to this place for another outing.

With some colleagues in town from Yelp's San Francisco and New York offices, I knew I wanted to impress with my dinner selection. I rolled the dice with The Treemont, since I had never been, and it worked in my favor!   We started at the bar with wine and cocktails. The complimentary popcorn is delicious! I could have happily munched on that all night long. But, we headed upstairs to our table and began our feast. To start, chickpea fritters, charred squid and squid ink gnudi. The fritters were light and fun, the squid worked really well with everything else on the plate, but the gnudi with brown butter and raisins were off. the. hook. I wouldn't think twice about ordering that dish again. And not sharing.  My dining companions seemed very happy with their fluke entrees. I went with the strip steak and was surprised to receive two large hunks of beef instead of, well, sliced strips of steak. I would have preferred the latter. I really liked the barley and mushrooms on the plate, and the red wine sauce was nice. I thought this dish went well with the lemony crushed potatoes.   While I didn't partake in the desserts, they went over well with our group. I'm interested to see the next version of the menu and I'd definitely like to return.

This place is awesome. I had heard about The 700 but it took me a helluva long time to actually get there. We swung through last Friday on a whim and grabbed some drinks downstairs before heading up to the "living room" dance party area. Drinks were very reasonably priced, and there was a variety that covered everything from cheap swill to schmancier libations.   Once upstairs, it didn't take long for the dance floor to fill up. This place gets packed very quickly, so my advice would be to get there early and claim your spot on the floor. The DJ was great, at first playing a random mix of Queen, Blondie and other old school tunes, then tapering into the more mainstream stuff that got the youngins excited. I was glad when the DJ brought back a mix that included some older stuff. I like to booty pop like the rest of them but after a while, every bubble butt song starts to sound exactly the same.   Before I got onto the dance floor, I actually thought the place was well air conditioned. But the moment I started dancing that was not the case. But as a friend told me, "If you don't leave with your hair plastered to your face, you're doing it wrong." And I agree.

My first visit to this Sweetgreen location was just okay. The food was great - my kale Caesar salad was delicious and I have been enjoying the butternut squash soup on the fall menu. My issues were with the cleanliness of the restaurant - there were flies everywhere near the produce behind the main prep area - and the lack of basic essentials - no napkins, no salt and pepper packets or shakers, etc. They were also out of turkey, which is featured in a bunch of their fall salads.   This is a brand new Sweetgreen location. Get it together!

Friendly employees who patiently answered all of my questions, and a super cute storefront, made a great first impression for my first visit to Prescription Chicken.   I'd had a large breakfast sandwich just a couple hours prior, so I wasn't feeling anything too heavy for lunch. That, and the fact that I'm saddled with a cold, made Prescription Chicken the obvious choice. The main soups are broth-based and you can get regular chicken, vegetarian broth, or another broth called the hangover. It's got a little kick and has some extra herbs to help cure what ails ya. There were also a few specialty soups that all sounded great!   Alisha S and I were offered little samples of both the regular chicken broth and the hangover. The latter had a little heat but it was just the right amount. Soups come with a choice of egg noodles, matzo balls, or both. I'm not big on noodles in soup (I know, super weird, right?) so I went for the matzo balls. I'm typically not a huge fan of those either but, I have to say, Prescription Chicken's version were just right!    I did find the veggies in the soup to be on the borderline of too crunchy (though I'd prefer this over being too soft) and some of the chicken pieces were a little too big, making for some awkward bites. I also thought the prices were a bit high - two pints of soup and two bottled waters came to nearly $20 with tax. They weren't served with crackers or bread or anything extra. That said, I feel like Philly is lacking in the soup department so Prescription Chicken is a welcome addition. I can definitely see myself grabbing some soup to go and picking up a baguette for dinner in the colder months.

Yay Animo! When I heard my favorite healthy lunch spot in Jersey was opening in Philly, I was absolutely joyous. I LOVE this place. From fresh juice to salads, burritos, and chilly gorillas, you can rest easy knowing that everything is fresh and free of additives and other junk. I even find delicious things to eat at Animo when I'm doing detoxes.   I stopped in the other day with intentions of ordering the burrito plato, which is one of my favorite things at their Haddonfield location. It's basically the ingredients of a burrito, but on a plate so there's less carbs involved. At the Philly location, they are instead offering burrito bowls, meaning you can order any of the customized burritos in a bowl. It took me a minute to find the one that most resembles the burrito plato I know and love, but the cashier was super sweet and didn't give me a hard time for not knowing exactly what I wanted the second I got to the register. My burrito bowl was delicious and kept me going until dinner.   If only Animo had been where it is back when I used to work across the street. Still, I don't mind trekking across the city if it means I get some Animo. Oh, and one more thing: never forget the hot sauce. It's the best tasting hot sauce ever.

Class by class, I am becoming addicted to Flywheel. The facility is brand new, clean and well-maintained. Staff members spray off the bikes after each and every class and the bathrooms and private shower rooms are always spotless and well-stocked with the essentials. I actually took advantage of the shower room one night after class when I had dinner plans nearby. I brought my own towel and toiletries, not knowing what to expect. Turned out, I over-packed. Towels, shampoo, conditioner and body wash are provided (Bliss brand!), plus disposable razors, q-tips, spray deodorant and other essentials, just in case you forget to bring your own. There are even plastic bags for wet gym clothes, which is great.   The staff is awesome. Hayley leads the charge and her energy is infectious. Everyone I've encountered is friendly and encouraging. They love their jobs and it shows. Of course, this extends to the instructors. I've only experienced two so far, but I keep going back to Emily's classes. She's energetic and motivating the whole way through those brutal forty-five minutes. And I mean brutal in the very best way. During a Flywheel class, you will be pushed the entire time, ensuring an awesome workout. Torq and RPM numbers on each bike are great for knowing where exactly you should be at any given moment. There's even an arm workout with a weighted bar.  Reservations for classes open every Sunday. You receive an email and any special classes that week are mentioned. Last night, I hit up Emily's "crunk" class, which featured southern hip hop throwbacks. Everyone was encouraged to dress for the theme and we received a glow bracelet when we arrived. Pure Fare and Vita Coco provided refreshments after class, which was a nice touch.   The only drawback I can think of is the cost of classes, which range from $20 to $25 a pop. The more you purchase at a time, the less the cost per class. It's by far the most expensive workout I've ever considered (I'm currently using a complimentary promotional pass). But honestly, I like the classes so much that I've been thinking about lowering my membership level at my regular gym, to help offset the cost of future classes at Flywheel. They do have a refer-a-friend program, which is cool. I may start channeling my inner saleswoman because I really want to work Flywheel into my budget. If you like indoor cycling and a challenge, this is a workout you should definitely check out!

I'm back at Sweat after a year at City Fitness, followed by several loyal years at Flywheel. I'll never stop loving my Flywheel, but I started to realize that if I wanted to change my body, I would have to do more than just cardio.   When the opportunity for me to try SweatX classes for free in February arrived, I jumped at the chance. The classes are offered at the Queen Village Sweat by an awesome team of trained professionals. The classes combine weight lifting techniques with HIIT. While I ultimately decided that these classes weren't the right fit for me, I did enjoy feeling stronger, and knew I wanted to continue weight training, so I signed on with Sweat.   Although it's not the most convenient, Queen Village is my preferred location. It's huge, clean, attractive, and has lots of class options. I love that the cardio equipment is in a quieter area upstairs overlooking the street below, offering a bird's eye view during an indoor run. However, when I became a member, I received two free personal training sessions at the Fitler Square location, closer to where I live. This is the location I used as a Sweat member 5+ years ago.   I have to admit, not much has changed since then. To put it simply, this gym has seen better days. It's unattractive and tight. The wall to wall windows facing Walnut Street on street level can make you feel like a zoo attraction. While the equipment and machines are fine (and constantly being cleaned, which is good), the entire place could really use a facelift. Starting with the locker rooms, which are outdated, ugly, stained, beat-up, etc. Sweat Fitler Square is about as no frills as you can possibly get when it comes to a gym.    So why the upgrade? Two words: Jamel Harris. Jamel gets ten stars, as far as I'm concerned. I've been training with him for about a month and a half and I'm very pleased with my results so far. He pushes me hard, corrects my form, and takes notes during our sessions so that I can continuously improve. He varies our workouts so I never know what to expect, and I always leave feeling spent but stronger. Best of all, Jamel has a great personality and attitude and I'm constantly laughing, which brings a level of enjoyment to the pain.  Shout outs also to the rest of the staff, who also deserve many more stars than the gym facility itself. Everyone is friendly and laid-back, which makes for a nice community feel.

My crew of ladies started our Friday girls' night out at Noche.  The place was crowded (but not overly so) around 7:30.  We grabbed a booth (which are very poorly constructed, I might add--unless reclining into your neighbor's table is supposed to happen) and ordered some nachos and a pitcher of beer.  Had we arrived earlier, we would have been able to take advantage of the buy one get one pizzas and half priced apps.  Luckily, Noche's nachos were worth their regular price.  The mountain of chips (some of which were a little browned from the oven--my favorite!) with cheese, chicken, jalapenos, sour cream, black beans, salsa and guacamole was the perfect meal to kick off the weekend.  Our server kept our pitchers a-coming, and the experience as a whole was pleasant.    One thing I don't get is the pool table.  It takes up way too much real estate, and it's almost impossible to get to either the juke box or bathroom without being speared in the kidney by a pool stick.

I've never reviewed Santucci's?!?! Wow. This is our go-to pizza place. Only most of the time, we don't go, we just order. Their delivery has always been fast and accurate. The square pizza is definitely unique in that the crust is much thinner than a typical Sicilian pie and it is topped with a thin layer of mozzarella first, and zesty sauce on top of that. The best topping we've tried is the sausage. It has a great flavor and always gets slightly crisp on top. Meatball pies are great too, but the meatballs have a distinct spice to them, something along the lines of nutmeg. So if that's not your thing, take note.   The Caesar salad is decent, but I always forget that their dressing is super creamy yet not very flavorful. I don't taste the saltiness or brine from anchovies at all whenever I have their Caesar. I actually prefer the house dressing that comes with the side salads. Sandwiches are awesome, and in addition to the good old cheesesteak, they also serve a garlic bread cheesesteak. Giddy up!   The boyfriend is a bit taken aback that I'm only giving four stars here, but I'm a Jersey girl and I know there's better pizza to be had right across the bridge. But I will go as far to say that this is the best pizzeria-style pie in Philly.

Egads.  Where to begin?  I'll start with the line outside, which stretched halfway down the block towards 16th, and moved at a glacial pace.  Some loudmouths walking down the street screamed out to the crowd, "You're waiting in line for Mad River Part 2!"  Never a good sign as I loathe Mad River (Ladder 15 is partially owned by some of the Mad River owners, so to be fair, I knew this going in).  Thankfully, one of the ladies in our group knew someone, and we only had to stand outside for a few moments until we were ushered into the bar.    The bar was crowded with mostly twentysomethings, many of whom looked to be leftover from happy hour.  The décor was decent, but nothing I had never seen before, although I did like the balcony-type area that ran along the left wall and up over the back.  Our crew stationed ourselves near the back bar, which is located near the two single stall bathrooms.  It was in this area that I started to observe some shady goings-on.  On multiple occasions, I witnessed groups of two popping into the bathrooms.  Not so suspect with girls, but the twosomes I am referring to were guys.  30 seconds and they were out. Meanwhile, one of the owners looked on from the vicinity.  This would not be a complete review without a quick mention of the poor attitudes of the female bartenders.  It was hard to tell which of the two looked more miserable.  The half smiles they attempted looked painful.  Maybe they both underwent recent jaw surgery?  I spoke with another friend over the weekend who had also stopped by Ladder 15 on the same evening, but during happy hour.  She said the burger was possibly better than Good Dog's, but the rest of the menu was uninspiring.  While I am curious about the burger, I don't think I'm curious enough to return to this establishment, and I certainly wouldn't wait in that horrific line just to gain entry.

I've now dined at Opa twice - once for dinner and once for lunch - and I really enjoy the restaurant a lot. While we do have a few options for Greek/Mediterranean food in the city, I can't think of another place that does it as stylishly as Opa. The decor and the cocktail selection bring the swankiness, while the food speaks for itself.   The spreads trio is my favorite starter. It comes with hot, delicious pita but also some veggies for dipping, which is great for anyone who wants a little bite without a ton of calories. Each spread packs loads of flavor, and I especially love the tzatziki.   For dinner, you really can't go wrong with ordering a bunch of smaller plates and sharing them all. That's what my boyfriend and I did during our evening at Opa. The mini lamb gyros are delicious. At lunch, the chicken gyro is lighter than a burger but loaded on taste. A side of dressed greens can also be swapped for fries.   Anyone with a sweet tooth will enjoy the dessert course. Two varieties of coffee are offered plus a couple dessert cocktails and about four or so desserts. I've tried the baklava which I am always a fan of, and have heard several raves about the loukoumades (fried dough with dipping sauces).   It won't be long before I'm craving those spreads and gyros once again!

Do you see the photo of the flowers that arrived at my apartment last weekend?! They were absolutely beautiful!   The arrangement was sent from my fabulous friend Aimee from St. Louis. She told me she sort of just picked a place and ordered. I was stunned when I realized the business didn't have any reviews on Yelp already. The flowers were just so pretty and perfect for spring and the occasion itself (my recent engagement!).   If you're looking for a Philadelphia flower delivery, give Philadelphia Flower a shout. They know how to pick some beautiful blooms.

After taking nearly fifty Flywheel classes, you'd think I would have stopped into the deli that shares the same breezeway at least once, but nope! It wasn't until last night that I decided to check them out for a quick meal to go after class.   Despite my ravenous appetite, I wanted to keep things relatively healthy. I ordered a wrap with turkey, turkey bacon, lettuce and tomato. It came with a side so I picked coleslaw, and once I got home I added it to my wrap. Delish!   I asked if there would be a pickle on the side (not leaving a deli without one!) and the cashier gave me a bag to take back to the pickle bar. YES.   The menu is pretty large and I'm especially excited by the mashed potatoes. I don't know, I just really love some taters so I'm really down with the potential to grab some to go.

My husband and his friends keep returning to Otis & Pickles in deep South Philly for beers, eats and hockey game-watching. Last week I decided to meet up with the crew to see what the fuss was about.   I really liked the industrial chic look and the chill vibes. The bartender, Vince, was super friendly and fun to chat with during our stay. I was drinking wine earlier in the night so planned to stick with that, but Vince wasn't sure if any wine was available. He did manage to come up with a bottle of chardonnay, which was fine with me at that point in the night. If you're not super choosy about your wine selection, you can probably grab a glass here. But if you're a wine snob and/or don't drink beer or mixed drinks this is not going to be your spot.   I was feeling a little peckish and ordered the fried pickles. Vince let me know that these weren't going to be traditional fried pickles but a medley of different vegetables. The mix consisted of jalapeños (whoo spicy!), string beans and onions. They were all right but I'd prefer traditional fried pickles. I also nabbed a few of my husband's french fries which were perfection, especially dipped into the side sauce served alongside.   I'm definitely feeling this place and look forward to going back and trying more of the menu!

I'm torn between three and four stars for my first experience with Real Food Eatery. I've been wanting to try it for a while and finally decided to place a delivery order on one of a small handful of days last week when I opted for healthy foods over carbs, cheese, more carbs and alcohol. The holidays, am I right?   I love the variety of choices for mains and sides. Don't like beets? No problem, there's about six other sides to select from. I went with salmon over brown rice, with sides of kale and mushrooms and parmesan broccoli. I also ordered a side of roasted apples.   The food arrived and I was very happy with the size of the platter. I wanted to eat healthy but I didn't want to go to bed hungry. I will say that the piece of salmon was minuscule, but perfectly cooked. The kale and mushroom side was extremely salty but was a bit more balanced when I ate it together with the rice. The apples were a perfect sweet treat with zero guilt.   I'll definitely give Real Food another try when I need something healthy but don't feel like cooking.

My husband and I were super excited to check out The Met for John Oliver's first night in Philadelphia. My husband is a born and raised Philadelphian and he never believed that he'd see the day when this majestic building would be made whole again. It's really pretty impressive how the restorations came together.   That said, I do wish some consideration would have gone into the comfort of the seating. The rows are very close together and our knees were touching the seat backs in front of us. After nearly two hours, I couldn't wait to get out of those chairs!   Staff members were hit or miss; some were friendly (ushers/bartenders) while others were super gruff (security).  The sound at our show was great and we had a great view to the stage even though we were seated in the loge area on the third level.    Very happy to see this Philly icon get a second life and I'm sure we'll be back.

After hearing how gorgeous the new Dandelion Pub was from friends, I was extra stoked to have dinner plans there just a couple days after the opening. The space was indeed pretty, if a bit overkill in some of the kitsch, like the room with all the dogs. I'm talking portraits of dogs, figurines of dogs (some of which had creepy illuminated eyes), curtains with dogs. It was a bit much. But the furniture was cool and a lot of thought went into the place overall, and I can't take away from that.   We sat down and there was a mix-up where most of the table received lunch menus while only one received a dinner menu. After making the realization, we were given dinner menus and were able to get down to it.  I was looking forward to a cask beer but should have read the fine print: all cask selections at The Dandelion are served at cellar temperature. As a rule, casks always seem to be served a little warmer than regular draught beer, and I struggle with this to begin with since I like my suds cold, but love the taste of cask beer. I had only ordered a half pint, and even that was hard to get down. My next beer was a regular draught, which was a bit colder. My last beer, a Narragansett can, was jussst right. And super classy-looking, I'm sure.  No matter! My cold brew went perfectly with my entree, fish and chips. A large hunk of battered and fried cod was served over wax paper on top of a cutting board, with a pail of thick cut chips and some very nice housemade ketchup. Delicious.  I sampled a couple other items off of the menu and, to be honest, I wasn't wowed. Apparently the selections were as true to English pub fare as could be, so I think maybe I'm just not a fan of that style. I'd probably order fish and chips on a future visit anyway, although the burger intrigued as well.  I continue to waver between three and four stars, even as I complete this review, but I'm going to ultimately go with four and see how things go on my next visit.

I've basically become obsessed with this place. The sandwiches are all filling and delicious. So far I've tried the turkey with cheddar and honey mustard, turkey with pear and gorgonzola and the tandoori chicken. Best of all, the nutritional information is easily accessible via the website. Which means no frustrating guesstimating for those of us on a diet.   The bakery area is filled with homemade items made out of healthy ingredients. The banana cookie, though small, packs a huge punch of flavor and for only 85 calories. If I had unlimited funds, I'd probably eat at Pure Fare every single day.

Once upon a time, many beers ago, I realized that a train called PATCO takes people from New Jersey into Philadelphia and back.  For a clueless and intimidated (yet thirsty) youngin' from the Garden State, Fado was the obvious choice as the 15th and Locust stop practically dumped me into the bar's lobby.    Years later, Fado is no longer a location that I frequent, but it was the first place that came to mind when planning a recent outing for my college girlfriends.  We're all at very different stages in our lives and coming from all over the place.  I needed to choose a venue that would be easy to find, not crazy-expensive and with an atmosphere that could satisfy the girls who wanted to sit and chat as well as the girls who wanted to get their drunken dance on.  Fado provided all of these things, plus a friendly server with blonde curly hair and a smile that didn't even falter when my friend spilled her drink the first, second and third times.  Yep, we were "those girls."    The negatives:  It was a very hot and humid night and for some ungodly reason, the windows were open and the a/c was not turned on until around midnight.             Bathrooms were kind of gross (the a/c probably would have helped here).  One of the guys trolling the dance area had obviously forgotten his deodorant and cleared the place out faster than you can say "raise your hands if you're Sure."  Understandably not Fado's fault, but still detracted from the experience.

I attended my first-ever class at Tria's Fermentation School earlier this month and plan to make it a regular occurrence. My guy and I attended the Spain v. Portugal Showdown, instructed by Michael McCaulley (who was appropriately just nominated for a James Beard Award). For ninety very entertaining minutes, Michael explained the nine or so wines we tasted, the characteristics of both regions and how the wines from each region compared. Audience interaction was encouraged and the classroom was a friendly, comfortable environment.   A sampling of cheeses, charcuterie, breads and accoutrements were served on little boards for each student, which was a very nice touch.   I am very much looking forward to our next class, and would highly recommend a session to anyone looking to enhance his or her knowledge while getting a good buzz on in the process.

Easily one of my favorite coffee shops in the city. I love the space - lots of seating between the picnic tables near the register, plus the stand alone tables scattered along the back wall and throughout the main floor.   Employees are always really pleasant. The last time I was there, the music was all old school stuff like Frank Sinatra - I loved it because it was so different from what you typically get at a coffee shop. The crowd is always really diverse which I like as well. You have your students but also your professional types.   I love the Americanos and the pastry selection is excellent. They have a savory pastry with goat cheese, sun dried tomatoes and spinach that is absolute perfection. I also dig that they have a cold case of to-go beverages and meal options for eating in or taking on the run. Finally, major props for the still and sparkling water station, with actual water glasses, instead of the shot glasses most coffee shops provide.   See you again soon, Parliament!

It's been a long time since I've wanted to attempt Bikram Yoga again. Four and a half years, to be exact. Previously, I had taken several sessions with my mom at a facility in NJ. I considered it to be an intense workout, but I had trouble focusing and the minutes (all 90 of them) dragged by as I shifted from pose to sweaty pose.   When my boyfriend recently came home after his first Bikram class, sweaty and exhausted, I knew I had to give it a shot. Leo, one of the instructors, is a friend of ours and has been trying to persuade us to take the class for ages. I was pretty nervous when we arrived on Friday evening. Especially as I mentally prepared myself for the class ahead while trying to adjust to the 115 degree heat.   The facility itself was nice, and the practice room was bright and had motivational words on the wall. My only issue was that the entire place was carpeted. It was the short kind of carpet that you usually see at shore houses, but carpet nonetheless. This freaked me out a bit since there are undoubtedly so many germs festering in the heat. The other facility I went to previously wasn't as nice (as in, no decent bathrooms or changing rooms), but it did have hard wood floors.   As for the class itself, once I got through the initial breathing pose, which I've always considered to be one of the hardest, it wasn't so bad. Difficult, yes, but not impossible. I surprised myself by being able to recall most of the positions and I was able to hold my balance better than I anticipated. I'm not sure if I'll be signing up for any 30 day challenges anytime soon, but I am going to attend another class this week and see how it goes.

My mom and I stopped by Brio to take advantage of their happy hour before heading to our appointments at Rizzieri nearby. The place is massive, with a huge outdoor seating area that looked to have some space for private gatherings as well. The inside also has several enormous rooms. Unfortunately, we weren't able to sit outside as the happy hour is only available in the bar area.   The distinct smell of bleach was distracting. I know it's a cleaning agent but it's really a terrible smell. And it didn't stop the occasional fruit fly from being present.   Aside from those minor (and very fixable) gripes, we enjoyed ourselves. The happy hour features $5 select drinks (a pretty wide selection, actually) and $3.95 select bites. We had a couple cosmos that were very boozy - they contained only vodka, cran and lime, which was perfect. I don't like a ton of mixers in my drinks and these were just right.   For snacks we shared a margherita flatbread, spicy shrimp and eggplant, and ravioli. The flatbread was very light; probably the least fattening of the three (but very tasty). The shrimp and eggplant dish was good, with just a little kick of heat and a creamy sauce. The ravioli were delicious. The dish had three very large pieces, breaded and fried and topped with marinara, some pesto and mozzarella.   When in the Jerz, options are somewhat limited to the selection of restaurant chains that line the highways. Brio is a good choice for an inexpensive happy hour.

Time has been on my places-to-try list for awhile now, so when a change of scenery was suggested after a couple drinks at nearby XIX on Saturday night, I finally got to check it out.  There are three main areas: a hip hop lounge upstairs, a smaller pub-like bar to the right of the main entrance, and a larger bar/restaurant on the left, which featured live jazz.  Almost every seat in the jazz bar was taken but there was still some standing room on the far side.  There was only one bartender so it was a little bit of a wait for drinks, but he had a good handle on the situation as a whole, all things considered.  I decided to try absinthe and made my selection from a list of options, none of which I knew anything about other than the listed ABV number.  The process was showy; water dripped from a big glass canister onto a sugar cube that rested on a spoon over the absinthe.  The end result tasted like a liquid version of Good & Plenty candy.  It was nice to try something different but it is unlikely that I'd order it again.    Overall, I really loved Time.  The vibe was on point, the people were chill and the jazz was a refreshing change from typical loungey background music.  I'd love to go back for dinner sometime as the food coming out of the kitchen smelled amazing.  I'll definitely return.

Pita Chip has quickly become one of my go-tos for fast, healthy food to go. I usually get the half and half bowl (rice and lettuce), with chicken shawarma, hummus, and a variety of fresh toppings. I love that there are so many vegetable options to choose from; everything always looks so colorful and healthy!   I'm a big fan of their vegan tahini as a sauce, but I recently tried the garlic sauce which is almost like an aioli. It would be great with fries! I haven't tried Pita Chip's fries yet, but when I do I will definitely get the garlic sauce for dipping.   My bowl rings in at eight dollars and change, which is really great for a hefty amount of food that keeps me going for hours. The employees are always friendly, and there's a loyalty card program as well as emailed coupons. Great spot for quick, healthy eats!

First time at the Fairmount location of Little Pete's! This is an old school diner all the way. I had a coffee within moments of sitting down and I saw all the usual breakfast staples on the menu. I ordered an omelet with onions, peppers and feta, and it was dropped off in no time at all.   My dining companion and I lingered for a while after breakfast and it became increasingly harder to get a coffee. But, overall, it was a very solid experience and a great option for a weekday, since it was relatively quiet.

Perhaps the "Speakeasy" part of the name rings a little too true - if my boyfriend hadn't pointed out the business, I probably would have passed it by dozens of times before realizing it.
