But behind the darkened windows lies a delightful little nook with great coffee, affordable bites and friendly staff members.   And cupcakes. Beautiful, perfect cupcakes... that I have yet to try! I know, I know, cupcake-queen and all that jazz. I definitely need to check those out. In the meantime, I'm loving their coffee (which unfortunately only comes in one size, although it's hella strong). I also enjoyed my breakfast sandwich yesterday, with egg whites, smoked cheddar and bacon on a crusty baguette with a lovely side of greens with pesto dressing.   This is a great neighborhood spot!

I am not a large festival type of person, but Bloktoberfest is the exception to the rule. It started off pretty small a few years ago and has since grown to a blocks-long party on South Street West. I'm a big fan of arriving early, grabbing some drink tickets and hitting up the cool craft beer tents and food trucks. After around 4pm the lines start getting pretty long and the streets are packed. That's generally when I start thinking about my next move.   The crowd is made up of mostly young professionals and families - I really enjoy that. No one seems to get out of hand (at least, during the daylight hours, from what I can tell) and they stop selling beer tickets at a certain point to help ensure that. The organizers are all about keeping the local businesses and neighbors happy and Bloktoberfest is a very well-run event overall. Can't wait for next year!

After two-plus years at my gym, I started feeling the familiar itch for change. The change of seasons felt like a great time to try something new, so I purchased a month-long pass at Tuck. They currently have a new student special for just $69 which offers a month of unlimited classes!  I had taken barre classes before and my experiences were all over the map; some classes were great, while others couldn't be over fast enough. Tuck strikes this amazing balance of a really hard workout that somehow still feels enjoyable. Also, the best part is that there are several instructors so every class feels different. Each instructor has their own style - it's really great for variety and keeps things interesting!   The studio is always bright and clean and the equipment is nice. I'm really enjoying my new workout and plan to continue through the summer, and perhaps even longer!

I have to hand it to the Dîner en Blanc organizers - they really stepped it up for year three. The location on Broad Street was amazing. So many photo ops. The party spanned from Chestnut to Pine Streets and every block was filled with beautifully decorated tables and some fine looking people.   As opposed to last year's location on the Parkway, this year provided much more space between tables, and there was a lot more foot traffic which made the event feel interactive with the city. Amazingly, the predicted rain held off, but had there been a weather catastrophe, we would have been moved to the Kimmel Center, which was on reserve as a pretty excellent back-up plan. Can't wait to see what year four brings!

My once-monthly BYO girls' night took place at Effie's last Friday.  We chose the spot based solely on yelp research (mine, of course) and we were once again very pleased!  We had reservations and a table was ready for us as soon as we arrived.  Service was friendly and helpful.  The four of us shared an app that had a little of everything: spinach phyllo triangles, chicken skewers, olive tapenade, hummus, roasted peppers, orzo and a couple other things.  And let's not forget the fresh-out-of-the-oven pita bread, which was so good that by the end of the meal, I was referring to the pita baby in my stomach.    My entree was a shrimp dish served over rice with a tomato/feta/green onion sauce.  A-MA-ZING basically sums up my feelings.    Despite being stuffed, we ordered dessert.  Baklava and some other phyllo pastry that was filled with custard and drizzled with honey.  Both were good but the baklava definitely came out ahead, in my opinion.  The only problem?  The desserts were nearly impossible to eat with a fork alone.  Had it been the early 90s, I would have called MacGuyver to help us out.  Ask for a knife with your dessert.  Trust me.    The best part was that dinner was only $30ish per girl-- which gave us plenty of extra cash for post-dinner drinks.    The restaurant itself was pretty basic, so if I wanted my Greek cuisine with a little more ambiance I'd probably lean towards Dmitri's.  But for a small group looking for some good eats at a very reasonable price in a comfortable atmosphere, I'd hit Effie's.  This is exactly the place I plan on bringing my mom and sister, to introduce them to the wonderful world of Mediterranean food.

The fab Alex W and I chose Pure Fare for our lunch date this week. I had tried one of their sandwiches before and was looking forward to tasting more of their goods.  The store was smaller than I expected but I loved the layout. A communal table in the center of the room provides plenty of seating for anyone wanting to eat there. A coffee and fresh juice bar is located on one of the shorter walls, while prepared items line the long wall. Some breakfast selections are featured in a display near the register.  I especially love that the calorie info is posted on every single item in clear view. I selected a spinach and artichoke frittata for only 200 calories, and I split the quinoa salad with Alex. The salad was filled with apricots, avocado, cherry tomatoes, basil and almonds. Very tasty. The frittata had a satisfying cheddar flavor without feeling heavy. I would absolutely get either item again. Alex's turkey sandwich with veggies was flavorful and had a nice crunch. All items totaled around $18, which seemed fair given the quality of the food. Looking forward to trying more!

Apologies for what may seem like haterade, but Rittenhouse Square simply is not my favorite park in the city. For me, a park should be a calming oasis where I can sit and collect my thoughts or have a quiet conversation.   Rittenhouse is like the Cherry Hill Mall of the outdoors. It's a melting pot of people from all walks of life (cool), which also includes lecherous men with lame pick-up lines and people who think nothing of chain smoking next to you as you try to eat lunch or simply breathe (not cool).   When alone, I always find myself walking through quickly and avoiding the eyes of people lined against the paths. Not exactly a feeling of serenity.   My favorite part of Rittenhouse Square Park is enjoying it from the outside, seated at one of Parc's tables, with a glass of white and a warm shrimp salad.

After finally getting acclimated to my new gym, I think the place deserves a solid four stars. I have to admit, I was scared off from signing a contract because of the many negative things I heard from former members. Instead, I opted for a month to month membership, which can be closed with something like two months' notice.   The staff members are always pleasant, and the other patrons are respectful and keep to themselves. I've never felt uncomfortable during my workouts, which is obviously a huge plus.   The cardio section is separate from the weights and resistance machines, which I like. The gated dividers provide just the right amount of privacy while still maintaining an open feel. The large windows facing Walnut Street are perfect for people watching during my runs.   The facility itself is a little old looking but everything still seems clean and well-maintained, so I'm fine with it. My only major gripe is that the treadmills cannot be set for more than 60 minutes at a time. I understand that the reason behind this is probably so that people don't have to wait for machines, but there isn't ever a crowd during the time I work out. For people who are training for longer runs, it's too much of a mindfuck to have to reset the machine 5+ miles in. This minor issue aside, Sweat is a fine place for people who just want to get in for their workouts and get on with their lives.

As I've been dabbling into meditation more and more, I've noticed Mama's Wellness Joint keeps popping up across my social feeds. Finally, the stars aligned and my schedule worked out so I was able to attend a session.   The space is lovely, with a nice reception area that has a pretty cool gift shop. Shoes have to be removed before heading into the main room, and there is plenty of space for that.   The practice room has a very soothing feel. For my session, only a few small spotlights provided some low lighting, and we made ourselves comfortable with the blankets and bolsters provided.   Mama's offers yoga, but there are a handful of meditation practices offered for all types of interests, by a variety of practitioners. I'm excited to explore more of these in the future!

Okay, I've been back twice and the counter staff could not have been nicer or the sandwiches (tasso ham and tuna - an awesome choice for something a bit lighter but still filling) more delicious. I love that they have a frequent sandwicher card so that I'll eventually earn one for free.   Once the weather warms up a bit and I become a little less lazy, I'll walk myself over there and enjoy a meal in their cute loft space.

This Starbucks left a lot to be desired on my visit this afternoon. There were only two employees working and one seemed to be training - and it was busy! We arrived when there wasn't much of a line but the queue got backed up several times while we were there.   Secondly, there is not much seating available so you really have to pounce on a table the moment it becomes unoccupied.   Third, the snack case was pretty barren and not super appealing. Perhaps this is a positive as it kept me from snacking!    Finally, the music was turned way loud. I'm certain that Starbucks has some sort of corporate policy about their music volume and this particular location was definitely not abiding to that decibel. Totally distracting.   My green tea latte was fine but the condiments station could have used a clean-up.

My sis raves about Johnny Mañanas. It's her go-to happy hour spot and she's obsessed with the margaritas and taco salads (see: Kate C's review). So we made plans to meet up last Friday so I could see what the fuss was all about.   First impression: kitschy but fun vibe, weird smell. Not like stale beer smell, but something equally not pleasant. As the place filled and the scent of cooking food took over, it got better. But still, might want to look into that.   Our server was sweet and checked in often. The margaritas were on point. The sour mix is house-made and the drinks went down easy. I was buzzing after one but totally went for round two.   The taco salad was pretty awesome. My sister said they normally come topped with shredded chicken and sauteed onions and peppers but our chicken was in strips and there were no sauteed onions and peppers to be found. Still, it was a tasty salad and huge.   I'm down for round two at this place.

Ladies and gentlemen, I FINALLY broke 100 in a game of bowling.  Yes, I do realize this still makes me the worst bowler in history, but an accomplishment is an accomplishment and must be recognized.  Rome wasn't built in a day, right?  Exactly.    I'd like to credit my outstanding play to Pinsetter, the Garden State's answer to Lucky Strike.  Formerly Maple Bowl, the place has been rehabbed and decked out in retro kitsch-- think Continental Midtown or Jones.  There are a bajillion lanes, all in semi-darkness with lots of blacklights.  The tunes were awesome and ranged from Death Cab for Cutie to Warrant ("She's my cherry piiiie!"  Haha, now it's in your head too!).  Best of all, the music videos for each song are projected onto the wall where you bowl.  Since MTV and VH1 tend to only show videos between the hours of too-tired-to-keep-my-eyes-open and oh-god-hit-the-snooze-button, it was cool to see that bands are still doing their thing.  The bartenders and wait staff were all friendly, and the turnaround time for a beer was about ten seconds.  Speaking of which, each beer was brought out in a very frosty glass which was awesome.  The menu had tons of options but I opted out since I'm trying to get back to breathing while in my skinny jeans.  I had a bite of the bbq pork sliders and they were delish-- I will have to hit them up the next time, mos def.    My only gripe is that the women's bathrooms were very smokey.  Seriously, ladies-- smoking is so 1985.  Give it up already, or take your lazy butts outside so I don't have to inhale it while I pee.

My BYO girls and I arrived at Little Fish on time for our reservation, but we ended up having to loiter outside for close to half an hour with a few other groups while patiently waiting for the limited number of tables to turn over. Once we were seated, the wine was opened and put on ice and our lovely experience commenced. We started with mussels, scallops and oysters. I tried the mussels, which were served in a light broth. For me, these were just okay. The scallops, on the other hand, were perfect. Two huge seared scallops sat atop a delightful pesto oil, alongside a smattering of mushrooms and some shaved truffle. I don't even like mushrooms and yet I found myself eating everything together with relish. Get the scallops.   For our entrees, one friend chose salmon, another ordered halibut and I went with striped bass. I hate to say it, but I was underwhelmed by my dish. The fish itself was perfectly portioned and prepared well, but the flavors of the broth and accompanying rock shrimp and artichoke hearts were nonexistent. Luckily, my friend didn't seem to mind that I repeatedly helped myself to her halibut, which was fantastic. Resting in the most delicious broth ever, I believe the fish was accompanied by fingerling potatoes, spinach and frizzled onions. The reason I'm not completely positive on the details is because I was lifting my fork to my mouth at warp-speed and the ingredients were kind of a colorful blur.   There were three dessert offerings, and since there were three of us it only seemed natural that we try them all. The crème brulee was spot-on, a peach tart was crumbly and delicious and the chocolate torte was very rich and decadent.   For me, Little Fish had a ton of hype to live up to in my mind. Perhaps that's why I felt a little let down by some of the things I tried. In the same respect, the plates I enjoyed were worth every bit of praise that Little Fish has been receiving. It's a must-try on the BYO circuit!

I like this coffee shop. It's small, but there are three high top tables with stools that are comfortable to work from or conduct a quick meeting. I've never seen all of the seats filled so it's not a bad alternative to the always-crowded Elixr across the street.   La Colombe is on tap and the prices are pretty in line with other shops. There's a small case of pre-made sandwiches and baked goods but I haven't tried anything.   Also, I remembered my last visit being somewhat chilly but the café was nice and toasty today. So there's that, too.

Wanting to get out of our section of town for dinner on Friday, the boyfriend and I jumped in the car and headed to West Philly. Destination: Dock Street Brewing Co.   There was one large, open area with tables, and a long bar that stretched across one side of the room with plenty of seating. We grabbed two bar stools near the open door to take advantage of the cool breeze on a lovely spring night.   I immediately gravitated towards the OMG Pale Ale, which was absolutely delicious and had just the right amount of hoppy flavor. We shared a Caesar salad, which wasn't super special but did take the edge off. Then we shared a margherita pizza and a parma pizza, with crispy prosciutto, crushed tomatoes and a four cheese blend. Both had light, crisp crusts and hit the spot.   Our bartender/server somehow managed to keep our beers and water glasses filled while handling take-out orders and answering the phone as well. Hats off to him!   Many of the other pizzas caught my eye, along with the fry trio featuring white and sweet potatoes and leeks. I'll likely go back soon for more of that OMG Pale Ale, and hopefully my appetite will return with me.

I relied on Yelp reviews to lead me to a new dry cleaner, and I was not disappointed. When I brought my clothes to Master Tailor, the owner meticulously combed over my clothes looking for spots or discolorations of any kind, marking everything with red tape. She was able to have my clothes ready for pick up just two days later, and everything looks great. This is my new dry cleaner. Thank you, Yelp!

Yeah guys, I went out after dinner too.    My friend invited me to join her at Raven Lounge, where she would be meeting up with her boyfriend and some of his friends.  The words "single" and "cute" were all this hot-blooded lady needed to hear for convincing and we were off.  Solid beats, cold brews and Hungry Hungry Hippos are where it's at.  This morning, as I was fishing through my bag I noticed a stray piece of Jenga had hitched a ride to Jersey.  Don't worry, Raven Lounge peeps, I'll bring it back soon.  Maybe.

Bayard's is a local chocolate company with three locations.  Each "chocolate house" is similar, but the one I have frequented most is the Cinnaminson location.  Every time I visit I am filled with warm feelings and the reminiscence of past holidays and birthday celebrations.    In high school, a friend of mine worked at the Cinnaminson Bayard's and every time we had a sleepover, she would bring BAGS of chocolates.  I can't imagine how many calories were consumed on those nights!  Now, I stick to just a couple pieces of my very favorites.  I cannot go into a Bayard's without leaving with a chocolate covered marshmallow for myself.  Does anyone remember that Sesame Street clip with the little kid and the chocolate covered cookie?  Am I jogging memories here?  That's me with the marshmallow.  Other favorites are the dark chocolate covered orange peels, which are so different from anything you would find at other chocolate stores and so very good, and the chocolate and vanilla butter creams.

Round two at Sampan was another very enjoyable experience.  This time around, we were seated in the larger room near the open kitchen.  Once again, it was difficult to pinpoint exactly which dishes we wanted to try.  Our server was knowledgeable about the menu and made suggestions based on our questions.    The first selection to arrive was the "Philly Cheese Steak," which consisted of four toast rounds topped with shredded beef, wisps of shallot and a drizzle of Sriracha.  Bursting with flavor and heat, they were a very promising start to the meal.  The next two dishes were repeats from our first visit: edamame dumplings and crab and curry fritters.  Again, these were good but the flavors seemed weaker this time around.  We decided that, had the ordering of the plates been: dumplings, fritters, cheese steak, the richness would have built and we would have appreciated the lighter dishes more.    Next up were the Korean rice cakes.  The little doughy discs arrived in a bowl, smothered with ground sausage, chopped green onion, spices and a tasty sauce.  At first, I wasn't sure how I felt about the texture, but it grew on me and I went back for more and ended up really enjoying the uniqueness.    The seared snapper followed, and while the fish was prepared well, I was indifferent overall.  The diced mango on top did not provide much flavor, as if the fruit was not yet ripe, and the sausage did not really blend with the fish for me.    Our last savory item was the petite filet, which we ordered medium.  The filet arrived with very little pinkness and only in the very center slices.  The soy butter foam provided some extra moistness, but the mustard smear lacked a kick.    For dessert, we tried the popular soft serve and the banana chocolate cakes.  The latter dessert was a picture perfect piece of food art, but I was partial to the adorable baby soft serve cones.  The flavors, vanilla butter popcorn and salted chocolate, reminded me of the frozen custard I grew up eating on hot summer nights down the shore.      I really enjoy Sampan.  The wide-ranging menu provides a new discovery on each visit, and the restaurant is versatile enough for a quick bite, cocktail at the bar or a complete dining experience.

I eye up Moustaki every time I drive past but rarely find myself in the area. I've always been curious because I absolutely love Mediterranean food! Last week, I finally made Moustaki my dining destination before heading to an event at the Franklin Institute.   The menu has a lot on it and there's definitely something for everyone. I'm trying to get into a more pescetarian diet so I gravitated towards the salmon platter. In an attempt to keep it healthy-ish, I went with rice and lemon potatoes, though I was definitely eyeing up the fries.   We started with the feta dip appetizer which I wasn't crazy about. The cucumbers that came with were past their prime; they had that soft, translucent look around the edges.   Fortunately, the main dish was really solid. The salmon portion was generous and I liked the potatoes a lot (the rice was fine, nothing extraordinary).   I'd give Moustaki another shot if I happened to be in the neighborhood again.

When it comes to new-to-me places, I can be as bashful as a child, refusing to go it alone for the first time, hiding behind my mom's pant leg while I assess the situation.   Even though I've been living in the city for almost six months, it took that long for me to check out the Schuylkill River Trail. Friends promised a safe and scenic place to run outside, but I just kept going to the gym. That, or - get this - driving to Jersey where my courses were plotted and I felt comfortable with where I was going and what to expect.  Finally, my boyfriend and I decided to take a walk, and to the Trail we went. Shocked was I at how well-maintained and well-populated the area actually was. I felt like I had made this amazing discovery, and I couldn't stop talking about how glad I was that we had finally taken that walk.   Yesterday, I enjoyed my first of what will likely be many solo runs on the Trail.

Never go here if you are easily distracted or hungover.  You will circle the racks for an hour or more, try on bikinis in December and will leave feeling frustrated and empty-handed while swearing to never return.  Of course, you will be lured back by promises of designer merchandise at a fraction of the price plus 25% off in the holiday sale.  Keep your wits about you and stick to your game plan.  You just might end up with a Christmas gift for the boyfriend and a hot minidress for New Year's.

Sunday morning marked my fourth completion of the Broad Street Run. That's ten long miles down Broad, starting in Olney and ending in the Navy Yard.   I love this race.   For me, the Broad Street Run is all about stepping outside of my comfort zone, challenging myself, and doing so with over twenty five thousand other people.   The sense of community that pumps through the air on the first Sunday of every May is incredible. In the beginning miles, priests and parishioners cheer from the steps of churches, while families wave from their doorsteps. As I passed a group of gentlemen near a fast food restaurant last Sunday, one yelled out something to the effect of "keep running; you've got junk in the trunk!" I did a quick survey of my neighboring runners, and hoped he was referring to the woman on my right. Regardless, I was inspired.   In the middle miles, throngs of supporters crowd the sidewalks from Arch to Ellsworth, and musicians keep the vibe upbeat.   At mile 8, the Rocky theme is played from... somewhere, and the knowledge that the end of the race is near starts to set in.   Finally, after what seems like the longest stretch of Broad yet, signs for the Navy Yard appear and a welcome breeze from off the water rolls in. Crossing the finish line is exhilarating, and the immediate excitement for next year's race takes over.

Friends and I hit Lucky's one Sunday morning recently when we were out on a bike ride. The outside tables along the side of the restaurant were nearly all full, so we were stuck grabbing the least desirable one in the back, which was on a bit of an angle and downwind from the dumpsters. Pandemic times, am I right? We were nonetheless happy to have a table to fit our group, and the staff who took care of us were great.   Brunch goers won't have many options here, because Lucky's is all about the burgers, dogs and fried things. There is a brunch burger that has an egg, if that's your jam. All burgers come as juniors or standards, and I loved having that option! I went with a junior classic (american cheese, bacon, lettuce, tomato, onion) and a side of fries for just two bucks more. This was the perfect amount of food and I felt like I was able to indulge without going overboard. Also, shout out to the bun, which was light but sturdy enough to keep everything together. A truly excellent burger!  My brother and SIL used to live by the Lucky's in Queen Village and it was their go-to spot. Now I see why! Looking forward to more bike rides with burger rewards in my future.

Le Virtu may be my favorite Italian in the city. I regularly crave the maccheroni alla mugnaia, a single strand of perfectly al dente pasta tossed in olive oil, garlic, hot peppers and pecorino. It's simple and perfect all at the same time. A basket of dried peppers is served alongside in case you want to add an extra kick.   On my last visit we had the peasant meatballs (palott cac' e ove), which don't involve meat at all. They consisted of egg and cheese and were served in a delicious red sauce. They were some of the best meatballs I've ever had, and I didn't even miss the meat. You also can't go wrong with the burrata or salumi offerings, or any of the pastas.   Earlier in the summer we had a granita dessert that was absolutely fabulous. There were four flavors and two were wine-based. Every flavor popped and it was a wonderfully light treat.   Another thing I love about Le Virtu is that even when you don't snag a table, the bar is a great place to enjoy dinner or even just some drinks. Their bartenders are lovely and always fun to chat with - and there's usually someone you already know sitting at the bar, anyway. What a gem in South Philly.

My man and I decided to take ourselves out for a nice Italian meal on Sunday night, after four long days of nonstop events. After perusing the reviews for Italian restaurants, we read Marcello's and out the door we went to Le Virtu.   With no reservations, I still thought the chances of snagging a two top were high for an overcast Sunday. Unfortunately, I underestimated the popularity of the place and we were banished to bar seating. We started off with a crisp white wine and bread basket, with some of the most delicious bread I've had in a long while, and perfectly olive-tinged oil for dipping.   To start, we tried the bruschetta foursome, of which each flavor popped. Most notable was the creamy ricotta with marinated artichoke and balsamic reduction. Our other starter was a special; silky burrata with slices of cured pork (similar to prosciutto, only harder and even more delicious).    For dinner, handkerchief pasta with braised duck and beef ragu. I was certain that the pasta would come in a red sauce, so when it arrived without anything red, I was a little disappointed. Then I tasted the dish and quickly got over my red sauce craving. My glass of spicy red helped to balance the richness of the meats. The smoked potato gnocchi with lamb ragu was also quite delicious.      We passed on dessert but there's no doubt that we'll be back to try other offerings from the menu. Next time, I'm making a reservation.

My husband and I had a really nice dinner at Nori this week. We arrived early on a Wednesday evening because we had tickets to a show nearby. There were very few tables occupied during our time there from around 5:30-6:45. I brought a bottle of white wine and we received an ice bucket upon arrival.   Since I arrived first, I ordered some edamame to take the edge off. They were simply salted, nothing fancy. Once my husband arrived, we ordered the tuna tartare to start. It was again on the simple side, just diced tuna and avocado with some tobiko. Fresh and light, a good start to the meal.   Next, we shared three special rolls: spicy girl (spicy salmon, spicy yellowtail, spicy tuna and crispy shallots), flaming hamachi (spicy crunchy yellowtail, tuna, jalapeño, scallion and sriracha), and blue ocean (spicy crunchy shrimp and cucumber, topped with smoked and fresh salmon, avocado and lime juice).   My favorite roll was the flaming hamachi, because I loved the crunchiness of the jalapeño, followed by the spicy girl. I'm not big on smoked salmon so the blue ocean was my least favorite, but my husband enjoyed it.   Prices were reasonable and there are some great lunch specials I'd like to try. Looking forward to next time!

After months of saying I was going to try Day by Day, that plan finally came to fruition last Saturday morning after the Undy 5000. The restaurant was bright and sunny, and kind of like a modern day diner.   Since Christopher R raved about the cinnamon buns, we decided to order one and share it between four people. How we achieved this without an epic battle of forks is still a mystery. The bun was soft and cinnamon-y, with just the right amount of sweetness from the delectable icing.   Katrina's huevos rancheros looked amazing, and it was a huge serving that she couldn't even finish. Vinny was also quite happy with his smoked salmon omelet. Art had mixed feelings on his eggs over chorizo and sweet potato hash, while I found my egg white omelet and homefries to be just right.   I returned a few days later for lunch and once again ordered an egg white omelet. I would have been pleased as punch had it not been for the undercooked eggs. I didn't even notice it until I got towards the center of the omelet, so I was already halfway through at that point. I picked around the runny areas but it was definitely a turnoff. Meanwhile, my friend's chicken sandwich and pasta salad looked awesome.   This isn't going to become my go-to weekend brunch spot, but I do expect it to become part of the weekday lunch rotation.

I have been planning to write a review update for Wegman's for some time, and in light of recent events, I can think of no better time than the present to update what started as a Michael Jackson shout out.   It has been slightly over a year since my original review, and while the honeymoon is officially over, I think Wegman's and I have what it takes to make it through the long haul. There have been some bumps along the road, as I'm sure there will continue to be, but for the most part I can think of no grocery store that could make me happier.   The prepared foods section is phenomenal. The Asian wokery bar has what I consider to be the best fast food Chinese, hands down. The salad bar has every ingredient you could possibly want, plus various other cold salads and even a hot foods section. My favorite improvement to this general area of the store is in the form of index cards that list serving sizes and nutritional information for most items. It takes the guesswork out of wondering which items are diet-friendly and which items will land you a spot on The Biggest Loser.   For the most part, the grocery area has everything I need. I stress, "for the most part" because there have been times when a particular brand I'm looking for is not available (Skippy reduced fat peanut butter in both creamy and chunky varieties) or a certain item is missing entirely. This happens even in the produce section, which I find especially odd for such a large store, and I quickly find myself getting irate when I have to make a special trip to the local ACME just to pick up the missing ingredient for a recipe. Weg's somewhat makes up for this in other areas though. There are many items around the store that make cooking so much easier for those who are short on time (or just plain lazy). My favorite item, and one that I suspect must be a favorite for others as it is not always available, is the bag of sliced onions and peppers in the produce section. Fajitas anyone?   As with any attractive and likable entity, many people are drawn to the Weg's. This sometimes creates a crowd that is nearly impossible to maneuver through with limited time and even less patience. To avoid high blood pressure situations or the blowing of gaskets, avoid the store on weekends or weekday lunch hours. Weekday mornings, mid-afternoons or late evenings are best, especially if you plan on utilizing a cart (for storing your items, not mowing people down).

I needed a bouquet of flowers, and I needed them quickly. I vaguely remembered a bunch of last-minute-men hovering around flowers on Spruce Street at around 5pm on Valentine's Day, but I couldn't recall the exact location of where this was witnessed. I jumped in my car and did a Spruce Street drive-by. Once I spotted Spruce Food Market, it all came rushing back.   I parked in the twenty minute loading zone across the street and surveyed the impressive array of bouquets. Mostly all, if not all, were reasonably priced under $20. I grabbed a lovely assortment that included roses, carnations, big stalk thingees I don't know the name of and a mix other blossoms. Some paper was wrapped around them and I was out the door in seconds. The flowers were well-received and I have Spruce Food Market to thank. I will definitely return the next time I need flowers.

I recalled my only experience at Mama Palma's as being pretty mediocre, but I was willing to give them another shot since there are so few sit-down pizza places in the neighborhood. The boyfriend and I ordered diet cokes, and after scoping out the beer prices, we were happy. $7 for a draft Peroni? Mama, please.   To start, a shared Caesar salad that was so bland, I could only hope the pizza would save dinner. The mostly-white iceberg was dressed in watered-down dressing. Either that, or the rinsed lettuce was still wet when the dressing was tossed in. Flavorless slices of dry bread topped the lettuce. Total cost, $10.  Our pizza was significantly better, with generous crumbles of sausage, mozzarella, some peppers and a chunky tomato sauce. The crust was not memorable. When two slices remained and we were given the option of boxing, we decided to just leave them behind.   Next time, I'll trek over to Pietro's or just order up some Slice.

I would like to take this time to appeal to the folks at the Royal in a request to get the chicken frankie wrap on the lunch menu. Yesterday I had a craving, and that craving was for more chicken frankie. Sad was my heart when, after reading and re-reading the menu three times, there was no frankie or even frankfurter for that matter. I went with my backup, the grilled chicken sandwich with pears and gorgonzola, but it was a very distant second to the wrap.

I was very pleasantly surprised by my experience at James last night. A friend and I met up for happy hour before joining a meeting that was taking place in the semi-private room towards the front. Happy hour is $2 off beer, wine or cocktails and there is also a menu of food items that are reduced in price from the regular menu.   I went with prosecco for my drink and really enjoyed what they were pouring - I forget the brand. To eat, I started with shrimp cocktail, which featured four huge shrimp and a slight twist on regular cocktail sauce. I also ordered the crab cake sandwich, with a side salad instead of chips. The crab cake was excellent and I ditched most of the bread in favor of the pretty sizable salad. Meanwhile, my friend had wings and fries, both of which looked and smelled great. I love that the menu offers something for everyone!   The side room where our meeting took place was cozy and perfect for a small meeting or cocktail party. Huge props that the room also has a TV, so we were able to watch the game as we got down to business. Now that James is on my radar, I'll be looking for a reason to return sooner than later.

Barcade is a cool spot for something different. Friends and I kicked off an afternoon of fun at the Ms. Pac-Man game, where it became depressingly obvious how far I've fallen from my youthful domination of video games.   The bartenders were friendly and willing to whip up one mean bloody mary in addition to offering helpful info during the beer selection process. The draft list is quite extensive.   I didn't eat but the food looked decent in a bar food kind of way.   Barcade isn't really a place I'd typically hang out which is probably why my feelings are so-so on the place. But if you like good beer and you love arcade games, this spot will be right up your alley.

After hemming and hawing between Indian and Thai tonight, we ultimately went with Indian Restaurant. It was our first experience and a good one at that. We opted for the delivery service via the website, which is super easy to use, with the ability to make edits or notes for each dish, and they accept credit cards for payment. I do wish there was a way to add on a tip for the delivery, though. Our delivery guy was unable to break a twenty which was all the cash we had. I'm making a mental note to swing by in-person this week so I can drop off a belated tip.   I hadn't realized how hungry I was until we opened the bag and the aromas took over. We tore off the lids and got down to it. Tandoori shrimp served over spinach were nice. I recently had tandoori shrimp at Tashan and these weren't exactly on the same level but they were good. The chicken vindaloo was very spicy, just like the little pepper icon on the menu indicated. I started hiccuping uncontrollably after just one bite, but I'm pretty sensitive to spice. That said, this dish was probably a little too hot for me, so I'd probably opt for something different next time. I will say that the chicken was perfectly cooked and tender. So I'm looking forward to trying another variation.  An Indian dinner is not complete without naan, and we tried the garlic and peshwari styles. Again, I just had these at Tashan so I'm totally biased towards theirs, but each of Indian Restaurant's naans were solid. The sweetness of the peshwari actually made the vindaloo a little more bearable for my sensitive palate. Three different sauces were included as well, with the slightly sweet one being my favorite. Again, probably because it helped tone down the spice.   We've got tons of rice and some of the vindaloo left over. It's safe to say we'll definitely give Indian Restaurant another shot soon.

Bloktoberfest is definitely one of the better fall festivals around. It's several blocks of beer tents, food trucks, businesses peddling their wares, live music and happy people. We pre-paid for our wristbands to save five bucks, and we followed the directions which specifically stated that you should print your ticket. Well, we arrived and, of course, mostly everyone in line was trying to use QR codes, which were not scanning properly. My boyfriend was the only one in our group of four who had not pre-paid, and he ended up getting his wristband before we did. So that was mildly annoying, but once we got our wristbands we were all good.   Next year, I'll probably buy the three card pass instead of the five, because I didn't realize how long the lines would get and how many restaurants would be selling drinks right from their windows, anyway. By the time 2 or 3pm rolled around, all of the beer tents had massive, slow-moving lines. But from noon to that time, it was great! We had our choice of whatever beer we wanted and with minimal wait. Same went for the food trucks. I was hungry upon arrival so there wasn't much of a wait for any of the trucks. We hit Cow and the Curd and my favorite, the Foo Truck, and had eats in no time. We also commandeered one of the many picnic tables on the street for most of the day, which was great since our growing group was constantly getting food or drinks.   I'm really not a huge festival person because I hate crowds, but Bloktoberfest is just right for me, and right in my neighborhood, too. Looking forward to next year!

A few of us stopped by Yellow Juice Bar on Sunday afternoon after a workout. There were two people waiting on a juice that was in-process when we arrived. We placed our order for three juices which came to slightly over $20. I got out my credit card and the juice bar employee asked me if I had cash - they were having problems with the system. I didn't think I had enough on me but just when I realized I did, the credit card went through, though I was unable to get a printed receipt or tip on my card.   The juices took a while to process and, I have to admit, the finished product didn't stack up to my favorite juice bar across town (the ingredients in the drink were almost identical to the blend I normally order at the other establishment). Nor did the experience overall with the employees. Hopefully Yellow Juice Bar was just having an off day but I'm not sure how soon I'll be back to find out.

I am thrilled with my experience with Millennium Flowers this week! I've ordered flowers for delivery a handful of times and I never remember the places I order from; I realize now that must be indicative of a so-so experience. Well, not anymore. I've found my go-to shop!   After checking out a handful of flower shop pages on Yelp, I kept coming back to Millenium - I loved the arrangement photos posted by other Yelpers - especially the one posted by Maria L. On the website, arrangements looked nice, though a bit outdated, so I called the shop to articulate exactly what I wanted. That's when I was connected with Yana, who went above and beyond to make sure I was happy with my order.   Yana explained that they have a great designer in-house and she was able to work with me on my price point. Today, I was pleasantly surprised when she sent me several pictures of the finished arrangement via text. She wanted to confirm that I was happy before the flowers went out for delivery. This has never happened before and I thought it was such a nice touch. As you can see from the photos, the flowers are gorgeous. Most importantly, my mom, who is retiring on Friday, absolutely loved them!

I wish I could remember the name of the juice I sucked down on Friday, but it had apple, cucumber, kale and ginger and was recommended by the gentleman behind the counter. Pure deliciousness. And served just the right temp, with just a few ice cubes.  The store is bright and the employees were friendly during my visit. When the guy who made my juice poured my cup, he even let me drink a few sips so he could top me off with what was left in the pitcher. Nice! I also love that the calories are listed for all menu items. That's huge, and super appreciated.   So glad Philly is catching on to the juicing craze, because I've been really into juice as an in-between snack, or as a complement to a lighter lunch. Sip-N-Glo definitely doesn't come cheap; my 16oz juice was more than $7! I'm willing to pay for that deliciousness every now and then for a treat, though I'd likely have it more often if it was a little more wallet-friendly. It is still juice, and not a meal, after all.

Interested to see yet another incarnation of 505 Haddon Ave, we stopped by on Saturday afternoon for a quick snack. I was surprised to see that the outside of the building had been completely redone to reflect the cuisine. A trickling fountain coming out of some stacked barrels, some fake cacti and a ranchy-looking paint job made the place stick out from its former failed selves. A little cheesy, but in a fun and definitely unexpected way.   The inside was less impressive. For a restaurant that had only been open for a few days, it already looked ready for a good scrub-down. Dust covered many of the sun-soaked surfaces and straw wrappers and dropped fries littered the floors.   Empanadas, duck and sausage were all out of stock, our sweet and somewhat nervous young server told us. We ordered the burnt end nachos, a bowl of chili and a side of sauteed spinach. The food was brought out pretty quickly, on plastic plates (though we had real silverware). The presentation looked really sloppy. Fortunately, the food was solid. We noticed other people had silver trays for larger orders, which looked a bit nicer. Real plates would probably make a world of difference here.   Will I go out of my way for Little Louie's? No. But it seemed that they were already doing a pretty sweet take-out business, and if I still lived in Collingswood I'd most likely be one of their take-out patrons.

Vintage has been on my to-try list for a while, and last night I finally got to check it out.  The wine selections were great~ I saw a couple of my favs featured which was cool, as well as some others that were unfamiliar and interesting.  There were probably two or three wines that were not available when we tried to order them, but there were so many to choose from that it didn't make much of a difference.   After a couple glasses of white, I had the liquid courage to try something new to me-- escargot.  They reminded me of mussels, taste and consistency-wise, but in prettier shells.  I would try them again somewhere else for comparison purposes, but I don't think they will become my new favorite thing.  My dining companion compared the gorgonzola and fig bruschetta to a jelly sandwich mixed with Fig Newtons.  I'm certain that's what the people at Vintage were trying to accomplish.  The cheese plate was presented nicely on a tiered stand; there was a whole bunch of fruit on one plate, a whole bunch of sliced baguette on another and a whole bunch of available real estate on the cheese plate.  Paging Donald Trump.  Don't get me wrong, there were four different samplings and each was very good, but the wedges were only slightly larger than the ones in the childhood game, Mouse Trap.    To sum it up, Vintage is a nice place if you are going for a side of ambiance with your vino, but I'd recommend Tria if you are looking for a decent accompaniment in the food category.

This is when an extra half star would come in handy.  I'm only giving three because I've been spoiled by the location in Marlton which is a hundred times nicer.  The lunch specials here are decent, but any roll deviating from the 8 or so standards will cost you.  Special rolls are kind of pricey for lunch but suitable for dinner.  The sushi is good but I probably wouldn't visit this location again unless I was picking up take-out.

Props to Dae Bak for handling our fairly tipsy and hungry group last night! A bunch of us were at Hop Sing for an event and decided to cross the street for some much-needed sustenance. We were seated at a large table by the window (fun people watching!) and kept servers busy with food orders and many rounds of Korean beer.   We started with a scallion pancake which seemed to include a lot more than scallions - maybe some seafood? All I know is that it was fried, filling, and exactly what I needed at that moment in time. The fried dumplings were also really tasty.   I did a chicken dolsot bibimbap bowl for my entree and it was extra sizzly. I spread the rice all around the bowl and it reached a very desirable level of crispiness. It's been a while since I've had a dolsot bibimbap bowl that was hot enough to achieve this and I was happy that Dae Bak's version was up for the challenge! Our servers were very sweet and really on top of everything.   Next time, I'd like to venture out of my comfort zone and try some other dishes!

Loved, loved, loved my first experience at Root on Friday night. I went for an early dinner in a small group and we were able to take advantage of the happy hour specials from our table. The rum old fashioned is how we kicked things off, and then I enjoyed several glasses of the vinho verde with my meal.   To start, we snacked on the fried chickpeas, crispy potatoes and corn zeppole. I could not get enough of those taters and chickpeas! We also enjoyed a cheese and salumi selection that was very nice, and a total steal with four selections at half the normal price.   Next, we shared the kale and escarole salad, spinach and ricotta gnudi, and meatballs. Each plate was absolutely delicious and I'd order any and all of them again.   Service was on point, relaxed and friendly. I really can't wait to get back to Root for another happy hour or dinner!

The long-awaited Rival Bros. coffee bar is as cool as the names of their signature roasts. The neighborhood seems to be on board big time - there have been people in and out every time I've swung by for a cup.   Last weekend, my fiancé picked up an herb scone from the bakery display and he made the mistake of giving me a bite. This was like no scone I've ever before tasted. Bakery products come from High Street on Market so it should have been no surprise that it was incredible.   Great addition to the neighborhood.

My second visit to Cafe Lift was even better than the first. I went with my boyfriend, who lives only a few blocks from Sabrina's. I told him that like Sabrina's, the food would be awesome and creative... and that unlike Sabrina's, there would be no hour-long waits outside, no hosts picking and choosing the next diners based on god-only-knows what criteria, and no elbow pads necessary as there would be ample room between tables. We walked in and sat down immediately.   Once my coffee was placed on the table, I searched the vicinity like a junkie for Sweet'N Low, but there were no pink packets in sight. Our server saved the day by procuring some from behind a counter. A few minutes later, she dropped off some complimentary chocolate chip bread pudding. I forgot all about that from last time so it was a nice surprise and really good.   My fritatta special with breakfast sausage, jack cheese and spinach was great. The bf had a panini with prosciutto, sharp provolone and some other items, which he loved.   Part of me wants to be greedy and not share Cafe Lift with others, but I also want this place to be around for a long, long time so I am obligated to spread the word. Get thyself to brunch!

This sunny little establishment serves up 100% fruit and veggie juices, plus frozen banana twirls and a few salad options. I've been there twice for juice, and I love that I can pick out one of the green juices and then customize it further by adding some apples to sweeten it up a bit. Can't wait to try their lemonade one hot day soon!

It has been a week since my last visit to Il Pittore, and still I cannot get the pasta coins with braised goat, mint and chili oil off my mind! Even if you're leery about goat (as I was), you should go for it. The meat is tender and soaked with flavor from the sauce. It's a very delicious pasta dish.   But to be honest, there isn't much at Il Pittore that isn't delicious. The bread basket arrives overflowing with house baked focaccia, rolls and crunchy breadsticks. The baked ricotta is generously portioned in a warm crock, with grilled focaccia alongside. The arugula salad provides a lighter option to start a meal, but at twelve dollars and with hardly any trace of the ricotta salata, it isn't a must-get.  In my opinion, the pastas at Il Pittore rival any other famous pasta makers' in the city. Pappardelle with wild boar and parmesan is wonderful, though I'd have a hard time choosing it over those aforementioned corzetti coins.   Deserts are nice but nothing to go crazy over (though the vanilla gelato is divine, served over little bits of chocolate crunch). At restaurants in the Il Pittore price range, you need to either accept the splurge and go all out or order very wisely. Personally, I'd be happy sharing an appetizer and two or three pasta dishes while savoring a couple glasses of wine and saving dessert for another time or another place.

I was the lucky guest of an invitee of Vernick's PR company to come in for dinner earlier this week. Though the upstairs area looks awesome with it's open air dining, we ended up sitting on the ground level in the back room, which was dim and relaxing with lots of wood, brick and gray accents. I felt miles from the heart of center city, when in reality it was right outside.   We started with the Maryland crab toast, which could have been great, but it was weighed down by a heavy mayo or similar dressing. I would have loved a lighter take with just some lemon and pepper. Fortunately, out of everything we ordered, this was the only disappointment. Our other starters, the grilled carrot salad with olive dressing and the shrimp and avocado salad, were both perfect. Each had just the right amount of varying textures and all ingredients shined.   My entree was the whole grilled dorade, stuffed with fennel (the veg part, not the seed, for all you like-minded fennel seed haters). It came with some random grilled lettuces and jalapenos, but I was happy to have ordered a side of sauteed greens. The fish itself was fantastic; super flavorful and expertly de-boned, except for one teeny renegade bone. At $38, it's definitely on the pricey side. I'm not sure I'd be so willing to order it again unless my dining partner wanted to share and order a couple sides to go along. It could definitely feed two people with the addition of some sides. My companion had the grilled black sea bass served over broccoli and roasted tomatoes. I really loved this dish - it was like having an Italian-style meal but without all the carbs.  For dessert, we tried the smoked hazelnut and chocolate parfait and the carrot cake. The parfait was great, but the carrot cake was heaven. Super moist and with just the right amount of creamy cream cheese icing, I had to ask our server to take it away so I didn't house the entire thing. A cup of L'Aube roast was the perfect touch. How I miss that café on South Street...  Also worth a look is the cocktail list, which is filled with classics and some new spins. I enjoyed a spicy margarita of sorts, served up in a rocks glass with a kick of cayenne. A green goddess drink featured a refreshing blend of vodka and cucumber.   There is a lot more on Vernick's menu that I'm anxious to try, and I just loved the space. I might even request to sit in that back room again on a future visit.

Love this new store on Walnut, and it's a definite upgrade from the previous tenant. I was surprised to find out that Madewell is part of the J Crew family. People say it's the younger sister of the brand, but the prices seemed just as... big sister-like. I didn't even look at the non-sale items. But I did make out with a new top, necklace and bracelet for under fifty dollars, which wasn't bad.   The clothes won't blow you away with originality; I found mostly basics that could be dressed up with some cool accessories. Solid.

Sarcone's makes the rolls that set the hoagie standard in Philadelphia. So how could the sandwiches from their deli be anything less than five-star worthy?  We arrived a couple hours before the first Eagles home game of the season. The two women working the counter were efficient. One had two phones in her hand while the other rang up orders and took walk-ins.   I was trying to keep it (relatively) healthy so I went with a turkey and cheese hoagie with lettuce, tomato, onions, pickles and hot peppers. The medium was the perfect size for enjoying half before the game (lunch!) and half after (dinner!). I tried a bite of the classic Italian and man was that good. Next time I go for more of a splurge, that's what I'm getting. And probably about a half pound of those sharp provolone-stuffed olives, too.

About 20-30% of my Christmas gifts for family and friends this year came from Open House. I really could have found something for anyone in that store. Fun, unique and quirky gifts were purchased for my brother, and I found the most perfect travel book for my boyfriend's parents, who are always jetting off to another exotic locale.   The prices are definitely high, though I still felt they were fair for most items. I saw some things that could be found cheaper at a Homegoods type of store, but I wasn't really there for those types of things anyway. I wanted unique and thoughtful gifts, and that's exactly what I found. Yay for shopping local!

We arrived at Forest & Main shortly before 5pm on a Friday, and the bar area was bumpin' for happy hour. We secured two seats at the bar and decided to stay there for dinner. Forest & Main is located in an old house, so having drinks at the bar felt like having drinks in a friend's den - so cozy and comfortable! We struck up a few conversations with friendly locals and had a great time.   There are about eight brews on tap. I started with the cider. It was served room temp which I don't care for - I should have tasted it first! I traded off halfway with my beau, who was drinking the Le Jeune. I enjoyed this style very much. Next, I went with the Fiso, which was bright and gently hopped. I liked it so much I ordered another.   For dinner, we started with the rosemary orange popcorn which was delightful. Slightly sweet and a little salty, it had a great flavor that wasn't too overpowering. There were a few specials on the night of our visit, so I ordered a skirt steak served with truffled mushrooms, fried cauliflower and hollandaise. The steak was cooked a perfect medium rare and the entire dish was great. My boyfriend enjoyed the chicken pie, which I thought was a little small for an entree. The fries we ordered on the side were great - served super hot, crispy and salty.   This was my first trip to Ambler and certainly not my last. I'm looking forward to a return visit to Forest & Main in the warmer months!

The closer City Fitness on South Street gets to completion, the closer I get to giving my notice at Sweat on Walnut. We've had a good year, but with the temptation of brand new equipment and clean everything, Sweat can't compete.   I generally hit the gym anywhere from two to four times a week exclusively to run on the treadmills. I choose the same machine every single day - one that's closest to the windows and without a TV, which usually guarantees that I won't have to work out on top of anyone else. So when the guy who cleans the equipment tries to squeeze through the half-foot between my machine and the wall, instead of simply walking around to the next aisle, my personal space feels a little compromised. I'm sure he's a very sweet guy; he seems to know the whole neighborhood. But even if he were a professional hockey player, I'd want him to back up off me while I'm trying to get my run on.   Mini-rant aside, the bottom line is that the machines are mega-old, the equipment is old, the locker rooms look old... you get the picture. Sweat, you are on borrowed time.

After the Yelp schwag was distributed at a record pace at the Night Market, we ended up at Kite & Key for a couple brews and a bite. We grabbed an outdoor table and enjoyed the crisp night air while sipping everything from west coast IPAs to Yard's ESA on cask (yum).   I was in the mood for something buffalo, so we ordered wings and asked for them well-done. Said wings came out rather quickly and didn't seem very well done, but it could also be because they were pretty large. While the buffalo sauce was nice and the blue cheese and ranch dipping sauces were on point (seriously, no skimping on the blue cheese), the wings were a little too juicy for my liking. No worries though, they also offer a buffalo chicken flatbread, which I'll likely hit up next time.   One beer turned into four, and before we knew it the windows were being closed since the patrons inside were getting chilly. We decided to join them at the bar to watch A-Rod take a swing of air so final it was felt all the way in Philly.   I really enjoyed myself at Kite & Key and I'll even go so far to say that I'd willingly go out of my way to hang out there again soon.

No me gusta.   At least, not for delivery. I have tried the tacos al pastor at Night Market, and they were incredible. I actually had to ask my boyfriend if he was sure that this was the same place.   Backing up to Sunday night, we had some friends over and we were all a bit hungover and indecisive. Somehow, the suggestion of taco delivery came up, and so we pulled up the menu for Los Taquitos de Puebla and spent a great deal of time making our selections. When the designated caller punched in the numbers, he was hung up on not once but twice. We should have taken it as an omen but didn't. We were going to get that order in, damnit! We found a way to place our order online. And then we waited.  Just moments after our expected wait time (one hour), the delivery guy arrived. We were all so excited to tear up some tacos! My first mistake was to order chicken tacos. The flour, chicken, lettuce, cheese and sour cream was congealed into one massive taco pizza thing. The tortillas were impossible to pick up so I just ate with a knife and fork. There were random bits of meat throughout, and the chicken was definitely not chopped with care to include only the tender, edible parts. I skeeve on fatty meat and random bits more than the average Jane so this, combined with my already unsettled tummy, was a big turnoff.   Meanwhile, my friend across the table took one bite of his tacos al pastor before his lips started tingling - a sign that his peanut allergy had been activated. When he tried calling the restaurant to see if they use peanut oil, the language barrier was too difficult and he received the dial tone yet again.   Moments ago, while typing this, my boyfriend pulled said friend's leftovers out of the fridge and stuck them in the toaster oven. I'd be lying if I said I didn't want a bite. They actually look far better now than they did the night they arrived.   The conclusion? Never, ever order taco delivery. I'll update this review once I try a meal at the establishment.

My first review of many on Yelp!  Went to Apamate with three girlfriends for dinner on Tuesday night.  We ordered 2 each of about 7 or 8 different things, since each dish has about two bites-worth of food.  My favorites were the little neck clams and seared salmon.  Everything else is basically a fading memory at this point.  The food was good but not good enough that I would want to go back... unless we're going for dessert.    I read the reviews so knew to order the churros; I don't think a day has gone by all week that I haven't thought about them again!  We tried the regular with cinnamon and sugar and a side of hot chocolate for dipping, the dulce de leche-filled and the Nutella-filled.  Each was better than the last, and I could have easily gone another round because they were THAT good (and I am a bottomless pit once I have a few drinks).  There were two servers working: the nice one and the mean one.  We lucked out and got the nice one, although the mean one did make a cameo appearance.  She dropped off a plate of shrimp, which we did not order.  When we told her this, she said it was on our order and walked away.  When we stopped laughing five minutes later, the nice server returned to pick up the shrimp and deliver them to their rightful owners a few tables down... more laughing and a couple "good thing we didn't lick them or something" remarks.    Bottom line: food- eh; churros- Amazing with a capital A; service- flip a coin!

I moved my business from Walgreens on 18th & South to CVS when it opened. I had a good rapport with the pharmacy staff at Walgreens but there were often long waits, strange clientele and a few instances when obtaining my prescription was somewhat of a hassle. I have never had an issue at the new CVS on the corner of 22nd and South. Everyone is super friendly, the pharmacist (Tim) always gives a call if there's a question or issue, and the store itself is clean and well-stocked. I'm a fan.

I'm going to update my review to four stars after another successful shopping trip at Madewell. A necklace I had my eye on last time was on sale, but when I attempted to pull it off the rack, a whole bunch of them got tangled in the process. One of the sales associates spent several minutes untangling them for me, which was super nice.   In the meantime, I made my way to the back of the store, where sale items were being additionally discounted another 40%. I tried on a handful of tops and decided to get two of them. Both are pretty unique and I have a feeling I'll be getting a lot of wear out of them this season.   There were several bags and shoes that also grabbed my attention, but the prices in that department are a little steep. I did score a $10 off online card with my purchase so perhaps I'll take a gander to see what's on sale.

I had not anticipated ever returning to this McCormick's location after my prior experience, but an unexpected turn of events had me back for round 2.  I grabbed a high top in the bar area and waited for my friends to arrive, while perusing the March Madness happy hour menu, which was being offered from 9 p.m. to close.  I sipped on a slightly dirty vodka martini with gorgonzola stuffed olives that was made to perfection.  Things were off to an excellent start.    When my friends arrived, one went into complete shock when he saw a half pound burger with fries for $1.99 on the menu.  Men... so easy to please!  We also selected potato balls for $1.99, mussels in red sauce and steamed clams, each still a bargain at $4.95.  It seemed like a lot of time elapsed between ordering our food and receiving it, but it was worth the wait.  My friend's burger was a tad dry but I also think he ordered it well done, which would explain that.  Still, he was happy.  The potato balls were like fried mashed potatoes, with a delicious horseradish sauce on the side that I wanted to dip anything and everything into.  The mussels and clams were very generous portions, and were served piping hot.  The only thing that would have made them better would be some bread on the side, to dip in the leftover red sauce from the mussels.    Drink prices are not reduced during the happy hour, but since the food is so inexpensive it really makes for a cheap night out.  I would not be opposed to returning again, but only to hang out in the bar area.

I ordered delivery from Square on Square one day this week just before noon. Though the food delivery websites stated that the only option at the time was for pick-up, I called the restaurant and they confirmed that they could deliver. So, keep that in mind if you want delivery.   I ordered a quart of wonton soup and chicken with spicy garlic sauce. The food was very tasty, and definitely better quality than some other Chinese take-out spots, but also more expensive. The chicken portion was on the smaller side though I did still get two small meals out of it, since I also had the soup.   I'll definitely give these guys another shot the next time I'm craving Chinese - would love to try some of their other options.

A nightcap (or two) at the garden bar on a perfect summer night is about as magical as it gets in Philadelphia. After dinner in Queen Village, we decided to take a stroll and grab a drink, when we realized how close were were to Talula's. There were only a few people left at the bar when we arrived, and soon it was just the two of us.   The cocktail list is full of refreshing options for summer. I tried their take on a Moscow Mule - it was tasty, but I do wish it was served in a copper mug. Drinks are pricey, with most in the $11-$15 range. That adds up quickly! Our bartender was great, and happy to answer questions. I'm really jonesing to return for a romantic dinner on the patio. Talula's is definitely in the running for my birthday dinner later this summer!

A group of family and friends and I had a really great experience at Firebirds in Moorestown in early December. We arrived right around 4pm, the beginning of happy hour (which lasts until 7, by the way - heck yes!), and sat at some high top tables by the fire. The bartender was our server and she was great about prompt drink orders and water refills throughout our stay.   Happy hour specials are pretty solid, and we ordered several rounds of drinks and a bunch of apps to share. Favorites were the soft pretzels with beer cheese and chicken tenders with all the sauces they have available because your girl right here loves some sauce options.   We did notice that the buns for our sliders were really hard and we mentioned something to our server about it. The manager came over to chat with us and graciously sent out another plate of chicken tenders and removed the sliders from our check. Such a nice gesture and definitely gave this place points in my book. I'm sure we'll all return for another happy hour sesh in the future!

I keep getting prompted to write a review for Barcelona since I checked-in there during my Labor Day weekend trip to St. Louis. But honestly, my experience didn't go too far beyond chatting with the cute young bartenders and downing far too many shots of high-end tequila with my sister from another mister, Aimee K. The bar was a pretty lively spot on a Saturday night and the food that went by looked good, though we didn't order anything. The bathrooms were clean. Next time I'm in St. Louis, I'll return to Barcelona and I'll actually get some food to go along with my tequila.

The last minute decision to try Tre Famiglia was reached because of the restaurant's close proximity to my apartment, along with the added bonus that it was a BYO that I had yet to try.  With no reservations, I was nervous about how my party of two would be received upon entering the restaurant, but the hostess greeted us warmly and quickly seated us at an open table.  It was located in the center of the first dining room, which was slightly claustrophobic and very noisy.  Alas, beggars cannot be choosers much like people with no reservations should be damn happy to even get a table at 7:30 on a Saturday night.  We started with the calamari, a perfectly sized portion of tender rings with a large cup of red sauce.  I almost always ask for additional sides of sauce as I am a lover of condiments in excessive quantities, but there was no need in this case which was great.  I would be remiss if I did not also mention the delicious olive oil that came along with the bread basket.    For dinner, I tried the tilapia livornese.  The large fillets were bathed in a tomato sauce with capers and salty halved olives, and were served alongside buttery julienned vegetables and a pile of creamy risotto.  Give me that fillet of fish, indeed!  This was easily one of the best entrees I've had all year.    I almost felt a little sorry for my dining companion, who ordered ziti with grilled chicken, tomatoes and broccoli rabe in a white wine sauce.  I tried a bite from his plate and we both agreed that while the components were good, the ziti did not taste like it was homemade (I checked the website and sure enough, the pasta is "imported").  I'd imagine this is rough for an Italian who claims to make his own from scratch.  Full from dinner, we skipped dessert and opted for coffee, which was strong and very tasty.  I'll probably return but will make reservations for the other dining room, which was slightly nicer.  I'd also stick to non-pasta options in favor of the many other seafood or protein selections.

This super cute market is located too close to me that I have only been once. I'm going to rectify that situation, especially now that I know they have a small but comprehensive selection of foodstuffs packaged to-go, veggies, coffee (I'm 99% sure it was my love, La Colombe), baked goodies and a varied menu great for lunch or dinner. There's also seating downstairs, which seemed to be a popular choice on the day of my visit.   I ordered an egg white breakfast burrito which was perfectly-sized and had a nice distribution of all ingredients. The salsa was served on the side, which saved me from any burrito mishaps. I'd probably ask for an extra side next time, since I eat everything breakfast-y laden with either salsa or ketchup. Can't wait to check out the other menu items, and pick up some of that delish-looking chicken salad to go!

I've only stopped by Tredici Enoteca for after-dinner drinks, but I can tell it's about to become one of my favorite spots. The wine selection is carefully curated and prices range from moderate to indulgent. I had a glass of the most fantastic verdicchio from the cruvinet and followed that up with some fabulous sparkling rosé.   The restaurant is larger than it appears from the outside, which I was happy to see, since I keep hearing how popular this place has become already. I really loved the sleek, upscale vibe, and I felt like I was in another city. Can't wait to return for a bite and many more glasses of wine!

Last night's Dîner en Blanc may have been the best party I've ever attended in Philly. And I've been to some parties, friends. It was really amazing to see so many people adhere to the strict guidelines that make this event so special - all white attire, tables no larger than 32", white linens, white place settings, white table decorations. Pulling together our load before the event, I wondered how everyone would fare with getting themselves to the meeting points and then to the final location. Philly impressed big time; everyone got it together and did so beautifully and with grace!  Table set-up was much easier than I expected. Everyone was willing to listen and participate which made the night that much better. At 7:30, we waved our napkins in the air and dinner commenced. My boyfriend and I brought a bottle of wine from our trip to Healdsburg, CA that we had been saving for a special occasion. It tasted even better than we remembered. Perhaps it was the company of 1300 people all having the time of their lives.   When the sky darkened, sparklers were ignited and the DJ turned up the volume. It wasn't long before people took the dance floor to the fountain. It was a fun little twist that had Philly written all over it. We can do classy, but we're not going to sacrifice any fun, either.   Seeing so many people smiling, laughing, taking photos and embracing their loved ones was a really awesome sight. The City of Brotherly Love is alive and well. I cannot wait until next year's fête!

Oh how I wish my pants had an elastic band.  Just finished brunch with 8 friends at Cafe Lift and it was gut-bustingly delicious.  Since they don't take reservations, I arrived early to see if I could get a table in the works for our large group.  By the time everyone arrived, we were seated without a problem and popping bottles of champagne for mimosas (it's byo, by the way).  Our server was efficient and kept the oj coming.  I ordered a fritatta with pancetta, sauteed onions, roasted red peppers and gorgonzola.  In an effort to curb calories somewhere in the meal, I asked for egg whites.  This was met with some hesitation (something about the fritatta not rising with only egg whites), so I asked for all the same ingredients in an egg white omelet.  When breakfast arrived soon after, my egg white frittata was indeed on the plate... so not sure what all the rising business was about, but it was fantastic!  Whole grain toast and potatoes were served alongside.    9 people left absolutely stuffed for under twenty bucks a person.  I will definitely be back!

If there was unfinished shopping or a lack of funds due to the season, it was not evident at Sampan on Christmas Eve-Eve.  The place resembled a busy Saturday night with no signs of slowing down at 8 p.m.  The décor was clean and dark, except for the glow of the ever-changing walls that filled the room.    Our server was pleasant as was every staff member we encountered on our visit.  The most memorable character was undoubtedly the food runner, who was filled with energy and clearly loved his job.      The menu had a ton of wonderful sounding dishes, and the buzz about the edamame dumplings was so fierce that they were immediately placed on the list of things to try.  The dumplings were light but full of buttery flavored goodness.  I don't think I could return and not order them again.  Same with the crab and curry fritters, my other favorite of the evening.  Like miniature crab cakes, they were packed with spice and heat, and went perfectly with the cucumber yogurt that rested underneath.    Other dishes I tried were the duck pancakes, which were dressed perfectly and with just the right amount of crunch from the veggies, the crispy chili crab noodles and the lobster gyoza.  The latter two were just okay for me, as I found them both on the very salty side.    The only dish I didn't try was the pork banh mi, which my date touted as one of the best he's had in the city.    We passed on dessert, although the miniature soft serve ice cream cones were adorable.  Next time!

I'm still going with the old A-OK for Fado. It's not a place that would become a destination on a regular night out, but when I revisited last week for Marcello's Flyers Faithful event, I had a good time. The bathrooms are still kind of scrummy and haven't been updated since my previous visit, but the rest of the place is all right. The sound system was impressively loud. Maybe a little too much, but I guess it was better to be a tad too loud than not loud enough considering we were all playing a game.   Our server stopped by regularly and split checks without even being asked, which was appreciated. I munched on fried pickles and sipped diet coke so I don't have much to say about the food, although I did like their version of fried dill chips. This bar holds a definite spot in my past but I'm okay with a return visit from time to time.

This review is for Memphis Taproom's beer garden, which is one of my favorite places to hang in the summer. I've actually never even had a beer in Memphis Taproom itself, though I've heard great things about their food so I'll have to try it sometime. But in the warm months, there's nothing that's going to separate me from that garden. Well, maybe a torrential downpour in the middle of an otherwise sunny day.   Why would you go inside when you've got lots of picnic tables (partial shade in some areas but don't forget the SPF!), cans of craft beer (with beer tab recycling program!) and awesomely creative hot dogs (veggie dogs available upon request!). The canned beer is a rotating list, which rocks. The hot dogs offer something for everyone. On my recent visit, a friend and I shared a deep fried dog with sauerkraut, onions and mustard and a grilled dog with chili, cheddar and macaroni salad. Hiyoooo!

Noble's earthy tones and woodsy decor make me feel like I'm in a treehouse. A grown-up treehouse, of course, with refined food, inventive cocktails and interesting bartenders.   I've only had dinner there once, which was delicious, but I typically find myself at Noble for the cocktail scene. First of all, Christian Gaal is on staff, so you know the libations are for serious (although every 'tender there knows how to make an excellent drink).  Most recently I enjoyed a simple drink from the menu which consisted of Bombay gin, housemade tonic and lemon. It was effervescent and clean, exactly what I wanted. Now that the weather is showing signs of warmth, I imagine I'll be back quite a bit to take advantage of the open window seating from my city treehouse.
