Free People is starting to take more of my money than Madewell, and that's saying something. My past couple experiences at this location have been great, with Sara upstairs helping me with outfit suggestions.   This store is always presented really beautifully, but as a savvy shopper, I rarely spend much time up front. Free People is notoriously expensive at full price but, once things go on sale, it's a whole new ballgame. I've found some great stuff in the sale racks, though you have to be prepared to really comb through as everything is squeezed together.   Finally, I'm obsessed with the reusable bags they give for purchases. I use these all the time over other reusable bags simply because they're so pretty.

Very cool venue in an inconspicuous area of Fishtown! I attended the inaugural Cooking Up Couture event at Front & Palmer on Friday night. The venue has several different areas which makes it perfect for a party that has to transition from cocktail hour to the main event. The decor was pretty industrial and open; brick walls, wood floors, exposed ductwork, etc. The only issue that stood out to me was the acoustics; the music and announcements seemed to echo around the larger room which made it hard to understand yet still extremely loud.    Because of the location, I probably wouldn't host an event with lots of out of town guests at Front & Palmer, though I'd absolutely host some type of cool function focused on city dwellers.

I've revisited this sweetgreen location a few times and haven't had any issues since my first experience early on. Last night I ordered the harvest bowl, which was delicious. I opted for dressing on the side and tried two different ones; I liked the curry yogurt for this particular salad a lot more than the balsamic vinaigrette. The salad was a nice size and all of the ingredients were very fresh and flavorful. Dinner was healthy but hearty, a combo I can get behind!

I can't really explain why I wasn't super satisfied with my experience at Llama Tooth, I just wasn't. The outside patio is gorgeous but it was like a graveyard on a perfectly nice Saturday afternoon. Besides our group of six, there were only two other tables occupied in the large space.   Krista P and I split a carafe of sangria, which yielded about four drinks total. With no guests in the restaurant and only a few outside, it took longer than expected for our round of bevvies to appear.   We didn't try anything from the food menu, so I can't comment there. I probably need to give Llama Tooth another chance... but with so many options in the city and limited funding, I'm not sure a return trip is in the cards.

I popped into Lost & Found over the weekend and walked out with two shirts for a little over sixty bucks total. The collection of tops, bottoms and dresses is small but nicely curated, and the sizing of the pieces seemed to be more in line with women's clothing than junior's clothing, which is often an issue with boutique stores. I also noticed that mostly everything I looked at was reduced in price. Not sure if I was just there during a sale or what, but I was happy.  The dressing rooms have super breezy curtains - be cautious! The mirrors are located outside the room and on a slant. The owner promised me that no one had ever returned an item due to false advertising in the slanted mirror! I tried my shirts on as soon as I got home and liked them just as much as I had at the store, slanted mirror or not. I'll definitely stop back in the next time I'm shopping in Old City.

I attended a wedding at Jack's Firehouse on Saturday night and I honestly can't think of one thing that would have made it better. The staff at Jack's was on point - everyone I encountered was friendly, professional and helpful.   The ceremony was held on the first floor behind the bar. It was a bit of a tight squeeze and a lot of folks were left standing but having everyone so close together made for an intimate vibe. After the ceremony, cocktails and hors d'oeuvres were served in the bar area and the outdoor space in front and to the side of the restaurant. I saw plenty of interesting looking cocktails making the rounds but a full bar was available as well. Having so many drinks prepared in advance was a great idea - everyone had a drink in hand within minutes after the ceremony and there really wasn't a wait at the bar for the rest of the night.   The passed apps during the cocktail hour were plentiful (and also really tasty) and ran the gamut from bruschetta to steak tips with blue cheese fondue. Meanwhile, chairs from the ceremony were cleared and the area behind the bar became the dance floor.   Upstairs, a buffet-style dinner was served, featuring everything from salads and pastas to fish and carved meats. There was a lot of seating upstairs which fortunately freed up the even better seating downstairs in the outdoor area.   The party was still going strong at 11:30 when I hit the wall and had to turn in for the night, but what a blast. If you're looking to host a wedding at an alternative venue, I'd strongly suggest checking out Jack's.

Walking through the garden on a hot and humid Friday night, I was relieved to be sitting inside. But only because of the weather. The garden itself is a wonderland of flora, lights and the sounds of trickling water. Truly magical.   Inside, the decor is a little more country farmhouse chic, and while the decorations can be a bit overdone in some areas, the overall feeling is very comfortable. We started with the seasonal sangria, served with fresh blueberries, green apple and basil. It was a refreshing choice for the day and I stuck with it on a second round.   First up was "Not Your Granny's" cheese plate, consisting of six cheeses ranging from soft and slightly funky to a bold blue. Each came served along an appropriate accompaniment, and a ramekin with the most delicious flatbreads.   Next we shared the peekytoe crab and lobster salad. I wasn't sure what to make of this, because every bite was different and I alternated between liking it a lot and not being so sure. I do have to admit, the substance covering the salad was a bit off-putting and I later noticed a neighboring diner picking around it as well.   Fortunately, my main course of seared scallops with pine nuts and watercress picked things up again. The scallops were cooked perfectly. I was also so happy we ordered the delicious chard and braised leek gratinee at the last minute - it went perfectly with our dishes, and provided just enough food for a filling (but not too filling) dinner. Art had the wild striped bass with red quinoa, which he absolutely loved.  For dessert, French press coffee and the gooseberry almond crumble, served with black pepper meringue and heavenly lemon ice cream that I would personally like to order by the vat.

I had a craving for some not-so-healthy, food court-style Chinese food. The kind of stuff we referred to as "crunchy chicken" as kids. I know many of the reviews for this restaurant focus on some of the more traditional plates, but Xi'an Sizzling Woks came through for my basic cravings all the same.   First off, I would have felt like a total loser if I didn't at least order something traditional/raved about in reviews. So I opted for the noodles with ginger scallion sauce. Unfortunately, I think these are probably best when ordered for dine-in. They were a bit dry and my husband didn't like them much at all. I was fine with them but they are the lone remaining item in the fridge.   We also ordered (please reserve judgement at this time): egg rolls, scallion pancakes, general tso's chicken and garlic chicken. 1990 called and I was there to answer.   In my opinion, this was the best Chinese takeout I've had in a while. Everything was packaged so nicely - no spills, and there were sauce packets, chopsticks and fortune cookies. The food tasted exactly how I hoped - hot and crispy, sinful and satisfying.   I don't think my husband was as big a fan as me, but I was pretty happy with the order. I ordered via Eat24 and the delivery was roughly on time and prices were better than other spots I've ordered from in the recent past. I've already recommended the biz to another Yelper and will likely order from Xi'an again in the future.

I went to Bourbon Blue for a brunch meet-up on Sunday, and I was extremely impressed with the entire experience, particularly with the service!   The hostess offered to check coats and chit chatted with us as we waited for our table. We had a fairly large group of about 15, and we were seated in a relatively empty section (until the restaurant started getting more crowded). That was great as we were all excited to meet one another and gab it up.   Our server was, simply put, on his A-game. He filled waters for everyone at the table, and then put carafes of water down so we could refill at any time. A couple of us were drinking coffee like it was going out of style, and a thermos was placed on the table so we could top off our mugs. Great thinking!   I ordered the crab cake eggs benedict, hollandaise on the side, add spinach. I know I was asking a lot considering the large group, but my dish came out exactly as requested. Also, everyone had their plate in front of them within minutes - no long wait for the entire table to be served. I thought my dish was very tasty. Perhaps the potatoes could have been more seasoned, but overall I thought it was really solid. The eggs were perfectly poached.    I was curious to see what would happen once the check was dropped, and had cash ready to avoid the usual credit card confusion. To my surprise, we were all presented with individual checks! I'm sure our group leader requested this in advance but I thought it was so incredibly nice of the restaurant and our server to accommodate us in this way.   Excellent experience at Bourbon Blue! I would highly recommend the restaurant for a group - they really have it down!

When Christopher R. suggested the Baja Room for an impromptu post-yelp event gathering, I was perplexed. How had I never heard of this Mexican outpost with outdoor seating and strong-azz margaritas, located right on South Street?   Sure enough, we took a cab to 15th and South and there it was, just across the street from Pico de Gallo, its sister establishment. A little entryway in the tall picket fence on 15th led to a patio containing four large picnic tables with red checkered tablecloths.   We wasted no time ordering up pitchers of margs and appetizers. The margaritas were curiously delicious, and I later found out that they were homemade with fresh lime juice and love.   The meatless nachos were easily my favorite of the foodstuffs, as evidenced by the fact that I woofed them down like I was going to win a cash prize for speed-eating. They were loaded with cheese, a spicy green salsa, pickled jalapenos, beans and sour cream. We had to order guacamole separate, which featured under-ripe avocados and a ten dollar price tag. On the flip side, there was a communication breakdown somewhere between our server and the kitchen, and we received an extra plate of nachos on the house.   The tacos were served like street tacos - loaded with the protein of choice (in our case, octopus and seared tuna) and a few basic ingredients. The octopus version was pretty solid and I wouldn't mind trying them again (I didn't taste the tuna ones so I'm not sure how those went down).    The staff was friendly and the place was chill. I'll definitely hit Baja Room again on another warm night.

Because my boyfriend is wonderful (and because I look like a scary Medusa when I wake up), he offered to pick up coffee and breakfast this morning. We pondered our options and settled on Healthy Bites to Go, which was a new one for me. After perusing the online menu, I noted that many items were not in fact all that healthy, but I brushed that thought aside as I selected my bacon, egg and cheese on an everything bagel.   At $7.50, it didn't come cheap, but boy was it delicious. The bacon was peppered on the edges and the cheese was actually a local cheddar. Delish. It was a bit heavy for my usual breakfast tastes but it will make for a perfect hangover meal at some point in the (near?) future.  Also, the coffee was great. A bajillion points for that. We'll return.

I finally made it to the Royal for dinner. Our Cuban spring rolls were tasty, but my boyfriend's chicken Frankie wrap was off-the-chain. In fact, it was so fantastic, I lost interest in my Caesar salad about half way through. The polenta croutons and somewhat odd sour cream dressing did nothing for me. My sister, who ordered the same thing, shared this sentiment, though she soldiered on. Fortunately, I was able to score multiple bites of the Frankie - soft lovash stuffed with curried chicken deliciousness. The fries alongside were hot, crisp and delicious, as always.  But the real stunner of the night? Truffled parmesan popcorn. It was so good, we debated getting another order to-go for our walk to the POPE (let the record state, we did not actually do this). Best thing pocket change can buy.

Central Park Corp. should file a lawsuit against this place for insinuating that their bagels are even close to something New York would produce. These things are balls of dough, some with seasonings. A toasted bagel is indistinguishable from one that isn't toasted. But if you ask for toasted, keep an eye out, because your "bagel" will sit on the counter until you have to ask for it. Terrible. If you want a real bagel, you must drive to North Jersey. One of the few things (I will admit) they do better.

My boyfriend and I went to Entree for dinner recently. Reservations for the weekend are a good idea; we saw several people get turned away. Most of the restaurant was reserved for a larger party that fortunately came in at the tail end of our meal. We were seated up front by the window. There wasn't a whole lot of room between tables. Also, it was quite chilly with the front door constantly opening and closing - wear something warm just in case!  Our server was nice but maybe a little inexperienced. Silverware was not replaced between courses; it was taken from our plates and placed back on the table. One of our dishes was swept away with a few bites left though we weren't asked if we were finished.   That said, the food was pretty good. We shared the wedge salad, mussels and calamari to start. The wedge was fine, the dressing was nice. The mussels were really good - I really loved the broth and the bread served under the pile of mussels sopped up that broth really nicely without getting too soggy, somehow. The calamari was a little overcooked but still tasty.   My main dish was broccoli rabe ravioli served in marsala cream sauce. The ravioli were topped with a mix of artichokes, olives and other tasty bits that I can't remember. The flavors were unexpected and unique but I really liked the dish. My boyfriend had a bite and was not a fan. He seemed happy with his steak, though.   We skipped dessert but there were a few options. I'd be willing to check out Entree again sometime.

I love this place, and I wish it was in my neighborhood!   While I don't get to the Fairmount area too often, I think Bar Hygge is worth a trip. From house-made brews to a thoughtful wine list, cocktails and impressive whiskey selection, they have libations covered.   The dinner menu is filled with surprises, like the build-your-own board. A handful of cheese and charcuterie options are there, but there are also tons of interesting selections like charred octopus, calabrian chili arancini, roasted sunchokes and much more. Great idea and super unique!  The rest of the menu offers a mix of elevated bar food and a nice array of entrees. There is an impressive use of vegetables across the menu and the descriptions sound really enticing. Though I only had a few bites from a board on my recent visit, I've got Bar Hygge at the top of mind for the next time I want to try something new and different for dinner.

My sister and I popped into Healthy Garden for lunch recently. The name implies that the business would be geared entirely towards healthy foods, but the menu read more like something from a diner, only with a lot of salad, juice and smoothie options. There were quite a few fried options available, and the restaurant itself looked like it had been a pizza parlor in a former life. So there's a lack of consistency across the board.   That said, the food itself was solid. We each had salads and juices. The juices were huge and priced really well for the size. The salads were also enormous and large enough for two meals. All ingredients were very fresh, and the dressings were great.   If I were in the area, I'd be down for some takeout but I probably wouldn't dine in again.

A five dollar cover and beat service on my last visit is the reason for my downgrade.  Cover charges are for places that make Arthur Kade feel special and shore bars.    Time is never the destination, yet it can be a viable option when you find yourself in the Midtown area without a plan (just not on Saturday night - see cover charge).  That's probably not the best description to give a place, but it's accurate for Time.

I recently had a working lunch at Rose Tattoo Cafe. The last time I had been there was about thirteen years ago with my college beau. At the time, Rose Tattoo felt romantic and the menu seemed exciting. On my recent visit, I was shocked by how little the place had changed, which made it feel and look extremely dated.   The menu didn't provide many exciting options. I had a crab cake sandwich with fries that was fine but nothing memorable. Our server, while nice, was slow and had several mixups. Rose Tattoo was better as a memory.

Excellent experience with illexotics on Sunday! I'd been meaning to take my orchid there for a while for some much-needed TLC. Over the weekend, I was gifted a funky new planter, which was the sign I needed to get over to East Passyunk.   The store is so cool; gorgeous plants everywhere, plus reptiles and amphibians (and some insects that I chose to ignore). The house chameleon, Blaze Blu, is so beautiful!   I was surprised by the activity going on at the store; there were quite a few people who were in and out during my brief visits to drop off and pick up. The guys who own the shop were so knowledgeable and pleasant!   I picked out a new planter for my orchid, and was given a selection of plants that would be a good fit for my other planter. The end result was even better than I hoped for; my orchid looks so amazing since being re-potted, and my new plant is a happy addition to my home. I will be returning for all my indoor flora needs from here on out!

This is actually a review for Rizzieri's spa as I've never actually received services at their salon. I've gone on two separate occasions. The first time, I had a wonderful massage with Sandy. This week, I had a facial with Christina.   Backing up to when my trio arrived, we admittedly walked in right at our appointment time, which is definitely a spa faux pas. We were extremely apologetic and even offered to pay the receptionist up front before our treatments, which she turned down. I wouldn't go so far as to say that she was rude, but she definitely wasn't warm and friendly.   We robed up in record time and walked into the waiting lounge just as my name was being called. Christina has fiery red hair and bears a striking resemblance to Mad Men's Christina Hendricks. She also gives great facial. For an hour I was rubbed with potions and creams all while nestled in a cocoon of blankets, my hands covered in lotion and inserted into warming mitts. My neck and shoulders received plenty of attention also, and the tightness in my neck from some recent strength training has completely vanished.   At the beginning of my session, Christina offered to write down some recommended products after we discussed my skin. After our respective appointments, my mom and I paid together and it was then that we realized the receptionist had papers for another woman with the same name as me but a different address. We pointed this out but she didn't really seem to make any corrections on her computer. In the shuffle, I never did receive the papers that had the suggested products. I'm sure that other Michelle will appreciate it on her next visit.   A spa experience should be just that, an experience. From the time she walks in to the time she walks out, a woman should feel like she has no cares in the world. I really only felt that way during my treatment, since the customer service at the reception was no better than what I'd expect from a department store. Nonetheless, I would definitely return since the treatments I've received from Sandy and Christina and the facility itself are top notch.

One billion weeks ago*, I fractured my ankle. After five weeks in a boot and four weeks in a brace, I was finally cleared to start physical therapy. My husband had been to Zarett before, and it also happens to be in our neighborhood, so I made an appointment and started my rehab.   It's been four weeks so far and, while I still have some time to go, I am so pleased with the results and the care I've received thus far. The staff members at this facility are incredible. Everyone I have encountered is professional, friendly and engaged.   My sessions start out with a ten minute warm up and then go into a solid thirty minutes or so of strength and balance work. The trainers rotate, but no one misses a beat from one session to the next because of thorough note taking. My sessions started out pretty moderate but have increased in difficulty over the weeks. I love that I feel like I'm getting an amazing workout in addition to rehabbing my injured ankle. After so many weeks of feeling out of sync in my body I am finally starting to feel like myself again.   After training sessions I head down to the physical therapy area where I usually see Ilan or, sometimes, one of the other therapists if he's not there. We talk about my progress while my injured ankle gets some extra attention. All of the therapists really know their stuff and I trust them - even when they are angling my body into weird directions that feel anything but natural.   I'm very much looking forward to the day when I'm injury-free, but I'll actually be a little sad when my rehab is over and I'm back to my usual gym. Pretty sure that's about as great an experience one could have at a rehab facility!     *Okay, 13 weeks ago, but it feels like one billion.

I've used Philadelphia Flower Co. on several occasions and have always been very happy with my orders and the service I've received.   Before my wedding, I called to order arrangements for my mom/stepdad, dad/stepmom and fiancé's parents. When I asked if they delivered to NJ (where both sets of my parents live), they initially said no, but they made an exception since they are still relatively close to the city. The delivery charge was slightly higher, but worth it since I have been so happy with Philadelphia Flower Co. in the past.   All of the flowers arrived the next day as promised. I was worried at first when my mom revealed that she had not been home all day, but there was a note in the mailbox that the flowers were left with our neighbor. All of the arrangements looked great and everyone was happy to have flowers in the house for the big weekend. I will definitely continue to call Philadelphia Flower Co. whenever the need arises!

To celebrate a pizza-loving friend's birthday, a group of us went here last week for dinner.  The staff was very friendly and the place was crowded- usually a good sign.  We were seated in the middle of the room, and every time the door opened, a draft took over.  Luckily, I had opted out of my usual camisole and jeans combo in favor of comfy layers to guard against the cold.  Otherwise, I would have been freezing.  We started with the polenta bread and a salad from the seasonal menu that had goat cheese, grapes and cranberries.  Everyone was pretty happy with both, especially the polenta bread.    After much hemming and hawing, we decided on a spinach ricotta pizza and a caramelized onion and prosciutto pizza.  Both were okay... but as so many pizza places go in Philly, not great.  Something seemed to be lacking in the spinach ricotta pizza, and the prosciutto on the other pizza resembled little squares of lunch meat ham.   Strangely, there was no dessert menu, so the meal ended after we finished our second bottle of red.  Normally, we would have popped open another bottle and hung out, but we noticed the corking fee sign posted conveniently on the wall which stated that a fee went into effect after "one bottle for every two people."  We packed up and peaced out in search of more wino-friendly pastures.

Swung through for lunch on Friday and was quite pleased with my chicken dol sot bibimbap. It didn't take very long before my number was called and I had a large sizzling bowl in front of me, with a side of that red spicy sauce to mix in, and some kimchee for a kick.   There were loads of veggies and nothing in the bowl was greasy. In fact, I'd suggest this as a solid option for a healthy lunch.

Plagued once again with a craving for sushi, I decided it was time to check out Sagami.  After hearing so many great things about the place, I'm not sure why it took me 2+ years to go to a restaurant in my own town.  I think the Route 130 location was a turn-off for me.  Anyway, I made my way over after work and got there a few minutes before 5:30, which is when they open.  There were several other people waiting in their cars as well.   Once inside, I made the mental note to never again wear heels to this establishment.  The ceilings were way low!  Other than that, the place was surprisingly cozy, dark and warm.  I felt like I was in the Japanese restaurant version of my grandparents' basement.  I know I've used this comparison before, but be assured that any place that reminds me of my grandparents' house is a really good thing!    The service was friendly and hella-fast.  Since I was dining alone, it didn't matter much but had I been with company it would have felt too rushed.  The food was very good, but Oh Yoko remains my favorite local spot for sushi.  Sagami has a decent menu but nothing fancy.  The price is definitely right, though.  Clear soup, a yellowtail and scallion roll and a spicy tuna roll came to under $15, plus tip.  I wanted to do a happy sushi dance, but refrained from doing so until I was back at my apartment.

I seriously love this place.  The menu looks like a newspaper and there are 3 pages full of items for adults and one page for kids.  There are about thirty different varieties of grilled cheese, and breakfast is served all day, every day.  The best thing about their breakfast is that the menu deviates so far from the traditional fare on diner menus.  Last Saturday I had a "Farmer's Market" egg white omelet with Swiss cheese, herbs and tons of fresh veggies.  There were about 12 other original omelets featured, as well as a "create your own" option.  The wheat toast that came with my order was thick-cut and grainy.  In other words, bangin'.     There are also loads of salads, sandwiches, soups and platters to satisfy any craving.  My sister loves the Foghorn Country Chicken salad, and it's so big that I have never seen her finish it.   Last but definitely not least, there is a HUGE ice cream menu that puts the Friendly's version from my childhood to shame.

Definitely not a bad stop for all your craft beer needs. There's a pretty decent selection for both refrigerated and non-refrigerated bottles. Prices seem to be on the more affordable side when compared with other local shops, at least for the larger-sized bottles.   The woman working the counter didn't say very much while we were in the store, if anything at all. So if you're looking to have a conversation about the suds, or if you need a recommendation, I'd probably shop elsewhere. But if you're open to adventure or you know what you're looking for, this is a great spot.

Victory Beer Hall is where I end up most every time I'm at Xfinity Live. I love the great beer selection and the food menu is pretty large and covers all bases. But service ranges from decent to abysmal.   On a busy night before a game, our party received apps before drinks, and our server was nowhere in sight for long periods of time. Food usually comes out quickly, which is good if you are trying to get to one of the stadiums; the service is what slows things down.   I've had the buffalo chicken wrap, buffalo chicken salad, and various appetizers and everything has been great. It's the perfect place for junk food, but there are salads with grilled chicken for when you want to be healthy.  I've also seen live acoustic sets, which is always fun. Xfinity Live can be hit or miss but Victory is a hit most of the time.

Thank you, P'unk Burger, for providing quality, BS-free proteins, in a plethora of ways (on a bun, as a salad, with lettuce leaves) and with an abundance of add-on options, from sauce to cheese to veggies to fried things to proteins and everything in-between.   I thoroughly enjoyed my incredibly juicy burger with tomato, caramelized onions, guacamole, pickles and mustard, wrapped in lettuce, last week. I cannot wait to try some of the fries next time - they smelled incredible!   Friendly service. Cash only (ATM on the premises).

Still so much love for Animo but, unfortunately, this location always - always - misses the mark. From forgotten salad dressings to guac with no chips to salads and burrito bowls that are missing ingredients. I love my go-tos from Animo but have basically had to accept that something is always going to be off when I place an order for pick up or delivery. I really hope their management is paying attention to reviews and does something to ensure better quality in the future.

On weekend mornings, when the craving for a leisurely brunch strikes, there is only one place on my mind as of late: Royal Tavern.   The bar has a chill vibe with servers to match. They constantly come around with water or coffee refills, which are often necessary depending on how late the previous evening lasted. Food selections are solid and range from the sweet (homemade granola with lavender honey) to the savory (cubano omelet with pickle salad and breakfast potatoes).  Easily, my favorite thing about The Royal is their bloody Mary. It has the most incredible taste with just the right kick of spice, and is garnished with a spicy pickle spear and lemon and lime wedges. The bloody is also offered with bacon vodka, although I've never tried this version.  Brunch is served starting at 10am on weekends, which is on the early side compared to most other bar/restaurants. Oddly enough, I have never visited for any reason other than brunch. I'm going to have to rectify that very soon.

Okay, I have to give some credit to Cava because I was impressed with their family meal delivery. My husband and I generally try to keep it healthy during the week, but don't always have the time or energy to cook every meal. I've been loving the family meal options that have come out from a handful of fast casual restaurants lately. I don't mind eating the same thing a few times during the week if it saves me time and the food is fresh and tasty!   Cava's family meal comes with your choice of greens, grains, chicken or veggies, and a bunch of topping options. We've built our own bowls at home for two meals so far and probably have plenty for at least one more round. The meal, plus fees and delivery tip, came out to around $60, which works for us.   I do wish they would edit their delivery menu to say that the family meal comes with pita. That wasn't clear so I paid for extra pita and then we ended up with an abundance of pita that we probably aren't going to get through. Other than that, this was a solid healthy option for the week!

My mom sealed my dining fate on Friday when she gave me a flier for buy-one-get-one at McCormick & Schmick's on Halloween. It was good for that night only, and since I hadn't yet decided on a place for dinner, this seemed like a great opportunity to check out something new.   The crowd: typical Cherry Hill melting pot. The young couple at the bar asked for A1 with their filet while the well-to-do family next to us at dinner bitched about everything (and got half their meal comped in the process).   It was very apparent that the back dining room is the more desirable location. Since it was very crowded, we weren't about to complain about being seated in the front. Our first course selections were iffy; a Manhattan crab chowder tasted like something out of a can and the wedge salad was just okay. (FYI: I'm about 1 for 4 on wedge salads lately. Someone PLEASE direct me to a place where I can get a good wedge salad!)   The main courses were better. Salmon stuffed with crab meat served on top of mashed potatoes and asparagus was really good, although the butter lemon sauce had no lemon flavor and we had to add our own, ghetto-style. My seared ahi tuna was nice, but the veggie sushi that came with it was as dry as two-day-old take-out rice, and the seaweed/cucumber salad was not memorable.   I have heard good things about this place from other people (and, I should mention, in other locations) but I was not a fan.

I'm so happy our favorite neighborhood cantina was able to give me a night off from cooking over the weekend. I'd been craving nachos so placing my order for those wasn't even a question. My husband ordered mahi mahi tacos and I ordered the steak tacos. We placed our pick up order through Caviar.   Soon after, the restaurant called to let us know they were out of steak, so they ran through the other options and I went with chorizo tacos. Our food was ready pretty quickly and my husband ran over to pick everything up. Everything was absolutely delicious, as usual, and we even had leftovers for the following day. While he was there, my husband saw that they are also offering to-go quarts of their delish margarita mix, so we may have to grab some this week for make-at-home drinks.   Wishing the very best for one of my favorite neighborhood businesses during this trying time. If you love nachos (and tacos, and guac, etc.), definitely give Los Camaradas a look for contact free delivery or pick up!

I had never even heard of this place until the other night when a friend suggested we go for a couple drinks and some appetizers.  The bar area was not very full for a Friday night, but Nola strikes me as more of a cozy little restaurant than a bar anyway.    We had oysters stuffed with crab meat and this Cajun shrimp thing with rice that was phenomenal.  I'd like to go back for dinner sometime to check out other items on the menu.  I never thought New Orleans-type cuisine would be for me, but the Cajun shrimp at Nola has me reconsidering.

Finally had lunch here today after hearing many rave reviews from others who have beat me to the punch.  The restaurant was not crowded, so my new coworker and I had our pick of tables.    Warm bread and olive oil started the meal.  I had a starter salad with a lemony dressing and huge slivers of parmesan cheese.  My coworker had a garbanzo bean soup that looked really tasty as well.    My lunch choice was penne with vodka sauce, which was loaded with pancetta and peas.  I had to sit on my hands midway through to resist eating the entire very-large serving.  I also had to put Windex on my leftover pizza in college so I wouldn't come home and drunk-eat it out of the garbage.  But that's another story...  Prices are not bad for lunch but dinner is an absolute steal.  This restaurant is definitely on my short list for upcoming date nights.  One negative that I hope will be corrected is that like LB, my sister had dinner reservations on Saturday night at 8:30 and waited over a half hour to be seated.  Collingswood is dry, so you can't just have a drink at the bar while you wait.  Still, the place is relatively new so a few kinks are to be expected, as long as they are worked out eventually.  I can't wait to return!

My first experience at the Troc was a few weeks ago for the Old Dominion concert. I knew from reviews that drinks are served upstairs-only when the crowd is all-ages, so my friend and I headed up the steps where we were greeted with several long lines. Luckily, the lines moved relatively quickly and we were able to have a couple beverages before heading back downstairs to use the bathroom (another long line) and then secure our spot not too far from the stage.   The band sounded incredible and the acoustics were great. I was thrilled with the show since I've been waiting for this band to come around since the second I first heard them about a year ago. I love seeing an amazing band in a venue like this because the experience is so much more intimate and special. The only downside is that general admission crowds tend to be a little pushy. But hey, I'll take the bad with the good if it means I get to be up close with the musicians!

Should have checked the Yelp app first. Tsk, tsk.  At Nail Polish, $18 (plus tip) will get you a run-of-the-mill manicure, a beating while your nails dry (which they refer to as a massage), and wide-eyed comments and titters about your height, if you are a statuesque woman like myself. I'm 5'10" before heels and have no issues with my tall-ness, but I felt kind of like a circus freak with the number of questions I had to field in front of an audience while selecting my polish.   I actually had to walk outside and catch a breath of fresh air while waiting for my friend's mani to finish up. This was probably the least relaxing manicure experience of my life.   Also, what is up with the mini-convenience store going on along the wall? Pregnancy tests and sample-sized shampoos were among the items available for purchase.

Have you ever gone to a restaurant with high expectations, only to drop a solid chunk of dough and leave feeling somewhat duped? Well I have, and it's not a good feeling. Fork is not that place. Last night, my friends and I enjoyed a great meal and we walked away feeling like our dollars were well spent.  From our pleasant greeting at the door to our dinner service, the staff was exceptional at their jobs and made us feel welcome. One of the biggest surprises came early, when we perused the extensive and smart cocktail list. One friend had an Earl Grey tea infused gin concoction, while the other ordered something with elderflower that mastered the balance of slightly sweet and still flavorful without overwhelming the palate. I was thrilled to see a champagne and aperol offering, since aperol is one of my favorite spirits and it's rare that I see it on a menu. The drink was just right and the bubbles went straight to my head.   The dining room at Fork is beautiful, with an open kitchen facing the main dining area and a nice, big bar, plus a banquette that runs along the wall providing more table space. After ordering, we had our choice of three types of bread, followed by the amuse bouche: smoked salmon pate on crunchy crostini. I really enjoyed this despite not usually caring much for salmon.   Two of us started with the soup: butternut squash with minced chestnuts. It was rich, buttery and perfect for a chilly night. Our other friend had one of the house-made pastas with pancetta, which was also extremely flavorful. While ordering, I had asked about the mackeral with olives and squid, but I ultimately ended up ordering the scallops. Needless to say, it was a very nice surprise when our server brought each of us a tasting of the mackeral between courses. It was delicious. The briny olives went perfectly with the flaky but meaty fish. I instantly regretted not ordering it as my main, but now I have a really great reason to return!  The scallops were no disappointment. They were perfectly seared and resting over sort of a hearty bean stew, with a crisp hash of apples and fennel bulb (hate the seeds, dig the bulb) between. My partner in soup had ordered the same dish, and our contrarian friend chose the pork chop, which was a great plate of chop, potato pancake, apple sauce and sauerkraut. Apparently, my friend is not a kraut lover, so I gladly relieved her plate of the slightly sour, bacon-flecked cabbage, which was just as good as my Gram's.   Stuffed, we accepted our check without soldiering on to the dessert course. This was easily one of my favorite girls' nights to date, and I'm so happy I was able to try Fork after many years of foolishly putting it off. I won't make that mistake again.

If they were to coexist on a school yard, Primo Hoagies would be the ass-kicking bully to dorky Wawa.  Blasphemous?  Perhaps, but the quality of breads, meats and cheeses are far superior at Primo to the limited selection at Wawa.    Yesterday I went in to pick up hoagies before the Phils game.  The woman at the counter offered to set them up on a tray and then she threw in three sides of extras without me even asking (pickles, banana peppers and sweet peppers).  For $35 (including a bag of chips), I fed five hungry, somewhat intoxicated adults and had leftovers for after the game.  Minus one star only because orders are occasionally messed up.  This only happened to me once but my boss refuses to go there because it happened to her a bunch of times.

I'm going to be straight with you. I am not usually a fan of frozen yogurt. It just doesn't do for me what ice cream or even water ice can do. But after several visits to The Igloo, my mind has been changed.   The Greek frozen yogurt is really, really good. I don't like plain frozen yogurt, but I like The Igloo's version. With some cookie crumbles on top, it's perfect. And something like 125 calories per serving. Just be mindful of that serving size while utilizing the single-size, serve-yourself bucket. I get the purpose of said bucket at a store that prices things out based on weight, but a single serving of fro-yo literally looks like... well, a drop in a bucket.   Another thing I like about this place is that they aren't just frozen yogurt. They also serve a couple types of gelato, and water ice is on the agenda for this summer. The owners are super friendly and really care about their customer feedback. I'm so glad this place is in my neighborhood!

It's been a minute (more like ten years!) since my last visit to Cafe Lift. That certainly wasn't intentional! I always enjoyed Cafe Lift but it sort of fell off my radar once I moved to Philly and walking distance options became more desirable. I've been wanting to get back for a while and today was my lucky day!   Since my last visit, the cafe now takes credit cards as a form of payment (yay!) and they also have wifi, which makes for a great working lunch locale.   I know that Cafe Lift's sweet options are absolutely delicious, but I was feeling eggs today, and was excited to see a broccoli, bacon and cheddar frittata on special. Our server told us it came with greens, so I ordered a side of potatoes. However, my plate arrived with potatoes, not greens... Folks, I'm half Irish. There are never too many potatoes. I got the side taters boxed up and plan to enjoy them with breakfast at home later this week.   My frittata was awesome and I had no regrets. My dining companion enjoyed her greens and grains salad as well. We asked for sides of hot sauce which was clearly made in house - delicious. Our server was friendly and kept the coffee and water coming.   Glad I made it back, and definitely looking forward to returning sooner than later!

I am pumped to have Los Camaradas so close to where I live! I've had dinner there three times so far and I'm loving what Joe and Theresa have brought to the neighborhood.  I'm a huge fan of margaritas and the ones served at Los Camaradas are delicious and on point. They use quality ingredients, nothing fake, and you can taste the difference. They go down easy. They also have a nice beer selection including a pilsner on draft named after the restaurant which pairs perfectly with the food.   Speaking of the food, I love that they have a nice mix of guilty pleasure foods as well as some items that lean towards the healthier side. Their nachos are on point, and I personally love the oozy cheese that they use in addition to all of the other great toppings. The tortilla soup is definitely a favorite, and I really enjoyed the Los Camaradas salad topped with shrimp on my most recent visit. I've also had the chuleta de puerco: thick slices of perfectly seasoned lean pork served with black beans and plantain rice.   I'm looking forward to trying brunch and am crossing my fingers for happy hour, because the only thing better than a margarita is several margaritas at a discount.

Jimmy J's was recommended for brunch by my girl Aimee K, who knows herself a good brunch. She didn't mention the place holds about eight tables max. Luckily, my beau and I were out and about early, and we only had to wait behind one other couple before we were seated. By the time we ordered our food, there was a line down the block!   Our server was hilarious and so chipper. We had a round of Bloody Marys to start and they were excellent. I don't normally care for a bacon bloody but I tried a sip and it was very good - tons of bacon and none of that rocket fuel flavor you normally get in a bacon bloody. My regular BM was quite delish as well.  The menu is expansive but I narrowed down to the eggs ranchero with chorizo. It was sized just right - not too big, not too small. It was good, but I'd probably try something else if I were to go back. Everything was delivered very quickly and it's clear that you are supposed to eat up and keep it moving. We ordered two more bloodies to go and enjoyed them on the streets of New Orleans, but not before my server gave me a goodbye hug!

I just realized that I never updated my review as I said I would after having a chance to dine in the restaurant. Well guess what? I had a meal at Los Taquitos de Puebla and if I took anything away from the experience, it was that this place is simply not for me.   The restaurant was very quick-serve, get in and get out, but that doesn't excuse trash on the floor. I'm a big believer in putting your best foot forward and that is possible even without fancy decorations or a big budget. Cleanliness is next to godliness, mis amigos.   There are still things to like: real coke in glass bottles, ridiculously spicy and flavorful salsas and the traveling tacos al pastor stand seen at farmers' markets and food truck gatherings. I dig these guys for street food but that's about it.

I took myself to the new AMC Dine-In on Monday to see Little Women. I bought my ticket online the night before, which was super easy. That said, I'm glad I arrived early, because the line for concessions was long and it didn't move very fast. My medium popcorn and drink came to sixteen dollars and change. Obnoxious.  Concessions aside, the theater was great. My seat was comfortable, and I loved the added heat feature! Also, super nice to have a little table with cup holder, so I didn't have to keep the popcorn in my lap.   I love some of the older, local theaters in the city, but they can't exactly compete with these comfy seats and large screens. AMC Fashion District has definitely earned a spot in my movie theater rotation!

A second meal at Talula's Garden was enjoyable, though I still believe four stars is appropriate. While some items soar, others leave me wanting. And at prices like Talula's, I'd hope for my socks to be knocked off. That said, the place certainly doesn't hurt for business. We saw a two top get turned away for not having reservations on a notoriously slow night. So people are clearly loving the place.   As was the case last time, the restaurant's decor was warm and comfortable, and service was perfect. We started with a fall cheese plate, which was really nicely done. The mushroom soup looked beautiful, but the creamy broth lacked the rich flavor I expected.   My skirt steak entree was very good, with vinegary cipollini onions, broccoli and crispy potatoes. One thing I will say about Talula's is that the portions are generous. I couldn't finish my entree.   For dessert, we shared the fig pudding, which is topped with butterscotch sauce and served with goat cheese ice cream. It's not the prettiest dessert, but on first taste I was absolutely hooked. One of the better desserts I've had in a while.

My wonderful boyfriend ran around town on Sunday picking up supplies for the days we'd be stuck inside because of the storm. Magpie was one of his stops. He grabbed a chorizo chili pie, some gouda and squash pie and a bag of pie fries with pumpkin dip.  The pie fries were totally addictive. What a delicious sweet and savory snack! Genius idea. The pie crust is the best part of pie, afterall.  We heated the savory pies up for lunch and both were very good. However, there was a leafy herb in the gouda/squash pie that totally overpowered the other flavors. I was not a fan of that at all but the rest of the pie was good once I pulled the herb pieces off. Still, I'd probably opt for something else next time. The chorizo chili pie was delish and came topped with corn chips and cheddar cheese. A side cup of sour cream was included for a nice touch.  I'm a fan and I'd love to try more of what they have to offer!

A friend and I hit up Jet Wine Bar for happy hour on a Wednesday. We were actively avoiding the Center City Sips establishments in hopes of bar seating and a quieter atmosphere. With only a few other people besides ourselves, we got just that.   House wines are $5 during happy hour but I'd recommend navigating to other selections for bolder flavors. Still, the house white was crisp and refreshing.   Complimentary breadsticks (baked by local coffee bar/bakery Nook, as indicated on the menu) were crunchy, slightly salty and totally satisfying. We shared a cheese and charcuterie plate which we ordered with truffled goat cheese, mimolette (on special), speck and sopressata. The plate also came with spicy cashews, apple slivers, olives, grapes, quince paste, and a few thin slices of bread. I've been spoiled after working at Sycamore so I'd love to see a spicy mustard and some honey in addition. Otherwise, the plate was lovely and we enjoyed it a lot.   After chatting with the owner and checking out the loungey area downstairs, I could easily see myself returning to hang out in either area.

Awesome: - The main floor is a piano bar. - The second floor is a dance party with great tunes. - The walls of the dance floor are mirrored (check out my bad self and these moves like MJ!).  The not so cool:  - No glasses of water, only bottles for purchase. Which leads me to... - Peeps be rip-roarin' wasted on you name it. Hence the charge for water. So try not to get dehydrated while working up that sweat, and if you do, save a few extra dollars. Why?  - Cash only.

I never intended to write a review update for my dermatologist, but when I looked up the address to confirm and saw Jon D.'s review, I reconsidered.  When I last described my experiences with Alta almost a year ago, I actually was not "kidding."  In fact, I returned yesterday for my annual and my experience was fine.  When I arrived to a crowded waiting room, everyone on the staff had a pleasant demeanor and paperwork was processed quickly.  Although the wait time was longer than expected, a TV tuned to NBC's coverage of the Phils provided a nice distraction.  Once inside an exam room, I did not have to wait long for the doctor, and he was personable yet professional as always.       I have recommended this practice to countless friends and family members and I will continue to do so because of the quality of care I receive on every visit.    One last note, the office will be moving to another building in the area sometime before the end of the year.

My fabulous BYO girls took me to Salt & Pepper for an early birthday dinner over the weekend. They didn't realize that S&P's move to Passyunk also came with a liquor license, so they brought wine along and agreed to pay the $10/bottle corkage fee.   We started with the three apps that were a special that night. One was a spicy tuna tartar with a strong wasabi flavor and some crackery crisps for scooping. The next was a goat cheese and pesto flatbread pizza and the third was a plate of fried plantains with sardines. That one was definitely very different but the plantains were spicy and savory. We were loving on all three of the starters and were excited for the mains.   We waited. And waited. And waited some more. Two bottles of wine were killed before our entrees made their appearance. I'm all for pacing and I enjoy a leisurely dinner, but at one point, I think we were all wondering if the chef had to run to the grocery for something. There were only about three tables occupied in the restaurant.   Finally, the entrees arrived. My friends who ordered lamb chops were thrilled, and my other friend who ordered fish was happy as well. My NY strip steak was just okay. I ordered it medium but it arrived well done and topped with a lot of gravy. The cut was also very different from what I expected. It was served in three pieces over the smashed potatoes and veggies. I ate it, but I wouldn't order it again.  For dessert, we shared the cheesecake, key lime pie, and a banana split. All three were basic but very tasty.   I didn't love my entree but everything else about my experience at Salt & Pepper was pretty good. I'd give it another shot.

My family have been loyal customers to various Bobby Chez locations for years. I'm excited to have a location in Delran that's easily accessible whenever I'm in the area to visit family.   The crab cakes are pricey and they seem to get smaller and smaller as the years go by. I typically buy one each for me and my husband but it never really feels like enough, though we love pairing the crab cakes with the mashed potatoes and have tried a bunch of the other sides as well.   Some of the other entrees have been hit or miss. The chicken parm we had was very tough and we were not fans. My sister said she had the same experience with Bobby's chicken parm and no longer buys it. More recently, I tried the buffalo shrimp and those were a hit. I will for sure look for those again next time I'm in the shop.

I'm still a fan but my lunch at CTH today was lackluster. I requested a Caesar salad with grilled shrimp and was told that they no longer have shrimp. Odd but okay. I ordered chicken instead. The chicken was sliced on top of the salad and it looked nice, but after moving the pieces around, most of them had layers of fat running through them. Layers of fat running through chicken. Clearly whoever prepared the salad saw this, so I wasn't sure why it was sitting on my plate. No one eating a salad would eat a piece of fatty chicken.  Fortunately, my boyfriend's margherita pizza was pretty tasty, and they had Deschutes Mirror Pond Pale Ale on tap, which I had discovered earlier in the week. Next time I have a meal at City Tap I'm going basic and sticking with pizza or a salad without any added protein.

People often ask me about my favorite restaurant, or what I'm loving at the moment, and I often struggle to come up with one, concrete answer. Partly because there's so many great restaurants popping up in Philly all the time (and so many classics!), and partly because there isn't ever one that stands out from the pack as being better than the others.   Well that has officially changed, because Double Knot rocks my world. And it's now my go-to answer whenever people ask me what's new and great in Philadelphia.   First off, the space is so cool and different. I love the vibe and the history of the place is pretty interesting. As our server last night said, "If these walls could talk." (Thankfully, they can't.)   I've been to Double Knot for dinner twice now and have some definite favorites from the menu, though nothing I've tried has been disappointing in the least. My must-tries are: tuna rice cracker, hamachi with shallot-ginger relish, edamame dumplings, scallop robatayaki and octopus robotayaki (do not forget to try these with the spicy mustard on the table!), broiled seabass, and brussel sprouts.   Also, do not miss the sushi. I don't know what it is about Double Knot's sushi but I was left thinking about it for days after my first dinner. The rolls are great, yes, but you have to go traditional here. This sushi is levels above other Japanese spots in Philadelphia.    The desserts I've tried have been great but I'm not huge on sweets and would rather eat more of the proteins. But if you do like dessert you won't be disappointed with the unique offerings.   Looking forward to my next visit, which is already on the books!

Philly Pretzel Factory can't have five stars, because my favorite soft pretzels of all time come from a small mom and pop in NJ. However, Philly Pretzel does serve up a tasty twist, with consistency across their locations. The fact that they were open on Thanksgiving morning until 1pm to provide my homemade beer cheese dip with a vessel (in the form of delicious, salty rivets) was a total lifesaver.

When I was a little girl, my dream was to become a singer. I would grab my microphone, head to the basement, and sing Cats show tunes at the top of my lungs. I sang Mariah Carey hits with my windows wide open in the summertime. I tried out for singing roles in the plays that my elementary school put on every year.   Psst: I have a secret.   I can't sing for crap!   Fortunately, self-awareness kicked in somewhere around 7th grade, so when I was recently invited to a karaoke party at Yakitori Boy, I got a little nervous. For about two weeks straight, I performed Internet searches such as "easy songs to karaoke to" and "songs anyone can sing." I ended up with a list that included Snoop and Nancy Sinatra. I was doomed.   The night of the party, I arrived at our (thankfully) private room to see friends already belting out hits from the 90s. It seemed that no one at the party was shy, so I figured I was off the hook. I ordered a martini and sat back to enjoy the show. Said martini was presented in a stemless glass the size of a fishbowl, and when our pleasant server returned to the room, I requested another... and maybe one more after that (they were really good!).   Liquid courage firmly intact in the last half hour of our time slot, I selected a song and boldly grabbed the mic. I soon realized that I was the only one in the crew who knew the words to Buckcherry's Crazy Bitch. I had to sing by myself with little help from the peanut gallery, but I sold it.   I may need to write another 400 reviews before I live down the night, but Yakitori Boy was a pretty okay time for a different kind of night out.

Overall, I'm a fan of Zio's. Their pizza is great and they have enormous salads that can serve multiple people or be split for two meals.   I popped in the day after Thanksgiving to grab a to-go salad - my usual, Greek with grilled chicken. I got it home and the salad looked great. And I love that they serve fresh garlic knots and bread on the side. Unfortunately, the chicken was really rubbery and I had to pick around it, which really only left me with veggies and dressing.   I still have to go with four stars because of all the great meals I've had in the past. Hopefully yesterday was a fluke but I may be off their chicken for a while.

Even though it's unlikely that I'll be a frequent shopper here, I do have to give Skirt props for their consistently rotating array of high end clothing and accessories. And, their sales staff have always been nothing but nice to me, even striking up casual conversations about my weekend plans. They are very sweet.   I received a $50 gift card for the store a few months ago, so I've popped in a few times. I quickly realized on my first visit that $50 wouldn't go very far - we're talking brands like Theory, Vince, Rebecca Minkoff, etc. I've continued to go back in hopes of finding something that I loved but wouldn't break the bank, and yesterday I found the perfect two-in-one necklace for my upcoming girls trip. It's beautiful and perfect for summer!   I also follow Skirt on Instagram and I'm always getting style inspiration from the cute outfits and style tips videos (thank you for reminding women that pants come in more forms than leggings!). I'll be keeping an eye out for their big sales, which I know happen only a couple times a year - you better believe I'll be there.

I've been to both Cantina locations a bunch, so I'm surprised this is my first time reviewing Los Caballitos. My husband and I popped in last night for an early dinner and a couple drinks. Our server was Emily F and she was really sweet and fantastic.   I was dying for a margarita but didn't want something really sweet or high in calories. They have their own version of a skinny margarita, which is made with Espolon reposado, lime and agave. The first round was quite tart but I assumed that was because they were going light on the agave. The second round was much more well-balanced. I hate inconsistency with drinks and I feel like it happens all the time with margaritas for some reason. Bartenders: please measure!    Of course, the chips and fresh salsas (verde and roja) are delicious, but I was trying to eat light so I only had a couple chips. Luckily, our food arrived relatively quickly so I wasn't too tempted. I ordered the chicken fajitas, no beans. Our server asked if I wanted to sub anything else, so I opted for more veggies. The plate arrived loaded with peppers, onions, mushrooms and chicken, plus some white rice, and a separate plate with pico, guac and tortillas. I ate about half and brought the rest home for a second meal. My husband had the chorizo tacos, which looked great.   Cantina is an old standby where you can go all out and eat heavy, cheesy Mexican, or choose from plenty of options when you just want to keep it light. I probably wouldn't go at a time when there's likely to be a wait but it's great during less busy hours.

I really wanted Indian for lunch so I decided to give Lovash a shot since it was one of the only Indian delivery options available at the time of my order. Delivery took well over an hour, which seemed like a long time for an 11:30am order. I do like that they package their food in reusable cloth totes. Props for that.   Unfortunately, the food was just not that great. The garlic naan was slightly greasy, which was surprising since I've never had greasy naan before. The chicken jhalfrezie was just okay. I was hoping it would resemble the jhalfrezie from my favorite Indian restaurant (which unfortunately does not deliver), but it wasn't even close. The chicken was not all white meat and the sauce was kind of soupy. I didn't even save my leftovers, and that's saying something.

While in the area I did a search for lunch spots and Tortorice's came up. With nearly 80 reviews and a really high overall rating, I was so surprised I'd never heard of the place before. A quick look at the menu revealed lots of veggie-friendly options, which is awesome, though I ended up going with their tuna sandwich, the Naples.   The shop smelled amazing and the staff member who took my order was super friendly. There was pepperoni bread on the counter that looked incredible - mental note for the future! The sandwich was ready pretty quickly and one was big enough to share for lunch with some chips on the side. I loved the sandwich but thought it was a touch on the salty side because of the olive tapenade. That wouldn't stop me from ordering it again, though. I can't wait to check out more of the menu!

I'm finding myself at Hungry Pigeon more and more often these days, and I like it. Employees are always cool and friendly and, the menu, while short, has everything I need. I dig the eggs any style (poached, with hashbrowns and toast) with a side of ham.   This week I tried the avocado toast. It comes on rye bread, which I was wary about because I hate caraway seeds. The staff wasn't sure if the bread was seeded or not, but I decided to go for it anyway. Wise decision. The bread was awesome, and I didn't detect any caraway. I really loved the splash of chili oil over the egg, which took a basic avo toast into next-level deliciousness.   I haven't stuck around long enough for the lunch menu, nor have I been for dinner, but I really would like to get back for both, and soon.

I was very pleasantly surprised by my lunch experience at Red Lobster! This location is close to my grandmom's house, and since she was treating my mom and me to lunch, it was grandmom's choice.   The restaurant was very clean and looked like it had been recently updated. We were seated right away. The restaurant was fairly empty so I gather their weekday lunch is pretty slow. This makes it a perfect choice for a lunch with family members or even just a quick lunch if you're on the go. Lunch prices are extremely reasonable.   When I first heard we were going to Red Lobster, I fretted over whether there would be any healthy options. To my surprise, there were plenty! I love the lunch combo where you can pick two types of seafood and a side. They have several fresh vegetable options in addition to standards such as baked or mashed potatoes, rice pilaf, etc. My lunch of shrimp scampi, broiled scallops and fresh broccoli felt like a splurge even though it was totally reasonable, calorie-wise.   Our server, a petite woman with dark hair, was so sweet and accommodating. We ordered some food to go for my grandfather, and our server made sure he had plenty of biscuits and everything he'd need for a good meal back at home.   We all agreed that this lunch was a great fit for everyone and we'd be happy to go back!

My mom and I went to Blackbird today because they were offering a South Jersey Restaurant Week deal that was too good to pass up: $15 three course lunch.  It was our first time dining at the restaurant, so we had no idea what to expect.  The décor was classy but modern.  The tables were neatly set with white cloths and really funky cutlery, which I loved.  There was a lot of wood and the walls were home to some really cool photography.  Our server was very pleasant but also somewhat busy serving four tables.  In hindsight, we should have mentioned that we were both on our lunch break, but had we been there with a bottle of wine on a free afternoon, the timing would have been appreciated.  For our first course, I chose a broccoli soup which ended up being really tasty and not too heavy, and my mom had a salad with greens, sliced cherry tomatoes and a very flavorful vinaigrette.  The crusty bread that our server brought to our table came with a high quality olive oil.  Next, my mom had seared scallops served on top of wilted spinach and risotto, with a tomato fennel sauce.  Normally the mention of anything "fennel" turns me off immediately, but when I tried my mom's dish I had instant food envy.  It was fantastic and I didn't detect the usual telltale flavors of my root vegetable nemesis.  For my second course, I opted for parpadelle Bolognese, which was topped with sliced cherry tomatoes and Italian cheeses.  It was very good, and perfectly portioned for lunch.  At this point, we both really had to get back to our respective offices so we got our dessert course to-go.  Our server brought out two nicely packaged apple tarts, and he also gave us each a $10 off card to use at any SJ Hot Chefs restaurant for a limited time.  Nice!  Back at the office with a freshly brewed pot of coffee, I dug into my apple tart.  It was heavenly down to the very last bite.  A quick email to my mom confirmed her shared feelings.  We will definitely be back!

Props to Jet Wine Bar for offering a bespoke wine shopping experience during the pandemic. I'm a bit of a wine snob and wanted to make sure that I had some good bottles in my cabinet for weekend imbibing. I reached out to Jet's GM, Nick, via email to discuss options.   Nick sent over the current list of wines by the bottle, and he made some recommendations based on my feedback. So far, we've had two of the four bottles I purchased. The Stellenbosch Vineyards Pinotage was particularly awesome and went really well with some Indian takeout.   Wine is probably the alcohol option that's hardest to come by right now, so keep Jet in mind if you're looking for something a bit more elevated than what you can find in the grocery stores. Not to mention, there's way less contact with others so that's obviously a win right now!

Karen F hit the nail on the head in saying that sometimes the shoes in Aerosoles come off a bit "old-lady." That said, they occasionally have something super unexpected and cute, and when there's a sale, it's worth stopping in just for a quick look. Not to mention, the shoes are designed for comfort, from sandals to wedges. Even the high heeled, open-toed, suede booties, which I'll be returning for late this month as the fall months loom.  The only problem with actually entering the doors is that the women who work in the store are serious sales professionals. They are experts in the art of shoe selling: complimenting the look of shoes when you have them on, mentioning how much they love their own pair at home, talking up the sale price, bringing out similar styles in addition to the pairs that you asked to try on, etc. It's easy to slip out of the store when you don't try anything on, but if you do, prepare for the hard sell.

A few months ago, I was kicking around the idea of purchasing a new piece of furniture for my bedroom, a lingerie dresser, to be exact. Fast forward to last weekend; my mom asked if I was free to shop around on Sunday afternoon in search of my birthday gift - a lingerie dresser. Yeeeeaaaaayyyy!!! We went straight to Howard Hill, the wood furniture warehouse I had always seen without really seeing while driving by hundreds of times on Route 130. We were welcomed immediately by a friendly employee who showed us the wares. The store was chock-full of beautiful creations ranging from desks to vanity tables to toys to water bowl holders for dogs. Most items come unfinished but there were several finished pieces available as well, although the markups were considerable.   Within minutes, we selected our favorite option but decided to shop around, for comparison's sake. I'm actually embarrassed to admit the other place we went; the items were so sub par with respect to their quality that it would be like comparing apples to... crab apples.   We returned to Howard Hill a few days later and were welcomed back by another gentleman from our first visit. In ten minutes, the stain and top coat were selected and everything was paid for and loaded into the vehicle.   The dresser has been stained and is awaiting a coat of protective finish. It's a beautiful piece of furniture that was made all the more special because of the hard work my mom put into preparing it for me. I'll cherish it for years to come!

El Azteca is about as close as you can get to authentic Mexican in South Jersey. As Christopher R pointed out, you won't find tongue tacos here, but at least you can get down with the basics, which is just fine with me.   The chips and salsa are legit; the guacamole is good. It won't become your favorite guacamole but it does the trick.   All of the combination platters have enough food for two, unless you want to go it alone and risk a food coma. I of course chose the latter, so by the time I got through two thirds of my number seventeen (a chicken burrito, beef enchilada, rice and beans), I knew that I would be generally unproductive for the rest of the day.   The servers are nice and the family who runs the place is very sweet. They also take credit cards.

I was contacted via yelp email by an orange-question-mark-head named Stevie B., who claims to be the Mad River Manayunk DJ.  According to him, because of MY review, he is now booking weddings at $1200 a pop!  Go Stevie B.!  Can a sister get a finders fee?!

This was our first stop for food while in New Orleans, and we liked it so much we went back for seconds a couple days later. First thing's first: this place is pretty divey inside. Don't let that scare you - the service is friendly (and so are the other customers) and the food is solid.   There isn't much on tap but the five or six beers are mostly local and cover the bases. I had gumbo on my first visit while my fiancé had a shrimp po boy (which I ordered on my second visit). Both were very good. The gumbo had a slow burning heat - use caution before adding any hot sauce! The po boy was overflowing with fried shrimp and it was totally delicious. When the touristy spots have lines flowing down the street, hit up Cajun Mike's for your fix without the wait.

I had some great meals during my recent Nashville trip, but Silo definitely took the cake when it came to my hands-down favorite. We were seated promptly upon arrival (we did have reservations and I would recommend making them) and I checked out the list of cocktails. Opted for a dark and stormy which was very large, nicely made and lasted through my entire meal.      My friend was disappointed to see that the menu had recently changed and the shrimp and grits were no longer listed. She ended up with the scallops, while I opted for the hot chicken, because when in Nashville, am I right? We also ordered sides of the mac and cheese, which had been mentioned in several reviews, and the pot likker greens. It should be noted that sides are huge and can easily serve 2-4 people.   The hot chicken looked amazing and was served over white bread and topped with pickles. On the plate was a side of creamy coleslaw, which was much-needed because DANG THAT CHICKEN WAS HOT! The chicken breast itself was juicy and fantastic. The skin was crisped to perfection. But, I have to admit, the overall takeaway was more heat than actual flavor. I would love if they toned down the spice level just a notch and kicked up the tang. Not to say I wouldn't order this dish again because I most certainly would.     And speaking of things I'd order again: that mac and cheese was the stuff of dreams. On first site it looked average, but once I dipped the spoon into the creamy noodles I could see that the cheese game was serious. The only thing that was remotely healthy was the collards, which I liked very much as well.   Our server was also really awesome and friendly. Totally hitting up Silo on my next Nashville visit.

PROS: - Products are high quality - Nail techs are friendly and efficient - Pedicure chairs have two different massage options (the usual back one and also an air pressure one for your butt and thighs) - The magazines are actually current - They have frequent visitor cards that eventually earn you a free mani - With regular top coat application after my Friday visit, my French manicure is still looking good on Tuesday!  CONS: - This location is tiny, so expect everyone in the place to turn around and stare when you walk in the door - Half of the patrons staring are snotty ten year-olds

Lest you think of Lil' Pop Shop as a summertime destination only, I'm here to tell you that they serve freshly-baked pie in a variety of flavors all. year. long.   I recently stopped in and was tempted by the beautiful pies on the counter, only to find out that there were even more available in a fridge. The chocolate caramel peanut butter pretzel pie had me at hello and it was every bit as sweet, savory and decadent as you'd imagine.

There comes a point in time where enough is enough with the unpredictability of Philadelphia's taxi system. When I recently needed a ride to 30th Street Station, I got in touch with The Classy Taxi via Twitter and booked an appointment. One minute before my pick-up time, a white cab came whipping around the corner and I was speeding away in the backseat seconds later. I dare say it was the first time I ever arrived to the station without heart palpitations and anxiety from running late.   A few days later I again booked Jack's services and was not disappointed. With baseball in the background, we chatted about this and that. It won't be long before my next appointment.

I went to Azuka Theatre with my sister for Bob: A Life In Five Acts and I have to say, I was impressed! I've seen a handful of live theatre shows in the past few years at various venues around the city and this show was probably one of my favorites. The acting was great and the show was entertaining and very funny.   As for the theatre itself, it was very nice! We sat in one of the last rows and could still see and hear everything clearly. The (gender neutral) restrooms were very clean as was the entirety of the venue. There was also a small bar with refreshments though we didn't partake.   I can't think of anything I'd change about this theatre. Looking forward to attending other shows in the future!

Chain or not, I love me some Rita's. In fact, I used to work at one in my hometown back in the day. Pretty sure the only reason I wasn't invited back the following summer is because I ate too much of the product that first year. But how else would I have discovered some of my favorite combinations? Chocolate water ice with the signature Rita's jimmies, half-chocolate-half-cherry getati with vanilla ice cream, and mango water ice with rum (whoops!) are just a few of my discoveries.  This particular location is my mom's preference because they also have fat free soft serve. The girls who work there are sweet and didn't bat an eyelash at my crazy combination during my last visit. And it came out just as requested, too. Five stars for water ice on hot summer nights!

My friend and I went to brunch here on Sunday and had a lovely experience.  We were looking to sit outside, but once we entered the restaurant and saw the beautiful décor and gigantic open windows, we were happy to take up residence at a table indoors.  The restaurant was surprisingly empty for 1 p.m., but this only made for more attentive service and a fantastic table by one of the aforementioned windows, across from The Academy of Music.    Fresh crusty bread and hummus was promptly placed on our table, and a complimentary cocktail was offered with our brunch order.  I asked for a bellini, praying that a classy place like Estia would get it right and use fresh peach juice instead of schnapps or some other imitation of the real thing.  The bellini was dropped at my table and was perfection; so much so that my friend made the switch to a bellini for her second round.     My "avga spanakia," which I requested with egg whites, was unique and very good.  It was supposed to include spinach, leeks, feta, scallions and tomato, but there was not any tomato in my dish.  It was served in an iron skillet and was very hot and bubbly, which I loved.  The side of sausage that I ordered never made it to the table; our server said they had run out.  Not a big deal, as the omelet came with a side of pita wedges and a small dish of chive-seasoned potatoes, which was more than enough. My friend had a smoked fish platter, which she seemed pleased with as well.  I would love to make it back sometime for dinner and sit in one of the semi-private banquette/booth type areas along the wall with a small group.

I had a sore throat and all I could think about was soup. Dan Dan's wonton soup was EVERYTHING, (including extremely overpriced, but it really did the trick).
