Since I didn't want to place a delivery order just for soup, I also got the spicy cucumbers. Fantastic, but similarly overpriced for the amount you get.  That has always been my beef with Dan Dan. I've ordered from them before and between my husband and myself, there are almost never any leftovers, even with several dishes ordered. And did I mention it's expensive?   Alas, Dan Dan is a once-in-a-while delivery option as opposed to once-a-week.

My grandmom is the pierogi maker of our family, and she makes them well. I've never had better pierogi from anywhere else. When I heard about Royal Cracovia in the late fall, I knew I wanted to take my grandparents there. They have a pierogi lab in the basement!   We finally made the trip last Friday, adding in a pre-dinner stop at Flying Fish Brewing Company's tasting room just a couple blocks away. When we arrived to RC, happy hour was still going so we sat at the bar for a drink. Happy hour offerings were kind of weak - Coors Light was the only beer on special, and they were out of pomegranate juice to make the featured martini. They did have some solid food specials, though, and we shared a plate of potato pancakes which were great. My grandfather said they were just like the ones his mom used to make. There was also a musician singing and playing guitar and he was pretty good!   We moved on to a table for dinner. A food runner brought over some water for the table... with a toothpick hanging out of his mouth. Not really a good look. Our server came over and got us started with drinks, and we placed an order for a pierogi platter, which was supposed to contain three cheese and onion, three meat and three sauerkraut. They were out of sauerkraut pierogi, which was a bummer, but we were able to get them replaced with cheesesteak pierogi. The plate arrived but we only found two cheese and onion, which was a shame because they were way better than the meat or cheesesteak (which were exactly the same as the meat, except sitting on a cheese sauce and topped with sauteed onions).  Entrees were enormous. I had the pork chop, which I thought would be really similar to schnitzel by the way it was described. Unfortunately, it was a lot thicker than I expected and very fatty. I did really like the mashed potatoes and sauerkraut sides, however. My grandparents shared a sausage platter, which is what my fiancé ordered as well.    In the end, everyone agreed that the food was just okay. We were all glad to have made the trip, but we probably won't be going back... Unless we need some bar snacks after our next trip to Flying Fish!

I LOVE World Cafe Live as an event space, so I'm keeping my rating at a four... but if I was rating the food I had the other night at an event, I'd probably go with a three- or even two-star rating.    Sweet potato fries were limp and had some sort of sugary coating that I thought made them way too sweet. The spicy dipping sauce was pretty nice, but not enough to counter the sweetness of the fries.   I ordered a sesame-crusted ahi tuna salad with wonton strips, cashews and sesame ginger vinaigrette. I expected a lush, healthy-looking salad. Sadly, I missed the part that said the romaine would be grilled. My salad looked pretty lame with a couple shrunken stalks of lettuce and two hunks of tuna, plus a smattering of toppings rolling around the plate. The taste was on par with the appearance. A little soy on the side to dip the tuna or some kind of wasabi sauce could have made it better, but I was definitely disappointed.   I'm going back for another event this weekend, and I probably won't be going in hungry.

I haven't stopped thinking about the breakfast burrito with sausage gravy I had at Grubhouse a few weekends ago. That's a pretty good sign that there is something awesome going on in deep Southwest Philly.   When a large group takes over an entire restaurant all at the same time, the potential for disaster is high. I was super impressed by how well the small staff handled the rush. My water glass was never empty for long and coffee refills were plentiful. Our table was one of the first to receive food, which was obviously awesome. Things did slow down a bit for some of the tables farther back but everyone's patience was rewarded with big plates of delicious looking food.   In short, Grubhouse is a super cute breakfast and lunch nook with a very solid menu. Really looking forward to my next meal there.

Thank you, Replica, for getting me out of a jam! I waited until the last minute on Sunday night to send a print job through Staples' website. I got all the way through the prompts, put in my credit card info and clicked the next button, only for there to be a glitch in the system that would not complete my request.   Panicked, I Yelped printing services and came across Replica. The location was ideal as I had other errands to run in Rittenhouse, anyway. I had a confirmation email waiting for me first thing in the morning and I swung by at 11 and the job was ready. It was also printed on much nicer paper than I would have received at Staples.   When given the option I always choose to go local, and now that I know about Replica, they will be my go-to for print jobs!

First experience at Middle Child: yeah, I'm a fan! I walked in when I found myself in the neighborhood after another meeting nearby. The gentleman at the counter (who I believe is one of the owners) greeted me with a friendly smile and answered my questions about the menu.   I opted for the shopsin club, to-go: turkey, bacon, lettuce, avocado, pickles and cranberry miso mayo on ciabatta. The sandwich was wrapped tightly and everything was intact when I opened it up at home. I requested the mayo on the side since I can be picky about mayo.   The sandwich was solid. I did end up using the mayo for some added flavor, though I think I would have preferred something with more of a kick. It wasn't until the second half of the sandwich that I remembered there were pickles - they with undetectable on my first half. All around, this was a good sandwich that I've thought about again (I really love sandwiches, y'all). I'm excited to get back and try more of the menu!

We've ordered sandwiches from Cleavers twice for Eagles games this season, and both times I was super happy. I've ordered grilled chicken cheesesteak wraps both times and, though they appear on the small side, they are actually stuffed with chicken and cheese. Half is usually enough for lunch and then I can look forward to the other half for dinner or as a post-game consolation prize.

For people in the Burlington County, Flagg's should be the go-to spot for all things merry and bright around the holidays. From live trees to synthetic, tinsel to ornaments, whosits to whatsits, Flagg's has you covered.   During the non-seasonal times of the year, think crafty home decor and everything your garden could possibly need, whether it be flowers or bird baths. The family-owned and operated store has a neighborly vibe and staff members are friendly and willing to assist!

The best way to win over an audience in a public speaking gig? Arrive bearing gifts. And if the audience is composed of college kids, arrive bearing edible gifts.   I called Federal Donuts the morning of my talk and arranged to pick up four dozen hot donuts in assorted flavors at 1:15pm. I arrived right on time and there was a sheet with my order, but it wasn't ready. In fact, they hadn't even started. I tried to play it cool but, inside, I was already a mess of nerves and this added to the stress.   Luckily, said donuts didn't take all that long to prepare, and I could tell the staff was hustling to get my order complete as quickly as possible. They even threw in a small box of fancies to set things right, which was a nice gesture.   A student followed up with me after the lecture and mentioned that everyone loved the donuts. I wouldn't know since I left the room faster than a scared rabbit the moment I finished speaking, but I was glad to hear it.   I still need to try their fried chicken!

My friend told me that I absolutely had to try butter cake while visiting St. Louis. So even though we were both still substantially full from our brunch, we carved out some room and stopped by Park Avenue Coffee. We shared one piece of traditional butter cake and each had an iced coffee, which was strong and delicious.   The cake was dreamy. How do they pack in all that buttery goodness? (Don't answer that.) I'd be interested to try some of the other flavors although I can't imagine that you could top the original.

I love Concourse! I've been twice and both times were positive experiences. Go early to avoid long lines and claim your spot on the dance floor. The crowd on each visit has been really diverse and I love that! Everyone busting a move in harmony is always a great thing.   The Friday night DJ was on point last night, mixing tons of old school jams with newer music. He read the crowd really well and made adjustments as needed.   I wasn't drinking but my friend had a couple different cocktails, including the grape crush and a fishbowl. I had a sip of each and thought the grape crush was surprisingly delicious - like a grape popsicle! Our bartender at the back bar with long blonde hair was a total doll.   I'm already planning my next visit and can't wait to get my dance on again!

In the days and weeks leading up to my ten year high school reunion, feelings of dread mounted in a crescendo of anxiety that had me strongly considering one last game of hooky for old time's sake.  In the end, curiosity won out.  Fortunately, I was already several beers deep after having attended the Flyers game that afternoon, so my jitters were under control by the time I met up with friends.    The bar was easy to find, located just off 130 in the area around where Holiday Lake used to be.  "Class of 99" signs beckoned from the doorway; 'twas time to meet my fate.  We entered a private room just off the main entrance, where a few other classmates awaited.  The room was appropriately sized and had several set tables on the outskirts and a bar on the left side of the room.  Honestly, it was much nicer than what I had been anticipating.  Small talk was a little painful at first, and we retreated to the bar in silent agreement that drinks would be lovely.  The bartenders must have been aware of the awkwardness, because wine pours were on the very generous side.    In no time, the room was filled with familiar faces and socializing became surprisingly easy when it was realized that everyone felt equally hesitant prior to the evening's festivities.  As with Jim H.'s experience, the social cliques still existed, but the lines were much more blurred than they had been back in the day.  Of course people still gravitated towards those who they felt most comfortable with, but that was to be expected.  Happily, (most) egos were checked at the door.  Midway through the event, I realized I hadn't eaten anything all day and decided to make my way to the buffet line.  There were several options and everything looked fantastic (as food often does to a tipsy, hungry girl).  I opted for some salad, penne and vodka and a piece of chicken.  Everything was prepared well and very good overall.    In the end, everyone had such a good time that we all went back to our town bar for a little afterparty action.  I never expected to say this, but I'm glad I went and look forward to seeing everyone come together again in another ten years.  The night would not have been so seemless had it not been for the staff at 45th Street.  I'd recommend holding an event in their private room to anyone who needs an affordable option without compromising quality.

Cathy's catered my sister's wedding rehearsal dinner at my dad's house and it was great!  There were mini sandwiches with lots of variety between the fillings, a wonderful tortellini salad and a delicious Caesar salad. Several people raved about a corn salad which I didn't try for myself.   The young lady who was sent to help serve and clean up was great. I had never heard of Cathy's before but would definitely recommend their catering after this experience. I'd even consider a trip across the bridge if I needed food for a party at my own home.

I returned to Bud & Marilyn's for brunch on Sunday with my husband and some friends - we had a great experience!   The covered outdoor seating was very nice though maybe a tad too warm for a sunny spring day. If you run hot, I'd suggest wearing layers so you can strip down and feel more comfortable!   Our server was amazing and on top of everything we requested. We started with some shareables: warm pecan cinnamon roll, cheese curds, falafel crusted cauliflower, crab fries. All delicious! I had the grapefruit mimosa and was super happy with the bitter but perfectly sweet taste.   By the time our entrees arrived we were already pretty full. I ate half of my breakfast sandwich (with bacon instead of sausage) and brought the rest home which made for a delicious weekday breakfast. I especially loved the sauteed kale on the sandwich - it gave a really unique flavor that made the meal.   Looking forward to my next visit!

Much love to the newest eatery on South! Yelptern Enid C and I met for dinner on Monday night and my cobb salad was so delish, I went back a couple days later and ordered it again, to go. Their buttermilk dressing is addictive!  Enid's sandwich was enormous and she took half home for another meal. I'm so excited to check out the rest of the menu. This is going to become one of my go-tos. Also, the staff is friendly, the prices are right and the place is super clean. Cute bathroom, too.  There is definitely five star potential for Miles Table but since I've only been twice and had the same thing both times, I'll go with a very solid four for now.

I walked into Di Bruno Bros. 9th Street Bottle Shop last week by accident. I was aiming for the cheese shop but saw the Di Bruno sign and went inside, only to realize I was in their newer bottle shop. I noticed right away that they had plenty of other merch, and since I only needed a couple things, I figured I'd find everything I needed while also shopping around for some wine.   The woman working that day was so friendly and helped me pick out a couple bottles. Maybe I didn't shop around enough but I thought their wine was on the pricey side; the two bottles were each in the $25-$35 range. After locating the sharp provolone and soppressata I came in for, I added a six pack of non-alcoholic Athletic beer, and that's how a hundred bucks was spent in the matter of five minutes.    Definitely a convenient one stop shop though everything adds up really fast!

While I'd typically choose any independent coffee shop over a Starbucks, the international giant certainly has its place. Like when I'm on a major highway, in an airport or in Jersey. For whatever reason, the area I grew up in is seriously lacking in decent coffee shops. After dropping my mom off at work, I had to put my thinking cap on to come up with a suitable destination for coffee, and the Moorestown Starbucks was the only place within five miles that came to mind.   This particular location is housed in a gorgeous building with a small patio out front. The inside is always very clean and feels more comfortable to me than most other Starbucks locations. Probably because I spent a lot of time there, catching up with friends during breaks from college.   The milk and sugar bar is always well stocked, and unlike many of the other Starbucks locations, the flavored powders are always available. Even the vanilla one, my favorite of the four.

I've spent a lot of mornings and afternoons (sometimes both in one day) and had a lot of awesome times in Fairmount Park. Some of the fields get pretty beat up (I played in a coed football league there for years so I know this from our many infamous Dust Bowls), but the grounds are massive and very accommodating for tons of events to all take place at once. Parking isn't too bad unless there's a race, in which case, you better get there early or you won't get there at all.   Today I ran my first 5K at the park, which was the Color Me Rad race. I got to see and enjoy parts of the park that I had never seen before.   This park has a reputation for being sketchy come nightfall. I wouldn't know, because I'm always far gone by then; most people are. On weekends, it's a great place to enjoy some sports and sun.

I truly love Palm Tree Market! If there was a location closer to my house, I'd probably never go grocery shopping again! As of now, I'll have to settle for swinging by when I'm in the area.    This store is pretty large compared to the others I've been to in Queen Village and Fitler Square. They have the same great deli selection and loads of snacks for whatever you're craving. The employees are friendly, as always. Palm Tree is a wonderful little deli/market with all the staples!

Yup, still not a fan.  I'm leaving two stars only because our server was very friendly and didn't question our requests to send back multiple items, including "soft" pretzels that looked about two days old and nuked in a microwave.   For some ungodly reason, people at my table ordered calamari-- which came with an olive salad that was piled on top, along with what appeared to be several spoonfuls of olive juice. One friend remarked that the dish looked like something from Fear Factor, and no one disagreed.    I suspect the cooks at The Field House must be getting paid in alcohol, because only a bunch of drunks could try to pass this garbage off for money.

It seems like every yelper in the garden state has been to Pour House in the past week.  I went for a last minute drink and bite to eat with my sister and her boyfriend on a recent Friday night.  The bar was absolutely packed, super loud, and it was very hard to get a bartender's attention.  Luckily, the guy standing next to me knew someone so he yelled out my round, which was awesome as I likely would have had to wait a while otherwise.  The beer list is pretty solid.  There is a decent selection on tap and an extensive list of bottles.    We put our name in for a table at the hostess stand and the girls said the wait was about twenty minutes and they would come and find us when a table was ready.  Forty five minutes later, my sister went over to check on the situation and was told that we had been crossed off the list because they couldn't find us.  Not sure how that happened, but within a few minutes we were seated.    Our server, while very pleasant, was also very forgetful or not detail oriented or something.  Other than beer, all we ordered was a burger, onion straws and nachos.  We requested that the chili be served on the side of the nachos and we also asked for a side of jalapenos.  The burger arrived without issue, the onion straws were fine as well, but the nachos came out with EVERYTHING on the side.  I'm not kidding, the server who brought them out (not our regular server) said, "nachos, everything on the side" as she placed a plate of tortilla chips with melted cheese on the table, followed by a plate with lettuce, tomatoes, onions, pico de gallo and sour cream.  No guacamole, although it was listed on the menu, and no jalapenos.  When our server stopped by to check in with us, I asked for the guacamole and jalapenos.  He returned with the guacamole only and my sister and I just had to laugh at this point.  The man clearly did not want to give me the spicy peppers.    The burger was allegedly delicious, according to my sister's bf, who housed the thing in record time.  His fries came with a cup of melted American, which we promptly used as a dip for our onion straws.  If there is a will to eat like a fat kid, there is a way.  I'll definitely give Pour House another shot, but if I see the anti-jalapeno activist coming my way, I'm requesting a server change.

Having wanted to try Rouge for ages, my friend and I finally made it our destination for drinks and dinner.  I arrived early and was fortunate enough to score a window table.  While sampling a couple different glasses of white, I enjoyed French music and people-watching, both in the bar and outside on the Square.  When my friend arrived, we ordered a bottle of Sauvignon Blanc, which I would highly recommend if I could remember the exact name.  Our server, Danielle, was efficient and helpful with any questions we had about the menu.  At her recommendation, we ordered the cheddar plate, which was an addition that day, as well as the Bibb lettuce and endive salad and the famous Rouge burger.  The cheddar was fantastic and came with dried apricots, quince paste and a honey that I believe was truffle-lavender.  Cracker Barrel, twas not!  The salad was perfectly dressed and came with large Roquefort chunks, cashews and slivers of red onion and green apple.   As for the burger--it looked heavenly, with a big helping of pommes frites, a perfect-looking pickle spear and side of ketchup.  Alas, it was too good to be true.  Don't get me wrong, I still inhaled the thing with the velocity of a Dyson, but it paled in comparison to the almighty Good Dog Burger.  To be honest, I was a little relieved.  It's hard to believe that a burger could get any better than GD's version, and if it ever were to happen I would certainly make a scene while convulsing in ecstasy... not exactly ladylike.    We should have stopped there, but the dessert menu beckoned.  We ordered the chocolate chip bread pudding with vanilla gelato and a caramel drizzle.  What was dropped at our table was reminiscent of a hockey puck.  For shame, Rouge line-cooks!  Danielle whisked said puck away and returned with a less well-done bread pudding.  It was, in her words, to-die for.  She even took it off the bill, which I thought was extremely nice.  Bottom line, I would certainly return for the ambiance and service, but it would likely be for drinks and small plates.

I was pretty excited to finally return to Morning Glory, but I thought the food was pretty bland compared with the last time I was there. On this visit, the coffee was perfectly hot, so that was great. But the frittata I was pumped to eat was just okay. It was enormous for sure, but didn't have much flavor. The potatoes on the side were solid and I really liked the multigrain toast. My friend seemed to have the same feelings about her breakfast as well. Maybe we were there on an off day, but I'll likely stick with my go-to brunch spots for a while.

J'adore Miel Patisserie! My Friday lunch meeting took place at this adorable French café - it was my very first visit and I was instantly charmed. The gentleman behind the counter was so super sweet - hooking me up with a delicious piece of chocolate to go with my latte.   The tables are small and space is a bit tight but once I was seated all was well. I ordered one of the pressed sandwiches which had mozzarella, tomatoes and pesto on sourdough bread. It hit the spot, and the delicious kettle chips alongside were great. This was a great place for a lunch meeting and I look forward to my next visit!

My friends and I returned to El Poquito for dinner last night and I was just as impressed by the food as I was during my previous visit. It was Tuesday, so there were plenty of taco Tuesday specials, and also a whole list of other specials as well.   We started with some guac, tuna ceviche, brussel sprout tacos and fried jalapeños for sharing. I thought everything was really solid though I wasn't crazy about the tuna ceviche. The fried jalapeños were absolutely addictive, however.   All four of our crew decided to get salads for the main course. I had the avocado salad and asked for the avocado dressing and also the shallot vinaigrette on the side. My salad arrived without any dressings but the food runner brought them right over when I asked, along with something one of my friends needed. My salad was delicious and all of the ingredients were so fresh (the shallot vinaigrette was great!).   The reason I had to pull a star is because our server barely stopped anytime she came to our table. I was sitting on the end of the booth so I was able to ask for a refill of my club soda, but my other friend never got a chance to ask for a second margarita. The restaurant was busy but we got more face time with our food runner than we did with our server, after placing our initial order.   Nonetheless, I still think El Poquito is great and I'd be there all the time if I lived in the area.

A search for "hoagies" yields many results on Yelp, and Cosmi's is among the top. Since my first choice (Paesano's, always) was out as they now close their Italian Market location at 4pm, Cosmi's became the place to grab sandwiches before Thursday night's Phillies game.   The gentleman who took my order over the phone was very friendly and recited everything back to me to make sure he had the order right. I like that. The guys at the shop were equally friendly when I arrived fifteen minutes later. The two half sandwiches I ordered were enormous, and clocked in around $18.   My ham and sharp provolone hoagie was delicious, but the shooter special with mozzarella, prosciutto and ham and provolone-stuffed pepper shooters was ridic. I think I morphed into a 250 pound construction worker on his lunch break because there is no other explanation as to how I ate my own sandwich, plus part of my boyfriend's. Normally, half of the half would have sufficed.   I will definitely order from Cosmi's again, and the fact that they also deliver makes them a very desirable partner on football Sundays.

I've been on a mission to visit Somerset Splits since first hearing about them earlier this summer. My friends and I were in the area on Labor Day and decided to check it out for one last long-weekend splurge. There were only two employees so the line moved slowly but, fortunately, the line was pretty short.   I loved the idea of a Kandy Kake milkshake but generally prefer my ice cream in a cone or cup, so I went for a hot fudge sundae with chocolate chip cookie dough ice cream. There were a few other sundaes listed but they were pretty banana-focused which isn't really my thing. I would have loved to see a few other options.   My sundae was just right; the perfect size and just the right amount of fudge and whipped cream. Overall a great ice cream option for the area!

This hotel is brand spankin' new and it was clear that the staff wanted to make a great impression. Everyone we encountered during our brief stay was friendly and accommodating. The decor is modern and pleasant. The rooms are quite large and perfect for extended-stay guests, as they include a sitting area and kitchenette.   The king bed was comfy and the bathroom area was big, with the vanity outside of the separate shower and toilet area. Neutrogena soaps and Bath and Body Works hair and skin products were a welcome surprise. I'd recommend this particular Homewood Suites to anyone in need of a place to stay for the night or even the week.

We drove across the city to try the newest restaurant on the Thai scene in Philly. Unfortunately, we found Baan Thai to be pretty on par with other options. That's not to say it was bad by any means; it was good... just not really a destination spot for someone living in Graduate Hospital. Hot and sour soup was standard; firecracker shrimp were tasty but par for the course.   My chicken pad thai was okay, and a plate of drunken noodles had a kick but tasted just like drunken noodles at every other Thai restaurant in the city.    Service was very nice but slow, and we were the only table in the restaurant. If I lived in the neighborhood, I'd probably return, but I won't be going out of my way again.

Plenty of folks love Sabrina's, so I'm sure they won't miss me as I go on break from them for a while. I've always avoided the place on weekends because of the crazy waits, but I've occasionally hit them up for a midweek breakfast or lunch and it's always been pretty good.   My most recent visits have been okay, but my experience a couple weeks ago has left me disenchanted. I ordered the blue cheese and bacon frittata and subbed in a side salad in lieu of potatoes. When the plate arrived, the size of the frittata was laughably huge. I ate about two thirds of it and was absolutely stuffed. I didn't make it far into my salad, however, because I found a plastic tab (the kind that you'd find on a bag of bread) mixed in. Stuff happens, I didn't think it was that big of a deal, but I did mention it to our server. The plate was removed from our check which I thought was a nice move on their part.  Personally, I'm more interested in quality over quantity and I don't really feel like I get that at Sabrina's. The food is okay but I feel like they rely on their gargantuan serving sizes more than the taste and quality of the ingredients. I'm off to explore other options for a while.

Pretty solid delivery experience from bop, with just one semi-annoying hiccup. We placed an order through Uber Eats and our food was delivered in about thirty minutes which was kind of incredible.   Unfortunately, instead of the tuna poke we ordered, we received salmon instead. I am super picky about salmon and I did not care for the look, smell or taste of this dish. If we hadn't been so hungry I may have called the restaurant, but we had plenty of other food so it wasn't that big a deal.   Next up were some KFC wings. Fantastic! Super crunchy and maybe just a touch on the too sweet side, but the spicy kick helped combat some of the sweetness.   My main was a pork bibimbap which was huge and had lots of fresh, delicious vegetables. The pork was fairly fatty and I ended up eating about half of it, but what I did eat was really excellent. I bet this would be even better in the restaurant served dolsot-style. I may try chicken next time, but I'd most likely go with the pork again and hope it wasn't so fatty.   Now I am excited to go check out bop in person!

I woke this morning with a mission to brunch, only I really wanted to try something new. There's certainly something to be said for the restaurants on Twitter; they grab my attention when I'm hungry and I'm more likely to check out their menus. Alla Spina's brunch menu offered several interesting-sounding bites, and I didn't have to ask my better half twice to make a trip to what is quickly becoming one of his favorite spots.   We pulled up to one of the prettiest corners of real estate I've seen in Philly. Route 6 and Alla Spina: nice work! The free parking in front of the church across the street wasn't bad, either.   The restaurant was even larger than I expected, and boasted a super fun atmosphere. I love the outdoor seating, the family-style table above the bar, and the lounge area. And the huge garage doors, which are clearly meant for opening on a beautiful breezy day. I loved it all.   Our brunch was awesome, too. I went a little crazy and ordered the egg panino, which comes with a sunny side up egg, provolone, house made pickles and bacon and pork terrine on a homemade English muffin. I typically stay away from any meat product I don't know the origins of but I decided to try something new and I'm glad I did. The sandwich was oozy and delicious and just the right size - not overly huge where I felt extreme guilt but just right. It also came with a crispy triangle of hash browns.   Also on our table was the crespelle, which expertly combined salty, savory and sweet. The kitchen graciously sent out a ham and eggs plate, which was another successful sweet and savory combo that I'd likely order next time.   The bloody mary I had at the start of the meal was nice, but the spritz was just perfect. I wanted another, but a third ten dollar brunch cocktail seemed excessive (the BM clocked in at $8). Especially in light of the fact that we had each sprung for the shakerato - espresso shaken with sugar and ice. Worth every penny.  I'm anxiously awaiting the first opportunity I have to check out happy hour. I'm crushing on this place hard.

I've been living in the city for nearly ten years, and planned on purchasing a bike in year one or two... I even got a bike helmet soon after moving to the city (safety first!). Alas, I never bought the bike. Flash forward to the present pandemic times, and there's nothing I have been wanting more than the sweet, sweet freedom to move around the city a little further than where my own two feet will take me.   I'm so happy with my experience at Kayuh! They started popping up on my twitter feed recently, and I noticed they were offering free delivery and pick up for bike repairs and purchases. They seemed really friendly and helpful which is what made me check out their website and get in touch. I worked with Henry and, after some emails back and forth, I selected a bike and he placed an order. The entire process from when I submitted a contact form to when I had my bike was about a week. That's pretty awesome, if you ask me.   I ended up picking up my bike in person so I could test ride it a bit. Also, I was able to add on a couple necessary accessories including a bike lock (with a bike mount) and a water bottle holder.   The bike is a bright, happy shade of orange, with really attractive tan accents. I rode home across town while my husband drove the car. Though I've only been on one additional ride so far, I can't wait for better weather so I can really get out and explore.   So happy to finally have a bike and I look forward to working with Kayuh again for all my bicycle needs in the future!

I can not believe I am the first person to review this place!  Then again, I wouldn't even know about it if it weren't on my street.    Cipolli Cannoli is a tiny little store that is open on Fridays and Saturdays only, and during limited times.  You can place an order in advance or just stop by and pick up a kit, which is what I did prior to a picnic last weekend.  A kit includes a dozen mini cannoli shells and enough cannoli filling to stuff each one, along with a little cup of either chopped chocolate or pistachios (to dip the ends in) and a little cup of powdered sugar to shake on top of the finished product.    The owner gave me a cannoli-filling tutorial, and I was on my merry way.  Two hours later, the "oohs" and "aahs" heard around the room as I made my cannoli creations were only matched by the "yums" and "so goods" after they were eaten.  Success!!!

I've gotta go with an upgrade here; Middle Child makes some bomb ass sandwiches! I've been back several times since my first visit to try the Shopsin Club. It's hard to deviate from the breakfast sandwich, which has become a favorite. The eggs are so plentiful and buttery; the cheese is oozy perfection!   Today, I was in the neighborhood again and decided to revisit the Shopsin Club. I do believe this sandwich was better than the last time I tried it. The roll was soft and slightly crunchy; it also did not overpower the ingredients. I ordered the miso mayo on the side since I'm weird about mayo, but I found myself dipping the sandwich repeatedly because the mayo really brought the taste to another level. The pickles were calling to me so I got a side of dill and sweet mixed together.   I arrived slightly before noon and it was already bumpin' with a ten minute or so wait. I happened to notice that there is a small selection of grab and go sammies which is a great option if you're in a rush.

Walking into Bar Noir late Friday evening was like walking into a frat party from my college days, only much cleaner, less crowded and with more blacklights.  I could have sworn the DJ had his equipment hooked up to my old roommate's Napster account ("doin it and doin it and doin it well...").    I only stayed for one drink, but I wouldn't mind going back for another impromptu dance party sometime in the future.

Cruisin' through South Philly late this morning, I had a sudden craving for a hoagie. To the Yelp app I went (my car was parked at this point - safety first!), where a plethora of options awaited my decision. Lombardi's was the closest to where I was at that moment, so I rounded the block and parked a few feet away.   This is a mom and pop shop to the core. Despite the many delicious-sounding choices, I wanted to keep my sammie light so I went with a small turkey and sharp provolone with lettuce, tomato, onions and vinegar. It may have been basic, but damn if that hoagie didn't taste good. Did I mention it was only four dollars? I didn't know you could get a meal that cheap anymore. I'll definitely return, and next time I'm going all out and ordering something more loaded.

I just re-read my last One Shot review from three years ago and, apparently, my taste buds have changed because I LOVED my iced coffee there this morning.   Though I was all set to order the "eggs your way" breakfast, I had a total change of heart when my breakfast companion said she would be having the A.B.E. sandwich: avocado (check), bacon (check), egg whites (check). These three things, plus greens, tomato and herbed goat cheese - in an unexpected twist, my decision was reversed! I asked for my sandwich on multigrain, which was no problem. The sandwich was huge, and I took half home for lunch.   The baristas were all friendly, the upstairs area provided a bounty of tables and seating for a working breakfast, and everything was right in the world.

One time, a woman drove directly into the back of my car, which was parked in front of my house, in broad daylight and during nice weather, three days before Christmas.  CollisionMax made my car look like new again.  One time, I stupidly left my car parked on a low elevation street down the shore... the night before a nor'easter.    CollisionMax tore out the guts of my car and, when I got it back, it looked (and smelled!) like new again.  The other day, I noticed something hanging down under the hood of the car.  In five minutes, the problem was taken care of - at no charge.  These guys are awesome, and I can't say enough great things about my experiences with them.  Should you find yourself in an unfortunate situation like any of those listed above, do not hesitate to call CollisionMax.

I love this beautiful shop right in my neighborhood! I've stopped in a couple times and the women who work there are friendly and knowledgeable about the products. Every time I pop in I tell myself I will buy something one of these days. Yesterday was the day! I splurged on a  rose-scented powder; I have a feeling it will become a staple in my beauty lineup. Looking forward to discovering more products and checking out their in-store events!

At first glance, Wine Legend is a wino's dream come true.  The store, or shall I say warehouse, is enormous and features aisles and islands and endcaps of vino, at a significant savings compared with the local competition.  The proximity to my house made Wine Legend my go-to spot for whenever I needed to stock up on adult beverages.  When I eventually noticed the solid selection of brew along the back wall of the store, I figured I was all set.  Unfortunately, I've picked up at least two bottles that tasted off when I got them home: Saison DuPont on the first occasion and, coincidentally, Avril (also by Brasserie Dupont) on a separate occasion months later.  These bottles don't come cheap and I definitely will not be taking a chance on suds at this particular store in the future.  For the occasional tailgate, cases of Bud Light and other swill have always been fine.

I've now been to Pizzeria Beddia twice within the past month and it most certainly is as good as it gets. My first visit was with a friend and we ordered two pies; a white pie special and a pepperoni pizza. We each did some damage but also got to take home several slices, which was awesome.   Over the weekend, I returned with a group of ten. We ordered six pies so that we could taste a wide variety. My favorites were the pepperoni (again!), the white pie special (different from my first visit) and a classic pizza topped with hot peppers and sausage. We had a full pizza left over which was basically a mish mash of all the pizzas we ordered. Later in the evening I tried the arrabiata pizza which was loaded with spicy peppers. It was also great!    An unexpected joy was discovering Pizzeria Beddia's soft serve! The sweet cream is absolute perfection. I also love the rotating Baba's Brew kombucha on tap. Last but not least, my servers were awesome on both visits.   Can't wait for next time!

Cosmi's is back on top as my go-to South Philly hoagie shop. I introduced my mom to the South Philly Italian and the Shooter Special (both on seeded rolls, of course), my go-to Cosmi's orders. She loved them and we had another excellent tailgate. Wish I could say the same about the game!

I hit Zavino last night for a quick meal before heading to an event in the neighborhood. It was surprising to see such a crowded restaurant early in the evening on a rainy Tuesday. Some of that could probably be chalked up to the awesome happy hour, which featured several wine, beer and food selections.   We passed on the drinks and stuck with non-boozy bevvies. To start, we ordered a grilled shrimp and avocado salad which was a special. It was served warm with cannellini beans and was absolutely delish. They should really make that a regular on the menu.   When we first walked in, a server walked by with a delicious-looking plate of pasta, so I had my heart set on ordering the same dish (fettuccine with pork ragu and parmesan). The homemade pasta was great. The sauce was flavorful though maybe a little heavy on some of the herbs. And I also came across a bone which was unfortunate. I also had a slice of the polpettini pizza which was really nice. I haven't had pizza from Zavino since they first opened their Midtown location, but I've clearly been missing out. Can't wait for my next visit, where I will undoubtedly partake in the happy hour!

I'm loving this place! I've been twice in the past month and just really dig the laid-back vibe. There are several TVs for sports-watching, plus a pool table. No food is served but you can BYO in that department which is awesome. Solid beer list and I love the local ciders that have been on tap.   My only negative comment is that I've heard about the legendary Bloody Marys served at Atlantis but they were out both times we visited. Hoping to catch them on a stocked day soon so I can try one!

I attended a surprise birthday party for one of my favorite girls on Friday night, and El Poquito did an amazing job as the host!  Prior to my visit, I was unfamiliar with this restaurant. I don't get to Chestnut Hill very often, which is unfortunate since it's such a cute neighborhood! We found street parking a couple blocks away, on one of the side streets. We entered and were led to a private side room which hosted about thirty people. The decor is cozy and comfortable. We mingled as we waited for the birthday girl to arrive, and servers were constantly coming around to take drink orders or take away empty glasses.   The margaritas were excellent! They were just slightly sweet and packed a punch - just the way I like them! After the big surprise, we were seated and had three courses, served family-style. I loved the chips and guac and shrimp ceviche, and the tacos and enchiladas from the second course were all very good. I was way too stuffed for dessert.  Overall, I was very impressed with El Poquito and would even go out of my way to have dinner there again. Next time, we're taking the train so my husband doesn't get stuck driving when I once again pull the I'll-drive-tonight-just-kidding card once we're already out.

I loved my first poke bowl from Philly Poké! I opted to create my own and went with white rice, tuna, cucumber, jalapeño, seaweed salad, masago, fried shallots and a little bit of spicy sauce. I asked for wasabi and soy sauce on the side.   My regular-sized bowl was a nice amount of food, though I would have liked a little more protein. I can't imagine needing any more rice but maybe the larger bowl comes with more protein as well? In any case, the ingredients tasted fresh and delicious. I'm a great poke bowl creator, if I do say so myself.   Philly Poké is located inside Chinatown Square on Race Street. There is cafeteria-style seating in the back of the market. I will definitely be back again for more of that poke!

Leziz had been on my radar for a long time, and we finally decided to check it out while passing through the neighborhood last week. For a Monday night, there were still several tables occupied and I saw some take-out orders being picked up as well.   We started with hummus and a spicy pepper dip with ground walnuts and olive oil. Both were a nice start to the meal, and the pita that came with was hot and fresh.   For my entree I chose the chopped chicken kabab, which was mixed with spices. It was good, though I'd probably go for the traditional chicken on a future visit. Just a personal preference. The kebabs are served over two types of rice, both addictive. I don't know what they put into Turkish rice but I am definitely into it. You can request a variety of sauces on the side to enhance your meal for a small price.   We were treated to a medley of desserts, my favorite being the pudding that had a toasted caramel-like layer (I can't remember the name!). It was different and I was into it.   Leziz also has awesome lunch specials, and I'll definitely be returning to check those out soon.

My husband and I enjoyed our date night at 26 North on Saturday. For a BYO, the restaurant is surprisingly big and has a gorgeous bar in the middle that is currently being used as a prep area for starters and desserts. I was really into the vibe and I think it would be a fun place to go with friends as well.  The bread service is on point. The bread was soft and dense, and was served with some marinated chickpeas, a delicious garlic pesto olive oil, and some butter with sea salt.   I started with the crab cake, served in shellfish butter over marinated artichokes. It was very nice, with very little (if any) filler, though there were a few bits of shell. Next up, I had the tuna, which was seared and served over mushrooms and Chinese broccoli, with a thick black garlic sauce on the plate. This dish was simple and delicious. I was very happy with my pick.   We skipped dessert but there were several that caught my eye on their way past our table. Definitely putting this one near the top of my list of BYOs to get back to sooner than later.

After going through a few different dermatologists over the years and not being very impressed with any of them, I was finally steered in the right direction to Alta.  Dr. Finkelstein's knowledge of dermatology combined with his excellent bedside manner makes him one of the best physicians I have encountered.  Because skin cancer runs in my family, I have had several biopsies over the years just to be on the safe side.  Dr. Finkelstein has performed these procedures with minimal pain/discomfort and hardly any scarring, which is amazing considering my scars from the years before I was referred to Alta.    Wear your SPF and self-check your skin regularly.  If you see anything out of the ordinary, do not hesitate to visit a dermatologist.  Skin cancer is one of the most preventable forms when caught early.    This concludes my public service announcement of the day!

I don't hit up J Crew very often these days, but this particular location is usually fairly put together and organized. I'll pop in occasionally if I'm looking for something in particular that I think they might have. Rarely do I actually make a purchase, though.   The employees have always been friendly and helpful, so that's a plus! And you can't beat the centralized location in the Cherry Hill Mall.

I've used Di Bruno Bros. Catering twice so far this year. Their catering contact, Amy Howe, is amazing; she recently saved my bacon big time when I had a last minute catering emergency. Amy got in touch with me soon after I left her a message and we discussed my needs. Within hours she secured everything needed for my event, from bartenders to food to ice, and I had a proposal in my inbox.   Whether you need a simple (but beautiful!) cheese tray for snacks at a small event or a full on spread with catering staff to boot, Di Bruno Bros. has your back. They also work with a big list of venues in Philadelphia, which means they have the necessary catering licenses in place to slide right in and save the day.   Can't recommend this team of professionals enough!

After my last Mad River experience in Old City, I never thought I'd set foot in one again-- that is, until I heard the words "free beer."  Philly Sport and Social Club chose this locale for their annual winter party so some members of my coed football team, the Bayside Tigers, decided to check it out.  I have to admit, the Mad River peeps put on a nice little shindig.  From 7-9, all PSSC members were sectioned off in a large room with tons of finger foods and free Coors Light bottles.  Five stars for the party itself.  And now for the reasons why I will never return:  -The dj was terrible and resembled a sleepy bear who was woken out of hibernation to play some cds... bad cds.  -The crowd was of the popped collar variety.     -The bathrooms were reminiscent of elementary school-- I guess the renovation money was only for the bar area? -It's Mad River.  Bonus reason: It isn't really fair to hold Mad River accountable for this but I'm going to anyway.  Because most of our team ended up drinking all night, we were all a little hungover the next morning for our playoff game.  Our play was severely hindered and we promptly lost to a team called Ridiculously Good Looking.  Damn you, free beer at Mad River, damn you!

Before the week leading up to New Year's Eve, I had never even heard of Ulivo. Turns out, it's a newish BYO that opened sometime in the fall. For some reason, it seems to have gotten a little lost in the shuffle of restaurant news. Maybe that's why we were so fortunate to score a table for eight just a week or so before the big night. Granted, it wasn't until 9:30, but beggars can't be choosers on the busiest night of the year.   Six of the eight arrived on time, while another couple showed up a little while later. Since it was already late enough, we decided to order the appetizers and pastas in a family style way, so we were able to try a little bit of everything. That kept things running smoothly when our friends rolled in. Our server was great and kept us on track despite the distractions of friends and a table covered with bottles of wine, beer and champagne.   We had a bunch of apps but the only two I really recall are the octopus and polenta. The octopus was okay, a little chewy, but the polenta was great. And that's saying something, because I typically hate polenta. It's a dish I've long lamented and just don't understand. But Ulivo presented it in an appetizing way - thickly fried sticks with marinara on the side - so I was willing to give it a go. It was hot, cheesy and flavored just right. I love when a restaurant changes my mind about something I think I don't like.  Next up was the pasta course. We ordered one of everything so I got to try it all. Standouts were the buttery pasta mixed with shrimp and the penne with cheese and potatoes. I realize these descriptions don't sound very gourmet, and I'm typically much better with details, but we got the party started early on New Year's Eve and by the time dinner rolled around, my brain wasn't really on full alert. The gnocchi was also good and had a nice truffle butter sauce, but the taste was really one note and needed some sort of kick.   By the time entrees came around I really wasn't even hungry anymore. My roasted chicken was very nice, though. The crispy skin was super flavorful and the chicken was moist. The side of lemony pearl pasta that came with was okay, but I instead opted for forkfuls of the risotto across the way.    An espresso followed by an affogato revved things back up as we toasted the New Year. I enjoyed my dinner at Ulivo but I wasn't wowed by it. If I do end up there again that would be fine, but it would definitely be for a group dinner where the focus is more on a nice night out with friends than one where the focus is on the food.

"We don't cock around here."  This sentence was repeated often and with great humor to men and women alike during my brief but entertaining visit to Barton & Chase.   Before swinging by, I gave a quick call just to make sure the place was open, would replace watch batteries, and could do one-stop service. When all requirements were met ("happily" was the exact response) I headed on over.   You would never even know what type of business this is from the street. Stepping in was like walking back in time a little bit. The owner told me they have been in the same space for 35 years and by the looks of all the boxes and old school filing cabinets, that much was evident.  No watch was too tricky for this craftsman; I got the feeling he likes a challenge anyway. All four watches were quickly replaced with new batteries at the extremely reasonable price of $20. And they take credit cards. Never thought I'd have a go-to watch repair place but now I do.

If opening night at Fathom Seafood Bar was any indication, the place is going to be packed to the gills (pun very much intended) on the regular. My man and I swung by on an impromptu visit and snagged the only open seats. Unfortch, they were at a table by the door, where we were blasted with cold air from the snowy night at regular intervals.   Aside from that, I loved Fathom instantly. The space was warm and welcoming; I could easily picture myself seated at one of the large captain's chairs around a big wood table with friends on a lazy afternoon in the summer. Also fun was the bathroom, with black walls and chalk for writing messages.  The beer/cocktail list was expansive and fairly priced, but the regular menu had me absolutely swooning when I spotted some of my retired favorites from Fish (fries with crab gravy, lobster grilled cheese, etc.). We ordered the aforementioned fries along with an order of crab Louie: tempura-fried claw meat, served in the same tasty sauce as the shrimp tempura at Fish's late night happy hour.   Our server was awesome, and he was happy to answer every single question we threw at him, and there were many. I can't wait to return for cod pierogies, tuna casserole, lobster grilled cheese, more Fathom fries... the list goes on.

My first Sancho Pistola's visit was a success. It was on a Monday night, so I didn't want to start off the week with anything boozy, but I will surely be back to hit up those margies in the future.   We sat at the bar and I took in the light, airy space with lots of windows. Jose's cousin is a lot more stylish but still just the right amount of laid back. I loved that there were sports on TV while great music served as the soundtrack.  We started with guacamole which was quick to arrive and loaded with flavor and quite a bit of heat. Next up were the tuna tacos. There were some flavors I really liked but I'm not sure if I was into them enough to order them again in the future. No matter, there are loads of other taco options including three other seafood versions. I did appreciate that the tortillas remained sturdy and didn't break apart as I was eating, which is sometimes a problem with corn tortillas.   Solid first visit, looking forward to my next!

This may be my new weekday escape when I need to get out of the house and focus on work. The iced coffee is delicious and, of course, you have your choice of sweet treats should you need a little pick-me-up. There is a decent amount of tables and chairs and I haven't encountered many other people on weekday mornings.   My only small suggestion would be to keep the music volume at a level where it would be reasonable for people to have a conversation. My first visit was great and the music was just right for background noise, but on my second visit it seemed like the volume was really loud. Perhaps just a fluke. I'll be returning soon and look forward to another great experience!

I returned to Jet to meet a friend for happy hour in the Jet Wine Garden. The garden is super cute and quite big - even with all of the tables very appropriately spaced. Masks are required any time you aren't in your seat, and there is hand sanitizer provided at each table.   Wines by the glass (a small plastic cup) are a little pricey but considering I'm not going out much these days, it's a worthy splurge. I enjoyed the Grüner Veltliner and Müller Thurgau on my recent visit. Food comes from the Rex 1516 kitchen and I really enjoyed the farmer's basket biscuits and pimento cheese. They were out of my first choice for dinner, the crab cake sandwich, so I opted for a caesar with grilled shrimp which was very tasty. Plus a side of fries, because fries.   The staff is friendly and helpful and I felt like Jet handled all of the new health guidelines very well. Looking forward to my next visit!

I went back to Iron Hill in Maple Shade on Saturday and my experience was a big improvement over last time.  Our server really knew his stuff and was able to talk about each of the beers in detail.  I ended up trying the India Black Ale, a special this month, and enjoyed it a lot.  It was similar to a regular IPA, but with a stout-y little twist.    We ordered the chicken nachos and they were also better than they had been on my first visit.  The toppings were held securely in place by the cheese and sour cream, and there was more chicken.   I shall return with cautious optimism.

I've ordered delivery from Kai twice now. It's not one of my go-to sushi spots but it may become one; my husband and I were very pleased with our dinner. We ordered through UberEats, and my only complaint is that the menu on that platform isn't very descriptive. The ingredients for each roll weren't exactly clear based on name alone, so I played it very safe and went with a tuna roll, spicy california roll and spicy tuna roll. My husband opted for a spicy tuna roll, salmon avocado roll and also the spicy crunch roll, which turned out to be tuna. The three roll option is $14.95, which I thought was pretty reasonable for dinner.   Everything arrived within the promised delivery time and the rolls were fresh and tasted great. I paid $2 extra for wasabi because it wasn't clear whether it came with the three rolls already. Of course, we ended up with wasabi in the container and on the side, so save yourself the extra cash and don't order extra unless you want double the amount. Otherwise, very solid option for delivery sushi!

This review is for the Victory Beer Dinner on 11/17/09.  I purchased tickets to this event on the recommendation of a friend who attended one of Victory's prior beer dinners.  My friend and I arrived slightly before the start time and we were instructed to sit anywhere.  The two tops were all taken so we nabbed a four top and prayed for no whammies.  Luckily, the musician of the evening and his buddy asked to join us, so we were in good company.  The first course was crab and arugula, and I expected a salad with some crab meat on top.  What we got was a bowl full of crab in a delicious lemon wine sauce, and a smattering of arugula in the center.  It was a very promising start to the meal.  The Helios Ale, which was introduced that night, was the perfect pairing.  Actually, all of the beers were perfectly paired with their courses, to be honest.  Next up was prosciutto wrapped shrimp over jicama slaw.  Total letdown.  I was expecting the shrimp to be warm and the slaw to be room temp to cool, but everything was chilled and it made for a slimy texture.  The sauces on top of the dish looked like tubes of ketchup and mustard (they were actually barbecue sauce and gouda aioli), and the overall effect was not appetizing.  I focused on the beer during this round, Moonglow Weizenbock.  The third course was a very generous filet mignon with lobster mash and grilled asparagus.  This hunk of meat was no joke, and I ate less than half to conserve some room for the final two courses.  No complaints with this dish, which was served with Victory's Festbier.  There was a very timely break at this point, which gave our new musician friend some time to catch up on the courses that he missed while entertaining the crowd.  The conversation was flowing in all directions; most likely do to the happy buzz from beers that ranged from 5.6% to 8.7% ABV.    For the fourth course: carmelized scallops and roasted sweet potatoes.  This was easily my favorite of the night.  I'm very choosy about scallops and tend to either love them or leave them, but these were right on the money.  They were perfectly prepared and the yammies were surprisingly complimentary.  Who knew?!  Baltic Thunder was the pairing.  At this point, I was ready to haul ass straight to bed but there was still another round left.  We were introduced to the brand new Yakima Twilight beer, which went along with a molten chocolate cake that was okay but dismissible.    Throughout the evening, service was fantastic and the event flowed seamlessly.  The chef made appearances to talk about the menu and a very gracious Victory rep thanked the crowd for attending.  I'd require little to no convincing to attend another event like this... although I will need some major cardio sessions to counteract the damage.

This location is definitely more my speed than the one on Passyunk. It's not nearly as in-your-face with regards to music and decor. There is plenty of seating, which I imagine is necessary to serve the weekday lunch crowd.   The menu is filled with healthy choices. I wish there were more places in Philly that catered to a health conscious crowd, and I applaud FUEL for being one of the few.   So the reason for only three stars is that my take-out salad ended up costing me over $12. Which would have been fine, since I was the one who chose to add grilled shrimp for three bucks, except my salad contained just three shrimp. Three. One dollar per small-sized shrimp. I felt a little had. They were delicious, I just wish there had been more for the cost of the up-sell.   I'd return if I were in the area and in need of a healthy option, but I wouldn't go out of my way.

I was impressed with the coffee at Bongo Java, which is located inside the Omni. Hotel coffee shops don't generally do anything for me but I was digging the beans at Bongo. The iced coffee was especially delish.   Didn't love the toast your own bagel situation but I guess it keeps things moving faster when they are busy. The staff was very friendly and I swung by several times. Plenty of seating, too.

McGillin's was the second (and final) stop of the night for a birthday outing with friends last Friday.  Why was it chosen to be the final stop of the night?  Because this was the only place I could think of in which a bunch of r-e-a-l-l-y intoxicated twenty-somethings could: 1. still get in 2. continue to get served and 3. carry on like a bunch of teenagers whose parents went away for the weekend and left the liquor cabinet unlocked.    Beer is super cheap here, and it should be.  How else could they possibly lure large groups of people into a bar that smells like a high school football team's locker room, post-game?  My sister actually had a more colorful description than that, but I'll spare those details.      Fun times were had for sure, but I'd rather drink a six pack of Milwaukee's Best in the Bog of Eternal Stench than have to smell the inside of that bar again.

On Friday night, all I could think about was pad Thai. So I knew that with an afternoon to myself planned for Saturday, I was going to treat myself to a movie and some takeout on my couch. Smile was one of the only places on Grub Hub with free delivery, although there was a $15 minimum. I ordered my pad Thai and threw in some lemongrass soup with shrimp.   The meal arrived hot within thirty minutes. The soup was just right - the perfect amount of spicy, sour taste, with fresh vegetables (still crunchy!) and three large shrimp. The pad Thai was enough for two meals. It yielded four cups (I measured). It was a bit drier than I would have liked but I did enjoy the fresh bean sprouts. Next time, I'll ask them to make it a little bit spicy, since there wasn't any heat. Next time will probably come very soon.

I've had two delivery experiences with Petit Roti so far. The first was for chicken pot pies and roasted veggies during winter. I remember loving the pot pies but thinking that the veggies were a bit heavy on the root vegetables. I wish I would have remembered that when I ordered the side of veggies again yesterday when I did the lunch combo. Again, it was a mix of carrots, possibly turnips or rutabaga (I think!) and beets. I haaaate beets! Not taking this away from the restaurant, of course, but more or less making a mental note to not order this side again.   The other part of my lunch combo was half of a beef sandwich with au jus, caramelized onions and roasted peppers. This would have been absolutely delicious if the beef hadn't been so fatty. I pulled off several fatty pieces and was left with maybe two ounces of beef. Maybe.   I really like this place but I think a little more attention to detail, and some additional options for sides, would be necessary to put them in four- or possibly even five-star territory.

Dark Horse is a bunch of little bars within a bar.  I love that Edward L. described the layout like that of a tree house, which is such a great analogy for the place.  It seems that every time I have plans to hang out there, I arrive solo and have to locate my company.  No one ever states which area they will be in, so it's always a manhunt (not a problem when meeting friends; a tad awkward when meeting a blind date).    I can't remember the last time I ate anything there (chicken fingers, maybe 2+ years ago?) but the stuff I see on my visits looks like standard pub grub.  Also standard is the beer selection.  In other words, there will not be a whole lot of deep thinking going on with regards to the menu, but sometimes that's okay.  The pros are the different bar areas, the dartboards and the numerous flat screens.  The cons include the bathrooms, which are always kind of gross and partially out of order, and the music selection, which on a recent night out with Yuri R. and friends, could only be described as 80s hair band-esque.  Really?  One or two songs is funny, any more than that is annoying.    One final note, which could fit in either the pro or con category depending on the evening, is that there are always a ton of men in this bar... and they are not at all shy.  Take that as you will but don't say I didn't warn you.

Glancing down at my receipt from yesterday's café au lait from Shot Tower, I notice the wifi password is typed along the bottom, clearly visible. That, my friends, is the sign of a business that thinks about their customers. If only I would have noticed it yesterday when my wireless card kept crapping out on me, I would have saved myself a ton of frustration! Next time.   The open space with minimal table seating (only one community table is available) and a ledge with stools that line the windowed walls is very inviting. So was the barista on my visit, who seemed to know every customer who walked through the doors. The stools became a bit uncomfortable after a while, which is why I eventually decided to move on, but I could definitely see myself hanging at one of the outdoor tables on a breezy fall day.   My café au lait was made with care, but I had to procure my own pink packet from my purse since my sweetener of choice was not available. I'll certainly return!

I'm glad I gave Sowe a second chance after my first experience, which was just for drinks. We dipped in for a nightcap on the evening of the soft opening. We were seated at a high top near the bar that was only inches from the next high top. The place was super loud even though it wasn't packed. The acoustics definitely need to be softened somehow. Either everyone was screaming or it just sounded like they were.   I chose the cheapest glass of wine on the menu, which was $9. Even Tria has glasses of wine less expensive than that. Meanwhile, several of the beers were also way overpriced (some have been adjusted since but they are still high for the neighborhood). Cocktails are all around $9, which is fine even if it isn't inexpensive. I left unimpressed.  Fast forward a couple weeks and we tried again for dinner. We were seated inside at one of the tables in front of the bar. It was close to 7, but we had missed happy hour, which is from 4-6pm. I'm not sure I know anyone other than myself - because I work from home - who could take advantage of this happy hour, anyway.   Our server, Julian, was cheerful and helpful without being on top of us. One thing I noticed about the menu on this visit that I hadn't noticed before was that there are a few cocktails with calories listed. I ordered a Skinny Mo, which is a lighter version of a mojito. At first sip, it reminded me of a drink I'd get at an all-inclusive. It was made with Malibu rum, after all. But at a mere 51 calories per drink, I was just fine with the tropics. My companion's bloody Mary was made with bacon vodka and had a bacon rim - genius! Normally, I don't like bacon vodka but the kind they use didn't taste like rocket fuel. It just had a nice, subtle bacon flavor.   For apps we went with the buffalo shrimp, which are served around a blue cheese and arugula salad. The shrimp preparation is comparable to shrimp pil pil, with a hint of heat but some sweetness. I'd like a little more buffalo flavor but they were still very good. We also had the mussels, which were in a somewhat heavy coconut broth. I prefer mussels marinara but anyone who likes this style would probably dig these.   At the suggestion of Julian, I ordered the crab cake sliders as my main and the bf tried the duck. He was pleased with his entree and my sliders were very nice as well. The fries were especially delish, though I tried not to eat too many. Summer is coming.   With two drinks, two apps and two mains (one from the sandwich side, one from the entree side), our total came to almost $100, before tip. Now, we normally don't order that much on a normal night but we did want to try an array of dishes. That said, while the food at Sowe is definitely good, I'd be hard pressed to spend that kind of cash on any given weeknight. I get that this place is not trying for a Sidecar or Grace Tavern vibe. But I still think the prices are way high when compared with similar neighborhood spots like Resurrection (which admittedly can get expensive as well), Pub & Kitchen and Rex. The product that Sowe puts out is most definitely worthy of four stars, but the prices keep them at three for now.

I've popped into Bimini on two occasions now and I'm a fan. I've tried a couple of their smoothies, which are solid. I like some of the combos at other smoothie shops a bit more, but I think with some tinkering around I can probably find a smoothie that hits the spot for me.   On my last visit I ordered a chicken caesar wrap to go. The wrap was substantial, not overly dressed, and came with a bag of chips.   Staff has always been very friendly. Great option for something healthy and fast to-go!

I've been a fan of Miles Table since they first opened. Their menu is a mix of brunch staples and some sandwiches and salads. If you dine-in, they often have a lineup of interesting specials. I've always had great experiences with their friendly staff, as well.   I've also ordered delivery on multiple occasions. Their delivery is always really fast and I've never had any issues with accuracy for my orders.   My go-tos are the build-your-own omelet, vegetable avocado wrap, turkey club and avocado blt (preferably on a wrap). Their chipotle sauce is amazing and I would eat it on anything. I have noticed that they can be a little heavy handed with onions on sandwiches and salads; my recent vegetable avocado wrap was a bit overpowered by them. Definitely something I'll want to remember when placing my order in the future. I'm sure it's only a matter of time!   Thanks for feeding the neighborhood, Miles Table!

Not much new to add here, but I did want to give a special shout out to the awesome fish tacos. Three corn tortillas loaded with tilapia, shredded cabbage, pico de gallo and guacamole. My stepmom's frittata was huge enough for two meals. Sabrina's is an awesome choice during the week.

I had an extremely positive experience at the Apple Store in the Cherry Hill Mall yesterday. My nightmarish day began when I realized my laptop wasn't charging, even though it had done so just fine the day before. I had two hours of juice before my screen went black. This, just as I received news that my car needed about two grand worth of work... but that's another story for some other time.   Frustrated, angsty, and a little worried that it was my laptop acting up and not my charger, I took everything in to Apple and grabbed the first employee I saw. In less than 60 seconds we realized my charger was faulty, and about two minutes later, it was exchanged at no charge and no hassle and without any paperwork.   My visit would have been five stars had I not stopped by the iPhone cover section, where an employee came over to assist with my questions. He wasn't super helpful and didn't really add anything to the conversation that I didn't conclude by looking at the packaging myself. So minus one star for that.

This spot has really grown on me over time. The bottled beer selection is sick and the draft list is constantly rotating. Prices are more than fair. Today I had a Flying Fish Hopfish for $3.50. That is a deal, my friends. I also had a turkey burger, which came topped with white cheddar, roasted tomato, arugula and avocado. Well, that's what the menu said, anyway. I expected some fresh slices of avocado but the end result was actually more like guacamole, which was mildly disappointing, but the burger was so damn good I really didn't care. Bonus, it was so big I brought half home with me. House-made kettle chips were lightly dusted with salt and eliminated any cravings for fries (which can be substituted for $1).  Live music goes down several nights a week and I know from experience that this bar is a great place to catch a Flyers game, where you can cheer along with other like-minded fans (and hound on the inevitable random who cheers for the opposing team).

The 30% off sushi deal from Sunday through Tuesday is most definitely what got me to Kabuki for the first time last week. I was dining solo and wanted something tasty but affordable, and Kabuki provided.  Once seated, my server offered a hot towel. This was a particularly welcome gesture as my hands tend to be cold as ice from October through April.  Three rolls were delivered shortly after placing my order. The spicy tuna and yellowtail rolls were both super tasty, while the sweet potato roll was... interesting. Which is kind of why I ordered it in the first place, so no complaints, although I probably wouldn't order it again.  I was in and out for less than twenty bucks, and now I have a new spot in the sushi rotation.

As I drove to Haddonfield on my lunch break today, visions of cupcakes suddenly sprung into my head. My thoughts picked up speed as they rolled down the hill of possibilities:   "Well there IS a new cupcake shop in town."   "I had a light breakfast, and I can choose a healthy lunch to offset the splurge."   "I'll just eat cereal for dinner. This time I mean it."   "Besides, I'm playing hockey tonight."   "CUPCAKECUPCAKECUPCAKECUPCAKECUPCAKE!!!!"   I parked the car, walked past the place I was planning to buy lunch, and proceeded straight to Indulgence Cupcakery.   The quaint, dark-hued shop had the goods displayed front-and-center, and a friendly gentleman was happy to answer all of my questions. There were many questions. I practically quizzed the poor guy on every selection. Yes, the red velvet is topped with a white chocolate disk. The s'mores cupcake is filled with marshmallow (!!!). They do make regular-sized cupcakes, on request and with an order. And so on and so forth.   Red Velvet is always my go-to, but the chocolate options to the left of the case emitted a siren call to my senses. I selected a chocolate peanut butter cupcake, which came to just under two dollars.   Now. I get that people may feel like the cost/cupcake ratio at this place is a little off, but personally, I'd rather pay a dollar and change for a few perfect bites of bliss than spend twice as much on something that will weigh heavily on my conscience and, not to mention, my ass. Bring the kids to a regular bakery. These cupcakes are for grownups.   The cake itself was moist and super dense, almost like a brownie. The frosting was a whipped style. While I typically prefer a denser frosting, the whipped was perfectly appropriate, because the added crisscrosses of dark chocolate and crumbled peanut butter cup on top brought tons of sweetness on their own. Almost an hour later, I'm still feeling cupcake happiness.  Or a sugar coma.  So, to answer Michael M.'s question, I think I love this place!

This weekend, I hosted a surprise birthday party for my husband and Dino's came in clutch with the giant, gold foil number balloons to celebrate the occasion.   I called on Wednesday, and knew I was cutting it a little close, but they were able to deliver the balloons to the venue on the day of the party. Helium is at a shortage right now, so between that and delivery of four (super large) balloons, I paid $70, plus a tip for the delivery driver.   Honestly? It was worth it. The balloons were a super fun add-on that enhanced the celebrations. And, my husband may or may not have found creative ways to wear the balloons as the night rolled on.

I'm still definitely a fan, but I did have an order slightly botched by Cosmi's yesterday. My boyfriend made the rare decision to work from home, so when lunchtime came around and we were both still in our pajamas, we decided to order delivery from Cosmi's. They use an online ordering system which is usually pretty great because you can make specific notes about your order.   We selected two sandwiches that were both supposed to arrive on seeded rolls. One of them did not. I also put pretty specific instructions about what we each wanted on our sandwiches. For mine, I said I did not want oil and vinegar. My sandwich arrived without oil and vinegar, but it was slathered in mayo. Since when do hoagies automatically come with mayo? I had to scrape it off with a knife and I wasn't really happy about that. Also, delivery took twice as long as we were quoted.   My advice to anyone looking for a Cosmi's delivery is to order early, and be very specific about what you do and do not want on your sandwiches.

So I've been back to Alla Spina twice and I'm still loving it. Both times have been at night for some drinks and bites. Drinks are on the pricey side and I've yet to take advantage of their happy hours, so my policy has been to stick with beer, which is never a bad decision anyway.   Favorites from the menu have been the soft pretzels with spicy beer cheese, the poutine, ciliegine salad (mozzarella balls with fresh corn and tomatoes), the delicious truffled mushrooms, the gnocchi (holy shit, the gnocchi!) and the beef tenderloin with mushrooms and pesto.
