And lest I forget, Alla Spina serves the best damn soft serve I've had in a long, long time.   There are so many more things that I'm dying to try. Notably, the beer cheese toast with egg and bacon and, of course, the fried chicken. Needless to say, there is nothing light about Alla Spina's menu, save for maybe the pickles and the oysters.   Also of note is the staff, who all come off relaxed but professional, and always knowledgeable about everything on the menu, from the beer to the bites.   If you haven't been to Alla Spina yet, grab some pals and jump in a cab. Hit up that late night happy hour and have some good times.

Honky Tonk Central is a great time. There are three big floors of live, local bands. I was truly blown away by the talent. Each band played four hour sets non-stop, and then when they were finished, the next band would set up. It was incredible! My favorite of the weekend was the Harold Allen Band, but there were so many other great ones. I felt spoiled.   The layout of the venue is awesome, with big, open floor to ceiling windows that have balcony railings which provide for a really cool indoor but yet somewhat-outdoor vibe.   Service was hit or miss. We scored with John, who took care of us on Saturday. He appeared out of nowhere every time we needed something, and he was as sweet as could be. On Sunday, our service was really spotty. We would have been better off just going to the bar and ordering there. But in all fairness, we only saw one girl working the entire second floor.   The beer selection is limited but when I session drink I tend to go for the easy stuff anyway (pro tip!). That said, the beers got progressively warmer as our Saturday tenure wore on. I don't know if they couldn't get those domestics on ice fast enough for the busy crowd or what, but by the end of the evening I was icing down my drinks in a cup of ice water. We did order dinner during one of our visits; the buffalo chicken wrap with tots was legit!  Definitely looking forward to return visits on future trips to Nashville!
...or maybe I should give Eulogy 1 star for getting me into all kinds of drunken trouble every time I take a seat at the bar.  Nah, can't blame anyone but myself on this one.

It's official: Kai is our official go-to for the three roll combo. The combo is on their menu for lunch or dinner, which is great, and there are quite a few choices so you can mix it up each time. The combo comes with soup or salad and the ingredients are always very fresh. A winner for weeknight sushi delivery!

My lunch at Walnut Street Cafe recently was really good. I walked in without a reservation, which was borderline chancey - the place was pretty bumpin' even at 1pm! Next time, I'll definitely make a res in advance.   We started with some shrimp from the raw bar - they were large and delicious. We also had the romaine salad, which is essentially a caesar. It was very underdressed and didn't have much flavor; I probably wouldn't order it again.   For our mains, we shared the ravioli with brown butter and the rigatoni with guanciale. Both pastas were excellent, but I think I liked the rigatoni slightly more. The serving size for both plates was on the small side, but perfect for a lunch that felt slightly indulgent without making me want to fall asleep. We took our server's recommendation for a white wine to pair, and he was spot on with his suggestion.   I did find the service overall to be a little too intrusive. I felt like we were telling someone everything was fine every three minutes. If your guests look like they're involved in conversation and don't appear to need anything, it's okay to pass on that table touch!   All things considered, I had a very nice first experience for lunch - the hype is warranted! Looking forward to get back for dinner sometime.

A Yelp friend once told me that she occasionally gets her nails done at this place so I decided to give it a shot. I was looking for something a little more low rent than my usual highfalutin places. At $45 for a mani/pedi, Rittenhouse Manicure & Spa isn't cheap, but that ten extra dollars gets you better services and a nicer environment than most of the quick and cheap spots.   The pedi chairs were mostly full when I arrived around noon on a Thursday, but there were still two that were open on the other side of a half wall. I actually preferred this area to the larger room; it was more relaxing. I grabbed a rag mag and tried to relax while also bracing myself for what was sure to be a painful pedicure. I have very sensitive skin which is one of the reasons I normally shell out mad dough for nice salons. Fortunately, Lee was very gentle and the pedicure was actually enjoyable.   Next up was the manicure. I normally ask to skip the cuticle cutters but my nails were in such bad shape that I just let it happen. And since Lee was so careful during my pedicure, I trusted that my hands would make it through without any bleeding. I think I had maybe one small nick when all was said and done but my nails look great so I'm not complaining. I only wish that she would have painted a little closer to the cuticle, since there is a small gap between the polish and cuticles. Why does this always seem to happen at certain salons?  As my nails were drying, I received a shoulder massage which was practically worth the extra money on its own. My nails look great and I'll likely return whenever I don't have the extra cash to plunk down on my fancier spots.

Though I haven't tried much from their new menu, the service I've received and the cobb salad I've enjoyed on two recent trips to Field House warrants a review update. I've been a fan of Chef Andrew Brown's since first trying his food at Opa. I was excited to see what he'd bring to the table at Field House, especially after their renovations and revised beer program.   The cobb salad is just the right size and features fresh, tasty ingredients. I love the use of bacon lardons in place of bacon crumbles. They pack so much more flavor and they are absolutely delicious. The salad is hearty enough for a meal but doesn't feel weighed down, with a lemon vinaigrette in place of a heavier dressing.   I thought I was done with Field House years ago, but the recent changes have me cheering for their comeback. I look forward to catching a game there sometime, and trying more from the new menu.

I had a great experience at Bufad for an impromptu Sunday afternoon lunch. My fiancé and I arrived around 2pm and there were plenty of open tables. The employees were so friendly - like we already knew them! I loved the decor of the restaurant. Very cool tables and light fixtures.   We started with burrata to share, which was just perfect. It was served with some parsley, roasted squash, walnuts and olive oil. We also split the margherita pizza and the sausage pizza. Both were perfectly cooked, toppings were just right and everything tasted great. I loved the breadcrumbs and spicy pepper oil served alongside.   We passed on dessert but received a small complimentary scoop of their salted caramel ice cream which was delicious! I would definitely order that on a future visit. Our total came to something around $50 including tip which isn't bad, especially considering they are BYO. Next time, I'm bringing wine!

I dig City Tap House for something different from the smaller pubs I usually frequent. The beer list is extensive and they always seem to have Bell's Two Hearted on tap, which makes me happy.   Even though the bar is located in University City and there is typically a younger crowd, I've yet to experience anyone acting like a fool. This is fortunate, as I love the high ceilings and open feel, plus the giant windows looking out onto a nicely sized patio with fire pits. I wouldn't want to give that up on account of a few jackasses.   The eats that I've tried in the past have been good, although the kitchen was closed at 11 on a recent Saturday when we rolled in with a crew for a late night bite. Either way, I still dig the place and I look forward to enjoying relaxed spring evenings on that patio.

I'll admit, sometimes it's hard for me to get into the holiday spirit. I hate seeing Christmas-themed-anything before Thanksgiving, and I don't want to play carols all through the month of December. Getting a Christmas tree is something I put off a lot longer than most people, and my track record for sending holiday cards is spotty at best.   That said, there are a handful of things that help get me in the festive mood, and Miracle on 13th Street is definitely one of them. Something about seeing the signage while approaching, plus the slow parade of cars, brings out my inner child. Witnessing a whole city block of residents come together every year to bring a little joy to the season is really heartwarming, even for a semi-Grinch like myself.

I finally made it in to Molly Malloy's for brunch with a large group on Saturday morning. The menu is limited, but everything sounded great. Think basic breakfast items done well.   The omelet I ordered had potatoes, cheddar and chives (I requested egg whites). It also came with breakfast potatoes and a breakfast meat, but I switched out the meat for fresh fruit, which came in a large bowl and included a medley of fresh fruit. My meal was good, but when I tasted the pancakes I had instant food envy. Buttery and crunchy around the edges, these cakes flapped my jack better than Aunt Jemima.   Our waitress was awesome and totally on point with water and coffee refills and anything else we needed. The restaurant wasn't very crowded in the early hours, so I'd definitely recommend it for a group or if you'd like to skip the wait at some of the other spots around town.

My in-laws recently celebrated their fiftieth wedding anniversary, and friends and family were invited to celebrate with them at the Colonial Dames yesterday!   I'd heard of this venue before but this was my first time experiencing it for myself. It's located right near Rittenhouse Square so pretty easy to find. There is a ballroom on the second floor but our party was kept entirely on the first floor, which has one large room and two smaller rooms that both lead to outdoor garden areas. It was really chilly so we didn't spend much time outside, but an event here on a warmer day would be absolutely gorgeous!   I think in terms of catering, there is some flexibility as my in-laws selected their caterer (Schulson) before choosing the location. The staff at the Colonial Dames was wonderful and so accommodating; I'd love to attend another event there and would recommend it to anyone looking for a beautiful event space accommodating up to 100 (best guess) for a smaller wedding or party.

I'm overdue on this review, but the roast pork sandwich that I enjoyed for lunch about a month ago remains a delicious memory. The sandwich, with sharp provolone, broccoli rabe, and a long hot, was hearty and a bit messy. I underestimated the amount of napkins needed. Nonetheless, I managed to eat the entire thing without making a mess, which was no small feat. If I had one suggestion it would be to chop up the broccoli rabe a bit, as it's not the type of veg that bites apart easily.   The platters with choice of protein and sides also looked really great. Definitely looking forward to many more meals from this spot!

The sister property to Conroy Catering's Glen Foerd Mansion, Knowlton Mansion is a gorgeous venue for any special event. The place retains much of its character from when it truly was a house. Living areas are furnished accordingly and seem to flow into the ballroom area. A cellar that is primarily used for cigar smoking feels like something out of an old castle; gray stone surrounds and old barrels and bottles and books are all over the place. Probably for effect, but I totally bought into it.   As always, Conroy Catering put out a fantastic spread at a recent holiday party. Hors d' oeuvres included spicy quesadilla slivers, curried shrimp salad, mini crabcakes and a fabulous sushi presentation. Dinner consisted of three stations; Creole, Italian and American. I didn't even hit up all three, going straight for the filet, green beans and scalloped potatoes at the American station and supplementing with some Caesar salad, gourmet cheeses and assorted charcuterie from the Italian station. While the desserts looked fantastic, I instead opted for a cup of coffee topped with fresh whipped cream... and Jameson.   I highly recommend Knowlton Mansion and Conroy Catering for any large scale event for a lovely experience that will leave a lasting impression.

Unless I have a seat at a bar and a drink in my hand, I most likely will not wait more than a half hour for a table, regardless of the restaurant. Therefore, I can only be found at Sabrina's on random weekdays, with a giant mug of La Colombe, some reading material, and a happy smile that probably reads, "I love my job and I love working from home."   I'll likely enjoy some type of egg white frittata roughly the size of a small country, served any way I want it, since everything is cooked to order. Basic but very tasty breakfast potatoes and thin, grainy slices of Le Bus multigrain toast, plus a puddle of ketchup and Frank's hot sauce will keep the eggs company. Friendly servers who don't make me feel the slightest bit uncomfortable about dining solo will refill my cup and tell me "no rush" when they drop off the check, and mean it.   I may laugh at the hordes of people standing outside the place on weekends, but I'm smiling like a Cheshire cat as I enjoy my peace and quiet at 11am on a Wednesday.

The process of getting a new phone is one that I dread, so thank goodness I walked into this location and got assistance from Shaun Butler. He was personable and made the experience - dare I say - almost enjoyable. (It's hard to enjoy the experience of paying off your old phone while signing your life away on a new one.)   Despite upgrading from an iPhone 6 to a 7 Plus, AND changing from my crappy, overpriced plan to an unlimited one, I am fairly confident that my monthly bill will remain very close to what I was already paying, thanks to Shaun's due diligence.   It should also be noted that this location is clean, bright and up to date. Displays looked nice and they had plenty of sample phones to peruse. I'd go to this location again if I needed anything for my phone, or when that dreaded time to trade up rolls around again.

Spuntino was our first stop for a meal upon arrival in Bucks County on Friday. The pizzeria is a walk-up counter inside of a building with several different food concepts. Towards the back of the building is a private room where Spuntino has table service on nights and weekends. My husband and I met the owner, Robert, while we were ordering and he kindly showed us to the seating area and served us himself, which was above and beyond in terms of service.   We started with a caesar salad which was great, then moved on to a special pie of the day with soppressata and honey, plus the capricciossa, with ham, artichokes, mushrooms and olives. I loved the thin, chewy crust and san marzano sauce; it was a toss up which pie I liked better because they were both great.  I am looking forward to visiting their Northern Liberties location for more delicious 'za ASAP!

My coworker and I went to Bistro di Marino for lunch on Good Friday.  The lunch buffet is the only option at that time of the day.  There was one soup, three salads, two pasta dishes, two chicken dishes and a bowl of fruit salad.    Normally, this selection would have been fine, but since it was the final Friday in Lent I was pretty limited with what I could eat.   The salads were fantastic.  One had walnuts, pears, blue cheese and vinaigrette and another had tomatoes, red onion, Kalamata olives and vinaigrette.  The third was a Caesar, which I skipped.   One pasta dish had fettuccine with eggs and some type of creamy sauce.  I found this combo to be somewhat odd for an Italian pasta dish, and it didn't really do anything for me when I tried it.  The other pasta was penne and vodka sauce, which I have had many times at this restaurant and have always loved.  I tried to pick around the pancetta but my efforts were futile.  At least I didn't eat the chicken, right?  For $12 a person, I would probably return again for lunch, but I definitely prefer the regular menu offerings during dinner service.

Now that the weather is getting nicer, we've been getting into a groove on weekends that includes a long bike ride and hoagie pick-up from Pastificio. It's easy to place an order online and then, when you arrive, just give them a call and someone will bring the order outside.   On my first visit I tried the Pastificio hoagie, which is a delicious twist on a more traditional Italian hoagie. I lightened things up for my second visit with a turkey and cheese hoagie, which was also delish. The bread is really great - harder on the outside, with a smattering of sesame seeds, but soft in the middle.   Looking forward to my next sandwich!

I really like Bud & Marilyn's, and the fact that, somehow, it's still relatively accessible despite being part of the absolutely bustling 13th Street corridor. One of the factors is that they take reservations. So appreciated, especially for brunch!   Speaking of brunch, it's the only full meal I've ever had at Bud & Marilyn's. Aside from that, it's always been drinks and snacks at the bar, which has always been pleasant.   At my recent brunch, I enjoyed the bloody mary and also a moscow mule. I wanted to keep things semi-healthy and opted for the shrimp po' boy benedict, hollandaise on the side. It was good but maybe not as reminiscent of a po' boy as I would have expected. Next time, I'd love to try that nashville hot chicken biscuit sandwich.   I'm still dying to try dinner so Bud & Marilyn's remains on my short list for suggestions when I make plans with friends.

I've got a go-to Thai restaurant, and I've grown accustomed to their food - it's always delicious and fresh-tasting. Tonight, I was feeling lazy so I decided to order delivery from Smile. The lemongrass soup with shrimp was delicious, as usual. The chicken with green curry was sadly not up to par. I didn't like the taste of the chicken and the brown rice I paid extra for was way overcooked to the point of being mushy.   Next time, I'll walk my lazy butt to my usual Thai spot!

I remembered AC Moore being the mad-cheap place to get all my crafting items back in college (sorority life = crafts for every occasion). I haven't had much of a need for these types of items since then, as I promptly ditched every desire to paint, frame and scrapbook the moment I graduated.   Cut to my job with Yelp, and the need to get crafty and creative on a budget has resurfaced. In need of cute but inexpensive materials to make holiday cards, AC Moore seemed like a no brainer. While they had everything I could possibly need to make a pimped-out card, I felt the prices were higher than I would have paid in a Target. Small plastic organizer bins started around ten bucks. Really? Even I know I can get those for about half the price elsewhere.   It's still a great place for one stop craft shopping, but next time I'll probably swing through Target first for less-expensive basics before hitting AC Moore for the niche items.

Despite my so-so experience last time, I couldn't stop thinking about my sandwich from Petit Roti, and especially that incredibly addictive spicy dijon mustard! I decided to try the pork sandwich this week, which turned out to be a hit. The pork was lean and flavorful. I do wish there was a little bit more meat on the sandwich, but overall it was very good.   This time I opted for a side salad, which was a basic but hearty handful of mixed greens and a side of vinaigrette. I also added a side of roasted potatoes, which were perfectly seasoned and exactly what I wanted. I threw half of the potatoes onto the salad and saved the other half for another meal. This half-sandwich, salad and potatoes combo was a total lunch win. Healthy but satisfying enough to get me through the day.

I'm back to show one of my favorite Philly hoagie shops some love. As it happens, one of my best friends just bought a house on the same block, so I expect my Cosmi's visits to be much more frequent.   I placed my recent pickup order through the Yelp page and everything was just as requested. I also threw in a pint of tuna salad so I could make some easy lunches during the week. The tuna salad was great!   Now that I plan to visit on the reg, I'll finally be able to branch out to other items on the menu. A girl can't live on Italian hoagies and shooter specials alone!

My first real pho experience!   After comparing and contrasting reviews for several popular spots for pho, Pho Ha came out on top. You cannot beat the fact that there's parking! Free parking in the city - happy day!   I like lean proteins and steer clear of anything outside of that category. So I took another Yelper's advice and ordered the #2, with lean beef and brisket. My dining companion, Maggie L, ordered the shrimp pho. A plate of sprouts, basil and jalapeños was set on our table, and a few minutes later, huge (and I do mean huge) bowls of pho were placed in front of us.  Y'all, it is really hard to eat slippery noodles with chopsticks and a small spoon! I probably could have done way more damage, but I essentially gave up after successfully shoveling all the protein (and only some of the noodles) into my mouth.   Two large bowls set us back $17 (plus tip). Cash only. What a deal! Looking forward to trying this again and hoping to be a bit more successful with my technique. Open to suggestions!

My mom and I returned for another lunch at Blackbird on Friday afternoon, just before Labor Day weekend.  The restaurant was empty, with the exception of our table.  Our server put our wine on ice and ran through the specials.  He filled our water glasses, returned to take our order and headed back to the kitchen... all the while, our unopened bottle of wine sat taunting us from the ice bucket.  When our server reappeared and said he was going to get us some bread, my mom decided to speak up about the wine.  All was well once the cork was released and the glasses were filled!  To start, my mom had the romaine salad with creamy lemon dressing and a parmesan crisp.  It was very good and the perfect size.  I opted for the soup du jour, a carrot ginger concoction that was delicious down to the last spoonful, which I obtained by tipping the bowl (that's the nice thing about having the restaurant all to yourself; no one is watching!).    For our meal, we both opted for the smaller portion of gnocchi, which recently won a Philadelphia Magazine "best of" award.  The gnocchi was not the thumb-sized variety that I've had in other restaurants.  It was smaller and paired well with equally sized bits of fresh mozzarella.  The tomato-based sauce was very rich and shreds of a bitey cheese were scattered atop the dish.  The smaller sized portion was perfect for lunch and is something I would definitely recommend.  We passed on dessert and lingered over our remaining wine instead.  I am once again looking forward to next time.

I'm happy to have this Chipotle in my hometown, and my experiences have been mostly positive. They sometimes have a huge crowd around peak lunch or dinner times. The line will be so long that I'll opt for another nearby option, instead. The handful of times I have had lunch or dinner (always to-go), I've been happy with my service and meal.

I had no idea Greenstreet Coffee was located so close to where I live until my husband suggested we walk over for a cup one morning when we made the sad realization that we were out of beans. The location is so cute and unexpected; I kept thinking how lucky the neighbors must have felt when a coffee shop/roastery opened right on their block!   We ordered two cups of coffee to go and picked up two bags of beans. We're currently making our way through the Mexican bag and I look forward to trying all of their offerings.

I haven't stopped talking about my incredible dinner at Res Ipsa last weekend. It was my husband's birthday dinner, so we opted for the chef's tasting menu (a steal, in my opinion, for $60/person). I'm usually kind of particular about my food choices but everything on the menu looked delicious so I was down for letting the chefs decide. We were not disappointed!   We started with three plates featuring zucchini, heirloom tomatoes and fried mussels. Each dish was better than the last, and the flavors of summer on the east coast were bursting with every bite.   Next up we had three pasta dishes, plus a smaller bonus dish which offered a bite-sized taste of a fourth pasta. The pastas varied as did the sauces, which covered the gamut from pesto to simple garlic and wine with clams.   You are given a choice of roasted chicken or whole fish as your entree. We did dinner at Res Ipsa about a year ago and remembered the whole fish fondly, so that was a no brainer. The fish was a mild white fish (dorade, I think?) and it was deboned perfectly. It was topped with salsa verde and served with a hearty side of vegetables, all of which were delicious and certainly not treated as an afterthought to the main course.   Last but not least, we received a dessert (with a candle!) to share. It was a fruit tart with the most delicious crust. The perfect ending to a perfect meal. If Res Ipsa has been on your to-try list, make a reservation and enjoy!

When my sister went to West Chester University, I pleaded with her to go to Iron Hill every time I visited.  This did not require much cajoling, as it was basically understood that I would be paying for dinner.  I loved the gargantuan plate of chicken nachos, juicy burgers and my absolute favorite, the mesclun salad.  When she graduated, I was a little bummed knowing that my likelihood of returning to the brewery was slim.    When Iron Hill opened a location in nearby Maple Shade, I was pretty stoked.  I finally got the chance to check it out one night last week with my stepdad.  Despite my original plan to keep it healthy, we ordered the chicken nachos, reasoning that it had been a while since our last outing together (any excuse will do when it comes to satiating one of my vices).  The plate arrived and took over most of our high top.  While the nachos were pleasing to the eye, they lacked considerably in taste.  Other than an abundance of melted cheddar, the toppings were lacking and what was scattered about did not stay in place.  Beans ran for their lives, rolling right off the chips, and jalapenos were scarce.  The area underneath the cheese layer was barren.  The chicken was practically nonexistent; it was almost as though we had ordered vegetarian nachos and a few little pieces had landed haphazardly onto the plate by accident.  Lame.  I had higher hopes for my salad, but the measly plate of leaves that was presented left much to be desired.  What I got was a fistful of mesclun, some pistachios, cranberries and apple chunks and a few shreds of white cheddar which were barely detectable... for $8.50.  Even Saladworks does more justice.      Fortunately, the beer was still on point from my memories at the West Chester location.  The brew managed to subdue my irritated feelings at the lack of effort on the overall meal, but I'd be hard-pressed to return for another underwhelming dining experience.

Well it took me a while to get back to Iron Hill in Maple Shade but last night I made it happen, along with my sister and our dad. The service was great and so was the food. We shared the nachos (creature of habit, here) and there was more than enough for all of us - we brought about a third of the serving home.   All three of us had Caesar salads - my dad's had seared tuna, my sister's had grilled chicken and mine had grilled shrimp. No complaints there, either, though my dad would have liked the fish sliced instead of served in two big pieces, which I would agree with had it been my plate.   To drink, my dad and sister each had one of the house brews while I sipped on water. And now here is my gripe: nachos, three dinner salads (with upgraded proteins on two of them) and two beers cost us $93, including tip. That. Is. Bananas.   Iron Hill's rewards card actually seems like a good idea if you go there with any sort of regularity. I'd imagine you'd easily rack up the rewards with those pricey dinners. Of course, to join the program, it will cost you $25 up front (and that's an annual fee).

Seated in the Kimmel Center for The Philadelphia Orchestra's Tchaikovsky performance, I gazed around the room and had the sensation of being seated in a guitar. The shapely walls were constructed completely in smooth wood, and the sound of the orchestra was crystal clear, even from my seat in Tier 3.   Every area from the lobby to the hallways to the glorious Verizon Hall itself was immaculately clean. Ushers were super sweet and helpful. Gazing out from the hallway on the third level, the architecture of the Kimmel Center was a beautiful sight.  My brother's family Christmas gift opened our eyes to an experience we all enjoyed far more than we expected. I look forward to stepping outside of the box and discovering new interests from here on out.

I finally, FINALLY made it to Sam's Morning Glory on Friday for brunch. Given the opportunity, I'd choose brunch over lunch every day of the week, and I love that many of Philly's notorious bruncheries are open for egg action any day I desire.   The restaurant was smaller than I expected. Now I get the long lines on weekends. I immediately noticed the metal mugs and was excited that my coffee would likely arrive hot and stay hot, but surprised to find that the coffee was just semi-hot, even when I received fresh refills. Also, I only spied Splenda so had to pull out my Sweet-N-Low reserves.   I ordered a breakfast burrito with egg whites, which is quickly becoming my standard brunch order. Every place does them a little differently. I enjoyed Sam's version because it really did taste healthy - there were fresh peppers and onions and just the right amount of cheddar, and the spinach wrap was topped with a red sauce and fresh chopped chives. I liked it, but I would have loved it with a side of pico de gallo or a little guac. No complaints, though. I also enjoyed mixing the homemade ketchup with some hot sauce. That ketchup would be bangin' as a sandwich spread.   Our table was in the middle of the room and an overhead HVAC system dripped just to the right of our table but not far enough away that I didn't take a few splats to the arm. So I'd probably get that looked at. Otherwise, a pretty solid first impression and I'll definitely return.

I've only had Honest Tom's once, but once was enough to know that I need more of Tom and his honest ways in my life. Breakfast tacos are just perfect. Eggs, bacon, guacamole, breakfast potatoes - what more do you need in life? Maybe a little hot sauce. Get it, in several different varieties, on the ledge of the truck.   I'm sure the regular tacos are great too, but I'll likely look for Honest Tom's during breakfast hours for my next visit.

I'm either too old for this stuff or Club Risque is just not up to par with other clubs I've had the pleasure of patronizing. I'm going with the latter.  First, there's smoking indoors. As if I wasn't already going to wake up and think "WTF?" about the previous night's shenanigans, now I also smell like an ashtray. Hangover multiplied.   The decor is outdated and kind of sad. The entertainment didn't do anything for me - there was no wow factor. Not that I frequent strip clubs but I've been to that rodeo enough and have always been kind of mesmerized by the dancing (amongst other things). Not so at Club Risque. And I'm sorry to go there but the "gowns" the women walk around in when they aren't on stage look super cheap and really flammable.   Maybe it was an off night, but with the smoking indoors, it's very unlikely that I will return to find out.

I visited Buffalo Billiards for the first time on Sunday, and I was impressed. I expected a dingy pool hall with a crappy beer selection... but was pleasantly surprised to find a posh looking establishment with fancy bar chairs, plenty of entertaining games, nice TVs and a great beer selection. Not to mention, cheap but tasty eats.   Our large group spent several hours playing skeeball and shuffleboard. I don't want to brag (lie) but I got the highest skeeball score out of my friends.   Quesadillas were huge and pretty tasty. They could have used a bit more time in a pan to crisp up, but besides that, they were satisfying. Same with the chicken nachos. The price was right and we had a great time without breaking the bank. Buffalo Billiards was the perfect place to spend a rainy afternoon with friends.

In what seems like months ago, Blake F., Caroline P. and I made plans to dine at Sycamore.  Our wait was finally over on a blustery Wednesday night, when we descended upon Lansdowne.  The restaurant was full but for one table when we arrived around 8:30.  The décor was warm and inviting, with rich fall colors and holiday accents.  Our lovely server, Elle, seated us and promptly brought water, bread and the amuse bouche du jour, a creamy potato soup, to our table.      Although Chef Sam Jacobson is a friend (full disclosure), he assured us on our arrival that everything we ordered would be served exactly as it would to a stranger.  In other words, he wanted us to have the most honest experience possible.  And since we're all being honest here, I can't think of a single thing Sam could have done differently that would have made the meal better than it already was.  We started with a cheese plate, which featured four very different cheeses that were well complimented by other items on the board, my favorite being the drunken raisins.  I want to eat cheese and drunken raisins every day!    Next up was a fantastic baby arugula salad and a delightfully crunchy carmelized onion, goat cheese and pancetta phyllo tart, which was served alongside a frisee salad.    For my main, I opted for the boeuf bourguignon (although the fontina stuffed meatloaf could be heard calling my name from the kitchen).  The beef was fork tender and served in a hearty broth over mashed potatoes.  The broth itself had strips of tender carrots and - brace yourself - bacon.  It was fantastic but I had to stop short of finishing in order to save room for dessert.  We shared an orange scented flan, a pumpkin cheesecake that had the most wonderful crust and a delicious banoffee tart that Sam claimed the Brits were first responsible for creating.  Many props to our friends across the pond for that one!  The check arrived and with it came three house-made cocoa dusted truffles.  It was a beautiful ending to a fabulous meal.  As Caroline mentioned, we were fortunate enough to catch a glimpse of the New Year's Eve prix fixe menu, and it sounded wonderful.  Do not hesitate to give Sycamore a try; it's a suburban gem and it won't be long before resies are hard to come by!

If I ever make it big enough to own a yacht or a multi-million dollar second home on the beach, I'd like all decor to come from Jonathan Adler. The bright, funky colors and cool patterns are like a modern-day nod to 60s decor.  The price tags on items like picture frames and table games made my jaw drop, but that didn't stop me from taking in every single sight during my brief visit. I was careful not to touch anything and I'd strongly suggest leaving small children at home or outside with the dog. Same with clumsy adults, for that matter.  I found myself oddly attracted to some James Bond-like matchstick holders, which had a rough surface to strike the match. I think to light candles around once a month but maybe I'd do it more if I had one of those nifty conversation pieces in my home.

Rosa Blanca is super cute - I really dig the diner-like vibe they have going in the front room, which is a great place to grab a quiet breakfast during the week. A few menu items caught my eye and I went with the breakfast tortilla, which isn't a tortilla at all but an omelet-like egg dish with potatoes. There are some nice curls of fancy ham on top along with some marinated veggies and also a saffron aioli that was drizzled all over which I would have definitely preferred on the side or not at all. I was really kind of turned off by that, actually. But the rest of the dish was nice.   I started the meal with a cafe con leche which was somewhere between lukewarm and hot but definitely not hot. Then I switched to coffee which was the same temp. I was a bit surprised to see that I was charged for the coffee and that it wasn't just considered a refill (total damage in lukewarm coffee drinks: $7).  My visit was definitely a-okay but what I would really like to do is get in there for dinner and try that delicious looking skirt steak with chimichurri that I've seen in the Yelp photos. Meaty.

I love Zavino so much I am upgrading to five stars. Between delivery orders (which always arrive as-ordered and just as delicious as when you dine-in), to experiences at the restaurant, I think this place is such an unsung hero on the Philly dining scene.   The cheese and charcuterie plate is huge and filling. My friend and I decided to scrap pasta/pizza and order just a couple small plates to round out our meal after devouring this medley of deliciousness last weekend at the bar. The spaghetti squash is so delicious I don't even miss real pasta. Paired with the meatballs, you have an incredible meal that doesn't weigh you down the way regular pasta would.   Our service at the bar was great and I especially appreciated the bartender's willingness to hunt down some after-dinner wine. The port was delish!

It amazes me that after almost a year and a half of working for Yelp I am still discovering new local businesses on a weekly basis. I came across this coffee shop simply because I parked nearby for a meeting. The place is really cool, and when I expressed my wonder, the awesome baristas encouraged me to check out the upstairs, too. This is a great place to either work alone in a cool environment or catch up with friends.    Sadly, I didn't love the coffee. I'm a La Colombe girl and One Shot's coffee just didn't float my boat. But that wouldn't stop me from coming back to try other menu items.

Res Ipsa lived up to the hype! This teeny tiny coffee shop is pumping out some insanely delicious eats. The breakfast sandwich was completely unlike any other I've had. Starting with the homemade english muffin and moving on to how they serve the eggs in frittata form, topped with asiago cheese. This keeps the sandwich from falling apart which I really appreciate. I added the sauteed spinach to my sandwich and it did not disappoint; it was a little drippy but not messy.   The side of potatoes were crispy, crunchy baby potatoes, topped with just the right amount of salt and some chimichurri (or salsa verde?). Delicious! The coffee was great as well.   I'm chomping at the bit to get back for dinner!

Field House is good for two things: watching sports and catching your favorite cover band.  However, if you plan on doing either of these, don't plan on receiving good service because the staff does not know how to handle large crowds.    On the other hand, if food and drinks are what you are after, do go when the home team isn't playing and no bands are scheduled.  The place will be dead and you'll get all the attention you could ever want or need from your server... You'll be the only person there, but at least you'll get a drink in a reasonable amount of time.

Wow. South Helm blew me and my three dining companions away on Friday night. Since the restaurant currently does not accept reservations, we decided to go on the later side and arrived around 9pm with two bottles of wine in tow. We were seated immediately and, while most of the tables were still occupied, they were all finishing up their meals and we ended up being the last table remaining at the end of the night. I felt a little guilty being 'those people', but the staff welcomed us with open arms and we even did some shots together after the meal which was pretty awesome.   But back to the food. The menu is comprised of small plates that change depending on what's seasonal and available. Our fantastic server told us it wouldn't be out of line to try one of everything and so that's what we did. See my photo of the chalkboard menu to get an idea of some of the plates, but be warned: the brief descriptions don't do an ounce of justice to convey the deliciousness of each dish. Maybe that's the point? Pick some things that sound good and then be utterly spellbound by the talent coming out of the kitchen. Worked for us!   It's hard to pinpoint my favorites out of an overall incredible dinner, but if I had to go there I'd say the carrots, seafood fra diavolo, leeks, soft shell bucatini, fried oysters, and stuffed veal chop were my faves. So yeah, basically every dish was stiff competition for tops in my book, and everyone in the group had their own lineup of what they liked best, no dish left behind.   Get thee to South Helm and do it quickly, because this South Philly gem is going to have lines for hours in the near future.

After a lackluster dinner nearby on the Square, I wanted to treat my friend to a drink at the new spot in town.  Off we went to The Franklin Mortgage & Investment Company.  We walked up, and I was very pleased that the bouncers were friendly and welcomed us without any trace of an attitude.  We were escorted inside and were instructed to wait for assistance.  We stood there for a few moments before someone was able to come over, and it was a little awkward as it seemed like everyone in the room turned towards the door when it opened... I even found myself doing it later in the night.  I guess that comes with the territory; it's a place for people watching.  We had a hard time deciding between the many interesting cocktails.  I knew I could handle something with gin but the various whiskey, brandy and scotch drinks had me a little intimidated.  Our server was extremely patient and very knowledgeable with regards to the menu, so with some assistance we were finally able to choose our libations.  My friend had a cocktail that tasted of strawberries and cucumber, and I had a gin concoction with bitters and... some other things, I can't remember what.  It was slightly sweet and very drinkable.  Next time, I'll don my big girl panties and try something a little more stiff.    I loved the vibe and the gorgeous interior at The Franklin.  And yet, while I also loved catching up with one of my oldest friends, I felt like the place would be better suited for a nighttime rendezvous with a hot date.  I'll definitely return, hopefully with an appropriate suitor in tow.

Last Saturday night we enjoyed a little double date action with friends at Rittenhouse Tavern's gorgeous outdoor patio. From the few glimpses I got indoors before settling at our table, the restaurant itself is very pretty and airy. There's a cool art exhibit when you first walk in and some awesome octopi lamps that I wouldn't mind getting my hands on for display in a future abode (I think it's kind of a requirement that you need an actual dining room if you want to own an eight-legged lamp or chandelier).   The cocktail list is well developed. All of the drinks seem like slight twists on classics, which is just what I like. I enjoyed the paloma fizz, although my second glass was a little heavy handed on the mixers. There is also an excellent selection of wines and beers, and prices are more than fair in the beer department.   We were fortunate enough to have some connections in the kitchen, and a round of bar snacks was sent out on the house. I tried the white bean toast and the pickled baby vegetables. Both were very tasty. It should also be noted that the bread basket contains some awesomely tasty carbs.   Next was the fluke crudo. It was a generous portion and the radish and lemon provided nice flavors, though I could have used a little something extra. Or perhaps I was only supposed to whet my appetite for the flavors to come. After waffling between the scallops and the skirt steak, I ultimately decided on the scallops at the suggestion of our server. So glad I listened to that advice! The skirt steak, which I was able to try, was nice, but the scallops were absolutely delicious. Perfectly seared and served in a delicious broth containing rhubarb and English peas, it was hard to share (but I did - reluctantly). A side of broccoli was just right for sharing and really delicious.   We passed on dessert but I'm sure we'll have the opportunity again. Rittenhouse Tavern is perfect for anyone who craves the sophistication of Rittenhouse dining with a slightly more relaxed vibe.

If the roaring headache I have today is any indication of the fun I had last night, then the Best of Philly party was certainly a doozy. Food stations in every corner (sushi!!!), passed hors d' oeuvres, a live band, lots of pretty people, and booze. Lots and lots of booze.     I mixed, I mingled, I imbibed. And then came the afterparty.

We ordered delivery from Anastasi last night. While our experience was a little bit lacking, I am willing to accept that it may have been an off night and would certainly try them again.   My husband ordered branzino with fries and I got the broiled crab cakes with fries. We also ordered a quart of Manhattan clam chowder to have with lunch today. I didn't see an option for adding on cocktail sauce and requested some in the notes of the order.   The order arrived and my husband's fish was served with rice and vegetables instead of fries. This actually wasn't too bad because my crab cakes came with so many fries that I was happy to share. Unfortunately, there wasn't any cocktail sauce and I thought the crab cakes were a bit dry. Today's chowder was great; filled with meaty clam pieces and vegetables.   Again, not the most accurate order but we love seafood and know Anastasi is one of the best places to get it super fresh. We'll give them another try soon and I will update when we do!

My first experience with DnA was for the Yelp's Big Primpin' event in August. The salon provided a discount for future appointments that were booked that night, so I went ahead and scheduled an updo with Jackie, who styled my hair the evening of the event.   Fast forward to the day of my updo. I wanted something cute but not overly done for an upscale event I was attending. Jackie worked her magic and had me in and out of her chair in probably thirty minutes with my hair looking fantastic. It also felt light and there weren't any bobby pins digging into my head all night.   The staff are all great - super friendly and welcoming. When you arrive you are offered water, beer or wine, which is awesome. While DnA has been around for a while, the space they are in now is brand new and very cool. Definitely check them out if you are looking for a new permanent salon or even just shopping around!

Palm Tree market never disappoints. Today was my first time in their NoLibs location, which is about twice the size of their other markets.  Ordering at the deli counter was quick and easy, and by the time I grabbed a couple snacks and headed to the register, my wrap was already ready.   I love that each location offers very consistent products. The deli meats and salads are always fresh and delicious, and the employees are always friendly. You also cannot beat the snack options. I'm amazed by how much they manage to stock in these stores!   Don't sleep on the cold cases, which have a nice variety of fresh fruits, veggies, cheese and other staples. The fresh cut fruit is always delicious year-round. I'm not a big fruit person but even I can get on board when Palm Tree does all the work of chopping it up for me!

Another 5-star worthy experience at Friday Saturday Sunday!  My boyfriend and I had reservations for the New Year's Eve seating at 8 p.m.  We arrived a little early and went to the Tank Bar upstairs for a drink... but waited and waited and waited some more for the bartender to have a free second to take our drink order.  She was understandably busy but there probably should have been another person working the bar.  Before ever getting a drink, we were summoned to our table, which was downstairs in a very cozy, romantic corner of the restaurant.  From there on out, our experience was excellent.  We started off with a bottle of white, and I chose the lobster bisque to start, while the bf had shrimp cocktail.  The bisque was good, but it was catapulted to greatness by the amount of lobster that was in it.    For my entree, I decided on the filet when I saw the dish getting dropped off at the table next to us.  It came alongside some haricots verts and a potato latke.  Wow.  It was probably my favorite meal in all of 2008.  Calorie count: who the hell cares?  It was delicious.  For dessert, we opted for two different types of cheesecake, which I was way too full to take more than a couple bites of, although each was very good.    In addition to the fantastic meal and awesome service, the owner of the restaurant threw in an extra special NYE touch.  He took professional pictures of each and every table and collected addresses so he could send a proof in the mail!  I can't say enough about how much I love this place.  I'm already giving the bf the wink and nudge and dropping hints (okay, more like loud statements) about V-day.

Valanni, you little devil!  When did you go getting all chic to die?!  I mean, I knew you had a facelift since the last time I dined with you but I didn't know you had a full body restoration.  You look fabulous!  While we only stopped in for a drink after dinner, I was impressed.  The decor is stylish, the music was great and my mojito was delish.  Best of all, it had a rock candy garnish!!!!  I tend to get crazy excited over the little pleasures in life and this was no exception.  My girlfriends had sangria and said it was excellent.  Can't wait to come back and try the eats as well!

I'm bumping Nordstrom Rack up to four stars. During my visit last week, I looked down at my watch and realized I had already spent two full hours browsing the store and trying on clothes and shoes. Two hours of my life!  There was a lot more variety with brands than my previous visits, and I actually had to force myself to put some things back so that I wouldn't spend a fortune. I walked away with some totally hot Donald Pliner heels that I imagine will get a lot of mileage on the dance floors of Las Vegas in a few weeks.

Welcome to the neighborhood, On Point! I checked out this new spot for a late breakfast today and was really impressed. First, I walked in and received the warmest welcome from pretty much all of the staff. Thanks, all!   Once seated, I took in the cozy cuteness of the room. I was never at the former business that occupied the space but I understand it was very different. On Point's space is fresh, bright and just really pretty.   The menu offers tons of great options and I can't wait to try all of them. I knew I was going to keep things pretty healthy with an omelet, but while I was talking to one of the staff members I found out that their fried chicken is made with tapioca flour, which makes it gluten-free. Duly noted!   I ordered an omelet with veggies and bacon and was extremely pleased. Not only were the eggs fluffy and amazing, but the ingredients were diced up and blended really nicely. The potatoes on the side were incredible. They were seasoned with lots of fresh herbs and I didn't want to stop eating them.   Can't wait for my next visit (it won't be long!), and wishing this team the best. If On Point adds wifi, they may never get me to leave.

Of all the movie theaters in a 30 minute Jersey-radius, this is by far my favorite.  Although... after going from the Ritz 16 to "Showcase at the Ritz," things aren't as good as they once were.  My main complaint is the bathroom sitch.  During two recent visits, the cleanliness of said b-room was questionable and paper towels were a thing of the past.  Maybe they are "going green" or something but I really hate touching the door with my wet hand.  Bring back the paper towels--I promise to only use one per trip!      Despite the bathroom issue, this theater is still my preferred place for movie-watching.  There are always a few indie flicks that you definitely won't catch at other suburban theaters.  And thankfully, whatever rule they have about excluding young children still exists, because I continue to enjoy my cinema in peace, without anything too obnoxious going on around me.    It should definitely be noted that the popcorn here is waaaaaay better than at other theaters.  I suspect it's because it's popped fresh and/or laced with cocaine because my good intentions of "just a diet soda" seem to fly out the window once I get my first whiff of buttery goodness. On the one in five visit when I do maintain my self-control, the coffee bar rocks my world.    Showcase might not be The Ritz of yore, but it still blows other theaters out of the water.
Whole Foods: The only time cooking dinner becomes more expensive than going out to dinner.   But they have a taco bar now!

I'm bumping up to four stars as a result of friendlier service, pitchers of water and bottomless coffee. Today I met a friend for lunch and ordered a whole wheat everything bagel with veggie cream cheese, tomato and bacon, plus a cup of coffee. The total was around ten bucks, which is still pretty expensive, but since it was lunch and not breakfast I didn't mind. There are now pitchers of ice water with lemon, which I'm happy to drink over paying for a bottle of water.   My bagel sammie was absolutely delicious, and it came with slices of fresh cucumber on the side, which I then stuffed inside to add a little more crunch and flavor. Again, this isn't an every day type of place, but for a really tasty bagel and a cute place to have lunch, it's solid. Also, the wood burning oven smells like a campfire. Who doesn't love that?

The raspberry iced tea is beyond delicious. And, it comes unsweetened, so I can add all the pink packet chemicals I want with no extra calories! The option to add fresh lemon and mint leaves is just frosty icing on the cake.   The lunch options I spied looked absolutely delish, and I'll surely return to check them out. If it's a nice day, the tables and chairs outside provide excellent people-watching. So glad I was turned on to this new-to-me gem in Old City!

There's a lot to like about Plenty. For example, the barista/server who was working while I was there this week, Michael, was really great. Friendly, helpful, didn't make me feel like I was annoying even though I was there for a while - pretty much everything you'd want in a barista.   My latte was superb. My food was... eh. I used to love sandwiches from Plenty but I just find them so lackluster now. Ingredients aren't really plentiful and I often find myself hungry again a few hours later. I do like that their chicken salad is made with minimal mayo and some mustard mixed in. I just wish there was more than two tablespoons of it on a sandwich!   Downgrading to four stars. I still love Plenty the cafe, but Plenty the restaurant isn't really wowing me.

I was lucky enough to sample some of Plenty's fare at the Flavors of the Avenue preview event. One bite of their pancetta mac and cheese and I was hooked. Then I tried a slice of the tasso ham panini, and the spices and flavor blew me away. Passyunk Ave requires a car ride for me, but I don't mind going out of my way for quality businesses I want to frequent.   Which is exactly why we jumped in the car to head to Plenty for a quick and easy dinner last night. The friendly owners apologized profusely because a shipment had not come in on time so some of the items were unavailable. No matter, I still had to decide between several of the sandwiches that were. Eventually, I ordered the chicken salad and my boyfriend chose the meatballs.   We took up a couple spots at the window counter space and our sandwiches were brought out a few minutes later, along with a side of their amazingly cheesy mac and cheese. The chicken salad was phenomenal; there was mustard mixed in with the mayo, so it wasn't too heavy-tasting. The mix also had diced celery and dried cranberries, which was great. The meatball sandwich was a bit messier but delicious, with just the right amount of sauce and very tasty meatballs.   I wish Plenty was in my neighborhood, but I'll settle for a car ride away!

For Christmas last year, my thoughtful boyfriend gave me four bottles of wine, each with a tag that listed the restaurant for which the bottle was selected. We decided to split them into seasons to enjoy throughout the year. On Friday, we went to Koo Zee Doo with the third bottle.  Our server told us right away that the portions would be large, and he recommended ordering a couple starters and sharing an entree. While Art lobbied for the special of the day, suckling pig, I had my heart set on the Portuguese steak. I reasoned that the red wine would go along perfectly. That steak ended up being absolutely incredible, with fried potatoes and a delicious brown gravy.   Prior to that we enjoyed the smoked sausage, which was easily the best appetizer as it was bursting with rich flavor. The braised kale alongside was incredible. Pureed potato soup with chorizo discs was very nice, and a chopped vegetable salad provided enough hearty veggies to satisfy a week's worth of requirements. Think broccoli, brussels, carrots, radishes and beets.  We ordered a chocolate bread pudding for dessert which turned out to be the only letdown. The dessert was more like a chocolate lava cake, and the strong, surprising taste of cloves completely overpowered. I did enjoy my coffee, which I had never heard of before my visit (Peregrine).   I have a feeling it won't be long before I'm craving that steak again.

Am I total tool for admitting that I actually like this place?  I'm not talking every night of the week, but I do have fun whenever I end up here.  Maybe it's because I'm usually half in the bag already, maybe it's because I'm reminded of my college nights in frat party basements or maybe it's because I'm just so damn relieved that the bathrooms themselves are way cleaner than the aforementioned frat party basements.  The point is, Drinker's always provides an experience that is both cheap and fun.  They also provide the Beastie's Licensed to Ill cd in their jukebox.

I had an Uber Eats credit and we were craving pizza, so decided to give LaScala's a try. I'd been to one of their other locations for a bridal shower before, and was really impressed with the food.   Our experience overall was solid, though delivery took a lot longer than the quoted time. I called the restaurant at one point after our delivery window to check on the status. They told me it was on the way and, sure enough, the pizza arrived about ten minutes later.  We ordered a caesar salad, large classic pie, and small white spinach pie. This was more than enough food for two meals plus a couple extra slices. The pizza was best after a quick reheat in the oven; I especially enjoyed the white pizza.

To be honest, I had avoided K'Far because I'd heard about long lines and I am not about the line life. One weekday morning I was out for an early walk with my husband and we ended up in K'Far's vicinity, so decided to pop over. There were only a few people waiting for orders so the timing worked out perfectly!   We ordered two egg and cheese Jerusalem bagel sandwiches, a hot coffee and a tehina chocolate chip cookie. My only wish was that I had the foresight to order more sweets to-go. The egg sandwiches were perfect! The bread was absolutely incredible, and the egg to cheese ratio was just right. The chocolate chip cookie that we shared at home later was delicious.   The good news is you can also place pick-up orders online which will soften the blow if there are any major lines happening. I'll be scheming my next visit for sure!

I love Nordstrom Rack, but I was skeptical over the new location in Center City, because I assumed that everything would be picked over by the lunch crowd. Not so, as I was pleased to discover on my visit today.   The store is still very new but I was impressed by the tidiness and selection, especially with regards to the lingerie department. While I will likely favor the Cherry Hill location, it's nice to have the option to shop the Rack in the city as well.

Another win by the Pub & Kitchen team. With no reservations on a Saturday night, we went early in hopes that there would be a table outside or seats at the counter. We were lucky enough to score a table in the dining room, and in the cozy corner by the window, no less.   The menu currently has an abundance of seafood, but there are some other options as well for those who don't partake. We were treated to some oysters to kick off the evening. They were small, plump, briny and just right. The perfect start to a summertime meal.   I wavered between a lobster salad and the oyster chowder, both on special that night. We ended up trying both, and if I were faced with a choice between the two I'd go with the chowder. The salad was nice and light, but the chowder had great flavors that really stood out. Throughout the meal, we had wines to go with each course and they all paired very nicely. The servers rotated and all really knew their stuff; it was clear they had sampled the menu and were able to provide personal recommendations, which is always nice.   My entree was scallops over mushy peas. I never thought I would willingly eat peas until I tried the mushy peas at P&K when they were served with the fish and chips several years ago. I hear the secret is butter. Lots and lots of butter. The dish was really awesome; the scallops were perfectly seared and the peas were great, of course. There was some asparagus thrown in as well. Lots of pretty green on that plate. My beau had the halibut with chorizo, which was awesome. Just do it. We also tried a few bites of the duck, which was excellent, especially when mixed with the fava beans and mushrooms.   At this point. I was completely stuffed and couldn't fathom another bite. Not even a nibble of what I'm told were the most awesome sugar cookies ever. I'll surely save room next time for some post-dinner cheese, which is apparently a can't-miss part of the meal at Fitler DIning Room. Next time, for sure.

I almost crashed my car the first time I drove by the large, newly constructed building with a sign that said "Coming Soon: Nordstrom Rack." Like Angela J, I missed the grand opening on May 5, but I am not one to shop in a huge crowd anyway. With some errands to run in Jerz on Friday, I penciled the store into my day, daydreaming of all the fab threads I was going to obtain.   Sadly, my balloon deflated just a bit when I arrived. Appearance-wise, walking into Nordstrom Rack felt like walking into a slightly nicer Ross. It was clear I was not in regular Nordstrom anymore. It may sound somewhat snobbish, but I loathe shopping in stores like Ross or Marshalls. Every time I give them a chance, I waste my time and come out empty-handed. My mom and siblings always have tons of luck, but perhaps they have more patience or a better eye for spotting the good stuff? I don't have the gift.   So I started to feel the same detached dizziness while circling the many racks of mismatched items, trying to find the few pieces that were right for me. As always, I ended up in the dressing room (which was quite nice, with enough space to move and plenty of hooks) trying on a bunch of ridiculous pieces that weren't right.   With some of my favorite brands like BCBG and Joe's Jeans on the shelves, I will definitely give this place another chance. But my first impression left a little to be desired, and I longed for a trip down the street to the real Nordstrom.

I finally made it to 10 Arts. Well, I made it to the lounge, anyway. It was a Thursday, later in the night and we arrived to a pretty lively scene. A DJ was situated in a corner and ladies were dolled up like it was prime time on Saturday.   Our threesome grabbed one of the only high tops available, and we perused the bar menu while ordering martinis and Manhattans. While I personally found the prices to be on the high side, we were undeterred as we had already imbibed and on empty stomachs no less. We ordered some oysters, some pretzels and a flatbread pizza.   The oysters were so perfect, so delicious, that we ordered another round. At $3 a pop, they add up quickly. The pretzels, while tasty when dunked in the spicy mustard and cheese sauces, were probably not worth their eight dollar price tag.   I will definitely return for another swanktified evening, but more likely for happy hour or the final drink of a night out.

You guys, Chick's is not playing around when it comes to breakfast sandwiches. They are $6 or $7.50, depending on whether you want meat. And hot damn these sammies are legit!   You have a choice of how you'd like your eggs, type of cheese, type of bread, and choice of breakfast meat. There are other toppings available for an additional cost.   I had scrambled eggs, American cheese and bacon on an english muffin. I ate the sandwich around 9am and wasn't hungry again until 3pm. I probably could have split it into two meals but it was so delish I polished off the whole thing! My husband, whose brilliant idea it was to get the sandwiches, was a little miffed that the english muffins weren't properly toasted and crunchy (they were warmed on a flat top). I normally would share this opinion but actually thought the muffin tasted great as-is because it was so fresh!   100% getting after these sandwiches again in the near future!

Blake and I decided to start the New Year off right with a little double date action on the first night of 2010 (or "ten," as the cool kids are calling it).  I was the first to arrive and was about a half hour early to our 8 p.m. meet-up.  This worked in my favor as I needed a hair of the dog drink to drag myself out of the foggy depths of one part NYE hangover, one part Winter Classic letdown.  The bar was fairly quiet, with only a few seats occupied throughout, mostly at the tables.  Trying to make a beer selection from the extensive list in my current state was not unlike trying to solve a Rubik's cube while intoxicated.  I decided to ask Molly, the lovely bartender that evening, for assistance.  Based on my preferences, she selected a seasonal draught with a high ABV content and tons of flavor.  I was feeling human again just in time for my company to arrive.    At this point, the tables were almost all taken, so we decided to set up at the corner of the bar, so we could still chat somewhat across from each other.  Although there were many items on the menu that sounded tempting, the fried chicken with German potato salad had my number.  I was not disappointed.  The chicken was drizzled with a spicy honey that was to-die, and the German potato salad was on another level.  Instead of bacon, it contained bits of fried chicken skin, and the salad had a tangier bite than the sweeter version I grew up eating.  My grandmom will probably beat me down with her little German fists shall she ever read this, but... Resurrection's potato salad had her recipe beat (just by a little, I promise!).    My date had a flaky turnover stuffed with duck confit, which was a special that had been on the New Year's Eve menu.  I might just lobby to get this onto their regular menu in the future.  It was excellent!    Several more beers and a number of very strong Irish coffees later, we finally called it a night.  Despite being in a section of the city that I was previously unfamiliar with, I will gladly go out of my way to visit this fine establishment time and again.

My experience at KQ Burger started off on the wrong foot but ultimately ended up working out well. I had a gift certificate from a promotion I worked on with University City Dining Days. My guest and I placed our orders on the kiosk and I mentioned the gift certificate to the employee, who told me that the certificate was no longer valid as it was part of a limited time promotion. There were no date restrictions or anything on the certificate, but there wasn't really anything I could do so I just paid for the order. Note to management: please put clear instructions on limited-time offers to avoid confusion!   As it was a Saturday afternoon, the food hall wasn't very crowded and my order was cooked right away, resulting in a five minute or so wait. The burgers were hearty and delicious. My guest had the classic, with a few modifications, while I had the smokey. We shared an order of cheese fries, which were really good. At $34 for two burgers, the fries, and two waters, I thought this was a pretty reasonably priced lunch. I'd probably avoid during super busy times because I imagine the wait could get long. Otherwise, I'd gladly return!

I dined at Fond with eight others the night before Thanksgiving. Service was excellent on all accounts, and it was clear that everyone on the staff was well-versed in all matters food and wine.   The guys in our party opted for the tasting menu, while the ladies went for a regular three course meal. The tasting menu is typically only offered if the entire table participates, but we were accommodated due to the size of our group.   I chose the mushroom risotto with hazelnuts and truffle to start. This was easily one of the best risottos in recent memory and I would highly recommend it. None of the ingredients overpowered and everything went very well together. My main course featured seared scallops, served with grilled romaine tossed in a Caesar aioli, with a roasted red pepper sauce alongside. Others at the table raved about this dish but I was a little underwhelmed myself. The fish special that one of the other girls ordered looked phenomenal, however.   The men generously shared their dessert course with the fairer sex. A chocolate torte with crunchy hazelnuts was enjoyable, but the French press coffee I ordered stole the show. Passion fruit meringues were a dainty little treat that packed a flavorful punch to close out the meal.   Fond's menu changes seasonally and there aren't many safe options for picky eaters, so leave those friends behind when planning a trip. I personally look forward to returning after the reincarnation of said menu!

My dad has been raving about this place for years. He especially loves their Caesar salad, which he apparently orders nine times out of ten. I wanted to see what all the fuss was about so we made plans to meet for lunch one weekday afternoon.   We sat at the bar and my dad introduced me to the friendly owner and we talked about food and restaurants for a bit. We both ordered Caesar salads and cream of asparagus soup to start. The soup was creamy and velvety and rich with flavor.   Then we received a plate of smoked salmon and capers and some duck spring rolls, courtesy of the kitchen. I'm not a fan of eating salmon cold but always give it a try anyway. I think my dad was new to this dish but he also tried it and seemed to like it. We both enjoyed the spring rolls.   Then came the infamous salad. To me, it was a good Caesar salad, with nicely grilled shrimp. To my dad, it was heaven. He got his with shrimp and chicken. Next time, I think I'll take the owner's advice and branch out to try some of their pasta. But I am glad I finally got to check out my dad's favorite lunch spot, and having some one on one time with him was certainly one of the highlights of the week.

I don't know if Uber's standards for their UberX drivers and vehicles has lowered to keep up with demand in Philadelphia, but it sure seems that way. In the past few weeks alone, I've been picked up in several shoddy cars, including some that reeked of recently-extinguished cigarettes. I've also had at least one driver with questionable hygiene.   Additionally, about three in four drivers are not familiar with the city enough to forego their gps. The major problem with this is that the gps system Uber uses has lately been way off in terms of accuracy. It's super rare that I get into a car and the most direct route is used. If I'm not paying attention, I could end up several blocks past where I should have been let out or turned onto a more direct route. I thought part of the Uber experience was to sit back, relax and let the driver do the work? Now, I'm often the navigator in a dumpy car no better than one of the city's cabs, the only advantage being that UberX is still slightly cheaper. I am over it. Perhaps it's time to give Lyft a chance afterall.

After going for sushi and striking out not once, not twice, but three times because of a lack of reservations, we took our bottle of white to Blue Cat in hopes that there would be an extra table for two. The restaurant was pretty busy but we were seated right away by the window. The bottle was popped, waters poured.   The menu sounded awesome, and by that point we were absolutely famished. Prices seemed great, even for what we thought were a la carte entrees. More on that later. We each ordered an appetizer; an empanada for him and a seafood stew for me. Both arrived hotter than the blazes of hell. I'm quite impatient, and I do enjoy my food served hot, but even I had to wait for this soup to cool down from boiling temps before going in. The soup came in a very large bowl, probably too big for a starter. A cup of soup as an option would be awesome. The broth was very flavorful and there was a lot of seafood. I tried a few bites of the empanada and enjoyed that as well.   There were two fish fillets of the day, salmon and cobia. I went with the salmon while the boyfriend opted for cobia. The menu describes the fillet of the day as being pan-seared and served with mango, avocado, cilantro and lime. This led us to believe that we should order sides separately, so we also ordered rice and beans and fried plantains. The sides came out first, looking awesome and once again in generous portions, but we were quite surprised when our fish arrived served over a mound of food, including fried plantains. I hate wasting food, and it was pretty obvious that we were going to have a ton leftover (which we couldn't take home as we were leaving for the weekend the next morning). It really bugged me that our server didn't say anything when we ordered that side of plantains, which we barely touched since there were plenty on the plate.   Aside from the fact that we had enough food on our table for double the amount of people, everything was really good. Well, from my point of view. I thought the salmon was excellent, and the various accompaniments (avocado mash, plantains, pico de gallo, mango salsa and salsa verde) only added to the dish. My other half was not as pleased. His cobia was breaded, and he felt that it was pretty flavorless. It was also presented differently, without the mango salsa. Our server never mentioned that the two fish fillets were prepared differently.   While I was more than happy with my meal, my boyfriend was less enthusiastic. I really want to try Blue Cat again, and I'm hoping to convince him to come along. We'll definitely make it a point to ask more questions.

We revisited Anastasi for takeout over the weekend, and I'm so glad we did! The pasta dishes were jumping out at us this time, so my husband ordered the linguini with mussels (red sauce) and I went with the lobster pasta, which came not only with a very generous portion of lobster tail, but also jumbo lump crabmeat, shrimp, and scallops, in a blush sauce.   We started with clams casino which I have to admit I'm extremely picky about. My Grandmom's recipe is my gold standard and I've yet to find a restaurant that comes close. My husband thought they were good, but I'd probably opt for something else as a starter in the future.   The pastas were priced in the twenties and thirties which I was fine with for a nicer meal on the weekend. However, the portions were sized to feed multiple people! My husband's linguini and mussels came in a small bucket while my lobster pasta arrived in a small aluminum tray, like the ones you see for catering! We enjoyed two hearty dinners plus one lunch thanks to these generous portions. Definitely looking forward to more Anastasi nights!

My stepmom suggested Curran's for a recent get-together over our usual local bar. Since I had never been, I wanted to check it out and see how the two compare.   First thing I noticed was the loud club music... at dinnertime on a Friday. Maybe fun for later in the evening but a bit out of place given the time and clientele (mostly families). I asked our server about their beer selection and the most unique offerings were Yuengling Octoberfest and Sam Adams Octoberfest. Very sad indeed.   The food is where things picked up. My stepmom had a chicken parm dinner with mashed potatoes and green beans and she raved about her food. The mashed potatoes were delicious and definitely homemade. I opted for a buffalo chicken wrap with curly fries and it was great. The wrap didn't fall apart and the ingredients were fresh and tasty. The fries were delicious and plentiful.   Service was slow at times but our server was clearly covering most of the tables, which seemed like a lot for one person. A band started setting up by the time we were leaving which is pretty cool. If these guys improved their beer game they would be super solid. But for now, I'm going with a-ok.

I was looking forward to checking out the bar at William Douglas for their 9 p.m. happy hour, which is featured on their website.  When I arrived, the scene was surprisingly dead for a Friday night.  I took a seat at the bar and inquired about the happy hour menu, and was informed that it was no longer offered and the website "had not been updated in months."  The bartender suggested that I try McCormick & Schmick's next door, which did have a 9 p.m. happy hour.  I text messaged my friends the change in plans and off I went.

Absolutely love having Bud & Marilyn's as an option when flying domestic in Philly! I popped in recently for a meal before a flight and was happy to see a wide array of options. I ordered the huevos rancheros, which came with vegetarian chorizo. I'm trying to expand my horizons with meatless meals and this seemed like a great opportunity to try something new. The dish was absolutely delicious!   Service was a little on the slow side considering the airport location, and a cup of coffee cost almost four bucks. Nonetheless, it's great to see PHL stepping up its game in the food and bev department. Fingers crossed the international terminal gets some love, too!

J'aime Brasserie par Niche!   My husband and I had a 7:30 reservation for Friday night and this place was pretty poppin' when we walked in. Tables were being turned so we headed to the bar for a drink. The bartenders seemed very busy but eventually one of them was able to grab us a couple glasses of the house white. Soon, our name was called and we were shown to our table.   Our server, Josh, was sweet and when he was unsure of something (wine) he'd ask the manager. I so appreciate that over someone just trying to BS their way through!
