The menu had recently changed a bit and when I mentioned that I had been eyeing up the scallops but saw they were now served with beets, which I hate, Josh definitively told me not to order the scallops. I appreciated that, because I ended up trying something I might not otherwise order.   We started with gougères (cheese puffs) for the table which were heavenly. Though I really wanted the French onion soup, I opted to keep my starter light and had the mixed lettuces salad, which was nice. My husband allowed me some tastes of his soup, which was heavenly. For the main dish, I had braised beef, served over potato purée, with bacon lardons and carrots. This dish was not only comforting but also perfectly prepared and delicious. My husband had the poulet au vinaigre, a rustic and wonderful French dish.  No room for dessert, unfortunately, but we really loved our meal and would definitely go back on a return visit to St. Louis!

This is a tough one. I'm between two and three stars (only because the restaurant is still fairly new), but I honestly feel like my experience was more of a two. I arrived around 5:30 and asked about happy hour specials. The response from the host (manager?) was "every day is happy here" or something along those lines. This made me smile, but when every other bar within walking distance is offering happy hour specials, you probably won't see me back at Barcelona during the hours of 5-7.   Nonetheless, wine prices are fair, and they also offer a choice between 3- or 6-ounce pours. The wine list is extensive and there's probably something for everyone. The bartender asked my friends and I our preference of still or sparkling water. Two of us went for still while my other friend chose sparkling. For the rest of our time there, another bartender continually topped off the still waters with sparkling. This was an example of the distracted service we witnessed during our time seated at the bar (though our female bartender was on point and seemed to be handling the majority of customers seated there).   We decided to order a handful of plates to start and go from there. We ordered the ensalada mixta, heirloom tomato salad, pulpo, scallops and mushrooms. To be blunt, both salads looked like something I could easily construct at home, and I am no top chef. The ensalada mixta featured olives, onions and tomato. The olives contained pits and were simply tossed onto the salad, which was essentially a plate of baby romaine hearts, some chunks of tomato, sliced onion and vinaigrette. The entire salad was covered in flecks of salt which was really heavy handed. The tomato salad was similarly basic - four slices of tomato with some more red onion slivers and a couple specks of basil. I did enjoy the sherry vinaigrette used on this dish but, again, it wasn't very special.   Our favorite dish was the scallops, which were lightly seared and served in some sort of creamy sauce. Which reminds me: not a single dish was served with a spoon or any type of serving utensil. So we didn't really get much of that creamy sauce, as we all had to pluck our scallops from the dish with our respective forks.   The pulpo arrived as one very thick chunk, smothered in sauce. We all agreed this presentation was pretty unappetizing. I thought the flavor was okay but the sauce really overwhelmed the octopus. Why not sear the tentacle and serve it over the sauce? Finally, the mushrooms. We all couldn't help but compare this dish to another local tapas restaurant's version. The mushrooms were fine but when you've tasted the others it's hard not to want for better.   At this point, we decided to cut our losses and bounce to another spot for heartier bites. Maybe we ordered wrong, maybe it was an off night, maybe a lot of things. All I know is that I was pretty excited to try Barcelona and pretty let down by the experience. I'll likely come back at some point but probably for a snack as opposed to a dinner.

I've got mad love for Green Aisle. Where else can you get all the trimmings from your favorite spots around the city and suburbs? We're talking creamy hummus from Zahav and those gorgeous meringues from Fond, locally farmed meats, produce and cheese, Severino pasta and Market Day Canelé, to name a few.   And let's not forget their killer cocktail mixers. A generous friend sent us a crate full of cocktailing goodies from Green Aisle, including several types of bitters, syrups and tonics. The crate was personally delivered to my doorstep by Adam, one of the brother duo who own the place.   About those brothers. They're about as helpful, charming and fun to talk to as it gets. If you haven't been to Green Aisle yet, go check out the merch and strike up a conversation while you're at it. It's one of the best things to do on Passyunk Ave.

I've been hitting up Le Pain Quotidien fairly regularly and have grown really fond of the place. The staff are all super friendly and they know the menu well. I love that the nutritional info is listed on every menu item - it makes choosing a healthy meal much easier. The warm grains bowl with goat cheese is decent, but I really love the vegetable quiche which is served with a side salad topped with the most delicious vinaigrette.   For a quick and easy meal, cup of tea or coffee or even a glass of wine (they have a small but solid selection of beer, wine and cocktails), LPQ works.

I was super pumped to try World Wide Burrito last week as I love burritos and anything even remotely resembling Mexican food (traditional or Americanized - give it all to me)! I ordered the Aztec and it was huge and super delicious. The chicken inside was nicely seasoned and tender. I loved the ingredients of the Aztec - they all blended together perfectly. The fact that the burrito never fell apart or got too messy while I was eating it was also awesome. As for the adorable guys who run the truck? Icing on the cake.

Mercato used to be one of my favorite restaurants in Philly, and I was pretty excited to return to celebrate seven years with my love on Saturday night. It had been a while since my last visit, and I remember the space being rather cozy, but I have to admit I was shocked to see that there is now only about two inches of space between tables - no exaggeration. I was (accidentally) elbowed by the person sitting next to me while he was eating. Tables are also small, and when the table next to us ordered the grilled artichoke, their rinds were placed into a bowl which practically rested on our table (and, in fairness, ours to them when we ordered the same thing moments later). Too close for comfort! Even our server remarked that he couldn't gain an ounce working there.   The food was still solid though not as great as previous visits. The artichoke is always a tasty start, and we loved a shared course of squid ink bucatini with spicy lump crab sauce. I wish this had been served on two plates instead of one, plus two side plates - it had the potential to be pretty messy and we missed out on some of the sauce while transferring to the smaller plates. Plus there was that pesky table space problem.   I ordered the strip steak for my main, which I hoped and prayed would be as awesome as the filet with potatoes and roasted brussel sprouts that used to be on the menu. Sadly, it was not. The portion size was huge but I had a hard time finding sections that weren't completely overrun by fat. The grilled broccollini was grilled to the point of charred and the potatoes were kind of boring.   We did end things on a sweet note with a shared affogato which was perfection. Our server was very sweet throughout and helped elevate the experience. I don't want to write off Mercato completely but I definitely will not return on a busy weekend.

Finding myself in the area with some time on my hands, I popped into Paper Source to pick up some cards, and came away super impressed not just by the variety of cards but also the array of small gifts. I could have spent a boatload in that store, but I held back and picked up just what I needed: a couple special occasion cards and a pack of cute thank you cards. Total was just over twenty bucks which is probably the cost of four cards at the drugstore.  I spent a few minutes chatting with one of the employees (possibly the manager?) and learned about some workshops that they host at the store. I'm considering signing up for one in the near future. I'm not super crafty but I would like to spruce up my skills a bit and this seems like a fun way to do it.

My first visit to Lovers & Madmen was quite a while back (March of 2010, actually). I loved the name and the fact that re-runs of The Muppets were playing on the TV. I didn't love the coffee, this I distinctly remember.   Fast forward a couple years and I found myself at Lovers & Madmen again for a meeting. It was super hot outside on the day of my visit, and I walked into the cafe and immediately realized that there was no AC flowing. Worse, the open windows weren't getting any breeze at all, and the huge front window seemed to serve only as a magnifying glass to the sun. With no available tables, I sat on one of the shoddy, sunken couches and felt my body heat rise.   My cup of coffee was from the end of a pot, so there were little dregs of beans floating about my cup. The barista offered to top me off before I left, since I had only received about 3/4 of a pour, but I passed. I'm not sure what type of coffee they brew, but I'm not a fan.

This might be a record for updated reviews, but RAH is my neighborhood bar and it's been a while since my last update. With the recent change in chefs, now seems like a good time.   The food going on at Resurrection right now is fantastic. I used to hate the constant menu changes but I've grown to love them because it keeps things fresh and different. The 5-7 weekday happy hour is great but even better is the 6-10 Sunday happy hour. That's a dangerous way to end the weekend.   Bar snacks are priced around $8-10 each. We ordered three on our recent visit (kale salad, cavatelli and soup) to share. We polished those off and had to check out the menu again, this time opting to share a "big plate" of mushroom risotto. The risotto was delicious but not at all what I would consider a big plate. Multiple dishes add up quickly here, so if all you really want is a snack, you're in for a delicious treat. But if you're hungry, I'd recommend selecting something from the sandwiches section or the fried chicken plate, which is plenty of food.

I'm not going to go jumping for joy over this post office or anything, but its parking lot alone makes me very happy that its our default location. How many other post offices in the city have a parking lot? Maybe they all do, I actually have no idea, but I'm thinking probably not.   The counter closes at noon on Saturdays but during the week it's open until at least 5. There's rarely a line of more than one or two people, and the woman who typically works the counter is efficient, if a little brusque. But hey, as long as I can get my stamps and packages in a timely manner, that's just fine with me.

Beautiful restaurant and the sweetest staff, but the limited and somewhat adventurous menu kept me from feeling the five star love everyone else seems to be feeling about Perla.   My two girlfriends and I had reservations for a Friday night at 8pm, and the restaurant was packed. We were seated at a roomy, comfortable table by the open window to the kitchen. Ice buckets were delivered for our many wines, and champagne flutes and wine glasses were produced. An amuse bouche of a delicious corn soup was served.   We ordered the octopus and mackerel to start. I had a bite of the octopus which was nice, though didn't partake in any of the mackerel as I'm not a fan of this fish. For the mains, we had the prawns, duck breast, and bone marrow fried rice. I transferred a bit of that rice onto my plate before my friend scooped the bone marrow on top (I know, I know - I'm basic with my proteins!). I thought the prawn dish was just okay but I was happily surprised to find that I really enjoyed the duck and especially so when combined with the rice. I didn't partake in dessert but they looked very nice.   I'm curious to see how Perla's menu changes over time and with the seasons. Perhaps the menu when I went just didn't mesh well with my tastes. I'll keep an eye out because I'd love to give this place another shot sometime. If you are into what's on the menu, definitely give Perla a shot because you'll probably love it as much as everyone else!

While I probably wouldn't choose this place as a dinner destination, I did have lunch here at least once every two to three weeks when I worked nearby.  The food is definitely a big step up from your standard take-out places.  It's got more of a P.F. Chang's vibe to it (meaning, stir-fried white meat chicken rather than random chicken pieces that are battered and deep fried to disguise their true identity).  I always alternated between the cashew chicken and the garlic chicken (not recommended if you plan on getting up close and personal with anyone for the rest of the day).    The Thai stuff I've tried is pretty good as well; particularly the chicken satay with peanut sauce and cucumber salad.    Bonus, you have the option of white or brown rice with your meal!

My man went out to run some errands on Friday and came home with a box of empanadas from a Jezabel's pop-up. We received two each of four different kinds and the box came with three side sauces/pickled veggies.   We heated up half the box for lunch on Saturday, but everything was so delicious that we decided to heat the rest and go all in! My favorites were the chicken with olives and beef with raisins, but the empanada with leeks was great, too. I especially loved the chimichurri sauce - I could eat that with everything! Looking forward to more empanadas in my future!

This store is a mecca for wine lovers ranging from sorority Boone's Farm novices to sommeliers alike.  There are rows and rows of grape goodness, all laid out in idiot-proof sections.  The amount of choices might seem overwhelming, but there are tags throughout the store featuring wines of the week and employee favorites.  The friendly and knowledgeable staff members are always willing to help if you aren't sure what you are looking for or just need a great recommendation.    They also have a huge selection of beer and other liquor, as well as every mixer or add-on you could possibly imagine.  To top it off, prices are significantly better than other area stores.

This was my first time trying an Orangetheory class in a different city, and I loved it! The studio was just about to celebrate their one year anniversary and still had that brand new, clean vibe. I registered online and was happy to see that I didn't have to pay any additional fees on top of my current 4x/month membership.   As usual, the class was challenging and I felt very satisfied with my workout. The instructor was motivating and clear with explanations. I'm excited to try other studios when I travel because of this experience!

With so many great reviews, I was sure Custard & Cakes Creamery was going to be awesome. However, their frozen custard just couldn't compare with the kind I grew up with at the Maple Shade custard stand. The vanilla was super light in consistency and didn't have much flavor. However, the hard ice cream I got to try was pretty tasty. If there's a next time, that's definitely what I'll get.   Prices are more than fair and probably the lowest I've seen at any local ice cream shop.

This review is going to be short and sweet because it's all about donuts and basically everyone knows that Beiler's has some of the best around. Personally, I like to keep it simple with my sweets. So I'm partial to the chocolate-frosted, cream-filled donuts or basic glazed/frosted. If you do like different flavors and toppings, there's definitely plenty of those to choose from as well.   The donuts are perfectly sized so you can enjoy one for breakfast without feeling like you blasted through half a day's calories. An excellent treat for these trying times!

My beau and I celebrated our five year anniversary in December at Capital Grille. My mom had just been there for a work dinner, and she raved about her experience so much that we booked our reservation immediately.   While the service was pretty good and the food was up to par with what I expected, I wasn't left with a wow factor. We were seated in a room that looked like it would be used for private functions to the back left past the host station. It was very loud and not particularly romantic. On a previous visit we had been seated in the dining room behind the bar in a booth, which was much nicer.    Our first course came out so quickly it was like the kitchen knew what we were going to order and had it ready. The second course came just as the first was cleared, and the main dishes hit our table as our soup and salad plates were being cleared. The twice baked potato, which we ordered at our server's suggestion, was excellent. The mushrooms were truly boring; not even close to the ones served at another steakhouse in town. The steaks were fine but, again, I've had better. I opted to upgrade my filet with crab and asparagus (Oscar-style) and requested the Bearnaise on the side. I'm glad I did because there was an overwhelmingly sweet taste to the sauce that reminded me of coconut. Very odd.   The cheesecake we ordered for dessert was nice but didn't seem homemade. It was served with some sliced berries that were not in season. I know Capital Grille is a chain but I always held it to a much higher regard despite this fact. After this visit, I'll likely opt for locally owned restaurants for special occasion meals. I do think Capital Grille is still an excellent option for expense account dinners or group events.

This bar is located at the end of my street and I've always eyed it suspiciously.  It has a dive-y look to it, and I never see anyone going in or out.  It wasn't until a friend in the area told me that I would have to check it out as a rite of passage for living so close by that I resolved to stop in for a drink.    A few friends and I decided to swing by after dinner on a Saturday night.  I was shocked to walk through the doors and into a pretty vibrant bar scene.  Sure, a few of the women looked like they were waiting for the Rock of Love Season 4 audition, but the overall vibe was a lot better than anticipated.  A round of four beers cost under $11, and rumor has it that the bar food is pretty decent.

I personally found this Maggiano's to be on the dank side compared to how I remembered the Philadelphia location. Granted, I haven't been to that Maggiano's in years but I always enjoyed the food, service and even the atmosphere. Cherry Hill Maggiano's was not feeling very lively on a Sunday afternoon, but I guess that shouldn't be too surprising considering the summer months and mass exodus to the shore each weekend.   My friend and I kicked things off with a glass of wine and some warm bread with olive oil. We shared the mussels in white sauce, the Maggiano's salad and a special salad with avocado, shrimp and crab. The mussels were pretty good, but I felt both salads were overdressed. Ask for dressing on the side if you're sensitive to that sort of thing. Despite this, both salads were crisp, fresh, and with just the right amount of toppings (although the shrimp and crab salad probably could have used more lettuce).   This isn't a bad option while at the Cherry Hill Mall, but I wouldn't go out of my way, either.

I'm in love with a bar.  There's a waiting area with a shoe shine.   There are candelabra with tall red candles.   There's a Lee in a perfectly fitted cranberry velvet suit.   Original prescriptions for alcohol during the Prohibition Era are framed and mounted to the walls.   Delicious cocktails that taste far more complex than their basic ingredients would indicate are creative and certainly make for fun conversation (new favorite drink: tequila with strawberry).  Bartenders are stylishly dressed, with excellent manners and service to match.  Yep, it's love all right.

My first visit to the SkyGarten was pretty great! I went around 5pm on a Thursday, which is probably the best time to go since they are currently only open Weds-Fri. I'd imagine Wednesdays are insane because of Sips and Fridays are insane because, Friday.   There are two outdoor areas though the one side is clearly the more popular, since it's next to a larger indoor area with a bar and tables. The line for this bar was significantly longer than the smaller bar towards the other outdoor area. So it's worth walking down the hall to scope the situation at the other end of the building. There were beer options and wine as well. I went with the rosé, which I shared with Billy Penn (see pic).   Outside, when you realize just how high up you are, it can be a bit scary. But wow, what a beautiful bird's eye view of Philadelphia! Ledges have been built in around the perimeter, about a half foot from the walls, which actually made me feel a lot more secure, since we weren't right next to the walls. For me, worrying that it would get too crowded was more of a concern, but I was assured that the staff keeps an eye on the amount of people outside.   Definitely looking forward to many more summer beverages at SkyGarten!

This location of OCF is huge and perfect for a meeting or just a hard core work sesh. The employees are friendly (especially the tall guy with the beard who also had to clean up our unfortunate water spill - sorry again and thank you for being so sweet about it!).    I ordered some eggs scrambled with veggies, which came with some potatoes and toast. This is exactly the type of healthy but filling breakfast I like to eat and I was happy to see this option on the menu. The menu here is definitely much larger than some of the smaller OCF locations.   Coffee was great; it's $1 to refill your cup. I can't think of anything I didn't like about my experience so I'm going with five stars for OCF!

SPiN was the perfect choice for a rainy day activity on Sunday! I can honestly say I really didn't have a huge desire for pick-up ping pong, but my opinion has completely changed after my visit. A friend is in one of their leagues and he suggested a group of us head there for some rainy day fun. It was either that or Netflix and chill all day, so I was sold.   SPiN has the underground, industrial look going for it. The decor is really cool and there are ping pong balls everywhere. One of the worst parts of ping pong is having to chase after the ball. Not at SPiN! It was hard at first to resist the urge to chase after every wayward ball but after a while it became part of the fun and held a lot of appeal.   Staff members walk around with ball collectors and constantly refill buckets next to the tables. I did notice quite a few damaged balls making their way back into the buckets, so I would just say they should keep a sharper eye out for those. Otherwise, this is the most fun I've had playing ping pong... well, ever.   There is a menu of bar food which we skipped since we had lunch beforehand, but we did try a couple drinks. My husband had a tequila and grapefruit concoction that literally tasted only of grapefruit, tequila and club soda. There was no sweetness or anything to balance it out and it was quite tart. I love grapefruit juice but even I had a hard time with this drink. I opted for the bloody mary, which comes with candied bacon. As far as bloodies go, it was very good.   Best of all, since our friend is in a league, we were able to play for free. I'm not sure if that was a one time thing or if league members get a certain amount of free visits, but that was a really awesome perk. In any case, I look forward to returning on another rainy afternoon!

Went to dinner here on a double date.  My friend and I are total food snobs and love going out to eat together.  We selected this restaurant because it was part of the Dining out For Life program, in which a good percentage of the check is donated towards AIDS research.  We might not have gone here otherwise, with so many other options in the city.  BUT, thanks to the program, I'm so glad we did!  Everything from the staff, the drinks, the bar, the decor and most importantly, the food was absolutely awesome.  We will definitely be back!

Yesterday I attended PhillyMag's Philly Cooks event at the Crystal Tea Room. I was a guest judge, which was especially fun since I was able to hobnob with some very interesting Philadelphians in the Judges' Lounge. I won't lie, I almost felt like a child who had somehow snuck her way into a seat at the adult's table - and I loved every minute of it!   During the judging, staff members quickly reset our place settings after every single course, and there were many. They did it with a smile and some humor. Afterwards, the event opened to ticket holders, and a flood of the young and hot took over the grand room. Particularly swanky was the Blackfish lounge, which was separate from the rest of the party.   Stations were arranged in such a way that traffic could flow pretty easily through the corridors. There were plenty of trash cans, high top tables, and stations for used glasses around the floor, which is always a good thing. "DJ Chef" Marc Weiss spun bumpin' tunes as he simultaneously cooked up some delicious-looking eats.   This was one fun party that I was glad to be a part of. I look forward to returning for another schmancy soiree!

The best thing about this Starbucks is seeing the line of cars wrapped around the building as you walk inside to no line. The worst part? Waiting because everyone working is handling all the requests from the drive-thru.   Other than that, it's an average Starbucks with the usual offerings.

Ultimo now has sandwiches from American Sardine Bar. You could get the popular turkey sandwich... but you should really go rogue and get the vegan potato salad sandwich, which is far superior. Take it home, pop it in the toaster oven to warm it up, and it's even better.

I am in an absolute food coma after Resurrection's revival of their famous twice-fried chicken.   Sadly, it was a one-time-only special event. I assume I'll go back to my mourning phase in a few weeks' time, when I start craving the deliciousness once again.   It all started when the fried chicken's signature side, The Most Amazing German Potato Salad Ever, was replaced in the warmer months by a watermelon salad. But by December, the plate was off the menu entirely. Despite moving to the 'hood, I couldn't bring myself to walk through RAH's doors to try other menu items. On the one night that I did stop by for a nightcap, I lamented to the bartender my grief over the lost chicken.   Today at noon, 68 orders of the amazing chicken and potato salad were up for first-come, first-served customers. Our party of six was already well-versed in the dish and ready to feast. The two pieces that arrived were enormous, extra crunchy and perfect overall. The potato salad was bangin'.  A friend debated for a long time over his second piece of chicken. He couldn't decide if he should eat it while it was hot or bring it home to savor a bit later on. When we mentioned this to Leigh, one of the owners, she told him he could finish his chicken, order another round, take a few bites, and she'd pack it up for him to-go. We think he's in love.  Resurrection, even if you don't add your chicken back to the everyday menu, please continue to have a Fried Chicken Day every now and again. What do you say? I'll even drop my grudge and start patronizing your establishment more regularly for other menu items. Deal? Deal???

2009 World Series, Game 1  For reasons still unknown to me (and against warnings from friends, family and spiritual advisors), I agreed to watch game one with a born and raised New Yorker, who had relocated to Philly in adulthood.  During discussions of where to watch the game, it was discovered that homeslice had never hung out in the Dirty Jerz, or more accurately, Southern New Jersey.  We agreed it was high time to pop that cherry, and I couldn't think of a more Jerztastic place to do it than Tom Fischer's.    The bar was packed with Phils fans young and old at game time.  Our waitress got right on our drinks and kept them coming through the night.  I had always heard great things about the bar food and it was the perfect night for enjoying some greasy grub.  Everything we were looking at was priced around five or six bucks, so we ordered three things thinking they would be on the small side.  Looking back, I do wish our server would have said something like "FYI, our servings are pretty big here!" or "Save some food for everyone else, fatties!" but we got none of that.  What we did get was a huge basket of pizza fries, a heaping pile of nachos with hunks of breaded chicken, loads of cheese and diced green onions, accompanied by salsa and sour cream, and buffalo chicken tenders.  About those buffalo chicken tenders.  I am thrilled to report to all city dwellers that you can cancel your Philly Car Share reservations because there is no longer a need to trek all the way to Pic-a-lilli's in Shamong, NJ.  Just hop on PATCO and jump off in Collingswood.  Walk east on Atlantic until you are smack dab in front of Tom Fischer's.  No joke, I would not know the difference from TF's buffalo chicken tenders and the ones they serve at the Pic.  The sauce was tangy but not too hot and with a touch of sweetness.  I would imagine the wings are comparable but I'll have to check them out sometime in the future.  They also do takeout- happy football Sunday to me!  Our experience was pretty awesome (for me, anyway - the New Yorker was a little butthurt) through the game.  The service was good, food was great, game was awesome and the people-watching was hysterical.  Please refer to my "local photo" to see what I mean.  After the game, however, things took a turn for the dicey.  Without getting into details, let's just say that sometimes small towns bring out small minded individuals.  A slob on the opposite end of the bar made a very loud, obnoxious comment that would have been inappropriate in any setting.  It was an unfortunate way to end what had been a really fun night, otherwise.  I know it's not the bar's responsibility to censor clientele, but it does speak for the types of clientele they attract.

I enjoy this coffee shop for a change of scenery from the usual haunts in my own neighborhood. There are plenty of tables and even some outdoor tables, tons of caffeinated options to choose from, wifi, and an extensive list of basic but solid breakfast and lunch items.   The coffee comes with free refills which is particularly awesome on a Monday morning.

My family has this weird tradition.  Every year on the day after Thanksgiving, we go to Bertucci's for lunch.  Forget the 50 lbs. of leftovers in the fridge, we want pizza!  So off we went, this time to the Mt. Laurel location.    Our server brought out piping hot rolls, which were really good, and plenty of oil for dipping.  The salad bowl had only enough salad for about two people, but we asked for another and rationed it out.    Our pizzas, the silano and shrimp bella napoli, came out soon after.  I didn't have any of the silano because I remembered the chicken being questionable from previous visits, but the shrimp bella napoli was really good.  Spicy red sauce with mozzarella and tons of shrimp on top made for a really good pizza.  Two carafes of sangiovese topped off the lunch.    I don't think I'd ever give Bertucci's five stars, but I always enjoy my visits.  I know what I like and what to stay away from, so I'm never disappointed.

My colleague and I popped into Bluestone for a hot beverage and to get some work done. On a Monday morning, I was surprised to see that the place was fairly bustling. The space is bright and airy - definitely a place I'd consider to be conducive to productivity.   The servers were very nice and I enjoyed my hot tea, which was served loose leaf with a little strainer. The brunch menu, which is served every day from 8-4, looked really delicious. Definitely looking forward to future visits and brunch almost any time of day!

YUM!  This spot has the best pizza by far in the Collingswood/Westmont/Haddonfield area.  I'm a big fan of their Sicilian style pizza~ and even my parents agree with me on this (they are very picky when it comes to good pizza)!   I give Finizio's 4 stars and not 5 because I'm not crazy about some of the other stuff on their menu, particularly anything with chicken.  They use the stuff that tastes like it's been frozen for 5 years and came out of a high school cafeteria... yuck.  The pizza will rock your world though, trust me!

A year and a half later, I finally returned to Fond for a date night. Our reservation for 6:30 was fortunate; it was early enough that we had the entire restaurant to ourselves until the very end of our meal. That was fun!   We started off with some delicious olive bread and salted butter. I could eat an entire loaf, it's so fantastic. The amuse bouche was a watermelon and chili gazpacho - perfect for a hot summer night. Also seasonally spot on was the menu. My tuna tartare was bursting with the flavors of bright avocado and lemongrass. The escargot's earthy nature was pronounced in a broth of fennel, heart of palm and mint.   There were several entrees I waffled between but I ultimately went with the special: pan-seared monkfish served with garlic scape risotto and lamb au jus. Wow, where to begin? The fish was cooked perfectly and had just a hint of salty crunch around the edges. The risotto was out of of this world. If there's anything I've learned from my meals at Fond, it is to order anything that features risotto. Lee knocks it right out of the park. The au jus added a slightly meaty tone to the dish, which elevated the flavors even higher.   Across the table, a tender steak served with local tomatoes and onion jam was another solid choice. Some toasted breadcrumbs kicked in just the right amount of crunch.   For dessert, brown butter cheesecake for my dining partner and malted chocolate ice cream with chocolate crumbles and peanut brittle for me. Both were absolutely delicious, the flavors matching their descriptions. Desserts at Fond are perfectly sized considering their richness. Share one and enjoy a few bites of heaven or get your own and hit the gym the next day.  There's really nothing I can think of that I would want to change about my meal. Five stars for our wonderful night.

Hyatt Place Nashville Downtown was hands-down the best place to stay for my bachelorette party weekend. Though I originally wanted to book at a nearby, higher end hotel, the room rates were outrageous. I remembered the Hyatt Place from a previous Nashville visit and knew: the location is ideal, it's a relatively new property, and the rates were in line with what we were looking to spend.    The rooms are large and perfect for sharing - the couch has a fold out single bed. The bathrooms are large and there is plenty of counter space. I also enjoyed the full length mirror in the room, just outside of the bathroom, which is located near an outlet. Even with three girls in my room, we had no problems getting ready at the same time. Like other reviewers, I did not care for the frosted glass sliding door on the bathroom. Privacy is not overrated!   A hot breakfast with tons of options is served every morning in the lobby. I was stunned to receive a plate of breakfast sandwiches, scrambled eggs and biscuits and gravy from my friends who were up early enough to take advantage of this perk. The lobby also features a bar and a small menu that is perfect for late night snacks.   All of the staff we encountered were friendly and helpful, but we were disappointed that our room was not cleaned after night one. We had placed the do not disturb sign on our door, which was there until around noon. When we left the room we noticed a bag of fresh towels, but we really wanted our room serviced since we had a bunch of plates and drinks scattered around. I called to request a housekeeping visit and was assured we would receive one. Two hours later when my sister went back to the room to pick something up, she called down with same request. Unfortunately, our room was never cleaned so by the time we left it was a bit of a mess.   That said, I can't dock any stars from Hyatt Place, and here's why: after being home for three days, I went to switch my purses around and realized with a pit in my stomach that the last time I had my other bag I was in my hotel room. That's when I also realized I had left another bag (yes, I brought three handbags on a weekend vacation), plus a pair of shorts and a tank top. On the day of our check-out, I was running late for a brunch reservation and was scrambling to get everything together - I must have forgotten to check the closet!   I called the hotel, thinking there would be no way that my stuff was still around. I was STUNNED when the manager confirmed that they had everything! I gave him my credit card number so that the hotel could ship everything back. The next day, I received a voicemail from the head of housekeeping confirming the shipment. Today, my items arrived, along with two additional shirts my future sister-in-law also left in the room. I've left pricey items in hotel rooms before and it has always been a lost cause (RIP, Joe's Jeans). I cannot believe my stuff has been returned and I am so very grateful to the housekeeping staff.   Next time I take a trip to Nashville, I know exactly where I want to stay!

One time, my adorable grandparents had us over to celebrate a birthday.  My grandfather excitedly announced that he had picked up a cake from ACME with buttercream frosting.  Mmm, buttercream frosting!  We sang, cut the cake and doled out the slices, but I eyed my piece suspiciously.  The frosting looked very much like that glorified Cool Whip ACME so loves to use in their bakery.    We all dug in but the confused reaction was instantaneous.  The frosting WAS the glorified Cool Whip kind! That's when someone picked up the box and read the made-up word, "bettercream."  My grandfather and his eyesight were had by ACME!    Flying Monkey's cupcakes are lovely to look at.  Unfortunately, they are too dry, and the frosting tastes like bettercream.

Yay! There's a new bagel place in town!   Boo. It's way overpriced.   When I arrived at Spread at 11am on Tuesday, the second day of its existence, there was a line of people out the door. As I got closer to the counter, I heard someone say that they were out of everything bagels. I saw that they offered whole wheat everything, and by the time it was my turn, I snagged the very last one.   I requested low fat seasonal veggie cream cheese, which I knew was available because the board read "LF." Au contraire! The LF stood for locally farmed. There were no lowfat options available, but I still went for the seasonal veggie spread, and I added sliced tomatoes. My bagel, a cup of coffee, and a bottle of water came to the grand total of $10.80. That's more than I'm willing to spend on a take-out lunch.   The bagel was tasty, and a little on the sweet side as I expected. I really liked the cream cheese, and I could taste the fresh red onions and radishes that were used to make it. The coffee was great, the seating area was very cute. Part of my money clearly went towards having some ambiance with my bagel. Oh yeah, and the air smelled like bacon, courtesy of the wood fire grill. That's always going into the pros column.   Later that day, while shopping at Wegman's, I picked up four freshly baked bagels for .70¢ each, and a tub of homemade (lowfat!) veggie cream cheese for $3.51. I'll be breakfasting in the comfort of my own home for the rest of the week.  If you've got the dough to drop on tasty but overpriced bagels all the time, that's awesome. For moi, they'll have to be a once in a while treat.

I was at a meeting nearby and needed an afternoon pick-me-up. I spotted the sign on the corner pointing to Gryphon Cafe so I ran across the street to check it out. The space is open and industrial-looking - a fun place for a meeting or to get some work done.   I had the cold brew and have to say I wasn't crazy about it. It could just be that it was my third coffee of the day so my body was trying to tell me something. It wouldn't stop me from going again to try another beverage. The baked goods looked amazing and the barista said they stock them from Machine Shop. The everything seasoning-topped bagels and breads looked delish.   There was also a big bowl of fresh fruit by the counter so I picked up a couple pieces for home. Solid coffee shop and I'd love to get back for another visit sometime.

I just walked out of lunch at Vicia and it was so great I had to jump on Yelp to talk about it. The restaurant is very attractive, with plenty of tables inside as well as on a covered patio (with space heaters). There is a smartly curated lunch menu which currently features a sandwich, a couple salads, a tartine and soup. You can pick two for $12 or three for $15. Such a great deal!   I opted for the ham sandwich and kale salad, plus a chamomile ginger spritz. Both of my selections were excellent! My husband had the sandwich and sweet potato soup, which was delicious as well.   My only regret is not having more time while we're in town to try dinner. Vicia is a gem!

Every single Friday, when the hands on the clock move in unison to the number 12, the door to my office building swings open, and out I run like a bat out of hell.  I'm not trying to escape, no.  I'm trying to scramble into my car and peel wheels, in the interest of ticking off as many errands as humanly possible during that precious hour of free time.  Often, it is on my return to the office when I notice my hunger pangs and remember that I haven't yet eaten.  A quick lunch to-go is always necessary, and lately I've found that pizza has been calling.  Last week, I happened to be near one of my old haunts, Finizio's.  Some time had gone by since my last visit, and I wasn't sure if the pizza would be as good as I remembered it to be.    I went with two slices, one plain and one tomato, plus a fountain soda.  The total came to six dollars and change, which seemed on the high side for two smallish slices.  Back at my desk, I decided the size/cost/taste ratio was more than acceptable.  The tomato slice was zippy and loaded with flavor, but the cheese slice was just as good, with the right amount of sauce and a liberal sprinkling of oregano.    I'm glad Finizio's is still keeping it real even when I disappear for a while.  I'll be returning again soon on another frantic Friday.

This Starbucks appeared to be clean and well-stocked, though I admittedly wasn't there for very long. This, my friends, is a good thing. These people had me in and out with my Americano in no time at all, and I was very grateful for it. My coffee was tasty and kept me revved until lunchtime.

Honeygrow is a local business that has really grown on me over the years. This particular location is one of the few healthy, fast-casual restaurants in the KOP Town Center, and I was grateful to spot it while in the area recently.   I ordered my usual salad, customized the way I like it. While I waited I saw several people swing in to pick up to-go orders. My salad was ready fairly quickly and I brought it over to the counter to grab some utensils. I noticed that the salt and pepper shakers were empty, which was weird since the restaurant was also empty at the time. One of the workers noticed me shaking away at an empty pepper shaker and he graciously offered to get more for me.   My salad was delicious, per usual. They have the best white balsamic vinaigrette! My only complaint is that I hate the bowls they use! I like to cut my salads and I can't do this in their bowls without toppling the whole thing. A minor gripe but it's something I notice every single time! Other than that, keep doing you, Honeygrow. I love having a healthy, local option!

I've been feeling the pressure to go big or go home for my 500th review (review updates = stalling for time), but my experience at Zento tonight was just so refreshing that I'm ready to go all the way.  The experience started with a call for reservations this afternoon. At the last minute on a Friday I wasn't expecting a miracle, but low and behold, I got my table for two at the desired time slot. Plus a very friendly interaction with the gentleman who answered the phone and who also reminded me that the restaurant is a BYO. The seed of a good first impression was planted.   We arrived to a small, mostly empty restaurant, save for one loud, cackling (drunk?) foursome, who thankfully left a few minutes later. The rest of the tables were eventually filled with respectful diners.   Our server was sweet and attentive despite the fact that she had lost her voice, and she stopped by our table at all the right times during the meal. We started with edamame, which was the only misstep. The soybeans were boring in comparison to our neighbors' rock shrimp tempura.   The edamame was forgotten once our sushi rolls arrived. Crunchy spicy tuna, "real" California and green (avocado and cucumber) rolls for me, a fatty tuna roll and a "square sushi" specialty roll for my boyfriend. Despite my hesitations, I tried a bite of the fatty tuna and it was mind-blowingly fantastic. One of the most pure-tasting pieces of raw fish I've ever tried. My rolls were equally pleasing. The thing I liked most about Zento's preparation is that they didn't go overboard with the extras. The fish still tasted like fish, just with minor enhancements from the supporting cast of ingredients in each roll.     This may not be the most glittery sushi joint in town, but the quality of the fish and the welcoming staff were more than enough to win me over. I look forward to returning.

Last night was my third time dining here, and probably my favorite.  It happens to be Buddakan's tenth anniversary and in conjunction with that, proceeds from each check are being donated to Project H.O.M.E. all week.  Reason enough to get out for the night!  My friend and I started with the wasabi tuna pizza, which was all right but probably not something either of us would order on a return trip... and that's okay, because what I was really after was a good old piece of meat.  Literally.  The char grilled aged beef was phenomenal.  The plate was huge and came with a watercress salad with a big side of szechuan fries on top.  The beef itself was tender on the inside but slightly crispy around the edges and seasoned perfectly.  I tend to stick to seafood when I'm out but I had tried this dish on another occasion and remembered how fantastic it was.  A side of wasabi mash was the second best decision made while ordering.  To die.    This was one of those meals that I simply could not stop eating, it was that good.  My iron count should be rocking for at least a month.    A shared creme brulee was the perfect finish to an amazing dinner.

This is my least favorite PJ's location.  Although it is the largest, and definitely the most popular, something about the vibe is just off for me.  Saturday nights always have a cover charge.  It's only $5, and I suppose this pays for the band, but I'd rather NOT see most of the bands they feature anyway.  Fortunately, the beer specials are consistent through all the PJ's locations, and $2.75 Blue Moon makes for a cheap night out.      An overcrowding of tables and chairs makes getting from one area to another quite challenging.  The bathrooms aren't the cleanest, despite an attendant, and the lines start to get long later in the night.   In closing, I'm a little cranky that I wasted a perfectly good Saturday night here.

Welcome to Philly, Halal Guys! I only sampled the eats from this super popular, NYC born-and-bred business for the first time at the October Yelper Party. I knew then that I'd be seeking them out once their Chinatown location opened, so imagine my excitement when they popped up on one of my delivery apps tonight!   I ordered the half chicken half gyro platter which came with lettuce, tomatoes, rice and pita, plus some of the hot and white sauce packets on the side. I also ordered a side of hummus for just a couple dollars more.   The food arrived and it was a gigantic portion and everything tasted delicious. I made the mistake of pouring the red sauce all over my food before trying it. Big mistake! That sauce is super hot and I ended up having to pull some of the sauce-covered pieces out of the bowl! Next time, I'll use this sauce sparingly and keep it to the side. My fault, for sure. The hummus was also delicious and there was an extra warm pita included as well. This will definitely become one of my go-to delivery spots.

After reading some awesome reviews and hearing so many great things after Yelp's Backstage Pass Party, I knew I had to cross town and check out Rybread. With our day off today, it was the perfect opportunity for me and the boy to check the place out for lunch.   The chalkboard of choices was extensive. Everything sounded so great but I was pretty committed to the Charlotte. Sadly, I made the unwise decision to switch to multigrain bread. This was sad because the bread got a little soggy with the pickles, honey mustard and tomatoes. My own fault, of course. Next time, I'll stick with the recommended bread option. The ingredients were all fresh and delicious; the price was right. Their counter staff was also very friendly.  The strawberry iced tea was delightful and I also got to take a coffee home after redeeming my check-in offer. I'll be returning soon to check another sammie off the list!

I've ordered from Minar Palace twice in the past month or so (I know, guys, I order A LOT of delivery). I'm definitely a fan and this is probably going to be my go-to when ordering Indian from now on. It's not super cheap but not overly expensive and the food has been consistently solid.   I think Minar Palace makes my favorite chicken tikka masala in the city, and that's saying something. I love that there are pieces of peppers and onions in the sauce. The chicken breaks apart when you put your fork through. Love. I really dig that they have papadum as well - it's a gluten-free cracker-type thing with spices. It's a fun add-on that won't make you feel entirely left out as your husband houses all the delicious garlic naan.   I do wish there was an option to add on some of the vegetable entrees as smaller sides. I always like to have a veggie with my meals, so a chicken entree and rice doesn't cut it. I've been adding vegetarian entrees to my order which ends up getting pricey, and is always far too much food; especially considering the extra container of rice, which is totally unneeded in my case.   Minar, please add some veggie side options so we can skip off into the sunset together!

My friend and I chose William Street Common as our brunch destination on Saturday. We arrived just after 1 and there was plenty of seating available. Our server dropped off hot coffee and donuts just after we sat down. The table had everything we needed already - napkins, extra plates, coffee mugs, silverware, condiments, etc. We ordered our first round of three breakfast cocktails (included in the $22 weekend brunch).   The coffee was hot and delicious, the donuts... were not. I was super hungry, which is the only reason I dug in for more than one. If you're going to serve donuts, they should be fresh and tasty. The Bloody Mary was okay - nothing special but it did the trick.   My friend ordered the eggs benny with short rib while I went for the biscuits and gravy with poached eggs. A big side of breakfast potatoes to share was also dropped off, and those were probably my favorite part of the meal. The eggs on my plate were way undercooked - most of the egg white was still extremely runny. I also wasn't crazy about the sausage in the gravy, which was very chewy and not really in a way I found enjoyable.   I'd go back for drinks with friends and possibly some snacks, but I probably won't be heading back for brunch.

The River Rink this year compared with last year is like night and day. While I haven't yet made it to Winterfest (currently open only on weekends through March), the awesome trees, lights and decorations everywhere, plus the seating areas and fire pits, really elevated a night of skating. Somehow, the view of the river was even more beautiful with the twinkling lights around the rink.   Tonight, we took my thirteen year old brother ice skating for his very first time. It was a fun activity for everyone, despite the varying age differences in our group. We clearly weren't alone in this thought process; the rink was pretty packed with families, couples and teenagers for the 7-8:30pm skate session and the ice got pretty snowy just forty-five minutes in.   Parking was a whopping twelve dollars, and since we came from various start points and had two cars to four people, that was a bummer. Skating costs only three dollars but skate rental is ten. Yowch. Had I known that flashing my Blue Cross insurance card would get our skating comped, I wouldn't have left it securely at home! Of course, moments after paying I noticed all the lockers (one dollar per use). Gah! So my suggestions to save a few bucks would be to carpool, and bring your own skates if possible. Don't forget that BXBS insurance card or student ID, if you've got one!

I was at The Prince Theater twice this week for Philadelphia Film Festival movies. Prior to this week, I had never set foot in the theater, so it was nice checking out something new (to me) in the city.   The multi-use theater is huge and offers stadium seating. Unless you were stuck in one of the very front rows for a movie, I don't think there is a bad seat in the house. Seating is definitely old school - don't expect luxurious accommodations - but it's fine for a movie or show.   My husband had popcorn on both visits and the bites I tried were good. He mentioned that they also sell wine, which is always a plus. I hope I have the opportunity to return to The Prince for future events!

Two stars because they have the drugs.  Three missing stars because once I started getting "the pill," I also started getting dirty looks from the pre-historic staff every time I picked them up.  Walgreens and I have been going steady ever since!

Did I REALLY just house an 830 calorie burrito?   According to Baja Fresh's website, yes I did.  Fuuuuuuuuuuuucccccckkkkkkkkk.  Not that I thought a pork burrito that weighed about the same as a newborn baby was going to be healthy, but the only toppings were pico and guac, so I thought I was still in reasonably safe territory.  Isn't pork called "the other white meat" because it's supposed to be good for you?  I'm clearly in some sort of holiday denial.    On the plus side, the burrito was pretty tasty so I'm bumping to two stars.  However, I'm not sure it was worth all the extra cardio it will take to burn that puppy off.  I should have re-read my first review before making such a poor hunger-based decision.

Once again, my BYO girls and I were out to dinner. This time, we chose Mercato at the recommendation of a friend who had been there twice in one month and loved it. Based on her raves, plus all the positive reviews on yelp, I knew we were destined for a solid dining experience.   First, we were presented with some really dense bread and a garlicky spread. Yummm. I've probably made it pretty clear by now that I am bread's number one fan, and this little plate-o-carbs did not disappoint!   We shared the roasted portabella and arugula puff pastry, the market salad and the roasted artichoke. I wasn't particularly excited about either of the first two selections, but I was blown away by both of them. The flavors were incredible. The market salad had a fantastic dressing and candied pecans, plus slivers of pear and a parmesan-type cheese that gave it a sweet-but-bitey contrast. Hands down, this is absolutely what I would recommend if I could only pick one starter from the three we tried. The puff pastry came with a little salad that had a slightly salty vibe, which went really well with everything in the pastry.   Now, we ordered the grilled artichoke based on the things I had read on yelp. It became clear when it was dropped at our table, that no one had the slightest idea what to do with the thing. I grabbed a leaf, dipped it in the creamy aioli (which was amazing, by the way), and popped it in my mouth. It was really tasty... until I realized something wasn't breaking down and had taken on the texture of tree bark. So, for any artichoke novices out there reading this, let me save you from looking like a cave person and fill you in on a little secret: you don't eat the whole leaf! Simply dip, and then use your teeth to tear the small amount of flesh from the piece. You're welcome.   For dinner, one friend had the roasted chicken, another had the short rib ragu over gnocchi and I had the fish special which was tilapia in a basil lemon butter sauce with spinach and a pan seared polenta cake. Wow. Each dish was phenomenal. Portions were on the large side, but we put a hurtin' on every one of them. I'm not sure I can pick one that I liked most, because they were all equally delicious in their own way.   Always saving a corner in our stomachs for dessert, we had the tiramisu and the warm pecan caramel tart. Now, the tiramisu was good, but it didn't stand a chance next to the tart. Let me put it like this: that thing gave great sex a run for its money.   Mercato exceeded our expectations and we were all in agreement that it has become our favorite BYO to-date. My girlfriends downright demanded that I give 5 stars in my review (one also wanted me to give a special shout out to the cute bathroom), and I'm happy to oblige.  From what I hear, the weekends get a little crazy and the tables are very close together.  Check it out during the week to avoid the madness and enjoy your experience to the fullest.

I went to Baja Fresh for the first time today at lunch, armed with a printout of the nutritional info as I'm preparing for the upcoming bikini season.  My plan was to order the Baja Ensalada and Original Baja Taco, which are BY FAR the only selections that are a reasonably healthy option (check the website if you don't believe me).  After watching the BF employees prepare the food, which a blind five year old could have done faster, I was on my way back to work with my to-go bag.  "I can't wait for my chicken taco!" I thought.  I almost, ALMOST, tore it open on the car ride back (have you ever encountered a hungry girl on a diet at lunchtime?  No?  Well then get the eff out of my way or you're gonna get hurt.).    FINALLY I was seated at my desk, diet coke open, salsas at the ready.  I opened the taco wrapper and saw... two (two???) tortillas with one, maybe two, chicken chunks and roughly half an onion scattered about.  Ohhhhkay.  "That shit cost me $2.25?" I thought as I tossed the onion taco with chicken flavoring in the garbage.    Salad time.  To be honest, the salad didn't look half bad, but the cotija cheese that was promised in the ingredients list was nowhere to be found, and though some of the chicken was okay, a lot of it had that fatty fake-chicken consistency that so many fast food chains try to pass off as "chicken breast."  It was pretty disappointing, considering how much I've heard people rave about this place.  I guess the food that makes this restaurant the "Top Mexican Chain in America for 2007" lies within the menu items that are covered in cheese and deep-fried, aka, every other item on the menu.  Baja "Fresh" my ass!

My girl Michelle and I had brunch here during our recent trip to Nashville (yep, Michelle squared - double trouble!). The bloody marys were great. We ordered a few oysters as well and our server did a great job describing them - they were on point. The only thing that bugged me is they arrived just after our mains. I hate when you try to course things out but then everything arrives at the same time!   My friend had "The Highway" - fried chicken on waffles. It looked great but she said the crispy breading kept coming off of the chicken. I pulled some random maneuver out of left field and played things safe with the "Southern Fried Egg Sandwich." It was good but not super memorable.   The restaurant is really pretty and definitely a classy brunch locale. There was live music (which I quickly learned is par for the course in Nashville) so that was a plus, too. All in all, The Southern Steak & Oyster is a solid spot!

Melissa P and I decided to check out Cafe Chismosa for a casual lunch/brunch on Saturday afternoon. With an outdoor table available in the sun, we were sold right away. The inside of the cafe is also super cute - bright and airy.   The menu is focused on Latin-inspired lunch and brunch items. I opted to keep my choices on the healthy side and was greatly rewarded with fresh, clean, flavorful food. To start, we shared the shrimp ceviche which was absolutely gorgeous and had loads of bright, tasty ingredients.   Next, I tried a smoked scallop salad with avocado and quinoa. Wow. I haven't stopped thinking about this salad since I had it, and I can't wait to go back and get it again ASAP. I'd never had smoked scallops before but they were perfect on this salad and the perfect match for creamy avocado.   I will happily go out of my way to patronize this wonderful business again.

Love my Photobot 3000 peeps! I've hired them for several large-scale events and they have always been great to work with - quick to respond to emails leading up and going above and beyond expectations at the events.   One of the things I like most about Photobot in particular is that they have the ability to customize the background screen for the photos. They have incorporated artwork that I used to promote my events and the end result was unique and festive.   Theresa and Scott are lovely to work with and I'd recommend them for any special event!

A friend and I swung by BSBH for a drink last week. We arrived during happy hour and requested outside seating from the friendly host. Draft beers were discounted for the happy hour special so we each ordered a brew. Our server asked if we'd like water and though we said yes, we never actually received it. No big as we were only there for one drink.   We also ordered the fried pickles which were okay, but didn't have much flavor. They tasted more like fried cucumbers than fried pickles; the briny taste of a pickle was not really detectable.   Based on this experience I'm going with three stars but I definitely want to get back at some point to experience more.

Before they blew up and became Cafe Madison next door, the space that is now Towne Tavern was the Madison Pub. I used to go with a friend every once in a while for a chocolate martini or three and some catch-up. At the time, they had several different chocolate martinis on their menu and some came with a Hershey kiss at the bottom which sealed the deal for me.   My brother had a gift card for the family of restaurants so we decided to check out Towne Tavern for drinks on Saturday night. The bar looked exactly the same but I didn't see any chocolate martinis on the current menu. I'm wondering if they put that menu at the newer, fancier Cafe Madison.    Only a couple tables were open when we waked in so we grabbed a booth and checked out the menu. The beer selection was really weak, though they did have Flying Fish HopFish on tap. My brother's girlfriend had a couple different flavored martinis that she said were okay but not super strong.   The crowd was mixed and by 10pm or so, we were one of the only tables left, outside of the people sitting at the bar. They had a guy singing and playing guitar who was decent, but the bar is so small that it was also a little awkward.   Our server, Holly, was a peach.* She kept the drinks flowing and stopped by at the right times to make sure were were all set.   Honestly, if my parents want to catch a drink at the Towne Tavern sometime, I'm all in. But the next time my brother and I go out for a drink we'll probably pick somewhere with a younger scene.     *I'm pretty sure I used to babysit her back in the day but I felt too weird (i.e., too old!) to say something!

I must be missing something, because my first experience at Royal Izakaya was just okay. We went for dinner with friends recently and I wasn't blown away by anything I tried.   This is one of those restaurants where items come out of the kitchen as they are prepared. Great if everyone is on board with sharing, not so great when everyone has an idea of what they want to eat and it's all different. I waited a while before any of the dishes I ordered made it to the table.   I had some gyoza, wings, fried scallops (a special), tuna avocado roll and spicy tuna roll. Everything was okay but I wasn't overly impressed. In fact, I downright disliked the spicy tuna roll, which tasted really fishy to me - not the clean, fresh way tuna usually tastes.   I really liked the vibe of the bar area and am definitely up for another visit to see if maybe I was there on an off night for the kitchen.

Whoa, Fountain Porter, I owed you this review update! Since that very first experience six years ago, we've kept the tradition alive and hit Fountain Porter every year after purchasing our Christmas tree. This year was no exception, even if we had to get our burgers to-go.   This spot is easily one of Philly's best deals. Six bucks gets you a perfect cheeseburger. It's not fancy, but it is delicious. And three dollars for a hefty order of crispy fries? Sign. Me. Up. Don't forget to throw in a side of pickles, because Fountain Porter's are addictive and you'll want more than the two that already come with your burger.  Dinner for two, plus a nice tip, came to under thirty bucks. Can't beat it. Looking forward to our next pick-up!

Five stars for the chefs at The Olde Bar and our server, Matt, who last night bent over backwards to accommodate my many dietary restrictions on the Whole30 plan.   After a week of cooking nearly every meal at home from scratch, a feat I normally accomplish once or maybe twice a week if I'm really feeling inspired, I desperately needed to get out and escape both the cooking and clean-up. Eating out on this plan is not an easy feat, and so I chose The Olde Bar based on the raw seafood selections and steak options.   My husband and I went to dinner super early on a snowy night, and were seated in a nearly empty dining room, save for a large party of adults, plus an extremely unruly child. We were seated right next to this group when nearly all the other tables remained open for the duration of our stay. I definitely should have asked to be moved and I still don't know why I didn't. (Hosts: please don't seat couples next to groups with loud children, if possible!)  Moving on. I had several questions about menu items which Matt graciously relayed to the chefs. In the end, I ordered the jumbo lump crab cocktail to start, which was absolutely delicious, plus the steak oscar made without butter or hollandaise, with sides of grilled asparagus and roasted fingerling potatoes. My steak was cooked perfectly, with a generous side of crab, and the side of artichoke jus was heavenly. I had enough potatoes left over to bring home for my Sunday breakfast (back at it in the kitchen!).    This was my first time ever in The Olde Bar and former Bookbinders and I really loved the old school vibes and the Garces Group's dedication to preserving some of that nostalgia. I'm definitely looking forward to returning once I'm back on the wagon - I'd love to share some drinks in one of the cozy leather banquettes or seated at the bar.

Yum.  This diner is very close to where I live and was recommended to me ages ago by a friend in my town.  I went there for the first time this past weekend and will definitely be making return appearances.  Service was friendly and quick, which is exactly what one would expect at a good diner.  I was pretty particular about my egg white omelet and was so happy when it came out spot-on with my requests.  It was awesome.  The standard diner cake display had me practically drooling when I walked by... I'll definitely be back to hit that up one night when my self control is waning and I feel like being a fat kid.

Me 'N" Mo provided me and a friend with a very pleasant lunch experience last week. The menu is simple. It's a whole lotta meatballs served a whole lotta ways. Get them with pasta, on bread, or in a Sarcone's roll. Choose your type (beef, pork, veggie, and a couple other options), your sauce (again, several choices) and the way you want them served.   I opted to keep things traditional and went with the beef meatballs with marinara sauce on a roll with provolone cheese. Extra sauce on the side 'cause I like to get saucy. My sandwich was absolutely delicious and was served with a nice arugula salad alongside. Looking forward to my next visit!

It would have been helpful to know that white tuna (aka, butterfish) is known for causing digestion issues... especially since I ordered the white tiger roll, loaded with white tuna, about an hour before I had to pedal my company's wares for three hours at an exhibit hall cocktail party nearby.    That information would have been useful.  Never again!  Last week's dinner/gastrointestinal lesson was my second time trying Raw.  My first visit was at least two years ago, during the dreaded Restaurant Week.  On that occasion, my friend and I had to send cocktails back twice and put up with a know-it-all server who insisted that eel could not be removed from (the top of) a specialty roll because "it would compromise the flavors of the roll." Although we did enjoy most of the dishes we ended up ordering that night, the experience as a whole fell flat and I did not return...  Until last week.  I was in the area and had time to kill, so I pulled out my iPhone and utilized my yelp app to find a nearby sushi restaurant.  Raw was very close, and since it had been so long since my last visit, I decided to give it another try.  My server was great, and repeated the specials several times at my request because I couldn't decide.  I usually stick with regular tuna or even yellowtail, but something on this evening told me to go balls to the wall and try something different.  Enter the aforementioned white tiger roll.  In fairness, I enjoyed the roll, although I still preferred the taste of regular tuna to the fattier consistency of white tuna.    The roll, a bowl of miso soup and a cosmo ended up costing a quick forty bucks, including tip.  I wish I could point my finger and blame it on the ambiance, or the location or something... but I can not.  I'm just not all that impressed and I think there is better sushi to be had, in swankier digs, around the city at the same price.

The boyfriend and I had some errands to run on Delaware Ave, so we wanted a low-key place with happy hour specials in that general area for dinner. I suggested Catahoula, despite my reservations from my last visit back in December. Since Art had never been he wanted to try it, and off we went.   As we approached the restaurant, we took in the large patio area, with plenty of available tables and lights strung overhead. It was an easy decision to sit outside for dinner, and a strong breeze cut through the warmth of the setting sun.   We started with a couple Abita Restoration Pale Ales, just $3.50 during happy hour, and the pickled veggies and hushpuppies, also part of the happy hour special. The beers were cold and delicious; the hushpuppies were crunchy, perfectly salty and a little spicy.   When my shrimp etouffee arrived, I knew I had ordered correctly. The rice was perfect, there was plenty of shrimp and the tomato-based sauce was delicious. There was so much, I brought half home for lunch (which I will be enjoying shortly). Art had two small plates: jambalaya, which was deliciously smoky and full of flavor, and New Orleans BBQ style shrimp, which were coated in a rich barbecue sauce and served along some of the best cornbread I've ever had.   There was only one server working from what I could tell, and things slowed down towards the end of our meal when it got more crowded, but we didn't mind at all. I definitely plan to return again to enjoy that patio and the delicious food before the summer warmth slips away.

First things first: I love the feel and vibe of this chill neighborhood bar. I dig the constantly rotating beer list, and the bartenders have always been great and fun to chat with.   However, I'm regretfully pulling stars after my recent dining experiences at Resurrection. Last time, a cheese plate was awesome but a risotto-style dish was a bit monotonous. Jalapeño-accented falafel bites were cute and tasty, but overpriced at eight bucks for five or so small pieces.   Today I was excited to check out brunch. A chorizo and manchego omelet with a side of greens caught my eye right away. My request for egg whites was unfortunately denied. After looking over the menu some more, I decided to deal with the extra calories from whole eggs and I went with the omelet. At first glance, it was pretty and nicely sized. But once my fork cut through, the plate was swimming in butter. I had a few bites of egg and picked out the chorizo slices, but turned my focus to the side of greens and the heirloom tomato salad we ordered on the side.   I want to love Resurrection and I want it to be my neighborhood bar of choice, but I never leave feeling truly satisfied... Unless it's fried chicken day.

Last week, I got takeout from Loco Pez for the first time since they opened in my neighborhood. I had the shrimp burrito and my husband got the vegan chorizo burrito. We also ordered chips and salsa.   When we arrived, everything was packaged and sitting on a table by the front door, so it was an easy, virtually contactless transaction. The burritos were delicious and I really loved the fresh pico de gallo, for which they provided a generous amount of chips. Also, they included three different types of salsas which was awesome. I'd happily order from Loco Pez again!

Once you get past the fact that you are going to pay ridiculously high prices for groceries, you will be able to enjoy your Whole Foods experience a lot more. Truth is, while WF may not carry the same brands you see in other big box groceries, they do carry many items you can never find in the other stores.   I found this out first hand during the past week. On Monday, I started a 10 day detox, which included a limited, mostly vegan diet. Days five through seven were particularly stringent, and I needed items such as apple chips (without any additives), brussels sprouts, organic apple juice (again, no additives), and a few other key elements. I picked up everything I needed at Whole Foods in the beginning of the week, but had to re-stock a few things midway through. While running errands in Jersey, I swung by Wegman's thinking I could just grab my necessities in their hippy section. I was shocked when their selection did not meet my needs. Back to Whole Foods I went - on a Saturday, no less, for the items I still required.  Whole Foods will not replace my main grocery store but I certainly appreciate it more now that I know I can find specialty foods there. Also, free, covered parking for shoppers is a super huge bonus for city dwellers.

I resisted updating my review after my last experience at Villa Barone's Collingswood location, and wrote off my so-so meal as a fluke.  After lunch there today, I have come to the conclusion that the food is either not as good as it used to be or not as good as I thought it was.    Service has always been great, so there is absolutely no problem there.  My downgrade in stars comes simply from the food.  The last time I had dinner with some girlfriends, my chicken saltimbocca arrived with prosciutto that looked and tasted more like deli ham.  Additionally, I distinctly recall that the dish had a gray palor, which is neither inspiring or appetizing.   Today, while lunching with a friend, my gnocchi pomodoro tasted like bloated potato puffballs that had been floating around the pot for too long.  Even the zesty pomodoro sauce couldn't mask the dull flavor.  I feel like my downgrade to three stars is actually being generous, as my past two meals were hovering closer to two.  The fresh baked bread and kind service keeps me from going lower.    Villa Barone, get it together or I'm going down the street.  You know where.

This particular Taco Bell/KFC was clean and decorated for the holidays on my recent, random visit. I did think the service was much slower than most Taco Bell locations, however. Also, it was clear that whoever constructed my soft taco supreme did not care about the placement of the sour cream. It was sloppily located close to the edges of the taco shell - a taco faux pas. Still, for cleanliness and holiday spirit, I say three stars are in order.

I have to give a little review update shout out to the staff at Drinker's Pub. On my sister's wedding day, our entire bridal party rolled in unannounced to grab a round and several photos (my sister and her now-husband actually met at Drinker's, believe it or not!). The bartenders were cool, and the patrons didn't mind letting us take over the bar for a minute (literally - my sister and her husband posed on the bar with the rest of us around them).   It should also be mentioned that the drinks are CHEAP. I ordered a round of four or five drinks and handed the bartender a twenty before running to pose for a picture. I came back with another twenty to settle whatever I owed and the bartender gave me change. Amazing.

I love Philadelphia Theatre Company! I've seen a handful of shows over the past couple of years and really enjoy the varied programming. One show is never indicative of the next show. The acting is always great and I find it fairly easy to get wrapped up in a production in a matter of minutes.   The theatre is comfortable and every seat offers a nice view. I also love the sets! My favorite show so far has been Small Mouth Sounds. The set was so simple but perfect, and I loved that they incorporated scent into the atmosphere - it really enhanced the experience! I don't want to give anything away, but if you're considering seeing this show, you need to just buy a ticket already. It was hilarious, heartwarming, and fun.

I dig El Vez.  Their guacamole is kick-ass and the blood orange margarita is as yummy as the previous reviews indicate.  Also, an old school photo booth that actually works?!  Yippee!  Lounge-y background music and glittery decorations make for a fun atmosphere.  It's been a while since I've had dinner there, but hanging at the bar for drinks the other night made me want to plan another night out as soon as possible.

I ordered a salad from Matt & Marie's for delivery today at lunch. This was my first experience with the business. The reviews about their salads were fairly positive, and the photos looked great.   My order was for the La Scala, which comes with roasted red peppers, tomatoes and fresh mozzarella. I added on carved turkey and croutons, at an additional cost.
