As the restaurant filled up, I noticed things got even louder, and I was distracted by both the music and the din of other diners' conversations. Some soundproofing might help.   We started with Italian salad, meatballs, and two types of bruschetta. My friend also had the egg drop soup. I thought all of these dishes sounded great, and they were all nice, but nothing blew me away. Also, realizing we spent $15 on four total pieces of bruschetta has me scratching my head a little bit.  My friends opted for large plates as their entrees while I went with the rigatoni. The pasta was cooked perfectly and I loved the texture and spicy kick of the sauce, but wasn't a big fan of the smoked chicken.    The desserts menu was really small, featuring just two main attractions and some ice creams and sorbets. We shared the torta della nonna for dessert, which was my favorite part of the meal. Everything about it was perfection, and I would happily pop in just to have that dessert and a cup of their really excellent coffee again.   One thing that irritated me was that our server continued to squeeze through a tight space between my chair and a chair from the table behind us when she could have walked around. She always excused herself, but I had to move my chair every single time which was really annoying. I'd suggest creating a bit more space between tables/removing a chair from the corner table where we were seated if this is a continuous issue.   Overall, I thought we had an okay meal, and the dessert stole the show. I'm interested in returning sometime to try more of the menu.

Finally, FINALLY, I can remove my oldest bookmarked business. The bf and I have had a taste for Italian lately and we decided to set our sights on Collingswood last night. Now, I worked in the building across the street from Sapori for over three years, and I lived in town for more than four, and yet somehow never made it in. Despite hearing tons of praise. After our meal last night, it's safe to say that we'll now go out of our way for a meal there.   After a quick stop to Moore Brothers (if you don't know you better ask somebody) we arrived around 6:45 on a Monday. We were the first table in the restaurant, but a few more trickled in during our time there (which was a very relaxed, leisurely amount thanks to nicely paced courses). The decor is very old world-looking, with some really bizarre kitschy pieces thrown in. Like a tiny lamp held by a rabbit in a suit.   To start, you receive bread with some oil and... ? We weren't sure if it was mashed garlic, beans or both. It was honestly a bit indecipherable, and there was no description given when it was placed on our table. I wasn't really a fan. Everything else from that point on was pretty great, with the exception of some spotty water filling.   I opted for the salad with figs, pears, walnuts and blue cheese as my starter. The greens were arugula, a favorite of mine, and the dressing was just a light olive oil and some spots of quality balsamic. Quite tasty. Art chose one of the specials that night: pork and chicken meatballs stuffed with prosciutto and Italian cheese, fried and served in a pistachio cream sauce. These were delicious.   For my main, a penne pasta in a red wine tomato sauce with onions, smoked pancetta and some finely grated dry cheese on top. The smoky flavor was awesome and, as much as I wanted to save some to take home, I couldn't stop eating. The whole fish, filleted tableside, was a light, flaky fish cooked with capers and tomato.   For dessert, a shared plate of tiramisu which came with two homemade chococello shots. The perfect ending to a really great meal.

I really loved my first visit to Alpen Rose last week. The restaurant has a Clue library vibe going on and I enjoyed it! My husband and I were dining with his parents, who had already had a great experience previously.   We really did it up, ordering both versions of the parker house rolls, the tomato salad, and the croquettes (a special) to start. We also tried the tuna carpaccio which was sent out by the kitchen. All of these were promising starts to the meal.   My husband and his father split the beef wellington, which was massive and presented with a whole slicing performance at the table. The only issue is that the restaurant is rather small and a large party had to squeeze past to get to their table, so about twelve people walked by this steak on a giant rollaway as it sat there waiting to be served. It was a little bit awkward, so a little less pomp and circumstance might be better.   My mother-in-law had the prime rib, which she declared to be the best prime rib she's ever had, which is definitely high praise! I had the filet which was exactly what I wanted. It went perfectly with our sides: mashed potatoes, roasted mushrooms, and onion rings (all delicious). I loved both of the house sauces on the table for adding a little kick!   For dessert, we shared the baked alaska, coconut cream pie, and french press coffee. I loved the coffee service; everything was presented so beautifully! The coconut cream pie wasn't too heavy on the coconut and therefore was more cream than coconut. The crust was fantastic! But the baked alaska stole the show. It's lit on fire tableside and every component was spot on, especially the meringue.   And now for my only complaint. Our server was very attentive, and he really knew the menu. That said, I ordered a non-alcoholic beverage, and I believe our server (incorrectly) assumed I was pregnant, because he made several unsolicited comments about the blue cheese in the tomato salad being pasteurized. Kind of awkward, especially since I was at a meal with my in-laws. Please don't make assumptions, servers (or anyone, actually)! That aside, this was a wonderful meal and definitely at the top of my list next time I'm craving a steak!

Ugh, Hallmark.  They lure me in with stores a-plenty and Gold Crown Rewards coupons.  Still, every time a holiday rolls around and I inevitably end up in the store, I want to scream.  Instead, I stare at the same cards for twenty minutes until I pick out something so generic, it could be sent to my dentist.     Then, I take my cards up to the counter, where one of four women is smiling maniacally and asks if I found everything I was looking for.  Instead of responding with, "No I didn't, because it's not 1965 and not everyone has parents who are still happily married to each other.  Oh yeah, and my stepdad is not my 'mom's special loved one,' he's my stepdad!"  I simply say yes, pay for my cards and leave, hoping a new card store will roll into town.

For a girl and her boyfriend who were eating nothing but cruciferous veggies, apples and pears for three days straight, the prospect of avocado and cucumber rolls made with brown rice was about as exciting as a steak-lover eating gratis at Barclay Prime.   While we loved that we were eating something new after three days of darkness, the rolls were just okay. The rice wasn't as sticky as I've come to expect from sushi rice. Pieces were on the small side, though each roll came with 12 (priced accordingly).   Service was lackluster. I immediately received a water when I arrived but we had to ask for one for my boyfriend. Also, we sat around for a while before our order was taken, even though we were the only people there at that point.   We chose Mizu because of the seating and option of brown rice, but I'll stick with one of my other spots for sushi in Rittenhouse now that my crazy detox diet is over!

I've been spending a whole lot of time in coffee shops lately and I've been especially charmed by L'Aube. My skim latte last Monday morning was absolutely dreamy. I can only imagine how amazing the crepes are - the smell was intoxicating!   Next time I'm in the mood for a little French rendezvous, I know exactly the place to go. Wonder if I can convince anyone to sing The Beatles' "Michelle" to me?

With some time to kill before the Victory beer dinner last night, I decided to meet up with some of yelp's finest in one of the city's diviest.  I'll admit, walking up to the bar I was a tad nervous that I'd be the only person to show, as there were some mixed messages during the day about whether or not a pregame was still taking place.  I opened the door and felt relief wash over as the smiling faces of Jim H. and Chris V. greeted me from the end of the bar.  While introducing myself to "Jack" and Stephen H., I became keenly aware that my loud mouth was carrying and that every other patron was now well aware that this was a meet-up of friends from the Internet.  Flustered, I took a seat and realized that I had walked right by Dan C. in the process (Sorry, Dan, I'm blaming it on the suit!), prompting me to get up for another round of hugs and hellos.     Finally, I returned to my post and ordered a Flying Fish.  The bartender gave a heads-up that the version on tap was actually the Grand Cru Winter ale, and since I had never tried it before, he offered a taste.  Happy day, I was met with what instantly became my new favorite seasonal!    My introduction to Doobie's was cut short as our event times drew near, but I was happy for the opportunity to check the place out.  The warm and friendly service we received is definitely enough to bring me back, and any place with rumors of David Bowie's presence in the 70s gets an extra star from me.  Any coincidence that Golden Years has been playing on a continuous loop in my head ever since?  I think not!

I was really excited to try Sate Kampar. I'm all about grilled meat on sticks! My husband and I went in for a casual date night with some beers in tow. The menu is slightly confusing and I felt that our server somehow made it even more confusing. He was sort of insisting that we order personal plates, but we were more interested in the shared plates. It was hard to determine exactly how much food to order. That said, our server did stop us from over-ordering on the skewers, which I greatly appreciated.  We ended up going for one of the specials of the day - a Malaysian version of chicken nuggets. These arrived looking super delicious but, to my surprise, they almost tasted like they had been sitting out or something. They didn't have a crisp, freshly-fried crunch. They were still good, but would have been much better if they had a crisper texture.   We also shared the rendang daging (beef braised in coconut cream - delicious!), mee hoon goreng bungkus (vermicelli noodles with egg - tasty), some jasmine rice, and the aforementioned skewers, which were oddly my least favorite dish. The skewers we ordered (sate kajang chicken and sate melaka pork) were a bit fatty. Especially the pork - it reminded me of pork belly, which I do not like.   I'm going with three stars after my first visit, but I'm looking forward to going back, trying some other menu items and hopefully updating my rating!

I loved my first visit to the Independence Beer Garden! It was pretty crowded at dinnertime on a Sunday evening. Luckily, my fiancé and his friends had already locked down a table. The Watermelon Wheat pitchers were flowing but I quickly switched to the gin, cucumber and elderflower drink at the suggestion of our server.   Speaking of whom, she was the sweetest, most soft spoken, lovely woman (blonde with pink hair, I can't remember her name)! Always right on top of anything we needed and knew the menu front to back.   I was super hungry and feeling indulgent so I ordered the cheeseburger and pickle chips. The burger was good; I've had better but it did the trick. The pickle chips were awesome; I see more of these in my future. Can't wait for many more warm spring and summer nights at the IBG!

After an incredible honeymoon in a French territory, I really wasn't ready to get back to everyday life when I returned. With one final day off before returning to work, we treated ourselves to a fabulously French dinner at The Good King Tavern.   I had only been to The Good King once before, for a lovely tasting dinner. I was excited to try some of the menu items on this visit. There were several specials, and the endive and roquefort salad jumped out at me. It was served in a neat stack, with a creamy roquefort dressing on the bottom and crumbles throughout, plus dices of apple and slivers of red onion. The salad was topped with a tangy vinaigrette. Delicious! My husband (!!!) and I also shared the olives, and he started with the escargot which he really enjoyed.   Next, I had the trout with whole grain mustard smashed potatoes and pea shoots. The fish was absolutely perfect and I loved the flavor of the mustard in the potatoes. I also ordered a side of haricot vert, which were delightfully garlicky and a perfect complement to my entree. I had a bite of the house smoked sausage with fingerlings and choucroute. This was the French version of a dish I grew up with in my German grandmother's kitchen, so needless to say I enjoyed that very much as well.   There was no room for dessert whatsoever, but we both enjoyed a cocktail or two after our meals (in addition to several glasses of the "better" house wine, which tasted fantastic).   Saying I loved this dinner would be an understatement. It was the perfect meal to end our honeymoon. I really think we need to make TGK a regular spot in our favorite restaurants rotation. It's casual enough for a weeknight while having plenty of charm for a date night.

The Industry has eased its way on to my short list of favorite bars in the city. I truly love this place. It's great for drinks, dinner, and brunch - sometimes all three if you hang out long enough (it happens). The service is always friendly and fantastic.   In my humble opinion, the food has been getting better and better over time. There's always a great selection for dinner ranging from salads and sandwiches to entrees. For brunch, I always go savory but would highly recommend sharing something sweet. I once had a few bites of their baked pancake special and it was phenomenal.  Super solid spot.

Okay, so I know I only wrote my first review of Porco's a couple weeks ago, however, I had to swing on back for a review update because I finally tried one of the pork sandwiches over the weekend.   Mind. Blowing.   Honestly, the cubano sandwich was one of the best things I've eaten all year. The pork was super tender and so flavorful. There were some crunchy bits that added great texture and pops of flavor. The pickled veggies and mustard aioli really brightened up the whole sandwich. The freshly baked bread held everything together and did not fall apart.   My husband and I have become weekday pescetarians and have been eating meat only on weekends. This sandwich basically confirmed that I could never go full-vegetarian. Unreal. I look forward to revisiting the cubano next weekend.

Despite my hesitations, our crew of four agreed to meet up with some other friends who were hanging at Mission Grill after the Flyers game on Saturday night. We were all dressed very casually in tees and jeans, and I thought there was a good chance we'd get turned away at the door, but that didn't happen. I felt super self-conscious around all the pretty young things dressed in bustiers and heels. Alas, a friend knew a bartender, and before I was able to change my mind I was handed a shot and a Miller Lite in of one of those vortex bottles.   It was NOT my typical Saturday night.  And yet, I had a really great time. The DJ was awesome, playing a steady mix of current and old-school beats. I couldn't help but get over my anxieties about being under-dressed and out of place (I'm sure the strong buzz I had going had something to do with it, also).   I danced my booty off. And I loved it.   The best part of the night was when a huge group of people showed up, all wearing AT&T t-shirts. To think we actually started an orange tee shirt trend! It was like a bizarre dream.

I ordered a salad from Torch-Wood Market for delivery and was very happy with my order! The salad was super fresh and had a nice amount of toppings. The dressing was served on the side, per my request. Best of all, I think the salad set me back something like eight bucks. I never get away with spending less than ten bucks for lunch so that was a true joy. Looking forward to many more happy memories with Torch-Wood!

Vernick Coffee Bar seems to be the it place right now! I went for a working lunch last week and brought my laptop so that I could stay and get some work done. Who knew I'd run into so many familiar faces that I'd actually get less done than if I were at my own house with all the usual distractions?!   Lunch was great. Our server was really sweet and knew the menu very well. I went with the chilled shrimp soba noodle salad and it was absolutely delicious. Super fresh and perfect for a light lunch!   Later on while seated by the coffee bar, I splurged on a salted caramel cookie which was, sadly, not nearly as tasty as it looked (didn't stop me from eating it, though). I'll have to try one of the other pastries next time, and there are plenty from which to choose. Looking forward to my next visit!

I love you, Insomnia Cookies. Since you've expanded your delivery territory to cover Graduate Hospital, we've ordered twice in the past month. Danger Zone, population: me.   My only (minor) complaint is that the presentation is a bit sloppy. Our recent order of six cookies arrived in a pizza box type thing and they were kind of all over the place, but still intact. The deliciousness of the slightly-crunchy, slightly-soft cookies was not impacted by the seemingly bumpy trip to our doorstep.   The chocolate chunk and double chocolate chunk are great. We even scored three of our cookies for free because of some sort of March Madness promotion that was on the Insomnia website. I love that they do stuff like that.   Also appreciated is the ice cream option, which always arrives still frozen. Flavors rotate but I can personally attest to the coffee and mint chocolate chip ice creams being a very good partner to the cookies.

It's been a week since my friend's wedding at Indian Spring and I think I'm just about recovered.  The ceremony was held on a patio that was attached to the reception room.  While my crew arrived early enough to get seats, there were a good number of people who didn't.  I'm not sure what that was all about, so I would suggest arriving early for anyone who plans on attending a ceremony before a reception here.  Immediately after the wedding party filed back down the aisle, the patio bar was open for business as was the bar inside the hall area.  A blonde bartender at the inside bar (I forget her name!) kept the line moving quickly while serving up some really great martinis.    Hors d'oeuvres consisted of the usual suspects; spinach and feta in phyllo, bacon wrapped scallops, sesame crusted ahi tuna, etc.  Everything I tried was very good, but the waitstaff was sparse.  Dinner courses were pretty ho-hum until the entree arrived, a filet (medium) with stuffed shrimp, mashed potatoes and veggies.  The filet was cooked as requested and was definitely above average for a large, catered event.  From what I hear, the restaurant on the premises is excellent, and I would happily check it out sometime for dinner.  After the wedding, almost everyone under the age of 50 headed straight for the downstairs bar.  Throwing caution and credit card statements to the wind, I drunkenly proclaimed that I wanted to buy the first round for my immediate group, which consisted of five or so people.  For hours, a gracious bartender put up with the slurred requests of about twenty to thirty people, singlehandedly.  Like a seasoned professional, she didn't even balk when I made the sudden switch from vodka and club to Old Grand Dad and coke ("I jussht tried hissh and it'sshh sssssshhooooo gooddd!!!!").  The next day, as stars and anvils chased each other in a frantic merry-go-round encircling my head, I located the receipt from that first round "on me."  The bill was for sixteen dollars and I had tacked on a well-deserved ten dollar tip.  Not only were the drinks potent, they were also very wallet friendly.  I shall keep this in mind when I return for my best guy friend's wedding in the fall.

I ordered delivery from Al Zaytouna based on the many reviews by friends who had also ordered, and enjoyed, delivery. My experience was no different. My order arrived fairly quickly and everything was intact and kept separate by a divided container.   The pita was a bit on the tough side but I didn't really mind. I liked the thinness of it; perfect for wrapping everything up into rolled sandwiches. The chicken from my kebabs was a little bit dry, but with some hummus and veggies, it still tasted good. There was so much food that I actually had some leftovers, which I promptly tore up after a night on the town later that evening. I'll definitely hit up Al Zaytouna again for future delivery.

Yesterday, we hosted my sister's baby shower on the outdoor patio at Sapori, and it could not have been more perfect!   I first reached out in February and worked directly with the owner, Franco, to set up details. Franco was flexible with our needs and so laid-back. As an event planner myself, I wondered if he was too laid-back, but I needn't have worried because everything about the day was exactly as we had discussed. A total pro!   Upon arrival, the patio was immaculately arranged and we were able to quickly set up the decorations and flowers. It was a beautiful day but the patio also has really powerful heaters just in case - truly this is an ideal venue for an outdoor event!  I dropped off wine the day before and we brought in our own dessert which was great; we appreciated the flexibility to do this as we had specific desserts in mind. Our head server handled all of the little details and really kept the flow. The tables were well stocked with water carafes, bread with oil, and Parmesan. Those little details go a long way with a big group!   We started with an antipasto course which was absolutely gorgeous and had everyone at my table excited for what was next. There were five entree choices and each dish looked fantastic! I had the cioppino but couldn't help but steal a few bites of casarecce and gnocchi -- all were excellent!   My mom and I had actually stopped by Sapori a few weeks before the shower to discuss some last minute details and have dinner. We had a wonderful meal that night and the food at my sister's baby shower was every bit as delicious.   Most importantly, my sister was so happy with her special day. This is all thanks to the wonderful staff at Sapori, who couldn't have been nicer and more accommodating. True hospitality professionals. I will be recommending Sapori for special events and look forward to my next meal there!

After reading Stephen H's ROTD for Stir last week, I checked out the other reviews and realized I needed to get in on the action as soon as possible. Little did I know how soon I'd be partaking - just days later I found myself walking down Chancellor with a bevy of yelp buds.   For some reason, what I pictured Stir to look like and what it actually looked like were two very different things. I had imagined a wall of dark brick and a long chestnut bar with little space to maneuver. What I got was a square bar in the center of a cozy room, plus another bar with more space in the back, and very tasteful décor all around. Added to that was a 'tender who knew how to make a martini just as well as he made every one of us Stir newbs feel welcome.   Thanks to Sue for letting me tickle her pickle. I quite liked it, actually.

I swung by Konditori on Sunday while I was strolling and shopping in the Rittenhouse area. The female barista was really nice and my iced coffee hit the spot. I commented on the double chocolate muffins which looked absolutely delicious. The barista said they make them fresh daily. I'll have to pop back in some other time to try one!

It's a double review day, because I couldn't give love to Small Oven and not Porco's! For those who don't know, Porco's and Small Oven are two concepts running out of the same space. Porco's is all about the meats, but they also serve some fantastic meaty substitutes!   Though they are known for their porchetta, I opted for a meatball sandwich the first time I tried Porco's. The sandwich was stuffed with pork and beef blend meatballs and the house-made mozz took the sandwich over the top.   I've also tried their vegetarian sandwich, which was loaded with layers of veggies and felt super hearty but also healthy.   Porco's is still slinging sandwiches despite these trying times, so be sure to call ahead for pick up at their take-out window, or order delivery straight to your front door!

Finally got back to The Corner with the intention of trying some of the food. I was not disappointed! For starters, there's an incredible happy hour with drinks and appetizers from 5-7. I kind of hate letting the cat out of the bag on that one. I'll soon be returning to partake again.   I don't think I realized how nice the downstairs has become since the APO days. On my other visits to The Corner, I've always headed straight upstairs to the lounge areas. I'm glad I was able to sit at the chef's counter to take in the action and the vibrant dining room.   My boyfriend is friendly with the chef, and a couple of appetizers were sent over. I loved the crunchy jalapeño cream cheese balls. They were like mini poppers. The pork belly sliders weren't my thing, but mostly because I'm not a big fan of pork belly. Fried pickles were awesome; by far one of the better attempts at the dish I've had (my favorites are the cornmeal-crusted coins at Jose Pistolas).    The Caesar salad was great, and at only $5 for happy hour, a total steal. The tuna tartare app which I ordered as my main was also excellent. There was just the right amount of spice and the tuna wasn't weighed down by too much sauce. My boyfriend's lobster pot pie was loaded with lobster and tasted great.   We had no room left for dessert but it won't be long before we're back for dinner again.

I had my very first Paesano's experience on a warm Saturday afternoon in April.  We walked inside the Italian Market location and were fortunate enough to snag two seats just as a table was being cleared.  The ten or so sandwiches were all tempting in their own right, and I had to knock them off the list one-by-one in order to narrow down my selection.  Despite my best efforts to keep it healthy, I soon realized that Paesano's is no place for dieters.  If the ingredients don't get you, the sheer quantity of the sandwiches will... because you won't be able to stick to just half.  If you attempt it, the other half WILL haunt you from its paper wrapping for the rest of the afternoon, until you give in to the devil on your shoulder and snarf it in your kitchen, hovered over the stove, when no one is watching.  What?  What happened?  I blacked out for a minute.  Anyway...  I ended up ordering the special that day, the Mamma Mia: turkey, sharp provolone, hot and sweet peppers, tomato, arugula and garlic mayo on a crusty long roll.  I'm not a huge fan of mayo so I asked them to go easy on it, which they did.  I'd hardly say that made my sandwich any more healthy, because it was stuffed to the gills and every bite was packed with addictive deliciousness.  Needless to say, I'll be staying far, far away from this place until after I get back from my trip to Mexico next month.  After that, all bets are off.

I am completely lost when it comes to the King of Prussia Mall. I don't know where anything is, I've only been there twice in the past ten years, and both times were for recent events I was hosting. Grand Lux was a stone's throw away from where I needed to be, so I decided to grab a quick bite.   The best thing about this place is the training they must do with each employee. Hosts make polite conversation on the walk to the table and any time they encounter you throughout the restaurant. My server was very friendly as well, and super apologetic when they were out of my first and second wine selections.   I wanted to keep things healthy so I opted for the simply grilled mahi mahi with a baked potato and steamed spinach on the side. The mahi mahi and potato arrived first, and I had to flag my server down to ask about the spinach, which was brought out after. When the best things about your entree are the sides, it's not saying much. My mahi mahi was way overcooked and super dry as a result - not even the accompanying tartar-like sauce offered much help. It's kind of a bummer that with such an extensive menu, a simple piece of grilled fish was botched. Next time, I'll give myself more time so I can investigate other dining options.

Yeah, it's true.  I'm that girl who never got excited about a trip to Monk's. My first experience was so-so and one subsequent trip for a quick beer during last winter's snowpocalypse didn't win me over, either.   For me, Monk's was a Philly fixture that blended with the urban landscape.  Why I heard myself suggesting the place as a lunch option the other day is still a mystery. Divine intervention? Perhaps. Because the pot of Ghent mussels, bathing in a Saison Dupont broth filled with bacon, leeks and blue cheese, were life-changing.  Also, it appears my previous gripe is null and void. Burgers are now served with a choice of greens or - wait for it - frites. Reunited and it feels so gooooood!

A friend/fellow yelper and I met for a drunken brunch to celebrate Labor Day.  We started our meal with bloody marys, which were just okay (but not bad enough to stop us from ordering a second round later in the meal).  Next time, I'll probably opt for one of Mixto's many other signature drinks instead.  We started with the platanitos; plantain chips and guacamole.  I like my chips salted, but the plantain chips were nakey so we just threw some salt on top of the guac.  No complaints though.  I order this starter often so I knew what to expect.  For my breakfast, I had huevos rancheros.  My dining companion and I gave a shout out to Monica S. at this point, the resident expert on this dish.  I was given my choice of breakfast meat and I went with chorizo, which ended up being pretty awesome.  Refried beans and some homemade tortilla chips completed the meal.  Shout out to our server, Louis, who was efficient and pleasant, despite our many questions and special requests.

I chose Redstone for lunch with a friend thinking it would be pretty quiet during the week. Oh how wrong I was! I walked through the doors and the area in front of the host stand was packed with people. Despite this, the hostesses were hustling and each group was seated shortly after arrival.   Everyone we encountered was very, very nice, and wait times for drinks and food were not long. They really have their lunch service down. Our server was so sweet and accommodating, especially with regards to my friend's one year old son.   I think I could have liked Redstone a bit more if I had ordered differently. The Caesar salad was on the small side, with just lettuce, croutons and a teeny tiny Parmesan crisp. But I will say that the dressing was delicious and the rotisserie chicken I opted to add on was tender and flavorful. I could have used another handful of lettuce and a piece of bread or something. My friend's flatbread looked pretty great.   Redstone's pricey but you wouldn't know it based on the crowds. Ladies lunching and business people filled the place. I love the patio and will probably return for drinks during the summer months.

My experience at Fishtown Brewpub last weekend was not great. A group of us were out for my birthday and we were hopping from place to place. I had this spot bookmarked because it's new and I thought it would be cool for us all to check it out together for the first time.   We walked in and there were some people seated at the bar, but for the most part the restaurant was fairly empty. Someone else in our party had already locked down a table in the back, so we made our way there. Maybe I misread the body language, but I swear the bartender gave our group some major side-eye as we passed by. It was just a weird reception and vibe that I wouldn't expect from a relatively new business.   Our server was very sweet and brought us all waters and menus. Mostly everyone was stoked on trying some of the house beers, but when we ordered we were informed that none of them were ready yet. So everyone came up with a second choice, but then it took a really long time before everyone at the table had their drinks (a couple cocktails but mostly draughts). We decided at this point to call it and move on to the next place. I'd be interested to get back at some point for a revisit once the house beers are available, and I hope to have a better experience.

I was so pleasantly surprised by my brunch at Cafe La Maude a couple months ago. There were a few tables set up outside but it was a warm day so we decided to eat inside. Fortunately, we snagged the last available table, but even if there had been a wait, it seemed like turnover was pretty quick. Still, the place was bumpin' on a Sunday morning!    The menu was much larger than I expected for a cafe, and they also had some specials. I went super basic with scrambled eggs and cheddar on a croissant, but it was delicious. The coffee was great, too. My friend raved about her salad. The staff was very friendly and one of the owners/managers swung by each table to make sure people were enjoying themselves. I can't wait to go back!

I had a great experience placing a wine delivery with Fishtown Social a few weeks ago. The full list of offerings is available on their website, with some notes about each bottle. I ordered two whites (including a dry riesling from local winery Wayvine - I love this wine!) and a bottle of bubbles.   Deliveries take place on Wednesdays, Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays. I placed my order through email on a Thursday night, received confirmation and paid on Friday morning, and received the delivery that afternoon.   There's really something for everyone on Fishtown Social's wine list, so give them a look next time you're stocking up on wine.

Martha, you are the jam. The menu situation is genius. Don't know what I'm talking about? Well, just pull out your phone and check out martha.menu - there, you will find an updated list of all menu items. No specials, no 86 this and that, just the bites and beverages available for purchase at any given time, straight up.   The bar itself is funky and chill, the backyard garden even better. It's like being in someone's backyard with its low-key, cute vibe. And, there's bocce ball. Love.   The hoagies are increds, the pickles are the best I've had in this city (seriously), and the warm spiced nuts are deliciously perfect.   Way to keep it cool and local, Martha. You're tops in my book.

When Smokin' Betty's was suggested as the locale for a Friday happy hour between friends, I was pretty stoked; especially because I missed Sam's MOOB UYE earlier that week.  Our rain soaked crew arrived around 5:30 to a completely empty restaurant.  It wasn't until a hostess appeared that we found out they were seating everyone on the second floor.  We went upstairs and were surprised to find a fairly crowded bar and a few occupied tables.  How we didn't hear the peeps and music from the first floor, I have no idea.  We were seated at a booth that fit all six of us, and my side faced a wall that featured a gigantic chalkboard filled with beers, cocktails, the day's specials and happy hour info.  Smokin' Betty's Blonde, the house beer, was only three bucks during happy hour so most of us started with that.  I thought it was similar in taste to Magic Hat #9 and I enjoyed it a lot.  When a friend wrinkled her nose after tasting the Curious Georgia (a bellini-like concoction of white beer, peach schnapps and a ginger syrup-marinated peach slice), I gladly took it off her hands as I adore bellinis in their natural state and I enjoyed this interesting spin-off as well.  (So yes, for those of you doing the math, technically I was double fisting for a short period of time but I'm half Irish and this is widely accepted in our culture.)  Our group was going to order off the menu but when we saw the cheap eats offered as part of happy hour, we changed our minds.  I had the spicy dry rub wings which were awesome, but what made them even better was the barbecue sauce I requested on the side for dipping.  Sweet but with a definite zip, it was one saucy sauce!  The onion rings and corn bread we ordered for sides were pretty standard.  A friend ordered the bbq sliders and I had major food envy.  I will definitely hit those up on my next visit, with an extra side of that sauce, of course!    A five star rating might be viewed as a bit generous by some, but there wasn't a single thing I disliked about my experience at Betty's.  The food, drinks and service were all on point and I will gladly return.

Walking into Bloom on Sunday, I had no idea what to expect, but I was surprised to find that the tiny shop was stuffed with clothes, accessories, soaps, candles and other little trinkets. I saw about a million great stocking stuffers during my short visit. I'm still thinking about the sequined business card holder I saw and wishing there was someone on my Christmas list who could use it.   I didn't end up purchasing anything, but I did walk away impressed by the selection. I will definitely stop by again the next time I need a cute gift for a friend or my sister.

I stumbled into Chipotle around 8 pm on Thursday night, straight out of a boot camp class. I can't imagine what I must have looked like. Hungry - no, starving, I told the guy behind the counter that I had never been to a Chipotle and asked if he could just run through the options. I decided to go with a burrito, since it would be traveling with me back to Philly and it seemed like the least messy choice. At that moment, he yelled "free burrito!" and nods were shared between the workers.   I don't know if it was because they were frightened of my sweaty self and wanted me out as fast as possible, or if it was because I was an eager Chipotle newbie, but I was so surprised and extremely grateful nonetheless. Back at my apartment, my burrito tasted like food of the gods, with two sides of salsas and some Mexican crema. I will undoubtedly return, hopefully not resembling the female Hulk next time.

I won't lie. I was a little surprised when I found out that Krispy Kreme would be going in smack between McMillan's and DiBartolo, two bakeries that I believe to be the creme de la creme of doughnut purveyors in South Jersey. I even voiced my suspicions on a Talk thread (and later got totally called out on it by a Krispy Kreme higher-up. Oops! Sorry, Braden.).   HOWEVER, I went to the Collingswood Krispy Kreme pre-opening party and have to say that the selection is pretty baller. I scored a mini doughnut and a sample of one of the legit sticky buns covered in frosting, but there was so much more that beckoned from the squeaky clean cases. The coffee was also pretty good. There was plenty of seating and rumor has it that there will even be a lounge area. This, along with a drive-thru lane, certainly sets KK apart from the other bakeries. Also, they'll be open until 11pm, which may take care of some evening munchies.   Am I giving up my old bakeries? Hells no. But is there room in town for another? I don't see why not.

There aren't many sit-down breakfast options in Midtown during the week, so Green Eggs fills that need quite nicely. It isn't my favorite brunch spot, but on weekdays when there's no wait, it's a solid option. On weekends, expect lines on lines. It's one of those brunch factory-type places, with huge portions that people go crazy over. I get that people dig that, but it's not really my scene.   I recently enjoyed an eggs benedict with a healthy side of breakfast potatoes (on a weekday, naturally). You get a choice of a couple different potato styles, and I chose the one with peppers and onions, which I liked a lot. The coffee is La Colombe, which I love, but it tasted burnt.   The restaurant is cash only, which is not convenient, though there is an ATM on site. I'll be back if in the area and craving breakfast, but if I have extra time and other options I'd likely choose elsewhere.

Giumarello's is still one of the best of South Jersey, as far as I'm concerned! I returned for a family dinner this week. My stepmom made a reservation for the bar area and our party of five was seated in a large, comfortable corner booth.   Service was excellent from start to finish; you can tell the management takes a lot of care with training their staff. The happy hour is awesome. One dollar off all drinks, three dollar beers, and a long list of reduced price food items.   We started with mussels in red sauce and steamed clams in white sauce from the happy hour menu. Of course, we were served two heaping baskets of fresh breads with a side of roasted peppers. My brother also ordered a cheese plate which was overflowing with four different types of cheese and a lot of great accoutrements.   I'm pretty hooked on the Mediterranean salad which is a caesar salad loaded with jumbo lump crabmeat and shrimp. I was so full from the starters that I ended up taking half of the salad home. My husband and brother both got burgers. On Tuesdays they are a special price and come with a complimentary draft beer. Both of them brought home half of their burgers and fries. My dad had a salad with blackened shrimp and filet, which he loved, and my stepmom had a brand new scallops app as her main which looked delicious!   I do not want another year to go by before I get back here! Definitely hoping to return for happy hour sooner than later. Next time, I'm taking the train so I can indulge in some of those martinis!

I returned to Vedge last month with a group of friends. Personally, I wouldn't go with five stars simply because I'm not vegan or vegetarian, but I can imagine that it would easily be five stars for someone who does fall into one of these categories. I do know that the food I tried was very good.   Our table of six shared the bite board. Honestly, we probably could have shared two boards between all of us, but we ordered enough larger plates that it wasn't necessary. The bite board provided some of my favorite tastes of the night, though.   I started with the cauliflower soup which was a bit on the "I'm on a detox diet" side. Meanwhile, my friend's gazpacho was absolutely delish and perfect for summer. Go with that if you want to start with soup. Next up was a plate from the dirt menu - fingerlings in a Worcestershire cream sauce. Basically, fancy french fries. Of course they were awesome.   My main course was a garbanzo crepe with lentils and hearts of palm. It was very tasty and reminded me of a vegetarian Indian dish. It was also filling.   The chocolate pot de creme and the cheesecake were both delicious. I feel confident that in a blind taste test, no one would have any idea that they are both vegan.   Much as I liked Vedge, I could see the place as more of a happy hour or light bite later in the evening kind of place for myself. But don't let that stop you from trying dinner there. It's worth a visit, regardless of your dietary preferences.

It's kind of a hike for me to get to this Shop Rite, but the money I save from my shopper card is totally worth it ($14+ on my last visit!). There's certainly no shopping incentive at Whole Foods, other than the free parking, which you always get at Shop Rite stores. I've also found that most Shop Rites have very similar layouts, making grocery runs so much easier.   I've never had issues with the quality of any item, from produce to meats to dairy. I'm also happy with a lot of the store brand products.   Jerry F points out in his review that the check-out staff is friendly AND competent, and I have to agree. There are always a decent amount of lanes open and no added frustration during the check-out process.

Last night I returned to Han Dynasty with a fellow fan and a newbie. We wanted to induct the new girl right, so we immediately suggested the dan dan noodles and cucumbers. Then she raised the stakes by ordering the dumplings in chili oil. Well played, rookie!  We each ordered a different entree and by the time our food arrived (pretty much all at once with entrees dropped just after the starters), we could have invited our respective men along and still had plenty to go around. I finally ordered the crispy rice with shrimp that I had long lusted over and it did not disappoint. The dish announced its presence with sizzling noises and the crunchy rice was incredible. I thought the shrimp were slightly overcooked but overall, I really enjoyed the dish. Kung pao chicken (the newb) was pretty standard although obviously far better than any take-out joint, and another chicken dish with hot peppers would have been really great if it hadn't been way too salty.   Everyone's entitled to an off night and I've had so many great experiences at Han that I can't take away from them just for a couple missteps. Service was better than in the past, although I probably would have ordered another beer had someone stopped by after we received our food. No big, I just had more room in the tummy for some Franklin Fountain deliciousness.

Popped into Vedge on a whim on Thursday for a nightcap. We were fortunate enough to enjoy the front lounge to ourselves for the entire time we were there, making for a really fun and romantic night out. The wine list was great, with some really interesting selections including a sparkling shiraz that was totally unexpected and completely awesome. Both of the mixed olives bowls provided for a very nice accompaniment. I may even be convinced to try dinner next time.

Tuesdays. $8.95 for bread, soup or salad and any pasta from their vast selection. That alone is worth some stars, but the deliciousness of my meal backs them up!  I joined my former neighbors for an evening of catch-up over dinner. We were all a little buzzy after some pre-dinner cocktails so it was nice that there was no wait for a table. In fact, we were the only people in the restaurant around 7:30. Hasn't anyone heard of pasta night?!  Our server was sweet and took care of us with a smile, even though we all felt a little guilty keeping her there late. We started with some dense bread that came with a big plate of peppers in marinara. Next up was the soup and salad course, and I opted for the salad, which was vibrant with veggies and topped with a very basil-rich tomato vinaigrette. Very nice.   For my main I of course chose one of the pastas, the Amatriciana, with pancetta, chopped tomatoes and onions. With shrimp added-on and some marinara on the side (I like it saucy!), the dish was simple but delicious. After a long run earlier that day, it felt good to carbo-load. We had so much fun and with a night out that cost around $20 a head (plus our BYO wine), we'll probably make it a regular occurrence.
You know what boyfriends like for Valentine's Day? Lingerie and Han Dynasty take-out. Served separately, of course.

Finally made my way over to Tired Hands the other night and super glad I did. Word is that they will be expanding into a larger space soon so I'm glad I got to check out their current, cozy location.   Jane was our server and she was pleasant and on point with her beer descriptions. I love that you can order beers in a 4, 8 or 16 ounce pour. 8 ounces is the perfect size for a beer. I wish all bars would start carrying 8 ounce glasses so I can move between different beers without downing far too many suds in a night.   The HopHands pale ale is a house beer that we were told is always on tap. Good news for me since I loved it. The First Level single hop IPA was also very tasty and smooth.   We shared two paninis between three of us - the Tired Hands with ham and Swiss and the Jeano's with Swiss, blue cheese and green beans (?!?!). Super random and I'm not sure that I loved green beans on my 'wich but both were still very tasty. The spicy mustard sauce served alongside is clutch. Definitely looking to get back ASAP.

I've gotta give it up for my hometown bar! For some, this may be an average spot, but to me, it's a place filled with memories. From high school field hockey dinners to night-before-Thanksgiving visits during college and now for catching up with my dad over a few cold ones during a game, the place has remained consistent throughout the years.   Everyone within a twenty mile radius knows that Whistlers and their sister property, the Jug Handle Inn, have the best wings around. I like them hot and well done, with a basket of carrots and celery on the side. They also have great cheesesteaks, salads and other bar food.   The draft list has gotten progressively better in recent years. Though I opted for Bud Light on my recent visit (give me a break, it was only noon), I saw a few worthy options for craft beer lovers.  Last year, a huge deck was added to the building with a large bar and several TVs. This is the perfect spot for watching a game in the fall. It's like tailgating, but with better bathrooms.  I'm looking forward to catching more games on the deck while the weather is still nice... and now that I've had their wings again it won't be long before I need another fix!

Loved my first experience at a.bar. This dark and sexy corner bar is prime real estate for people-watching. Somehow, the shades on the windows kept people from really looking in, but were still perfect for looking out. No fishbowl effect.  The menu looks really awesome, but I didn't have anything to eat since we had dinner reservations at a.kitchen. But I did try the Pamplemousse Spritz, which was a perfect summer cocktail. Drinks are pricey, but considering the location I think that's to be expected. Said libations pack a punch so I have no complaints.   Really looking forward to my next rendezvous on the corner of 18th and Walnut.

Mixto is probably my favorite of all the Cuban/Caribbean places I've tried in and around the city.  The décor is really nice and makes you feel all vacation-like, which is always a plus... well, sort of.  Vacation-like feelings make me think I'm entitled to drink as many mojitos as if I were actually on vacation, and on a work night.    The happy hour specials are pretty special indeed.  Mondays and Wednesdays offer $4 regular mojitos (that's half-price!), Tuesdays and Thursdays offer $4 margaritas and Fridays are $2 off any drink.  Bonus--they use Bacardi rum in their regular mojitos, even for the happy hour specials.  When my (intoxicated) group of three sat down for dinner, we each ordered an appetizer--fried calamari, papa rellenas (small potatoes stuffed with ground beef) and platanitos (plantain chips with homemade guacamole).  The general consensus was that the food was good but the calamari was probably the processed frozen kind that you can get anywhere.  I was asked to remove one full star from my review because of this apparently unforgivable offense.    Luckily, no other stars have to come off because I truly liked everything about my meal and it appeared that my dining companions did also.  After reading Stephanie M.'s review, I got the Ropa Vieja and was not disappointed.  It was really delicious and there was so much on the plate between the meat, plantains, black beans and yellow rice that I actually had leftovers.  We saved no room for dessert but I hope to check that out next time.  I can easily see Mixto becoming one of my favorite spots.

You know what? I don't even care if their ice cream is overpriced. It's homemade and delicious and just better than anything else out there. The mint chip has those thin slices of dark chocolate that melt on contact, rather than chew up all waxy-like. And the mint is so refreshingly delicious. My only problem is trying to catch every last drop before it drips off the cone. That's not a bad problem to have.

Wow, this TJ's is a lot bigger than the one I'm used to in Jersey. But being in the city means there are far more people to contend with. Even though I wanted to check out all the merch, I couldn't because I felt weird taking up time and space for more than five seconds in any one spot. But I'm guessing Friday evening around 5pm isn't the best time to swing by.   Backtracking a bit, I knew there was parking but I wasn't sure where. I circled the block twice before I decided that yes, the parking lot with the line into the street was the free lot for Trader Joe's and not a paid parking lot. There was even an attendant at the front to let the next driver know when a spot opened up. We chatted for a bit and he said they mostly do this on weekends and before holidays. Nice.   The selection of produce was far superior to the location I'm familiar with in Marlton. Actually, across the board, options were plentiful in mostly every area. I couldn't find croutons for the life of me, but I did find about three different styles of pistachios.   Check-out was painless even with so many people in the store. It seemed like all the registers were open. A hand basket full of groceries came to something like twenty-five bucks. I was also able to get up to $50 cash back from using my debit card. That's more than any other store I've been to. Next time, I'll try to sneak in during the day to escape the masses.

Last night, I found a new happy hour spot for my rotation. My two friends and I randomly decided to check out The Coffee Bar, and I'm so glad we did. The two baristas/bartenders were very friendly and knew a lot about beer, which is always a great sign. I opted for a glass of red while my cohorts selected their brews.  While checking-in on my Yelp app, I noticed a special offer on the business listing: "$10 beer & lunch, Monday through Friday. Choose any sandwich, wrap or salad" and enjoy a "beer of the day." NICE!   Already planning my return visit, we grabbed the check as last call was made. I was confused to see that my $9 glass of wine was listed as something around $5 on the bill; my friends' beers were also nicely discounted. Then we found out that happy hour runs from 6-8, every weekday night. The three of us left in very good spirits and we all plan to return.

It's the first time you are making dinner for your:  a. lover  b. family  c. domesticated friends d. Yikes, all of the above!  Why chance it by making something from scratch when you can guarantee a great meal from the good people at Bobby Chez!  They have jumbo lump crab cakes (fried and broiled), chicken parm (awesome), chicken pot pie and at least one or two other daily specials.  Side dishes include the always amazing lobster mash, garlic mash, grilled veggies and many others.  Everything is partially cooked so all you have to do is throw the goods in the oven for the recommended cook time listed on the handy little sheet they give you with every order.    And hey, you can always pull a Mrs. Doubtfire and toss all the containers and bag in the outside trash.  Go ahead, tell them you slaved all day.  Chances are they won't believe you, but at least everyone will enjoy their meal!

I wanted to send a friend flowers for a special occasion, but considering she lives nearly 1,000 miles away, I had to turn to Yelp for guidance. Petals by Irene was one of the first results and, since they work with Yelp's delivery platform, my life was made easier as my info was already stored as part of my profile.   In just a few minutes, I selected a pretty, modern arrangement, crafted a personal message, paid for the flowers and moved on with my day. Delivery was $25 which is STEEP, but I really loved the arrangement and was willing to pay for convenience rather than spend more time shopping around.   After placing the order, I received a confirmation. On delivery day, I received a photo of the flowers! This was such a nice surprise that made me feel confident with my purchase. My friend received the flowers as scheduled and said they were beautiful. Very pleased with my experience and would recommend Petals by Irene to anyone ordering from out of town (or in town!).

My first experience at Porta was pretty solid! We were seated by one of the cheerful hostesses in the second room with long, family-style tables. They had a DJ, and between the music and the crowd, it was loud almost to the point of distracting.    We shared a carafe of house red. I thought it was fine, my husband wasn't crazy about it. In fairness our server did tell us that it wasn't her favorite red when we asked, but at $20 for a carafe I couldn't resist. Next time we'll splurge for a bottle.   To start, we shared the housemade mozzarella, meatballs and cavolo nero salad. The mozz and meatballs arrived first and both were really delicious. Next, the salad arrived. It was a huge plate of greens that would have been shareable for up to six people. We brought about half of it home. Finally, we had the 14.5 pizza, which is topped with San Marzano tomatoes, mozzarella, ricotta, and hot soppressata. This pizza had a kick and was really delicious!   We were pretty stuffed after all of this food but we really wanted to try a little bit of everything. I'm very curious to check out a weekend night because I've heard the other Porta locations are known for their dance parties. I'll be back, next time with a group!

It only occurred to me today, as I was walking out of this particular Wells Fargo location after another very pleasant experience, that I should probably write them a review. Without fail, every single time I conduct any sort of business at this branch, I receive a friendly greeting and a genuine "How are you doing today?" I've probably told the tellers here more than they need to know about my day/life just because they are so darn friendly.   My new husband and I had a particularly great experience last Saturday when we were depositing checks and cash from our wedding. The name of the gentleman who helped us is escaping me (I'm so sorry!) but he was so wonderful - setting us up in a private area so we could endorse our checks, and handling all of the transactions with a smile.   Maybe I just go at off hours but I never notice too much of a wait, either. Definitely the best Wells Fargo in the area, as far as I'm concerned.

Admittedly, I've never actually been to El Zarape, but I've now had their tacos al pastor on two occasions: Flavors of the Avenue and the Flavors preview party. The tacos are delicious. The meat is perfect; lightly seared to a crunch but not burnt or too dry. The chopped onions and cilantro meld with some homemade sauces into a medley of Mexican love. These are the best traditional tacos I've had outside of Mexico, but the advantage goes to El Zarape for not throwing me a side of Montezuma's Revenge.
A full service gas station in Philadelphia???   *puts away hand sanitizer*  This Jersey expat is one happy camper. I'm never going to the stations on Broad ever again.

The Living Room is a newish spot for coffee, quick bites, solid background music, wifi, and a nice environment to get some work done. I swung by with some time to kill for a cup of coffee and to get a few emails out. The woman working the counter was super friendly and came around to refill cups since there were only a couple of us in at the time. I enjoyed my coffee and will have to swing back next time I'm in the neighborhood to try the food.

I was thrilled to see Bacchus open on Christmas Eve as I was walking home from the gym and needed a grab-and-go lunch to tide me over before my annual feast of fishes. A blackboard special grabbed my attention: turkey, cooper sharp, bacon and some sort of delicious aioli. These ingredients were served on a toasted multigrain roll that was large enough to share with my husband. The sandwich was delicious!   I noticed loads of people popping in to pick up catering items, and made a mental note for the future. All of the employees were wearing festive hats and were so friendly. I've only picked up a sandwich from Bacchus maybe one other time but this experience definitely put them back on my radar!

If excellent cocktails, toe-tapping tunes from the 50s and beautiful portraits of gorgeous, naked women are not things you enjoy, head elsewhere.  Otherwise, join me at one of the booths along the fabulous vintage red-and-black-velvet wallpaper, and order yourself the bartender's choice. You'll be asked a series of questions regarding how you like your drinks, and a few minutes later you'll be presented with a potion that was tailored to suit your palate.  When the wind is howling and the summer sun seems like a dream, ask about the hot beverages, which aren't listed individually but are certainly offered. Raise that toddy to your lips and let it warm you from the inside out... as if that gorgeous brunette on the far wall didn't get you hot under the collar already!

A toasted whole wheat everything bagel with low-fat vegetable cream cheese and a large cup of L'Aube coffee? The perfect start to my Sunday morning and the fuel I needed to make it through a workout I really wasn't in the mood to start in the first place.   Decent bagels are so few and far between in Philly that South Street Bagels are automatically elevated to four star territory. There are better bagels to be had, but you'll have to travel to Jersey to get them. In the city, this spot corners the market.

I was initially bummed when APO closed its doors, but happy to discover that The Corner remains mostly the same, only with better cocktails and a food menu.   While I haven't tried any of the snacks, I have had several drinks including classic old fashioneds and martinis, plus one or two selections from the specialty cocktails menu. The Mother's Little Helper is like an old fashioned with a pumpkin twist. Pretty delicious.   My family also was quite pleased with the libations on a recent visit, when we all pre-gamed before going to see the Philadelphia Orchestra. The family that cocktails together gets cultured together, I suppose. We'll be back!

My sister and I made our maiden pilgrimage to the POPE on Saturday night after having dinner nearby. First impression? Nicest bar staff in the city. Also, cool dungeon!  From the moment we sat down to the moment we left, every bartender was happy to offer a suggestion, give a taste, have a chat, or whatever else was needed at the moment.   My sister is a light beer swilling girl, but in an attempt to break her out of that repressed world, I asked the bartender to recommend something easy-drinking for her to try. He pulled not one but two tastes, both of which she liked.   The following day, I ran into a friend who told me the POPE has some of the best fried chicken in the city. And since you know your girl loves some fried chicken, I'll be sure to return with the quickness.

I was part of a large group dinner at Spice 28 on Wednesday, and we had a great time. It's hard not to compare a lot of the menu items to the other king of Sichuan in Philadelphia, but Spice 28 is a very close second. And if it's ambiance you're looking for, Spice has the edge.   The great thing about this place is the variety of the menu. Creative selections like wontons with guacamole and tempura lobster add an extra layer to your main dish.   Speaking of the main dishes, the two I tried (dry pepper chicken and hot pot chicken) were so spicy that they bordered on unenjoyable. I could taste no difference in the degree of heat between spice levels two and three; both were hard on my pansy palate. That said, both were executed well, so I'll just opt for the lowest spice level next time. And there will be a next time.   The price was right and I've got a 10% off check-in offer that I plan on utilizing soon. Looking forward to my next round of tastebud ass-kicking.

I found Gene through a search for window cleaning and Yelp did not steer me wrong! I sent a message through the Request a Quote feature and heard back on the same day. Gene and I talked a couple times to figure out the best day for him to come out. He was always easy to get in touch with - something I definitely do not take for granted!   Within a week, Gene was at my house, giving my windows the thorough scrub down they so desperately needed. Insides, outsides, screens and windowsills - everything is spotless. My rooms are noticeably brighter and my house feels so ready for spring! It's also worth mentioning that Gene was courteous and professional - someone I would absolutely recommend to friends and neighbors looking for window cleaning (or power washing and carpet cleaning, since he does those, too). The price was very reasonable as well.   I'm extremely happy with my experience and look forward to calling on Gene again in the future!

I stopped by Bonejour on a whim on Sunday afternoon when I realized I still needed a gift for my sister's dog, Chubbs. The fluffy-haired kitty in the window knew how to work it when we walked in - she immediately started meowing at us and brushing up against her cage in a very cute way. How someone hasn't taken her home already, I have no idea. She almost had me convinced!   Once I broke my gaze I was able to focus on the many toys, treats, outfits (Chubbs has many) and other accessories. I grabbed a couple holiday items and braced myself for the total, which turned out to be very reasonable. The woman working was very helpful in answering questions about whether the things I selected would be appropriate for a small dog. I was even able to get everything gift wrapped in a bag with really cute paw-print tissue paper. One more check on my Christmas list!

I've been to this Crate & Barrel twice and experienced excellent customer service, both times by the same woman (Felecia).   On my recent visit, I picked up a pair of herb scissors (an amazing pair of scissors with about four sets of blades slightly spaced out so you can quickly dice up fresh basil, cilantro, etc. - genius!) as part of my mother's birthday gift. Naturally, I had left my card, bag and tissue paper on the couch at home, and when I mentioned this to Felecia, she promptly wrapped the shears in a nice bag with pretty tissue paper and gave me a little card. She saved me a trip and some money, and I was a happy camper.

Not that I've been to loads and loads of them in my life, but Woody's seems to be a gay bar with training wheels. It's got the tee-hee factor with the name, plus dance parties several nights a week with hordes of young, sweaty twenty-somethings grindin' up on the dance floor to Lady Gaga's latest and greatest.   Personally, I have to be feeling pretty good to not mind being closely surrounded on all sides while in a bar. That is absolutely unavoidable at Woody's on a busy night, so if you're squeamish about tight crowds like me, plan to drink heavily. Drinks are a bit pricey for the size but they're strong so they get points there.   Go in a group, have some fun, dance it up, but don't expect to be blown away. Well, maybe.

I ordered delivery from Al Zaytouna yesterday and went with my usual Mediterranean pick of chicken kebabs. I opted for grilled veggies instead of rice for $2 more. Unfortunately, as I have noticed in the past with orders from this restaurant, my chicken was once again super dry and actually difficult to cut with a knife. All other components of the platter were great. I'm downgrading to three stars since there are other Mediterranean spots that I like a bit more.

I can't believe I'm the first person to write a review for the new Grubhouse at The Bourse! My husband and I dropped by for breakfast. Grubhouse is known for their belly busting breakfast creations, but I like to stick to the lighter side, especially during the week. Still, my breakfast sandwich with turkey bacon, egg and cheese felt like a splurge. It was delicious! The brioche bun was super soft and flavorful and the single slice of American cheese was just right.    My husband had the sausage and pepper hash with egg which was sizeable and very tasty. It should be noted that breakfast at Grubhouse is also a bargain, with the sandwich costing six bucks and the breakfast bowl ringing in at only eight. Coffee is hot and served in a large to-go cup.   I look forward to many more breakfasts here! Pro-tip: They are one of the only vendors in the new Bourse Food Hall that is starting out with Sunday hours.

I attended a baby shower at Maurizio's in Cinnaminson* last Saturday and I have to say, it was quite nice. There were maybe two servers who worked a room of at least 50 women, and they did so with patience and haste.   Bread baskets filled with shiny, hot garlic knots were placed at every table, and dressings for the starter salads were served on the side so everyone had control over how much and what kind. There were three options for lunch: chicken parm with spaghetti, a chicken panini with spinach and provolone and ravioli in tomato cream sauce with mozzarella. I went with the ravioli, which turned out to be the perfect size for an afternoon meal and quite delish. The paninis that my friends ordered were large enough to feed a linebacker (or a pregnant woman, take your pick), but my girls reported their selections to be on the bland side. Coffee was offered immediately after plates were cleared but before dessert, the way it should be.   While I don't find myself dining out in this neck of the woods very often anymore, I would recommend the place for those who do, or as a decent venue alternative when you can't cram everyone into the living room.   *I tried to change the address as this restaurant is not in Burlington, but it has not yet changed over. A friend ended up in Burlington when she looked up the restaurant and put it in her GPS... she was an hour late to the shower.  Wah-wah.

Eat-A-Pita has been on my to-try list for lunch ever since I attended their event for Yelp's In It To Thin It in the spring. So after a meeting nearby this morning, I popped over to grab a pita to go. My wheat pita, stuffed with carved turkey, avocado, lettuce, tomato and sprouts was absolutely delicious. All of the ingredients were plentiful and terrific. The parmesan peppercorn dressing I received on the side was probably the most tasty sandwich topping ever.   I noticed a sign with a list of soups above the register. I'll have to try some next time. Contrary to what I originally thought, Eat-A-Pita is a local establishment, not a big national chain or franchise. Everything is made in-house.   My only regret is that I don't live closer to this awesome lunch option. I'll probably just start creating excuses to visit Midtown Village around lunchtime more often.

I love Martha! While I'm sad we can't take advantage of their adorable outdoor patio right now, I'm very happy we can still swing by for takeout. While running errands in the neighborhood last week, we placed an order for a couple sandwiches, the olives, and some beer to-go. There were several other people picking up orders around the same time, which is always good to see.   The ordering process was easy and included options like sauce on the side, etc. I tried the Al's Toona and it was great! I opted for the sauce on the side and received a dressing, olive tapenade and sliced fresh jalapeños in small containers. This was especially appreciated as I saved half of my sandwich for the next day. The chips and pickles that came along with the sandwich were awesome! My husband got the Gladys, which he enjoyed. The olives were great as well and we enjoyed them as a snack.   Hopefully we'll be able to dine in again sooner than later but it's great to have Martha to-go in the meantime!

Peanuts roasted in-house, four different ways (but no option for salted, darnit).  Pistachios, cashews, jordan almonds, caramel popcorn, trail mix, dried fruits, animal crackers, chocolate and chocolate covered treats, those minty pastel-colored nonpareil thingers and pretty much everything else you can think of from your childhood five and ten can be found in this store.    Nuts to You is the PERFECT place to stop before a baseball game.    And now I want a snack.

A mix of old meets new, Sugarcube is a dream for fashionistas and frugal shoppers alike, male or female. Every item is hand selected by the dedicated staff, and the owners are passionate about their customers just as they are about their business. Anyone searching for a unique piece that no one else will have should consider this store.   In the fall, I coveted an 80s-inspired silky black and white blouse with billowy sleeves and slender, buttoned wrists; the back was cut in a sexy but flattering v-shape. Much to my chagrin, the piece was one of the new items and therefore, out of my price range. I'm still a little tormented by the memory of feeling like a stone cold fox in that top. Next time I have a little extra green to shell out on something special, I'm going back.

I stopped by Bodhi for the first time yesterday afternoon and I have to say, my feelings are inconclusive.   What I loved:  The quaint shop, with bright colors and a country feel.   Cupcakes are from Betty's Speakeasy (which is located in my neighborhood and is a place I frequent).  The barista was friendly and engaging.  In addition to the indoor seating there were a couple tables and chairs outside, where I happily sipped my iced coffee, even if I was on a major angle.  What I'm unsure about:   The coffee. Which is kind of the point here. Something about the taste was just off to me, and yet strangely addictive at the same time.   More visits are required for me to really decide my feelings, so until then, three stars.

"What do you get for the guy who has everything?"  If you find yourself asking this question sometime during the holiday season, or really anytime for that matter, make an appointment at Henry A. Davidsen. Gorgeous ties in every color and pattern fan across a long shelf filled with unique accessories like pocket inserts that have colorful scarves attached and argyle-patterned wood iPad cases. An array of cufflinks are located in a case nearby, along with metal collar stays and wallets. Boardwalk Empire fans will be interested to know that Henry A. Davidsen outfits cast members of the show with their custom bow ties.   Suits and shirts are made on the premises and everyone on the team has a real love and eye for fashion. Price ranges are all listed on the shop's website, so you can get an idea of what you'd be spending before ever walking through the door. As a bonus, the accompanying blog offers up some excellent styling tips for any guy, regardless of budget.  The items in this store come at a price but the quality is second to none. This is the perfect place to shop special gifts for a fashion-conscious man or one interested in transforming his closet from frat-guy to man-about-town.

Just got back from my first experience at Birra and I'll definitely be returning. It smelled like heaven when we walked through the doors around 4:30. The large bar takes up most of the space but tables along the outskirts provide additional seating.   Large plates aren't available until after 5pm but we were there for salad and pizza. The Caesar salad was large enough to share and came tossed in a delicious homemade dressing with a large parmesan crisp. We ordered the Gabagool pizza, with capocollo and arugula. The sauce was on the sweeter side and the meat wasn't as spicy as I was expecting. The toppings were generous and the pizza came straight from the oven. I'd probably switch it up on my next visit and try another type of pie. Looking forward to my next visit!

I met up with a friend at B2 recently and it was my first-ever visit. Really enjoyed the casual vibe and the extra large tables. I could definitely see myself getting some serious work done in that environment.   The coffee tasted great and it was strong. I was caffeine-buzzing all day long off of my large cup. I didn't have any food and I think the menu is pretty basic, but a toasting everything bagel smelled terrific, and the current main photo of the cucumber and goat cheese sandwich looks great. I'll be making a return trip soon.

After a meeting in the area, Maggie L and I decided to hit Pod for lunch. We started with the chicken lettuce wraps, which were really great and also very filling for two people. I wanted a martini but considered my workload and ordered an unsweetened iced tea, instead. It was super flavorful and served with a slice of orange - very nice!   Next up were: the jumbo lump California roll, a spicy tuna roll topped with rock shrimp, and a spicy yellowtail roll with fresh jalapeño slices (my favorite of the three for its lightness and extra heat!). I was very happy that all of the rolls were well balanced (not overly sauced) and easy to eat (not too big, not falling apart). This was the perfect amount of food for two fairly hungry people. If you're not feeling as hungry, the lettuce wraps and two rolls could suffice.   Our server was friendly and helpful yet a little slow for lunch. But I enjoyed my experience so much that I definitely wanted to bump up my rating to a more appropriate four stars!

As far as Panera locations go, I thought this one was okay. I didn't like it as much as the location I frequent most in Delran. I did the You Pick Two combo with French onion soup (I really like their version because it's not too heavy but still delicious) and the roasted turkey and avocado BLT which was super boring. The tomato was flavorless and the applewood smoked bacon was very reminiscent of microwave bacon. But it was one of the healthier options on the menu, without the mayo.   I do really love the Panera card because I seem to rack up rewards pretty quickly. As far as chain breakfast/lunch spots go, I'm a fan.

The bright colors of Honest Tom's Taco Shop pop from the grays, browns, bricks and stones that make up the rest of the landscape of 44th Street in West Philly. Inside, a lone table and some counter seating are available, but I wouldn't bet on free seats given the modest size of what will undoubtedly become a popular breakfast, lunch and dinner destination.   Since I had only tried Tom's breakfast tacos on one other occasion (and loved them), I decided to check out a chicken burrito on my first of what will probably be many visits. We beat a small rush by mere seconds and waited patiently at the counter for our food, which was up pretty quickly. My burrito was basic and yet really satisfying. There was more than enough chicken, plus rice, black beans, cheddar and guacamole. I would have dug a little sour cream but honestly, it wasn't needed. Instead, I doused the thing in that same delicious hot sauce that I had used for my breakfast tacos. I need a bottle of that for my house to add to the growing hot sauce collection.   The menu is small but that's okay for a couple reasons. One, they just opened. Two, this isn't fine dining Mexican or a place that you are going to enjoy a long and leisurely meal. It's a quick, satisfying option. And six or eight bucks for lunch is definitely okay with me. I'm looking forward to my next visit and seeing the business settle in.

Some friends and I had a pretty awesome Sunday Funday at The Industry yesterday. I was quite happy to be reunited with the Ghost of Mary, one of my favorite spin-offs of a Bloody Mary that I had long missed since the closing of Swift Half.
