After several of those, our table decided it was time to share the Mummer's Punch. The serving suggestion is for 4-6 people, and we had three with two latecomers. There was more than enough for everyone.   Two people at our table were at The Industry long enough for brunch and dinner. I heard good things about brunch but can only report on dinner. The burger with bacon was good, not great. I'm not going out of my way for it, but it is a decent option. The pickle mayo (which I asked for on the side) provided a nice dipper for the fries. A lot of the menu consists of items for the more adventurous palate (sweetbreads, pig ears, bone marrow, lamb neck, etc.). I am most definitely not in that category but there were still plenty of things to choose from. I'm interested in trying the porchetta sandwich and the fried green tomatoes.  Our servers were great and very attentive throughout our long stay. The music selection was awesome (although the Internet jukebox provided for some say in the matter - not complaining at all, just an observation). I'm looking forward to my next visit.

On opening weekend, a certain amount of confusion and back-up should be expected. My boyfriend and I heard the news that entry was delayed by a couple hours. We were bummed, but accepting of the fact that we would be able to receive free tickets to attend at a later date. Since we were in the area anyway, we decided to walk over just to see if anything had changed from the earlier reports. Luckily, we picked the right time because we were able to get in only a half hour after our original appointment time. While we waited, a glass of wine and some live jazz helped pass the time.   Once inside the collection, it was clear that we wouldn't be able to take everything in during the designated hour. But what we did see was absolutely incredible. And I'm pretty sure my buzz from the wine (and okay, the beers we had at a bar nearby before that) added to our enjoyment. We'll definitely return once the initial excitement wears off so that we can enjoy the works with less of a crowd. But in the meantime, a walk around the gorgeous grounds (that are actually still in-process) isn't out of the question.

In my experience, the city version of a national store is usually lacking. I'll pick the 'burbs versions of Target, Lowe's, etc. any day. But I have to give it up to the Philadelphia Pier 1, because it's not half bad.   From small pieces of accent furniture to summer patio necessities, I've done my fair share of credit card swiping at this location. I especially love that you can see online if an item is available for pickup at the store. You can often have items shipped in for store pick-up for no extra charge, as well.   Check out the sales racks near the register, where there are often really cute stationery options and other office items for a steal!

My girlfriends and I ordered dinner from Luigi's one weeknight last week. They ordered a portabella mushroom pizza with whole wheat crust and a salad, and I went with a grilled chicken Caesar salad with tomatoes and dressing on the side. Everything arrived as requested, with extra pieces of grilled garlic bread for everyone.   Delivery was very fast. If I find out that they deliver to my neighborhood I'd definitely give them a try again.

Lately, it seems every time I use Pacifico Valet, I find myself waiting on the airport island with my luggage, tapping my foot and becoming increasingly aggravated as time ticks by. 15 minutes, 20 minutes, 25 minutes...   It wasn't always this way. When I first started using Pacifico, I would be swiftly dropped off at the airport in my own comfy car, and after I returned and retrieved my luggage, I'd give a call over and be picked up in ten minutes flat, maybe a couple minutes more during peak times. Easy peasy.  At 6:30 am this morning I stood in the freezing cold, waiting to be picked up, as snow flakes danced around me. The airport was dead. There was no way I would have to wait long. But after 25 minutes of waiting for my pick-up, I finally had to pop the collar on my wool coat for warmth. Yep, I was that cold. The driver blamed my icy windows for the delay. In fairness, my defrosters have been finicky so perhaps the windshield took longer to clear. However, why bother giving flight information at all if my car wasn't going to be prepared in advance?  On another trip last summer, I was returning from Mexico and had a bad case of traveler's flu. If you have ever been sick in this way, I don't have to tell you: every minute counts. Unfortunately, my crew and I were left waiting and waiting for my car to finally round the bend and come into sight.    I don't want to wait anymore. What's the point of using this service and giving flight times and all the rest when I end up being the last girl standing at the carpool lane?   Pacifico isn't a bad option; I have always been treated nicely and have gotten to the airport quickly, but providing a swift getaway after a long flight doesn't seem to be a priority anymore. For me, that's a deal breaker.

I had the unfortunate opportunity to go back to Champps for a friend's birthday.  The bathrooms seemed cleaner this time (although I lucked out on door #1 so who knows what was behind doors 2 through 5) but the experience as a whole managed to bring the place down to a one-star level.  Our server was terrible.  It was crowded and we had a big party, but the guy would take drink orders from two people and then scurry off, completely ignoring the other people at the table.  It took him twenty minutes to tell me that the wine I wanted wasn't available and another ten to bring me something else, which I didn't like (not his fault, I know, but frustrating nonetheless).  I flagged down a manager and calmly requested that he exchange my glass of wine for a 22 ounce beer (bigger is always better, but especially when you have to wait a year for your next drink). I made it clear that I was asking him and not our server because I didn't want to wait another twenty minutes for my first drink.  Perhaps a little harsh to get the manager involved, but when I spotted my rejected wine on our bill at the end of our visit, I felt it was even more justified.  The next time my friends want to hit this place up, I will NOT take it like a "champ" but will instead meet them at the after-party.  Harumph!

After driving around Manayunk for a good hour trying to find parking during the Arts Festival, I was feeling pretty hangry (hungry +cranky = hangry).  My group of three decided to hit up the brew pub since we know the food is decent and it was right in front of us when we finally hit Main Street.  Oh how I wish we had kept on walking.    We entered the restaurant and, despite a plethora of open tables, the hostess had to "get something ready" for us (did they not get the memo about the annual arts festival that would be taking place all weekend?).  We were eventually seated against a half-wall, very close to the tables that were backed up to us.  Table space was tight, and I threw my purse on the back of my chair.    We ordered nachos which were delish but kind of small considering they were $12.  The brewery's own Bohemian Blonde and Whistle Whetting Wheat went down pretty damn easy but could have been a little colder.  Perhaps it was right about the time of my second beer when the shady characters seated behind me ganked my wallet right out of my purse.    Or maybe they waited for our main course.  We would have been easily distracted as the food didn't come out for a good long time and we were all pretty focused when it finally appeared.  My friend and I each got salads that were good but again on the small side.  My bf had a margarita pizza that he wasn't overly impressed with.    It was at this point that we decided to cut our losses and get the check, which after about two drinks each and the aforementioned fare, came to $80something dollars (not including tip).  Kind of hefty for a lunch that didn't leave anyone feeling very full or very buzzed.  Reaching for my purse, I knew something was wrong when it felt light.  A missing Coach wallet that included identification, methods of payment and various membership cards will do that.    Also missing was the couple who was previously seated at the table behind us.  According to their server, they had soup and then paid their check in cash... probably my cash.  Fuckers.  I wonder; at what point in their dating history did they discover their shared love of soup and stealing?    I know I can't fault the brewery for the actions taken by two assholes.  That wouldn't be fair.  But I can fault them for their unprepared staff on a big weekend, slow service and small plates with large price tags.  The food is decent for sure, but there are a million other places on Main Street that I'd rather check out in the future.  P.S. To the people who stole my wallet: I know you can't use my debit or credit cards because I cancelled them immediately (sorry about that), but if you plan on doing any shoe shopping in the near future, could you do it at DSW and use my membership card?  I get $10 gift certificates mailed to me for every few purchases.  Thanks!

I enjoyed my first Nom Nom Bowl experience! This is an order-by-screen situation so it's probably wise to consult the menu first. I ordered the goma tuna poke bowl and thought everything about it was delicious. I loved all the ingredients (even if I wasn't totally sure what all of them were) and the slightly spicy kick was a pleasant surprise.   I do think a build-your-own bowl option would be a nice addition to the menu, since I sometimes like to customize my own. Regardless, I definitely see myself enjoying many more bowls in the future!

I've been a Moorestown Mall shopper since my allowance days. This was the mall of choice during my grade school years, when Spencers, Time Out, the food court and movie theater were the only things that mattered.  As an adult, the variety of stores is limited, but less crowds makes for better parking and getting in and out and on your way quickly. This isn't the mall I'd choose if I were doing a major shopping trip, but if I just needed a basic top or pair of shoes or something in a cinch, it would do the trick. I'm a fan of Lord and Taylor for those items. And after all these years, the food court is still pretty decent.

I am one lucky lady with all the men in my life giving me flowers lately! Recently, I was gifted with a lovely arrangement from my friend, Dan F. Almost a full week later, the blooms are still sprightly and holding it down on my windowsill (see pic, aerial view).   I'm sure all the other sills in the 'hood are jealous, and they should be. Not all of them are fortunate enough to hold fresh, herbal greenery mixed with blossoms boasting the most amazingly accented petals.   Well. The secret's out now that the array is from Poppy. So all those green-eyed sills can just go get their own pretty mix. After all, imitation is the sincerest form of flattery.

I don't get down to The Industry as often as I'd like. This is one of the most laid-back, chill places to drink or grab a bite in the city. Worth a special mention is the service, which is always very friendly and accommodating. I really believe servers at The Industry stand out from the pack when compared with other restaurants of similar style. The environment is fun and the music is always varied and awesome.  The drinks are where it's at. The Ghost of Mary is one of my favorite cocktails ever and I will sing its praises to anyone interested in listening. The Mummer's Punch is a good time, and the beer list is great. Happy hour specials are on point.  I'm not as enthusiastic about the food as I am the drinks but there is still a lot left for me to try. I did really enjoy the wedge salad on my recent visit. I was dying to try the banana pound cake but there wasn't room for dessert. Instead, I went with a double espresso and it was so smooth and well-flavored that I ordered another. Often, I order espressos to get my caffeine fix. I got that, plus I actually really enjoyed the espresso itself. Looking forward to my next visit sooner rather than later.

Two girlfriends from high school and I had a mini reunion last night at Lo Bianco.  When I walked in, the restaurant was empty and I was instructed to choose any table, so I selected one by the window.  The décor was very nice, although the ceilings reminded me of an office building.  I probably would not have noticed this normally, but since I was the only person in the restaurant I had a chance to really take in my surroundings.    When my friends arrived, our server poured our wine and dropped off large glasses of water and warm rolls.  She informed us that there were no specials, and I soon found out why.  The restaurant remained empty, except for our table, through the entire night.  While it was nice having the place to ourselves, I wondered if the freshness of our meal would be compromised, as there was not a constant flow of patrons through the evening.  For my first course, I had a grilled romaine salad, with pancetta, goat cheese and pesto vinaigrette.  It was definitely different from any other salad I have had in the past.  The smokiness of the grilled romaine reminded me of a steak dinner.  While I enjoyed it, I'm not sure that it would be my first choice again in the future.    My entrée was a braised beef short rib with yakitori glaze and whipped potatoes.  It was fantastic.  The beef was so tender it did not even require a knife, and the flavor of the glaze was absorbed all the way through.  The potatoes were buttery and sinful, as all good mashed potatoes are.    One friend ordered the bouillabaisse, which looked and tasted great (I tried a mussel).  However, many if not all of the clams in the dish were not open--NEVER a good sign when it comes to shellfish.    For dessert, the three of us shared a chocolate cake that had the consistency of fudge and that was topped with whipped cream, as well as a lemon pound cake, also topped with whipped cream and berries.  Both were very rich and neither were finished, but not for a lack of trying.    I would certainly return to this restaurant in the future, but most likely on a weekend night when the scene is livelier.  I do hope they thrive because the food and service were wonderful (reluctant clams excluded), and it's always nice having another option besides Italian pasta in the neighborhood.

I was back at Cork for a low-key night on Thanksgiving eve. The bar was pretty crowded for a restaurant-- not sure if it was because of the "biggest bar night of the year" thing or because Wednesday is 80s night. They were playing 80s tunes and had about ten 80s-inspired cocktails for $5.50 (similar to the ones featured at Alfa). We were seated at a booth near the bar, but you had to be at the bar to get the specials. We weren't looking to have any fruity drinks so it wasn't a big deal.   Our server, Marissa, had waited on me once before so I knew she was good. She was friendly and always around when we needed a new round of drinks.   Speaking of the drinks, Cork has one of the best beer menus I have seen on this side of the bridge. Golden Monkey, a winter version of La Chouffe and two varieties of Chimay stood out amongst many others. Yeah, they are a little pricey, but you can also get your buzz on after only one or two (or at least, I can)!   The Mediterranean plate was tasty as usual, as was the tomato pizza. Curiously, there was no tomato sauce on the pizza, just a pesto and olive oil base. Probably not very diet-friendly but considering the smorgasbord of Thanksgiving food the following day, I don't think it really mattered.

Fergie's is a great Irish pub that I only end up at every once in a while, but every time I do, I'm happy. Recently, I went for a meet-the-brewer event. The subject brew was Allagash, and every style I tried tasted super fresh and went down like water.   Now that the kitchen is being run by Mark Coates of Bebe's BBQ, I'm anxious to go back for dinner one night. I was lucky enough to sample a few bites of brisket, and the smoke flavor was off the charts. I can't wait to return with a full appetite and unleash my inner carnivore.

YES! Thank you, Zoe's Kitchen, for bringing fast-casual Mediterranean food to South Jersey! I'd seen the positive reviews from Yelpers and made a mental note to swing by the next time I was in the area. That happened today while I was running errands and I realized I had to figure something out for dinner.   The woman behind the counter could not have been nicer. She told me all about the menu and let me know that everything was completely customizable. I'm doing this low carb thing currently (I know... I'll be back on pizza in no time), so I went with the chicken skewer dinner which comes with a small Greek salad and rice pilaf. I subbed in hummus and cucumbers in exchange for the rice pilaf, and I nixed the pita (sad times). My to-go order was ready in mere minutes and I was out the door for a little over ten bucks.   I had a couple other errands to run before I was able to dig in, so by the time I got home I had no idea what state I'd find my dinner. To my pleasant surprise, everything was packaged neatly and held up well. The dressing for the salad was served on the side and the hummus was in its own cup. Same with the cucumbers. Despite the lag time, the food was delicious!   I am totally impressed, Zoe. See you again soon!

While I feel really bad about removing a couple stars from 11th Street, it has to be done. The guys who work there are the sweetest, and I don't doubt that they know their way around cars, but on my recent visit, I was told that my check engine light was on for something really minor and it was turned off and I went on my merry way.   When the light came back on a few weeks later, I took the car to my dealership and found out that my catalytic converter needed replacing. This is no cheap affair, but had it not been replaced, the engine could have blown, which would have been a catalytic catastrophe on my savings.  The guys at 11th Street were spot on about the heater's issues, so I'll give them that, although the temporary fix they finagled still left me on the receiving end of cold air after a day or so.   As much as I hate shelling my hard-earned money over to the dealership, at least I know my car is safe and the issues were addressed appropriately.

We had such a great experience at Birra last night that I just wanted to give a little update. After being seated at a nearby pizza restaurant and being ignored for a solid five minutes or so, we decided to cut our losses and head to Birra. I am so glad we did! Our server was totally great from the second we sat down.   We ordered the meatball appetizer and were told it would take about fifteen minutes to prepare. It ended up being a little longer, which wasn't a huge deal, but our server said that she took care of a round of our drinks to make up for it. What a pleasant surprise! I thought the meatballs were well worth the wait, but this was a nice gesture all the same. And as for those glasses of wine, if you order two of the same, they will bring over a half carafe, which easily provides for about three glasses total. I am a fan.

This is just like South Philly Paesano's, only a little rougher around the edges. Everything is delicious... As if there was any question. Call ahead if you want to skip the borderline risqué chatter from the cooks.

A friend and I met for lunch at Tria Taproom recently and I was shocked to find the place totally empty. So if, like me, you've had trouble getting in there on a Saturday night because of the crowds, check them out for lunch if you can!   I started with a glass of iced tea (definitely looking to getting back there for wine, however) and it was really delicious. Fresh-brewed and with some flavor. My friend and I ordered several plates to share. The octopus was tender and tasted great and the cobb salad was awesome. Plenty of thick-cut bacon and gorgonzola. I had the three cheese flatbread as well and really enjoyed it. There were nice slices of tomato on top that added just the right amount of acidity.   Really looking forward to more visits at Tria Taproom!

In terms of honeygrow experiences, this one was just okay. The ordering process was straightforward and easy as always, and there was a lot of seating in this particular location. I was in the mood for something different from my usual salad order. I had tried the red coconut curry before at an event so decided to go with that.   It took a while for the order to come up but since I was getting something hot instead of a salad, that was fine. When my name was called, I had to ask for a cup and the extra slice of bread that I ordered. I feel like this happens a lot at honeygrow; something often tends to be missing from the final order (occasionally, it's the salad dressing, which is super annoying when you get it all the way home!).   My noodles were so lightly dressed there was barely any flavor. I was glad I added on crunchy onions at the last minute, otherwise there woudn't have been much taste at all.   I really like honeygrow overall and especially their mission to use high-quality ingredients, but the experiences can be hit or miss.

What? I've never reviewed Han Dynasty? It's only one of my favorite restaurants in the city, and THE destination for Sichuan cuisine. That's right, Sichuan. This is not your standard Chinese spot. "Chinese food" is in the mall, at the food court. The cooking at Han Dynasty (aka, handy nasty) is on another planet, in another galaxy far, far away, where there are no snowmageddons or other undesirables. Only perfection.  That said, go with an open mind. I personally don't get down with tripe or tendons or rabbit or what-have-you, but I do enjoy trying new flavors and combinations that are unexpected and different. Close-minded, stubborn folks need not bother.  Take last night, for example. My boyfriend and I were in the middle of our first course, spicy dan dan noodles with crumbled sausage and crunchy cucumbers in garlic chili oil. We hear the gentleman behind us tell the waiter he would like fried rice for dinner. The waiter makes a joke about how fried rice is on the kids' menu. The waiter returns to the kitchen and a few minutes pass before Han makes his way to the table. An awkward (but hilarious, to our eavesdropping ears) conversation ensues with Han explaining that the restaurant serves authentic Chinese, and that fried rice is only available for children.   I think the guy eventually got his fried rice, but I was too busy focusing on my own perfectly sticky white rice with dry fry pork to notice or care. Despite being deliriously happy with my meal, I was already taking notes on what to order next time as I scoped out the neighboring diners' plates. Next up: crispy rice with shrimp and double cooked chicken with chili oil and black bean sauce.

Sugar Bar Salon is a brand new, gorgeous salon in Rittenhouse. I went for a sugaring treatment on their opening day and was really impressed by the space and my service.   There's a super cute wine bar and some really pretty spaces that will be perfect for hosting little parties in the future. The service room I was in was spotless, comfortable, and roomy enough for a tall girl like myself; that hasn't always been the case at other salons I have visited.   Due to the Covid shutdowns, it had been a while since my last sugaring service and I was nervous. But my esthetician was an absolute pro and made the entire process as quick as possible. It wasn't without pain but I am optimistic that my next appointment will be even smoother. It's also worth noting that sugaring doesn't leave me with any residual pain which is great. Once my service was over I went about my day and that was that!   Pricing is competitive with other popular salons in the city and Sugar Bar happens to be more convenient to my house than my previous salon, so it's a no brainer for me. Cheers to this lovely new local business!

Van saved my eyebrows from extreme unibrow territory when I blew through the doors of 4 Sisters yesterday afternoon. After a struggle with the meter outside, which wouldn't take my singles OR credit cards (what else is new, PPA?), I plopped in two quarters and had fifteen minutes to get in and get out.   The salon was clean and cute - I was surprised that I had never been there before. Van introduced herself and brought me to the private room, where in less than five minutes, my brows were shaped and looking good.   I'll definitely give 4 Sisters a look the next time I need a quickie mani or pedi as well.

I'm starting to realize I've got a thing for locally-owned neighborhood grocery stores. Walking into Riverwinds Produce over the weekend, I realized my ideal neighborhood grocery exists, even if it's located on the opposite side of the city from where I live!   This place has everything! From a nice selection of fresh produce to nearly every Philly-made baked good, snack, or beverage. We stopped in to stock up on Movement Labs' Yerba Maté, after learning it's no longer in production (wah!). We ended up finding several other items to get us through the week ahead, plus a friendly staff who were all happy to help. I'll be back the next time, and probably every time, I'm in Fishtown!

After securing tickets for a 10 p.m. flick at "the movie theater formerly known as the Ritz," we set off to find a BYO in the area.  Taking chances with random restaurants is not really my favorite thing to do, since dining out gets expensive and you want to have a good experience when you do get out.  All worries were cast aside when we realized how many people in the restaurant were speaking Italian.  Olive Garden, this was not!  We ordered the warm buffalo mozzarella app, a special.  It was served with basil, tomatoes, grilled zucchini and a balsamic reduction.  It went perfectly with the crusty bread on our table.    I asked our server if wheat pasta was available and was so happy to find out that it was.  Nothing beats fresh pasta but when I can get it in the wheat variety, I'm a very happy girl.  I ended up with wheat penne and vodka sauce, which was to-die.  My date had chicken topped with roasted red peppers and served alongside veggies and potatoes.  The chicken was so flavorful and very tender.  The dessert tray looked phenomenal and we ended up with a chocolate mousse that was served on top of chocolate cake and topped with fresh whipped cream~ all encased in a circular wall of dark chocolate.  It's a good thing I was already pretty full, or things could have easily gotten ugly with a battle of forks over this dessert.  It was fantastic.    Like Remmie, my one and only complaint about the restaurant is the decor.  There is none.  This place clearly runs a good business and I think it would be even better if they just updated their dining rooms and repainted the bathrooms, which were really beat.  However, I'm happy to turn a blind eye for Italian food this amazing!

I've always been a fan of Peter McAndrews' restaurants and I'm really happy to see Modo Mio reinvented in Queen Village. My husband and I went with his parents for dinner last week. The restaurant was bustling and it was quite loud, but a good atmosphere.  Modo Mio Taverna has a full bar and pretty extensive wine list. Our server made a couple recommendations and they were spot on for what I ordered.  We shared a few plates to start: mozzarella en carozza, arancini, beet salad (a special, I think). I don't like beets but I was able to avoid them and still really enjoy the salad. We all loved the mozzarella dish which had great flavor and was pretty hearty for a starter. The arancini were okay; I'd probably try something different next time. Despite three starters and each person ordering their own entree, our server still tried to upsell us a bit which I always find really irritating.   I didn't try the other mains (gnocchi alla romana, the braciole, and a ravioli special) but I believe I had the winner of the night, regardless. The melanzane stufato, stuffed eggplant with tomato sauce and ricotta, was delicious! It had every bit of the zesty tomato taste I wanted but without any meat. It was large enough to bring home leftovers for lunch the next day.   For dessert, we shared the tiramisu (different from traditional tiramisu but delicious!) and my dining companions shared a cannoli. If you've never been to one of McAndrews' restaurants before, know that you won't be eating typical Italian. This is Italian food jacked up with bold flavors and interesting ingredients. Looking forward to future visits!

I absolutely loved Paperdolls Boutique! It was so much larger than most boutique shops and had a great array of clothing, from casual to dressy. I tried on an armful of items and found several pieces that I could have taken home. In the end, I went with a long skirt and a cute top. Neither piece was on sale but I liked them both so much that I didn't care.   The shop gals were friendly and helpful. There are also tons of accessories and small gift items. Great place to shop in St. Louis!

I popped into this Snap Kitchen location yesterday to stock up on meals for the week. The layout is exactly like the one in Old City, and there were friendly employees ready to answer any questions I had.   From this round of goods I've so far tried the curried chicken salad (very flavorful and perfect for a healthy, high-protein snack), the goat cheese and tomato tart, which was excellent, and the chimichurri beef. After trying several of the medium-sized entrees, the beef was easily the heartiest and most filling.   Snap might seem pricey, but when I compare it to the amount of ordering out I generally do during the week, it all evens out. I definitely feel like my meals are way healthier when I buy in advance for the week, instead of waiting until 2pm day-of and making terrible choices because I'm too hungry to think straight.  Snap, I am picking up what you're putting down.

I appreciate local businesses and water ice is a very welcome seasonal treat born out of Philadelphia. However, I wasn't super impressed by my experience at Pop's. The young woman working the window was a little curt and my order was incorrect. When I realized this and went back over to the window, I was given a brand new full-size replacement, no questions asked. That was nice.   The water ice itself was extra watery and the flavor was kind of bland (I had cherry and lemon). Maybe we stopped by on an off day. I'd give it another shot if I was in the area. Also, they sell soft pretzels and there's nothing like a water ice and soft pretzel combo!

I don't understand the obsession with this place.  Yes, they have a great beer selection.  So do many other establishments in the city.  The food is okay but is it worth having to wait an hour and change in the overcrowded aisle next to the bar for a table at 10 p.m. on a Friday?  Hell to the no.    The duck spring rolls are bland compared to others I've tasted in the city (Pearl and XIX) and the Monk's Burger is like a red-headed stepchild next to the Good Dog's Good Dog Burger.  Speaking of which, who orders a burger and thinks, "what I really want on the side is a nice, dainty pile of spring mix salad?!"  It's like they trick you into ordering the fries because who really eats a burger without fries?  Infuriating.  I'd go back if I were outnumbered in a group of Monk's devotees, but not by my own free will.

NEVER AGAIN!!!  Actually, I'm pretty sure I said those exact words several years ago when I was last at Mad River.  However, it was my sister's 23rd birthday, so I had to suck it up and go with the program. We arrived around 9 or so on Saturday night, thinking the bar would be relatively empty since the Phils game was postponed.  Not so much.  There was a Penn State alumni event going on, so the place was packed and we had to wait in line in the rain.  We should have known right then and there to cut our losses and go elsewhere.  Once inside, the bar was so packed with people that I started planning out a fire escape plan.  It was nearly impossible to get anywhere near the front bar, so we made our way to the back, where there was more room.  Only thing was, the floor was covered with puddles of beer, plates, napkins and food.  What the hell happened before we got there? Employees were trying to clean up the mess but it was a lost cause.  Nearby, I witnessed a guy spitting on the floor. I started to pray, knowing that only a stronger force than myself could get me through this night.  The $2 domestics that were being featured were actually plastic cups that were filled 60% of the way if we were lucky.  After a while, the back bar ran out of draught beer completely so the only option was to either pay for bottles or attempt to get to the front bar without getting felt up by every drunk guy in the place along the way.  I still can't believe we each paid $5 to get in.  The stamp should have said "sucker" because that's exactly what paying for anything in that dump made me feel like.

What an adorable old-timey ice cream shop! How my very first visit occurred just two nights ago, after the majority of my adulthood has been spent hanging out in the city, I don't know.  My small dish of coffee ice cream topped with homemade hot fudge was one of the best experiences in ice cream I've ever known. I had no idea what real hot fudge was before tasting it at Franklin Fountain. Smooth, buttery, chocolate - that's what.   The prices are steep but the quality was so high that I'd gladly fork over my hard-earned cash. This could seriously become an addiction.

Decent local bar, good for catching the game and some snacks. The kitchen is open late every day, which is something that isn't always easy to find. The beer selection is pretty solid.   Friends and I stopped in on Thursday night for some beers and snacks. We ordered cheese fries, cheesesteak egg rolls and a chicken quesadilla. The food was good enough for late night munchies, but I probably wouldn't seek out New Wave for a regular meal. That said, I'd be fine with popping in while in the neighborhood to view a game and enjoy a cold one.

Cute coffee shop which would serve as an excellent place to read a book, have a meeting or get some work done. I opted for a cup of the cold brew on nitro which was smooth and delicious and required less cream than I'd normally put in my coffee.   My meeting took place on one of the comfortable couches. Afterwards, I moved myself to a table in an effort to get some work done. Unfortunately, the wifi was down so I ended up having to leave for another spot, but I'm looking forward to returning for either a meeting or just a quiet, cool place to work.

McMillan's is probably the greatest bakery ever.  A friend of mine is so obsessed with their cakes that he will use any and every excuse to make a stop.  Rumors of the infamous cream donuts at McMillan's made their way to me when my coworkers discovered my weakness.  I didn't believe the hype, opting to stick with my old standby, Dunkin Donuts' kreme-filled chocolate-frosted (occasionally with sprinkles) donut, on the rare occasion that I started my day with such an indulgence.  One day, a visitor to our office brought in a huge bakery box filled with deliciousness from McMillan's.  There were several cream-filled donuts and I think I visualized my name written in the powdered sugar on one of them.  It was love at first bite.    I still have love for ya, Dunkin Donuts, but I hope you don't mind being the side piece for now on.

G's, you've still got it!   My sister and I brought my dad to Giumarello's on Wednesday evening for a belated Father's Day outing. Despite the rainy night, we opted to sit outside under the covered patio since it was much brighter outside than inside. The bar area at Giumarello's is dark and classic, but the patio is where I want to be during the summer months. We were in good company - the outside bar was already packed and most tables were taken by 5:30!   There is a gigantic list of reduced-price apps and all drinks are $1 off for happy hour. Wednesdays also feature buck-a-shuck oysters and clams, plus half off bottles of wine under $75. Quite the deal!   Our server dropped off a gigantic bread basket which looked incredible, but I saved my cals for the delicious clams in white wine sauce, plus a Caesar salad with crab and shrimp. For $20, that's a pricey salad, but there was so much seafood that I was more than okay with it.   Giumarello's is such a classic South Jersey spot, and it had been way too long since my last visit. Definitely not going to make that mistake again; I'll be back this summer for sure!

Nick's is a South Philly dive with cheap domestics and ultra delicious roast beef sandwiches and delightfully greasy, crispy fries. Sports play on the TVs over the bar.    Don't expect coddling of any kind from the servers; they are rushing around and their only mission is to deliver the goods and get you out of those seats as quickly as possible. On a recent visit, our group stood awkwardly by the door for ages without being acknowledged by anyone. Eventually, we made our way to the bar and took over a couple high top tables. In the bar area, you can order food and drinks directly from the bartender, which was just fine with us.  Everyone in our crew was in agreement that the sandwiches hit the spot. We shared a couple orders of the gravy fries which were sinfully fantastic. Paul R hit the nail on the head when he said it's a great spot to bring friends from out of town. I can't wait to go back for another visit, myself.

Second attempt at Spice 28: delivery via Dining In. An order of dan dan noodles, spicy cucumbers, dry pepper chicken and hot sauce style chicken came to just over sixty bucks, including a tip for the driver. All I could think was that dinner had better be good, for the price of dining out. I will say that the delivery time was on point, and only about forty-five minutes, which is on the low end for Philly. Props for that.    The food was good, but I think the prices are a bit steep, especially for take-out. I remember thinking everything was such a steal when I dined in the restaurant. I'm wondering if that's just because I went with a huge group and we shared a bunch of plates? Either way, I liked our second meal from Spice 28 but I didn't love it as much as that first time. The hot sauce style chicken was not really my thing (intense peppercorn flavor in the sauce but no breading or crispness to the chicken), though I really enjoyed the dry pepper style chicken. It's hard to know what to order because the menu descriptions list the ingredients but not really anything about the preparation or cooking style. That would really help.   The dan dan noodles were great, but the portion size was definitely smaller than Han's. Same with the spicy cucumbers. Sorry to compare the two yet again in this review but I feel like it's unavoidable.   While I wish the prices for delivery were a little lower, I'd still probably order from Spice 28 again. I'm also looking forward to getting back to the restaurant sometime.

Months ago, after a bachelorette party filled with copious amounts of alcohol, exotic male dancers, pole dancing contests and a regretful late night stop at Public House, I awoke the next morning and found two cards in my possession, each for $50 off any service at Bernard's salon.  Apparently, I had received them at Club Risque, but the reasoning behind why is still unknown.  Your guess is as good as mine.  Nevertheless, I somewhat forgot about the cards until I was flipping through Philadelphia Magazine last week.  The Summer Fun Guide feature had a blurb about spa services, and Bernard's Golden Pedicure was highlighted.  I booked my appointment at once!    When I got to the salon, the receptionists were friendly and my nail tech, Gina, came out to get me a few minutes after I arrived.  She set me up in a chair and let me relax for a bit before the service.  The pedi itself was filled with scrubs and creams galore, each smelling and feeling more luxurious than the last.    I have very sensitive skin and I mentioned this up front, but somehow I still ended up with a small knick anyway.  Minus one star.  Also, the scrub part was a teeny bit painful in a hurts-so-good kind of way, but I was reminded of a saying in my family that has been handed down from generations of women, "You must suffer to be beautiful."  I looked down at my legs and I could practically see my reflection, they were so smooth and shiny.  Well worth the "suffering!"  I probably wouldn't spend $60 of my hard earned cash on this exact pedi again, but for ten smackers plus tip, I could not be happier.  My toes look far better than they do at my regular pedi joint, so there is something to be said about salon quality services.  I will likely return, probably for a regular pedi and definitely with Gina!

This movie theater and I go way back. It used to be part of the Ritz group and it always had a very arty, coffee house vibe.   Now, it's part of the AMC fam so the feel has changed a bit. While the concessions are solid, the rest of the theater is not on par with other area AMCs that have been upgraded.   Still, this is one of the better options in South Jersey for catching a flick, and one of my preferred theaters if I'm rolling solo. Fingers crossed for some upgrades!

Turns out, my car isn't going to spontaneously combust as I'm driving back and forth across the Ben Franklin! So said Frank of 11th Street Auto Repair, when I brought my car to him last week. My issues were: check engine light on, cold air blowing out of the heater, suspicious noise coming from somewhere near the front of the ride.   My check engine light was triggered by something that was basically a non-factor, so that was turned off. The noise was something minor that can be rectified after the winter, when the snow/ice/pothole season ends for good (the likely trigger for the noise to begin with). Lastly, my heater was temporarily fixed, but the bad news is, I'll have to replace a part with the actual dealer, which will be costly. However, the temporary fix will get me through until I'm ready to part with the chunk of change that will be required for the part.   Frank explained each of my car's problems, what he did or didn't do and why, what I should do in the future, etc. Every guy there was a complete gentleman and no one made me feel the slightest bit uncomfortable, despite not knowing jack about the topics at hand. Best of all is that Frank handed over my key and sent me off with no charge at all. Stunned, I tell you. But, 100% grateful that my concerns were addressed and I can drive with confidence knowing that my wheels are safe.

I hate to say it because Cork used to be one of my favorite spots in my old neighborhood, but things have changed. I returned with excitement last night for my mom's birthday. Once again, the bar was packed while the restaurant was mostly empty. We talked it over with the hostess and she agreed to let us sit in a booth near the bar where we would receive both table service and happy hour pricing. Great!  It took a while before we received our first round. The beer my stepdad ordered was out, so he had to choose another. Shortly after our drinks arrived (which were well made, as always), we received our fish tacos and Korean tacos. We started with the fish, which were bursting with flavor. Unfortunately, the beef in the Korean tacos was so fatty, it was impossible to even chew. We ended up pulling most of the meat from the tacos.   Next up was a Mediterranean plate, which we have ordered on almost every visit. It came out looking totally different than we expected, and it was then that we found out that a new chef had taken over the kitchen. A little later we tried to order a pizza and were told that pizzas were out but flatbreads were available. A short time later our server came back to tell us they had run out of flatbreads, too.   We ordered one last round of drinks and ordered a pizza to-go from Treno. Now that I live in the city and visit the area less frequently, I don't know that I'll make an effort to go back to Cork when there are other local businesses that I'd rather revisit.

Walking into Cucina Forte about fifteen minutes early for my girls' night, it seemed evident that we were going to have excellent service.  How did I come to this conclusion?  I was the only person in the entire restaurant.  A few minutes later, my friends arrived and we were asked to choose our table.  For the remainder of the evening, we dined in privacy... well, sort of.  Everything we talked about was heard loud-and-clear by our server, considering she was the only other person in the room.  Still, that didn't stop our conversation from heading straight towards the gutter, once a couple glasses of wine were consumed.  I don't think she minded, considering she chimed in at various points and we discovered a shared interest in Bret Michaels' Rock of Love.  As we were the only patrons that evening, we were instructed to order anything we wanted and how we wanted it.  We shared a gnocchi platter to start.  Half was spinach with a pomodoro-type sauce and the other half was cheese with a gorgonzola cream sauce.  Sweet Jesus.  If I could go back and have this dish as my entrée, I would.  Unfortunately, I choose the tilapia special, which sounded better than it tasted.  The white wine sauce lacked flavor, so I squeezed some lemon to give it a much-needed kick.  Still, the fish was extremely bland (even for tilapia) and the chopped tomatoes in the sauce were mushy and lacked any taste of acidity that tomatoes usually provide.  There was also some sort of spice that tasted very strongly of Christmas trees.  'Tis the season and all, but pine is best in the form of trees, cones or sol.    Dessert was better.  We shared a flourless chocolate cake that was so satisfyingly rich, we did not finish it.  That's right- four girls did not finish a single piece of cake.  Someone call the Guinness Book, I think we have a winner.  We also shared the gelato, in chocolate hazelnut and peanut butter flavors.  It was so delish, I almost excused the piece of hazelnut shell that found its way into my mouth... almost.    Bottom line, I would like to try this restaurant again but I would be pickier about my entrée.  It seems that pasta and gnocchi rule the menu, while proteins take a back seat.  My advice would be to choose wisely, and beware the hazelnut shells.

This is one of my favorite Wawas, because I generally walk in looking like a swamp creature after my bootcamp class and no one even bats an eye. In fact, the employees go out of their way to be friendly and conversational.   The store is well stocked and there are always fresh cut mangoes in the cold case. Two thumbs up.

I never think to make Omoi a destination, but visits tend to happen whenever I find myself walking by. Last Saturday, a friend and I were walking past and she said, "What is that place?" Stunned, I dragged her into the store. I thought everyone knew about this cute little shop with Japanese flair!   There are so many fun little gifts and trinkets to peruse. I immediately spotted a suede magenta bag that I could envision as my pop of color while wearing a black dress. It was forty bucks. I'm still thinking of going back to grab it. I bet I'd use it all the time.   Instead, I ended up picking up a card from their wall of terribly amusing creations. There's a little section for every imaginable scenario. And I feel pretty confident that my recipient won't have already come across said card in every single drug store across town.

MOD is a great fast casual option for customizable pizzas and salads. That said, it is not your standard pizza parlor pie, but more of an upgraded make-at-home version. I love that you can select from some tried and true combos or simply design your own. The pizzas are ready in minutes, so that's definitely a plus.   Last week, I stopped in for a pizza and salad to go. The guy who took my order was nice and patient. I was bringing everything back over the bridge so my husband got the oven started so we could reheat the pizza once I arrived; definitely a good call as the crust is so thin that the pizza cools quickly. I knew one pizza for two people would be stretching it which is why I also got a salad. The Italian dressing was great!   I'd probably lean towards dining in for the future because the food is best when served right away.

In my opinion, this is by far the best restaurant on Haddon Ave.  The martini list is a mile long, the newly renovated bar is really classy, service is always wonderful and the food is consistently fantastic.    I've probably gotten crab cakes 90% of the time I have eaten here, and they are always fresh and made with big chunks of crab meat.  Portion sizes are on the very large side.  You will never leave here hungry, and if you do, I would suggest a Lap-Band.  Seriously.      All desserts are homemade and brought around on a large tray so you have to physically look at them before you decide.  It kind of breaks my heart a little on the days that I pass and just have a coffee instead, because my head is screaming "GIVE ME THOSE THREE ON THE UPPER RIGHT!!!!!!!"  However, if I'm here for a special occasion, I'm always down for splitting something sweet!

I'm pretty much loving this place. I've landed at Boot & Saddle as my closer bar on three occasions now. Our servers have been great despite the crowds, and we've somehow scored seats pretty quickly each time. I love the dim lighting and the original artwork and wall decor from the bar's previous incarnation.  The draft list is pretty solid and rotates often. I was thrilled to see Pliny the Elder during a recent visit but it was gone just one week later. Glad I got to partake while they had it. If you don't fancy any of the drafts, the bottle list should have what you're after.   The food menu is small but solid. While I wasn't crazy about the roasted pumpkin and kale soup (I was expecting creamy but it was broth-based), I did love the grilled cheese and hash browns with spicy cheese sauce.   Really, the only thing I don't love is the cocktails. I've made my way through most of the offerings and they just aren't doing it for me. Stick with beer or drink your whiskey straight for best results.

I had been told repeatedly by a friend before my trip to Nashville that I had to visit Las Paletas while there. The place reminded me a lot of Philly's Little Pop Shop, with interesting flavors and pops starting at $2.50. I wanted something light and fruity so I chose the cantaloupe flavor. It tasted like biting into a fresh cantaloupe, only as a popsicle! It was awesome. My friend enjoyed her chocolate with banana chunks pop. Definitely worth a visit on a hot day!

I had been to Champps once before and didn't remember being all that impressed, but my sister insisted that they have the best nachos ever and that they would feed all three girls in our group who were jonesin' for some junk food.  We enter the restaurant which appears to be in decent shape and we head to the table.  Appearances can be deceiving!  The floor was littered with straw wrappers, food and other random debris.  It looked like a toddler convention had taken place in the dining area.  Once seated, I kicked the chicken chunks out from under my chair and announced that I was heading to the restrooms.  Of 5 toilets, only one of the three that remained unoccupied was not flushed.  You know you are in a crappy place when the patrons can't be bothered to flush the toilet.  Pun intended.  Back at the table, my appetite still miraculously intact, we dove into a nacho plate that was good, and definitely huge, but not good enough to ever get me back in this place.  I'm giving two stars because the food wasn't bad and our server was awesome.

This was the closest liquor store to my apartment when I lived in Collingswood, so it got some pretty decent business out of me during my 4+ years there. Cook's has an okay selection of craft beer for such a small store, and the prices aren't too bad. Wine options are solid and fairly priced. Now that I live in Philly where even a bottle of Ecco Domani will cost you, I can appreciate the place even more. I also like that there is always a nice selection of chilled whites ready for BYO-ing. And the staff has always been great. I miss regular Jersey liquor stores!

I fell in love with this adorable store on Passyunk when I first stopped in around the holidays. At that point, my shopping was complete but there were so many cute gift ideas that I knew it was only a matter of time before I would return.   In need of a baby gift and recalling the locally-made and locally-inspired onesies, I returned to find something cute for my best guy friend's adorable baby girl. This time, most of the onesie designs were super hipster. This would be great for some of my friends but totally lost on this particular couple. Fortunately, I spotted some handmade baby blankets. So soft and with gently colored patterns, it was immediately evident that this was the perfect gift. And the price was more than fair. The woman working wrapped the blanket in pink tissue paper and placed it into a simple brown shopper with the store's name. Easy peasy! Next time I need a gift that doesn't break the bank, I'm checking out Nice Things first.

I was skeptical as I turned onto 9th Street and saw a mile-long line of people waiting to get into the Starlight Ballroom for the Ting Tings show. To my surprise, once the line started moving, we were at the doors in no time.   Once inside, I was immediately a fan of the venue, which reminded me of the roller rinks from my childhood. Circular half-booths lined the sides of the darkened room, neon light fixtures dangled from the ceiling and hot dogs spun on wire grates at the snack bar. The bar area was relatively large and the lines moved quickly.  Although I didn't see one, and I can't imagine that there was a need for it on such a mild night, the smell of a lit fireplace filled the air.     Expecting the worst, we inquired about beer costs. That was when I heard the magical words, "two dollar PBRs." Oh hellllllllls yeah! I got that party started.   The show itself far exceeded my expectations. The sound quality was great and there was plenty room to dance. The crowd was friendly and it seemed like everyone was just out to have a good time. The only issue was that the room temperature skyrocketed once everyone got moving. I felt like I was dancing in hell and at any point I might look over and see John Candy in a devil costume, laughing maniacally, from that scene in Planes, Trains & Automobiles. On the upside, I didn't pass out and I'm pretty sure I worked off the fried green beans from earlier that evening. Win-win!

Bar Ferdinand had long been on my "to try" list. Our party of four plus a dog arrived on a Sunday evening and we were fortunate enough to get a table outside right away. We took some time discussing the menu and came up with a pretty extensive list.   Highlights for me were the surtido de carnes (charcuterie board consisting of four delicious cured meats), patatas bravas (fried potatoes in a tasty aioli), datiles rellenos (stuffed dates), queso de cabra cocinado (baked goat cheese with pine nuts) and the almejas (steamed clams). These items would all make my list on a return visit.   Items that left me less impressed were the empanadas, which had so much potential but ended up tasting kind of bland. Same with the stuffed peppers, which had little flavor other than the peppers themselves. The hits were far greater than the misses, and I'm looking forward to seeing how the menu changes with Ansill's reign.

The food here is fresh, authentic Mexican and it's awesome.  I order the chicken burrito enchilada-style 90 percent of the time, and the green salad that comes with most of the dinners is the best pre-meal salad I can think of anywhere.  It is huge and comes topped with shredded zucchini, carrots, Mexican cheese (I think cotija) and some tortilla strips.  Always order the homemade cilantro vinaigrette.  Also, they ask if you want chips before they put them on your table~ I think they might charge like .50 cents for them or something... but they come with 3 different types of homemade salsas which are fantastic.  The reasons I don't give the last star:  1. Mexican chain restaurants have better margaritas.  2. The interior needs a major spring cleaning or perhaps even a little refurbishing (keep the Frida art though).  3. My girlfriends and I once sat on the attached patio, which backs up to the woods.  We were on the side closest to the woods, when we heard rustling in the nearby foliage... a skunk and some cats!  Nice.  We spent the entire meal with one eye on the skunk and the other on the cats, hoping they wouldn't scare Pepe into spraying us all.

My fiance proposed in April with a ring from Barsky. I couldn't have done better if I had picked out the ring myself - it was exactly what I wanted!   Fast forward several months. The ring has always been loose, but over the winter it has been looser than ever so I knew I had to get it resized, and quickly. I brought the ring to Barsky the day before Valentine's Day, because I like to torture people. Kidding, but I happened to be in the area so I made a stop, knowing I would most likely have to leave the ring for several days. I was told it would take about a week. When I mentioned that I had an event to attend on the following Wednesday, the gentleman helping me said he would get it done in time.  I called on Wednesday and sure enough, my ring was ready for pick-up. The end result was stunning. Not only does the ring fit perfectly but it looks like it is back to its original condition - all sparkly and shiny! We'll be heading back to look at wedding bands and I'm looking forward to that experience as well.

I had frozen yogurt for the first time in my adult life at Yogorino last night. Turns out, it's changed a lot since I was little and isn't at all like the stuff found in the freezer section at the grocery store. Creamy, slightly tart but still just sweet enough, I took one look at the plastic jugs of fake syrup toppings and instead opted for some fresh chopped nectarines.   As a few others have pointed out, it is hard to distinguish what each topping is just from the sign on the wall. Meringue pieces looked like mochi, the sauces were unidentifiable from each other, etc.  The price points were fair, and I left satisfied but not too full from a small cup.

So my friend and I are standing outside of Capogiro, deciding where we should go to continue our wine buzz from the two bottles we killed at dinner earlier.  Next thing we know, this guy starts chatting us up and invites us to join him and his friend Brian at Apothecary for a drink.  Free drinks at the new place with all the buzz?  Fanfuckintastic!  I love being a girl!  Turns out, "friend Brian" is one of the owners and we have an interesting conversation about the lounge as I order my first drink ~ the Sage Wisdom.  The mustached man from Carrie's review was my bartender (she was right--that is one nifty-ass mustache), and he got to work mixing the contents of all kinds of unfamiliar bottles and vials.  Supposedly, the drink is supposed to clarify memory and purify thoughts, but my thoughts were less than pure as I text messaged my boyfriend later in my slightly intoxicated state.  But that is neither here nor there.  The drink was slammin.      Next drink!  The Dermis Fantasticus tagline is "achieve the glow," which sounded like a good idea to me.  This drink was garnished with a slice of ginger and a sliver of cucumber.  It was interesting, but not as delish as the Sage Wisdom.  Still, glowing skin?  I'll drink to that!  Apothecary is definitely carving itself into a unique niche in the Philly bar scene.  The concept is interesting and fun, and everyone seated at the cozy tables and mingling on the deck outside seemed in no hurry to leave.  I wish Brian and his partners the best, and I'll definitely be back!

I can't stop thinking about my dinner at Friday Saturday Sunday earlier this week! Especially dessert. More on that later.   I'd been to the revamped FSS several times for drinks (I love their bar scene and the bartenders are tops!) but Tuesday night was a first for the dining room. My last dinner there was circa 2008. Back then it was a totally different vibe, different menu, different boyfriend! The new iteration is much brighter and very elegant.     Our server was excellent (I forget his name - he was so patient and knowledgeable!). He knew the menu inside and out and was able to highlight the gluten-free items for one of my friends. In an effort to keep things light, I went with the asparagus as a starter and the halibut entree. I don't think I've ever ordered a veggie for a starter, aside from the obvious salads, but FSS was a great place to try it! The asparagus was beautifully presented and the broth was bursting with flavor and texture from the black walnut crumble.   My halibut entree was perfection. I was that girl who didn't offer a bite to my friends because I was hoarding it all to myself. Served with a warm potato salad, the halibut was just wonderful. I enjoyed my meal with glasses of txakoli, which was crisp and effervescent.   All of us were trying to be reasonably healthy but, when dessert appeared on the house, were weren't turning it away! The panna cotta with blueberries was a hit but the black and tan sundae was right up my alley. I can't believe we (meaning, me) managed to leave a few bites behind. I need that sundae in my life again. Safe to say it won't be long before I'm finding a reason to get back!

I went to this store to experience the famous Blue Bell ice cream. My Southern and Texas friends swear it is the best ice cream on the earth. When someone says, "Best on the earth," that is like throwing down the ice scoop to a challenge.   The Blue Bell is located in the front of the store. It's on the backside of the huge glass display case for the truffles, caramel apples and specialty chocolates. When I went, I was expecting maybe six or so flavors being offered on a rotating schedule. To my surprise, there were over two dozen flavors to choose from. For a brief moment I felt like a kid in a candy shop. Oh wait, I was in a candy shop, that had an ice cream parlor too.   The young lady working the counter was very patient with me, as I was having a hard time selecting my first Blue Bell flavor. I finally went with, Birthday Cake. It was a rich creamy vanilla with pieces of chocolate cake and swirls of chocolate icing and bright colored sprinkles. I'm sure you have heard, sprinkles are for winners. After enjoying my Blue Bell, I now understand not only the love the South has for this ice cream, but why the South has an obesity problem. This ice cream is too good to resist.   Now, I'll talk about the RSC. This store was amazing, I had no idea they had so much to offer. They had pre-boxed, by the piece, Jelly Belly jelly beans, Weight Watchers candy and some the most decadent caramel apples. This is a great place for picking up a gift for that special Aunt, Grandma or person that stumps you every time on what to get them.   Personally I prefer local chocolates, Kakao and Bissinger's, but for gifts and Blue Bell, I will keep this candy store on my shopping list.

It's a Walgreens. It's a chain. It's in my hood. Being in my hood, is reason enough to bump them up a star. Actually, the extra star is my Christmas gift to them. Because, their great sales made my budget for "Secret Santa" at work go further. I wasn't even looking here and found a perfect gift as I entered and it was 50% off. More gifts, the merrier the recipient.   I am also a fan of their photo lab. It is so easy to submit pictures via the Walgreens app. Once my photos are ready to pick-up, they'll text me. Then all I have to do is jump in the car and drive up Hampton a couple of blocks. It usually takes less then two hours and the quality is good.   I don't use the pharmacy, but this is my go-to for over the counter drugs. The prices are good and I've never seen them out of stock for any of the products I use.   It is a busy Walgreen's as everyone has stated. So have patience when it is time to check-out. Management is quick to open additional registers when a line starts to form.   Will I return? - I support my hood, even if it is a chain store.   When: December 13, 2017 Why: Photos and Secret Santa Shopping

Two things I can not believe, 1) That I am doing an updated review on a gas station and 2) that I am raising them to a 5 Star rating.  However, I am doing it because they deserve it.   As Christine stated in her review, the customer service here is outstanding. Everyone of the employees I have meet are friendly, out going and helpful. It is like they all take Pollyanna pills before their shift.  It is so good to see people enjoying their work and spreading a little happiness. You do know that stuff is contagious. If not stop by this U Gas and you will see customers come in with a frown and walk out with a smile and they didn't even have to pay for it. Smiles are free.   The store is always super clean. The booze is super cheap. I can  get my Scotch, vodka and beer here at a savings when I do not have time to make the pilgrimage out to Costco. Their selection and variety of convince store staples have also saved my ass numerous times already.  They also sell me winning Scratch Lottery Tickets. I am hoping for a big win on Mega and Power some day.   Their prepared foods are done by Gigi and the selection and variety is better then their competitor QT. I've tried the salads, a couple of the sandwiches and I like the way the also package fresh fruits and cubed cheeses for snacking.  My only draw back on the prepared foods is that they do not have the little box that gives you the Nutrition Facts. Being a dieter, I like to have that information at my fingertips.   Be alert in the parking lot, as this place has gotten popular the parking lot has gotten a little crazy.  Everyone rushing in for affordable gas, winning lottery tickets, cheap booze and great customer service makes for a parking lot derby.

Bailey's Chocolate Bar moved upstairs and Dave Bailey transformed this space into an entirely new experience. Having recently been to New Orleans, I can tell you the decor is very similar to the trendy & chic little restaurants in the French Quarter. I cannot wait till spring to enjoy the outside dining.   My dining partner and I started off sharing, a Lump Crab Cake, Blackened Shrimp and a Cornmeal Waffle. My favorite was the Blackened Shrimp that came with a Cucumber Ranch. I tried it, it was cool and refreshing, but I ate my shrimp without it. The spicy flavor, was reminiscent of the cajun seasoning I experienced in NOLA. My DP, favored the Crab Cake. It was topped with slices of grapefruit and avocado. Make sure you get a mixture of all three in every bite. It makes for an interesting combination on your palate.   Our Cornmeal Waffle was a tad cold, so we sent it back. The second one was warm and served with a large scoop of soft whipped butter. I enjoyed the texture of the cornmeal and the taste, but would have preferred some other type of topping in addition to the butter. Perhaps, a little cup of syrup. After all, it is a waffle.   We went in different directions on our entrees so we could each sample each others. Being a fan of catfish, I choose the Crab Stuffed Missouri Catfish. It was served on a bed of poblano grits and topped with a garlic dressing. You can not go wrong with crab and catfish in the same dish.  It's amazing how the older I get, the more I am developing an appreciation for grits. These were some of the best I have had.   The DP went with the Shrimp and Grits. The shrimp were the same as the Blackened Shrimp we enjoyed as an appetizer. She liked them. They were hard to photograph in a dimly light bar, so trust us when we say they tasted better then they photographed.   Being a bar diner, I was highly impressed with the comfort and style of the barstools. The back was low, giving good back support and they had armrest for extra comfort. Only thing lacking at the bar was hooks underneath for ladies to secure their purses and outlets to allow social media junkies to keep charged up.   Nathan was a great bar host and mixologist. He's a transplant from Tulsa and is adjusting to new city very well. Stop by and welcome him to STL.   Will I return? - I hang out in Lafayette Square - so, YES!  When: December 28, 2017 Why: It's new, hot and trendy. You should go, too.

Three Dog Night had a popular song that hit number 1 on the charts in the 70's. It was appropriately called "One". In the lyrics, it stated, "One is the loneliest number that you'll ever do". That may be true in love, but when it comes to dining sometimes you just want to dine alone.  If you do, avoid HWK.   Not once, but twice I have been turned  away when wanting to dine here as a single person. The first time when I called to make a reservation, the young lady who answered informed me they preferred not to sit single diners at tables and that I'd have to eat at the bar.  At first I was content with that arrangement, but then she continued to tell me that  those eating at the bar can not select from the entire menu. At that point, I decided not to make the reservation.  I wanted the true HWK experience. After all the reviews have been amazing.   The second time, I stopped in for early lunch while shopping the main drag in Maplewood.  Once again, I was told I'd have to sit at the bar and order from a "limited menu". When I asked if I could be seated at one of the hightops in the window, she told me she needed to save those for parties of two. The kicker came when I asked if they were already reserved and she said, "no".  I ate else where that day.   What I do not understand, is why can I go to Chicago dine at such top restaurants such as; Girl and the Goat, RL, The Pump Room, Table Fifty-Two, The Purple Pig, Frontera Grill and The Publican and be welcomed with open arms. Many of the chefs at these restaurants have been on Top Chef and published cookbooks.  How is it that their establishments are welcoming to the lone diner, yet a small Maplewood restaurant is not?  I understand they have a small space, but if you are going to sit single diners at the bar, let them order from the entire menu. Before posting, I shared this review with other friends who are single diners and being women, they said for them they would not feel comfortable eating at the bar and would not eat here if a table was not an option.   Disclaimer: I did dine here as a couple opening week and was not impressed. I contributed that to opening week jitters and wanted to give them another chance. It is a shame that I have not had that opportunity.

I am embarrassed at how many times I have walked by this little boutique and haven't walked in to shop. Thank goodness, I discovered them at their outside booth during the Lafayette Holiday House tour.   My cousin and are the family shoppers and after browsing the items at the outdoor booth, we headed up the street to check out the store. We weren't the only ones with this brilliant idea, the store was packed. After finding several gifts for different people on our Santa list, we opted to return later to make our purchases and avoid the crowd.   Without giving away details, because a recipient may be reading this review. We found several unique and STL themed gifts for local sports fans and bar items for the boozers. We do not discriminate, we shop for the naughty and nice.   The staff was friendly and very helpful with our selections. This little shop will now be one of my go to stores for unique gifts and I'll be shopping local.   Will I return? - YES!  When: December 10, 2017 Why: Naughty or Nice List

I thought when I went to the Early Bird Special today I'd be joining a bunch of diners my age and older. To our surprise, we were the oldest ones in the dining room. It was all young professionals taking advantage of the $9.95 dinner special.   Both of us enjoyed the 8 oz Ribeye which came with a salad and a side dish of your choice. I choose my favorite vegetable, asparagus as mine. It was five stalks, that were prepared perfectly. They were tender with just enough snap. My dining partner went with their pasta with red sauce. He said the penne noodles were done al dente and the sauce was a traditional marinara.   The Ribeye's were tender and we both had them done medium rare. 8 oz may seem small to some, but it was the perfect size for a lite dinner. Our Early Bird Dinner also included a dinner salad, making this a very fulfilling meal.   If you're on a budget or just want to save a few bucks, eat early (3PM - 6PM Monday-Thursday) at Joey B's and you'll enjoy a great meal.

I am happy to say, Cassy the owner and executive chef at HWK has contacted me and was in shock that I had the experience that I did. She assured me that was not their policy and was going to use this situation as a teaching moment with her front of the house staff.   I appreciated her outreach and will attempt to dine at HWK again. Once I do, hopefully you'll see another increase in stars.

Wow, this is the best Marshalls I have ever shopped. It was clean, well organized and had stuff I actually wanted to buy. The other day I went shopping at The Rack, looking for a short sleeved linen shirt and had no luck. I found it here and for only $20. What a deal. I hope they can keep it up. If they can, I will be a repeat offender. I mean, I will be a repeat shopper.   I only shopped the Men's Dept., but the shoe selection looked huge as did the home area.   Deer Creek Plaza has been totally redone, I'm looking forward to shopping the other new stores as they open.

This is a pretty amazing bar, it has the feeling of a true neighborhood bar, and like Kelly B. said, "that happens to be downtown." If I lived downtown, I'd have a name plate on one of the bar-stools.  I would never drink at home alone, I would be here with all my friends. This is the "Cheers" of St. Louis.   The drinks here are cheap and with the free pour that the bartenders do here, they are worth every cent. Some of their rail liquor is what some bars offer as "call brands".   The party room downstairs is a great place for a friends gathering to celebrate special occasions. I only got to sample a few food offerings the night I visited,  from a small buffet. What I did sample was good bar grub, but I want to go back and taste what I here is, "the best cheeseburger".   Jack I'm giving you fair warning, I'm going to be back.

It's Sunday night and the Cards are in the playoffs, we're not cooking or going out for dinner. We didn't want pizza, Chinese or any type of fast food. We were at a a loss for ideas. I was searching Yelp for ideas and checked to see if Joey B's did carry- out and to my surprise they did.  We checked the menu and made the call.   We ordered two of their Blue Plate Specials; Country Fried Chicken and Homemade Meatloaf. Both came with mashed potatoes and gravy and corn on the cob. The meatloaf also came with a side salad that was humongous, it was big enough for both of us to share. My Homemade Meatloaf  with a brown gravy truly had to down home taste. It is way better then other "Blue Plate Specials" near and on "The Hill". My SO enjoyed his Country Fried Chicken and its white gravy topping. Their great taste surprised us coming from a sports bar which is known for burgers and pizza.   I think Joey B's will be getting some more carryout orders from us.  They're close, the prices are right and the food is good.

If you've ordered pizza from Bono's you know it's the real deal. However, this review I was to highlight their Chicken Wings. Many local pizza joints and chains offer chicken wings, but none of them compare to those at Bono's. They have the best wings of all the pizza delivery places in my hood.   Bono's wings are good size, meaty, juicy and well coated in their house sauce. I've been know to order a double order for a night of movies at home. To make it a true meal, I add a Caesar Salad. Or I just add an order of Cheese Garlic Bread and let the movie roll.   Great pizza, but I love their wings too.

Had lunch here the other day, and it's time to bump Joey up to a four.  The service is always friendly, the portions are hearty and the food is more flavorful then most sports themed bars.   We started our lunch with some Hot & Spicy Chicken Wings. They defiantly are H&S, but not that big & meaty.  Next time I want to try their Butter Garlic wings - they just sound Paula Deen good.   I had their Pork Tenderloin Sandwich and it was better then Johnson's Corner in Alton and they are known for theirs.  It was huge, it hung off the bun in all directions.  The tenderloin was breaded, crispy and oh so tender when bitten into. It was so full of flavor, I didn't even use any of the sauce they provided. I am such a naturalist.   Brad had the Crispy Chicken Salad and it was huge. Romaine lettuce, Breaded Boneless Chicken, Cheddar Cheese (no Provel), Green Onion, Bacon and Tomato with Honey Mustard. Salad was acceptable, could have been better if they didn't use bacon that came from a bag. Fresh bacon would made it pop so much more.  The salad was so huge that  two could have shared.  Brad didn't even finish it, however I finished my sandwich.   What made my most recent visit enjoyable was watching the other diners.  It was fun to watch the interchange between the "career girls" and their Uncles and Dads while they seemed to be having a "working lunch".  The bond with a dad is so magical.

If you haven't heard, the Tuesday Blue Plate Special is now Tacos and it is a sure fire way to get a good Mex-Fix.  You'll have three tacos; a chorizo, a carnitas, and a mixed-vegetable, along with rice and beans. As usual you'll get the flavorful house salad and a glass of iced tea. ( I love their salad dressing, wish it was available bottled.) Now let's talk about the new blue plate itself. I'd be hard pressed to select which taco I thought was best, each was in a class of it's own.  I was surprised that I actually liked the vegetable taco. The broccoli had a crisp snap and the red pepper and onion added extra flavor. The beans were just okay, need something to give it  a bang. Ask for their hot sauce, add it to the rice and you've got a great side to your tacos.  This place is still the best value for lunch.

Good-bye cupcakes, you are a thing of the past. Bundt cakes are the new sweet treat in town.    I already know, this is where my birthday cake will be coming from this year. These delightfully moist bundt cakes, are going to be my new go to for satisfying my dessert cravings. The icing is made with cream cheese and butter and is a complement to the cake.   The Bundtlets are about the size of a traditional cupcake, so one cake is a single serving. Since, I am currently dieting, I cut mine in half to enjoy over two consecutive days. They also offer full sized bundt cakes and tiered, but these little ones are so darn cute. If you order the Bundtinis, which are the bite size ones, you'll have the opportunity to taste more flavors.
