Speaking of flavors, the ladies working told me that the top four favorites are; Lemon, Chocolate Chocolate Chip, White Chocolate Raspberry and Red Velvet. I'm a sucker for Red Velvet and was about to order one of those, when I saw next to it, a Cinnamon Swirl. When I moaned, and uttered "Cinnamon Swirl", one of the ladies said it was her personal favorite.  So I took her word and ordered it. I can always go back for a Red Velvet, or even a Lemon. They were sampling the Lemon today and the sweet/tart flavor had it going on.   Convenient location in the Brentwood neighborhood. Only a couple parking spaces in front, but there are plenty others in the back of the small building. I like that they are close to the city, so when I crave I can get there quickly. I'm afraid if they were any closer to my home, I'd become an bundt cake addict.  When: February 24, 2016 Why: Afternoon Sweet Treat

Katy Perry, kissed a  girl and liked it. I had a McRib sandwich and didn't like it.   The other day on my way to work without a lunch the morning DJ's were talking about the McRib and the limited availability. In all the years McRib has been offered, I have never tried it. With it's departure from the menu coming up soon and the positive spin one of the DJ's gave, I thought I'd try one for lunch.   I ordered a McRib combo meal with a small french fry and small coke. Kevin the DJ, said he orders his without pickle and onions. I like pickles and onions, so I kept them on mine. I'm glad that I did, the bun along with the crisp pickles and onions were the best thing about the sandwich. The processed meat was tasteless, it was over sauced with a BBQ that was way to sweet. I thank my luck stars that I had an order of fries. I only wished I had upgraded to a larger size to fill the void left by a flavorless sandwich.   This is a very clean and friendly McDonald's. I will not lower their star rating due to a seasonal sandwich that I did not enjoy. However, I would not recommend a McRib to anyone, not even my worst enemy.

Is the Egg White Delight McMuffin, delightfully delicious? Yes, if you add Frank's Hot Sauce.   When you break down the nutrition facts and compare the new Egg White to the Regular McMuffin, there really isn't that much of a difference. You save 50 calories and 5 grams of fat ordering the EW. Ordering the regular Egg McMuffin you lose 1 gram of fiber and get 20 mg less of Sodium. If you count points on the Weight Watchers program, a regular McMuffin is 8 points and the new Egg White is 7. One point is not that big of a savings. The egg whites and white cheddar is not exclusive to the McMuffin, you can try it on any egg & cheese sandwich. Which means, you can have it your way. Oh wait, that is another burger joints phrase.   Normally I am not a fan of McDonalds, but this one is close to work and surprisingly is better then any of the ones near my home in Saint Louis. When I am in need of a quick breakfast, this is a great place to stop. The staff is friendly and awake when I stop by at 5:30 AM.

Once again, I have died and gone to foodie heaven after eating at Farmhaus. This place is so worthy of its #4 ranking on the famous Ian Froeb's STL 100 List. It truly is one of the best places to eat in the Lou.   Tonight, surprise-surprise, I sat at the bar since I was dining alone. When asked if I'd like anything to drink, I responded, "It depends, can you make a good Old Fashioned?" The young lady who asked me, kinda hesitated. However, your co-worker spoke up and told me how she'd make and the gauntlet had been thrown down. She went to work and when she presented it to me, my breath was taken away. It was the same caliber of masterful cocktail mixing that I expect at a bar that specializes in classic cocktails. It went down smoothly.   Also tonight, I thanked my lucky stars that I do not have a peanut allergy.  As an appetizer, I enjoyed the Chicken Wing Lollipops. They were made with a Thai peanut sauce, compressed cucumber and carrot, ponzu mayo and roasted peanuts. The flavor was incredible, best way to describe it, is dipping a wing in peanut butter instead of blu cheese  or ranch dressing. They were so juicy and tender, you could suck the bones clean. Every morsel was enjoyed.   My entree was my second favorite seafood next to sea scallops and that is, Soft-Shell Crab. I've lived in Boston and traveled a lot in Florida and this by far is the best Soft-Shell Crab I have ever had. It was Corn Flour Fried and served on a bed of lemon anchovy aioli and tomato and corn salsa. The glass of Pinot Grigio was a refreshing beverage for this seafood entree.   I went total hog wild and blew my diet when I saw French Toast listed as a dessert. It was house made brioche, maple meringue with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. WOW! You've heard of a foodgasm? This dessert will give you multiple ones.   Staff is incredibly knowledgeable of the menu. When each of my dishes were served, they'd explain what it was and how it was prepared. It was like a verbal menu, explaining to you what you had ordered and what you were about to enjoy.   The only negative I experienced, is that they did not keep up with my alcohol needs. Which I guess could be a good thing. I wasn't over drinking, I only had the Old Fashioned and a glass of wine. However, an after dinner liquor with my sensational French Toast Dessert would have made for an incredible finale.   When: August 13, 2016 Why: Dinner & STL 100 List

A Labor Day celebration is not complete without at least one of the following; a parade of union workers, a BBQ Pork Steak and a visit to the St Nicholas Greek Festival. Being able to have all three is like winning the Triple Crown.   I work weekends, so Monday was my only chance to experience the festival. Determined to beat the crowds we arrived early and got Prince parking in the garage. Actually it was so damn good, I'd call it parking for a King. It wasn't luck, we just got there REAL early. In fact, we had to wait for them to set up and get ready to open.   For those of you who have never attended this Greek Festival, visualize Six Flags or Disney World without the rides. To make it easier for all the attendees, maps are provided with menus from each booth. Arriving early paid off, we were able to read the menus and get in line early. Not being too smart, we got beers and sat at a hightop table and people watched. Before we knew it, some of the lines were already 20+ deep. We immediately got in line at the Athenian Garden Deli, because we knew we wanted chicken wings and a Shish-Kebob.   For a church festival I am always amazed at how high of quality of food that is being served. These wings were huge, tender and seasoned oh, so well. Our Shish-Kebob was marinated tenderloin, seasoned with lemon and herbs, grilled on skewers over hot coals. The tenderness of the tenderloin, again surprised me for a church parking lot festival.  To satisfy our sweet tooth's we enjoyed a Loukoumades which is a Grecian beignet covered with honey and nuts. Having one of these, you will go nuts. It is sticky and sweet from the honey and the nuts give it a slight salty tang.   In addition to the Loukoumades, we had a Baklava Sundae. Don't judge us, there were two so having two desserts is like having one each. The sundae they claim was, tasty low calorie vanilla ice cream topped with crumbled baklava pieces. The Tweens ordering ahead of us, added Hershey's Chocolate Syrup on top. So when I ordered, she asked if I wanted it as well. I told her, "No, that would be blasphemous." The little old man working the soft serve machine laughed and said that he totally agreed with me. I hope that ice cream was low calorie, because it needed to balance out the calorie intake of the best Baklava I have ever had at a Greek restaurant or festival.  We both were on sugar highs after chowing down two desserts. Remember, it balances out to one each.   This festival only happens once a year, make sure to mark your calendar and attend.

Ben (chef/owner)  from Salume Beddu and Andrey (General Manager)  from 33 Wine Shop have taken an old 1930's gas station and turned it into a trendy little wine bar. The bar area is compact, cozy and all the windows give it a felling  of being larger then it really is.   Great wine by the glass, tasting flights measured to perfection and an impressive selection of liquor as well. I went craving a red wine, but when I saw they offered Tito's Vodka my favorite I was swayed away.   We enjoyed a sampling of artisan cured meats and hard cheese served with fresh bread and oil.   A great place for Happy Hour or after theater drinks.

Before my last visit I quick tipped this business as a great asset to our neighborhood, I may have jumped the gun. It has a long way to go, but they are still fairly new, so I am sure they are suffering from growing pains.  First thing that we found distracting is the big cooler in the lounge area. Find it a new home, it ruins the ambiance that you have created and it is a good feeling. Secondly, don't down grade yourself with the Robert Mondavi - Woodbridge table tents. Your serving quality wines, and everyone knows Woodbridge does not fall into that category.   The staff is friendly and provides good service, but while we were there they seemed to be over staffed and falling over each other.  They've decorated well for the holidays and I love the heated front patio and the fire pit in the back patio.   I'll revisit and I am sure they'll pull it together so I can upgrade my # of stars.

Disclaimer: The decanter at the front door is not cucumber infused vodka.   When I first entered The Island, my eyes immediately went to the large dispenser containing clear refreshing liquid with thinly sliced cucumbers floating inside.  I jokingly asked, "is that cucumber infused vodka?".  The jovial cashier, gave a hearty laugh and informed me it was "just water". I have to admit I was disappointed, but once I sampled and filled my bowl with Froyo I was whisked away to a tropical "island".   Those big chain Froyo shops have nothing on The Island, in fact The Island has them beat with flavor, toppings and customer service. I'm a purest,  I like my yogurt plain like my flavored vodka. I like to experience their true flavors to the fullest.   My "island" experience included; Madagascar Vanilla, Root Beer Float and Cheesecake. The Root Beer Float was as if you truly were having one, except it was all yogurt and no soda. If you crumbled up some graham crackers with the cheesecake, you'd think you were eating the real thing. However, the Madagascar Vanilla was my favorite, it had true vanilla flavoring. Even as a child my favorite ice cream was vanilla, I guess old habits are hard to break.   I also grabbed some Banana FroYo to go, we had a neighbors birthday to celebrate when I got home from this UYE.  I forgot to mention this was a UYE sponsored by Miss Soulard herself, Mandie M.. If it were not for her, I would have never discovered this delightful yogurt shop.  By the way, the banana went great with a chocolate cake.

Reading some of these other Yelp reviews, I figure someone got spanked at this store and most likely got spanked hard. The reason I say this is, every time I have shopped here the customer service is has been the quality of a high end retailer and we're shopping for office supplies here. They now know the importance of good CS.   There is an OM closer to my home, but when I am in need of office stuff, I drive the extra distance to this OF. One reason I like this Office Depot, is that I can get certain supplies such as: paper clips, rubber bands, binder clips, etc. in the color orange. Orange is my favorite color and kinda my signature color, so it seems appropriate to have these daily work items in orange. Oh, who am I kidding - the reason I buy these things in orange is so I know when some one has "stolen" my desk stuff.  Great store. Clean, well organized, good selection and as mentioned above - very good customer service.   Feels kind of weird giving an office supply store a 4, but they deserve it.

It doesn't get much better then Olio when it comes to hand crafted specialty cocktails. It still amazes me that this cool, relaxing little bar is a renovated 1930's gas station. I wish Edward Hopper was alive today, because I'd love to see his vision of this classy bar. It would be so cool to see myself and Norm H. enjoying one of the amazing drinks made by our favorite mixologist John. I just call my vodka and let John create whatever he thinks I'll enjoy and he has never led me wrong.   Sitting at the bar and watching the bartenders mix, shake and serve up cocktails is like watching the Food Network for booze live. The music provided by a turntable playing vintage vinyl records, adds to the magical atmosphere.   One of my favorite treats to enjoy while sipping my cocktail is the Egg Salad. Be sure to add the white anchovies for an additional $3, it is totally worth it. That salty little fish, adds a boost of flavor to the creamy egg salad. I so want this in my lunch sack for work.   Happy Hour or late night drinks, Olio is the place to be seen and enjoy. It is good for romantic couples or groups of friends out for fun. Hope to see you the next time I'm at Olio.

Surprise, Surprise, yes I am actually surprised. With the way this donut shop was being promoted,  I thought for sure i was going to be a hater. However, once I visited and saw the selection and tasted their magic, I was sold.  It is a great addition to the mix of businesses in Maplewood.  You can call them "strange", but I call them creative.   On my first visit I tripped on the wild side with five different donuts. I wanted to experience as much as possible.  I shared them, so don't judge me,  in reality I only ate two and half donuts. Here's their breakdown:  Apple Fritter - It was good as World's Fair and Donut Drive-In, which I consider to be two of the best mom and pop donut shops in STL.   Bart's Revenge - Chocolate, Chocolate Icing and Crumbled Butterfinger, give me a cold glass of whole milk and forget the fat free. It may be Bart's revenge, but it is a true delight.   M & M - Yellow cake donut, white icing and crushed M & M's piled high. I love M & M's, but less M & M's would make this one better.   Chocolate Icing - A simple donut with chocolate icing and sprinkles. Like their icing, I have never been a sprinkle fan, but I went outside of my comfort zone. After all, it is Strange Donuts.   Gooey Butter - Didn't get the GB, but it was a very flavorful donut, that goes great with a nice dark roast coffee.   The staff has bubbly personalities and their smiles are contagious. The space is compact and they use the space well. My only negative was the overly loud music.  It may help your donut makers in back jam, but it was a little overbearing for this customer.   Looking forward to my next "Strange Donut".

Nothing will get me to go west beyond 270 quicker then an International Supper Club gathering. What motivation to expand my horizons, eat with fellow Yelpers and enjoy some international cuisine. The hospitality of Spiro's was outstanding and my entree was so good, I will be venturing west of 270 without the need of a ISC gathering.   10 vivacious foodies arrived at the Chesterfield Spiro's around 6:30 PM. I do not think Harry the Maitre d and Stacy our sensational server knew what they were in for, but they handled us all like champions. They made each one of feel special and unique. Stacy was incredible, that girl knew how to sell not only the steak, but the sizzle as well. Or in my case, she sold me on the Scallops.   I love scallops, but already had selected what I wanted this evening. My mind was made up, so I thought. Then when Stacy in her perky, animated way described the grilled sea scallops on top of linguine, I was persuaded to change my order. I was so glad I did, those six huge sea scallops melted in my mouth. The grill marks were like I was eating a meaty steak. The bed of linguine underneath the scallops was filled with various fresh vegetables.   Harry kept stopping by the table to check on us and making sure everything was good. However, with an outstanding server like Stacy we were in good shape and enjoying our night of Greek Cuisine.   After a night at Spiro's, I'm creating two new list; Sea Scallops and Sensational Service.

Incredible lunch, that totally blew my New Years diet and I am totally fine with that.  After lunch today, we can not wait to go back and experience their dinner menu. Pan D'olive may well be on its way to being a favorite.   After receiving our ice tea, a basket of fresh house made breads and olive oil was served. The baguette was great, but the olive bread was the star of the basket. I'd love to know how Sam makes it, it is that good. The olive oil was very light, making it a perfect accent to the olive bread.   We then ordered two small plates; Calamari and Mussels. The Calamari was the best I have had in the metro area. So many other restaurants over cook Calamari, leaving to dried out and tough chew. Here it was done to perfection, it was tender and an easy chew.  We also shared an order of Mussels. Yippee, I have another addition to my, "I Want Mussels" list. I could not resist the garlic, tomato, clam jus. The extra slices of baguette came in handy for soaking up the broth.  Our two lunch entrees were true Mediterranean fare. I had the Grilled Salmon with lemon and capers with a side of sautéed spinach that would have made Popeye happy. The SO enjoyed the Trout which was Walnut Encrusted and also served with that amazing spinach that makes Popeye a strong man. I am not a fan of walnuts, but it added an incredible flavor to this trout. It almost made me nutty for this trout.   We were filled after our small plates, but pushed on and still enjoyed our entrees. Being truly filled after the entrees, we knew we couldn't stop. Being true Yelpers, it was our duty to try a dessert so our review of a new establishment was complete.  I wanted Creme Brûlée, but the SO is over Creme Brûlée, so we went with the Hazelnut Tiramisu. Once again I am not a fan of nuts on my food, but I liked it. Normally I find Tiramisu to be too sweet, but not here. It had just the right amount of sweetness. Next time, I'm getting the Creme Brûlée and enjoy it all by myself.   When I go back, I'm trying the Lamb Sliders.

Drizzle, Drazzle, Drozzle, Drone. Time a this one to have a frozen custard.   One of the rewards of shopping at Garden Heights Nursery on Big Bend is being able to enjoy a treat from Mr. Wizard. I have recently had enough sweet treats, that I am now in a position to agree with Stephanie S.. Ted Drews can only wish he could be as good as Mr. Wizard.   The custard at Mr. Wizard is richer, creamier and more flavorful then TD's. It is so good, I can even enjoy his custard plain with no toppings. When I do, they add just the right amount of topping to the concrete. They even have me expanding my choices in flavors. My most recent choice was Nestle Crunch.   I am thankful that I do not live close to Mr. Wizard. If I did, I would find some reason to reward myself with a custard treat almost everyday and I'd most likely end up being  the same size as the governor of New Jersey.

Yawn! Boring. Nothing special. Chocolate Covered Cherry use to be my go to order, but tonight it fell flat. My taste buds felt no excitement while I ate my, concrete.   What happened to you Mr. Wizard? I use to love you, but you were totally bland tonight. To be honest, there was absolutely no flavor to your custard tonight. I also am doubting if your staff got my order right. I think they actually served me yogurt instead of custard.   Product wise, I'd give you 2 Stars, but the friendly and professional young lady working the window got you the extra star.   When: July 19, 2016 Why: Ice Cream/Custard Sweet Treat

Sometimes you have to revisit a place before writing a review on Yelp. My first visit here when they first opened was not stellar and I held off on my review until I was able to come back and give them a second chance. Giving them six months made a difference.   My second visit was after Reeds made the STL 100 list. If it made Ian's list, I knew I had to give them a second chance. However, I also knew I wasn't going to be able to order Ian's "must order", Braised Beef Cheek. I'm adventurous, but on this night I didn't want to be trying something new and have it jeopardize my second visit.   Dining alone, I opted to sit at the bar and enjoy my meal. I was torn between the catfish or Reed's Cheeseburger. I decided I had enough catfish during lent, so I went with the cheeseburger. Ian was right with his comment about the St Louis burger elite, this burger was a true gem. When I ordered it, the bartender informed me that they only prepare it medium rare and asked it that was okay with me. Of course it was, that is how I normally order my red meat.   It was juicy, tender and perfectly done. The melted white cheddar was draped evenly over the entire burger. I was totally impressed with the garnishment of the burger. I would have never thought of putting a pickled green tomato on a burger. Also, the use of boston bib lettuce gives this burger more class then a typical cheeseburger. The fries were slender and crisp and accompanied with a little cup of ketchup. The burger had a side of tallow aioli, which I used for the fries. The burger was seasoned well enough and that pickled tomato was perfection for me. I'll be back to try the catfish.   Bartender, other wait staff and manager on duty were all attentive and friendly. Probably the best service I've gotten sitting & eating at a bar.   The big negative I have for Reed's and my advice to you, is do not let them sit you upstairs. It is claustrophobic, cramped and dark. If they start to take you up the steps, tell them you'll wait for a table downstairs and go enjoy a drink at the bar.   When: April 24, 2016  Why: Dinner & STL 100

I live right in the middle of Colors of Springs and another nursery. I will be honest and say, I support both of them. However, I will say when it comes to trees, bushes and roses, I buy them at Colors of Spring.  I am amazed at how healthy and beautiful their selections are, and how they have flourished in my yard. I've bought 4 trees, 5 bushes and 3 roses and love'm all.  Their staff came to my house and assisted us in the placement of our new landscaping. Not being versed in planting, I paid for their services to plant our new landscaping. We've gotten so many complements on our yard thanks to Colors of Spring.

Yippie! I am so happy that Tim Hortons has opened near my work. This location is conveniently located on Lafayette Avenue, just up from the 55 South and 44 West exits.  It makes it so easy for me and my co-workers to make a quick stop before clocking in at work.  This truly is a; Location, Location, Location - location.   I'm a coffee purist, I enjoy my coffee plain and black. I love the Tim Hortons dark roast, it is way better then some of the other leading coffee shops and donut chains. The House Blend ain't bad either.  I'm also a big fan of donut holes, so it goes without saying that I love a box of Tim Bits. My other favorite sweet treat from Tim is his Chocolate Long John. What sets his above the others is the icing itself, it's not overly sweet, but has a rich chocolate flavoring. Being a Canadian chain, the donut itself isn't as heavy and cake like as most local donuts, it is lighter and fluffier.   The staff is friendly and being a new store, they are quickly learning their morning routine.  I'm fairly confident this is going to be my new stop for coffee in the mornings, I'll just have to use strong self-control so I don't get a sweet treat everyday.   Will I return? Absolutely.   When: Mornings Thursday-Sunday Why: Morning Coffee and Sweet Treats for co-workers

My recent visit to The Block, gives them an extra star. I'm happy to say, the CWE location is now on the same level as their sister location in Webster Groves.   As those who follow my reviews, know I am a big fan of Fried Green Tomatoes. So when I saw them on the menu as an appetizer, I couldn't resist. Their green tomatoes were almost like a salad with the additional mixed greens and strips of bacon. The coating around the tomatoes was thick and crispy, but still giving you the great taste of fresh green tomato. If dining at lunch time, it could almost be a meal itself.   My entree was the Pork Chop, which was thick, tender and juicy. It was served in a hot cast iron skillet with sautéed vegetables. I love the other white meat and The Block always serves it up well.   I saved room for dessert, so I was excited to try their Vanilla Bean Creme Brûlée. It was a sweet treat.  If creme brûlée is on the menu, I order it and The Block, did it well. I'm always amazed at the crisp top on a brûlée and how creamy it is beneath. The vanilla flavor of this one, was strong which is fine with me, since vanilla is my favorite flavor.  A special touch that I like here at The Block is the way they serve salt & pepper. They don't use the typical shakers, they have small ramekins with tiny spoons. I've never had to use them, my food has always been seasoned well, but I like the unique presentation.   I'll be returning soon to try their burger for lunch. Plus, I want more Brussels Sprouts, since I didn't enjoy an order this visit.   When: June 25, 2006 Why: Dinner

I've eaten here several times and I can tell you it is a step above sports bar grub. The portions are excessive, so excessive that most diners walk out carrying an eco-unfriendly container with leftovers. I'd rather have a portion I can finish so I am not putting a Styrofoam container in a landfill.   As stated, the bar food is typical sports bar grub. The pizza is by far the best thing on their menu and the wings come a close second. Both are perfect for sharing with a group of friends.  My most recent lunch was a burger. I choose the Jalapeno which was stuffed with the spicy pepper and cover with  Soft Cheddar Cheese with slices of Jalepeno Peppers. I enjoyed it, by the time I took my last bite I had little beads of sweat on my forehead. Sweat means those peppers were damn good. Next time I order it, I will have them hold the bun and give me half the cheese topping(remember, I said they do things in excess).  The staff is friendly, but sometimes the service is slow as stated in other reviews. Slow service is okay if you're there watching a game, but when you want to get in and out for a work lunch it is not acceptable. Staff is easy to spot, they are all in neat black Joey B's t-shirts and the bartender is dressed in a Target Cami (good for getting bigger tips).

My New Year's Day started off with a pleasant surprise. Actually, I first was disappointed when the restaurant I wanted to enjoy lunch was closed for the holiday. As I drove home from Kirkwood, grumbling all the way, I tried to think of  places closer to home that would be open. As I drove past Joey B's, their busy parking lot beckoned me .   I was greeted and seated immediately by a hostess with, attitude. It was obvious she did not want to be working a holiday.  When my server, McKenzie approached  the table to my drink order, her attitude was just the opposite. She was cheerful, fun and made my first dining out experience of the new year a good one.   As she fetched my Pale Ale, I read the burger section, since that is what I was craving. I really wanted my usual, the Jalapeño Burger, but decided to  try their Cowboy Burger. After all, it did win best burger in St. Louis Magazine. However, I went in a totally different direction when McKenzie returned with my brew and told me the daily special. It was a House Salad and Mac-n-Cheese (Baked). She told me it was Shell pasta and a blend of two cheeses; Cheddar and Provel. I almost said, "no thanks", but thought of my Mac-n-Cheese list here on Yelp and that I needed to be more adventurous in 2014. So I said, "Yes" and am glad I didn't go the way of  the burger.   The House Salad was huge. It was a combination of Iceberg and Romaine lettuces. Normally I am not a fan of Iceberg, but being in a mix is okay. I choose their House dressing which is a creamy Italian. Major kudos to the kitchen for tossing the salad in an appropriate amount of dressing. When my Mac-n-Cheese arrived, it had spots of crispy cheese, where you can tell it had been baked or under the broiler. For me it is a nice touch to the presentation. The cheese blend was flavorful, I didn't mind the Provel being in the mix at all. It was served with two slices of Toasted Garlic bread. The serving was large, so I was only able to enjoy half of it at the restaurant. The other half and one slice to the Garlic Toast made a great lunch for work the next day.   Chatting more with McKenzie after eating, we both confessed our dislike of Provel. Neither of us like it on our pizza or burger, but thought it was very tasty in this Mac-n-Cheese. I enjoyed it so much, I'm going to add it to my list, even if it is made with Provel. Keep in mind, this is a frequent daily special and is not always on the menu.

How loud would you like me to sing the praises of 21st Amendment? Never mind, you really don't want to hear me sing, I sing off key. However, I will tell you that there is nothing off key about this small boutique sized bar. It is old school charming, leaving you totally relaxed and ready to conquer the world. Or at least, more of the French Quarter.   I stopped in here around 3 PM-ish and followed the advice of Charles H. and enjoyed a Old Fashioned. I am so glad that the character Don Draper on Mad Men brought back the love of this classic drink. It has become one of my regulars in my rotation of cocktails. Feeling the classic vibe of this bar as I entered, I knew they would make a fine one and they did.   Jason the bartender told me about the live music that night and suggested I come early to nab a seat, because it eventually would be standing room only. The rest of my day got changed around and I didn't make it back, but that leaves me something to look forward to on my next visit to NOLA.   When: August 28, 2016 Why: Don Draper's favorite cocktail

I had to raise my rating to 5 Stars after Friday nights dinner at Farmhaus. Everything we had was totally off the charts. We had a blast sharing comments about our feast with the table of ladies next to us.  Our table started out with Butternut Squash Soup, Roasted Mushroom Salad and Fish Chowder. I wish the bowl of Fish Chowder was bottomless, it was that amazing. The seared Tuna Steak Floating in the bowl was the best Tuna I have ever experienced.  Our entree's were the Escolar and the Bacon Wrapped Meatloaf. Both melted in your mouth, with the Escolar getting the highest marks. I wanted to try the Blackened North Carolina Amberjack, but having a guest from Texas I wanted him to experience the "famous" meatloaf. The desserts, let me just say I'll be doing extra laps around Tilles Park.  Service at Farmhaus is incredible, they always friendly and make me feel special. If you haven't gone to Farmhaus  I have only one question for you. What are you waiting for? When you go I recommend reservations, it's that popular.

First I have to thank the BBQ place across the street for having a ridiculous long line at 1:15PM. Their line was at the backdoor, and we were told it would be 45 minuets to an hour before we could be served. Sorry, but no BBQ is that good. So across the street we go to experience The Good Pie for the first time and we were glad we did.  This has to be the best pizza pie in Saint Louis. The ambiance is rustic and charming. I love the exposed brick and old bicycles as art. The tables are a mixture of high tops and regular height tables, we chose a high top. We could see the wood burning oven where they bake the pies from our table and it was fun to watch the chefs create masterful pies.   We took advantage of the lunch special which is available 11AM till 1:30PM.  To experience two toppings we ordered one sausage and one Genoa salami and we each got the Caesar salad. I highly recommend adding white anchovies for an additional $2.50. It will add an extra kick to a already top notch Caesar. Keep in mind their dressing is house made and is done with raw eggs. If you forget, they have a raw egg warning on the menu.   Both toppings kicked ass, but if i had to choose only one it would be the sausage. The fact that they use fresh Mozzarella Cheese, is awesome. What I found cool, is that the pies were not perfectly round, they had a slight oval or deformation. One of our pies was slightly burned on the edges, it added character and flavor.   Our server was friendly and to our surprise as we chatted, we found out he was one of the owners.  We continued to chat through out our lunch and he ask us to share our honest opinion with him before we left. We told him, we'd be back and that they truly had the best pizza pie in the Lou.  Now we need to go experience their other restaurant, Half & Half and if it is half as good as The Good Pie it too will blow my taste buds.

Attention: I hope my 5 Star Rating draws attention to their need for DONATIONS. My recent visit found thin and boring retail racks. Please donate, especially men's clothing.   What a major disappointment. I had heard such great things about this shop, so I thought I'd give it a visit. I was shocked at the small and poor variety of items. I hate to admit it, but I have more clothes at home in my closets and off season racks in the basement then they did in their entire mens department. I felt so bad for them, that it inspired me to go home and clean out my closets to make a donation. Which I will be dropping off next week.   This charitable organization does such great work in our community. Their work alone deserves 5 Stars. The Scholarship Foundation of St. Louis is a nonprofit organization providing access to higher education throughout our community. They provide interest-free, fee-free loans and grants to over 600 area students. That's something our government doesn't even do.   Please, donate and shop the ScholarShop.   When: June 28, 2016 Why: Checking it out.

I've tried to come back to you this year Ted, but it just isn't working for me anymore.  Your custard isn't as thick and creamy as it once was and your staff is developing attitude.   You are no longer the only custard in town, you now have competition and they are all serving up a better product. Even Andy the new boy in town is providing a superior cup or cone of custard.   I know I am giving a big thumbs down to a St. Louis institution, but it really isn't that good, guys and gals.

When: March 2 & March 7 Why: Lunch & late night dinner  We found another surprise in our neighborhood and another reason to kick ourselves in the ass. Many moons ago when Bellacinos opened I ate there, and never went back. Now I wonder why.   Our first experience was a grinder for lunch. We ordered the Italian Grinder - House Specialty (18"). I was totally impressed. The "Yellow" sandwich shop should take lessons from this place. The bread is made from scratch & baked oven fresh daily. Unlike the "yellow" place who barely puts anything in their sandwiches, Bellacinos fills theirs with quality meats, cheese and vegetable toppings. You can make your Grinder a complete meal by adding chips and a soda.   The grinder was so good, we wanted to try the pizza. Again we went with a house specialty, Bellacino's Pride. It had hand-tossed cross, but was still cut into squares like a St. Louis style pizza. The sauce had a spicy little flavor to it and they were very generous with toppings. They use mozzarella cheese, so those who detest provolone  will be happy.   A big plus, they deliver with no minimum order. They do however, add 15% gratuity for delivery which is fine with me. Our delivery was very quick. The customer service in house and on the phone was polite and good.   We will be going back and having delivery again, they proved they do both grinders and pizza well.

U Gas I gotta tell you, while you were being built I was miffed that you were coming into my neighborhood. I thought the last thing we needed is another gas station with a convenience store inside. Now that you are open, I can see that you are truly an industry leader.  Your store is crispy, clean, spacious and the staff is friendly.   I was totally impressed with your liquor selection. It may be small, but the selection and prices were good. You have my favorite Vodka and it is cheaper then other places on sale. You also have a good selection of other beverages.   I just took a quick look at the prepared foods by Gigi and I can tell you when I need a quick breakfast or a lunch on those days I was too lazy to pack one Gigi will be coming to my rescue.   Now let's talk about your gas prices. Did you know that your prices are as low as Costco and Sam's Club and all I have to do is pay cash. Hot damn, I now know where I will be buying my gas.   Welcome to the Lindenwood Park neighborhood!  I look forward to having you in my hood.

Nathalie's is a true farm to table restaurant. It is owned by Overlook Farms, so it definitely is connected to a "green" farm.  Not only is it green and farm to table, but it also gives you the white linens dining experience at a very affordable price. We were impressed from our starter, to the entrees and the finale of a fabulous dessert.   I was anxious to experience Nathalie's, so I made sure we were one of the first to be seated on their opening night to the public. My jaw dropped when I saw how they transformed the interior. The soft green walls with gold leafing  trim gave a warm sophisticated feel to the dining rooms on the main level. They also, redid the fireplaces, so being seated next to a working fireplace on a cold winter night added the beautiful ambiance.   We begun our feast with Crispy Sesame Quin Crab Cake (2) and Pate Maison. The crab cakes were served with a small side avocado, grapefruit salad with a citrus vinaigrette. The cakes were thick and impressive in flavor. Our second starter was their Pate Maison. To accompany the pate on the Cristin, the plate had red onion jam, grain mustard and dried cherries. Both of these starters went well with my Prosaic.   Our entrees were an amazing set of chops. I enjoyed the Pretzel Crusted Pork Chop and Brad experienced their Pomegranate Lamb Chops. Both were outstanding, but he by far had the best chops. They prepared those lamb chops to a perfect temperature of medium rare. Lucky for me, I was able to snatch one of the chops off his plate. The Pomegranate demo glaze was a unique twist on one of my favorite meats.   My Pork chop was huge and a thick cut. Even with the current pretzel craze, I would have never thought of crusting a pork chop. It was served with Braised Red Cabbage and German Potato Salad. The lamb chops were served with Goat beard Farm Moussaka, that a vegetarian would love as an entree.   We finished our night off sharing only one dessert. No we weren't being cheap, we were just that full. We choose the Iberia Cake, which is a flour less chocolate, cinnamon, almond, orange with a panache glaze. If I were not already a fan of flour less cake, this one would have converted me.   The staff was super attentive to all details. Napkins were placed on our laps and refolded each time we left the table. When replacing silverware, an entire tray of silverware presented in pockets made from napkins  was carried to the table. We also had the privilege of meeting the owner Nathalie and the Executive Chef Jimmy.  I think Nathalie's is going to be one of the new hot spots to be seen dining in the future.

It's time to update my review for Five Star Burgers and I think I'll give them a raise. It is a well deserved raise, as they never disappoint me. I have learned, that with this location it is best for single diners (those dining alone) and those without "little people" to dine in the bar area. Kirkwood is a great family community and at times the main dining room, can be like a family reunion or day care center field trip. It will be bursting with high energy "little people" and dining in the bar area, allows for a more relaxed dinning experience.  I'm normally a specialty burger guy, I love their; Bison, Lamb and Potsticker burgers. However, today I had to order the Dad's Green Chile Cheeseburger. My ex always use to order it and now Ian Froeb says, it is the "must order". All I can say is, "Hello, Daddy!". Where has this burger been all my life? Why haven't I ordered it before? I can admit Ian is right, but damn saying the ex has been ordering the best burger is a hard one to swallow-LOL.   I ordered my burger medium and the server confirmed that I wanted a solid pink center and I confirmed, yes. The Angus beef at Five Star is all natural, it's hormone and antibiotic free. Trust me, you can taste the difference. Dad's cheeseburger is topped with Pepper Jack Cheese, Crispy New Mexico Hatch Chiles and a smear of Green Chile Mayonnaise. I have no need, for the; tomato, onion and lettuce that they offer on the side. The green chilies and pep jax cheese make a perfect burger and a small order fries are the perfect side.   When: April 18, 2016 Why: PM Meal & STL 100

I came the other night with a large group of friends. It was our monthly International Supper Club gathering. We were seated at two large tables, since there was about 14-16 of us in attendance.   I wasn't that hungry, so I ordered two appetizers as my entree; Fried Spring Rolls and Crab Rangoon. The spring rolls came with 4 to the order and the rangoon had 5. The Crab Rangoon's were larger then most and the pocket was full of creamy cheese and a fair amount of crab. For the price, I couldn't expect a full crab leg in each rangoon. They were better then any carry-out Chinese.   The Fried Spring Rolls were a major disappointment. They basically were nothing more then a rolled pastry shell. The inside was filled with air and the vegetables inside could not even cover my thumb nail.   We had two servers and they were like the stereotypical cops, one playing good server and the other playing bad server. When one of our guest questioned the preparation of her favorite Thai dish, the one almost became argumentative. When they spoke in their native language (which is fine),  about the situation, you could tell the one was trying to make the situation right.   Once my friend got her right entree, I think she had the best dish of the night. It looked so good, I'd like to return and enjoy it.   Dealing with a large group, the kitchen had a good flow of the food to our table so I give them around of applause for that.   When: March 13, 2016 Why: International Super Club

If you need a gadget or gizmo for cooking or baking, chances are you'll find it here at Kitchen Conservatory. KC is like a Williams-Sonoma, Sur LaTable and the kitchen department at Bed, Bath and Beyond on steroids.  Instead of shopping a chain, you can shop local and buy your gadgets and gizmos here. You'll pay substantially more, but it is worth it because you are supporting a local business. Also, it is common sense that the knowledge from the staff is worth the extra cents.   I've heard their cooking classes are some of the best in the city, so I'll be checking them out so I can hopefully bump them up a star or two.

This is not my usual Lowe's, but next time I need to shop the "Big Box" I will think of this one. During a recent rain and wind storm, I lost one of my favorite ceramic pots. My banana plat survived, but I was left with a "cracked pot" and it was orange my favorite color.   I went on a mission shopping, trying to find a replacement. I wasn't even looking for another orange pot, I just wanted a style and size that could accommodate my plant. Being the end of September, my selection of pots was limited. Or at least pots that meet my standards. This Lowe's was my fifth store, yes I was that obsessed with finding the right pot.  As I entered their garden area, it was love at first sight. It was the right size, not breakable, on sale and it was orange. I could not have been happier.   My usual Lowe's is Kirkwood or Loughborough, but now that Maplewood has won my heart, I'll be back. Funny thing, the Maplewood location is closer to my home. I guess Dorothy is right, "there is no place like home".

Everywhere we go, people want to know, who we are...... We are the birds, the mighty, mighty birds.......  That is part of an old high school cheer. I'm a graduate of Southwestern High School and the Piasa Bird was our mascot. So the Piasa Bird has a special place in my heart. Growing up in the area, I remember another location of the bird being painted on the bluffs. It was sit back further from the road, so this present day location is more tourist friendly.   When visiting the Alton and Grafton area, it is worth a stop to view the painting and to read the legend of the mighty, mighty Piasa Bird.

I am glad we have another option for dining while shopping at the Galleria besides the food court and The Factory. However we've got to be honest, it is a chain restaurant that is an upscale version of Houlihan's and Applebee's.   I was anxious to try BlackFinn again after attending a special VIP Dinner Party. I wanted to see how the "real service" was going to be. We were seated for lunch at approximately 12:45PM and there were a few booths filled around us. Different servers were attending to their needs, but no one acknowledged us. We finally spoke up as one was serving tea to another table and asked if we could get some tea too.  He quickly responded and sent our server over with our tea. Once we got our tea, our server was very attentive explaining the lunch specials and various other points on the menu. So, I will attribute the slowness at first to new opening jitters.   Our lunch begun with an order of Crispy Calamari, which also has cherry pepper  mixed in with the Calamari. A big bonus for us being fans of Jalapenos, was the fact that there were also slices of Jalapeno fried with the Calamari and peppers. For me, this just made this better then any other Calamari I have experienced recently in Saint Louis.   Our lunch entrees were Stir Fry with Chicken and Fish - n - Chips.  The Stir Fry was by far the best of the two. Like I said in my review of the VIP Dinner, the vegetables were done to perfection. Vegetarians are going to love this place. For our SF we added chicken, you can also add shrimp. Our chicken was tender and moist, but when I order this again and I will it will be just the veggies.   The Fish - n - Chips was your typical FnC, nothing to write home about, so do not expect a post card. It fulfilled my craving for fried fish, which you would have thought should end after Lent. The Haddock had a beer batter that was extremely crisp and the fish was flaky and the french fries crispy the way a fry should be.   I will return, in fact next week I will be back to check out their Happy Hour.

A spin-off just never seems to be as good as an original. I love Lester's in Ladue, I can always count on good food, good service and a fun time.  This spin-off location captures the look and good food, but lacked in service.   A friend was celebrating an anniversary of her birth and since half the guest were west county residents we choose this Lester's. I was the first to arrive of our group. That was my plan as I needed a nice cold Stella Artois. The bar crowd was not as "party" as the Ladue location. It was a more mature and stuffed shirt crowd. However, I was able to enjoy a Stella before the other guest arrived.   Once our party of six arrived, we were seated in the dining room. We quickly ordered a round of alcoholic beverages and begun to scan the menu for our selections. The guest of honor had not eaten at Lester's before, so I provided her with several suggestions. None of which she took. Which proves you can lead a horse to water, but you can't make them drink.   Once our liquid refreshments arrived we ordered our appetizers and entrees. As appetizers, we had two orders of pretzels with mustard and onion rings. Before we could even pass the apps around the table, here came a manager with our main dishes. Talk about poor timing, made it feel as if they were already rushing us out the door.   The onion rings were crisp, not limp like many rings are at sports bars. They'd been a good side for a burger. Our pretzels with the two mustard's were a disappointment. Once you have had the pretzels at The Tap Room, you are spoiled from other bar pretzels.   Six people dining and five ordered the Pulled Pork Sandwich. I was not one of the five. I always have to march to my own drum. They all enjoyed their sandwiches and sides. Poor babies, none of them have ever been to Pappy's or Bogart's.   I ordered the Lemon Pepper Chicken Wings and a side of Fries. As always I had them to the wings extra-crispy. For me that just seems to bring the flavor out and the meat inside is still juicy. They offer their wings in 6 & 12. I opted for the 12 knowing 6 would be going home for the SO.  I had a good giggle, as the honoree patted me on the arm and said, "they weren't very good" pointing to my other six wings. I grinned and replied, "no, they were damn good. these are going home for later'.   Earlier I informed the server that i needed a half order of ribs to go. This time he had his timing right and brought them out just as he passed the separate tickets out. Providing separate tickets is a nice touch. A shame he was spacey and hit-n-miss while serving.  My (for Brad) Ribs carry-out was tasty. The baked beans and cole slaw were both New York Deli good. The ribs themselves were meaty but, not fall off the bone.These you had to work to clean the bone.  When choosing between the two Lester's, I prefer Ladue.

We've expanded our Bono experience and tried their Calzone and am glad we did. It was awesome, a nice change from doing pizza and wings.   Calzone & salad a perfect lunch for when stuck at home alone.

Once again the International Supper Club has introduced me to a new restaurant. Going to these monthly gatherings has expanded my taste and horizons. I have always been a fan of Tapas type restaurants, but had not been to Mojo. So when I saw that last meeting was going to be here, I jumped at the opportunity to attend.   It was a Tuesday night and they had a special on their Housemade Sangria when you bought a pitcher, so why indulge and enjoy more then one glass. Don't worry I didn't drink all the nectar myself, several of us shared.  I'll try it by the glass next time I visit to see if there is a difference in flavor. I found the pitcher to be good in flavor, but weak in the kick of liquor.   With all the flavorful small plates available I could not believe I found myself ordering a Mojo Burger, but I am glad I did. There will be many other visits to expand my Mojo taste buds. The burger was a meaty 8 oz of beef, topped with a spicy chipotle BBQ Sauce, Cheddar Cheese and Crispy Red Onion Straws. It was so perfect, there was no need to add any additional condiments. As a side they gave me a hearty portion of Battered Fries dusted with Garlic & Parmesan and a little cup of Housemade Spicy Ketchup. I love my ketchup served in a little cup. Take note of my list of other places who offer this as well.   Our bartender was friendly and ready to help us party. Which got our evening off to a great start. Then our server was just there. He took our orders and brought us our food with no personality. Which I guess was alright, because we had all the fun people at our table enjoying supper.   I'm going back for Sexy Grits and an order of Mussels.

Great little new pet shop, that is off the beaten path. If it is near your neighborhood, it is well worth searching out. It is just east on Elchelberger off Hampton.   They have a good selection of premium pet foods, toys and collar & leashes. What also makes this place stand out is the friendly staff and customer service. I also liked the area where you can wash your own four legged friend for a minimal fee.   We're all taking the Yelp pledge to shop local and this would be a great place to shop for you fur-babies.

When is Yelp going to give us the 1/2 star? This visit on their third day open was a solid 31/2 stars. This is close enough to my home that I know I will be a regular this spring and summer once the huge patio opens.   We meet after work at the bar and pigged out on some delicious low-carb treats.  Being a fan of Mussels, I enjoyed how they prepared theirs with bacon, thyme and Porter. It was a nice twist. A big piece of bacon with a mussel was very tasty.   My vegetarian friends will love the Cauliflower Gratin. Fresh cauliflower, seasoning and cheese, what is not to like. I thought they cooked the cauliflower perfectly, it was soft with just enough firmness for a crunch. Miss. Norma,  would prefer that it was cooked a little more, she wanted less crunch. Either way, the flavor was a winner.   The stand out of our three dishes was the board of Charcuterie, and Artisan Cheese.  Their terrine became a battleground, we all loved it and wanted the last bite. A nice touch to their board, the names of the cheeses was written on a piece of paper so you knew what you were enjoying. One of the servers came over and made sure someone told us about them. I was amazed, he explained how each of them was prepared and a little history as well. Nice touch, TFT.   Having gone low-carb, I am looking forward to going back and enjoying the 12 oz. New York Strip Steak. They serve it with Roasted Mushrooms, which is so low-carb friendly.   The bartenders and servers we interacted with were friendly and professional. The bar area is open with a high ceiling which is the original tin, which makes for a loud environment. The music when you could hear it, did not fit the vibe. It was as if you were listening to, KSHE.  I will forewarn you, parking is a challenge. There is a small lot and the street. So good luck on getting prince or princess parking.

Walking here and back home, helps me justify the calories. (Round trip is about 5 miles) My favorite concrete is M & M's, for some reason - I just keep ordering it time again and again. I also like raspberry. However, every year my first order is always just a dish of the custard plain - to experience the best frozen custard in the Midwest. Whatever your favorite is, it will make a great concrete or sundae. You'll also enjoy checking out all the celebrity autographs in the window

Making New Years resolutions, that involve living a healthier lifestyle sometimes forces you to shop at stores that normally are not on your store radar.  That was the case with this Sports Authority and I must say they impressed me.   We were on a mission to find "manly" yoga socks and were not having much luck.  When we entered the store, I immediately was impressed with its size. I had never seen a SA this big. I guess size does matter, because we not only found what we needed, but received good customer service as well.   Wanting a sport type sock, we walked over to the shoe department thinking they would be there.  In addition to the socks, we also were considering the Vibram Five Finger shoes. Unfortunately they did not carry the Five Finger shoes, but the sales associate was still very helpful. When we asked about the yoga socks, he told us they'd be in the yoga department. The what? Yoga has it's own department? That's impressive alone.   What made him a stellar retail associate for me was the fact that he walked us over to the "yoga" department instead of doing the typical retail trick of pointing and saying "over there".  He assisted us in finding the socks and then excused himself to return to his own department.  We found a "manly" two shades of Grey sock that is going to  work just fine for the beginning yoga class.   The one detail that kept them from getting a 4 star rating is their pricing. The yoga sock was the same brand we found earlier at Whole Foods selling for $9.99 and on sale for 20% off, was selling here for $11.99. Damn it, why did WF only have the girly pink socks in stock.   The cashier girl was friendly & witty making the experience of paying more money then I would have at Whole Foods pleasant.

Johnnie you are my hero. You saved my ass this St. Patrick's Day and I don't think it was just the luck of the Irish. You know your holidays and offer up a large variety of merchandise to meet the needs of all who celebrate.   It was the 16th of March and I had procrastinated getting some green to wear at work on the 17th. I was driving home from work on 44 West and it was almost 5 PM. I   quickly exited at Jefferson and the stoplights were in my favor. The Parking Angels were also with me and I got the space right outside their entrance. As I entered, on the heels of four other shoppers, we were greeted with, "We're closing in 5 minuets". Having been in retail, I know what it is like to have new shoppers arrive right at closing. It's frustrating, but the staff here still gave their A-Game in service.   Johnnie is so smart with his merchandising, he had all the St. Patty's Day stuff up front near the entrance. All of us quickly shopped, found our treasures for the next day and headed to the check out.  I found a great headband, with antennas that had spinning shamrocks on top and a shamrock beaded necklace with a Leprechaun. Everyone loved the headband, so it is a true keeper. I'll be wearing it for years to come.   Don't just think Johnnie Brock's is for Halloween and Mardi Gras, he's got you covered for all the holidays. So let the party begin.

I have an evil co-worker and that is not a bad thing. She's evil, because the other day when she arrived to work she was carrying two pizza boxes from Caleco's. Her shift starts at 1:30 PM, so many of us had already taken our lunch breaks. However, that did not stop us from enjoying a slice of these flavorsome pizzas.  Since the co-worker was surprising us with pizza, she picked the toppings and one of the combinations I would have never thought of. She choose; pepperoni, sausage, onion, cheese and spinach. I like all four toppings, but it would have never occurred to me to mix spinach with pepperoni & sausage. The combination of the toppings provided a tasteful mix of meat & veggie.   However, the one that most of her co-workers were drawn too was the; BBQ Chicken. A pizza made with bbq sauce topped with red onion and white breast chicken and cheese. For those who do not like Provel cheese, here at Provel and Mozzarella. It was the first pizza box to be emptied. Does that tell you how tasty-tasty it was?  I've totally forgotten about Caleco's. I have only used them as a meeting place for a beer before a ballgame. After enjoying these two pizza pies and looking at their menu on line, I need to give them a full visit.   When: January 26, 2017 Why: Co-worker surprised us with pizza

Hey McDonald's, I'm going to give you an idea that can really make McDonald's a "happy place". It will also increase your demographics with the 21+ age group.   Yesterday after a horrific day at work, I wanted a refreshing drink for the drive home. So I took a detour thru your drive-thru to experience your new Frozen Strawberry Lemonade. Ugh, more horror to my day, the $1 try me promo was over and I had to pay regular retail price.   Any way, back to my fantastic idea. Your Frozen Strawberry Lemonade was good and had a great presentation with the two colors swirled together in a clear plastic recyclable glass. To be totally honest, for my taste it was to sweet, I like mine more tart. Make those lips pucker. Gotta get back to the idea.   Here it goes, it will knock those big clown shoes Right off of Ronald's feet. You need to sell miniature bottles of booze to accompany the frozen lemonade. You know what I'm talking about, those cute little bottles you get on the airplane. Just offer a few, I'd recommend Citron & Strawberry Vodka or perhaps a Captain Morgans Rum. Now these will make that frozen lemonade sell.   Of course if you do offer these, picking them up at the drive-thru may endorse drinking and driving. So only make them available at the counter so your employees can ask if we want fries with that.   Side note - This McDonald's has the most normal and polite staff I've seen at a Mickie D's.

Safe and Secure, that is how I feel with ADT Security Services. I originally started out with Brinks Home Security when I had a system installed in my home. Then with mergers and buy-outs, I am now with ADT and in my opinion it is for the best.   When I wanted to get rid of my landline, ADT made it so easy for me to transfer everything over to a cellular program. Most recently, ADT notified me of changes to the cellular program and sent a tech out to my home to make the necessary changes to my equipment. This visit was at not cost to me. That makes me a happy loyal customer.   On occasion I have had to call the customer service department for various reasons and have never had a long wait period. My calls and questions have all been dealt with in a minimum amount of time. I believe that since they are dealing with, "security" that they respond quickly.  If you are looking for a home or business security system - I recommend ADT.

It's New Year's Eve Eve, AKA the night before New Years Eve. The place is basically dead, because everyone else is saving themselves for the next night. We're staying home NYE, so this is our special dinner out.   We started out with Brussels Sprouts as a appetizer. They were flash fried with house smoked bacon, caramelized onions, lemon and toasted almonds. If momma fixed brussels sprouts like this when I was a child I would have loved them back then instead of discovering their fabulous taste in these late years of life. The smoked bacon, lemon and toasted almonds made this vegetable shine. It was a fight to see who could scoop the most up the fastest, we both loved them.  We shared two sides, Mac-n-Cheese and an additional Beef Rib. Mac-n-Cheese was good, but the Webster Groves location does it better. They had a special on Beef Ribs and they were offering additional ribs, so we took advantage. Our rib was fall off the bone tender.  Our entrees were the Amish Chicken and the Pork Chop. I enjoyed the pork chop which a thick cut and was flavorful. When I cut my first bite I was concerned, I thought it was going to be tough.Then I realized it was my steak knife. It wasn't that sharp.  Once my bite was in my mouth, I realized the tenderness. As I ate my chop I didn't see my server to get a new knife, so I just dealt with it.   Brad's Amish Chicken was good, but not the pieces of the bird the waiter said it would be. He was told it would be a thigh and leg and when it was served, it was an Airline Breast. It was fine that it was the breast, but Brad's favorite piece of chicken is the thighs so there was a little bit of disappointment.   The CWE Block was just, A-OK. The Webster Groves, Block is much better all around. I'll give the CWE another try, in hopes it was just an off night. They may have been saving themselves for NYE.

If you're from STL, you know JBD is the place to go for your Halloween costume needs and Mardi Gras Beads. I recently learned it is also the place to go for Elf and Santa Costumes, too.   My cousin told me she was searching for Elf accessories that she could wear when volunteering at the USO's Christmas event. I told her I'd swing by Johnnie's and see what I could find. It was like I found the pot of gold. They had a huge variety of all types of accessories to create a whimsical elf outfit. I was also amazed at the huge selection of tradition style Santa suits in a wide range of prices.   Other departments I noticed on this shopping expedition, was theatrical make-up and crowns. They had an amazing selection of rhinestone tiaras for Homecoming Queens or beauty pageant winners.   The store is huge, well kept and the staff can give you creative ideas to get you started. On occasion, you'll come across the store cat.   I'll be back? - Oh, yes.   When: November 10, 2018 Why: Elf Accessories

I know 5 stars for a donut place is outrageous, but when I need a donut fix this is where I go. What's even more weird, I just like your basic donuts. My favorites are Chocolate Long John and the Traditional Glazed (circle donut with the hole in the center). I really like the the donut holes, the part they cut out to make the hole. I'm glad they make them into their own special treat.

I love this place, the food is good and the drinks are even better. I never make it beyond the bar area.  I always end up eating at the bar so I can not speak of the table service.   I hate to make this call out, but anyone who goes here for Happy Hour or anytime for that matter knows it is a true "meat market" and it does not matter which team you play for. So this makes for a very fun and festive night.

I told you I'd be back to try those Lamb Sliders and I'm here to report they are fantastic. The small plate comes with two thick sliders, topped with tomato and sliced cucumber and mint yogurt on the side. Tonight we over indulged to experience more of the menu, but in the future I know these two sliders and a Caesar Salad are the perfect amount of food.   We also shared an order of  Salmon Bruschetta, which was two large pieces topped with dill ricotta, capers, onion and thin shreds of Salmon. Again a major note to self this, a salad and glass of wine can be a perfect meal.   Next we had, yes there was more food. Don't you remember I said we over indulged. Any way, we each had a Caesar Salad with anchovies. Their website described it with white anchovies which I am a big fan of, but our salads arrived they were "normal" anchovies. When I questioned the difference, they apologized stating they had changed the presentation and forgot to change the website. Being a fan of the white anchovy, I was surprised when the front of the house manager stated the feedback they'd received since opening was anti white. Hey STL, don't you realize the white anchovy taste better?   Finally, we had our entrees and 2/3 of each of them came home for the next days lunch. We knew our eyes were bigger then our stomachs, but we planned it that way. There was a method to our gluttony.  The SO had the Baked Cannelloni with bolognese & béchamel. I went vegetarian with the Capellini with roasted  tomato, mushroom, capers, calamata olives and spicy tomato sauce. These were healthy portions, don't have too many small plates before hand like we did or you'll have to take home in carry out containers that are not eco-friendly.   Again, I must say their house made olive bread is sinfully good. Tonight we sat in the bar area at one of the high tops and it gave us a more informal casual feel then the dining room. Service in the bar was equally attentive and when it's just two dining I think I'd do bar sitting again.   Pan D'olive, I recycle so I was disappointed that  your carryout container was not more eco-friendly. Please find a better alternative to using the Styrofoam and you'll have 5 Stars.

Call 314-647-3800 now and make your reservation for dinner. You will be totally amazed.   Kevin continues to amaze me and the entire city with his creations. He was totally deserving in his Food & Wine Best New Chef 2011 honor.   Last night three of us were dining and sharing. I love sharing small plates, it allow you to experience so much more. Last night the menu had 14 featured items and we shared 9. Some missed their photo opportunity, because we just begun eating soon as it arrived.   Blue Plate Salad - their standard house salad. Always a hit. Hey, Kevin let's bottle that dressing to sell.   Grilled Asparagus Salad - I love asparagus and when combined with mixed greens, goat cheese and grilled ramp Caesar dressin' you have my attention.   Roasted Mushroom Salad - The best salad of the three. Greens, goat cheese, toasted pecans and warm bacon vin. We were all scrambling for the last bite.   Conch Fritters - So good we did it twice.   Beet Risotto - I'll remember it always from the stain on my shirt.   Escolar - Dill and butter poached, grilled Pacific Blue prawns and asparagus. The fish melted in your mouth like the butter that it was poached in. The asparagus was two green & one white - I grabbed the white - best ever.   Grouper - My surprise - best entree of night. Slow roasted with mashed potatoes. We told both tables next to us, to order it. They did and agreed.   Bacon Wrapped Meatloaf - Bacon, Meatloaf and sweet & yukon gold potatoes smashed. Enough said.   Dry Aged Ribeye Grilled - meat was perfection. Again smashed potatoes and asparagus - hot damn.   They offered five desserts, we shared three. By this time I was in food heaven and wine bliss. I remember the basil ice cream taking my breath away and wanting to not share the chocolate. Katie what are you going to dream up next?   On my Yelp profile I have changed my last meal to "dinner @ Farmhaus".

This bread co is my go to before work. I recently changed work locations and am now stationed directly across the street. I'm thrilled that they open early. I usually arrive between 6:30 & 6:45AM, so I can easily be at work at 7.   Arriving early the pastries and bagels are filled to the brim and ready to go. My morning order varies, but I'll say the orange scone is my favorite.  I also, enjoy their dark roast coffee.   The customer service at this location in my opinion is better then the one close to my home in STL and it is much larger. The morning staff is always friendly and remind me about what rewards I have available.   This new food relationship is off to a good start.   Chances of returning: Sun-Tue, you'll find me here.  When: Every Sun-Tue Why: My morning cup of joe

Living Room - Southhampton is a great addition to my hood. It is also a great use of the bar space in Craft Beer Cellars in the early morning hours.   LR serves coffee, other morning specialty beverages and a variety of pastries. They're open 7 AM till 1 PM, six days a week. They're closed on Sunday, so you'll have to go over and visit their location in Maplewood.  My favorite latte is the, Salted Honey. It's the perfect combination of sweet and salty all combined in my morning coffee. My other favorite morning drink is, Britt's Cold Brew.   Unfortunately they do not offer the same delicious hot breakfasts that are available at the Maplewood location. However, they do have the same delicious pastries. I love their scones. I have even tried the gluten-free cookies and they're equally as delicious.   The staff are hipster barista's. They're friendly and take great pride in the preparation of your morning drink.   I'll be back? - Yes, I support my local hood.   When: July 10, 2018 Why: Hot new coffee shop in my hood.

Great pizza! I love thin crust and this is one of the best in town. The toppings are plentiful and the hot chicken wings are great too. Delivery is quick and the staff is friendly. This is our favorite place for a quick meal when we're not up to cooking after a work day.

Oh, sad day in the land of Yelp. I have a new restaurant listing on my No-No list.  Our lunch today at Tin Can Tavern was a total disappointment in all categories.   We started out with chicken wings, that were rubbery and tough. It also grossed me out that I could see the yucky bumps on the chicken skin. I'm not sure, but I think they were just tossed in Frank's Hot Sauce and that was it. The Blu Cheese they served as a side, was thin and soupy. Two strikes, and we have only had our wings.   The burgers were 5 oz of over cooked beef. When we placed our order, the server started to leave the table and Brad stopped him and asked if he wanted to know the temps for them. He said don't worry they'll be fine, we wont over cook'em. Really?  Our burgers were served well - well done. It was like eating the leather sole of your shoe. When ordering, I did not realize they top all burgers with grilled onions and bacon. I pushed mine aside, the bacon was hard and cold.  Side dishes were equally as bad as the burgers and wings. My side was their House specialty Mac - n - Cheese. How they can call this rendition a "specialty" is beyond me. I took one bite and sit it aside. Brad took a bite and said he could not understand how a cook could taste this and say it is good to go, it tasted that heinous. Brad's side was Tater-Tots, it is kinda hard to screw up Tater Tots, but Sonic does a better job.   The service was minimal, the two men working were more interested in watching the hockey game on the TV behind the bar.  They never even took the time to do a follow-up after we were served our food. Were they busy? No, it was us and another table of three ladies only drinking beer.   Hell will freeze and pigs will fly before I come back to this dive bar.

Another discovery through the Taste Cards I bought on LivingSocial. I had no idea I was going to discover so many new restaurants when I bought these cards.  This adventure took us down to Soulard to visit a gin joint, Nadine's Gin Joint.  We stopped in for lunch on a Tuesday so it was kind of slow, only a few other tables out on the patio and us on the inside. When using a Taste Card, I always let the server know up front during the meet & greet. I feel it is only fair that they know we are using a coupon. Like most Taste Cards Nadine's offer is $10 off of $30, no booze.   We started out by enjoying an order of Blackened Chicken Nachos. It was a nice twist to the traditional ground beef nachos. It had large pieces of blackened chicken, Monterrey jack cheese sauce, tomatoes and chives over corn tortilla chips. I would of liked some jalapenos tossed in the cheese sauce for an extra kick.   Normally we order different entrees, but today we both were craving a burger.  I ordered the traditional cheeseburger with pepper jack cheese and the bf enjoyed a Chorizo Burger. The Chorizo burger was suppose to be a mix of chorizo and ground beef, but you could barely taste the Chorizo. His came with pepper jack, red onion & mayo and he requested tomato and lettuce as well. When our burgers arrived, they forgot the additional garnishes.   The burgers were hand pressed, meaty and juicy. Both were grilled to our medium rare request. I was happy with my simple cheese only burger and the hand cut french fries. I liked that the fries were extra crispy and we didn't have to request them that way.  Also, those that know me well, know that I love it when a restaurant serves ketchup in little cups instead making me use a bottle on the table.   I plan to return to try their clams, I've heard great things and Erin's picture makes them look so good.

This is the type of store you'd get if you combined Whole Foods and Lucky's together. It actually reminds me of the Fresh Market store that was on Olive in Creve Coeur and I loved that store. I like the small boutique feeling and the mass selection of organic foods. Being similar to WF & having organic foods, the pricing is on the high end.   The meats and seafood reminded me of the high quality you find at Whole Foods. Their vegetables and fruits selections reminded me of the produce at Lucky's. The merchandising was crisp and clean, making their products very tempting. There was no hard liquor, but they had an excellent variety of wine and craft beers. Their brand offerings are not the typical mass brands you find at our neighborhood grocers in town. It will take some experimenting to get to know these brands.   I was there three hours after opening, so judging the customer service would not be fair. Those that I had interchange with, were friendly. However, you could tell some of the staff was overwhelmed with the volume of people visiting on the first day. I have confidence in them, as time passes, their skills will improve.   Will I return? Most defiantly, I'm in that area often and like variety in my grocery shopping.   When: February 8, 2017 Why: It was their first day opening & I like Grand Openings.

Urban Matter is one of the best kept secrets of the city. It is also one of the absolute best, original and unique gift shops in the metro area. I am so glad that they have chosen STL as their home and location for this amazing store. It is off the beaten path, with nothing else really around it. However, I highly recommend that you visit them this holiday season, or anytime you need a gift for that special someone or that one that is so difficult to buy for. Trust me you'll find it here.   Some of the gifts that caught my eye were; Jord Watches, Spices & Condiments, Cocktail Garnishes and Accessories, Leather Goods, Everything for a man with a beard, Original Jewelry and Adult Coloring Books. I walked out with a couple of gifts and will be going back again before the holiday.   The customer service was friendly and engaging. The young lady working was informative and did not hover around me. She'd leave me alone, but would circle back to see if I had any questions. When I did, she'd answer them effectively without pressuring a sale. It worked, I bought it.   Don't judge this boutique by its location - it is amazing and worth the adventure getting there. If they were in, Maplewood, Kirkwood or Clayton, they'd be packed from open to close.   Shop local and visit this gift shop.   Will I Return: Absolutely - Gotta Shop Local  When: November 9, 2017 Why: Gift Shopping

I have experienced HWK as a single diner. I went to Brunch on April 15th and was to sit at one of the hightop tables in the front window. When I called to make my reservation, Tori the dining room manager answered the phone and was very perky and pleasant. She asked me if the hightop would be acceptable and I responded, yes. When she asked for my name, I admit I did use an alias. I figured they'd be on the alert for a Steven and I did not  want special treatment. Once I gave my name, she commented that she thought I had been there before, but I said "no this will be my first". (I think they knew it was me)  When I arrived that Sunday morning, I was seated at the hightop close to the hostess stand. It was comfortable and I had great light for reading, since I was dining alone.  I love a Bloody Mary at Brunch, HWK calls them a Bloody Wilbur. Their twist has; Bacon Vodka with tomato juice and garnished with pickled asparagus.  I was famished, so I ordered two entrees; Biscuits and Gravy and Eggs Benedict.   After I place my order, John the husband of Cassy approached my table and asked me if I were the Steven from Yelp. Yes, I was busted and I wasn't surprised.  Part of being a good Yelper is taking ownership of your reviews, so with a smile I acknowledged who I was. Our conversation was very pleasant and as Cassy (his wife and executive chef) said to me in private messaging they are thankful I brought the single seating to their attention and apologetic my previous experience.   Now let's talk food, after all that is what restaurant reviews are all about.  I'll break it down item for item.   Bloody Wilbur: Love the bacon vodka, proving everything is better with bacon. I also enjoyed the the garnish of pickled asparagus. Asparagus is my all-time favorite vegetable so adding it to a brunch cocktail, is A-Okay in my book. Their choice of tomato juice, held this drink back from being spectacular. The juice was weak, a rich and thicker type tomato juice have made this classic brunch cocktail truly pop.
