Biscuits and Gravy: They made this old farm boy proud. These truly were some kick ass, B&G. A picture is suppose to be worth a 1000 words, but B&G do not photograph well. So let me tell you the best I can. When you have buttermilk biscuits with chives and cheddar topped with gravy containing huge chunks of sausage - it does not get any better. These Biscuits and Gravy will be added to my Yelp list of Best B&G.   Mimosa: Meyer Lemon is a staple in my kitchen/bar at home. So when I saw that they use it for their mimosa, I was already sold. I found the the sparkling wine served with the Meyer Lemon and honey to be a refreshing twist to traditional Mimosa. Two thumbs up and remember I am dining alone.   Eggs Benedict: No English Muffin, they use a Grits Cake instead which gives an original twist. I'm not a fan of grits and I enjoyed the difference in texture and flavor. The eggs were poached perfectly and the use of Tasso gives it a Cajun kick. They then top it off with a Spicy Hollandaise and Flash Fried Spinach.   I'm glad I finally got to experience HWK and I'll be back for a lunch soon. My rating is more of a 3 1/2 Star (wish Yelp would let us do 1/2's soon). If Wilbur would have been bloody better, it would of been a 4.

Joey B your salads are huge. I don't know how I finished the whole thing, but I did. Glad it was a late lunch, because I will not need to eat dinner now. Wish you offered a half size.   My salad of choice was the Primo House Salad. It was mixed greens, provel and Parmesan cheese, mushrooms, pimentos, green onions, ham and Oldani's salami tossed in their house salad dressing. The salad was a complete meal in a bowl and it was so satisfying.   My dining partner started out with a cup of Potato Bacon Soup and said it was very good. Looking at his spoonfuls of meaty cubes of potato and pieces of bacon, I can only imagine he's telling the truth.   He also went with a huge, salad. He chose the Crispy Chicken Salad with Honey Mustard dressing, since he had been craving one for a while. Sad to say, the only lettuce in this salad was iceberg. It was good, but would be so much better if it were made with mixed greens instead. In addition to the  diced breaded boneless chicken tenders, the salad had green onions, bacon, tomato and shredded cheddar cheese.  The Honey Mustard dressing was served on the side, which is a nice touch. it allows the diner control how much dressing it applied to the salad.   We were not offered and bread with butter or crackers which I appreciated. It made it easier to resist those hateful little carbs. Our iced tea glasses were kept full, which means our server was attentive and aware of our tables needs.   Our salads were so good, I'm adding Joey B's to my Sensational Salads List.

Sometimes when you find a good thing and become a regular at that establishment, you totally forget to update your review on Yelp. Or at least that is what happened to me and Three Flags Tavern. My first review was written after they had only been open a few days, I've been back numerous times, in fact I've been back so many times that a percentage of the staff know my name.   To get caught up I'm just going to highlight things that I order on the regular:  Brisket Burger - It easily is one of the best in the city/bi-state area. It was even highlighted in St. Louis Magazine as one of the Top Six Burgers.   Brussels Sprouts - One of my favorite veggies and they do them well.   Fried Chicken - Crispy, Juicy and just the right amount of spice. I always clean my plate, so no leftovers for the next days lunch.   Steak Frites - Best way to handle a hungry man.   Lobster Beignets - A simple dinner with a glass of Pinot Grigio.  Chicken Wings - Perfect for when sitting at the bar.  Ian Froeb ranked them #25 on his STL 100 List for 2016. So you can see I am not the only one who thinks they are pretty damn good. Added little bonuses for me; they serve their ketchup in little cups and have linen napkins. Those two details are my hot buttons.   Why: One of my go to restaurants in STL When: Too many times to keep track.......

While I was in the French Quarter, a friend called and immediately asked me if I had been to Mr B's yet. When I replied no, he told me I had to go. I finished my conversation with him and since it was almost 5:30 and I was close to Royal Street, I headed on over. They technically were not open, so arriving early was a good plan. I was able to get myself a prime seat at the bar. I was amazed at how fast the entire restaurant filled up once if was officially open.   Loving my Old Fashioned's and Manhattans being made with Maker's Mark, I couldn't resist trying their signature cocktail 201. It too, is made with Maker's Mark. It then has St. Germain, orange liqueur and a touch of lemon. It is served up in a rock glass for only $10. A hand crafted cocktail in the French Quarter and only $10 was a deal. Considering how strong it was, it was also a steal.   One of my true seafood loves is Sea Scallops. When I saw them on the menu under appetizers, I had to have them. It was two jumbo sized sea scallops pan seared and served with baby arugula drizzled with white truffle oil and shaved Parmigiano-Reggiano. It was perfection. I could have had a second helping, but I had to get going to my original dinner plans at another restaurant. It was also served with a personalized mini loaf baguette - that was boring as hell. Everyone else rave about it, but I found it bland and flavorless.   I love sitting at a bar when dining alone and Mr B's made it very elegant. They put out an opened linen napkin as my placemat, provided me with silverware and an additional linen napkin. A classy treatment for dining at the bar.   I'd visit Mr B's again and next time sit at a table and have the full experience. I can see now, why my friend was so adamant that I go experience this restaurant.   When: August 27, 2016 Why: A friend insisted that I go

The Good Pie in my opinion is, The Best Pie in Saint Louis.  I agree with Karen G., in loving this style of crust. The bubbly edges with charred spots not only add character to your pizza, but flavor as well. I too tend to eat each slice with a fork, but at times I just fold it half creating a Stevie B Calzone and take a big bite of the chewy pie.   Today for lunch we shared a Chopped Salad, which they were more then happy to divide on separate plates. When we saw our split portions, each were a hearty serving.  The dressing was a little heavy for my taste, but the flavor was rich and creamy.  I loved the burn that was provided by the pepperochini.   I took advantage of the Pizza Del Giorno which was; Spinach, Sausage, Roasted Peppers topped with a dusting of  Parmesan Cheese. Spinach is slowly becoming one of my favorite vegetables and combined with roasted peppers and sausage made me wish this was a regular feature and not just today's special.   The SO ordered the Atina and if a picture is worth a thousand words, look at the picture I posted. It will show you how over the top good this pizza is. The roasted mushrooms alone were worthy of their own pizza and when they got combined with tomato, prosciutto di parma and pecorino my taste buds danced for joy.   The finale of our lunch was the most incredible Salted Caramel Gelato. Creamy and the perfect blend of caramel and saltiness. Service as always, friendly and attentive.

Best lunch in town.  It is a set menu, so the only decision you need to make is do you want regular ice tea or sweet tea. I highly recommend the sweet. Each day is a different "Blue Plate" special. I two personal favorites are Monday for Fried Chicken and Wednesday for Bacon Wrapped Meatloaf. Each comes with two sides that are perfect matches to the main dish.  The perfect mindless and delicious lunch.  Staff is very out going and friendly, adding to the total experience.

Hell has frozen over and pigs are flying, I finally made it to Black Thorn Pub. I now get to check off one of my Yelp bookmarks, as experience accomplished. Oh, what a feeling.   It may have taken me years to get here and I am glad I finally made it. Black Thorn Pub serves up a decent Chicago Style Pizza,  by Saint Louis standards, so it still has room for improvement. I absolutely loved the tomato sauce with its strong peppery bite. The crust was a lite golden brown, crispy on the bottom and edges, no burnt areas, making for a perfect crust.  The cheese not being provel gave them bonus points, but the excessive amount  of cheese took them away.  I thought the day would never come that I'd hear myself saying, "Too much cheese".  We selected four toppings; sausage, mushroom, black olives and onion.  The black olives were plentiful and the mushrooms were fresh and thinly sliced. So thin, I could almost read The Riverfront Times through one. The bulk sausage, was nothing to write home about, so I'll say nothing about it here either. The onions, are another story worthy of their own paragraph.   Our pizza did not have onions on it. Did we notice the fact that they were missing? No. Did we complain? No, we didn't know they were missing. As we sat there eating, drinking beer, discussing the ambiance and flavor of  our pie, the bartender walked up with a pizza box and said, "here's your pizza".  I guess the looks on our faces, asked our question, "thought we were eating our pizza?" Because she quickly explained how someone else ordered the same thing, minus onions and that was the one we were enjoying. Amazed we were being given "our" pizza, I asked "what about the other people". She assured me they were rushing their pizza through by preparing it in the hottest spot in the oven. Hope they got at least a free beer, we got a free pizza.   We didn't even finish the pizza we were eating and now we had another medium deep dish pizza.  What we going to do with this one? We already had our fill of BT. Driving home we came up with an idea and quickly called one of our neighbors and informed them we were on our way bearing gifts. When we arrived and handed him the box, he was shocked at the weight. I opened the lid to show him the pie and he went bug eyed. He said, he'd be eating off that pizza for two days. He too, had never been to Black Thorn.   Black Thorn is good, but not the greatness everyone sings. I love me a dive bar, but this place could use some TLC or a good power hose. The staff is friendly and can spot a first timer easily.  However, I think a bus boy/pizza runner would be a great addition to their staff. It would keep the tables clean and the delivery of pizzas straight. Having folks order and getting drinks at the bar is fine, just adding a food runner would improve the customer service and cleanliness.  $45 for a medium deep dish and 3 beers seemed high to me, but I'll return for a carry out order in the future.

It's a Walgreens and actually one of the better ones within the city. The selection of items is also larger and most extensive then the other Walgreens I frequently shop.   As stated by Shawn M., this is a very busy location. The staff moves the number of customer in and out quickly. I just wish they did it with more finesse. I would rather have better customer service, then to be moved in and out of a store like a bunch of cattle.   I like this store, I will continue to shop here, I just want friendlier customer service when I'm here.

As I sat in the Cell Phone Lot waiting for the BF to return from his NM vacation, I had a wicked thought. I wondered if I could check-in on Yelp. So I searched for Cell Phone Lot and to my surprise it was, so I checked- in and now here is my review.   What a lifesaver and $ saver this place is. Who would have imagined this concept years ago. In the past we all had to pay to park when picking someone up at the airport. Then again we use to be able to go all the way down to their arrival gate to meet them. Oh, my have times changed.   I felt as if I were at a drive-in movie sitting there reading the huge arrival board. Be warned, that board is not accurate.  The BF's flight status remained blank. It never showed, "On Time"  "Late" or "Arrived". Then all of a sudden my Bejeweled game was interrupted by a phone call telling me, the plane had arrived and he was at the luggage carousel. I guess that is why they call it  "Cell Phone Lot", because the communication from cell to cell is more accurate then the "big sign".   Once I got the "call" and drove to the arriving flight area, he was curbside and ready to return home. Life is so much simpler now with our cell  phones, or at least picking someone up at the airport is so much simpler.

Selection for those of us who wear a wide shoe is limited.   Also, the prices are not that reduced. To get the best deals you need to be member of their rewards program. If you have a normal sized foot, sign up for their rewards and you'll save. Those of us who have wide feet, need to shop else where.   I'll be back? - I'll check back periodically to see if they have my size.   When? - June 13, 2019 Why? - Shopping with a friend

Not impressed!!! Pissy attitude and overpriced pastries that are no better then those you could buy at your local grocery store. Perhaps after reading all the 5 Star reviews I was expecting to be blown away. Well I was and it was with disappointment.  First off the staff is very dry and look down their noses at you as if they are better then the customer they are waiting on and who is paying for their overpriced pastries.   Secondly, even though some think the black glove they use to retrieve to macaroons from the case is cute, I thought it to be unhealthy. It is worn by multiple employees, waded up and thrown back into the drawer. It just made my skin crawl thinking how nasty and dirty that glove could be.  We did try the macaroons and for being a signature item, again I repeat, I was not impressed.   Thirdly, the Easter Shortbread Cookies were kind of okay. The shortbread itself was good, but was ruined by a very unflavored icing.   Best thing about this place is they serve Chauvin Coffee which in my opinion is the best coffee roaster in Saint Louis.   There are a lot better bakeries in our city that offer more flavor and bang for your buck then this place and they will be getting my business.

I have lived in Saint Louis for 32 years and never had a St. Paul sandwich. How did I ever do it? When I saw the posting for a UYE celebrating a sandwich, that I have been avoiding for 32 to years I knew it was time to give in and have one.   A crowd of Yelper's meet at Hon's Wok, to experience the wonders of a St. Paul Sandwich. I relied on the guidance of experienced St. Paul fans and ordered the Chicken St. Paul.  They assured me it would taste like a Chik-Fil-A.   For those of you who do not know, the St. Paul sandwich is only available in Saint Louis. Who else would want to serve this sandwich?  It basically is a egg foo young patty served between two slices of white bread. You can give your sandwich more flavor by adding, beef, pork or chicken. They then add lettuce, mayo,  dill pickle, white onion and tomato as condiments. Mine did not taste like a Chick-Fil-A, but it had its own unique flavor.    It was a little greasier then I'd like, but the Wonder bread soaked it up. Many of the other Yelper's that where enjoying their sandwiches, thought they needed more salt. I on the other hand, thought they were extremely salty.  However, let me clarify that by saying, I am not a fan of salt, period.   I also, experienced an Egg Roll which was fairly good for a fast food Chinese.   The staff was friendly and very accomendating to our large group taking over their dining room for a party celebrating the St. Paul sandwich.  Their customer service was so great, I'm coming back to try more of the menu.

If you don't follow your favorite restaurants on Twitter, I highly recommend that you do. If I were not following, Farmhaus on Twitter, I would have never known that they were preparing one of my favorites on Mother's Day weekend. When they sent out the tweet that they were serving, Soft Shell Crab that week-end, I responded back with a simple, tweet. "I'll be there."   Arriving on Friday night, I seated myself at the bar. Being a lone diner, I hate tying up a two-top table from the servers. Besides, other fun people also dine at the bar and I like a good company. Sitting at the bar, I of course had to start my evening out with a cocktail. I'll have a, Manhattan, please. Farmhaus is not known for its' cocktails, but I will say they do an excellent job making a classic Manhattan.   As I read the menu, I got doubly excited. Not only were they serving one of my favorite seafoods this evening, they were also serving one of my favorite vegetables - asparagus. Life is good and I know this dinner is going to be delicious. If that were not enough excitement, on the dessert menu was, Lemon Poppy Seed cake with vanilla ice cream. I am so glad I am a Twitter follower of Farmhaus.   My asparagus was served, "loaded". It had prosciutto, Gouda Espuma, Shoe String Potatoes and Spring Onion Ash. The asparagus was prepared to the perfect tenderness. To my delight, I enjoyed two soft shell crabs split in half and corn flour fried. They were served with a soy-lime aioli, pickled ramp and english pea salad. Some may frown upon eating a shell, but this is my second favorite seafood, right behind scallops and they are a very close second.   Dessert completed the evening. To accompany my Lemon Poppy Seed Cake, I enjoyed an after dinner Grand Marnier. The LPSC was basically a pound cake and it was moist. It was served with a small scoop of vanilla ice cream and pieces of orange meringue. The fresh citrus taste made this a very refreshing and lite dessert.   Service at the bar is always attentive. I still miss the, Blue Plate lunches of years gone by, but dinner at Farmhaus is always a 5 Star experience.   I'll be back? - Absolutely, it's one of my favorites  When: May 11, 2018 Why: Soft Shell Crabs

Meet cousins here after the Sunday Cards game. They attended the game, we just meet them for the after game festivities.  Let's make this simple:  Our beer was great after all it is Schlafly's. So enough said.  Not much in variety when it came time to order food. Those eating basically stayed with a "Bison" theme.  Bison Burgers and Bison Nachos. All dining, said they enjoyed their food. My young cousin who had not experienced Bison before even enjoyed his. My experience here, is they put out the best Bison in the city.   I was happy to find a new member to my list, "Dry My Hands". Yes, this location has  Dyson Airblade Hand Dryers.

A group of cousins gathered here for our Christmas celebration and had a blast.  How could we not have fun, when we had 30 draft beers to choice from and some of the best pizza in the Bi-State area. We were in the bar area which is referred to as Tony's Third Street Cafe. The bar has a more casual and relaxed dining atmosphere and the wait staff makes your experience fun.   There were three couples and a single in attendance and everyone raved about their food. Alex the single diner, ordered the Cheeseburger pizza and had them hold the mustard.  It was so tasty, it actually tasted like a big meaty burger. I may have to order that one on our next visit to Tony's. I didn't pay close enough attention to what the other couples ordered, but I can tell you what we had; Onion Rings, Large Caesar Salad and Tony's Special Deluxe Pizza.   The onion rings were big thick slices and evenly breaded. I can see these being a perfect accompaniment to a "real" cheeseburger. Our large Caesar was definitely enough for two to share, or it could be a "meal" for a person watching the weight.  I enjoyed the salad, but for my personal taste I like my Caesar dressing to have more of an anchovy bite to it.   Our pizza was flawless! Tony's offers two types of crust; thin and thick and they should not be confused with the traditional types. Tony's thin crust is more like a flat bread and his thick is the bastard child of traditional and thin crust pizza. What that means is; the crust of the pie part is more like a traditional thin and the edges is like a traditional hand tossed pizza. I wish other pizza parlors offered this type of crust, because it gives you the best of both.   Another thing that makes Tony's pizza stand out from others, is his sauce. As stated by James M. it has a little "sweet" twang to it. When it is combined with all the toppings on my Special Deluxe it made things pop. That sweet sauce covered in meats, onions, green pepper and black olives was a true heavenly delight.  If a picture paints a thousand words, the one I posted of my pizza is worth thousand calories.   Our server was a blast, she knew it was a holiday celebration (gift exchanging made it obvious) and she made sure we were well taken care of.  I wish Tony's was closer to my home instead of my work so I could become a true regular.

The team from Polite Society has created a new culinary paradise. They have taken the old space once occupied by Element and transformed it into, The Bellwether. Last night I was honored to be part of the soft opening of, The Bellwether and am looking forward to their Grand Opening on the 31st of May.   As always, I took a sit at the massive bar. It's a beautiful bar. The back has multiple shelves filled with liquor and delicate stemware. There are so many shelves, that the bartenders have a library ladder that slides the full length of the bar, so they can reach the tools of their trade.   My cocktails were masterfully made. I judge bartenders on how they make my favorite classic cocktails. I'm a fan of a Manhattan and Old Fashioned. Dustin, made me one of the best Old Fashioned's I've had recently. He shared with me, that he too is a whiskey fan. I guess that is why his OF was so good. He also, made me one of The Bellwethers signature cocktails, Catcher in the Rye. It will be in my cocktail rotation when I return.   Now, let's talk about the food. OMG! I started out with the Roasted Carrots. It's one of their Small Plates and is large enough to be shared. They were full sized carrots and roasted perfectly. They were tender, but yet still had enough snap. After I received mine and raved, the diners to my left and right also ordered them. They were definitely the hit of the bar.   I figured the new staff had most likely already tried most of the menu, so I asked Dustin (bartender) what his favorite was and he quickly responded, "Pork Steak". It was an 8 oz boneless pork steak, served on top of, German Potato Salad and Compressed Red Cabbage. The BBQ sauce was an Carolina Mustard. I normally am not a fan of bbq sauces, but this one really accented the tender pork steak. This steak was regular knife tender, no need of a steak knife. It melted in my mouth.   Dessert? Oh, no. I am so full, I just couldn't. We have, Carrot Cake with Carrot Ice Cream. Oh, hell. I gave in and I'm glad I did. The thin slice of cake accompanied with the scoop of house-made ice cream was a perfect finale to a wonderful meal.   For a soft opening, the kitchen did a fabulous job. I'm looking forward to many return visits to try the Rib Eye, Pub Burger and the Octopus. Once I've tried more of the menu, I am confident they'll be bumped up to 5 Stars. I'm also looking forward to bonding with a the staff of bartenders at TB, as I become a regular.   I'll be back? - Hell, YES! I'll be here for the first night of official biz.   When: May 29, 2019 Why: Soft Opening

We had lunch on Fat Tuesday at Baileys' Range and were totally surprised. I have drug my feet coming here due to the mixed reviews and now regret that I didn't come sooner.  Not only did BR amaze us with burgers, but their wings, chili and fries were equally as good.   Our feast at Bailey's begun with Smoked Pablano Chicken Wings and a Cup of Chili. We enjoyed the wings, they provided a different twist to the traditional "hot" wings and the chili was kick ass. The chili had a spice that provided a good kick that we could not name, but loved it just the same. It was topped with melted cheese and croutons. Croutons are a nice upgrade from oyster crackers and add an additional flavor.   To test a new burger restaurant, we figured it was best to try the "basic" burger. If they can not do a basic burger, how will they be able to do the "specialty" burgers. They nailed it! Our burgers were juicy, cooked to our specifications and served with all the toppings. Bailey's doesn't stop at a good burger, they put it on a house made bun, that can rival some bakery buns.   We shared a small order of fries and I can tell you a small is enough to satisfy two. Their fries are house cut, no frozen pre-cut fries at BR. As our sauce we choose "crazy catsup", which I wish could be bought to take home. I love the way they serve their catsup, in the small mason jars. I recently have become a big fan of places that provide catsup in small cups instead of nasty bottles.   A visit to Bailey's Range would not be complete without having a shake. Again, we went with the a traditional shake instead of one their now famous "boozy shakes".  I had my favorite flavor, strawberry and Brad got creative and mixed vanilla ice cream with blueberry sorbet. They said, they have not had anyone mix ice cream and sorbet before. His creation was fantastic, he joked that he is glad we do not live in a loft downtown, because he would have one everyday. The shakes were better then a specialty parlor down on Locust.   Our waitress was friendly and provided great service. I will be honest, the reason they did not get a five is fault of the kitchen. All the food was excellent, but we had just received our wings and chili when another server approached with our burgers. Next time, we will hold back and not order burgers until we are finished enjoying our appetizers. However, they took ownership of the error and without complaining they made it right by treating us to our shakes and removing them from our bill.   Bailey's Range, I'll be back. You gave me good service, good food and I like that your carryout vessels are eco-friendly.

Color me surprised, another new QT has opened up in the city. Quick Trip is becoming like Walgreens and Starbucks. It almost seems that there is one on every corner. Or at least every other block. This QT is a prime location - it has easy access on and off of 44 and is just a hop, skip and a jump from 64/40.   I'm driving to work earlier then most people get up for work and a convenience market is important to me. It may be a gas station, but their selection and variety of coffee satisfies my need for caffeine. This new location is one that has the kitchen in the center, I can't wait to try it. However, for now I can tell you, if you need a quick breakfast their 99¢ Sausage Biscuit will hit the spot and fill the void.   The staff seems to be friendly and professional and if they can do that in the wee hours of the morning - they've got a good team.   Will I return? Yes - I've fallen out of love with my current gas station and convenience store.   When: March 25, 2017 Why: It's new and I needed coffee.

Ted, it has been two years since my original review and figured I needed to give you an update. I am glad I waited till now and did not do it last fall. At that point, you were starting to lose me as a fan, but this season you are on a strong A-Game.   Your custard is rich, creamy and can be turned upside down without any consequences. I have even been able to turn mine upside down after a 2 mile drive home.  I've tried other flavors, but I will always be true to my M & M's  being my favorite.   I also want to commend you on your staff. Your front window employees are always friendly and know how to move the line quickly. Then  I wonder how those who make the sweet treats, how they can turn them so fast. Your custard truly is a treat of Saint Louis and Route 66.

Note: This review is about the meeting rooms - no overnight stay was done by me.   My work was having a special training class and the size of attendees exceeded the capacity of our in house conference room. We shopped around for a meeting room and since when we have employees from out-of-town visiting STL, we use this Holiday Inn, they gave us a good deal.   The table and chairs they provided were comfortable and accommodating to our needs. Most importantly, was the sound. With all the meeting rooms in the hallway being in use, there was no distractions of hearing what was going on in the other rooms.   My co-workers who came in from other cities and had to stay over-night in the rooms - I heard no complainants.   If you work in the area and need a small to larger meeting room for your business or organization, this HI can fill your needs.

This is not my regular Schnucks. However, whenever I am heading home from Costco and cutting down Loughborough to Hampton, I stop by for items I just cannot buy in bulk at the warehouse store for a single man.   In my original review, which is now several years old, I complained about the produce department. Wow, things have really changed. I will now say this is one of the better produce departments in STL. It's always fresh, organized and well stocked.  I've also gotten use to the lay-out and can shop the aisles with ease. Another area that is pretty good, is the butcher counter. Give me those pork steaks for that backyard grilling.   The staff has done a full Three-Sixty on their attitudes. Even during this pandemic when everyone seems to be on the edge, they were upbeat and positive.  While shopping during the COVID pandemic, I felt safe with all the safety precautions this store had in place.   Will I return? - For, sure.   When: June 4, 2020 Why: Grocery items I cannot buy in bulk.

Thank goodness there is practically a Walgreens on every other block, because this one is so discombobulated. It is cluttered, kind of dirty, in serious need of some TLC and has nil customer service.  I was expecting so much more being located in the Brentwood area, but once inside the store it might as well been in a ghetto. Management, you may have a high volume sales store, but do not let the small details get out of control. If this location was the one closest to my home or work, I'd switch over to CVS or drive to the next closest Walgreens. After all, there is practically one every other block.   Also, be aware of the self important people backing out of parking spaces and arriving in the parking lot while talking on their cell phones. It makes for some defensive driving and a new addition to my Parking Lot Derby list.

Weither you are shopping for perennials or annuals, Colors of Spring is a place you need to check out. The other day, I was searching for hanging baskets for my four Shepard's Hooks in my backyard and had success at Colors of Spring.   This year we are wanting to attract Hummingbirds to our yard, so we are only using red and purple flowers to increase our chances. I have always been a fan of Petunias, and I guess you could say it is genetic. My mom and her twin sister both had a green thumb when it came to Petunias. They use to pick the old blooms off in the morning as they enjoyed a cup of coffee. I wonder how amazed they'd be with these new Wave Petunias that are a hybrid and no longer need the old blooms removed.   As I shopped, I asked one of the young ladies if their Petunias were Wave and she replied, "yes, all of them". She and I then shared a laugh on who wants to pick and pull off old blooms daily. My hanging basket has doubled in size since I hung it in my backyard. Now I want to see Hummingbirds feeding off their nectar.

Brad and I meet up with Mary Kate A here for a Martini and gab session. I was pleased to see this place is still amazing after all these years. It is a small charming neighborhood bar that serves a quality Martini or Cosmopolitan. I am sure they offer typical bar drinks, but i don't know why you'd order them when the Martini's are creative, go down oh so well and are reasonably priced.   I think this is the great place to go with friend(s) to to relax and have a quality "cocktail". Our bartender was charming, cute and attentive to our alcoholic needs. I'll be back.

I am more of a doughnut guy, but how you spell it doesn't really matter. Because, these are some of the best tasting cake donuts I have had in the St. Louis metropolitan area. They are moist and the icing is not overly sweet. As Goldilocks would say, " These donuts, are just right."   The price point is a little higher then your normal doughnut shop, but lower than the area "gourmet' and "trendy" doughnut shops. Either way you look at it, it is well worth the money. The creative doughnuts with added toppings like M&M's is done way better here, than at other shops in the area.  One of the highlights for me being a dog daddy, is they also offer house-made dog treats. With today being, Love Your Pet Day, I couldn't resist stocking up on a very extra treats for my Fur-Babies.   The staff is friendly and the owner himself is a delight to speak with. He made selecting and buying donuts fun.   When: February 20, 2021 Why: Needed a doughnut and killing time.

It's been three years since my last update for Bono's Pizzeria and I am still a fan.  The other day I stopped by to take advantage of their lunch special. It's a 10" single topping pizza, house salad and a soda for $7.55.  This special is offered Monday thru Friday between the hours of 11 AM till 3 PM. Damn, it was good and I was surprised how big the 10" pizza was. I had enough left over, to enjoy later as a snack and two slices cold for breakfast the next day.   I like how fresh everything is at Bono's. They make the pizza dough, sauce and salad dressings daily in house. You'll taste the freshness. Also, a lot of the recipes were brought over from Sicily by Tony's great-grandmother. History and freshness, makes for a tasty lunch.   The service is always friendly and one of the Tony's is always present.   It doesn't matter if you; dine-in, carry-out or have it delivered. You'll have a great meal from Bono's.   Will I return? Yes, I support my neighborhood businesses.   When: January 30, 2017 Why: Lunch - I deserve pizza

I always have a basic cone when experiencing a new custard place. That way I can get a true flavor of the custard before adding ingredients  to make a sundae or concrete. The custard here was thick, creamy and no flavor.  When I returned to my car, I saw the "Colombo" sign in their window, which is a kiss of death in my book. Colombo is a pre-mix used by many small ice cream business and I have yet to see one produce a quality product.   What a disappointment, I really needed a new place for concretes.

This Thanksgiving I was thankful for J Gilbert's. I was thankful that I was able to get a reservation at the last minute at the time I wanted. Most importantly, I was thankful for an amazing Prix Fixe Thanksgiving Menu, that satisfied me need for a traditional Thanksgiving dinner.   I liked that J Gilbert's did a Prix Fixe menu instead of a buffet like so many other restaurants that were open on Turkey Day. Buffets usually are overpriced and overwhelming. Where do you start? What should you eat? and the hardest question of them all, "When do I stop eating?"   Our dinner was reasonably priced at $38 and included three courses. The first course was a choice of two types of salad and two soups. I choose a Caesar Salad and my friend Norma went with the Maryland Crab Bisque. The size of my salad was appropriate for a lead in to a large meal. I enjoyed the dressing, which was proportionate to the amount of Romaine lettuce. The asiago cheese crisp was the perfect carb match up to the salad.   The second course was the main attraction; a Traditional Thanksgiving spread. When the plate was first placed in front of me, I thought it was skimpy servings. As I started to eat, I immediately realized I was wrong. I needed a to-go vessel, that provided me a nice lunch for the next day at work.   The traditional spread included; roasted turkey (both dark & white meat), yukon mashed potatoes, cornbread and sausage dressing, gravy, glazed yams, green beans with pecans and cranberry orange relish. I had everything that I wanted and if I closed my eyes, I would have thought I was down home on the farm instead of an upscale steak & seafood house.   The third course of course was dessert. You got to select from three of their most popular desserts and of course pumpkin pie. Miss Norma went pumpkin pie, but I had to stray off menu. I saw a Vanilla Bean Creme Brûlée pass by our table and instantly knew I had to have it. When I asked our server if I could substitute she was accommodating to my request. It was so delicious with the fresh raspberries on top. Actually, the serving portion is so huge that two diners could share.   Let me back-up to the beginning of our evening and tell you about our appetizer and cocktail.  One of my favorite cocktails is the Moscow Mule, so I was thrilled when I saw J Gilbert's made theirs with my favorite vodka; Tito's and my favorite ginger beer; Fever Tree. Most MM's are $8, but to have my two favorites in my favorite cocktail was worth the $10. Plus, they poured heavy, it was a good strong cocktail.   Being a fan of crab meat, I couldn't resist ordering the Jumbo Lump Crab Cakes. Excellent! You are served two huge cakes and if you order this item for lunch, for me it would be the complete meal. They also served up a small loaf of piping hot house bread with two types of butter.   The service was; friendly, attentive and not rushed.  A couple of friends have told me J Gilbert's does a great job on lamb chops and scallops. So I know I will be back, as those two entrees are on the menu of my last meal on earth. Can't wait to give them a try.   When: Thanksgiving 2015 Why: Thanksgiving Dinner

Simplicity is what makes me a fan of Twisted Roots. The decor is minimalist, they offer 11 beers and easy to make cocktails. There were no thrills here, but all is good. If it were not for a UYE sponsored by Brian M., I most likely would have never discovered Twisted Roots. So, to Brian who is a beer connoisseur, I thank you.   On my inaugural visit, I enjoyed two of their in house brewed beers and both were rather refreshing. Being more of a whiskey/Manhattan man, for my final drink I ordered a Manhattan. I quickly learned, that was a little beyond their skills. However, they still took care of me. They didn't have sweet vermouth, but one of the staff members got creative and created me one tasty cocktail. (I'll stick with all beer next time)   My friends all enjoyed burgers, but I ordered the Thunder Thighs. They were like boneless chicken wings, but made with the meat of a thigh. An order of these were appetizer to munch on while drinking a cold beer.   Other positives - Happy Hour and great hand dryer in mens room   I'll be back? - Have a lot of beer loving friends.   When: June 6, 2018 Why: UYE

Yummy, Yummy I have pizza in my tummy and I like it.   A delightful Monday lunch outside on the sidewalk cafe. We started our experience with a full pound of Blazed Wings served with house made blue cheese and carrots. The wings had enough spice to give them a kick, but not to much to kick you in the ass later. I normally do not dip my wings, I like the natural taste of the wing. However, the blue cheese looked so good I could not just let it sit there without tasting it.    I did not waste one of the flavorful wings, instead I dipped one of the carrot sticks into the most amazing blue cheese ever. I truly like how Pi offers carrots over the typical celery that most places offer with their wings. Plus the fact, carrots are a healthier veggie then celery so I do not feel guilty when I indulge in chicken wings.   We followed up those delightful Blazed Wings with a thin crust North Beach Classico. I know where South Beach is, but not sure about North Beach. However, it really doesn't matter, because the pizza was fantastic. The pizza was covered with the rich Pi tomato sauce, mozzarella cheese, sausage, mushrooms, onions  and green peppers. That combination of toppings is awesome enough, but we added ricotta & fresh basil. OMG, that pizza was amazing. It was so amazing I wish Pi delivered.   Our server was friendly and charming, which adds to the dining experience. I've have now dined at the CWE and the Delmar locations. In the future you will see me dining at the best of the two, Delmar.

After seeing Patt C's review mentioning Red Velvet Cake I knew I wanted to give Yogoluv a try. I was out in West County picking up special diet food for my Shelties' and noticed Yogoluv was just down the street from my Shelties vet and thought way not give it a try.   I was trilled to see that Red Velvet Cake was one of the flavors of the day. I grabbed a small cup and began my journey down the the dispensers. Of course I started out with Red Velvet Cake and then I added the following three; Vanilla, Birthday Cake and Thin Mint. Only the Red Velvet Cake impressed me.   On my first visit, I found the vanilla to be lacking in true vanilla flavor. I also found the Birthday Cake from Blue Bunny Ice Cream to be a truer and better for that flavor.  Being a BIG fan of thin mint cookies, I couldn't wait to try the Thin Mint YoGo. Sorry to say, I was disappointed. Not only was it thin and runny, but no chocolate flavor and the taste of mint was minimal.   The Red Velvet Cake saved the day and I look forward to trying another Yogoluv closer to home.

Warning Will Robinson, Warning! Do not make the same mistake that I did on my first visit to Mr. Wizard's. I ordered a cone and did not specify, yogurt or custard. That is why I wrote my first review giving only two stars and mentioned the sign for Colombo's. Now that I have experienced the custard, they jump to an amazing 4 stars.   When you order the custard and you will be blown away. The thickness and the flavor is unbelievable. While eating mine, I had to convince myself that it was like a Coke Zero and had not calories. I am so thankful that Mr. Wizard is not as close to my house, because I would easily be the reigning Duke with a very large waist.   I love their sign in the window where you place your order, it is truly a ordering ice cream for Dummies. Wish I saw it on my original visit. The photo did not take well, so I've re-created it below:                                          Ordering  1. Size - kiddie, small, medium, ect........  2, Flavor - Turtle, Oreo, Strawberry, ect.......  3. Item Type - Cone, Sundae, Concrete, ect.......  4. Custard or Yogurt  5. Extras - whip cream, extra toppings, ect......  6. For here or to go  My editorial comment: Pay close attention to step 4, the correct answer is CUSTARD.

Gentelin's is easily the premier restaurant in Alton. If you are fortunate to be seated by their huge windows, you'll have an amazing view of the Alton Bridge. Besides the spectacular view, you'll experience white linen service at a small town locally owned restaurant.   I've come here twice for a Saturday before Easter dinner with my favorite cousins. I apologize for not writing about last years amazing dinner, but I'm making up for it this year. Our appetizers, entrees and desserts were all amazingly delicious. Each one was plated and presented beautifully.   There were six of us, so we started out sharing three appetizers. With my love of Jalapeños, one of them had to be, Goat Cheese Jalapeño Popper. It was three fairly large jalapeños stuffed with goat cheese. (are you surprised?) Served on top of a roasted red pepper jam with candied bacon. I got one of those peppers all to myself and loved it.   Our other appetizers were the; Creamy Spinach and Artichoke Dip and Santa Fe Wraps. Some of the Southwest/Mexican restaurants in STL can learn a thing or two on how to make these wraps from Gentelin's. They were, crisp and full of flavor. So much so, that I didn't use the salsa for dipping. I did try the red pepper mayo and enjoyed it for the extra kick.  The final app CSAD, was served with roasted garlic and parmesan crostini's, which separated it from other restaurants which serve just plain crostini.   Our entrees were a good variety of the menu. I went with the Cowboy Ribeye. It was served over a Yukon Gold potato hash with caramelized red onion, red peppers, scallions, roasted garlic and bacon. I'd love to see this hash served at breakfast it was so good. My Ribeye also had Roasted Asparagus and was topped with Cowboy butter. The meat was tender and flavorful.   Other entrees included; Aunt Jayne's Chicken, Grilled Chicken Pasta and  their famous Pork Chop. My cousin who lives in Alton and is a semi-regular, swears by it and claims it is the best PC he has had in a restaurant.   I by far had the best dessert, Vanilla Bean Creme Brûlée. The other two desserts enjoyed were, Raspberry Sorbet and Donuts and Coffee. I will say, the Donuts and Coffee was very original and creative.   Service was great, cocktails made professionally and strong and as others have said, the bread basket was kept full.   I'd recommend Gentelin's for a special occasion, or just an evening out. Treat yourself, get out of the city of STL and cross over the bridge to Alton for a fabulous meal.

I live within walking distance of three Mexican restaurants and I drove to U-City from South Hampton to give Mi Ranchito a try. Why, you ask? Because 25 of my Yelp friends have given them 4 or 5 Stars and I thought it was time for me to give them a try. It is well worth the drive.   Mi Ranchito is tucked away in a strip center across the street from Vernon's BBQ, an easy landmark to help you find this little unknown Mexican restaurant. It is extremely clean, well lit and decorated with murals and bright colors. The staff is exorbitantly friendly. Our server was remarkably helpful, assisting us to make our selection from their huge menu. He listened to our likes and favorites and guided us to entrees that satisfied our Mexican taste buds.   As stated by other reviewers, the chips are fresh and warm. The salsa is just average, but good enough to dip the free chips in. We also enjoyed a side dish of Guacamole, which was creamy with chunky pieces of avocado. Presentation of the Guacamole was laking, they served it in a small dish that was almost the exact color as the Guac. A contrasting color would have been so much better. After all, presentation is everything.  As my entree, I choose the El Plato Grande. It was kind of like a make your own soft taco kit. I was given grilled steak and chicken breast with tortillas and all the ingredients I'd want on my taco; lettuce, tomatoes, pico de gallo, guacamole and sour cream. If that wasn't enough, it came with sides of refried beans and rice. The steak and chicken was tender and seasoned well. I'd definitely order it again, it was fun assembling my own soft tacos.   Walking to my local Mexican restaurants may be good exercise, but I'll be tempted to drive to Mi Ranchito next time I have a craving for inexpensive Mexican.

Did St. Louis need another steakhouse? Yes. I'm a meat lover, so there can never be too many steakhouses to satisfy my red meat cravings. Carnivore is a nice addition to the Italian dominated "Hill".   When dining at a steakhouse, in my opinion there are only three drinks you should be drinking. Two are classic cocktails and the other is a traditional red wine. So today, I started my visit with a, Manhattan. I had to smile when the bartender replied, "I can't believe how many orders I am getting for Manhattans, since we opened." Right there is proof that I know my booze.   Being a fan of Jalapeños', I could not resist one of their appetizers. They offer, Smokey Stuffed Jalapeños. Beware, these are not little peppers, they are HUGE. They're stuffed with Italian Sausage, Cream Cheese and Cheddar and lightly breaded. They were not overly spicy, but my body may be immune, since I eat them all the time.   I then had a Herbivore salad, before my entree. It was a true, Italian salad. Hey, they're located on, The Hill, so a little Italian has to show up on the menu. It was a good mix of romaine and baby spinach. Tossed with cucumber, pimentos, green onions, provel and feta cheese. Then it was all mixed with their house made Italian dressing and garnished with peperoncino. Actually it was one of the better salads I've had on The Hill.   My entree was a 10 oz Sirloin with a side of asparagus. I requested it to be prepared, medium rare and it was done to perfection. It was seasoned perfectly as well. I had no desire for and sauce or flavored butter on top - it was perfect.   When my entree arrived, I was ready for a second cocktail. Others at the bar were enjoying, Dirty Martinis so I joined the crowd. My earlier Manhattan was made well, but the bartender really shined with a Dirty Martini.   With them still being fairly new when I visited, the service was friendly and attentive. I was seated at the bar and felt I got the same amount of attention as those who were seated at the tables.   I'll be back? - Yes, the prices are very reasonable.   When: July 7, 2018 Why: New steakhouse in town.

BCD - I'm bumping you up to a 5 Star rating, it is well deserved. The quality of your sandwiches is superior to all other deli's in the STL area and your service is super fast and super friendly.   I arrived yesterday 10 minutes before opening and there were already 25 customers ahead of me in line. That there shows you how much people love this St. Louis favorite. Once the doors were opened, it is amazing how fast they move the line. Lucky for me, several of the people ahead of me in line were picking up to go orders. They left with boxes and bags full of sandwiches for their co-workers.   As stated in my previous review, I love Pastrami. Surprisingly, I have never tried the Prez Reuben. When I saw that Ian Froeb said, it was the "must have" on his STL 100 List for 2016. I knew it was time to update my Yelp review for Blues City Deli. Ian was right, this is a must have for anyone ordering a sammie at BCD.   The Prez Reuben is a messy sandwich, so beware. It's messy because it is filled with; New York style Pastrami and Swiss Cheese, Sauerkraut and Thousand Island Dressing. Get a good grip on it, so it doesn't slip, slide and away from you. As always, I choose rye bread over the Sourdough. My rye bread was toasted perfectly within the Panini press - I love seeing the grill marks on my sammie. The small was more then enough for me, I actually only ate half and saved the other half for a mid-afternoon snack.   BCD - you are my deli of choice. I love your sandwiches.

This is one of my favorite nursery's in St. Louis. It is  my place of choice to find flowers and greenery for our planter sconces and hanging baskets.  The plants here just seem to be more hearty and healthier.  I think it is from the TLC they get from the staff.   The staff is very knowledgeable, and can make recommendations to meet your yards needs. We described the amount of shade and sunlight we receive and ideas flowed.   The indoor shop is very cool, lot's of great gifts for any gardner on you gift list.   Spring has arrived, I can't wait to go and make my annual pilgrimage to Garden Heights.  Another bonus,  Mr. Wizard is down the street so treat yourself to a cone while you browse the plants or as a reward for a job well done.

Patience is a virtue and it is one that I do not have when dining out. If I can not be seated fairly soon, or there is not a bar I can relax in while waiting, I will move on to plan B. So when I see a long line at a fast food or sandwich place, I keep on moving.  That is why it took me three visits to Blue City Deli to finally experience its' greatness.   My first visit the line was out the door and down the sidewalk past the size of the building. Oh hell no, I will not stand in that line for a deli sandwich. The next time, again out the door with about a dozen folks outside. My third visit was the charm, the line was just to the door with only two folks standing outside. To be honest, I was determined to try BCD and ready to break my waiting rule that day any way, so a small wait was better then a long one.   Once inside, I could see the workings of a very well organized operation. Every employee had a responsibility, which made the process of ordering, preparing and delivering as smooth as silk. Kudos to the owner and management for training and orchestrating such a tine team.   Upon moving up in line (which moved fast), I arrived at the soda cooler and smiled bigger then a Cheshire Cat. BCD had bottled "Frostie" Root Beer and I have not seen that since I was a child. I didn't even know my favorite soda was even still being produced. Of course it goes without saying, I grabbed a bottle and hoped it was still as good as I remembered.   Next was a large display of chips, which offered every flavor imaginable. You could choose from a poor mans' Jays Chip all the way up to the gourmet hometown favorite Billy Goat Chips. I love me some Billy Goat, but today I took the poor mans' chips, Jay's Cheddar & Sour Cream.....yum.   I judge a deli by it's pastrami and roast beef, this day I was testing Pastrami. When I ordered, the cashier asked me if I wanted it on rye or sourdough. I looked at  him and responded, "Rye, of course". He laughed and said he agreed, and  commented, that some folks like it on sourdough. He also offered Swiss and a house  made brown mustard. I turned down the cheese, because I wanted to truly  experience the pastrami, but I had him add the brown mustard. The mustard is very good, I suggest adding it to your next BCD sandwich.   After ordering, I was given a little plastic number to identify myself for the delivery  boys bring out orders from the kitchen. The wait was short and I was soon on my  way home to enjoy my inexpensive lunch. While driving home I again was taught the  lesson that patience is a virtue. The aroma of the pastrami, made me want to pull  over to the side of the road and devour it immediately. I increased my speed and  enjoyed  some very juicy pastrami, chips and a chilled "Frostie" at home.   It took three visits to finally experience the great deli sandwiches of BCD. They say, "third time is the charm", but now I regret missing out on my first two attempts.

I've only been to Bubba's twice and I wish it had been more. It was in my old hood and I feel guilty that I didn't support it more. It's a quaint little sandwich shop that has a limited menu, but what they serve is top notch and delicious.   I did not realize I am a true creature of habit until I started to write this review. On both of my visits, I ordered the same sammie and didn't even realize it. I ordered, The Cuban. On my first visit it was grilled like a true Cuban should be and was tasty. The second visit, it was served on a Sesame Hoagie type bun and cold. I found it to be odd, but the rich flavors from the smoked pork and ham were still there. My friend who joined me for lunch, liked his as well. We both just thought it was odd that it was served cold. I'm guessing someone was new in the kitchen or they were out of the regular bread. Either way, Bubba's is still a solid 4 Stars and worthy of a visit or two, or even more.   The staff is super friendly and much more customer service oriented then the deli over on Jamieson. During COVID they have hands free menu and hand sanitizer available for their customers. Plus, Bubba himself is a real cutie.   Will I return? - I may have moved away, but when back in my old hood, I"ll stop for a sammie.   When: August 29, 2019 and September 26, 2020 Why: Local deli in my hood.

This KFC is very close to my work and convenient for a quick lunch when I have forgotten, or didn't have time to pack a lunch. It is not a full menu KFC, it is an KFC Express. Its' limited menu offers; wings, tenders and popcorn chicken. It also offers Chicken Little Sandwiches, salads and fries. Yes, I would like a full regular chicken dinner with their cole slaw & mashed potatoes, but this menu does the trick when I'm hungry.   It's tucked inside the small food court located inside the Gateway Station downtown. At times, the lines can be long due to the arrival and departure of buses and trains, but the crew moves the lines quickly. My food has always been hot and fresh. The staff has a positive attitude, which can be a challenge when dealing with stressed or rushed travelers.   Will I return? Yep, it's a good quick lunch when I need it.   When: Numerous times. Why: Work lunch

The loveseat in my entertainment room is ready for retirement. It definitely has seen better days and needs to go away. I've periodically heard the radio commercials for Mueller Furniture on Y-98 and thought I'd give them a visit.  I was totally impressed with the variety of selection and the affordability of price. Kay my sales associate was knowledgeable of the merchandise and offered several suggestions to meet my needs. She was totally professional. She helped me find two items that fit my needs and budget.   However, after completing my Labor Day shopping, I put the retirement of the loveseat off for a couple more months. When it is time, I will be returning to Mueller Furniture and talking to Kay one more time.   Savings Note: If you buy in IL and have delivered to MO - you pay no sales tax.  When: September 6, 2016 Why: Need new loveseat

The staff here is very knowledgeable and eager to help their customers. We explained what we wanted to create, our sun exposure and our color preferences. Our sales associate guided us through our selections and even helped draw out the placement of the perennials in our fence sconces. Their customer service is outstanding and their love for plants shows.  If anyone needs perennials or annuals for their yard, I would highly recommend Garden Heights Nursery.

Neil Sedaka use to sing a song about, "Breaking Up Is Hard To Do" and he was  so right. Ted, we've been together so long that it breaks my heart that I have to tell you that there is now another custard in my life. I've tried to see both of you, but after our last outing I just can not do it anymore. I am leaving you for Mr. Wizard.   While I was seeing you both, I admit I was doing comparisons ordering the exact same thing to see which one would satisfy me the most. Mr. Wizard was slowly taking the lead and when I compared the Cherry Chocolate Chip Concretes,  he knocked it out of the custard ballpark. However, what really pushed me to the Wizard was the melting, or the not melting.   My drive from Mr. Wizard to home is 2.5 miles and his custard is still firm, thick and ready to be enjoyed in the comforts of my own home. My home from you Ted is 1.2 miles and with  the air conditioning blasting, your custard is soup when I get home. We can drink our concretes. Also, Mr. Wizard is blending my ingredients better and the finished product has a better presentation.   We were together 35 years Ted, so I'm still going to give you 3 Stars. Plus, you are an institution on Route 66 and all the tourist coming to STL need to experience you. However, Mr. Wizard is now my Custard Man.

I was so excited to have a lunch date yesterday with one of my  Yelp friends, Ms. Tracey W. When Yelpers get together, it is always so hard to pick a place to go. Being a gentleman, I told Tracey she could pick. She thought we should go some place new for both of us and doing that with two active Yelpers can be a challenge.  After extensive debating, we selected The Fountain on Locust. I had been there once before, but was waiting for a second visit before reviewing and Tracey W. had it on her bucket list. TFL is a ice cream shop for adults. The menu of Martinis make me droll, I wanted a Dreamciscle Martini so bad, it just sounds luscious.  Tracey W and I did have several good giggles. Starting off with our waiter having to come to our table multiple times just to get our order.  Then posing our malt, shake and sandwiches for their closeups.   I told Tracey on my first visit I had alcohol, but this time I wanted to experience a shake/malt. When you're at a soda fountain, you've got to experience a hand made shake and TFL does it oh so right. Every since I was a wee lad I have loved malt flavoring and the best malts are chocolate. Tracey went with a shake and choose chocolate too. I like the touch of bringing you the extra pour in the stainless mixing glass. Both of our drinks made that funny noise, when your straw has nothing else to pull up. That is a sign of a good drink, not bad manners.  For lunch I had the Hot Roast Beef Melt and it was near orgasmic. I am a big beef eater and am partial to Angus Beef, which this is made from. Those big black cows, paid for my college education. This sandwich is savory Angus beef with white cheddar and grilled onion. It is served on a fresh baked baguette, that has Subway uttering, "how do they do that". It is also served with a house made horseradish sauce. I use to not be a fan of horseradish, but theirs has changed my mind and I'd buy in a jar if were available. (hint-hint)  As a side I choose the Orange Onion Salad with Poppyseed Dressing. It is what the name says, oranges and red onion and nothing else. There is no lettuce in this salad. Once again, TFL impressed me with their house made dressing. It totally blew me away & I have family in the salad dressing business.   Tracey's sandwich looked equally impressive. She was the perfect "girl" date ordering a Mixed Salad Sandwich. She was right in her review, saying the shake really didn't go with the food. However, we drank & ate what we wanted. Visualize a fresh baguette with melted Parmesan  and Mozzarella Cheeses then stuffed with mixed lettuces, roasted red pepper, tomato, artichoke and a smear of house made pesto. You can make it St. Louis Style by adding meat (chicken), which Tracey did. I will order that sandwich on my next visit.   I was tempted by her side salad which was the Stutz Salad, but I would have had to have them hold the walnuts. Not nuts about that nut. Otherwise, baby spinach, plump Mandarin oranges, goat cheese and a creamy marmalade dressing would be a perfect summer salad.   Tracey W. mentioned our next outing we would drink and I  must say that is great, but it also scares me. Without booze, we still managed to share family/life secrets. I'd be scared to see what we'd share if we had Vodka & beer in us.  In closing if Tracey would have suggested ice cream for lunch, I would have called dibs on the Banana Split.

Let me repeat my opening line from my review back in 2013, "The staff here is very knowledgeable and eager to help their customers." Seven years later, this is still true. The customer service here, is truly the gold standard.   My dogs nanny, gifted me with two beautiful African Violets. I found the perfect spot in my sun-room for them to be inside and have ample light. However, I do not have a green thumb. I watered them and I may have over watered. They shriveled up and I was losing them.   I was besides myself, I wanted to save them. Due to the pandemic, Garden Heights was closed and I could not get the assistance I needed at Home Depot or Lowe's. When GHN finally opened, I headed over immediately for help. Told them my situation and they knew the solution. They recommended a self-watering pot for my violets and they are flourishing now.   In addition to the great customer service, GHN is practicing safe social distancing and enforcing a face mask for customers and staff policy.   Will I return? - Yes!  When: June 27, 2020 Why: Self-Watering Pot Shopping

Food - B+ Service - A- Ambiance - C  I was so excited when Five Star Burgers announced they were opening in Kirkwood. Being a fan of the Clayton location, I was glad to have one closer to my home.   I tried to visit Five Star Burgers on New Years Day and they were closed. So I was keeping my fingers crossed they'd be open today on Martin Luther King, Jr. Day. We arrived around 1:45 PM and the place was the place to be. Lucky for us, they were able to seat us immediately.  First thing we ordered, was their Fried Pickles. As Abbie our server placed our order, we decided on the rest of our order. When she returned, I ordered a Schlafly Pale Ale and Brad had a Ice Tea. We also, requested glasses of water. I ordered the Bison Burger and Brad had his usual, Dad's Green Chile Cheeseburger.   When our Fried Pickles arrived they were good, but not as good as the Clayton location. The breading and the Tzatiki sauce here were rather bland.  My Bison Burger was ordered medium, and came out well done. There was no pink at all, which is not a good thing for Bison. To my surprise, it was still flavorful and tender. When I saw that it was well done, I was so afraid it was going to be dried out. Dad's Green Chilies Cheeseburger, was as good as the Clayton location. In fact, Dad's is most likely one of the best burgers in STL.  Angus beef, Crispy New Mexico Hatch Chillies and Green Chile Mayonnaise is a perfect burger.   A large basket of Natural Cut Idaho Russet Fries is the right size for two to share. No ketchup bottle here, it's my favorite "Cup of Ketchup". We finished up with a mini cone filled Serendipity Ice Cream, our flavor was Salted Caramel. $1 a cone, is a sweet deal.   Ambiance is as plain and boring as it can be, but I don't come here for the decor I come for the burgers.   When: 20 Jan 2014 Why: Lunch

Not my usual Dierbergs Market, but I wish it were. I stopped in with a friend who was doing some serious grocery shopping. I was amazed at how much nicer this location is compared to the one closer to my house. It's true when they say in retail, "Location, Location, Location." It does make a difference.   What impressed me, was the produce and meat departments. WOW! very impressive. I'm not even Jewish and I was also impressed with the Kosher section. So impressed, that I grabbed a few items that were on sale.  One section that was sort of a disappointment was their discount section. I guess everything really gets bought up here, because the variety of items was not as impressive as at my regular market and I do love a bargain.   When checking out, I had to change lanes. The cashier was so rude and mean to the two people ahead of me, I was afraid of what I would say, if he crossed me. So I politely went to the next lane and waited my turn there. Some folks are not made for customer service, especially old curmudgeons.   Will I return? - I would if I still lived in STL, but I've moved.   When: September 17, 2020 Why: Power Grocery Shopping with a friend.

If you love Scallops, like I love Scallops, you've got to visit The Bellwether pronto. My most recent visit, I enjoyed their new dish, Scallop Soba and it had my taste buds dancing with joy. It's a unique twist to my favorite seafood.   Their Scallop Soba has three huge beautifully seared sea scallops on top of, squid ink noodles with, shiitake mushroom, yu choy, miso dash broth and wasabi tobiko. Having scallops as my entree, I started a seafood theme with my appetizer, by having Fried Oysters. Again, The Bellwether put their own twist on this popular dish, and made it a stand out.   Dusting the oysters lightly with rice flour made a huge difference in flavor and the thin coating covering the big oysters. Then they they're placed back in their shell severed on top of cheesed spinach and seasoned with fennel seed, red chili flake and garlic. You'll never find fried oysters this good at BOB's or Red Lobster.   I've been numerous times in addition to my scallop meal, so I'm just hitting highlights of various items:   Ribeye - 14 oz Prime Beef - steakhouse delicious Mushroom & Ginger Dumplings - Light, refreshing and shareable  Dulce de Leche Tart - All desserts are incredible, save room to enjoy. Bar Burger - A very upscale bar burger.  Cocktails - Specialty or Classic, they are on point.   Service is always friendly and the ambiance has an upscale contemporary feel. It's the perfect spot for a first date or celebrating a special event.   I'll be back? - I'm already a regular.   When: May 29, May 31, June 6, June 15, June 22 and Aug 17. Why: It's hot & new and it's my new favorite place for dinner.

Big disappointment, it started out with poor customer service. The staff was just rude, and could careless that we were there. We ordered an 8 piece box with biscuits and large side and an extra large side. Our order was carry out and when we got home, we realized they shorted us our second large side. Then when we opened our box of chicken, 4 of the 8 pieces were legs. Stopping by the next day, to mention the shortage of a large side, we were told we should have come back that same night, that it was to late now.  All they had to do is say sorry, and they couldn't even do that. Our chicken business will be going somewhere else.

Kiss, U Gas good-bye and say Hello to, On The Run.   Last year, U Gas was bought out by On The Run and finally this month all the signage and brand of gas has been switched over. The gas is no longer Phillips 66, it is now Mobil. The signage and retail products inside is now all On The Run.   During the transition, I strayed and started going to the QT up the street. i quickly loss interest in their offerings and customer service and started to come back here. I am so glad that I did.  It is actually better now then when it was U Gas and I really liked them. I've needed to grab an easy breakfast/lunch for work and have been impressed with the offerings from OTR. For quick and easy packaged food they're better then those at QT and what was previously offered by Gigi's at U Gas. Also, I enjoy your coffee way more.   Customer service is cheerful. I've just started back as a regular and they are already remembering me. Nice touch.   Welcome to my hood, On The Run. I'm glad the transformation is complete. You're looking good.   I'll be back? - Yes. Morning coffee and empty gas tank.   When: Jan & Feb 2018 Why: Gas & Coffee

I'm giving this Schnucks 5 Stars, simply because they had what i needed and wanted. One of my main Christmas gifts was a bottle of Rye from the local distillery, Switchgrass. Living in Illinois now, Switchgrass is not available. It is not distributed there yet. Hope they come soon.   Any how, the liquor department at this store was impressive. They had plenty of the Switchgrass offering and had the Rye, that I wanted so badly. Honestly, it should be a 4 Star rating, but they had an associate working the alcohol aisle and that made me much it up a star.   Love, Rye? Want to support local? Buy, Switchgrass.

I am going to ask a stupid question. Why can't all grocery stores be like this one?  This grocery store is amazing, it totally blew me away. I'd been to the new Dierberg's down the road and fell in love with it a couple months ago and now I fell like I already am cheating on it.   You know you are talking upscale grocer when wine and beer each have their own walk-in coolers, with two entrances each. The wine cooler is shared with cheese, but the beer cooler is all BEER.  You have local breweries, craft beer and imported beers to choose from and they're all ice cold.   Schnucks is also supporting local vendors which is obvious by, Sallume Beddou having their very own case. Fortunately for me, I live within walking distance of Sallume Beddou in the city, but I was glad to see their product readily available for the suburbanites.   The prepared foods, deli, sushi bar and Seafood and Shrimp Bar all had my mouth watering and I had just finished breakfast at First Watch.  As, their competition down the street, they have an amazing Gluten Free Department. The Kosher selection was even more extensive then I have seen in other stores.   I'll be honest, normally I do not like produce from Schnucks, but here they have taken fresh vegetables and fruits to a new level. To the level, where I was doubting my loyalty to meat. What is happening to me? This new year new me, has me developing a new love for vegetables.   The associates here are a throw back to the days when Schnucks promoted themselves as, "the friendliest stores in town". Every associate we had contact with was extremely friendly and helpful. One lady in particular was a major stand out. Every time I turned around, she was there. I kept going back and forth down the center horizontal aisle taking in all the vertical aisles. She kept asking me if I needed help finding something and I told her no that I was just taking it all in. At that point I realized she was staying in the center aisle so I asked her, "Are you here in the center aisle to give directions?"  To my surprise, she said yes. She was there to make sure customers found what they needed and wanted. Now that is top notch customer service.   I wish my Schnucks was just like this one, because going back to it now will be such a disappointment. The SO laughed when I said, this will be my new regular store. He knows me to well, I do not shop ahead - I shop for the meal. If I lived near by, I'd be here daily.

The Blue Duck has finally arrived in Saint Louis. Their original location is very popular in Washington, MO and I think selecting Maplewood as their STL location was a good move. My visit was on their fifth day of being opening and I so wish Yelp had a program where I could give a half star. My visit truly was between a 3 & 4 Star experience. As they get acclimated to their new city, I'm confident it will be a solid 4.   I started out with a craft beer and was impressed that the bartender asked if I wanted my glass to be chilled or at room temperature. I choose chilled. As an accompaniment to my beer, I selected; Fried Brussels Sprouts from the "Starters" on their menu. They had a bourbon pickled mustard glaze and were tossed with bacon and parmesan. I instantly was in love. These are by far the best brussels sprouts I have had at a restaurant and I eat them all the time.   The sprouts were a large serving and easily could have been my meal, but dining at a new restaurant I pushed on. I was torn on what to order next. Should I do a burger? Or my favorite seafood, Sea Scallops? Or even better yet, Smoked Fried Hot Chicken? The "hot" chicken won. I couldn't say no to a chicken that is breaded in Red Hot Riplets. It was two boneless breast, covered in a crisp coating and served a side of smoked fried potatoes. The pickled pepper gravy, did not impress me, but I was okay with just enjoying the chicken. I like it when a "hot" chicken makes me sweat. For me, that it is a sign that it is good.   I was too full to try a dessert, but I gotta come back and try the Gooey Butter Cheesecake Shake. It just sound delicious.   The ambiance is very minimalist. It's very stark and plain. When I return, if the burger and Sea Scallops win me over, I wont mind sitting in a minimalist environment. After all, I'm coming for the food, not the ambiance.   As time moves forward and word gets out that The Blue Duck has opened in Maplewood. I think this will be one of the "hot spots" on Manchester. Don't worry about parking, there's a large lot behind the restaurant just off of Sutton Avenue.   Will I return? Gotta try that dessert and Sea Scallops  When: February 19, 2017 Why: New restaurant in town

My momma raised me right. When ever you get a gift, you send a thank-you card. I recently celebrated the 32nd Anniversary of my 29th Birthday and received some very special and unique gifts. So in turn, I thought it was only appropriate that I send some very special and unique cards.  Hallmark was not an option. I needed the best from a local source, so I headed over to, The Firecracker Press.   The variety of note with STL themes were nice. However, I found two cards that were designed as a Thank-you card and they served my purpose very well. I did see other cards that caught my eye and I will return for another occasion.   Then to my surprise, when I got home and reached into my bag. TFP had given me a little thank-you postcard. It entitled me to 10% off on my next web purchase. I'm more of a brick and mortar shopper, but to save 10%, I can shop the web.   Will I return? - Yes, here and the web.   When: November 17, 2017 Why: Thank-you Cards

Huge fan of Katie's on Manchester. So when I finished up with my dentist in West County, I decided to give this T&C location a try. I'm glad to see the quality of food and service has carried over to this newer second location.   You cannot beat a better lunch special, then the one at Katie's. You get your choice of two delicious dishes for only $14.50. My first dish is always my favorite salad, Famous Fried Artichoke. It's a delightful and delicious mix of spring greens, artichokes, pistachio, asparagus and goat cheese. All tossed lightly in a Balsamic Vinaigrette. All I can say, is it's a Sensational Salad.   Normally, I get one of the lunch size pizzas, but today I ventured off to experience something new. On the bartenders recommendation, I choose, Prawn Panino. It was an amazing sandwich, served on a ciabatta bun. Between that soft bun was seared prawns, avocado and shaved fennel and a smear of lemon aioli. It's a very unique mix of ingredients and full of flavor.   The ambiance is very similar to the original location, sleek, contemporary and modern. Only thing I disliked, was the positioning of the two TV's at the end of the bar. I wasn't even watching, but their placement kept me thinking they were an afterthought in the design. It would have been better if they totally omitted them.   I'll be back? - If in the area, but I'll definitely be back at the Rock Hill.   When: October 2, 2018 Why: Lunchtime

It's been almost two years since my last review of Olio. Since that time, there have been staffing and management changes and when that happens the atmosphere of a business also change. Olio is still a relaxing and comfortable place to enjoy a masterfully created cocktail, but it no longer has the warm fuzzy feeling it once had. The service has almost become, cold and stiff. It is still very professional and attentive, just not as welcoming as it use to be. For that reason, I need to drop them down a star.   I do agree with Ian Froeb that Olio is definitely one of the top 100 restaurants in St. Louis. However, I disagree with on the must have item. I do enjoy his recommendation; King of Kings hummus, served with pieces of both pita bread and baguette. The portion is huge and will have a low-carb eater, forgetting their ways until the bowl of hummus and basket of bread are empty.   My recommendation of the "must have" is their egg salad and you must add the white anchovies. The creamy egg salad is served on slices of baguette with those salty little fishes resting on top. This is by far the best egg salad in the St. Louis area. If they sold it by the pound like a deli, I'd be an addict.   What makes their service stand out is that when  you're seated at the bar and your order is ready, they do not just sit it in front of you from the bartenders side of the bar. Which would be the easy and quickest way. They walk around and serve it from your back and to the left side. That fine dining etiquette, making them a class act.   I hope the warm fuzzies come back, because I love a good cocktail & their egg salad.   When: March 22, 2016 Why: After Work Cocktails

Rockwell is a great addition to the craft beer scene in STL. The ambiance is minimalistic and the outside patio is totally relaxing. Their patio faces busy Vandeventer Ave, but with a cold beer and a burger from Brasswell's kitchen you'll never notice the busy traffic buzzing by.
