Everyone has mentioned how great the beer is and they aren't wrong. It's very smooth and refreshing. I not a true beer person, I'm more of a whiskey man and love a good Manhattan. When I meet friends here, they were aghast when I ordered a Manhattan and not a beer. However, we were all surprised, it was top notch. I drink a lot of Manhattans all across this city and I could easily rate this one from a craft brewery in the top 5.   The food here is top notch. The small kitchen is called Brasswell and it is run by those at Brasserie By Niche. The burgers are smash burgers, thin juicy and topped with onions, american cheese, pickles and dijonaise. Their fries are addictive, skinny, crisp and just enough salt. During Lent on Friday's they offer a Fried Cod Sandwich with the same great fries as a side.  Rockwell is great place to hang with friends. I would also make it a stop when showing out-of-town guest around our city.   Special Note: Rockwell pays their employees a livable wage, so there is no tip line on your credit slips. The staff is professional and friendly.   I'll be back? - Yes!   When: January 10 & March 22, 2019 Why: UYE and Friday Fish Special

Foodies beware, $10 Entree specials does not mean a cheap meal. (lol) Everything here is al a carte, so by the time you add glasses of wine, salads and one dessert you reached $80. Oh, well we still enjoyed our experience.  We started out with a beet salad that was just over the top, full of flavor. The Caesar  Salad was in my opinion the best in STL. Their dressing had the perfect taste of anchovies, and the romaine was evenly covered with just the right amount.  Our $10 entrees had one success and one miss. The Chicken Soto was a success, it was charbroiled with roasted garlic and lemon. The chicken was tender, moist and very flavorful. It came with mashed potatoes,  and asparagus (3 tiny stalks). I would have liked more asparagus, it's my favorite vegetable, but hey it was a $10 special.  The Porchetta Panino was another experience, it was flavorful but the pork was extremely tuff. It was chewing old bubble gum. The truffle Parmesan fries were so good, I think they might have been made by angels.  The table next to us were ahead of us in the dining experience , so I took note of their desserts. They had pumpkin cheesecake, yum. They raved about it, so I knew that is what i wanted. We ordered ours to go, it's so fun to eat cheesecake while you watch the end of Biggest Loser on TV. When we got home, our cheesecake was just that cheesecake, not the pumpkin. Yes, I was disappointed, but it was still awesome cheesecake. It had great flavor and texture, can't wait to go back and actually have the right one. We'll be back for sure, leathery pork will not turn us away everything else was just too good.

A big shout-out to The Bellwether & Polite Society on #ThankyouThursday. I enjoyed that you combined both of your menus and provided #touchless #curbside service at The Bellwether. You made it so easy. Who would have thought a restaurant on the third floor, could do it so smoothly. Those cameras did a great job.   I've ordered my favorite, Butcher Steak a couple of times during this pandemic and each time, it was delicious. Once I added a bottle of your house red wine and it was perfect accompaniment. I'll be ordering it the next time I'm sitting at the bar when this damn thing is over.   I changed up sides up, my first time I enjoyed my favorite Brussels Sprouts and Fries. The second time was for the Yelp's Big Night In. That night, I enjoyed a side salad and Broccoli with my steak. As a bonus, I had Mac-n-Cheese, too. This was the night I enjoyed the wine. I plated it on my fine china, which I hardly use anymore and served the wine in Waterford crystal. My place sitting never looked so good. The food from, The Bellwether made it shine.   Again, you made the #curbside service so easy. I pulled up, popped the backend of my CRV open and waited for my delivery. One of my favorite staff personnel came down with my order and placed it in my designated box in the rear of my CRV. We chatted through my open window, doing the social distancing. Service may have been #curbside, but it was still personalized and top notch, just like if I were upstairs.   Will I return? - Pandemic cannot get over fast enough.   When? - April 11, 2020 and earlier date Why? - Yelp's Big Night In and a Friday Night Carry-Out Dinner

We were totally blown away with our first visit to The Block. I will say, it is by far the BEST BURGER and Best Mac - n - Cheese in the city. Both of these menu items were totally off the charts.  Our lunch started with two salads; Asparagus Salad and Block Salad. I enjoyed a small Asparagus Salad, which was the perfect size to enjoy before a Block Burger. I'm confident that a large would be a meal by itself. Which would be a dream for a vegetarian. It was not only grilled asparagus, but it also had mixed greens, roasted beets, goat cheese (my favorite), toasted walnuts and tossed in a balsamic vinaigrette .  The BF enjoyed The Block Salad which was not your typical chef salad. It may sound like it, but when you add their bacon, smoked ham, smoked cheddar to greens, tomato, egg, red onion and toss it with a Buttermilk dressing it becomes a culinary masterpiece. He too, enjoyed the small size. Again, the large would be a perfect meal for someone who is watching their weigh or just wanting a health choice for lunch.   Now let's talk about the two items that are taking the #1 position on two of my Yelp list. The Block Burger was a huge 8 oz. grass fed beef, grilled medium and topped with farmhouse white cheddar. It was the most juicy, well seasoned and grilled burger I have had in a long time. I do not know what kind of grass those cows were eating, but it made that burger the best. If that wasn't enough, the Garlic Herbed Fries were the perfect accompaniment with a little cup of ketchup.   I had heard so much about their amazing Baked Mac -n - Cheese, that I had to have some. Since we both had salad and entrees, we ordered a small so we could experience a little bit of heaven. It was rich, creamy and baked in a little cast iron casserole dish to give a perfect crunchy top. The table of three next to us, ordered a large portion and it was perfect for sharing. It would of been enough it they had a fourth.   Paula Deen may be in need of some comfort food right now and I know what would make her feel better. A healthy portion of the Shrimp & Grits at The Block. Their grits can put a smile on any Southern Belle or Gentleman. Add 4 huge shrimp on top of the cheddar grits and you've got a great lunch.   My only negative is that we arrived early for lunch early and as others arrived they clustered them around our table. They had everyone on top of each other. In a large dining room, it made us feel cramped. However, making 7 of my list and a cute water faucet  that resembled a old fashion water pump in the men's room gives them a solid 5 Stars.

My update for TBD is long overdue. They've come a long way since, they first opened. I was thrilled when they sold the location in Washington to focus on this one. The attention to details and creativity in the menu shows and they've won me over. They've won me over so much, that I have become a semi regular.   I highly recommend that you follow them on Facebook, so you can see the weekly chef specials and weekly Slam Burger. The Classic and Sam Elliott Burgers are regular menu items and favorites of mine, but the weekly Slam Burgers also, gets my attention.   Benedict is always a favorite Brunch item for me and I like how they kick it up and get creative with it here. I absolutely love the Catfish Benedict. It is so delicious. (It is now Trout) They serve theirs with a fried poached eggs and a brown butter hollandaise. The home fries are crisp and seasoned beautifully.   The cocktails are equally as amazing and creative as the food. Specialty cocktail menu changes regularly, so always be sure to check it out. I'm a Classic Cocktail type man, but my last visit I enjoyed two of their specialty cocktails. Aww, Kenny and Complicated Martini were both good and I'd recommend them for anyone who's a fan of an Old Fashioned and a Dirty Martini.   The service is always friendly and attentive. Sitting at the bar for me is a plus, the other regulars who sit there as well are always up for good conversation.   I'll be back? - I'm a regular.   When: Multiple times Why: I'm a fan of their burgers and fish

A delightful little florist shop. I discovered it on Small Business Saturday when I was shopping at Four Muddy Paws, next door. The staff was so friendly and helpful. They made me feel so welcomed in their flower and gift shop.   While shopping, I was able to find a yard flag holder and a holiday flag to start my collection of flags.  I have always wanted one of these and when I moved into my new house,  most of my neighbors all had them. So, I thought it was time to take the plunge and make the purchase. I'm glad it was from a local small business and not a chain or mail-order. I also, purchased a new ornament for my Christmas tree. You can never have too many holiday decorations.  I'm hosting my family Christmas dinner this year, so I plan on having Wildflower doing my centerpiece. Don't worry, my gathering will  be within the CDC guidelines.   Will I return? - Yep!   When: November 28, 2020 Why: Small Business Saturday

It was a Grand Day on South Grand Blvd today, as Urban Matter held its Grand Opening for their new location. I was a frequent shopper at the original location and I plan to continue at this spacious new one.   One of my favorite cousins birthday is next week so I was in need of her gift. Last year, I got her a beautiful blue leather purse from UM. So since that gift was such a hit, I came back for this year. I knew I couldn't repeat the same theme, even though they once again had an amazing selection.   As I browsed their new layout, I found a perfect gift. Well, actually it was a gift bag. It was a canvas and leather wine gift bag. My cousin loves wine, so this was perfect. I grabbed the bag, found some cocktail napkins and a notepad for making a Market List. Now all I need is a bottle of wine.   When I gift shop, I usually find something for myself, too. Today, I found a Travel Straw.  I'm anti plastic straw, so this collapsable/adjustable stainless steel straw in a plastic case. This is awesome, I can be environmentally friendly and still enjoy my drinks with a straw.   The staff at UM is always top-notch. Friendly and professional is the way they do business and I like it.   Will I return? - They're the best place for gifts.   When: July 20, 2019 Why: Grand Opening and need of gift.

I was looking so forward to my first visit Crown Candy Kitchen, after-all I have lived in Saint Louis for 33 years and had never gone. When it was featured on the Food Network for the Heart Stopping BLT, I knew I had to make time and go. I knew as soon as I walked in I had not missed much those past 33 years.   The building outside appears so run down, we were not even sure they were open. At first I was surprised to see parking meters, in such a dilapidated neighborhood. Once inside the ambiance did not improve. The floor was in need of being replaced and the booths could use a fresh coat of paint. To be honest, the entire place felt claustrophobic and dirty. I was willing to over look those details and consider it character if the food was good, but it was horrible.   My Heart Stopping BLT was heart breaking. The bacon was cold, rubbery and chewy as hell. I was expecting hot fresh off the grill bacon and it was far from it. Actually it tasted as if it were fried the day before. I've had better malts at Steak - n - Shake. I took a bite of the SO's Ruben and thought the Corned Beef was fatty and the sandwich had to much Thousand Island Dressing.   I could go on about the limp potato chips, warm pickle and lackluster service, but I have got to shake this negative experience and move on. Thank goodness, we had Yelp Mints in the car to rid our mouths of the horrible after taste we both had.   This is a tourist trap and I am embarrassed that it is representing my hometown.

Not my shot glass of vodka and I love vodka. How this place was selected as one of the best 100 restaurants in STL is beyond me. The only thing that saved it from getting a two star rating and being placed on my Terrible Two's list was the $1 off my cocktail for checking in on Yelp and the fact that the Pork Pelmeni which Ian Froeb recommended was actually good.   What I did not like was the odor that hit me in the face as I entered. It was not a just freshly cleaned smell, it was an unpleasant scent. I just ignored it and took a seat at the bar. Which was a big mistake. I think I would have been better off at a table. Not only did I have to brush away fruit flies, but the bartender was busy servicing the tables more then she was the bar. At first I thought it was strange that she kept rushing me and pushing me to order everything at once. She also seemed put out when I asked questions about the items on the menu.  Then I realized, she was hustling and working the bar and both sides of the restaurant as a server.   Here's the run down on my order:  New Old Fashioned - I've had better, but can I really complain about a $5 cocktail.   Brussels Sprouts Salad - The bacon was rubbery and the burnt honey vinaigrette was bitter  Pelmini - Good pork flavored Russian style dumpling. Saved them from only getting 2 Stars  The fruit flies were a big distraction, having to wave them away constantly. The bartender even waved them away from my area. I gave up on eating my salad when I saw two resting in my salad bowl.   I also felt sorry for the bartender/server. They were way to busy, to so understaffed. If she wasn't so rushed to do everything, I'm sure she'd been more attentive.   When: August 9, 2016 Why: Lunch - STL 100

Bemiston Cocktail Club is exactly what its name says, a cocktail club. There are no bells and whistles. It's a just a great place to go and enjoy an amazing, masterfully made cocktail.   It's a simple little bar tucked away down a long hallway. There's no table service. You order your cocktails at the bar and then select your table. When your cocktails are ready they'll set them at the end of the bar for you to retrieve. Eliminating the server is reflected in the price. The prices here are much lower then some of the more popular bars in the STL area.  I am a lover of the "classics". By that I mean, I love the classic cocktails. You know what I'm talking about. Give me a Manhattan, Old Fashioned and a Dirty Martini and I'm a happy boozer. During this visit I truly enjoyed a masterfully made, Old Fashioned. When I was ready for a second one, I was torn. I didn't know if I should go with a Manhattan or try their Dirty Martini. After chatting with the bartender, I knew it had to be the Dirty. He informed me, the Dirty Martini was one of their most popular. It was so popular, that they made them by the pitcher to keep up with the demand.   BBC's focus is cocktails. They have a very limited menu, but it offers just enough to have a nosh to accompany your cocktails. I choose the, Fried's. It was a basket of tater tots and onion rings with two dipping sauces. Tasty tots, but my rings were a little overdone. However, I did enjoy both dipping sauces. Good nosh, but on the next visit I'm going for the Nacho Popcorn.   If your group is small and you can sit at the bar (limited sitting), I highly recommend it. I did and I enjoyed chatting with the bartenders. I also enjoyed watching them make all the other cocktails. It was like a floor show.   I'll be back? - Hell, YES!  When: August 8, 2019 Why: Needed a cocktail.

I'll give them 3 Stars, because I like West Elm. However, I gotta tell you the customer service here was zero. Both associates stayed seated at the center desk and did not greet me as I circled the showroom twice.   Another customer entered the store with a mail-order return and one of the associates got up and assisted her at the front of the store. As I passed the seated associate for my third time, she finally asked me how I was doing. I replied, "I'm fine, thank-you." I then exited the store and went home and placed an on-line order for what I wanted.   I prefer brick and mortar over on-line shopping, but customer service like this is what pushed me to the internet.   Will I return? - I'll give them another try.   When: March 5, 2020 Why: Saw something I wanted in my Facebook Feed

Great addition to The Grove. The service is fast & friendly just like their other locations. You order at the counter, then you get a card marker to take to your table.  No name calling here, your calzone is hand delivered directly to you. After you're done dining, you don't even have to bus your own table, they do that for you as well. All the service is basically like a sit down restaurant, except you order at the counter.   My usual order is the Meat Me in St. Louis, but today I changed things up. I ordered, the Fatty B which Ian Froeb said is the "must order" on his STL 100 list for 2016. The Fatty B is filled with; Pepperoni, Meatballs, White Onion, Provolone, Roasted Garlic, Ricotta and Garlic Oil. Of course, it had a Spicy Red Sauce on the side. Damn, it was good. A little too garlicky for me, but lucky for me I had some Yelp breath mints in my pocket so the problem was easily rectified.   This may become the most popular location for SOTS. With the night life of The Grove, this place is going to be a hot spot. I know for me, this location is closer to home and I'll be stopping by for lunches on my days off. Salads, Calzones and craft beer - life is good.   When: October 18, 2016 Why: Lunch & Checking out the new location

Excellent customer service and excellent pricing. When I did a gut rehab of my kitchen, I shopped here for an estimate. They beat every other estimate, including the company who was doing the remodel.   I got all new stainless steel appliances,  and they all had rebates which made the deal even sweeter. I love'm all.  With a gut rehab, I needed a small refrigerator  and freezer to get through me through the weeks of no kitchen. They also, made me a great package price on these items.   I recommend this appliance store over any Big Box store. You'll get true personalized service.

Having a baby shower at work for a male employee who is a Cardinal fan? Let me tell you what the best gift ever, is. It's a stuffed bear or pup in a St. Louis Cardinal uniform from Build-A-Bear. Being a dog lover, I went for the Chocolate Chunk Pup. I named him, Yadi.   The stuffed pup may have to sit on the shelf until the newborn is older, but it was a major hit and favorite gift of the dad.   Build-A-Bear is a great hometown company that allows you to create a special toy for that child or adult who has everything and needs a new companion. Check it out. Perhaps you need a new friend, too.   Staff was friendly and helpful. As an adult purchaser, they weren't totally turned on as I have seen them with children creating their new friend. Which was just fine with me.   Will I return? - Next baby shower for sure.   When: Sometime in 2017 Why: Gift for a baby shower

My experience was not as bad as all the previous reviews. It's fast food, so I did not have my expectations set high and they exceeded my expectations.   It was a lazy day and I didn't want to cook. I was craving chicken wings and just heard a commercial for the new boneless wings at Arby's served with Crinkle fries. I didn't need to hear it twice. Wings and my favorite type of fries was a winning dinner for me.   I choose to go inside instead of waiting in line for drive-thru. Once inside, I cheerfully greeted and informed that someone would be with me shortly. The crew of four was hustling preparing orders. They each seemed to have a task and were moving at a good speed.   The young man working the drive-up window, stepped over to take my order and apologized for the small delay. I ordered my boneless wings and made it a 9 piece combo. By the time I got my soda and picked up some additional condiments, I only had a brief wait for my food to be ready.   My drive home is short, I live only a mile away. By the time I got home, plated my food, took Yelp pictures and sat down in front of the TV to enjoy my fast food, it was still warm. That tells me, my food was made fresh and was not under a heat light ahead of time.   Typically, I only give fast-food places 3 Stars for the simple fact that they are, "fast food". However, I'm making an exception this time, because this staff was doing a good job and my food was sports bar good.   When: November 14, 2021 Why: Lazy Dinner

As promised, I came back with friends for Happy Hour and we had a good time.  Let's talk cocktails, we ordered; Stan The Man Manhattan (like the hometown twist), Cucumber Infused "Water" (and it went down as refreshing as water) and Pinot Grigio. Wine is wine, but let me tell you the Manhattan and Cucumber water were damn good. I'll have to be careful not to have too many Cucumber drinks before shopping. I may need to keep them as a reward for a job well done after a power shopping experience.   As we enjoyed multiple rounds of "adult" beverages, we snacked on chicken wings, Seared Ahi Tuna and Flatbread with Shrimp & Pesto. The Chicken Wings, were not your typical bar wing. I liked that there was just enough sauce to coat the wing and give you the flavor. I hate wings that are overly coated and your napkin looks like you're eating BBQ ribs. Also, being a little anal retentive, I liked how the wings were neatly stacked on the plate and not just piled on.   Having had the Seared Ahi Tuna at a private party I was anxious to have it again. To persuade my friends to order it, I pulled out my trusty iPhone and showed pictures of how fantastic it looked. When it arrived at the table my heart sank, it looked nothing like what I had experienced. At the party, it was presented on thinly sliced cucumber and today it was just sliced and presented on a plate. How boring, the cucumber completed the presentation and flavor. However, this way the Tuna was still very flavorful and I am not a sushi fan.   When we ordered the Flatbread, we requested that the Shrimp be grilled. Our server checked with the kitchen and they said "no problem". When ours arrived, the shrimp was not grilled. Oh well, I guess we were pushing our luck with a special request. Serving it their way was still light and refreshing. You really can not go wrong with pesto and shrimp.   Our server was great, as was the hostess, bartender and one of the managers who stopped by our table to chat. I will be honest in saying, my biggest complaint and it is something that they can not really do anything about was a six and eight year old sitting at the bar.  I have no problem with children, I just wish they were in a  booth so we could have adult conversation without worrying about what we are saying.

If Garden Heights offered punch cards for their frequent shoppers, I would have filled numerous cards this season. After having a multi level retaining wall built in my front yard, we needed to fill it with perennials and annuals that can handle sun. We stripped the front yard bare and were creating a entire new look.   We made a couple of visits in preparation for the completion of our project. Once it was finished, we were ready to do some serious shopping. We pulled into the parking lot, which even at early afternoon weekday was bustling. My regular parking space was taken, so I took the next best one. After parking, I opened the hatch on my CRV, because I knew we were doing some serious shopping.   At the end of this shopping expedition, we filled our CRV with; Green Velvet Boxwood, Vilet Filli Crapemyrtle, Scaevola, Colocasia, Russian Sage, Daylily, Lantana, Zinnia and Periwinkle Vinca.  The staff at Garden Heights was extremely helpful in assisting us in selecting the combination of plants we choose. I love how they work as a team and make the entire shopping experience fun. Truly the best customer service I have found at a nursery this season.

I typically work on Saturdays, so I never get a chance to attend TGFM. Then I discovered, they do a smaller version on Tuesday nights as well. It may not be as massive as the Saturday market, but it is still a great opportunity to pick up some fresh veggies and meats, too.   In addition to the variety of farmers selling their produce, you'll also find a variety of other vendors promoting their wares. As I browsed the booths, I munched on freshly made pretzels and sipped a 4 Hands Beer. Now that is shopping in comfort. My best find of the evening was, fresh corn on the cob.   Another big bonus of TGFM is the food trucks. Before you shop or after you've completed your shopping you can enjoy a quick dinner from one of the many food trucks. I had meet a group of friends and we all took our blankets and had dinner picnic style. In addition, to the food trucks, there was a mobil comic book truck, which sent one of my friends over the top with excitement.   Oh, before I forget - they also have free yoga class on Tuesday night.    I can only wish my work schedule changes, so I can experience TGFM on the grander scale on Saturdays.   I'll be back? - Yes, I'll take my cooler to buy some grass-feed beef.   When: August 21, 2018 Why: It was a CYE (Community Yelp Event)

Hello Darkness, my new friend I've come to devour you again Because a vision of chocolate Left its crumbs while I was sleeping And the vision that was planted in my brain Still remains within the pleasures of La Patisserie Choquette  It's been over three years, I guess it is time to do an update to my review. I've been wanting to making my Terrible Two's List shorter, so when I saw La Patisserie on Ian Froeb's STL 100 List for 2016, I knew it was time to re-visit. Wow, I've been missing out these last three years. My first visit was during their first month and I should of been more understanding of the newness.   This time around the staff was charming, friendly and very helpful. Not only is Simone an amazing & artistic baker, her professionalism in customer service skills blew me away. As I enjoyed my coffee and The Darkness, I could over hear her on a sales call and she nailed it. Her soft spoken voice and verbiage painted a perfect picture of their services. After the phone call, she worked the dining area and made sure every guest was content and pleased with their pastries.   On my revisit, I had to enjoy; The Darkness. Not only am I a certified chocoholic, but Ian said it is, "the must order" on his STL 100 List. I knew I couldn't go wrong with a chocolate croissant. Layer upon layer of flaky chocolate drizzled in more chocolate. I was in total heaven. I've looked at their catering and I will definitely be using them this upcoming holiday season.   LPC is worthy of 5 Stars, but I'm being selfish and giving only 4. I'm taking a star away, because of the parking and being closed on Monday. Monday is my day off and I can't come enjoy these delicious pastries. I told you, I was selfish......LOL.   Go & try The Darkness.   When: October 26, 2016 Why: The Darkness and Ian Froeb

Do you love STL? Or perhaps you know someone who loves, STL. If you answered yes to either of statements, this is the store for you.   Everything here shouts, STL. You'll find caps, hoodies, T-Shirts, mugs and much more branded with St. Louis, STL or a  simple Fleur-de-lis. I absolutely loved it. I bought several ornaments for holiday gifts and a cap and mug for myself.   The shop pops up on you faster then you'd think on Brentwood, so be prepared. Also, there are limited parking spaces in front, but there are some along the side and back. Hope and pray that you get one in front.   Will I return? - Do I love, STL?  When: December 4, 2020 Why: Christmas Gifts and Gift Bag for YEE

When I moved over to the Riverbend area, I was worried about finding a good BBQ restaurant. After all, I had so many to choose from living in the city of STL. There it was like finding a Walgreens, there practically was one on every block.   After a few misses at other restaurants, I thought I'd give Fire-n-Smoke a try. Actually, I was driving back from STL and my go to in STL was closed due to a water pipe break, so I had no BBQ in the car. When I programmed their address in the GPS, I was shocked how close it was to the intersection of 111 and 255. This was going to be an easy pick-up and back on the road to home.   First impressions count and this place was super clean, practicing social distancing and everyone was wearing mask (correctly) and the staff were also wearing gloves on both sides of the counter. Win!   Being a first time visitor, I'll admit I went overboard with my order. I ordered way to much food for one person, but I got to sample many things and I divided it up into additional meals. Not only did I have today's lunch, but I also have lunch and dinner for tomorrow.   To sample multiple meats, I ordered the Three Meat Platter. I choose; Baby Back Ribs, Burnt Ends and Pulled Pork. The young cashier recommended the pulled pork, she said it was one of their most popular. Out of the three meats, it was my favorite. The ribs had good flavor, but did not totally fall off the bone the way I like it. I had to do some work,  to get all the meat off the bone. The Burnt Ends were good, but a little fattier then I am use to. However, I'll give them another try.   My platter came with two sides. Everyone raves about the Mac-n-Cheese in the Yelp reviews, so it was a no brainer to choose it. Again, I asked the cashier which other one I should choose and she recommended the Fried Potato Twisters. I didn't want two heavy carbs, so I asked if they did the BBQ Beans in house and she said, yes. I know it's another carb, but it just seemed a better choice. Also, easier to split up into another meal than cold fries.   I liked the Mac-n-Cheese. I really appreciated that it was baked and served in its own separate tin dish. Could have had more seasoning for me, but that can be resolved with a pepper shaker and spices from home. The BBQ Beans were pretty standard and had good flavor and lots of brisket pieces in it.   In addition to the Three Meat Platter, I ordered 6 Chicken Wings and I'll tell you now, these little babies will be a go to for me. They are smoked over oak before being tossed in the fryer and tossed in the sauce of your choice. I had the Buffalo sauce served on the side for mine. No sauce needed, these little beauties tasted divine, just as they were. Best of all, they also packaged them, 3 flats and 3 drums. If you know me, you know I want the numbers to match.   Service was friendly and as stated earlier, they were following CDC guidelines to the max.   So glad I finally gave them a try and realized it's only a 12-15 drive from home. Not bad for good BBQ.   When: February 20, 2021 Why: Lunch and Searching for a BBQ joint to call my own.

What a fun dive bar.  I've been here just for a cocktail and I've been here for a couple of their fun events. They've hosted two events that I've attended. One being, Meat Bingo. Yes, MEAT. It was a typical bingo game, but instead of winning money, you won various meat packages from Kenrick Meat Shop. I Bingo'd and won a cut-up chicken for frying. My friend won a couple pounds of boneless chicken breast. Cash is good, but so is MEAT.   The other event I attended was a Wine and Pizza Pairing. The pizza was TJ Pizza and a local liquor vendor who spoke of the wines he paired to the various wines. It was a fun event. I was surprised at how flavorful the frozen pizzas were. Next time someone is selling TJ Pizza, I will consider buying one.   On the other hand, the wine paired with the pizza was totally impressive. So impressive, that I bought a case of the one of the featured wines. They offered single bottles or a full case for purchase.  Got a price break for the full case, so others in my group liked the same wine, so went for the case. Holiday gifts at a savings.   Staff, owners and other patrons are all friendly. This has to be the best dive bar in STL.   Will I return? - Yes, Meat Bingo is a monthly event.   When: It's a dive bar, can't share that information now.  Why: Need an escape.

1-800-Got-Junk is what it is and what it is, is a life saver. Some may say, they are a rip-off and over-priced. I say, they are worth every penny. Their staff is professional, polite and clean-cut. The ones doing my job, truly were the boy next door types. The trucks are well maintained and extremely clean for being trucks designated for hauling junk.   Why would I pay someone to haul away my junk? My free time is very valuable to me and I don't have any friends who own pick up trucks. Plus, I'd have to research where to dispose of my unwanted items and sometimes you need permits for proper disposal. Got Junk, takes care of all of that for me and when they can, they recycle.   It's easy to schedule an appointment. They truly do come when it is convenient for you. So, don't keep living with that junk you hate - call 1-800-Got-Junk and start living your life junk free. You'll be glad that you did.   When: September 27, 2016 Why: I had junk

A very cute bakery on Cherokee Street. I had just enjoyed breakfast down the street at The Mud House on a vacation day and thought since I was in the neighborhood, I would drop in for some sweet treats. I've tried to shop here before, but their schedule and mine do not mesh. My regular days off from work are Monday and Tuesday and those are their off days too. So I had to jump at this opportunity to buy a sugar rush for later in the day.   The ambiance is warm and cozy. Nothing fancy, just down-home comfortable. I found the staff to be a little lackluster. Most of the other new bakeries in town, the staffs are bubbly and very charismatic. Here, the customer service was plain Jane and monotoned.   Stopping in at 11 AM , the counter had sold down, but I found two items that caught my eye and teased my taste buds.  Loving pumpkin, this is my time of the year. So when I saw their Pumpkin Scone, I knew I had to try it. My other treat was their Popcorn Cookie. I had to see what that combination would do to my taste buds.   The Popcorn Cookie made my taste buds dance. It was moist and I enjoyed the combination of sweet and salty. I could see myself ordering these by the dozen.  Their Pumpkin Scone, was not a true scone. The flavor was great, but the texture was more of a muffin. It was in the shape of a scone, looked like a scone, but tasted like a muffin.   Great bakery. I'm a fan, I'll be back next time I have a PTO day. Or when they start to open on Monday or Tuesday.

Love me some Mississippi Mud Pottery!   I've received a couple of gifts from MMP and have truly enjoyed them. I use them when entertaining guest and as an decorative accent when there is no party in the house. I like the Mixed Berry pattern, it has a rich red tone and a masculine feel to its' design.  In fact I like it so much I have gone myself and added additional pieces to my collection.  The staff is very friendly and it is cool that you can view an artists working right there in the showroom. Another thing that I think makes them unique, is that a couple getting married can pick or design their own pattern and have it registered for gifts.  Almost makes me want to get married just for the pottery. Just kidding, I'd marry for money first.  So next time you go to Fast Eddies or the Loading Dock in Grafton, stop by MMP and get some amazing pottery.

I am going to start this review the same way I started my last review 10 years ago, "Love me some Mississippi Mud Pottery!".   I am blown away that they have been around for 38 years. That is longer than some of my friends marriages have lasted. MMP is one its second pair of owners. The first couple owned from its creation in 1983 till 2006. The current owners, Chad and Felicia took over in 2006 and have been throwing that mud and creating the same high quality pottery since then.   After having a delightful lunch at, Brown Bag Bistro next door, I strolled over to MMP. Whenever I am in the area, I stop by to see what's new. Today I spotted a dip cooler and thought it would be a good gift for a cousin who entertains frequently. Only thing, I wanted it in a smaller size and different pattern than what was on display.   I shared my request with the associate working and she said they were done accepting orders for Christmas, but they could try to get it done. I told her there was no rush, that if it wasn't done in time, I'd just add it to my gift drawer and give it for another occasion. It was a close call, it was the week of Christmas, but they called and they had it completed.   Since it was the week of Christmas and I was working everyday 12 hour shifts, I asked if I could pay for it over the phone and send someone else to pick it up. They said, it was okay and they'd have it ready for my personalized currier service. To my surprise, when my cousin who picked it up for me brought it my work, they had already prepared it as a gift. That is good customer service.   In closing, I'll give you some information from their website -  Mississippi Mud Pottery specializes in wheel-thrown stoneware pottery, made for everyday use. Fired to a high temperature, these wares are microwave, dishwasher, oven, and food safe. The quality of the finished work is suitable for daily use, yet can be displayed when not in use.  Shopping here you are not only supporting a local business, but also a local artist.

Boo-Hiss! Strange Donuts has lost their luster. They no longer are a shining star in my donut universe. The donuts we experienced this morning were bland, flavorless and dried out as if they were yesterdays product. Out of the four donuts purchased, not one was entirely eaten. Each only had bites taken out of them, before being thrown into the trash. These donuts were being shared between two people and both gave big thumbs down.  Banana Chocolate Peanut Butter - No banana taste at all and it was supposed to be the featured flavor. Very dry texture.    Maple Bacon - This one could have been a winner, but the bacon was like chewing Bazooka Bubble Gum. I wanted to experience that contrast between salt and sweet.  Bart's Revenge - A chocolate cake donut with chocolate icing topped with crumbles of a Butterfinger candy bar. This was a repeat of a previous visit and it did not repeat the quality we had before. The donut was dry and the flavor of the Butterfinger could not be tasted, the chocolate donut dominated.   Gooey Butter -  Another one we repeated and another disappointment. Again, I do not get the Gooey Butter flavor. It was more like a gas station cheese danish.   Customer Service is always spot on friendly, but selling these donuts at $2 each is only worth 2 Stars.

So much has happened since I last reviewed this Imo's. There has been a change in ownership and a disastrous fire that had them closed for almost a year. I am happy to say, that once they reopened, they are back and better than ever. In fact, I will go out on a limb and say they are better then a corporately owned Imo's in STL.   I'll start out saying the rebuild after the fire is a vast improvement on the previous restaurant. It is a minimalist feel, which is relaxing and inviting for dine in pizza parlor.   Since they have re-opened, I have done carry-out a couple of times and I have had delivery to my work and home addresses. Each time, my orders were done correctly and the ones that were delivered were speedy and efficient. Each delivery the delivery person was masked and offered no touch delivery which was appropriate during this pandemic.  Some of my go-to order are; a 1/2 Deluxe Salad with House Dressing, my favorite sandwich is the, Imo's Extra Special and I always get it hot. My favorite pizza is Italian Sausage with Jalapeños or the Deluxe pizza which basically has everything imaginable on it. Oh, I like their wings too. Trying the pasta is on my bucket list for local restaurants.   The customer service is top notch. They are very personable. The two brothers who are the current owners are very customer service focused and I appreciate that.   I am thrilled beyond belief that I get to remove this Imo's from my No-No Collection.

I am so glad Wellspent Brewing is back open in the Lou. I was also surprised to see that their old check-in on Yelp was gone. When I checked in, all that popped up was this new one. Either way, I am thrilled they are back and considering the large standing room only crowd, I am not the only one.   The Wellspent brewery is small, compact and cozy. There are several stools at the bar, multiple tables and several high-tops as well. In addition to all the indoor seating, WB has a relaxing patio. While I was there for the Grand Opening, several patrons enjoying cigars outside. In addition to stogie smokers, there were also some K-9's enjoying the re-opening with their owners.   Great locally brewed beer, friendly staff and K-9 friendl. Welcome back to the local craft beer scene, Wellspent.   When: February 15, 2020 Why: Grand Re-Opening

Three visits = 3 Stars.  What impresses me most about Yolklore is that they are very eco-friendly. I like that they use their dirty trays for composting. I try to recycle as much as I possibly can, so when I see businesses doing something for our environment, I'm impressed.   Food wise, I like their crispy potatoes and for quick serve counter food, they do a very good Biscuits and Gravy. The buttermilk biscuits are flakey and moist and the Sage Sausage Gravy is seasoned well. As I have said before, I was raised on a farm and I know B&G's. These receive a former farmers seal of approval.   I've eaten; Classic Breakfast, Johnny Ham Hands and their Nest Egg. Out of the three, I'd say the Classic Breakfast was the best. It truly is a classic breakfast. It has two eggs your style, meat of choice, a biscuit with sage sausage gravy and their famous crispy potatoes. Having this breakfast, you will not go away hungry.   Johnny Ham is a Plain Jane ham sandwich, nothing really impressive. The Nest Egg was a major disappointment. The biscuit shell was hard and tough, my eggs were under poached and the bacon was equally as tough as the biscuit shell.   What holds them back from getting a fourth star is their customer service. I'd highly recommend the staff go visit other businesses similar to theirs and see how counter service should be done. The staff here is cold and very unfriendly. On one of my visits, I was the only person there and on the other two visits had two and three other diners and they arrived as I was leaving. So being overly busy was not the excuse for providing cold inattentive service.  Also, with large windows and an open view of the kitchen, the cooks should be aware that all eyes are on them. Some things should not be seen.   Well I return? - If a friend wants to go, I'll give them another try. Otherwise, I have too many other breakfast cafes closer to home.   When: August 5 & August 8, 2016 and January 23, 2017 Why: Breakfast, of course.

I've lived in Godfrey for a year and have enjoyed eating meals from Joe's multiple times. I just realized, I have not sung their praises. So it's time to show them some love with a Yelp review.   Joe's offers dine-in, carry-out and delivery. I have done two of the three. I haven't experienced, delivery. I live so close and have such short patience, that I just go pick-up my order. However, I can say the dine-in experience is attentive and friendly and my carry-out is always ready when I walk in.   My go to for pizza is thin crust. I'm a true STL man and love my pizza crust crispy and thin. My favorite toppings are always, Italian Sausage and Jalapeños. For me, a pizza is not a pizza if it doesn't have jalapeños. Joe's is generous with their toppings and cheese, so the pizzas are extra flavorful. I also like that they cut the pizza like a pie and not in those squares like a popular STL pizza does.   I have also enjoyed the chicken wings here. The offer both bone-in and boneless. My favorite is the bone-in. They fry them extra crisp and their buffalo sauce give just the right amount of zing. Their salads are mostly iceberg lettuce, but the toppings and dressing makes them acceptable.   A bonus of dining-in, they have an amazing variety of wine and beer to enjoy with your meal. They have 12 different wines and 12 draft beers. That's more than some sports bars and regular restaurants have.   I'm going to keep coming back and I plan to try some of their pasta dishes and sandwiches in the future.

I'll give them 3 Stars, because they're a QT. However, this is my least favorite Quik Trip in STL. It is totally crazy in the parking lot and at times unsafe.   Why unsafe? Other customers are not paying attention to the surroundings and driving like they are competing in a Stock car demolition derby. Also, on my most recent visit, I was hassled by two different homeless people. Typically, I am one who helps and gives them a buck or two or take them inside and treat them to what they want. However, on this day, I was uncomfortable.  So uncomfortable, that I left and never even made it into the QT. They lost a sale of gas and snacks.   Great location!

I'll try to make this one simple.  Pros  New (fairly) Convenient  location - next to my favorite Lowe's & 55 too.  Clean and well kept.  Cons  Unfriendly staff - actually rude Poor lay-out Selection not the same as other Schnucks Poor produce  Hey Schnucks, how can you get it so right at one location and miss it at another? This location should be a gold mine.

As I am eating my way through Ian Froeb's STL 100 List for 2016, I am realizing how I haven't written updates for some of the popular restaurants. I just continue to eat there, but forget that time has passed and I need to keep current. Bad me, but I am now trying to correct this bad behavior.   Bailey's Range is one that I have continued to eat at, without doing an update. BR has consistently served up quality burgers and fries. When I want to be bad, I go with one of their incredible shakes. If the devil is inside of me, I enjoy a boozy shake with no regrets.   This recent visit was a simple one. I went after seeing two of David Bailey's restaurants appear on Ian Froeb's List. I sat at the bar/counter and enjoyed a Lou Dog form Modern Brewery. I didn't want a heavy lunch, so I went with Ian's "must order" and enjoyed a Basic Burger and Small Fries. I added a White Cheddar to my burger and just catsup with my fries. My garnishes were only lettuce, onion and pickles. Once I saw and tasted the pickles, I did not waste them on the burger. I ate them all by themselves and relished in their flavor.   My burger was prepared to a perfect medium and the fries as always were crispy and tender on the inside. I do believe it was Bailey's Range that got me obsessed with my ketchup being served in a little cup. For me it makes a better presentation and I also think it is also a cleaner and healthier way of serving a condiment.   Bailey's Range is a great place for a burger and a downtown lunch. Service can be slow, but patience is a virtue. Just kick back, relax and enjoy an amazing burger. Oh, don't forget to try the wings and chili, too.  I gave them a shout out in my first review and their excellence still stands true.   When: August 10, 2016 Why: Lunch - Ian Froeb's STL 100 & I needed to do an update

#curbside #togo #pandemic  Applause to, The Blue Duck for their well organized #curbside service during the #pandemic. The process was so easy. I placed my order on line, paid with a card, included my tip and drove over to Maplewood. Once I arrived, I called to let them know I was there and they brought my order out. They placed it on a table, I then picked it up and went home with a juicy delicious slam burger. There was no touching or contact. We were both gloved and living the life in a pandemic world.   In addition to my slam burger, I also had an order of Tortilla Chips (house made) with Queso. I got these to enjoy the next night during a virtual UYE Happy Hour. Of course, I had to sneak a few while they were warm and fresh. It was a challenge not to devour them all right away, they were that good. However, I'll let you know they were just as tasty the next night with a little warm up in the oven for the chips and the queso did a quick spin in the micro.   This weeks Slam Burger special had my name written all over it. I'm a sucker for Mexican food and I love a good juicy burger. It was called, the MoMex. They started it out with 8 ounces of house ground chuck with melted white cheddar. Then it was garnished with; bbq sauce, refried beans, house made chorizo, shredded iceberg, tomato, onion and my favorite food accessory, jalapeño. All that goodness could not be put in a regular hamburger bun, it had to have something special. It was all stacked inside a, Green Chili Brioche Bun. OMG! This burger prepared medium rare was kick-ass. This fat boy who has been dieting during this lockdown was in heaven. We all need to cheat once in awhile and being a bad boy this once was so worth it.   Thanks, Blue Duck for providing your amazing and delicious food curbside during the pandemic. It is making life so much more tolerable.   Will I return? - Can't wait for this lockdown to end so I can go inside.   When: April 22, 2020 Why: Curbside - Burger Fix

Gotta give a special shout out to Sara D. for reminding me to write my review about the deplorable service that I experienced at Mi Caribe. It is a shame as a Brand & Marketing Manager she hasn't learned the lesson of, "don't poke the bear". I've been poked, so I gotta speak up.   I'll be nice and start out with the only positive thing about the night I was at Mi Caribe. Since it took three hours to get my food that evening, I immediately had to have them put it in a to-go vessel to enjoy the next day. When I opened the container (non-eco friendly) with my Mango & Curry Chicken Wings, co-workers immediately asked me what I was eating and where I got them. Yes, the aroma was that strong and good being ice cold. Even cold, I enjoyed them. (Did I tell them of the horrible service - HELL, YES) These wings saved them from getting a 1 Star review.   My main entree was the Chuleta. This is a thick cut pork chop marinated dominican style, deep fried and topped with onions. The seasoning was good, but I was not impressed with the cut of the chop. It was tough and had excessive fat on it.   Now, I'll share with you the true reason for the low rating. The general manager on duty was a curmudgeon. He was rude and condescending. Our large group had made a reservation, so they totally knew we were coming and should have been prepared. Upon our arrival, Mr. Duval approached our table and gave us rules that we had to follow in our ordering. He wanted us to select from 5 or less entrees, to make it easy on his kitchen. Since he knew our group and another group of 12 were dining at the same time, perhaps he should of staffed his kitchen appropriately. Instead of putting the responsibility on his patrons.   When I asked him, if we were 4 tables of 4 that walked in behind each other, would he be making the same request. He replied, "that would never happen". I don't know about anyone else, but I've seen it happen at many restaurants and I eat almost every evening meal out. However, I guess it doesn't happen here, since our table, the other table of 12 and a couple other small tables were the only diners that evening. Not being busy, there should have been no excuse for the length of time our food took to come out of the kitchen.   The majority of this could have been avoided if they kept taking alcohol orders and got the appetizers out ahead of the entrees. Our group would have been content drinking and munching on our appetizers. Instead, we had to go to the bar to retrieve our additional drinks or order one from the curmudgeon and receive the wrong drink. My entree came out before my appetizer of chicken wings.   Rude service and disorganization will keep me from returning or recommending Mi Caribe. It's a shame that their Brad & Marketing Manager is an agitator instead of one who resolves negative experiences at their restaurant. This is one restaurant that truly is deserving of being on my Terrible Two's List.   When: August 2, 2016 Why: ISC

I'm a little late, but I want you to know how thrilled I am that you have finally arrived in South Hampton. I'm confident that this will become your most successful and popular location.   Today when I stopped by, I was amazed at how much more spacious it was then Lafayette. Not only spacious, but simply beautiful. There's plenty of tables for couples and families to sit and enjoy their nice or naughty ice cream.   Normally, I always go straight for the "naughty" case, but today I was feeling rather "nice" and changed things up. I did a double scoop in a traditional bowl of; Front Porch Mint and Salted Crack Caramel. It was the perfect treat after the burger special at The Mack.   Keith S. commented how you didn't have, "normal" flavors. For me, that is why I love you so much. Your flavors are unique and creative. You're not afraid to think outside of the carton and come up with some of the most amazing flavors that tickle the taste buds.   The service was delightful, the young ladies working were friendly and professional. In addition to my ice cream, I also added a couple of enamel pins to my collection. One was a cute ice cream cone and a set of "Nice" and "Naughty" pins. Those two are going to be great for holiday parties.   Clementine's, I love you, but you being so close to my home may be a problem for my for my sweet-tooth and waistline.   I'll be back? - Hell, yes.   When: July 26, 2019 Why: First Visit - love their ice cream

Just take me out and spank me now. What was I thinking when I ordered from Imo's. I know what I was thinking, I was hungry and desperate for delivery at work. Being new to the Alton office I wasn't sure who would deliver and all I could find was Imo's and Domino's. I had two evils to choose from, so I flipped a coin and Imo's won.   Amiee's talk thread about Toasted Ravioli got me kinda craving them, so I ordered some ravs and a 10" Deluxe pizza. Their deluxe has; sausage, mushroom, onion, green pepper, bacon & cheese. We all know which type of cheese, so I will not even go there.   If these were my first toasted rav's, they would have turned me off and I would have never tried them again. They were rubbery, chewy and several out of the 10 were burnt. The so called "meat sauce" that was included for dipping was oily and nasty. The one rav that I did dip was spat out quickly. I only ate four of them and tossed the remainder into the circular file cabinet.   The pizza was a major disappointment. I will be honest and say, I do like the thin crispy crust for my pizza and this was ultra thin and crispy. However, the toppings did not make the grade. The bacon was plentiful as were the onions. The green pepper was cut to large for me, combined with the sausage it left a stuffed pepper taste me my mouth. The mushrooms were kinda on the mushy side of being done. Again, we all know which cheese they use, but this was the most minimal cheese I have ever seen on a pizza.   When I ordered I did not expect greatness, but I did want at least average. What is sad, is my mom use to live in Godfrey and enjoyed going here for a personalized lunch pizza and a cold beer when I visited. She'd roll over in her grave knowing that this place in the last couple years has gone to hell.   Thank goodness I keep a toothbrush & paste at work, because my mouth was in need of a good cleaning after this lunch. Also, another good thing about this lunch, I got a new addition to my No-No List.

Super Bowl LI and I needed dinner. My intentions was to have a beer at the bar and order carry-out. When I arrived, it was later then I thought and the game was starting. I luckily got a spot at the bar directly in front of a TV.   I quickly ordered a Big Walt from a local craft brewery, O'Fallon. It was a refreshing Blonde Ale, so refreshing, I enjoyed two during the first half. My original plan was to order a House Salad with house dressing and Garlic Butter Wings to enjoy at home. However, once I had a primo seat at the bar, I ordered a Jalapeño Burger Fries.   The Jalapeño Burger is one of my favorites. They take fresh chopped jalapeños, stuff them into the beef burger before grilling and then top it with a soft jalapeño cheddar cheese. I get mine done medium rare and served with a side of crispy fries.   Service today was a little off, it was slow. However, I cut them some slack due to the fact that it was Super Bowl. The bartender was hustling keeping up all the drink orders for the tables and at times I had to wait longer then normal. After enjoying my beer & burger I headed home to enjoy the halftime show and second half in the privacy of my home.   Will I return? I always do. Love their burgers and Early Bird Dinners  When: February 5, 2017 Why: Super Bowl LI Dinner

GM+T will easily win every Best Fried Chicken poll for STL in the coming future. We've all loved Rick's chicken from other restaurants he has been chef, but this is by far the best he has created.   His creative ability to take a marinade + a dry rub to produce an extra crispy, juicy and flavorful chicken. To have a true comfort meal, I added some traditional Southern sides; slow cooked field peas, macaroni & cheese and cracklin cornbread.   The macaroni and cheese was made with white cheddar and Gouda. I would've never thought to put Gouda in a mac & cheese, but it made it so rich and creamy.   I could not resist dipping my cornbread that was made with pork renderings and topped with a caramelized honey glaze into the slow cooked field peas broth. Come binding the two was a treat within itself. Telling you that the peas are made with salt cured bacon, is enough. It is as if your southern grandmother prepared them for Sunday dinner.   I did start out with an appetizer, their fried green tomatoes. Fannie Flagg would be proud and jealous of these  delicious treats. I loved them and I do not like red tomatoes. I only eat fried green tomatoes.   The service is in true Southern hospitality style. Rick and his team know how to do it - they nailed it on opening day. I can't wait to return.   Will I return? - I gotta try the catfish  When: September 13, 2017 Why: opening day lunch

What a great little gift shop located on the heart of Main Street in Edwardsville. It is eclectic and full of unique and vintage gifts. It is a great place to shop for the person who has everything. The selection is so unusual and creative, your gift will be remembered and cherished forever.   This little shop was a pleasant discovery while we were having lunch at Cleveland-Heath. It is the type of store you'd expect to find on an antique row. It would fit in perfectly on Cherokee Street in St. Louis on in the historic downtown of St. Charles.   I'm not an early holiday shopper, but stopping by The August Garden (name is wrong on Yelp), I have already marked a couple people off my list.

Those who say the best Italian in STL is on, "The Hill" is totally wrong. This place in Clayton is amazingly delicious. It is tucked away at the  back-end of a small strip center just off Wydown. The small boutique size makes it intimate and almost romantic.   I meet up with fellow Yelper, Christal for lunch on the Tuesday after Labor Day. Our luncheon was 12:30pm, towards the end of their lunch rush. I arrived first and selected a table on their small patio. Being a dog dad, it was nice to see they had water bowls making the patio pet friendly.   We started out with some Cauliflower Hummus. In addition to the crostini, they offered a basket of soft Italian bread dabbed with garlic butter. This worked out great, because I preferred the crostini and Christal wanted the softer bread. I enjoyed the uniqueness of the cauliflower hummus. In addition to the hummus, the plate had a small spinach salad with pine nuts and balsamic dressing. It was a nice touch.   For my entree, I channeled my inner child and ordered a half order of spaghetti and meatball. I choose the chicken.The ground chicken was blended with breadcrumbs. It was moist and tender. Noodles were prepared to a perfect al dente. I don't think Italian food can really be classified as a comfort food, but this Southern Italian Southern food, brought me comfort this afternoon.   No booze for me, I enjoyed a tall refreshing glass of ice tea. Christal was having a rough day at work and enjoyed a glass of red wine. I found it odd that it was not served in a traditional wine glass. It was served in a small juice/water glass. I thought it was perhaps because we were on the patio.  Then the table next to us ordered a bottle and did have a traditional steamed glass. Just weird.   Our server was professional and very knowledgeable. He described their food and recommended wines for Christal like a true pro.   Will I return? - Most definitely.   When: September 5, 2017 Why: Italian lunch with a friend

SugarFire, since you made my Memorial Day rock, I came back to see if you could do it for my Labor Day. Again, you made my three day holiday special. Why anyone would stand outside in the unbearable heat to grill their own meat is beyond me. It was so much easier placing our order, having a variety of meats and sides and relaxing. After all, isn't that what holidays are about just relaxing.   This Labor Day we each enjoyed Two Meat Plates with two sides. As always we had to get your Brisket, which I still claim is the best of BBQ joints in the city. The BF for his second meat enjoyed 4 Ribs. They are so much better then Pappy's. My second meat was Smoked Turkey, it was the first time and it was so juicy and tender. Can I place my order for Thanksgiving with you now?   We both enjoyed an order of the Schafley Beer Baked Beans with Burnt Ends. Neither of us ate our entire order, which made great take home for later. We also had the Mustard Potato Salad, which is always a picnic type holiday classic. I ordered the Fries, because I have never had them and I wanted to see what all the hype was about. I remembered on Facebook you talked about getting a crinkle cut machine and everyone was saying, no that they liked them just they way they are. Your fries are the first thing that has not impressed me. They were OK, but your other sides are so much more unique and flavorful.   As our beverages we enjoyed your Watermelon Sangria which was perfectly refreshing. Can I have the recipe? I'm asking for a lot aren't I.   The other day I thought I had found the best pastrami in Saint Louis, but that was before I had yours. I've always thought Bogart's was great and last week The Shack impressed me, but neither of them have the flavor, tenderness and juiciness of yours. Before leaving we got an order of your Pastrami and two slices of Pecan pie to enjoy with our leftover baked beans for dinner later that day. All we had to add was some homegrown corn on the cob and we had another great meal.    As always, your staff was friendly and professional on a busy holiday. They know how to hustle.

Spencer's Grill is a rock solid diner. It is classic is all sense of the word. I stopped by this morning to join in the 70th Anniversary celebration. To celebrate 70 years as diner, shows you how good it is. The food is consistently top notch, breakfast or lunch.   They are known for their Crispy Pancakes and I normally order them when ordering breakfast. However, today I went with a #8; Biscuits & Gravy with two eggs and a side of meat. I had my eggs scrambled and choose bacon as my meat. The farm boy inside of me, made me order it.   The gravy was thick, full of sausage and draped over the fluffy biscuit with extra gravy to spare. Surprisingly I needed to add to salt, which is a good thing for those who do not like over salty foods. My scrambled eggs were blended well, making for a soft yellow presentation. The bacon, was crisp, no limp wimpy bacon here. The coffee was black and the cup was kept full. My breakfast was very filling, but I wish I would have ordered a side of Hash Browns. I would have been over-stuffed, but they serve the best HB's.   As always, the staff is friendly and they keep the diner running smooth and fast.  Breakfast or lunch, give Spencer's a try.   Will I return? I always do.   When: October 24, 2017 Why: 70th Anniversary Celebration

In all fairness, I thought I needed to give Vida a second chance. I have a friend who is leaving STL for a new job in Rochester, NY and we wanted to meet for a final lunch. With The Galleria being the midpoint for both of us, I thought I'd give them a second chance. So glad that I did, now I get to raise their score to two stars. Our waitress was so cute and perky, I just couldn't help myself from going out on a limb and giving the extra star.   Being a Margarita lover, I know they are high in calories so I was excited when I saw that they offered a "skinny" Margarita. I would like nothing more then a good Margarita with a reduced amount of calories and my search will continue. The one Vida offers basically tasted like a watered down regular margarita. There truly was nothing special about it and it cost $2 more then a regular Margarita.   Vida does offer a lunch special offered between 11 AM and 3 PM for $8.99.  You get to choose two from: salads, soups, tacos, enchiladas, quesadillas, taquitos and tostadas. We both took advantage of this savings and our "twos" were served with rice topped with black beans. The rice was extremely dry, but I did enjoy the black beans. They defiantly had better flavor then a can of Bush's.   My friend is a chicken man, so for his two he ordered a taco and quesadilla. He enjoyed the taco, but left the majority of the quesadilla on his plate. I had a Fish Taco and Spinach & Mushroom Enchilada. The fish was hand battered, but a little  greasy on the inside. My enchilada was a disappointment, both the mushrooms and tortilla were chewy and rubbery.   Our waitress was friendly and attentive. I liked how she presented the chips and salsa. When she brought them to the table she said, "Here are your complimentary chips and salsa."  We've all eaten at enough Mexican Restaurants to know, the chips and salsa are usually "free", but the verbal delivery made us feel special.   The manager doing table touches around us kept looking at our table, but not once did he approach us. I guess we did not meet his demographics.   I'll continue to satisfy my Mexican cravings at Milagro. Vida is pretending to be a high end Casa Gallardo.

Yes it is a chain, but I like their crust and sauce so I will let Pappa in my house.   I've recently gotten burned out on my hometown pizza delivery joints and have started to revisit the national chains. Papa was the first and he delivered us a good pie. I hop on-line, built our own pizza with Spicy Sausage, Onion, Green Pepper and Baby Portabella Mushrooms. I then entered my payment information and clicked the final button. Thirty minuets later, we had a flavorful pizza at our door.   I use to be a BIG fan of thin crust pizza, but I am slowly leaning and appreciating a thicker pie crust. Imo's may claim that their toppings extend to the edge of the pizza, but I love Papa's crust and the Garlic Dipping Sauce they include with your pizza. Yummy.   Papa and I may not see eye to eye on politics, but we are eye to eye on his pizza.

It is a gas station, nothing more nothing less. However, it has saved my ass  many times when my gas gage has been down to one bar and I'm scared I wont make it much further. This scenario happens more then I'd like to admit. It is easily accessible from Interstate 44. You can get off, fill up and get back on the road with ease. The prices are relatively competitive, considering the prime location. You'd think they'd be  higher considering the convenience.  As others have commented, the convenience market is extremely small. It is about the size the of a shipping container. It may be small and compact, but they make good use of every available inch for merchandising. Unfortunately when I have gone in to shop, I've walked out empty handed. Due the the smallness, the variety of products is limited.   I'm a pay at the pump customer, so I've only gone inside to interact with the staff a few times. However I must say, the automated gas pumps always thanks me for shopping.

Had to increase my stars from three to four today.   We stopped by today to get some of their house made Salsiccia sausage for pasta - it is fantastic.   The customer service here is always friendly and outstanding. They were smoking ribs in the parking lot today and they smelled like heaven. I'm sure it attracts many customers. Come on spring, I'm ready to start grilling regularly again.

"You're going to like the way you look" may no longer be their catch phrase, but I liked the way I looked at an Old Hollywood party I attended for Yelp and it was all thanks to the staff at Men's Wearhouse and Tux.   I stopped by about a week ahead of the special event, to see what styles were available. The tux specialist was very knowledgable in sizing and what would be appropriate for my Hollywood party. I was up front with my associate, telling her this was just a fun party and I wanted to go lower-end, but still look good. She totally understood and fixed me up in a fashionable Calvin Klein. When it came time to pick my accessories, I told her they had to be orange. After all, orange is the new black and it is my favorite color. The orange vest and tie, made the tux scream me.   If you need a tuxedo for a special event or a wedding, I highly recommend MWAT. They are way better then Savvi Formalwear in the Loop. When you shop here, ask for Jasmine, she is an amazing.

Thanks Sugarfire Smoke House for making my Memorial Day lunch a success. The 10 oz Brisket Sandwich was a true classic and your Brisket Cheesesteak put all Philly Cheesesteaks to shame. Philadelphia should be scared.   We shared four sides; Potato Salad, Baked Beans, Creamy Cole Slaw and Pasta Salad. The portions were so huge, we took most of them home to enjoy with the Brats we grilled at home that evening. However, we ate every bite of our sandwiches. I truly love your cole slaw and baked beans. I'd love the recipe for both, but know I'll never get them.   No matter how busy and slammed you are, your staff is always friendly. They  take the time to make sure all diners are greeted appropriately and make small talk as place your order. I always feel welcomed, which in addition to the great food is why I keep coming back for more. Give me some Sugarfire!

I came with the good intentions of ordering their famous, Steak Sandwich on Garlic Cheese Bread with a side of fries. As I sat at a high top table in the bar, enjoying a O'Fallon Brewery IPA, my server told me the nightly special. I immediately was persuaded to order it.  The nightly special was Prime Rib. I'm sure you can now see why I was so easily persuaded.  I enjoyed a house salad with their famous and unique White French dressing, a side of asparagus and a nice slab cut of Prime Rib. That's a lot of food for $19.95. If you've never had their White French dressing, I highly recommend that you do.   My piece of prime rib was prepared medium rare and served with a side of creamy horseradish. For the price point, I was pleased with my selection. Instead of a tradition baked potato, they offered asparagus. I couldn't say no, to one of my favorite vegetables. However, their asparagus was thick and not pencil thin as I prefer. It was so thick it could have been prepared a little longer to make it more tender.   Biggies is a good neighborhood bar providing great service and pub grub.   Would I return? Yes, I can walk here, it's in my hood.   When: December 27, 2016 Why: Dinner

We had a BOGO coupon and went to City Diner today for lunch. Once again, CD surprised the hell out of me. I use to only do breakfast here, then I had a great dinner and now I had a fantastic lunch.   Following the burger talk thread, I was inspired to try a burger from a diner and see how they fare. It was simple burger with no thrills, except a slice of melted Swiss on top and on a toasted sesame seed bun. Served with a pickle spear, rings of red onion, lettuce (not Iceberg) and tomato.   My burger was cooked to order, perfectly seared on each side with a pink tint to the inside. It was juicy, seasoned well and the cheese melted perfectly over the top. Their burgers are a 1/2 lb. that fills a normal bun well. I am not a fan of iceberg lettuce, so I was pleased to see that is not what they serve to compliment the burger.   My friend had a Classic Ruben, which was served on a Marbleized Rye and was huge. He gave it a thumbs up and we both loved our crispy fries that were served with our sandwiches. They truly were crisp, no wimpy limp fries at this diner.   Our service was excellent. Diner servers are so much fun, you can joke and banter with them so much easier then other restaurants.   I now know City Diner is good for; breakfast, lunch and dinner. I guess the next thing I need to experience is the late night, post bar scene.

What a deal, buy 8" and get another 8" free. I found a Entertainment Coupon that was a Buy One - Get One Free and that is a deal you just can not pass up.  We ordered a Italian and a Chicken Parmesan. Once home, we cut the 8" in half so we each got to experience both. Tonight the Chicken Parmesan was the winner. A chicken breast and pizza sauce with other garnishes, make for a tasty sandwich.   Their fries are some of the best in fast food. Big Idaho potatoes, freshly cut with skins left on and deep fried to a crispy treat. A large order is sufficient enough for two to share. To wash it all down, a gallon of their fresh squeezed is the perfect beverage. Normally, I love Penn Stations lemonade, but this time it was way too sweet. I'll forgive them this time.   Staff is always friendly and you can watch them make your order. While you are waiting be sure to sign up their e-mail alerts, you'll get special discount announcements.

Friar Tuck came to my rescue. I was on a search for a particular Bloody Mary mix and they had it. When I recently went to Washington, MO for a day trip I discovered, Tony's Sweet Heat Bloody Mary Mix. I wanted to add it to a gift box I was creating for someone and really wanted to avoid having to make the trip back to Wash MO to buy another bottle.   Oh, did I mention Tony's is a local brand? It is, it is......Fenton, MO.   I visited Tony's website and found out who carried it locally. I tried to buy it from small local shops, but they were all out (tells me how good it is), so I had to buy it from a BIG chain. However, I will say the price was $2 lower then what I paid in Washington, MO. Also, I was surprised by the attentiveness and friendliness of sales associates assisting on the floor.  The cashier was even a pleasant asset to the store.   Will I return? - They rescued me once, I bet they do it again.   When: December 13, 2017 Why: On a Mission

Off the beaten or should I say eaten path, but a good find. It is hidden on a side street in Overland in an old Taco Bell building. If it weren't for Ian Froeb's putting Chef Ma in his Top 100 restaurants in STL for 2016, I would have never discovered this amazing little Cantonese restaurant. Chef Ma has won an Iron Chef competition back in 2009. It's not the Iron Chef that we all know from watching the Food Network, but it was similar and still something to brag about.   When I arrived, I got in line behind two blue collar workers ordering carry-out for themselves and several co-workers. After they were finished, I went to place my order. They had ordered cokes and got them out of a case bottled. I saw a fountain machine and told the gentleman taking my order that I'd prefer my diet coke to be fountain. He then asked me if was dining in and when I replied, yes. He told me to sit down and he'd wait on me. So heads up, if you want carry-out order at the counter and if you're eating in, take a seat for table service.   Ian Froeb and several others recommend ordering the Hainan Chicken Rice. However, their description made my tummy do flips. Room temperature and slippery skin did not sell  it for me. However, the table next to me was braver and ordered it - now that I have actually seen it, next time I'll be brave enough to give it a try.   I went safe on this visit and enjoyed the Beef Short Ribs. The beef was tender and the vegetables were done perfectly. The veggies had enough crunch and yet soft enough to enjoy. Dieting, I didn't eat that much of the white rice, but it was fluffy and did not stick together in clumps.   Their menu also offers Americanized fare and traditional Chinese fare. As Ian said in his article, you go for the authentic.   The service is friendly and quick. Nothing fancy, but the food is damn good and plentiful.   I'll be back and I'll be brave enough to try that room temperature, slippery skinned chicken.   When: September 26, 2016 Why: Lunch & Ian Froeb's STL 100

Need a fast breakfast? Go to Bread Co., it is far better then a sausage  biscuit from a fast food place.  The breakfast sandwiches are totally awesome, as are the small quiches.  We can never make up our minds so we share several items to get a taste of our favorites. We'll share a sandwich, quiche and a scone (for something sweet).   The customer service here is down home friendly. I'd highly recommend this be the location used for training the staffs of other STL Bread Co's.  My only negative of this location is that they are putting in a drive-up window.  I know it's weird, but I just don't like drive-up windows. I prefer to park, go inside and experience true customer service in person and not through a speaker box and window.

Larder and Cupboard is another great addition to the constantly growing Maplewood community. I knew I was going to shop local this upcoming holiday, but I can now tell you the majority of my gifts will be from Larder and Cupboard. There are so many items that will be perfect for the foodie and boozer on my gift list.   My family and friends who enjoy the alcohol beverage, may be getting a gift box of bitters or a kit to create a kick ass Bloody Mary. Others may get a gift basket created with the large variety of different honey jars. My personal favorite has to be the Hot Honey, a perfect topping on cornbread or a biscuit. I can even create a condiment basket with gourmet catsup, Soy Sauce, Worcestershire Sauce and variety of mustards.   The staff is friendly and eager to assist you. As they increase their inventory, I am confident that I'll be filling my own personal kitchen cabinets and creating several gift baskets.

I normally do not like to wait for a table, so I was scared to visit H&H with all the comments about the long waits. I will tell you now, that my wait wasn't that bad and it was well worth it.  I already know that I will be back to visit on a weekday.   If it's Sunday Brunch, you gotta have a Bloody Mary and theirs is pretty awesome. What makes their Bloody Mary unique and special is the garnish. They garnish with a fried dill pickle. You don't just give a thick slice, you get an entire spear to enjoy.
