The mix it self is spicy enough and the pour of vodka is generous.   We started our brunch with Cornbread topped with Blueberry Butter and drizzled with honey.  The BB Butter was a flavorful addition to the cornbread which was served a room temperature. It would have been so much better if it were served warm, so the butter could melt into the bread. Also, it would have been easier to wipe up the drizzled honey.   Both of our entrees were impressive, I had the Bavarian Ham Benedict ($16), but I'd say Brad's Steak-N-Eggs ($13) was the best of the two. He had his steak prepared rare and they accommodated his request for poached eggs instead of the sunny side up offered on the menu. The steak was fork tender and juicy. It was pre-cut in to bite size pieces, topped with Tabasco Onions and then topped again with a Hollandaise Sauce. Potatoes were served on the side and they were crispy on the outside and oh so tender on the inside.   My Bavarian Ham Benedict, was a good twist on the traditional Eggs Benedict. What perplexed me, was how Bavarian ham could be $3 more then steak. I think they need to flip the prices on these two offerings. Any way, my poached eggs were done perfectly and like the steak my BH was  fork tender. I was able, to slice through egg, ham and muffin with no knife at all. The hollandaise sauce had a good flavor, but was runny. I like my HS to be thicker, so it clings to the food.   Any one who knows me, knows I am a true Brunch-A-Holic (name given to me by Allison) and I enjoy experiencing as much as I can when brunching. However, our server did not know that, nor did he care too. We had only taken two bites of our food and he was already giving us our check. As he put it on the table, he told we could pay the cashier when ready and he kept moving. We were both stunned and I looked at Brad and said, "oh, no he didn't. I'm not done."    Brad was able to get his attention and he returned to take our additional order. I'm at Brunch, at Brunch I have both a Bloody Mary and a Mimosa. That way I full-fill two of my daily fruit requirements. Their Mimosa was bloody good, again they were generous with the booze pour. $ alert, both the Bloody Mary and Mimosa are $8 each.   When we first walked in, we commented on how it reminded us of an Apple Store. The ambiance was stark, crisp and clean with all the servers/staff in the same blue T-shirts. However, the servers do not match the caliber of service you get at the Apple store. In fact it is cold, it is to obvious that they are wanting to turn the tables and rush you out the door. When I am spending $65 for breakfast for 2 do not rush me, let me enjoy it to the fullest.   I still believe they deserve the 4 Stars on the food alone. I will not let the lack of service from our server to lessen their star rating. We had a nice chat with a manager in a positive tone and he understood and addressed our comments. Before leaving, our server came to us and apologized. Takes a big person to say those words, "I'm sorry".  As I said earlier, "I will be back."

Andre's Ribs do their ribs "Julie's Way". I don't know who Julie is, but she knows how to do ribs. The meat is so tender, it actually falls off the bone. I've never been able to clean a rib this clean before. Andre's is a tiny little space located on S. Kingshighway next to Eddie's Donuts. The space may be small and compact, but the flavor in their ribs and brisket is huge.   The dry rub on the baby back ribs is amazing. It is so flavorful it can stand on its own. It is so good you will not need sauce, but do try it especially the hot. They only offer two house made sauces, mild and hot. Do not be turned away from the word, hot. It is not that hot, it just gives you enough kick to add pizazz to the ribs.   I've said in previous reviews about other BBQ places that I judge the tenderness of brisket by being able to break off a bite size piece with a plastic fork. Here at Andre's all it took was a poke with my finger. It was so tender it melted in my mouth.   They only offer four sides at Andre's; Eugenie's Homemade Potato Salad, Pete's Homemade Baked Beans, Cole Slaw and Green Beans. We only sampled three of the four, missing out on the green beans. Eugenie's Potato Salad was very unique, my guess it was a combination of mayo and a brown mustard. Pete's Baked Beans were seasoned well and the cole slaw was creamy which is always a plus for my personal taste.   The staff is small and extremely friendly. When I asked questions about Turkey Ribs, they explained and even showed me what they looked like. They truly made us feel welcomed and were excited to find out how we discovered them. Yes, I did drop the Yelp bomb. We'll be returning to enjoy a full rack of ribs and an order of Turkey Ribs as well.

I live in the city and drive all the way out to West County to visit this vet. That in itself, should tell you this is an incredible vet. The entire staff is professional and very caring. I have three Shelties and they have a true understanding of the breed, so I know they are getting the best care possible.  A vet that provides good TLC.

You know what burns my butt besides a flame that is 30" high? A very well kept secret. I always knew that City Diner was good for breakfast, but no one shared with me the fact that their dinner is pretty damn good too. Who knew?  We  both had a stressful day at work and wanted some good ole fashion comfort food to make our day better. We bantered several other places around until I remembered that I had a BOGO coupon for CD. For you frivolous diners, a BOGO is buy one get one. That means, a free meal of equal or less in price. That alone can make a stressful day better.   Let's be honest, parking on Grand is a bitch. However, we lucked out and got the next thing closest to princess parking. Our day just keeps getting better. Once inside we were greeted and seated by a just okay hostess, but once our waitress arrived on the scene it was a fun night. She was cute, perky and full of ideas of what to eat. I like it when a server knows their product, and can sell the sizzle with the steak.   For his dinner, Brad did not stray far from his usual breakfast of Country Fried Steak. Instead of hash browns he had mashed potatoes and in place of eggs he enjoyed corn. We both were impressed with the corn. It was actually cut fresh from a cob of corn, no can. For a diner that is damn impressive.  Our perky server guided me to the Meat Loaf Dinner and boy did she know me. It was perfect. When I ordered green beans as my vegetable, she alerted me that it was made with bacon and onions. I replied, "as they should be". She giggled and said she agrees with me, but some folks freak out when they see it served that way. I can't imagine who, because they were almost as good as my Grandma's and she was one hell of a good cook.   My Meat Loaf was smothered in brown gravy as were my mashed potatoes. The potatoes were manly potatoes. They were not over whipped, they thick and hearty. The type you'd see served to lumberjacks or farmhands. Again, it was obvious they were made from scratch.  The portions were huge,  but some how I still managed to clean my plate. As I moaned in disbelief that I accomplished such a feat, our perky little waitress showed us her "evil twin". She had the nerve to come up and start telling us about all the fabulous desserts. I thought she'd never shut-up, she just keep going & going and each one sounded tempting. However, she had me with the first one she said, "Red Velvet Cake Cheesecake". How do you say no to two of you favorite desserts combined into one? Either do I, so I took Brad's advice and got it to go. Brad also got one to go, he selected the White Chocolate Raspberry Cheesecake.  When we enjoyed them later that evening, both were heavenly. How could a layer or red velvet cake, cheesecake, red velvet and cheesecake again be bad? It can't. The White Chocolate Cheesecake Raspberry was the best of the two, but the RVC was still outstanding.  Moral of the story: You really don't save with a BOGO coupon, because you get two dessert as  carryout.

It isn't what it use to be.  I remember when the food and service here was fantastic and breakfast was a treat. Today, the best thing we had was the Bloody Mary Bar and we made those ourselves. The pour of vodka was generous.   We started out with the Irish Salmon with bagel. The salmon was good, the bagel was tough and chewy, the tomato a typical out of season tomato and the red onion was rather woody.   I had the Hickory Smoked Ham & Pepper Cheese Omelet. The coloring and folding was close to picture perfect. When sliced into, is when it got disappointing. The inside was runny (the egg, not melted cheese) and the ham was ice cold. The side of hash browns were seasoned okay, but again they were cold. Either they don't have a heat lamp, or they had the potatoes made way in advance.   My partner had the Eggs Madison, the portion of salmon was generous and the eggs were done well. The big disappointment was the hollandaise sauce. It was not made from scratch which you'd expect for the price they charged. It tasted and looked like Knoor's  powdered mix. Loving bacon, he also had a side as an extra treat. When they sat it down on table, I thought it looked like over processed beef jerky soaked in grease.   The service was poor at best, the young girl serving us was very scatter brained and gave off the vibe that she'd rather be somewhere else. The guys serving around our table were more attentive then she was.   Perhaps my expectations were too high, but when breakfast cost $55 I just want more bang for my buck.   The highlight of the breakfast was running into a friend who retired from Louis Vuitton.

This is not my typical Steak 'n Shake, I'm usually a Hampton location boy. However, this morning we thought we'd change it up. It wasn't bad, but I think I need to stay with my regular location up on Hampton.   Our server was friendly and attentive. We were fairly early and as the restaurant filled up you could see the community camaraderie. So many of the diners all knew each other and our server would greet them by name. Even with this being our first visit, we still received the same quality of service as her regulars.   The grill-man did a great job on preparing our eggs over easy and making our Hash Browns extra crispy. I always request crispy HB's, my taste-buds just like them better. The SO's side of pancakes were evenly golden in color and his patty sausage were Jimmy Dean good.   I have mixed feelings on two of my sides. My bacon appeared to have been fried in advance and waiting for an order. It was chilled and chewy. The biscuit was dry, but when combined with the thick sausage milk crazy it was enjoyable. However, if it were a moist flaky biscuit, it would get two thumbs up from this pudgy ex-farm boy.   Overall, a good visit for a inexpensive breakfast.

Wow! WTF, happened. I was so hoping to be able to bump them up to a 5 Star rating on my recent visit and instead, I gotta take them down a notch. Luckily I had been here before, so I am only taking them down to3 Stars. If my recent visit had been my first, it definitely would have been a strong 2 Star rating.   Have they gotten overly cocky, having been selected as one of Ian Froeb's STL 100 and winning Best BBQ 2016 from the RFT. Winning these two titles, you'd think they'd keep their A-Game going, but instead, they have gotten sloppy all around. Both food and service had declined from my last visit.   My recent visit I ordered the 1/4 slab & 1/4 Meat Combo with two sides. I choose the brisket as my meat and it was tender and flavorful. I enjoyed the Texas Chainsaw sauce on mine, it has the extra kick. The 1/4 slab was an embarrassment. It had way to much gristle, was greasy, overly charred and to be honest - flavorless. Even adding my favorite sauce, couldn't save these ribs.   As my sides, I selected Sprouts with Belly and Fresh-Cut Fries. The sprouts here are 5 Stars on their own, I love'm and with belly - they totally steal my heart. Their fresh-cut fries disappointed me. They were limp, cold and tasted as if they had been fried in old oil. Not one of them had a crisp coating, they were all mushy. Also, the tortillas were on the tough and chewy side today.   The portions here are plentiful, they are not stingy with portions. So as I was ready to leave, I requested a to-go vessel. When a styrofoam container (not eco-friendly) was presented to me, I was informed that they are always at the end of the counter. When I glanced to the end to see them, I was informed that next time I could get it myself. Okay, with her tone and attitude, I did not leave with a warm and fuzzy feeling about their service.   I loved this place on my first visit and hope to return. I just hope that my recent visit was just an off day. Or that they get over their big head and refocus on doing the quality job that they were doing earlier.   When: September 7, 2016 Why: Lunch in Belleville

I've heard the saying, "Don't judge a book by its' cover" and found it to be true. I read many a good books that have had boring covers. I have now learned not to judge a pizza place by its' store front.   I've driven by Epic Pizza many times on my way to various other eateries in Soulard and have thought to myself, what a hole in the wall, their pizza can't be any good. Lucky for me I finally looked them up here on Yelp and was amazed at the high ratings from people I trust. So the other night when we were crazing pizza and a new experience we headed over to EPAS.   Beware that on Monday they do not open until 5 PM, the hours currently posted here on Yelp are incorrect. We arrived before the their scheduled opening, but that is not a problem when ITAP is right next door. It was a good thing, that we did arrive early because talking to the ITAP bartender, she informed us that EPAS will deliver our food to us if we choose to eat on their patio. Trust me, this is a win.   We went back to Epic and ordered chicken wings and their 16" Epic Pizza. We had to go with the Epic, because it has all my favorite toppings; sausage, pepperoni,bacon, mushroom, onion and green pepper.  It was cut into pie slices and we had two left over for breakfast the next. The toppings were plentiful and I always love a wood fired pizza.   The only disadvantage of having them bring our food over to ITAP, was they delivered the wings and pizza at the same time. We would have enjoyed having the Wood Fired Wings served first. When ordering the wings I did not notice that they too are wood fired, which gave them extra flavor. They definitely earned a place on my Wings List.   Staff is friendly and goes beyond customer service by delivering your next door.   Lesson learned: Don't judge a pizza joint by its' exterior. You may be missing the best slice of your life.

Understand this review is based on a carry-out order.   I stopped by Four Muddy Paws yesterday to pick up food for my fur-babies, and found a new place for a lunch. No, not Four Muddy Paws, Square One Brewery which is just down the street.   I checked to see if they did carry-out and then persuaded my co-workers to change things up and order from somewhere new. We'll be ordering again soon...  Here's how they earned their stars:  1. Friendly Service 2. Eco-Friendly carry-out containers 3. Take-out ready when promised 4. Great Food! We loved the Beer Battered Onion Rings, Ruben and the Chicken Jerk Sandwich.  This was carry-out done well!!

SINFULLY SCRUMPTIOUS!  After filling our bellies for lunch at Mission Taco Joint, we still couldn't resist walking down Delmar to Piccione and getting a box of sweet treats to take home. We were tempted to fill a large box, but we remained strong and only chose four items and we shared them once we got home.   We filled our box with the following:  Piccione Signature Cannoli - a lighter twist on the traditional Sfoliatella Riccia - Flaky layered pastry with a creamy orange ricotta filling Rum Baba - Rum soaked yeast cake served with or without Piccione cream  Ricotta Cheesecake - A light & fluffy take on this yummy treat  Once we got home we could not wait, we had to try at least one of these decadent treats. We choose the Cannoli and the cream filling had my taste buds dancing a happy gig. The shell was flaky and the cream filling was oh so sweet. This is definitely the best Cannoli I have ever had.   We cooked at home that night and for dessert we enjoyed the cheesecake with fresh strawberries that have been macerated. I served the strawberries, on the side so we could taste the cheesecake without a distraction. I will say, this is the best cheesecake in the city. I've had the factory, daddy's and Hank's and I am here to say this is by far head and shoulders above all three of them. We both gasped and said, "Oh, my God" as we took our first bites. The strawberries were a treat on the side. We both enjoyed our cake plain.   The Sfoliatella Riccia was perfect the next morning with coffee. I can not remember when we ate the Rum Baba, but I do remember that I was pissed off that I had to share it and did not get to eat the whole thing.   Now that I have been to Piccione Pastry, I will change my eating habits when dining in The Loop. I will be sure to always leave room for a sweet treat from PP.

Sooner or later I will try something else on their menu, but for now I am satisfied with ordering their Chicken and Waffles every time.  As stated in a previous review, I try to order something different every time, but when the waitress ask me what I want, "Chicken and Waffles, all white meat, please", comes out of my mouth.  I always enjoy the hash browns, eggs, 1/2 waffle and chicken wing. The breast, which is always huge I take home to enjoy for lunch later in the day. I wish after GGD closes at 2pm, that they'd re-open at 5pm and serve this amazing fried chicken for dinner, but I am happy to thrilled to enjoy it as my breakfast meat.   The service here is always classic diner, friendly. Marica my most recent server, was a true jewel. Everything here is always pristine. The bus boys' white shirt even pressed and more crisply starched then a county courthouse lawyer.   I know I keep repeating myself, but Goody Goody Diner serves up the BEST Chicken and Waffles. If you haven't experienced it, I highly recommend you go today or tomorrow morning. Don't be scared on the neighborhood, it is totally safe and it is all part of the charm.

Goody Goody Diner is what all other diners strive to be. We heard the buzz of the Chicken and Waffles, and we just had to experience for ourselves. This weekend with a out-of-town guest, it was the perfect time. We arrived at 8 AM., and within an hour all tables were filled and the diner was bustling.  My other half and friend had the Chicken and Waffles Supreme which came with two eggs and grits. I got a smaller version; 4 wings and a half waffle with a side of Hash Browns with grilled onions.  Once our food was delivered our table fell silent, the food was so good there was no need for good conversation.  We all agreed the fried chicken was some of the best we'd experienced and the waffles in my opinion are better then some I have had at high end Sunday Brunches.  The grits received two thumbs up and my hash browns were good, but they weren't true hash browns they were more American Fries.  Staff was friendly and chivalry is not dead at Goody Goody. When food was ready, one of the men would carry out the large tray of food for the ladies to serve - good team work.

I am not a fan of Subway, but I am a fan of Potbelly. They know how to make a fresh sandwich fast and with friendly customer service.  We were running errands in Creve Coeur and just wanted a quick lunch. What can be quicker then 8 minutes? Potbelly promotes that you'll be through their line in 8 minutes max. I have no idea what happens if it does take longer. With the speed they move, I don't think it would ever happen.   We enjoyed an Italian and the Wreck, both were very enjoyable. What sets Potbelly above their competitors is the ratio of ingredients to bread. The sandwiches here are not overpowered by bread like they are at Subway. The ingredients are the true star.    I wish we had a Potbelly in city, but I'm glad we don't. If I had one closer to my house, I'd have a Potbelly from eating so much Potbelly. What would make Potbelly a 5 Star is if they had fries like Penn Station. Now that would be an awesome fast lunch.

I love me some pastrami. I love it so much, that I have a list dedicated to it here on Yelp. In my opinion, Bogart's has some of the best in STL. It's ranking on Ian Froeb's STL 100 at 23 is well deserved and I of course agree with his "must order" recommendation; Pastrami.   My favorite thing to order is the pick-two plate and one of the meats is always......wait for it.....Pastrami. I mix it up for the second meat with burnt ends and brisket being my other two favorites. Occasionally I'll just go for a half rack of ribs which are fall off the bone delicious as well.   As I've stated in my previous review, I would pay good money for their baked bean recipe. I truly love the smokey flavor. Another of their sides that I'm a big fan of is the cole slaw. I like how finely chopped it is and the sweet creamy sauce that coats it. As a child I use to love the cole slaw from KFC. Now as an adult, I look back and laugh at what I use to like. I'm so glad my tastebuds have grown-up.   I work downtown, so stopping by Bogarts when I get off at 3PM makes for an easy dinner. At times, I may not get what I truly wanted due to them being sold out, but I can roll with it. Why get upset and disappointed when there are so many delectable choices on their menu. I just always check the wipe board to the right of the cash stand to see what is not available and alter my plans accordingly.   Great service, great BBQ and unbelievable pastrami.   When: March 31, 2016 & April 22, 2016 Why: Pastrami and STL 100

New and improved. Heritage Veterinary Hospital has moved across the street to a fabulous new location. They have built a state of the art facility to match the excellent service they provide to canines and felines.  To make sure my previous review from their original location transfers over, I am going to cheat with a cut & paste:    I live in the city and drive all the way out to West County to visit this vet. That in itself, should tell you this is an incredible vet. The entire staff is professional and very caring. I have three Shelties and they have a true understanding of the breed, so I know they are getting the best care possible.  A vet that provides good TLC.

If you have taken the Yelp pledge to Shop Local this holiday season this is a store you must visit. The majority of the people on my gift list are one of two things. They are either female or big entertainers and this store has it all for both.  I was able to mark 4 off my "nice" list shopping here. They have a small, but good selection of wine that offered a good starting point to create goodie gift bags. In addition they have unique holiday serving dishes that were perfect host/hostess gifts for those who are always entertaining friends and family. The cocktail napkins had me laughing out loud and I found many that fit the personality of a couple "naughty" list friends.   We live in STL, so Fleur de Lis themed gifts are always good and you'll find plenty of them here. I keep saying, if I ever get a tattoo it would be a Fleur de Lis. Now I just need to decide where to put it.   Vera Bradley is a big thing for some ladies and TP has a small but impressive variety. If you have someone on your list who is a VB fan, I'd recommend buying it here to support a local business.  Shopping local will keep you out of the mall.   Cathy the owner was working the day we were shopping and she was witty, charming and made our shopping experience fun. She was full of ideas and we found ourselves still visiting after we had completed our purchase.   I'm glad I shopped local here and when I need gifts in the future, The Porch will be one of my first stops.

Fred M., my newest Yelp friend turned me on to a very well kept secret here in St. Louis. The BBQ Ribs at Biggie's are FABULOUS and only available on Saturday night.   I've been determined to go ever since Fred made the announcement in his review and last night I finally made it. I arrived just before seven and a good thing I did. They were almost sold out already. The waitress informed me that the Ribs are so popular that they sell out early in the evening. 7 is early? I guess those rib lovers come "real" early to get these hearty ribs.   My waitress was a true jewel, she was very accommodating. I ordered a full slab of ribs with the intention of eating half myself and taking the other home for Brad when he got off work. I mentioned this to her while ordering and to make things easier, she held half a slab back in the kitchen until I was ready to go. That is good service. It was provided without me even requesting it.   The Ribs are huge, meaty, tender, moist, fall off the bone good. I have not seen bones come cleaner at any other rib joint. I guess you'd say they are done KC Style, because the ribs are basted and served with the BBQ sauce already on them. In this case that is fine by me, because the flavor was astounding.   I enjoyed a Dinner Salad with Sweet & Sour Dressing which I liked more then the White French I had on my first visit and a Baked Potato. What is it about Baked Potatoes, they always seem to taste better out then the ones you make yourself at home. I guess food always taste better when someone else is doing the cooking.   Can't wait for this week to get over. I'm getting another full slab as carryout next Saturday.

Spencer's Grill has won my heart and is now my go to for a hearty breakfast. I fell in love immediately on my first visit. With multiple returns, I have not only been recognized as a regular on Yelp, but the staff has started to remember us as well.  Their two egg breakfast with your choice of meat and hash browns is a great way to start your day. When eating out, I always request my hash browns extra crispy. Here at Spencer's I do not need to make that request, they always serve theirs crispy on top, on bottom and moist on the inside. I always have them hold the side of toast and order a Half Order of Biscuits and Gravy to complete my breakfast. This takes me back to my childhood and being raised on a farm.    We've also enjoyed a Slinger and a Slammer. A Slammer is just like a Slinger, except the two eggs, meat and hash browns are covered in white milk gravy instead of chili. Either way you go, it is a winner.    The ambiance is vintage 50's diner. In the back little room, where I have enjoyed most of my breakfast it is decorated with sports photos and photos of the famous "Saturday Morning Breakfast Club". One morning a member of the SMBC was seated next to us and shared some great stories. That same morning a regular in the front room was celebrating his birthday and the entire diner sang "Happy Birthday", as he was served a stack of pancakes with a candle. Usually at restaurants this annoys me, but here it was total fun.    My experiences have all been breakfast, but I cannot wait to go back soon and have a diner style burger.

Welcome to my hood, Salt + Smoke. I've been in love with you since you opened on Delmar and am totally ecstatic that you are now closer to my home. On your first day I could not wait to get off work so I could come be part of your opening day festivities. If I didn't have to work, I most likely would have stayed the entire day and tried everything on the menu.   I could tell you guys are true professionals, because you nailed it on opening day. As Lance M. stated in his review, "Our service was outstanding and seemed as if the place had been open for years."(that is what he said, review has been removed) I'll take it a step further and include the bartenders and kitchen staff. Everyone was giving their A-Game. I have attended many a grand openings for restaurants and this one was the best by far.   As my usual, I sat myself at the bar and have already found my favorite stool for when I dine here. Another habit that is hard for me to break is my first cocktail, a Manhattan. It's one of their featured classic cocktails. It was stirred and served up, as a quality Manhattan should be. However, I would preferred a dark filthy cherry as my garnish.    My evening begun with Fried House Pickles with Flaxseed Mayo. The pickles may be fried, but flaxseeds are healthy, so that makes the scale balance. Am I right? Even if these  may not be the healthiest, they are damn tastiest. The pickles are covered in a tempura like breading that is crisp and thick enough to coat and protect the pickle. The enclosed pickle still had its own snap, no limp pickles. I'm normally not a mayo man, but it being blended with flaxseeds won me over and had me dipping my pickles.   My second cocktail was an Old Fashioned. OMG! They need to feature this beauty on the cocktail menu. This beauty was absolutely the best OF I have had in STL. It totally outshines even the premier cocktail bars in our great city. It may be my go to cocktail when dining here in the future. I had it made with rye and when the bartender served it and it had that murky look, I knew it was going to be a star.   My entree was a Beastie Combo with two meats. I enjoyed a 1/4 rack of ribs and Brisket. What sits S+S above other BBQ joints is, when your order Brisket, you get to choose; lean, fatty or burnt ends. I always will go with burnt ends. The rib meat was tender and fell on the bones easily and the burnt ends were mouth watering tender. The rub is full of flavor with the seasonings, that I never fell the need to use any of their sauces.   The plates come with two sides. I'm a creature of habit when Mac-n-Cheese is offered and had to have it. They use White Cheddar and Crackers. I think they use Ritz and how can you go wrong with white cheddar. My other go to is pit beans. BBQ and pit beans are a match made in heaven.   Bonuses for those who sit at the bar are hidden underneath the bar itself. They offer hooks for purses, jackets, backpacks or whatever else you carry that will fit on these hooks. The also have strategically  places outlets, so social media junkies like me can keep their devices charged up.   I'm so glad Salt+Smoke is in my hood, I hope they are up to having me as a regular.   Will I return? - Already have a regular stool at the bar.   When: October 29, 2017 Why: Opening Day - Dinner & Cocktails

After my lunch at Spaghetteria, no vampire in their right mind would come near me. Reading between the lines, that means Mamma Mia is a little heavy handed on the GARLIC. I love me some garlic, but here it was the dominating flavor in my food.   It was lunch time and I was dining alone, so driving by Mamma I thought I'd give her a try. I was surprised upon my arrival to discover they were offering an $8 lunch buffet. Normally buffets are not my thing, but I thought this was an opportunity to try multiple entrees.   My vegetarian friends would have been in heaven. They actually had a good selection of vegetarian friendly options. To be honest, they outnumbered the meat offerings on the day I dined. The grilled veggies were my favorite - I love zucchini with those fresh grill marks.   The pizza island always had two offerings and one was always a vegetarian (at least while I was there). Their pizza is thin crust, and the sauce was very flavorful. Again, my favorite was a vegetarian which had spinach and mushrooms - yummy.   Ambiance is rustic, minimal and close-out special, but they make it work. For a buffet service was still friendly and attentive. For that location, the crowd was a good cross-section of people. They had everything from; businessmen closing a deal, red hat ladies, parent/child, true buffet eaters and a trans-gender who held court during the lunch hour. She looked damn good, she was dressed to the 9's.   Like Stewart P., I may go back, but I'm not sure. The over powering garlic may keep me away, as it keeps vampires away from me.  However, the coupon I have may  persuade me to go and try a dinner. I really should never judge a restaurant by a buffet unless that is all they do.

The original needs to watch out, this new location is fantastic.  Our service was fast and friendly. The menu selection is a little smaller then South Grand location, but they put out some good diner food.  I live in between the two locations, and I may now find myself preferring the Fox diner over the original.

Bummer. Seriously, it totally bums me out that Half & Half is closed on Monday. Monday is one of my days off, so that is one day less that I get to go enjoy the delectable delights at H&H. I feel so cheated, but once I do get to eat breakfast or lunch here, I'm thankful for my other days off. I'd be hard pressed to choose which meal I like better; breakfast or lunch. I love them both so much. Their famous Bloody Mary with a Fried Pickle garnish goes perfectly with either meal.   One of my favorite vegetables is Brussels Sprouts and until I came to Half & Half, I would have never thought to put them in a omelette. Now that I have had one, it is so logical. A fresh vegetable, served up with Cheddar cheese creates a delicious overstuffed omelet. The sprouts were sautéed perfectly and as a side they served up a side of breakfast potatoes that were fried crisp. I couldn't resist, I had to add a side of bacon. I think next time I'll have them add the bacon to the omelet. This is by far my favorite omelet of all time.  When it's lunchtime at Half & Half, it's time for a burger. I love jalapeños, on my Mexican food and I love'm as a topping on my burger. H&H slices fresh jalapeños and mixes them up with caramelized onions.  Then they top the entire burger with cheddar cheese and place it on a  brioche bun with aioli. The final result is a thick and juicy burger with a side of house cut fries.   Whether it is breakfast or lunch, you cannot go wrong at Half & Half. Just remember, they are closed on Monday and are only open for the first two meals of the day. No dinner is served.  These last two visits I've been seated at the bar and I will say the service was better then when I have been at a table or booth. If you are dining alone or just two of you, I highly recommend that you belly up to the bar.   When: May 24 & June 8, 2016 Why: Lunch & Breakfast

Why would you go to another sub shop that only offers you 6" or a "foot long", when you can come to Penn Station and tell them how many "inches" you want. Yes, at PS you can have it "your way" by telling them how long you like it. PS offers; 6", 8", 10" and a huge 12" which will have you saying, "I can't believe I ate the whole thing."  Of the sub chain shops, PS serves up the best Cheesesteak. Steak, provolone, banana peppers and spicy mustard, stuffed in a mini loaf of bread that is not only vegan, but kosher too. Sorry gluten free folks, their bread does have gluten. Order a 12" Cheesesteak, large order of their fresh cut fries and a gallon of their hand squeezed lemonade and you have lunch for two. You'll also have enough lemonade left over to add some vodka when happy hour rolls around.   The SO never varies from the Cheesesteak, but for me my other two favorites are Chicken Teriyaki and Grilled Artichoke. When we go our separate ways on the sub, we still share that large order of fries that are cholesterol free (they use peanut oil) and we always and I do mean always have the lemonade.   If you're a dessert person grab a chocolate chunk cookie, they're baked fresh. I always eat mine much later, because I'm so full from my sub & fries.

I agree with Stephanie, the karaoke is a 5 star experience. Allison the karaoke hostess, knows how to get a crowd pumped. She keeps the flow of entertainers going and encourages duets and groups to sing their very best. Also, as pointed out by Stephanie.....the song book is huge. I don't think the Mitch Miller song book was ever that big.   Okay, I know you young folks are now going to have to go Google Mitch Miller to find out who he is. Thanks to the Internet old singalongs are not lost.   The drinks were cheap. I didn't pay the same price twice and I was drinking the same thing all night. I never challenged it, because it kept getting cheaper. Either the price goes down when karaoke begins, or it was my lucky night.   The staff was friendly and the crowd was a good mix of ages. The only negative of the night was sitting next to a plus size couple making out and I mean serious tounge and breast grabbing. The bartender was flipping ice water on them to cool them down. Nothing slowed them down.   If you're a fan of karaoke, Frailey's on Friday night is your spot.   No food was consumed on this visit, but the appetizer sampler plate served to my right and left looked like a good accompaniment to a cold beer.

I am so glad this location finally opened near my work. I use to drive to work the opposite direction to the Maplewood location (I live in the Lindenwood Park), then back track into the city for work. My work day begins at 5 AM so, I like a place that is open 24 hours, so I can start my day with a fresh cup of black coffee and a breakfast treat.   If someone asked me what my favorite donut is, I'd have to reply.....a donut hole. With that being said, I am a huge fan of the TimBits. A variety box of 10 and I'm as excited as a little kid on Halloween night.  If I need something more savory, I order a Bagel B.E.L.T.. I have yet to see any fast food restaurant make a breakfast sandwich as good as Tim Hortons.   I admit the drive-thru is a little crazy at this location, but it works and gets me on my way.  The staff is always chipper and friendly in the mornings. Tim Hortons makes my mornings easier.   When: Early AM Thursday-Sunday Why: Coffee and a morning treat

Another great spot on Main Street in Saint Chuck for picking up goodies to create gift baskets. Or better yet, mixes and goodies to help you look like a shining star at the holiday party.   If you are looking for gift ideas, for that friend or family member who is always in the kitchen this is the place to shop. You will come out with all sorts of spices, glazes and marinades.  I was amazed at the huge selection of Hot Sauces. Who knew there are so many ways to get heartburn.   Pat C. is right,  there are so many options, that a cook could get dizzy.   Bad Byron's Butt Rub! I had to buy it just for the name.

My annual update to tell you how cool and wonderful this little shop in Soulard is. It always makes my holiday shopping easy and I have some difficult people to shop for. It doesn't matter if they are on the nice or naughty list, you'll find an appropriate gift here. The gifts I find are unique, affordable and always received with excitement from the recipient.   This year, one of my recipients said, "I bet you got this at, The Porch." I just sat there with a Cheshire Cat grin on my face.   So I encourage you to shop local in one of the most historical neighborhoods in Saint Louis. Once you are done shopping at The Porch, treat yourself to some BBQ or Tacos across the street. You'll be eating local as well.  Will I return? - I always do......  When: November 28, 2017 Why: It's that most wonderful time of the year

Yida, you haven't even opened yet and you already have left a bad taste in my mouth. Monday night we were at the Galleria and saw all the excitement around your entrance. People were hustling and bustling in and out and we thought a Margarita and Mexican fare would be a great choice for dinner.   We entered with others and stood at the hostess stand as they organized tickets and chatted amongst themselves. Finally the primadonna host in a pink bow tie asked what I needed. I requested a table for two and this is how our conversation went:  Host: What time is your reservation? Me: We don't have a reservation.  Host: We only seat people with reservations. (In a condescending tone) Me: Really? (Shocked and disbelief tone) I could see a fourth of the restaurant empty Host: Yes. (More attitude in tone)  At this point the SO and I decided to go else where for dinner.  I looked at the young man shook my head in further disbelief and said "whatever". As I turned to exit, a manager who was standing by and heard the conversation, stopped me to explain why I could not be seated. What a shame the little host did not think to do the same.  The night was for Friends & Family of the opening staff only.  In other words, they basically were having a soft opening.   I informed the manager that the internet stated they were open and with no signage outside or on the door stating "private party" it was misleading. He gave me a card for a free appetizer or dessert. The card was a nice gesture, but to late. With it being a soft opening, I hope that manager used this as a teaching moment for his front of the house. The young man's attitude totally turned me off from ever returning and even tarnished my opinion of your sister restaurant Black Finn.

The Cinnamon  Rolls at Amy's are scrumptious. They are gooey, soft, loaded with big flavor and proof that size does not matter. The are small  in size, but big on flavor. Even though they are smaller, I am sure the calorie count is something I really do not want to know.   They're an incredible value at $1.25. What makes them even more special is when you order,  they ask if you want a center piece or an edge piece. I've had both and they both taste the same, but some who those inner center ones just seem to be softer and more gooier.  If it were a brownie, I'd take an edge piece.   I've also stopped in for a weekend breakfast and enjoyed big cup of Kaldi's coffee with an order of Biscuits and Gravy. The portion is small, but plentiful. Their House made biscuits are covered in a light brown milk gravy filled with large chunks of sausage.   Amy and her staff are always a delight to chat with while you are ordering. If you dine in, the great open space gives you the opportunity to watch them create their sweet baked goods.

It's not fair to compare Kirkwood Farmer's Market to Soulard's Farmers Market, but we all do. I visited on a Tuesday at lunch time, so I don't think I got a true feel of what this market really is. However, I did leave some amazing jellies that are locally made.  My shopping partner didn't read the labels as well as I did, the jelly he choose was from Ohio. I felt like I was doing a Pace Picante Sauce commercial, pointing out where his jelly was made. He's in training learning how to shop local.   The produce on display was plentiful and fresh. I also grabbed a loaf of bread from one of the many local bakeries on display. They also have a great selection of holiday decorations, but I thought the price point was a little high. Good price for Kirkwood, but I will bet you Michael's Crafts will have the same thing cheaper. If not, I'll be back and pay the inflated price so my front yard looks cute at Halloween and Thanksgiving.  I will say, that the staff here is bright eyed and bushy tailed. They were so perky, I'd swear they were on a coffee I. V. Drip.   I work weekends till 3PM, so I am glad to see that they stay open till 6PM. I will have plenty of time to shop after work.

As I got ready to create my new list, Biscuits and Gravy I read over my reviews of my memorable B&G. To my surprise, I did not mention B&G in my GGD review and they were pretty awesome.   Since my first visit, we have been back several times to GGD and each time we have had the intentions of trying something new. I don't know what happens, but when the waitress walks up and ask us what we would like, "Chicken and Waffles" just pops out of our mouths. I guess when you find a good thing it is so hard to stray away and try something new.   Being a farm boy, I was determined to try the biscuits and gravy on our last visit  and ordered them as a side dish. I was glad that I did, they were true country/farm style.  A huge flaky biscuit topped with a thick milk gravy with ample chunks of sausage. I ate all of my B&G and ended up taking my big piece of chicken breast home. Which  was a perfect lunch.  Now that I have experienced the Biscuits & Gravy at GGD, perhaps on my next visit when asked what I want, I may say a full order of  B&G.

Simple, stark and satisfying are the three words that come to mind when describing, Six Mile Bridge. Their set up is simple, they offer one thing and that is their craft beers. The decor/ambiance is stark, tables and chairs, with a minimalist decor. Then the most important word of all, satisfying. The beer is so refreshing and the decor is so relaxing, you'll feel totally satisfied with your experience at Six Mile Bridge.   When visiting a brewery, I always recommend getting a flight so you can experience a variety of brews. I will tell you now, I am not a fan of stout beers, but the Irish Stout from SMB has me reconsidering my opinion of stouts. I truly liked the smoothness of theirs and how the chocolate and coffee blended together. My second favorite of the flight, was their Irish Red Ale with honey. The other two offerings in my flight were; Bavarian Hefeweizen and Session IPA. Both were refreshing, but for me the stout and Red Ale were the stars.   I also enjoyed a glass of the Belgian Winter Ale, which had a rich taste of dark caramel, raisin and mandarin orange. For me personally, this was like a dessert beer.   The staff is extremely friendly and go out of their way to make you feel comfortable. The only in house food is freshly popped popcorn. Which is salty and makes you drink more craft beer. However, Frankly Sausages food truck is parked out front on Thursday-Saturday nights, giving you the perfect sandwich and fries to enjoy while you sip your flight of SMB brews.   I highly recommend that you visit the Heights and check out the new brewery in town. I am confident you'll be pleasantly surprised as I was with Six Mile Bridge.   When: January 7, 2016 Why: UYE

If it were not for Ian Froeb's STL 100, I would have never discovered the BEAST. With all the popular BBQ joints in the city and near by county, I would have never thought to cross the river, to enjoy a pork steak. A pork steak that was so fork tender, that I had no need for a knife. Ian is right again, this is a "must order".   The pork steak is huge, so huge that I had enough leftover for my evening meal as well. It came with two sides and I choose; Pit Beans and Brussel Sprouts. Steven C. recommended them saying they were, "burning hot and delicious". They indeed were spicy hot and I liked the big chunks of burnt ends floating in the beans. Brussel Sprouts are one of my favorite vegetables and they do theirs with pork belly, making it totally mouth watering.   The dry rub and smoked flavor was sufficient enough for me, but I still could not resist trying all three of the sauces provided. The Standard, was just that, a fairly standard BBQ sauce. Your Plain Jane's would love it. Their Cherry Chipotle is spicy sweet, giving an extra zing to your meat. I enjoyed it on my flour tortilla like Ian recommended. He gave me two good leads on this visit. The third and my personal favorite is the "Texas Chainsaw". A hot & spicy that is not to hot. It was just enough heat from the habanero to make you go WOW.   The service is extremely friendly. If dining in, I highly recommend sitting at the counter so you have some fun interaction with the staff. You'll also be amazed with their selection of craft beers. I like that on the menu they match each sammiches and plates with a recommended beer. Made my life so much easier.   I may have multiple BBQ joints close to my home, but now I am wishing the BEAST was one of them or at least a little bit closer.   When: April 26, 2016 Why: Lunch and STL 100

Do you love large breast? If so you need to visit Pat's Bar & Grill and have their fried chicken dinner. The breast they serve, are the largest I have ever seen and the accompanying pieces are impressive as well. Thick meaty thighs, curvaceous legs and wings that look as if the chicken has been pumping iron at the local gym. Big pieces, crispy flavorful coating and juicy meat.   I have been a fan of their fried chicken since the mid 80's. Yes, I have been coming here that long and the consistency of their quality product has remained the same. In my opinion, they serve the best chicken in the city. Their Onion Strings put those Bloom'n Onions at a steak house to blooming shame. They're served with horseradish sauce for an extra kick, but I like them plain with only the seasoned breading.   You can tell it is a true Irish Pub, the majority of the decor is green and in the back they have a clock counting down the time to Saint Patrick's Day to the second. The service is always friendly and a team effort. You'll never here "sorry, not my table" here, they want to make sure your experience is as enjoyable as it can be.

Friday we ordered Chicken Wings and Double order of Fries for the crew at work. Everyone was amazed at the wings. The wings were hot & spicy and the sauce was not over whelming. I hate wings that you have to wipe your fingers and mouth after every bite.   The fries were like baby steak fries, they were crisp and seasoned well. When I create a list of the best french fries, they'll be on the list.

We just had lunch at Russell's on Macklind and to borrow the words of Jack Buck, "that's a winner". It was amazing! I could not find fault in anything we had or in the service. It was all outstanding and I can not wait to come back to experience dinner and Sunday Brunch.   The BF enjoyed a Cuban Grill with Soup of the Day, Broccoli and Cheese and a side of Billy Goat Chips. The Cuban was perfectly grilled, toasting the bread to a nice crunch and melting the swiss cheese just enough to cover the pork, ham and pickles. It may have been 95 degrees outside, but the Broccoli Cheese Soup still hit the perfect spot in our tummies. It was rich creamy and filled with small bite size pieces of broccoli. The hometown Billy Goat Chips are always perfect with any penni type sandwich.   Having a list on Yelp, I felt an obligation to order their Mac-n-Cheese that was served with side salad. The Mac-n-Cheese is probably the best I have ever had at a restaurant, anywhere. The noodles were a perfect al a dente and evenly covered in a flavorful cheese. It then had multiple big croutons like those on the side salad perched on top. The portion was so huge, I will be having a small serving for breakfast in the morning.   The side salad was mixed greens with veggies, shredded Parmesan, garlic croutons and tossed with a Herbed Balsamic Vinaigrette. We thought it was odd when reading the menu that all salads had the same dressing. Are they lazy and taking the easy way out? No, the dressing is that good, that they don't need to offer another option.   Sarah S. said the workers here are a highlight. I'll agree, but change the word to a "delight". You may have ordered at the counter and the food was delivered by a runner from the kitchen, but they still out shined some servers I've had at a sit down restaurant. When no one was at the counter, they'd work the cafe like a hostess at a party. Making sure that everything was to your satisfaction and filling beverages.  It was a delight talking with the young lady with blue hair.   With all the sweet treats on display, we couldn't leave without stocking up. Yes, we bought more then one. We walked out with two cupcakes that will put Jilly's to shame. Bring on the cupcake wars and Russel's on Macklind would win hands down. We also got two different Gooey Butter treats Peanut Butter and Three Berries which will be served up for breakfast tomorrow.   I can not wait to go back for Brunch and taste those made to order biscuits and their house made Bloody Mary mix.

Dorothy was right,  there is no place like home when searching for a good Turkish restaurant. Okay, perhaps Dorothy wasn't searching for good Turkish food, but I was and I found it within blocks of my home. It took the International Supper Club to get me here and now I can't wait to go back. The entire night was amazing, the ambiance, the company, the liquor and the food.    We started our dining experience with martini's, our first one was "Majik Carpet Ride," made with Ketel One and other booze it was so good I had to have a second ride. Our server was very suggestive and recommended the "habibi" which was made with Tangueray gin, he warned us it was dangerous, so we shared one. Oh my God, it was so smooth and yes it was dangerous.   We begun our feast with two Small Hot Plates, one of which was Kalamar Tava (calamari) and the other  Borek (crispy fried filo stuffed feta cheese and parsley).  Jason R said it right in his review, "Calamari is either good or not good". I will tell you I have been searching for the "perfect calamari" and I have found it here at Aya Sofia.   While enjoying our Small Plates, our "suggestive server" kept plying us with samples of red wines that he thought would compliment our entrees. He nailed it and it was the perfect match to our lamb.   The climax of the evening was our entrees, Kuzu Incik (lamb shank) and Kuzu Pizola (lamb chops). Jason R has already sung the praises of their Kuzu Incik, so I'll sing about the Kuzu Pizola. I make incredible lamb chops and these put mine to shame. These chops were grilled and seasoned to perfection. The meat was so tender, it melted in my mouth and the side of vegetables could have converted me to vegetarianism.    The service was outstanding and I cannot wait to go back. Thank-you, Aya Sofia for a magical night.

My love affair with Spencer's Grill has continued on. They offer good food at a great value, served by some of the perkiest and friendliest staff. I have almost eaten my way thru the entire menu, if I haven't enjoyed a listing one of my friends dining with me has.   As promised in my last review, I've been back to try the diner style burger. There just is something about a grill seared burger from a diner. It is simple and full of flavor. I enjoyed a Double Cheeseburger with lettuce, tomato and onion. This burger was better then those I have had at Carl's Drive In. The fries served as a side were well seasoned and extremely crispy with a hot and soft inside.   My favorite breakfast at Spencer's is one of their omelettes. They are made with only two eggs, which in my opinion is large enough. They are also filled with the appropriate amount of ingredients. So many other places, over produce omelettes and I am unable to finish my order.  Here, I clean my plate and feel totally satisfied.   I must also let pancake lovers in on a little secret, Spencer's serves them up with a twist. Here you can order them crispy and they'll come to you with crisp edges. I don't know how they work their magic, but it adds an extra kick of flavor.   In closing, I just want to give an extra shut out to the wait staff. They are all exceptionally friendly and well trained. They work as a team and make sure everyone is treated as if they were family or a personal friend.

If it were not for a co-worker going here for lunch one day, I would have never discovered the haven of wings. They offer 18 different flavors of wings and 4 different levels of heat index. When I've been craving chicken wings at home, I've had local pizza joints deliver them to me. Not any more, my wings will be coming from the Wing Zone.   The wings are a good size. As Goldielocks would say, "Not to big and not to small, they are just the right size." They offer a Buddy Pack of 20 wings (2 flavors), Family Pack 35 wings and a Party Pack of 50 wings. The family and party packs allow you to pick 3 flavors.  You can have your choice of original or boneless. To me, boneless is just baby chicken tenders. Give me the bone.   I've tried three different flavors; Buffalo Bliss, Lemon Zinger and Garlic Parm. I liked the Buffalo, but next time will increase my heat index and order the Hot Shot. The Garlic Parm, was just okay and those who are fans of Lemon Pepper will enjoy Lemon Zinger, as I did.   Sides are fast food okay. The onion rings are obviously dumped from a frozen bag, don't waste your time ordering them. If you need a Fried Pickle fix, theirs will do the trick, but seriously they are nothing to write home about. The Wedge Fries, are a good companion to their chicken wings. Don't waste your time or money ordering a salad.  Counter service is polite. I suggest you call ahead and order if you want to pick-up, otherwise you'll be standing and waiting while they make your wings. I'm excited to know my house is within their delivery area, making my cravings for chicken wings an easy fix.

It was late at night, I was working overtime covering the midnight shift at work and needed food. Not much was open at such an ungodly hour. The service was quick, the food was hot and fresh.  I was impressed that the lot was pretty much litter free, which is impressive considering its downtown location. Normally I do not use a drive-thru window, so I was shocked with the speedy and polite service I received. I had a good giggle while in line for the drive-thru, the car ahead of me was actually a golf cart. He was a security guard from a nearby nightclub.   Not my typical WC, but I'd come back for a slider or two.

Don't be shocked that I gave a chain 4 Stars. IHOP is what it is and that is a hearty breakfast at an affordable price. However, I myself was shocked to find out that I am older then, IHOP. I got over that real fast when I realized I got to order from their 55+ menu and save me some dollars and cents while enjoying my breakfast.   This is a relatively new location, they remodeled a shuttered Fazoli's. I'd much rather an IHOP in my hood, then a Fazoli's. There use to be a old A-Frame IHOP across the street, but it closed years ago and was torn down for a new bank. My neighbors in the Lindenwood Park and St. Louis Hills neighborhoods are excited about its return.   I created my own omelet this morning with; Pepper Jack Cheese, Bacon,  Onion and Green Pepper. They did not skimp on the ingredients. I liked that the onion and green pepper, still had a little snap to them.  The best part was that it came with two of their famous Buttermilk Pancakes. I always use the Old Fashioned Pancake Syrup. They have flavored ones available, but I'm old and old fashioned. (LOL)  Being new, the restaurant was extremely clean. The staff was friendly and being a holiday Monday were hustling to keep up with the high volume of diners.   Will I return? - Yes, it's a quick and easy breakfast. It's cheap, too.   When: October 9, 2017 Why: New and I needed breakfast the most important meal of the day.

We needed a quick an easy lunch after doing grocery shopping at Dierbergs and with TB in the parking lot, it was an easy choice. This Taco Bell is actually a combo restaurant. It's 2/3 TB and 1/3 Pizza Hut. It offers a full TB menu and a limited PH menu. They only offer personalized pizzas and breadsticks for PH, no full sized pizza.  If you enjoy Nacho flavored Doritos, you'll love a taco shell made out of those addictive chips. I like that they build these tacos in cardboard holders, so you do not get orange stained fingers from holding the shells. A price you have to pay for a more flavorful shell.   There are two types of Doritos Locos Tacos, regular and supreme. I like simple tacos, so I ordered 3 regular and the SO prefers the extra toppings so he went with 3 supreme. Both come with seasoned beef, crisp lettuce and cheddar cheese. The additional ingredients for a supreme are; chopped red tomato and reduced fat sour cream. (I bet the SO didn't know it was reduced fat) Both were good and we topped them with their hot sauce.   In addition to the tacos we ordered, Bean Burritos which were simple. A soft flour tortilla wrapped around hearty beans, cheddar cheese, diced onions and a tangy red sauce.  I will admit we both had minor heartburn later in the day, but it was worth it for a quick cheap Mexican lunch.

I've just showered with a glycerin soap from Maven and "I feel pretty, oh, so pretty, I feel pretty, witty and bright".  I will admit, I have always used two soaps when showering. I use a deodorant soap for the manly areas and a Dove for Men product for the rest of my body. After this shower, I am flipping that bird off and replacing it with the locally made soap from Maven.   The scent I bought on my first visit was, "my boyfriends t-shirt". I can assure you it does not smell like the t-shirts of the Sharks and Jets after they have been dancing on the rooftops and streets of New York City.  In stead it smells like fresh clean laundry that has dried in a fresh summer breeze. The fragrance was so soothing that I also bought it in a Wood Wick Soy Candle and Solid Perfume.   I can tell you now, I will be a repeat customer at Maven. I may even have to start considering myself to be a metro sexual, which I have not in the past.

Saint Louis is slowly building a reputation for good pizza. Yes, I know we will never be New York or Chicago, but we have come a long way.  Among the leaders in this new trend is PW Pizza.  First thing that impressed us was the fact that only two of their pizzas (Big Balls and Sausage) offered on  menu actually had provolone as the main cheese. All the others  were much more creative in their choice of cheese.   Our eyes at lunch time were much bigger then our stomach. Actually, we just wanted to be able to try more then just one pizza. We ordered The Wolf, a tomato sauce base, with house made fennel sausage, pepperoni, apple-wood smoked bacon, caramelized onion, green pepper, roasted garlic and mozzarella. Now I call this a true "meat lovers" pizza with mozzarella being the perfect "cheese".   With a new years resolution to lose weight and eat more vegetables, I ordered the Popeye an Olive Oil which is one of Wendy's favorites.  It starts out with roasted garlic olive oil, which is topped with spinach, roasted red pepper and one of my favorite cheeses, "goat cheese". I love spinach and goat cheese so this pizza was a home run.   Let me regress, we started our PW feast with Roasted Dry Rub Chicken Wings and they were incredible. As Mark P. mentioned, the menu claims they are healthier then the traditional fried wing.  I do not know how much healthier they are, but being a fan of wings I will take any amount of healthiness.   I took a to-go-menu on my way out, for future use. I am totally planning on ordering take out in the very near future.

A big thank you to Livingsocial for introducing me to Spiro's in the Lindenwood neighborhood. I am embarrassed to admit it, but I will. I live in the Lindenwood neighborhood, I am The Baron here on Yelp and I have never enjoyed the Greek cuisine at Spiro's.   When I saw the Livingsocial coupon, I jumped on the opportunity to have a lunch at Spiro's.  The day we lunched was late, we got there about 1:30 PM and there was only one other table. However, in the back party room they were serving a large funeral lunch. Even with the large banquet going on, our service was attentive.   What would a lunch or dinner at a Greek restaurant be without an order of Saganaki? Enjoying Flaming Cheese is part of the experience. OPA!! They flash fried the Kassen Cheese right at the table and it was the perfect accompaniment to the fresh bread.  We also shared another popular Greek appetizer, Dolma. A large grape vine leaf stuffed with rice, ground beef and lamb then top with egg lemon sauce. Both were very flavorful and will be enjoyed again.   The SO enjoyed a large Athenian Greek Salad, with slices of rotisserie lamb on top. These salad is defiantly large and could be shared by two who can also share an appetizer or two. Momma always told me a good boy shares.   I enjoyed a Gyro Sandwich, which was very very good. Yes, I meant to do a double very very, it was that good. It was the most tender and flavorful rotisseries lamb I have had in a Gyro. As with all Gyro's, it was served in a pita bread and garnished with fresh tomatoes, onion and tzatsiki sauce. As a side dish they served up thinly sliced potatoes that were fried with a crispy shell and a hot moist meaty inside.   We were so stuffed, we could not try their Baklava, but we are looking forward to that experience on our next visit.

I am still amazed how good the customer service is at this store. The staff is always friendly, helpful and go beyond the normal retail associate. It is also well maintained and merchandised.   Did you know that if you find a "published" lower price on an item sold at PetSmart that they will match it? I didn't, but I found that out today and wanted to share that with my fellow pet owners on Yelp.

For those of you who are early risers, it is time for you to take advantage of the Early Bird Special at City Diner. Every day except holidays, between 7 & 9 AM, CD offers one of the best values in the city.  $4 will get you two eggs prepared how you like them, a choice of bacon or sausage, hash browns or American Fries and toast. That is a lot of food for $4.   This morning we took advantage of the Early Bird special and shared a half order of Biscuits & Gravy. A half order is only one biscuit topped in gravy for $3 and a full order is two biscuits for $4.50. The biscuit was HUGE, when split in half it is plenty for two to share. Add your typical morning beverage and you have a great feast to start your day.  I've never been disappointed with the service here, it is always friendly. Even when it is your first visit they make you feel as if you are a regular.

Once again, this is a place that Yelp needs to give me the opportunity for a half star. I came here for a luncheon that was a fund raiser for a young lady battling breast cancer. We had special postcard designating a percentage of our meal went to her fund. Kudos to MM for sponsoring and supporting events like this.   I was the only gentleman among our ten diners. I was also the biggest "foodie" amongst the group. Several of our ladies enjoyed salads, I got a couple pictures and others enjoyed sandwiches. Being a man, I had to go for the wings and pizza.   As an appetizer, the five hot wings were the perfect serving size. It was just enough, to give me something to munch and cut the hunger pains until my pizza was ready. They were not overly sauced and the "heat" from the spicy was rather mild for my tastebuds.   As usual, my go to pizza toppings were; Italian Sausage and Jalapeños. I ordered a small and half of it went home. I was impressed with the sauce, cheese and the amount of toppings. The dough for a chain pizza joint, was also impressive. I like how the bottom was crisp and was thick enough to still be a little chewy.   All the ladies I dined with liked their salads and sandwiches. The salads I was able to photograph, were impressive looking.   I liked that they had Coke Zero as a fountain drink option. My only issue with MM, was the service. It was so, s-l-o-w. Our lunch dragged on forever. If I worked in the area and came for my lunch break, I'd be called into the bosses office for taking extended lunchtime.   Will I return? - If someone ask me to go, I'll go.   When: August 16, 2017 Why: Fund Raiser Lunch for Breast Cancer Battle

Wow, their carryout is as good as a dine experience. I love how they double wrapped our 1/2 rack of baby back ribs and 8 oz of brisket. First it is wrapped in a saran wrap and then foil, making for a neat clean trip home. They also package each of the side dishes separately in plastic containers with lids. Our pie was simply put in a Styrofoam container with a flip lid. Boo hiss, Styrofoam not environmentally friendly.   Back to the food - as last time the brisket was fork tender. I was able to break off my bite size pieces with a simple pressure from my fork. This time when I packaged up some sauces, I got some of the Coffee BBQ Sauce and I must say it is now my favorite. The 1/2 rack of baby back ribs were cleaned to the bone by the SO. He said they were "fabulous".   We had to order our favorite sides from last time; Mac-n-Cheese and The Pasta Salad that has black beans and corn. Oh my, Oh my, I love this Mac-n-Cheese. As my second side, I expanded my experience and tried the cole slaw which is a creamy slaw. I prefer a creamy slaw over a vinegar slaw any day and this one is a winner.   This time we got to experience pie and since I was the one picking up the carry out, I got to pick the flavor and I choose Pecan. My only regret of selecting Pecan is that I only bought one slice and I had to share it with the SO. Damn it! I love Pecan pie and this is the best I have had at any restaurant. It is even better then Art Smith's Pecan Pie at his restaurant Table Fifty-Two in Chicago and that is a serious compliment.   Portions were large enough that I have a lunch for tomorrow at work. My coworkers are going to be jealous.

Hello, Menards! There is a new home improvement big box store in town and it is taking competitive shopping to another level. Menards is the Aldi's of home improvement stores. The prices are extremely low, but they will be brands that you are not totally familiar with. If you research and shop wisely, your savings can be money in the bank.  The store is laid out beautifully. I like that it is two levels of shopping space with moving ramps for easy access with your shopping cart. They sell practially everything from A to Z. It blew my mind that they had Watkin's products. I haven't seen them in years and didn't even know they were still available.   The selection of patio furniture was very reasonable and had a variety of price points to accommodate every budget. I'm not a handyman, but was totally blown away by the tool section. I was also amazed at the selection of cleaning products, Mr. Clean would be in ahhh.   This location is way better then the other Menards I have shopped. I hope they keep up the high standard that they are setting up now.   When: April 16, 2016 Why: Patio Furniture & Checking out new store

The Customer Service here is amazing. They are friendly, have positive attitudes and project a team spirit. Your order is made right in front of you, so you know it's going to be good. Having all of that, you get quality service and food. The fresh cut fries are great and the hand squeezed lemonade is the best. If you can wait till you get home, a splash of Vodka in the lemonade gives it an extra kick. I've tried multiple sandwiches and all of them are yummy, but the Philly Cheesesteak is still a favorite. When you leave, the positive energy here will have you leaving with a smile - hence a "Happy Meal".

Oh, Happy Day! I have been waiting for this new location to open and I was so anxious, I was one of the first to arrive on opening day. They informed me I was the first to sit at the bar and that is an honor I will cherish for ever. This location is much larger then the Clayton location, but still has the same decor and feel.   This morning I made it an avocado themed breakfast. I started out with avocado toast. I call it my breakfast appetizer. It's so simple and yet so delicious; wheat toast, feta, cilantro, lime, cracked pepper and smear of avocado. Yum-Yum.   Next was my entree, Avocado and Spinach Benedict. It was a traditional English Muffin topped with avocado, sautéed spinach and two poached eggs with hollandaise sauce. I consider this a healthy breakfast - LOL. In my humble opinion, Half & Half has the best hollandaise sauce.   I like that they serve Blueprint Coffee, which is a local roaster. It's nice to see local businesses supporting each other. I try not only to shop local, but to eat local too.   The staff was professional and friendly. I liked how they were asking everyone their names, so they can learn and greet their future regulars.   Will I return? - I'll be there tomorrow for breakfast again.   When: September 5, 2017 Why: Breakfast on Opening Day

As Bette Davis said in Beyond The Forest, "What a dump." However, in the case of Uncle Bill's, it gives character. I can honestly tell you that UB has not been remodeled or redecorated since I moved to STL in 1979 and that is part of its charm and ambiance. To be honest, it had been at least 8 years since my last visit to UB's and when I walked in for my recent breakfast it was as if things had never changed. That was because they hadn't.  We were quickly seated, which surprised me since it was a Sunday and around 9:00AM. I guess everyone was either at church or sleeping in. The restaurant was still very full and the tables are cramped very close together. Keeping the closeness in mind, you may want to keep that in mind when picking your subject of conversation. The lady next to us was telling her friend about her son in prison. I had to bite my tongue, I so bad wanted to ask her if her son had a bitch or if he was one of the other inmates bitch.   Our waitress was very attentive, made sure we quickly had our morning coffee. She also had a good sense of humor, she chuckled when I asked if there were any off the menu specials. Since they had no specials we went with the Country Fried Steak and the 2 Pork Chop Breakfast. Both came with two eggs and hash browns on the side. In addition to these hearty breakfasts, we shared an order of biscuits and gravy.   The Country Fried Steak was very good, a nice big piece of tender beef breaded and covered in flavorful milk gravy. The pork chops were not as good, they were a thin cut and overly cooked making them dry and tough. I was hoping for a thick, juicy chop. Our eggs were  cooked over easy and done well, as were the hash browns. They're not your traditional hash browns, but are more an American Fries.  The star of the breakfast was the hearty serving of biscuits and gravy. We got two huge flaky biscuits covered in milk gravy filled with pieces of sausage. Next time I need a comfort breakfast, I may just come here and order Biscuits & Gravy with a side of hash browns.

Watching the other diners is like watching the characters from Tales of the City. It is entertaining and makes for great conversation. The food is above average for a diner. Breakfast is by far their best meal. The service is way better then Alice and Flo at Mel's Diner. Get out and experience city life and have breakfast at City Diner.

Great addition to The Grove. Gezellig is an amazing Beer Hall that offers a large variety of craft beers. You have an impressive amount of draft beers and a enormous selection of can and bottles. If you cannot find a beer to satisfy your taste buds, you need to be drinking whiskey up the street at Intoxicology.   The bartenders or the masters of craft beer are very helpful and personable. During my visit, I enjoyed two flights, each was 3, 5 oz samplings of different beers. I selected the first flight and allowed the bartender to surprise me with the second. I shared with him, my typical likes and dislikes and he magically created a flight that was to my liking.   What makes Gezellig unique to other beer bars, is the variety. It's impressive that you can not only enjoy a cold draft beer, but you can go to the coolers and select a bottle or can to enjoy as well. If you find one you really like, buy it and take it home too.   I'll be back? - Yes, it is a craft beer paradise.   When: March 7, 2018 Why: Meeting Yelp friends for a cold beer.

I've got to start rereading my previous reviews before dining at restaurants. When you dine out as much as I do, you forget small details about your earlier meals. I forgot how they present their Calamari, here at Tavolo V and didn't request my spicy tomato sauce to be served on the side. I do not always dip my Calamari, I like it plain with just a squeeze of lemon.  Our last visit we did not enjoy any of their amazing salads, but this time we enjoyed two of their most popular. My dining partner ordered the Beet Salad. It had a HUGE Fried Goat Cheese ball in the center of Frisee, which was surrounded by cubes of red and golden beets. It was all tossed with a white wine vinaigrette, which added a simple burst of flavor.   My salad was the Del Pietro, a simple house salad that could rival those at Rich & Charlie's. I'm not a fan of Iceberg lettuce, but Tavolo V mixes it with Romaine, Parmigiano Cheese, red onion, tomato and then tosses it with a house vinaigrette.  A glass of wine, with their fresh bread would make this salad a perfect lunch.   Seeing their Lasagna being served to the table next to us on our last visit, my dining partner knew what he wanted. The portion is so huge, two adults could actually share it as an entree.  It is a mixture of beef and pork with ricotta and parmigiano cheeses in a rich thick tomato sauce. He could only eat half of it and enjoyed the remainder the next day for lunch. Our server commented, he has never seen anyone eat it all in one sitting.   For my pasta dish, I enjoyed the Pomodoro. It was a spaghetti dish with olive oil, garlic, diced fresh tomatoes, basil and goat cheese. I am a goat cheese addict, so this was the perfect entree for me. I found this dish to be light and refreshing for a pasta entree.   I've always had excellent customer service here and look forward to my next visit.  Before ordering next time, I will be sure to reread my reviews so I know to order the Brussels Sprouts and the Spaghetti with Meatballs.   When: 3 MAR 2014 Why: Dinner

Great place, I have never been disappointed. The staff is friendly and provide great service. The Ari's Greek Salad is big enough for two to share and then some. If you're sharing a Ari's Salad, share an order of Flaming Cheese...YUM! Breakfast on the weekend, for $6.95, it is the best value in the city. I can not sing the praises enough of the breakfast buffet at Ari's. It is simple, filling and worth the $. The made to order omelets are huge and stuffed with the items of your choice. Make it a true weekend brunch and enjoy a Bloody Mary

I love this store!   I am not an Apple nor a computer geek. When it comes to computer skills, I am just an average man. Nonetheless, I love my electronic gadgets/toys and this is the best places to buy them.   My most recent addition to my collection of gadgets is the iPad2. Now that I have it, I wonder how did I ever make it through life without one. That is also the same wonderment I had when I got my iPhone. They keep me organized, on schedule and most importantly they keep me connected to Yelp.   I appreciate the fact that the sales staff here is not commissioned sales. They listen to your needs and guide to the appropriate item(s) that fulfill your needs. There are no high pressure sale pitches, just good old fashion features and benefits selling.   The support staff here is also pretty amazing. When I bought my Mac Book the One to One sessions were so helpful in getting me transferred over from a PC brain to an Apple mindset. The Genius Bar has saved my ass several times and their workshops are always teaching me something new.   I'll say it one more time, "I love this store."  Did you know this location is the largest Apple store inside a mall?

Biggie's is in my neighborhood, it is less then 3 blocks from my home. So when I noticed I was about to write my 200th review (a Biggie), I thought it was appropriate to dine at a restaurant named Biggie's. What is amazing, is I have lived here for 8 years and have never eaten here.  Was the food good? Yes. Was the service good? Yes. Was it a weird experience? Oh, hell yes.
