I really can't put my finger on it, but this place made me feel as if I were in a time warp. Perhaps it was the decor, the walls are covered with historic pictures and sports memborbila. The rest of the decor reminded me of a rural small town Illinois restaurant, where everyone knows your name and business.   I had a dinner salad with their "white French dressing", it is so popular they sell it bottled there in the restaurant. Did it impress me? No. I found it to be rather flavorless.  I will choose another dressing on my next visit, because the salad itself was above average for a dinner salad.   I asked my server what I should order and she was very open and honest about what she liked. I ordered the steak sandwich. She recommended that I upgrade to garlic bread with cheese. Can you guess what type of cheese? You are so right, Provel.   The steak was grilled perfectly and it was tender. I think doing the garlic bread over the standard french bread was a great touch. Having the provel was neither here nor there. Could have done without it.   The trays of pasta and pizza going to other tables did look good.   I'll go back to try the ribs, Fred says they are the best in town.   Not the experience I wanted for #200, but hey it was A-OK.

OMG! I am in shock. I went to Aya Sofia and didn't order lamb chops. I was all set and ready to order my usual and then Emily our server told us the special of the night. She sang its praises by saying it was her favorite and how she always looks forward to it being a special offering. So glad, I listened to her, the Grilled Swordfish was seafood at its best.   I started out with a Mediterranean Mule. It was made just like a Moscow Mule, but instead of vodka, it was made with Milagro Blanco Tequila. To be honest, not my cup of Mule, but I'm glad I gave it a try.   As an appetizer I ordered, Kalamar Tava. I kept with a seafood theme for my entire meal. It was lightly breaded calamari, served with homemade garlic aioli. Delicious. I'm happy to say, this was probably the best calamari I have ever had. The pieces were huge, crisp and the aioli would be a great condiment for anything. Wish I could buy it by the jar.   The piece of resistance of the meal was of course the, Swordfish. It was a large steak, grilled beautifully. Each bite, flaked perfectly. They served it over a bed of sautéed spinach and garlic mashed potatoes. If this is offered as a special on my next visit, I'll order it again.   Service is always top notch. Aya Sofia is a 5 Star experience. It deserves more recognition then it receives.

A chain store with a neighborhood feel. The staff is friendly and it  is almost always a given that you will see someone you know. Or at least your dog will see someone they know. On select weekends one of the local rescue groups can be seen in the parking lot offering pets in need of a forever home.   This trip was all about a scoop and you know what type of scoop I am talking about. In the past we have worn medical gloves and filled plastic grocery bags. Yuck and the bags are not biodegradable. So this year we're going to be very green and dispose of our K-9 hills and mountains properly in the yard waste dumpsters.   The selection of scoops were almost over whelming. who knew they could have so many designs and styles. We selected one with a rake and spade and a large scoop. After all we do have four dogs. With a scoop and a bucket,  biodegradable bags that attach to our leashes for walks, we are responsible pet owners.   They have a vet (Banfield), grooming, food, toys, and so much more.  If Petsmart does not have it, your pet most likely does not need it.

When: March 8 Why: Lunch   I can't wait to go back. You can only eat so much on your first visit, but trust me I tried.   This place is amazing! The customer service is top notch. As soon as we entered we were greeted with hand shakes and a welcoming rib. The line was constantly 6-8 customers deep, but they kept it moving. Once we placed our order, we had to wait for a space to dine. We ended up sharing a table with another fun couple.   We ordered a special they were offering, 1/2 slab ribs, another meat (we chose prime rib) two side and a soda. To make it a meal for two, we ordered an extra soda and side. Our sides were; baked beans, BBQ Pork Skins and Deviled Egg Potato Salad.  The Baked Beans were smokey, meaty and the best I've ever had at a restaurant. Deviled Egg Potato Salad is a creative twist to a traditional side, that will have you doing your best Oliver Twist imitation of "more please". For me personally the Pork Skins are nothing special, but I have never been a pork rinds boy.   The highlight of my lunch was when they walked up and asked if we had tried their Pastrami. I love Pastrami and have never been able to find good Pastrami in St. Louis. When I answered a heartfelt "no", they presented us with a sampling. I have found my pastrami in St Louis, it was moist and smoked to perfection. The first words out of my mouth as I tasted it was, "this is orgasmic". The host laughed, patted me on the back and said he was glad I enjoyed it. I will go back and buy it by the pound for work lunches.   Bogarts is a winner, I see them expanding very soon.

We are so lucky here in the city, we've got both Pappy's and Bogart's. We even have another great spin-off of the two, Adam's Smokehouse. So I am thrilled to see that the county is finally getting their own great BBQ place to enjoy. I can only hope that now that they have their own, it will make the city lines shorter...LOL.   Meet a couple of friends here for lunch. With two county dwellers, one county worker and a city dweller with the day off, this seemed to be the perfect place. When we arrived there was the typical line, out the door. Being a delicate flower, I thought I'd melt in the heat, but the line moved quickly. Dalie's also showed their excellent customer service skills by having a hostess outside offering cold water and menus to those in line. Nice touch, impressed me.   Wanting to experience as much as possible, I ordered the Pick 2 Plate. That way, I got to experience two meats and two sides. I love brisket and being a fan of Bogart's pastrami, I had to try Dalie's. The brisket was tender, plastic fork tender. My favorite sauce was Uncle Joe's Original. I fell in love with it so much, that I bought a mason jar full of it for only $5. The pastrami matched Bogart's, but seemed to be more salty.   My sides were Mac-n-Cheese and Fried Fire & Ice Pickles. Both were winners. Anyone who knows me, knows I am the King of Fried Pickle and these are true winners. Spicy, lightly breaded, thinly sliced and fried to perfection. They're definitely getting a space on my Fried Pickle list. The Mac-n-Cheese was rich and creamy, but could have had more of a crunch top. However, it will not stop it from being added to my prestigious Mac-n-Cheese list.   The carry-out for the roomie was a half slab of ribs, that was fall of the bone delicious. These ribs were better then Adam's which is within walking distance from my house. His carry-out also had the same fork tender brisket. He enjoyed both, very much. I had to sneak a bite of the sides; Pit Baked Beans and Missoula Slaw; the creamy slaw had celery seed which brought out the flavor. I must agree with some of the other reviewers and say that these are some of the best baked beans I have enjoyed at a BBQ joint.   Once you place your order at the counter, one of their friendly staff will bring it to your table. There is plenty of seating inside and out. Once they bring your food to the table, they continue to check on you just as a full service restaurant would do. So you not only get quality BBQ, but you get good souther hospitality as well.

This is where used car salesman got their sleazy reputation.   I wouldn't shop or buy anything from this location.   After leaving had to go home and shower to get rid of the sleazy grime feeling that I got from their sales manager and staff.   We caught them in a bald face lie and the more they tried to save face, the more they tripped over their words. It was a prime example of the right hand not knowing what the left had is doing.

I have got to give a big thank you to the Humane Society of Missouri for having a fund raiser called, Dining Out for Dogs. If it were not for this fund raiser, I would have never heard of,  or discovered Nora's. She is a quaint unpretentious little sandwich shop in Dogtown that serves up hearty soups, salads and sandwiches.   We arrived for lunch about a quarter past 12 and the small dining area was already about half full. We studied the gigantic menu chalkboard and selected our sandwiches. I pretended I was a vegetarian and choose the Veggie Melt. It is made with house Smoked Portabella, Artichokes, Black Olives, Roasted Red Peppers, Caramelized Onions, Provolone, Cheddar, Avocado, Sprouts, Lettuce, Tomato and a large smear of Chipotle Mayo. They use Hoagie type rolls and I went with wheat. This is very likely the best Veggie Melt with a Portabella mushroom that I have ever had. The only con, they smeared way to much Chipotle Mayo on the samey for my taste.   The SO went with one of their cold Sandwiches and choose the Smoked Chicken Salad. They smoke the chicken breast in house, pull it and mix it with diced celery, red onion and Chipotle Mayo. It is then topped with lettuce and tomato and served on a fresh Hoagie Roll.   Their sandwiches are served with a large pickle spear and a choice of Cole Slaw,  Potato Salad or a bag on Miss Vicki's Chips and they have four flavors to choose from. We both wanted Cole Slaw, but they were already out of it. I had to ask myself, how can you be participating in a fund raising event and run out one hour in to the event? It almost cost them a star, but once I ate my Veggie Melt I decided to let them have 4.   Dieting, we did not want chips. I had to be strong, Miss Vicki is one of my favorite bag of chips. The SO went with the potato salad, but I am not a fan of potato salad that is mustard based. I asked if I could have a house salad instead with a minor up charge and they agreed. The potato salad got a thumbs up and the salad with their house dressing got two thumbs up.   Staff was friendly and were giving constant attention to diners and keeping things straightened. I am glad I supported the HSMO by having lunch here today and I will return to fill my own tummy in the future.

OMG! After listening to Mark P. sing the praises of Diana, I finally visited her bakery on our last pilgrimage to Cherokee. We lucked out and got princess parking right in front and were immediately overwhelmed with the aroma when we exited our car.  Entering the bakery definitely smells heavenly and the selection on my first visit was overwhelming.   There was so much to choose from, I didn't know what to experience first I should have paid closer attention to recommendations here on Yelp. I like the idea of picking up a tray and tongs at the front door and filling the tray with your selections it makes the check out easier.   One of the treats we bought was a couple slices of Flan and if I were not trying to lose weight I could of enjoyed another slice. Now that I have discovered Diana, we'll be stopping every time we are on Cherokee.

SugarFire Smoke House is such happy place. Every time I visit, all the employees have smiles and true happy faces. Hell, even all the diners are happy. Why shouldn't they all be happy? They're serving and eating the absolute best BBQ not only in St Louis County, but they beat all the city places, too.   I've put on some pounds, I like to refer to them as my "Yelp Pounds". To drop these pounds and get back to my "Pre-Yelp" weight I've gone low-carb. SugarFires' menu makes it easy to follow the low-carb lifestyle. Today I had an amazing lunch. I choose the Meat Daddy, which is two meats and two sides. As always, the brisket and turkey were fork tender and smoked perfectly. I've recently developed a love for Kale, so one of my sides was the Kale Caesar (I picked out the croutons) and Collard Greens was the other. I've always thought Collard Greens looked nasty, so I never tried them until today. I wish my mom was still here, so I could tell her I finally tried Collard Greens and liked them. Since they were my first, I can't say they are the best, but I can say they turned me on to a new vegetable and that is amazing.    So glad SugarFire is spreading their "Ribs" and opening new locations. I wish them the best and I will continue to be a regular at the original location.

I am here every 24 - 30 months so I figure, it was time to finally write a review. Seriously, I do not know how lucky I can get being called for Jury Duty every two to two and a half years on a regular basis. I do believe, I have definitely served my civic duty.   The ambiance of the waiting area is not plush, but you don't need to worry about the decor, you will not be there long. The most important thing to remember about Jury Duty, is to listen. The staff moves things along, very quickly and if they have to repeat themselves, that is when they get gruff. Otherwise, it is rather painless.   I brought magazines and both of my iPads, in preparation of a long wait. My start day was Wednesday, not the typical Monday so the selection pool wasn't as large. My number was called in the second group, so no time to play on iPad or read any magazine articles, because once you are in the courtroom all those items are taboo.  Once the Voir dire (jury selection) starts, that is when the real entertainment begins. My jury pool was 48 city residents and each and every one of them had some type of story. Some had more then one story, to share with the judge and lawyer. The selection process took close to a full 7 hours. During that time we did get a lunch break, of just over an hour. However, it made for a long day 8 AM - 5:30 PM.   I've served on one criminal, two civil (one as foreman) and one grand jury. I guess I had too much experience, because this time I was not selected to serve.

Six years? I haven't updated my review in, six years? How did I let this happen? I've got to get this corrected, now. I know I've posted updated pictures, but have forgotten to follow-up with an updated review. So, here it comes.   This past Thursday (September 20th) was National Pepperoni Pizza Day. I know that is a shock to some of you, but it true. One of the most popular pizzas in America has its' own special day. When I realized this "special day" existed, there was no doubt in my mind where I'd celebrate.   I stopped by after work to order a carry-out. As I waited for my 12" pie made with a tangy tomato sauce, fresh mozzarella cheese and slices of pepperoni covering the entire pizza, I enjoyed a Paul's Pils. Of course this refreshing craft beer is made by, Charleville Brewing Co. It so refreshing on a 95 degree day.   My pep pizza was perfect. I love their house tomato sauce and who wouldn't prefer mozzarella cheese over provel. It's also impressive that they cover the entire pizza in pepperoni. 12" is a nice size pie, so after eating a few slices, I had plenty left over for a work lunch and a snack the next night watching TV.   My service at the bar placing my carry-out order and enjoying my beer was typical of all the Hamilton Group restaurants. It was friendly, attentive and professional.   I'll be back? - Yes. Pizza, Wings, Salads and Beer - it's all good.   When: September 20, 2018  Why: National Pepperoni Pizza Day

This place is a hoot. I would have never discovered it if it were not for an Yelp event.  When I described this place to the So, I said it was like the child of a Waffle House and a Yogurt place. You order a waffle and then pick your toppings. How fun is that?  It is personalized just for you.   In addition to waffles, they offer flavorful lattes too. Their "Hair of the Dog" caught my eye. It's a fun take on Bloody Mary's, but in addition to Vodka, you can select your booze of choice as well. The fun doesn't end there, you can have a tall PBR in a brown bag. Appropriately called, "The Brown Bagger".  Seriously, do you want your friends to know you are drinking a PBR?   The staff is friendly and provides good attention to their guest. The ambiance is just this side of tacky. Afghans cover many of the seats and are even wrapped around the trees outside the restaurant. Are they tacky? Yes, but it adds to the charm of this Patch neighborhood waffle joint.   Want a waffle? Head to Melt and enjoy good times.

We had a plan, to arrive at Bogart's when it opened to have a fabulous BBQ lunch on site. Our plan backfired on us, because I did not check to see that they opened at 10:30AM instead of 11:00AM.  Who wants lunch at that time of the morning? Obviously a lot of people. When we arrived at 10:45AM, all the tables were filled and the line was ready to go out the door.  We got ours to go and enjoyed it at home.   In the Stevie B taste test, Bogart's wins the best BBQ in the city. I love their Brisket! I can enjoy it with just the rub or with their sweet sauce. If you love your BBQ hot and spicy, they have a sauce that is perfect for you. Their hot sauce will leave you with that burning feeling. (I'm a wimp, I mix the sweet & hot)  As usual, our sides were their amazing Pit Baked Beans and Deviled Egg Potato Salad. If the Golden Retriever who wants to sell the Bush's Baked Beans family recipe can get hold of this one, I will gladly pay him for it. The smokey flavor and thick texture, make these my favorite baked beans.  As stated in my previous review, all I want to say about the Potato Salad is, "more, please.".  The mixture of deviled eggs and potato make a farm boy happy.   A trip to Bogart's is not complete without taking a pound of their pastrami home. This time we could not wait, we were eating from the container on drive home. Peppery, smokey, juicy and tender. Jewish deli's should be jealous.   What sets Bogart's above Pappy's is the customer service. The staff here is friendly, upbeat and charming. They go out of their way to make you feel comfortable and welcomed. When you are there, you know that your business is appreciated.

A unique store in the heart of Soulard. You can buy home decor, fashion accessories and wine all in one stop and shop. What makes it even better, is that you #shoplocal and #shopsmall.   Every year since I discovered this gift shop back in 2012, it has been one of the first stops for my holiday shopping. I have always been able to check off several people on my list, especially the naughty ones.   If you haven't checked this store out, do so the next time you are eating at Bogarts or Mission Taco. You'll be glad that you did.   Would you come back? Yes, it's one of the best shops for creative gift giving.   When: December 9, 2016 Why: It's that time of year to gift shop.

Taco Circus is a mixture of a dive bar, greasy spoon, hole-in-wall and taco shack all combined into one. Combining all these atmospheres makes for a fun dining experience. I've had TC bookmarked for a long time, ever since Chip K. had the Review of The Day for it on New Year's Day 2016. Then in March, when Ian Froeb put it on his STL 100 List for 2016, I knew it was time to get up off my lazy ass and get to Taco Circus.  As I entered the circus, I was cheerfully greeted by the staff. When I walked up to the counter, the employee asked if this was my first time. I guess I had that lost boy look on my face. When I told him, yes and that I was there because they had made Ian Froeb's list. I told him I wanted a beef and chicken fajita taco. I didn't realize you could customize, so he led me through all my decisions. He recommended a flour tortilla with cilantro & onion on top. He also recommended the guacamole with chips. This man knew his stuff, he led me a delicious & filling lunch.   Both fajita tacos were good. I normally do not like cilantro, but I truly enjoyed it on both of these tacos. So much, that I didn't use any of the sauces. The onion, cilantro and the seasoning of the meat were enough for me. Ian said the beef was a must order, but for me I'd say the chicken is a must order.   However, I did enjoy all four of their sauces on my chips. I sat there trying each and everyone of them on single chips. I'd squeeze a little out on a chip as if I were adding ketchup to a large steak fry. My favorite is currently called; Burnie Sanders. It had a nice kick to it, with no after burn. The guacamole was creamy and smooth. I found the chips to be better and less salty then some of the more popular sit down Mexican restaurants.   Addresses are based on what street your front entrance faces - if their door faced the main drag instead of the side street it would be so much easier to find. Morgan Ford is a better known street, but with GPS in my CRV I was able to find this little taco delight with no trouble.   I'll be returning to try a Frito Pie, a Burrito and a breakfast taco as well.   For those of you who stay away from circuses because you are afraid of clowns, there are no clowns here. So come experience Taco Circus.

WTF! I had no idea, that Meatloaf was a breakfast meat, but I do now. H&H this Sunday was offering a Bacon Covered Meatloaf served with two sunny-side up eggs and potatoes. Their meatloaf was moist, juicy and the most flavorful I have had. I am sure the smoky flavor came from the crispy bacon that wrapped the loaf as if it were a gift. Diners who serve comfort food and proud themselves on their meatloaf should visit H&H to see how to truly serve MEATLOAF.   The SO enjoyed another unusual breakfast meat, Fried Chicken Livers. He too got to enjoy two sunny-side up eggs and potatoes. As a bonus he got a small side of tobacco onions and caper aioli. I not a regular fan of chicken livers, but my sampling of his has me reconsidering my taste buds.   We arrived only 30 minuets after opening and we still had a 20 minuet wait which went quickly. While we waited, we ordered and enjoyed Bloody Mary's with their signature fried pickle spear on top. I love their version, the pickle truly makes it their own.   I will say the only thing that keeps H&H from getting a 5 is the service. The service here always seems to be lacking. I understand they are busy and have to hustle, but if you can't keep up go get a job at a slower restaurant. Our waitress on this visit was cute, but had the personality of a wet wash rag. I think the management really needs to focus on customer service skills, they've nailed the cooking.

Five Below is novelty store that is affordable. You can find lots of unusual items and cheap candy.   Today, I was shopping for the dogs. Especially my little Princess. She recently had a sleep over at a friends house and had a blast playing with one of their huge balls. You know the kind, the type you played dodge ball with in elementary school. They had all different types, even colorful volley and basketballs. Perfect. They had just what I wanted and needed at a cheap price.   While I browsed the store, I found some real cute dog sweaters. If my dogs weren't full-coated, I would have embarrassed them by buying one or two.   Service here is the bare minimum, but hey you're pay a bare minimum price. My only interaction with an associate was at check-out and she was friendly. I left happy with my pink volleyball and a cold Diet Coke.   In the news, Five Below recently announced they'd be carrying items over $5 in the future. If it happens here, I guess we'll be seeing the $2 store soon.   Sprite hates her new ball! I guess it's more fun to play with someone else's then your own. I even bought it in her signature color, pink.   I'll be back? - I love a cheap deal.   When: November 15, 2019 Why: Sprite needed a ball

What a combination, Irish Pub and Fried Chicken and some of the best Fried Chicken in the city. The new spicy flavor gives a extra kick of flavor, but I prefer the original - it's as good as Grandma's. If you're eating fried food, you might as well splurge and have their livers or onion strings too. However, I recommend ordering hot sauce for dipping the livers. They provide cocktail sauce which I just find to be weird. Service is friendly & top-notch for a bar & grill.

Why has it taken me so long to experience SZVB? I mean it has been in the CWE for 13 years and I'm just now getting here. Seriously, what is/was wrong with me? I use to be a vodka drinker, before I discovered whiskey. Being that, I should of been a regular at this bar. Now that I've discovered it, I will not follow the advice of Elsa in Frozen and "Let it Go". I will now become a frequent visitor.   On my first visit, I had to sit at the famous "Frozen" bar. The bar has an "ice" strip going down the center of the bar. Such a great concept for a bar that is known for its sushi. It is also a great way to keep your cocktail chilled. Since I was having a burger, the bartender covered up the ice with a thick board like placemat.  It was lunch time and my weekend, so I started with a Bloody Mary made with Pepper-Infused Vodka. Infused with 4 peppers! It was a delicious Bloody Mary, but I wish they had their own mix instead of using Zing Zang. A house made mix would make it even better.   My burger was top notch! I love jalapeños, so I had to go with the Jalapeño Popper Burger. Not only did Aaron B's picture sell me on it, Carlton the bartender said it was his favorite. Mine was juicy and cooked perfectly to my favorite temperature of medium rare. The fries were crisp and came with a little cup of ketchup.   I agree with others, the combination of sushi and burgers at a restaurant bar are a weird combination, but somehow Sub Zero makes it work.   Will I return? Absolutely, they have many more jalapeño items on the menu.   When: October 2, 2017 Why: Lunch on my weekend

I've sold and I've bought from here numerous times, but most recently The Green Goose helped save me some major dollars.   During this pandemic, I decided it was time to move. I found a house I liked within an hour of it going on the market and I bought it within 36 hours. House bought, now to sell mine.  After some fluffing and staging my old house went on the market and sold within 48 hours. The selling and buying market was hot during the pandemic.   My dilemma, I was moving from a 950 sq. Ft. Bungalow to a 2200 sq. Ft. brick ranch home. I was gaining a second bedroom, formal dining room and a great room. I needed furniture.   I was able to split up my current living room furniture between the great room and living room at the new home. I just needed a few filler pieces to help me out. My new living room was huge and I had a lot of space to fill.  Lucky for me, I found two pairs of upholstered chairs that would coordinate with each other and a trunk that I could use as a table. I couldn't believe  the prices. They were so inexpensive and in excellent condition.   It took me two  trips with a small pick-up truck, but I got them moved to the new house in IL. As guest would come and see the new house, they would comment on the new chairs and could not believe they came from a Consignment shop.   If you haven't shopped at the Green Goose, you must check them out. They've got good merchandise and the service is attentive and helpful, too.   When: August 12, 2020 Why: Furniture for new home.

"This taste so good, I never want it to end." Those are the words of a friend who I took to Mac's for their first visit. He was totally blown away by how thin they smashed the burger and the crispy edges.  Then there were fries, he definitely preferred the Rip.   When we ordered, he followed my lead. We both enjoyed a Lumberjack. It's a two patty burger, with one beef and one pork. They top it with Pepper Jack Cheese, Bacon and all the traditional burger toppings of; Ketchup, Mustard, Pickle and onion. It is oh, so good. Having the mix of beef and pork is what makes the flavor of the burger, sensational.   Today, I took two of my IL cousins for their fist time and they too were equally impressed. They enjoyed, a Dirty Sancho and L.O.U.I.E. and an order of Rip Fries. It's so much fun bringing burger lovers here for their first time.   After eating at Mac's, I highly recommend that you check out their little retail store. There you'll find an endless variety of locally sourced items to stock your kitchen pantry. The young man who works the store is very knowledgeable in all the items and will talk passionately about them. Beware, his charming personality and his accent are part of his selling skills. (smile)  I'll be back? - Best burger in the city.   When: February 20 and March 27, 2019 Why: Taking first timers for lunch.

The best thing about Restaurant Week is no matter where they're held, is that you get to experience new restaurants at an affordable price. Currently, The Hill is having theirs and I took advantage of it and went to J Devoti Trattoria for my first time.   I have heard nothing but great things about JDT and how they are a true farm to table restaurant on The Hill. As my usual, I arrived and took a seat at the bar. The bartender (Jacob) immediately asked me if it was my first time dining. Once I told him yes, he begun sharing with how they are truly farm to table. He told me how they butcher in house and they have a garden on site and at the home of the chef who lives on The Hill, too.   The servings of the three course meal were small, they were the size you'd normally get with a tasting menu. What I liked about JDT, is that in addition to the printed special menu, they were offering off menu specials. I went off printed menu for two of my choices. The first was the, Housemade Spaghetti. Instead of the mushroom, they offered a pork ragu. The pasta was cooked al dente and the seasoning on the ragu was true Italian. The second course, I also went with the off menu special. They were offering my favorite seafood, Scallops. They served up two huge grilled sea scallops that melted in my mouth. Finally for the third course, I went with one of the desserts offered on the printed menu. I knew I could not go wrong with a Apple Handpie wit a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream.    In addition to the three courses, they surprised me with a sampling of their bread with a delicious spread. Sorry, I totally forgot what the spread was. Then at the end, they gave me a chocolate chip cookie that any high end bakery would be proud to serve.   The service was spectacular and the food impressive. Thanks to another Restaurant Week, I've discovered another great restaurant.   I'll be back? - Yes. I love farm to table.   When: April 24, 2019 Why: Restaurant Week on The Hill

It is time once again to announce a winner of a Stevie B Yelp Award for 2013. This category is Best Biscuits and Gravy and the nominees are; Goody Goody Diner, Southwest Diner, Billie's Fine Foods, City Diner and Uncle Bill's. Without further a due, the envelop please. The winner is, Billie's Fine Foods.   My friend Christian K. had the ROTD for Billie's Fine Foods one day last week and I thought it was time I checked it out and I am so glad that I did. They truly live up to their name, "Fine Foods". It may not be creative gourmet cuisine, but it delicious comfort food that will fill your tummy and put a smile on wallet.  I was raised on a farm and still have a true fondness for Biscuits and Gravy and Billie's does them right. They start out with big fluffy hand dropped biscuits and then drown them in thick white gravy filled with chunks of sausage. There is just something about an odd shaped biscuit that screams "house made".  Those perfectly shaped biscuits, that flake in layers just don't have the love and flavor of a hand dropped.   We were eating at "brunch" time on a Tuesday, so it was a late breakfast for me and an early lunch for the SO. I enjoyed the Meatloaf Omelet and the SO had Liver and Onions with Mashed Potatoes with Brown Gravy. The Meatloaf Omelet was good, but next time I think I'll go with a traditional Western or Mexican one. I was expecting chunks of Meatloaf through out the omelet, but instead it was a three egg omelet wrapped around an full thick slice of Meatloaf with American Potatoes tossed in. They then smothered the omelet in the same white gravy served on the biscuits. My diet was totally blown to hell this day.   When the SO ordered the Liver and Onions, he knew it was either going to be good or bad and it was "GOOD". I may be a farm boy, but I never have liked liver and onions. I will admit, Billie served up a good presentation. The mashed potatoes served as the side were red potatoes, and they left the skins on. I love mashed taters that still have the skins. The brown gravy was flavorful and I can imagine it on their open faced Roast Beef Sandwich.   The service was friendly, but slow. As the diner filled up for lunch the waitress got sidetracked in bringing our service to a close. There is no ambiance here, it truly is decorated in early greasy spoon.However, they do offer free Wi-FI.  I can only imagine what the late night crowd would look like after seeing the lunch clientele. Which was a mix of the cast from two movies, Deliverance and The Green Mile.   This place is so colorful, I'll be back and it is also being added to my "Breakfast of Champions" list.

Lola Jean's is a heartwarming little coffee shop. It basically is a pop-up, because in the new year it will become Lola Jean's Pizza and I'm looking forward to that switch over.   Right now, LJ is offering the delicious pastries from Russel's on Macklind and enjoy a cup of coffee from local roaster, Kaldi. What makes this little coffee shop so heartwarming is the fact that the profits from each month are donated to a local charity.   Bring a friend, relax and catch up on each others lives. Or, you can bring your laptop and catch up on that work you've putting off. You can do both of these things, in a very peaceful and relaxing atmosphere.   The menu is small, but keep in mind all the profits are giving back to our community.   I'll be back? - YES!  When: November 18, 2018 Why: It's a giveback coffee shop

This station has been open for almost 4 years and so many times gets written up as Amtrak or Greyhound Stations, when actually it is a shared station owned by the city. Saint Louis finally is getting caught up with other major cities and has created a transportation center. It is a station shared by trains, buses and Metro. It makes it easy for travelers to make connections when using multiple types of mass transportation. They can come in from Springfield, IL on Amtrak, hop on Metro to the airport and get a plane to New York and beyond.   I commend the city of Saint Louis for finally creating this type of station. It is centrally located downtown, just across the street from Scottrade Center. The station is open 24 hours and has a security staff and management on duty at all times making it a safe environment for all travelers.

My cousin had a holiday party on the 9th of December over in IL. As we were partying, we decided we'd allege out for brunch on Sunday. We selected, Square One as our destination to meet up. Whoops, none of us remembered that it was the Lafayette House Tour on that day. Which turned out to be okay. We did not partake in the house tour, but we got to enjoy all the other festivities.   As we waited for our table for Brunch, we got to go out and shop all the business who had tents set up in the square. Surprisingly we found gifts for people on our "nice" list. Once our table was ready, I received a text and back to Square One we strolled.   We had a group of five. Being a Yelper, my family has learned not to take a bite or disturb their plates until I have taken a picture. We started out with Bloody Mary's, Beer, a whiskey drink (missed that photo) and Mimosa's. How else do you begin a Brunch? The Bloody Mary's were all made with, Spirits of St. Louis Jalapeño Vodka. One cuz commented that she liked it. Guess who came back later and bought her a bottle for Christmas? TeeHee, you're right, I did.   Take note of all the photos. Pictures speak better then words sometimes.  My entree was the Chicken and Waffles. At a time in the past, I did not like tenders as my chicken when served with waffles. Now, I am actually preferring a boneless piece of chicken with my waffle. Square One serves up some good chicken on Sunday nights and this chicken & waffle was as equally good. The server offered me a side of two eggs for a minimal uncharge, which I took advantage of. Wrong! Once it all arrived, it was too much food. Good, but I was overly stuffed.   All the other entrees received thumbs up from those who ordered them.  From my observations, the 4 egg omelets are massive. The Huevos Rancheros looked good, and is a dish I will come back to try after I've had the Lox Bruschetta. Who needs a bagel when you can have your Lox on toasted french bread.   Another great thing about Square One, is that it is part of St. Louis Spirits. Being a family that loves whiskey, it was so easy to come here and pick-up a couple bottles to round out Christmas gifts for the cousins.   Will I return? - Burger, Mac-n-Cheese Nights. Fried Chicken Sunday are three reasons alone.   When: December 10 & 13, 2017 Why: Brunch and Gift Shopping

Love this Big Box hardware store. It may be a major chain, but the customer service is on par with a small town hardware store. Oh, wait it is a small town hardware store, that just happens to be a major chain.   Moving to the Alton area from the big city of STL, the first thing I noticed on entering this Home Depot was the cleanliness. The HD close to my home was always kinda grungy and unkept. This one is kept fairly clean and well organized.   The next thing that surprised me was the customer service. The associates here, actually approach you and ask if you need assistance. They don't avoid eye contact when you meet them in an aisle. The ones who have assisted me thus far have been knowledgeable in their given area.   A new feature that I've learned to take advantage of at this location, is ordering items on line that are available at this location and having them shipped to the customer service counter for pick-up. Damn, this makes life so much easier.   In the city, I was not a fan of HD, but this one is winning me over.   When: Multiple visits within the last 6 months.  Why: Bought a new house

LOVE IT!!!!  What a fantastic addition to the neighborhood.   I will admit that when I first saw the sign for a consignment shop coming, I rolled my eyes. I was not looking forward to a clothing consignment shop. A home furnishing shop is a whole different game.   The selection is great and all the items are in excellent condition. The ladies are very selective on the items they accept, keeping an upscale feel to the shop. They have everything from Love Seats, Leather Chairs, flatware, dining tables, and oh so much more.   Before shopping at Week-Ends Only or Rothmans, check out The Green Goose. Chances are that you will find a better quality item at a cheaper price.   While shopping, we asked if they had specific items and they knew exactly where they were and even was able to do suggestive selling as well. Great customer service in a consignment shop is a major plus!  So next time you are dining at Matthew's Kitchen or getting a Mystic Tan at the Tan Co. stop in and check out the Goose, you'll be glad that you did.

Did you know Square One serves up  fried chicken on Sunday? I didn't until it was mentioned in Catherine C's ROTD earlier this year. That is why it is good to always read the ROTD, you never know what new discoveries you'll find in our wonderful city.   This past Sunday, I finally got to remove my Bookmark for trying the fried chicken at Square One. I can tell you it is not a one time thing for me, it was so good that I already know I will be back. The chicken dinner  is three large pieces of crispy, juicy chicken, mixed steamed vegetables, Mac-n-Cheese and a Biscuit. It was a plateful of delicious food. So much, that I took the majority of my breast and biscuit home for lunch the next  day.   The chicken had a nice crispy coating, that you could easily taste the sage seasoning. The steamed veggies were a good mixture of broccoli and cauliflower with red pepper and onion. Only problem, it was cold. Everything else was piping hot, so I am not sure if this dish was intended to be served cold or not. It did not effect the taste and the vegetables were done to the right texture.   I enjoyed the Mac-n-Cheese, it was the traditional elbow pasta that you could tell was baked in the oven by its extra crunchy top. George my dining companion thought the biscuit was doughy, but I found it to be just fine. I may not have been flakey like some biscuits, but the gooey coating of honey drizzled on top made it finger licking good.   Normally I'd enjoy a glass of ice tea with a fried chicken meal, but this night I was craving a Bloody Mary. My Bloody Mary was made with their house distilled Jalapeño Vodka which was smooth as silk with a little kick ass burn. I loved it.   Square One is getting added to five of my Yelp list and that is an impressive accomplishment.

When ever I am in the Alton area and get the craving for custard, I head over to Shiver's for my fix. I especially get the craving when I drive by and see one of my favorite flavors on the marque as the featured flavor. Some how when I see Chocolate Malt, Yellow Cake Batter or Mint Chip on the sign, my car automatically pulls in. With autumn finally here, I can't wait to enjoy one of their Jack-O-Lantern Concretes.   If you're in the Alton area and your sweet tooth kicks in, head up to Godfrey and treat yourself to a frozen treat at Shiver's.

I've had a long love affair with Sidney Street Cafe that dates all the way back to the original owners and continued when Kevin took over. I may not eat here as often, as I would like, but it is still one of my favorite upscale restaurants in STL. It is so worthy of it's #3 ranking on Ian Froeb's STL 100 for 2016.   I was having a momentous birthday and all my family was out of town and my closest friends were also out of town. However, I was not going to let that stop me from celebrating or getting depressed about turning 60. I dressed a few notches above business causal and took myself to SSC. I have no problem eating at the bar. I always like a spot at the end and close to the wall. I like that location, because it's more private and I'm out of the way.   Peggy & Spencer were working the bar that Saturday night and did a fine job of making me and all the other diners at the bar feel welcomed and special. I was amazed at the number of folks that enjoyed their entire evening at the bar instead of moving to a table in the main restaurant. I guess others are on to the fun of staying at the bar for their meal.   I started my evening off with a Manhattan on the Rocks. To be honest, it wasn't one of the best Manhattans I've had, but I sipped it as I studied the appetizer menu. I already knew before arriving, that my entree was going to be the Sea Scallops. After discussing the Lobster Turnovers or the Poutine with Spencer, I choose the Lobster Turnovers. Absolutely delicious, it was Lobster wrapped in fillo dough with a tomato brandy reduction. There were three to the serving, enough to share or enough for a birthday man to eat all by himself.   The Manhattan was done, by the time the Turnovers arrived, so I needed a second drink. This time I asked Spencer how he made an Old Fashioned. He explained his process and it sounded good, so I ordered one. Way better then the Manhattan - Don Draper would have ordered a second one of these. Spence and Peggy knew I was in no hurry, so they asked when I was almost done with the turnovers if I wanted to put the Scallop order in now. I said, yes.   A house salad came with the Pan Seared Scallops, so I continued to enjoy my Old Fashioned with my salad. They did offer me a bread basket, which I declined. Spencer said so I wouldn't be so tempted to eat all the bread, he'd bring me one with only one piece. Nice - good  customer service. Fresh baked bread is always a good accompaniment to a salad.   When my scallops arrived, they were the talk of the bar. One lady couldn't believe they were scallops due to their black color. I then explained that was due to the lobster squid ink emulsion. The scallops also came with; caramelized brussel sprouts and sunchoke puree. I've never had a scallop that I didn't like, but I loved these. They are so worthy of a spot on my Scallops List.   I ended my night with a Grand Marnier bought by other diners at the bar for my birthday. How sweet is that, we had a great time sharing laughs. Spencer then brought me a Birthday Brownie with a scoop of vanilla ice cream that had a single candle in it. What a sweet ending to a scrumptious birthday dinner.   After eating my brownie, Spencer asked me if I still wanted to order the Apple dessert that I had deleted earlier in the evening. I told him, I was way to full and would have to enjoy it next time. I so did it tho, it sounded so good. It was Salted Caramel Creme Brulee, Caramel Apple Butter, Pickled Apple, Caramel Brown Butter Ice Cream.   Not taking a star away for this, but what confused me was that I was charged for the Birthday Brownie. I was not expecting anything free, but if you knew what dessert I truly wanted, why didn't you just put a candle on it instead? I would have just thought it was great customer service adding the candle to my dessert. Just saying......  When: November 12, 2016 Why: Celebration Dinner

I was watching Show-Me- St. Louis on Monday and they were doing a featured segment on The Muddled Pig Gastropub. While they were interviewing the two chefs, they talked about their Tuesday Special which is; a burger, beer and a shot of bourbon. I like those 3 B's so they had my attention.   When Tuesday rolled around and I was ready to start running errands, I made The Muddled Pig my first stop. I positioned myself at the bar, ready to enjoy a burger, beer and bourbon. You get to select your beer from any of the 4 Hands Brews that they currently have on their beer menu. I choose Single Speed. The bourbon, you've got to go with what they serve you and that is; Old Grand Dad Bonded Bourbon. I liked that they served it in a snifter instead of a shot glass. It makes for a better presentation and for me it made easier to add a few cubes of ice.   Now let's talk about the main B in the 3 B's, the burger. They grilled it perfectly to my specifications; medium rare. It was seasoned well, topped with cheddar cheese and bacon. The bun was lightly toasted and bigger in circumference then the burger. I like my burger to completely cover the bun. I would rather have a thinner burger that covers the entire bun, then to have a fatter burger that sits in the middle of a bun. Otherwise, the burger was fine. I just want full coverage of my bun.   To make it a complete lunch I added a side of their House Fries, which was served with their House Ketchup. My fries had skins on and were served hot and crispy. I enjoyed the smokey taste of the ketchup and that it came in a small squeeze bottle.   A Tuesday Special, + fries = affordable lunch with two alcoholic beverages. Total with taxes was only $14. What a deal.   When: July 12, 2016 Why: Tuesday Special as my lunch

I would have never discovered The Post if were not for a talk thread on Yelp. Everyone was sharing their favorite places in Maplewood and several mentioned The Post. I became curious, so one day I checked it out and now know what all the excitement is about. In fact, I already established myself as a regular with check-ins on my iPhone.   The Post offers some very good bar grub. I will say, they are #1 in my book for wings. Their wings are good size, meaty and very juicy. What I love is they offer for an additional 50¢ to bake your wings. After your wings are done like normal wings they give them a ride through the pizza oven. This bakes their fantastic and flavorful sauce into the wings and it also makes them less messy while eating.   On our first visit I was surprised to do my iPhone check-in and get a 20% off coupon on my entire bill. Now that is one hell of a Yelp deal.  We chowed down on wings, cheeseburgers and fries. I love bars that offer my favorite cheese on their burgers. No, I am not talking provel. I am talking about pepper cheese for that extra bang of flavor.  Our drinks of choice  were soda which gave us another surprise, they are served in plastic tumblers that you get to take home. When I got home, I washed mine and placed it next to my other souvenir glasses from the 2006 World Series and 1983 Miss Universe Pageant. I have a very varied collection.   The next visit was a dinner to experience their pizza. I have a hard enough time choosing my topping, now at The Post you need to select you crust. The Post offers 8 different types of crust. We choose Parmesan Peppercorn to complement the "Kitchen Sink"  toppings. We ordered a small size and it was enough for two, with enough leftovers for a next day lunch for one.   My only complaint about The Post is that there are not enough TVs to watch a sporting event. Ha Ha - just kidding. TVs are plentiful, and you have a great view from any chair or bar-stool in the restaurant.  Young ladies if you are looking for a hot man, go to  The Post on game night you will plenty to choose from. However, to get their attention from the TVs or their lap tops and fantasy teams may be a challenge.

IKEA definitely is a shop till you drop type store. This store has everything you'll ever need for your home. If you cannot find it at IKEA, chances are you may not need it. I have never been to an IKEA, so I was blown away by the massive variety and selections available. I was also amazed at the prices, they totally put discount retailers like Wal-Mart to shame.   Normally, I am not a fan of RTA (ready to assemble) furniture, but I think IKEA may win me over.  I like the fact that you can go to their website, click on the instructions for the item you are considering and see how difficult the assembly will be.   The housewares department is by far my favorite. So many gadgets and gizmos to make your kitchen complete. They also have a great selection of pots and pans, dishes and flatware. I was shocked to see that they also sell appliances. I fell in love with one of the gas ranges.   You may be able to shop till you drop here, but shop wisely and keep in mind, "You get what you pay for". The prices may be rock bottom low, but take a look at the quality before putting it in your cart.   IKEA is a great addition to the city, I'm glad they choose the city over a county location. It now gives those county residents another reason besides our sports teams to come downtown.  * My 900th Review on Yelp

Most of us have heard the song, "Thank heaven for little girls" from the Oscar winning film "Gigi". Well I am thankful that my neighbor has one who just turned six and had never been to The Magic House. What a great opportunity for an adult who has never been to TMH, but has always wanted to go.  As the Uncles next door, we grabbed this Brass Ring and took Terra and her mom out for a fun filled day at TMH.   We arrived around 10:30AM on Tuesday, which turned out to be perfect planning.  The closer it got to Noon, the more crowded it became. The young gentleman who sold us our tickets, shared a plan of attack for us. He made sure, we started our adventure on the Third Floor of the Purple Building before it got overly crowded. The third floor is popular, because that is where The ElectroStatic Generator is located. Every child wants to see their hair stand on end.   Terra had a blast visiting for her first time. One of her favorite things was the bubble room. One of the activities she got to stand on a disk and as we pulled a rope and she became enclosed inside a huge bubble. The picture came out great and it was so fun everyone cheered for each other. I think the parents were being competitive, seeing who could enclose their child in the best bubble.   She also enjoyed, climbing up the giant Jack in the Beanstalk Climber. Why use a normal staircase when you can climb a beanstalk just like Jack.  Then she had fun in the Oval Office and Courtroom. Not what we expected from her, but we're glad to see she has her eye on a bigger prize.   Being a fan of CSI and Law & Order, I personally had fun in the Forensic Lab and Can You Solve the Mystery rooms. Nailed, them. I know, it is geared towards children, but I still got the right answers.   If you have children, this is the place to take them. If you do not have a child, I suggest that you borrow one from a friend or family member so you yourself can experience the "MAGIC" of The Magic House.

A new adventure and a winning one at that.  I knew some of my most trusted Yelp friends gave it high-marks,  but I was still pleasantly surprised. I already know that I will be going back to experience the Roasted Cauliflower and Brussels Sprouts, plus the Spaghetti with Meatballs and the Lasagna. Seeing them pass by our table made me want to change my original order.   As we glanced over the menu, we were served warm complementary bread with olive oil and finely grated Parmesan cheese. The bread was so soft and flavorful, I had to resist when they offered to bring us more. Yes, we ate every bit of the original serving and would of loved more, but had to say  "No".  I liked how they served the olive oil and grated cheese in separate little ramekins. It made the dipping of the bread easier then smearing it on a plate.   Since this feast was a birthday celebration, I let the birthday man choose the appetizers and entree. He had us start out with Mussels and Calamari. Good choices, I was going to select the Mussels as my entree if I were picking on my own. Their Calamari is flash fried and was done so perfectly. I like the presentation, they do a dollop of tomato sauce on the plate then place the Calamari on top. However, I always do not like to dip mine in the sauce and with this presentation it was unavoidable.  Next time I will remember to ask for the sauce on the side.   The mussels were served in a black cast iron pot, that was extremely hot. I know that because, I touched it - ouch. The reason we ate our entire serving of bread, is that we dipped it in the white wine broth that our mussels were served in. A couple of the mussels were overcooked, but all were open. I hate it when you order mussels out and two or three in your pot are still closed. I just hate to see a mussel go to waste.   The 50 year old wanted pizza, so we shared a Sugo's which would be a meat lovers dream. It is a simple pie. It has minimal tomato sauce, that is covered in sausage, pepperoni, bacon and hamburger. Then topped with Mozzarella Cheese, that  was so gooey and  stretchy good. They probably should have gotten 5 Stars just for not using provel as their cheese.   When our pizza was served, we were ecstatic that it was actually cut in pie slices and not those stupid little squares. It was so huge as others have mentioned, we each only ate two slices and had four slices to take home providing each of us lunch for the next day.   The ambiance is a vast open room with a view of the kitchen. It is kind of fun to see the worker bees creating their masterpieces. I like the garage door that can be opened when the weather is permitting to connect the patio with the main dinning room. Our server Alicia was attentive and charming. I like it when a server ask you to return and tells you when they work so she can serve you again.  I shall return and I will be sure to request her as my server.

It is time to give out the first Stevie B  Yelp Award for 2013. My first award to be given out this year is, Best BBQ and the nominees are: Bogart's Smoke House, Pappy's Smokehouse, SugarFire Smoke House, Capitalist Pig and Southtown Pub.  The envelop please, and the best BBQ in Saint Louis is......SugarFire!!!!!!!!  We arrived for lunch at noon, the place was packed, but the line moved smoothly and the available seating turned quickly. We ordered, were served, ate and were back out the door within 40 minutes. That was a quick lunch and it was quality.  I am a fan of brisket and theirs absolute was the tenderest I have experienced in the Lou. So tender and moist, that a plastic fork could break off a bite size portion. I tried all the sauces, but the tangy House was the best. The 4 Bones were incredible, the dry rub was so good I didn't even try any of the sauces on the ribs. Again, tender meat making it easy to suck the bones clean.   Our sides dishes beat the other nominees hands down. The baked beans made me go weak in the knees. They were better then my momma's and she made some damn good beans. Rich thick sauce, and the beans still had a little bit of snap to them. The potato salad is the type your favorite aunt would bring to a family picnic on the 4th of July. It was a mustard potato salad, which is always better then a mayo.   The two star sides were the Mac-n-Cheese and Black Bean and Corn Salad. The BBCS, was light and refreshing and most likely the only side that actually was good for my diet. The cumin seasoning gave it a nice kick.  SugarFire knows how to do Mac-n-Cheese. They make it the old fashion way, they make it Mac-n-Cheese. Some other BBQ places try to make MnC frilly and fancy which just isn't necessary as a BBQ side.   I didn't get to try one of pies, but the slices on display looked like those you'd see at your hometown diner and for me that is a compliment. They have a wide range of beverages, from fountain soda, beer and adult milkshakes (they have booze).  For me the decision was easy, they had Frostie Root Beer as one of the fountain selections. It was a flashback to my childhood and those family picnics.   I live in the city, driving to SugarFire may be an extra two miles for me, and I may not be supporting a city biz, but I am still eating local from an independent locally owned restaurant.

On the 19th of February, Three Kings Public House was one of the amazing restaurants in the STL area that took part in the 1st Annual Dining out for Dogs. It was a fund raiser for the Humane Society of Missouri. I commend the TKPH for giving back to their community and supporting an organization that supports our Fur-Babies.   Three Kings has an impressive Pub Grub menu. I'm currently dieting so I could not enjoy it like I normally would. However, once I drop a few more pounds I will be back to enjoy it the way Pub Grub should be. I meet a couple of other Yelpers for a UYE here and their food looked totally amazing.   Dean B. and Angela S. shared an order of House-made Chips that looked better then those that I have seen at other Irish Pubs. They were sliced thin and fried crispy, I will be back to enjoy my own basket of those chips soon.  What separates TKPH from other pubs, is how they offer side dishes to their burgers and sandwiches. Most only offer you fries, but here you have multiple choices and a couple are actually healthy. You can choose between; Natural Cut Fries, Sweet Potato Fries, Sautéed Vegetable of the Day, Cole Slaw or a Small House Salad. This made me happy since I on a mission to lose weight.   I choose the All-American Burger with Pepper Jack Cheese and had them hold the bun. As my side I choose the Small House Salad with House Dressing. My burger was grilled medium well and the seasoning was flavorful. Yes, I would have loved a side of fries, but I was happy with my salad.   Dean B. made me jealous by ordering the Muffuletta. Another big bonus for TKPH is that they offer their Muffuletta a whole, half or quarter sandwich. Dean got a half and it was huge, two could have shared this sandwich and been content. His half was served in two quarters and he took one home for the next days lunch. As a side, he choose the Sweet Potato Fries. I did cheat and tried one of his fries and thought it was better then Pappy's. Dean thinks Pappy's makes a better Sweet Potato Fry.  He's entitled to his own opinion, it's a shame he is wrong.....LOL.   Angela S. enjoyed a Buffalo Chicken Wrap, which was a 12" flour tortilla stuffed with tender breaded chicken breast tossed with TKPH wing sauce, bleu cheese, shredded lettuce & tomato. It was huge and she too ended up taking half of hers home for lunch on the next day. With a lack of fried food, my brain is blocking what she choose as a side. I think it was Natural Cut Fries, but it could of been Cole Slaw.  Which ever it was, I know she enjoyed it.   Thank you, Three Kings for being a local business that supports a local charity.

Stopped by ABC for St. Louis Burger Week. Their offering was a Cowboy Burger. It was a savory 1/4 lb. tenderloin patty topped with a cracklin onion ring, applewood smoked bacon and house-made steak sauce. It was suppose to be served with a hand-cut spicy pickle spear, but I didn't get one. However, even without the pickle spear, this was a damn good burger. It was juicy and full of flavor. I really liked the big onion ring, it added extra crunch and kick to the burger.   As a side, I ordered the Shoestring Fries. They were crisp and served with just enough salt for flavor. Having a dislike of ketchup bottles in restaurants, I was thrilled to see they used little cups to serve just enough ketchup for your order of fries.    Of course, I couldn't go wrong with any of their beer selections on draft. I went with Fyler Flyer to accompany my burger. Then I saw what they recommended, Hop, Lock & Drop It Pale Ale. Wished my bartender would have recommended it, but that's another story. However, I like Fyler Flyer and have given it a 4 on Untappd.   So here's the story on the bartenders. They are the reason of a three star rating instead of a deserved 5. The service was a 2 Star experience. A wet bar rag has more personality then either of the two ladies working. They were boring, did not interact with any of the customers in the store. In fact, they were downright rude to one group of businessmen at a table. They were also evasive to the four of us sitting at the bar.  The best interaction was with the gentlemen who brought our food out from the kitchen.   I'll be back? - I'll give them another try, but if either bartender is on duty when I walk in, I'll turn around and walk back out.   When: August 2, 2019 Why: St. Louis Burger Week 2019

Be still my beating heart. I may have found a new love. I've discovered a restaurant that has three of my favorites and they do them all well. I'm besides myself with excitement and can't wait to tell you about it.   My inaugural  visit here was with the ISC (International Super Club). As my usual, I arrived early. This gives me an opportunity to relax at the bar before all the members arrive. Tonight I started out with one of their signature adult beverages.  One of my favorites is a Manhattan,  which we will talk about later.  However, their Heartbreak and Setbacks is kinda similar, so that is where I begun. The. Bonded Rye was smooth and being served on the rocks made a refreshing cocktail.    As I enjoyed my cocktail,  I munched on their Crab Avacado.  Once you have enjoyed this appetizer, it will be hard to go back to regular guacamole.  It's a smooth blend of avocado,tomato,onion and cilantro.   Then it is topped with shredded crab meat and served with lotus root chips. It's the perfect nosh while sipping a cocktail.   Somehow my H&S was gone before the appetizer and I needed a second adult beverage. For my next cocktail, I went with my favorite, a Manhattan. To test the masterfully skills of a barkeep, I take mine up. She nailed it. Happy boozer, here.   As our members arrived, we moved to our tables. Here I started out with another of my favorites, chicken wings. They were served crispy and the mix of lemongrass and Thai Chili, was a delicious mix of tangy and heat.  Before I could order my entree, Stevie needed another cocktail. #3 would be an Old Fasioned. Again, the young barkeep nailed it. It's good to see that in addition to being creative in mixing and creating new cocktails, they are still mastering the classics.     Finally, the piece of resistance of the whole night was the Bao Soft Shell Crab.  Soft shell crab is not only one of my favorites it is one of my weaknessess.  Whenever I see it on the menu it is a must have.  This is the first time I have had it on a bao  and I can honestly say it will not be the last.  I was expecting the softshell crab to be in pieces, but to my surprise it was one entire crab placed between the bao. I first enjoyed eating my way around the bao, experiencing the delicious soft shell crab. Then I ate the bao getting the full experience of the; eel sauce, masago, kaware and mayo. That is when I said, be still my beating heart. I was in love.    The ambience is extremely comfortable and modern. Their service is detailed, friendly and professional.  A combination that provides you a relaxing and enjoyable dining experience.   I'll be back? - Hell, yes.  They've got three of my favorites.  When - June 21, 2018 Why - International Supper Club

My car blew up and died, right when I was buying a new house and selling mine. The last thing I needed to do was also buy a new car all at the same time. So, I borrowed my cousins pick-up for a couple of months.   When everything had settled down, I took my cousins truck to Auto Butler for a good detailing before returning it.  The staff was friendly, professional and they did an excellent job. I was pleased with the vacuuming, clean windows and tires.  I normally read Yelp reviews before going to a business, but this time I didn't and I am kinda glad I didn't. If I had, I would not have gone. The experience I had was totally different from those posted. I now have my new ride and will be getting my RAV4 detailed here.   Will I return? - Gotta keep the new ride clean.   When: November 25, 2020 Why: Detailing my borrowed ride.

I'm a regular at the Webster Groves location now, but I still need to give a shout out to the location that started it all.   This visit was not about breakfast, it was about lunch. I arrived in time to snatch a barstool at the bar. Dining alone on a Wednesday has its advantages. I prefer the bar over the community high top, especially when I am alone. My personal space is more controlled at the bar.   I started my lunch off with a Dark & Stormy. Another advantage I had is being off on Wednesday, means I can drink at lunchtime. The D&S was so cool and refreshing. Served in a traditional tall collins glass, with a circular lime garnish. I got a giggle that took me back to my childhood. This adult beverage was served with a bendable straw. How cool is that.   My entree was a, Hot Fried Chicken Sandwich with Fries. I just could bring myself to order the breakfast potatoes as my side at lunchtime. The fries were a long slender cut and served hot & crisp. The HFC, reminded of Nashville Hot, but not as intense. At least for me, however it did have a few beads of sweat pop up on my forehead. It's served on a brioche bun with lettuce and a spread of aioli. Then it is garnished with one of their famous house pickles. Oh, so delicious. It was a nice switch up from a typical burger which is very good here as well.   Will I return? - Yes, for memories. Loyal to the Webster Groves location now.   When: Sometime in 2017 Why: Lunch Break while shopping in Clayton

I've never been to The Post late at night, or to watch a sports event. I've only been for lunch and for that it is a winner for me.   Why it is a winner? It is because I can get a big juicy burger with fries and a craft beer or an order of chicken wings - baked for that extra crispiness and a side of fries and of course, a craft beer. Either combination is a perfect lunch for a day off and a break from running errands. The Post is definitely a step up from the typical pub-grub sports bar food.   The service is always attentive and friendly. Sometimes I sit at the bar, but my usual go to is a high-top for two. It's a little more private and allows me a chance to get caught up on my social media.   There's countless number of TV screens, so if you want a bar to watch the big game and have some good food - I'd say, this is a place to go.

I was craving pizza and needed to satisfy it before my clean eating diet started in two days. Being at work, I took to Yelp to find the nearest pizza delivery. Papa came up first. At first I was concerned about two 1 star reviews, but when noticing how old they were, I went ahead and ordered.   Ordering on their website was easy. I selected a small Pepperoni and Meatball. It told me an approximate time of delivery and when it arrived, it was almost spot on. The delivery man was friendly and showed sincere appreciation for a cash tip instead of adding it to the charge.   The pizza however, was just average. It reminded me of why, I haven't ordered Papa John in awhile. When ordering, I even put his political views aside. I actually, like the sauce. It has a nice spice kick. The crust for me is too doughy.  I was also disappointed in my toppings. There could have been more cheese and pepperoni. The meatballs were tasty and plentiful.   This pizza satisfied my craving, but I was still disappointed. It's going to be awhile, before I have another pizza.......gotta get this extra weight off.   I'll be back? - I'll give them another chance, but not real soon.   When: March 12, 2019 Why: Had the crave for pizza

Five Below is a budget friendly novelty store. Everything in this store is priced in even dollar amounts and it's all under $5. Hence the name, Five Below.   It's amazing what you can find here. It's kinda like shopping at a TJ Maxx. You need to shop often, because the variety and selection of merchandise is constantly changing. You can find things for yourself, the kids, pets and the home. One of my best finds was a vegetable cookbook.   If you're a movie goer, the candy isle here is a perfect place to stock up on treats to enjoy while viewing the latest blockbuster. Why pay the the high prices at the movie theatre when you can fill your pockets or purse with bargain saving sweets from Five Below.   I'll be back? - See you at the movies.   When: April 23, 2018 Why: Bargain hunting.

Yes they have good sandwiches, but that is not why I visit LeGrand's. I go for their butcher counter and wood chips when it is grilling season.   Next time your in ordering a sandwich, take note of the quality meats and create something of your own.

OMG! The "Famous" Slider Mary is meal all by itself. It's a spicy hot Bloody Mary and has an, The All American slider as a garnish. That is right, a Slider is perched on a skewer towering high above your cocktail. Order a side of Fried Pickles, Parmesan Fries or Fried Green Tomatoes and you've got a light lunch. However, that is not what I did......I ordered more.   By chance I walked in on opening day.......a surprise to me, but it was a delightful surprise.  After being served one of the best Bloody Mary's and sampling the beef slider, I had to have more. I ordered the Slider Plate, which allows you to enjoy two regular sliders and 1 regular side. Being the King of Fried Pickles, I paid an additional $1 upgrade to have pickles instead of fries or house chips. The pickles were traditional dill pickle chips and only lightly dusted with a seasoned coating. I really liked that the taste of the pickle dominated the flavor instead of the breading which happens at so many other restaurants.   Now, let's talk sliders. The menu has a variety of beef sliders, just like any burger bar, the only difference is they are "sliders". They also had multiple chicken sliders, veggie sliders and for those who need gluten-free, they've got you covered as well. Since, I had the All-American with my Bloody Mary, I opted for The Classic Ruben and Nashville Hot Chicken as my two choices.   The Classic Ruben was the perfect size to go along with my fried pickles. It was served on a small pretzel bun and the corned beef is made in house. They topped it with big eye swiss, sauerkraut, caraway and 1000 Island Dressing. I love a good Ruben and this one hit the spot.   My Nashville Hot Chicken, surprised me. It actually lived up to its' name, "HOT". It may have had a burning sensation to it and definitely had me wiping my brow, but it got my curiosity up on how good their chicken wings may be. The Nashville Hot Chicken was hand breaded fried chicken, the piece was huge and hung out on all sides of the white slider bun. It was topped with coleslaw, pickle and that hot and tasty Nashville Secret Hot Sauce.   The service was extremly friendly and welcoming. Slider House is based in Nashville and it is apparent that they have brought Southern Hospitality with them. In addition to my server being bubbly sweet, others stopped by to get my opinion on the Bloody Mary and Fried Pickles.   This is going to be a great place for lunch, Happy Hour and business luncheons. It's going to be a restaurant for everyone, but this is definitely a mans restaurant. I see the Slider House being one of the Hot new openings of 2016.   When: February 24, 2016 Why: Lunch

My Godfrey cousins pointed out to me that I needed to update my Shivers review. They informed me a new owner/management had really turned things up. So while I was in town yesterday, I made it a point to stop by.   The flavor of the day was German Chocolate, the cousins admitted it was one of their favorites. So being a chocolate lover myself, I thought I'd give it a try. However, when I started to read the extensive menu, I saw Kit Kat and Dreamysicle, so I had a dilemma. After very little pondering, I went with Dreamysicle. After all, orange is my favorite color. It was refreshing as an orange sherbet, but made from a rich and creamy custard. The small size was a perfect serving. I could not imagine anyone eating a larger size.   The staff was extremely friendly and perky. At the time of my visit, they were extremely busy and I was impressed how quick they got all the orders out. A true sign of team work.   If you have a dog, bring them along to Shivers. When you bring your fur-baby, they get a free puppy cone. That's right, "FREE". I love places that are dog friendly and last night there were several pooches enjoying their cone.  Will I return? - Absolutely, I want a Kit Kat Concrete  When: June 25, 2017 Why: Sweet tooth attack and needed to update my review.

Once again, the International Supper Club pushed me out of my comfort zone. Which is a good thing. They got me to experience Lebanese cuisine and to visit a neighborhood that I do not frequent. All was good.   We had a group of 13 and Layla was able to accommodate us with a long table, in a side dining room. Lucky for us we had the room entirely to ourselves. Our waiter hustled as quickly as he could with a group that large. He smoothly went around the table taking orders and answered questions professionally.   When our food started to come out, there were some pauses in between the deliveries to the table. I think with such a large group, the kitchen did an okay job keeping up the pace. The pauses were not that large, just noticeable. Those who got their food first, dove in and started to enjoy.   I love lamb, so when I saw they had a lamb burger I knew what I wanted. A juicy medium rare lamb burger with, Mediterranean Pico, Tzatziki, Feta and Romaine was a winner. My side was their Seasoned Fries, which were crispy, crispy and came with a little cup of ketchup. We all know how I like my little cup of ketchup, I have a list dedicated to my appreciation.   I got a dessert to go, Gooey Butter Baklava. As they say on the menu, St. Louis meet Beirut. Some diners enjoyed it at the restaurant and had mixed comments. Once home, I got to sneak a bite before giving it to the roommate who was craving something sweet. I thought they did a great job on combining these two desserts into one. Layers of crispy paper thin dough layered with walnuts & brown sugar soaked in honey syrup and topped with Gooey Butter Cake. It then had a sprinkling of fresh mint on top which added a pop of flavor. The baklava was done well and the GBC could rival those that you get at Park Avenue Coffee.   Overall, I liked my first experience at Layla and would be happy to return to experience their menu in a smaller group or alone.  When: 11 FEB 2014 Why: International Supper Club

"The Square Beyond Compare"  and I'm not talking about no damn pizza with provel cheese. I am talking about the square biscuits you get at Russell's on Macklind  for Sunday Brunch.  5 made to order biscuits from scratch. Yes, made to order. They do not  make these incredible flaky and flavorful morning biscuits until you order them, so please be patient. It is well worth the wait.  I kicked back with one of their Bloody Mary's ($6.50). It was served in a Mason Jar rimmed with coarse salt and garnished with a stalk of celery.  I found it to be the perfect way to relax and people watch until my plate full of hot biscuits arrived.   My plate of 5 Biscuits ($5.95) was served with honey, whipped butter and preserves. Until my order arrived, I had no idea it was 5 biscuits. I was totally expecting only 2 and that was all I could eat. It truly is a dish to share with one of more friends.  The three biscuits I took home, were still great the next morning.  I am a fan of biscuits and gravy, but these biscuits are so good, they stand on their own. There is no need to smother them in gravy, they are the "square beyond compare".    Biscuits and a Bloody Mary may not be a healthy breakfast, but it was damn good.

I've been several times since my last update. What amazes me, is how this is well above average pub grub. I still kick myself in the a** for not eating here sooner.   Since my last review, I've done carryout twice and have been pleased with both. The first one was a pizza. I don't know about you all, but I love eating a pizza while watching the finale of The Biggest Loser. It just seems like the right thing to do.   I ordered a medium sausage and peperoni plus a dinner salad with that infamous white french dressing. Experiencing the "white french" a second time left me with a more favorable impression then my first dining experience. Their pizza is St Louis Style with the thin crust, cut into tiny squares. Toppings were plentiful and an even mix of both choices.  Their cheese fooled me. While eating I didn't think it was provel, I think with the combination of flavorful sauce and my topping it confused me.   My next carryout was a full rack of ribs on a Saturday night and a large Caesar Salad. Both were top notch. Their ribs are the meatiest ribs I have ever seen. Pappy's and Bogarts ribs do not come close to this much meat. The Cesar was huge and a typical "Hill" Caesar. We did Baked Potatoes at home and had a fantastic dinner.   When I picked up the ribs is when I discovered they use provel on the pizza. I asked one of the servers and she very proudly answered provel.  Oh well, it still tasted good and I'll eat it again.   Earlier this week Brad and I stopped in for lunch. The weather was great so we opted to take advantage of their outside seating. It's not a patio, it just out on the sidewalk, but you're outside.   We ordered burgers. I choose pepper cheese and traditional fries and Brad had Soft Cheddar and Waffle Fries. Both burgers were grilled well, not well in temperature. My pepper cheese melted better then his soft cheddar. They'd be off offering true cheddar instead of that scoop-able cheese.
