Loved my traditional fries, but the extra seasoning on the Waffle Fries was a surprise bonus.   The wait staff here is always friendly, giving it that neighborhood & family feeling. When I'm lazy, or can't think where to go, Biggies will be the first to come to mind.

You've heard of a dive bar. This is a dive deli and you'll love it just as you love your local dive bar. If it were not for a Meet-Up group, I would have never found this little mom & pop sandwich shop in The Patch neighborhood.   28 members of, Dudes, Dining and Dives descended on this small neighborly deli (They knew we were coming) for an amazing lunch.  Typically you'd order at the counter, but with our special group, we had our own waitress in a separate dining room. 28 diners vs 1 server and she won. I'll admit, there were a few bumps, but she and the sandwich building crew got them resolved quickly.  For my lunch I did a small side salad and 1/2 of Navy Chief. The salad was a good mix of iceberg and romaine lettuce, tossed with diced tomatoes, shredded provel cheese and  topped with parmesan cheese. When ever enjoying a salad out, I always go with the "house" dressing. Here, it was a flavorful vinaigrette.   Having a salad, I only ordered a half of a sandwich. I went with, The Navy Chief. Many of the deli sandwiches have a nautical theme name, which is apropo for the delis name. My Navy Chief had, salami, pepperoncini, pepper jack cheese and garnished with; tomato, onion, lettuce, pickle and provel cheese on toasted garlic bread. They are not stingy with the toppings, so I glad I went with a half - I was stuffed.   Only downside to RDPYC is that there is no view of the yachts coming and going from the docks. If they had the view, they'd definitely be a 5 Star deli.   I'll be back? - It's off the beaten path, but yes I'll return for a sammie.   When: January 23, 2018 Why: Lunch with large group

This review is all about the dog food. Wow! I was totally impressed with the huge variety and selection of dry and canned foods. They offer something for everyone and every budget.   If you buy just your everyday run of the mill dog food that is offered at a lower price point, they've got it for you. If you're the type who is picky, want USA made, grain-free, all natural food for your dog, they've got that for you, too.   The store is well maintained, it's clean, no odor and that is an amazing accomplishment for what I'd call a big box pet retailer.   I also found the staff to be attentive and friendly. My cashier was extremely polite and engaging with all customers.   I'll be back? - A simple, yes.   When: May 28, 2019 Why: Emergency Shop after work.

I'll admit, I am not a fan of RTA furniture. I'll buy it on occasion, but it's not my thing. However, one area that I love about IKEA is their home goods. When I shop their kitchen accessories, I can always find something and it will be at an affordable price.   Another thing that I put in my shopping cart at IKEA is the Cinnamon Rolls. They are so tasty for a weekend breakfast or even better, on Christmas morning.   One thing that IKEA does need to be praised for is their displays. How they tell you the square footage and then show you what can be done is so amazing and creative.   Why: New kitchen gadgets

I'm not a crafty person, but I still shop Michaels on occasion. Today, I found some cute Valentine items to complete the holiday look on my mantel. I even got a couple  of pieces for St. Patrick's Day. They were just starting to put the St. Pat's items out, so I may have to make a return visit.   Not being a craft person, I never know where to look for an item. I totally get lost, but it's easy to find an associate who can guide you. Today, I was looking for a large plate stand and the associate who I asked help from, gave better directions than Siri or Alexa.   What kept them from getting 4 stars, is that this store did not have the selection or variety that the St. Louis stores have. Hopefully, the amount of merchandise is due to the holiday just ending.   When: January 9, 2021 Why: Decorating Mantel for the next holidays

I recently attended a private event at the Fox and when I checked in on Yelp, it said it was my first check-in.  I immediately thought, "I don't think so", but then I realized that when attending the theatre, checking in on a social media website, it the last thing on my mind.   The Fox and I go way back, in fact I am proud to say I was there on opening night after the renovation. It was September 7, 1982 and the show was Barnum. That night was the beginning of my long love affair with, the "Fabulous Fox". Every time I enter the lobby, I hear the opening lines from the Bugs Bunny theme song in my head, "Overture, curtains, lights,  This is it, the night of nights". And every time, whether it is a Broadway show or a concert, I am never disappointed. The magic of the theatre is alive at the Fox.   The acoustics are better then Powell Hall. The sight lines from your seat are equal or better then some Broadway theaters in New York. I highly recommend taking the backstage tour and treat yourself to a pre or post show cocktail at the Curtain Call Lounge.   When: Countless Times Why: The Show Must Go On

With a ranking of #11 on Ian Froeb's STL 100 List, I was expecting to be blown away with an incredible Italian meal. I was not that impressed. Worthy of #11 or being in the top 25? No. Worthy of being in the top 100? Yes, but only in the alphabetical group of 75.   Arriving a half hour after they opened on a Sunday night and being a single diner, I opted to sit at the bar for my dining experience. There was a slight delay on the greeting and welcoming from the bartender, but that gave me time to glance over the drinks menu. A few of their house cocktails sounded very tempting. However, I went with my new regular standard cocktail, the classic Old Fashioned. He gave me the option of rye or bourbon and I choose bourbon. It wasn't one the better OF's I have enjoyed, but it went down smoothly.   I begun my feast with a Spinach Salad, which is larger enough for two to share or one to have as an entree.  The garnishes were plentiful, there were lots of pancetta, egg, cherries, shallot   and gorgonzola cheese. I liked that it was lightly dressed, so many restaurants over dress the salads. Also, the cherries provided a different tangy twist to the flavor.   For my entree, I went with Ian's "must order", the Pappardelle. It's a white bolognese with a cured egg yolk. The pasta was perfectly prepared al dente. I wish every time I ordered pasta out, that the noodles could be prepared this well. The white bolognese and the egg yolk, were the star of my meal. After the first couple of bites, I couldn't resit and had to break the yolk so it would run and blend into all the noodles. This was seasoned so well, I had not need or desire to add additional salt or pepper.   I decided to be a bad boy and have dessert for the second night in a row. Being a chocoholic, I ordered the Chocolate Torte. Major disappointment. An after dinner liquor or an ice cold glass of milk could not have improved this dessert. I thought the Mint Pistachio Brittle, would have made it interesting, but it was rather bland.   Randolfi's is a small space. I'd estimate they can sit approximately 50 diners at a given time counting those seated at the bar. The reason I am sharing this is, that I felt rushed. It was as if they wanted to turn my stool as quickly as possible. I wasn't going to loiter, I just wanted to enjoy a leisurely dinner after a long work week. I let them win, finished my meal and went home to my dogs.   Will I return? Yes, I definitely want to try a pizza and the scallops. Besides, I want to give them a second chance on customer service.   When: August 14, 2016 Why: Dinner & #11 on STL 100

What a major disappointment. I so wanted to like this nursery, but they dropped the ball big time.  They have Neiman - Marcus quality plants, but the customer service of a Family Dollar.   I am working on a major landscaping project and have been visiting all the major and small nurseries through out the metro area and this one by far was the worst. On the day I visited, it was the third out of five. I normally do not like to drop $ figures, but on this given day I spent between $100 - $400 at each nursery. I did not spend a blood cent at Greenscape.   When we arrived we asked if they had a specific plant, the two girls working the counter, were to busy talking and flirting with a young man who kept lift his shirt to show his belly. All they could do was point and tell us "down there, you'll see them".  Wow, all the other nurseries we shopped at took us to what we wanted and helped educate us on the needs and care of each plant. Not here, they just point and direct. I guess that is why they have such good signage so customers can wait on themselves. Why not put in self checkout too.   When we got to the area we needed, we did find another employee who must have been the "water boy" because he couldn't really answer any questions we had. He at least said, he was sorry for not knowing. We looked around a little more and left.   As we got into our car, I looked inside and the two girls were still behind the counter. I think they are trained like a dog with an invisible fence, and they can not get out from behind that counter. Keep in mind, we were the only people there besides the man flashing his belly and got not service what so ever.   I do not need to think I will not be back, I know I will not be back. Another addition to my No-No List.

Taco Circus's new location is definitely a three ring circus. The main ring of course is the bar area, with the other rings being a large dining room and huge colorful patio. I attended their soft opening and was luck enough to snag a seat at the bar and had a prime view entire show.   Let say first, I was impressed that all Margaritas are made from scratch. There are no mixes at this circus. I enjoyed a House Margarita and it was as fine and strong as a top shelf at many other local Mexican restaurants. I can't wait to go back and try the Circus Margarita and the Mexican Martini. The gentleman next to me had the martini and he raved about it.   To accompany my Margarita I had an order of chips and queso. They claim the queso blanco is the creamiest in town. I cannot confirm that, but it was thick and would cling to the thick chips making the dipping so much easier.  The chips were thicker then most and also a little more salty. I may hold the salt on the rim of my Margarita, but I'm a saltaholic, so I enjoyed the extra salty chips.   My main attraction was a Steak Quesadilla. They take two XXL 12 - inch tortillas and filled them with Skirt Steak and Cheese. It was so huge, I had to take half of it home. So this is a dish that could easily be shared. It was seasoned well and had plenty of cheese oozing out and around the good sized pieces of steak.   Considering it was a huge crowd and a soft opening, I think the staff and kitchen did a good job keeping up with the high volume. I'm looking forward to future visits once they have officially opened their, "circus".   I'll be back? - May be my new go to for Mexican.   When: September 12, 201 Why: Soft Opening at new location.

I normally do not like anything, small. However, a concrete is one thing I do enjoy being on the smaller size of things. It allows me to have a sweet treat and not worry about it bringing back all the weight I have lost. When it comes to frozen custard I have a weakness and very little self control. So Shivers, small size has me singing their praises and eating their custard.   When I announced to friends that I was moving east, they all told me I was going to miss Ted. My love affair with Ted ended love ago, for me it was Andy I hated leaving. My family on the east side, told me Shivers would fulfill my needs. I was doubtful, Andy not only made me heavier, he stole my heart. To my surprise, Shivers is pretty damn close. It's way better then Ted and is super close to Andy's. It's close enough to make me a regular and a new fan.   My go to at all custard stands is always the M&M. I like that they use the mini M&M's here. One of my favorite candy bars is a Kit Kat and I have never found it on the menu board at any other custard stand until now and it is going to be in my custard rotation. The pieces of Kit Kat were huge, cold and made my treat extra special. However, with only 4 visits since my move to Godfrey, I gotta say, the Dreamsicle is to die for and by far is my favorite thus far.   The staff is super-super friendly. They truly turn on the small town charm.  Using the drive-up or the walk up windows during COVID, the service is fast and safe.   Will I return? - Yes, I haven't tried the chocolate or strawberry custard.  When: September 18 and 23 October 1 and 3, 2020 Why: I do have a sweet tooth, every now and then.

New location, same great smash burgers!   National Cheeseburger Day was a great day to have a Grand Opening. Upon entering their new location, I could immediately see why they re-located. There was many more tables for diners, a nice patio and best of all - a craft brewery in the same space.   One upside of the new location is a larger kitchen and grill. Our burgers came out extremely fast. I barely had my beer from the bar and our delicious smash burgers were being served. The only downside, is that the lines to order your burger and fries is still extremely long. If you're coming for a work lunch, you'll be pressed for time. We waited in line close to 40 minutes, so I recommend you get yourself a pint or a flight to enjoy while you wait your turn to order. It is well worth the wait.   My smash for the Grand Opening was, The Lumberjack. It's made with two patties; one beef and one pork, with two cheeses; American and Pepper Jack. Then it was topped with my favorite toppings which are so simple; bacon, ketchup, mustard, onion and pickle. I don't need fancy toppings on my burger. Lumberjack is a classic.   The staff was friendly. A nicer touch to the new location is runners delivering the food to your table instead of getting a text from the kitchen. Having a table marker is so much better then a text.   Congratulations on your new location, Mac. I think you've got a winner.   I'll be back? - Yes, I'm a burger addict.   When: September 18, 2019 Why: Grand Opening Lunch

My dogs are big fans of Heritage Veterinary Hospital. They love Dr. Sanford and the entire staff from the receptionist to the vet techs. All of them are true dog and cat lovers and it shows in their bedside manner. Be it a regular check up or a serious issue, they are professional and compassionate.   Buddy, my boy dog was due for a dental cleaning and we recently discovered a sty on his right eye. Lucky for us, they were able to take care of both at the same time. Buddy's sty was not a typical sty, it was growing down and inward on his eyelid so it had to be removed. Buddy is feeling rather handsome since he had his teeth whitened and a eye tuck.   Modern technology is so cool these days. They took pictures before and after of his teeth so we could see the vast improvement. It has made those morning kisses fresher and more enjoyable. They also kept me informed through out the day of his progress with text and phone messages. Which put me at ease, because I am a worry wort doggie dad.   I am a true city man and I drive to the county for my dogs healthcare. I think that alone speaks volumes of the care you receive at Heritage Veterinary Hospital.

I have a fabulous looking living room thanks to the selection of furniture available at Slumberland. Do not get mislead by the name, like I was for many years. I'd shop at Costco and see Slumberland off in the distance and think it was a bedroom store, boy was I wrong.   Slumberland carries many top brands including Lazy Boy. What amazed me, is Slumberland offered lower prices on the exact same item that was on sale at the Lazy Boy store. Our sales professional Kathy was a true gem. She was so much fun to work with, while I created the look I wanted.  She listened intently to my needs and wants and showed me a love-seat that I would have overlooked in the showroom.   With me being a little anal retentive and a very visual person, she allowed me to move a few things around so I could see how my final selections would look together. My final purchase ended up being a love-seat, occasional chair, ottoman, two side tables, rug and two custom made toss pillows. My living looks like it is ready to be photographed by Better Homes and Garden.   My entertainment room is the next to be redecorated and I already have my eye on a few pieces at Slumberland.

What a great second location for the Green Goose. This larger space allows Robin and her friendly staff to show larger pieces of furniture that the cute smaller shop on Hampton could not accommodate. They have a larger variety of sectional sofas and dining room tables, that would be great for a young couple starting out.  Or that recent college grad furnishing an apartment, after landing a professional job.   If your an empty nester and down sizing, the Green Goose is the place to sell those larger or extra pieces of furniture that will not make the move with you to the new smaller home. You'll not only find a new home for your cherished furniture, but you'll put some extra $'s in your own pocket. Also, while you're selling yours', you just may find an item or two for your new home.   Selling or buying, the new Green Goose is a must stop for decorating a home.   When: September 23, 2013 Why: Always on the look-out for new home furnishings

Ooh, La La. These possibly may be my new favorite macarons.   I recently moved from STL city to the IL side and this past week-end had a few friends over for dinner. When they arrived, they gifted me a box of macarons. So, honestly I must say I have not been to Le Macaron myself, but I can testify that these six macrons rocked my world. When I finally ate the last one, my heart was broken. However, I knew I was going to STL this week for a Yelp event and could swing by Le Macaron and stock up on some more.   Their macarons were just the perfect amount of sweetness and each one had its own distinct flavor. I could easily name each one, without being told what flavor they were.   I can't wait to see their actual space and I'm thrilled that they are in an area that I frequent often.   I highly recommend you check this place out. I know I will, thanks to my friends getting me addicted to these perfectly delicious French delicacies.   When:  July 17, 2021  Why: Gift for hosting dinner party

WTH! I cannot believe I did not discover this place until I moved out of STL. So glad my friend Norma H. wanted to have her celebratory birthday lunch here, otherwise I'd still be in the dark. What stumps me the most is, I use to shop the PetsMart and Office Depot next-door and I didn't even notice this bar.  Yes, it's a dive bar/sports bar, but the quality of food and drink was far beyond my expectations. My Buffalo Chicken Sandwich was better then some I have had at well known sports bars in the city and county. It had just enough spicy kick and the breast was tender. The skinny fries as side were crispy, just how I like them. Norma's wings were not breaded, the way she likes them and they were accommodating by putting the hot sauce on the side along with the Blu Cheese.   I guess I should have known better going into a dive bar and requesting a Manhattan. The bartender was up front and told me they didn't have sweet vermouth, so I passed and asked if she could do a Dirty Martini. That she could do and I'll tell you, it was one of the best I have had in awhile. It was so good, it turned out to be a "3" martini lunch.   Cary was the bartender and server and she was doing a great job covering the entire bar. She had a good crowd sitting around the U-Shaped bar and another table or two besides us.   Bomber O'Brien's is a well kept secret of south city. It's in what is now being referred to as, The Crown District and it's definitely a jewel in that crown. Your dollars will go a lot further here and you'll get more bang for the buck.   When: 26 May, 2021 Why: Friends Birthday Lunch

Boo-Hiss!   I came to celebrate, National Egg McMuffin Day and was totally disappointed. It was a time you'd think they'd have their A-Game going, but they did not. I went through the drive-thru about, 6:45AM.   Since I was there to celebrate their special day and I am sure they're the ones who created it, I ordered the Breakfast Combo #1 which is the Egg McMuffin.  My drive to work is less then 5 minutes from the restaurant and my food was ice cold. The Canadian Bacon was tough and chewy. The best thing out of the combo was the cup of coffee. It was hot and strong.   The service was questionable. I wished them a Happy Egg McMuffin Day and neither the money taker or the one passing out the food at the next window, seemed to know what day it was. You'd think they would be the ones to be extending the celebratory greeting.   I'll give them another try, because I do like their Double Cheeseburgers on occasion, but my experience on Egg McMuffin Day is a solid #2. Yes, I meant the grade school humor in closing.   When: March 2, 2021 Why: National Egg McMuffin Day

Who needs Red Robin and their bottomless fries, when you have Stacked STL in your hometown? You don't. Stacked STL, will make you a better burger and the serving of fries is large enough that you'll never need to ask for a second serving.  I have a love for a little hot pepper called, "Jalapeño" and their burger; En Fuego has stollen my heart. A big juicy burger topped with my favorite cheese; Pepper Jack and covered in breaded Jalapeños. As if that isn't enough, they drizzle it with Chipotle Aioli. My second favorite is, The Goat. It's a simple burger served with melted Goat Cheese and topped with an onion jam.  Their fries are made from Russet potatoes with the skins on and fried crisp and seasoned well. As mentioned in my opening, the serving is so large, I can never finish them all.  Stacked STL offers an extensive offerings of cold craft beers, that are the perfect accompaniment to two of my favorite appetizers. My personal favorite is Fried Pickles. If not in the mood for pickles, I go with Garlic Butter Chicken Wings. Either way they are winners.   The ambiance is very causal and relaxing. The service is personable and friendly, they treat everyone as family. It is ambiance, service and mostly the juicy burgers that keeps me coming back.

The Gramophone is a peculiar little sandwich shop and that is a good thing. It reminded me of coffeehouse in the 1970's. The crowd was very eclectic, which is part of it's charm and comes from it being located in, The Grove.   I stopped by for lunch on a Friday. As I walked in, a young lady was playing an upright piano on a raised stage in the front window. Hence, the flashback to a 1970's coffeehouse. She was tickling the ivories with vintage songs that only our grandparents and great- grandparents would know. It added to the vibe of the shop.   It's a simple process here. As you enter, one of the staff yells to you (in a friendly tone and matter) where the menus are and where to place your order when ready. I already knew what I wanted, I had read Yelp reviews and was going on the recommendations of Max R. and Midori G.. Max, highly recommends the, "Jive" and Midori loves the Mac-n-Cheese.   Somewhere, I read a half is enough, so I only ordered a half sandwich. Whoever said is, is right. Half a sammie with a side is more then enough for lunch. Max was so right, I loved my Jive. It was a perfect blend of; turkey, bacon, swiss and the avocado spread and pepper mayo were perfect condiments. However, I did not have the same love as Midori for the mac-n-cheese. It was creamy, but I found its flavor to be bland. I did like the crumpled bbq chips on top.   Once you've placed your order, you're given a table marker with a number so the runners can find you. The staff is friendly and the runners were kept busy. I didn't take note if it's a full bar service, but they had a good selection of craft beers.   Side note: I was the only one there without a visible tattoo and I was old enough to be everyones grandfather. Made me giggle.   I'll be back? - Yes, I want the People's Pastrami   When: May 24, 2019 Why: It was lunchtime.

What? I cannot believe the other reviews here have not mentioned their amazingly delicious pies. How can anyone go here and not have dessert, is beyond me?   I hosted a small gathering of cousins for a Christmas dinner and one of my cousins brought two pies for dessert. She knew my favorite pie is Pecan, so it was one of them and the other was Lemon. She dropped them off at my house the day before Christmas. Having a freshly baked pecan pie in my house was a huge temptation. I had to use all my strength, I wanted a slice so bad. Christmas Day could not get here any faster. I wanted that pie.   Once we were done with dinner and our gift exchange, it was dessert time and you know what I wanted. I've enjoyed a lot slices of Pecan Pie in my day and I will say, this is one of the best if not the best I have eaten. Another one of cousins who attended our holiday dinner raved about the Lemon pie.   If their pie is this good, I cannot wait to go and experience their lunches. The cousin who brought the pies, is a semi-regular diner, so I will tagging along with her for a lunch in 2021.   When: Christmas Day Why: Dessert for holiday dinner

Ian Froeb rated Pataria #10 on his STL 100 List for 2016 and it is well deserved. The only reason I am giving them 4 Stars is because they only offer their vegetables as a side dish after 5 PM. I want those scrumptious Roasted Brussels Sprouts for lunch. They're roasted in olive oil and chili making this my favorite place to have my favorite veggie.   Moving on to the other amazing dishes here at Pastaria. The Shaved Kale salad comes in two sizes. You can order small and enjoy it as a lead in to your entree or order the large size and have it as an entree. Either way it is a win-win. I wish they bottled the creamy anchovy dressing. I'd do almost anything to have it in my ice box at home.   I've enjoyed two different pizzas; the Salume Beddu Nduja which Ian recommends as his "must order" and the classic Margherita. If you like spicy sausage, then trying the SBN is a must for you. It looks like a typical sausage pizza, but once you sink your teeth into  it, you'll realize it is a life changing pizza. The Margherita with its' fresh basil on top of mozzarella cheese sets it far above any other pizza in town. It's simple, yet flavorful.   Forgive me for losing my notes on the lasagna I enjoyed. If my memory serves me correctly, it was a pesto. Whatever it was, I remember the noodles were done perfectly al dente and that I was wiping the bowl clean with the complimentary bread which is oh, so fresh.   Normally, I drink a draft beer when dining at Pastaria, but on my last visit I ordered my go to cocktail; an Old Fashioned. They bartender did an excellent job, proving to me that the bartenders are a masterful and the chefs in the kitchen.   I've never sat at a table here at Pastaria, I always remain at the bar. It's easier that way when you are a single diner. On my next visit I plan to sit at the chefs table and watch the preparation of all the food.   Would I come back? Is the Pope Catholic?  When: Most recently; August 6 and October 7, 2016 Why: It's Italian and Ian Froeb's STL 100

Once you start shopping at The Green Goose you will realize how fun it is to shop at consignment stores and how many $'s you can save. For me it has become a very repetitive behavior, I bounce back and forth between selling and buying at TGG. I love the Love Seat I bought at TGG, it is so comfy for watching TV.   If you have a tight budget this holiday season, I highly recommend TGG for your gift shopping. I was there today and the selection was amazing. They had all types of framed art work, mirrors, decorative home accessories and so much more. You can even find Christmas decorations to make your own home festive for the holidays.   Another great thing about a consignment shop is that they can help you sell your "stuff". Selling through a consignment shop gives you more customer traffic then you'd get having your own yard sale. It also, allows you to actually get what the item is truly worth. When you take your items into TGG they'll work with you on pricing your merchandise. Keep in mind  they get a percentage when your item sells, but it is well worth it. After all, they did the merchandising and their sales associates provided the customer service.   If you've taken then the Yelp Pledge to Shop Local, The Green Goose would be a great place to start.

OMG! This was totally not what I was expecting. To be honest, I didn't check Yelp before going. I have two friends who check-in here on Yelp semi-regularly so I thought I was good to go. When I entered and saw all the servers dressed as if they were doing a fashion show for Victoria Secrets, I was a little taken back. The two friends who frequent here, play for the other team if you get my drift. If they come here on the regular, I knew the food had to be good.   I had to circle the first bar area twice, before a seat opened up. Yes, it was that packed at lunchtime. Why wouldn't it be, with the special uniforms the ladies were wearing for Valentine's week. The service was still attentive and friendly. For me watching the ladies was fun, they knew who to flirt with for that extra tip and who to be more demure. Nice.   I started my experience off with a, Dirty Blonde Beer. It's exclusive to Twin Peaks and is made by a favorite craft brewery, Schlafly. I wanted a light lunch, so as I sat at the enjoying my icy cold beer I finally did check Yelp for ideas of what to order. Friends and others sang the praises of the Chicken Wings and they were oh, so right.   I ordered the Lemon Pepper wings and had them Smoked and Grilled on the recommendation of the bartender. I only ordered 6, but you can also get 12 or 18 in an order. For 99cents more, I got a side of fries as a side. These wings were the bomb. I'm almost willing to say, they're now my favorite in STL.  They were meaty and equally portioned, 3 flats and 3 drummies to my order. The fries were crisp and seasoned with both salt and pepper. I'm a big pepper fan, so it was nice to see they season their fries with both spices.  Shocked, but not put off by the special Valentine's uniform. So now I gotta come back and see what the regular attire is. Just on a side note, I don't think this would be a place to dine with young children. This is definitely a place for adults to have fun.   Chances of returning? - I want to try some spicy wings and a burger.   When: February 13, 2019 Why: Lunch

Location Alert - MLE is located inside Tamm Ave Bar.   Once you've made it inside, Mac's ordering window is in the center room. You'll order and pay for your food at the same time. If you want a beverage, you'll then have to see the bartender at TAB. Both are separate businesses and operate individually. Yes, it is a pain in the ass. However, it is worth dealing with to enjoy this bodacious burger joint.   I love flat grilled, diner style burgers and MLE takes them to another level. I altered the Dirty Sancho, instead of two pork patties, I went for beef and they had no problem accommodating my changes. Their toppings are my go to for a burger, so I was ready to go - Pepper Jack Cheese, Onion and Pickled Jalapeños. It was delicious. I also had to try the, Riplet Fries. Crisp, fries seasoned with the same seasoning as STL famous Red Hot Riplet Potato Chips. It's better on fries, then it is on a potato chips.   There's no ambiance. It's rustic, beat-up and a minimalist would even want to add to the decor. However, you're not there for atmosphere, you're dining for a bodacious burger.   The service from MLE, is very hospitable and friendly. The service from TAB could be better, but it is what it is and I still got a cold craft beer.   I'll be back? - Yep. I may even host a UYE here.   When: January 31, 2018 Why: Wanted to experience the burger

I've been five times myself and once for a party. I think it is time to a review.   Every Christmas for the last couple of years Santa has been bringing me a, "Box of Chocolate" and I am not talking Godiva. I'm talking a Charleville beer. That was all I knew them for, so I've been exploring many more of their craft beers and haven't been disappointed.   Let's start with first impressions. Once you enter you'll instantly feel relaxed in this beautiful bar. I love the natural wood and almost rustic feel. No high-tech, modern decor. It is down-home comfy, the way I want to feel as I sip on an ice cold craft beer. I even like the art on the walls. Some are my favorite quotes that I use, often.   Now, let me tell you about the food. I'll make this simple, by doing a list.   Spiced Tortilla Chips with Cheese Sauce - Order it. The chips are spicy, fresh and the right amount of saltiness to accompany a cold beer. Also, the cheese sauce adds to the flavor. (Chips are better then some fast Tex-Mex restaurants)  Hand Cut Fries - No frozen from a bag here. It is so obvious they are hand-cut. They are crisp, plentiful and served with a little cup of ketchup. This is another, order it. A perfect nosh for mindless eating while drinking beer.   Bacon Wrapped Meatloaf - Seriously? It's meatloaf and it's bacon wrapped what is there not to like. I don't make meatloaf at home, so when I crave it, I'll be heading here.   Mac-n-Cheese - They use Rotini noodles which is my favorite for Mac. The cheese was rich and creamy, but could have covered the noodles a little more. Bonus point for serving it in a small black cast iron skillet.   Chicken Wings - Another food that is perfect for the beer drinker. They're beer brined, fried and tossed in a Buffalo sauce. Be still my beating heart.   Fried Catfish - It's Cornmeal dusted and fried. Who needs the road trip to Grafton when this is available.   Ambiance and food gets them a solid 4 Stars. I'm sure in due time, they'll reach a 5 Star rating. What's holding them back? Service. Oh, don't get me wrong, it is attentive and friendly. It is that when I sit at the bar, I feel as if the bartender is rushing me to move on. I've been at a table once and didn't feel rushed. Being single and dining and drinking alone, I prefer the bar so I do not tie-up a table that can accommodate more patrons. Just let me relax and enjoy my down time and you'll get your 5th star.  Will I return? - I've already been back 5 times  When: 5/24 & 28, 6/10, 8/15, 10/1/17 Why: Dinner & Craft Beer

Tucker's Place is a great steakhouse. It's also a great restaurant to celebrate special occasions. A group of us Yelpers came here to celebrate the retirement and farewell of fellow Yelper, Paul K.. We're all going to miss him and this was one of his favorite restaurants in STL.  I've always been a fan of the Soulard location and now I can see why Paul has been a fan of this West County location.   As per my usual behavior, I arrived early. I hate arriving to any event or occasion late.  I made myself comfortable at the end of the bar. The bartender was friendly and greeted my promptly. I requested an Old Fashioned and enjoyed it as I waited for my other friends to arrive. It takes a true talent to make a good OF, this bartender fell short. I was not that impressed. When I got seated at our table, I ordered a Manhattan and she made  it much, better.   Several of us bought various appetizers for sharing. Being a fan of chicken wings, I treated everyone to two orders. They were fried and tossed in a mild buffalo sauce. I was glad they weren't too hot, so everyone got to enjoy.   My meal of the night was a 10 oz Sirloin. It came with a house salad, I always choose their house dressing. I love it, in fact I buy at the grocery store and have a bottle in my refrigerator at all times. I wanted veggies as my side, but was brought a plain baked potato. Our waiter was doing a decent job for the size of our party, so I just went with the flow. I've always enjoyed their potatoes, crisp skins and the inside is so fluffy. All I need to add is butter, a shake or two of salt and freshly ground black pepper and it's seasoned perfectly.   The sirloin was grilled to my specifications, medium-rare. It wasn't overly seasoned, so I got to enjoy the true flavor of the beef. It's not the prime steak that you'd find at a true upscale steakhouse, but for $15.95 it is a great value.   Would I return? If I'm in West County, but I live much closer to the Soulard one.   When: January 9, 2016 Why: Special Occasion Dinner

I am thrilled that I finally found out about this chocolatier. She (Meggie) currently does not have a brick and mortar store, but she's working on it. She currently is only doing website sales and pop-ups at various venues throughout the city and county. Her chocolates are not only delicious, but they are beautiful as well.   All of my Valentine's gifts came from Bijoux this year. I took various sized gift boxes to my, dentist, hairstylist,  2 BFF's and my dogs even gave a box to their groomer. I can honestly tell you, each of the recipients raved about the chocolates once they tried them. Her beautiful Bon Bons come in box sizes; 4,6,12 and 24.   I can also tell you, Bijoux makes some amazing toffee. I personally had the Salted Almond and loved it. I bought the Cinnamon Pecan for a BFF and she swears she's now addicted to it.   Bijoux was featured in Feast Magazine in October 2018. I missed the article and had to travel to Columbia, MO for a birthday party on January 28th to find out about these chocolates. I don't want you to miss out like I did. So, until Meggie has a brick and mortar, I highly recommend that you check out her website and also check her posted schedule of monthly pop-ups. These chocolates are not to be missed. They're all handcrafted and made in small batches.   Chances of returning? - I'm a chocoholic, it's a given.   When: I've placed three different orders in February  Why: Fabulous Bon-Bon's

Get out your crayons and color me surprised. This planting season, I searched high and low for plants, new pots and potting soil. After visiting many of my favorite nurseries, I ended up here at Menards and was shocked that they had some of the best offerings and definitely the lowest prices.   My new advice to shoppers who are searching for an hard to find item - Check out Menards, they just might surprise you. They colored me surprised.   Well I return? -Yep, I never know what I will find.   When: May 10, 2017  Why: Patio needed new plants.

Major disappointment. If it were not for #CareyKStrong, I would have given them a 2 Star rating.   I came for breakfast want to show my support for the #CareyKStrong movement in my new neighborhood. In my opinion, breakfast is one of the hardest meals to screw-up, but Joe K's managed to do it.  I love a hearty breakfast. Having a big breakfast, I can usually skip lunch and have an early dinner. The morning of my visit, I ordered the, Hungry Man Breakfast . I had my choice of meats, I choose, bacon. It came with two eggs, I had mine fried hard with the yolks broken. For my potatoes, I requested my Hash Browns be done extra crispy and instead of toast, I paid the uncharge for $ sized pancakes.   Positives of the entree; the pancakes were full sized, not what a city man would call $ sized and they were fluffy and good flavor. My eggs were also done as I requested and none of the food was overly seasoned with salt or pepper. Also, the coffee was very good and the servers made sure my cup was always full.   The negatives are, cold, chewy and twisted bacon. I mean, ice cold. I know a lot of diners prepare bacon in advance to make things easier and faster, but this bacon tasted as if it were from the day before. My Hash Browns were not extra crispy, they were not even semi crisp. They too, were cold like the potatoes you'd get on a buffet line.   The service was attentive and they were all wearing masking. The tables were spaced for social distancing, but they did not skip booths, so those dining in a booth were right next to each other.   I'll give them another try, because I've heard the lunches are very good. I not only want to support a local diner, but I want to support the #CareyKStrong fundraiser as well.   When: January 14, 2020 Why: Breakfast

I can finally mark it off my Bucket List. I attended a wedding at The Jewel Box.   A wedding at the JB is very compact and romantic. The beauty of the plants and the historic greenhouse adds to the ambiance.  The acoustics are surprisingly good, making it easy to hear the ceremony and the string quartet. At the beginning, it wasn't too warm in the box. However, as the ceremony progressed, I did start to feel the warmth of the greenhouse.   In my opinion, the true beauty at The Jewel Box is the grounds that surround the vintage greenhouse. The manmade ponds,  landscaping and sculptures are truly a beautiful sight. They are all maintained so well. It is why TJB is considered a true "jewel" of Forest Park.   The only downside of having a wedding at The Jewel Box is the time limitations. They keep you on a very tight schedule. They only unlock the doors shortly before the ceremony for guest and when the service is over, it is hustle and bustle to get out.

This Steak n Shake has always been consistently good for me. I've done breakfast, lunch and mostly TAKHOMASAC from this location.  My most recent visit was another carry out order of 2 cheeseburgers with everything, 2 orders of regular french fries and 2 milk shakes; 1 banana and 1 strawberry.   When I approached the counter, I was cheerfully greeted by a manager who took my order and processed my coupon. He told me my order would be ready in a moment. I barely had time to sit down on available stool, get my iPhone ready to check in on Yelp and a young waitress walks up and says, "did you have 2 cheeseburgers and fries?"  I was in shock, this could not be my order. How could it be ready that fast? I said, "Yes, but I also had two shakes." She responded, "A banana and strawberry. They'll be here soon. " Still in amazement I said, "okay, thanks".  I then finished checking in on Yelp and she was back with my shakes.  Wow! That was some fast carryout. Another fast food joint down Hampton with Golden Arches can't put food out that fast.  Once the food was home, everything was made to order and was the perfect easy meal for a night of TV. SNS knows how to do fast food fast.

Bumping you up a star, SB BBQ. You're now A-Okay.  You're not my favorite BBQ in STL, but you're a great neighborhood restaurant. On my most recent visit, I was impressed by the comradery that was felt in the restaurant.  The servers were shouting out and calling customers by name and asking about family members who were not in attendance.  It gave a warm fuzzy feeling. Being kind of a newbie, they all reached out to me as well and made sure I felt equally as welcome.   This time around I enjoyed another Two Meat Combo. My last visit, I learned with a sampling of Turkey that was one of the meats to order. It did not disappoint, it was tender and smoked just right. My favorite sauce was, Texas Spicy. It added just the perfect kick, to the smokey bird. For my second meat, I gave the Brisket a second chance. This time it wasn't dry like my previous visit, but it was still a little tough.   My combo came with two sides; green beans and mac-n-cheese. The mac-n-cheese has improved drastically from my first visit. It was creamier, cheesier and much less garlic flavoring. It was a pleasant side, that I'd enjoy again. The green beans, were summer fresh, yummy. A vegetarian could come here just for this side dish. I could do without the Texas Toast. I'm not a bread man, but this TT is impressive and a nice touch to a combo plate.   Smoking Barrels, I'm glad to see your food has improved and I hope it continues on. Also, your customer service, truly gives a warm hospitality feeling. Last time I didn't think I'd be back, but I wanted to give you a second chance. This time I know I'll be for more of that neighborhood feeling.   When: June 12, 2016 Why: Dinner & Update review

Free WI-FI and Special Menu for those who are 55+.   Worst service I have ever experienced, or should I say NO SERVICE. We arrived shortly after 10 AM. The only words we heard from the hostess was, "Follow me".  She walked us to our table, tossed the menu down and told us our server would be with us shortly. 15 minutes later, no one has approached our table. We couldn't even get the attention of those walking past us. We had enough, we got up and walked out.  This Denny's has been removed from my Breakfast list and added to my No-No list.    Free WI-FI is a nice offering, but it doesn't get them any more stars.

It is hard to believe all the years I worked at Plaza Frontenac and would stop by Sportsman's Park for Happy Hour, that I never ate any food. How could this have happened is beyond me. The other day I finally got that corrected when I meet up with fellow Yelper extraordinaire Sarah S.    When enjoying bar grub I usually like to enjoy an order of chicken wings, before my burger with my dining partner. However,  with Ms.  Sarah being vegetarian that was not an option.  So I had to decide what did I wanted more, chicken wings and fries or a Jack Buck Burger with fries. With all the memorabilia of Jack Buck on the walls, it was a no brain-er, I went with the burger.   The burger was char grilled juicy and to my perfect temperature, medium. As my side I choose "steak fries", I love a thick and meaty french fry. My burger was seasoned so perfectly, I had no need to add any condiments at all. The dill pickle sliced lengthwise was the only garnishment in addition to the "Monterrey Jack" cheese.  I was a couple of orders of wings go past our table and I'll be returning to give them a try in the near future.   Sarah enjoyed some type of vegetarian wrap (you can read her review to see how tasty it was) that was huge.  It was so huge, she could only eat half and took the other half home in a non-eco friendly container.  Styrofoam?  Come on SPR, you're classier then that, get with it and provide your customers with an eco-friendly container for carry-out. Your lucky I didn't dock you a star, but my burger was too juicy good so I left you at 4.   The service was attentive and as the small dining room filled up with the bustling Ladue lunch crowd it did get LOUD. The sports memorabilia alone is worth stopping by for a beer and a browse.

I didn't see any dead people, but I did see some amazing and historical monuments to dead people. Bellefontaine Cemetery has about 50 or so movers, shakers and historical people of importance buried in their meticulously cared for grounds. If you walk the tour it is 4.2 miles, you'll have a good workout going up and down hills.    I highly recommend splurging and spending some of you hard earned money on the $5 booklet that gives you history and details. Some folks on the list you'll know and others you wonder who they were, but will understand once you read their blurb. They also have a second booklet on Civil War graves for $3. We opted out of that one. One can only handle so much excitement in a day.    It is interesting to see how in the past, families truly paid tribute to those who had left our world for green pastures. These grave markers, ranged in variety from a mausoleum to a simple plaque in the ground.  You'll even get insight to the, "mine is bigger then yours" rivalry between certain families.   I hope to have a second Saturday of the month off this fall so I can go back and take one of the tours with a guide. Touring cemeteries can teach you so much about history. I also plan to visit Calvary Cemetery across the street, I had no idea my favorite playwright (Tennessee Williams)  was buried in Saint Louis.   If you haven't made your final plans, there are still plots available here at Bellefontaine. Then perhaps you'll be on the tour some day and  strangers will stand by your grave reading in the booklet why you were famous or infamous.

Can you believe it? I went to a wood fired pizza restaurant and ordered a salad and it was a sensational salad. Their house vinaigrette, was incredible. If they bottled it, I would buy it.   What impressed me most about this salad, is that it had no iceberg lettuce in it at all. It totally was a mixture of mixed greens, in bite size pieces. In addition to the mixed greens, it had artichoke hearts, kalamata olives, roasted bell pepper, house-made croutons, parmesan cheese and then was tossed  with that amazing signature vinaigrette. It was huge, two people could share it if they were also ordering a pizza. For me, it was the entire meal.   My friend Christy thought it was wrong that I was at a pizza joint and not having one, so she shared hers with me. She was enjoying a Sara with some slight modifications. Being a fan of goat cheese, I think hew switching the parmesan cheese for goat, really made this pizza the real deal. I enjoyed the cracker thin crust and of course the wood fired char.   The service was friendly and attentive for our group of 9 and the server did not flinch when we asked for separate checks. They did however add 20% gratuity on to each of our bills. Which was okay, because our service was worthy of the full 20%.   I'll definitely be back, perhaps for a lunch special so I can try a pizza all to myself.   When: August 6, 2016 Why: Unofficial Yelp Event

A name change and need for some old fashioned candy brought me back. For me I can say, it was a positive change. The sales lady was friendly and helpful. This time I did not walk out empty handed, I walked out with a bag busting at the seams. The goodies I found, completed a fantastic gift that I am sure will be the envy of our gift exchange.   Great selection, much better customer service. I am so glad I came back and even happier that I can raise the stars from 2 to 4. Congratulations, Itsy Bitsy, you no longer are on my Terrible Two's List.   Would I come back? When the need arises for old fashioned, what I grew-up calling "penny candy".   When: December 20, 2016 Why: Gift Stuffers

I've been here twice and my 3 star rating is the average of the two visits. My first visit was a solid 4 star experience. I visited during their opening week and our lunch was well worth the price. They kept the food fresh and the variety was extensive. As Travis stated, it was very bright and clean.  My second visit was Christmas day, we couldn't decide where or what to do that day and finally we just thought Chinese. We called and they were open till 7PM. We got there around 3PM and they were busy, busy. Being busy, was no excuse for lack of table service and dried out and poorly presented food. You'd think they'd be on an A- Game being a holiday, but they got only 2 Stars for Christmas.   Also, we saw no signage for the higher price for the holiday buffet. Normally a holiday buffet offers extra features, but this buffet looked no different then the lunch I experienced their opening week. I guess I shouldn't bitch to much about the higher price, they at least gave both of us the SENIOR discount. I do not look that old...lol.

A greasy spoon diner, a white linen napkin and servers with a sarcastic sense of humor is what you get at The Grill. It is a classic dive, diner. The cup and saucer didn't match, but the coffee was strong and black. Just the way I like it. If James Beard gave out awards for divey diners, The Grill would be a winner.  There are no bells and whistles here, but the breakfast I had was down home good. It was simple, two fried eggs with bacon and hash browns. It also came with wheat toast, which was cut off-kilter which added to the charm of the experience. My eggs were done just how I like them, yolk broken and hard. They even had the crispy little edges around the whites. The Hash Browns were good, but I would have liked them a little crisper.   The banter among the servers and grill cooks is totally entertaining. It is almost like getting a floor show with your meal.   If your in the French Quarter, do yourself a favor and stop by The Grill for breakfast or lunch.  I know I'll be back on my next visit to NOLA.   When: August 29, 2016 Why: Breakfast

There is a new diner in town and it is totally living up to the phrase painted on it's front window; "A Taste of the Southwest on Southwest". I first visited them on Monday for breakfast and quickly returned on Tuesday to experience their lunch menu. Both were an escape to the Southwest and has you wishing they were open for dinner.  For breakfast my SO experienced their Mexican Burrito served Enchilada Style with Red Chile and Cheese on top. It was amazing! A burrito stuffed with scrambled eggs, cheese, green Chile, home fries and sausage. No more Western Omelets, this is the way to go.   My breakfast was Jonathan's Famous Fiery Scramble, a perfect start for my day. Spicy eggs, a side of bacon and home fries. I passed on my side of toast, because we ordered a half order of Biscuits and Chorizo Gravy. After all, what is a visit to a diner without experiencing B&G.  Normally I always add hot sauce to my scrambled eggs, but not these. They live up to their name "Fiery". The bacon was crisp and home fries are winning me over from traditional hash browns. The Chorizo Gravy was great, but I think they need to work on their biscuits to make them truly please this farm boy.   Lunch on Tuesday was a true winner. We started off with Chile Cheese Fries, that gave me a spicy burn twice. (I am sure you know what I am talking about). Fries are cut in house, with skins on and were crispy. They then topped them with Green Chile's and Cheese. They may not be heart healthy, but I'll be getting them again.   I enjoyed the Green Chile Cheese Burger, a typical diner burger with all the traditional toppings with the added bonus of Green Chile's and Longhorn Cheese. Yummy. Since we had the fries as an appetizer, I ordered  Onion Rings as my side. They accidentally brought it with fries and quickly noticed the error and brought us some Rings.   The SO had the best lunch, Red Chile Enchiladas with Beef.  It was served with Pinto Beans and Rice. Sampling his lunch, I know I will be ordering this on my next visit.  Mexican restaurants in the Lou should take note of these Enchiladas, I've never had them this good. Also, the Pinto Beans and Rice were better then most.   Southwest Diner is a great addition to the Saint Louis diner selection. It is off the beaten path, but worth finding.

Not my usual Lee's, but it was the most convenient while I was out running errands for me to pick up  our chicken dinner. The staff here was friendly and professional, just as those on Kingshighway. Also, as at any Lee's, the iced tea is kick ass good. It is equally as good as any you would be served in the deep south.   I favor the crispy chicken here at Lee's. It always has a good crunch and is juicy on the inside. One thing that Lee's offers as a chain, that separates itself from local chicken joints, is that they do not uncharge for requesting 3 thighs in the 3 piece dinner. That is quality customer service.   If this Lee's is in your hood and you're craving a fried chicken dinner, I would recommend you give them a try.

A charming little movie theater nestled inside a boutique hotel. Which just happens to be located in one of the hottest and trendy neighborhoods in Saint Louis.   CPPC has the feeling and look of an "art house" movie theater, but it primarily shows current blockbusters. The theaters are small and very intimate. Making them the perfect venue to see; a chick flick, comedy, foreign and indie film. I do not recommend seeing action/adventure or big blockbuster type films here. For those I highly recommend you visit a movie house that offers stadium seating. In fact, I insist that is what you do.   The patrons of this theater are respectful of each other, which makes the viewing a pleasant experience.  Like other reviewers have stated the theaters are small and you do hear everything. However, my experiences have been once the actual  movie starts, everyone is attentive and quite.  Aimee's friend Mr. Popcorn Guy, has never been watching the same movie as I. Another bonus about the attendees of this movie house, I have never seen any children. The youngest people I have ever seen are those working the refreshment stand.   They have the traditional concession counter treats and some very nice upscale ones as well. I always enjoy a small bag of  Lake Forest Chocolate Malted Milk Balls.  Knowing I paid an obnoxious amount of money for a treat, seems to make them last through the entire movie. Another big plus, on their concessions is that you can see them making the popcorn. So many places now bring out big bags of popped popcorn from the back and you really do not know how fresh it really is. It is so cool to see a place doing it the old fashioned way, of right at the counter. Also, the smell of fresh popcorn popping is so tempting.   CPPC was one of, if not the first movie theater to offer beer & wine in STL. Even though almost everyone is doing it now, it is a nice touch. A glass of white wine, chocolates and a chick flick makes for a good matinee.

My most recent visit was just cocktails. We were meeting friends for custard at Andy's and finished shopping in Kirkwood early so we stopped by Bar Louie. It was a Sunday, so I enjoyed a Bloody Mary and my friend had a Mimosa. Lucky her, they had a promo going on for unlimited Mimosa's and she slammed a couple down before we crossed the street for custard.  Unfortunate for me, not such a deal. However, I did enjoy an amazing Bloody Mary made with Absolute Peppar.   Service was great and attentive. They kept the cocktails flowing.

As I sit here to write an updated review for Southwest Diner, I am staring at a stack of receipts from all of my visits. Honestly, I have close to two dozen. SWD is close to my home, they offer a quality breakfast and lunch at very affordable prices. They also have a frequent diner punch card, that rewards you for being a repeat diner. 10 punches and your 11th entree is FREE.   If I had to pick a favorite from SWD, I would be hard pressed. However, I can say my go to is their, Jonathan's Famous Fiery Scramble. It's scrambled eggs that are served; spicy and cheesy. Along with your choice of a breakfast meat, home fries and toast. Even though the home fries here are tasty and well done, I do an even swap for Calabacitas. Since I'm losing weight, a side of Zucchini is more diet friendly then potatoes. Occasionally I cheat and enjoy the home fries.  Another favorite is the Greek Omelet and I have been known to add bacon. We all know everything is better with bacon.   My favorite spot to sit is at the counter, right at the corner on the end towards the front door.  It's comfortable and gives me a great view for people watching. Some of the other entrees that have graced my plates at the counter are: Medio Egg Combo, Desavuno Skillet, Rocket to Bacon Land, Bat Out of Hell and my own created omelet. If you're doing lunch, you have got to do the Double Green Chile Cheeseburger. You'll think you're in diner heaven. Also, always check out specials, during the summer I loved the Fried Green Tomatoes.   Before I wrap it up, telling you that the service is always spot on and friendly. That they serve Kaldi's coffee and you'll never feel guilty enjoying a Bloody Mary on weekday. I gotta tell you about, Tamale Tuesday. Yes, you can get tamales for breakfast and lunch from the famous Tamale Man here at SWD. That my fellow Yelpers, is a double win.   So glad Ian Froeb put Southwest Diner on his STL 100 List for 2016, it is well deserved.   Would I come back? I do, time and time again.   When: Too many times to list....... Why: Mainly breakfast, but lunch too.

Yelp, when are you going to give us that little button that will allow us to add that half of a star? Hwy 61 is good, it is better then A-OK, yet I'm not a fan. I am wavering between the 3 & 4 and a 1/2 would make me happier and let my fellow Yelpers have a better understanding of my review.   Hwy 61 Roadhouse & Kitchen truly is a sampling of Memphis and New Orleans cuisine. I have been wanting to try this place for a  while, not that I am stalking places that Guy Fieri has featured on his show, but the ones I have eaten at have impressed me. Also, I had no idea this was a "local" business. I thought it was a chain like Applebee's and Chili's. I am so sorry I "assumed".   We started out with Moscow Mules, one of my favorite drinks. I know now not to order them here. The MM is basically the reason I needed the half star. Who in the hell serves a MM in a mason jar? I want my copper mug. I love the combination of vodka (my favorite liquor) and Ginger Beer. Come to find out, they don't even use ginger beer, they use a ginger syrup and club soda. Not a true MM and that coast them a star.   Our appetizers were very flavorful. They offer full size orders and a "Tasting" which is like a half order. This is a smart idea, allowing your diners to have an appetizer and not over stuff themselves before their entree is served. We choose to sample a tasting of Hush Puppies and a full order of Fried Okra. OMG! The fried okra was lightly breaded and the okra was soft inside, making it melt in your mouth like butter. The Hush Puppies were made with a savory cornmeal, stuffed with Pepper Jack Cheese and chopped jalapeños. They were deep fried to a light golden brown. Some places over fry their hush puppies, which loses the flavor of the actual Hush Puppy.   I enjoyed a burger, a 1/2 lb of well seasoned ground beef with Pepper Jack Cheese and a side of Waffle Fries. They used shredded cheese as my cheese which melted so evenly over my entire burger. The Waffle Fries were golden crisp and hot and meaty on the inside.   My friend had the best Beef Brisket Sandwich.  It was slow smoked in-house, thinly sliced and topped with caramelized onions, provolone cheese & jalapeño mayo. They then serve all that yumminess on grilled sourdough. I was impressed with how tender and flavorful the brisket was. I wished I had ordered the same.   Hwy 61 is a short drive from the city, so I will be returning for another lunch.

So glad to see Southwest Diner is back on their A-Game. I will be honest, my last couple visits were less then stellar. I was there for their one year anniversary week,  a couple times later and witnessed a downturn in food and service. I loved SD so I didn't post a negative review, I just removed them from my Breakfast and Biscuits and Gravy list. I am now happy to say, they are being added back to both list after a very enjoyable morning.   A friend who had never been to SD wanted to meet for breakfast and that is where she wanted to meet. I went with the flow, in hopes that they were back on track. We arrived early, just as they were opening and were greeted cheerfully. Two of us ordered Bloody Mary's and their spiciness was a great way to start the day.   Our friend ordered, my favorite Jonathan's Famous Fiery Scramble. It's a spicy, cheesy scrambled eggs served with a choice of breakfast meat (sausage patty) and home fries. She liked it, she really liked it. Brad went with the Egg Combo Grande, a champion of breakfast. Two eggs, bacon, home fries and a short stack of buttermilk cornmeal pancakes. We also, shared a half order of Biscuits and House Made Sausage Gravy. Fluffy biscuit and a true milk gravy with huge chunks of sausage.   My breakfast was the Southwest Slinger, it was so good I'm creating a new list for slingers. It may be the only one on the list for awhile, but I am sure it will hold the #1 spot even longer.  The serving was huge, two normal people could share a single order. The plate is first covered with home fries, which are cubed roasted potatoes, covered in melted longhorn cheese, then two beef patties covered in green chilies and topped with two fried eggs. I loved it!  Southwest Diner is back in to my breakfast rotation.   When: 13 Jan 2014 Why: Breakfast with friends

Clean restaurant, friendly staff and fast service.  My roommate swears by the #9 which is the Italian Club with hot peppers. It's his favorite sandwich. Since I'm not a big fan of Jimmy, he takes advantage of enjoying this sammie when I'm working and he is off.   I haven't found a favorite, I've tried the #10 Hunters Club, #12 Beach Club and #13 Gourmet Veggie Club. Just like Subway, I find the bread to overwhelming. What also scares me about these sandwiches is the nutritional information. The sodium and carbohydrates are through the roof.   If I want a deli sandwich, I'd rather go to two other "local" deli's that are located in my hood.

I fell in love with this store while visiting the French Quarter. It's a great little boutique with NOLA themed silk ties, bow-ties, pocket squares and dog collars. They also had items for women and the home. It's all custom designed and manufactured locally in NO & LA. The designs are unique and creative. I'm from St. Louis so a Fleur de Lis has a special meaning to me, too.   I honestly had to make myself leave before I started to scoop up multiple items for myself and my dogs. I thought I was safe, until I got home and discovered they have a website that I can order from. Guess who's getting new collars and who's going to get new pocket squares?    I cannot wait to place my first order.   When: August 27, 2016 Why: I'm a Shopaholic

When this new IHOP opened, it wasn't open 24 Hours any day of the week. I am now happy to say, it has expanded it's hours for Thursday - Saturday to 24 Hours.  This location use to be a Denny's Diner that closed several years ago and sat vacant. IHOP came in did a full remodel and has brought new life and a new breakfast place to the Alton area.   Part of my work schedule requires me to work in Alton on weekends and except for the local McDonald's the choices for an early breakfast were bleak. Now that this IHOP has expanded its hours, my options have expanded. I can easily stop in grab a quick coffee and a Simple Breakfast and still be at work by 6 AM.   Their Simple Breakfast is a good value. It's simple, two eggs, choice of two bacon strips or two sausage patties, Hash Browns and Toast. I have them hold the toast, the Hash Browns are enough starch for this dieting man.   The staff from what I have experienced is small town friendly and attentive to their diners. I may find myself getting up a little earlier just so I can have a hearty breakfast. After all, it is the most important meal of the day.

Tuesday Morning is not a pretty store. It is not merchandised well and at times it is a little cluttered. However, all that can be over looked when you find the perfect item for your home at an insanely low price.   TM is one of those stores you have to shop frequently. The inventory is constantly changing, so every time you shop it is like an entirely new adventure. There are times I stop by and walk out empty handed, but I know the next time it will be as if I hit the Powerball.   You'll find inexpensive gadgets and small appliances for the kitchen and decorative items for the living room. My last visit I found a Queen size set of sheets that included two extra pillowcases and it was the color and thread count that I prefer. Like I said, sometimes you hit the Powerball. Having four pillows on my bed made this set a winner.  Tuesday Morning even has a great selection for both kinds of children; two and four legged. They have an excellent selection of dog beds and bowls and for the two legged toddlers they had an amazing variety of toys.   I have always found the staff here to be friendly. So many times the staff at discount stores can be on the gruff side of service, but not here. They have always been perky and upbeat when I have shopped.   My advice to you, is shop TM often and search out those bargains. Shopping here will make your gift giving dollars go further, meaning more dollars for you to spend on yourself.

If you are in Kirkwood and craving a cupcake, Smallcakes can satisfy your craving. It wont WOW you, but you'll be satisfied.   I was surprised at the small variety that they had to offer and I was there during lunchtime. Lucky for me they had one of my favorites, Wedding Cake. An almond white cake with almond flavored buttercream frosting sprinkled with edible pearls. So my roommate wouldn't feel left out, I got him a Peanut Butter Cup, a chocolate cake with peanut butter cream cheese frosting and peanut butter cup crumbles on top.   Each of us found the frosting to be the best part of the cupcake. Both of our small cakes were on the dry side, they definitely needed to be more moist to compliment the amazing frosting.   The counter person was robotic, did not have the energy that I'd want and expect at a cupcake shop. Also beware of the parking lot it is crazy. Spots are a premium so be aware of those drivers around you. I had someone pulling in to my space before I had completely pulled out.

I have been on a mission to revisit all the businesses that I have given 2 Star ratings, in hopes that they can prove themselves worthy of an increase. Today I visited Oh Lolli Lolli and unfortunately they showed me that they actually deserve a 1 Star rating, but I couldn't bring myself to lower their rating. The ambiance and location saved them, but they are still a 2.   The young ladies working were unfriendly and when I asked questions their answers were short and curt. Once again I walked out empty handed. Later that day, I visited two other candy shoppes on my quest for a specific need and they both offered me exceptional customer service. Their excellent customer service resulted with me spending money in both stores. What a shame that the cash register did not ring at Oh Lolli Lolli - Itsy Bitsy Candy Shoppe.

It's Sunday night, your stay-cation is just beginning and your craving steak for dinner. You get on Yelp and do a search for something new and different. 801 pops up and you think, why not. It's Sunday, they've got their prix fixe menu and 801 is on Ian Froeb's STL 100 List - so let's go give it a try.   As I approached the restaurant, my parking angel that hangs from my rearview mirror got me prince parking on the street. Winning! I immediately know that it is going to be a winning night.  I get inside the restaurant and tell the hostess, I'll just go sit at the bar. I circled the bar once, like a dog getting ready to lay down. I wanted to make sure I had a good space and no one else was on top of me and that I wasn't invading theirs as well.   I studied the menu before my arrival, so I already knew what i wanted. I started out with a Manhattan (Happy Hour $8). I asked the bartender not to laugh, then I asked him if I could have an order of Brussels Sprouts instead of a typical appetizer. He said yes, but recommended that I get a half order since the regular size is meant to be shared when dining. It was a perfect serving and I enjoyed how they roasted them. I'm not a fan of toasted Walnuts, but when it was combined with Garlic, Orange Zest and Parsley - they made this dish really pop. My second cocktail of the evening was an Old Fashioned (Not Happy Hour $18) Ouch, it was good, but Don Draper wouldn't even pay that much for one.   With the prix fixe menu, I got a salad, entree and dessert. For my salad, I chose the Caesar, my entree was a 6 oz Filet and dessert was Creme Brûlée. The Caesar is my go to salad,  especially when it has house baked croutons and white anchovy. My Fielt Mignon De Burgo was served with Boursin Mashed Potatoes and Grilled Asparagus. The filet was moist, tender and grilled perfectly to medium rare. The Creme Brûlée was one of the best I've had here in STL. It was the perfect ending to a Prix Fixe meal.   Would I come back? Yes, for special occasions. The service was top notch as you'd expect and want for the price you're paying.   When: November 6, 2016 Why: Steak Craving and STL 100 List

On their front window, The Boardwalk Cafe boost, "Best Breakfast in Town". Is it a gourmet breakfast? No. It is a down-home, diner, greasy-spoon, truck stop breakfast. The portions are huge and full of home-style flavor. Neither of us could clean our plates and both of us are hearty eaters.  I was raised on a farm, so when I see Biscuits & Gravy on a breakfast menu it is a must have. Lucky for me, TBC offered a half order that I could order and share with my dining partner. Being the Siskel & Ebert for Biscuits & Gravy, we both gave our order this morning, 2 thumbs up. Flaky biscuit with a thick creamy milk gravy, is always a winner.  Each of us ordered one of their Country Skillet Breakfasts. I went with the hometown named skillet, Arch and my DP went with the Denver. Both start off with a hefty serving of hash browns, their menu calls them home fries. The Denver has grilled ham, the Arch has sausage, tomatoes and jalapeños. Both had onions, peppers, Monterrey Jack and Cheddar cheeses. The skillets are then topped with two eggs, fixed your way. Both skillets were huge, so huge that we each took half of our skillets home to make into omelets the next morning.   The Boardwalk Cafe is now going to be in my breakfast out rotation. It's a good, cheap breakfast. I want to go back and try one of their burgers for lunch. If they do a good diner breakfast, I can only imagine what they do to a burger.

When: Feb 22 Why:    Birthday Celebration Lunch  It's a sports bar and a well decorated one at that. I liked the fact that there were all these little private rooms available for large groups. I wish more places, had this type of venue to offer.   We had five in our party so we had a good variety of food ordered. Even with Alberts name on the place, it's a sports bar so our expectations were not that high. We had a few surprises.   Buffalo Drummies - Nice and crisp. Too much sauce and sweet.  Grilled Fish & Slaw - Yummy. The slaw was better then some delis.   1/2 Slab Ribs & Fries - Ribs were nothing to write home about.  Mushroom Burger - Big juicy and good combination of cheese & sh-rooms.  Prime Rib Sandwich & Roasted Red Potatoes - Best of the bunch.  Pujols Burger & Fries - Nice, but the burger was too thin. Give me some meat.   The fries were seasoned fries, give me normal crinkle or steak fries.  I liked the fact that the two who did not want fries, were allowed to substitute. That is how we discovered the awesome slaw and red roasted potatoes.   Our server was very attentive and even split the tickets without us asking. His assistant or bus boy was on caffeine or a natural speed demon. He cleaned, filled our water and brought extra cheddar biscuits for us to enjoy.  The two of them were a great team.   I don't get out to West Port often, but when I do I will consider eating here again.

And on a clear day... On that clear day... You can see forever... And ever... And ever... And ever more!  When you get to the top level of the Lewis and Clark Confluence Tower and burst in to song singing, On A Clear Day You Can See Forever, I can tell you, you will not be the first. All those tower guides have heard it before, it's not that original. However, I do think my rendition was note worthy.  I've been twice, I had to do a re-visit because on the first it was an overcast day.  It was amazing how far I could see when a few clouds were removed from blocking my view. Each time, our tour guide was knowledgeable about the history of the area and Lewis and Clark. Our first guide on the cloudy day was witty and put his own spin on the presentation of information. The second guide sounded like a rehearsed tour guide, but you still get the info you need.   It's a great outing for a family or a couple who just wants an adventure up the River Road.

And they're off and you're off to a fun afternoon or evening of fun. FPRT is one of the places that I need and want a half star, so I can make this 3.5 Stars.   The best way to describe FPRT is a dive bar with horse races. The facility is old, rundown and in serious need of a renovation. However, that gives it character and adds charm to the gambling experience. There is enough down time between races, to enjoy drinks, visit with other characters and select your next horse to win, place or show.   I would have never thought of going to FPRT if it were not for my friend Norma wanting a day at the racetrack for her birthday. When you get to our ages, we usually have everything we want, so a fun social outing like this makes the best type of gift.   You can sit in the grandstand, or get down and dirty outside right next to the racetrack. We started out in the grandstand, but moved down to trackside and that is when it really got to be a fun time. The regulars, are true characters. I'd love to see a reality showed filmed here, it would be hysterical.   The beer, nachos and other stadium type foods are cheaper then a ballgame. I cannot rate the food, I only enjoyed the Blue Moon beer on draft. My beer was only $4.50 and it was a large glass. The staff behind the betting cages are very helpful to the newbies. I stayed with the same lady and she was amazing. She remembered my bets and would joke with me. I had the luck of a newbie, I won and I lost and when the day was over, I was Even Steven.   I had a fun afternoon, I'll be back with more friends for another fulfilled outing.

I have to admit I have not eaten at a Denny's for at least 15 years and was surprised at what I experienced. It was a Sunday morning, we wanted a quick breakfast and a new experience.  One of us built a grand slam and the other an omelet. Both were presented very well and the omelet was huge and fluffy. The hash-browns were the best I've experienced in awhile, they had a crispy finish which I think makes hash browns. My partner loved his grits, the bowl was big enough to feed a family. Our waiter Louie was attentive and witty - I could so easy see him doing extremely well in another venue.  Denny's will not be a regular stop for me, but I will not wait another 15 years to re-visit.

Great meat counter and the entire staff is so friendly and personable. I mentioned that I discovered them through numerous Yelp friends and they thought that was so cool. We bought a couple of Rib Eyes, that grilled up so nicely. They were tender and juicy.   They informed us as we chatted, that Monday is usually not a good day to shop. Their inventory is low after a busy weekend and deliveries begin to arrive on Tuesday. Brad asked about certain cuts of meat and they informed him that they'd be happy to special order them for us. That is going the extra step in customer service.   I'm not a fan of beef jerky, but the SO is so we gave it try on the recommendation of Chris Z.. I am here to tell you now, I like beef jerky. Theirs is the best jerky I have had, and will set the standard for any other jerky I try in the future.   They offer some grocery items and many were hometown products. It was good to see an independent meat counter supporting other hometown vendors. Team work, breeds success for our city.   I will be back this coming Tuesday, and many more to follow.

Oh, Lolli Lolli you disappointed me so much. I heard and read such great Yelp things about you and was so excited to shop your little candy shoppe, that I made a special trip to the De Mun neighborhood.
