When I arrived I thought the location was cute being next to a playground, giving you an endless flow of customers. I also enjoyed the compact size, you made use of every inch. Your staff was perky, friendly and was offered good customer service.   What disappointed me was your selection of sweet treats. There was nothing unique or special. I have a huge sweet tooth and I walked out empty handed.

It is off the beaten path and when you do find it, you'll think, "No way in hell, is this a restaurant". It's on the edge of an industrial area, but it adds to the, diner dive ambiance. The decor inside is simple. It's a diner and you are there for heart stopping breakfast or a comfort food lunch.   I've been for breakfast and I can say the portions are generous. I like my Hash Browns done crispy and usually have to request that at most diners. Not here, they do them right. Crispy on top and bottom.  They also serve up a good version of Biscuits and Gravy. I pretty sure the biscuits are not made in house, but I'm okay with that because the sausage gravy is what makes them delicious. I need to add a little more pepper for my taste, but I'm a pepper fiend. What is nice, they do not over salt anything I've had. I'm not a big salt lover and I've even had to give some of my food a shake or two at the table.   The coffee is strong and the servers are attentive in keeping my cup full. I will agree with others, that they do give more attention to the regulars, but the service is still good and adequate for a greasy spoon.   This diner is really a 3.5 Star. If you are looking for an adventure and a true old fashioned diner experience, I say, give this place a try.   Will I return? Yes, I want to try their lunch menu.   When: October 16, 2017 Why: Breakfast at a Diner

Yes, I am a fan and a loyal fan at that. I have been here numerous times and keep getting the same constant good service and food. Here are some of the highlights of some of my  most recent visits:  Carne Adovada - A daily special that was amazingly good. I enjoyed pulled pork from the shoulder that was braised in red chilies from Mexico for five hours. It was topped with two eggs over easy and a side of home fries. I stuffed the flour tortillas they provided and had a perfect late breakfast.   Slinger - A foundation of Home Fries, which are topped with either red or green chilies, (I've done both) and the two eggs.  Their home fries are the best in the city. I wish other dines would take lessons from SWD on how to prepare good and true home fries. The red chilies make it a spicier dish, but flavor wise I prefer the green.   Malted Waffle - A good waffle, but for my personal taste, I want more malt flavor.  I do love how they serve their maple syrup. They have it in a squeeze bottle which makes it so much easier to add to the waffle.   Burrito - Fat, stuffed to the maximum and full of flavor.  Service is always friendly and I never feel rushed as I have been at other diners in the city.

Not impressed at all. Candy was boring and overpriced. I did not pay that much attention to the soda selection as I am not a big soda drinker.   I did find several humous signs that would be great joke gifts for various friends and family members.   Service was minimal, not even a greeting or  a thanks for coming in. With that type of customer service, I most likely will not be returning.

Poptions!, I am going to remove you from my Terrible Two's List, because you made one of my co-workers happy. She moved here from CA two years ago and loves Kettle Corn and has not found any that compared to the popcorn she loved back on the west coast. So after I shopped the plaza across the street, I popped in to see if you had some available. Lucky for her, you did and she loved it.   However, I will still say your customer service, sucks. I hope the distinguished curmudgeon who was working is not the owner. If he is, I highly recommend that he hire some friendly, upbeat employees and stay off the front line of his store. You're selling a fun product, a treat that everyone loves. Be happy when you're selling it, don't be a Donald Downer.  When: March 30, 2016 Why: Searching for Kettle Corn

Came back this morning and I can say it is still just a solid 3 Stars. It's nothing special, but it is a good affordable diner breakfast.   I'll start out by saying, they've changed their Bloody Mary mix and it was a nice improvement. Now they need to get rid of celery as a garnish. Another big plus for me, is a pot of hot fresh coffee being placed in front of me. When I need my cup of Joe filled, I can do it myself.   This morning, my breakfast of choice was, Chicken and Waffle. It came with a side of two eggs. I had mine scrambled. The chicken was a boneless breast. It had a thin crisp coating of seasoned breading. It wasn't that warm when served, but the flavor was good. The waffle was chewy, and tough to cut with a fork. It's hard to mess up scrambled eggs, so they were a okay.   Service at the bar was friendly, speedy and comfortable.   I'll be Back? - Most likely not. It's a drive for me and I pass too many other diners on the way.   When: July 11, 2018 Why: Wanted something new for breakfast.

My current crush, David Z. from  Eat This Not That fame, highly recommends "NOT" eating at P. F. Chang's, but sometimes you just have to turn the other cheek and be a bad boy.   Actually we were going to celebrate a friends birthday who works at P. F. Chang's. So off we went with card and witty fabulous gifts in tow. We asked to be seated at the bar, so we could watch the Cardinals play, it was the night we got had a lead then got slaughtered. Taught me never go to an upscale Chinese restaurant to watch baseball.   While watching  a disappointing game we dined on; Chicken Lettuce Wrap, Seared Ahi Tuna and Crab Wontons. We also tried the cold Living Jewel Sake, which was the perfect ending to our heart stopping and raised blood pressure fare.  The sodium content here is off the charts.   The Crab Wontons were some of the best I have ever had. The wonton was light in color, I hate it when they are left in the oil too long and come out a dingy light brown. The filling was rich and creamy and their sweet-n-sour sauce added the extra kick.   The Seared Ahi Tuna, was totally perfect. We fought over who got the last piece. As always, I won....lol. My only only complaint, is the Chicken Lettuce Wrap. I am not a fan of Iceberg lettuce and that is what they use for their wrap. Could I please have Boston Bib or may-be some Red Leaf Lettuce? Why take away from the well prepared and seasoned chicken with a low end lettuce.   Back to the birthday celebration. When we asked for out friend to be told we were seated at the bar, we were informed no such person worked there. Instantly a look of horror came across Brad's face and he laughed out loud. We were at the wrong P.F. Chang's. We toasted Leslie's birthday anyway and knew we had a funny story to share.   David Z and my doctor may not recommend to eat here, but if you do in moderation and not daily P. F. Chang's is some pretty awesome Chinese food.

Today was my first visit to Starrs. I have driven by numerous times and never gave it any thought. We had lunch Fozzie's  across the street and thought this would be a great opportunity to check it out.   Loved the beer selection, it was comprised of micro brews and craft beers. There was not one A-B, Miller's or Coors's product to be seen.   There selection of wine was wide and varied, but I have seen better prices. With New Year's Eve approaching, their selection of champagne was the best I've seen in a single store and the prices were reasonable.  Customer Service was good considering the fact they had two sales representatives for distributors in the store. They bounced back and forth between customers and the reps. They made sure our needs and questions were answered.   I'll be back they had one of my favorite micro beers that is hard to find and it's a secret ingredient in some of my recipes.

As I enjoyed my breakfast of two eggs over medium, hand pressed sausage patties, home fries and a sopapilla with honey I double checked who was on my naughty and nice list. It was at that point, I realized I was sitting in a place that could help me check a couple of these good and bad little boys and girls off my list. What a better gift for a foodie friend and those that love breakfast with a Southwest theme, then a gift certificate to the very diner I was having my breakfast in.   SWD is offering a $20 gift certificate for only $15 and all you need to do is text DINER to 70000 and sign up to receive their promotional text. What a deal. This special offer is going till the first of the next year. I may even grab one of two for myself...lol.  Breakfast here for me is always done right. They get my eggs fried to perfection, they have the best crispy home fries in the city and a hand pressed local sausage patty will always beat a machine pressed patty that so many other diners serve up. Not to mention the sopapilla with honey, satisfying the sweet tooth.   Their newest addition is booze and nothing beats a good Margarita or Bloody Mary.  You may be having breakfast, but remember it has to be noon somewhere.

The other day I was out running errands and discovered where I wanted to have lunch was closed on Mondays. I was so bummed, but I moved on to my next errand further down Manchester Road. As I pulled in to the parking lot, of my next shopping errand, I saw Katie's and my lunch dilemma was resolved. To the amazement of many of my friends, I have never eaten at Katie's. So this was a great opportunity to expand my culinary adventures.   When dining single, I find it easier and more relaxing to sit at the bar. For those of you who do not know, they have a fantastic lunch menu that is served Monday-Friday 11 AM - 3 PM. For the incredible low price of $12.95 you select two delicious dishes. The bartender on duty was Grace and she assisted me in my selections. I narrowed it down to two items in each category, then she told me the best selling or her personal favorite. She knows what she is talking about.   I started out with a 1/2 Salad, mine was the Artichoke Salad. I knew I couldn't go wrong with this salad when it had many of my favorite things. I love; asparagus, pistachios and goat cheese. So when you add them to a spring mix and toss them in a balsamic vinaigrette, you have an sensational salad.   For my second delicious dish, I choose a personal sized pizza; Ted's Meatball. It truly was a pizza with pizzazz. A small pizza pie, topped with fresh Mozza and Neapolitan Meatballs on a San Marzano red sauce. The combination of the sauce and meatballs had me wondering why it took me so long to experience Katie's.   I almost forgot, while I waited for my salad and pizza, they served me a loaf of hot fresh bread with olive oil. This was a very relaxing lunch. I had my iPad, a couple of draft beers, the lunch special and a James Bond movie playing on the big screen. If I didn't have things to do, I might have stayed a little longer. I know I'll definitely be back.   When: November 23, 2015 Why: Lunch

I have a crush on Crushed Red. It truly is an urban bake and chop shop. I would be torn if I had to decide which I liked more the salads or the flatbreads. To be honest if you order right, they compliment each other.   Size does matter when ordering your salad. If you're sharing or enjoying a flatbread by yourself, a mini is the perfect size. I enjoyed a Farmer's Market which was mixed greens, smoked turkey breast, goat cheese, sunflower seeds, granny smith apples and diced cranberries. Hold the turkey and it is still a great salad for a vegetarian. They recommend honey mustard dressing and I too give it a thumbs up.   The SO ordered his favorite Cowpoke Smoke. It too is a great chop with roasted sirloin steak, roma tomato, red onion, blue cheese and crispy jalapeño straws tossed with mixed greens and goddess dressing. He also ordered a mini size and it was plenty since we were sharing a Five Cheese Flatbread.   The flatbread was sliced into four pieces, making it the perfect accompaniment to two salads. It was like having a slice of cheese garlic bread. You cannot go wrong with a flat bread brushed with extra virgin olive oil and roasted garlic, then topped with goat, feta, gorgonzola, parmesan, mozzarella cheese and sprinkled with fresh basil.   You'll stand in line, order in line then select your table and wait for your food to be delivered by a cheerful staff person. Lunch time is prime so finding a good table may be difficult, but the food is good.

I love that Landmark brings in some independent and foreign films that other theaters will not touch. The actual theaters are small, kind of boutique size. They're traditional style, on a gradual slope. No stadium seating here, but it is not needed due to the small size.    It was a nice touch that the projectionist came in before the movie and introduced himself. He also talked about the theater, services and thanked us for choosing Landmark. That was customer service you'd never see at a Mega theater.   Unfortunately the concession stand employees did not have the same skills. The young man selling tickets and treats, oozed attitude. He made it obvious to us that we were disrupting his S&M (standing and modeling) time. When you asked him a question,  you can tell it just grated him that he had to answer. How can you have two employees be so different.   This movie theater may be in Plaza Frontenac, but do not let that intimidate you. It is still just a movie theater where you go to be entertained. Dress as you would to go to any other theater. No need for designer clothes or fur coats here. When you're done at the movie, go downstairs and enjoy a Margarita at Canyon Cafe.   When: 11 Feb 2014 Why: To see a movie

Partner was home sick, craving an old fashioned cheeseburger with all the toppings and he didn't want one of those "stupid burgers". Stupid burgers, would be those you find at other "fast food" places with cute marketing names. So I stopped by the neighborhood Steak 'n Shake on the way home.   I arrived about 9:00 p m and the place was hopping. It was a good mixture of families, seniors, and couples enjoying hand made burgers, fries and shakes. The manager was working the counter and check out and was very personable. He made everyone feel as if they were the only customer and he did this while keeping tabs on his team.  I ordered a Steak burger with cheese with all the toppings, small fry and a Banana Milk shake for the partner. It was the best medicine ever, the next morning he was up a feeling much better.   All I had was the Chocolate Covered Strawberry Milk Shake which is offered for a limited time. It's a perfect shake for the Valentine season which is approaching quickly. (I ate at work and that is addressed in another posting)  Best place for a quick quality burger and for skinny fries you can not find a better place.

I love Costco!  It is not only a great place to stock up on staples, but you can find many other bargains for things that you just can't live without.   Their meat selection is better then some butcher shops. We always stock up on Rib-Eyes, Boneless Chicken Breast and Butterfly Pork Chops.  The  fresh vegetable and fruits look good, but being a couple the amount is too much.   Don't just think Best Buy or Ultimate Electronics for your HD TV, the prices here can put them to shame.   The clothes section is just like a TJ Maxx, it constantly changes and you have to shop and check it frequently. I have found Ralph Lauren several times and when I do, I buy one of every color.   You may need to buy a membership, but Costco is worth the investment.

Their prices are amazing. They are so competitive, you'd be a fool to  use one of the national chains, when you can support a local business.   I've had invitations for special occasions designed by a friend and then printed here and they blew me away with the end result. Each time, the quality, was top notch impressive. They've even printed banners for me.   The staff is aways professional and friendly. The Ink Spot is my go to, for printing and I recommend that it be the same for you, too.   I'll be back? - Absolutely   When: Numerous times.  Why: Custom Printing.

What do you get when you combine; Whole Foods, Dierbergs and Soulard's Market? Answer: Fields Foods, the newest grocer in town and the hottest addition to the Lafayette neighborhood.   Now that Fields Foods has opened in my "work" hood, I may never have to pack another lunch again. They have a very affordable salad bar, prepared foods counter, small hot foods bar and a Grab-n-Go section that will make my work lunches so much more interesting. I'll no longer need to call local restaurants for carry-out, on the days I forget to "brown bag". I'll just run over to FF and find something to my liking. Their offerings are less expensive then WF and in the same price range as Dierbergs.   My first lunch was a Orzo and Kale Salad, Pork Tenderloin and Green Beans with Red Potato. All three were good, with the Orzo and Kale leading the way. The Green Beans were fresh, but I needed to add pepper and salt for my taste. Which is better then being over seasoned.   I cruised the aisles quickly picking up treats for co-workers. Chips, snack crackers and bite size cupcakes. As I cruised, I was impressed by Seafood, Vegetables, Meats and Wine offerings. Everyone at work was excited to find out their treats were from FF, who is just down the street.   FF may not be my go to all my groceries, but it will be the place to go for lunches and treats for my work family. Residents of Soulard and Lafayette are some lucky folks to have this new grocer in their hood.

Today was party central at the Tap Room, everyone was there to join or renew their memberships to the "Schlafly Imperial Pint" Club. Known to members simply as the SIP Club. My cousins have always been members and we meet them there for lunch today as they renewed their memberships. With all the excitement we became members too.   While sipped our pints, chatted about the holidays we munched on some yummy delights. We started our feast with a Flat-bread Pizza and Bavarian Pretzels that were served with a White Cheddar Cheese dip. The pretzels are great, recommend for anyone who may just be out drinking some brews.   We also had an order or Frog Legs (not I) and White Chicken Chili (that's what I had). The FL's were small, they kinda resembled wingettes. I passed on the opportunity to try them, even being told they taste like chicken didn't persuade me. Those that had them, told me on the side they had better and were glad I didn't have them as my first taste of FL's.  White Chicken Chili - I make better, enough said.   Now for the star of the event, besides the beer.  Three of us had Traditional Mussels, and they were awesome. The portion was huge.  The only negative I can say about them, is I wish they offered some french bread to soak up the incredible broth. They came with a side of French Fries that would be a good compliment to any burger.   One of our diners had a Turkey Burger and it was huge and the other had a special order of Chicken-n-Dumplings that look so good, I may need to order on my next visit.   Joining the SIP Club, the Mussels and being with family made for a perfect day after Christmas.

Jimmy, I love you. You gave us the best Sunday Brunch ever. We were impressed with the service (Joel C. you rock as a server), live music, booze and most of all incredible food. It was the perfect way to begin and enjoy a Sunday morning.  The ambiance of Jimmy's is warm and relaxing. We were seated in the Bistro side near the fire pit. If it were truly a cold winter day it would have added to the charm, but they understood our request to turn it off due to the toasty warmth. A duo of electronic keyboard and trumpet provided soft jazz to our dining experience.   We started our brunch with a traditional Bloody Mary that surprised me being served in a short glass. The glass may have been short, but it was full of spicy zing. After two rounds of Bloody Mary's, we switched to a Mimosa and Bellini when our entrees were served. Drinks were $5 each, a great price for the quality we received.   Our friends Brett and Jillian joined us, so we got to order and experience more food. We started out with the Smoked Salmon with Cream Cheese and the Smoked Trout. Both were freaking amazing and the portions were huge. Both were great, but I can see one person having the salmon and being totally satisfied.   For entrees Brad had the Crossiant French Toast, I ordered the Spinach Artichoke Benedict and our friends had the Buckwheat Pancakes. All were good, but my Spinach Artichoke Benedict was the best. They make a cake out of the artichoke and spinach and then place a perfectly poched egg on top. Totally yummy and healthy.  B & J's pancakes were huge and fluffy with fresh strawberries on top. Brads Crossiant French Toast was a good twist on a traditional brunch treat.   Congratulations Jimmy, you are now my favorite Sunday Brunch. I normally work Sunday, but when I have that day off - you will see me there.

A small well maintained county park. Every little detail is well kept. The pavilions and picnic tables are in above average condition. Each pavilion has clean restrooms, one for each sex and a colorful jungle gym for the tiny tots to play near-by.   The roads circling the park were smooth and pot hole free and the laking lots for the pavilions looked better then some of the local malls. I was also impressed with how well maintained the landscaping was.   This truly is a great park for a romantic picnic. It is even great for a family reunion, company function and a small charity mixer.   I wish the city kept their parks, this well maintained and clean.   When: September 19, 2015 Why: A party for Shelties

When I lived in the CWE I was a regular at this Straub's, I loved the meat counter, deli, prepared foods and produce. Straub's is to specialty foods what Whole Foods is to organic and as pointed out by Cherie O. Straub's does that job very well.   Now that I live in the Lindenwood Park neighborhood, I make a very worthwhile drive for special occasions. You will not find a meat counter like Straub's at any other major grocer in the St. Louis area. The butchers are knowledgeable and personable in their services. Many times I have needed special cuts of meat and they have gotten them in for me as a special order.   If you like the prepared foods section at Whole Foods, stop by and check out Straub's. You'll be amazed how you can create an amazing lunch for yourself or a romantic dinner for two. Another section I have rediscovered recently is the frozen foods. They offer brands, that are not offered at the chain grocers. Yes, they are higher in price, but the quality is well worth the additional $.   The staff is always friendly. Many of the butchers still remember me from living in the neighborhood and make it a point to say hello, even if they are not the one serving me. Which shows the high level of customer service that they provide.   In closing,  I want to give a shout out to their BBQ. Occasionally during the summer months they grill and BBQ in the parking lot. If you see that taking place, it is well worth stopping by and partaking. I have been known to call to discover the schedule so I know when to make the commute over to the CWE.

You know you are a true Yelper when a restaurant owner sends you a private message telling you about a new item on their menu that they know you will enjoy. Jonathan one of the owners of SWD, sent me a message telling me that they are now making their Biscuits and Gravy with their house made sausage instead Chorizo. This old farm boy who loves B&G's got there as fast as he could.   I have always been a fan of the sausage patties at SWD. There is just something about a hand pressed, oddly shaped patty, bursting with flavor to make a breakfast complete. Switching their gravy to their own sausage over the Chorizo, is a vast improvement. For a farm boy, pork sausage is the way to go when making gravy to top biscuits.   This morning we also enjoyed their daily special, "Grits on Fire". I will admit, I am not a fan of grits, but love their Adovado pork, so I gave it a try. It basically was a grit cake topped with the Adovado pork, corn, queso fresco and topped with two fried eggs. It was on fire and so was I the rest of the day, but I didn't mind because it was that good.  However, as I stated earlier I am not a fan of grits and if they offer Grits on Fire again, I think I'll have them hold the grits and put mine on their famous perfectly crispy home fries. As, George O. said, Grits on Fire deserves a place on their permanent menu.

It's true, it's true. Bigger is better. Reading my morning dose of Yelp  reviews, I saw that Jessica C. mentioned that they expanded, so I added TJ to my list of errands.   Upon entry I immediately impressed with the expanded produce and dairy section. A 3 lb. bag of Honey Crisp Apples for $3.99. At other grocer's they're $3.99 for 1 pound.  They may be smaller in size, but they still have the same big flavor of a Honey Crisp apple.   As always, all the other selections are unique, organic and exotic foods. Don't forget the wine and booze.......good bargains can always be found.   So glad this TJ finally got to expand. With the store having a claustrophobic feel when I shopped and the parking lot being a demolition derby, I always shied away. Now that it is bigger, all I have to worry about is the crazy parking lot.

Packed? Not even close, but perhaps that is because we were there for lunch on a Tuesday. There were only three other tables, two of west county ladies who lunch (4 or 5 at each table) and one with two business men having a beer lunch.   I was there with two co-workers, we all had Tuesday off and meet up for drinks and lunch. Our drinks were Bud Select, Margarita and Tickled Pink. I was drinking the Tickled Pink on the recommendation of our waitress. I told her I liked vodka, and I think she made her suggestion based on that and the fact I was in a pink polo. It was kinda sweet, but vodka served in a martini glass - I'm game.   We started out with the Bruschetta, which was served in a giant size Martini glass. It was light, flavorful and a perfect start to a afternoon or cocktails and munching.  We then continued our feast with three small plates, we each got to choose one. Our three were, Grilled Chicken Nachos, Loaded Fries and Chicken Wings (Szechwan). The Szechwan was great, spicy with a sweet tang. The loaded fries were good, for my taste they could have been crisper to handle the weight of all the toppings. The G. C. N. were the best of the three, one person could make it a meal.   Our waitress was perky and fun. When we were ready to go, she told us she only had two more hours to go on her shift and she'd love us to stay.  A few times she was slow bringing the next  round of drinks, but that wasn't her fault. I could see the bar where I was seated and the bartender had a problem staying within her work area.   Great ambiance, I had fun and the food was above average bar grub. I'll go back.

Basso is a great place to meet friends for Happy Hour and that is what I did this past Monday night. I meet up with a group of Yelpers, shocking isn't it. We started our week out right by hooking up to enjoy a few drinks and appetizers. We were all surprised when we checked in on our smart phones and discovered our first glass of wine or beer was on Basso. Damn, it is good being a Yelper.   The bartenders on duty were awesome. They were attentive to us and offered up tastings to those who were having a hard time selecting their beer or wine. I had no trouble selecting mine, I was in a Prosecco state of mind. Listening to one of the young ladies describe the beers was as if she were a brewmaster. She was selling me on a beer and I was already content with my Prosecco.   I love the vast open space and the large rectangular bar. It makes it easy for a group of friends to stand/sit and enjoy their evening. Also, it is fun to flirt with other patrons across the way. Also, it fun to walk over and see all the hustle and bustle of the kitchen.   We did order several appetizers, but I only focused on two. I totally fell in love with Stretch Armstrong, a pizza made with buffalo mozzarella, stracchino and garlic. A simple cheese pizza stole my heart and most likely clogged an artery or two as well.  I also enjoyed the Roasted Cauliflower, which would make any vegetarian happy.  Whipped Ricotta, Gremolata and Breadcrumbs made this cauliflower sensational.   Now that I know Basso is good for Happy Hour, I'll be back to check it out for late night drinks and dinner.

I love Cole Haan shoes and this store to me is what the shoe departments at Neiman - Marcus and Nordstrom are to most women. I can find every type of shoe I need and want here. I can even find shoes that I didn't even know I needed and wanted here. The selection is so vast, I can not figure out why anyone would buy their CH at a department store of other specialty shoe store when you a direct source right here.   In addition to great shoes and boots, they have messenger bags, duffel's, belts, socks  and shoe laces. Selling shoe laces is a big point for me. Have you noticed how some shoe stores sell you a pair of shoes with laces and when you want an extra pair of laces, they tell you they don't sell laces. Not here, they've got'em and they have them in a variety of colors to match your shoes.   Prices may be higher then your typical "shoe store", but you are getting what you pay for and that is a classic well made product. My Cole Haan shoes seem to last for ever and I am  hard on shoes. I watch for sales and periodically treat myself to a full priced pair, when I just can not resist the temptation.  Which may be very soon, since I found a pair that are screaming, "buy me, buy me".  Dorothy had her "Ruby Slippers", so why shouldn't Steven B have his "Orange Loafers".  Orange is my signature color.   The entire sales staff is friendly, knowledgeable and professional. I'd be hard pressed to pick a favorite.

I love this Whole Foods. It is totally head and shoulders above the Brentwood location. It's a Tiffany's diamond compared to Brentwood's Jared's diamond. They both sparkle, but Town & Country give you more bang for your buck.   At times when I shop here, I am overwhelmed. I catch myself going from side to side and back-n-forth. Finding treasures and tantalizing treats every aisle. Love the house brand 365, quality product at a reasonable price.   The selection and variety seems to be larger then those offered on Brentwood. The bright lighting and wider aisles makes for a more enjoyable shopping experience.   The prepared foods section make me want to pull up a chair and a TV Tray  and graze the afternoon away. Of course I'd have to have one of the chilled bottles of wine or beer to accompany all the fine foods.   Another thing that makes this location better is the staff. The employees that I have encountered have no attitude problems. They're friendly, helpful and full of suggestions. Some of the attitude drenched employees of Brentwood should come out here and observe what good customer service actually is.   I live in the city, and I will make the extra drive for this store.

I miss Lester's, but Kingside Diner is a great new addition to the CWE. With the closing of The Majestic, the CWE was in dire need of a restaurant to provide a good, hearty, diner type breakfast and Kingside in doing just that. Looking at the menu and their Blue Plate Specials, looks as if they'll be taking care of lunch and dinner too.   I enjoyed a delightful breakfast on the opening day. They offer six options, to which you can have as an omelette, burrito or flatbread. I choose #3, Romesco, goat cheese, spinach and red onion. It stuffed full, fried to beautiful golden yellow and served with a side of Hash Browns. The portions were the perfect size for a breakfast and price.   A couple of friends attended the soft opening and raved about the Cheddar Drop Biscuits with Chorizo and Sage Gravy, so I had to give them a try. My friends were right, these biscuits and gravy were the bomb. I liked the fact they served the gravy in a gravy boat and you got to slice your biscuits and control the amount of gravy. It also made it easy for me to only eat one of the two biscuits and take the other one home.   I'm looking forward to going back for lunch and trying the BLTA Sandwich. It caught my attention with the fried green tomato and avocado.  I also want to try, Thanksgiving All Year. Thanksgiving is my favorite food holiday, so a turkey sandwich with, chutney cranberry, stuffing and pepper jack cheese on it has to be a winner.   In closing, I give them a BIG shout out for using Eco-Friendly carry-out containers and a bonus point for them being black and white to follow the chess theme.

Scarlett O'Hara could have many a new dresses shopping here. They offer many styles of drapes/curtains at a very affordable budget. In addition to window treatments, they have table and bed linens as well. You can also, find decorative holiday items and some kitchen accessories.   Don't come here expecting to find name brands. Shopping here is like shopping for groceries at Aldi's. It will be brands you have never heard of before. I asked for Egyptian Cotton sheets and quickly learned they did not exist in their inventory.  Many of their sheets were a blend of cotton and polyester. I did find a set that was 500 thread count and 100% cotton, but you could not buy additional matching pillowcases. That is one reason I do not like buying my sheets in sets, I like to mix & match.   Anna's is a good place to shop for college dorm rooms, the guest room & bath and the summer lake house. She also can help those on a limited budget, make their home look and feel like a Better Homes and Garden creation.   The sales associates were extremely friendly and helpful. I walked out not making a purchase, but it was no fault of theirs. They did their job and actually did it better then some associates at BB&B.

Clayton Restaurant Week is a great way to experience new places that you haven't tried before. Cantina Laredo has been on my list of Yelp bookmarks for awhile now, so I took action during CRW to get it removed. Now that I've been here, I'm wondering why it took me so long.   I arrived early and took a seat at the bar, arriving early I got to take advantage of the Happy Hour as well. I started out with a Casa Rita, a house Margarita that is made with fresh lime juice. Being an upscale Mexican restaurant, I was pleasantly surprised to see that they offer complimentary chips and salsa. They offered two salsa's; mild & spicy. I emptied the spicy dish, it was that good. Since I got free chips, I ordered some Queso off the Happy Hour menu. When it arrived, I was shocked at how huge it was. It was delicious, but way too much for one person. If you are there with friends for HH, order it, it's a good value.   To celebrate CRW, I started out with Ahi Tuna Tacos. There were two mini crispy tacos filled with Ahi tuna poke, jicama slaw and chipotle aioli with a scoop of guacamole. I would have preferred them in a soft shell, but the tuna was flavorful, so I didn't mind the crispy shell.   My main entree was Salmon. It was grilled with chimichum sauce, served on a bed of lime rice and a side of black beans. The Salmon was grilled to perfection and the sauce was a nice topping. I wasn't a fan of the lime rice, would have preferred another side. Perhaps some Mexican Rice or Sautéed vegetables would have been a better choice.   Dessert kicked-ass. I enjoyed Mango Tres Leches. I loved the Mango Cream sauce and tart cherry coulis. I almost got the Churros, with raspberry and chocolate sauces, but I'll have them on my next visit.   The service was attentive, but not overly friendly. I like a bartender who's more personable.   Will I return? Yes, I gotta try those Churros.   When: January 23, 2017 Why: Dinner - Clayton Restaurant Week

Okay, it has been over a year and I have punished you enough. It is time to give you back your 5 Star rating.   When ever I come to Costco, the first thing I do is go fill my gas tank. Their gas is always cheaper then the stations that gives you the 5¢ discount for paying cash. Saving on gas, gives me more to spend inside on other necessities.   One of my favorite things to buy here is booze! It's way cheaper then any grocery store, drug store or warehouse liquor store. We get our vodka, scotch, Schlafly's beer and select wines here. It is a great place to stock up the bar for your next big party. Sometimes our basket looks kinda scary. We hit the liquor section first and there is nothing else in it, so we look like some serious party animals.   They also have an excellent meat counter. Their lamb is as good if not better then lamb I have bought at Straub's. Other stand outs are; ground Bison, Rib Eye Steaks, Butterfly Pork Chops and Perdue Skinless & Boneless Chicken Breast. Our freezer is always stocked with a variety of their meats.   It is also a great place to stock up on household staples.  We're only a household of two, so we have to be smart on what we buy in bulk. However, what we do buy, saves us big. What is an added bonus, is once a month Costco sends out a coupon book that saves you more $ on the already low warehouse prices.   The staff is always friendly, I have my personal favorite cashiers and will wait in line just so I can have them ring me out. On occasion, I have had to return or exchange an item and the customer service desk makes it a smooth transaction.   If you're looking to join a warehouse club, I highly recommend Costco.

I recently attended the first St. Louis Food Media Forum, a two day conference that was held in the Chouteau Room at Moulin. The room was the perfect venue for 80 -100 foodies to congregate and discuss; food blogging, recipe writing, food photography, food writing ethics and marketing/branding.   Having attended my fair share of business meetings and conferences, the two things that are always topic of complaints are acoustics and room temperature.  Here at Moulin neither of those were an issue. The sound system made it easy for the speakers to heard through out their entire presentations and PowerPoint displays could be seen easily from all tables. Even with three digit temperatures scorching the city of Saint Louis, the Chouteau room held a very comfortable coolness.   Our first day lunch was provided by Moulin, which was a variety of cold sandwiches  & wraps served family style at each conference table. Jimmy John's and Subway could learn a thing or two from Moulin on how to make a good sandwich. The second day PW Pizza treated everyone to a pizza buffet that had me gaining weight just cruising the line. If you're going to cheat your diet with Pizza, it might as well be a PW.  How could I go wrong with a Popeye & Olive Oil? After all, Spinach & Goat Cheese is healthy, right? For our breaks, snacks were provided by a variety of local bakeries, breweries,  wineries, chocolate and ice cream businesses.  If I am ever in need of a conference venue, I will consider Moulin as my first choice. The location, service and food makes it an easy choice.

I never knew this place existed until I was walking over to Washington Avenue from The Peabody Opera House. I'd seen the building, but always thought it was either a court house or part of the library. To my surprise it is a very well kept museum for our soldiers. I was amazed how well maintained the building and displays were kept. How have I lived in STL for 33 years and never visited our Soldiers Memorial.   Saint Louis has many well kept secrets and this is one of them. Don't let this hidden jewel remain a secret, visit it soon and tell those  history buffs you know that this is a must see on your next visit downtown.

Stinger's is a delightful little hometown restaurant that has the feeling of Cheers. It had that warm small town fuzzy feeling. I would have never discovered this hidden little jewel in Cahokia if it were not for a friends 40th birthday and college graduation combo party. It is off the beaten path, but easy to find and a good find once you start to enjoy the food.   Lisa (owner) and her staff were providing top notch hospitality. They set up a special buffet for all of party guest and kept it well stocked during the party hours. It was a simple menu; salad, Mostaccioli and a variety of pizza. I believe I had the house salad dressing, which was a flavorful Italian. I rarely have Mostaccioli, so I must say, this is one of the best I have had. It was done well with a flavorful sauce and the melted cheese. However, the pizza definitely was the stand out of the buffet. It was a hand tossed crust, a sweet tomato sauce, no provel cheese and plenty of toppings. They offered a variety of toppings, with my favorite being pepperoni.   Plenty of televisions in the bar and dining area makes Stinger's a great place to drink beer, eat pizza and watch your favorite sports team with a group of friends. Oh, forgot to mention they have great prices on their draft and bottled beers. Sometimes it pays, I mean "saves" to drink at a small town bar.   When: July 11, 2015 Why: Birthday and Graduation Party

It has been a year and Fields Foods is still a solid 4 for me. It is not my regular grocery store, for me it like a big convenience market. I am able to make a quick stop here after work and pick up last minute items for an evening meal.   I am happy to say, there has been an improvement in the fruits and vegetables since my last review. Caution is still used in my selection, but the quality is better then before.   The craft beer selection is vast for a grocery store of this size. Their variety of wines is also impressive and has a wide price point, to fit every budget.   Favorite departments are still the butcher counter and hot prepared foods. Shhhhh.....I have been know to grab some chicken wings from the hot bar and a six pack of craft beer for dinner.   Will I return? - Stop by at least once a week.   When: Numerous days Why: Odds and Ends in the grocery world.

Compassionate care at an affordable price.   There are no bells and whistles here. The waiting area and examining room are minimalist. That is why the prices are reasonable. You're not paying for prettiness. You truly are just paying for the medical care of your pet.   The vet techs and vets are truly caring for your pet. They ask questions and help you find the best care and treatment for your fur-babies within your budget. I was here with a friend and they truly helped him find the best solution for his dogs ailment. They even pointed out another issue and treated it as well.   The only downside is they do not make appointments. It's like an urgent care, you show-up and wait in line for your turn. If you've got the time to wait, on a budget and need/want top care for your pet - this is the place for you.   Chances of returning? - Follow-up for Grace.  When: January 23, 2019 Why: Big Grace needed care

First off, I gotta say kudos to Planter's House for being part of, "Dine Out For Life 2019". It is so rewarding to see a local business giving back to a local charity.   Planter's House was my third stop for Dine Out For Life. It's an important charity to me, so I try to get out and support it through as many of my favorite restaurants as I can. Lucky for me, I was here during HH so a couple of my masterfully made cocktails were $3 off.   Yelp was hosting the event here at PH, so I got to start my evening off sharing and toasting the event with Max our fabulous CM. I started off with a Slope and Max enjoyed a Tommy's Margarita (spicy). My Slope, was sort of a Old Fashioned made with Rittenhouse Rye, my favorite Rye. I will definitely add it to my cocktail rotation here.   Knowing I had one more stop on my evening out, I only ordered the Strawberry Salad. I figured I'd make my evening like a progressive dinner party. Loved this salad. It was made with my favorite lettuce, Bibb. It addition to the fresh strawberries, it had; shaved fennel, dill ricotta and rye bread croutons. All of this was then tossed with a  lemon-poppyseed dressing, another favorite of mine. It all blended well together and the rye croutons were a nice twist.   I closed out my evening before moving to my final stop of the night with a Kentucky Breeze. I choose it for two reasons. One, it's made with Four Roses Small Batch Bourbon and it also had strawberry infused Bonal. I thought it was appropriate to stay with the strawberry theme. It was a perfect finale.   Service is always top notch here and every mixologist will make your cocktails like a true pro.   I'll be back? - It's hard not to return here.   When: May 2, 2019 Why: Dine Out For Life 2019

The Piccadilly is my new favorite fried chicken restaurant.  It is so juicy on the inside and the outside is  an even golden color that is crisp and perfectly seasoned.  It is so perfectly done, that I'd bet it is pan fried. This type of perfection can not be achieved by deep frying.   It is served with two sides; green beans and mashed potatoes with gravy.  The potatoes were whipped fluffy, but still hearty. I would have preferred a truer "yellow" chicken gravy, but their light brown was rather tasty. The green beans, were seasoned with the basics, salt and pepper and very well could be the best green beans I have enjoyed in a restaurant.   The OD (other diner) enjoyed a 1/2 Rack of Baby Back Ribs, that could compete with some of  our more popular BBQ joints in the city. The meat was extremely tender and juicy. It was so easy to completely clean the bones of every morsel of meat. What our local BBQ joints could learn from Piccadilly is how to serve up good Baked Beans and Cole Slaw. Both of these sides were worthy of a Blue Ribbon at the county fair.   We started out with a couple glasses of wine and an order of onion rings. I know wine and onion rings don't go together, but it just that way. The onion rings were crisp and the ring of  onion inside was soft, with just a little snap left in it. For me that is a good onion ring.  We also shared an order of Baked Mac-n-Cheese. It was rich, creamy and baked with bread crumbs on top. Man-n-Cheese should always be baked like this.   The service is down home friendly and personable. Piccadilly is located in a residential area, in an old house and you actual get the feeling you at a large dinner party in someones home.  Many of the diners around us were regulars and when they found out it was our first time, they began chatting and giving us recommendations.   One of the regulars, comes from Town & Country every week for a dinner. I was embarrassed, when I had to tell her I lived 1.7 miles away and had never been. She made it worse when she told me she has only lived here six months. However, now that I have discovered Piccadilly, I will be a regular.

Better late, then never. I posted pictures of my lunch at Billy G's, but forgot to follow up with a review. I like Joey B's on The Hill, so while I was shopping in Kirkwood I thought I'd try Billy G's Kirkwood. It seemed logical that I'd like it since both are part of the Gianino family restaurant group.   My visit was in the autumn and I was out on the patio, which is a beautiful place to dine if the weather permits. I started my lunch with a cup of their Steakhouse Chili. The cup serving was the perfect size to take the chill off and kept my tummy from growling while waiting for an awesome burger.   I'm a sucker for the Jalapeño Burger at Joey's, so I tried Billy's and he did not disappoint. It was the same high quality grilled burger, topped with Pepper Jack cheese and lightly breaded and fried jalapeños. They grilled my burger, to my requested medium rare temperature. The fries that accompanied my burger were slender, crispy and lightly salted. Just like Joey's, the burger here a Billy's was a winner.   When shopping in Kirkwood, keep Billy G's in mind when you get hungry and keep your dining dollars local.

I use to favor the Rock Hill, Stein Mart. Now that I have discovered this one, my loyalties are changing. This location not only has a better selection of mens clothing, but the customer service here is also superior.   I am not afraid of color and I love the selection of colorful dress and sport shirts offered here. When shopping, the first racks I check out are those with the sign toppers offering an additional  percentage off the already lowest reduced price. On this last visit, I got three shirts for less then I would have gotten one at a local department store. Hell, the prices were even lower then the outlet mall.   The homewares department may be small, but it is amazing what you'll find. Again, on this last shopping expedition, I discovered Riedel wine glasses. I was in no need of glasses, but I bought a couple boxes to tuck away in a closet for future gifts.   I'll still stop by the Rock Hill store when I'm in that area, but this is my go to Stein Mart for now.   Will I return: Absolutely   When: December 20, 2017 Why: Shopping for me......

The time has come to write my 900th review on Yelp and I couldn't pick a better restaurant to celebrate my milestone. Some say, our city is becoming over saturated with fried chicken restaurants. I say, that isn't so. So many of them are boring and flavorless, but not Byrd & Barrel. Byrd & Barrel is flavorful buttermilk fried chicken, a true "Southern" delight.  I am so glad that the owners had the courage to put their restaurant in the Marine Villa neighborhood. There are so many great neighborhoods in our city and each one has its own personality and B&B found a perfect match. They renovated an old Popeye's and opened it with a rustic feel.   It was a busy night, but we were able to be immediately seated at the bar. We had checked the menu out on line, so we quickly ordered our appetizers. We had to try the Fried Chicken Skins and South Side Poutine. I am glad we tried the Fried Chicken Skins, but I would not order them again. They were crunchy and covered in a gooey sauce, but I found them to be flavorless. However, the South Side Poutine was the opposite. It was extremely flavorful, with cheese curds, tater tots, smoked chicken and mushroom gravy served on a 1/4 sheet pan. Double an order and you've gotten an entree for me. Add a cold beer and you've got a great lunch.  If you're having appetizers, you must have a drink from the specialty cocktail menu. I enjoyed a Jack's Fork; Daniel's whiskey, tea, orange juice, lime juice and topped with Vess Peach soda.  So refreshing, it almost went do to fast. Ms. Norma enjoyed The Big Piney; Bombay Sapphire and San Pellegrino Grapefruit soda. All the specialty cocktails are created by mixologist at other bars, but credit is given where credit is due on the menu. The specialty cocktails sold for $6.   Now on to the stars of the night, our fried buttermilk chicken. What I love, is that you can order your pieces ala carte. I love wings and breast, so adding two sides made a meal for me. For my sides I selected Mac-n-Cheese and Cole Slaw. My chicken was served piping hot and crisp. At first I was concerned how dark my chicken was, but once I bite into it, it was juicy and done to perfection. The seasoning and flavor was all the way through to the bone.   The Cole Slaw is a creamy Kale Slaw and is definitely the best slaw I have ever had. If you go, take my word and order it as your side. My Mac-n-Cheese was creamy, but lacked flavor. I think the lack of flavor is due to the fact that it is made with Provel. I thought the red hot triplets would have added some kick, but not so much. However, to my surprise the leftover that I took home were better cold.   Service at the bar was a little slow and the bartender got argumentative with two patrons that were wanting to place carry-out orders. The customer may not always be right, but there is no need to argue with them in front of other patrons.  Otherwise, all the servers are personable and look like metro lumberjacks.   I definitely will be returning for this succulent chicken.   When: September 26, 2015 Why: Dinner

CRAZY. Just call me Crazy. I go to an Irish Pub for lunch and what do I order, a Grilled Tuna Steak Sandwich. At an Irish Pub, what was I thinking? I don't know, but I'm glad that I ordered it. It was damn good.   I'll backtrack to that amazing sandwich, but let's start at the very beginning a very good place to start. When you read you begin with A, B, C. When dinning at an Irish Pub you begin with A Beer and Chicken Wings. A cold Guinness and a pound of Chicken Wings. Not the best wings in STL, but I am adding them to my list of Favorite Wings. They were meaty and coated with just enough sauce. The sauce provided just enough "bam wow" to make them memorable. A cold Guinness is a cold Guinness, enough said.   The other half ordered John D McGurks Burger with bacon and bleu cheese. He swears it tasted as good as it looked and it looked flavorful. Like a magnet to iron, I'm usually drawn to anything with bacon. However today, I choose a different path and ordered Tuna.   Now, let's talk about that awesome Grilled Tuna Steak Sandwich. I love Tuna Steaks, Salmon, Swordfish any of those type seafood steaks grilled. So when I saw it as a sandwich I had to order one. It was simple and out of this world.   The Tuna was grilled to a perfect rare temperature. It was then placed between two slices of Toasted Wheat Bread with lettuce, tomato, onion and lemon basil mayo. Whoa, I am not a mayo person, but this mayo made this tuna pop. I am so glad that I took another path today and did not got with the usual Irish Pub grub.   Both the tuna and burger came with Irish Chips and I must say these too, were done perfectly. My experience with Irish Chips, is they are overly fried and come out brown, nasty and too crunchy. These were light in color, crisp, not greasy and a perfect compliment to our sandwiches.   Now the other shoe is going to drop. The service today was off, off big time. It was a glorious day outside and they seemed shocked that everyone was wanting to be on the patio. The hostess actually asked us if we were sure we wanted to sit outside. To be seated outside we had to sit at the bar which was okay, but our service was slow. It was noon and they seemed to be short staffed and disorganized. Other patrons put at the bar were commenting about it as well.   I hope it was just an off day and this isn't what popularity has caused McGurks service to become. Because it was down right sad and embarrassing.

Sometimes when you visit a neighborhood restaurant on the frequent, you forget to update your  reviews. I had no idea that I had not updated my opinion of Adam's since my initial review. With Adam's being on Ian Froeb's Top 100 STL Restaurants for 2016, it is time to update my review.   Numerous times when I have come for lunch, I have selected their signature smoked salami as one of my meats when doing the Pick 2 Plate. It has always been a perfect companion for my other two favorites beef brisket or turkey breast. Today I went with Ian's "Must Order" and enjoyed the Salami Sandwich (6 oz).   As I order my sandwich, the cashier recommended adding brown mustard as my condiment. Being a fan of brown instead of yellow mustard, I grabbed a couple of packets to try on my sammie. For some he may be right, but not for me. I agree whole heartedly with Ian, give me a dab of Cranberry Cayenne Sauce (my favorite) and that sandwich is a winner.  I am not a fan of white bread, but it was fresh and soft. What I think would make this sandwich go over the top is a hearty beefsteak rye. I think next time I'll get mine to go and rebuild it at home.   My two sides always seem to be the same, or at least one of them does. I love their pit beans, I think they're most likely one of the best if not the best in the local BBQ joints. Their overly creamy and sweet cole slaw has grown on me and slowly has won me over. I normally prefer an oil & vinegar cole slaw, but this one has it's merits.   Some would say, the staff is overly friendly. I say it is southern down-home hospitality. They just want everyone to feel welcomed and they treat everyone as if they were from the immediate neighborhood. That is why Adam's is in the Top 100 Restaurants in STL - it has good food and good service.   When: March 16, 2016 Why: Lunch & STL Top 100

Great shoe store, especially for women. If a lady has an addiction to shoes, this is the place to shop for variety and price.   If it is so great, why am I giving them only 3 Stars? It is because of my feet. I have wide fat feet and DSW does not always have my width. If I had normal feet, I would definitely give them 5 Stars and I'd have a closet, just for shoes.   The selection for men is not as large as the ladies, but they still offer a good variety of; dress, casual, boots and athletic shoes. Some visits, I can walk out with a couple pairs, other times it is just one pair. The majority of my visits I walk out empty handed, due to my size.   I give major kudos to the staff, they are always helpful and willing to check warehouse inventory and to see if the shoe I like comes in a wide.   Like #41, George H. W. Bush, I enjoy a colorful sock and DSW has an excellent selection to choose from.   I'll be back? - I keep checking for my size.   When: December 3, 2018 Why: Brown Casual Shoe

It's been almost three years since my last review of Basso and I am still a fan. It is a solid 4 Star restaurant. It continues you please me each and every time I visit them. My most recent visit was for a quick dinner before I headed over to The Fox & Hound for a wine tasting. I figured it was also a great time to try their, Mafalda which Ian Froeb said was a "must order" on his STL 100 list.   I've been dieting to lose, what I call my Yelp weight, but tonight I thought what the hell and went ahead and ordered the Mafalda. It's a flavorful pasta dish of ribbon cut noodles toss in a beef and pork ragu, with pecorino and romano cheeses and breadcrumbs. I like how the blend of the two cheeses and breadcrumbs add a thickness to the ragu. I was impressed with the richness of Italian flavor from a restaurant that is not located on "The Hill".   It may not have been the best choice to accompany a pasta dish, but my Manhattan was a true classic. They make each drink from scratch, so it takes time, be patient please a for hand crafted cocktail. If you cannot wait for a masterfully prepared cocktail, I suggest you order one of their many craft beers instead. You'll have plenty to choose from and you'll be just as happy. After all it is called "happy hour".   When: April 12, 2016 Why: Dinner, Happy Hour and STL 100

The French Market Inn was my home away from home for my 4 days and 3 nights in the French Quarter. I found them by chance on the internet when I clicked on FrenchQuarter.com.  The photos, location and price were good. Then when I looked at reviews on Yelp, I was sold.  I am so glad I selected this hotel and I'd recommend it to anyone who is visiting the FQ.   My room was on the third floor in a semi-tower structure off the courtyard. There were only three rooms on the floor with a fourth one whose entrance was in the stairwell. When I first arrived at my room, I was concerned at how close I was to the elevator (take note of pic). However, I quickly learned that I had no worries. With only 1 floor above me and 4 rooms per floor, I rarely heard it in use. When I did, it was extremely quite and did not disturb me at all.   The room was a King Bed Deluxe room and it was well appointed. It was long and narrow, with two windows over looking the courtyard. It had a flat screen television, a desk and a small table for two. It also had a keypad safe in the closet. Also, in the closet was a iron and ironing board which always comes in handy. A small refrigerator would have gotten them a fifth star.   No tub, but a walk in shower big enough for two made it a stellar bathroom for me. The towels were soft and sized for an average man. They offered a few complimentary toiletries, but I never pay attention to those, as I'm picky and always bring my own.   The front desk associates and the concierge desk were friendly and helpful. This boutique hotel is on the outskirts of the French Quarter and a few blocks walk to Bourbon Street, which I liked. If I was closer to Bourbon Street, I might have gotten into more trouble....LOL. It was nice to have a relaxing stroll to and from all the excitement in the Quarter.   When I return to the French Quarter,  I will be checking the availability of this refreshing boutique hotel for a second stay.   When: August 26-29, 2016 Why: Small vacation

After seeng a double feature at LPFC, I figured it was time to write an update to my review. When I re-read my previous review, I realized much had not changed and I honestly could cut and paste a couple of paragraphs. Wonder if Yelp allows that?   Any way, I still love that this theatre is more like an art house, in that it brings independent and foreign films to the STL market. The selection of movies alone, is why I bumped them up to 4 Stars. As stated in my previous review, the size of theaters are small with a gradual slope in the seating. The seats do not recline, but are comfortable for my size and they have a cup holder. I felt very relaxed while I watched my movie.   Where I could cut & paste in the following paragraph:  It was a nice touch that the projectionist came in before the movie and introduced himself. He also talked about the theater, services and thanked us for choosing Landmark. That was customer service you'd never see at a Mega theater. (This is a simple touch, that I like.)  As my previous review, the concession stand employees are always the problem. One young Millennial got flustered and kept calling for help from her co-workers. She finally gave a big sigh, looked at me and said, "I guess I can go ahead and take your order." I only needed a small popcorn and soda. She managed to pull herself together and provide me with my movie treats. Once she completed my order, she insisted she needed help. (They were not that busy.)  As stated in my previous review, do not be intimidated by the location of this small boutique theater. It may be located in an upscale mall, but it welcomes everyone who love a good movie. When parking, I highly recommend parking on the backside of the mall and use the mall entrance down from Saks Fifth Avenue. If you use this entrance, when you go up the steps into the mall - the theater is directly ahead of you.   Go see a movie and be entertained.   When: January 4, 2017 Why: Double Feature

Smallcakes came to my rescue and helped me save a birthday celebration at work. I had been off for a couple of days and when I returned, co-workers informed me that it was our gluten-free co-worker's birthday. Being the group party planner, my response was, "What? Are you sure?" Lucky for me she was off today, so it gave me a day to plan and organize. We'll just celebrate her b-day a day late.   I started calling around to some of my favorite bakeries and was having no success. Finally, I thought of Smallcakes and gave them a call. Yippie, they had gluten-free cupcakes. Lucky for me, I was already in Kirkwood running another errand, so it was an easy stop. What made it even better, I was able to select the icing for each of the four cupcakes.  To give our birthday girl a variety, I selected; Pink Vanilla, Wedding Cake, Chocolate and Birthday Cake. All four were boxed up in a pretty pink box.   The young lady working was also the one I spoke with on the phone. She was professional on the phone and a delight in the store. Her personality was perky and bubbly, just what you'd expect at a cupcake store. Her suggestions and ideas were spot on.   Next time I need cupcakes, I'll remember Smallcakes as the one who rescued me.   I'll be back? - Sure, thing.   When: May 17, 2018 Why: Work Birthday Celebration

Did St. Louis really need another craft beer taproom? Of course, we did.  A city can never have too many brew hubs. Especially when the city was just named #1 for Best Beer Scene 2018 by USA Today.   BHT is tucked away and kind of hidden on Oakland, but it is a great addition for the city and area. So many restaurants have come and gone in this space, but I think this one is going to make it.   During my first visit, I was alone and sat at the bar for lunch. The bartender was attentive and helped me select my Flight of Four Beers. My favorite of the four was one she suggested, KeyBilly. I'm looking forward to coming back and trying their Chicken Wings which are made with the same beer.   Talking with the bartender, I mentioned I was a fan of lamb and she then recommended the Lamb Burger. I'll admit it was not as good as 5 Stars or Scottish Arms, but for the price I was damn impressed. I'd definitely order it again. No fries here, all burgers and sandwiches are served with a side of Brew Hub Chips. They are house made and crisp. They're a nice change from the standard fries at bars.   As stated, the service was attentive and friendly. They have free Wi Fi which is great for those of us who are addicted to social media. Gotta stay connected to; Yelp, Untappd, Instagram and Twitter.   I'll Be Back? - With a friend in tow.   When: March 13, 2018 Why: Lunch at the Bar

Thai Table is a delightful addition to the Maplewood restaurant scene. It's in a inconspicuous space on Manchester, so look for the Escape Room and you'll find Thai Table. They actually share a main door then you go through a second door for either business.   When I first heard of TT, I thought it was going to be a order at the counter and carry-out restaurant with perhaps a few tables for those who choose to eat in. Yes, they do a lot of carry-out business, but to my surprise they offer table service for those who want to dine in and it is very friendly and attentive.   I started my experience with Crab Rangoon. The menu stated it was made with spicy cream cheese and they were not kidding. I really liked that it had that little extra kick. They were served to my table so piping hot, I had to take a pause to let them cool down. They were delicious, so I am looking forward to trying the Spring Rolls on my next visit.   My entree, Pad Kee Mao with beef was extremely impressive. I choose spice level, medium and still felt the slight burn in the back of my throat. Don't get me wrong, that is a good thing. I enjoyed this dish more then I did the exact same dish at a Thai restaurant downtown last week. This dish did not have the plate presentation of the downtown restaurant, but it exceeded on flavor. The presentation here was more like your friends mom or your favorite aunt is in the kitchen and was filling your bowl. They want to make sure you have plenty to eat and it was scooped up with love.   The ambiance is minimal. Most of the walls are bare and one wall had many-be four pictures. There's nothing fancy about this place at all.  The prices are totally affordable, you're not paying for ambiance in addition to the food.  As stated early on, the table service was friendly and attentive. The young lady was served me, asked me questions to make sure I was ordering what I actually was craving. She also, followed up with couple of visits to make sure I was enjoying my meal.   There's no booze, but I can eat a meal without a cocktail. I enjoyed a glass of ice tea and they kept it full while I dined.   I'll be back? - Most definitely.   When: October 22, 2018 Why: Dinner and it's Hot & New

What? I am shocked that I have not written an updated review for Piccadilly for four years. I am, bad. I was just there Friday night and ordered something new for me off their regular menu. So, it is time to update. I'll sing praises to my new discovery and give a few shout outs to some of my all time favorites.   My new discovery was the, Fresh Salmon Filet. Not that it is important for me, but this entree is completely Gluten Free. The filet was grilled to perfection and served with steamed broccoli. It also came with a side of gourmet greens tossed lightly in their house Italian dressing. This is a perfect meal for someone dieting, who loves Salmon or those who do require the gluten-free entree.   Some of my all-time favorites are; The Famous Piccadilly Fish Sandwich. It is one of the best and most perfect dinners during Lent and other times, too. During Lent and occasionally through out the year, they'll add a Seafood Pot Pie to their offerings. It is as amazing as the famous Chicken and Beef Pot Pies offered year round.   Two of my biggest favorites are specials they offer on the regular. During the summer months they'll serve up one of the most tender and delicious pork steaks. They are huge! Rarely am I able to eat the entire steak. The sides change with the special, but they've never disappointed me. They're always a perfect pairing.   My final favorite and biggest shout out is for the Smoked Prime Rib. It is usually offered on Saturday night. If you go and it is the special, order it.  It is big, juicy, tender and smoked, just like you'd expect from a steakhouse.   I enjoy sitting on the back patio when a small table is available. It is enclosed and has heaters during the colder months. If they are extremely busy, I'll sit at the bar to allow to enjoy the tables.   All the staff is friendly and remember the regulars. I'll admit, I have my favorites, but I'm provided good service by all.   Oh, before I forget. I gotta give one last favorite. The Piccadilly Manhattan is my go to cocktail here.   Will I return? - Damn straight, I will. Especially on a Saturday night.   When: December 15, 2017 +many more Why: Home-Cooked Dinner

It's a drug store. A chain drug store and it meet my needs.   I was at the dentist awhile back and they took my blood pressure before they started work on my implants. I was a BP monitor style that I had not seen before and it was a CVS brand. Instead of a regular cuff that I'd have to put around my arm, this one slipped over the wrist. So easy.   My regular doctor wants me to check my BP on the regular, so I came here to buy one. It was an easy find in the store and a great value when compared to the Omron brand also available in the store.   Store was well organized and the staff was able to answer my questions about my investment in a new BP monitor.   I'll be back? - I own stock in Walgreen's, but I just may be back to this                         store. They did a good job.

Need new kitchen knives, shop Bertarelli.  Need your current kitchen knives sharpened, take them to Bertarelli.   Need some new gadget for the kitchen, shop Bertarelli. My favorite gadget was battery powered pepper mill. It was so cool.  Customer Service is great.

When dining at Adam's Smokehouse, I am a creature of habit. I am a big, big fan of their ribs. I love the rub and the crispy glaze that they put on their ribs. They are seasoned so well, that I do not use any additional bbq sauces on them when eating. Also, their ribs are extremely meaty. In fact, they are so meaty, that I have made an entire meal out just eating the ribs and saving my sides for the next day.   Another of their offerings, that wins me over every time it is a special offering, is their Burnt Ends. Chunks of tender beef, with a crisp coating. If I'm lucky enough, I order two plates. One to enjoy immediately and the second to enjoy the next day at work for lunch.   As I stated in my review last year, I do not waver from my two sides. The baked beans, aka pit beans are the best from any bbq joint in the city. Also, the more I eat their cole slaw, the more it wins me over. It has totally gotten me to enjoy a creamy slaw. I also enjoy how finely chopped it is, it makes scooping it up on a fork so much easier.   It's a true neighborhood bbq smokehouse. Everyone here is happy and when you leave, you'll have a smile on your face, too.   Will I return? Yes!  When: January 21 & 27, 2017 Why: Ribs & Burnt Ends

I am going to predict the future, I  see Taste being named the best new restaurant in St. Louis for 2011.  If you have heard the expression, "A Taste of Heaven", you will experience it at Taste. Each dish is unique and magical in it's preparation.   We attended one of the soft openings and then went back for dinner when the doors were officially open. The decor is reminiscence of a speak easy during the days of prohibition with a semi romantic twist. Black curtains cover the windows and entry. leading you into a totally private dining experience.   I love the fact that more new restaurants are doing the small plate format. It not only serves you a healthier portion,  but gives you the opportunity to experience more options by sharing. We opted to share, so we could get a good taste of "Taste".   We begun our feast with The Country Terrine. An excellent pate, with a whole grain mustard on the side and slices from a crisp baguette. They offer this is three levels, 1-2-3 depending on the number of terrines you want to try. We then shared a Arugula Salad, that was incredible. I normally do not like anchovies, but the white anchovies in this salad made it pop. The dressing was a simple olive oil and fresh squeezed lemon juice.   Our entrees were the Fish & Chips and Lasagna. Their Fish & Chips are not typical Fish & Chips, they use trout and serve it pan seared. It was unbelievable! I will not share it again, it will be all mine. It was such a good find and to find it during Lent is a double bonus.   The Lasagna will be a favorite of vegetarians through out the city. It is amazing how something so simple can burst with flavor. Four basic ingredients; ricotta, escarole, radishes and parmesan. They then add their magic and presto a lasagna out of the ordinary.   We then cleansed our palate with Rosemary Lime Sorbet before moving on to our desserts. Yes, I guess you could consider the sorbet a dessert, but it this case we were using it as a intermezzo . The sorbet was refreshing.  I would have never thought of adding rosemary in sorbet, the dessert chef is a master of creativity.   Our actual desserts were Sticky Toffee Pudding and Pigwiches.  My favorite was the STP, it's a true English pudding so it is more of a cake with a side of vanilla ice cream. The cake was moist and sauce was full of toffee flavor. The Pigwiches, are two cookies cut into the shape of pigs with a smear of sweet bacon cream between them.  Yummy.  The service is top notch and I love the fact that you can see the magic of preparing your food in the back of the dining room.

This has to be a first for me. I was asked to leave a bar before I could even order my first drink. It appears that Taste Bar has a rule of no standing at their bar and I was violating that rule.   We were celebrating a friends birthday and decided to meet at Taste Bar to enjoy some of Ted Kilgore's libations. What a better way to toast another year of life then with a cocktail made by Ted and his staff. Our birthday girl and escort arrived first and got two seats at the bar. I arrived shortly past six and as I entered was cheerfully greeted by the hostess. I smiled, returned her pleasantries and joined my friends at the bar. Hugged the birthday girl and gave her a fun birthday card.  Once they handed me a drink menu, is when it started to get ugly.   Once I had the drink menu in hand the hostess was on me like white on rice. She tapped me on the shoulder and wanted to know if she needed to get us a table for three. I turned to the others and said, "we're just having drinks aren't we?" When they responded yes, the hostess said,  "We don't allow standing at our bar". I was taken back and responded, "What?" knowing I have stood at this bar many times before.  "We're a small establishment and you standing at the bar makes us look smaller." was her answer with a side of attitude. (She flipped my switch)  I admit I am overweight, but I really doubt my extra 10 lbs. standing at your bar makes your establishment look smaller. It is your attitude and treatment of customers that makes you small. At this point, I just looked at her and said, "Fine, then I will leave." She quickly tried to back pedal, offering to get us a table. However, she did not know how long it would take and while we waited, I COULD NOT STAND AT THE BAR.  This was crazy, I just left.   As I walked to my car, I could not understand the rule so I returned to Taste and asked the hostess who was in charge. She told me Jack the GM, but denied me speaking to him to understand how me standing at the end of the bar to enjoy a birthday cocktail with a friend would effect their ambiance. Again, she said she'd get us a table, but I could not wait at the bar. When asked where do you want me to wait, her response was, "you can't stand at the bar".   No table, can't stand at the bar and wait for a table. What other choice did I have, but to leave. I bought a round of drinks for my friends who were lucky enough to have seats and went home. I'll just have to wait for Ted's new business to open for me to enjoy one of his fabulous cocktails.

Whisker Bones is a fun doggie boutique on Main Street, just down from one of my favorite E-ville restaurants. They offer a variety of services. They not only make all natural & organic treats, they also offer pet photography, grooming and unique pet accessories.   Oh, did I mention the large selection of decorative home accessories? In addition to the countless magnets for your car or whatever.  When I shop, I get frustrated when I see things for dog mom's and nothing for us dad's. Not here, since this doggie boutique is owned by two dog dad's, there was plenty of dad stuff for me to choose from. I'm also obsessed with the color orange and I found the cutest paw print bowl.   The staff is friendly and helpful. Even though I live on the Westside of the river, I signed up for their rewards program. I come over frequently enough to eat at some of my favorite restaurants. Now that I have discovered WBS, I'm be stopping by every time I come to E-ville to dine.   Will I return - You know it.   When: August 31, 2017 Why: I'm a sucker for a doggie boutique

My yearly update for Adam's and I am upgrading them to 5 Stars.  I love their ribs. I mean, I truly LOVE their ribs. Half a rack or a Full rack, they are delicious. The way they torch the glaze on to those delicious ribs is amazing. My mouth waters for them, as I write this update.   To repeat myself about the sides; I do not waver - I order their creamy cole slaw and the pit beans with burnt ends. Even as I am doing a low-carb diet, I cannot resist their pit beans. If you like the cole slaw at KFC, this slaw will blow your taste buds away. It is so similar, yet so much better in my opinion.   I am also a big fan of their mouth watering burnt ends. To be honest, I have been known to take them home and toss them with buttered egg noodles. Serve them up with a side salad and you've got a great meal.   Staff here is always friendly. It amazes me how they remember the majority of their regulars name. To be called by name as you enter, is a nice touch.   I'll be back? - They serve the best ribs in the city  When: May 26, 2018 Why: Memorial Week-End BBQ

After shopping the little boutiques on Argonne, we continued down the drive to Billy G's. We ordered a variety of appetizers and called it lunch.
