We arrived at1:30PM on a Monday and were surprised at how busy the restaurant was. That in itself tells you how good the food must be.    We started off, Pretzel Bites. Being bite size, they were easier to manage then tearing off a huge bavarian pretzel.  They're served with a White Cheddar Cheese Sauce. It was good, but I would have liked something with a little more spiciness to it.   My cousin aka dining partner for the day, ordered the Sweet Chili Crab Cakes as her lunch. They were hand blended lump crab cakes over baby greens and served with a sweet chili remoulade. The cakes were thick and huge in circumference. The serving is large enough to share and she did. I ended up eating one of them and I'd say they were as good as those you'd get at Peacemaker.   I'm a fan of the Trashed Wings here, so that was my appetizer lunch with a side of fries. The Trashed wings are deep fried, then tossed in wing sauce and re-fried until crispy. They're served with little cups of wing sauce and house-made buttermilk ranch dressing. For me, the wings are so tasty, I don't dip them, but I do double dip my fries in both little cups.   It was a non-booze lunch, so we both enjoyed refreshing glasses of iced tea.   The service was attentive and friendly. Surprisingly the food from the kitchen came out very quickly considering how busy they were.   I'll be back? - Yes, big fan of their patio in good weather.   When: November 19, 2018 Why: Shopping in Kirkwood

Very nice hotel. I stayed here for a wedding in Alton and we had a block of rooms for the weekend. The staff was very professional and accommodating. I personally was impressed with how friendly the entire staff was. Every time I passed a hotel employee, they spoke and gave some type of personalized greeting wishing me a great day.   I lucked out and got a room on the top floor. It had a view of the atrium and pool. Noise from the pool was minimal and did not bother me at all.  My bed was a king sized pillow top and had the right combination of firmness and softness for a comfy nights sleep. Best part of the room was the A/C. My room was chilly, chilly cold, just the way I like to sleep snuggled up under a blanket.   The bathroom was typical compact sized for a hotel. It had plenty of towels of all sizes and they were soft and fluffy. They had complimentary toiletries just in case you forgot to pack yours'. The second best thing about the room was the rain shower head. There was plenty of hot water and that shower head has me thinking of making changes at my home. It was so relaxing.   Other perks of my room and this hotel were:  A real closet, not just a rack in the open. Safe for valuables in the bottom of said closet.  Icebox and Microwave in room. Free Wi-Fi Complimentary Breakfast - Buffet in the lobby  The only downside of the hotel is the humidity in the lobby. That problem I blame on the architecture and mother nature. With all the glass in the atrium, a swimming pool and the hot weather outside, the a/c just could keep that big space cool.   Oh, before I close, I gotta tell you to check in on Yelp. When you do, you'll get a coupon for a "FREE" beverage at Great Rivers, the bar attached to the hotel. That's a win.   I'll be back? - If I need a hotel in Alton.   When: June 29 & 30, 2018 Why: In Alton for wedding.

I don't get the love for this place at all. I have tried this place numerous times with friends and each time we all walk out scratching our heads. The service is minimal at best. Our most recent visit, we were the only ones sitting at the upstairs bar and we still had a hard time getting waited on. The young lady working that bar treated us as if we were an inconvenience and an interruption to her night.  We drank half of our cocktails, which were made very amateurish and left.   There are too many other bars in Saint Louis where you can get a professional and masterfully made cocktail, so I suggest you take a pass on Planter's House.

Oh, Happy Day! I absolutely love it when I get to remove a business from my Terrible Two's List and double their rating. My visit on a Saturday night was so stellar, that I went back the very next night and took a friend to experience the greatness.  St. Louis Magazine did an article naming 6 Burger Spots that you should visit right now and Planter's House was one of them. I had never had their burger, so I thought this was the opportune time to re-visit and see if I not only could remove them my TTL, but have a good burger as well.  My visit accomplish both goals.   This visit I opted to sit at the main bar, to enjoy a cocktail before my burger. Since it World Whiskey Day (May 21), i ordered a Manhattan - Planter's House Style. It totally rocked my world. I'm pretty sure it was the best Manhattan I have ever had. I sipped it slowly as I savored the two bourbons and their house vermouth served up as any Manhattan should be.   I wanted a little nosh to accompany my Manhattan, so I ordered the Sambal Pickled Egg. It is pickled in house, so it is freshly done. It's a single egg sliced in half and served in a small ramekin, drizzled with Sambal sauce. The sauce was spicy, but not to hot. Making it a dish that can be enjoyed by everyone.   It was time to order my burger, but I needed another cocktail to accompany it. Wanting to stay with the World Whiskey theme, the bartender recommended; Whiskey Kiss. It was so refreshing with the mixture of rye, raspberry liqueur, Cocchi Rose and lime, that I could see myself sipping this poolside later this summer.  It was the perfect cocktail for the burger, so glad I didn't switch over to a cold beer.   Now for the main attraction of the evening and what brought me back for another visit, the Burger. STL Mag is right, this definitely a burger you should experience. It's made of two 4 oz patties, instead of a big thick 8 oz making it easier to bite and chew. The patties are topped with a white cheddar puree, smoked Worcestershire,  cole slaw and pickled mustard seed on a challah bun. It truly hit the spot, after a 10 hour work day.  It was perfectly cooked to my specifications, medium rare. Normally, I am not a fan of mustard, but I enjoyed the pickled mustard seed. It gave me a new perspective on mustard.   My burger came with a side of House Fries and you get to select your salt from 3 different seasonings. I went with the Habanero - I wanted mine to have some kick to them. The serving portion was smaller then most other places, which is perfect to me. They're a side dish, not the main attraction. Besides, I have no self control with fries, if you give me a heaping plate, I'll eat them all. So having a normal serving with my cup of ketchup, made my burger even more perfect.   As stated I returned the very next night with a friend and below is an abridged review of what we had:   Cocktails: In A Pickle, Fountain of Youth, Bramble and Purgatory  Appetizers: House Fries and Reuben Gourgeres   Entrees: Duck Confit and Lamb Belly Mac & Cheese   Cocktails all got double thumbs up. House Fries really kicked it for my friend. The Reuben Goourgeres were just okay. I loved my Lamb Belly Mac & Cheese. I would have even loved it without the lamb belly, it was that delicious and creamy. My friend liked her duck confit, but she is not a fan of spicy and there were jalapeños in it. We picked the jalapeños out and I added them to my mac & cheese - double win for me.   Service both nights was attentive and friendly. Good food, good booze and attentive service gets Planter's House off my Terrible Two's List. Congratulations, Planter's House for winning me back - I'm sure I'll now be a regular.   When: May 21 & 22, 2016 Why: STL Magazine recommended the burger

What the Cookies?  That is a polite way of saying, "what the F".   My advice to Grandma is to remove all those working Tuesday from her will.  I was so looking forward to her cookies after reading such great reviews here on Yelp. I was doing my "local" holiday shopping on Main Street and wanted a sweet treat to munch as I strolled & shopped in historic Saint Charles. Three times I visited her tiny shop and not once did anyone acknowledge me or offer me service.   My first visit,  as I approached the counter I noticed there were only three (green) sugar cookies on display. I stood there reading the sign and waiting for the woman who was standing in the doorway to the kitchen with her back to the shop to offer assistance. She glanced at me once and said nothing, but continued to chat with her coworkers. I left in disappointment.   I continued to shop and as I passed Grandma's a second time, I thought for sure more fresh cookies would be fresh out of the oven. I entered a second time, and same three cookies on display. No staff to be seen, only heard in the back. This time I was vocal and called out a friendly, "hello". I would have bought the sugar cookies.  No one answered or responded to my call out.  Again, I left in disappointment.   Why I gave them a third try after finishing my shopping is beyond me, but I did.  Guess what, same three cookies on display. This time I noticed one of the booths was filled with day old  or it could have been 4 day old cookies being sold at a reduced price. Okay, I'll give them a try, only if someone would wait on me.   There was a lot of commotion in the back and finally a man on a phone came out and sat down at the other booth that was covered in paperwork. He kept yelling a woman's name and no one responded to him. He said, nothing to me. He could have informed me someone would be out shortly, but he did not. All he did was yell her name again and continue talking on the phone. I turned and left for a third time and I will never return. Three strikes and you are off my shopping list.

I never thought I'd be impressed with delivery from a fast food pizza joint, but this Domino's has done exactly that.   About a month ago, I wrote a review about another pizza delivery service and how disappointed I was. Thanks to a Yelp friend (Lavanya N.) who read my review, she immediately turned me on to Domino's and her favorite order. I must say, she was totally right.   When I decided to try her recommendation, I originally planned to use the Domino's near my home. However, I got the craving this past Monday at work and ordered her favorite. OMG! I never would have thought to mix jalapeños (a personal favorite) with pineapple. The true secret for this combo is the, garlic parmesan white sauce on top of a thin crust.   This pizza was perfect for me. I enjoyed the cracker crisp crust and the spicy sauce. Not to mention the jalapeños. Then the sweetness of the pineapple, blended well with the heat of the peppers. In addition to the pizza, I ordered a small order of their Parmesan Bread Knots.  They went well with the salad that I packed as my original lunch.   Last time I ordered from Domino's was almost six years ago, they definitely have upped their game. Next time I was pizza delivery at home or work, I'll be calling Domino's. I like how you can follow the progress of your order with their tracker. They keep you informed step by step.   I'll be back? - Yep.   When: April 29, 2019 Why: Lunch time pizza craving.

Taste Bar, you blew me away last night. I've always known you were good, but last night was exceptional. My cocktails were masterfully prepared, the fries were crisp and plentiful and my scallops were scrumptious. It was a night of pure perfection.   I may over over indulged in the cocktails, but after the smoothness and perfection of my first one, I just wanted more and more. I started out with my usual, a Manhattan. The bartender asked if I wanted it up or on the rocks, I choose up. It was served chilled perfectly, and the mixture of the bourbon, vermouth, with the bitters was spot on. It was a perfect cocktail to sip as I munched on my fries.   Now let's talk about those fries. OMG! They were served in a bowl and piled as high as the rafters. When they were placed in front of me, I could hear Diana Ross singing, Ain't No Mountain High Enough. There were so many crispy shoestring type fries, that I asked a young lady seated next to me if she'd like to share. She graciously accepted, which I was thankful for, as it was way to much for even this foodie.   My next  cocktail was my second most ordered, an Old Fashioned. My heart skipped a beat, as it was absolutely the best Old Fashioned I've had in STL. It was severed with one large cylinder type ice cube and a sliver of orange peel. It was so smooth and refreshing. It went perfectly with my Scallops.   Anyone who knows me well, knows I have a deep love for Scallops. They are my absolute favorite seafood. I follow TB on FB and when I saw they had added them as an entree to their menu, I got here as fast as my work and social schedule would let me.   My entree was six huge sea scallops, I prefer sea over bay. I'm going to give it to you straight from the menu - XO marmalade, cornbread-pistachio crumble, celery root pumpkin seed oil. Let me tell you, the crumble had my toes curling and my taste-buds doing a happy dance. The menu also tells you that, "large plates" requires a longer cooking time. Trust me, it is well worth the wait. Enjoy a cocktail as you wait, it really isn't that long.   For dessert, I had another cocktail. If they did a masterful job with a Manhattan and a Old Fashioned, I had to see what they'd do with a Sazerac. I've traveled to the City of New Orleans where this cocktail is famous and those bartenders need to come try one at TB to see how they're suppose to be done. It was a wonderful finale to a great meal.   The young man seated next to me enjoyed a Pork Burger and when it was presented to him, I couldn't resist taking a picture. I'm a Yelper, it just comes natural. He asked me if I've had on before and I assured him that I had, but my heart belongs to scallops.   Being seated at the bar as usual, both bartenders on duty were friendly and attentive to all of us. I appreciate their friendliness and professionalism.   I'll be back? - Absolutely   When: December 13, 2019 Why: Scallops now a featured Large Plate

This review is based on multiple visits and is an average score. For breakfast Chris' gets a 4 and for dinner he get only a 2 which averages out to a 3. The breakfast that I have enjoyed here have been awesome, but the dinners have not fared so well.  My advice to Chris is  concentrate on breakfast or work on improving your dinner options.   My favorite breakfasts here are:  Biscuit & Gravy Platter - Two biscuits with gravy & two eggs. I always get a side of Hash Browns. I have them do my hash browns extra crispy. The grill cooks at Chris' understand extra crisp.   Country Fried Steak - Come with 2 eggs, hash browns and your choice of toast or pancakes. My choice is always is pancakes - yummy. Chris does pancakes better then IHOP and they specialize in pancakes.   Country Omelet - A hearty sausage, onion, hash browns & cheddar cheese omelet covered in country gravy.   Veggie Omelet - 3 egg omelet with broccoli, spinach, mushrooms and tomato. I love steamed broccoli, but I don't like it in my omelet so I always have them hold the broccoli and it is still damn good.   My two biggest dinner disappointments:  Slab of Ribs - Not good, dry and over sauced. The mixed vegetables were unseasoned and over steamed meaning limp and flavorless. Baked Potato was over baked, almost to a burnt taste.   Fried Chicken - Dry, totally flavorless and definitely in the deep fryer way to long. The veggies and baked potato were the same as the rib dinner. If I were not eating on a BOGO coupon I would have sent this meal back.   I highly recommend Chris' for breakfast, but not dinner. The customer service is average, it a hit or miss and you just need to deal with it.
This review is going to be short and direct.  Popcorn - Stale. (They should be embarrassed)  Customer Service - Poor & Unfriendly.  Flavors - Unique. (Saved them from getting a lone star rating)

Costco has everything, they just don't have everything all the time. It's a wholesale club, so all items are not available at all times. They offer items at the best prices, so availability changes. Deal with it and adjust your shopping to save big dollars at check-out.   My favorite areas are meats, frozen foods, cleaning supplies, toiletries and canned goods. Meats are amazingly high quality.  I can package them with my FoodSaver and save big $'s. I also can save on future meals with selected frozen food and canned goods. I like the frozen salmon and some beef patties. They both make it easy for work lunches and quick dinners. Their canned goods are priced better then shopping at a grocery store with double coupons.   You can't find better deals on cleaning supplies and toiletries then Costco. For a single person, they'll last forever, or you can share your super savings with your BFF. That way you'll both be clean and be living in a super clean house.   Another area to always check out while shopping, is the clothes. You'll be surprise at what you'll find. I am amazed at the designers that are periodically available and the prices shock me. You may not be dressed to the 9's, but you'll feel like you are with the savings.   I'll be back? - I'm a member and loyal shopper.   When: June 19, 2018 Why: I shop twice a month...it's my stock up store.

It is with great pride that I am happy to announce that I am increasing my  rating from 4 to 5 Stars for Dogtown Gallery & Frame Shop. No pun intended, but Jaynelle knocked this one out of the ballpark for me. She framed all of my 2011 World Series memorabilia.   I had my treasures tucked away, waiting to find the right person I could trust with my  Jon Pils signed 11-11 print and my three World Series tickets. I wanted this framing and matting to match my framed memories from the 2006 World Series. The 11 in 11 World Series meant a lot to me. My birthday is 11 - 11, so I felt a special connection. After seeing how Jaynelle did such a fantastic job on a poster, I knew she was the one I could trust.   I brought my print, tickets and my framed 2006 art work in to the shop for Jaynelle to see. She was very detailed, she not only made notes, but she took pictures too. This way she had a visual reference to what I wanted. We discussed things and made a few little minor adjustments, for the good.   I love my finished product. My only wish now is for the Cardinals to win another World Series so I can have Dogtown Gallery and Frame Shop frame more winning tickets.

I'm giving Jet's 4 Stars for the simple reason that they sell their pizza by the slice. There are so many times that I crave pizza, but go without because I do not want to order an entire pizza pie. Now I can stop by Jet's, enjoy a single or two slices of pizza and be satisfied. I can grab it and go home, or sit down at one of the several tables available in their small dining room.   I've also ordered an entire pizza for pick up. I live so close it is quicker to pick up then to have one delivered. I like having the option of adding flavor to the crust, it gives it a extra kick of flavor. Their sauce has a sweet tang, they are generous with the toppings and cheese. Being  a chain, provel is not the primary cheese.   The staff is friendly and the facility is super clean. It's a chain, but it is still a nice addition to my hood.

Another great lunch at Katie's, is eatable proof that it is so deserving of it's place on the STL 100 Restaurants. Ian's, "must order" for Katie's was the Cured Meats pizza. I'm not a fan of things that are overly salty, so typicallly I would have avoided this pizza. However on this day, I took a chance and ordered it and I am glad that I did.    As usual, I asked that I be seated at the bar for easement and comfort. Since beer is the most perfect beverage to accompany pizza, so I ordered a Tropical Pale Ale from Boulevard Brewing Co..Believe it or not, there is no way I could ever eat an entire pizza by myself. So, I like that during lunch Katie offers personal sized pizzas along with a half salad. It not only easier on the waist size, but the budget as well.   This outing, I went with the Market Vegetable Chop Salad. It was a good mix of current fresh vegetables, but it was challenging to fork up. I enjoyed it, but I prefer the Artichoke Salad. As expected, the Cured Meat Pizza was on the salty side, but the flavor and mix of the meats was worth it. It was nothing that an extra sip of beer or water could not balance out. Ian may say, the Cured Meats is a "must order", but I say, Ted's Meatball is a "must order".   The service at Katie's is always professional and attentive. I gotta get back soon and try a pasta dish.   When: May 10, 2016 Why: STL 100 & Lunch

OMG! I have to admit, I had no idea they offered 5 different crust. Seriously, I thought all they had was Deep Dish. Recently I was waiting for my order and as I read the posters and discovered they had five different crust.   Being a fan of STL Thin Crust, I was excited to see that was one of their offerings. My favorite toppings are Italian Sausage or Pepperoni with Jalapeños. Actually, put jalapeños on any pizza and I'll be a happy diner. I also enjoy the flavor of their sauce, for me it has a rich, robust Italian flavor.    I've ordered on-line and have stopped by for a quick pick-up when I've been out and about. Either way, the service has always been quick and friendly. Compared to the other chain pizzerias in my hood, Jet's takes the Blue Ribbon for both flavor and service.   I'll be back? -Definitely, I love a good thin crust pizza.   When: February 24, 2018 Why: Discovered they have thin crust.

When the most positive thing I can say about a new restaurant is the ambiance, "Houston, we have a problem." They've created a very beautiful space to relax and enjoy your meal. However, the most important points of a restaurant, food and service fall short.  I heard some great things about CSS, so when I was in Creve Coeur at lunch time, I stopped by. Being a lone diner, as my usual, I choose to sit at the bar. Looking over the Signature Cocktail list, they had one of my favorites, Smokey Old Fashion. How could I resist? I should have. It was weak and bland with no smokey taste or garnish. However, I did like the water being served in a Cobalt Blue glass.   After reading the entrees, I choose their Mixed Grill, but was told it was sold out. They wouldn't have it until dinner, after they received their delivery.  Bartender explained it was very popular and they sell out of it regularly. I then choose their Crispy Catfish Sandwich with Fries.   Since I was doing a sandwich and not a full entree, I decided to add an appetizer to my lunch. I was torn between the Crab Cakes and the Tempura Green Beans. I asked the bartender and she informed me the crab cakes were really good and were another of their most popular items. I went with the Green Beans, because I wanted a green veggie.  They were crisp and very lightly coated for a tempura item. The sweet and spicy sesame syrup served as a dipping sauce was delightful.   My crispy catfish was an extremely thin piece that was dominated by the bread. I did like the hot peppers as a topping to the catfish. When I choose the sea salt chips as my side the bartender informed me they no longer did them and it was fries. When I asked what type of fries, she replied, steak fries. I love steak fries, they're my favorite. So, I said yes to fries instead of the side salad.   Bartender needs to be educated on the difference in fries. When they arrived with my sandwich, they were Hand-Cut Fries. My second favorite, so I was to upset. However, some thick cut wedges of fries would have been nice.   Service was not that attentive. The bartender was busy talking with the manager on duty. She was friendly, but considering I was the only one at the bar and the restaurant only had three other tables, you'd think the service would be spot on.   They're new, I'm sure they'll overcome these little details and bumps.   I'll be back? - For dinner, I want to try the Mixed Grill  When: May 17, 2019 Why: Hot & New and Lunch

I've been twice and both times I have been pleased with my experience. My first visit, I enjoyed a Pretzel Wrapped Meat made with Cajun Chicken. It had just enough spice and kick. Paired with a large drink, it made a satisfying lunch.   My visit today, I just wanted a snack to hold me over till dinner. I was torn between an order of Nuggets or Two Softies. After looking at the size of the softies and the lowest number of nuggets in an order, I went with the two softies. Being a lover of jalapeños, I had to select the jalapeño cheese sauce for dipping.   It's a very clean operation. As you order at the counter, you have a full view of the kitchen, where they make their tasty pretzels. The staff is young and friendly.   I'll be back? - Next time I'm craving a soft pretzel, this is where I'll go.   When: April 18, 2019 Why: No lunch, needed a snack before dinner.

#curbside open during #pandemic  A big shout out to F&B for offering curbside service while we're all in quarantine. Your burgers, especially the Double Cheeseburger have been a delicious treat during this lockdown.   I've been several times and each visit the service was quick, easy and done in a safe manner. One visit, I thought it was extremely nice that the owner, came to the door, waved and gave a shout of "thanks" to all of us waiting curbside.   My go to is always the Double Cheeseburger with pickle and onion only. I love how they smash that burger patty and get those edges perfectly crisp. Occasionally, I add a side of fries when I'm feeling skinny and they too are always done with a nice crispy crunch.   To show you how good these burger are, I recently had a friend helping me with yard work. When we were finished, I treated him to an F&B burger. He had never been and he loves a good smash/diner type burger with fries. So I figured this would be a great reward for all his hard work.   I ordered him a Double Cheeseburger with everything. He got the works. It had lettuce, tomato, pickles, onion and all the condiments. When we got back to my house, I went inside to get drinks and he took the food to the patio. By the time I got back outside, he had already started to eat. So there is no picture of his with everything. It would have been a great pic.   Now to share his comment, about his burger. He said, it was better than the place I introduced him to last summer and he loved those. Not to call  any place out by name, but I'll tell you they use to be in Dogtown and moved to Cherokee. For those of you who can read between the lines, that is one amazing compliment and he use to be a chef and knows his food.   Will I return: Absolutely. During our lockdown and beyond.  When: Multiple Visits Why: Burger Time

Lily's is a cross between the authentic Mexican restaurants down on Cherokee and a Qudoba. What? I know it is a weird combination, so let me explain. The food is good and authentic reminding me of Cherokee street, but the service is order at a counter  go sit down and that reminds me Qudoba.  We had top shelf Margarita's which are made from scratch and Poppa is proud of his creation. Our dinner was a Lily's Special, Chile Relleno, Chicken Enchilada and a Beef Tamale. I enjoyed all three, you could tell they were hand made with love. We also had appetizers, Queso and Guacamole. Their guacamole is the best I have had in the city, even better then some I've had down on Cherokee.   When your food is ready, the girls or momma bring it to your table and are chatty when making the delivery.  My question is, if you bring the food out why not take the order at the table as well.  I think providing complete table service would add to Lily's experience and may even get an increase in stars and patronage.

I'm going to miss this BB&B. It use to be my go to when I lived in STL. Hell, I'm going to miss BB&B period. I've moved to the IL side of the river and the closest one to me is going to be in Fairview Heights. I may just have to make the drive.   Any way, I was over in the city and since I had a pocket full of BB&B coupons, I thought I'd swing by and pick up a few things for the new house. Toilet brushes are one thing that I have always tossed and start with a new one in a new home. Having two bathrooms, with different finishes, I grabbed a chrome and nickel finished brushes.   I donated my old two slice toaster to my work, so I was in need of a new toaster for home. I upgraded myself to a four slicer with setting for bagels, toast, english muffins, waffles and pastry. Look out Pop-Tarts you've got your own setting on my toaster. I may live alone, but I figure with family near by, I'll be entertaining for breakfast and brunch in the near future.   The associates here are always friendly and check on you regularly as you shop. They want to make sure you are finding everything you need and perhaps really do need, but want. I also, always have to give a thumbs up to the cashiers who make sure you've got your "coupon".   Will I return? - I like them so much, I'll be making the drive.   When: September 30, 2020 Why: Making house pretty.

I hope in 2018 Yelp finally gets their act together and gives us a box to click on for a half star. Clover & Bee is deserving of a little more push towards that 4 Star rating.   The food, like its sister restaurant, Olive & Oak was an amazing 5 Stars.  I enjoyed the Roasted Asparagus. They prepared both the asparagus and poached egg perfectly. The almond pesto and romesco were delightful accompaniments.  Now you're probably wondering if the food was 5 Star, why only a 3 Star rating. The reason for that would be the service. I was taken by surprise that they choose to be a order at the counter set-up. With the high quality food, I was hoping for the same type of service received at O&O.   After ordering, I had to wait until I was given permission to take a seat. I was then seated at the long banister type table down the middle of the dining room. It was very cramped and uncomfortable. The group of four seated next to me actually had them pack up their food to go and left due to the crowdedness.   With the large staff running around delivering food to the markers on tables and the others bussing the tables, it seems feasible to let them be true servers for the tables. Then those that want carry-out can do so at the counter and it would not be as congested.   The food is excellent, you'll enjoy, However, the service is on the level of St. Louis Bread Company without the vibrating pager.

WARNING: This is my harshest review to date. Some folks may be offended by some terminology that I use. I do apologize to those offended, but somethings just have to be stated openly.    I must have hit a bad day, because the only words that come to my mind after my lunch here are, "What a dump". The service was snotty young people who thought they were better then the customers they were assisting and we had to send food back to the kitchen for a redo. The counters were cluttered, disorganized and the area around the soda/tea was yuck.   The cashier was a throw back to the early eighties, a total "Valley Girl". I use that term, instead of the dumb blonde. She had no idea what she was selling. When we informed her it was our first visit and could she recommend something. We got the deer in headlights look. We rephrased our question, "what's popular". This time we got the look of why are you asking me questions. Finally, my friend said, "I guess everything is good" (with a chuckle). Then the light went on in the young girls empty head, "Yeah, everything is good". Well she was wrong, everything is not good.   Now let's talk about the food. My friend had a Yellow Fin Tuna Steak Sandwich, (not on take out menu or website so I do not know the exact name) and I had the Skinny Californian.   Yellow Fin Tuna - Sandwich is huge, served club style with three slices of bread. My friend and I both agreed it would be much better between only two slices. This is the one we needed to send back for a redo. The Tuna was nasty, huge pieces of skin hanging on to it making it difficult to chew.  When my friend asked to send it back the young man working the tables, told her that is the way Tuna is served. My friend informed him that she was eating Yellow Fin Tuna, before he was breast feeding. and she'd like another sandwich. He went to talk to the kitchen and when he came back to remove her plate, you could tell he was not happy.   One of the chef's brought out the new sandwich and waited as my friend inspected the tuna. It was great. He apologized for the earlier one and returned to his kitchen duties.   Skinny Californian - How can a crepe stuffed with Roasted Chicken, Avocado, Bacon, Swiss Cheese, Tomato with Mornay Sauce be bad? By being served inside a rubbery chewy crepe. If we hadn't already sent one item back, mine would have been returned. I ended up eating only the stuffing (which was very good) and very little of the crepe. I know making crepes is an art, and you'd think a place with crepes in it's name would have mastered that art.   As we were leaving my friend thanked the server/busboy and told him that she enjoyed the sandwich and she'd defiantly be back. His reply, "Uh-huh, sure". What happened to, "Thanks, glad you enjoyed your meal. Look forward to seeing you again". The staff (excluding the chef) need an attitude adjustment. I've gotten better service at a greasy spoon.   Don't know what is sadder, the fact that I had a bad experience or the fact that I'm going to give them a second chance. I feel obliged to revisit since I am friends with the wife of one of the owners.   They have free WI-FI, Yippee.

Lowe's selection of table lamps and shades, is pretty amazing for a hardware store. I was searching for some Neo-Classic style lamps and found two here that meet my needs. Not only did they meet my decorating needs, but they came in well beneath my budget requirements.   They sell their lamps and shades separately, so you can totally create the look that is your personality. All you have to do is make sure they have the same code letter.  Its kind of like matching up your Garanimals for a cute children's outfit. "M" shades go with a "M" lamp base and the same for "S" and "L".    Take note of Lowe's full name, it is Lowe's Home Improvement Warehouse. So it is not just a hardware store. You can find many decorative things to make your home, your castle. I have found great window treatments at better prices then BB&B (without a coupon) and patio furnishings.   It may be a chain and a warehouse store, but the selection and prices keep me coming back.

Once Upon a Time, there was a teeny tiny dive bar in south Saint Louis and this teeny tiny bar was called, The Silverleaf Lounge. The bar is full of smoke, serves cheap drinks and is full of characters that would be perfect for a reality show.   CHEAP DRINKS! Seriously, the only way you can enjoy a cheaper drink is to drink at home. We ordered 3 Michelob Ultra's and the bill was only $6.  Don't make the same mistake that I did and that would be asking, "What Schlafly's beer do you have." When I did ask, the response from the bartender was classic. Her eyes bugged out, she pulled her back like a diva and responded, "No, we have AB products."  She put me in my place and had me feeling like a snob for requesting a craft beer...LOL  When drinking in a dive bar, you never know who you will run in to. One of my drinking buddies ran in to one his co-workers from a previous job. Both were surprised to see each other in a dive bar. No need to worry. What happens in a local dive bar is like what happens in Las Vegas, it stays there.   If you are not claustrophobic, go have a drink at The Sileverleaf Lounge. It is an experience everyone in STL should experience.

When you are buying a "birthday" rib eye, you don't want it from a grocery store. You want a quality cut of meat from a true old fashioned butcher shop and Kenrick's fills that need.   I have shopped KMM several times for summer grilling and have been very pleased with experience. So when it was time for the double nickle birthday celebration, I knew I wanted my steak to come from Kenrick's.   The service here is what all meat counters should be; personalized, professional and friendly. As you stand there drooling over all the beautiful marbleized beef, you hear a cheerful voice offering assistance. Having been raised on a beef farm, I know a good steak when I see one and can quickly pick out the ones I want out of the display. What impressed me about the service is what was given to another customer who had no idea about selection. I listened as the young man explained why he pulled the steaks he did, so the customer would understand and know the next time.   Kenrick's also has a impressive deli counter of cold cuts and cheeses. Plus, catering and carryout meals.  You've heard the classic question, "Where's the beef". Will the answer is, "Kenrick's".

I have been to this HD numerous times since my initial review and I can still say the sales associates are top notch. Every time I have shopped here, there has  always been an salesperson ready to assist.   My most recent visit was to pick up a replacement light bulb for the hood over my stove. Now I thought this would be a simple task, but to be safe I still took the burnt out one with me as guide. I make my to the light bulb section and not only do I find one like the burnt out one I brought with me, but a half dozen more. Who knew there could be so many little light bulbs that illuminate your cooking surface.   I was totally confused, I couldn't tell one from the other and needed help. I looked around for a store employee and spotted one standing at the end of an aisle within ear range. I asked him if bulbs was his area and he said, "No, but I know a little about them."  He tried to help, but ended up being as clueless as me. Even though he was clueless, he took control of the situation. You ask, how can someone who is clueless take charge? He does so by excusing himself to go find someone who can help me.   He returned in a New York minute with one of his coworkers who was a whiz with light bulbs. I showed him my burnt out bulb and he quickly showed me which one was the right selection. He even took time to explain why it was the right one.  When I asked "what if it is wrong", I was told I could bring it back for a refund. Wow, I can return a bulb after I ripped open the packaging, that is service.   I am shocked when others do not get good service when shopping here.  As a side-note, I own several hundred shares of Lowe's stock and I shop at this Home Depot.  I know it is kinda strange.

When: March 8 Why: Shipping a package  I've used the UPS office for years and have never been disappointed.  The location is great. It is on Jefferson between 64 & 44 making it easy to get in and out.   The customer service has always been friendly and helpful. Even when I have seen a long line they move it quickly and still provide a top notch attitude.

I cannot believe that I have not written a review for Corner Bistro - I've eaten here so many times that I have almost experienced the entire menu. I guess I thought all the pictures that I have posted, were my review. After all, they do say that a picture is worth a thousand words.  Since I've eaten here multiple times, I am just going to list some of my favorites:  Bistro Burger - A hand pressed burger, topped with Applewood crisp bacon, cheese, lettuce, tomato, onion and what I can only assume is a secret Bosnian spice. The flavor is unique and makes the burger stand out from a typical American hamburger. It was served with crispy fries and a little cup of ketchup.   Spicy Chicken Wings - Ooey Gooey Spicy sauce covered the entire wings. Finger licking good and good thing they have paper napkins over linen, because you need to use serval to keep fingers clean.   Ham & Cheese Panini - Puts Panera Bread to shame. Thinly sliced ham, smoked cheese, roasted red peppers, lettuce, tomato and mayo on a Ciabatta bread. The sandwich is crisply toasted on the outside and the ingredients on the inside are piping hot. A side of crispy fries makes this a winning combination.   Their pizzas are some of the best in STL. You'll be surprised how tasty they are and they do not use provel.   Chicken & Mushroom - Freshly sliced mushrooms and diced white meat chicken.   Meat Lovers - Hamburger, pepperoni and bacon. The perfect combo of meat.   Buffalo Chicken - (My favorite) A zesty cheese pizza topped with chicken tossed in buffalo sauce and drizzled with ranch dressing and more buffalo sauce. Totally different and worth the experience.   I also give a thumbs up to the house salad and Bruschetta.  I've dined in and I've called ahead for carry-out and every time I have been pleased with my meals. The service at times can be slow, but that has never bothered me, because the food is that damn good. The dining room inside is small, but when the weather is good the patio almost doubles the amount of tables available.   I want this place to continue to succeed, so I recommend it to all pizza lovers. I just hope it doesn't get so popular that I cannot get in to enjoy one myself.

I think management of this store saw, read and took to heart the comments of Jessica C in her 13 Jan 2011 Yelp. The assistance and customer service I received on Monday before the Yelp Garden Party was outstanding.   I entered the store knowing I needed a hot glue gun to create my Martini Hat for the Garden Party, but had no idea where to look. The ladies at the service desk were busy, so I stopped an associate who was walking pass me. She admitted she was not sure, but asked me to wait and she'd find out. She quickly asked a coworker in the paint department and came back and informed me it was in aisle 18. I thanked her and then the amazing service kicked in.   As I thanked her, she informed me she'd lead me to the aisle. (When I worked/trained retail, I taught the importance of leading the consumer, not just pointing) I informed her I was good and thanked her again. When I'm on a mission I move fast. To my surprise, when I got to aisle 18, she was on my heels, making sure I found my glue gun.   I browsed the aisle quickly, an experienced shopper/retailer knows the organization of merchandising and can find an item once in the right area. The associate who followed me, quickly found someone responsible for that area and pin pointed the area just as I did. She smiled and said I just wanted to make sure you found it okay and now I'll know where to find it next time someone ask me. We wished each other good day and I was off to the checkout.   Even with only one item, I never use those self checkout systems. I try to save a job by using a real person. I had a second surprise today, a friendly cashier who enjoyed her job. I was greeted with a smile, exchanged friendly banter and asked to come back again.   I left HD with my glue gun and the bewilderment that I actually shopped a hardware store. Jessica, I hope your next visit has the same top notch customer service.

Jet's Pizza doesn't get the recognition that it deserves. It's actually very good. I admit, I'm guilty of forgetting about them and I drive by this location all time. It's actually the closest pizza joint near my house and I've got them all. Today I was motivated to order from them because of a coupon I got in the mail. Who can turn down a 50% off offer.   Today I ordered, Hot Boneless Chicken Wings and a Small Thin Crust Three Topping Pizza. For my toppings I chose; Pepperoni, Italian Sausage and my favorite topping, Jalapeños. To wash it all down, I choose Diet Pepsi as my beverage.   The boneless wings were nice big pieces coated in hot sauce. The sauce was most definitely, hot. It was so hot, I had beads of sweat appearing on my forehead at my hairline. I enjoyed the spicy flavor. I only ate half and packed the remainder up for lunch at work tomorrow.   My pizza was equally delicious. I really like the flavor of their pizza sauce. It compliments the Mozzarella cheese that tops it along with your selected toppings. Yes, no Provel Cheese here, they use the good stuff, real Mozzarella and they're not stingy with it. They're also heavy handed when applying the toppings.   The staff is very personable and friendly. They answered my questions and prepared my order quickly as I waited. Okay, I did leave to run a quick errand and my order was ready when I returned.   I've never been disappointed with any of the times I've ordered from this location. I just need to remember to enjoy them more in 2020.   I'll be back? - YES!   When: December 14, 2019 Why: A man has got to eat and he was craving pizza.

What? It's been 6 years since I've updated my review for the Tap Room - I'm bad. I didn't even write an update when I celebrated my double-nickel (55) birthday here at The Tap Room. I gotta get an update done now, to let everyone know that I am still a fan of The Schlafly Tap Room. A big fan!   It was my cousins birthday and he's a craft beer connoisseur, so having lunch here just seemed to be the logical choice. His love for beer, is shared by his son who joined us for this celebration. We started out with a Expo IPA for each of us and a Bag of Pretzels to share. The bag had three huge Bavarian style pretzels and came with a white cheddar sauce dipping.   While we munched on the pretzels, which are the "must order" from TSTR on Ian Froeb's STL 100 List for 2016, we decided which, "On Bread" sandwiches we wanted. The birthday man, choose a Reuben. It was Corned Beef piled high on Marble Rye and topped with Kraut, Swiss and 1000 Island. It made him happy, so "Happy Birthday". He paired a Smoked Stout with his Reuben for his second beer.   His son is a fan of Cuban Sandwiches, so his choice was easy. I must say, for me it was the first Cuban I've seen served on a hoagie. Whatever bread you serve it on, pulled pork, ham, swiss cheese with mustard sauce and pickles makes for a delicious lunch. His second beer was a Coconut Ale. He liked, but I'm not a fan of coconut so mixing it with beer is a no-no for my taste buds.   In my humble opinion, I was the most adventurous in selecting my sandwich. I choose the Meatloaf Muffin. The name even says, yumminess. A slice of bacon wrapped meatloaf, fried eggs, crisp onions all served up on a toasted English Muffin. A glass of Double Bean Blonde was the perfect brew to wash down this delightful "on bread" entree.  All of our sandwiches came with hand cut fries. They were crisp and still had the outer skins left on. The serving of fries was huge and not one of us was able to eat our complete order. Which in hindsight was good. Our server figured it out that it was my cousins birthday. It could of been the birthday cocktail napkins I brought to use, that gave it away. Any how, she brought out a comp order of Sticky Toffee Pudding. Lucky for me and his son, he shared with us so we got to satisfy our sweet tooth.   Would I come back? Yes, it's  a must in my family.   When: July 5, 2016 Why: Birthday Celebration

As Molly Brown once sang, "Belly up to the bar, boy's. Better loosen your belts. Only drink when you're all alone or with somebody else." On this evening, I was all alone and I bellied up to the bar.  I was enjoying myself at the 18th best restaurant in STL according to Ian Froeb's 2016 list. By the time I was done, I was loosening my belt.   Sitting at the bar is always a treat, it's like being seated at a chef's table and watching the masterful work in the kitchen. Except in this case, you are watching the creative talents of a bartender. My two drinks this evening were classic cocktails; an Old Fashioned and a Manhattan. Some may think these are simple cocktails to make, but they are not. There is a true talent getting the right mix of whiskey with vermouth or bitters. Here at Taste Bar, they nail it. I loved that they use only one large ice cube in the Manhattan and also use a dark cherry instead of those nasty maraschino bright red cherries.   I'll tell you up front, I over ate. I had no idea the portions were going to be so large. I started out with Cheese Curds. Those of you who are only familiar with Cheese Curds at Culver's, will be blown away and you'll never order them at Culver's again. They were crisp, fat and filled with gooey cheese. Best part for me was the Jalapeño Aioli for dipping - yum yum.   My entree was the Pork Burger with an insane amount skinny fries. The burger was a thick patty, that was juicy and tender. Restaurants that specialize in burgers, should take note of how they are done at Taste Bar. As stated the amount of fries was insane, just look at my picture. They were crispy on the outside and the inside was hot and soft. Instead of ketchup, I continued to dip them in the tasty Jalapeño Aioli.    Not only is Taste Bar one of Ian Froeb's STL 100, it is a 5 Star Restaurant for me. I'm glad I'm able to raise Taste Bar back up to a deserving 5 Stars!  When: August 7, 2016 Why: Eating my way through Ian Froeb's STL 100

Times are a changing, but I hope we can hold on to our USPS. We all love getting mail, or at least I do. Personalized mail and not junk mail, is what I prefer.   I live just down the street from this post office, so it is only a short walk. A very short walk. I can step out on my front porch and if the parking lot is super full, I know to wait until a few cars leave. The only reason I dropped them a star, is the slower service time. Since I moved into the neighborhood, several of the employees have retired and the newer ones don't hustle as quickly to keep the lines moving. However, since it is off the beaten path, this post office still moves quicker than most.   To keep the USPS going, I enjoy sending greeting cards for holidays other than the typical Christmas. It catches friends and family off guard and gives them a grin. I also get a kick out of sending small packages via the USPS. When I find a hideous picture of a cousin or another relative, it is always a good laugh to frame it and send it through the mail for them to enjoy.   The use of regular mail may be down, but the variety of regular stamps is up and I am enjoying the variety. I always go for the dog, silly or historic figures when buying mine.   I'll keep doing my part to save the USPS.   When: Multiple Visits

This location has become my go to Bed Bath & Beyond, since the one in Brentwood relocated. The newer BB&B on Eager Road, just doesn't do it for me any more.    This store is where I go for kitchen gizmos and bed linens. I can always find some new gadget or small appliance that I cannot live without in my kitchen. They also stock bed linens that have fully elasticized fitted sheets with excellent thread counts.   The staff here is also more helpful and personable then those at my old favorite location. What's also better about this location, is it is closer to my home.   I'll be back? - When a gadget or gizmo calls my name.   When: April 18, 2019 Why: Coffee Pod Filters and new pizza pan

Impressive!   I was totally blown away as I walked through this store. With every corner I turned, my jaw dropped. The variety of china and crystal was amazing. If you have inherited family heirloom china and are missing a piece or two, this is the place to come. If they do not have it here in St. Louis, they may have it in their store in St. Petersburg, Florida. If not, they still are the ones who will be able to help you locate those missing pieces.   Personally I have inherited three sets of china, one set is soon to be 80+ years old and several sets of crystal. So I am thrilled to find this store in my hometown.

Hey Yelp HQ, when are you going to give us a 1/2 star? I really could use one for this review. Taco Buddha was better then 3, but not quite a 4. However, it was so close.  Let's get the reason why TB didn't get 4 Stars out of the way first. It was the Baja Taco and the customer service. The Baja taco was flavorless. A fish taco is always one of my go to when eating Mexican and I'd rank this one at the bottom of all the ones I have ordered in STL. A Mrs. Paul's Fish Stick would have been better then the one they served me.   The second reason that held me back from giving TB 4 Stars was the service. The young gentleman who took my order was friendly and personable. His co-worker a tall older man, creeped me out. Made me feel very uncomfortable. Also, the food runners were just that - runners. No interchange at all, they dropped your food and kept running. I understand it's lunchtime, but asking if everything is okay and if you need anything else, would be a nice touch.   Now, let's talk about the points that were pushing them towards that 4 Star review. The thin crisp tortilla chips that had just the right amount of salt and the delicious queso that accompanied them gets two thumbs up from me. Also, my quesadellia with green chilies and Tinga Chicken (recommended by the gentleman who took my order) was one of the best quesadellias I have ever had. It was fabulous. I could only eat half of it and the other half was just as good at home and cold as it was on their patio in the bright hot sun.   They were giving samples of their frozen Margaritas, but I'm a rocks kinda guy and ordered mine with no salt on the rocks. It was refreshing. I didn't see them pour or make it, but I'll say it did not taste like a mix. I finished mine before my entree arrived at my outside table. I would have enjoyed a second, but didn't want to go inside and wait in line again. Next time, I'll order two at once. Or, I'll just say give me a double.  Taco Buddha is a order at counter, take a table marker and find a seat. Some of the tables are community tables and some other diners do not like to share.   I'll be back? - Yeah, I'll give them a second try. Just not the Baja  When: September 6, 2019 Why: Mexican Lunch

I'm going to be honest with you. I almost turned around and walked out on my first visit here and that was on their second day being open. I am so glad I didn't. I normally do not do self serve, except for pumping my own gas and was kind of turned off of the concept at first explanation. Now, I think it is kind of cool and fun.   When you first arrive, you check in with your ID, (like I don't look over 21) and a credit card. You are then given a bracelet that will activate the Taps for a huge variety of craft beers that are constantly rotating so each visit is a new journey. They also, activate a small selection of wines.   Some folks put the bracelet on their wrist, not me. It's not the style of accessory I'd wear, so I put mine on my glass. It makes activating those magical taps so much easier. What won me over to Tapped, was the ability to pull the tap and pour myself as much of a selected beer as I want. It makes trying new beers so much easier and adventurous.   The menu offerings are styled to be the perfect accompaniments to a vast selection of beers. There's no table service per say, you go to the back counter and order your food. Again, they'll use your bracelet to add it to your total bill. They'll then give you a table marker, to make it easier for them to find you when delivering your food.   If you're wanting a snack while sampling a variety of craft beers, I recommend the following: Toasted Ravioli, Spinach & Artichoke Rangoon and the Bavarian Pretzels. I was totally blown away by the Rangoon and highly recommend it. The Toasted Ravioli is round and just your typical TR, but still good. Pretzels, are always a good go to for beer.   Want more then a snack? You can not go wrong with any of their pizzas. They still have the oven from when the space use to be Pizza Story and I do believe they are using their old recipes. My favorite is the asparagus. For me, a favorite vegetable on top of a pizza is always a winner. Another winning entree is the Fish & Chips. I didn't open until after Lent, so next year, my Fridays during Lent may be spent at Tapped.   One item on their menu that I am not a fan of, is the Chicken Wings. It breaks my heart too, because I am a big wings fan. What turns me away most is that they do serve the whole wing. The only time I want entire wing, is when I am enjoying Fried Chicken. When I am enjoying wings in a bar, I want the "tip" part cut off and out of sight. They were also over sauced and messy to eat.   The staff is friendly, helpful and knowledgeable on the different craft beers. If it is your first visit, they'll take you over to the taps and demonstrate how they operate. Questions while you're there? Don't hesitate to ask, they're there to make your visit enjoyable.   When checking out, you'll get an itemized list of your pours and cost of each one, plus your food. They'll be a line for a tip, which goes to a local charity. So be sure to ask who the charity of the month is. They've introduced me to some very rewarding charities that I did not know were here in STL.   In closing, if you go to the taps to get another brew and are not coordinated enough to get it to work. It is time to go home with Uber.   Will I return? As long as they keep serving beer, pizza and Fish & Chips. I'll be there.   When: Too many times to list dates Why: I needed a craft beer.

The "Computer Eye" at Sherwin - Williams saved our ass. We are doing some major landscaping and when we had bushes removed the foundation behind them needed to be painted to match the rest of the foundation. I painted the foundation, years ago and worried how are we going to match something that was done six years ago.   Luckily, we had one area that was starting to chip and we pulled off a swatch and took it to Sherwin - Williams. We shared our story and they said, "no problem". They took our swatch and their computer matched it perfectly.  Very knowledgeable staff, they made our painting project easier then we thought it would be. Thanks SWC for a job well done.

Mama, Mia! Who would have thought an Italian restaurant would be a place to go for breakfast? I sure wouldn't. If it were not for, The Telegraph a local newspaper during an article on the best places for breakfast in the River Bend area, I would have never discovered Mama Mia's.   I ordered the, Mama Mia's Breakfast. It included; two eggs, two strips of bacon, two sausage links and two pancakes. Wow! That is a farmers breakfast in my mind and it was so filling. I had my eggs scrambled and they were extra fluffy. My bacon was freshly prepared and straight. I hate it when my bacon is all twisted up when dining out. The links of sausage were seasoned well and I liked the grill marks on them.    Everything in my breakfast was good, but the star of the meal definitely was the pancakes. They were a light golden color on both sides (yes, I look). They were so warm, that when I added my butter, it started to melt instantly. Best of all, the Maple Syrup was served warm. I have not had warm syrup brought to my table since I moved to this side of the river. The warm syrup is what got them bumped up to 5 Stars.   My coffee was prepared the way I like it, strong and black. Best of all, my cup was never less than half full. My server and his co-workers were very attentive to everyones needs. Speaking of my server, he was very friendly, professional and made me feel welcomed on my first visit.  I commend the restaurant and staff on making the dining experience safe during this pandemic. They encourage social distancing, provided hand sanitizer and did a thorough job cleaning tables and booths as guest departed.   I was so impressed, I will be back for another breakfast. It's only a 15 minute drive from my home.   When: August 21, 2021 Why: Breakfast

Being a friend/fan of Jimmy's on the Park, I received a pleasant surprise in my e-mail this week. Jimmy sent me a coupon for $10 off a birthday celebration and I took advantage of it this morning enjoying brunch.   Brunch is not complete without a Bloody Mary, it is a kick-start to the feast. Jimmy may serve his in a short rocks glass, but it is totally big on flavor. The rim is salted, with a small area not rimmed for sipping.   I enjoy spinach, bacon and goat cheese. So when I saw all three combined in an omelet, I had to have it.  The omelet was big, fluffy, stuffed and served with a slice of bacon on top. The SO had the Tenderloin Benedict which was flavorful, but skimpy on the Tenderloin. Both were served with breakfast potatoes and and fruit cup. The potatoes were crispy little cubes with grilled onions, but the fruit missed the mark. I love honeydew melon, but theirs was long over due causing the cup to be a disappointment.   Timing was a little off today, which is the reason I have removed a star from my original rating. I will not go as far as to say they were rushing us on purpose, but that is how I felt. The service was great, but seemed to have misunderstood that we wanted to enjoy the Salmon, Cream Cheese and Toasted Bagel before our entrees. We barely had them assembled and our main dishes were being delivered to the table. So poor timing and mushy honeydew lost them a star.   Being a birthday boy, the delivered a celebration treat with a sparkler letting everyone around know it was my special day. Thank God, there was no singing and clapping.

Two things that attract me to Dewey's, is that they use Mozzarella Cheese and that they cut their pizza like a pie - no squares here. These simple things make me a fan.   Coming here, I felt as if I was cheating on my regular Dewey's in Kirkwood. To be honest, I didn't realize one was closer to home. I noticed, there really isn't much difference. They both are family friendly and provide quality pizza and salads at affordable prices.   I visited this location on a Thursday night. As a lone diner, I took to the bar so they could keep tables open for multiple diners. As I read over the menu, I enjoyed a craft draft beer. As I drank my, Mamoot Mild Ale, I questioned my bartender about the Thanx program. It's an easy way to earn points and get some free pizza at Dewey's. I enjoyed a free side salad just for signing up.   I do enjoy some of their specialty pizzas, but tonight I created my own. I went with my standard pizza, Italian Sausage and Jalapeños. OMG, it was so delicious. The spices in the sausage and the extra kick from the jalapeños, rocked my world. My Peppercorn Ranch salad before the pizza was impressive, too. You really cannot go wrong with, Romaine lettuce, bacon, tomatoes, shaved Parmesan Cheese, red onion tossed in a Peppercorn Ranch dressing.   Service is always friendly and attentive at Dewey's. Being a pizza restaurant and family friendly, it can get loud with the little ones running about. The tiny tots can watch the kitchen make pizza through big windows, so there will be squeals of excitement. It doesn't bother me, I just sit at the bar and giggle to myself watching their antics.   I'll be back? - Beer, Pizza and Salad close to home = Yes.   When: September 6, 2018 Why: Craving Pizza

I enjoy Dunkin Donuts coffee and love my Keurig for morning coffee.  I have been bitching for a while now, that they did not offer their coffee in a K-Cup. Yesterday I was watching the Today show getting informed on the daily news and to my surprise Dunkin Donuts had a commercial for their K-Cups. No wonder I couldn't find them in the stores or the Keurig website, they are only exclusive at a Dunkin Donuts store.  Tuesday was my day or running errands and I planned my route to take me by a DD. As I shopped their display of K-Cups, I realized the other customers at that time were also buying boxes of DD K-Cups. They had their regular blend in both full strength and decaf as well as a couple flavored and hot coco for sale. I bought two boxes, but hesitated in my purchase. They were expensive, the quantity vs price did not compute like the ones on the internet or at other stores. They were more then a high end grocery store. Drink your coffee DD and wake up. There is no middle man here, it's your store and your product. I am sure you can price your K-Cups at a more reasonable price.   Since I was there, I thought why not grab some breakfast so I ordered the Sausage Pancake Bites. The banners made them look so cute and tasty. Besides, I thought how can you go wrong with a combination of pancake and sausage. You can, it tasted like a old corn dog, so I do not recommend them.   Service was average. The girl working the check out was perky, but the girl who tossed my order on the counter said, "3 pancake bites" in a rather surly tone.

It was election night and I thought it was best to stay home to watch the returns. This years results called for comfort food, so Jetman to the rescue.  It was just me watching the results at home, so a 4 Corner Pizza was the perfect size. I choose my toppings of Italian Sausage and Jalapeños and called my order in for a pick-up. I also added a 20 oz Diet Pepsi to my order. My election night dinner would be ready in about 20 to 30 minuets. Sounds like a lot of other voters needed comfort food while watching the results.   Recently I've only been getting pizza by the slice here, it satisfies my pizza cravings. I like their one topping slices of pepperoni, sausage or just plain cheese, but tonight I got to have my favorite topping - jalapeños. The semi deep dish pizza with the sausage & jalapeños made my night a little more bearable.   I could only eat three slices, so I had one left over for breakfast. At least that was one win I could deal with.   The staff here is always so friendly. I guess working in a pizza joint, just makes you naturally happy.  When: November 8, 2016 Why: Election Night Comfort Food

It's been almost 8 years since I posted my first review for this USPS and my opinion hasn't changed. I'll admit, I may be a little biased since it is at the beginning of my street.   When you live this close to a PO, it does make life easier. It is so easy to buy unique stamps, ship packages and mail those thank-you notes your mother taught you to write. If I walk out my front door and see a full parking lot, I go back inside my house and wait until the lot is emptier. Yes, that is one of the perks of living close. I watch the lot and I never have to wait.   The staff here on average is fairly friendly. Like most postal workers and DVM workers, they don't move real fast, but they do complete their task efficiently.

Alton Restaurant Week  WOW! I am so glad I came here during, ARW. I was totally impressed. So impressed, that I am confident Bossanova will be become a regular in my restaurant rotation, here in my new neighborhood.   Upon my arrival, I choose my favorite spot at any bar, a stool at the end. I like this space for its privacy, especially now during a pandemic. I started out with a Dirty Martini, made with Tito's. The bartender commented that was her favorite drink and I believe her. She made my cocktail so superbly, you'd think she was making it for herself.   For my dinner, I choose to go with the 10 oz Filet. They prepared it to a delectable medium-rare. Before my filet, I enjoyed a Caesar salad topped with Parmesan cheese and crunchy croutons. I would have liked some fresh cracked pepper, but the freshly ground in the shaker did the trick. As my side, I went with the Green Beans instead of the creamy garlic mashed potatoes that the bartender recommended. The green beans were top notch, they were prepared with bacon and we all know bacon adds that extra flavor. On my next visit, I'll try those garlic rich potatoes.   For my dessert, I choose the Gooey Butter Cake and had packaged to-go. I was stuffed and had no room to eat it that night. Being a recycler, I was pleased to see their carry-out vessels are Eco-friendly. Being from STL, I am spoiled with Gooey Butter Cakes, so I found this one to be just, okay. It was good, but not as flavorful as those in the city where it originated.   The bartender was delightful in conversation and attentive in service. I'm looking forward to sitting at the bar again on my next visit.   When: January 15, 2021 Why: Alton Restaurant Week

Not my normal BBB, but I was in the neighborhood so I thought why not save time and shop here instead of driving to the one in Richmond Heights. This location seems to be older and not as well kept as my usual BBB. However, considering the time of year, I am going to say it is the holiday craziness that made this store seem cluttered.   My hand mixer died and not wanting to  pull out the full size mixer every time I needed to do a small amount of whipping, I grabbed my BBB 20% off coupon and went shopping. I wanted an orange one to match my other small electric appliances, but no such luck. I did find a nice steel grey one with 2 sets of utility attachments and a storage bin.   If you need kitchen gadgets or small electronics grab your BBB coupon and go shopping. I do not recommend shopping at BBB without a coupon, because some of their regular prices can be on the high side.

This is truly an architecturally vintage post office located in the heart of Maplewood. The history and the architectural design of the building, is actually the  best thing about it.   This post office is a convenient location to buy stamps and get a quick money order when you need one. However, they are very similar to your local Wal-Mart store. That means, they will only have one window open for customer service. So, be prepared to wait.   When: September 29, 2021 Why: Friend needed money order

F&B Eatery is a quaint little sandwich shoppe serving both hot and cold sandwiches. The burgers are hand pressed and grilled to your liking, my medium temperature is always done right. They also, hand cut their house fries regular or sweet potato, which is a nice touch. Being small, they put a lot of details and preparation into their sammies. The garnishes; lettuce, tomato and onion are available upon request.   Their soda offerings are local - they have Excel available on the fountain and the have bottled Ski in a cooler.  The staff is friendly and as you become a regular diner, they'll remember your name. F&B Eatery is a good addition to my neighborhood. I'm looking forward to going back and enjoying a Rueben on my next visit.  When: February 17, 2016 Why: Lunch

I am not a certified BBQ judge, and I do not play one here on Yelp. Nor am I an expert in BBQ. I am what I am and that is a Blue Blooded, All-American, South City Man who knows and enjoys good BBQ when he has it. In my opinion Smoking Barrels missed the mark.   Seeing all the rave reviews on Yelp, I was tempted to try SB for dinner the other night. I am always up for supporting a business in my hood.  We opted to eat in, instead of doing carry out. The ambiance is nice. We liked the hole in the wall, neighborhood feel that it had. Also, the barrel tables gives a rustic true BBQ feel to the dining room.    After reading the menu, our game plan was to order two, 2 Meat Combos which came with two sides each. This was our way of being able to experience 4 different meats and 4 different sides. Aren't we ingenious?  The following is how we placed our order:  Ribs and Sausage with Cole Slaw and Potato Salad  Pulled Pork and Beef Brisket with Baked Beans and Mac - n - Cheese  Out of the four meats, the Sausage was by far the best. It was a nice touch that they pre-sliced it in to bite size pieces. It reminded me of a Johnsonville Sausage that you'd do on your grill in the backyard. The Baby Back Ribs had a fair amount of meat on them, but were dried out. No tenderness or juiciness when you bite into them.   Our Pulled Pork was tender, but had no smokey flavor that I could taste. At first look and taste, I thought it had been boiled. The Beef Brisket was the biggest disappointment, it like the Ribs was dry and tuff. I am use to being able to break off a bite size piece of brisket with a plastic fork, here I was using a typical flatware fork and had to use a saw like motion to break a piece off.  Were the ribs and briskets leftovers, reheated? Made us think.   When the young man serving us asked how things were and the BF informed him how tuff the brisket was, he offered to bring us something else or another serving of the brisket. We opted for more brisket, but to be honest there was not much improvement. The Pit Master brought us out some Turkey Breast and it was the absolute best of all. A shame we did not order it to begin with, it was juicy, smokey and tender.   Their sides can compete with most of the other BBQ joints in town.  Cole Slaw was creamy, thinly chopped and a flavorful. Potato Salad was better then some delicatessens. The Mac - n - Cheese was creamy, but was in need of some more cheese and less garlic. Baked Beans were good, they did have chunks of pork, but so does the cans of Bush's in the grocery aisle.  The Garlic Bread was as good as you'd get at Texas BBQ and that is damn good.   The ice tea was fresh and they had my favorite artificial sweetener, Splenda. We'll let the growing pains pass and will re-visit on a weekend to see in there is a difference.   Remember, I am not a BBQ judge. This is just my opinion on a social medium.

I came here for a International Supper Club, gathering. I attend these ISC dinners to expand my international palate and I was totally impressed with the food here at KET.   My Thai experience begun with an order of Crab Puffs. Which basically were crab rangoon. It's a fried wonton parcel with cream cheese, imitation crab and severed with sweet chili sauce. They were crisp, served warm and the sweet sauce was perfect for dipping.   As and entree, I choose Pad Kee Mao and added beef as my protein. It was a healthy serving of stir fried egg noodles, soy sauce and a mixture of vegetables; green beans, bell peppers, onions and seasoned with Thai basil. The pieces of beef, I added as my protein were large and tender. I found this entree to be very flavorful and filling.   The bar seemed to be very limited and the server had to look up how to make a classic cocktail. That concerned me, so I ordered a house red wine and was pleased with its quality.   The ambiance is minimalist industrial. It was simple and comfortable.  My only negative comment about the experience, was the downtown parking, but that is part of city life.   I'll be back? - Sure, I'll even go to their Fork & Stix.  When: October 17, 2018 Why: International Supper Club

When I lived in STL, this was my go to Lowe's. Ah, hell, it was my go to hardware and nursery store, period. Being immediately off of 44 on Lindbergh, made it easy access.   Until I was prepping my house for sale, did I realize I haven't updated my review for 6 years. Bad me, bad Elite Yelper. Not how perfect you think your home is, when it is time to sell, there are various things that always need to be tweaked and repaired. Having this Lowe's close to home and always well stocked came in handy.   I admit, I am not the sharpest tool in the shed when it comes to being a handyman. My "handyman" would send me to the hardware store for various parts and supplies and I always came here, because the associates would always help me find what I needed.  Back tracking to my opening paragraph, I also came here for a lot of my nursery/gardening needs when I was doing landscaping at my STL home. Many times I found better deals on plants and containers then at many of the local nurseries near my LIndenwood Park home.   I'll miss this Lowe's. You served me well while I lived in STL.   Will I return? - To Lowe's yes, I have stock.   When: September 24, 25 and 30, 2020 Why: Supplies to sell home in STL

I'll have a cold craft beer, please.   First stop of our birthday tour of Edwardsville. We were celebrating two cousins birthdays and our family loves craft beer. We love it so much, we follow each other on Untappd. Since we are big fans of craft beer, we thought GBTH was the perfect place to start our celebration.   GBTH is a simple bar with what appears to be an endless row of taps.  The menu changes regularly and on their blackboard they list ABV and IBU of each beer they serve. Tonight, I went with the very first one on the list - Murphy's Irish Stout. My boy dog is named, Murphy so it was a no brainer. It was smooth, creamy and just a slight flavor of coffee.   The ambiance is simple. There are lots of hightop and regular tables. They also have an area full of leather sofas and chairs for a more relaxed sitting.   The only downside to GBTH is they do not serve food. However, that is not a problem - you can bring your own treats. We didn't bring anything, but other patrons had everything from chips and dips to boxes of pizza.   A big plus, which was a total surprise to was - they are dog friendly.  As long as you keep your dog on a leash, it can come with you. How cool is that?   I'll be back? Yeah, it's a fun place in E-ville.   When: July 13, 2018 Why: Celebrating a 60th and 65th B-Day.

A local, privately owned and operated business that provides quality work at a reasonable price. This a true Saint Louis mom & pop business. Because most times it is a Viviano helping you in the store or installing  the products at your home.   They have installed doors and windows at my house and most likely will be doing an awning or two later this summer.  I have shopped around and their prices are very competitive. Proving the "big box" is not always the best deal.  The customer service is personable and they are based in my hood.   When I need doors, windows or awnings, it is Viviano's for me.  I hope you'll do the same.

Opening Day & they nailed it!  I can already tell you, this is going to be the place to meet your friends, before and after a STL Cardinals game. The bar selections and the food are top notch.   I always judge a bar by their ability to make classic cocktails. Today, I tested them with a Manhattan and an Old Fashioned, two favorites. To my surprise, they were made with extreme care and professionalism. I'm tempted to say, the Manhattan was one of the best I've had in 2019.  Another go to for me when seen on a menu, is Fried Green Tomatoes.  Theirs was prepared with a thick, crisp crust and the green tomato still stayed firm. Nice. The tomato jam and the tomato aioli were nice accents to the flavor. When reading the menu, I questioned the ricotta in my head, but was proven wrong. To swirl my bites of the tomato in the ricotta before eating, added to the flavor.   I knew my eyes were bigger then my stomach, but I could not resist. I wanted it all. I ordered the Sampler Platter and got it all. It consisted of; 3 ribs, brisket, pastrami, pulled pork, turkey and 2 Smoked wings. Of course I did not eat it all, I have a fantastic lunch for working OT tomorrow.   Brisket - Best in the city.  Pulled Pork - Moist & Flavorful  Turkey - Seasoned well & fork tender.  Pastrami - I am in love. Replaces my old time favorite from Soulard.  Ribs - Dry Rub, thick & meaty.  Smoked Wings - LARGE & meaty. Not a fan of the tips still being attached, but I dealt with it.   Sides: Mac-n-Cheese and Pit Beans. The Mac-n-Cheese reminded me of Grandma. The Pit Beans, were just okay for me, but I'm sure others will love'm.   Service was top notch. Ben has recruited an incredible staff.   Chances of returning? - Hell, yes!  When: March 1, 2019 Why: Opening Day

5 Stars is not enough for Dogtown Gallery. Jaynelle is truly a Gold Medalist when it come to custom framing. She is so meticulous and detailed in her work and it shows in your finished product. You'll love it.   I am sure if you're reading all my new reviews, you are getting tired of hearing me say, I got a new house.
