However, when you get a new home, you do a lot of redecorating and shopping. I needed a poster for the guest bath framed and most importantly photos of the old Busch stadium reframed.   Once again, Jaynelle did a great job on both. She matched the frame on the poster to a print I already had that would be hanging in the same bathroom. She also made sure it had a non-glare glass since it was in hanging near a large window. I wanted to save the mat on the Busch photos since the description was had written by the photographer and she masterfully accomplished my request. It looks as good as when I bought it in 2005.   I may have moved to the eastside of the Mississippi, but when I need anything framed, I will be driving to the westside and to Dogtown.   Will I return? - Damn, straight I will.   When: September 30, 2020 Why: Custom framing for new house

Happy Cuatro de Mayo!   Not everyone gets to celebrate cinco, some of us have to work. Actually, I've been celebrating Cuatro for several years now to beat the crowds. I think this year, others have taken my lead. Pueblo Solis was packed.   Tonight I was dining solo and I always find it amazing how single diners are treated differently then "couples" or "groups". I'll address this issue later, but first let me praise their food.   The chips here are some of the best in the area. They are light, crispy and just the right amount of salt. Most places only offer uno salsa, but here you get tres. I like the variety, but not a fan of them being served in plastic cups. I understand it makes life easier for the dish washer, but it takes away from the presentation. I just hope that do recycle.   I bounced back and forth between their regular margaritas and the top shelf. I recommend that you pay the extra $'s for top shelf it is worth the bang.   When ordering Queso Fundido, be warned it is not your typical queso. It is not made for dipping chips, it is very hearty and is meant to be spooned on to tortilla. To much work for me. Spoon, fill and roll. I would just rather dip and eat. It was good & different, but give my thinner queso that I can dip in both my salsa and cheese dip.   I wanted to experience as much as possible so I created my own Large Combo Plate. I choose tres items and they were served with Rice and Beans. My tres choices were; beef hard taco, beef tamale and beef enchilada. Let's highlight each item:   Beef Hard Taco - Bottom did not get greasy and soft like other places. Shell held its crunch holding flavorful beef, lettuce and cheese.   Tamale - Hot Damn! A Tex-Mex place in Saint Louis who knows how to make a tamale. I'll be back just for Tamales.   Enchilada - Beef is seasoned well and the sauce and cheese were the perfect complement.   Sides - Rice was "the" best rice I have had in a Mexican restaurant. It was cooked perfectly and full of flavor. So many places over cook their rice, but not here. Here at Pueblo Solis, they over cook the beans. The beans were mush, you'd thought they were pureed to make baby food. Flavor was good, but the texture was not.   Service "was off the wall" BAD "off the wall". The bartender was the server for the entire patio. A patio of 12 tables with a variety of sizes.  His service was taking order and that was it. He had bus and one assistant who did everything else. To get a second Margarita I had to go tell him at the bar. Then had to flag him down to get my third and final.   The other thing that freaked me out was that he was wearing blue medical gloves. I can understand wearing them to cut limes and lemons at the bar, but take them off when you come to wait on my table.   When settling my tab, I asked if they were understaffed that night, trying to give him an out. He replied , "No". When I asked if he always waits the patio, he explained that his boss understands he needs money and lets him wait on tables too. Hey boss, this man can not multi task. Either have him wait tables or bartender. He can't do both. He cost you a star.  The assistant was doing a better job.   I'll be back, but no matter how nice it is outside - I'll be inside and will make sure he is not a waiter full time. He's an okay guy - just not a server.   I felt for his helpers and still tipped 20%. I feel bad that I rewarded bad service.

It's been 7 years since my last update of this Home Depot and I need to remove a star from their rating. The customer service here has dropped considerably. When you need service, you have to track down an associate. When you find one it will be a 50 to 50 chance that they'll be able to answer your question.   I recently visited while I was prepping my STL house for sale. My handyman sent me to get a part for my outside faucet. Knowing I'm not the sharpest tool in the shed, he sent me with the old piece to show the clerks, what I needed. I went straight to the plumbing area and there were three associates assisting one customer. I politely waited my turn and when I showed one associate the piece I had been sent with, he quickly told me they didn't carry it. In shock, I responded, "really?". He then asked his co-worker and he too, said they didn't have it. I asked them, if I should go to Lowe's and they said, yes.   I went to Lowe's and the associate informed me they did not have that piece individually, but I could get it by buying the complete kit. No problem, I need the piece, so give it to me. If the clerks at HD thought out of the box, they could have had a larger sale. The complete kit was only $12, which is nothing when you're prepping a house for sale.   I'll admit, I went back two more times since that visit, but I found what I needed by myself and I even used the self check-out which I never do. Those two times, the service was amazing.   Will I return? - I've moved, so not likely.   When: September 9, 12 & 26, and October 7, 2020 Why: Selling house in St. Louis

My stock broker would get a laugh and shake his head at this review. I have a wheelbarrow overflowing of Lowe's stock and when I need a big box hardware store, this is the one I come to. It is convenient to my home and in my humble opinion has exceptional customer service.  I know others have complained about the associates and customer service here, but for me it is pretty top notch. I always get assistance, they can answer questions or find someone who can and the cashiers are always friendly and chatty as well. My only theory is that when I walk in to a hardware store, I look so out of place that they take pity on me and help. It's an illusion, because I do know what I'm doing.   Recently I needed a filter for my A/C unit, the big size 16x25x4. I normally order them on the Internet, but forgot and they were coming to do the seasonal checkup that day. As I walked through the store an associate asked if I needed help and I told him what I needed. He referred me to aisle 16. When I got there, the only filters I found were on the end cap and not the size I needed. As I was leaving, I ran in to the same associate and he stopped me to tell me he gave me the wrong directions. It was actually aisle 14 for filters. I told him the end cap on 16 did have filters, but not my size. He asked me my size and he said his at home was the same and they do carry them. He then said, "let me show you". I told him I'd be alright, that I could find them.  He still insisted and took me directly to the aisle and they had the same ones I order on line and at the same price. For me, that was going the extra step. He could of been the typical retail clerk we see to often these days by pointing and uttering they're over there.   When checking out, my cashier was friendly, quick and thanked me for shopping Home Depot. I always use a live cashier, you'll never see me using those automated check outs. I enjoy service with a smile.

Fields Food is the grocery store between my work and home, so on many occasions it is my go to for last minute groceries. It offers a great butcher and seafood counter. I have never been disappointed with any steak that I have purchased. My favorite seafood is sea scallops and theirs get a thumbs up.   I have even been known to grab dinner from their Hot Entree Counter. I can recommend the fried chicken, catfish, baked chicken and meatloaf. My favorite sides are the Brussels Sprouts and Mac-n-Cheese. Also, I am a huge fan of their chicken wings off the hot bar. My favorite is the Lemon Pepper. I think they are better then some restaurants in the Bi-State area.   I'm not to impressed with the fruits and vegetables here, they kind of a hit or miss. Gotta watch closely what you are selecting. However, I am a big fan of their dairy selection. I grew up on Farm Fresh Milk and I am so glad to see it in their dairy case. You also can not go wrong in their beer and wine selections, you'll always find something to satisfy your alcoholic needs.   On a lazy night like tonight, I grabbed a top sirloin steak for grilling, some asparagus from the hot entree bar and those tasty lemon pepper chicken wings to munch while I grill my steak.  This is a quick and easy dinner and my leftover steak will be tomorrows breakfast with eggs.   I also like the Round-Up for Charity at the register. Rounding up is pocket change and right now it is going to the Police Foundation. Gotta love our men & women in blue.   Will I come back? Yes, it is convenient and meets my needs.   When: Numerous Times Why: Groceries

So long, farewell. Diablitos Cantina will be shutting their doors after service on Valentines Day. When I heard this news, I knew I had to get in at least one more visit. So I came this past Saturday night and the party was on. This Mexican restaurant was packed, there were a lot of fans saying their goodbyes just like me.   As I sat at the bar enjoying Top Shelf and a House Margaritas (not at the same time), I opened my Yelp app to refresh my memory of what I've enjoyed in the past. To my surprise, I had posted pictures, but had forgotten to write a review. Bad me, but I want you to know, I've always been a fan of this restaurant and will miss them.  Just check out all of my pictures.   This night I went with what I remember enjoying on my first visit to Diablitos Cantina; Queso Blanco with Chorizo, Deviled Legs (chicken wings) and Papas Fritas. I made a good choice and I'll be back to devour some tacos before they close.   I'll miss the Salsa Bar. Some folks complained about the $3 charge for chips and salsa, but you get what you pay for. The variety of salsa's and the fresh chips are worth the $3. Way better then the "free" that is offered at some establishments.   In closing, I give a real big shout out to the staff for being upbeat and positive. They still were giving friendly and attentive service. They simply were doing their jobs, even though they know in two weeks, their lives will be changing.   Will I return? I hope to visit at least one more time........  When: February 4, 2017 Why: Shuttering February 14, 2017

They lost a star today, due the their attitude and customer service.  The other half is a smoker, I know "yuck", but hey he's a good bud so I can over look one flaw. Any way, he went to get a carton of cigarettes before we got in line to check out.  The girl in the cigarette cage, said he had to pay for them there, that they no longer allowed you to just take them and put into you cart.   When we got to the check out we asked one of the customer service supervisors who was walking around if she could get a carton for us. She "flipped" her hair with attitude and told us "no" you need to pay for them over there. Then turned her back on us. We only wanted to pay once, we didn't need or want two sales receipts. Schnucks and Dierbergs both run and get the cigarettes when you are checking out. Why not Costco? They had enough staff, I guess they are no longer concerned with customer satisfaction.   May be a minor detail to yank a star away, but it was more the "attitude" of the supervisor then the new rule itself.

Now serving breakfast!  It is so good and down-home, that I already know that this is going to be my go to place for breakfast on Wednesday. The service is friendly and personable. It amazes me how they remember names of their regular patrons. It's a touch when you are greeted by name as you enter the restaurant. Another nice touch is that they are flexible in preparing menu items. I'm a big fan of jalapeños and they have them on hand and are willing to add them to my order.   Today, I tried their Slinger. OMG! The Slinger already is a St. Louis classic breakfast dish and this one shoots to the top of my favorites. I already knew F&B made an awesome burger, so using it as the meat was a no-brainer. The base was grill fried potatoes, then the burger patties, two sunny side up eggs, and house made chili. It then is topped with onions and shredded cheese. Yummy! It was just spicy enough and not overly salty as some other Slingers in town. The serving is huge, so I definitely had a hearty breakfast. I also like that their coffee is a hometown roaster - Kaldi's.   My previous visits for lunch, I enjoyed their Pork Steak Sandwich and the Rueben. Both of them were winners.   This is a great little breakfast & sandwich cafe. If you haven't gone, I suggest you go soon.   Would I go back? Yes. I plan on being a regular for breakfast on Wednesday.   When: January 25, 2017 Why: Breakfast

I have two Lowe's that are closer to my home, but I drive an extra 3 miles to shop at this location. Even with the price of gas. I will drive the extra distance. Why? you ask. It is because they go the extra distance with their customer service. Every time I shop here the staff is friendly and knowledgeable of the area they are working.   My most resent shopping trip was for deep seat cushions for our patio furniture. Deep seat cushions are not an easy find, but Lowe's came through for us. They not only had the cushions we liked, but they had the matching pattern for our black rod iron dining table on the patio.   The young man who was helping in the garden area was a hoot. He was so helpful as we filled two shopping carts full of our stripped cushions. As he assisted us, I was eying the basket of markdowns he was working on. I kept looking at them and looking at him. I wasn't sure if they were available for sale yet. He finally said, "If you see something you want, you can take it."  At that point, I made everyone laugh.  I reached in and took a set or pruning tools that were marked down 50% and said, "Look, they're color coordinated to our new cushions."   I know the SO and sales associate were laughing "at" me and my comment, but it was fun. As he laughed, he informed me I had to be the first person he'd waited on that coordinated their cushions and garden tools.   May have been a silly story, but the service I get here in any department in always good and that is what brings me back time and time again.

Fuddruckers is a weird burger joint. They make their own buns, which sets them apart from other specialty burger restaurants. However, I want the beef to impress me, not the bun. For me it just wasn't a good piece of meat. The works bar, where you dress your own burger, freaked me out too.   The french fries are wedge aka Steak Fries. They are seasoned well, but my order could have been done a little crisper. They were soft on the outside and the inside wasn't that hot. My friend had onion rings as his side and you could tell they were fresh and done in house. A shame they lacked flavor and the portion was skimpy.   Highlight was the fancy high tech coke machine. I got a real charge out of pushing all the buttons for my perfect ice chilled beverage.   My friend and I differed on the rating, I say 2 he said 4. So I went with the average, 3 Stars.  Next time I am in this hood and crave a burger, I will be stopping at Five Guys down the street.

Great addition to Maplewood and a great place to enjoy a beer or two or three. They not only have a large selection of beers, but they have whiskey and wine as well.  The atmosphere is minimalist, very stark and simple. As Kelly B., pointed out it is cute and cozy. Their serving hours are limited, Tue-Thu they are open 3PM-10PM and on Fri & Sat they open at 12PM and stay open an extra hour, closing at 11PM.   SPC has a very friendly staff and the ones we spoke with are very knowledgeable about the brews they are serving. I'd recommend SPC as a great place to start your evening out or as a relaxing place to enjoy a beer after dinner on the main Manchester drag in Maplewood.   Warning: Be aware of a step marked only by a strip of lights on the floor, leading you into the bar area. Several patrons arriving misstepped and stumbled while we were sitting at the main bar. No one got hurt, they just shook it off and laughed. Kind of embarrassing when you do misstep and you are sober.   Hope they add some type of munchie soon, so you can stay longer and enjoy the LARGE variety of beers.

The weather outside is frightful, a hearty breakfast would be delightful. It's  a winter wonderland and the roads are covered in snow and ice, but that is not going to keep me from enjoying a breakfast out. We choose Chris', for its' convenience to home. That way we avoided all the traffic problems that they were reporting on the news.   Due to the weather Chris' wasn't as busy as a normal week day, so we were seated almost immediately. We both took advantage of a January Special, Sunrise Sampler.  It was two eggs, 2 slices of bacon, sausage (link or patty), Salsiccia, Hash Browns and your choice of either toast or pancakes.  Who could ask for anything more.  This was the hearty breakfast we both were looking for, a good kick-start to our snow day.  I barely had time to complete my check in on Yelp and our food was arriving to our table. Being one of six tables in the restaurant, they got our order out pronto. As, our server presented our identical orders, expect for the preparation  of our eggs, he stated our pancakes will be right out. By the time I added hot sauce to my eggs and diced them up, our pancakes were at the table.   Chris' is known for serving up quality breakfast. They got our eggs cooked to order, one over easy and the other over medium. When served, you could see the difference. At other breakfast joints, they always look the same and come out the same, here they know the difference. They also, prepare their Hash Browns crispy without having to ask them to be done extra crispy.   Service was good and warm as it should be at a mom and pop type restaurant. As we were leaving, the regulars were starting to arrive and the dining room was filling up.  A snow day, or a regular day, Chris' serves up a hearty breakfast.  When: 21 Jan 2014 Why: Breakfast on a snowy day

Color me surprised. When you do, make sure you use a bright and festive one.   I drive by Fazoli's on the regular and have seen them promoting new chicken wings the marque. Being a chicken wing lover, I was tempted to give them a try, but was hesitant to do so. I just couldn't wrap my head around a fast food restaurant serving up good wings. Lucky for me, a cousin gave them a try and told me they were not bad.   Hearing a thumbs up from a family member, I was ready to give them a try. So last night on my way home from work, I drove thru their drive-thru and ordered the Boneless Garlic Parmesan (10 pieces). When I ordered, they offered me Ranch or Blu Cheese for dipping. I'm not a wing dipper, so I declined, but I want you know it is available.   My cousin was right, they were fairly good for the price and coming from a fast food pasta restaurant. The pieces were a variety of sizes and even with the difference in size, they were perfectly prepared. I was expecting a more dry garlic parmesan, but this one was more of a heavy sauce. I want to go back and try the buffalo sauce.   I'm also thinking about cheating and buying the Garlic Parmesan again and bringing it home to dice up and add to a homemade Alfredo sauce. It make a nice and simple pasta dish, really fast.   The young lady who was working the drive-thru was super sweet. I would vote for her as Miss Congeniality.  She was super perky over the intercom and even more so at the window.   When: January 5, 2021 Why: Giving the wings a try.

Greatness does not come by mere association. Greatness needs to be earned. Just because Adam's Smokehouse is associated with two of the most popular BBQ/Smokehouses in Saint Louis, does not mean it is great BBQ. They need to earn that greatness themselves and judging from my first couple of visits it is going to take them a while. Andre's on South Kingshighway is far better.   When I first saw the the signs go up in the windows on the space now occupied by Adam's Smokehouse, I rushed home and did a Goggle search. I was so stoked, to find out the new BBQ place in my hood was part of the Pappy's & Bogarts. Once they opened and I dined twice, I learned quickly that what Kevin R. said is so true.  This is average BBQ at best. It is no different then the BBQ you'd get at a church fundraiser.  Here is a breakdown of what I've experienced:  Chicken - ordered the half chicken. It was juicy and flavorful. Took the breast and wing to work for lunch the next day and it was even good cold.   Potato Salad - Not made in house and you can tell it. Bland.   Cole Slaw - Overly creamy, and too sweet for my taste.   Pit Baked Beans - Made in house, very flavorful for me, but the friend said they were too sweet and they had to add mustard to cut the sweetness.   Brisket - Tender, but no flavor.   Ribs - First visit, very tender and good. Second visit, ate in house and given a sampling while I dined. The sampling I was given was an embarrassment, fatty and tough. Glad I had the good experience first.  Burnt Ends - Two visits, arrived around noon and already sold out. Once, I can understand, but twice.   BBQ Sauce - Of the three bottles offered on the tables, my favorite was Sweet Jane's and it wasn't that great. I ate most of mine without adding any sauce.   Customer Service is good, but a little awkward. They're trying to recreate the upbeat greetings of Bogart's, but they just don't have the smoothness. As you watch the greetings, you can tell who they already know and those that are "just a patron".  I can recommend one change, your cashier. Take the perky blonde girl who was in back, running food and cleaning the dining room and make her cashier. She is friendly and was selling a positive attitude. Then replace her in back with the current big guy cashier. He was very dry, like a McDonald's employee.   I want to love Adam's, but right now it is just not happening. I'm going to give them a couple weeks to get over their opening bumps and then revisit. Hopefully I'll see improvement and will be able to give them my love.

The customer service here is worthy of bumping them up to 5 Stars. It's not often that I shop a paint store, but when I do it is good to have a friendly and knowledgeable sales associate. When you come in, don't be judgmental. The majority of the staff here is female, but they know their stuff.   I'm prepping my house for sale and needed some paint to touch up the foundation. I knew I had bought it at this store, so i stopped by to grab a gallon. They found me in the system, but did not have the grey foundation paint on record. The young lady suggested I get a chip off the foundation, since it was peeling anyway and bring it in for the computer to figure out. When I went home, lucky for me I found a almost empty container of the paint we used last time we painted. Sometimes it pays off to be a hoarder/pack rat.   Any way, back to the paint store when I was ready to paint with can in tow. The young lady waiting on me, asked some basic questions to make sure I was purchasing the right type of paint for my job and then looked up the "recipe" in the computer and got things mixing up for me.   I informed her of the other items my painter wanted and she took me over to that area in the retail shop. She then assisted me and made recommendations on which one to buy. Of course she showed me a higher price point, but when I told her it was going to be used once and tossed, she showed me another one and said it would do the job fine.   The paint was a perfect match and my painter ended up using the brush for the entire job instead of the roller. He liked it that much.   If you've got a paint job coming up, this is the paint store for you.   Will I return? - Sad to say, no. I've moved to another state.   When: August 21, 2020 Why: Paint and Brush Shopping

Not as impressed as everyone else. Yes, it has a fabulous retail space and the merchandising and selection of the plants is great. What the down side is, most of their plants are overpriced and not all employees are as knowledgeable as you'd hope. In fact, some of them are down right aloof.  Keep talking to the various people working, you'll find one who knows the answer.   When shopping here, be sure to know the market price, especially if you are doing a large project. We did find a couple very unique plants for our front retaining wall and paid the inflated price. However, all the other plants we were considering we found at other city nurseries at a noticeably lower price. When you are buying in volume, it does add up quickly.  I will still continue to shop the nursery here, it just will not be my go to one.   I look forward to returning to experience the restaurant.

Gather around, I've got a story to tell about a snobby shopper, that I know very well. He always shopped at the big name stores and never gave any thought to going to a Big Lots store. Until one day he was checking out the Burlington store next door for a specific item and thought, what the hell I might as well check out Big Lots, too.   To his surprise, BL was nothing like he thought it was. It was well organized and clean as well.  Who would have thought, a discount store would be this well maintained and have bargains galore as well. It had everything from kitchen gadgets, cleaning supplies and garden accessories. Big Lots even had party supplies like Party City. He never dreamed items like these would have been found at his local Big Lots store.   Even though the snobby little shopper did not buy anything on his first visit to a Big Lots store, he knows he will be back. When spring is finally here and it is time to do spring cleaning and fix up the backyard, he'll be giving Big Lots another try. The Shepherd's Hook with a Solar Light is going to be looking mighty fine his backyard.   When: February 22, 2016 Why: First Time to a Big Lots Store

I love, The Shack. It is one of the absolute best places to go for breakfast. Creve Coeur is one of their newest locations and it already is providing the high quality service and food that The Shack is known for.   On my inaugural visit, I sat at the bar as my usual when dining alone. For the short time they had been open, they already had regulars (group of retired men) who were also enjoying their breakfast at the bar.  One of the reasons I like sitting at the bar is, I find the service to be more personalized. The bartender/server always ask my name and uses it in conversation. It just makes me feel more welcomed and relaxed.   Today I created my own omelette. I made it with sausage, jalapeños and Pepper Jack Cheese. This meal was before I went low-carb, so the rest of my meal was carb heavy. I enjoyed some crispy hash-browns and a biscuit. I don't know what I was thinking this morning, because I also ordered a side of Biscuits and Gravy. Actually, I knew what I was doing, I just didn't expect a side dish to be so BIG.   It was all delicious. Being a farm boy, I'm a tough judge on B&G's and they do them right. I wish I could have finished them, but there always is next time. Next time, it will only be B&G's with a side of bacon.   One of my favorite, Adult Swim beverages is the White Trash Screwdriver. The mixture of pear apple cider with vodka and orange juice is so refreshing.   Will I return? - Yep.   When: May 22, 2018 Why: Breakfast at the new location

I'm really torn on how to rate this restaurant. My tacos & Margarita were good, but the atmosphere and overly loud music has me holding back a star. Also, it is a shame that they do not offer table service. They have too many employees mingling and standing around not to offer it. They were all eager to remove your dirty dishes. So much, they were practically tripping over each other to do so. Also, the patio not being covered makes it uncomfortable. You're in the direct sunlight and if a cloud burst happens, there is limited space inside for you to relocate.   I knew going in that it was counter service, so I was surprised when they told me I could sit at the bar and be serviced. So, my recommendation to anyone dining here, is sit at the bar. The bartender was extremely friendly and shared his recommendations from the menu. He also, told me which ones were proving to be customer favorites. With his guidance, I had an enjoyable and flavorful lunch.   I started out with a House Margarita and Club Tots. The Margarita was a simple and "classic" Rita. The fried tots toped with white cheddar, freshly toasted green chilies and topped with a free range fried egg. I'd want these for breakfast instead of hash browns, they were that good.  I went with a trio of tacos; Traditional Bisteca, Deep South and Southern Fried Tomatoes. I had a nice mix of classic, deep south poultry and vegetarian. The Bisteca was typical - the flank steak was tender. My Deep South was creative and unique. I liked the fried chicken breast, but I'm still not sure how I liked mashed potatoes in my taco. To my surprise, my favorite was the Southern Fried Tomatoes. I love Fried Green Tomatoes and the way they created this taco. The tomatoes are fried in cornmeal, tossed in a Thai sweet chile sauce and served with one of my favorite cheeses, Goat cheese. So it was a total winner for me.   Wanting to tweet my excitement about the Fried Green Tomatoes Taco, I asked the bartender what their tweeter account was. He admitted he didn't know, but went to ask the owner who was working on his laptop at the counter. When he came back, he informed me that they didn't have one. I was surprised that in this social media society that they didn't have one as a new business. I encouraged the bartender to get his boss to get one soon, that it is a great way to get publicity. (Side-note: I found it odd that as the restaurant filled up at lunchtime, the owner did not mingle with the diners - he stayed focused on his computer)   Will I return? Perhaps, if I'm in Kirkwood and want a quick Mexican lunch. Would I make a special trip to Kirkwood and eat there? No.   Also be aware, there are no chips and salsa or Queso or even Guacamole.   When: July 11, 2016 Why: Lunch at the New Hot Spot

5 stars for a Post Office! You may be shocked, but this PO deserves every one of these five stars.   When I moved into my neighborhood 8 years ago, I had no idea how convenient would be to have a PO down the street. When friends found out where I moved, several commented I had moved near the best kept secret PO in the city. It is tucked away on a side street, making it convenient and away from busy traffic. Your able to get in and out with no problems.   I've never known them to be out of shipping supplies and they always seem to have the unique stamps that I prefer to use.   Best of all, they workers here are genuinely happy. When a worker is happy, they provide good customer service. I have seen lines here, but this crew knows how to keep the flow flowing.   Shhhhhh. Remember this is a well kept secret how good this PO truly is. Let's just keep it between us Yelpers.

Thanks to social media, Adam's has been teasing me with their Brisket Burger. Every time, I'd be at work or out of town. Today, when I saw the announcement, it was lunchtime and I drove right over to get mine.   The burger was thick and covered the entire bun. If you want cheese, you're given the choice of having it placed on top, or injected inside. I choose to have mine injected. It was so cool, when I took my first bite cheese oozed out. There was so much cheese.   When it came to choosing my bbq sauce, I opted for no bbq sauce. I wanted to taste the true flavors of the smoked brisket in the burger. Yum. When I got home, I did add a nice slice of onion and a few hot pickles to compliment the big burger.   The brisket burger special came with two sides. I choose my two favorites at Adam's, their Pit Beans and Cole Slaw. The Pit Beans were a perfect pairing for a smoked burger. Don't get me wrong, the cole slaw was good to, but the pit beans were just better.   The staff is great here. They make me feel like Norm on, Cheers. They know my name, always use it when speaking to me and thank me for coming in each time I visit.   I'll be back? - Yes. They make my favorite ribs.   When: May 30,2019 Why: My first Brisket Burger

I'm bumping TC&TB up a star for having gotten rid of ordering at the counter and taking a table marker. You now are seated and one of the numerous servers running around take your order and there is no silly marker.   Another reason for the increased star, is their amazing Bloody Mary.  Made with not only a spicy mix, but the salt & pepper rim had a kick of its own. Definitely one of the better Bloody Mary's I've enjoyed in awhile. I also give them kudos for the simple garnish of just two olives.    My breakfast entree this morning was the, Cold Smoked Salmon. It was light and refreshing. A toasted Everything Bagel with a heavy smear of Chive Cream Cheese, a small cup of Crispy Capers and a healthy portion of thinly sliced smoked salmon. Along side of all that, was a crisp cucumber salad. A breakfast of champions.   The food and beverage here is outstanding. However, the customer service still needs work. Even though they have gotten rid of the order at the counter, they need to get their staff to focus on service. So many of them will be standing around in groups of three or two talking while there are diners needing service & attention. Also, the staff needs to be a little more cordial to the guest. If the staff becomes more attentive and friendly, this definitely will be a 5 Star establishment.   I'll be back? - Yes, I love the food and want to see them reach a 5.   When: January 30, 2018 Why: Breakfast

Yippie! It's been a long time since we've had a new baby in our family and we finally have one on the way.   Since those little people grow so fast, they are in and out of sizes so quickly. I was shopping with a friend and while they looked for clothes in the adult section, I strolled through the baby section.   I was impressed with the variety and more so with the price point. This new addition to our family is going to grow so fast, why spend a fortune on outfits, when you can make him look cute at bargain prices.   I really not an Uncle, but I have had that title bestowed upon me. So as this little guy grows up, I'll be shopping here periodically to add to his closet and drawers.   I don't recall seeing any associates on the sales floor, but I am fairly self sufficient when I shop. The cashier when checking out was fast and efficient.   When: September 1, 2021 Why: Baby Clothes

When you have a fantastic poster to frame, you need a fantastic frame shop. When you need a fantastic frame shop, you go to Dogtown Gallery &  Frame Shop. When you go to Dogtown Gallery, Jaynelle will take care of you and your fantastic artwork.   I recently found a cool City of Saint Louis Neighborhoods poster from STyLe at the Collective MX. The only problem, it wasn't framed. For me not being framed really isn't a problem, I like creating my own showcase for the art I buy.   This poster is so cool, how it highlights all the small hoods that make up our great city. Many of these neighborhoods I never heard of till I started Yelping and checking into businesses on my smart-phone. Now I have a map that shows me exactly where all these little hoods are tucked away. When I explained to Jaynelle what I visualized as my frame, she totally agreed with my vision. I had told her, I just wanted a simple frame and no matting. I wanted the focus to be on the map and did not want matting to distract the attention. She asked me where it would be hanging and I told her a hallway with no natural lighting. She then recommended that I still upgrade to the non glare glass just in case I do move the artwork to a new location that did expose it to natural light. The upgrade to that type of glass was minimal and it was something I normally do anyway.   I was so pleased with my final piece, that I told Jaynelle that I will be back very soon. I have a drawer with several pieces of art that have been waiting for me to find a talented and skilled framer and my search has been completed.

This LensCrafters is not what it use to be. I feel bad that I have to take a star away from them, but the customer service has declined on my last visit.   Prior visits the sales associates were hustling and bustling helping you find the perfect frame. Now, they just sit at their desk or stand around and talk to each other. After I made my selection, all by myself, her attitude was condescending as she checked me out. Don't talk down to your customer, we're why you have a job and are there working.   I also saw a difference in the quality of frames that were on display. I know Luxottica owns LensCrafters and many of the brands they offer in the store. So it was disappointing to see a drop in the product quality.   When my glasses were ready and I came in to pick them up, the service wasn't much better. They handed them to me and asked if I could see clearly. I was so tempted to say, "Yes, I can see I will not be coming back here for future frames."   Seriously, they truly did deserve a 2 Star rating, but I like Antoine Eye Care that is attached to the store. That is why I only dropped them to a 3 Star rating. In the future, I get my eyes checked at Antoine and take my prescription somewhere else.

Outstanding!  Service, food and ambiance are all 5 Stars in my opinion. I was totally blown away on my recent visit. I cannot wait to go back. If I still lived in the STL metro area, I would be a regular here.   I was in the big city to run errands and have lunch with a friend. The original restaurant I wanted to dine at, was packed and we couldn't get a table. My friend recommended, Perennial on Lockwood and I am so glad that she did. Both of us were impressed and luck her, she has already returned for a repeat visit.   Instead of a table, we opted for the bar and Carson the bartender was a delight. He was friendly, a skilled mixologist and spoke professionally about the menu items we asked about. He described them so fluently, we could not resist ordering them.   Starting out we ordered some liquid refreshment. I enjoyed the, Fall Old Fashioned and my friend enjoyed one of their many craft beers. The FOF was made with; rye, spiced apple cider, big o walnut and angostura bitters. It was the perfect welcoming to the autumn season.   To accompany our first adult beverages we enjoyed an order of their house made, Onion Rings. They were the perfect size. Not super large and not to small, as Goldielocks would say, "They were, just right." The light crisp battering is what made them, the perfect starter to our lunch.   When our glasses got empty and it was time to fill them up again, my friend ordered a couple of their 5 oz beers (sorry, forgot to capture a photo) which was smart. It was a great way to sample multiple brews. I on the other hand, switched to the, House G+T. Once Carson explained and told me how he enjoyed the dry-hopped brokers gin, I was sold. It was so refreshing, I could enjoy this cocktail year round.   For our entree, we decided to split, Claire's Grilled Cheese. I have no idea who Claire is, but she makes on hell of a grilled cheese. It was delicious, but next time I will add bacon and take it to the next level. The fries that came with the sammie, were some of the best I have had in a while. They reminded me of the Shoestring fries you use to get at Steak-n-Shake (when they were good). The fries were super crisp and seasoned perfectly with both salt and pepper. To our surprise, Carson and the kitchen split our order on to two plates without us requesting. That is outstanding customer service.   Other things that always make me happy when dining at a bar, is outlets under the bar for charging electrical devices. I was surprised they didn't have hooks for purses and jackets, but I'll take outlets by themselves. I also, am a big fan of linen napkins over paper. Linen just makes dining better.   If you have not been to, Perennial on Lockwood, I insist you go immediately.   When: October 28, 2021 Why: Lunch with a friend

One of my favorite spots in STL for a burger. If size is important to you you'll love a Seamus burger.  Their flame broiled burgers are HUGE and are full of flavor. A flame broiled burger, just seems to be juicier. They offer crinkle cut fries as side and they always give me more then I can eat and I love fries. The fries are done crispy, but I am fairly certain they are from a bag.   Our last visit we discovered their Club Sandwich and Chicken Wings are also worthy of a good shout out. I love experiencing new items off their menu, but it is their burger that will always have my heart.

A very good Irish Pub in the heart of Dogtown.  The burgers here are off the charts - they are some of the best in the entire city. They are grilled over open flame pit and the flavor is amazing. They also have a Rib Eye Steak Sandwich that is shockingly better then the burgers. The french fries are done to perfection as a side. If two of you are getting burgers, one of you needs to get the onion rings so you can share the two sides. Yes, the portions are large enough to share. Want to eat healthy? The Chef Salad is as the menu says, "a meal within itself". Beer is ice cold and the servers make for a pleasant dining experience.

The angels were definitely singing the night I dined at Twisted Tree. I will be honest, if it were not for the stellar review from Joan G., I may have never tried TT. I hate to admit it, but what kept me away was the fact that  a steakhouse was connected to Syberg's. I questioned how a restaurant known for its chicken wings, and being a sports bar, could prepare a high quality steak? I learned my lesson on being judgmental very quickly. They can do it very well.   I arrived around 6:30 PM on a Saturday night without a reservation. As my usual protocol, I informed the hostess I did not mind sitting at the bar. She directed me to the left side, where 4 stools were awaiting and told me to make myself comfortable. As I selected my throne for the night, I was cheerfully greeted by Lindsey one of the multiple bartenders working that evening. She took my order for a Manhattan and quickly began to prepare it before my eyes. Her skills were fast and masterful - I enjoyed my Manhattan so much, I had two that evening.   When she presented me my cocktail, she asked if I'd be dining at the bar. When I replied yes, she immediately set me up with a white linen place sitting. I knew I wanted the infamous onion rings, so I placed my order for them. When they arrived, they totally lived up to their reputation. They're light, flakey, crisp and the seasoning is like no other onion ring. I normally don't dip my onion rings, but they presented a buffalo sauce and ketchup for dipping. Most of the rings I ate without dipping, but the buffalo sauce provided an extra kick to those that I did dip.   As I munched on the rings, Lindsey and chatted about her favorite sides. I told her I was famished and most likely would order two sides. An extra side with an entree order is only $3. When you see the size of the serving, you realize it is a steal of a deal. I also had the option of not having a salad and enjoying the two sides. I was a glutton and wanted it all.   For my entree, I ordered an 8 oz Prime Rib, medium rare. I also enjoyed; Caesar Salad, White Cheddar Potatoes Au Gratin (a Lindsey favorite) and Fire Roasted Brussels Sprouts (my favorite vegetable). The prime rib was prepared to my requested temperature. It was so tender, my steak knife slid through it like a warm knife through butter. I then tried just breaking off a bite with my fork and it again was simply done. It was capital T - tender.   Both side dishes were, killer good. I will always order Brussels Sprouts when I see them on a menu. These are definitely prepared well. They had that crisp fresh texture. They were not over cooked or under cooked - they were just right. I am so happy that I listed to the bartender and tried the Au Gratin potatoes. She also recommended the mashed, but I choose Au Gratin, because of the White Cheddar. Go with one of these potatoes, you can get a Baked Potato anywhere.   Once again, my eyes were bigger then my stomach. I had enough food to take home and make my co-workers jealous with an incredible lunch the next day. To be honest, I still came home with some Brussels Sprouts and Au Gratin Potatoes from that work lunch. No worries, the sprouts made a flavorful frittata and the potatoes became breakfast potatoes.   Even though I was stuffed and didn't clean my plate, I had to have dessert. I love Wedding Cake and had to try theirs. I had seen so many pictures on Yelp and everyone raved how good it was. Everyone was right, it hit the spot and satisfied my sweet craving without being overly sweet. It a great way to enjoy one of your favorite cakes, without getting married or going to wedding. Yes, I had left-overs and I took them to work and finished off the slice of cake with my morning coffee. It may not have been the healthiest breakfast, but it was damn good.   A highlight that makes Twisted Tree stand out above the other upscale steakhouses is that; a salad and one side is included in the price of your entree. Everything is not A la carte. That is a win-win.   Will I return? - I'm a meat man, so that answer is, YES!  When: December 2, 2017 Why: Dinner - Super Belated Birthday with Gift Cards

I've been long overdue for new glasses and have been putting off the purchase for some time. Yesterday I finally took the first steps to improve my vision of the world. However, I kind of do things backwards from most people. I shop multiple times searching for the perfect frame, before finally getting my eyes examined.  We were in the Galleria and I thought why not check out LensCrafter one more time for frames. This time I found a couple pair that were a possibility. One was a tortoise Ray Ban and the other a cool pair of Oakley's. Then it happened, as we browsed the last section of frames a pair of Dolce and Gabbana screamed my name. They were black with highlights of my signature color, orange. They looked great on me and I loved 'em.   Nerea, who is the Sales Supervisor was assisting me and was able to get me in with the doctor at Antoine Eye Care fairly quick making my process of choosing these frames easy. She held the frames for me, I got the eye exam and we closed the sale.   Modern technology is mind blowing. I remember the days when they use to mark your lens with a sharpie for vision lines. Now you put your new frames on, they take your picture with the computer and your done. I swear computers are taking over the world.   My lens are not easy, so it will take about 10 days before mine are ready. Normally I am one who wants instant gratification, but this time I will wait patiently because I found a frame that I love.

It's amazing how a year and a pandemic can change things. My most recent visit wasn't what it use to be. I truly was disappointed.   A friend and I were out running errands on a Wednesday in December and stopped by for lunch. We were seated on the back patio. I stopped to use the bathroom before joining my friend on the patio. When I entered the patio, I was hit in the face with a strong odor. The bathroom I just used smelled better then the patio. I have a sensitive nose. It didn't seem to bother my friend, so I kept it to myself, but it did effect my experience.   We each had a draft beer to accompany our sandwiches. I had the Cheesy Bacon Burger and my friend had the Buffalo Chicken Sandwich. Both of our sammies came with a side of fries. Both of us enjoy crinkle fries, so we were pleased that is the type Seamus serves and their position is always generous.   My friend was pleased with her Buffalo Chicken, but my burger was not up to the level I am use to getting at Seamus. The grade of beef seemed to be different and my burger was over cooked. I also could not get beyond the odor, I should have spoken up and moved inside.   In closing, I'll say the customer service wasn't what it normally is, but it was obvious they were short staffed, so I will not judge them on that.   I haven't given up on Seamus, I'll still go back and hope for a better outcome.

If you love vintage, you're going to love shopping at Strangelovely. I am so glad Kim relocated her fabulous shop from Chicago back to her hometown roots. It fits perfectly inside this historical home.   Her boutique has not only fashions, but decor for the home. I missed out on two fabulous nude male sketches for my new bathroom. They were snatched up by another shopper and we had a good laugh. He was buying them for the exact same reason.  One table displaying a large variety of serving pieces really caught my eye. It had something for everyones taste. It was a good mix, of silver-plate and brass. With these pieces, a novice could create a stunning table for entertaining.   I only made a small purchase, but it was a favorite item. I added two soy candles to my collection in masculine scents, Tobacco and Black Pepper. I can't wait to strike a match and have the aroma fill my new house.   Kim and her associates were charming and helpful. I'm looking forward to shopping again, since it is less than a mile from my home.   When: February 6, 2021 Why: Shopping Local

We all know the burgers at Seamus McDaniel's are some of the best in the city. So when I do updated reviews, I like to give shout outs for other items of their extensive menu. Why let their burgers have all the glory and limelight.   Our recent visit was for a late lunch, we arrived between 1:30 & 2 PM. As we glanced over the menu, we ordered a couple of ice teas and an order of Onion Rings. If you haven't ordered them before, do so soon. They are huge rings of onion heavily breaded, deep fried to perfection. They're always served hot and crisp. I cut mine in half for easier eating and dipping in ketchup.   My sandwich of choice was the Pork Loin with Fries. You have a choice of either deep fried with buffalo sauce or grilled with lettuce, tomato and onion. I went for the bad boy and choose fried. I went with the buffalo sauce on the side. The piece of pork loin was huge, it spilled over the entire bun. I had to cut it in half to enjoy  and to be able to dip it in to the buffalo sauce. The fries are frozen, but I love a crinkle cut fry so I am a happy camper.   My lunch partner also took a different path then the typical burger. He choose the Philly Beef. Roast Beef sliced from the prime rib, pile high on a toasted bun with Philly cheese, sautéed green peppers and onions and a side of au jus. As always, I some how to manage a bite. This was some of the most tender beef I have ever tasted on a Philly.   The lunch service is always down home friendly and quick. We were in and out within an hour, which is great for those on a work lunch break. I also give them a shout out for having all three of the artificial sweeteners, they've earned a spot on my Rainbow of Sweetness List.   Remember, Seamus is just not for burgers.   When: 3 Feb 2014 Why: Lunch

This is embarrassing, I just realized I haven't updated my review for 7 years. How could I have forgotten to write a new review for one of my favorite restaurants for burgers, chicken wings and onion rings. It's an error, I need to correct now.   I'll start with the Onion Rings. No matter what I am having, burgers or wings, I always start out with an order of OR's as an appetizer. They are huge rings, that are hand dipped and coated with a flavorful batter that is fried to a crisp. No side is needed for dipping, but sometimes I dab a little ketchup on one or two of them.  Their burgers are 10 oz. of Angus beef. My go to order is always a cheeseburger. My cheese choice is Pepper Jack and I have it prepared to a medium rare. Their kitchen always get the temp right and I love how the cheese is completely melted and dripping down the edges like icing on a cake. The fries are always crisp on the outside and soft and hot on the inside. Best of all, they're crinkle fries which are my favorite to accompanying a burger.   In closing, I tell you Seamus has some of the best wings in the city. They are not batter, fried crisp, meaty and tossed in a house sauce that is a medium spicy. I'm a counter, so I like that when I order the wings at Seamus, I get the same number of flats and little drums. If your not a sauce person like one of my friends, you can order the wings plain and have your sauce on the side. They also give you a choice of Ranch and Blu Cheese for dipping. I like their sauce so much, I don't dip in either dressing.   Customer service is what you'd expect at an Irish pub. It's attentive, but they also leave you alone so you can have a conversation.   My visit during the pandemic were safe. Once I was on the patio and recently, we were one of two tables in the dining room with plenty of space between us.   If you go, order the Onion Rings!   When: January 13, 2021 and a couple times in 2020.  Why: Usually lunch.

A group of ten meet here around 9pm after doing three hours of volunteering. We were eager to reward ourselves with cocktails and food. Once we all arrived we were meet with disappointment, the kitchen was closed. It appears they put a new floor in the kitchen and it had to be closed ALL DAY. Oh well, our server kept the drinks flowing.  You'd think a business owner would have paid the extra $'s to put the floor in after the kitchen closed the previous night so it would be ready for the next days business. I'm confident the money made for an open kitchen would have paid for the extra expense, instead of losing an entire day of  food sales. Just think, if they served us food they might have had a fourth star and if the food was good a fifth.

It was time for a work birthday party and we discussing cake. One of my co-workers, said how about trying, "The Cakery". I immediately light up and said, YES! YES! I grabbed my smartphone, and showed them reviews and pictures on Yelp to sell them on the idea of ordering the cake from, The Cakery.   My enthusiasm sold them and we ordered the birthday cake. The honoree is a big candy lover, so we selected one topped in a variety of sweet treats. The cake was a two tiered chocolate separated by a vanilla butter creme. The top was close to a Tiffany Blue dripping down the sides. Beautiful presentation.   Our birthday boy loved his cake and my co-workers who had never experienced, The Cakery were totally impressed. They loved the rich flavor and how moist the cake was. This was a total win.   Perhaps we'll celebrate the next birthday with cupcakes from, The Cup. I already started singing the praises of their cupcake store.   Would I go again? Yes, I always love a good cake.   When: October 7, 2017 Why: Birthday Celebration

How do I judge a hot chicken wing? If it makes beads of sweat pop up on my forehead, I have a winner. Today for lunch, I ordered the Spicy Fresh Jalapeño Chicken Wings and before I bite into them, I knew I had a winner from the aroma. When the server placed my tray in front of me, I instantly got a rush from the jalapeños. After a few bites, I had the confirmation I was looking for, the beads of sweat started to appear.  I love jalapeños, when I see them on a burger menu it is a must order. So when I saw them on the menu today, it was a no brainer.  I did the Combo #2, which is 5 wings each of two flavors, small side and 20 oz beverage. A pretty good deal for a lunch. My second flavor was the Lemon Pepper, another of my favorite wing flavors. I like the tangy tartness of the lemon mixed with my favorite simple spice, pepper.  Both wings were done well, they had a crispy crunch coating. Which is the way wings should be in my opinion.  As I waited for my wings, I read other reviews on Yelp and realized I should have ordered the Red Hot Riplet Wings. All my friends raved about how tasteful they were. I guess the only thing I can do now, is go back for another visit. In the meantime, I can decide which other flavor I want in my #2 Combo. Should it be; Rally Squirrel, Dry Rub or Caribbean Jack? Decisions, Decisions.   My fries were also, very crisp on the outside. The portion was huge, for a small serving. It easily could have been shared by two.The large serving must be gigantic. I also liked that they still had the skins on. I'm fairly certain that they were a frozen product, but they were a top quality. If they are house cut, they should promote them as such on the menu.   St. Louis Wing Company offers over 15+ flavors of wings, so I guess I'll be coming back for lunch again and again. It's going to take me awhile to eat my way through all the flavors, but I love an eatable challenge.   When: July 6, 2016 Why: Wingin' It for lunch

I be bad. I thought I had written a review for Grapeseed and then noticed I hadn't written a review for one of my favorite restaurants in the South Hampton area. I have dined alone, with a friend and in a group of good size and each time the food and service has been stellar.   Having been raised on a beef farm, I am very partial to grass fed beef and Grapeseed offers one of the, if not the best grass fed burgers in STL. It comes from Rain Crown Ranch and is served with a true special sauce, lettuce, cheddar cheese, homemade pickles and onion all served on a Brioche bun. I've had it on the bun and without and either way I love it.   When I'm going low-carb, I go without the bun. However, I have been known to go bun-less so I can enjoy their amazing house cut fries with house aioli. Now these I will say, without a doubt are the best fries. They are thick cut, skin on, seasoned well and fried crisp. In addition to the house aioli, you get a little cup of ketchup.   Another great meal is combining my two favorite small plates; Tagliatelle and the House Smoked Trout Cake.  The tagliatelle combines Double Star farms lamb with Salume Beddu pork bolognese mascarpone with pizzicato cheese & oregano gremolata. Those who dine with me, have the risk of getting forked if they try to sneak a sample off my plate.  A picture is worth a thousand words, so look at the one I posted of the trout cake and you'll see how delicious it is.   The menu can change based on deliveries from the local farmers, but when and if you see the Flank Steak on the menu - order it. It will be tender and mouth watering. I always get mine done rare medium.   My favorite cocktail is the Moscow Mule and I like their version; Macklind Mule served in the traditional copper mug.   I'm glad Grapeseed is in my hood. I will continue to support them and hope you will give them a try.

What an amazing "Little Shop".  It is, Estate Sale goes boutique.  They've got some unique art work, delicate china and crystal and antique/vintage furniture. The items for sale would be considered to be "best" of the best. It may be the best, but the prices are still affordable and 100% of the proceeds go to the Missouri Botanical Gardens. Resulting in guilt free shopping, because you actually are donating to a charity.

Grapeseed is in my rotation of my local hood restaurants that I can get a quick and satisfying dinner. It's another one that I am not surprised that it made the STL 100 List. It did surprise me that the "must order" recommendation was the Turkey Nachos.  I'm typically a breast man, especially when comes to turkey. I love the turkey breast at thanksgiving and enjoy a smoked turkey breast at BBQ joints. So when I saw, that these Turkey Nachos were made from the leg, I never thought to order them. Now that Ian, said they are a must order, I've given them a try and they are a winner.   They make for a light and simple dinner with a craft beer. The turkey is from Buttonwood Farms, which always a plus. The foundation of the nachos is crispy sweet potato chips, topped with the meat of a turkey leg, braised in house "firecracker" sauce, grape tomatoes, red onion, roasted red pepper and topped with a buttermilk dressing. Best thing- it's gluten free for those who need to be concerned about that type of diet.  The Burger and the House Cut Fries will always be my favorite and would have been my "must order". If you are having trouble finding a place to park on the street, don't fret, you can park in the lot over at Tom Bess Automotive.   When: April 16, 2016 Why: Nachos and STL 100

I heard such great things about Johnny's, but for me I was not impressed. Their cash register receipt says, "Even Our Failures Are Edible!". I can totally agree with that, because I ate one of their failures.  First let me tell you that they are a cash only business. If you're like me and don't carry cash, they do have an ATM machine on site. I didn't use it, so I cannot tell you the actual fee that they charge. Lucky for me, I just happened to have enough dollars in my pocket to cover my Po-Boy.   Also, don't just look at the menu posted up and behind the counter. On the meat case, they had a small combo special posted which was a better deal then my sandwich by itself. I wish I would have noticed it before I ordered. If I had, I could have enjoyed 1/2 of a sandwich, a cup of gumbo and a refillable soda. That would have been a good deal.   I had a Shrimp Po-Boy Dressed. I enjoyed the shrimp, but the rest of the Po-Boy was a disappointment. The bread, was crusty and kind of dried out. I don't want to use the word stale, but it definitely was not made that day. The bread at Subway or Jimmy John's is better quality then the bread here. Also, I was expecting a little more when I ordered mine dressed. But, for an additional 60 cents, I guess I got what I paid for; iceberg lettuce and an almost ripe tomato.   However, the shrimp was fried and seasoned well. I opened up my sandwich and picked them out and enjoyed the shrimp by themselves. The portion was plentiful, they did not skimp on the amount that they served.   Service was nothing special. It was what you'd expect of a semi-high volume tourist attraction cafe. Ambiance is kinda divey which adds to its' charm. Would I return? Most likely not, I've gotten better Po-Boy's in STL at a restaurant that has seafood flown in daily and makes their bread fresh daily as well.   When: August 27, 2016 Why: Wanted a true Po-Boy

WOW! I cannot tell you how excited I was waiting for the Copper Pig to open. Now that it has opened, I am sad to say, it is the winner of a Stevie B Yelp Award. It is the winner of; The Absolute Worst Meal at a Restaurant in 2015. They disappointed me with; food, cocktails and service.  Let me start off with the positive points that saved them from getting a 1 Star Review:  1) Linen Napkins - They're always give a nice upscale feeling to any restaurant.  2) Eco-Friendly To-Go Vessels - Thinking of our planet.  3) French Fries - European style fries & a little cup of ketchup.  4) It's in my hood - Brings variety and vitality to the neighborhood. 5) Girl with water pitcher always made sure your glass was full. (Also see negative point)*  Now the reasons why it was The Absolute Worst Meal at a Restaurant in 2015:  1) Service - Very rushed. We ordered cocktails and three appetizers. When our drinks were served, waitress asked for the rest of our order. We stated we wanted to wait until our small plates arrived. Later when the small plates arrived, she again asked for order. When we ordered a second round of drinks, she responded, "I meant your entrees". The time we were there, it was obvious they wanted us to eat, drink and go as quickly as possible.  2) Deviled Eggs with Bacon Chips - Had the taste of refrigerator. 3) Crispy Brussel Sprouts with Miso and Bacon - Bacon dominated the dish with Brussels Sprouts that were undercooked and hard. Dish was overly salty. Good thing for the water girl.  4) Beet Fries - Tasteless. I love beets and these were flavorless mush. I think they were prepped to far in advance.  5) Bulgogi Cheesesteak - Tough and hard to chew. Disassembled sandwich to see if that would help, but it was the actual beef that was making it tough and chewy.  6) Board Burger - Mealy burger, with a grey tint. My friend said, it resembled a burger patty from McDonald's. Her dog wouldn't even eat it when served the leftovers which were the majority of the burger. (Take note of photo) 7) Cocktails - Weak and unprofessionally prepared. Obvious their bartenders are more comfortable opening beer bottles and pour a draft beer. No skills in a well crafted cocktail.   After leaving CP we went down the street to another establishment and ran into several other diners who where at the CP as well. We all compared notes and were in agreement that they have a lot of improving to do.   I hate for a business in my hood to be on my Terrible Two's List. So I'm going to give them a couple weeks to work their kinks out and hopefully they will. Then I'll revisit them again and hopefully be able to raise my rating.  When: November 12, 2015 Why: Belated Birthday Dinner

United Provisions is another great addition to The Loop. This store is an excellent blend of a Whole Foods type grocery store, with a mix of an ethnic market and a breathtaking selection of craft beers.   It's not close enough for me to do regular shopping, but I can't resist popping in after a lunch or dinner at Mission Taco Joint.   I'll be honest, the single bottle sales of craft beers and the ability to create a six pack has helped me create some cool gifts for various family members. This service alone makes me a fan.   If you're in The Loop, shop United Provisions, you'll surprise yourself with what you can find.

What a delightful surprise and too think we almost didn't come to Schneithorst because come of the reviews on Yelp. After reading them more carefully, we decided it was one of those places that you either love it or hate. We loved it.   After dropping off our foster dog at the doggie spa, we needed breakfast and headed over to Schneithorst. We were promptly greeted as we entered and taken to a table for two. As we were seated, they promptly asked what we'd like to drink. We opted for ice tea, since we already had plenty of coffee at home. When our server returned, we asked for more time to glance over the menu since it was our first time.   The selection of breakfast items was much larger then your typical IHOP or Denny's. Or at least it seemed so to me, there was so much to choose from. Would you believe it, with such a variety of choices, we both wanted the same thing. We ordered their "Southern Pride",  which is two farm fresh eggs, golden hash browns and authentic Southern style biscuits and gravy. We differed on our side dishes, bacon for me and sausage patty's for him.   I love the salesmanship that goes into the writing of menus. I giggled when I read the word, "authentic" in the description of their biscuit. Come on, how authentic can a German restaurant make a Southern biscuit. Well, the laugh was on me. This was the best damn biscuit I have "ever" had. It truly was a "authentic" southern style biscuit and the gravy would put a farmers wife to shame. The biscuit was the moist and flaky, not dried out like I have found at so many other locations in the Lou. The milk gravy covering the two biscuits, had chunks of sausage and the right amount of pepper to give the flavor an extra kick.  Their kitchen did a great job on our eggs too. I like'm over medium and Brad ordered his over easy. You could see the difference, in our yolks and that is no joke.  Sorry, I just couldn't resist saying that. The hash browns were good, next time I will request them extra crispy.  As simple as our sides were, they were very good. As usual, our eyes were bigger then our stomachs and we took half of our sides home as a treat for the dogs.  I found the service to be very friendly. You can tell they have a lot of regulars, because everybody kinda knew every-ones name. There was also a lot of glad handing between tables.  If this were in my hood, I'd make it a regular breakfast stop for sure.   *The above review was my 400th review on Yelp.

I love this theater, I like the stadium seating. I am a short person and enjoy the fact that I do not need to worry about a member of the Harlem Globetrotters sitting in front of me. However, it does amaze me how all the attendees do seem to congregate in the same area of the theater. We were the first to arrive and as the other viewers arrived, we chuckled how they clustered around around our seats.   There is a Walgreen's adjacent to this AMC and if you shop before your movie, you'll see a display of theater candies on sale. Their signage actually says, "theater candy", 3 for $3. They are truly taking advantage of their location.  Being winter we had deep pockets for stocking up on treats and bottled beverages that were on sale for only a $1 as well.   The theaters are always clean, as are the restrooms and as I stated in my previous review the staff is friendly.  Only thing that is a negative, it the volume is always louder then I think they need to be.

I don't remember getting hit in the head, but it must of happened. Why else would I have been craving JITB Tacos all morning?  All I ever get from Jack is his Ultimate Cheeseburger. It has probably been 8 years since I had one of his tacos and they were all  I could think about this morning. This one I can not figure out.   When lunch time came around, I gave into this unusual craving and went to visit Jack. As I entered his front door (I hate using a drive-thru) I noticed a poster promoting 2 free tacos with purchase if a Cardinals home game was a shutout. I knew the boys of summer were in town last night, but did not here the score. To my surprise, it was a SHUTOUT and I got my tacos FREE. Hot damn, that is a winner. All I had to buy was my diet coke and I had lunch.  My taco craving has been satisfied, but if the Cardinals have another shutout at home this season, you just may see me in line for some free tacos.   If you're a big fan of JITB and want to receive mobile offers from Jack, just text JACKSTL to 31278 and guess what? You'll get 2 FREE Tacos.   The staff was friendly and eagerly promoted the free tacos. True Cardinal fans or dedicated Jack employees? You make the call.

I love this store. I don't shop here that often, but when I do, I always find what I am looking for. It has an amazing men's department and the shoe department will blow your mind for both men and women.   I am sure you've all heard about the customer service at Nordstrom and it is true. Every time I have shopped here, the service has always been attentive and beyond what you receive at any other local department store. As we see the business at major department stores dwindling away, Nordstrom is still bringing their A-Game with merchandise and customer service.   I'll be back? - Hell, yes.   When: June 13, 2018 Why: Wedding clothes.

I closed my previous review with, "We'll be going back.". This review I will begin with,  "Were done with Olympia, we'll not be coming back."   We arrived for a late lunch, we strolled through the front doors at 1:45 PM. They had a sign up that read, "Please seat yourselves" so we selected a table near the big front window. As we waited to be greeted and have menus brought to us, we noticed the table was extremely sticky and the area around us looked like the floor at a Chuck e Cheese after a 4 year old birthday party. So we got up and moved to a booth in the bar area. This area was better, but there were still tables that needed to be bused and cleaned.   We waited and we waited, finally a waiter brought us menus and said,  **** will be with you shortly. We waited and we waited again. I saw on the wipe board as we entered the daily special was Cod Sandwich with Fries. I was sold. Finally a waitress came to our table, we ordered ice tea. As we sat there, I noticed the other waiter had closed out his tickets, tipped out the busboy and went on his merry way. Our waitress was the only one left covering the entire restaurant and in the other room was a very large party. No team work here. She did the best anyone could being left alone to tend to the number of tables she had.   Olympia may be a Greek restaurant, but we both went with the special. The fries were served steak fries style with skins left on the potato, major points. However, the oil they were fried in was old and needed to be changed. The bun for the sandwich was fresh and soft a perfect match for a fish sandwich. A shame it was a rectangular piece of processed fish. I was so hoping for a true fillet cut of Cod and not the kind that resembles one from Mrs. Paul's.   This lunch could of been a 3 Star review for an average quick meal, but it was the cleanliness of the dining room that nose dived it to a 2.

This is the most entertaining grocery store I have ever been in. The cast of characters  are endless, ranging from the sales associate who also works at the circus as "the tattoo man" and the customer with multiple children who will never win "mother of the year".  Sit me at a high top table in the center of the store with a bottle of wine and some cheese and crackers and I can people watch all day.   I was impressed that they had an aisle tagged "Bosnian". That is going the extra step in customer service and I applaud them. It shows that they know who their customer is and they satisfy their needs. The sales associate "tattoo man" who assisted us, knew his store well. I thought Lard would be in the baking aisle, but no it was in the "Bosnian" aisle. If it weren't for him, I'd still be walking up and down aisles searching.  I agree with Tracey,  I did not have a fondness for their meat department. The selection was fine, but it was cluttered and disorganized making it hard to find the cut of pork we needed for Tamales.   One of their massive merchandising displays caught our eye. The SO commented, "what the hell is that?"  The New Amsterdam Vodka bottles were all capped with  special little security tops to prevent shoplifting. At Walgreen's they have my cold tablets and condoms behind locked Plexiglas and know my Vodka at the grocery store is being secured. Didn't realize my shopping habits needed to be kept under lock - n- key...lol.   The biggest thrill was when we were leaving and spotted Little Edie from Grey Gardens exiting the store at the same time. Yes, she was buying cat food. The Paparazzi missed an opportunity.

I love that a local business, Carol House Furniture  also gives back to our community by helping control the pet population of Saint Louis. Brook and Amy are both big homeless pet advocates and for me it speaks volumes that they walk the talk by providing this clinic to the Saint Louis area.   Having your pet spayed or neutered not only helps control unwanted litters, but it also improves the health of your dog or cat.  Many of us pet owners know, having your pet fixed can be a costly procedure. Here at CHQFPX, you can do it at a very reasonable price. Dogs are only $59 and cats can be fixed for only $39. The month of February 2013 they are having a cat special for only $20.   On Saturday, between 12-2 you can also get various shots for your pets at a fraction of the cost as well.   Let's  not have any unwanted litters and increase the number of pets in our local animal shelters. Take this opportunity and have your pet spayed or neutered  here.

Are we having fun yet? If you're at Mission Taco Joint, you'll never have to ask that question. Because from the moment you enter the door, the party begins.  The entire staff here is always cheerful, friendly and truly go out of their way to make sure you enjoy your time at "The Joint".  In addition to the good food and booze you can feel a positive energy generated through out.   We arrived almost at peak dinner time and had a small wait of about 20 minuets. Which I did not mind at all, it gave us time to enjoy a Mission Margarita at the bar. We told the bartender, that we wanted "the best Margarita" and he delivered.  Not only are they one of the best Margaritas in town, but watching them be made is a show in itself. James Bond would love'm, because they are "shaken, not stirred".   Once seated, we were greeted by Betsy who remembered us from our last visit. Gave us a warm fuzzy feeling. We were glad we had her again too, she's a great server.  We quickly ordered Chips and Salsa, so we could munch while be debated what would be our new MTJ experience. Don't be cheap  order the C&S, you'll understand the difference in what you get at other places "free". There is no comparison, these chips will make your taste buds dance.   I would have loved to experienced the Carne Asada Fries again, but the Crab Taquitos were calling out to me and I am glad that I listened. Crispy tortillas stuffed with Blue Crab Meat, Roasted Corn and Spicy Avocado Sauce. Don't worry about dipping or smearing them in the garnishes on the plate, they are perfect just the way they are served. I can see myself ordering these again with a small side of the Roasted Street Corn as my main entree.  Speaking of Street Corn, their large order is enough for three people to share. We both enjoyed a good serving and I still had enough for lunch the next day. Having it for lunch was a real treat, I tasted it cold before reheating and it was so damn good, I ate it cold. I would love to do a side by side taste test of Mission Taco Joint and Milagro Street Corn to see which one is really the best, because I think it is a close tie.   Earlier the young couple next to us at the bar were enjoying a Piscojitos, so when we ordered our second round of drinks we switched over. Only thing that could make these possibly better, would be a sandy beach and a sexy cabana boy or girl.   The SO continued his quest to experience all the tacos on the menu. The only one I got to get a bite of was the Nopales. Yummy, Yummy. Who knew cactus could taste go good, when served up with goat cheese and roasted jalapeno salsa. I'll be ordering one of these soon.   I also learned on this visit, I should of paid closer attention in high school Spanish instead of being the class clown. I ordered the Chorihevo, which is one of their featured Tortas and I was disappointed. No fault of theirs, the flavor was outstanding and would make a great breakfast sandwich with the sausage, fried egg and pickled jalapeno, and smashed black beans. I just was not expecting it to be served on a very large bun. Again, I stress GREAT flavor, just not what I expected or wanted.  The Chili Crusted Potato Fries that were served with my Tortas, were seasoned well and a perfect accompaniment to the Tortas. Next time I will ask that mine be done a little crispier.   Now on the next visit, I shall start my quest of experiencing ALL the tacos. Only because, this is a TACO joint.

The pastries here, truly are works of art. Each one is masterfully detailed. They're almost picture perfect.
