So perfect, you may not want to eat them, but you will and your sweet tooth will glad that you did.  My first visit, I was so tempted to try the, Ruby (my mom's name). I love the combination of chocolate and raspberry. However, when I went to order, Jarmo-Pistachio came out of my mouth. I guess my love of pistachios overpowered me. The cake was moist and had a perfect combination of salty & sweet.   I also ordered a Chocolate Chip and Pecan Cookie. It amazed me how they made this cookie. It had a crisp bottom, but the top was soft and chewy. What I like about the pastries and cookies here, is that they are not overly sweet. They simply have a nice balance. I like pecans, but for me there were too many in my cookie. However, there was plenty of gooey chocolate chips to make me smile.   Space is very small for dining in. It is best to grab and go. I originally wanted to enjoy my Jarmo in house, but the ladies who I thought were leaving, when I was placing my order were actually just getting up to order more. So I just asked the staff to box mine to go, when I realized I had no place to sit. It still tasted the same at home.   I'll be back, I gotta have a Ruby. Plus, I love macaroons. For me the best macaroons are in Chicago at; Vanille Patisserie.  So, I am wanting a more local bakery to satisfy my cravings for macaroons. I want them more often, then my regular trips up to The French Market in The Loop.   When: September 20, 2016 Why: Hot New Bakery

West County is so lucky. The Fresh Market selected them as their first location in the Saint Louis market. I went their opening day and was totally impressed with the merchandising, freshness and customer service. If they open other locations in the Saint Louis market, they will be setting a new standard for groceries.   The Fresh Market is a grocery store that has a boutique type style. Best way to describe it would be that it is a cross between Whole Foods and Trader Joe's. Lot's of organic products, grass feed beef, gourmet baked goods and unique brands you may not have heard of before. The pricing is high end like Whole Foods. I wish it were more like TJ's.   If they keep up the standards of opening day, this new grocer is going to be a smashing success. The only negative I experienced was the parking. The lot truly was a parking lot derby.

All Steak 'n Shakes are not  the same, when it comes to serving breakfast. The one near my home in STL serves up a fantastic breakfast, but this one was just sad.  I would of been better off going to the IHOP down the street and paying full price instead of trying to save money with a coupon.   Let me start by giving the positives which really make this a 2.5 Stars (Yelp needs to give us the power of the half) review.  My waitress was friendly and hustling being the only server working. My Hash-Browns was crispy and a large serving. They also got my eggs done right, I like over medium and most places either over or under fry them.    Negatives;  only got a half cup of coffee to start out, had to wait for fresh to be made.  My refill was hot & fresh, but I was done eating and only enjoyed two sips. Even though my eggs were cooked correctly, they were greasy. The biscuit, was hard, dried our and almost flat as a pancake.   I will revisit this location for a steak-burger, but it is out of my breakfast rotation.

I was in the market for new tennis shoes and my first stop on my search was here at New Balance. I've worn NB in the past, but it has been awhile.  When I did buy them in the past, I always got them at another store and not a specialized NB one.   We were greeted promptly as we entered. When I told the associate what I needed, she showed me what shoes were available and also pointed out which ones were on sale. They were having an additional 25% off the sale price, which really peaked my interest. New shoes at a savings, I'm there.   We measured my feet and I was shocked to hear how big my feet were. NB measured me two sizes bigger then anyone else has ever measured me. I selected the shoes I'd like to try on and surprise surprise, they were out of my size on all the sale ones. So I tried on a pair that was at regular price. Unfortunately I did not like the fit and choose to continue my search.   As I was striking out the SO was hitting a home run finding a pair of casual shoes that are very similar to a pair of clogs. They aren't to my liking, but they made him and his feet happy so our shopping trip to NB was not a total bust. Perhaps the next time, I will be the lucky one and my feet will leave happy.

Coffee and an Orange Scone (my favorite) before a movie inside the mall.   Service was iffy, not as attentive and friendly as other St Louis Bread locations. They kept running out of coffee, I only got a half cup when filling up first time and then when I went back for a re-fill all dispensers except the flavored were empty. Having worked in the coffee biz, there is no excuse for empty coffee crafts.  Great location in the parking lot of an upscale mall. Allows you to shop high-end and eat within your budget.

Spotted Sweetie's Candy & Cones as we were crossing the street to enjoy lunch at The Block.  Was excited to see the words; candy, ice cream and snow cones in their window. I figured there had to be a sweet treat inside waiting for us after lunch.   After stuffing ourselves at The Block we strolled down Lockwood and ventured inside Sweetie's. It is a collective little shop of candy of days gone by and current day favorites. It also offers Snow Cones, but it was the Ice Cream that caught our eyes.  The SO went with a Pistachio with White Chocolate Covered Almonds, it was damn good. It was actually better then mine. I had a hard time choosing my flavor since they had two of my favorites; Mint Chocolate Chip and Birthday Cake. I went with the Mint, and it satisfied my sweet tooth. I've seen "The Very Best Cookies" in Straub's and had no idea they were baked right here in Webster Groves. In fact, they are baked here at Sweetie's.   The gentleman working was very personable and made us feel welcomed in the tiny little shop. It's a collective little shop, worth a stop when in the area.

The Carousel Bar was my first stop during my weekend in the French Quarter. I arrived fashionably late for Happy Hour, so there was no way I going to get a seat at bar. I did make a walk around the bar so I could see how this fun concept of rotating bar stools was set up. Once my curiosity was satisfied, I mingled off into the packed bar and found a comfy leather wingback chair to relax in.   Shortly after being seated a server was asking for my order. Since I was spending the weekend in New Orleans, I thought it was only appropriated to begin my drinking holiday with a Sazerac. For those of you who do not know, it was declared the official cocktail of New Orleans by the Louisiana Legislature. After one sip, it had my vote. It was a magical blend of Sazerac Rye Whiskey, Simple Syrup and Peychaud's Bitters. It was slick and smooth just like the politicians who bestowed the title upon it.   With my cocktail the server sat down a small bowl of bar mix which was a nice nosh as I enjoy my Sazerac and listened to Robin Barnes perform in the bar. My first bar stop was a great springboard for the rest of my weekend. After one cocktail, I was off to explore more of NOLA.   When: August 26, 2016 Why: Sazerac

We needed lunch at work and no one wanted to go out into the nasty weather. So I thought of Park Chop Suey, knowing that they delivered.   Our food was surprisingly good and delivered fast. I will say, the Crab Rangoon was the best fast Chinese I have ever had. They were huge, and you get six instead of the usual four from other restaurants. Their egg rolls were small, but full of flavor. Our main entrees were Special and Beef Fried Rice.  I always worry that  Fried Rice will be dry, not here it was moist which made it's flavor pop.   Next time we need lunch delivered, we're calling Park Chop Suey again.

My CRV had an emergency visit at St. Louis Honda directly across the street from Bartolino's South and it was lunch time. Neither of us had ever been, but were familiar with their location at the Drury Inn on Hampton in the city. So we took our own lives in to our hands and walked across the busy five lanes of Lindbergh.   I knew before we were seated what I wanted for lunch. I absolutely love their Bartolino's Special Salad. It's a huge bowl filled with mixed lettuce and your choice of either turkey or salami. I choose turkey. Then they toss it with provel cheese, pepperoncini, kalamata olives, artichoke hearts and tomatoes in their famous house dressing. This is always a favorite for me, I enjoy it regularly as a carry out from Osteria.   My dining partner enjoyed a Pan-Fried Chicken Milanese Sandwich with Seasoned French Fries. It was Italian-style breaded chicken with a hint of lemon served on toasted garlic cheese bread. He was only able to eat half, so the other half is going to make another great lunch tomorrow. The Seasoned Fries were your typical fries out of a bag, but still a nice side dish for the sandwich. In hindsight, a side of pasta would have been better.   The decor is old school Italian, a lot of dark wood and dim lighting. The service was attentive, as you'd expect from an Italian restaurant with this price point. Our waitress and her assistant made sure our glasses of ice tea were always full. They also promptly removed our plates when we finished eating.  Nice lunch. Glad I finally ate here, but I doubt if I'll be back. Why would I when I have Bartolino's Osteria in my hood? In closing I will say, the Bartolino's Special Salad is one Sensational Salad and will be added to my Yelp list.

Major Disappointment!    Staff 4 Stars, Ambiance 3 Stars, Food 2 Stars get an average of 3 Stars.   The best thing about The Corner Cup is the friendly staff and and the tables that are obviously done by Rustic Grain. Otherwise, it is not the cup for me.   We arrived around 11 AM and was greeted by a cheerful staff member. When I mentioned I really wanted a Bloody Mary with my breakfast, he said I could get one next door at Tamm Avenue Grill. The staff next door was more then happy to fulfill my request, I just had to pay on their register. The Bloody Mary was the best part about my meal.   I ordered the Portobello Benedict. Sounded great on the menu, but the presentation and preparation was lacking. The mushroom was tough, I could not slice it with a fork and it was a hard cut with a knife. They did not brush it with olive oil, season it and roast it. They stuffed it with minimal sautéed spinach, raw. The mushroom was dried out and shriveled around the edges. The poached eggs put on top had the yolks already broken and there was no hollandaise sauce. What is a Benedict without hollandaise or Béarnaise sauce? It's not a Benedict in my book.   Brad ordered the Caveman Omelet without the hamburger, but it still had ham, bacon and turkey sausage. The eggs themselves were overcooked and the meat inside was dried out.  Overcooked eggs and dried out meat made for a chewy omelet. Adding cheese to this dish would help with the texture.   I love Sweet Potatoes, but the side dish of Sweet Potato Hash that came with each dish was served at room temperature. It also lacked any creativity. It basically was just cubed Sweet Potatoes, onions, thyme and way too much Rosemary which gave it a bitter taste.

I love my new shoes. I now have, "Happy Feet".    One of my New Year, New Me Resolutions was to actually use my gym membership. I've been going regularly and doing a minimum of 4-5 miles on the treadmill as my warm up.  Shelby, one of my Shelties has gained weight  and I've also been giving her daily walks around the neighborhood. With these increased activities, I've noticed my feet hurting after each of these activities. I finally realized my inexpensive tennis shoes from the warehouse club were not the right shoes for my fat feet.   As we entered True Runner, we were cheerfully greeted by a sales associate. I quickly told her I needed new shoes for serious walking. She measured my foot and asked me some key questions, before recommending a couple of shoes. The first one she showed me fit fine, but I was not wild about the color scheme. She then showed me a second pair and that color scheme was more to my liking. When I tried that pair on  and walked around I knew they were a winner. The gel in the sole had me walking on air.   When Laura asked me how I liked them I responded, "Much better, then the other." She said, "Really." I asked her why she was surprised. She responded that she wasn't,  she was just amazed how definitive I was in my answer. She said, most people aren't that exact in their answers. My feet felt so good and were so happy, I could not walk out without these shoes.   A great selling point here was the treadmill. They had an actual high end treadmill that they allowed you to use while trying on the shoes. It was like buying a car, you actually got to take them out for a spin ride before buying. This store could be dangerous for me, they had lots of orange items and if you know me well, you know I am a sucker for anything orange.   When I'm ready to kick my program up a notch and become a "True Runner"  they'll be able to help me. They offer a Newbie Running Clinic where I'll be able to get all my questions answered. If you're a runner, I recommend this store.   Big bonus, they have parking to the side of the building so you do not have to worry about that crazy parking lot, that we all dread when going to  Whole Foods or Nordstrom Rack.

Top Notch Service!!!  My garage door opener died, sometimes it would work sometimes it wouldn't. I finally disconnected it and did it the old fashion way, I got out of my car and opened it manually.  I suffered, moaned and groaned for about a month before I broke down and called Overhead Door.   I called early in the morning and was surprised they were able to come out that afternoon.  They gave us an arrival time of 12 - 4PM and they arrived at 12:43PM.  I knew my system was old and when the service man arrived he agreed. We joked that the Smithsonian was waiting for it to be donated.   My garage opener tech was, Anthony and he was very professional. He explained my options; he could replace my control buttons in both car, garage and give me an extra opener or he could totally replace my system. The price difference was less then $200 to get an entire new system with two openers, motion detectors and a lock on the garage pad. I knew the motor was old and most likely wouldn't last much longer so I choose to get the new system. What closed the deal was the fact that he had the new system in his van and I'd have instant gratification. When I want something new, I want it now.   I was amazed how fast Anthony got the new system installed. From his arrival, installing and showing us the new features was under one hour. I love my new Overhead Door garage opener, it glides so quietly and I already like the motion detectors. When the time comes that I need a new garage door I know who I'll call.

I stopped in Acero for a cocktail and nosh before meeting friends a few doors down on Manchester. I sat at the bar, enjoyed an amazing Manhattan and for my nosh I had, Gnocco Fritto~"Meat Donut" Prosciutto di Parma, Sea Salt and Olive Oil. OMG!  I am not a Manhattan type guy, I am more of a Martini man. I do not know what possessed me order the Manhattan, I blame it on the ambiance. Acero just has a whiskey type feel. My drink was smooth, refreshing and of course I had it up like my martini's.   Now let's talk "Meat Donut". A strange donut does not get much better then this one.  A fluffy, flakey puff pastry shell wrapped in Prosciutto, seasoned with the perfect dash of sea salt and drizzled with olive oil. They were the perfect appetizer to accompany my Manhattan.   I saw a serving of their Sea Scallops pass me by at the bar and I know I will be back to enjoy them as well. Of course, I will be enjoying another order of these amazing "meat donuts".

Jack, it is time for your annual review update and I've got some good news and bad news for you. First the good news, you didn't lose any stars this year like you did last year. Your burgers, primarily the Ultimate Cheeseburger and the semi-friendly staff here kept you at a solid 3 Stars. Also, your Chicken Biscuit Sandwich is decent for a fast food joint.   Now for the bad news, some of your new breakfast sandwiches suck. You offered some decent coupons in the Sunday paper so I thought I'd get them a try.  The first one I tried was the Egg White & Turkey Breakfast Sandwich. All I had to do was buy a small coffee and I got the sandwich free. The sandwich was pathetic. I was expecting a turkey sausage, but it was two slices of turkey deli meat.  Deli meat is not breakfast meat, in my world. A nice turkey sausage patty would have made this sandwich so much better. The two slices on a hamburger bun looked rather skimpy. I did enjoy the cup of coffee that I paid for and am so thankful my  EW&TBS was FREE.   The next coupon I used was a BOGO coupon. We all love it when you buy one and get one. I ordered the Sausage and Egg Biscuit x 2. The coupon was promoting new Southern Style Biscuits and I have yet to figure out where in the south that they prepare biscuits the way do you. I tossed the biscuits aside and dumped the sausage, egg and cheese in to a bowl. I then added some hot sauce and had an enjoyable meal. The biscuits were crumbled up, feed to the birds outside of work and who gave them  2 talons up.   Jack, it's good to see you have faith in this location with the current remodeling and expansion of the dining room. It's about time, I do not think this one has been updated since my college days and that was before we had the internet.

A great little coffee shop with no bells and whistles. There are no frills here, just good coffee. Good coffee that is made with the same smoke and mirrors that a magician uses in Las Vegas.  After your first sip you'll be saying, "wow how did he do that".   No frills means, no muffins or pastries of any kind. You come here for some serious "Joe". Why would you want to distract from the true star of the show, with  a cheese danish or Poppy Seed Muffin.   Those who think anal retentiveness is a bad thing have not been to Sump and had a coffee drink made by Scott. His preciseness in making your latte, cappuccino or espresso will have you smirking the next time you pass a Starbucks.

Big fan of the Bug Store on Shaw, so yesterday after having lunch in Kirkwood I checked this location out and was equally impressed. If you have a friend or family member who is big in to gardening, this is the place to shop for their next gift. If you yourself are a big gardener, this place will provide you with items to bedazzle your yard.   The variety of birdhouses, decorative yard figures, patio furniture, wall hangings and yard flags were all unique. I was impressed with the variety of Cardinal stuff they had to show your support for our Boys of Summer.   The statuesque lady working was charming and helpful. She was very skilled at servicing the multiple shoppers all at once and knew her inventory well. When a customer described an item, she knew exactly where it was and quickly hustled to retrieve it.  I was also very fond of her assistant, Buddy. A very distinguished mix breed, who served as greeter and I believe security.   I will be loyal to the Bug Store on Shaw, but I will now make it a point visit this location whenever I am in Kirkwood.

We use to be loyal fans of Panda, but recently strayed to another Chinese Restaurant on Chippewa. Last night we were craving Moo Shu and thought it was time to go back to Panda Pavilion.   In addition to our Moo Shu Pork, we ordered a Chicken St. Paul, Egg Rolls, Crab Rangoon and Plain Fried Rice. I am happy to say, the Moo Shu Pork, Fried Rice were very good. The Crab Rangoon were huge and had plenty of filling. However, the Egg Rolls and St. Paul tasted as if they were fried in old oil.  They were extremely busy, so I highly recommend calling your order in ahead of arriving. This evening I did not call ahead, but they still got my prepared quickly.

First off, let me say that I can not believe there have only been 5 reviews written about Kirkwood Ice & Fuel. Hopefully once, my review is posted here on Yelp we'll see an increase, because they offered up some fairly amazing wings and burgers.   We had been running from nursery to nursery selecting and picking up things for our major landscaping project when we realized, it was lunch time. To be honest, it was past lunch it was 2:30PM and we be starved. I keep an Entertainment Coupon book in my car and remembered there was a coupon for KI&F, so we headed exited 44 and went for lunch.   KI&F is a typical sports type bar, 7 TVs 6 turned to a variety of different sporting events and one on Animal Planet. TVs were positioned well, making for easy viewing from any table. My only complaint, they did not have subtitles on . I wanted to know what the commentators were saying.   Now let us talk about the food. We started our late lunch with Raspberry Chipotle Chicken Wings. The wings were good sized as Dave F., mentioned and are juicy. The RC sauce was heavier then I normally like, making them messy and a need for extra napkins. However, the rich flavor made up for needing to wipe your mouth and fingers in between wings. They were a very pleasant change from a traditional hot wing. Next to The Post wings, these may be my new favorite.   Next we had cheeseburgers that were char grilled to perfection. I do medium and Brad does Medium Rare and you can honestly see the difference when served. Pepper was our cheese of choice and we added all the other great toppings; white onion, lettuce, pickle and tomato. As their lettuce, they offer green leaf, not iceberg like so many other sports bar do. Burgers, were thick, juicy and seasoned just right.  For those of you who love O'Connel's, this is a better burger. We think it may be the best in the city.   I choose fries as my side and Brad got onion rings for an extra $1. We always do that, then share we we can experience more.  Their fries were crinkle cut, which is my second favorite fry next to steak. They hold ketchup so much better then a regular fry.  Their onion rings, were just okay. I enjoyed them, but not anything to write home about.   The service was excellent, our waitress was friendly and attentive to our table.  I have three more coupons and I will be back to use them all before they expire.

Why anyone would go to Arby's when you have a Lion's Choice a few doors door the street is beyond me. When you compare the two, there truly is no comparison. Lion's Choice wins hands down every time. LC's is more tender, is served rare and has better seasoning.   Neither of us wanted to cook last night, so the Entertainment.com Coupon Book came to the rescue. Lion's Choice had a BOGO Coupon which made our dinner easy. We enjoyed regular roast beef sandwiches , one with soft cheddar and the other with Swiss. In addition to the sandwiches we enjoyed small orders of fries. I love that their thin fries have the skins on the potatoes. It makes them stand out from all the other fast food fries. Another big bonus is that LC serves Dr. Pepper, both regular and diet.   Since I was saving on the sandwiches, I splurged and treated us to dessert. I ordered a chocolate milk shake and a couple white chocolate macadamia nut cookies. When I got home, I put the shake in the freezer to make it more like ice cream when we were ready for out sweet treat. It was the perfect ending for a perfect roast beef dinner.

I am not a regular mall shopper, so when I arrived at the Galleria to buy chocolates for my hairstylist I was surprised Bisssingers had left the building. I had a hair appointment across the street, so I needed something to go with the bottle of wine as her holiday gift. I quickly regrouped and headed over to Godiva and they saved the day.   The manager was very helpful in showing me different gift boxes that were on sale and another table that had mix and match items that would be great stocking stuffers. What made her customer service extra special is that she came out from behind that huge counter displaying all the sinful delights and joined us in the sales area. She was very personable and persuasive.   I left with not only a gift for my hair stylist, but a few extra gifts to have on hand just in case. I also signed up for their rewards program. By being a member I get a free non liquor truffle every month for just stopping by, no purchase necessary. That may be motive enough to get me into the mall more often.

I'm not a fan of Ramen, so when Vista use to be called Vista Ramen, I never came. Big mistake, but I am so glad I finally made it here.   The space is small, but the food and cocktails are big on flavor. The service was even pretty impressive. Our bartender and server, both were big on friendly and attentive personalities.   We had a group of 7 and we all agreed the star of the evening was the, Korean Fried Chicken. These sliders served on a Hawaiian roll, were the tastiest little chicken sliders I have ever had. They are served 2 for $10 and a worth every penny. Order these with a side of fries and you've got a meal.   The night we were dining they had an appetizer special of Pork Rinds.  They were unique with their dipping sauce, but I'd order the sliders again, before these. If you're doing low-carb - this would be an appetizer for you.   For my entree I went with a Double Cheeseburger. I will admit, I was a little skeptical, but other pictures on Yelp sold me. When it arrived, I was blown away. It was done diner style and was better then some of my favorites in STL. I'll definitely will be coming back for this beauty.   My cocktail of the evening was also a beauty. It was called, Measure Up and was a slight variation of a Manhattan. It went down smooth.   I'll be back? - Those sliders and cheeseburger are calling me, now.   When: July 21, 2018 Why: Dinner with fellow Yelpers.

It's been almost a year and time for an update. I'm glad to say, Grapeseed is still 5 Stars for me. If I had to rate my favorite restaurants, they'd definitely be in the Top 10.   My recent visit was on a Friday night. Before my arrival, I'd been searching Yelp for Fish & Chips. After all, it is Lent. I then remembered, Ian Froeb said his, "must order" for Grapeseed on his STL 100 for 2017 was their; Texas Gulf Shrimp and Cheddar Grits. Okay, I can do shrimp & grits for dinner. However, when I checked the menu online, I saw that they had a Fish & Chips - Small Plate on the menu for March. I moved at the speed of, Flash and was there in on time flat.   I didn't want to rush into the F&C's, so I enjoyed a Manhattan and a House Smoked Shrimp Cake, first. My Manhattan was smooth and helped me relax after a tough day at work. The Shrimp Cake, was an amazing and tasty twist of the traditional crab cake. I hope this stays on the menu, beyond the Lent season. It was served with a Spicy Remoulade, that was so good, I wanted to lick the plate.   The Fish & Chips was described as; Pub Style Battered Cod. I've not experienced any other fish like this at a pub. This was far superior. The batter/crust was thinner & crispier then others and the cod inside was moist and flakey. This may be only week four of Lent, but this was the best so far. The menu stated it came with; shoestring fries. I was disappointed it wasn't going to be their typical fries, but went with the flow. To my excitement, when my plate arrived, it was their typical fries that are my favorite in STL. I was a happy man. The accompanying cole slaw, is the type of slaw I'd like to see served with my ribs or a good pork steak. BBQ joints - come check out this slaw.   The service here is always friendly and attentive. I feel relaxed and welcomed every time I dine.   Would I come back? I always do.   When: March 24, 2017 Why: Fish & Chips - Lent
I live in the city, and when I go to a movie this is my choice when I want a big screen. The staff is friendly, it is clean and who doesn't like stadium seating.

I am redecorating my living room and am looking for three club type chairs to create a cozy conversation area. We were on the way to Costco for our bimonthly pilgrimage and thought, why not pop into La-Z-Boy and see if they have what I/we are looking for.   Wow, was I impressed. La-Z-Boy has changed over the years, I remember the days when all they sold were tacky recliners. Now they offer a large variety of upholstered and leather chairs, sofas, love-seats and sectionals. I'll even be able to get my Lift Chair at La-Z-Boy when the time comes.   We were greeted by a perky saleslady who listened to our needs and guided us to a couple chairs that she thought might work. While strolling to the chairs she recommended, we found one that we "really" liked. We even liked it the way it was shown on the floor and wouldn't have to pay the up-charge for a custom order.  The young lady checked and they had three in stock at their warehouse. Better yet, we qualified for a 25% discount due to the $ amount we were spending. I was using my smart phone calculator and getting excited, this was all within budget. Then she dropped the bomb and I in turn dropped mine. She informed us delivery was going to be $50 per chair for a total of $150. I did not blink once, I looked at her and said, "that just lost you this sale".  She had no comeback.   Adding the $150 on for delivery reduced my sale price by 25%. Do they not realize how the economy is today? If you have to charge for delivery, give a smaller discount on the sale and tell me the delivery is "Free". I'll be clueless that the delivery is a hidden fee, but I'll be happy that I got something "FREE".  When I'm giving you $2,000 for 3 chairs, I want my delivery free.

I've got to stop assuming these new burger joints are order at counter. I kept avoiding coming to 5 Star Burgers until I read the reviews closer and discovered they had table service. I like table service, so I was thrilled to have a new burger place to explore. We immediately were greeted by a cheerful hostess who seated us near the front windows. I am really starting to enjoy tables next to a window, natural light does wonders for the presentation of food.   A bus boy or server assistant to be politically correct, was quick to bring small glasses of ice water and a wine bottle filled with backup H2O. When our server Molly approached the table, we already knew we wanted an order of Fried Pickles as an appetizer. My drink of choice was the Salted Caramel Shake and the BF "just" had ice tea.  Damn, I was hoping to try two flavors of shakes.   When our drinks arrived, we ordered our burgers and a Mixed Basket of Fries. I enjoyed a Natural Angus with Pepper Jack Cheese with the works, (lettuce, tomato, onion and pickle). A pure delight, it was as good as one fresh off the backyard grill. The BF had the absolute best burger either of us have enjoyed in a long time, Dad's Green Chile Cheeseburger. Oh my, Crispy New Mexico Hatch Chilies on top of Angus beef patty, with Pepper Jack Cheese and  Green Chile Mayonnaise. As a bonus, we added bacon. As every Yelper knows, everything is better with bacon. Both burgers were nestled between a Butter Toasted Brioche Bun. Culver's, you should be scared, these burgers put your butter burgers to shame.   The Fried Pickles were crinkle cut dill pickles served with Tzatiki Sauce. The pickles were true dill pickles in flavor with a crisp outer shell. The Tzatiki Sauce was a perfect accent to these fried treats. Our Mixed Basket of Sweet Potato Fries and Regular Fries were served in a cute deep fry basket.  Each were served with Little Cups of Ketchup and Maple Cream. The Sweet Potato Fries stood alone on flavor. Also, the same sauce for the pickles were a better accent then the Maple Cream. In my humble opinion, the Maple Cream doesn't know what it wants to be, it was rather bland for both of us. The fresh Natural Cut Idaho Russet Potatoes, were seasoned with the right amount of salt.   I've saved the best for last, the Salted Caramel Shake was perfect. I had them hold the whipping cream, but still had the toasted marshmallow and cherry on top. The sweetness of the ice cream from the infamous Serendipity in Webster Groves and the saltiness of the caramel created a perfect balance. It was so well balanced, that I was able to sip it and enjoy it through my entire meal.   I'm coming back for sure. I've got a lamb burger and a bison burger to experience.

A Gastrobar is just what Lindenwood Park, needed. A relaxing place where you can grab a cocktail or cold beer. They've got plenty of room at the bar, dining room, game room and back patio to accommodate a group of friends.   My first meal here was their flat grilled burger. It was a double patty with cheese and the edges of the burger had those crisp edges known to a diner burger. The Garlic Parmesan Fries were crisp and the special sauce was perfect for dipping. As an appetizer, I munched on a warm soft pretzel with beer cheese sauce.   The ambiance is definitely sports bar, man cave type of vibe, but it is relaxing and works well.  Their staff is friendly and are quickly learning the neighborhood folks. They're wooing them over to be regulars.   It's within walking distance of my home and I'm looking forward to being a regular. Can't wait to try the Meatloaf and Steak & Frites. The folks next to me had them and gave them thumbs up. Would have gotten pictures, but I thought it might have been odd to ask a stranger if I could photo their food - LOL.   Will I return? - It's in my hood & I support my hood. Hell, yes.   When: March 11 & 12, 2017 Why: Cocktails (11) Dinner (12)

Great place to recycle your florescent bulbs. I took in  several 4 ft bulbs and they charged me .48¢ each as a service fee. I will gladly pay that minimal fee to save our environment.   I also did not walk out empty handed, I was in need of a couple flashlights for when the power goes out and found some in my favorite color orange. If it is orange and something I can use, I will normally buy it. I need a support group for those attached to the color orange.   Great customer service, they make shopping for bulbs and batteries and enjoyable experience.

Yummy, Yummy, I have comfort in my tummy.  Today's' lunch was a true southern experience.  I am so thankful that the owner opened Mama Josephine's to honor her mother and to have her recipes bring pleasure to others.   Understand that this place is about home cooked meals, this not a place where food is made in advance and waiting for your order to come across the computer. The ambiance is simple, tables and chairs with a portrait of Mama Josephine herself hanging on the wall. Keep in mind you are not there to enjoy plush surroundings, you are there to experience some down home southern cuisine.   We started out with a Garden Salads, I experienced their house made Honey Mustard dressing which is by far the best Honey Mustard Dressing I have ever experienced. I also enjoyed the fact that the salad had no iceberg lettuce. I hate iceberg and always appreciate it when a restaurant excludes it from their salad mix.   Our lunch entrees were Chicken Fried Steak, Mashed Potatoes with White Gravy and Fried Southern Okra and Meat Loaf, Mashed Potatoes with Brown Gravy and Fried Corn. The Meat Loaf was true home-style meatloaf rich in flavor and juicy. The slice was a hearty piece and the tomato/ketchup topping was just like Mama's. Their Mashed Potatoes were smooth with a few lumps, which gives you proof that they truly are made from scratch. Then there was Fried Corn with pieces of diced onion that I had to hold the bowl in hand while I scooped it quickly to my eager mouth.   The Chicken Fried Steak was the biggest I have ever seen. The breading was seasoned well, making me want to come back and experience their "real" fried chicken.  If this breading/coating is what they use on their fried chicken, it has to be awesome.   Another reviewer poo-pooed the Fried Okra saying that it came from a bag. To that all I can say is, "Hell No". When we ordered the fried Okra the chef came out and asked if we wanted it true "southern style" or what is typically served in St Louis. I asked for clarification, not knowing there was any other way but Southern Style. St. Louis style has a heavier coating on the okra and Southern Style is just a light dusting of seasoning and corn meal. We opted for Southern Style, which we both grew up with. When it arrived at the the table, it was so appealing I totally forgot to photograph, because we began eating it so quickly.   Desserts were Pecan Pie and Banana Pudding that were as good as my Auntie Ruth's and Grandma Roberts and that means they were damn good.   As Stephanie S. commented, we loved the fact that the owner came to each table making sure we were pleased with our meal. She is so charming, that sweet southern accent just pulls you into her warm southern hospitality. We will be back.

Yes, I am a fan of Treats Unleashed. You want to know why? Because, no matter what store I shop, I know I am going to get high quality freshly made in house treats for my fur-baby. In addition to the treats, I will receive top notch personalized service. The associates are always friendly, knowledgeable and make me feel like my dog is the best in the world.   TU is also a great place to buy quality dog food. This is when the staff really shine. They are so knowledgeable in the nutritional facts about the various brands. My baby eats totally grain free dry food and he's healthy as can be.   If you're in need of accessories for your four legged friend, you can find beds, toys and colorful collars and leashes.   If you love your K-9, you need to shop here. They're the best.

Jack, you know how to make a good cheeseburger.  I love the Ultimate Cheeseburger, in my opinion it is most likely the best fast food cheeseburger available. When it comes to my cheeseburgers I am a purist. I do not want anything else on the burger distracting me from the main attraction, "cheese". You can keep your fresh lettuce, tomato and rings of onion to yourself, I don't need them I have cheese.   The Ultimate is made for people like me. It is two beef patties, American, Swiss and Cheddar Cheese with a mayo-onion sauce, mustard and ketchup on a sesame seed bun. What more do you need? That is a perfect cheeseburger.   When I visit JITB, all I get is my Ultimate and a coke. I guess this is my Cheeseburger Cheeseburger.   Smile and say "Cheese".

As I sat down in front of my computer to create a new Yelp List for Fried Pickles, I realized I have not updated my "The Mack" review to highlight their Fried Pickles.  How could this be, one of the first places I experienced the decadent appetizer and I did not mention in a review. Proof that it is important to keep your Yelp reviews up to date with your experiences.   The Fried Pickles at The Mack are crinkle cut dill chips covered in a thick crisp batter and served with a Southwest type Ranch dipping sauce. The SW Ranch gave an  extra kick, to an already tasty pickle. As Jennifer T. suggested, keep some of the dipping sauce for your fries as well.   The Mack already is on my list for burgers and chicken wings and now it is on my new Fried Pickles list.

Do you want to enjoy Fish Fry Friday during Lent, but want to avoid those insane long lines and loud crowds at the local church? If so, head on over to SqWires Annex and chow down on a better quality of food and in a more relaxing atmosphere.   The food is served buffet style, which typically I am not a fan of, but it works for a Fish Fry Friday. It was nice to see that they also offered a baked fish for those, who do not eat "fried". I admit, I'm kinda crazy, because the only time I really eat, fried fish is during Lent. This evening, I chose the beer battered fish and I was given two large pieces. As my side, I choose; Hush Puppies and Mac-n-Cheese.   For me, a fish fry is not complete without those cornmeal balls being fried to a crisp. Their Mac-n-Cheese was creamy and I liked the use of Penne noodles. None of the food was overly salt, which you'll discover at some of the church dinners. However, I love pepper and needed to add several shakes to the Mac-n-Cheese. The dinner also included a dessert, I choose a Chocolate Chip Cookie over the variety of pies and cake.   They also had a full service bar available. I enjoyed a cold local craft beer, as i sat at one of the tables for two. The annex was sit up with a variety of tables, so it was easy to accommodate groups of any size.  Another nice and relaxing aspect of this event was the live music. It was simply a man singing with his guitar. It reminded me of the old days, when you'd go to a coffeehouse and hear folk singers perform.   Would I return? - I recommend it. This year, I have too many more to experience.   When: March 10, 2017 Why: Friday Fish Fry

I cannot being to tell you how excited I was to find out Casa del Mar was related to Canyon Cafe out at Plaza Frontenac. Canyon Cafe is one of my favorite places to enjoy Tex-Mex and a Margarita. When I worked in Plaza Frontenac, CC was my go to for lunch and Happy Hour after work. Let me tell you, Casa del Mar is the redheaded step-child to Canyon Cafe. They are no way near the level of quality in food or service as my beloved Canyon Cafe.   I should of known that I was going to be let down when I entered the restaurant around 2 PM and there was only 1 other diner. I'll start off with the positives points first. There are only two and neither of them had anything to do with the food or beverage. While sitting at the bar, I sneezed and the bartender said, "Bless, you." That is positive point 1 and the second positive point was giving me an orange pen (orange is my favorite color) to sign my charge slip when I was ready to leave.   I ordered a top shelf Margarita and 3 Street Tacos. I wasn't offered any chips and salsa, so I do not know if they are complimentary or if you pay a small fee. If I had to pay, I would have done so and I would have enjoyed munching on them while I drank my Margarita and waited and waited for my tacos. Yes, I meant to write waited twice. However, I guess the conversation at the other end of the bar with other employees was more important.   My tacos arrived and one was incorrect. I ate it any way, because trying to get the attention of the bartender and having to wait again, was something I just did not want to deal with. The tacos I ordered were; Fried Fish, Crispy Chicken and Spicy Beef.   Fried Fish: Instead of Fried, I got Blackened. The Blackened Fish I actually liked, but the condiments it was served with distracted from the flavorful fish.   Spicy Beef: Mushy pulled beef and not spicy at all.   Crispy Chicken: Reminded me of Orange Chicken at Panda Express in a soft shell taco.   As I shopped the Galleria after dining, I asked the sales associates what they thought. I did not get one positive comment. One point that they all made, is one I noticed as I looked at their website. Their hours are not accommodating to shoppers or employees getting off work. They close at the same time as the stores. Why not stay open longer so employees can relax with a drink or snack and a shopper can recharge before going home.   Been here and I will not return.   When: September 15, 2015 Why: Lunch while shopping

What a pleasant surprise. I have lived in Saint Louis for 35 years and have never been to a Chocolate Chocolate Chocolate store. I've been to Ted Drew's countless times and have picked up carry out at the Chinese restaurant next door, but never step foot inside CCCC. Today I was at Chippewa Eye Centre and when I left, I made a point to walk over and experience what I have been missing all these years.   I say this with chocolate love, this place is a poor mans Godiva, Kakao or Bissinger's. I couldn't believe the price I paid for 6 truffles that tasted as if I should have been paying more. The three flavors I experienced were; Georgia Peach, Red Velvet Cake and Pumpkin. Georgia Peach lived up to its name, tasting like a juicy peach. The Red Velvet Cake also tasted like its' name sake, but was the least flavorful of the three. With autumn just around the corner, I am going to remember these Pumpkins Truffles. They were very flavorful, bursting with rich pumpkin flavor.   I also bought one of my favorite treats to take to a movie, Malted Milk Balls. These were some top notch MMB's. I enjoy popping one in my mouth and letting it melt. Then the next one I will crunch and then continue alternating back and forth until they are gone or the movie is over.   I got a good giggle at all the different molds they had for their milk chocolate. Who wouldn't love a Milk Chocolate Fur Coat. They even had some nude male and females that could be a great bachelor or bachelorette gift.

Wow, this store blew my socks off! I never knew that a store who specializes in batteries could be so awesome.   I was out in Creve Coeur picking up dog food, for my fur-babies and wanted to stop by Froyou. As I parked my CRV, I noticed there was a Batteries Plus right next door. I put my craving of red velvet cake yogurt on hold and popped in for a visit. After-all, I needed AA batteries for my new RC helicopter.  When I entered, I was cheerfully greeted by a employee who quickly asked if I was looking for batteries or light bulbs. I was surprised to hear that they sell light bulbs, too. I told him that I needed double AA's and I grabbed a package I was standing in front of. He was quick to point out a larger package that on sale for only a $1 more. He helped me get more bang for my buck.   As he was ringing me out, he asked if this was my first time in a Batteries Plus store and when I said yes, he proceeded to tell me all the benefits of shopping with BP.  I had no idea, they sell all different types of batteries, from the tiny one I put in my pedometer all the way up to a car battery. They also have all types of light bulbs. What also impressed me, is that they recycle batteries and light bulbs. They need to charge a minimal fee for some, but at least I now have a place to take my bulbs and batteries - Yeah!  When I need batteries and bulbs, I now know where I'll be going. Batteries Plus, your a specialty store that is truly special and I like that.

I may be dating myself with this, but what the hell.   How many of you remember the song, "McDonald's is my kind of place, (clap, clap) It's such a happy place" Will let me tell, you the reason they stopped using that song is because of the customer service at this location. Not only are the cashiers and staff rude, but so are the managers. I guess they lead by example.   What makes this sad is the fact that for a McDonald's the food is better then most. I live in between two McDonald's both on Hampton and this one has the better Egg McMuffins and Sausage Biscuits when we have the morning craving.  I have also, stopped by when the Cheeseburger craving hits too.  I hate to admit it, I put up with the poor attitude, to get the better food.   I never use their drive-thru, it is to slow. I have always found it faster if I park and go inside. When I am exiting with my food, most of the cars in line have made little or no progress at all.   The ambiance is more upscale then those with attached Playlands, and as previously stated the food is better then other McDonald's. If they could improve the attitude of the entire staff, believe it or not this would be a 4 star McDonald's.

Where do I begin to tell the story of how great a lunch can be? Well, for us it begun with an order of Chips and Salsa. They are not complimentary here, but you do get what you pay for ($3) and that is quality chips which are fresh and lightly salted. The chips come with two house made salsas. My favorite had a smokey flavor and was so "hot", I am fairly certain that Alicia Keys wrote "Girl on Fire"  after eating some. Seriously, it was the best salsa I have had at any Mexican restaurant.   We then had an order of Carne Asada Fries, that stole my heart. I will never be able to eat or even look at an order of typical nachos again. They filled a plate with Chile crusted potato fries and then topped them with; melted Chihuahua, grilled flank steak, guacamole, Mexican crema and pico de gallo. Diffidently made to be shared or as a meal for one.   The SO ordered 4 tacos, so I got a Burrito so we could get a fuller fell of their menu. I choose, The Cowboy. It was so massive I could hardly get a hand or my mouth around it. I had to enjoy it with a knife and fork. I didn't realize I had to request roasted tomato sauce and melted cheese which would have been an extra $1. However, I enjoyed mine without the toppings. The house made corn tortillas stuffed with beef brisket, black beans, cilantro rice, roasted corn, Chihuahua and arbol salsa was perfect just the way it was served. I only ate half and enjoyed the left over portion for a work lunch the next day.  As stated earlier, the SO experienced four of their amazing tacos. He choose; Beef Brisket Birria, Baja Fish, Roasted Duck and Cochinita Pibil. I was so content with my Cowboy, I only sampled the Baja Fish and I will be ordering a pair of them on my next visit. I liked the fact that you can have either fried or grilled fish in your taco. He claims the beef brisket and roasted duck were mind blowing, so I'll take him at his word.   We couldn't leave without trying the Churros and they were the perfect ending to our first lunch at MTJ. Oh, I forgot to mention the House Margaritas served up in a logo branded glass. They were so tasty, I had to have two at lunch time, It was okay, it was my day off. The servers were cheerfully fun and truly knew their menu. We can not wait to go back for more.

Love this Lion's Choice, the Roast Beef is always tender and full of flavor. The beef always has a little pink to it, so you know it hasn't been over cooked like some other fast Roast Beef restaurants.  I agree with Chrissie, ask for extra seasoning on your sandwich. Another flavor booster I recommend is mixing Lion Choices BBQ Sauce with the ketchup for dipping your french fries.

Before writing this update, I removed John Donut Co from my No-No List. It has been over two years since my first John Donut and I thought it was time to revisit. My last review was based on a box of donuts brought in by a coworker, so I missed out on the ambiance and customer service that is offered at JDC.  When experiencing a donut shop, I use my three classic donuts as a base for judging. They are the traditional Glazed Donut, Apple Fritter and the Chocolate Long John, or Chocolate Bar depending on which name you grew up calling it. The Apple Fritter was good, but the best in my humble opinion Donut Drive-In still is the best. I grew up calling it a Chocolate Long John and thought this was above average, it goes well with an ice cold glass of milk. Their Glazed Donut, is a true classic. In my earlier review I stated Homer Simpson wouldn't eat them, I now stand corrected.   Not stereotyping, but I am surprised I did not see any policeman at JDC. It's a great location in Soulard. It is off the beaten path in the industrial area of Soulard, but still easy and safe to get in and out of on a busy day. It's not in my hood, but when in the area and craving a donut I'll be apt to return. If you decide to go remember as most donut joints, it is cash only.

I ATE THE BONES!   I ATE THE BONES!!!!!  Isn't it amazing the power of marketing and stupid television commercials can get us to do things we'd normally not do.  It is rare that I eat KFC. I may enjoy it every other Blue Moon and since the 23rd was going to be a Full Moon, I thought that was close enough for me to enjoy some Original Recipe.   I ordered the two piece Snack Box and it actually was not bad. It was boneless, skinless and had the Original Recipe just like the TV ads said. I was curious as to how the pieces were going to look and they  basically are drastically deformed Chicken Tenders.  Almost like a science project gone bad.   As a side I choose Mash Potatoes with Gravy, you can never go wrong with smashed taters. KFC offers the big Steak Fries, which are my fry of choice, but they do not do them right. I will pass on them every time. The biscuit was Plain Jane and would embarrass any true Southern Woman.   Staff and service here is typical fast food. Don't expect much and you'll get what you are expecting. A decent fast meal at a reasonable price.

Whenever I'm shopping at Carniceria Latino Americana, I fantasize that I'm in a little grocery store in Cuernavaca. I roam up and down the aisles visiting every nook and cranny.  Many of the labels test my high school Spanish to the limits. However, I usually can figure it out by the labels. They're pretty much the same, just a different language.   The staff is friendly and helpful. There are no language barriers here, just good customer service. So when preparing your own versions of Mexican Cuisine at home I highly recommend shopping here for your supplies.   The only downside to shopping here is when you exit.  You'll  realize you are still in Saint Louis and have only been shopping on Cherokee street.

Zippy Burger is a solid 3 Stars burger joint. I'm glad I experienced it and I am able to remove it from my list of bookmarked businesses. However, it is not a place a would or will be rushing back to enjoy.   The Pros:  Fresh & Soft Bun Burger thin, simular to a Steak & Shake burger and the toppings were fresh and plentiful Secret Sauce was good, but let's be serious, how secret is it?  Small intimate space.   The Cons:  Serve Pepsi products Only have ketchup packets. Packets are for to go orders, get a pump with little paper cups for those eating in your dining room.  Fries were crisp, but flavorless. No seasoning.  Poorest Customer Service - You only have 6 or 8 tables in your restaurant, how about bringing an order to the person instead of yelling - "Hey, here's your order." I was the only person in the restaurant and it was lunch time. Five Guys is larger and they bring you your order. Learn from the big guys.  If you want a beer with your burger, not alcohol is served here.   Burgers are good, if you get them I'd get them to go and enjoy them at a park, in your car or at home.   When:March 15, 2016 Why: Lunch & Check off my Bookmarked List

Another good experience at Filomena's.  What impresses me most about this family business, it they are consistent in their customer service and food quality. Every time I have dined here, I have been totally satisfied with my meal.   My most recent visit was our International Supper Club meeting of 14 hungry Yelpers.  I was excited when I saw they had added a Tutto Mare with Penne Pasta to their menu. It was a rich tomato, butter sauce with shrimp, scallops and mushrooms. The portion was large enough for me to take half of it home for dinner the next night.   I also enjoyed a small house salad which is Romaine lettuce with mozzarella and provolone cheeses, artichoke hearts, red onion and tomato served with their house balsamic vinaigrette. Dressing is damn good.   14 of us ordered separately and they still managed to time all of our food to come out in a timely fashion. Specializing in carryout, they were very cordial and accommodating to our large group of diners. When ever I'm  in Glendale around mealtime, I'll always think of Filomena's.

Congratulations Copper Pig, you're a lucky pig. Why, are you lucky? I'm removing you from my Terrible Two's List. I gave you 7 months to get your act together and re-visited your restaurant and saw improvement, so I'm giving you an additional Yelp Star.   As I studied the menu, I enjoyed a El Chapo. El Chapo is a vodka cocktail served up. Being a true vodka man and one who loves Green Chiles, this cocktail called out to me. It is made with St. George Green Chile Voka, Triple Sec, a splash of sour and served with a salted rim. It's a very unique cocktail, I could smell the aroma of green chiles as it was placed on the table in front of me. It was refreshing, but one is enough. It's not one of those cocktails that you can slam down more then one. Order one, experience and enjoy it at least once, but then move on to your next favorite drink.   I started my re-visit with one of their most popular "Starters", Standard "Lollipop" Wings. It's a very creative and unique way to serve the little drummies of the chicken wing. They somehow cut and push all the meat up on the drum, so it looks like a "lollipop". They are very crispy and served drizzled a Vietnamese fish sauce caramel. Flavor was just okay, in hindsight I should have gone with the daily special wings that was a Sweet Chili sauce. As stated, the "lollipop" style is unique, but give me a traditional chicken wing.   My main course was a Chicken Biscuit. I had reread the menu on the website before arriving (which needs to be updated) and then as I read the menu in the restaurant, I was not even considering the Chicken Biscuit. Then the lady at the next table had it served to her and my mind was made up, I had to have it.  I couldn't say not to a fried chicken thigh, topped with bacon, cheese and bbq sauce on a flakey biscuit. It basically is the heart attack I've been looking for...LOL. It was served with House Cut Fries and a Little Cup of Ketchup. (I really like little cups, I dislike bottles of ketchup at bars). The breading was overwhelming and made the thigh look bigger then it actually was. The BBQ sauce had a sweet twang that complimented the sandwich.   I'll definitely say the food was an improvement since my last visit. However, it is still average bar food at best, it really isn't anything that I'd recommend or rush back to have. If a friend wanted to go, I visit again, being a team diner. The service is friendly, but they have a tendency to rush you out of there. I do commend them on the variety of clientele. While I was dining, it was a mixture of young families, senior couples and male couples. Kudos to The Copper Pig for being a great place for everyone.

The Mack is truly a hidden jewel in South Hampton neighborhood. I would have never discovered the diamond in the ruff if it were not for Mark S. telling me about it in a Hamburger talk thread here on Yelp. Thanks Mark, for expanding my burger world.   We went for lunch yesterday and had a totally enjoyable meal. When having a burger for some silly reason, I always need to start out with an order of chicken wings. I always get a giggle when a menu says, "Our Famous Chicken Wings". The Mack, lives up to that boast. Their wings are crispy on the outside and moist on the inside. They have just the perfect amount of spice and kick.  After the wings,  I had a Half Pound Burger with Pepper Jack Cheese and the SO enjoyed The Southside Burger. Both were charbroiled to perfection and I love it when a burger is hand pressed. There is something, about a burger that isn't perfectly shaped that seems to add flavor.   My burger was topped with rings of white onion, lettuce and a slice of tomato that made it perfect. It was as if I were enjoying a juicy burger at a backyard cook out.  The Southside Burger was topped with Cheddar Cheese, Crispy Onion Rings and BBQ Sauce. Both burgers were huge in size, so huge that we had to take some of ours home. When they brought us our box to take our leftovers, I was pleased to see that their container was Eco-Frinendly.   They offer two kinds of fries to compliment your burger; "traditional" and "waffle".  The traditional were slender, crispy and had a seasoning similar to Lawry's. which is A+ to me. The waffle fries were huge and I loved how they held the ketchup when dipping.   Their server did a great job of waiting on the tables and serving the bar, she is trained well. By that, I mean she is trained like Pavlov's dog. When food is ready, the kitchen pushes a buzzer that you can hear behind the bar and off she goes to retrieve it. I found it funny and when I shared my laugh with her, she laughed too. She commented that she never thought of that, but it was so true.   I am a new fan of The Mack and it is being added to 3 of my lists; Burgers, Wings and Eco-Friendly.

I am not vegan. I am not vegetarian. However, I do love the slices at Pizza Head.   I am a big fan of pizza and when I find a restaurant that serves pizza by the slice, I'm there to check it out. Even if it is one that specializes is vegan and vegetarian pizza. I can not be trusted with an entire pizza pie, I'll eat the whole thing, so I prefer to order just a slice or two to satisfy my craving.   My late lunch was two slices; White Slice with Spinach and Artichoke and a traditional Pepperoni. The Spinach & Artichoke was amazingly delicious. The young lady working the counter, informed me about the Garlic Powder and how tasty it is and she was so right. I sprinkled it on the WSSA for an extra kick. Even with the pepperoni being plant friendly, I couldn't really tell the difference. A little sprinkle of red pepper flakes, gave it a kick too.   The customer service was casual and friendly. It was fun sharing pictures of our dogs. The ambiance is dark, edgy, inviting and very relaxing.   Will I return? - So many slices to try.   When: July 20, 2019 Why: On South Grand at lunchtime.

What was I thinking? Seriously, did I think I was going to get some good fried chicken here. The problem was I didn't pack a lunch,  I was not in a burger mood and nothing else was close to work. So it was KFC or starve to death and I am not ready to die. I have too many more Yelp reviews to write.   My lunch wasn't that bad, but it wasn't that good either. KFC has just been going downhill over the years and there are just so many other places that do a better job.  I had a Tenders combo, which included three strips (only available extra crispy), a side dish and beverage. My original side was their huge fries, but they were out at 12:30PM. Again I have to ask, Seriously? It is lunch time on a work day and you are already out of a popular side. They told me it would be 5 minuets, before they had fresh ones. I am not a patient man, I selected mashed potatoes so I could get out of there and back to work.   I did notice this was a KFC that had the lunch buffet where you pay a flat fee and can eat like you are at a Hometown Buffet, but the only main entree is "chicken". While getting my diet Pepsi, it balances out the effects of eating "fried food", I noticed the sides available on the buffet.  The sides did not impress me, most looked like they were heated up straight from a can. What happened to making things from scratch?  Back at work, I ate my lunch. My tenders were a nice size and crispy, but lacked flavor. The potatoes were another story within themselves. Who in the hell puts "brown" gravy on potatoes served with fried chicken? You'd never see that on the farm. I also hope they know they are not fooling anyone with those instant potatoes. You could not get more instant then these. Once again I have to say, "no flavor".   KFC, there are too many privately owned chicken joints that are putting out a better meal then you. What saved you from getting a lower score then 3 was; friendly staff, clean dining area and from what I could see of the kitchen it was spotless as well.   I'd love to see you get back to the KFC I remember as a child when we'd get a bucket after church and go over the river and through the woods to visit grandma.

We had a coupon and thought we'd try a new Chinese takeout. It was lunch time so we ordered two lunch specials, and were pleased with both. The egg roll was excellent, and the Crab Rangoon's were some of the best carry-out I've experienced. The pork fried rice as a side was also very good. Out of the two entrees we ordered, the Orange Chicken was the best.  For lunch portions I thought they were very large.  Very close to house so it is easy to pick-up, but delivery would be nice.

What a bummer. I found out this morning that the breakfast muffin sandwich that I've fallen in love with, was a limited time offer and is no longer available. The Bacon and Gouda Cheese Muffin Sandwich was the bomb. It was like getting a breakfast sandwich at an upscale coffee shop. What was funny, is the fact the slide show on the screen next to the menu, still featured it and showed how it was made. The staff was very apologetic, and pointed the finger at corporate. Perhaps if I had reviewed the sandwich earlier, sales would have increased and it could now be a staple on the BK Menu.   Since I couldn't have my Gouda, I enjoyed a Sausage and Egg Muffin with American Cheese. Wasn't as upscale, but it still is better then the Muffin Sandwiches the clown makes. I also enjoyed, a refreshing Caramel Iced Coffee that was not bad, considering the fact that it was created in a fast food operation.   A side note from a previous visit:  I love donut holes and they are now available here at Burger King. You'll receive 5 holes, in a box. Crazy me, don't know what I was expecting when I ordered them. They are microwaved right before your eyes, so don't set your standards to high. In fact, do not order them at all.   Over all, I still like this BK located close to work better then the Golden Arches. I pass the clown and over shoot work to visit this King when urge arises.

If someone did not tell you where Blue Sky Tower Grill was located, you'd never find it. It is so off the beaten path of Brentwood, that you'd drive by and not even notice that it excised.  It sets across from the Galleria in the main level of that tall dark skyscraper known as the University Club Tower.  I had just gotten my haircut at Mitchell James and my stylist was telling us about BSTG's good Happy Hour and salads. So we thought we'd give them a try since they're right next door to The Boulevard.   It was the final night of the playoffs so we were wanting something quick and light.  The menu seemed to have a large variety, but we focused on the salads and choose; Fried Chicken and Cobb. As an appetizer we went with Truffle Fries, to balance out the healthiness of salads.   The Truffle Fries were good, but a little limp. I would have enjoyed them more if they were crispier. Both salads were served in huge bowls and had a nice presentation.  The amount of toppings in both were plentiful. My Cobb had a huge amount of Blue Cheese that almost overpowered the other ingredients.  The SO's  Fried Chicken Salad was huge and he said the chicken was flavorful. The salads are so BIG, that if you get an appetizer, two people could share one salad.   Their ambiance was overpowering for me. The colors were to bright as were the lights. Our waiter was friendly, but neglected to tell us the nightly specials. Once we had eaten and he was taking the order from the table next to us, he told them about a Meatloaf Special. I admit we went in wanting salads, but both us would have been tempted away with meatloaf. I think that will be my next new Yelp list, "Meatloaf".  Looking at their Martini selection, I think I'll revisit for a Happy Hour and see how happy they can make me.

I just realized my last two reviews or Laurie's are written on the same day two years apart. Well, it is time again for new work shoes and I'm earlier. I guess I have been working harder, so my shoes need to be replaced.   As stated in previous update, no fun shoes at my employment. They've to be black, lace-up and a no skid sole. Having wide feet, it is hard for me to buy this type of shoe at outlet and discount stores. Trust me I have tried and to be honest, the prices are not that much different. Here at Laurie's I get excellent customer service from an experienced shoe expert. Who makes sure I am slipping my massive food into the correct size. No wonder my feet have hurt in the past, I was wearing the wrong size.   Laurie's also has some very fashionable Cole Hann and Dexter loafers that I wear when I am not working. Also, if you have children, I highly recommend Laurie's. They have a huge variety of cute little shoes. I have watched them work their magic on getting the tots to calm down and slip their tiny feet into new shoes.   Remember, shop local and keep our hometown stores in business.

The only thing that could improve Culver's is table service and ice cold beer. The Double Deluxe Hamburger with crinkle fries is a great treat after some power shopping at Costco. On second thought, who needs beer when you can have a Culver's Root Beer. Once you've tasted it, you'll wish it was available in a six pack to take home. Always share an order of onion rings, it just makes the meal complete.

Had the Greek Salad with gyro meat, the meat was very tender and flavorful. The plate was extremely small for the portion of salad. Whenever you forked a bite, lettuce and meat would slide off the plate. Would it be asking to much for a large plate? Let's be serious, you're not fooling anyone if you are trying to make the portions look larger.  Our waiter was extremely friendly and made our dinning experience enjoyable.  We'll be going back.

Oh, Hell No. Consignment shops and places like Goodwill and Salvation Army have better furniture then VCF.   On my mission to redo the living room, I was exploring as many options as I possibly could. Obviously I was not thinking when I made a stop here. We were promptly greeted by a "sales professional"  and I informed him what we were looking for; club chairs that do not rock, swivel or recline and no leather.   He acknowledged my guidelines and lead us towards the middle of the store.  He then pointed out one chair that he thought we'd like. It looked good, so I walked over  and touched the arm. In amazement I said, "I can feel the frame."  His reply was an honest one, "Look at the price, what do you expect."  He was right, for that price I was lucky the chair frame was covered with upholstery.   We should have left at that point, but we continued to follow him further through the store pointing out other selections. I did no more chair touching. As quick as he suggested another chair, I responded "No". Finally after I think the third suggestion, he politely said, "Perhaps we're not the store for you."  Wonder what gave him that idea? Once again, he was so right.   The biggest plus of shopping at VCF is the fact that El Maguey is across the street. After browsing through their store, I needed a Margarita.

Where's the beef? Oh, I forgot I ordered the new Impossible Whopper.  The Impossible Whopper is vegetarian and vegan friendly, because it is plant based and it taste just like real meat.   I'm not vegan or vegetarian, but I've had a Impossible Burger at several restaurants in STL and have enjoyed them. When I heard BK was now offering one, I had to give it a try. BK is right at the  street entrance to my work location, so I stopped by on my way home. Is it good as a Whopper with "real" meat? No. Is it good as a Impossible Burger at a sit down restaurant? No, but it was still good and I am sure the vegans and vegetarians of the world are thrilled it is available at a fast food burger joint.   My IB had good flavor, it had all the same toppings as an original Whopper. The only complaint I would have is that it was a tad smaller then the bun and that it was crisp around the edges a little on the dry side. The crisp edges and dryness, I'll give them a little leeway since it is new to their menu and it is only the second day they are making them.  I'm looking forward to trying it again here and at the BK near my home.   The staff here is not the friendliest, but they are always quick with the service. It's fast food fast, so I can tolerate the staff being aloof.   I'll be back? - Sure.   When: April 2, 2019 Why: Impossible Whopper released April 1, 2019

I get a chuckle that J & A's is a smoking bar, except between the hours of 10 AM - 2 PM. Why you ask? It is so all the employees from local businesses can come in and enjoy their amazingly good burger and fries. It may be a four hour reprieve from smoking, but the place still reeks of smoke and grease. It is an aroma that lets you know it is a true dive bar.   The staff is always friendly and if you sit at the bar, the regulars make you feel like you are one of them. However, I prefer to sit at one of the tables opposite the bar and people watch. As I've said in other dive bar reviews, the clientele is right out of a reality show.   Cheap drinks, good eats and fun customers is why this dive bar  is the oldest bar in the Lou.

I have always enjoyed New Balance tennis shoes. I have another brand that I wear to the gym and they look like a gym shoe. Getting ready for a vacation, I needed a tennis shoe that would look more fashion forward then like I was headed to the gym.   When I entered the store, a young lady greeted me promptly and I told her what my needs were. She totally understood and showed me a couple that would fit my needs.  I selected a simple white on white walking shoe. To give my new shoes an extra kick, I bought a bundle of bright colored ankle socks and a couple different colored laces to add color to the white shoes.  I'm going to be doing a lot of walking on this vacation, so these new shoes are going to be a great addition to my wardrobe. I now have Happy Feet.   All the associates at New Balance are well trained and certified in selecting the appropriate size shoe for their customers. I am pleased with my new walking shoes and I am making sure I've got them broken in before leaving town.   A bonus of shopping at his location is there is an Orange Leaf next door, so when you are done buying new shoes you can have some FroYo.

WOW! I had no idea how cool this place was. I was in the area for a lunch with friends at another restaurant, and saw signs providing directions to O'Fallon Brewery. So, after an amazing BBQ lunch, I stopped by O'Fallon for a quick beer.   When I arrived, I honestly was just expecting a brewery offering cold brews and nothing more. To my surprise, they are a fun blown restaurant. I was in awe watching all the plates going by and then I'd read the menu to match it up. I'm coming back and enjoying some wings or a flatbread for sure.   Any way, on this visit all I had was a Vanilla Pumpkin beer. At any given time, there are 20 O'Fallon Craft Beers on tap. Back to the Vanilla Pumpkin, it was refreshing and may be my new Octoberfest beer.   Bartender was attentive and professional. He didn't mind that I wasn't eating and that I only stopped in for a beer.   I'll be back? - Yes, now that I know that they're a restaurant, too.   When? - October 3, 2018 Why? - Signs directed me to the brewery

Gourmet Italian at carry out prices and it is not located on The Hill.  Now, that's Italian. I'm a fan of Filomena's and proud that they are my 500th review.   I first discovered Filomena's attending a Elite VIP Dinner and have been a fan ever since. The other day I was at Laurie's shopping for a new pair of shoes at the perfect time. Lunch time and with Filomena's next door it was easy to decide where to chow down. If you have ever bought a pair of shoes at Laurie's you know they offer you a Dad's Cookie as you're paying. We declined the cookie saying we were going next door for lunch. Several of the staff immediately started telling us their favorites and saying how great it is for lunch.   Dining at Filomena's is made easy. You order your meal at the counter, let them know if you'll be dining in or doing the easy carry out. We choose to eat in, choosing a table in the corner. The SO normally doesn't like Toasted Ravioli, but occasionally I do. So I ordered a small  (6) piece appetizer. Surprisingly the SO liked theirs and so did I.   Our lunches were brought to our table in "cute" recyclable containers. The lid was tucked under the main dish making it easy for us to just pop the lid on top and go with our leftovers. I've been craving spaghetti with meat sauce for a while, so it was an easy order for me. I even added two meatballs on top. The meat sauce was thick clinging to al dente noodles and the meatballs were moist. This Italian Grandma knows what she is cooking.   The SO choose the Penne Alfredo with Grilled Chicken. Great Alfredo sauce, but  did not appear to be grilled. Our guess is that it was poached or baked. It lacked that extra kick true grilled chicken provides. Nonetheless it was a good lunch. Both were plentiful lunches resulting in us popping the lids on and having a next day lunch.

Cool zen type ambiance. The booths are cube like, as Mark P. has stated in his review making a very cozy atmosphere for a couple or a group of six. The staff is friendly and knowledgeable about their menu and were honest in their recommendations.   Both of us started out with Miso Soup which was very warming, since we had been walking all over downtown playing tourist.  The SO also ordered a house salad which was sad. A salad made with iceberg is bad enough, but when the lettuce is limp and wilted that just makes me sad.   We also shared an order of Mozzarella Tempura, which was light and refreshing. One of my favorite vegetables is asparagus and MT was made with fresh firm stalks. Some pieces of tempura were filled with cream Mozzarella cheese and others were the asparagus. I wish they were combined, then this appetizer would have really won my heart. The menu claimed it came with a dipping sauce, which we did not see and did not realize we missed out until we got home and reread the menu while writing this review. Wonder if missing out tasting the sauce cost them a star?   My entree was Blackened Sesame Chicken, which was real easy to eat with chopsticks and I am not a master at operating them. It was succulent  pieces of breast  meat sauteed in house made Korean style sweet and sour sauce then coated in crushed sesame seeds. I would have enjoyed it more on a bed of brown rice, but it was still very good. It came with the side house salad, which is basically iceberg lettuce with a few mixed greens tossed in for darker color.  I'm not a fan of sushi, but the SO is and ordered the Rolled Combo #2 which was a lunch special. I tried one of the Philly Rolls and was not impressed, but keep in mind I am not a sushi fan. I will say, the presentation was not as pretty as most sushi I have seen.   I think Takaya New Asian is a great addition to the Washington Avenue mix and once they get past their opening and groaning pains, they'll be well on their way.

Pure Plates is an easy and affordable way to pack and plan your lunches for work. I would easily spend between $7 and $10 for lunch if I went out, so I do not mind paying that for a healthy and well portioned meal.   Each prepared meal comes packaged in a recyclable container with a nutritional label giving you all the information you want to know. Each meal only needs to be heated up for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, which is a lot faster then any fast food joint. It's healthier, too.   My two favorites so far are: Spaghetti Squash with Turkey and Pecan Crusted Chicken. I can't wait to explore more of their wide varieties of prepared meals.   Will I return? - Yes, makes my work lunches easier.   When: May 10, 2017 and other dates Why: Too lazy to cook work lunches.

I found a new place for breakfast and it's downtown. I had to pay for street parking to eat, but it was so worth it. I already know I'll be coming back here, on the regular.
