BLT's is set up where you order at a counter, you're given a table marker and you seat yourself. Or, you can do what I did and sit at the bar where they give full table service. I normally place myself at the bar anyway, so this was a no brainer for me.   After reading the menu, viewing pictures on Yelp and reading a couple of Yelp reviews we decided what to order. Being raised on a farm, I had to go with the Farmers Breakfast. I've never seen so much food on one plate. It was two eggs, house-made sausage, bacon and pork-belly. Plus, a biscuit smothered in milk gravy, topped with shredded cheddar.  If I had this on the farm, I may have never left.   My friend ordered my second choice, the Chicken and Waffles. It was a half breast cut in half. I say that, because the pieces were bigger then a typical tender. The pieces were crispy and had a wonder crunch to it. The waffle almost covered the entire square plate. It came with whipped butter and maple syrup. I'll be getting it on my next visit.   I'm addicted to Bloody Mary's and they do a kick-ass one here. It was spicy and you could see the flakes of black pepper in the mix. The BM was so good, I had to try their Mimosa's as well. Josh one of the owners was bartending and asked me if I liked my Mimosa's more OJ or champaign? Hello, more champaign. He laughed and said, he kinda figured that's how I would like it.   The food is excellent. Josh and his staff provide relaxed and friendly service.  I highly recommend that you check this place out. Pay the parking meter and enjoy a fantastic breakfast. Oh, they do lunch and tacos, too. I gotta check those two out, too.   I'll be back? - I plan to be a regular.   When: November 20, 2018 Why: New breakfast restaurant.

After a day of running endless errands, I was beat and had no energy to cook when I got home. Since I was in Maplewood and a prime parking space was near Acero, my problem was solved. It also provided me with an opportunity to try the Egg Raviolo that Ian said was the "must order" on his STL 100.   It was a busy night and all the tables were filled and couples were waiting at the bar for an opening table. I asked the hostess if it were possible to be seated and served at the bar and she said absolutely. The bartender was knowledgeable on both the drink and special food offerings. I'm confident my service at the bar, dining alone was the exact same as if I were at a table. It was attentive and professional.   I've enjoyed an Acero Manhattan before and was tempted to have another, but I changed my mind after the bartender told me about the Black Manhattan. It's made with Bone Snapper Rye, Averna Amaro, Angostura Bitters and Amerena Cherry. I usually enjoy my Manhattan's up, but he encouraged me to have this one on the rocks. Telling me, their ice was a large cube that would melt slowly and keep the drink chilled as I enjoyed it. He was oh, so right.   I listened to the nightly specials, but kept my focus on the Egg Raviolo. I can always be swayed away by sea scallops, but I'll come back and enjoy them within a Four Course Tasting Menu. The Egg Raviolo was a Three Cheese. I paired it with a side of Brussel Sprouts, so I'd have my green vegetable of the day.  The Egg Raviolo was absolute perfection. At first, I cut off a small bite from the outer edge. The blend of the three cheeses melted in my mouth. When I went to slice off my second bite, I couldn't resist. I had to cut it down the center so I could see the yolk run free. It was absolute perfection. I am so glad that I had not nibbled on the fresh bread that the bartender had placed in front of me. I ended up using it to wipe my bowl clean of the delicious cheese sauce and runny egg yolk.   My Brussels Sprouts were roasted with pancetta & pecorino. I'm still in amazement that as a child I hated brussels sprouts, but now as an adult they are one of my favorite vegetables. As I was dining, I would eat some pasta and then some of the sprouts. Towards the end, I was struggling with which one did I want to enjoy as my last bite. To have that last lingering flavor in my mouth until I returned home and brushed my teeth. I lost control, devouring all the food, so my last bite ended up being a sip of my Black Manhattan.   I'm going back for the Tasting Menu - hope they let me do it at the bar as many times I am a single diner.   When: March 30, 2016 Why: Dinner -

Once you get past the "Diva Hostess" who thinks she is superior to those she is seating, who'll have a pizza that will have you saying, "wow, this is what a pizza should be". We had the chicken wings as an appetizer and were pleased with the flavor, you can taste the chili seasoning. Our pizza was the CWE, thin crust and was fantastic. I can't wait to go back and expand my experience by trying a deep dish. Our waiter, was a delightful & charming, he made up for the "heroin chic" hostess. He knew she was an issue and downer.

When: February 13 Why: Valentine Beer Dinner  Gotta love this place! We've been to four of their beer dinners, and have never been disappointed. The staff is always witty and the food that they pair with each brew is creative and original.  Pairing a beer with food, I think is more of a challenge then do the pairing with wine.   This dinner featured Goose Island Brewery, this is what we experienced:  1. Brie & Mushroom Quesadilla with Pear Chutney      Beer - Sophie 2.  Belgian Beef & Onion Stew       Beer - Matilda 3.   Curried Lamb Meatballs over Thai Risotto       Beer - Pere Jacques 4.   Dessert ......it was by Angela (she always does a good job)        Beer - Forgot to write it down, sorry. It was good.   A representative from the brewery that is being featured, talks about each beer while it is being served. You get to hear history and fun stories that you'd never know from just buying it at your local grocer or booze joint.  The glasses may be sample glasses, but they keep filling them through out the tasting. So you get plenty.   My metro-east family dines here frequently, and seeing the sampling of foods they create at these beer dinners I can see why.   The next beer dinner is April 3rd and this time it is going to be Mark the owners favorite beers and not a specific brewery.  We'll be there at our usual table, sipping and tasting.   Heads Up: These dinners sell out fast.

What a great addition to the dining options at Plaza Frontenac. Our most recent shopping pilgrimage to the plaza was around lunch time, so we asked our sales associates as we shopped, where to have lunch and they all unanimously said, "Brick Top".  They all recommended the same things, Burger or Fish Tacos. With so many endorsements and recommendations of good ideas we were sold.   After shopping till we were ready to drop or starving to death, we headed out to Brick Top for a satisfying lunch. Our friend at the Omega watch store told us be sure to sit at the bar. He said the bartender always makes it a fun experience and he is right about that. Tammy and her coworker Steve, made sure that we were taken care of in style and we were only drinking ice tea with our meal.   We started out with Deviled Eggs and Sugar Bacon. Three eggs sliced in half, deviled and three slices of gooey chewy bacon for $9. Highway robbery? Hell, yes. That is some major markup on three eggs and slices of bacon. Worth the $9? Not really, but that bacon was so sweet, chewy and good. The deviled eggs themselves, were just average, but I am glad I got to experience them.   The Fish Tacos were Blackened Fish of the Day served in a soft tortilla shell with your typical taco garnishes. I normally am not a Fish Taco fan, but these had me scratching my head in wonderment as to why. I think it is because I had not experienced these little jewels before. The Blackened seasoning gave them a good kick of flavor and except for the side of fries, it was a healthy lunch.   What sold me on the 4 Stars was my burger. It is proudly being placed #1 on my burger list. The lunch special was a Bleu Cheeseburger with your choice of slaw or fries. I went out of my comfort zone and I am so glad I did. By that I mean, typically I am not a Bleu Cheese type guy, but this was the bomb. Bleu Cheese burgers I've had or seen in the past basically just had a scoop of the cheese dolloped on top of the burger. Not this one, theirs was evenly melted across the entire burger and even had a golden bubble to it like a pizza cheese. I ordered mine medium and it seared and the perfect shade of pink inside for my taste.  I agree with George, these are some of the best fries in town. Their house seasoning which has sugar in it, is what makes them stand above the rest.  A big bonus for me is they serve ketchup in small cups with your order. I am not a fan of nasty ketchup bottles on the table.   I may have to shop PF more often, it will give me an excuse to eat at Brick Top again and again.

With a recent talk thread about the best Chinese, I realized that it was time to give my favorite an update on Yelp.   We enjoy PP so much, it is programmed in to our iPhones for easy access. On those days when we both are to beat from work to cook, it is Panda to the rescue. We start our Chinese feast with Egg Drop Soup (the best I have ever had) and a share order of Crab Rangoon. In my world if you are having Chinese, you have got to have an Egg Roll. We have been known to make a meal out of just those three items.   When we order an entree, Moo Shu Chicken has become our favorite. Others that have pleased our palate; General Tso's Chicken, Orange Chicken and Szechuan Beef. In our hood, Panda Pavilion was the first to offer brown rice as an alternative to the traditional white rice.   Another big plus, is that PP now offers a "Healthy Diet Menu" which offers different items steamed. My favorite is chicken with vegetables. They use no oil, sugar, salt or corn starch and serve it with natural steamed rice with a side of brown garlic sauce.  I get my Chinese fix and make my doctor happy at the same time.   Healthy options, delivery and good food makes Panda Pavilion a Steven B favorite.

So glad I can come back and sit at my corner of the bar at Stone Turtle. I had to giggle how they had areas marked off with blue tape so customers would not sit at certain areas at the bar. They're taking the social distancing seriously. My usual stool was available, so I was a happy drinker.   One of my favorite summer drinks is a, Boulevardier. The Compari makes a refreshing cocktail to sip while visiting with a good friend. Norma my BFF enjoyed a, Aviation. If you're a fan of Gin, you'll love it, too.   We both needed something to nosh on, while we enjoyed our cocktails and chatted. Norma knew immediately that she wanted the, Pork & Cashews. I gotta agree with her, how can you go wrong with a salty mixture of pork belly & cashew nuts. Yum-Yum.   For me, I went with, Tiger Roll. It was my first time and it will not be the last. They were f-ing amazing. The serving size was, 3 rolls. If you order these on my recommendation, I suggest you do a double order. Because, I'm telling you now, you will not want to share them.   These rolls are wontons stuffed with; spicy crab, shrimp and cream cheese. Then for dipping, they're served with a Cilantro Jam. I'm one of those people who thinks, cilantro taste like soap. However, this jam won me over. It provided a nice splash of extra flavor when you dabbed it on your wonton.   We needed a second cocktail. For me, I had to have my all-time favorite, a classic, Manhattan. If you've read my previous review - they do them right here. I loved it and I had it on the rocks. Norma, got a little adventurous and tried a, La Socialista. It was a perfect blend of; Rum, Blood Orange, Lime Juice and Vanilla. Rum and Vanilla for me personally is always a winner. It must have been good, she finished it before I finished my Manhattan.   The staff were all wearing mask and I as I stated in my opening, they were on top of the social distancing. So they get a big, Thank-You for doing it safe.   Will I be back? - Yep, it's one of my favorite Dogtown bars.   When: July 1, 2020 Why: Getting out of the house.

Mama Josephine's is your typical 5 Star restaurant. It isn't prissy white linen service, it is simple down-home southern country comfort food. I recently attended a UYE here for dinner and it was so good, I got carry out for the other half who stayed at home. Then the next morning we both returned to Mama Josephine's for breakfast. So within twelve hours, I had two comfort meals that put a smile on my face and had my heart questioning what the hell I was doing. To make the heart happy, I did seven miles when I got home.   Dinner - Fried Chicken, all white meat. I enjoyed one breast and a wing with a side of Mac-n-Cheese and Green Beans. The chicken reminded me of the chicken my mom would fry up on the farm in the cast iron skillet. So many places over cheese their Mac-n-Cheese, but not Mama Josephine. She coats the macaroni with just the right amount of cheese. The green beans, tasted as if they were picked that morning and made fresh for dinner.   Carryout - Fried Chicken, dark meat. I requested two thighs and they were very accommodating. I changed things up for this order and did Fried Okra and Cooked Cabbage. OMG! The cabbage had me changing my opinion of cooked cabbage, their seasoning had me wanting a second serving. If you've had true Southern Fried Okra, you know down south they do not coat the okra in breading. They just dust in lightly allowing the flavor of the okra to come through and that is how MJ serves her okra.   The morning after having a fried chicken dinner, we headed back to MJ to enjoy two big huge country breakfast.   Southern Delight - 2 fried eggs, a piece of country ham and potatoes. I am not sure if they use a grill to fry their eggs, but again they reminded me of those in a cast iron skillet. The ham was a nice size serving, to accompany the eggs and potatoes. Their potatoes were what I grew up with on the farm, sliced potatoes fried. No fancy hash browns.   Three Egg Breakfast - 3 fried eggs, sausage and potatoes.   Being the farm boy and a fan of biscuits and gravy, we shared an order.  These were true farmer biscuits and gravy. Flaky made from scratch biscuits and a milk gravy filled with chunks of pork sausage.   The service is always over the top friendly. If you do not feel the love, something is wrong with you.

This is just what STL needed, another craft/microbrewery. Seriously, it is what we need. The more the merrier.  I would love to see my hometown become craft beer capital of the world. Variety is the spice of life and it likes a variety of craft beers to go along with it.   As many of the other reviewers have stated, the ambiance is stark. It is plain and simple with no thrills and that is okay. You're coming here for the variety of craft beers and good conversation with friends. There's no kitchen, but they usually have a food truck parked next to the entrance to provide some nourishment to accompany your brew.   They're only open Friday and Saturday, so be sure to put it in your busy schedule. It is well worth the stop for a beer or two. If you fall in love with one, buy a growler and have it filled with your new favorite beer to enjoy at home.   The staff is friendly and knowledgeable of their brews. If you tell them what you normally like in a beer, they'll guide to the best match of their taps.   The crowd is a good mix of aged beer connoisseurs and beer hipsters. Along with a mix of cool city dwellers and county folk who braved the city for a beer.   I'll be back and one of their growlers will be a gift for my beer loving family and friends.   When: May 27, 2016 Why: Beer with the "B" brothers

This Starbucks is still just a solid 3 Stars. They get the job done, but without any extra pizzaz in customer service.   I stopped in to pick up a Grande Cold Brew before my class over at the Apple store. The cashier was very dry, to be honest I do not remember her even thanking me or ordering. The wait for my beverage was minimal, considering two others were ahead of me in line. The young lady who presented me my drink, did thank me for coming in. So I figured, it was her job to say, "thanks".   I wish Starbucks would go to paper straws or the new lids that are like a travel mug and do away with the plastic straws.   Will I return? - Only if I am taking a class at the Apple store.   When: February 27, 2020 Why: Liquid refreshment for class

I scream, you scream, we all scream for ice cream. We especially scream when it is the orange sherbet and vanilla twist from Northside Dairy Haven. It's the absolute best.  I noticed NDH as I was driving down IL 159 aka N. Main to meet family for dinner in downtown Edwardsville. It was a cute little nostalgic ice cream drive-in and I thought to myself, if it's open when I come back by, I'll stop for a quick cone.  Lucky for me it was still open and I experienced an amazingly good ice cream treat.    When I approached the window, I ordered a small cone thinking they only offered vanilla. When the young girl asked, what flavor and she told me my choices, I immediately up-sized to a medium. I had to have a larger cone, when vanilla and orange sherbet are available in a twist. A soft serve Dreamsicle, is a dream treat.   As described by John H., it is kind of hidden off the beaten path. It is nestled in a wooden area on a gravel lot. It is as if it were grandma's cottage tucked away in the woods were she serves up sweet treats. The service is warm, mom & pop, small town friendly. If you're in E-ville, save time and room in your tummy for an ice cream treat at NDH.

It was time for new work shoes and the last pair I bought at Laurie's were winners so I went back for the exact same shoe. At work we have a dress code, so not much fun in buying shoes. They have to be black,  a no skid sole and they have to tie, no slip on. I know it's yawn city, but Laurie's helped me find a pair that does not lead to depression when I put them on.   At least while I was there, I made note of a new pair of tennis shoes and loafers to make my feet truly happy.   I've said it before and will say it again, when you are in the market for shoes you've got to check Laurie's Shoes out.

It's a dive bar.   You'll have a good time drinking well prepared drinks at an amazingly affordable price.   The ambiance is bland, but remember it is a dive bar, so that actually adds to its beauty.   There is no bar food. Your snacks and munchies come out of a vending machine that is also reasonably priced.   They have hooks and outlets under the bar. Nice asset for a dive bar.   Bartenders are friendly, attentive and mix a good cocktail. They can even open a bottle or can of beer with finesse.   I recommend that you grab some friends and head over to SC for a fun time. Or, you can go alone and make some new friends sitting at the bar.  I'll be back? - Who's going with me?  When - November 14, 2018 Why - Cocktails with Max, he's the man.

When you first enter here you may say to yourself, "Where's the beef? Where's the pork?" What you need to do is stop and think. What is the name of this BBQ joint? It's Gobble Stop Smokehouse and it is, "Where Bird is the Word".  Which means their specialty is chicken and turkey. It's a specialty that they truly have mastered. So you'll soon forget that they do not offer beef brisket or pulled pork.    I would have never discovered GSS if it were not for Brian M. organizing a UYE lunch. To my surprise it is just down the street from my dogs vet, so I know I will be visiting again and again. Now I will be requesting appointments near lunchtime, instead of the early morning.   My lunch was the Smoked Chicken Wings and they were Gobble-icious.  They were served drummette style and seasoned with their signature herbs and spices. They may have been slowly smoked, but I gobbled them up fast. I had the sauce served on the side, but was totally satisfied with the signature rub. As my side, I choose Green Beans which had pieces of ham. They were the perfect accompaniment to BBQ as they would be a Sunday fried chicken.   I couldn't enjoy a new BBQ place without taking some home for the other half who was working in the yard. A Half Smoked Chicken with two sides would be the perfect reward. As his sides, I choose Cole Slaw and Potato Salad. He was so impressed with their Smoked Chicken, that he wants to check out their fried chicken in the near future.   If you are in a hurry, I suggest calling ahead and ordering. The service is friendly, but is on the slow side of Southern Hospitality.

Dogtown has a new shining star. I am so glad the space that was vacated by Felix's has finally been filled. Stone Turtle is an excellent addition to the diverse mix of restaurants in Dogtown.   As my usual, I took a seat at the bar. Being a whiskey bar, my first drink had to be a Manhattan. Big bonus points for using a single large cube of ice and a dark filthy cheery. Those are two of my requirements of a good Manhattan and you got them right. Also, points for stirring.   Needing a munchie to accompany my cocktail, I selected the Mango Habanero Chicken Wings. They had good flavor, not as spicy or hot as I would have liked, but good. I also, would have preferred them to be crisper. They were to soft/mushy for my chicken wing taste.   After wings and a Manhattan, I was ready to move on to an entree and second cocktail. My #2 go to drink is an Old Fashioned and this one did not disappoint me. It was top notch from the get go. The young man sitting next to me, told me on my next visit I needed to try the Smoked one, which is their signature drink. If it is half as good as their classic Old Fashioned, it will be a winner too.   My entree was the Steak & Frites. The main attraction of the plate is the 14 oz house cut Ribeye. It is served with Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Frites. The Brussels Sprouts had bacon and we all know everything is better with bacon, so they totally made my taste buds do a happy dance. The Frites were crispy and were served with little cups of Mayo and Ketchup. (Little Cups get bonus points with me) The actual Ribeye was prepared to my liking, a nice medium rare. It was tender and seasoned well. It was a little fatty for my personal taste, but I understand that can be a hit and miss with a Ribeye. I'd still recommend ordering it, if you are a meat man.   Watching other orders arrive around me, I know that I need to go back and try the; Fish & Chips, Grilled Salmon and Pork Chop. The Mac & Cheese also looked delicious. Again, the young man seated next to me said it was tasty and he allowed me to photograph his order.  So I definitely gotta give it a try on the next visit.  Service was friendly. It was kinda slow, but they are still new and being a Friday night, they were getting fairly busy while I was there. Keeping all that in mind, they did a good job being attentive and making sure everyone was taken care of. I also applaud them for having Eco-Friendly To-Go Vessels.   I'll be back? - I have a lot more to try.   When: January 19, 2018 Why: New Hot Spot & I needed dinner.

As I was enjoying my coffee on the morning of May 12, 2021, I checked to see what was selected as the ROTD in STL. To my surprise, it was a restaurant in Alton, IL and barely a mile and half from my house. Once I saw that, it was an easy decision on where I'd be going for lunch that day.   I remember eating at Olga's when I worked in various malls in STL, but I seriously had thought they had disappeared. To my surprise the one at Alton Square Mall is still going strong. What is sad, is that it literally is the only thing that is open on the second level, but the Alton community still supports them and keeps them going. Honestly I am surprised they haven't moved to a strip-center where they'd get better traffic.   Any way, let's talk about my lunch. I was very pleased and most likely will be returning, but will do carry-out as I saw many others doing. The day I dined, they had a special which included; The Original Olga, small Olga salad and a side of Olga's seasoned curly fries. Now that was a filling and delicious combo meal. I enjoyed the small Greek salad and the gyro meat was tender. Those crazy curly fries are a treat plain and when they are seasoned, they truly are a treat. Visiting during COVID, they provided me with a "Little Cup of  Ketchup" for dipping my fries. To be honest, I always prefer my ketchup in a little cup, so I was extremely delighted to see it on my plate.   My beverage of choice was iced tea and when I asked for Spelenda, they brought me individual packets and placed them on the table. Again, it was a good and safe precaution during our pandemic.   The service was friendly and attentive. Their ambiance was bare bones and simple. When I lived in STL, I had so many choices for a gyro. Here in Alton, the choice are minimal. I'm glad I have re-discovered Olga's and that their gyro satisfies my craving. I'll be calling and doing carry-out in the very near future.   When: May 12, 2021 Why: Lunch - It was todays, ROTD.

Northside Dairy Haven was the third stop on our tour of Edwardsville for a birthday celebration. We had to drive like bats out of hell from our second stop, because we just discovered that NDH closed at 9 PM.   When we arrived, the young ladies working were already starting the closing process, but were still extremely friendly and ready to take our orders. There are so many sweet treats to choose from, but we all knew what we wanted. We wanted that infamous vanilla and orange sherbet twist cone. There were six of us, so it was a slam dunk easy order. The clerk even got a giggle at how easy our order was.   We all enjoyed our cones on their small patio and then headed out to the final stop of the the birthday celebration.   If you're in Edwardsville, you owe it to yourself to stop by NDH and treat yourself to one of their ice cream treats. Next time I go, I'm trying something from the food menu. If the ice cream is tasty, I want to see what they do with something savory.   I'll be back? - When in Edwardsville, I'll be there.   When: July 13, 2018 Why: Dessert for a birthday celebration.

I gotta be honest, I do not see the love for all these different yogurt/froyo stores. They are a dime a dozen pushing basically the same thing. Flavored yogurts with insane amounts of toppings to choose from. We all have our addicitions, this is not one of mine.   I will give this Yogurtland kudos for having the largest selection of flavors to choose from and the best pricing. On my visit I sampled; Red Velvet Cupcake, Caramel Almond, Chocolate Milkshake, Dulce DE Leche and Madagascar Vanilla.  Funny, my favorite was the Vanilla and the Chocolate Milkshake came in a very close second.   The Toppings Bar here was the most extensive that I have seen and the best maintained. I normally do not add toppings to mine, I like to enjoy the true flavors provided by the yogurt itself. However,  with the presentation of this toppings bar I may be tempted on my next visit. The reason other toppings bars have turned me off is the drippings and sloppiness of other patrons. Here the staff keeps their bar nice and clean.   This Yogurtland also has a prime location, its neighbor is Five Guys Burger and Fries. Which makes this little strip center the perfect location to break you diet.

Homer Simpson wouldn't  eat these donuts.  I never thought I'd see the day when I'd find a donut I didn't like.  These are the most flavorless donuts I have experienced.     I can not comment on the customer service, the box of donuts were brought in by a co-worker.

I am so torn on what I should do. Should I start a support group for those of us who are addicted to the Baja Fish Tacos at MTJ? Or, should I start a fan club and appoint myself president? Until MTJ came along, I would have never eaten a fish taco. My ex made me try one once and now, I have to order one every time I visit. I prefer the fried, but when I order I do order a Wood-Fired Grilled one as well. The ratio is typically 2:1.   Their Baja Fish Taco is simple; fish, Chipotle Baja sauce, shredded cabbage, pico de gallo and quest fresco. They have gotten me through a couple of Fridays during Lent and has been my go to for Cinco de Mayo for the last two years. I recommend them to everyone that I send to MTJ. It is a "must order" for me.   Mission Taco Joint being on Ian Froeb's STL 100 List was a no-brainer. It didn't surprise me at all. What did surprise me was Ian's "must order" recommendation. He said, the Beef Brisket Birria taco was the "must order". So on my recent visit I had a little competition, it was my Baja Fish Taco vs Beef Brisket Birria. The slow roasted brisket was so tender, it absolutely melted in my mouth. I also enjoyed the huge piece of avocado garnish and the fiery arbol sauce. I still love my Baja, but Ian is right on this one. If you dine at MTJ, you gotta order the Beef Brisket Birria. Or you could do what I'll be doing now and order one of each.   Let's talk chips and salsa real quick. I am still hearing people whining that they have to pay $3 at MTJ to get what most places give complimentary. Get over it! Don't be cheap, order the chips and salsa. The quality is far and beyond what you're getting free at those other restaurants. The chips are always fresh and warm when they're delivered to you and the two house sauces never disappoint me. I wish I could remember the names when they tell me - the green one on my last visit is by far my favorite of all time. I truly enjoyed the burn it gave me.  Service is always relaxed and friendly. It has a true neighborhood bar feeling and I like that.   When: April 5, 2016 Why: Checking out Ian's "must order" recommendation

P-A-R-T-Y!!!  Rhone Rum Bar is going to be one of those places you'll go to hang with your best friends. Heck, you'll even come here to with co-workers after a hard day of work. The Caribbean themed drinks, food and decor,  makes it an easy place to just let loose and relax.   I was fortunate enough to be able to attend a soft opening. Sure they had some bumps, but they still put on a good showing of what is to come. RRB is defiantly going to live up to its name, serving over 50 different varieties of Rum.   Their specialty cocktail menu offered a variety of frozen and boat drinks all priced at a reasonable $8. My bartender recommended the, Buschwacker. It was a frozen cocktail made with six different liquors. My only wish is, that the next time I have one, it is one a Caribbean beach. It was so refreshing, I want to feel the warm sun on my face and sand between my toes.   I also, tried a couple of boat drinks (non-frozen). I really liked the, Pirates Paloma. The combination of grapefruit juice and ting, with mango rum was a winner. The Vodka & Ting, was a simple cocktail. I'd recommend it for those who don't like exotic beach cocktails.   Their food menu some would describe as limited. I'd say it is, selective and focused on popular Caribbean food. I enjoyed an order of Jerk Chicken Wings and Conch Fritters. The chicken wings were huge and meaty. They were served as a whole wing, not drummies and flats. That being said, they were a little messier to eat. Don't worry, that is why you're given bright colored linen napkins to wipe your mouth and fingers.  The Conch Fritters were crunch on the outside, with a soft inside. When it comes to food, I'm rarely a dipper. However, the key lime remoulade served with these fritters had me dipping every bite.   The staff is friendly and I can see them making this a fun place for Happy Hour and beyond.   I'll be back? - Do you like, Pina Coladas?   When: December 5, 2018 Why: Soft Opening.

Meet some fellow Yelpers here for a UYE Breakfast. While our food was good as usual, the service this morning was not what it normally is. I should of been prepared when the BF and I were the first to arrive and one of the servers told us they are short staffed. Why didn't I hear those warning bells?   When the other attendees arrived and we were seated, I commented to the young lady that it looked like she got some help and wasn't going solo. She gleefully responded, "yes, we got someone to come in early." Let me tell you, it didn't help. To get attention to order or to ask for anything additional and our checks, we had to wave them down.   Our food however, was exceptionally good. The UYE theme was Oktoberfest, so I ordered the German Utopia and recommend it to anyone who loves a bratwurst. It was two huge brats, cut in half lengthwise and grilled. They were so big, I'd been happy with one, but I did manage to eat them both. They came with a spicy mustard for dipping, two fried eggs and potatoes. I would of liked my potatoes to be crispier, but they did do my eggs perfectly over easy.   The BF had the Corned Beef Hash and said it was spot on for him.  I've never understood CBF, so I'll take him at his word. It was breakfast, so he also wanted a side of bacon and sausage. We asked if we could have a side of two bacon and two sausage and they were accommodating with our request. We should have asked the price? $4.29 for two pieces of bacon and two swiveled up sausages. That one is on us and we'll not do it again.   Good food, but service was lacking and they did not seem to be that busy.  The servers did seem to know everyone else dining. Perhaps our service lacked because  we were not regulars?

Here's the break down of my three star rating. They got one star for each of the following; ambiance & patio, music and the free chips with a Yelp check-in. Did you notice they got no stars for food? That is because, it was embarrassing. Some of it they should have been ashamed of even bringing it out to a table.   While we were dining, there were only two other tables eating and one drinking. The table service was minimal, but when present just some what friendly. They seemed to be tired and preoccupied. Was it because we were there the day after a holiday or is it always this way?   Checking in on Yelp got us a basket of assorted chips dusted with lime salt. They were served with bleu cheese dipping sauce which was good, but I am not a bleu cheese fan. I would rather of had a tangy mojo.   All of our small plates came out fairly together. Soon as our server sat one down, he was back with the next. It was a quick, 1,2 and three.   First to arrive was the Ceviche, which probably was the most refreshing.  It was a shrimp & vegetable citrus "cocktail". They say it is "Wildly" refreshing, I think that is an exaggeration.   Next was the Wicked Good Shrimp. Now this dish could have been good and mean really good. It had fresh tiger prawns sauteed in spices; served with bread for dipping. The shrimp were huge, which would have been the making of a great dish. However, the spices, were over powered by SALT. My SO, Brad loves salt and it was even to salty for him. When we mentioned it to our server, that we thought it heavy on salt. His only reply was, "yes it is". Perhaps instead of saying, sauteed in spices, saying sauteed in salt would be a more honest description.   Our last small plate "Frita", was Cuban pork & beef choriz sliders topped with Monterrey Jack cheese & crispy Yukon gold potatoes; served on a Cuban sweet roll. This plate had the most flavor of everything we experienced.   The very last thing, our House-Made Dessert, Caribbean Queen Cake was the worst of all our plates. It was hard as a hockey puck. I could not cut through it with the side of a fork, I had to grip the fork in my fist and jab the prongs down into the cake to have it break into bite size pieces. I have to admit, we ate it all. Not because it was good, we kept trying to figure out what was wrong with it and what was missing. It had us stumped.   They are lucky I gave them 3 stars, it seriously should have been 2.  Talking with other friends who had similar experiences, we all think this space may be available for a new venue by the end of summer.

It's just sad. The majority of this mall is empty and boarded up. What national chain stores that do remain, have not been updated in years.   On a positive note, if you're a mall walker, you can walk at a good speed. There will be no shoppers in your way.   Best thing this developer could do, is build a strip center on the outer edge of the parking lot, move the last valuable tenants and tear this dinosaur of a mall down.   Will I return? - Only for Olga's.   When: November 2, 2020 Why: Shopping Anchor and ventured out into mall

Are you ready to party? If not, you need to stay home, because when you come to Ballpark Village, it is a party. You'll have 4 restaurants to satisfy your food cravings and 6 bars to quench your thirst. When they have live music, you'll instantly have your dancing shoes on.   BV is a great place to meet before or after a baseball game and as we all recently witnessed it is also a great place to watch our hometown team during a run to a Stanley Cup victory. Let's Go Blues!   Downtown? Going to a ballgame? Want a fun time with friends? Get yourself over to Ballpark Village and let things naturally happen and it will be a good time.   I'll be back? - Let's play ball.  When: May 23, 2019 Why: Party!
They now deliver! Wish I could take credit for now offering this service, they started as soon as my comment appeared.....lol

One thing that I miss living across the river is not having a MTJ within a short drive. So while I had time to kill waiting for my dogs to get finished at the dog groomer in Kirkwood, I got my MTJ fix.  What I love about MTJ, is no matter what location you go to, your experience is always going to be the same. They're very consistent with their service and  quality of product.   Some folks complain that you have to buy your chips and salsa, but I say, get over it and pay for it. They're going to be a better quality and the salsas themselves are worth the minimal bucks. I will say, what I wish is that you could get a combo that had one salsa and a small queso. I like to double dip my chips and that would make me happy.   I've been a longtime fan of the hand made and shaken Margaritas and today I fell in love with, Tough Love. Having an addiction to jalapeños, I can now quench my thirst with their Mission Margarita flavored with fresh jalapeños. Oh, I cannot put into words how refreshing this cocktail was.   My choice of tacos for todays lunch were; Mango Kween Taco (Pride Month Collaboration), BLT Taco and Hot Fried Chicken Taco. I simple could not have gone wrong with, grilled flank steak, beer battered bacon and crispy habanero marinated chicken breast. I loved them all, so do not ask me to pick a favorite.   When posted on Facebook that I stopped here for lunch waiting for the dogs to be finished at the groomer, I was accused that I did it on purpose. I responded that I did not plan it, but it is now part of the plan for future grooming. The dogs get pretty and daddy gets MTJ.   When: June 16, 2021 Why: Taco Tuesday a day late

Hickory Grove is a new addition to the Alton restaurant scene. To my understanding it is a rejuvenation of a Hickory Grove that closed in a nearby town several years ago.   It is your typical traditional American fare of food. They offer your standard breakfast menu, a wide variety of sandwiches for lunch and a menu full of comfort foods for dinner. There is something for absolutely everyone on their menu.   My first visit was for a hearty breakfast. I selected a Bacon and Cheese Omelet that was served with a side of Hash Browns. Being an old farm boy, I have a love for Biscuits and Gravy, so I also had a half order of them.   The omelette was 3 eggs and was adequately stuffed with bacon. I would have enjoyed a little more cheese, but there was an sufficient amount. My Hash Browns I requested to be extra crispy. They were more charred, then made extra crispy. When I return for another breakfast, I will try their American Fries and see if they are a better choice.   Let's talk B&G, now. I was worried they'd be over salty, but that was not the case. In fact, I had to give mine a few shakes for the salt container on my table. However, they had the perfect amount of pepper. The biscuits were fluffy and I think the gravy was actually made in house and not from a mix.   The service was friendly and attentive for a new restaurant.   Be aware, they prefer cash as a form of payment. If you use any type of card they will add a 2.99% Non-Cash Adjustment to your bill.   When: March 27, 2021 Why: Breakfast

WKD is what you see in your head when you think of a classic diner. So why only see it in your head, come have a classic breakfast or a lunch plate. Chances are you may have to wait for a seat, they're are only 28 in the whole diner. If you are in a rush, they do offer carry-out, but I've been told the wait for carry-out can be a half hour, so do call ahead.   I've always wanted to come here, even before the filmed the modern day romantic drama, White Palace here on location. That movie was made 28 years ago and I am finally getting here. Damn, I'm embarrassed that it took me so long.   I came with a friend who lives downtown and only a block away. He's a semi-regular and said I had to experience it. Now that I have, I can honestly say, WKD is by far the best diner in STL. My breakfast was great & I'll be back soon to experience a diner burger.   My breakfast was a three egg omelet with bacon, cheddar cheese and jalapeños, with a side of Hash-Browns. The omelet was perfectly grilled for me, no extra dark brown spots on the outside. Mine was a beautiful light yellow all around. The inside was stuffed with large pieces of bacon and an ample amount of jalapeños all smothered in the cheddar cheese. My side of HB's was super crispy on top. Normally, I like to be crisp on top and bottom, but these having a super crisp top were very satisfying.   The friend who encouraged me to go, ordered a Super Slinger. What a classic diner treat. Hamburger patty, eggs, smothered in chili and topped with diced green peppers and white onion. He joked that he'd probably have heartburn, but it is always worth it.   The coffee was diner strong and the service was down-home diner friendly. Ambiance is stuck in a time warp and that is all part of the charm of this tiny diner.   I'll be back? - Gotta try a burger  When: March 20, 2019 Why: Breakfast

I can't shop or go to the new Apple store without a Frappucino after-wards. It's just one of my unwritten rules. It's a refreshing treat to celebrate a new purchase or resisting the urge to make a new purchase.   I like the new store location over the old kiosk version. However, I disagree with John H., I think the line moves slower. Perhaps my line was longer then his, because they were moving slow. I found it odd that two associates were taking orders and only one making all our drinks. I may be crazy, but wouldn't the line moved faster if two were making the drinks?  We all know the baked goods are shipped in to each Starbucks. There are no Kebbler elves in the back stockroom baking. Even though they are shipped in, I love the petite vanilla bean scones.   Staff is always friendly and pleasant. They should be, Starkbucks treats their employees very well with benefits and $.

Going to make this review short and direct. I like this Target because it has a liquor department and the Target near my home does not. I am so jealous that a county Target has something my city Target does not. The county Target may have booze, but I will still remain a city resident.

This is my go to place for Chinese carry out when I am at work. It is a convenient location to get in and out of without any trouble. I work so close, that when I walk in the door to pick my phone order up, it is coming out of the wok. Making it so hot and fresh.   I love their fried rice, beef is my favorite. A half order is big enough for me to have two lunches. My lunch yesterday, I wish I would have taken a photo of the crab Rangoon, it was picture perfect and so was the taste. They by far make the best fast Chinese Crab Rangoon I have ever had and I think it may even beat PF Chang's.   The two Chinese carry out joints near home, have disappointed us recently. I am thinking the next time we have the craving at home, I will drive the extra distance for Park Chop Suey.

Broussard's was one of my many Happy Hours that I participated in on a Friday night in the French Quarter. Before my arrival in NOL, I posted to the Talk Thread on Yelp asking for recommendations and the Chicken Biscuit and Ramos Gin Fizz here at Broussard's came up more then once.   I normally always sit at the bar, so it just came naturally to me to do it here for Happy Hour. It was impressive that I still experienced the same white linen treatment that I would have gotten at one of their many tables.   Dean was working the bar and doing a great job. I was entertained watching him masterfully making cocktails for servers and others sitting at the bar. When I ordered my Ramos Gin Fizz, he informed me that it was more of a dessert cocktail. I told him that I still wanted it, because it came highly recommended.  He was absolutely right, but I am still glad I experienced it.   The RGF is made with Gordon's Gin (not my favorite Gin), Triple Sec, Powdered Sugar, Half & Half, Lemon Juice, Egg Whites and Soda Water. As you can see, a drink with powdered sugar, H&H and egg whites definitely makes for a dessert cocktail. For me the Gin and Triple Sec, toned down the powdered sugar, but it still made for a rich and creamy drink. Next time I have one of these, I'll request a better Gin and I'll enjoy it after an amazing meal.   If Chick-fil-A served a chicken biscuit like the one here at Broussard's, I'd be a dedicated fan. Here, it's just not a "biscuit"; it's a Sweet Potato Biscuit.  Combining that with the Red Chili Glazed Fried Chicken, you have one tasty biscuit sandwich.  What made it even better is that it was topped with my favorite cheese, Pepper Jack. Also, the Pineapple Citrus Slaw garnish gave it some extra zing.   Would I come back? Next time I'm in the Quarter, I'll be here.   When: August 26, 2016 Why: Best Happy Hour Tour of the French Quarter

I hate Walmart, so giving a store I hate 3 Stars is probably like a normal shopper giving them 5 Stars. The store is super clean, but it's not even a month old yet. I hope they can maintain the cleanliness, because that is one of the details that turns me away from shopping at Walmart when I need too. Also, I find the merchandising to be bland and done with no creativity.   I liked that they had "store map" at the front entrance, so it was easy for me to maneuver to the departments that I needed to shop. However, I wish they had arrows on the floor like IKEA, because I got deeper into the store then I wanted to be. I finally found my way back to the front of the store and found a cashier ready to take my cash. She was very robotic, no personalization to her service. Hope my dollars spent aren't going to help Kroenke build a stadium in LA.  It frustrates me when manufacturers make particular items only available to certain retailers. When that happens, it forces shoppers like me to enter hell holes like Wal-Mart to purchase that particular item. Then it pisses the hell out of me when they are sold out and it was a limited supply.   Best thing about this store was the 50¢ soda machines outside the entrance. I give them 3 Stars, 1 for each machine. They had my favorite, Coke as well as; Pepsi and Dr. Pepper. If they had a container to recycle the cans it might have gotten them a 4th star. No, not really, 3 is the best this store can do.

What a great bar!   It has everything you'd want.   1) Dimly lit. 2) Dive bar atmosphere 3) Well stocked bar and masterfully made cocktails 4) Outlets, USB ports and hooks under the bar 5) Friendly Bartenders  6) Diverse Crowd 7) Free shot at 10 PM compliments of, The Party.   The night I stopped by was their first and last night of karaoke. To be honest, none of the performers could carry a note. They all admitted it, but they still sang their hearts out and had fun. Best of all, the crowd cheered and applauded their performances.   It's so sad that the Cherokee District is losing this great bar, its last day of business will be the 18th. If you can go before this Saturday, I urge you to go and experience the fun of Propaganda.

Love a good cocktail? You'll love Intoxicology, because a good cocktail needs good liquor and good ingredients.   Intoxicology may be a chic little booze boutique in the trendy, Grove neighborhood, but their liquor pricing is very competitive. I was immediately impressed with the variety of brands they offered in such a small space. I was pleased to see that a local shop was offering and showcasing local distilleries. Local supporting local is always a win-win.   In addition to quality liquor, they offer vintage bar and glassware. They also offer a small selection of books about the art of mixology. I had to purchase the one about my favorite classic cocktail, The Manhattan. It was titled; Manhattan: Story of the First Modern Cocktail. Such a good read, with a Manhattan served up at my side.   Will I return? - I love, a good Manhattan  When: November 28, 2017 Why: It's that time of year.

I've found another "thrill" on "The Hill".  We just blindly headed down to The Hill for lunch and an afternoon of exploring. As we were about to enter another eating establishment we saw Milo's and I quickly checked their star rating on Yelp. Having 4 stars we diverted from our original path and crossed the street to a new adventure.   Being a beautiful autumn day we took advantage and enjoyed our lunch on their huge patio. Being a Monday at lunchtime, no one was playing bocce ball, but it was cool seeing their huge court for playing the sport. I want to come back sometime when the game is being played to see how and what all the excitement is about.   Our lunch started off with Grilled Chicken Wings. They were an nice change from the traditional fried wings you find at most bar & grills. Milo's offers both and I highly recommend paying the extra 80¢ to enjoy them grilled. You'll have the same hot spicy flavor, with grill marks.   I took advantage of the daily special which was a Fried Grouper Sandwich served with Sweet Potato Fries. It was a large thin piece of Grouper with a light breading and served on a toasted bun from Fazio's Bakery. These Sweet Potato Fries are head and shoulders above the quality you get a Pappy's. I appreciated their size, almost a small steak fry, not the normal shoestring or waffle that I normally find  when ordering SP fries.   The SO enjoyed the Milo's Special which is a huge sandwich, so big that half of it went home. It too to served on fresh bread from Fazio's and filled with Roast Beef, Ham, Salami, Provel, Onion, Pickle, Lettuce, Tomato and drizzled with Vinegar & Oil Dressing. You can have it served hot or cold and the SO went hot.    They serve their "special" with a bag of chips, but the SO said we could take those home so I can have them in my next brown bag lunch for work and he ordered a regular order of fries. I will tell you, these were crispy delights. They were so good, I am considering creating a list for French Fries.   The wait staff was attentive and fun. I know they can not control the breezes, but be aware smoking is allowed on the patio  and smoke can be blown your way. The bag of chips I mentioned earlier, never made it to my brown bag lunch. They were enjoyed with the portion of the Milo's Special that went home with us.

In the past if you mentioned pizza and vegetarian in the same sentence, I would have looked at you as if you were crazy. By in the past, I mean before  April 14, 2016. Now, I totally get it. The pizza at Pizzeoli, it truly top notch and worthy of a spot on my Yelp List - Pizza with Pizzazz.   When it was announced that the April gathering of ISC (International Supper Club) was going to meet at Pizzeoli, I rolled my eyes. I love my group of ISC diners, so I put my diet aside and my distaste for vegetarian pizza. Besides, Ian had them on his STL 100 and said i "must order" the Bianca.   My Bianca was a wonderful choice. It has no tomato sauce, instead it is Béchamel Sauce with extra virgin olive oil, fresh mozzarella, garlic, rosemary and parmesan. With it being wood fired it had the perfect amount of char on the outer crust. I never knew a pizza without meat could taste so good.   The surprise and most popular pizza of the night was the nightly special - Brussel Sprouts. We all wanted to try it, but were hesitant to try it as our only pizza. So Sarah S. treated us all to one & we got to experience a slice. Once I tried it - I wish I had ordered one entire pizza for myself. It too was, Béchamel Sauce, mozzarella, garlic and then roasted brussel sprouts on top. It was pure heaven! As we were leaving we told the owner - he had to add it to the regular menu. If it's on the menu when you visit, order it - I guarantee you'll love it.   Our server, Kevin was a real trooper. Taking care of 9 diners all with separate checks is no easy task and he did it like a champion.   I'll be back, hopefully for another Brussel Sprouts pizza.   When: April 14, 2016 Why: International Supper Club

I told you I'd be back. Today I cam back and tried the Lamb Burger and it was amazing. I love lamb chops, leg of lamb and now I love lamb burgers. 5 Star serves up a fresh ground lamb burger and tops it with black olive tapenade and fried pickles. On the side they give you chunky tzatziki. My first bite I did not add the tzatziki and the burger was very good. The next bite I added the tzatziki and the burger instantly became exceptional.    Again, we started our lunch with an order of Fried Pickles. They were good, but they didn't seem to be as good as our first visit. The SO is so in love wit the Dad's Green Chile Cheeseburger, that he went with it again and was as pleased as he was the first time. To expand our experience at 5 Star, we shared a small order of their Natural Cut Fries and an order of Onion Rings. Their fries are a winner, but both of were disappointed in the quality of the rings. They were just Plain Jane.   Last time I had the Salted Caramel Shake, so today I tried the Strawberry. The Salted Caramel is by far the best. The strawberry did not match in quality and reminded of an upscale Steak-n-Shake shake.   A couple of disappointments, but not enough to remove a star. I will return again, because the Bison Burger is calling my name.

Stellar experience. I went last night for my second night out for Clayton Restaurant Week. I dined early, which to my surprise ended up being a double win. I was able to combine the CRW Menu with their Happy Hour Menu, creating an fuller dining experience. I even ordered a  side dish of Brussels Sprouts off the regular menu, that made my tummy very happy.  I made my reservation on-line at Open Table, stating in the special notes area, that I was a single diner and sitting me at the bar would be acceptable. When I arrived, the hostess offered me one of the charming little booths for two in the bar area. I graciously declined, selecting a  stool at the end of the bar. Perks of bar sitting; blue placemats with matching linen napkins and purse hooks under the bar for the ladies. (they hold messenger & backpacks, too)   Since my visit was based on a special menu for Clayton Restaurant Week, here's the break down on what I selected from the special menu.   Wedge Salad - Simple, a wedge of iceberg lettuce topped with Louis Dressing. I loved the dressing. I could of had Clam Chowder, but I passed on it, even though it was the recommendation of the bartender.  New Bedford Sea Scallops - Seared (three large scallops), served with Roasted Butternut Squash Puree, Oyster Mushrooms, Bacon Lardons, and Cranberry Chutney. This entree was a true winner and will be added to Sea Scallops List here on Yelp.   Chocolate Mousse - It was chocolate, enough said. Plus, it was topped with a sauce made from one of my favorite fruits.   To round things out, I enjoyed a Crab Rangoon and a Fish Taco from the Happy Hour menu. The fish taco was topped with; red onion, jalapeño, salsa and sour cream. The jalapeño made the taco for me, but I am a BIG jalapeño fan. The Crab Rangoon was a true Crab Rangoon, so good, you'll never order CR from a fast food Chinese restaurant again.   Being a fan fan of Brussels Sprouts, I had to have a half order from their regular menu. I was in heaven - they were equally as good as the ones served across the street at their sister restaurant 801 Chop. If I ordered a full order, I could make it a meal.   I had great service at the bar. My bartender was charming, friendly and very attentive. Various other servers brought me my food and each of them were equally as professional. Top class service.   Would I come back? Yes, CRW has introduced me to a great seafood restaurant.   When: January 24, 2017 Why: Clayton Restaurant Week

What a pleasant surprise. I can not tell how many times I have passed Las Palmas by and never gave them a second thought. The other night I was craving Mexican, before a very exclusive elite event at Pie O'My.  My time was limited so I stopped in for a quick dinner at Las Palmas. In just one visit, I can tell you I am already a fan.   Their salsa served with the chips has a nice spicy bite to it and our basket of chips were warm. Warm chips are always a nice touch. It was Happy Hour, so how could I say no to a Margarita with no salt?  It was refreshing, but I agree with Christie S. it could of  been a little stronger.   When experiencing a Mexican restaurant for the first time, I usually go with a combination plate so I can try a couple different things. Tonight a did a soft chicken taco and a beef burrito. They were served with cilantro rice and re-fried beans.  I was impressed that the burrito was shredded beef  and not the typical ground beef.  It was stuffed pretty full and the meat was tenderer then some BBQ places that serve shredded beef. The chicken taco,  was  garnished with lettuce and tomato. The chicken was seasoned well enough, that I did not need to add any salsa for flavor.   The sides were very impressive for me. I am not a fan of cilantro and their cilantro rice won me over. It was moist and the cilantro flavoring was not overpowering. It was light and refreshing. I liked the fact that the beans was a mixture of whole beans and smashed beans. So many places serve up re-fried beans that look like brown mashed potatoes.  They were great as a dip with the extra chips we had left in our basket.   The service was great. They were doing the typical team service that you see at many of the Mexican restaurants. One of the other male servers, just stopped by to make sure every thing was to our satisfaction.   When I am craving inexpensive Mexican, I'll drive to Maplewood to satisfy my fix and I three Mexican restaurants that I can walk to from my house. So what does that tell you?

Every so often, it is good to update the reviews of some of your favorite haunts. The Mack is close to my home, making it easy to grab a great char-grilled burger. Yesterday I stopped for a quick lunch and enjoyed a Four Cheese Burger. Did you hear that, Jack? Four Cheese! That kinda puts your Ultimate Cheeseburger to shame. My burger was char-grilled to a perfect medium rare and topped with cheddar, pepper jack, provel and american cheese. I paid the additional $1 and upgraded from regular fries to Criss-Cross Fries aka Waffle Fries.   In addition to great burgers, they offer up an amazing grilled chicken and steak sandwich as well. They also offer a large variety of craft beers on draught and in bottle. The atmosphere is a relaxed smoke-free neighborhood bar.

Another great Beer Dinner at Bigelo's! I love these events, this is the 4th one I have attended.  They are so much fun. A great way to see and learn the art of pairing foods with specific beers.   This dinner was with local micro brewery, Perennial Artisan Ales Beer.  Cory King, the Brew Master of Perennial was present to explain each of the brews that were paired with the foods from Bigelo.   These are the pairings we experienced:  Ceviche Style Crab Salad, Corn Cake Beer: Saison DE Lis  Merguez Slider, with caramelized onion and harissa mayo with creamy yogurt slaw. Beer: Hommel  Rensing Farms Baby Back Ribs with Mole BBQ Sauce and Mashed Sweet Potatoes Beer: Abraxas  Dessert: A custard type custard pie with rhubarb on top and a graham, walnut crust. Beer: Black Walnut Dunkel  Stands out for this dinner were the Merguez Sliders and the Baby Back Ribs. The ribs truly were finger licking good. The sliders were a blend of  two of my favorite meats; lamb and beef making  me wanting a second slider. We'll be going back for both of these delightful entrees.   The only miss was the creamy yogurt slaw. I've had better from the deli counter at a grocery store and we all know what they are like.   Overall, the Beer Dinners are always A+. You'll  always experience good food and great micro brewery beer. The servers are attentive, witty and make sure all in attendance have fun. It is always so cool to see familiar faces from previous dinners in attendance. Keep in mind these dinners sell out fast, so I suggest you watch Bigelo's website for the next one and order your tickets fast. I will be there too in my usual seat.

Oh, sweet baby Jesus. It's beginning to look a lot like Christmas and It's a Wonderful Life. If you are not in the Christmas spirit when you leave here, you definitely are a Scrooge. This is the place to be seen this holiday season.   The ambiance creates a fun filled atmosphere. This pop-up bar is decorated in trailer park tacky, but I LOVE it! Just like an ugly sweater party, it adds to the fun. They even have a section of the bar decorated for Hanukah.   Their specialty cocktails were all $12 and have cute holiday themed names. In addition to the cocktails, they created a special snacks menu ranging in price from $5 - $7. My personal favorite was the Lumps of Coal, a perfect snack for a naught boy. It was Oreo infused Rice Krispie treats.   The staff is bubbly and they make sure everyone is having a good time. You definitely come here to celebrate the season and have some good cheer.   Would I come back? If they continue to pop-up, I'll continue to come back.   When: December 13, 2016 Why: It's a Pop-UP Limited time open

This place is amazing! The selection is over whelming,  I felt like a child in a candy store. Once I got my focus, it was a great shopping experience.   If anyone needs new drawer pull, or any type of decorative hardware this is the only store in town to shop. They offer the best lines and some of the most creative.   The sales professionals are truly that, "professional". They listen to your needs and wants and guide you to fulfill your dreams.

Time for another update and this time John is being bumped up to 4 Stars. They are easily my co-workers choice, when it has  been designated donut day. Our favorites are the Chocolate Long John and the Glazed Buttermilk. Both are scrumptious. Our dozen is usually 6 of each.   Other donuts that you'll find in our box on occasion are; Cinnamon Twist, Apple Fritter, Cinnamon Roll and a traditional Glazed or Sugar donut. Depending on who is working, you may even see a Jelly Donut in our box.   The donuts are always super fresh. If you need coffee, I'll warn you, this is not Starbucks. John serves up a good strong cup of black coffee, the way it should be drank.   The staff is friendly. They remember their regulars and welcome new customers as if they were regulars.   I'd give John 5 Stars, but they're closed on Sunday and sometimes we really need donuts on Sunday morning. Otherwise, they are top-notch donuts.   Would I return? - I do every week.   When: I'm usually there Friday or Saturday Why: Keep my co-workers happy.

I was Saturday sometime between breakfast and lunch. I wasn't eating, but I still wanted a Bloody Mary. By chance I stopped by Cafe Lafitte and was totally blown away with the Bloody Mary they served up. Being a dive bar, I was expecting vodka and some bland BM mixer. I was totally wrong. I got a strong pouring of vodka, a spicy BM mixer and enough garnishment to snack on and satisfy me until I decided what I wanted to do for lunch.   I love Bloody Mary's so much, that I have a list dedicated to them here on Yelp. I consider this to be one of the best. It may be a dive gay bar, but it's Bloody Mary is better then some upscale restaurants. My one picture is now the wallpaper on my smartphone.   Great service too, the bartender let me use the outlet behind the bar to charge my phone.   When: August 27, 2016 Why: Steven needed a Bloody Mary

Several months ago I attended a UYE that introduced me to the addicting sandwich, "St. Paul". Ever since that UYE, I have been on a mission to experience a St. Paul at as many Chinese restaurants that I can. When ordering, I always get the Chicken. According to my pushers, Tracy and Jessica the chicken taste just like a Chick-Fil-A and they are right.   If you look a St. Paul Sandwich up on the Internet, you'll discover that it is a Saint Louis thing, just like provel and toasted ravioli. You'll also discover that Park Chop Suey is credited as being the creator of the now famous St. Paul Sandwich.  http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Paul_sandwich  Today I had an Egg Roll that was flaky, crisp and full of flavor. It was so good, that I did not need to add any Soy Sauce. As usual, their Crab Rangoon blows the doors off. They by far make the best of any fast or fine dinning Chinese restaurants in the city or county.  However, they missed the mark on the sandwich they are credited with creating. The bread was not fresh, however the meat of the sandwich was a trend setter.   Park Chop Suey, I wish you were closer to my home, but at least I have you close to work when I crave Chinese.

I'm late, I'm late, for a very important date. Last night was a meeting of the International Supper Club and Siri my new assistant got the start time wrong. I arrived fashionably late, really late. Like an entire hour late. However, Lindsay and the kitchen were rock stars and got our food out on time with the rest of our large party.   We immediately started our night off with Peroni, a nice chilled Italian beer served in a pilsner glass. Our Peroni was quickly followed by Baked Goat Cheese, with Marinara and fried pita bread. Goat Cheese always makes me happy, this was a winner.   My House Salad ($4) was not included with my pasta entree and next time I will take a pass, it did not impress me. Unlike the SO, my salad barely had any dressing on it at all, perhaps they double dressed his and missed mine. Also, the artichoke in mine was tough and had to be politely removed from my mouth.  I enjoyed the Pasta Alla with a Marinara sauce that included zucchini, red pepper, red onion and portabella. As a bonus, when it arrived at my table it also had yellow summer squash as well. The noodles were done to perfection. It was good, but seeing some of the other dishes pass by I'll be having a pasta with meat next time.   The SO ordered the Cioppino, a fish stew and had issue with the clams. He shared one with me knowing my love of clams, but did not tell me I was testing quality control until it was in my mouth. Luckily mine was good and I did not have to remove it like the artichoke. He said, he would not reorder the Cioppino on our next visit.   Service was great, our party was 10 and a party of 16 was seated next to us and the servers working both groups were doing a kick ass job. My only negative about Anthonino's Taverna is the acoustics. With an original tin ceiling and  vast open space it is understandable, so I will give them some leeway.   I'm not firing Siri for making us late, but it defiantly will noted in her personnel file.

I'll take a King over a clown any day.   New Burger King with a very contemporary style giving an upscale ambiance feel to fast food. I've always been a fan of their "flame broiled" burgers over the clown who fries them on a grill. However, this visit today was coffee and breakfast. I enjoyed a Sausage and Egg Croissant with cheese. It was a nice change from the typical biscuit that so many fast food joints offer. As they were preparing my breakfast sandwich, I noticed they now carry Cinnabon's. Making that discovery was a BIG mistake, but not as big as you'd think.  I will admit I have always enjoyed a hot and fresh Cinnabon, but always cringed at the size and cost.  When you see them at the mall, they are HUGE and the price is not right. Here at BK you can satisfy the Cinnabon craving at a fraction of the cost and size. Theirs has the same great taste,  smaller in size and more manageable price.   I've got to go back and play with their high tech soda machine, it looked like something out of a space-age movie.  The staff was friendly and awake considering the fact that I was there in the very early AM. Close enough to work, so I will be making a return visit.

My favorite place to celebrate birthday or anniversaries. The service is very attentive, they make all guest fell like royalty. My personal favorites are the Pepper Fillet or Pepper Strip (can you tell I like Pepper). However, they have some of the best Prime Rib I have ever experienced. Bake Potatoes are huge, for an extra $1 you can make it "Sweet" and it's worth every penny. Asparagus is one of my favorite vegetables and I highly recommend getting a side of this green treat. May be a few extra $'s but the experience and food are worth it!

It's not Christmas without a trip to Intoxicology. When the majority of the people you buy gifts for are cocktail snobs, this is the place to find the absolute perfect gift.   Intoxicology has some of the best premium liquors and mixers.  Today I was shopping for bitters to complete a whiskey gift box I was creating. Oh, my they had so many for me to choose from. They even had small gift box of multiple samples to give the recipient variety. If your not the creative type, or just want things simple and done for you, they had pre-made gift boxes. Which makes gift giving, easy-peasy.   I admit, I am a garnish snob. If I'm drinking a premium liquor in a craft cocktail, I want a garnish to be of the same quality and Intoxicology has what I need. They've got the dark cherries for my Manhattans and olives for my Dirty Martini.   The gentleman woking is always friendly and makes shopping in his shop a pleasant experience. That is why I enjoy shopping local and supporting a small business.   When: December 4, 2020 Why: Holiday Gifts

Awesome! We rented the penthouse for a bridal happy hour shower and it was the perfect event space for our thirty guest. Having a full kitchen, island and huge dining table gave us plenty of service space for all the booze and food. The large living room was roomy and allowed all the guest to gather around as the bride opened all her gifts.   The penthouse also has two bedrooms each with its own bathroom and a laundry room. Everyone joked how they could live here. It truly is that homey and comfortable.  A true highlight was huge and I do mean huge balcony with a view of the majestic Mississippi river. A gas grill and two dining tables on the balcony would be perfect for a 4th of July party to view the fireworks.   After the BHHS, a select group of the ladies spent the night and loved it.  This is a hidden gem in the Alton area. If you need a B &B in the Riverbend area, I highly recommend the Alton Cracker Factory.   I'll be back? - If the opportunity arises & highly recommend.   When: April 28, 2019 Why: Bridal Shower in Penthouse

3 is my luck number and evidently it is Laurie's Shoes too. Why you ask, because every time I shop here I walk out with 3 pairs of shoes.  I use to buy my shoes at one of those "warehouse" type stores where you wait on yourself, until I went to Laurie's with a friend. I was just tagging along, so I thought. I was amazed at the customer service and knowledge that the sales staff had about selecting the right size and fit. My feet have never felt better.  I've become addicted, all my shoes have now been from Laurie's. They've provided me with dress, work, casual loafers and even a pair of Reef Flip-Flops that have a bottle opener in the sole. Which has proved to be very handy at summer BBQ's.  Next time you need shoes, I highly recommend visiting Laurie's and seeing if you become as hooked as I have.

#curbside #togo #pandemic  Nailed it!   Let's be honest, yes I would have rather been sitting at the bar with a Margarita enjoying my chips, hot salsa with a side of queso. However, taking my carry-out order home and enjoying it with a classic episode of Law & Order was just as enjoyable and delicious. The carry-out Margarita, surprised me. It had the same refreshing taste, as if it had just been shaken behind the bar. Of course, I gave mine a good stir before pouring it over ice at home.   I also enjoyed two of my favorite tacos, Hot Chicken and Baja Grilled Fish. When I saw that the to-go vessel held three tacos, I felt guilty not ordering a Portobello as well. My ride home is approximately 5 miles. The tacos were still as warm as, if they were carried out from the kitchen and placed in front of me at the bar.   The process of ordering on-line was simple. I was out running errands and decided I wanted Mexican for lunch. So I drove over to Soulard, parked and ordered on my iPhone. After completing my order they gave me approximate time it would be ready and when it was being bagged up, they sent me a text message telling me it was ready. So easy and well organized.   To make it safe for everyone they have signage up encouraging everyone to stand 6 feet apart while waiting for you order. They even took it a step further and have marking on the sidewalk for those who do not know the difference between 6 inches and 6 feet.   Will I return? - Hell, yes. Curb-Side or Dine-In   When: May 8, 2020 Why: I worked Cinco De Mayo and needed Tacos.

I am so lucky. I pretty much live smack dab in the middle of both of the Misson Taco Joints. So which ever direction I back out of my garage, I'm pointed in the direction of a MTJ. I couldn't ask for a better GPS and today it just happens to lead me to my 800th Yelp Review.   Our first couple of visits to the new Soulard location were a little bumpy which can be expected when a "joint" is opening with new staff in both the front and back of the house. On our most recent visit, it seems that everyone is now broken in and bringing  their A-Game to the table.   Soulard is serving up the same high quality tacos, burritos, street corn and Margaritas that I have grown to love over in The Loop. However, after drinking a Mission Paloma here in Soulard, I may never drink another Margarita again. The Mission Paloma may be my new regular drink at MTJ. It's reposado tequila, agave nectar, grapefruit beer, served in a salted rim pint glass. It kinda was a Moscow Mule with a Mexican twist and I loved it.   Eric was an excellent server, he gets bonus points for leading me to the MP. He may be my go to waiter when dining at the Soulard MTJ. I'll be back soon, it just depends which direction I back out of my garage.

There is nothing special about Lemmons. It is just a typical south city bar with food, that blends right in with all the others. I will give them kudos for the clean, sleek, modern and minimalist decor. Again, I'd like to give 3 1/2 stars, but Yelp has not come up with a half star system yet.   The best thing that I've had on the menu is their Chicken Wings. They're Applewood Smoked and have a Rakija Glaze. They are very flavorful on their own, so I saw no need to dip them in the Smokey Ranch Dip. It was a nice touch that they provided paper napkins and wet naps with the wings.   Sandwiches, that I have tried are; 50/50 Burger and the Crab Burger.  I'm a big fan of Crab, but I do not recommend this sandwich. It was bland and flavorless. The 50/50 is a different twist on a typical pub burger with an egg on top. It's 50% beef and the other 50 is beef bacon.  I question beef bacon and the server could not explain it, either. Has me scratching my head.   Either way you get your fries, the regular or Chip Twister they are a winner. Not being a fan of bottled ketchup in a restaurant, I am pleased that they serve theirs in little cups.   Cocktails are good. I've enjoyed a Tennessee Mule in a pewter mug and a Cardinal Sin which is very refreshing. The cardinal is a blend of vodka and tequila, with orange and cranberry juice.   I've eaten here several times. I've dined alone, with a friend and with a large group. Each time, the service has been friendly and attentive. One of the reasons for the 3 Stars is that on my last visit, one of the young lady servers kept ripping on the bartender in Bosnian. I don't speak it, but by her tone and attitude, his reaction, she was not being a professional or a lady. It made the bar atmosphere uncomfortable when she approached.   Will I return: For more wings.   When: Multiple Visits Why: Lunch, Dinner & Group Dinning

Today was my first day shopping at this Aldi and I can already tell you it will not be the last. I was amazed at the produce selection and the low prices. The variety may have been smaller then other major stores, but the quality is the same. So, I'll save $'s and buy some of my produce here.  Aldi's is also a good place to stock your pantry with daily staples, or buy the basics for party. Once the unknown brand of roasted peanuts are poured in bowl, no one will know they are not Fisher's or Planters. The same will stand true for those tortilla chips and salsa. I also like their selection and prices on cheese and who can beat a dozen eggs for $1.59.   Store is clean and the staff is friendly and helpful, making this a good place to shop for groceries. So the next time you get a circular in the mail for Aldi's, check it out before throwing it in to the recycling. You will be surprised at what they offer and the prices.

Love me some MTJ tacos. However, my recent visit for lunch I went with a burrito and was totally surprised. I was not only surprised by the amazing flavor, but by it's HUGE size. It totally could handle a hungry man, or feed two if they shared an appetizer.   My festive lunch begun with a Margarita. MTJ serves their in a salt rimmed pint. It's made with Blanco tequila, agave nectar, lime juice and dry orange curaçao. Then it is hand shaken. You wont find those pre-mixes here at MTJ, it's all fresh and that makes for a better Margarita.   Normally, I always start out with their Chips & Salsa. Some people complain that you have to pay $4 for them, but to those folks, I say, get over yourself. They are totally worth it. However, today I kicked my appetizer up a notch and ordered the Wild Mushroom Empanadas. The blend of roasted wild mushrooms with poblano peppers, goat cheese and other ingredients made me wonder why it took me so long to try them. Perhaps next time I'll have my chips & salsa and the empanadas as my entree.   Thinking about going Vegan, so when I saw the New Years Resolution burrito, I thought I'd give it a try. A whole wheat tortilla stuffed with; portobello mushroom, black beans, vegetable quinoa, crispy onion and jalapeño salsa. I didn't even miss the meat, it was that good. As I stated earlier, it was HUGE. I ended up taking half of it home. I scrapped the insides out at home and added it to a frittata.
