Now the true reason I bumped MTJ up a star is my second Margarita. For once, I read further down the list of cocktails and saw the description of custom made Margaritas. One that they suggested was; Spicy Jalapeño. Those of you that truly know me, know I love jalapeños. OMG! Slices of fresh jalapeño in a Mexican drink that I already love? Yes, it was love at first sip. I loved it so much, I took to my twitter handle singing its praises.   Will I come back? - That is a dumb question. Hell yes, I'll be back.   When: October 23, 2017 Why: Lunch

It's only been two days and I am already upping my score for Nathaniel. I will be honest and tell you, I am a macaroon snob. I am such a macaroon snob, that I have not found any in the city of STL to meet my high standards. Lucky for me, where I work every day someone is in Chicago and when I crave macaroons, I have them brought in from my favorite bakery in the Windy City. I may not like the Cubs, but I do like the macaroons from Chicago.   So the other day when I was having my first experience at NRB, I saw the amazing display of macaroons. All I could think about for the next day was, wonder if they'll live up to my expectations? I was so scared, I wanted to try them, but I was afraid that if I didn't like them, that it would taint my opinion of NRB and I didn't want that to happen. I built up the courage and returned to give them a try. I made a strong promise to myself before entering. I told myself, that if they didn't make my sweet tooth ache with joy, that I would keep it to myself and no-one would be any wiser.   I'm happy to report that it was love at first bite. I will no longer will have to have my macaroons brought to me by co-workers via a trip to Chicago. I will now be an independent man and will drive over to Kirkwood and pick them up myself.   Nathaniel, thank-you for bringing quality macaroons to the St. Louis area.   When: September 21, 2016 Why: Macaroons

I use to live in STL and was a regular customer of their flagship store on Park Avenue for 10 years. So when I knew I was moving to the IL side of the river, I was glad to know they had a store in Edwardsville to fulfill my fur-babies needs.   The E-ville store is a lot smaller, but with strategic rack placement and creative merchandising, they get everything to fit perfectly. It's taken me awhile, but I now know where all my regular items are located. I could have been blindfolded in STL and would still find what I needed, I was there that often. Now that I do not live or work as close to one of their shops, I have to plan my trips.  When I do shop, I really stock up on treats and buy a larger bag of dry food.   If you're particular about what you feed your four legged children, the high quality selection here should meet your needs. I, myself, only feed my fur-babies food and treats that are made in the USA or Canada. I just feel safer that way. If you need help selecting a new brand, the staff is very knowledgeable in the products that they sell.   The staff is friendly and of course the store itself is dog friendly. Just be sure to have your baby on a leash and if you use an extender leash, make sure it is locked for the safety of all.   When: October 24, November 28, 2020 and January 9, 2021 Why: Fur-Babies gotta eat.

BLT's = Breakfast, Lunch and Taco's. I've already experienced their amazingly delicious breakfast. When it was time for National Margarita Day, I thought I'd check out their tacos.   I still came during breakfast hours, so I ordered one each of their breakfast tacos. My favorite was the Steak n' Egg. It was a corn tortilla filled with flank steak, pepper jack & cheddar cheese, onions, peppers and of course, eggs.  There was so such filling, they also need to double up on the tortilla wrap.   The other two tacos were equally as delicious. I'd say the Sunrise came in second for flavor. It had a filling of; eggs, bacon, avocado, roasted tomato salsa, pico de gallo. It was also served in a corn tortilla.   My last taco was the Chorizo n' Egg. It was the most simple of the three. A typical flour tortilla stuffed with; spicy chorizo, eggs, potato and white cheddar. It was good, but for my taste buds, it was definitely the bronze medal winner.   Of course, with it being National Margarita I had to have a Margarita. Ordering one so early in the morning took the bartender by surprise. Once I told him it was, NMD, he totally understood and made me one from scratch. I love it when I see and hear a shaker being used for a Margarita. Those that come straight from a bottle are nasty.   Friendly bartender, refreshing Margarita and overly stuffed taco were a great start to my celebration of National Margarita Day.   Chances of returning? - I see a UYE in the future.   When: February 22, 2019 Why: 1st Stop on National Margarita Day

It's National Taco Day on a Taco Tuesday and I'm at a Pizzeria. What is wrong with this picture? Absolutely, nothing. I got to enjoy some amazing Blazed Chicken Wings, a Deep Dish pizza and two Pi exclusive craft beers from local breweries.   As my usual, I'm dining alone, so I strategically place myself at the bar. I positioned myself in the middle, so I could easily read the taps on the two sets of draft pulls. Immediately I noticed that that two of the most popular local craft breweries in town had exclusives, just for Pi. Being a Schlafly fan, I started out with their Pi Common. I gave it a 3 on Untappd. It's a California Common style beer, with a ABV of 5%. It was refreshing, but the PiPA by 4 Hands was my favorite. It's a Pale Ale - American style beer, with a ABV of 5%. On Untappd, I gave it a 4.  A cold beer always goes well with wings and pizza, next time I will only order PiPA.   What makes their wings stand out above the other bar wings? They are dry-rubbed and oven baked. They're not fried and that is a big plus, for me. Being oven-baked, one bite and the meat fall off the bone. Even the carrots served on the side are oven roasted. I'm not a dipper with my wings, but here I am tempted. They serve up a yogurt-cucumber dressing, that is way more flavorful then typical Blu Cheese or Ranch. I do dip the carrots, but the dry rub seasoning on the wings is flavorful enough for me.   Ian Froeb has Pi on his STL 100 list and his "must order" is the; South Side Classico. How can you go wrong with a pizza covered in; berkshir sausage, mushrooms, green pepper, onion and mozzarella cheese. What? No, Provel? That's right, a STL pizza joint that doesn't use that weird cheese mixture. That is a wonderful thing.   Dining as a single diner, I had plenty of leftovers. It was nice to see, that their To-Go Vessels are eco-friendly. So, in addition to having a great meal, I have two lunches for work this week.   Would I return? Like Joan G., the chicken wings will bring me back every time.   When: October 4, 2016 Why: Pizza on National Taco Day

This is a poor excuse of a store for H&M. In my opinion it is the "red headed step child" of the chain. It has the poorest selection and variety of merchandise. Not to mention the worst customer service.    My visit last week had me wondering if Kennelwood had not been there and installed an invisible fence around the check out counter. While I shopped, the only two associates I saw, stayed behind the counter discussing their previous night dates in a volume that could be heard in the middle of the store. I approached to ask a question and was given a short quick answer, "no". They then went back to their conversation.  I then continued my shopping at another store in the mall.

The Village Bar opened in 1879. I moved to STL in 1979. It's 2018 and I finally made it here. I'm not one to rush into things, but now I'm kinda pissed off that I didn't come earlier.   TVB is known for their delicious burgers and onion rings. While dining the other folks at the bar told me the chicken wings are damn good, too. I could only eat so much, so I'll have to try the chicken wings on the next visit.   The burger is grill fried and you can see the grill from the bar. I went with a single patty, with Pepper Jack cheese. Before my burger, I enjoyed a half order of Onion Rings. Smart move on their marketing to offer two sizes, many times I will not order an extra side or appetizer due to the size. With my OR's I had a strong powered Vodka with Club Soda. The Rings were a variety of sizes (of course) and all were covered in a crispy and flakey batter. I'd say they are far better then, Seamus McDaniel's and they use to be my favorite OR in STL.   Logically I had to have an order of French Fries with my burger. They were crispy crisp and served with minimal salt. Which is a plus. I'd rather add salt and pepper to my liking. The burger was a true delight. I liked that I got to choose my favorite cheese, Pepper Jack instead of having to go with American or Cheddar. The only sides mine came with were onion and pickles cut lengthwise. The burger was a 1/4 lb ground chuck. According to the menu, it is all fresh and never frozen. That's how I like it.   The ambiance is dull and drab. It has a feeling of a dive bar or south city neighborhood bar and it's located in West County. There are plenty of TVs to watch and the music is loud, but not so loud that you cannot have a conversation with your friend.   I sat at the bar and the bartender was attentive to my needs. Always made sure there was vodka in my glass. Watching the servers, they were hustling and and having a fun time with the diners.   Will I return? - Gotta try the Chicken Wings  When: January 3, 2018 Why: Scoping it out for a UYE.

Love me some, Lion's Choice. It is a quick and easy fast food fix. The Roast Beef is always so tender and juicy. I like the fact that there actually is a little red tint to it.  Other fast food places, over cook their RB, leaving it dried out. The seasoning, also puts Lion's Choice above the others.  Speaking of their seasoning, it is now available for purchase in their restaurants. I've grabbed a couple of bottles to use as fill-in's for some of my holiday gifts. Spices/Seasonings are always great gifts for a foodie friend.   To accompany their sandwiches, their long thin fries are always hot and crisp. I use a combination of BBQ Sauce and Ketchup for dipping. For those who are fans of horseradish on their sandwich, Lion's Choice offers it as a condiment.   Other highlights, that set LC above that other fast food place that serves, "the meats" is crushed ice and soft serve ice cream cones. Oh, I don't want to forget to mention, Orange Freezes. Yummy!

Some times it pays off to be a single diner when going to one of the newest and hottest restaurants in town. That way you can sneak in without a reservation, sit at the bar and experience what some are waiting weeks to do with a reservation. That is exactly what I did.  I went on a Sunday night and was able to snag a single seat at the bar next to the wall. Yeah, it was a little cramped, but I was comfortable and it was a great spot to watch all the bar activity. Another advantage of sitting at the bar is service. With multiple bartenders working, those seated at the bar receive endless and attentive service. I'll say, the service was sensational and extremely friendly.   I'm normally a vodka man, but I started out with Cocktail #69 (giggle). I just had to see the Torched Rosemary garnish. I found the mix of whiskey, lemon & lime, Big O and egg to be a refreshing classic cocktail. It's one of those that you can sip, relax and totally enjoy.  I was wanting a light dinner, so I went with their Crispy Chicken Wings and a side of Roasted Cauliflower. Both dishes were top notch. The wings were simple, no messy sauce coating the wings. They were what they were called, Crispy Chicken Wings. They were served with a little cup of Chili Mustard Butter for dipping. Myself and the group next to me liked the wings so much, neither of us used the sauce that much. It was good, but the wings stood by myself as well.   So many popular restaurants are serving Brussel Sprouts, which I do love, but it was great to see Olive + Oak go in a different direction. O+O offers Roasted Cauliflower and Charred Broccoli. As stated, I ordered the Cauliflower and am looking forward to my return visit to try the Charred Broccoli. It is good to see more restaurants are offering vegetables as starter and side dishes. We all need that extra push to eat our veggies.   I closed out the night with a Cocktail #51. This one is made with vodka, my liquor of choice. It also had Rose infused Dolin Blanc and Lemon Bubbles. I don't want to sound sexist, but I should have known with a rosebud garnish, this drink would be more popular with the ladies. It was refreshing, but not a repeater.   I'm confident Olive+Oak is going to be a great place for Happy Hour and dinner with friends. I cannot wait to return and try the; Kale Salad, Blue Crab Gratin, Gnocchi with Lamb Ragu and the Seared Jumbo Sea Scallops. I'm also looking for someone to go and share the 34 oz Prime Cowboy Ribeye. Any low-carbers want to give it a go?   When: February 21, 2016 Why: Dinner and checking out the new hot restaurant

Farewell, Joanie. A friend organized a party at your Pizzeria, so we all could say good-bye. I had never been, so it was a first and last time for me.   Being on a diet, I didn't order pizza. I enjoyed a Caesar Salad and their house made dressing was top notch. I also had an order of Buffalo Wings, that was a special that evening. For pizzeria wings, they were pretty tasty.   Our server was accommodating and friendly. She said business had jumped up drastically, since the closure announcement. However, it's still too late to save the business.    It's sad to see a local business close, especially one who had been open as long as Joanie's. However, from my one visit, I could tell it hadn't changed much since it's opening and perhaps that was the downfall.   When: February 5, 2020 Why: Announced Closing

In my humble opinion, New Balance tennis shoes are the best. I've tried other brands, but I always come back to NB. I'm also a creature of habit and select the plain white on white walking shoe. To add a little pizzaz to my shoes I pick up some colorful laces to coordinate with my shirts.   Another reason I like getting my new NB's here, is the knowledgeable sales associates. They listen to my needs and measure my feet for the appropriate size. Today, I got lucky and the shoe I wanted was even on sale. I'll take that as a win.   My sales associate today, recommended inserts for my shoes. I was amazed at the difference they made my feet feel. Being one who is on his feet and does a lot of walking, I was sold. You can purchase NB at many of the supermarket or warehouse shoe stores, but the customer service here makes it worth the trip.   Will I return? Yes -   When: July 10, 2017 Why: New walking shoes

Simply said, "Winner, Winner Chicken Dinner".   CB has been doing some major marketing promoting their new, Southern Fried Chicken. They've done so much with billboards and television spots, that they pulled me in. If that wasn't enough, Sara W. had the ROTD here on Yelp two days ago. She sang the praises of this fried chicken dinner, so I knew I had to give it a try.   For a chain, this was a winning chicken dinner. The breading was seasoned well and extremely crisp. As I bite into each piece, the chicken was juicy. It was a true half chicken, consisting of; a breast, thigh, wing and leg. Only downside of my meal, is that my pieces were nowhere from the same chicken or even similar in size. My wing and leg were small and the breast and thigh were from a much larger chicken. My favorite pieces are the breast and thigh, so I was thrilled that they were on the bigger size.   To make my meal a true comfort food meal I choose, Green Beans and Mashed Potatoes. I like that CB let's you choose between brown or white gravy. With chicken, I always choose white. The green beans were seasoned well with bacon and just enough salt and pepper. That last thing to make this a true southern dinner, was my tall refreshing glass of iced tea.   The service at the table was true southern hospitality even here in the mid-west. It was attentive and my ice tea glass was never less then half full. Also, a trip to CB is not complete without a quick browse through their country store. I was so tempted, but controlled myself. However, I tell you, they have an amazing selection of Lodge Cast Iron.   My only negative, would be the cashier. She lacked southern charm. She even lacked basic customer service skills. She was downright rude. Since she was my last contact before exiting CB, they lost a star.   I'll be back? - Another, CB. I'm rarely in St. Charles.   When: August 23, 2019 Why: Southern Fried Chicken Dinner (Lunch)

On A Clear Day You Can See Forever. So jump into your car and head over to Union Station and ride The STL Wheel. It's a sweet ride.   My visit was a Thursday afternoon with my two cousins. It was a slow day, so our group of three was able to have our own gondola, that typically seats six. The gondolas are climate controlled and ours was toasty warm. I was also impressed with how clear/clean the glass windows were. It made taking pictures of the majestic views so easy.   The ride itself is smooth and easy. It' a slow ride and times you almost don't realize that you're actually moving. Typically, I am not a fan of heights, but being enclosed in the gondola, I was totally comfortable.   The staff assisting riders on and off The Wheel, were extremely friendly. The young man responsible for assisting us was a hoot. His smile was huge. Every time we passed him doing our rotations, he'd show us his big smile and give us a fun silly wave.   So, the next time you have out of town guest. You have two tourist attractions to take them "UP" in and show them the beauty of our city.   When: January 9, 2020 Why: Supporting my local tourist attraction.

I really wasn't that impressed. I admit, I only stopped by for a Hurricane and did not eat any food. The bar was very dark, had wood paneling and gave a warm feeling. I was expecting a true Hurricane glass, since I had read the story and understood how the name came about. Instead mine was served in a plastic tumbler like you'd get at a Saints football game for your beer.   The flavor of the actual Hurricane was just a glorified Hawaiian punch. It was also the weakest alcohol drink I had during my entire weekend in NOLA. With all the  social buzz and popularity of this drink, I was expecting to be blown away.   One positive note, I was able to sit along side a wall with a small rail for my drink and use an outlet to charge my phone. Also, it was very entertaining to watch a group of intoxicated men pick and organize their fantasy football teams. I saw more ass slapping then you'd see at a gay bar. They definitely were having a good time.   Next time I'm in NOLA, I'll return to eat, but no more Hurricanes for me. For any type of Hurricane, once is enough.   When: August 27, 2016 Why: Hurricane

It's still good after all these years.   I only use to get NDH when I was visiting family on this side of the river and we were parting in E-ville. Now that I live on this side of the might Mississippi River, I can get it whenever I want it.   Last night I had dinner in downtown Edwardsville, so I made sure to leave a little room in the tummy for dessert. My route back home, takes me right pass Northside, so I just had to stop. Typically, I always get the same thing, it's one of my true favorites. A twist cone made of their vanilla and famous homemade orange sherbet. However, tonight I went to my second favorite, an M&M Concrete. Many places use the mini M&M's, but not here. They use full-sized and when blended, it kinda makes a very light chocolate out of the vanilla as you get to the bottom of your cup. Keep in mind, the small here is still a good size and very filling.    I did not use it tonight, but for the first time I noticed their drive-up window. There's no fancy electronic ordering sign, you simply pull up to a small window on the side of the building and place your order. It's just as if you walked up to the front of the building, but you remain in your car. How super cool is that?  The service is has been consistently the same over all the years. The young ladies working seem to take pride in working at such a traditional ice cream  stop in E-ville.  I just discovered that today, August 14 is Creamsicle Day. I may have to go back and enjoy a twist cone to celebrate.  When: August 13, 2021 Why: The question is, Why, not?

Heating and Air Conditioning are things we all need to keep ourselves comfortable in this miserable Missouri weather.  To keep my heating & cooling equipment in tip top condition, I use Martin - Jetco.  I started out using M-J for my seasonal check-ups and when it was time to upgrade my system it was almost a no brainer. Even though I knew the end result, I still got other bids for both new heating and air conditioning. I was right, Martin - Jetco beat everyone hands down.   I love my new system, I've experienced both seasons and have been both toasty warm and chilly cool. Of course I have them come prior to every cooling/heating season to make sure everything is performing at its best.   Hometown biz, excellent customer service and quality work.

I was drug here while taking a friend around the neighborhood to run errands. I had not been here since my last visit back in 2015. I did not venture very deep into the store. We only shopped the grocery and meat department.   I will say that their prices were not that impressive on the staple items I checked. However, I will say that the meats looked good and the prices were similar to those that I see and pay at my Costco. The grocery area was clean and well maintained.   The check-out was a nightmare. It was just like all the stories I've heard. Only two cashiers working and both of them were working slow as molasses. I do not use self checkouts, but I was so tempted to do on this visit.   I'm not a Wal-Mart supporter. I'm not a fan of the Walton's or Stan Kroenke. If you are, this is was of the better stores. Just beware of the parking lot, it gets kind of crazy.

I've been a steady customer of their E-ville store for a year now and I can say the service and product offerings are as good as their flagship store in STL.   The variety of dry and moist foods for both canine and feline is impressive. If you're wanting to change up your fur-babies diet, talk with one of the sales associates and they'll be able to guide you to  one or more of their offerings.  They can even help you find the perfect bag of treats to make your best friend a happy snacker.   My dogs are so spoiled they have their own closet in between the kitchen and laundry room. It's filled with different bowls, leashes, collars, dry and moist food and a variety of treats. I'm pleased to say, it all came from Four Muddy Paws. They're the best when shopping for your best friend.

Disclaimer: The owner reached out to me after my initial review and treated me and coworkers to another pizza. He was truly concerned about the service we received and wanted to make things right.   I will say this time it was a drastic improvement. The service on the phone and delivery person were both polite and personable. The delivery was quick and the pizza was piping hot.   Now that we have made amends with Papa, he may not be in our house, but he has been in our office multiple times. For pizza downtown, it is quick, fresh and delivered fast.

When opening this great little diner, the owner was not concerned with; Location, Location, Location. He knew like in "Field of Dreams", if you open and provide quality food, "they will come".  This diner is off the beaten path in an industrial park area, but it served up an incredible breakfast with friendly and attentive service.   Today I had a heart stopping breakfast, that wasn't even the one on their menu called, "Heart Stopper". My entree, their Big Biscuit Breakfast was a platter filled with every breakfast treat that I love. It's foundation was a split flaky biscuit, topped with two thick hand pressed sausage patties, 2 eggs (mine were over easy), American cheese and covered in thick creamy country gravy. On the side they scooped up true home style fried potatoes. Hand cut, each was different like a snowflake and yet they were all "fried" to perfection. Each one crispy and seasoned with the right amount of pepper and salt.    Our waitress was glad to hear we discovered them on Yelp and encouraged us to come back telling us about their "All-You-Can-Eat" Sunday Dinner which is like going to Grandma's house. If they serve up dinner like they did our breakfast, I am sure it is amazing. I know I will be back for breakfast and I may check out the dinner too.

Close, convenient and cheap.   It is an open lot with no covered parking spaces, but if you choose the the entrance on the right and go straight there are some amazing white pine trees that provide shade for your ride.   The shuttle drivers are friendly and helpful. One member of our group of six forgot he had a pocketknife in his "pocket" when he arrived at the SW terminal to be dropped off. The driver took the pocketknife back to our travelers  SVU and slipped it into the wiper well. When we returned from our trip, the knife was there waiting to be reunited with its owner.   Arriving back to STL, we were picked up by an equally friendly driver and returned to our vehicles. The daily rate here is $8 and that is a deal. When I fly, this is where I park my ride.

Carondelet Diner has reopened its' doors with new owners and I am glad they are back. I enjoyed a Philly Omelet, that was grilled to a perfect golden yellow and was stuffed with thinly shaved Ribeye steak, onion and green peppers. It was the perfect breakfast for me or anyone else who is eating low-carb. The omelet was huge and very filling.   My dining partner enjoyed their Ultimate Breakfast, which was a manly breakfast.  It was two eggs your way, a choice of bacon or sausage (patty), hash browns and two pancakes.  I got a taste of the sausage and it was very flavorful. It had a nice peppery tang to it. The pancakes were HUGE and he could not finish them, but said they were very good. This breakfast is down-home and very filling.  Speaking to one of the owners, they are all about buying and using local vendors. All the meats they are using are from Kenrick's Meat Market, a great south county business. The ambiance is plain jane, but the service has a warm neighborhood feel. I almost felt as if I were eating at a neighbors kitchen table.   Look forward to coming back and checking out their lunches and daily specials.

I shop Walmart for one reason and one reason only and that is Dr. Scholl's Custom Fit Orthotic Center. I'm thankful I only have to buy them may-be two or three times a year.   There is no customer service here. Hopefully with the raises Wal-Mart is planning to give their employees will help change this.

Wow! What Penzeys is to spices Vom Fass is too oils, vinegars and liquors. You can find those hard to find ingredients for that special new recipe. That staff is very knowledgeable, friendly and will guide you through an amazing shopping experience.  You not only get to select your oils and vinegars, you select the container and size. When you got back for your next purchase (I know you'll go back) - take your empty container and have it refilled. How "green friendly" can you get.  Their liquors are amazing too. Treat your vodka and scotch friends to a small bottle of their amazing varieties - you'll become their BFF.

I have worn glasses or contact lenses since I was 10 years old. So I have had my share of eye examinations and I am here to tell you the best is Koetting Associates.   You will get the most extensive and thorough eye examination you have ever experienced. As you are being examined, you'll wonder why your previous doctor never did each of the test that KA completes on your eyes. Before you enter the examination room for your vision, you are taken to a separate room for approximately 8 different test.  These extra test, is what puts them ahead of the class. Being over 40 now and having monovision, I appreciate the extra time they take making sure my distance and closeup vision are both good.   The entire staff from Dr. Castellano to the receptionist are professional and personable. Thanks to their professionalism, I can see clearly now.

I can now say, "Been there, ate there." I will also say, it is very likely that I will not return. Like Ms. Hao, nothing WOW-ed us. It was "just ok", which for me is a step down from A-OK.   There were two of us dining and we had three entrees. The first one we shared as an appetizer and it was the Topped Sweet Cornbread. This is their creative version of Biscuits and Gravy.  They were nice enough to cover half of it with the Wild Mushroom Gravy and the other with Fennel Pork Sausage Gravy. It was nice to be able to taste both gravies. However, the cornbread was so sweet it dominated our tastebuds. The mix of sweet and savory did not blend together. The sweetness dominated the dish.   For our main (second) entree we each ordered a different Cornbread Benedict. I had the Sautéed Spinach and Avocado and my friend who loves Pork Belly had the Smoked Pork Belly. Each came with a side of Breakfast Potatoes, which were crisp cubes of potato with sautéed onion. I also think they did a good hollandaise sauce, but like the previous dish the cornbread over dominated and did not let the other flavors blend together.   My friend said the pork belly she buys at Trader Joe's is better then what was on her Benedict. I enjoyed my mixture of Sautéed spinach and avocado, but think the avocado would have been much better as a solo act instead of the duet.   The alcohol drinks were made fresh to order and the star of the brunch. When they say, fresh squeezed juice, they mean it. You could see them squeezing each orange for the Mimosa and the grapefruit for the Italian Greyhound at the bar. For the Bloody Mary, for an additional $2 you can add their house infused pepper vodka. I always like an extra kick to my Bloody Mary.   In closing; the service was attentive and friendly. By itself the cornbread is delicious. I'd love a chunk of it by itself with some honey whipped butter, but mixed in with the entrees did not work for either of us. Also, be sure to park on the street or between the green parking stripes or Hodak's the chicken joint next door will have your car towed.   Like Hao, I do not regret giving it a try, but it is unlikely that I will return.   When: December 6, 2015 Why: Brunch

It's Pizza Hut, we had a coupon. I have no excuses.  They had a special offer, a large 3 Topping Pizza and an 8 piece order of chicken wings for $16.99. We thought this would be a nice treat while we watched the SAG Awards. Of course, those actors were dining on much better food as they handed out their trophies.  When we called to order we were informed all they only had thin crust and pan pizza available. What? Are you shocked as much as I am? How can any pizza place be out of hand tossed crust? We were disappointed, but still placed our order for a thin crust with Italian Sausage, Green Pepper and Onion.    Ordering our chicken wings was a big deal. Not having ordered from Wing Street before, I had no idea there were so many different types of wings. We had to decide if we wanted boneless, bone-in or traditional. I was so confused, I had to ask for clarification on bone-in and traditional. Wouldn't a bone-in be traditional? Oh no, a bone-in is breaded and traditional is not. We went with traditional in buffalo sauce.   Since we live in a neighborhood that has so many pizza joints within driving distance, I always opt for carryout. I may have to get out of the house and drive, but I get my food faster. When we arrived here, outside the employee door some of the employees were experiencing some, "sister drama". Their loud voices, spurting out profanities is not the first thing a new customer wants to see and hear.   Once inside the counter staff was friendly and very helpful. At this time we noticed different levels of hotness for the buffalo wings. We quickly asked which level we ordered and they said the hottest. Again, quickly we asked if ours had not been sauced if we could drop it a notch. Ours had been tossed, but they had an order after ours that had not. They quickly tossed them in the next level down and gave the next order ours. Talk about perfect timing.   I liked that when they brought our pizza out, that they lifted the lid to show us our order. For me that is taking customer service to the next level.   Once home, the wings were a sad excuse of chicken wings. They were tiny, tiny. If I didn't know better, I swear they were from baby chicks because they were that small.  The sauce was bland, perhaps we should have stuck with the Extreme. The pizza was just okay. I did like the way they chopped the green pepper and onion. They were larger pieces and not diced like so many other pizza joints.  I'm still miffed that they didn't have hand tossed crust.

I was actually impressed. Impressed with the pretzels? No. Impressed with the service? No. I was impressed with the pristine kitchen that they are prepared in. It was bright, clean and I loved the red and white tiles. It was totally not what I was expecting when I shopped.   I had only bought Gus' Pretzels from street vendors or at my local gas station or Walgreen's. To be honest, I never knew Gus had a retail outlet until I ate Benton Cafe across the street. I thought they were just a wholesaler. Wow, was I wrong.   The pretzels are just okay, but not as good as Wetzel's. They're good for the price and they are local, so I guess I have to be happy about that fact. I was wanting bites or nubs, but did not see them on the board. I later learned they call them Endz. I'll remember that for a future visit. I instead ordered 3 Sticks and a Cinnamon & Sugar Twist. The C&S Twist had a bad taste and a worst after taste. Their sticks did taste better fresh then those from the bought from a street vendor.   The staff was kind of pushy. There were three of us waiting to order and reading the board menu. We all stated we were not ready to order as we stood back behind the line to order. Different workers kept coming out and snapping, "I'll help whoever is next". Once I placed my order, the clerk was still rather cold and rushing. I hope this was not normal service and was because they were working New Year Eve's Day.

I end up going to this Walgreens more then the one close to my home.  Why? It is so easy to stop by on my way home from work. It is conveniently located on Lafayette making it so simple to shop and then get on 55 South or 44 West, which ever one takes you home.   This holiday season, this Walgreens saved me $'s on my gift wrapping.  Every year I get my cousins (7) a themed gift. It's kind of a joke and kind of a semi-serious gift. It is more about the fun and laughs then the actual gift. With that being said, I don't want to spend a lot of money on the packaging aka gift wrapping. They all have to open them at the same time, and each of the gifts is selected to fit their individual personalities.   This year the gift was themed socks. So I just needed a small gift bag. I searched at various other stores similar to, Tuesday Morning, TJ Maxx, etc,etc....with no luck. Then one day before Ho Ho was to arrive, I was in this Walgreens and walked down their Christmas aisle. To my surprise I found the perfect little holiday sack and it was on sale for only 29¢. What a steal, I mean deal. I sheet of tissue paper and these little sacks made for the perfect wrapping.   Besides making my holidays bright, I want to give a shout out to the staff at this location. Some may say it is located on an edgy part of town, but I'd say the customer service here is some of the best of the Walgreens I shop. They always make me feel welcomed. Keep up the good work.    Will I return? - It's an easy stop on the way home.   When: December 17, 2017 Why: Gift Wrapping

I discovered this place to late in my visit to the French Quarter. It was Sunday afternoon when Marielle told about Vacherie. When I went after the Yelp Summer Splash Social, I discovered on Sunday evenings they have limited service.   However, I was able to enjoy a refreshing vodka cocktail and and an order of Brussels Sprouts with bacon at the bar. Vodka is my booze of choice and Sprouts are one of my favorite vegetables, so I was still a happy diner.  On Sunday they have Happy Hour 3-7 PM and serve an abbreviated dinner at the bar 6-10 PM.   When: August 28, 2016 Why: Dinner, but settled for Happy Hour

This Nordstrom Rack is proof that bigger is not always better. This NR is larger then the one on Brentwood, but lacks in selection that the smaller one has near The Galleria. I also, did not like the floor plan. It lacked the easy flow that the Brentwood location has. However, this location had a staff that was friendlier and more helpful.   I was shopping for summer short sleeve cotton shirts to go along with some of my solid colored shorts. A man can only wear so many Polo shirts. The selection here was not that good and the prices really were not any better then a sale price at the regular Nordstrom or Macy's. I finally did find a pink madras one that will go great with my pink shorts.   For my Rack shopping, I will continue to be a supporter of the smaller Brentwood store and let this bigger store for the west county patrons.

General Candy Company is one of the best kept secrets in Saint Louis. They are a wholesale candy and snack supplier, that has been family-owned and operated since 1924. It is located in the Tower Grove South neighborhood just off of Kingshighway. Justin, gave an excellent description, "think small candy warehouse that is open to the public". The prices are better then those you'd find a Sam's or Costco.   The entire time I was browsing inside GCC, the song Candy Man by Sammy Davis Jr. was playing in my head.  "Alright everybody, gather around The Candy Man is here What kind of candy do you want? Sweet chocolate? Chocolate walnut candy? Gum drops? Anything you want You've come to the right man because I'm the Candy Man"  GCC has every imaginable kind of candy. They have the popular names like Twix & Payday and names I'd forgotten, but loved as child; 5th Avenue, Zagnut and Zero. You'll also find sugar free candy, Laffy Taffy, Pez, nostalgia candy and bulk candies for your wedding. I'm coming back to buy my Halloween candy here. If your organization is looking for a way to raise funds, General Candy can help you with that as well.   If you have a sweet tooth for candy, you owe it to yourself to go and check GCC out. You really will feel like a kid in a candy shop.

I love this place! I am so thankful that I finally made it here. My friends have been raving about it for months, but I just never made it here. Once I did, it was love at first sight. It has a simple ambiance, racks of craft beer that you can buy by the six pack or mix and match buying single bottles and creating your own six pack.   I have been searching for a particular beer since my Colorado vacation in 2013 and have not been able to find it at any other liquor store in STL. When I was told by one of the cool employees what they were serving on draft that day, I squealed with glee. They were serving my favorite Colorado beer from Great Divide, Orabelle. They also had my second favorite, Colette.   When shopping for Craft Beer, I will now come to  CBC. They had my beer, when other stores in town told me they couldn't find it and that I'd have to buy something else. CBC you are my hero and you are rock stars in my eyes.

I had recently bought some new upholstered furniture at another store and mainly was looking for accent tables and possibly new dining table and chairs. I was not impressed with they're going out of business sale. The prices are still fairly high for the quality product you are getting.   They still have a lot of merchandise left and IMHO, it is ugly. My suggestion to Mr. Phillips is take the inventory and move to your Weekends Only Store and call it a day.

A great new addition to my neighborhood. Vinnie's is a simple sandwich shop focusing on Gyros and other sandwiches featuring; Italian Beef or Sausage and Meatballs. The prices are reasonable and the portions are hearty.   We stopped by today for a late lunch around 2PM and were greeted cheerfully by Vinnie himself. His hospitality was warm and friendly. It was as if we were sitting in his kitchen at home.   Both of us choose a Gyro, one went traditional and the other went Colossal. The difference between the two is the Colossal has lettuce and Feta cheese added to the already huge sandwich. The Gyro meat is tender and well seasoned. For my personal taste there was too much Tzatziki sauce, but that can be remedied by request a small portion or getting it on the side.   Looking at the side dishes, I was surprised that they did not offer French Fries. However, once we experienced their "Fried Potatoes" the craving for Fries escaped us. These were Baked Potatoes, that were then cubed, tossed in secret seasoning with Parmesan Cheese and then fried with a few onion strings. These potatoes burst with flavor. In addition to be a great side dish, they'd be great as an appetizer too.   The ambiance is simple and relaxed. You order at the counter and once your food is complete they bring it to your table. There's no booze, they offer bottled Coke products. With spring and summer in sight, their patio will be a great place to have lunch or an early dinner.

Oh, hello Donna, well, hello Donna It was so nice to have you as our server You're truly professional, Donna, I can tell, Donna  I normally do not call a server out by name, but the sensational service we received from Donna was exceptional. She was witty, honest and handled our large group of 12+, like a true champion. She kept the pace and did it with no assistance from her co-workers. She is was a true delight.   Forgetting it was International Supper Club night, I had a huge lunch, so my meal this evening was on the small side. Instead of ordering from the Italian side of the menu, I went Tapas. I started out with, Guido's Signature Salad. It's a basic salad with iceberg lettuce and spring mix. They also top it with Parmesan cheese, tomato, red onion, black olives, artichoke hearts, and pimentos. In my opinion, it's a Pasta House Salad with a different dressing. It was a nice lead-in to my two tapas.   Lamb is one of my favorite meats when dining out, so I couldn't resist the Cordero Lollipops. Two charbroiled lamb lollipops were served with mint jelly and a small scoop of Cabrales Mashed Potatoes. A dab of Spanish Bleu Cheese always makes smashed taters tasty.   My other small plate was Datiles con Tocino. Which translates into; bacon wrapped Dates stuffed with Cabrales. Yes, more Spanish Bleu Cheese. I don't know about you, but I wish all my "dates" could be wrapped in bacon. (lol) This dish had bacon and cheese - enough said.   Beverages of the night were a Manhattan at the bar while waiting for our entire group to arrive and an Old Fashioned at the dinner table. Both were made with Makers Mark and were acceptable. Not a fan of Maraschino Cherries being used as a garnish.   I like their motto/slogan; "A Taste of Spain in the middle of Italy."  Would I return? Yes, I need to try the Italian fare and they have linen napkins.   When: January 30, 2017 Why: International Supper Club

Great place for breakfast if you live in the neighborhood, but it is not worth the drive. We drove across town for the experience.  We had the American and English Breakfasts, both had a good presentation. The bacon was good and I love the fact that the ham was thinly sliced. Both were cured well. The eggs cooked over easy, were a little over done and the scrambled eggs were fluffy and flavorful. The Roasted Potatoes, were not roasted at all - big disappointment.   Another disappointment was the service, it was minimal and I do mean minimal. They did as little as possible to make you feel welcome or to come back. Chances are, we will not go back.

Congratulations Porter's you are back in my good graces and I have placed you back on my Crispy Chicken List.   I had been a while since we had treated ourselves to a fried chicken dinner and when we decided to treat ourselves we also agreed to give Porters another try. We were pleased to see that they are back to the Porters that we fell in love with originally. I enjoyed a 3 piece dinner with 2 breast and 1 wing. I do like the "special dinners" they offer at a slightly higher price, because I can select the pieces that are my favorites. The sides I choose were the usual mashed potatoes and creamy slaw. I'm fairly certain they are not house made, but they are still good.   This time the SO tried their Chicken Liver Dinner with the same two sides. We were in shock at the amount of livers. It was seriously enough to feed three people. I guess not that many people order livers and they wanted to get rid of them, because the amount was huge.  Not encouraging you to over eat, but if you're at Porters do get a side order of Okra. Theirs is so good, I think Paula and Bobby Deen both would give them a thumbs up.

Some of the best things in life are never the same in our lovely hometown. All I can hope is that once the "A" grade Nordstrom at the St. Louis Galleria opens that our Rack will improve. Right now this rack reflects the "C" grade Nordstrom that is at the West County Center.   Nordstrom Rack offers some incredible buys for men, but not at this Rack. I can only hope that the ladies department is better. I guess I'll continue to do my Rack shopping when I am out of town.

Bad Steven, Bad Steven. Again, I have not updated my review to a restaurant that is in my regular rotation. It's coming up on four years since my last update and I have totally become a fan of this restaurant. I've got to start reading & keeping up with my past reviews. It has been a great place to grab a lunch alone at the bar or to have dinner with a friend. So when it made Ian Froeb's STL 100, I was not surprised. I however, was surprised as to what he said was the "must order".   Ian recommends, The Southsider. Which is; griddled country style bologna, topped with a sunny up egg and cheddar fondue on a brioche bun. Is it messy to eat? Hell, yes it is, but you'll lick your fingers and wipe your mouth with enjoyment. The house cut fries are a perfect side dish and be sure to have a cold craft beer as well.   Some of my favorite past dinners have been; Country Fried Steak, Fried Chicken and Meatloaf. Yes, these are some good ole down home comfort foods, that satisfy me every time. The sides that have accompanied these meals have been; mashed potatoes, beets, squash and Mac-n-Cheese. I greatly appreciate that they offer the appropriate gravy to match the entree. Milk gravy for fried chicken & country fried steak and brown gravy for the meatloaf.  If you're stuffing yourself with comfort food, you might as well go full hog and have dessert.  I love their pies, my favorite is the Apple Caramel and my ex use to love the Banana Cream. If you're to stuffed, take them home in a eco-friendly container to enjoy later as you watch TV.  Ian ranked them 22 on his 100 list. If I had a list, I'd most likely have them in my top 10.   When: April 9, 2016 Why: Lunch & STL 100

When: February 20 Why: Brunch  I am glad I ignored some of the Yelp reviews and went to experience Lola for myself. It was totally amazing  Sunday Brunch without a Bloody Mary is unheard of in my book and the Bloody Mary's at Lola are the absolute best. I have always thought the Bloody Mary's at RL in Chicago were the best, I now know that they at Lola's.   They offer three levels, Mild - 3 Olive Tomato Vodka, Medium - Absolut Peppar Vodka, Hot - Habanero Infused Absolut Vodka. Combined with their in house BM mix, make them the best. An added bonus is you can buy them by the pitcher and save $.   We ordered the Smoked Salmon Benedict, which was very flavorful. The eggs were done perfectly and the  Salmon gave a new twist to a traditional brunch dish. What was nice, you get two so it was easy to share. We also ordered a side of Roasted Potatoes, that were sliced in large pieces and cooked to perfection.   Our second entree was the Savory Creole Breakfast Bread Pudding. No need to go to New Orleans, you've got an authentic creole dish here in downtown St. Louis. Again the portion was large enough for two to share. Before heading down to Soulard for Mardi Gras, stop by here for brunch and have this dish to kick off the celebration.   We were so impressed with our main entrees we had to experience something sweet so we ordered one of the Banana Sweet Crepes. Chocolate, Bananas, whipped cream and strawberries.....YUMMY.  Our server Ava was fantastic. In fact the entire staff was friendly and strived to make our visit enjoyable. This may very well be our new place for Sunday Brunch.  We are now planning our second visit to experience dinner. I gotta try that Lobster Dog.

If I found a magical lamp with a genie and was given three wishes, one of them would be that the Crab Cake Benedict would be a regular menu item at TOPH. Yes, it's that good and worthy of one of my wishes. Not only will I be happy, but it will allow other diners experience this delightfully delicious Benedict.   As we arrived for breakfast, my knees almost went weak when I saw "Crab Cake Benedict" on their chalkboard next to the hostess stand. I instantly knew what I wanted, there will be no need for me to glance over the menu. I would miss having a side dish of their most tasty pancakes, but I could steal a bite from my dining partners plate.   My Benedict was everything a Benedict should be. It's foundation was a toasted Wolferman's English Muffin, which was topped with a homemade Crab Cake, basted eggs and hollandaise sauce. It was served with their fresh hash brown potatoes. My crab cakes were thick, they had a thin crisp outer coating. The meat inside was moist, flakey and huge pieces of fresh crab meat. These are the type of crab cakes you'd expect to be served at a little crab shack in Maryland.   The service here is always prompt, quick and friendly. I've dined at both TOPH's in our metro area and I can tell you this one is head and shoulders above the Chesterfield location. Jessica is my favorite server, so today I am adding her to my Sensational Service list.   When: 14 MAR 2014 Why: Breakfast

This is the friendliest & most helpful staff I've ever experienced in a Walgreens. They make my visits before work totally enjoyable. I just wish they had the variety & selection of the Walgreens that is closer to my home. Oh, well, it helps me try new products.

A smokey neighborhood bar where everyone knows your name, except those of us who do not live in the neighborhood. I didn't mind that the bartender didn't know my name, but at least acknowledge me when I sit down at your bar. He was to involved in the football game on TV.  Once the game went to a commercial, all was good. Some of us like football and some of us like myself like baseball, so I forgave him.   I asked to see a menu so I could do a carryout order. Brad was craving a French Dip and we had heard their "Stallion" was one of the best. They slow simmer the Italian Beef with peperoncini, crushed red pepper and their special blend of Italian Seasoning. It is then served on garlic French bread with provel cheese. Brad loved it, said it was good comfort food. I was not impressed, I thought the bread was dried out, they were skimpy on the meat and provel cheese. To me the sandwich was mostly bread.   To go with the Stallion we had Felix's Wings. A 1 lb. serving that has been trashed and thrashed with Jalapeno Ranch.  These wings were great, so great that I will be adding Felix's to my list for Wings. They were large, crispy and seasoned perfectly. What I liked most is that they did not a heavy sauce on them, it was like a dry rub. You could eat and enjoy with no mess.   After placing my order to go, I asked how long it would take and I was told about 20 minutes. I had a motive in my asking, I saw they had a special for $6.45 that included a slice of pizza and a pint. What a deal. I had a Schafley's Pale Ale and Italian Sausage. The slice was a large slice of the pie and very good. I enjoyed the spicy tomato sauce and there was plenty of sausage and cheese. Who knows, I may be returning to have a couple of pints and a whole pizza pie with a friend.   Only negative, lot of smokers and I was the only one not smoking at the bar.

I am so excited and looking forward to the CBC opening a location in the South Hampton neighborhood. It's my "hood" and will make my beer shopping so much easier.   In the while, I love this location because they always have what I am looking for. I recently was gifted a six-pack of beer. I wish it were a six-pack stomach, but I'll take the beer. Any way, I really liked it and wanted another. Tried a couple of grocer stores with no luck and another large local store did not have it as well. I come here to this little boutique beer shop and it's here.   The beer was Saluki Dunkeldog, by Big Muddy Brewing. Its' alcohol by volume is only 5.4% which means I can enjoy more then one. This beer for me is very approachable with a smooth distinctive taste. I like the hint of chocolate roast.   Service here is always top notch. I like beer, but still am kind of novice. They are patient, listen and make recommendations on what I like.   Hurry up and open the store near me!  Will I return? - Yes, until the opens near my home.   When: Sometime in 2017 Why: Beer Searching.

Salt + Smoke is the best thing that has happened to The Loop, since the beginning of The St Louis Walk of Fame. The aroma from their smoker will seduce you as you stroll down The Loop and before you know it, you'll be inside enjoying some incredible Brisket and Baby Back Ribs.   We started our lunch with two appetizers; Deviled Eggs and Fried Pickles. I use to think my mom made the best deviled eggs. After all, she was always the one who made them for all the family summer picnics. However, the Deviled Eggs here at S+S, have a unique twist that made them out shine moms'.  They were perfectly cooked, seasoned and sprinkled with bacon chips. What made them unique, was being served on top of a smear of pimento cheese. Adding the cheese to your bite of egg will have your taste buds doing a happy dance.   I've been known as the King of Fried Pickles here on Yelp, with a semi-famous list of the best places to find these delectable treats. What I liked best about the FP's here, is that you get a variety of pickles; spears, midget and chips. I wasn't wild about the breading on the pickles, but the Flaxseed Mayo for dipping was a winner.   We both went for the Bestie Combo which allowed us to order two meats with two sides. Both of us ordered Brisket and 1/2 Rack Baby Back Ribs, but ordered different sides so we could have a bigger experience. Our four sides were;  Pit Beans with Smoked Bacon, Sweet Pepper Potato Salad, White Cheddar Cracker Mac and Green Bean and Tomato Salad.   The Brisket was fork tender and full of flavor from the dry rub. I tried two of the three sauces, with my favorite being My Sweet Bestie. The portions are huge so I had leftovers to bring home and the other half said, the Brisket was the best in STL. The ribs were the shining star of lunch. The dry rub on the ribs, had a nice little kick of fire in its' flavor. They had just a little bit of fat, to give that extra juicy flavor. I easily was able to tear the ribs apart, enjoy tender meat and leave the bones clean as a whistle.   Pit Beans - Thick sauce, holding the beans tightly together. These are the backed beans I like, I hate runny sauces that bleed all over your plate.   Potato Salad - Creamy mayo base with red potatoes and sweet red peppers.  Cracker Mac - Real Old School Mac-n-Cheese, that is different and full of flavor. I like that they use white cheddar and is the right ratio of cheese to pasta. It truly was a flashback, to have the crumpled crackers on top.   Green Bean & Tomato Salad - The perfect side for those who are clean eating or doing low carb. Fresh green beans served chilled with cherry red and yellow tomatoes in a light dressing. It was simple and delicious.   I love the big thick gingham napkins, that gives the feeling of a backyard BBQ. The Hello My Name is...on the sauce bottles gave me a giggle. Today I enjoyed iced tea, but cannot wait to return and take advantage of their full bar. Servers were friendly and were well informed of the menu. They also get bonus points from me for having eco-friendly carryout boxes. I'll be back again and again.

They tore down an old fashioned style Taco Bell at this location and built this new ultra modern Taco Bell. It offers Wi-Fi and outlets at the tables and booths for your electronic devices. This allows you to stay connected while you enjoy a quick fast food lunch. I will say, the new building is a vast improvement over the old.   The menu is still the same, fast food Mexican that will satisfy a craving and give you heartburn or gas afterwards. I agree with Josh J., the customer service is lacking. The night I stopped in for a couple of Combos for a lazy night dinner, the cashier was more occupied flirting with a young lady then servicing ordering patrons. He rushed us through one by one and in between, kept flirting hoping to make a "score".    The tacos were good by TB standards.  I also ordered a Bean Burrito, which was a disappointment. The tortilla was cold, tough and chewy.   I really do not  recommended for lunch or dinner. If you've been out drinking and have a fair amount of liquor in your system, give it a go.

A solid 3 Stars, that I am confident will be 4 Stars on my next visit.   I started out with a House Margarita, which is made from scratch and hand shaken. In fact, it was rather strong which allowed me to sip it through out my entire meal. As an appetizer, we ordered the House Made Chips and Guacamole. We both were surprised by its' flavor,  it could easily be ranked up there with some of the higher end Mexican restaurants here in STL.   To get the full experience, we ordered the SNR Plate, which gives you 2 ribs, 2 tacos and 1 side dish. The ribs were meaty and tender. The dry rub on them was sufficient enough seasoning for me. I did try a couple dabs of their sauces, but preferred my ribs without. We ordered four different tacos; Chorizo, Cachete, Carnitas and Chicken.  The Cachete and Carnitas were the favored ones out of the four. I will be sure to try the battered fish on my next visit.   As our sides, we choose Mac-n-Cheese and Cole Slaw. Both were good, with the Cole Slaw out shining the MnC. Some of the other BBQ joints in STL may want to take note, this is the type of slaw that is the perfect accompaniment to ribs. The Mac-n-Cheese was creamy, but I would of liked just a tad more flavor.   The ambiance was rather industrial and stark, which actually made it rather warm and cozy if that makes any sense. SNR is a great addition to Benton Park and is an easy find in the neighborhood. It's just across the parking lot from Hodak's.   I'll be back to try more ribs, a different taco and I hope to see you there too.

I am not impressed.  Cool concept and kind of fun ambiance being located in the back of an art gallery, but beyond that everything else is pretty much a miss.  Food is way overpriced for the quality received. They truly need to rethink their menu and pricing if they want to succeed. Can't believe they haven't even been open a month and have already raised their prices for food that isn't that good.   We had two platters today for lunch, Pulled Pork ($15) and Beef Brisket ($17). They claim their beef  is Certified Angus and wet aged 21 days. Could have fooled me. Wet aged beef is suppose to be incredibly tender because the process prevents it from losing juices. The CP's was so far from being tender, we had to request a knife. I agree with critics of wet aged beef, that the process (may) tenderize the beef but prevents the meat from developing much flavor. Dry aged beef is more flavorful.    The pulled pork was more tender then the beef, but lacked any flavor. If a dry rub is good I will totally skip the sauce, but here I was eager to try them all. Their Blackberry Ancho was the best, with the Sweet & Smokey a close second. The House Sauce was bland.   Their platters come with two sides, so we each ordered differently so we could experience more. The White Baked Beans with Root Beer were actually red, so major disappointment and nothing spectacular. Crispy Cole Slaw was bitter and could have been chopped a little smaller to be bite size. You can make their White Cheddar Mac & Cheese at home by buying Kraft White Cheddar in a box and adding nutmeg. Then there was their Crispy Potato Salad that was seasoned well with dill, capers and tarragon making it a winner.  The corn muffins served with  whipped honey butter were huge, moist and had kernels of corn inside like a chocolate chip muffin.   I commend them on using containers and utensils that are compostable and providing a container for those who dine in house to recycle them. However, all their beverages are served in glass or plastic bottles and they do not have a receptacle to recycle them. Why be earth friendly one way and not the other? Staff is friendly taking your order, but they kinda make it obvious they'd prefer you to leave and not eat at the tables provided. They really want it to be take out only, but still charge you prices equal to sit down dining with waiter service.

Porter's produces a flavorful chicken that is crispy on the outside, moist and tender on the inside. Their boxed dinners include cole slaw and mashed potatoes with a mass produced dinner roll.  The cole slaw is excellent, wish my local deli's slaw was as good. Mashed potatoes are mashed potatoes, and the white gravy is better then the brown gravy you get at KFC.   The staff is friendly and accommodating to your request. We wanted one of our dinners to be all thighs and it was no problem. My only question is, who carves their chickens. The thighs and breast are cut stranger then I have ever seen. Hey, I can over look a weird cut, when the flavor is this good, but inquiring minds still want to know.

If I lived in New Orleans, Addiction would be my Addiction for coffee. What a great find, on the Yelp app.. Everything about this little coffee shop is unique. Creativity flows from the beverages and out into the ambiance and marketing. Take your time and relax. There is so much that will catch your eye and stimulate your mind. The music playing will also take you away into another dimension.   I got a giggle out of the verbiage they used for selling their beverages. It wasn't called a, "menu" it was referred to as; "The Goods". It was then broken down into three categories; Habit - Fix - Lit. My beverage of choice was the last one listed under, Lit. I was craving a cold brew. The barista commented that I had made a good choice. He then asked if I liked it black and I told him that was how coffee was intended to be drank.   Great service, great coffee and it is all at an affordable price. If you're in the French Quarter, stop by and you too will be addicted to Addiction.   When: August 28, 2016 Why: Cold Brew

Three cupcakes today; Pumpkin Spice, Peanut Butter and Red Velvet. I will admit all three had great flavor, with the Pumpkin Spice leading the way. However, even though they all had great flavor, they all lacked moistness. All three cupcakes were extremely dry. If one were dry and the other two were moist, I'd kept them at 4 Stars. When all three end up being a dry cake, they lose a star. Thank God, for a cold glass of milk.

This is a Taco Bell? Seriously, I had to ask myself that question when I entered this location. It is a fairly new location and the inside is crisp and clean with multiple booths, tables and even a cool island with bar height counter top and stools.   It is the same Taco Bell menu you get at all the other locations, but some how when I ate mine it seemed better. The tacos were filled fuller and I swear the burrito was fatter.  I am sure it was all in my imagination that they were bigger, but having better flavor was not.                                The staff was friendly and their management has taught them well about the importance of customer service. I was cheerfully greeted as I entered and the young lady taking my order did it with a smile. When she presented me with my order to go, she thanked me and invited me back. Again, I had to ask myself am I really in Taco Bell.  Sales clerks at Macy's rarely invite me back. TB is building that solid customer base.   Some may be scratching their head wondering why I am reviewing a TB. I will tell you, we all slum it once in awhile and while I was slumming at this TB, they impressed me. When you impress me, it does not matter if you are white linen or fast food, you get a big shout out for a job well done.

Momma Mia! I've found my Italian market on The Hill.   How have I missed this amazing little market? I go to Bertarelli's and Amighetti's and I yet I have strolled right on by DiGregorio's without taking note.  What was wrong with me? I am so glad that I finally ventured inside to experience this wonderland of Italian delights.   I was mesmerized by the large selection of oil olive oils and different vinegars.  Not to mention the large container of Virgin Olive Oil that you can buy a bottle and get refills at a reduced price. The pasta aisle was filled with more fettuccine noodles then I knew existed and the variety of  tomatoes and prepared sauces were endless as well.   The deli counter seemed to have more then my local Schnucks, and they have the most reasonable prices on veal chops in town. I got a giggle out of a sign they have taped to their meat counter which states, " We will be happy to serve you when you are done with your phone call."  Love it!   What I loved more was what I noticed in the case behind the sign. I discovered that they  have white anchovies. I've been having a love affair with white anchovies ever since they were introduced to me at The Good Pie. Oh, the flavor they add to a Caesar Salad or hand tossed pizza pie.   They've also got kitchen gadgets, booze and Italian candy. The customer service was as if you were family.  When we asked questions, they'd walk with us to show the item and make sure there were no more questions. Some high end retailers should take lessons.   I have my Mexican grocer down on Cherokee and now I have my Italian grocer on The Hill. This fat boy could not be happier.

Porters does chicken well, but they lost a star for their Cod Fish. The pieces were square. I wanted the catfish, but was informed it would be a 20 minuet wait. To save time, I went with Cod. Big mistake, not only was it square, but had a greasy nasty taste. I've heard good things about the catfish, so next time I will order ahead, so I will not have to wait.   We also enjoyed the Chicken Tender Dinner tonight and it was a winner. It included four huge pieces of white meat chicken, that were crispy and juicy. These tenders were way better then those you'd get at any other fast food type business.  My bad choice of Cod Fish caused them a star, but I am confident once I experience the Catfish the stars will go back up.

A solid breakfast place, it's nothing more and nothing less. I've been here several times since my first review and I can say that neither the food or service has been consistent. It's been a hit or miss on one or both each time I have visited. Once, it was a hit for both, shame it can't be that way every time.   My favorite which is a hit every time, it the Madame Verde. Asparagus is my favorite vegetable, so I always enjoy this egg dish with a side salad. My next favorite is the American Breakfast, it is so simple. How can you go wrong with scrambled eggs, roasted potatoes, bacon, (or ham) and toast. Add a bottomless cup of coffee and you've got the perfect start of your day.  Today, The Mud House was featured as the Yelp ROTD, so we thought we'd go and help them celebrate the big honor. It is unusual for both of us to order the same thing when we go out, but today we both ordered "The Mud Slinger" with bacon. This dish definitely is full of flavor and is a huge portion. It's a serving of roasted potatoes, red onion, black bean chili, cheese and topped with two sunny eggs. The black beans added a big boast of flavor. One of the misses today on this dish was the potatoes. We both thought the cubed pieces were too large, they could of been cubed smaller. Also, they were pre-boiled and finished in a skillet or on the grill. I would of liked them to been finished a little more crispy, they were very soft as if they were ready to become mashed.   Ordering the same dish, we were surprised at the difference in our bacon. My dining partners bacon was hot and crisp, as if it were made to order. Mine on the other hand, was cold and chewy, as if it were pre-made and waiting to be served. We did not discover this difference until we were discussing our meal on the drive home. I should of commented while we were eating, if I knew his was "fresh" I would have commented to the staff. I just thought it was like bacon you see at some breakfast buffets.   Staff is friendly in a hipster sort of way, and the decor is eclectic which makes it a fun place to enjoy your first meal of the day. I will continue to patronize The Mud House in hopes of being able to bump them up to a 4, for now it is a 3.5.

I do not know if it were my prayers to the Retail Gods or my wish on a shooting star, but  my last visit to this Rack has me doubling my original stars. I was so pleased with the selections that I actually made two purchases within the same day. If they keep it up, I might even raise them to 5 Star status.   It is good to see that they have improved the selections in the men's department. However, this may backfire on someone who is a clothes horse. The items I selected were name brands at a price lower then sale prices at the regular department stores. They were even lower then stores like Stein Mart and TJ Max.   Sales associates were friendly, as were the cashiers. It was so cool having my sales receipt sent to me via email. Downside of the emailing is, forgetting to do your updated reviews. I normally keep a wad of receipts to remind me to do my Yelp thing.   The money I save here, will help me not feel as guilty when I buy groceries at Whole Foods. I'm not going to look at the math real close, because I am sure I will find out it truly is not a win-win situation.  Still, I am glad they have improved since their original opening. I look forward to shopping NR every time I'm at WF and vice versa.

When you work every Sunday and you have one off during vacation, what do you do? You go out and enjoy Brunch at a restaurant that you typically do not get to enjoy on a Sunday morning.   As I checked in, I realized I have never done a review for my evening meals here. What a bad boy, but I can't dwell on that now, it's in the past. Let's just talk about Brunch.   They promptly opened at 10:00 AM, a small crowd was waiting outside. There was a group for a birthday party and another for a baby shower. Luckily all of those folks went out to enjoy the relaxing patio. Since, I as usual was dining alone, I opted for the bar.  Brunch is not Brunch without a Bloody Mary or Mimosa. Since I have a list on Yelp for Bloody's, that was my drink of choice. The bartender told me about the unlimited Bloody Mary Bar for $30, but I opted for a single drink at only $10. I had other things to do and didn't need a booze buzz that early in the morning. However, it is a good deal. I choose to not have a salted rim and called my Vodka. I love Tito's. The Bloody Mary mix was not overly spicy, and offered just enough kick.   As an entree, I was torn between Eggs Benedict or Chicken and Waffles.  The Buttermilk Fried Chicken with a Malted Waffle and Banana Maple Syrup won. The chicken was two large pieces of boneless breast meat. They were crispy on the outside, you hear a crunch and so juicy on the inside. The banana maple syrup was a perfect accompaniment to the malted waffle. The young man next to me thought not and requested regular syrup when his order arrived. He was wrong, I am right, enough said.   Service at the bar was relaxing and attentive. The bartender was extremely busy taking care of all the servers, but she still made and had time to tend to the needs of those eating at the bar.   Will I return: Yes, I gotta re-visit so I can review the regular menu that I've missed doing.   When: November 5, 2017 Why: Brunch

I am a loyal customer of St. Louis Honda and have recommended them to friends who have also become loyal customers.   I will also confess that I am one of those car owners who gets everything done at my car dealer. Is it more expensive? Not really, by the time you go to those drive in and quick oil change joints and by the time you pay for the upgrades that you want or need the price is the same. Also, I like having all my car records in one place. I consider them cars doctor. All my medical records are with my doctor, so why should my ride not have the same convenience that I do.   The service advisers are friendly, personable and are not high pressure add on sales professionals like a quick oil change place. Also, they know my car and its history so I do not need to worry about them pushing unnecessary repairs. My CRV rides smooth and easy thanks to STL Honda.   As stated in my previous review, I always wait while my car is being serviced. They offer a comfortable waiting room with free Wi-Fi, coffee, bottled juice or water and Krispy Kreme donuts. They also have a playroom for customers who are waiting with toddlers, making the other customers very happy.   When I'm ready for a new car, it will be another Honda and it will be from Mungenast St. Louis Honda again.

When I'm in the area, I stop in and visit this B&NB. I don't shop the regular priced books, I shop the clearance and sale book tables. I especially like the books that are featured on sale in the entryway. That is where I always find the best bargains. I can always find a great cookbook for an upcoming gift. I have found some titles on clearance here, to be cheaper then Amazon. I didn't have to pay shipping and got instant satisfaction.   Staff isn't that friendly, but that could be because I only shop clearance....LOL.

When: March 1 Why: Craving Ribs and our 1st choice was closed.   Drove to Kirkwood from The Hill to satisfy our craving for Ribs and Brisket. It's a short drive straight down 44 to Big Bend and across Kirkwood Road.  Their Ribs were good, not great, but definitely between above average and great. We called ahead since our first choice was already closed, and it was a good thing. They were almost sold out too. We ordered ours with sauce on the side and I'm glad we did. I enjoyed the dry rub seasoning, the sauce for my palate was on the sweet side. As stated in a previous review, the meat does fall off the bone. They come clean with very little effort.  The Brisket was another story, we were disappointed. I give them some leeway as it was the end of the day (6:00 p m), but know when not to sell what's left. To me, it was obvious it was the last of the best. It had good flavor, but it was the butt end and dried out.   Our sides were seasoned fries and Cole Slaw. Fries were crisp, but not what I expected with BBQ. The Cole Slaw was very similar to what you get at KFC. They were out of Baked Beans, which always go with Ribs and we didn't want green beans or apple sauce.  If you live in or near Kirkwood, these are good Ribs at a fair price. However, I'd recommend you do your own sides.

Great little bookstore, they carry some off the wall titles that make them  in class of their own.  I love the little section that has books on local neighborhoods, restaurants  and history of St. Louis. Another thing I found very helpful were the shelf talkers that gave blurbs and recommendations on books. Also, look for bookmarks sticking out of the books, it means that it is autographed by the author.

* I moved this review to the correct listing here on Yelp.   Carondelet Diner has reopened its' doors with new owners and I am glad they are back. I enjoyed a Philly Omelet, that was grilled to a perfect golden yellow and was stuffed with thinly shaved Ribeye steak, onion and green peppers. It was the perfect breakfast for me or anyone else who is eating low-carb. The omelet was huge and very filling.   My dining partner enjoyed their Ultimate Breakfast, which was a manly breakfast.  It was two eggs your way, a choice of bacon or sausage (patty), hash browns and two pancakes.  I got a taste of the sausage and it was very flavorful. It had a nice peppery tang to it. The pancakes were HUGE and he could not finish them, but said they were very good. This breakfast is down-home and very filling.  Speaking to one of the owners, they are all about buying and using local vendors. All the meats they are using are from Kenrick's Meat Market, a great south county business. The ambiance is plain jane, but the service has a warm neighborhood feel. I almost felt as if I were eating at a neighbors kitchen table.   Look forward to coming back and checking out their lunches and daily specials.
Great gift boxes, I am sure they'll be a hit in the kitchen this year.  Shopping today was packed almost claustrophobic, but the staff was handling it and the shoppers were having a great time.

I guess every restaurant has a bad night. If this is true, then S+S had one last night.  I'll admit, for a Tuesday night they were packed at 6:30PM and many of the tables were large parties. Our table was 10, next to us was a party of 14 and in the next room I could see tables of 6 and 8. However, that should not have effected the quality of service and food, but it did.   As an appetizer I ordered the Smokey Wings to share with my friends. They were huge, meaty and definitely smokey. For some of my friends who tried them, they were too smokey, but they tantalized my taste buds.   For my entree I choose the Brisket Plate which came with two sides. Eating low-carb, I selected the cole slaw and green bean and tomato salad as my sides. Their GBSS is always a winner for me. The cole slaw is a vinegar base which I favor over a creamy dressing. It's a simple slaw, cabbage only and the dressing, which makes it an easy accompaniment to BBQ.   When ordering Brisket, I like the fact that they give you three different options. You can choose from; lean, fat or burnt ends. They even allow you to mix two of them.  In the past, I have always loved their fork tender brisket. However, tonight when I ordered the lean and burnt ends, my brisket was dried out and tough. I had to apply pressure and saw like movements to break it into pieces. It was also overly SALTY.  Salt may be in your name, but do not make it the primary flavor that I taste.   I promised the roomie I'd bring home a plate for them to enjoy and almost backed out on my promise after eating my meal. I stayed with my promise and brought him home brisket with baked beans and mac-n-cheese.
