To my surprise and delight, his brisket was the fork tender that I had experienced on my earlier visits to S+S. As in my previous review, both the mac-n-cheese and pit beans are winners. I also, brought home a slice of pecan pie and in the words of my roomie, "This Pecan pie would make any Texan, proud." Which in translation is damn good.  Service was friendly and they were willing to separate all the checks, which is always a nice gesture to a large group. However, service was slow, orders brought out by a variety of different servers and orders were mixed up with different sides. I think most of the problems tonight were in the kitchen, dealing with a full house and several large groups. I'll keep the issue with the bartender to myself, but it was a major flub up.   I know S+S is better and am also confident they'll be back up to 5 Stars on my next visit. I hated to take them down a couple of stars, but had to be honest.

Color me surprised and color my friend happy. After shopping all the other major department stores and some very popular boutique stores with no success, I asked my friend if she want to try JCPenny. She said, she didn't care where it came from,  as long as she found what she needed.   My friend has tickets to the Kentucky Derby and we were searching for her dress to wear on Friday at the Kentucky Oaks. It is known the world over as the Derby's "sister race," this contest takes place the day before and celebrates the sport's finest filly racers. She already has her dress & hat for the actual Derby.   If you've never been to the Derby, when you buy your tickets they come with a dress code. You especially have a dress code if you're in the really good seats. The Friday dress code, required that her dress be pink or have pink as a prominent color to celebrate the fillies. We also had to find a purse within the dimensions allowed. We found a dress, hat and purse all for under $125. What a deal.   The service we received was friendly and professional. They young lady who processed the sale, totally impressed me. She was more attentive then some associates that work at a regular Nordstrom's.   So give JCPenny's a chance next time you are shopping. You just may find what you're looking for and at a major savings.   When: April 4, 2016 Why: Derby Attire for a friend

Fast Eddie's Bon Air is a true dive bar with a grill. The drinks and food, are both inexpensive. If you need a cheap date, this is the place. The decor is tacky, but the ambiance is still fun.   Fast Eddie's may have waitresses, but they don't do food. They only do drinks. If you want something to eat, it is a simple process. Go to the grill counter and order it yourself. It's a short wait and then you return to table and enjoy your eats with cheap drinks that the waitress will bring to you.   After a fun-filled day in Grafton and driving the scenic River-road, we thought it would be a fun ending to our adventurous day. We arrived late in the afternoon, so the crowd was small. We selected a hightop with a good view of the large room, because when at Fast Eddie's people watching is one of the highlights.   We ordered a couple of ice cold beers from our waitress, who reminded me of Flo on the old TV show Alice. When we tried to order food, she snapped at us in true Flo style that we had to do that ourselves. As I waited for the beers, Norma worked her way over to the "grill counter" and ordered us up some snacks. We munched on a Big Elwood on a Stick which is marinated tenderloin with peppers. The tenderloin does not melt in your mouth, it's a little chewy. What do you expect for the cheap price? We also shared a basket full of French Fries, that were crisp and enough for two. The fries were the perfect accompaniment to our 1/2 lb. Fat Eddie Burgers. Their website says it is the tastiest burger I'll ever eat. I wouldn't go that far, but it is better then a burger at McDonald's.   Fast Eddie's is a hoot. When you go, don't expect much and you wont be disappointed and you'll have fun.

The customer service today was stellar and the store was bustling with holiday shoppers. The sales associates were multi-tasking, assisting shoppers and they were doing it all with positive attitudes.   We found gifts for those who were on our nice list and we even found some for those who were on the naughty list.  Of course you can never shop at Sur La Table without adding something to your own kitchen.  They could have gotten a 5 star rating if, a male manager and a female staff member were not having a conversation that should have been conducted in the stockroom or somewhere private. Shoppers did not need to hear the "drama".

Great store for party accessories. They have one aisle full of plates, napkins, cups and plastic-ware in every color imaginable. If you can not find a color to work with your party theme, I'd be surprised.   My recent visit here was to pick up goodies for a 60th birthday celebration. I found a DVD that highlights all the news, music, sports and movies of 1953. I also found several typical joke gifts for the celebration. My personal favorite resembles crime tape, but says "caution 60th birthday celebration in progress".   The customer service here is minimal. I was greeted on the sales floor, but when I said I was okay they quickly went on their way. No friendly chat to up-sell. I thought retail associates were there to increase sales. The cashier was quick to ring me out, but again no friendly conversation to encourage me to return for future party needs.   Great store for party needs you'll find almost anything you need for a fun party, but they need to improve their customer service.

I was torn on weather to write this review or not. Should I keep it to myself, so I will not have to wait for a table when the crowds rush to experience their greatness. Or do I sing their praises, to guarantee their success so I can continue to enjoy their tasty breakfast for a very long time. As you can see, I am singing and singing loud. This is my new favorite week day breakfast.   This past Tuesday, I kind of created my own special Sunday Brunch type breakfast.  I started out with a Bloody Mary, made with a house mix which smooth and not overly spicy. The BF enjoyed a Pimms Cup and I will say it was the best Pimm that I have tried in Saint Louis. If you're a fan of a PC, I suggest you try one here.   I heard great things about the Chicken Biscuit and it rates right up there with an order of Chicken and Waffles. The house made biscuits, smeared with sriracha butter, then topped with two spicy fried chicken breast and drizzled with clover honey. I was in heaven. They came with a side of potatoes that were diced in to huge pieces and fried crisp.   The BF enjoyed the Jax Benedict, which was not your typical Benedict. No English Muffin here, the foundation of this Benedict was a potato leek. It was then layered with salmon, a perfectly poached egg and  sauce béarnaise. That potato leek, put this Benedict in a league of it's own and it was a winner.   Being a farm boy, I could not resist and had to order of their biscuits  and gravy. Two of their big flaky biscuits smothered in house made sausage gravy. I really liked the gravy, it was seasoned just right. Normally, when I get B&G's out, they are overly seasoned with salt, but not at Jax Cafe. We shared this tasty country delight and we couldn't clean the plate, it was a hefty serving.   The service was great and I look forward to my next Sunday off. I normally work Sunday, but my next one off I will be here for brunch.

Get it straight people, Adrian was Rocky's girlfriend, not Adriana. Whenever I have mentioned Adriana's to others, they always say, like Rocky's girlfriend? No, you need to add an additional, A and pronounce it correctly. Oh well, that's another story.   Any way, Adriana's is an old school deli and what modern day deli chains should strive to be. The bread here is soft and fresh. I pretty sure, there are little old Italian grandmothers in back making it daily.   My go to is usually the Half & Half lunch special. I get half of a sandwich and a side. My go to is the house salad with house dressing. Franco is a favorite choice for my sandwich. It has; hot turkey, Onion, Roasted Red Pepper and Cheese. Eating this, excluding the bread, I feel as if I'm eating somewhat healthy. The salad is always a winner for me. It's never overdressed as you normally get at other Italian establishments.   As stated by others, you order at the counter and then listen for your number to be shouted out. No runners here to bring you your order. The staff is too busy, hustling with making your order and busing tables after others have left.   To my understanding, the character who on occasion is taking orders at the cash register is Adriana herself. She's a delight, a true Italian Grandmother. Rest of the staff is friendly and are here to provide you with quick service.   The decor is bright yellow and blue. Tables are covered in plastic blue gingham tablecloths. It is tacky as hell, but charming as hell at the same time. It's makes the ambiance of this neighborhood deli,  just perfect.   Congratulations on being #25 on The Top 25 Places to Eat in STL.  Will I return: In The Hill and it's lunchtime.   When: June 12, 2017 Why: Lunch

I am so excited that Cha Cha Chow now has a brick & mortar space.  It makes me happy that it is close to my home. For those lazy nights when I do not want to cook, I just need to take an earlier exit off of 44 on my way home from work and I am there.  What makes it even better, is that I will be able to enjoy a cocktail or beer at Gaslight Lounge while my food is being prepared to go.  I can eat here two night in a row and it will be like eating at two different restaurants. The first night I can have Grilled Fish Tacos with a side of Black Beans. Then the next night I'll have their burger which is made with local beef and seasoned with their homemade rub.  (I knew immediately that I was going to like CCC when I saw that they spell "ketchup" the same way that I do. I am not a catsup, person) They top the burger with spicy ketchup, cheese, poblano pepper and grilled onion. To make it even more different from all other burgers, they serve it on a toasted baguette. Yummy!   I try not to eat too many carbs, but I am a french fry junkie. I truly love a fresh-cut, skin-on, crispy french fry. Give me a little cup of "ketchup" for dipping and I am in heaven for that brief moment of ecstasy. Cha Cha Chow's Spicy Ketchup makes that brief moment linger and last just a little bit longer.   See you tomorrow afternoon, Cha Cha Chow - I'm craving a burger as I type.

KSDK just did a news story on this Walgreens, showing how friendly the staff is.  So glad others have noticed what I did over a year ago.  The staff here are superstars especially Mae.   They should have this staff do the customer service training for all Bi-State Walgreens.

Patience is a virtue and it is one I do not have. Sometimes when I want something, I don't want to wait. I want it and I want it NOW. I'm starting a low-carb diet and was wanting the New Atkins book and cookbook. Sure, I could have gotten on the internet and ordered it from Amazon at a cheaper price and waited a week for its' arrival. However today, I was able to walk in to B&NB, get both books, not pay shipping and start reading tonight.  The store is easy to navigate. If you know the type of book and category it would be located in, it should be an easy find. I found my books with ease. My cashier was friendly and tried to sell me their frequent shopper/readers card. It offers some nice perks, but for me the $25 annual fee wasn't worth it. If you're a true bookworm, it would be a bargain.

When: March 6 Why: Shopping for area rug  Thought this was suppose to be a "Super Target", with a larger and better selection then the others. If so, I was not impressed. My usual Target had the same selections.   I found this store to be poorly organized, cluttered and just on the other side of dirty. It did not make for a pleasant shopping experience. The clerks we dealt with, were too busy doing task work then providing customer service and closing a sale.   Enough has been said about the parking, after all it is The Promenade and it is always a pain.

Quincy Street is an A-OK restaurant. To be honest, it is kinda weird. It's as if they are not sure what or who they are yet. Once they figure it out, they may be the new hot spot on Gravois.  When you enter QSB, your first visual is a great old wood bar and lots of exposed brick giving a warm feeling. However, when you are taken to your table for lunch all of that ambiance is lost. They lead you to a room towards the back of the first floor that looks as if you are in the unfinished basement of a friends house. The walls are institutional green, glass block windows and the only decor is two flat screen TVs.  Why not carry the exposed brick decor into the dining area?   I was lunching with Miss Norma H. and we each had a burger. Even though it is a nice touch on the menu, it gave me a giggle. They have at the top of the burgers, the definitions of the different temperatures you can have your burger grilled. Having been raised on a beef farm, to me that is just common sense.   Miss Norma had the Black & Bleu Burger which was topped with Smoky Bacon and crumbled Bleu Cheese with a side of cottage cheese. She was such a good girl, choosing the health side to complement her burger. I had the Blackened Cajun Burger, which was dredged in Blackening Spices and topped with melted Pepper Jack Cheese. I wasn't as good as Norma, I went with the Tavern Chips over the Seasoned Fries and I am glad that I did.   Both of us thought our burgers were just okay. If I wanted to go out for a burger, QSB would not come to mind in the future. The buns were funky, not your typical hamburger bun, so we set them aside and ate ours without. The bacon and crumbled bleu cheese on Norma's were nice portions and she liked the bacon. However, my Blackened Cajun Burger was another story. When I order Cajun, I want sweat to bead up on my forehead while I'm eating. The flavoring was good, just not as spicy as I would have liked.   Our service was sporadic and at times I felt like we were being either ignored or rushed.   Upon leaving, I noticed an open door with a huge staircase, the type used in the musical "Hello Dolly". I asked the bartender what was upstairs and she told us we could go have a look. Wow, now I know what happened to the exposed brick ambiance, it's all upstairs. The dining room upstairs was totally cool, what a shame they only serve lunch in the bland room downstairs.

I do not care if Dr. Oz says fried food is not good for me and fried chicken is not really on my diet. I love Porter's and will treat myself occasionally to a traditional Sunday Dinner of fried chicken.   We love the fact that Porter's has what they call a "special" dinner. That is where you get to select your pieces. The SO loves thighs, so he gets three thighs in his box. I'm a wing and breast man, so I order a breast with two wings. Neither of us care for legs, so ordering this way we both get to enjoy our favorite pieces.   As stated in my previous review, I love their Cole slaw. I do not know if it is house made or if it is bought from a wholesaler, but it is damn good. I'll have to ask next time I'm ordering our "special" Sunday dinner, if it is made in house.   I wish they offered livers and gizzards as a side like French Fries and Jalapeno Poppers instead only offering them as an "extra". The portion size of an "extra" is to huge when you just want to satisfy the L or G craving. I like gizzards and the SO prefers livers, so ordering one just never satisfies all involved.   However, an "extra" order of their Okra is just right.  To keep temptation away on the drive home, I put the bag in the back seat so I can not sneak my hand in for a treat. I love how the aroma of that southern delicacy fills my car. I speed home, just so I can taste those dusted in cornmeal delights. If I ever get pulled over for speeding, I am confident I can bribe the policeman with Okra or a piece of chicken.   Porter's in nestled between The Cue and a laundromat so parking is prime. Luckily, four spaces in front of the restaurant are clearly marked for Porter's customers only. Even though it is "clearly marked", the cashier on occasion has to chase a Cue customer down and have them move their car. Keep this in mind when backing out to leave, others will be rushing and pushing their way into your space making this parking lot a new addition to my Parking Lot Derby list.

Thanks again to the Yelp International Supper Club, I experienced a new restaurant. I'm always open to enjoying some new Greek cuisine. Tonight I wasn't that hungry, so I ordered a Gyro Salad. It was a large and I do mean large Greek Salad. It was a hearty portion of lettuce, cucumber, tomato, red onion, green pepper, kalamatra olives, crumbled feta cheese, tossed in their house made dressing and topped with gyro meat. It was a low-carb friendly meal in a bowl. It was served with toasted pita bread, for those who are not eating low-carb. The meat was tender and tossed in the perfect amount of dressing. This was one of the better Greek Salads I've had with Gyro meat.   Apollonia has a great location, it is just half a block from the intersection of Gravois & Loughborough. If you do not nab one of the prime parking spots on Gravois in front, don't worry there is a prime parking lot behind the restaurant with a walkway directly to the front entrance.  The service was a little slow, I think our server was overwhelmed with a party of twelve. Even with the help of a co-worker our orders came out of the kitchen at a slow pace. However, they were extremely friendly and hospitable making Apollina worthy of a future visit.

I came back and I can tell you, I will not be back again. They just do not impress me in any way shape or form.  My rating is really 2 1/2 stars because the food is bland and not that memorable for me, but for others it may be good bar food.   This visit we ordered, Chicken Wings - Hot, Buffalo Chicken Salad, Caesar Salad and Margherita Pizza. Tonight our drink of choice was ice tea.  Listed below is how I rate the before mentioned food.   Chicken Wings - The wings themselves were good size, meaty and juicy. They were coated heavily in a breading, one of us liked the breading and one did not.  However, we both liked the flavor of the sauce and juiciness of the meat.   Caesar Salad - It's a Caesar Salad with romaine lettuce and a creamy dressing. Reminded me of those Caesar Salads in a bag you can buy at a grocery store.  On our servers recommendation we added a Grilled Chicken Breast, which was a nice bonus. The entire breast was placed on top of the salad with slashes through it, giving the illusion that it was sliced through. It was not, making the first bite of chicken awkward.   Buffalo Chicken Salad - Iceberg & Romaine lettuce, red onion, tomato, Grilled Chicken Breast, Crumbled Blue Cheese, Homemade Croutons and a Spicy Buffalo Ranch Dressing. The chicken breast was the best thing of this salad, huge, grilled well, juicy and spicy as hell. This was the first salad that I've seen that they seemed to be stingy on lettuce. There was more breast then lettuce. I saw very little crumbled blue cheese and only had three croutons on the entire salad. Again, the breast was not sliced completely through resulting in picking up the entire breast with the first jab of the fork.   Margherita Pizza - Oblong shaped and cut into squares - nice presentation.  The crust was thin and crispy, kind of had a crunch to it when you bite into your slice.  Their homemade red sauce had a "little" spice to it, giving it a tang. The Roma Tomatoes were ripe and thinly sliced and they strategically placed the fresh Mozzarella Cheese on top of the tomatoes. The menu stated it is also made with fresh basil, it may of been fresh at some time but not on our pizza.  It was not dried basil, but the freshness was gone from what we experienced. We did not finish the pizza and I had the leftovers for lunch the next day. The crust of course lost its' crispness, but the flavor was actually better cold. (Disclaimer: I am a fan of cold pizza)  Our server was friendly and chatty and the bus boys were very attentive to clearing our table and refilling our tea. The service is what allowed them to keep the 3 Stars instead of being dropped to 2.

I agree with Jackie M., I heart the new JCP.   Previously I only shopped here when I needed gifts for my mom, or I was in instant need of a new belt or tie and did not want to drive to The Galleria. Back then, I remember this store to crowded with racks, poor merchandising and not what I was looking for. Now I see it through an entire different view.   Again, I was in instant need of new pants for work and did not want to drive to the nearest Macy's. I popped into JCP at Hampton Village and was pleased to find  the navy Dockers I needed available. However, once I started searching for my size, it was not available. Bummer. Seeing their display of St. John's slacks, I proceeded to check them out. Navy, check. Flat Front, check. Acceptable Fabric Content, check. My size, check. They had everything I needed and a lower price then Dockers. As Charlie Sheen would say, "Winning".  I've worn them several times already and love them.   I also took note of other items that are staples in a mans' wardrobe; shorts, Levi's and sport shirts. Found several items that I liked and to be honest with you, if I go back to purchase them, I do not think anyone would be wise enough to know they came from JCP.   JCP, you've changed your image and I'm a new fan.

Once you have pancakes at The Original Pancake House, you'll never eat them at any other breakfast joint. Yes, they are that good. They are made with rich, flavorful buttermilk and grilled to a perfect golden color.  Then served with whipped butter and maple syrup. They're also the perfect size, about 6" in circumference. If their plain pancakes are this amazing, I can only imagine how off the charts the flavored one will be.   The BF enjoyed the Bacon Works, which includes two eggs any style, two slices (extra long slices) of bacon, hashbrowns and a short stack of three pancakes.  The eggs were done over easy, the hashbrowns extra crispy and the bacon was cut wide and long.  All three got a thumbs up from the BF and the sample bites I got, I must agree.   I tried one of their Oven Baked Omelette's with Egg White, Spinach, Turkey Sausage and Feta Cheese. It was puffy, fluffy and oozed with feta cheese. I was expecting ground turkey sausage, but was surprised to see that they use link sausage and dice it to bite size pieces.  I wish they stuffed more spinach in, but the normal person most likely would have been satisfied. I just like spinach and wanted more.   Knowing how great the pancakes are now, I regret that I declined the side of pancakes and substituted them for hashbrowns. However, I did enjoy my hashbrowns. They are grated  fresh in house from Idaho potatoes. Best of all, when you ask for extra crispy, they get it and so do you.   The ambiance is a large open space with natural light spilling in through multiple skylights. In winter we'll be able to enjoy a fireplace that is open on both sides. Service was quick and friendly. Our server, knew the menu and made suggestions just as if she were selling an upscale dinner menu.  First Watch should be scared, TOPH is going to be some serious competition in the Breakfast of Champions category.

2/3's of the way to work from my house sits a Hardees & Red Burrito restaurant. It is located on Route 3, close to the 270 interchange.  It's a weird little area of Granite City, but I over look that and just get my morning needs filled.   Since working in IL, I have only stopped here three times for a morning coffee and some type of breakfast biscuit. This morning when I checked in I was named Duke, with no fanfare. The workers went about with their morning duties as if I didn't exist. Finally someone spoke up and said, "we'll be with you soon, Sir". At least I got the respect of being called, Sir. I admit I arrived right as the doors were being opened, (5AM) but stop the morning busy work and give me my coffee. That sounded a little bitchy, sorry about that.   All I've ever gotten here is coffee, a sausage or steak biscuit and today I went totally crazy and had a small order of hash browns. It's typical fast food breakfast and beats stopping at the QT closer to work. It fills the morning void in my stomach and makes me whole again.   The staff is pleasant, considering it is not even dawn when I visit.  Kinda weird being Duke of a place your not totally excited about, but I'm glad it fills my morning needs when it's required.

Did I feel as if I were in New Orleans? No, but it was close enough for a winter night.   We started out with cocktails and an order of Mussels Sauvignon. Cocktails were strong, with only needing some tweaking to make them perfect. My friends Brandy Milk Punch was good, flavor-wise, but was served over ice, instead of straight up like it is in New Orleans. The only flaw with my Manhattan, was the cherry. I prefer the dark cherry garnish over the maraschino type. Otherwise, Cheers!  The mussels were plentiful enough for two to share as an appetizer. If one person wanted too, it could easily be an entree. They use Atlantic Blue mussels and prepare them in a red wine tomato bouillon. Since two of were sharing, we needed to ask for more toasted French bread. When enjoying mussels it is not complete, without the grilled bread to soak up the savory broth.  After my half of the mussels, all I wanted for dinner was a simple Who Dat Creole Burger, served with fries. It was a half pound burger with creole seasoning, grilled perfectly to my medium rare specifications. As garnishments they provided shaved Vidalia onion, romaine lettuce, a Creole tomato and a cherry pickle and all was presented on a butter toasted baguette. My fries were a overly unhealthy portion, but some how I still managed to eat them all. I think I was able to do it because, they were not overly salted and were also seasoned with my favorite spice, black pepper.   My lady friend went real New Orleans and ordered the; Fried Oyster Po Boy. How could she go wrong with hand-breaded Pass Christian oysters in red Cajun gravy? Hers' also came with;  romaine lettuce, a Creole tomato, cherry pickle and had the bonus of Parmesan. It too, was served on a butter toasted baguette. It was presented open faced, and there is no way a lady or man could eat it neatly as a sandwich. She opted to enjoy this Southern decadence with a fork.   Neither of us had room for dessert, but may-be next time. I got an Entertainment Coupon book for Christmas and Evangeline's Bistro has one for BOGO up to $18. So you know I'll be back. I'd be back even without a coupon.   When: December 13, 2015 Why: Late Dinner after shopping

My God, I thought we'd never find a place to park.  Searching for a parking space here was like holiday shopping at The Galleria. I do not know how many times we had to circle the lot before we found an opening.  Ha Ha, just kidding.  As George N. says, this parking lot is gigantic and only has 4 or 5 cars in it at a time. Makes me wonder, what this use to be before a Rothman's that it needed such a large parking lot.   Our salesman looked as if he were an extra on the show, "Jersey Shore".  If you can stereotype used car and furniture salesman, he fit the mold.  He was slick, smooth talking, but not overly pushy. He said something to the effect of, I am not here to "sell" to you, but to "assist"  you in finding what you need.   He showed us an area that had all of their club type chairs lined up in rows like little soldiers. He then scurried off to greet another customer. He was good at bouncing back and forth between customers. The row of chairs  wasn't much for visual merchandising, but it made it easy to walk down the row and say, "No, No, Maybe, No, etc. etc.".   Our salesman also pointed out their clearance area which was in the next room.  The clearance room reminded me of the Island of Unwanted Toys, each piece wanting to be in a home for the holidays.   After living in Saint Louis for 33 years, I finally visited  Rothman's and I can tell you it is not  my style of furniture.  Not sure who their demographic is, but it is not me.

In the words of Stephanie S., "Not bad!".  In our search of  3 club chairs to create a conversation area in our living room, Phillips was either stop 3 or 4. Siri my new assistant has been great in helping me make notes and take pictures of the chairs we are considering and right now Phillips is in second place and very close to first.   What I liked about PFC was that they did not have an up-charge for changing the fabric from the one on the floor.   We're in no hurry, so waiting  the extra 6 weeks is not an issue for us. They have two different chairs that we like, and only the one style would we want to change the fabric. Our saleslady showed us the other fabrics available and I'd ruffly say there had to be close to 50. With that many to select from, I'm confident when we make the final decision on our chairs, we'll find one to match our decor.   The store was fairly busy the day we shopped and the sales professional still made us feel welcome and did not rush us.  She truly listened to my request and asked open ended questions to get more information so she could understand my likes and dislikes.   If we do not buy our club chairs here, I am confident we'll be back for something else in the future. Even when you do not buy, receiving good customer service gives you reason to return.

The boss treated to lunch today, and part of our order came from Papa John's. We had some team members who appreciate a more traditional crust over the St. Louis thin crust, so their choice was Papa.   Papa may be in the house, but his pizza just doesn't make the cut.  I will admit the topping were plentiful and there was plenty of cheese, but it was tuff and chewy.   Delivery girl was just so-so, nothing to write about. When you deliver to me, I want to see some gratitude, make me want to order from you again.   I am done with larger pizza chains, I am learning that the privately owned and those who only have a shop or two are the ones who are truly mastering the art of pizza.   The next time the boss treats to lunch, I taking charge and driving outside the city limits and exposing my co-workers to a true pizza experience.

Hello Lola, and welcome back to the good graces of Stevie B.  As you can see in my previous reviews, I went from 5 to 2 stars in my reviews. That is a big drastic change and I commend the management of Lola's for reaching out to me to address my disappointments. They listened, agreed and took action. I will be open and honest with you in saying a portion of my recent visit was covered by a gift card from their management. However, it in no way influenced the upgrade to 4 stars. They re-earned each and everyone of them.   Our visit was with a friend who was leaving St Louis for New York to attend Columbia University, on a full ride scholarship. Damn, I've got some smart friends. To be fair, I introduced myself and let them know I was dining with a management gift card. No surprise here, they knew who I was, thanks to Yelp. Chris was off that night, but happened to be in for a private party and still made time to chat. He reminded me that we meet on my first visit to Lola and that he would look for my new review.   We started off with cocktails and an order of Tempura Fried Calamari with Cajun Aioli. It was served hot and the pieces were huge. The batter was crispy and flavorful. We all favor the tentacles were digging to see who could find the most. I am not a fan of dipping, (except for fries) but I did like the Cajun Aioli and our guest really liked it's kick.   Brad had the Tuna Nicolse, which was seared Ahi Tuna served on fresh green beans, hard boiled egg, Kalamata olives & field greens tossed in Tarragon Vinaigrette. Take note of the picture, the tuna was seared perfectly. I could also see this dish served with salmon, too. We keep fresh tarragon on hand at home so the tarragon vinaigrette was a big hit.   Our guest had the Carmen. Tenderloin, Boursin Cheese & Wild Mushrooms - yum. Topped with fried shallots, (more yum) mixed greens  and balsamic reduction. You really can't go wrong with tenderloin, cheese  and mushrooms. We do recommend getting the balsamic reduction on  the side if possible. That way you have control like you do when getting  salad dressing on the side. On our visit, the balsamic had a heavy pour  and dominated the flavor. The tenderloin is to good to have that happen.   I love mussels and when I see them on a menu I've got to have them. For my meal I enjoyed the Mussels Pernod and a side of Pomme Friets with roasted Garlic Aioli and Red Pepper Ketchup.  Next time, I'll make a meal of just the mussels, baguette and a bottle of Pinot Grigio.   They were Prince Edward island Mussels with Pernod, shaved fennel, cherry tomatoes, shallots, garlic & butter. I sometimes judge mussels by the broth, and I could not keep my friends from dipping bread in my bowl of mussels. A few times they almost got jabbed with a fork.   The Pomme Friets proved themselves to be a pleasurable side to the mussels. The Red Pepper Ketchup was a perfect accent. Is it available by the bottle?  The only thing that kept them from regaining the 5 star rating was our finale; their Creme Brûlée. It was over baked and over produced/presented. Make it simple, a good Creme Brûlée can stand on it's flavor alone.   The service was attentive and friendly. They made sure everything was to our satisfaction without making it an overkill.   So in closing, good job Lola. We'll be back.

21 days in to the new year and I am sticking to my resolutions of going to the gym and eating more healthy. After a hard work out at Club Fitness, I wanted to keep the momentum going by having a healthy breakfast. I knew I had errands to run in west county and remembered First Watch had a section on their menu called, "Healthier Side", so off we went to the suburbs.   We were cheerfully greeted by a waitress who seated us at one of the first tables near the door. Not bad, but every time a new patron entered, we were hit by a gust of winter air. We passed on coffee, having had enough at home and just opted for water. I knew they brought you a craft of coffee, but I thought bringing us a pitcher of H2O filled with ice and slices of lemon was a nice touch. After a gym workout, we were still thirsty.   I stuck to my plan and ordered the "Healthy Turkey". It is an egg white omelet with turkey, house roasted onions, tomatoes, spinach and feta cheese. Served with a dry English Muffin. I have never had a egg white omelet, I'd only heard about them on "The Biggest Loser" and since I am trying to lose, I thought I'd give it a try. I am now a fan, it was full of flavor just like a normal omelet, just looked bland due to the lack of color. The spinach, onion, turkey and feta cheese would make any omelet flavorful.   My biggest concern was the "dry" English Muffin. Dry just makes you want to say, yuck. To my surprise the dry English Muffin was laid upon four slices of beautiful red tomato. I hate plain tomato. Or at least I thought I did. I had no choice, but to dress up a dry EM with those tomatoes. One slice perfectly covered the muffin, I added a little salt, pepper and a dash or two of Cholula and my previous opinion of a plain tomato had been changed.   The SO  wasn't as strong as I, he went with the daily special which was a Spicy Chicken Sausage Skillet. It was a typical skillet; the sausage, sautéed onion, red & green pepper, cheddar and jack cheese and scrambled eggs a top grilled potatoes in a skillet. It looked good and he did ask if I wanted a taste, but I replied, "be gone Satan."  This Des Peres location is great. After breakfast or lunch you can shop Trader Joe's for groceries  and Treats Unleashed for your Fur-Babies.

For the last three years I have been Yelping and in a relationship with a professional chef. During these past years, I have gained 35 lbs. as a result of experiencing multitudes of fabulous foods. I knew I needed to do something, but my recent visit with the doctor confirmed the fact. I had gotten fat and need to lose weight.   I choose this Club Fitness to help me get back in shape. It not only is close to home, but the staff has a positive attitude in their approach to helping you achieve your goals. There's plenty of Cardio equipment, free weights and machines that I have never had to wait. I also like the mix of members, you have the buff ones you strive to be, ones like you and those that make you look hot. I checked out another gym on Hampton, but their staff and clientele had me feeling like a "the biggest loser" and not in a winning way.   Another big plus is the cleanliness. Not only does the staff keep the facilities clean, but members respect each other by wiping down and cleaning the equipment after a sweaty workout.  The only thing I could recommend is giving the mens' locker room a face lift. It's clean, but is showing some wear & tear. Glad I live close and really do not have a need to  use the locker room.

Lola, what happened to you? I was there last night with a group of seven for Yelp Eats Out and I was totally disappointed in you.  As we were leaving we discussed our # of stars and our consensus was 3. As I sit down to write this review, I could not bring myself to give you a 3. There is an old saying, "if it's not broken, don't fix it", Lola you are broken, now fix it.  I'm a simple man when it comes to drinks, give me vodka and I'm happy. However to night you were out of many call brands and finally had to go with a flavored one. That was okay, but how can you be out of three name brand vodkas at the same time?  My meal started out with envy, the Polenta Fries looked way better then my Calamari.  The Calamari was served cold, not luke warm, but cold. It was also flavorless. The sauce provided for dipping had a nice kick to it, just wish my Calamari was warm.   My main entree was the Cajun Chicken breast.  The Chicken breast was sliced into four slices that were seasoned/blackened very well. The meat was also moist and tender. However, the red beans and rice were a sad mess. Those reading this review, look at the picture I posted and ask yourself, would you serve this to a guest? I've had better red beans and rice at a chain chicken joint.  Now for the Blueberry Bread Pudding, it was a total disappointment.  I have never experienced a drier bread pudding then yours. We were actually thumping the top of it with our spoons and it sounded as if we were knocking on the front door of a friends house. As Miss Stephanie said, "even more blueberry sauce could not help this pudding".   Lola, what happened? My first review was a 5 and now you are getting a 2 and a place on my No-No List. I can understand one out of my three items being off, but tonight you struck out.  I'll end on a positive note, our server was cute and charming.

Great Maplewood location, providing a larger space to produce more of those great chocolates and brittle. The bacon brittle and sea salt caramels are my favorites.   Same great friendly customer service.   Now I have one close to work and one close to home. I am a happy chocoholic.

I guess I need to lower my standards and expectations. I really was expecting to have my Sombrero blown off, with some fantastic creative Mexican food. Instead, I received food that wasn't worth writting home about, so here I am on Yelp telling you all about it.   First off, they did a fantastic job converting the old Rothchild's  store into a chic upscale Mexican restaurant. The large windows, not only give you natural light, but provide you entertainment watching all the exccite passing by on McPherson and Euclid Avenues. I prefer the booth seating over the tables, but a table directly next to the window can be a prime seat.    As we entered we were cheerfully greeted by a host and a hostess and taken to our booth by third young lady. It took three people to seat a table of two. As we waited for our server, we studied the list of Margaritas as if we were cramming for a final exam.  I was laughing and making fun that they had Margaritas on "Tap" and "Hand Shakin".  Who would order a Margarita that would come from a tap? Not me, I want mine hand made and shaken.    When our server arrived we immediately ordered  two hand shaken Margaritas, the Classica and Tamarindo Margaritas. We also informed him that we'll be wanting the Tableside Guacamole. He left to fetch our drinks, so we could narrow down our taco choices. When he returned with our drinks, I was shocked at the size, they were smaller then most Margaritas that I have enjoyed.  The Classica  didn't fill the glass and the Tamarindo looked and tasted like dirty dish water.  We ordered six tacos: Hongos, Al Carbon, Grilled Fish, Octo, Chicken Tinga and Chapulines.   Now it was time for the show, or at least that is what I was expecting when you order Tableside Guacamole. When I order an item to made table side, I want a show. If you can not give me theatrics, at least give me a monologue. Our server just went through the motions without an explanation of anything. As we would ask questions, he stumbled to answer them. It was as if he was going through steps and motions not know what or why he was doing them.  The finished product was good and enjoyable, but knock two bucks off the inflated price, make it in the kitchen and call it a day.  The large bucket of chips that accompany the Guacamole was more then enough for two+ people to enjoy the entire bowl.   When you arrive, you do receive a small bucket of chip and salsa. Refills are 95¢, which I think is fair. No need to have those who eat the chips as theri meal  eating through the bottom. I liked the chips, they are thinner then most Mexican places and ours were not as salty. The salsa for me was also pleasant. It had just enough spice, wasn't overly chunky and not a puree either.   Before our tacos arrived I needed another Margarita, but was not impressed with the ones we already had.  At that moment a tall chilled glass filled with a Margarita passed our table. I asked our server, which one was that Margarita? He told me it was the one on tap. I said, I know I'm going to hell for doing this, but I'll try one. I've been saved! Not only have I been saved, but I learned not to stick my nose up at Margaritas on tap. This tap Margarita was better then the premium hand shaken one. So when at Gringo's order the Gringo Margarita and save yourself $2. That will get you two refills of chips and salsa.   Now to tell you about the taco. I'll tell you about them in descending order:  Chapulines - Sautedd Grasshoppers. It's one the menu, it's unique you've got to try it, right? Not in your right mind. The BF took one bite and spit it out, pronto. I already had my bite, as he was removing his so I had no choice but to chew and swallow. Remember, Nice People Swallow. Would I have taken a second bite? NO!!!  Am I glad I had the experience? Yes, it will be good cocktail party conversation.   Octo Taco - Grilled octopus. Chef needs to learn how to prepare octopus. The Black bean puree was a nice accent, but was lost in the chewy fishy octopus. (Yes, I've had octopus before and liked it)  Al Carbon - Hanger Steak, citrus slaw with red Chimichurri. Good flavor, but steak was a little on the tuff side.   Chicken Tinga - Breast of Chicken, ripe avacado, tomato  chipotle and a touch of cilantro made for a tasty taco.   Grilled Fish -  Napa Cabbage Slaw, Fish, chipotle crema and toasted pepitas. I would have liked the fish to be multiple smaller piece instead of a large wedge, but the flavors were above average.   Hongos - Has me scared, I think I may be going vegetarian. I loved the Ozark Forest Mushrooms with the black bean puree, fresh arugula. Very refreshing and healthy.   It was a 50/50 crap shoot on the tacos, being somewhat good. Their still new and the menu has other offerings, so I will be back. With a name like, Gringo I was expecting so much more on my first visit. As the BF said, "Gringo. Good name! No self respecting Latino would claim credit"

When: March 6 Why: Traditional Sunday Dinner  We decided we wanted to have a traditional Sunday dinner, so we choose fried chicken. It is amazing how a television commercial promoting 10 pieces for $10 pushes you over the edge. (Next Sunday, I'm cooking a pot roast myself.)  I remember when all KFC had was the original flavor. Now you get to choose between, original, crispy and grilled.  We mixed our bucket with original and crispy. For an extra $6, I got to add two sides and four biscuits. I love the Cole Slaw. In fact I have been know to buy large containers, place in a "cover dish" and take it to a pot luck picnic. We selected Mash Potatoes as our other side, fried chicken and MP's just seem to go together. I'd prefer a nice white milk gravy, but their brown is seasoned well.   What made this KFC stand out was the customer service. The young ladies behind the counter were cheerful and actually seemed to be enjoying their job. Brad loves thighs so I asked the young lady if she could  make sure we got two thighs in each flavor. She giggled at the way I asked her and said she'd do her best. I didn't care what the other six were as long as he had his thighs. She made it happen.  For those of you who are doing math and figuring 10 pieces is a lot for two people, don't worry. Four pieces were left over for lunch the next day.

I have gotta tell you, our service was over the top and the food was very good.  We started our night out at the bar with cocktails. The bartender Jason was very personable and charming. He always checked in with us to make sure a good time was being had by all.  He remembered our drinks and I love it when a mixologist remembers my drink. It shows an extra effort in customer service  After a couple rounds of drinks, we were ready for dinner. We informed the hostess who was cute as a button (I never did understand that expression, are buttons really cute?), that were ready to be seated. We wanted a table up on the raised platform, but it was all reserved for a large private party and had to settle on a table by the windows. Which ended up being the better choice.   Our waiter was attentive, knew his menu and how to sell each featured entree. In  fact he sold two of them so well, that we only experienced two of their entrees. If I had to choose between the two, I'd have to go with the one that Jillian and I enjoyed; Grilled Salmon served with Grilled Asparagus and Couscous. They grilled it to a perfect medium-rare and the asparagus was grilled to the right tenderness. I am always amazed how I can eat salmon medium-rare, but don't you dare offer me sushi.   Brad and Brent had the Bison Hanger Steak which was served with Mashed Potatoes and Green Beans. Their Bison was so tender, it could be sliced with your fork and you could tell the mashed potatoes were whipped with whole milk. Let's not forget green beans that were prepared with the right snap  Portions were huge, so huge that we had to ask for a take-me-home box. To my surprise, they offer a totally eco-friendly container.   Good liquor, good food, good service and eco-friendly containers for carryout will bring me back for another visit.

I am sad to say, I am subtracting a star and removing Porter's from my Crispy Chicken List. Our last two dinners were lackluster and if either of them were my first experience at Porter's I never would have had the love affair I did with them. They seem to have lost their focus on both customer service and frying up crispy chicken.

Cupcakes are the perfect size cake in my opinion. They provide portion control and satisfy the desire for something sweet.   The presentation here at The Cup, is fantastic. They decorate each cupcake as if it were a full sized cake. Making them a perfect treat or for celebrating a special event. Their staff is polite and engaging, making you want to return time and time again.   My favorite is by far the Red Velvet. It is always moist and rich in flavor.  Another one that I favor is Raspberry Truffle, yummy yummy.   I know they do a fine business here, I just wish they were on the main drag of Maryland instead of being hidden in the "rear". I think more people would notice them and it would bring in more new biz. I myself forget about them when I'm in the Plaza. Out of sight , out of mind and these cupcakes are too good to miss out on.   My next party or celebration,  desserts are coming from The Cup.

Brian M. has made a valid point, the one in Chicago on State Street is better. However, shopping on State Street and Michigan Avenue in Chicago is always better then shopping here in the Lou. We've got a better baseball team and they have better shopping. I think that is fair.   I have found this Nordstrom to still fill my needs for men's' accessories, casual clothes and a few home items as well. My newest obsession is their socks. They offer so many brands and colorful patterns. I love being able to wear weird and colorful socks with my work uniform and when I go out causally dressed. It's a little way that a guy can show his true personality.  Also, the belt selection is vast enough that I can find one for jeans and for a suit as well.   The fun of searching comes in when you shop for shirts on their circular racks. Don't always count on your size being in between the appropriate markers. Glance over the other sections and if you see a print, color or pattern you like, check the size it may just be yours. Some shoppers are known to not put things back where they belong, or they could be hiding it to return the next day.  I've snagged a couple of good finds that way. I have also been known to be the one who hides the shirt too. (My confession for the week)  I love the Rack in Chicago, I'm a fan of this one and can't wait to finally check out the one in West County. I am sure they give that location better merchandise then Brentwood.

Disclaimer: I really wanted to give Little Hills a 2, but they offer a 25% discount to Yelpers who check in on their smart phones, so I bumped them up a star for supporting Yelp.   Little Hills has a great patio, unfortunately when I was there the weather was not allowing outdoor dining. I was seated in the little room to the left of the bar that overlooks the patio. I was the only one in there and from the looks of the dust on everything, no one had been in there for some time.  Daily maintenance would help this from happening.   I love chicken wings and burgers with pepper cheese and have list on Yelp for those places that impress me with theirs. LHW will not make either of those list.  My wings came out first as an appetizer. Flavor was good, but they were cold. I mean cold, not even luke warm. I would have sent them back, but I rarely saw my server since I was the only one in the room. I couldn't even get the attention of the hostess and a couple of female servers who were talking "dirt" about a co-worker.  They were ripping her up on side and down the other and everyone could here. Damn, I miss All My Children.   I ate some of the wings cold and pushed the others aside. I also found it odd that the celery was presented diced instead of sticks. My burger followed fairly quick after wards and had huge well seasoned steak fries as a side. I prefer hearty steak fries and these made up for cold wings. My burger was overcooked from what I ordered, but it had my favorite cheese.  Once again, since I was the only one in the room there was no followup on my meal. I ate my well done burger, which still had decent flavor. (Medium Rare would have been better)  My server showed up with my check and I showed him my check-in on Yelp to get the 25% discount. He said, "what is that?". It is a discount for checking into this restaurant on Yelp. "Can I show this to my manager?".  I said, yes thinking he'd go get his manager. Oh no, he grabbed my phone and off he went. Manager claimed she did not know what it was, but she'd honor it. I thanked her for her kindness and suggested she check with owners or other managers, because I was confident she'd see it again.  I was ready to leave, but really didn't want to go. Those girls were still talking dirt, some serious dirt. I think they've missed their calling in life, they need to be writing scripts for the new GCB series.

Sometimes I hate the fact that I get emailing from Sur La Table. They are always tempting me and luring me out to their store, which can be a dangerous thing. I see things I need or want in their e-catalog and then when I get out to the brick and mortar store I end up spending more $.   We were on a mission for one of those meat thermometers probes that lets you know when the meat is done by a digital reader on your counter.  I researched the night before and Sur La Table had the one we were looking for. When we arrived, I was amazed at the even larger selection of styles and models they had. What impresses me most about SLT, is someone there is always able to give a true testimonial of the product you are interested in purchasing.  Surprisingly, it is not always the higher priced item that they recommend.  Honesty is good customer service.   When shopping here, always be sure to check out the "Clearance Corner" in the back right side of the store.  This last visit we got a juicer for $14.99 that was originally $60.  It may be Lime Green, but who cares you saved some $'s. Besides, you'll only have it out when you are making fresh orange juice or lemonade.   Great kitchen gadget and accessory store. Between here and C&B my kitchen is to die for.

OMG! Who knew? I didn't know until my friend Norma, took me here on a shopping outing. She had a coupon she wanted to redeem and as we browsed the store I was in total amazement. I was totally blown away by the selection and prices.   It's a big box like Lowe's and Home Depot minus all the bullshit. By that I mean, there is no lumber, garden shop or appliances. They totally focus on tools and hardware. I saw things I have always wanted at lower prices and discovered new gadgets that I never knew I wanted or needed.   If you go, by all means sign up for their mailings and e-mails. You'll receive coupons that will get you discounts on their already low prices. If your a handyman or handywoman, you owe it to yourself to check Harbor Freight Tools out.

Great south city dive bar. You do not come here for the service or the ambiance. You come here for the good BBQ and the neighborhood camaraderie . My most recent visit was for a UYE, which ended up being just me and Norma. Thank goodness we had smart phones and were able to check  the Yelp App and see that everyone else had bailed for some reason or another.  Oh well, they just missed out on some good south city BBQ.   I enjoyed a couple of Schafly IPA's on draft and Ms Norma was drinking vodka and tonic tall. Filling a beer glass is easy, but some how they had trouble with  making a simple vodka and tonic. They were very stingy with the pour of vodka, her drinks were extremely weak.   We started our UYE with a Smoked Chicken Wing and we each had an Atomic Turd. The turds were hollowed out Jalapeño peppers stuffed with G & W Sausage. They were very tasty, and packed some serious burn power. When we commented to our waitress how hot they were, they informed us most people do not eat the tip of the pepper. She explained that they can not clean all the seeds out at the tip and that is where the burn came from. As a server, I would have shared that tid-bit of information when I served the dish.    The Chicken Wings are their claim to fame and they were smokey and tender. I found them to be on the small size, but flavorful. They are priced individually at 90¢, for either piece little drummie or wing section. Raise the price to maybe $1.75  and give me both sections in an order.   I had a Jacked Up Sammy with brisket which was topped with melted Pepper Jack Cheese on a bun. The portion of meat was huge and it was cut with a fork tender making it easy to bite and chew. I had Mac-n-Cheese as my side and it was good enough to earn a spot on my Yelp List for Mac-n-Cheese. Elbow macaroni covered in a rich creamy cheese and baked just enough to give a crunchy top. YUM.   I forget the name of Norma's sandwich, but it began with Alabama. It had chicken , cheese and bacon, so it had to have been good. Her side was Potato Salad and we both commented how huge the chunks of  red potato were . She gave it a thumbs up approval.   The service was hit and miss. Our server was kind of  a space cadet. We had to wave her down more then once during our time there and she only had three other tables.  Then again, as I stated in my opening, you do not come here for the service, you come for the BBQ.   Great place to meet friends, chill, have a cold beer and some BBQ.

Dados is a fairly new little cafe in the St. Louis Hills neighborhood. For me it's a great place to grab a quick lunch. It's conveniently located on Hampton Avenue near Eichelberger.   I stopped by one day during the holidays, when I needed to rejuvenate myself after some power shopping. The menu is simple and my eyes were immediately drawn to the Mile High BLT. I can tell you, there is no comparison with the one you get at Crown Candy Kitchen. Dados does it way better. They toasted the bread perfectly, just enough mayo, crisp lettuce, fresh tomato and of course crisp and crunchy bacon. I was glad to see that the fries they offered as a side, were the thick cut Steak fries. They're my favorite. I would have liked them to have been fried a little more crisper, but my BLT was so good I didn't mind.   I plan to stop by again to try some of their Greek dishes like the salad and gyro. Also, a burger with those big steak fries would be a nice lunch, too.   When: December 11, 2015 Why: Lunch

I've been back to this TB a couple of times since my initial visit and have decided to lower their overall rating to 3 stars.  The ambiance and customer service are still 4 star worthy, but the food has dropped to 3 stars. It has become your typical TB fast food. Good for a quick cheap lunch or a post bar late night treat.   Today's visit was to experience the highly promoted "Dorito Taco" that is being chatted up and down on our local Yelp talk thread. It wasn't that bad, the shell really tasted like a dorito chip.  Would I want my taco shell to taste like a dorito all the time? Hell no, but this one time was okay. I do give extra credit points to TB for serving the dorito shell in a cardboard sleeve.  It prevented me from getting "orange" fingers.   Overall, I still say this is one of the best Taco Bells I have visited. As for the Dorito Taco I can at least say, "been there, ate that".

Have you ever wondered what the test kitchen looks like for Hardee's?  I am confident that it is clean and has some of the coolest kitchen gadgets and appliances. What I am curious to know is what the staff who creates their new menu items look like. They can not look like the sexy actors & models who appear in Hardee's commercials. Their high fat and calorie loaded menu items have to be created by little Pillsbury Dough boys and girls.   Being a fan of bacon, when I saw the new commercials for the Bacon Bacon Biscuit, I knew I'd be visiting soon. How can I resist a flaky buttery biscuit, filled with crispy bacon strips, Canadian bacon, cheddar cheese and a fluffy egg. I heard my arteries closing up as I ate my breakfast treat. Hardee's biscuits are by far the best fast food biscuits. I'd even say, they can beat some of the diners in quality. It is obvious they are made by hand and not frozen.   Now that I have tried the BBB, my next adventure will be their Jalapeno Burger. I'll be doing extra reps or time on the treadmill to burn those extra calories.

Southtown Pub is a good neighborhood dive bar that serves some delicious smoked BBQ. It is a dive bar, so there is no ambiance. The bartender who also is your server is friendly and knows how to sell their menu. Young ladies be sure to look into the kitchen and see the chef, you may find him to be good eye candy.  He looks like Daughtry.   What makes the bar food at SP unique, is nothing is fried. That is right, they are bar that serves food and they do not even have a fryer in their kitchen. It also seems wrong not to have fried food in bar, but once you experience their smoked meats you'll understand. However, it just seems weird eating wings without fries.   The wings are sold individually @ 65¢ and are huge, spicy and dry rubbed. They are smoked well and Meg T. is right no sauce needed the spicy rub is enough. Those of you who want to add sauce, they provide a six pack variety ranging from sweet to hot.  They offer sliders for $2.50 and you can choose from any of their five smoked meats; Pulled Pork, Pulled Chicken, Beef Brisket, Turkey and C&W Sausage. I forgot to ask, but I think it was a typo and they meant G&W Sausage over on Parker Avenue.  We ordered Beef Brisket and I'd say it was above average. It was tender and seasoned well just like our wings. When you look at the price paid, all the food was well worth the $'s.  For dessert we had to have the Bacon Chocolate Bread Pudding with Ice Cream. Why does everyone think they can just add bacon to anything and it will be fine. Bacon is good and Bread Pudding is good, but this creation is where two positives made a negative. It was served warm, with a scoop of chocolate chip ice cream on the side. The pudding was moist, but the bacon on top was cold and tough. I'd recommend adding a chocolate or caramel sauce.  SP is good and I'll be back, but I will not be in a hurry.

Thanks to my Entertainment Book I not only saved $7, but I got to experience a new place on The Hill. There are so many family owned tucked away on our "The Hill", that many of the little ones are well kept secrets. If it were not for my coupon, I may have never discovered Guido's.   We visited for lunch and after being seated informed our server of the coupon. She was so excited to see hear that it was our first time and that the coupon was our motivation. I wish other places had this upbeat positive attitude about patrons using coupons.   After reading over the menu, the BF went with the Muffuletta and Fries. We are on The Hill where some of the best Italian food is prepared in the city and he orders a deli sandwich. He loves Muffulettas and when he sees them on a menu, he loses all focus and can only order one thing and that would be a Muffuletta.   He enjoyed his sandwich, but didn't think it compared to ones that he has had at various deli's in the Saint Louis area. The French Fries were done the way fries should be done, crisp on the outside with a hot and meaty inside. They reminded me of the TV commercial where they hold a French Fry horizontal while they apply ketchup to the top and it holds the weight. You could hear a faint snap when you broke one in half.    I on the other hand, will eat the specialty of where I am dining. So, I took advantage of their daily pasta special which was a Seafood Penne. Goldilocks would have liked the portion, it was not to big, not to small, it was just right. I  also enjoyed a small Caesar salad, which was the perfect size to accompany my pasta.  Look forward to coming back and experiencing more of their Italian fare.

Meet several friends here for lunch, and I must admit I was pleasantly surprised. Being closely bonded with these friends, we shared our entree experiences. I had the Stuffed & Grilled Portabella Sandwich - FANTASTIC! (the favorite of all) I loved the combination of red pepper, asparagus, and avocado was amazing and the waffle fries were better then a steak cut french fry. My friends had the Fried Chicken Salad and the Red Lion Soft Cheddar Burger, and both were very good. The combination of beef, pork and lamb in the RL Burger adds a kick of flavor that will take you by surprise. The Fried Chicken Salad, is a huge salad with Chicken Tenders on top. I have said it before, this is not for a dieter. The staff was friendly and made our lunch a fun experience.

Only one visit to the new location and I am already feeling the love. It is way down south on Jefferson Avenue, directly across the street from the infamous Sump Coffee.  Parking at the old location was a challenge due to the horrid chicken place next door. Here, they have plenty of street parking and their own huge lot directly across the street. The new location also has patio sitting out front and in back, so you can enjoy outdoor dining when weather is permitting.   The food and menu is basically the same as the old location. The only difference is truly the ambiance. The quality of food is the same, you still have the same service staff and kitchen crews providing top notch service.   Prior to their move, I had one last visit at the original location. I indulged in their Chorizo-Queso Dip and a Pulled Pork Sandwich with House Cut Fries. The queso dip was the "must order" from Ian Froeb's STL 100 List 2016. Spare No Rib made the list for the second time and is totally worthy. It is such a cool restaurant and I love how they combine Mexican and BBQ all in one menu.  My Pulled Pork was served on a toasted bun, with cole slaw as the foundation. The pork was tender and smoked beautifully. It was seasoned well and with the cole slaw, I had no need to squirt any of the available sauces on top. The accompanying fries are hand cut, fried to a crisp and masterfully seasoned with only salt and pepper. Normally, I dip fries in ketchup, but here I am content eating them plain.  Visiting the new location, I started off with a cold 4 Hands beer and an order of Tortilla Chips and Salsa. Their chips amaze me, the are thick, warm and being addicted to salt, I love how on some of the chips you can see the salt. Even though you can visually see it, they are not overly salty. The offering of three different types of salsa always makes it a challenge for me to decide which one I like best. The chips and salsa are not free, they are a very affordable $4 and totally worth it. If you don't order them, you are missing out on some of the best in STL.   For my entree, I totally went off my regular pattern. Instead of ordering a couple of tacos or a BBQ plate, I went with; The Honest Burger. It's a simple burger, seasoned with only salt and pepper. I had cheddar cheese added to mine and it was garnished with; onion, lettuce and tomato. It is so simple and so good. As, with my Pulled Pork from an earlier visit, the Hand Cut Fries, still kick ass.   Love the new location and I'm glad I'll be able to enjoy Egg at the original location on Tuesday and Wednesday, my days off from work. For me, it's a win-win.   When: April 27 & October 25, 2016 Why: Lunch, New Location and Ian Froeb's STL 100

Warning: Do Not and I repeat Do Not order the Maple Sausage,  Egg and Cheese Biscuit.  In one simple word it is, "nasty".   When I saw the combinations of the two words, sausage and maple I thought Hardee's had created another tasty unique breakfast biscuit. I was wrong, this creation is a total miss. The three link sausages resting on top of the neatly folded scrambled egg did not do the biscuit justice. The maple flavoring tasted artificial and left an aftertaste in my mouth. Thankful I keep a toothbrush and paste in my locker at work.   This location is the midpoint between home and work, so it is a good place to refill my travel  mug with coffee if need be and to grab a morning biscuit if I didn't eat breakfast at home. The staff is always perky and friendly at 5:20 AM which is impressive.   I will still rely on this Hardee's  on certain mornings, but I will not order the Maple Sausage Biscuit again.  It is still haunting me 3 hours later.

So glad I gave Blaze, Kirkwood a second chance. They've worked the kinks out of their and they are on FIRE.   I love jalapeños and really love them on a pizza. Instead of creating my own as I usually do, I went with one of their signature pizzas. Their, Hot Link which has many of my favorite toppings, was delicious.   It is much more fun to walk down the line and watch them build your pizza then it is to watch the staff at one of those sandwich or Mexican restaurants who build it for you. My mouth actually fell open as I watched them pile all my toppings on of the spicy red sauce.   The Hot Link, is full of spiciness. In addition to the jalapeños, it is topped with sausage, black olives, red onion and banana peppers all smothered in mozzarella cheese. With  all the toppings, I couldn't eat the entire pizza, so I had enough left overs for the next day.  I had a cold slice for breakfast and re-heated a couple for lunch and it was still delicious.   Beverage? Blaze as I reported in my first review is a Coke restaurant. However, I recommend their Lemonade. It's so refreshing and not carbonated. (I'm on this new no carbonated drinks kick)  The staff is friendly and they actually look like they are having fun and enjoying themselves. If you're a first time visitor, they take the time to explain how the system works and literally walk you through the line.   I'll be back? - Yes, it is quick, easy and delicious.   When: March 7, 2019 Why: Lunch 1 PM

I'm not a shopper, I'm a dropper. I drop off donations to help change lives within my community.   The donation process is very easy. Just follow the signs that will lead to the back side of the store. There you'll find a loading dock for unloading all your goodies. One of their friendly workers will come out and help you unload your donation. Be patient, they may not come out immediately, but they're fairly quick. They'll also give you a signed and dated form for your charitable donation. The IRS likes them signed.   It is so easy to donate, you have no excuse to not clean out that closet or basement of all those things you no longer wear or need.   Will I return? - I "drop" by again real soon.   When: December 27, 2017 Why: Year End Donation

Fashion Forward and Classic frames at very reasonable prices. Customer service was great. I visited a couple of times and each time they took time to assist me in frame selection and to figure my out of pocket after insurance.   I'll be honest, I ended up ordering my new glasses from another optical store, that saved me more out of pocket $'s.  However, I still want to give SEE Eyewear 4 Stars for selection and service. My SO who does have insurance used a Groupon and got a great pair of glasses. I highly recommend SEE and will check them out again when it is time for new glasses.

I love this store. I have organized my basement and made my laundry room totally functional. Not to mention all the goodies they have for making a closet pop for a clothes horse like me.   I am a firm believer in you get what you pay for, and at CS you do pay a higher price, but it is so worth it. I recently needed a very small rolling rack to hang clothes to dry that can not go in the dryer and went to another store besides CS. The rack was only $10 and I thought, "hot damn, I've found a deal". The bargain rack fell apart within a week, it was no bargain. I took it back and headed to CS. The rack at CS was $24 and totally worth the additional $14.   My relationship with CS actually started a few years ago when I started to downsize my life and moved from a 3000 Square Foot Condo to a 1100 Square Foot house.  I have never been happier in my smaller space and CS showed me how to take advantage of every inch.   I agree with Sarah S., they have the coolest lunch boxes. I've bought two at CS and everyone always ask me where I found such a cute and functional lunch box.

Why buy your Halloween candy at the local drug store or warehouse club, when you have a local candy company in your hometown? If you haven't been to GCC, you've got to go and take a trip down memory lane. You'll find candies that you have forgotten about and they'll be at prices that will be easy on your wallet.   I pick up my Halloween candy here and am able to offer my little ghost and goblins full size instead of those midgets or fun size the other houses will be giving. This is also the place I stock up for the candy dishes at work. Yes, I said the plural word candies, not singular candy. We have issues.   This candy warehouse is a very well kept secret in STL and it shouldn't be.  Go support a local business and satisfy your sweet tooth.   Will I return? - When the candy dish is empty and every Halloween.   When: To embarrassed to tell Why: It's Halloween time

If someone asked me, "What is your favorite restaurant in St. Louis?" or "What is your go to restaurant, when you want to go out and grab a quick meal?" The answer would be the same for both questions and that is, "Polite Society". Why, you ask? It's an easy answer. I can get almost anything I want and they do it right.  I can stop by for a cocktail and one of their amazing appetizers. The Tempura Portobello, Shrimp & Grits and Deviled Eggs are three of my all time favorites. Recently I have gotten attached to  Braised Beef Bruschetta, which can almost be a meal if not being shared with a friend.   My three all time favorite entrees are; Bistro Steak, Diver Scallops and the infamous, The Jimmy Burger. You can honestly not go wrong with either of these. The Bistro Steak is tender and I always have it done medium rare. I'm a huge fan of Scallops and am very picky about how mine are prepared. For not being a restaurant that specializes in seafood, they knock it out of the park.   The Jimmy Burger, puts restaurants that specialize in nothing but burgers to shame. This double patty with American cheese, onion straws and a sweet smokey tomato glaze on a pretzel bun is a high class whopper that takes two hands to eat.   My newest discovery is on their fall menu, Cioppino. This fish stew is based with spicy tomatoes and then filled with; shrimp calamari, cod and mussels. It is served with a baguette, but I highly recommend that you order the Sweet Potato Cornbread that is served with Jalapeño Honey butter. It is the absolute be accompaniment.  Now let's talk dessert. They have a new pastry chef and she is turning out some amazing dishes. Currently I can only speak of two and they both made my sweet tooth extremely happy. The Triple Chocolate Cake is moist and a chocolate overload, which I enjoy being a chocaholic. The Tiramisu Crepe Cake is one of a kind. No lady fingers here, each layer and there are multiple layers is a paper thin crepe. This delightful dessert is not only unique, it is pure decadence of deliciousness.   Service is always friendly and attentive. I hope you go visit soon if you haven't already and find out why this is by far my favorite restaurant in STL.   I'll be back? - It's my favorite in STL.   When: Seriously, you don't want to know how many times.  Why: Again, I said it was my favorite.

I am not very experienced in Vietnamese cuisine, so I was excited for a new adventure when the International Supper Club decided to dine here. Normally, I would have asked one of the other diners to assist me in ordering, but tonight I went it alone. I saw one of my favorite items listed on the menu and took a major leap of faith and ordered it as my entree.   I started my evening out with a Mojito. I was totally surprised that a Vietnamese restaurant made probably the best Mojito that I have ever had. It was damn, good. Look at the picture I took, it's so refreshing. As an appetizer, I ordered Crispy Rolls. They were stuffed with shrimp and pork & they came with a lime sauce for dipping. I found these to be way better then a typical Chinese Egg Roll. I really like that ISC gets me to try new ethnic foods that normally I'd shun away.   For my entree, I ordered Curry Scallops. I love Sea Scallops. When I was ordering, it took me awhile to get the server to understand my question, "Are they sea or bay scallops?" He just kept telling me there were a lot of them. I prefer sea over bay, so when I realized he wasn't really understanding the question, I just took the risk and ordered them any way. Lucky for me, they were sea scallops and they were delicious. I'm not even a fan of curry, so this was a extra big risk and it paid off. I would happily order this entree again.   Our server may not have understood my scallop question, but he and his co-workers were friendly and very attentive to our group of 16 International diners. They didn't even blink an eye when they had to prepare multiple checks at the end of the meal.   Monsoon taught me not to be afraid of Vietnamese cuisine, so they easily deserve 4 Stars.

Like their sign says, "Where the beer and the bison burgers roam".  TS, knows how to serve up a ice cold beer and they truly know how to grill a bison burger. I've had bison at several bars here in the Lou and Trainwreck does it best. They understand the importance of making a bison burger rare to medium rare. Nothing ruins a burger quicker then over cooking it and so many other bars cook them like a regular burger.  Their long, crispy, slender seasoned fries are the perfect accompaniment to these burgers.   I wish they offered their chicken wings during lunch, but due to their popularity and the small kitchen they do not offer them during lunch. If you want to experience the wings, be sure to arrive after 2:30PM.  However, for those who have ice tea at lunch time, they offer all three of the major artificial sweeteners in addition to the real thing.   When you dine at Trainwreck Saloon, be sure to sign up for Telugo. It is a virtual punch card for your smart phone.  After you have paid your bill, they'll scan the QR Bar Code at the bar and after 10 scans, your 11th lunch is free.

It may not be original, but DAMN, The Dam is good. In fact, it is real good. The concept is smart. They offer easy carryout, a small dining area and my favorite option, go next door to The Amsterdam to enjoy a beer and have your food brought over when it is ready.  Their burgers are made with premium Black Angus beef. It is fresh, never frozen. Having been raised on a Black Angus farm, I appreciate it when I see a restaurant promoting Black Angus. Especially when it is  antibiotic and hormone free.   My burger of choice today was, The Dam. It's a two beef patty delight. One was topped with American and the other with Swiss. They were then placed between two slices of grilled Sourdough bread that had smears of their special Damn Sauce. I added grilled onions for a mere 75¢. It was perfect!  My friend and dining explorer, skipped the burgers and went for his favorite sandwich, The Muffalata. When ever he sees a Muffalato on a menu, he loses all self control and has to have one. The gentleman taking our order, told him that theirs was not the typical round Muffalata and he was comfortable with trying something new. Once it was served to him over at The Amsterdam, he declared it was the BEST Muffalata  he has ever eaten. I got to sneak a bite and I must say, I liked it better then some of the better known deli's in town.   We shared a order of Belgian Style Fries. I liked that their menu stated, extra crispy. It saved me having to make that request. The small order was enough for the two of us to enjoy with our huge sandwiches.
