The staff is friendly and as stated above, they are willing to deliver your order to the bar next door.   When: 30 Jan 2014 Why: Lunch

This review is long over due. If anyone here follows me Twitter, you have seen/heard me singing the praises of Polite Society. It easily is my favorite restaurant in STL and has become my go to for dinner. I easily dine here a couple times a week.   I have enjoyed a simple meal of PEI Mussels with a glass of white wine and a Jimmy Burger with a beer. In addition to these meals, I have also been delighted with their Diver Scallops, Lamb Chops and Bistro Steak. I like both my lamb and steak prepared medium rare and they've nailed it on both. The lamb chops were tender and succulent. They were better then any have had at a Greek restaurant and I use Greek as a standard for lamb.   If you need to get in a serving of your veggies for the day, you can not go wrong with their Asparagus, or Brussels Sprouts. The Potato Crisp are as equally as good as any that are served at a Irish Pub.   The cocktails are masterfully made. I am a classic cocktail drinker, usually enjoying an; Manhattan or Old Fashion. However, when here, their house, Bourbon Murray is my go to. I'm also a fan of Bloody Mary's and they kick it up a notch here. Not only do they have a spicy traditional red BM, but they also have created a green and yellow Bloody Mary as well. It makes it hard to decide which one to have at brunch.   The service is always friendly and professional. I feel as if I am in an upscale Cheers, where everyone knows my name. If you stop by to experience for yourself, look at the far corner of the bar, that is usually where I am seated.   Would I go again? - I'm going this morning for Brunch  When: Numerous times - look at all my pictures Why: Dinner & Brunch

I'm taking golf lessons through the community college and the classes meet here. A very convenient location and much more then just golf. They offer in addition to instruction, a driving range, mini golf, Par 3 golf course and batting cages.   The mix of customers is wide range, you have beginners like myself and seasoned athletes working to improve their game with both the club and bat. My instructor is friendly and patient, which is needed when dealing with a group of novice players. Other staff members I've had contact with are also very pleasant and accommodating to customers. I think they exude the positive attitude working in an environment  & sport they enjoy.   My only negative comment is parking.  Even though they have a large lot, parking here reminds me of Christmas at the mall. As one car backs out of a space, three cars appear out of nowhere wanting that space.   Have three more weeks of class and looking forward to signing up for the next level. Gotta be able to play golf with friends  & family instead of waiting at the 19th hole with a vodka martini in hand.  Wonder when they'll teach me to yell FORE! As a beginner, I think I'll be saying that often.

What other meat market offers you a beer while you are browsing over their meat counter? It may only be a Busch beer, but hey it's the thought that counts right?  It is actually kind of humorous to see customers sipping on beers waiting their turn to select some of the best bratwurst and sausages in the city.   It was my first visit to G&W, I had heard great stories so I bought a discount coupon off of one of those sites. It was a great deal and saved me $20. Being our first visit, we were like little children in a candy store. We were wanting it all and had a hard time narrowing it down. Our selection was their Original Bratwurst, which has been served at Grants Farm for over 30 years.  We also got  Andouille, a Cajun style sausage, which made a very tasty jambalaya.   We didn't stop at brats and sausages, we also got some ground beef for chili and I found the best Pepper Jack Cheese. Pepper Jack is by far my favorite cheese and this is the best I have found here in STL.   To go along with the sausages and brats they have a good selection of brown & yellow mustard's. They also have the famous Billy Goat Chips. Not having tried their new "Kicker" chips, we had to grab a bag of those as well.   The customer service is down home southern hospitality. Remember, they offer you a beer as you shop.   P. S.   Attention: Bambi Killers aka Deer Hunters  G&W does offer on site deer processing and they process each deer separately so that the meat you get is your sweet innocent little Bambi.   I thought this was an amazing service for a business located in a major city.

I could not have personally picked a better restaurant to fill this space that use to be filled by Milagro. The space has only been altered by some fresh coats of paint and different artwork. The food they served our group was equal to if not better then Layla in The Grove.   I really wanted a Kill Bill Burger, but I am dieting and went with a Caesar Salad anded Lamb as a protein. It was so filling and satisfying. I loved that they served the dressing on the side without asking, so I could control the amount I used. I was also impressed that the lamb was shaved and not large thin slices. It made it so much easier to mix with the Romaine lettuce and enjoy with each forkful.   I'm an early bird, so I always arrive at events early. I was so early for this ISC, that I sat at the bar and enjoyed a cocktail. I'm a big fan of Manhattans, so when I saw The Lux Capacitor on the cocktail menu, I knew I had to have one. It was very similar to a Manhattan and made with Makers Mark a favorite of mine. It was so delicious. Mike my bartender not only made a great cocktail, he offered excellent customer service. He created great conversation as I sat at the bar waiting for my friends to arrive.  I'll be back? - Yes, drop a few more pounds & I'll be back for that burger.   When: April 3, 2019 Why: ISC Gathering

Stellar! An absolutely delicious and delightful experience. Everything was totally on point, from the greeting, to the service and most definitely the food and cocktails. I highly recommend, Yellowbelly for your next dining experience.   My delightful experience began with an classic cocktail, Old Fashioned as I glanced over the menu. I quickly ordered the, Deviled Crab Fritters and an appetizer. The order came with 6 Fritters and a small cup of Passionfruit Mustard for dipping. The mustard was unique and tasty, I enjoyed it, but I enjoyed the scrumptious crab fritters plain, more.   For my entree, I choose the Wu Tang Clams. I also got an order of their Sea Biscuits (Cheddar). Discussing my order with Tim, he agreed the biscuits would be a good companion to the clams. The broth was so delicious and the soft cheddar biscuits allowed me to enjoy every drop.  The clams were combined with a Portuguese sausage, which gave it an extra salty kick that wasn't too overpowering.   My beverage of choice with the clams was their signature drink, "Yelllowbelly". I'm not normally a rum drinker, but this cocktail of two rums, coconut, turmeric, ginger falernum, pineapple & lime juice, had me wanting a pitcher. This is one of the best tropical cocktails I have ever had. I was ready for the beach or at least poolside at a resort.  I wanted dessert, but was not in the mood for Grandma's Coconut Cake.  So I enjoyed one more cocktail a, Pina Colada. It was refreshing and a perfect ending to an amazing first experience at this new restaurant.   I'll be back? - This will be the new place to be seen in the CWE  When: September 24, 2018 Why: It's Hot & New

I love Taste Cards, they get me out of my routine and give me discounts to experience new places. That is how I discovered Racanelli's in Webster Groves.  We stopped in for lunch and took advantage of a lunch special. Racanelli's is very generous with their lunch offerings. They allow you to order from the lunch menu between the hours of 11 AM and 4 PM. Hell, if you play it right you can have a late lunch or early dinner and save.   Racanelli's Choice Meal, was our selection for lunch. It gave us a 14" One Topping Pizza, either a Caesar or Garden Salad and two 24 oz Sodas. This definitely was enough for two, in fact we had leftovers for a late night snack. Okay I'll be honest, we also enjoyed an order of Cheese Garlic Bread with our Caesar Salad.  That is if you can really call it a Caesar Salad. It mainly was made of iceberg lettuce and the dressing was not creamy like most Caesar dressings. Normally I may have questioned it, but the Cheese Garlic Bread was a great accompaniment. Ordering at a counter, I was afraid everything would come out at once, but we did get to enjoy or salad and garlic bread first.   We were well half way through our salad when they brought our NY Style Pizza to the table. I liked that they had the traditional pizza stands to place our pizza on. Having those saves so much space on the table. For a one topping (Italian Sausage) pizza, which is enough for lunch, the pizza was fairly good. I can only imagine how tasty it could be with multiple toppings. The pizza was cut in pie slices, not those stupid STL Squares. Being cut in the pie slices made it easy to pick-up, fold and enjoy.   If you haven't eaten at Racanelli's, I say give them a try. If you haven't bought a deck of Taste Cards to save at 52 restaurants, I say buy a deck soon.

I overate and I don't care. Yes, it was that good and totally worth being stuffed to the brim.   You cannot beat their Pint & Slice deal. It is great for those of us who are craving pizza and just want that one slice of heaven. Unlike other places that sell pizza by the slice and you get to choose between; cheese, sausage or pepperoni. Felix's lets you choose from their entire menu, or you can create your own. Wow! That is giving your customer some great options.   Before I enjoyed my slice of heaven, I had to have an order of Felix's Trashed Wings. They just don't fry them once, they do it twice. This makes them extra crispy on the outside and the inside is still juicy and moist. After being twice fried, they smoother them in a not to spicy buffalo sauce. Then on top of the buffalo sauce, I had them drizzle Jalapeño Ranch. They also offered, Sweet & Spicy Thai Chili. I'm having to try that next time.   One pint, and an order of wings finished. Now to move on to a slice of pizza and another pint.  For my pizza I went with; Tamm Avenue. It's an Alfredo based pie with chicken, spinach, pepper bacon and artichoke. The toppings on my single slice were plentiful. This one slice was a meal all by itself.   The service was sensational - they were friendly and more attentive then some white linen restaurants. You could see the team work and camaraderie, which made for a pleasant and fun dining experience.   For those beer drinkers who want to know how what beers I enjoyed:  Wings - Grapefruit Sculpin - Ballast Point Brewing Pizza - Irish Red Ale - Six Mile Bridge  When: March 12, 2016 Why: Craving Pizza

Bob primarily sells to the wholesale market, but they've got their very own little retail store to serve us lovers of seafood. The staff is well knowledge and helpful in selecting your purchase. They assure you everything is fresh and encourage you to smell it before you buy it. The sniff test does works when buying seafood.   We stopped by today and picked up some farm raised Atlantic Mussels and a half dozen huge Atlantic caught sea scallops. You know I love mussels and sea scallops, since I have a list dedicated to them here on Yelp. Our purchase today was so fresh and cost friendly, I'm adding Bob's Seafood to both list. We may have done the cooking ourselves, but it's the same seafood we would have eaten at a restaurant. So it is so worthy of a place on my special list.

My Christmas goodies bag are once again going to have treats from Kakao. This year each bag is going to have a box of 5 Sea Salt Caramels, containing 3 milk and 2 dark chocolates.  These caramels are truly orgasmic. Some of the bags will also have chocolate scented pencils, Kakao Chap stick, Cocoa Grilling Rub and a chocolate Santa.  They have "Happy Holidays" box available but I choose the traditional brown box. The friendly staff also offered me holiday ribbon, but again I choose the traditional Kakao orange ribbon. One of the ladies asked me if I was sure, I guess she thought being a guy a needed help with my wrapping. I quickly explained to her that orange is my signature color and everyone would know it was from me having an orange ribbon. Her coworker giggled and said, you must be comfortable here with all our orange.   If you need stocking stuffers you should be shopping here. They've got it all in a chocolate theme. Just to give you some ideas of other items I bought; body scrub, hot coco mix, truffles and that previously mentioned chap stick that rivals our Yelp Stick.

I have owned three Hondas and all three of them came from St Louis Honda. The Service Department is excellent, I get everything done for my CRV here; check-ups, oil changes and anything else.  The service dept. staff is professional and it shows in their customer service.  I usually wait for my car, the waiting room is small but has WiFi which makes the time pass quickly.  Have a Honda or need a Honda, this is the place.

I am shocked that this restaurant made Ian Froeb's STL 100 2019. Don't get me wrong, I love me some Ben Poremba's restaurants, but this one fell short for me. I was expecting so much more and it was just an okay experience.   I sat at the bar and started out with, The Benevolent Martini. The menu stated that it was served extra chilled. Mine was luke warm. When I read extra chilled, I'm expecting frosting on the chilled glass. It was actually warmer then most Martinis I've had. For $15, I wanted a kick ass cocktail.   My first dish was the Charred Carrots. The carrots were tender and charred, but there was more citrus and pistachio nuts then carrots. However the seasoning from the elderflower and urfa pepper did make it an interesting and flavorful dish.   The second dish I ordered was, Lamb Meatballs. I will admit, they were huge and could have easily been shared by two people. Hint for date night. The lamb was complimented by a smoked tomato sauce. For me, the dish could have used a little more sauce, to make sure each bite of lamb had some with it. I would have like to seen the couscous on the bottom of the bowl and a foundation, instead of piled up next to the meatballs as a snowdrift. It did compliment the lamb.   The service was average, not as attentive as Ben's other restaurants. I was given follow-up, but when it was time for my check, I had to wait.   I'll give fair warning, the restaurant is small and intimate, which means it is a LOUD restaurant. You will hear every conversation in the restaurant and have a hard time hearing the one at your table.   Chances of returning? - Only if someone ask me to join them.  When: March 6, 2019 Why: Ian Froeb's STL 100 2019

I'm excited to say that I attended Hamilton's opening night. Not the musical, but the newest steakhouse in Saint Louis. I can proudly say, it was a standing ovation. Applause, Applause.   As my usual, I seated myself at the bar. I'll start off by saying, the remodel of closing off the upper level of Charleville Brewing Company, created a very comfortable and relaxing steakhouse. The restaurant itself seats 60 and the bar can accommodate an additional 12.   I started out with a, Fashion This. It was a modern twist on an, Old Fashioned. It went down very easy and was a great cocktail to sip and enjoy as I pondered my menu choices. Arriving early, I was able to take advantage to the Happy Hour menu. As an appetizer, I choose, Fried Chicken Wings with a Tangy Asian Sauce. I received 6 drummies and 3 flats. They were crispy and tasty. A nice twist to the traditional, buffalo that is served at most restaurants.   After wings, I had to have my classic cocktail, a Manhattan. I requested it be made with Rye Whiskey and to be served up. It was perfection, just what I'd expect from a Bourbon Bar.   As my entree, I selected their Baseball Cut Sirloin. It came with one side and I choose one of my favorite vegetables, Asparagus. Being a glutton, I wanted a second vegetable and went with my other favorite veggie, Brussels Sprouts. The Brussels Sprouts were flash fried and absolutely delicious. The asparagus was steamed perfectly. It had a good crisp bite and the béarnaise sauce made me smile.   My steak was prepared to a perfectly medium rare. I love that on their menu they offer, Black & Blue. For those of you who do not know that terminology, that is for a steak seared raw. Yum.   It was a rough day at work, so one more cocktail. One of the servers recommended, the Apricot Sage Lemonade. After reading the description on the menu, it was a go for me. Bourbon and sage infused lemonade is a perfect summer drink - I want it poolside.   I went whole hog tonight and after discussing the desserts with Wendy, I ordered the Bourbon Chocolate Pecan Pie. Fresh made in house and topped with a refreshing house made vanilla ice cream as well. It was a perfect ending to an incredible dinner.   Other points of interest that are hot buttons for me; a hook under the bar, linen napkins, eco-friendly to-go vessels and special Happy Hour prices.   I'll be back? - Absolutely. I loved it. Wendy & Paul have a showstopper.   When: July 12, 2018 Why: Dinner and Opening Night

I cannot believe I haven't updated my review in over eight years. That is just wrong and I apologize. If you are organized to the point of being just this side of OCD, this is the store for you. It will have you organized in a flash.   I have used products from here to organize my kitchen drawers and today I organized my spice cabinet. Penzeys Spices would be so proud of my newly organized shelves.   While I was redoing my spice cabinet, I also grabbed a new standing drying rack for the laundry room. We all have those favorite items, that just cannot go into that dryer. It's compact, rust-free and made in the USA.   Earlier this year I also, bought a small five drawer rolling rack for my personal stuff at work. My new work location does not offer lockers, so this little jewel keeps all my personal items neat and tidy.   Love this store!   I'll be back? - I just said, "I love this store!"  When: April 19, 2019 and an earlier date that I can't remember Why: Spice Cabinet make-over

Selecting the first review of a new Yelp year is always a challenge for me. I want it be upbeat, positive and truly a place I would recommend. This year it is Rooster on S. Grand. I have always been a fan of their Bloody Mary's, but now I am enthralled with their Honey Nut Old Fashioned. It is the perfect adult beverage for me to start my weekend brunch.   Normally I am not a fan of anything that has walnuts in it, so at first I was hesitant to order the HNOF. It is made with Walnut Bourbon and that had me a little leery. It was the day after Christmas and I had to work the holiday, so I thought it was time to throw caution to the wind and give it a try. I am so glad that I did. The cinnamon bitters, honey and lemon, made an excellent adult beverage to celebrate the holiday a day late.   I choose an entree that was also holiday appropriate. The menu name is Pork Steak and Eggs, but it actually is two slices of pork loin that are seasoned with a spicy rub. It's served with two eggs and potatoes. I had my eggs scrambled, which were served nice and fluffy. Being a farm boy, I like that their potatoes are served like good ole fashioned fried potatoes. They were simply seasoned with pepper and salt. Instead of boring toast, I opted for a biscuit, after all this is my Christmas Brunch.   As my usual, I sat at the bar and the service is always friendly and attentive. To be honest, I'm not sure I'd be a fan of those long communal tables. However, I guess it would be a great way to meet new foodies.   Will I be back? Yes! I want one of those HNOF's right now.   When: December 26, 2016 Why: I worked Christmas and this was my holiday breakfast.

I can not sing the praises loud enough about this amazing place. They are all saints in my eyes, they saved my precious Peaches. Peaches got extremely ill on the 4th of July, seriously she was bout to cross the Rainbow Bridge. As Sarah and Chip have stated,  they give you a low & high estimate and explain in details the options. They help you make the right call for your pet. The staff is compassionate and true animal lovers.  Peaches had to stay in ICU for three days and our bill was $1200.00,  and worth every penny. She is back to her ole-self  at being a spoiled diva.  If you ever have a pet emergency, I recommend VVS.

Neveria La Vallesana has won my heart, or at least my tummy. I will admit, when we were first greeted and seated, I was grumbling. No chips and salsa brought to the table and no liquor license, which meant no Margarita. How do they expect me to eat Mexican food without chips and liquid refreshment? To my surprise I enjoyed my street tacos much more, because I had not filled myself up with countless chips and a boozy drink.   The SO was in the mood to make his "world famous" tamales so we made a trip down  to Cherokee for his special ingredients.  We knew not to grocery shop on an empty stomach, so we stopped in Neveria La Vallesana. We each had three street tacos and a side of beans. I choose, shredded pork, chicken and grilled steak.  All three were flavorful, but next time and there will be a next time I will be ordering all three chicken. Yes, the chicken was that flavorful.   The service was friendly and with the good food, this will be one of my regular haunts for Mexican food. Can't wait for them to get a liquor license.

Dado's loses a star with me. I stopped by for the Sunday Brunch and they did not impress me. I found the food on the buffet not to be up to the standards of their regular offerings. I felt the food was rather bland and flavorless.   It would have been nice if they offered an omelet bar or a carving station and charged a little more. Some fresh fruits also would have been a nice touch.   I'll be back to try the Prime Rib special, I've heard great things about it.  Hopefully, after a good piece of prime rib I'll be able to bump them back up to at least 4 Stars.   I'll be back? - Yes, to try the Prime Rib  When: November 4, 2018 Why: Sunday Brunch

I am not positive, but I am fairly certain that Moonlight was the first restaurant that I experienced as a child.  I remember all the special occasions,  we celebrated here enjoying the Talk-N-Chic, which is their house secret, trademarked recipe for fried chicken. It has been passed down 4 generations and it is so good I'd be tempted to marry into the family just to get the recipe.   Living in Saint Louis now, Moonlight is close, but yet so far away. I agree with George O. and wish they'd open a location on the west side of the river. However, with family still on this side of the river, I will coordinate my visits around lunch or dinner time to satisfy my fried chicken cravings.   Our recent lunch was no disappointment, as with every visit memories floated through my head. We ordered two 2 Piece Platters; one with two thighs and fries  and the other a wing and breast with a baked potato. All the pieces were huge, crispy golden brown and juicy.  The fries were crispy and the baked potato was baked throughout. As a bonus, you can order a small side of chicken livers with your dinner, which we did. I am not a liver fan, but here at Moonlight is another story. When those livers are breaded in the family secret and fried to perfection, I become a fan.   Let me regress for a moment, and talk about our salads.  More importantly the dressing. Their house dressing is Ramon, which is the off spring a Caesar and Mayfair. This is a dressing that should be on your local grocers shelves, not that stuff from PH. Along with the salad they serve up a basket filled with warm, thick sliced Italian bread and whipped butter.   The service here is always stellar. Best way to describe it would be "down home friendly". They are attentive and know how to hustle. When your order of chicken is ready, it is out to your table in no time flat. Lana took care of us on our last visit and when I found out she'd been there 32 years, she and I strolled down memory lane.   In my book, Moonlight has the best fried chicken, period.

I'm really glad some of the more popular Food Trucks are opening brick and mortar locations. It is the only way I am able to finally get to try some of their tasty treats, since food trucks are prohibited from coming anywhere near my work. Also, my work schedule unfortunately prohibits me from attending the fun-filled Food Truck Fridays in Tower Grove Park.   When I saw, that Ian Froeb rated GSF #15 on his STL 100, I knew this was one I had to try. It's a perfect location with plenty of easily accessible parking. It has a small charming little dining room and they play some great tunes which adds to the ambiance. Most folks were coming in and picking up carry-out, but I stayed and relished the entire experience.   As I'm eating my way through Mr. Froeb's STL 100, I try to order his "must order", whenever possible. Here at GSF, it was an easy order. I went with the; Flying Pig. I couldn't say no to; slow roasted pork, Sriracha, fried garlic,a one hour egg and numerous other spices and ingredients, all served over steamed jasmine rice. I also enjoyed a single BBQ Pork Skewer and a bottle of Excel Red Creme soda. It was a flavorful dinner at a very affordable price.   I'll definitely be back, there is so much more that I want to try. I just don't know if I'll order Old School or New School on my next visit. Only time will tell.   When: September 29, 2016 Why: Dinner & STL 100 List

I'm bad, I cannot believe I have not updated my review over the last 11 years. So, I am raising them up to 5 Stars and it is well deserved.   My go to order here at  Lester's is always the chicken wings. I like my wings extra crisp, so they oblige me when I order them, extra crispy. They do it, without drying them out. They're crispy and the meat is still juicy. The wings are seasoned so well, I never use any dressing for dipping. If you do, they offer both, Blu Cheese and Ranch.   To accompany my wings, I order a small house salad and that is when I order the Blu Cheese. Many restaurants I have the dressing served as a side, but I trust Lester and they do not over dress. They toss the lettuce with just enough dressing to provide a light and flavorful coating.   My recent visit, I was fortunate to have Deborah as my server. She is a delight and for those of you who do not know her, she has been there since day one. This lady knows her stuff and is attentive to your needs as a diner.   Dining during the pandemic, I was pleased to see hand sanitizer available and tables marked unavailable to provide social distancing. They even had the statue of Stan the Man wearing a Cardinal face mask outside at the entrance.   In addition to the wings, I love their pastrami.

My fabulous hair stylist (Cate) moved her clientele over here to Jonathan's shortly after hair salons re-opened at the beginning of this damn pandemic. I am so glad that she did. I love the smaller salon feeling that Jonathan's has, while still offering all the amenities of a larger salon.   When the hair salons reopened, the salon Cate was originally working, really wasn't following the recommendations of the CDC and St Louis County guidelines. She wanted a safe place to work and a safe place for her clients to return too. So, she found Jonathan's.   Let me repeat, I am so glad that she did. First off, I love how she cuts my hair. I prefer scissor cuts to a clipper with a snap comb attached, which so many use for a mans hair-cut. She takes the time to totally scissor my hair and only uses a clipper to trim up my neckline. We've had a professional relationship/friendship going on 15 years.   Now, why I am so glad she moved. Jonathan's is really protective of their  staff and clients. When you arrive, outside they have a table where you are required to spray the bottoms of your shoes with a sanitizer. Once you enter, if you don't have your own personal mask, they'll provide you one. They also, provide gloves for the clients to wear while in the salon. In addition to these protective measures, they sanitize the chairs and workstations in between each client. I feel totally safe!   A bonus of coming here, is the other staff members. I just adore, Queen. She makes me smile every time I visit.   Will I return? - Every 6 weeks, like clock work.   When: Most recently, September 23, 2020 Why: Hair-Cut

Let's be honest with ourselves. What would you prefer to have, 6" or 8"? I don't know about you, but I'll take 8" over 6" any day. Seriously, there is no comparison between Subway and Jimmy John's. The 8" sandwiches at Jimmy John's are better.   My personal favorite is the #9 ITALIAN NIGHT CLUB. It is real genoa salami, Italian capicola, smoked ham, and provolone cheese all topped with lettuce, tomato, onion, mayo, and Jimmy John's homemade Italian vinaigrette. As the menu says, you have to order hot peppers on it. They just add that extra kick to the flavor. As a side I enjoy their Jalapeño Chips.   Depending how hungry I am, I can devour the entire sandwich or cut it in half and have lunch the next day. If it is a work day the next day, I almost always cut it in half.   The staff is always freaky fast with a side of friendly.

I'm the donut man at my work, so I was so excited to see that Tim Hortons is open 24 hours. My work day starts at 5:15 AM and many of the local donut shops do not open till 5 AM making it impossible to pick-up and make it to work on time. The only place I've been able to patronize is John's in Soulard, so now I have a second place to satisfy our donut craving.   I will admit my first visit was on their second day open and I arrived at 4 AM. They were just starting to bake and there were no donuts. All I had to choose from was danishes and Timbits. The next day, I arrived at 4:30 AM and they had a nice selection of donuts waiting for me. The day before I told them my situation, they listened and recommend me arriving at the later time.  I'm a donut hole addict, so I am already in love with their TimBits. They offer a large variety of flavors. They may have a different name here, but I will always call them donut holes. My coworkers love Tim's chocolate, so anything dipped in chocolate or chocolate on chocolate is their favorite.    As with any new business they are experiencing some hick-ups, mainly slow service as they are all learning a new job and customer volume. However, their helpfulness and friendly service is making up for the slowness.   The donuts and the coffee are winners for me and my co-workers, so we say, "Welcome to Saint Louis, Tim Horton".

A friend asked me if I've ever been here and when I responded, "no". She said, "You've got to go. I'm taking you, the next time I go." So, I gotta give a shout out and a big, thank-you to Norma H. for exposing me to SCS.   I'll be honest, SCS kinda blew my mind. Typically, I do not like most ethnic/Asian grocery stores. It's not that I dislike the variety of their merchandise. It's my sensitive nose. I can easily smell odors and other stores stink to me. Making it an unpleasant shopping experience. Here, my nose did not zero in on any unusual odors and I even dropped my mask a couple of times to see if it were blocking my sensitive sensor and it wasn't.   I was totally taken back by the  unique variety of vegetables and fresh spices. The larger bundles and lower prices of the fresh herbs will make all home chefs happy.   If you're a fan of the, "Goya" brand, you've got to shop here. I never knew they made some many different things. I was like a little kid in a candy store, my eyes were big as saucers.   In the snack aisle, I was amazed at the selection of chips. They had Mexican Fritos and I'm addicted to American Fritos, so I had to try the, Sausage and Chipotle. It was the bomb, I may have to make return trips just for these chips.   The organization of the store, has a lot to be desired. There seemed to be no rhyme and reason to the flow of the aisles. Which makes it necessary to go up and down them all, until you get familiar with their system.   There were staff members everywhere working the aisles, so if you have questions, they're there to help. An impulse item at the check-out, was a cloth face mask. It was only $2.99 and is one of the best mask I have bought during this pandemic.   Will I return? - Sure, I've still got more to see.   When: July 2, 2020 Why: First Visit

Being a new resident of the Godfrey/Alton area, this is my new Lowe's. In the past I was use to the one in Kirkwood, MO a suburb or STL. I was expecting a major difference between an upscale neighborhood and a small town store, but there really wasn't that much difference. In fact, the biggest difference is, you get better customer service here.   I've shopped various departments and have always found what I needed. The staff in the paint department was able to assist me in matching my new houses paint so I could do touch up. Then the clerks in the bathroom department helped me with new towel bars and other accessories.   What surprised me most was, the garden department in January. I had received several small plants as house warming gifts and they have out grown their pots. I was able to find new pots to my liking and special indoor potting soil. In the dead of winter, I thought finding gardening supplies would have been a challenge.   I already have my eye on new lighting fixtures for my entryway and hallways, so I'll be coming back for those.   When checking out, I always use a live person and those that I have experienced, are friendly, fast and efficient. I'm liking this Lowe's.   When: August 28, September 8, October 27 and 29, November 14, December 10, 2020 and January 30, 2021

When I first experienced Blaze in Chicago, I wanted one to open in STL. Now that it has, it does not compare to the one in CHI. I think they are still working out new restaurant bumps. I'll return, because I'm hoping they become as good as the one I'm in love with in CHI.   My pizza was good. I always build my own, with Italian Sausage and Jalapeños. I also choose classic red sauce and mozzarella cheese. The red sauce was a little too sweet for me, so next time I'll most likely change that up. The pizza is a hearty size, so since I am dieting, I got three meals out it. A big eater, will be stuffed if they eat the entire pizza.   Blaze, is a Coke restaurant, which makes me happy. However, today I went for iced tea and theirs was refreshingly fresh.   The staff is what kept them a star short of the Blaze in CHI. Sad to say, they had an attitude problem. They reminded me of snotty high school kids. Let's get a little perky and show the customer how happy your are that they are visiting your pizza parlor.   I'll be back? - Yes, I'm a fan of CHI location & want to be one in STL.   When: June 5, 2018 Why: Lunch and wanted to experience Blaze STL

Are you serious? A restaurant that serves both, Chinese and Mexican and they do them both well. I'll admit, I was skeptical and I love it when I'm proved wrong. This little hole in the wall of a restaurant, nailed it.   As a group of Yelpers meeting for a UYE, we started out  sharing three appetizers among the six of us. I would be hard pressed, to pick which one I liked best. The Crab Rangoon, was a very thin, flakey and crisp pastry shell stuffed with a flavorful creamy filling and served with a side of chili sauce. The chicken wings took me by surprise. They were extra crispy and coated in a sticky, sweet and spicy sauce. I'm a counter and I appreciated that the order was a perfect split of 5 each; drummie's and flats.   Our third app was Choriqueso. It was a creamy cheese sauce topped with Mexican sausage with a side of house made chips. The chips were a thick cut and sprinkled with sea salt. It was spicy and better then some restaurants that specialize in Mexican.   I was torn between so many on their entrees. Should I do Orange Chicken, Fish Tacos or Chorizo Fried Rice? I was so confused. When it came time to order, I was still clueless. So I asked our server, what her favorite was and she recommended the Chipotle Chicken Noodles. I went with her recommendation and loved it. It was spicy, had a slight little burn after each bite and yet had a sweet little tang as well.   Service was low-key, attentive and not rushed.  Chances of return? - Not in my hood, but I'll make the drive again.   When: February 6, 2019 Why: UYE

Great place to get a quick quality lunch. Any of the NY Deli sandwiches are great, but my personal favorite it the Hot Pastrami. Another great lunch is the BBQ salad - not a dieting salad, but a hearty meal. Happy Hour, sit at the bar and order the wings and a side of french fries. The Garlic Lemon Pepper are my favorite and I order them extra crispy (I like the crunch). Another great thing to have at the bar is the Mini Burgers and a side of Sweet Potato Fries. Great Mix of people, a true melting pot.

Oh, what a beautiful morning. Oh, what a beautiful day. I just had a delicious breakfast at, Morning Glory Diner.   Yes, I just participated in the first round of, "Meet the Diner". It's a new monthly CYE, that is going to expose us all to the fabulous and delicious diners within our great city of STL. Best of all, you get to do experience them with fellow Yelpers aka foodies just like yourself.   David one one of the co-owners was the perfect host. You could hear his passion as he explained each item on his breakfast menu to our group of Yelpers/foodies. He shared which were his personal favorites and which contained house-made items/ingredients. Seriously, whatever you selecte, would be the right choice. Nobody was disappointed with their choice and everyone cleaned their plates.   Max, this was a fun CYE. I am looking forward to the next diner, and personally, I am hoping to make it to each and everyone on the diner tour.

I disagree with Brian M., I highly recommend getting an appetizer. Especially the Fried Pickles, they are the best I've ever had and I love Fried Pickles. However, Brian is right about the entree sizes are huge and you will have leftovers, which make for a great lunch the next day.  Just use some self control when ordering and if you have room for dessert you are a better person then I.   We did a road trip over to IL for lunch, we'd been talking about going to Lotawata for their Chicken Fried Steak, which is a real heart stopper.  When we arrived we were disappointed that it was not offered on the lunch menu and we didn't want to order the main entree, because we knew it was too huge.  Nonetheless, we found other heart stopping lunch specials that satisfied our Lotawata craving.   First I must tell you about those amazing Fried Pickles.  The serving was enough for a party of four, but some how we managed to eat almost 2/3 or the serving. I just couldn't stop munching and dipping them in the Spicy Ranch dressing. They take a Dill Pickle Chip and roll it in their homemade breading, just coating the chip enough for flavor. I like to be able to see the ridges in my pickle chip and I definitely could here. Then they fried them to a rich golden brown, allowing the pickle to still have its' own snap. These were tasty, tasty.   The BF enjoyed a Fried Seafood Plate. You can tell it is a Southern restaurant, almost everything is "fried".  His plate was covered in fries, small shrimp and huge pieces of white fish. Plus, he had Hush Puppies and Cole Slaw. The fries were crispy and seasoned, he could not finish them due to the huge amount served. The menu said the plate came with 8 shrimp, but he had over a dozen. Did we get more because they were on the small size or did someone in the kitchen lose count? The fish was truly southern fried, crispy spicy and flavorful breading around a moist piece of fish.  These Hush Puppies were better then my dad's and he made a mean and tasty Hush Puppy in his day.   I opted for the Chicken Fried Chicken which came with only one side. Like I could of eaten a second one. It was a large Boneless Chicken Breast rolled in breading and fried to a flakey golden brown & topped with homemade country gravy. As my side, I choose Mashed Potatoes so my entire plate was covered in the rich country milk gravy. I cut my breast in half and divided the potatoes and instantly had my lunch for work the next day and I was still stuffed to the gills.   Brian M. is right about the bread and butter, it is amazing. When I asked for a to go vessel to  pack my leftovers, the waitress brought us a bag of fresh bread and butter to take with us. We still had half of our original serving on the table and we were going to take it home. Guess no one goes home hungry from here.   The service was down home friendly and be aware of the ice tea. They offer true Sweet Tea from the South and it is sweet. For those of us who like to save a calorie or two they offer the "Rainbow of Sweetness" all three of the artificial sweeteners; blue, pink and yellow. Also, you'll get a laugh when the waitress ask the classic question, "Did you leave room for dessert"    I'll be back, we'll be back and may order the Chicken Fried Steak and share it.  I know I gotta have my Fried Pickles.

Seriously, I cannot believe I have not updated my review until now. I've bee eating here on the regular for four years. It goes to show how we get so comfortable going to our faves, that we forget to give them a shout out. So here it is, "Hey, Vinnie. I'm giving you that well deserved 5 Stars."  My go to when I do not want to cook, or just want a simple salad for dinner is a Large Greek Salad with Gyro Meat. It is huge and fills me up. They're not stingy with the Gyro Meat that is place on top of the salad. I could go for a little less dressing, but I always forget to tell them to go light. That's on me, but it is one of the better Greek dressing in the neighborhood.   Another of my favorites is the Reuben Sandwich. If I remember correctly it use to be an occasional daily special that has made its way on to the regular menu. Mentioning daily specials, that is one chalkboard you need to take note of when ordering. Tonight I finally made it here to experience their famous, Cheeseburger Cheeseburger.   The Cheeseburger Cheeseburger is flat grilled, diner style. It is two patties, both topped with American Cheese and then topped with thinly sliced white onion and dill pickle chips. I ate half of mine with not ketchup or mustard. The simple seasoning of salt & pepper was enough. For the last few bites, I did add ketchup. Simply because I am a ketchup freak for my burgers. The bun was also lightly toasted on the grill.   If you are super hungry, order the famous Vinnie's Fried Potatoes. They are Baked then fried and tossed in parmesan cheese and Vinnie's seasoned salt. The serving is so massive, be sure to have a friend to share them with.   Service is neighborly. The staff is always ready to chat while they prepare your order. I'm so glad this #smallbusiness is succeeding in my hood.   Will I return? - I support my hood.   When: January 2, 2018 Why: Burger Time

Macy's and Department stores in general aren't what they use to be. I recently shopped the Men's department before an appointment at the Apple store and was majorly disappointed.   The only associates I saw were at the fragrance counter and in the Ralph Lauren area. I did find a shirt in the Ralph area, but there was no assistance. It basically was self-serve, as if I were at the outlet store. The one associate was so busy ringing shoppers out and processing returns, she couldn't get out and truly "sell" the brand.   I think in a few years department stores and malls, are going to go the way of dinosaurs.   When: August 5, 2021 Why: Killing time & shopping RL

Maplewood is so lucky to have another amazing and delicious restaurant added to its community. I'm so lucky, that I live close enough to be able to enjoy it on the regular.   I went on opening night and arrived around 8:30PM. The restaurant was about half full, but as per my usual I found a empty seat at the bar. Also per my usual, I started my night off with a Manhattan. Excellent. I totally judge a bar by its ability to prepare a classic cocktail, and the young lady, nailed it.   As a treat, I started out with their Short Rib Beef Jerky Skewers. It was a flavorful salty, jerky. I had two with my Manhattan, as I read the menu and decided what I wanted as an entree. I was torn between the grilled pork steak and the Bangs Island Mussels. The mussels won and they were spicy and delicious. I absolutely loved the szechuan spice and how the bottom of the bowl was layered with the shoestring potatoes. They were dry, not setting in a rich broth like most. However, the flavor was boundless.   My drink of juice for my entree was another classic, an Old Fashioned. Again, it was prepared well. Something else intrigued me on the menu, it was the Twice Fried Potatoes. I enjoy a Twice Baked, so why not a twice fried. They were crispy for sure, they would be a perfect pairing with the Beef Jerky.   For dessert I had a third cocktail. Tuesday night is the start of my week-end and I was ready for it. For my finale of the evening, I went with one of their specialty cocktails, Four Roses Yellow Label. It was smooth and refreshing.   Service was attentive and friendly. Chris the managing partner, made the rounds and spoke with each guest. That is a class act. Other points that I always look for and are important to me are; linen napkins, hooks & outlets under the bar, were both covered. Also, I thought the neon sign directing you to the restroom, was clever - WC.  Chances of returning - It's a given.  When: January 22, 2019 Why: Opening Night

If you find yourself not having plans on a Wednesday night, I'd highly recommend you head over to Hamilton's. I can give you two good reasons. One is a bar special only and the other is available at the bar and table service.   The bar special only is chicken wings and a shot of whiskey for $12. The shot of whiskey has to be from their vast selection that are $10 and under. The second Wednesday special is a favorite of mine. It's 16 ounces of Prime Rib and one side for $34.99. If you're super hungry and do both, I wont judge you. To be honest, I've been known to not eat all day so I can do that exact thing.   I'm usually a single diner and always sit at the bar to enjoy my meals. (I do come on the other days of the week, too.) I had talked so much about Hamilton's and posted some of my meals on FB, that my favorite cousins wanted to have our annual Cousin Pre-Christmas Dinner here. I made the reservations for 6 and we were given top-notch service.   They all raved about their entrees which ranged from; a special, which was a Porterhouse for Two with two sides, a 6 oz Filet and a Kansas City Strip. We were all stuffed after the entrees, but we found room to share a couple of desserts.   So, in addition to the great Wednesday night specials, Hamilton's is great for special occasions, business dinner and a extra romantic date. Get here, soon.   I'll be back? - I guarantee I'll be back.   When: December 21, 2018 and March 14, 2019 Why: Meat, baby.

Was running errands in West County and needed a few items for dinner that evening. Traffic was already getting bad on Olive, so I stopped by Schnucks in Bellerive Plaza. As usual, the county Schnucks was bigger and had a larger selection then the city stores that I am use to.   What really blew my mind was the produce section. It was HUGE! It was so impressive, that if this were my regular Schnucks, I'd probably become a vegetarian. Yeah, it was that amazing.

Hell No and I do mean Hell No. I will never step in to Mai Lee again and I was looking so forward to finally having lunch here.   Strike One - We entered during lunch and the restaurant stank more then Jay's International on S. Grand and anyone who has shopped there knows that place smells bad.   Strike Two - We tell host party of two, he says nothing, but turns around and starts to cross the dining room floor. Being educated we finally figured it out that we were suppose to follow. He tossed two menus on a table and kept walking. We seated ourselves at the table and started to read the menu. Water served without a word and server disappears.   Strike 3 - 15 minutes pass, no one has approached us. During this time we realize the menu is for dinner and we were wanting a light lunch. As we were getting ready to leave due to the lack of service, our server appears. The SO says, "we were just getting ready to leave" and the servers response was, "Oh, you need more time." We then asked if they had a lunch menu, he responded yes and left to go get one. When he returned, he only brought one, it was a folded piece of paper and he pushed it down so hard on the table I am surprised it did not collapse. He then said, "Lunch, you only get Chinese, no Vietnamese for you." He then turned and walked away again. The point of coming to Mai Lee was to experience Vietnamese food, so we left.   I knew from reading reviews here on Yelp that the service was bad, but had no idea it was going to be this bad. Reading more reviews before writing this one, I see others have had trouble with the "lunch menu" issue. @ Mai Lee, sorry to say with your pissy attitude I will not be back.

Yippie! I am so glad that Kevin's Place relocated closer to my home. I heard such great things about his pizza, but never went down to Cherokee to experience his masterpiece of a pizza pie. Now that he's only a mile and a half from my home, my waistline may be in danger.   I was craving pizza for lunch and wanted to experience some place new, so I did a search on Yelp. Yeah, Yelp of all places of informed me of Kevin's new location. Seeing how close he was to my home, it was a no brainer to head on over for lunch. Kevin's Place has a small dining room and a good sized patio to enjoy your food.   Reading reviews, I discovered they all raved about the wings as much as they did the pizza. So wanting the full experience, I had to have an order of them as well. I had my wing prepared, hot & sweet. The sweetness, toned down the hotness. They were flavorful and meaty. I like my wings to have equal portions of flats and drums, but my order was 2/3 drum and 1/3 flats. Since, I favor drums it was okay.   My pizza was the bomb. I can easily say it is in my top three for quick pizza delivery pizza. It was a typical thin crust pizza and it was nice and crisp. I had mine topped with sausage, jalapeños and onions. It was so good, I couldn't control myself. I ate all of it, except for two squares. I really was hoping to take more home. At least, I took half the wings home for the afternoon snack.   The small dining room is kinda cluttered, so don't judge by looking at the decor. If you do, you'll be missing out on some of the best pizza in the STL area. Only downside of dining at Kevin's is no booze, but I can suffer through that. His pizza is that good.   I'll be back? - Absolutely.   When: August 8, 2019 Why: New pizza experience.

I have been wanting to try TDD ever since Lynn A. had the ROTD back in January of this year. I love donuts and I wanted to give their bite size delights a try. So, when I heard my favorite radio station was broadcasting live, I was motivated to make the trek out to the county.   Being early morning (8AM) and having a popular radio station present, there was a short line of about 8-10 people. You place your order and pay with a cashier. Once you've told the cashier your selected flavors, the magic begins. The team of associates, drop the donuts in the hot oil, apply your topping and box your order up to go. It's a very impressive and smooth operation. It's like watching your sandwich be assembled at Subway, but it's a mini donut.   I went with two tradition donuts; Cinnamon Sugar and Chocolate Icing. My third, I went a little crazy and choose Strawberry Cheesecake. They definitely were bite sized and flavorful. The chocolate was my favorite. To be honest, for my sweet tooth, they were a little too sweet. They were way sweeter then a typical donut.   The staff was pleasant and worked quickly. Making the process from ordering to walking out the door with a box of donuts fast and easy.  I'll agree with Lynn, as I entered the first thing I noticed was the smell of frying oil. It smacks you directly in your nostrils as you enter, but it's worth it once you eat one of your donuts.   I'll be back? - Only if I'm out in the county. It's a novelty. I'm a city man, with too many full sized donut shops to choose from.   When: July 26, 2019 Why: Radio Station KY98 Broadcasting Live

I love the VIP Sale at Macy's. Who wouldn't love shopping your favorite departments and getting 20% off regular prices, sale and clearance prices too. Normally my favorite department is excluded from these promotional sales, but not this time. This time the Ralph Lauren department was included and I took advantage. I got shirts, shorts, socks and hats all at a huge savings. Sale goes till Sunday and there's some leather goods that may be calling my name.   The ladies of this department were so helpful in assisting me in finding my sizes and recommending items I had not noticed myself (which is rare, I know that dept. well). Part of my purchase was done as a pre-sale the day before the sale actually started. They then hold it till the actual sale day and you go back to the store with no worries of your wish list being sold to someone else.   Some of these ladies know exactly what is hanging in my closet and that scares me. Or is that good

Woohoo! As good as it gets!, is right.   I had been putting off replacing the windows on my sunporch for years. I kept putting it off, until recently. In the past, I hadn't really utilized the room that much, it was just a room I crossed through when I entered and exited the back of the house. Now, I created an entertainment room and needed to improve the windows.   I had spoken to Renewal by Andersen at a craft beer event and kept their information on hand. They did call me a couple of times, since the event and didn't mind when I'd ask them to call back in a couple months. When they followed up the last time, I was ready and meet with one of their salespeople. The sales pitch was professional, informative and low-key, no high pressure. I was sold. The next step in the process was a tech coming out and getting very accurate measurements, since all windows are custom made. Again, this step in the process was professional and took minimal time.   Six weeks later, my windows were ready to be installed. They were very accommodating working with my work schedule and coming on my day off during the week, so I didn't have to waste a personal or vacation day to get my new windows installed. My installer was scheduled to arrive at 8 AM, he pulled up 5 minutes early - nice. I like it when a repair/service person is on time.   I meet the installer out front and walked him to the back entrance of my home, where the sunporch is located. I went on about my business doing errands within the house, keeping the dogs quiet and I even wrote a couple Yelp reviews. Periodically I'd come back to watch his progress and chat about the job. As I watched, I was impressed with the attention to details and how meticulous he worked.   When he was done and I walked into the room for the first time, I knew I made the right decision. I immediately could hear the difference in acoustics and feel the difference in temperature. Not to mention the aesthetics of the room.  It was a good investment, that I now wish I would have done it earlier.   Would I use them again? Yes. As I replace additional windows in my house, they'll be Renewal By Andersen.   When: Early December 2016 Why: Needed new windows (3)

An exquisite dining experience. I arrived early for dinner on their official opening day, after a special seating for Valentine's  Day. I had no reservation, because I normally can find a seat at the bar. To my surprise, they do not have a bar for patrons to sit. Lucky for me, they were able to accommodate me with a two top. Note to self and for others, this place is hot - make a reservation.   I judge a bar by their ability to make a classic cocktail. I started out with my go to, a Manhattan. They presented it, on the rocks with a large cylinder single piece of ice. The glassware was not bulky barware, but thin stylish glassware for elegant dining.   I might as well finish reviewing of the other cocktails, I enjoyed. My other go-to favorites are; Old Fashioned and Boulevardier. Bothe of these were also superbly prepared. My only complainant would be in the Boulevardier, the pour of Campari was on the heavy side. Also, I am old school and would have enjoyed it in an appropriate up glass instead of a rocks glass.   My feast of flavorsome food begun with my all-time favorite seafood, Scallops. The presentation was art on a plate. My pan seared sea scallops were served with a ginger puree and mushroom blend. I loved the watermelon radish and the sprinkling of Bait seasoned popcorn. How novel is that? I could come back and pair this with one of my next dishes and have a complete meal.   Next, I had their Flash Fried Brussels Sprouts and Mussels. For my mussels, I choose the white wine with roasted tomato and leeks. The originality of the dishes is what amazes me here at Bait. My B Sprouts were not just flash fried, they were served with grilled pineapple, chiles and candied pine nuts on top of an avocado puree. Now you can see why I'd want to pair it with my scallops.   The mussels were delicious. I enjoy a simple broth for my mussels and the white wine fulfilled my craving. Many of the shells were empty, but I was able to match them up to loose mussels in the bowl. However, for me, pulling the mussel from the shell is part of the experience.   Dessert was Creme Brûlée - not made in house, but made by one of the better know French bakeries in West County. The top was not crisp like most, but the sweet flavor was a perfect ending to a new restaurant experience.   As I dined, the house manager stopped by to do a greet and meat. Very nice touch, for their official opening day. I discussed my surprise of no bar with her and how being a single diner, I do not like to tie up a table. That is why I am always eating at a bar. She assured me no to worry about that in the future. That they are aware they'll have single diners.   We also discussed the amazing plate presentations, refreshing & professionally made cocktails and I did mention my mussel issue. (Not as a complaint) I was more laughing at myself wanting to pull that little mussel out of its shell. To my surprise, after being totally stuffed and done eating - my server brought out another order of mussels, compliments of the chef. Some how, I managed to eat them as well. Mussels do go down easy.   My server, George B. was attentive and friendly. I was impressed how well he knew and spoke of the menu with it only being opening day. You could hear his passion for the food in his descriptions. He had large tables all around me, but he still made time to check on me and to make sure I was equally taken care of.   Chances of returning? - Lobster Fries, Bourbon Shrimp and many other dishes are call my name. (I just wish they had a bar.)   When: February 15, 2019 Why: New & Hot

My county and Illinois friends now have another reason to come to downtown Saint Louis, besides a Cardinal or Rams game. Taze is a creative new twist on Mediterranean food, it is high-end fast food at an affordable price. It is build your own, with fresh, quality ingredients.   Think Chipotle or Qudoba, or even Subway. You first pick your type of pita, I choose whole wheat. Then you select your meat and all the fresh toppings you want. Then you select a side; mine was fries. As if that isn't enough food, they offer you a scoop of humus as well. My meat was beef & lamb, which was tender as tender could be. The fries were skin on Russet potatoes, that were gourmet burger joint quality. Being a fan of Jalapeños, I couldn't resist their Jalapeño humus and it left me speechless.   Enjoy before or after a game. Or make a special trip downtown and enjoy Taze. It is well worth risking your life and making the trip to downtown Saint Louis.   When: June 28, 2015 Why: International Supper Club Meeting

I love this store. I cannot believe I did not discover it until I moved away from STL and came back for a day of shopping and eating. The scary thing is, I lived at Jamieson and 44 which wasn't that far away. Oh, well at least I finally found it.   This store has gifts and fashions for everyone. If you need a unique gift for that person, who is like me who and hard to shop for, come here and you'll find the perfect gift. Once you've given it, they'll be telling everyone how awesome you are and how you give the perfect gifts. It will be a win-win for everyone. I personally knocked out my family Christmas gift exchange and a upcoming family birthday.   My only negative, is I was followed around the store the entire time I was browsing and shopping. It was as if I were being stalked. I felt as if she did not trust me and was watching me to make sure I did not shoplift. I am sure she thought she was providing good customer service, but it made me feel extremely uncomfortable. Luckily I was with a friend, so I didn't call her out on her behavior.   Will I return? - Yes, it's a dynamite store.   When: November 10, 2020 Why: Shopping before lunch at Frisco

What? You'll find yourself saying that a lot at Hofbrauhaus. The acoustics here are extremely poor. Especially when the band is playing. Also, just the natural rumble of all the guest talking and having a good time can make the noise level almost deafening.   However, if you come here with a group of friends, you'll definitely will have a good time. The live band is more then happy to acknowledge birthdays and they'll bring over this extremely long horn and play it right next to the b-day person. For them it is all about fun and entertaining.   Also, be sure to have someone in your group to do the, "Shot and Swat". They give you a choice of four different liquors as your shot. Once you've downed your shot, you have to bend over and take your swat. They had me empty my pockets and bend over a chair. The young man who gave me, my swat did not hold back. It had a good little sting to it.   The food, to be honest is nothing to write home about. For me, it was just okay. I did enjoy the pretzel and a few of the sausages. The sauerkraut was rather bland, it did not have a sour or sweet taste to it. To balance things out, the beer is very good.   I do recommend that you go at least once in a large group. Go enjoy some beer, eat some pretzels and have a good time.   I'll be back? - I doubt it. Been there, done that.   When: November 10, 2018 Why: Veteran's Day & Birthday Celebrations.

Needed an extra key for work, so I stopped by Krause since it is in my hood.  I could not be happier with the service I received. I was greeted by a friendly associate, he made my key and I was out the door in under 5 minutes and that was with small talk.   If and when I need more keys made, I'll keep my business local and come back to Krause.

VVS is staffed by angels. Their doctors, technicians and front office staff are all professional, caring and compassionate. They not only take care of our fur-babies, but they take care of us as well when it is a time of crisis.   It had been 1 year and 11 months since our last emergency visit to VVS with my diva dog, Peaches. Again, we were back with symptoms of pancreatitis. When they did an x-ray they found three masses in her intestine. So much for three being my lucky number, it ain't anymore.   The doctor explained to me our options and used layman terms so I'd understand the option of surgery. I said I'd like to consult her regular vet and within a flash, they had her on the phone for me. The VVS specialist informed her of Peaches condition and what they recommended and then I spoke with her. We were all in agreement that surgery was the way to go.   The SO had a human doctors appointment, so I drove him back home and returned to be here for Peaches. She made it through surgery fine, unfortunately during recovery she had difficulty breathing and she had to be connected to a machine. They allowed me to come back in to the hospital area (which was amazing to see) to be by her side. Finally, her little big heart stopped and she crossed the Rainbow Bridge to join so many other dogs who have gone before her. After regaining my composure, I asked if I could see her again and they kindly placed me in a private room with her and told me to take my time saying my final goodbye.   If I ever need emergency veterinary services in the future, VVS is still my #1 choice. Who wouldn't want an angel to care for their dog.

I am a BIG fan of Brunch. Unfortunately, I work every Sunday. So, I am constantly on the search for a restaurant that serves it up on a Saturday. Lucky for me, Big Sky Cafe does just that.   Kyle greeted me as I entered, and I told him I was dining alone and didn't mind sitting at the bar. He obliged me and escorted me to a very colorful tiled bar. As he got me situated, he offered me coffee, which I accepted. I told him, no brunch is complete without a Bloody Mary and I would like one of those, too. He recommended, Tito's for the vodka and that was just perfect, since it's my favorite.   As he greeted other guest, I studied the menu and sipped back and forth between my two beverages. When Kyle returned, I told him I had narrowed it down two entrees. I was torn between, Big Sky Benedict and Cornbread and Jalapeño Gravy. Without missing a beat, he recommended the Cornbread and Jalapeño Gravy. We just meet and he knew me so well. I am a fan of jalapeños and as a farm boy, I love biscuits and gravy. Putting the two together, made for a winning combination. In addition to the house made cornbread and the tangy, spicy jalapeño gravy, it had Geisert Farm, Smoked Bacon and a fresh farm egg.   What kept BSC from getting 4 Stars, is the cornbread was a little on the dry-side and I did not enjoy the Bloody Mary mix that they used. Otherwise, it was a good Saturday Brunch and Kyle offered excellent customer service.   When: February 15, 2020 Why: Saturday Brunch

I'm not a vegetarian, but sometimes I eat like one when I come to Yellowbelly for lunch.   Yellowbelly was my second stop for, Dine Out For Life 2019. I choose YB for lunch, because I knew I could eat light and healthy with a couple dishes from their, Snacks & Sides or Small Plates. Both of these categories on the menu offer delectable veggie and seafood treats.   Todays lunch was simple. A green vegetable, Crispy Brussels Sprouts and a root vegetable, Charred Carrots. I absolutely love their Brussels Sprouts, but a warning to true vegetarians, it does have pork belly in it. Also, a heads up for peanut allergies, they too are in this flavorful dish. Mixed with Thai Chili and Garlic. For me the mix of spices, pork and peanuts, make this one of the best if not the best Brussels Sprouts in STL.   There are not enough words to describe the deliciousness of the Charred Carrots. They are always perfectly done. They are soft with just enough snap and firmness in them. I love Macadamia nuts, so having them as a garnish on these carrots is a bonus.   My cocktail of choice was an Old Fashioned. It was raining, so a classic cocktail just seemed appropriate. Mentioning rain, I gotta give a shout out to the hooks under the bar. They really came in handy today. I was able to hang my rain jacket under the bar as I dined.   Friendly staff, who always make it a reason to return.   I'll be back? - Most definitely.   When: May 2, 2019 Why: Lunch - Dine Out For Life 2019

At work we celebrate the 12 Days of Christmas. Starting on the 12th of December until the 24th a different person is responsible for bringing in and serving lunch to a staff of 12. The other day, one of my co-workers had breakfast/lunch catered by Saint Louis Kolache.  The boxes of savory Kolaches were a major hit with everyone working. It was a nice touch having a posting of codes and labeling of the kolaches in their boxes. It made it easy to make your selection. As a team, we all differed on the length of time one should heat the kolache in the microwave. Some thought 15 seconds was enough and others went with 30. However, we also had a couple who thought 40 seconds was the perfect length of time to heat up theirs.  I tried the Steak Kolache and the Slinger. Being a true STL man, I just had to try the Slinger. The pastry ball was filled with; hamburger, chili, egg and hash browns. I would have never thought I could enjoy a hand held Slinger until this holiday luncheon. I want to go visit the actual store so I can try a Jalapeño Popper.   Would I go back? Yes, I have so many more Kolaches to try.   When: December 14, 2016 Why: Catered Lunch at Work

I absolutely love the lay out of this store. My hometown Target is in the midst of a remodel and I can only hope it looks like this one when they are done. The flow of the aisles and staggering of the different departments, makes for a pleasant shopping experience.   The store is always super clean and well merchandised. I do believe they even have some more upscaled items that are not available at the Alton store. Today I was shopping for a baby shower gift and found a fabulous Aveeno mommy & baby gift basket. It was perfect, a little something for the momma as well as the new baby.   The check out process took some time, but that was okay. It was obvious they were training new cashiers. We all need to have patience. Remember, it is a virtue.   Many of my favorite places to shop in E-ville are near this Target, so it makes it easy for me to stop by whenever I am in town.   When: October 20, 2021 Why: Baby Shower Shopping

I absolutely love this place and that is odd. Why, you ask. I'm not a bread person and it's a toast bar. Plus, it is small, tightly compact and crowded and I can get claustrophobic. All those things aside, this place blew me away. If it were not for Norma H.encouraging me to go and Ian Froeb putting them on his STL 100 List, I would have never discovered this little hidden gem of a restaurant.   My favorite and must have every time I go, is the Apple Cheddar Melt. It was the "must order" from Ian's list and once again he is right. White Cheddar is melted on top of a layer of apples that are placed on top of a smear of apple butter on a thick slice of toast. I've always enjoyed slices of cheese and apples as a snack, but pairing them with toast and apple butter is genius.   Another of my favorites is Simple Toast with Peanut Butter and Honey. It's a gooey mess, with the melting peanut butter and gooey honey running off the toast. Be sure to eat it with a knife and fork, so you can sop up every drop of the PB&H.   My third favorite Spiffy Toast would most likely be a vegetarians first choice. It's made with Mushroom and Goat Cheese. Goat Not only does this one have my favorite cheese, but they use truffle oil as well and mix in fresh herbs. This Spiffy Toast makes for a great light lunch.   No booze here, but I have found that the Cashew milk is the perfect accompaniment to the Peanut Butter Simple Toast and a Japanese Ice Brewed Coffee goes well with the Apple Cheddar Melt.   The staff is small and professional. Be patient, things can be slow as they are multi-tasking and doing multiple jobs. On your first visit, they may not be warm and fuzzy, but when they see you back for a second and multiple visits, they totally warm up to you.   A restaurant serving toast is a unique concept for STL. Go check it out, you'll be pleasantly surprised.   When: April 19, May 3 and a couple other times. Why: Norma told me too....

It's been a year and four days since my last visit and I get to bump them up to 5 Stars. They truly have got it going on now. I arrived shortly after 9 AM and positioned myself at bar for a power breakfast. I needed all the nutrition I could get, as I was determined to finish my holiday shopping that day. My mission was accomplished, at least for the power breakfast. The shopping, is another story or should I say another Yelp review.  In my book of rules a weekend breakfast is not complete without a Bloody Mary. So I had to start out with theirs made with house infused pepper vodka. The Bloody Mary mix is also house made, giving this morning Wakey Wakey drink some extra kick. It had a simple garnishment of three olives and a lime.   I was torn between the Corn Bread Benedict with Sautéed Spinach & Avocado and the El Cerdo which is one of their Hashes with Two Poached Eggs. I asked the bartender for his recommendation and he said, "El Cerdo". I'm glad I asked for guidance, he was so right. It was the perfect pairing with my Bloody Mary. I like hot & spicy and both of these delivered.   My El Cerdo was Carnitas, Potatoes, Spinach, Corn and Jalapeños all topped with two perfectly poached eggs. I'm a sucker for any entree that features Jalapeños as one of its main ingredients. As I was ending to the bottom of my El Credo, they brought me a couple of housemate tortillas to soak up all the juices at the bottom of my dish. It was good to the last drop.   Since I regularly work weekends, I am so glad that Egg is not just for weekends anymore. Even though I enjoyed them on a vacation Saturday, I will now have them in my breakfast rotation on my regular days off during the week.   Will I come back? I just said, that I would.   When: December 10, 2016 Why: Spicy Breakfast

If I lived in Creve Coeur, I'd be a true regular of Edgewild Bistro. I truly love this place. I need to force myself to come out to the county more often so I can enjoy Edgewild Bistro.   The other day when I was running an errand on Olive Blvd, it got to be rush hour and the traffic became totally crazy. I live in the city and drive less then 5 miles to work, so I am not use to this stop & go and cut someone off in traffic. So I had to get off of the Blvd and Edgewild came to my rescue.   I went in, sat at the bar and enjoyed an ice cold craft beer. If your having a cold beer while waiting for the traffic to calm down, you might as well have an order of chicken wings. At least, that is the attitude I took. Their menu describes them as JUMBO and when they arrived, they definitely were plus sized. I ordered the Smoked Triple Dry Rubbed over the traditional bar Buffalo and I am glad I did. They were neater to eat and the dry rub seasoning offered more flavor then a messy buffalo sauce.  Service is always professional and attentive.  A couple things I've got to check out are their Beer Club and Sunday Supper. Both sound very tempting.

Two of my friends have had ROTD's for Big Baby Q and I still hadn't given them a try. Then I saw the announcement that they were moving downtown into the Flying Saucer space and I thought, I better experience now in their original habitat.   Everyone praises their brisket and I love pastrami, so it was a no brainer on what I was going to order. I choose the, Pick Two Meats Platter. Wow! Everyone is right, this has to be the best and most tender brisket in STL. If it's possible, it had just the right amount of fat and leanness. The smokehouse flavor was perfect, I had no need for any of their sauces.   I have always been a fan of the pastrami served at Bogart's. I am now torn on who I can say serves, the best. Like the brisket, their pastrami was oh, so tender and seasoned perfectly. I know I am going back and ordering it by the pound.   While paying for my lunch, I glanced over at another diners meal and gasped. He was enjoying the nachos and they not only looked messy, but were delicious as well. I was tempted to ask him if I could take a picture, but I thought it could be a little weird considering we had just meet - lol.   My platter came with two sides, I choose; Mac-n-Cheese and BBQ Baked Beans. The Mac-n-Cheese was thick and creamy. It was served in a tiny cup and you could tell it had been baked by the golden top. The BBQ Baked Beans, were seasoned extremely well, but I found them to be to runny. There was more sauce, then actual beans.   They primarily do carry-out business, but there are a few tables inside and a picnic table outside for those who want to dine in. Be prepared for an unhappy response, you tell them you're dining in. It was obvious that they want their customers to pick-up and go. However, they are very cheerful and grateful for your business. They will all thank you for coming in.   I'm looking forward to their arrival in downtown. They'll be a popular space to visit before and hopefully after a Cardinals game.   In closing, be aware there is no public restroom.   I'll be back? - I want more pastrami and to try the nachos.  When: October 3, 2018 Why: UYE - Lunch

Good Bye Ted, Hello Murray. Murray can satisfy my sweet craving with much fewer calories and fat.   I've lived in the Lindenwood Park area for over 8 years and have never gone to Murray's Shaved Ice. I had no idea what I was missing. This is a great little mom & pop shaved ice shack. A perfect complement to our neighborhood.   They offer a huge selection of flavors and I was pleased to see my two favorites were among them. I am very partial to wedding cake and dream-sickle. Six sizes are available from Kiddie all the way up to Murray's Monster. Prices are great too. The Kiddie is only $1.75 and the Monster is $4. Tax is included, making it so much easier for those out walking.   Tonight I ordered a small Wedding Cake and it was just perfect. Totally refreshing treat for the walk home and to finish on the patio.   A big bonus point or extra star for Murray's is that they offer Doggie SnoCones. They rotate the flavor between beef and chicken. That is so cool, my dogs love ice cubes as a treat and in their drinking bowl. Can't wait to see how they will react to chicken of beef flavored ice.

What do you do when you literally have eaten everything on the menu? You check and see if there's an off the menu special of the night. That's what I had to do the other night and the kitchen at PS knocked it out of the park with their special.   The special was a Ribeye and they did it equally as well as any steakhouse in the city. They prepared it to my requested medium-rare and served it with Fingerling Potatoes and Green Beans. It all was delicious and as always my Manhattan was a perfect pairing.   PS never disappoints me, with food, cocktails or service. I cannot wait to see what they do with The Bellwether. I'll have two great places to frequent.   I'll be back? - PS is my go to in STL.   When: February 27, 2019 Why: Late Dinner

Oh, Happy Day! I love it when I get to raise a restaurant up a star, especially when I have had to remove a star in the past. Originally I had given Salt+Smoke 5 Stars and then had to drop them down to 3. They have gotten back into my good graces and I'm raising them up to 4.  Dining with a friend, we started off with two appetizers; Burnt Ends Toasted Ravs and Fried Pickles. I can now say, I've had the Ravs, but I will tell you I will not order them again. They were okay, but not worth repeating. The fried pickles on the other hand are always worth repeating, I can order them every time I come and never get tired of them.
