Being at a BBQ Bourbon place, I had to have a Manhattan. Normally I do my Manhattans up, but today I did it on the rocks. It was a nice blend of 4 Roses Small Batch, Cocchi Vermouth di Torino and Angostura Bitters. I was in heaven after a long day at work.   I was motivated to come back for the brisket. It still impresses me that you get to select how you want it; lean, fat or burnt ends. I also like that they let you mix it up, I choose lean and burnt ends. The lean is always tender as can be, melts in your mouth and the burnt ends gives me that crusty crunch coating to the tender meat.  For sides you can never go wrong with their garlic and herb fries, or the white cheddar mac-n-cheese. On my last visit, I let our server pick my two sides. I know that is a dangerous thing to do, but I put my trust in her. I allowed her to bring me her two favorite sides and one of them I would have never ordered on my own. She brought me; Creamed Corn which turned out to be a delightful surprise. I would have liked it a little thicker, but the flavor was still a good accompaniment to the brisket. The second side was; Sweet Pepper Potato Salad. Which was rich and creamy with an extra tang from the sweet peppers.   I'm glad Salt+Smoke made The STL 100 and I will be back for more of that delicious brisket.   When: April 7, 2016 Why: Dinner & STL 100

Don't get it. Seriously, I do not understand all these 5 Star reviews for these donuts. I was not impressed. I stopped by when my favorite radio station was broadcasting live, expecting to be blown away. It didn't happen.   I always judge a donut shop by their  Chocolate Long Johns and the one I had here was dry and rather flavorless. It was chewy and a bottle of milk didn't even help. I think my second one was a Buttermilk type donut. This one, I took only a single bite and threw it back in the bag. Yeah, it was that good.   It had to be an off day, they were slammed with a popular radio station in their parking lot. Next time I'm headed south to shop at Costco, I'll detour and give them a second chance. As of now, I think the donuts at TDS are just average. A Long John at QT is fresher and better.   The staff was friendly and I liked that the young lady asked if I wanted my Long John plain or creme filled. Customer Service was good and they kept up with the busy crowd.   I'll be back? - Everyone deserves a second chance.   When: August 9, 2019 Why: 1st Experience - Radio Broadcast

One of the things that  I didn't want to give up when I moved out of St. Louis, was my Dierbergs.  I was a regular at the one located in Mackenzie Pointe, which was relatively close to my home. It was less than 5 miles.   The departments that I favored were;  produce, prepared foods/deli and meats. I am happy to say, I like my new Dierbergs.   My new Dierbergs isn't as close, it's 16 miles away. However, it is well worth the drive. I hosted Christmas dinner for a small group of cousins and to make my hosting duties easier, I ordered a couple of side dishes from their prepared foods. The glazed baby carrots got rave reviews from my guest.   Their liquor department is also pretty awesome. I was able to add gin, hard seltzer and craft beer to my already well stocked bar for my holiday guest. They even had a good variety of mixers to fine tune my cocktails. I was able to stock up on; ginger beer, tonic and club soda.   Shopping here during the pandemic and a holiday season, was safe. They required all customers and staff to wear mask. They sterilize the shopping cart handles between use and they wipe down cash wrap areas in between each customer.   A bonus of shopping here is the other nearby stores. When I come to Edwardsville, I can have a day of shopping and fulfill my all needs.   Will I return? - Yes, I'm a fan of Dierbergs.   When: December 23, 2020 Why: Groceries for the holiday dinner.

If you are a smart shopper, you will never pay retail at Macy's. They are always having a sale, coupon or have a clearance rack tucked away somewhere. My favorite are those clearance racks. I shop them like you'd shop the racks at TJ Max or Marshall's and I always find something in my size. In my opinion it's better quality and more current to fashion trends.  I'll give up my secret, my favorite rack is the Ralph Lauren.   My other favorite departments are:  Men's Shoes - They have Cole Hahn and the men who work the dept. are always helpful and knowledgeable.   Men's Suits - When my job required my attire to be "suits", Macy's put places like Mens Wearhouse to shame in both selection and pricing.   Housewares - Watch for sales when needing to add new pots and pans to your kitchen.  Bed & Bath - The Hotel Collection is equal to Pottery Barn and a much better price and larger color selection.  It's a department store where you can find many of your needs at a good sale price.

Living in STL, I had a vast selection of bakeries to choose from for satisfying my sweet tooth. When I moved to the Riverbend area, I was concerned that I'd lose that variety of sweets. I am tickled pink, that I was wrong on my assumption.   Dolci di Anna is one of the first little bakeries that I discovered in the downtown area of Alton. My first encounter with her delicious treats was dessert at a local restaurant. As I ordered, the server told me it was made by a new and upcoming bakery in the area. I immediately, put the name in my memory rolodex.   I immediately fell in love on my first visit. It's a small shop with a small display case of daily treats and small cakes. Her cakes are so damn cute, I know I will be ordering one for my birthday celebration later this year.   My purchases on my first visit were a Strawberry Brownie and a sampling of her Macaroons. OMG! How can you go wrong blending strawberries with a brownie? The brownie was oh, so moist and the fresh strawberries took away the guilt of having a brownie. I felt like I was having a daily serving of fruit. The only thing that could improve this brownie, is a cold glass of whole milk.   Now let's talk about one of my sweet obsessions. I love macaroons and to find a good one, I had to drive out to west county in STL. Now, all I have to do is drive less then 5 miles and my cravings will be satisfied. The day I visited, she had four flavors available. She had the traditional, vanilla and chocolate. Then for special flavors, she offered, raspberry and pistachio. All of them were true to their flavor. However, I will say the pistachio is the one that totally knocked me off my feet. Next time, I'll be buying multiples of that flavor.   I forgot to ask if the young lady working the counter was the actual baker herself. Whomever she was, the service was friendly and knowledgeable. She really sold me on those strawberry brownies.   When: March 13, 2021 Why: Sweet Cravings

We all know, or at least most of us know Egg is an excellent place for breakfast. However, in this review I want to give a shout out to something on their menu that most folks would not think to order and that is, a burger.   Yes, a burger. It is simply listed on the lunch menu, as The Burger. It is served after 11 AM and comes with LTO (lettuce, tomato and onion) & Fries. It is a thick patty, hand pressed and prepared to your liking. I choose medium rare and it was done perfectly. I cut mine in half for easier handling while eating and the inside was a beautiful pink.   I opted to add cheese and bacon to my burger. The bacon was thick-cut, crisp and extended well beyond the bun. I cut the excess off and munched on it in between bites of burger and fries. Mentioning the fries, they are made in house and seasoned simply with salt and pepper.   This is now one of my favorite burgers and it's from a place known for eggs. I think the next time I have a burger here, I'll have them top it with an egg.   I'll be back? - Yes  When: January 16, 2018 Why: Wanted to see if the burger was as good as it is at Spare No Rib.

PASSION x 3 = Blood & Sand.   Blood & Sand is where you will find owners, a chef and a staff that are passionate about excellent food, drink and service. Their love and strong enthusiasm is obvious from the moment you enter the door.   The ambiance is cool and relaxing. They could film an episode for Mad Men or The Playboy Club here without any adjustments.   Passion #1 - The owners: TJ & Adam made it a point to visit our table more then once and to make sure everything was to our satisfaction.  As stated in a previous review, they make it a point to know your name and to use it during conversation. Their positive attitude carries over to their staff. Adam's energy explaining their Tasting Table, had me sold on the experience from the get go.   Passion #2 - A Chef: My apologies, I forget his name and he deserves a big shout out. He is very creative and passionate about his craft. I was shocked to hear that he not only does the main dishes, but he also creates the desserts.  I can not wait to come back and sit at the Tasting Table and "taste"  more of his creations.   Passion #3 - A Staff: Bartenders and Servers who make sure no detail is missed in your dining experience.  You are treated as if you are dining in a 5 Star restaurant. Oh wait, I did give them 5 stars, but you know what I mean.   The night I attended  I was a guest of Tim & Erin G.. It is good to be well connected on Yelp. We shared five small plates and two desserts and the servings were plentiful for three Yelp adults.   Steamed Clams - I had to remember sharing is the right thing to do. These were some awesome clams.  Truffled Tater Tots with Parmesan - A nice change of pace from the typical frites or fries you get at most places.   Smoked Trout & Potato Salad - Order two of these, they smoke the trout in house and the potato salad is the perfect complement.   Local greens, pickled watermelon rind, goat cheese, pecans and spiced cider vinaigrette - Double the size and I'd be in salad heaven. The size was big enough for three to sample, but it is worthy of being a meal itself.   Fettuccine all a Carbonara - Places on The Hill would have someone knocked off to have a fettuccine dish this good on their menu. Once again, the bacon is smoked in house.   The chef continued to amaze me with every dish and then I learned that he also does the pastry desserts as well.   Chocolate fondant, pistachio creme anglaise - a chocoholics dream.  I would love it in a bowl with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream and my favorite show on TV. That would be a perfect night at home.   Local maple syrup panna cotta, toasted pine nuts - the perfect ending to all the fabulous dishes we enjoyed. The panna cotta was rich, refreshing, and light at the same time. It was so enjoyable, I think it would be the perfect ending to every meal. I'd never get tired of eating it.   My next visit will be with the SO sitting at The Tasting Table, watching the action in the kitchen and eating the special dishes created just for us.

One of my favorite places for breakfast, but my work schedule and their hours of operations don't match up. Typically, I can only eat here on Tuesday & Wednesday. I do take advantage of that as often as I can, but I really love their Biscuits & Gravy Breakfast. It is only offered Friday-Sunday and I start work at 5 AM, so no go for me. So, when vacation time comes around, I am here for a hearty B&G Breakfast.   Their Biscuits & Gravy Breakfast comes with two cheddar biscuits topped with homemade sausage gravy, two eggs prepared your way and hash brown potatoes. These biscuits are soft, flavorful and the combination of cheddar and sausage milk gravy is a winner for this farm boy. Today I had my eggs fried over hard with the yolk broken, how I got on to this kick is beyond me. Their hash browns are good, I'd like them to be a little crisper, but they still make this a stick to your ribs breakfast. I added a side of bacon, it just makes the morning meal complete.   For a restaurant bottomless cup of coffee theirs is pretty good. The service is always attentive and the ladies are friendly and make your dining experience very relaxing. At times there can be a long wait for tables, but they don't rush you out. If you have no patience for waiting, I suggest you download No Wait app on your smart phone, it is a valuable tool in time management.   Will I come back? Yes, during the week I enjoy pancakes or Benedict and when I have the weekend off, it will always be Biscuits and Gravy.   When: November 11, 2016 Why: Birthday Breakfast - B&G

The sandwiches here are pieces of art. Just look at the photos, the sandwiches are all masterfully constructed in layers, creating masterpieces. Not only are they beautiful to look at, they are delectable to eat.   I was moved to come here for lunch by Ian Froeb's STL 100 List. His "must order" was the Smoked Beet Sandwich. Being a lover of beets, my arm did not have to be twisted to try his recommendation. This sandwich is especially a winner for vegetarians. However, being a big meat lover - I'd definitely come back for a repeat.  The Smoked Beet is served on Ciabatta Bread, that of course is baked in house. It's created with  layers of; tasty beets, sauerkraut, emmenthaler cheese, hard egg and Thousand Island dressing. I'll be honest it is a messy sandwich to eat. It slips and slides as you left it up for a bite. I giggled as I looked at my fingers that got a little stained from the beets. Which was easily remedied by finger licking. The combination of beets with sauerkraut and emmenthaler cheese was genius.  The cole slaw that I had as my side is worthy of a Stevie B Award - Best Cole Slaw. I honestly could make a lunch with a double order of cole slaw, a baguette and a glass of Pino Grigio.   You may wonder why I held back a fifth star if I loved it so much, I'll tell you. Even though the bread was fresh and baked in house, it was too much. The slices were extremely thick, I would have enjoyed a thinner cut. Also, I could not get the attention of a server while I was sitting at the bar to get a knife so I could lift the top portion of bread off and eat the remainder as an open face sandwich. I am sure when I return for a "meaty" sandwich, I'll be bumping it up.   When: June 15, 2016 Why: Lunch and Ian Froeb's STL 100

Alton Restaurant Week - January 2021  I meet a couple of my cousins here for lunch during the ARW. For me it was an affordable way to experience another restaurant in my new hood.   The lunch special that I choose was, a large house salad with a soda or ice tea. However, I did not want a soda, so I opted to enjoy a Pinot Grigio instead. The salad was huge and made with Romaine and Iceberg lettuce. It also had multiple toppings, including; ham, volpi salami, shredded provel, parmesan, black olives, tomato, onion and pepperoncini. It was served with Decaro's creamy house Italian dressing on the side.  I like my dressing on the side, so I have control of how much I use. It was a meal!   Before our lunches, we shared an order of Toasted Ravioli. A trip to a St Louis area Italian restaurant, is not complete without enjoying an order. The order was six jumbo sized raviolis, which was easy to divide up among three diners. The raviolis were round, and crispy around the edges, with the rest being perfectly toasted. The red sauce on the side for dipping, had enough flavor to do the job, but was not mind blowing.   The service was hit and miss at first, then extra staff showed up to help with the large crowd that had arrived for the lunch. Since this ARW was taking place during a pandemic, they were following the CDC guidelines and tables were spaced for social distancing.   The ambiance is minimal, but that kind of adds to the charm. I plan on returning, the pizzas and pasta dishes that I saw being served to other tables, looked pretty good.  When: January 15, 2021 Why: Lunch - ARW

Welcome to my neighborhood, Knead. I wish you much success, but I am not impressed. I've been to your establishment three times and not one of them wowed me.   Your variety of selections are extremely limited and those that I have tried were just okay. They are nothing that I'd rush back to have and I can walk to your establishment. Being a bakery, I was wanting to be blown away with your bread, donuts and morning buns. Even your sandwiches on your own house made bread are nowhere worth the price you are charging.   Also, your staff is not the most friendly. They were not engaging, nor did they provide the type of service that would encourage a repeat customer. Being a new business, I was not even thanked for coming in.   Again, I am glad you are in my hood. I'll let you get acclimated to being a new business and revisit you after the first of the year. Perhaps it was grand opening jitters that I experienced. Everyone else seems to think you are the cats pajamas.   Will I return? - I'll give them a 4th chance  When: November 29, 30 and December 2017 Why: In my hood, I want them to succeed.

I don't get the love everyone has for this place. I have tried time and time again, to feel the same love, but I just don't have it. My friends love this place, for me it's just okay and I have to stretch it to give it 3 Stars.   I've tried numerous dishes; Com Chien Duong Chau, Bo Xao Chau and Ga Xao Gun. I've tried two soups; Thap Cam and Bun Bo Hue. I've also tried; Cha Gio, Crab Rangoon and Goi Cuon.  Those  of you who go often and feel the love, am I ordering wrong? Ian Froeb placed them at #24 on his STL 100 List for 2016. I just find the food to be bland with little flavor.   I also, find the service to be less then desirable. I've always sat in the bar area or actually at the bar. The service is basically the same as ordering at a counter restauratnt. They take your order, bring you food and that's it. After listening to the young man working the bar, make fun of professional athletes and local political figures after they left, saying they didn't know how to order or eat Vietnamese food. I can only imagine what he would say about me, because I most likely gave him enough material for a comedy routine.   Would I return? I do, I'm trying to feel the love.  When: June 22 and November 1, 2016 (most recent visits) Why: Ian Froeb's List

There are two things that currently shock me. One - I cannot believe I have not written a review for G-B Grill. Two - I cannot believe they did not make the list of the Top Ten Places to Eat Breakfast in the RiverBend Area.   I personally, can only correct one of those things and I am going to do it right now. I am going to share my love and admiration for this tiny vintage diner that is off the beaten path in Alton. The only reason I can imagine it did not make the Top Ten, is being only open 4 Days a week and the capacity of diners it can handle. Even in non-pandemic times, it is limited. However, I was glad to see that they had booths blocked off to have social distancing between guest.   Being an old fashioned diner, the kitchen is right there in front of you and you can see your eggs, bacon and Hash Browns being prepared on the flat grill. That in itself is a show. The menu is a marque, so be sure to bring your glasses if you need them.   Now let's talk food. I've only had breakfast, but do plan to return and have lunch in the near future. They do not start to serve lunch until 11 AM. I love my eggs over hard with the yolk broken and they do it masterfully here. Believe it or not, many  places will not do it for me. A nice touch they do for those of us who order bacon, is that they ask if you want it crispy or soft. That there tells you, the bacon is made to order and not done ahead of the game like so many places do for the breakfast rush.   Another detail that is pretty epic is that their hash browns are also made fresh. Frozen hash browns are a no-no here. Which means they will always be crisp and prepared well. Not to many places can say they make hash browns from scratch.   My most recent visit, when I noticed I had not done a review, I finally ordered the Hot Cakes aka Pancakes. You can have your choice of quantity and I choose, two with bacon. Both of my hot cakes were thick and fluffy. Most importantly for me, they were a perfect light golden color on both sides. Yes, that is a detail I check. Both pancakes were warm and huge smears of butter had already melted into them. The syrup for the pancakes was Mrs. Butterworth, but for a dive diner, that is considered gourmet.   The service is super attentive by both dad and son who work together in this family business. It blows my mind that they call so many of their customers by name. I am looking forward to when they know mine some day.   When: Multiple. Most recently, September 16, 2021 Why: Meeting High School Friend for Breakfast

Running errands and in need of a quick lunch, so I stopped by the Atomic Cowboy. It was late lunchtime, closer to 1then 12. I picked a stool at my favorite place to dine, the bar.   I started out with one of the neighbors down the street craft beers, UCBC Forest Park Pils. It's always one of my favorites, I order it all the time when I'm at UCBC. As I studied the menu, Poutinelicious jumped out at me. I wasn't that hungry, but wanted to satisfy the hunger pains. The menu described it as crispy fries topped with, smoked chicken, cheese curds, burnt onions and chicken love. I will say the toppings were correct and they did add flavor to the fries. However, I thought the fries were limp before the toppings were added. Should have gone with the Swordfish Tacos.   Service was a little lack luster. The staff seemed more pre-occupied with doing prep work and getting prepared for the evening business.   Will I return? - Yeah, I'll give them another try.   When: February 27, 2017 Why: Lunch

A solid 3 Stars. I had not been to a Bob Evans in years and not only needed but wanted breakfast before shopping at Costco. Upon entering, it had a crispy and clean appearance. While dining I learned, they had just been remodeled within the last two months. The new look is a winner.   My breakfast was the Farm Favorite Omelet, which was a fluffy omelet filled with baby spinach, portabella mushrooms, dice onions and Swiss cheese. I was just an okay omelet, I probably would not order it again. The spinach was folded in well and the onions had a little snap to them.  On downside, the mushrooms were rubbery making them chewy and they were very skimpy on the amount of cheese. The side of Hash Browns were crispy on top, but not on the bottom. I like mine to be crispy on both.   My DP (Dining Partner) enjoyed The Homestead Breakfast. This is the breakfast to order, here. A hearty breakfast that includes, two eggs cooked to order, a cup of sausage gravy, your choice of Bob Evans sausage or bacon, choice of side and specialty breakfast bread. The DP opted for sausage patty, after all Bob is known for his sausage and biscuit. This truly was a country style breakfast.   First I must warn you, it is not a cup of sausage gravy, but an entire bowl. Even with him having two freshly made flakey biscuits, he did not use all the gravy he was served. The biscuits and the gravy surprised both of us, neither of us expected a chain restaurant to serve up some kick ass Biscuits and Gravy.  The gravy was full of sausage chunks, creamy and seasoned with the right amount of pepper.   Our server was good, but kinda over the top saccharine sweet. She'd been a wonderful kindergarten teacher. I do give her extra points for using a variety of adjectives to describe the entrees she was selling. She also knew the importance of asking for the add-on.   Will I go back? Yes, but I will not be rushing. It may be another couple of years before I return. Or it may not be until I retire, then I'd fit in with the rest of the clientele that was dining while I was there.

Once again, the International Supper Club got me to a restaurant that I would have never found on my own. It is a little restaurant tucked away in the 3200 block of South Grand Blvd. It may be small in size, but it was totally big in it's authentic Brazilian food.   When ordering my cocktail I wanted to be as "authentic" as I could be, so I ordered an Caipirinha. It's the official drink of Brazil. They make it with limes, sugar and Cachaca, then serve it over ice. I was worried that it may be too sugary, but it wasn't. The mixture with the fresh lime, made it rather refreshing. Not knowing Cachaca, I asked the server what it was similar to and he compared it to rum. Which made sense to me, since it was a tropical cocktail.   My entree, I selected Frango Ao Molho Branco. Translation - Grilled Chicken Breast in White wine sauce. It was served with a scoop of white rice and sautéed vegetables. I enjoyed their Brazilian twist on collard greens. My chicken breast was tender and moist. The portion was the size of two large tenders. I would have preferred a full breast, but for the price point I paid and the serving, I was satisfied. The white rice was prepared almost perfectly. It was not lumpy and did not stick together. Other restaurants need to take lessons from them on to prepare rice.   Our server was hustling to keep up with our group of 15 and waiting on other tables as well. At times the bartender would come out and assist when serving the food. They were professional and kept a positive attitude.   I plan on going back and checking out their lunch buffet. I want to experience more of their Brazilian offerings.   When: May 31, 2016 Why: International Supper Club

It's been awhile, so it is time to update my SCG review and give them an extra star that is well deserved.   Reasons they deserved an the extra star:  1) They open at 6:30 AM. I'm an early riser so this works perfect with my daily itinerary.   2) You can order just "One" Biscuit and Gravy. Biscuits are big & fluffy and the gravy would make a farmers wife proud.   3) Greek Omelet is one of my favorites.  4) Weekday Scrambler is an affordable and filling breakfast.   5) Great dark roast coffee. It's self serve, so you never have to wait for a server to fill your cup.   6) Works of local artist adorn the walls. Best of all, it's for sale.   Will I return? - Silly, question. What do you, think?  When: November 29, 2017  Why: Breakfast, duh.

The Good Pie is not same anymore. Moving to the Loop was not a good move in my opinion. When they were in Midtown on Olive, I use to love going there for lunch, it was relaxing and the service was always friendly. The Loop is the exact opposite.   The first red flag I received was when we entered for lunch at a prime lunch time and there was only one other diner in the restaurant and not one more came in the entire hour we were there. After the service we received, I understand why TGP was so empty. The majority of the time we were there the server remained behind the bar, laying over the top and playing on his smartphone. I guess texting and posting on Facebook is more important then creating a memorable experience for the customer. Oh wait, you did. It was so memorable, I will never return.   When we entered, the before mentioned server yelled out that we could sit where ever we wanted. Once we selected our table, he walked over and asked if wanted drinks.  I asked what bottled beer they offered and he told me they did not sell bottled beer. I then asked for a Bloody Mary and he informed me they were sold out of their house mix and had to wait for the lead bartender to come in and make it. I enjoyed a glass of water. My dining partner ordered ice tea and when it was served, the only sweetener offered was Raw Sugar. When he requested a sugar substitute, he was rudely told that they did not offer that option. He drank his tea, unsweetened.   I enjoyed a Caesar Salad with White Anchovies and the DP took advantage of the lunch special. For his lunch pizza he selected Four Cheese with the house salad. The only saving vice of my salad was the white anchovies, otherwise it was rather bland with minimal dressing. The Four Cheese pizza, was perfectly charred from the wood fire oven, but did not have the flavor of the old location.   I think we'll see them on a closing list in the very near future.

Fast food fast, that doesn't taste like fast food made quickly.  We were in the mood for hamburgers, but not in the mood to cook, so off to Sonic I drove. When I returned home, we were pleased our meal was still warm.  Our cheeseburgers were meaty and had the perfect amount of toppings. One of us had tots, they were crispy and a good change from the typical french fries. However, I had the french fries  and was totally pleased. In my book, Tater Tots are for breakfast. We shared an order of Onion Rings which were sit down restaurant quality. In closing, I'll tell you the Banana and Caramel shakes were just, "Yummy"!  Can't imagine eating in my car, but as carry-out - I'll be back to Sonic.

Was in the area and thought I do a flash back to when I worked and hung out in the grove area before it was, "The Grove".  To drive down the street and get a bag of "belly bombers" at the end of a night  was a good way to cut the booze.   A White Castle is only good when you have enough liquor in your system to counter re-act. However, I will say the french fries and chocolate shakes are good.   Now I remember why I only crave these once every blue moon.

I am shocked as you, that I am writing a review for Domino's. What shocked me even more, was the fact that I ordered from Domino's. It was a Friday night, both adults in the household has rough days at work and no energy to go out or to cook at home. So it was Domino's to the rescue with their $5.99 Carryout Special.   Their special was a large two topping pizza for only $5.99. To get this deal all you had to do was order on-line and go pick it up yourself. What a deal. They also offered me a two liter Coke for $2.99 and gave me an opportunity to add $1 to my order for the St. Jude Foundation. Pizza, soda and a charitable donation all for $10. What a deal.  Our pizza was a Pepperoni and Italian Sausage. It was covered in plenty of toppings, the sauce was spicy. Making it tasty cheap dinner.   When I arrived, I was surprised how small the space was and how efficient the team of 8 worked. The kitchen and shop was clean and they all were working at a rapid speed. They were friendly to customers as they entered and the young man answering the phone, actually had phone etiquette and skills.   It's not Bono's or Pizza a GO-GO, but when they have a special like this, I'll order from a chain.

Entertainment.com coupons get me to experience new places, especially when it is a BOGO coupon.  Getting something free will always get me to try something new.   JAB is a mix of a dive bar and a neighborhood diner. The booze is cheap and the food is inexpensive. Keep in mind you get what you pay for, it is average bar food at best. The ambiance is cluttered with a huge aluminum ladder leaning against the wall and holes in the walls that needed to be patched.   Our burgers were good, but they were way smaller then the buns they are served on. I want my burger to reach the edge  of my bun. Both of our burgers were cooked to our requested temperature. Looking at posted pictures, I was excited to see they served Steak Fries with their burgers. However, we were disappointed that they now use Crinkle Fries. At least they were crispy and still a good accompaniment to the burger.   The highlight of our experience was the Lemon Pepper Chicken Wings. They were perfectly done to a crispy coating. The lemon seasoning gave the perfect tang and the pepper gave it a spicy kick. LP CW is a favorite of mine and these were some of the best I have found in the city.   The service was hit and miss. The bartender was busy serving tables and doing the bar-tending while other coworkers were running around getting ready for a Friday night of live music upstairs.  No teamwork here, it was obvious the dining area was filling up.   I heard they also serve up a good breakfast. I may have to return and try the most important meal of the day.

I don't get this OfficeMax, it just feels weird. It also seems to be a lot smaller then your typical OfficeMax. Staff isn't as friendly and helpful as other OfficeMax stores.  However, when shopping at the Schnucks next door it is a convenient location to quickly pick some needed office supplies. I got what I needed and got out.

Splish, Splash, my car took a bath.   I use to be a fan and regular of the Hampton Car Wash. When it closed last month I wondered if my car would ever be clean again. So, I was on a search to find a new car spa for Carlos my CRV. I had no idea I was going to hit a gold mine on my first visit to a new car wash. No disrespect to the now shuttered HCW, but wow is there a difference in service and staff. Why did I stay with you so long?   This Waterway is kept as clean as the cars they are detailing. The staff is friendly and professional. In fact, they look as if they were recruited right of a private prep school or a J Crew catalog.   The prices are a little higher then what I have paid in the past, but the quality of work is better. So paying more $'s to have Carlos look his best, is well worth it.  The staff at WGW make him scrubby dutch clean.

This store must have been born again. I shopped this store before reading any reviews on Yelp and was totally pleased. The Shoe Carnival near my home on Watson Road closed and this is the next closest, so it was logical I'd give it a try. Is it in the greatest neighborhood? Not really, but it is still a safe one.  This staff was extremely helpful and friendly. I truly believe each and every associate in the store (5) spoke or had some type of interaction with us while shopping. I was impressed with cleanliness and how well organized the store was presented. I was also surprised to see that they offered various brands. I had no idea SC carried Ralph Lauren. However, I did know they are one of the better places to get affordable Nikes.   Those that know me, know that I have an obsession with colorful socks and shoelaces . I may have found my favorite selection of shoelaces at this SC, they had colors that I have been searching for to complete my wardrobe.   Give this Shoe Carnival a try!

It is still a four star experience, but I am not a fan of their Stuffed pizzas.   This visit we tried the Chicago Style, Stuffed pizza. It was truly stuffed to the edges with toppings, or should I say fillings. However, for our personal taste it was way to much dough. The way they create their stuffed pizza is simple, they just make a regular pizza and then top it with another pizza shell on top. They then add a minimal more toppings to complete the Stuffed Pizza. Like any Papa Murphy's pizza you take it home and bake. Only exception is, this pizza is baked at 375.   I agree with Tom C., beware of the size of pizzas. The large is way to large for two. You'll either have leftovers for breakfast or lunch the next day. Next time we're going to try cutting it in half. We will then prepare one half and freeze the other half for another day.   Great staff, they are always friendly and professional. They were extremely busy on a Sunday night close to closing and it was amazing how clean they kept their prep area.

It is a sad day in Yelpland when I have to give a 2 Star rating and add a restaurant to my No-No List. It is even sadder when it is a restaurant that use to be a favorite.   I use to love coming to Llywelyn's and having an order of Welsh Potato Chips as an appetizer. However, the ones we were served at lunch the other day had me scratching my head wondering why I ever liked these. The order we had were cold, rubbery and tasteless. Thank God for Malt Vinegar and ketchup. They use to be so hot and fresh when they arrived at your table. This order has me thinking they are made way in advance and scooped out of a tub when ordered.   We ordered two salads, the Country Chicken Salad and The Cobb Salad. I enjoy a good Cobb Salad during the summer. It is always a light and filling lunch. However, the one here at Llywelyn's was a big miss.  The first thing that was a disappointment was the presentation itself. It looked as if they just threw handfuls of the toppings on top of the lettuce. The second major boo-hiss were the hard boiled eggs. The yolk was outlined in green, meaning that they were over cooked. That tells me the cook was less then amateurish.  This salad was so bad, I only ate a fourth of it.   The Country Chicken Salad had a better presentation and was also better in flavor. However, not enough to make us want to come back and order it again. The SO only ate about half.   Our server not once asked if everything was alright, he just gave us our bill. We  paid it and as we walked down to Vino Gallery we discussed what we would have for dinner.   The best part of the lunch which kept them from getting a 1 Star was the ice tea in a cool plastic tumbler. I also like the fact that they offer all three of the artificial sweeteners.

Holy Mackerel, Batman getting new license plates at Deer Creek License Bureau has changed. Check in is now totally automated. You check-in at a touch screen, with either your cell phone number or you can choose an old fashioned paper ticket. It then tells you what your wait time will be. If you entered your cell phone #, they'll text you when it is your turn. Which makes it easy for you to wait outside or go browse the racks at a near by store. Just make sure you run back when you get the text.   On a large screen behind and above the heads of the staff  you can see where you are in line and how much longer your wait will be. When it is time for the next customer, an automated voice pages you by the last four digits of your phone number or the four numbers printed on the paper ticket.  It was more fun watching this screen then watching the numbers at the local deli.   The staff here provides better customer service then most license bureaus. I'm getting license plates for my car, so I don't need perky, but I don't want surly either. They now accept debit and credit cards, which is a plus for me. I was charged an extra $1 for the convenience. I hate to share the secret, but this place is much faster then other locations I have visited.

A fabulous pet store in Soulard. It is room after room of everything you'd ever need to spoil your dog or cat. At first you'd think it looks like a hoarders house, because they make use of every space imaginable. What makes them not like a hoarder, is it all is merchandised well and they know where everything is.   They have a large variety of quality pet foods and the staff we spoke with were very knowledgeable about their ingredients and difference. They also hooked us up with some new biodegradable scoop bags. Gotta be Eco friendly when walking the K-9's.   Friendly staff and endless goodies makes Pets in the City.

Warning: This review is about alcohol only. No food was consumed while researching for this review. Those who are teetotalers may skip this review and proceed to the next.   This place has two happy hours daily. That has got to put a grin on your face. If that doesn't make you smile, the prices will definitely push the blues away. You can get happy between 3pm and 6pm and if you need to get happier come back at 10pm till close.   The prices that will make you smile are all rail drinks and draft beers are half price. I'm normally not a rail drinker, but if it's half price I can lower my standards to get a good buzz on. They also offer appetizers for $6 and I agree with Julia P on this - "seems like a normal price".   Service was above average, only once did I have to remind our server that we were ready for another round as I worked my way to the restroom. (Oh, by the way they do not have Dyson Air Blades) When all the happiness was coming to an end, our server did check with us to see if wanted to make one more purchase before the price increase.   Overall if you are just drinking and want a nice ambiance or patio, Houlihan's can be fun.

I love coming to Peacemaker,  siting at the bar alone and enjoying a cocktail. It's so relaxing. I can order a couple of sides and totally make a lunch out them. I pick from a mixture of; Brussels Sprouts, Fried Green Tomatoes, Fries or Hush Puppies. Two of the four can always make me content. Sometimes a plate of fresh oysters and cold beer even hits the spot.   My recent visit was to celebrate them making Ian Froeb's STL 100 List. I'm really enjoying eating my way through his list.  His "must order" for Peacemaker is the Lobster Roll, which I've had and I can tell you the Connecticut Style is better then the Maine. When I arrived today, I was tempted to have one, but the market price was $24 and I took a pass.   I enjoyed a Louie cocktail which is a mixture of vodka (the fountain of youth), ginger liquor, lemon juice and cucumber juice with a cayenne and salted rim. Drink from a straw, because you'll burn your lips off with that rim. However, that drink is so refreshing, I'd drink from the rim all over again.   To accompany my cocktail, I had an order of my favorite Fried Green Tomatoes and a Clam Roll. This was the first time I had ordered the Clam one and was pleasantly surprised. My roll was filled with fried strips and a light aioli sauce. I also had an order of fries. Yes, I was a little heavy on the carbs, but it was worth it.  Saying the words, "worth it", my cocktail, fried tomatoes, clam roll with fries were less then the lobster roll - I call that a deal that is really, "worth it".  Perhaps next time, I'll be frivolous instead of frugal and enjoy the Lobster Roll, Connecticut Style.   When: April 20, 2016 Why: Lunch & STL 100

Trick or Treat! I open with that, because I came here on Halloween night. My neighborhood doesn't get many ghost or goblins going door to door, so I snuck out to grab a bite to eat. I was actually headed elsewhere and as I was driving, thought to myself, "hey let's go check out the new girl on The Hill."   They call themselves, An American-Italian Joint. I guess that way they can offer up a good mixture of offerings on their menu. Being Halloween, it wasn't that crowded, so I sat at the bar. I agree with Virginia, I wish they would of altered the bar area, because it feels small and cramped.   I wasn't that hungry, so I just ordered an appetizer and salad. If you like shrimp, I recommend you ordering the Spicy Pickled Shrimp - it is fantastic. I had no idea what I was ordering, but when I took my first bite I was hooked. I could easily just have it with a glass of white wine or craft beer and call it a meal. I thought pickling was only for vegetables, had no idea you could do this to shrimp and it would taste so heavenly.   When I see Fried Green Tomatoes on a menu, I gotta try them. These were huge cuts of green tomato with a thick coating of breading. They were then tossed on top of a salad consisting of butter lettuce, house-made cheese, black olives and topped with a white balsamic dressing. It comes in two sizes. I choose the smaller and still thought it was huge.   Will I be back? Gotta go back and check out the lunch and Happy Hour.   When: October 31, 2016 Why: Dinner and new hot spot in town

WARNING: This pub is a smoking bar. If that keeps you away, you are missing out on a great pub.  To be honest, I didn't even realize it until I was leaving, I was having that much fun and enjoying some outstanding bar grub.   We started out with a pitcher of beer. I don't think I've ordered beer by the pitcher, since I was in college. I've enjoyed, buckets of bottled beer, but not a pitcher. I thank our waitress for stirring us in the right direction on that one.   I love how you can or order your chicken wings here. It's simple and I wish other bars would follow their lead. You can order in increments of 6. 6,12, 18 and 24. Then of course for catering, they offer 50. After selecting your quantity, you choose your cooking style; Traditional Fried, Hand-Breaded and From The Pit. My mind was blown when I got to select from 21 sauces. We ordered a 6 Hot and a 6 Lemon & Pepper. L&P has become my favorite when it's available and Nick's did not disappoint.   For our entrees we both went Fish-n-Chips. Four large pieces of fish, crinkle fries and two pieces of toasted garlic bread. The fish was crispy on the outside, with a hot and flakey inside. I'm okay with fries at a bar being from a bag of frozen fries, especially if they are crinkle. I like how the crinkles hold on to the ketchup. I enjoyed the garlic toast, I was able to create little open faced fish sandwiches.   I've also been here for two private parties and I can say the mixed drinks and pizza are top notch, too.   If you're looking for a fun bar with cheap beer, good mixed drinks and some of the best bar grub in the city - check out Nick's. You just might see me there.

It's been over 7 years since my last review update for LV and they're still deserving of 5 Stars. Side Note - This is my 1200th review.  LV is a quality product, that is durable and strong. It's an investment, that will be with you for a long time. I'm amazed at how my wallet & checkbook are still looking good at 11 years old. You get what you pay for and at LV it is top quality leather goods. It's worth it.   One of my favorite pieces is my daily planner, it keeps me organized, on time for appointments and is a safe place for all my Yelping notes. Even with all the electronic devices I have, this is still my fave. I guess, I'm old school.   I may not buy a new leather goods product every year, but I always stop in at years end to buy my planners inserts for the upcoming year. This year they did not receive the inserts and had to order mine. It took awhile to come in, but I did not mind the wait. However, the first couple weeks of January I was kinda lost...LOL.   No matter the $ amount I am spending, I am still treated with professionalism and friendly customer service.   I'll be back? - Definitely. I already have my eye on something new.   When: January 16, 2018 Why: Inserts for Daily Planner

Had to work Easter Sunday, so no Brunch for me. I was totally bummed out. Scottish Arms to the rescue, they offered up a dinner that made up for having to work on a holiday.   I had been craving Fish & Chips all through Lent and just never seemed to find the time or place to fulfill the craving. I also have been wanting to try the F&C at the Arms, I read somewhere that they're excellent. So off to The Scottish Arms we trek.   I love the fact that TSA looks like a Pub, but you are having your meal served on white linens. Gives the experience at bit of class, in a very relaxed atmosphere.   Our meal was simple for a holiday, but I fulfilled all my cravings. We started out with Black Atlantic Mussels and Crab Cakes. The Crab Cakes were moist and full of flavor.  I love the fact that they were pan seared and not fried like so many of the other places do.  The Mussels were good, but I have never meet a mussel I didn't like. Mussels for me are like oysters to others.   We both ordered the Fish & Chips and were pleased. The serving was two huge pieces of fish and a side of french fries. The breading was crisp, yet the fish itself was tender and flaky. A squeeze of lemon was all I needed, no tarter sauce for me.  The fries were okay, would have liked them more crisp and firmer.  Our beverages of choice were two cold draft beers; Scottish Ale and Twisted Thistle. Both went great with our choice of food.   As always, the service was great and atentive.

I love this store. Every time I shop here I ask myself, "why don't you make this your regular grocery store". I have to drive a little further to get here, but the short distance is well worth it.  The produce section amazes me, the presentation is as if they were getting ready for a photo shoot. (I'll take a picture next time). Also, the vegetables are fresher then the other grocer I usually shop. Plus the fact that there always seems to be a produce clerk there to assist and answer your questions. The prepared foods section is amazing, great place to pick-up lunches for work or those lazy nights when you just don't want to cook. No need to stop at the butcher shop for those special cuts, they're here. I can go on and on, we had so much shopping here this morning getting ready for holiday baking.  The staff was helping us find things and laughing with us about our craziness. At least I hope it was with and "not at us".  This is now my grocer of choice.

Home of the Original Muffuletta. Don't believe it? Google it, it's true.   I wasn't introduced to a Muffuletta until about three or so years ago. After having one at various restaurants back home in STL, I found one that I favored and would only order them from that one deli. Having experienced the one here at Central Grocery, I am ruined for life. I will never be able to order one back home again. I have experienced the gold standard and will not accept or settle for second best.  Where do I being to describe this incredible sandwich? Do I start with the freshest and softest bread? Or the layers and layers of meat and cheese? (mortadella, salami, mozzarella, ham and provolone)  Or the marinated olive salad that totally completes and pulls the entire sandwich together? Wherever I begin, I'll end up with dancing taste buds and a satisfied tummy.    The line for Muffuletta was long, but it moved quickly. I was here in off season, I can only imagine the insanity during peak season or Mardi Gras. They do take debit and credit card, so it makes it easy for those of us who have forgotten what real cash is and looks like. They also have single size bags of chips and cold soda to make a complete lunch.  Being a fan of hot sauces, I enjoyed browsing theirs as I stood in line for my sandwich. I also grabbed a grocery tote for the friend who introduced me to a Muffuletta. I may not have been able to bring home or send him a sandwich, but at least he gets the tote. I guess it's kinda like, "I got this lousy t-shirt" that you can buy for family and friends, but it's the thought of a gift that counts.   There is community tables in back to sit and enjoy your sandwich, but I went over to the Moon Walk to people watch. So glad that, John L. H made that recommendation to me on my talk thread. I ordered a half sandwich and being alone, could only eat half of the half. It's a shame that they do not offer 1/4 sandwiches for the single diner. The other 1/4 stored nicely in my hotel room and I munched on it when I'd return through out the day.   Before leaving on Monday - I went back and bought another half to enjoy as my meals on the train back home. It was amazingly good, even hours later on the train. Oh, how I wish the place back home made them as good as the Home of the Original Muffuletta.   When: August 28, 2016 Why: Lunch - Muffuletta

This Firestone has been here as long as I can remember. It was here when I worked downtown in the past century and it is still providing top service to the downtown area. Recently they came to the rescue when George had a flat tire downtown. Or should I say, two flat tires since his spare tire was flat as well.   Luckily I have a portable air compressor and we were able to inflate the tire on his CRV enough to drive to this Firestone from Washington Avenue and Broadway.  We had to pull over and inflate the tire three different times, but we made it safely.   They had to cut the lock nut off the spare tire, because we could not find the key to remove it. They then inflated it and replaced the one that was seriously flat. It had a hole that you could stick a finger through.   They were professional, helpful and no high pressure sales. They understood George had to wait till this Fridays paycheck to buy the new tire. They flipped these tires around for the low fee of $30. That is a deal.   If you're in the downtown area and need auto care, I recommend this Firestone.   (If you want to hear a funny story to this incident, I will share it with you at some future Yelp event)

We look forward to each new issue of Sauce. At times we pick up two copies so we don't have to wait for the other to finish reading.  It provides good information about events, new openings and still highlights restaurants that have been here awhile as St. Louis favorites. Another reviewer didn't  think they gave honest criticism, I do. I just want the facts, I'll decide if it is to my liking. I don't trust movie critics, so why should I trust restaurant critic.   Keep up the good work Sauce, your doing a great job on educating the public and encouraging them to expand their experiences in food.  Sauce is free, it is worth my time and once you've read it I'm sure you'll be looking for the next issue.

Going to The Cup today, I discovered a new fashion boutique that gives me a reason to shop local. The shop offers women's and men's fashions. They also have a fabulous selection of watches, purses, messenger bags and shoes.   I was impressed with their selection of sweaters and hoodies. The sweaters ranged in price from $169 - $89 which I found to be very reasonable. One of their hoodies was by a San Francisco artist who is originally from STL and sold for a mere $60. Many of the shirts were also unique in design. It is so much fun wearing something that is so different then the "mall" fashions that people ask, "where did you get that" and that is what you'll hear when you shop 10denza.   Next time you are in the CWE drinking or eating on Maryland, I suggest you stop by 10denza and discover for yourself what I discovered today.

Citygarden is another beautiful Saint Louis park. It is filled beautiful sculptures, beautiful landscaping and beautiful fountains. What makes it even more beautiful, is you get to enjoy it for free.   It's a great place to go and escape the stresses of our crazy lives. A quite stroll through the park will have you feeling completely relaxed and refreshed. As an added bonus, you can enjoy breakfast or lunch on the patio at Death In The Afternoon which is located on the Chestnut side of the park.   I highly recommend a visit to our city residents and tourist. I also encourage our county residents to come down and experience the beauty and peacefulness of Citygarden.   In closing, I will say it one more time, this is a beautiful park.

Good old fashion Italian deli. We went today for lunch, it was my partners first time. We loved it. We had a Hot Salami and Italian Trio.  The line was long when we entered, we took our number and were amazed at how fast the line moved. The ladies of Gioia's know how to give good customer service and make a quality sandwich fast.  They've got Billy Goat Chips, which are a perfect side to a huge deli sandwich.

There is a new smokehouse in Saint Louis and I am sure it will set the standard for those that follow. It will also, have our already established BBQ restaurants adjusting their game. WildSmoke has entered the competitive STL BBQ market with an outstanding menu, customer service and atmosphere. My drive from the city to west county was totally worth every mile.   Today, I was greeted by a cheerful hostess who thanked me for coming in on their first day and explained the flow of their business. I then went over to the counter to order, I already knew I wanted Burnt Ends, so all I needed to select were my sides. My BE's"s came with two regular sides and I selected Root Beer Baked Beans and on the recommendation of the cashier I choose Sweet Potato Gratin. Being extra hungry (no breakfast) and being a fan of Mac-n-Cheese, I ordered a Premium side of Jacked Up Mac-n-Cheese.   Once your order is taken, you're given one of those numbered pagers that sit down restaurants give you when waiting for a table. You then select a table or booth and wait for your food. After a short wait, a friendly runner/server brought my food to the table. My device didn't even vibrate, he just knew where I was.   All the sides are made in house and you taste the love and creativity that went in to each of them. The Root Beer is made in house and when it is added to their baked beans, it gives a sweet twisted taste that makes these baked beans taste better then any that I have had at any other BBQ restaurant or backyard BBQ.   The Sweet Potato Gratin, deserves its very own star on a culinary walk of fame. The thinly sliced sweet potatoes were layered and topped with a crispy brown sugar top. This side was spicy enough to give my throat a little tingly burn and to have a few beads of sweat appear along my hairline and forehead. I want this recipe! I want it at Thanksgiving and every BBQ meal I enjoy. They were so good, I wonder if I need to create a list for Sweet Potatoes here on Yelp.   Their Jacked Up Mac-n-Cheese, is made with traditional small elbow macaroni. It is evenly covered in a rich creamy cheese sauce. I normally like it to be backed, but the flavor is good enough, that I didn't mind.   Finally, I have found a BBQ that knows how to serve burnt ends. They serve them as burnt ends, as full pieces of meat. I am so tired of some BBQ joints trying to be creative and dicing and slicing their BE's. They sauce and toss their ends, with just enough sauce to coat them lightly. As I enjoyed the tender pieces of meat, I had no need to add additional sauce.   I had the opportunity to meet and chat with the owners. I was also impressed with the hustle and bustle of the staff in making sure the opening day went smooth. I was so impressed with this lunch, I taking a friend back tonight for dinner. I gotta try the ribs, corn on the cob, onion rings, red neck potato salad and of course the Bourbon pecan pie.

Love me some Sauce On The Side. It is so gooey, goody, good, you need to eat with caution. Otherwise, you may end up with sauce on your front.   I'll be honest when SOTS won so many of the RFT awards recently, I was skeptical. So when the International Supper Club was to hold its May meeting at here, I was eager to experience Sauce magic. Now that I have experienced that magic, I can tell you they deserved every award.   The night immediately got off to a good start when I got Prince parking right in front of the restaurant. I was the first arrive and waited patiently on a bar stool. As I started to read the menu, to narrow down my selection, I was greeted by Dan one of the owners. He immediately knew I was one of the large group coming to dine and asked if I wanted a beer while I waited. What great customer service, they even allowed me to run a tab to which I added my meal and a carryout for the BF when I was ready to go.  Let me begin by saying, their beer list is huge for a small specialty restaurant. I stayed local with my selection and enjoyed a Schlafly Pale Ale in a chilled beer glass. Once all our Yelper's arrived we begun chatting and catching up on our lives outside Yelp. As another large group arrived, Dan who was chatting with us suggested we quickly get in line and place our orders. It was a nice gesture, but seriously his team knows how to hustle. They had those calzones and salads out for both groups pronto.   I recently have become obsessed with jalapeños, so I enjoyed a Pancho Villa.  In addition to jalapeños, my calzone was stuffed with Chorizo, yellow peppers and smoked cheddar. Then it is basted with Smoked Chili Oil and served with a side of Queso for dipping. It was so good, I was texting pictures to my cousin while eating, telling her it would be a great spot to eat before or after a Cardinals game. I even snapped a pic of Anita K.'s Smokehouse Salad to send her. Anita, shared a sampling and it was amazing. Don't be fooled by the name, there's no meat on the salad. A vegetarian would love it. To go I got the Costanza, for the BF. It was stuffed with pepperoni, eggplant, mozzarella and Ricotta.   My cousin and her family went Saturday after the Cardinals won a shut out at home. As they ordered they chatted with guess who? Dan. They told him they came on the recommendation of "me" and Yelp. He treated them like royalty and they loved their food. They enjoyed an Italian salad and Meat Me In St. Louis.   SOTS and Dan have me being a fan, which will bring me back time and time again.

Michael's is not a place you go to for location or to be seen. You go there for a good burger or gyro. On our recent visit we were still able to take advantage of their patio and enjoy the autumn weather.   We started our midweek lunch with an order of chicken wings. The wings here are different, they sprinkle them with Parmesan cheese and serve them with two big slices of french bread. Their wings are served as if they were mussels, they sit in an excess of sauce. So instead of broth, you can soak up extra spicy sauce. I found the excessive sauce to be messy and a deterrent of ordering them again. They also lacked in flavor.  However, the burgers were another story, they had true flavor. The odd shape of our burgers made it obvious that they are hand pressed right before grilling. We ordered our burgers, one medium rare and the other rare. Once they were bitten into, you could see the difference in texture. So many times when we order our burgers out, they are grilled the same. Not here, they truly know how to grill a juicy burger.   As Chris Z. says, they offer two kinds of fries; steak and seasoned. I am a big fan of steak fries and whenever they are offered I take advantage of them. I just love the thick wide cut a steak french fry. The SO had the seasoned fries and regretted the selection once we saw the two orders side by side.   Our server that day could be cast in the lead role in the upcoming movie, "The Absent Minded Waitress". She was constantly forgetting to bring stuff to the table. Then she'd just giggle and say she wasn't normally like this and she was having an off day. If she'd been on her Game, Michael's could have had a 4 star rating.

Great down home pet store. They have an excellent inventory of quality dog/cat  foods. They can help you select one that is perfect for your pet.  When ever we're shopping or dining at some of favorite spots in Maplewood, we always stop in to grab a couple cookies for the fur-babies at home.

There was no improvement and it didn't get worse, so it is still a solid 3 Stars.   Bob Evans normally isn't on my radar for breakfast, but today I had an early appointment at St. Louis Honda down the road and wanted breakfast before going. My choices in the area were fast food, Denny's or Bob. Bob won.   I didn't want a big hearty down on the farm breakfast, so I went with the Turkey Sausage Breakfast. It sounded healthy and was listed as only 350 calories on their menu. I think it is a nice touch to provide that information for those who are dieting or have health issues.   TSB was a small, but filling breakfast. It consisted of one turkey sausage link, scrambled egg whites, seasonal fruit and dry wheat toast. Pairing this up with a cup of black coffee made for a very satisfying breakfast.   Service was just okay. It was attentive and they offered me a coffee to go, which is always a nice touch. However, you could tell who the regular diners were, because they were getting much more attentive service.   Will I come back? Perhaps, when I am in need like I was today.   When: October 17, 2016 Why: Breakfast - Early Morning

Sometimes it is scary walking into a store and all the sales professionals know your name...LOL. What makes the customer service so great here is that they take the time to know and listen to their customers.  Even with all the SP's on duty today being with other customers, they each wished me a  happy holiday season as we passed.   The new item that I wanted today had not arrived yet, and they assured me I'd be called when it did arrive.

I've been been back and once again I've been drawn to the naughty side of the case. How they create their magical flavors is beyond me. My last visit, I enjoyed a White Russian and Old Fashioned. They absolutely taste like the cocktails, that I enjoy at my favorite watering holes.   It was no surprise to me, that Clementine's made Ian Froeb's STL 100 for 2016. They may only serve ice cream, but the distinction is so well deserved. The excellence that they provide in making ice cream, totally sets them high and above all others.   I am so excited that they are opening in the SOHA neighborhood, it will be much closer to my home. Almost too close, but thankfully I'll be able to walk there and burn off a portion of the calories I'll consume eating a cone as I walk back home.   As a child, my favorite ice cream was strawberry. In his listing of Clementine's, Ian recommended; the Strawberry with Balsamic and White Pepper as his "must order". It was nice to see that he recommended a "nice" instead of a "naughty". Way to go Ian, I've got a pint of it in my freezer. I think I have a new favorite strawberry ice cream.   Their naughty will always be my first love, but I am learning to be a nice boy, too.   When: April 1, 2016 Why: I scream for ice cream

It was Monday morning in the French Quarter and I needed a coffee to sip while I decided where to have my last breakfast in NOLA. My fellow Yelp friend and coffee aficionado, Christy messaged me when she saw my check-in at Addiction the previous day and told me to check out this shop as well.  Glad she told me, because I'd have never found it due to its tiny size. It truly is the size of a walk-in closet.   When I read their menu on a chalkboard, I had to go no further after seeing the first listing. I had to have the, Hellfire Mocha. They make it with habanero bitters. Don't fret, it's not like cooking with habanero peppers. The bitters are mild, but give an extra kick to the espresso and mocha. The barista suggested it iced and I'm glad that she did. I found it very refreshing.  The young lady is front of me was doing a drink run for her co-workers so we had time to chat.  She was part of the NCIS New Orleans production crew. It kinda sounded corny, when I told her I loved her show, but she thanked me. I then mentioned that the lead actor was from my hometown. She grinned real big and said, "Then you're from St. Louis". I can only assume, Scott talks about our great city.   Service is great, they have bendable straws and the coffee is more then amazing. This super tiny coffee shop is proof that size does not matter. Great things come in small packages or little storefronts.   When: August 29, 2016 Why: Coffee & Christy told me too

Was on jury duty and this restaurant was convenient for our lunch break. I live close to both Chris' Pancake and Bartolino's Osteria, so I thought this would be a good choice. It was just, okay.   I'm a big fan of the Bartolino's Salad. I've had it at the Osteria and also at their South location, so when I saw it on the menu here, I wanted it for lunch. What they served me, was no where near the Bartolino salad that I love. It wasn't even a good salad. I would have better off ordering breakfast for lunch, because Chris always does breakfast right.   Will I return? - If I get called back for Jury duty in 2 years  When: May 3, 2017 Why: Lunch at Jury Duty

I miss the Original Spicer's. It use to be one of my favorite stores. When it closed, I was so sad, but took advantage of it's Going Out of Business sales.   When this new Spicer's reopened with a very similar format, I was happy again. I once again, had a fun place to shop for unique children's gifts and even for adults who had a child trapped within.   Now I'm sad again, my last visit was a total disappointment. The shelves were sparsely stocked, merchandising looked haphazard and the variety of quality merchandise was lacking. Which made me wonder if we may be seeing another going out of business sale soon.  I was greeted by the lone employee, but beyond a "hello" there was no customer service. This visit was so disappointing, that I may never return and I love to shop and give gifts.   Times have changed, times are a changing, but I want my original Spicer's back.  It truly was a trip over the rainbow.

I am a member of the Houlihan's e-club and recommend it to those who enjoy saving and getting free stuff.  They'll send you text, e-mail messages telling you of special offerings and coupons almost every week. Some of them are short notice, but if you're flexible you can attend a great happy hour or enjoy a very cheap dinner.  Best offering of all is your birthday coupon. You get an entree up to $15 free with the purchase of an equal entree. Helps your SO or friend save $ when taking you out for your special day.   My B-Day feast started with Calamari and Asian dipping sauce. The presentation is cool, they bring it to the table in a Chinese carryout container with chop sticks. Even though the presentation was cute, we dumped the Calamari out on the plate for easier eating. The tentacles are always my favorite.  We enjoyed entree salads as our main course. Mine was the Fire Grilled BBQ Salmon served with a Sweet Citrus Vinaigrette. It had the perfect amount of dressing,  I had very little on the bottom of of the plate when I was finished eating. The spicy pecans, red onion and tortilla straws were a nice addition to the mixed greens.   The SO ordered the Prime Steak & Wedge Salad, but had a special request. He didn't want the wedge, he wanted it chopped and served as a regular salad. Our server had a hard time grasping that idea, but the kitchen did understand. However,they forgot to to dress it with the Buttermilk Bleu Cheese Dressing and we had to request it as a side. The steak was done perfectly rare, but the grilled asparagus was under cooked. Overall, a good salad and I would give it another try.    Having salads and seeing a fantastic dessert served to the booth across from us, we were an easy sell when Anthony asked us if we would like one. We shared a Chocolate Brownine with Vanilla Ice Cream. It was a perfect ending to yet another b-day celebration.

On May 6th, La Bonne Bouchee was the Yelp Saint Louis ROTD. I bookmarked it and went in the same day. When I see 28 flavors of Macaroons in a review, I did not want to waste time getting there. Convenient for me, my Buddy had a vet appointment just west of LBB that very afternoon. So stopping to buy Macaroons was daddies reward for his dog being good at the vet.   I was blown away by the beauty and selection of cakes and other pastries, but I kept my focus on the Macaroons. I didn't count how many flavors were on display, but I'd say there were a couple dozen. Macaroons to some are a simple sweet treat, but it  takes skills to masterfully make a GOOD Macaroon and La Bonne Bouchee has done it with finesse. I have been searching for quality Macaroons in our city and have finally found them in West County.  The Mango was my favorite, with many others coming in a close second. My supplier in Chicago I am sure is now going to see a drop in their internet sales.   The Yelp International Supper Club was meeting that night, so I bought a box to treat my fellow Yelpers. Everyone raved, how good they were and cool it was that our sweet treat was the daily ROTD.

We've all seen the television commercial where the dog goes crazy for Beggin Strips as a treat. That is my dogs react to the treats from Treats Unleashed. They especially go crazy for the Soft Bites in Peanut Butter. TU understands dogs with allergies, and doesn't want them to be denied flavorful treats, so they also offer their Soft Bites in a Wheat Free version.   In addition to the Soft Bites, TU offers other amazing treats cut out in various shapes, designs  and decorated with dog friendly icing making them almost to pretty to eat. What ever the season, holiday or celebration may be, TU always seems to have the perfect cookie for the good dog in your pack.   They may have become popular for their dog cookies, but their staff is also very knowledgeable on all the different brands and type of high quality foods. Let them know what your dogs dietary and health needs are and they can assist you in finding the perfect food.   Let's not forget the fashion forward canines. At TU they'll be able to find a wide selection of collars and leashes to make their owners proud when they are out for their daily stroll.  The toy selection also seems to be endless and containing everything from plush toys to the ones that can not be destroyed.   If my dogs had their way, they'd spend all of their allowance at TU.

Was on my way to St. Mary's to visit the roommate who just had a appendicitis and I needed breakfast. I selected The Market for convenience, being located down the street from the hospital. I've been to The Restaurant and Basso, but not The Market so  I was looking forward to this breakfast.   When I entered, I was immediately greeted by a cheerful man, so I followed his voice and veered to the right. It appeared to be the right direction, there was the counter to order, a coffee bar and tables. I ordered the Smoked Salmon Breakfast Sandwich and a black coffee.  I was given a HUGE cup and saucer and told they'd bring my sandwich out when it was ready.   I filled my cup with a rich dark roast coffee, selected a high top table and started working on my iPad. Shortly, the perky young man brought me my sandwich. It was a simple, but tasty sandwich. It was smoked salmon and a fried egg on toasted wheat bread that had been smeared with chive cream cheese.  Now, this is the way to start a morning.   Once I finished, I bussed my table and walked over to see what I thought was the "retail part" of The Market. To my surprise, it was no only retail, but more seating space and a huge stone fireplace. OMG! If I sat down in one of those big comfy chairs next to that roaring fire, I may still be sitting there today. That fireplace was so inviting. I could be comfortable sitting there, sipping coffee and working on my computer or iPad all day. They'd be asking me to leave.....LOL  Great place, I gotta come back to try lunch.

A mom and pop diner offering decent food at an affordable price. It has zero ambiance. In a long shot gun type dining room, the decor is plain and simple. Their servers are graduates of the Flo's School of Waitressing and I am fairly certain, Mel is in the kitchen cooking.   Breakfast is the best deal, but they turn out a good Angus burger for lunch too. You get what you pay for, so you'll leave satisfied.

Pier 1 Imports is always a fun store to find a simple gift. Especially if you are buying for someone who entertains, or if you need a holiday themed gift. It's also a great place to purchase a house warming gift, so many unique items for a new home owner.   On my most recent visit, I was on a mission for a specific item. I already knew that they had it in stock by shopping on the internet. Another coordinating item, I had to order from the website because, all STL stores were out of stock.   I found my item with ease and browsed the store for other gift ideas. I saw several items, that I most definitely will be circling back to get. With the unique variety at Pier 1, you can usually find something for that difficult person who has everything.   Also, I highly recommend that you always check out the clearance rack located somewhere in the store. Sometimes it moves around. You may just find an incredible gift on the super cheap.   As I shopped, one sales associate would breeze by and check in with me, making sure I didn't need assistance. That part of the customer service was great, it was when I got to the check-out that things went a little sour. I requested a gift box and was abruptly told my gift was too small for what they had. She showed me the smallest box and I told her, that would be perfect. I explained how I had to order the rest of the gift from the website, because all the STL stores were already sold out. When combined, that size box was just fine. I got my box, but she huffed, puffed and sighed. She then handed me my bag and not a word of thanks. I thanked her and as I left I told the other associate that her co-worker needed a break.   Will I return: Yes, I found things I can't live without.   When: November 3, 2017 Why: Specific item for cousin gift.

One of the main reasons I like Yelp is that it exposes me to new experiences. It guides me out of my box and my comfort zone.   With that being stated, I would have never experienced this totally cool neighborhood bar in Soulard. As Jenny P stated it is small and divey, but in my opinon that is what gave it all it's warmth and charm. The regulars were welcoming of new patrons and engaged conversation.   They've just opened a new game room that  offers a good variety of bar amusements. To make it easier for you to get your drink on while you get your game on, they have a second bar located in the new addition.  The staff is friendly, and the bartenders make a good drink. I was totally amazed at the quality of food from a dive bar. The crab cakes could win a blue ribbon at a county fair and the chicken strips put other bars to shame. My new Yelp friend Matt C., is right the thin crust pizza is "really good". I didn't take a menu home, but wish they delievered on The Hill.   Next time I'm in Soulard, I'll stop by 1860.

Great neighborhood bar for awesome burgers. I bounce back-n-forth between two for my visits; The Royale (Wagyu Kobe) or Bison (MO raised).  Keep in mind both of these type of burgers can not be cooked over medium. I get mine done medium rare and they are just perfect.  Your burger comes with one side, and french fries are not available. I just love it when a restaurant gets creative and doesn't offer them.  I'm a big fan of our home town Billy Goat Chips, but when at The Royale, you've got to experience their house made Sweet Potato Chips. As a child I hated sweet potato's, now I can't get enough.  Sometimes when I/we visit it's for their taco's. We'll order two each of their Smoked Brisket and Fish then share. These are the only fish taco's that I like. Save room, and I do mean room for dessert. You've gotta have "The Boozy-Q". Devil's food cake, Irish cream, Chambord whipped cream...... plus more chocolate toppings. Don't ask about the calories.

St. Louis is so lucky that Wes Johnson selected our city and within our actual city limits to open Salt.  Salt is going to give our county friends another reason to drive into the city besides a major sporting event.   The ambiance and layout of this new "hot" dining establishment is totally on mark. You can choose a cozy formal experience inside or a very casual informal one outside on the patio. Upstairs they offer two private rooms that are perfect for announcing an engagement or celebrating an anniversary or promotion.   When I saw the menu, I knew St. Louis had gotten itself another top notch restaurant. It reminded me so much of some of my favorite spots in Chicago. I couldn't wait to begin ordering and either could Brad.  Here's what we experienced:  Rosemary Manchango: sheep, spain hard $5 Rabbit, pistachio, Blueberry Terrene $5 (Brad ate this one I can't bring myself to eat Thumper) House Cured Citrus Gravlox $5 Pork and Black Garlic Rillette $6 Broiled Mussels $7 Seared Scallop $9  Wine Braised Marrow Bone $5 Duck Fat Frites $6 Mint BBQ'd Lamb Steak $16 Cheesecake $7  The house treated us to a sampling of Apple Braised Crispy Pork Belly and Pork and Fennel Meatballs. Yes, we were given a comp sampling  but that has nothing to do with me giving them a 5 star rating. They earned it, big time!!  I could make a meal out of the Broiled Mussels and the Seared Scallop. Pair them with a good white wine and I'd be in heaven.  I love lamb chops, but their lamb steak with mint bbq melted in my mouth.
