We give thumbs up for everything we experienced and look forward to going back to experience more of the menu and their Brunch.  For those who think I give too many "5 Star" ratings, and for those who thrive and feed on negative remarks, I personally didn't like the pork and fennel meatballs that were given to us on comp. However, I will try them again.   The staff was on their A-Game (Friday April 8) if they keep up the great service and Wes continues to serve up breath taking food, this will become a place to be seen.

When I scream for ice cream, I scream Clementine's.  When I try a new ice creamery, the first flavor I always try is vanilla. That's right, the first one is plain ole vanilla. My logic is, if they cannot rock my taste buds with a simple flavor like vanilla, then the rest is going to be a challenge. Clementine's Madagascar Vanilla, not only rocked my taste buds, but it knocked my socks of as well.  It is rich, creamy and oh, so yummy.   However, I must confess that I am a big fan of the naughty ice cream. My personal favorite is my favorite cocktail; Moscow Mule. I got so excited when I saw the tub of ice cream labeled, "Moscow Mule". Even though I was excited, I was also filled with doubt. How could they possibly capture the taste of a MM, in an ice cream? After a sampling, I was totally sold. It was like I was enjoying a frozen & creamy Moscow Mule. I immediately ordered a double scoop.   I'm such a bad boy, every time I visit I order from the naughty case. My last visit I tried the Bee's Knee and again I was totally blown away. I gotta start ordering from the nice side and see what I am missing by being a good boy.

If a Sunday Brunch is judged by it's offerings of Bloody Mary's and Mimosas, Scottish Arms would win a Gold Medal. They offered up one of the best BM Bars that I have experienced in St. Louis.  Five different vodkas to choose from and the bartender poured generously. Then the ingredients offered to create your own masterpiece were endless. My creation was very tasty.  As I sipped my BM and pondered on my entree selection, I noticed a blackboard promoting Endless Mimosas with Tropicana for only $14.99. OMG, what a deal. I drink Tropicana at home, add some endless bubbly, I'm game. However, I noticed it to late and instead of having a second BM, opted for a Mimosa with fresh squeezed OJ for $7.99.  Fresh squeezed is oh so fresh, makes the bubbly go down oh so smooth.   Now, on to the food. It was as amazing as my brunch beverages. I ordered the Seamus MacBenedict, which is two poached eggs with smoked salmon & hollandaise on biscuits. The poached eggs were done to perfection and the salmon was divine.  However, the hollandaise could use some improvement.  The biscuits which were the foundation of the total creation, were unbelievable. It was obvious these were not Pillsbury biscuits, but the work of a master baker.   We also ordered sides of bacon and American fries. The bacon was incredible, we found out it was cured at their sister restaurant "Shaved Duck".  What sold me on the potatoes was the use of sea salt, big fan of that type of salt.   The wait staff was friendly and made for a pleasant dining experience.  I loved the fact that they were all dressed in Kilts to follow the Scottish theme. Of course, the classic thought did go through my mind, "what do you have on under that kilt".
After 50 years of serving the Lindenwood neighborhood, this IHOP has closed its doors. They were a great inexpensive place for week day breakfast. They'll be missed by many.

Was craving Pumpkin Pancakes so we visited Sunday morning. This place is small and they cram as many booths and tables in as they can. With this being the case, the noise level is loud.  Our food was very good breakfast fare, our bacon was crisp, sausage seared well and the eggs done to order.  We ordered the same special so we had a good chuckle, my plate had more bacon and sausage then my "SO". I guess math skills are not really required to cook at IHOP.

I have to begin by thanking Aspin for her review on Yelp. If it were not for her, I would have never discovered Mini Corral Hamburgers and it is only four blocks from my work.  It may be on "Main Street", but Main Street in Alton is not the main drag, so it is off the beaten path. Now that I have discovered it, I may never brown bag again.   My first visit I enjoyed a Cheeseburger, with just the basics; ketchup, mustard and pickles. The hamburger was hand pressed and char broiled. It tasted as good as one I would make myself in the backyard. It extended the entire circumference of the entire bun. As I took each bite, I wondered why any one would go to a fast food burger joint when they have MCH in their town.   This has to be the first place that I have been to that gives you a choice of traditional fries or steak fries. I'm use to choosing between seasoned, curly or sweet, but never steak. I'm a fan of steak Fry's, so I will always go with a thick meaty fry. Their regular fry is a crinkle cut.  They also offer onion rings, can't wait to try them.  In addition to offering some of the best home made Root Beer by the glass or by the gallon for $4.59, they also have home made Red Cream soda. As a child, red cream was my favorite soda.   The staff is small town friendly, so they offer service with a big smile. I can order ahead and my order is always ready when I arrive. The menu is extensive and I can't wait to try some of the other offerings. It has sliders, catfish, chicken tenders and even steaks. Keep in mind it is a cash only business and there is no ATM on the premises.    Next time your across the river in Alton, I recommend you stop by and enjoy a Root Beer and a slider, so you can experience one of the jewels of Alton. You'll then realize there is more to Alton then, Fast Eddies and Moonlight.

Besides raindrops on roses and whiskers on Shelties, Sunday Brunch is one of my favorite things. I have a set work schedule and normally work Sunday during regular brunch hours. So whenever I have one of those special Sundays off (any Sunday off is special) I make sure to go brunch and  The Scottish Arms, is usually one of my first selections.   I recently celebrated a birthday here with an incredible  omelet.  However, the celebration started with a Bloody Mary that you can make yourself at a very extensive Bloody Mary Bar. They'll bring you a glass with your vodka of choice, I choose Absolut Peppar and the pour in my glass was very generous.   The mixes and the garnishes seemed to be endless.  You can choose from over 5 different hot sauces to spice your Mary up. Or you can add A-1, Worcestershire or Jack Daniel's BBQ sauce to give it an extra kick.  Then the garnishes are like selecting from a pickled vegetable market. My favorites are; asparagus, okra and pearl onions. Then of course I gotta throw in a couple jalapeno peppers for an extra zing.  I ordered the Feta-Spinach & Asparagus Omelet, which comes with a side of home fries. When I placed my ordered the server informed me that they were out of feta and that they'd have to substitute goat cheese in my omelet. He wanted to make sure that it was acceptable to me. I grinned like the Cheshire Cat and told him, Goat Cheese is my favorite and that was more then acceptable.   TSA uses fresh farm eggs which for me adds flavor to the eggs. I guess that is the farm boy that is still inside of me that can tell the difference. My omelet was fluffy and stuffed with spinach and diced asparagus. Next time I order this omelet, I may ask them to substitute goat cheese again, because it made the omelet.   To finish out my Sunday Brunch experience, I relaxed and enjoyed one of their Fresh Squeezed Mimosa's. It was the perfect ending for a perfect meal.   The service here is always attentive and friendly. There is just something about your server being in a Scottish Kilt that adds to the ambiance.

Having Elite status on Yelp you'd think I would have the common sense to check a businesses hours before heading out to lunch. Not this past Monday, I had my tummy set for Bailey's Range and off we went to dine in downtown STL. I was thrilled to get Prince parking only two meters away from the door. No wonder I got royalty parking, BR is closed on Monday and Tuesday. Thinking fast, Yelp on the iPhone was to the rescue and recommended another David Bailey establishment downtown, Bridge Tap House and Wine Bar.   The parking fairies felt my pain and provided me again with a parking space directly across the street from the entrance to BTH. Upon entering, I fell in love with the ambiance of the bar and how comfy it felt. There were three of us lunching so we were taken upstairs. The upstairs is nice, but not for me. I am short and the low ceiling upstairs even made me a height impaired person fell claustrophobic.  I will be dining at the bar on my next visit.   While dining at BTHWB, I was so blown away by the Mac-n-Cheese that it inspired to create a new list.  Some have reviewed saying it is the same thing as their Queso, I didn't have the Queso so I do know or do I care. It was spicy Mac-n-Cheese with a zest for life and I liked it. If someone told me that is all you get to eat in hell, I might just have to become a bad boy.   We also had the Cuba, Missouri which is a knock off of a Cuban and a damn good one at that. The other sandwich we ordered was a total disappointment, the Toasted Cheese. You'd think a tap house with amazing cheese board would have an equally as amazing toasted cheese, but not here. It was bland and had minimal cheese.  For drinks we had beer and wine, surprise surprise. Our service was above average, I think it would have been better if the waiter wasn't being run ragged. He appeared to be the only server working and the place was filling up fast and he was running up and down the steps as fast as he could. When you had his attention, he had an A game going on.   I'll be back.

Why can't my local Schnucks have a produce department like this one? I know, they gotta cater to the neighborhood the store is located, but we're talking fruits and vegetables. It's not like I'm asking for cuts of meat or other high end services. I just want my veggies and fruits to be as fresh and plentiful as this location.   This produce department is "almost" on par with Whole Foods. WF of course has more "organic", but this is still an excellent selection and variety.   I guess I'm just going to have to drive out of city into Clayton, to shop this Schnucks in the future. Which scares me to a small degree. As stated in other reviews, this is not the safest parking lot. It's not hoodlums you need to worry about, it is other drivers. However, I will take the risk to create a masterful meal at home.

I miss the Gap of days gone by. I use to be a true Gap addict.  Now, I just do not shop there as often as I use too. Many moons ago, Gap switched their house credit card over to a Gap Visa where you earn gift rewards for shopping in the store. The card has a good percentage rate, so I held on to it for large purchases. I recently got a rewards certificate to go Gap shopping.   My recent shopping experience was some what disappointing. I found nothing in the clearance/sale section, so I moved on to the short sleeve sport shirts. I could always use a colorful Madras Plaid shirt for attending a summer cookout or Yelp Event. I found a couple that I liked and was ready to go until I tried them on.   I've been dieting and have lost 30 lbs., but when I went to try a large on, it was too small. What? Even when I was fatter, I did not wear an extra-large. Size is a mental game, even if I liked the shirt, there is no way was I going to buy an extra-large.  So, I was back to browsing the store.   My eyes immediately were drawn to the back corner where they had colorful socks and boxers/briefs displayed. I've been thinning out and redoing my sock inventory, so this was a win. I have to wear an uniform to work, so I love accessorizing with colorful socks.   The service today was bare bones, I did not see a sales associate until I was at the cash wrap ready to check out. Again, I remember the days when they would be assisting, suggesting and working to build that sale.   * Side note - I found a shirt at Tommy Bahamas and I got to buy a MEDIUM. Why can't the fashion industry use the same sizing standards and guidelines?

Love this place, I have multiple pieces and enjoy them all. The quality is excellent - worth the price. Treat yourself - you'll be glad you did. The sales professionals are top-notch, they are friendly and make a pleasant shopping experience. I agree with one of the other reviewers, I wish St. Louis would get more of the latest releases.  However,  you can always have it shipped to the St Louis store.

They've added a nice addition to their deli and prepared food, Bob's Signature Smokehouse BBQ. It may not be Pappy's or Bogart's, but it is damn good for quick meal. They've got Baby Back Ribs, Beef Brisket, Pulled Pork or Chicken, and Turkey Breast. You can also get Smoked Salmon and a Whole or Half Chicken.   We've tried the 1/2 Rack Baby Back Ribs and Beef Brisket. The meat fell off the bones  and the brisket will have me going back for more. They offer eight different signature sides, but we made our own at home.   You can see the smoker as you enter the store, it sits right out in the parking lot. If you don't notice it, chances are you'll smell the apple and cherry wood that they are slowly smoking the meat over.

Once again my Entertainment Coupon Book has introduced me to a new restaurant.  The featured coupon for BPCCB was a Buy One Get One Dinner Entrée free up to a $15 value. What a deal!  We each choose a specialty sandwich for $11.95, so one of them was FREE.  They have several tables on the sidewalk, providing outside seating. As we approached, I commented that I wanted to eat inside because Arsenal is too busy of a street to be able to enjoy the good weather.  Once we entered, they had a live musician and the music was so loud I opted to eat outside on busy Arsenal.   I spotted a Bloody Mary at the table next to us and thought, that looks good so I ordered one as I read the menu. Normally, I only enjoy a Bloody for Breakfast, but I'm glad I broke my norm and had one for dinner. It was bloody good. Brad opted for a Four Hands IPA as his read the menu beverage. We also started out with the Spicy Chicken Quesadillas. It was a great way to begin our first vista to Benton Park Cafe. It was huge, so we saved half of it for my work lunch the next day. It was better then some quesadillas that I have had at local Mexican restaurants.   Our sandwiches came with a variety of sides and we both choose the Caesar Salad.  Surprise, surprise.....Benton Park Cafe does not offer French Fries as a side. They don't even have a deep fryer in their kitchen. That alone is worth a star. The dressing was not your typical creamy Caesar dressing, it was a vinaigrette bursting with flavor.   Both of the sandwiches were winners. I enjoy going out and swapping sandwich halves so you actually get to taste two. The Marinated Beef Tip Melt was my favorite. Tenderloin Tips marinated with sun dried tomatoes was smothered in my favorite cheese, Pepper Jack and served on Toasted Pesto Sourdough. Brad being a fan of Blue Cheese favored the Blackened Beef Tenderloin. It was a 6 oz. beef tenderloin, topped with Blue Cheese on a Kaiser Bun. Either way you go, you'll be amazing at the big flavor.   I'll be back to check out the breakfast food. The menu selections looked good and the pictures here on Yelp have my taste buds waiting for my return.

I heard people on Yelp love this place, so I thought I'd check it out. It is a great neighborhood coffee & cafe nestled in Soulard. As you enter, you instantly feel the warmth of a true neighborhood business. It was obvious we were new and out of our hood, but they still cheerfully greeted us as we entered. They made us feel as if we were regulars on our first visit.  It wasn't crowded, so we choose a table for two in the main area on the first floor. After ordering a Brie Veggie Omelet, Hash & Eggs and Biscuit & Gravy, I got up and walked around while we waited for our food. The patio would be a great place for breakfast in good weather and the upstairs has booths for that cozy feel and original artwork displayed on the walls for sale. The art is unique, local and very affordable.   The omelet was made with three eggs, stuffed with spinach, roasted portabella mushroom and red pepper. It is then topped with Brie cheese and served with a side of home fries. Their home fries are red potatoes cubed and fried crisp. I was surprised by the amount of spinach that they put in to the omelet, it was a hefty amount.   Their Hash & Eggs were not your typical Hash & Eggs. They serve theirs in a bowl first layered with house fries, then the Corned Beef and topped with two poached eggs and lemony tarragon hollandaise. If that isn't enough, you get a side of fresh fruit as well. The Corned Beef was good, not overly salty and the eggs were poached perfectly, they were soft and runny. However, the hollandaise was a disappointment , it was obvious it was a mix.   We also shared a single Biscuit & Gravy. It was a huge biscuit, smothered in a true country milk gravy filled with pieces of sausage. The gravy was seasoned well with pepper and salt, but the biscuit was hard and crunch. I complimented the gravy to the server, but questioned the biscuit. She apologized and explained someone new had made them and that the normal biscuits are soft and fluffy. She removed them from our bill and I promised to return to give them another chance.   I'm sure I'll be able to bump them up a star when I return, because I plan on adding SCG to my breakfast out rotation. It's good food at reasonable prices.

I love the OfficeMax Brown Bag 20% Sale, that they have this time of year. For those who are not familiar with this sale, it is when everything that you can fit into a traditional paper grocery bag is 20% off. The bag you need to use is sent out in the Sunday paper and it is a fun way to shop. I can pack that bag tight and save a bundle. It is how I stock up on home office supplies for the year.   This location has improved on its' customer service since my last visit. They finally are taking the lead of their major competitor on greeting and serving. I just wish they offered more variety like the other office big box store.

Where do I begin, to tell the story of how great a pizza can be? Let me start off by telling you about the group of four who walked in after us and sat at one of the larger tables by the window. After looking over the menu, they all got up and walked out. When the server asked them, they told her they thought they were a "regular pizza" place. Big mistake folks, you should have stayed and experienced a Neapolitan pizza baked in a wood burning oven. You would have been talking about it for days.    We started off with their house made Sangrias. I enjoyed the multi-berry with lemon cello and my friend had the peach. Both of them were refreshing and a nice compliment to our appetizer of fried calamari. I have never seen calamari served in big rings, they were very similar to onion rings. The flavor was as big as the rings themselves. The breading and seasoning was so great, I didn't even need the puttanesca sauce for dipping. I did try the sauce, which was different from the traditional marinara that is usually served with calamari. I highly recommend you try them on your visit to APS.   Wanting a full experience of APS, we took advantage of their lunch specials and ordered one pizza and pasta to share. The pasta came with a small garden salad that we enjoyed at the same time as our calamari. It was a good mix of greens, halved cherry tomatoes, thinly sliced red onions in a vinaigrette. The salad and calamari together would have been a nice lunch, but why stop there.   Our choice of pizza was the thriller. It was spanish chorizo, tomato sauce, mozzarella and oregano. Don't be fooled, when served the chorizo looks like pepperoni, but the flavor will far exceed. I loved the crisp bottom, with char marks from the wood burring oven. The fettuccine all'amatriciana, was one of the most unique and flavorful pastas.   The service was quick for a lunch time and friendly. The owner even came over and chatted. He truly is concerned about the quality of product and his patrons satisfaction. I look forward to experiencing Happy Hour and dinner at APS.

This place is awesome. When I was prepping for a Florida vacation, I checked out a couple local tanning salons before selecting this one for my pre-trip tan. The facility is extremely clean and the staff is friendly and professional. My trip was over a year ago and I still visit Tan Co. it helps keep my tan dark and I feel like I just got back from the beach. I also, like their Mystic Tan, it covers the body well and does not look like some lower quality spray tans. I'm a big fan!!!

Pencils, Scissors and Sharpies. Oh, my! I love an office supply store, almost as much as I love a kitchen gadget store. They both captivate me while I shop. I can mindlessly wander up and down the aisles putting things in a shopping basket that I had no idea I needed.   However, when it is time to send a card or personal note to friend, I can always color coordinate the ink to the card. Also, my filing system at home would put most office administrators to shame.   This recent visit to Office Depot had a mission. I wanted a second three hole punch. I've gotten tired of having to adjust the distance between my large three ring binders and my smaller one. So I decided it would be wiser to just buy another one and then they'd both be permanently set for each notebook.   As I entered, I was cheerfully greeted by a sales associate who walked me straight to the area where a variety of punchers were displayed. It was not an easy choice, but I managed to pick one out after examining the display models. Since it was going to be a duplicate, I let price point be the deciding factor.   I thought having a sales associate take me directly to my needed item, would keep me focused. Wrong! I still managed to find other little goodies as I walked to cashier. I found a little bundle of mini (pocket size) composition books. These are going to be great for taking Yelp notes.   Store is well organized and clean. The sales floor associates and cashiers are friendly and professional. Be sure to sign up for their rewards program.   When: July 11, 2016 Why: Hole Punch

I'd say Crow's Nest is 3.5 Stars and very close to 4. Come on Yelp, figure out away for us to give 1/2 stars it really does make a difference.   I was in Maplewood "shopping local" on Manchester Avenue and was hit with the lunch time hunger. I took the opportunity to not only shop local, but to dine local as well and what a better choice then the new Crow's Nest.   I was promptly greeted by the bartender as I entered and told I could sit wherever I liked. I took one of the open booths across from the bar and started to take notice of their draft beer taps. They had one of my favorites, Schlafly's Pale Ale so it was a no brain er.   After looking the menu over I choose the Cheeseburger with cheddar and Waffle Fries. As the server AKA bartender,  (he was doing double duty and doing it well) left my table, I checked my iPhone for the time. Since there have been so many comments about how long it takes, I wanted to time it. Must have been a good day, my burger was at my table in under 15 minutes.   I ordered mine medium and it was done to my liking. It was garnished with lettuce, red onion and tomato. I do not know where they get their tomatoes,  but for a late fall tomato it was excellent. When presented, I thought the bun was a little over toasted on the grill due to the dark coloring, but I was wrong.  It was better then a grilled one at Culver's or Steak - n - Shake.  To be fair Crow's Nest, I will tell you now that I will be back.

Bobby, your frozen custard is so rich and creamy. It is so flavorful and delicious that if you were located on the Missouri side of the river, I'd be tempted to cheat on my regular custard boyfriend Andy. In addition to your custard, I fell in love with your caramel apples. You'd have me cheating on Merb, my favorite candied apple man.   I've stopped by twice while I have been on the Eastside and both times I've been impressed. My go to concrete is an M&M, which I tried on my first visit and my tastebuds did a happy dance. On my second visit, I expanded my concrete experience and had a mini Heath Bar. The mix of the Heath chocolate and crisp toffee, with Bobby's custard made a great afternoon delight.   As I was in line to place my custard order, I noticed the huge rolling rack of caramel apples. I then noticed all the busy staff off ladies making and wrapping these decedent treats. The apples are huge, covered in a thick layer of caramel and then covered completely in a variety of toppings. I choose traditional, pecans. The apple was so huge, I had it for dinner the next night. Hey, it may not be the healthiest dinner, but I had a fruit.   Seriously, Bobby's was a pleasant surprise. The ambiance is a throwback to the days of drive-ins and the music completes the mood. The servers are friendly and on both of my visits, were a older and more mature staff. I am a man who is not afraid to wear pink and obvious Bobby is not scared of that color either - it is everywhere.  Will I return - My Sweet Tooth, says yes.   When: July 12 and August 31, 2017 Why: Eastside custard experience

Congratulations, Bobby. I'm bumping you up to 5 well deserved stars. I am so in love with your frozen custard. It's so rich and creamy. The popular custard stands in St. Louis cannot compare to the quality of product and customer service that you provide. I am a fan and you are so worth the drive. I stop by every time I have dinner in Edwardsville.   On my way to a dinner, I stopped and bought Carmel Apples for the other guest and of course, one for me. While at dinner, I made sure to leave room for a mini concrete on the way home. The Yummy Drummy, satisfied my sweet tooth, before I drove back to STL.   I'll be back? - You betcha.   When: October 14, 2018 Why: Carmel Apples and Best Frozen Custard

A classic little ice cream shoppe, tucked away in Historic Old Webster Groves. We've all heard the saying, "You scream, I scream, we all scram for ice cream'. Well let me tell you, after eating some of Beckie's creative creations, you will be screaming with delight.   I first discovered Serendipity, by enjoying their ice cream while having dessert in several of the popular restaurants in the metro area. It was so yummy, I finally promised my first born child to a server to tell me who was the supplier of the masterful ice cream. He gladly shared the information with me and did not require me to keep my promise. (Good thing, because I have no children) I was pleasantly surprised and happy to know that it was an ice cream shoppe right here in the Lou.   With the flavors changing daily and seasonally, it is hard to pick just one favorite to tell you about. So I'm going to tell you about several flavors that make my toes curl and my tummy happy. My #1 favorite and will be required eating at my last meal is; Sea Salt Caramel. Ice cream and life can not get any better.   Others that come in so close, they'd have to be tied for second place are; Cinnamon (best for breakfast) Chocolate & Orange (total YUM), Mint Chocolate Chip (brings back my inner child), and  Gold Coast Chocolate ( send me to Betty Ford for chocolate addiction). Seasonal favorites are Pumpkin Pie (a must for Thanksgiving Dinner) and Caramel Apple (no need for Merb's Bionic Apple).   I wish they were closer, but I am thankful they are not.  However, I live close to 44 & Jameison and Serendipity is close to 44 & Big Bend making it a very easy trip for these sinful treats. Keep your Froyo and  give me the real deal, Serendipity Ice Cream.

My most disappointing meal in NOLA, was here at TOCPR.  Anyone who knows me, knows I love a Sunday Brunch. I wanted somewhere that the locals go, I didn't want one of the touristy traps for my favorite meal. So whenI asked around, The Old Coffee Pot was always one that was suggested. I even had two friends back home recommend it, so I thought I was safe. I should of researched Yelp more or gone with a touristy restaurant.   Let me begin with the positive. My experience was the opposite of Matt E., my service was southern hospitality and the food was bland and tasteless as hell. The service was as if your favorite aunts were serving and taking care of you at a family reunion. There was a lot of lovey-dovey name calling, which made you feel right at home. Almost as if you were a regular.   The food on the other hand was a major disappointment. I can only guess, that they may have been breaking in a new cook, because the waitresses kept yelling at him. I used the word cook, because a true chef would have never sent food out of his kitchen prepared the way mine was.  My entree was the Crabcake Jonathan, which is their version of an Eggs Benedict. I ate the crab cakes and enjoyed them. However, the rest of the entree was a mess. The poaches eggs were over cooked, they basically were hard boiled eggs. The yolks were completely  done. Having lived with a chef, I've learned the art of hollandaise sauce and I've had better from an envelope of Knorr's then what was drizzled on top of my breakfast. I also think they totally forgot to toast my English Muffin. If they did, it was very light. My side was a cold serving of potatoes. The only other bright spot of this entree was the two little breaded and fried shrimp.  In closing, I'll say my biggest disappointment was the Bloody Mary. When I don't finish a cocktail, especially a Bloody Mary at a Sunday Brunch, you know it is bad.   Will I return? No and I suggest the locals raise their standards or look for some place new to enjoy brunch.   When: August 28, 2016 Why: Sunday Brunch on vacation

Love to entertain at home? Then this is the store for you, it will make your entertaining so easy and impressive.  I like their selection of housewares, stemware and oh, hell I like every department. Parts of my house could be an C&B Outlet store.  I hate to admit it, but when I walk in to The Boulevard store, it is like Norm walking into Cheers. Everyone knows my name.  Perfect place for the housewarming gift, or Bridal Registry.

A delightful lunch. We started out with Toasted Ravioli's, (which I normally don't order) and they were actually very good. We ordered, Veal Parmesan and Tuto Mari with red sauce. The veal was tender and flavorful and the seafood was abundant in the pasta. The house salad was a great beginning to the fabulous entrees. Fresh bread, butter and oil were readily available. The entire staff were friendly and provided 4 star service. Can't wait for my next visit.

Before shopping here make sure your car insurance is up to date. These craft people may be creative, but they lack driving skills. I think they are so excited to get home with their goodies and start creating new "crafty" things, that they lose all common sense behind the wheel.   However, while I was in the store I found everything I needed to create a Halloween costume and discovered they have a lot of other stuff that I didn't know I needed. They had aisle after aisle of stuff you can use to make other stuff. Who knew there was so much stuff in the creative craft world.  Walking through the store was like walking through a time warp, one aisle you're celebrating Halloween which is later this month and the next couple of aisles is Christmas which is months away. The aisles in between were dedicated to autumn and Thanksgiving. Hobby Lobby can make help you make your home festive for any holiday or celebration.   There seemed to be be staff everywhere,  putting out new merchandise and keeping displays organized. Being overwhelmed with all the stuff, I couldn't find gift tissue so I asked a girl putting out scented candles. She politely told me they were over there next to the gift bags. Wow, why didn't I think of that. Maybe it was because I was so overwhelmed with all the stuff. Yes, I then had to ask where the gift bags were hiding.   If you're creative, Hobby Lobby is your candy store.

There are two things that I do pretty much on the regular and they are; celebrate Cuatro de Mayo instead of Cinco and go out for New Year's Eve Eve instead of New Year's Eve. I have just as much fun and I avoid the crowds and madness.   This year I was pleased to see that, The Libertine was offering its' NYE menu on the Friday and Saturday nights before the "real" NYE. What a deal! It was just what I needed and it was at one of my favorite restaurants in STL.   As my usual, I took a seat at the end of the bar. Having studied the menu on Facebook, I already knew my choices, but took time to re-read and perhaps have a change of heart or tummy. As I pondered my choices, I enjoyed a Manhattan made with Rye and decided to stay with my original menu plan.   I started my NYEE celebration with, Wild Blue Crab Hush Puppies. It was a serving of six crispy hush puppies. Their un-uniformed shapes, told me they definitely were hand-made. They were tastier then those I have had in New Orleans.   Being a fan of Brussels Sprouts, I could not resist having the Brussels Sprouts Salad as my next treat. The salad was huge, could have easily been shared by two diners, but I managed to eat most of it all by myself. It was shredded brussels sprouts tossed with, dried figs, Missouri apples, toasted pecans, crispy caramelized red onion and topped with Gorgonzola Bleu Cheese. The dressing, a Maple-Mustard Vinaigrette is what pulled all those items together to do a happy dance on my taste buds. I'd like to see this become a menu staple here.   My main entree, Dayboat Jumbo Sea Scallops was a true, piece de resistance. They were simply pan seared and served with local honey glazed heirloom carrots. Yes, they truly were JUMBO and I wish Chef Samantha and proprietor Nick would offer them more often as well. Between us, they were better then 801 Fish and I love their Scallops.   I'm always pleased with the service at the bar. Tonight I had Matthew using his talents to make my NYEE enjoyable. He even made a wine recommendation for me to have with my scallops. It was perfect.  The service was attentive and I was impressed how quickly my food came out. I did not order everything at once. As I finished one item, I order the next and it still came out extremely quick.   Will I return - In 2018, I will. TLNE is one of my go to's in Clayton.   When: December 30, 2017 Why: My New Year's Eve Eve Celebration

Not impressed with this new location. I never visited the one across the street, so I cannot compare the two, but this one disappointed me. Yes, it is ultra modern, but it stark and modular. It is cold in design and the staff is cold as well.   The quality of food and beverage still meet the high standards I expect from SLBC. I also, liked what I'd call the Progress Board, which allows you to watch the status of your order. If you watch the board, you'll know your order is ready before they call your name out.   Unlike Kay, I am so glad they did not put a drive-thru at this location. I am anti drive-thru at any business. So when I see a new one that opts out of that service, I am a happy customer and in this case a happy stockholder.   I'll be back and hopefully the staff will be adjusted to the new digs and have a better attitude.

We were pleasantly surprised with our dinner tonight.  This little mom and pop BBQ restaurant that has been around since 1999, totally hit it out of the ball park. It is located on a side street, the storefront is very plain and the dining room is as stated in another review, very minimalist. However, their ribs and side dishes are top notch. In fact, they are better then some of the popular BBQ joints in the big city of STL.   I drove by after work, running a local errand before going home and saw on their marque, Rib Dinner for 2 $23. Sounded good to me, so after completing my errand I called home and suggested their deal for dinner. We agreed to take a chance and give Carver's a try.  I already know I will be picking dinner up from here again, in the future.  Our dinner included; a full rack of ribs, four individual sides and two dinner rolls. Both of us enjoyed the cole slaw which was in a light vinegar and oil dressing with sunflower seeds sprinkled on top. Great flavor, it was not neither to sweet or tart. Goldie Lock's would say, "it's just right".   I enjoyed the the green beans, which were fresh and made with bacon. Enough said, we all know everything is better with bacon. My dinning  partner loved  his baked beans. They were in a rich flavorful sauce and they too had pieces of bacon.  It was obvious the sides we choose are definitely made in house.   Our ribs were the biggest surprise.  At first I had my doubts, when I saw they placed them in a Styrofoam container. I thought they'd wrap the whole rack up in aluminum foil, so we could cut them up at home. To our delight when we lifted the lid on our container, it was full of individual ribs. They had already done the carving for us and each rib was full of pull off the bone tender meat. Their dry rub added enough flavor for me, so I did not need either of the sauces they provided.  The DP, did use the sauces and totally preferred their house which is a spicy sweet.    The service was what you'd expect at a mom & pop, small town restaurant. It was relaxed, casual and friendly. They say, good things come in small packages. Perhaps we can also say, good restaurants come in small towns.   When: 28MAR14 Why: Dinner

I am not a DIY type guy, but I will say out of the Hobby Lobby stores I have shopped when I need to, this one in Kirkwood is the best.   Today I wasn't even shopping, I was only here to meet up with my favorite cousin to have lunch in downtown Kirkwood. With that being said, I walked out of the store with a bulging bag of gift boxes and gift tissue. It was all 50% off and the holiday season hasn't even begun.   My gift wrapping is going to be so easy this year. All I need to do is make fabulous bows and having worked at Tiffany's, I can make a mean bow.   I'll be back? - Not often, but when the need arrives I'll return.   When: November 19, 2017 Why: Mindless Shopping

Wanted to grab a quick breakfast after getting gas at Costco and before taking my car to the dealership for repairs. Checking my options on Yelp, this Chick-fil-A was going to be the fastest.   It located in the parking lot of South County Mall in a very cramped space. Even in their own parking lot, they had cones up blocking the direction and path you could travel. There were more people using the drive-thru then coming inside to pick-up their food. Does anyone get out of their car anymore?   I've recently gotten hooked on Cold Brew Iced Coffee and was impressed to see that Chick had one on their menu. However, it had more ingredients then I wanted. Chick-fil-A Iced Coffee is handcrafted daily, made with a custom blend of cold-brewed coffee and fresh 2% milk, sweetened with pure cane sugar and served over ice. I just wanted the coffee with no milk or sugar. It was good, but I didn't want the sugar.   My breakfast was a plain and simple Chicken Biscuit. How can you go wrong? A chicken biscuit is definitely more tasty then a sausage biscuit. The biscuit was fluffy and the chicken was crisp and juicy.   The service was typical cold fast food service. There was nothing warm and fuzzy about the interchange with the staff.   I did like that they had fresh flowers and a box to "Save Our Sauce". It was also cool to see a motion sensored trash can.

If it were not for Aaron B. I would have never discovered the Bon Bons here at Serendipity. He is so right, they are the BOMB BOMB. They're the perfect ice cream treat. They're the famously flavorful Serendipity ice cream dipped in chocolate which forms a hard shell. They're bite size and you can't just stop at one.   I love that Serendipity is expanding their brand beyond their parlor in Webster Groves. Recently I enjoyed a mini cone at Five Star Burgers and I always ask at local restaurants who does their ice cream before ordering. Serendipity always closes the deal. While at a recent Yelp event at SHIC, Beckie announced to us that her ice cream will be available at Field Foods.   If Serendipity keeps expanding their brand, my waist will expand too. Who needs Ben & Jerry when you have Serendipity in our hometown.

Great place to buy those hostess gifts this holiday season. Not everything is monogrammed and you can seriously find something for everyone.  They have gifts for the young city girl, things a grandmother would enjoy and everyone in between.   I entered the store at the same time as  a lady close to my age and we both went about our shopping. The young lady working asked the woman if see needed help and assisted her. As the sales girl was going to the stockroom, she stopped and asked me if I was with the lady. When I responded, "No.", she immediately apologized for not asking me earlier if I needed help. She said they were not use to men coming in the store. I grinned and said, "Men shop, too".   I found a couple of holiday gifts and a birthday gift as well. I mailed the birthday gift on Friday and got a call this morning from the recipient raving how much they loved it.   Like Aimee, I may not shop here often, but now that I now what they have I will be back for those special little gifts. Who knows, I may just get something monogrammed next time.

It's a Starbucks. What makes this one different from all the other Starbucks, is that they are slow as molasses that has been kept in the ice box. I don't even get complicated drinks. I order cold brew, black and it still takes forever. However, they do provide me with a laugh. They can't spell my name right. I could understand if they spelled it with a ph instead of the v, but here they spell it with a b. The last poor barista who tried to call my name out had no idea how to pronounce Steben.  I give him credit, he politely asked how to pronounce it. Since the v & b are next to each other on the keyboard, I just smiled and told him it was a typo.   This Starbucks is in my hood, so I'll continue to support them. I'll just take a deep breath before walking in and make sure my patience switch is flipped to the on position.

Fannie Flagg would love this place. PLAC serves up the absolute best Fried Green Tomatoes. What sets them above all the other FGT's that I have had, is that they are pickled green tomatoes. The pickled flavor, gives them an extra zing and the crisp breading completes well. What was sad about these tomatoes, is the fact that they were the best thing we enjoyed that night.  Here's the rundown on what else we enjoyed:  2 Types of Oysters were not impressive for $3 an oyster. I've had equally as good oysters at other establishments at a lower price. The staff here still needs some training on how to shuck an oyster. The Thai Ginger sauce was spicy and a good accent to the oysters, but the Watermelon one was totally flavorless.   Hush Puppies were overdone  and an embarrassment.   My main entree was the Mussels and I was so disappointed. Not only was the portion of mussels served was small, but so were the actual mussels. The broth they are served in, was very forgettable.   My friend who's birthday it was, ordered the Lobster Roll Maine Style. Which is served cold and with Mayo. He enjoyed it, but for me it was way too much mayo. When I return, I'll try the Connecticut Style which is served warm and with butter. I've lived in Boston and that is the way I like 'em. The accompanying fries were good and I like that they serve ketchup in a small cup.   Being a birthday celebration, we had to have dessert. We choose two of the pies with soft serve ice cream on top. Having lived in Louisville briefly, I went with their Derby Pie and the birthday man choose Apple Caramel. Birthday boy had the best pie, the apple and caramel melted in your mouth. The Derby Pie had good flavor, but it was the first Derby Pie I have ever seen with crust over the top. I think the extra crust, diminished the flavor.   The ambiance is cool and relaxing. Our server was friendly and knowledgeable, but at times I felt as if I were being rushed.   I'll return to experience more, but this is not going to be a place that I frequent often.

Yum-Yum!   So many forget that Serendipity was the trend setter for homemade ice cream in the St. Louis area. They blazed the trail for those newer ice cream shoppes that have popped up in the last couple of years.   Being in Webster Grove's for  a YEE at The Frisco, a group of stopped by afterwards for a sweet little treat. Some of my friends went whole hog and got huge cones or house made ice cream sandwiches. I was already fairly full and opted for a kid's cone. I like the fact that they let adults order the kids cone, some of the other parlor don't.   I'm a sucker for any ice cream that has, "cake" in it's name, so my flavor of the night was, "Birthday Cake". It was so tasty, I'll be going back for more in a few days, when it truly is my birthday.   The staff is typical ice cream parlor staff, high school kids. They work quickly, are courteous and friendly. May be young, but they're doing a great job.   I'll be back? - Yep, for more, Birthday Cake Ice Cream  When: October 30, 2018 Why: Sweet Treat

Mid-Town has another winning restaurant to add to its' collection. David Bailey amazes me how everything he touches turns to gold. Hugo's has a simple menu and minimalist decor and it is a winning combination.   I saw a tweet this morning from Sauce Magazine announcing that today was opening day. Seeing that, it was easy to decide where to go for lunch. The location is directly across from two other mid-town famous restaurants. With all these great restaurants clustered together, parking still was not an issue.   I started out with a locally craft beer from Urban Chestnut and  some Crunchy Brussels Sprouts. I never liked brussels sprouts as a child, now I gotta have them every time I see them on a menu. These were roasted in a cast iron dish, with house bacon and topped with asiago cheese. Delicious! It's a sharable size, so order it and share with your friends.   My entree was, a Hot Chicken Pizza. The chicken on this pizza was; buffalo chicken pepperoni. It is one of five different pepperoni's available. The other four are; house (100% beef), Spicy Beef, Duck and Vegan. Making it easy for everyone to find a pepperoni pizza to satisfy their needs. In addition to the buffalo chicken pepperoni, mine had; siraracha sauce, mozzarella cheese, pine nuts and celery. I would have never thought of adding pine nuts and celery to a pizza, but they truly added to the flavor.   After my beer, I enjoyed a house cocktail. boulevardier. It is a blend of bourbon, campari and vermouth. If you like a Manhattan, you'll love this cocktail. It will be a classic.   As another diner was leaving, she raved about the Blondie for dessert. I was already stuffed, but I couldn't resist.  I am so glad, I over indulged. I spoke with the chef and I agree with him, there is no need to have anything else on the dessert menu, this one does it for everyone.   Will I return: Absolutely  When: September 20, 2017 Why: Lunch on Opening Day

Yippie! I finally have eaten at all four of the local MTJ's. What I love about MTJ is the consistency. It doesn't matter which location I enjoy, the food, drinks and service are always top-notch.   This visit to MTJ, I was introducing family members to one of my favorite taco haunts. We started out with chips and salsa and an order of guacamole. My sister loved the guac. I'm a fan of their chips and salsa. Some complain about having to pay for them, but you get what you pay for and that is quality freshly made salsa's and house made chips. Those free chips and salsa at other Mexican restaurants, cannot come close in comparison to these.   Our drinks of choice were; for me a Mission Margarita, all those fresh ingredients go down so smoothly. My sister, not a fan of Marg's enjoyed a Vodka and Lemonade. She was pleased, they used Tito's, her favorite vodka. Steve her husband, had a Busch beer. All I can say about an A-B product is that it was a 16 oz can.   Before ordering food, I educated my guest by showing them my pictures of everything I've eaten at MTJ. It was like a photo menu. Every item they asked about, I had eaten and had a picture to share.   My sis wanted a Burrito. I kept telling her they were huge,and she still ordered the, South Beach. She has recently completed cancer treatments, so her appetite wasn't a big as her eyes. She ate only about a fourth of it and I got to bring the rest of it home for lunch the next day. We were both happy. Steve went with Empanadas and Carne Asada taco. He was impressed with the flavor and also that the order was 3 separate empanadas.   I went with my usual order of three tacos. Baja Fish (fried),  Mango-Hop-Anero Shrimp and a Habanero Chicken. My favorite has always been the Baja Fish, but today the Habanero Chicken stole my heart and may be my new favorite and go-to order.   The service was personable and friendly. Just like it is at all the other MTJ's. Again, I repeat myself, I love the consistency of MTJ.   If you love tacos and Margarita's, you gotta give any of the MTJ's a try.   I'll be back? - May-be not St. Charles, but I'll be back to one closer to home.   When: August 21, 2018 Why: Lunch with the sister

Last year when Ian Froeb announced his STL 100 and Niche was #1, I couldn't wait to go.  Before I knew it, Gerard was announcing it's closure and I didn't get a reservation in time. I missed out on experience Niche. So when, Sardella landed on the list for 2017 at #6, I wasted no time and went immediately. When I say immediately, I mean I went Saturday night right after his list appeared in GO! Magazine insert to the week-end Post-Dispatch.   I arrived around 5:45 PM and took a seat at the bar. Dining alone, you can always find a spot at the bar. I started off with one of their signature cocktails; Welcome to Heartbreak. It was a delectable bourbon cocktail, that I was able to sip and enjoy as I relaxed at the bar. I then debated with myself if I wanted Mussels. It wasn't a serious or long debate, I ordered them.   Their Mussels are listed under, "Small Plates", but my bowl of mussels was huge. They were prepared with; white wine, Creme Fraiche, Thai Chili and Smoked Paprika. Along side these succulent mussels, was a ginormous slice of toasted bread that i used to soak up the mouthwatering broth. Serving size is perfect for sharing, or as a complete light meal for one.   Since I knew I was coming, I held back all day on eating, so I could feast. After my mussels, I ordered; Gnocchi of the Sea. It is what Ian Froeb says is a, "Must Order". It was scrumptious. I'm a big fan of Crab, so when it was Ian's must order, I was game. Seasoned  with tomato, Chili and Bone Marrow. It's listed as, "Pasta", but the serving size is definitely a "small plate".   My second cocktail was a, Manhattan one of my favorite Classic Cocktails. Damn, was it good. I always love it when a bar, uses a single large ice cube for my Manhattan. It's  the attentions to details that make a dining experience complete. Sardella pulls out all the bells and whistles on the little details. In addition to the large cube, they offered up cloth napkins, a seafood fork for my mussels and a USB slot under the bar for charging. With the attention to these details, you'd think they'd take notice of the bowl they served my Mussels in. It had chips in the enamel and should be tossed. However, the flavors were so strong, I'm overlooking it and still giving them 5 Stars.   The bartender who did double duty as my server, was charming and warm. He made me feel comfortable dining at the bar, as we chatted the art of making drinks and their garnishes.   Will I return? - Gotta experience breakfast and lunch  When: March 4, 2017 Why: #6 on Ian Froeb's STL List 2017

St. Louis Union Station Soda Fountain is the perfect spot to have a quick lunch/bite before or after riding, The St. Louis Wheel.   Our party of three arrived at noon and there already was a wait for tables. Over half the restaurant was filled with convention attendees. It was easy to spot them, they all had lanyards hanging around their necks.  Even with the crowd, our wait was not long.   Normally, I like the coziness of a booth, but today we were seated at a four-top table in front of the actual soda fountain. It was a great show, it was fun watching the, to use a classic term, "soda jerks" make all the sweet treats. Numerous times we were asking our server, "what's that?". They all looked so delicious. For our sweet treat, after our lunch we ended up enjoying, The King.   Now let's talk about the real reason we came here, our lunch before riding The Wheel. I ordered the Single Grilled Cheeseburger and my cousins enjoyed, Fried Chicken Sandwich and a BLT. To accompany our sammies, we all shared two sides; Crinkle Fries and Onion Rings.   I enjoyed my burger, which was loaded up with the typical, LTOP. A single was enough, I could not imagine eating a double along with a side and one of the sweet treats. My cuz who had the Fried Chicken Sandwich said it crisp, moist and flavorful. She normally doesn't like mayo and had them put it on the side. When it arrived, it was a flavored mayo in a little cup and she liked it. Her husband, enjoyed the BLT. He said the applewood smoked bacon was a flavorful twist on the classic sandwich.   We were so glad we all shared the our sides. The portions are plentiful and enough to share. The crinkle fries (my favorite style) were crispy and seasoned with just enough salt. The onion rings I found out are not made it house, but I'll tell you that they were pretty tasty for being a frozen product. It could have fooled me, they were that good.   The dessert, our finale was a delicious sweet treat. As I stated earlier, we went with, The King. It was a delightful mix of sweet and salty. It all centered around a big scoop of peanut butter banana ice cream, surrounded by sliced bananas and covered in peanut butter sauce, topped with bacon and chopped peanuts. A sundae is not complete without the whipped cream topping and maraschino cherries on top.   Eric our server was a delight. He was honest with his recommendations and didn't mind splitting our checks and that we shared our sides and dessert. I was also impressed that one of the managers was hands on assisting all the servers. She even took time out twice to chat with us about our first visit. The floor captain also came over and thanked us for coming in as we were getting ready to leave. Overall, very friendly staff.   When: January 9, 20202 Why: Lunch before riding, The Wheel

Their menu boost, that they have over 8, 721,000 different burger combinations available. I am not a mathematician, but with their 5 step burger ordering process I guess it could be true.   When ordering or should I say "creating"  your burger, you have 5 simple steps to follow:  1) Pick the burger 2) Degree of doneness 3) Pick the Bun - Honey Wheat or Kaiser Roll 4) Pick the Cheese - 9 Cheeses to choose from 5) Pick the Toppings - 26 different toppings to cap off your burger.   What totally surprised me on our visit is that, Cheeburger Cheeburger  has table service. I was so expecting the same as Five Guys and Smashburger, order at the counter and a runner would bring you the food. Having a server who was friendly and knowledgeable about their menu makes for a much more enjoyable lunch.   It was a cool, non-rainy day so we opted to dine on the patio. Even though it basically sit out into a strip center parking lot, it enjoyable. We started out with Fried Pickles, which could compete and most likely beat some of the local bars on being the best.  They were thinly sliced and the batter was very similar to a Tempura, making it very pleasurable for the palate.   When having a burger out the hardest decision for me is,  do I want fries or onion rings? Cheeburger Cheeburger makes that decision easy for me. They offer the "Best of Both", which is a basket that is half fries and half onion rings. We ordered the small basket and it was more then enough for two grown adults. The onion rings had the same tempura like coating which was a nice change to the usual heavy breading onion rings around town. Fries with their skins on are bonus points for me. They use Idaho potatoes and cut them in to fries in house. Fresh, that's nice.   I went with the Classic Burger (1/3 lb.) and the BF choose the Semi-Serious (1/4 lb.) Burger. We both ordered the Honey Wheat bun and after seeing the Kaiser Roll being served to the table next to us, know we'll be ordering it the next time. Having Fried Pickles, Onion Rings and Fries, we tried to make a healthier choice selecting the Wheat Bun.   This time we held back and did not experience their milk shakes, but I will next time for sure. I will be having one. I love Snow Cones and Ice Cream that taste like Birthday Cake and that is one of their many flavors available. This visit we did enjoy our ice tea served in mason jars. Another bonus point for them was as I call it, "Rainbow of Sweetness". Not only do they have "real" sugar, but they have all three of the artificial sweeteners; pink, blue and my personal favorite, yellow.   Cheeburger Cheeburger like their name, is worth repeating and I will back.

Craft Beer and Pizza are a perfect pairing. Here at Firecracker you can mix and match pretty much to your hearts content. First off, you'll be blown away by the 66 different craft beers on draft. To compliment your beer, you can pair it up to 9 of their signature pizzas or create your own, which can be an endless variety.   What won me over is that they offer pizza by the slice. I love pizza and since I'm a single diner, I don't order pizza out that often. I either lose all control and devour the entire thing, or it goes to waste being too much food. So, when I find a place that allows me to just order a slice or two, I'm a happy pizza lover.   After seeing a friends posting on Facebook about Firecracker, I was tempted to give them a visit. So the next day, I stopped by for lunch.  For my craft beer choice was, Blood Orange Wit by Six Mile Bridge.  Being a fan of pepperoni pizza, I choose Pepperonis Monster.  Who wouldn't love a pizza topped in king-size pepperoni, red onion and mozzarella cheese. The crust was thin and crisp. I actually enjoyed the crispiness of the crust. I also, thought the house red sauce had a nice tang to it.   I had some beer left in my glass, so I had to have a second slice. This time I went with the bartenders favorite, No Sleep 'til Brooklyn. It was a very creative and tasty pizza served on their house white sauce. I would have never thought to put turkey pastrami on pizza. It was also topped with; sauerkraut, mozzarella and swiss cheese, thousand island dressing and toasted caraway. By all these toppings, can you guess what it taste like? Yep, it was just like a rueben pizza.   The ambiance is simple for a pizza joint. Bar to the left, open kitchen to the right and tables down the middle. Nothing fancy, just simple and relaxing. Kinda has a little hipster feel to it.  The service was carefree and friendly.   If you're a beer and pizza fan, I highly recommend you check Firecracker Pizza & Beer out. However, keep in mind it is located in The Grove, so parking is going to be a challenge aka a bitch. Go & have fun.   I'll be back? - Yes, they offer pizza by the slice.   When: July 25, 2018 Why: Lunch

Morning Glory Diner is a perfect addition to the eclectic collection of businesses on Cherokee street. It's intimate and has a little bit of a dive feeling. It's hours are limited to 7AM-3PM seven days a week, giving you the best two meals that a typical diner can offer; breakfast and lunch.   I stopped by on opening day and enjoyed simple breakfast. My main entree was their, Platter. It consisted of two eggs, choice of meat, Hash Browns and a side of toast. I choose to have my eggs scrambled, my meat was bacon and I passed on my toast. However, I'll let you know you can choose between wheat or white. I passed on the toast, because I enjoyed a half order of Biscuits and Gravy.   Nothing beats a diner breakfast. My eggs were fluffy, bacon was done to the point where it was just starting to get crisp and their Hash Browns may be my new favorite in STL. They were served extra crisp without being told. The best thing, they were crisp on top & bottom. Most places you only get them crispy on top, but not here. They do them right.   The Biscuits and Gravy would make a farmers wife proud. The biscuits are buttermilk and made in house. They them top them with a house made sausage gravy that if filled with large chunks of pork sausage. The gravy had the perfect amount of salt, I personally needed to add more black pepper, but for most I'm sure it would be just fine as they serve it.   The service is friendly and attentive. My coffee cup was never more then half full, they kept topping it off. I like how none of the dishes or flatware match. The eclectic mix adds to the charm of the diner.  Chances of Returning? - Gotta check out the lunch menu.   When: February 14, 2019 Why: Opening Day & I love breakfast from a diner.

Pure class. It was a class act all the way, from the service, to the ambiance and the presentation of food and cocktails. Definitely one of my favorite bars during my recent visit to New Orleans.   I stopped by The Bombay Club, shortly after Happy Hour had started. Their HH goes from 4-7 PM and the menu they offer would make anyone happy. As a light snack to hold me over till my dinner later that evening, I enjoy an order of Boudin Rangoons with Steen's Sweet n' Sour Sauce. $4 made it a great value. After enjoying them, I wanted a little more nosh, so I ordered the Pork Belly Tacos with Smoked Black Beans and Kimchi Slaw. Both were very good, but I favored the PBT's. Gotta love my pork belly.   The weather wasn't a typical hot and humid NOLA day, but my Pimm's Cup ($11) was cool and refreshing. Strong, too.  I have a favorite place for Pimm's back home in STL, but this one put it to shame. I wanted to stay and have a second, but when in NOLA for only three nights, I wanted to experience as much as I could, so it was off to the next adventure.    Great time. I'll be back on my return visit and most likely will be one of my first stops.   When: August 27, 2016 Why: Happy Hour

The Grove has been blessed with a new WC. The old fashioned building was razed and a new castle built in its place. This new WC is a palace compared to the old one. It has a slick ultra modern design and the flow inside and out is much more customer friendly.   I could have been overwhelmed with the new decor, but I think the customer service was even kicked up a notch. The staff was polite, friendly and attentive. They even hooked me  up with a Free-Quency Card. I buy 5 Combos and get one FREE. What a deal! I don't know about you, but I love it when I get something free that I'd be willing to pay for anyway.   My double cheeseburgers were and hot freshly made. The crinkle fries were perfectly salted and crisp. This #2 Combo is my go to and most likely will be the one I choose when I finally get my FREE one.   So glad this location is back up and running. I had a long love affair with the old one, but an update was long overdue. As was my updated review. I'm so glad I got to do it for the new, White Castle.  If you're a craver, go check out this new castle, it really is a palace.   I'll be back? - I'll come to this location before the one closer to my home.  When: March 7, 2017 Why: Saw it was open and wanted to try it. Wasn't even hungry.

A fantastic neighborhood bar. It's actually a well hidden gem. Babe's is located on Ivanhoe, across the street from Vinnie's and down the street from Pizza-A-Go-Go. Making this a popular area on Ivanhoe.   The reason I mentioned the nearby restaurants, is because Babe's has no food. However, you're welcome to enjoy a Gyro or a pizza from one of  these nearby venues.   The outside patio is spacious and comfortable. It's a great place to enjoy a cocktail or beer with friends. Especially now during this post-pandemic time.    The cocktails are cheaper than most popular bars and the cordial bartenders make them strong.  Which makes Babe's a perfect place for day drinking.   Will I return? - Yes. It's in my hood.   When: July 2, 2020 Why: Day Drinking in our Post-Pandemic World

Several of my friends love this place, but I'll be honest, I don't feel it. The only positive thing I can say is that the service is friendly and efficient. If it were not for the good service, I may have given them a one star review.   I've been here twice with good sized groups and each time I found the food to sub-par and flavorless. After the first visit, I was disappointed, but wanted to come back and try the lamb. I love lamb and was hoping an Ethiopian lamb dish would win me over.   My recent visit, I ordered the Yebege Alecha Wat. The menu described it as tender pieces of lamb. It wasn't. It was tough, chewy and some pieces had gristle attached. The description also said it was marinated with Ethiopian spiced butter and sautéed with ginger, garlic and turmeric. My lamb was served, soaking in a pool of the melted butter. The only spice I could taste was garlic and it was so heavy, I could not wait to get home and brush my teeth. This was the first time I have ever been disappointed in a lamb entree.   The injera, is a flat sourdough pancake and is an Ethiopian staple. It is served with every entree. In fact, you actually use it as an eating utensil. It makes eating with your hands fun, but I'm not a fan of the rubbery texture.  Sasha, commented in her review on being served silverware with an ant crawling on it. I too, was turned off by some of the cleanliness of the restaurant. The table signage were dirty and my chair and those next to me were sticky to the touch. They are in serious need of being wiped down.   I tried them twice and two strikes is an out for me at this restaurant.   I'll be back? - NO!  When: July 25, 2017 Why: UYE and wanted to try the lamb

On Fathers Day I was like an expecting mother. I had a craving for Fish - n -Chips all day. When craving FNC, the best place to go is The Scottish Arms. I swear they serve the best in the city. I worked Sunday so I quickly announced my craving when I arrived home.  Twisting arms was not necessary, the other half is also a fan of TSA's Fish - n - Chips. I changed costumes from work to casual dinning and off we went to the CWE.   We arrived shortly before the true dinner crowd and were seated in what they call, "the formal" dinning room. It's the room adjacent to the bar and all the tables have white linens. We requested a booth, but the hostess said not for 2. They reserve them for seating groups of four, due to their large size. She seated us at a nice deuce top  positioned in the front window. It was nice having the natural light, lighting our table.   Our server arrived quickly and informed us of many new things on the menu and asked for our drink order. Tonight we just wanted to  enjoy a good glass of ice tea. As he retrieved our beverages, we glanced over the menu and the new items were tempting, but we stuck with our original meal plan.   When he returned we ordered an appetizer of Prince Edward Isle Mussels in a White wine broth. I hate sharing mussels, but it is the right thing to do when dining with someone else. Then we both ordered the Fish - n- Chips.  It had a crispy Scottish Ale Batter and the North Atlantic Haddock was so moist and flaky.  It naturally came with fries, a portion large enough for two and as a bonus we enjoyed Sautéed Peas. The peas are worthy enough to make my Vegetable list here on Yelp.   I am not a fan of Tarter Sauce when I eat fried fish, or any kind of fish for that matter.  However, The Scottish Arms serves theirs with a Lemon Caper Sauce that has me asking for seconds.   The service was pleasant, it is always fun being waited on by someone in a Kilt.  At one point as the dining room filled up, he got slammed and was not able to get back to us with more ice tea and Malt Vinegar. Management stepped in, assisted and got things back on track. It is good to see management step in and help. It shows a good team work ethic.   I'll be going back soon, I want the lamb burger I saw on the menu . I need a new addition to my Steven Had a Little Lamb list.

I miss Off The Vine, but SOHA is a good  replacement  and addition to my neighborhood. It was sad that this space set empty for so many years, but it has been brought back to life with a non rowdy sports bar that offers an unbelievable amount of craft beers.   I've been here a couple of times now. We've popped in for a chilled beer and for lunch after running morning errands. The night we stopped in for beer, it had the feel of a neighborhood bar. As we enjoyed our cold one, conversation with the other patrons flowed as easily as the beer. We even ended up doing shots with our new friends.   Our next visit was all about the food. I heard from my hair stylist that the BLT was to die for and she was so right. Crown Candy Kitchen should come here for lunch and see what a "real" BLT should look and taste like. It may only be 8 oz., but it's the perfect amount and prepared the way bacon should be prepared for a BLT. The honey, mayo combo is what makes this one stand above all the other BLT's I have enjoyed.   I selected Mac N' Cheese as my side dish to accompany my sandwich. Knowing one of the managing partners is from the now shuttered Tin Can I was scared. I was not a fan of the MNC at TC, but this is not the same. SOHA tops their Mac N' Cheese with crumbled Nacho flavored Doritos making them very unique.  The SO ordered Fish N' Chips for his lunch. The fish was 8 oz. of beer battered Pollock fillets served with huge steak fries sprinkled with Parmesan cheese. If and I will order it myself, I will have them not sprinkle my flies. They were very flavorful, but I like my fries plain and simple. Especially when they are my french fry of choice, "Steak".   I'll end with what we started with, which was Chicken Wings. We ordered our wings Hot and liked that they bake them again after being tossed in the sauce. I can see us ordering these with some steak fries and picking them up for a quick lazy night dinner.

#curbside during the #pandemic   It was a rough day at work and it was getting ready to storm. Being an essential worker and going home to a K-9 who is fearful of storms, I needed a treat for "me". As I cruised down Hampton, the thought of wings and rings popped into my head. So, I made a quick turn into the parking lot for one of the best little dive bars in my hood.   I knew what I wanted, so I quickly pulled out my cell phone and called the number posted on their curbside promotional sign. A young lady cheerfully answered the phone. When ordering the wings, she asked if I wanted bone-in or boneless. For some reason, I always go bone-in. Boneless is just another name for nuggets. When I ordered my onion rings, she promptly asked if i wanted a full basket or a side order. What? She explained the difference in size and since it was just me, I took advantage of the side order. That was great customer service, because I would have wasted food not eating a complete basket.   These wings and rings both hit the spot. My wings were, Butter Garlic Parmesan. The order was 6 pieces, perfectly divided into 3 flats and 3 drums. I'm always impressed when a bar makes sure they are equal portions of the two. My  wings were crisp, juicy, meaty and full of garlic flavor.   For a dive bar, their rings are top-notch. No frozen rings from a bag here. They're Panko encrusted, seasoned and served with a remi sauce. Breading in house, makes a difference. For me, the rings had enough flavor, that I only dipped once in the sauce. Gotta love a crispy ring.   SOHA is organized well for #curbside service and is producing the same quality food that you receive inside. They're also offering growlers to-go.  Doing my best to keep our small businesses flourishing.   When: April 28, 2019 Why: #curbside #to-go

When I tell people I went to Wash U, it isn't as prestigious as it sounds. The Wash U I went to is a laundromat.   I have a washer and dryer at home, but there times when size does matter and you just need something bigger. Those larger capacity washers and dryers come in handy when you need to wash quilts, comforters or rugs.  Why put rough wear and tear on your own when you can use a commercial size down the street. In addition to 3 stars, I also give Wash U 3 C's for convenience, cleanliness  and cheap.   So the next time someone tells you they went to "Wash U", you can ask them do you mean the university or laundromat?

Welcome to the city Papa Murphy's! Papa John's will no longer be in my house. Or any other delivery pizza for that matter. I may have to get in my car and come to you, but your concept of Take - n - Bake is a winner. To have a gourmet pizza piping hot out of my own oven was a true treat.   We selected Papa's Favorite for our first experience with Papa M. It had red sauce, Pepperoni, Sausage, Ground Beef, Mushrooms, Mixed Onions, Green Peppers, Black Olives and Cheese. Major bonus, their cheese is not provel. All toppings and cheese were plentiful, they did not skimp on anything.  The pizza is made right in front of you on a cardboard type pan. They'll tell you to bake it on that pan. They then wrap in plastic wrap and send you home to bake at 425 degrees. You do remove the plastic wrap just like on a frozen pizza, but this one is fresh. Your house will smell like a pizza parlor as it bakes and the aroma will have you waiting with anticipation.   We also enjoyed one of their Italian Salads which was big enough for two. What I enjoyed most of the salad, it was Romaine lettuce. No cheap Iceberg lettuce for Papa Murphy. For dessert I grabbed one of their Chocolate Chip Cookie dough. I'll have to edit this review when I bake them, we were too full after our large pizza.   The staff was extremely friendly. I was totally impressed when my order was ready that instead of just handing to me over the counter, they walked around and handed my pizza and a bag with my salad, cookie dough and bottled sodas. For me that is good customer service, the removed that barrier and personalized the closing of the sale. They asked me to come back and to tell my friends friends. So I am telling you, "Papa's in the city". I'm going back and I encourage you to go too.

It's a QT, enough said. They're all pretty much the same.   This one has an amazing location. It's probably one of the most busiest corners in the city. Which can cause some craziness in the parking lot. Just be alert to when you are backing out of a space or pulling away from a pump.  Also, be alert to the fact that not all entrances, allow you to exit. For that simple reason, I'll put this QuikTrip in my Parking Lot Derby Collection.   The inside of this QT is kept clean, including the restrooms which is important during this pandemic. Their customer service staff is also very hospitable, making it a pleasant shopping experience.   Again, it's a gas station and convenience store rolled into one. It has the QT Kitchen which is a bonus. So, this QT beats most 7-11's and Circle K's by a long shot.   When: December 3, 2020 Why: Gas and liquid refreshment

The Hot Salami sandwich at Gioia's Deli truly is one of the best sandwiches in the city of St. Louis. It is sliced fresh to order, so you'll never see that pre-sliced salami like you do at those chain sandwich shops. Gioia's recommends the cheese garlic bread, but my favorite is wheat. I agree with their recommendation of cheese and that is Pepper Jack. It is absolutely the perfect cheese for Salami.   When it is time to garnish, that is when you truly can make the sandwich your own. I always top mine with jalapeños, pepperoncini, lettuce, onion and black olive. For condiments they offer 3 types of mayo and two mustards. I use on condiments on my deli sandwiches, but the staff will recommend and encourage you to use spicy mustard on the Hot Salami. Perhaps, I'll give it a try next time. I'm always up for a new food adventure.   They're primarily a Pepsi deli, but to offer a variety of other bottled and fountain drinks. They also have a selection of chips to accompany your sammie. I always choose the hometown favorite; Billy Goat Chips.   The staff is bubbly, friendly and always wearing a smile. If you are confused and don't know how to garnish, they'll guide you with popular choices and their personal favorites.   I'll definitely be back to Gioia's, there's no doubt about that. The only question is, "Will Steven ever order another sandwich besides the Hot Salami?" Only time will tell. It was one of his favorite sammies, before Ian Froeb said it was the "must order" on his STL 100 List.   When: May 2, 2016 Why: Lunch & STL 100

I agree with Chris Z , this location is FAST, efficient and unfriendly. I do not need them to be my new BFF, get me in and out as fast as possible.   I was prepared to wait like I normally do at the South Kingshighway location, but I was in and out in 5 minute. No need to have my iPad for entertainment.   Highly recommend for those who have no patience or are in a hurry.

I'm in the money, how lucky can I be. Who knew the boxes and bags of CD's stored in my basement would be worth $$. We've been cleaning, merging and purging so many things in our house. Selling possessions that are no longer prized. There are so many great consignment shops to sell household furnishings and clothes, but what do I do with all my old CD's?  In the world of iTune's and having the majority of our music on our iPod's or iPhone's the need of a CD has diminished. Driving by FYE., I noticed in their window they buy used CD's. Hot damn, I thought I gotta give them a try. I took up a small percentage of my collection and was energetically greeted by an employee when I told them I had some used CD's to sell.   After taking my personal information as a seller, the associate begun scanning the UPC bars on the back of my CD's. He neatly stacked them to two piles. The one to his right were ones they'd be interested in buying and to his left on the counter in front of me were the losers. As he picked up the next one to scan, in my mind I'd guess which pile it would end up. I surprised myself with how many I got wrong. I guess my taste in music has a good resale value.   I was thrilled with the amount of cash they offered me. If I wanted a store credit the $ value went up $16, but I wanted cash. Cool, hard cash. I still have one small box and a gift bag full of CD's and I will be returning to FYE tomorrow.

Sweet baby, Jilly! You exceeded my expectations.   After hearing so much about her cupcakes and seeing her tempting lunches on a TV commercial, we knew we had to stop by Monday. When you first walk in, of course the first thing you notice is the daily selection of cupcakes. I was excited to see they had an Egg Nog Cupcake. I love Egg Nog, so I knew that was the one I wanted.
