However, we had to have lunch first.  Our lunches get two thumbs up, I was amazed at the quality and quantity we received. We started out with the Famous Barr's French Onion Soup, a great start to any lunch. As our sandwiches we selected the Monte Cristo and The Cubano. They were plentiful, and better then some that I have seen at popular Tea Rooms.   As we feasted on our fabulous lunch, there was a steady stream of patrons coming in and getting cupcakes. My partner was facing the cupcake bar, and noticed when the last Egg Nog Cupcake was snatched up. He broke the news to me, I held myself together and did not cry like John Boehner. After all there was a Turtle Cheesecake and a Chocolate Orange waiting for us. The cupcakes were moist, rich, full of flavor and not overly sweet. They were just perfect.   The staff was fantastic. I kinda hate to use the word "darling", but that is the word that comes to mind when I think of the young lady who assisted us and explained our selections. I also, learned that if your doing lunch, tell them which cupcake you want and they'll set it aside. I never miss out on my first choice again.  My 50th Yelp Review - 12/14/2010

The best Italian restaurants are not always found in, The Hill neighborhood. Sometimes they're simply tucked away in a residential neighborhood, like Princeton Heights.   Onesto serves up some of the best, upscale pizza if not the best in STL. They have several specialty pizzas on the menu and usually have a nightly special. I've enjoyed the nightly special when it was a Lasagna Pizza and once I created my own with, Italian Sausage, Onion and Jalapeños. Their sauce is sweet and tangy and when it comes to the toppings, they apply them plentifully.   Their salads can be a meal themselves. The size is huge, if you're dining with a partner or friend, it's big enough to share. My personal favorite is the, Italian Chopped. I'll also give you a heads up about the deadly delicious Garlic Knots they serve complimentary. Eat and enjoy. These little knots of carbs are made from their pizza dough.   Onesto has a full bar, but I only get one alcoholic beverage when I dine here and that is their House Made Sangria. It doesn't matter what the flavor is, I know it is going to be refreshing and a perfect drink for my meal.   They have a fabulous patio that is dog friendly. The indoor dining room is causal, relaxing with friendly and attentive service.   I'll be back? - YES! I want to try a pasta dish.   When: July 8 and August 3, 2019 Why: Craving Pizza

I grew up in Alton and have fond memories of being downtown and smelling the fresh baked bread at the Colonial Bakery. Now the bakery is long gone and as an adult, I enjoy the smell of freshly brewed craft beer.   They offer so many different brews to choose from. My personal favorite is Gentle Giant, which is named after, Robert Pershing Wadlow who was, "The Gentle Giant" from Alton. Others that have pleased my beer palate are; Citrus Wheat, Yellow Beer and Magnum Pale Ale. I've even enjoyed a non-beer beverage from their fully stocked bar. They may not serve a Moscow Mule in a copper mug, but it is still a very refreshing cocktail.   As you drink your craft beers and or cocktails, you've got to munch on something and Old Bakery Beer has a variety of choices. If you love spicy, I highly recommend the Jalapeños stuffed with Cream Cheese. Or if you want something salty, go with the large plate of Tortilla Chips and Spicy Queso. You should also enjoy the Soft Pretzels with Mustard Dipping Sauce.  If you're really hungry and need a sandwich, their Cuban is one of the best.   I've been here to drink and for two different parties and the service has been outstanding each time. Old Bakery Beer is a shining star for the downtown Alton area and should not be missed the next time you are across the river.

When it comes to furniture, I am very picky and New Frontiers Home Furnishings meets and exceeds my expectations. Being constructed of solid hardwood is a must and 8-way hand-tied springs are at the top my demands. For me, buying furniture is an investment. When I buy, I buy quality so it last forever, or until my taste take a drastic change.   My taste in home furnishings are fairly traditional, with a slight lean towards country and NFHF fulfills them with a large selection. In addition to styles on display in the store, you can order from manufactures catalogs.   Keep in mind, many of the items and brands at NFHF are made to order and are not sitting in a warehouse waiting to be delivered. If you want quality, you need to be patient. Good things comes to those who wait.   The Sales Professionals here are down-home friendly, no high pressure selling like you get at most furniture stores where the sales people work on straight commission. They listen to your likes, request, price range and guide you to the best selections available in house or via special order.   Delivery is not free, there is a minor fee, but it is worth the price.  The men who have done all my deliveries have been courteous and respectful of my home. This last time when my McKenzie Queen Size Storage Bed needed assembly, they took extreme care with my new investment and its surroundings.   If you are looking for quality furniture, make the drive across the river to Alton and shop New Frontiers Home Furnishings. When you're done, stop by Fast Eddies for a good cold beer.

TSA is quickly becoming one of my favorite places to go.   Warning to "Pork" themed restaurants, The Scottish Arms has a Pork Burger that is the "bomb". It is full of flavor and when paired with an ice cold draft beer (Whale from Six Row Brewing Co.) it makes a refreshing summer meal. Enjoying it on the Scottish Arms patio makes it perfect.   In addition to the Pork Burger we enjoyed their classic Fish -n - Chips.  I dare anyone to find and introduce me better F-n-C's, here in STL, then those served at TSA. I'll be surprised if you do.   The service here always amazes me, it is top notch. Their staff is always friendly and very accommodating. To give you an example, the night we were there a young lady on the patio was chilled. It was one of those recent cool nights we just experienced. To make her comfortable, the server gave her an extra table cloth to wrap around herself like a shawl.  That is a step beyond the norm.

For those of you who are out there searching for the best diner burger in STL, at all the local greasy spoons and dives. Stop it right now. You'll never find it at any of those places. The best  diner burger in STL is right here at, The Libertine in Clayton. Yes, an upscale restaurant in chic and fashionable Clayton is serving up the absolute best diner burger I have ever had.   It not only is the best diner burger, it is a double diner burger which makes it twice as delicious. The two grilled patties are covered in white cheddar cheese whiz, served with daily pickles and placed on a made from scratch "bacon" bun. Eat with caution. It will be slippery with all the cheese, but it's so well worth the messy fingers. You wont fell guilty about licking them in public.   It is served with crispy frites, that has its' own little cup of ketchup. Whenever a restaurant serves its' ketchup in individual cups, it puts a smile on my face. At some point in my life, I started to despise the ketchup bottle in public. So now, I prefer to see my ketchup in small individual cups along side my fries. For me, it makes for an more enjoyable and pleasant dining experience.   The Libertine, also has one of the best Happy Hours Tuesday-Friday. It's runs from 4-6:30 PM and draws a pretty fine looking crowd. They have special drinks at the bar and offer a special menu of munchies as well.   I've had numerous cocktails here and each one has been masterfully prepared. Sometimes they scare me during the preparations, especially when they pull a blow torch out to add a finishing touch. Here's an abbreviated list of some of my cocktails; Millionaire Cocktail, Old Fashioned, Amateur Physician, Moscow Mule, Kerouac's Idea of Moderation and Manhattan.  They've all been great, but my favorite is the classic, "Old Fashioned". They also, made me an excellent Manhattan.   When: It's a monthly thing Why: Cocktails and Diner Burger (Ian Froeb's STL 100)

Nice! The ambiance is simple and rustic. Making for a very comfortable atmosphere to relax and enjoy craft brews from Bluewood and some of their guest taps.   The bartenders of course are very knowledgeable on the beers on tap. If you're not sure what you'll like, tell them what your preferences are and they'll guide you. Today I didn't take advantage of their flights, but they do offer them. So many of our local breweries don't offer flights, so I'm happy to see Bluewood is on board with offering them. It's a great way to experience multiple brews, to find out which one is your new favorite.   A BIG plus for BB is having Mac's Local Eats sharing their space. The combination of the two makes for a fun filled experience. Beer and Burgers, what more could you want.   I'll be back? - Hell, YES!  When: September 18, 2019 Why: Grand Opening with Mac's Local Eats

I am a fan of Old Bakery Beer. I love supporting a local business that gives back to their community and that is what OBB does. On the third Monday of every month OBB sponsors, Drink For A Cause. Between 4 and 9 PM 25% of their beer sales are donated to a local charity. So go have a beer to support a local brewery and you'll also be helping a local charity.   I've never been disappointed with any of the food at Old Bakery, but I'll tell you my favorite is the Caesar Salad with White Anchovy's. The salad is huge and has the perfect combination of Parmesan and croutons. I always add anchovy's and they are not stingy with those salty little fishies. They also toss the salad with just the right amount of dressing.   Staff is hipster, which is perfect for a craft brewery.   Will I go back? - Gotta support local charities.   When: Multiple times Why: Supporting local charity or meeting up with family.

I have never been to, Alton Sports Tap. However,  I've had food delivered to my work through To-Go Delivery. If their food is good when delivered through a delivery service, I can only imagine how good it would be if I were sitting at their bar.   When I was searching the restaurants available thru To-Go, I saw that Alton Sports Tap, boosted about having the best chicken wings in Madison County. That got my attention, so I ordered. I ordered my mild and they were definitely spicy enough for my taste buds. Best in Madison County? Not sure, but they were damn good. Hopefully next time I have an order, I'll be sitting at the bar in AST with a side fries and a cold beer, too. I like that my order was split in half with 5 flats and 5 drummmies. It' one of my pet peeves when the flats and dummies aren't the same number.   In addition to the wings, I ordered a Deluxe 1/3 lb. Angus burger. Being deluxe, means it came with lettuce, onion and tomato. My burger was cooked to my choice of medium rare. Again, for delivery I was impressed with the tastiness of the burger.   For food delivery, it was A-Ok. I'll order again and hope to dine at AST soon. Hopefully, when I dine at AST I'll be able to bump them up to 4 Stars.   I'll be back? - Sure, more delivery for sure.   When: April 30, 2019 Why: Lunch Delivery

Raising Cane's Chicken Fingers, is a fast food restaurant that specializes in chicken fingers. The entire menu is nothing but chicken fingers and that is okay, because they do them right. Sometimes it is good to keep your focus and do what you do best, instead of trying to please and accommodate all.   From this point forward in my review, I have to refer to the fingers as tenders. I just can't call them fingers, because when I say chicken fingers I think of the actual chicken claw and lose my appetite. RC's tenders are large in size and the breading is just enough to give a crispy coating to the hot and moist white chicken meat. These tenders will put any other fast food chain tenders to shame. They can even put the tenders served at some pubs to shame.  A perfect lunch for me is the 3 Chicken Finger Box. You enjoy three meaty pieces of chicken tenders, Cain Sauce, crispy crinkle fries, a slice of Texas toast and a regular soda. I am not a dipper of tenders, so I can not speak to the Cain Sauce. However, I can tell you that the seasoning of RC's tenders satisfies my taste buds, as an non-dipper.   One thing that I do dip is my fries, especially crinkle fries. I love how the ketchup clings to the crinkles of the fry, when you can dip it in to a little cup of ketchup. RC's does not give you packets of ketchup, they have little paper cups that you can fill with Heinz ketchup. It may not be a secret sauce, but it works for my crispy fries.   I think it is so cool that the restaurant is named after their dog and being a dog lover I'd love to give RCCF 4 Stars, but it is a fast food restaurant. This is when Yelp really needs to give us those 1/2 stars. A-OK is a "good" rating and I am glad that I now have a RCCF closer to home.  I do have those days when a simple 3 Chicken Finger Box makes for a good quick lunch.   When: November 19, 2015 Why: Lunch

The Wagamama is an amazing gift shop for a dog or cat lover. The best way to describe this shop is with a clip from their website - The Wagamama, a Japanese word basically meaning spoiled rotten child sums up the vision of our brand; a pet obsessed boutique where animals are loved and spoiled.  I first discovered them on Facebook and knew immediately, that I had to shop this pet boutique. The moment I walked in, I was hooked. They had some of the most unique breed specific and generic gifts that I had not seen at other pet boutiques in the STL area. Best of all, they had special tags letting you know which items were "locally made" and there were a lot.   Being a dog dad, I always get frustrated that there are so many items available for, "dog mom's". I was pleased to see many, "dog dad" items here and a couple of them ended up leaving the shop with me. I was also pleased to see my breed of choice, Shelties to have several items available as well. Yes, those items left with me as well.   If you've got a dog or cat lover on your Christmas list and haven't found their gift yet, you need to shop here. My cousin is a black Lab mommy and I found the perfect item to round out her holiday gift.   It was a delight chatting with the young lady working. I feel bad that I'm confused on her name - I think it was, Christina or Christine. I'll find out when I return and I'll be sure to remember it. She was very helpful and made it a point to be sure I saw all the Sheltie items.   As I shopped another lady came in with her fur-babies, so being a pet boutique your babies can come shopping with you. I told her I'd be back, with my two fur balls in tow to try on the variety of Christmas scarfs and collars.   I'll be back? - I'm a dog daddy who spoils his doggies, so, YES!  When: December 13, 2019 Why: It's a local pet boutique

Father forgive me, for I have shopped at the Catholic Supply store and liked it.  No forgiveness need, I seriously think it is a cool store. You'd be surprised at what you will find.   Any one who is selling their house, shopping here is a must. You've heard the myth, that burying Saint Joseph in your front yard upside down expedites the sale.  It's no myth, it has worked for me every time.  My first time I was a little embarrassed going in and asking for the Saint you bury to sell your home.  However, the staff is use to that question and put me at ease. They have miniatures boxed up with the instructions on how to make Joseph work his magic.  He has helped me sell four houses, so I am a believer.   I also buy my Christmas/Holiday cards here. They have the best selection I have seen. Of course, I am cheap and buy at the post holiday sale for the next year. Their selection of sympathy cards are more true to heart then Hallmark and American Greetings.   If you have a preschooler, check out their story time at 10:00 AM with Georgy on Wednesday. It is a great activity for mommy and child.

I am so proud of, The Grove. I use to bartend in the area before it was actually called, "The Grove". Yes, I am that old. Back in those days, there were a lot of boarded up building between the bars that were open and setting the trend for the future.   Now, it is thriving STL community that supports many popular restaurants, breweries, coffee shops and alternative nightclubs. What makes me proudest, is that the residential community is growing as well. The Grove, is a thriving STL neighborhood that is growing by leaps and bounds.   I hope they keep up the development. I smile every time I drive through or visit one of the businesses. It is a neighborhood, that shows the diversity and love of each other in St. Louis, that sometimes gets over-looked.

Woot-Woot! I've become a regular at this Target in my new neighborhood and I'm loving it.   It may not have as large of a collection of things in some departments as the stores in STL, but I am still fulfilling my needs. I was surprisingly surprised when I found all the accessories I needed for redoing the bathrooms in my new home. The colors of the towels offered, were a perfect match to my paint. I will also admit, I have purchased several items from their Magnolia department. I guess I am watching to much HGTV.   What surprises me the most about myself, is I am shopping the grocery area more then I did in STL. It is so easy to just pick-up some items here and there instead of having to stop at the grocery store, too. The quality is pretty much the same and also not much difference in price.   I've said it before and I'll repeat myself, the customer service here is pretty damn, good. The sales associates on the floor are very helpful and the cashiers are quick and friendly.   Glad to bump them up to a well deserved 5 Stars.   When: January 14, 17, 27, 30 and February 26, 2021 Why: Supplies of Life

It was inauguration day and I needed comfort food. Nothing brings me more comfort, then a Double Diner Burger at The Libertine with their amazing Frites. At least that is what I thought, until I saw Chicken Two Ways on their menu. I may have a new vice, it brought the comfort I needed.    I started my evening out with an Old Fashioned and a order of Poutine (Happy Hour menu). It's a smaller portion of their famous Seared Foie Gras Poutine. My knees go weak, frites covered in beef marrow gravy, sweet peas and garlic cheese curds. This was the perfect lead in to my night of comfort food.   I came this evening with all intentions of ordering their popular Double Diner Burger, but as stated in my opening I got sidetracked by a new item on the menu. Chicken Two Ways, is a half chicken that is fried & roasted. They serve up a wing, thigh and drumstick fried with a crispy buttermilk coating. The breast is boneless and roasted. The buttermilk grits and spicy greens, took this the Southern inspired entree to another level. I'm typically not a grits man, but these had me scraping every last morsel. The spicy greens, put those specialty southern restaurants to shame. It's great being a foodie and enjoying great food like this.   I already blew my diet to hell, so why stop now. I continued the night of comfort eating with an order of Bread Pudding. I ate it all, but seriously it could be shared by two. So, on your next date night at The Libertine, I highly recommend ending the night with a serving of their Bread Pudding.   Service is always top-notch, cocktails (Old Fashioned, Manhattan and The Liberal) are masterfully made and if your lucky, you'll get to chat with Nick himself.    Will I return? Yes, I always return to places I give 5 Stars.   When: January 20, 2017 Why: Inauguration Day

I need a support group. A support group for shopaholics who are addicted to Crate and Barrel. I shop here at least once a month, when I come to get my haircut at James Mitchell. As I browse through the store, I can easily find something I cannot live without. Or at least I think, I cannot live without it.  Either way, I love this store.   I am a kitchen gadget junkie and I can always find some new gizmo here. Another thing that I like at C&B is their selection of dinnerware and stemware. It is so vast, I can find the perfect items for entertaining at home, or a gift for any occasion.   When shopping for new furniture, I usually start here, too. It's high quality and soundly constructed.   Shopping at Crate and Barrel makes me happy. Can't believe I hadn't updated my review in the last 8 years. Well, I got that corrected today.   I'll be back? - I addicted.   When: April 3, 2019 Why: It's a monthly thing.

Can I have a drum roll, please. I have reached another milestone on Yelp. My 5 Star review of Juniper, (A Southern Table & Bar) is my 1000th review. I could not be prouder, to have this amazing restaurant that is ranked 14 on Ian Froeb's STL 100 List, as my 1000th. I've eaten and drank here numerous times, without a review. So it is now time, to sing their praises.   I've enjoyed a meal at one of the tables, but my favorite place to sit by far is at the bar. I enjoy watching the bartender mix and serve the handcrafted cocktails. So many times, I have caught myself saying, "That looks good, I'll have that next." I've enjoyed; Hollywood & Vine, Keep The Change and a Moscow Mule. However, my favorites are two true classic cocktails; a Manhattan and Old Fashioned. You can call me "old fashioned", but I am still a fan of the good ole classic cocktails.  You may scratch your head and wonder way you should pay for a Breadbasket, but once you order it, you'll understand. All I will tell you, is be sure to order the Angel Biscuits and Hush Puppies in your mix. The biscuits will be light and fluffy as the clouds from which angels perch and your in a Southern restaurant so ordering Hush Puppies is just common sense.   Next let's discuss those small plates for sharing. If the Pork Ribs with Sea Island Red Peas are available, go for it. Again common sense will come into play when ordering; Fried Green Tomatoes or Fried Pickles. If you are lucky enough and both are on the menu at the same time, don't try to decide which one to get - get both. My last visit, they said it was going to be another week or two before they had local green tomatoes. I can't wait, but I will. In the meantime, I scarfed down some amazing Fried Pickles. I enjoyed the light dusting of seasoned breading barely covering the pickle, so the green color of the pickle showed through.  Another great Small Plate for sharing or keeping all to yourself is the Deviled Eggs. Sit me at the bar, with a Old Fashioned and a plate of these Deviled Eggs and I'd be in heaven. For me, that would be perfect "Happy Hour".   Entrees here are referred to as the, "Main Attraction" and every time I come I get the same damn thing. When I enter the restaurant, I swear I am going to try something new, but when I order, "Fried Chicken" comes out of my mouth. One of these days, I am going to surprise myself and say, "Fried Catfish". Any way, the chicken is crispy, juicy and definitely southern comfort food. The chicken comes with mashed potatoes & gravy and a vegetable. I've had green beans and asparagus. Both were good, but for my farm boy roots, the green beans was the best match up. They also, change the gravy from time to time. I've had a traditional brown gravy and once I had a spicy red tinted one that gave a nice twist.   It is sad to say and I am also embarrassed to admit, I've never had a dessert at Juniper. By the time the evening & meal are coming to a close, I am overly stuffed and do not have room for another bite. I think in the future I need to not have a small plate, so I can finally have something sweet to write about.   I have always found the service here to be appropriate for a Southern Table & Bar - it is down home, Southern Hospitality. When packing up your to-go vessel which is eco-friendly, they write the date and Juniper on the box, too.   When: Numerous - most recently, June 28, 2016 Why: Comfort Food

I popped into Pop, before meeting friends down the street. We were having dinner in the next block and I arrived early as usual and needed a drink and thought a nice bubbly would do. This was right before, we all were told to stay home and off the streets during this pandemic. Damn, it. I want this Covid-19 over, so I can return to Pop and experience more.  As a child, I thought Deviled Eggs were disgusting. I didn't even like the hard boiled eggs, the Easter Bunny brought. Now that I am an adult, I love'm. If I see them on a menu, I've got to have'm. So it was a no brainer to order them as an accompaniment to my Seelbach.  The spicy mustard, in these little devils, gave them a little extra twist and kick.   The reason I enjoy a Seelbach, is that it is like a mash-up of a Manhattan (my favorite cocktail) and a Champagne cocktail. When you combine those two, it definitely is a winner. Pop uses, Old Forester 100, Cointreau, bitters and of course "bubbles" aka champagne, to make this a very refreshing cocktail.   Being a single diner/drinker, I have a couple of "hot buttons" that I always look for and enjoy when seated at the bar. 1 - A simple hook under the bar. It's nice to have for hanging a light weight jacket or for the ladies to safely secure their purse. 2 - Linen Napkins. I just prefer them over paper. I hope this pandemic doesn't make us all switch over to paper napkins when dinning out.   Pop, I'll be popping back in as soon as this Covid-19 has passed. I'm looking forward to some more bubbles and experience more of your innovative menu.   When: March 7, 2020 Why: Bubbles before dinner.

Bubbles and Burgers, what a delightful combination.   Once restaurants got to open up with patio sitting, I was ready for bubbles. POP had a coupon in the EXP, so I had some redeeming to do before they all expired. I enjoyed a nice glass of Brut on their back patio, it was very relaxing and refreshing to finally be out and a bout.   Normally I like a beer with a burger, but having the glass of bubbly was a nice twist. When you think burgers, POP may not pop into your mind, but it should. Their Smash Burger is damn good. It's two patties that is topped with roasted onions, liquid cheddar and pickles. The bun is a sesame challah and it comes with a side of fries. I've always been a fan of serving ketchup in a little cup and was glad to see them serving theirs that way. Honestly, I don't know if that is the regular way, or it it's the new pandemic way. Either way, it makes me happy.   The customer service was attentive and it was obvious they were following CDC protocols to keep everyone safe.   When: August 13, 2020 Why: EXP Coupon

Riverside Diner is a well kept secret in the Patch neighborhood of STL and it has got to stop. It is well hidden in an industrial park area of The Path neighborhood. When you go for your first time, you'll tell yourself there is no way a diner could be in this hood. Then at the last minute, you'll find it and you'll still be confused.   When you enter, you'll notice it is stark and simple in ambiance. It simply is tables and a few booths. You'll seat yourself and one of the servers will deliver you a  menu and ask if you want coffee. It's a diner, so there's no Bloody Mary's or Mimosas. However, the coffee is good and strong and the servers keep your cup full.   I've been to RD twice, on my first visit I enjoyed the Boneless Pork Chop Breakfast. This was truly a comfort breakfast. I was expecting one chop, but I got two thick chops. They were fried with a thick crisp coating and the inside was juicy and tender. I love pepper and these chops were seasoned with the perfect amount of pepper.   The chops also came with two eggs any style, I choose scrambled. To make it a true comfort breakfast, it also came with an order of Hash Browns and a Biscuit with a side dish of Milk Gravy. This took me back to my days growing up on the farm. It was a hearty breakfast, that lasted me the entire day.   My second visit, I took advantage of the Daily Special. It consisted of two eggs (again I went with scrambled), House Fries, Sausage Patties and One Biscuit with their house made Milk Gravy.   Riverside Diner, is a true classic diner with good food and service.  I'll be back? - I'd be a fool not too. Want to try lunch.   When: Feb. 7 and May 31, 2019 Why: Breakfast

I am so old, I remember this place as J P Drive-In. When I'd visit my cousin, we'd ride bikes over for a treat. So I thought it was time, to visit King Louie's. Living in STL, the King just isn't on my radar. However, I was on this side of the river to attend a party in Wood River and took the opportunity to swing by for a quick burger and Root Beer. I knew I'd be eating later, but I couldn't resist giving KL a try while I was in WR.   So I swung by the King and ordered a simple cheese burger and  small Root Beer. Their version of a burger with everything is; mustard, onion and pickles. I'm now a mustard person, but it actually was good. I liked the blend of diced white onions, dill pickles and the mustard. I'm a ketchup fan and I didn't even add it to mine.   The house made Root Beer, did not impress me and I am a big Root Beer fan. Locally, I think the Root Beer at Mini Corral Hamburgers in Alton is far superior. I found their RB to be bland and having very little flavor.   Will I return? Yes, I want another burger and I want to try the potato planks - their version of French Fries.   When: August 10, 20117 Why: A trip down memory lane

I've got to be honest, I really do not like the new location and layout. I've been holding back on doing a review since they moved, but after my last shopping experience I gotta comment.   I was shopping for a 16x16 pillow insert which, I thought would have been included in, bed or beyond in their inventory. They had no inserts of any size. How is someone supposed to change their decorative pillows cases, if they don't have the insert which is the foundation?  Just walking through the store, many shelves were sparse in inventory and the merchandising wasn't as sharp and clean as it use to be. The biggest thing I noticed was the lack of staffing. Usually I could find an associate every few aisles, but today I only saw one or two on the sales floor. Even my cashier was lacking skills. She did not engage conversation by asking me if I found everything I was looking for.   I may not have found my pillow, but I did get a box of K-Cups for my coffee machine on sale and that is always a win. I also, added a goodie to my Halloween decorations and my Thanksgiving as well. So my shopping excursion wasn't a total loss.   I'm hopping the current state of disarray is from the pandemic and not the decline of BBB.   When: September 17, 2021 Why: Need a pillow insert

Even with COVID going on, when it's National Fried Chicken Sandwich Day, you've got to venture out and get the full experience. For me, it was the first time I enjoyed the "famous" Popeye's sandwich and I will tell you now, it will not be the last.   The drive-thru line at this Popeye's, blows my mind. It is always super long. I visited today during peak lunch time and there were 10 cars ahead of me. Having no patience, I noticed the inside was open. I quickly parked and went inside. Once I got inside and read the menu board, I saw a banner across the sandwich photo. It said, "Be back Soon!". I thought to myself, oh, hell no.   Instead of just walking out, I waited for my turn to order. When I asked if they were really out of them, the young lady behind the counter laughed and said,  "no, our sign lies." I immediately ordered a spicy combo with cajun fries and a diet soda for balance.   OMG! Everyone is right, these sammie was amazing. It was a huge, thick piece of chicken breast with a crispy coating and juicy meat inside. I'm a spicy type guy and this one had just enough heat from the breading and special sauce.   The young lady who was working the counter was very professional and had a great customer service skills. I wish I knew her name, because she deserves a personal a shout out for a job well done.   COVID Report - Customers required to wear mask, employees wearing mask, social distancing inside and limited number of guest inside.   Will I return? - They won me over.   When: November 9, 2020 Why: National Fried Chicken Sandwich Day

As soon as I entered, I knew I had found a good Mexican restaurant. The dining room was filled with numerous tables of Latino blue collared men, chowing down for their lunch break. If it was good enough for them, I knew it would be a winner for me.   If it weren't for Taqueria Durango being on Ian Froeb's STL 100, I would have never discovered this place. I'm glad I decided to eat my way through his list and experience new places. It truly is an inconspicuous little restaurant tucked away in a small strip center of stores. Even using my GPS, I missed it and had to backtrack.   They offer a basket of complimentary chips and three salsas in squeeze bottles. They also, provide you with two small bowls, but I just squeezed directly on to the chips. Like Nicole, I don't remember which was the spiciest, but I think it was the darker red one, because that is the one I liked the most.   One regular sized Margarita was big enough to enjoy throughout my entire meal. It wasn't anything special, it was a typical mix. However, for the price, it was the perfect beverage for my Mexican lunch.   For my entree, I went with Ian Froeb's "must order" recommendation; Torta Ahogada. It's a pork sandwich totally smothered in red-chile sauce. It was more bread then I anticipated, but I just pulled the top off and made it an open faced sandwich towards the end. The pork was tender and the red-chili sauce had just enough fire & kick to it.   I'll definitely be back to try the tacos.   When: September 27, 2016 Why: Lunch & Ian Froeb's STL 100

I'm going to let you in on a "dirty" little secret. The "dirty" chicken wings at SOHA are phenomenal. The wings themselves are huge, meaty and juicy. They have just enough, spicy kick, to be the perfect accompaniment to a cold beer.  These wings are so incredibly good, I am placing them in the #1 spot on my Wings, Wings and more Wings  list.   SOHA with it's amazing wings, enormous variety of beers and multiple TV's, is the perfect place to watch your favorite sports games. Or, you can just stop by for a cold icy beer and an appetizer before going home after a hard day at work.

When looking for a tree, where should you go? A Forest, of course and we went to Sherwood Forest. They have a certified Arborist on staff who can assist you in picking the perfect tree for yard.   Working with a small space, we knew we would need to focus on dwarf trees. The two we selected were a Walkingstick and a Crimson Queen Japanese Maple.  For 60% of the retail price they will plant your new tree for you and give you a two year warranty.  If you plant it yourself, it is only a 1 year warranty.   Our Walkingstick was so tall we had to have them deliver it,  so why not have them plant it too. Their truck was so cool. It has a robot arm that lifts your tree off the truck, extends itself and lowers it to its' new home. It was so cool to watch and it made their job so much easier.  We could of done the Crimson Queen ourselves, but had them do it as well.   They do have other greenhouses, but our focus was trees and we are happy customers. I just wish I could have a tree big enough for a tree-house.

When you move from a 990 square foot house to a 2100 square foot house, you need a lot of new furniture. To fill all of this extra space, it was a no-brainer for me to come back to NFHF. Especially now, since I had moved to the Alton area, it was a logical choice. I'll be honest, I did shop some of the local chains, but they could not match the quality and prices I found here at NFHF.   When I moved to Godfrey, I gained a great room, formal dining room, breakfast nook and a second bedroom. So you can see why I needed lots of furniture. The entire staff knew me by the time I was done with all my selections. I'd get dimensions and go home to measure, making sure it would fit. Then I'd take pictures to text to friends and family, to help  when I could not decide between two items. All the staff was so patient and helpful with me. I could not have asked for any better customer service.   Here's a breakdown on what I purchased:   Dinning Room - A bar cabinet and Sideboard Great Room - Sofa, Coffee Table and Comfy Chair Breakfast Nook - Drop-leaf Table and Two Chairs My Bedroom - Nightstand to Match my Bedroom Set I bought 10 years ago.  Second Bedroom - Wood & Iron Bed-frame - Queen Size Front Porch - Unfinished Chair to paint orange   Having a larger bedroom in the master suite, I was excited to see that they still offered the same set that I purchased 10 years ago. I was able to finally purchase the nightstand. It was a wise move to select a traditional style that stays in fashion in home furnishings.   All my guest who have visited my new home, love my new Bar Cabinet. They all comment how unique and different it is from the regular bars you see at other major retailers. What has blown most of my guest away the most is the upholstered items I purchased. My friends and family from the Alton area had no idea, that NFHF had upholstered items, they just knew them for their quality wood furniture. One of them has gone in and purchased a sofa for themselves.   My personal favorite items that I purchased are the drop-leaf table and chairs for the breakfast nook and the chair I bought for the front porch.  I love relaxing in my breakfast nook and the orange chair on the front porch, is a great eye-catcher for people to find my new home.   If you are in need of quality solid wood furniture or some upholstered items, I recommend checking this place out. New Frontier Home Furnishings has made my new house a home.

I can munch on snacks and sip 4 oz samplings of beer all afternoon or night at Bridge Tap House. It's a great way to experience a wide variety of craft beers locally and from all across the country.  My go to snack is the Tortilla Chips with an IPA Cheddar dip. The chips are actually better then some of the local Mexican restaurants. Until Ian Froeb recommended the Smoked Paprika and Sea Salt popcorn on his STL 100 List, I would have never tried it. I never imagined bar popcorn would taste this good. I should have know better, since it is a David Bailey establishment. I'm not sure want is the perfect accompaniment, the popcorn or the craft beer. Either way, they both go together extremely well.   Will I return? Just try to stop me and see what happens.   When: September 11, 2016 Why: Craft Beer Sampling & STL 100 List

Wing Stop's catch phrase is, "The Wing Experts". I don't think so. They were not "bad", I've just had better. In fact I've had better from a pizza joint or a pub and I was hoping for better.  The fries, were limp and tasted as if they were prepared in old oil. Another big disappointment, after reading Shelly D's glowing review.   My co-workers get carry-out frequently from here, so I'll re-visit too in hopes of a better experience. Perhaps they were just having an off night.

I have been a customer of the Mungenast car family for twenty years. When I lived in St. Louis, I was a three time buyer at their St. Louis Honda. Now that I live in Godfrey, I've switched to their Toyota dealership. I've always been a CRV driver, so flipping over to a RAV4 was easy.   Once I moved to the small town of Godfrey in Illinois, my 13 year old CRV was ready to be replaced. Being in a new town, I wanted to support a business in my new community and with the Toyota dealership being owned by Mungenast, the decision was easy.   I knew what I wanted. I had researched the web, shopped the lot and other dealership lots before I went into Alton Toyota to make my purchase. When I arrived, I met with Amber my sales professional. She listened to my wants and most importantly my needs. She showed me the RAV4's that they had on the lot and I test drove a hybrid and a regular RAV4. The hybrid was amazing, but with only a 3 mile drive to work, i choose to go with the regular.   I liked the features on the one they had, but I was obsessed with the color, Lunar Rock. So obsessed that I wanted my new RAV4 to be that color. At this point, Amber went the extra mile and researched other dealerships and found me what I wanted. I had to wait an extra 10 days so they could get it transferred to Alton, but I got what I wanted and in the color I wanted.   On the day I picked up my new SUV, Amber had patience while she taught me all about the electronics and features my new ride had. Once she was done teaching this old dog new tricks about his ride, I met with the finance manager. We completed all my paperwork and what impressed me the most, is Alton Toyota is totally full service. They are set up to issue new license plates. When I bought cars in Missouri, I had to go to the DVM to pay my sales tax and to have my new plates issued. Mungenast did it all and made my life easier.   When: November 27, 2020 Why: New Ride

The IHOP in my neighborhood closed after 50 years and we kind of miss them for a cheap breakfast. I wish they'd tear down the old building and build us a new one like this location. The inside is more modern, but still very compact and tight. They make use of every inch, but doing so puts the tables close together. It also makes the table tops small and crowded once your food arrives.   However, IHOP serves up a good cheap breakfast. Their Breakfast Sampler gives you everything you'd want for your morning meal. You'll enjoy two of everything; eggs your way, bacon, sausage, ham, pancakes and a hearty side of hash browns.  It's almost too much food, I always bring some bacon and sausage home for the dogs.   I like my Hash Browns extra crispy and today when ordering I forgot to mention my quirky request. When they arrived, to my delight they were perfect. Crispy on top and crispy on the bottom too.  So many diners serve them crispy on top and mushy on bottom, but not here. Your HB's will crispy top and bottom with moist flavorful taters inside.   This location is extremely clean and the staff was attentive and personable. When we are craving our IHOP fix, this location is close enough to make us happy.

Riviera Maya is the second closest Mexican restaurant to my new home and I like it a little bit better then the one that is closest. You know, when that urge for a taco kicks in, you gotta fulfill that craving fast.   Besides tacos, the one thing I judge a Mexican restaurant on is their, Margaritas. Here at Riviera, I recommend taking the plunge and ordering the Top Shelf. Some restaurants, there is very little difference, but here I can definitely taste and feel the buzz difference. If you're a two Margarita type drinker, I'd say start with a Top and then step back to a regular. I myself, usually go jumbo and just have one.   They offer complimentary chips and salsa, but the menu alerts you that refills are $1.75. Dining alone, I never need a refill, so I do not know if that is truly a fact.   I do know, that when I munch on chips that I need something besides, just salsa. I've ordered both their, White Queso Dip and Bandito Dip. I favor the Bandito dip. I like the blend of Mexican Pork Sausage and cheese dip. Dining alone, I don't get trouble for dipping a chip in my Bandito then the salsa. When you eat alone, double dipping is permissible.   Off their taco menu, I favor the Big Tacos. They're simple tacos topped with just lettuce and shredded cheese. You get three tacos and they allow you to mix the hard & soft. I'm kinda crazy, I like my hard (crunchy) tacos to be ground beef and my soft tacos have got to always be pulled chicken.  This entree is perfect on a Taco Tuesday.   However, my usual go to entree when dining in a Mexican restaurant is a Chicken Quesadilla. The one here does not disappoint me. It's the perfect size, especially after noshing on the chips and Bandito dip.   The service is friendly and attentive. My visits have been during the COVID pandemic and they've been following the CDC guidelines. Tables are spaced further apart then regular and all staff wear mask. Most importantly, they do a very good wipe down of tables in-between guest.   When: October 13, 2020 and February 10, 2021 Why: Taco Tuesday and Needing a Margarita

I was gifted Pottery Barn gift cards during my birth month of November of over $100. I was eager to spend  them, since I also became an G-Uncle during the same month. I wanted to spoil the new little boy addition to our family.   I made two complete circles walking through the entire store and actually embarrassed for the staff. I have never seen a store so disorganized, cluttered and dirty. I know it was during the holiday season and they were most likely under staffed, but there is no excuse acceptable for how bad this store looked. I've refrained myself from posting pictures.   Not one sales associate acknowledged my presence in the store. Also,  you could hear the frustration in the voice of one associate who was on the phone explaining to a customer why they didn't have an item in stock and most likely would not be getting it before the holiday. I felt sorry for that associate, because without hearing the other end of the conversation, you could tell in was a Karen.   I  spent 25 years of my professional career in retail and the majority of it was in high end retail. So my I will give this store another chance, but for now they'll be added to my No-No Collection until they improve.

Decorating on a budget? Then BB&B will help you save BIG $'s and give you the look you want.   I recently, completely redecorated my entire living room. Only two pieces from the original room were allowed to stay, everything else was tossed out to the ally or given to charity. Once I had all the new upholstered furniture delivered, the original linen drapes with red stripes from Restoration Hardware no longer coordinated with the room. Not a problem, I'll just move them to another room and go get new ones at RH.   Do you have any idea how much solid brown silk panels cost at RH? It has been almost 9 years since I bought my last drapes and I totally passed out when I saw the prices. When the handsome paramedic brought me back to consciousness,  he whispered in my ear, "Go shop at Bed, Bath and Beyond, you'll save money."   Okay the paramedic may be a fantasy, but the savings at BB&B are real. I found similar drapes to the ones I loved at RH. The only major differences were; one was silk the other was polyester and one was $250 per panel and the other was $49 per panel.  It was the look I wanted, the fabric really didn't have to be "real" silk.   The real savings came when we checked out and the cashier let me use multiple coupons. I had three 20% off one item coupons and one $5 off purchase coupon.  Hot damn, I saved BIG $'s and the windows in my newly decorated living room are stunning.

I've always been a fan of OBB and I am even more so now that I live less than five miles away. Living so close makes it easy to swing by to fill my growler to grab a variety of 4/6 packs of cans. Why buy it from a third party, when you can get it directly from the brewery.   For me, OBB is also a great place to go for lunch on my days off. For example on St. Patrick's Day, I got to enjoy, Corned Beef and Cabbage for only $10. It was delicious, but I was so tempted to order the Burger of the Week. It was a half-pound steak burger with jalapeño cheese sauce and onion straws. I thought to myself, St. Patty's is a once a year thing, that steak burger will be offered again.   I also, enjoy their daily specials. I'll share them with you, so you too can enjoy them.  Monday - Fill 64 oz Growler for $10 Tuesday - Double Cheeseburger with Fries $7 Wednesday - Boneless Chicken Wings $9  Thursday - 14" Pizza $14 or $20 with a pitcher or 4 Pack Friday - Fish n Chips (Fries and Hush Puppies) $12 Saturday - Fried Chicken Sandwich - $10 Sunday - Vegan Special   So as you can see, they've something for everyone.   When I moved from STL, I did it with 4 cousins and after we were done in record time, I brought my crew here for dinner. We had a fun time celebrating my move. We enjoyed a lot of booze, appetizers and a variety of entrees.   The crew here is always friendly and during the pandemic they have offered curbside to-go, patio seating and now are able to offer inside dining with social distancing.   Hope I don't develop a little beer belly, now that I live close to a brewery.   When: Numerous Visit - Oct 23, 2020 was my moving celebration Why: Supporting a local brewery

Odd place to celebrate St Patrick's Day, but that is what I did. I enjoyed a Blarney Zone. My calzone was stuffed with; pastrami, corned beef, smoked gouda, swiss, white wine herb onions. The "sauce on the side" was Horseradish Ranch.   The calzone as always is enough for two, but it was St. Patrick's Day, so I ate it all by myself. I enjoyed the mix of pastrami and corned beef. Having the corned beef in the mix, I felt as if I were still celebrating with the Irish. The smoked gouda and onions, put an extra zing to the zone. My "sauce on the side" was a little runny, being a horseradish ranch I would have expected a thicker and more clinging sauce.   The ordering at the counter is fast and easy peasy. Once your food is ready, the speedy runners bring it out to you. So there is no need to listen for your number or name being called out. They find you by the little marker they give you when you place your order. Again, it is so easy peasy, all you have to do is enjoy your Calzone.   As always, the staff is friendly and polite. So polite, that I want to compliment their mom's for raising their children well and I'm putting them on my Sensational Service list.

Could there be a better place to celebrate, National Double Cheeseburger Day? Perhaps, but I choose here for the nostalgia of the drive-in and the fact that I haven't been here since moving back to IL.   When I arrived, the car-hop was busy bringing out to-go orders. She did acknowledge me with a wave and ran back inside. I was kinda looking forward to having the tray with my burger and fries attached to my window, like the good ole days. However, it dawned on me my car will be a year old in November and I still have not eaten food in it.  About that same time, I noticed a sign on the dining room door saying it was open. When the carhop/server returned, I told her to make things easier for her, I'd go inside and eat.   Once inside, I am glad I made that call. Picking up a paper menu, I was able to see other offerings that were not on the board outside. Being a jalapeño junkie, I was immediately sold when I saw the Lion Tamer. It's a smashed burger topped with fresh jalapeños, two onion rings, spicy mayo, pepper jack cheese, lettuce and tomato. Actually, I had them hold the tomato for me.   This burger was perfect for my celebration. It had my jalapeños, my favorite cheese and a spicy mayo. The two big onion rings were a bonus. To accompany this delicious burger I added a side of fries. To my surprise, they were cut with skins on and fried crisp. Gotta love a fry that has slight crunch to the bite.   Oh, before I forget, they make their own Root Beer. It is so refreshing. It's way better then any mass produced you get out of a typical soda fountain.   They had a limited staff, but it is a small business and they were hustling as fast as they could. Even while they were hustling, the service was friendly and professional.   King Louie is a short drive for me, but for a quality smash burger, it is well worth the drive.   When: September 15, 2021 Why: National Double Cheeseburger Day
So long, farewell, auf wiedersehn, goodbye.   I loved Borders much more then Barnes & Nobel. Who am I to judge, I am just a Yelper in St. Louis.

This review is one of the times that I wish Yelp had 1/2 stars. My experience was truly a A-OK+ visit. I'm sure after another visit or two I could easily be a fan. The food we had was great, what held the score back was the service. The service was just a little slow.   How we ended up at Molly's was a surprise to us both. We were driving around wanting some place new and being in Soulard - there was hardly a place we hadn't tried, so Molly's is where we ended up.   We ordered multiple appetizers to create a meal for two. As you will see, we went with a seafood theme. We started out with Tuna Summer Roll and Crab Cake. The Tuna Summer Roll was better then some I have experienced at a Sushi bar. The Crab Cake was moist and flavorful, not like one you'd get in Maryland, but good.   We also tried their BBQ Shrimp & Green Fried Tomatoes, as you can see it doesn't photograph well and the taste was similar. This dish did not impress us, Broadway Oyster Bar does something similar so much better.  The last two items I'll mention were the best by far. Molly offers, Alligator Rangoon, something I have never heard of before. I have eaten Alligator and love Crab Rangoon - so why not give it a try. It was very unique and I look forward to having it again. We also tried Baked Macaroni & Cheese which was the bomb. This m&c could be a favorite of mine easily.   Look forward to revisiting and see if I can't bump them up to a 4.

Kingside Diner is not your typical diner. It is an upscale diner, that serves delicious comfort food for both breakfast and lunch on the edge of downtown Clayton. It has a full service bar and they make one killer Spicy Bloody Mary that is always a go to for me.   On my first visit I intended to order their, Slinger after seeing chef Eric preparing on TV. Come on, The Slinger is a St Louis classic breakfast, why wouldn't I give it a try? Then as I sat at the bar, I saw the pictures posted of their Damn Delicious and thought I'd give it a try. The server also shared with me that the DD was chef Eric's favorite.   As I got ready to order, my attention went in another direction. I saw another picture posted here on Yelp of the Veggie Hash. I love Brussels Sprouts, so I was sold. I enjoyed a full plate of fresh, crisp sprouts covered with two eggs over easy. Delicious! I couldn't be totally healthy, I had to add a side of bacon and Hash Browns.   My next visit I choose, Damn Delicious. The DD is very filling, it is a lot of food. They take two scrambled eggs with bacon and put it between a sliced croissant. They then smother that with sausage gravy, shredded cheddar and chives. If that isn't enough, it is served with a side of Hash Browns. I was so stuffed, I skipped lunch that day.   I'll share a little secret with you, I prefer the Clayton location over the CWE. The service here is more personal and friendly. Veronica is a delight, excellent server. I also think the food is prepared and presented better.  Note - the address is on Bonhomme Ave, but you actually enter the restaurant on Brentwood.   I'll be back? - Yes! Gotta try that Slinger  When: June 6 & 13, 2019 Why: Breakfast

I gotta admit, I only shop here with their coupons. If you don't have a coupon the prices are not that much different then any where else.  Today we went and got a digital scale for the kitchen, it is time for holiday baking.  We researched on line before shopping and were pleased they had the one we wanted in stock. We also needed a bread spatula, no luck with that item.  Normally when I shop here the staff is average to below average at best, but today they were above average. They were friendly, out-going and actually helpful. We chuckled as we observed, it looked as if they had gone to "The Grove" and recruited their holiday staff. Which was a good thing, for their customer service.

I'm loving my new hometown Target. The layout is a lot different from my old big city Target, but I'm adjusting to the flow. The staff here is also more down to earth and friendly. Just walking through the store, whenever I pass an associate, they all speak and ask if I am finding everything I am looking for or need. It is obvious, the management here is focused on customer service and has trained their staff well.   As others have commented, this store is always clean and well organized. Having just moved into a new house, I am making numerous runs to this Target. I am amazed at the things I didn't need in my old house, I now need in my new house.   Best of all, they have a spot where you can take a selfie with the Target Dog. My big city store didn't have that. Small town Targets, rock.   When: Very Often  Why: New home owner, I need stuff.

Don't get wrong, I am still a fan of Peacemaker, but I need to remove a star from my rating. I'm confident they'll earn it back fairly soon.   My two visits in November of 2017 were not stellar. Both times sitting at the bar, the service was lacking. They either need to put a second bartender on duty to expedite service. Or, they need to sign the male bartender they have up on match.com. Better yet, get him a date. He was more interested in working the single ladies then serving up cocktails.   Another reason for the removal of a star was the preparation of one of my favorites here, the Mussels. The night in question, they did not have the same flavor I am use to and enjoy. It was off and left an after taste. I only ate four and left the remaining in the bucket. Luckily I had started the night with Fried Green Tomatoes which are always a winner.   My other go to's did not disappoint me in November and that is the Clams and while their Chips are a delicious side, I always upgrade to the fries. I can also, never go wrong with an order of Hush Puppies. They're always a tasty accompaniment to my Manhattan.   If you have room for dessert, the Soft Serve with a Magic Chocolate Shell will take you back to your childhood and make you smile.   Will I return? - They gotta get their Star back  When: November 8 & 24, 2017 Why: Seafood

Do you like your cookies soft and moist or dry and crunchy? If you like them like I do, soft and moist, you'll enjoy Insomnia Cookies. They are hot, fresh, chewy  and they have cold milk too.   You may ask, it they're made the way I like them, then why only 3 Stars? It is because of the unfriendly staff who are more concerned about conversing amongst themselves then providing top notch customer service. Another reason for only 3 Stars, is the offering of ice cream. They boosted that they had Prairie Farms ice cream, as if it were a gourmet ice cream. Don't get me wrong, I like PF. I was raised on a dairy farm and we use to sell our milk to PF. It's local, which is great, but I can get PF at my local grocery store. Give me something like Blue Bell that is unique to ST Louis.   Good cookies, poor customer service, but your sweet tooth will be satisfied.

PAGG is a pizza parlor that serves pizza and only pizza. They do one thing and they do it right. The only other thing on their menu is soda. Majority of their customers do what I do and that is carryout. They do not offer delivery and table sitting is limited. Which makes it a true neighborhood pizza joint.   They only offer two sizes Small which is 12" and Large 15" and their prices are lower then the major pizza chains. What is weird is their hours, they are open 4-9PM Sunday - Thursday and 4-10PM Friday and Saturday. Then of all days they are closed on Wednesday. Guess they like having hump day off.   Their dough is hand tossed so while waiting for your order you will always be treated to a show. Love how they give the pizza a nice crisp bottom. We like the Special which gives us; sausage, pepperoni, mushroom, green pepper & onion.   PAGG can not be compared to Good Pie, Dewey's or PI. They are in a different class of pizzas parlors. In my hood PAGG is the better choice over Domino's, Cecil's and Papa John's.

Where shall I begin, do you want to hear about the white cheese dip, the Mountain Dew type Margarita or the hair in my food. Got your attention didn't I.   Let me say, they did a great save on the hair. They did not challenge me, (it was threes longer then anyone near our table) they apologized, took the entree off our bill and gave me a complimentary Margarita.   Now the food, it is fast cheap Mexican food. I doubt if their chips are made in house, they appear to have come out of a bag and just warmed up. Their salsa is spicy and most folks would give it a thumbs up, but for me there was too much onion and cilantro in it.   When I crave Queso, I do not just want a bowl of melted white cheese. I want cheese preferably yellow with some pizazz and kick to it.   Our entrees were okay, one of us ordered the beef enchiladas and I ordered the chicken enchiladas. The beef were by far the best of the two, the beef was tender and seasoned well. My chicken was a tad on the dry side, but seasoned well.   Now, let me close with my Margarita review. When my first one arrived, I giggled and commented how it looked like a glass of Mountain Dew. I sipped, gulped and finished it fairly quickly. I really couldn't taste any liquor at all. Ordered a second and it was pretty much the same as the first one, left me asking where's the booze.   Then the free Margarita arrived and this one I could taste the booze! Perhaps it had always been there, because when I got home it was NAP time and I slept like a baby.   El Paisano is near home so I most likely will give me another try, when I crave Mexican and do not want to venture far.

Attention Hotel Guest Next Door: St Louis may be in the name of this restaurant, but it is not a good representation of true St Louis BBQ. I highly recommend that you get in your car and drive to one of the many other BBQ restaurants in the area.   The best thing we had was the Cucumber Salad and that was a side dish. In fact, it is what saved them from getting a single star. Fresh cucumber, tomatoes and white onion in a vinegar & oil dressing was a perfect summer salad.  We started out with two orders of Chicken Wings; Dry Rubbed and Sweet & Spicy.  The wings were small in size. The Dry Rub was the best of the two. The S&S was really neither, it was bland & mushy.   My Half Rack of St Louis Style ribs were very dried out. I cannot say for fact, but to me they seemed like they were left over from the previous day. I am so use to fall off the bone meat at other BBQ restaurants, here I had to chew and chew to get the meat off the bone. My dining partner ordered the Brisket and she too was not impressed with the tenderness or flavor.  The other two sides we had to accompany or meat were; Baked Beans and Green Beans. A can of Bush's beans would have been better then what we were served. The Green Beans did not look nor have the texture of a fresh green bean.   I've saved the biggest negative for my closing. While dining at our table, we had to wave away tiny fruit flies that kept flying around our booth.   Sad to say, I doubt I will ever go back and I've got a new addition to my Terrible Two's List.  When: May 18, 2016 Why: Dinner @ New BBQ in town

Okay this place is winning me over, I tried it again and my second pizza was pretty damn good. I ordered a sausage and pepperoni and the sausage pieces were big and meaty. The sausage was  excellent, but I wasn't  wild about their pepperoni, so next time it will be sausage and onion.  I can already assume that one will be a winner. Also, the sauce and cheese impressed me more this time then on my first visit.   I've gotten so use to St Louis thin crust, that I'm enjoying having the crust around the edge when I order from Pizza-A-Go-Go. I know my dogs enjoy the crispy crust, they think it's a special treat made just for them.   Keep in mind if you visit this parlor, that it is bare bones. If offers pizza and soda and that  completes the menu. I guess you can bring your own beer or wine in because I saw a table with bottles of Budweiser while I waited for my carryout.

I do not Vape, but I enjoy hot sauce. If it were not for an article in RiverFront Times, I would have never known about this delightful little store. It is two retail shops in one location. One catering to those who vape and the other for those of us who love their food/spices "HOT".   I'll never shop for my "hot sauces" at the grocery store again. The variety of spice and intensity of heat here at Saucy-One are good enough to keep my burn'n love a burn'n. In fact I may need to keep some extra Tums or Alka-Seltzer Heartburn Relief Chews on hand.  Not only do I have a love for a variety of hot sauces, but my family does too. So discovering Saucy-One at the holiday season was perfect. Several of my gift boxes, are being filled out with goodies from their shelves.   The sales associate working (forgot name) was friendly and very knowledgeable of the product. Pointed out his favorites and shared secrets on how he used them (recipes).   Will I return? - I'm always in need of hot sauce.   When: November 30, 2017 Why: Shopping Local

I've been to two other Pi locations; Delmar and Central West End. I always use to say, the Delmar location was my favorite, now that I've given this Kirkwood location a try, I'm torn on which would be my favorite.  I stopped by for a quick lunch after running errands in Kirkwood. My plan for a quick lunch, quickly became a leisurely lunch. Sitting at the bar was so relaxing, I had the new issue of Feast Magazine and a locally craft beer. In addition to the beer, I started my lunch with an order of their Blazed Wings. What I love about their wings , is that they are dry rubbed, oven baked and served with seasoned carrots instead of the typical celery sticks. Normally, I do not dip my wings in ranch or bleu cheese dressings. However, Pi serves up yogurt cucumber dressing, it was cool and refreshing. I liked it.   I kinda created my own pizza, I took the Grove 2.0 and replaced the salami with spicy sausage. The jalapeños, mozzarella cheese, oregano and spicy red sauce, were perfect accompaniments to my selection of spicy sausage. Being a native of STL, I am a fan of thin crust. Pi's thin crust is super thin and crisp. Allowing the true flavors of the toppings shine through.  In addition to me sitting at the bar, the bartender was also taking care of several tables and the service was still very attentive. He always, made sure that all my needs and request were fulfilled.   Will I return? Yes, good pizza, wings and craft beer always get me to come back.   When: September 25, 2017 Why: Lunch

I love a good cup of coffee and believe it or not, White Castle serves up a good cup of java. Ever since I bought my Keurig coffee machine, I have commented that I wish WC would sell their blend in K-Cups. My wish has come true and it seems everyone else had the same wish. It took me three visits to different White Castle restaurants before I found one who wasn't sold out.   The Kirkwood location has a huge glass display case of all the retail items White Castle offers and I was so excited to see a box of K-Cups being featured. When I requested a box for my very own, the cashier responded, "I hope we have some in back." I heart sank when she returned empty handed, but I quickly had a smile on my face when she walked around the counter and said, "Let me see if this is a full box or just a display." Sure enough, it was factory sealed and full of K-Cups and she sold it to me.   The Kirkwood restaurant may now be missing their display of a hot new item, but they demonstrated good customer service. When I need another box, I will be sure to come back to this location.

Great old school, mom and pop watch and clock repair shop. Best place to get your watch battery replaced. While we wait, browse the antique clocks for sale and the large variety of cuckoo clocks.   Service is fast, efficient and they know what they are doing. I'd bring my watch here for a new battery, before I'd ever trust one of those young kids working the watch kiosk at the mall.

I should have my taco card taken away from me, for not knowing about Chava's. How have I not known or experienced Chava in the six years they have been open? I do not know, but I do know now that Chava may be my favorite Mexican restaurant now.  We were in Lafayette Square and Soulard doing some "local" holiday shopping and needed lunch. I recently saw a review for CMR, so I knew I wanted to give them a try. I thought we were going to experience a "new" place,  but found out it was just "new" to us.   As we entered, we were greeted by a cheerful hostess who escorted us to our table on the main level of the restaurant. Once we were seated, our server promptly approached us and closely behind him was a young man with chips and salsa. We ordered House Gold Margaritas while we glanced over the menu selecting our lunch.   Being a first visit, I needed more time to read the menu so I ordered Cheese Nachos with Seasoned Ground Beef as an appetizer to buy me more time. These were the best Nachos I have ever had. I loved their presentation, it made for easy and neat eating. Instead of piling up chips and dumping on toppings, Chava neatly tops each individual chip making them a very flavorful and enjoyable finger food. Sour Cream and Jalapeño Peppers were served in the center of the platter for you to add.   We ordered our entrees, the SO being a master of Tamales ordered their Tamale Plate to see how they compared with his and I requested the Fajita Tacos.  Both came with the typical Mexican sides of beans and rice. I was impressed with both. Usually I think most Mexican joints over cook their rice, but not here. Their rice was more of a dirty rice and would be an excellent side to many different entrees.   I knew the Tamales were good when the SO took his first bite. His eyes seriously rolled back into his head. Growing up in Houston and living part-time in Mexico, the SO knows how to make a Tamale. He shared a bite with me and they were amazing. You could tell they were made by hand. When the server asked how they were, they shared a giggle in Spanish. The SO was telling him, that they were almost as good as his.   My Soft Shell Fajita Tacos were bigger then most tacos served at many of the popular Mexican restaurants. I enjoyed one each, Grilled Chicken Breast and Seasoned Sirloin Steak. Next time I will have both of them be the Sirloin, it satisfied my red meat crazing.   They serve their Margarita's in a tall glass not the "traditional" Margarita glass, which was fine with me. If the booze is there, I could careless about the glass.   I will be a regular here soon, in fact the Duke or Duchess may want to watch their back or lose their title.

I've been to, The Capital Grille for Happy Hour. I enjoy ordering off their bar menu and sipping, a Stoli Doli or an, In Fashion. So when the summer edition of Clayton Restaurant Week rolled around, I went for dinner.   I couldn't change my typical game by too much, I still sat at the bar. My first cocktail was my favorite, In Fashion and to make my CRW experience bigger, I started out with their Cast Iron Garlic Shrimp from the bar menu. I got 5 huge shrimp, that actually would be a light meal with a glass of white wine. However, I prepared myself for this big night of eating by not eating all day. I was ready for a feast.   When it was time to begin my CRW meal, I begun with the Wedge Salad. It was just okay, I should have gone with the Caesar. It could of had more Blue Cheese dressing and smoked bacon.   My main entree was a 8 oz Filet Mignon. It was delicious. It was so tender and seasoned perfectly to bring out the true flavors of the filet. I requested medium rare, but it came out more medium. They offered to re-do it, but I declined. It tasted so good, I didn't care. At this point I needed my second cocktail, a Stoli Doli. It's one of their signature and most popular cocktails. Once you have one, you'll understand.   For my side I got my daily green vegetable in, French Beans with Heirloom Tomatoes. The green beans were prepared to a perfect crispness and the tomatoes were blistered and a nice accompaniment.   Dessert followed a great meal. It was a rich and creamy cheesecake with a variety of fresh berries. It was just the perfect size, so did not fret over the calories.  As always, the service is top notch and professional. The staff is friendly and they create a neighborhood bar feel in an upscale atmosphere. I highly recommend for you to try TCG. If budget is an issue, treat yourself during CRW. You'll be glad that you did.   I'll be back? - Yes. I can make a meal out of the bar menu.   When: July 16, 2018 Why: Clayton Restaurant Week - Summer 2018

Gather around, I got a review to share about a new restaurant in Kirkwood. It's early, but I think this is going to be a place to be seen. It is a great place for ladies who lunch, closing the big business deal, meeting friends for happy hour and a simple dinner. The ambiance is simple, stark and clean. A minimalist would love the decor.   Being a fan of chicken wings, I could not resist ordering their signature dish, Sweet Buffalo Wings. The menu states they are cooked to perfection and indeed they were. They were huge, meaty and juicy. Each drummie and wingette had grill marks that not only added to their presentation, but the flavor as well. I will be enjoying these again, during a Happy Hour with friends.   My lunch entree was another Signature Dish, the MexiCali Cobb Salad. When it arrived, I was surprised at the size, it was much larger then I expected. It was served on a large square plate and piled high with the Creamy Avocado Dressing on the side. The Romain lettuce was covered in Herb Roasted Chicken, Roasted Corn Salsa, Tomatoes, Applewood Smoked Bacon, Cheddar Cheese and Spicy Tortilla Strips.  I had them hold the Spicy Strips out to save carbs. Just reading those toppings, I am sure you can tell how my taste buds were doing a happy dance.   My lunch friend started with another one of their signature dishes, Smoke House Gumbo. He wanted to experience the Gumbo by itself so he asked that the cornbread be served on the side, instead of the Gumbo on top of it. This Gumbo is made in the true traditional New Orleans style. It was filled with Smoked Andouille Sausage, that gave it a good spicy kick.   His lunch entree was the Big Blue Burger. It was an 8 oz. burger topped with lettuce, tomato, Applewood Smoked Bacon, Blue Cheese Dressing and served on Brioche Bun. The burger had great seasoning and presentation with all the toppings, but unfortunately they overcooked his medium rare. The waitress noticed it herself and commented on it and asked if he wanted it sent back. He said, no that it was okay.  The Brioche Bun did not hold well and made it difficult to pick up the burger for a hearty bite. When you want a burger, the last thing you want to do is eat it with a fork.   The manager soon stopped by our table to inform us that he had removed the burger from our bill. What? We told him he didn't have to do that, that it was okay. He said, no that he wanted us happy. We went back and forth a couple times, then we finally gave in. That is the first time I have had a discussion with a manager to put something back on bill. This was quality customer service.   Before going I saw a quote from one of the owners, Mark Winfield on their website. It simply said, "You will walk into Winfield's as a customer, you will leave as a friend and part of our family" He speaks the truth, this is a down-home sports bar. I can not with to come back.

Yummy Yummy Yummy, I've got Gooey Butter Cake in my tummy.  Like another reviewer, I live fairly close to Gooey Louie and drove by frequently. My waist line regrets that I finally stopped by.....lol. This is little bakery is fantastic - it offers the best gooey butter cakes in the city that is know for Gooey Butter Cakes.  I've taken these to work, family functions and just home for us and everyone loves them. They are moist and bursting with flavor. The original is best by far, followed closely by Chocolate Raspberry and Chocolate Chippewa.  When craving Gooey Butter Cake, go to Gooey Louie for the best.

Best Happy Hour when you are wanting an Mexican theme. The Top Shelf Margaritas are one of the best if not the best in the city, we buy them by the pitcher...lol. Their chips and regular salsa are a great compliment to the Margaritas. (I'm glad you can get them at your local grocer) I sneak off to the bar and get cups of the other two salsa they have available as a bonus. My favorite entree is the Wet Burrito it rocks with flavor.  I hope they re-cycle the little cups the salsa come in.

I enjoy shopping, dinning and going to a movie here at Plaza Frontenac. Typically I'm not a mall shopper, but I love the selection of stores here.  I basically shop the home stores, Bissinger's, Louis Vuitton and enjoy a cocktail or two at Cardwell's.  I have shopped here in bummy jeans and unshaven and have gotten the same quality type of service when I am dressed to the nines.

OH, DADDY! OH, DADDY! I am so glad I finally stopped and gave you a try. You may cheesecake in your name, but you are so much more then a cheesecake shop.  We're both off on Monday, so it is our day to run errands and have lunch out. I have had MDC bookmarked for awhile and thought it was time to mark it off my list. When we arrived, we were amazed at the vast menu for lunch and the large selection of cheesecakes. Close to two dozen different flavors of cheesecake, how can a fat boy choose?   For lunch I had the Daddy's Combo which includes 1/2 a sandwich, and your choice of salad or cup of soup. I picked a cup of chili and Roast Beef on Wheatberry as my sandwich. My sandwich was very good, I liked the cut of roast beef and was blown away by Daddy's wasabi horseradish mayo dressing. Close friends know that I do not like mayo, so for me to say that is a big deal. The cup of chili was so good that when Brad tried it, he had to go order himself a cup.   Brad ordered the Tuscany Trio, which was an excellent choice. A flavorful blend of ham, salami, provolone cheese, tomato, lettuce and onion. Then it's highlighted with herb mustard and lemon pesto mayo on focaccia bread.  The sandwich is huge, two diners could share it easily. He took chips as his side, which were Kettle type chips. No bad, but it would have been nice to have hometown Billy Goat.   When ordering lunch, they do a great add-on telling you can have a slice of cheesecake for $1 off as dessert. What a deal. After we finished our lunch, we were so full we had to take our cheesecake home as a treat while watching TV that night.   The two slices we choose were Berry Swirl and Dulce de Leche. Both were very good and if I had to compare them to The CC Factory, Daddy would win.   I look forward to going back and experiencing their breakfast menu. Also, I picked up a menu so we can do takeout in the future.

Tucker's by far is the best steak value in the city. A 10 oz. Sirloin, side salad and a baked potato for $13.85 is a bargain to me. Add the Yelp check-in free appetizer to your meal and you've got a full belly.   My steak is always seasoned well and cooked to my request temperature. The side salad my primarily be iceberg lettuce, but with the red onion, bacon bits and their Lemon Pepper house dressing it is a perfect lead in to my juicy steak. Then there is the huge baked potato that I can never finish. It's a baked potato, but it's so good. I take the other half home and make my own American Fries for breakfast.   The friendly service and relaxed atmosphere makes for an enjoyable steak dinner.
