I was eating here, long before it appeared on Ian Froeb's STL 100 List for 2016. If I had my own list, TTKAB would have been somewhere in the top 25. I've done a couple of brunches when my work schedule permits and I've also enjoyed a few dinners and Happy Hours at the bar. Each one of them was delectable.   Ian says, the Duck Poutine is a must order. I've never been a fan of duck, so I cannot speak to the excellence of that dish. My must order would be the; Asparagus, Nueske's Ham and Egg. You can't go wrong with one of favorite vegetable's, local farm ham and a fried egg. If you're here for Brunch, you gotta order the Lemon Ricotta Donuts. I love donuts holes and these simply are the best holes, I've had. They're fried donut holes tossed in cinnamon sugar and served with a Blueberry Compote and Lemon Curd  for dipping. The holes are; big, soft, fluffy and not overly sweet for being tossed in sugar.   I've had a few cocktails here and they were all expertly hand crafted. They get major kudos for offering different sized ice for the appropriate cocktail. Adult beverages I have enjoyed are as follows; Dorothy Gale, Old Fashioned and Manhattan. For brunch, I have downed several, Bloody Mary's, Mimosa's and Sunrise Shrub. During dinner once, I enjoyed an entire bottle of Cloudline Pinot Noir and then had to order a single glass as well. (Someone was sharing the bottle with me.)  My brunch tasting have been; a Chef's Special which was an amazing Benedict, an Egg White Omelette and Chicken & Waffle. Having lost weight, I found all three were health portions. A brunch entree and sharing an order of donut holes was quite filling.   My favorite way to go for dinner when dining with a close friend is "sharing". I'm not a fan of sushi, but I highly recommend that you and your BFF share an order of Surf & Turf Sushi Roll.  It's; Tuna, Flame Kissed Tenderloin, Tempura Asparagus, Avocado and Truffle Micro Greens. I am blown away every time I share it. Since we've got the sharing thing going on, I'd recommend doing anyone of the Tasting Boards. My personal favorite is the; The Seafood Trio. You'll be served up individual servings large enough for two to share bites of; Sesame Seared Ahi, All'Amatriciana Salmon  and Sizzling Soy Mahi Mahi. So good and so healthy.   Items that have disappeared from the menu, but found my love are their Brussels Sprouts and Mac-n-Cheese. I've enjoyed both of them as a side and as a dish at the bar with a cocktail. Hopefully they'll make a return or at least a guest appearance on the menu in the future.    I agree with Brian R., a dinner at The Tavern is not complete without dessert. I know Jeni's is just across the street, but the Chocolate Chip Cookie here is heaven. When someone tells you, you are half baked, it kind of is an insult. However, this half baked cookie topped with house made ice cream and peanut butter mousse has my sweet tooth singing its' praises.   The service is always friendly, relaxed and knowledgeable. That is exactly what I'd expect of an upscale restaurant that is worthy of 5 Stars from me. My only negative and it isn't bad enough to remove a star is - the dish towel napkin. That is a phase that I wish would go away, in the more upscale restaurants.   When: Multiple Visits  Why: Brunch, Happy Hour and Dinner

A couple of weeks ago when they did a teaser commercial for upcoming news, saying Qdoba closing 6 Saint Louis locations, my tummy did not flip flops. I immediately prayed to the taco and burrito gods asking them to please save my local Qdoba. I don't eat there often, but I like having it in my hood when the craving arises within me.   As the news anchor started to read the list off, I kept my fingers crossed. When she was done, I had a sigh of relief and wiped the sweat from brow. The city locations had survived the closings, the shuttered stores were all on the east side of the river and out in the county. In celebration of the good news, we decided it was a Qdoba night for dinner.   Neither of us were really hungry, so we just ordered some Queso and Guacamole. We had salsa at home and cold Mexican beer  to round out the snack. The two bags of chips were huge and more then enough for both us to enjoy with some left over for the lunch sack the next day. The chips at Qdoba are a little salty, but I like their lightness and crispness. The Queso is always good and their guacamole can beat some of the local cheap eat in Mexican restaurants.   The staff here as many fast food places is like a revolving door. It is constantly changing, but each time they are friendly and efficient in preparing our order. Even thought it was all new faces, I told them I was glad they survived the closings. I had an anniversary reward to redeem on my Qdoba card so our snack dinner was only $3.  What a deal!

I will admit, I was skeptical when I heard KK was moving into this delightful small space. I had never experienced their food truck, but reading their menu I just scratched my head. Now that I have eaten here twice, I am thankful they are in my hood.   Both times that I have been in the staff has been extremely energized and eager to assist. My first visit they encouraged me to try the Spring Rolls with Cucumber and Mango and one of the featured Steamed Buns. I'm usually not a fan of Spring Rolls, but their combination of cucumber & mango won me over, with a Ginger Sauce.   My second visit, soon as I entered, they welcomed me back. Christina, quickly grabbed a menu and said, we've added a few things to the menu since your last visit. I was amazed, that she remembered me and what I had. That is detailed customer service. She first pointed out the new Baby Romain Salad, I was sold immediately when I saw it had White Anchovy and House Miso Dressing. This was a Sensational Salad.   She also recommended a new Steamed Bun, the Togarashi Spiced Catfish Po' Boy. I had just been to New Orleans and this beat some of the Po' Boys I had down in the French Quarter.   Kounter Kulture is "Truly Local" and I'm glad they are in my neighborhood. The hours are only Monday-Friday 4:30 PM till 9:30 PM. Which makes it an easy stop for a dinner pick up on the way home from work. KK is definitely being added to my regular restaurant rotation.   When: August 4 and September 20, 2016 Why: Dinner and Dinner  & Ian Froeb's STL 100

It's a brewery with good bar grub! Enough, said.   Was running around Kirkwood and wanted a new experience for lunch. We had been wanting to try Kirkwood Station Brewing Company for a while and decided today was to be the day.   We were greeted cheerfully by a hostess who seated us in a booth, which is my preference when two are dining. The two men in the booth next to us were playing Backgammon, while enjoying lunch and the rolling of the dice was annoying at times. However, I'd rather hear the roll of die instead of a screaming or crying child.   I'm a huge fan of Fried Pickles, so I had to order their "Beer-Battered Train Tracks". It's an appropriate name, since they are located so close to the Kirkwood train station. Their version of fried pickles includes both chips and spears. The breading is okay, I'll add them to my FP list, but i don't think I'll order them again. I'm just way to picky about my fried pickles.  My dining partner totally surprised me by ordering; Fish-n-Chips. WTF? Well any way, he liked them. The menu claimed it was s house specialty! It was tender, flaky North Atlantic cod dipped in their own beer batter, fried to order and served on a bed of homemade pub chips. It's also served with homemade tartar sauce and pineapple coleslaw. The pineapple in the slaw got a thumbs down from both of us. It was a weird taste.   I originally wanted wings as an appetizer, so when I went with the Fried Pickles instead, I ordered Chicken Wings as my entree and added a side of French Fries. The wings were pretty awesome, you can tell they take some pride in serving them. They were seasoned jumbo wings dredged in flour and then fried to a golden crisp. I had them tossed in their; Hot & Spicy sauce which is homemade. A plate of fries made from Idaho potatoes with the skins on, made a perfect lunch. Two of their house brewed beers were a refreshing beverage for these wings and fries. I just wish I could remember which two I had.   Service was great and the bar grub definitely was above average. Kirkwood is overrun with great restaurants and bars and I can honestly say, I'd come back to this one.

Meet me in Saint Louie, Louie, Meet Me At The Fair........  When meeting friends for a baseball game in St. Louis you say, "Meet me at  the Stan statue". For 45 years, when Cardinal fans are meeting up with friends or family before or after a game, the logical place to meet is, The Stan Musial Statue. It is conveniently located at Gate 3, the Third Base entrance on Spruce Street.   It is a huge bronze statue that doesn't look anything like him. It doesn't have his right batting stance and the bat isn't proportionate to the statue itself. There's been talk of replacing it, but it most likely will never happen. We love our Stan just the way he is and Stan himself defended the artist when people would criticize the statue.  This statue is not only a great meeting place when attending a Cardinal baseball game, but it is a tribute to one if not THE greatest players in Cardinal history. He played outfield and 1st Base with our team for 22 seasons, 1941-1963. In 1969 he was elected in to the Hall of Fame on the first ballot with an amazing 93% vote.   So the next time you are meeting friends at the ballgame, tell them you'll be the one in RED and have them meet you at "The Man" and bring home a winner.

I wanted breakfast out and was getting bored with my favorite restaurants in the  city. So I did what any adventurous Yelper would do, I grabbed my passport and went west. I mean, way west. I went so far west, that I crossed 270. I visited a restaurant that fled the city for the county and had an amazing breakfast.   We each started out a different Mary's, I enjoyed a Veggie Mary and my dining partner went "hog" wild with a Meaty Mary. Both were cucumber Effen Vodka and SHACK - seasoned rim. I enjoyed the seasoned rim so much, I tossed my straw aside. However, my friends MM was garnished with bacon and had a beef jerky straw - OMG, it was awesome.  My friend raved and raved about his Breakfast Tacos. He's a big fan of pork belly and said, this was one of the best pork belly tacos he has had in STL. His second taco was chorizo and he claimed it was equally as good. His entree came with Hash Browns and they were the perfect Hash Browns. They were served crispy without even requesting that they be served that way. I was so jealous, they looked so good and I wanted them so bad. Sometimes it is hard giving up carbs.  Not only did he enjoy those Hash Browns, but he also had a side order of Biscuits and Gravy. It was one big fluffy biscuit smothered in thick milky gravy with chunks of sausage. I have to admit, I became weak, took a bite and now have a new addition to my Biscuits and Gravy list. These were better then B&G's I have had a diner or breakfast only restaurant.   My breakfast was the Greek Omelet with sliced tomatoes as my side instead of those amazing Hash Browns. It was a three egg omelet filled with; chicken, tomato, onion spinach and feta cheese. Both the onion and spinach were lightly sautéed before being added to the omelet, making them a flavorful accompaniment to the chicken and feta cheese.   The service was super friendly. The ambiance of old doors and being able to write on the walls makes it a unique and fun filled restaurant.   Bonus - They still honor the Taste Cards discount for the old Laclede Avenue address.

I have a new addiction, or perhaps I should say, "love". I am totally hooked on their Steamed Bun with the Togarashi Spiced Catfish with Shishito Pepper and Cherry Tomato Remoulade. As stated in previous review, it is better then any Po' Boy with Catfish that I had down in New Orleans. The crispy catfish is also superior to my current fried catfish fix here in the city. I just don't know how I'm going to break-up with my previous love, because I'm hooked on Kounter Kulture's.  Also, the Baby Romaine Salad - I can eat this every day and not tire of it. The soft cooked egg, white anchovies and their House Miso Dressing makes for a perfect evening meal. All I have to do is uncork a bottle of white wine and I am a happy diner in my own home.   I wish all carry out restaurant offered the same top notch professional service that they offer here. They are always professional and as attentive as if you were dining in. They truly make you feel welcomed and understand their menu and offerings.   I promise to try the Rice Bowl or Gyudon on a future visit.   When: Septembe 22, 2016 Why: In love with their Catfish and Baby Romaine Salad

Winfield's lives up to it's name - it's a great Gathering Place. It is relaxing, peaceful and a fun place to lunch and enjoy Happy Hour.   On this day of running around with the BFF, we needed to stop for lunch. With the BFF being a hard core low-carber we were looking for a place to accommodate her dietary needs. After looking at various restaurants on Yelp, we decided to dine at Winfield's and we are glad that we did. Our server totally understood what my friend wanted and the kitchen did not mind doing her chicken wings dry with no sauce at all. The wings were crispy, juicy and perfect for a low-carb diet. Their wings are served on a small sheet pan, a very unique and creative presentation.   I too enjoyed some of their chicken wings, but I had the Spicy Asian. Again, they were crisp and juicy. The spicy Asian was a flavorful change from the typical Buffalo or Lemon Pepper wings that I normally order. Along side of my wings I had a house salad, that I did not expect to be as big as it was. I ordered both, thinking the salad would be small. If I had known how BIG it was, it would have been a sufficent meal.   The service was sensational, we shared doggie pictures with Kyla and discovered she lived in our hood. Her warm personality, made us feel at home. In closing, all I can say is, Winfield's is a true gathering place. I encourage you to come, relax and experience it for yourself.   When: January 11, 2016 Why: Lunch with the BFF

Gaslight is a new fun place to to meet your friends for a cocktail. It's not just a bar. It's a recording studio, music school and lounge all combined into one venue. It's an interesting combination and they make it work.    There is a floor to ceiling window between the lounge and recording studio. How cool is that? I haven't been there during a recording session, but I can't wait to see one in action. It will be fun to experience a live feed from the acton in the studio.   I was impressed with the masterfully created cocktails. My current favorite is the Crystal Palace. Being a fan of vodka, I was immediately drawn to this one. It's Mastermind Vodka, Orchard Creme de Violette, Lemon Juice - Sparkling White topper. It is served up and the violet color reminds you of Liz Taylor's eyes.   A big bonus for drinking here, is that Cha Cha Chow the famous food truck has a kitchen next door. You can order from their amazing menu and they'll bring it over to you in the lounge area.   Drink - Eat - Music & Be Merry @ Gaslight  When: March 22, 2016 Why: Needed a Cocktail

If you were eavesdropping to the conversation in my kitchen the other night, this is the conversation you would have heard:  SB: What would you like for dinner?  SO: I don't want to cook.   SB: Wasn't asking you to cook, I asked what would you like.  SO: I'm not that hungry, just something light.   SB: Panera's?  SO: No, not tonight. I'm going to go walk Gracie. You pick and go get it.   I wasn't that hungry either and was craving a good salad. I flipped through our supply of local delivery and carry-out menus and found Cecil. I thought we haven't ordered from them in a while, let's give them a new try.  I quickly called and ordered a Caesar Salad with Grilled Chicken and Cheese Garlic Bread. It's only approximately three blocks from the house, so I walked up myself to retrieve it.   As we enjoyed the salad and cheese garlic bread with a glass of white wine, the SO commented that this is the perfect meal for those nights we just are not hungry enough to cook. I totally agreed. The salad and order of garlic bread were big enough for two and the glass of chilled wine was the perfect accompaniment.

I am writing this review as a seller. I probably have way more Louis Vuitton then a man should actually have. I love it all, but I've gotten to a place in my life where I do not need or use it all as regularly as I did in the past. I asked a friend who is also a LV junkie, if they'd like to buy some of my pieces and they referred me to The Vault. It was the best advice that friend has ever given me.   Before walking in with the pieces I wanted to sell, I entered to store and scoped it out. I was impressed with the variety of merchandise, displays and the sales associate. I asked, if they took items in anytime of day and the young lady said yes. I excused myself and went to my car to retrieve three LV items that I wanted to re-home.   When I re-entered carrying three LV boxes, another young lady escorted me over the processing area for evaluation. They took my information and informed me three customers were ahead of me and they'd be with me as quickly as possible. As I waited and watched these ladies work, I was impressed with their thoroughness to authenticate each and every item. I commend them on a job well done and for knowing fashion and high end products.   The lady before me brought in a very nice Coach purse, which they very politely declined to take. They explained that it was a spring line and they were buying for autumn now. Even though, they were declining the item, they did it professionally and in a friendly manner.   Now it's my turn. As stated earlier, I had brought in three items. As they went over my items, they commented how good of condition they were in. After, the inspection they offered to buy two of my bags. The third one, they had carried before and had a hard time selling it. I totally understood, it is an unique item. However, for the two they did buy, I was thrilled with the $ amount they offered. It was a very good business transaction. If I wanted a store credit, it was a few dollars more, so that may be a better deal for ladies.   My friend follows The Vault closely and later that day sent me a text showing me that my LV had already been promoted on their site. The Vault is a great store, if they had a men's version, I'd be a regular shopper.   When: August 9, 2016 Why: Re-homing my LV

Went out drinking the other night with a couple friends and enjoyed several drinks. Had a great time, but when I got home I was a little hungry. The BF had already eaten, so I was on my own.   Lucky for me Cecil is only three blocks away, so I ordered a medium two toppings pizza. When I want a simple pizza, sausage and pepperoni are my go to toppings.  They told me my order would be ready in 15 minutes, so I doodled for a few and then headed up to get my pizza. The staff is your typical pizza carry out staff. They're kind of hipster off the wall, but friendly.   My pizza was just coming out of the oven as I arrived. By the time I paid, my pizza was sliced, in the box and ready to for the trip home. When your hungry, you can overlook the provel cheese. Actually, with the read sauce and my choice of toppings the provel complimented  my pizza and satisfied my hunger.   When I got home and the BF saw how good my pizza looked, there were instant hunger pains. I am actually glad I had someone to share the pizza with, otherwise I would have eaten the entire pie. Can't believe I forgot to take a picture of the pizza. I must of really been hungry.

The staff is great and friendly. While waiting for a carryout they engage you in their conversation.  Location is tucked away like a well kept secret.   How do I fell about the pizza, I'm not really sure. My partner really liked it, we ordered "the special". My first reaction was where's the toppings, they were hidden under a large amount of "real" cheese. The amount of toppings were minimal compared to other pizza parlors and the pizza sauce had minimal flavor.   It's close to home, my other half likes them so I'll give them a second chance. Once I do, I'll post again.

We've grabbed lunch here several times, and it has always been good. I enjoy the fact that they offer some of their menu items, "naked". Which is nice for those days when you are watching your weight. Which I should be doing everyday.   I love their tortilla chips! They toss them with lime and kosher salt,  which makes them a step above some of the local non-fast food Mexican restaurants.   Today when I stopped by after visiting the AT&T store next door, I just wanted some Grilled Chicken Nachos to snack on while working around the house. The young man working the front line provided great customer service. He asked me if I wanted my chips on the side? Being me, I asked "why?". Since my order was to go, he explained the chips may be limp by the time I got home. I would have never thought of that. He put my toppings in a bowl and the chips in bag. What a great afternoon snack, it was like having a layered dip.   I have used the Qdoba catering before and it was a major hit.   My only wish is that Qdoba offered Margaritas.

Back home I would have balked at the thought of paying $13.75 for a cocktail, but this was vacation and Arnaud's French 75. So I threw caution to the wind and ordered a French 75 and it was the absolute best one I have ever had. A mixture of; Courvoisier VS, Sugar, Lemon Juice and Moet & Chandon Champagne, are the ingredients that made it worth every penny.   Being a jalapeño junkie, I was tempted to get the Brie and Jalapeño Stuffed Shrimp. However, after discussing with a bartender who also loves jalapeños she recommended I go with the Soufflé Potatoes, which I had expressed as my second choice. I'm fairly confident she guided me the right way. These Soufflé Potatoes were little pillow puffs served with a hollandaise sauce. I was content single dipping these delightful puffs of potatoes, but Charles H. idea of double dipping and making them a gourmet Cheetos, is genius and devilish at the same time.   I had planned to return Saturday night to try the Brie and Jalapeño Shrimp, but got sidetracked. It just gives me another excuse to come back in the near future. One thing that I die fell guilt about my visit at Arnaud's French 75, is the fact that the song, "The Night They Invented Champagne" from the musical Gigi was constantly playing in my head.   When: August 26, 2016 Why: The Night They Invented Champagne

Thank God my Sea Scallops were top notch and as always the Sangria went down smooth. Otherwise, this was a very disappointing visit to one of my normally 5 Star restaurants.   The service on my recent visit was on the level of a greasy diner.  The hostess, was not only snotty, she was snooty, too.  I found her looks of disdain at our party of 10, to be unprofessional. It was obvious she was not pleased that we were all not arriving at the exact same time. We all did arrive within 15 minutes, but she still seemed miffed.   Upon my arrival one of our party was already at the bar, so I joined him. I was cheerfully greeted by the bartender and I in return cheerfully said I'd like to enjoy a Sangria and showed her my Yelp check-in.  It were as if a switch was flipped, she quickly snipped, "We've had some major changes here and we no longer honor that." I responded, "Okay, I'd still like a Sangria, please." I am fine that they no longer honor a check-in special, but cut the tone and snippiness. I don't need to know about your "major changes", just say "I'm sorry that offer has expired and we no longer honor it." The words I'm sorry, go a long way in damage control.   Once we were seated, I was thrilled beyond words to see that Sea Scallops was one of the specials for the night. It made my decision process on what to order so much easier.  Pan Roasted Sea Scallops served over Butternut Squash Risotto with Passion fruit Gastrique. I was a happy diner. I have not idea how a guy raised on a beef farm, loves sea scallops so much, but I do.   When ordering, I requested, Jalea (a small plate) to be brought out first. I wanted to enjoy the crispy fried fish bites, shrimp and calamari before my scallops. When our server brought out other diners, salads, soups and other small plates, mine and another diners Jalea were missing. We thought the server went back to get them, but he never returned. In fact, we never saw him again until he brought out our entrees.  I just thought he didn't hear that part of my order and didn't worry.   When he brought my friends entree and my scallops, he also had our Jalea. My friend was a gentleman and kept his, I declined mine. I had scallops and nothing interferes my taste buds when I'm enjoying sea scallops. Our server understood and did apologize profusely. I was even offered to take them home after it was removed from my bill, but I declined.   The House Sangria here is always a winner, so I treated our table to a pitcher. If two or more are drinking the Sangria, I highly recommend ordering a pitcher. If you need or want dessert, I highly recommend the Torta de Chocolate. I took a slice home to the other half and with a cold glass of milk it was gone in a flash.   The food here is still excellent, but the customer service has taken a serious nose dive. If there has been a change in management, I hope they get this turned around quickly. Bad service can out shine excellent food. I will be back and like Sarah, I hope for better service and a more positive attitude.   When: 13 Jan 2014 Why: Dinner - Group of 10
Good selection and prices for sterling silver. You can find something for every age, and sex.  May not be in a blue box, but this store is still great for gift giving.

At first I thought they were a local business, then I found out they are actually a chain.  Weird that they only have two items on their menu and that they close at 8 PM. These tacos would be a great post bar treat.   I enjoyed my taco, but was surprised to see that it was a puffy fried shell. It's bigger then most fast food tacos and so is the price. It's simple fare, seasoned beef, tomato, lettuce and cheese. The combo with two tacos and a soda was more then enough for a weekday lunch.   The location is off the beaten path, but I guess with the near by industrial parks that they do a brisk lunch business. They're not near my hood, but if I am craving a quick taco when heading to Brentwood, I may just pull in and give them another try.

Cheap fried chicken done right and done simple. You'll have no extra sides to choose from, they only offer one and it is crinkle cut fries. Your order will then be placed in a plain white box with a flip lid. They focus on flavorful chicken, not presentation. Your boxed lunch can be a 1/4 or 1/2 chicken and be mixed, all dark or my favorite all white.   The pieces are above average in size and seasoned with a peppery coating. Pieces may be a little greasy, but the box absorbs it up so it really is not an issue. They also offer burgers and from what I've heard, great milk shakes. I need to expand my experiences here, but every time I walk up to the window, I order chicken.   Keep in mind that there is no where to eat here, it is take out only. You'll walk up to a window that is outside, place your order and go enjoy your meal elsewhere. No ambiance, keeps the chicken cheap.   Yes, this is the same Fast Eddie as Fast Eddie Bon Air. If you enjoy him at the Bon Air, check out his chicken.

Smoking is allowed at The Famous Bar and you'll know that the moment you enter the door. The smell of smoke immediately hits your sense of smell. However, it doesn't take long for your to realize the smell of smoke is really the smell of fun. Okay,  it is a smokey smell and your clothes will smell like smoke when you get home, but all of that can be overlooked because of all the fun you will have while drinking in this classic dive bar.   The bartenders know their craft and produce some amazing cocktails in a comfortable, unpretentious atmosphere. The original tin ceiling is a you must see for its beauty. Let your hair down, be adventurous and come have some fun in a smoke filled dive bar.

When: March 8 Why: Dinner  First for those that don't know or realize, Mangia Italiano and Mangia Mobil are NOT the same people. They are not connected in any way.   I've walked by this place many times going to the City Diner and figured it was time to experience it first hand. Brad had eaten here several times, but I hadn't. As we settled into our dinning experience,  I begun to read their reviews on Yelp. That's when I discovered they had new owners and management. Don't know how it was before, but this new team kicked ass.  We enjoyed a bottle of wine at home before heading out, it took us that long to decide where to dine. So with our dinner we had ice tea. However, we were pleased to hear on Tuesday night "any" bottle of wine is half price. For me, that is a winner and a reason to return.   Our service was good, the waitress was friendly and very personable. There were two bus men or assist servers who filled tea and brought our food. My negative on the service is the slowness of bringing us our bread and olive oil. It was so slow, we didn't know we'd get it and ordered Garlic Cheese Bread. The bread with the olive oil, was warm and fresh and the best of the two.   We each had an order of Mussels, which were served in a white wine cream sauce. The sauce was unique and so good when soaked up with the fresh bread. My only complaint on the mussels, which is just me....the mussels were on the small size......I like'm big.   My entree was Spinach Manicotti which was incredible. Four tubes filled with fresh spinach and cheese then topped with tomato sauce. It was so filling I could only eat two tubes, and saved the others for lunch the next day. When I warmed my lunch @ work, all my co-workers wanted to know where I dined. Brad had the Parcini Tagliatelle and it was equally good.  We're going back and it will be on Tuesday to enjoy that half off bottle of wine.

Bigger then my regular Office Depot, but being bigger didn't make it better. Good thing I am fairly self efficient when shopping. I knew what I needed, and with the good signage in the store I was able to navigate my way directly to the office supplies I needed. I easily found an orange three ring binder and highlighter to keep me organized on my quest to visit all the 250 Birthday Cakes in the Cakeway to the West.  What I found sad, is that there were 6 sales associates in the store working and not one of them offered assistance. How could they? They were all gathered up front talking amongst themselves. My previous career was retail and this store would have been a shoplifters dream with all the employees clustered together.   Great variety and selection in a bigger store, but I will continue to shop my smaller city store that offers superior customer service.

Next time you are preparing an Italian dinner, get out of the pasta aisle at your favorite grocer and take yourself to J. Viviano & Sons on The Hill.  You will be amazed at the variety of ingredients to help you create a truly authentic Italian meal. They've got it all and at prices you will not want to resist.   I have always been a fan of their typical ingredients; tomato sauce, paste, spices, fresh cheese and etc. etc., but this last visit I experienced something totally new. I tried their frozen ravioli and was shocked how well it went with our awesome homemade sauce. They are made and frozen in house, so it is almost like you made the pasta yourself.  I'll keep it a secret, if you do.   The staff is always friendly and helpful. If you have questions, do not  hesitate to ask, they'll give you ideas on that masterful meal.   As we were leaving, at a perfect time. A huge charter bus pulled up in front and droves of little cute silver haired ladies headed to the front entrance. I had no idea, Viviano's was a tourist stop.

I normally shop the Galleria store, for convenience. However, when I needed a Genius Bar appointment the other day this location fit my needs better.   It is so small compared to the newer and expanded store at The Galleria, that I felt claustrophobic. There were so many shoppers, folks in for One on One sessions and then those of us who need the use of the Genius Bar that I felt like I was in a downtown nightclub on a Saturday night.   I do praise Apple for their crowd control. You're first meet by a greeter, who directs you to the concierge, who then checks you in for your scheduled appointment. The two work well together creating good crowd control. (My claustrophobic feelings are on me and not a reflection of the store) It provides good customer service, because shoppers are directed to the correct areas and introduced to the specific person who can help them.   I am not a nerd and at times I admit I am just stupid when it comes to computers. Why I am a big fan of the Genius Bar is that they talk to you, not down to you. They understand I'm not as Apple savvy as they always present the answers in layman terms that I can understand.   The Galleria will always be my go to store for convenience and size, but when in a scheduling jam it will be West County to the rescue.

How lucky is the Patch neighborhood, to have Lucky's in their hood? I'd say pretty damn, lucky. Lucky's is a great place to belly up to the bar and enjoy a cold beer and burger. I like that the bar is vintage it is all the old natural wood, so warm and inviting. It's a true neighborhood bar. Can't wait for the good weather to return, so I can enjoy the patio.   I was torn on what to order for my dinner, but when you have a burger named, "Burger from Hell" I can't resist. I love jalapeños on my burgers and Pepper Jack cheese is my favorite and this burger had them both. It also had, sautéed onions, Cheddar cheese, Hot Sauce and was served between a toasted Kaiser Roll. I had them hold the Cheddar and the burger was still heart warming, or should I say heart burning wonderful. I can alway tell when something is spicy enough, when little beads of sweat appear on my forehead.   As my side, I choose Steak Fries and Lucky's serves them huge. To me these were more like wedges, but nonetheless they were awesome. They were seasoned well, not just with salt. Mentioning salt, being one who watches my salt intake, I did not feel that their food was overly salted as mentioned in previous review. I only got about 8 fries, but due to their largeness it was the perfect portion.   I'll be returning to Lucky's to try their Roasted Chicken Wings and of course their Fried Chicken Dinner - I've heard it is a winner, winner.   When: January 27, 2015 Why: Dinner

I live near Stellina and never visited until a couple weeks ago, and I kick myself for not visiting sooner. It taught me to never judge a restaurant from the curb. It may not look like much from the outside, but the food is incredible. My first visit was a house salad and Lasagna, the portion of lasagna was large enough for me to save some for lunch the next day at work. I was so impressed, three days later I ordered carryout for lunch. My partner and I had the Braised Beef and South Side Smoke. Both sandwiches were large and full of flavor. Stellina Pasta is big flavor in a small cafe.
This Einstein Bros was a disappointment.   Unfriendly staff - flavorless sandwiches - weak tea.   I'll stick with my Einstein Bros in the city.

I've always enjoyed the street tacos at Canyon Cafe.  The Bison, Fish and Vegetable are always my go to order. I also love their top shelf Margaritas and house chip with salsa. This last visit, I don't know what possessed me. I went totally crazy and ordered chicken wings at a Tex-Mex restaurant and I am glad I did.  Their wings were spicy, huge, meaty and crisp. They were better then wings I have enjoyed at a sports bar and a specialty wings restaurant. I'm still a fan of the street tacos, quesadillas and huge salads here, but now I'm having to put these amazing wings into my rotation.   In addition to the wings, I shared an order of Queso Dip with my friends. This creamy dip was served with fresh house made tortillas as well as warm chips. I favor the chips, but the tortillas are easy to dip in the queso, too.   The service was attentive and friendly. Amanda our server was actually a delight. She made our dining experience fun. She knew we were dining between two movies and made sure our drinks & food were served promptly. Orange is my favorite color and I'm a fan of linen napkins, so wiping my mouth here after a hearty bite, puts a smile on my face.   Canyon Cafe is a great place to eat after shopping the plaza, meeting friends for Happy Hour, or after a movie at Landmark.   Will I return? - These margaritas will always bring me back & now I want more of these wings.   When: January 4, 2017 Why: Snack between movies of a double feature afternoon.

You've heard the expression, "Don't judge a book by its' cover". Well, I am hear to tell you, do not judge a taco shop by its name. I have been ignoring Fuzzy for a long time and now I regret that I didn't give them a try earlier. I was expecting a Taco Bell type restaurant and that was the furthest thing from my experience.   Fuzzy may not offer table service, but the quality of food exceeds some of the better known Mexican restaurants that do. As you enter the taco shop, you place your order for food and alcoholic beverages. Yes, Fuzzy has booze and their frozen Margaritas will give you a brain freeze and kick your ass. I was amazed how strong they were. I'm normally not a fan of frozen drinks, but this one is one of the best frozen Margaritas I have ever enjoyed.   After placing your food order, you move on to the next counter around the corner. Sometimes you are given a vibrating beeper or you just wait until your number is called out. They hustle in the kitchen and our food was prepared in minimal time.   There are no free chips and salsa here and I like it that way. So many times when a restaurant does offer them, you munch and munch until you are to full to enjoy the entree you ordered. We ordered Chips and Queso and the portion they served was the perfect size for two. Both of us liked how they sprinkled the chips with chili powder. The queso is thick and clings to the chips after being dipped.   We both ordered Taco Plates which comes with two tacos and two sides. We both ordered Tempura Fish and would rate it second best in the city. Our second tacos were Fajita, one beef and one chicken. Both were tender and seasoned well. Sampling each others, we agreed the beef was the best.   As side dishes, we both selected the Cilantro Lime Rice which was way better then the traditional Mexican Rice you get at the budget Mexican Restaurants. I had the Refried Beans, which again surprised me with the quality. However, my friends Borracho Beans will be what I will order next time. They were spicy and the perfect side dish for tacos.   Next time I want inexpensive Mexican food, I'm driving past all the local little El and Del blanks and going straight to Fuzzy's Taco Shop. I take better food over table service any day.   Also, for all my single lady Yelpers, there were a lot of hot single men dining alone at Fuzzy's.  I'm just saying.......  When: September 4, 2015 Why: Dinner

"Grease" is the word. Greasiest fried chicken I have ever experienced. All the food here taste the same, like old "grease" that is long over due for a change. The cole slaw is flavorless, the crinkle french fries are mush, and Mrs. Paul makes a better onion ring. Why people think this is the best fried chicken in St. Louis is beyond me.

Have you seen those CVS television commercials where a customer says,  "this is my CVS."? Well, this is MY Target, but I share it with most of south Saint Louis.  Like other Yelpers, I can not shop here and walk out with just one item. Target merchandisers are the masterminds of end caps. They know what pushes our buttons and how to motivate us into adding it to our carts.   Here are a few reasons I LOVE this Target:   1. They have a Starbucks inside. Who doesn't love to sip a Latte while browsing through a discount store.   2. Better greeting card selection then a Gold Crown Hallmark store.   3. Great housewares department, prices equal to Bed, Bath and Beyond.   4. Fabulous toy department when I need gifts for the wee-ones. Saves me from going to Toys 'R Us.   5. K Kups for my Keurig. When they are on sale, they are cheaper then ordering them on-line.   6. Men's clothing department that has a surprisingly decent selection of casual wear.   7. A totally awesome Christmas department at that time of year.   I could go on and on, but then everyone from the county would be coming here instead of the Brentwood location and I do not share that well. Nor do I like crowds.   I highly recommend parking in the garage, or on the side of the building to avoid a parking lot derby. Parking can get crazy on the lot in front of the building. If you park in the garage, you'll be able to see your shopping cart ride down the escalator.

WTF! Seriously, what is wrong with this J Crew? They are selling a fantastic product, but their customer service is lacking big time. This may come to you as a shock, but if you want to be treated equally, I highly recommend that you shop the J Crew at Plaza Frontenac and avoid this location.   I love me some J Crew, it such a good traditional and quality brand. I pay full retail and I too like Katherine B., ravage their sale section. I have shopped this location multiple times and each time the customer service has been at a minimum. On my most recent visit, I will admit I had a clean grungy look going on. I was unshaven, baggy cargo shorts and an over sized polo shirt.  I am a self  sufficient shopper, but I do like to be acknowledged. At least let me know that you are aware I am in your store.   Product 5 Stars, Customer Service 1 Star = 3 Stars overall.   As stated earlier, shop the J Crew at Plaza Frontenac where they treat everyone equally. They know not to judge a book by it's cover. Some of the best shoppers are not always dressed to the 9's. When shopping 6's and 7's will do.

So glad to see that on my last shopping experience that they have totally raised the level of their customer service. We were greeted as we entered the store and when we had questions an associate was available to assist.   I love this time of year when they have the pumpkin mixes for quick bread and waffles. They make a delightful fall breakfast.   As stated by the infamous Patt C. they have some impressive cookbooks. I should know, in our house there are over 200 cookbooks so I think I know a good one when I see one.   Glad I was able to raise your stars, WS.  You deserved it.

I will always prefer to shop at a Target over an Wal-Mart and I am lucky to have one this good in my neighborhood. I use to be a fan of the one on Brentwood, but since this location did a complete renovation a couple years back....wow.  The store is clean, the selection is great and the customer service is top notch for a major discount store.  The parking is easy, plenty of space on a private lot and a parking garage. It is so cool they have a escalator for your shopping cart so you don't have to carry all your bags down to your car.  I've never walked out of here empty handed, I usually walk out with more then I went in for.

If you're a gourmet chef or if you just play one at home, Chef's Shoppe is a place you gotta check out. Seriously, they have everything you will ever need for your kitchen and then some. You'll feel like you are shopping at Sur La Table, Williams-Sonoma or Bed, Bath and Beyond, but you'll be shopping LOCAL.   Being a old farm boy, I love their selection of Lodge Cast Iron cookware. Nothing beats a nice big skillet to fix up some Sunday Fried Chicken. I also like the large selection of hot sauces and spices. It has assisted me in creating several gift baskets for friends and family who like things on the spicy side.   If you're a popcorn addict, they have an awesome popcorn shoppe within the store. They offer a wide variety of flavors and tins to make gift giving easy. Or just buy yourself a couple bags for your next Netflix marathon.   Next time you need gadgets and gizmos for the kitchen, remember to shop local and remember Chef's Shoppe.

This is "my" Target of choice. It is close to home and always has what I need and want. It is always clean, well organized and for a mass merchandiser, the staff is helpful and friendly.   Whenever I need a greeting card, this is my go to store. They offer a large variety and I can always find a card to match the personality of the recipient. They even have a line of cards that are printed on recycled paper - Go Green.   I'm a huge fan of, Harry's shaving products and have ordered them online for years. Target recently started carrying their products, so when I forget to order them directly from Harry, I can run in to Target and stock up.   Two other departments I am a extremely huge fan of are, the housewares and home furnishings. I recently was looking for a small accent table and was considering ordering from Wayfair. I then checked things out at Target and they had the perfect table at a cheaper price and I did not have to assemble my new table.   The homewares department is like a mini Bed, Bath & Beyond and the prices are practically the same. I recently was able to find some great house warming and wedding gifts for friends and relatives.   Keep up the good work, Target. You've got a fan.   I'll be back? - Of course, I will. I'm a shopper at heart.   When: October 14, most recently Why: Cards, Harry's and a few odd & ends.

I stand corrected. This is not a chain as I was originally informed. My internet searches were misleading and the site I visited has been corrected. So eating here, you are supporting a local business.

I found my Christmas Dinner at Blueberry Hill and had a fun time, too.   I was one of the many folks who had to work on Christmas Day and when I got home at 3:30PM, the last thing I wanted to do was prepare a holiday meal. As I relaxed with nice cold winter beer, I search Yelp and the internet for restaurants open for dinner.  I found a couple open and serving luxurious prime rib meals, but after a 10 hour work day, I just wanted simple and relaxing. I then saw Blueberry Hill was open and thought, "Why not, it should be fun."  I finished my beer and we headed over to The Loop. I lucked out and found Prince parking directly across the street. As we exited the car other diners were arriving. Once in front of BH, I pulled on the door and it was locked. Immediately I thought, Oh, no. Then I read the sign, they'd be opening at 5PM. We arrived 15 minutes early and it was a good thing we did. In a flash, there were over 2 dozen folks waiting for the doors to open and by the time they did open there were 4 dozen.   Once the doors opened, it was obvious who had been there previous years. They knew how the system was going to work and rushed to the appropriate lines.  Once inside, you were informed that there was no table service and to place your order at the back booth. When you placed your order, you got a number and they told when to be at the kitchen pass through window to pick up your order. This may sound like a pain in the ass, but they had it down to a science.   We enjoyed a beer, a shot of scotch while waiting and when it was my time to be at the pass through window, my number was called shorty after I arrived. My dining partner claims his was the best Fish-n-Chips he has had in STL. I think they were good, but not the best. My Reuben with a side of French Fries made for an unusual Christmas Dinner, but fulfilled my needs and received a spot on my Reuben List.   It was obvious some of these diners come every year. The crowd was fun and full of the holiday spirt. I hope to be prepared for future holiday dinners better, but BH made my 2014 Christmas, unique and memorable.

First visit and I actually was impressed. I was never a fan of the Shop N Save that was in this same space. I normally shop the Hampton Village store, but I may be changing my loyalty.  The store was laid out a little differently, but it was still easy to navigate and find all the groceries on my list. Departments that impressed me, were the produce, deli and the self-serve hot bar.   Here's my take on things, the produce was better organized and cleaner then the Hampton store. The deli workers had personality, were actually cheerful and went back to the cooler to find my request. Then there was the hot bar - which will be an easy place to grab a fast lunch or easy dinner.   I'll admit, I did miss the butcher counter. There is just something about a hand-cut steak. Hopefully they'll add one in the near future. Some complained about the decor, but I feel considering how fast they flipped the stores, that they did a great job.   I actually think this location may give some of the neighboring Schnucks some competition within the company.   I'll be back? - I sure, will.   When: November 21, 2018 Why: Groceries for T-Day at work.

I love me some Cleveland-Heath. I can see why Ian Froeb ranked it #7 on his STL 100. If it were on the other side of the river, I would be there every week and most likely a couple times a week. So when it was time to celebrate my birthday with a favorite cousin who lives on the IL side, C-H was the logical choice to meet for an amazing lunch.   I arrived early as usual and grabbed my favorite barstool on the corner near the front door.  While I waited for my cousin to arrive, I enjoyed a Red Wedding. Of course it was an alcoholic beverage. It was made with; Jameson, Campari, Apple, Ginger, Lemon and Honey and served in a tall slender glass with no ice. It was refreshing; I liked the combination of Jameson & Campari. It was the perfect kick-start for my 60th birthday.   As I write this review, I am now amazed at the amount of food and booze we consumed at lunchtime. When my cousin arrived, we opted to stay seated at the bar instead of moving to a table. The bartender was attentive as our server and the hostess kept us entertained by stopping by and joining in on our conversation.  It made for a long, fun-filled and relaxing lunch.   Now let me tell you about the delectable food we devoured. We started off with their Chilled Beets. Growing up my cousin hated beets, but awhile back she tried them here at C&H and has been hooked ever since. They serve their beets in a horseradish cream with pickled red onion, radish, dill and rye crumble. Honestly you could serve me this for dessert and I'd be happy.   For our entrees we each selected a sandwich. Mine was the Open Faced Ham and hers' was Pulled Pork. We each selected fries as our side, but we also ordered a side of Brussels Sprouts to share. Their sprouts are served in lemon vinaigrette with capers and shallots.  The fries are slender fries and are a mix of regular and sweet potato.   Open Face Ham - Thick cut, served on Texas Toast topped with pimento cheese and a Sunnyside up egg.  Would also make a great breakfast.   Pulled Pork - pork is from Rensing's Farm and it is topped with house made pickles, blue cheese coleslaw all on a Pretzel bun.  The coleslaw really pulled it all together into an amazing sandwich.   During all this eating we also enjoyed multiple cocktails, Old Fashioned, Manhattan, Bloody Mary and Stag Beer. Each and every one of them went down smoothly.   Celebrating a milestone birthday, you've got to have a momentous dessert. We choose a Bourbon Pecan Gooey Butter Cake. We just couldn't say no to the whiskey caramel, candied pecans and praline pecan ice cream. The serving was definitely large enough for two to share.  To my surprise, I was also served an order of Beignets with a birthday candle. No one sang to me, thank goodness, but the order of beignets made my special day more special.   Side Note: My cousins' husband always likes it when we meet for lunch, because he knows we over order and he'll have our leftovers for dinner.  I like that the to-go vessels from C&H are eco-friendly.   Would I come back? I always do.   When: November 10, 2016 Why: Birthday Celebration

Not my usual Schnucks, but we were shopping on The Hill and thought what The Hell why not.   I will say this, FACE-LIFT! This store in is serious need of an upgrade and remodel. It just felt and looked very dated. We found most of what we needed, found it odd that a grocer near The Hill did not have fresh basil in stock.   It is extremely clean, to the point of scrubby dutch clean and spacious. Spacious to the point of they have a lot of wasted space that could be utilized to increase those sales $'s per square foot.   The staff here is crazy. They just seem to be having way to much fun at work. Cracking jokes, bantering with customers and each other. That is a work energy I can respect. I think we may have had the same employee who helped Christine with her whipped cream in a can. Either that, they all have dirty little minds. Didn't there use to be a hospital on Arsenal for crazies?   My new list  "Parking Lot Derby" was created after shopping here. Why you ask? There was a young man driving around the parking lot talking on his cell phone. To be more honest, he was zig zagging from one side to the other, with no regard to traffic flow or parking spaces. As we were leaving, it took both of us to keep track of  him so we could leave the parking lot safely.   As we exited on to Arsenal,  thinking we were in the clear here comes Mr. Zig-Zag out of the other entrance cutting in front of us. Yes, still on his cell phone. Brad looked behind us and saw him pull back into the parking lot. Guess he was practicing driving while talking. Trust me, he should park and talk.

The Erker's have brought fashionable, unique and affordable optics back to the CWE. Their selection is cutting edge and fun. If you're like me, I like a couple frames I can change into depending on my mood or attire. With the prices available here at Eye Roc, you'll be able to have a pair for dress/work and a pair for casual/playtime.   The staff was extremely friendly and knowledgeable. I'm due for new frames later this summer and I'll be shopping at Eye Roc.

Why is it, that when a store or business is located in "Ladue" that the employees get a pissy attitude. This store could be great, but the customer service pulls it's rating down. It has a great selection and variety in all departments. It is clean and laid out and merchandised well. It is the lousy attitude of the employees that bring this rating down.   Today we stopped by to pick up some produce and could not find what we were searching for. We looked around for an associate to assist us and none were to be found. This is the first Schnucks I've shopped that there was not an associate working the department. To get assistance we had to go ask someone in the prepared foods to find someone. They had to go in the stockroom, which we had opened and yelled into. She returned, saying someone would be out shortly. We waited and waited. Finally, a short, stocky, gray haired man, hit the doors open with a bit of attitude.  "What?" We told him we needed shallots. He pointed to the left and said, "look over there, they're in the baskets. How did you miss, them" He kept on walking the entire time, did not even stop to talk to us. What if we had other questions? This was the worst customer service I have ever seen in a Schnucks and I've shopped around.  I've gotten better service at the one on Lin dell.  Side-note, one of the shallots we bought was rotten. Good thing we bought extras.

Decor is over the top, but it adds to the fun time you'll have at Amigo Joe's. Their top shelf Margarita's are fantastic, be careful they can sneak up on you. The salsa is thick and spicy a nice compliment to the chips. For the price point offered at Amigo Joe's, the food is well worth the price and beyond. I've done both dine in and carry-out and have been pleased with both. The staff is witty, friendly and very helpful.

Jeni, let me first apologize for visiting so late. I told by an individual that you were similar to Baskin & Robbins Ice Cream. What were they thinking? The only think you have in common with BR is that you have more then one flavor of ice cream. That is it. Otherwise you are in a class way beyond BR and that comparison makes no sense at all. I think I am going to have to reevaluate that friendship.   I always judge an ice cream shoppe by its vanilla. If you cannot produce a high quality vanilla, that rocks my world, why should I bother trying your other flavors. Good news, Jeni, Ndali Estate Vanilla Bean, stole my heart. I loved it! The other flavor I tried on my inaugural visit was; Salted Peanut Butter with Chocolate Flecks and it was another winner.   Your staff at the CWE location are top notch. They were friendly and provided so much product information as they offered me samples. The information oozed out from them so naturally, it was friendly conversation instead of a sales pitch.   I'll be back most likely every time I am in the CWE, now that I know you are nothing like Baskin-Robbins. The only thing I wish for is that you'd offer the ability to buy only one scoop instead of two. I have weight issues resulted from portion control and being able to order just one small scoop would be nice. I hate ordering and throwing half away. It seems so wasteful of such a quality product.  When: August 8, 2016 Why: Sweet Treat

This location is slowly winning me over as a regular and it is doing it at good pace.  I stop here on my way home from work, so I do not need to pass my house and visit the one at Hampton Village. I'm thinking in the future, instead of going to HV from home, I'll head over here to Arsenal.   I'm still not comfortable with the lay out of this store, but I can learn a new floor plan.  The vegetable and fruit department is smaller, but the selection seems to be fresher.  I rarely buy my meat from Schnucks, but the butcher counter here is as good as any other location. I also, like the fact that they periodically offer samples. I have never seen samples being passed out at Hampton Village.   What truly sets this location above other locations, is that the staff still practices Schnucks old motto, "the friendliest stores in town".  They by far have the best customer service skills of "any" grocery store I have shopped in the Lou. Having this, makes it worth the drive of a couple extra blocks.   Another side note making it worth to shop, it has some of the best eye candy in town.  Whatever catches your eye,  you'll see some hottie's in the store.

Plaza Frontenac is the Saint Louis "high roller" mall. I know that, because I giggled the other day when I earned a new Yelp Badge called, "High Roller" while shopping at some of my favorite stores. PF is an older mall and could use a face lift or shot of Botox, but the staff keeps the Williamsburg style grounds and building in excellent condition.   I rarely shop the anchor stores of Neiman-Marcus and Saks Fifth Avenue. I go for the heart of the mall and shop the smaller specialty type stores. While shopping here, I have never experienced pretension or rudeness from store associates or other shoppers and I have shopped unshaven and in ratty jeans. To be honest, I have seen more attitude at The Galleria then here.   My shopping at PF can be broken down in to four basic groups or reasons:   Leather - Louis Vuitton, Cole Haan, Coach and Tumi Home - Pottery Barn, Williams-Sonoma and Sur La Table Clothes & Jewelry - J Crew, Lucky Brand Jeans,  Tiffany & Co. and Omega   After some power shopping or browsing, I can recharge my batteries at:  Canyon Cafe, Cardwells at The Plaza, Brio Tuscan Grille or Brick Top. All four of these have great bars for a quick drink or a leisurely meal. I can also treat myself to some hometown chocolate at Bissinger's.   I just had an idea for a UYE  - Bar Hopping @ Plaza Frontenac.  We can sip on Margarita's and Martini's and sample an appetizer or two.   Another great thing about PF is the Landmark Theaters which in my opinion is one of the better movie houses in the area. They bring in a lot of titles that Saint Louis would miss if it were not for them. Some of us enjoy foreign and art house independent type films more then those big blockbuster films.   Plaza Frontenac is small, quaint and fills some of my shopping needs, so in Yelp standards, "I am a fan"  and a big fan at that.

I absolutely love this store. Once again, so many of my Christmas gifts came from here. Each of the ladies on my gift list got something from the GB and I even found something for one of the guys. The holiday has passed, so I can tell you each gift received great praise when it was opened.  This store kinda reminds me of Pottery Barn or Williams-Sonoma Home, without the high prices and snobby attitudes. The staff is always friendly and goes out of the way to assist and accommodate you.   If you are looking for unique items to decorate your home, or an unusual gift for that hard to pleased friend - this is the place to shop. So the next time you are in Edwardsville, be sure to make time and stop here to shop local.   Chances of returning: You can bet money on it.  When: Three times within a 10 day period in December Why: Holiday Shopping

Gallagher's is definitely a, "Winner, Winner - Chicken Dinner". I've heard great things about Gallagher's for years, so for the celebration of my friends 29th Anniversary of their 29th birthday, we decided to do a road trip to Waterloo. It took us only a half hour from downtown STL and it is so worth the drive. It was less time then driving out to west county.  Sunday is Family Style Chicken Dinner for $12.95. Family Style is the polite way of saying, "It is all you can eat". Our table was covered with a platter of crispy & juicy fried chicken, a bowl of fresh green beans with ham, another bowl of corn custard and yet another bowl of mashed potatoes and finally a gravy boat of milk gravy. Then when you are done stuffing yourself with all these home cooked delights, they offer you a piece of Susie's Sheet Cake for dessert. The flavor changes on the regular, so our flavor was Blueberry Lemon.  Fried Chicken: Large pieces, crispy crust & juicy inside, not spicy or overly salty - just perfectly seasoned.   Green Beans: Simply seasoned with ham, salt and pepper  Corn Custard: Unique in its' own way - everyone loved it once they tried it.   Mashed Potatoes - Whipped heavenly, with a very lumps to show it truly is homemade.   Milk Gravy - Life doesn't get any better then gravy made from fried chicken drippings.   Sheet cake: The sweetness and tartness of blueberries and lemon made a great finale.   The whiskey and craft beer menus will blow you away. You'll never expect the variety they offer from a small town restaurant. The birthday honoree loved their Whiskey Sour and my Manhattan had good flavor, but a tad too much vermouth for me.   The service was your typical down home, small town friendly with a twist. Some of the staff was clean as a whistle, boy/girl next door type and others were hipster/lumbersexual. Making for a nice mix of service with a smile.   I loved the fried chicken dinner and cannot wait to go back and try their ribeye.   When: April 17, 2016 Why: Friends Birthday Dinner

If you like Restoration Hardware, Pottery Barn and Williams Sonoma Home. You're going to love Gingham Buffalo and you'll be shopping local as well.   Your creative juices will start to flow as soon as you enter the store. You'll see how a few simple accessories can jazz up a room and make it feel new again. As I shopped, I wanted to curl up on the sofa with a glass of wine and a good book. Then I saw a bedroom staging and was ready to snuggle up for a nap. Each staging had me wishing it were in my home.   They have so many unique and unusual gifts that no one would dare think of returning or exchanging them. They'd be cherished for years to come. Take your time shopping and notice all the details. You'll be delighted at what you'll find to make your home more beautiful and enjoyable.   If you have questions or need some basic decorating suggestions, ask the staff on duty. They are eager to assist you at any level. This store is a definite stop for me every time I am in Edwardsville.

The Book House gives you multiple reasons to shop local. First, you receive a 20% discount on a purchase over $10 when you check in on Yelp. Second, you can buy a Yelp Deal - $12 for $25. Both are a super savings.  As other reviewers here on Yelp have stated, the new and used books are all mixed together. This is very disorganized and confusing for even the most experienced book shopper. However, I did like how they separated cookbooks with a special section for "vintage". I found a couple that caught my eye, but had to go home and double check my collection before buying.  Looking at several of the used book prices, I found them to be slightly over-priced for the condition of the book. The ones I viewed, they had multiple copies and had them priced only a few dollars less then the original publishers price printed on the book. I understand that they are not a BARGAIN bookstore, but let's get real about the pricing. A used book is USED book.   I also found the customer service to be lacking and unfriendly. No thank-you for shopping at the check-out, or did you find everything that you were looking for? I know a couple of true bookworms and they are introverts, so I guess I need to cut them some slack on the poor, limited service.   If you love books, don't mind waiting on yourself and can muddle your way through their disorganized bookshelves, The Book House is a good find in Maplewood.   When: March 15, 2016 Why: Shopping Manchester on a Spring Day

Oh, the old gay bar, she ain't what she use to be.  She ain't what she use to be.   Don't get me wrong, you can still have fun at Novak's, but it seems to have taken a different path recently. Some of the staff seem to have developed an "Attitude" and it is not a pretty "Attitude".   What makes Novak's a fun place to go is the melting pot mixture of patrons who frequent the bar regularly and those who are coming to see what all the hype is about. It's not Ellis Island, but it is close enough when you are mixing the straight and LGTB communities.   My most recent visit was meeting friends for drinks before dinner at Sanctuaria. Shannon was our bartender and she served a very good cock-tail. She was also very pleasant and made sure those of us sitting at the bar were fully taken care of and entertained.   The night we were there was a game night and they had two teams playing Family Feud. We were seated at the end of the bar near the stage. We began to banter and have fun with one of the teams and were quickly put in our place by the game show host. We were told to "shut-up" and not talk to the contestants. (Attitude) I'm sorry, I thought this was a bar to have fun. It's not like we were giving them the answer to the last question on "Who Wants to Be a Millionaire". We became mute and our new friends still won the feud.   The biggest disappoint of the night was the patio. It was a cool breeze night and sipping cock-tails out there would have been grand. Instead, it smelled to high heaven and everyone who went out to enjoy it quickly returned. It had the smell of stagnant water and stale beer. Get out the power-hose and wash it down.   Shannon was a delight, so next time we're in The Grove, we'll stop by again. After all, with gay bar turn over in STL Novak's is quickly becoming one of the oldest.

Nixta was my third and final stop on National Margarita Day 2019. Their Margarita took the Blue Ribbon for best of the day.   It's hard to believe, that I had not been to Nixta before. You'd think that someone who likes Margaritas and enjoys Mexican cuisine would have been here earlier. I can tell you, now that I regret I had not visited earlier.   I arrived around 8PM. With it being a Friday and NMD, it was packed. Lucky for me, there was one spot open at the bar. I made myself comfortable and pulled out my St Louis Passport. Having my STL Passport, I got two traditional Margaritas for the price of one.   On the recommendation of the bartender, I matched my first Margarita with, Sikil Pak with Chips. It was delicious! Best way to describe it would be a Mayan style hummus made with pumpkin seeds. It was such a nice change from traditional guacamole or queso dip.   My second Margarita was paired with their, Flautas De Pollo. I couldn't resist the, chicken tinga with goat cheese and burned tomato crema. They were smaller then my favorite chicken flautas at another local popular restaurant, but their flavor much bigger.   Considering the busyness of the bar, my service was still attentive. I give my bartender kudos for her descriptive descriptions of their food items.  Chances of returning? - They're very good.   When: February 22, 2019 Why: National Margarita Day

If you love Gin, or if you are wanting to learn about Gin, then you've got to have a cocktail at; The Gin Room. I stopped by the other day with a friend to enjoy a cocktail. Ms Norma had told me how knowledgeable Natasha was and she wasn't kidding. Natasha knows her, Gin and she'll share that knowledge with you as she makes your cocktail.  I'm a vodka drinker and love Moscow Mule's and when I shared that with "The Gin Girl", Natasha made me a, "Gin Gin Mule". It simply is a mule made with a high-end Gin. I was amazed how more flavorful the mule was with Hendrick's Gin.  If you're hanging out with friends on S. Grand, I highly recommend that you stop by The Gin Room.

Cecil Whittaker gave me 12" for my birthday. A 12" one topping pizza and all I had to do was buy two beverages. What a deal. I highly recommend signing up for the VIP Rewards at CWP. In addition to the birthday gift, they have special offerings almost every week that are only available to VIP members. You'll also earn points, to receive more free stuff.   In addition to the two beverages, we added chicken wings to create a lazy night dinner. I must live in a "pizza hood", because all of the pizza joints always have friendly employees.

Great neighborhood coffee shop. Great location making it easy to stop by on your way to work or while you are out running errands.   They have several tables in a small dining area that is brightly light by a large window and colorful walls. Making it a great place for a morning meeting with a coworker or business associate and gossiping with BFF.   I didn't see much of pastries available, but I stopped by early afternoon for a holiday flavored Latte. However, I did see a menu offering soups and salads for lunchtime fare. I hope they get a website up soon so we can see their menu at all times.   They use one of the most popular roasters in Saint Louis, Kaldi's for their coffee so you know it will be a good brew.  Also, they have a frequent drinkers card that you get punched and after 7 lattes or 7 cups of coffee the 8th one is FREE. Who doesn't like a free cup of morning Joe? A nice touch to a neighborhood shop.   When walking the dog(s), this will be my reward.

Picture this; 18 foodies from a social website called Yelp having an International Supper Club meeting at Mango. Now imagine, these foodies being divided up into groups of 9 and seated at tables that are perpendicular to each other. As a final visual, give these hearty partying foodies only one waitress. Can you guess what you get?   You get one hell of a fun night and a waitress named Kelsie who I bestow the title of; "Best Waitress of 2011". When we were seated and I realized Kelsie was going to be waiting on our entire group alone I thought to myself, this is going to be a disaster. Miss. Kelsie proved me wrong, she is one top notch professional waitress. She treated us as if we guest in her own home.   Kelsie worked our tables making recommendations and taking our orders as if she were a socialite working a charity fund raiser. She knew her menu product and asked open ended questions to figure out which items would be best for each foodie.   She had me starting my night off with a Mango Passion Fruit Martini. I could have had more then one, but I was my own designated driver so I had to refrain from saying, "more, please". When my main entree arrived, I switched over to a glass of Sangria which they are famous for and rightfully so.   I started my feast off with Aguadito Pollo. I enjoyed a dinner size cup, which was a hearty portion. It is a homemade soup of grilled chicken, rice, vegetables and Peruvian spices in a citrus-herb broth. A very creative and flavorful soup.   I love mussels, so when I saw Choros Sudados on the menu I knew it was meant for me. Nothing fills me up like a big bowl of steamed mussels in white wine and good French bread to soak up the broth.   When it came time for dessert i was already fairly full, but Kelsie told me I had to try the Torta Chocolate.  I had to listen to her, she hadn't guided me wrong all night.  So I ordered it along with a side of vanilla ice cream. In my foodie world chocolate cake with fudge icing needs either ice cream or a big glass of cold milk. Kelsie informed me that the cake was a family recipe. To be honest, that is what sold me on trying it over the Flan. The cake was moist and I wish I were in the family so I could get my hands on that recipe.   Mango and especially Kelsie a big hearty thanks for making our International Supper Club so awesome. I'll be back and you can bet your last dollar I will want Kelsie as my waitress.

This Schnucks is so old, I think this is where Noah stocked up on groceries before the big flood. A face lift or even some botox would help this aging grocery store.  The layout of this store throws me, it makes me discombobulated. I am use to the ones closer to home in Saint Louis. However, this one is a great location and close to work making it easily accessible when needed. It is such a deep store, that they have a horizontal aisle cutting all the verticals ones in half. I think that is what cause me to be totally lost in the store.   The staff here is extremely friendly and very helpful. When I shop here it is the wee hours of morning, 5:30AM and they are perky even at that hour.  As stated in a previous review, it is extremely clean for an older store. The thing that boggles my mind is that they have a security guard at this location. I didn't think it was that bad of a neighborhood. Perhaps it is just a deterrent. If so it works I feel very safe.   Schnucks, you've got a good location and good staff how about giving this store some well needed improvements?

Big thumbs up for the Spinach & Portabella Mushroom Quesadilla. A meat lover like me was amazed at it's flavor and it has become one of my favorites. If you need "meat", Mama's Quesadilla is excellent with it's grilled chicken, fajita vegetables and Jack cheese. Salad lovers, order the Blackened Salmon Caesar and you will have the perfect lunch. Dieters, this is filling and bursting with flavor. "Limit 2 Margarita's" the Top Shelf Commemorative is top notch, enjoy two at the bar with house made chips and salsa, to have a perfect "Happy Hour".

Great news, this ancient grocery store is getting a remodel. As with any remodel where the store remains open, there are obstructions to maneuver around. Shoppers may have a little inconvenience now, but it is well worth it. The areas that have already had their face lifts, are looking fabulous.   This is my before work grocer, I pick up supplies for the office and on occasion lunch items. I have found this staff to be, small town friendly. They give new meaning to the friendliest stores in town. They are so excited about their remodel, they take real pride in their store. So with a remodel and energetic employees, I am bumping them up a star. They deserve it.

Wow! Impressive! Wonderful customer service.   Last weekend we had a celebration to attend and waited to the last minute to get our gift. Yes we procrastinated, but Lesher's came to our rescue and will now be our florist of choice in the future. They truly went above and beyond in their service.   As I arrived home from work at 4:45pm, I was informed that we had no flowers to take that evening to the party.  I quickly went reactive instead of proactive to find a florist.  I immediately visualized my hood and pictured Lesher's. I quickly looked them up on Yelp and dialed fast. When they answered it was minutes after 5 and they were closed.  They won my vote right there answering a phone after hours.   I quickly asked when they closed and the young lady who answered informed me that they were closing now. I said, thanks and quickly told her my dilemma. She promptly asked me where I was and how quick I could get there. Wow, what customer service. I was calling from Fyler and Hampton and she said, hurry up I'll wait for you.   Quickly we drove up Hampton to their location and upon arrival were greeted pleasantly at the door. The young lady asked what we were hoping for and bust our buttons, they had a fresh delivery of Sunflowers that morning. She quickly took us to the cooler to show us what she had. She then recommended  a vase and curled willow branches to compliment what we selected.   As we stood in amazement, she whipped together a fabulous bouquet that blew our friends away at their businesses second anniversary celebration. This is why if I ever need flowers in the future, I will call Lesher's. In my eyes, they went beyond the call of duty.

I came to Copia for my second night out for Clayton Restaurant Week. To my surprise, it was not listed on Yelp. So as I sat at the bar, I added them as a new business. I miss, Morton's which use to be at this location, but Copia is a nice addition to the Clayton restaurant mix.   I'm pretty predictable when I go out. So it should be no surprise, I started out with a (Amaro) Manhattan. Copia is known for wine, but they made a very strong and refreshing cocktail. Thumbs-up!   To expand my experience, before starting my CRW meal, I ordered from their Happy Hour Menu. I choose the, Southwest Egg Roll. For $3 I was expecting 1 small egg roll, but I received two large egg rolls, sliced in half. They truly did have the spiciness of the Southwest. A craft beer would have been a better pairing, but they still were good with my Manhattan.   For my CRW dinner I choose; Caesar Salad, 8 oz Prime Rib and for dessert, Bread Pudding.    The Caesar Salad was good, it was a typical Caesar Salad. My entree, the prime rib was served with steamed broccoli and mashed yukon potatoes. The broccoli was steamed to the right texture, soft enough, but yet crisp enough for a snap. The potatoes were rich, creamy and smooth. My prime rib was tender, a regular knife was sufficient, there was no need for a steak knife. A nice touch from Copia was that their CRW menu offered a glass of red or white wine to accompany your meal in the price.   I was disappointed when the bartender told me they had sold out of the Bread Pudding and had to substitute.
