The brownie was served warm and was topped with a soft chocolate chip cookie and a side scoop of vanilla ice cream. It wasn't bread pudding, but it was a delicious sweet treat to finish the meal.   Even with the business of CRW and being a fairly new restaurant in Clayton, the service was friendly and attentive.   I'll be back? - Yes, I want to see what they do outside of CRW.   When: July 17, 2018 Why: New in Clayton and CRW Summer 2018

Is this place heaven or a warehouse store for booze? I absolutely drool from their selection of Vodka. How am I ever going to have enough time to try them all? Cucumber Martini was a refreshing summer treat.  To visit the beer selection pull out your passport, its a trip around the world in 80 brews. I love the fact that they separate by country, it makes the selection process so much easier. Got a holiday parties? Let Randall's help you stock-up the staff is helpful and they know booze. Their wine selections will make great hostess gifts.

Amigo Joe's Mexican has an American chicken place right next door. It's not your typical chicken, it's Pressure Cooked Fried Chicken. The seasoning is fairly good and the pieces are on the large side.   The meals come 2,3 & 4 pieces and include two sides and a biscuit. The biscuit was more of a dinner roll in my opinion. They offer eight different sides; corn, green beans, baked beans, vinegar & oil cole slaw, creamy sweet cole slaw, country mustard potato salad, creamy mayonnaise potato salad and mashed potatoes with brown or country gravy.  They don't hide the fact that some of the sides are Orval Kent products that are available from most major food distributors. After all, the containers are right in view in the glass door ice boxes.   The mashed potatoes were the best I've had from a fast fried chicken joint and I liked the fact that you can choose your gravy. Give me white gravy, I have never understood the brown gravy you get at KFC. Another bonus, for a couple more bucks you can name your pieces, I love my white meat and it's worth it for me.   It's close to home, so when I'm craving chicken I'll re-visit Amigo Joe's Chicken.

Poor customer service, the staff was too busy standing around and talking to each other, then assisting shoppers. I'm going to assume they were holiday help and not the regular staff.   I found what I needed, but could have probably bought more if someone would have approached me and done suggestive selling. (For every $50 you spent you got a $10 coupon)  You would think that they'd turn it up a notch for someone who is carrying a competitors bag from the other end of the mall.  Wouldn't you want to try to make that person a loyal customer to you?   When I went to check out the ladies at the register turned on the charm but, it was too late. They should have had them on the sales floor and those who just wanted to stand working the register.  It would have been nice to have gotten a $10 coupon, but they didn't deserve my $50.

Saint Louis, I am here to tell you some the best pasta entrees in the city are not on, "The Hill". More and more pasta cafes and Italian restaurants are popping up in different parts of our great city and are rising above and beyond "The Hill".   Stellina Pasta Cafe, is winning my heart with incredible salads and an ever changing offering of pasta dishes. I am a BIG fan of their "BIG" salad, which is so huge it can easily be shared by two diners.  It's a great mixture of Romaine lettuce and Spinach, that is mixed with; cucumber, red onion, carrots, turkey, ham, bacon, white cheddar and sunflower sprouts. It then is tossed with a house made sweet onion dressing and served with grilled bread. This in my opinion is the best salad in the city.   When visiting for lunch recently, in addition to a "Big" salad the SO and I shared an order of Semolina Fettuccine. An incredible dish with pancetta, shallots and spinach in a garlic cream sauce.  Again, we split the order and the portion was adequate for lunch.  Be sure to take note of the pictures I've posted here and you'll see why I am a fan.   We went for a late lunch and the place was still jumping. I think everyone else had the same idea. Our server Elizabeth was a pro. She was charming, knowledgeable and the perfect hostess to all the tables and she was serving about 8 (tables) of us at one time.   I am lucky and proud to have SPC in my hood. As Mr. Rogers use to say, "It's a good day in the neighborhood."

According to Webster's dictionary A-OK means, excellent, fine, in working order, ect. : a generalized term of commendation. So for me to say that my hometown airport is A-Ok is a good compliment.   Is the best airport I have flown in or out of? No, it is dated and needs a major face-lift to bring it up to the same level of other major cities. However, it is easy to navigate, TSA lines move quickly and it is kept clean. I do prefer the East Terminal over the Main Terminal, but that could be that I fly Southwest more often then other airlines.   When it is time to fly out of the Lou, Lambert is A-OK and that is a good thing. So go explore other cities and get Yelping.

Not only does Lesher's do incredible floral work, but their customer service is outstanding. They truly go beyond the call of duty. I recently needed flowers delivered to a friend who works from home and it required a little more details in the delivery. This friends schedule is sporadic, she is in and out of her home office often. I asked Lesher's to call and make sure she was home before delivering and they said that was no problem. Flowers were delivered to rave reviews from my friend.   Lesher's is on speed dial with my younger cousin who now lives in Little Rock, AR. As he started to reignite a relationship with a girlfriend here in Saint Louis he called his older Yelp cousin for a florist recommendation. He has now used them multiple times, stopped in to meet them when he was in town for a Blues game and is truly on first name basis with the staff. The joys of a Ma and Pa shop with good solid local roots. Oh, the girlfriend Kyndall has loved all the bouquets from Lesher's.   If you need flowers, use Lesher's.

Been there and ate there, now I can mark Don Carlos Restaurant off my Cherokee Street Bucket List. Like Christian K. I am going to meet Don half way on a good rating. Rarely do I forget what I ate at a restaurant, but this visit I had to review my pictures to refresh my memory. So glad I am a true Yelper and photograph all the food I eat out. I remembered the Margarita, Chips & Salsa, Guacamole and Flan, but could not recall my entree. Guess I wasn't that impressed.   We started out with regular Margarita's that did not skimp on the booze. I enjoyed the extremely coarse salt on the rim of my, "no salt" request. Seriously, I did like how they salted their rim. It was not the typical bar salt.   The chips here are not impressive, but the two salsas they serve with them makes up their lackluster. I favored the Smokey Chipolte over the Chili Arbol Salsa. We also had a side order of Guacamole which was huge. It had a unusual flavor that I could not pinpoint, but I think that may have been its winning vice.   The entree that I blocked out of my mind, was two tacos  and a side of refried beans.  I enjoyed a Chicken and Barbacoa Taco. Unlike George O., the Barbacoa did not blow my knickers off. It was good, but I favored my Chicken and wished I had tried the fish when I realized they grilled their fish. Grilled is so much better then fried.   We shared a slice of Flan for dessert and it would have their Abuelita rolling over in her grave knowing how they butchered an old family recipe.   The service was a tad on the slow side, but the Señorita was working the entire sidewalk cafe alone and was doing The Hustle the best she could.   We shop at Carniceria Latinos Americana, so I know we'll be back to enjoy  another Margarita and something else on their menu.

Love, it! Love, it!   I am so glad Craft Beer Cellar opened an additional location in South City. They made great use of an old car repair shop. The retail area is compact and well organized. They offer a good variety and it is all priced individually, or as a six-pack and case.   To be honest, what makes this location better then it's sister location in Clayton is the bar area. It's larger and offers more craft beers on draft. You can sit at the bar and chat with the bartender, or you can sit at one of the tables with a group of friends. There's no kitchen, but if you need something to munch as you sip a craft beer, they don't mind if you bring your own.   If your not sure what you want or you're wanting to try something new, talk with the sales professionals, they'll give you good guidance. The staff is friendly and are true lovers of craft beer.   A bonus - In the mornings, the bar area is a coffee shop - The Living Room.   I'll be back? - I'm confident I'll be a regular, here.   When: July 19, 2018 Why: Grand Opening Party

Great little boutique jewelry store. Love their sterling silver - hence "The Silver Lady". They have fantastic pieces at  a variety of price points.  The sales professionals are suggestive and not over bearing in their approach.   Recommend this place for any holiday or special occasion that deserves a gift.

Celebrating 15 years? Yemanja Brasil has been in STL for 15 years and I never been or heard of them. I must of been living under a rock. I am so glad The International  Supper Club introduced me to this fantastic little gem.   Being a Tuesday night, Brad was off work and able to attend this ISC. With a extra mouth of taste buds, I was able to experience more of the menu, then if I were attending alone. Trust me, we took total advantage of the opportunity doing a 3-2-3 experience.   We started out with three appetizers:   Marisco Buzios - Fresh Mussels. The mussels were fresh and steamed in a white wine seafood broth. The mussels were great, but the broth was on the watery side. I love a richer broth that I am eager to soak up with fresh bread.   Aipim Frito - Fried Yucca Root. Move over french fries, these things were the bomb. They were cut like big steak fries, sprinkled with Parmesan Cheese and served with a curry dipping sauce. I loved it and I don't like curry. Who knew a root could have so much flavor.   Ceviche do Sul - Seasoned Bay Scallops, shrimp, onion & cilantro in Tangy citrus tomato marinade, served chilled. Great way to start a meal, light and refreshing.   Next we had two entrees:  Bobo de Camarao - Jumbo Shrimp in a spicy yucca coconut cream sauce & rice. The shrimp truly were jumbo and prepared to perfection.  The sauce was just spicy enjoy to give it a flavorful kick.  I recommend this to any shrimp or seafood lover.   Espentinhos Gaucho - Charbroiled Sirloin Beef Kabobs, with Julian Vegetables and Rice. The Kabobs were grilled medium rare and seasoned just enough to allow the true flavor of the beef shine through. For a beef lover this is a good dish, but when I go back I'm ordering the Jumbo Shrimp again.   For a big finale, we ordered three desserts. We like going out with a Big Bang and these three set off fireworks.   Pudim Carioca - Flan. To die for, the best Flan I have ever had and I love Flan like Stephanie S. loves Bread Pudding. I highly recommend this, it is light, cool and refreshing.   Pudim de Coco - Coconut Bread Pudding in a rich Caramel Cream Sauce topped with coconut. Stephanie will love it! Bread Pudding, Caramel and coconut makes for a dreamy dessert.   Pavee da Nena - Brazilian Tiramisu. You like chocolate, you like this dish. It was rich, heavy and full of chocolate flavor for the chocoholic in all of us.   That completed our dinner with ISC and we were content.   The patio was a great venue for a large group of foodies. It was a cool night so it made for pleasant dining. Pleasant until it got closer to dusk and those feisty mosquito's wanted to start dining on us. Thank goodness our event was over and we were leaving.  When it was time to spilt the bill, they struggled. There has to be a better way to seperate a bill for a large group.

Shhhh.....we gotta keep this a secret. The Happy Hour, at Bartolino's Osteria, is top notch. They celebrate HH, 3-6 PM, every Monday thru Wednesday. On Thursday, they celebrate Happy Hour 3- Close in the bar and on the patio. Now that is how HH should be scheduled.   In addition to discounted adult beverages, they have a special bar menu offering super deals on a variety of finger foods. Some of the most popular are; Toasted Ravioli, Pizza Fries, Crab Cake, Lobster Rangoon, Mini Cheeseburger and a One Topping Pizza.   The bartenders are old school. They free-pour their creations, making them extra strong. Many of the patrons sitting around the bar are regulars. It's almost shades of Cheers. They all greet each other by name as they position themselves on a bar stool. Don't worry if you're not a regular, they're all extremely friendly and welcoming.   Will I return? - Yep, I love a good strong cocktail.   When: July 2, 2020 Why: HH - Out running errands and day drinking with a friend.

When I moved out of the big city of STL, one thing I knew I was going to miss was all of the speciality boutiques. As I learn my new hometown, those needs are being fulfilled by new discoveries.   I have always enjoyed buying my olive oils  and balsamics from small speciality shops. Especially, little mom and pop stores. Their personalized customer service always seems to go a step beyond. I find that to be true here at the, Olive Oil Marketplace.   Moving in a pandemic and cooking more at home while restaurants are shut down for eat-in, my inventory of olive oil was getting depleted fast. While I was shopping for furniture across the street, I noticed OOM as I returned to my car. Needing to stock up on olive oil, I popped inside and was pleasantly surprised. Their offerings were as extensive as some of my favorite boutiques in STL, so I felt at ease.    The sales associate working that day was extremely knowledgeable and helpful. She asked about my preferences and different things that I liked. She also offered me little samplings to assist me in making my decisions. I was immediately sold on the, Jalapeño Olive Oil. Her letting me sample and sharing her opinion on, Tunisian EVOO sold me. It was so smooth and it was organic, too. In addition to the two bottles of olive oil, I purchased some Italian Herb Balsamic. No kitchen is complete without a bottle of it.   While I was checking out, they signed me up for their rewards program. Which is a good thing, because I know I am going to be a regular. Good inventory and customer service is going to keep me coming back. To my surprise, you get a small free bottle on your birthday and since mine was just a day or two away, they honored it. I selected, Hickory Smoked Balsamic. Yum-Yum!   When: November 14, 2020 Why: Needed Olive Oil

This store is outdated and in serious need of a remodel, but it by far has the best customer service of any Schnucks I have ever shopped. The staff here still lives up to the old Schnucks motto, "The Friendliest Stores In Town". Every employee from the shelf stockers and the produce men to the cashiers and the baggers make sure your shopping experience is a good one. Seriously, this store should be used to train new hires in customer service.   Even though I am shopping here more, I still get confused in the aisle layout. That is where the stockers come in handy, they are always there to guide me to the correct aisle. The produce staff has gone the extra mile going to back and searched for items that were sold out on the floor. Once I am done cruising the aisles for my food and reach the check out, I am greeted by a friendly cashier who actually chats while they scan. The baggers even say more then, "paper or plastic" and actually know how to separate and bag items.   I also like the fact that they always have a sufficient amount of staffed check out counters open. I hate using those self checkouts, I want to  protect another persons job.  As I said in 2012, this location also has some great eye candy that makes the shopping for groceries enjoyable. If they'd remodel this store, it would be the bomb.

So glad someone stepped up and re-opened the old Hilltop. This neighborhood needs a good ole dive bar.  I stopped by for a quick lunch after making a shopping expedition out to Costco. It wasn't very busy, so I took a stool at the bar. I started out with a 5-Day IPA, a local craft beer from O'Fallon Brewery. As I sipped my beer, I checked to see if they have one of my hot buttons for sitting at the bar and they did. Underneath the bar, they offer hooks for jackets and purses and best of all outlets for us social media junkies to re-charge.   My decision for lunch was easy, a friend who had already been here told me how good the Sloppy Joe was. On the menu it is called; Beckerles Burger, it is loose ground beef, seasoned with a tomato sauce that has a tang on mustard and topped with white American Cheese. I actually enjoyed the flavor that the mustard added to this Sloppy Joe. They don't offer fries, their sandwiches come with a large serving of rippled potato chips.   Being here in winter, I didn't get to experience the patio. I asked the bartender what their plans are and he said they were still working things out. Hope the neighborhood allows them to have live bands, it's a perfect setting.  It also would be a nice place to go with your leashed dogs, but they already have signs posted, saying no dogs welcomed. Bummer.    I'll be back? - Sure, my friend lives in the hood.   When: January 24, 2019 Why: Lunch after Shopping

This Sonic is off the beaten path. It is tucked away in an area that resembles an industrial park for fast food restaurants. It sets so far off the main road, you could miss it if you did not know where to find it.   Work was over, I was headed home and the chocolate cravings begun to sneak up on me. I wanted a cool refreshing chocolate malt for the drive home. So veered off the main drag and into fast food lane, to satisfy my craving.   Pulling up to the Drive-Thru menu I was meet with instant disappointment. Sonic does not sell malts. I couldn't wait to get back into St Louis to stop at my neighborhood Steak-n-Shake, so I lowered my expectations and ordered a shake. It was chocolate, it was thick and creamy. It just lacked that malt flavoring I wanted oh so bad.   The drive-thru service was nice and pleasant. No scratchy speaker voice, it was crisp and clear. Was hoping to see a carhop on skates, but no such luck today. Perhaps another day when I craze one of those slushy icy drinks for the drive home.

I am so HAPPY. I am a true fan of Culver's and was thrilled when this new location opened closer to my home.  I'll still visit the one next to my Costco when I'm out shopping, but this one will now be my go to.   This location has a much nicer outdoor patio to enjoy your Butter Burger, Fries, Onion Rings or Concrete. The dining room has a fire place and a flat screen TV that was playing Culver's trivia questions while we dined. The staff as I have found at other Culver's are way friendly. No surly fast food servers here.   My favorite is and always will be a simple single Butter Burger with cheese. When dining with the SO, one of us gets fries and the other onion rings in our combo's and then we share. Culver's makes their own root beer and all I can says is, "bottoms up". It's that good.   If you want a burger fast, don't go to your typical fast food restaurant. Come here to Culver's and get a better quality burger for about the same price. I know with this new Culver's being closer to home, I'll have to turn my will power up a notch so I don't blow the diet.

Amigo Joe's was my second stop on National Margarita Day. I was driving by at lunchtime and thought to myself, I haven't been there in awhile, let's make this a Margarita stop. I quickly parked and went in.   They offered me a table, but I asked if I could sit at the bar. I took the end spot by the door and servers station and had a great time.   I didn't want a heavy lunch, so I just went with an order of Chicken Nachos. I always add jalapeños to my order. Johnathan my server asked if I wanted pickled or roasted.  What? I've never been offered an option before. I showed him a picture of my last order and he said those are the pickled. I then asked him, which did he recommend and he said, roasted. I said, "let's do it your, way". OMG, I'll never go back to pickled again. The fire roasted jalapeños made the nachos, so much better then the standard pickled.   He also, recommend the Ultimate Margarita. The ultimate is 50% tequila. Now that is the way to celebrate, NMD.   Great service, good food, affordable prices and damn good Margarita's.   Chances of returning? - It's in my hood and I eat and shop local.   When: February 22, 2019 Why: National Margarita Day

It was my friends and she love tequila. So selecting her gift was easy, I'll get her tequila. The only problem, I don't drink tequila the way she does. I only drink it in a Margarita. So I was going to need help.   Randall's is usually my go to for booze and since it was on the way to the party, I stopped by to get her gift. Being clueless, I stood in the tequila aisle totally confused. One of the sales associates came over and asked if I needed help. Lucky for me, he was a tequila drinker himself. He showed me several bottles and shared which ones he liked. I asked him about one that was in a gift tin and he pointed out its high rating. It had a 94 out of 100 from the Ultimate Wine Challenge. Best of all, it was on sale. My gift was the hit of the gift table.   Thanks, Randall's for making shopping for a birthday gift easy.   I'll be back? - Yes, I drink.   When: March 13, 2019 Why: Birthday Gift Shopping

I have had Old St Louis Chop Suey bookmarked on Yelp for a long time. So tonight, when I saw Jess P. check-in, I knew it was time to go. Knowing from other reviews, I stopped by my local ATM to get cash, since they are a cash only business.   When trying a new Chinese restaurant, I always start out with an Egg Roll and a small order of Crab Rangoon. These are the items I use as a foundation in judging the quality of food they serve. My Egg Roll was crisp, the inside ingredients were warm and the outside was a medium golden tone. I hate it when some places overcook the egg rolls, but this one was done just right. The Crab Rangoon was plump and the pockets were full of creamy crab sauce. They too, were deep fried perfectly. They had a light golden color, which was appealing to their presentation.   My main entree was an half order of, General Tso's Chicken. Half Order? It was enough for two meals, so I had it for lunch the next day. On their menu it is listed as hot & spicy, but I didn't think so. Don't get me wrong, it was good, but I would of liked a little more spice and heat to mine.   I was impressed with the cleanliness of the restaurant and how friendly and professional the counter staff was. I also thought it was kinda cool, that the entire staff was dressed alike and all were wearing American Flag baseball caps.   I have two other Chinese restaurants closer to my home, but when I have the craving in the future, I will make the drive to here. Yes, that's right, they impressed me that much. That I'll drive and extra mile or two to eat here.   Will I return? I gotta try the St Paul Sandwich, Beef & Broccoli and Fried Rice.   When: August 13, 2017 Why: Craving Chinese

This restaurant has absolutely no ambiance, but that is ok. Why is it, okay? You're not here for the decor, you're here for comfort food. Comfort food that is prepared in good ole homestyle fashion.   Being new to the area, I am on a constant search for a good breakfast place. Having breakfast out is one of my favorite things. I swung by Village Inn on the recommendation of a Chicago Yelper. Yes, a out-of-towner turned me on to a diner in my new neighborhood. She loved their pancakes and she's a pancake snob.   So, I went with one of their Wipe Board Specials. I choose, the Pancake Combo. It was a huge amount of food. Not only did I get two pancakes, I also enjoyed 2 eggs scrambled, 2 sausage links and 2 strips of bacon. Next time, I'm just going for the pancakes and a side of bacon. For me, it will be enough.  Service was attentive, my coffee cup was constantly warmed up. They were friendly and you could tell who the regulars were, they greeted them by name.   Will I return? - Good pancakes always bring me back.   When: November 3, 2020 Why: Breakfast

Disclaimer: I've never eaten here, but I have done a lot of carry-out.   I am totally in love with their Bartolino's Special Salad. I have loved this salad, since they were at the old location down Hampton Avenue. So it has been ordered as my entire meal for a night and as a salad to accompany a steak grilled in the backyard. I've called ahead and it is always waiting for me and living 5 minutes away, I have just driven up and ordered when I arrived.   It's basically a simple salad; lettuce, choice of turkey or salami (my favorite is turkey), tossed with provel cheese, pepperoncini, kalamatra olives, artichoke hearts and tomatoes in their famous house dressing. It never disappoints us.   3 Stars is a good rating for carry-out. If I enjoyed the salad in the actual restaurant, I'm sure it would be a 4 Star review.

I am slowly transitioning over to this Schnucks from the one on Hampton. Why? Customer service. The staff here is so much friendlier and professional. This location also seems to always have enough cashiers working, so the lines are not insanely long.   It has taken me awhile to adapt to the different lay-out. I'm now favoring the shorter aisles, that are cut in half with a center aisle dividing them in the middle of the store. Which means more end-caps to display those sale items and implies items we should all avoid.   I'm finding the same fresh produce,  quality meats and regular grocery items that I need and want. The frozen foods section is laid out and organized much better.  Plus, with the superior customer service, it is a no brainer to shop here over my previous favorite.   Hope they get a remodel soon. They deserve it.  Chances of returning: It's a work in progress When: January 17, 2019 Why: Grocery Shopping

An amazing bookstore that has been around since 2015 and it just recently appeared on my radar. It is off the beaten path and definitely on a road I do not travel, but that will not keep me from returning and supporting this local and family owned business.   So many of our privately owned bookstores are struggling right now, so we all need to reach out and give them as much support as we possibly can. EyeSeeMe, fortunately has a special niche in the market. It has an extensive inventory of books written for and supporting the children of our African American community. Through their success, they now provide and offer books for high school student and adults as well.   Today, I attended a virtual book reading co-sponsored by EyeSeeMe and was totally inspired. Before attending the event I shopped the store and picked up a couple of the books being read. Now that the event is over, I cannot wait to give them to a co-workers son. In fact, in the future, I will be doing a lot of gift shopping here for those hard to buy for friends on my list. It will be easy to find something for them here and it will be inspiring.   I cannot encourage you enough, please shop local and please support black owned businesses, too. It makes our community stronger.   When: February 20, 2021 Why: Virtual Book Reading Event

Seoul Taco in The Loop reminded me of some of the little carry out restaurants you'd find in the French Quarter down in New Orleans. Off the beaten path, small in size, no ambiance and basically a hole in the wall, but great cheap food.   I will admit this was not my choice place for lunch, but I am glad the SO persuaded me to spread my wings and expose my pallet  to new experiences. Reading the very small and limited menu, I selected a Gogi Bowl with Chicken.  It was served in a aluminum foil bowl that you normally see used for carry out. It added to the charm of Seoul Taco. It was filled with rice, fresh veggies, chicken, tossed with sesame oil, a dab of spicy gochujang pepper sauce and topped with a fried egg. It was very filling, full of flavor and that pepper sauce was damn hot. Oh, and the fried egg was fried better then some places that specialize in breakfast.   The SO went with tres tacos, 2 Bulgogi (steak) and only 1 Spicy Pork. He originally had one each and went back for the second steak taco, so I will assume that was the best.  We also shared a side of Kimchi Slaw which was flavorful and crunchy, but the serving size was not worth $2.   The staff was friendly and personable adding to the intimate environment that a small hole in the wall provides.    Just like The Trainwreck not serving their famous chicken wings until after 2:30 PM, here at Seoul Taco they only offer their Pot Sticker at dinner time. I swear they do that on purpose to get us to come back again. Well it works, I'll be back for the Pot Stickers soon.

On one of the walls in the dining room is a quote from, Craig Culver. It says, "People know quality when they taste it." I must agree with him and on my visit today, my ButterBurger tasted no different then a burger I'd get at the Golden Arches. So, today I am taking away a Star on my Yelp rating.   My guest and I were both craving a ButterBurger and could not believe our disappointment. Seriously, they were no different then the ones we'd get at other fast food chains. Our onion rings didn't seem to be the same either.   However, the crinkle fries and the Root Beer were still the same quality we remembered. I also, give a shout out to the staff. They were upbeat, cheerful and full of energy. I don't know if they were short staffed, but those working had some pep in their step and were getting things done at a quick pace.   I'm hoping the drop in burger quality is just a pandemic thing and not the way of the future. I'll be back or I'll stop by another Culver's in the near future to see how things improve.   When: September 1, 2021 Why: Needed a ButterBurger

I stopped by for lunch yesterday to check out the Hot Pastrami sandwich. Ian Froeb said it was a "must order" on his STL 100 list. As i waited for my food at the bar, my favorite place to be seated when dining alone. I checked out my previous review on Yelp. To my surprise, I hadn't done a review on my previous visit. So after I tell you how fabulous this lunch was, I'll highlight my previous meal.   Being seated at the bar, I felt obligated to order an alcoholic drink. Okay, I used it as an excuse to enjoy a Crispin Cider. Ashley my sever, was fantastic and she agreed with me that a Cider would be the perfect accompaniment to a pastrami sandwich.  The Hot Pastrami here at DITA, definitely is the gold standard for pastrami. Everything for this sandwich is made in house. So it, can't get any fresher then that. They take a pretzel bun, smear it with mustard mayo and then stuff it sauerkraut and pastrami.   For an additional $2.50 I was able to add a side dish, I choose a side salad. Oh, how I wanted fries, but I had them before and wanted something new and healthier. I was shocked to see that their salad was made with Boston Bibb lettuce and a dressing that was so good, I wanted to lick the bowl clean. The side salad along with the pastrami and ciderI - made a perfect lunch.  Highlights from my previous visit -   Bloody Mary - a salted rim, spicy and only available at brunch. Worthy of my BM List. Fried Pickles - Crisp pickle chips with a buttermilk ranch for dipping. Worthy of my FP List.  American Stuffed Grass Fed Cheeseburger - Single patty with house fries. 5 Stars Breakfast Sandwich - House made English Muffin with fried egg, white cheddar & house made sausage. Served with fried potatoes. This is what a breakfast sandwich was meant to be.   Death In The Afternoon is a great restaurant with a relaxing atmosphere. It has limited hours of operation being only open 11 AM till 3 PM. I highly recommend them for lunch, the staff is friendly and professional. They also hustle, making it easy for those who work downtown to dine and get back to work within a reasonable amount of time.   When: June 13, 2016 & previous date Why: Lunch & Brunch

Attended the Opening Day Festivities and I'm so glad I did. The staff and hometown man of the hour, Danny Meyer, nailed it. I am sure there were a few bumps along the way, but for my experience it was spot on.   As expected, the line was out the door and down West Pine. I arrived about 45 minutes before opening and the line was already about 40 burger fans deep. While we waited, at various times the staff would  come out lead us in cheers and run down the line giving those waiting a "high-five". They also passed out samples of lemonade and cups of hot chocolate. As if that were not enough, those in line were also given; Shake Shack Texting Gloves and a Shake Shack Lollipop.   Menus were passed up and down the line, to make things faster once you arrived at the counter. I had already checked things out on the web and knew what I wanted. My meal was a Double Cheese ShackBurger, with a side of Fries and a vanilla concrete with Pecan Pie from Pie Oh My.   The burger was kick ass. It was totally an upscale diner burger. Flat, grilled fried with crisp edges. Being raised on a beef farm, I appreciate the 100% Angus beef. It may have upset the PETA protesters outside, but it made my taste-buds and tummy very happy. The lettuce, tomato and ShackSauce was all it needed to make it a complete.   I am a huge fan of crinkle cut fries. I know it doesn't really effect the flavor, but the crinkles make it easter for dipping in ketchup. Today, mine were crispy, crunchy and just enough salt. Another thing that is one of my hot buttons, is ketchup served in little cups. Thank-you, SS for making me a happy french fry dipping man.   The concrete with a local pie makers, Pecan Pie blended in to vanilla custard will have me spending an extra half hour at the gym. It was totally worth it. I love me some Pie Oh My and when it's blended with custard, life just gets better.   The staff was extremely cheerful and helpful. You could feel their excitement of opening day. Most impressive was Danny Meyer, he was mingling with the guest and thanking them for coming out on opening day. I am glad Shake Shack has finally come to STL. It's going to be a great addition to the CWE mix of restaurants.   Will I return? - Burgers this good, you know I will be back.   When: December 11, 2017 Why: Opening Day

5 Stars and Beyond! My experience truly was magnificent.   This past Sunday, I went to enjoy their new, Butcher & Baker Special (Only available on Sunday). It totally blew me away. I enjoyed a Seasonal Salad, 12 oz Prime Rib, Two Sides (Soy Glazed Brussels Sprouts and Sam's Mashed Potatoes) and a Warm Apple Crostata with Vanilla Ice Cream. All of this delicious food was only $45. WOW! I had enough leftovers for a light lunch the next day.  My pictures speak pretty much for themselves, but I'll give you a few quick comments. The salad was bigger then I imagined and was tossed in a light house dressing. My Prime Rib was a perfect medium rare and oh, so flavorful. The portions of the veggies were insane, two folks could have easily shared, that is why I had leftovers for the next day lunch. I loved how the mashed potatoes, had the skins visible. (That is how I make them at home.) They were so rich with butter and fluffy. The Soy Glazed Brussels Sprouts, out of this world delicious. The older I get, the more I love Brussels Sprouts and these blew me away.   The meal ended with a Warm Apple Crostata with house made vanilla ice cream on top. I admit, my pic is a little off due to lighting, but it was the perfect finale.   Of course, the cocktails I enjoyed were masterfully prepared by Michale and his service at the bar is always professional and charming.  I'll be back? - Yes, I want to try the Salmon Wellington  When: September 9, 2018 Why: Butcher & Baker Sunday Special

I'm almost embarrassed to admit the previous time I was here was December 13, 2013. I was treated to the Chef Grand Tasting Menu with Wine Pairings as a Christmas gift. I raved and raved about my meal and the wine pairings to all my foodie friends and family. Now as I sit down to write an updated review about my fantastic lunch, I realize I never wrote an original review. Oh, well they're still a 5 Star winner. Ian Froeb had them listed as his #8 on the STL 100 for 2016.   This past week I was doing a stay-cation, so I decided to treat myself to some of the better restaurant in STL. I thought of coming here and doing one of their tasting menus again, but opted for a lunch instead. Every once in awhile we, need to treat ourselves and I did with this white linen lunch. I also figured I needed a treat for surviving this election season and voting this morning.   When I arrived, I told the hostess I'd be happy sitting at the bar since I did not want to tie up a table for just one person. She informed me they had a table for me and that a large group was taking up the entire bar area. It was nice having a little deuce, all to myself. I could of sat at the bar, but the table of 12 next to it were kind of rowdy.   My favorite seafood is Sea Scallops, so I couldn't resist ordering them as my entree. Prior to the scallops, I enjoyed a Romaine Salad. It was chopped, tossed in Bleu Cheese dressing with tomato and bacon. It was the perfect lead in to my favorite seafood. The scallops were served with; pomme purée, vegetables and a light sauce. The menu stated you could have extra vegetables for an additional $4. That is an nice offering for the big eaters.   When my entree arrived, the sea scallops were huge and perfectly pan seared. For me the amount of vegetables were the perfect amount along with the pomp puree. The vegetables were a mix of peas, carrots and mushroom caps.  I had a glass of Pinot Grigio with my salad and scallops and they served an amazing house made bread that was so good it could also been a dessert.   Service was top notch from the hostess to my server. I promise not to wait three years for my next return meal.   When: November 8, 2016 Why: Stay-cation and end of the election season

I've just completed a "Triple Crown". I can now say, "I've eaten at all three of The Shack restaurants." It is a pretty cool accomplishment for me, but the the major accomplishment is for, The Shack. After eating at the three locations, I can say they are consistently the same. All three of them offer excellent customer service and delightful breakfast dishes.   Arriving this morning and informing the hostess, that I was dining alone, she quickly informed me that the bar and open and I could seat myself there. I was more then happy to do that. At The Frontenac location, I boldly walk pass the hostess and aways sit myself at the bar. Being new to this location, I wanted to follow protocol. The bar here is huge and rectangular in shape. It's a great place for single diners and couples to chow down on their hearty breakfast.   Instead of a cup of black coffee this morning, I choose to go with an Adult Swim beverage. These are their signature drinks that get back at the dog that bit you. I choose, The Dude Abides. It's a refreshing mix of vodka, kahlua, milk and iced coffee. This may be my new favorite. My usual always was the White Trash Screwdriver. Either one is a great way to start the day.   For breakfast, I was a good boy and selected from the, "Healthy(er) Habits section of the menu. I choose, Brussels 'N Eggs. It's a skillet filled with egg whites (I choose to keep my yolks), onions, green and red pepper, turkey sausage. I had my eggs prepared scrambled, so all the other ingredients blended together well. (with Brussels in the name, I wish there were more in the dish) They then top it with fresh shredded parmesan and bruschetta mix. It was served with a side of fresh fruit. Today it was two of my favorites; Strawberries and Blueberries.   The serving sizes here are hearty. I like how Niki S. described it, "It's comfort diner food with flair." So if you are in need of a hearty breakfast, stop by any of the three, The Shack and you'll feel like you just sat down to Grandma's kitchen table.   Will I return? - If I need breakfast in Chesterfield  When: January 2, 2018 Why: Breakfast

Absolutely, Marvelous!  Totally worthy of being my 700th Yelp Review.   Like Aimee, I am embarrassed that it took me so long to get here. However, I must say it is better late then never. I also owe an apology to Cleveland-Heath for things I have said in the past about restaurants that do not take reservations. In the past I have said, no food is worth waiting for, which translated into I wouldn't eat at a restaurant that did not take reservations. We got here early enough that there was no wait, but after this incredible feast, I will be happy to wait on my future visits.  We started our Saturday Brunch with the CH Bloody Mary which has my favorite vodka, Tito's. They make their own mix, which makes this Bloody Mary one of the best I have had and I know Bloody Mary's, see my list. They serve it with a little beer chaser, gotta love that.   So much good food, how can we try it all? We couldn't, but we gave it a good try, enjoying all of the following:  Foie Gras Short Stack - Breakfast of Champions (seared foie) Kale Salad - The Parmesan chips and lemon vinaigrette made it sensational Mac-n-Cheese - Creamy Sharp Cheddar, made it #1 in my book Cheeseburger - The best I've had since moving off the farm. True grass feed beef. Quail Alla Plan aha - I don't eat wild game, but the DP (dining partner) raved.  Old Fashion Cherry Pie - Sinfully good, I hated that I was sharing.   The entire experience was friendly, from the hostess, to our waiter and the other guest around us. We all were having a good time, enjoying fantastic cuisine.   I'm coming back. I don't mind the drive and next time if I have to wait, I wont mind that either.

Let me start out saying, I enjoy Six Row Brewing Company Beer. I really like their Whale, but my experience here was not acceptable.  It all began with our entrance and how we were greeted. We did not hear, "Hi, welcome to Six Row Brewing Company" or anything similar. Instead the bartender said, "seat yourself, we'll get at you soon".  Okay, I do not mind seating myself, but welcoming me before barking an order to seat myself would been more personable.  Now I know they were extremely busy, they had three people at the bar and two others seated at a table, so we understood why it took 5 minuets to come over to our table. Which gave us time to find two menus laying on another table and begin to decide what we wanted to eat.  Very limited menu and it really isn't a typical pub food.  When the bartender came over to take our order, we asked what she would recommend and what was her favorite. She would only tell us what was popular, which isn't a rousing endorsement when you are not willing to tell what you like.  I love pastrami and when I asked where theirs came from, she replied "I don't know".  I refrained from asking her go check, figuring it might stress her out. We then asked to give us a moment to decide what we wanted.   As she returned to the bar, we made the decision to leave.  We excused ourselves, saying thank-you but we wanted something different. All we heard was, "okay". I must expect to much, I can deal with "okay", but let's add, "hope to see you again". We may have not stayed today, but at least tempt us to come back.   We went to The Scottish Arms and enjoyed a couple Whales on draft a great meal and incredible service.

I hadn't been to Frank & Helen's for years and I do mean years. Then the other day, I saw one of my good Yelp friends checked in on their smart phone and it brought back memories of the broasted chicken and the fabulous creamy garlic house salad dressing. So when I got off work Sunday, I knew I wanted to a traditional Sunday night chicken dinner.   We arrived about 6:00 PM and the dining was half full or half empty which ever view to take. Either way, it didn't stay that way long. In a New York minute, it was packed.  As we waited for our waitress, we glanced over the menu and watched other tables be served their pizzas and the famous broasted chicken. I giggled as I looked around, the place hadn't changed since my last visit. Oh, did I mention my last visit was in the late 1980's? Yes, it had been that long and trust me it still looked the same. The same tacky plain Jane ambiance, but you don't come here for ambiance you come for comfort food.   The Creamy Garlic house dressing was as good and amazing as I remembered. As I've aged, I do not like my salads made with only Iceberg lettuce, but when Frank & Helen's house dressing is drizzled on top all Iceberg is okay.   What is so cool about ordering chicken here, is they let select various combinations in your half chicken. I went with the traditional mix, but the BF loves thighs and went with the three thighs. My side was Steak Fries and the BF with with Mashed Potatoes with Chicken gravy. The mashed taters were awesome, you could tell they were truly made from scratch. The steak fries could of been a little crispier, but I always enjoy a big meaty fry over a crinkle cut.   As an appetizer we stayed with the chicken theme and choose chicken wings in their Original Spicy. They were tangy, but I found them to be a little too greasy or too much sauce. I'd skip their wings and try something else.   The service was a team effort. Since they got slammed with a full restaurant very quickly, everyone was helping and making sure things continued to run smooth in the dinning room.   I'll be going back to try the pizza.

We know that MBMC has good doctors, surgeons, nurses and support staff. We wouldn't expect anything less. After all they are part of the BJC Health Care.   I want to sing their praises as a visitor.  My recent experience was as the SO waiting  for a surgery to completed. Once we had all the necessary paperwork and pre-op stuff completed, I was given a pager as if I were at a restaurant waiting for a table.  When the surgery was completed, they'd beep me. The supportive volunteers, explained how long it would be and where I could go within the facility to kill time.  Of course being early morning I asked for directions to the cafeteria.   Upon my arrival at the Mayfield's Cafeteria, I was impressed with variety of items to choose from for breakfast. At first I noticed the buffet offering; bacon, sausage, scrambled eggs and a country favorite Biscuits and Gravy.  They also, offered much healthier options, such as oatmeal, cereal and fresh fruits. However, I saw a small line forming in front of a little man and discovered he was working a omelet bar.   This omelet bar located in a hospital cafeteria could compete with one for a Brunch in a high end restaurant. They offered a huge selection of savory ingredients and cheese to make yourself a most flavorful omelet. The man working the bar, was a true master of his craft. He cooked the eggs to perfection and his showmanship of flipping his finished masterpiece was impressive.    Also while being a "visitor in waiting", I had the opportunity to shop their gift shop. It was so impressive, I thought I was in a Gold Crown Hallmark store. If you forgot a get well card, gift or a treat for your sick friend, this shop had it all.  What is an added bonus, is the shop is managed by the hospital auxiliary, ran by volunteers and all profits go to programs benefiting patients & advanced medical care.  Good to know your $'s go to a good cause.   However, the real treat is a Starbuck's Coffee Cart at the west entrance.  Where you can get your typical espresso drinks and caffeine fix.   MBMC not only takes care of its patients, but it takes care of the visitors as well.

It's Dairy Queen. It's Fan Food, not Fast Food.   These previous 1 Star reviews are old and really not fair. As I stated, it's a Dairy Queen. I was hungry after work and after hearing a DQ commercial on the radio about their Cheeseburgers on sale 2 for $4, I was sold. I didn't need anything else, I had a drink already and wanted no fries.  My burgers were prepared fresh and fairly fast. They were pretty tasty. For me they had the exact amount of ketchup, mustard and pickles. My burgers even had the perfect amount of onions and the cheese was melted over the entire beef patty.   The dining room and lobby was clean and the kitchen area that was in my view was also clean. Best of all, they have a large flat screen in the dining room and the night I stopped by they had the Stanley Cup playoffs on with Blues fans watching.   This  DQ is close to my entrance on to 255 which is my route home. It's so convenient, I am sure I will be back. I think the next time it will be for a Blizzard.   I'll be back? - Before I hit the road home after work.   When: June 9, 2019 Why: Cheeseburgers on Sale

I'll be honest, Doc's is not my typical type of bar. However, I am glad I went out of my comfort zone and gave them a try. When I use to commute to my work in Alton from St. Louis, I always passed Doc's and they always seemed to have a good crowd. Now that I have moved to Godfrey to make my work commute shorter, I thought it time to give them a try.   When I entered the main entrance, I was surprised to see that there were two separate businesses. To the left, was a dinning room and to the right a bar. Due to the current pandemic, I entered the bar and took a stool at the end of the bar.   I immediately was greeted by the bartender (not wearing mask). I ordered a beer and she offered me a menu. WOW, I could not believe how extensive it was. To my surprise, there was no wings and that is what I was craving. When I went to order the onion rings, I mentioned I really wanted wings. The bartender, apologized and gave me a menu exclusively for wings. How cool is that, a menu just for wings.   I am a wing junkie. I love going to a bar and just having a cold beer or two and an order of wings. I prefer my wings not to be breaded and that is how Doc's serves them up. Better yet, I get to choose how many I want (10,15, 20 or 25) and 15 different flavors. This is something that you typically do not find at a sports bar.   My usual go to flavors for wings are Lemon Pepper or Garlic Parmesan. However, today I was thrown a curve ball. As I read down the list of flavors, the last one took my breath away. It was, Pineapple Jalapeño. If you've read my reviews, you know I love jalapeños, so I had to give these a try. They were even tagged, a House Favorite.   The wings were good sized and meaty. They are served them up with equal portions of flats and drums. I liked the flavor, but personally would have liked more jalapeño kick to it. It was a nice touch that they gave me a empty pizza pan to stack my bones. I'm looking forward to coming back and trying the Garlic Parmesan and the Medium and the Blackened.   Service was good, I just wish the staff were wearing mask.   When: January 14, 2021 Why: Lunch - Wings

Once again, our Yelp International Supper Club introduced me to a restaurant that I may have missed out on experiencing. This time, ISC showed me a restaurant that gave me some true Jalapeño love. I not only enjoyed a Jalapeño Margarita, but my Diablo Fajitas were also highlighted by Jalapeños.  For a Jalapeño lover, this was a double win.  Being a dieter at this time of year, I only sampled a taste of the chips and salsa and I will tell you it took all my well power not to devour the entire basket of chip and dish of salsa. Also, one of my co-diners shared her guacamole and I cursed her for doing so. Again, it was too good for someone who is avoiding temptation.   My Diablo Fajitas were absolutely perfect. The mix of grilled steak, chicken, onion, jalapeños, and red peppers made a perfect entree. I choose corn tortillas over the traditional floor and only used one of them. The tortilla was excellent, but dieting, I just enjoyed the perfectly seasoned meat and vegetables alone. Their Jalapeño Margarita was a perfect drink to sip and enjoy slowly with this spicy entree. To my surprise and delight, I didn't have heartburn later that night.   The service was excellent, our waiter was very attentive for our large group. He kept up with all our special request and didn't flinch when we asked for separate tickets. He was a true champion, considering he had two other tables similar to ours at the same time.   It's a nice touch to have a strolling minstrel who serenades the diners. When he approached our table and asked for request, my "Roar" by Katy Perry was responded with.....I don't know that one. Luckily Juan was dining with us and was able to request a song in Spanish and the gentleman strummed his guitar and sang beautifully.   I'll be back for another Mexican dinner and again, I am so thankful to ISC for introducing to another International restaurant in our great city of St. Louis.   When: February 16, 2016 Why: International Supper Club

First visit and I was impressed. My dining partners were, too. We were a group of five celebrating the 34th anniversary of my 29th birthday. It was an early lunch and we choose to sit at a couple of high tops in the bar area. It soon became obvious, that it was a popular lunch location as the bar and the other tables filled up fast.   Once we were seated, I shared my Yelp research with my friends and cousins. I told them the Fried Brussels Sprouts were on point and that they were also known for the Sweet Potato Tots. I must of been a good salesman, because we ordered both of them as our appetizers.   All five of us raved about the Fried Brussels Sprouts. They were crispy and tossed in a red wine agrodolce. Then topped with both bacon bits and walnuts. I am not a fan of walnuts and I was even impressed with the flavor they added to the sprouts.   They offered the tots in a small and large serving. We opted for the small, since we had sprouts and each of us would be having an entree. Small? It was still an ample serving for five adults to share. The tots were crisp on the outside and the inside was warm, soft and creamy. Being Sweet Potato, they were a nice twist to the regular tot.  My entree as the Birthday Prince, was Smoke on the Water. It's listed on the menu as an appetizer, but I enjoyed it as an entree. It's dry rubbed and smoked chicken thighs. They were served on top of coleslaw and topped with white BBQ sauce. Absolutely delicious. I ate about two-thirds and took the other 1/3 home for a snack later.   Two of the other guest enjoyed the, Wild Mushroom Flatbread and both of them cleaned their plates. The guest who ordered the Pulled Pork Sliders, enjoyed them, but after one, she pulled the meat out and left the buns. As I did with thighs, she really liked the seasoning and dressing on the coleslaw.   The final diner celebrating my b-day, is a burger man and really liked his, Petite Foundry Burger with Fries. He's a big athletic type guy and couldn't imagine someone eating the full version as he was stuffed eating a petite.   His burger had everything. It was made with house ground chuck and topped with bleu cheese steak butter, balsamic onions, cheddar cheese, bacon, bib lettuce, pickles and tomato. What more could you want on your burger. He claims his fries were crisp and a perfect side.   Prior to this lunch, I did some shopping on Main St and still arrived early. While I waited for everyone else, I enjoyed one of their signature cocktails. It was the, Brown Sugar Old Fashioned. Being a regular drinker of Old Fashions, I truly enjoyed this flavorful twist on this classic cocktail. Side note - something I always check for and luckily they had them and that is, Hooks Under the Bar. Jackets or Purses, these hooks always come in handy.   Service at the bar and our table was friendly and attentive. We're a crazy group when we get together and our server played along with our silliness.   I'll be back? - For, sure. It was a fun experience and good food.   When: November 13, 2019 Why: Birthday Lunch with Cousins & Friends

Sometimes when a place becomes a favorite or one of your go to restaurants, you forget about doing updates on your review. Bartolino's Osteria is one such place for me. Since my last review, I have dined in the restaurant several times for lunch and have continued to order their amazing Bartolino's Special Salad as a carry-out.   Most recently, I dined with a co-worker while attending a seminar across the street at the Holiday Inn. When we broke for lunch, he wanted to go to one of the fast food burger joints. I persuaded him to join me at BO, since they had a $10 lunch special. He knew immediately that he'd easily spend that at Hardee's or Wendy's.  My co-worker once he read the opted for a Steak Sandwich over the $10 lunch special. He's a meat and potato man and enjoyed the 8 oz breaded strip sirloin broiled and topped with sautéed green peppers and onions served on a toasted garlic cheese bread. I was surprised that he selected cole slaw over fries as his side dish, but said both of them were excellent. He was so impressed with our lunch and the ambiance, that he's thinking of bringing his wife back for a Valentine's Day dinner.   It should be no surprise to you that for lunch I had the Barolino's Special Salad. I just can't stop myself from ordering that huge bowl of lettuce with turkey (you can also select Salami), provel cheese, pepperoncini, kalamata olives, artichoke hearts and tomatoes tossed in their house dressing. It is truly one of the most Sensational Salads in the city, I love it.   The service is always top notch with attentive servers and assistants. With an extremely attentive staff, glasses were kept full and empty dishes removed promptly. I've got to come for a Happy Hour and dinner soon, so I can experience their entire offerings.   When: January 20, 2016 Why: Business Lunch

When I told friends I was going to Rosie's they polietly told me, "you know that is a dive bar".  Like that was going to stop me. I told them I was aware of the "type" of bar I was going to and as long as they had vodka things would be A-OK.  The drinks are cheap and the bartender gives a healthy pour. So it is real easy to get your buzz on. The decor is simple; bar, stools, high top tables and a juke box.   It is a true neighborhood bar, with a good cast of regular drinkers. It was fun to watch as each new arrival entered the dive. There would be waves , handshakes and hugs from the other drinkers. A true "Cheers" bar, "Where everyone knows your name". Which is a good thing, because I think some drinkers there might need a little reminder of who they are before the night was over.   When visiting Rosie's just beware, you may run into someone you know and just like Vegas, what happens at Rosie's stays at Rosie's.

A Kolache is better then any biscuit or McMuffin from any fast food place.   Their freshly baked pastries are stuffed with a variety of hearty ingredients making them a perfect breakfast or light lunch.   Get there early for the freshest, and keep in mind they close at 2 p m.   Wish they were closer, but they're an extra treat when we are in the Brentwood area.

Bolyard's is where you will find a true butcher. A man who knows his meats and how to cut them. This is how I remember a butcher shop when I was growing up. You'd only see a minimum variety of meats in the case. Why? Personalized service and selection. You tell the butcher, how thick you'd like the steak or chop to be cut and he'd custom cut it just for you. He'd even cut up the chicken on the spot.   The prices are higher then you'll see at your local grocer, but the quality of meat you are getting is well worth the extra dollars. I highly recommend Bolyard's for a single person, couple or empty nesters to buy their meats. However, this may not be the place for a family to buy its everyday meats.  You ever have a recipe that calls for lard and you wonder, where in the hell am I going to find lard? You'll find it here for the low price of $8. You'll also find house-made seasonal ketchup, beef jerky and a pig ear for the dog.   I'm going back for bacon and whenever I need a good piece of meat for a special occasion.  I'm a meat man and a meat man knows the finest meats are found at Bolyard's.

Hacienda is what it is and you either love it or hate it.  It may not the best Tex - Mex in the city, but it is the most consistent. So many of the other Tex-Mex places in the Lou have become hit or miss recently and when I come to Hacienda I know what I am getting.   I enjoy their Margaritas and always favor the Top Shelf with no salt on the rim. Their chips are not the best plain, but with some Chile Con Queso or Guacamole, they can be jazzed up. I wish they'd change the salsa they bring to the tables with the one you can get at the chips bar in the bar area. The other salsa in thicker and has more flavor.   When dining here, I do not venture off the path very much. I stay with what I know is good and that is the "wet" burrito and a combination plate that I create myself.  A combo plate with a taco, burrito and an enchilada is always satisfying.   The servers here are always cheerful and make my time at Hacienda enjoyable.  I'll be back, because as I stated above, I know they'll be consistent.

I was shocked when I found out a friend had never eaten at Cleveland-Heath. Since we were coming over to E-ville for the Gingham Buffalo holiday open house, I thought it was the perfect opportunity to correct this dining out mistake.   My regular spot at the bar was open and my friend didn't mind eating at the bar, so we perched ourselves upon a couple of stools. A Saturday Brunch is not complete without a Bloody Mary, especially one with a Stag beer chaser. Their house mix is just spicy enough, to give it a little extra kick.   To assist my friend in ordering her entree, I showed her pictures I have taken and a few from other Yelpers. She finally decided on the BLT Sandwich with a Kale Side Salad. It was huge, she took half of it home for dinner. If I didn't know better, I would have sworn there was a pound of bacon on that sandwich. She absolutely loved the kale salad, she devoured it entirely.   Having been raised on an Illinois farm, I had to go with the Biscuits & Gravy. How could I go wrong with biscuits, breakfast sausage gravy, a side of bacon and two sunny side up eggs. It was a perfect hearty breakfast for a local farmer, or an urban man who use to be a farmer.   The gravy was creamy and peppery, the way I like it. For me a milk breakfast gravy can never have enough black pepper. The bacon was crisp and my eggs were done a little over sunny, the way I like'm.   The staff is always bright and cheerful. I love how they interact with all the patrons,  it gives the restaurant a real neighborly feel. They even make us STL diners, feel part of the regular hood. I got a giggle when the bartender remembered me sitting in the same space to celebrate my 60th birthday.   I'll be back? - I can't stay away  When: November 3, 2018 Why: Sharing my love of C&H with a friend

Let's Party!  Simply said, Party City is the place to go for party supplies. They literally have it all. You'll find every color imaginable, special occasions and themed party supplies at affordable prices. It's also a great place to go for balloons, greeting cards and gift bags. I may not shop here often, but when I need certain party supplies, this is the place to go.  What ever you're celebrating, Party City can help you celebrate it in style.   I'll be back? - When it's party time.   When - April 23, 2018 Why - Party goodies

I'm going to be honest - if it were not for Ian Froeb putting Lona's Lil Eats on his STL 100 List for 2016, I would have never came here. Asian Fusion and vegetarian is not the type of food that are picked up on my food radar. I am so glad, I decided to eat my way through Ian's list. I've learned a valuable lesson in food and have fallen in love with the wraps at Lona's.   After enjoying a Lemongrass Turkey Wrap here, I question those who eat at Subway and Jimmy Johns. Why would you want all that starchy, carb filled bread? Here you get a rice paper thin wrap around your ingredients, that allows you to actually enjoy the flavors wrapped up inside. My wrap was stuffed to the max with; pulled turkey, jasmine rice and  lemongrass pesto wrapped in a giant rice paper. As a side, I enjoyed a serving of fried rice. It was way better then a bag of chips you'd get at a deli.  The size of the wrap was overwhelming. I couldn't eat it all and brought half home. They were kind enough to give me an eco-friendly container to bring my left-overs home. The associate, politely told me, that the texture might be different later when I ate it. It was fine, no complaints here - it made for a light and filling dinner.   Will I return? Yes, I'll definitely be back. I've learned my lesson well. My food radar will now pick-up on Asian Fusion and Vegetarian foods.   When: November 15, 2016 Why: Ian Froeb's STL 100 List

I love this store. I bought several holiday gifts here. What gave me a chuckle this year is, I received many gifts from here as well. I've talked so much about how cool this store is and the unique selection of home furnishings, that my family finally listened and shopped local for me this year.   The store is beautifully merchandised. Having worked a number of years in retail and home furnishing, I can honestly say this is a top-notch store. Others in reviews have commented that the prices are on the high side. I take the other road and say they are extremely reasonable. Many of the items are unique, but others that I have found at a competitors store are less expensive here at GB.   The staff is always available for questions and when the owners are present, they are totally approachable as well. In fact, they are eager to assist all the shoppers. They make shopping at GB a fun & pleasant experience.   Will I return - I stop by overtime I'm in Edwardsville  When: August 31, November 8, 2017 Why: I'm a Shop-a-holic

The menu selections are few, but the sandwiches are big in flavor. I choose the Sloppy Joe and it was the best Sloppy Joe I have ever had. It was topped with my favorite cheese, Pepper Jack and pickled Brussels Sprouts/Kale. I would have never thought of pickling brussels sprouts, let alone putting them on top of a sandwich. Wow - they really added to the flavor of this Joe.   Your sandwich comes with your choice of chip or drink. It was a beautiful day, so I choose chips and added a Schlafly beer to my order. I enjoyed my sandwich outside on one of their picnic tables, creating the perfect ambiance.   This was Bolyard's first time making Ian Froeb's STL 100 List and it is well deserved. They may only serve sandwiches, but they are top notch. Stop by and experience the deliciousness of Bolyard's.   Well I return? Yes.   When: March 8, 2017 Why: Lunch - Ian Froeb's STL 100 2017

I hope most people are not as stupid as I was. For twenty years I have driven down Manchester, past K Hall Designs and thought it was a company that did interior design or some type of marketing. Silly me, I've lost 20 years of shopping that I can never get back.   On the day I shopped, I was out running errands with a friend while my boy dog was having a dental cleaning at the vet. As we drove down Manchester she asked me if I ever been there and pointed to K Hall. I responded, "It's a store?" When she told me yes, I immediately turned around so we could go check it out. I was totally flabbergasted. It was such a cool store.   At first when I entered, I was impressed with the variety and selection of the Soy Candles. If I was not already overstocked on candles at home, I would have bought at least two if not more. Good scents and reasonably prices.   As I browsed, I was happy to see that the shop was not just for the ladies, they had small sections for men and K-9's too. I'll definitely have them on my list for gift shopping in the future.   My biggest delight was finding a large iron easel that I needed for a display on my mantel. I had found one through mail-order, but the price was astronomical. The one I found at K Hall was half the price and excellent quality. I was also thrilled to find a box of Stainless Steel Straws. I try to be eco-friendly and I want to save the turtles, too. These will be perfect for drinking on the patio this spring and summer.   The young lady working was very friendly and attentive without being overbearing while I shopped. I am so glad my friend educated me on K Hall, actually be a store. I hope to never make the same assumption, again.   When: March 5, 2021 Why: Shopping!

Warning: You will not see Jack, Janet or Chrissy sitting at the bar and Jack will not be working the kitchen. This is a hometown sports bar that is all about cold craft beer and good pub food.   It's a great place to gather with friends, or as in my case cousins. The variety of beers is vast and it is always served in a frosted glass.   They serve up some better then average pub food. Their burgers are thick and juicy and the variety of pizzas available can put some pizza restaurants to shame.   If you are in the Alton or Godfrey area and want a bar to have a fun time with your friends or family, I highly recommend the Regal Beagle.

This store just amazes me every time I shop here. What impresses me most is the fact that it is privately owned. The merchandise is top of the line and they also have some unique and original gift ideas.  Best of all, when I do shop here, I am shopping local.   In addition to having every kitchen gadget, gizmo and cookware that you could possibly want, CS also offers fresh coffee and loose leaf tea. If you are in need of a snack, they've got you covered as well with their gourmet popcorn. They offer so many flavors, I can never leave with a couple junior sized bags of some of my favorite flavors. My most recent visit, I finally tried their in house made fudge. OMG - the Orange Dream won me over & I'm not a fan of fudge. It truly tasted like a orange sherbet and vanilla twist cone.    The customer service here is also top notch. The entire staff is friendly and extremely helpful. Be ware of the ladies in the popcorn area, they like to offer samplings, which can lead to you buying more bags of the delicious and freshly popped snack.   I wish they were closer to my home, but it is probably a good thing they aren't for my bank account.   I'll be back? - When in E-ville.   When: November 3 & 7, 2018 Why: Christmas Shopping

It's a McDonald's. We're in a pandemic and they're short staffed. So I gave them a break, the rating really should have been a 2 Star.   First impressions, last a long time. My first vision was unprofessional signage duck taped to the marque menu and a rude order taker over the intercom. Let me first say, I have not been to a McDonald's in over a year. So when I pulled up to the speaker, I was shocked to not be greeted with a greeting promoting a menu item or a simple, Welcome to McDonald's. Instead, I simply heard, "you can order when ever you're ready." As, I was looking for what I wanted on the large menu, I heard, "Aren't you ready to order?"  It had  not been that long of time, but I quickly, ordered a Double Cheeseburger and a small french fry.   Pulling forward to the payment window and then the actual delivery window, those associates had good customer service skills and that is why I bumped them up to the three stars. As I was at the delivery window, I could see the young lady taking orders and her same sour personality was still being spewed over the intercom.   My Double Cheeseburger, hit the spot and satisfied my hunger. The fries were crisp and hot. However, they had an unusual flavor. The unusual flavor is on me, since I am not your typical fast food diner. I was just pleased, they were fresh and hot.   With a closed lobby and only one drive-thru lane open, I will also give them a shout out for moving the long line of cars quickly.   When: October 23, 2021 Why: Hungry after doing shopping errands

Santino's is a blend of Olive Garden and Outback Steakhouse with white linen table cloths and napkins. The decor is old school Italian restaurant, which kinda gives an upscale feel, without the price point on the menu. I'll tell you up front, you get what you pay for.   Since I moved back to the Alton area and started to re-connect with friends of the past, many of them sang the praises of Santino's. Since I was hearing so many great things, I thought I'd give them a try. I actually gave them two tries. Once for lunch and once for dinner, just too fair. In all honesty, if a friend or family member wanted to go, I'd tag along, but I don't think I will be returning on my own. I was not that impressed. It reminded me of the Pasta House in the 80's.   Let's break it down:   Booze: Lunch - Manhattan - They had to find someone on staff who could make one. It was okay. I should of known when the bar area was closed off to guest.   Dinner - Pinot Grigio - I went wine to be safe. This time I was sitting at the bar and realized each server is their own bartender.   Salad:   Lunch - Romaine lettuce and a decent Caesar dressing and the breadsticks with olive oil is a winner.   Dinner - House Salad with House Dressing was a total loser. It was bag iceberg lettuce and the dressing was comparable to Wishbone Italian. Again, breadsticks and olive oil was a winner.   Pasta:   Lunch - Tortellini Carbonara. Cheese stuffed Tortellini with onion and bacon in a creamy Alfredo sauce. Bacon is always a bonus. Menu did not mention mushrooms or sun-dried tomatoes in the description. I am fine with both, but what if someone had allergies?   Dinner - Farfalle. I was craving, Tutto Mare and this was the closest thing on the menu. It was bow tie pasta served with; shrimp, scallops, sound-dried tomatoes and artichoke hearts sautéed in a light vodka sauce. The seafood was prepared well and there were 4 large shrimp and 3 large scallops in my serving. I like artichokes, in fact I keep a jar in my refrigerator. However, they dominated the pasta dish, which made them a little over-powering. The vodka sauce was no different the one I buy at the store to make Sloppy Joe's at home.   Service:  Lunch: Friendly and attentive. The young lady was hustling, they were packed and obviously short handed. Normally, I like to sit at the bar since I dine alone, but I was told that area was closed off due to the shortage of staff.   Dinner: Seated at bar with other single diners and one couple. No bartender, our service was discombobulated. We did receive attentive attention, but it was from all different people. It was like it took a village to serve a customer.  That's how I see, it.   When & Why: Lunch - August 20 and Dinner - October 8, 2021

If you go to, The Golden Hoosier expecting to find a bar similar to, Southtown Pub that use to occupy the space, you'll be disappointed. The two are no where close to each other. Southtown is where, hoosiers hung out and The Golden Hoosier is a classy drinking bar making a play on the word, hoosier.   If you are from St. Louis, you know that the word Hoosier has a totally different meaning in our city. In St. Louis, Missouri, the word is used in a derogatory fashion similar to "hick" or "white trash". Then the word, golden in American English, is used to say that someone is in a very good situation and is likely to be successful. So I enjoy the creative way that they brought the two words together to create a strong positive image.   This review is based on a Happy Hour and it's a strong 3.5 Stars. I've been wanting a half star from Yelp since, I started writing these reviews and this is one time, I really need one. It's so close to a four, but still needs to work out some kinks to get there.   Let's talk about some of the positive things that I really liked, that other places miss. Huge shout out for using, paper straws. Save the turtles and the environment. Hooks Under the Bar - great place for the ladies to secure purses or for everyone to hang a jacket. Gender Neutral Restroom, the door locks, we can all share. Guys, just be sure to put the seat back down for the lady who follows you. Little details like these, make them a step above of the others.   Now I'll sing the praises of what I love most, Cocktails. I loved the special cocktail menu for, Happy Hour that included one of my favorites, Old Fashioned. It was so good, I wished, Don Draper was sharing one with me. It was HH, so I also tried a couple of my other favorite cocktails. First I tried a, Dirty Martini and then a Rye Black Manhattan. The Dirty was made with my favorite vodka, Tito's and the Black Manhattan was so good, it almost brought tears to this grown man. My BFF, enjoyed the Blackberry Collins so much, she had two.   Our food was not really that impressive. It was good, but they need to get some kinks worked out in the kitchen. It's still early, so I'll definitely be back to give them another shot. My Superman Potato with Steak was acceptable, but it was not a true Superman. They may want to research and see what a real Superman Potato is suppose too look like. I do give them credit, my steak was overdone and they did re-grill it for me. My friend enjoyed the Wedge Salad and could not finish it, so it was a plentiful serving.   We wanted to try the wings, but the bartender could not describe them to my liking. He was not really sure, but thought they were prepared as an entire wing and not separated into flats and little drums. Now that I have seen pics of the Tandoori Wings posted after my visit, I'll return to give them a try. I also want to try the Pork Steak, it has proven itself to be very photogenic.   Their beer taps offer a good variety of "local" craft beers and a classic local AB product, Busch as well. I like that they offer the Draft Busch and a shot of Four Roses Bourbon as a Happy Hour special. Cheers!   The inside decor reminds me a private gentleman's hunting club. Some may be offended by the abundance of taxidermy, but I say, get over it.  It's just a decor theme that makes for a unique and relaxing atmosphere. The outside patio is what we all want our own patios to look like. It would be where all our friends and family would want to hang-out on week-ends.   The Golden Hoosier is an impressive replacement for Southtown Pub and I am looking forward to re-visiting soon. If I still lived in STL, I would have already re-visited.   When: June 24, 2021 Why: Scoping out the new trendy and hot spot in South City.

We all ready knww that Bolyard's offers great meat and sandwiches, but did you know about their Saturday morning breakfast? If not, let me tell you've got to check it out.   It's a simple Saturday morning breakfast. If you've ever ordered a dinner from them on Tuesday or Thursday night and gotten their unbelievable biscuits to accompany your entree, you know how delicious they are. On Saturday morning, they've kicked it up a notch, they've taken their "golden gems" and smothered them in house made sausage gravy. If you're not a Biscuit and Gravy lover like me, they also offer a breakfast sandwich that changes weekly. The description can be found on their social media.   I'm so in love with their biscuits, they make this ole farm boy actually miss the farm. The gravy is beyond what any farmers wife or the farmer himself could create.
