It was full of big chunks of pork sausage and perfect consistency of a milk gravy. It was not to runny and not to thick. It was perfect. I would have loved two, but one big biscuit was a very filling breakfast. Next week, I'll be trying one of the sandwiches.   If you want a coffee with your biscuit, they have a craft from, The Living Room which is right next door. Or, you can do what I did and visit the LR first and bring your our coffee over to Bolyard's. They don't mind.   So now you know, Bolyard's is not only your butcher and place for lunch sandwiches. It is also your place for breakfast on Saturday's only.   I'll be back? - I now have three reasons to return.   When: December 14, 2019 Why: Biscuits and Gravy for Breakfast

I had no idea we had such a great popcorn place in the Lou. As I approached The Kitchen Sink, I was overcome with the aroma of freshly popped corn. I then saw the sign boosting the daily special, "Kettle Corn with Sea Salt". I was immediately sold and knew I had to have some to take home after enjoying lunch.   Like its' neighbor, Harrison's Popcorn lacks ambiance. However, the customer service  is personable and true mom & pop. As Dennis W. pointed out it is a walk up, the small area you stand in to place your order through a window is no bigger then a handicapped  public bathroom stall. Once you place your order, it is passed out to you as if you are at a drive-up window at a fast food restaurant.   As we placed our order, the BF was complaining that he was old and should get a senior discount. Mr. Harrison told him he wasn't old and the BF replied he'd be 50 in two weeks. After some bantering back and forth and I'll show you mine if you show me yours (photo ID/DL) they realized they were not only the same age, but shared a birthday and year as well.   My Kettle Corn was fantastic and I am a hard judge of KC. Our second bag was Caramel Toffee and it was good enough to be a dessert. We were amazed at the number of pecans mixed in with the rich caramel coating. If they make these two this great, I will be back to try the Loop Trolley Mix which is Cheddar Cheese and Caramel Mix. I will not longer need to order the Chicago Mix from Garrett's in Chicago.   In the future when I create gift baskets with local foodie goodies, you can be assured a bag of Harrison's Popcorn will be front and center.

When: February 15 Why:    Lunch   We can't wait to go back so we can give them their fifth star. The ambiance, chips & salsa, Margaritas, and the food were all excellent.  However, the customer service was totally lacking.  I can only assume that the Valentine diners the night before exhausted the staff and the wind was totally taken out of their sails. Our service was basically; "what do you want" and "here it is". I know they can do better.   This was kinda our VD celebration, Brad had to work cooking for all the romantic couples at his place of employment. So it is always fun to go out and have others do all the preparing.   We started out with Blood Orange and Milagro Margaritas. The Blood Orange will be my Margarita of choice when dining at Milagro, it goes down so smooth. I'll just have to watch my quantities.    The chips and salsa were a great lead in to a fantastic lunch. As many Yelpers have stated in many Mexican reviews, you can judge how the food will be by the salsa & chips and here they are top notch.   We begun our feast with Tuna Ceviche and Traditional Quesadillas. Both were excellent, I loved the Tuna and raw fish is not my thing. It totally won me over. The Quesadillas filled with Mexican truffles, wild mushrooms and Chihuahua cheese, oozed with flavor.  We then experienced the Beef Enchiladas Rojas and Street Tacos.  On the Street Tacos we tried the Barbacoa Beef and Cochinita Pibil. Both were good, but the Cochinita Pibil (pulled pork) would take the gold medal. It's flavors were more pleasing to the palate.   The finale was the Tres Leches Cupcake, which I will never share again. It was so good and it's sauce was one of my favorite fruits Raspberries. Who knew a traditional yellow cake could be so good.   I/we will be back soon, I 'm a fan.

Shaved Duck, you just kissed a star goodbye. I am beginning to think that maybe lunch is not for you. Perhaps you need to just focus on Happy Hour and Dinner.  The reason I think lunch is not for you is because the last three times we've come in to experience your fabulous St Louis Style Spare Ribs  they're not available.  WTF, do you realize how disappointing that is. Once we were so disappointed, we walked out and took our business else were. Today however, we stayed and enjoyed your Beef Brisket.   Since we didn't get to have a full rack of ribs, we started out with some of your Smoked Chicken Wings. They were slow smoked to perfection and the dry rub flavoring is enough for me. However, I will say the mango, ginger, habanero sauce that comes on the side is your best sauce.   We both ordered the Beef Brisket Sandwich, one with Home Fries and the other with Man - N - Cheese. Holy Mackerel, Batman that is the best MNC in the city and the only way to improve those Home Fries would be to "Smoother" them.   Our waiter was friendly and attentive. He even listened to pissy rant about not being able to get our ribs. I am sure once we get to have the STL Spare Ribs, you'll get your other star back.

Attending a private party at Smashburger was a blast! I enjoyed my food so much, I couldn't go home to my SO empty handed. I ordered an Ultimate Cheeseburger, Smash Fries and a Gooey Butter Cake Shake to go.    The staff that made our party so special, was equally as nice when preparing my to go order. They truly provide service with a smile.   Being a city dweller, I was concerned about the long drive back into the city with a carry out order. No problem, it was still warm and the shake was awesome.  Actually I was hoping to get the shake, but no such luck. For once the SO's sweet tooth was as sweet as mine.   As the SO devoured the burger & fries, they received rave reviews just as I raved about the ones at the party. We both talked about wanting to revisit Smashburger but dreaded the long drive to St. Charles. To our surprise, we learned a new one is opening in Chesterfield very soon and that drive we can deal with.   Five Guys, Smashburger has you beat.

Sometimes, "a man's gotta do what a man's gotta do". For me, that was pulling into one of those quick oil change places and letting them do the dirty work. Now don't think for a New York minute, that I normally change my own oil. I haven't done that since the 1980's. Why I stopped doing it myself, is a story that can only be told over cocktails.   Normally I am on top of things and get mine changed regularly at my dealership. However, somehow this summer, I became somewhat discombobulated and totally forgot to change my oil. I was out running errands and happened to glance up to the oil change sticker on my windshield. I freaked out when I realized I was over by three months or 5,000 miles.   In my eyes, I had no time to lose. I immediately pulled in to my neighborhood VIOC and got it taken care of. The pit crew here was friendly, professional and did not hard sell me for upgrades. They were informative with their sales pitch, but did not overly push. They had me in and out in under a half hour.   I'd recommend this quick oil change establishment to those who use them and if I ever need quick last minute service again, I definitely will come here.   When: August 30, 2016 Why: Oil Change, of course

Hello, Andy! You're a chain, but you may be my new BCF (Best Custard Friend).   I really try to shop/eat local and am a big supporter of Missouri Made, but your custard made my taste buds do a very energetic happy dance. It was nice to see that you offer your rich and creamy custard in both vanilla and chocolate, unlike our hometown favorite which only offers vanilla.   Your small is smaller then the regular at TD's, but it is the perfect portion for a sweet treat. On our recent visit, we enjoyed two concretes. My choice of blended treat was Reese's Pieces. However, my friend had the best of our two. He went with, Key Lime Pie. I enjoyed my favorite candy blended in my vanilla custard, but his vanilla custard blended with a sweet-tart pie with graham cracker crust, definitely won the blue ribbon.   As we stood at the window to place our order, we could smell the aroma of brownies being baked fresh on site. The staff was personable and the service was fast. With the large windows you can see a pristine kitchen and two large machines churning out the fresh custard.   I can walk to Ted, but when the custard craving hits, I'll be driving to Andy.

I am so glad that Three Dog Bakery moved to a new location at Town & Country Crossing. The new end space down from Whole Foods is fantastic. You can not miss it when you enter or leave the center. When you shop for yourself at WF, be sure to stop in here at TDB to pick up a treat or two or three for your favorite four legged friend.   My Fur-Babies love the little mini bone biscuits that I buy in bulk. I also always treat them to several goodies from the case. This visit they got some Sweet Potato Cookies dipped in a vanilla icing, Peanut Mutter Cookies and Dottie Spots Cookie. They also got a quart of Strawberry Creme Wafers. These pretty red cookies, were so tempting that I couldn't resist. Yes, I took a bite of one and so did the SO. I wouldn't want to sit down and enjoy a couple with a glass of milk, but I now know why my dogs go crazy for them.   The staff here is always friendly. It amazes me how they always remember me and ask specific questions about my dogs. I think next time I am just going to make a special Three Dog Bakery trip to west county and bring the Fur-Babies so they can see where all their tasty treats come from.

Tommy, The Pinball Wizard would be in heaven here at OBL. In fact, I would not be surprised if he were a silent partner.   OPL is all about pinball. The tables in their booths are old pinball tables. The artwork on the wall are pinball tables and then they have a room full of Pinball tables you can play. Now you can understand why Tommy would love this place.   In addition to pinball, they have three Skee Ball Machines that are only 25¢. I know nowhere else where you can go and humiliate yourself in front of friends for only a quarter. The pinball machines range in playtime from 25¢ - 50¢. So bring a sock full of quarters or roll of quarters and have some fun. If you forget, don't worry they have a machine that will gladly give quarters.   If pinball, Skee ball are not your thing, they have classic box games available to play as well. These are the ones I saw: Battleship, Connect Four, Boxing Robots, Checkers and Trivial Pursuit Cards on the bar. Let the games begin.   The bartenders are awesome,  they are so friendly and add to the fun. They pour a good vodka. The beer selection for buckets is a throw back to my college days of PBR and Stag. It is hard to believe those use to be beer of choice. (Yes, I am that old)   If you come to Orbit Pinball Lounge and do not have fun, it is on you.

If Professor Harold Hill in the Music Man sang about the trouble in River City, I can only imagine what he'd sing about Bourbon Street. It is a street that has everything, except a Christian Science Reading Room. If it does, I didn't find it. What I did find, is a good time being had by all.   Bars that have live entertainment open their doors so the music spills out into the street. Giving birth to the phrase, dancing in the streets. If the neighboring bar has a live band too, the music just gets louder and louder. It almost becomes a battle of bands competition.   At any given moment, a small parade will appear and march down the street. It disappears almost as quickly as it appeared. Then there's the street musician and performers who will keep you mesmerized with their talents.   If you get the munchies while partying on Bourbon Street, don't worry. There'll be plenty of slices of pizza, fried chicken, oysters and other quick bites to keep you going. Also, there is no need to worry about booze, you can get a drink everywhere.   My only warning, is watch your step. There are partiers out there who just can't hold their liquor and toss their cookies onto the sidewalks of fun-filled Bourbon Street.   Bourbon Street is a must see for everyone visiting the French Quarter. To be honest, it isn't as decadent as the media makes it out to be.   When: August 26-29, 2016 Why: I had to get away

Do you remember Rizzo's on Chippewa? This is the same Rizzo's and the pizza is fantastic.   I visited for an early lunch and ordered the 10" Cheese pizza and House Salad for $6.95. I added two toppings sausage and jalapenos for $1 each. The crust is a cross between traditional St. Louis thin crust and a hand tossed pizza. The tomato sauce has a rich Italian zing and the cheese is a blend of mozzarella & provel. My toppings of choice were sausage and jalapenos. Why I said jalapenos when I was ordering is beyond me. Some how it just came out of my mouth and I am glad it did. The jalapenos were pickled and added a major kick to the sausage, making my lunch pizza totally flavorful and memorable.   The salad was most likely the best salad I have experienced from a pizza parlor. It was a good mix of romaine and iceberg lettuce with onion. They then tossed it with three cheeses; Pimento, Provel (a St. Louis favorite) and Parmesan. What impressed me the most, the ingredients are chopped in pieces that are actually bite size. I hate it when you start enjoying a salad and the pieces need to cut like a steak.   The ambiance is mom & pop charming. The front dining area is tables covered in traditional red & white checkered tablecloths with cafe chairs. They can accommodate 20 inside and also have the "party room" for groups of 10. If weather is permitting, they also have outdoor seating.  The artwork shows you the history of the building, taking you back to when it was actually a gas station.   It is not in my hood, but it is close enough to call in an order and go pick it up. With that being said, I will be back.

This little piggy went to Salume Beddu and went, yum yum yum all the way home. Seriously, I can walk to Salume Beddu and have never gone until the other day. Now I am kicking myself, wondering why it took me so long.   On my first visit I purchased;  Berkshire Cured Bacon, Salametti and Croccantini. I will now review each item individually below.  Berkshire Bacon - It is simply the best bacon I have ever had period. I am a farm boy and I know bacon. We had it for breakfast and I held some slices back for my lunch. I added it to a smoked turkey, coby jack cheese sandwich on Parsley Dill Rosemary Bread from Hampton Bakery.  I would have gladly paid for my own creation at deli it was that damn good.  Salametti -  An old ad campaign once said, "everything is good on a Ritz". That may be true, but with this salametti just give me a glass of wine, a block of colby jack cheese and I'll be content. Sure a Ritz would be good, but let savor the flavor of salametti.   Croccantini - Do Not Buy! I repeat, Do Not Buy!  You want the reason why? If you don't buy it, that means there will be more for ME.  These cracker thin treats are as addicting as Billy Goat Potato Chips. They are so simple, they're only made of flour, water and spices. Three ingratiates and they are damn good. Heavy on the pepper, but I am a Pepper Boy and I do not mean Dr. Pepper.   If you haven't been to SB - stop reading Yelp and go now. Before going. please check store hours.  Thank-You.

Oh, Happy Day! I could  not be happier. I finally have a quality BBQ restaurant within a mile from my house. When I'm craving ribs or brisket, it will now only be a short drive to some of the most tender brisket and fall off the bone ribs in the city.   We couldn't resist having dinner on opening day. We went hog wild and ordered a full rack of ribs and brisket. As stated earlier, the ribs were fall off the bone tender. They were done in a dry rub, that provided enough spice and flavor that neither of us used any of the BBQ sauces. The brisket was shredded and tender. The brisket, I did use sauce. I preferred the medium which had a sweet tang. My dining partner liked the hot, which had a spicier twist.   Out sides were Mac-n-Cheese and Baked Beans. When I took I first saw the Mac-n-Cheese, I instantly feel in love. It was so obvious it was baked, by it crispy topping, it reminded me of the M-n-C my favorite Aunt use to make for family potlucks. The beans at first sight, had me worried, they looked like Van de Kamps baked beans. However, once I took my first bite the spices won me over. The sauce was a little runny, I normally like a thicker sauce for my baked beans, but the flavorful seasoning had me won over to this thinner sauce.   My only concern with having such a fantastic BBQ joint close to home, is that I may get burned out. I'm not going to give that a second thought, I'll never let that happen. I will have Andre's in my rotation of favorite restaurants and will enjoy every bite.

Great service without the attitude. This is a top notch hair salon, that provides great cuts, and from I have observed fantastic color and highlights.  I love the fact that my stylist actually runs on time, my experience  with other salons, is that you have to wait almost as long as you do at a doctor's office - but not here.  Everyone is friendly and greets you as you walk through the salon.  Another review commented on the noise, I actually love the hustle and bustle - it adds to the atmosphere and conversation. A bonus of coming here is I get to shop at Crate & Barrel before or after my cut - like I need an excuse to shop...lol.

Another great meal at Mathew's Kitchen, I am so glad they are in my neighborhood.  One entree has inspired me to create a new list promoting Fish - N- Chips and MK will be holding the top spot.   After having a ruff day at work and both arriving home to tired to cook we headed over to MK. We've only been here a couple times since it opened, but the staff is doing a great job of remembering those of us who already are repeat customers. It truly shows that they want to be a neighborhood restaurant.   We took one of our regular tables in the bar, we like the cozy feeling it has over the dining room itself. Also, you'd be amazed at the variety of beers and call brand liquors they offer for a restaurant.  Even though they have a great selection, tonight we both went with the house Pinot Grigio. Which made a great complement to our Fish - N- Chips and Lobster Mac - N - Cheese.   The LMNC is a huge portion of rich creamy cheese (white) coated pasta with a whole lobster tail split in half and served in its shell. I managed to clean my plate, but honestly two people could have shared it or I should have saved half for my lunch the next day.  Trying to use my best table manners, I struggled to remove the lobster from it's shell. In the future I'll ask them to remove the shell in the kitchen so I do not look like a duffer.   Brad had the Fish - N- Chips which were served with  a vinaigrette cole slaw and some very yummy thick cut steak fries.  The piece of fish was huge and the breading is what made it stand out from other FNC's. Their breading was like a corn flake coating that was seasoned well. It gave a crisp coating and the fish inside was still flakey.   On my return visit I will be torn between ordering the Fish - N- Chips or finally trying the Meatloaf which I have heard from Non-Yelpers (if there could be such a thing) is pretty awesome. I hear Farmhaus may have someone giving them a run for best Meatloaf. However, if it is a Wednesday I will have to try the Fried Chicken.

I did not need Ian Froeb's STL 100 list to tell me that Milagro is one of the best restaurants in ST. Louis. However, I did need it to remind me that I needed to update my review. When you become a regular, you are so comfortable checking in and ordering your favorite cocktails and food, that doing an update on your review totally slips your mind. Or it could be the fact that you enjoyed one too many Top Shelf Margarita's and just forgot to do the update.    I slipped into Milagro Modern Mexican on a Saturday night, it was early so the dinner crowd was just starting to arrive. Dining alone, I opted to sit at the bar so I wouldn't tie up a table. Actually, unless I'm with a group larger then three, I prefer sitting at the bar. It's very relaxing and your service is still very attentive.   As always, the first words out of mouth are, "I'll have a Top Shelf Margarita with no salt on the rim, please." Their top shelf cocktail is made with their very own, Maestro Dobel Tequila and shaken with dry curaçao. When the bartenders are making two at once, it is as if they are playing you a song with maracas. The sound of two Margarita's being shaken is so soothing.   In his list, Ian said the "Must Order" here at Milagro is the; Classic Funded. A hearty portion of Chihuahua Cheese baked in a cast iron skillet with homemade Chorizo & blackened chile. They serve it with a couple of flour tortillas that you can rip and smear or tear and fill with your fork. I enjoyed one of the tortillas, but I preferred dipping aka scooping with their chips. The Classic Fundido, is unique and different, but I still prefer the Queso Con Chorizo. They both have the house made Chorizo Sausage, so it's a win either way.   When I went to order my entree, I even surprised myself with what came out of my mouth. I didn't order any of my usual favorites; Baja Fish Tacos, Steak Fajita or Beef Brisket. I said, "Grilled Vegetable Burrito". What? I'm not a vegetarian, I love me some meat and fish. My subconscious must have been trying to tell me something and I listened. When the HUGE burrito arrived and I had taken several bites, I joked with the bartender that this burrito could possibly convert me to the dark side.   It was a whole wheat tortilla, stuffed with' chayote squash, corn, cilantro rice, black beans, jalapeños, cilantro peptic pesto and topped with chile guajillo sauce.  The mix of the squash, black beans and jalapeños is what pulled me closer to that dark side. Oh, so delicious. Meat eaters should not be afraid to order this vegetarian delight.   Service is always top notch, just like the cocktails and food. If you're craving Mexican and want to kick it up a notch or two, head over to Milagro Modern Mexican. If they're only two of you dining, sit at the bar and have a fun time.   When: April 23, 2016 Why: Dinner and STL 100 List

Arrived at The Boulevard early and had time to kill before Crate & Barrel opened, what a perfect opportunity to finally check out Nadoz Cafe.  I didn't have breakfast before I left home earlier to drop the Fur-Babies off for their holiday grooming, so a coffee and pastry was calling my name.   As I entered NC, I was impressed how crisp, clean and inviting the cafe was. I also was impressed to see they use Chauvin Coffee which I consider  the best local roaster for their coffee. They not only use it for their brew, but they offer bags of the beans so you can have gourmet style coffee at home.   I ordered a Gingerbread Grandee Latte and one of their Cinnamon Rolls. Having been a Barista for over five years, I was not impressed with the length of time it took to make a simple drink. There was only one person ahead of me line and had gotten her drink and left. Finally as I stood there waiting a girl asked me if I was the Gingerbread Latte, and I replied "yes". She then had me totally repeat my order, and what type of milk I wanted. I had no problem with repeating my order, but you'd think by repeating it to the Barista who was making it, you'd get the right drink. Not in this situation, she made me a Cappuccino. As a Cappuccino, she did a great job, but I wanted a Latte. I drank it just the same and enjoyed it along side my Gooey Cinnamon Roll.  Good friendly customer service, allowed me to overlook the minor error.   However, what I found weird about this visit was the Men's restroom. Upon my arrival I went to use the facility and when I entered there was a young man cleaning himself at the basin and mirror.  He had a large duffel bag on the floor and told me to come on in that there was plenty of room. I thought okay, but when I went to enter the stall he had his coat and clothes hanging on the hook. I backed out, and again he told me it was OK. Not in my book, I'm not using a public restroom with someone else clothes hanging in it. I left and went back out to place my order and enjoy my breakfast.   After finishing my Cappuccino and Cinnamon Roll, I thought for sure he'd be done and gone so I could use the facility. I was wrong. When I entered the second time, he had less clothes on then he did earlier. I felt like I was at an airport or major train station when you see travelers cleaning up between connecting flights or trains. I just left and went to C&B.   I know you are thinking, why didn't I say something to the staff. Normally I would have, but I had seen male employees going in and out of the restroom and that is why I thought he was gone. Evidently a man cleaning himself in a public restroom at a cafe didn't bother them. This was just weird.   I will be back to experience lunch, in January after my haircut at Mitchell James.

We drove a little further to get lunch the other day and I am glad we did. It was my first visit to Sweetie Pie's and for the life of me I can figure out why it took me so long to get here. Let me first comment on the "ladies" of Sweetie Pie's, they are amazing, so friendly and down home. They make you feel as if you are dining at your favorite Aunt or grandma's house. I had the fried chicken wings and two sides. Don't know where they get their chickens , but I think they are on steroids. The wings were huge, biggest wings I've ever seen. My sides were Mac-n-Cheese, which reminded  me of my favorite Aunt's and Green Beans that were equal to my Grandma's.  The servings were so down-home plentiful, I had lunch for the next day.  I'm going back and on my next visit, I'm dining in so I can experience the true experience of Sweetie Pie's.

Love this park! If Forest Park didn't have a Zoo, Muny, History Museum and a 1904 Worlds Fair connection they'd be equal.   It's a great place for a "stroll through the park" with a romantic connection or "walking your best friend" (dog). The city does a great job on keeping the parks landscaping looking picture perfect.   As mentioned by Pamela R. the pavilions rent cheap and are great for a large group party or family reunion. I've attended many birthday, graduation and work parties under one of these pavilions and each one was a blast.  I bet you are wondering why I gave TGP only 3 stars. Let me tell you.  Twice now, when I have been at a party under one of their pavilions a park ranger has come around to tell us they are locking the bathrooms. What? They are telling us this between 4-5PM, just when the party is kicking into high gear and the beer is flowing. This is a bummer, it is like they are telling us our party is over. Can't they leave them open to at least dusk? What is a girl to do? A boy can be adventurous and risk the chance of being arrested for indecent exposure.  Besides them locking up the restrooms early, TGP is a great jewel in the crown of Saint Louis.

This place came to my rescue, so I'm a fan. I had visited several shoe stores looking for shoelaces to replace a pair in one of my favorite work shoes. None of them had the type I needed. How can  a shoe store sell you a shoe with laces and not have the replacement laces when you need them? Finally a sales clerk at one of the stores I visited referred me to Hampton Shoe Repair. (That was excellent customer service.) What a shock, the store is in my neighborhood and I never thought of going there. I was pleased with the selection of laces, and they had the exact one I needed for my shoes. I was also amazed at the selection of work boots. I don't need the boots for work, but they look great with jeans and flannel when you are going for that outdoorsy look.  After reading Kelly B's review I'm taking a pair of loafers in for a sole-lift.

Brown Bag Bistro, you're simply delicious. I will admit, I am sort of a snob and prefer table service over ordering at the counter. However, your friendly cashiers made it such an enjoyable ordering experience. They created a casual conversation and I didn't even feel like I was ordering. Next thing I knew, I had a table marker and was heading back to my table.   When dining at a sandwich shoppe, my go to is either a Pastrami on Rye or a traditional Reuben. If a deli/sandwich shoppe can master these two, they've got my patronage. BBB won my support with their Sammy Roo. Sammy Roo is a fancy creative name for a Reuben. Plain and simple, it was, Yummy! Their sliced corned beef, was topped with Gruyere Swiss, a sauerkraut mix with special house Reuben sauce is all stuffed between two slices of grilled marble rye bread. The bread was grilled perfectly, it still had a firmness and crunch. So many Reuben's get soaked from all the sauerkraut and sauce, but not here.   My cousin who was one of my dining partners got the Rosie Roo. The menu claims it's Sammy's Mrs. It was a Reuben made with turkey, sharp cheddar, a coleslaw mix with a house Reuben sauce served on the same Marble Rye bread. We didn't share bites, but she said it was amazingly good and I take her word.   My cuz had a friend join us. Well to be truthful, I heard where they were going for lunch and I was the luncheon crasher. Any way, her friend had the Bistro Club. It was huge, how anyone could get their mouth open wide enough to take a bite would surprise me. It was made with the typical club ingredients, all stacked inside a Ciabatta Sandwich Roll.  What set this Club Sammie above others was the roll and their house cranberry aioli.   They have a variety of "Bistro Beginnings", which I am sure will be extremely popular once they start having live bands on the outdoor patio. Being a fan of pretzels, I had to give theirs a try. The order came with four huge soft pretzel sticks served warm with two dips.  Normally, I favor a beer cheese, but the honey mustard here had me wanting to double dip.   For those who need adult beverages, no need to fret. They've got you taken care of. They're offerings may only be craft beer and wine, but you'll be pleased to know that many of them are locally made.   I'll be back? - Looking forward to patio dining.   When: April 17, 2018 Why: Lunch with a cousin

I am so glad that someone has bought and brought the Three Dog Bakery franchise back to St. Louis.   The location is further out in West County, but well worth the drive. It's located in the new Town & Country Crossing. You can shop Whole Foods, have lunch at Five Guys and pick treats for your favorite K-9.   They have all the fabulous cookies you remember from the previous Ladue location and many new ones as well. When I returned home with a bag full of mini bones, Fire Hydrant Cookies, Cranberry Cookies and Dottie Spots, I was greeted with 4 wagging tales.   In addition to all the yummy dog treats, they an excellent selection of doggie accessories and necessities.   Check their website for special events, sales and promotions.   My Four Dogs are glad Three Dog is back in the Lou.

Love having a great neighborhood park like Tilles. The city keeps it well maintained and the locals do their part to keep it beautiful.  I love the walking paths, as much as my dogs do. It's amazing how many dog walkers you see in the mornings and evenings.  Tilles is just the perfect size.

Have you seen Wicked? No, not the Broadway musical, I 'm talking about the Smothered Fries at Shaved Duck. They are wickedly good. So good that your doctor probably does not want you to eat them. We've all learned the valuable lesson of what is GOOD, is always not GOOD for us. These fries are one of those things and I do not care. I will eat these every time I go to TSD.   Smothered Fries are crispy hand-cut fries (I think they're fried in duck fat), topped with pulled rib meat and "smothered" in homemade cheese sauce. Paula Deen would love these fries, but now you can see why your doctor may not.   We then shared a full slab of St. Louis Style Spare Ribs. I loved the dry rub so much that I only used a little sauce of the three they offered. Of the three my favorite was the Kansas City. Kinda funny putting KC sauce on STL Ribs.   Our sides were Mac-n-Cheese, Cornbread and Jalapeno Cream Corn.  The Cornbread was served in a little black iron frying pan with Honey Butter. It was true southern cornbread, moist and came out of that skillet clean as a whistle. The Honey Butter was so damn good, I wanted to do butter shoots.   At Thanksgiving, I want a big bowl of Jalapeno Cream Corn. This has to be the best cream corn I have ever had and my Auntie use to make some killer cream corn. The jalapenos in this corn was damn hot. It was hotter then the hot sauce they offered for the ribs. Southern Belle Paula Deen would be saying, "yall I want this recipe".   I haven't forgotten about the Mac-n-Cheese, oh wait I have forgotten it.  It wasn't that memorable and will not reorder on my next visit.   The service was friendly and attentive. We enjoyed a table outside and watched the colorful locals walk by

I am so glad I had this past Saturday off and finally got to experience the BEST Biscuits and Gravy in Saint Louis. Flaky house made biscuits covered in a thick creamy milk gravy topped with crumbles of pork sausage. These are down on the farm style B&G's with a Southern twist.   It was so much fun sitting at the counter, enjoying a Bloody Mary as I waited for my B&G. Watching the ladies working their magic on the grill was truly entertaining. When my order arrived, I was shocked how huge the biscuits were and how they were covered edge to edge with that sensational gravy.   As I sat at the counter, I noticed a basket with fruit filled biscuits which I learned are called, "Jammers". They looked so good, I had to have one to take home. I choose the Peach and Raspberry.  Cassidy boxed it up in an Eco-Friendly container and told me to heat it in the Microwave for about 20-30 seconds when I was ready to enjoy. It was a perfect sweet treat later in the day.   A friendly staff, great home cooked food makes Luvy Duvy's Cafe a great place for breakfast. I can't wait to go back and experience lunch.

You'll definitely have love in your tummy after dining at Southern. It may be heart stopping and you'll have heartburn, but it will be true Southern comfort food love. I honestly think the only healthy food items on the menu are the Cole Slaw and Succotash. Fried Chicken and comfort foods are not about being healthy, they are about COMFORT and Southern provides that in a big way and with BIG flavor.   I'm a little quirky. Let me explain; I do not like tomatoes, but I do like Fried Green Tomatoes. So whenever I see them on a menu, I cannot resist and they are totally irresistible here. They're thinly sliced with a very light breading. Normally I am not a dipper, I enjoy the natural flavor of the FGT. However, here I have changed my ways. They serve up a side of Buttermilk Lime Dressing, that gives their fried tomatoes and extra tang, that had my tastebuds dancing a Souther jig.   I was warned by other reviews and I didn't listen. I ordered the Medium Chicken, not knowing they had a new mild intensity that wasn't listed on the menu. It was big in spicy flavor, but it had beads of sweat popping up on my forehead and my lips tingling and burning from each and every bite of some of the best chicken in Saint Louis.   I ordered a 2 Piece White which included an above average sized wing and an extremely large breast. Enjoying a comfort food lunch, I doubled my carbs and ordered Mac-n-Cheese and Mashed Potatoes with Pan Gravy. Pan Gravy? Being a farm boy, I was confident this was just a marketing play of words. I was wrong, I could honestly tell from the pan drippings that it was the real deal. Their mashed potatoes and pan gravy are worthy of a Sunday night dinner down on the farm.   My other side; Mac-n-Cheese was also a winner. It was baked Mac-n-Cheese, the way it is supposed to be served. It was small elbow macaroni with a rich and creamy sauce. What set it above others was the crispy baked topping. I may have been a bad boy having two carbs with fried chicken, but I enjoyed every bite.   My dining partner wasn't as adventurous and ordered his 3 piece Dark Chicken, Original. He may have been the smarter diner. Next time I'll being going Original. It had the same big flavor from the seasoning, just minus the extra fire. His sides were Succotash and Hoppin John. The Succotash was a healthy mix of vegetables. According to him, the Hoppin John had good flavor, but was on the dry side.    What would a Southern Fried Chicken dinner be without a refreshing glass of sweet tea? A total waste of comfort food, is what it would be. However, you do no need to worry about that here. Southern has brewed up what I consider some of the best Sweet Tea I have enjoyed in my life. It is the perfect blend of added sugar, so it is not overly sweet.   My only complaint about Southern is their hours. I have a weird work schedule and it does not coordinate well with their open hours. The only day I can make it, is Wednesday. So I guess I'll be having lunch here every other Wednesday.   When: August 19, 2015 Why: Lunch

Their recent commercials got me to stop by and try their new, Reese's Outrageous Blizzard. It's a blend of vanilla custard, Reese's Pieces, broken up Reese's Peanut Butter Cups and Caramel. Sounds delicious, right? Yes, if you have a serious, sweet tooth. For me, it was too overly sweet.  I admit, I've been known to order a Blizzard with Reese's Pieces in it or one with their Peanut Butter Cups. Alone, each of those made for a good blizzard. However, mixing the two and adding caramel as a third ingredient, made for an overly sweet treat. Next time, I enjoy a simpler Blizzard with only one ingredient or may-be two at the most.   In closing, I'll say the staff is always friendly and professional. This location is truly a neighborhood DQ.   Will I be back? - Their commercials for a new Blizzard always catch my eye.   When: August 21, 2018 Why: Outrageous Blizzard

My first visit here was for Abby's Farewell, and I will return for the true Latitude experience.  I got enough of a tease to know it will be amazing.  It may sound weird, but I judge a Mexican restaurant by its Margaritas, chips and salsa and queso.  If they can pull those three things off,  you've got me hooked.  The staff was extremely friendly and made us feel as if we were attending a private party in someone's home.  I'm sure I'll raise my stars after I experience a full meal.

I am a big fan of Costco and this GFS has impressed me. It is restaurant quality, you can still buy in bulk and no membership is required. They had many name brands on some items and their house brand GFS. Just imagine a Costco or Sam's with only the food section and you've created GFS.   They also had an aisle with party supplies. Who needs Party City when you can pick up your plates, cups, catering trays, napkins and table cloths at the same store you're picking up your party food.   The pricing was very comparable to the warehouse clubs and on some items it was even lower. The staff was upbeat, helpful and walked us directly to various items when we requested them. Just like the warehouse stores, they had a sample lady who was passing out goodies.   I think Jenny S. hit the nail on the head, GFS is the baby of Sam's and Aldi's.

Scarlett, I am so disappointed. Don't worry, I'm not disappointed with you, I'm disappointed that I normally work weekends and cannot enjoy your brunch more often. Lucky for me, I had this past Sunday off and got to enjoy a delicious breakfast with a couple of friends.   Anyone who knows me well, knows that brunch in my eyes is not complete without a Bloody Mary. Yours' rocked my world. I loved that as I sipped it up my straw, there was a thick pulp to the mix. It was also extra spicy and I like it that way. I'd be willing to say that your Bloody Mary is probably one of my favorites now.   A feature of your menu that I liked, it being able to order half orders or small portions of select entrees. Being one who loves, Benedict's and Biscuits & Gravy, this allowed me to be a glutton and enjoy both. Enjoying two half orders was still way too much food, but I just had to do it. I rarely get to enjoy a Sunday Brunch so when I do, I over indulge.   I earlier this fall enjoyed a vacation in New Orleans and had Eggs New Orleans in the French Quarter. I am here to tell you, yours are way better. Your crab cake was huge, flakey and flavorful. My ex was a chef so I got spoiled and learned what a good hollandaise sauce should be and the sauce that topped my eggs made me smile. It was total perfection.   Now what really amazed me was the Biscuits & Gravy. I reluctantly ordered them, thinking a wine bar could not possibly make decent B&G. Color me surprised. I'm a farm boy and not easily impressed by many orders of B&G, but you now deserve a spot on my list. Your gravy was a true milk gravy, thick and full of chunks of sausage. It wasn't overly salty, but for my personal taste could have had a few more shakes of pepper.   The servers were witty and charming. The pace of service was slow, but I've learned that is part of the charm of Scarlett's and Sasha's. Being slow today, made for a very relaxing and enjoyable brunch.   Would I come back? Yes, whenever I have a Sunday off, I'll be here for brunch.  When: December 11, 2016 Why: UYE- Brunch with friends

Marking another one off the Ian Froeb's STL 100 List and this one I may repeat again and again. The first time I dropped by for lunch they were out of the ingredients for Ian's "must order", Prosciutto Cotto sandwich. The cool guy working, recommended The Beddu Muffaletta. So I trusted him and gave it a try. I enjoy Muffulettas at other sandwich shops, so why not here.   It was excellent. I liked that they served it with Croccantini's instead of potato chips. However, I will tell you when I returned for my second visit and was able to have the Prosciutto, it was instant love. It was the closest a sandwich has ever brought me to a food-garam. The sandwich itself is small, but it is mighty. The bread was so fresh and the mixture of salumi with gruyere, pickled onions and grain mustard made my knees go weak. I'm typically not a sandwich guy, but this one has my heart. Now that I have discovered it, I think it will be a weekly thing.   Great job Salume Beddu and congratulations on being on Ian's STL 100 List. It is well deserved. Ian, if you see this - thanks for turning me on to this amazing sandwich.    When: June 23 and July 20, 2016 Why: Lunchtime

Sweet Mother of God, this place is unbelievable and I would have never discovered it if it were not for Yelp and Livingsocial. There is bare bones ambiance, but they offer warm friendly service and mind blowing affordable food. I felt like I had escaped to New Orleans and was dining at a dive cafe on a side street in the French Quarter.   There is no table service here, you order, pay at the counter and then find a open booth or counter space for the size of your group. Keep in mind, there are only approximately 20 spaces to accommodate those who choose to eat in. We arrived for an early lunch so getting a booth was no problem. However, as we were getting ready to leave, people were getting pushy to slide in to our space. I barely was out and a lady was sliding into my side.  I jokingly said, "oh, I guess were leaving." She had no sense of humor.   I totally blew my diet, but I did not care. Every calorie and carb I ate was worth it and I'll just work harder at the gym tomorrow. After all Scarlett did say, "tomorrow is another day".  Today we did not experience their burgers, so I know another day of a blown diet is in my future. The ones we saw were huge and are luring me back.   Today we experienced; Chicken and Waffles, Jerk Wings, Special Ed Sandwich and Bistro Fries. The Jerk wings are grilled and had the right amount of jerk seasoning for me. The orange marmalade dipping sauce is the perfect sweetness to the jerk.  The Bistro Fries are hand cut, skin on making them a true fry.   I had the Chicken and Waffles, which is two waffles and five pieces of breaded wing pieces. I choose vanilla waffles and as I waited I could smell them being prepared in the kitchen. The aroma got me anxious for their arrival. These were by far some of the best waffles I've had. They were a perfect golden yellow, with a light crisp outer shell. I loved how they are served in a tin plate/bowl that you see around a campfire. The wing pieces are served on top of the waffles. The seasoning of these wings is light, making for a good combination with my flavored waffle. The waffles are huge, I would have been satisfied with one, but they serve two.   The SO enjoyed The Special Ed which is BBQ Brisket, Red Cabbage Slaw, Fontina Cheese and Homemade Tangy Russian Dressing Grilled on Rye Bread. Damn, that is one good sandwich. If this excited my taste-buds, I can only imagine what their burgers will do.   The gentleman who work here are rock stars. They are friendly, personable and make sure their customers feel welcome are satisfied. I'll be back and I encourage you to go and experience TKS now.

I love this place! What a hoot and a holler. They have some great T's and they'll help you design your own as well. After freaking out about creating part of my Halloween costume, I called STLStyle for help. They couldn't do what I needed, but they knew who could and referred me to Baked T's. How cool is that?  One local biz helping and referring biz to another.   When we arrived at Baked T's, I was surprised how small and compact the store was. The staff quickly showed us how they turn out a big powerful product within a small space. They promptly greeted us as we entered and asked what they could do. I jokingly replied, "I need a Tshirt. Are you surprised?".  When I explained what I needed, the designer quickly sat at the computer with me and started showing me clip art.  In less then 10 minuets, we had designed a focal part of my costume. Wow!  They helped me create a cool custom Tshirt for less then all the craft stuff I bought earlier in the day. They saved me time and money. (It took about another 20 minuets to press and finalize my Tshirt.)  The entire staff was so friendly and helpful. As I was creating my shirt, the SO was chatting up other employees and sharing cartoons and pictures on his iPhone. Before I knew it, they were downloading his favorite cartoon off his phone and making him a Tshirt too.   So many ideas have gone through our pretty little creative heads, that our friends and family should be scared. I see Baked T's being a destination store for gift shopping. Like them on Facebook and receive 10% off your purchase.

It was love at first sight. The moment I walked in and saw the large selection of Lodge cast iron pots, I knew this was going to be a store for me. As I continued through the store, I found more and more items that I wanted to make my kitchen complete. It was as if I fell into my own Pinterest List; Gadgets and Gizmos for my Kitchen.   I was totally blown away by the huge and I do mean HUGE selection of cookie cutters. Then I was blown even further away when I saw the price. Each and everyone of these cutters were only $1. I went totally crazy finding at least one to match the personality of everyone on my holiday list. I'm going to work the cutters into the bows on their main gift.   After shopping the main floor, I worked my down to the basement where I was totally blown away yet again. The basement was full of Fiesta Ware of every imaginable color; including my favorite color ORANGE. They had everything from plates, mugs, platters, bowls and pitchers. These dishes will make your next dinner party, so colorful.   My most favorite item that I found in the entire store was also in the basement. They carry Peterboro Baskets and the prices were so reasonable. I love a great picnic basket and Peterboro has been making them in New Hampshire since 1884. I still have my mothers', but now I think I want one of my own.   The gentleman working, as well as the lady both were friendly and knowledgeable. They both did suggestive selling without being high pressure. I'll be back, I've fallen in love with this great little kitchen store.

Did you know that the Catfish at Southern is as good as their chicken? I didn't even know that they served fish, until I was searching for a restaurant on Yelp last Friday. I didn't want to fight the Friday night fish crowds, so I gave them a try.   As I waited in line to place my order, I had to remain strong. I so wanted to order the 4 Wing Plate, or the 2 Piece White. When it was my time to order, I discovered their Catfish was nuggets. I was instantly bummed, but the cashier assured me that they were farm raised and that I would not be disappointed. He looked like an honest soul, so I took him at his word and ordered the small fish plate. As my sides I went with my favorite, Mac-n-Cheese and tried a new one; Maple Glazed Butternut Squash.   You're abel to get your fish in the same intensities as the chicken, so I ordered mine "mild". The "mild" level is equivalent to buffalo chicken wings you'd get in most sports bars. It gave my nuggets, a simple a nice little kick. I rather enjoyed being able to eat my catfish as a finger food. As always, their Mac-n-Cheese but a smile on my face. My new adventure of sampling the Butternut Squash was a road well traveled. The Maple Glaze baked on top, made this side one worth repeating.   My order was a carry-out and they get gold stars for being eco-friendly in their to-go vessels. I was also pleased to see they do paper over plastic for their bags.   Lent is almost over, so I do not mind sharing this secret about the flavorful fish at Southern. I will be returning on Good Friday to enjoy a second helping of "Southern" fried catfish.    Ian recommends the three piece dinner. In addition to that, I highly recommend the Fried Green Tomatoes (see my previous review).   When: March 18, 2016 Why: Friday Fish Dinner

Had to revisit the very next day after my first visit. We ate all our gifts, and thought of others who would enjoy these fabulous chocolate treats.  Today the customer service was incredible. Everyone there had their A-Game on which made for a pleasant shopping experience.   I made my purchase and as I was leaving, hand on the door knob they spoke of the Egg Nog Truffles that were just coming out. I turned and said, "did I hear Egg Nog?".  I love Egg Nog, and these Truffles are bursting with flavor.   Chocolate lovers you've got to go visit this place, it is amazing.

Simple update - I am a fan of their "Garden Mix" which is a mixture of top soil, mulch and just a small amount of sand.  Perfect for planter boxes.  We recently used it to top off an area of our front yard to start new growth. We're starting with a clean slate and a good foundation of "Garden Mix'.

My name is Steven and I am a Chocoholic.  It has been a minute since my last chocolate fix. In all seriousness, I can not tell which decadent treat was my favorite, but I can tell you they are all incredible.   The Sea Salt Caramels are the best I've ever had and trust me, I have had a lot. I've also got to give a shout out to the Candy Cane Bark - Oliver Twist would be saying, "More Please".  Christmas packages are going to be adorned with Chocolate Snowmen, Milk and Dark.   Now let's talk about Brittle. Brittle is a non chocolate treat that I normally shun, that is until now. We were driving down Jefferson when my partner gave me a piece of  "The Big Squeal Bacon Pecan Brittle" and all I could say was, "Oh, my God, oh, my God".  I love Pecans and Bacon is my favorite breakfast meat. The brittle was rich, lush, full of flavor and just the right amount of crunch. I normally don't like brittle because it is so hard  I fear breaking a tooth. No worries here, the crackle and pop was perfect. This brittle amazed me and so did the "Cowboy Candy Pecan Chipotle Brittle"  Now I need to tell you why they got a four and not the five that they truly deserved. The young lady working the counter stayed on the phone longer then she should have taking an order. I understand good customer service is important, but those standing in front of you should come first. There were three people waiting to check out, and she continued to chat away. In my opinion she should have asked the phone customer if she could have her number so she could call her back to complete her order. I am sure once she explained she had a line in the store, the phone person would have understood and allowed her to call back.

Great News! Mathew's has expanded it's hours and is now open for lunch. It is so nice now to have a wider selection in our options for lunch. If they give comfort food a twist, wait till you see how they serve up lunch.  My two personal favorites are the Cobb Salad and The Burger.   How can you go wrong with a Cobb Salad? Mixed greens, chicken, egg, bacon, bleu cheese and tomato. All you need to add is a chilled glass of white wine and you have a perfect summer lunch.   The Burger is in a class of its' own. The table next to me saw mine when it was served and three of the four said, "I'll have what he's having".  Wasn't the scene out of, When Harry Meet Sally, but the line was very similar.  The Burger, is 8 oz. of Certified Angus beef (I grew up on an Angus farm so I am very partial), Gruyere & Bleu Cheeses, Onion & Bacon Compote (what sets it above the others) on a Brioche Bun (no sesame bun for this burger).  What would a burger be without a side a of fries? Normal fries would not do this burger justice, so they offer Bistro Fries. These fries are hearty, meaty wedges of potato. They are so large, you only need a few to make a complete meal with the burger.   The wait staff here is always friendly and remember those of us who have become some what regulars. This is also, the restaurant where I first noticed no ketchup bottles in use and I have become a big fan of that trend.

I had a very disappointing lunch on Maryland Avenue. Thank goodness Bissinger's was just a few doors down and able to rescue the afternoon in the CWE. There's nothing like a good piece of chocolate to put a smile on my face and chase the bad lunch blues away.   Today I experienced one of their new Salted Caramels. The name alone had me sold. How can you go wrong with a name like, " Apple Ghost Chili Salted Caramel". I love it when I can rationalize eating a piece of chocolate by thinking I am getting a partial daily serving of a fruit and vegetable.   Anxious to taste the new caramel, I popped the entire piece into my mouth. Hot Damn! That Ghost Pepper, made that little caramel go zing. They may be bite size, but I highly recommend that you savor the flavor by making it a two biter. They are delicious, as all Bissinger's chocolates are.   The staff at Bissinger's is always top notch. They are well informed of the product they are selling and share the excitement with you. Like Joselyn, I loved the old location on McPherson, it had so much charm. However the new Maryland location makes me feel like I am in a  "real big city" like Chicago or New York.   Keep up the good work Bissinger's, man can not live without chocolate. At least this man can not.

I am embarrassed that it has taken me this long to check out the Luvy Duvy's Cafe. It was Jake K. who gave me the final push, saying they had the best biscuits and gravy. He also praised their Bloody Mary. Having Yelp list dedicated to these popular menu items, I knew I had to go pronto.   Upon our arrival, I was immediately disappointed. When I told Cassady I heard about their amazing biscuits and gravy, she informed me they were only  a Saturday special. Damn it, I was here on a Tuesday. I work Saturdays, but I am off on one in December and I guarantee you I will be back.   I at least got to experience their spicy Bloody Mary served in a mason jar. It had just the right amount of spicy kick to start my Tuesday off right. It was garnished with a dill pickle spear and a pepperoncini. My glass of milk was even served in the classic mason jar.   Great breakfast! Their menu selections may be limited, but they've got the traditional start your morning basics. Their grits are true southern grits, thick and creamy. Jackie works that grill well, serving up crispy hash browns and tasty thick cut bacon. She's even masterful at getting your eggs fried the way you like them, for me it is over medium. (Cassidy likes them that way too)  As a special treat the girls gave us a slice of Grandma's Spice Cake to make up for my disappointment in not being able to have biscuits and gravy. What a sweet treat and great customer service. That Spice Cake was worthy of a place on a Thanksgiving buffet.   Superior service, good comfort food and great value will have me coming back.

What is wrong with me? What took me so long to shop here? I don't know the answer to these questions, but I am glad that I finally got here. I can tell you now, the majority of my holiday shopping will be completed right here in my hood. I'll be shopping local and keeping my neighborhood strong.   I was amazed at the variety of unique and quality gifts. They have something for everyone on your list. The entertainer, the chef, the alcoholic, the sports fan. She has an entire wall section full of the funniest stuff for Cardinal and Blues fans. There was so much stuff, you could create an entire gift basket. Also, she has serving pieces for the hostesses with the mostest. Another favorite of mine was the huge selection of Fleur-de-lis items.  I could go on and on about all the goodies I saw and added to my list of gift recipients.    If you're a fan of Melissa & Doug, this is the place to shop. I've never seen such a large selection of their merchandise. A little Munchkins would love any toy bought here for Christmas.   The sales associates were informative and outgoing. They made me feel appreciated and welcomed me into the store.   Will I return? - I'll shop till I drop this holiday season.   When: November 1, 2017 Why: Scoping out for the big holiday season.

I've had Steve's bookmarked for quit awhile, so when the BF said he wanted to go here for lunch I agreed. I'll disclose up front, I am not a Hot Dog eater. Normally, the only time I eat a dog is at a Cardinals game and occasionally in someones backyard.   I will start off by saying it is a cute little shop specializing in Hot Dogs. Can you say, Urge.  I got a giggle out of the occupancy sign above the front door stating the maximum was 18 people and when I counted the chairs at the tables, there were 22. Which was okay with me, I would have given them 24 or 26 occupancy.   The staff was extremely friendly and was really excited to be selling Hot Dogs. She smooth talked us both into ordering the Two Dog Combo for $11.99. We saved a dollar each by showing our check-in on Yelp.  When I made a comment and selected the A&W because it was diet. She quickly guided me to the Craft Soda, Empire. Telling me that it was a much more flavorful soda. The bf tried the Sarsaparilla by Empire as well. Both were damn good, now I need to find out where I can buy them by the six pack.   From what we were told, Steve hooked up with Vitales Bakery across the street and created his own special Hot Dog Bun. It basically is pizza dough made into a bun for Hot Dogs. Neither of us were impressed with the bun, it was way to chewy. It was also had to cut in to bite size pieces. Many of our dogs were covered in plentiful toppings making it hard to pick up and bite. We wanted so bad to slice them in to eatable bites.  I wish they offered an old fashioned bun as an alternative for us old fuddy dud-dies.   Doing the Two Dog Combos did give us the opportunity to experience four different dogs. Selecting from the large (16) variety was hard, but we quickly narrowed it down.  Steve's Famous Chili - Cheese, St. Louis - Chicago Dog, Crazy Cajun Creole and Bacon - Bacon Jamaican. All four had good presentation in their little red baskets and Steve is very generous with the toppings.   The Chili - Cheese was very messy and hard to hand handle. This one for sure, needs to be cut and eaten with a fork. The Chili had a good flavor and can easily stand on its own in a bow.   I like the fact that they smoke their own dogs and brats on site, we saw them at work as we approached the entrance. The STL - CHI Dog was a true ballpark frank. I could enjoy this one at a Cardinals and Cubs game. The only change I'd make is removal of the tomato,  I'm not a fan of tomatoes. I'd also reduce the amount of onions, to reduce the heartburn.   Bacon - Bacon Jamaican Dog, was a disappointment and it had two of my favorite things; bacon and pepper jack. The description said, two slices of bacon and I expected two slices, one of each side of my dog. Instead, it was chopped and on top.  However, the jerk seasoning and sweet chipotle sauce was a nice touch.   The winner of the four was the Crazy Cajun Creole. A locally smoked Andouille sausage with grilled onions, spicy brown mustard and Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ Sauce.  This one I could hand handle and enjoy, but still found the bun to be chewy.   If either of us return, I know we will go with simpler toppings. The ones we selected on this visit gave both us heartburn, indigestion and upset stomach. We must have delicate digestive systems.

Bentley's is a great new addition to the many pet boutiques in St. Louis. It has an incredible selection to top rated foods for my fur-babies. They also have grain free and made in the USA treats. I was particularly impressed with the bulk section, because they offered a variety of flavors and sizes in treats. They also have a selection of dog beds, toys and of course collars and leashes.   On my first visit, the service was friendly and helpful. Being a first time shopper, I got a goodie bag with coupons, sample of dry dog food and a couple of treats.   When shopping Lucky's, or Stien Mart or dining at The Slider House or Katie's Pizza, Bentley's will also be on the itinerary when I'm in the Rock Hill hood.   Will I come back? YES!  When: October 12, 2016 Why: New pet boutique

Forget a co-workers birthday? Can't get out of the office to get a cake for the celebration? Don't worry, Hot Box Cookies will be your hero. They deliver and they even brought a small ballon, for the birthday honoree.   Our box of cookies were still warm when they delivered them. Being a true Yelper, I had to block my co-workers from grabbing the delicious cookies, so I could get a photo first. We had a great variety, Peanut Butter, M&M, Chocolate Chunk, Oatmeal and White Chocolate Macadamia. There was something for everyone.   I was amazed how fast they delivered after we placed our order. I wish my pizzas or Chinese could be delivered this fast. The delivery girl was perky and made our birthday girl feel special.   Will I return? Only have had delivery, gotta go check out the shop.  When: February 22, 2017 Why: Birthday Celebration at work

I'm sad to say that the stars went down for my return visit.  This place is truly Tex-Mex for beginners. The night of Abby's farewell they must have been on their best behavior, because what I saw today for lunch was poor.   Let's start off with the service, one waiter maybe four tables being served and he kept forgetting simple things. We had to ask for water, three times. He seemed to be pre-occupied with other duties and it wasn't giving needed attention to his tables. He also, had a hard time understanding that we wanted the Tamales as an appetizer. He kept telling us, it was an entree. We had to explain to him that we knew that, but wanted to experience the tamales. He finally got his head wrapped around it and allowed us to order them as an appetizer.   We should have listened to him and not ordered them at all. They were no were near traditional tamales. They were over stuffed, any one who has had true tamales know they are not suppose to be bursting at the seams from their stuffing's. The pork inside was extremely dry and no flavor.   We were surprised that the menu did not offer the opportunity to create our own combination platters, but went with the flow and ordered both The Latitude and Longitude.   Latitude: Beef Brisket Nachos, Cheese Chile Relleno, Soft Chicken Taco.  Longitude: Tostado, Crispy Ground Beef Taco, Chicken Enchilada.   The only items worth while out of the two platters were; the Beef Brisket Nachos and the Chicken Enchilada.   I/we were truly disappointed, we wanted a new mexican restaurant to visit and we will not be back to this one.

Earning badges here on Yelp, takes me back to the days when I was a boy scout.  Except achieving a badge on Yelp is a lot more fun. I can not tell you how many Margarita's I have drunk or the number of tacos and burritos I've eaten to earn my Mexi-can badge.  I thought it was never going to happen. Then the other night while attending an International Supper Club gathering at Milagro, it did. Making it the most memorable badge I've earned. I was at my "favorite" Mexican restaurant and with 11 of my closest Yelp comrades.  I always feel like I need to go to confession after having a Margarita at Milagro, because they are sinfully good. The "featured" Margarita was Mango-Pear, which went down rather smooth. So smooth, that I had to have more then one and would of had more if I did not have to get up at 4AM for work. Still I am fairly certain I'll be doing several Hail Mary's for what I did consume.   As an appetizer I shared Chorizo & Roasted Pablano Chili Queso Fundido with the SO. Their house made tortillas were perfect for dipping in and filling with the flavorful Queso. We both ordered the same entree which is unusual for us, but the Tacos en Cazuela just sounded to tempting. For me these were the perfect tacos to eat after earning my badge. The portions were huge, leaving me a little of each meat along with some Charro beans and street corn for the next day at work. I may not of had one of the corn tortillas left, but I still made my coworkers jealous at lunchtime.   Praise Jesus for Milagro's Street Corn. If is not only off the cob, but off the charts in flavor as well. Friends have always said, that certain foods were their "crack" and I've never understood that phrase, but I do now. This street corn is so good that if need be, I'd work the "street(s)" to be able to have more.   It is always a team effort at Milagro to make sure your dining experience is top notch.  Their kitchen staff is willing to accommodate special dietary needs when possible and the wait staff has a "no problem" attitude when it comes to separating checks on a large party.   If you haven't been to Milagro, stop reading now and go. You'll be glad that you did.

Let's talk some dirt. I mean some serious dirt, the kind that will make your garden, flowers and landscaping grow.  I never knew there could be such a large variety of mulch and dirt. Their staff knows the dirt and will be able to tell you which one is best for you.   With spring finally here, and our green thumbs looking to get dirty this is the place to shop for dirt. As pointed out by Ms. Sarah S., they do have a high delivery fee for those of us who do not drive a pick-up truck. So I highly recommend that you find a friend who does.   Now let's get out there and get dirty in the dirt.

I am going to make this one short and sweet.   I love the salsas, jellies and spreads form Harry & David. The Jalapeno jelly is one of my favorites.   On my last visit they had Chicken Pot Pies on sale for half price. What a deal, how could I pass on this opportunity to try something new.  It made for an easy dinner that night and we were impressed. The pie had lots of vegetables and white breast meat. It was large enough to feed 5 adults, or in our case lunch the next day.   The customer service was friendly and extremely helpful. When I asked about one of the spreads, they went to the back and brought out an opened jar for sampling. What a nice touch.   Be sure to sign up for their email list so you will be informed of sales and on occasion they send you coupons and we all like coupons.

This DQ has grown on me. They've recently turned their game up. I think they've done it as a corporation and as a franchise. I don't stop by that frequently, but when I do, I'm not disappointed. A soft serve cone or a Blizzard can always satisfy a sweet tooth craving.   What motivated me to stop yesterday, was seeing a poster promoting a Dipped Strawberry Blizzard. How could I resist a blizzard with one of my favorite fruits, strawberries and Ghirardelli chocolate. It's so cool how they turn it upside down when presenting it to you. If they don't, your next one is free. My blizzard was rich, creamy and tasted just like a Chocolate Dipped Strawberry. I ordered a small. It was so delicious, I wished I had ordered a larger size, but thankful that I didn't.   The staff was friendly and the kitchen area in view was clean.   I'll be back? - Sure, don't know how quickly, but I'll return. Can't control my cravings.   When: February 4, 2018 Why: Dipped Strawberry Blizzard

Patience is what you need to shop here. If you have them, chances are you will find a good bargain or two. I came to BCF looking for a specific item, which they did not have, but I still walked out with several new items at a bargain price.   Whenever I am in a discount store like this, I always check out the pet section. My dogs have more dog bowls, beds, collars and leashes then they actually need, but I spoil them. Today at BCF, I didn't find any bowls or such, but they had a nice selection of Scoop Bags aka poop bags. They had the colorful biodegradable ones at a price cheaper then any of the local doggie boutiques. This was a major find for me, since I am a conscientious dog walker and scoop the poop.   Another department I always check out of course is the mens fashion department. This was a nightmare. The only positive things was that the racks were not packed as tight as they are at Marshall's. Another positive thing is they had the jeans separated from all the other types of pants which made it easy to browse. From the the brief time I looked, the prices and name brands seemed good. When I need a new pair of jeans, I may pop back in to take a closer look.   The best bargain I found was colorful socks. I love bright colored socks and BCF had them on sale 5 pairs for $9.99. What a deal - I normally pay that for one pair of socks at The Rack. The sign on the table said, "Brag About It", so I am. I got 5 pairs of amazing sock for only $9.99 and this sock-aholic is one happy shopper.   The cashier at check out was friendly and wrapped the sale up quickly. BCF is out of my way, but knowing the savings on got on scoop bags and socks, I may be back and put up with the hot mess and disorganization.   When: February 22, 2016 Why: First Time in a BCF

Chicago may have The Magnificent Mile, but Maplewood has Magnificent Manchester. It's the main drag through this revitalized little city that has everything its' residents could want and need. Magnificent Manchester even has the attractions that draw people in from the big city and county of Saint Louis.  Magnificent Manchester gives you the opportunity to dine at Acero, Water Street or Reed's American Table. If you want is a more casual dining experience, you can eat at; A Pizza Story, Crow's Nest or Boogaloo. If you want Mexican, Magnificent Manchester has Las Palmas and if you got to watch the big game you can stop by The Post and enjoy a burger or pizza.   If you want to feel pretty, MMM has you covered as well. Bee Naturals, Bouffant Daddy and Maven will have you singing, "I feel pretty, oh, so pretty".   Those of you who play creative chef at home, Maplewood's Magnificent Manchester may not get you a James Beard award, but it will help you get rave reviews from friends and family. You can shop for all those secret ingredients at; Cheryl's Herbs, Larder & Cupboard, Vom Fass and Penzey's Spices.  The shopping doesn't stop here, it continues on and on. You can find things for your home and  the backyard farmer at Intaglia. You can satisfy your chocolate craving at Kako Chocolate and Airdale Antics will have everything you fur-babies desire. A bookworm will feel right at home in the Book House.   I love Maplewood and its' Magnificent Manchester.

Three Dog Bakery, made the holidays a howling success for my Fur-Babies. My dogs will celebrate any holiday if there is a cookie involved and TDB has them all.  They have celebrated Hanukkah, Winter Solstice, Christmas and Kwanzaa with delightful and tasty treats. One of our Shelties even celebrated a 10th birthday this week with a TDB cookie. With all the holiday treats I didn't order a cake, but will be getting one for Big Gracie's birthday in February.   I even picked up some great little bags of treats to give to our cousin dogs and neighborhood dogs making us the cats meow.....LOL.   Keep in mind Three Dog is not just a bakery, they also have a large variety of dog accessories and their own line of premium dog food.   Also,  the staff here gives exceptional customer service. They not only remember my name and call it out when I enter the store, but they remember what breed of dogs I have too.

I was in Kirkwood running errand and when it became lunchtime, I wanted something new and different. I had by MOD Pizza several times and thought it was time to give them a try. I have been to a pizza restaurant in Chicago that is the same quick serve concept, so I was anxious to give MOD a try.   Great job, MOD Pizza! Your service was friendly, attentive, fast and most importantly you served up a tasty salad and flavorful pizza. Some folks get excited when a restaurant serves their favorite Pepsi or Coke. Here at MOD I was excited to see they make their lemonade from scratch. It was a good mix of sweet & tart, so it was a refreshing drink to enjoy with my lunch.   My pizza of choice was the, Calexico. I love jalapeños on my pizza and when I saw the Calexico had them with grilled chicken I was sold. It's a red sauce base with two cheeses; mozzarella and gorgonzola and then finished off with hot buffalo sauce. Their menu states, "It's Hot", but being a fan of jalapeños, I didn't find it that hot. For me it was just perfection.   In addition to my pizza, I enjoyed a Mini Caesar Salad. They warned me, (which I thought was good customer service) that their Caesar has diced tomatoes in it. I thought that was odd, but I was game to give it a try. The mix of romaine lettuce, parmesan cheese, asiago cheese, croutons and the diced tomatoes tossed in their house Caesar dressing served up a sensational salad.   If you're in Kirkwood, craving pizza or need a quick lunch or dinner. I recommend you give MOD a try. For those of you who do not know, MOD = Made On Demand.  When: June 7, 2016 Why: Lunch

This is not my usual movie theatre, but I was lucky and got FREE tickets to  sneak preview of Trainwreak; so I found myself expanding my movie theatre experience.   I was elated to see that the theatre had stadium seating. Being height impaired, I always seem to get a basketball player in front on me. With stadium seating, I don't need to worry about my vision being blocked. However, the seats seemed to be worn out and in need of re-conditioning. I've seen chairs at a consignment shop and Goodwill with better spring support.   The concession stand was extensive and had several combo offerings for two to share. I always go with the classic movie treat; popcorn and ice cold soda. Half way through the movie, I wished I had gotten the nachos. Why? Someone behind me was enjoying them and I could smell the jalapeños. The aroma alone won me over.   The theatre lobby, auditorium and restrooms were very clean for the volume of traffic that was going through that evening. I also, found the staff to be extremely friendly. The young men at the box-office and taking tickets were both witty, adding an extra touch to their customer service.   The reason for only 3 Stars is due to the technical difficulty in getting the movie to start and having to pause and re-start again. Thank goodness, that they fast forwarded to the beginning of the movie so we didn't have to sit through the leaders again.   When: July 14, 2015 Why: Special Sneak-Preview Movie

I love Mussels, beer and Pommes Frites. My previous review for Tripel showed my love for these culinary delights and was selected as a Yelp ROTD. When I saw this honor had been bestowed upon me, I knew I had to return and celebrate.   This night I enjoyed a nice blonde brew, Affligem. It was a good accompaniment to both our Toost Kanniball (steak tartare) and my A la Chouffle with Cracked Pepper (Mussels). I've now experienced three of their six offerings of Mussels and can't wait to try the other three.   The steak tartare is one of the finest I have had in the St. Louis area. It was so good lightly spread on a crostini with a slither of dill pickle and a smear of spicy mustard.  As stated in my original review, I love shucking all the mussels first, so I can enjoy the mussels at a steady pace. I am a pepper fan, I use more pepper then salt on all my food, so these mussels with "cracked pepper" got two thumbs up from me.   If you enjoy Mussels as much as I do, I highly recommend you visit Tripel. I also recommend sitting at the bar if you're a party of two. It is comfy, cozy and the bartenders not only provide good service, but they're entertaining as well.   When: 11, JAN 2014 Why: Celebrating my ROTD

A special thank you to my Chicago Elite friend Lupe d, for sharing her LivingSocial coupon with me. She got so busy having fun in our great city, that she didn't have time to enjoy Kitchen Sink and her coupon expired on the 6th of September. I wasted no time on going and went for lunch today.   I not only wanted to make sure I got there before the LS coupon expired, but I wanted to go one more time before they shut their doors on September 30th. Yes, the 30th of this month is their last day in this cozy, comfortable hole in the wall diner. Then they are projected to reopen at their new location at 255 Union Blvd. in the space previous occupied by the infamous Rhine House.   Our lunch today diner delightful. As we entered we were cheerfully greeted by one of the young men working. He quickly offered us menus and glasses for the ice cold filtered water. Having been here before and knowing what we wanted, we handed the menus back. As I pulled my LivingSocial coupon out, he told me to put it away and we'd worry about that later.   I ordered a Tejas Burger, that will defiantly make my burger list here on Yelp. It was a 1/2 beef burger mixed with roasted Jalapeños & bacon then topped with Cilantro, diced avocado, onions, fried Jalapeño and Queso Fresco sauce.  It was juicy and grilled medium at my request. What is it about a hand pressed burger, that makes it taste so good? Is it the odd shape, or the love that the chef puts in to his work.   The BF enjoyed a Pat "Say Jack". Which honestly didn't look like much, but when you took that first bite your taste buds start screaming, "more, please".
