It is grilled Andouille, roasted pork loin, Jalapeño bacon, Swiss & pepper jack cheese. Then it is garnished with stone ground mustard, fried pickles & fried banana peppers.  Now you understand why your taste buds request another bite.   We both wanted Bistro Fries so we shared a large and it was huge. Once again, I love fries that are hand cut and served with the skins on. In addition to the filtered water, they offer a variety of canned soda and we choose Root Beer.   I'm looking forward to the new location where they will have a full service bar and table service, but I will also miss this sleazy hole in wall that had so much charm.

This has to of been the worst 8" I have ever experienced. We're talking pizza here Yelpers, this is a review for Imo's. Now let's get to the facts of why this 8" was so disappointing.   Once again, I must have not been thinking when I ordered Imo's. I did not bring lunch to work and discovered that Imo's offered their Lunch Box special till 4 PM which coordinated well with my lunch break. A box containing an 8" two topping pizza, 4 Toasted Raviolis, 6 Provel Bites and 2 CinImos for $9.95 such a deal. Would be a deal if you could eat it all.   I ordered my pizza with bacon and onion, thinking everything is good with bacon. Not true, I think the provel killed the flavor of the bacon. The Provel Bites, were bite size, I'll give them that. Otherwise, they were tasteless. I would have gotten more flavor chewing on the cardboard box. The CinImos were basically two turds of pizza crust with sugar and cinnamon sprinkled on them, chewy and flavorless.  The four toasted raviolis were the best item in the lunch special. They came with a side of marinara sauce for dipping.   The quality phone service and the friendly delivery man  kept this Imo's from getting the dreaded 1 Star.

Oh Mathew, Oh Mathew. Hump Day (Wednesday) was never as good as it is now with your Fried Chicken Special. I have been wanting to try it ever since you opened and finally got to taste your succulent fried chicken. I am listing you in the #1 spot on my Crispy Chicken List.   I was determined to have your fried chicken last Wednesday, nothing was going to stop me from experiencing it. I ate a very lite lunch, to save calories and tummy space for that hearty dinner. As dinner time approached, I experienced a bump in my plans for my "hump day" dinner. I needed to be home for a last minute commitment.  Fear not, carryout to the rescue. I called in an order for two dinners and was picking them up in 20 minutes in eco-friendly containers.   The chicken was served with the daily vegetable which was brussels spouts with bacon, whipped potatoes & bacon milk gravy and a cheddar biscuit. Can it get more country then that? The breading on the chicken was crispy with huge flaky pieces. When you bite into it, the inside was juicy and moist.  Grandma could have taken a few lessons on fried chicken from Mathew.   Growing up I was not a fan of brussel sprouts, they are a vegetable I have learned to love with age. If I had been served these sprouts within huge pieces of bacon, I would have become a fan much earlier. Mashed, smashed, or whipped however you  call them, potatoes with bacon milk gravy is a winner in my book.   When I arrived the restaurant was packed and once I had my dinner at home I could understand why. The staff is always friendly, and the bartender giggled as I walked in, she recognized my name on the carryout. Mathew's Kitchen is a great addition to my neighborhood and the city of St. Louis.

Sweet, Mother of God! Tripel is amazing.   I can not tell you the last time I had something this good in my mouth. I could, but one of us (me) might blush. From the first bite of Terrine, to the last bite of Creme Brûlée my taste buds were screaming, "OMG, don't stop, faster, give it to me faster, I want more."   Proving that every dish was a foodgasm.   We started off with a Terrine, which was made with chicken liver and bone marrow. I am not a fan of liver, especially chicken and this Terrine won me over. It was served in a small mason jar with crostini's on the side. I had no idea, a chicken liver could taste so good.   I love escargot and this is the best I've had in my entire life. I bet even Lucy Ricardo would have skipped using ketchup and enjoyed these exquisite snails. They were served with bone marrow and with the two of them combined on a baguette, totally set off fireworks in my mouth. If you are a fan of both of these culinary delights, you'll understand how delicious it would be when they're combined into one.   Next we enjoyed two pots of mussels. A la Marimiere, was a traditional white wine shallot broth and Provencales, a tomato, garlic and fresh basil broth. They were served in small black pots on plates with slices of baguette on the side. When the top was removed, it was the perfect place to discard the shells. It made it so easy to shuck all the mussels at once. I was then able to enjoy my mussels with a soup spoon as if I were eating a hearty soup. When I was done, I wanted to pick up the pot by its' handles and do my best Oliver Twist imitation, "More, please".   We were both stuffed like the Thanksgiving turkey, but it did not stop us from exploring the dessert menu. If you're going to over stuff yourself, why only share one dessert? You might as well, go hog wild and experience two. We ordered the Belgium Waffles with Baked Apples and Cheesecake with Cherries and Candied Bacon. The bartender claimed the Cheesecake was his favorite, so I ordered it instead of my original intention Creme Brûlée.  The house made cheesecake with the candied cherries and bacon was unbelievable. Forget about breaking me off a piece of that Kit Kat Bar, break me off another piece of that candied bacon, it is so addicting. The Belgium Waffles with baked apples was like eating an ready to assembled pie. It was a great way to end our meal.   As a bonus, the bartender treated us to a Creme Brûlée. He wanted to make sure, he didn't steer me wrong on ordering his favorite. He was right his was the best of the three, but the Creme Brûlée was still outstanding. I'd be torn on which one to reorder on my next visit.   The ambiance is a mixture of blast from the past  (classic cocktail lounge) and as Megan stated, "industrial chic". It is both relaxing and romantic.  This is an ideal place for a date night, business meeting or hanging with friends. The staff is extremely friendly and very knowledgeable about the menu offerings. I was so impressed, I plan on being a regular at Tripel.

Epic failure = MAJOR disappointment   My last two visits have been lackluster, with today's being a major disappointment. We both ordered the daily special, Ham and Cheese Quiche with Hash Browns for $8.95. Overpriced for what we were served.  It was not a true quiche. The crust was house made, but had no flavor and was to thick. The bottom was almost half as thick as the "quiche". Their so called quiche, was basically just scrambled eggs with small cubes of ham baked in a pie shell. There was no flavor what so ever. Our hash browns were cold, I admit we were eating outside, but they shouldn't have cooled down that fast.   Our server was sweet and attentive. However, her coworker was another story. When he was serving coffee to his table, which was next to ours,  he totally ignored us and did not fill our cups. To get more coffee, we had to flag down the hostess and she seemed bewildered that we'd ask.   The outside patio is a great place to enjoy breakfast and Cassidy as always was great at greeting all the regular customers. However, after two disappointing breakfast, Luvy Duvy's going down to 3 Stars. It is just A-Ok in my eyes now. I am also taking Luvy Duvy's off my Breakfast List.

On a recent West County outing, we had breakfast at The Egg and I then drove down the road to experience the new mega Dierberg's. A big bonus immediately is the covered parking. It keeps your car cool during the summer and is a big plus when the weather is nasty wet.   I have recently started to favor Dierberg's over Schnucks basically for their produce and meat departments. To be honest, I think their dairy and seafood departments also have the upper hand. Once I entered this store, I knew Dierbergs had won me over.   I was totally blown away by the produce department. It truly would be heaven for a vegetarian. Not only was the selection and freshness amazing, but the merchandising had me wanting to drop to my knees and convert right there to vegetarianism.   No need to say, "cheese", just seeing the cheese department here will have you smiling ear to ear. I was so happy to see that they were featuring Marcoot, Bajeta Farms and so many other local dairies in their selections.   Yellow mustard is not for me, so I was totally  impressed with the large selection of fancy and brown mustard's. They even have a gourmet selection of vinegars to make a home gourmet cook feel like a Food Network star.   Fortunately I do not need to worry about a Gluten Free diet, but if I did this store makes it easier. I do love a good wine and here they have what every grocer needs and that is a wine tasting bar.   Normally I avoid grocery store restrooms like I do a fast food restroom, but after multiple cups of coffee at breakfast I could not wait. To my surprise the men's public bathroom was fancier then a high end restaurant. It was downright, prissy elegant. If were not for the urial, I would have thought I entered the wrong room.   I could go on and on, on how great this grocer is, but come see for yourself. You'll be wishing you lived closer.

Bigger and better then the Huck's close to my home and they offer gas too. It's like a mini U-Gas. Great selection of fountain drinks and convenience mart type items. They even had a small area of table and chairs for those who want to sit and grab a bite to eat.   What makes Huck's special is the fact that they are employee owned. When the one waiting on you is part owner, you know you'll be getting good customer service. If I lived in Kirkwood, this would be my convenience mart and gas station of choice.

The produce and sea food departments alone get this Whole Foods a 5 star rating. The fresh vegetables and fruits are perfect for starting the new year eating right. Eating right sounds so much better then dieting.   The counter person in seafood was so friendly and helpful that he had me laughing while making my selection.  Excellent customer service.   The cashier is the last image you have of a shopping experience and it needs to be positive. Mine wasn't, but I did not let that effect my star rating. My cashier said the same exact thing to me as she did the two customers before me - come on change it up. The most annoying thing to me was the young lady's style of chewing gum. She chewed it like a cow chewing it's cud. Not only did she chew aggressively, but she made it snap and pop.  I must be old, I remember the days when people in retail or food service were not allowed to chew gum while working.

It was time for the new license sticker and this year I was reactive instead of proactive. Bad me. Realizing I have waited to the end of the month, I started to panic. I did not want to be in those long lines at the license office on my days off next week, so I quickly went into action.   I live less then two blocks from FAR, and I had seen their signs advertising they do state inspections. So I hopped in my CRV and drove up the street to see if they could get me done today (Wednesday). I was greeted by very professional gentleman who assured me they could. It got even better when he looked the card sent to me by the state and all I needed was the emissions test. They could do it pronto, it would be less then 15 minuets. That was GREAT news, but then I realized I left my wallet at home. They laughed with me, at least I hope it was with me and not at me and told me to just come back later and it'd be ready.   Walked home, got the wallet and decided to have lunch with Brad before picking it up. When we arrived, sure enough it was ready to go. As another young man checked me out, he recommended Deer Creek for picking up my actual stickers instead of S. Kingshighway location. He told me they were much more efficient and quicker. He was right, watch for that review.   Great friendly, and prompt service. I am proud to have them in my neighborhood.

Welcome to my hood Mathew's Kitchen! You have just given the county folks another reason to venture into the city and experience comfort food with a twist.   My first visit was for a quick little Happy Hour with Brad and Norma, we just had to see what all the excitement was about the new addition to St. Louis Hills. As we sipped our cocktails, visited with the bartender and wait staff our mouths drooled at the entrees being served in the front dinning room. We even got to meet the man himself, Mathew.  After  a couple cocktails we knew we'd be back to experience the food.   The first big shout out I need to give Mathew is for not following the trend of "small plates" that so many of the new restaurants do. He is truly serving up "comfort food" and serving it up right. The servings are not overwhelming, they are the perfect size for a healthy portion.   Last night Brad and I arrived early, I'd say it was close to 5:30PM. It was a good thing we did, because MK filled up fast. It was a good mix of customers, ranging from young couples to seniors and families to large groups of friends.   Going in, the one thing I knew I had to try was the Grilled Caesar Salad. The Romaine lettuce is truly grilled, you can see the grill marks on it like a steak you grill in your backyard. That grilled flavor is accented by their own creation of Caesar dressing. The salad is the perfect size as a side to many of their entrees. It was so good, that I'd like to see a larger size offered as an entree. Think about it, Mathew. I think it would sell.   Every night they have a Turf-n-Turf special and Braised Beef & Ribs were the feature. Oh my God, I haven't had beef or ribs this succulent in awhile. The brisket literally melted in your mouth and his sauce was just the right mix of spice and sweet. When finishing the ribs, there was not a morsel left on the bones. Again the meat was so tender, you were able to enjoy every single bite to the fullest.  Roasted potatoes were the side dish, and I liked how they were diced up smaller then most other establishments.   Our other entree was the Beef Stroganoff and the menu says "just like grandma's". I don't know which granny she is, but she can make some damn good stroganoff. Again, I will refer to size. I loved the fact that the beef was already in bite size morsels. The broth was thick, creamy and coated the egg noodles well. Granny had to have made those egg noodles too, because you could tell they were made fresh.   While dining, I tried to convince Brad I was hearing the voice of the "Bread Pudding Queen" telling me I had to try the Blueberry Bread Pudding. He didn't believe me, but I got to order it any way. We also had the Half Baked Turtle Brownie and being a chocoholic I must say it was the best of the two. Not selling the bread pudding short, because it was a true bread pudding and totally delicious.   I was happy to see several "brown bags" being picked up at the bar, giving me the signal that they do "carry-out". This may quickly become a favorite place for those nights you don't want to go out and yet you don't want to cook at home. Looking at the website today and seeing the Wednesday special is Fried Chicken I have a feeling we may be doing carry-out tonight.  The only reason for a 4 star and not a 5 star rating, is that there was a lot of down time between ordering, salad, entree and dessert. Hey, it's only been a week, they'll get that kink worked out, they've mastered the food.

This store may be compact and cramped, but it offers a great shopping experience. I enjoy the small boutique feel that it offers. It has that true cosmopolitan feel. Normally I do not like crowds, but here the hustle and bustle are exhilarating.   My three favorite departments are there at the front door; bakery, produce, wine and seafood.  Whoops, that's four not three, that is because every time I shop another department impresses me.   The produce here is totally out of this world. If I were a vegetarian, I'd be a regular in this department. Other local grocers can not match the quality of these fruits and vegetables. The only one who can come close is perhaps a farmers market or your own backyard garden.   Trying to reduce the amount of red meat I eat, I've had a recent love affair with Salmon. The best I have found has been right here at WF, it is even better then the specialty seafood store in U - City. I've even bought and grilled some of their big shrimp. However, I must say it is had to keep my focus when their meat counter is to the left and I see mouthwatering steaks.  Especially their selections of Bison.   Besides the Vino Gallery in the CWE, this is my stop for wine. Opal, a refreshing white wine and an exclusive only to WF is one of my favorites. I fill one of those wine bags up every chance I get. Who doesn't like getting 10% off your wine purchase when you buy six or more bottles?  Normally I am not a bread eater, but I do need a baguette or a freshly baked loaf to make a Penni sandwich this  is where you'll find me. When I'm getting bread, a sweet treat or two may fall into my basket as well.   The staff is friendly and willing to answer questions and assist any way they can.  I always get a giggle out of the one cashier who has, "Parking Lot Ranger" on his name tag. I commented on it once and he told me to be careful out  in their lot because those people drive crazy". I had to laugh, because it is so true. I can only imagine what it is going to be like when Michael's Craft's opens later this summer.

Point of Interest: This South County and the St. Charles location are not connected in any way.   Visualize the Red Headed love child of IHOP and Denny's and you've created Gingham's. What does that mean? It means you have a good place for breakfast at a reasonable price. The ambiance will be stark and Plane Jane, but you will not care you are there for the greasy diner quality breakfast. Their servers make you feel like a regular, even when it is your first visit.   Anyone who follows my reviews know I am a fan of Biscuits and Gravy and I am happy to say, Gingham's is being added to my list here on Yelp. I enjoyed a flaky biscuit and a milk gravy filled with chucks of sausage. I only needed to add some more pepper to make me truly happy.   I prefer my Hash-browns extra crispy and even when I request them prepared that way so many places just don't get it. However, the grill master here at Gingham's not only got it, but he impressed me. These truly were the crispiest hash-browns I have ever had. He also understands eggs over easy. Not paying attention, when ordering got me two sausage links instead of patties like the SO. I do prefer a patty over a link.   The SO got three pancakes with his breakfast and they were served a light golden color. They were served hot, making it easy for the packaged "whipped spread" to melt before adding the maple syrup. They were good, but I want real butter on my pancakes.   I will not make a special trip from the city to eat here, but when we are going to Costco and want breakfast before shopping we'll be back.

When I saw a new Mexican restaurant was opening in my neighborhood, I moaned and groaned. We already had three within walking distance of my house and none of them impressed me. That is until now. Today El Tapatio opened and they impressed me from the salsa to the flan. They are a welcome addition to my hood and the other Mexican restaurants should be concerned that there is a new Amigo in town.  I started out with a Margarita. It was okay, typical mix type Margarita that you find at most Mexican restaurants of this price point. I wasn't expecting a made to order, hand shaken one. I knew it was a mix. It still was a nice beverage to sip while munching on warm chips dipped in a spicy chunky salsa.   The BF ordered the Burritos Tipicos and gave both burritos a thumbs up. One was a beef and bean and the other chicken and bean. Both were smothered in cheese sauce and topped with lettuce, pico de gallo, sour cream, guacamole and their special red sauce. I got to sample each and they were very good and we both were impressed with the pico de gallo.   So I could experience a little more then one thing, I ordered a Create Your Own Platter. I choose three items; Soft Shredded Chicken Taco, Beef Tips Burrito and a Pork Tamale. They were served with Mexican Rice and re-fried beans. I was impressed on all items.   Soft Taco - Filled with well seasoned white chicken meat, shredded lettuce and cheese sauce. The soft tortilla was perfect, not over chewy as I've found at other local restaurants.   Burrito - Beef tips were tender and topped with just enough red sauce for an added flavor booster.   Tamale - Best I have had in St. Louis. These Tamale put those down on Cherokee to shame.   Mexican Rice - Moist, mixed with a few corn kernels and just lightly seasoned.   Beans - So good with the chips that we had left in the basket.   Dessert - Best Flan I have had in the city. Hopefully they'll stop putting the whipped cream and sprinkles on top, because it is so good, you do not need that distraction.   Service on their first day was okay. They were attentive as they filled up fast. It is amazing how fast word spread that the open sign had finally been turned on. We meet Alex the owner and chatted with a couple of the servers, I think this will be a popular new restaurant in my hood and am glad it is close enough for me to walk.

My mama told me, you better shop around Oh yeah, you better shop around. When Smokey Robinson sang those words years ago, it was about love. Recently, I learned it is also true about rocks. Who would have ever though the price of rock would differ so greatly, but they did. What amazed us most was that the larger and furthest businesses from the city were the most expensive.   After "shopping around", we found the best price for Iowa Rainbow to be at Brentwood Material. Being novices at buying rock they showed us how to figure out the amount we'd need to fill in a 2 1/2' x 13' area. After moving 3/4 of a ton of rock, I can tell you it is a gym workout. However, never having to mow that small area between our house and sidewalk is a win.   Good Pricing and Good Customer Service has Brentwood Material Co. leading the pack.

Pizza delivery be gone, I no longer need you. I will gladly order my pizza and salads from Station Pizzeria and go pick them up myself.  I want quality over the convenience of delivery.   Tonight we dined on their house salad with house dressing.  A good mixture of iceberg, romaine, onion, pimento, provel and Parmesan.  As stated n my previous review, I like that the pieces are actual bite size and do not need to be re-cut to enjoy.  Their house dressing is a Italian vinaigrette, which adds the perfect touch to the salad.   Our pizza was The Godfather, a flavorful mixture of sausage, pepperoni, mushroom, green pepper and onion. For an extra kick we had them add jalapeno. With or without the jalapeno peppers this is an excellent pizza. It's a traditional St. Louis thin crust, but is cut into pie shaped pieces, not squares.   If you love pizza and have not had one from here yet, you do not know what you are missing. I suggest that you correct that situation as soon as possible.

To our surprise, this was some of the best Tex-Mex we've had in Saint Louis. The biggest surprise was that it is in Overland and not down on Cherokee Street.  We discovered Las Palmas through a Entertainment.com Coupon and when I checked it out here on Yelp, several of my friends had given them 4 Stars. So we thought why not give them a try.   The SO had an ice tea, but when I'm having Mexican fare, I need a Margarita. Theirs is made with a good mix, it's not too sweet and not too sour. It's just the right mix and they do not skimp on the booze either. One Margarita at lunch had a nice punch.   They were quick to bring chips and they bought us two small dishes of salsa. When the server sat them down,  I asked him if one was spicier. He informed us  they were the same. How cool, we each got our own dish to dip our chips. No need to worry about double dipping.  The chips were fresh and still warm when they arrived to our table.  We also experienced their Cheese Dip which was the typical white cheese dip that you get at most inexpensive Tex-Mex restaurants.  Our entrees is what separated Las Palmas from the other Tex-Mex places we've been to. Both side dishes really shined. The Cilantro Lime rice was a pleasant change from the traditional Spanish Rice. It was moist and refreshing. Their re-fried beans were a nice change too. You could actually see beans, in a spicy thick broth.   The Burrito Supreme was huge. It was packed tight with beef and topped with melted cheese and sour cream. A side of Guacamole was the perfect accompaniment. My Pollo Ranchero was a burst of flavor. The grilled chicken, big pieces of pepper, onion, black olives and broccoli. They served it with some fresh flour tortillas. I filled two of the tortillas, but the chicken and veggies were so good I finished mine without using anymore tortillas.   We ended the feast with an appropriate dessert, Flan. When ever I see Flan on a menu, I have to order it and I am glad I did so here. This is best Flan I have had and I had to share it. Next time I'll know better and order my own.   Our server was good, but he was rather quite. I don't think he spoke that much English.

My first use of Uber was in NOLA and loved it. It was so easy and simple. Not to mention the huge price difference from the cab companies. When I arrived I at the New Orleans Passenger Terminal, I hadn't used my Uber app yet, so I just hailed a cab. The short ride to my hotel was $12 +tip = $15. I was more organized on my departure and used Uber and my ride back to the station was $6.07. That's a major savings, even with a 50% tip.   I was amazed how quickly my driver arrived. I requested my ride on the app, got my confirmation of driver, make of car and price. In the meantime, I was claiming my stored luggage from the concierge and noticed my ride was already pulled up outside. Wow - that was fast. The car was in pristine condition and the young lady presented herself professionally.  She even helped place my luggage in the trunk, which was way more then what the cab driver did.   If you need a ride in the  French Quarter, after drinking too much? Or just to get to the other side of town, I highly recommend getting your ride from Uber.   When: August 29, 2016 Why: Needed a ride

Excellent breakfast! With Eclipse being attached to a hotel, going in I was a little concerned about the quality.  My experience with restaurants attached to hotels has not been good in the past, but Eclipse has totally changed my opinion.   Our breakfast started out with a spicy and flavorful Bloody Mary. I enjoyed a Three Egg Omelet with bacon, onion and pepper jack cheese. I'm trying to go low carb, so our server was very accommodating and allowed me to substitute my side of hash browns with asparagus. My omelet was fluffy, filled with the bacon and onion and had the cheese melted and poured on top. It was a delightful twist, to the typical cheese inside.   My dining partner enjoyed Eggs Benedict with asparagus and a side of Hash Browns.  For a hotel and only $9, this was an impressive Eggs Benedict. We both enjoyed the asparagus, it was done to perfection. Butter, a dash of salt and steamed to a perfect snap. The Hash Browns were served crispy, my favorite way. I had to be strong and stay low-carb.   Good friendly service, great food and free valet parking makes Eclipse worthy of my Breakfast,Bloody Mary and Benedict list.

For me this AC does a good job.   I primarily use them for my shirts and slacks. I'll admit when it comes to my clothes, I'm high maintenance. I separate my shirts in separate piles, for different starch levels and those shirts I want dry cleaned. They've never gotten them mixed up and they are always done well.  I also bring in all of my dress and casual slacks. On occasion, I have brought in jeans to have them heavily starched. As I've stated before, I wish they'd do a light starch on my Docker's. When needed, they've also done an excellent job on my suits and sport coats.   AC use to only take cash or check and now they take debit and credit cards. To be honest, this use to be the only place I wrote checks. Being someone who does a lot of dry cleaning, I am thankful they send out coupons on the regular. If I run out, I can also print them out on the company website.   I'll be back? - Almost every 10 days.   When: Way to often.  Why: Gotta look good.

To my surprise, I have found the perfect breakfast at the Living Room. It may not be perfect for you, but for me it fills all of my morning cravings. The Biscuit Breakfast includes; asiago cheddar cheese biscuit, a soft boiled egg covered in white cheddar and peppered bacon. Egg, bacon and biscuit. A farm boy couldn't ask for more.   The biscuits are drop biscuits, not those cookie cutter type that you find at other restaurants.  Being asiago cheese makes them better, then a typical buttermilk. I enjoy how they serve the egg & bacon in a small bowl. The presentation is simple, your soft boiled egg is covered with melted white cheddar and three slices of peppered bacon are cut in half and standing upright along one side of the bowl. The bowl is then placed on a plate with the biscuit and a tiny cup filled with fresh butter. The numerous times I have had this breakfast, the soft boiled egg has always been done to perfection.  Recently I have become addicted to cold brew, so it should be no surprise to me hear me say, that I love their Bitt's Cold Brew. I drink mine black, no sugar or cream and it is smooth and refreshing.   The ambiance is a simple causal rustic and the staff is super friendly. They treat you as if you were visiting them in their "living room". The only downside is that they are closed on Monday. Making it one less day that I can enjoy my cold brew and breakfast at the Living Room.

We all know that the Humane Society of Missouri is a great place to adopt a new Fur-Baby and a place where you can get very affordable veterinary  care for your pet. What a lot of people do not know that they are also a place to go when your beloved pet has crossed the Rainbow Bridge. For those of you who do not know what the Rainbow Bridge is, here is a link to help you understand. http://rainbowsbridge.com/poem.htm  Last week my neighbors feline friend of 20 years, crossed the bridge peacefully at home.  As any one of us pet lovers would be, he was a little distraught. So I assisted him in wrapping Thomas up and taking him to the HSMO for cremation.  The staff was very compassionate and caring as they filled out the necessary paperwork. They offer a variety of urns and boxes for the ashes, but with Brian being a woodsman he opted for the ashes to be returned in a simple bag and he'll create something special for his beloved friend.   Some may think it is creepy to save the ashes of a pet, but some of us don't. So it is good to know that this type of service is available at a very reasonable price.  Our pets gave us unconditional love. So the least we can do is give them a proper ending.

A great mom & pop donut shop. Staff is friendly and the coffee is strong and fresh. When visiting a new donut shop I judge them on two basic donuts, Chocolate Long John and Glazed Donut Holes and Mister Donut does them right. The LJ was moist and the chocolate icing was perfectly smeared end to end. I've been a sucker for holes since I was a child. I really love them now, eating a couple holes satisfies my cravings for an entire donut.   I noticed they offer other breakfast items as well, especially Biscuits and Gravy. I may have to leave for work a little extra early some day and see if they are worthy of being on my Biscuits and Gravy List.

Scarlett, I'm going to be honest with you, it took several visits for me to become a fan. However, I saw the potential  that you had and kept coming back to give you a second, third and finally a fourth chance. On that magical fourth visit we finally clicked and now I can sing your praises.  I'm confident those earlier visits were growing pains and you got all the kinks worked out and you're now a favored spot in the CWE.   What won me over on the fourth visit was the Pan Seared Norwegian Salmon. Once I saw that on the menu, I knew I had to go beyond the booze. It was a healthy portion of salmon, served with potato gnocchi, prosciutto, asparagus and tomatoes in a light garlic cream sauce. I love salmon and this entrée inspired me to create a List on Yelp to give shout outs to those who do it well. You will be my first addition to this list.   Normally I am not a dessert person, but Bread Pudding is one dessert that can always win me over. I especially was excited to see Pumpkin Brioche Bread Pudding with Cinnamon Ice Cream and Maple Syrup on your menu. However, my heart sank when I was informed that it had been replaced by, Triple Berry Bread Pudding. I would have preferred the pumpkin, but the Triple Berry satisfied my Sweet Tooth (another list for you to be one).   Prior to my fourth visit, the customer service lacked. That is why; I'd have only one, maybe two drinks and move on to other locations for dinner. This time, even with the same staff, it was a different game. They were spot on, offering friendly & professional service. Sitting at the bar, they made me feel totally welcomed and were attentive to my needs and those around me. Much, much better then my earlier visits.   Would I come back? Absolutely. I got to try the Brunch and Flatbreads.   When: October 15, 2016 Why: Dinner

I can not believe it, no one has written a review for this great co-op boutique. I was here for a Halloween party before their opening and just now got back to actually shop. I am now remorseful for not returning sooner.   There are about 40+ vendors offering all sorts of goodies. Ranging from clothing for women and men, to hand made soaps, posters, candies, candles and so much more. One vendor offers some very creative and tasteful stationary. I'm a sucker for note cards and thank you cards.   Next time you are downtown, make it a point to stop by and shop this "Collective" boutique. Chances are you will find something to your liking. I did. I love my new poster/map that shows all the neighborhoods in Saint Louis. Now I know where all the Yelp Dukedoms are located. Also, the Milk Chocolate Triple Dipped Malt Balls from, Oh Lolli Lolli melted in my mouth. Yes I am dieting, but I can still have a treat and these malt balls were truly a treat.

We all know that Four Muddy Paws is a great place to get "quality" dog food for our Fur-Babies, but did you know it is also where Santa Paws shops?   FMP has an extensive selection of collars and leashes. Our Buddy, got a set earlier this year and our two other Fur-Babies have put new ones on the top of their list.  Looking at their variety, we found Curious George, Fleur de Lis, a colorful Peacock type and a studded leather. So you can see whatever your dogs personality may be, FMP will have a collar to fit it.   Our Fur-Babies treat their toys differently. Two play with plush toys and they still look as good as the day they received them. Our other dog is another story. She needs the type of toys that cannot be destroyed, she is very playful and destructive. We have to keep their toys separate and schedule their playtime with toys separately. Their Christmas Stockings will be stuffed with toys from FMP.   We'll be leaving cookies out for Santa Clause and Santa Paws will be leaving Christmas themed treats from Treats Unleashed for our four legged friends. They are also available at Four Muddy Paws, making it a one stop shopping experience this holiday season.

I arrived extremely early for a dinner with friends at Preston's, so I popped in at The Chase Club for a cocktail. I arrived the same time as a huge group of Wells Fargo sales representatives were arriving for a conference. I thought it would take forever to get a drink, with this large group all descending on the bar at once. To my surprise, the bartenders hustled and had us all enjoying our drinks in a timely fashion.   I'm normally a vodka man, but recently I have fallen in love with Manhattan's. A Manhattan is a classic cocktail. Like a martini it is strong, so I sip it and enjoy it for a longer period of time. The Chase Club makes their Manhattan's with Marker's Mark. I watched my bartender make my Manhattan and I was pleased to see he stirred it. I prefer my martini's to be shaken, but I like my Manhattan's stirred. Trust me it makes a difference.  As a bar for Happy Hour, I'd say the Chase Club is A-OK. It's a great hotel lobby bar.   When: June 6, 2016 Why: Happy Hour - Manhattan

Great service and Great food! Our last visit was a simple meal, salads and mussels and if anyone knows me, they know I love "mussels".   The SO enjoyed a Beet Salad with Goat Cheese and I had the Caesar Salad. Both were very good, but the Beet Salad was the best. I loved the large thick slices, topped with Goat Cheese. The Romaine Lettuce in my Caesar Salad was diced and cut into bite size pieces and coated in the appropriate amount of dressing.   We both took advantage of the nightly special of, Prince Edward Island Mussels. They were so good, we easily could have ordered a third bowl to share. PEI Mussels in a White Wine and Garlic broth is always a winner for me.   Everyone who works here is friendly and attentive to the diners needs. We always feel welcomed here with their warm hospitality. Once again, I am so glad Mathew's is in my neighborhood.

Once again, I am thankful I bought my deck of Taste Cards on LivingSocial. I never would have thought of coming to The Shack, but when you give me $10 off my $30 purchase I'm ready to go.   Before arriving, we researched their website and knew we'd start out with their Fried Pickles. Fried Pickles is one of my new addictions and when I see them on a menu, I order them. These were the first that did not impress me. We both thought that they were heavy on the breading, which killed the dill pickle taste. They came with a TK dipping sauce that I found to be flavorless. The fried pickles actually tasted better without the sauce. Next visit I will try the Green Eggs & Ham Loaded Fries, friends have informed me they are the best way to start your Shack visit.  OMG! I enjoyed the Pastrami Sandwich and it is now my favorite Pastrami in Saint Louis. It was served on the best Marble Rye bread, that was so soft and flavorful, that I had to ask where they got it. It came from Fazio's on The Hill. It was packed full of juicy Pastrami and Swiss Cheese. Look at my close-up photo and see how thick this amazing sandwich was. It came with a side of Idaho House Cut French Fries, that were lightly seasoned with salt. I love a fry that still has the potato skin on. They could have been a little crisper, but they still were the perfect side to my Pastrami.   The BF enjoyed the Southern Fried Salad. It had big chunks of chicken tenders tossed with Iceberg lettuce in a Ranch dressing. Ordering a salad at a place that primarily serves pub grub is crazy. It was way to much Iceberg for me and way to much dressing. I highly recommend getting the dressing on the side, to avoid the overdressed salad.   Our waitress was nice, as was the busboy. The busboy was actually friendlier and more attentive. The day manager even stopped by our table to make sure everything was OK and thanked us for coming in.   I'll be back to enjoy a burger and beer and hopefully it will be cooler weather and all the garage doors will be open connecting the patio and bar area.  I loved the sign at the entrance, telling you no one under the age of 21 after 9 PM. What a shame they have to wait till 9 PM to enforce this rule.

Pop's Blue Moon is the Grandaddy of all dive bars. The decor is tacky, the building is in need of renovation and plaster is falling from the ceiling. All of that makes for a dive bar full of charm, warmth and coziness.   They offer cheap beer, of course Blue Moon and I was pleased they offered Schlafly's APA on draft. I was also impressed with the selection of brand names that you could call for your liquor drinks. Some regular bars don't offer the selection that Pop's has.   Our bartender was friendly and personable. I thought he looked like one I would see at Bad Dog or JJ's Clubhouse. The other patrons come and go, some stay to themselves and others will enjoy conversation with newbies. I had a fun time and would love to go back and enjoy some live music.   Remember, Pop's only takes cash. So don't leave home without it, because there's no  ATM to save your ass.

I wanted something new and different for breakfast and lucky for me I found The Barn. I had to scroll deep in to my "breakfast" search on Yelp to find my new adventure and to my surprise it was only 7 miles from house. How could I have been missing out on something this good? I have a lot of catching up to do, to experience the entire menu.  This morning I did a little role playing and ordered, "The Ranch Hand Breakfast". It was a manly breakfast of Biscuits and Gravy with two eggs on the side. I had my eggs scrambled, my new obsession with eggs. The B&G were a huge serving of milk pan gravy covering flaky biscuits. I must say, I have a new winner of a Stevie B Awards in the category of Best Biscuits and Gravy.   My dining companion ordered Eggs Benedict with Barn Browns as his side. Barn Browns is a creative name of Hash Browns. Whenever he orders Eggs Benedict out, I cringe in fear. He is a Benedict snob and I always have the fear they are not going to be up to his standard. We had a winner and I got to sample a bite. The eggs were done to perfection and the Hollandaise sauce was impressive for a small cafe. They even served up the Hash Browns, I mean Barn Browns, extra crispy without even having to request them that way.   Working weekends, Tuesday is my weekend so I enjoyed an early morning Bloody Mary. I ordered mine Hot, with UV Sriracha Vodka. The glass was rimmed in spicy salt and garnished with three olives and a lemon slice. Oddly it was served in a short glass, but it was big on flavor.   Service is relaxed and friendly and the ambiance is warm and cozy. This little gem is definitely in my breakfast rotation. Good food, good service and the prices are very affordable. If you are looking for a simple place to enjoy a breakfast out, check out The Barn.

Out of all the Dry Cleaners in my neighborhood, this is the one choose. I am a loyal patron, I enjoy the fact that they call me by name when I enter the store. I get all my dress shirts, suits, coats and even get my jeans starched here.  My only wish they would starch my dockers. The customer service is friendly, they all are very personable.

I recently had lunch at Fazoli's and was pleasantly surprised. Earlier that morning had oral surgery and was given eating guidelines for the next couple of days. Nothing chewy or crunchy, which meant no steak or crunchy tacos. I was told soft foods, were the way to go.  When I got home from surgery, I took one of those "fabulous" pain pills and took a late morning nap. I can see how & why Rush Limbaugh likes them so well. Any way when I woke up I was hungry and ready to eat. My mind went to work on soft foods and all it could think of was Ted Drew's and Mr. Wizard's. I was tempted, but knew custard was not a good lunch idea and remembered there was a Fazoli's near my home and pasta was soft. So off to Fazoli's I drove.  When I arrived I was shocked at the selection available on their menu. It definitely was more then I anticipated. So I could experience more then just one item, I ordered the "Classic Sampler". It was a trio consisting of; Fettuccine Alfredo, Meat Lasagna and Spaghetti with Meat Sauce. I also got to choose between a slice of pizza or salad as a side dish. I went with Cheese Pizza thinking the salad would be to crunchy.  Of the trio, I liked the Spaghetti with Meat Sauce the best. It was head and shoulders better then what The Spag Fag down on Lacledes Landing serves and this is fast food.  The Fettuccine was off, or my numb mouth just wasn't tasting it. Their Lasagna is basically the spaghetti, just a different noodle and cheese added to make it a different dish. My slice of pizza wasn't anything to write home about, so I won't write about it here either.  Now for the breadsticks - these would be like crack to the Pillsbury Dough Boy. I only had two and was instantly addicted. Wish I never learned the fact that you can buy them by the dozen. They are buttery,  soft and oh so much garlic. They'll be a perfect snack with a glass of red wine while watching True Blood.  I'll be back and not just for the Breadsticks, I want to try a few other entrees when I'm in need of a quick meal. Perhaps I'll make it my destination after future dental appointments.

I am glad and sorry I discovered this store. It can be a dangerous place for someone who has an addiction to M&M's and Jelly Belly's. They have both in bulk bins, allowing me to buy my favorite flavors of Jelly Belly's or my favorite color of M&M's.   I was in need of little individual bags of the Jelly Belly Cocktail Classics and was having no luck in finding them in the city. Sweet Be's had the Cocktail Classics in bulk. A distinguish gentleman who assisting shoppers told me if i bought it bulk, the young lady at the counter would bag in separate small bags and bow them for me.  What a deal. I bought about 1 1/2 lb. and she did her magic separating in to 8 little clear bags with orange (my signature color) bows. They're gong to be perfect gifts on Jelly Bean Day which happens to be on July 24th.   While shopping the BF called, so I asked what treat could I bring home. I was told, chocolate, toffee and caramel. So I found funkychunky - Sea Salt Caramel, which was a tasty blend of popcorn, chocolate, caramel, cashews & sea salt. You talk about a tasty treat, it was sweet and salty.   Candy galore, unique gifts and excellent customer service from Sweet B's is going to have me returning for more sweet treats.

My skin crawled when I walked into this new Hobby Lobby. However, I realized sometimes you have to put political choices & opinions aside when you are shopping for specific items for your DIY art project.   I will admit that HL does have some great items for all sorts of DIY projects. However, I will also admit, their store is poorly organized and laid out. Also, it could use some serious signage to make it easier to find the items you are shopping for. None of the aisles were tagged as to what is in them. I had to search up and down until  I found one item on my project list. I had to search long and hard to find it.  While browsing the store looking for my creative tools, I did find some great future gifts for friends and family. I also saw some decorative items that just may find their way into my home.  Customer service on the sales floor and from the cashier was lacking. I can only imagine what I may have spent if I actually had gotten assistance and was made welcome in the store.   When: June 22, 2016 Why: Big Creative Art Project.

Like Danielle B., I had never been to a Red Mango before until just the other day. My Yelp friend Kat V. asked me to join her for lunch at RM and I said, "sure, what time". After we settled on a time, I had to go  do a Yelp search to find out what Red Mango was all about.  Being new to RM, I let Kat give me guidance and she recommended a Smoothie for my first visit. I went with Mixed Berry and was not disappointed. It was good to see that they use "fresh fruit" and not frozen.  We sat there in RM and chatted, but if I were shopping I could so easy see stopping here first and sipping my smoothie while I shopped.   Now that I know about Red Mango, I will stop by on my next visit to West County Centre and try their fro yo. I was tempted by many of their flavors and the toppings oh, so many to choose from were presented in a clean and organized case.   Another big plus for Red Mango, is that the website provides all the nutritional  facts of the smoothies and fro yo. Which is good to know for those of us who are trying to prevent their waist from getting larger.

I'm sure what I am about to say is not that original, but it is so appropriate. The Stellar Hog, serves up some "stellar" BBQ. A few friends had given TSH a try and gave me the push to go try them for myself.   On my first visit, I was so disappointed. Not disappointed in the food, but with myself. I thought I was extra hungry so I ordered the small version of the, Pulled Pork Fries as an appetizer. Their idea of small and my idea, are two different servings. I was stuffed like a Thanksgiving turkey after enjoying these fries. It was like nachos on crack. A mountain of crisp french fries was piled up on a quarter sheet tray and then covered with chili and pulled pork. That's off the chain!   When I came back to try more of the menu, I got smart and skipped breakfast. It guaranteed I'd be extra hungry and have room for more food.  I knew I had to have more of that chili. So I started my lunch off with a cup. This is the type of chili I'd want on my Chili-Mac and perhaps a Slinger, too.   Today I had a Brisket Sandwich. It was tender as tender could be. They get major bonus points with me for cutting theirs thick. I absolutely hate paper thin cut brisket. I'm a meat man and I want my meat, meaty. I also, liked the crisp edges around the brisket. As a side, I enjoyed more of their crip fries, without all the toppings.   As I chatted with Alex the Pit Master, I discovered all the sides are made in house. I will gradually work my way through them all. He gave me a sampling of the cole slaw and it was amazing. It has citrus juices in the dressing and it is like no other slaw in STL.   The Stellar Hog is not Alex's first rodeo. He was the original Pit Master at Adam's Smokehouse on Watson, so he definitely knows his way around a BBQ Pit. I am excited to try more of his menu and look forward to being a regular at TSH.   During good outdoor weather, the patio is dog friendly.   Will I return? - Gotta try the ribs and burgers.  When: November 16 & 30, 2017 Why: Duh, BBQ!

Has anyone mentioned the view in their review of Cielo? Of course they have, how could you not mention the spectacular view. This rooftop is the perfect place to meet friends for drinks and relax in the big comfortable chairs.  When it gets dark and the flame above the water fountain is turned on, the ambiance increases three fold.   Brad and I meet up with a group of friends who spent the day at The Four Seasons Spa for a Bachelorette party. Yes, we were the only men included for the party and the girls already had their drink on when we caught up with them on the rooftop.   The drinks are on the pricey side, but they are made with a hearty pour. My drink of the night was the Cucumber Fizz, which is made with Cucumber Vodka and Ginger Ale with Fresh Mint. They went down so smooth.   The wait staff was attentive and made sure that entire group was having a good time. Other groups sitting around us, joined in our celebration and fun making it one big party.   The only thing that stopped me from giving a 5 Star rating was the music. The mix just didn't fit the mood and atmosphere.  Three Dog Night was the first concert that I attended at Kiel Auditorium, but hearing "Momma Told Me Not To Come" just didn't feel right.

Last night I died, I mean dined and went to foodie heaven. I was lucky enough to be a guest of fellow Yelper, Joshua H. who had a gift card for two to enjoy an evening at TCP. This has to be one of the most unique and flavorful restaurants to open in Saint Louis.   I arrived early and positioned myself at the bar to enjoy a cocktail. Their menu of specialty cocktails was impressive. I choose, Final Word, because I am a fan of Rye. FW was a mixture of, High West Double Rye, Green Chartreuse, Luxardo Liqueur and Lemon. It was oh, so refreshing.   We started out with two of their Shareable's. I'm a fan of brussels sprouts and deviled eggs, so it was an easy choice for me. The Chicken Fried Brussels Sprouts was a very original take on my favorite vegetable. The coating was a true fried chicken coating and the sprouts were soft, but still had a good snap to them. If you like sprouts, I highly recommend these.  Our other shareable was the, Barbecue Chicken Deviled Eggs. If your a fan of deviled eggs, I can tell you these are not the ones your grandma brings to the family picnic. These are smoked chicken topped deviled eggs with crispy chicken skins. The STL BBQ sauce blended with the yolk gives it a special kick. The eggs are then served on top of pickled sweet peppers and kale for a stunning presentation.   My entree made me go weak in the knees. I had the Seared Diver Scallops. Scallops are my favorite seafood and this dish may now be my favorite scallop entree in STL. It was four huge, perfectly seared scallops served as a very autumn dish. They were accompanied with butternut squash puree, pumpkin relish, smoked mushrooms and crispy brussels sprouts leaves. I was in total foodie heaven.   To close out the eventing my dessert was, Candy Bar. It was a sugar rush for sure. Maple bacon, ice cream, hazelnut, toffee, caramel and milk chocolate = decadent dessert. Loved it!!!  The ambiance is industrial chic and very relaxing. My service at the bar was extremely attentive and the cocktails masterfully made. I also like that they have outlets under the bar for those of us who need to charge up so we can keep up with our social media. Our table service was provided by Jackson and he too did an excellent job giving white linen service to this new trendy restaurant.    I'll be back? - Can't wait to return.   When: November 14, 2018 Why: Hot & New and a guest of fellow Yelper.

Andy,   I will never cheat on you with another custard stand. You are by far my favorite custard in STL. In the past I have had brief love affairs with a Wizard and a Ted, but neither of them satisfied my sweet tooth and ice cream (custard) craving like you do. You're consistently rich and creamy. Also, your portion of mixers are always the right amount and are blended throughly thru out the concrete.   I live smack dab in the middle of your Richmond Heights and Kirkwood locations. So if I do cheat on you, it will be with another Andy's. Living so close to two of your custard shops, is a curse to my waistline, but it is a curse I am willing to live with. I just need to enjoy your decadence in moderation.   Love ya,  StevenB  Will I return? You bet, I will.   When: August 11, 2017 (Friday) Why: Love Affair with Andy

I wish I had children so I could take them to the City Museum. It is such a fun place to play. It can bring out the inner child in all of us, so I guess I could go alone and just have fun.   Recently the Oscar Road Trip made a stop at City Museum and it was the perfect place for all of us movie buffs to have our fantasies come true of winning an Oscar. Or at least hold it for a brief moment and pretend that it is ours.   Come and play, everything is okay at the City Museum. It's a fun place for kids of all ages.

St. Louis Magazine did an article on, "5 Items Under $10 to try this August" and TOD was featured. The featured diner special, was their Ying-Yang. You ask, what is a Ying-Yang? It's a classic, Slinger with both Chili and Gravy on top. Yes, instead of having to choose your favorite topping of gravy or chili on your Slinger, Tiffany's gives you both.   What also surprised me, is I got to choose my meat. I didn't have to have the usual hamburger on my Slinger. I got to choose between, sausage, bacon or the traditional hamburger. I went with, sausage. My two eggs, I had fried hard. When having a Slinger, i don't want a runny yolk.   The Hashbrowns at Tiffany's are homemade. They make them from scratch, everyday. That's true dedication, if they have the patience to boil, peel and grate potatoes daily. That's true diner love. You can't tell under the gravy & chili, but it was perfectly divided. Each side of my plate had an egg, sausage patty and a serving of the delicious hashbrowns.   The coffee that TOD serves, is from their neighbor down the street, The Living Room. That guarantees you a good strong cup morning brew. It's always nice to see local businesses supporting each other. Another local biz that TOD supports is, Happy Dog Hot Sauce. I've always been a fan and was excited to see that they sell it as a retail item. The server/cook told me it is a favorite of their customers and that is why they decided to start selling it.   TOD, is a true diner experience. There are no booths or tables. Everyone sits at the counter and watch your diner comfort food be prepared right before you. The crowd itself can be entertaining and the regulars will include newbies in their conversations.   If you haven't been, I recommend a visit to Tiffany's Original Diner. After dining there, you can tell your friends you had, "Breakfast at Tiffany's".   I'll be back? - Yes, I want to try a burger.   When: August 7, 2019 Why: St. Louis Magazine article.   Notes: Free Wi-Fi and Cash Only, but ATM on site.

SHOW ME THE MONEY!!!  Who would have ever thought that a tiny little shack of a building on South Kingshighway would be the best place to sell your old gold and sterling silver.  It is such a small place that I actually passed it twice before realizing which building it was.   Once you are inside, you'll realize there are no thrills here, it is strictly business. You're there to sell and they're buying. No need for a fancy store. For security you'll be buzzed in or the big burly security guard will open the door.    When it is your turn, you'll show them what you have to sell and they will test it, separate by k count and type of metal. Next they'll compute the figures and tell you a shocking $ amount. I got double of what I was anticipating and they pay cash on the spot.    Raymond F. is right, they pay better then their competitors in the city and county.  When selling precious metals it is always better to shop around, but KSDK got that consumer report right.   The only negative and I will not subtract a star for it, is the location. When I left, I walked out alone and was approached by a street person. I just quickly got in my car before he could get closer and kept telling "no" to his request. If you hit a big pay out, ask if the guard can walk you back to your car.   So clean out those jewelry boxes and china cabinets and you too will be saying the classic line from Jerry McGuire, "Show me the money".

Alton Restaurant Week   Enjoyed their lunch special during ARW.  I enjoyed it so much, I'll definitely will be returning.  I enjoyed a, Beef Tenderloin Mushroom Melt with au jus and French Fries. It was marinated beef tenderloin tips topped with sautéed wild mushrooms and Swiss cheese, served on toasted French bread.   The sandwich was a good portion and the fries were crisp. It was a very filling lunch. Personally, I would have preferred, Provolone cheese on my sandwich, but the Swiss was fine. During this pandemic, I would have preferred the ketchup to have been served in a "little cup", but they did wipe down the bottles between diners.   The restaurant is in a space that was previously a store in a strip center, so it is a very vast space. Being a large open space, there's an echo, but not so much to disrupt your conversation.   The staff was doing a good job following CDC guidelines, making sure all guest were maintaining social distance and wearing mask. They also, did  a through job sanitizing when guest left.  In addition to providing, friendly and attentive service.   When: January 23, 2021 Why: Lunch - Alton Restaurant Week Jan-2021

Looking for a fun and cheap night out? You'll find it at Chimichanga's.  The ambiance is bright colors, the Margarita's are a pre-mix, but the liquor is poured heavy and the food is plentiful and affordable.   Stopped by on my way to a private party with a few other friends. We wanted to have a little something in our system before drinking with the big boys. I arrived first and snagged prince parking on the side of the building. As I approached the entrance, I was alerted to their security system. I was immediately put at ease. Check my pictures, to understand.   I went to their bar on the patio to wait for the others and ordered a Cadillac Margarita. It was served in a huge frosted mug. As stated in the intro, it was a pre-mix, but they definitely were not stingy with the booze.   Once my fiends arrived, we got a table inside due to the heat. I was hungry, but not that hungry, so I just ordered some Chicken Nachos. Jalapeños were not in the description, so I asked if they could be added. Our server, said no problem. When they arrived, I was impressed. Other casual Mexican restaurants when I ask them to be added, put them in a small dish on the side. Not here, they went ahead and topped my tortilla  chips with them. Nice!   It's a dive of a Mexican restaurant, but it's fun and the food is good for the price.   I'll be back? - Sure, I love a strong Margarita and cheap food.   When: July 11, 2018 Why: Pre-party eats

Andy, it's been two years since my last review and I want to let people I am still in love with you. I have pissed off some of my friends when I tell them, you are better then our hometown Ted.  However, once they come and visit you, they too start singing your praises.   Your custard is so much richer and creamier then your competitors in town. I'd be hard pressed to say which one of your many concretes is my favorite. I like the fact that you are constantly offering special flavors that tempt me to go beyond my traditional M&M. I recently had a love affair with your, Ooey Gooey (I think that is the name). I couldn't believe you had three of my favorite flavors all mixed into one delicious treat. If you made one with a Kit-Kat Bar, I'd be besides myself. I'd had to order a large instead of my typical small.   The staff at Andy's is always super friendly and always willing to assist you in selecting the best sweet treat.   Andy's is by far the best frozen custard in St. Louis. I am so happy to see them expanding with new locations. However, the Kirkwood one will always be my go to and favorite.   When: To embarrassed to tell how many times.  Why: Frozen Custard

Michaels you are so much better then Hobby Lobby. Your aisles are marked, making it so easy to shop your store. I was able to find what I needed for my DIY art project. I even found items to take it up an additional notch.   Your staff was helpful on the floor and your cashier made small talk that complemented my selections. Not being a crafter, I left your store feeling like a top designer and an established artist. Look out world, here I come.   When: June 22,2016 Why: Craft Project

It is November 11, 2011 aka 11-11-11 and it is your birthday. Where do you go for that special meal? The only logical place to go would be, Eleven Eleven Mississippi.   To show you how in demand eating at EEM on 11-11-11 was, the private dining/party rooms were booked 6 months ago and regular reservations closed over 2 months ago. Believe me, we kept checking for an opening.   Being determined to eat there on my special day, it was my double nickle (55) I showed up for lunch without a reservation. Upon arrival, the place was packed and you could feel the energy and excitement people felt for this once in a century date.   Not having a reservation, I sat at the bar and had a wonderful time chatting with all the other guest waiting for their tables to open up. I got to meet a set of twins and another gentleman also celebrating the same birthday. Also, the two working the bar were friendly and provided excellent service.   For my birthday lunch I selected, Eleven Eleven BLT with Spicy Fries and a glass of Pino Grigio (2). This BLT is not your typical BLT. Here at Eleven Eleven a BLT is; B=bourbon apples, L= Maine Lobster and T=Thyme. The sandwich is also accented with remoulade and watercress sprouts.   The BLT was light and refreshing. I wish the toast was sliced thinner, i pulled one slice off and ate it as an open faced sandwich. Their spicy fries were crisp and I liked the fact their was more pepper then salt in the seasoning.  Another bonus is that they serve your ketchup in a cup, no messy bottle on the table.   As a sweet treat, they treated me to an order of Gooey Butter Cake for dessert. Making a perfect ending for my celebration.  This is my 300th review on Yelp.

Love me some Four Muddy Paws. All of my dogs food and treats come from this pet boutique. I appreciate their attention to the the quality and manufacturing of the products that they carry in their inventory. I am a label reader and whatever I buy for my fur-babies has to be natural, made in the USA or Canada. My babies do not eat anything that is made/processed in China.   STL recently participated in Dining Out For Life. FMP may not be a restaurant, but they stepped up to the plate and offered 25% of their sales on May 2nd as a donation for this incredible charity to end HIV. Also, during the month of June they have stepped up shown their "Pride".   On the day of Dining Out, I had to stop by and grab some treats and a couple new bowls for my K-9's. To be honest, my K-9's did not need a new bowl. They have more then a soup kitchen, but who's counting.  Then during this month of "pride", I've stopped by to buy them special treats made by, Treats Unleashed another great and supportive company here in STL made to show the Rainbow.  Customer service here is always great. I am such a regular, that most of the staff knows my name. I highly recommend becoming a regular here, they'll track your purchases of dry food and after 10 purchases of the same size brand/size bag, your 11th one will be FREE. Gotta love that.   I'll be back? - If I don't, the dogs will lock me out of the house.   When: May 2 and June 15, 2019 (most recently) Why: Gotta keep the dogs happy

If size matter to you, this is the place for breakfast. The portions are so huge, I can't  finish a skillet or omelette. I always take at least a third of it home to enjoy the next day. BB&B is related to another of my favorite breakfast restaurants, The Boardwalk Cafe in Webster Groves. Now I can head south or west for a hearty breakfast.   Today I had The German Omelet, which was stuffed with sausage, peppers, onion, tomato and cheddar cheese. Going low-carb to lose weight, they accommodated me by replacing my hash browns with fresh sliced tomatoes. I also enjoyed a side of fresh spinach. My omelet was stuffed to the maximum and was extra fluffy too. I missed the hash browns, but the spinach & tomatoes were a satisfying substitution.   My DP went with a burger, the Double Bacon Cheeseburger. He raved, saying it was now his favorite in the city. He even went as far as saying, he liked it better then the burgers at Carl's Diner. The beef was hand pressed, well seasoned and prepared to perfection on a diner grill. The fries were crispy, making them a perfect accompaniment to this juicy, tasty diner burger.   Our server was friendly and made good recommendations from the menu. The ambiance is nothing to write home about. It is obvious it was an old Wendy's that became a BBQ place and is now BB&B. When its breakfast, diner food, I can deal with a divey, tacky decor.

I was so excited when Stein Mart opened a store closer to the city, I hated the drive out to Ballwin to get my SM fix. For those of you who are not familiar with SM it is a TJ Max and Home Goods in one store. When I shop SM my focus is the Men's Dept. and occasionally I wander into the home accessories. In the Men's Dept. I can always find a bargain. I start out with the sale racks, and work my out to the regular priced racked. You can find many designer names and some of SM name brands are just as good. Trust me I know, I am a clothes horse.   The sales clerks are friendly and helpful. On my last visit they were doing a floor change, and they informed me of the sale they were sitting up. Love 30% off already low prices.

Kohl's is better then TJ Max, Marshall's and even Stein Mart. I just wish they were at a better location so I'd remember to shop them more often. This location is not on my normal path for shopping so I have to make this a destination store.   Great for men's casual clothes and accessories. The home goods are pretty impressive as well.  I have gotten  several good deals on pots and pans and other kitchen goodies. Their prices were lower then BB&B.   Only downside is the customer service, it is bare bones. If you need assistance on the floor, good luck on finding someone.  The cashiers are perky and cheerful, just a shame they do not have the same type of associates on the sales floor. It pretty much is a self serve, self find department store.   Small warning to those who are claustrophobic, this store is cluttered. Very cluttered, they pack in as many racks and tables full of merchandise as they possibly can and that is why you save big $'s on your purchases.

Have you ever left home, going the opposite direction of your favorite gas station and realize you are down to two bars on your gas gage. Two bars is the danger zone and time to fill up. You're pressed for time and cannot turn around to go get gas at your normal station.  As you ponder your dilemma, you see a 7-11 ahead and it's one that has a gas station. My ass has just been saved.   For connivence it is a pay at the pump, so I am not tempted by that big Slurpee machine inside. I slide my card into the slot, answered all the questions and filled my CRV with gas. To my surprise it was the same price on credit, as I would have paid for paying with cash at my regular spot.  The lot where the gas pumps are located was litter free and the computer prompts were courteous. I was in and out with self service and that is the way I like it at 7-11.

It was time for our big girl Grace to get a new harness.  After shopping around without her,  we narrowed our selection down to those at Four Muddy Paws (no surprise to me), but I had to let the other half do the diligent research. On the big shopping day we loaded Grace into the CRV for a day out with daddies.  She felt so special, the two Shelties had to stay home and she had her two daddies all to herself.   Once we got to FMP, we realized how clueless we really were about  selecting a harness for a 65 lb. dog. Grace walks well on a lead, but at times she does have a mind of her own. Those city squirrels and rabbits always seem to catch her attention and a regular collar or Martingail collar just does not do give us the control we need.   Being clueless, Marty came to our rescue. He explained the difference between the variety of harnesses they carry and shared his own testimonial for the one he uses on his own dog. Marty even allowed Grace to try them on and adjusted them for her body frame. We tried two on, the second one she was in between sizes and it did not fit her body type properly. (We've all been there) So we went back to the first one for a second fitting. He was so patient with us and Grace. He made sure it was a good fit and that we understood how to make adjusts if needed. Now that she has a new Freedom Harness, I just know her being a good bitch she'll be wanting new coordinated collar and leash to match.   A special treat and I do mean treat was getting a free soft bite cookie with our Yelp check-in. Grace not only got a new harness, but she got a FREE cookie as well.  The Shelties were so jealous when she returned home from her outing. As if they're not spoiled themselves.

Stein Mart doesn't carry designers that you would typically know here in the midwest. In the mens department, a lot of the designers are those that you'd see in a pro golf shop or a mens boutique in Florida. You may not know them, but the designs and quality of merchandise are still top notch.   In fact, for me Stein Mart has practically become my go to place for shirts. I am one who is not afraid of color and the designers that SM stocks use a lot of color. When shopping, always be sure to check the clearance rack. I find most of my best shirts on these racks and who doesn't love to save a few dollars. Today I walked out with three short sleeved shirts for under $55 and one of them was 100% linen.   Other areas I always check out are mens socks, pet accessories and home entertaining items.  The customer service is friendly and when you need assistance on the sales floor, someone is always available.   I personally find better deals here, then I do at that Maxx store.   Will I return? - I am a clothes horse, what do you think?  When: March 11, 2020 Why: Spring is here, so I needed new short sleeve shirts.

Once again, I need that half star that Yelp does not allow us to have.  The food here is a solid 4 Stars. The service is 3 Stars, so this rating is actually a 3 1/2 Stars.   My go to's here are the Baby Spinach Salad, Grilled Salmon Filet and the Grilled Shrimp. The BSS is topped with crumbled Goat Cheese, Candied Walnuts and tossed in a Wild Berry Vinaigrette. I'm typically not a fan of walnuts and will pick them out, but not here. They have given me an appreciation of walnuts that I did not know I had. The dressing is also one of those restaurant vinaigrettes that I wish was sold in the bottle. Being a fan of Goat Cheese, I am pleased that they are generous with their crumbles.   The Grilled Shrimp is on the menu as an appetizer, but I order it as an entree. After my Baby Spinach Salad, these beautifully grilled shrimp are just enough to satisfy my hunger. I'd say in my humble opinion that they are better then some seafood restaurants.   My other favorite entree is the Grilled Salmon which is topped with a dill sauce. The filet is a large portion and is served with vegetable rice. I'd prefer a side of steamed vegetables, but the rice is still an except-able side dish. Again, it is a quality that you'd expect from a seafood restaurant.   The service can be hit or miss here. To be honest, if you have a male server, it is a hit. If your being served by a female, it is definitely going to be a miss. The male servers here are more friendly, attentive to details and make it a pleasant dining experience. The lady servers are less friendly, are slow, forget things and are more interested in turning the table then creating an enjoyable dining experience. I've been here enough, to be able to make this comparison.   Will I return? - Yes, with hopes of a male server  When: December 19, 2017 Why: Christmas with friends

Twisted Ranch, surprised the hell out of me. I'm not a "ranch" person so, I was in no hurry to go here. When I saw that there was a UYE on a Saturday that I was off from work, I thought, "why not give it a try". I was expecting chicken tenders, wings, salad and plain ole Ranch dressing. WOW! I had no idea there were so many different flavors of Ranch dressing and that it went with so many other foods.   They immediately won me over by having Fried Pickles. It came with two different Ranches for dipping. Being a fan of Jalapeños, I choose Jalapeño Popper and I don't remember. However, I can tell you I loved the Jalapeño Popper one. The coating on the pickles was coarse like bread crumbs, not a finely ground powder like many other places. I loved the texture, it made them stand out from the typical fried pickle.  For my entree, I went the safe route and ordered; the Twisted Ranch Burger. It was a 1 /2 lb prime ranch seasoned ground beef patty, grilled and garnished with lettuce, onion, tomato, pickle, choice of cheese. For me the cheese was Pepper Jack and for my ranch, I had to repeat Jalapeño Popper. All of this was served on a warm brioche bun. I like my burgers medium and they got the temp, right. I think ordering medium is more difficult then well done or rare. I recently went low-carb and I now dream of the fries served here and it ain't no nightmare, it's savory dreams.   Now let's talk cocktails. I started out with The Grinch, since it was the holidays and I had done some serious shopping before my arrival. I'm no Grinch, but I just had to try this green drink with a peppermint garnish. It was like the punch at a school dance, after one cup you've had enough. I then moved on to a very flavorful Bloody Mary, that spiced things up after the sweetness of the Grinch.   Our server Robin, was a rock star waitress. We were a large group of 12 and she didn't mind splitting checks and she kept everything straight and organized. The kitchen also did a great job getting the food out to the table in a timely manner.   My experience at this UYE was so positive, I will be returning to the Twisted Ranch to try other items on their twisted menu. I learned that Ranch goes well beyond the Buttermilk at Hidden Valley.   When: December 12, 2015 Why: UYE Luncheon

I had a delightful Sunday Brunch at Cafe Osage. It was a busy morning, but we were seated almost immediately. We were placed at a small cramped two top against the far wall next to a locked entrance. It was cozy, warm and had a great view for people watching.  I begun my Sunday Brunch the way I begin every Sunday Brunch, with a Bloody Mary. They use a house made mix, that had just enough spice and kick. Brad my dining companion started his with a Cherub's Cup and on round two of drinks, he switched over to a Bloody Mary after sampling mine.   So many menu items to choose from, we were so torn on what to order. I choose, 2 Eggs Your Way and my way was over medium. My meat was Nueske Bacon, a smoked apple-wood bacon. It was a thick cut and was fried crisp. It also came with Roasted Potatoes, which were cubed with skins on. I normally do not eat toast when having breakfast out, but when it is served with homemade jelly I chow down.   Brad enjoyed the Baked Eggs, which include spinach, shitake, basil and fontina. His side was a salad of mixed greens with fresh fruit, topped with a vinaigrette. As I stated, there were so many good items on the menu, that we had to share a couple of sides to experience more. We shared an order of Cheese Grits and Bison Sausage, plus they allowed us to have a half order of Biscuits and Gravy.   I had to experience their B&G, because they are not your normal biscuits and gravy.  They use cheddar & chive biscuits topped in gravy made of creamed chicken, mushrooms and leeks. It takes this traditional breakfast dish to an entirely different level.   Our service was friendly and our server kept up with the fast high pace of the morning. Their sugar bowl needs a special shout out. I always add a restaurant to my Rainbow of Sweetness list for having the blue, pink and yellow artificial sweeteners. Cafe Osage also offers the green and raw which truly covers all the sweetness a person could ask for.   I will be back for a regular day breakfast.   When: December 15, 2013 Why: Brunch

When I saw that another Mexican restaurant was opening near my house, I rolled my eyes. I already have four. Do I really need a fifth one?
