Last night I went to One Way Cafe and Bar and answered my own question. Yes, I do. I was totally surprised by the quality of food at a very affordable price.   As other reviewers have stated, the chips and salsa are average. Hey, they're complimentary so average is good. To kick it up little I ordered a side of Cheese Dip and that made mine more enjoyable. Next time, I will try the Guacamole.   My server was attentive and very chatty. When I arrived, I was craving Nachos. However, as we talked he recommended the Tamales and said he preferred the beef over the chicken. I went with his recommendation and he gave good advice. What makes their tamales unique is that they wrap them in banana leaves instead of corn husk. It gives them a slightly different texture and flavor.   Driving by you can miss it, as it sits back from the other buildings. It is smack dab in between Midwest Money & Hampton Shoe. The restaurant is small and intimate with a larger patio when weather is permitting.   The staff is extremely attentive and friendly. I was impressed that they talked about their menu and described their offering. It was obvious that they are proud of what they are doing.    I'm looking forward to them obtaining their liquor license, so I can enjoy a Margarita. Until then, I don't mind drinking a diet Coke.   Will I return? - Yes, and I'll pass three other Mexican restaurants to get here.   When: November 1, 2017 Why: Dinner

Some of you may say that I am lazy, but I say my time is valuable. I'd rather be out experiencing a new bar or restaurant, then sweating as I mowed my lawn. Yes, I could save money doing it myself. However, as Miss Dolly Levi said in Hello, Dolly!, "Money, pardon the expression is like manure. It's not worth a thing unless it's spread around, encouraging young things to grow."   Manicure Lawn Maintenance is not be a young company. In fact, they've been servicing the St. Louis area for 30 years. So I am encouraging others to support a mom & pop local business that is top notch. They not only mow my yard, they've trimmed my bushes, shaped a tree and taken care of my leaves in the autumn. They've also done some beautiful landscaping for my friend (who referred me), so this year they'll be assisting and doing my two tiered retaining wall in my front yard.   I truly do enjoy arriving home from work and as I exit the garage, I get the aroma of fresh-cut grass. As I look around from my patio, my yard is perfectly mowed, edged and all the trimming put away. They mow my yard every two weeks and will come in between at my request. My yard is a typical inner city postage stamp yard in front and back and the price they charge is worth every penny, to give me more free time to Yelp.   They have an extended service area, primarily the south county and inner city. However, they are still growing after 30 years and they are servicing new areas. Give them a call and see if they can make your life easier.   I'll be back? - They'll be back to make yard beautiful and well maintained.   When: All of 2017 Why: A well kept yard.

Bumping up a Star today for the outstanding customer service. They went beyond my expectations in helping me find what I was searching for.   Again, I will state I am not an arts and craft person, so I rarely shop stores like Michaels. I was on a mission, I needed a pillow insert that measured 16x16. I have decorative holiday pillow covers I use for a chair in my foyer. When I bought a non-holiday cover, I accidentally bought it in a smaller size. That is when I learned that when shopping on the internet, you've got to make sure you've checked all the right boxes.   Wanting to put my non-holiday pillow out, I needed my insert NOW. I was going to be in STL for the day, so I thought I try various stores to find the size I needed. I had no luck. Even the store with 3 B's in its name didn't have one.   As I turned right on Brentwood from Edgar, my brain clicked and thought of Michaels. I made a U-turn (legally) and drove back to Michaels. I immediately was captivated by fall and Halloween decor. I snagged a couple of pieces for my home and continued my search for the pillow inserts. Bummer, I couldn't find them and went to the check-out to pay for my purchase.   That is when the outstanding customer service kicked in. The cashier asked if I found everything I was looking for and needed. For once, I was honest and said, "no". She and the other lady behind the counter immediately quizzed me on what I needed. When I told them a pillow insert, they knew that they had them. The one finished ringing me out, while the other ran upstairs (it's a two level store) to fetch my pillow.   After being rung out, I stepped out of the way for social distancing and so other shoppers could be rung out. While I stood there, the one lady radioed the cashier and asked her how many inserts I needed. They indeed had the pillows. I responded, I just needed one. Before she could return with my pillow, another associate working stock noticed me standing there and came over to make sure I didn't need any type of assistance. I informed her that her co-workers were on it and taking care of me.   When the associate returned with my pillow insert, it was perfect. It was exactly what I was looking for and needed. She then took me to a register and opened it up, so I did not have to get back in line to check-out. All of this was service beyond my expectations. To have this type of service is impressive,  wither it is during a pandemic or not. I am a fan of Michales now.   Sorry for the long review, just for a pillow insert, but I wanted to share the story and give them a good shout out.   When: September 17, 2021 Why: In need of pillow insert.

I love their selection of HIGH quality pet foods. My fur-babies eat grain free food and FMP has an excellent selection of these type of foods and their prices fit my budget. Plus, they have a frequent buyers program.   Shelby finally made it in to select her new collar and leash, but her first choice was out of her size. They offered to add it to an order they just placed, what great customer service. However, Shelby declined the offer and went with her second choice. The apple doesn't fall from the tree, like her daddy she wanted instant gratification.   Again, I gotta give a shout out for their great customer service. They always insist on carrying my dog food out to the car for me. I decline the offer, but it is always nice to hear. Great friendly service.

Been here, shopped here and did a return here. I am not impressed.  I am not a craft-er, but I can appreciate a craft store and this one did not make the cut. The location is good, so most likely I will return when the need arrives and that is why I am giving them a 3.

Great little shop for the Fur-Babies. I was down the street picking up a Gooey Butter cake and knew I couldn't go home without treats for the children.   While selecting the treats, I also browsed their selection of collars. I'll be re-visiting soon with Shelby so she can select a new collar.  They also have a great selection of toys and quality foods.   The staff was friendly and provided excellent customer service.

I'm not a fan of the Queen. I find her soft serve ice cream to be bland. Even when it is twisted in a cone and you have vanilla & chocolate combined together. To show you how bad, after two bites/licks I tossed my small cone in the trash. When a pudgy boy tosses a cone in the trash, you know it is bad. I've also tried their Blizzard and once again, even adding my favorite M&M's it comes out with no pizazz.   For me I'd give DQ a 2, but my SO likes their Chicken Tenders that  are served with milk gravy so I'll give them a 3. When he is sick, these Tenders are his "comfort" food. There is something about dipping tenders into milk gravy that makes him feel better.  I've sampled them and like their ice cream, it's not for me.   This DQ has recently had a major remodel and does look good sitting on the corner of Hampton and Eichelberger.

It is what it is. A diner dive that provides a very inexpensive breakfast in a short amount of time. So inexpensive that they only except CASH.   After dropping the three fur-babies off at the groomer we wanted to experience a new place for breakfast and thought of Tiffany's Original Diner. Neither of us had ever been and we thought, why not get her a try.   We were greeted by the patrons already seated at the counter drinking coffee and discussing the morning news. No cliques here, everyone was very welcoming. Our server/cook was kinda mundane, but that was okay. It went with the feeling of the diner.   Our breakfast was simple. I had a small order of biscuits & gravy and a sausage omelet with crispy hash-browns. I was hoping to have incredible b&g with it being a diner, but not the case. The biscuit was fresh and flaky, but the gravy lacked flavor. My sausage omelet had American cheese, as Sarah C. stated it is the only option for cheese. It served the purpose, but wasn't fluffy as most omelets. A drizzle of hot sauce can make any egg dish pop with flavor. She was accommodating on my hash-browns, leaving them on the grill longer to get them extra crispy.   Brad had a more simpler order, he enjoyed two eggs over easy, sausage (two patties), hash-browns and a side of grits. Easy eggs can not be screwed up and fried sausage patty is simple too. The grits were served in a bowl big enough for two and they all went to waste. Only two bites, our advice is do not order grits at Tiffany's. They'd make any true Southerner cringe.   What amazed me the most, is that you can buy lottery tickets at this little dive hole in the wall diner. Order breakfast, buy a ticket and share your dreams of winning with your fellow diners.  2 stars for food & experience + 1 star for selling lottery tickets = 3 star rating. Will I go back, most likely not. Am I glad that I had the Tiffany's experience, hell yes. It was a trip back in time.

A classic diner with an ambiance that is stuck in time and that is part of its' charm.  The waitresses are a cross between Alice and Flo and the short order cooks are a cross between a young Mel or Oleg.   We were in need of a new breakfast adventure and had other errands to run on Olive, so I thought OD, would fit the bill. We lucked out and snagged the last booth upon our arrival. The breakfast selection was so huge I had a hard making my choice. I knew I wanted biscuits and gravy and was pleased to see I could just order 1 b&g. That way I get a taste and can still enjoy another breakfast entree.   My breakfast partner knew instantly what he wanted, The Hot Hash & Holly. Which is; Potatoes O'Brien (hash browns with onions, green peppers and ham grilled in) topped in melted cheddar cheese, then two eggs your way and then topped again with their house made Hollandaise sauce. I could hear his arteries clogging as he ate, but I knew he'd die happy from his grin that went ear to ear with every bite.  I wasn't that adventurous, I went with one of their three egg omelets. You create your own here, pick one cheese and three ingredients. My choices were; Pepper Jack cheese, with sausage, onion and jalapeños. A side of crispy hash browns and wheat toast completed my entree. The omelet was fluffy and stuffed with my selected ingredients. They were not stingy with any of them. In fact, they could of held back on some of the jalapeños. They were so spicy, I started to sweat on the top of my head.   The one buttermilk biscuit was flakey, split and topped with creamy sausage gravy.  Huge chunks of sausage were visible in the gravy. I hate it when you need to get out your reading glasses to see the sausage, but not here. I don't think the biscuits were made in house, but I could be wrong. It was just to perfectly shaped to be house made. However it really doesn't matter, because the creamy gravy topping it made things okay.  When: 27 Jan 2014 Why: Breakfast

Their Reuben is truly Best of The Best. It is, Corned Beef with Kraut, 1000 Island Dressing, Swiss Cheese, Grilled and Served on Marble Rye Bread. It is huge, it is so big that I only ate half of my sandwich and took the remaining half home for dinner. I may have had the same thing for lunch and dinner that day, but it is was totally amazing.   It is a small sandwich shop, with the ambiance of a dive bar. It is dark, has a mixture of hightop tables and video games. In addition to the sandwiches, they offer a variety of chips and bottled soda. I was here mid afternoon and the place still had at least a dozen folks enjoying a late lunch. The lone man working was outgoing and very personable. Why anyone would choose Subway or Jimmy John's over S&S is beyond me. We shop local, now is the time to eat local as well.   I can't wait to go back and try their Pastrami and Pig on Wing. Even if I am not hungry, I will stop and get a sandwich to go and enjoy it later.

My recent visit was for the St Louis Burger Week. TCP, served up one delicious burger. Their offering was; Pimiento Cheese Double Double. It had pickled jalapeños, bacon and was served on Brioche Bun. How could it not be delicious? It had two of my favorite toppings, jalapeños and bacon. Normally, I'm not a fan of pimiento cheese, but on this burger, it won me over.   Sitting at the bar, I started my evening off with a Queen Bee. $1 from each QB sold, TCP donates the funds to the Honeybee Foundation. I got to enjoy a refreshing cocktail and support a charity that's important to me. Unfortunately, my second cocktail was a disappointment. It was the poorest made Old Fashioned, I've ever had. It was weak in flavor, it looked like colored water.   In addition to the delicious burger, I enjoyed an order of Smoked Buffalo Cauliflower. Who needs Buffalo Chicken Wings, when you can have the SBC from TCP. It was the same great spicy buffalo flavor, on a healthy vegetable. That's a big win. The cauliflower was prepared to the perfect texture and then tossed and coated in a traditional buffalo sauce. Yum!  While I was there, they had a live vocalist performing. The young lady had an incredibly beautiful voice. However, the volume was extremely loud for the small bar space. Having the live entertainment was nice, but they need to drop it a few decibels.   If you're curious as to why I lowered, their score from 5 to 4 Stars when I have raved about the food, it's because of the service. Sitting at the bar, the service was super slow. I sat at the bar amongst dirty empty glasses before either of the bartenders acknowledged me. They took my drink order, but left the glasses. Later they took my food order and still left the glasses.Finally, a waiter walking by asked if they were my glasses and if he could remove them. It would have been easier if the bartender had done it.   Watching both bartenders, they must have been new. Neither of them could keep up with the pace of those drinking at the bar and preparing cocktails for those dining at tables. Watching them was a total cluster f**k. They were so disorganized. There poor service and disorganization, caused The Chocolate Pig a star.   I'll be back? - Yes, the food is to good to pass up.   When: August 2, 2019 Why: St Louis Burger Week 2019

It was Taco Tuesday and I wanted a new experience. One thing I do miss about living in STL, is the vast selection of Mexican restaurants I had to choose from. I have a few near my home in IL, but they're basically the same and I wanted something new this Tuesday.   I arrived a little after 8PM. When my server came to the table I immediately ordered a house Margarita. While my server was retrieving my drink, another brought me a basket of chips and salsa. The chips were crisp and warm and the salsa was a typical salsa, but it had a little more pepper taste to it.   For an appetizer, I tried their, Choriqueso. It was served in a cast iron skillet and the cheese was almost scorched and there really wasn't that much flavor. Next time I'll just get good ole white cheese dip or guacamole.   I did enjoy a hard shell beef taco, since it was Taco Tuesday and it was fairly decent. The beef was seasoned well and the toppings completed a good experience. My main entree was a Chicken Fajita Quesadilla. It was very good. However, I do not understand why none of the Mexican restaurants on this side of the river, slice the quesadillas into sections. They've all served them in one big piece. The side of rice that accompanied my quesadilla, was some of the most flavorful that I have enjoyed on the IL side.   One of the highlights of going to any Mexican restaurant is always, the Margarita. Unfortunately, that was not the case here. I had two and both of them were very weak. My first one was a medium size with no salt. When I ordered a small for my second drink, I would have thought the server would have remembered, no salt. He did not and they were not that busy.   Service was friendly, even if he forgot my "no salt" request. They also, did a steady and good job cleaning between diners. Being seated near the cashier stand, I was impressed with the number of carry-out orders they were processing and that guest came in wearing mask.   I'll give them another try. I heard you have to try the, Joe Morales Tacos, which are Fried Tacos similar to those you get at Jack-n- The Box. I also, want to give their burritos a try.   When: August 31, 2021 Why: Taco Tuesday

This really should be a 2 Star Review, but the Jerk Chicken Wings got them the extra star. I came here for our monthly International Supper Club meeting. We had a reservation for a large group of 16. Since we all had arrived, we started to order. Once we did, we could sense something was a little off.   Our drinks came out slow and staggered. Being seated near the bar, I could watch the bartender. An immediate red flag was that she was reading recipes and measuring every drink with a shot glass. My "Big Easy" a Hurricane type drink was weak and so bad, I sent it back and had it replaced with a simple vodka and club soda.   Once our food started to arrive, again it was very staggered. Finally our server informed us that the bartender had called in and quit at the last minute. So they had to pull another server to act as bartender and he was the only server for the entire restaurant. Poor guy was doing the best he could do considering the circumstances, but a very bad call by management. Management should have been either behind the bar or waiting on tables. This made a very bad first impression for many diners at our table and those around us. I saw two tables, get up and walk out.   However, as stated the Jerk Chicken Wings saved them from being added to my Terrible Two's List. My french fries were also fairly good, as an accompaniment to the wings. I also had a carry-out of Red Beans and Rice for my roommate and he thought they were pretty good. Another bonus point for me, is the carryout containers are eco-friendly.   I'll give them another try. I'm hoping this was a one night screw up was not their typical service.   May 4 - Dinner (International Supper Club)

A local company that serves the nation via their website.   Who knew there could be so many puzzles. The variety and selection was mind blowing.  My reason for shopping here wasn't for a puzzle, it was for a Christmas Trivia game. My cousin and I wanted to add some fun to the, "Rob your Neighbor" gift exchange at the Christmas gathering. They had a clever little deck of Christmas Trivia Cards that did just the trick. We had so much fun reading the questions, that we continued after the gift exchange was over.   Will I return? - When I need a gift for a puzzle fan.  When: December 20, 2017 Why: Trivia Game

Four Muddy Paws is a solid 5 Stars, even during the Covid-19 pandemic. They're offering #curbsidepickup and free same day delivery within a 20 mile radius from their store. That not only is top notch customer service, it is taking care of our community. As we continually hear, "we're all is this together" and FMP is doing their part to help us care for the fur-babies.   I've used the curbside pick-up several times. Each time their amazing staff has made it so easy. I've used this service when I needed my regular 20 lb. bag of dry food and a re-stocking of the treat jars. They even helped me pull together Easter gifts for my Shelties and gifts for a couple of friends dogs as well.   During a pandemic or not, when I need something for my fur-babies, I'll be shopping at Four Muddy Paws. Inside the store, or curbside, they've got my business.

Some folks find their thrill on, Blueberry Hill. I found mine on West 9th Street in Alton. It may not have been a true, "thrill", but it was an amazing and delicious burger, fries and shake.   This colorful little shack that is hidden in an area that is sort of a ditch, totally blew me away. I in no way, expected the quality of customer service and preparation of food that I received today. The server was bubbly, friendly and very attentive. I went expecting dive diner food and received, upper sports pub food.   For my burger I choose the, Marilyn Monroe. Which was a 1/4 lb. burger with American cheese and all the fixings. It had; bacon, onion, lettuce, tomato, pickle and shake rattle & roll sauce. It was served on a standard hamburger bun, which was super fresh. The burger was prepared medium and to my liking, even without me requesting it. Their "special sauce" was just a good smear on the top bun, so it just added flavor and was not overpowering.   As a side I choose, Frenchies. I thought that was a cute name for the krinkle cut french fries. For those of you who are not fans on the Broadway/Movie musical Grease, Frenchie was one of the female characters name. The fries were crisp and lightly salted and seemed a little bigger then most krinkle cut fries I've enjoyed.   Their milk shakes are hand scooped and flavor of the month is Pumpkin Pie. It's October, how could I say no to a shake made to taste like a pumpkin pie. It was rich and creamy and topped with whipped cream and had a small candy pumpkin and cherry on top. I was only able to drink half of it, since I've lost weight my sweet tooth isn't as active as it use to be, but it was very tasty.   My first visit, I enjoyed their patio, but in the future I will just get carry-out. Or as we call it now, #curbside.   Will I return? - Yep, I gotta try their hot dogs.   When: October 7, 2020 Why: Late lunch - early dinner

Believe it or not, Stein Mart is where I buy my cocktail napkins. I have found a  better and funnier selection here then at Party City or any other party supply outlet. They may only have one spinning rack of napkins, but they almost all get a chuckle.   When I went on a family vacation, I stocked up on a variety of different ones pertaining to beer or drinking in general . When we'd arrive at the different breweries (we were on a beer-cation) and our server would start to put out the plain white cocktail napkins I'd stop them and say, "We've brought our own".  Each server always got a chuckle out of my selection. Then when we'd leave to move on to our next experience, I'd let our server have what was left in the package so they could have fun with other drinkers .   SM is also a good place for men's for inexpensive silk ties, handkerchiefs and those I hate to wear them white shirts. I have also, found great dog bowls at rock bottom prices that make my dogs feel like they are eating off the good china.   These off the rack stores are becoming more competitive and Stein Mart leads the way with a more organized and upscale feel.

Sorry Four Muddy Paws, but I have to snap a star away from your ratings. Why, you ask. It is because your customer service is in a downward spiral. It is almost nonexistent.   Two visits ago, the only one who helped me was your house dog who followed me through out the store. It is always a delight to see that little blond bombshell of a dog.   Then my visit last week was not much better. There was no greeting when I entered the store, the clerk was too busy talking and laughing over the half door with the groomer. She was so oblivious to my presence, I literally could have walked out with merchandise. Once I got to the counter to be rung out, she continued to chat on the phone about various things. When I was in retail as a career, we'd put the phone person on hold to assist the "live" customer in front of us. Once she got off the phone, her conversation with me was minimal and no apology for having me wait. This is not the type of customer service I got use to having at FMP. I want the top notch, we love you as our customer service back.   I have two more purchases to go on my frequent buyers program, so I hope  to see improvement. I will tell you now, if I do not I will be taking my business else where and will gladly drive a further distance to get better service. The market for your services is getting to competitive in the Saint Louis market for you to be dropping the ball.

Yippie! I get to give The Shaved Duck their 5th Star back. I'm a big fan of Burnt Ends and TSD has the best ones in the city and county. They smoke for hours, so they're only available after 5 PM. So I highly recommend that you get there right at Happy Hour, because chances are they may sell out. After hours of being smoked, they then toss'm in my favorite sauce - Black Isle. Pair these Burnt Ends with an ice cold craft beer and you've got the perfect start to a BBQ feast. (For some, it could be a meal) However, on this night, I pigged out and continued to eat.   Seriously, I skipped lunch so I could totally pig out here at The Shaved Duck. After devouring my entire order of Burnt Ends. (I was dining alone, so no one to share with and I kinda liked it that way). Next I ordered the B.O.S.S., it was the "must order" recommendation from Ian Froeb on his STL 100 list this year. I couldn't wait to sink my teeth into the thinly sliced Tri-Trip, smothered in bacon swiss sauce and topped with onion rings. The sandwich came with one side, I choose the Hand Cut Fries. Being a huge fan of Brussels Sprouts, I also ordered a second side of them. In my old age, sprouts have become one of my two favorite vegetables.   I sipped my Charleville Tornado Alley at the high top table in the front window of the bar area and waited patiently for my food. Soon I saw a young man different from my original server approaching with a tray of goodies. He first sat down my Sautéed Brussels Sprouts, then Hand Cut Fries with a Little Cup of Ketchup and finally my BIG sandwich. He smiled, told me to enjoy my food and walked away. When I took a closer look at the sandwich, there was no meat on it. It was a vegetarian sammie. Did I mistakenly order the wrong thing? I couldn't have, or did I. The young man re-entered the room and I waved him to him. When he came over, I told him I had ordered the B.O.S.S. and he quickly corrected the error.   My server was going on break after she placed my order and was also ordering her own dinner to enjoy. It was a simple absent minded error, she ordered her sandwich as mine. They box up the mistake and let me have it as well. It made an excellent lunch at the next day work. The Brussels Sprouts, tomatoes, red pepper with a smoked habanero sauce was still full of flavor.  When my server came back from break, she apologized deeply. I told her no worries and we had a good laugh at how it happened.   Back to my original sandwich, The B.O.S.S. is totally the boss. The Tri-Trip was tender. The Bacon Swiss Sauce was finger licking good and the crispy onion rings gave it a crunch and additional flavor. My Sautéed Brussels Sprouts were done to perfection. They were done to the point that they were just soft enough, but still had a little snap to them. Then the hand cut fries, crispy coating and a hot meaty potato inside. If you follow my reviews, you know I love my ketchup served in little cups. So seeing it served that way here, made me smile.   My "must order" is the Burnt Ends, so next time you are at The Shaved Duck - order them and enjoy.   When: May 17, 2016 Why: Burnt Ends and Ian Froeb's STL 100

I walked in with seven old coins with face value of $3.08 and a sterling silver necklace and walked out with $152.  How do you like them $'s. Of course, Patt C.'s sister would say, "why bother".  If she'd clean out her coin purse, she might be singing a different song.   Check out those old coins and jewelry you've tossed in to a drawer they may be able to provide you with a night on the town or give you some extra money for the holidays.   The staff is knowledgeable and friendly, making your transaction fun.

PTC, saved my ass. I am one of those peps who drives until their gas tank needle is so close to  E, it is scary.   Actually, I forgot to get gas when I left work, I was in the zone to get home. Working in IL, once I'm on 255 and merge on to 70 to come back home to STL, there's no exit with a gas station until you see PTC. I was down to one bar, I couldn't risk continuing my drive across the bridge. I needed to get gas.   My experience is only at the "pump", but I'd say the customer service was spot on. The pump even asked me if I wanted a receipt. The area around the gas pumps well maintained and free of clutter and litter.  This PTC offers a Taco Bell and Subway for those who are hungry. I'll be honest, I miss the old days when a truck stop had a huge glorified diner. The food back then was good ole comfort food and not fast food.   I'll be back? - If I'm leaving IL and down to one bar again.   When: June 3, 2019 Why: I was outta gas.

Hey, chicken sandwich place that is closed on Sunday, have you tried the Ch'King at Burger King? It's pretty damn, good and during Pride Month for every one they sell BK is donating 40¢ to the Human Rights Campaign. That's pretty awesome.   When I heard the news of the new chicken sandwich and the 40¢ donation, I knew I had to give it a try. Since I have a BK near my work,  I swung through the drive-thru, on my way home. To my delight and disappointment, when I placed my order, they told me they were sold out. I can always come back later and that is what I did.   I gave them a day to get re-stocked and returned for lunch. The young lady taking drive-thru orders took my order and suggested the spicy version. I love spicy food, so I couldn't resist. I made it a small combo with fries and a diet coke. This quick lunch was more about the sammie.   The piece of chicken big, crispy and the meat inside was juicy. I love it when you can feel and hear a crunch when biting into a sandwich. My bun was fresh and soft and the special sauce gave it just enough extra kick. If I were in a sit-down restaurant I would have asked for a side to dip my fries in. As for the spiciness, it could have been kicked up some for me, but for everyone else it most likely is spot on.   I like that many of the fast food places are constantly re-inventing themselves and adding new items to the menu. I'm really proud of BK and will support them more now, knowing they took part in Pride and made these donations.   When: May 17, 2021 Why: Lunch and new Ch'King Sandwich

This BK had a kitchen fire a while back and was closed during restoration. It is now reopened and has a brand new attitude. Similar to those who go to the plastic surgeon and get botox. When you feel and look prettier, you have a better attitude.   I've been dieting, but dieting does not mean I am dead and can not crave a cheeseburger. As I was filling up with gas next door at U Gas, the aroma of the charbroiled burgers filled the air. It then had me wondering what their new fries were like. They've been boasting about them on TV. Could they be that much better?  I finished filling up the CRV tank with gas, now it was my turn to fill my tank up. I drove next door and went inside for service. I kept strong and only ordered a simple single cheeseburger and a small order of their new fries. My cheeseburger, hit the spot. It was so much better then a regular cheeseburger at the Golden Arches.   Those new fries they been boosting about, they are being modest. These fries are better then; Mickie Dee's, Jack's, Sonic and Hardee's. Can you tell I like fries, it is one of the reasons I am dieting. The new BK fries are a larger thick cut fry and deep fried just enough to give them a crispy crunch. Another thing I liked, they were not coated in salt, they had just enough to give that boost of flavor.   The most impressive thing about this BK reopening after its' restoration is the customer service. The new staff was friendly, polite, thanked me coming in and when handing me my order,  said they hoped to see me again.  I don't eat fast food often, but with the service I experienced here, I will be back.

Saw the commercials for the new Tacos at Burger King and thought I'd give them a try. I've tried the Impossible Whopper and enjoyed it, so I thought may-be the taco would be good, too. It wasn't. I put it on the same level as Jack in the Box. If you've got the I've been drinking munchies, it may satisfy you. If you're sober and wanting lunch, I'd order a burger instead.   I can not for the life of me, figure out why businesses just don't continue to focus on what they do best and what they are known for, instead of trying to expand their menu. Do something well, instead of serving mediocre everything.   Another reason to lower the star rating is the customer service here is on the decline again. There's not interaction between the staff and customer. They take your order and that is it.......if you get a thank-you you're doing good.

When: April 23  Why: Dinner - Carry- Out (dining alone)   Menu: Whole Grain Tuscan Linguine with Parmesan-Crusted Chicken   Let me sing the praises first, before I slap them down a notch or two.   I was impressed with the vegetables in my entree. The broccoli florets were cooked perfectly , they had that fresh veggie snap. I loved the fact that both the red pepper and onion were cut vertically and not horizon ally. The button mushrooms were also not over cooked which I would have expected from a fast food noodle place.   The Parmesan Crusted Chicken Breast was large in size, pre-sliced and as flavorful if not more as one you could get at the Pasta House.   You can watch them prepare the food and it appeared to be a well oiled working team.   Big bonus points that their carry out containers are #5 and can be recycled after washing.   Now for the slap down. When I entered, I was greeted promptly (yes, that is a good thing), but they lost it after the greeting. I stated it was my first time and wanted to study the menu. When I stepped up to order, the young lady (rudely) interrupted me, wanting to know which size i wanted. I did not see on the sign that I needed to say size first.   She obviously in her fast food career has not been taught how to up sell.  Until I was leaving, did I realize I could have made it a trio. If I were at McDonald's or Hardees, you know they'd want to add fries or make it a value meal.   Now for the biggest slap down. SODIUM. If you watch your sodium intake do not eat here. As I ate my entree, I knew there was too much sodium. When I checked their website, most dishes had either half or exceeded your daily recommended intake.   I was going to give them 2 stars, but IBC Creme Soda (in a bottle) saved their ass.

Major disappointment. I have shopped and found some incredible bargains at the Ross Dress for Less in Maplewood and was hoping for the same at this location, but no such luck. At least not in the fashion area, my only good find was gardening tools.  As others have commented, the store has a lot of dead space and the racks & shelves are not as full as you typically see at other Ross stores. It almost gave me the feeling that they were in the process of closing the location. However, it was a Monday and there were many store associates bringing out new merchandise and restocking the floor.   I was shopping with a friend who was searching for a special dress and we had no such luck. The selection in her size was minimal. However, I will say we saw some of the same dresses that we saw earlier at Nordstrom's Rack at a much lower price. I quickly shopped the men's department, but nothing caught my eye.   This store isn't totally off my list for bargain shopping, but for now it has to be on my Terrible Two's list until I have a better experience.   When: April 4, 2016 Why: Shopping for Derby attire.

Great place to enjoy a cocktail before and after The Fox. Or, get a group of friends together to enjoy their Happy Hour and amazing view of downtown STL.    If you go for Happy Hour be sure to arrive between the hours of 2-6 PM. That way you'll be able to enjoy special prices on select cocktails, wine and local beers. You'll also be able to enjoy some tasty appetizers at a reduced price.   The service at the bar and tables are both attentive and friendly. If the weather is permitting, I highly recommend that you get outside and enjoy the terrace with a view.   I'll be back? - Absolutely.   When: A couple of times. Why: Happy Hour

I love this place, so I had to raise their stars to 5. I recently went to a party and had two other guest come up to me and tell me they tried Mitchell James because of my review on Yelp.   I have been coming here for almost three years + and never been happier with a salon and stylist. My stylist of choice is Cate McDonald, she is so talented and personable. As I have stated in previous review, I love a scissor cut, do not use those snap combs on a clipper on my hair.  I want a precision cut and Cate delivers.   I am a natural salt & pepper hair color so I do not need a colorist, but Michelle Abernathy who has the station next to Cate is a color artist. In fact the two work as a team, Michelle does the highlights or color and Cate creates the fantastic cut. I have seen many of their masterpieces over the years and am amazed how beautiful ladies look when they are finished.   I may be just a simple man cut, but you will not find me going any where else. Mitchell James is the salon for Steven B..

I miss living close to Penzeys. I use to love just running in when I needed a spice, or just to explore for new ideas. Unfortunately with the pandemic, shopping in the store isn't possible. However, you can browse the on-line store, place an order, check-out, select the store you live close to and they'll have your order bagged up and ready for you at their front door contactless curbside pick-up.    I'll be honest, the reason I dropped them a star is selfish. Not living in STL anymore, I was in the city for a day of shopping and errands. I had placed an order figuring I'd be able to pick it up while in town. Unfortunately, they never called me saying my order was ready to pick-up until I was back home in IL. Then when I went to select a time for pick-up the next day, all the early morning spots were already taken. I know it's a pandemic, but next time I will just order and have it shipped to my home. Or perhaps, they need to have more staff on duty at the shop pulling orders.   Either way, I love Penzeys and only use their spices for cooking and baking.

This truly is a 3 1/2 Star review. They are not yet a 4, but I am sure they'll get there very soon. My first visit was a carry-out order and it had a couple of bumps, but they were not bad enough to keep to me away. My next visit, I will be sure to dine in and see if that doesn't bump them up to a 4.   My carry-out order was simple. I ordered two appetizers; a Crispy Egg-Roll and a order of Crab Rangoon. As an entree, I ordered their VP Fried Rice. My wait was what I'd consider a typical wait time at a Chinese take-out restaurant. As I waited, a couple folks came in to pick-up phone orders and another man did a walk-in order like me. They carried a bag out of the kitchen, called my name and handed me the bag.   When the bag was handed to me, I thought that it was extra heavy for what I ordered, but didn't say anything. I take responsibility for that, because when I got home, it was not my food, it was no where close to what I ordered. I drove back and when I walked in, the employee in his broken english said, "Not your, order?" All I could do was smile and say, no. (Honestly, I was pissed, because of the drive and I was starving. It was a rough day at work and I just wanted to eat.) I kept my cool, understanding that they were still new and mistakes happen. They switched my order with the correct food and I was on my way home.   They pack their carry-out in styrofoam, which needs to be vented to release some of the steam from the heat. My Pork Egg-Roll and Crab Rangoon (6) were not crispy. They had great flavor, but were more on the mushy side. Poking holes in the lid would have made a big difference.   The VP Fried Rice is served in a plastic bowl with a lid and traveled well. I'll also say, this is most likely the best Fried Rice I have had at any Chinese or Asian Fusion restaurant. It had a robust flavor with the mixture of; smoked bacon, sweet & sour Chinese sausage, BBQ chicken, egg, green onion, kimchi peas and carrots. The serving was huge. My plan was to only eat half of it and take the remaining to work the next day for lunch. That plan did not happen, it tasted so good, I could not stop eating and devoured the entire order.   I'll be back? - Yes. Need to experience their dining-in service.    When: March 8, 2018 Why: Dinner & Craving Chinese/Asian Food

The quickest way to make your co-workers jealous of you is to order lunch from Sugarfire and not tell anyone your doing so. It also is the absolute quickest way to get them pissed off at you. Whatever happens, you are going to have one tasty lunch all to yourself.   Working downtown, I can tell you how excited I was when I heard SugarFire was opening downtown. I was even more excited when I discovered that they'd be delivering to the downtown, Lafayette Square and Soulard areas. This is going to make my lunchtime so much more enjoyable, on those day that I don't brownbag it. Since I was excited about the delivery service, this review is based on that excitement.   I work the morning shift, so typically my lunch is at 10:30 AM. Since they do not open, till 11 AM, so I enjoyed a late lunch. I called right at opening and the phone was cheerfully answered.  When I told the young lady I wanted to place an order for delivery, she asked if she could put me on hold for just a brief minute. When she returned, my order of a Full-Rack of Baby Back Ribs with two sides and a fountain soda was completed quickly. She asked if I wanted a certain time of delivery, or ASAP. I said, ASAP and she informed me they'd have it out right away and it should be delivered within 30 minutes. (it took 40, but I didn't mind)  The young lady delivering was perky and professional. My order fun slab of ribs were doubly wrapped in plastic wrap and foil. They were still warm when I unwrapped them and filled our break room with the aroma of BBQ. It was about this time that the second shift was arriving and the jealousy begun. I was able to control the situation by slicing off a bone and letting them taste the magic of SugarFire. Even after sharing a couple of bones, I still had enough for my lunch and lunch the next day at home. So two co-workers can easily share a full rack for lunch.   My sides were Cole Slaw and Baked Beans - SugarFire easily makes the best Baked Beans of all the BBQ joints in STL. Their Cole Slaw is creamy, I prefer a vinegar & oil slaw, but I do like theirs because it is chopped in larger pieces. They also do not over dress it, the slaw is lightly coated, so it is not swimming in excess dressing. My fountain soda, was the infamous local cola; Excel. For the delivery, they actually gave me a chilled bottle of Cola.   I'll be a having late lunches on the regular, now that SugarFire is downtown. My co-workers have gotten on board already and are ordering too. I think we're going to create a SugarFire day at work when we all order - LOL.   When: April 3, 2016 Why: Late lunch at work

The Pump House is a damn good sports bar. Great selection of beer, crispy chicken wings and an extensive menu to satisfy any craving.  The bar is spacious and to my understanding from speaking to others at the celebration I was attending, the PH has added on numerous times during their growth. Which means they are popular with the locals and after my experience I can see why.   I was here for the celebration of a friend paying off their college loan. Yippie, she did it in six years. For those of you who still have those loans, know that is a major accomplishment worthy of a celebration. Due to the lay-out of the bar, we were spread out in to two areas, but with some mingling it worked out just fine.   I enjoyed a couple of craft beers and an order of chicken wings at the beginning of the party.  Wings were impressive for a sports bar. Their wings are never frozen and prepared to order in their own breading. They offer a large variety of styles, I chose the servers favorite, Garlic Parmesan. She gave me good advice.    As the evening winded down, several of us decided to stay for dinner. We all were glancing over the menu, then our server told us that the Thursday night special was a Ribeye for $14.95. At that price how can you go wrong. It came with a side of Green Beans and a potato. I wanted, their infamous Potato Balls, but they had been 86 for the night. 86 = Sold Out. Damn, it. I ended up choosing their regular french fries.   Service was attentive for the huge sports bar crowd. It was nice to see outlets and purse/coat hooks under the bar. Nice customer service for a sports bar.   Will I return? - Sure, if I'm on that side of the river.   When: August 10, 2017 Why: Celebration

On their menu, they boost that their wings are fresh, never frozen and they are Jumbo. If you're like me and size does matter, these wings are for you. They are definitely larger then other sports bars that I frequent. My only complaint, is that they did not distribute the drums and flats in equal numbers. I had 5 flats and 2 drums. It just my little quirk, I like them to match. Otherwise, I'd been bumping the Pump House up to 5 Stars.   The specialty sauce I choose was, Spicy Glazed. I asked the bartender about the, Dirty Rum. Anything dirty, like a martini always catches my eye. She explained what it was and it did sound very tempting. However, when I asked what her favorite was and she told about Spicy Glazed, I was sold. A mild hot sauce with a touch of honey is a perfect combination. I was impressed how even after being tossed in a sauce, the wings were still crispy and when bitten into, you could hear and feel the crunch.   Being one who dines mainly at the bar, I am always impressed when a bar offers hooks underneath for jackets or purses. I'm even more impressed when they offer outlets to plug our devices in for a charge or to continue working off site.   This recent visit, I experienced exceptional customer service. The two bartenders working my area were friendly and polite. It is rare that we hear the words, please and thank-you and you are welcome, as well. These young ladies were raised by some good momma's.   I'm coming back for some more wings and next time, they'll be the Dirty Rum.   When: March 17, 2021 Why: Had enough Corned Beef already, needed wings.

I grew up going to Mister Donut after church. What a sweet reward for sitting through a church service. I looked forward to that final, Amen. Once it was said, I knew I'd soon be biting into a Chocolate Long John.   Years ago, there use to be lots of Mister Donuts all through out the bi-state area. Now, this one in Godfrey is the last one in the USA. Another chain bought all the others up and this lone franchise refused to sell out. If you go to Japan and other Asian countries, there are thousands of locations.   I was so glad when Y98 did their Diner & Donuts Tour this year that they included Mister Donut. MD is about a mile from my work, so I had to make an appearance while they were broadcasting live. I didn't care if it was my day off, I still made the trek over to Alton/Godfrey to be park of this celebration.   The staff offers up small-town hospitality. Which is way better then, Southern Hospitality. I also have a soft spot for the decor. I'll admit, it's kinda dated and tacky. It's so 70's, but when my favorite color is orange, I gotta love the ambiance.   I'll be back? - It's too close to my work, what do you think?  When: August 15, 2019 Why: Y98 Broadcasting Live

There needs to be a support group for people like me. I am a coat-aholic. I like jackets and big winter coats. How I got this disease is beyond me, but the only cure is to go coat shopping and that is what I did.   I had already hit a few shops with no luck. None of them carried the type of medication I need. I was looking for something that was fashion forward and screamed my personality. I searched a couple of rounder racks and found nothing to my taste. As I was ready to make my exit, a display on the wall caught my eye.   I immediately went over to take a closer look. It was a  black poly filled car length coat, by Izod. Looked good on the hanger and looked even better on me. When I reached up to get the empty hanger and proceed to the check out, I noticed a lone "burnt orange" one  hanging in the very back. The coat Gods must have been with that day, because it was my size. Which simply meant it was meant to be mine.    Stein Mart isn't for everyone. It's basically like Marshall's and TJ Maxx, in that you have to shop regularly to find the good items. I can not speak about the women's department, but I find the men's to be for a more mature preppy man. Definitely the golf set. It is obvious they are based out of Florida. I've never seen anything for a young trendy man.   I've found some great items in the pet department and I occasionally score a decorative home item. I have also scored majorly with some very colorful and fun socks.   Not my go to all the time, but when I do find a winner like an orange coat for $59, I am a fashionista.

The Pump House may be a "sports bar," but for what it is, I gotta bump them up to 5 Stars. Their food has never disappointed me and the service is always friendly and attentive.   During my recent visit, I was torn between a couple of menu items. When I asked the bartender which of the three I should order, she did not miss a beat with her recommendation. She quickly responded, "The Pork Fritter Sandwich." She then went on to say, that I would not be disappointed. Damn, she was so right. It was one of the best Fried Pork Tenderloin Sandwiches I have ever had. It is even better than the one at another local restaurant that is famous or their Pork Tenderloin Sammies.   The sandwich was a true Midwest classic comfort food. It was battered deep fried pork tenderloin, served on Sourdough bun. Of course, as with any  Midwest pork tenderloin sammie, the pork is always larger than the bun. Instead of placing the toppings on the side, as most places do, my sandwich was fully assembled. Typically, I would not put the tomato on my sammie, but this time I enjoyed it.  The combination of the lettuce, onion, pickle and the tomato, truly complimented and completed the flavor of the sandwich.   I also gotta give a shout out to the crispy hand cut fries. They were the perfect side. I love it when you bite into a fry and you can hear a faint crunch. That is a crispy fry.   I commend the staff for their positive attitude, great service and hustle. They continue to make dining during this extended pandemic, a positive experience.   When: August 19, 2021 Why: Dinner

Yesterday I did something that I can not believe I did. I went to a restaurant without checking it out on Yelp first and that was a big mistake. We wanted a new experience, and we got it. I also learned to not pick a restaurant by a road sign promoting what food choices are at the next exit on I-170.   After we were seated, I made the comment to the BF that I hadn't checked Yelp. I quickly pulled it up on my iPhone and was shocked to see a 2 Star rating.  We took the high road thinking it can't be that bad and stayed. Reality check, when looking at the average Yelp ratings, they are spot on.   When we looked at the drink menu, I got excited to see that they offered Jalapeño Margaritas. If they offer Jalapeño Margaritas, the food can't be that bad, can it?  Yes, it can. However, the Margarita was the bomb, I loved how the jalapeño gave it an extra kick.    They offer one serving of chips and salsa complimentary. If you want "bottomless"  you can pay $4. One serving was enough. The chips were thicker then most chips and also were over done for my taste. The salsa was chunky, but for me had way to much cilantro. It was overpowering to my taste buds.   My entree was the Fat Taco Sampler, which included three tacos, rice and beans. I choose the Grilled Chicken, Grilled Mahi Mahi and Blackened Tilapia.  All three tacos were topped with lime spiked cabbage, pico de gallo & homemade sauce. The amount of toppings overpowered the selected flavor/protein. The toppings were so plentiful you could not pick the soft tortilla up to eat. This was the first time I had to eat a taco with a fork. I picked through the toppings and just ate the protein.  Grilled Chicken - Huge pieces of grilled white meat, the best of the three.  Grilled Mahi Mahi - Small broken up pieces that had little flavor.  Blackened Tilapia - The overpowering toppings ruined this taco.   Rice and Beans were extremely dry and flavorless. The beans were pasty like a mud pack at a health spa.   The service was okay, our server was attentive and did good touch backs with us while dining. However, a good Margarita and table service is not enough to bring me back to Flaco's Cocina.

You're back to 3 Stars for me. Even with Free Wi Fi, I gotta take a star away from you.   I admit, I am not a crafter so I do not come here often. Lucky for me, what I was looking for today was on sale. It was buy one rubber stamp and get a second one 50% off.  However, the selection sucked and I did not find anything to my liking. If you're going to have something on sale, have ample stock. I walked out only buying to new colored ink pads and they were not even the brand I normally like and they were smaller in size, too.   I really don't like the politics of HL, but when I do something crafty, they always seem to have what I want and need. Michael, I need you to improve your game, so I don't have to spend $'s at HL.   Again, I'll say the staff is friendly and professional. Also, attached to my receipt was a 40% off coupon for a single item. Nice touch, but it expires on April 27, 2019 and that is too quick for me.   I'll be back? - I hope, so.   When: April 19, 2019 Why: Ink Pads and new Rubber Stamps

Not only do I love this store for stocking my own spice rack, but it is also the perfect shop for creating gift boxes. They have bright yellow colored boxes that you can fill with spices of your choice. The box can hold two large jars, one large and two small or my personal favorite four small jars. Choosing your own spices, allows you to be able to personalize each box to the recipient.   This year I created one for my young cousin who thinks he is a master griller. I created him a box with different types of spices and rubs for his steaks. I also put in a small jar of their, Frozen Pizza Seasoning. If you haven't tried it, it is a must have. This magical little jar can spice up any frozen pizza. Even the super cheap ones.   The customer service is always friendly and the staff is so knowledgable of the products they sell. I've totally stopped buying spices at my local grocer and make a special trip to Penzeys. It  is so worth the extra effort.   Would I come back? When I need a new spice, I'll be here.   When: December 7, 2016 Why: Gift Box Creating

Psst, come here and I'll tell you a secret. No, come closer I've got to whisper it or everyone will know. Some of the best Italian in Saint Louis is not on The Hill, it can be found on Lindell near SLU.   I will be honest, I may have not ever discovered Vito's if it were not for my Chicago Yelp friend, Lupe D.. She had Living Social Coupon she was not going to be able to use and shared it with me. Wow, it goes to show Yelp friendships can extend beyond your hometown.  We begun our Vito's experience with Calamari Fritti and it was a great way to start.  The pieces were huge and covered in enough breading to get a crispy texture. They were served with a side of freshly made marinara sauce, but I enjoyed mine with a fresh squeezed lemon.   Next was Crispy Caesar Salad and fresh hot baked bread. The bread was so warm when served to our table, that the butter melted easily. Making it a perfect complement to our salads. Vito's uses only the hearts of romaine for their Caesar Salad and combined it with Crunchy Croutons and Shaved Parmigiano Cheese. My tummy was content at this point, but we still had more to come.   Our entrees were Parpadelle Bolognese and Linguine Con Vongole, both were superior to fare I have had recently on "The Hill". The Parpadelle had a rich Marinara sauce combined with ground beef and peas. They then topped it with fresh shaved Parmigiano. My Linguine Con Vongale was absolutely perfect. I was amazed at the large number of littleneck clams that they tossed in white wine, olive oil, fresh garlic, lemon and parsley. Both servings were large enough for two to share after having a salad.   Our server was friendly and attentive to all the tables around us. Taking note of the other food being served around us, we know that we will be back for more great food at Vito's.

This store is a hoot. It has been years since, I had the opportunity to shop here.   Today we were on a mission, Brad needed a pair of readers for work and now that I am back to reading contacts, I wanted to check some out too. He had already looked at several places with no luck. We started to brainstorm, were can we find inexpensive readers so if they get ruined, it is no financial loss and we thought of the dollar type stores.   When we entered DTS, we asked the cashier if they carried readers and she directed us to where they were in the store. I was surprised, they had two racks filled with all different styles and they were all only $1. What a deal, shame we didn't like any of the frames they offered.   Since we were in the store, we thought we walk around and see what other bargains could be found. Wow, what a great selection of gift bags and other wrapping items and at such a low price. Totally means you can spend more on the gift.   I walked down the toiletries aisle and had a good laugh.  I saw Baby's Butt Aid, with the caption "relief for the un-happy butt". I laughed out loud, but like Norma H. I remember the 20/20 report and would be scared to buy any product like this at a $1 store. However, I'd be tempted by the Scooby-Doo products.   The store was extremely clean and I was amazed how many employees were on duty. Next time I need gift bags, I will stop by Dollar Tree.

Now I understand why BB is in a downslide as a big box retailer. I stopped by for a particular item. Don't judge me, I was looking for a Bluetooth Selfie Stick. The customer service here was nill. I walked around in amazement looking at how BB had changed since my last visit and not one sales associate approached me.   I checked all the departments I thought a selfie stick would be located, with no luck. As I was about to give up and walk out and order one on Amazon, a sales associate finally asked if I needed assistance. When I told him what I needed, he gave me directions to the correct aisle. He said, see that sign over there, it's to the right of it and then you'll see a marker with Selfie Sticks. He then, kept on walking away from me.   I spent 25+ years in retail and the stores I worked in, that would never be accepted customer service. As a sales associate, it was our job to "assist" our customers. Good customer service would have been walking with me over to the specified area and putting the item in my hands. There was multiple sticks to choose from and it should have been his job to up-sell me the best one. Instead, I had to do that myself. Glad I did research before shopping so I knew what I wanted.   Experiences like this, I understand why customers are flocking to Amazon and avoiding brick and mortar stores.   I'll be back? - I doubt it.   When: April 3, 2019 Why: Buying a Selfie Stick (don't judge me)

"This is disgusting." is what my friend said, as he shoved another fork full of the Cheesy Pulled Pork Fries, into his mouth. I knew he was joking, he barely took a breath before he filled his fork again.   When I take friends to TSH for their first visit, I always order a half size of the Cheesy Pulled Pork Fries as our appetizer. They are always wowed by the crispy fries covered in pit beans, pulled pork, cheesy sauce and BBQ sauce. Honestly, I can make a meal out of the half order paired with a beer. So, I always enjoy sharing an order.   My most recent visit a friend who's a retired chef, had him raving about the food. He swore the ribs at TSH were the best he has had in STL. He was amazed at how tender all the meat was and how easily it feel off the bones. We shared the half rack with its two sides. I wanted the Brussels Sprouts and he wanted the Citrus Slaw. We were both satisfied with our choices. I personally could not finish the BS's, and took half of them home to add to my morning scrambled eggs.   Earlier this year I took another friend, who lives closer to the restaurant then I do  and had never been. She too, was amazed at the deliciousness of the CPPF's. Those fries get everyone hooked on Stellar Hog. After our appetizer, we shared an half rack of ribs and brisket.   Ordering two lunches, we got to share four sides. Yes, we were gluttons this day. We shared; Creamy Cabbage, Slaw, Mac-n-Cheese and Pit Beans. Both of us were blown away about the cabbage. It's served warm and is delicious. The m&c was creamy and definitely cheesy. The slaw is good and the pit beans are better as a topping on the fries, then a side dish.   The service is hit or miss here. My first visit (Jan 16) the young lady was attentive and fun. Most recent visit, was a miss. The server was distracted, she had a lot of area to cover. She was doing the dining room and the patio. The outside was open and providing service inside and out. Things would have gone smoother if the bartender could have come from behind the bar and helped with the tables inside.   I'll  be back? -  Yes. I love introducing new people to TSH.   When: January 16, 2019 & April 6, 2019 Why: Lunches with friends who had never been.

I love a good pastrami sandwich. When I moved away from STL, the one thing I knew I was going to miss, was the good ole Jewish deli's. Once I was settled into my new surroundings, I had an epiphany. I suddenly remembered this little sandwich shop from when I worked in Alton years ago. To my surprise it was still open and going strong.   Their pastrami sandwich is as good as the finest Jewish deli's in STL. It's made simple. It a big pile of pastrami, topped with Swiss cheese and served on marbled rye with a smear of spicy mustard. You can have either cold or grilled. I highly recommend grilled, but if you choose cold, I promise not to judge you. However, I may talk about your choice behind your back. LOL  Fries would make a great side, but it's a sandwich shop so they have a large variety of chips for you to enjoy as your side. I'm not a soda drinker, so I did not notice if they have fountain drinks or not. I just grabbed myself a bottle of Straight Up Iced Tea.   The customer service was just average. The three workers were more into talking to each other about some drama with a common friend. I didn't mind because as I watched them make my sammie, I knew it was going to be great.   Lucky for me, the drive home is fairly short. The aroma of that pastrami was making me more hungry as I drove and if I didn't live close, I would had to pull over and take a bite.   Will I return? - Jewish or not, this is going to be my new deli.   When: October 1, 2020 Why: Craving Pastrami

I know there are some Yelpers who do not want us to review fast-food restaurants, but they still get our business and need to be rated.   I visited BK simply because we were lazy, needed dinner and had received a coupon in the mail. Our coupon in-titled us to; two Whoppers, two small fries and two small beverages for only $6.99.   We enjoyed the Whoppers, they were big sloppy burgers with all the toppings. The French Fries were awful, why would anyone want to eat the fries at Burger King. Our beverages I filled with no ice - we had ice at home.   The customer service was better then any thing I have received at a McDonald's or any other fast food. I have to be honest, I'll only be back with a coupon.

I am bewildered. Should I be upset that PBP is all the way out in Chesterfield? Or Should I be happy that it isn't close to home? I'm going with the later, because this popcorn is damn good.   I noticed Papa as I was approaching, The Shack for a late breakfast and made a mental note to visit once I had eaten. Once I finished eating, I headed up to PBP. The parking lots for both strip centers are connected, so it was easy-peasy. I didn't have to get back on Clayton Road.   As I entered the store, I was immediately greeted by one of the young men working. I was also overwhelmed with the variety of popcorn flavors. I was also impressed that they offer Chicago and Big Chicago in their flavor varieties. Big Chicago has more cheddar mix on the popcorn in that blend. I was pleased with the amount on Chicago, it was a perfect blend to the caramel.   Heads, up! The caramel they use here is house made and is an old family recipe. A nice touch for a local business, to share a family treat with the community.   They also had a variety of candies, including the famous, Jelly Belly's.  If shopping for a gift, you have a variety of sports tins to choose from.  GO BLUES, CARDINALS and MIZZU!   This is an easy find now that I know where they are. Only problem is, that it is near my dentist. Guess I'll be definitely flossing on the regular after eating this popcorn. As fast as my bag disappeared, is testimonial of how good it is.   Will I return? - I bought a bag at 11 AM and it was gone at 2 PM  When: January 2, 2018 Why: It's a popcorn store and I love popcorn

This vet is awesome!!! Everyone here is friendly and totally professional. I love their approach to holistic care.  They even give followup calls, to make sure everything is okay after a change in treatment. Totally recommend this vet, and we have a family of four dogs.

For those of you who do not know what REI stands for it is, Real Expensive Inventory. It may be expensive, but you will get what you pay for and that is quality. Since it is so expensive, I do not think I have ever paid full price for anything here, I patiently wait for that magical word, "CLEARANCE" to appear on top of the various racks and those are the only racks I allow myself to shop.   REI was part of our search for yoga socks, don't know why we called a outdoor, camping and biking store for yoga stuff, but we did and to our surprise they had them.  Well at least the person who answered the phone said they did, when we got there we found out otherwise. Terminology is very important in retail, all five toe socks are not yoga socks. (We did find out later, REI only has yoga socks on line)  Explaining what we needed and wanted, the sales professional in shoes introduced us to Vibram Five Finger shoes. These are some wicked shoes, each toe has it's very own slot to slide in, making them weird looking and not a good fashion statement.  May not be fashionable, but they will help us keep that New Years Resolution of living a healthier life style.   The shoes he showed us were pricey and not on sale. Not wanting to spend the $$'s, he suggested that we go home and check the clearance section at REI.com and perhaps we'd find a pair there. We are so glad he did, because looking at the ones on line we discovered TheShoeMart. com and they had a pair for a 1/3 of the cost at REI was charging.  REI may have lost the sale, but he offered up some good customer service.   Since I haven't reviewed REI before, I do want to give them a couple of good shout outs. I bought my sailing jacket here and love it. It is lightweight, hooded, keeps me dry in the rain and is perfect for late in the season late night boating on the Mississippi with the family.  Also, my job requires me to be outside at times and with winter winds, the silk long underwear from REI is the best I have found. Who'd have thought silk would keep you warm and toasty.    I may not be the typical REI customer, but when I need their products, I do love them and love them more when they are on sale.

This is my go to store for my Fur-Baby. I am very selective about the dry & canned foods I serve my dog and FMP offers some of the best. Being selective, pays off. FMP has a rewards program so after buying 10 bags of dry food (same size) I receive the 11th bag FREE. I was born in the 11th month on the 11th day, so I am all about the #11.   In addition to Murphy's food, his multiple leashes & collars have all come from this little doggie boutique. I have also purchased a collapsible water bowl and scoop bag dispenser that attach to the handle on his leash. Yes, they are all color coordinated.   This year right at the beginning of the holiday season, they had a clearance table. I made off like a bandit grabbing gifts for the family dogs. I got a Cardinals Dog Bowl for my cousins dog named Yadi. Then for another cousin who's dog in named, Louie after the Blues zamboni. I found a St. Louis Blues Bow-Tie that attaches to the collar. I am now the best Uncle to these two dogs.   Another great gift & canned food I discovered, is the Merrick Christmas Dinner and New Year's Eve Paw-ty. In addition to Murphy, I gifted these to some of my favorite dogs in the neighborhood.   The service here is always friendly and knowledgeable. They remember my name and my dog as well. I really like it when, Foster the owners dog is working the sales floor. He's the sweetest K-9 and can persuade me to give him treats every time I see him.   Will I return? - Best shop for my fur-baby  When: Easily 2 - 4 times a month Why: I spoil my dog

China King is my new favorite carry-out Chinese restaurant in my new hometown. Now only are they nailing it with their food, but the way they handle no touch curbside/carry-out is stellar.   Let's first talk about their Crab Rangoon. OMG! I hate to admit it, but I've been known to just ordering it as an afterwork snack. Yes, it's your typical fast-food Crab Rangoon made with imitation crab, but they do it right. If size matters to you, theirs are huge and filled with a creamy center. Best of all, is how they wrap it up to-go. Instead of the little wax paper bags, they use a foil/paper bag that I remember carry-out fried chicken being put in as a child. Having this type of bag, keeps them good and warm during the drive home.  I also like their egg rolls and for an entree, my go to is Beef and Broccoli.   Their set up for touch-less pick-up is engienous. There's a separate sliding drawer/compartment for payment and then a huge box area with doors for grabbing your bags of food. You're totally protected by acrylic panels and glass. They also, use better carry-out vessels.   The only detail that keeps them from getting that 5 Star rating is the customer service. As others have stated, at times it can be rude. I think that is because they are so busy and are rushing to complete all the orders in an orderly fashion.   When: Most recently February 8, 2021 and numerous other times.  Why: Crab Rangoon.

The following is a recent conversation in my home. Yes, I am bi lingual. I'm similar to Dr. Doolittle, I speak dog.   Buddy: Dad, I want a new collar and lead.   Me: Why? You have a very nice Coach one.   Buddy: I know, but it 5 years old and I'm ready for something new.   Me: Do you want a new leather one from Coach?  Buddy: No. I want a nylon one like my sister Shelby got at Four Muddy Paws.    Me: Okay little man, if that is what you want let's go shopping.   We hopped in the CRV and drove over to Lafayette Square. Buddy was very excited about his outing with dad. He knew this was not a vet or grooming visit, it was just a fun trip with dad and we were going shopping. The apple does not fall far from the tree, I think he enjoys shopping as much as I do.   As we entered the pet boutique, they promptly greeted us. Foster, who I previously refereed  to as the shop blond bombshell (did not know he was a boy dog) even came over and introduced himself to Buddy. Vera the sales associate helped us look at various collars, until Buddy finally said that is the one.   While we were looking at collars, I also mentioned that my little boy dog was scared of thunderstorms and fireworks.  Jeff one of the co-owners was also in the store and got involved in our conversation. He showed me various holistic treatments to help Buddy deal with his storm stress. Vera showed me a t-shirt that he could wear, that would also help him remain calm during thunder boomers. (one of my friends highly recommends the t-shirt) It was good to know I have other options to assist Buddy dealing with his fears.   This was the type of customer service I had gotten use to at Four Muddy Paws. I guess my last visit was one of those misses that just happen every now and then. It is good to see that they are back on their A-Game.

Need a spice for a new recipe? If so, get out of that spice aisle at your local grocer and get yourself over to Penzeys Spices in Maplewood. Once you have arrived, you will realize that you have arrived in the "mecca" of the spice world.  The large selection of your "typical" spices and the very "unique" spices will have you amazed. I love the fact that you can buy spices in a variety of sizes, to fit your immediate needs. They offer a great selection of gift boxes that make perfect holiday gifts for your "foodie" friends or a house warming gift for those who can afford to buy now.  While visiting Penzeys, drop by Vom Fass down the street for a "mecca" of oils and vinegars.

Not a fan, but I'll give you 3 Stars. Your waffle fries and the actual chicken breast saved you from getting 2 Stars.   What I found disappointing was your bun and customer service. The bun was more like a steamed bun you'd get at White Castle then the toasted bun as described on your menu. Mine was so moist; I pulled the serving of chicken off the bun and ate it plain. The chicken itself was seasoned well and provided excellent flavors to my pallet.   My second disappointment was the customer service. I admit I was there at the beginning of lunchtime (11:37 AM). The counterperson aka order taker was cold and had the personality of a wet washrag. No perky personality, she was very robotic. She did not make me feel welcome at all. She then handed me the red marker thing, with no explanation. After getting my soda, I stood patiently waiting for my order. Then a man came up and tried to pull the marker from my hand. Not knowing what or who he was, I resisted and pulled back. At that point he finally said, "I've got your order." In this day and age, you'd think someone would identify who and what he or she is doing before invading ones space. A simple, "Thanks for waiting, here's your order, hope you enjoy your lunch" would have been a nice touch.   As stated, your waffle fries saved you from being placed on my Terrible Two's List.  I don't know why, but your waffle fries are the best waffle fries I have had. Perhaps it is because they were my first waffle fries, way back when. We always remember our first.   Would I come back? Yes, but I'll order tenders instead of the sandwich and it won't be real soon.   When: October 11, 2016 Why: Lunch

I'll be honest, I really don't want to like HL because of some of their political views that are known to everyone. However, shopping with my cuz this holiday season, HL has grown on me. I wont become a true regular, but you'll find me here when I have special needs.   This past holiday season, HL made my life so much easier. I bought multiples of their gifts boxes, bags and tissue. It made my gift wrapping this year, a breeze. All I had to do was tie a Tiffany style bow around each of the boxes and I was done. It was so easy-peasy and when I bought it all, it was 50% off.   Since I had so much luck with the gift wrapping, when it was my turn to host the holiday luncheon at work I came back. What did I get this time? I got coordinating plates, napkins, glasses and paper table cloth. I even got plastic utensils in red & green. Again, the prices were 50% off and lower then Party City. My table looked stunning.   Customer service here is helpful, but not that cheerful. I overlooked the cheerful, due the holiday season. (However, I will say the service in the Kirkwood store is better.)  Chances of returning: Sad, but true, I'll probably return.  When: Nov 27, Dec 5 & 12, 2018 Why: Holiday Wrappings & Party Supplies

Only recently have I become a fan of Aldi's. I've learned that it is the place to go when you are wanting to fill the pantry. You will not see your typical brands that you do at the mainstream stores, but the quality of the brands sold at Aldi's will be the same quality.   Before I discovered this location, I was a regular at the Maplewood. That location filled my needs, but this location is like - WOW! The selection of merchandise is more vast, especially the produce and meats. It even has a larger variety of the non-food merchandise. I'm always amazed at the good buys I can find for my garden, kitchen gadgets or something for the tool box.   What also makes this location better then other Aldi's, is the lay-out. The aisles are wider and the coolers and cases for merchandising their products are newer. It makes a big difference in the presentation. Another big plus, is the friendly and fast cashiers.   I'll be back? - It's my Aldi of choice now.   When: May 17, 2019 Why: Weekly Grocery Shopping

Three visits and Twisted Biscuit is a winner for me. Don't judge me, but I have a funky work schedule, I work on Sunday. So I like to experience brunch on a weekday morning or on a Saturday morn and TB lets me do just that.   Here at Twisted Biscuit, I can relax with an early morning Bloody Mary or Mimosa with my cup of coffee as I read over the menu and select a hearty breakfast. Booze with breakfast makes for a special day.   My first visit, TB was packed and I was lucky to get a stool at the bar. To experience as much as I possibly could on the first visit, I order the flight of Bloody Mary's and Biscuits. To accompany them, I added a side of Baked Bacon and Home Fries. When they brought me my order, they accidentally gave me grits instead of Home Fries. When I pointed it out, they let me keep the grits and brought me my original order.   I am so glad I ordered the way I did, I got to sample three of their popular BM's and got to taste four of their biscuits. My favorite biscuit was the Bacon is My Jam and my fave Bloody was the I Like It Dirty. The Home Fries are done in little cubes, and they are fried to a crisp - nice. The Baked Bacon, could take home a gold medal if at the Olympics.   I tried the grits which were served to me by mistake and was pleasantly surprised. I actually liked them.
