Normally I only eat grits with Shrimp, but these were actually good.   My next visit I enjoyed, Mind Ya Biscuits. I had my two eggs scrambled, bacon, home fries and then a farm boy favorite, one biscuit with gravy. Even with no chunks of sausage in the gravy, this was a winning breakfast. The white gravy was still seasoned well enough and topping a cheddar biscuit gave it enough flavor.   The third visit, I went with my servers favorite, Huevos Twisteros. Wow - the chili was full of spice and flavor. It was good, but I'll be honest, I will not be repeating it. On my next visit, I'll be checking out the, Nashville Hot, Sticky And Sweet. That's a Belgian Waffle, topped with Twisted Tenders and Nashville Hot Honey. I love hot honey, so I cannot wait to see how theirs taste.   The bartenders and servers I have experienced were friendly and attentive. They were hustling and doing a great job.   My cousins went on my recommendation and enjoyed themselves. They did however, make a little fun of me liking the place. My favorite color is orange and when you see the decor and mugs - you'll understand why they poked fun at me. It's all "orange".   When: July 3, 10 and 23, 2021 Why: Breakfast with Booze

I have to agree with, Kevin W.. All Aldi's are not the same. This Aldi's is way better then some of the other stores I have shopped. It's bigger, cleaner, merchandised better and seems to have a better selection of products.   When I receive the Monday sales fliers, I'll be honest, Aldi's is the first one I glance through. I then compare the prices of sale items to the other two major grocers in STL. Most times if they all have similar products on sale, Aldi will have the lower price. Especially on fruits and veggies and all the produce at Aldi is "organic".   Most of the brands you see on the shelves at Aldi's may not be the national brands you are familiar with, but the quality is equal and the prices are lower.   The staff is friendly and those working as cashiers, are fast and efficient.  This has become my favorite Aldi's and slowly is becoming one of my main grocery stores.   When: January 8, 2020 Why: Shopping with a friend and picking up items for myself.

Out of the five Mexican restaurants near my home, Dos Reyes is my absolute favorite. Originally they were called One Way, so glad they changed the name and more excited that they kept up the quality of food.   I'm gradually working my way through the entire menu. My recent visits, I tried a Steak Chimichanga and then a Chicken Quesadilla. Both were very good, of the two, my favorite was the Quesadilla. It was filled full of chicken and thinly sliced onion. The guacamole and sour cream were the perfect accompaniments. I also had a serving of Cheese Dip, that was no pun intended, was great for dipping.   When I'm craving nachos, this is my place to go. They make'm with chicken and they are totally loaded with all the extras. Especially my favorite, jalapeños.   The chip are always fresh, they're still warm to the touch when served. The complementary salsa, is better the other Mex restaurants in my hood. I'm also a fan of their made from scratch Margaritas. I just find it odd, they serve them in a mason jar.   Patio is dog friendly, so that is a winner for me.   I'll be back? - I said, it was my favorite.   When: October 1, 2018 Why: Dinner

They had me the moment I saw their Red Velvet Ice Cream. I quickly asked for a sample and it was a winner, so I ordered a scoop. The friendly associate asked me which topping I wanted and I said none. He was a champion salesman, informing me that my first topping was free. When I still said no thank you, he told me most people blend brownies with the RV. He even gave me a sample of the brownie to help me make up my mind. I gave in and enjoyed my Red Velvet Cake Ice Cream blended with a brownie.   For me Maggiemoo is better then Cold Stone. On a revisit, I blended white chocolate chips and for me that was a better topping then the brownie.   Also, keep in mind that Maggiemoo's offers  Yelp Deals.

Now, I understand why the parking lot is always so full in this strip center. This little cafe serves up an amazing little breakfast.   During the pandemic, I moved to the IL side of the river. When I lived in STL, I bought all my pet supplies and food at Four Muddy Paws, so I was thrilled that they had a store on this side of the river. When I started shopping at their store next-door to Teaspoons, parking was never a problem. Now, that the restrictions have been lifted and dine-in has resumed, parking is at a premium.   On a previous visit, I mentioned to the staff of FMP that the parking is now a zoo and they informed me it was because of TC was back in full service and they served an amazing breakfast. So when I showed up to shop at FMP before they opened, I took this opportunity to experience, Teaspoon Cafe.   Immediately I was impressed with the cheerful and helpful staff. Then I was taken back by the extensive menu offerings. I was expecting just bakery items, but they offer full fledge breakfast items. I was torn between the Breakfast Burrito and pancakes. Two of the associates working the counter, both recommended the pancakes, so that is what I ordered. I added, a side of bacon, because we all know breakfast is not complete without bacon.   I was impressed with the fluffiness of my pancakes and their light golden color. They were even served with real whipped butter. Having real butter is a win all by itself. The accompanying bacon was crisp and fresh. I could tell the bacon had just been made and not prepared ahead of time like most diners.  My beverage of choice was an iced Turtle latte and it was refreshing for a hot day.   I now may have to schedule my shopping at Four Muddy Paws early in the morning, so I can also have a breakfast at Teaspoons Cafe. It will be my treat, before I buy treats next door for my fur-babies.   When: July 16, 2021 Why: Breakfast, while waiting for Four Muddy Paws to open.

Let me start off by saying, this really should be a 4 Star review, my food was delicious and my Fire Margarita was a 5 Star cocktail.   The reason that I need to lower their rating to 3 Stars, is because of the ventilation in the restaurant. With the open kitchen concept, the smoke was a unpleasant experience. My eyes kept burning and when the group I was with exited, we all could smell smoke on our clothes. The other point that brought them down to a 3, is our server wore a light weather jacket while she was waiting on us. It wasn't that cold in the restaurant. However, the service was attentive and good.   Now let me sing the praises. My Fire Margarita was off the charts. It was made with Thai Pepper infused Tequila and Grand Mariner, then mixed with sweet & sour and served in a tall glass rimmed with salt and hot pepper. I'd love to see this served at my favorite Mexican restaurant.   I started out with their Blue Crab Rangoon. It's made with "real" crab and served with sweet chili sauce. Their rangoon is not served as a typical wonton, theirs are more like a small egg roll. They're very flavorful and full of crab.   My entree was, Pad See Ew - Beef. It was absolutely delicious. As it was placed in front of me, you could see the steam rolling off the thick flat rice noodles. They were not stingy with the beef, I would have liked to seen more broccoli, but there was enough to make most people happy. The sweet soy sauce, had just enough sweetness to be a perfect accent to this dish.   If it were not for the smoke, this would be an awesome place. The food is great and the ambiance is contemporary. Hope they get the smoke problem resolved.   I'll be back? - I'll do carry-out, to avoid the smoke.   When: June 13, 2019 Why: International Supper Club

Fresh Thyme is a great addition to the CWE. The other grocery stories in the neighborhood should be shaking in their boots, with this new kid in the hood.   I have always been a fan of the FT in Kirkwood and this one totally blows them away. The produce and meat departments were very impressive, they were making my inner chef want to buy one of everything.   The lay-out of the store flows well and the aisles are wide enough for a smooth flow of two-way traffic. I was also impressed with how they used end-caps on each of the aisles to feature and promote "local" products. Fresh Thyme may be a national chain, but they still care about the local vendors.   Be sure to also check out, Iron Drop Biscuits and Beyond. I'll just say, they are mind blowing for this ole farm boy.   Only thing that I saw as a negative, is no cashiers. It was all self check-out, which I am not a fan of, but it is the way of the future and I am learning to go with the flow.   When: November 10, 2021 Why: Grand Opening

Nothing attracts me faster to a big thick burger,  then the addition of Jalapeños. If you add Pepper Jack Cheese, my favorite cheese, you totally have a winner in my eyes.   Hardee's may be a fast food joint, but it has created a winner with its' new El Diablo Thick Burger. The couple, okay several El Diablo burgers I have had, have all been sit down restaurant quality. They not only serve it with sliced Jalapeños, but they add Cheesy Jalapeño Poppers as well. Double Jalapeños, now that is a winner. Then to really top it off, they use Pepper Jack Cheese, add bacon and a Fiery Habanero Sauce.  The customer service at this location at times is lacking and service may be slower then most fast food joints. However, I am able to overlook the poor service, when I am served a Jalapeño burger.

Beer! They've got it all, draft, bottled and can. They've got local, regional and out of state craft beers. They've even got the boring major brewery beers for those who like that type of brew.   To be honest, I accidentally found ITAP. I wasn't paying attention to the entrance as I was going to Epic Pizza. It was a Monday and when I pulled on Epic's door it was locked (they don't open till 5 PM). Not paying attention as I stated, I tried the door to the left and presto, I was in beer heaven.   Once the bartender explained to me that I was in a different biz, I was impressed with knowledge of beer. She answered questions and got us set up with a couple of chilled draft beers. Then she made my night, telling me Epic will deliver to us here at ITAP.   We enjoyed some beers on the side patio. Then we went next door ordered pizza and wings and continued to enjoy more beers on the patio. With or without the pizza, ITAP is a great place to enjoy a cold one.

Okay, Pie Oh My! has won me over so I am increasing their rating to a well deserved 5 Stars. With them serving pie, I knew I could not and would not stay away and I am glad I didn't.  My last two visits were so good, I'm tempted to bestow the title of Honorary Aunt on Jane. Her pies were "family" good.   Last Saturday I started craving pie at work, so when I got off duty I drove like a bat fleeing hell to arrive at POM before closing.  I normally do drive like a bat fleeing hell, but that is besides the point. I work in IL and did not want to miss out on a slice of pie.   Oh, Lucky Day. When I arrived a fresh batch of Pear Apple Cranberry Crumble Pies had just come out of the oven. Being 5" they were the perfect size for two.  Jane boxed one up for me and since it was so fresh out of the oven she recommended venting the lid. I told her, l lived close enough so leave the lid open and I'd drive cautiously.   The aroma filled the car as I drove home. When I entered the house carrying the white box the SO quickly asked, "What you got?"  When I replied pie, he followed me to the kitchen and was amazed to see that it was still warm.  The crumbled top looked so inviting, but we waited till it cooled. It was hard to wait, but it was so worth the wait.  The combination of Pear Apple and Cranberry was a magical combination. A scoop of vanilla ice cream was the perfect accompaniment.   Chatting with Jane, I told her the SO's favorite was Banana Cream and she informed me she makes a different cream pie everyday.  She then said, she'd do Banana Cream on Tuesday. With my little Diva dog crossing the Rainbow Bridge on Monday, I didn't make it to POM. However, Wednesday we enjoyed Coconut Cream, Chocolate Pumpkin and Chocolate Bourbon Pecan.  How can you go wrong combining Chocolate & Pumpkin? You can't.  It is a winner.  Also, for me any pie containing pecans is always a winner.   The crust is flaky and the fillings are ample for the size. I truly love the 5" size pies, as stated they are the perfect size for two or for someone who wants to say, "I ate the entire pie." My taste buds are happy that I have returned to Pie Oh My!, but my waistline isn't so sure.

Let me begin by saying, I am not a fan of Indian cuisine. Or should I say, House of India has won me over and changed my view of Indian cuisine. I think I've just been eating at all the wrong Indian restaurants. I always been hesitant in my ordering, but loving lamb I felt safe ordering their Lamb Krahi.   Lamb Krahi is stir fried with fresh bell peppers, onion, tomatoes, ginger and spices. I ate most of my entree without adding the rice, because it was so filling and flavorful all by itself. I did enjoy the rice, it was perfectly prepared. Many other Indian restaurants have always served me rice that was over cooked, dry and sticky. HOI served rice that was moist and flakey, making it a perfect accompaniment to and entree.   Our group of 13 (International Supper Club) did not phase the server. He didn't mind that we wanted 9 different separate checks. The kitchen even kept the flow of food to our table consistent, so we were all eating together and not in shifts.   A big thanks to House of India for showing me the true way Indian food should be served and prepared. Next time a friend suggest that we go out for Indian food, instead of trying to convince them to go somewhere else, I'll recommend we go to House of India.

Even being on a busy street like Bemiston in Clayton, I still enjoyed a relaxing lunch on their patio. The traffic was not loud or distracting and at lunch time there was enough shade to make it comfortable. If the weather is permitting, I'd highly recommend dining outside.   When at a wine bar, of course I had to have a glass of Pinot Grigio. Mine was; Stemmari. It's an Italian wine from Sicily. It was a perfect accompaniment to the Bronzed Mahi Mahi. It was served with Shrimp and top of a bed of Green French Lentils. It was a perfect healthy lunch and I'm glad that it was. Because, it made up for me cheating on my diet and enjoying the incredibly delicious Bruschetta & Tapenade basket.   My only disappointment was that after enjoying the bruschetta and Mahi Mahi, I was too full to enjoy their famous Bread Pudding for dessert. Oh, well that gives me another excuse to come back in the near future.

I paid $5 to park across the street for lunch and it was worth every dollar. Plus, it was a convenient location since the BF was wearing a fashionable cast on the right leg.  We arrived at the end of a typical business lunch time, so our service was quick and friendly.   What would a visit to Flying Saucer be without a cold beer? It would be nothing, so we ordered a Avery White Rascal and a New Holland Poet to enjoy with an order of MoJo Chicken Wings, which had a Cajun spice. They were crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside, just the way I like them.  I also enjoyed how they serve the wings in a stainless steal bowls.   We followed up the tasty wings with two burgers. I had the Saucer Burger which is a 1/2 lb of Angus Beef, which is a premium beef. It was garnished with a mustard-mayo, red onion, tomato, lettuce, pickle and topped with Pepper Jack cheese. They grilled my burger to medium rare, just the way I like it.   The BF ordered the San Miguel Burger, which I think is the best burger in STL. It is a combination of beef and chorizo, grilled to your specifications. They then garnish it with Tabasco-Mayo, red onion, lettuce and tomato. To set it above all other burgers, they add avocado, pico de gallo, queso fresco and then topped with a fried egg.  Now that is a burger. I only got a bite, but I know what I'll be getting the next time I visit Flying Saucer.   Sophia was our server and she said it was only her second day. Wow, if she is a newbie, her trainer did a great job. She was friendly, attentive and sold/knew her menu well. I found one of my favorite things in the Men's room, a Dyson Hand Dryer. i am confident Flying Saucer will be my stop before or after a Cardinals game.

I've been back for lunch and a UYE since my original visit and I'm impressed enough to raise them up a star. Yes, Good Fortune is, As good as it gets!  My first visit back was for lunch. Since I was so impressed with their Manhattan and the Rangoon appetizer, I had to repeat them. I was not disappointed. I think I may be addicted to these Rangoon's. Being a fan of the infamous St. Paul Sandwich which supposedly was created here in STL, I just had to see what GF did with this classic. Normally I go for a chicken St. Paul, but the lunch menu was only offering a vegetable. Still, I was delighted to chow down on what they had put between those two slices of white bread.   The most recent visit was another dinner and a UYE. This one I was really excited about. I not only was going to finally enjoy their scallops, but I was going to be dining with a group of foodies. Having dined here before, I told my table we had to share the dumplings and rangoon. Which we did and we also shared  the pork ribs.   If all gluten free food taste as good as these ribs, I just may go "gluten free". Not really, but these ribs with a cumin rub and chili glaze were pretty tasty. The meat was very tender and fell right off the bone. On a return visit, if dining alone I can easily have an order of 5 ribs as an entree.   Now for the main reason they got their 5th star - amazingly delicious, scallops. Scallops are my favorite seafood and Good Fortune impressed me. I'm not a fan of turnips and was concerned about the turnip puree in the description on the menu. However, with the country ham xo sauce and pickled mushrooms along side, the sea scallops rocked my world. I didn't even mind the turnips. In fact they peaked my interest enough to give turnips more of a try.   Service is always outstanding. The entire staff is personable and friendly.  I'll be back? - Been three times and don't plan to stop.   When: June 12 and 24, 2018 Why: Lunch and Dinner/UYE

It is so simple. Check-in, name called, blood drawn and you're on your way.   I had no idea this location was so close to home. I have always used the Quest closer to my doctors office, stopping by on my way home. This time I had to have blood drawn a week before seeing a specialist, so I Googled Quest and found this location which is conveniently located in my hood. It is hidden on the backside of the building so it is unnoticeable as you drive by the medical building. Out of site, out of mind.   I did not go on-line and make an appointment ahead of time. I just showed up, signed my name on the registry and took a seat. I barely had time to check in on Yelp and my name was being called. I presented the technician with my paperwork, insurance card and ID. She quickly got busy, preparing the vacutainer tubes as I tried to relax listening to the music playing from a small boom box she had sitting on the floor. I HATE having my blood drawn and have veins that most technicians hate. My veins are small, roll and hide when it is time to be poked and drained. My tech was not chatty, but she was professional. I give her four stars because, she jabbed me without hurting me and got in a vein on the first poke. I was In and Out in nothing flat, it was express service at its' best.   Now that I know a Quest is near my home, I may make this location my choice for blood draws. Instead of using the one near my doctors office, I'll come here. When I'm  finished here, I can get myself a treat at Starbucks or Ted Drew's which both are conveniently located across the street. You get a treat when you donate blood, why not get one after having a blood draw.

I already know I gotta go back and when I do I'll have to totally cheat on my low-carb diet. I've been told the Double Decker pizzas are incredible and from the ones I saw being delivered to tables around me, I can agree without even tasting one.   This JJ Twig's is small and compact. They made use of every square inch, so the tables are placed tightly together. If you're seated at a two top table in the center row in the back dining room, you may feel claustrophobic. The music is also a tad to loud, with the smallness and high volume it made it hard to have a normal conversation.  Now that I have the negatives out of the way, let us talk food.   We started out with an order of Chicken Wings, Trashed. Crispy chicken wings, tossed in a hot sauce and then put back in the frier. Spicy and crispy, makes for a good chicken wing. They came with a side of more hot sauce, but we totally did not need to do any extra dipping.   My entree was a Sensational Salad, the Lou Que. A huge portion of mixed greens, red onion, tomato, cheddar cheese and BBQ Pulled Pork with a Buttermilk Ranch Dressing. The pulled pork was tender and I was totally stuffed, to be honest I could empty my bowl.   My dining partner ordered one of their sandwiches, Italian Beef with a side of Onion Rings. The beef was tender and topped with Mozzarella Cheese and Jalapeños. The menu claims the Onion Rings are hand battered, I doubt that. To me they came from a bag, but a good bag. They just seemed to be processed.   The service is friendly and sitting so close to other diners, chances are you'll banter back and forth with a table or two. Being a causal restaurant in Saint Louis Hills, it draws a large family clientele. I'll be honest, I normally don't like to be surrounded by little diners, but one kept me totally entertained. I still smile thinking about her antics.   It is so good to have another option for dining in my hood.

Great gift and souvenir shop on Decatur Street. It's larger, cleaner and more organized then some of the shops closer to Bourbon Street. I also, found the prices to be a little bit less expensive. So walk a little further and enjoy a cheaper price and larger selection of product.   They lured me in with a display that was close to the main street entrance. It was a couple of racks with dog related plaques and magnets. Being a Sheltie lover and having to find a gift for my pet sitter who also loves the breed, it was perfection.   The staff was friendly and personable. As I was being rung out, they asked about my dogs, which for me is like asking about my kids. You ask, I will gladly show you a picture or two.   Great selection, service and prices. I'd shop here again.   When: August 29, 2016 Why: Sheltie Merchandise

I am sad to say, I have to get my magic eraser out and remove two stars from my review of Arcelia's. Our second visit was not as favorable as our first. Do they do lunch better then dinner? Or was our first visit a fluke or was this last one a miss? Not sure, but last nights visit on a Taste Card coupon was a major disappointment.   House Margarita - Weak. Ordered with no salt, got it with salt. Drank from straw.   Queso with Chorizo - Tortillas were tough and chewy.   Chips & Salsa - Salsa to0 strong in garlic. Chips reminded me of a multi-grain chip from a bag.   Tamale Dinner - Made in house was questionable due to their quality  Beans & Mexican RIce - No flavor and dried out.  Large Combination Dinner - Soft Chicken Taco - Good, best thing of the night.  Burrito top was hard under the melted cheese. Enchilada was just okay.   Flan - Was over cooked.   Service - It was obvious he wanted to be elsewhere.   It is a shame my food did not taste as good as my pictures looked. With the difference in the two visits, I am not sure I will be returning. I am thankful I got $10 off with my Taste Card. Which brings up a question, wouldn't you bring on your A-Game when you know a diner is using a coupon? That way you'd persuade them to return and pay full price.

I'm going to make this one short, sweet and direct. When alcoholics dream, they dream of Total Wine & More. TWM has is all....if you want booze, they've got it. It you want it at a reasonable price, they've got that too.   Stocking up the bar for the holiday parties? Shop Total Wine & More.

Very friendly staff, they provide excellent customer service.  It is a very cute and comfortable shop. It's cozy like a neighborhood coffee shop be.   What attracted me to visit Park Avenue Coffee was the fact they were featured on the Food Network and won the best Gooey Butter Cake competition. Not sure who did the actual judging, but they made a bad call. I was not impressed, nor were my friends who I shared the original cake with. Other bakeries and grocery stores do a much better gooey butter then the one I got from PAC.   Visit PAC for the coffee, ambiance and good friends - not the GBC.

If I've said it once, I've said it multiple times, there is no difference in all these different froyo joints. Now that I have been to Orange Leaf, I can no longer say that.  OL's selection and variety of flavors and toppings totally has me screaming for ice cream.   On my first visit I was impressed with the customer service right off the bat. As I entered the store, I was greeted by the two young men working and was told that if I  wanted to sample. Samples? What a sales tool, none of the other froyo places I have visited have ever offered a taste test. I didn't abuse that opportunity, but it did help me fill my cup.   During Snow Cone season, my favorite flavor is Wedding Cake and I almost "screamed" when I saw it available at OL. I combined WC with Orange and created my very own Dream Bowl. I always thought orange and vanilla was a good combo, but using Wedding Cake made me a new favorite.   I was picking this order up to go, so when I arrived I called the SO and read off all the daily flavors. He selected English  Toffee and Crumbled Heath Bar as his topping.  He was silent as he emptied his bowl. That translates into, this is some good froyo.   Being curious, I timed my travel time for the drive home. Using side and back streets, I made it home in 6 minuets with little to no melting. I am not sure if this is good or bad news. The good is, it is close enough for ice cream treats. The bad news is, to close and can easily sabotage my diet.   Side Note: Orange is my favorite color, but that fact had no effect on this review and star rating.

I thought for sure my experience was going to be dreadful, but it actually was fast and easy. First I went to the wrong office and it had a huge line. Luckily a cheerful and helpful lady came over and made sure everyone was in the "right" place. When I explained my situation, she informed me I just needed to go to the Collector of Revenue and they'd have my tax bill on file.   When I arrived, the line was short and only one person was ahead of me. When it was my turn, I told the young lady my story/problem. I had lost my personal property tax bill. Only thing I could figure out is that it fell into the recycling and got thrown out.  When I told my story she giggled, smiled and quickly printed me a new copy. Best thing, I didn't have to pay the penalty for being late. Now that is great custom service.

Books and a Beautiful Building, who can ask for anything more.   The Grand Hall is absolutely gorgeous and I enjoyed the displays of local history.  They had the bell from the KMOV-TV show Cookie & The Captain, which I got to ring when my Cub Scout Troop were the audience for one of the shows. Oh, the flashback of memories.   Great quiet spaces to study and do work projects, with an endless amount of references available at your fingertips. If you need a computer, they have that too.   If I lived downtown, I'd be a regular here and perhaps the Duke.

Best cookie trays in the area. I can go to a party and spot a Cose Doci cookie tray in an instant. They're beautifully presented and the cookies themselves burst in flavor. I just want to get a cup of coffee or a glass of milk and totally indulge myself.    If you need cookies for a party - this is the place and it is totally worth the drive to Ferguson. While there get yourself some rugelach and stash it away for yourself. It is so good it's not worth sharing.

When: February 13, 2011 Why:    Lunch  We arrived just as the doors were being unlocked. There were dozens of folks crowded around the door waiting for it to be unlocked. You would have thought it was the famous Filene's  Bridal Dress Sale.  As we entered, most of the crowd had worked their way to the tables of choice.  It was our lucky day, we got the last booth.  The doors opened and they were slammed, but this did not stop the servers from providing top notch service.  Our server was perky, friendly and seemed to be actually interested in the rest of day.   We ordered ice tea as our beverage, we explained we were going to a beer dinner that night and didn't want to start our buzz early. We then saw chicken wings on the menu, which I never noticed before so we had to try them. Our order was balanced out with two cheeseburgers and one order of fries.   It goes without saying, the grilled burgers were flawless. They are always big, juicy, and have that flavor of just coming off the backyard grill. I'd like the fries here to be more crispy, but the portion is large enough for two to share.   Now let's talk wings, OMG!!! A place that is famous for their burgers, also has amazing wings. The wings were above average in size and not breaded which is always a plus for me. They were crispy on the outside, moist and tender on the inside. The sauce was just a nice coating, with a spicy temp between warm and hot. The only bad thing about these wings, is that don't do carry out at O'Connell's. If they did, I'd be a true regular.   Watching the other tables, on our next visit we've got to try the chili and onion rings.   Again, the service was excellent for a place that filled up fast and had a line waiting for openings. I always use to cringe at the fact they served on paper products, but I now understand. With the volume they serve, toss away plates and bowls is common sense. Glad it is Eco friendly.

One of the best, if not the BEST Margaritas in the Saint Louis area. No mixes are used here, it is all fresh hand squeezed juice. Which makes the Margaritas go down oh, so smoothly.   Norma H. and I had the same day off, so we meet up for lunch at Maya Cafe. I had a Entertainment.com Coupon for a buy one get one free. I really never save with these coupons, I always end up buying more drinks and appetizers. However, it does give me more to Yelp about.  I've already told you about the awesome Margaritas and they were the perfect accompaniment to the chips and pico de gallo. Their chips were thick cut and tossed in a coarse salt. No soupy, overly pureed salsa here. They serve a spicy pico de gallo. The diced tomato, onion and cilantro was a perfect topping for the chips.   We also enjoyed an order of Calamares (Calamari). It was served with two dipping sauces; a Criollo Gaze and Chimichurri Dip. Both were good, I favored the Glaze and Ms. Norma preferred the Dip. Our waiter, said he loved to double dip, he'd dip in both for extra flavor  Norma had the lunch portion of Pollo En Pepian Dulce. It looked fabulous, she loved it and I was jealous of her side of asparagus, my favorite vegetable. I forget what mine was called, but it was our waiters favorite. It was a chicken breast fried, served as a sandwich with refried beans, lettuce and tomatoes. It was one tasty sandwich that you'll never see at Subway.   Service was great and personable. I've gotta go back, we forgot to try the Flan.

Menard's is a cross between Lowe's/Home Depot and Big Lots. It's a home improvement store with a mix of everything else too. It has a small clothing area and even a few bizarre grocery items. They even had a pet department, where I found a new dog bowl for my fur-baby.   The store is laid out weird, the flow of aisles changes thru out the store making it difficult to shop. However, I am sure it is an advantage of the cash registers. As you wonder thru the store looking for the one single item that you came in for, you find stupid items that you realize you can't live without. I had no idea I needed duck tape with a cute little dog and dog bone on it, but I bought it. It's so cute, I'll probably never use it.   If you are a brand shopper, Menard's may not be your store. The majority of the items sold here, were off brands that I was not familiar with. However, being off brand, the prices are very similar to Big Lots. Just be sure to check the quality before buying.   Shopping in winter, I was impressed with their patio furniture on display. When it's closer to patio season, I'll go back to see if they expand the selection.   Unique store with low prices and minimal customer service. You get what you pay for.   Why: Wanted the Menard's experience When: January 11, 2016

What? That is the attitude I had when my co-worker told me she ordered the cake for our managers baby shower from Wal-Mart. I was even in more shock, when she told me she also ordered the tray of sandwiches from them. The shock went deeper, when she said it was from the Maplewood Commons location. I told her that location was on my "Terrible Two's" list on Yelp. See admitted it was a rough store, but assured me it would be okay.   She was right, they did a great job on the cake. I was surprised how flavorful it was and smooth and beautiful the icing was. The sandwiches were just average. In fact they forgot about them and didn't have them ready when she went to pick our order up. However, they quickly prepared them and discounted our order by 10%. In the rush, several of the dollar sized sandwiches missed the cheese. Oh well, at least they hustled and tried to make it right.   Congratulations Wal-Mart, I'm removing you from my Terrible Two's List.

Yawn City! This brunch no way in hell deserves 5 Stars. In all honesty, 3 Stars is the best I can do. It is way over priced for the quality and selection of food that they serve. I was almost turned off immediately when we went through the buffet line. We had to set two bowls and one plate aside to get one that was clean.   The positives were the Eggs with Spinach, the bacon, the link sausage and the chili. On the salad and pastry side, the potato salad with sweet potatoes was very unique and flavorful. The small cinnamon roll was good, but it was the same mass produced one you get at almost every brunch in STL. Having small bagels with cream cheese and lox, was a nice touch.   The negatives were the potatoes on the hot buffet and the french toast which were ice cold. Their potatoes had no seasoning and the french toast was rubbery. Also, when they replaced the link sausage with patties, they were tough and chewy. The chicken salad was bland as bland could be. A high school home economics student could make a better chicken salad.   A major disappointment was Dr. Dan the Pancake Man. Being a big celebrity, I guess he thought it was okay to arrive late. He didn't even show up till after 10:30 AM and wasn't even making pancakes when we left at 10:45 AM. We arrived early so we could enjoy his masterful art work in pancakes, but that did us little good.   I was not impressed enough to return. However, if you do come, sit in the backroom, the front is way too crowded with the buffet, live music and Pancake Man.

New location, same great food. Can't wait until they get their liquor license. A good beer or a Bloody Mary will go so well with their Cajun - Creole cooking.   I really enjoy their chicken wings. They season them well and fry them to a crispy golden color. I prefer to have my sauce served on the side, because I enjoy several of them plain. Today we selected, their House and Hot Buffalo sauces. I liked the tanginess of the House and dining partner liked their Hot Buffalo. I'm normally not a fan of super hot sauces, but found the HB not to be that spicy hot.    I loved their burgers at the old location and still love them here. At home, I have a burger press that measures and makes my burgers all the same size and shape. However, when I am dining out I get excited when I see a hand pressed burger. I know it is strange, but a odd shaped grilled burger just taste better. Especially when it is topped with fried Jalapeños.   My DP enjoyed a Muffuletta that was huge and his was a half order. It was grilled like a panini and stuffed with meat. By the time we shared small orders of both Onion Rings and Bristo Fries, he had to take half of his half home. The Bristo Fries are house cut with skins on and the Onion Rings were thick cut and a crisp beer batter breading.   Our server was Dora, no she is not the explorer and she's heard that joke before. She was attentive and was able to describe and explain items in a appetizing way. The ambiance was plain as plain could be. I remember when that place was a jazz club in the early 90's with all the rich paneling of the entry and hallway. The bar was massive and made of the same rich wood. What a shame previous owners destroyed all the historic beauty.

The customer service at this store gets a strong 4. We had a wedding to attend and Brad recently has added a few pounds to his his frame. (He's given me permission to tell this story) So instead of going out and buying a new suit, when we know the weight is coming off, we opted to rent a suit for the evening. We did our research and found Savvi to be the closest one to home to fulfill our needs.   When we arrived at the store the gentleman working was a true professional, he could size Brad by just looking at him. He would say what the size would be and then proved himself right with the measuring. The selection for suits is not as vast as tuxedos, but a simple black suit is just what we needed for a late afternoon wedding.   Brad picked up the suit the day before the wedding and he looked rather dapper with his own shirt, tie and shoes. Brad's best friend was so glad we came to see her youngest son marry his sweetheart. It was after the wedding that all hell broke lose, or should I say the waistband on the rented suit broke.   We actually made it to the reception and were seated at our table for dinner, when Brad started to feel the difference in the trousers.  The adjustable waistband on both sides were totally shot. We tried to fix them, but had no luck. He couldn't walk without them starting to fall down, the only thing we could do was leave.   I am better in a crisis situation then Brad is and he'll admit it. As we left the reception hall Brad was on the phone to Savvi telling them the situation. He was one pissed off customer. He could not believe he was going to have to miss this reception and what would his friend think of us leaving. While driving I see a Casey's Store, keep in mind we are out in rural Illinois and pulled in hoping they'd have what I need. See that review for that part of story. They totally rocked.   I get safety pins from one of the girls at Casey's and fix the pants so we can return to the reception. We make it back before the bridal party and no one is the wiser to the drama.  Who are you kidding, the story was too funny not to share.   When we returned the suit, they did not give a full refund like the girl on the phone said, but they did give a 50% discount.  Even after they examined the pants and admitted they were totally unwearable.   Customer Service 4 - Product 2 which averages out to a 3 Star Rating.

Meet West County friends here for happy hour and it was a pleasant experience. However, I must say being in a strip center with multiple businesses, parking is a pain and we got there at 5 p.m..  Appetizers were half price till 6 p.m. which was a great deal. We had chicken wings, quesadilla and Black Angus Sliders. We also had an order of french fries and a Crispy Chicken Salad.  We were pleased with all the food.  The service was very good, the waitress was friendly and provided top notch service. I have been here several times before, the clientele has changed and it just doesn't have that festive fun feeling anymore. I'll come back, hopefully it was just a Tuesday crowd that wasn't in a party mind set.

When: February 25 Why: Late Night Dinner After Work  We've ordered a Chicago Original Deluxe a couple more times and have enjoyed each and every one.   This time I ordered the daily special off the kitchen calendar. Oh, guess I better explain "kitchen calendar" before I go further. It is a monthly calendar they place on top of your pizza box that has different special offerings each day. The night I ordered it was a two topping large pizza (St. Louis Style), a house salad (big enough for two) and an appetizer of your choice (we choose chicken wings) for $19.99.  Our pizza was sausage with pepperoni and it was damn good. This place I am learning, can do both Chicago and St. Louis very well   On one of our future orders we are trying Chicago Style with the sauce on top and our wings extremely hot.

Damn, it!! I want to give you 5 Stars, but can't and yet you deserve more then 4. Yelp has got to figure out a way for us to give that 1/2 Star when a business is fluctuating between two stars.    The food here amazes me, it is so simple and yet so very good. It truly reminds on the convenience stores in the French Quarter with small kitchens in the back. There is no fancy presentation here. It is quality Cajun, Creole, and Comfort Food served in a tin pan dish that you'd eat out of on a camping trip and I am totally fine with that.   Our most recent visit, we shared a Captain Dee's as an appetizer . Three crispy cakes that were fried crisp on the outside and yet the seafood inside was moist. Out of the three, the crab was our favorite. Then it would be the shrimp and salmon. They were served with a portion of Arugula in the center. It would of been a nice touch if the arugula was tossed in a simple vinaigrette. This could easily be a light lunch.   Having started a Slinger list here on Yelp, I ordered The Sink. It just felt like a breakfast for dinner night. Two fluffy biscuits (and I do mean fluffy), two sausage patties, tater tots, two eggs over easy, sausage gravy & topped with diced jalapeño bacon, white cheddar and pepper jack cheese. Be still by beating heart. Wait I think my heart did stop after eating this, but it was so worth it. The gravy was rich and creamy and covered the entire entree. The spicy sausage and the jalapeño bacon were the perfect accent. This may be a different twist to the traditional Slinger, but it is still worthy of a spot on my list.   My dining partner, Brad ordered wisely. He selected the 4 Horseman, which gave you a sampling of four different entrees. In two different tin pans, were sampling of; Étouffée, Jambalaya, SBR (sausage, beans & rice) and Seafood Gumbo. These servings were so large, that two adults could of shared. We differed on our rankings of which one we liked best, but agreed all four were pretty damn amazing. The Seafood Gumbo and Jambalaya were defiantly the shining stars.   Parking here is not my issue, I have the most amazing Parking Angel, that always makes sure I have Prince Parking. My only disappointments were that there is no liquor  license yet and the slow service. I know the license is beyond your control, but I really wanted a drink and can't wait to see how you prepare a Bloody Mary. The service  you can control and it just needs a little adjustment. Our server was bubbly and friendly, but got easily sidetracked. If I had that Bloody Mary, I most likely could of cared less. We probably all suffer from ADD now and then....LOL   Get that liquor license and your guaranteed 5 Stars.

21 custom colors of M&M's need I say more?  Multiple flavors of Jelly Belly's, including one of my favorites, Popcorn in bulk or pre wrapped. Wall full of unique and candies of days gone by. This place is what tooth fairies dream of. A heaven for those who truly have a sweet tooth.   This candy boutique is the perfect place for creating little gift bags full of candy treats for a child's birthday party or in my case a 60 year old. I was able to snag candies from yesteryear and create a gift bag that will have the memories flowing.   The customer service is cheerful and helpful. The young lady assisting me made me feel welcome and I could really tell she appreciated my business. I rarely need a place like this, but when I do Miss M's will be my destination.

I am not going to break the trend of 5 Star ratings on this cute & darling little spice shoppe. Cruising through this store, I was able to fill my little picnic basket, (not  a plastic one like at most grocers) of goodies to take home and make themed gift baskets for holiday gifts.   I created one basket for my cousin who thinks making popcorn is cooking dinner. I was able to get a variety of Amish popcorn, oils and toppings that will make her popcorn dinner gourmet.   Another one I created was a "Heartburn" basket. I could not believe the variety and intensity of Hot Sauces they offered.  Then when I went to check out, next to the register they had a display of Ghost Pepper Powder, the perfect final touch to my basket. I was so excited to see it, I almost squealed with glee. The lady ringing me out was so cute and helpful. She quizzed me, to make sure I understood what a ghost pepper was. I assured her that I did and that we cook with fresh ones at home often. Good customer service, making sure that I was an educated shopper. She shared story of those who didn't know the power of the ghost and how they reacted.   I'm a city dweller, but OTSS is worth the drive. You'll be impressed with their selection and the variety they offer of each item. Plus, the ladies who work here know the product and are having fun selling it.   I will be back.

Booze, this review is just about the cocktails we enjoyed while sitting at the bar. It was a day of shopping and bar hopping and we finished our day at Gamlin Whiskey House. We were pleasantly greeted by our bartender. As we enjoyed our cocktails his attitude got cocky, as if he were the Bees Knees.  Speaking of Bees Knees, that was one of the drinks we enjoyed and I must agree with Erin G. this is one of the best cocktails I have ever had. It's  a sweet blend of Knob Creek Rye and Ginger Ale that is served on honey laced ice. OMG, this drink is perfect for winter or summer. I can enjoy it pool side or fire side.   However, the other drink we ordered was a major disappointment. Big Bacon Daddy, did not live up to its' description in their cocktail menu. The menu boosted bold flavors of bacon infused rye, the sweetness of maple syrup & the complexity of pomegranate shaken and served with a bacon strip garnish. This may sound good, but we found it rather blah. It was so blah, we didn't even finish it. You know a cocktail is bad when a seasoned Yelper doesn't finish their cocktail.   Some day I'll stop by for another cocktail, but I will not be in a hurry.

I have never been so pleasantly surprised and disappointed at the same time as I was here a Stratton's Cafe. The food was great, but this counter service and busing your own tables sucked. It was so disappointing, that it cost you a star.   I will admit I am at fault for not reading the reviews closer. I quickly looked at the star ratings and pictures posted by friends and hopped in the car. When I arrived, I had prince parking right outside the front door, I was ready for a great breakfast. When I walked in the door shortly after 7 AM, I was shocked to see that it was order at the counter and more shocked to see that I had to go fetch my order just like at the Bread Co..  I'll break it down in to Pros and Cons. Let me begin with the cons, so I can end this review on a positive note.   CONS:  1. No table service, you order at the counter and have to pick up your own food.  2. When you are finished eating it is like eating at home, you bus and clean your own table. You scrape the leftover food in to the trash, separate the dishes, silverware and baskets.  3. Plates are placed inside big bulky black plastic baskets, taking up more room on the tables.  4. They serve Kaldi's coffee.   PROS:  1. The food was seasoned well, they did not overly salt anything. I who normally does not add salt to anything gave some of my food a dash.  2. Good Biscuit and Gravy, worthy of being on my list. Don't think the biscuits are made from scratch, but the sausage gravy was excellent.  3. Offered an Egg White Scramble with Spinach and Feta Cheese, that was very yummy.  5. Prepared Over-Easy Eggs, correctly. Buttermilk pancakes were okay, big in size, but lacked flavor.  6. Hashbrown Casserole was cheesy and tasty.   This could easily been a 4 Star Review if they offered table service. Doing half the work myself cheapened my breakfast. When I pay $30 for two people to enjoy breakfast I want to be served and not treated as if I am dining at a fast food place.  Food was good, but not having table service to match the prices, I will breakfast else where.

It's been over a year, so it is time to do an update.  I am still a fan of their Chicago Style Pizza. I love the original Deluxe which has White Chicken Meat, Spinach, Bacon and Tomato. They give you the choice of sauce on top or bottom. We bounce back and forth, but usually go with bottom. Chicken and Spinach on a pizza to me makes it healthy. (lol)  Add a House Salad and you've got a meal for three or next days lunch for two.   Fast and friendly delivery.

It's not St. Louis style pizza, it is Jersey Style pizza. So it is not for the faint of heart. It is a true east coast pizza.   The crust is house made and in not cracker thin like the typical STL crust. It is hand tossed, chewy and full of flavor. In addition to making their own dough, they make their pizza sauce from a family recipe. If you're going to do all that, you might as well go all the way and use real 100% Mozzarella Cheese. The slices are cut pie style and can be folded in half for easy eating. The bottom of our pizza was crisp, making it obvious it was baked in a brick bottom oven.  It made it for easy handling. I was able to pick it up for a big bite.  We started out with the 10 piece Buffalo Hot Wings. They were heavily coated in hot and spicy buffalo sauce. To make the serving easier and neater at the table, they come with a small set of tongs. Must say, that is a nice customer service touch. After munching on our wings, we over estimated our appetites by ordering, "The Boss" one of the speciality pizzas.   The Boss, is a gigantic 18" pizza topped with; pepperoni, sausage, mushrooms, onions, bell peppers and black olives with a touch of garlic. The pizza was fully covered edge to edge, with all of my favorite toppings. We both loved it, but each of us could only eat two slices each. We ended up having enough to take home for both of us to enjoy the next day for lunch.   I'm a big fan of cold pizza and The Boss did not disappoint. It was as good cold as it was piping hot.   The Patch is becoming a hot little neighborhood with Feraro's and its across the street neighbor, Stacked STL. If you can't get in to one, go to the other.  When: August 25, 2015 Why: Dinner

OMG! I think I need to add Louie's to my speed dial.  Saturday night both my partner and I were getting home late from work,  I was arriving home first so I was responsible for ordering dinner. He said, he wanted to be surprised, so that was my challenge.   I knew ordering from our regular Chinese or pizza joints would not be a surprise, so what could I do. I flipped through our take out menus/coupons and found Louie's. I knew this place from passing it when I went to my local Tan Co., and thought we'd expand our experience and try something new.  I'm a fan of St Louis style pizza, so when ordering from Louie's I stepped outside my safety zone and ordered their, "Chicago Original Deluxe". We were totally blown away, the combination of chicken, fresh spinach, bacon and tomato was amazing. The Italian seasonings in the sauce and Louie's secret blend of mozzarella cheese made every slice of pizza a masterpiece. I'll still love my St. Louis Style pizza, but I have now become a bi-pizzal.  I also ordered their Original Spicy chicken wings, and House Salad. The salad was "A" typical pizza parlor salad, little larger and more generous with the toppings (love my black olives). Their Original Spicy chicken wings were bone sucking good and hot enough. I could not imagine what the "Extreme Heat" would have been.    The phone customer service was excellent, very friendly and helpful in determining if I lived within delivery area. I was given a delivery time of 45 minuets which was perfect with my plans. Delivery was quicker, made it in 30 and delivery person continued the excellent service.  My partner was surprised, we were surprised by the quality, so my challenge was completed successfully. We will be calling Louie's again and again.

If you join Louie's email club, you a free appetizer for your birthday. All you need to do is buy a small pizza and you can get one of their many tasty appetizers at no cost to you. You may have to buy something to get your gift, but I was happy with an order of Hot Chicken Wings as a gift. Combining a small pizza and the wings made for a perfect lunch as we did our house chores.    The staff here is friendly and when picking up my order, they always engage me in witty banter.

I am so happy that Frankly Sausages has opened a brick and mortar store. Rarely do I have an opportunity to eat at any food truck. So when I find one that I fall in love with, I keep hoping that some day they'd open a "real" restaurant. This time my wishes came true.   FOC is a great addition to the Cherokee strip. The space is simplicity at its best! Very minimalist. I love the industrial style tables that are long and meant for sharing space. The rustic lighting hanging above the tables completes the ambiance, in the simplest way.   The counter for ordering is at the back of the shop. You'll make your selection from the slate menus hanging on the wall, again in a very industrial style. Tonight on opening day, I had to go with my favorite, Lamb. I discovered this delicious sausage once at Six Mile Brewery and have enjoyed it every time I have had an opportunity. It is topped with; red onion, feta and fresh oregano. No sauces needed on this sandwich, the meat flavor stands alone.   A must order with any sausage is the famous fries at Frankly. In my humble opinion, they are by far the best fries in the city and county. They offer a variety of sauces for dipping, but my choice is the house made ketchup. It has a rich smokey flavor that gives your fries an extra little kick. I like that it is served in a Little Cup, just one of my personal quirks.   They don't have a full liquor license yet, so I enjoyed a Mexican Coke. Once they get their full license, an ice cold craft beer will be perfect.   The staff is welcoming and friendly. After ordering, they bring the food to your table and check on you frequently. Then once you are done eating, they'll bus your table.   As I dined, it was heart warming to see other employees from near by businesses coming in to welcome them on their first day and to enjoy some incredibly delicious sausages.   Will I return: I'll be back weekly.   When: November 17, 2017 Why: Opening Day and a favorite food truck

Frankly my dear, I do give a damn. I give a damn good shout out for Frankly Sausages. To be frankly honest, these are some of the best sausages I have had and they're from a food truck that is parked in the lot a craft brewery in the Heights.   I meet up with some friends (7) at Six Mile Bridge for Happy Hour and was totally blown away by this awesome food truck. They offer about six different sausages and two sizes of Hand Cut Fries with six different dipping sauces. I am a BIG fan of lamb, so when I saw one of their sandwiches was named; Mary's Little Lamb, I knew what I was ordering.   MLL was a lamb sausage served on a bakery fresh bun from La Bonne Bouche. How classy is that? An Artisan Sausage served on a bun from a French bakery. The sausage is topped with grilled red onion, feta cheese and fresh oregano. If I were judging a competition, Mary's Little Lamb would take home the blue ribbon.   I would have enjoyed a second MLL, as many of my friends did, but I wanted to experience more of their menu. My second sausage I went simple, I choose Bolyard's All Beef Frank. It was served in the same French bakery bun and topped with the classic toppings of catsup, mustard and relish. I made an excellent second choice, but Mary's Little Lamb will always have my vote.   The Hand Cut Fries are thick cut, skin on and only lightly salted. They were extremely flavorful, but for my personal taste they could of and should of been a little crisper. However, the variety of dipping sauces ranging from Pesto to Honey Mustard to Chipotle and three others made it hard to choose which one you wanted for your fries.   Even though the buns from La Bonne Bouche are freaking amazing, Frankly Sausage does take into consideration some of us do live a  low-carb lifestyle. So, if you want they will present your sausage on a bed of lettuce.  Frankly Sausages and Six Mile Bridge are only open Thursday-Saturday, so I highly recommend you go this weekend.   When: January 7, 2016 Why: Happy Hour

Sorry, Rooster you are still on my Terrible Two's List.   The food this morning was Denny's and IHOP quality. One item had to be sent back and one item  was so bad we totally had it removed from our bill and our total bill was $70 with tip for two people.   We arrived at the perfect time, approximately 8:30 AM, just ahead of all the Bears fans, so were seated immediately. When our server arrived, we quickly ordered a Bloody Boleyn, which is typical Bloody Mary with a champagne float on top and a MiMo which is a Mimosa layered with pomegranate juice. Both were majorly good.  The champagne float, gave the Bloody Mary a little extra kick and flavor.   The Biscuits and Gravy with Sausage was a vast improvement over our last visit. Enjoying today's biscuits, we realized the last time they must of made a mistake and served us the vegetarian version. This time, there was plenty of sausage floating in the thick creamy gravy. The biscuit was also an improvement, so they can go on my Biscuits and Gravy list.  Our main breakfast dishes were the Scramble with Goat Cheese, Spinach and Red Onion and the Savory Crepe, Sirloin #3. I had the Scramble. It was scrambled eggs served on top of breakfast potatoes with the before mentioned ingredients. Without the Tomato Jam that was served on the side, this dish would have been rather bland. It was the jam, that added the pizazz. The OD (other diner) had Savory Crepe - Smoked Sirloin #3. It was a crepe filled with mushrooms, caramelized onions, asiago and of course tender sirloin. I got a bite and the horseradish sauce I dipped it had a nice bite and I am not a fan of horseradish.   We also ordered three side dishes. The side of bacon was plentiful, done well and totally worth the $2. However, the other two sides were misses. A side of breakfast potatoes were so COLD, that we had to send them back to the kitchen. As out potatoes were going back to the kitchen, we noticed the side salad was sad and I mean real sad. The mixed greens were so wilted, that if they were at my house I would have thrown them out. Not here, they plate it and send it out to a customer.  When our server returned with our potatoes, we just had her take the salad back and remove it from our bill. Their breakfast potatoes were a little greasy and were heavily seasoned in chili powder giving them a red tint.   Our second round of drinks, OD stayed with the MiMo and I tried their regular House Bloody Mary. My second one was not as good as the first. Without the float of champagne, this drink seemed extremely weak. Their glasses for Bloody Mary's is large, so I think they need a little more vodka in MHO. So it is not worthy of my Bloody Mary list.   Gwendolyn our server needs to make a career change, she is not cut out to be a server in a high volume restaurant. She was not personable, nor attentive. Could it have been that I was wearing orange and it was the Sunday the Rams were playing the Bears. If so, you still need to provide superior service to tourist. The hostess and host seating guest were not much better.    I'm still not impressed. Rooster I think you are on my Terrible Two's list permanently.

I have never slept so well in my life. Ever since we had our Temp Pur Pedic - Cloud Select Queen size mattress delivered, I have experienced the most sound sleep. I think my dreams have even improved sleeping on this mattress.   Our last mattress was bought only 3 1/2 years ago from one of those stores that sells closeouts, "as is". We thought we were getting a good deal. When actually we were taken.  It did not take long before the mattress felt and looked like two Sumo Wrestlers had either slept or wrestled on it regularly. We suffered as long as we could. We had to break down and get a new mattress for the one that had broken down.   We did our research and knew we wanted to go Temp Pur Pedic. It was Columbus Day weekend and the majority of the mattress stores were having their annual sale. In the mail we received a sales brochure for Mattress Firm and looked at the addresses and headed out. Our salesperson Sean was great, he listened to our wants and needs and recommended a couple different mattresses. He was not high pressure and knew when to step away so we could talk about our decision.  When he stepped back into the conversation, he let us know which ones were in stock and those that we'd have to wait for. We selected our mattress, added the protective mattress cover and applied for the 24 month same as cash.   One week later our new mattress is delivered. When the young men making the delivery arrived I jokingly said, "Hey, you're not the guys on TV'. Without missing a beat, the spokesman replied, "No, we're better looking". He was right. The delivery guys were clean-cut, polite and professional. I was shocked how fast they brought the new one in, unwrapped it and had it positioned on our platform frame. We had them take our old mattress away to be recycled. They quickly wrapped the old one in the plastic wrapping from the new one with ease and went out the door. For those that are concerned, yes they put their little booties on at the door.   We spoke with the customer service department at Temp Pur Pedic before shopping to find our who they recommend as a retailer and were informed that Mattress Firm is one of their "Elite" retailers.  This Elite Yelper recommends this Elite Temp Pur Pedic retailer.

My most recent day off (May 4), I was out running errands and planned my route to pass through Webster Groves on my way back to the city. I was determined to have lunch here after reading multiple Yelp friends high praises. Once again, my fellow Yelpers were right.   I arrived about 2:15pm, thinking most of the lunch crowd would be done and gone. I was wrong, all but two tables were filled with happy diners and several waiting for take out orders.   The customer service here is amazing. I placed my order and was informed that if I ordered that, I 'd be spending more then if I ordered the lunch special. The lunch special offered me two extra pieces of chicken, so I had two pieces I could take home and share with the SO.   I asked if the two other pieces could both be thighs (Brad's fav) and I was assured that was totally doable. They even let me have my original two breast. I offered to change it to breast and wing and they wouldn't hear of it. My side was crinkle cut fries, no blah for me like Pat C.. I like crinkle, they hold ketchup and pepper much better then smooth fries.   As I stood waiting for my order, the young lady came around the counter carrying my order and a carryout box (eco-friendly). Be startled, I asked if that was mine and she asked where I was sitting. I pointed to a high top by the window and said, "I guess there". I told her, I didn't expect her to bring it out to me and she informed me that they do that for everyone.   What a personable touch. When I was in retail management, I always taught my cashiers when handing a customer their purchase to step out from behind the counter to do so. It takes that physical barrier out and makes a lasting impression. It even works at a fried chicken joint.   Now for the food - chicken is crunchy crunchy with moist juicy meat inside. Brad ate his hours later when he got off work and was sill impressed. I wish they were closer to home, but we'll make the trip again for this impressive chicken.   Carry-out containers are Eco-Friendly!  Got a giggle - they had a sign up advertising Craw-fish Tacos for Cinco de Mayo.

Great independent hardware store, with exceptional customer service. We're always greeted when we enter and when inquiring about a particular item, a sales associate always takes us directly to the item. On my last visit, I got distracted by a display (I'm fun to shop with)  and stopped following the associate.  He came back to  me with item in hand and closed the sale. The display also closed a sale, with the power of merchandising.   For a hardware store, they've got some great plants and accessories for the yard and garden.   I have stock in a big box hardware store and I shop here whenever I can.

It was Sunday Brunch with the favorite cousins for the holidays. There were 7 of us, snow and nasty weather did not scare us.  If you're having Sunday Brunch, you've got to have Bloody Mary's and Monk's Mimosa. Their house mix for the Bloody Mary is no doubt the best I've ever had. RL in Chicago use to be my favorite BM, not anymore. Sorry Ralph Brasserie just dethroned you.  I love the fact that they offer their mimosa's in a carafe, makes it easy for the refills.   We all started out with a grapefruit 'brulee' - who would have thought you could broil a grapefruit. The glaze on top made for a new experience. We all loved it.  Seven diners, six different entrees. Two of us ordered the steak & fries, and we were pleased with the tenderness, flavor and how they were cooked to perfection. The portion of fries that come with the steak is overwhelming. We could have shared one order.   Now I'm just going to list the other entrees and a comment made by the diner:  Hazelnut Waffle: I am on a sugar high,  Croque Madame: I love this, best ham and cheese sandwich ever. Brasserie Burger: Love Blue Cheese Eggs 'benedict': Oh, my gosh. Eggs'en Cocotte': Just perfect, love the fresh creamed spinach.  The brunch was perfect except for one mishap that was my fault. While we visited, my cousin showed us pictures on his Blackberry. As I was passing it across the table, I fumbled and The Blackberry fell into a "corpse reviver". Hopefully my cousin will not have to go tell his employer that his phone fell into a martini.   Great place for family and friends to celebrate the holidays.

Okay Rooster, I'm going to take you off my Terrible-Two's list, but it's a stretch.  I honestly cannot believe the difference between the downtown and South Grand locations. I love the South Grand location so much, I'm going to let you ride on the shirt-tales of them and bump you up to 3 Stars.   My favorite drink at Rooster is; The Honey Nut Old Fashioned. I suggest you send your downtown bartender to South Grand to learn how to make a good one. The one downtown was weak and watered down. However, your staff makes a decent Bloody Mary.   Having been raised on a farm, I have had my share of Biscuits and Gravy. Two things that I like about your B&G's is that your biscuit is square and that the gravy isn't overly salty. So many restaurants overly season the gravy with salt, but not you. Yours is seasoned almost perfectly, I only had to add pepper, but I love pepper.   My main breakfast entree was Scramble #2, but I substituted the ham with chicken. It was good, but I did not like the mushrooms, I ate around them. They tasted gritty and dirty. Next time, I'll go with #3 so I still get my onions and spinach in the scramble.   The service here at the downtown location is attentive, but not as warm and friendly as S. Grand. I also wish the downtown location opened earlier, the earlier opening on Grand is one of the things that attracts me to that location.   Will I return? Mostly likely not, I'll go to S. Grand.  When: January 18, 2017 Why: Remove from Terrible-Two's List

We all see things differently - I find the VG staff to be friendly & outgoing. They listen to your likes and dislikes in wine and guide you to new & exciting experiences. As for the class on Thursday night, I found it to be informative. I found the talking patron to be rude. There are no excuses for bad behavior.  The "you'll impress...." comment, I found it to be a humorous opening. If she lost you after that comment, perhaps you're ADD. I have shopped multiple wine shops in the St Louis area and find this staff to be the most friendly and knowledgeable.  *This was my first Yelp Review

The Chicago was so good the other night, that we went back for the St. Louis Original Deluxe. How can you go wrong when your pizza is topped with the following:  Sausage, pepperoni, hamburger, bacon, chicken, anchovies, onion, mushroom, green pepper, black olive, green olive, tomato, jalapeno, pineapple, spinach and minced garlic.  As we were chowing down,  literally we both looked at each other and said, "this is the best pizza ever".  Yes we were extremely hungry, but still for a delivery pizza it was one of the "best".   Again, we ordered the House Salad as a side making it a complete meal.   Louie's is now a 5 Star pizza in my tummy.

Okay, let's be honest. We may not want to admit it,  but we all eat at a fast food burger joint ever now and then. They're fast and provide a quick meal at a good price.   When this happens, I visit Hardees easily located at 44 & Hampton. This location is also a Red Burrito, so you can satisfy a burger or taco craving at the same time. Which comes in handy when a couple can't come to an agreement on whose craving is most important.   The customer service here is unbelievable for a fast food joint. The entire staff is friendly and personalize the classic line, "you want fries with that" with their own flair and style.   Here's my take on some of their menu items:  Breakfast:   Cinnamon Biscuits: just the right amount of sweet. Biscuits & Gravy: quick, easy and avoid the mess at home. Sausage Biscuit: Jimmy Dean would be proud.   Lunch/Dinner/Late Night:  Six Dollar Burger: Meaty with all the toppings Tacos: Better then Taco Bell or Jack-n-The Box French Fries: Cut from rosette potatoes  Their newest addition the "Turkey Burger"  is a great asset.  I actually was surprised at it's flavor. It let's you feel like you are eating healthier at a fast burger joint.   Need or Want fast food? Visit Hardees over McD's.

I'd been told by numerous friends that Carl's has the best pastrami in the STL area. I didn't believe them, so the other day I stopped in to see for myself. When I entered the delicatessen and saw the condition of the dining and kitchen areas, I knew there was no way the best pastrami could come from a place in such a disarray.   I was cheerfully greeted by a young man behind the counter, so I thought what the hell, I'm here I might as well give it a try. I told him I wanted a pastrami. He asked what kind of bread and I replied rye. For me, rye is the only kind of bread for a pastrami sandwich. As he made my sandwich, he asked more questions; cheese? No. Spicy or regular mustard? Spicy. Heated or Cold? Heated.   My sandwich was handed to me in a brown lunch bag and off I went to enjoy it at home. From the first bite, I knew I now would be one of those people telling others that the best pastrami is at Carl's. It was juicy, tender and just the right amount of fat. The bread was fresh and the spicy mustard gave it the extra kick. I shared half with the BF, who also said it was the best.  Next time, I'll add some Swiss cheese.   There is no ambiance here at Carl's it is still in the 1970's and appears to be very cluttered and disorganized. However, you will learn as I did, not to judge by appearance, because they'll serve you up one tasty pastrami sandwich.   A got a giggle from a Ziggy cartoon, posted near the register saying an ID was needed for spicy mustard.  They didn't require me to have one, but I gladly would have shown mine.

I need to start traveling more, because I found the best luggage store in St. Louis. They have it all; day packs, back packs, duffel's and traditional suitcases.  In addition to fantastic suitcases, they have messenger bags and top of the line briefcases.   The Tumi store at Plaza Frontenac is crisp, clean and merchandised well. There is no clutter, each style and type are grouped together in focal groups. Their sales professionals provide excellent service, they listen to your needs and wants then guide you to an appropriate item in the store.   I've got my eye one two bags, so I guess I better plan a trip too.

Will I ever be able to take the Pointersaurus challenge and devour a 28",  10 lb. pizza in one hour with a dining partner? Hell, NO! We had leftovers for the next days lunch from our 12" Deluxe pizza.  However, I have ordered the Pointersaurus for large groups and celebrations at work and it has always been well received. I would be a beached whale if I ate half or even a fourth of one of  those monsters.  It was Wednesday night and neither of us had the energy to cook.  I had an hair appointment at Mitchell James at 6 PM., so I came up with the brilliant idea to have Pointers Pizza as a treat. It had been awhile since I enjoyed one of their pies and the BF had never experienced one. When I was finished getting the hairs trimmed back to their appropriate length, I called Pointers for a pick-up order.   I ordered a 12 piece Hot Chicken Wings and a 12" Deluxe Pizza.  All of their crust is hand-tossed and your can choose; thin, regular or thick. We went with regular which is a happy place between thin and thick. It provides with just enough dough, so there is a balance between it and all your toppings.   Our Deluxe was topped with read sauce, which had a sweet taste to me. They then added; pepperoni, onion, green pepper, sausage, mushrooms and cheese that was not provel. The toppings were plentiful and were diced in large bite size pieces. It was a nice change from the delivery places near our home.   The HOT Chicken Wings, were not HOT, to be honest I think they gave us regular wings. They did offer us either Ranch or Blue Cheese for dipping sauce and I choose Blue Cheese. However, the wings were flavorful enough that neither of us dipped our wings, the flavor was strong enough to stand alone, it just did not have the "fire" you'd expect from a HOT wing.   The staff was friendly and personable on the phone and when I arrived to pick up our order. We miss being in their delivery area by a half a mile or so, but being close doesn't cut it in pizza delivery. No need to worry, I can always pick us up some Pointers after an amazing haircut.

It has been a year since my last review of Urban Chestnut. So, since it made Ian Froeb's 2016  - STL 100 List, I thought it was time to update mine. I'll start out by saying that Ian has nailed it when he says, the "must order" is the Pommes Frites. They are the perfect carb to munch while enjoying their many beers. They're served in a simple brown bag, along with a little cup of ketchup making it easy to dip your frites.   On my most recent visit, I hadn't eaten all day, so I needed something else to go along with my frites. I choose my favorite sandwich served at UCBC; the Strammer Max. It's an open faced sandwich, consisting of; ham, Gruyere Cheese, a fried egg and onion jam on rye toast. The two of them along with an ice cold craft beer, is a perfect lunch or dinner.   This is a great beerhall, where everyone is your friend. The service is always friendly & professional. If you're not familiar with their beers, they can guide to make the right selections.    I wish they could go back to letting dogs come and enjoy the fun times with their owners.   When: June 19, 2016 Why: I needed a beer.

It is what it is and what it is, is a small cafe inside a Holiday Inn.  I was attending a training class in their conference rooms for work and on our second day we  had a short lunch break, so the FPC was chosen for convenience. The service was friendly, but the food coming out of the kitchen was extremely slow. There was only one other table in the dining area and it was a single person having breakfast. Our party of three, continued to wait while he ate and our orders were taken back to back.   However, I will say once my burger and fries arrived it was well worth the wait. I enjoyed a Blue Burger which was topped with crumbled blu cheese and two crispy slices of bacon. I had no need to add any other condiments, the seasoning of the beef and the two toppings were enough flavor. The bun was fresh, soft and toasted just enough to give a thin crispness to the sides facing the burger. Then there were the fries - they were kick ass good. Seasoned with enough salt and black pepper that I did not even dip them in ketchup. When I have no reason to dip - that's a good french fry.   To make the lunch complete, for my ice tea had "yellow" artificial sweetener - they had the entire rainbow of sweetness making everyone happy. Then one detail that I really enjoy - they had linen napkins.  Will I personally go back? Probably not, but I do recommend it to anyone who is staying at the Holiday Inn. For what they are and do, they do it well.   When: January 22, 2016 Why: Lunch

I have begun a new love affair with Livingsocial. I never use to buy any of these Internet type coupons.  Now I watch them closely and purchase myself new experiences at local restaurants. That is how I discovered Arcelia's in Soulard.   We arrived for an early lunch and were cheerfully greeted by one of the young men serving lunch. As we were being escorted to our table, the other gentleman greeted us as well. What a great start to our experience, it was warm and hospitable.   I immediately ordered myself a regular Margarita with no salt on the rim. When experiencing a new Mexican restaurant, it is one of the unwritten rules that you have to have a Margarita. For a inexpensive restaurant, their regular Margarita was above average in flavor. It was not a boozy Mountain Dew like so many restaurants try to sell you.   We also enjoyed an order of Guacamole with our chips and salsa. The Guacamole was fresh, creamy and light on the salt which is a bonus for me. The creamy avocado, was accented by diced tomato and white onion. Their salsa had a nice bite to it, but was heavy on the garlic. Which made me a little self conscious of my breath while shopping after lunch. The fresh, warm and thick cut tortilla chips were a perfect accent to both the guacamole and salsa.   Our server asked if it was our first time and I confessed that I was a Arcelia's virgin.  He understood and showed me kindness as he guided me to the most popular entrees. He even ranked them in order of the top three. I went with Chile Verde, which he claimed was their most popular entree.
