I understood why as I broke out into a light sweat from the spicy green tomatillo sauce, that accented tender chunks of pork. It was served with Spanish rice, re-fried beans and two tortillas. The SO went with the servers  #2 recommendation Fish Tacos. Which got Big, I mean HUGE bonus points by being sautéed and not fried.  However, I think the little ole lady at the next table had the best lunch. It was the Super Burrito and it was gigantic. It was the size of a small baby. I swear I'm getting next time and sharing it with my lunch partner.   Thanks Livingsocial for introducing me to another great restaurant.

Let's start out with some positive points:  1. I liked the movie I saw. 2. Great old theater and the architecture is incredible.  3. Good location, close to the true city and in a neighborhood that is alive      with activity. Which makes for a fun-filled day or date night.  4. Well maintained and I love the fact that all the movie poster on display have a St. Louis connection.  Now for the negatives:  1. Stale old popcorn and we were attending the first matinee of the day.  2. Prices were very high for a matinee show. 3. Young man selling tickets and working concession stand was not friendly. He was also wearing aviator sunglasses inside, I hope it was for a medical reason. If not, it was not cool. I like to have eye contact with the person I am conducting business with.   I've been spoiled by other art houses for film, but the Tivoli Theatre is a St. Louis tradition. I remember it when it was a single screen, so I will be back to give them another opportunity. One bad experience is not going to keep me away from a St Louis Landmark.

Pretty, oh so pretty, but not worth the price tag.   We're getting ready to redecorate our main seating room and are shopping for three matching club type chairs. Before shopping at Whole Foods, we thought we'd pop into Arhaus and see what they had to offer. We did see a couple chairs that we liked, but once we examined them closer, we were shocked at the poor construction of these chairs. They were wanting $1,000+ and when you gripped the arm rest, you could feel the wood frame. If I am going to pay over a thousand $ for a chair, I want to feel the padding that is going to give me comfort while I relax in my new chair.   The sales staff was friendly and helpful, I just was not impressed with the quality of the merchandise for the price of  they were asking.

My first visit was only appetizers and cocktails at the bar and I am already impressed. I was shocked to see their cocktail menu featured some classic cocktails; Manhattan and Old Fashioned. To my surprise, they were masterfully made and refreshing accompaniments to my appetizers.   I started out with Salt Cod Rangoon. They were not folded like a typical rangoon. These were rolled more like a cigar or fat cigarette. The flavor was intense - I actually liked it better then crab. My second app was the, Shu Mai Dumplings. It was a serving of four dumplings, perfect for two to share and almost enough for one to eat as a entree. They were delicious.   The service was attentive and friendly. Other reviews have commented on serving size and price point, I thought they were spot on. Prices were reasonable and the serving size matched the price point for the quality of food.   I'll be back? - Yes, I'm a fan of scallops and I want to try theirs.   When: May 23, 2018 Why: Dinner

The other day as I was driving my boy dog to his veterinarian for a "cosmetic" procedure, (nothing to serious) I noticed Ray's Donuts in a small strip center. After getting Buddy checked in to the out-patient surgery, I looked Ray up on the handy dandy Yelp app on my iPhone. He had two 4 Star reviews from two of my friends, so I thought daddy needed a donut for the ride home.   As I entered the donut shop, I was cheerfully greeted by the busy worker behind the counter.  I thought to myself, Ray must serve up a good donut, because one of the two display cases was already empty. Lucky for me, they still had one of my classic favorites available. When it comes to donuts, my taste are simple. I like a Glazed Donut or a Chocolate Long John.  My other obsession with donuts is the donut hole, but I didn't see any here and forgot to ask if they are on their menu.   Ray must be from be from Texas, because some of his donuts were the biggest I've ever seen. My Chocolate Long John was a few extra inches longer then the typical Long John. Which gave me a few more bites of flavorful pleasure to enjoy during the drive back in to the city.   Now that I have discovered Ray, I'll be stopping by for a treat when my Fur-Babies have a vet appointment.

It's a Walgreens, just like all other Walgreens. The only thing that sets this one apart from all the other Walgreens is that there is no customer service. More then once, we've been given the, "talk to the hand" gesture. There's another Walgreens in the next block and that is where you'll see my $'s spent.

Decisions, Decisions. I use to think I had hard decisions to make when ordering my food at MTJ. Now with three locations to choose from, I have to make the decision of which MTJ I am going to, before I can even think of what to order. It is a pleasant dilemma that I am willing to live with.   My favorite place to sit is at Gringo's was the bar and I still feel the same way with MTJ moving into the same space. I like the outlets and charging stations under the bar and the hooks to hang various things out of the way. Plus, the main advantage of sitting at the bar, your Margaritas are re-filled much faster.   I've Tweeted about the chips and salsa at MTJ, so I'll say it here. "Don't be cheap - Pay the $3 for the Chips and Salsa" They are worth it, you get what you pay for. Those free chips and salsa you get at those other places, can not even begin to compare to the freshness and flavor of MTJ.   My favorite taco is the Baja Fish Taco & I prefer the fried over the fire grilled. It may not be the healthier choice, but for me it is the best. On my first visit to the new Euclid location, in addition to my fish taco, I went totally crazy and ordered Carne Asada Fries. I couldn't resist an order of chile crusted fries topped with wood fire grilled steak, chihuahua cheese and topped again with guacamole, crema and pico de gallo. It was delicious. I couldn't clean my plate, it definitely is an item meant to be shared by two or more.   I'm also a fan of the Margaritas at MTJ. They're made from scratch - no mix and you can taste the love they put in to it. My second favorite is the Mission Paloma. I find both of them to be refreshing.  Looking forward to my next Baja Fish Taco at MTJ in the CWE.   When: May 25, 2016 Why: Scoping out the new location

Brasserie by Niche is consistently a 5 Star restaurant for me. It is so deserving of its' #16 ranking on Ian Froeb's - 2016 - STL 100. They even take a simple burger and frites to a remarkable new level.   I stopped in for dinner on a Sunday night, and sat at the bar. When dining alone at the Brasserie, I have always gotten the same quality service I'd receive at a table. They spread the linens out and make you feel as if you're the main attraction. To my surprise, I was dining during the Happy Hour, so I got my burger and frites for $10. Having Happy Hour on a Sunday is a true winner.   I started out with a 2nd Shift draft. A cold beer is always a perfect choice for a double cheeseburger and frites. Two thin beef patties each topped with American Cheese, a smear of dijonnaise, some lightly grilled onions and dill pickles. Brasserie may be a French themed restaurant, but this burger is an All-American treat. The frites that accompany it are skinny fries, that are served hot and crispy. They are seasoned lightly with salt, and are so perfect, that I didn't need any ketchup.   As I waited for my burger, they brought out a house made roll with whipped butter. I left it alone, because I had a plan. When I had finished my beer, I moved on to a true classic cocktail, an Old Fashioned. Then when I finished my burger and frites, they went to remove my plate and the fresh roll as well. I stopped them.  As I sipped my Old Fashioned cocktail, I munched on the fresh roll, making it a delicious dessert.   Would I return? Absolutely. Brasserie is truly one of the best in STL.   When: July 3, 2016 Why: Ian Froeb's STL 100- Dinner

We all know Cracker Barrel is good for breakfast and good  southern comfort food, but do you know what else they are good for?  Christmas decorations. Most of my Christmas ornaments, garland, tree topper and other holiday decorations came from CB. When guest are visiting and ask where I got my festive and unique decorations, they are shocked and amazed that they came from Cracker Barrel. The prices are affordable and they look as if they came from a pricey boutique.  So next time you are feasting at CB, stop in the Country Store and shop.

An historical train station in the heart of Kirkwood.  This station is well kept and staffed by energetic volunteers who assist Amtrak passengers who leave and arrive on four trains that pass through. This station gives you the true feeling of days gone by, so I highly recommend you stop by for at least a quick visit next time your shopping or dinning on the main drag in Kirkwood. It will give you something to talk about the next time you visit grandpa or grandma.   Keith D. was looking for Bing Crosby and Danny Kaye to show up and sing White Christmas. I was watching out for the Andrew Sisters, to sing Bugle Bugle Boy from Company B.

I am so glad that Treats Unleashed has opened a location in Creve Coeur. My fur-babies vet is in Creve Coeur, so this will be a great place to stop and reward them for being good little doggies while visiting the vet. Also, so many times I'm out running errands and stop at other TU locations and they never get to be with me, now it will be all about them.   In addition to the made in house treats, they offer an excellent variety of premium dog foods. They also offer a very fashion forward selection of dog collar and leashes and a multitude of toys.   As with all Treats Unleashed locations, they are always dog friendly and the staff is knowledgeable and friendly. This location is offering grooming as well.   My fur-babies are now looking forward to their next vet appointment.   When: April 19, 2016 Why: Shelby went to the vet

I shopped on the 2nd of January, this store looked like it had been pilfered after a riot. However, the staff was still friendly, helpful and professional. I'm giving a 3 star rating to be fair, after all I'm shopping a toy store after the biggest toy holiday.   Earlier I had found the perfect gift for the little princess next door at another store and when I went back to purchase it, they were sold out. I was left scrambling for a replacement gift. Originally I had found a huge collection of Barbie clothes at Costco, so I hoped Toys R Us would have something similar - no such luck. They were totally sold out of clothes.  What I did find was a Poop-n-Scoop Barbie, that is the actual name. (Barbie come with a dog that eats treats, poops, and Barbie has a scooper) I laughed so hard, I had to buy it. The little princess loves our dogs so I thought this would be a good gift.   To our surprise, when she opened the Barbie, she screamed with glee it was the one she wanted and Santa did not bring. It's amazing how things turn out. I still found a perfect gift at a store that already was picked over.

Total disappointment - it was the most flavorless breakfast I have ever had. How they can mess up fried eggs & hash browns is beyond me. Over easy eggs were over cooked and the hash browns under cooked. The bacon & sausage were done well. Our side of biscuits and gravy had no flavor. Thank God, salt and pepper were on the table. Service was friendly, but minimal. The server took our order and delivered the food, period. Which was sad, considering there were only three tables being served.

A testimonial update from the holiday purchase:  The  Ghost Pepper Powder is fantastic. We have made chili, taco soup and a couple other dishes with this spicy addition and each had their recipe improved with the addition of the powder.    Nothing beats a fresh ghost pepper, but when you don't have one handy, this is a great substitution.  Thanks, OTSS for making it available.

In, Up, Fixed and Out. Those words may be an advertisement for a local tire and auto repair shop, but they work for Total Access Urgent Care as well. I had to make a visit on a Sunday due to a painful rash that was spreading rapidly. I went in around 1 PM and was done by 2 PM.  That truly is; "In, Up, Fixed and Out".  The entire staff was friendly and professional. Starting out with the receptionist who checked me in and out. To the nurse who did my pre-check of vitals and the doctor who did my diagnosis. Each one of them put at ease and had me feeling as if I were the only patient in TAUC (which I wasn't). My comfort and care was their top priority. They also spoke to me in layman terms and made sure that I understood my diagnosis and treatment plan. Nothing was rushed, it was all done at (pardon the pun) a healthy pace.   One of the medications I was prescribed they did not have, but the main one I was able to get filled in house at a very reasonable price. When I took the second prescription to my normal pharmacy, they didn't have it ether and it had to be ordered. So, do not judge them for not having one of the treatment drugs in house. My regular pharmacy had to order it as well.   As others have mentioned, they have small flat screen televisions in all the exam rooms. It made the wait time go by so much easier. The only bad thing is, that they are so well organized and efficient, that I was not able to see the end of Flip of Flop on HGTV. I also, was tempted to ask if I could stay till the end of the program to see how it ended.   I really didn't want to share with my fellow Yelper's how wonderful this place is. I wanted to be selfish and keep it to myself, but figured that I don't get sick enough to keep them busy. If you ever need a quick fix for an illness or have a non-life threatening accident. Don't go to an traditional ER, come here instead. You'll be treated with respect and you'll be in, up fixed and out, before your name is even called at the hospital ER.   When: September 18, 2016 Why: Skin Rash

Pappy's Smokehouse ranked #20 on Ian Froeb's 2016 STL 100 List. I wouldn't have put them in the top 25, but they have set the standard for many of the BBQ restaurants in the St. Louis area. So, perhaps that alone is reason enough to rank them towards the top.   My go to order that I usually pick up on my way home from work is a 1/2 slab of ribs. It comes with two sides for $16.50. As a bonus, you can order 1/4 pound of an additional meat for $4. I like this deal, because I can get two meals out of it. I enjoy the ribs and only half of each side and take the additional meat and the remaining sides to work the next day for lunch. For me, this is a winning combination.   I love the dry rub on the ribs, so for me there is no need for sauce. The only time I use sauce at Pappy's is for the brisket and pulled pork. My two favorite sauces are the original and Holly's Hot Sauce. I really like the extra kick that Holly gives. I enjoy it especially on the Burnt Ends when I can get them. So many times, by the time I get there after work they are sold out. That tells you just how good those damn burnt ends are.   I always order the same sides. When Pappy first opened, I wasn't a fan of his Baked Beans, but they have won me over and now I order them every time. No matter what meat I am enjoying, the beans are the perfect accompaniment. My second side, I mix it up between Fried Sweet Corn on the Cob and Green Beans. Both are made fresh and taste like they came out of a country kitchen.   Lines are long, service is friendly, polite and fast. You can not go wrong eating at Pappy's.   When: Multiple after work visits Why: Dinner & next days lunch.

Oh, Happy Day. Murphy, my Fur-Baby is so excited about this new Treats Unleashed location.  His pet stylist is just around the corner (Little House of Dogs). So now he can come here and shop for treats after being groomed. I like the convenience, too. Murphy gets car sick, so he doesn't get to go for that many car rides, so this allows him to two outings in one.   I love that all the treats are freshly made in house and they offer a great variety of quality dog foods. Their offerings of toys, collars & leashes and other pet accessories are top notch.   The staff is always friendly, knowledgeable and when your dog is with you, they make them feel as if they're the best doggie in the world.   For those who are DYI folks, this location has a bathing/grooming room. Appointed very nicely.   Will I return? Yes, Murphy and I will be stopping by every time he is groomed.   When: July 18, 2017 Why: Shopping with Murphy

It was Labor Day and we thought we should do a road trip. So we hopped into the car and left the city. It wasn't a long drive, we just drove out to West County to experience the new The Egg & I.  Sometimes you have to throw caution to the wind and go outside of your comfort zone. Venturing outside the city, was a good thing.   We arrived right around 8:30AM which was a perfect time. After we enjoyed our breakfast and were ready to leave, they had a wait list. I think the word is out that breakfast at The Egg & I is good and we are in agreement.   Having enjoyed a couple cups of coffee before leaving home, we opted for ice tea as our beverage. I liked how they bring you a craft to fill your own glass as needed. To sweeten your tea, they had every color in artificial sweeteners and they even had raw sugar for the serious sweet tea lovers.   Those that know me,  know the farm boy in me comes out every time I see Biscuits and Gravy on a menu. We shared a side order which was one split biscuit covered in a sausage gravy. The gravy was seasoned well, but a little runny for my taste. I would like a thicker and truer milk gravy for my biscuit. The biscuit itself was done well, flake and soft on the inside with a golden top.   Our main breakfast entrees were; Hiker's Benedict and Cambridge Skillet. Mine was the Hiker's Benedict and was the best of the two. The SO sampling mine, agreed I had the best dish. What attracted me to it was the asparagus and portabella mushrooms. In addition, it had diced ham, tomatoes and top poached eggs on top of a split English Muffin. The hollandaise sauce was impressive for chain restaurant.   By accident they brought the SO a Condon Bleu Skillet instead of the Cambridge. After a few bites and realizing chicken was an ingredient, we pointed the error out to Tammy our server who was attentive and fun. She apologized for the error and quickly got our order corrected.   The Cambridge Skillet was diced ham, bacon and hollandaise sauce on a bed of ranch potatoes with melted cheese and two eggs any style with an English Muffin.  We wanted to substitute a pancake instead of the English Muffin, but were told no substitutions allowed. Bummer, I really wanted to see one, Tammy said their pancakes were 10". That would have to be one big plateful.   Overall, you get a good breakfast at the Egg & I. For those of you who like First Watch, you'll love The Egg & I too. I'm looking forward to The Egg & I expanding their market in the Saint Louis area.

Momma, Mia. I mean Mama Gustos, you make a fine pizza pie. I was impressed with your sauce, crust and generous amount of toppings and cheese.   I had heard so many great things about Mama so when meeting friends at Melt and seeing her next door I knew I was going to get a carry out. When I popped in to order my take out, the staff was friendly as were those sitting at the bar. The chattiness gave it a real neighborhood feel. I felt assured when the men at the bar gave a thumbs up to my order, saying it was their favorite.   First thing that impressed me was the availability of four different styles of crust and not one of them is thin style. I ordered the traditional style which was a little thicker then hand tossed. As my topping I went simple, Italian Sausage and Pepperoni. The cheese was evenly melted over the entire pizza and it had plenty of both meats.  Best of all, the crust around the edge of the pizza was a light golden brown.  I don't need to worry about what I'll do with their crust, I'll eat it.   Mama, I'll be coming back. You are close enough to drop in for a quick dinner and close enough to do a quick pick-up of carry-out. If you did delivery, I am confident your business would soar.

It's been two years since I wrote my original review, so it is time for an update.   I am still a fan of shopping here on Wednesday to take advantage of the overlapping sales fliers. I particularly like the produce sales. However, I will say, you have to be selective on your choices. Don't just grab and go, take notice of the freshness before putting it in your shopping cart. Some of the sale prices here, beat Aldi's and we all know they have low prices.   As I said two years ago, the other department I like is the fresh meats.  I buy out of the butcher counter more then the packaged. I'm a big fan of the house peppered bacon. It makes a great bacon & cheddar omelet and totally delicious fried cabbage. Be alert and watch the seafood ads to treat yourself to your favorite when it goes on special. I watch for the Sea Scallops.   The staff at this store has gotten more friendly and now put them on the same level of customer service as a Trader Joe's.   Will I return? - Is it Wednesday? I'll be there.   When: December 27, 2017 It's a Wednesday Why: Filling the Pantry

Have you ever put something in your mouth and your taste buds instantly make your eyes pop out of your head? I am fairly certain that is what happened to me this morning, after taking my first bite of a glazed twist from WFD.  I hadn't even bitten down , to take a bite and the buds were already, singing praises.   I took my first bite at the stoplight, before entering on to 44 east and immediately tossed it back into the bag. This was not a donut to eat while driving, it was a donut to enjoy with a hot cup of coffee or a cold glass of milk once I arrived to work.  I kind of always thought a glazed donut was just a glazed donut, nothing special to write home about and now here I am writing about one on Yelp.  It was moist, had a unique sweetness to it and I scratch my head in wonderment if they use buttermilk.    In the Homer Simpson guide book to eating donuts, I think it is rule #4, you should never just order or eat just 1 donut. So not wanting to break one of Homer's rules, I also enjoyed a Chocolate Long John.  The John was good, but not as amazing as the glazed delight. It did have an ample spread of chocolate from end to end and side to side, giving it an edge over other donut shops within the city limits.   I was disappointed that they do not serve my favorite "donut holes", but with a glazed twist like the one I had this morning I can forgive them.  Plus, the couple who were working the early morning shift (5 AM) were picture book Grandma and Grandpa.   If you think there is no dough ($) to be made in donuts, take note of the Mercedes Benz in the parking lot with a personalized license plate - DONUTS.   WFD is now marked off my Yelp Bucket List and I recommend this STL jewel to everyone.

When: March 6 & 13 Why: Sunday Brunch  This is a great place to get a kick start to your Sunday. The service is always top notch. They have great Bloody Mary's, Mimosas and a specially created brunch drink by Chad the bar-master.   Then there is the food, the Eggs Benedict are by far the best in St. Louis. The hollandaise sauce, has an extra kick due to the whole grain mustard. You can make the Croque Madame a true breakfast delight by adding an egg to the top. Each Sunday they also have a special Quiche, I experienced; spinach, bacon, chicken and roasted potato. It was served with a side salad which made it a light fulfilling meal.   Let's talk potatoes, Brasserie does some great approaches; The Oven Roasted Red Potatoes are better then Hash Browns and I love me some Hash Browns. Then their fries/ frites, if a hamburger joint could only come close to matching the quality.

It was Good Friday, it was past lunchtime and I was hungry. As I cruised down Big Bend, I remembered this VFW Post got great raves in a talk thread about being good. As I drove by, I noticed they started at Noon, so I made a quick right turn into their lot.   As I entered their banquet hall I could see they were set up cafeteria style. A young lady greeted me and said she'd take my order over at the table she was standing at. They offered both, Cod and Catfish with the typical fish fry sides. When Catfish is available, that is my go to. I also cannot resist fries and Hush Puppies with my order of fried fish. If you're going "fried", you might as well go all the way.   My order was packaged to go, but I asked if I could go have a beer in the bar and eat my food. They assured me I could and informed me, that they were open to the public and I could come anytime I wanted. They were proud to say, they were like a dive bar with good cheap drinks.   When I went into the bar, I was impressed with the number of local craft beers they had on tap. I went with a 4 Hands - Single Speed and the bartender informed me since I was eating, I'd get it for only $4.   The ladies informed me to that they may be doing a fish fry once a month, so to keep alert for the announcement. I'm going to pay attention to any type of food event they have - I had a good time and experience.   I'll be back? - Yeah, my catfish was good and they were very welcoming.   When: April 19, 2019 Why: Good Friday Fish Fry

As their website says, "The White Rabbit - A Vintage Chic Boutique".    What a great boutique to find unique and original gifts. When you enter the store you know you have found a #shoplocal #shopsmall store that will help you finish your holiday shopping. I found so many amazing gifts for those hard to buy for cousins. There were vintage items, that took me back to our childhood memories and I cannot wait for them to open their gifts and have the same flashbacks as I did shopping.   I got a chuckle out of the candy jar for well behaved children. It's a shame they don't have one for well behaved adults as well.   Would I come back? Yes, when I need a unique gift that you can't find anywhere else.   When: December 11, 2016 Why: Gift Shopping #shoplocal

Absolute perfection. I am so happy to find a new 5 Star restaurant and even more excited that I discovered it in my hood. It is so close, I practically feel as if it is in my backyard. I only have a short couple of blocks walk and I can wine and dine in a very relaxed and casual atmosphere.   I meet up with the BFF for our annual Christmas dinner and gift exchange. Part of our tradition is to dine at a restaurant that neither of us has experienced. That in itself can be challenging, but we found J McArthur's and discovering it may have been the best gift of the night.   The BFF and I are both big fans of a Moscow Mule, however with it being a night of new experiences, we tried their Kentucky Mule. It was served in the classic Copper Mug, but made with whiskey instead of vodka. Next time I'm at the Kentucky Derby, I'll be drinking one of these instead of a Mint Julep. We enjoyed two rounds of cocktails, the BFF stayed with the KM, but I switched over to a Classic Manhattan. Like my martini's I like my Manhattan's up and J McArthur's did not disappoint me. It was chilled and served in a stemless glass. The only thing I would change, is I prefer a dark cherry over the traditional maraschino cherry.   Our appetizer was the appropriate size for two to share. We enjoyed their 16-Hour Braised Todd Geisert Farms Spare Ribs. The meat fell off the bone and melted in our mouths. They were basted in Charred onion top Korean BBQ sauce and served with a side of vegetable chow-chow and Alabama White Sauce for dipping the ribs. The ribs were so fantastic, that we only sampled the sauce and continued to eat our ribs without it. The vegetable chow-chow, if served in a larger portion, could be an excellent salad.   Being a fan of sea scallops, I knew instantly what I was going to have as an entree when I saw it on the menu. How could I pass up, Cast-Iron Skillet Seared Diver Scallops? I was in absolute heaven with my four large scallops. They rested in a smoked butternut squash bisque and served with brussel sprouts, bacon, confit buttermilk squash. The rich and creamy bisque, was a perfect accompaniment for the scallops and I also enjoyed the sage pesto that rested on top.  My BFF had a perfect meal for a low-carb eater. It was the special of the night, a Smoked Bone-In Pork Chop that was served on a bed of Brussel Sprouts. The pork was so tender, it could be cut with a fork and the Brussel Sprouts mixed with bacon had the right amount of crispness. We both were totally satisfied with our meals and look forward to another one very soon.  When: December 29, 2015 Why: Christmas Dinner with BFF

As stated in my previous review, I got to stop by Ray's for a treat today after my Shelby had her Senior Wellness appointment at the vet. Today the place was hustling and bustling with blue collar workers, west county ladies and medical office personnel and only one worker. However, everyone was patient and courteous, because the lady working was working as fast as she could and was charming everyone with bubbly personality.   Today I was thrilled to see a tray half full of my favorite, The Donut Hole.  No waste here, if Ray's holes taste this yummy and sweet I can only imagine how fantastic his glazed donuts are. Shelby enjoyed a couple of the holes, since she was a good girl at the vet.   The BF likes Apple Fritters and the ones on display were HUGE, so I had to get one to take home. When I got home, I tasted a small piece of the Apple Fritter and said the classic words out loud, "Oh, my God". I have tasted many a apple fritters in the city, but this county fritter was the best of the lot. It was filled with large pieces of diced apple, deep fried the glazed with sweetness. If I were judging at the state or county fair and it was an entry, it definitely would win the blue ribbon.   With three dogs, I am looking forward to the next vet appointment so I can stop by Ray's again.

Not in the food court. FG's has it's own outside entrance on the first level near the Chico's store. At first I found it weird that it wasn't in the food court, but realize it was a smart move. Diners can actually eat here without going into the mall itself.   In the food court, you have screaming unruly children running around while parents eat cheap sushi and talk on their smart phones. Yes there were children here at FG's, but they were better behaved. They knew they were about to have a good burger and awesome fries. While waiting for their treat, they worked on their dexterity skills cracking and opening peanuts.   The Little burgers at Five Guys are big enough for me. I can't imagine what the normal one would look like, it must be huge. A regular order of fries here is also way too big. Two normal eating folks can share a regular size. I've experienced their seasoned fries, and prefer the normal.  Give me little cups of ketchup, my fries and I'm in a happy place.   For the $, FG's gives you a good burger experience. The boys/men working the grill and fryer, had better customer service skills then the young lady working the counter. Take a lesson girl.   FG's I know it is part of your image, but put those big sacks of potatoes in your stockroom not out in the dinning area. We all know they're cut fresh and don't need them as a reminder. They gave me flash backs to when I worked at a vegetable farm during high school and college.

Charming (sorry for the pun) little candy shop. Is it off the beaten path? Yes, but it's perfectly located. It is just down Macklind from Copper Pig, The Mack, Russel's and Clementine's. I was in the area for lunch and experienced two of them before ending my Macklind experience in this candy store.   Once I entered it was a flash back to my childhood. I saw so many of my favorite candies from being a kid that I don't see in the candy aisle at Walgreens. They had Bonomo's Taffy! I loved that when I was a wee lad. I wanted it so bad, but with crowns in this aged mouth I couldn't risk it.   However, I did find and buy some of the "new" Tootsie Roll Pops. I treated me to three of them. They're fruit flavored with a contrasting fruit center. My sweet tooth is happy.   The young lady working was charming. I'm assuming she's the owner because she talked of her recent visit to the candy trade show. She also, was able to continue three different conversations with the different customers in the store.   I'll be back? - Yes, I wanted more, but held back since I had just eaten a double scoop of ice cream.   When: July 26, 2019  Why: Zac M. had the ROTD July 21, 2019

Attention Pie Lovers: If you walk into Pie Oh, My and they have Apple Crumb Pie with Green Chilies available, buy it - You'll LOVE it. I have had this pie several times and it is amazing. I stopped in yesterday for a pie fix and was excited to see they had my new favorite pie available. I was cooking a Mexican theme meal and a apple pie with green chilies made for the perfect dessert.   I also bought their new Cranberry Meringue, which is going to be a great hit for the upcoming Thanksgiving holiday. A flaky crust, tangy cranberry filling, a picture and flavor perfect meringue has me knowing what I will be taking to work with me on Thanksgiving day. Yes, I am one of those unfortunate folks who will be working on that day, but with pie in tow I'll manage to make it through.   When I stop by POM, I can never just get one. I also grabbed a couple of their bite size pies for work lunches. I got a Maple Walnut with Schlafly's Pumpkin Ale and a Pumpkin Toffee. The Maple Walnut did not make it to the lunch box. I'm not a fan of walnuts, but mixing them with maple and my favorite autumn beer had me wanting more. The Pumpkin Toffee is in the lunch box for today,   I was thrilled to see them offering quiche and since I hadn't had breakfast yet, I bought one. The combination of sausage, onion and sun dried tomatoes made for a perfect morning treat. I'll take it over a Egg White McMuffin any day.   They are offering candles made by Maven that smell like a pie is baking in your oven. It is so good to see all the Maplewood businesses work and support each other. As always, talking to Jane is a delight. Can't wait for my next slice of pie.

Ross is a weird version of TJ Max, Marshall's and Stein Mart. It actually reminded me of Marshall's in the old days. Their racks of clothes really had no organization, except for the fact that they were separated by size. The sales associate who assisted us informed us they get trucks daily, so since they didn't have what we wanted today to check back because the inventory and offering change daily. Wow, rocket science in the world of retail.   I didn't find anything to add to my closet, but they had some great offering on gadgets and gizmo's for my tool box. The housewares department was rather small, but offered some good bargains. They also had some great gift baskets with sweet and salty treats for the holiday gift exchange. Some of them were even labeled gluten free.  The employees were friendly, but the check out system moved rather slow.  Even though I found the store to be disorganized, I think I'll return. After all, they get trucks everyday which means it will be a new shopping experience.

Meet my first Yelp friend Norma here for Happy Hour. Having my first golf lesson later tonight (6Jun), I couldn't stay long, but I did make time for a Bubble Bath (Erin G. recommendation). A Bubble Bath is three glasses with 3oz pours of champagne. I love the place-mats that the pours are presented on, it makes for easy notes and knowing what to buy by the bottle when you fall in love with one as I did.   All three were incredibly good, but the NV "J" Brut Rose, took my breath away. If I didn't have a golf lesson, I could have stayed and nursed a bottle till it was gone.   The bartender Frank and the wait staff all dressed up in fun t-shirts were top notch. I will make sure my next visit does not need to be cut short due to a golf lesson, I want  to experience the true Robust.

The other day when I was driving to work, I noticed Hardee's had changed their marque. When I read "Fried Bologna Velvetta Biscuit," I threw my hands in the air and said, "Jesus take the wheel". He immediately took the wheel and guided thru the drive-thru to a magical box that asked me, "Do you want to try out new Fried Bologna and Velvetta Cheese Biscuit?" Instantly I said, "YES!"  This biscuit was a throw back to my childhood, when I use to enjoy a fried bologna with a Kraft American Cheese slice on Wonder bread sandwich. However, this version kicked it up a notch being on a Hardee's freshly made biscuit. As most of Hardee's featured items, this is not a healthy entree. It may not be healthy, but it will have you singing the Oscar Mayer song about your bologna.   If you are a fan of bologna, you've got to give this biscuit a try, at least once.

I can see clearly now, my eyes have been examined by Dr. Michael Antoine.   Sometimes the convenience of having a doctor of Optometry office attached to eye glasses boutique is to your advantage. Okay, calling Lenscrafter a eye glass boutique is a stretch, but still having the two next to each other is a big plus.   I finally found a pair of frames I liked at Lenscrafter and Nerea my sales associate was able to get me a walk in appointment with Antoine Eye Care. Extra bonus points, they took my vision insurance so it was no money out of pocket for me.   Dr. Antoine was friendly, explained each test and questioned my computer use to make sure he put me in the right lens. When it is time for the next eye exam, I will not procrastinate like I did this time. I will call Antoine Eye Care and get it done.

I came here Wednesday night with a group of 9 for Clayton Restaurant Week. Bocci was kind enough to put our group of Yelpers in a little private dining room.  The ambiance of the entire place is nice and relaxing, but having our own private room was a nice touch.   Overall I have to only give Bocci 3 Stars for this visit. With it being Clayton Restaurant Week I would have thought they'd have their A-Game on. Instead, they were at best a B- or C+. I have friends who enjoy Bocci immensely so I will give them another try.   I will break down my first impression in to Pros and Cons.   PROS:  Private Dining Room for large group Waiter with foreign accent Bocci Salad is made with Bibb lettuce and the Avocado was super fresh Vanilla Gelato with Caramel Sauce and Biscotti made my knees go weak Fantastic Bread and Olive Oil for dipping No trouble splitting checks  CONS:  Discombobulated bartender, she seemed very disorganized  Draft beer not served in chilled glass Grouper Milanese was sub par - I've had better prepared for me at a grocer Portion sizes of Grouper varied greatly from each serving. I understand it most likely was done by ounces, but the size varied so much in appearance that we were giggling like kids saying mine is bigger then yours  Risotto was too mushy for my personal taste and had minimal zucchini  Chocolate Mousse Cannoli was a total miss - Cannoli over baked and coco in the chocolate was to heavy handed and I am a chocoholic.   I will revisit soon, to see if I can fall in love with Bocci like my friends have.

Damn you, Target. Why can't you sell The Dr. Scholl's Custom Fit Orthotic Inserts? It's your fault that I had to commit a big shopping sin and go to a Walmart to fulfill my needs. When I confessed my sin the priest was so shocked he said, "You did what?". Even he was shocked that I would stoop so low. You don't even want to know what I had to do to be forgiven for such a dastardly sin.   I'm on my feet constantly at work at my feet were starting to feel the discomfort. By the end of the day, my feet were hurting and I knew I needed help. I'd seen the commercials for Dr. Scholl's and The Good Feet Store and knew Dr. Scholl's was more within my current  budget. I not only researched, but I heard testimonials from friends who sang the praises of the affordable ($50) inserts.   So I came here early to do my shopping, 8:30 AM. Store employees were busy stocking the shelves and paid no attention to me hidden behind my Ray Bans.  I'm assuming they stock shelves first then the cleaning crew comes in later, because it was in need of some TLC.   I found the machine in the pharmacy department and followed the instructions.  You stand, lift one foot then the other. It was kind of like doing the Hokey Pokey with a doctor. It evaluated my feet and told me I was CF 430.  I now have a stabilized arch and my feet don't hurt at the end of the day.   This early in the morning there was only one cashier open so I had to wait in line. As I waited, I browsed their $1 bins near the check out. Those cheap impulse items will get you every time. I always say, "If it is orange, I'll buy it". I added orange mixing spoons, spatulas and paring knife to my purchase.   As I was being rung out, the cashier asked me about my inserts. I told her what I knew and Brad shared his experience with her as well. I'm not positive, but I think she'll be getting her own inserts next payday.   To be forgiven for such a dastardly sin, I had to promise not to do it ever again and not to shop at the outlet mall for two weeks. It's a hard cross to bear,  but at least my feet don't hurt anymore.

I'm bad, I just realized after all my visits to Pappy's that I haven't written a review on Yelp. Perhaps it is because of the saying, "nothing to write home about". I know Pappy's gets a lot of positive press and awards, but for me they are not consistent in producing their product. My visits have ranged from a stellar 5 star experience to a you should be ashamed of yourselves for even giving this food to a customer 2 star rating.  When Pappy's is good, he is damn good and that is what keeps me coming back hoping that they are on their A-Game the day I am visiting.  I was thrilled when Pappy's opened and was serving their Ribs as a Dry Rub with the sauce on the side. Many visits they have been done so well I haven't even needed to add any sauce, the dry seasoning was flavorful enough.   My favorite things from Pappy's are the Beef Brisket and the Pulled Turkey. I have not experienced any other place that can beat the brisket here at Pappy's. When Smokin' Al's was open on Hampton many moons ago, I only enjoyed his pulled turkey. So I'm kinda glad Al is closed, because my loyalty would have flipped to Pappy.   Now let's chew the fat about their sides:  Fried Corn on Cob - order it - eat it - it will wake up your Southern taste-buds.   Potato Salad - As good as a New York Jewish Deli  Cole Slaw - Oil & Vinegar -  A healthy choice  Sweet Potato Fries - They still haven't mastered this side.  Baked Beans - Canned Bush's are better. Open a can and order one of the other sides.   Green Beans - Good  & gets one of your daily green vegetables in for the day.   Apple Sauce - Grandma smiles.   When having a busy day at home or work our favorite E-Z Carry-Out is the #2. When doing a carry-out, there is no need to worry about the sauce, they give you plenty of all three. My personal favorite is the Sweet Baby Jane. I just hope she doesn't grow up to be like Betty Davis in, "Whatever Happened to Baby Jane". The Holly Hot Sauce, which is suppose to be Texas style would make any true Texan laugh. It is very mild.   Patience is a virtue and it is one you need to have when visiting Pappy's. No matter what time of day I have visited, I have stood in a very long line. If a genie granted me an extra wish, I'd wish that Pappy's would expand so they could handle their large crowd of adoring fans more quickly.

We both were craving Eggs Benedict and The Egg & I, offers 7 different versions so it was easy to find one that satisfied our tastebuds. Being a beautiful day, we enjoyed our breakfast on the patio. I admit the view is a parking lot, but at least we were outside in the fresh air.   My Dining Partner ordered the, New Orleans Benedict which was a Home-style biscuit topped with Andouille sausage and tomato gravy, diced ham, green onions, two poached eggs and hollandaise sauce. The biscuit was flakey and the mix of tomato gravy and the hollandaise sauce was interesting. It made for an enticing mix of flavors.  I choose a healthier one, the Veggie Benedict. Two English muffin halves layered with mushrooms, spinach, artichoke hearts, asparagus and tomatoes. Topped with two poached eggs, hollandaise sauce and fresh green onions. I was sold on this one when I saw, spinach and asparagus in the same dish. Adding artichoke hearts and mushrooms was a bonus.   For those of you not familiar with The Egg and I, it is very similar to First Watch. It is only open for breakfast and lunch. It closes at 2 PM and on Saturday and Sunday, stays open and extra half hour. It focuses on the first two meals of the day and does them well.   Worth the drive from the city? Probably not, but when in the area it's a good choice.

Gian-Tony's is one of those hidden treasures  on The Hill. It is kind of off the beaten path on the corner of Daggett & Macklind.  However, once you have dined here I can guarantee you will be back for more and will be telling your friends and family about your find.   My first experience here was with our International Supper Club and I was so glad that we choose it as our monthly meeting. The staff was extremely friendly and did their best to accommodate 10 foodies who were enjoying Tony's Southern Italian Cuisine.   I got lucky the night we dined, because one of my favorite appetizers was an off the menu special. I love Mussels and they presented theirs in a extremely flavorful butter and garlic sauce. The sauce was so yummy, that everyone was dipping their bread into my bowl. In fact, we had to ask for our bread basket to be replenished.   My entree this evening was Pasta with Scallops. A hearty portion of angel hair pasta with scallops & mushrooms in a combination of marinara and cream sauce. The serving was so large, that I had enough for lunch the next day and it was just as tasty.   The man who came out in the chefs coat that Allison mentioned was indeed the executive chef, Tony. It is a true sign of professionalism when the chef takes time out of the kitchen to touch base with diners.   After mussels and a scallop pasta dish, I was to stuffed to try dessert, but I really really wanted to experience their Terra Missu. I understand it is  a family recipe that followed Tony from Sicily. Next visit, I will be sure to leave room for a sweet treat.

Hello Hardee's,    I am not sure if you have noticed the construction next to you where the old car wash use to be, but it's that little red headed girl named Wendy. If I were you, I'd be scared.  With another fast food burger joint right next door you need to improve your customer service.   I'm a fan of your Turkey Burgers, Tacos and Chicken Tenders, but your customer service is on the down slide.  My last couple of visits, the cashier and other front counter staff have been just down right rude. Then on my last visit,  I understood why. A Manager was assisting with the front counter passing out orders and he was equally as rude as his employees. I guess his staff was just following his lead.   I think your TV commercials are sexist, but you do put out a good "heart stopping" burger. Improve your customer service or I'll be getting baked potatoes, chili, frosty and a square burger from Wedny when she opens.

Great nonsmoking soccer bar. They offer a good beer selection which goes well with the food you can order next door at The Dam. If you're not a beer drinker, they're a  sports bar and will mix you up a simple bar drink too.   The ambiance is definitely soccer. This is the place to be seen watching a World Cup or any soccer game for that matter. Our bartender Matt, was friendly and attentive. He told us about the patio expansion which is going to be great for this coming spring and summer.   The Amsterdam has always been a great little bar and now with The Dam next door, it just got better.   When: 30 Jan 2014 Why: Enjoying a burger from The Dam

My bosses 14 year old son knows that I Yelp and the last time he was visiting the office, he informed me I had to try Bonefish Grill. This young foodie told me, Bonefish Grill is his favorite restaurant. With a recommendation from my bosses son, I had to give it a try.  I arrived at peak lunch time and the dining room was full. The hostess informed me I could sit at one of the communal tables in the bar and order from the same menu. I selected one that was empty, so I didn't have to share my space. My server arrived quickly and cheerfully welcomed me. I already had skimmed the drink menu and knew I wanted a Fat Tire. Their selection of beers is small, but they had an impressive martini menu. I'm going to have to return for Happy Hour to enjoy a martini.   Wanting a quick lunch, I opted for the Fish-n-Chips and they did not disappoint. The fish was done Tempura style and the fries were crispy. I am not a fan of tartar sauce and I surprised myself by trying and actually liking theirs. I also liked that they serve ketchup in little cups, its' one of my little quirks.   I never got to  snap a photo of their offerings of sweetness, but they have them all and deserve a spot on my Rainbow of Sweetness list. I thought it would be awkward to ask the people next to me enjoying ice tea to snap a photo of the sugar.   With us in the peak of Lent season, Bonefish Grill is going to be a great place to grab your fish on Friday.

Every time my dogs go to the doggie spa up the street we have to stop here. Honest to God, the last time I was pressed for time and passed TU. My boy dog started to bark and he never barks when traveling. He was telling me, I missed the turn off for TU. I circled the block and we went to TU, so I could have peace at home. Murphy was a happy K-9.   My dogs are big fans of the soft bites. Their favorites are peanut butter or blueberry. They are so healthy and all the treats are baked in house. It cannot get any fresher then that.   For special occasions like birthdays or gotcha days, they can personalize a cake or cookie with your dogs name. At my house, we're happy with the ones that say, Princess or Prince. After all, my fur-babies are royalty, at least in my eyes.   The staff is always friendly and as I stated in my previous review, they always make your dog(s) feel welcomed and special.   Chances of returning: It's a guarantee when the dogs get groomed.  When: Every six weeks at least if not sooner.  Why: Treats of course.

Reddddd Rob-in! Did you sing, it?   I am so glad that I now have a Red Robin closer to home. There are times, that I just want a big juicy burger from RRGB. Not to mention their thick steak fries that are served bottomless. I never seem to get beyond my first serving, but they are one of my favorite fries at a restaurant.  Jalapeños are one of my favorite toppings on a burger and Pepper Jack  is my cheese of choice for a burger. With that being said, Burnin' Love is my go-to burger here at RRGB.   Another of my addictions at RR is their onion rings. They are huge, crisp and comes with two sauces for dipping. I'm so glad that they now offer, The O-Ring Shorty. The Tower was always way too many "rings" and filled me before my burger arrived. Now with "shorty" I can enjoy "rings" and my burger.   This visit, I discovered that RR has their own draft beer. It's made by New Belgium Brewing Company. The bartender gave me a sample and made a good sales pitch for me to try it. To my surprise, I liked it.   The service at this new location is good. I actually like it better then the staff at the Des Peres location. They're friendly, professional and attentive.   I really wish Yelp had half stars, because this is one review that I'd use it for. It was more then a 3, but just shy of a 4.   I'll be back? - When I get the craving for a RR burger.   When: - August 20, 2018 Why: - Steak Fries and Burger

Got a birthday dog in your family? If so, you need to come to TU and get them a special cookie. You can buy one of the generic Happy Birthdays or they'll personalize one for you. Today, I just went with a generic one, but I added some extra smaller cookies to make it extra special.   I also grabbed a couple of cookies for the Cardinals opening day.  Love the staff here, it is becoming my go to of all the TU's in the area.  Shop local!   I'll be back? - My dogs insist on it.   When: March 30, 2019 Why: Murphy's 7th birthday

We were at Deer Creek shopping at GFS and thought we should walk around to check out the other stores as well. We are so glad that we did, because we found some good bargains. Here at Ross Dress For Less, we found a pair of Nautica khaki shorts for $4.99. That is an insanely low price! That is yard sale or Goodwill pricing. You have to be patient and flip throughout the racks, but you can dress for less at Ross.

Let me start out by saying, my experience here started out as a solid 4 Star review. It nose dived in the last 60-90 seconds. I'll explain that in the closing, let me hit the highlights that had them at a solid 4 Stars.    The hostess asked if I was dining alone, when I responded yes, she escorted me to a booth for two. When we arrived at the small booth, she asked me if it was okay. (Nice touch for customer service) I told her it was perfect.   Shortly thereafter, my server arrived and asked me if I needed a drink and if I was ready to order. I ordered an ice tea and told her it was my first time. I shared with her how every morning on my work days I would see their billboard as I took 55 on the IL side to go meet up with 255. After a month of viewing the billboard I thought it was time to give them a try.   I knew I wanted the fried chicken (they're known for it), but asked for sometime to read the menu and see what else they had to offer. As I read, I could see why so many senior couples and families were filling up the other tables. It was a menu full of "comfort food".   When Jessica returned with my ice tea, I ordered a small order ofToasted Ravioli as an appetizer. I stuck with my original plan and had a half fried chicken dinner. It came with; soup, salad and one side. I told her, I'd skip the soup, but she quickly offered me an additional side in it's place. I opted for green beans to accompany my baked potato.   My side salad came out first, I would have liked the toasted ravioli first.  However, after enjoying the salad with house dressing first, the flow of the food made sense. The salad was large for a dinner salad. The croutons were also huge and I always enjoy a pepperoncini on my Italian salad. Not sure if the dressing is made in house, but the creamy Italian was delicious.   When the Toasted Rav's arrived, they were round, not your typical squares that are served on The Hill in STL. They were crisp, puffy and filled with meat. They had a buttery taste, that made my taste buds do a happy dance. I actually liked these more then some spots on The Hill. They were served with a HUGE cup of marinara sauce. It was too much sauce for me. I actually only dipped a couple of time, because the rav's tasted that good on their own.   Now, for the main course. I can see why they are so popular on the Eastside. The chicken was served hot, crispy and juicy to the bite.  However, I can tell you my pieces did not come from the same bird. The wing was a small size and the breast was extremely large. The leg and thigh were an average size. I was able to overlook the variety of sizes, because the flavor was so good. I'm betting they cut the chicken in house, because the thigh was an old fashioned cut that I don't see that often when eating out.   My sides made it a complete comfort food meal. The baked potato was large and cooked to the center. I smothered it in butter and seasoned it heavily with pepper. Loved it. The green beans were made from fresh green beans and prepared with onions and bacon - down home cooking.  At the end, I was asked about dessert. I had to decline. My server told me about their amazing pies. I shared with her that I had experienced one at our recent Christmas Dinner. One of the other guest had brought one.    I had so much food, I needed a to-go vessel. The next day at work, I had the perfect lunch. The chicken breast cold was as good as the other pieces I ate hot and the green beans heated up well in the micro.   I'll give a shout out to my server, Jessica who was very personable and attentive to me and her other tables. Also, to management who was walking around the dining room, making sure everyone is content.   When you are done eating, you pay your bill at a front counter. This is where they lost their additional star. The counter was staffed by, for a lack of better words, three snot-nosed high school girls who were more interested in gossiping then providing customer service.   The blonde grabbed my ticket, said nothing to me, but kept talking to her two co-workers. She walked over to the register, came back to me and laid down the tickets and said, "top one is ours the bottom is yours". Turned, walked away and was still talking to the other girls. When I asked for my original itemized receipt back, she sighed loudly, went to retrieve it and tossed it in front of me and said, "there". Again, she never missed a beat in her conversation with her friends. I don't use the word co-workers, because they weren't doing a damn thing.   These counter girls are the last impression of the dining experience. They should have been thanking me for coming in, suggesting I take a whole pie home with me, asking me if I enjoyed everything and most importantly to return. She also should have handed me my ticket, instead of just tossing it on the counter. Customer Service is important.   Chances of returning: Yes  When: February 23, 2019 Why: Dinner

How lucky can you get when you shop Lucky's on Wednesday? You can get double lucky, because on Wednesday you get to shop the sale prices of last weeks sales flier and the new one that is starting. It's a double sale! Wednesday may be hump day to some, but to me it is double savings day.   I absolutely love the produce department. The prices of the vegetables and fruits are so affordable and when they are on sale, they are insanely low. The produce here also, makes me want to go vegetarian, they are so fresh.   My second favorite department is the fresh meats. Watch their sales and stock up on your favorite cuts of meat. I love the pork loin chops. I buy the thin cut for breakfast and the thicker cut for dinner. Also, check out their made in - house chicken sausage. It comes in Hot Italian or Sweet Italian. Whichever one I take to work for lunch, I always hear the words, "That smells good. Where'd you get it?"  The prepared foods counter is pretty amazing. If you had a hard day at work, you can totally get an entire meal here. If you want a dessert to go with that prepared meal, check out the bakery goods on various tables towards the front of the store. Many of these sweet treats are from various local bakers.   Another area that is worth checking out is the bulk area. Being a single man, I like the fact that I can buy in the amount I need as an individual. I always hate buying a pre-packaged item and having some of it go to waste. Be able to buy these items from the bulk area, is a savings for me and there's no waste.   Lucky's is a great addition to the grocery market here in Saint Louis. I live in the city, but the drive out to Lucky's is well worth the selection and savings. If it's Wednesday, you'll see me checking in on Yelp at Lucky's.

Oh my, Oh my, Pie Oh My. A specialty pie shop in Saint Louis has been long overdue.  Jane the owner is charming, friendly and eager to please her new customers. As pointed out by Stephanie S., Jane is open to request of specific pies and will do what she can to fulfill those request.   Having grown up in a "pie" family, I was anxious to experience these delightful treats.  The photos on their website almost jump through your monitor with flavor. However, when we arrived at the shop which is cute as a pie shop should be, the items on display were not as photogenic.   We needed dessert for that nights dinner, so we purchased four small tarts. It was mid-afternoon and Jane was apologetic for the small variety left. She is very chatty and does provide good customer service.   That night when dessert was served, disappointment set in. When it comes to pies, I think I may have been spoiled when I was growing up. My mom came from a family of 14 and 8 of them were sisters and they all could bake pies. I think at family reunions, they secretly watched to see who's got devoured first.   Now that I have given you background on me and my love for pies. I can honestly say, I was not impressed with the crust on our tarts and thought the amount of filling to be on the stingy side. For the price we paid per tart, I would have wanted more bang for my buck.   For those not raised in a pie family, these may be the bomb.   I am hoping these may be attributed to jitters in opening a retail space, instead of just being a supplier to other venues.  Not only does STL need a pie shop, to  be an alternative to the endless cupcakes. but I need a new supplier as well.    We all deserve a second chance and I'll be giving one to Oh my Pie.

When I checked in my Yelp App today at the City of St. Louis Collector of Revenue office, it told me I had 4 check-ins and if I kept it up I could be a regular. Seriously? Who wants to be a regular or the Duke of an office that collects taxes? Visiting once a year is enough for me. I don't need to be a regular.   However, I will say this office is no way similar to the local DVM. The ladies that work here are polite, professional, friendly and fast. I was in out, in a flash. With the great service I'd be tempted to come back more often, but paying personal property tax and real estate tax once a year is enough for me.

Uncle Linny's is the last one on my list of the restaurants who made the top 10 best breakfast places in the River Bend area. Is it worthy of its placement? Yes, they provided a very good breakfast. However, the service was slow and my coffee cup went bone dry on two occasions, so that is why they get only 3 Stars.   What surprised me most about the menu, is that a majority of the egg entrees had three eggs instead of the typical two. Which means they serve up some hearty plates here. I wonder if it's because it is located primarily in a blue collar neighborhood. Whatever the reason, I did not go away hungry.   I was torn between so many choices, that when my waitress came and asked for my order, to my surprise, I ordered, the Chicken Fried Steak Platter. I had my eggs scrambled and enjoyed a side of Hash Browns instead of American Fries. When My food came, I got a giggle that they brought it on two different plates. Eggs with the potatoes on one and the Chicken Fried Steak on another.   My eggs were extra fluffy and a beautiful light yellow. There were no darker brown markings from the grill. They were picture perfect. The Hash Browns were crisp, the way I like them and I think they were made fresh in the restaurant. If they weren't, it was a very good brand of frozen. The coating on the chicken fried steak, was a thin crisp layer and the milk gravy, was seasoned well. By seasoned well, I mean it was not overly salty. I had to add a few shakes of pepper, but I'm a pepper junkie.   My coffee was good and strong, like it should be at a diner. I just wish they kept it filled more. The staff was friendly, but with the place being super busy, they just couldn't be super attentive.   Uncle Linny's is a great place if you live close by. For me it's a half hour drive and I have places much closer to my home.  When: September 3, 2021 Why: Breakfast

Alton Restaurant Week - January 2021  I enjoy a good Bison burger and when I saw that BCG was offering one as their lunch special for $12  during Alton Restaurant Week, it was a no brainer to come here for lunch. One of my favorite cousins, is also a fan of Bison, so she joined me for a delicious lunch.   Their lunch special for ARW was a, Whiskey Bison Burger, that was ooey, gooey good. It was a third pound of chargrilled bison topped with a house made whiskey sauce. In addition to the sauce, it was topped with; provolone cheese, sautéed onions and mushrooms. Plus, they add traditional toppings; tomato and lettuce. The toppings were plentiful and placed between a gourmet bun. There were so many toppings, it made for messy eating. All the ingredients would slip and slide between the bun as I took each and every bite. However, that is why it is good to have linen napkins to wipe your fingers and mouth. Because every bite was worth it. To accompany the burger was fresh cut fries and a little cup of ketchup. I always prefer my ketchup served that way and really appreciate it during this pandemic.   Reading over the placemat menu, I'll definitely need to re-visit after ARW.  The service was attentive, in addition to our server, other servers would stop by to make sure everything was fine and we didn't need anything.   When: January 16, 2021 Why: Lunch - ARW

Congratulations, Courtesy Diner you have been removed from my No-No list. I was up early on St. Patrick's Day and after dropping a friend off at his work in Dogtown, I needed breakfast. I didn't need anything special or fancy, I just needed a simple breakfast. As I turned on to Hampton Avenue to head home, I saw you to my right and thought you needed a second chance.   As I parked my car I got a giggle from all the signs you had posted warning people not to park in your lot for the parade. I don't blame you, you gotta protect those spaces for your patrons. After the parade I am sure you had your share of drunk partiers in need of a sobering meal.   Okay, now the reason why you got off my No-No list. I wanted a cheap, simple and filling breakfast and you delivered. What I liked most is that you offered 1 egg instead of 2 egg breakfast entrees. Sometimes two is just too much. I was able to enjoy my egg with crispy hash browns and 3 slices of bacon. I said no to my side of toast, because I wanted to enjoy one biscuit with sausage gravy. The gravy needed more pepper and salt. Overall everything was above average and worth the price.   At 6AM the diner was clean and ready for a new day. The staff was cordial, but once others arrived, you could easily tell who were their regulars. CD, you may be off my No-No list, but your still not ready to be in my regular breakfast rotation. However, I will be back at another time.

A "Shack" closer to home, I could not be happier. I'm a big fan of their Valley Park location and now I am thrilled to have a shorter drive to enjoy their breakfast entrees.  What makes this location even better is that they will be open for Happy Hour and dinner with an extended menu.   This morning I enjoyed, Shack De Madame. SDM is; honey glazed ham, thick cut pecan wood bacon & white cheddar cheese on Texas toast topped with SHACK cheese sauce & a sunny side egg garnished with green onions. It comes with a side of some of the best Hash Browns, it the metro area. I love my HB's crispy and The Shack does them right. I don't even have to request them extra crispy when ordering.   I had to make sure the new location did the biscuits and gravy the same way, and they do. Big fluffy biscuits, smothered in rich and creamy milk gravy would make any farmers wife proud.   My dining buddy enjoyed one of his favorite breakfast entrees, Chicken Fried Steak and gave it a true thumbs up. I'm sure it would have been two thumbs up, but he refused to put the fork down. In addition to a large piece of CFS, he had two eggs and Hash Browns.   A visit to either locations for breakfast is not complete without enjoying a White Trash Screwdriver. The mixture of vodka, orange juice and pear apple cider, is a refreshing way to start the day.   The decor is old doors and paneling, covered in graffiti provided by the diners. This time I am remembering where I wrote my message. I wrote on the walls at Valley Park and to this day, cannot remember where.   The staff is friendly, I am sure I will get to know them all well as this Shack will definitely be in my breakfast rotation.

I'm raising the Saint Louis Galleria a star and taking them off my, Terrible Two's List. I'm simply doing this for their approach to the pandemic. They are requiring all shoppers to wear mask and they have hand sanitizer dispensers that are foot operated. Also, store that were open, when they reached the allowed amount in, they'd pull the gate down or close the doors until someone exited. Thank-you for making my shopping experience safe.   However, on another note, this mall is still super sad. If it were not for; Apple, Lenscrafter and Tommy Bahama, I would not be a patron. On my recent visit, I had appointments at Lenscrafter and the Apple store. In between my appointments, I walked the mall and was shocked at the number of closed stores I use to frequent. I was also surprised at the number of popular chain stores that were missing and newer stores that this old man has never heard of, taking their place.   The staggered openings of all stores was also, confusing. Some opened at 10, others at 11 and some were closed with no signage telling you when they'd open. I understand staffing is difficult now, so I will withhold judgment. However, I will still say that the kiosk and carts are tacky as hell. Get rid of all the carts, they are just nasty.   As anyone who lives in STL can tell you, there have been shooting here and at other malls as well. We all just need to be aware of our surroundings.   I believe the days of malls are a thing of the past.

This PAC may be off the beaten path, but you still get some of the best roasted coffee in the city. In fact you may not find it any fresher, since it is roasted right on site.  What I love about Park Avenue Coffee - The Hill:  Best Black Coffee in the city  Almond Milk is offered for Lattes  Yummy Gooey Butter Cake  Powered by Solar Energy  Earth friendly, they recycle and use reclaimed materials in their decor.   Frequent Buyers Club  Friendly Staff who provide top notch customer service  Need coffee and a relaxing place to work on the laptop? Skip Starbucks and find your way over to Park Avenue Coffee on Columbia Avenue.

I needed a cocktail and so did my friends. We all had been cooped up at home during damn pandemic and needed some out in public time. We knew 58hundred had their patio open and most importantly, we knew they made good cocktail.   We showed up right at opening time and kinda made our own Happy Hour. We picked a table toward the back that was kinda in the shade. Our server was great, David understood we were just there for the booze and would not be eating. However, being a good server, he still tempted us by sharing the daily specials.  My cocktails were my usual; Boulevardier, Martini and Manhattan. Variety is the spice of life. Before the pandemic, we all had been semi-regulars at the bar inside and were happy to have the bartender bring our drinks out to the patio when David got busy with another table.   Good service, masterfully prepared cocktails and a patio providing safe social distancing makes 58hundred the perfect place to escape COVID-19. You can also bring your fur-baby with you.Yep, the patio is dog friendly.   Will I return? - Yes, I gotta get my fix of Brussels Sprouts Tacos  When: June 25, 2020 Why: Pandemic Escape

I am so glad 58hundred is in my hood. We were in need of a quality, New American cuisine restaurant. It's a great place to grab an easy lunch or a flavorful dinner. Their bartenders are also masters of making classic cocktails like a Manhattan or Old Fashioned and that makes me happy.   I've been here multiple times and will say, I think they make my favorite taco in the city. One of my favorite vegetables is Brussels Sprouts and 58hundred takes them to the next level putting them in a taco. In addition to the sprouts, they mix them with lime creme, pickled red onions, caramelized onion and toasted almonds. The combination of these ingredients make for a simple lunch, or a delicious appetizer.   Two sandwiches I've tried are the 58 Burger for dinner and Hot Ham & Cheese for lunch. The burger is a traditional smash burger with white cheddar. I always upgrade to a double for an additional $4. I could run it through the garden for another additional $1, but I like my burgers simple - cheese & meat. I'm starting to really prefer a smash burger over the big thick burgers, they're more manageable to eat and I think they have more flavor, too. The garlic herb fries are a perfect side.   On the day I stopped by for lunch, I couldn't resist the Hot Ham & Cheese when I saw that the cheese was,Jalapeño Mornay. I'm a jalapeño junkie and it with country ham and caramelized onions made a huge sammie. It like the burger came with a side of fries.   The Pretzel Bites with Jalapeño White Cheddar Cheese Sauce are a great small plate to nosh on while you sit at the bar and sip on a Classic Cocktail. I've also tried the Nashville's Pimento Cheese Toast, but it did not impress me. Don't get me wrong, it's good, the toast was just to soft for my liking.   Service at the bar is always friendly and attentive.   I'll be back? - Yes! Want to try the grilled salmon and pork chop   When: Multiple Visits most recent May 31, 2019 Why: Lunch and Dinner

What do you do when you've had a rough day at work and you don't have the energy to cook? Go out? That's what my plan would be, but I didn't even have the energy to dress up and put on a pretty face. So, Louie's came to my rescue with delivery.   We ordered an appetizer of Lemon Pepper Chicken Wings and a small Chicago Original Deluxe Pizza. The LP wings were a nice change from the typical hot or BBQ wings. They had a tangy taste, blended with pepper. They were not as good as Jefferson Avenue Bistro, but were a good accompaniment to our pizza.   When you order a Chicago style pizza from Louie's, they'll ask if you want the sauce on bottom or top. Being a STL man, I always say "bottom".  I've tried it on top, but prefer my ingredients on top of the sauce. The original deluxe is my favorite ingredients so it makes it so easy to order instead of creating my own. Chicken, spinach, bacon and tomato are some good healthy choices. We ordered a small and had two slices left over for a work lunch the next day.   When ordering for delivery or carryout, the staff has good phone etiquette and customer service skills. If you opted for delivery, the drivers are clean-cut and friendly. A bonus of picking it up yourself is a Yelp check-in "prize". You'll receive a FREE 32 oz soda. That is more soda then I drink in a month, but you can get one for just showing some Yelp love.   The only reason I am lowering my stars from 5 to 4 is the fact that I am getting more stingy with my 5's. I'm still a BIG fan of Louie's, I just don't think it is as good as it gets.

It's always scary when you have to visit the "collector of revenue", but it doesn't need to be that way. These ladies have seen and heard it all. They could probably write an Emmy winning sitcom from all the bs they have heard from the citizens of the Lou.   What I thought was a major problem, was a speck in the whole picture. I didn't even have to write a check to correct my problem.

The envelope, please and the winner of best Fish Fry of Lent Season 2019 is, Edibles & Essentials. At least in my opinion it is.   Every Friday during Lent, E&E had their food truck, Essentially Fries parked out front serving up the absolute best fries and fried fish. With a food truck that specializes in fries, you already know the fries are going to be good. Well, let me tell you they can also fry up some crispy, flakey and flavorful fish. I had a lot of fish this Lent season and even though this was my last on Good Friday, it was also the best. I wish they'd do this at least once a month. If they did, I'd be here.   After ordering from the food truck and paying at the food truck, you could go inside and enjoy your meal. I enjoyed mine with a couple glasses of white wine.   The staff here is always so friendly and engaging. It may be order at the counter and take a table marker, but the service is still top notch and attentive.   I'll be back? - Absolutely!   When: April 19, 2019 Why: Lent - Good Friday - Fish Fry

I admit, I strayed away from Lucky's for awhile, but I am back now as a dedicated shopper.   Now that I am eating healthier, Lucky's produce department is becoming part of my new life. Especially on Wednesday when their sales brochures overlap. Their sales fliers always have good deals on veggies, fruits and great deals from the butcher case.    Shopping LM is similar to shopping at WF and Aldi's. You'll see brands that you haven't seen before at the local major grocers in town. However, once you have tried them, you'll realize they're basically the same quality. In some cases, better.   The staff is friendly. Those woking in produce and the meat departments have always been extremely helpful when I have had questions.   I'll be back? - Yep, give me those veggies   When: April 17, 2019 Why: Stocking up on fresh produce

I admit, I am a closeted Craver. It's not that I am embarrassed that I enjoy these steamed burgers cooked on a bed of onions and served on a steamed bun as well. It's just that some non-cravers just do not understand the love for these tiny burgers. After all, they were the first fast food hamburger back in 1921. OMG! in 6 years they'll be celebrating their centennial.   My favorite slider now is the Jalapeño. Instead of the regular American cheese, they top the beef patty with an American cheese flavored with pieces of Jalapeño. The mix of the grilled onions and the Jalapeño cheese, just makes the heartburn so much more enjoyable. The fries may be frozen, but they serve the crinkle cut, hot and crisp.   I'm glad that WC is a Coke restaurant and that they keep the fountain soda lines clean. I can personally tell the difference between freshly cleaned lines and those that have been neglected. A clean line, always makes the soda more refreshing.   The staff here is at times a little scattered brain, but I have never had a mistake in my order, I've just had a long wait.

I hate this store! I really do hate, it. You're probably wondering, if I hate it so much, how can I give it 4 Stars.  To be honest, it is more of a love/hate relationship.   Every time I come here looking for a specific item, they never have it. Yet, when I do come here looking for the special item, that they do not have, I never walk out empty handed. I usually walk out with one, if not two shopping bags full of things that I didn't even know I needed or wanted. This store has almost everything you'd want or need to make your house or apartment, your "Home".   Think of it as a very mini BB&B. It has many of the same items, just not the variety or selection to choose from.
