You also have to be a smart shopper and look at the off brands they have to make sure it it a quality item for the price. I primarily stay with name brands that I am familiar with, unless it just a decorative item.   HomeGoods is also a great place for spoiling the dog of the house. They have great pet beds, dishes and other items that will have your favorite K-9 thinking they are King or Queen of house.   Like its' sister store, TJ Maxx, you have to shop often, as the inventory changes quickly. See it today, don't think about, it may be gone tomorrow.   This last visit, I came in looking for curtains and left with new baking sheet pans in two sizes and new set of cooking utensils. This store can be dangerous.   When: February 9, 2016 Why: Things for the Home

Pointer's is a solid, A-OK above average fast order pizza joint. What makes it stand out from other fast-food pizza, is their New York style.   I was on my home from a Happy Hour in Clayton and needed dinner. As I drove down Big Bend, I started to crave pizza and Pointer's came to mind. My go to pizza toppings are sausage and jalapeño and that is what I ordered. They were not stingy with toppings and they do not use provel - win, win. My 12" pizza was enough for two meals.   The service at the counter was friendly and fast. I was surprised, just stopping and ordering my pizza had me in and out in 12 minutes. I'd recommend Pointer's over Domino's.   Will I return? - If in the area and I need a pizza.   When: October 19, 2017 Why: Dinner

This was a COVID visit and they handled it very well.   You call your order in advance, then when you arrive you call again to let them know you've arrived. When I arrived, the young lady running orders out was already making deliveries to other patrons and just stopped by car to ask which order was mine. When she returned with my order, she used the passenger side, so we did not have to touch each other passing the bag of food. The lady was friendly, detailed and was hustling to take care of all the cars waiting for carry-out.   Being new to the neighborhood, this was my first visit. I ordered, an Egg Roll, Crab Rangoon and General Chicken with Fried Rice. I was not impressed by any of the items. My Egg Roll was over cooked. The pockets on the Crab Rangoon's were small and contained a very small portion of crab. My entree, General Chicken was very dry and was more breading then chicken. The Fried Rice was, just nasty.   I'm still searching for a good Chinese restaurant in my new hometown. I may circle back to China Wok, to give them a second chance, but until then, I'll continue my search.   When: December 14, 2020 Why: Dinner - Curbside

I found out about D's Place when it was featured as the ROTD here on Yelp. When I arrived, I could tell from the outside it was a dive. Then when I entered, I smiled even more. I was a true dive bar. Or as Eric N.  said, in his ROTD, it is as close to "your neighborhood watering hole" as it can get. The proof was as I sat at the bar enjoying my lunch, all the other patrons greeted each other by name. That's a true neighborhood bar.   My biggest dilemma was should I order wings or a burger. After getting recommendation from the bartender, I choose to go wings. Especially after I found out, I could choose two different flavors in one order. I went with my favorite, Lemon & Pepper and a bar favorite, Garlic Parmesan.  When ordering wings, I am a stickler for my order having the same amount of flats and drums. D's impressed me, they not only gave me the same amount of flats and drums in my order, they also made sure each flavor had the same amount.   My wing pieces were good in size and fried to a crispy crunch. Being a true fan of Lemon & Pepper, it was my favorite. I love the tang of lemon and kick of pepper. I can see why their Garlic & Parmesan is a bar favorite. However, I would not recommend them on a date night. I say that with a smile, because they're garlic flavor as good as it was, it was strong. I guess if you share the order, with your date all would be good. (smile)  I was not impressed with the fries that I had as a side with my wings. I'm super picky about my fries and don't care for the type that are seasonally coated. I heard their onion rings are good, so when I come back to experience the, Hell Fire Burger that has fried jalapeños on it (another favorite of mine) I'll order onion rings as my side.   Service was dive bar friendly. The bartender called all the other guest by their name. Not knowing mine, she just called me, "Babe" when she checked on me frequently. With only a single bartender covering the entire bar and tables, the service was attentive.   I'll be back? - Hell Fire Burger is calling my name.   When: September 11, 2019 Why: 9-4-19 ROTD on Yelp

Bad Rooster, Bad Rooster.  How did you ever get a 4 Star rating on Yelp? My experience today at Brunch was a total disappointment. The only "saving grace" that kept you from getting a 1 Star rating was our sweet waitress, Grace.   Wanting to beat the crowds we arrived early to get our day off to a good start. We were promptly greeted and seated in a room where four other diners were waiting for a server. I immediately got excited when I saw the large blackboard boosting 7 Mimosa's and 11 different Bloody Mary's. Once our orders started to arrive, my excitement was gone and I became displeased with our choice of Brunch.   To make this easy, I am going to list the disappointments numerically:  1. The House Bloody Mary - Which is their own secret blend of 17 ingredients, is in no danger of being stolen. It is bland and flavorless. A can of Low Sodium V8 and a rot gut Vodka can make a better BM.   2. Half Order Biscuits & Gravy - Great house made biscuit, which was fluffy, flaky and uniquely square in shape. However, the Sausage Gravy that topped this incredible biscuit lacked in flavor. We saw no evidence of sausage in the gravy and definitely no flavor. I'm not a fan of salt, but come on use at least a little. When I have to add salt at the table, there is a serious problem.   3. Savory Crepe - Bacon #3 - Bacon (of course), Oven Dried Tomatoes and Goat Cheese. The Crepe was rubbery and tough, which went along with the over cooked bacon that had the texture of beef jerky. What a shame the wonderful Goat Cheese went to waste in this mixture, along with the Oven-baked Tomatoes.   4. Breakfast Scrambles #6 - Bacon, Mushrooms, Emmenthaler and Arugula. Great presentation on the plate, but not the palate. It had a gritty, dirty taste. It was so unpleasant that the SO sent it back and exchanged it for pancakes.   5. The Pancakes with Caramelized Bananas and Nuts were a good replacement. However, reduce the amount of nuts and plate it differently, there was no room for maple syrup.   6. Accoustics, there was none to speak of. The music (enjoyable) was loud making conversation difficult.   7. Cleanliness - The floor looked as if it were not swept the day before and dust covered the edge of the booth. With all those windows letting in natural light, these housekeeping flaws stood out and took away from the hipster ambiance.   Once again, Grace was a fantastic server. If it were not for her winning personality I would have given Rooster a 1.

I absolutely love this store. It is one of my go to stores for Christmas gifts and also unique gifts for that person who is always hard to buy for.   First off let me tell you the name can be a little misleading. Yes, they do have gardening items, but they are also a home decor store. Today I found a couple of decorative Easter themed items for my mantel in the living room. I change the mantel for every holiday or season, to for me these were great finds.   In addition to the gardening and home decor, you'll find cookbooks,  a small variety of gourmet food items and entertaining accessories. Those who know me, know I have a love for jalapeños so I almost went crazy when I found a jar of, Jalapeño Pickles. The brand is, Natural Pickled Pink. So, I guess you could say, I was tickled pink.   I am also known for my cocktail napkins. I take them to parties, gatherings with friends at restaurants and I usually add a package to coordinate with gifts. So, if you too are in to unique and funny cocktail napkins, come shop the rack here. I can guarantee you will walk out with more then one package.   Whoever is working, the service is friendly and attentive. It the type of service you expect and deserve when shopping a higher end store.

I love me some Home Goods, but this location is not one of the better ones.  When I shop here, I am kinda lost and confused. The store lay-out and merchandising is totally different then my regular HG stores that I shop.   I can still find a treasure or two here when I shop, but the selection seems to be far less then what I typically find at the Kirkwood and Edwardsville stores.   Also, the staff is less engaging than the other stores.   I'll still frequent and shop this store when I'm in the area, but it's not one of my favorites. Hopefully I'll find a true treasurer some day and have exceptional service and I can raise their score.   When: August 7, 2021 Why: Accessories for the home.

I am not a fan of Indian food, but I was impressed here at Himalayan Hut. I came with a group of friends. Our little group meets monthly as, International Supper Club and they help me push my taste buds to explore and discover new things.   Even though we call it, "supper" club on this day we did a lunch. We came to HH for their lunch buffet. The spread was small, but had plenty of offerings for lunch. I'm not normally a buffet person, but all the food was fresh and at a good temperature. I liked it because, I was able to sample a variety of entrees and different sides. It was a great way to educate my taste buds about Indian cuisine.   The service was professional. Even with it being a buffet, they made sure we always had full water glasses and the baskets had plenty of pita bread.   I'll be back? - I actually think I will.   When: February 16, 2019 Why: Lunch with friends

I am so glad I finally discovered this hidden "little coffee gem", as Christy A. calls them. I've been to Scarlett's at least a half dozen times and never noticed this jewel until today. After enjoying an amazing brunch, we ventured over to Northwest to check them out.   So many coffee shops claim to be or strive to be a "hipster" coffee shop. They have a long way to go to compete with NWCRC. It is tiny, compact and a cool atmosphere. I had just eaten, so I only got a black coffee to go and it was delicious. I'm a purist, I drink my coffee plain and black. This truly was one of the best black coffees I've had in the city. It's totally way better then Starbucks and Kaldi's.   I cannot wait to come back and try the waffles. A big attraction to me is that they open at 6:30 AM. I'm an early riser and this opening works well with my schedule. Their customer service was friendly and professional. They totally made me feel welcomed, even though I was just ordering a small black coffee to go.   For those of you who do a lot of your work in coffee shops, they offer free WI-FI and also have a printer that you can access. That is top-notch customer service.   Would I go back? - I'll most likely be there tomorrow.   When: December 11, 2016 Why: Coffee to go

Lucky for Godfrey this Hardee's is also a Red Burrito. Or I should say, lucky for me. When I lived in STL, the Hardee's close to my home was also a Red Burrito and I sorta became a fan of their tacos. For a fast food chain, their tacos really hit the spot.   Yesterday was National Taco Day and National Crunchy Taco Day and I didn't get to celebrate. I tried to go to Taco Bell, but the line was way to long. When I drove pass Hardee's on my way home, I realized they too were a Red Burrito, but I was in the wrong lane to make the turn. So I am celebrating a day late.   I ordered two crunchy beef tacos and one soft chicken taco. For some reason when I'm doing fast food tacos, I prefer mine just as I ordered them. I don't like my beef soft or my chicken crunchy. They were all topped with fresh chopped lettuce and a decent amount of shredded cheese. The piccata sauce they provided gave it an extra boost of flavor.   If only they had Margaritas to go it would have been the perfect after work snack. However, the Schlafly Pale Ale I had at home was a fine substitute.   This visit was during COVID and I had to use the drive-thru. It was nice to see the staff was still being cautious and protective by wearing mask. They were also, polite and friendly. Which is a rarity in fast food.   Will I return? - It's in my new hood and I support businesses in my neighborhood so, YES.   When: October 5, 2020 Why: National Taco Day a day late

Seriously, what has happened to this mall? It use to be the premiere mall in St. Louis. It use to be where the "best stores, put their best store". It could not prove that to me on my last visit. I was shocked at what it has become. I can only hope that when Nordstrom finally opens, that it will bring a breath of fresh air.   Who ever is responsible for leasing the kiosk and those tacky carts needs to be publicly spanked. They should make it an event and spank them in center court. The selection of these carts is an embarrassment to the high image that the Galleria tries to project. When I walked from one end to the other on both levels, these carts made me feel as if I were at the Gypsy Caravan on Memorial Day Weekend.   Tenants like Sunglass Hut and Solstice Sunglass Boutique should be outraged that they rent carts to folks that sell cheap knock offs. I guess this could work to their advantage, shoppers can compare and see you do get what you pay for.   The other carts just seemed to be the same thing cart after cart - cell phone accessories. Come on lessor, get out do some research and bring some unique carts to the Galleria. I would rather see no carts, then the ones you are currently offering.   I will continue to use the Galleria as a destination shopping mall for stores like Apple and Restoration Hardware. Otherwise, I will continue to shop boutiques and out of town.

It's been 10+ years since my last review of this, First Watch. So it definitely is time for an update. Since that first reviewed visit, I have been here numerous times and I can say it has consistently been good. FW is a little pricey compared your other typical breakfast restaurants, but the quality of food is well worth the price. Here there seems to be a lot more healthier choices to select from. I just wish they all offered alcohol, like the new location on Brentwood.   My visit today was to kill time while Murphy was at the day spa getting groomed. First thing I noticed when I entered, was that they had spaced the tables out to make sure they were social distancing all their guest. Another thing I noticed when seated was my table tent advertising, Crab & Avocado Toast. Being a fan of Avocado Toast and loving crab meat, it was a no-brainer on what to order. In addition to the toast, I added a side of their infamous Million Dollar Bacon. These two light and refreshing breakfast dishes paired with a cup of black coffee, made for a perfect breakfast.   The avocado was smooth with little chunks of avocado and topped with shredded crab meat that was garnished with pickled red onion. I may have been enjoying it for breakfast, but it very easily could be a perfect lunch, too.   Don't worry, The Million Dollar Bacon doesn't cost a million dollars. It only cost $5.49, but it seems like it is worth a million. It's 4 perfectly prepared slices of their signature hardwood smoked bacon. It is baked with brown sugar, black pepper, cayenne and drizzled with maple syrup. You'll have sticky fingers, but they'll be finger licking good.   I've never had bad service here. The staff is always pleasant and friendly. My server today was  quite charming. I also appreciated all the precautions they had in place during this everlasting pandemic.   Parking lot wasn't as bad as ten years ago. I am now one of those older drivers and there were less diners crowding the parking lot - LOL.   When: February 19, 2021 Why: Healthy Breakfast

My first visit here did not include food, but I will be back to experience that very soon. This visit was all about connecting with old friends who were passing through town and St. Charles was the best connecting location. I selected Prasino due to friends reviews on Yelp and they did not let me down. The cocktails were masterfully created and the service was attentive, friendly and sincere.   I arrived much earlier then my friends, so I placed myself at the bar and ordered one of their signature cocktails, The Urban. OMG! Life truly would be good if all apple juice tasted like this cocktail. The mixture of rye, St. Germaine, apple juice, lemon and baked apple bitters, with a slice of Granny Smith apple as a garnish. It went down so smooth, I finished and needed another cocktail in no time.   My second cocktail I went with one of my favorite classics, a Manhattan. The bartender offered it up or on the rocks. I said, even though I liked their small little cubes I'd take it up. I then mentioned I prefer the big solid cube and he quickly informed me that they had those. Nice. I judge a bartender how they make a Manhattan and this gentleman nailed it. It was strong, smooth and perfectly blended.   Since I had skipped lunch, I ordered some Tortilla Chips and Guacamole from the Happy Hour menu.  It was a simple nosh to have a little something in the tummy as I sipped my strong cocktail. The guacamole was impressive for a non Mexican restaurant and the chips were better then some of the restaurants down on Cherokee.   When my friends arrived we moved out to the patio and they placed their drink orders. Two enjoyed Bloody Mary's and the third had a Bombay Gin & Tonic. Both BM drinks gave them a thumbs up, but one likes'm really spicy so she had them bring her a small bottle of Tabasco so she could kick hers up a notch.   My final drink of the evening was an Old Fashioned, which should be no surprise to those who know or follow me on Yelp. Again, I was totally impressed. I truly did not expect the cocktails to be this high quality. That is what is going to bring me back from the inner-city to have another and to try the food.   Will I come back? Most definitely.  When: August 14, 2017 Why: Happy Hour with friends.

Sweet EM's is just what Dogtown needed times two. Dogtown was in need of a coffee shop and a ice cream parlor and Sweet EM's gives them both all rolled into one cute little shop.   I discovered Sweet EM's while I was sitting in my car waiting for one of the frame shops to open. I was craving a coffee and was wishing Dogtown had a coffee shop. I finally saw someone crossing the intersection and then I saw them recross with a coffee in hand. I immediately jumped out of my car and went in the direction I had seen them go. To my surprise I found Sweet EM's.   I not only was impressed with my simple black coffee and muffin, but was also impressed with their curbside service during COVID. They were offering service through a walk-up window from the front sidewalk. The young lady working was perky and friendly.   Next time I have dinner in Dogtown, I'm definitely saving room for dessert. That way I can come here and try the ice cream.   Will I be back? - I scream for ice cream.   When - October 29, 2020 Why - Needed Coffee

What in the hell is going on? I have no excuse for why I haven't written a review for, The Bug Store. Honestly, it is one of my favorite stores to shop for the yard and unique fun gifts for friends and family. I even take out of town guest here for the experience.   All I can say is, if you haven't been, you've got to go now. You will find the most fabulous items for your home decor and garden. The staff is helpful and friendly making for a pleasant shopping experience.   Just a heads-up, they do not sell bugs.   When: Countless times Why: My garden and gifts

Let me begin by stating this visit was during COVID. It's a dive diner that serves up comfort food and has a staff straight out of Mel's Diner on Alice. 3 Stars is a good rating, it is stating that things are A-OK.   I have just moved into the Godfrey township and am out exploring places to enjoy breakfast. I've driven by Round Table and have seen lots of folks dining under tents in the parking lot in front. Today when I arrived, all the tents were gone and folks were dining inside. To be honest, I was a little hesitate about going in, but bit the bullet and went inside.   I was pleased to see they were spacing their diners out, staff was wearing mask and they had hand sanitizer available. They were following all the CDC guidelines. Good job.   Being an old farm boy, who moved to the big city and is now returning to his roots and who loves biscuits and gravy was pleased to see them on the menu. I was really excited to see that they offer a plate with; one biscuit and gravy, two eggs and a choice of meat. Give it to me with bacon. For me this was a perfect little breakfast and at a great price. Add on a cup of black coffee and life is good.   The biscuit was huge and fluffy and the gravy had a good amount of sausage floating within it. It was also seasoned mildly. Not overly salty, but it could have used more pepper. However, with the shaker on the table, I resolved that problem.   My eggs were scrambled and kinda on the cold side. As were the bacon, but the bacon had wonderful flavor and was crispy. I'm confident that in future visits, because I already know I will return, that this little dive diner will be bumped up to more stars.  Will I return? - I love eating breakfast out, so hell yes.   When: October 7, 2020 Why: Breakfast Out

Edibles & Essentials is a great little cafe & market on South Hampton. It's a great cafe to enjoy lunch with friends, grab some gourmet carry-out for dinner or relax with a Saturday Brunch. If you play chef at home, their market has some amazing and hard to find ingredients. I've grabbed a few unusual spices and such for gift baskets and they've gone over extremely well.   My most recent lunches have all included their delicious fries with house made ketchup. They are perfectly done, crisp on the outside and soft-n-meaty inside. This is not easy to do with a thin cut try, but they do it well. Their house ketchup is spicy and has a nice tang to it. It is served in little cups on the side of your hot fries.   The sandwiches I have tried are; Meatloaf, Thai Chicken Burger and Veggie Burger. I'd order all three of them again, but I'd say the Thai Chicken was my favorite. The Thai flavors, made it a truly unique sandwich.   I rarely have a weekend off, so I was excited this past weekend that I finally got to try their Saturday Brunch. It's nothing fancy, it is a simple brunch at a very affordable price. A brunch isn't a brunch without a Bloody Mary and here I got to enjoy one for only $5. They also had, Mimosas and Screwdrivers available for the same price.  Being a farm boy and growing up on Biscuits and Gravy, I had to give theirs a try. It was a single large biscuit split and covered in a sausage milk gravy. A farmers wife would be proud of the way they served it up. Once I moved to the city, I became addicted to Benedict's. This morning they were offering a Smoked Salmon Benedict. It had a nice serving of Salmon on top of the egg and then topped with the Hollandaise sauce. Having lived with a chef for several years, I'm spoiled - I think the hollandaise could have been better, but hey it was only $10, so it was totally worth it. I enjoy it and cleaned my plate - both of them.   The staff is always friendly and helpful. I keep forgetting about the Prix Fixe menu on Monday and their Tapas Tuesday. That wont be happening again - I put a reminder in my smart phone so I can go and experience those two events as well.   Will I be back? It's in my hood and I support my local businesses. So the answer is, YES.   When: Multiple previous dates and most recent 11/12/16 Why: Lunch and Brunch

Had my first golf lesson at Tower Tee the other day and while driving to class I noticed this Fortels in Affton. It gave me flash backs to when I worked at Plaza Frontenac and we'd order multiple pizzas from the Fortels in Kirkwood for the entire store. Damn, those were good pizzas.   All I could think about in class was Fortels Pizza and the scene in Fast Times at Ridgemont High where Sean Pean had a pizza delivered to class. I resisted the urge and kept my focus on my long shot. Knowing I could stop and get carryout on my way home.   After class, my first stop was Fortels. One of the nicest thing about Fortels pizza is no provel cheese, they use 100% Mozzarella Cheese.  (I've always thought Mozzarella sounds like the sister of Crurella De Ville or a Drag Queens name) Another thing that makes the pizza at Fortels stand out is the sauce, a flavorful mix of sweet & spicy.   Tonight's order was a 12" Sausage & Peperoni and a Large House Salad with house dressing. Once I got home I realized the salad was way to much and placed in icebox for a work lunch the next day. In fact it was so big, it made lunch for two days. It was nice that they had given me two small containers of dressing, they must have known. The pizza was very good, I just can not allow myself to indulge after every golf class.   Special perks at the Affton location is Gluten Free Crust and Lottery Tickets. What a deal pizza and powerball all in one stop.

Do you want to relax and have a good time with friends? If so, this is the place to visit for Happy Hour or a week-end afternoon. UCBC has created a huge beer hall in The Grove neighborhood, that will having you escaping daily stress and finding your "groove" again.   A couple of friends meet here to support a friend who just lost a beloved dog. UCBC is a dog friendly establishment and Elke had been numerous times, so we thought it was an appropriate place to celebrate her life. Also, we had her K-9 sister Ms. Bunny with us.   We enjoyed four rounds of different beers, we had a rule that you could not repeat a beer. After all, when you are at a brewery, so you should experience as many  different beers as you can. We also enjoyed a variety of snacks/appetizers from their kitchen. Items we enjoyed; Pommes Frites, Deviled Eggs, Currywurst and Pork Rinds. After beer and savory treats, we treated ourselves to their sweets; Liege Waffles and Berliners. I'd recommend all of the treats, except the Pork Rinds. We all found them to be bland.    I give a thumb ups to all the beers I tried; On The Wings of Armageddon, Winged Nut (personal favorite), Fantasyland and Geiles. I would have posted pictures, but all beers look alike when photographed.   As a reminder, this is a dog friendly brewery and a great place to bring your K-9 to enjoy a beer.   When: July 1, 2015 Why: Gathering of friends

There were enough police on hand today, to make sure there was no "Raising Cain" during the opening of "Raising Cane's" Chicken Fingers on Hampton. I am not a proponent of fast food, but I do like chicken fingers at RCCF.   Their menu is simple, it is limited to only chicken fingers; aka chicken tenders. They are served in boxes, combos, sandwiches and tailgates. The fingers are made fresh to order and are from chicken breast tenderloins that have never been frozen. Since Raising Cane's make everything to order, your fingers will never sit under a heat lamp. It will come out of the kitchen, straight to you.   They offer two sides; cole slaw which is made on site daily. They also offer Crinkle-Cut Fries, that are cooked to a golden crispy outside and a soft  inside. They are only lightly salted, unlike other fast-food joints that overly salt their fries. Being someone who watches their sodium intake, this is greatly appreciated.   Then they have the famous, Cane's Sauce. Supposedly the GM makes a fresh batch everyday at each location, to keep the recipe Top Secret. Yadda, Yadda, Yadda....... I think the breading on the fingers is flavorful enough, so I have no need for these sauce. No even for my fries.   Two more positive points before I share my only next one. They serve Coke products - Yippie.  Also, they spell ketchup the correct way. My biggest beef with RCCF is their to-go vessels are styrofoam, which makes them non eco-friendly. However, I will point out that they are vented so heat can escape.   It was opening day, the staff was pumped and full of energy. Let's hope they continue on with their positive attitudes.   When: March 29, 2016 Opening Day Why: Late Lunch

I have a bone to pick with O'Connell's and it's a chicken bone. Why do you only offer the best wings in the city only on Sunday?  Big Dramatic Pause.......  Never mind I figured it out. If you offered these everyday of the week, they might over shadow your fantastic grilled burgers and put other wing places out of business.   Those of you who have not had their wings, go this next Sunday. You'll experience spicy hot, burn your lips, meaty, moist and juicy wings.   We went last night, forgetting O'Connell's would be the perfect place to take dad for his special Hallmark Day. They were packed to the rafters, but the wait staff was working the room and turning the tables fast and still giving attentive service.  I also need to give a big shout out to the kitchen staff at O'Connell's. They prepare the "perfect" burger. No matter how you order it, they do it right. They're so thick, that I have a hard time getting my mouth around it and I have a big mouth. They only offer two cheeses; American and Swiss. No provel at O'Connell's, that one is worth an additional star.   Had the Onion Rings last night and they were better then my favorite place for rings. I'm beginning to believe whatever O'Connell's offers, they've perfected it. I swear O'Connell's is like a good wine, it seems to be getting better with age.

Another one of my favorites for #shopsmall and #shoplocal. The unique gifts that I have found here have always been well received. Don't be distracted by the name. Yes, there are lots of great things for the garden and gardner, but the decorative items for the home will impress you.   This year I was thrilled with many of the holiday decorations that had a vintage look. I have several people on my gift list that go way over board when decorating for the holiday and I was able to find their perfect gift here.   One of my signature gifts, it's actually a fun add-on for a laugh is a package of cocktail napkins. I have alway been able to find a package or two here that fit the personality of my gift recipient. TGG also, has a selection of greeting cards that you will not find at your local Hallmark store. Making your card much more memorable then the others.  Being obsessed with the color orange, I have to use my self control when shopping the gardening tools. My family says, I'll buy anything orange, so some of the tools that are orange I just drool over and hope Santa or someone thinks of me when they shop The Gifted Gardener.   Would I come back? - The seed has already been planted.   When: December 11, 2016 Why: It's beginning to look a lot like Christmas

We went Saturday around 11 am, one of us had breakfast and the other did a lunch fare. Both were very good, with the lunch fare being the best. Don't get me wrong, the breakfast was still very good, the club sandwich was just better. The parking is plentiful, but beware of the senior drivers who pull-up to drop or pick-up their friends. Which is fine, I have no problem with that happening. However, while I was there they were lined up like they were waiting for valet parking, and we had to wait to back out of our parking space. It gave us a good chuckle, knowing that would proubly be us in the future. Recommend | Not helpful

Helen has been around for ages and she is starting to show her age. It's probably been 8 years since my last visit and things haven't changed at all.  I'll take that back, on the menu there was a couple items marked with a shamrock with the word New inside it.   We had an Entertainment.com coupon for $5 off $20, so we thought we'd give Helen a try.  Arriving around 2PM, we were after the lunch rush so The Grill side was fairly empty. The host asked us if we preferred a booth and we responded, yes. He seated us, asked for our drink order and quickly returned with our ice teas and told us who our server would be. As we waited for our server, I noticed they had a green cup on the table with dice, pencils and score cards. How cool, you can play Yahtzee or Classic 6 while you dine.   Our server showed up, we declined appetizers (watching weight) asked a few questions and requested more time to glance over the menu. When he returned, I asked about the daily special and decided to order it, which was a Turkey Wrap with Fries. The SO ordered a Cajun Chicken Wrap with House Chips.   My wrap had an enormous amount of turkey that was accented by bacon and cheddar cheese. The crinkle fries were larger then most crinkle fries I've experienced and were seasoned well with a mixture of salt and pepper. I only ate half of my wrap, meaning I have the bulk of my lunch for work tomorrow ready to go.   The Cajun Wrap wasn't as good as my turkey.  Nothing can ruin a wrap quicker then a mealy tomato. However, the House Chips in my opinion were better then those served at Llwelyn's or Dressel's. Sliced thin, fried crisp and the right amount of salt seasoning gave them one of my three stars.   The service was lack luster, I think our server must have been worn out after the lunch rush. I was disappointed to see their to go vessels are Styrofoam.  May have been embossed with a pretty design, but it isn't Eco friendly.   When visiting Helen keep in mind, The Bar is a meat market for the young to hook up and The Grill is more for the aged to get a meal with friends. Helen has been around for years and it will be years before I return.

I had been in STL partying with friends and just needed some finger food to munch on the drive home. So as I drove pass this WC, I pulled in and ordered my favorite, which is Combo #2. I also wanted a small order of onion rings, but they were sold out, so I tried the Mozzarella Sticks instead.   The Combo #2 is; two Double Cheese Sliders, fries and a drink. For my drink, I choose a Diet Coke. Having a diet soda balances out the calories and carbs from the combo meal. My burgers were hot and gooey, just like a slider should be. The fries (Crinkle Cut) were hot, as were the cheese sticks.   The young lady taking the order over the intercom and my money at the window was polite and efficient. I was through the drive-thru in nothing flat and back on the road to IL, with a tummy filling snack.   I rounded up for some charity, but I don't remember which one. I'm a sucker for round-ups.   When: August 4, 2021 Why: Snack for Road Trip - cutting the booze

Did you know, Santa shops here? If it is good enough for the fat man with a beard who lives at the North Pole, it definitely is good enough for me. I love the uniqueness of all the gift items and the fact that shopping here is shopping local and supporting a small business. Santa being a small business man himself, knows the importance of #shopsmall #shoplocal.   This year I found 8 gifts for those on my "nice" list. However, I must confess now that the holidays are over, that as I went to wrap one of them, I decided to keep it for myself. It was a cookbook and it would get more use with me then the person who was to be gifted. Don't worry, I found them something at another local store.   This year I found a variety of Christmas ornaments that were perfect accents to my bows on the holiday gifts. As usual, this is the place that I found the perfect cocktail napkins for entertaining.  As a heads up, because I stocked up while Christmas shopping, I discovered their greeting card rack. These cards are witty with adult humor that you will not find them at a Hallmark or American Greetings store. Check them out, these are cards that people will cherish as a keepsake.   Next year if you want to get me a Christmas present, I'll be happy with anything from The Gifted Gardner. Just letting you know.   Will I return? - In a heartbeat.   When: November 11, 2017 Why: Holiday Shopping - both B-Day & Christmas

I have to agree with everyone who has reviewed Herbaria before me, it truly is a 5 Star skin care boutique. As their website says, "You'll find pure pleasure in every bar." All of their soaps are natural handmade and their minimal packaging is made from recycled paper. Good for your skin and eco-friendly packaging is a winner.  I'm a "bar hopper", I like a variety of different soaps. I switch things up from week to week and even have been known to have two different bars in the shower at the same time. Being a "bar hopper", shopping at Herbaria helps me save $. When I buy 6 bars, I get 1 free. Even when I buy my usual boxed set of "Gentleman's Choice"* which includes 6 manly bars, I still qualify for the free bar. I've not taken advantage of it yet, but if I'd buy 4 more bars at the same time I'd get another one free. That's a big savings, buy 10 get 2 free.   Three bars that I want to give a Stevie B shout out to are; Traveler's Choice, Gardener's Hand Soap and Shaving Soap. The Traveler's Choice helps you cut down on those 3.5 oz bottles when going through those TSA check points especially for men. This handy little bar serves three purposes for you; soap, shampoo and shave. Which eliminates two bottles in your travel kit and you don't have to use those tiny bars of soap at the hotel.   I can not sing the praises enough of their Gardener's Hand Soap. I try to wear gloves when working in the dirt, but getting down and dirty without them, is so much more fun. Cleaning up after planting a bed of annuals or perennials is now a breeze with their GHS. Also, I am now a big fan of their Shave Soap. I no longer need to buy an aerosol can which are not good for the environment. I just lather my face up and shave.   When you go to Herbaria, I must warn you about Soapy. She is one of their Customer Service Specialist and she is a sales animal. Once she greets you and your eyes meet, those big brown puppy dog eyes will win you over. She'll have you right in her paw. Then if you knell down to her level and get butterfly kisses, you might as well give her your credit card. She has closed the sale.   If you haven't figured it out, Soapy is the house dog and she is true delight. On my most recent visit, the owner a distinguished gentleman greeted us as we entered and asked if we had been there before. As he was asking, Soapy entered the room and shouted out to her and she ran over. The man laughed and said, "Obviously you've been here before". I shopped, got a free bar and as I was leaving, I shouted goodbye to Soapy who had retreated to the work area. Everyone laughed out loud, because after I said my goodbye, a single bark came from the back-room. It was as if, Soapy was saying goodbye back to me. Now that is a Customer Service Specialist.   *Gentleman's Choice contains - Pompeii Pumice, Bay Rum, Traveler's Choice, Natural Citronella & Marigold, Sassafras Birch and Evergreen.

Shelby and Buddy always feel so pretty, when they have had a visit to "the doggie  spa". That is what we call a visit to the groomer in our house.  Who doesn't feel re-energized after a refreshing bath, shampoo and a mani-pedi. Then on their nightly walk that evening, Shelby barks to everyone she sees, to make sure they see how BEAUTIFUL she is. It as if she is saying, "Hey, look at me. Your dog could look this good if you took them to Little House of Dogs".    The staff here are true dog lovers. Mary the office manager is friendly and truly remembers every dog. She even calls the day before your appointment to reconfirm.  Now that is good customer service. Our favorite stylist is Cathy, she has been doing my Fur-Babies for 8+ years. They've developed the same trusting bond, that I have with my own personal stylist. Hope they don't talk about me, to her.   As with most privately owned pet stylist shops, it is cash or check only. You'd get a giggle if you saw my checkbook ledger. I'm a true debit card man and the only checks I write are to my hairstylist and to LHOD for my dogs hairstylist.

OMG! I have held off going here, because so many friends gave it the thumbs down. They moaned and groaned about the wait and size of servings. What is wrong with, them. I was pleasantly surprised with the quality of product, the size of serving and value.  I admit, I was here right as they opened on a Tuesday, but I shocked how fast they young lady made my ice cream. I placed my order and as I checked in to Yelp on my smart phone and read the adult ice cream menu - she was done. I wanted to start watching her and she was scooping it out of the mixer and adding my toppings. So much for a scientific show. I'll have to pay closer attention when I come back for a boozy ice cream. Mrs. Marshall's Old Fashioned is calling to me.   I went with Ian Froeb's "must order" recommendation from his STL 100 list, the Salted Dulce de Leche Custard. Again, I must repeat, OMG! It was so rich, creamy and decadent. The regular size is big enough, how anyone can eat a large by themselves is beyond my comprehension.   Ices Plain & Fancy is being added to my Sweet Tooth list and will now be in my ice cream parlor rotation. It's off the beaten path, but is an easy find with plenty of street parking.   IPF is dog friendly. They can make a special ice cream for your fur-baby to enjoy on the patio, or in a to-go container to enjoy in the comforts of his dog house.   To those who complain about the wait time - get over it. Once you enjoy this decadent treat, you'll understand it was well worth the wait. A quality product, takes time and that is what IPF is serving.   Will I be back? Yes. My waistline may not like it, but I sacrifice and make cuts in others calories, so I can enjoy this sweet treat.   When: November 15, 2016 Why: The time had come to experience decadence.

I was shocked today to learn that CJ Muggs is a local business and not a chain. I knew we had two in the Saint Louis area, so for some reason I just assumed it was a chain. I have never been so glad in my life to be wrong. It is similar to a TGIF or Houlihan's with hometown ownership.   After dropping more $'s then I normally do for tennis shoes, I wanted to save some $'s on lunch so I flipped through the Entertainment Coupon Book and found one for CJ Muggs. It was a BOGO which would give us a savings of $8.   We were strong and skipped having an appetizer. I stuck to being good on my diet, and enjoyed the Smoked Salmon Spinach and Field Greens Salad. Spinach, mixed greens,  crumbled blue cheese, toasted walnuts,  roasted red and yellow peppers, al dente green beans topped with a nice size piece of smoked salmon and tossed in their strawberry vinaigrette. It was a nice mix, but they were heavy handed on the dressing. I would also recommend breaking the salmon up to make it easier to enjoy.   The SO enjoyed a small house salad with blue cheese dressing, which was just a typical small dinner salad. Then he enjoyed a half size of Muffalato with their house french fries. They did a great job on the Muffalato. It may not be Blues City Deli, but when in Clayton it will do. Their fries were made in house, I love it when fries have the outer potato skin on and are fried crispy.   Service was good, our waitress was friendly and chatty making our first visit enjoyable. I think on our next visit we'll check out their location in Webster Grove and see which one is the best of the two. After all, I have more BOGO coupons.

Maeva's is simply amazing. It's a throwback to the vintage coffee shops of the 70's. If I walked in with a tie-dyed t-shirt on and sandals, I would have felt right at home.   Maeva's is tucked inside a old school and they've converted one of the old classrooms into one of the most charming coffee shop in Alton. Even with its local popularity, it is still one of the best kept secrets, that needs to be let out.   They have a very extensive drink menu for both hot and cold beverages. What blew my mind, is when I found out they do all of their own baking. My Blueberry Coffee Cake was to die for and I cannot wait to come back and try their "famous" Monkey Bread. Another item on the food menu, that is an  must try is the quiche. They are the perfect size for one, almost like a personalized pizza.   I love how they worked the old school house charm into the decor. They have old fashioned encyclopedias on bookshelves Many of us grew up using them, before there was the internet and Google. Good to see they can still be used today.   The staff/barista is not what you'd find at a Starbucks. They're much better.   If you're in Alton and needing a cup of coffee, be sure to check this place out. I guarantee, you will not be disappointed.

Great service during COVID. I've been borrowing a small pick-up truck from my cousin during my move to a new house. While using it, I noticed it was time for an oil change, so it just seemed to be the right thing to do and get it done.   The day before yesterday, while I was stopped at a stoplight, a kind gentleman pulled up next to me and informed me that the taillight on the drivers side was out. So while I was getting the oil changed, I asked if they could do that as well and they could. That was a win-win for me.   The staff was very friendly and when I explained that I was not the owner and was borrowing they truck, they offered to print out a report for my cousin so he knew what they did.   They were also did everything within social distancing guidelines. I was allowed to stay in the truck and all of the staff made sure they had mask on when they approached the side of the truck to speak to me.   I've just moved into this neighborhood and when I need an oil change, this is where I'll think of first.   Will I return? - What did I just, say?   When: October 7, 2020 Why: Oil Change in the O-Mobil

This diner is, delicious and delightful. It is down-home, comfortable and affordable. If I lived in this area, this definitely would be my go to place for breakfast.   After a fun-filled Saturday with family, that included lots of liquor, we all need a hearty breakfast Sunday morning. I searched Yelp, but my cousins knew about Clifton Country Inn. They also knew I would enjoy it and they were so right. I didn't go back and check, but I swear the kitchen at CCIR has to be filled with a team of Grandma's and mother's cooking. It was homestyle cooking at its' best.   The breakfast menu was fairly extensive and satisfied all the cravings of our group of 7. When eating breakfast at a diner, especially a country one, I always have to order a side of Biscuits & Gravy. It's the country farm boy that is still deep inside of me. I want to see how fluffy the biscuits are and how thick and creamy they make the milk gravy.   I lucked out here, because ordering the #2 - Country Inn Sampler, I got the best of everything. This hearty breakfast came with two eggs, a sampling of all three meats; bacon, sausage and ham and Hash Browns. If that wasn't enough, it also included one big biscuit smothered in Sausage milk gravy.   This ole farm boy was in hog heaven. My eggs were scrambled fluffy, the sausage patty had a peppery taste, my sampling of ham was fork tender and the bacon and hash browns were both crisp - the way I like'm. Most important, the biscuit was house made and the gravy was chuck full of sausage crumblings.   Two of the other entrees, I'll make mention of are the omelette and pancake. I joked that I can hardly finish a three egg omelet in the city and here, they boast a 4 egg. I was also impressed that they offered a whole grain pancake. It wasn't oversized, just big enough to enjoy with a side of bacon.   The ambiance is simple, it is as if you were eating in the breakfast room of a country home. The service was attentive and non-rushed. It made for a very relaxing and enjoyable meal.   If you are in the Grafton and Alton area and it is time for breakfast or lunch, give this place a try. As my cousins were confident I'd enjoy it, I'm confident you will, too.   I'll be back? - When in the area, eat as the locals do.   When: - April 29, 2018 Why: Breakfast with the cousins.

I am totally a fan of Treats Unleashed and I love this CWE location. It is such a  convenient location. It is close to some of my favorite restaurants, making it easy for me to stop by a grab a few treats for my fur-babies.   As all locations, they have an amazing selection of freshly made in house treats. In addition, they have top quality dry and canned foods for K-9's. They also have a huge selection of plush toys, that can make any dog do the zoomies with excitement.   Staff is friendly, it's obvious they love dogs. It's also nice that this location offers grooming. Dogs need a spa day, too.   I'll be back? - When I dine in the area, I'll be there.   When: December 13, 2019 Why: Treats for my Fur-Babies.

Location - Location - Location.   This Freddy's is going to make a killing. They offer a great burger and fries and are directly in front of a huge movie theatre. This is going to be a mecca for dating couples and families before taking in a flick.   I was in Creve Coeur for a dentist appointment and thought I'd stop by and see what all the buzz was about. I'll be honest, what truly tempted me and got me to stop by was seeing a picture of, Freddy's Famous Jalapeño Fry Sauce. If they offered a burger with jalapeños, I would have been in heaven.   I ordered a Freddy Original Double Combo Meal. I did mine with cheese. The bun was toasted and then topped with; mustard, onion and pickles. It came with an insanely large side of fries. The only downside of the combo was the drink - they're a Pepsi restaurant and I'm a Coke man. However, I did survive. Drinking a Diet Pepsi, did not kill me.   Their burgers are flat grilled, fairly thin with crisp edges. They're true diner burgers at their best. I'm normally not a mustard guy, but with the thin slice of white onion and dill pickles cut length wise and double cheddar cheese - this was one hell of a good burger.  The serving of fries that came with my burger was insane. If you are there as a couple, order a combo meal and a second sandwich. Trust me, there will be enough fries for the two of you. The fries are thin cut, super crisp and seasoned perfectly with salt. I enjoyed the Jalapeño Fry Sauce, but thought the word "HOT" on the label was a little misleading. For my taste, it was mild at best.   Being a fan of Onion Rings and allowing myself to be a glutton for lunch, I also ordered a small side of OR's. They did not me my standards. For me they were very bland. I'm guessing they came from a mass produced bag.   Service was fast and efficient. Order at one counter, pick-up at another, find a seat, sit down and enjoy your meal. As others have stated, it's crowded and loud, but what do you expect - it's a causal fast food diner. It's all part of the ambiance.   I'll be back? - It's a drive for me, but could be a regular stop after dentist  When: September 19, 2018 Why: Burger Lunch

I was attracted to this donut shop by all the raving 5 Star reviews.  Sorry to say, for me it's just an average donut shop that is no better then a donut from the QT.   The shop itself is cluttered, poorly organized and dingy. Everyone raved about the friendly staff, they must be off on Wednesday. The lady working this morning was surly and rather rude. There was no greeting and no thank-you. All she said, "What do you want?" and "That's 95¢"  I have too many donut shops near me to make the trek here for just an average donut and below average service. I'll pass on this donut shop, but for those who love it, I wish them well.   I'll be back? - No.   When: October 17, 2018 Why: Raving Reviews

This location use to be The Barking Lot and is now Little House of Dogs.  The original owner lost her battle against cancer, but some of the staff have kept the business going under a new name.   You are still going to receive the same high quality pet styling your had  under the TBL name. I wouldn't trust my three dogs to any other grooming shop. The entire staff here are truly pet people and pet professionals.   The building may be "little", but the service you receive is HUGE.

A while back I was shopping in E-Ville and as I was leaving a shopping plaza, I spotted Golden Oak. Being one who loves to eat breakfast out, I made a mental note to remember to come back and see what it is about. Wow, I am so glad that I did.   GOPH is simplicity at the best. The ambiance is minimalist and the food offerings are a simple straight forward breakfast and burger/sandwich and salad lunch menu.   Since it was my first visit, I went for a traditional breakfast. I enjoyed two eggs over medium, bacon, hash browns and pancakes. The fluffiness of the pancakes blew my mind. They were some of the best pancakes I have had in a while. I could not believe how thick and fluffy they were. I was served two, but one would have been enough, since I had all the other food to eat as well.  My eggs were done perfectly, which is a hard task when a diner orders over medium. The bacon was crisp and my hash browns were crispy with all specifying that in my order. The portion of food was plentiful. I was not able to clean my plate, but I was full and very satisfied.   The service was very pleasant and attentive. My server seemed to know several of the other guest around me, as regulars. When I see that, it gives the business a nice homey feeling, which is nice.   When I paid at the cashier, I complimented the manager on his staff. He was apprecitive and I told him, that I would definitely be back.   When: November 6, 2021 Why: Breakfast before shopping in E-Ville

Yes, I can already tell, Mr. Pancho's will be a regular in my Mexican restaurant rotation. Mexican food is comfort food for me, so being in a new hood after moving, I was on the hunt for Margaritas and Quesadillas.   My first visit was during COVID restrictions, so I enjoyed my experience on their spacious patio. I was quickly greeted as I entered the patio and told to select my table and they'd be right back with a menu. I distanced myself from others and the server wearing a mask came back with menu, chips and salsa. I informed him it was my first visit and I needed a Margarita.   As he fetched my Top Shelf Margarita, I glanced over the menu. When he came back, I ordered some Choir Queso. It was a spicy queso with Chorizo blended in it. Their chips were served warm and the salsa was above average, but I still would have liked a little more kick in the flavor.   I was torn, on what to order and my server gave me several recommendations. I wasn't too hungry, so I went with the Steak Quesadilla. After, chips and queso, I was getting full. However, once my quesadilla arrived, I did manage to eat half of it before requesting a to-go vessel. In STL, when you order quesadilla they slice them into manageable pieces. I've noticed on this side of the river, they serve the quesadillas in one big tortilla.   The lunch offerings look great and they have a Margarita Tower, that I have got to get friends or family to come back with me to enjoy.   The service was friendly, attentive and fast. They made me fell welcomed and encouraged me to return.   Will I be back? - A Tower has my name on it.   When? - October 8, 2020 Why? - Dinner

Places like this scare me, at the same time they are amazing to me. When you first walk in the place looks cluttered and disorganized, but then all of a sudden you realize there is a method to the madness. If you can't find what you are in need of ask one of the employees (they're all family) and they'll take you right to it.  How they know where everything is in the huge warehouse will blow your mind.   Allan C. warned you about the senor chimes welcoming you as you enter, but he forgot to tell you they are "Hello Kitty" sensors. Once she speaks in English and then the next one will be Chinese. As we walked deeper into the store there were the more traditional chimes like doorbells and each one had a different chime. It's like being a dog on a leash, they know where you are at all times. I started playing a game and I only won once. I'd let Brad walk ahead of me and see where the next chime activated, then I'd try to pass by without setting it off. They were so hidden in merchandise, that only once was I able to sneak by.   It is a restaurant supply store, but if you play "chef" at home and need hard to find "chef tools" check this place out. They also have dishes, signs and those cute little plastic baskets that your burger and fries come in at some places. If you come here to shop, keep in mind it is not Crate & Barrel or Williams-Sonoma.

JJ is still consistently a 4 Star for me. It's in my hood, but I kind of forget about them until I'm driving by. Recently they're popping up in my mind rolodex easier and I've stopped by for lunch and a couple evening pizzas.   I'm a big fan of jalapeños. I love them on a burger and really love'm on my pizza. For lunch I have stopped in to Build-A-Burger. I'll always do a Pepper Jack Cheese and add those magical jalapeños for an extra kick. I'm not wild, about the style of french fry they serve, but the burger and cold craft beer make up for them. The fries are crisp, but I'd prefer a krinkle cut or steak fry.   I've built my own pizza with Italian Sausage and of course, jalapeños. Two of my favorites off the menu are; First Date and Southside Pride.  First Date is just like one I'd build with Italian Sausage and Jalapeños, but they add; garlic and onion. It's really not a pizza for a first date, but it is mighty tasty. (Be sure to have breathe mints with you)  The Southside Pride I've enjoyed as a Double Decker. Which basically is two pizza on top of each other. I saw to gentleman enjoying one at the bar and they highly recommended it and go me hooked. Again, it has Italian Sausage with Pepperoni, Bacon, Onion and Banana Pepper.  Good mix of meat and I would have not thought of Banana Pepper on a pizza. The double decker is very heavy and very filling. I easily got three meals out of it being a single person.   I enjoy the rotating offerings of craft beers. The staff is friendly, but can get sidetracked taking care of the regulars. I'm low maintenance, so I'm okay as long as I have my pizza and cold beer.   Will I return? - I support my hood, so yes.   When: June 19, June 21, July 23 and December 1, 2017 Why: A man has got to eat.

My love - hate relationship with this store continues. I was struggling finding various decretive items for this holiday season. The pandemic has everyone getting into the spirit of things and most stores are sold out. Not Home Goods, they had me checking everything off my list and I didn't even have to check it twice. I even found things that I didn't even know I needed.   This HG use to be practically in my backyard. Now that I have moved out of the city and state of Missouri, I miss my quick trips here to find little and big treasurers to make my house a home. Now, I need to plan my trips here, but they are still well worth the travel miles and time.   If you have a new home or need to give your current one a face lift. Shop here and you'll save dollars.   Will I return? - I can guarantee it.   When: December 15, 2020 Why: Christmas Decorations

Ranch House is a dive bar with a down home comfort food kitchen.  Ranch house has been around easily 50+ years. I remember going there after a movie date in high school for a burger or as a special treat a week-end breakfast out. I wasn't a foodie back then, but I can tell you now, I give them a thumbs up for what they are.   What are they? They're a dive bar that hasn't been redecorated since the last century. They're a dive bar with friendly and attentive customer service, who welcomes everyone. While I sat at the bar, I was treated and given the same quality service as all the other guest they called by name. With the quality of food at reasonable prices, I am sure they'll know my name eventually.   Now, let's talk food. Two of my weaknesses are,  Jalapeño Burgers and Fried Chicken and they have delivered well on both. A Fried Chicken Dinner is their Wednesday night special. I enjoyed a crispy half fried chicken with two sides. I went county boy for my sides and choose, Green Beans and Mashed Potatoes with White Gravy. Whoa, the chicken was crispy and oh, so juicy. It is equally as good as Pat's Bar and Grill in STL, which was a favorite of mine before moving. My two sides were also, equally as good. Real mashed potatoes, not instant and the green beans, were perfectly seasoned with onion and bacon. I've also enjoyed the fried chicken as a carry-out.  After experiencing their winner, winner chicken dinner and seeing a Jalapeño Burger on the menu, I had to come back. The burger was a smash burger done on a flat grill, topped with Pepper Jack cheese and smothered in plenty of jalapeños. If I could add jalapeños to everything I eat, I would. The toasted bun and crispy fries as a side, completed this meal. Oh, the local craft beer was a nice touch too.   Ranch House is close to my home. I actually could walk there and burn the calories I'd be consuming eating the delicious comfort food. I will definitely be adding them to my rotation of restaurants.  When: May 12 & 20 and July 14, 2021 Why: Comfort Food

My Shelties have been coming here for years and they'll continue to come here. It doesn't matter that I have moved to IL and it is now a 45 minuet drive. I like the quality of work they do and my dogs love Cathy, their stylist. The pricing of their grooming is also, very reasonable and affordable.   In addition to Cathy, the rest of the staff that I have encountered are friendly and it is obvious they love dogs. A good way to judge a grooming salon is by the way your dog acts arriving and leaving. My two are spoiled little daddies dogs, but the do not hesitate to go with Cathy with I drop them off.   I highly recommend, Little House of Dogs to anyone who lives in Kirkwood and an area close by. Or if you're like me and don't mind the drive, you'll be pleased that you made the trip.   Oh, I too still see my STL hair stylist, so I schedule our appointments on the same day. It's our spa day in the big city.

Another great shopping day at Costco.  Was out in West County running errands and picking up a special ordered item from another retailer and thought we'd swing by for some household staples that we were out of.   The Customer Service is always top notch. It is amazing how the staff keeps a positive attitude with the volume of shoppers they handle.

Van Gogh does not get the recognition that it deserves. It not only is a great neighborhood and Martini bar, but they serve up some amazing food as well. They've been featured in the last two decks of Taste Cards, so it is an affordable way to eat out. I saved $10 on a $30 food tab.   Recently I've had two different types of chicken wings at Van Goghz. I really enjoyed the Garlic Parmesan, they were juicy and the garlic was just strong enough for flavor without being overpowering. Most recently I had the Van Gogh Style and they were dried out and lacking flavor. I know now to stay away from them and order the other styles they offer.   I have also recreated my own masterpiece from their burger menu. The chef always gets my burger grilled to the correct temperature with no problems and the seasoning accents the beef. As my side, I always go with the crinkle french fries. They get bonus points with me by serving the ketchup in a little cup.  My visit this past Sunday, they had a special burger that sounded to weird to pass up. How can you say no to, Bacon Mac-n-Cheese Burger? I couldn't resist, I had to see what it looked like and tasted like. It was a hand pressed beef patty, grilled, placed on a bun with a scoop of mac-n-cheese on top and crumbled bacon on top. Basically it was a bacon and cheeseburger with extra carbs from the pasta. They added a slice of american cheese between the burger and pasta, they should have left it off. You get enough cheese flavor from the mac-n-cheese and it would make for a better presentation as well. This time I tried tater tots and realized I'm truly a french fry man. They were good, but just not the same as a crinkle fry.   I was impressed with the flatbread my roommate ordered on Sunday. I can so see myself meeting friends here for Happy Hour, having a beer or martini and enjoying a Del Po. The Del Po had; prosciutto, caldarello sausage, onions, peppers, fresh basil and mixed Italian cheeses. Neither of us saw any fresh basil, but it was still a tasty flatbread.   The drinks and food are always good, I just gotta remember to come here more often and I hope this review inspires other to do the same.

It's time for a pizza party!    We celebrate the 12 Days of Christmas at work. We don't celebrate with a partridge in a pear tree, or twelve drummers drumming, we celebrate with lunch. On each of the 12 days leading up to the 25th, a different co-worker is responsible for bringing in lunch for the crew. On the 10th day of Christmas we had no Lords a Leaping, because we were chowing down on thin crust pizza from Cecil Whittaker's.  My co-worker ordered it up right. She started us out with; The Cecil Salad, which is a combination of fresh Iceberg lettuce, ripe olives, red onions, Provel and Romano cheeses, all tossed in their house dressing. Also a St. Louis pizza party would not be complete without a big pan of; Toasted Ravioli, served with meat sauce and grated Romano cheese. Everyone loved the toasted ravioli, the big pan disappeared quickly.   In addition to the salad & ravioli, we shared 10 large pizza. My personal favorite was a toss up between the bacon and pepperoni. Of course, being a local pizzeria, the cheese on their pizzas is Provel. It's an acquired taste and it works well with Cecil's sauce and toppings. Our toppings ranged from; sausage, bacon, pepperoni, hamburger, cheese and veggie. We had it all. We even had enough left-overs, that some of enjoyed cold pizza for breakfast the next morning.   The delivery girl was friendly and assisted in sitting everything up for our luncheon. It's been awhile since I ordered from my hoods Cecil, if it is as good as this one - I'm going to be ordering from home soon. This was one good pizza party.   When: December 22, 2016 Why: 12 Days of Christmas Luncheon at work

There is nothing Pint Size about this new bakery on Watson except their size. The flavor of thier baked goods is totally HUGE. Today I taste tested their scones, brownies and cookies and all three of them should have near by coffee shops and bakeries shaking in their chef hats.   I love scones, the one I tried today was a savory Asiago Cheese and Artichoke. This scone had a perfect light crunch outer crust and the most moist inside I have ever seen in scone. It would be a perfect accompliment to a salad, chili or bowl of soup. I enjoyed mine with a nice cold glass of milk at home and was totally satisfied.   A must for everyone to try is the Cranberry Crunch cookie, it has potato chips in it and taste fabulous. I think I'm going to go get another one after writting this review.   My brownie today was the Blondie,  which was the first to disapper from my plate.  That alone should tell how good it was.   They serve Kaldi's coffee, are closed Sunday and Monday. The staff is super friendly and if you get to meet Christy the owner and baker, you'll love her.  I am so glad they are in my hood and within walking distance. They have a Loyalty Card that can get you $5 of free baked goods. Everytime you spend $5, they'll punch your card and once you have 10 punches, you get the $5 free. I plan on filling my card up very soon.   Pint Size Bakery is a great addition to my hood.

When it comes to greasy, old fashioned diners in the Saint Louis area, Courtesy Diner on Kingshighway is by far the best. This original location is even head and shoulders above its' more modern sister location on Hampton. Nothing beats a cast iron grill.   It was a simple breakfast before heading over to Home Depot. We started with an order of Biscuits and Gravy. Our waitress was great, she suggested having the B&G's as an appetizer. How cleaver, normally when we share an order, it comes out with full breakfast. She even separated our full order on to two small plates. Great customer service! She was working that counter and other booths as if she were Tony Bommarito schmoozing folks at Tony's.   We both ended up ordering the same thing; two eggs over easy, hash browns and sausage patties. Eggs fried to perfection, peppery sausage and extra crispy hash browns made a fulfilling breakfast. Like Patt C., we saw the poster for Frito Pie and are planning to return for lunch.   As stated earlier, our waitress was friendly and she also provided top notch service. The cook even delivered our food, when she was busy with another table. Their team work, was impressive.

It was time to bring a busy day, to an end and we wanted to relax, nosh and drink. We thought it would be a great time to try Retreat Gastropub. Being a Sunday night, it wasn't very busy when we arrived, but the hostess was sitting everyone next to each other. She placed us in a corner deuce. We felt cramped and the table next to us was having an intense conversation, so we opted to move to the bar for more comfort.   Once seated at the bar, I ordered a Manhattan and my friend had a Southside. My friend enjoyed her Southside, but I must say the Manhattan was the worst one I have ever had. I couldn't wait to finish it, so I could order a Paloma which they did well.   We grazed through our small plates, ordering them one or two at a time. Brussels Sprouts is a favorite vegetable for the two of us, so we knew we had to start with them. Undercooked and minimal flavor. Next we moved on to chicken wings and fries. Both of these got thumbs up from both of us. I preferred the parmesan aioli over the smoked tomato sauce served with the fries.  The chicken wings were deep fried and we choose the garlic herb butter over buffalo sauce and I recommend that you do the same.   The night ended with Candied Bacon and Pork Toasts. You really can't go wrong with crispy bread, goat cheese (my favorite), braised pork and micro greens. I'll order this again, but I'll have them hold the micro greens, they just didn't add flavor to the toast for me. The Candied Bacon was a big yawn and proved to us that ordering the bacon dish is not always a good choice.   The atmosphere is casual and relaxing, a little loud, but you're still able to have a conversation with ease. I want to come back and hopefully raise my rating once I try the Mac-n-Cheese, burger or veggie sandwich. Also, instead of a house cocktail, next time I'll enjoy a cold craft beer.   When: November 8, 2015 Why: Dinner

Some my say that Lafayette Park is the Red Headed step-child to Forest Park, but it is not. It is the petite and prettier little sister. It is also proof that size does not matter. It may be smaller, but it has all the amenities and beauty of FB without all the traffic congestion of the tourist attractions.   It is a great park to stroll before or after enjoying dinner at one of the many restaurants on Park Avenue. Also, it's a paradise for a photographer. That is why you see so many weddings being photographed within the well manicured grounds. I'd say don't stop with weddings, do your engagement, senior and family portraits as well. Heck, bring you camera or smartphone and take a couple of cool pictures of just the natural beauty and landscaping.   We are so lucky to have so many beautiful and well maintained parks in Saint Louis.  Get out and enjoy them today.

I dine out alone a lot and have a habit of just showing up at some of the most popular restaurants without a reservation. I do this because, I don't mind being seated at the bar. Normally it is a win-win situation. For the restaurant, I don't tie up a table and for me, I'm still able to enjoy a fabulous meal.   When I showed up at Meauxbar, I was surprised how small it was and got a little worried that my normal plan may not work. However, the host was very accommodating. He had a two top table available and wouldn't need it till 8:30 PM for a reservation. That gave me one hour and forty-five minutes - that is more then enough time for me.   Prior to my arrival, I had studied the menu and knew what I wanted. I started off with a "snack" of; Brussels Sprout Pan Roast. These small sized sprouts were done perfectly. They were soft, but yet had a snap, crunch to them for freshness. Sprouts are my #2 favorite veggie so I order them when ever they are offered on a menu. These were the absolute best that I had in New Orleans.   My large plate was the, Hanger Steak Au Poivre with Parmesan Frites. The steak was tender and prepared to requested temp. It also was seasoned perfectly, allowing the natural flavor of the steak to shine. My frites were thin, crisp and had fresh shavings of Parmesan on top. No ketchup was needed for these frites. The combination of this hanger steak and frites made for an exquisite meal.   I had no room for dessert, I was stuffed. I finished in plenty of time and thanked the host for making room for me. My server was delightful and the bartender allowed me to charge my phone behind the bar. Top-notch customer service all around. I loved Meauxbar.   When: August 27, 2016 Why: Dinner

I'll admit my dogs are spoiled, very spoiled. They are my children and I take very good care of them.  I watch their diets very closely and would never feed them a dog food I could buy a grocery store. TU carries some of the best dog foods available, many of them are highly recommended by Whole Dog Journal.  The staff is very knowledgeable in all the foods and can recommend for your dog based on its health, age and size. However, lets not forget about the freshly baked treats, after all "treats" is in their name. My dogs love all flavors of the Soft Bites, and Peanut Butter Barkers too. (Next door is a Fannie Mae so you can get a treat for yourself.)

I cannot believe I drove all the way to Clayton for a doughnut when I have countless donut shops near my home in the city. I was motivated by VVD being listed on Ian Froeb's STL 100 for 2016 and the announcement that they are coming to The Grove.   Vinnie, is okay that I call you Vinnie or do you prefer Vincent? Either way, I was an instant fan when I entered the shop. I almost wept for joy when I saw your two huge bowls of doughnut holes. In the city, I requested them once in the city at WFD and the lady behind the counter replied in disgust, "We don't do donut holes." She said it as if were a bad thing. So I am glad to see that you go beyond your artistic talents and snobby location and still offer a good ole fashion hole.   Holes are actually my favorite doughnut. I know they are simply made, but I like the bite size. It allows me to satisfy my doughnut cravings. Do you ever do them in a chocolate glaze? That would be nice, if you do or could do.   My other doughnut was the Grand Marnier with Orange Swirl. Nice. It wasn't overly sweet and had just the perfect amount of icing. I was tempted to get the Vanilla Glazed Doughnut that Ian recommended in the paper, but how could I pass up a doughnut made with my favorite after dinner liquor.   Another big bonus point is that you do not serve Kaldi's coffee. Nothing against Kaldi's, but it is everywhere in STL. It was good seeing that you are proud to serve, Sump Coffee. It was delicious with my doughnuts.   Can't wait to see you in The Grove.   In closing, I am also glad to see you spell "doughnuts" the correct way.....LOL  When: June 22, 2016 Why: Breakfast & Ian Froeb's STL 100

Kelly B has the right idea, "Get the bread" and she is right about loving it.  My advice is shop early, get fresh. Their bread is their best seller.   I've tried the Parsley, Dill and Rosemary and it made great sandwiches with turkey and bacon. Going back to try the Hot Pepper & Parmesan and gotta get me some Irish Soda Bread.   Tried the mini chocolate chip cookies and was disappointed. They looked so cute in the case, but lacked in flavor. I also tried a Red Velvet Cupcake, moist and good flavor. However, it's appearance was lacking. I think places like The Cup and Jilly's have spoiled us on cupcakes.   Parking can be a pain, but I just park at the empty business next door and walk over.   I want them to succeed, so I will be back for bread and promise to be open to trying other pastry items.

Love this place!! I have had a couple of lunches and Sunday Brunch and all have been excellent. The staff is extremely friendly and attentive. Their service makes you feel as if you are at a friends home.  Sunday Brunch is a bargain at it's price which includes your first Bloody Mary or Mimosa. A huge variety of food which makes it hard to decide where to start and when to say stop. The Nachos are better then any Mexican restaurant, the ribs are a notch above Pappy's  and the chicken wings are crispy and offer a different twist to the typical restaurant wing. Love the Patty Melt when offered as a daily special. My only nay, is the Cuban sandwich is a little over done and dry. Visit this place, you'll love it!

II am not sure if it was the prayers to the Shopping Cart Gods or if it was the coin I tossed into the Wishing Well, but Schnucks finally has gotten new shopping carts.   We shop like New Yorkers, only buying for one or two meals at a time. So those big bulky carts are way to big and those plastic hand held baskets are way to small. As Goldilocks would say, "These two tier small shopping carts are just right".   Thanks Schnucks for making my shopping experience easier and more enjoyable by offering a shopping cart that meets my needs.

If you are a knowledgeable wine drinker, do not shop here. This wine shop caters primarly  to inexperienced young women who are drawn to "cute labels" and no substance.  Their selection of quality wines is small and limited. You are better off shopping at another local wine store where your selection of "good" wines are a smorgasbord.  It's a shame that a prime location and presentation are wasted on such a selection of wines.

Big disappointment. I try to use local businesses and those near my home to keep our neighborhood strong. However, when I tried to purchase a full set of tires at Auto TIre their customer service went flat. I wanted to use AT, because I could walk back home & be productive. Who wants to sit in a tire store waiting area?  When I stopped by, they informed me they'd have to order my tires. That was no problem, I could come back easily. I told them my next day off and they assured me they'd have the tires. When I arrived on the scheduled date, a manager with the look of a deer in your headlights informed me he forgot to order my tires. Being a busy professional like most of us, I took my business elsewhere that day. They lost a $700 sale.  I do give them an extra star for being totally honest.

Three Monkeys has gotten three strikes and they are no longer a favorite place to visit. I do not know what has happened, but they need to fix it and fix it fast. The problem is not front of the house, they still have some of the friendliest and best service in town. The problem is in the kitchen, they are not up to the quality they once were. Did they change Executive Chefs?
