We  had a carry-out that was a BIG disappointment, during a birthday celebration with multiple friends we had entrees sent back and then the final was a Sunday Brunch that had us walking out saying, "WTF happened here?" Please fix the problem, I want to be a fan again.

I recently bought new accent tables for my living room, that had tops made with natural tile blocks. I loved the look they provided, but wanted to protect the tiles with glass tops. I knew I needed to protect those beautiful tiles from pesky cocktails rings.  Immediately I thought of Kirkwood Glass, because they had done a great job rehanging my huge bathroom mirror when it became detached from the wall. Ordering the table tops was easy and within a week they were ready for me to pick-up. Now I can entertain, serve cocktails and not worry about my beautiful titles being ruined.   Jocelyn at the store when I ordered my table tops and Adam who came out to my house to hang the mirror, both were extremely friendly and professional. If I ever need a windshield replaced, I will consider them for this service as well.

The Top Ten Reasons to Love Carl's Drive-In  10. Fries and Onion Rings from a bag. 9.  Soft Grilled Buns. 8.  Counter Seating Only - Small & Cozy 7.  Biodegradable China 6.  Prompt Service with Attitude 5.  Nostalgic Ambiance 4.  Milkshakes in only two flavors 3.  Foot long Hot Dogs 2.  House-made Root Beer in Frosted Mugs  And the number 1 Reason:  The Best Flat Grilled Burgers in Saint Louis!!!

This Walgreens was my bank on a recent trip to NOL. I don't know about you, but I hate paying ATM fees. This Walgreens was not only in the French Quarter, but was conveniently located close to my hotel. I normally card everything, but at times it's nice to just have some cash in your pocket. So I'd come here make a small purchase of something I "really" needed and got cash back, avoiding those ATM fees that I hate so much.   Being in located in the French Quarter gave this Walgreens some extra personality. It definitely was an older store with wear and tear, but that was part of its' charm. It felt cluttered and cramped, but that could only be that they were providing as much merchandise as a normal sized Walgreens.  I always found what I needed and it was at a normal price, not jacked up due to the location that caters to a lot of tourist.   The staff was as colorful in personality as you'd expect of a French Quarter store. They were charming and helpful as you'd expect in the deep south.   Would I go back?  When I'm in town, I'll be there.   When: August 26-29, 2016 Why: Vacation & Hate ATM Fees

Just a few blocks away from the busy Delmar Loop, you will find a BBQ place that will excite your taste buds. It is located at the corner of Kingsland and Vernon in a renovated gas station, that now serves up some of the best Baby Back Ribs, Smoked Chicken Wings and Hot Italian Sausage. In addition to the BBQ classics; Pulled Pork, Brisket and Turkey Breast, they offer Smoked Tofu for all of our vegetarian friends.    I've done both, dined in and carryout and each meal was a winner. The Baby Back Ribs are always a must for my order.  We'll either have a full rack with a couple of sides. Or enjoy a half rack with some Smoked Chicken Wings and a couple of sides. Either way, our tummies are always satisfied when we are done eating.   The chicken wings are on the plus size, which is always a bonus. They're served as one big piece, no drummies and wingettes here, you'll be eating your wings like a real man. The Baby Back Ribs, will have you saying, "Oh, Baby Oh, Baby". Their dry rub is so good you will not need to add one of their 5 sauces. However, if do want to add a sauce, my personal favorite is the Tai-B-Q or XXX.  BBQ is only as good as the sides that accompany it and the sides at Vernon's do not disappoint. For the low-carb eaters, I highly recommend the Tequila Lime Green Beans. If Green Beans are not your favorite vegetable, they will be after you enjoy these. My dining partner swears the Red Beans and Rice are the best he has ever had and he is old and traveled extensively. Aunt Jan's Burnt End Beans has me wishing she was my Aunt so I could steal the recipe. Be alert when ordering and watch for daily specials, I once had some amazing Collard Greens that had me fantasizing that I was in the deep south.   Speaking of the deep south, the hospitality and customer service is so friendly, you'll feel right at home. Keep in mind the restaurant in located on a street named "Vernon, it is not the name of the owner. All employees wear shirts with the name, Vernon embroidered upon it. So when you say, "Hey, Vern" a half dozen heads will turn your way.

Give me the keys to the bulldozer, I'll drive. This shopping mecca should have been leveled years ago. There is no reason to come here, unless you are a "mall walker".   How Sears survives is beyond me.   Amanda Z., I don't think Ikea could even bring this place back to life, it is dead.

I thank my lucky stars that I only  shop at a Toys R Us two times a year.  Once for the birthday of the  little girl next door and then again at Christmas. These two times are enough, if I had to do it a third time I think I may have to commit myself to a mental hospital. Seriously, it's not that bad.   They have a huge selection of toys, after all their name is Toys R Us.  I mainly focus on the Barbie section, a new doll and several outfits. Finding the Barbie section is hell, but as I search for it I am amazed at all the other toys and the variety of themes that I come across as I hunt that bitch down.   What drives me crazy is that their aisles are like a maze, they go every direction imaginable. They'll go vertical, then they'll switch to short horizontal aisles. The store is huge, so it does make sense to switch it up, because those would be some long aisles.   Once I find the bitch who has everything, I make my selections and head to the cashier. The staff here are a bunch of big kids and that is a good thing. They are friendly and truly seem to be having fun while at work.

This nursery is within walking distance from my home which is good and bad. The good is that it is convenient to shop. The bad is, sometimes I never finish my walk because I stop to browse the plant, end up shopping and have to go back home and get the CRV to retrieve the new purchases.   My thumb is not as green as most would think from looking at my yard. I have a lot of support from many local nurseries and Michelle here at Bayer's has been a great help this year.  We have eight scones on our fence in the backyard and each year we change it up for variety. After so many years, our own creativity has fizzled out and we needed help. We explained to Michelle where our scones were located, amount of sunlight they have and we even threw in my favorite color - which happens to be orange. In less then a blink of an eye, she knew what to create.   She guided us through the selection of flowers that could handle direct sunlight and made sure some of them were "orange". To give the sconce variety, we have height from grass and dramatic draping of vines on each end. I've posted a picture so you can see how great it looks. Our neighbors love it almost as much as we do.   It is so good to have a great garden nursery in our neighborhood that we can trust. Even if Lindenwood is not your hood, Bayer is worth the drive. The entire staff is always friendly and helpful. Michelle is our favorite because of her great "eye" and ideas, but we're welling to share.

It's not the New York store. It's not even like the Michigan Avenue store in Chicago. However,  we do have a Tiffany's  in St Louis and it lives up to the experience. The selection of sterling silver jewelry is classic & fashionable for both women and men. They offer a large variety of price points so everyone can find a bobble within their budget.  As for diamonds, you will not find more sparkle for your $. The sales professionals are truly professional. They'll educate you on the importance of the 4 C's. Bigger is not always better, you've got to take the color, clarity and cut into consideration.  Two other categories you need to check out are the pearls and watches. Every woman needs pearls & not Barbara Bush pearls. A classic single strand or a 60" strand that can be looped for a strong fashion statement.  As stated in my profile I'm a watchaholic and love my two Tiffany watches. Everyone deserves a gift in a Blue Box.

How is it that a place that is known for it's burgers, puts out a better salad? We went yesterday for lunch and were surprised that Brad's salad was better then my burger.   We started out with their Towering Onion Rings, which were awesome. They're huge, crispy on the outside and a fresh ring of onion on the inside. I dipped mine in the Tangy Campfire Sauce and Brad preferred good ole ketchup. The TCS had a good soft kick to it and if it were available in a bottle you'd find it in my ice box.   Our lunches were the Red Robin Gourmet Cheeseburger and the Crispy Chicken Tender Salad. I love that the burgers come with bottomless steak fries, but can not imagine anyone ordering more. When I declined more fries, I asked the server if anyone ever orders more and she said it was rare. Still it is a nice marketing tool and gesture.   Brad's salad was huge. It was a nice mix of greens with hard boiled eggs, tomatoes, cheddar cheese and applewood smoked bacon. What made it stand out above other Crispy Chicken Salads was the fact that the bacon is fresh and not Baco Bit's. He choose a Honey Mustard Poppyseed dressing. I'm not a Honey Mustard guy, but his being mixed with Poppyseed gave HM a new twist that I liked.   Loved my Steak Fries, but the burger was a disappointment. Great bun, plenty of toppings, but it had me using the classic line, "where's the beef". A place that is suppose to be known for it's burgers, I'd expect a big beefy patty hand pressed instead of a thinly machine shaped burger. My burger was totally hidden in all the toppings. I could hardly taste the meat.  Our lunch beverage of choice was ice tea and after a couple ice teas I need to use the restroom. I'll be honest, I really wanted to see if they had Dyson Airblades. They didn't have Dyson, but they had televisions hanging from the ceiling and positioned towards the stalls.  I'm surprised sports bars have not thought of this. A man can sit on the porcelain throne and not miss a play in the game.   Our server was cute, sweet and friendly.

Great Margaritas - watch out they have a delayed kick.....lol. Love the Chicken Nachos and the salsa has a good flavor too. Combination plates offer good variety. Portions are good, at times I can not clean my plate. Decor is tacky at best, but you're there for good inexpensive tex-mex not ambiance.  Staff is friendly and offer table service as a team.

I have boosted before that Pint Size Bakery has the best scones in Saint Louis and this morning they once again proved me right.  My savory scone this morning was Sweet Potato Bacon, what a winning combination. Then the sweet scone made me weak in knees it was so good. The apple and caramel made me feel like I was eating a slice of apple pie for breakfast. Both were so good, they made me wish I were not sharing them and had the entire scone to myself.   If you have not experienced Pint Size Bakery yet, you need to get yourself there now and try their scones. You can also try their; cookies, brownies, muffins, cupcakes and more. Whatever you enjoy, you'll be back for more.

I have always loved this bookstore, the selection is overwhelming. I love the fact that they open at 11 AM. on Sunday. It makes for a great shopping experience after breakfast. You'll always find a good read for a lazy afternoon.   I think one of my good traits is that when I'm dumb, I can openly admit it. In fact, sometimes it gives me a good laugh and that happened Sunday when I visited Left Bank Books. I had no idea there was an entire lower level of used books. I was amazed at the variety of selection and quantity. Next time I'm in a store and see a staircase, I'm taking the adventure and following the steps to see where they lead me.   Cat allergy alert - they have a house cat who is very friendly and loving.

I can get spoiled shopping @ Culinaria. Downtown dwellers have it so good. If I lived closer, this would be my grocer of choice.   I work downtown, so this is a great place to pick-up lunch/dinner from their prepared foods section. I love the way the staff sell and describe the daily offerings. They do it as if they were waiters at a trendy cafe.   I've also gone in and picked up some non-perishable items on my lunch hour and have drooled over the extra selection of items available to the Culinaria stores. It still isn't Whole Foods, but damn close.   The staff is friendly, almost beyond believable. They must have selected the best of all their stores and transfered them to this location.

Color me surprised and use the color orange. It has been eons  since I used a taxi in the city of Saint Louis. I normally only use cabs when I am in Chicago or some other major city.  So I needed a ride earlier this week and called Laclede and they impressed me with an A-Game.   It was a simple ride from the Lindenwood neighborhood to The Gateway Station downtown. The dispatcher who answered the phone was pleasant and cheerful. She assured me the wait time would not be long and it was under 15 minuets. When the cab arrived at my home, it looked as if it had been freshly detailed. Not only was the car clean on the outside, but the inside was pristine.   My driver was  articulate, making small talk on the short trip pleasant. We shared a chuckle when I got in and stated "Gateway Station" as my location. He responded, "bus station?" and I in turn said, "train station, it is all the same." Nobody calls it by the correct name, typical Saint Louis. However, being a good driver, he knew where I wanted to go.   So many times when in a Chicago cab, it is like riding an amusement park ride and you exit with white knuckles.  Not on this trip, my driver would get the safe driver discount from All State. Also, he was as clean as his cab. His white shirt was pressed and starched for  going to church.   In my hometown I normally do not have a need for a cab, but when I do my new assisant Siri will be calling Laclede.

Lee's may be a chain, but they offer up some good friend chicken. My favorite is their crispy and I always order the Breast Meal. It includes one very large breast, with a biscuit and as my sides  I choose mashed potatoes with brown gravy (they give you a choice here) and cole slaw.  For a beverage,  I always go with their Sweet Iced Tea. It is done in a true Southern style.   My advice to you is do not turn your nose up at Lee's because it is a chain. Give them a chance, they do chicken right. This location is always extremely clean and the staff is courteous and friendly.  I never do fried chicken at home, it is the one meal I always let someone else make.

I've wanted to try this place for awhile, but have been hesitant  due to some comments I've heard and read. I must have visited on a good day, or they've gotten their act  together. We we're greeted soon as we entered, seated promptly and our server magically appeared.  The menu is a simple read, it offers American Comfort Food for all three meals. Keep in mind American Comfort Food is aka "fried food".   Our breakfast  started out with Bloody Mary's, it's our Sunday morning ritual.  My other half had a heart stopping breakfast (The Sloppy Fireman) that was to die for. Seriously my arteries hardened just looking at it. The masterpiece was 2 eggs, ham, sausage, bacon, green pepper, onion on 2 biscuits, topped with sausage gravy & mixed cheese.  He swears it is his new favorite breakfast. His side of Home Fries, were better then my hash-browns.   I'm trying to ease myself into a  New Year's Resolution of healthier eating and ordered "The Medic". It was a perfect omelet. It was filled with spinach, tomato, green pepper, onion, black olive and mushrooms. I was amazed at the eggs texture and how the omelet was folded picture perfect. My hash-browns were crispy, but I needed to add salt which is unusual for me.   The service was fair at best, but got the job done. It was a simple breakfast, I don't need white linen hovering service.  We'll go back for lunch or dinner, we want to try the ribs.

I love my watches from Tiffany's and it was time for one of them to get a new battery. Taking your watch in for maintenance can be dangerous, because it gives you time to browse and browsing can lead to shopping. This time I discovered some new crystal pieces that I want personally and others that will be great for upcoming weddings. A Blue Tiffany Box with that White Tiffany Bow on a bridal gift table, makes a statement and gets noticed by all.   Besides weddings, I also use Tiffany's for baby gifts. Why not help your friends child be born with that silver spoon. I also help them start saving for their first Tiffany purchase with a bone china piggy bank in blue or pink.   My watch is being sent to the mother ship in New York, to have it's battery changed and to be cleaned as well. When it comes back to the Lou, I'll be able to do some more browsing and shopping when I go to pick it up.   The customer service and sales professionals here are always top notch. They are the high standards which you'd expect from the brand Tiffany's.

We were in West County running errands and it was lunch time. A burger, endless fries and a tower of onion rings sounded like a good deal. Allison had mentioned a free burger for birthdays on the talk thread and I wanted to get signed up for my next bd. We all like free things, especially when it is food.   Our lunch began with a Tower of Onion Rings. The tower is 13 rings tall and there is nothing unlucky about this #13. These rings are sweet yellow onion, breaded & crisply fried. They offer two sauces, tangy campfire and ranch.  We both preferred the tangy campfire over the ranch. It just offered a move flavorful kick.   I've recently developed a fondness for Jalapenos and when I saw the Burnin' Love burger, I knew my name was grilled on it. Visualize a big Red Robin burger seasoned with cayenne, topped with crispy fried jalapeno coins, tangy salsa and pepper jack cheese. In addition they add a couple traditional burger toppings of lettuce and tomato. Then it is all served on a Jalapeno Cornmeal Kaiser Roll with a smear of chipotle aioli. Of course it was served with those endless steak fries.  The SO enjoyed his Whiskey River BBQ Burger which is basted in their bourbon-infused Whiskey River BBQ sauce, then topped with cheddar cheese and onion straws. Like my Burnin Love, they also added lettuce and tomato. All of this served between a Sesame Seed bun with a dab of mayo.   As we enjoyed our burgers, I was busy using my smart phone to sign up for their Red Royalty rewards program. Lucky me, I didn't have to wait till next year for my birthday burger. When they swiped my card to activate it, it rewarded me with my burger and my birthday was earlier this month.   For a chain, Red Robin gets a thumbs up. Good burgers, Very good Onion Rings and endless Steak Fries (I never order more) and good customer service. Not to mention their boozy milk shakes. I always come during the week for lunch to avoid the load noise made by kids who frequent this place.

Fresh, warm, soft and delicious. Better yet, they'll deliver these scrumptious cookies to your work or residence. Reward your staff for a job well done, or chase the blues away at home with a box (eco-friendly) of these insanely delicious cookies.   Their traditional flavors; Chocolate Chunk, M&M, Sugar and Peanut Butter Chip are only the beginning. More traditional flavors like, White Chocolate Macadamia Nut and Oatmeal Raisin will have you coming back for more. Do I dare tell you about my favorite Deluxe Flavor - Chocolate Peanut Butter Cup? Give me a gallon of milk and a dozen of these and I'll be doing a happy dance.   Great location on Washington, but you're to close to my work - be gone satan. However, I do love you. It guess without saying, I'll be back and so will all of my co-workers. Customer service has always been spot on, glad I didn't have the trouble Kate did.   When: November 25, 2016 Why: I am a Cookie Monster

Oysters, mussels and wine make for a perfect evening. Add fabulous ambiance and attentive service, you've created DeMun Oyster Bar. It is the perfect place for a romantic evening of two or a fun place for a group of friends. Our recent visit was the latter, a group of friends and we had a blast. Our server was so attentive to our needs, he made each of feel as if we were royalty.   Words can not begin to explain how luscious our food was. After 3 different oysters, I would be hard pressed to say which one was my favorite. I might even have to say, I liked the steamed mussels or poached salmon better. Not to mention the Pomme Frites and the Sweet Chips we munched on as well. Oh, I can not forget the Beignets we used to soak up the incredible broth from the steamed mussels.  It was a night to remember, even after three bottles of wine.   If you're an Oyster lover, treat yourself soon to the magic of DeMun Oyster Bar.

I've always been a fan of TU, as stated in my previous review. They carry the best of the premium dog foods and this weekend they saved my ass. I shop local and try to support businesses within my "hood".  However, my usual dog food store got shorted on my brand and size and I was disparate. I quickly called TU and they had Now Senior in stock and I was a happy dog daddy.   When I arrived, it was great to see they held my bag behind the counter. My dogs not only got the premium food they enjoy, but bags of wheat free treats as well. If your dog has wheat allergies, come here for treats.   The customer service is always great, they're friendly and true dog lovers.

Five Below is the Neiman - Marcus of dollar stores, but you'll find no Needless - Markup here.  The prices on some items may be 5 times as much as the dollar store, but just like Neiman - Marcus, you're getting a better quality for your $.   On my most recent visit, I learned that several of the brands available at Five Below are exclusive. Just like the warehouse clubs, FB has created their own products to pass savings on to their shoppers and here you do not need to have a membership card to save.    This shopping visit was all about my New Years Resolution to live a healthier lifestyle. I remembered seeing Yoga mats on my last visit, so I came back to get one for the class I am starting. The mat is very comparable to others I've looked at for $20-$25 and I only paid $5. I was also able to get a Yoga block for only $4.   I also found some very functional and practical containers for packing lunches. Now I have no excuse not to pack a healthy lunch. It will stop me going out for fast food.  Another goodie I found was a small cookbook called 100 Healthy Foods.  Logically it listed 100 healthy foods and then gave you a healthy recipe to enjoy them.   I avoided the temptation of their huge candy department. The cashier even commented on my strength. She saw me circling the display, with the eyes of a child.  If you're headed to the movies, I do recommend you come here and buy your movie treats and sneak them into the theater.   When I shop here, I shop like I do at Bath and Body Works and that is with no basket. That way, when I can not hold or carry any more items to buy I know it is time to stop shopping and check out fast.

Major Kudos to Schnucks for being Proactive and having their store appropriately staffed for all the snow storm shoppers. I was shocked to see every check out lane open and each one had their own bagger. The check out process was smooth, easy and the cashiers kept a positive attitude. Which was amazing, lines for each check out wined down the closest aisle of items.   Also, a big shout out to my fellow city residents. You were all in good spirits, you were not fighting over something meaningless or being bitchy about the approaching storm.   This is my closest Schnucks to home and I'll admit at times I get frustrated with them, but today you had an A-Game.  Today I would have given them a 5 star if they still had rock salt while I was shopping. Shame they had to lose a star over salt.

One of my favorite places to buy dog bowls. Why pay the high prices at a doggie boutique when you can find bowls just as cute and functional at TJ Maxx at a fraction of the cost.   TJ is also a great place to find colorful socks and pocket squares. Again, why pay the high prices at a regular retail store when you can find them here at a majorly reduced price. Shirts and pants, I've never had much luck here, but I keep looking hoping some day I'll find a keeper.   Another area, I always check out is the kitchen accessories. You can always find a new gadget or gizmo for the kitchen. I already have a great set of pots and pans, but here I can always find a little sauce pan or a specialty pan at a great price. Seriously, who cares if it doesn't match my main set of pots? I'm just using it for cooking and keeping it shut up in a cabinet or drawer when it's not being used.   If you're in the area, TJ Maxx is always worth a quick walk through. You'll never know what you'll find.   When: March 7, 2016 Why: Replacing a broken dog bowl

Congratulations Autotire, you are off my Terrible Two's List.   One of the tires on my roommates CRV kept needing air added to it. When adding air the last time he noticed the culprit, a nail. He was adding air at U Gas, so he just drove over to Autotire which is close to our home.   The current staff was friendly and professional. Living close, he just dropped the car off to have the tire patched. They called later, to let him know the nail was too close to the sidewall to be patched. He bought a new tire and got an alignment. With the alignment, he claims his ride is riding better then when he bought it.   Thanks, Floyd and Bill for the good customer service and making my Terrible Two's List shorter.   When: 13 JAN 2014 Why: Fix a flat tire

This place is a friends favorite restaurant so we took her there for a birthday celebration - a group of ten. The service was great, they made her and our group feel special. However, I can not say the same for the food. Every entree was poorly presented and looked bland. The rest of us chatted after the dinner, except for the honoree, no one in our group was impressed.

Best way to describe Walnut Grill is an upscale sports bar. They have 30 beers on draft and there is not a seat in the restaurant that does not provide you with a good view of a television. If you are a sports buff and need a place to watch the big game, with good food and an amazing selection of beer, check out WG.   WG is a great addition to the Sunset Hills neighborhood and is way better then the Ruby Tuesday that use to occupy the same space. I've been twice, once for dinner and another time for lunch. Both meals were totally different and satisfying. I'm looking forward to going back and experiencing the most important meal of the day, breakfast.   When I went for dinner, a friend joined me for their soft opening. As with any soft opening I have attended, there were a few bumps in the service, but the food was spot on. Both of are lovers of Brussels Sprouts and we were totally blown away with the Flash Fried Brussels Sprouts. They were so flavorful being dusted with candied walnuts and tossed with Gorgonzola cheese and a balsamic reduction. Yummy in the tummy.   I had the New York Strip Steak, which was tender and cooked to my temperature of medium rare. However, I think my friend had the best entree. She enjoyed, Walnut Salmon. It was; Pan seared, with a walnut crust and orange marmalade. She loved it.  I'm not a fan of Walnuts, but after sampling it, I too thought it was the bomb. I may order it the next time I go for dinner.   Four days later, I returned for lunch. This time I went for true sports bar food. Of course I started out with a local craft beer, O'Fallon Brewery Pumpkin Ale.  I also begun my lunch with an order of Chef Mike's Dry Rub Chicken Wings.  They were crispy and spicy. I prefer a dry rub over a traditional sauce on wings and this one is one of the best I have had. The seasoning, had just enough tang and a little spicy burn for that extra kick. The beer was the perfect, accompaniment for the wings.   After my wings, I ordered a Classic Cheeseburger with Pepper Jack Cheese and Fries. Since my beer glass was empty, I decided to be adventurous and try one of their Bloody Mary's. If you come here for brunch or breakfast, this Bloody is a must order. It is strong and one of the spiciest I've had in awhile. I'd say it is definitely  in my top 3 Bloody Mary's in STL.   The burger is ground steak and topped with your choice of cheese. I don't know how many cheeses they offer, because I stopped my server once I heard, Pepper Jack. PJ is my favorite cheese for a burger. The burger was flame grilled and the seasoning made it a memorable burger. For me, they got bonus points for serving ketchup in a little cup. That is how I like my ketchup served - I despise ketchup bottles in a restaurant.   On both visits, the service was attentive and friendly. Yes, there were a few bumps, but they were minor and truly not worth mentioning. As with any new restaurant, in time they'll be worked out and everything will be smooth.   Will I return? Yes, I want to experience their "Happier Hour" from 3-7 PM  When: October 13 & 17, 2017 Why: Dinner & Lunch

Not really a mall shopper, but I am slowly becoming a fan of this mall. I use to be a die hard Galleria fan, but in my eyes the Big G is on a down slide. WCC is a nicer mall to stroll through and the maintenance crew keeps it much cleaner then the  G.   WCC offers me the stores I like and better dining options (nonfood court). I've also noticed that the stores I shop, the staff is more customer focused and lack the attitude of the G staff. The Macy's at WCC seems to offer a larger selection in the Men's Dept, especially Ralph Lauren.  Wish they had a J Crew, but that is okay. Gives me a reason to go shop at Plaza Frontenac, since that is my favorite Crew.   The biggest negative of WCC is the parking. The problem is not the amount of parking, there is plenty. It is the fact that other shoppers do not follow the direction of the arrows painted on the pavement of each aisle. My last visit, a lady zipped up an aisle going the wrong way to beat me to an available space as I approached and it wasn't even the holiday season when spaces are prime. This isn't the only time I have witnessed crazy parking, I have just come to expect it here at WCC.

I've found another place to add to my breakfast out rotation and this one is a healthy choice.   I meet Ms Norma here for a late breakfast the other day and was totally impressed. We arrived right at the cut off for breakfast, so next time I'll know to get there earlier. The selection of breakfast entrees isn't as large as diner or a restaurant that specializes in breakfast, but you'll still have a hard time selecting what to order. Every description pulls you in and makes you want to order it, until you read the next one and then you want it.   Ms Norma and I went back and forth on which one we wanted and who got to order what.  She finally selected, The Hunter Omelette and I went with the Caveman Slinger. Her omelette was a  pork lovers delight. It had bacon, ham and sausage. As a bonus, it's fourth ingredient was avocado. Loving brussel sprouts, she added a side as an accompaniment to her breakfast. After our breakfast, she went off to work full and totally satisfied.   My Caveman Slinger was like no other slinger I've had, it was a healthy delight. The foundation was shaved brussel sprouts, sweet potatoes, pork sausage, toasted almonds and then topped with a farm fresh egg. No cheese, no chili - a healthy and satisfying dish. After our breakfast, I was off to an afternoon of shopping filled with energy.   In addition to my slinger, I enjoyed a Berry Bright Smoothie. I'm not a smoothie person, but if Revel was closer to me, I could easily become one. It was thick and creamy like a milk shake, but healthier.   At times, I am easily amused and their water dispenser amazed me. It not just offered tap water, it offered three types. You could select from; sparkling water, ice cold and room temperature water. There was also fresh lemon available as a garnish.   Parking is not a problem, since there is a parking garage right next door with ample parking for the retail outlets. The staff is also courteous and friendly. I'm looking forward to my next breakfast and also stopping by for a lunch.   When: February 22, 2016 Why: Late Breakfast
Flavorless BBQ and the meat was dried out. I've given them two tries and both times were a total disappointment. No need for the third strike, I'm done.

Savory or Sweet, Pint Size can fulfill my morning cravings.  I will admit, at times it is hard for me to stop saying, "I'll have one of those and give me two of these." Before I know it, I have filled two boxes of treats. Yesterday morning was a prime example.  First thing I always ask about and check out is what cupcakes are available. The SO loves how Christy makes her cupcakes, so I always have to grab one or two each time we visit. This visit, we experienced; Cookie Monster and Chocolate Raspberry . Cookie Monster, had a crumbled chocolate chip on top of the icing and dark chocolate filling. However, the best was the Chocolate Raspberry. Rich chocolate cupcake with pretty pink raspberry icing.   The morning savory treats were a slice of quiche made with tomato, basil and mozzarella cheese. Couldn't stop with just a slice of quiche, I had to have a savory scone too. Their daily savory scone was a Three Cheese Rosemary Cayenne. The cayenne gave a kick to the cheese blend and rosemary.   Sweet tooth was satisfied with Citrus & Olive Oil Pound Cake and a Prune & Almond Scone. Both were very good, with the pound cake taking the prize. It was moist and the citrus flavoring was perfect. Oh, I forgot the Dreamsicle Sammie, two Sugar Cookies pressed together with Orange Icing in the center. I almost drove back for more.    In addition to the sweets and savory treats, PSB offers Kaldi's coffee. Which is a major bonus for when grabbing a breakfast on the go. If you seen any of my list, you know one of them is Rainbow of Sweetness. I give a shout out to businesses who offer, all three of the popular sweeteners. PSB is being added to my list and I like the way the display them in little silver buckets.   Pint Size Bakery, you are big in flavor.

I have been converted. Before last night when I attended the International Supper Club, I would have told you I do not like Indian food. I quickly learned  that it wasn't that I didn't like Indian cuisine, I was just eating at the wrong places.   I will admit the service started out slow, the waiter would take half of our drink order and disappear. Then reappear with the first round and finish taking the rest of the orders.  Perhaps a dozen Yelpers could be intimidating.   Once he started to take the food orders, a spark appeared in his personality. He truly seemed to enjoy talking about the entrees and the spice levels of each dish. He issued warnings to some diners and those who did not listen to his wisdom, had beads of sweat building up on their upper lip and forehead.   My entree was Chicken Palak, which was chicken (given) and spinach with Indian seasonings. I was a wimp and choose my spice level as a 2 1/2. For my reentry in to Indian cuisine that was, but next time I'll be able to kick it up a notch.  The entree and rice are served in separate bowls, (almost family style) which made it easy to share samplings of other diners choices.   Portions were large enough for take home and the other half enjoyed my experience when he got home from work.   The ambiance is simple and casual which makes for a very relaxed dining experience.   Thanks Saffron for introducing me to good Indian cuisine.

FREE Wi-Fi is available at Diner's Delight and that is the most positive point about this diner. With the majority of the reviews on Yelp being 5 Stars, I was expecting to be blown away with some down home cooking. Instead, I was served food that made me wish I was bulimic.  All the food was overcooked and flavorless. Yet it left a horrible aftertaste in my mouth. I couldn't get home fast enough to brush my teeth to rid myself of the terrible taste in my mouth.   We had two Chicken Dinners with two sides, two ice teas and 1 Peach Cobbler with Ice Cream. Total cost of lunch $27 with tip. No alcohol, poor service and bad food. I think I've been robbed. I would not recommend this place to a homeless person.

Who knew shipping could be so easy? I sure in the hell didn't.   I have U-Verse for my TV service and love it. When doing a major redecorating of one of our rooms we decided to eliminate a television from our service. Three TV's for a household of two and three dogs seemed to be a little obsessive.   I was instructed to take the third receiver and the power cord to a UPS Store, along with my account number. Being anal retentive, I typed up a form with my account number, the serial number of the receiver and my confirmation number of downgrading my service. I thought I was being a good boy scout and being prepared. When I arrived to the UPS Store, the associate tossed it aside, asked me a few questions and presto a better form was printed out for my return. It was so easy peasy.   The staff was friendly, professional and if I need to ship anything in the future, I will return

This is another restaurant that I would have never discovered if it were not for Ian Froeb's STL 100 for 2016. I am so thankful that I choose to eat my way through this list, I have enjoyed so many meals, that I would have missed otherwise.   I stopped by for lunch on a Friday. Ian's "must order" recommendation was the, Khao Soi. Since, I was in the beginning stages of the sniffles, I thought it was a good choice. Who needs chicken noodle soup, when you can have a big bowl of Khao Soi. It's a Northern Thai egg noodle curry soup. Served with red onion, pickled mustard greens, cripsy egg noodles. I loved it and the spiciness opened up nasal passages and sniffles were gone. Next time I start to get a cold, I'm coming to Fork & Stix.  To accompany my huge bowl of soup, I ordered Thai Stix. They basically were similar to a Crab Rangoon, but better. Here they are; Cream cheese & Crab mixed wrapped in spring roll wrapper and deep fried and served with a Thai sweet chili sauce.  Service is quick and friendly in the small space. A heads up that parking can be a challenge. Be sure to pay the parking meter to avoid getting a ticket.   Would I come back? More to try, but I fell in love with the Khao Soi  When: December 9, 2016 Why: Eating my way through Ian's list

I just discovered Gelato Di Riso and I am already a fan. I love their Salted Caramel.  I also tried their Cherry ____(drawing a blank) and it was rich and creamy. I was almost tempted to order it, but I love Caramel too much. I also tried the BF's Tiramisu and it was tasty too.   I will be coming to Gelato Di Riso and buying Gelato by the pint and quart in the future. I'm sure I'll be enjoying a cone on the drive home. Why it took me so long to discover this cute little Gelato shop on The Hill is beyond me.

EXQUISITE!   Central Table Food Hall is a food court for a foodie with discriminating taste. I was fortunate enough to attend a Tasting Dinner for Yelp Elite last week and after being teased with all those delectable tastings, I was anxious to return. I am also proud that Central Table is my 600th Yelp review.   The ambiance is magnificent and impressive as a Grand Hall should be. It is vast and open with massive amounts of natural light  spilling in through the windows. (The natural light was perfect for taking Yelp pictures.) Their extensive windows has the large  space feeling extra large. The bar is perfectly positioned to enjoy the natural light, with seating all around. It is then surrounded by tables for two and communal tables for large groups, or making new friends.  SUCCULENT!  As we sipped some Lucy Rose, we narrowed our entree choices down from their; Hearth, Grill, Raw and Sushi selections. We also munched on the complementary bread which was not your typical bread and butter basket.  It was two pieces of bread, with a sampling of provencale sauce and grated cheese. Yum.   Before our entrees, we shared a Caesar Salad. What attracted me to their Caesar, was that it had White Anchovies. I love White Anchovies. For those of you not familiar with them, White Anchovies are the more elegant cousin of the briny brown fillets that most are familiar with. White Anchovies are filleted into two pieces and packed in an oil and vinegar marinade. The vinegar gives a snap to the anchovies.   Back to the salad, it was bite size pieces of Romaine lettuce, Parmigiano - Regianno and of course my favorite White Anchovies. The croutons were also a stand out. In addition to being flavorful, they were deformed. Each crouton was like a snowflake, different in shape and form. Letting you know these were fresh, made in house and not pulled from a bag.   The BF choose the Sushi Combo with Spicy Tuna Roll and 6 pieces of Chefs Choice Nigiri. He proclaimed this to be the best Sushi in the city. After placing our orders he was bantering with the server about Sea Urchin. He commented he can not find anyone who can do Sea Urchin right. The gauntlet was thrown down. The server knew their chef could do it and do it right. He returned with a Sea Urchin "shooter" and he was correct, his chef did it RIGHT. The BF loved it!    I normally am not a fan of Sushi, but I will say the one Spicy Tuna Roll that I enjoyed has me reconsidering my distaste for Sushi. I've always been told if you do not like a food, it is just because you've never had it made appropriately. This may be the case with my past Sushi experiences.   My entree was the Scallops. I enjoyed three large Sea Scallops with some Summer Squash, Bok Choy and Argula. Each of my Scallops were large enough to provide me with three bites each. I'll take Sea over Bay Scallops any day. I loved how they had wafer sliced squash on the plate and then multiple mini balls of squash. How creative to scoop the insides of the squash with a melon ball tool. I'll be trying this at home. The Bok Choy was sautéed tender, leaving enough snap showing the freshness. They use  baby/mini Bok Choy which makes a better presentation on the plate.  If you're out for the experience, you might as well go whole hog and do dessert. Our server recommended the Affogato which is Caramel Gelato with Espresso. The Gelato is served in a coffee cup and then when it is brought to your table they pour just enough Espresso on top from a French Press to cover it. A perfect ending to any meal or for just stopping in and enjoying a night cap. I just wish I could have gotten a picture before he added the hot Espresso.   I already know I will be coming back soon. I am determined to experience the Gooseberry & Lamb Pizza. Gooseberries, Lamb Bacon, Goat Cheese, Honey and Black Pepper. Doesn't it sound decadent?

Post = Post Office Commons = a gathering place accessible to all members of society.  Post Commons = A fun new coffeehouse in Alton  The ambiance is simple, relaxing and vintage. I love how they kept a lot of the details showing that it was once the main post office of Alton. The space is large and filled with eclectic tables and chairs. There is also a large event space that can be utilized by groups for meetings.   The lunch menu is small, but what they served was done well. I was dining with two cousins and we each ordered something different. My one cousin does not like eggs, so she ordered the Hash Bowl without the fried egg. OMG, she was missing out. I sampled it and with an egg in it, would have been top notch. The mixture of sweet potato, black beans, bacon and poblano chili sauce, were already a winner and a fried egg would have taken to another level.   The other cuz got the Breakfast Burger. It was a house made pork sausage patty, accented with poblano, avocado aioli and topped with a fried egg. It was served on a toasted Brioche Bun and a side of HashBrowns. He enjoyed it. Looking at his HB's, I would have wanted mine a little crisper.   I went for a deli sandwich and ordered a Pastrami on Marble Rye. They were not stingy with Pastrami and topped it with two slices of Swiss Cheese. I made mine a combo, so it came with a bag of Miss Vickie's Chips and Diet Coke.   My cousins enjoyed cups of black coffee with their breakfast themed entrees. As we waited for our food, I ordered a Bloody Mary and my closest cuz ordered a Mimosa. Sad to say, it was just an average Bloody Mary. Found it odd, they did not serve it on ice.   I hope the residents of Alton embrace this new coffeehouse and support its concept of a "commons" where everyone is accepted.   I'll be back? - I'll try to stop by whenever I'm in town and have some spare time.   When: April 10, 2018 Why: Lunch with cousins

When your handsome baby boy is turning 4 and he already is spoiled, how do you make his birthday extra special? You go shopping at Treats Unleashed and and go crazy buying him and his older sister special treats to celebrate his big day.   The cakes and cookies at Treats Unleashed are so decorative and professionaly created, a human could be tempted to eat them. For Murphy, I choose a Happy Birthday Bone in orange. I also got him and his sister a Cupcake Biscuit, which is one of those treats that could persuade a human to eat. It's a good sized cookie cut in the shape of a cupcake and decorated as if it were in a Ladue bakery. Oh wait, it is in a Ladue bakery, a bakery for dogs.   In addition to his treats, Murphy will be getting a fashionable new bandana to wear on his special day. Murph will also be dining in style, I got him a can of a premium canned food to use a topping on his dry food. Merrick has an excellent variety of Grain-Free soft foods that have names as descriptive as Southern Comfort restaurant. He'll be enjoying, Cowboy Cookout.   Pets are always welcome at Treats Unleashed, so on my next visit Murphy will accompany me so he can try on a new collar & leash. TU is growing by leaps and bounds, so check and see if one is near your hood. Then take your favorite four legged baby and shop local instead of those national chains.

Congratulations to Pint Size Bakery for being included on Ian Froeb's STL 100. I've been in love with PSB ever since they opened 4 years ago. I'm thankful that their current and new upcoming location are both within walking distance of my home. The only way I could love them more, is for them to be open on Monday.   When I was a wee lad, growing up on a farm in Illinois, my favorite treat after school was an Oatmeal Cream Pie by Little Debbie. Back then I thought those were the real deal, with a glass of cold milk. Now that I am an old man, with taste buds that have experienced the Oatmeal Cream Pies from Pint Size Bakery, I realize as youth, I was totally slumming it with Little Deb. The oatmeal is by far the best, but do give Dreamsicle & Chocolate a chance as well.   Ian recommended the Oatmeal Cream Pie as his "must order". Once again, I have to disagree with him. Yes, I love me a OCP, but for me the scones at Pint Size are the star attraction. I favor the savory, but there are times when a sweet scone steals my heart, like this morning. I was so content ordering my savory, which was  Kale & Mozzarella. Then out of the corner of eye, I saw  a Raspberry with White Icing. I had to have both.   Once I was home, the savory was the perfect accompaniment to my morning milk. I thought I was going to leave the sweet scone until later in the day for a snack. That did not happen, it kept calling my name. I soon was devouring it with a cup of coffee and this morning, the sweet was the best treat.   If you've got dogs, they sell little bags of dog bones for $1.50. I highly recommend these and so do my dogs. My dogs love'm and by me buying these, I get to enjoy my treats in peace from Pint Size as K-9 children enjoy theirs.   The service at PSB is always top notch. They remember the regulars and if you're not a regular, they'll still welcome you as if you were.

Cheap, Cheap, Pizza, Pizza.  Can not beat the price. This was my first experience of Little Caesars and we tried the Deep Dish with pepperoni. The sauce was flavorful, they topped it with plenty of pepperoni and cheese. I know it was deep dish, but it was still too much dough for me. Next time we'll save $3 and order the regular pizza.   We also tried their chicken wings, the pieces were kind of small, but the flavor big for the price. They offer 7 different flavors, we choose traditional "spicy".   When funds are low, or you're in a hurry Little Caesars can provide you a quick good meal for the price.

I love this AT&T store. Like Shelly, a wireless store is not one of my favorite places to go, it's kinda like going to the dentist. You go because you have to go.   When going to a AT&T store I always make sure it is a corporate store and not a privately owned one. I just feel you get better service when you are shopping in the mother ship. The store over on Clayton Road across from the Galleria use to be my store of choice, but not any more. The customer service here is so personalized and more friendly. They've helped me through both iphones 3 & 4 and were instrumental when my iphone fell into a rain barrel. Helping with that drama, I will always be indebted   Todays visit was a simple tech visit. I kept get a message to enter a password for my voice mail - I didn't know I even had one. I walked in and immediately (no waiting) had my problem resolved.  They coached and helped me learn the solution with fun witty banter. We all had a good laugh when I realized I had 40 voice mails. 40 voice mails that I had no idea I had. No wonder I had a few friends pissed off that I didn't return a call. Hey, with text who uses voice mail any way, it's so 20th century...lol.

Today I had one of the best lunches I've had in a long time. I'm a Facebook friend of Vernon's and have seen them post pictures of their Reuben sandwich which they feature as a special on Wednesday. I am so glad that I made it a point to drive to U-City and enjoy this incredible sandwich.  They describe their Reuben as; Corned Beef, Smoked Vienna Kraut, Melted Swiss, Smokey Russian on toasted Gateway Rye. The Corned Beef is so tender a person with no teeth could enjoy eating it with no difficulty. They melted the Swiss Cheese perfectly, so it wrapped around the Smoked Vienna Kraut holding it together with the Corned Beef. This sandwich is huge, but I managed to eat the whole thing. As we chowed down, my DP (dining partner) both agreed that this is by far the best Reuben we have ever had.   Ordering our sides we stuck with the specials of the day and enjoyed; Cucumber Salad, 3 Bean Brisket Chili and Smoked Peaches. When our order was delivered to the table, the peaches were still warm. I could not resist, I had to sample one before I tried anything else. The peaches of Georgia have nothing on this sweet and smoked local peach. All I needed was some vanilla soft serve ice cream and these peaches would have made a fantastic dessert. However, they were very flavorful alone. I got my daily fruit intake for the day.   I enjoy a cool and refreshing cucumber salad. Normally I have seen them with the cucumbers slice in circles and the onions in ringlets. Vernon diced his onion, cubed the cucumber and added diced red pepper to the mix. The vinegar and oil dressing was lite, so it highlighted the natural flavors of the fresh vegetables.   If you're a Reuben fan, you've got to go to Vernon's next Wednesday.

I really don't know what is harder to do. Is it harder to take a restaurant from 4 Stars down to 2 Stars or is it harder to raise a restaurant from 1 Star up to 4 Stars? I'm going to say, it is going from 1 up to 4. Why? Because, I have to swallow my pride and admit, that I was wrong. However, I am happy to say that I have removed Diner's Delight from my No-No List and it most likely will be a place I frequent when I am to lazy to cook (which is often).   After seeing DD appear on Ian Froeb's STL 100 List for 2016, I knew I had to give them a second chance. He raved about their Oxtail, but that is not for me. Luckily he also raved about their fried chicken and that is more to my liking.   In fact on my recent visit, I ordered the exact same thing I did on 7/11/2012 which was my last visit. Eating the exact same food on 9/13/2016, I wonder to myself, how could I have ever given them only 1 Star. This food is delicious and simple comfort food. The fried chicken is juicy, crispy and simply seasoned with salt and pepper and maybe a little love. There's no over powering spices, it just simple fried chicken like your granny use to make on Sunday after church.   This time, I feel in love with the Mac-n-Cheese. As I'm enjoying it with my chicken, I'm wondering how it would match up to the Meatloaf that I saw on the steam table earlier. Oh, that definitely will be a future meal for me. Those green beans that I had, will also be a repeat in that meal as well.   DD, I did you wrong 4 years ago. You truly are one of the best 100 restaurants in STL. Your food is simple, it's not overly produced and it is comfort food at its' best. I am so glad you are no longer on my No-No List. It was a No-No for me to have put you on it in the first place.   When: September 13, 2016 Why: Lunch and Ian Froeb's STL 100

White Castle to the rescue.   Sometimes when you're out having a good time and you drink too much, you need a good ole belly bomber. Yes, the best treatment for over drinking is a combo meal from White Castle.   My go to combo is the #2. It includes, two double cheese, a small french fry and a small soda. I just love the double cheese, especially with the jalapeño cheese. Also, I'm a big fan of crinkle cut fries. They may come  from a frozen bag at WC, but they're always crisp and satisfying.  If the dining room is open, I always go inside. I am not a fan of drive-thru's at any fast food establishment. The staff here was friendly. I was shocked at the amount of plexiglass that they were secured behind. At least WC has their safety in mind. Even with a barrier of plexi between us, the service was warm and personable.   I'll be back? - If in the area and hit by "the crave" I'll stop by.   When: January 5, 2018 Why: Drank too much

Fingers or Tenders, they're still the same thing, boneless breaded chicken.  If you want chicken tenders for lunch or dinner, why go to a burger joint? You should be going to a place that specializes in chicken tenders. RCCF serves nothing but, chicken fingers/tenders, it's their specialty and they have mastered it well.   Big shout out to the Texas Toast, feed me those additional carbs. The fries are crinkle cut and I'm pretty sure, they are right out of a bag. I can't complain about frozen fries, when my chicken is totally fresh.  I'm not a sauce man, so I am pleased with the seasoning of the tenders. I was able to enjoy them, plain and simple. However, when it come to my french fries, I do like some ketchup. Those of you who follow my reviews, know my love of little cups for my ketchup. RCCF meet and exceeded my expectations, when it came to ketchup.  They did not hand me a couple of packets, instead they had a pump machine of Heinz ketchup (my brand of choice) so I could fill my own personal little cup of ketchup.   The staff was over the top friendly and personable. If the young man who took my order was a graduating classmate, I'd vote for him as most outgoing. The service was fast, which is good for those on a tight schedule. The decor is vintage movie posters, with a couple of them being St. Louis themed.   It's okay that I'm only giving 3 Stars, it is a good review, it is a fast food restaurant. If I worked or lived in the area, I'd enjoy lunch here on a regular.  As a reminder, if you like chicken tenders and fries, don't go to Hardee's or McDonald's, come here.

A Choose Three + an extra side is a good lunch for two. We enjoyed Rib Tips, Brisket and St. Louis Style Ribs with Baked Beans and then added Potato Salad as our extra side. We were amazed at the size of the portions of the three meats. We were so full after eating lunch, we didn't need dinner  The potato salad was a mustard base, which is my favorite. It was big chunks of potatoes, cooked perfectly. Not too soft and not overly firm. It was the kind of potato salad you'd see at a family picnic made by your favorite Aunt. The Baked Beans were in a thin runny sauce, but seasoned well.   The four St. Louis Style Ribs were meaty and had just the right amount of BBQ sauce. Of the three meats, the Brisket was my favorite. Multiple slices of tender brisket, smothered in their BBQ sauce that has a tangy, vinegar tang taste. Seeing the other reviews rave about the Rib Tips, I ordered them as our third meat. Neither of us were impressed with the tips, which cost them the 4th star.   Roper's is a true Mom and Pop BBQ joint and it will be mom and pop serving you. They are friendly, personable and they both make sure you feel at home in their little restaurant. So if you are in north Saint Louis and craving BBQ, stop by Roper's for a treat of down home BBQ.

I live close to this Schnucks and want it to be my favorite grocer, but it just misses the mark. I do shop here a lot because of the closeness, but they need to improve the two most important departments.  Those would be produce and meats, they are just average compared to other grocery stores  near The Hill. Please work on improving these areas, I can not be loyal to a grocer based on canned and frozen goods.   The staff is great, they are friendly and extremely helpful while you are shopping.

I'm a meat man and I totally enjoyed my evening at Bombay Food Junkies. I'm also not a fan of Indian food, or at least I thought I wasn't. However, when it is served vegetarian style, it won me over. These are two of the main reasons I love the International Supper Club. It forces me out of my rut and to experience new and different cuisines.   The dinner here is billed as all you can eat, but the servings they provided were enough to satisfy me. I only took a second serving of the Sweet Corn Soup and the Manchurian. I will say they definitely were my two favorites on all the offerings last night. I exclude the Mango Ice Cream for dessert, because we were only allowed one serving. If we could have more, I'd been requesting two scoops.   For me, I'd want more of the first and second courses, totally skip the third and go straight to dessert. Don't get me wrong, the items offered in the third course were good and unique, they just didn't send off any fireworks for my palate like the first two did.   Thanks for a great evening BFJ and thanks once again to ISC for showing me a world beyond meat.   Would I come back? If a friend asked me, I wouldn't hesitate to go again.   When: November 28, 2016 Why: International Supper Club

To the right of SugarFire BBQ is a good restaurant that gets overshadowed by the greatness of its neighbor. Thanks to Taste Cards I saved $10 off of $30 and got to experience some of the greatness of Fallon's Bar & Grill.   Keep in mind Bar & Grill is in their name, so the food is typical bar fare. Being a big eater, I found the portions to be hearty. So hearty, that we needed to go boxes. I also found the staff to be extremely friendly. Almost every server who passed our table, said some type of greeting/comment. I think they were all on some type of happy pills.   We started out with one of my favorite appetizers, Fried Pickles. Some Yelpers have proclaimed me the King of Fried Pickles, for my love of this weird treat. Fallon's presented a fairly good pickle. I liked the light breading on the dill pickle chips and the Spicy Ranch Dressing for dipping. These pickles are worthy of being added to my prestigious Fried Pickle List.   My entree was Fish & Chips, which is Guinness battered Cod and house-made Tarter Sauce, served with coleslaw and a choice of fries or house-made chips. I was not impressed with the fish, I've had better at Captain D's and Long John Silvers. However, the chips are as good as those you'd get at some of the local Irish Pubs. Also, I am not a fan of Tartar Sauce, but I tried theirs and was impressed. It has me reconsidering my dislike of tartar sauce. The Cole Slaw was also a winner, a shame the fish was such a disappointment.   The star of the meal definitely was the Shepherds Pie enjoyed by dining partner. They claim it is a family recipe straight from Ireland. I do not know who I have to sleep with to get this family recipe, but I am willing to do it. Yes, it is that good. It was a huge serving of Baked Mashed Potatoes, seasoned ground lamb and ground beef, Guinness Gravy, Peas and Cheddar Cheese. I want to make this at home on a cold winter day, it is a great comfort food. I plan to return and enjoy a serving of this dish on my own.

At this time of year, I look forward to two things; Catholic Church Fish Fry's and Clam Strips from White Castle. I don't know what it is about the clam strips from WC, but I like them. I really, really like them. I grew up enjoying the clam strip dinners at Howard Johnson's and these strips take me back to those memories. It's a simple quick easy finger food lunch.   This year they introduced Crab Sliders and I'm looking forward to giving them a try too. Today, I paired my strips with my favorite Double Cheeseburger and fries. I balanced it out with a Diet Coke. For me the best fountain sodas come from White Castle. They keep the soda lines clean and have the right combination of flavored syrup and carbon dioxide with purified water.   Normally, I do not use a drive-thru, I always go inside a restaurant if the dining room is open. However, today I had my fur-baby Murphy with me and I didn't want to leave him in the car alone. It was a long line in the drive-thru, but I was amazed how fast they moved through the process. The young lady over the speaker spoke clearly and was charming and polite at the window.   Will I return? I'll return to WC, but I'm normally not in this area to hit this one up.   When: February 28, 2017 Why: Lunch - Clam Strips

TAB is a dive bar in Dogtown, that is host to Mac's Local Eats inside. They both operate in the same space individually, so you need to order and pay each of them separately.   The beer menu at Tamm Ave Bar is impressive, so it is easy to find a craft beer to accompany your delicious burger and fries. They also have a menu of specialty cocktails for those non-beer enthusiast.   The atmosphere is rustic and minimalist at best. I found it odd that a UK - Kentucky Wildcats flag was hanging in a STL dive bar. However, I was able to overlook that oddity when I discovered they had hook and outlets under the bar. Nice touch.   Service at TAB is typical dive bar service - I'll get to you when I can. The bartender was busy talking to friends in the bar and on her cell phone, before realizing I was seated at the bar and needing a drink. Once she realized, all was good. She was just a little slow on the uptake.   Warning - Beer is served in plastic glasses.   I'll be back? - Yes, Mac's is in the same building and I love dive bars.   When: January 31, 2018 Why: Eating at Mac's and wanted a beer

Hey, Joe. I like this location way better then your location at the Brentwood Promenade. The store lay out seems to have a better flow, it is way cleaner and the staff truly understands the Trader Joe's philosophy, meaning they offer better customer service.   I am a big fan of their Organic Vodka Sauce and it is a secret ingredient in a dish I make and it is not a pasta recipe. As others have stated, TJ is not a place where you will see the major brands and where you'll come to shop with coupons from the Sunday flier. The brands here are unusual and many are owned by TJ. It is kind of like shopping at Aldi's, at first you may not know the brand names. You'll have to do what I do and that is experimenting to see what you like.   However, here at Trader Joe's they are a little more expensive, then Aldi's.   Did you know that they are owned by the same company? I didn't until another Yelper pointed it out to me. The things you can learn on Yelp.   None went in my cart today, but I can tell you the potato chips and tortilla chips here are party worthy. Also, the salsa and dips are perfect as well. Another treat that I look forward to each year and each year I hold my breath that they do not discontinue it, is the Oreo type cookie with peppermint icing filling. Christmas would not be complete without it and I am already looking forward to next year.   I do not mind the extra drive here from the city. Here I get better customer service and I do not need to worry about Parking Lot Derby at the Promenade.

If anyone wants to know what Baseball Heaven is like, all they need to do is visit Busch Stadium. It truly is, where a Field of Dreams come true.   As a stadium it is only 5 years old and already is home to 2 World Series Championships, 1 Allister's Game and 3 incredible concerts; Dave Matthews in '08, The Eagles in '10 and an unforgettable U2 in '11.   Busch Stadium is also the only place I will go and will happily pay $35 for 4 beers, $22 for 2 Hot Dogs and Fries and still walk away with a smile and not feel like I've been overcharged (even though I know deep down inside I have been). After all watching the Cardinals win is "priceless".   The stadium work staff is friendly and it is obvious they all have that "Cardinal Fever". Some of the concession stand employees move to slow for me, but that's because I want to get back to my seat and cheer on my true "boys of summer" to victory.   Thanks for a very memorable first five years and I look forward to many, many more. Let's see how many Championship Pennants we can place on your brick and mortar.

Impressive Quik Trip.   I stopped by in the early AM and could not believe how busy it was. I needed gas and almost pump was in use. After filling my tank, I pulled forward and parked to go inside for some lunch supplies at work. Again, I was shocked at how busy it was. I grabbed my Gold Peak Ice Tea, a donut and a bag of chips. I was tempted to get something from their kitchen that prepares food fresh. May-be next time.   When I went to pay, there was only one cashier and the line was long. I took my place at the end and was impressed how fast the young lady checked everyone out. She worked that line and quality customer service did not suffer. She still talked to her regulars and thanked everyone for their business. QT needs to promote her to corporate training.   I'll be back? - It's close to my work exit/entrance on 255.   When: August 12, 2019 Why: Down to Two Bars on the Gas Gage

When my friend Norma and I went to Ferguson to finish up our holiday shopping, we knew we wanted to have lunch at Ferguson Burger Bar. I commend the owners of this fantastic little burger cafe. It takes courage to place your "burger" business directly across the street from a McDonald's. McD's should be scared, FBB&M serves up some kick ass burgers and fries.  Norma enjoyed a single patty Garbage Burger, which was anything, but garbage. It's a grill seared patty garnished with; lettuce, bacon, fried egg, onion, cheese and mayo. Who wouldn't want to enjoy a tasty burger like this instead of a Big Mac. My Double Cheeseburger with Pepper Jack Cheese would put any double cheeseburger to shame. Thick, juicy patties seasoned perfectly and placed between two slices of Texas Toast. The french fries were crisp crinkle cut fries and seasoned with pepper more then salt. We both enjoyed the fact that they were heavily seasoned with pepper.   It is counter service and they call out your number when your food is ready. Another cool treat at FBB&M is the free Vess soda with your combo meal. My Creme soda was the perfect refreshing beverage, it was a throw back to my childhood.   The owner was most gracious and the perfect host. I wish them well in their business and with the quality of food and service we received, I'm confident they will be around for a long time.

After being introduced to a St. Paul Sandwich while attending a UYE, I am now trying to experience them at my regular Chinese restaurants. Fortune Express did not disappoint me, it does a St. Paul as well as it does the rest of their menu. I never thought I'd see the day that I would enjoy a sandwich placed between two slices of Wonder Bread.   Egg Drop Soup, a St. Paul Sandwich (chicken) and an Egg Roll makes a nice little lunch.

This is a great little park/garden that honors Robert Pershing Wadlow, who is known as  "The Gentle Giant".  Other names he has be known to be called, are Alton Giant and Giant of Illinois. He was born in Alton, IL Feb. 22, 1918 and passed away at an early age of 22 on July 15, 1940. When he died he was an amazing 8' 11.1" tall and weighed an astounding 485 lbs.  He achieved this great height due to hypertrophy of his pituitary gland which results in an abnormally high level of human growth hormone.   In the park you will find a life size statue of Robert and also a life size statue of a  chair that was made especially for his large size. Next time you are in Alton, watching the eagles, passing through to Grafton or getting your drink on at Fast Eddies, stop by the park it only needs to be a short visit.  Then you can stand next to The Gentle Giants statue and just see how small of a man you really are. Then have a seat in his big chair for a good chuckle.  Best of all it is "free".

Jessica C. has called this one out right. This is by far the best Costco in the St. Louis area.   The selection here is superior to the other locations. When they say, "location, location, location"  makes a difference I guess it helps to be located in West County.  They have products and brands you will not find at the other two locations.   I will drive the extra miles to shop here and I'll miss my Culver's lunch which was a treat when I shopped the South County location.

The service is friendly and fast.   The food was fast Mexican food fast.   Our beers and margaritas were ice cold. I'm fond on traditional margaritas, but my cousin had a mango one that was fantastic.   She also, had the best entree which was grilled shrimp and fresh vegetables (forget the name on the menu).   Atmosphere, drinks, good customer service and above average Mexican food make this a good place for an inexpensive meal.

Even during a #pandemic and only providing #curbside service/sales, my experience today was top notch.   There were two associates working and they were hustling it. The door to the store was locked for safety. There were a couple of us waiting our turn and as they'd bring out the purchase for the previous customer, they'd ask who was next. When it was my turn, I showed the young man the two type of bulbs I needed and the quantity of each.   The older man working, came out with the bulb for my track lighting and informed me that that bulb was no longer made. He recommended, another one that he did have in stock. I agreed to purchase that one instead and when I got home, I actually like the light it makes better. I also, picked up some bulbs for my recessed lighting in the kitchen.  I always take my used bulbs here for recycling. Today, however when I asked the younger associate if they were accepting recycling during the pandemic, he told me no. As, I was waiting for my order to be processed, I returned my bag of recycling to my car. As I was walking back to the storefront, the older man came back out and asked for my recycling. He said, since I was making a purchase, that they'd be happy to accept my used bulbs.   When the young man brought my purchase out, he thanked me for my business and told me how much they appreciated it.   I've said it before, if I need bulbs or batteries, this is my go to store. The customer service I have experienced here, has always been top notch.  Will I return? - When a bulb burns out or I need a battery.   When: May 23, 2020 Why: New Bulbs

Wow! What a major disappointment. I came here after shopping at Lowe's. I read the reviews and saw that 5 of my Yelp friends rated them 5 Stars. I thought I was in for a good steak dinner. Then I saw the Early Dine special and I thought it was a double win. Boy, was I wrong.   To be honest, the only positive things I can say about this dinner is that they have linen napkins, the price I paid for the Early Dine Special and the Cajun Horseradish Sauce. Everything else was the major disappointment.   First disappointment was their beer offerings. They offered no local craft beers on draft or in a bottle/can. I understand they are a national chain, but they should be able to offer local breweries, especially when they are located in in major craft beer city like St. Louis.   Second disappointment was the timing of all my food. I'm a fan of Fried Pickles so I ordered them as an appetizer. My plan was to relax, sip my beer and munch on the fried pickles. The pickles arrived quickly. I barely had time to to pick-up one pickle chip and did it in the sauce, when my Caesar Salad was delivered. As I was rearranging my plates, here came a third server bringing me my steak. All three of my items, came out, bang, bang, bang. I do give them credit for FAST service.   I do give credit to the third server, he did offer to hold my steak until later. I declined, knowing that it most likely would dry out being under the heat lamp in back. Since I was eating at the bar, the bartender stepped up, laughed and said, "I don't know how they all came out so fast."   My comments on the food:   Fried Pickles: The chips were thinly covered in breading, did not have much flavoring, but done well. They still had the crispness for a pickle.  The Cajun Horseradish sauce was even good for dipping bites of my steak.   Caesar Salad: Bland. Romaine lettuce was cut in good bite size pieces. Dressing was watered down and bland. Only two croutons on entire salad. I understand I was enjoying a Early Dine, but some shave Parmesan and a couple more croutons would have been nice.   Green Beans: Out of a can, with bacon and onions added. Actually, they stunk when delivered to my barstool.    Sirloin Steak: Tender, with minimal seasoning. I like a steak with only salt and pepper, but this was less then that.  Requested medium rare and was served more medium well.   I always sit at the bar when dinning alone. I always find that a bartender is more attentive to a single diner at the bar then a server is at a table. However, on this visit I totally ignored. The bartender was more interested in regulars seated at the other end of the bar and talking with other employees. My only interaction with the bartender was taking my order, laughing at my quick deliveries and asking for my check. I had to flag her down for my check and I still had to wait and they were not that busy.   I'll be back? - Most likely not. I was really disappointed.   When: June 18, 2018 Why: Dinner

Friendly staff gets them 3 Stars, the weak coffee gets them a  2.   I ordered Buddy The Elf Mocha and it was the most flavorless and bland coffee drink I have ever drank. How can an espresso drink with steamed milk, dark chocolate sauce and maple spice syrup topped with whipping cream have no flavor? Not one of those flavors came through the entire drink. They either forgot to add ingredients, or they were using old stale ingredients.   There are many other places to get a latte or mocha on Manchester, so I suggest you stroll up or down the road and get your caffeine fix elsewhere.

How do you make a sports bar upscale and classy? You let Lester do it.   I have always been a big fan of Lester's in Ladue and was excited when I heard the news of them opening a third location in the CWE. I was hoping he'd give the CWE location a different twist and he did not disappoint. They still have the same fantastic bar grub, but it is just served in a more upscale and classy venue. This will be the place to watch Mizzu and Rams games. Also, now that the Cards are in the playoffs, besides the stadium, Lester's will be the place to be.   One of my all time favorite things at Lester's is the chicken wings. I always order the Garlic Lemon Pepper and request that they be done just a little crisper then the norm. For me and my friends, it just seems to lock the flavor in more.  No need for dipping these wings, their seasoning needs no condiments.   Lester's also serves up some true New York Deli style sandwiches. His pastrami hits the spot when paired up with a side of fries.  On the recent visit, we tried the Chopped Chef Salad and it was awesome.  It includes Romaine and Iceberg lettuce, house smoked turkey, honey baked ham, bacon, tomato, red onion, hard boiled egg, cucumber tossed with your dressing of choice and topped with seasoned croutons, cheddar & provolone cheese.  Not being fans of Iceberg lettuce and provolone cheese, we asked if they could use all romaine lettuce and use more cheddar instead of the provolone cheese and they were more then happy to accommodate our request.   I love forward to future lunches and happy hours at the CWE Lester's.  It is a great addition to the Maryland Plaza mix.

Great little neighborhood liquor store. As stated by Kelly B, the store has no merchandising sense, but the inventory is unbelievable and they know where everything is located.   I got turned on to this place a few years ago when I was searching for the new Espresso Vodka by Van Gogh. None of the major booze retailers had it, but would order it and I'd have to wait several days. HHL had it in stock and gave me instant gratification. They may be small, cluttered and a little dusty, but they are cutting edge and have always provided me with good service and good prices.   CJ H. get serious, when you are buying booze at a liquor store at 10:30 am with the wino's you kinda gotta expect bad behavior. Unfortunately  when you shop at Arena or Randall's you'll see the same thing and the owners are helpless. It's sad, but true. Next time call the police and file a complaint of a flasher.

#23 on The 25 Places to Eat in STL in 2017. That is according to the Yelp Blog and now that I have been, I couldn't agree more. This is a relatively small cafe, with a big personality. It definitely is a neighborhood spot, that welcomes outsiders with open arms. I left the neighborhood before 2Schae opened, but if I still lived directly across the street, I'd be here every morning. I was impressed that much.   I knew about 2Schae, but thought it was just a "coffee shop". I had no idea that they had such an extensive menu for breakfast and lunch. The large variety of omelettes available, just blew my mind. In addition to all the ones that they create, you can also select your own ingredients and they'll make one specially for you.   One of my favorite vegetables is Asparagus and I'm a fan of Goat Cheese. So when I saw them with bacon and sun dried tomatoes in the French Quarter Omelette, I knew that one was for me.
