It was a three egg omelette filled with small pencil stem asparagus, the most flavorful kind in my opinion and rich creamy Goat Cheese. The bacon was crisp and sun-dried tomatoes were cut into little strips. Great presentation and the four flavors blended together wonderfully. It was so huge, I brought half of it home is a true, "Doggie Bag" that is eco-friendly.   The coffee they serve is Wildhorse, which is from a local vendor. I like it when a local business supports another. At their condiment counter, they offered both skim and half & half for those who need a little cream in their coffee.   2Schae is divided in to two sections, with an open working kitchen in the middle. On one side you have small tables and chairs and on the other is plush chairs and sofas and a counter in front of the window. Either side is relaxing and work friendly.   Mr & Mrs Schaeffer (owners) are very hospitable and were thrilled to here that I came in because of the Yelp Top 25.   Will I return? - Gotta try lunch.   When: November 17, 2017 Why: Yelp Top 25 Places to Eat in STL

When I crave Chinese (Carryout), Fortune Express will now be my destination. I have been favoring the other Chinese restaurant east of Hampton on Chippewa and needed a change. I am so glad we used the coupon that came in the mail.   Our dinner menu included; Crab Rangoon, Egg Rolls, Chicken with Broccoli, Kung Pao Chicken, Ham Fried Rice and Egg Drop Soup.   The Crab Rangoon and Egg Rolls were great. I was impressed that they were not over deep fried as many places do. My broccoli was crisp, not limp and wimpy. Seasoning in both main entrees, were spot on.  Egg Drop Soup was flavorful and one of the best EDS I have had.   Yes, I will be back.

Great neighborhood bar. They live up to their name and offer some great martini's. I love  a good dirty martini.   Their bar menu is typical, I've enjoyed a couple of the St. Louis style pizzas that were impressive. Yes they have provel on them, but you're in St. Louis deal with it and enjoy a slice.   I gotta get back and enjoy a breakfast and trivia night.

Impressive BBQ on The Hill.   Let me start off by congratulating, J. Smugs GastroPit for being on Ian Froeb's STL 100 for 2019. If it were not for his list, I may have continued to drive by your establishment. Who would have thought BBQ on The Hill would be as scrumptious as yours.   I stopped by for a quick lunch. Ian said, the ribs were aggressively seasoned, so I had to give them a try. I also wanted to try the brisket and the young lady working the counter said she could do me a sampling for an additional $3. I took the deal.   My ribs came with one side, I choose Mac-n-Cheese. It's my go to with BBQ and other reviews raved about it. I also, added a second side of Pit Beans. PB is one of those sides that you always have to have when eating BBQ. My eyes were bigger then my tummy. I had to-go vessel coming home with me.   The ribs were dry rubbed and had a hard crisp outside. When I pulled them apart and bite into them, the meat was tender as could be. The brisket was delicious. It had a crisp outer edge from a dry rub as well, with just enough fat to make it super fork tender.   Normally, I am not a fan of sauces. However, Ian raved about the Dr. Pepper sauce, so I gave it a try. Damn, it was so good, I may have to reconsider my dislike of sauces. I even tried the Bianca, which was a white peppery garlic. Two sauces, that I like and they're both at one Gastropit.   As a reminder my sides were, Mac-n-Cheese and Pit Beans. The Mac was extra creamy and made with the traditional elbow pasta. Their Pit Beans, were tasty and had a sufficient amount of meat blended in. The beans could of used just a touch more seasoning, for me they were leaning towards the bland end of the spectrum. The MnC, was rich and creamy the way it should be. It gets a total thumbs up. I'm just a pepper freak, so I squeezed a little Dr. Pepper sauce in mine for an extra kick.   The young lady working the counter was awesome! Personality, plus. She was very talkative, greeted everyone who came in and immediately started telling them about the daily special. The ones she knew as regulars, she told them about the specials for the next two days. Excellent, customer service. You may order at the counter, but she makes it easy and enjoyable.   Just a heads up, J Smugs will be offering fried fish during lent.   Chances of coming back? - Yes. It's a quick and easy lunch.   When: March 6, 2019 Why: Ian Froeb's STL 100 2019

I was so looking forward to Bobby's opening. I thought I was going to have another restaurant within walking distance to home, for a good burger or chicken wings. Wow, was I dreaming or what. Not only was the service embarrassing, but quality of food was even worse.   They have a special lunch menu that offers, some popular items at a major savings. I guess you get what you pay for. I ordered the Bobby's Double with Cheese. This is two 4 oz burgers grilled, served on a toasted bun with American Cheese. The menu said, it came with Steak Fries, when it arrived at my table they were regular fries. I tried three fries and they left an aftertaste in my mouth, so I tried the burger. The patties were so over grilled that they were dried out. The cheese appeared to be processed cheese from a shrink wrapper. Two bites of the burger and I gave up. I pushed the basket aside and tried numerous times to get the attention of my waitress for a check.   When my waitress finally came over, she did ask if I wanted a box. When I declined, she asked me if anything was wrong - I told her to just bring me my check and I'd go. I was willing to pay for my uneaten lunch.  I watched as she spoke with another staff member. When she came back with my check, she did have my lunch removed. I paid only for my beer. That customer service gesture got them a 2 Star rating over a 1 Star. She also asked me to elaborate on what was wrong so she can let management know.  She seemed shocked when I told her how bad the food was.   I agree with, Joe D., I think training is an issue here. Perhaps they opened to soon. The table next to me was also grumbling about the service and quality of food.   Like Joe D., I will not be going back when I have other better quality restaurants in my hood.   When: October 24, 2016 Why: New restaurant in my hood

It's National Donut Day and I needed to celebrate. Actually, what I really needed was a donut. I have not had a donut since last year. I'm trying to lose weight and donuts are one of my weaknesses, so I have avoided them. Can you think of a better time to give in to the urge? It's donut day!   Instead of going to one of my regular and favorite donut shops, I decided to celebrate somewhere new. I had heard great things about this little mom & pop shop, so here is where I celebrated. My go to order for donuts, is always pretty much the same. I stay with the classics, a Glazed Donut and a Chocolate Long John.   As everyone has stated, this shop is small. Actually, it is very small. The display cases are at unusual angles, making the waiting area for customer very compact. The selections of donuts is limited. When I arrived around 10:30AM, there were many empty trays. So they must of had a very successful morning.   Jessica M.'s husband can laugh at me, too. These donuts are dense and fluffy at the same time. After eating my two, I did not feel weighted down. These donuts were also, not overly sweet. The chocolate was a lighter chocolate, which did not sit well with me. It was good, but I prefer a darker and richer chocolate on mine. The Glazed donut was flavorful and had just enough glaze added to its outside. Other donuts shops, overly glazed and you're constantly having to wipe your fingers.   Staff was obviously two generations working in a family business. My two donuts were only $1.60. What a deal. You're not paying for ambiance. Your paying for just donuts.   I'll be back? - It's good, but next time I'll go back to my usual.   When: June 7, 2019 Why: National Donut Day

Recently we strayed away from Fortune Express after they messed up a carry out order. They also served up an order of Egg Drop soup that looked like a mixture of ED and Hot and Sour Soup. Now we're bored with our new fast food Chinese restaurant and thought it was time to let bygones be bygones and come back to FE and we're glad that we did.   When I have Chinese, I have to have an Egg Roll. It is just one of those weird Steven B. unwritten rules and I am always pleased with the ones I receive at FE. We shared an order of Crab Rangoon (5), which you can get FREE if you have the coupon on the back of their menu and spend over $15. Giving you a savings of $2.50.  The SO doesn't do Egg Rolls so he ordered Pot Stickers (6) as his extra treat. They were okay, it was kind of obvious that they were a frozen product and not made in house.   My entree was Hunan Chicken and instead of the traditional Steamed Rice, I choose Fried Rice which I think really made this spicy dish pop. A half order and I still had enough left over to enjoy at work the next day. The SO went off typical path and enjoyed Chicken Low Mein. Proving that, change is good.   So you know where this little Chinese restaurant is located, it is across the street (only a 100 ft) from Ted Drews.

It ain't Grandma's Sunday Fried Chicken, but it's fried chicken done fast.   I like the fact that they offer Oven-Roast, Crispy+Spicy as well as their Famous Recipe. Have no idea what their famous recipe is about, I am a crispy+spicy fan. Their pieces seem to be larger then most of the other "fast" fried chicken coops (chain & local) in town. Which is great, because when I'm craving fried chicken I want BIG pieces.   One thing that gives Lee's a cutting edge above KFC, is the fact they offer gizzards and livers. They may not be as yummy as those served at Pat's Bar on Oakland, but they can satisfy a gizzard craving. I know it is weird for those who know me, I will not eat tongue or Thumper but I will eat a gizzard.   Lee's biscuits are buttery good. Flaky and moist not dried out like those I have experienced else where. The gravy they add to the I am fairly sure instant potatoes, makes them more then palatable. It's better then Heinz Gravy in a jar. Their cole slaw is cole slaw, all the chicken places seem to taste pretty much the same. The green beans are the best side to pair up with your mashed taters. They're seasoned with bacon and onion and would make a Southerner proud.   Another thing that Lee's has done right and would make the same Southerner proud is the ice tea. The sweet tea would have Paula Deen doing cartwheels at a family reunion. I recommend buying it by the gallon, one glass will not do.

You've heard of the "Never Ending Story", well Dunaway Books is the never ending bookstore. There are bookcases after bookcases on the first floor and mezzanine. As if that weren't enough for you to browse through, the basement is full of more treasured reads.   Each bookcase or section is plainly labeled to make your search easy. They also have little maps like at an amusement park stating, "you are here" and showing you where you need to go for the type of book you have on your shopping list.   When shopping most used bookstores, they feel musty and dusty to me, but not here at Dunaway. It is well organized and very well kept. The salesman with his British accent made me feel like I was in an old 40's black and white movie and he was the shopkeeper.   I didn't find the two books I was searching for, but this place impressed me just the same and I am now a fan. I recommend this bookstore to any avid reader aka bookworm. It will totally give them a readers orgasm if there is such a thing.

That perky little red head Wendy is back in town and she is totally changing the game of fast food burgers. She is giving you an upscale contemporary dining room with fireplace, flat screen TV, high tech coke machine and a bakery case equal to Starbucks.  I've never seen a fast food restaurant look this good.   Her Value Menu can not be beat, all the items are 99¢. For a small lunch or late night snack you can not go wrong. When the burger urge hits, I now know where I will be going. In addition to the square burger, I'll be enjoying a cup of chili and Frosty. To my surprise Frosty is now available in vanilla. I remember the early days of Wendy when it's only flavor was chocolate.   The staff is friendly and I hope they can keep the positive attitudes beyond their Grand Opening.

3.5 Stars. Wish it could be 4, but it's easily 3.5.   I enjoyed the Lamb Chop Kabobs. They were extremely tender and were seasoned well. The flavor was actually good.  However, for the price, I felt cheated by the thinly sliced chops. There may have been four chops, but their size was still extremely small.   My entree was accompanied by rice and a  small mixed greens salad. The rice was bland and dry. With the number of entrees that include rice, I was expecting to be blown away and it was a disappointment. The mixed greens salad was actually the best thing of my meal. I added, feta cheese to mine. Wasn't told it would be a $1 uncharge, but it was worth it - I love my cheese.   As stated by Mary H., the service was ho hum. Our server had zero personality and couldn't remember who got what. Also, she took the drink orders for our table and missed me. I was all game for a gin cocktail, but ended up enjoying a glass of St Louis water. By the time she circled back to our table, food was being served and I was over the craving for Gin.   I'll be back? - I doubt it. For the price and service, I wont be in a hurry.   When: January 29, 2018 Why: Dinner / ISC

Yippie! I no longer have to drive over to Belleville to enjoy the best Pork Steak in the metro area. Now that the Beast has opened in The Grove, their Pork Steak can be billed the best in the state of MO.   Their Pork Steak is so delicious from the seasonings of the dry rub, there is no need to use any sauce. It is also so tender, there's no need to use the steak knife that is provided. I was able to pull and tear it apart into small bite size pieces without using the knife.   The sides are sold separately. To accompany my huge pork steak, I choose; Bacon-Mac and Brussels Sprouts with Belly. How could I go wrong with either of these. The Mac was rich and creamy with cheese and then adding bacon made it even yummier. The Brussels Sprouts were crisp and served with pieces of pork belly. What a great way to get your green vegetable in for the day.   The restaurant is order at a counter and find a seat with a table marker. Runners will then bring you your order on sheet trays. Ambiance is retro contemporary minimalist (if that can be a thing). The staff is friendly and attentive, very similar to that of the original location in Belleville.   I'll be back? -Yes, I love that Pork Steak  When: June 15, 2019 Why: Grand Opening

Great neighborhood nursery.   They offer a good selection of perennials and shrubs. All of my hanging baskets come from here each year and they survive the entire season.   Their staff is very knowledgeable. When I bought plants at a competitor and they got sick, the staff still coached me into saving my plant.   Best prices on stepping stones and garden statues.

Hogtown is a great addition to Dogtown.   When I heard that Hogtown Smokehouse was opening in Dogtown, I thought to myself, does St. Louis really need another BBQ joint. After enjoying their pork steak which is only available for dinner this evening, I am so happy that they have opened.   Their pork steak was fork tender. I was able to pull bite size pieces from the steak, without even using my knife. I did however, use the plastic knife to make it easier. I just wanted you to understand how tender and mouthwatering this pork steak was. It was a thin cut steak and had just enough sauce that I did not need to add any other sauces.   The pork steak came with one side, but I paid extra to have two. I choose, pit beans and one the recommendation of the bartender, my second side was Mac and Cheese. I enjoyed both of them. The Pit Beans, had bite size pieces of sausage, that gave them a spicy kick. Their Mac and Cheese was made with Rotini, which is my favorite pasta noodle. The sauce coating the noodles was thick and creamy. For my own personal taste, I would have liked some red pepper flakes added to it, or seasoned well with white pepper for that extra kick.   Hogtown is a order at the bar, take a table marker and find a seat type restaurant. Which is very similar to some of our other popular BBQ joints in STL. The bartender was friendly and I appreciated her side recommendation. I also chatted with the food runner and Rico an owner. They all were equally friendly and appreciative of my business.   There's a full bar with a wide selection of national beers and local craft beers. They even have a decent selection of wine to accompany your BBQ. Another big perk is their patio in back is dog friendly.   I'll be back: Got Brisket, Pulled Pork and Turkey still to try.   When: September 5, 2019 Why: Dinner - Hot & New on Yelp

Sometimes you just need to let the professionals do the packing and shipping. When one of those times arise, I come to the UPS and let them do it for me.   I bought an owl cookie jar for my cousins birthday gift, along with other miscellaneous smaller gifts. My original plan was to drive them down to Columbia, MO myself. However, life happens and my schedule changed up and I needed to get his gifts to him pronto.   His three gifts were all wrapped in gift paper and the greeting card celebrating his 29th birthday was ready to go. When I arrived at the store, I was immediately greeted by a cheerful staff member. He listened to my needs and asked if any of the items were fragile. When I told him yes, he explained the necessity of using a larger box to accommodate the bubble to protect my fabulous gift.   After completing the paperwork, he gave me a tracking number and informed me that my gifts would arrive the next day. I texted the tracking number to my cuz so he'd know he had a surprise waiting for him when he got off work.   UPS rescued me, delivered my gifts quickly and safe. The price was more then a tank of gas, but it was well worth it. My time is valuable and this saved me big time.   I'll be back? - If the need arises, I use them again and again.   When: January 29, 2018 Why: Shipping priceless birthday gifts.

A fantastic little Mom & Pop hardware store with excellent customer service. I was in need of a stiff bristle brush to clean the BBQ grill and did not want to venture that far from my hood. Since I was out running other errands in the neighborhood like getting my 4th of July tan at Tan Co., I stopped by STVH to see if they had what I needed.   As I entered the store, I was immediately greeted by a young man and asked what I needed. I told him what I needed he walked me over to a variety of brushes that meet my needs. When I commented it was to clean the BBQ grill, he picked one up that also had a scrapper attached and said, "I recommend this one." He was right, it was perfect and exactly what I was hoping for.   The same associate then walked me to the check out and proceeded to ring me out and close the sale. He then thanked me, wished me a happy holiday and asked me to come back again. My entire shopping experience was with one person, how refreshing.  I was in and out of there with what i needed in under 5 minutes.   Who needs a Big Box store when you have Big Service at a mom & pop store. Support your hood, shop local.

I love this soap. I bought it once just to try it and now I am hooked. I originally went in to just look at the gift items and the aroma of the soaps pulled me in further. I originally bought a couple bars of different vanilla themed bars. I couldn't believe how soft my skin started to feel after just a couple showers.   In addition to buying full sized bars, I also buy boxes of the samplers to try try different fragrances and ingredients. All the soaps are hand made in small  batches and all natural ingredients. Until recently I didn't know and I quote from their sampler box, " sammysoap is a job-creation machine for adults with intellectual disabilities discussed as the world's best soap company. We are not a not-for-profit. We provide real, gainful employment by managing to the strengths of our employees to create the best soap around." Wow, another great reason to support our local business, they truly are paying it forward.   I just don't love their soaps, they've got great gift items as well. Next time your at The Bug Store of dining a Billy G's, stop by sammysoaps. You'll be amazed at the quality and affordable pricing.   When: Often  Why: Best Soap in town.

Fallon's is a great local bar. Being next to a popular BBQ joint, it sometimes does not get the recognition that it deserves. They serve up a good variety of craft beers, many of them local. Best of all, their food is way better then your typical bar food.   I was motivated to stop by today, to support their fundraiser for the Down Syndrome Association of Greater St. Louis. They were donating $1 for every pint and . 50 for every can of Great Divide Brewing Co.. They're doing this for the entire month of May.   While enjoying a couple pints of GDB's Titan, my friend who has a down syndrome grandchild and I shared a couple of the most popular items at Fallon's. We shared an order of chicken wings and split and split a Reuben Sandwich with fries. It was more then enough food. We were both stuffed sharing these items.   The chicken wings were meaty and as other reviewers have commented, they have a perfect blend of heat and sweet. I'm a counter and I was pleased to see that they serve up the exact same number of flats and drums.    What makes their reuben stand out from your typical deli reuben, is that they serve theirs on a rye hoagie. The hoagie was a nice twist, to the typical sliced rye bread. They also, bake the corned beef in house, before topping it with sauerkraut and melted swiss cheese.   Our servers, were great. All of them were friendly and attentive. Dan one of the owners even came by our table and talked about their fund raiser. I love it when a local business gives back to a local charity.    I'll be back? - Yep.   When: May 16, 2019 Why: Lunch & Fund Raiser

I am happy to announce that Crusoe's Original is no longer on my Terrible Two's List. It is now on my The Yelp 100 Challenge and Entertainment Coupon Book List.   Being  lazy, neither of us wanted to cook dinner last night. So I grabbed our Entertainment Coupon book and thought we'd might as well make it a night of savings. I knew my earlier experience at Crusoe's Original  had not been good, but so many of my Yelp friends gave it a thumbs up that we thought we'd give it a try. Besides, we had a BOGO coupon and that always makes things better.  We arrived at peak dinner time (for south city) 5:45 PM and had about a 10-12 minute wait for a table. We could see a few two tops available, but they still had us wait and I am glad they did. When were seated, they gave us a four top which is much more comfortable for two grown men. I just always feel cramped when eating with another diner at one of those small tables.   Once we were seated, Jessica our waitress immediately came up and cheerfully introduced herself and her trainee for the night. I always let my server know up front when I am using any type of coupon. When I shared this news with Jessica, she said that would be great training for the new girl because she had not done an Entertainment coupon yet. We then ordered Ice Tea and Onion Strings. Before leaving home, we scoped out their website so we already knew what we wanted.   Our opinion of the Onion Strings differed. We both agreed their presentation, ease for eating and sauce were better then Pat's. However, on the seasoning and flavor we did differ. The SO preferred CO and I still remain loyal to Pat's for having the best Onion Strings in the Lou. CO's are good and I'll most likely have them again, but I have my loyalty.   Normally  we both order different entrees so we can experience more, but when they boosted that their fried chicken was the best of all the Saint Louis area we had to see for ourselves. The entree came with two sides and each additional side is 99¢ with a limit of 2 additional. Who can eat that many sides? Any way, again we ordered the same sides which were a dinner salad and baked potato.   I am not a fan of iceberg lettuce and that is what their dinner salad was made of, so it got a thumbs down for me. Next time I'll know to order another green vegetable instead. The baked potato was a fair side and done perfectly well. I enjoy eating the skin on my baked potato and here the skin was soft and not dried out making it very enjoyable.   Best fried chicken in all of the Saint Louis area? No. Not for me or the SO. We enjoyed it, but other establishments would receive the title before they do. The pieces were above average in size, just the right amount of breading  and the meat was moist and juicy.   Being a half chicken, it was a lot of food and we each only ate two pieces. Which means we had lunch for the next day. As we enjoyed our chicken the SO quipped, "I wonder if this is the type that is better cold?" I just had my lunch at work and the breast I brought with me, is better. It seems that the seasoning, became more flavorful over night.   Since I was using a coupon, Jessica knew I liked to save $ and encouraged me to sign up for their rewards card, "Shipwrecked Island". Just for signing up, we'll get a free appetizer on our next visit. Another bonus of the card is that infamous free birthday meal that I love so much. Looks like Crusoe's may be added to another list come this November.    Crusoe's is dog friendly. No you can't bring your dog in the restaurant, but as you are leaving they have dog treats in a goodies bag so you can take one home to your K-9 friend.   With a rewards card and seven more Entertainment coupons in my collection, I know I will be back to Crusoe's Original to check out their burgers, wings and so much more.

Definitely the best of our three Whole Foods stores. The salad and hot food bars are going to be a big draw for the employees of the Barnes and Cortex campuses. It is easily accessible from all areas of the CWE and the parking garage eliminates the nightmares of the parking lot at the Brentwood store.   This location has the same high quality meat and seafood departments as the other locations. The produce selection outshines any of the other grocery stores within the CWE neighborhood as well. It's obvious they took the width of the aisle into consideration when designing this store. They are much wider and easier to navigate with shopping carts.   As with all WF stores, the staff is eager to offer friendly and professional assistance.   Whole Foods is a great addition to the Central West End. My future shopping trips to WF will be done here.   When: May 25, 2016 Why: Grand Opening

I was at work with no "brown bag" lunch and was starving. Didn't want a fast food burger and fries. Nor did I want tacos or burrito from South of the Boarder. What was I to do, with no breakfast I really was famished. I guess my only option is pizza, to satisfy these hunger pains.    The next step was who to order my savory pie from. No to the Square by Compare and I didn't want "Poppa in my house" or at my work. That narrowed it down to Pizza Hut, which actually is the closest. I opted for carryout, since they're less then a mile away. I called up as soon as they opened and ordered a Spicy Sicilian Hand Tossed Medium Pizza. Which is Seasoned Beef, Italian Sausage, Sweet Red Onion and Spicy Jalapeños and Cheese. They said it would be ready in 15 minutes. Oh, the joys of being the first order of the day.   I waited 15 minutes and the left the office. When I arrived my order was just coming out of the oven. Fresh pizza, to satisfy my hunger pains. The staff was friendly when I entered and when the young lady brought my pizza to the counter, she asked me if I wanted to see my pizza. I responded, "sure". I thought that was a nice touch, to show me my pie before I left. It looked good.   Back at work, I couldn't wait to have my first slice. I am not sure if it was because I was so hungry, but this pizza was damn good. I game plan was to only eat a few slices, leave some at work for the next day lunch and take a few slices home. I will tell that did not happen, because I ate the whole thing. I ate the entire medium pizza all by myself. I enjoyed it and hope the next time I order, it is as good as this experience.

The Boathouse is a delightful venue for a reception after a beautiful wedding at, The Jewel Box. It is only a short drive through one of the most stunningly beautiful parks not only in STL, but the entire USA.   The reception I attended was held in the Annex which is a separate area from hustle and bustle of the public area. Within the annex we had our own restrooms and most importantly our own bar. (A quick shout-out to the bartenders for doing a great job.)  The annex was air conditioned giving us comfort from the 90° weather. The space is also large enough for a DJ, dancing and for 100+ guest to mingle before and after dinner. We also had our own patio area to sit, mingle and celebrate.   For dinner, we were seated outside under large white tents. All the tables were set with white linens, china and wooden white chairs. It all looked so pristine. It had a true country club vibe.   Our food was served buffet line, but each dish had a server for safety during this pandemic. The kitchen at The Boathouse is run by the infamous SugarFire BBQ and our host took advantage of it. Having a late summer wedding, the served up Brisket, Fresh Green Beans, Scalloped Potatoes and more. The food was delicious and the serving staff was charming and professional.   If you are looking for a private event space for a special intimate celebration, be sure to check this place out. It has my recommendation.   When: September 12, 2021 Why: BFF Wedding Reception

Good little sandwich emporium and I do mean little. If you are claustrophobic, get your order to go. The small dining area can get very crowded with those ordering and waiting for their carryout.   We ordered two sandwiches; Club Med and Big Bend Mafia and shared an order of regular chips. The Big Bend Mafia was the best of the two, a combination of Italian Beef and Salsiccia with provolone on a garlic hoagie was excellent. The salsiccia was grilled, which made the flavor pop.   Club Med was served on flat-bread which made for a messy eat. The grilled zucchini and summer squash, with grilled chicken and goat cheese was fantastic. It was topped with lemon-oregano vinaigrette which add flavor, but made for a liquidity messy eat.   The regular chips get a big thumbs down, they had no flavor and were greasy. They'd be better off serving hometown favorite "Billy Goat Chips" or some other popular bagged chips.  The staff was extremely friendly and proudly promoted their menu. With the crowd that was present, I was shocked how fast our order was ready. Neither of our sandwiches were cut in half, but when asked they did so and brought them back to our table. Due to the size of the sandwiches, you'd think they'd do it automatically.   We'll be going back to try Miss Piggy and The Black N Blue.

I was given a McDonald's Gift Card, with a note telling me not every meal out needs to be a "Yelp" night out. My cousin told me, "You need to slum it once in a while". I carried it in my wallet for almost a year, before I finally used it. Many times I thought of giving it to a homeless person begging at a stoplight, but I'd always give them a dollar instead.   The other day, I skipped breakfast and as lunch approached I was starving. I was pressed for time and wanted something quick. I just passed a billboard promoting McDonald's new Triple Cheeseburger and thought of my gift card. I pulled in to the first McDonald's I saw and placed my order.   It was a simple order, a Triple Cheeseburger and Coke. My Coke was cold and refreshing. I enjoy an occasional fountain soda. Especially if the soda lines are kept clean, like these were. The soda taste so much better.   My Triple Cheeseburger on the other hand was disappointing. It had me wondering if I really was eating beef. Yes, it was fresh and hot but lacked any flavor. It was on special for $2 and I still feel as if I overpaid.   Staff is friendly and fast, as it should be at a fast food joint.

Great store!  I discovered Batteries Plus earlier this year out in Creve Coeur and immediately look for one closer to home. I love the fact that they recycle batteries and light bulbs for you. Which helps protect our environment, something to keep in mind as Earth Day approaches.   This store is older then the West County store, but that gives it some rustic charm. However, the customer service is the same having a knowledgeable and friendly staff.   This is my store of choice for batteries and light bulbs.

Five Below is a fun store and gives new meaning to the $ store. Instead of everything being a dollar, it can be any dollar amount up to 5.   It is a great store to shop for things you really do not need or want at bargain prices.  If you've got a young child to buy for, this is a fun store. We grabbed a couple of goodies for the little girl next door and she loved it.   They've got travel size toiletries, school supplies, DVDs, toys, hair accessories and so much more. If you are on budget, Five Below may be able to help you stretch those $'s.

Hooray, for Gus's! I attended their soft opening and have been back a couple of times so I can honestly say, "I am a fan."   Gus's fried chicken may be world famous, but it may take awhile before it is St. Louis famous. After all we are in the Show-Me-State and the people of STL love their Hodak's and Porter's. I personally think Gus's is far beyond those two in quality of fried chicken. They out shine them in seasoning and flavor. Gus's pieces are juicy on the inside and crispy on the outside, the way Southern fried chicken is suppose to be. Also, the size of the pieces will not disappoint you. When referring to pieces of fried chicken, size does matter.   For some taste buds, Gus's may be to spicy. I'll admit, as I enjoyed my chicken I did have to blot little beads of sweat on my forehead. To me, that is a sign of a good spicy chicken. My friend who dined with me once, said it was too spicy for her and that she'd most likely not return. Me on the other hand, Gus's will most likely be my go to for fast fried chicken.   On two different visits, I tried a couple of their appetizers and both of them did not disappoint.  I am a huge fan of Fried Pickles and was impressed with the thick breading that they used on the dill spears. I am so use to seeing fried pickle chips, that it was a pleasant surprise to see spears. The breading was crisp and when you bite into the pickle, it was extremely warm inside...again, nice touch.   The second app I tried was a true Southern delight; Fried Green Tomatoes. The slices were thick and they had the same bread coating as the Fried Pickles. I know that makes it easier in the kitchen, but a difference in coatings would have set these two apart. However, they were still an excellent choice and I am glad Fannie Flagg wasn't with me, because she probably would not have shared.  Each time I've gone, I've had the same sides. I know, I need to try the others, but the Mac-n-Cheese is so good. It reminded me of some of the mac-n-cheese I enjoyed as a child at family picnics. The cole slaw is good, but being a pepper man, I had to add a few shakes of my favorite spice.   In closing I'll give a quick shout out to their sweet tea. Usually a Southern restaurant makes the sweet tea overly sweet, but Gus has tweaked it just right. Also, what is a Southern dinner without a slice of pie? It's a dinner that is not complete, so order up and enjoy a slice of Pe-can pie, because u-can.   When: Multiple Times Why: Fried Chicken

El Mezcal is the closest Mexican restaurant to my new home. It's not the best, but when you're craving some South of the Border fare, it does the trick. Actually, I think as with any restaurant I need to discover what is good and stick with that as a standard order.   The Margaritas are not hand shaken, but they satisfy the craving. I paired mine with a half order of Chicken Nachos with added jalapeños. This is a dish worth repeating. The tortilla chips were heavily topped with both shredded chicken,  diced jalapeños and that good ole white Mexican cheese.   In addition to my nachos, I ordered a Beef Burrito and a Fried Taco off the Sides menu. Being ordered as a side, I thought they'd be smaller. I was wrong, I ordered way to much food. However, on the bright side I got to experience more of their menu. The beef burrito was your typical fast casual Mexican, it was satisfying, but not memorable.   I don't remember fried tacos being a thing in STL, except for Jack in the Box. Over here in IL, every Mexican or river pub offers, "Fried Tacos". Personally, just give me a classic crunchy taco or a soft taco and I'm a happy camper. Thus far, I have only experienced one fried taco that I've liked and the one here wasn't it. I will not be ordering the one from here again, it was just to weird.   The service was attentive and they were doing a decent job following the guidelines for safe dining during this pandemic. Mask were being worn by all visible staff and they required all guest to wear them upon entry and moving about the restaurant.   A fellow Yelper recommends the Carnitas Tacos, so they'll be the next thing I order.   When: February 22, 2021 Why: Dinner

If you are on, The Hill and need a cup of Joe to keep you going or to start your day, Shaw's is the place to go. They are by far the absolute best coffee shop on The Hill. I myself have been known to stop by for an iced coffee, just simply because I am in the neighborhood.   They've been serving, The Hill and STL community for over 20 years. What I like best is that they do their own roasting and do it multiple times during the week so the coffee is always super fresh.   The Baristas also help with the weekly roasting, so they have a true love and knowledge of the coffee bean. A good barista is like a good bartender, so be sure to tip accordingly.   When: March 5, 2021 Why: A morning cup of coffee.

Hell has frozen over, pigs are flying and I am defiantly going to hell. The only way all three of these could happen is because I shopped at Walmart.  The only time I shop a Walmart is when I am desperate and Easter Sunday I was really desperate. I had to work, so I did not plan ahead for Easter Sunday dinner when I got work. It wasn't till I was at work that I called home and sent them to SugarFire to pick up a smoked ham. Then I quickly was piecing together the rest of the menu to create a memorable meal. You can tell I no longer work in retail, I totally forgot most stores are closed Easter Sunday.   I needed fresh vegetables, primarily spinach for side dishes. As I drove home, I stopped at convenience stores and they were not making things convenient for me. As I drove down Route 3, my regular Aldi's was closed celebrating the holiday. In the distance I could see at the next stoplight, the Walmart was open. Gotta love the Walton family for making their employees work on a religious holiday when other retailers are letting their employees spend time with family.   I swallowed my pride and pulled in to the parking lot. I was shocked to see how full it was at 5PM on a holiday. As I walked towards the entrance, I asked forgiveness for the sin I was about to commit entering this hell hole. At the same time I was also hoping that they had a grocery department to fulfill my needs and get me out of my dilemma.   WOW! As I entered the main entrance I was smack dab in the middle of a huge fresh produce department. I immediately found spinach, sliced portabella mushrooms and arugula. Glancing around I was impressed with the freshness and prices. I quickly gathered my veggies together and headed to the check out.   This Walmart was nothing like the ones I have experienced in Missouri. It was brightly lighted, clean, well laid out and the associates I had contact with were pleasant. Again, I wonder if being located in a smaller town doesn't make a big boxer retailer better.   Seriously this probably should be a 4 Star review, after all they did save my Easter dinner. However, I just do not have it in me to give 4 Stars to Walmart.

Why did I ever leave you BOB? It was that new circle of friends that lead me a stray. They didn't care for you and I just went with the flow. I was so wrong, I should have sneaked off and seen you on the side. Then it would have been just you and I one on one. You fulfilling my needs, with those succulent oysters.   I was so glad that when I finally returned after our separation which had been way to long that you welcomed me with open shells. You let the past be behind us and served me up a meal that had me ashamed that I ever left you. I am so glad that my new SO loves you as much as I do and we look forward to many threesomes.   Our night begun with Broadway Shooters, Mussels and Voodoo Wings. You knew I loved Vodka and couldn't go wrong with those shooters. They went down oh so smooth. The tomato garlic wine broth was a good companion for the mussels and soaking up the broth with bread was an added bonus. Your tequila hot sauce for our wings made them taste like no other wing I have ever had.   Then our server who was so friendly brought us a second round of beer to accompany our oysters on the half shell. I may be a vodka man, but the gin cocktail sauce that is served with the oysters make them pop right out of their shell.  Time finally rolled around for our entrees; BBQ Shrimp and Fried Catfish. The shrimp were huge and lived up to your claim of them being an NOLA classic. My Catfish Dinner was top notch. The only time I have had better catfish is up in Grafton on the river and that is had to beat.   My only dislike on our reunion was the Cajun Chips. They just didn't do anything for me, but you did the right thing by removing them from my bill. I am so happy that we have been reunited and look forward to many more encounters.

If I could turn back time, if I could turn back time If I could turn back time, oh baby -  I'd be setting at the bar at Tick Tock Tavern, having a drink with you And munching on a Hot Dog from Steve's next door  TTT is a dive bar that is stuck in a time warp, with class. The drinks are good, strong and cheap. Not only is the staff friendly, they're eager to know your name and make you feel like a regular. Each of the bartenders introduced themselves to us and asked us our names. I found that to be a real nice personalized touch.   A bonus to TTT, is the fact that a side door inside connects the dive bar to Steve's Hot Dogs new location. This is a perfect set up. You can slam down a couple of beers, order hot dogs from Steve and watch your favorite home town sports team on TV. What really kicks ass is the staff from Steve's will bring it over to you when its ready.  Tick Tock Tavern, you're my new favorite dive bar.

Cute and simple cafe. Not only do they offer hand brewed coffee, but you can get a shrub cocktail or a mimosa to start your day.   I was impressed with the pour over, Chemex preparation of my coffee. They use Perc Coffee which is out of Savannah, GA. It's a decent coffee, but with all the great coffee roaster here in STL, I wish they supported another local business.   As of now, the pastry offering are minimal. However, I must say they are very good. I was surprised to find out they are done in house. I devoured a Spinach & Feta Croissant and thought it was from a popular French bakery out in West County. It was that good.   The only negative I will comment on, is the service. The staff was not friendly or engaging.  In fact as I watched them during my visit, they hardly smiled. They almost were robot like.  Smile, engage and encourage me to return. It's a great place, if they kick up the customer service.   Will I return? - Yes, I'll give them another try.   When: November 2, 2017 Why: Morning Coffee

WOW! Amazing food, I was totally blown away how good everything I ordered was. I was also amazed at the portion sizes. Even the small plates were healthy servings. Excellent food, with friendly and helpful service makes it easy for me to give Tai Ke 5 Stars after only one visit. I already know I will be back for more.   Tonight I was with a large group of about 15 diners. It was our monthly gathering of International Supper Club. First I gotta give a shout out of thanks to Kevin and Christine W. for guiding us unexperienced diners in Taiwanese cuisine. With their suggestions and also those of the staff, who answered as many questions and explained things with patience and professionalism.   I started out with a Street Snack, The Rice Sticky Hot Dog. It really isn't a hot dog, but a small Chinese sausage, wrapped aka sitting on top of a bun made of sticky rice. It had a bit of a sweet taste and adding some of the hot chili sauce that was on the table, gave it a real nice kick.   My eyes were way bigger then my stomach. I read a previous review and a Yelper said the portions were small, I shouldn't have believed her. They are huge, at least to me. Anyway, I ordered the; Braised Beef Noodle Soup and the Signature Three Cup Chicken. Both of these are an entire meal by themselves. The chicken comes with white rice, but I enjoyed mine just by it self.  The Braised Beef Noodle Soup was enough for two people to enjoy. It was a bowl full of rich dark beef stock and thick noodles prepared to perfection. The meat was tender and flavorful. At first I was afraid of MSG, but if they had used it, I would already have a major headache and I don't so that is good news for me. I wish they offered this in a smaller bowl, because I'd enjoy it before an entree, instead of having it as an entree.   I know other reviewers have stated it, and it is true. Everyone should order and enjoy the Signature Three Cup Chicken at least once. It is bone in chicken chopped up and served in a clay pot. They had a challenge getting the lid off of mine, the steam had it held on tight. The chicken is simmered in a sauce of soy sauce, sesame oil and rice wine. It also had a strong ginger taste that was pleasant to the palate. Others were enjoying theirs with white rice, but watching carbs, as stated earlier, I ate mine without and it was still top notch.   The ambiance is - nothing. It is a simple plain as plain can be dining room and that works for them. The food is so delicious and the service so attentive, that you don't need more ambiance.   So many of my friends entrees looked equally as appealing as mine. I will definitely be coming back here for lunch or dinner to experience more and more of this extensive menu.   Ian Froeb's was right, this is one of the Best 100 restaurants in STL.   When: September 21, 2016 Why: International Supper Club and Ian Froeb's STL 100

I've been shopping here for 4 years and can say, the service has consistently been top notch.  The staff may have changed time to time, but the friendliness and professionalism has always been the same. Light bulbs and batteries aren't like they use to be, they are getting more and more specialized and at times you need guidance to make sure you are making the right purchase.   Being an avid recycler, I do recycle everything that I possibly can. I've been a recycler since, the first Earth Day back in the 1970's. As stated in my previous review, recycling is one of the services they provide here at Batteries Plus Bulbs. When you come in to purchase your new bulbs, you can drop off the old ones and they'll make sure they are disposed of properly, so our environment is protected.   I said it before, this is my store of choice for batteries and light bulbs. They're items that I don't need that often, but when I do - this is my store.   When: September 23, 2016 Why: Batteries and Bulbs

I was craving cheap Chinese for lunch, so I headed over to Fortune Express. It was a simple lunch, I went with a Half Order of Beef Fried RIce, a single Eggroll and an order of Crab Rangoon.   As always, I had to have an Egg Roll with my Chinese food. FE does a good ER, so my craving was satisfied. I was also craving some Crab Rangoon. I know it really isn't Chinese, but it's American Chinese and when you're hungry, it's okay. However, today it wasn't okay and that is why I need to take a star away from Fortune Express. The pockets holding the filling, barely had anything in them. I was so disappointed.  My main dish, the Beef Fried RIce was excellent. It had plenty of beef and a half order was more then enough. With the two appetizers, I could only eat half of the half order.   It's a small family business, so the service is friendly and personable.   Would I return? - When I have a craving.   When: July 24, 2019 Why: Craving inexpensive Chinese

A coupon brought me back and they've now earned a spot on my Crispy Chicken List. We ordered the Spicy Crispy and our pieces were huge. They had the right amount of breading giving the chicken a flavorful crispy coating and a juicy meaty inside. The spicy flavoring beats Popeye's any day of the week. In fact, when I was leaving I think I saw him at the drive-up window.   As our side dishes we always choose mashed potatoes and gravy and cole slaw. I can not imagine eating fried chicken without smashed taters. If I want green beans, I just open a can at home or steam some fresh ones .  Lee's also gets bonus points for offering their livers as a side order.  Some other places only offer them as a meal and that is way to much liver for me.   This customer service on my last visit was impressive. The cashier was friendly and knew the importance of add on sales. As I ordered my ice tea she grinned and said, "I'm glad you ordered tea today, I was going to recommend it to you." As she processed my order, her coworkers were busy getting it ready. I seriously had no wait time at all. They were one well oiled machine, working as a team.   I've praised their sweet ice tea before and I'll do it again.......I LOVE IT!

Sometimes I am attracted to a business by a rant rather then a rave and that was the case with Everest Cafe. After my visit I could not find anything to rant about, all I found was things to rave about.   I will start out with their customer service, it was friendly and full of true hospitality. As our large group of 14 were dining, they made sure each diner felt like a VIP.   My meal begun with Miso Soup which had organic spinach and was by far the best Miso Soup I have ever had. I followed it up with Lamb Tarkari with Organic Vegetables.  It was so nice to see that the vegetables they serve are all organic.   I gotta get back and try their lunch buffet. I heard it is better then their dinner and their dinner was totally satisfying.

It is times like this, that I wish Yelp had little box we could check next to the stars that would add a half star to our rating. El Maguey is what it is and that is cheap Tex-Mex, but this time our food was REALLY good. So they deserve a bump in their stars, but not a full star.   We went out of our comfort zone and ordered something we had never ordered before. I ordered the lunch special Fajita Quesadillas with chicken. It basically is a quesadillas stuffed with all the goodies you'd get with a fajita platter along with some cheese. It was very good and filling, it may become my new regular order. However, when I order next time I'll ask if I can substitute re-fried beans for the rice.   The SO ordered the Fajita Burrito with beef off of the lunch specials and was equally as pleased as I was. Where I do not care for the rice here at El Maguey, the SO says they do a good job for a cheap Tex-Mex restaurant in the Midwest.   The servers work as a team here, so your glass never gets lower then half full and you can make a request to anyone walking by your table. All of the men (I've never seen a female) are all personable and will humor you when you try to speak Spanish.   Best thing about this lunch was we dined with an Entertainment.com coupon so we saved $6. That is almost two gallons of gas.

It is time for me to come out of the closet and admit, I am a "Craver". There, I've said it and I feel so much better admitting that I like White Castle. I not only like their "belly bombers", I enjoy the Breakfast Sliders and their new Grilled Chicken. I even like the crinkle cut french fries.   I am now excited that they are offering, My Size Meals for little cravers. If I can get away with ordering one with no child in sight, it will be the perfect size meal. I'll get to pick one from four entrees; an original slider, slider with cheese, savory chicken and 3 piece chicken rings. Then I can choose between two sides; Mott's apple sauce or kid size fries. As a beverage, I get to pick between Mott's 100% Apple Juice, Milk or a kid size soda. This will be perfect portion control for someone who is dieting.   I have always favored this location due to its closeness to my work. It makes it so easy to grab a quick breakfast slider and coffee in the morning. At lunch time, it is just a couple blocks away, making it so easy to grab the new Savory Chicken sandwich with those crinkle cut fries. A friendly staff helps the belly bombers go down.   Now that I've opened up and came out, I will be able to go to a White Castle near my home and hold my head up in pride.

Say, what? Yes, it is true. There is a vodka distillery in Bethalto. Who would have thought it? I wouldn't, I was totally surprised and I am glad my Yelp friend, Tina S. introduced me to this hidden delight.   When I say, hidden I do mean hidden. If I had not seen the sign by the road, I would have driven past it. Even when I pulled into the parking lot, I was saying to myself, this cannot be right. Then I saw the door simply labeled, Bluestem.   Once you are beyond the door, you are in a minimalist style bar with a friendly bartender. I hope you like vodka, because that is what they sell and it's what they offer. They're working on a "Gin" so hopefully they'll be offering that in the near future.   Just offering vodka is fine with me, because Dirty Martinis has recently been my go to cocktail. I was pleasantly surprised how smooth and silky the Bluestem vodka was. In fact it was so smooth, I enjoyed more than one Dirty. I was also surprised, I had no headache the next morning. Typically, when I drink an affordable vodka over a premium vodka, I may have a headache the next morning. So, I guess I can say Bluestem's quality is in the premium class.   If you need something to nosh on while sipping and drinking the vodka, they offer a variety of frozen pizzas. If that is not your thing, the restaurant near by will make deliveries to the distillery.   I had so much fun, I have joined the group that meets here once a month for Happy Hour.   When: February 26, 2021 Why: Happy Hour

When I was out experiencing Burger Week, I discovered J. Smugs had moved. They were no longer in the cute little renovated gas station on The Hill. They have relocated to the dark, seedy and dingy Gaslight Lounge, where Cha Cha Chow use to have their brick and mortar.   They may be in a new location, but the BBQ and the sides they prepare are still top notch. For Burger Week, Smugs served up a dynamite Brisket Burger with Bacon Jam. I added a nice slice of cheese to mine and added a side of fries.  The burger was tender, juicy and full of flavor. My fries were extra crispy. It was a perfect quick lunch. They get bonus points for toasting the bun, which for me is always a nice touch.   I miss the charm of the old location and the friendly customer service they had. I love me some Gaslight, in fact I was the First to Review them. However, the service is not the same now. The service is still good, but it has gone from a family restaurant to a dive bar service and atmosphere. So I'll just have to roll with it.   I'll be back? - Yes. Food is that good, but not happy about new location.   When: August 1, 2019 Why: Burger Week & new location.

Seriously? I am shocked that Ian Froeb put this restaurant on his STL 100 The Best Restaurants in St. Louis RIGHT NOW. It is just okay. It is nothing great and nothing memorable. It was an average meal at best. I'm not a professional food critic, but I wouldn't have selected them for my top 100.    Dining at lunch time, I took advantage of the Lunch Basket Special. I enjoyed a Beef Shawarma Sandwich and Seasoned Fries for only $6.99. It definetly was a good value for the price. It's made with thinly sliced beef, that has been seasoned and cooked on a rotisserie. It is wrapped in a fresh pita and garnished with; tahini sauce,tomatoes, onion, parsley, pickles and pickled turnip. Then they press the pita in a panini grill, giving the outside a nice toasted crust. After enjoying half of my sandwich, I tore it open and then I really realized how tender and flavorful the meat was. The fries that accompanied my sandwich were seasoned with Mediterranean spices, but should of been a little crisper.   I had a Orange Smoothie for my beverage, and was disappointed in the flavor and thickness. It was very thin and strong flavors of banana or orange did not come through.   The service was discombobulated. As other Yelpers have stated, they simply seem to be very disorganized. They tried to be friendly and attentive, but you could tell they were thinking of what they had to do next. Then they'd scurry off, to complete the next task at hand. Before leaving, I discovered they were short staffed, so that kind of explains the short attentiveness and hustling off to the next task.   Would I come back? Only if a friend asked me to join them.   When: September 12, 2016 Why: Ian Froeb's STL 100

Dewey's is a No Provel zone and for that I say, "Praise Jesus".  Pizza with Mozzarella cheese is so much better. Pizza cut like a pie is so much better then a square. Dewey's just on those two points, I like you "so much better".   The menu at Dewey's is simple, salad and pizza and they do both well. We ordered the small size salad which was the perfect portion to have before a 13" pie which is cut into 8 slices. To please everyone, we ordered a half & half pizza. As our toppings we choose; X - Pepperoni and Bronx Bomber. The Pepperoni was the best "pep" pizza I have ever had, that Mozzarella Cheese was a great accent to the Pepperoni.  Next time when I do not have to make others happy, it will be a whole Bronx Bomber.  The mixture of Pepperoni, Sausage, Black Olives, Mushrooms. Onion and that gooey melted Mozzarella Cheese was really the "Bomb".   Our salads were, Caesar, House and Peppercorn and each one was excellent in it's own right. As stated earlier our smalls were a good serving, so I can only imagine the large would be a meal or big enough for two to share.  We were celebrating a birthday and another big bonus is Dewey's does not sing "Happy Birthday" to the aging customer. They do not offer you a dessert like other restaurants. What they do offer you is better then a song and free dessert, which only last for a moment. They give you a Dewey's glass to take home, so you can remember your special birthday celebration again and again.

Let me say first off that I am not a regular Shop 'n Save shopper, but with what I experienced today that may be changing soon.   I was across the street at the new ka-ka-o Chocolate Store picking up Valentine chocolates and needed a few groceries so I just popped across to Shop 'n Save. After all, I just needed a few staples and a couple things for the dogs.   The merchandising was not like the two other leading grocers in our city, but the prices were great. For the humans in our household I needed milk and eggs. The dogs needed green beans and pure pumpkin. I was shocked at the low prices on their Del-Monte French Style Green Beans with No Salt. They're my dogs favorite, and it was the best price I've ever seen.  I couldn't find Pure Pumpkin which did not surprise me, after all it's not Thanksgiving. So I proceeded to the check out, where I had a very friendly and personable cashier. After checking out I stopped at the Customer Service to ask about the Pure Pumpkin and that is where the real service took off. I said, "I know it is out of season, but do you have Pure Pumpkin in stock?"   The lady working the desk assured me that they did and that it was in aisle five. I told her I looked there and did not see any. She popped out of her box and said let me go check for you. As she headed out, she asked how many would I like if she found some. I told her, I needed a large quantity and to just give me good directions.   She returned promptly, gave me excellent directions to the canned goods I needed and off I went. No wonder I couldn't find it, I'm short and it was on the top shelf. However, to my delight like the green beans the price was an affordable low low price. I grabbed a shrink wrapped case and headed off the cashier.   I loved it when the cashier and man behind me in line commented how I must be making lots of pies. I just grinned and said, no this is for my dogs they love pumpkin toppings their dry food.   As I walked out with my case of pumpkin, the lady in the customer service box waved good-bye.  Good prices, good customer service. I'll be back.

I've been back two more times and need to remove a star. The reason for the removal is solely based on service. The service is extremely slow and at times not that attentive.   On the 14th of November a group of us meet at the bar for Happy Hour. We took position at the corner making it easy for all of us to talk and to share a variety of appetizers. Our favorite appetizer as I've stated in my previous review was the Brussels Sprouts. They are totally the bomb.   What was frustrating, is that we had to flag the bartender down for additional drinks/beers and to remove our empty dishes. We ordered our appetizers two at a time and when they brought the new ones out, they did not clear the empty ones. This made for a very cluttered space for us to enjoy our evening.   Then on the 27th, I returned to see what their breakfast is all about.  I highly recommend that they save payroll hours and stop breakfast. Or only do Brunch on Saturday and Sunday. My Monday morning breakfast at 9 AM took forever. I will say, my sweet tooth enjoyed the Zeppole aka donut holes. As my main dish, I had the Veggie Frittata.  It was good, but the length of time it took to receive at my table in a practically empty restaurant was crazy.   Also, the morning staff struggled making my Bloody Mary and it was not near the quality I raved about in my first review. It was weak and tasted more like a V-8 then a spicy Bloody Mary. Pulled them off my Bloody Mary list.   The minor bumps I thought they'd get worked out by now, are still a struggle. Speed of service and attentiveness is what they need to focus on for the prices they are charging in this hood.   Will I return? - Not in a rush  When: November 14 and 27, 2017 Why: Happy Hour & Breakfast

I said, I'd come back and give them a second chance and I did. When Retreat Gastropub made Ian Froeb's STL 100 List, I knew now was the time. In my original review, I stated I wanted to come back and try the Mac-n-Cheese and a burger. Ian said, the must order item was the Farmhouse Burger, so I went with his recommendation. Thank you, Ian. My Farmhouse Burger was incredibly delicious.   Dining alone, I sat myself at the bar. I find bar dining to be relaxing and also an opportunity to meet new folks who are doing the same. As I pondered my order, I enjoyed a masterfully made Old Fashioned. My last visit, they had difficulty making a simple Manhattan, but this Old Fashion was done perfectly. It truly was a classic cocktail, made the old school way.  Should be no surprise that I ordered Mac-n-Cheese and a Farmhouse Burger. I did not realize that fries came with the burger, so my ordering the Mac-n-Cheese was way too much food. I took several bites of the MnC and enjoyed the three cheese blend. It was just enough coating on the large twisted noodles and a crispy topping. It was a large portion, so I had them box it up in a to-go vessel and will have it for lunch tomorrow. They get a bonus point for having eco-friendly containers for their carry-out.   My burger list here on Yelp may not be as prestigious, as Ian's Top 100, but Retreat Gastropub has earned a spot on there as well. This double patty smashed burger, topped with candied bacon, a fresh egg and cheese sauce on a alehouse bun would make any lover of burgers a fan of RG. I like how the fries were seasoned more with pepper then salt. It also pleased me that they offer ketchup in little cups instead of a bottle. That and linen napkins are two of my hot buttons.   The service was relaxing, friendly and attentive. They had great music playing in the background, but at times it was drowned out by the loud noise of all the other patrons enjoying themselves. The acoustics are not very good at RG, but what the hell.......I'm there for good cocktails, craft beer and food.

If your sweet tooth is acting up while you're in Alton, you need to head over to LuciAnna's Pastries. If you cannot find something in her pastry case to satisfy your sweet craving, that is on you. I was amazed at her variety of sweetness and thrilled that she had one of my favorite pies.   After a fabulous lunch up the street at, Brown Bag Bistro, my cousin and her friend wanted dessert so we headed up Broadway to LuciAnna's. LP just recently moved to this new location and the ladies wanted to check it out. I just wanted something sweet, my sweet tooth was aching big time. From what I was told, this new location is more spacious and inviting to the patron that wants to linger and enjoy their treat with a cup of coffee.   I have two favorite pies. One is, Traditional Pecan Pie and the other is, Chocolate Pecan Pie. The day I visited, LP had  decadent offering of the later. The precision positioning of the pecans on top of the chocolate, blew my mind. It truly was picture perfect and so was the rich chocolate flavor.   My cousin is a fan of Tiramisu and could not resist enjoying one of the thick slices on display. She said it was moist, extremely flavorful and a perfect accompaniment to her cup of black coffee. Her friend ordered the Chocolate Mousse Cheesecake. She made it to the table before the rest of us and started eating, so there is no picture of her delightful and delicious dessert. My cousin, informed her when dining with a seasoned Yelper like me, she has to wait for pictures to be taken before eating. Lesson learned. Next time she joins us, I may still give her a kind little reminder - LOL.   Again, if in Alton and you're craving pastries from a French trained chef, check out LuciAnna's. You'll be glad that you did. It's also a great intimate tea room to meet up with friends for a gab-fest.   I'll be back? - When in Alton do as the locals do - yes.   When: April 17, 2018 Why: Dessert

When I lived in the CWE, I was a regular at Dressel's. I'd easily eat there once a week. Since I moved to another hood in the city of STL, it fell out of my restaurant rotation. When I saw it listed in Ian Froeb's STL 100 for 2016, I knew it was time for me to go back and eat.  I stopped in for lunch and as usual took a spot at the bar. It's always fun sitting at the bar. I get to enjoy conversation with the mixologist and the servers as they come up to retrieve alcoholic beverages for their tables.   Since I hadn't been in awhile, I went with Ian's "Must Order" from his STL 100 list and order the burger. It was a classic pub burger, I'll say it is probably my favorite burger in Saint Louis now. Yes, it was that exquisite. It was perfectly prepared, medium. The only topping I had was cheese and I used no other garnishes, or ketchup or mustard. The natural flavor of beef and the seasonings used by the chef were enough to make this a perfect burger.   The handful of House Chips were the perfect accompaniment to the burger. I love my french fries crisp, but these chips were a little overly crisp. I like the chips to be less crispy. I enjoy them being kind of 3/4 crisp and a 1/4 limp. I know that is odd, but that's the way I like it.   I'll be back for another burger and to revisit other menu items that I use to love.  When: August 8, 2016 Why: Lunch & STL 100 List

Since my last review, I have now moved on to the east side of the river and this Friar Tuck is now the closest, "Big box" liquor store to my new home.  Since I now live on this side of the river, Friar Tuck is satisfying one of my vices by keeping me stocked with craft beers and whiskey.  On my recent visit, I was searching for mini bottles. I needed them for swag bags for a party I hosting. To my surprise they had an over-whelming selection. To my disappointment, they  did not have the quantity I needed in the brand I choose. However, the sales associate checked the back stock and provided top notch service. She even gave me a lead of where I might find what I was looking for.   Don't worry, she did not lose a sale. I still bought some craft beer and a couple of canned cocktails. The sale was just smaller and I am sure future sales will make up for the shortage on this visit. After all, the holidays are approaching.   When: October 20, 2021 Why: Shopping for mini bottles

I moved to this side of the river over a year ago. I felt guilty that I hadn't been to this WC, since my move. I blame that on the pandemic. However, I have corrected that and I am pleased to say, that they are still one of the better White Castles in the metro area.   The night of my visit, I choose to use the drive-thru. The line wasn't, too long and it was late. So I thought it was my best choice. To my surprise, the line went very quick and smooth. I might have to consider using it again in the future.   Lucky for me, they were still offering the, 1921 Slider in celebration of their 100 Years. I just gone one, so I could say I had it. It was just a typical cheese slider with tomato and lettuce. The tomato and lettuce did give it an extra boost of flavor. Glad I had one, I am loyal to my usual order.   Did you ask what my usual order is? Well, it is Combo #2 which is two DoubleCheese Sliders and a side of fries. I don't always add one, but tonight a side of crispy onion rings, hit the spot.   For a fast food staff, the staff here has always been consistently friendly and professional. A few of them are still here from when I started stopping by when I commuted to work from STL.   If you're a Slider fan, I recommend you check this one out.   For those who are curious. Yes, I did have a buzz on when I stopped to get my slider fix.

Friar Tuck, you're my hero. You had a beer I was searching for, that isn't available in Missouri. I just hate it, when a distributor only offers craft beers in certain states. Let us all have the good brews. I was meeting the cousins for lunch in Edwardsville and stopped by on the recommendation of a sales clerk from Craft Beer Cellar in Clayton. Us beer lovers have to stick together.   This was the first time I had ever stepped inside a Friar Tuck store, so I took some extra time to walk through the entire store. I was impressed with the variety of whiskey, vodka, wine and of course craft beer. The pricing wasn't that impressive, but I was glad that they had beer from 21st Amendment. Hell or High Watermelon was as refreshing to drink as it was to finally find it.   The sales clerks were extremely helpful. Before arriving, I called and the young lady over the phone was professional. She told me that indeed they did have the beer I was looking for and told me all the different packaging they offered. When I arrived and was shopping, she remembered our phone conversation and offered my another option she did not mention on the phone.   I have plenty of liquor stores to shop at over in STL, but if I'm on the Eastside and need booze, I'll definitely be back.   When: July 12, 2017 Why: Needed beer not available in Missouri

So long, farewell! 1 week shy of their 26th anniversary Brazie's is closing it doors. They were known for being the best Italian food, "Off The Hill".   I'm embarrassed to admit, I could walk to Brazie's from my house that I have lived in for 17 years and had never gone. I wanted to, but I took for granite that they'd always be there. So when I heard the announcement, I made sure I went for dinner. Now I'm sad they are leaving and truly disappointed with myself for having missed out on some great meals.   After such announcement, of course the restaurant was packed with their loyal regulars. The phone was ringing off the hook with people making reservations through the week. Being alone diner, they found me a space at the bar. I enjoyed talking with all the regulars, they all knew each other and had a true love for the restaurant.   I enjoyed my usual cocktail, a Manhattan. It was wonderfully made and $3 cheaper then I usually pay. My dinner started out with a House Salad. It was a typical Italian salad made with Romaine and Iceberg lettuce. It also had Prosciutto Ham, Green Onion and a mix of both Provel and Asiago Cheeses. What set it above other Italian Salads was the dressing. Other Yelp reviews sang it's praises and it's true, most likely the best Italian Dressing in the city.   My entree was the, Tenderloin Pepper Steak. It melted in my mouth. The meat was so tender and prepared to a perfect medium rare. I love pepper, it's my favorite seasoning and this tenderloin was rolled in pepper before being charbroiled and topped with a white wine dijon mustard sauce with mushrooms. If I were a regular, this would have been my go to entree. As my side pasta dish, the bartender recommended the pink sauce. I personally would have preferred a veggie, but they're really old school and pasta was the only option. It was delicious. The pasta was a "perfect" al dente and sauce was rich, creamy and a perfect blend of a white & tomato sauce.   Even with the hectic crowd with everyone wanting a last meal here before the closing, the service was friendly and attentive. Even on my first and only visit here, I could tell this was a true mom & pop, Italian family business. You could just feel the love. I'm sorry I didn't come sooner.   Wish the staff the best, on their next adventure.   I'll be back? - I can't they're closing.   When: April 17, 2019 Why: They're closing.

Steve nailed it with this new location in Tower Grove. Locating next door to a dive bar like Tick Tock Tavern was a smart move.  Having them connected by a secret hallway, is the true winner. The hallway is not a secret, we all know it is there. If you don't, you are missing out on some good hot dogs to enjoy with your beer or cocktail.   I enjoy your Hot Dogs Steve, but I just cannot get into your buns. I understand they're your creation with Vitales Bakery, but they are just too chewy for my taste. However, it's your dogs that are the star. Your toppings are plentiful and some of your combinations are creative, unusual and totally out of this world. I had wieners in my mac-n-cheese as a child and I love bacon as an adult. Now I can chow down with those toppings on one of your hot dogs.   Cute little shop with great service. Delivering next door to Tick Tock Tavern is excellent customer service. I just wish I liked your buns (it cost you a star), but I'll get over it because your dogs are so good.

3 1/2 Stars now, can easily be 4 Stars on a future visit.   They offer a variety of sizes to accommodate all appetites. You can get a full waffle, a half or even a quarter. For me, a quarter was the perfect size. To compliment my soft, fluffy and sweet waffle, I choose King Cake. Their ice cream is made by a local & popular ice creamery; Serendipity. It was a perfect pairing for a super sweet treat on a Monday afternoon.   My waffle was made fresh, right in front of me. It was so warm, just enough to allow my King Cake ice cream to soften just enough for easy eating. They sprinkle powdered sugar on top, way too much. Next time, I'll make sure they don't sprinkle so heavily.   A simple plain waffle, with scoops of ice cream pressed inside it, is way better then a cone made from a waffle.   At least, in my world.   The shop is super tiny and kind of laid out awkwardly, but it works. It definitely is a place where you get your treat and leave. There's a very limited space in the front window for sitting, but I recommend strolling up and down Manchester as you enjoy your waffle sandwich filled with ice cream.   The service is as cordial and sweet as the ice cream they serve. The young man working was very bubbly, chatty and did a great job providing customer service.   Would I come back? Yes, it's a unique way to satisfy my sweet tooth.   When: February 27, 2017 Why: Needed something sweet after lunch

I'm a fan of Chava's in the Soulard neighborhood over in STL. So after a day of shopping in Ed-ville with my cousin we needed a light lunch. After discussing our options, a cold Margarita won the debate.   Once we were seated, we immediately ordered two Margaritas with no salt. When I'm with my cousin, all we do is laugh, shop, drink, eat and laugh some more. I kind of felt sorry for our server at first, because every time she came to take our order for food, we were laughing to hard to order. She'd just giggle and politely say, "I'll be back".   I told my cousin how I enjoyed the nachos at the STL location and showed her pictures on Yelp how good they are. Easy sell. I ordered the Cheese Nachos with Seasoned Ground Beef and she ordered the Fajita Nachos with Grilled Chicken Breast. The serving are so large, neither of us could finish ours, so we to-go vessels.   The reason I am a fan of the nachos at Chava's is their presentation. They are not just a pile of chips covered in all the ingredients. Chana's neatly prepares each large chip with toppings, making them finger foods easy to enjoy. Check out my posted photo - a picture will make easy to understand.   Both Chava's are winners for me. It's Americanized Mexican, at its best.   Will I return: Soulard is closer, but if in E-ville, I'll stop by.   When: November 4, 2017 Why: Margarita Time

I do not know what possessed me, but one day I returned here and gave them another try for breakfast and was pleasantly surprised.  The Sausage, Egg and Cheese on a bun was actually enjoyable and no heartburn after wards.  Not a fan of the tater tots/hash browns, so when I want a side I just order the regular fries.   The staff is friendly and always have a positive attitude which is good to see at a fast food business.   Like Dunkin Donuts, I am becoming a fan of their open your eyes dark coffee. Wish they offered it in Keurig K Cups for a quick cup at home.

I loved this store when I lived in STL. My hood was Lindenwood Park, which is close to the South Hampton area. Being that close, made it easy to shop at Southside Hardware.   When I was preparing my house for sale and getting the occupancy permit, the inspector had me get new fire and carbon dioxide alarms. Mine were connected to my alarm system and if the purchaser did not continue the service, they did not have alarms. Really didn't want the expense, but I understood.
