A nice little neighborhood grocery market that also has a decent deli with meat and three plates.  They actually have parking which makes it easy to do some quick shopping for needed items.  Martin's BBQ is also has one of their locations right next door so you can combine a grocery shop and BBQ stop all in one.

This space has gone through several restaurants over the years and so I felt compelled to sample the latest development.  I'm quite a fan of Thai food so I was excited to sample some of their offerings.  I started with the Tom Yum soup and got Pad Thai as my entree.  The food wasn't the best I've had but it was tasty.  The interior of this establishment hasn't changed much from the previous tenants but it is a very nice and comfortably designed space with a fantastic location on Maple Street.  I would probably choose La Thai, Basil Leaf, or Sukho Thai over the food here but if you're in the area this place can certainly satisfy your Thai craving.

They have a plumbing supply business and also a retail display store with bathtubs, sinks, faucets, lighting and other associated home decor items.  They seem to mainly carry higher end items in the retail store but some things can be ordered in a cheaper configuration.  They want you to sign in when you first walk in the retail store and the wait for a salesperson can be a much longer time than you would expect so they use the sign in list to determine who gets the next available salesperson.  The plumbing supply business can get really busy especially in the morning as they carry one of the largest selections of plumbing supplies in the area.  I have been given some incorrect parts before but they have always been easy to work with to exchange them.

The Fly is a bit of a locals secret that sees far less tourists than many other areas of the city.  Being hidden back behind the zoo also makes it more fun as you get to get high up on the levee and look down on the zoo below.  There is a good amount of open grassy space to play games, picnic, throw a Frisbee, let your dog go for a good game of fetch or otherwise enjoy a bit more open space than a lot of other areas in the city.  It is also a great space just to get a bit of sun or watch the Mississippi River pass by as you sip on a daiquiri or some beers.  This is a very relaxing spot or a great spot for activity depending on your mood.  Unfortunately they keep building more and more stuff out here taking away from the open space and natural beauty of the area and that development has drawn enough complaints that it seems they have at least paused most additional development for the time being.  Overall this is one of the nicest spots to kick back and have fun outside in the Uptown area.

Perlis is one of the better clothing stores in New Orleans.  They primarily focus on men's clothing but they do have some women's and boy's items also.  The Perlis brand is most famous for their crawfish logo items and you will see many local folks proudly wearing these clothes.  In addition to crawfish logo items they also specialize in fleur-de-lis and Mardi Gras items.  Perlis is also noted for their selection of suits, ties, and shirts with the suits coming with their offer of free lifetime alterations.  The prices often do seem a bit expensive but they do often have some good sales and also have things you can't find anywhere else in the area.  They will also special order items and will really go out of their way to search for things for you.  I have several of the Perlis polo shirts and I like them "ok" I just wish they fit more like Brooks Brother's which I find more comfortable.  They thing they provide better than just about any other area clothing store is service!

I've got a special place in my heart for this old joint that was Bruno's for most of its existence as I attended many a good rugby party here and did nude Zulu Warrior ceremonial jogs around the block on multiple occasions.  Things have certainly changed since this place got nastier when this bar became Rocco's and now waaay too calm and grey haired as Redd's.  I think we need to bring a rugby party back to this joint and reclaim our old bar!

This is one of the few meat and three places in New Orleans except in New Orleans it is almost always a meat and two which is the case here but you can add a third.  They have nice vegetables and their meats are good along with having a rotating selection of daily specials.  They offer a quick meal at a good value that will satisfy your appetite.  Service is traditional meat and three cafeteria style.  They only offer breakfast and lunch and close by 2pm so unfortunately don't plan at having dinner here and they are also closed on the weekends so if you can't make it for the weekday you are out of luck (which is really unfortunate for folks that don't work downtown or have the flexibility to make it here during the weekday).    Overall this spot offers a hearty lunch for a good value and their changing daily specials keep things interesting.

This is still a really new place and they definitely have some kinks to work out with service and keeping the buffet stocked.  It was taking upwards of 20 minutes for items that had run out on the buffet to get restocked so certainly that is an area for improvement.  The service was also very inconsistent and it took quite a while to get a drink refill.  The food was very well spiced and at a generally higher level of spice than the other area Indian food restaurants in the area.    Overall I enjoyed the food but for the moment I would advise to order off of the menu if you are in any kind of hurry.

This is a chain and some really clever people came up with the idea for this chain.  Every time I drive past this joint it seems to have some folks inside and even later in the night/early morning.  They serve WARM cookies, warm milk and cookie ice cream sandwiches.  Apparently their cookies and milk recipe is pure genius as the college kids seem to be addicted to it like crack.  I generally don't go out of my way to go to chain joints but I was right across the street at Bruno's so I gave in to my curiosity and had to check what all this hype was about.  I got a cookie and I wasn't expecting it to be all hot and fresh like right out of the oven deliciousness which it most certainly was... the warm milk, usually not my preferred option, but with the warm cookie ohhh nice... the finale with the ice cream cookie mmmm ahhhh yeahhhh.  Ok so they ARE serving crack here and it is VERY dangerous so be VERY cautious if you choose to sample their goods as you will NEED more sooner than later.

NOSH is in the space that used to be Tommy's Wine Bar and they offer a daily happy hour.  Most of the food items on offer for their happy hour menu are pathetically small and a waste of time and money to even order while the main decent special they offer would be the 50 cent raw oysters.  The service is really slow and mediocre at best.  The drinks are ok but their happy hour prices are not all that happy and still seem overpriced.  The crowd usually seems that it isn't a very friendly or happy gathering type so this place just lacks the usual happy friendly vibe most NOLA establishments generally offer.  The bar itself has a nice ambiance and very comfortable seating which is unchanged since before Katrina and still works quite well.  Overall without the 50 cent oysters there would really be no need to even visit here and even with the oyster special Superior Seafood offers a more enjoyable friendly crowd along with their 50 cent oyster special which also offers much better drink specials.

The ice doesn't compare to Hansen's or Plum Street and the flavors taste like the commercially made ones.  This is about the only game in town along this stretch of Jefferson Highway so unless you're willing to travel about three miles further in either direction you won't find another snowball treat.  I've only ended up here due to the fact that a Concentra drug testing lab is next door where yippee ki-yay I get to pee in cups for drug tests due to the line of work I'm in so after I pee I saunter over to this joint to get a snowball.  The good thing about the remoteness of this place is I've never had to stand in a long line or seen a long line here but that could be due to my timing.

This is a very casual spot with a warehouse/barn type construction with a large open seating plan.  They offer a pretty respectable seafood buffet here which is a bit pricey but its the only one I've ever seen that has soft shell crabs on it.  The seafood here has lots of fried options with some boiled choices.  If you choose to order off of the menu they have a good selection of typical Louisiana seafood dishes and some chicken and beef choices along with po boys and burgers.  The gumbo includes sausage so it isn't a pure seafood version like I prefer.  They also have some non-local seafood like snowcrab and some unique items like their Mardi Gras rolls. The service is a bit slow sometimes but generally acceptable.    This is certainly a good place to chow down on lots of good local seafood and your biggest issue will be choosing between the buffet here or the all you can eat boiled options at the nearby Salvo's.

The downstairs bar and lobby area along with the restaurant space are quite impressive.  The Three Keys "intimate music venue" is quite a unique spot to watch live music as the crowds swirl past among the bars between the restaurant, Josephine Estelle, and the lobby bar.  I never made it up to the rooftop pool and garden space, Alto, where there is another bar and restaurant but the YLC Wednesday on the Square after party is there so I'm sure I will get there soon.  The prices for drinks outside of happy hour seem too rich for my taste and the beer selection seems to be lacking my preferred options.  This is certainly one of the trendiest  and happening spots right now in NOLA.

This place has some of the best vegetables of anyplace in NOLA.  I really love the mashed sweet potatoes, the creole okra with shrimp, the collard greens, and the green beans.  I used to work across the street from here before Katrina and I ate lunch here everyday so this place really does hold a special meaning to me.    I really like the daily specials (with a choice of yummy veggies) which are pretty much the same goodness as they have been but the new training format they have started since Katrina has resulted in substantially decreased and consistently bad service (where before Katrina I always had great service).  If you can't get here by well before 11:30 then you should expect a very long wait generally to complete your meal.  I understand that this is a training ground but the training used to be much better and they need to institute more discipline and control to get this ship running right again.

This is causal restaurant with some fine dining options that has been displaying a vigorous lunch crowd and more relaxed dinner scene.  They have a decent private back room for meetings or events.  The location in a strip mall on Metairie Road leaves a lot to be desired aesthetically but provides ample parking.  This is definitely a vast improvement from the last restaurant in this space, Zeke's Restaurant, that even Gordon Ramsay couldn't save.

Luke is a German themed restaurant with some seafood thrown in for good effect.  They have some good cold seafood "towers" of various types of shellfish.  They offer some changing daily specials with a core selection of consistent items on the menu.  It is a very pork heavy menu and there is a relatively small selection of main dishes.  They have a few beers that they have specially made for them and they offer some specialty cocktails.   My favorite thing to do here is go for the Happy Hour raw oyster special.  The oysters used to be 25 cents each but the BP troubles (that caused us to release lots of fresh water into our wetlands and the fresh water, and not oil, killed off a lot of our oyster beds) caused an oyster shortage resulting in the price doubling to 50 cents an oyster but $6 for a dozen is still a great deal.  The happy hour goes from 3-6pm and it gets pretty crowded by around 4 so it can be a bit challenging to find a bar stool sometimes.  The entrees I've sampled here have been "ok" to good but often the portion size left me wanting more so usually I stick with the oysters and beer.

I was here during Christmas time and they really do a nice job of adding a lot of holiday fun, decorations and add in Santa being available for kids.  This is a nice space and I really found it far more pleasant than the Gaylord Resort at National Harbor I had recently visited prior to this one.  This is also located at the famous Grand Ole Oprey and right next to a large shopping mall (pro tip: you can park at the mall for free then take a free shuttle bus to the Convention Center).  This is a very large space with a great deal to see so make sure to schedule a pretty large chunk of time to fully explore this space.  The convention center is also very nice and this is one of the best places to attend a conference that I've ever experienced.

During normal times Superior Grill USED to be the "go to" Wednesday party place for Uptown.  That was years ago back when they actually had decent prices on margaritas.  The prices for drinks now are just ridiculous and it survives now based on past legends and fantastic location.  The last time I came here was on a Sunday many months ago and I had dinner and a few margaritas and my bill (for just me) came out to over $50.  No thanks!!! I can eat at  nice fine dining places or go on a margarita bender for 3 days at Juan's Flying Burrito for that price.  Tex-Mex is basic simple food and cheap tequila margaritas are very simple pre-made things that don't warrant the premium that is charged at this establishment.    Currently during the COVID-19 times Superior Grill has been one of of the consistent places that has been able to handle decent sized numbers of people to dine inside and they have maintained service standards where many other spots have failed.  They are still often overpriced for Mexican food but they generally put out good food these days.  In an crazy world they seem to have adapted better than most.  In these insane times they have been consistent and reliable while many other spots have been much less so.  Video Review Here:  https://youtu.be/Y_Dp3EvHe7c

They have some wacky flavors in this place and just their chocolate flavors take up an entire corner.  There is almost always a line to be served here and they offer free tastings of their many and varied flavors.  I'm all old fashioned and mainly just stick to my strawberry but I sometimes mix it up with one of their chocolate flavors or anything else that might catch my eye.  The only big negative about this place, other than the sometimes long lines, is that they only take cash.  They also have the infamous Tchoupitoulas Sundae challenge, that consists of 8 scoops of ice cream and then a huge onslaught of toppings, and completion of this challenge gets your name on the wall (I've never achieved this accolade but I could certainly eat the eight scoops but all those toppings just gross me out).

They have a plumbing supply business and also a retail display store with bathtubs, sinks, faucets, lighting and other associated home decor items.  They seem to mainly carry higher end items but some things can be ordered in a cheaper configuration.  They want you to sign in when you first walk in and the wait for a salesperson can be a much longer time than you would expect so they use the sign in list to determine who gets the next available salesperson.

This is more than just a mere Po Boy shop as it is far more of an actual restaurant as they offer an impressive selection of entrees with the rare and elusive country fried steak that is actually a made from a steak (a ribeye steak properly served with brown gravy instead of that nasty white gravy).  They have a nice selection of breakfast, daily specials, steaks, seafood, pastas and desserts.  They are not scared to give big portions and the roast beef po boy reminds me a bit of the meat used at R&O's. The exterior is pretty much all black & gold so this is a big time Saints and LSU business.  There is a lot of seating inside and you simply just order at the cash register then get your number and take your seat and place your number in the designated holder and the food is quickly brought to your table.

Blah boring chain burger place that's slightly higher quality than McD's.  A much better restaurant is deserving of this prime location and this place would be better served next to some other fast food places.  I really could do without the steel cage basket they serve things in.  Maybe this place will do ok as there isn't any other fast food joint within eye shot of this place other than Subway but I think a local joint would have done better business and fit in much better with the neighborhood.  Personally I could do without it and probably won't be back as there are much better burgers for a similar price nearby in the bars.  I guess this would be a good spot to bring kids.

This is a classic New Orleans fried seafood joint that loads you down with some very large portions.  Strangely (for me as a very carnivorous meat loving person and seafood addict) I think my favorite thing here is the mac 'n cheese.  The seafood plate is huge and has a lot of stuff on it.  The only downside (as with many fried things) is that many of the items end up tasting very similar.  They have a pretty decent gumbo and I've generally enjoyed everything I've eaten here.  Most people seem to need a "to go" box but I've always managed to eat enough of my food to have never needed one (so far).  The one thing that I've had here that was very bad were the raw oysters and they were hands down the WORST raw oysters I've ever eaten anywhere in New Orleans (they tasted like they had been shucked days ago and had a texture like they had been sitting in a refrigerator for a long while).  This place always seems to have a really good crowd but I've never had to wait for a table.  Service has always been quick and "old fashioned" New Orleans friendly (with lots of dawlin's and sweethearts from the servers).  One of my friends, from Hattiesburg, MS, especially loves this place because it is among the few in NOLA that actually serves sweet tea pre-made.  They do close relatively early by New Orleans standards so plan accordingly.

Puckett's is a local Tennessee chain with locations in some pretty cool spots.  This location in Franklin is often SUPER BUSY especially on weekends with generally about an hour plus wait to get in but you do often get live music to go with your meal.  They have a really great and really large selection of some pretty dang tasty food and this is one of those rare places you could probably eat at everyday of the week for a few weeks and never get bored with the food.  The service is also friendly and attentive with focusing on the finer details of keeping folks happy.  For a place so busy and with so many food options they still somehow manage to put out a good BBQ brisket along with their own house BBQ sauces which is pretty impressive with all the other things on their menu.  The only item I'm not really a fan of is the skillet pecan cobbler but some folks might love it.  Overall I might just eat here everyday for a couple of weeks if it wasn't for the crazy wait times.

The upstairs balcony view is an enjoyable space when the weather is nice.  The food was inconsistent on my initial visit with the gumbo having undercooked okra but overcooked shrimp while my trout was alright.  The crawfish au gratin tasted exactly like au gratin potatoes with crawfish added which is far better than plain potatoes but could have been kicked up a bit more.  Overall it is a decent spot and still seems to be getting the engine up and running at full speed.  I will have to give it another try in a few months and see how they have progressed.

This is a great little park in the CBD that is host to YLC Wednesday on the Square and the Harvest the Music series of events.  Many other festivals and events are held here and this is a great location for such celebrations.  When events aren't going on this is just a nice park spot just to enjoy a picnic or anything else you might want some green space for such as frisbee etc.

So for the same price as just an oil change at most other places you can also get your car washed and vacuumed here.  There is usually a bit of a wait but they have a pleasant enough waiting area with some creatures and magazines to read.  You don't always get the best car wash and interior vacuum but if you're getting your oil changed anyway its not a bad deal.

I feel so utterly betrayed as the recent law, requring disclosure of the origin of seafood from restaurants has gone into effect now, has revealed a dark truth I would never have wanted to accept.  The current menu at Slim Goodies reveals their crawfish are sourced from foreign lands even though they are literally across from the amazing seafood distributor of Big Fisherman.  I feel utterly betrayed over my patronage of this business over the years as they have proven to favor China over local Louisiana... so so heartbreaking....

This is a pretty solid diner with good quality diner level food.  I'm not big into breakfast but occasionally I will grab the crawfish etouffee omelet here.  They also have some pretty solid sandwiches and other menu items are also good.  They also have a really great back patio that a lot of people don't ever check out that looks like a wild jungle!!!  They open really early so they are among a handful of places in the Garden District to grab something to eat at 6am.  Update:  1) Good, they finally take credit cards!!!  2) Bad, sadly like many places service has declined and isn't as good as it used to be.

This is an old school New Orleans Creole Italian place that  was in Bucktown for years (and the Quarter before that) and had to relocate to the West End due to the Corps of Engineers work on our levee system after Hurricane Katrina.  Their new location is a lot nicer with better space than their old cramped space so the move has been a blessing for them.  I've only eaten lunch here as dinner often gets really crowded and every time I've attempted dinner there has been a long wait. They have a good selection of local seafood dishes and po'boys along with the usual Italian options.  The seafood gumbo is ok while they sometimes are a bit stingy with the red gravy on some of the pasta dishes.  The service has always been friendly and efficient at keeping my drink filled. They have a pretty decent lasagna here and the prices are reasonable.  I rarely ate here when they were in Bucktown because R&O's was right across the street and really the only time I ended up at Two Tony's was when the line was too long at R&O's.  This is still a good place to grab some decent Italian for lunch and it might be nice for dinner too but I've yet to experience their dinner menu as the wait has been too long every time I've attempted it.  Overall this is a decent spot to eat some New Orleans Creole Italian food and seafood.  My video review of Two Tony's is here:  https://youtu.be/e0wI2milvzc

Brought to us by the same folks that gave us Slim Goodies this is a bit more of a nicer restaurant feel as compared to Slim Goodies casual diner concept.  The food is pretty similar and some dishes are exactly the same and actually the menu is consistently larger at Slim Goodies while Horn's varies between breakfast, lunch and dinner.  Horn's also offers quite a selection of cocktails to enjoy along with your food.  Service is a bit lackadaisical so don't think your drink will get refilled quickly or often.  Overall its a nice spot for a meal in a slightly bit of off the tourist path location.

This is a nice new addition to the expanding Vietnamese restaurant scene of Magazine.  I'm getting a bit concerned about the sheer saturation of Asian and Mexican joints on Magazine Street but this place is affordable and I liked their pho.  They also offer a crazy giant pho challenge that consists of a huge bowl with 2 pounds of meat and 2 pounds of noodles that you have to eat within one hour.

This is a grocery store that has a nice deli and bakery along with a good selection of typical grocery store items including a large alcohol selection.  They seem to be well noted for their seafood enchiladas, king cakes and making a lot of popular sausages.  Their deli and bakery should certainly be investigated as they have some good hot food and nice looking desserts.  If you find yourself in Belle Chasse this is certainly a place you should visit and see for yourself.

This is one of my secret hide aways that I like to go to for cheap but great raw oysters and good seafood options.  They do good boiled seafood and grilled fish (or you get several other options on how you want it cooked).  The po boys are good yet smaller than I like but that leaves room for some of the other good options (like the delicious fried seafood appetizer, gumbo, or turtle soup).  Sunday through Wednesday ALL DAY they have 50 cent oysters (used to be 25 cent until BP) so I like my $6 a dozen deal.    This place can get crazy crowded with a substantial wait on the oyster special days so there might be a line out the door waiting to be seated sometimes.  I've always had great service and I prefer to sit at the bar to enjoy my food.  There are always some interesting characters in here and this is certainly a great spot to see and hear things that you are hard pressed to find elsewhere.  I find the oyster size more consistent at Luke but generally more interesting people here.

This is a pretty solid diner with good quality diner level food.  I'm not big into breakfast but occasionally I will grab the crawfish etouffee omelet here.  They also have some pretty solid sandwiches and other menu items are also good.  I've always had just outstanding and very friendly service here that is completely 5 Stars I just don't think diner type food can be more than 3 Stars generally in my ranking bias.  They also have a really great back patio that a lot of people don't ever check out that looks like a wild jungle!!!  I don't get here very often and when I do I usually forget that it is cash only so remember to bring your cash.  They open really early so they are among a handful of places in the Garden District to grab something to eat at 6am.

This is an old diner style restaurant with a NOLA spin and a dash of Greek.  You can get breakfast and lunch here most of the day.  They have one side of the menu dedicated to their lunch offerings and the other side is their breakfast.  You have a lot of choices here and there should be something on the menu to satisfy almost anybody.  They also are very fast here and typically get your food out to you within a matter of minutes.  It's got the old dive ambiance that we love in NOLA and I like sitting at the counter.  The menu and food probably haven't changed in years which has its good points and bad points to various folks tastes.  This is a solid choice if you're in the mood for a quick meal at a fair price in a diner type setting.  Before Katrina this was a 24 hour establishment but unfortunately, like so many other businesses, they haven't returned to that schedule.  The only real disappointment I get here is waitresses don't call me "love, darling, sweetheart, or honey" like they do at other NOLA joints like this.  I would skip the burger and the turkey plates.

Overall this was a 2.5 star experience for me.  They still have some kinks to work out with the biggest issue being the time it takes to receive your food but hopefully they will get that ironed out with experience. The ordering process is a bit confusing as there isn't a clearly defined ordering space so they need an "order here" sign or something similar. I was most irritated with the child size micro cup my iced tea came in so they definitely need bigger cups.  I ate lunch here and got two sliders and fries. I hate donuts but my friend I dined with ate one and liked it. I had a chicken slider and cheeseburger slider as did my friend. Both sandwiches were good with the chicken having the best flavor. I was disappointed in the very small chicken nugget I got on my sandwich which seemed smaller than my friends. The fries I wouldn't get again as they just were not that great with a cheese sauce on them and plain cheese would be better. For the price I don't think my meal was a good value and I was left still hungry but I would eat the sliders again for a cheaper price. The interior of this establishment has really been fixed up nicely and would make a good bar. They have a small patio in the back that could be a nice spot to escape to. I'm not sure if this place is going more for coffee shop or gastropub so it will be interesting to see how it develops. If they have a slider happy hour I would return for that.

This is a great old school Mid-City steak house that has barely changed over the years and is a New Orleans icon.  I've usually had good food here with a few inconsistent and less tasty visits but always good times.  I've often gotten the Porterhouse for 2 and found that to be one of my favorites here (and sometimes instead of eating it all myself I actually share it with someone).  The sides are pretty simple and basic here and I rotate between the sauteed spinach, broccoli au gratin, spinach au gratin, and peas. Most people usually get an order of onion rings and a salad but what Crescent City does better than any other steakhouse is give you an amazing assortment of potatoes to choose from: au gratin, french fried, German fries, Lyonnaise, Braebant, cottage fries and shoestrings!  I really like the booths with the curtains you can pull shut and plan to take over the world with your co-conspirators.  The service has always been great here (except for the abrupt opening of my tightly closed curtains).  I know they need to bring stuff to me but maybe they should have some kind of signal system to let you know they will be entering your private cocoon soon so you won't be so surprised when they yank it back and reveal the glare of the outside world. It can be a bit expensive for what you get but ambiance like this is nearly impossible to find outside of New Orleans!

Typically long lines and the food just doesn't have a whole lot of flavor to me.  The tortillas are very "gummy" and just don't have a very good consistency to me while at the same time being too dry and often falling apart.  I'm just not a fan of "better" fast food that takes a cafeteria line approach and then just doesn't taste as good as Taco Bell.  For the same price I can go to an actual Mexican restaurant and get better food with actual service while actually being able to enjoy my dining experience.

This is definitely an interesting and uniquely New Orleans type of diner experience.   There are several Dot's Diners around but this is the only one I've ever stepped into.  The place is always open so that does take away from the cleanliness factor but I've seen far worse.  The service staff are very friendly and engaging  and they seem  to always have folks inside.  I'm not a big breakfast fan but they have all sorts of other offerings and I got the sliders which were actually rather large for sliders and very filling.  It definitely isn't the best or most tasty food I've had and "greasy spoon" definitely sums up most of what is dished up here but they are always open.  It wouldn't ever be my first choice for a meal but if it were really late/very early and nothing else was open I'd probably venture here again if I was stuck in the area.

A nice little neighborhood grocery market that also has a decent deli with meat and three plates.  They actually have parking which makes it easy to do some quick shopping for needed items.  Martin's BBQ also has one of their locations right next door so you can combine making groceries  and a BBQ stop all in one.

This is a great place to get your wine or beer fun on when it is nice outside as there is only outside seating.  They have some great cheese plates and the outdoor chef's are usually making some good food with some good music playing.    The good news & the bad news is the outdoor seating as it gets really hot and rains a lot in NOLA so there are definitely better times of the year to experience this place than others.  Another growing problem is the popularity of this place is making it harder and harder to actually find a seat so you need to get there mighty early to secure a spot and finding parking is never an easy task.  The only other thing to watch out for is there are sometimes some people with really stinky BO in there that need a good hosing off (I'm not sure when it became fashionable to avoid bathing) so that could be the benefit of going after it rains as maybe those folks will smell better.  Another benefit or problem depending on your point of view is that folks will often bring their children with them to hang out on the patio.  I don't have  any problem with kids and find them nicer than most snotty adults that don't like them so I think it just adds to the entertainment and flavor of the place to have entire families enjoying themselves and to have a place I can go with my friends that have kids that want to go somewhere like this.  I wish we had a place like this closer to Uptown so I didn't have to go so far to enjoy it.

I've eaten here many times and had many private events here.  I have always had a great time with outstanding service and food.  Muriel's has some amazing gumbo and they usually have a special for around $30 for a 3 course meal.  Some people don't know you can usually get a drink downstairs and go and enjoy the balcony upstairs and this is one of the best places to people watch all the interesting things going on down around Jackson Square below.  They also have an interesting "Egyptian" themed room upstairs. Always a great place to go with a group, book an event, or just eat by yourself at the bar.

This is a pretty cool bar which is right next to Smoked BBQ which offers some nice meat.  There seems to be quite a few locals that frequent this place and it is the perfect location to grab some good BBQ then go hang out at My Brother's Bar after.  Overall this is a nice neighborhood joint with some friendly folks and good bartenders.

I just stopped in here to drink a few brews and I had not yet had a chance  to try the food but as the burgers here do look nice I decided to sample one.  Looking at the menu I decided on the mushroom Swiss burger with a side of slaw... with the results that the burger was sadly mediocre but I have had worse while the slaw was absolutely not to my liking at all and I couldn't eat it (first time EVER I have met a slaw I couldn't eat). They have some nice outdoor seating and the indoor seating is a larger space than many bars offer so this has more of a restaurant vibe than bar but they still have a nice long bar to sit at as well.  The service was friendly and attentive along with telling you what their favorite beers of the moment were.  This is a pretty popular spot in this neighborhood and seems like a generally fun spot to be and I would return for the beer but not the burgers or slaw.

This is a nice addition to the expanding Vietnamese restaurant scene of Magazine that I have been eating at for several years now.  This is a nice spot for a quick and delicious meal with their offerings of a variety of rice dishes, noodle dishes, spring rolls, pho, Vietnamese po boys/banh mi, Vietnamese tacos/sliders/banh gap and many other delicious items.  Their stir fried beef banh mi is one of the best beef po boys in the city!  My video review of Pho Cam Ly is here:  https://youtu.be/E2TfP_bLwBg

Out of all the new Vietnamese places that have opened on Magazine recently this is by far the best.  They have a selection of nine different types of pho including a rare (at least in NOLA) spicy shrimp one.  They have a good selection of spring rolls and egg rolls along with bun (noodle dishes), rice dishes and salads.  They have beef, chicken, pork, and tofu banh mi (po boys).    The only three things I didn't like about the place is that they don't fill your bowl of pho to the top like they do at Westbank and Metairie pho places and they made me share my sprouts, greens, and peppers with my friend I was eating with.  I'm a very selfish person when it comes to my pho fixings grrrrr I don't want to share and I want my own plate of stuff grrrr!  I also thought the price at $8.25 for most of the pho's was a bit much for a non-full bowl compared to other places.    The seating was far more comfortable and service was far faster than at the other two new Vietnamese places so if you want some good Vietnamese on Magazine this is your best option.  And yes for you freaky vegetarians they did have some tofu pho but I don't know if the broth is vegetarian :)

Superior USED to be the "go to" Wednesday party place for Uptown.  That was years ago back when they actually had decent prices on margaritas.  The prices for drinks now are just ridiculous and it survives now based on past legends and fantastic location.  The last time I came here was on a Sunday many months ago and I had dinner and a few margaritas and my bill (for just me) came out to over $50.  No thanks!!! I can eat at  nice fine dining places or go on a margarita bender for 3 days at Juan's Flying Burrito for that price.  Tex-Mex is basic simple food and cheap tequila margaritas are very simple pre-made things that don't warrant the premium that is charged at this establishment.    The food is mostly "ok" typical Tex Mex blah.  Most of the dishes here come out with some rather greasy looking melted cheese on them and usually the best bet are the fajitas.  Probably the best thing they have here are the chips and salsa which are actually FREE and they keep them coming to you if you sit at the bar so that is a big bonus.  Unfortunately I've had multiple occasions after eating here where I've gotten sick and it has usually been with the ground beef so I have learned through painful experience to stick to the chicken dishes.    I rarely go here anymore except during Mardi Gras; as it has become a common meet up spot over the years for many people I know.  Back when this place pulled in lots of cute ladies it was a LOT of fun and it actually IS a nice atmosphere with generally excellent service.  I still have a few friends that love this place but MOST people I know don't go here anymore.  Superior used to also have lots of fun parties outside with lots of great people.  Sadly it has been a LONG time since I've seen lots of nice looking people in this place and usually the only times I will even bother is during Mardi Gras as even Cinco de Mayo draws a sketchy looking crowd now.

This is an old Italian place that  was in Bucktown for years (and the Quarter before that) and had to relocate to the West End due to the Corps of Engineers work on our levee system.  Their new location is a lot nicer with better space than their old cramped space so the move has been a blessing for them.  I've only eaten lunch here and they have a good selection of local seafood dishes, po boys, and the usual Italian options.  The seafood gumbo is ok but the rue is a bit thin for my taste.  They have a pretty decent lasagna here and the prices are reasonable.  I rarely ate here when they were in Bucktown because R&O's was right across the street and really the only time I ended up at Two Tony's was when the line was too long at R&O's.  This is still a good place to grab some decent Italian for lunch and it might be nice for dinner too but I've yet to experience their dinner menu.

This is causal restaurant with some fine dining options which has been displaying a vigorous lunch crowd and more relaxed dinner scene.  Generally Porter & Luke's averages a bit over a 3.5 star mainly due to consistency issues as they absolutely can put out some four and five star food when they are firing on all cylinders but they seem to often have misfires.  They have a decent LARGE private back room and smaller private side room for meetings, events or other private dining groups.  The location is in a strip mall on Metairie Road which leaves a lot to be desired aesthetically but provides ample parking.  This is definitely a vast improvement from the last restaurant in this space, Zeke's Restaurant, that even Gordon Ramsay couldn't save.  My most recent visit was during St. Patrick's and the special was corned beef and cabbage and the corned beef was on the tougher side and certainly could have been better while the gumbo I also got was good.  Overall this is USUALLY a nice spot to get a good lunch or dinner and I've been to some good events here.  My video review of Porter & Luke's is here:  https://youtu.be/uLEkT9jOf28

So I've kept a deep dark secret that I sometimes get a craving for a big bag of Krystal burgers and I had long heard White Castle was a very similar burger so I ended up staying in a hotel very near this White Castle which seemed like the perfect opportunity to finally lose my White Castle virginity. So on getting my food I certainly noticed the similarity to Krystal but I have to say that overall I just didn't find the experience anywhere nearly as pleasing as my deep secret sin I very rarely engage in with Krystal usually is.  The flavors of White Castle were simply not quite as flavorful and nice a flavor fix as I gain to my taste buds with a big bag orgy of Krystals.  White Castle just didn't provide me the same naughty pleasure swerve that my long affair with Krystal has always succeeded with inducing.

I had the enchiladas and they were exceptionally bland.  Everything just seemed very disorganized and while the place only had a handful of tables with patrons there seemed to be more than enough staff it took a very long time to have my order taken.  After that waitress brought my food out very fast she quickly disappeared for quite a long while.    I had initially been planning on going for a second trip to sample the tacos to see if those might redeem the place but when I never got a single drink refill on my iced tea I was done with the place.  There were literally four staff members sitting at or behind the bar just doing NOTHING and nobody managed to pay attention to me and get me a refill on my drink (and I was sitting at the bar).  Until I started waving around my credit card to pay while making plenty of noise and run out of the place I received no attention after my food was delivered.  Too many better places at better price points with better service to deal with buffonry like this.

In more civilized days when individual HONOR had meaning and men were willing to put their lives on the line for it, other than just in warfare, this area of City Park was very frequently used for duels.  Originally there were two dueling oaks but unfortunately one was destroyed by a hurricane in 1949 so we have the last remaining and singular dueling oak standing.  There is a commemorative plaque explaining the historical significance of this oak and the area around it (at least until Maoist Mitch and the rest of of his Cultural Marxist Red Guard continue their destruction of history spree and remove it and cut down the tree).  We sorely need to re-legalize dueling in City Park and I would be happy to meet all the honorless Cultural Marxists in duels under the dueling tree at such time.  They would lose in a simple battle of wits as they lack logic and facts to justify their destruction of history.

Did I mention that I HATE the new "GASTROPUB" concept going on in New Orleans recently.  Just like all the "gastropubs" that are going on in New Orleans why bother and just go to a real restaurant or bar where you can actually eat a real plate of food that will fill you up instead of being a snack.  Did I mention I HATE GASTROPUBS and all these small plates!!!    They often have decent to good music in here and it seems to always be crowded so it can take awhile to find a seat.  They are also smoke free which is a big bonus.This was one of the first "Gastropubs" to open in NOLA and I heard all sorts of great things about it.  I finally went all excited and at first thought it could be fun but I soon discovered it was packed crowded, with a considerable wait to order ANYTHING (if you ever get a table the service gets much faster and much improved), and the food portions were very small.   I don't like snacks I like meals and the menu doesn't do much for me here.  I was also in shock at the end of the night when the bill would have easily covered a very nice night out at a fine dining restaurant yet I was STILL hungry.  I just don't "get" it and don't see any reason to go back.  Tiny plates of "ok" food at inflated prices with expensive cocktails just doesn't work for me and I will just stick to real restaurants and go to actual bars.

If your looking for a quality smaller gun store with a reliable and straight shooting owner that knows what he is talking about then this is the place for you.  Meplat Group is an FFL with a small but notable stock of firearms and is happy to do do transfers for $20.  They buy, sell, trade, and transfer firearms of all kinds including Class III weapons like machine guns, silencers, short barrelled rifles and shotguns.  They also provide training through their NRA certified instructors and give a great level of service and knowledgeable advice to help customers in the selection and acquisition of firearms that meet their needs.  The owner, Kenneth Bossetta, is an attorney and can also set up NFA trusts to assist with the process of acquiring NFA items.  Mr. Bossetta is also a great person to do business with and is definitely a step up from your average gun store interaction.

This is a great old school Mid-City steak house that has barely changed over the years and is a New Orleans icon.  I've usually had good food here with a few inconsistent and less tasty visits but always good times.  I've often gotten the Porterhouse for 2 and found that to be one of my favorites here (and sometimes instead of eating it all myself I actually share it with someone).  The sides are pretty simple and basic here and I rotate between the sauteed spinach, broccoli au gratin, spinach au gratin, and peas. Most people usually get an order of onion rings and a salad but what Crescent City does better than any other steakhouse is give you an amazing assortment of potatoes to choose from: au gratin, french fried, German fries, Lyonnaise, Braebant, cottage fries and shoestrings!  I really like the booths with the curtains you can pull shut and plan to take over the world with your co-conspirators.  The service has always been great here (except for the abrupt opening of my tightly closed curtains).  I know they need to bring stuff to me but maybe they should have some kind of signal system to let you know they will be entering your private cocoon soon so you won't be so surprised when they yank it back and reveal the glare of the outside world. It can be a bit expensive for what you get but ambiance like this is nearly impossible to find outside of New Orleans!  Watch my video about a recent visit here:  https://youtu.be/Nr1N7x7D4qg

I was at Ole Miss when the very first McAlister's came into existence (initially it was Checker's but a burger joint already had that name taken so they changed it to McAlister's to franchise it out). It's really just a boring bland franchise chain now so in the land of delicious po boys I just don't find myself eating here.  The sandwich quality seems to have declined with the franchising but the iced tea is still great so I mainly stop at this location for iced tea as its near my office.

This place is a solid three star 24/7 dive bar with very comfortable bar stools with bonus points for the 24/7 part.  Metry still allows smoking in the bars so that will drive me out of a place really fast but fortunately on my last visit nobody was committing smoke suicide.  This is also a spot where you can get your bartender to cook you a burger and I had a discount coupon so I took a chance and tried the burger and I probably would never get the burger again unless it was 4am and there were no other options but there usually are better options even then so I would choose those.  So just come here to drink drinks and play some chess or something like that.

This Whole Foods location is much larger than the one Uptown and has a much better parking setup.  Unfortunately this location also has a generic desgin and has none of the charm of the Uptown store.  They have a hot food bar and offer a much larger selection of prepared foods here than Uptown.  The lines can frequently get long here and they recently did a redesign of the dining area that removed one of the cash registers.  They really needed to add and not take away cash registers as this place gets packed around Noon and any hope of a quick check out to eat lunch here will be dashed if you don't arrive at 11:00.  Another big issue they have here is that frequently the hot food bar isn't transitioned from breakfast to lunch in a timely manner along with the food choices often getting into stagnant lulls where they do the same dishes over and over.  It also seems a lot harder to find grass fed beef here than Uptown.  While there is definitely room for improvement in many areas this is still a great store with some great products.  One last review of ONE Star goes out to all the LAZY people that leave their carts strewn all over the place in the parking lot!  Yes I'm talking to YOU yeah I think all of YOU should be sentenced to picking up cigarette butts from the side of the road for one month every time you leave that cart anywhere it doesn't belong!

I've only been to the CAC for parties, bands, and events.  Honestly I've never found most of the art here very interesting but I'm not really into modern/contemporary art as I much prefer the more classical approach.  This place is a great party and event venue and I've had lots of good times here.  Admission:  $5 General Admission $3 for Students & Seniors FREE to CAC Members

Fresh local produce along with boiled peanuts, tamales and other assorted treats so what's not to like?  They take credit cards and actually have pretty good parking around the building.  If you want some local Louisiana love or need to satisfy that boiled peanut craving this is a great place to do it and it's probably the nicest and best Becnel's produce option out of the several out there.

This place has a great selection of some of the most amazingly fresh produce, meats, and seafood anywhere in the area.  They also have many Asian fruits and vegetables that are difficult or impossible to find elsewhere.  They have a large selection of products and prepared food items from across Asia.  They even carry a decent selection of cookware.  The prices here are generally very affordable and they have some great values.  They also have a deli where they make some good things with most people seeming to focus on the banh mi.  They do have a few things missing that I like to get from Asain stores but other than those they have nearly everything else I've ever looked for.

I popped in here during my Running of the Bulls weekend of madness.  It sort of gave me a bit of déjà vu for a moment when I first walked in and made me think I was back Uptown at St. Joe's Bar but while there are a few similarities this place has a personality all its own.  I liked this place a lot more before I ate here.  The bar is a very enjoyable place and still has a hint of its past dive bar ambiance while gaining a much more sophisticated flair.  The food was disappointing as when I was deciding between the regular burger and turducken  burger I was going to order the turducken burger but I didn't want dirty rice as my side but the server told me there would be a $4 charge to make a substitution to fries.  Ok so I just ordered the regular burger instead and was in a grumpy mood for not being able to have a choice of side.  The appearance of the regular burger reminded me of the fantastic burger at Le Petite Grocery but the meat was disappointing to me and wasn't that good.  I might return to drink here but now I'm cautious about the food as the burger was really disappointing and the lack of flexibility with the sides is laughable when it comes to cheap items like fries and rice.

This establishment is a coffee house that does some baked goods, desserts and sandwiches.  I was really leaning towards two stars as I HATE the hours this place keeps.  I made it in here once, right after they opened, and they were sold out of everything.  After about 20 more attempts I finally made it here before their posted closing time of 6pm but they stop serving sandwiches at 5pm.  Holy Batman I was getting frustrated BUT the owner saved the day and one star by stepping up and making one last sandwich for the day.  While I was waiting for my French Dip roast beef sandwich I also ordered an apricot raspberry pistachio bar which was pretty good.  The sandwich was pretty good too with rare roast beef on real French bread with a dipping sauce that seemed to be French Onion Soup.  The food was good but a bit overpriced and this seems to mainly be a breakfast and lunch joint.  I would like this place a lot more if it were open late as I'm a night owl and have to work during the day.

The Colombian style arepas sandwiches here are definitely a unique experience in the New Orleans dining scene.  I had the chicken and avocado which seemed very filling while being very healthy.  I really only got the taste of avocado and didn't notice a whole lot of chicken which with most sandwiches would make me grumpy but somehow the whole was greater than the parts.  I've been able to sample most of the other arepas and they have all been tasty and their liquor drinks are all done decently.  I've made several attempts to eat here when they are not yet open for their posted times so plan accordingly that they will often open late and close early.  Expect to have a much slower pace of most everything while here.

The ambiance inside this place is nearly non-existent and doesn't encourage dining inside.  This place is generally very fast but it really isn't one of the better po boy joints in the city.  You do get a free drink with your po boy but they only have Pepsi products and no fresh brewed iced tea.  The roast beef po boy here is the sliced variety with no real gravy but it does have some green pepper and onion coating that gives it a bit better flavor than just plain sliced roast.  Unfortunately they also don't have creole mustard here.  If you're in a hurry or its late at night and want a mediocre po boy this place will work but there are far better places to go.  Its also cash only so be prepared.

I've been to The Shed BBQ many times but I'm not sure why they decided to throw a semi-replica of the BBQ joint up in the middle of this museum and make it the centerpiece of the space.  The rest of the exhibit seems to mainly be placards of different Southern states with some of their signature food items.  The place really seems like an episode of Pickers was devoted to decorating the place with random memorabilia of various signs and containers and as Christopher W. aptly described it the feeling is a bit like a junk yard.  There is a demonstration kitchen that could be interesting and then they have Purloo restaurant hidden behind a giant curtain.  There were no signs really indicating where to go for anything and the multiple entry doors were randomly locked or open with no logic.  I came mainly to eat at Purloo for lunch but wandered into the museum looking for the restaurant and then when I tried to exit after eating all the doors were locked.   This place has potential but seems pretty disorganized at the moment.  I think they might want to work with Ole Miss and their Center for the Study of Southern Culture that hosts the Southern Foodways Alliance to add some more substance to the exhibits http://southernstudies.olemiss.edu/  They should also hire me as director of this museum or at least as a consultant as I know a lot about Southern food, beverages and culture along with being a graduate of Ole Miss several times so I would be able to get this place into the full potential it has because anthropologists do it better.
