This is probably the most comprehensive grocery store in the entire French Quarter while most of the other options are more convenience stores with limited grocery items.  This Rouse's is surprisingly larger than you would think it was from the outside but still smaller than most other Rouse's locations.  They pack in a lot of items for the space and it is a well stocked grocery for the Quarter.  There are frequently gutter punks that hang out in the area that will hassle you but if you ignore them they usually leave you alone.

This is a really cool independent movie venue that focuses on local area films.  They have mainly relied on word of mouth thus far and the nearly secret location is inside an old Wash-Dry-Fold laundromat.  The brother and sister team that run this place, Will and Hayley, are very passionate about independent local films along with wanting their patrons to have a great experience.    Tickets are only $5 and half of that goes to the filmmaker.  They have a few basic snacks available and its also BYOB so you can have quite an entertaining time.  They have very comfortable chairs set up and this seems like it could develop into a great and unique venue for films you just don't get to watch anywhere else.

Yes its gotten waaay more crowded than it used to be to the point of being extremely inconvenient compared to the more laid back and less crowded days of the past.  Yes the portion size of SOME of the food along with the price on ALL of the food has gone up.  Yes there are long lines to eat, drink, use the port-o-lets, and throngs of crowds packed up against the stages.  If you've been to Jazz Fest this is nothing new but FQ Fest for awhile was a "bit" like Jazz Fest used to be before it became the gigantic corporate monster it now is.  Well both FQ Fest and Jazz Fest are now both very large and healthy monsters but sometimes you gotta face the monster, tame it, and learn to ride it then you can have a great time.    If you don't like the lines, crowds, and HEAT you can always go to one of the hundreds of French Quarter bars or restaurants as it is still a FREE festival!  I love wandering all over the Quarter during FQ Fest in addition to just staying in the boundaries of the "official" fest areas of the river front, mint, and Jackson Square.  They have other stages set up all over the Quarter and you can have a great time all over the entire area.  I love to snack on as many tasty treats as I can on a food booth grazing tour but a lot of the items are things that as a local I can get everyday so the key is to target the booths with things that are usually only served during fest time.    If you want a smaller and less crowded festival then just go to Wednesday on the Square or be a total fest whore like me and do it all!  Tip 1:  Leave the baby strollers at home as they are the worst offenders at causing pedestrian traffic jams.  If you MUST have a baby and its stroller at the fest then just stay away from the river front as it isn't safe for the baby or others that might get smashed into your stroller by the crowd.  Tip 2:  Leave your chairs at home as there isn't enough space to set up long lines of chairs and it is a real safety hazard and I will still barrel through your comfy encampment in a heartbeat on my way back and forth to get beer or go to the bathroom so don't think you're safe from my big ugly feet stomping through your "section" just because you're in a chair.  Your very rude and inconsiderate actions in blocking off massive areas to walking traffic force me to be slightly less inconsiderate to force a path through your little fortress of solitude not to mention the thousands of people behind me pushing me onwards.  If you MUST bring your chairs to sit in make sure to not smash them all together and leave space for people to walk through or both you and everybody around you will be miserable.  Its sad I even have to mention this but common sense obviously isn't so common anymore much less common courtesy.

This is a bar with games that also frequently hosts events like comedy nights etc.  They have bottle and can beers and a limited selection of other types of booze.  It's an alright place with a decent vibe but it rarely seems to be hopping outside of their events.  This is generally a pretty laid back and low key joint to duck into for a few beverages and maybe to play a few games when events aren't happening.

Warning this review is not intended for children, vegans, vegetarians, or PETA people as animals were definitely harmed in the making of this review.  Well I really love meat but I just didn't love the food here even though I really wanted to.  I got the lamb neck which is exactly that... the entire neck of a lamb between where it's cute little snugly head was to its wooly soft body.  This is a really large portion of meat but it just isn't a very good quality of meat from this anatomical area of the aforementioned and formerly cute and cuddly lamb.  The neck is simply served over a large portion of black-eyed peas with some random pieces of corn, pig fat, and pickled peppers thrown in.  The menu also said this dish came with a mint chow chow and I never tasted anything with mint in it or saw anything that looked like a chow chow.  Picking off the meat around the vertebra might even freak some folks out but I felt like a lion tearing into its prey except I found the meat to be similar in texture to pot roast or lamb shank but a lot less flavorful.  The entire "dish" of the lamb neck and black-eyed peas really had no other flavor but saltiness.  I think this portion of meat would probably work better being cooked down into a stew of some type and the dish as a whole just really didn't work for me.  I've never eaten the neck of anything in its entirety other than a turkey neck (and turkey neck I've only used when cooking down some greens) and now I know why as it just isn't a very tender meat location on its own and needs to be cooked down into a stew or ragut of some type.    The real kicker is that my lunch with just the lamb neck entree and an iced tea ended up costing $30 with tip.  It was a huge portion but the going rate for lamb necks is somewhere around $6-$8 a pound, as it is a much cheaper cut of meat than about anything else on a lamb, so there is quite a markup.  For the price I paid I would have expected at least some turnip greens or another side other than just a big bed of peas but even if that were added this meal just wasn't worth the price and I can get much higher quality cuts of lamb (like chops) for a cheaper price at many other NOLA places.  Honestly I could have used the same ingredients and easily created a much better tasting dish (at least to my palate).    Hummm... well maybe some of the other things on the menu are better but I would never order this ho-hum-blah-boring lamb neck dish ever again.  Poor cute lambkins the mean ole butcher chopped off your head and sacrificed your sweet little wooly cuteness for such a sad dish.  Poor little bahh bahh I sure wish I could have eaten your yummy leg or shank instead of your rough ole neck.  Your neck would make a lovely cheap stew though I'm quite sure.

This is a fantastic park and they have several distinctive areas.  The Carousel Gardens Amusement Park is one of my earliest and most enjoyable memories featuring the fantastic antique wooden carousel along with several other rides such as a ferris wheel, the Red Baron mini-plane and, another of my favorites, the miniature train ride.  Storyland is another great area for kids with 25 storybook exhibit play areas.  You can also rent boats & bikes, play golf & tennis, or enjoy the equestrian center.  People also fish, play rugby, soccer and all other manner of sports on the park grounds.  There are also the attractions of the Botanical Garden, the Sculpture Garden and the New Orleans Museum of Art.  I've got many memories of the Museum of Art with the earliest being making multiple trips to stand in LONG lines to see the King Tut exhibit and after many attempts FINALLY getting in.  There are also several other areas and spaces available for rental and hosting of events.  Christian Brothers school, Tad Gormley Stadium and the Pan-American Stadium are also located on the park grounds.  There are many festivals and events that are hosted here with Voodoo Fest probably being the largest.  They even have a dog paradise for your pet to enjoy at "City Bark."    This is a great park!

I typically only end up here when I decide to take out of town friends on an adventure on the Algier's Ferry and this usually ends up being our first stop where we grab some food and drinks as it is the closest bar to the ferry.  From here we usually continue to the Crown & Anchor and Old Point Bar.  This is a good sized space and they usually have a decent selection of food with some of it being pretty good but most of it is just "ok" for the most part.  I've rarely seen it crowded but it does seem to draw a fairly steady stream of tourists who decide to go on the Algier's ferry adventure as well.

This is one of the best hotels in New Orleans and is home to fantastic pieces of NOLA history and legend like the Sazerac Bar.  This hotel would often donate food to the place I worked prior to Katrina so I often got to take the elevator deep down into the bowels of the lower levels of this place which was fascinating as there are many functioning antiques down there that still keep this place going.  I've been to many Mardi Gras balls and other fun events here over the years and it was a sad time after Katrina when it was closed for so long.  It was a happy day when they finally reopened and added even more new restaurants and reinvigorated many of the traditional spots.  The most special time here is during Christmas and they do some serious decorating above and beyond nearly any other location in the city and it is a definite destination during that time of year!

This is a cool little Oriental store that has a lot of things you might not even find at Hong Kong market.  They have herbal remedies I like such as ginsing with royal jelly.  The prices are a bit more expensive and this place is more of a convenience sized store but they pack a lot of items for the space.  This is one of the few places where you can find many Asian items in Metairie.

The bar that invented the Flaming Dr. Pepper shot!  I don't like Dr. Pepper so I've never done that shot but I usually have a really fantastic time in here.  This is a classic late night dive spot in the quarter where you can escape the nastier aspects of Bourbon Street.  They usually are playing great 80's music and there are wild crazy people dancing everywhere (but not necessarily doing a good job of it).    The are a few negatives:   1)  You always have to pay a cover to get in and although it is usually crowded sometimes it is crowded with people you don't like being around and you can't tell anything about the crowd until you get inside.  2)  The drinks are a bit expensive on the New Orleans scale but about on par with most of the rip off prices in the French Quarter and occasionally some random dishonest bar tender might try to pull a fast one on you and overcharge you but I've rarely had this problem and found most of the staff here to be good hardworking fun folks.  3)  They are usually only open Thursday-Saturday and sometimes closed on those days so if you open a tab (and you have to give them your ID also) on a Saturday and forget to close it then you can't get your credit card or ID back until maybe Thursday at the earliest (I don't know anything about this from personal experience right...).  When Bourbon Street is getting deserted that is about the time that this bar is beginning to get crowded so 2am and later is the time to get here.  They have lots of old school 80's video games and other fun things to occupy your time if you don't feel like dancing the night away.  There are always interesting people in here and the crowd typically includes several bachelorette parties along with people dressed up from weddings, balls, costume parties and the million other random things that go on in New Orleans.  You probably want to make sure you never arrive here sober as that would just be too much too fast for any person in that state of mind to be able to handle so do yourself a favor and booze it up really good before entering here or you will be overwhelmed by the sheer decadence unleashed in here.

The vast majority of seating here is an outside covered patio so that comes with the benefits and risks of the NOLA outdoors.  There is also a great deal of hookah smoking so that is an additional element to consider if you're gong to eat here.  The food is decent but not as good as most of the other Middle Eastern restaurants in NOLA and Mona's would give you a better experience.  The service really was unacceptably slow at many points and it seems the staff have a lot of distractions.  This is probably a spot best reserved for those that are looking to smoke a hookah and if you're just in the mood to eat you will probably be happier elsewhere but the patio could be nice.

This place is just "ok" BBQ and they are similar to but slightly below Corky's for a BBQ experience.  They give you a very good portion of meat on their plate specials BUT they dole out their BBQ sauce, like it is liquid gold, and you only get a tiny little cup of it that isn't nearly enough to go with your meal.  The brisket is very similar to that at Corky's but it isn't the moistest and is more on the dry side so it certainly needs some sauce.  They also only give you ONE napkin and I'm always suspicious of any BBQ that doesn't take multiple napkins to eat.  They do have some of the most FANTASTIC vinegar cole slaw I've ever had and I've rarely enjoyed eating such marvelous fresh and crunchy stuff as this with such amazing flavor.   Besides the slaw I would probably not return here again as it is so similar to Corky's and the location is far out of my way.

This is a cool dive Italian restaurant in the usual Metairie strip mall.  The place is just old and kind of dirty the way you expect a dive joint to be.  The food is much better than I would have expected and it is some of the best  casual Italian food in the area that its in.  They even managed to surprise me as they serve their lasagna with a side of angel hair pasta and that's something I just haven't seen anywhere else at the local Italian places.  In addition to their pasta entrees they also have pizza and po boys. Overall I like both the dive ambiance and the food here along with the fact it is a great place to grab a quick lunch at a good value.

Food inspired by the Yucatan with drink prices inspired by New York City with $4.50 Abita Amber, $5.50 Negra Modelo, $8 house margaritas (served in a small glass) and $8 for a glass of sangria. Food service is fast and the flavor of most things is good. The drink prices are too expensive and while the food is good the prices are a bit too much for what you get.  The spider theme of the interior decor is too year round Halloween for this section of town and doesn't seem to contribute anything other than scaring young children.   My part of the bill came out to $27.16 (before tip) which was for the 3 tacos with 2 sides combo, a shared tamale, an iced tea and one house margarita.  Mexican food is cheap peasant food with most things wrapped in some form of tortilla and no valid reason to be pricey and the same goes for Mexican beer and house margaritas.  There are as good or better Mexican options in the city for a much better value on food and drinks so I'm not confident in the longevity of this place and I probably won't make many return visits.    Tip: the à la carte seafood tacos are probably one of the better values on the menu.  Hint:  The main competition in the area for this joint is Rum House.  The drinks at Rum House are substantially cheaper and larger.

This location has had several bar and grills located inside it and so far the current one is the best.  They provide really good and friendly service along with some decent to good food.  It does seem to draw a mix of tourists and locals from the area and it actually has quite a spacious interior that can accomodate larger groups.

One of the oldest Yacht Clubs in the USA the SYC has a long and distinguished history in the annals of yachting.  This is the epicenter of sailing for the NOLA area and the club has some fantastic programs.  They have a nice pool area with a smaller kid friendly splash pool.  The clubhouse has nice facilities overlooking Lake Pontchartrain and the food is generally good to excellent depending on what you order.  This spot is always a hub of activity and it is certainly a popular venue for many events and activities.

This is the bar of New York Pizza.  I like this place for the fact they offer a $5 pint and a slice special which is a pretty awesome deal.  There isn't a limit on this special and you can just keep eating and drinking as many $5 slice/pints as you want.  They also offer the full menu of New York Pizza usually so you can get some good options here if you don't feel like pizza.  Some nights they stay open late and other nights they just close when they want to close.  The inconsistent hours is the main thing that irks me about this place but generally its a good place to grab a quick slice of pizza and a pint of beer.

Probably the best Little Tokyo location I've been to so far.  Larger portions and better service seem to characterize this spot.  The ambiance doesn't really scream sushi joint and is more generic restaurant.  Quick and easy spot to grab some food at a decent price and all day happy hour on Sundays.

This is the nearest sushi joint to my office and I eat here occasionally when I'm in a hurry.  I much prefer Kanno in Fat City but they have some strange hours sometimes and close for extended periods so this is a decent backup place when the need for sushi arises.  I also like Shogun but I hate dealing with Veteran's traffic not that Causeway is much better but this place is much closer to my office.  They generally have good selection and quality at decent prices.

Four stars for the drinks and three for the food.  The Magazine location is where I usually end up going as it is close to my house (and Sunday they usually have happy hour all day and I like to get my double margarita for the price of a single).  I need to disclose that I'm not really  a big fan of Mexican (and I got really REALLY burned out on Mexican food and anything wrapped in a tortilla while I was exiled to Austin for a year and half due to Katrina).  They often play headbanger music (sometimes WAY too loud) so that is a bit of a strange combo of Mexican food meets goth death metal.      This can be a great place to eat by yourself and grab a quick bite to eat or go with others and hang out for awhile.  I usually get either the tacos or enchiladas here as it is a quick and relatively cheap meal (they usually bring you the green and red sauce but you have to REQUEST the yellow habanero sauce).  They have a good rotation of different specials (as much variety as can be expected within the limited repertoire of everything has to involve a tortilla in someway Tex-Mex food).  It does get very crowded sometimes and there can be a wait.  The bar usually turns over pretty quick but some days people just linger for awhile.   They have some very well decorated people working here (and by decorated I mean seriously tattooed up) so it can be entertaining just to watch the staff in action and they do usually provide really good service (the Mid-City location is famous for bad service and that is why I rarely go there).  They make some of the best margarita's in New Orleans and have some good cold beer so a great place to drink and decent place to eat.

This is a good basic bar with a dedicated local following.  It is like stepping back into the New Orleans of old as the place is actually in good repair while still having a vintage feel (so yes hipsters love to come here and attempt to absorb all the vintage they can).  The crowd is like many other NOLA neighborhood bars with a mix of young, old, dirty, clean, blue collar, white collar and just plain weird.  The prices are decent and they have good TVs for game days.  They have some bar grub and often will have crawfish during the season.  The parking can be a bit challenging sometimes as this area often seems to get crowded as there are several other attractions in the area.  My main complaint with this joint is that it can get too smokey for my tolerance.  Overall a decent place to hang out and enjoy some drinks among interesting folks.

The food here is very well prepared and has a nice balance of flavors with balanced spices.  This certainly ranks among the best Indian food I've ever eaten and it is also the most expensive I've ever eaten.  This is also the only Indian restaurant I've ever seen beef served and the sacred cow was divinely delicious.    The entrees here seem to vary widely in proportion so you should discuss this with your server prior to ordering.  The scallop dish seems to be one of the smaller entrees while the beef special ranked as one of the largest servings I've seen here.  The curried gumbo is really great and provides a marvelous Indian fusion spice up to a NOLA staple.  I was a bit disappointed in the small serving of naan that comes in an order when compared to the very generous portion you get at Nirvana.  The vegetable sides are quite pricey and the desserts are very over priced considering the very small portion size.  Generally I would stick to the entrees and specials along with a selection of the starters, such as the phenomenal gumbo, and skip the sides and desserts.

The owners went on some insane rampage and fired all the long time staff in this once great joint.  The burger seems to have really slipped in quality and the meat portion has gotten smaller.  Everybody that knew what they were doing seems to be gone so the once fantastic burger seems to have died with the departing of the long term staff.  Another great thing that just ain't there no more :(

It pretty much seems just like Phil's Grill but now a bit more expensive.  It isn't really bad but then it isn't really fantastic either.  The cost of the food makes it a poor value for just a burger and I spent $20 for just a burger, cheese fries and iced tea.  At that price point I don't see any return visits.

This is a cool little music festival at the Mint and its FREE.  They used to hold it in conjunction with the Seafood Festival but that fest has grown too large and has branched off into its own big event so that has decreased the food options at this fest.  The Creole Tomato Fest is also going on at the same time as this event so you can check that out also.  They have some good music and this is a good opportunity to have a good time but the heat can make it a real challenge.

This is a Rouses on steroids.  They have an exotic meat section where they sell Vietnamese python meat.  The layout of the store takes a little getting used to as they have crammed so much stuff into a smaller space.  They have a lot going on in this place so it will probably take a few visits to take it all in so just grill some python, relax, and plan your next grocery shopping trip.  Although I'm not sure why we can't just get some of that giant invasive python from the Everglades to keep it local...

Hummm I'd have to rate this as one of the less good Chinese joints on the Carroltton corridor.  I've eaten inside which is a bit of a stark prospect and not a very enjoyable dining experience.  The food while not terrible isn't the most tasty and tends more towards the blah.  I'm probably not going to be tempted to ever make another visit here.

Arnold's really surprised me as I was just expecting a typical Southern meat and three joint slinging simple food.  As seems to be the norm in much of Nashville parking was a bit of a challenge and then there was a long line to stand in before getting to eat.  I had read some reviews that mentioned the rare roast beef and I was pretty thrilled to see that I was fortunate to have arrived on a day when that roast beef was being served.  I was expecting the roast beef to just be sitting in some pan being doled out but instead they had a huge roast at a carving station with a man freshly carving off the amazing meat directly into your plate and then adding a bit of au jus love to it.  I was also sorely tempted to get the country fried steak as this seems to be one of the few places that do it without that nasty white gravy and instead use delicious and proper brown gravy but I had to get the rare roast beef so the only logical answer was to just get both.  The only thing I was less than happy about is that there were no lemons for my iced tea which that also seems to have been a thing during my Nashville visit as apparently there is some great lemon shortage in the area or something.  Overall this is a fantastic place with the cooking approaching gourmet levels of awesome deliciousness that really set it at a higher level than your typical meat and three joint.

Did I mention that I HATE the new "GASTROPUB" concept going on in New Orleans recently.  They don't have Abita Amber here and the food is way overpriced for the basic and not so great food.  Just like all the "gastropubs" that are going on in New Orleans why should I bother with mediocrity and when I can just go to a real restaurant or bar where you can actually eat a plate of food that will fill you up instead of being a snack and actually get a selection of more than 4 beers.  Did I mention I HATE GASTROPUBS!!!  There seems to usually be some decent looking women in this establishment and it seems to be one of the more trendy places to be "seen" but it just doesn't work for me and I really don't like what they did with all the "modern" renovations to this classic New Orleans building.  I really like Lilette and I enjoy dining there so it is very surprising to me that I dislike this place so much.  I think it just goes to the core of the fact that I love to DINE and not SNACK and that is why I just can't seem to stand any of the places called Gastropubs so far (and that none of them have my BEER).  It seems to me that I have a far more enjoyable experience eating and drinking at Lilette with far better quality food, a larger selection of drinks, and more comfortable seating so why should I bother with anything at Boligny Taven other than the motivation that women like small plates and go there in large groups.  Ahhh it just doesn't motivate me and I will be staying on the Lilette side.

Ok I will give the first male perspective review about this place:  Yawn... boring... typical chain type fare.  I've only eaten at this chain in the past when traveling and no other good options presented themselves but I stopped in the new Metairie location to give a fair evaluation.  Panera Bread locations in general are really more of a coffee shop type environment that just also happen to "bake" bread.  Their "baking" and "bread making" is done via "par baking," which is short for partial baking: a process in which about 80 percent of the bread-making process (largely until yeast activity stops) is completed at a factory and the remaining steps, including final baking  occurs at the restaurant.  You definitely don't get the same quality and experience as you would from an actual bakery.  If you're in the mood for a quick and slightly more upscale fast food type experience then this place will do the trick.  If you want a Starbucks like experience with pastries and all those type of snacks with the added benefit of unlimited caffeine this place just might make you happy.    Personally I'm not a big fan of coffee shops or most chain restaurants.  I'm also really not very fond of the sandwiches or breads at Panera as I love whole grain breads and Panera's whole grains just don't give me the oompha I love in a whole grain bread and seems far less whole grain than most whole grain breads I can get at a grocery store.  I got the roast beef sandwich on whole grain and it just really failed to make me happy as I can make a far better sandwich from stuff I get at the grocery store.  My honest opinion of their whole grain bread is that it just plain sucks ass and while some of their other breads are better you would think they could do a decent whole grain at least on par with a grocery store brand.  I also tried their oatmeal cookie for the first time and it was one of the worst oatmeal cookies I've ever had.  For this kind of sandwich and for about the same price you can get a far superior and better quality product at Martin's Wine Cellar.  I can't make a better sandwich like Martin's makes from grocery store ingredients and while it might take a little longer at Martin's in my book it is definitely worth the wait for a MUCH better sandwich and better environment.    The good thing about Panera's Metairie location is that there seemed to be a fair number of attractive ladies in the joint and, in fact, it seemed to be almost all women in this place so I guess that is the target demographic of this chain.  So if you just want to watch women and drink caffeine this place is good for that.  For good sandwiches go to Martin's or Stein's.  For fresh baked breads and pastries go to one of our many actual bakeries in New Orleans that actually make and bake their items.  If all I wanted was coffee or tea and a place to use the internet I would probably pick this place over a Starbucks but I never go to Starbucks either as I prefer drinking beer to caffeine.  Overall the food here is pretty blah mediocre to me and the environment is very chain blah disgusting to me.  The unlimited caffeine drinks are cool and the attractive female customers can improve the ambiance slightly with their magical distraction powers.  Personally I doubt I would ever return as it just isn't a good value for what you get and I just don't find the sandwiches anywhere good enough to compete with Martin's, Stein's, or my own.  I also would much rather see my money go to support local businesses that keep more money in our local economy instead of siphoning it off to out of state corporations.

One of the best burgers in NOLA by far!!!  Huge sides that could be a meal in themselves.  One of the most unique selections of burgers anywhere I've ever seen in the area.  This is where I go when I'm craving a really good huge burger.  It also lets you enjoy your food in classic NOLA dive bar French Quarter style with attentive bar staff that keep your drinks full and keep things interesting.  I love the Bull Fighter Burger, Blue Cheese Burger, Chili Chedder Burger, and most of the others....   Those are some tasty burgers!!!  They could make them even better with some custom made buns.

Its still quite a popular mall but it seems to frequently have stores "disappear" from closing.  I rarely venture into this space as the parking seems insanely busy all the time.  This is really the only remaining true shopping mall experience with a large selection of stores and sizable food court left in the New Orleans area.  Now if only Banana Republic still had a Jeep coming out of their window and still sold Gurkha shorts I would be in 80's bliss!

I'm from the South and this is my General Robert E. Lee on his prime pedestal in the center of our Lee Circle looking defiantly Northward at you invading Yankees with your dirty hipster and sloppy tourist ways!  Verily I say unto thee bathe thouselves well and learn to behave in decent civilized ways to dress appropriately for dinner.  Truly do not arrive wearing shorts or jeans to present in our fancy eating establishments.  Do not whine, balk, or complain about not being allowed entry due to your lack of appropriate regalia when such dress codes are clearly posted on websites and the exterior of establishments.    Appropriately honor our monuments to the War of Northern Aggression with due historical respect and leave your snide comments about Southern culture and peoples back in your frost laden Northern lands.  Repent of your Californian attitudes of despising our heavy use of butter, cream, and deep frying in making things deliciously decadent.  Imbibe in the holy consumption of alcohol to achieve the nirvanic state of inebriation so that you might fully embrace all that our Southern hospitality has to offer and join us in the revelry that we freely share.  Releasing your preconceptions and fully embracing living in the space and time that you're in New Orleans will unleash a multitude of  delectable possibilities.    Now salute General Lee and march on to eat something scrumptious!!!

I've been to all of these since they first started and I've still yet to get a po boy at the fest.  They always seem to run out of most things by the afternoon and there are almost always really long lines.  The problem I have is I hate lines and standing in line for a regular po boy I can get all the time in NOLA isn't going to cut it and I only want the "special" po boys you generally can only get at this fest.  The challenge is the "special" po boys sell out fast and rapidly develop long lines.  I arrived right as the fest was opening last year and there were already lines!  Ahhhh standing in line for a sandwich I just can't take it...  The crowds are also completely out of control packed and make it a misery to attempt to walk down Oak Street.  They really need to extend this fest to more days or to a larger area.

Another new place that has jumped on the recent rolled ice cream fad.  They have a much shorter line and slightly better prices than the very popular rolled ice cream joint in the Bywater.  They have a decent selection of flavors and quite a lot of seating inside.  This is definitely a very family friendly place and it seems quite popular with kids in the area.  The service seems to be faster than I've seen at other rolled ice cream joints in the greater New Orleans area as well.  They have an interesting space here and seem to have invested some time with doing some decorating of the place in bright and cheerful tones.

The New Orleans Wine & Food Experience benefits local Louisiana non-profit organizations.  The events showcase local food and chefs along with national and international wines.  This is a five day event which has been nationally recognized as one of the most prestigious festivals of its kind.  The events feature over 175 wineries, 1000 wines and include dozens of international wine and food experts.  The events include wine and food seminars, wine dinners at some of the city's most celebrated restaurants, one-of-a-kind wine tasting events, and two Grand Tastings.    I've only attended the Grand Tastings and the Royal Street Stroll so far.  The Grand Tastings in my experience were very crowded and had very long lines that greatly diminished my enjoyment so I'm not sure I would be motivated to return to that portion of the celebration.  The Royal Street Stroll is a wine tasting and gallery tour that proceeds down Royal Street in the French Quarter and I've done this event for many years and had a great time.  Overall this is a fantastic celebration of food and wine and a good experience that will give you a uniquely New Orleans and Louisiana experience while including a global appreciation of food and drink.

This is the best Academy in the GNO area and probably the all around best place to shop for your sporting gear.  They consistently have the best selection of firearms and maintain the largest selection of ammo of just about any other sporting goods or firearms dealer in the area.  The prices on their firearms are generally significantly lower than any other local competitors.  They have a nice selection of local team fan gear for both professional and college levels.  They often have nice surprises in the sale racks.  The fishing, hunting, sports and fitness sections are well stocked as are their clothing and shoe areas.  This is generally the best place to start when looking for something you need in the sports and outdoors genre.  Academy also sells hunting and fishing licenses for those that might need them at the last minute.

This venue has a small bar space downstairs with the majority of the venue being upstairs.  They have two large bar areas upstairs along with a nice outdoor patio with some nice comfy patio furniture.  I find the drink prices at night to be a bit too expensive, as many places in the Quarter are, and I'm not sure if they ever do drink specials or have a happy hour as I've never been in early enough to discover that.  I've also only been here for crowded events so I'm not sure what its like on less crowded nights.  The ambiance is quite nice and they have made a really nice space here.  It is more of a fancy club scene with VIP options which isn't really my favorite type of venue as I prefer just a plain old bar or live music venue and I hate DJs.  Most of the bartenders here are really nice but I have run into one surly grumpy one before.  This place does attract quite a horde of very nice looking ladies but it does seem to attract a much younger crowd generally.

This is a pretty cool bar and one of the best places to watch jazz.  They also have a nice second floor.  The cover charge can be a bit steep sometimes by Frenchmen St. standards.  This place can also be very touristy and some of the folks here want a concert hall type atmosphere instead of a bar atmosphere and will shush you.  I'm generally more into being all fun and rowdy and not being seated all quietly so I don't end up here much as I get shushed a lot.  I appreciate jazz as a great music and it was largely developed in the famous Storyville brothels of New Orleans where you didn't ever get shushed.  I enjoy New Orleans Jazz the way it was meant to be experienced.

Wow this place has nearly totally collapsed from what it used to be at its prime.  This used to be a really amazing mall and had lots of fantastic stores.  Unfortunately this place has been on hard times for a long while now.  I never go to this mall anymore and I rarely did before as its waaay out in the suburbs.  I was really shocked at how deserted its gotten when I made my last visit out here.  Back in its prime it did have a lot of hot ladies dressed to impress which it certainly doesn't seem to have anymore but I guess the same can be said of the bygone glory days of Canal Street...

This is probably the best Middle Eastern/Kosher restaurant in Metairie.  They have different lunch specials daily and a solid regular menu.  I've enjoyed everything I've eaten here and they have several dishes that generally are not found at other Middle Eastern restaurants in the area.  The prices usually seem a bit more expensive than other restaurants of a similar type but you also seem to often get a bit healthier portions depending on what you order.  While it is located in the typical Metairie ugly strip mall hell they do their best to redeem the interior with an atmosphere that is one of the most intricately decorated among restaurants of this type.

This is a small little bar located (and connected to) directly behind the Azalea Grill.  They have a nice side patio that's actually larger than the interior of the bar.  They have crawfish boils every Friday (during the season), ladies night on Wednesday and other specials along with occasional live music.  The patio definitely seems like an awesome hidden away spot to enjoy a nice day.  This is certainly one of the cooler bars on Jeff Hwy and I will certainly be returning to enjoy the patio.  They only have a Facebook page and no direct website so Yelp won't let me enter that for the address so you will just have to use Google to find that page.

They have a parking lot but currently almost all of it is filled with picnic tables (perhaps in preperation for Gretna Fest) so parking can be a bit of a challenge as this is a very popular lunch spot.  They have some cute and friendly waitresses here that generally take good care of you.  The roast beef po boy is decent and is of the pulled variety but they only have a small size and the bread I had mine served on was toasted way too hard and crunchy.  The burger is a better choice here but they also have a wide variety of items to select from on the menu.  This is one of the better bars in Gretna and I usually only end up here during Gretna Fest but will occassionally stop in for lunch when I'm in the area.  My biggest complaint about this place is they don't serve fresh brewed iced tea and use the aborrent fountain type instead.

Mr. Santos has always been quick, pretty affordable and even downright cheap for lots of things I've needed a tailor for.  I've had many pants hemmed by him and well as things taken up and let out.  He has also gotten me out of some embarrassing jams like one time when I had a zipper on my fly rip off during a conference in Metairie he was able to get a new one sewn on in about 10 minutes and save me a drive back to Uptown to change into a new pair of pants.  Numerous times he has sewn buttons on for free for me.  Mr. Santos has always done efficient and quality work and I would certainly recommend him for your tailoring needs.

I really want to like Herbsaint, as it has a fantastic location and great ambiance, but I've just never been excited by the food here.  I've eaten here many times and I've always been left HUNGRY as the portions are always too small for me (and I doubt I will eat here again without some major temptation).  They do make fantastic drinks and the bar, although very small, can be fun at times (especially during Wednesdays on the Square to beat the heat and enjoy the A/C).  The service has always been excellent and the bartenders are usually on top of their game.  For the portion size and what you get I generally find the food is just is a poor value and my money is much better spent elsewhere to eat but this is a good place to drink.

Decent food for a tourist trap with slightly inflated prices due to the location.  They have acceptable boiled shrimp and crawfish.  The seafood gumbo is good and the fried items have a nice spice to them.  The ambiance isn't very spectacular and the bathrooms are upstairs which could be problematic for some folks.  The food is brought out pretty haphazardly with some people getting served quickly and others at the same table still waiting for their food 15 minutes later.  The servers do their best to keep things flowing well but it often gets crowded so that causes challenges.

This place was really more like a 2.5 star overall.  The staff were really nice but they were a bit slow on refilling my iced tea even though there were very few people in the restaurant.  The building and atmosphere were nice and much nicer than I thought they would be.  The food really disappointed me as it was served in really small dainty portions and the flavors were not very impressive.  I got the Gulf fish and it was a really small portion that made it a very poor value and only a snack with both the fish and watermelon/olive accompaniment being a bit bland.  My friend got the goat tacos and I got to eat one of those and I found it very tough and dry without a lot of flavor.  The dessert I had was probably the best thing I ate and it was a zucchini bread served with peaches and a blueberry syrup.  Overall I'm not sure I would have a great deal of motivation to return as I'm not into dainty small portions and bland flavor but the ingredients all seemed to be quality and fresh so there is certainly potential for a better experience.

I've been going to Tips for many years and I've seen many shows.  I've had friends in bands and gotten to hang out backstage.  I've been to many a New Year's Party and more special events here than I can even begin to count.  I've even seen midget wrestling here.  Ultimately Tips is just a fantastic venue and has some fantastic bartenders.  They often have shows that will run until dawn so make sure to pay attention to the music schedule.  The bathrooms can get nasty as there are some nasty people out there but thankfully it is now non-smoking and you can breath fresh air in here.  This is a place to dance, drink, and enjoy yourself in a crowd so don't think you will be sitting down and having lots of personal space to yourself.

This is one of the better spots to watch some music on Frenchmen and they often don't have a cover.  The crowd can be pretty variable in here and it can be hit or miss a lot of times depending on what other bands are playing in the area.  I've always had relatively quick service here with some above average issues with my order being wrong as the bar is so close to the band that it is often hard to communicate or hear anything.  When on Frenchmen it is certainly one of the main venues to investigate.

The lasagna here has the most meat of any lasagna I've ever had and they also offer it in an Alfredo sauce version if you prefer (I couldn't finish the full size version so the half size lunch portion might be the best choice).  The roast beef po boy here probably has the most meat on it of any roast beef po boy I've ever eaten so plan accordingly as it is also quite nice and sloppy.  They have very large burgers and will often do daily special burgers.  The seafood gumbo here is quite respectable and is usually of the hard gumbo crab with shrimp variety.  They offer a lot of bang for the buck here and portions are huge.  Service is fast and friendly here and they have some nice specials.  The only downside is the location and parking make it a bit dangerous to get in and out of the tight space on the angled road that doesn't have the best viability.

This is a nifty boutique chocolate store that has some very interesting and often local themed confections.  This is a great place to get a tasty gift for those who love all things chocolate.  I personally ate about 100 pieces of their chocolate this past Christmas so I might possibly have sampled almost every "flavor" of chocolate that they offer (including the blue frog... yes they really have a blue frog chocolate).  Every time I've visited this store they seem to have something new and interesting so it is always a great place to check out.

If you grew up watching the Dukes of Hazzard like I did then there is only one way to review this place.  In summary:  KICK ASS!!!  This place is fantastic for all things about those Duke Boys and sometimes ole Cooter himself is around to further kick this place up to Infinite KICK ASS levels of AWESOMENESS!!!  I'm going to go shoot my bow now (obviously with some arrows attached to dynamite) before I call it a day so I can then start hitting up some of Uncle Jesse's special distilled magic and just wait for Daisy to show up and demo some wrastlin moves with me before we take a romantic ride off in the General Lee to ramp off some dirt embankments.

For my 1000th review I want to give a big loving Yelp hug to my neighborhood.  Yelp gimped up my 1000th review and put it under a place it did not belong in its quest to associate everything with a business but this is a neighborhood not a business.  I had to delete that review and yet again add my neighborhood.  The Garden District is my home and where I live.  This is one of the most beautiful areas of New Orleans and has some of the most amazing architecture.  There are amazing restaurants and fun bars.  This is a prime place to catch Carnival Parades and St. Patrick's events.  There isn't anywhere else like this neighborhood in the world and I love living here!

Well now it has finally happened and NOLA has achieved being more expensive than New York, Los Angeles and Austin so hipsters rejoice.  The Caldo de Pollo at El Pavo Real is the most expensive I've ever had anywhere at $14.25 so with tax and tip it was a $20.83 lunch so I would've done better going to Commander's Palace.  This is also the laziest version of this soup I've ever had as the chicken came on the bones and it ended up being the least amount of meat I've ever had in any version of this dish as all I got was two chicken wings, one drumstick and small cut of thigh.  Usually you hope to eat your soup without having to dig your hands in but this one definitely requires the hands and fingers to get immersed and your shirt will get splattered so plan on a messy eating experience with this.   In Austin I used to eat Caldo de Pollo in an upscale restaurant for $8 and that included my iced tea and buttery biscuits drizzled in honey.  At nearby Taqueria Guerrero this dish is $9.99 and comes with much more stuff in it.  I could get a Vietnamese Pho Ga with way more food in the soup for $6 or $7.  So under a $1 in meat and maybe another $1 in vegetables makes quite a killer profit margin for this dish but it kills my desire to return as this Caldo was among the least desirable I've ever encountered and the price is outrageous for other than hipsters (OTH).

This place is a bit different from your typical Tex-Mex joint and offers some things most of the other area Mexican type places don't as the Honduran owners put their own slightly different spin to some things.  They have their "cebollitas" grilled green onion appetizer that is tasty.  They offer the usual taco, burrito, and other options wrapped in some type of tortilla like most Mexican joints do.  I usually opt for one of the entree platters to get a selection of several different things.  This is one of the few places to offer beef tongue as a meat option to stuff your taco or other tortilla wrapped entity.  This place does frequently get crowded and nearby parking is at a premium so it can be more challenging to get here than the usual restaurants in this area so if driving be prepared to park further away and walk a bit.

DBA is probably the bar I like the best on Frenchmen as they have a great beer selection and they usually have some of the best music.  I think their beers are overpriced for New Orleans but other than that I've usually had a good time here.  There is usually a good crowd in here but it is rarely so crazy crowded that you can't get a good spot to watch the band.  The bartenders are usually pretty quick and efficient and I've rarely had bad service.  Always a good mix of locals and tourists so there is almost always the opportunity to meet new and interesting people.  I'm also really happy they have gone smoke free!!!

This is quite an interesting venue that has a vintage ambiance with a hint of rustic to it.  They host a variety of events here from art exhibits to pop up restaurants.  I attended the Mosquito Supper Club's fais do do brunch here and it was like being transported out into the bayou to a Cajun house party.  There was not a lot of table space for eating and the chairs were quite small and uncomfortable as they want you to hurry up and eat to get out on the dance floor  as quick as possible.  Overall this space provided a good environment for a fun event in an unique space that fit it perfectly.

You can eat whatever you want here as long as its a burger.  The setup of this building is a bit confusing where they have both the upstairs and downstairs sections and if you didn't know you needed to walk upstairs you could've been lost as to where to go once you walk inside.  They also seem to consistently have challenges keeping all their menu items in stock but since they are still new and getting slammed by the restaurant of the moment crowd that should improve with time.    The upstairs bar and dining area was much nicer than I expected so even if this place doesn't make it on burgers alone the bar should be a draw.  The burgers here are good and everyone at my table enjoyed what they ordered.  They were out of all their various bacons, guacamole and some of the "exotic" meats they offer along with the sweet potato tots I wanted.  The fries were good except they were served in a mini fryer which took up too much space and was just unnecessarily kitsch.   The service was good and the beer was fairly priced but I still ended up spending about $30 for a few beers, a burger and fries so that did add up to more than I planned.    Overall its a place I will return to see how it develops as they get into their groove as its conveniently near my house.

Ok I had a bad ass go kart in the 1970's that looked like a Formula 1 race car and it hauled some serious ass.  I have to admit I was a bit disappointed when I saw the very un-race car appearance of the karts at this place.  My kart also had bigger ass race car looking wheels that could spin out and do all sorts of cool moves.  The wheels on the karts here looked tiny and weak.  Now the fiberglass body on my old go kart didn't hold up so well to my more "aggressive" style of driving .  This is the aspect where I learned the special magic of these go karts as the crazy twisting and turning track here makes this more like a SuperMario Kart race with people smashing and crashing into you so these carts are made to take massive amounts of damage while staying upright and not getting you killed.    The proportions of the karts here make them very uncomfortable and rough to drive for adults and the ten minute races will really wear you out.  I felt extremely beat up from my first race and I was also really unhappy with my helmet visor that kept fogging up so that I couldn't see but they don't let you leave it up for "safety" reasons.  They have rabid super racers that come out with all their own equipment and really try to smash and crash you up as they haul ass all over this track.  Overall this is a pretty cool place and it is highly entertaining for both adults and children.  The biggest negative is they get all nickle and dimey on you and charge $5 per adult in a vehicle just to enter the park and then you pay for whatever else you do once inside.  Bonus: You get to keep the ninja mask they give you to wear under your helmet.

I've been eating in this place since they were on Vet's in Metairie and now they have moved into my neighborhood and are much more convenient for me to access.  The food here is generally good and they have some Korean style noodle soups that are decent.  They have both a "Chinese" and "American" menu but many of the items are the same on both menus with some notable exceptions.  This place has always been easy to get in and out of and I've never had to wait to eat.  They did irk me a bit the last time I ate there on St. Patrick's night when I ordered a dinner special and they then didn't bring me anything but the entree and said I just ordered that when I had POINTED on the menu to the "Dinner Special" that came with soup and egg roll. If you are in the area and need a quick and good meal this place will meet your needs.

I had some really high expectations on walking into this place as it seemed to be a really great space AND I saw a fantastic looking burger (seriously it had a Pulp Fiction treasure GLOW to it; look at my pic of it) come out of the kitchen so that got me excited.  Things went down pretty rapidly after that as the hipster hostess gave an exceptionally prime demonstration of an apathetically slow reaction time to acknowledge and seat my party which was then passed off to an even more angst ridden and even more slowly moving server.  After a painfully long wait time in even getting our orders in I was much later quite insulted at the portion size of brisket I got for the price I was charged in this joint.  The brisket was also on the tough side and then to add insult to injury they performed the heresy of doling their BBQ sauce out in a tiny little plastic cup like it is made of some secret gold unobtanium.  The brisket tacos seemed to have been constructed of slightly better brisket but still for the price a very tiny serving.  Their chips and "guacamole" were also a really pathetic and lame tiny size for a high price which honestly Taco Bell puts out better flavored options.  To their credit the burger does look fantastic here so maybe that is the item to focus on in this joint that is clearly a special hipster hell.  I might return to sample the burger but I have EXTREME reservations after this experience.

The entrance to this space begins with the wait to get on the elvator to go up and the end of it is to wait to go down again in the elevator. On finally arriving upstairs, while it wasn't crowded,  it still felt a bit congested.  The whole design aesthetic of the space seems to be trying too hard while making it have more of a scattered feel to it with random brick-a-brac everywhere.    I was also rather hoping the downstairs dress code enforcement would extend to this bar but unfortuantely it doesn't.  The bartender's uniform of blue jeans with tweed caps doesn't exactly carry an encouraging dress code theme to me either. The service leaves something to be desired and my experience was too slow for my preference.  The price of drinks certainly trends more on the expensive side with $4.50 Miller Lite along with a limited beer selection.    The highlight of the experience is the viewing terrace which does give a spectacular view of New Orleans and is worth the wait of the elevator.  Overall, I just don't see this space being part of my regular rotation but it would be worth visiting just to show tourists the view and have one drink before returning downstairs or on to other venues.  I would also suggest eating the mile high pie downstairs.

I didn't know anything in this strip mall was even open anymore as I have only driven past this area in the daytime and it has always looked deserted.  Well what do ya know this is a strip mall full of bars that gets busy at night. They had a friendly bartender and friendly patrons here on the night I visited.  This place was so smokey that I had a hard time staying inside it very long.  The "music" mash up by the DJ was absolutely atrocious and pained my ears.  When the noise of the DJ ceased it was replaced, to my horror, with karaoke.  I have a deep disdain for karaoke except when done by bachelorette parties at Cat's Meow or by people that have a fear of public speaking.  I ran out of the door in great fear of my soul being eaten by the karaoke machine.  This place has two doors with one in front and one in back and I ran out of the front door frying pan and into the fire as right next door to this joint is the Devil's Bayou bar and Joe's Caddy Corner Bar which had more karaoke going on!   If Pair of Dice just played regular music and got their beer colder they would be a three star joint for the area.  A smoke filter wouldn't hurt either.

Ahhh the food is ok and the ambiance is not my style at all.  There are usually some decent looking women in this place but it is always so loud that any attempts at conversation are usually futile.  It also can take unacceptably long times to get your food here and often service is extremely SLOW with everything.  I have literally sat for an hour waiting for my completed sushi order ticket to be taken and longer still for my drink to be delivered and that was at the sushi bar.  The food here is consistent but nothing that has ever excited me as it has always just been... ok.  It is very rare I ever go here and usually only when I'm with other people that want to go here.

Nasty dive bar combined with nasty college bar and voila you have TJ Quills!  They typically have cheap booze here and that matches up nicely with the usually nasty and leaky bathrooms full or vomit and urine going everywhere.  There is a time and place for everything but I think my time for this place is long past so I can't say if I will ever return.

I'm afraid the only thing this place has going for it is late night hours and cheap prices.  I pulled into Nashville around 10:40PM and was badly in need of some food so this seemed to be about the only nearby option.  On walking in I quickly wished I would have skipped the nearby option and went to the late night Greek option instead but I thought I would risk going ahead with eating here despite my instincts telling me otherwise.  It was pouring down rain and when I walked in there was a leak dripping water down from the ceiling.  I at first wanted to order the country fried steak but they could only do it with white gravy and were not able to make it with brown gravy which I've never been anywhere that couldn't do that.  So instead I just ordered a cheeseburger.  Next I observed that the iced tea was that lazy processed fountain kind that comes out of a concentrate instead of freshly made tea.  Then they had no lemons for my iced tea which seemed to be a constant Nashville theme for some reason.  When I got my burger it was a pretty pathetic looking creature and it tasted even worse.  I considered trying a biscuit to maybe add some redemption to the place but again only gross white gravy could be done.  This joint is cash only but it still took forever to pay.  This was by a large margin the worst food and experience I had in Nashville during my visit.  Maybe the cheap prices and late hours make the food acceptable when you are drunk outta your gourd but other than that I just see no reason anybody would ever eat here as the food was just awful.

This place is located in a small little snack stand of a structure and you can only order Mexican food to go at the walk up window.  It has tiny little tacos just like the kind you get out of a real Mexican taco truck except they are less good than most I've ever had out of those trucks.  I got the chicken tacos and they were way more dry and flavorless than most any other I've had.  I think the tacos at Taqueria Guerrero are much better for this "authentic" style of Mexican taco.  I've only had the tacos and usually the only time I'm in this area I'm heading to 9 Roses for some pho so given the choice between these tacos and pho I will go pho nearly every time.  Pho sure!

Mid-City's attempt at a New York style/Pizza Delicious style pie.  While the size is comparable the pizza flavor and quality is not.  Its an "ok" pizza but the crust is very chewy and if you attempt to eat it the next day it will be very tough and hard.  For the price I would much prefer Theo's in Mid-City.

Dear Tips,  Raising the price of Abita Amber to $5 and the for real imports to $6 is just a rip off and pure greed!  I can go to Maple Leaf and most places Uptown and on Frenchmen and get cheaper beer and watch great music.  I simply can't afford to pay cover and then shell out $5 for a beer that I can buy for $13 a 12 pack or go to Ms. Mae's up the street and get for $2.50.  I've been a VERY good customer for years but I'm not paying that much for a LOCAL beer!  I might show up for a few shows but far fewer than in the past and I will be doing all my drinking at Ms. Mae's and not at Tip's during those shows.  Maybe if I smoked weed it wouldn't matter so much but I don't and I only like my beer.  Y'all have the freedom in our great country to charge whatever you like but the market dictates to me that you are way out of line with the value of what you're selling so I ain't buying no more.  $5 for Yuengling is outrageous!!!

This place gets really crowded for games and it can get a bit sardine can style packed at times.  The bartenders at not the fastest and some of them seem pretty surly and grumpy to even be there.  The crowd at my last visit was way too hipster for my preference as hipsters love to spread their miserable angst ridden ways to everybody as they hate joyful mirth.  I have to say that the nearby Von Elrod's Beer Hall and the Germantown Pub are just a much more pleasant and fun environments during game time.

This is a Metry dive bar (on that lovely strip mall hell known as Veterans Memorial Blvd) that pushes their Swamp Burger.  I've only been here a handful of times and it was always to eat.  I've only stopped in as I've been driving past the bar and see their sign that it even comes to mind that I should stop in for a Swamp Burger.  It is a nice sized meaty burger just not as big as I was expecting from all the hype they give it.  There are a few other things on the menu but I've never tried them but all the prices seem pretty reasonable.  The ambiance is your usual Metairie dive  bar with sports paraphernalia everywhere and it seems it usually has female bartenders that range from sweet to a bit gruff.  One of my visits ended up being on lingerie night (where women just walk around and "model" lingerie) so that definitely made the burger taste better for that trip.  If you're in the area it is worth a visit to sample the burger but I wouldn't make a special trip.

Jacques-Imo's is one of the most fun dining establishments to enjoy in New Orleans.  I have often waited 3 hours or more to eat but you get to enjoy the bar (or even the bar next door at Maple Leaf).  Chef Leonardi is often at the bar (and at Maple Leaf) and he has often bought me drinks as my group waited.  Many people from out of town seem to get irritated with the wait but most locals find it just gives us more time to enjoy our drinks.  Just use some common sense and if you don't want to wait then make sure you go early!    The worst thing I can say about the place is the bathroom situation is "challenging" in that they are small, often a wait, and a bit hard to find.  Some of the tables can also be cramped and a bit close to one another but that usually just helps you meet new people (so if you're anti-social this probably isn't your place).  Chef Leonardi sometimes has a bit too much fun and gets a bit too tipsy for some peoples comfort but that only seems to bother tourists for the most part (so just enjoy his exuberance and merry making).  The only other problem here is that Jacques-Imo's is only open for dinner (but you can find the fried chicken and some tasty po boy's at Chef Leonardi's lunch time venue Crabby Jack's).  The food is fantastic and great value for what you get!  The menu is very comprehensive and has a great selection of meats, poultry, seafood, and vegetables (and probably a few other food groups that we only eat in Louisiana).  Jacques-Imo's also has some of the best fried chicken of anyplace in the South (much better than Willie Mae's Scotch House).  I do have to seriously caution you about the deep fried roast beef po boy (it is listed as an appetizer) in that you should probably only eat one in your entire life as it is so much fried goodness that it certainly has to have fatal levels of grease in it.  I've always had great service, great food, and great times here so it is ALWAYS a great time to go to Jacques-Imo's!!!

The most comfortable bar in a greenhouse I've yet been to.  It was pretty cold outside on my last visit but a nice fire was going outside keeping it nice and then inside was all toasty warm as well.  The beer prices were quite fair and the service was friendly and efficient.  This spot in Green Hills also makes do as a decent sports bar as they have a good number of TVs about the place to watch your preferred event.  I saw mostly preppy SEC type folks in here and hardly any hipsters so hopefully that is the normal crowd in here for college games as nobody likes nasty surly hipsters not even other nasty surly hipsters.  Decent crowd of folks seem to frequent this place with a focus just on having fun making this just an easy spot to kick back and enjoy yourself.    Overall this is certainly a unique place with a great laid back vibe where it is natural just to have fun like a plant growing in the sun.  Tip:  Don't eat or drink the fertilizer that's for plants not humans.

I used to hang out here all the time before Katrina when it was Moonlight and it seems they have made many improvements in the space with each of the restaurants that have followed and developed into the current Down the Hatch (they just recently added an improved patio in the back).  They advertised a night time happy hour from 11pm til 2am one time when I was there but then they didn't have it when I returned so that made me a bit unhappy (along with the fact they were OUT of roast beef for the roast beef po boy).  They do have some mighty tasty burgers here and I really do enjoy eating those here.  They have bison and lamb burgers available sometimes as well.  I would like to sample the roast beef po boy but I as I mentioned before I was foiled in my attempt.  This place is usually open til 2am so it is a great late spot to grab a tasty burger or sample some of the other things on their menu.

This is a nicer bar with a wine focus that comes with a nice courtyard and indoor seating.  The owners are the same folks that own Tropical Isle and they are often in here and they seem like very nice people.  I've yet to eat in here but the menu looks to have some good things available and I plan on sampling the food soon.  I've enjoyed several drinks here and this is definitely a nice spot to escape the madness of Bourbon street and certainly a step above most of the dive bars in the Quarter.

It's a big corporate chain but at least they are offering healthy organic products.  They probably offer the best soft corn tortillas I've had in NOLA and you get a huge amount of food for substantially less than most other options.  I'm usually not a fan of chains and fast food but Chipotle offers a fresh and healthy alternative that dominates their niche.

The snowballs here are a bit more hard/crunchy with thicker ice than I prefer but they do have some of their own natural flavors they make.  They are quite generous with their flavoring pour and the prices are quite reasonable.  Service is very fast and there never seems to be much of a wait.  They could upgrade their seating a bit and it would make the patio area far more pleasant.

This place offers a decent selection of entrees and sandwiches in the Elmwood area.  I was a bit disappointed that they only offer one size of po boy and don't give you the option for a half or whole and honestly I found the size they offer is on the half size which left me a bit hungry still.  They do some traditional NOLA dishes with a bit of a unique spin so this is certainly a spot to check out for  a quick meal with some more unique choices than offered in many other places in this price range.

This is a VERY popular ice cream joint and people stand in quite long lines to get their fix.  I drove past this location several times on several trips to Nashville when the lines were just longer than I was going to deal with and after many attempts I finally scored a good time with no line outside.  There was still a line inside so I waited for my time to get up to order and finally got to see the different options available and I also got to see it also is on the expensive side for a small serving.  I made my choice and sat down to enjoy my ice cream and it was alright but I have certainly had better so I'm not really sure what the hype is all about that rates standing in line so long but these days in Nashville there seem to be lines all over the place for all sorts of things.

They have an upstairs to go along with their downstairs and usually have some good live music.  This is generally one of the main spots to stop in and check out during a visit to Frenchmen.  Usually there is no cover and the crowd is always a decent size while usually not getting overcrowded.  The only thing I'm not the biggest fan of is that their drinks are more expensive than Blue Nile and DBA.

It's like Nirvana but on Metairie Road!  That would be Nirvana Indian Restaurant not the actual state of "Nirvana" because the same folks that own Nirvana also own this place but you might still find your actual Nirvana here if you love Indian food.  I've been eating here for many years and they have the same type of buffet deal as Nirvana.  The food choices are a bit different and the set up is much smaller but it is still some decent Indian food and one of the two choices you have in Metairie for Indian other than Tandori Chicken.  The parking lot here is really crazy, tight, and you have to park at a really weird angle so getting out can be a challenge if you aren't used to it.

The lunch specials are really not very impressive to me and I don't find them to be a good value.  In fact I would NEVER eat the Monday special of the Cuban steak ever again.  Perhaps the other items on the menu are far better but after sampling several of the lunch specials I'm just not impressed.  They do provide very rapid turn around on your order and the specials are served within minutes of ordering them.  Service is non-existent here and you just order at the counter and they put your food out on the counter when its ready.  Pho Orchid is a block away from here and I much prefer lunch there.  I will return to sample the dinner menu at some point and see if that brings some greater love to the disappointment I've experienced here so far.

I've eaten here at lunch MANY times and had dinner here several times and it has always been very good.  They always have at least 2 different fish specials for lunch along with several other very tasty options.  You get a very large fish portion compared to almost all the other area restaurants.  I especially love when they have Amberjack and Acropolis easily gives you three times as much fish as a comparable special at Drago's.  You get a choice of soup or salad along with your lunch special and the soups are usually the way to go (they have this amazing 6 onion soup with a pastry top that you need to sample ASAP).  They have chicken, meat, and kabob specials that are also delicious.  I've also ordered from the menu and found everything to be very well done.   They also have several Italian dishes and they are very tasty and I really like the lasagna.  They usually have at least one pasta special during lunch and it is a LARGE portion and usually very good.  They also have many excellent Greek versions of dishes you also find in Middle Eastern food such as kabobs, stuffed grape leaves, and hummus showing the wide reach of Greek culture.  If you don't arrive before noon (sometimes before 11:30) then there can be a long wait to be seated as this is a very popular place.  Parking can fill up rapidly in the front and there is additional parking in the back with a back entrance that is easy to miss if you don't know it is there.  This place is definitely worth a visit and some really nice folks working here.

This is just a great old school honky tonk music hall with a lot of history.  The beers are cold and the music is fantastic.  It was mostly older folks cutting a rug out on the dance floor but they have far better moves than most young folks I've seen so I enjoyed watching their skillful dancing along with the great music.  This is a nice spot to catch some great music for the price of what you pay for your drinks. Friendly folks, great bartenders, great music and just a great time along with very easy parking.

Sunday doesn't seem to be the most fun day to get crawfish here.  I've never had so many uneatable mudbugs anywhere in my life as I received in my serving here and I soon learned why.  It seems they had boiled a huge amount the day before and they were mixing in the old crawfish with the fresh crawfish which unfortunately had the effect of overcooking the older crawfish making it mushy and inedible.  I would've been fine with having some of the older crawfish being mixed in with the fresh but they could've just mixed them together AFTER pulling the newbies out of the water and letting them cool down a good bit before combining them and pushing the day olds into an overcooked mush zone.  Friday and Saturday would seem to be a safer bet for the best crawfish here.  I also didn't find the spice overly strong but I like it spicy while I did really miss the fact that they don't use garlic in their boil.  Overall I would probably say you would get a three star or above experience here but my Sunday experience was quite a disappointing batch of crawdaddies as the majority of them were good but far too many of them were bad. Nice folks running the place but for my money I still very much prefer Big Fisherman as my go to spot for consistently awesome boiled crawfish and shrimp (with lots of garlic).

This is a HUGE space accompanied with a mega sports bar with lots of TVs and generally it's quite a nice ambiance.  I still must profess I prefer the original location in Metairie which might be among the handful of times I prefer Metairie to the city limits.  While this is an amazing spot where you can get the fantastic charbroiled oysters and other Drago's signature items just like at the original location it seems to cater to a majority tourist crowd so I favor the more local feel of the original.  You still can have some great food and fun times here so if you've never had a Drago's charbroiled oyster there is no time like NOW!  Overall I prefer the lower prices, better service and usually better food at the original Fat City location in Metairie but I'm always up for some oysters.

This is your basic coffee cafe with desserts, salads and sandwiches that could be in Anytown, U.S.A.  They have some pretty good cheese cake and the iced tea and coffee are decent.  I only came here because it was close to an office I was working out of.  It seems to definitely attract a more "mature" crowd during lunch and not that anything is wrong with a  mature crowd but I mean this place seems to be almost competing with the nearby Peppermill so it isn't a place to frequent if you like to see females that are easy on the eye.  So this certainly isn't your typical coffee shop place like you will find Uptown full of young folks doing homework.  The few times I came here they seemed to frequently run out of things in the afternoon and they get slammed during lunch.  This place is also pretty expensive for what you get.  This just wasn't a place that appealed to me very much, it just wasn't my type of place, as I don't really like coffee shops to begin with but they can serve as good work spots but I can't see getting much work done here.  This place would probably be at least three stars to most other people but it just grates against my soul and if I need a coffee place in this area I'm going to the nearby Morning Call that has a lot more local flavor.

P & J is a New Orleans institution that has been around for generations!  Almost all the best restaurants get their oysters from P & J.  The BP oil spill hit them hard but they're back up and roaring.  These are generally among the highest quality oysters available anywhere in the area.

This place took some adventuring for me to locate and it looked rather scary on the outside but the staff was very accommodating and friendly on the inside.  The atmosphere is definitely that of a run down dive restaurant but they certainly are not going to let you go hungry in here.  I ordered the chicken parmesan and what I was served might be the largest example of that dish I've ever been served.  The food was certainly not the best I've ever eaten but they definitely give you value for your money here.

This is pretty basic and overall pretty bland Mexican food located at the small corner of a strip mall.  The service is nice but you had certainly better point to the exact item on the menu you want or you might get something else.  This is the kind of Mexican food that makes me not such a big fan of Mexican food as most of the selections are just something rolled up into a tortilla of some kind and in the end most things end up tasting exactly the same as each other.
