They do have some decent combos and you can get some items not rolled into a tortilla.  Overall basic and very bland Mexican that will please the most New England spice hater.  The Margaritas will work some special magic on you sometimes though and then if you check out the patio it might turn into a fiesta.

Falafel King looks a bit like a dive outside but is much nicer inside and they really offer a LOT above and beyond what most other Middle Eastern restaurants in the area are doing.  Falafel King has a brick oven fired up slinging their delicious flatbreads and then they also are surpassing most other places in Metairie by offering some really amazing fresh fruit slushies that really need to be experienced to fully appreciate how delicious they are.  Falafel King also is the only Middle Eastern/Mediterranean restaurant I know about that offers consistent daily specials every day of the week except Sunday.  The thing that Falafel King really dominates in is their AMAZING table service if you dine in they really treat you as an honored guest and your drink will certainly stay filled during your visit.  All of the food I have had so far has been really delicious and they really use quality meats along with seasoning the dishes to have fantastic flavor.  They also have a great selection of sauces they serve with your food that take a lot of things to a totally different level with their garlic sauce, yogurt sauce, tahini sauce and spicy pepper sauce.  Their bread really is a step above the typical pita most of the other Middle Eastern/Mediterranean places serve and they have a flat bread that is NOT pita and much more delicious.  They really treat you like an honored guest here and often they give out free samples of many of their amazing food offerings to tempt you into indulging more while also teaching you how GOOD so much of their food is.  I got a free sample of one of their fresh fruit slushes made with fresh watermelon and it was AMAZING and totally convinced me to add their slushes to the items of MUST have at Falafel King as I had pre-conceived notions of a Slush-Puppie or Icee which the Falafel King's version is NOTHING like those as they are real fruit and some of the best frozen things I have ever samples so you have to try them!!!  Do yourself a favor and try this place out as they really take great care of you from my experience.  Check out my video review of my experience here:  https://youtu.be/Iogkjx2STcU

I tried this place out for lunch and Chef Ron was there to greet us and he took our order.  He explained that everything was made fresh from the best ingredients and sourced locally whenever possible.  He also explained that it might take a little longer to get our food since everything was prepared fresh but I found the timing to be very fast and efficient.  The gumbo was ok but didn't seem to have very much seafood in it and was a bit bland for my taste.  The roast beef po boy is pretty good and it was a sliced style with a thinner gravy.  It wasn't my favorite gumbo or roast beef po boy but it was "ok" and it is close to my office so I will probably give it a few more tries as they do have some good looking things on the menu and Chef Ron seems like a real stand up guy.

This is one of several of this chain of hispanic markets that offers a wide range of Latin American groceries.  They also have a very busy deli and bakery offering an impressive array of items in impressive serving sizes for comparatively miniscule prices.  They have many Latin American things that your typical grocery will typically not have.  For just the deli and bakery this place is worth a visit.

The Cabildo is part of the Louisiana State Museum and features exhibits about the history and heritage of Louisiana.  The building features Spanish and French architecture and has served many functions during its history with most of them being governmental.  This building was the site of the Louisiana Purchase transfer ceremonies in 1803.  If you're looking at the front of St. Louis Cathedral the Cabildo is to the left of the church.    Admission price:  Adults  $6 Students, Senior Citizens, Active Military  $5 Children 12 and under  Free Groups of 15 or more w/ reservations  20% discount School groups w/ reservations  Free Purchase tickets for two or more museums  20% discount AAA membership discount, with card  10% discount

This is a cool little bar that is part of a house right in the middle of a residential neighborhood.  I recently discovered this joint during my adventures along the Metairie Road St. Patrick's parade.  It is a long rectangular building with a long bar that covers most of the length of the structure.  We had a cute bartendress, that is also a nurse, and she took good care of us during our visit.  We learned that they frequently have free food here and that this is a popular spot in the area to watch Saints games.  During my visit they had some sausage pasta and mac n' cheese.  There were some serious smokers in here so I really didn't enjoy that aspect of this establishment.  I met some interesting characters in here and I even got invited to go on a  fishing trip to Grand Isle.  This seems like a nice secret spot to go and grab a few drinks and there are certainly some friendly and interesting people in here.

Gordon Biersch is a Harrah's Casino partner restaurant and are located on the Fulton Street Square entertainment district.  Gordon Biersch has some good beers they brew and good food.  Out of all the various restaurants operating in the Harrah's Casino sphere this is probably one of the best.  They have some decent deals on beer samplers and offer some decent specials for their happy hour.  When it is nice outside they also have one of the better outdoor dining areas/beer gardens in this area as well.  As an army vet I also want to give an extra THANKS to Gordon Biersch for offering military veterans a free meal on Veterans Day and I would really like to offer my great appreciation for this fantastic gesture they offer to vets.  Overall this is one of the better spots for good and affordable food and drink in the immediate area, although it is a national chain that won't give you the local NOLA flavor like you can at some of the other spots nearby, this establishment is the only brewery in the Harrah's area so that is something to consider.  My Gordon Biersch restaurant review video from Veterans Day 2020 is here:  https://youtu.be/GMKOhETHFeM

This is a really great Italian joint in Rivertown that offers a lot of bang for your buck.  There was another Italian restaurant right next door to this one several years ago that wasn't such a hit so if you are recalling hearing about less than good Italian in Rivertown it will be that now closed establishment and not this great spot.  The space is pleasing with classic Italian themed music and attentive service.  The huge meatballs here with their very affordable and amazing "Meatball Gendusa" appetizer being one of the stars of the show will certainly please the largest of appetites.  The po boys are very nice here and priced at a great value.  The pizza is done very well and they have really nice roasted garlic as one of their toppings that will cure what craving you might need in the hunger and flavor department along with a more than fair price.    Overall this is fantastic food at a fantastic price in a nice restaurant in the cool area of Rivertown.

This is an interesting joint that has the unique offering of serving several wild game options.  Since I'm an old mean animal killing hunter carnivore I do like to eat some wild game so obviously I was just like a moth to flame here.  They really do have an extensive menu here and even if the thought of wild game terrifies you and your Vegan soul demands non-animal protein grub they will still likely have something here you can stuff your face with.  I really liked the interior decor which was lots of taxidermy meets old wooden shack aesthetic and just made me feel right at home.  The food was nothing outstanding but it was solid descent food that trended more to the bland side for my taste but since I live in New Orleans I'm used to a large degree more spice kick than the average diner.  Overall I would certainly never hesitate to grab a meal here and they really provide a cool environment along with some unique food items not easily found in most restaurants.

The menu looks to have prices that are in line with other area Chinese restaurants at first with the exceptions of the drinks which are at $3.00 (and they also didn't have any hot or iced tea available yet which is very un-Chinese).  My Eggdrop soup was good but they had already put the crunchy wontons in it which had gotten soggy and I generally don't like to have those in my soup anyway so it would be better if they left those on the side for my taste.  The Shrimp Wontons had a good taste but were a bit of a small portion for the price on the menu but... they had the wrong price listed so it was a decent deal for $8 instead of $10.  The Dry Chili Chicken seemed to be a really small serving size for dinner and it didn't even come with rice (maybe they forgot to bring it?) so that made this dish not very competitive with other area Chinese options.  Fried rice is much more expensive here than at other area joints so I'm not sure if you have to order the rice separately for the higher price or if should come with an entree?  Overall this place is brand new and just getting up and started so hiccups should be expected.  The menu is still very concise for the moment and they plan to add combos for lunch starting later in the week.  It was quite crowded during my dinner visit like many new places tend to be when first opening so it will be interesting to see how this restaurant develops.  Service was 5 stars but the food I had was certainly more of 3 star experience and the prices certainly made it much less of a value for the quantity along with the lack of rice or other items being included with dinner entrees.  There are a lot of Chinese options in the area so hopefully this place can find their niche and get their secret sauce worked out.

This is an airport, a great restaurant and a beautiful work of art.  The restaurant here is a great establishment that is nice for weekday meals and weekend brunches.  The entire building is a work of art in an art deco theme and inside there are eight fascinating murals done by Xavier Gonzalez in 1938.  This beautiful space has been featured in movies and is certainly worthy of a visit or booking an event.

This is an Italian food and po boy joint located in a mini strip mall on Veteran's (aka strip mall hell).  The food is ok here and they offer the only version of a "seafood muffaletta" I've seen other than at Johnny's Po Boy's.  They have a few other specials and pasta dishes in addition to their large po boy selection.  The service is usually rapid and the lines still seem much shorter than they were before Katrina.  This is always a good place for a quick lunch but sometimes the portions are a bit small for my appetite.

This bakery puts out very hearty loaves made with as much locally sourced grain as possible and in fact the owner is leading a movement to establish more local sources for grains.  Personally I am not a fan of white bread and like my bread dark and full of whole grains and the Bellegarde breads certainly deliver in the hearty strong category and blow the weak white bread options away.  The bread is so hearty and many varieties so chewy I find them not always the best suited for sandwiches and some varieties are better used in other applications or just stand well on their own.  My favorite Bellegarde bread so far is the Country Rye.

This is one of the better dining establishments on the Westbank and one of the best values in Italian food in the New Orleans area.  The decor is a bit dated 80's style but I LOVE the 80's so that doesn't bother me!  They have a couple of different rotating daily lunch specials along with their regular menu.  The food is good here, served in nice quantity and they have a unique seafood gumbo that is more like a gumbo z'herbes as its rather green but very tasty.  They give you both yeast rolls and garlic bread with your meal.  On my most recent visit I had the lasagna which was nicely done and very tasty.      The service here is very friendly and accommodating.  The family that owns the establishment is usually present and very friendly and engaging.  The location is a bit off away from most things and parking can get a bit cramped.  Really the only two main things I would like to see improved are that they don't offer real butter with your bread and they don't have towels in the bathroom to dry your hands and only offer an air dryer.    The food quality, value and friendliness of this place definitely warrant a trip to the Westbank to visit this establishment.  Tony Mandina's video review:  https://youtu.be/a8Q-y4jAXIk

I've got many years of experience eating banh mi and po boys at a multitude of locations and this was really disappointing to me.  I've heard about this place for years and my expectations had gotten rather high but the shrimp option did not deliver.  The menu is really small and only offered a selection of 4 "po boys" and a grilled cheese.  The "po boys" are nothing at all like a NOLA po boy here as they are really small banh mi style sandwiches that use some Vietnamese elements thrown together with some other options but they don't offer creole mustard or any other mustard so you have it their way and get no choice of condiments on your own.  For a banh mi size sandwich the price was insane as most banh mi are around $2-$6.  The flavor of the shrimp was just off and didn't taste right at all with lots of bitterness.  One of the other people that I was eating with got the grilled cheese and that was also insanely overpriced for the end result.  There are just far too many better options at extremely better values than what is offered here.  To me this place just doesn't cut the mustard.

Tujague's is an institution in the French Quarter and though the food might not be the best in New Orleans it is still pretty good for what it is. They have a very limited selection of items on the menu and I usually prefer to just stay with the brisket that includes its awesome, spicy, creole, horseradish sauce (they give everybody a sample but I always want more).  I also really like the chicken bonne femme (when I can tear myself away from my red meat addiction) as it is some of the best fried chicken you will ever taste.  I've been here for many private parties and had many good times here so this has always been a fun place for me.  The bar is quite a great thing to experience and they sling some good cocktails that should make the most discerning cocktail snob happy while having a good selection of beer that makes me happy.  In addition to enjoying drinking in their bar I really love eating in their bar as it is also the only place you can order their FANTASTIC brisket sandwich.  Eating in the bar is a completely different experience than in the restaurant so some might find they enjoy one over the other.  They are open nearly every day of the year so this is a great place to go for holidays and other days when many other places are closed.

Looks like a really cool dive bar from the outside but when you go inside ouch it is waaaay too smokey.  This was the smokiest place I encountered during my whole visit to Nashville and it was even more smokey than Santa's Pub.  I couldn't stand being turned into a ham so I had to get outta there as fast as I could and instead planted myself next door at nice and smoke free Tenn Sixteen.

Ahhh Drago's charbroiled oysters are a beautiful thing to see, smell, and slurp a few dozen down like the addict to them I am!!!  What's better than getting 3 dozen grilled and another dozen or two raw???  The downside is nothing is exactly cheap at Drago's but it is cheaper at this location than their new space at the Hilton.  I'm also rather disappointed in the portion size of their fish lunch specials as you get about three times as much fish at nearby Acropolis for a much lower price.    They have a lot of great seafood options and are one of the few local places that offers lobster as a consistent special on their lunch menu.  The other menu options are very good and they also offer a good selection of po boys.  They have some really good gumbo and lots of changing daily seafood specials.  Did I mention the oysters and how you just have to eat those charbroiled oysters.  Excuse me I have to go somewhere... must have oysters now!!!

Honestly in the world of national chain fast food sandwiches I think Subway does a better sandwich.  Why would you even want to eat at this option when you could get a locally made po boy from a local business that would keep more money in the local economy?  This store seems generally well run and clean along with keeping a pretty good volume of business so I guess they are doing something right but it just isn't my cup of tea.

This is one of the better dining establishments on the Westbank and one of the best values in Italian food in the New Orleans area.  The decor is a bit dated 80's style but I LOVE the 80's so that doesn't bother me!  They have a couple of different rotating daily lunch specials along with their regular menu.  The food is good here, served in nice quantity and they have a unique seafood gumbo that is more like a gumbo z'herbes as its rather green but very tasty.  They give you both yeast rolls and garlic bread with your meal.  On my most recent visit I had the lasagna which was nicely done and very tasty.      The service here is very friendly and accommodating.  The family that owns the establishment is usually present and very friendly and engaging.  The location is a bit off away from most things and parking can get a bit cramped.  Really the only two main things I would like to see improved are that they don't offer real butter with your bread and they don't have towels in the bathroom to dry your hands and only offer an air dryer.    The food quality, value and friendliness of this place definitely warrant a trip to the Westbank to visit this establishment.

For some reason I could never get Yelp check in to work here?  I was excited to try this place and when I walked in it looked and smelled fantastic to further excite my palate.  My party ordered the pastrami sliders, swallow cloud soup and General Lee's Chicken.  Sadly I was really disappointed in how bland everything ended up tasting and I would have rather have gone to any other Chinese or Vietnamese place for better tasting food.    The General Lee's Chicken came out first and it is a HUGE portion so you get a lot of food for your money with this entree but I found it just didn't have a lot of flavor or spice to it while it sure looked pretty.  Next came out the swallow cloud soup (which didn't seem to have any greens in it as described on the menu) while the dumplings in it had some meat that did actually have some good flavor the broth was pretty bland to me and the noodles seemed to be the same type you get in a cheap ramen noodle packet.  Finally the sliders came out and they were the most disappointing item of the night as they were just like Vietnamese tacos but with far less on them and the main flavor on the sliders came from the kimchi while the cubed pastrami didn't do much for me.  I really wanted to like this place but it seems like some bland food loving Yankees were in charge of the flavoring for for the night as so much of my meal was just in need of much more spice.

I love this place and I hate this place.  I love the food and all the fried seafood po boys are excellent as are the slow roasted duck and the fried green tomato shrimp remoulade po boys.  They have some good plate lunches but the portions are on the small side (especially when compared to the huge po boys).   I HATE the fact that they don't have but ONE public restroom to wash your hands before and AFTER you eat. I HATE the fact that there is very limited seating and I HATE the fact they ask for tips when they don't provide any service (back when they had cute girls working there I didn't mind so much but those days seem to be long gone).   I love the fact that the po boys are so overstuffed that you usually end up with so much food left after you eat your sandwich that you have nearly a whole other meal to finish with what has fallen out (this process is messy and you frequently want to clean up after but you have to rely on napkins alone!).  They do have good parking but they could probably stand to expand the dinning area and lose a few spots.  So to sum it up I would recommend just getting your food to go and you will be happy as if you attempt to dine in it just isn't very enjoyable usually.

This is a really great Italian joint in Rivertown that offers a lot of bang for your buck.  There was another Italian restaurant right next door to this one several years ago that wasn't such a hit so if you are recalling hearing about less than good Italian in Rivertown it will be that now closed establishment and not this great spot.  The space is pleasing with classic Italian themed music and attentive service.  The huge meatballs here with their very affordable and amazing "Meatball Gendusa" appetizer being one of the stars of the show will certainly please the largest of appetites.  The po boys are very nice here and priced at a great value.  The pizza is done very well and they have really nice roasted garlic as one of their toppings that will cure what craving you might need in the hunger and flavor department along with a more than fair price.    Overall this is fantastic food at a fantastic price in a nice restaurant in the cool area of Rivertown.  Gendusa's Italian Market video review:  https://youtu.be/a8Q-y4jAXIk

I had been wanting to try this place for awhile but the hours have always been inconvenient for me since they are only open for breakfast and lunch.  On entering I thought "this place has potential" and the ambiance inside is intimate and nice as they had a musician playing.   I became a bit concerned when I noticed almost everybody in the restaurant was wearing a conference ID badge as many of the other reviews for this establishment had noted that it was quite the tourist trap.  I was also a bit disappointed as I had been planning on getting the lasagna that was listed on the online menu but they didn't have it listed on the actual menu on Saturday when I arrived.    I eventually decided on getting the signature red gravy pasta and adding two meatballs.    While the pasta and sauce were decent and one meatball was good while the other one was cold it definitely wasn't a lunch that was over $30 good for just spaghetti and meatballs with an iced tea (along with the added expense of having to pay for parking).  For that price point I can go to Commander's Palace or another fine dining restaurant and have a multi-course meal with far better service and environment.  The service at Red Gravy was mostly on the acceptable side but my drink was left unfilled for some longer pauses than I would prefer and at their prices I should be able to expect better results.  For pasta with meatballs there are lots of other places that are on par with the food here at half the price or less so I probably won't be returning and I will leave this spot for the tourists that don't know any better.  The food is three to four stars but the high pricing really makes it a poor value for what you get for this type of food so there are just many better choices at their price point so that drags them down to two stars.   It probably is worth a splurge for brunch or lunch at least once just for the experience and to add it to your been there done that list but definitely not a regular spot for most locals at their price point.

This seems to be a very popular coffee shop for the night time study crowd.  They also have a nice board with upcoming music shows and other events posted.  The coffee was not the best to me but it was not the worst either.  The tables seem too small to me for comfortable studying but I guess I'm old and used to books and notebooks instead of all electronic all the time but I still need to write things down myself to really help my memory take them up but maybe that is my outdated brainwashing from my ancient schooling jading my opinion (except for the research that proves otherwise).

Ok nice big space here and it is a decent place in a decent location to watch live music or attend other events.  Big huge minus is the fact that they seem to always be out of any decent beer (they advertise Heineken everywhere here but NEVER seem to have it) and seem to always just have PBR and Miller Lite for $5.  No wonder so many people seem to indulge in getting themselves into a drug induced rave haze of one kind or another prior to arriving here in order to enjoy themselves despite the  poor choices at highway robbery prices.  The other great aspect is that they only take cash at the bars so you have to travel with large sums of cash to have any hope of enjoying any alcohol induced bliss here (and carrying lots of cash in NOLA is never the best idea).  Anyplace that sells PBR for $5 just makes me angry (and I'm just insulted by the sheer gouging of such a cheap beer at that price) and being left with low alcohol lite beer as my only other choice makes me want to stick a vodka IV in myself so I can finally catch a buzz to enjoy the freak show bands that usually play this venue.  They generally don't play the type of music I like here anyway so fortunately I rarely have to endure the hyperinflated swag beers here.

New Orleans Ice Cream Company has some pretty nifty local themed and often sourced flavors of premium ice cream.  This brand can be a bit of a challenge to find and so far I have only seen it at local groceries like Rouse's, Zara's, Langenstein's, Dorignac's, Breaux Mart, Fresh Market, Winn-Dixie and Whole Foods.  Their Po Boy Ice Cream sandwich is probably the finest ice cream sandwich I have ever had and I believe Parkway Bakery offers those also.  I first tried their ice cream at a Yelp event and I have been a fan ever since.  This stuff has to be really good to occasionally break me away from my normal Creole Creamery and Angelo Brocato's addiction.

I've only eaten here at lunch but I've eaten here MANY times at lunch and it has always been very good.  They always have at least 2 different fish specials for lunch along with several other very tasty options.  You get a very large fish portion compared to almost all the other area restaurants.  I especially love when they have Amberjack and Acropolis easily gives you three times as much fish as a comparable special at Drago's.  You get a choice of soup or salad along with your lunch special and the soups are usually the way to go (they have this amazing 6 onion soup with a pastry top that you need to sample ASAP).  They have chicken, meat, and kabob specials that are also delicious.  I've also ordered from the menu and found everything to be very well done.   They also have several Italian dishes which is a bit strange in a Greek place but they are very tasty and I really like the lasagna.  They usually have at least one pasta special during lunch and it is a LARGE portion and usually very good.  They also have many excellent Greek versions of dishes you also find in Middle Eastern food such as kabobs, stuffed grape leaves, and hummus.  If you don't arrive before noon (sometimes before 11:30) then there can be a long wait to be seated as this is a very popular place.  Parking can fill up rapidly in the front and there is additional parking in the back with a back entrance that is easy to miss if you don't know it is there.  Definitely worth a visit and some really nice people working there.

The gumbo here is a 2 star and most of the sandwiches hover between a 2 and 3 for me.  I find the BBQ shrimp po boy alright but it is probably one of my least favorite versions of it in the NOLA area.  The "Breathtaking Beef" roast beef po boy has always disappointed me as it sounds fantastic but tastes bland and I've never been able to taste any horseradish on it.  The garlic oyster po boy and the Reuben are probably the best sandwiches made here.  The seafood platters and shrimp remoulade are also good as are some of the daily specials.  The ambiance of this place is the biggest redeeming factor as it is a complete and total classic New Orleans dive with lots of character and characters that can be seen here.

It has been several years since I last ate lunch here and my recent experience left me extremely displeased.  My father had a CEU class that he had to be at at 1:00 and we arrived for lunch at exactly Noon which for the simple food that Tujague's does should have been plenty of time for us to eat.  Multiple tables that arrived after us were served and their checks were paid and those people departed and new people were seated and served as we still remained waiting.  Finally when our food did arrive I made my one request of the day to have more of the horseradish sauce to eat with my brisket.  The staff member assured me twice that it was on its way but it never arrived.    We finally left the restaurant at 1:30 which was far too late for my father to attend his event.  I've always been a fan of this establishment but they definitely had the amateur team working today and need to take some serious action to improve service.  I also saw numerous people walk in from the street to only be left standing around and nobody ever greeted them so they finally left so they are also losing lots of business from their lack of service and attention to detail.

This is one of the best po boy joints in the area.  They excel in everything from roast beef to seafood (both grilled and fried).  Unfortunately they close before dinner so this is mainly a lunch spot and there is limited seating.  The biggest issues here are that they only take cash (which is always a huge hassle) and it is usually slow (which if you're getting quality I don't mind and usually you do here).  Rumor says they have the best shrimp po boy in the city and I probably can't argue that point.  The roast beef is also among my top choices and is very multiple napkin worthy.  This is a classic New Orleans po boy joint atmosphere and a unique local experience that everybody should sample.

I checked this place out for their opening weekend.  It will be a cool place to enjoy a German style beer garden.  The main food options are almost totally pork based with even the no-pork options seeming to be stuffed with some kind of sausage or pork item.  I am disappointed they only had a pork schnitzel as I love some veal, chicken, beef and venison schnitzel.  They have some appetizer snacks like pretzels and such and actually had a small but decent dessert menu.  Overall this should be a good addition to the neighborhood but I really hope they expand the schnitzel offerings for those of us that don't eat that pig meat.  *Update: they have added chicken schnitzel.

This appears to be a simple spaghetti or pizza place from the outside but when you walk inside you discover it is actually an intimate restaurant doing Northern Italian in a fine dining atmosphere.  Even though the restaurant's atmosphere seems to be fine dining most of the customers seem to be dressed causally.  This might be one of the smallest restaurants in the entire city but there always appear to be people sitting outside enjoying themselves at the sidewalk tables.  From memory the servers recite the longest and most deliciously detailed descriptions of their daily specials that I've ever heard at any restaurant.  The menu has a good selection of other options if by some improbable chance the specials don't entice you.  My biggest disappointment here is that I'm not a fan of their lasagna and I would certainly recommend steering clear of that.  The pasta prices are rather expensive for pasta and I think the meat and seafood entrees are often better choices if you don't go with the specials.

The most dive of dive bars and it is ALWAYS Christmas!!!  The dedicated don't even go til 4am but happy hour is 9pm-Midnight.  It is a glorious dream & dank nightmare that blurs and melds into an alcohol induced numbness of sensation that both terrifies and fascinates all at once (damn that tiny evil Santa!).  Always an interesting crowd and the most unusual things to see and hear going on.  Usually some pretty good music being played by the bartenders and somehow shots (usually Jager or Jamison) always end up being put in front of you whether you ordered them, want them, or even run from them.  I've seen & experienced some very strange things in this filthy glorious place but I don't recommend sitting on the couch just from what I've seen.  Sadly when the sun comes up they kick everybody out and make them go home (or to Ms. Mae's or Brother's Three but that is another story).

How strange I used to have a review for this establishment but yet AGAIN somehow YELP has made it disappear???  Gordon Biersch has some good beers they brew and good food.  Out of all the various restaurants operating in the Harrah's Casino sphere this is probably one of the best.  They have some decent deals on beer samplers and offer some decent specials for their happy hour.  When it is nice outside they also have one of the better outdoor dining areas/beer gardens in this area as well.  As an army vet I also want to give an extra THANKS to Gordon Biersch for offering military veterans a free meal on Veterans Day and I would really like to offer my great appreciation for this fantastic gesture they offer to vets.  Overall this is one of the better spots for good and affordable food and drink in the immediate area, although it is a national chain that won't give you the local NOLA flavor like you can at some of the other spots nearby, this establishment is the only brewery in the Harrah's area so that is something to consider.

Tujague's is an institution in the French Quarter and though the food might not be the best in New Orleans it is still pretty good for what it is. They have a very limited selection of items on the menu and I usually prefer to just stay with the brisket that includes its awesome, spicy, creole, horseradish sauce (they give everybody a sample but I always want more).  I also really like the off menu Chicken Bonne Femme (when I can tear myself away from my red meat addiction) as it is some of the best fried chicken you will ever taste.  I've been here for many private parties and had many good times here so this has always been a fun place for me.  The bar is quite a great thing to experience and they sling some good cocktails that should make the most discerning cocktail snob happy while having a good selection of beer that makes me happy.  In addition to enjoying drinking in their bar I really love eating in their bar to order their FANTASTIC brisket sandwich and the Chicken Bonne Femme.  Eating in the bar is a completely different experience than in the restaurant so some might find they enjoy one over the other.  They are open nearly every day of the year so this is a great place to go for holidays and other days when many other places are closed.  Unfortunately Tujaque's will be moving to a new location after more than a century at their current spot in the Fall of 2020.  You can watch my video here:  https://youtu.be/f2iMXCfns2o

I love this place and I hate this place.  I love the food and all the fried seafood po boys are excellent as are the slow roasted duck and the fried green tomato shrimp remoulade po boys.  Their fried chicken is also among the best to be found in New Orleans.  They have some good plate lunches but the portions are on the smaller side (especially when compared to the huge po boys).  I HATE the fact that they don't have but ONE public restroom to wash your hands before and AFTER you eat. I HATE the fact that there is very limited seating and I HATE the fact they ask for tips when they don't provide any service (back when they had lots of cute girls working there I didn't mind so much but those days seem to be long gone).  You also need to get here at least by 11am if you want to eat inside without a wait and then they are only open for lunch and close at 3pm.    I love the fact that the po boys are so overstuffed that you usually end up with so much food left after you eat your sandwich that you have nearly a whole other meal to finish with what has fallen out (this process is messy and you frequently want to clean up after but you have to rely on napkins alone!).  They do have good parking but they could probably stand to expand the dinning area and lose a few spots.  So to sum it up I would recommend just getting your food to go and you will be happy as if you attempt to dine in it just isn't very enjoyable usually.  My video review of Crabby Jack's is here:  https://youtu.be/90vAm9gxejQ

I've eaten at the original Parran's Poboys in Metairie many times but this was my first experience in this location.  It was a bit bittersweet to me coming here as I was a big fan of the sushi joint that was here previously and it was really strange to me seeing how much of the space had been moved around and changed.  I certainly felt a bit like a fish out of water and a man out of time with how so much had changed in here.  Of course I ordered a poboy combo and as it has always been in the past Parran's put out a good product and I enjoyed my poboys.  I don't know if I will ever quite get used to this being a Parrran's instead of my long time sushi joint but it is a nice addition to this area.  Overall Parran's has a long history of doing good food but I still think there is more character at their original location in Metairie while the food is good at both locations.  My video review of Parran's Poboys Uptown is here: https://youtu.be/Vc7HhfiMI98

This is one of the best po'boy joints in the New Orleans area.  They excel in everything from roast beef to seafood (both grilled and fried).  Unfortunately they close before dinner so this is mainly a lunch spot and there is limited seating. Rumor says they have the best shrimp po'boy in the city and I probably can't argue that point.  The roast beef is also among my top choices for a sliced style roast beef and is very multiple napkin worthy.  If you don't want a po'boy they also have some great listed daily specials on the menu along with chalkboard specials that are also fantastic choices which have included gumbo, oyster artichoke soup, shrimp stew etc. etc. which give you more options of deliciousness! Overall this is a classic New Orleans po'boy joint atmosphere and a unique local experience that everybody should sample.    My video review of Guy's Po'Boys is here: https://youtu.be/asgRGYpUcgg

The food here has drastically improved since my last visit years ago.  Their turtle soup is amazing with huge chunks of turtle in it larger than any other turtle soup I have ever eaten.   The BBQ shrimp po boy has really stepped up and now is much bigger with a LOT more shrimp than the last time I ate it.   The "Breathtaking Beef" poboy has also drastically improved from my last sampling of it although it could still use more horseradish and some Creole mustard added to it.    Speaking of Creole mustard that is the only thing that fell flat on my three visits I made over the past couple of weeks as all three times when I requested Creole mustard on my po boys and on my cheeseburger it was never applied so I had to make another request to find some mustard.    The crawfish etouffee is also quite nice while the burger is really large and the fires that are served with it are nice as well.  The garlic oyster po boy and the Reuben are also nice sandwiches you should try at some point.  The seafood platters and shrimp remoulade are also good and they have a decent choice of daily specials.  The ambiance of this place is the biggest cool factor here as it is a complete and total classic New Orleans dive with lots of character and characters that can be seen here.    My video review can be found here:  https://youtu.be/lu-sxxWt4CM

I LOVE Deutches Haus so much I joined and became a member!  I'm German on both sides of my family so it just seemed like the natural thing to do.  It was a very sad loss when the old Mid-City location got "taken" by the hospital development that still isn't developing.  The current temporary location of the Haus in Metairie is certainly not as much fun as the historic location BUT the new location is going to be AWESOME and is right next to the Fairgrounds.  The Haus is renowned for Oktoberfest but they have MANY events and festivals throughout the year.  They also run the Haus like a bar from Wed-Sat so you can just stop in for some awesome German beer.  I think Deutches Haus is a fantastic organization and I highly recommend anyone that is of German ancestry, interested in German culture, or just interested in having fun check it out and consider becoming a member.

Leni's Café is one of the most affordable restaurants for New Orleans breakfast and lunch in the Warehouse District.  Many locals say it is their choice for the best value for a New Orleans breakfast restaurant in the area. Leni's Café is a popular neighborhood spot for the residents and workers in the Warehouse District. Leni's Café has become noted for their affordable daily plate lunch specials that feature a lot of great New Orleans and Southern food. This is a great spot for breakfast and lunch with daily specials, burgers, po-boys and other traditional New Orleans food.  Overall this place offers some great value on good food.  My video review of Leni's Restaurant is here:  https://youtu.be/C3NY-U-x-l4

I'm not a coffee shop person as I would rather have beer than coffee.  If you find yourself in need of a coffee shop this is a beautiful location in an old bank.  They have a large downstairs, sidewalk seating and a cool upstairs so you can find the perfect nook to use your computer, study, read, stalk the other coffee shop patrons or whatever it is that people do in coffee shops.  I've stopped in here a few times to use the WiFi and it seems like it usually has decent connectivity and speed.  You should keep in mind that this joint is frequently very crowded and they only take cash.  The coffee isn't anything outstanding and cost more than coffee should and in this area I would rather go to Cooter Brown's to use their WiFi and drink beer.

The Ogden museum is five floors and they have a rooftop patio at the top.  This museum showcases all aspects of Southern culture with permanent collections and rotating exhibits and includes a weekly event known as "Ogden After Hours" featuring the best of the diverse talents in Southern music. Ogden After Hours takes place every Thursday (excluding holidays) from 6-8 PM and is quite a popular and fun event.  Admission:  Free Members $10 Adults  $8 Seniors, 65 and over  $8 Students (with current i.d.)  $5 Children 5-17 Free UNO Students, Faculty, Staff (with current i.d.) except special events (i.e. Ogden After Hours - $5). Please note other special event prices may vary. Free Children under 5 Free LA Residents Thursdays 10 a.m. - 5 p.m.  Adult group tours are $8 per person with a minimum of 10 adults.

This is a really cool museum that would appeal to younger children.  I've only been here for events and parties and this is a fantastic location for fun times.  I've never been here when there were actually children in the museum but they have some really cool interactive displays that I have to assume most kids would find fascinating as I still find many of them to be interesting.  Admission:  $8.00 per person, adults and children. LCM members and children under the age of one are admitted FREE. Adults must accompany children under 16 years.

This is an ok seafood spot on Magazine famous for their tile interior and decent to great oysters.  The main drawbacks to this place are that they close for the Summer (usually from May-September) and they only take cash so it can be a bit of a hassle.  They are a bit unique in New Orleans for not using French bread on their oyster loaf and instead use some stuff akin to Texas Toast they call "Pan Bread" (I also get irked that they seem to eternally be out of creole mustard as that is what I like on mine).  It has seemed more inconsistent in quality over the last few years and there are certainly better places at better prices but it's unique tiled interior makes it worthy of a visit just to see a classic New Orleans oyster bar.

This is probably the worst and most expensive movie experience in the area.  The seats are not comfortable to me and the screens appear smaller than any other venue.  They do have servers that will bring you food and alcohol for a premium price but the food isn't that great.  This place is dead last of any theater I would want to watch a movie at.  I appreciate the concept and I've seen it executed very well in other cities but it is not done well here.  I would far prefer going to Prytania or one of the AMC locations for a cheaper ticket price, easier parking and far better experience.

For Metairie this is ok Thai food but really I think I've had some better Pad Thai at some Vietnamese places.  The lunch portion is very much on the light side of a serving size for the price.  I would far rather go to any of the Thai places in Orleans Parish but if you are trapped in Metairie this is one of your few options for Thai.  The parking is also pretty limited and challenging so be prepared for that.

For the NOLA area this is good Mexican food but it is WAY overpriced for what it is.  Surprisingly the menu selection is quite limited.  This place is attempting to be fancy fine dining in a very Metry kind of way which doesn't work for the peasant food that Mexican food is.  Nothing here is awe inspiring or must have and I was slightly excited by the prickly pear margarita but it didn't impress so the only decent one in the area is still at Rivershack Tavern.  They do some things with lobster that might interest some people.  I seriously doubt I will be returning as this place just doesn't work for me but it might work for some out in the burbs.  At the price point of this place there are hundreds of other places I would much rather go to with far superior food.  I'm sure there are lots of people that will love this place and it should do well but it just isn't my style.

The gelato was alright and quite authentic with an interesting flavor selection but they are not being competitive with Brocato's as Piccola only allows one flavor for their small serving and doesn't allow two flavors until the medium size while Brocato's will give you two flavors in a small.  I also sampled their espresso and sadly it just did not impress and Brocato's and most other places in town have much better espresso.  The space is set up nicely on the interior especially considering it is in one of the out of place strip malls on Freret Street that would be more appropriate for everywhere else strip mall U.S.A.    Overall it is really the only Gelato or ice cream option on the Freret Street corridor and they do have some creative and good flavors to their credit.  For the price and experience it doesn't compare to Brocato's, Creole Creamery or Sucre but they probably have a niche location here that should help them with some success with all the Tulane students that probably don't even know about the existence of any other area of New Orleans or the dessert treats outside their bubble.  They have some definite unique wins with their flavors so if they can just adapt to allowing multiple flavors on a small and work on the espresso they can go far.

I go to Le Bon Temps often and they have some good music.  They also have FREE oysters on Fridays but they go quick so you need to get there early!  The kitchen serves food til pretty late and I don't even know when they close it down so that is an option to keep in mind.  The bar is divided into 2 main areas with the front being full of pool tables and the back where the bands play.  This is usually a really fun bar to watch music until the point that it gets too crowded, which is way too often, but you always have the front area of the bar to escape to.    The back area, where the bands play, can just get miserably crowded especially on Thursday nights when Soul Rebels play (it also is a bad "tradition" that the Soul Rebels NEVER start on time so it is like 12:30 or 1am before they start usually so if you have to work the next day that really is a challenge).  There are also some people that take their pool games WAY too seriously in here and I've seen a few fights break out over a stupid game so don't get in those folks way.  Parking can sometimes be a bit of a challenge but if you get far enough away you can always find a spot.      They usually have pretty quick bar service and I usually prefer the front bar when there is music as it is quicker to get served than fighting the often formidable crowd in the back.  There is always an interesting crowd here and there is a special plaque on the bar involving a historical person that I will let you discover yourself.  There always seems to be something going on here when it seems nothing else is anywhere else in the area.  FYI:  This is yet another of the bars that claims the notoriety of having had Lee Harvey Oswald as a frequent customer.

They have expanded their offerings and I was able to get a great plain flavored kombucha tea and a great green smoothie.  They have a lot more products and menu items available now and this a great place for some healthy items that you aren't going to find anywhere else in the area.  For such a small place they pack a lot of punch and they take credit cards.

The ambiance and location of this charming Italian restaurant, located in River Town (in Kenner Bra), force me to use words I typically only use when describing a puppy or baby.  This little gem is adorable, precious and amazingly cute.  Italian is spoken by the staff, who just happen to be from Italy, and you get a completely authentic Italian experience.  The one big downside to the complete authenticity is that they don't serve American size portions and you will really need to get multiple courses to have an adequate meal.  Recently at lunch I got the chicken Parmesan and it is the smallest serving of food I've ever had in the USA (but very European sized) as it was a very small chicken breast that came with maybe two tablespoons of pasta.  Just my entree and an iced tea cost $20 with tip and I was still very hungry after so to get full here you will have to plan on spending more.  The other authentic challenge is that nothing is going to happen fast here and you need to get ready to take some time to enjoy your meal.  If you've got time and don't need to get back to work anytime soon and have some extra money to spend this could be a nice spot for lunch but most folks have tighter schedules and budgets these days so that makes lunch here challenging.    Considering all of these factors dinner is probably the better choice for dining in this delightful spot.  Overall the ambiance of this place is five stars but the prices and tiny portions really drive the value down when compared to all the other Italian restaurants in town.  Pasta is very cheap so it really is inexplicable they don't give you a better serving size. They definitely take the time to do things right and make quality food but its still at a premium that is bit too high for the out of NOLA location no matter how charming that location is.  I would certainly return here occasionally for the charm but it definitely isn't a spot I would ever be a regular at.

This is probably the worst and most expensive movie experience in the area. The seats are not comfortable to me and the screens appear smaller than any other venue other than the Broad. They do have servers that will bring you food and alcohol for a premium price but the food isn't that great. This place is dead last of any theater I would want to watch a movie at. I appreciate the concept and I've seen it executed very well in other cities but it is not done well here. I would far prefer going to Prytania, Broad or one of the AMC locations for a cheaper ticket price, easier parking and far better experience.

Yes its a tourist trap and they sling those crazy Hand Grenade and Horny Gator drinks that will eat the polish off your shoes but you can have fun here as a local because they actually get some decent music here.  The Tropical Isle's are all best experienced in great moderation just like the Hand Grenades so make sure you pace yourself.

This Acme is typically a lot easier to get into than the one in the French Quarter and the food is exactly the same because this place has pretty much become a chain.  The raw oysters are always good and the fried seafood and po boys are typically the things they do the best at.  The gumbo is terrible and I would just skip it.  The prices are expensive for what you get and I think there are many better places with better prices.

This is a pretty cool looking venue with a nice patio area (AKA "Backyard" area).  After sampling the bbq brisket, burger and chicken I would have to say the brisket is definitely the winner here.  The guy at the register told me he thought the brisket was better than the Joint's which he was a bit off as I would put it in second place to the Joint and then I would also recommend they start offering it as a BBQ plate option as all you can currently do is get it as a sandwich.  The burgers and chicken sandwiches are ok but for the price didn't really impress me other than during their lunch special they offer.  You also get quite a selection of sides with regular fries, tater tots, sweet potato fries, potato salad and cole slaw all being offered at an unfortunate extra charge.  For my dinner trips this place has never been that busy and food was brought out fast while at lunch (when they offer their combo special deal that should be an all the time deal) the place is packed and food delivery was quite a bit slower.  So if you have a short lunch break this might not be the best option when this joint is crowded.    Overall I would say just get the brisket and enjoy it.

I stop at this Rouse's location pretty often as its on my way home from work.  What I like most about this location is that they always seem to have a quick check out process compared to other locations I go to.  They also seem to always have a better selection of seafood and have a higher quality choice of cooked seafood items than any other Rouse's in the area.  This place is always busy but the wait at the deli counter for sandwich meat is usually significantly faster than at the Tchoupitoulas location.  I like the efficiency of this store.

I've been to this Rouse's location once with a friend of mine and I found it a bit smaller and less well stocked than the usual branch of this grocery but it still met my needs.  They seemed to have things set up in a bit of a unique way here with a different layout than most other Rouse's I've visited.  It looks like this store is certainly needed as there are definitely not a lot of other good grocery options in this area around UNO.

This is a decent Ethiopian restaurant with a nice ambiance inside.  They have a small courtyard in the back that still seems to be in the process of getting finished.  The food here seems less flavorful than you would expect and the portion sizes are less than I've had at other Ethiopian places. The flavor and portion sizes are both superior a bit further down Magazine at Café Abyssinia.  They will actually give you silverware here if you want it.  Overall its really about a 2.5 star experience.

I was really excited that I might finally be able to avoid the tourist trap that the original location has become but then I was quickly disappointed they didn't have the veal like they do at the original location.  I wasn't in a fried chicken mood and when they didn't have the veal I decided to try something different and got the shrimp plate and it just wasn't very good fried shrimp.  The butter beans are great just like the original joint but the ambiance is very lacking in here.  They really need to add a TV behind the bar so folks can watch football etc. to take their minds off the generic environment.  The service was pretty mediocre and there were not even many people in the restaurant.  They also really need to get longer straws as the ones they use are swallowed up by the glasses they use.  I would suggest just sticking to the chicken in this location or better yet just go to the original location.  I don't think I will bother with this location again unless they do some serious catching up to what you get at the original in terms of ambiance, selection, service and overall experience.

Debbie Does Doberge has a new location that is open late and slings some amazing desserts.  On my several visits now there has always been a good crowd of folks enjoying the desserts.  They also have other food but so far I've only had the desserts.  Lots of folks seem to like to grab their treats to go and take them down to enjoy at Courtyard Brewery.

This is one of my least favorite festivals.  In past years this festival has been held in  in a really small and cramped space with too much crammed into the tiny area but this year they moved into a larger nicer spot in Armstrong Park.  There is some GOOD music and that is the only redeeming factor to this event other than the move to a larger space.  Even though the space isn't as small the line for drinks is usually LONG.  Unfortunately a lot of the food is disappointing here and very sadly many of the gumbos are AWFUL!  There are still some good things to eat but this festival has among the highest level of disappointing food options of any festival currently held in New Orleans.

This place seems a lot cleaner since the new ownership took over.  The food is still about the same "ok" quality as it always was but the menu is a bit different than the old one.  The service is absolutely HORRIBLE and you have to make substantial effort to get anybody's attention after they initially take your order.  I would suggest sitting at the bar and you will probably get slightly better service as compared to hardly any service at the tables.  The only awesome five star thing about this place is that it really is 24/7 so you can always get something to eat here.  If the service wasn't so very bad it would be a three star joint and it also seems they cleaned out a bit of the character that used to be here... or at least a lot of the characters that used to always be eating in here.

I'm not the biggest fan of food trucks but I had just experienced an unsatisfactory meal at Rum House and I was still starving.  Lucky for me this truck was right outside of Rendezvous so I thought I would roll the dice and finally sample some trendy food truck grub.  I got chicken tacos which, at $8 for three baby tacos, I thought was a rip off but they were the same size as the three baby tacos that I had just eaten at Rum House (for like $18) so they were a comparative bargain.  I got the "stupid hot salsa" for my sauce and didn't find it all that hot really but it was alright.  I could have gotten double the food at this truck for what I paid at Rum House for a similar product but honestly I don't think the tacos at either place are worth more than 50 cents each.  I've gotten tacos this size made by real Mexicans in taco trucks in Austin for like $2 but I guess you're paying for the convenience of the food being right in front of the bar.  These tacos are definitely better than many made in stationary restaurants but for the price they charge I might be tempted to make a run for the Taco Bell border... oh wait never mind the drive through line is around the corner; so instead I would go for the $5 pint and a slice at New York Pizza.

This restaurant is a fun NOLA anomaly because the vast majority of locals will look at you really intently if  you DARE call the streetcar a "trolley" and they will quickly correct you and say "you mean streetcar!"  That being said this is a great little spot for breakfast, lunch, and dinner food.  This place has a bit of a diner feel but with classic New Orleans dishes available early and open late.  They used to be 24 hours all the time but now they seem to only be 24 hours on certain days which are usually around the weekend even though they advertise being open 24/7.  I've always gotten really great and friendly service in classic NOLA style with the waitress calling me darl'n, sweetheart, and luv.  The food is a good value and this is a favorite spot of NOPD who seem to have largely abandoned St. Charles Tavern for here.

Ok the owner contacted me as he was concerned about my negative review and informed me that he had recognized the drop in quality and that he had worked with a chef to revamp the menu and that I should return to try it out again.  I will raise my prior 1 star (that I wanted to give a zero for) to two stars just for the fact that he has recognized there are some serious issues here and he says he is working on it.  I'm nothing if not reasonable and I really do care that our NOLA restaurants meet a certain standard.  So I'm perfectly willing to sample a revamped menu and try food again.  I also LOVE food and I would be extremely happy if Nacho Mama's served food I liked as it would give me more dining options.    My initial plan was to return three times to sample things to give a fair evaluation.  I asked the owner what he recommended and he told me the tacos (with his favorites being the panko crusted catfish and the arbol steak), the taquitos appetizer, shrimp chimichurri, fajitas, or one of the signature tortas.  So one day when I wasn't feeling particularly hungry I finally got the courage up to sample some Nacho Mama's food again.  I really had to force myself to go inside as I've got powerful memories of bad experiences in there and getting sick from eating the food so I had to really focus some willpower to just walk in.  First impression was that there was a fantastic smell of food cooking so that is a big thing and eased my initial anxiety.  The menu is definitely revamped and much improved looking from what was in there previously.  I ordered the two taco plate and got a chicken and lime shrimp with a side of guacamole, and an iced tea.  My initial visual impression when I got my food was that the rice in a scoop ball looked like I didn't get very much rice (it was plenty but visually it initially looked small until I spread it out); I also thought the tacos were a bit lighter on the fillings compared to other places;  I also hought the shrimp were smaller than all the other shrimp tacos I've had in the area which isn't necessarily bad as sometimes they can soak up more flavor but my initial thought was ummm small baby shrimp.  The food smelled good and I started with the chicken taco which had some good flavors but I found it very dry (compounded by the corn tortilla which I think might be the worst chokingly dry soft corn tortilla I've ever had and it crumbled apart it was so dry).  The shrimp tasted good but again the tortilla was very dry but not as dry as the chicken.  If I didn't know better I would say they were stale but all they really needed was a bit of steaming to soften them up more so an easy fix to greatly improve that experience.  I next ate my rice and black beans which had a very good flavor and I liked those.  When I payed my bill it came to $13.44 so with tip that seemed a bit expensive for two tacos so that didn't seem like a good value to me for what I got and I would probably head to Juan's or Sarita's if I just wanted some tacos and I would get more bang for my buck.  So I was thinking that it was improved from what it used to be but it still isn't that great... and then I had a slight bit of a tummy ache that night which I attributed to the tough tortillas.  Sticking to my initial game plan I decided to once again venture forth and sample the fajitas.  I ordered the shrimp and steak combo and when it came out I was rather shocked at how small an order it was.  There were only four shrimp and five pieces of meat on the platter!  I had a huge plate of "fixings" with guacamole, sour cream, fresh salsa, cheese, and lettuce that was much larger than my fajita plate.  There just seemed to be some great disconnect between the two things and I was left with lots of extra fixings.  My fajita's alone were $18.66 (before tip) and for like another $2 they would have thrown in rice and beans.  The fajitas tasted "ok" but I felt that it was a horrible rip off for such a small portion of meat and I could have had a lot better food at many other places for that price.  I was still considering returning one last time to fulfill my initial plan until my stomach started gurgling and then I got to spend all last night and a lot of this morning with a very sick stomach.  I have figured out that this isn't due to food poisoning as the effects on my stomach are much more akin to what happens when I eat something with evil fake fat, like Olean, in it.  So something that they are using to cook with is having a serious adverse effect on my stomach but it isn't to the same degree as food poisoning.    My END evaluation is that the food here is a terrible value that just isn't up to par (cheap drink specials though).  I seriously believe this place needs EXTREME changes to produce decent food and I gave the owner the contact info to apply to Gorden Ramsay's show.  I can't see myself ever returning to eat here unless Gorden whips this place into shape as I don't want my stomach feeling like this again!

I'm an expert in eating BBQ across the country and addicted to beef brisket as you can quickly tell from my Yelp reviews and this place has made me a happy camper as it is very near my house.  This establishment has all the trappings of a pure and simple BBQ joint while having really excellent brisket and burnt ends.  I really hope they bring back some of the amazingly awesome sides they had back when they were in Metairie briefly as the short lived Smokin Buddha Bbqieux as the handful of experiences I had at that establishment ranked among my all time favorite BBQ experiences with the best sides I've ever had with BBQ anywhere.    Currently you get a choice of three sauces for the meats (brisket, burnt ends, sausage and pork butt) with a selection of four sides (mac and cheese, spoon bread, rice salad and slaw).  I would like them to add fresh brewed iced tea and expand their sides to some of the great things I had before when they were in Metry but the meat seems to definitely be a contender for ranking among the best BBQ to be found in NOLA.  So far the only real downside of this place is that they often sell out before I can get back from work to get some brisket or burnt ends for dinner.

It looks a lot more like a New Orleans seafood joint than a Chinese joint from the outside.  The food was alright but really heavy on the pork and light on the shrimp in the shrimp fried rice.  I probably wouldn't make a special trip out here just to eat here and I would probably end up at one of the other restaurants in the area before eating here.  Inside was nice and clean with attentive staff.  The food at dinner might perhaps be better than the lunch experience I had as I just found my food on the bland side.  If I lived in Lakeview I would probably stop in to eat here when I needed some Chinese and they do seem to have some decent lunch specials along with a lot of parking.  It is very hard to tempt me in here though with Russel's Marina Grill and Two Tony's so VERY near.

This is just a magic Willy Wonka candyland!!!  They have some fantastically decorated desserts and sweet treats in here that are nearly too pretty to eat but they taste mighty good when you do!    They generally have a nice selection of good but not fantastic gelato (as several of the flavors are very mild and if you were blindfolded you might have problems discerning some of the flavors from the others).  I'm also not the biggest fan of their espresso (I much prefer Angelo Brocato's).  Sucre is also a bit pricey for what you get but they do give very large scoops for even their smallest size of gelato.    It is hard to find anywhere else that has such beautiful presentation and artistically crafted deserts along with the fact they stay open very late (especially on weekends) so just for that they rank 5 stars.  They recently added alcoholic concoctions and I haven't yet sampled any of those so that is an adventure still to be had.

Their hot & sour chicken soup is 5 stars but everything else is around a 3 and sometimes a 4.  I always get an extra large bowl of the soup; as I do love that lovely velvety like texture of it (equally as good as La Thai's version just not as much stuff in it with a bit of a different flavor profile).  They have had some good seafood specials that I've experienced here and the curries are decent but not anything special.  They have recently added a sushi bar which seems a bit out of place in the manner in which they have installed it; so I'm still not sure what to think about that and I don't plan on ordering sushi here anytime soon as I come here for the Thai (really mainly the SOUP).  This place has certainly always been consistently good and their seafood specials have always seemed to be the things I've been most impressed with (other than the SOUP and I will come here often just to eat that!!!).  So in summary I think you can agree I think you should really try the hot & sour chicken soup.

This is probably the worst Middle Eastern food I've eaten in the entire Greater New Orleans area.  The few times I've eaten here it seems to be run only by a husband that does the cooking and his wife that is the only waitress/cashier/hostess.  I have found the portion sizes to be extremely small for the price and the flavors are very lacking as compared to all other Middle Eastern food I've ever had.  I've never had bad Middle Eastern food before so I gave this place several chances over the years and I hate to report that every visit was a disappointing one.  This place has always been very deserted during my visits and I've only seen at most 2 other people dining here (which unfortunately is probably a good measure of the quality of the food).  The family seems nice enough but the food just doesn't really merit a return visit from me ever again.

This is probably the most dive like Thai place in the NOLA area.  Before Katrina I used to frequent this place several times a week for their lunch buffet.  I don't believe they ever brought the buffet back after Katrina as I haven't seen it since.  It was never the best buffet and the food I've ordered at dinner is also not the best example of Thai food I ever had but it is always tasty and filling.  This usually isn't my first choice for Thai but if I'm in Cooter Browns and want some Thai this is the place to go.  The best thing about this place is they usually have the cutest actual Thai waitresses working and they are very nice people that give great recommendations.

This is one of the most massive convention centers around.  I first came here way back during the 1984 World's Fair as a wee child and it has grown more than I have since then.  In its current incarnation this huge venue hosts various events like conventions, like the Comic Con I've attended, and numerous Carnival Balls I've danced my way through.  I don't suggest eating here as there are too many far superior options in a city like New Orleans noted for its excellent food culture.  The one continuing issue I've had with events here is they frequently don't post the actual location of the event and with such a huge facility you need to know exactly where you're going to as otherwise you could spend a very long time walking around so you might have to call the convention center to confirm the location.

I've eaten here four times over multiple years since they first opened and it has been consistently terrible with basically everything consisting of just a big pile of bad-melted-greasy-congealed-plastic "cheese" over some very substandard mush of tortillas and whatever else you happened to order as your filling (and it tastes worse than it sounds and we won't discuss what it does to my stomach).  I'm not the biggest fan of Mexican food but I can't even qualify this as Tex-Mex (or really as edible food).  This is just some of the worst food I've had anyplace.  The service is pointless to even discuss because there is none.  Most of the other reviews here are just being WAY too nice or are counting in the cheap drinks BUT the drinks don't even come close to redeeming anything about the place.  I observe people eating the food OFTEN on my way to drink at the Bulldog and it looks consistently disgusting and people often leave large portions untouched at deserted tables.    I usually wish the best for anyplace contributing to business in NOLA and want them to succeed but this place has been so BAD for so LONG they just need to close and make way for something better to replace it.  I'm ASHAMED to have this place in my neighborhood!!! This joint is a ZERO and not even worthy of 1 Star.  This is permanently on my "no go" list!

My friend recently expanded his catering business to include a retail restaurant.  NOLA Boils offers boiled and fried seafood options along with po boys, grilled oysters and daily plate lunch specials.  The fried shrimp and oysters are among the largest I've seen at any restaurant while the prices are a substantially better value than other nearby places like The Galley (which I find quite expensive).  The dining room is small but nicer than many other joints and they also have a few tables outside.  I only wish they had fresh brewed iced tea instead of fountain drink tea and also offered seafood gumbo in addition to their chicken and sausage gumbo.  For a brand new establishment they are doing great food at a fair price and I'm sure they will continue to improve all aspects of their operation going forward as they expand their restaurant based on their extensive catering experience.

This is one of the events put on by the Krewe of Oak.  This is a fun event where you get some unique blends of New Orleans crazy characters and fun spilling out into the neighborhood with the after party at the Maple Leaf Bar late into the night/morning.  You need to be a member of the Krewe of Oak or know a member of the Krewe of Oak to attend this event.

Consistent good results can be expected and this is probably one of the better fast food chain joints for burgers.  They load you down with a lot of french fries here and the service is typically fast and efficient.  With so many options available to customize their burgers they have always gotten my burger correct which isn't the case with most other fast food joints.

This is the best and most flavorful Chinese I've had in a long while!  They use plenty of wood ear fungus (which is very healthy for you) in their tasty hot and sour soup and other Chinese places have been so stingy with this ingredient I was beginning to think it was an endangered species or something.  The freshness of the ingredients is evident and there isn't any evidence that they're using pre-made frozen stuff they're just reheating like a lot of the lazier Chinese places have gotten.  They have really good specials and have many things on their menu that are authentic Chinese along with Americanized dishes.     I'm really unhappy that I got charged for an entire extra soup when I asked to substitute hot and sour for the egg drop with the lunch special when the two soups are EXACTLY the same price!   So I might not eat lunch here again and pout for awhile before I return for dinner.

I had the crawfish bread and that was really great and then their cheesecake was also very nice. Unfortunately I was very unimpressed with the BBQ and would probably skip that from this point forward.  They had a much larger menu with several great looking items outside of the BBQ realm that were more NOLA style food.   Overall they should probably focus on their other food and give up on being a BBQ place as they don't come near The Joint, Central City BBQ or even Frey or Blue Oak.  The service was really friendly and they took great care of all the folks.  I would say you should certainly visit for the food but definitely not the BBQ part of the menu.

This is a solid Italian bistro with a small and intimate atmosphere.  Lunch is  a good value here with a nice selection of specials that rotate Monday through Friday along with an affordable selection of their regular entrees.  Dinner is a bit more formal and offers a much larger and nicer selection of items on the menu.  I've enjoyed everything I've ever eaten here and it has been consistently good while nothing has ever just blown me away.  This isn't really a fine dining atmosphere but it does attract an older crowd for dinner that tends to dress more formally.  Lunch generally draws a business crowd and business casual would be the typical attire.  Overall this is a great place for lunch and an affordable dinner option if you're in the mood for Italian.

I love the concept but the execution often falls short and when demand is high the system often breaks down and wait times can get very excessive.  The actual streetcars themselves are fantastic and I live right off the St. Charles streetcar line.  For me its usually a very convenient way to get around except during special events and until after Midnight when the streetcars seem to get much more rare than their published schedule would indicate.  You need a $1.25 so have it ready and get ready for a rambling ride through history.

I've been nearly every year and this year was by far the worst.  The bathroom situation was out of control bad.  I've always gotten a 3 day pass or 3 day VIP pass.  I had such a bad time this year I gave my armband away and didn't return after Friday.  The single day tickets have gotten outrageous and when a festival costs more than Jazz Fest you're losing most of your locals.  Hardly any of my friends went this year and the line up was terrible other than the local bands (and I get to hear them often and for far less than what the prices at this fest are).  They had freaking carnival rides this year and it just was totally out of place along with what seemed like very diminished crowds.  I'm not buying a pass for next year and I will need to hear about substantial changes to return again which is very unfortunate as this is the best weather of any fest in NOLA.

Mardi Gras is one of the things that New Orleans is famous for and arguably something that New Orleans does better than anywhere else.  Mardi Gras strictly refers to Fat Tuesday but in common usage it often refers to the entire Carnival Season which starts after Twelfth Night, on Epiphany (Jan. 6th). It is a season of parades, balls, and king cakes.  Celebrations are concentrated for about two weeks before and through Fat Tuesday (Mardi Gras in French), the day before Ash Wednesday.
