There is generally at least one major parade each day and many days have several large parades. The biggest parades take place during the final five days of the season. For the last week of Carnival events occur EVERYWHERE in New Orleans and the surrounding area.  Parades in New Orleans are organized by Carnival krewes and the Krewe float riders toss "throws" to the crowds.  Throws include beads, doubloons, plastic cups, and toys.  Living in New Orleans and experiencing an entire Carnival Season is an unmatched experience and makes life anywhere else during that time painfully dull!

The food is decent except when they run out of things or haven't defrosted things which has happened on every visit.  The service is just unacceptable and its a miracle if you can get your drink refilled.  I hope I don't have to ever come back to this joint and I would far rather go to the City Diner next door or Tic Tock Cafe across the street for much better food, much better prices and light years better service.

This is one of the best venues for events anywhere.  The most amazing thing I ever saw here was probably the Pink Floyd show.  The energy and excitement during a Saints game is hard to match.  They have a large selection of food and drinks but need a better beer selection.  The main negative with this place is the total rip off prices they charge and especially the price gouging they do with beer!  This is the home of Who Dat Nation and they are one of the loudest and most creatively dressed fans of any in the NFL.  I've been to many events here over the years and always enjoyed myself other than the extreme lightness in my wallet after paying some of the ridiculous beer prices.  The Dome is at the center of life for many of the most enjoyable things available in New Orleans and they are done in ways that only New Orleans can do them.  After Katrina we all feared that the Dome and perhaps most of the city was done for but the rebirth and rise of the Saints to the Superbowl infused our city with a new energy.  You will never have a boring time here!

I've had GMC/Chevy vehicles for all my life except for a stint with a Jeep Grand Cherokee.  I purchased my last GMC vehicle here, a Terrain, and I've had my vehicle serviced here.    I haven't really been happy with my Terrain (which is a GMC design issue and not the dealers) and it will probably end up being my last GMC/Chevy vehicle as my experience with it has led me to decide that I will most likely go with a more reliable manufacturer in the future.  I find the Terrain to be a dismal failure as an SUV as it is far too low to the ground and has far too low of a clearance for NOLA driving along with a less than ideal turn radius along with frequent flat tires from the poor tire design and choice that don't work well for New Orleans pot holes and other rough driving realities.  The battery design of the Terrain is also so ludicrous that nowhere but the dealer can change the battery as they have it locked away in a manner that requires special tools to access it that only the dealerships have so any battery change will cost you.    I have been generally happy with the service department here as they allow you to schedule a time to bring your vehicle in and they are VERY good at completing the service within one day and getting you back on the road in a far more efficient manner than I've experienced at other car repair locations so the repair department is worthy of four stars for that.  Unfortunately GMC is not worth many stars from the poor design of the Terrain which ended up dying with less than 75,000 miles on it which is unacceptable for a modern vehicle or ANY type of SUV.  So now I've gone back to a Jeep Grand Cherokee.

Inconsistent seems to be the best way to describe this place.  They seem to attempt to be all things to all people and don't do all things well.  I've had some good dishes here and then I've also had terrible food served to me.  They also do sushi here which can be variable from good to less so.  They just have such an ambitious menu covering so many things that it is hard for them to execute everything well.  The building and interior of this place are modern and clean which are aspects that don't always exactly blend in that well with St. Charles Ave. but it is tolerable for what it is.  The best thing about this place is that gets them an extra star bump is that they have later hours so you can find something to eat when many other places are closed.  Tolerably average is the best way to sum this place up.

A great spot for a picnic and a very tight squeeze for festivals.  The French Quarter Fest and other events are held here and it can get really crowded very fast in this narrow strip of land.  I love fests but I also appreciate this area when it is calm and you can enjoy looking out at the Mississippi River and have a long lazy picnic as the world on the water slowly drifts past.

Its a holiday that I get the day off for that folks in other parts of the country have no real clue about.  This is the end of long and amazing Carnival season that really distinguishes New Orleans from the rest of the United States and most of the world.  Being virtually anywhere else on Mardi Gras day but New Orleans is a terrible idea as this is the center of an amazing celebration that is roaring to its conclusion until next year.  There are so many activities, king cakes, parades, events, balls, parties, dinners, lunches, snacks, excessive costumes, total lack of clothing, elegance, decadence and sheer exuberance.  There is just nothing else like it!

Kyoto is the closest GOOD sushi restaurant to my house so if I'm in need of a quick sushi fix this is where I will head.  I really like the area that this establishment is located and there are several great places to eat clustered nearby.  They have a lot of interesting rolls that are unique to them and they are generally very fast with getting your food out.  The Poke salad is probably one of the most outstanding things they make here and many of the cooked items from the kitchen are often overlooked but still very tasty.    * Quick Tip: If you sit at the sushi bar you get a free bowl of miso soup.                            ALWAYS sit at the sushi bar!!!  It often does get crazy crowded here at night (and especially on weekends) but it has always been a quick lunch spot (if you sit at the sushi bar).  Parking can be problematic at times (and I miss the days before Katrina when they wouldn't hassle you about parking in the strip mall parking lot across the street).  It is also really nice that you can run to Creole Creamery next door for dessert.

They have really improved the fish selection here and offer a menu that details both the local selections then those that come from Japan.  I find the sushi bar here to be better than many of the kitchen items generally.  I have found many of the rolls are often not rolled tightly enough and come apart easily.  In the sushi restaurants selection of the Metairie area I would place this location of Little Tokyo at around third place with Kanno being #1 then Shogun at #2.

This is a bit of a hidden away space where you might want to sneak into if you determine your quest necessitates you to escape the crowds of Bourbon Street.  This is a very concise venue with some craft cocktails to encourage some higher prices.  The ambiance leans towards a bit of a tiki bar theme.  The target audience seems to be the hipster folk.  It could be an alright place for a few drinks but I don't think it would ever rate on my regular rotation.

Good boiled crawfish and shrimp at decent prices.  The crawfish pie is one of the pre-made varieties and not made at the store.  The shrimp was  properly boiled and not over cooked which seems to be a hard thing to find these days.  They also offer Banh Mi style po boys, fried seafood and some Vietnamese and other Asian options which are also nice.  This establishment is run by a very nice Vietnamese family that takes good care of you.

To me a snowball is mostly about the ice and ice here just doesn't inspire my love like Hansen's does but it's better than some other joints and they have definitely improved the quality of it of late.  They have a nice selection of flavors and they also expand beyond just snowballs to offering other food items which might be part of their problem.  The places that seem to be the most awesome snowball places tend to specialize in just doing snowballs.  This place does offer a great value as you can get a very large snowball for not a lot of money.  The wait is usually significantly less here than many other popular snowball purveyors in the area.  This place is alright but when compared to the nearby Hansen's it just doesn't compare as Hansen's snowballs totally blows them away except if you're in a hurry and can't wait in line at Hansen's this will do in a pinch.

I avoided this place for awhile as I didn't know they had an inside but then my waitress from Mona's defected so I had to try it out.  This place has some of the most tender and tasty lamb I've ever had!!!  I've been several times and enjoyed everything except the giant burger, which I found was too much bun and not enough meat.  I recently went with a group of people and we got the giant combo kabob platter and that was a LOT of food for the price and we all enjoyed it so much that even though we were full we got more food as the meat was just so tasty.    Nice people running the place and the owner has very high standards for his food and wants to get fresh organic produce whenever possible.

The really standout thing about this place is their fantastic backyard and patio area which is one of the largest and most amazing of any in NOLA!  They have bananas growing on their trees ready to eat along with an amazing cabana and bar area ready for a party.  The interior of the hotel is nice but some of the rooms are quite small so be specific about what you need when booking a room as there is some variation.  Hotel Storyville definitely has more of a friendly hostel feeling to it than a fancy hotel.  Depending on what you're looking for this place might exceed your expectations or make you wish for more fancy digs but for most folks it should be quite adequate.

Ok definitely do yourself a favor and stick to the burgers.  I had a bland and dry chicken dish with some bitter "citrus" rice that I could have cooked myself for under $3 and mine would have tasted light years better (first alert).  Some of the other entrees the people were eating next to me looked good but they were very unhappy with one of them and didn't eat it so the bartender was nice enough to comp theirs (second alert).    My poutine fries, that I also ordered, were nothing to write home about either and I also had the pleasure of biting into a chunk of sharp glass that was in the cheese topping them (third alert).  Now I understand all sorts of things can end up in food so that wasn't that a big a deal to me and the bartendress, once again, was nice enough to comp the fries and the kitchen guy apologized to me and that would have all been fine with me EXCEPT that I spent the entire rest of the night and into the next day with terrible stomach issues from some poison or contamination that I had eaten in my meal (fourth alert).    Once again places don't always have control over those issues but when multiple things like this all happen at once it really starts to concern me.

Karaoke isn't something I enjoy being around and it was the main theme of the moment when I visited here.  Maybe it is more fun on other nights without the karaoke.  The crowd was very light during my visit and they also have darts and pool to distract you if you need those games.

This is probably the best vitamin and supplement store in the New Orleans area.  Stupid Whole Foods stopped carrying the majority of things I use so now this is where I get my Nature's Plus vitamins and George's Aloe Vera (two of the secrets to my eternal youth).  The only disadvantage of this store are that they often don't have the best selection and the prices, sales, and specials aren't usually as good as what you can find on the Vitamin Shoppe's website.  I'm glad the physical store is available when I need something fast but I generally order most of my products from the website.

This place really encourages you to eat a great deal and they don't want you leaving here hungry.  When you first walk in they ask if you've been before and they explain the process and sometimes bring little extra items for you to sample.  They have a large selection of items on their "buffet" and then you order grilled meats from the grill counter.  All of the grilled beef items I had seemed very similar in taste and the guy working the grill didn't seem to understand English so well so maybe something was lost in translation.  I ate three plates of meat and a large plate of "buffet" items and was very full for lunch.  This is a place where they want to you linger and enjoy your meal and really get your money's worth and I like that attitude a lot.  The folks that work here seem very attentive to wanting you to have a good experience.

Its a chain and it does VERY mediocre BBQ and its a bit expensive for what you get.  The jerk chicken is probably one of the better things on the menu while the brisket just doesn't impress me.  The corn pudding and sweet potato soufflé sides are decent for what they are.  If you're into great bbq you will probably be disappointed by this place but if all you want is fast food style dining then you will probably be satisfied.

I used to eat lunch here pretty often, when I worked in the area, and it was always a really good experience.  I really love the ambiance of this place, as it is in an old converted house, and they have given the dining rooms a really intimate feel with a fine dining look while keeping a casual atmosphere.  I've still never managed to make dinner here but the dinner menu looks very good and I've always heard good things about it.  The thing that I've eaten at lunch here the most (AND at the many festivals  Boucherie does food at)  is their 12 hour roast beef po boy, as it is one of my favorite roast beef po boys and that is saying something!  They also have a duck confit po boy that is one of my favorite duck po boys; so a restaurant that scores two po boys that are among the top of my lists is doing a whole lot of good things.  They also have a lot of other fantastic things with their Wagyu beef brisket being one that stands out as one of my preferred choices.  The main shortcoming in their menu is that I would like to see more seafood on it but they usually have a good selection of specials that often include seafood.

This is the relaunch of the former Courtyard Grill with what seems to be a bit more of a casual and more sandwich focused menu.  They have added breakfast and made the menu much smaller.  Personally I liked the old menu, name and theme of the Courtyard Grill but a lot of the food is the same but some of the more unique things are gone.  They still have some good options here you won't find at most of the other Mediterranean restaurants in the area.

The Bob Hope show is good and has some talented performers.  The price of drinks with an Abita Amber costing almost $7 is absolutely ludicrous so I can't recommend drinking here for performances.  The upstairs seating isn't the best view or seating arrangement so downstairs is far better.

This place really, actually, truly is one location of a chain so that is why it feels like a chain and it has a bit better than Applebee's quality food.  Generally, this is a very BLAH place and should be avoided unless one likes chain type food.  Granted this is a Louisiana chain so that makes it far better than the typical chain but there are so many better places to eat at that really only tourists go to this place (just look at the vast majority of non-local reviews).  It just makes me feel a bit sorry for the folks that were blown away by the mediocre food here that they missed out on some our our truly amazing food but to each their own.

So far all I've had here is the kombucha tea and it was very good except they didn't have any plain and all of them were fruit flavored.  I prefer my kombucha all plain and nasty sour the natural way.  They had some very limited hours and were just getting started when I went so it sounds like they have expanded to doing a lot more good stuff and I need to get back soon to try out some of the other great things they are doing!!!

This is a long narrow space with a bar that runs nearly the full length and then it opens up to a small rectangle in the back for pool and the bathrooms.  I used to frequent this bar much more frequently after rugby 7's practice on Scout Island in City Park in past Summers.  This is the only bar where I've had the experience of a female walking up to me and my friend in our dead sexy short rugby shorts and sticking her hands down our pants and grabbing our male parts!!!   I still make my way here every few months or so and it always has a nice crowd having good times.  They have some really cheesy and bad karaoke that is entertaining to watch just for the sheer horror of it.  The service is generally efficient and the drinks are decently priced.  Make sure to check out the wooden Indian and say hello to him for me.

So this place is hidden away and it just looks like somebody's house in the neighborhood.  When you walk up to it you might think you're sneaking into a secret mafia joint that you will need a secret password or membership card to get in.  You WILL need a very big appetite because Tony Angello's is famous for their FEED ME menus!!!  If you dare to order the main Feed Me menu (and don't eat all day if you plan to) be prepared for about 30 courses (or more) that just goes and goes and goes for what begins to seem like hours as your belly gets so full but you can't stop eating all the tasty goodness.  The only dish I've consistently heard people say they aren't that wild about is the cold beef salad (it isn't bad it's just not as good as all the other stuff and it is cold beef so ahhh yeah beef better hot).    They have a lot of other fantastic options on the menu but everybody should experience the ecstasy and pain of the Feed Me at least once in their lives!

This is the main karaoke bar of the French Quarter.  This place is ALWAYS packed with tourists and several groups of bachelorette parties.  The drink prices are a complete rip off and the vast majority of the performances are horrible but it can be entertaining here for very limited spurts.  They do have the bonus of a balcony where you can watch all of the tourist madness pass below on Bourbon Street.  So tourists inside and tourists below so you can be completely surrounded by a bunch of out of control people that act like they've never had a drink before.  The sheer joy of all this is that I've seen more fights in this bar than any other.  We're not talking about normal fights either we're talking about one group of girls getting pissed off at another group of girls and making up stories to the bouncers to get them tossed.  We're talking about one girl getting pissed off at an old married couple and drinks being thrown and hair being pulled.  So yes my friends we're talking about cat fights here... now sometimes there are real dude fights too but the cat fights are far more common.  Drama and trauma keeps the bouncers very busy in here so that alone can be entertaining to watch for awhile.

This is probably one of the top dining destinations in Meraux.  They have a really diverse selection of items on the menu going from Asian to Cajun to Creole to Italian and Mexican.  The seafood enchiladas here are some of the largest and most seafood stuffed I've ever seen and probably are better classified as burrito sized and they are also very delicious.  They offer 3 types of fish prepared in 3 different ways on the menu with  redfish, red snapper and mahi-mahi being the fish selections.  The mahi-mahi I had on my last visit was very well prepared with the "St. Catherine" option which is "Bronzed Fish Topped with Crabmeat & Roasted Peppers in Alfredo Cream Sauce Served with Seafood Rice & Saute Green Beans" which I would sum up as delicious.  The service was efficient and friendly and they kept the drinks filled.  Overall this is definitely a restaurant to check out if you find yourself in the area and have a group of people that have a wide range of different ethnic food they are in the mood for as this is definitely one of those places that seems to have something to please almost any palate.

This is probably my second favorite brewery after Wayward Owl for their beer.  The brewery itself is a bit nicer than Wayward Owl and has a nice courtyard outside.  They usually have one or more food trucks conveniently positioned for any chow needs. The visits I've made here seem to confirm this brewery as the place for parents to bring their babies to enjoy some beer as it is often just chock full of kids of all ages with plenty of newborn looking critters too.  They also host plenty of dog parents too with numerous folks having their dog babies in addition to their human babies.  This is more the way many of the regular bars USED to be before Katrina and the tyrannical Mayor Maoist Mitch started destroying our culture and the crazy Louisiana State ATF started their ridiculous garbage too which has caused a lot of harm to our NOLA culture and traditions.  Thankfully we have this brewery workaround for now until we can fight off the totalitarian forces of Marxism and Fascism to re-establish our former freedoms and go back to our live and let live culture.

I'm a bit hesitant to post this review as I don't want hordes of tourists invading this establishment and making me have to wait in lines like my other secret tasty places I've reviewed but here goes.  This is a French Quarter dive joint that slings up some delicious food.  They have among the top tier fried chickens in the entire area along with great lasagna, pastas, po boys and other tasty entrees.  They take their time and do things right so you might have to wait a bit but its definitely worth it.  The service moves at an equally leisurely pace and they don't always do the best job of recognizing customers are ready to order but once they get in gear they do a decent job typically.  They really have a nice variety of items on the menu and everything I've eaten here has made me very happy at a good price.

This place does a bit of a confusing combination of American breakfast and Thai food.  I'm not a fan of American breakfast so I'm sticking to the Thai food which is pretty good here.  The Tom Yum soup is some of the best I've had in the area and the other dishes I've had here are all very flavorful.  They have some good lunch specials but the portions are a bit on the smaller side.  They have outdoor sidewalk and patio dining that is nice when the weather cooperates.  The only negative experience I've had here was on my last lunch visit when there were very few other customers but it still took an excessively long time for my food to arrive.  Overall its a nice place to grab a casual meal but use caution if you have a tight deadline.

I've eaten at the original Memphis location of Corky's many times and I find that this chain location, like most of their locations, conveys the flavor of the original food to a good degree.  I'm not a fan of chains (and generally avoid them), but this one is at least true to the original example's menu and quality.    I typically get the beef brisket which is a decent but not outstanding example of how to bbq that cut of meat.  Corky's brisket seems more consistent with a long cooked pot roast in consistency rather than a nice flavorful bbq'd brisket but there are some definite smoke flavors that make it a bit more flavorful than a bland pot roast; just not to the degree you would expect of bbq brisket done properly.  The turkey and chicken are a bit more flavorful and are good choices.  I also like their hot tamales and I've found that they make a good sized catering dish of them that is nice to bring to parties and most people seem to love them and are very surprised to discover they came from Corky's.  Another interesting dish is their BBQ spaghetti (that I had many times in Memphis but haven't tried at one of the chain locations before).  In the limited choices we have for bbq in the NOLA area this is a relatively cheap and quick place to grab some fast food style ok but not great bbq.    I've always had outstanding service at this location and every server I've had has been extraordinarily prompt, courteous, and professional in their work.

I usually end up here after the Wednesdays on the Square.  They usually seem to have a nice crowd of nice looking ladies about the place so that is always a nice bonus.  I've also noticed a few sloppily dressed hipster type people hanging out around here sometimes and I'm not a fan of the hipster culture (so that makes my evil, preppy, Republican soul recoil a bit).  I also believe this place is smoke free which is another big bonus for me (as I always see people outside smoking and getting up to go outside so I'm assuming smoking is not allowed inside).  They have some good burgers that I've tried and those have some of the toughest (not in a bad way tough more like hearty real bread tough) and chewiest hamburger buns of anyplace I've ever been.  I'm also a bit unhappy with the fact they charge $12 for a burger and it doesn't come with any side (so fries will cost you extra).  There are some other interesting items on the small menu that I've never sampled and I'm sort of interested in the chicken & dumplings but not at the price they charge.  The bathrooms are a bit strange and a little bit of an adventure to get to so you might need to ask directions if you've never been before.    Have I mentioned I usually HATE Gastropubs but this place seems to have a good selection of beer I like and it feels comfortable (like a normal bar with people that I like to be around) so I don't hate it and actually like it but I won't be eating here on a regular basis.

This place is immediately next door to R&O's and it is a bit nicer on the inside.  This is actually a small local chain and they have two other locations on the Westbank and Northshore.  The food has a slightly different flair than what you find at many New Orleans style food places and they have some unique items.  I really prefer the food at R&O's so I only end up here when the wait is too long there but this place can certainly please the palate when needed.

I've been in this establishment a few times and they work towards producing a 1920's vibe.  There is both an upstairs and downstairs bar and even though the space seems a bit narrow a surprising number of people still fit inside.  They have a full menu and the food is decent but there are far better places to enjoy eating and spend your dining dollars so I would suggest just drinking here.

Just opened and very cool space!  In the short time this place has been around it has quickly become one of my favorite watering holes and its getting very popular. They offer a great selection of beer, cocktails, and daiquiris at fantastic prices.  All drinks here are served in mason jars to give you that down home feeling.  They have a great stage and space for live music and the sound was nice during their first live show.  They don't plan on having a kitchen and instead they will rely on food trucks to provide all the victuals.    One of the awesome things about this place is that its SMOKE FREE!  The only irksome things is they are not allowed to offer go cups and have mandated closing hours because of the STUPID Freret Street development zone "rules" and "good neighbor agreements" which are just code words for killing our NOLA culture and traditions.  Make sure to hold our politicians accountable for every instance of these infringements on our way of life and the serious retardation of economic development these "agreements" cause so complain loudly and often to them!  Best new spot on Freret yet!

So I've heard about Manchu chicken wings for decades about how they are among the top tier in the area.  Well I don't care for chicken wings so that never perked my interest but I finally went to check out the joint to sample some of their other stuff and decided on the Manchu Boneless Chicken from the rather large menu selection.  Holy Batman, Robin, Batgirl with Superman and Wonder Woman flying over them and Aquaman swimming underneath them they give you among the largest servings of food I've ever seen for around $7 (CASH only)!  They also have a gourmet selection of the finest Mad Dog 20/20 with flavors even I haven't tried before...    They give you a heaping portion of rice, an egg roll and a big huge portion of chicken that would be 3 or 4 servings for an average human appetite while for me it actually lasted for 2 meals.  They must have some serious MSG crack added into their rice as I had a really hard time stopping myself from eating the stuff and the little carrots in it somehow were just super delicious carrots (I think they were carrots at least oh wait no they are bright orange shrimp).    Overall very interesting place but gets a bit on the shady side during the night time hours so you might want to limit your visit to lunch unless you've indulged in a lot of Mad Dog 20/20 (I suggest the Kiwi vintage).

This is always a pretty consistently good bar with a decent crowd.  They have gone non-smoking in the main part of the bar but they allow smoking on the back "patio" which isn't really much of a patio as it is all enclosed.  They have a pool table crammed in between the bathrooms and the men's bathroom is among the smallest of any bar in New Orleans.  They are noted for their mixed drinks and particularly for their blueberry mojito.  I've never seen this bar get slam packed like some other establishments and it always seems you can generally find a place to sit and relax while you enjoy your drink.

I have to admit I had avoided going here for many years as I was leary of sampling Middle Eastern food in a Westbank strip mall but now I'm sad I didn't make the attempt long ago as this place was a fantastic delight even though it is in an awful strip mall location.  Great food and great service makes this a really enjoyable place to eat.  They give a different type of pita from most other Middle Eastern restaurants in the area and it is more of a puffy type.  They give really good portion sizes and the food is all well done.  You get free pita and a selection of pickled vegetables and olives lagnappe as a starter.  Prices were a good value for the portion size you get.  Overall it is one of the better places I've eaten at on the Westbank and it seems to have a dedicated following among Middle Eastern folks in the area.

This bar has some good seating and a nice cushioned bar so you can't bang your knees and hurt yourself due to any drinking accidents.  The bartender that served me was one I recognized as he used to used to work at Snake and Jake's so that was a bonus.  They have a decent number of TVs so that makes this a good spot to watch sports.  Definitely a nice retro dive bar full of New Orleans uniqueness.  I did think the beer would be cheaper due to its location and they didn't have any specials going on during my last visit but its still gotten very popular with folks in the neighborhood.

They have some of their own beers and have some beers from other places.  Their brewery made beers seem to all start at $5 and go up so these are some more expensive local beers by my standard of Abita.  The beer I had from the Courtyard Brewery had some kick too it and smelled of some strong alcohol content so I guess you at least get your money's worth of alcohol in the beer here.  The courtyard environment is alright and they often have a food truck so you can have a snack.  The real downfall of this place for me is they have very early closing times and I'm a night owl that doesn't like early closing times and this place is often closed before I'm even thinking of going out.  This place reminds me a lot of some of the Austin, TX food truck parks that have proliferated in that city.

The cheeseburger was worthy of at least three stars and I enjoyed it as it was a thick patty of juicy meat.  Everything was downhill after the burger... the fries were rather limp and not so good... the strawberry milkshake I got had ZERO flavor and was so bland I threw it away after not even consuming half of it.  I attempted to sample a slider also but they were out of those.  I might go back for the cheeseburger but everything else was pretty disappointing and would distract me from wanting to make a return visit.  The bathroom floor was also super slippery and is a lawsuit waiting to happen so they probably want to address that ASAP!!!

This is the bar at Pontchartrain Landing and it actually does have a rotating light above the bar like a lighthouse.  This is a patio bar so its all outside and there are a lot of tables and chairs along with the bar stool seating.  There is also a pool and hot tub adjacent to this space so you can enjoy those amnesties as well.  There is always an interesting mix of people in this space and its definitely a change of pace from the usual New Orleans bar scene.

This is probably one of the best bars (and maybe the best) on the Esplanade side of the French Quarter.  There is usually a majority of locals here with a sprinkling of tourists and other random people.  They have food here but I've never eaten it or really even desired it as Coops is so very close I always think why even bother with anything else.    My main complaint about this bar is the fact that they have absolutely inadequate bathroom facilities with two one hole bathrooms with one for each sex and signs proclaiming only one person at a time is allowed.  the size of this bar would easily allow for better bathroom facilities and they are FAR overdue to expand the current pathetic situation.   I've always found the service of the bartenders to be outstanding and they deal with large crowds very efficiently and seem to find a way to always provide rapid service.  I've ALWAYS had an interesting time in this bar and it is also a great venue to catch some great events that pass right in front of it like the Krewe du Vieux.

This is a small wine store that also includes a bar side where you can also hang out and enjoy drinking your purchase.  They have a really nice and affordable selection of wine even though they have a more concise inventory than many other spots upon first glance it is actually a good selection of wines that you don't usually see at other wine stores in the area.  They frequently have events and their staff is very helpful and knowledgeable in the ways of wine, beer and liquor.  It is also a bit hidden away in the American Can Company so it seems to usually be a locals place with hardly ever a tourist in sight like so many other places that have been overrun and taken over by the tourist hordes or recent hipster transplants that seek to ruin our superior NOLA ways and joie de vivre with their unpleasant hipster angst.

This is a nice little spot to sit at the bar or dine downstairs, upstairs or on the awesome balcony.  They have an oyster bar and offer a nice selection of local traditional seafood dishes, creole staples and some unique creations.  The service is generally very good and they definitely seem to put a focus on friendly customer service and outside of the classic NOLA Creole flagship establishments this is some of the best service to be had in the Quarter.  The prices are a bit on the expensive side but they do offer a 15% discount to locals.  Currently this is probably the best environment to sit at an oyster bar to eat raw and grilled oysters in the French Quarter and even though this place draws a lot of tourists you still won't be waiting in line like at Felix's or Acme as the hordes haven't taken over this location yet.

This is my favorite offering by Emeril.  I have to confess two things that add big bonus points to this place for me:   1) I've never had to pay to eat here and I've been going here for years!!!  I have been fortunate enough to have worked for organizations and attended many events here where I've had the great luck of having my food and drink paid for by others.  The fact that these organizations would choose this restaurant to do such things attests to how good it is!  I certainly would pay for the food, as it is worth it, but I get invited to regular events here so I might not ever have to :)  2) It is close to my house and very convenient.   So with those evil influences out of the way I can give my "unbiased" review.  I love the ambiance of this place and find it just seems very comfortable yet classic.  Everything I've ever had from lunch to dinner has been fantastic.  This was the first restaurant I ever even heard of "Kobe beef" (and that was many years before the term began to be tossed around commonly in restaurants and TV cooking shows) and at lunch they have a mighty fine Kobe burger.  The service has always been exceptional with only Commander's Palace rivaling it.  As I've never had to pay or make reservations I'm not sure about how difficult or how long a wait there normally is so that needs further investigating.  Why I don't finally pay to eat lunch here and go more often I sometimes wonder other than I'm usually not Uptown for lunch much these days but I certainly might give in and pay for dinner soon.    Definitely a great place to sample for both lunch and dinner!!!

I finally broke away from my regular Westbank Vietnamese spots and sampled a chicken pho here for lunch.  The chicken quality wasn't as good as most other spots but the broth was fantastic.  They also serve my preferred jasmine tea which makes me happy.    Now there were some things that made me unhappy.  First they didn't bring a lemon or lime with my tea (but they brought me one when I asked).  Second when I began to pour my hot sauce in my soup the freaking lid plopped off right into the bowl.  Third I received no follow up service and had to find somebody to refill my drink.  The menu here is a bit different from most of the other places in the area and their menu featured many dishes made with goat.  They also had a selection of udon noodle soups that peaked my interest.  They definitely have many things I would like to return and sample but the lack of service grates me a bit still.  The price was a good value and overall I enjoyed my experience (other than the issues listed above).

I thought to myself, "Oh wow look at what an innovative idea with yet another generic Mexican joint to add to the already over-saturated Mexican restaurant scene of the Greater New Orleans area?"  Well then I finally got dragged here kicking and screaming all the way but at least it wasn't a total loss as this joint at least had descent tasting food and decent prices which puts it ahead of more than half of their competition these days.  Overall it was a good value with their lunch specials and they offered a decent sized mixed fajitas plate at a decent price.

This is a basic bar in the Riverbend that offers a consistent experience.  It never seems deserted but never seems crowded either.  It has a very long bar and several tables and chairs so there never seems to be a lack of seating.  They have decent drink prices and usually good service.  They also have pool and a few other distractions to entertain you.  The main downside is that this place can get really smokey at times.

Its the home of Jazz Fest, horse racing, a casino and lots of fun times.  They have a grandstand with a clubhouse that often books bands along with multilevels of numerous little food booths, bars, and all manner of nooks and crannies to explore.  This is also the epicenter of the popular NOLA Thanksgiving day tradition to eat, drink, and bet on the ponys.  Some of the most fun times to be had here, other than Jazz Fest, are during the Starlight racing series.

I really really really wanted to eat some great Greek lunch options here which if I did I'm sure this place would have been four or five stars to me.  Sadly I went in the morning and they were only doing the breakfast menu.  I'm not the biggest fan of breakfast food and I like regular food all the time so I was really sad I could not get my awesome looking Greek food on my last in Nashville for my last meal in town as I was heading out.  I will certainly be returning to sample the awesome looking Greek food here on my next visit!

Emeril's very "pig fat love" based cooking is not my favorite and I avoid pig fat whenever possible but he still has some magic he can do.  I've done the tasting menu here and it was one of the largest and "BAMED" up experiences I've ever done with a tasting menu (just the freaking dessert was a huge TRAY of more things than 10 people could eat!!!).    This isn't one of my top places in New Orleans and I don't frequent it (not from any bad experiences or dislike of it just that I've got other places I prefer) but I certainly think the tasting menu (or degustation menu as they call it) is certainly worth putting on your list to do at some point.  The food is generally very good and well prepared but the crowd seems to be more tourists than locals, which is fine, it just isn't where I usually go to enjoy myself.    I would recommend that you go ahead right now and book the tasting menu if you haven't done it yet; after starving yourself all day as it will be an enjoyable and very filling experience :)

This place has been popular for a long time and the patrons are mostly much older folks that have been eating here forever.  The menu has some good selections and some not so good executions of some of the dishes; as I have found that most of the things I've ordered here are rather bland which they have probably adjusted to meet the needs of the older crowed that typically dines here.  This can be a very pleasant place to see some of the manners of a bygone time but I would like them to add some flavor and spice back to the food.

They have free parking and late hours which are great bonuses.  The food seems reasonably fresh but often in some less than optimal combinations.  Speaking of combinations pretty much everything here seems to mainly be either a salad or a sandwich.  I was taking a carb break so I was off the bread so that really just left me with a salad option which really I just wanted a big plate of meat but I got the chicken salad instead which didn't really float my boat.  This is so far the least liked food I've ever eaten in Nashville.  Maybe they can do better?

A dirty ole dive bar in a dirty ole neighborhood that is quickly gentrifying.  There are often some dirty ole gutter punks in here that stink to high heaven.  The drink prices are affordable NOLA style and NOT New York City style like lots of other pretentious new upstarts.  Most of the patrons are usually friendly other than the typically boring gutter punks that have their usual ridiculous abrasiveness.

So for the VIP level tickets you got a decent selection of food and drinks generally but the logistics of this event are run pretty poorly.  They opened the Will Call for the tickets early in the afternoon of New Years day so I went right at opening to stand in line to pick up my two tickets/armbands and when I finally got to the end of the line they wouldn't give me the tickets as everybody getting an armband has to be present... Ok so never have I ever had that experience in New Orleans EVER EVER for any of gazillions of events like this I've attended but I guess "public safety" or something similarly nefarious was afoot and I expected to find some version of Robespierre lurking about.  Well later when I had my complete party assembled and descended back upon this event at the exact time of the opening there was zero line and it was easy to grab the armbands and proceed immediately to the milkings/drinkings/eatings so I guess to moral of the story is early planning gets you exactly negative results here so just show up exactly on time for better results.    So on finally entering the event it is a bit of a long series of rides up and down escalators and curving around to finally arrive at the event space.  There were already lines forming at the food and drinks so obviously I went and stood in line for a drink first and VERY oddly when I finally got to put my order in they ONLY had ONE kind of beer which was one of the big major commercial boys light beers and they told me that the non-VIP drink table probably had more beer so I bounced over there and true enough they had a large selection of appropriate beers to choose from.  This all seemed rather odd but I later learned there were more VIP bars to select from and all the others were far better equipped with beer.  The food in the VIP area was turkey and a nice steamship of beef for the main carnivore events I was interested in and then they had some other side dishes, desserts and pasta.  The non-VIP food was some sad looking jambalaya, fried cheese balls and fried boudin balls that I wouldn't recommend to most folks.  The VIP food would rate a solid three stars while the non-VIP food would rate a one star on my scale.  The first VIP food area I found myself in had no seating left so it was standing room to eat only.  Later I also discovered that there were other rooms with VIP seating and food which were wide open with no lines and plenty of space to sit.    The entertainment options were also like the food and bars spread out among multiple rooms.  There was a burlesque event, bands and a performance by the 610 Stompers.  All of these events seemed to really happen fast and transition from one performance to the next quickly.  the space available to really get up near to see the performances was also a bit limited and got crowded fast.    Overall I think this experience could have been really improved with better logistics.  A map with a schedule of the events would have been quite useful for this event so you could know of all the various locations and times of the various performances along with the various eating areas and bar locations.  Ensuring all the bars were properly stocked also would have been a really great idea.  Proper project management should have been implemented to fully utilize all the energy that went into the event planning and execution of this event and that clearly seems to have been lacking from my experience.  This event could be fun and while it seems to be mostly tourists you do get a decent selection of a variety of entertainment options along with plenty of food and drink for your New Years experience here.

I had a friend from out of town that booked this Inn for his family and I had the opportunity to stop in and check it out.  The location is nice and it is easy to access the French Quarter and Frenchmen Street while being far enough away from the ruckus on Bourbon Street.  The downstairs common areas were decently appointed with a good amount of character.  The hotel room I saw looked reasonably comfortable while a bit smaller than what I have typically seen at other local spots.  My friend informed me of the price he had gotten the room for and it was more than reasonable for the time of year along with being such a good location for what his family wanted to do.

This spot has some great Greek lunch specials along with a really impressive menu of all sorts of other items which include plenty of non-Greek items like burgers.  Some nice choices are the appetizer sampler platter, captain's platter, mixed grill and combo plates so you can get a nice selection of multiple items and I really enjoyed the Greek Combo lunch special.  With so many great options you could certainly eat lunch and dinner here multiple times for a few weeks without repeating anything.  They also put on a big breakfast menu and while I'm not the biggest fan of breakfast food I have to tip my hat to what an impressively large menu they offer for their breakfast.  I do prefer regular food all the time so I'm  really sad I can't get my awesome regular Greek food during breakfast time so I wish they would be a bit more flexible on their "rules" of what you can order at what times.  The only real food criticism I have of the place is the baklava has a bit of thick dough and is more on the tougher side than any other baklava I've tried before.  The online menus available for Athen's Family Restaurant don't do justice to the real menu selection they offer in the restaurant so the owners might want to update those as they are selling themselves short with all the great choices they offer.  Overall I've certainly had better Greek food in my travels but this is the best Greek I've had in Tennessee.

Lots of parking at this joint and in an oddly shaped location that I wouldn't have guessed was a coffee shop if I hadn't noticed their sign.  There is a drive through but I usually don't like to mess with those so I headed inside.  I was in desperate need of some coffee when I found this spot and I certainly got a decent cup of coffee very fast that helped me power though the remainder of a VERY loooong day.  They have quite a bit of comfortable space in here so seating doesn't look like it would ever be a problem.

They have some good food and fantastic hot sauces here.  The lunch buffet usually ranges from alright to great and they often have a good selection of items but on average I think if you order off the menu you will have a better experience here.  The service can be painfully slow sometimes so if you aren't getting the lunch buffet this isn't a reliably fast place to eat if you're in any kind of hurry but they are getting faster.    Boswell's has also become a long time Jazz Fest (and other fests) favorite as they give you a much needed boost of some good veggies and they are usually next to the strawberry lemonade booth as a bonus.  They don't have fresh brewed unsweet iced tea at the restaurant and only have sweet tea which is a big pet peeve of mine so that irks my scotch bonnet to the core.

Antoine's Bakery opened back in 2015 and since then they have been baking among the best Greater New Orleans cakes and special desserts to be found in the area. If you like delicious cakes, nice pastries, and other special desserts for the holidays, special occasions or just any regular day then Antoine's bakery has the desserts which should interest you.  Antoine's Bakery has a nice variety of delicious cakes with their Chantilly Cake, Queen Cake and King Cake along with plenty of other great desserts for Mardi Gras Carnival season or any other occasion. Antoine's Bakery literally invented the Queen Cake which is a super upgraded King Cake stuffed full of up to five different fillings.  They also do custom made cakes and have a great selection of all manner of other delicious dessert items.  You definitely should take the time to pay a visit to enjoy the beautiful looking desserts before you make the really hard choice of what to order!  Overall this is a really great spot for some really delicious sweet treats!  My video review of Antoine's Bakery is here:  https://youtu.be/RcanCe6vBvA

This is a really beautiful building and has many layers of architecture and design to appreciate inside.  I have only been here for Carnival balls and I always have enjoyed myself in this venue.  The downstairs bar and the smaller bars on the sides of the upper levels are nicely designed.  The seating arrangement in the theater makes it easy to see the stage quite well from all of the seats for the most part.  Overall this is a nice venue for balls but I can't speak to it otherwise from my experience.

I pay for electricity and gas so Entergy usually provides it except sometimes when they don't and then I miss those things so I'm glad I have them even if I'm a caveman at heart as I like A/C and TV.  I'm not that fond of all the prices as I don't use that much but it still seems to end up costing a lot whether I've even turned anything on or not in my house.  I've definitely used a lot more electricity and paid a lot less for it in other places but I'm thankful I can buy the gas and electricity to keep my things running.  Give me some solar or other option to generate all my own power and I would love that option but then I would still need to buy gas from Entergy...

This is a popular tourist trap spot but it does offer some decent food in an authentic French Quarter environment.  The seafood gumbo is about average for the French Quarter so it isn't the greatest in the city but I've had worse.  The gumbo z'herbes is actually quite good and it is very uncommon to find anywhere in NOLA that serves this dish on a regular basis outside of Gumbo Shop.  The roast beef po boy is on the bottom tier in the area and doesn't compete well with many better options so I would go with other options.  The seafood is probably a better idea to stick with for most items on the menu and they do have some nice options and unique items not found in other spots.  The Shrimp Creole is alright but the shrimp are the same size as the gumbo shrimp so a bit below average size for Shrimp Creole.  The biggest issue with this place is before the pandemic they had crammed far too many tables into the space so that the waiters literally had to squeeze through between tables and chairs to do their job and that often made the place uncomfortably crowded.  There was a constant line for the bathrooms during popular times in this space and while on my last visit on a Monday after Easter that wasn't the case but there was a line to get into the restaurant.  The bar setup is also a bit strange with it just being a cube against the back wall with no bar seating so if you are a solo eater this spot unfortunately offers no bar seating so they might want to think of a redesign of that feature in the future.  Overall this is a high tourist population joint that tourists will likely enjoy that will have a smaller sampling of locals thrown in the mix and it is worthy of sampling the gumbo z'herbes, the combo sampler plate and seafood options.  My video review of Gumbo Shop is here:  https://youtu.be/B05rDwhtYdk

Classic New Orleans place of the type that seems to be harder and harder to find.  Extremely simple decor as this place is all about the food.  The menu is very comprehensive with something for almost everyone including seafood, poboys, crawfish pie and Italian food (with good pizza).    Maybe because the food is so good and I love to eat so much of it my bill is usually much more at R & O's for lunch than other casual dining places and I spend nearly as much as I would for lunch at Commander's Palace but I'm much more full (and far more sober without the 25 cent martinis!!!).   The Italian Roast Beef Poboy is one of my favorites of all time!!!  The gumbo is extremely tasty with some of the best flavors of any I've experienced and if you're nice to the waitress she will drown you in gumbo crabs and keep asking if you want more.  You also really need to sample the hot tamales (actually sample everything).  They have daily lunch specials and so many good things that you can go for a LONG time and keep eating new things.  They also have great salads and cold beers so a great place to eat lunch by yourself or go out with a big group and enjoy (also extremely kid friendly).

This place is an alright bar with mostly decent bar food but nothing that is going to knock your socks off.  The most crowded I usually see this place (other than Saints games) is during lunch when people are going to eat.  This place seems to be a popular spot for lesbians to meet so while it isn't totally a gay bar I think it might be the closest thing to one for ladies of that persuasion in Mid-City.  I rarely make an appearance in this venue as it never seems to have very much going on other than during Saints games.  I've never really had very much fun here and it doesn't seem to be the optimal place for a single man to meet single women.  This might actually be my least favorite bar in Mid-City as I've just always seemed to have kind of blah boring experiences here.

Video link review here:  https://youtu.be/LQGzQgISN4Y

This is the same family that ran La Thai on Prytania Street for many years.  My favorite thing is the hot & sour soup and it always puts me in a good mood to eat that awesome stuff.  They have some very tasty options on the menu and some unique "cajun Thai" fusion dishes that work well.  The owners and staff have always been very helpful and want you to enjoy your food.

The Ugly Dog is definitely a better bar than a BBQ and it usually seems to have a decent happy hour crowd.  There is always an interesting mix of people in here and they have a nice small patio in the front.  The inside of this building is basically a giant open rectangle with lots of tables and a large bar.  They serve "alright" BBQ and they do decent steaks here.  The brisket here is definitely not the usual slow smoked BBQ and it seems more consistent with something done in an oven as there is no indication or even a hint of a smoke ring.  The brisket is usually moist and has some decent flavor but definitely needs some sauce on it.  I would probably opt for the steak over the BBQ options.

Parkway has been and is one of the top places for a fantastic po boy in the NOLA area.  The location is a classic New Orleans awesome dive joint next to Bayou St. John.  I usually prefer sitting at the bar and enjoying my meal, with a beer or iced tea, but they have also recently added a nice patio outside.  I don't have a single favorite thing here (as everything is great) and I usually rotate BUT one thing I really like (that most other places don't have) is the Surf & Turf that has roast beef topped with fried shrimp and roast beef gravy.  They also have a pretty respectable LOOKING burger but do yourself a favor and stick to the po boys as the burger isn't anything special.  Big Minus: No Oyster Po Boy!!!  No Oyster ANYTHING since BP!!!  This place has been getting more and more crazy crowded of late as the word has escaped to the masses so sometimes there can be a wait.  Even when it is crazy crowded (like during Bayou Boogaloo) I've always had EXCELLENT service and the food has never disappointed.  So I would totally recommend this place except I don't want anymore tourists overcrowding my space when I'm ready to eat so don't believe anything I say and just stay in the Quarter :)

Yet another mysterious disappearing review Yelp has unleashed on me so where did my old review go...???  This is a dive bar and grill type joint in Mid-City that can get pretty rowdy during athletic events. Thursday is $5 pizza night and that is a popular time in here as well.  I have only sampled the pizza here and honestly it isn't my favorite pizza but it is edible so for $5 it is also a good deal.  The service has always been relatively decent here and they get your drinks to you fast enough.  There always seems to be a decent crowd in here and they serve food later than most other joints in the area.  If you are in Mid-City this is a decent spot to check out.

I've been here a few times but I rarely get here.  The rare times I get here are when I decide to take out of town friends on an adventure on the Algier's Ferry.  This bar along with the Dry Dock Cafe & Bar, and Crown and Anchor are the usual stops I will make on my ferry excursions to Algiers.  This always seems like a pretty laid back bar and it is about the only place to catch live music on a regular basis in this area.

Five Happiness was absolutely the best Chinese food in the NOLA area before Katrina.  I used to love how all the waiters had the exact same haircut and you got outstanding service.  After Katrina the service has never really recovered and the food is similar but just doesn't seem to hit the high marks that it used to.  It actually depresses me to eat here these days as I remember how fantastic it used to be.

Simply the best snowball ever!!!  Once you have a Hansen's you just don't want any other snowball as the Hansen's ice is the best thing ever!!! They make all their own flavors and focus on quality.  I usually get one of the delicious tart flavors or coconut and actually there are a few of the regular flavors I'm actually not very fond of.  If you want a completely different experience get one of their cream flavors and then the snowball takes on the characteristic of an ice cream cone that banged a snowball which then gave birth to the cream flavor snowball!  The regular strawberry flavor here really doesn't taste good to me while the cream strawberry is awesome and has real chunks of strawberry in it so definitely make a point of trying a cream flavored option at some point!  The only bad thing is the sometimes very long line in the very hot heat as they don't have air conditioning here.

Bearcat Café is a newer restaurant to New Orleans opening back in 2017 and in 2019 they opened a second location with a bar downtown.  This is my first successful visit to Bearcat Café as I have made many failed past attempts as this is a very popular spot which has always had a line of people waiting to get in every time I've tried to visit in the past.  The Uptown location of Bearcat Cafe serves breakfast and lunch all day but has no dinner service (their downtown location has a full bar and does serve dinner according to their website).  I decided to start my first visit with something simple and basic so I ordered the bison burger which was a juicy delicious burger with a bit of soggy bun soaked in grease.  The burger was served with a nice side of roasted potatoes that I enjoyed far more than standard french fries as they had a lot of good flavor.  The service was friendly and attentive and I enjoyed my meal and I look forward to returning to sample some of the more interesting things on the menu.  My video review is here:  https://youtu.be/68_CIlh-wi4

So another new bar but with old school video games?  Why yes thank you I will play these games and what a nice selection.  What a new bar that isn't a pretentious gastropub or craft cocktail emporium that actually has a good selection of beer?  Well yes praise baby Jesus bring on some of those cold tasty suds!  What more could I possibly desire? Maybe a patio could be nice for when the weather is nice and what a surprise by some miracle they have not one patio but TWO.  Well then we just might get along after all Barcadia if you just wouldn't charge $4.50 for Abita Amber as I find $4 is more than a fair price for a LOCAL beer.  I also was disappointed that some of the video games stole my quarters and didn't work.  This place is also all new and shiny like something that should be in Austin or somewhere in California with people that look like they are from those places so if you're looking for NOLA ambiance this isn't the place.

Dunbar's has long been famous for their Creole food, fried chicken and daily specials.  There new location has been decorated with lots of bright colors and they do have off street parking.  They have a great selection of items on their menu and there should be something on there to please most tastes.  Dunbar's fried chicken is always among the top options in the New Orleans area when discussing the best fried chicken in the area.  They have also added some enormous burger options and their entrees are really great.  The service here is friendly and they keep your drink refilled along with being very good about explaining daily specials on offer.    Overall this is great place that needs to be on your must visit list to experience the great food joints of New Orleans.  My video review of Dunbar's Creole Cuisine is here:  https://youtu.be/kOf-JmHhD_w

I've been so many times over so many years I can't even count them and ALL my experiences have been outstanding.  Commander's ranks as among the best overall dining venues ever with among the best service by the staff anywhere, anyplace, anytime that I've experienced.  I've heard stories of people that had bad service but I've never seen such a thing.    I prefer lunch to dinner as they have the great 25 cent martini special that will quickly get you in trouble as they have some kick.  Commander's is also noted for a really nice Jazz Brunch.  I should also confess that I'm an extra big fan of Commander's as I can throw a rock from my house and hit it so that makes it very convenient.  They always have some amazing specials made with locally sourced fresh ingredients.    If I had a complaint about the food it would have been a few times when I didn't love an entree and thought it was just ok but that has happened very few times considering (and not every dish is to everyone's taste).  I have also noticed a bit of a lack of change on the menu the last few times I've dined at Commander's and the dishes all seemed pretty familiar, which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but generally I've come to expect a bit more rotation in what is offered from visit to visit.  There are few CIVILIZED dining establishments left these days where one is expected to dress properly and Commander's is one of those places!  I'm so very glad that Commander's has not given into the sloppy tourist's & newly arrived yankee "locals" demands that they be allowed to wear the nasty casual fashion trends of the moment (with their smelly hipster flip flops) so if you plan on dining here do remember to dress up!!!  Ladies I shouldn't have to tell you but obviously it needs to be said:  Please remember that blue jeans, no matter how much they cost, are NOT business casual for lunch and should NEVER be seen at night!!!  Dress to impress and live like a civilized local (and by civilized I mean dress up and look extraordinary as you drink and eat to excess!!!).   I also want to give extra KUDOS to wait captain Mary's section as she really makes sure that you have an outstanding time with impeccable service!!!

The Blue Crab still seems to still be building some finishing touches on the outside but the inside is already up to full steam.  I arrived for a late lunch on a Friday and the place was packed.  The main dining room is very loud and for a bit of a quieter experience the bar or small patio, which has a great view of the water, are better choices.  The lunch menu here has a much better selection with better values than its nearby neighbor and the other new kid on the block Brisbi's.  The service was friendly and my order came out quite fast.  I had the amberjack and a cup of gumbo which were all done well other than needing a bit more seasoning.  I think this place will do very well and its a nice addition to the area that brings back a bit of the old school places that used to be at West End.  Tip: The whole stuffed flounder (broiled or fried) is amazingly huge and awesome!

This is a New Orleans classic and a must visit!!!  This place has some good gelato (and they have been doing gelato since way before "gelato" become cool) and tasty Italian "ices" that are great during the hot times of the year.  They have great Italian cookies, cannolis, pies, and all sorts of other tasty desserts.  They probably have my favorite espresso of anyplace in New Orleans and quite possibly the entire United States.  The best time to visit is during Christmas when they go INSANE with so many great treats!!!  It can get crowded at night so make sure to plan accordingly and it is ALWAYS a good time to pay a tasty visit to Brocato's :)

McHardy's often makes the list of the top fried chicken in the NOLA fried chicken wars.  The fried chicken here is good fried chicken in the larger scheme of the world but personally I find their chicken to definitely be on the more bland side as far as spice heat for my taste except for a big rush of pure saltiness.  In the smaller world of New Orleans there is definitely better fried chicken to my taste but this chicken is definitely still good so give it a try and maybe your taste being different than mine might find it better than the others.

This is a popular tourist trap spot but it does offer some decent food in an authentic French Quarter environment.  The seafood gumbo isn't the greatest in the city but I've had worse.  The gumbo z'herbes is actually quite good and it is very uncommon to find anywhere in NOLA that serves this dish on a regular basis outside of Gumbo Shop.  The roast beef po boy is on the bottom tier in the area and doesn't compete well with many better options so I would go with other options.  The seafood is probably a better idea to stick with for most items on the menu and they do have some nice options and unique items not found in other spots.  The biggest issue with this place is they have crammed far too many tables into the space so that the waiters literally have to squeeze through between tables and chairs to do their job and that often makes the place uncomfortably crowded.  There also seems to be a constant line for the bathrooms during popular times in this space so plan ahead if your Sunday brunch cocktails might invoke the call of nature.  The bar setup is also a bit strange with it just being a cube against the back wall with no bar seating so if you are a solo eater this spot unfortunately offers no bar seating so they might want to think of a redesign of that feature in the future.  Overall it is a high tourist population joint that tourists will likely enjoy that will have a smaller sampling of locals thrown in the mix and it is worthy of sampling the gumbo z'herbes and seafood options.

This is quite a collection of all sorts of items and all manner of categories.   The prices were not in the bargain basement range for the most part with some descent deals to be found.  There were quite a number of interesting things to look at and they have a respectable assortment of tiny collectible knickknacks scattered around.  If you are out on River Road this could be a good stop before heading over to Rivershack Tavern.

I had a review for this joint when they were still at their previous location that got destroyed so not sure how Yelp seems to keep "losing" so many of my reviews (and I hear from many other Yelpers this happens all too frequently).  This is a long time Thai joint that has been a staple of the CBD lunch scene for many years.  Their current location is nicer than the one that got destroyed.  They do have some decent lunch specials and while the food is generally OK it isn't quite as flavorful and spicy as many of the other Thai options in the NOLA area.  It is still the best Thai in the CBD as it is the only Thai in the CBD but it used to be a lot better when they were at the old location.

Parkway has been and is one of the top places for a fantastic po boy in the NOLA area.  The location is a classic New Orleans awesome dive joint next to Bayou St. John.  I usually prefer sitting at the bar (or at least I used to before COVID-19) and enjoying my meal, with a beer or iced tea, but they have also have a nice patio outside.  I don't have a single favorite thing here (as everything is great) and I usually rotate BUT one thing I really like (that most other places don't have) is the Surf & Turf that has roast beef topped with fried shrimp and roast beef gravy.  They also have a pretty respectable LOOKING burger but do yourself a favor and stick to the po boys as the burger isn't anything special.  Big Minus: Oyster Po Boy is ONLY available on Monday & Wednesday!!!    This place during normal pre-COVID-19 times was getting more and more crazy crowded as the word has escaped to the masses so sometimes there could be a wait.  During the pandemic there are not many tourists around these days so I haven't had to wait very long at all the line is only a few folks.  There is also no more condiment station so you need to order everything you want on your poboy.    My video review of Parkway Bakery & Tavern is here:  https://youtu.be/YsJZexicSqI

This is a great dive bar with a huge neon sign at the end of Canal Street.  They have a good burger and also do a decent tuna steak sandwich.  The burger seems to try to emulate Port of Call a bit much, with the unmelted cold shredded cheese, but it is probably a better burger than that declined tourist trap that is now Port of Call.  The burger is certainly  a nice large burger and probably one of the bigger one's available in the area.  The best thing about the food and drink at Beach Corner is that it is a GREAT value.  The burgers are around $5 and the tuna steak is like $8!!!  There are lots of other things on the menu that I've never tried (as I always seem to end up getting the burger or tuna) that also might be good.  I've never just hung out here so I'm not sure if it is a fun place as a bar as I've only stopped in to eat and have a few beers.

Best crazy late night scene in the Uptown area!!!  People of all ages end up at F&M's for fun into the wee hours of the morning.  Always a good time with tasty cheese fries and pool table dancing.  Sometimes it gets crazy crowded but some of the best bartenders in the city keep things moving smoothly.  Occasionally some out of town idiots try to cause trouble and start fights as they have stayed up way past their bed times and don't know how to behave themselves on New Orleans time but usually just a lot of people having a really good time dancing to mostly great music with the occasional crappy rap song thrown in.  The men's bathrooms can get filthy beyond all legends and who knows what foul things might drip on you sometimes but despite all these minor issues it is always a fun time to dance the night away til dawn at F&M's!!!    It is worth a visit for the cheese fries alone!

The ambiance here is just old, dirty, complete DIVE with all sorts of great stuff on the walls from many years ago and the totality of the place makes the atmosphere a complete 5!  Unfortunately the po boys here are not the best in the city but some of the po boys are certainly tasty.  I do like the fact they put several kinds of mustard on some of the sandwiches (as I'm a bit of a mustard freak!).  The portion size here is smaller than you get at most other places so I find it takes at least two po boys to fill me up here.  They also only take cash which makes it very inconvenient.  It is certainly worthy of a visit just to experience the place but it isn't on my regular rotation.

I had high hopes for a worthy competitor to the Joint having possibly arrived.  I was happy with the larger selection of items on the menu and especially pleased to see beef ribs.  The BAD:    Service was not up to even keeping my iced tea refilled and I was sitting at the bar at around 4:30 pm with few other customers around which makes that situation even worse.  (on my next visit the service was much improved when we were sitting outside at a picnic table and the manager even came by twice to check on us so looks like they are addressing that service issue fast).  Quantity on the brisket plate was less meat than the Joint.  No toast or pickles came with my brisket plate.  Mac n Cheese isn't an official side dish so you have to order it separately for like $6!  MAD INSANITY ya gotta include smaller serving sizes of the various mac n cheese options as a side!!!  Crazy pricing scheme on their menu for biscuits as I thought I was getting 5 for $2 but actually they are $5 for 2 biscuits which is crazy overpriced for plain biscuits that most places give out free with meals.  The biscuits were also so dry and crumbly I couldn't really spread the butter on them without them just falling apart.  Texas Toast and corn bread are each counted as a side so you can buy one slice of their house-made Texas Toast for $3 or also get some corn bread for $3... That price is like at least one whole loaf of bread or a whole pan of corn bread and this might be the worst value on the entire menu.  Their brisket chili comes with beans in it... Texans don't put beans in their chili and then even though this place isn't Texas they still shouldn't put beans in a chili that is going on my hamburger as I don't want beans on my burger as that reeks of Vegan too much for me.  Price was a poor value as with tip I rang up a $29.50 bill so that is approaching Commander's Palace 3 course lunch price that also gets me 25 cent martinis!!!  This is also double the price of the Joint for less meat (Joint includes toast and pickles so I wouldn't have needed to also order the rip off $5 crumbly biscuits to satisfy my appetite too).  The GOOD:  The bar area is a pretty nice setup and could be a good space for watching games.  Heinekens and several other beers are just $3 and then they also have the expensive super hipster beers too along with quite a selection of cocktails.   The brisket was decent and is probably about in third place to my taste preference in the NOLA area currently.  They have 3 BBQ sauces (and one additional white sauce for those weirdo Alabama folks that put that crazy white sauce on their meat).  Beef ribs!!!  This looks to be the only place that will be able to constantly serve beef ribs in the area (Black Label is the only other option but they have never had it every time I tried to order it so I have given up on them).  Burgers are decent here and they are a filling size served with a side of fries.   Overall I hope they get this new bbq spot up and going full speed ahead and get all the kinks out to make it a viable competitor to the Joint in quality, quantity and value.  I would also suggest they take a hint from some of the awesome BBQ joints of Austin, TX and set up a condiment bar space with pickles, sliced onions and hot peppers along with serving the plates with toast/bread and they might need to outsource their house-made Texas Toast to one of our great local bakeries if they can't price it better than $3 a slice.

The ambiance of the building is fantastic and has the potential to be among the top tier of most amazing places to eat and drink in NOLA.  Sadly the service and food don't live up to the price.  The gumbo was far too small a serving coupled with blandness to justify the cost while the burger just didn't do much for me and left me wishing I would've gone to La Petite Grocery.  There was also no Tabasco or other Louisiana hot sauce to be had so Sriracha was the only option.  While I'm generally not very enthusiastic about hipsters I will at least give them a chance (which I should probably stop doing as they excel so much at meeting every tired stereotype about their species) and I was able to get exactly ONE iced tea refill from my manbun sporting hipster server. If you find yourself in the mood for bearded hipsters with armsleeve tats and manbuns served with lots of angst with customers that also largely meet that same unfortunate niche then this hipster hell den might meet your needs.  They do have a small choice of affordable beer starting out at $3 along with quite a craft cocktail program going for those of you that need that too.  There was also talk of adding a brunch at some point soon so maybe that will offer some improvement.
