Overall I'm just not hipster cool enough for this place currently and I'm thankful for that while I can hope, wish and pray that this place might get the service and food up to New Orleans standards my expectations are low at this point and it just doesn't deserve any more of my hard earned money as there are just way too many better places to eat at their price point but maybe many of you can enjoy a drink and snack here.
Ok so FINALLY they have oysters back on the menu BUT only on Mondays!!!  Geez Louise BP is long over and there are good supplies of oysters now so c'mon do them all the time please!

The ambiance here used to be just old, dirty and a complete DIVE with all sorts of great stuff on the walls from many years ago and the totality of the place makes the atmosphere a complete 5!  Unfortunately they have gentrified and cleaned the joint up a lot from the way I used to LOVE it.  The  po boys here are not the best in the city but some of the po boys are certainly tasty.  I do like the fact they put several kinds of mustard on some of the sandwiches (as I'm a bit of a mustard freak!).  The portion size here is smaller than you get at most other places so I find it takes at least two po boys to fill me up here.  They used to only take cash but now they take credit cards and they also have a whole LOT more tourists here than there used to be.    Overall it is certainly worthy of a visit just to experience the place but it isn't on my regular rotation and without Miss Dot around it definitely isn't the same anymore so make sure to visit before it changes any more.  My video review of Domilise Po-Boys & Bar is here: https://youtu.be/Y_mPKggh9Lo

This really is a great candy and ice cream store!  This location is the newest of Laura's Candies which has been in business since 1913 and they have two other locations in the French Quarter.  This new location in Metairie is now their production facility and has also added an ice cream parlor.  They really have a fantastic selection and do a lot of great seasonal/holiday items along with a lot of great New Orleans and Louisiana themed scrumptious candy treats.  Their chocolate truffles are the absolute most AMAZING I have ever had anywhere with intense bold flavors that really stand out from any other chocolates I've ever tried anywhere else in the world.  They have some really great Louisiana and New Orleans themed gifts that should make most folks pretty happy not to mention they are also delicious but some are so pretty you almost feel bad about eating them.  Overall you are wasting time if you haven't visited here yet so hurry up and start enjoying life more through the AMAZING chocolate and other treats here!!!  My video review of this location of Laura's Candies is here:  https://youtu.be/QJz8Lgvin6o

Five Happiness was absolutely the best Chinese food in the NOLA area before Katrina.  I used to love how all the waiters had the exact same haircut and you got outstanding service.  After Katrina the service has never really recovered and the food is similar but just doesn't seem to hit the high marks that it used to.  It actually depresses me a bit to eat here these days as I remember how fantastic it used to be.  They have improved from the very low point they had fallen too after Katrina but it still isn't up to where it was. The dinner prices are definitely way up there these days which makes Five Happiness a much better choice for their lunch specials than dinner these days.  My video review of Five Happiness is here: https://youtu.be/-t-lcANcd6E

Frankie & Johnny's opened up back in 1942 and has remained a popular spot in the neighborhood for great seafood ever since. In addition to staying popular with all the locals in the area Frankie & Johnny's has grown in popularity among tourists who have come to love their New Orleans Creole food which can make it get a bit crowded in here sometimes. If you find yourself craving some great New Orleans seafood then Frankie & Johnny's can help satisfy your desires for some fantastic seafood.  They have some amazing fried seafood, delicious gumbo and a great bar.  The big downside is the prices have really gone up over the years so it is definitely on the higher side of the price scale these days for a neighborhood joint.  Overall this is a great spot for some good food in an old school neighborhood joint but just be prepared for a bit of a sticker shock depending on what you order.  My video review of Frankie & Johnny's is here: https://youtu.be/bwMMjPhVfYk

This is a really fun bar with 3 stories and a rooftop with each level having their own bar and live music so you get a different vibe in each area and can easily rotate between the spaces.  The rooftop is really great just to look around and see all the folks outside and all around at the other spots on Broadway.  I really enjoyed everything about Tootsie's Orchid Lounge other than the price of drinks which definitely has some tourist soaking built in.  There is no cover and with so many bands they do have to make some extra money to pay for the music but whoa there maybe they could cut some deals like buckets of beer or something to soften the blow as the prices definitely slowed up my intake and encouraged me to nurse my beer a much longer time than normal.

This is the second location for Hard Rock Cafe in New Orleans.  I had a lot of fun times at the original location along with a LOT of nostalgia for the space so I was a bit sad to see them relocate to their current location on Bourbon Street.  This location is better placed to draw more tourists and they have brought over a lot of the old memorabilia from the original location.  Hard Rock Cafe always has some good food and their burgers are always very nicely done.  This is a great spot to check out for some good food along with some rock & roll history.  They have the usual great gift shop with lots of items for the Hard Rock Cafe collectors.  Overall this is a great spot for fun times with American food in the New Orleans French Quarter if you are not in the mood for any of the local Creole cuisine.  Hard Rock Cafe also offers military veterans a discount all the time along with a free burger on Veterans Day which is a really great show of support for our veterans!  My video review of Hard Rock Cafe New Orleans is here:  https://youtu.be/uHt5J5EEkKQ

This is a deli type joint with quite a few options.  They have counter orders for coffee and sandwiches and then a food case with carry out entrees.  They also have a selection of adult beverages along with a nice selection of other food focused items.  For a finale they have pastries and other desserts to finish off your meal.

Brown Derby is rightfully well noted for their carry out buffet that offers a lot of great choices everyday which they serve in huge portions at a value price.  There really isn't anywhere to sit down and enjoy your meal after you purchase it so this is strictly a carry out only place.  Brown Derby is also a convenience store and offers an assortment of all manner of other items so you can do a bit of shopping before getting in the often long line to enjoy some of the food from this spot.  This is a very popular spot in the area so the line for the food can be longer especially around breakfast and lunch so plan accordingly.

I really want this place to be good, as I frequent happy hour and the bars on Oak, and I would have loved a nice quick place to grab some food.    Unfortunately after several visits and giving it several chances I can't see ever going back again.  Way too overpriced for what it is and the decor looks like they just ripped it off a 5 Guys Burger. On my last visit my burger and bun just disintegrated and crumbled apart as I attempted to eat it and they were completely out of iced tea.  The place was also nearly deserted on my last visit but all the tables were covered in trash.  They actually want tips even though it is exactly like any other fast food burger joint and they don't provide any "service."  Bud's Broiler is better.  They might be able to redeem themselves with some major work but it will take something major to get me back in here as Camilla Grill is a far better and cheaper burger of the same type and nearby GB's is far superior.

This festival has improved and grown dramatically over the last few years.  The move to City Park has made for a much more enjoyable and spacious venue to enjoy the food and music but I really miss the shade form when it was in Lafayette Square.  There are lots of great food booths doing amazing things with our local seafood, great music, and many local vendors selling their crafts.  This is like a mini Jazz fest without all the lines and FREE admission. The City Park Festival Grounds don't have a lot of shade where they set the stage up so make sure to prepare for bright sunlight with a good hat, shades and sunscreen.

Minus one BIG star for no longer being all you can eat MEAT.  They got sneaky and changed the wording to all you can eat sides and they no longer do all you can eat meat.  I mainly like brisket and the brisket here just plain isn't that good to me and they really focus most of their energy on the pig.  I pray at the alter of the cow so this BBQ temple seems less and less inviting to me.

They probably have the largest selection of different po boys of any other place in the area.  The muffaletta here is now better quality than the one at Central Grocery.  They make decent po boys here but the line is usually way too long for what it is.  The biggest hassle here, other than the crowd, is that they only take cash.  The roast beef po boy is ok but certainly not among my favorites and not worth dealing with the crazy lunch wait with the crowded dining area (they are also only open for breakfast and lunch closing at 4:40 in the afternoon).  This is probably a place you should visit once just to see what all the hype is about but it certainly won't ever be on my regular rotation as it has essentially become a major tourist destination and there are too many other great places to eat for a similar price with much better amenities and you also might even get service for the same price as the no service here. They also have a nice little surprise for folks with their upstairs dessert area that has some tasty treats if you have any room left in your belly after your main course.

They have some really great soups here with the "Spanish Town" being a real standout and then their sides are quite flavorful with the rice and peas, callaloo and plantains really pleasing my taste buds.  The chicken and seafood dishes here are really nicely done while the goat curry wasn't my favorite.  Lunch is usually quick and easy here while during dinner it can get crowded when they have entertainment.  The only thing that I don't like about this joint is they don't offer iced tea.  This is definitely a joint worthy of a visit for some satisfying delicious food that leaves you with a healthy satisfied feeling.

This is one of the last cool music CD and record stores around NOLA and they probably have one of the larger selections of any of the few remaining stores.  On a recent visit they actually didn't have the music I was looking for but that's a rare occurrence that has only happend this once.  They also have a selection of used music for sale along with t-shirts, posters, hippy smoking junk and lots of other knick knacks.

Before Katrina I saw some great shows here and the interior of this place is amazing.  They have a "magic" ceiling that transitions from daytime with moving clouds to a star filled night sky!  Well here it is nearly 2013 and they still haven't reopened but they have been hard at work doing renovations so let's hope all goes well and they reopen again soon.  The area of Canal that the Saenger is in definitely needs revitalization and economic development as its still a very shady area.

This is a bit of a secret and out of the way bar in Elmwood.  Inside it looks very fresh and clean.  Drink prices were reasonable and they have ladies night every Wednesday.  The crowd looked to be mixed with older and younger folks all having a good time.  The service was fast, friendly and easy on the eye.  This seems like quite a popular place in the area.

I've been in here a handful of times and they used to have a large and popular ladies night where the ladies got to drink free but I don't think they have that anymore.  Every time I've visited I've just had a couple of beers and left as it just doesn't seem like my type of crowd and it has always been really smokey.  The few occasions I've visited this establishment it seems that often there were near fights or actual fights breaking out here so I don't like dealing with the hassle getting stuck in the middle of any stupid bar brawls.  They seem to have a decent menu of bar type food but I've never eaten here.  They have some pool tables, a dart board and some other entertainment devices.  They have a lot of TVs so this is probably a decent place to watch a game.

The food here probably ranges from a 2 to 3 star depending on what you get.  The worst thing I ever ate here was a seafood lasagna that was so bad I couldn't eat more than a few bites of it.  The regular lasagna, manicotti, spaghetti, eggplant dishes, and parmesan dishes are usually good.  They have decent pizza and pasta with some inconsistent execution of their main entrees.  The best thing about this place is that you typically get good value and large portions so you will definitely never go away hungry after a meal here, however, you should save some room for dessert at nearby Brocato's after.

This is the easiest AMC for me to access and right off I-10 for quick in and out.  The ticket sales are ground level and then you ride an escalator to the top level where the theaters are located.  They used to have problems with teens running wild in here but they instituted new policies that don't allow unescorted teens after a certain time so that seems to have calmed it down.  Some Chinese company recently bought all the AMCs in the area so I'm not too happy with giving the commies money but since they own all our debt anyway its hard to avoid these days.  I'm still stubborn and go to the Prytania a lot more now but some movies only play at the AMC...

This is a total dive located in a shack off of Veteren's right behind Jigger's Grill in Metry.  The ambiance here seems more 1970's style than anything else I could pin on it.  They have decent po boys, hamburgers, sandwiches, plate lunches and they offer fried chicken.  They offer a "chicken loaf" which is half of a bone in chicken fried and served on top of two halves of garlic buttered French bread.  They have some good seafood gumbo and some daily specials that are ok.  The roast beef po boy is alright but could be better if it had more gravy.  They have a few indoor seats and very limited outdoor seating.  Most folks just pick up to go orders here.  About the only issue I have with this place is they don't brew their own iced tea and rely on fountain "tea" which never tastes right.

I've only had a few drinks in this dive bar and I can honestly say that this is the most sketchy bar in the entire Warehouse District.  It is a bit challenging to even tell this place is a bar and you really need to know where you're going as you could easily walk past this place without knowing it.  I've never eaten here or known anybody that has so I don't know if I will attempt it until someone else gives me a full report.  The exterior of this place is also a Pepto pink so that sort of makes my tummy feel strange...

This is probably one of the best bars in Mid-City and certainly one of the best bars in all of New Orleans.  If you can't actually watch the Saints in the dome then the best place to be on a game day is Finn McCool's as they have a neighborhood cook-off / throw down with patrons and Finn's cooking up theme dishes based on who the opponent is with a bar tab going to the winner of the best dish (one of the best I've had yet were the Maryland Crabcakes).  It has been getting more and more crowded for game days so you need to get here a good while ahead of the game or you will be standing and it sometimes gets way too crowded.  They have constant events going on and sponsor many of the local teams.  I really don't know of any other bar that does as much for any community ANYWHERE as Finn's and they are constantly doing new and fun things.  This is also the go-to place for European and British Empire expats in the area as it is one of the best places to watch Rugby (the only real sport), soccer, cricket etc. and they will open very early/stay open very late to accommodate the game schedules.    The only negative aspects I could comment on about the place is that it is always majority male and good looking girls are usually not that plentiful in the place.  I'm also more of a professional, clean cut, military vet, Southern preppy kind of fellow and this place isn't my usual crowd and its a bit more blue collar, old drunks (maybe I'm one of those), grunge, with some random smelly hipsters and a good smattering of Euro/Southern Hemisphere folks thrown in.  Regardless the vast majority of the people are fantastically nice and usually just having a good time.  This bar can also get amazingly smoky and gross sometimes too, unfortunately, and they have experimented with some smoke free times that I hope they expand.  The parking can get to be a bit of a pain and require parking a ways away and the neighborhood might scare some out of town folks to walk in (I've never had any problems but always use caution and common sense).  The bartenders are AMAZING and stay incredibly on top of things no matter how crowded it gets and they seem to have photographic memories of what you drink.  The prices are more than fair and you get amazing service for an excellent price and often free food to boot (and food for sale as well from their kitchen) so it is certainly worth a visit to this very Irish and friendly bar.

This is actually a lot nicer and more convenient spot than either Cafe du Monde or Morning Call's other horrible location in a strip mall.  This location is aesthetically pleasing both inside and out with the panoramic awesomeness of City Park all around you.  They also serve their beignets  without powdered sugar so you add your personally desired amount.  Kicking it up an even higher notch than Cafe du Monde is they also have real food and other desserts in addition to just coffee and beignets.    You might not get the same level of people watching weirdness here as you do in the French Quarter but you do get a much better selection, convenient parking and AIR CONDITIONING inside or you can choose to sit outside on nicer days.  The other awesomeness about this location is that it is 24 hours so a very needed spot in this area of the city.  I'm not really much of a coffee and beignets person but I like this place!  One big minus is that its CASH ONLY!  Redeeming quality is that most things are so cheap it won't cost much cash.

This place advertises itself as "Bistro Orleans, Traditional New Orleans Cuisine" but they only offer THREE entrees: red beans and rice, chicken tenders, and pork chops.  They have a seafood platter selection of five choices along with a selection of salads, po boys, and hamburgers.  The biggest selection of the menu is under the pasta section but they don't have my desired lasagna as one of the choices.  They offer  a seafood gumbo, a meat gumbo, and a cream of oyster and artichoke soup.    The high point of this location is that they really seem to have done a lot to transform the interior of this bland suburban sprawl building into about as nice a place as possible with what they had to work with and I thought they did a very nice job making it a pleasant dining atmosphere so I hope they kick up the food the match the decor.     When I ate lunch here I had their special of shrimp creole and I found that it was "ok" tasting but it used very small shrimp.  I also had the seafood gumbo which wasn't terrible and while it really was just "ok" it was without much flavor kick to it.  Overall I just didn't think my meal was all that great a value as it just didn't impress me that much.  For a place promising "Traditional New Orleans Cuisine" I've got much higher standards.  I might return to sample the po boys, burgers, or some of the pasta but I really wasn't motivated to return by the really "ok" NOLA food I had as there are just so many better versions not far from this area.

Part convenience store, part grocery, part deli, and part Chinese food restaurant...  What else could it be on Magazine but the Magazine Discount Market.  When you walk inside you get transported back to at least 1970 if not earlier as nothing has changed inside since then.  I've ventured inside this joint several times to purchase lottery tickets and I've thought about trying the Chinese food but when I've looked at it I've been uninspired and afraid of it.  They have a lot of canned goods in here and some produce but its definitely more of a convenience store with hot food than grocery.   They do have some booths you can sit and eat in...    If you've been brave enough to eat the Chinese food in here let's hear about it as I've never known anybody that has!

The ambiance is awful inside with a cavernous industrial hard feel composed of concrete, metal and glass construction that also leads to terrible acoustics so that it gets so loud (with not that many people) it is hard to communicate with other humans or hear much of anything specifically.  The food is interesting and they do have some unique spins on most menu items.  The small portion sizes of most dishes really don't justify the prices that are charged.  For example the Llama burger at lunch is delicious but it isn't one of the larger burgers in town and all it is served with is a very tiny side salad that is maybe two tablespoons worth of greens so this dish left me feeling quite hungry still.  Overall it is worth one visit for the unique menu items but the terrible acoustics and small portion size for the price really will limit my desire for frequent visits.

They have a good range of pastries, pies, cakes, cookies and other sweets here.  The owner and chef is from France and he is usually at this location.  They are probably best known for their cakes, with their French style "galette des rois" King Cake being one of the most noted.  I actually prefer the French style myself as I don't like all that colored sugar that most Louisiana style king cakes have on them. The prices seem to frequently get more expensive here but they maintain a good product.  This is always a consistent place to go for your dessert needs.

This is one of the classic New Orleans Creole fine dining establishments of legendary lore.  New owners have taken the helm and seem to have been improving upon it while experiencing some inconsistencies that seem to be smoothing out.  The food has generally been good here but I've had some things that didn't meet my expectations a few times.  The biggest issues here seem to relate to service and at an establishment of this caliber service is certainly held to a high standard by those of us who hold our New Orleans dining traditions sacred.  I think they have put the right team in place and seem to be running a more consistent operation.  The bar has been top notch on every visit I've made so if they can maintain consistency in the dining room service and kitchen operations they should easily earn more stars from me.  The courtyard here is a very pleasant space when they weather is agreeable while happy hour and their Jazz Brunch are probably two of the best times to sample the offerings here.

I've driven past this place many times when working on the Wank and I always thought it was a place I would never venture into.  Well during a recent Yelp bar tour I finally expanded my possibilities and dove right into the naughtiness of the Knight.  For some reason I had always had the impression that this was some type of strip club but it is actually just a crazy bar that has been trapped in time since the 70's.  I was a bit unhappy with the selection of beer as they didn't have any local Louisiana beers or special beers at all beyond Bud, Miller, and Coors products.  Other than our group there only seemed to be about three other people in the whole place.  Service was very slow as the grandma bar lady was pretty tipsy and took awhile to get to you.  I'm glad I now know what Naughty Knight is but I don't think I will ever have much motivation to return unless it is with another crazy group.  If they still had disco here that would be a different matter entirely.

The happy hour is a great deal and snagging a spot at the bar is the best seat in the house.  This place is very popular so even on a Sunday at 3:00pm (their daily happy hour goes from  2:00pm-5:00pm) expect a substantial crowd. You order at the counter and then get a server that sporadically checks up on you but the service isn't adequate generally at the tables (so you can go awhile without a drink refill so sit at the bar, if possible, where you can get full service).  I also wish you got a bit more choice in building your own pie instead of the set menu as there are very few options.  The pie here does have a nice crunchy crust with good flavors that can stand on their own even without toppings.  They did a really great job with the build out here and its a very nice space to enjoy some pizza and drinks.  Overall I would only go here for the happy hour and it might be worth it to wait for a spot to open at the bar for the vastly improved service available there as the table service is a disorganized mess.  If it is too crowded here or you miss happy hour just go to New York Pizza for the $5 pint and a slice deal.

Out of the three Korean places we have in the area I think this one comes in third place.  They still seem to be trying to get up and going and have a lack of servers and lunch is still a very slow crowd.  The food is alright but the price is rather steep for what you get.  The menu at lunch was a pretty limited selection compared to the other Korean joints in town and the lunch prices were rather expensive for lunch.  This place still seems very new and probably still has a lot of work to do to find its optimal niche in the area.

I eat lunch here very often and I really love the chicken pho.  It isn't a regular or large bowl like other places usually offer but a nice in between size that fills me up the perfect amount.  I especially like the Jasmine tea (I've heard some honky folk complain about the taste being too strong for them).  I get in there before Noon and usually get extremely rapid service but when I've gone later it can take a bit longer to get served.  They have a great selection of items on the menu and the only complaint I've got about the place is the really bad techno/rap music they blare.

Let's do the time warp again!!!  Whoosh on back to around 1970 and enter this eatery and you will probably see quite a few older folks that have been regulars here since at least 1970.  I've driven past this spot for many years and always wanted to get around to trying it but just never did until today.    The menu here is HUGE and includes almost everything you could think of relating to breakfast.  There is even a large selection of six different syrups: pecan, blackberry, blueberry, boysenberry, strawberry and regular.  They have a much more limited selection of sandwiches and hot lunch specials but their limited selection is the equal of most other restaurants complete selection.  Service is very attentive and your order is brought out extremely fast.  I'm not a fan of breakfast as I only will do brunch as it involves a lot more fun and about the only "breakfasty" things I like to eat are grillades and grits, shrimp and grits or steak and eggs.  The music would make any elevator proud and the only things that gave away I wasn't actually transported completely back to 1970 is that one of the soup specials was lentil and one of the hot lunch specials was chicken shawarma so I guess some Middle Eastern ownership has possibly had a slight influence.  So the important things to remember about this place are that when you want a retro time warp experience they have chandeliers, breakfast and chicken fried/country fried steak.  They take credit cards but they only allow one check per table.

When traffic is flowing I like this bridge but when traffic backs up I get very frustrated with this span across the Mighty Mississippi.  Generally traffic flows more smoothly from the Eastbank to the Westbank because in the opposite direction there are toll booths that back the traffic up and cause delays.  You can get a toll tag and pay a reduced fee if you make regular jaunts across this bridge or pay $1 for a journey from the Westbank to the Eastbank.  I've been trapped in traffic on this bridge more times than I like to recall and I always hope and pray for smooth traffic flow as I HATE being trapped in traffic on bridges (actually I hate being trapped in traffic anywhere).  You do get some FANTASTIC views of the city from this bridge and its great to see how the Mississippi River meanders between the two banks.

I ate here soon after their reopening and went with a group.  We were a bit frustrated that many items listed on the menu were not available and had less than acceptable service.  I finally settled on a typical platter of fried seafood and, although I enjoyed it, I wasn't inspired to make the drive back to eat here again.  Judging by the other reviews on here I'm probably way overdue for another inspection soon.

Tchoup Yard is the newest addition to the bar scene right off Tchoupitoulas Street nestled in-between Second and Third Streets.  It features a huge courtyard with a rotating offering of food trucks.   Fun is afoot with a great selection of draft beers, frozen drinks, wine on tap, wine in bottles and plenty of mixed drinks.  Tropical breezes from the river help cool down the patio and keep the enjoyment  going.  This place is so new they don't even have the phone connected or a website yet.  Bonus Tip: They have a huge parking lot accessed via Second Street!!!

This is an alright joint with a pretty good bar and quite a few large screen TVs for your viewing pleasure.  They have an interesting selection of po boys done with a unique spin from the traditional offerings.  The duck po boy isn't anywhere as good as Crabby Jack's version but its OK.  They are too much into bacon fat frying for my taste and folks that don't eat pig should note they mix pork into many of the other sandwiches.  I am a fan of duck fat frying and the duck fat fries will probably be needed as a tasty addition to any po boy as I find their sammich size to be too small for my appetite.    I give them kudos for their creative spin on their food and using quality ingredients but a meal here can get pricey quick (especially for a sandwich).  The bar is a good deal and they have some good prices on the drinks.  Overall its a place to go when you're in the mood for something a little bit different and unique and can splurge around $20+ for a po boy and fries (or on one of their other interesting sides).

Mid-City is one of the great neighborhoods of New Orleans and includes beloved locations such as the Fairgrounds, Bayou St. John and City Park.  There are many great neighborhood restaurants and bars that keep the legendary hospitality of New Orleans alive.  There are lots of friendly residents in this area who are proud of their neighborhood and have worked very hard to bring it back from the devastation of Katrina.  They have many festivals and events throughout the year that keep this area busy having fun.

I've eaten here many times and they do have some good drink specials here.  The food here is generally simple and a good value like Mexican should be.  They don't have a lot of parking and this smaller location is popular so it can get challenging to park and a bit too crowded inside at times.  Overall its a decent place to grab a taco or burrito and have some drinks all for a good value.

I enjoy the lunch specials here.  They have a really good hot & sour chicken soup.  You also get to choose between multiple types of rice to go with your meal so that makes it a bit more interesting than your typical Chinese place.  I've heard some complaints from some people that have used this place for catering and I've also had some occasional slow service.  In general I've always found this to be a reliable spot for a quick and tasty meal that is a bit more upscale for a Chinese style restaurant.

I ate at this joint a few times before I knew it was a chain.  I used to work in the area so this was a convenient lunch spot but I really never found it all that great but I tried many of their offerings before I just got bored with it.  When it first opened it seemed like WAY too many people were getting catering from this place so I quickly got burned out on almost everything here.  For a chain type place its an ok sandwich type experience but I think I would rather go to Subway.  I doubt I would ever eat here again as I'm just left with a huge feeling of MEH about it...

This has to be the most fun bowling alley anywhere in the world!!! They offer live music with plenty of dancing for those that don't want to bowl along with a full bar and a decent menu.  This is always a fun place for all ages and it is a truly unique New Orleans experience to enjoy everything that happens here.  I have to confess I really miss the old location (and the new super slick lanes make me a bit sad and I miss the old "broken in" stuff) but new space is better than no space so let the good times roll.  There are always some great people and fun times at Rock'n Bowl.

This is not always the best sushi but this place generally gives you a great deal of quantity and they have some great lunch and dinner specials.  This is never my first choice when in the mood for sushi but I occasionally stop in when I'm in the area.  It sort of has a fast food ambiance about the place as they have a drive up menu.  I have often been amazed at the quantity of food I've gotten at times here so this place can be a good value.

I hadn't been in this place since the early 90's and decided to return and sample some of their beer again.  I recall the food had been pretty decent the last time I had eaten here but with so many choices in NOLA this place just doesn't come up on my radar often as it is so touristy.  Their house beer here is more expensive running a bit over $8 for a large glass but is decent beer.  They have a well experienced oyster shucker shelling out some good shellfish and they seem to still offer decent food.  For a restaurant that caters mainly to tourists they still seem to offer better quality than many other of the tourist focused joints in town.  It probably isn't a spot I will ever frequent but I wouldn't have a problem occasionally popping in for a few of their beers and some oysters.

This review is for the now gone El Patio Mexican Kitchen and Tequila Garden.  Add this to the list of soon to be closed businesses in 2018.  $5 per tiny taco is absurd and then you get to pay for chips and salsa.  There is absolutely no way this place will stay in business with their current menu and pricing.  Looking at the menu I thought I was ordering a taco plate and not just ONE taco because NOBODY charges $5 for ONE taco!!! The dry bland taco was a .50 cent size and a Taco Bell taco would have been infinitely better.  This is the uber hipster place to go for terrible food at insane prices.    Overall you would have to be utterly demented to eat here as this is the worst Mexican and one of the worst restaurants in NOLA.   To add insult to injury my stomach is doing salmonella somersaults from likely poor food prep...  Wake up call they need to visit Juan's Flying Burritto, La Casita, Taqueria Guerrero, Felipe's and other area Mexican joints to see how outta whack they are pricing themselves.  The only good news is they had some $4 beers.  La Casita ran El Patio but ran it quite differently than La Casita but fortunately they have recognized the error of their ways and seem to be returning this place to their La Casita model that works.

It is the best movie theater in Mid-City and it is also the only movie theater in Mid-City!  It is smaller and more intimate than I thought while the actual theaters and seating inside of them are reminiscent of a shotgun design being long and narrow.  The bar seems to be the heart and soul of this place and it really looks nice.  The movie watching experience itself was rather different than any other theater I have watched a movie in as the sound system audio presents a less encompassing experience that at times presents a challenge to hear dialogue; it is also a bit distracting that bright light emanates from the entrance (that did not dim when my movie started); additionally the screen appears quite smaller if you sit further towards the back (much more so than other area designs.  The parking lot was a bit of a chaotic mess on my most recent visit and I believe I will just choose street parking over their lot for future visits.    Personally I still prefer the experience at Prytania Theater but that might be more loyalty to my hood and Prytania only has one screen to the Broad's four and the Broad also has far better seats while I would rate the audio and visual experiences better at Prytania.  I don't like Canal Place one bit so I would certainly choose Broad over Canal Place all of the time.  It is of course always great to have options and Broad certainly is a great option to have so to mix things up occasionally I'm sure I shall visit this place now and again.

The return of a classic seafood restaurant location with new ownership that still honors New Orleans traditional seafood classics along with some good Italian dishes.  Fresh, live, fried and boiled seafood is offered along with alligator.  Muffulettas, po boys and hamburgers are also on offer.  A great spot to check out for lunch or dinner.

This is one of the top clothing stores in the metro area and its locally owned and operated.  They've been around since 1924 and carry  designer collections that you won't find anywhere else in the area.  Not only do they offer a fantastic selection, outstanding service, and valet parking but this store is also often used as a great party venue.  I've been to several great events here and always have enjoyed all the time I've spent in this store whether shopping or at a party.  This is one of the few remnants of the glory days of the Canal street corridor when ladies wouldn't go shopping in the area without their gloves on.  One of their uniquely New Orleans items they have started to offer are Streetcar logo polo shirts so if you need a uniquely NOLA gift you can add that to your list!

I work on the Westbank sometimes and I've eaten Hi-Do's products many times while I've only stopped in the actual store a few times.  The location in a strip mall really doesn't inspire confidence that you will be experiencing anything special.  On entry you will quickly surmise that this is a  Vietnamese bakery that offers a selection of pastries, breads, cookies, cakes and other treats.  This bakery is well known in the area for their king cakes which have a different texture than most others and they will produce them in non-traditional shapes like crawfish and fleur de lis.  They also make some good French bread that many restaurants use for their po boys.  Its a really big hassle that they're cash or check only and they could really use a website to make ordering easier.  If your on the West Bank this will be one of your few bakery options and worthy of a visit.

This is a very popular eating spot at the Lakefront and its a kicked up gourmet diner with typical staples and strong NOLA influences.  Lots of people like breakfast here but I'm not a big breakfast person and I prefer their sandwiches and entrees.  They have a nice selection of seafood options here and very good burger.  They make their own desserts and have some seriously good pies.  The biggest issue here is typically getting in as it seems to be crowded most of the time as this restaurant has a perfect combination of good food with a great spot on the lake.  Overall most of the food here is a good value for the amount and quality of food you get.

It is an iconic symbol of our city and THE CHURCH of New Orleans.  It is pretty inside and out and you can tour it for FREE as well as attend mass here.  It honestly doesn't rate up there with the mighty cathedrals of Europe and actually there are bigger and better churches even in NOLA but there is nowhere else quite like it.  If you're not into touring churches and listening to history then this probably won't be your thing and you will probably have a lot more fun doing other things in the city.  If you're interested in history, old churches, and interesting stories then you will probably enjoy your visit to this New Orleans landmark.

This is a classic fried seafood place with some shockingly modern overpriced food in small portions that doesn't seem to have a lot of flavor.  The fried food is decent but there are many better places in the area and the service seems to get a bit worse every time I visit.  I rarely go here anymore as there are so many other places:  a) I like better  b) that I get more food  c) that tastes better to me  d) for a lower price.    It might be worth a visit for the sheer experience of a place that has been around for so long but temper your expectations.  It isn't a bad place and it can be fun just don't expect to be blown away by the flavor as it will mostly all taste the same of fried batter.

You can not only eat here but also do your laundry, make some groceries, or they even will let you sleep here as they also run a Bed and Breakfast.  This is a really groovy place to grab some food and they also have a brunch.  Schiro's has both an Indian menu with some pretty good stuff and then more of a traditional New Orleans food menu.  They also do a daily selection of deserts.  This place also has a good bar inside of it that is a comfortable place for both eating and drinking.  The roast beef po boy is not their strong point and I think the Indian food is generally the better choice when dining here.

I evacuated into here after being poisoned nearly to death by the extreme smoke content at 3 Crow Bar and was very happy to find a good smoke free environment.  They had a great happy hour going on and I enjoyed my time here.  It looks like this could be a good sports bar spot for viewing some games.  Service was attentive and friendly with the bartender giving some good info about local craft beers.  The food on the menu and that I saw folks eating looked good but I had already eaten so I had no space left in my belly to sample anymore.  Overall this looks like a good spot in the 5 point area to hang out.

This is a pretty authentic Mexican restaurant that offers a few things that aren't generally offered at most of the other Mexican and Tex-Mex places in the NOLA area.  The margaritas are not that great but the food definitely offers a good value and some very good flavors that are bit more distinctive than most of the other Mexican joints.  If you're bored with the typical Mexican restaurant selection this place can introduce you to some new dishes and they have a nice sampler plate to eat alone or share.

Great spot that seems to have out Hong Konged the Hong Kong Market.  They have one of the most amazing selections of fresh greens I've seen at any grocery or farmers markets ANYWHERE so far in my life.  The fresh produce selection really puts most other grocery stores and markets in the area to shame.  They seem to have a larger selection of pan-Asian food items than even Hong Kong market (Hong Kong has gone more multicultural now offering Hispanic and Middle Eastern options that take up more of their space that had been all Asian before).  They also have a little BBQ space in the back with cooked pigs and ducks on display.  They were still celebrating Chinese New Year when I visited so they gave me a little lagniappe of some ramen noodles during checkout.    Overall you definitely should check this place out and do some shopping here and try something out you've never eaten before.

The portions are a bit small but the flavors are good.  They only have bottled drinks and I would be much happier if they offered fresh brewed iced tea.  They have a decent selection of sandwiches along with a few pasta entrees.  They also have a small deli with a selection of meats, cheeses, olives and other items.  You order at the counter then your order is brought to your table and since there are no drinks to refill you really don't get any service beyond that.  Overall a decent place to grab a sandwich or some pasta for a quick casual lunch.

I don't really like all the extra gunk they do with making their shakes.  I just tried the ice cream and that didn't really have much flavor to me.  The service was very friendly but the process of getting a shake made is VERY slow so I had to wait quite a much longer time just for a scoop of ice cream than any other NOLA place while just two people in front of me got their complicated gunk shake.  Overall I just don't see myself coming back as the lack of flavor in the ice cream and the lack of my interest in having a gunk filled shake just don't match with this joint.  The interior ambiance and their ice cream looks real pretty but just like some people look pretty on the outside sometimes they end up not having much to offer on the inside to somebody else just like this place for me.  I'm sure other folks can end up having a lovely, long and fulfilling relationship dating this joint but she just isn't my type.

This place is like an atomic bomb bunker filled with hazy smoke and they usually keep plenty of provisions on hand just in case.  If it is "possible" I usually get cheaper beer here than at Ms. Mae's (and I used to think that was impossible).  This place NEVER closes and I think they have an ongoing pissing match with Ms. Mae's to see who can serve the cheapest booze and attract the most dive of dive bar crowds.  This place has a much more intimate and comfortable feel to it than Ms. Mae's and the bartenders can come off a bit gruff but they like to joke around and have fun with the customers.  They seem to cater more to the country music crowd than most other dive bars in NOLA   They also do some nice free holiday meals for their patrons that happen to be drinking here during those times.  I had no idea they did this until 8am one Thanksgiving morning (ok yeah I was having a really long night/morning out) when the bartender was kind enough to invite me to their meal.  They have some pool tables and I think I have some hazy recollections of darts being played but I don't ever venture that far back into the bunker as I like to keep my eyes on the daylight so I can find my way home again otherwise I'm afraid I might become a bunker zombie and never leave.  This place is really like a 3.5 star place to me and would be a 4 except there never seem to be more than 10 people in it... of course maybe that is because I never find myself here before 8am.

I love Theo's Pizza!!!  This is probably my favorite pizza place around.  The thin crispy crust makes me a very happy eater.  I enjoy the wide range of interesting combinations they offer.  The Eccentric & the Spicy Mexican are two of my favorites but my usual fix is the Hippy with either chicken or meatballs added.  I always get a side of their tasty marinara to dip my crust into; although often it isn't needed I still love the sauce and will just drink it!    I also really love their ice as it goes so well with their iced tea and I think it might be the best ice in NOLA and I want to find out what kind of machine makes it as I want one.  They also have good beer and wine specials.  The sandwiches are very tasty but maybe a bit overpriced for their size.  The salads have always been very good also.  I have heard a few negative reviews from some of my friends about the Canal Street location with their crust not being done properly but I've never had a problem here or at the Magazine Street location.  The Canal location is far more spacious but I prefer the Magazine location cause it is closer to my hood.

This review is for Dominique's on Magazine and I'm not sure how the name got changed to Apolline (rumor says Dominique's is moving to a new Magazine location).  My last visit here was one of the most expensive I've had in recent memory and my portion of the bill was around $200 for three courses and our table split three bottles of wine (but I did go with some of my wine snob friends that think the wine isn't good if it isn't expensive).   The menu was very compact but they had several off menu specials that sounded tempting and I opted for one of them.  Everyone in my group enjoyed their food and we all focused on different versions of red meat (I enjoyed my lamb).  The space is a bright, comfortable, and fun environment while respecting the historic features of the building it is in.  You get free cotton candy for dessert which is interesting but a bit sticky and messy.  Overall it wasn't my favorite style of food but it was good and I enjoyed the atmosphere.  It certainly is worth an occasional visit but I probably won't be a regular here.

The food here is good just not as good as at the Marigny location BUT they do have booze here so that makes it more convenient in some ways.  For the price I think I much prefer the food at La Thai on Prytania but this place is probably a bit more "authentic" if you want to be a purist.  The atmosphere is a bit sterile and while the interior has lots of space I find it a bit too "modern" for my taste.  It is a good addition to the area and if you want a bit of a change it can be a nice spot for a quick Thai experience.

The setup this year was moved to Woldenberg Park and was just like the setup they do for French Quarter Fest.  The problem with this setup is that they have vendor booths that run right next to one of the stages so that creates a mass of traffic cluster as the crowd from the stage gets smashed into the lines for the vendors and make it really difficult to access those vendors.  They really need to move those vendor booths to a different location to provide more room for the music fans and a better traffic flow for folks to access the vendors.  They had a nice selection of vendors and the lines were nowhere nearly as long as at the BBQ fest that was going on the same day in Lafayette Square.

I've only had a few drinks in this dive bar and I can honestly say that this is the most sketchy bar in the entire Warehouse District.  It is a bit challenging to even tell this place is a bar and you really need to know where you're going as you could easily walk past this place without knowing it.  Somehow (I guess due to the proximity of this place to hotels) the majority of people that seem to find this place are tourists.  I've never eaten here or known anybody that has so I don't know if I will attempt it until someone else gives me a full report.  The exterior of this place is also a Pepto pink so that sort of makes my tummy feel strange...

They have some good gelato and caffeinated beverages here.  The prices are leaning towards the outrageous side and this really is a tiny little spot without a lot of places to sit and enjoy your platinum diamond encrusted dessert that requires a trust fund and mortgage to acquire.  This place is so small they don't even seem to offer a bathroom.  I'm used to my New Orleans standard of Angelo Brocato's so I was a bit sad they didn't also have a selection of Sicilian pastries and related sundries.

This place has been several Vietnamese restaurants in succesion.  This incarnation has an above average amount of chicken in their Pho Ga.  During Mardi Gras they made me happy as they actually allowed table dining during the insanity instead of only offering "to go" like the prior restaurant Pho Orchid had been doing.  Service was friendly and attentive and so far it seems to be running better than the past restaurants.

This place is reminiscent of a 5 Guys Burgers but with more bun and topping choices and less good tasting meat.  For the price in this section of Metairie I prefer Phil's Grill as you get a more delicious burger.  They do provide really great customer service here and come by your table frequently to check up on you.  They don't have mustard available on the table or condiment area which is also a real drag to mustard fanatics like myself.  Overall a decent joint to grab a burger and worth trying out but I would probably head to Phil's Grill for a similar experience and better tasting burger for my money.

This is a shooting range for all things shotgun.  If you're looking for sporting clays this is your place.  They have a circuit range of multiple configurations that are fun and challenging to shoot.  This establishment offers things you just can't easily replicate on your own and is a great place to hone your shotgun skills.

Yes it is a little bit cheesy but it is also a New Orleans tradition to get your daquiri on.  This is the best location to grab an iconic, icy, tasty beverage before heading off to the Fly for a fun filled afternoon or a Carnival parade.  They have some fantastic flavors and you can always add extra shots and get sizes all the way up to a gallon.  I personally like to stick with the strawberry so I can delude myself that it is mostly healthy and it isn't packed with a weeks worth of sugar.  The biggest negative for this location is there isn't a legendary drive through so you have to walk inside and parking can get pretty crowded around this oddly located building (that can be a bit clumsy to navigate around).  Some people actually even hang out here but I've always just grabbed mine to go.

This is one of the better snowball places in the area and is a distant second place to me after Hansen's (as nobody else has such ethereal ice as Hansen's).  I usually get their Chinese take out box size which is very adequate to cool you down on a hot day.  They have a large selection of flavors and often make new additions to the line up.  Similar to Hansen's and most other snowball places in the Summer expect long lines and a wait for your icy treat pleasure.

Hat's off to these ladies!  They did a fantastic job for their first time.  I had to return to my house to debead three times they were so generous with their throws!  Wednesday night has been raised to a whole new level and I look forward to seeing them again next year!  Last night was probably the most fun I've ever had on the Wednesday before Mardi Gras so great thanks ladies of Nyx.

This restaurant opened in the former gym on Freret.  If you aren't in the mood for traditional NOLA food and want a sandwich that isn't a po boy then this place might fit the bill.  They have sandwiches, salads, meat pies, cheese plates and a few other items with some daily specials.  You order at the counter and they give you a number and then bring your food to you so not exactly table service.  They have a bar with a weirdly positioned TV that seems more for the benefit of the kitchen than the patrons.  They have a cute crew of ladies working the front of house that are pretty attentive to drink refills.  This place certainly seems to have potential but they still seem to be taking it slow and haven't come close to meeting their full potential yet.  The sandwiches are decent but for the price I would rather have a po boy.  For a sandwich and iced tea you will spend $15-20 that comes with a side of chips.  The best way to describe this place is that its the Uptown version of Cochon Butcher with much better seating.

I was hoping the goat tacos would compare to the amazeballs delicious ones Johnny Sanchez formerly made but unfortunately these were nowhere close and the goat didn't have much flavor.  This was your basic Guatemalan joint and the tacos and fajitas were ok and decently priced but nothing really jumped out at me as being anything above average.  I was also a bit sad they didn't have a Caldo de Pollo on their soup menu.  So decent authentic food with slower than average service.  It is alright if you are in the area but I wouldn't make another special trip to it.    WARNING: They also are all about some karaoke in here!!!

It is an ok little market with some good local and organic produce.  They have an interesting assortment of items here in addition to food.  The prices seem more expensive than what you would find at Whole Foods and the selection is far smaller.  If I lived in the area I might pop in to shop occasionally but since I live in the Garden District the only time I've ever ended up here was when I had people from out of town that just wanted to check it out.  Yes you heard me right this is now a tourist destination with some of the folks I know that come into town.

I was getting worried that Nashville had gotten so crowded that standing in line to eat had just become the new normal at meat and three joints.  I was very happy that I was able to encounter no line or wait inside Dairy King and the process was not only completely painless but also quite pleasurable.  The nice ladies at the food counter were very helpful and accommodating and then a gentlemen that was working the front dining area ushered us into the hidden VIP special back room area that was quieter and more spacious.  One of the days menu choices was fried flounder and I was VERY tempted by that option but since I live in New Orleans I get to eat flounder all the time so I judged that I had to go with another option. It was also turkey and dressing day so I fully indulged and it was a good meal accompanied by a fantastic cranberry sauce along with the best green beans I had during this Nashville visit and my squash was full of fresh flavor and cooked to perfection.  Parking was also very easy here and the prices were fantastic.  It is certainly worth escaping the hustle and bustle of a lot of the rest of Nashville to make your way to Dairy King to eat with good local folks where few tourists seem to venture.

A fantastic and relatively new annual festival and tradition to add to our list of kick ass events in New Orleans!  Yes the actual run is very short, fast, and early but actually this is a 3 or 4 day fun filled event that you can wear your uniform of white with accents of a red sash and bandanna everyday.  It generally kicks off on a Thursday with a wine dinner, Friday is the El Txupinazo party, Saturday at 8am is the actual running of the roller derby bulls (El Encierro) with an after party til around Noon, Saturday night is the Fiesta de Pantalones, and the grand finale is Sunday for the El Pobre de Mi brunch and party.  So if you were counting they actually cram 5 separate parties into 4 days but if you do it right it is just one long party.  Yes the roller derby girls will painfully whack you with their bats so run fast.  I've been doing this from the beginning and have only missed it due to having to be out of town for work requirements once.  The secret for beginners is don't TRY to wake up for the 8am running just stay out all night instead!

This is a dive bar trapped in the 70's from whence it was formed and hasn't changed since.   That is actually pretty groovy as anything past the 90's sucks and is tainted with hipsters anyway.  They had great prices on their drinks and a nifty selection of brass name plates on the bar that have rather entertaining names on them.  They had a section for pool and darts and this place seems to be quite popular with the smokers.  I'm not a fan of smokers but this bar seemed less smokey than some of the others in the area.  I've also heard legends and rumors of a steak night on Thursdays with the infamous touring Metry lingerie ladies in attendance.  I actually know a guy that married one of those ladies.

This festival has improved dramatically over the last few years.  The move to Lafayette Square has made for a much more enjoyable (and shade filled) venue to enjoy the food and music.  There are lots of great food booths doing amazing things with our local seafood, great music, and many local vendors selling their crafts.  This is like a mini Jazz fest without all the lines and FREE admission.  A great little festival for all ages.  I'm sad that I have to go out of town on Sunday for work as I would love to go for all three days of food and fun!  The only negatives from the food at this fest were that some vendors ran out food early and 7 on Fulton's gumbo was at least 98% sausage and was advertised as seafood gumbo (I don't like sausage in my seafood gumbo!).

This was some good pizza and I was also really tempted to also try their meatballs but I was too full.  The same folks that own Kay Bob's Grill & Ale next door to this place also own Pizza Perfect so you can get the food from both Pizza Perfect and Kay Bob's in both spots along with their drink specials.  Really friendly staff and good service along with prices that made it a great value made this a really great spot.

Vega Tapas does some really great food and it is one of the more enjoyable restaurants to dine at in the Metairie area.  They do some really good paella and their other entrees are also quite tasty.  Their tapas are very nice and they typically give you good portions.  I've also really enjoyed Vega's food when they catered the Running of the Bulls event where they really out did themselves and provided some fantastic food.  This has always been a fun place that I've enjoyed eating at and I've enjoyed nearly everything I've ever eaten here.  They sometimes get a bit too creative with some new fangled style dishes that don't often appeal to me but as long as I stick to the traditional things I'm a happy camper.  When I'm in the mood for tapas this place makes my very short list along with Barcelona Tapas and Lola's.

They like blue lights in here a lot!  I've never really had a good time here.  This is a hotel bar that is attempting to be upscale but with more of a modern and hip vibe but comes off as more of a techno nightclub.  People "dress up" to hang out in here typically but they do it in a bit of a cheesy way for the guys and the girls often seem to wear overly tight and too spandexy dresses.  The demographic looks very similar to what you find in the Metropolitan nightclub and most of these people appear to be coming in from the area suburbs or tourists.  It just isn't my scene and I don't really know anybody that hangs out here.

Not the best environment for dining inside the restaurant and primarily a take out place.  The food is decent but nothing really outstanding here.  I've eaten here a handful of times but it doesn't really inspire me enough to ever be a first choice for Chinese food.  If your looking for basic Chinese take out this place will fit the bill.

This is a fantastic event that transports you to another culture and fully immerses you in a Vietnamese festival.  These folks really know how to throw and party and have a good time and there are plenty of drinks along with great food like plaintain friiters, various soups, kabobs, spring rolls, egg rolls and all manner of other things in Vietnamese that I don't even know what they were.  This is one of the most packed festivals of its type I've ever attended and there is no shortage of fun for children so this is an event for all ages.  Firecrackers and silly string are in full effect and you never know when they will be used.  The entertainment and main stage are all top notch and could give a Vegas show a run for the money.  The only negative thing I could comment on is that nasty honky hipsters were skulking and sulking about in their nasty depressing hipster ways.  Hoi Cho = Festival  Tet = Vietnamese/Lunar New Year  Versai Hoi Choi Tet is the Vietnamese New Year's Festival at Mary Queen of Vietnam Church in New Orleans East.  The festival typically begins on Friday around 6:00 PM and ends on Sunday around 10 pm. Opening ceremonies with lion dance are Friday around 6:30 PM. The big entertainment with Vietnamese pop singers and local community talent are on Saturday night, around 8 PM.  Entry is FREE!  Food, Drinks and Live Entertainment!  BRING CASH (as its cash only)!

I think this might be some of the most BLAND Mexican style food I've ever eaten!  This is equivalent to an Applebee's or Chili's level of dining and the food did not impress me as Chili's makes more flavorful stuff.  The taco was probably the best thing I ate while the enchiladas were covered in some very disappointing sauces.  They offer very limited selections for their "combo" meals and whereas most Mexican restaurants give you a choice of the type of sauce you get on your enchiladas no such option exists here.  If you're used to bold and spicy flavors then this isn't the place for you but if you've got grandma with a delicate stomach then this might be the perfect chain experience place.  The service was friendly and accommodating and they had some interesting drinks.

This is a very easy restaurant to park at compared to most of the other Middle Eastern places in the area so that makes it one of the most conveniently located places to grab a good meal.  All of the food I've had here has been very good with excellent portion size.  I especially like the fact that when I request hot sauce here they usually bring me both the usual red and a green one that nowhere else in NOLA gives you.  The service has always been excellent and I've never been here when it was crowded so my food has always been prepared very fast.  An excellent and convenient choice to get your Middle Eastern fix!!!

This place has a nice selection of seafood and Mexican items along with a good drink selection.  They have quite an oyster selection with raw and different cooked versions available.  The Baja Charoysters that come with a 3 cheese blend topped with grilled mahi mahi and crabmeat sounds pretty fantastic but ultimately it sadly just ended up tasting like nothing but cheese as so much cheese is put on top of the oysters that the other toppings just seem to go to waste in the flavor department.  The olive herb oyster seems to end up being a better choice if you want to appreciate more of the oyster flavor.  The rest of the menu offers quite a selection of seafood and the normal expected selection of Mexican items that are generally well executed.  They also have different daily specials including the nearly mandatory Taco Tuesday.  The location can be a bit challenging to find as it is a bit hidden away in an area that looks more like an apartment building but they have a good sign to guide you.    Overall this is a spot worth checking out and they have an interesting mix of some traditional NOLA items with some unique Mexican twists thrown in along with the normal Mexican restaurant fare.

So my tenants washing machine goes out so I'm shopping for a replacement.  Walk into Lowe's and bam they have some "refurbished" appliances in the front.  "Wow that looks like a great deal on a nice front load washer," I say to myself as I look at the price marked down from around $700 to $250.  Bam! I love a good deal and I'm in good deal fever so I quickly locate a staff person and go up to a Lowe's staff lady and say, "Hey, I'm interesting in purchasing this item if it is fully repaired and you guarantee that it works."  "Oh yes they fixed that in the back it is completely repaired and should work great and we just marked it down so much because of a few dents and scuffs," replies the staff lady.  "Great I'll take it!" I say.  So it takes four of us to load this 500 pound beast into the back of my vehicle and then I recruit three more folks to help me haul this massive creature into my tenants space and remove the old broken machine.    The next morning I get a text informing me that the new machine just fills up with water and won't work.  I again recruit people to help move it but this time I can only get two to assist with lifting the now even heavier beast with the added water weight trapped inside.  We manage to drain most of the water out of the machine but it still seems far heavier and painful to lift than when we had one more man assisting us.  Finally on returning to Lowe's I give the return lady the receipt and say, "Ok I bought this thing yesterday after being assured that it would definitely work but this thing definitely is broken!"  "Oh we only put things out for sale like that when they just can't be repaired so this happens all the time," replies the returns lady.    Seriously if something can't be repaired what in the name of ever loving Bacchus are they selling it advertised as "repaired" for!  It is 100% that if it doesn't work customers are going to be returning such items!  If it is only good for scrap or being broken down into replacement parts don't advertise something as "repaired" when clearly it isn't!  Ludicrous behavior and poor management to ever do such a thing!

I thought I had already reviewed this place years ago...  Well the aquarium is a nice quick trip for folks to take their kids on and is much faster than the zoo.  It is also interesting for adults who want to learn some more about water dwelling creatures of the Americas as in addition to a very large collection of fish they also have turtles, snakes, alligators, macaws, parakeets, penguins and sea otters (most kids seem to prefer the otter antics).  I've also been to several events here and it makes a decent place for a party.  The IMAX theater here is also pretty nice but it is really under used and they could have a better rotation of movies.  My main disappointment is after seeing all the delicious looking fish I get really hungry and they don't have a seafood restaurant in their food court.  For the steep price of admission you should get a fish dinner included in the cost.

I very rarely eat fast food but Wendy's generally makes some of the better quality fast food available in the area.  Generally I see no reason to even review fast food joints as they are all generic but this Wendy's location has earned EXTRA SPECIAL RECOGNITION...    Over the years on the few occasions I've visited this location one thing has been 100% consistent and that would be that they 100% of the time get my order WRONG!!!  I've complained to the little link/number they give you on the receipts but I've NEVER heard back.  I had some small hope that once they completely tore the old building down and rebuilt a totally new store that maybe they would be reborn as a competent establishment... Well that hope was dashed as once again and keeping their 100% FAILURE rate they once again got my very simple order completely WRONG again!!!    Just don't go here and do yourself a really big favor if you must have Wendy's then go to the location on Claiborne where they can at least comprehend how to accurately fulfill an order.  Better yet just go to one of our much better local joints and avoid the fast food experience so you can have a beer with your burger.

I stopped in here for the first time this past Wednesday.  It was pretty crowded when I arrived and it kept getting more packed.  I got the ginsing chicken soup which was a small chicken stuffed with rice and other items.  The dish didn't exactly come out the way I thought it would from the menu description and I wasn't planning on having to dissect and eat so much chicken but it was still a decent and large dish.  I don't think I would order this particular item again as it was one of the blandest Korean dishes I've ever had and I really like the spice of other Korean things I've eaten.  They only seem to give you three pickled snacks while you get more things at the Korean place in Metairie and those little snacks are one of my favorite parts of the meal.  I will probably return to sample more things here and I'm glad we have a Korean place Uptown but I like the menu at the Metairie Korean place a lot more at this point.

This place has some good brisket, great BBQ beans, and nice mac n' cheese.  Continuing the recent trend, that seems to be happening in the fast developing NOLA BBQ scene, they offer five distinctive types of BBQ sauce.  The brisket was very tender and flavorful but unfortunately lacked the hallmark of a distinctive smoke ring to really give the brisket maximum flavor.  The brisket was served with a side of horseradish sauce which was a welcome flavor addition.  The BBQ plates here are served with sweet potato muffins that are very tasty.  I was never fond of this location when Ignatius was here and I still think it is a bit small and cramped but it might add some unique charm to the place.  The BBQ options in NOLA continue to grow and improve and while this place certainly does offer some good BBQ and great sides the brisket at The Joint greatly outshines what is offered here.

VERY disappointing!  I have been waiting in great expectation since October for this place to open and had the most disappointing Vietnamese meal of my life here.  This place is very popular at the moment and it was packed full of people in the small space like a sardine can and I was sat in the tiniest baby chair I've ever attempted to sit in within the most cramped space I've ever attempted to eat in. This place looks a lot like a trendy gastropub and what a surprise they also serve stupid SMALL portions of food just like a stupid gastropub too.  I was served the smallest serving of pho I've ever had in my life anywhere!  They have one bowl size and it is smaller than the small size at all the other places in the area.  If the size of the serving wasn't bad enough they dished out the bean sprouts and greens like they were made of gold and then only ONE slice of jalapeno.    So after this tiny snack I attempt to pay my bill and noticed that when I got my credit card slip back that somehow they added on TWO special coffee drinks to my tab that I didn't have.  It took three times longer to take care of my bill than it did to eat and in the end all they could figure out was to just give me cash for the difference they had charged to my card.  I don't like small portions and dainty little snacks and I don't like being crammed into a sardine can and then forced to sit in a baby chair.  I'd be betting I probably won't be returning to eat the micro pho here so do yourself a favor and get a real bowl of pho elsewhere.

I've been here several times over the years hoping that it would improve at some point but it hasn't.  The only good point of this place is they have some VERY cheap food and drink specials.  You also get what you pay for here and I've never had a good or even decent meal here.  The service has always been lacking and I've just never had a good time here.  This place seriously needs new ownership, new management, new staff, new everything in the personnel department.  Hey maybe they can get on one of those reality TV shows and improve.  Before that happens I really can't recommend anybody go here and 100% of my friends describes this place as follows: "That place sucks!"  I really wish this place could be good as it would be fantastic to have another option when R&O's has a long wait.  Please owners get yourself on one of those TV shows ASAP!!!

I've been going to Bruno's for years and frequented the old location often for rugby parties (I fully deny all reports that I did naked zulu warrior runs around the block even if those reports MAY be true).  The new location is a very nice space and the bartenders are generally very efficient.  There is often a good mix of people of all ages in the bar until later in the night when it seems mostly college age.  There are lots of televisions, pool tables, and other games available.  They have some decent food here and some very tasty debris fries.  My favorite time here is on Tuesday when they have $2 almost anything... well actually almost every night of the week they have some really great drink special going on so it is always a good place to go for cheap drinks and decent food.

Seems like a pretty cool bar if the beer prices on the menu are accurate but they are still having some issues with getting the prices on the menu and those in the computer to agree so make sure to double check your bill.  The pizza here is very similar to Domenica and Ancora.  The crust has a nice consistency and taste while the pie is pretty light on the toppings.  The majority of the seating is outside and inside is all bar seating.  Parking is always an issue in this area but this seems like a nice addition to the neighborhood.

It's not a bad place and it's not a great place.  It sort of reminds me of a smaller and way less cool One Eyed Jack's with a bit more of a dive bar edge.  They have bands and performances and unless it's a band or performance I want to see it just doesn't really motivate me to go here.   It definitely has a nasty hipster and smoker vibe to it which makes me pretty out of place here with my non-smoking and old school preppy ways that draw the wrath of the uber hipster entitled class that frequents this place.  Oh yeah I also wear my polo shirt and khaki's purposefully just to irk those hipsters because if believing that I choose my mode of dress to irk them makes them feel more entitled and special then I hope it makes them drink more PBR so maybe they will become better people one day and less special because if all hipsters drink PBR then there isn't anything special about it.

This isn't the worst gym and it certainly isn't the best but it is conveniently located.  They have most of the basic weight and exercise equipment that you would need along with a good offering of different classes (yoga etc.) that come with your membership.  They also have outdoor pools that are open seasonally and offer many different events throughout the year.  They do have some unusual hours closing early on Friday and for several days during Jewish Holidays but then they are open when other places are closed (like Christmas).  I was a member here for many years but they raised the price of membership every year and they closed too early for me to get there often so I finally let my membership lapse as I was unable to fully utilize my membership with the hours they were open.  I'm also having far better results with using P90X and saving all the money I once spent on my membership here!!!  This is a much better value for families that have children as they have lots of good programs for kids.  If you are looking for a gym Uptown this is one of the better options if you can't get a good deal at Tulane's Reily Center.

This is a great place for breakfast, brunch, lunch, and dinner.  I don't really like breakfast food but they make me like it here with oysters and soft shell crab.  I'm really not a fan of their Korean Roast Beef po boy... I would rank it as one of the most unique and interesting roast beef po boys in the city but it just wasn't really my thing.  They also have some really great burgers, po boys, salads and soups.  It has a great location right off Jackson Square so it is a great place to people watch and see all the interesting action going on.
