There can often be a bit of a wait to get in at certain times and especially on the weekend.  I usually like it and you should try it to see if you will too!

Good raw oysters, some good seafood dishes, and "ok" ambiance but too starkly industrial modern for my taste.  The drink prices are expensive but you can get a schooner of beer.  Overall it seems like a hotel restaurant designed for tourists with tourist prices.  They do have some great lunch special prices but most of the dishes don't really float my boat and the prices for the other lunch items are really expensive for lunch and don't get me started on the dinner prices.  For my schooners of beer I will probably be heading to other locales unless they get a good happy hour going or I win the Powerball.

Their main claim to fame is they are open late and deliver.  The sandwiches are a bit over priced for the size.  The pasta dishes are a good size and the pizza is definitely not my favorite but better than say a Domino's or Papa John's.  They have relocated to the old orphanage down the street from their previous location so you have to do a little searching inside the old large maze of a place to find them.

This is probably my least favorite of Emeril's offerings and it is self described as "casual and funky" which isn't my usual dining preference unless I'm going to Jacques-Imo's.  Regardless of that this can be a fun place to go when in the French Quarter but usually wouldn't be my first choice.  The food here is generally good and the service has always been acceptable.  The tables are a bit close together and I have, at times, had to wait a bit longer than I would have liked to have a new drink brought to the table.  The crowd usually seems to be a slight majority of tourists with some locals thrown in.  The quality and preparation of food are usually good but the ambiance just doesn't work for me and for the price there are many other places I would prefer to enjoy but it certainly is worthy of sampling occasionally.

Most of the food here is pretty decent.  The fried food is usually the focus of a trip here and they also do some good chargrilled oysters.  They also feature a seafood pizza and some various other items along with the expected po boys.  I enjoy the little boiled potatoes they bring as a snack while you wait for your food.  I've generally had pretty good service here and sometimes there is a wait but usually not too bad except on the weekends and during lent.  The boiled shrimp have ALWAYS been WAY overcooked here EVERY time I've ordered it (or tried other peoples).  The BBQ shrimp is usually WAY better here than the boiled shrimp.   I usually only end up here if the wait at R & O's is ridiculous or on days when they are closed.  After so many chances over so many years I would have to say avoid the boiled shrimp but enjoy most everything else.  It isn't my favorite seafood place but it does some things well.

The new permanent location is right across the street from Bon Ton and I much prefer a BBQ joint to the prior tattoo parlor at this location.  Unfortunately the beef brisket was tough and rubbery like a shoe and I KNOW they can do better as I had better back when they were just doing pop up at Dante's.  I don't know if its because they have been so busy being newly opened and needing to put out a high volume or what but the brisket was definitely in need of a lot longer time in the smoker or it was cooked at an incorrect temperature.  I was also pretty disappointed in the portion size as the Joint gives you a whole lot more meat for about the same price.  The chicken and pig seem to be the things they excel at here but I'm a brisket fan and unless they go off and learn from some Texas pit masters or our very own brisket masters at the Joint I'm going to keep my BBQ love for the Joint.  I really hope they get the brisket down as this place is a lot closer to my house than the substantial trek I have to make to the Joint.  I like how they offer a wide selection of sauces but they have got to focus more on the MEAT and do a LOT of work on the brisket!!!  The cole slaw was decent while the mac and cheese still needs a lot of work and it just doesn't seem very cheesy.  The only thing that really has flavor and is well done here is the chicken.  BYOB.

Pat O's is a legend in the French Quarter that is a popular venue for both tourists and locals alike.   The bar actually consists of several bars spread out from a central courtyard with a flaming fountain.  They also serve decent food here and the service has always been acceptable.  The stereotypical Hurricane and other overpriced concoctions that you can purchase a souvenir glass for are always prevalent here.  Personally I just stick with the beer because I like to be able to not fall over on Bourbon Street or yak everywhere.  There is ALWAYS an interesting crowd here and there is a line to get in here on Christmas afternoon.

One of my least favorite Chinese joints in Metry.  I rate this place slightly above the Tea Garden.  Its located in the expected suburban strip mall environment that lends to a complete lack of character.  The food mostly tastes like reheated prepackaged stuff that can be gotten cheaper at other takey-outtey places.  It is doubtful that I shall ever engage in a return visit.

This venue seems like it will be at its prime when the weather outside is nice as they have an upstairs patio and downstairs patio that gives it more seating outside than inside.  The service is above average for a Mexican joint and this place actually serves some unique items that are a bit different than the typical Mexican joint like pasta, crab cakes and a burger.  The enchiladas were a bit on the small side for my appetite as were the tacos.  The flavor of everything could have used quite a bit more spice kick to it for my taste.  The drink menu had quite a varied selection and didn't offer that many margarita options compared to what other Mexican themed joints typically offer.    Overall it is a decent place for a meal if you aren't that hungry for an entree to fill you up and don't mind depending more on the rice and beans to fill you up.

The ambiance is very modern and industrial which fits with the location inside the Rice Mill Lofts in the Bywater.  The food is "Italian-inspired cuisine" and is a bit different than most of the other Italian restaurants in the area.  I recently had the black linguini and while it was a decent meal the pasta was a bit past the al dente point.  The chocolate terrine I found wasn't really to my liking and wouldn't order that again.  The drink prices seem quite out of line with the location in the Bywater and seemed quite expensive all around so I wouldn't suggest drinking here.  This could be a decent date venue but for my tastes there are far better environments in NOLA that are much more interesting than the bland industrial vibe this place gives.  Service was inconsistent with the server disappearing for stretches at a time which isn't really acceptable at this price point.    Overall its a decent spot to check off your bucket list but I won't be making it a regular stop on my dining rotation.

This is a convenient covered patio bar located at Lakeshore Landing next to the marina on Lake Pontchartrain that offers live music in the afternoon along with a concise menu of good pub grub.  The establishment is both kid and pet friendly so that makes a good checklist for folks that need those options.  This spot offers some great views of the lake along with lots of great boats to check out as well.  This is a laid back spot to have some outside time along with the inclusion of a roof over your head that makes it nicer than the average uncovered patio just in case one of our frequent NOLA rain showers breaks out.  Current operating times are:  Saturday from 2pm - 10pm  Sundays from 12noon - 6pm    They also currently advertise drink specials all weekend long.

This used to be just a basic cool college bar.  Now it seems to rotate between being a gay bar, a lesbian bar, and whatever else bar.  I liked it when this joint was just a plain bar and I don't have the patience or inclination to discover what rotating night of the week which sexual orientation will be spinning through.  They have remodeled and attempted to reinvent themselves but I've got no desire to play the sexual orientation roulette wheel that this place has become and neither gay or lesbian bars interest me so I will just stick with plain ole regular bars.

I have seen this place for years when I would eat lunch at the nearby Randazzo's Restaurant and I've always been curious about it and I finally got a chance to check it out.  This Metry strip mall bar has some efficient and friendly lady bartenders that are easy on the eye and one was wearing a pair of sexy tiger ears on the night I visited.  The drinks were decently priced and they had a lot of space dedicated to pool and darts.  This place brings in the smokers and while it wasn't that bad while I was there I could see that it could get unbearable for me when it gets more crowded.  Its definitely a very local crowd here that seem very serious about their darts.

I had gone past this bar for years but always thought it looked way too shady to venture in which is hilarious when I consider that I usually saw it when I was on my way to the super shady Saint.  A friend of mine moved a block away and so I ended up meeting them here one night and discovered that this is actually a really cool bar.  The vibe is very laid back and there seems to be a good group of regulars here.  It is usually a bit too smokey for my preferance but overall this seems like a great little neighborhood bar.

I had my first experience of McClure's this past Tuesday night and I found it to be a very enjoyable experience.   It was an awesome value for $15 which included all you can eat food along with your non-alcoholic drinks (and beers running about $1).  They do the meal in a "family dining" style where you share a large table with several other people and they bring plates of food out to the table to be passed around.  The meal started with a lagniappe (but the server called it an amuse-bouche but I'm going to be rebellious as I think lagniappe fits better here) of a small bowl of chili topped with fritos.  The sides, which consisted of corn bread, mac n' cheese, cole slaw, potato salad, and pork n' beans, were then brought out and passed around.  They then brought out a "special surprise" of BBQ bologna sandwiches that were quickly inhaled.  The main event then made its debut as the meats, chicken, beef brisket, pulled pork, and pork ribs, were then brought out and filled the atmosphere with their mouth watering-smokey-aroma highlighted by the beautiful sight of the perfectly charred flesh characteristic of expertly crafted BBQ.   The hands down star of the show was the very flavorfully smoked, BBQ chicken, which is among the best I've ever had.  However, I regrettably have to admit I was disappointed by the brisket which seemed to be of the "extra lean" variety and I greatly prefer mine to be the more fatty "extra moist" variety and the brisket seemed to lack a nicely developed "smoke ring" on it so I would have to say that Smokin Buddha Bbqieux , Whole Foods, and the Joint's brisket are still better to me at this point.  The most amazingly unique thing to me about the meal were the numerous homemade BBQ sauces available to sample that covered so many various styles and flavors (however all of the sauces described how well they went with chicken or pork with no mention of my true love beef).  I've never been to any BBQ place that had such a variety and that really added a whole other dimension of flavor to the experience.    While I wasn't knocked over by the brisket I was suitably impressed by the whole experience to definitely desire a quick return to eat more of this food.  I hope the brisket was just due to an off night or cut of meat and I look forward to sampling it again.  The whole family dining experience has its benefits and challenges.  I enjoyed meeting some new people but the plates of meat that were brought out were a bit small and went very quickly (you could go up and request more of course, as it was all you could eat, but it was just a tad bit inconvenient to my BBQ lust as it slowed my inhalation of tasty meat; yet perhaps that was their intent to tease my senses).  I closed my meal out with some of their very tasty corn bread and one last helping of the amazing chicken (with a few squirts of yet another of their many BBQ sauces).  I then departed into the darkness of the night with an extremely full belly and a great need for a nap with the result that when I arrived home sleep quickly descended upon me and I dreamed wonderful dreams of a rainbow of BBQ flavors dancing in my head all the night through...  How long until next Tuesday night?

This is both a restaurant and bakery of wonderful cakes, pastries, and French bread (with which they make wonderful bahn mi).  Dong Phuong provides their delicious bread for bahn mi to almost all of the other Vietnamese restaurants in town and I greatly love their bread.  The restaurant has a large selection of items and you can have any type of pho you want as long as its beef.  You can get a banh mi on the bakery side and bring it over to eat in the restaurant side.  Service can often be slow and sporadic depending on how crowded it is.  This is certainly one of the more unique places you can eat at in the New Orleans area with such an interesting selection of food available with both the bakery and restaurant providing an excellent spread of choices.

The Boot was GREAT during my undergraduate years but it is waaay too young now (or am I just too old) and plays mostly bad music these days.  Back when I was a crazy undergraduate rugby player we had some great parties here for the Tulane Rugby Tournament.  I still sneak in once a year during Carnival, for old times sake, to grab a few beers in the huge plastic cups which come in very handy for wandering around during the parades.  It is just like a nasty  little piece of Bourbon Street was transplanted Uptown.

This place is definitely not the king of anything.  I had the single worst bowl of pho ga I've ever eaten in my life here.  The chicken pho came with the least amount of meat I've experienced and that small amount of meat was low quality and rubber in texture while the broth was blah.  My jasmine tea was nearly clear and had zero tea flavor to it.  I hope their other dishes are far better but this is the worst food I've ever eaten at a Vietnamese restaurant.  Go to Pho NOLA or Pho Orchid for much better food.

The location is in the typical and terrible suburban strip mall hell.  I eat lunch here on occasion and the extensive menu is generally in the Italian Creole realm.  They have some well executed dishes and I've generally focused on the seafood options with the occasional chicken or veal parmesan.  They often will have some surprising things that you wouldn't expect on the menu and it is always a good place to eat.  They have some dinner specials that can be a good value.  The service is variable and certainly more laid back than anywhere near fine dining standards.  Much of the food often gets up to four stars but the ambiance, service and strip mall location of the place make it less enjoyable than it could otherwise be to me.  The interior is far nicer than you would think from seeing it from the outside but it still lacks the character you could have in a different setting than the limitations of a generic strip mall.

Phil's gets the award for the most choices of different burger types anywhere in the area.  Most of the burgers are pretty good but none are fantastically memorable.  Phil's is a little above a fast food place and around par with an Applebee's in atmosphere.  You have a whole series of steps to go through to "build" your burger.  There are an amazing number of choices and more choice is certainly better than less choice, usually, so you can have an amazing variety every visit you make here.  I've sampled many different things here and had many different types of burger meat but unfortunately in the end most of it tasted very similar.  Not a bad burger and certainly worthy of sampling but not an outstanding one either.

I have found neither the food nor the drinks to be anything special here.   I was first drawn here many years ago by the reports of all of the high level margaritas and other mixed drinks.  I have sampled pretty much all of their drinks and none of them were very impressive to me and I was especially disappointed in the fact they used CANNED pineapple in their drinks.  The Blood of the Devil drink is unique (and painful later) but still nothing I really would want to repeat.  The food was the typical Tex-Mex stuff wrapped in a tortilla with a few other dishes that I find to be nothing special or even very flavorful.  I've eaten Tex-Mex all over Texas and "Mexican" all over the Southwest and, while it isn't my favorite style of food, I've eaten enough to know when something is special and El Gato isn't anything beyond average.  They do get an extra star for some girls flashing their tits to me the last time I was in here.

This is the best Thai place in the burbs around NOLA that I've yet experienced and certainly the best in Jefferson Parish.  The drunken noodles were good but not as good as the ones I've had at La Thai and Sukho Thai in the city limits.  The Thai chicken coconut soup was good but could've used a bit more spice for my palate.  Overall I would say this is one of the best places to eat in the Elmwood area and among the top Asian restaurants in Jefferson Parish.

They have quite a selection of ready to cook prepared items in addition to quite a nice selection of high quality fresh meat.  The crawfish and crabmeat pies are good sized but I still really prefer the crawfish pies at Big Fisherman.  For just sheer size of selection this is a great one stop shopping spot if you have multiple items you want to acquire.  They also have freshly fried pig skin if you need some of that.  Overall this is a decent spot to get a great selection of Louisiana food items while I find the spice level to be a bit too tame for my taste.

This is a nifty joint on the Wank that I would probably enjoy more as a bar than an eatery.  The pizza here is alright with the Odyssey pizza being decent but there are just much better options to my palate so I probably wouldn't spend money to eat the pizza here again and the Margherita pizza is especially in need of improvement.  If you are on the East Bank and feel like something a bit different hop on the ferry and come on over to try this joint out.

"The Home Of The Tacky Ashtray" is the way this dive bar describes itself.  I'm not a smoker and unfortunately with all the ashtray love this place can get smoky at night so that is a big minus for me.  The barstools are an entertaining sight to see and I won't describe them so you will have to see them yourself.  This place also makes some mighty tasty food and has some pretty great lunch specials that range from Southwestern influenced to NOLA classics like turtle soup.  They have some good burgers and other typical bar grub but the lunch specials typically kick it up a notch or two (or sometimes more).  They also frequently have live music and although the space is a bit tight for dancing they will move the tables out a bit more if there aren't too many people sitting in them.  I've always had a good time at the Rivershack and make it a point to keep it in my occasional rotation as both a good lunch spot and a fun nightlife/music venue.

Wrong Iron seems to be getting a lot wrong. The bar seems to still be suffering new opening disorganization with not having beers that are advertised on their beer menu.  There is only one bar inside and it seems strange they didn't put an outside bar for the patio crowd.  On my last visit the parking lot was totally full but then there was not a very big crowd inside and it was also a cool night yet most of their patio fires were not even lit.  Seems like they are putting serious effort at going full tilt at a half-azzed effort at doing the basics.  The patio also gives me a weird put-put golf course kinda vibe.  The space has the potential to be decent enough with rocking chairs outside being one of the best comforts but they gotta step it up and stop acting like a bunch of disorganized wankers.

One of the larger and nicer Robert's in the area and one of the very few grocery options in Lakeview.  Convenience sometimes has its price and they know that they are the main grocery option in the area and charge higher prices accordingly.  I've only been in here with friends of mine from Lakeview that were in a hurry to buy something but personally if I lived in the area I would take the extra few minutes just to dive the short distance to Dorignac's.

This place had some glory days I remember when they were pretty good and I actually liked this place.  They then began to slowly decline and get inconsistent as their chain empire expanded and then collapsed.  Lately they just seem to mostly be unacceptable as their chain-ful death continues.  This used to be an inexpensive and quick place to grab a decent meal before a movie but of late they just have not lived up to expectations and my dining dollar feels drawn elsewhere.  I think if they can institute some quality control and go back to the roots of what made them what they used to be they could vastly improve this place.

This is a very interesting lounge/restaurant/cigar bar as they seem to be many things at once.  They have lots of different theme areas from the main bar area, to a wine cellar, to a cigar lounge.  The decor seems reflective of their attempt to be many things at once and is a bit disjointed and confused in many places but the cigar lounge was comfortable.  They make nitrogen infused cocktails that belch smoke out and give a mad scientist effect along with decent wine flights.  The food seems to frequently change and bounces all over the place as they want to focus on the most seasonal produce so it is hard to describe what direction they are going in at any particular moment.  I've always had a good time here and I will be curious to see how this place develops and gets focused on what they want to be.

This is a great spot I was glad to discover as it was new to me along with also being near a spot I used to work at so I wish I would have known about it sooner.  A husband and wife own and run this place and they are some really nice folks.  They have a nice rotation of daily specials during the week and it is a pleasant place to enjoy a meal.  I have only managed one visit so far to sample their burger and some fantastic onion rings but I still really want to try their daily specials which look fantastic.  I am really craving their pot roast and I'm looking forward to sampling that as soon as possible.  My video review of Ernie's Cafe is here:  https://youtu.be/x00w_BiEOxk

They have done some very nice renovations to this bar and it has started to draw an interesting mix of people.  The location is unique without a lot of other stuff around it other than houses.  The inside is mostly taken up by a huge bar and then they have a nice patio.  J'Anitas has been doing the food here since they moved out of Avenue Pub and they have some good food for your dining pleasure (with some fantastic burgers).  The main downside I've experienced is that it can get very smokey even when it isn't all that crowded.  I've only been here a few times so far since they reopened and I've always had fantastic service and interesting conversations with a wide range of people.  This bar looks like it has a great future ahead of it and they have been hosting live music.  This is an area that doesn't have a lot of other venues so it should be interesting to see how it develops.

This is a fantastic event that transports you to another culture and fully immerses you in a Vietnamese festival.  These folks really know how to throw and party and have a good time and there are plenty of drinks along with great food like plaintain friiters, various soups, kabobs, spring rolls, egg rolls and all manner of other things in Vietnamese that I don't even know what they were.  This is one of the most packed festivals of its type I've ever attended and there is no shortage of fun for children so this is an event for all ages.  Firecrackers and silly string are in full effect and you never know when they will be used.  The entertainment and main stage are all top notch and could give a Vegas show a run for the money.  The only negative thing I could comment on is that nasty honky hipsters were skulking and sulking about in their nasty depressing hipster ways.  Hoi Cho = Festival  Tet = Vietnamese/Lunar New Year  Versailles Hoi Choi Tet is the Vietnamese New Year's Festival at Mary Queen of Vietnam Church in New Orleans East.  The festival typically begins on Friday around 6:00 PM and ends on Sunday around 10 pm. Opening ceremonies with lion dance are Friday around 6:30 PM. The big entertainment with Vietnamese pop singers and local community talent are on Saturday night, around 8 PM.  Entry is FREE!  Food, Drinks and Live Entertainment!  BRING CASH (as its cash only)!

Warehouse space that has been updated into a restaurant space is the best way to describe this restaurant.  The front of house seems pretty disorganized as there was no hostess when I arrived so I sat at an empty bar seat but then was told that it might already be taken by somebody on the wait list but then I got to keep my seat as it seemed there was no list.  The service was really lacking and my iced tea never got refilled and my server frequently was just absent for long periods so thank God they give you your own bottle of water to serve yourself. The pizza was OK but it really isn't as good as all the other many new pizza places that have opened recently and you're already so close to Pizza Delicious in this area so personally I'm skipping the pizza at this establishment from now on.  The other dishes here seem decent with the genre seeming to mainly be Italian.  I had the panna cotta for dessert which tasted good but was overpriced and gave me a bit of a stomach ache.    This is quite the trendy new spot of the moment but for the price it just really underwhelmed me.  They only offer a very limited menu so they have to ensure that every dish is great.  I hope they do well and get their issues smoothed out but there are so many really great restaurants near here that I would be hard pressed to be tempted back here again.  If I do return it will be awhile so that maybe they can get the front of house organized and I definitely won't be getting the pizza or the overpriced dessert.

I got lucky and found an AirBNB right in the middle of all the bars in Midtown (Johnny Cash's old pad they say).  So I made a visit here during my tour of some of the bars in this part of Nashville I haven't visited before.  Kung Fu Saloon is a national chain and I usually avoid those like the plague BUT they do have video games and I need to play my old school video games.  The outside area looked cool and also had games but there were no people out there as it was cold and a slow rain was drizzling down during my visit.  I have driven past this bar during nicer and warmer times of year and it has been much more active so I need to make another visit when the weather is nicer on one of my future trips to Nashville.

This is really cool dive bar with a lot of beers on tap that also unfortunately still allows smoking but at least they keep it decently ventilated so it doesn't get too disgusting.  It is very disappointing for my last visit on a Sunday when there was a 2 for 1 special that I got charged 1 for 1.  I also take issue with this establishment taking credit for having the "Original Bushwhacker" as everybody knows FloraBama invented that beverage.  They have a decent menu of food here and serve some items late.  The service could be better even though they usually have a lot of staff working behind the bar I have been left with an empty glass of beer needing a refill for far too long several times; even when it wasn't that busy as the staff was around the corner smoking or having a long conversation.  Overall this is a decent bar to go to and especially during one of their 2 for 1 beer specials although it would be much nicer without the nasty smoking.  It would make a LOT more sense if the smokers should get put out on the non-smoking patio area so all that nasty smoke could escape instead of being trapped inside the building.

Port of Call is a place I've gone to for many years and I can honestly say it ain't what it used to be in the food department.  It is still a great dive bar and back when the burger was consistent it was a good tasty burger (but never the best and many people have found the cool unmelted cheese more of a distraction than a unique charm).  Currently the food can best be described as inconsistent and a bit overpriced.  The service can be described as sometimes good but usually inconsistent.  They also can make an acceptable steak and the baked potatoes are usually pretty decent (if they can ever get your order right these days). I would never wait in the crazy lines that often form here to eat (usually on the weekends) as there are too many other fantastic options in the area.    The wacky tiki glass drinks they make here really add to the ambiance of the bar and the fact that this place has become quite the tourist trap has both good and bad qualities.  The good is that you will always be able to meet some new people from all over the place and the bad is the ridiculous wait to get in during most weekends along with the tourist pricing.  I've still got some locals I know that love this place but not as many as I used to know and I rarely end up here anymore.    Certainly Port of Call is something you should to do, at least once, just to experience the wrath of one of the tiki drinks and say you've had the burger.  It is worth a visit just for the sheer ambiance of the place.  I might be a bit nostalgic and too generous with my three star rating and remembering way too many fun times here but try it yourself and let us know how you liked it!

This is a dirty dive bar focused on live music.  They used to focus mainly on metal but seem to be expanding the genres of music they book since getting their live music shut down for awhile due to permit issues but the bands are back.  The drink prices don't seem very dive like and seem in line with what you would pay at most nicer bars.  This place attracts an eclectic mix of mostly Bywater folks with a few preppy freaks like me occasionally thrown in the mix.  The main draw to this place for me is the fantastic food done in the pop up here, Kuhnya, that does some great Slavic dishes and a mean burger.

They get some good bands here but this is probably one of my least favorite venues to see live music in New Orleans.  The service is usually very slow and the drink prices are too expensive for New Orleans.  It can also get crazy crowded and the poorly designed venue has plenty of bad spots for watching the band.  I used to have a lot of friends that were members of the Foundation Room so I used to go in there pretty often but almost everybody I know has dropped their memberships because the House of Blues just doesn't deliver what we expect in New Orleans.  It is overall a decent place for events and music but I greatly prefer other venues.

This is probably the finest remaining example of a traditional New Orleans neighborhood  casual creole-Italian restaurant and one of my favorite places to eat.  They basically have the vast majority of all the dishes that I LOVE in the New Orleans food repertoire.  There is a fantastic selection of different daily specials every day they are open.  Mandina's serves fantastic turtle soup, gumbo, po boys, seafood, etouffee, red beans and rice along with Irish influenced dishes like corned beef with cabbage and beef stew.  Some people whine about their "Americanized" Italian dishes but I love them and I will drink their sweet awesome marinara sauce.  The menu is a fantastic example of the glorious blend of all the ethnic backgrounds that melded to create our rich creole New Orleans food tradition.    The quality of the food here had slipped a bit before Katrina and then it slipped a lot after and they were running on only 2 or 3 cylinders for awhile.  Well now they are roaring along on all 8 cylinders, like a fine tuned race car, and the food is once again fantastic!  They have also FINALLY started taking credit cards!!!  They only thing that remains to be a great inconvenience here is the sheer popularity of the place, as there is often a long line to get inside, but that is just further proof of how great this place is.  The one thing that would make this place even more fantastic would be the addition of an oyster bar as the lack of raw oysters is a significantly felt and glaring omission in a place such as this.  For the portion sizes you get here it is extremely hard to beat the fantastic value that this place offers.  If you want to experience the epitome of traditional "everyday" New Orleans food this is probably the single best place to look into its soul.  Mandina's is what a lot of places in New Orleans used to be and it's the "it" that many places are still trying to recapture.  Sure there are all sorts of new places and innovative "new" spins on food but when it comes to my dining raison d'être of NOLA food my orbit will always be drawn to circle the bright sun of the traditional dishes here.  Tip:  I'm not a fan of the turkey and oyster dressing plate here as it just doesn't taste good to me and I much prefer the Thursday turkey special at Joey K's and I have to say the same for the corned beef..  Once Again: They NOW Finally Take Credit Cards!!!  Hooray!!!  See my video of Mandina's here:  https://youtu.be/rn_0WPi04nM

I've been going to this spot for years, back when it was the original Bruno's, and  I frequented this location often for rugby parties (I fully deny all reports that I did naked zulu warrior runs around the block even if those reports MAY be true).  This is a classic old neighborhood bar that switches to more of a college bar the later it gets.  I've still got some friends on pool teams that like to hang out here and play (Tulane holds an NCAA championship in billiards from years ago and the fellow that won that for them still shows up to play here sometimes).  They often have some good drink specials and it this bar has an ambiance that has been in the works since the 1930's that the new Bruno's just can't reproduce.

I've been several times and it just doesn't float my boat.  I've sampled multiple things and I just would much rather be at another tapas place than this one.  (I'm not sure if the same people that ran the previous short lived restaurant, Catch, at this location are still involved now but I think they are and that was some of the worst food I've ever had in NOLA.) Every time I've been I've sampled something different and found it mediocre at best and I hoped that at least the sangria could have some saving graces but unfortunately it did not.  This is now officially on my "no go" list and I won't be returning.  5 visits and 5 strikes and they are out; which is unfortunate as they are near to my house and I would have liked to have liked the food but I find it nowhere close to Spanish tapas or any other food I like (it seems generally more like Central/South American food with some strange NOLA fusion attempts).    I can see how this place might appeal to women but I should also confess that I HATE the small plate concept (outside of traditional tapas and sushi) as I like to eat and I'm a man that needs a good portion so if the price of multiple small plates to fill me up costs more than one regular plate it makes me very unhappy.  An old caveman like me needs a big hunk of meat to be happy and a man's belly being unhappy is the source of most of the trouble in the world ya know...

They have expanded the offerings here from beyond just golf to all sorts of different traditional athletic games along with arcade style video games.  The games here are done in lanes that are like rectangular rooms where you have a lot of space to interact and I even saw some folks bringing their own real golf clubs to play here.  They have revamped the menu a few times and the current menu is more of pub food style along with some items that kids will probably like too.  My Big Texan burger was decent and the fries were crisp.  The service was friendly and attentive while giving good suggestions about the menu.  They have daily specials and seem to be working towards more of a bar scene during the later hours while being more family friendly earlier on which is the case with many places in the area.  It certainly seems like an interesting setup with their games approach and I want to get back to play some of them.

This is a long and narrow dank dive bar hidden right off Bourbon Street.  There is generally a mix of locals and tourists hiding deep inside this place and I've generally found myself drawn here at the peak of night when I've gotten the need to hide from the madness on Bourbon Street.  I've rarely had problems finding a seat in here so when you're in the mood just to cozy up next to the bar and enjoy some drinks then this might be the place to escape to.

I don't like strip clubs and they just don't do much for me so about the only time I'm in one is when I get dragged along by my friends.  On one such occasion I got dragged into this joint.    What I found extremely amusing about this place, out in the middle of nowhere in New Orleans East, was that the girls just parade around on top of the bar.  The great thing about this place is they don't completely rip you off on their drink prices like 99% of all other such establishments as this.  If you have the need of a strip club for a bachelor party, birthday, or whatever else this is probably the best place in the NOLA area to do it.

This is one of the most fantastic and elegant hotel bars in NOLA!  Why compromise your standards to go to a pretentious and cramped "gastropub" when you can go to an actual space with real class, an amazing bar, and real dining like the Sazerac offers within its bountiful allure.  I really don't even like sazeracs but I will down one here just to get my out of town friends to experience it.  I would suggest dressing up a bit as this space deserves it.  This is a great place to just get comfortable and enjoy the company you're with or meet new people.  I also think they serve some fantastic food in the restaurant.  I've had some really good gumbo here and I've always been happy with the quality of the food and service.  I much prefer the food here to the next door Domenica but the happy hour specials aren't as generous. The best time to visit here is during Christmas when they really bling the entire hotel up to make it a true wonderland.  This is definitely a "must do" spot and a great place to enjoy some good food and drink in a civilized setting.

This location of Martin's is far less exciting than the downtown location but still manages to have a nice long line to stand in as you wait to order.   It is easier to park here and a bit easier to eat at this location and much easier to get drink refills on iced tea.  The BBQ actually tastes better to me here than at the downtown location as well but it still could use some tweaking for my taste (and by tweaking I mean bring in some Texas Hill Country folks to do it right).  The brisket chili actually had better texture and flavor to me than the regular brisket.  To my taste I think the nearby Edley's has better brisket but they will sometimes sell out there so you can have this location of Martin's as a backup BBQ plan.

The BBQ brisket here isn't fantastic but its decent and the cole slaw is pretty good.  The folks that work here seem really nice.  The parking lot for this place is microscopic and has room for just four cars and one handicapped spot.  Sadly the BBQ doesn't come close to the Joint but maybe they will keep working on it.

Why compromise your standards to go to a pretentious and cramped "gastropub" when you can go to an actual space with real class, an amazing bar, and real dining like the Sazerac offers within its bountiful allure.  I really don't even like sazeracs but I will down one here just to get my out of town friends to experience it.  I would suggest dressing up a bit as this space deserves it.  This is a great place to just get comfortable and enjoy the company you're with or meet new people.  Make sure to check out the 1878 Ascot Cup, which was designed by Queen Victoria as a trophy for the famed English horse race of that year, which was purchased by the Roosevelt Hotel in 1938.  I also think they serve some fantastic food in the restaurant.  I've had some really good gumbo here and I've always been happy with the quality of the food and service.  I much prefer the food here to the next door Domenica but the happy hour specials aren't as generous. The best time to visit here is during Christmas when they really bling the entire hotel up to make it a true wonderland.  This is definitely a "must do" spot and a great place to enjoy some good food and drink in a civilized setting.

I'm still on the fence as to my feelings on this place as on the one hand they do have some unique spins on some food while offering some unique dishes not really found elsewhere in NOLA but on the other hand some of the execution and flavors don't work for me.  Their lunch lamb chop for example sounded like a good idea and while it mostly turned out alright the breaded crust that was put on it was just unfortunate and the meat would've been far better without it.  They are a popular breakfast spot but I'm just not really into breakfast food.  The service has been a bit strange and inconsistent and the the prices definitely reflect the current gentrification trend of going towards New York City pricing to make the Tulane students from the Northeast feel like they are back home again.    I don't even know what genre to put this food in as they describe themselves as "eclectic mix of international influences" and "Mediterranean flavors, local favorites, and homespun classics" but I don't recognize anything here as NOLA food or really even much that could be Southern U.S.A. homespun or Mediterranean or even really diner food as everything is quite a bit of a unique mix.  I'm going to have to eat here for at least a few months I think to finally make up my mind as many items on the menu just overall do not seem to appeal to me that much from reading the descriptions but maybe they could be good so I'm still just left rather unsure of where the food compass here is going so that could be good or bad depending how the journey goes.  At their current prices it might take awhile for any journey as there are many other of my old familiar places I find I would rather enjoy a meal at for a much better value.

Jazz venue in the Sheraton Hotel.  Good music and expensive drinks.  Several Blue Dog paintings in the venue.  A sedate environment for more of the seated type of Jazz enthusiasts and not the dancing type.

This is a cool place for quality, locally sourced, and artisanal craftsmanship.  Less cool for portion size as I've always still been hungry after eating one of their sandwiches and ended up having to get something else to eat later.  They have a good selection of sandwiches and prepared foods and some other cured meat, deli, & sausage selections you can buy in larger quantities.  It has been getting more and more popular with tourists and it is getting a bit hard to find parking and even harder to find a seat the last few times I've been.  I usually only  eat here when I've got something to do in the Warehouse district but I think I still prefer Martin's Wine Cellar as my "go to" deli as their sandwiches are large enough to fill me up and it isn't so cramped.    I also generally prefer meat and veggie plates (that I can eat with silverware instead of using my grubby paws) to eating sandwiches but the food is great quality and it is certainly worth a visit as they make good sandwiches.  Unfortunately, if I'm hungry then getting full here will be too expensive for me as I would have to pay for multiple sandwiches so I'm better off going to a fine dining restaurant at that price range.  Great for tasty snacks for me though and I do like the duck pastrami sliders!

JB's Fuel Dock is a popular neighborhood pizza joint with a good bar for getting pizza and sandwiches on the lakefront.   They have seating indoors and even more seating outside.  They have some pleasant views from their outdoor dining areas and they often have different drink specials on offer.  The pizza is decent and there are not many other places to get pizza near the lakefront.  The bar inside takes up about half of the indoor space so there usually seems to be available seats there if all the outside seating is taken but they have so much outdoor seating I've never seen it close to being at capacity.  The service is friendly but you generally have to take your drink up to the bartender to get refills as you put your order in at the bar and all service has been from the bartender on all my visits.    Overall this is a great spot for enjoying some nice views at the lakefront with some good drinks and decent food.  My video review of JB's Fuel Dock is here:  https://youtu.be/b5EbhqCuevg

This is a cool little spot for music, drinks and BBQ out on the lake so you get a waterfront view as a big bonus.  There were no other customers by the time I arrived for my last visit but the band was still there winding down playing to an audience of just Papa Turney's staff so I definitely got attentive service.  The brisket was moist and the grilled cabbage was probably the most delicious grilled cabbage I've ever had so definitely order that as a side.  The service was friendly, the music was good and the beers were cold along with it being cold outside too so maybe that is why nobody else was here.  During warmer weather this is a great spot to hang out for some decent food, good music and fun times.  During colder weather it is still decent food, good music and the fun times just end much earlier.

The drink prices here are really expensive and eating a meal here gets too pricey for what it is when compared to other Middle Eastern places in the area.  This place does seem to do well as a quick to go place but then I really think you could do the same to go food at other places for better quality food at a better price.  The food is decent but for the price, quality and quantity Byblos Market is a much better value.  There are also better Middle Eastern restaurants on the Westbank but in this specific area this is about the only one so if you can't travel far this joint can meet your need for a Middle East feast.  To my taste and sense of value I doubt I will make a return visit.

This is still a very new spot that will probably adapt and change more as they get going.  For a new place they seem to be up and running very well.  The staff were all extremely friendly and everybody from the host to the bartender shook my hand and greeted me warmly and then again when I departed shook hands again and wished me goodnight.    The food was more on the expensive side for the portions and I found the flavors to not really be anything that stood out to me.  The BBQ shrimp were cooked perfectly (although blazing hot when I got them) while I'm not sure what the added peanuts really added to them flavor-wise (other than scare off peanut allergy folks in addition to the shellfish allergy folks) and it would have been nice to have another plate or bowl to put the shells into.  For the current price point and portion size I don't see any reason for choosing the BBQ shrimp entree here again over Pascal's Manale.  The "Floating Islands" dessert was alright but again nothing out of the ordinary other than being too bland for my taste.    My entree of the BBQ shrimp, iced tea and dessert came out to nearly $40 with tip.  Due to the small portion sizes my appetite was barely filled so I had to eat a second dinner to satisfy my hunger.  At this price point I have had much more filling and flavorful experiences at many of the other restaurants in the New Orleans area.  As this is an offshoot of Coquette though the portion size does not surprise me as most meals I have had at that establishment also left me in need of further sustenance.  This certainly looks like more of a small plate joint where you will need to spend quite a bit more on multiple plates to satisfy your appetite.  My understanding of the concept of Thalia was that it was going to be a casual and more affordable neighborhood establishment but my experience certainly puts it more in line with the fine dining range of price points in NOLA instead of the casual/affordable and I fear that at their current prices they will have challenges winning repeat business.  This is still a very new place so I assume they will still test things out and adjust as they go so I do wish them well with building the dream of the concept they have.  They have quite a nice selection of craft cocktails and decently priced wines but I would DEFINITELY like to see a better beer selection with some more affordable beers outside of just Miller High Life.  I will wait awhile and check this place out later and see what direction they decide to steer the place.  I'm certainly interested in sampling their steak night at some point...   Overall this place is brand new so go check it out for yourself as your experience may very well vary from mine and I like what I like and you should too so you might love everything here.

This is a glitzy new renovation of a corner grocery store that seems to primarily focus on selling booze, lottery tickets and a few grocery items.  They seem to have built quite a bit of infrastructure to sell prepared food items and to perhaps do po boys but it isn't functional at this point.  It is nearby my house so it is a convenient location to buy lottery tickets for me but I usually find myself going other places.  I hope they get the kitchen up and running to make a decent neighborhood eatery.  Verret's Bar and Lounge is right across the street so this is quite the developing spot at the moment.  Update 7/8/16 the deli is now OPEN!!!

I went for Saturday lunch with my sister and mother and none of us were happy with the results here.  We were served some of the worst gumbo I've ever had containing ONE shrimp along with half a tiny crab soaking in a cool rue.  The Ruby Red shrimp were ruined the way they cooked them (resulting in them being dry, flavorless and tough) and the shrimp toast appetizer was just an unfortunate choice. I tried to order one of their foreign non-Gulf oysters to see if I would like it and was informed the minimum order was half a dozen even though the menu priced it per oyster.  I can't remember EVER going to a seafood restaurant where EVERY food item I ate was so very unappetizing.  Expensive prices and food that is way under expectations.  Perhaps dinner is a much better experience but now that they have made momma unhappy nobody is going to be happy so I will not return for lunch and definitely won't be bringing anybody back here unless I try dinner sometime and have a radically different experience.

It took quite a bit of adventuring and travel time to find the location of this festival and I was really looking forward to attending it and putting down massive amounts of tasty gumbo as I do love some gumbo...  Wow what an incredible disappointment as this is some of the worst gumbo I've ever had in my life!  I couldn't believe I was still in Louisiana as the "gumbo" was such a bad watery thin flavorless concoction that it wasn't fit for consumption.  I literally ate half of it and threw the rest away it was so bad (and I was starving).  This event was one of the least favorite fests I've EVER been to.  It was so sparsely attended and depressing that I was in and out of this festival in 20 minutes and I really don't think I would ever return to this event!

I went to check this place out on a Sunday afternoon and it was a crowded madhouse that had people going everywhere all at once.  The small parking lot was a traffic nightmare and I never want to go back into that area after getting trapped for twenty minutes just to do the small loop and escape.  They have a very respectable fresh produce section with a decent deli area and the rest of the sections get pretty small from there.  They have packed a lot of stuff into such a small space so as crowded as it was on the day I was there it can make some of the isles seem very cramped.  The upstairs could have been used better as they just cut a lot of it out to make a balcony area but as crowded as this place was they certainly could have used more seating for the coffee bar area that is located there.  All of the liquor, wine, and beer is located upstairs and they have a sign saying no drinking on the premises which is a VERY un-NOLA rule so I'm not sure who came up with that stupid idea unless it was some zoning requirement they got hit with (there was a lady giving out free wine samples so I got to break their rule that they were breaking themselves).  Overall this is a pretty nice place with organic produce that seems priced the same or a bit cheaper than Whole Foods.  This is very near my house so I will certainly end up stopping in here for produce but because of its small size it has a limited selection of other items I like and use.

Its a bar and its a real rotating carousel.  They recently remodeled the bar and expanded the space and the updates look really nice.  They have decent drinks and nearly always a crowd.  They often have music and it is an enjoyable space.  Like most hotel bars it isn't cheap and you pay a premium for the experience.  There are generally a fair number of locals here mixed in with tourists.  Definitely a spot to check out for a drink or two just for the experience.

There are some mighty tasty things done here with duck and rabbit along with many other worthwhile options to satisfy the craving for local Louisiana food.  This is great Louisiana style food, that leans more towards Cajun than creole, that stays close to tradition and doesn't go flying off into any of the trends of the moment.  The restaurant space creates an intimate dining experience that can be good for couples or smaller groups.  The food and service have always been outstanding and there isn't really much that I would complain about or suggest changing other than it is a bit expensive (but certainly worth the price for the high quality ingredients and care that is put into the food).  This is highly recommended and I always enjoy it.

They have expanded the offerings here from beyond just golf to all sorts of different traditional athletic games along with arcade style video games.  The games here are done in lanes that are like rectangular rooms where you have a lot of space to interact and I even saw some folks bringing their own real golf clubs to play here.  They have revamped the menu a few times and the current menu is more of pub food style along with some items that kids will probably like too.  My Big Texan burger was HUGE and the fries were crisp.  The service was friendly and attentive while giving good suggestions about the menu.  They sometimes have daily specials and seem to be working towards more of a bar scene during the later hours while being more family friendly earlier on which is the case with many places in the area.  It certainly seems like an interesting setup with their games approach and I want to get back to play some of them and try this place out later at night as just a bar & lounge.  Overall this is a decent spot for lunch and they have their own parking area which makes it easy to access.  They have an above average bar menu and it never seems busy during lunch so you can get in and out very efficiently.  It might be a fun place for their games and night life but I haven't experienced those here yet.  My video review of LOFT18 is here:  https://youtu.be/kH3TzVWwEKQ

I ordered the spicy tenders and they either got the order wrong or they make the blandest spicy tenders I've ever had.  They have quite a selection of sides here but they don't have them all on the menu so you have use psychic powers to determine what they have or observe and see what all is being served as you wait in line.  I find Popeye's to be better in nearly all respects so that might explain why this is my first visit to a Church's since the 70's.

Batture Bites & Brew is a new business that is a café, coffee shop and great dessert location.  Batture is right in front of Camp Parapet which is a historic location that dates back to the War Between the States.  Batture Bites & Brew has a nice selection of breakfast and lunch items along with a good selection of caffeinated beverages and desserts so in some ways it is better than Cafe du Monde.  New Orleans coffee shops are special places and this is much more than just a coffee shop with all they offer.  My first visit was at peak New Orleans Carnival season and Batture has a nice selection of New Orleans Mardi Gras themed treats with New Orleans King Cakes along with many other sweet treats that are Carnival themed.  During my visit I had the turkey sandwich, a petit four, oatmeal cookie and a macaroon which were all delicious.  They also have done a great job with their location which really is beautiful and has a lot of interesting touches added to make for a very pleasant ambiance.  During my visit they also had a regular stream of customers so they seem to be developing quite a loyal following with all the great things they are doing.  My video review is here:  https://youtu.be/-zsNAzVgFXA

So this was my first experience with Hattie B's as I have always eaten Prince's Hot Chicken in the past but I had heard a lot of great things about Hattie B's so I figured it was time to try their version of Nashville Hot Chicken.  I have gone with the maximum heat at Prince's before but I had stuff to do so I decided to just behave myself for once and got the medium heat chicken tenders which were still decently spiced although just like with Prince's I found the spice to be all on the outside and I didn't get any spice on the inside of the chicken.  For my sides I had blackeyed peas that were good and cole slaw which was drowned in a bit much mayo for my taste.  Overall this was more of a fast food experience as was the environment but it was some good fried chicken that came out fast.

This place is still pretty new and still has the initial new crowds of folks checking out the hot new spot in the area.  The picadillo taco and burrito I had seemed pretty bland and lacking in flavor to me.  The chicken options seemed to bring more to the flavor experience.  The chips and salsa were complementary and alright but the salsa could have used a bit more spice for my taste.  Service was a bit on the slower side and it took longer than it should have several times to get my drink refilled.  Overall it doesn't seem to bring very much new to the already overcrowded Magazine Street Tex-Mex selection.  Currently I would still have to give preference to the nearby Juan's Flying Burrito over this spot.  Maybe they will develop their niche here with their drink and happy hour options?

This is actually a nice bar that not a lot of people seem to know about.  They do some nice drinks here and the service has always been good.  The most unique thing about this place is they have a hidden away "basement" on a lower level down some stairs that if you don't look carefully you might easily miss.  The "basement" makes this a fantastic place to hide away and enjoy some privacy from all the hustle and bustle of the French Quarter.

Nothing really impressed me with the food while it was all edible in a decent mediocre sort of way.  The service was inattentive and too slow for my liking but they did eventually get around to refilling drinks etc.  I have certainly had worse and certainly I have had better so this place does do some NOLA style food which is probably better than many other places outside of of New Orleans.  There is a decent little courtyard and a decent bar while the bathroom was back inside the hotel and was a bit of trip to find along with being unclean (also they were out of towels to dry your hands with).  Certainly seems more of a tourist haunt/hotel restaurant joint than anyplace I would make a regular habit of visiting so it is what it is and I guess it serves the hotel guests and tourists well.

Decent burger and really nice people running the place.  I got the 9th Ward with blue cheese.  The meat was way too raw inside next to the stuffing but it is difficult to get a stuffed burger perfect on the grill and they might want to do a bit of time in the oven with it to keep things more consistent.  I would probably stick with the non-stuffed version of the burgers here.  They also don't allow children inside due to the video poker machines not being in a secluded area (no other bar/restaurant in New Orleans bothers with this rule so I'm not sure why they do).  Overall I'm just not that inspired by the food to frequent the place but I would like to be so I hope they step up their game.

The main memory I got from this years event was a really long line that took an hour and a half to ride the train which was a quick trip to then experience more lines to play the games (which were nearly all some version of throwing something through a hole) for small rewards.  In the past there was a great deal of candy being given out but this year the treats were very hard to get.  I think the children still ended up having some fun but there were a lot of grumpy and unhappy behaviors brought on by the long waits.  This event definitely seems to have declined from what it was in the past and is now just very crowded.

This might be the best Chinese food I've had in the NOLA area.  Their Mongolian beef is one of the finest examples of that dish I've ever had.  The front of the restaurant has roast duck and pig on display.  They make some amazing Chinese vegetable dishes but I wish they offered them in smaller portions as more of a side item as I want to eat all of them on every visit which doesn't work well if you are eating solo or just a couple of people.  The service is friendly and efficient and while the location isn't the fanciest it is conveniently located near the Westbank Expressway.  They also offer one of the best lunch values anywhere with their $6.95 daily lunch special.

I eat here often and I really like this place.  My favorite thing is the hot & sour soup and it always puts me in a good mood to eat that awesome stuff.  They usually have a $5 appetizer special on Tuesday nights that brings in a fun crowd.  They have some very tasty options on the menu and some unique "cajun Thai" fusion dishes that work well.  The owners and staff have always been very helpful and want you to enjoy your food.

This is a 24/7 diner style dive.  They have lots of breakfast items along with a few sandwiches, hamburgers, po boys, steaks, country fried steak and chicken.  I'm not a big breakfast person but they have decent sandwiches and burgers with the roast beef po boy being respectable.  The service is friendly and efficient and the prices are generally a good value.

Bonus points to this joint being 24/7 and they have some pretty huge looking donuts.  I don't like donuts so the huge looking donuts do nothing for me but I did try the burger and sadly I would have had a better tasting burger at any fast food joint so I can't recommend the burger at all.  The french fries tasted very similar to McDonald's actually so those were good at least. The staff were very nice and accommodating and did they best they could with what they had.  I keep seeing more and more of these Sweet Things & Grill all over now as I've seen one in the French Quarter and one on Veterans in Metry so hopefully they improve the burger ASAP.

This festival has improved and grown dramatically over the last few years.  The move to City Park has made for a much more enjoyable and spacious venue to enjoy the food and music but I really miss the shade form when it was in Lafayette Square.  There are lots of great food booths doing amazing things with our local seafood, great music, and many local vendors selling their crafts.  This is like a mini Jazz fest without all the lines and FREE admission. The City Park Festival Grounds don't have a lot of shade where they set the stage up so make sure to prepare for bright sunlight with a good hat, shades and sunscreen.

This used to be one of my favorite bars and a total 5 star experience.  They used to have some of the most amazingly clean unisex bathrooms of any bar I've seen anywhere.  They used to have a great crowd of young professionals and it would get packed with lots of pretty people (and by pretty I mean preppy as I'm biased that way).  The crowd, that used to be drawn from the young professionals that lived in the Saulet prior to Katrina, has certainly shifted to a much different vibe and I just don't enjoy it anymore.  They still do make some of the best mojito's anywhere and they do allow dogs but beyond those two redeeming qualities most of what I loved about this bar seems to have been swept away by Katrina.

They have some fun and free tasting party events here but they do some larger markups on their wines than some other places.  Dorignac's has many of the same wines for a cheaper price but Swirl is convenient and the owners are very nice folks.  Almost every Friday they have a fun wine tasting event that draws a good crowd to congregate for these events and the neighborhood is a fantastic area.

The food and drinks are just like the other Juan's locations except not as good.  They left off my guacamole on my Flying Enchilada's and the exterior of the enchiladas was extra crispy burned.  After they break in the new staff I imagine they should get up to speed and be as good as their other locations but I've heard multiple reports from other folks about problems they have experienced at this location so they need to jump into some serious quality management ASAP!

This is a nice space with generally good to excellent food and sometimes inconsistent service.  I'm also happy they make some attempts at enforcing a dress code so you don't have to eat amongst people who look like barefoot savages.  I've been to several private parties here but usually I prefer to eat at the oyster bar and they do have consistently good oysters.  This place is a bit pricey so it loses some mojo for value but the food is certainly what you pay for and has always been very good with a very nice ambiance that is both classic and comfortable.  This is certainly a place to visit and enjoy some good food and drink!

The actual UPS store here seems decent enough and the people that work here seem to generally be on top of things but there are some other circumstances (perhaps out of their control) that make this a difficult place to do business for me.  I've had a mailbox here for years and I seem to get most of my mail but I've always consistently had a problem with mail that is sent to me being returned to sender (even when the address is completely correct so I'm not sure if that is the Post Office or the UPS Store's fault but something is certainly not working 100%).  The mailboxes are very expensive here, especially compared to the post office, but I mainly pay for the convenience of being able to have things delivered and signed for by UPS and FedEx as I'm rarely at home to accept deliveries.  (There are so many places that refuse to ship to PO Boxes so it is a shame the Postal service can't offer this same service for a much cheaper fee).  My biggest complaint about this location is that the parking lot is always a painful experience to get out of and if it is anytime around 5pm it becomes a nightmare.

Definitely a unique experience and completely unexpected atmosphere in the Bywater. The space itself is a bit of an adventure to find as it is hidden behind a large wall with just a very small sign identifying the place as "N7" which when you open the gate you are rewarded with a very pleasant looking patio and interestingly appointed building complete with a driveway with a classic Citroen in it that transported me back to France for a moment and really gives it a great ambiance. I had expected the wine prices to be more affordable but gentrification has certainly grasped the wine list firmly here.  The canned options are interesting and probably worth sharing with some folks as an appetizer.  The cooked fresh entrees are very small portions so be prepared to do multiple courses and share food more like a tapas experience here which can add the bill up quickly when matched with the wine prices.  The only concerns I have are that the service is slow, the music was too loud and they only have one unisex bathroom for the customers so there can be a wait at times to get into the WC.  I could also do without the "Asian Fusion" dashes they add here and there to the menu but that is just my personal obsession with classic French cuisine and dislike of nouvelle cuisine.  Overall it is an interesting spot for the occasional change of pace to try something quite different from the usual NOLA fare but I probably wouldn't put it on my regular rotation due to the very small portions coupled with the higher prices that make it a poor value when compared to other similar spots more near and dear to mon coeur.

This is the old Sun Ray Grill location.  I would stick more to the grill than the sushi here.  For the price there is better sushi in the area.  The flaw of Sun Ray Grill was that the menu became too complicated as it tried to do too many genres of food and that mindset has continued into this establishment.  They need to focus on making their grill items the best they can be and leave the sushi to sushi joints or dedicate to being a full sushi joint.  They do most things good but with a bit more focus they could do things great.

They have a lot of things on the menu that many other local Chinese places don't such as some dim sum.  The main draw for most local folks here seems to be their lunch buffet.  They might possibly  have one of the most unhealthy selections of food of any buffet in the area as the majority of things are all deep fried but they all taste really good.  The egg rolls here are pretty fantastic and are chock full of huge chunks of goodness.  They also have a great hot & sour soup which they unfortunately never have on the buffet (they only have egg drop and won ton soup on the buffet).  They will often have shrimp or crawfish in the buffet selection and it usually seems there is almost always a spicy bean sauce as the base for one of the entrees.  The menu has a lot of choices and is always is great option at dinner or if you don't want the buffet at lunch.  The food tastes great but I do my best to eat the buffet rarely as you won't live to be very old if you eat it often.

I've eaten here a handful of times and its your basic factory made Chinese buffet items that get reheated for the most part.  The service has always been attentive and they get your drink refilled promptly.  The food just doesn't have a lot of flavor and isn't the best quality.  I probably won't return as the quantity just doesn't get me past the low quality of the food.

I drove past this neighborhood dive joint for years but as it has no visible sign on the outside, other than some neon beer signs in the curtained windows, I had just assumed it was somebody's house.  Well what do you know this is actually a deep cover bar that has a focus on firefighter regalia as the current owner was a fireman.  They have a jukebox and card tables along with some televisions that are usually playing sports channels.  You have to get buzzed in to enter and this is a place that tourists rarely will venture and I've never seen more than a handful of people in here.  The drink prices are a great value and the only downsides are it can be smokey and they often close early by NOLA standards.

I got the burger with the egg minus the bacon and it was a good burger but it didn't knock me out.  The service was a bit slow and I would've tried one of their soups and dessert too but things went so slow I ran out of time to order anything else.  Hopefully they are just still breaking things in and service speed will increase with experience.  The menu has too many pork things for my taste but they do have some tempting offerings and I look forward to returning for some of the other options.

The few times I've been here are when I decide to take out of town friends on an adventure on the Algier's Ferry and this usually ends up being everyone's favorite bar in Algiers.  We usually end up at this bar after stops at the Dry Dock Cafe & Bar, and Old Point Bar.  This is a bit of a small space but they take their British Pub theme very seriously and serve beers in full Imperial pints along with a selection of British crisps for sale.  The last time I was in here there were small children here with their parents so I guess it is also family friendly!

I've been to many meetings at this library and they have some decent meeting rooms that are really more like classrooms.  This is a very large library and they seem to frequently have events happening.  They also have some good things to check out from their collection.  They even have a cafe here but I've never been inside it so I can't really give any opinion on it.  Overall this is a good spot to host a meeting in a classroom style environment or if you need a library this is one of the larger public ones in the area.

This is where everyone local seems to meet up after a nice looong lunch in the Quarter and it is an especially crowded epicenter around the Friday before Christmas and around Mardi Gras time.  It is always generally full and there always seems to be some interesting people in there.  The prices have seemed to be getting way ridiculous over the years and many people have just resorted to grabbing three for one drinks at the Bourbon Cowboy across the street and bringing them over.  They take credit cards but when they are busy it usually is much better to use cash here or you might be waiting awhile.  The bartenders are usually very efficient and get to you rather quickly all things considered when it gets crowded.

Ahhhh It is ok but the cost is too much for what you get on average.  This is certainly nowhere like the size of a sandwich you get at a real New York Deli like Katz's.  They make ok sandwiches but they always leave me hungry and it takes about two to fill me up.  They do have many items that are hard or impossible to find at other locations in New Orleans.  Steins also has a very nice selection of cheeses and beer.  They also have some interesting events.  Usually not my first choice when I'm in the mood for a sandwich but it is pretty near my house so it is good for a quick fix.

Cool diner atmosphere with good prices for the French Quarter.  They offer a military discount which is always appreciated.  This place has a good burger and they offer a lot of breakfast items along with sandwiches, milkshakes and desserts.  Definitely a nifty spot to grab a quick bite in the Quarter that offers good value for your money with friendly service.

If you've been to good night clubs in Vegas casinos this is just so pathetically sad...  They really could have at least made this its own separate area so it would somewhat more resemble a "club" instead of just another bar in the casino.  They have go go dancers in cages but what began with a lot of hype is an epic fail and I hope whoever designed this concept is ashamed of themselves.  It isn't that hard to build a nice club environment inside a casino as you've already got multitudes of successful examples in Vegas of which NONE of them resemble what they did with Masquerade.

Wow the main thing that can be said for this place is HUGE portions.  People rave about the mac'n cheese here but it isn't my favorite (although it is probably the largest serving anywhere and could feed an entire family).  They have multiple selections and rotating daily specials (keep in mind they only have the seafood gumbo on Fridays).  It isn't the best food you will ever taste but it might very well be the largest amount of food you ever attempt to eat.   A good solid place to eat with interesting local characters so certainly a great unique place to visit!!!

This is a real old school man's barbershop.  There are no fancy haircuts here just the standard buzz cut and trim.  They also offer a classic straight razor shave for those times you've had to let the beard grow long or just when you feel the need for a professional job prior to a big event.  This place typically draws boys brought by their mothers and older men as they don't mess around with lots of metrosexual or hipster hair styles.  They know how a man's or boy's hair should be cut in the classic 1950's style and you can have it that way or go pay more somewhere else.  The prices can't be beat and compared to most other places in the metro area its just plain fast and cheap!

Places like this are why I often hate Bourbon Street... Places like this get tourists to do things that give New Orleans a bad rap when its usually the tourists that ain't from here doing the nasty dirty things...  Places like this piss me off when they charge rip off prices for LOCAL beer like Abita Amber...  Places like this piss me off when shot girls don't understand no MEANS no...    They get one extra star just for their 3 for 1 drink deal during daylight hours which are actually a decent deal but once that special ends do expect to get ripped off big time.  Total tourist trap and for the prices you can go to much better and far cooler places.  Actually at their prices it might be cheaper to drink in the rip off tourist trap strip clubs...

This is one location of several of Danny & Clyde's chains that are both gas stations and NOLA food stores offering po boys, muffalettas, hamburgers, and other assorted fare.  The po boys are certainly not the best and the seafood is usually much better than the roast beef.  They also offer wheat po boy bread and offer some optional muffeletta choices like turkey and seafood.  They have some changing daily specials so you can get a very cheap po boy and it will be difficult to find a seafood po boy as cheap as one of their specials.  The other great draw of this place is that it is open 24/7.  They have a nice little self-service computer terminal with a touch screen where you get to put your order in so that any mistakes can be avoided.  This really isn't an enjoyable atmosphere to sit and eat but they do have some tables available.

This is my favorite location of this local chain and offers wood fired pizza, pasta, wraps and salads along with some other specials.  The food is generally affordable and the food isn't great but its consistently good for the most part.
