Unfortunately for this establishment there are so many other fantastic restaurants in this area that I very rarely ever eat here. They have a Chase ATM that I often make use of when in this area.

This is one of the nicer hotel bars in the city and I really like both the Ritz and the Davenport Lounge.  The music is fun and the crowd is more upscale.  The drink prices always confuse me as I get charged different amounts the vary with the bartenders.  Jeremy Davenport is usually the main attraction and he certainly does a great show.  I've been to many events and had many good times here.  Of late on my last several visits the crowd has seemed to be trending much more mature...

The ambiance of Kelley's Village Inn reminds me a groovy 70's restaurant and bar.  This is a very popular spot in the area with their offering of boiled crawfish, crabs and shrimp along with raw oysters and chargrilled oysters.  Seafood is also offered in the fried variety and the softshell crabs are nice.  The menu also offers pizza, pasta, muffuletta, and po boys with one if the best options being Thursday steak night,  They offer a lunch buffet that includes salad bar, pizza, veggie of the day and cobbler.  As a great bonus there is also a nice selection of 80's video games.  Overall this seems like a family friendly neighborhood joint that will have something to make most folks happy at a decent value and allow the adults to enjoy some adult beverages.

The single best word to describe O'Henry's is: BLAH!    I think this place is terrible and this local chain is the New Orleans version of Applebee's or Chili's.  They do give free steaks to people on their birthdays but beyond that I just can't say much nice about the food.  Some people say it is impossible to have a bad meal in New Orleans but the handful of times I've eaten here ALL qualified as bad meals.  The food is bland, boring, lifeless, and has no discernible flavor.  If your just looking for a burger, steak, or chicken tenders go to the nearby GB's Patio Bar & Grill behind Madigan's for a much better meal.  This O'Henry's location is awesome with a great balcony but it is hands down the worst food to be had anywhere in the area.  You can eat generic crap food like this anywhere else in America so do yourself a favor and eat at a real restaurant to enjoy the food that makes New Orleans the special place it is.  If your the kind of person that likes their McDonald's, Applebee's and Chili's then you will LOVE this place so please go here as you won't like real New Orleans food anyway.

I've been slurping noodles at Pho Tau Bay for many years and I've enjoyed all my various versions of pho that I've slurped and gulped down here.  I also really love the jasmine iced tea and many of the other dishes they offer like the tasty little po boys.  This place offers incredible value and is lower priced than just about any other pho place I know of.       The only bad experience I've ever had here is I once likely got a bit of nasty food poisoning here from some of the spring rolls (as evidenced by a friend and I were both in serious pain one day after both eating those here but one time out of hundreds isn't a big deal and can happen in the best of restaurants).  This is definitely a great place to eat and I journey to the Westbank a few times a month for work and I generally eat either here or 9 Roses as one is open on the days the other is closed.  This place can get really crowded so it is best to go before noon.

This seems to be a cool trendy hip place of a coffee shop happening spot in Nashvegas.  The coffee was ok and the espresso was a better choice.  The parking can be a bonus here as you can park for 2 hours for free in the pay lot but you still have to get a ticket.  Very fast service and the staff were very nice.  I'm used to New Orleans coffee so I found the coffee here a bit weak and lacking in flavor as I'm used to the chicory added to our bayou brews but I'm told this is the best coffee in the area.  C'est la vie...

I used to LOVE playing here as a kid... Truthfully if I was still small enough I would still play here as I'm still a kid at heart!  The only difference between men and boys is the size of their toys, right?  Seriously this is a great place for kids to play and an awesome venue for birthday parties.

This is an echo of the long time favorite in this Prytania neighborhood of Kyoto that closed due to the death of the owner.  They have a few of my past favorites from Kyoto like the Chirashi but the execution is not quite up to the same level while the prices here are certainly higher.  Sadly like so many things that were around before Katrina hit that survived and then faded away after the brief revival we had this seems to be a shadow of what used to be.  In the immediate area it is still probably the best sushi in the area but it definitely leaves me longing for what used to be and ain't there no more.

This place is in a bit of a hidden location and easy to miss if you aren't getting gas across the street.  They have a nice concise selection of cookies, cakes, pastries, cake balls and different sized petit fours.  They also have a selection of bottled drinks.  The lady at the counter was friendly and attentive while giving relevant guidance on the various products.  All of the items I ate were appropriately dessert deliciousness.

They have some excellent fine dining options and one of the very best hamburgers in NOLA!!!  They always have great specials and have always given great service.  I have always had a great and tasty experience here and would never hesitate to bring people to enjoy this little gem.  They also have some good drinks and unlike many better known places there has always been space at the bar with very attentive and fun bartenders to take care of you every time I've been.  They seem to always have some creative and interesting dishes going on along with their consistently good regular menu.

This used to be a four star place before Katrina and one of my favorite places to sneak off to eat.  Unfortunately with each move they make they seem to go down in quality.  Their Friday and Saturday buffets used to be AMAZING with some really great food.  I'm not sure if there was a change of ownership or what but the food quality along with the care and pride that used to be evident in the food just doesn't seem to be there anymore.  Some of the dishes they used to always have are no longer present and the ones they still do just seem to use lesser quality seafood and meat than before.  It is still an ok place to go but I don't really go anymore as I'm so very deeply disappointed in how far they have let things slip from how great it used to be.  They still have an awesome bread pudding with an excellent brandy sauce... perhaps my favorite of all time!  I so very much hope and dream they will get back to what they were but I haven't seen any evidence of that on my sporadic visits back over the years since Katrina.

What happened to my review I had posted?  Wow this place is already closed and my old review disappeared?  Well they had an interesting selection of burgers and then they had a great weekly special for 50% off the burgers.  The service was friendly and attentive and kept the drinks flowing.  The food was decent but nothing exceptional and reminded me of less tasty Phil's Grill.  The mac'n cheese wedge was one of the best and most notable dishes here.  I had my doubts this place would make it in this location and those doubts proved accurate so my psychic food powers of restaurants are growing...

I got my windshield replaced here which I arrived at 1:00 and got out at 5:00 because so many people were ahead of me.  Once they got to work on it the job was completed quickly and efficiently.  I get my bill and pay the front desk folks and they hand me my receipt and tell me all I need is that and I have three days to get a new brake tag.  The next day I go to get my new brake tag and I tell the inspection dude that I got a new windshield and hand him the receipt. The inspection dude looks at the receipt and tells me that doesn't work and he has to have the old inspection sticker number and there is a number written on the receipt so I had just assumed that was the number but no apparently not.  So I call the glass place and explain that I need my old brake tag number and they say hold on and then report back that the glass was put in the garbage and the garbage was already taken so they can't help me.  So I get to shell out $25 extra for the brake tag for a total of $49 for just one year.  Clearly somebody here must be mistaken so I send an email to my city council rep to get clarification and get a speedy reply that it would be the glass places fault and my fault for not writing the number down...    So wouldn't the glass place be expected to know as a matter of their typical course of business that they should have a place on their receipt for the old brake tag number?  What kind of absolute scam is the city of New Orleans running with their brake tags that already cost double the brake tags the rest of Louisiana uses that they then setup a situation like this?  Is it any wonder that most people choose to register their vehicles outside of Orleans Parish to avoid this scam that is also accompanied by inspection stations that have terrible hours that don't work for people that work regular work hours.  Does the city not understand that car insurance rates are substantially cheaper outside Orleans Parish and there is every motivation to avoid getting your break tag in the city so thus they are losing huge amounts of money with their asinine system?    So as usual in NOLA the people that follow the rules and obey the laws get the shaft when you could've just been slim shady and kept an old cracked windshield and bribed your way to a new brake tag or just registered it somewhere else like Mississippi that did away with their inspection stickers.  So the glorious new brake tag was somehow changed to go from a rectangle to a circle so our government can accomplish kindergarten tasks of changing shapes while being unable to make the process user friendly for citizens as they continue to waste and steal our money so we can enjoy more pot holes and crime.

If you need a special unique item that screams Louisiana this is your place.  This shop offers such varied merchandise as art, maps, books, china, stationery, toys, jewelry, and gifts etc.  Located in a convenient stretch of Magazine Street the parking is usually easy in the area and there are several other shops and art galleries around the area.

Decent pasta and sauces in a hipster type environment.  I first sampled their food when they were still on Magazine and then tried them a few more times at their new Bywater location.  It really worked better for me at the Magazine location as it seemed to meld so well with the wine bar.  The new location has a lot less charm and aesthetics than their Magazine location but much more space.  The food is decent but I find the portion sizes to be quite too small for me.  You get a choice of several pastas and then several sauces with which to pair with each other.  I suggest either doing a double order or going to Pizza Delicious.

Maximos is good and fresh Italian with a bit of New Orleans thrown in.  They are mighty proud of their grill and recommend a lot of their "fire grilled" items and the fire grilled seafood is pretty decent but not outstanding.  I've only eaten here a few times but I've found that it is pretty consistent and good but for some reason I find myself thinking I'm in an Olive Garden more than a French Quarter restaurant (maybe they went too modern in the design).

I've been here for a wedding and a few other events.  Its an interesting Victorian house and there are some rather eclectic decorations inside along with the sort of spooky "Doll House Museum."  The outside courtyard is a nice space for an event and makes a good wedding spot.   This is definitely a uniquely New Orleans location to host any type of event.

Three stars for the new owners (old owners and Po Boys are now at Tracy's) cleaning the place up substantially and improving the draft beer lines.  Food is probably two stars for the one time I sampled it.  The bar is usually not crowded and it is a nice calm place to grab a drink and watch sports etc.  I've tried the new menu and the food was ok but I've never had a desire to go back and sample anything there again as it was nothing special (I had the roast beef po boy & gumbo).  I will occasionally stop in here for a beer but if I'm going to eat it will be back to Tracy's for the Roast Beef Po Boy probably.  This past St. Pat's block party is the only time in many years that I've actually been able to walk inside Parasol's and order a drink as most of the crowd seemed to be down at Tracy's or on the street so it is nice to have the addition of both bars to spread the crowd out on that day.  If you're in the area you should just grab some drinks at both Parasol's and Tracy's and find the spot that you feel most comfortable at.

The food menu really didn't inspire me much as other than traditional Spanish tapas I'm not that inspired by small plates and a great deal of the food seemed to be some type of ceviche with a Peruvian flair to all the dishes.  The cafe & bar space really seems much more bar than cafe.  They do have some happy hour specials here and the space is still very new so not many people even know about this spot yet with the result that the space is sparsely populated with customers.  The location is a bit off the beaten path but some intrepid tourists and locals might be drawn to escape to this location as it currently offers an excellent space for privacy or introverted reflection.  Overall I'm a bit confused why they called this place Catahoula as that is a very Louisiana dog and Parish which isn't reflected in anyway whatsoever it the food or culture of this cafe & bar.  I'm really not sure why they didn't go with some Peruvian name as this place seems to be all Peru and nothing Louisiana other than location.

For the price it just really doesn't work for me.  You can get better quality food that tastes much better at local places in the area.  You can get better prices on the same beers at other local places in the area.  It is a nice space and has a great set up for watching sports.  The service is really friendly and attentive.  They do have some beers other joints in the area don't have so that would be about the only reason I could think of having a desire for coming here.    Ultimately the sad reality facing this place is that mediocre food just doesn't cut it in NOLA so if you can't bring an "A" game of deliciousness you will fail at scoring high marks.  Seriously just don't even bother with their burger as there are fast food chains that make better versions than this bar chain.  Leave this place to the tourists if you're a local and used to our great NOLA food and our superior burgers.

This establishment is mainly a bar but they do some decent bar food and BBQ.  Their brisket and BBQ sauce are Memphis style with a very sweet sauce that they also use in their beans.  Both the sauce and the brisket at Moby's taste very similar to Corky's to me.  The brisket plate is also a bit pricey here ($15.05 before tip for the brisket plate and iced tea) but you do get a good quantity of meat, beans, slaw, and fries.  Personally I much prefer a Texas style brisket and the sauce here is too sweet for my taste but its still decent BBQ.  The burger here is a nice larger size hunk of meat and you get a choice of regular or wheat bun.  They have a $1 up-charge for cheese which is a bit steep for a bit of grated cheese.  They also sometimes have daily specials and its a decent place to grab a meal in a bar environment.

This is a medium sized Asian grocery that has a good selection of many products.  Their produce is variable and you're never quite sure what you might find available.  I was happy to find my liquid ginsing and royal jelly here which is an herbal infusion I like to occasionally indulge in to make my chi extra strong.  This certainly isn't as large or nice a store as Hong Kong Market on the Westbank and they don't have nearly as good a selection of fresh produce but they do have some things that even Hong Kong doesn't have.  They certainly could take a bit more time to clean the large amount of garbage out of their parking lot.

The food is decent while nothing really has excited me here.  The best thing here is they have campy tiki drinks in big goofy tiki style glasses.  The ambiance is entertaining to me in this joint and it is probably the best atmosphere of any Chinese place in the Jefferson Highway area.

Cash only bar that gets very popular for football games.  They are now serving food here and have some decent bar grub burgers and related victuals.  Thankfully they have gone non-smoking and that has certainly improved my experience of this old joint.  For such an old school place they have maintained it very well so it doesn't have the typical grungy grime that most old dives do in NOLA.  Generally a nice spot to grab a cheaper drink in a classic NOLA bar.  This is yet another of the bars that claims the notoriety of having had Lee Harvey Oswald as a frequent customer.

They have a nice happy hour here with 2 for 1 and an interesting menu with some unexpected surprises on it.  This is a very interesting bar that looks like it is a combination of a ski lodge meets a lumberjack camp.  I found my phone service to be very weak in here so they must have a pretty old school thick ceiling and roof so maybe this could even serve as a nuclear bomb shelter.  The bartenders here were really friendly and attentive as they made sure to keep my happy hour very happy indeed.  There was a nice crowd inside having a good time and then there is also a small patio to the side.  This is a really vibrant and interesting area of Nashville and there are several great spots to check out along with the nearby nice park area.

In Jefferson Parish the Irish and Italians combine forces and do a combined St. Patrick's & St. Joseph's Day parade at the Louisiana Irish-Italian Parade.  This parade is a larger event with traditional floats, truck floats and marching clubs that follow a route on Veterans Memorial Boulevard in Metairie.  Throws include beads, cabbage and other vegetables.  I'm not the biggest fan of parades on Veteran's but this event can be a decently good time.  The crowds are usually one line thick so it is pretty easy to navigate around.

My past review of this establishment seems to have mysteriously disappeared...  This is an amazing French Bistro that as its namesake indicates offers crêpes along with other traditional bistro fare.  They offer good seafood options along with a delicious selection of expected bistro options.  They offer nice desserts along with good cheese selections.  They have an affordable selection of quality wine, liquor and beer.  The ambiance is quite simply magically fantastic while the service is usually on point they do have hiccups occasionally depending on the server.  They also are open a bit later than some other options these days and offer a Sunday Brunch.  This is certainly a marvelous place to bring a date for an enjoyable evening.  Fun Fact:  I don't particularly care for crêpes and I've tried them in multiple places and flavors in France but I've never actually tried them at La Crêpe Nanou.

This is a huge wholesale food warehouse.  Most of the items are bulk purchases but they do have a respectable selection of things you can purchase as single items.  You need a business license to get a membership here generally and they do have some great prices on many items.  Half of the store is a gigantic walk in cooler and they have all sorts of vegetables, meats and seafood.  Many people put on the provided cold weather gear to walk into this chilly side while I love it in my shorts and t-shirt and would love to set up my bed and just take a nap in here.  They also have a great selection of frozen items on this side.  This is a really fantastic place!

This place is located in strip mall on Airline but they do have some nice Chinese exterior architectural elements to set it apart.  The service has always been decent here and the food is generally good.  You typically get good value for your money here as the portions are large.  This is probably the best Chinese restaurant on all of Airline.

Johnny Sanchez is the newest branch of the family of Sanchez eateries and he has teamed up with New Orleans own Chef John Besh. Offering a selection of taquería offerings that take a few spins outside of what New Orleans other Mexican establishments offer with such items as squash blossom tacos, lamb neck enchiladas and steamed masa cake. the menu is concise while being both familiar and exotic at the same time. Drinks are expensive here with the small house margarita being $9 and the cheapest beers start at $4.50 and go up from there. Two tacos come in an "order" and will cost $8 per order but you need at least 2 orders for a meal.   Great service with fun ambiance but I hope they have a nice happy hour with better drink prices. You get a complimentary jar of green salsa and a jar of red salsa (both of which I found extremely tame on the spice scale) along with a metal bowl of corn chips with a few fried plantains thrown in.  My experience with the chips and salsa leads me to believe they need to rethink the salsa jars that aren't the most balanced items with their attached lids open so they easily tip over.  I also got a lagniappe guacamole dip that was most appreciated.  The goat taco is some of the best goat I've ever eaten while the fried fish (red snapper) tacos were as good as most other places in NOLA.   Four star food and service with overall three star rating for weak drinks and high prices. I liked my experience here but at a price of $29.63 (before tip) I didn't think it was worth nearly the price of a weekday lunch at Commander's Palace for 4 tacos and a margarita so I'm looking forward to another great Besh happy hour special.  Overall good food, fun vibe and decent margaritas (I've had better, larger and stronger) but really this is an expensive option for Mexican food and drinks.

The main draw of this place is the really large patio; while the inside isn't all that great and is rather cramped.  During game days this place attracts a mostly older, rowdy, loud crowd with a good mix of other ages drawn from all over the neighborhood.  They have food here but I've never sampled anything.  The service has often been VERY slow here at the inside bar while the outside bar seems much faster (even though it is usually more crowded outside).  They have a HUGE space behind this bar with lots of parking and an occasional volleyball area.  The bathroom situation is sometimes not adequate for the number of people that can gather on game days, so that can result in quite a wait, so they really need to add more bathroom space.  The super patio is the main reason to visit here so if it is a nice day outside and you're in Mid-City stop in and enjoy the space.

Some things are good here and some things are less good here.  The ambiance is fantastic-classic-New Orleans dive bar/restaurant.  They have some daily specials and a pretty good selection on their regular menu.  I often find the seafood options lacking and usually not a good value.  They are pretty skimpy on the shrimp and oysters whether on a po boy or a platter.  I've never had a really memorable meal here so generally I think I would suggest just stopping in here for a drink to enjoy the space and go somewhere else to eat.

This is a diner style joint in Fat City that offers breakfast and lunch items all day.  They have an interesting selection of items with a definite slant towards pork love.  They seem take a bit longer to get your food out than most other area diners but they cook it right in front of you.  Overall this is a decent spot for the diner genre and for breakfast fans you should be more than happy with their substantial selection of items.

Passable mediocre burger at an expensive price.  The volcano burger caused no taste eruption in my mouth and bored my palette to death.  Fast food ambiance but they still want tips for providing zero service.  Many better burgers for equal or lessor price in the area.  I doubt I shall ever return.

I used to eat in this location frequently when it was Byblos and they have certainly made some cosmetic changes to the interior.  It is MUCH darker inside to the degree that I would say its too dark and they could definitely turn up the lighting.  The pizza wasn't great and wasn't bad but I probably wouldn't ever get it again as there are just better choices I like much better like Theo's.  The size of the pizza is perfect for two people to share but they definitely don't load you up with ingredients.  The lasagna here is just really embarrassing as they just put one slice of cheese on the top of the stacked noodles and meat and obviously just reheat it.  It wasn't the worst lasagna I've ever had but it definitely isn't worth more than about $3 and definitely not worth what I paid for it which came out to $21.80 with an iced tea and tip.  I think I can get better pizza and pasta from the grocery deli so I probably won't be back to eat in this joint but maybe I will drink in here.

This place is usually ok and a decent place to hangout to see some good local music.  Sometimes they get some stranger bands that draw lots of hipsters and then it gets uncomfortably crowded and a lot less fun.  The biggest issue here is that they have very limited bathroom facilities which makes for a big problem when this joint gets crowded.

This place has nice drinks and decent food and many folks from the area seem to frequent it.  My first experience with this place was many years ago during Carnival time when a much older lady who frequents this place and is known as "Hot Mama" burst up into the bar and looked at me and said, "I'm Hot Mama and I've got a tight pussy!" as she pulled her shirt up and flashed me her rather wrinkly boobs.  That is a Carnival moment that actually surprised me and I'm very difficult to surprise!  They have a pretty good burger and roast beef po boy here but I can't recommend the view that Hot Mama offers.

I came here with a group of people (and by people I mean all women that I work with) during one of my random and irregular Wank workdays.  This place is located in a giant metal building which doesn't generally excite my taste buds and makes me think I'm going to a tractor auction or roller rink.  The inside is a cafeteria line type set up that is very much like a super sized mall food court set up.  The portion sizes here are very large which is a plus but the flavor/quality of the food seemed to be about on par with a Sbarro's in a mall somewhere.  I had the lasagna and a couple of slices of different pizzas (because people/women never finish their food so I got extra).  The food was ok but it just really gave me 1980's mall flashbacks and I started looking around for valley girls.  If I'm trapped on the Wank around this area and need some cheap huge portions this might be the place to go but it is low down on my list of preferred pizza and lasagna joints (does anybody know where I can get some parachute pants?).

This place seems to constantly get worse all the time.  I have vague recollections of when this place bordered on being good but that was a very long time ago.  I sometimes get emails about some really good drink specials that I'm tempted to go sample but my last food experiences have really burned me on wanting to ever return to this place.  Ownership must admit that it is far past time to call Gordon Ramsay!!!

Some very nice folks running the place that were very passionate about their food.  They never seem to be very busy so it should be easy to grab a table here most of the time.  The food is overall pretty good when done correctly but sometimes they seem to get inconsistent with less optimal results.  Some items seem to be better executed at other area places like Mona's and Shawarma On The Go to my taste but your experience may differ.  They do have some things that are just a bit different than most of the other Middle Eastern places so vive la différence and give this place a whirl when you want something a bit off the normal experience.

This is your basic no frills dive bar in the Quarter that is slightly off Bourbon BUT right across from Pat O's so you always get a mix of locals and tourists boozing away.  I've never had a great time here but I've never had a terrible time here.  This is just an "ok" place to go grab some drinks when you want to escape the crowds of Rue Bourbon or Pat O's.

This is one of the great music and dive bar venues of New Orleans.  A great night is to begin at Jacques-Imo's and end it early in the wee hours of the morning at Maple Leaf.  This is also home to the Krewe of Oak which parades in full splendor in August and Mardi Gras season.    This isn't a place where you're usually going to sit down or relax to "watch" a show (just like Tips).  This bar is for interactive folks who will be dancing and getting their groovy funk on in a crowded sea of people all smashed together having a good time.  When it gets crowded, like it often does for good shows, it might even take a little while to get your drink so plan ahead and if you frequent the place they get really good about knowing what to serve you.  The great thing about Maple Leaf is that the shows start late and end early in the wee hours of the morning.  The gross thing about Maple Leaf is how smokey it can get in here and I hate nasty cigarette smoke!  The bad thing about Maple Leaf is that when you have to work the next morning after a Sunday, Monday, or Tuesday show your head often really pounds (as you vainly attempt to remember what happened to your great idea you were going to just start drinking water and then some vague memories float up of stopping in at Snake 'n Jake's that you attempt to block out) and you then discover you're mighty sleepy so always remember to take a nice nap ahead of time!

Yelp editors have some serious accuracy and comprehension issues.  I entered the original business entry for Bayou Wine Garden but for some completely incompetent reason the Yelp editor that reviewed my listing changed it to a duplicate entry for Bayou Beer Garden even though I already have a Bayou Beer Garden listing.  I contacted them about their mistake and the now doubly incompetent Yelp staff left the listing as a duplicate of Bayou Beer Garden and after further attempts at getting their mistake corrected they just made my review of Bayou Wine Garden an updated review of my listing of Bayou Beer Garden.  Yelp IQ at the HQ is not impressing me at this point...  Mid-City's new premier wine destination brought to you by the same Krewe that brought you Bayou Beer Garden.  An amazing patio with an outside back bar (which connects with Bayou Beer Garden) along with the large front indoor bar offering wines on tap.  The beer selection sucks but you can walk easily next door to Bayou Beer Garden to take care of that issue.  The food is significantly upgraded from the offerings at Bayou Beer Garden and they offer gourmet cheese, artisan sandwiches and house cured meats that will go well with the wine.

This place was fantastic when it first opened but as the popularity of Frenchmen Street increased both the quality and service here had an inverse reaction and decreased.  They still have some items that are good on the menu sometimes but the output from the kitchen has gotten so inconsistent I just don't bother anymore.   They still have potential but the potential waves up and down so much it just isn't worth the effort to me.  They seriously have to establish AND maintain some consistency or they just have lost all credibility with me.

This is a pretty cool bar with some good food and most of their menu was done by the J'Anita's folks with many of the old favorites, like the St. Chuck Duck, returning.  The location, on St. Charles Ave, has a great ambiance and they have a good beer selection.  They have a 25 cent raw oyster special for happy hour which is great.  Some of the sandwiches are really expensive for the small size (St. Chuck Duck will hurt your wallet for just a sandwich) but they are very tasty and I really like the fact they continue serving food late into the night.  They have a small patio porch on one side and a larger patio area in front that are enjoyable on nice days.  They are still in the "breaking in' period, as a relatively new place, and still have a few bumps with keeping enough things on hand as they have been out of a few menu items on some of my visits.  This is overall a great little bar to hang out in and grab some above average bar food.

This place is always really busy and you usually need to schedule an appointment as they will not typically have space for walk-ins.  I've only been able to book appointments on Saturdays which isn't my favorite day to get a haircut as I'd rather be doing other fun things.  Overall it's a decent place that is better than most of the other places cutting hair in the area that I've tried since my barber retired but I really miss my barber.

The Avenue Pub has an extensive selection of beer and offers many beers not found anywhere else in the area.  Avenue Pub's beer lines are MUCH better than most of the other establishments in NOLA with the possible exception of the Bulldog.  I don't think this place ever closes as I've been here past dawn and closer to noon a few times.  I used to frequently eat late night J'anita's food in here but I haven't eaten in here since J'anita's moved and Avenue Pub started doing their own food but I hear the food is still good.    The location of this bar is fantastic on St. Charles Ave (and bonus points for being within a reasonable walk from my house).  The two story building is a classic New Orleans experience with balconies and a patio in the back.  The interior also has its own unique NOLA ambiance with lots of interesting internal architectural features set off by all sorts of kooky "additions" of various "art" that have been collected over the years.  I would probably come here more often but they charge a lot more for their beer than most other places in the area.  I'm all in favor of places making a profit and I'm certainly willing to pay more of a premium for some of the unique and hard to get beers they offer but their prices on our local Abita and NOLA brews are too expensive so I wouldn't drink those here.  They have some very hard to find, high quality, and very high alcohol ales and beers that are really nice except they serve them in under 12oz glasses at premium prices.  I like to enjoy a few of their uber brews but I would like to be able to mix it up with some more affordably priced local beers.  So your best bet is to stop here as a short pit stop to sample a couple of super quality beers then go elsewhere (like across the street to the Blind Pelican) for your local beer fix to get a much more affordable and market price.  The Avenue Pub is the main choice to get your uber quality beer fix in NOLA and probably the entire South.

I've been dragged here a few times for karaoke.  I'm not the biggest fan of karaoke but if I'm being dragged off somewhere to do it then I will do it to the best of my super awesome ability to belt it out!  I've never been here when it has been crowded and I've had to get a taxi to finally escape to where there were actually people as my friends won't ever leave.  I get bored pretty quick in here and have a limited karaoke shelf life as once I've done my performance and put so much energy into it I just don't have much left to hang out with just 5 other people while they keep on and on doing karaoke til dawn!!!  If you want a bar nearly all to yourself to karaoke this is your place.

Hello 1980's!!!  My very first visit to this place was when I was in 8th grade and after a VERY long interval I returned for my second visit this past Saturday for lunch as they are moving locations so I wanted one last view of the old spot.  It still looks and sounds just like it did on my last visit so that was sort of a cool flashback!  My one and only Hard Rock Cafe shirt I owned during the 80's was also from this location although I have been dragged to other locations across the country and world.    It was, very surprisingly to me, very crowded at 2pm in the afternoon when I arrived for lunch and it was an older looking crowd of folks that probably were young back in the 80's and still think it is cool to eat at a Hard Rock in every city you visit.  I admit I also briefly entertained that thought myself in the 80's but now I think it is about as cool as eating at a McDonald's in every city you visit.  I sat at the crowded bar and Wayne, my server, really was outstanding and kudos to him for providing some of the best service I've had at a bar in a really long time.  Unfortunately the side of the bar I sat at had a funky and sour dirty dishwater smell so that was a negative.    The menu is completely different than it was way back when on my last visit and they definitely have a total corporate chain and tourist trap marketing science down to a well honed art!  I got the burger which really is a great burger that is very large and filling.  I thought the burger was fairly priced for the large size but charging $2.99 for iced tea is highway robbery!  I was also going to order the apple cobbler but when I returned from washing the hamburger grease off my hands in the bathroom somebody had stolen my seat!  It had been a long night/morning and I needed more nap time so I wasn't in the mood for any discussion with an idiot tourist over stealing my seat so I paid my bill and left.  Overall the service and burger were four stars but the funky smell and rip off iced tea price reduce the rating by one star.  The tourist stealing my seat irks me but that was the tourist's fault and it did cost the restaurant added profit if I would have eaten their cobbler.  The place is definitely a tourist trap so this was most likely my last visit at this location and it will probably be a very long time, if ever, that I visit them at their new location as there are just too many better places to eat than at a chain in New Orleans.  The outstanding service by Wayne was impressive and that alone might give me some motivation to return at some future point.

Ok just as a disclaimer I'm not the biggest fan of Tex-Mex as I got really burned out on it after Katrina, when I lived in Austin for a year and half, and had to eat it for nearly every meal.  That being said I ate enough of the stuff to definitely know what is good and what is not.  I also need to confess I'm absolutely terrified of the Kramer painting outside the men's bathroom here!    The food is definitely 2 stars and the bar might get up to 3 stars (not for the quality of drinks that are average at best) but based purely on the fact the crowd is generally pretty nice with some decent looking ladies working there.  I would certainly recommend just avoiding eating here and just hang out at the bar or on the patio to drink some decent (but not great) margaritas or better yet just stick to the beer.

Before Katrina this place had an AWESOME ladies night where ladies drank EVERYTHING FREE.  This brought in an excellent assortment of nice looking women and really made this a fantastically fun spot to be at to kick off the night before heading to the now defunct TwiRoPa.  Unfortunately like many things this special has not returned to previous levels and this bar just doesn't have the energy and fun like it used to.  They still have very attractive ladies tending the bar and they have decent prices on drinks.  The food here has always been pretty solid and sometimes they have even ventured beyond the standard bar grub to borderline gourmet food.  They have a good jukebox here with lots of Sinatra and some games.  I rarely get here anymore though as I do so miss those old times that are not forgotten...

This place is usually alright and generally seems to average pretty fresh food.  They are probably the most expensive sushi place in the entire NOLA area and I'm not really sure they are worth the price most of the time.  They have SOME items that are worth what they charge but overall it is often not worth the time, trouble and expense of a special trip to eat here unless you are already in the CBD for something.  I can't say that I've ever had anything here that spurs me to crave returning so I very rarely eat here.

I'm really not the biggest fan of fast food and I'm definitely not a fan of chains.  Some chains do put out decent food and sometimes every few years I will indulge in some of it.  Chick-Fil-A was a place I used to love to eat back when malls were cool in the 80's.  I still think they have one of the most fantastic fried chicken sandwiches and the pickle they throw on there brings out some extra zing of flavor.  I also had my first experience with waffle fries at a Chick-Fil-A back in the 80's and those things are also pretty damn skippy tasty.  I once worked with a young lady that loved Chick-Fil-A so much she ate it EVERYDAY for lunch for the three years I worked with her and when she finally had a kid I was amazed it didn't have feathers and cluck.    This location is way more convenient than the one in the  Lakeside mall and their drive through seems to be eternally busy.  I've actually never even been inside this place and I've only had food from the drive through here.  I can count on one hand with plenty of fingers left over how often I ever eat here in any given year as I'm not that into fast food but I do enjoy the tasty chicken here.  I also think it's great the owner has values that he stands by and he isn't afraid to run his business by his values.  I'm glad we still have some semblance of a free market in this country and the right of free speech where people can agree or disagree and if you like nice fried chicken you can eat it or not.  God help us when the PC thought police lunatics take over and force us to only eat fried tofu and only engage in group think with anybody that disagrees with them being swiftly sent for "recycling" to fertilize more soybeans to make more tofu.  Remember kids PC is EVIL and being non-PC is way COOL!

Pascal's Manale specializes in Creole Italian dishes but it's main focus is the BBQ shrimp (that they claim to have invented).  This is my father's favorite place to go in New Orleans and I like it rather a bit myself as I have been eating here for a very long time.  When you first walk in they have an awesome oyster bar (probably one of, if not the best, old school oyster bars in the city).  You walk past that to find the host and you are then seated in one of two dining rooms (which used to have lots of great old photos but the building suffered extensive flooding during Katrina and all the stuff that survived is now on display in the bar area).  They had a slow and painful rebuilding period to get their level of service and consistency back after Katrina but it seems they are back to firing on all cylinders again.    They have a great turtle soup and gumbo and finally they have brought back their lunch specials.  During lunch they have a BBQ shrimp po boy (for the cry babies that can't handle peeling their own shrimp) but you can't get that at night so get ready to peel and enjoy the messy ecstasy with your cute little bib if you decide to dine at night (as that is part of the joy)!    I've had nearly everything on the menu and I've enjoyed it all.  One of the great things about this place is that it still seems to largely be off the tourists radar and almost always easy to get in without reservations.  This is a great place to have a really nice lunch in a classic New Orleans setting or an enjoyable dinner with friends.

Coops is really a good restaurant that just looks like a bar and they don't play around with the food!  This ain't no pretentious limited menu "Gastropub" as they have a great full menu with full servings at a fair price!  Coop's probably has one of the finest examples of shrimp creole I've ever sampled.  They have an extensive menu that also includes some great po boys and other NOLA fare.  The gumbo is usually just "ok" so I usually skip that.  The one item they fall far short on is their burger and fries as it is one of the worst to be had in the French Quarter.  Coop's is also frequently rumored to have some of the best fried chicken in the New Orleans area but we keep that kind of talk quiet as we don't want tourists finding out ;)  Coop's generally serves food until pretty late / early in the AM so it is a great place for a later dinner.  I've enjoyed everything I've ever eaten here (other than the burger) so it is definitely a great place to check out for lunch or dinner.  They have some things I still haven't sampled, as I always seem to crave the shrimp creole too much, but I must use some discipline and expand my sampling!

Its all Elvis all the time so like it or leave.  This is generally a pretty cool place and has a blue collar vibe to the place.  The prices are a bit more than I would expect in a place like this.  I got really turned off about this joint when they put Obama stickers on all the beer taps.  I'm all for you supporting your candidate and all the joys of democracy but I don't think a beer tap is the place to put political crap like that.

This is a healthy vegetable focused joint that throws a bit of meat in some dishes but offers almost everything with a Vegan option.  I'm a carnivore and like more meat than they feed you here but this joint has pretty decent food that can give you a healthy high.  If you're some kind of mamby pamby lightweight that can't handle our NOLA rich foods and need your "light and healthy" fix then this place will shut your whiny mouth up!  So next time you hear somebody complaining about "too much butter," "too rich," "all fried" or "too heavy" then send them here so I don't have to hear about it.  Now that we've taken care of the hippies this is also a great place to go when you're in the mood for something a little bit different and most of the food has some good flavor profiles so this is a refreshing spot that whips up some food you won't find anywhere else in the area.

Ok just as a disclaimer I'm not the biggest fan of Tex-Mex as I got really burned out on it after Katrina, when I lived in Austin for a year and half, and had to eat it for nearly every meal.  That being said I ate enough of the stuff to definitely know what is good and what is not.  I also need to confess I'm absolutely terrified of the Kramer painting outside the men's bathroom here!     The food is definitely 2 stars and the bar might get up to 3 stars (not for the quality of drinks that are average at best) but based purely on the fact the crowd is generally pretty nice with some decent looking ladies working there.  I would certainly recommend just avoiding eating here and just hang out at the bar or on the patio to drink some decent (but not great) margaritas or better yet just stick to the beer.

This is probably the most authentic Thai place in New Orleans and all of the different food I've had here has been very tasty.  Some things on the menu seem overpriced for what you get and service is sometimes slow.  Overall I've always had a good time when I've eaten here with groups or on my own.  For what the tasty soups cost I wish they gave you larger servings.  I always get soup, sometimes one of the tasty salads, and a selection of entrees.

It's definitely not much of a grocery store market but more of a small indoor vending booth mall.  There are selections of various foods and drinks available along with a few other specialty items.  It definitely seems to be a hangout for the gentrification crowd and it serves as the Whole Foods of this area (minus having a great produce selection like Whole Foods does).  This is definitely a spot to visit if you want to try several different types of items all in one spot.  The prices seem out of line to me and trend to being on the expensive side.  It is a beautiful building and a pleasant environment to enjoy some food and drink.

Wow the food has just reached rock bottom here and I just will never be back.  Such a very sad and heartbreaking thing to see such a formerly fantastic place change into this terribly awful low quality place.  The price has drastically gone down for the Friday and Saturday night buffets but even then you are overpaying for imported Asian fish and maybe the small shrimp are local but wouldn't surprise me if they were imported too.  Literally every item on the buffet I sampled was just awful and so far degraded from what was once fantastic here that it is just officially now in the category of Ain't Dere No Mo' to me.

Whoa the new Martin's takes up the length of the entire block!  It now seems more like a supermarket sized institution instead of a mere wine cellar.  They have a large parking lot adjacent to the building and another smaller one across the street.  This was always my Martin's before Katrina as I used to live in the neighborhood.  I've greatly missed having the deli Uptown and I'm very glad its back but I would be lying if I said I didn't still miss the original building.  The new building is very spacious and modern looking (which I'm not the biggest fan of "modern" as it looks more like a joint that would belong in California, Texas or Metairie than Uptown NOLA and in fact from the front it looks a LOT like the Metairie store but I imagine most folks will like it) and it has a lot more seating for the deli than the old location or the Metairie location.  A new feature has also been added with a separate counter with a napkin, silverware and condiment "guard" to make sure you retrieve those items in an orderly and proper fashion.  They have lots of staff on hand with plenty of cash registers at the deli so there was never any significant line while I was there and everything seemed to move efficiently.  I hope they are going to be putting chalkboard menus up behind the deli counter like they had previously and still have at the Metairie location as it makes ordering a bit easier for the consistent menu items.    Martin's is consistently a great place to eat and shop for gourmet food items (with a great cheese selection), wines, beers and liquor.   In the past they would've rated a four star easily but the stiff competition and sheer increase in the selection and quality of other bistro/deli's and gourmet food vendor's in the city has brought the standard up higher so for price value they lose a star as there are some great lunches that can be had in the area for about the same price as just one of Martin's sandwiches.  I'm a fan of Martin's but I'm also a fan of many other delicious places in the city so I'm still going to frequent this establishment but just not as frequently as I used to.  Overall I'm glad its finally re-opened and it makes things finally seem a bit more like they are returning to the glory of my nostalgic pre-Katrina days.

Small little space that has been many different types of restaurants over the years and most recently settled into Tex-Mex.  The star of the show here seems to be their enchiladas and they do have a nice selection of enchiladas and I might go so far as to say these might be among the best enchiladas in the New Orleans area.  They also do their beans in a very unique way that is different from all the rest of the NOLA area and even most other places I've eaten at in Texas and they are most similar to what they call Borracho Beans in Texas but with a bit more flavor and more vegetables added while seeming to have a bit more liquid in them.  Overall quit a nice little spot to sample some fresh Tex-Mex that is a bit different than most other options in the NOLA area.

This is a small shopping mall in the Garden District quite near my house.  They actually have a parking garage underneath the building so that makes it easier to park here than a lot of Magazine Street these days.  Honestly the only business I've ever patronized here is the coffee shop, Still Perkin.  There are a random assortment of other shops and offices here that I've never had a need or desire to go to and it mostly seems like women's shopping with nothing of interest to a grumpy ole dude such as myself.  Maybe they could add a gun & fishing store to excite me one day... haha who I'm I kidding this is Orleans Parish and they can't do anything like that as they would rather all the tax revenue go to Jefferson Parish.

I've only been here for events and never stayed in the hotel.  This is a nice hotel and it has some nice features.  They have a smaller bar area than most New Orleans hotels which still works for them as they seem to have the space they need.  The conference areas are a bit tired and worn looking and could use some new furniture and the rest of the space looks well used.  They have some good but not great food (on the New Orleans scale) they do for the catering at large events so that probably makes it great food anywhere else but in NOLA it is pretty average food.  If you are looking to book an event I would certainly suggest taking a look at the exact space you are booking as there is some range in the conditions of the event rooms here and for the rate being charged you might be able to find a nicer space at a similar price and use that leverage to negotiate a cheaper rate for the more "lived in" looking rooms.

This is definitely more of a bar than a restaurant.  The beef pasteles was ok but not a lot of food for the price and too much on the bland side for me.  The taco also suffered a similar fate as it was not a good size for the price.  The chips and queso were really not very good as the chips were too hard and the queso tasted strange.  This is the only place in the NOLA area offering the pasteles option that I'm aware of so that does give it some unique points but overall the price just doesn't make it a good value and the flavor doesn't really encourage me to want to eat here again.  I might be back just for some drinks though.

I'm a big fan of local fresh sourcing and focusing on seasonal produce and MiLa generally does some very good things with this idea.  I've always experienced outstanding service here with very knowledgeable servers, rapid refills, and constant monitoring to ensure my table had everything it needed.  The vibe is a bit too trendy and modern "hip" for my taste and I prefer the classic old atmospheres that New Orleans is famous for.  My favorite dining experience here, so far, was doing the sampling menu which was overall very good with my only disappointments being some attempts at molecular gastronomy with some foams and another chemical experiment for dessert (I'm just not that big a fan of the whole molecular fad and I never want any kind of foam involved in my dining other than beer foam floating on my beer).  My main disappointment in the tasting menu and the food in general at MiLa is the small portions which really don't give good value for the price (and when I say small I mean I had to go get a second dinner as I was still really hungry after eating the tasting menu).   I've also spent some time in the bar at MiLa and they do some very creative and flavorful cocktails that remind me of some of the things Green Goddess comes up with yet in a bit of a different way.  MiLa is certainly is a place to watch and the chefs certainly have the potential to get up to a five star status with a few tweaks and a bit more consistency (and portions that will actually feed me).

This is where most of the better quality national stores in New Orleans are to be found.  I've also attended some decently fun events here such as "Sippin' in Seersucker."  They also currently have the only full service food and beverage movie theater in the New Orleans area.  I primarily have utilized this location for their parking garage and the excellent Brooks Brother's store.

I'm not the biggest fan of chains and generally I think in the New Orleans area we can get far superior food at a much better price than most national chains can provide.  It has been several years since I last ate at a Cheesecake Factory so I caved in and gave the new Metairie location a try (mainly because I was hankering for some cheesecake).  I've eaten at quite a few Cheesecake Factory's across the country from Nevada, Texas and Georgia and they are all pretty consistent as you would expect a chain to be.  As a chain comparison the Cheesecake Factory's food and ambiance is better than an Applebee's but less so than a Houston's. My theory on chains was proven as for my lunch portion of the shepherd's pie, iced tea, and a cheesecake the cost was $25 so I could've just gone to Commander's for a way better experience at a comparable price (that would've also included 25 cent martinis at Commander's so that bonus blows Cheesecake Factory out of the water).    The shepherd's pie was a hamburger patty broken up into the gravy and vegetable mix with mashed potatoes put over the top and while it was ok it was one of the least flavorful shepherd's pies I've ever had and probably one of the least well executed dishes that I've ever had at a Cheesecake Factory.  I had the chocolate mousse cheesecake and it was decent but I've definitely had better cheesecake locally and from Whole Foods.  The real price shocker is that the iced tea was nearly $3 which is ludicrous for plain unsweetened tea.   Their are some definite positives here as they do have a very large menu with a selection of items that should make most people happy.  The staff provided great and friendly service and were literally tripping over each other providing attention to my needs.  Clearly their reputation has proceeded them and there is frequently a large line waiting to be seated at this location as at many of their locations I've seen around the country.  Other than the wide selection of cheesecakes and some tasty burgers I'm not sure what would really draw me here on a regular basis and put up with the crowd.  Personally I prefer the food at local establishments and find that at the Cheesecake Factory's price point I can have far better dining experiences elsewhere.  The good news is that now out of town tourists and suburbanites can now have a place to go to and leave my local gems unsullied by their uncouth and overly casual habits so I hope they enjoy waiting in their line.

I hate to even do a review on this joint as I want to be selfish and keep the secret to myself and not have hordes of tourists take over this authentic old school NOLA neighborhood diner.  This place is truly one of the very few remaining authentic and unchanged neighborhood dining venues of its kind in the NOLA area.  It is literally like stepping back in time here and that holds true of the prices too as they offer a good value for your money. Tessie's offers a menu of amazing New Orleans classics and refuses to cave into Yankee political correctness as they still proudly offer their WOP Salad on the menu (if you are going to show up and complain like a snowflake about it then keep your PC cultural Marxist ways with your local ANTIFA potluck dinner and stay away from my WOP salad or I will put on a MAGA hat to trigger you... after I go and purchase one first then wear it to trigger you).   They really aim to please the customer here and offer a lot of choices and variety within the selections.  I think this might be the only restaurant I've ever been to that actually offers you a choice between thick cut or thin cut onion rings!  They also give the option of a regular size burger or a large size burger.  Daily specials are offered along with delicacies like soft shell crabs (available in multiple sizes), pasta specials, fried chicken, soups, sandwiches, po boys, burgers with seafood and non-seafood choices all abundant so with so many options available there should be something to please almost anybody.   The only negative about this place is the parking is very limited and it can be challenging to find a spot in the area around lunch time when this place is popular.    Overall this is just a classic in every sense of the word and just a pure delicious slice of old NOLA neighborhood life that gives us the amazing gift to see how awesome just a regular joint for normal folks in a neighborhood used to be.

Ahhh Rendezvous I had some really great times there before and right after Katrina.  This was a super popular place where I used to know the majority of people in the bar.  Unfortunately the crowd has shifted and I rarely know anybody in this place anymore and it has gotten a whole lot more smokey in here.  As a non-smoker I often find it difficult to stay in this place for long.  They do keep the A/C at a nice cool temp and keep it nice dank and dark (the way I often like my dive bars to be).  They also have some pretty good specials on beer and the bartenders are usually very on top of things with good service.  As an extra bonus they often offer FREE Nirvana Indian food on Sundays!!!

This is a good place for a quick and easy lunch in a typical Metry strip mall (I really love those strip malls...NOT).  They have a good selection of appetizers, sides, salads, sandwiches, wraps, entrees, and desserts.  I like their po boys, gumbo, and some of their seafood and Italian entrees.  The really weak point here is the burger that I would probably never get again.    Two really big negatives and pet peeves I have about this place are that:  1) They only have mustard in the stupid little packets so if I'm not getting it to go they should have a squirt bottle of it like they do for the ketchup so I don't have to deal with the stupid little packets!  2)  They use "fountain" tea for the "fresh brewed" tea and that stuff is disgusting!  I just don't really trust anyplace that won't take the time to brew their own tea!  One really nice aspect of this place is that it opens at 10:30am so if you need to pick up some food earlier then you don't have to wait til 11am like most places.  Most of the prices seem to be a good value and they also have a catering menu which seems to be fairly priced as well.

I'm not a coffee shop person and the only reason I ever willingly end up in one is when I need an internet connection to get some work done.  The internet connection here has never served me well and in fact it has epically failed me.  For a coffee shop I guess this is a relatively cool joint and the coffee is better than at some other joints.  Lucky for me I like beer much better than coffee so I can just go to the Rendezvous and use their WiFi instead and get more work done while I drink beer.  Its cash only which also makes it inconvenient.  Minus one star for terrible WiFi!

This was the chain that brought Tex-Mex food to most of the South outside of Texas. In the early 1980's you might have gotten your first exposure to Tex-Mex at one of these joints.  I had my first taste of a margarita and tequila at Cuco's (at least at the time I thought it was tequila but I'm not sure they really use tequila in their margaritas).  Most of the food tastes like they have been storing it in a deep freeze from the 80's and just reheating or re-frying it.   This place was everywhere like Applebee's back in its day but now this location and one in Hattiesburg are the only one's left I know about.  Sadly enough the one in Hattiesburg is probably slightly better than this one.  I don't know how much more life this place has if it doesn't do some serious changes.

This is a convenience store and very small grocery with a kitchen in the back slinging food.  The quality and flavor of the po boys is really more of a two star but the very cheap prices bump them up a star.  This is probably one of the cheapest places in the city limits to get a po boy.  They also have some ambiance and character inside with the best collection of beer signs of anybody in the city.  The roast beef is pretty forgettable and not worth getting.  The seafood options are generous portions but the batter could really use some pepper or Tony Chachere added into it as the shrimp, oysters and soft shell crab really end up tasting quite bland and flavorless.  This store is really small and stuffed full of things so its really best to call ahead and have your order waiting for you to pick it up as there isn't a lot of standing room to wait and nowhere to sit and eat.

This is a bar with a WW2 Spitfire airplane theme.  Decent atmosphere here with an interior setup that reminds me of Molly's at the Market with front bar and back area with pool tables.  Add it to your Decatur Street pub crawl and see how you like it.

Ok I've had much better fried chicken in many places and in NOLA Fiorella's, Lil Dizzy's and Jacques-Imo's have far better fried chicken than here.  I really find the fried chicken here rather bland.  I did really like my butter beans as those were very well done.  This place seems to have suffered from becoming too well known and isn't what it used to be.  The prices and sometimes long waits, due to tourists checking it out, really have made it a place that isn't worth a return visit for me especially with so many other places with better chicken (at least to my taste buds).  The butter beans here are mighty fine though.

The seating is mostly outdoors with some seating inside that they don't seem to want you to use for some reason.  The menu at lunch is pretty simple and my server didn't understand the confusing rotisserie shared plate options so I never got an understanding of what was going on with that.  I had the lamb french dip sandwich which was ok taste wise but for the price it was on the small size especially considering it didn't even come with any sides so not a great value.  The dinner menu looks more interesting so maybe that will be worth a try at some point.

This place is famous for their Sunday free Indian food meal.  The free food seems to start around 7:15pm but if you arrive around 6pm you can have the full temple experience.  They have around 2 hours of chanting, music, dancing and various ceremonies that take place before a teaching lecture.  You can definitely have an interesting cultural experience before the feast and just come prepared to sit on a carpet for quite a large part of it.  Very friendly and happy folks that are welcoming and highly encourage you to participate even if you have no clue about what is happening.  The food is Vegan and free so it is hard to beat the price and mine was served with a nice lemonade.  There were actually far fewer folks that arrived for the food line than I would have thought and the line moved really fast.  Overall an interesting cultural experience to learn about how other folks do things and the great diversity that exists in NOLA.

This a nice French style bakery on a convenient section of Magazine street.  They have nice breads, pastries, sandwiches, quiches, and sometimes pizza and other daily specials.  This place seems near to bakeries I've been to in France and is a nice place to get your baked goods or grab a quick breakfast or lunch.

GB's is right behind Madigan's Bar and the menu here is some basic bar type food with a nice red meat focus.  The main draw is that they USUALLY offer the best burger in the Carrollton area and some decent steaks.  Most of the time I've had the burger here it has been very good but there have been a few times that it was off for whatever reasons.  I've also had some very bad service in here occasionally but usually it has been decent.    This is just a NOLA neighborhood bar type atmosphere that is usually not too crowded and not at all trendy so you can actually enjoy eating your food (with the added bonus of a patio).  I would say that the burger is far better here (and better priced) than the other nearby options of Tru Burger or Cowbell.

This is a chain so that always gives a lot of NOLA folks a pause as we like supporting our local joints.  I have been to several Korean BBQ places and the concept is very similar here.  I opted to really blow it out for the holidays and did the "Supreme" all you can eat menu.    So the all you can eat menus here are a total lie as it is really all you can eat in 90 minutes (they list the time requirement on the menu).  That is also a lie as the service is VERY slow about bringing the food and then you also have to cook many of the items on the BBQ which adds a lot of time to that 90 minutes that don't involve eating.    To kick things off I tried to order an iced tea but here for some reason they told me they don't have the "machine" to make iced tea so each tea is separate charge.  So pretty much 100% of other restaurants in this price range offer unlimited iced tea so that is just total balderdash and no machine is required to make fresh brewed iced tea other than some hot water, tea and container to store it in.  They were out of the Spicy Tuna Volcano and I wasn't informed of that until I tried to order it so they should certainly inform you when they are out of things like that on the menu for the price they charge.  The meat BBQ dishes were all good, even though it took them about 20 minutes to bring them out to start on the BBQ, and the other options of small plates, soups etc. were good to decent.  The highlights of the experience for me would be the salmon, the filet mignon and toro beef.  The desserts were also a disappointment as the sorbet and ice cream were both rock hard when brought out so it took some thawing time to be edible and they are totally something to just skip and  eat more meat instead.   Overall for the price, time limit and slow service scam to work into their time limit I think the Korean BBQ options are an all around better deal for your money.  The overall service experience was a 1.5 while most of the food was around a solid 3 other than the desserts that were around a 1 and then the lack of refillable iced tea is a big fat ZERO.  This is an alright  experience to try once but I doubt I will be back with so many time wasting tricks they build into their "rules" about the process of eating here.

This might be the best Chinese food I've had in the NOLA area.  Their Mongolian beef is one of the finest examples of that dish I've ever had.  The front of the restaurant has roast duck and pig on display.  They make some amazing Chinese vegetable dishes but I wish they offered them in smaller portions as more of a side item as I want to eat all of them on every visit which doesn't work well if you are eating solo or just a couple of people.  The service is friendly and efficient and while the location isn't the fanciest it is conveniently located near the Westbank Expressway.  They also offer one of the best lunch values anywhere with their $7.50 daily lunch special.

This is just a review of the bar and I didn't stay at the hotel.  From the outside the hotel maintains the 60's design elements until you get to the ground level where they throw a raspberry beret onto it and go full hipster.  The interior of the hotel lobby/bar area has had a lot of effort put into the design with some of the elements being overdone.  The bathroom for example has a square shaped toilet which looks interesting but the form does not fit the function.  The prices for the beers here are above my tolerance levels along with the selection not being very large.  It is an interesting place to visit and check out but certainly won't be on my regular rotation as it is way too hipster for me.

This is a nice little Middle Eastern spot right next to the Crescent Market halal grocery.  They have some nice fresh food here that I might guess uses some ingredients from next door at the market but I might be wrong or I could be right.  The portion size on my kabob plate seemed a bit smaller than most other Middle Eastern places I've eaten at in the area but there was plenty of good flavor involved.  Service was a bit on the slower side and it took a bit longer to get a refill on drinks than I would like even though there were only a couple of other tables with guests.  Overall it seems like they have one guy working the front of house and then some folks in the kitchen so they have some good food but are stretched a bit then with service.

This is an old school restaurant that has a good selection of items on the menu.  I was happy that they had prime rib on the menu for the night but then I was told they had sold out but then I got lucky as actually my order got put in before they ran out.  Then my luck ran out again as when I got my steak it was much more of a well done than the medium rare I had ordered but at that point I just soldiered on and ate it.  Seems they need a bit of kitchen help... Our server was very enthusiastic and seemed a bit young but he provided great service despite his inexperienced appearance.  Overall this seems like a nice spot for a good meal if you get lucky and have a night with good staffing when they are firing on all cylinders.

Best place about this dive diner is that it is 24 hours, next best thing is that it is cheap for Bourbon Street & the French Quarter, next best thing are the tasty burgers. I have been to several Zea's but I had never been to this one before.  This location is probably the least favorite experience of any Zea I have visited.  The building was generally not as nice as the other Zea's while the service was exceptionally below the average of other locations.  The food was up to par in the flavor department but my tomato-basil soup was barely filled and I have never had such a small serving at any other Zea's.    Overall I hope this was just an off day for this location but I would certainly be hesitant to return to this location as it was so below what I have encountered at every other Zea location.

This is a pretty tiny festival compared to some of the others but it brings some heavy hitters in for food vendors.  The food has always been among the best... of course I do love oysters so I might be a bit partial.  This event has been growing bigger and better every year so enjoy it before it gets too popular.  The main negative about this fest is that the time of year they have it makes it really hard to bear the heat for long periods of time.

I''m not the biggest fan of NOLA Brewing beers but I do love beer.  Typically at the bar the NOLA beers cost at least $1 or more than Abita beer so I love some Abita and usually go for that option instead of NOLA beers.  With that caveat being said I have to say they do a really kick ass brew tour here if you're into drinking a lot of beer and getting to sample all the different brews NOLA makes.  The tour here is far longer and more enjoyable than what you get to experience at the Abita Brewery tour but it isn't free like the Abita tour and you do have to pay $5 which gets you a glass to drink out of and take home.  I definitely prefer the NOLA Brewing tour's superior format far more than the current Abita format as I was able to have a whole lot more fun and meet more interesting folks.  Sadly I heard NOLA Brewing is planning on changing their current format at some point soon and they will possibly begin charging per beer so enjoy it while you can!

Amorino has a nice selection of ices and gelato along with macaroons.  With Sucre closing we are low on joints offering macaroons so another option is nice and the macaroons here are not as good as Sucre's were but I have definitely had worse in the area.  The coffee here is also decent and had acceptable flavor.  What is less nice is the service and the ordering process where you pay first and then get served which seems disorganized and they forget to give you items from your order (they might want to switch to order and get items and pay at the end to make it easier on their staff to keep up with everything).  The prices are also on the expensive side which would be expected due to the prime tourist location of this establishment.  Speaking of a prime tourist location this place does often bring in quite a crowd of tourists so you should plan on waiting in line for awhile unless you luck out and catch it between the waves of dessert craving tourists.    Overall this is a decent place with a comfortable environment to enjoy dessert except when it gets too crowded.  Likely I will rarely if ever return to this establishment as I will be sticking with Angelo Brocato's and Creole Creamery far more often due to the logistics of the location of Amorino.  The location alone should ensure this establishment will be around awhile and be quite profitable for the owners.

Impastato's is owned by the brother of Sal of Sal & Judy's fame.  Some of the dishes are very similar to what you can get at Sal & Judy's but some are very different and still very tasty.  I've enjoyed all of the food I've had and there are still many dishes here I still want to sample.  The service has always been very excellent and the servers have made some very good food and wine recommendations.  Impastato's has a very unique atmosphere with an impressive collection of sports memorabilia, worthy of any sports bar, decorating the entire restaurant (and the owner seems to always be in the restaurant and happy to talk about his passion for collecting every time I've been there; and there might even be a few well known coaches or athletes dining along with you).  There usually is live music and you might have to chase a violin player away but that can add to the fun.  Certainly worthy of a visit and an interesting and great place to take a date.

This smaller offshoot of the main Haydel's on Jeff Hwy. isn't quite up to the amazing status of the original but it does have some of the famous Haydel's great offerings in King Cakes, Kringle Cakes, Russian Cakes, Doberge Cakes, cheese cakes, cookies and a more limited selection of some of the other offerings the original has.  They also offer their treats in different sizes than the original location so you can't get the smaller snack size squares but larger cuts instead here so it is less practical to get a sampler box of multiple items. This is still a fantastic NOLA place to visit if you're in the mood for sweets and need to get your dessert fix satisfied and you don't have time to drive out to the original location.

Yakuza House specializes in handrolls and also has developed a following for their omakase.  This is a tiny spot on Veterans Memorial Boulevard that has grown quite popular and it is often packed so you often need to get a reservation, get her early or come at off times.  They get most of their seafood from Japan and they offer some interesting items.  The omakase experience is a lot of food and they give a nice variety of items.  I found my  handrolls on my first visit to have a lot more rice than other handrolls I've had which seemed to overwhelm the flavors of seafood while the single handroll I had during my omakase experience was much better balanced. The prices trend more on the expensive side compared to other area sushi restaurants and their omakase is substantially more expensive than other area sushi joints.  I also tried the tempura ice cream dessert which was alright but I wouldn't get it again as it really wasn't my thing.
