The service has always been friendly and efficient and they tend to take good care of you.    Overall they provide an nice experience while the prices make this a spot that many folks won't make regular visits too although they seem to have plenty of regulars that love the food and can afford the premium cost.  To my taste there are several other sushi joints around town that I like more that cost less but many folks seem to be big fans of Yakuza House so try it yourself and see what you think.  My video review of Yakuza House is here:  https://youtu.be/EPxVXOQu-cM

This place seems to have the ambiance of a fine dining establishment while the focus is on slinging burgers.  The menu at Three B's is pretty concise with the main focus being burgers and other sandwiches.  The previous occupant of this space was Lakeview Harbor (and I will fully confess my attachment to that place with many fond memories in the space and it saddens me that the space ain't dere no mo but they have re-opened in a new spot) and to my preference Lakeview Harbor actually had a much better menu with steaks and other options in addition to burgers so it seems strange to me Three B's has no steaks.  This place seems designed more as an upscale bar with maybe a focus to take the overflow from the next door Velvet Cactus so maybe that will be their target demographic.  The concept here seems confused as they have done a nice job of creating an upscale feel to the interior along with being a decent wine and cocktail bar so you would expect a better menu than the basic burgers and other sandwiches they offer.  From the presentation of the place you really have high expectations for the burgers here and while the burgers are good they just aren't as good as they should be for the price and the expectation the venue creates.  Ultimately this is a nice bar to enjoy but when it comes to their food there are just better burgers at better prices around the city.  My video review is here:  https://youtu.be/EM9MXrig58w

This is a pick up to go type BBQ joint.  They are attached to a seafood restaurant, Castnet Seafood, which I believe to actually be a better choice than the BBQ option here.  The beef BBQ at Walker's doesn't seem to be an area where they shine to my taste preferences which I prefer the Texas Hill Country or Kansas City style.  I was rather pleased when I saw they had burnt ends but sadly they ended up tasting far more like pot roast (instead of the excellent local example available at The Joint) and the beef is served with a Memphis style thick sweet molasses sauce (and Memphis has never been noted for their skills with beef BBQ unfortunately).  The sides were a mixed experience as the cole slaw had nice spice kick to it while the potato salad was terrible to the point I couldn't even eat it.    Overall for beef BBQ fans like myself this location just doesn't deliver and there are far better options for those of us that choose beef while for you pig and chicken fan folks you might find what you want here.

Howling Success is a fundraiser for the LA/SPCA  that features 30+ landmark restaurants and businesses serving signature dishes, specialty hors d'oeuvres, drinks and the chance to bid on unique auction items.  The theme this year was superheros and guests were invited to dress in the costume of their favorite hero.  They had a nice selection of food and drink and the mood was calmly festive.  Yelp had a sponsor table and Elites were invited to attend which was a really excellent and valuable perk.  The Yelp table also had the most interesting costumes and was probably the most festive group at the entire event.  The band was passable but there was definitely room for improvement in the music area.  Elites that missed out on this event definitely missed out on a lot of great food and drink and they were definitely needed to help us spice it up a bit and show the other folks a few new choice dance moves.  This was all for the puppies and who doesn't love puppies!    Yeah and for those cats too... yeah cats...   I'm sticking with the puppies you can play with the cats!

Somehow I had never visited Vinnie's Sports Bar & Grill until recently and as it is hidden away in a strip mall on the Westbank it is easy to miss if you don't know to look for it.  I recently heard a rumor that they had good burgers here so I decided to check it out as I'm always looking for the best burger in the USA.   Vinnie's Sports Bar & Grill offers 35 beers on tap and advertises they have the "Best Burgers in Town."  Vinne's has been a Westbank locals favorite restaurant staple for over 25 years and during normal times they offer pool, video poker, darts, trivia night and live music.  They definitely have big burgers here and I enjoyed my sautéed mushroom burger with Swiss cheese with a great side of onion rings that they are nice enough to serve with a side of delicious comeback sauce.  I was also really impressed with how large a selection of items they offered on their menu so I definitely intend to make a return visit for one of their amazing looking steak nights and to sample their roast beef po boy!  Check out my video review here:  https://youtu.be/6wD_AnN3Tg8

This is the iconic New Orleans park with the statue of Andrew Jackson on his horse honoring the memory of the Battle of New Orleans against an attempted British invasion during the War of 1812.  This park is also framed by the landmark St. Louis Cathedral.  This park is one of my earliest memories as a child and I've often walked inside it throughout my entire life for various activities ranging from work to pleasure.  Many people consider this location the heart of the city and there always seems to be activity centered around this area.  The importance of this area can be seen in that local New Years celebrations are focused here and crowds congregate just like they do at Times Square in New York.

This is a national chain and as I live in New Orleans we in that area are generally not the biggest fans of chains but some chains do rise above the usual disappointments that most of them offer.  The only other location of this chain I have seen was in Austin, TX and it was nowhere nearly as impressive looking as this location so I didn't bother to even consider eating at that location.  I am a member of a professional group and the Nashville chapter has their meetings here at lunch.  The building housing this restaurant is really a beautiful place and for extra bonus points they also have a parking garage behind it where you can park for free (which with parking in Nashville often being a challenge to find these days getting LOTS of parking for FREE is awesome).  The interior is equally as nice as the exterior and is a very pleasant place to pass a good time. The location is easy to get to from most spots in central Nashville. The food here is average good for many of the items with some of the items being very good.  This seems to be quite a popular spot in the area and usually seems to attract a lot of customers.  Overall this is definitely an easy and enjoyable place to grab a good lunch or dinner in nice surroundings.  Overall I would say Maggiano's Little Italy, Houston's and Ruth's Chris Steak House are the top chain restaurants I have ever eaten at in the USA so while I usually don't make recommendations for too many chains this is certainly a good option for Italian food of the American style.

This is some of the best BBQ in New Orleans.  Smokin Buddha Bbqieux  and Whole Foods are the only other Briskets available in New Orleans that I've had that come  as close to being as tasty.  I really like their brisket and I know a bit about BBQ (from spending considerable time at many of the best Texas BBQ places and attending the Memphis in May World BBQ Championship for many years).  This would probably be a three star place in Texas or Memphis but on the NOLA scale of BBQ it is among the best.  FYI for those that have never been or haven't been to the new location.  There is no table service and you have to order at the counter all the way in the back.  You can also call ahead to place your order.  On my most recent visit this past Saturday night, even with the Hogs for the Cause event going on, there was a line of about 40 people going from the cash register at the order counter to out the door and around the sidewalk.  This place is on the tourists radar now so do your best to either get there early or call your order in.  Hopefully it won't be packed like it has been BUT from past experience expect a crowd.  The benefit of calling your order in is that you get to just go to the bar to take care of it so you can have a tasty beverage while paying for your food instead of standing in the normal order line.   I suggest avoiding the chicken as it isn't bad it just isn't great.  The beef brisket is outstanding and ranks as one of the best in all of NOLA and is done Texas style.  The ribs and pulled pork are also favorites of many people and those are Carolina style.  You can get up to a three meat combo plate and I highly suggest you make brisket one of your meats.  The sides aren't all that fantastic but who cares as it is all about the meat!  The mac 'n cheese is pretty weak so I would generally advise against that, the potato salad is ok, the slaw is alright, and the beans would probably make most people the happiest, and finally the salad comes with a pretty tasty salad dressing lots of people seem to like.    They generally give you really good portion sizes (much more than nearly anywhere else) and again the sides are "ok" but much less impressive than other places.  It's been getting crazy crowded and longer waits the last several times I've visited.  I've also recently noticed a lot more people calling in their order ahead of time even for dining-in.  I live in the Garden District so this place is certainly a bit out of the way for me but it is worth the trip.

This place seems to have the ambiance of a fine dining establishment while the focus is on slinging burgers.  The menu at Three B's is pretty concise with 6 small plates of various options, 3 salad choices and 2 bird sandwiches.  The burger was alright while the bun was strangely cold. The previous occupant of this space was Lakeview Harbor (and I will fully confess my attachment to that place with many fond memories attached to it and it saddens me that the space ain't dere no mo) and to my preference Lakeview Harbor actually had a much better menu with steaks and other options in addition to burgers so it seems strange to me Three B's has no steaks.  This place seems designed more as a bar focus to take the overflow from the next door Velvet Cactus so maybe that will be their target demographic.  For myself I just don't see myself coming back here as there are just better burgers at better prices around the city.

A Classic Creole New Orleans establishment!!!  I love Arnaud's food and atmosphere and I ALWAYS have a fantastic time here.  This is probably one of the better (if not the best) Sunday Brunch locations in New Orleans.   I always wear a suit (and that is what everyone else typically wears in my groups) but, unfortunately,  it does seem the dress code is getting more slack to accommodate the increasingly sloppily dressed tourists.   I have eaten here frequently over many years.  I also attend many seasonal group functions here, during the course of our busy New Orleans social calender, and we typically begin with substantial time at the French 75 Bar before preceding to our table where there are many traditions and fun additions to the usual dining experience (be warned: the bread has a "fold" in it that makes it look like a certain part of the male anatomy and during holidays my boisterous groups usually end up throwing a few of those around; seriously whoever came up with baking bread like this is hilarious so make sure to notice it).  I've always found the prices to be very reasonable for the quality of food and quantity of drinks that are enjoyed in this most excellent venue!!!

Most of us in NOLA are not big into chains and especially this close to the French Quarter but for a chain this place fills a niche that they do well at.  This is definitely one of the main spots to eat mass quantities of meat in the NOLA region and is the best example we currently have of the Brazilian style steakhouse genre.  Service can be over the top with being so attentive and frequent that it becomes nearly intrusive with going overboard with changing your plate out far too many times.  If they pull back on the aggressive plate changing the service experience would be at a great level.  I find the meat to be acceptable but on average trends towards too overly well done for my liking and they do attempt to accommodate your level of preference.  The meat is brought at regular intervals but the servings were on the small sides at times.  The food bar contains a decent selection of items if you want to expand your feasting beyond the carnivore realm and they have even more meat on that in the guise of salmon and ham.  It is fairly priced during lunch while a bit on the pricey side at dinner and overall I think I would generally just prefer a nice steak but this establishment does have its moments when you are just in the mood for some debauched gluttony of meat.  Tip:  The best meat I've had here are the lamb chops.

Hana has some pretty good food and the largest regular sushi rolls of anyplace in the NOLA area.  They are not scared to give you very large (for sushi) pieces of fish in this place.  The one consistent problem here seems to be the service that always seems to be slow and your drink always seems to wait way too long to be refilled.  If you sit at the sushi bar (like you should in most sushi places) then you get a special little noodle lagniappe.  The rolls here are mostly pretty basic and often seem a bit bland when compared to some other NOLA sushi places but the quality is always consistently good and the portions large (for sushi).  This place is a bit hidden away in the river bend and can be a nice change of pace place to enjoy a good sushi experience.

This is a small and intimate little wine store with a decent selection of wine and bubbly.  They also carry a selection of liquor and beer.  This is one of the nicest sections of Prytania Street so that makes the location of the store quite convenient if you need to pick up something to bring to dinner at one of the restaurants in the area or the Prytania Theatre.  This is also right down from St. James Cheese Company so you can do a nice cheese and wine shopping pairing with that propitious synchronicity.

Some of the prices here can be much steeper than what you will find at Academy or online but the firearms sold here do come with an extra warranty on top of that offered by the manufacturers.  The customer service can be lacking at times with some of the staff while in contrast their affiliated shooting range at the nearby Shooter's Club the staff are always pleasant to deal with.  They offer concealed carry classes, FFL transfer service and consignment for used firearms.  They also have a selection of accessories which include holsters, magazines, ammunition and law enforcement items.  This store probably has the largest selection of firearms available in Jefferson and Orleans Parishes.

Copelands is good stuff for a chain restaurant. If you have to eat at a chain this is usually one of the better options to find out there among the Applebee etc. etc. options that exist out there.  Copeland's actually still has really great biscuits unlike Popeye's which for some inexplicable reason decided to replace their formerly great biscuit with a hockey puck.  They also have some above average dessert offerings here that deserve some investigation.  They definitely can make some great New Orleans style fried seafood and if you are outside of Louisiana and there is a Copeland's and another New Orleans style restaurant the Copeland's will often produce a more authentic version of New Orleans style food.

This is a great old dive bar on Bourbon that has lots of great history.  I've had many good times here and wish I could remember all of them but they have a deadly purple daiquiri here that causes memory loss if used improperly (which I have done many times).  There is always a good mix of locals and tourists so there is always someone interesting to meet in this establishment.  The street in front is a common stopping place for the mule carriages so if you sit outside do expect the lovely poo odor of days past to waft their perfume around to add to your olfactory experience.  One of my favorite spots on Bourbon St and usually away from the crazy crowds that build up the closer to Canal St. you get.

The new location is finally open!!!   Some old favorite pieces from the old store made it over to the new location to add some nostalgia.  The new space is large and inviting.  The coffee and beignets are as good as they always have been.  This spot is only short of parking so that will be the only challenge you might encounter.  My video review of Morning Call is here:  https://youtu.be/3UngE0W8VgU

If you want the full Nashville tourist experience on Broadway then you have to stop in for a visit to Robert's Western World for the old school vibe and classic honky tonk music offered up here.  There are plenty of newer and more "modern" spots to visit on Broadway but there are few of the old classics like this left so make sure to visit and see a little bit of what Nashville used to be like before the population explosion.

I love this place and the jovial owner is usually there to greet and speak with you when he is not too busy.  This is most Spanish of all of the Tapas places in NOLA and since the owner is from Spain that probably helps.  Chef Laurentino recently built a patio in the back that will be very nice to enjoy in the Fall.  My only complaints are:  1)  The amazing Lasagna has not been added back to the menu and it is the best lasagna I've ever had!!!  2)  If the owner, Chef Laurentino, isn't around the service can sometimes be poor which is unacceptable.   They have the most tender and amazing calamari I've ever had anywhere in the world and I've never had anything but great food here.  It can be a bit more expensive than I would like to eat here alone but if you have a  group (and this food is meant to be enjoyed with others) it becomes cheap.  I've had many great times with small and large groups in here.  The sangria pitchers keep the excitement going along with the exquisite use of garlic.  I LOVE the garlic soup and want to just have an IV of it in me always.    They have also just announced a happy hour special where you can get a free small tapas with your drink between 4:30 and 6:30.  Another good update is they are FINALLY taking credit cards at long last!!!  Good Food & Good Times!!!!

This is probably one of my least favorite fests as it is held at the absolute hottest time of year in New Orleans and it is usually doesn't draw many people so that lowers the fun vibe.  It is a free festival and it is still New Orleans so you can definitely still have fun at this event just don't expect it to be on the same level as most of the other local festivals.  There are a limited number of vendors as the limited space doesn't allow for many.  If you're a hard core Jazz fan that doesn't like crowds and doesn't mind the heat you can really enjoy yourself.  I have to concede that my least favorite fest in New Orleans is much better than the best festival most other places :)

I was really impressed with my first visit to Pedro's as they really ahve made an impressive space inside their strip mall location.  I wasn't even aware they were a chain as they gave such an impressive impression on my first visit.  This Greater New Orleans Mexican restaurant in Harahan has become noted for their giant pina colada, Mexican martini and margarita offerings along with their food which many folks say is the best Mexican food around.  Pedro's is one of New Orleans newest Mexican food restaurants and has quickly become one of the most famous Mexican food establishments as they have great lunch specials and offer fun happy hours which has helped make them one of the most popular Mexican restaurants in the Greater New Orleans area. Pedro's is located in a strip mall but still has become known as one of the largest and nicest looking Mexican restaurants in the Greater New Orleans area along with hosting live music.  They have an extensive menu with enough items to please nearly any taste. Many people consider this some of the best Mexican food in New Orleans and they provide a lot of food at a good value along with a lot of fun. Even though Pedro's Tacos & Tequila Bar is a chain restaurant that has multiple locations in Louisiana, Mississippi and Florida and I usually hate chains they do such a great job here it is hard not to love them and they also have live music.  Overall this is an enjoyable place that puts out some good food and great drinks.  My video review of Pedro's Tacos & Tequila Bar Mexican restaurant is here:  https://youtu.be/c98ooWSbZZs

Gonzo's Smokehouse & BBQ is absolutely the best BBQ in Louisiana I've ever had. Gonzo's specializes in central Texas style BBQ which is one of my favorite types of BBQ. This is some of the top food Louisiana offers in the BBQ category so you definitely want to try out the great food here. This is the best BBQ restaurant in the New Orleans area and all of Louisiana along with giving many of the famous Austin, TX BBQ joints a run for their money.   I have eaten BBQ at many of the top places in the USA and most of the top rated spots in the Texas Hill Country/Austin, TX area and I really loved the food here. For BBQ this is the best place to eat Louisiana BBQ and Gonzo's deserves to be crowned king of Louisiana BBQ!  Gonzo's has amazing brisket, fantastic turkey and their brisket smashburgers are super juicy and they have so many more meat options to try.  Gonzo's also takes a lot more time than most other BBQ joints with their sides and they really make some fantastic tasting sides. All of the sides I've had have been fantastic with my favorite so far being the sweet potato casserole which was more of a dessert!   The only negatives about this place is they are only open for Friday lunch and then they often get a line for the single day they are open.  Gonzo's also does catering so keep that in mind for your events.  Overall you just simply need to make sure you get to Luling on a Friday before 11:30 to get a place in line and eat this amazing BBQ!  The good news is that the line typically moves quite fast and you can also order carry out and they let the carry out folks get their orders before the dine in folks.  My video review of Gonzo's Smokehouse & BBQ is here:  https://youtu.be/4JQLXLGMCyE

I mainly come here for the raw oysters and everything else is the typical "ok" deep fried seafood that doesn't cause any long term flavor memories for me but I still like to eat it occasionally (they do have some other stuff on the menu too but I just don't recall it even after years of going).  I much prefer stopping in here to eat than at Acme and I think many of the items, like the gumbo and po boys, are much better here (BUT the portion sizes at both places is waay too small).  I really enjoy looking at the poor tourists across the street waiting in line and still waiting when I'm leaving after eating while they still just stand in line (I really hate lines AND darn you Yelp there are starting to be lines at Felix's now too).  So if you need an oyster fix you will have a much more rapid experience here (and it is certainly worth a visit) and then if you want you can still go get in line across the street.

This is a location of the Bear's family of eateries that are also in Covington, Slidell, and Mandeville that is located behind Genaro's Bar on Metairie Road.  They are noted all over the Greater New Orleans area for their roast beef po boys.  Their roast beef has more of an au jus than an actual gravy and they seem to use more of a sub bun than po boy bread so it is more of a roast beef sandwich than a classic po boy.  I do like the flavor and texture of the meat and it certainly is a good roast beef sandwich but it is a zero to 1 napkin sloppy level and I like my roast beef po boys dripping with thick gravy and want to have to use multiple napkins to clean myself up after diving into my food.  They offer several more po boy options with my other favorites being the oyster, shrimp, and BBQ beef.  They also have some very good burgers here with my favorites being the blue cheese and the "New Orleans Burger" that is topped with their roast beef debris.  The service here is friendly, quick, and efficient and the atmosphere is definitely a dive type environment.  They have a lot of nearby parking here which is a big bonus for making this place very convenient.  This is certainly a good spot for a quick and filling lunch or dinner.

Before Katrina the place where I worked often had me bring folks "out" to visit places and this was one of the places we would visit.  Most people I brought here found this place not very interesting and I can remember doing this tour as a child and being slightly bored by it myself the first time.  There is some cool antique furniture here that I would love to have in my house along with some interesting historical items but this is still a very brief tour.  The Cabildo and Presbytere both offer more interesting tours with many more things to see but adding this location to your visit to the Cabildo and Presbythere is a convenient, cheap ($3) and quick addition if you want to check it out.

This is probably the oldest sushi and hibachi restaurant in the New Orleans area.  They are consistently good and they are probably the best hibachi in the metro region.  From the outside this place doesn't look like much but the interior is much nicer than you would assume from the exterior.  Personally I think the hibachi is better than the sushi and I generally prefer the sushi at Kanno but Shogun does have some great spicy sauces they use on their sushi.

I've eaten lunch here several times but haven't been inspired to sample their dinner yet.  The food and service are good but this is one of my least favorite Italian restaurants in the area.  It might be better at dinner but for lunch the food just doesn't make me as happy as other Italian places.  The servers have always been pleasant and they play some fun old school music.  Overall for the price there are many places I would rather eat but this place is near my office and will suffice if I'm in a hurry.

This is a small neighborhood po boy joint offering a total of TWO parking spaces.  Most of the business here is call in and taking it to go but they do offer a few tables for dining in.  They offer a generous selection of entrees, po boys and burgers on their menu along with seafood gumbo on Fridays and other rotating daily specials.  They are one of the few joints that still offer trout on their menu which is a great option for those of us that love trout and look at catfish with disdain.  The prices here are also very reasonable and you get good value for your money.  The lady that usually runs the cash register and takes orders is a hoot and it is pure entertainment just to interact with her and watch her take orders from other customers.  They have a nice big burger, meatball po boy, roast beef po boy and their trout is nice.  The only thing that I don't like is the lack of real fresh brewed iced tea and they only offer fountain soda (with that fake iced tea) and bottled drinks.  You should certainly do yourself a favor and pay a visit here for a po boy or lunch special.

Before Katrina the place where I worked often had me bring folks "out" to visit places and this was one of the tours we would take.  This was the least popular and quickest tour that we would take folks to as this is basically just a building without much to see inside.  There are a few interesting architectural details and they will often use the space for some exhibits but as a stand alone tour it doesn't offer much which is reflected in its admission price of FREE.

They do some alright po boys and other food here.  The hot roast beef po boy is relatively sloppy (in a good way) and has good gravy.  They have a nice old school ambiance about the place and the staff all seem very friendly.  The food has always come out quickly and I've never had anything bad here but I've never had anything great here either.  The best thing about this place is that it is very consistent and the worst thing about this place is that it is not easy to get here so you really need to know where you're going to find it.

The first time I tried this place I went solo and that just doesn't work with the huge portion of the flat bread serving "tray" they put all your food on.  If you've never had Ethiopian food it reminds me a bit of Indian but has some unique flavors.  They don't give you any silverware and you are expected to eat with your hands and use more rolled up flat bread pieces to pick up your food.  I always cheat and get the tea so I can use the spoon they give you to scoop stuff up onto my bread.  Very very filling so you probably want at least 4 people just to take care of the bread serving tray.  This isn't food I would (or even could) eat all the time as it fills you up so much but it certainly is nice for a change of pace.

This bar certainly used to be a four or five but has suffered some setbacks over the years.  As a life long preppy fellow I appreciate the generally more dressed up nature of the crowd here but unfortunately too many poorly dressed, hipster type, and non-preppy folk have taken to crowding this bar over the last few years.  It has seemed to be making a comeback lately and I do hope those that don't like preppy folk and don't understand that our "dressing up" is just what we wear everyday for work AND fun so they will probably be much happier at our great dive bars with their sloppy unprofessional looks.  It is a great thing to be sloppy and go to a dive bar sometimes but it is also great to have a place you can go in your work clothes... well actually I go all preppy all over the place and I really like wearing a suit in Snake n' Jakes!!!    Overall Monkey Hill is a very comfortable bar and they do some good drinks with good service.  The crowd has been very variable over the last few years so it is hard to predict what you will find until you get there.

This location is still just teetering along with inconsistent service and often being very slow to get orders out.  The French Quarter location is much more on top of their game than this location and literally I could drive down and find a parking spot and walk to the Quarter location and get my food faster than I did on my last visit to this location so to say I was forced to wait an inordinate amount of time for my order would be an understatement.

This is an "ok" place for men's business clothing and formal wear.  They have some deals and a few rip offs here depending on what you get.  I'm not at all a fan of many of their wedding rental options as I've been forced to wear some atrocious looking combinations of things for weddings where I have to assume the groom let the bride pick out the grooms outfits with all sorts of horrible color schemes (unless you're doing a Mardi Gras or 70's theme wedding the only appropriate colors for formal wear in my book are black, midnight blue, white, and maybe grey unless you're Scottish and have a tartan).  When being fitted here I've often had to send things back as they were done in the wrong size even though I know my measurements.  They do make good efforts at customer service here and they certainly do well on the initial stages but sometimes they drop the ball in the execution.  This is definitely not on par with  Perlis, Brooks Brothers or even a Jos Bank but it can be a good resource for last minute things you need in a hurry and they often have decent prices on many items with a good selection.

Alright to good sandwiches, salads and breakfast type items like bagels, scones, brioche and quiche.  The coffee, tea and other drinks are now self-serve and on my last visit they seemed to be out of fresh coffee and  had older lukewarm coffee that tasted watered down and blah.  They used to serve great fresh coffee in a French press brought to your table but now the coffee is stored in a thermos you pump it out of.  The ambiance of the inside just isn't inspiring to me while the outside patio is the best spot in nicer weather.  The location looks like somebody decided to open a restaurant next to their house and the parking is less than fun to deal with in the area.  Most things here are probably around a three or four star when they are done properly but having bad coffee is just not an option in a joint like this.  Seems like the quality has gone down here and gotten inconsistent.  Granted I'm not much of a breakfast person so this is just not my favorite spot for breakfast, brunch or lunch but many folks love it.

They have the second best roast beef Po Boy in Mid-City and their other sandwiches are pretty good too with their Peacemaker po boy being a good highlight.  Their boiled shrimp and crawfish just aren't as good as my other preferred spots and on my last visit the crawfish were really undersized compared to several other places I had recently eaten some bugs.  The seating can get pretty hard to find on the weekends in here but during the week it is usually easy enough to grab a spot at the bar.  Sometimes you can order from the bar but when it's crowded you just have to stand in line and order at the front register and then hope a seat clears out after you have paid for your food.

The food is just like the City Diner location I eat at near my work in Metairie except I found the service to be lacking and they got my easy order substantially wrong.  The location and interior are substantially nicer and far more fancy than the Metry location and I could see this being an interesting joint later at night.  I hope any future visits I make are met with the standard of service I've come to expect at the other location.

This is some good classic American food with a few local NOLA additions added to spice it up a bit.  I'm a big fan of the happy hour here with the 75 cent bbq sliders and meat pies.  The meat loaf is HUGE and is the thing most of the staff usually recommend you get if you're hungry.  Most of the things I've tried I've liked here and there have only been maybe two things I wasn't happy with just because the portions were small as compared to the mega portions of most of the other choices.  Very easy parking after 3 as you get to park free across the street and happy hour happens 7 days a week so a nice place for a snack and laid back happy hour.

Delachaise is one of the more interesting venues to visit Uptown.  It has been doing the same thing all of the new "Gastropubs" were doing years before anybody decided to call a bar serving semi-fancy food that silly name.  The food is generally a bit pricey and ranges from average to very excellent with frequently changing items.  They also offer several cheese plate selections that are very nice quality.  The food seems to be more of a French Bistro style than what has been done at the other "Gastropub" incarnations.  They unfortunately don't offer Abita Amber but they generally do have some very good wine and some German beers that will satisfy me.  The charm and curse of this place is the long and narrow architecture of the building that limits seating and allows it to easily get crowded.  The bathroom situation really doesn't do well with crowds.  Service can be slow when the bar is crowded and if I can't get a seat at the bar I just go elsewhere as I'm not waiting that long.  The crowd is variable and some nights it is great and other nights I have no clue what alien planet landed their ship outside the bar and let their refugees out.  It is certainly a good place to hang out if you can get I seat and I prefer the less crowded times.

This is probably one of the the better establishment to outfit all of your fly fishing needs in the NOLA area.  Uptown Angler is a specialized shop focusing on fly fishing so the nearby Professional Sport Shop is a better store for all things not fly fishing  so check out both stores.  Uptown Angler also is about the best fly fishing shop I've ever seen in the region.  They offer a great selection of apparel, sunglasses, sun protection, accessories, books, videos, bags and luggage and about anything else related to fly fishing you could possibly need.  As you would expect they also offer a great selection of fly supplies, rods, reels, and lines.  After getting all your equipment needs taken care of and you find you're also in need of a boat and location to fish they also offer charter services.

An uber hipster joint with overpriced small portions along with long lines and a menu that just doesn't float my boat.  The Pagoda space is pretty groovy and the all outdoor seating area is nice at certain times of the year but other than the aesthetics of the space there isn't much that works for me here.  Much of the crowd seems to be tourists and a lot of recent transplants to the city that definitely ain't from NOLA.  They do cater to Vegans and other special diet needs (other than the diet needs of folks that love traditional NOLA Creole food).  I hate breakfast tacos (which I gained great exposure to during my Austin, TX exile) and that is one of their big things here and then their sandwiches just don't offer much size or flavor to my preference.  Their baked goods are probably their strongest point and might be the best thing to focus on as they have some unique flavors but the long slow line and long slow wait for the food just makes it not at all worth the experience for me as there are just far too many other nearby choices offering much better food in the area that are easier, tastier and faster to eat at along with giving much better service with better VALUE.    Overall this place might totally float your boat but it doesn't work for me so I've got no reason to return so if you are a surly hipster you will likely love this place but most other folks will likely find other spots far more enjoyable.

This is an ok dive bar that attracts very different crowds downstairs and upstairs but, being New Orleans, there is a bit of a mix where some of the usual upstairs folk will hang out downstairs and vice versa.  The main point of this place is they have a balcony to sit on and serve food later than most other places in the immediate area so, as a last resort, you can always get something to eat here.  I generally only find myself here when going from the Bulldog to another destination down the street and just decide to stop in for a drink.  The draft beer certainly doesn't taste as good as the Bulldog's BUT the prices are a lot cheaper and they have some good daily rotating specials on bottled beer.

Its a 24 hour bar that I've actually NEVER had a drink in... I might go so far as to say its the ONLY 24 hour bar in the Garden District/Uptown that I haven't had a drink in.  I've walked inside this place a few times but I've never been motivated to stay as it smells funny on top of being very smokey.  My last visit here was when I was coming out of New York Pizza after eating a slice and a woman begged me for a ride to Lucky's but upon entering my car she reeked of crack, meth, or some combination of strong chemical odors and was obviously on some type of illegal substances.  I dropped her off at Lucky's and escaped as rapidly as possible.  No good deed goes unpunished ya know!

They usually have ALMOST anything you need here and have extremely good service.  The staff are very helpful with an extensive knowledge of where everything is located in the store.  The only downside to this place is that it closes at 6pm M-F so that makes it challenging for me to get there after work if I happen to need something.  I really like the fact that this location has plenty of parking and I've always been able to get a great parking spot.  I've been renovating an old shotgun double so I've had many occasions to sample many of the options around and, unless I need something after they have closed, I'm usually heading here first.

This is a seedy dive bar with a host of interesting characters always inhabiting it.  I only end up here after Wednesdays on the Square and I've got a limited tolerance for it as it gets so smokey inside.  They have a really LONG bar and the space is just a long narrow rectangle so that where the bar ends the billiards begin.  This place typically has quick service and you can usually find a bar stool.  It has a feeling like you've gotten trapped in the 1970's and you might not ever make it back...

The food often just doesn't measure up in the flavor department and the menu is small.  The ambiance is decent and it doesn't look like they have changed it up very much from the last restaurant that was in this space.  The parking for the tiny strip mall the restaurant is located in is horrendous and you will most likely have to take advantage of their valet parking.  The service has been adequate but I'm really not a fan of their "uniform" of blue jeans here.    The burger here is less than impressive and while decent doesn't equal those available at the nearby Bear's or Château du Lac.  The french fries are horrendous and are limp undercooked things that should just be avoided.  The seafood is where you should focus your menu selections and they do have some good specials during Saints and LSU games.   I would really like to like this place but it has a lot of work to do and its the worst of Ralph Brennan's restaurants I've experienced.  I've got high expectations of Ralph Brennan establishments and the food here just doesn't meet the level I'm accustomed to.   If they removed the burger and soggy fries they would immediately rate a bump up to three stars but the fact they would serve such an unimpressive burger and unacceptable fries is damning.

The lunch menu definitely doesn't impress and the small menu is nearly all sandwiches.  Parking is also not adequate or easy to navigate in the space available so you would probably do better to park across the street.  I had the "stuffed" shrimp po boy with a tomato sauce.  It tasted ok but it definitely didn't seem stuffed full of shrimp to me.  You get a half po boy which comes with no sides and with the addition of an iced tea I spent $20 with tip which left me still quite hungry so I had to go elsewhere for second lunch.  It took one hour for my small little sandwich to arrive so this is certainly not a spot to go for a quick or filling lunch or for good value.  I hope their dinner menu is better but I can't see returning here for lunch.

This is a small little dive po boy place tucked away in a neighborhood one block off Jeff Hwy (turn at the Blue Tomato / Jefferson Feed Pet & Garden Center then first right on Ellen about a block in).  This joint has a dedicated following of local fans that frequent this establishment.  They have good seafood po boys and different specials each day of the week.  Legend says they have some of the most fantastic fried chicken but I've not yet been able to sample it.  The folks that work here seem friendly and like to strike up conversation when it isn't too busy.      This place is only open for lunch so its location makes it challenging for me to get to often but I will return to sample the daily specials when I'm able.  The only thing that disappointed me (but probably would make most folks ecstatic) is that they didn't have unsweet tea and only have sweet tea here.

This is a nice Mid-City neighborhood bar that is located on the bottom floor of a house adjacent to a baseball field so you can drink and then play games.  The name of this bar is a play on the fact that the water level in the neighborhood during Hurricane Katrina was very high (aka it was flooded) and the bar is built out of refurbished flood damaged wood.  They have pretty comfortable inside and outside seating.  The bartenders are attentive and efficient and the beer is cold.  They have crawfish boils on Fridays when the bugs are in season but the last time I ate them there I ordered at 5pm and didn't get them til 8pm and they were WAY overcooked and MUSHY!!!  This bar attracts an interesting and eclectic mix of people of all ages and ranges from sparse to crowded depending what is going on and the day of the week.  When this place gets crowded it can get really smokey inside and it often gets crowded during Saints games when they usually have some free food.  This location is certainly worthy of a stop on a Mid-City bar crawl.

This is a cool neighborhood cafe that gets really busy for brunch and lunch.  The breakfast items look to be the star of the show but as someone that isn't really a fan of breakfast food I got the burger.  Since the same folks that own this place also own Cafe Navarre, where they have a really good burger, I had high expectations for the burger here.  Sadly the burger I got here could have come from a fast food joint.  It wasn't a bad burger but it was a thin piece of meat and small for the price while it did have a fantastic wheat bun.  If the best thing about a burger is the bun then that burger needs some work!  The breakfast creations looked fantastic and did tempt even my breakfast food hating palate so sticking to the breakfast section here is your best bet.

This is probably the highest level example of a fine dining po boy place in existence.  I used to eat here pretty often when they first opened but now the wait and prices have gotten outrageous and there are simply too many other places to get a po boy.  The prices are sometimes crazy expensive.  The last time I went and ordered a regular shrimp po boy they told me the "market price" of the shrimp would make it nearly $30 (they then offered me a smaller popcorn shrimp po boy for $15)!!!  The Big Fisherman seafood market down the street was still selling the biggest shrimp for $9 a pound so I'm not sure what market they were using.  I got a bit worried back in the days when I ate here often when several Hollywood actors, of the famous type, started slumming it up here and before too long the tourists started showing up in droves and there was a line out the door to get in the place confirming my worst fears.  They do use local, fresh, quality ingredients and I'm all for making profit but wow I've never heard of a $30 po boy anywhere else ($15 for oyster at the height of the BP troubles is the closest I've ever seen).  I really like all of their seafood selections and especially their fried green tomato and grilled shrimp po boy and they use huge shrimp in their gumbo (that they only make on Friday but they never seem to make enough and always run out so I never seem to be able to get that anymore).  I also liked their turkey but wasn't so fond of their roast beef (go to Tracy's for a better and quicker one).  If there isn't a line it might be worth checking out if the prices have gotten back to reasonable levels.  They also seem to have some decent happy hour specials on beer.  Usually they have some pretty nice people working in the place that are good about taking care of you and bringing you refills promptly.  I would still expect to pay around $15 for a po boy which that is not very po and would get you a decent dinner at several nicer places.  If you are in the mood for some fine dining po boys then this is your place!

They have a great lunch and dinner here.  This is like a dive vibe funky restaurant that serves great upscale food (why go to a gastropub when I can have food like this?).  This is a great place to chow down before seeing a show at nearby Tipitina's (or anytime you want a great meal).  I've had some very healthy slabs of meat served to me here so they generally give you very good and filling portion sizes here.  The food has always been excellent and they have a great selection of items on their menu.  It always seems like a very friendly place and the bartenders, hostess, and wait staff just always appear to be in a great mood and they ensure that you enjoy your dining experience!  There is often a wait and they only take reservations for larger parties so be prepared to enjoy yourself with some drinks awhile before being seated.

Ouch this place has higher prices and smaller portions than Hansen's!  This is a small little trailer snowball stand located at Spanish Plaza that caters mainly to a tourist crowd and they charge tourist prices.  The ice and syrups here are pretty good but not as good as Hansen's.  The upside is that I've never seen a line here so if you're willing to pay the price you can avoid standing in line at other snowball joints.  I'm willing to pay Hansen's prices for their unique product (as they have the best ice and handmade flavors which come in larger sizes than you can get at Imperial Woodpecker) while the snowballs here just seem very undersized and overpriced to me.  They have a good product here but I find it a very poor value due to price and dainty portion size so I will leave it to the tourists.

Live local music schedules will be read out so you can keep up with what's going on everyday.  Louisiana music, interviews, and stories involving all the musical and cool happenings in the NOLA area.  They are the innovators of the Jazz Fest Brass Pass and support and are supported by so many fun fests and events.  They don't always play music I like but they always have something interesting going on.  They have internet streaming and I know folks all over the world that listen to this station.  This is unlike any other radio station anywhere else and is a unique NOLA treasure.

The very first McAlister's started in Oxford, MS while I was in college at Ole Miss.  It was a great little place until they morphed into a corporate chain and the quality dropped off.  I've eaten at many locations of this chain across the country due to my early association with it but I've got to say this one disappointed me more than any other location on multiple occasions.  I used to work in the area and I gave it several chances before I finally gave up on it and decided to stick with local po boy options that were consistently great instead of consistently disappointing like this place.

This is a much better than the average diner and they have some good to upscale options on the menu at great prices.  Their menu crams a great deal of choices into a few pages that ranges from appetizers, salads, soups, entrees, burgers, po boys, sandwiches, and breakfast.  The food seems to range from average to pretty good and the service has always been very friendly and efficient.  I'm not the biggest fan of breakfast food but they make some omelets that even I like.  They also make a a pretty decent country fried steak and good meatloaf which are served in large portions (like most things here).  They also have a good selection of New Orleans style food with a nice selection of seafood dishes.  For this type of food and this type of diner style restaurant there isn't a better place in the area.  Large plates and large portions at a good value make me happy and this place does just that so this place makes me happy.

Really nice building with a patio downstairs and a great balcony upstairs.  Both the downstairs and upstairs bars have a very large draft beer selection of 64 beers so they are beating the Bulldog.  Food is Italian Pie with some bar food items added to their regular menu.  The design is definitely sports bar themed with many large screen TVs surrounding the space.  Abita Amber was $4.50 so that's about 50 cents too much for that local beer.  Very sparse on any customers the last several visits I've made and during the last Saints game there were about 4 people downstairs, 2 upstairs and three on the balcony.  With no drink specials and no people my friend and I drank one beer and went the short distance to Superior Seafood for their happy hour special to drink cheaper $3 beer and eat $6 a dozen oysters with a fun crowd to boot.  They are still very new but need to advertise and run some specials to get some folks in here as it really is one of the nicest bars Uptown and has a lot of potential if they can entice a good crowd.  Parking in the area is a bit tight with everything else in the area so plan accordingly but it has been easy on every visit so far as so few people seem to be going here.  A lot of former Bulldog patrons like myself that got driven away by their price gouging would love to hang out here if the beers were more fairly priced (Abita Amber for $4 and cheaper at happy hour as I can drink beer cheaper in this area at Milan Lounge, Mayfair, Delachaise and Prytania Bar).

This is the largest theater venue in the NOLA metro area.  They sell booze here which is great but at inflated prices like all the items here which is infuriating so you should still sneak in your own.  Some Chinese company just bought out all the AMC's in the area so I don't like giving commie's my money so I'm not as keen on going to this place and go to the Prytania a whole lot more now.  They do have nice theaters and have IMAX and stadium seating and all the other newest movie bling you could need.

This place has two very different personalities for lunch and dinner.  The lunch is a 3 star and the dinner a 4 star so really this is about a 3.5.  The lunch (which is a pretty great value) reminds me of what I would call an old Southern ladies Sunday brunch that usually consists of a pasta dish, salad, soup, quiche, and some mini buns for sandwich meats (and very tasty shrimp salad & chicken salad).  The dinner menu might give Brigtsen's and Clancy's a run for their money.  In the Summer they sometimes have an early dinner special and they often have special wine dinners.  I like both the lunch and dinner incarnations of this place and they have a nice tiny patio in the back (with music sometimes).  The dinner prices are very reasonable and this is one of the best fine dining values in the area.  I've never made a reservation here so it has always been very accessible (the parking is very limited and tight on the street) but I've always eaten here on the early side of the evening.

The prices are a good value here and its in a nice location as long as you don't mind ordering to go or sitting outside in their very small courtyard (which won't keep you dry if it happens to be raining).  I had the brisket plate and it was decent brisket with a large serving but it still doesn't reach the deliciousness level of The Joint.  The brisket at LA23 is better and more tender than most of the other options currently available in the GNO area other than the reigning BBQ champion, The Joint.  The beans and slaw were ok but nothing amazing other than the slaw being exceptionally fresh.  My pet peeve of having the BBQ sauce doled out like it is made of diamonds is practiced here and thus you only get a small little container of it with your meal instead of being able to add your own quantity from a squirt bottle.  The sauce was too sweet for my liking and I would have liked some more spice and vinegar to it.    The best thing about this place is that its right next to the Becnel's Farmer's Market so you can add some more variety to your meal.  The people working at both the BBQ and the Market are really nice and friendly folks.  They only have canned drinks here along with bottled water and I would like to see some fresh brewed iced tea.    Overall it is a nice little trip out of the city to visit this place for some BBQ and do some shopping at the Farmer's Market but it still isn't going to tempt me away from the Joint very often unless I just happen to be in the area on my way to fish or shoot but this is certainly one of the few real BBQ options around Belle Chasse and should do very well.

This is a consistently good to excellent fine dining venue that has an enjoyable atmosphere.  It is located in a nice area right off Prytania Street and the owner is usually there to greet you.  They do a yearly garlic celebration and I do love garlic so that always makes me happy!  They  have a good gumbo and turtle soup.  The only complaint I would have is that they serve soup in dainty little teacups so you never get enough and I don't like dainty and I think only tea should be served in teacups!  This place is often crowded so it would be advisable to make reservations.  It is certainly worthy of a visit but they are only open Wednesday-Sunday.

Great dive bar in the Quarter and probably, on average, the cheapest place to get drinks in the entire French Quarter.  It seems to be crowded most of the time, in the afternoon and at night, so getting a seat can be a bit of a challenge.  The bartenders usually seem to be pretty quick and on top of things and the crowd is usually interesting.

This is one of the nicest spots in the Warehouse district and I've always enjoyed myself here.  As the name implies they have a nice selection of wines while also offering a good choice in beer and spirits.  They have a comfortable bar along with table seating.  If your looking to escape the normal bar scene and want a more sophisticated and civilized location then this is your place.

This is the original location of Slice which has started to expand to other locations.  This location is nearest to my house and the most convenient to me.  If all your in the mood for is one slice of pizza this is probably the best place to get a highly customized slice to fit your hearts desire.  The pizza here is ok to me and I like the availability of all the topping choices.  I still rarely end up here as when I'm in the mood for pizza I usually go to Theo's, Pizza Delicious, or the $5 pint and a slice deal at New York Pizza.  This is certainly a decent place for a slice but I always need more than one slice!

Its a bit of a tiny hotel bar set inside alongside a tiny little swimming pool and patio outside with the two areas being separated by windows and a doorway.  They have a lot of posh fluffy chairs with disco lighting done as if they are preparing for a rave.  I've never been here when this place has had a crowd so it seems on average its a nice calm place to grab a drink in a disco lighting psychedelic environment.  Overall its not really my kind of spot and there are a lot of other places I would rather hang out as this place is too trendy and seems out place in the Quarter.

I work on the Wank sometimes and during Carnival people expect and need their king cakes.  This is many folks favorite king cake and Gambino's has a location on the West Bank to help make folks happy.  I'm much less fond of this location than the one in Metairie and they tend to sell out of things fast here.

This is the smallest Whole Foods I've ever been inside (other than the old school one on Esplanade).  The produce section is very respectable while the baked goods/dessert section is far smaller than most other Whole Foods locations and lacks a lot of the items you find in those.  This is a good addition to Mid-City but I would like to see them expand to offer more of the things you expect to find in the other locations too.
This bar has gone smoke free and vastly improved their beer tap system upstairs so I've become a much more regular customer with those great additions!!!

So the interior was nicer than I expected from the exterior view and then they had a nice surprise of a little patio in the back.  I got the pho and found it decent (and I've certainly had worse) but it wasn't like most traditional Vietnamese pho I've had.  The pho was also a bit confusing on the menu as you get to pick 3 proteins but greens are counted as a protein for some reason and I would avoid the chicken as it was just in small less generous chunks than the beef.  I was also disappointed that they didn't fill my pho bowl all the way up and left about 2 inches below the spot most other Vietnamese joints will fill it up to.  I was also quite pleasantly surprised by the other items on the menu which looked quite tasty and interesting so I would like to return to sample some of the other things here but I don't think I would go for the pho again.  The prices were also quite reasonable despite the slight hipster vibe of the joint.

Fantastic that Chef Rob has returned from his hiatus after the sad closing of NOLA Smokehouse.  This new location in partnership with Chef Burgau has taken all the great things about NOLA Smokehouse and upgraded it substantially to add all the elements that were missing and then some.  This new facility is HUUUUUGE.  They have a full bar with a full time bartender and quite a few other staff members to keep the process moving.  Currently the front part of the building is complete while they continue to work on the back which looks even larger along with another HUUUUGE patio space they also look to be continuing to develop.  They also have added fresh brewed iced tea much to my pleasure and delight.    This place certainly looks to be developing into the top BBQ experience in NOLA.  They have been selling out pretty fast since they opened so that would be my only complaint (other than the minor one of that I would prefer my bread to be toasted or to have a toaster to toast my own bread) and that they don't seem to get into dinner time much so lunch is your main time to experience it right now BUT they do have some HUUUUUGE smokers so they appear to have the capacity to expand once they get up to full speed to drastically increase their meat output.  I haven't been this excited in quite a long time and this is HUUUUGE!!!  I am starting to get pretty grumpy over not ever being able to get burnt ends after many attempts. My visit today I arrive all bright and early only to be informed burnt ends are only available with some $50 sampler platter!  That is bad BBQ etiquette as if they got em I should be able to order them as the long standing rule is first come first serve!  To add insult to injury I got sliced brisket since they refused to serve me burnt ends but I got a substantially smaller portion than on past visits.  I never had such problems at the old location so WTF...  I guess I have to start calling ahead or some other irritating worthless waste of my mojo.

This place has some pretty decent sandwiches and burgers.  They also have authentic Chicago style hot dogs.  They usually have some different daily specials and desserts that are pretty good.  I eat here a few times a year but not really on a regular basis.  I've also heard some good things about their breakfast and brunch food but I'm not really a breakfast person.  The service has usually been a bit on the slow side and the food seems to take awhile to come out especially if just sandwiches.  Not the cheapest or the most expensive place and about midway on my scale of places to eat.

Before Katrina this was the worst and most shady Walmart I had ever been inside despite the fact it was brand new.  There were always things thrown around all over the place and things were never in the right place.  So they have drastically improved in the years since Katrina and there seems to be more of a diverse crowd in here than when it first opened.  That being said this is still one of the worst Walmarts I've been inside and there is ALWAYS a slow line at every register so it is an ordeal to get out of this place.  Essentially I really hate coming here and only frequent their Chinese slave labor products when they are the last resort.  However this review isn't really about the actual Walmart store but about all the LAZY people that shop there and leave their shopping carts strewn all over the place.  It only takes about 10 seconds to push the cart over into one of the NUMEROUS  provided cart storage areas in the parking lot.  So to all you LAZY cart leavers y'all are the prime examples of why the U.S.A. is collapsing.  If you don't have enough character, pride, or just sheer courtesy to get your cart out of my way you deserve to grow obese and suffer all the maladies of lack of exercise with no benefit of my tax dollars paying for your self-induced disease of selfishness.  Hey Whole Foods people that do the exact SAME thing this goes out to you too!  Put your freaking carts away or I will do a deep dark Huna chant to put some heavy voodoo on your soul!

This place, while far from fantastic, does consistently OK food.  I have eaten here a handful of times and really didn't find anything particularly memorable about it but it was decent food for a decent price for a 24 hour spot.  They have the usual New Orleans dishes with fried seafood, po boys, and such.   My least favorite dish so far has been the grilled chicken that was a tad dry and a bit bland but tasted alright for what it was.  They seem to give decent portion sizes with most of their menu items and the staff are friendly and efficient while the food was brought to the table in a very timely manner.  I have to admit a bit of large disappointment that none of the staff were actually wearing Daisy Dukes...

This place offers extraordinary value for the quality of food that they offer.  This is a bit of a hidden gem that many people miss due to its location in Exchange Ally across from Green Goddess.  I've enjoyed many dinners and some private events here and always had a great time.  The service sometimes has been less than expected when it gets crowded but I train waitstaff pretty well that if they don't pay attention to me I will go to the bar for a drink in a heartbeat before waiting for them (thus diminishing their tip).  It can sometimes get loud in here but that usually doesn't bother me (and it doesn't approach the levels of say the Oak Wine Bar).  The food here has always been outstanding and the prices much lower than expected (especially during certain times of the year) so this place is probably the best value in the entire French Quarter for fine dining!!!

This is a nice seafood market with both New Orleans style seafood and Chinese dishes.  The prices are very affordable and they have a very nice selection of seafood with a huge menu selection.  They have a pretty nice building with seating inside and a patio outside.  Unfortunately they don't sell beer or fresh brewed iced tea and only have a selection of sugary bottled beverages and bottled water.   Their gumbo is a mix of everything with chicken, sausage, crawfish, and shrimp.  I like my seafood gumbo all seafood so that wasn't my cup of tea but some folks like a gumbo with everything under the sun in it so there ya go.  Unique among all seafood places like this they also offer frozen yogurt.  They take credit cards and also have an ATM on site.  This would be a total four star joint if they just sold beer and fresh tea!

This place is a good Metry dive bar & restaurant.  They have a pretty good sized menu but they have a sign outside proclaiming "World's Greatest 12oz Burger" so that is what they specialize in.  The burger was very large and I had a few bites that were difficult to get into my mouth as the burger was so thick.  The burgers start at $8 and go up from there based on the toppings you get BUT they don't come with any sides (plain fries will set you back another $3).  This isn't the best quality burger I've ever had but it was pretty good considering the large size and I would probably get another one (I just couldn't handle doing it often as big, juicy, and greasy as they are).  They only have fountain drinks, beer, booze and wine and don't make their own iced tea (only pre-made fountain iced tea).

This is probably the nicest looking library in the entire New Orleans Public library system.  The book selection isn't the largest but they do often have book sales in the carriage house behind the main building.  There sadly doesn't seem to be much of the original house interior left but those rooms that still have the original features intact are impressive.  This is certainly an interesting place to investigate and great place to find some awesome deals on some very interesting books during their sales.

Its a hot dog joint that sells hot dogs but they have some mighty fancy hot dogs here.  I'm not the biggest fan of hot dogs but I've eaten here a few times and I actually think the fries are better than the dogs.  They moved to a much larger location with a large patio with lots of picnic table seating.  It is a bit pricy for a hot dog joint and they only take cash which is always a hassle but if you want a hot dog have at it here.  I've also sampled their veggie dog and it just consisted of a vegetarian hamburger patty sliced in half and put on the bun and yes it tasted terrible.  At least they have beer...  I really like the patio and the beer but I'm just not a fan of the food and find it overpriced for just a hot dog.

This is a bit of a hidden away neighborhood dive bar and it would be easy to drive right past the joint if you didn't know that its there.  The prices here are a bit expensive for Mid-City and for a neighborhood dive bar.  This place never seems overly crowded and they do have a pool table and then a raised indoor "patio" type area with a couch to watch television.  Lot's of smokers seem to frequent here so that can make the air nasty in here if too many of them congregate.  The inside looks much nicer than you would think from the outside and when it isn't smokey this is a pleasant place to enjoy a relaxed time.

Hummm this is a bit of a challenge to rank as I've been going for such a long time and the Tracy's folks used to be the Parasol's folks so it gets a little confusing.  The new location seems to be doing well and that is saying something as NOTHING has survived here in a long time and many places have failed here over the last several years.  The main time to be here is for the St. Patrick's Day block party and the Tracy's location is a far more spacious and enjoyable place to be than when everything was centered just on Parasol's and you can actually find a bathroom with the new set up.    They have decent prices on beer and often have a decent crowd.  I think the Roast Beef po boy is pretty good here but not the all time best (it tastes exactly the same here as it did at Parasol's to me).  The size of the po boy for the price doesn't make it a very good value as it would take two of them to fill me up and that would make it an expensive Roast Beef po boy!!!  The food is comforting and familiar to me but the prices have jumped to a bit of sticker shock over the years (still much cheaper than Mahony's).  They also stop serving at 10pm so no late night food here.   I don't go here daily, just weekly, as the draft beer often has a bit of a funny taste and they sometimes run out of bottles for the beer I'm drinking so that is a bit of a hassle.  Usually decent service but if it gets crowded it can be slower.   The bartenders often have some wild stories they will tell you or the entire bar so you might be entertained or disgusted depending on your outlook on life.  The bathroom has seemed less than clean and smelly the last few times I've been (but the same can be said of lots of bathrooms in NOLA).    Generally an OK place to stop for a few beers and get a po boy snack with some inconsistencies at times.  The best times to be here are during the Irish Channel St. Patrick's Parade (Saturday before St. Pat's), the St. Patrick's Day Block Party, Saints games, and during Mardi Gras after parades.  It is also nice in the cooler Fall & Winter days when they open up all the doors and it is like a patio (but with a roof which comes in handy with our frequent monsoon rains).

The last time I ate here I was a kid but it still looks just the same.  The place is a tourist trap in a lot of ways but it still has some charm to it.  The biscuits are still great while my steak was less than acceptable as it had far too much gristle in it.  The rest of my food was just good Southern food and the staff was friendly and attentive.  This is much more than just a Cafe as it was also a motel that has since turned all those motel buildings into different shops and art displays along with a big ole barn in the back they use for different events.  This place provides a lot of Disney level ambiance and while you can find some better Southern food at other places this spot is still worthy of a visit just to experience the grounds and the biscuits are usually among some of the best in the South.

I've been here a few times for happy hour and it is in a great location in the Roosevelt Hotel.  The interior design is a bit too modern and "hip" for my taste as it doesn't seem to match the classic ambiance of the rest of the Roosevelt.  The happy hour food special here is the half priced pizza.  I've sampled a few of the pizza options here and several of the appetizers and everything was good but nothing was really outstanding.  There are a few entrees on the menu that looked interesting that I would like to sample at some point in the future.  Overall it is a good place for a few drinks but I've had much better pizza and, even at half price, I think I would recommend getting something else off the menu.

This is a really nice upscale bar in the Windsor Court Hotel and I've had many great times and attended some fantastic parties here.  This is an old school sophisticated New Orleans establishment where you should dress to impress.  They sometimes have music and there is a lot of comfortable seating.  This bar draws a good mix of locals and tourists and it definitely is an oasis of civility away from the madness that can overtake the Quarter.

This is a beautiful building, on the exterior and interior, that beckons you to investigate it with an elegant and understated small sign framed by dancing gas lights which tempt you to investigate this slightly mysterious establishment.  Unfortunately once you enter you discover that they have marred the interior with artwork that doesn't really fit the New Orleans soul of the building (the art is mainly drawn from "contemporary British artists" who have no connection to New Orleans).  Further disappointment is found in that the focus on everything here is small and limited.     CellarDoor has an exceptionally small menu with very limited offerings of both food and drink.  Their website describes that, "CellarDoor is best described by its creators as a conceptual work of art.  Conceptual art, also referred to as 'idea art,' is based on the notion that the idea is more important than the end result." I must heartily disagree as results are ALL that matter in the real world and only offering 6 beers (one of them non-alcoholic), 4 white wines, 4 red wines etc. is not a good result.  The food menu is also very small and the choices are best described as... "interesting" but not always in a good way.  New Orleans is a city of excess and severely limiting my choices with inadequate service does not bring me bliss or create a good end result for my bar or restaurant experience.    Overall this is yet another attempt at a gastropub, or as CellarDoor describes it "gastro-lounge," and for the most part I've not been a fan of of this new trend in establishments offering small menus of food and drink along with inflated prices and pretentious snack food. This will be a place for those that need their fancy craft cocktails to sip while they eat a tiny snack but it just isn't the type of establishment that I enjoy.  The building is a five star while the food, drink, service and artwork hover around a 1 or 2 for me.  The only New Orleans thing about this place is the building and once you get past that the rest could be anywhere else in the world as it seems to have no connection to New Orleans other than the stage upon which the rest is set.  For those that are fans of places such as Bellocq, Bouligny Tavern and Cure this will definitely be your type of environment.  I do like the building and location so I hope they get out of their initial opening unrealistic dreamland and wake up back to the reality that their results are all we can judge them by.

I end up here mainly for the bar and not the food.  The food is decent but there are really far better places to eat for the price and this is a fantastically great place to get your fancy drink on.  This place is certainly more on the expensive side and definitely a spot you want to dress to impress.  The atmosphere has a bit of a fancy British pub look to it and they are one of the few places to actually ENFORCE their dress code.  They have a great rectangular bar that dominates the space with side booths that have curtains you can pull closed (similar to Crescent City Steakhouse) and a nice little courtyard.  They often have music here and this place is a fantastic place to enjoy a civilized night out in the French Quarter.

You get what you pay for and this place even offers a bit more.  I had several friends that worked in this establishment and for the price and location its hard to beat if all you need is a place to sleep and keep your stuff.  This is more of a hostel type environment than a bed & breakfast except you get the option of private rooms.  Everything is really basic here and there are no TV's or telephones in the room (if you're visiting New Orleans why would you need those things anyway?).  Compared to most other hotels and guesthouses this place is a good value but it certainly isn't anything fancy.  They have a small pool and  usually there's an interesting cast of characters around to make friends with.

This place has definitely seen better days and most nights in here are pretty lackluster these days.  There is some history here so it is worthwhile to visit but the drink prices are way out line with most of the other places in the area.  I live nearby this place but the only times I end up here are when Armand St. Martin happens to be playing or when something like Marielle's UYE happens.

This hidden away spot behind the Delachaise Bar has a good selection of sandwiches and a large selection of milkshakes.  They have a nice menu of specialty sandwiches and also offer po boys.  I've eaten the Cloony's Choice chicken sandwich and the Blue Heeler roast beef sandwich so far which were both ok but didn't really give me any memorable flavor bursts which I found unusual for sandwiches listing so many ingredients.  The prices for sandwiches and shakes seem fair enough here and the people working the counter seemed pleasant enough.  I still haven't sampled a milkshake but I plan on that on my next visit.  This probably wouldn't be my current first choice for a nice sandwich but there are still many things for me to sample and it is a quick and convenient location to my neighborhood.

This is a hidden gem (or was til Treme outed it) of New Orleans Italian Creole restaurants.  It is a bit of an adventure to get here as it is hidden way over and then some on the West Bank.  Let's just mention Oysters Mosca and MMMMMM good.  They have some great food here but you need to bring lots of people as it is all family dining style.  You better be hungry and be ready to chow down on some great stuff and did I mention Oysters Mosca?
