I went to original Chuy's pretty often back when I lived in Austin (and actually my first meal in Austin after evacuating from New Orleans due to Hurricane Katrina was in original Chuy's).  I had given up potato chips and corn chips and all types of chips for about 3 years when I first walked into Austin Chuy's so damn you Chuy's for runing my strict discipline of all those years and getting me back on the chips.    So I was surprised to find a Chuy's in Nashville sitting a stone's throw away from the hotel I was staying at so I had to make a visit and check it out.  For some reason some PC buffoon somewhere decided to rename the infamous Chuy's "Mexican Martini" to the "Texas Martini" which is just plain dang silly.  I still ordered the "Mexican Martini" and they knew what I was talking about.  I was sad they didn't have a prickly pear margarita on tap but the bartender said they rotate the flavors seasonally and they would rotate it in again at some point.    Overall it seems pretty close to the food and flavor of the original Chuy's but perhaps a bit more bland but Austin Tex-Mex is pretty bland compared to other locations in general.  They have some good drinks so it is worth stopping in here just for the booze alone so make sure to order the MEXICAN martini and sample several margaritas.

This place has a lot of old school roadhouse style charm out on River Road not far from Destrehan Plantation.  The menu has a VERY extensive history of the evolution of this place into its current form and makes for an interesting read.  The ladies working here were very friendly and gave great service.  They also have some awesome daily specials and I was sorely tempted by their seafood lasagna special but I had to try the roast beef po boy on this visit.    I decided to sample their tamales for an appetizer and cautiously ordered the large 18 inch roast beef po boy with the expectation I would have some left over.  The tamales were decent but tasted like most other tamales I've had.  The roast beef po boy was imposing when I first unwrapped it and the French bread was perfectly toasted.  The roast beef itself was good but there wasn't a great deal of it on the sandwich and there also wasn't a lot of gravy.  The meat was adequately juicy but it just had a hint of gravy flavor that I wanted more of.  The thin layer of meat enabled me to easily finish the entire 18 inches of the sandwich with no problem.  As a point of comparison eating the "smaller" whole roast beef at R&O's leaves me far more full as there is a greater quantity of meat and the flavor of that po boy still leaves R&O's as my top choice for a roast beef po boy.  St. Rose Tavern definitely makes a good roast beef and I will certainly return to this charming spot to sample more of their menu.

This is an uber hipster clothing store with vintage clothing.  They have some good buys here and you can pick up stuff for $5 which is a great deal these days.  Its right next to Juan's Flying Burrito so you can shop here while waiting for a table.

The chicken pho here comes with the skin on which is the way many Vietnamese folks prefer it and it does add some extra flavor but just take note if you don't like skin in your soup.  They offer quite a few good goat dishes here and several Vietnamese folks I know tell me they think this is the best place to eat goat.  They only have plain iced tea and no jasmine iced tea.  The service is fast and efficient and the prices are decent.

I had pretty low expectations of this joint going in as its a chain but actually it pleasantly surprised me.  The brisket was decent and the turkey was good.  They had a selection of 3 sauces and the spicy had a nice kick to it.  They also had more seating inside than you really can tell from the outside.  They have free soft serve ice cream and kids eat free on Sundays.  This place is far better than Hillbilly BBQ so this is probably the best BBQ currently available in this area.  Its certainly not the Joint or NOLA Smokehouse but if I'm around here I will certainly not hesitate to stop in for some BBQ and good music.

This is one of the oldest and most unique health clubs in the USA.  They have their own bar and library.  They have an extensive list of classes and activities.  They have a lot of old school classic ambiance along with a lot of old school equipment mixed in with newer equipment.  If you want a full size boxing ring they have you covered.  You also get parking included in your membership and since this club is in the French Quarter that alone could be worth the price of membership.  This is certainly one of the most unique health clubs in the country and one of the top clubs in the New Orleans area but it probably isn't for everybody so make sure to do a trial membership to check it out first.

Seafood gumbo (Bucktown cracked crab stew as they call it) with huge shrimp and a 50 cent oyster special so what's not to like?    Well one thing not to like is the gumbo should really be called gumbo and not made into an entree that ends up costing $31.34 for just that and an iced tea with tip as I could go to Commander's Palace at lunch for that and then right across the street at R&O's is much better gumbo at a much better price.  I was also really irritated that there was no hot sauce on the tables or anywhere else and the Bucktown Cracked Crab Stew was pretty bland and certainly needed it!  Seriously who doesn't put hot sauce on tables in Louisiana?  Needless to say I won't be getting this dish again here...  The 50 cent oyster special will be every Sunday during football season and they don't have a regular happy hour set up yet so we will see how that develops.  They do have a lot of fresh seafood specials and I like the idea of where they are pointing but there is certainly some tweaking to be done here to make it realize its optimum flavor possibilities.  The inside is on the smaller side and bar seating is probably the best place to be while they also have a small area of patio seating in the front.  This place has serious potential and could become one of the best places to hang out in the Bucktown area if they make sure to pay attention to flavor, spice and everything New Orleans nice.

Prior to Katrina I lived near the previous Uptown location of Martin's and I really miss their deli.  The Magazine Street location is still a good spot to grab some good wine and they have a decent selection of liquor and beer.  Martin's is always an easy spot to grab a quick gift or stock up for a party.  I very much look forward to their return to Baronne Street and the reopening of the Uptown deli!

This place does make great cakes but this review is just for the immediate satisfaction bakery experience.    This bakery is mainly a place to order cakes and such baked goods for future consumption.  They have a small display case (that always seems very bare when I've visited) where you can buy items like cookies and petits fours.  I've heard legends that they have a greater selection in the morning but all I do in the morning is wake up and go to work so I will never get here in the morning.    All the other bakeries serving decadent sweet treats in NOLA seem to keep their cases stuffed full of seductive items no matter the time of day you visit so I find it very unfortunate that this one doesn't.  I would love to give this place a better rating and I would love it if they kept up a decent selection.  Maybe the limited selection here is just their dedication to their highly limited and exclusive high standards of only serving the freshest and best but unfortunately for whatever reason that leaves them far behind the other choices for tasty sweet treats in the area.

Always some good food and the service can be good if you know how to work with people.  The staff (especially one older gentleman) comes off as a bit gruff mainly because so many people ask so many stupid questions (especially the date I had that night... she says "what's good" and he says "everything" and she says "but really what's good" and he says "everything" and he is right but she just gets mad like most silly people).  So just don't be silly and everything will be great except on the nights that he really is grumpy!  This place is hidden away over the Apple Barrel in a small space and there is usually a wait to get up there.  They also don't have a lot of patience hunting people down so if you don't pay attention when they call your name you will probably lose your place so PAY ATTENTION.    They have some really great food and once you get used to the sometimes gruff attitude of some of the servers (to usually silly people) then you can have a fantastic time!  I've still got many things to sample here but everything I've had so far has been outstanding.  It is cramped and you will probably have to wait awhile before eating and parking in the area is always a challenge but still very worth the effort!

There are two menus one for the bar and one for the dining area.  They have made some nice updates to the interior with the Irish theme but not really an Irish comfy pub feel as it seems much more like a fine dining establishment (they are making lots of updates and additions that are making it more comfortable).  I ate from the "nice" menu but wished I would have gone for the bar menu.  They start with bringing out some tasty Irish soda bread and butter.  I had the meatloaf appetizer which I would probably never get again as it just wasn't my cup of tea as it had a very sweet honey like sauce with it along with a very crisp/burned crust that I didn't find to my taste.  I then had the salmon with colcannon, cherry tomato-pepper ragout and beurre blanc which was good but not anything special.  For dessert I had the apple crumble which was decent but unfortunately not nearly as good as the nearby Houston's version.    I will go back to sample the bar menu but I certainly won't be drinking in this establishment as the cheapest draft beer is Abita Amber for $5.50 (which is one of the highest prices in the entire city for Abita Amber) and then the other beer prices go up from there.  They certainly won't be taking any business away from Finn McCools or drawing me away from Commander's Palace and Galatoire's lunches with those drink prices.  I think the space is nice and it could be a great bar to hang out in but at the current beer prices I don't see a crowd of folks hanging around very long in there.    It was also extremely slow and it took way over an hour to get my food.  There were not many other people even in the establishment as I arrived right at 5pm but didn't get out until 7:30 (but the Chef did take the time to come to my table and apologize so kudos for that).  Granted I also did go on the very first day they were open so they get some leeway for that as I usually never go on an opening day (but I thought an experienced chef would have whipped his troops into shape) and I do like Irish bars.  I don't mind waiting for great food but I didn't find the food to be up to that standard yet.  Perhaps they will make some adjustments and find their niche.  I hope they go for more of an Irish pub environment and bring the beer prices down to a more reasonable level in line with the rest of the area so I can enjoy the place more; as it is far closer to my house than Finn's but further away than Commander's so that is some stiff competition for my fine dining patronage but much easier for my very consistent bar presence.  I'm thinking the fish & chips will be my next attempt (I had the fish & chips at lunch recently and they were quite tasty!)  Ok so another visit and I had the roast beef po boy and sadly I have to report that it was the most disappointing roast beef po boy I've EVER had (1 Star or less).  There was very little roast beef even on the sandwich and the gravy just didn't seem to have very much flavor.  I still want to sample the burger and the shepherds pie but this was a very disappointing experience.  The ambiance was quite nice on a Saturday night and it seemed to be a pleasant crowd but a bit loud from so many voices.  Went again on Friday for lunch and it was pretty crowded and I had the shepherds pie and it was ok but a bit on the small portion size.  I then returned on Saturday for lunch and had the burger which was a very NICE burger BUT it didn't come with fries???  I've never been to any Irish place that didn't include fries with their burger so I'm very confused about that (the menu seems to have changed and now it does)!!!  They have been showing the rugby world cup and I would love to watch it here if the beer wasn't prohibitively expensive.  (They hosted several late night events during the Rugby World Cup and had some $4 specials on some beers which was much more reasonable).

Food and drinks are like every other Felipe's I've visited in the area so the quality is consistent.  Service at the bar was a bit slow and disorganized and seemed one of the bartenders was not familiar with the menu or how to enter a combo into the register.  In general Felipe's taco portions are just so small I always end up having to order more here and somehow end up spending more than I do  at other Mexican joints and even then I still seem to be a bit hungry afterwards.  I do like the little salsa and topping bar they have as you get to really sauce up your food and that is my main attraction to this joint as I'm a saucy salsa freak.

I used to really love Ninja and they used to be one of the best sushi joints in town.  My last many visits though have just really disappointed me.  Some of my rolls have just tasted bad and they have often just fallen apart into a crumbled mess.  I have just found that I really no longer have a desire to go there and when I want sushi I really just greatly prefer Kanno.

I had a very enjoyable dinner at Johnny V's with a group of friends. This is certainly an upscale fine dining restaurant so I would suggest dressing appropriately. The ambiance is a bit reflective of a French Quarter courtyard, with some iron work railings and the ceiling looking like a star lit sky. The menu here is very creative and unlike any other in New Orleans. There is very little influence from traditional creole cuisine and while many local ingredients are featured the preparations and combinations are often rather unique with a general underlying French flair to many of the dishes. If I didn't know where I was I really wouldn't think I was in a New Orleans restaurant based on the food so if you are in the mood for something a bit different this place will fit the bill.  I started with a mirliton and crab claw bisque then for my entree I had a Dijon crusted rack of lamb that was served with a Chinese black rice cake and mint edamame. For dessert I had goat cheese ice cream but they initially made a mistake and brought out the goat cheese appetizer which was very good but they quickly remedied their mistake and the ice cream was even better. I was extremely pleased with the portion sizes and found myself pleasantly satisfied while not feeling stuffed (in fact I was still full the next day). The service was excellent and even though there were a few mistakes with our orders these were quickly taken care of. This is a great spot for an intimate dinner or a small group to enjoy some good food and drinks in a pleasant environment.

First off I rarely drink coffee and second I'm really not the biggest fan of coffee shops as I like to drink beer in a bar instead of hanging out in some lame hipster infested coffee shop.  This place had intrigued me for awhile though and I wanted to check out what it offered.  They really did a good job of cleaning up and remodelling this long deserted building and it certainly is better than the eyesore that was there previously so kudos to them for that.  They actually had some interesting looking dishes for carnivores on the menu but I only wanted a cup of coffee as I was really tired and needed a caffeine surge to power me through what was going to be a very long night.  I really find a great deal of satisfaction with the fact this place has signage outside boasting of its Vegan Coffee and food but inside they offer several beef and egg options so they are keeping it NOLA real here despite the Vegan angst that would drive Morrissey to slit his soul over the animals murdered for this psudo-Vegan joint.  I do have to admit though I'm very confused by this establishment as I thought all coffee was as Vegan as any plant could be but as all plants are covered in billions of living microorganisms and a host of insect and other animal life which gets mixed into all plants Vegans eat they are all only posers and eat plenty of non-plant creatures (although most Vegans I know subsist largely off of desserts so I consider them dessertarians or carb addicts).   Continuing with my confused state of mind as I perused the coffee menu here I can honestly say I've never seen a more confusing coffee menu in my life.  They have descriptions next to all the coffee varietals they offer akin to what a wine flavor profile description might be but many of their coffee descriptions include "sweet" and "sugar" in them.  I don't want sweetness or sugar in my coffee as I like mine black and bitter with nothing added like cream, milk or anything else idolarating my pure coffee darkness.  When it comes to coffee my soul is very dark and black as night!  After frustratingly looking for a coffee that might meet my needs on their world encompassing coffee selection I finally just picked one and hoped for the best.  The price was rather higher than I was expecting to pay and the time it took to prepare was rather longer than I was accustomed to.  While I was waiting for my coffeee I perused the offering of their Vegan desserts and I saw a few things that mildly stimulated my interest yet ultimately I wasn't tempted to indulge in any of them as I was still feeling a bit wounded in my wallet because most other dessert and coffee shops in NOLA would have netted me both a nifty snack treat and a coffee beverage for the same price I paid for just my coffee here.  Due to the price I paid I had high expectations of my special African coffee bean selection and it was served in a rather larger than average coffee mug.  The taste started out a bit smooth and velvety but ended with a bit of saltiness and a hint of beef broth.  The beef broth finish might have totally have been in my imagination though as I had been focusing on looking at all the interesting beef dishes they offered on their menu and I do love looking at some beef dishes in a Vegan establishment!  Ultimately I just wasn't that impressed with my coffee and I don't think I would really return for more or to hang out here with the extra groovy hipster crowd that seemed to be loving the angst of this place.    I wish I could like the coffee here more and I'm a bit tempted to return and try some of the beef dishes and I'm really glad these entrepreneurs fixed up this long deserted space but as I was leaving some douche hipster on a moped pulled right up behind me and parked on the yellow triangle illegally behind my legally parked vehicle and was about a half inch from my bumper... I hate damn idiot douche hipsters on their mopeds that park illegally and try to block me in... I refrained from throwing the moped at the hipster and thankfully I have a rear camera on my vehicle that makes maneuvering and parking much easier so I also avoided the temptation to smash the little moped with my bumper and after much microscopic maneuvering I was finally able to escape this enclave of hipster buffoonery.    Maybe I will stop in again as there were a few cute ladies hanging out here that had only minor hipster angst upon them but it will be a tough sell if I want coffee and freedom from douche hipsters.  So unfortunately my main impressions are less than optimal coffee and then my experience being totally ruined by bad douche hipster customers which the coffee is all HiVolt's responsibility and the douche hipsters bring it all on themselves and earn all the sterility and impotence their skinny jeans bring upon them.  Maybe Vegans will like the pseudo -Veganism of this place as much as hipsters do and psudo-hipster Vegans will just eat this place up!  Morrissey he just hates this place and me.

I just was really turned off by the ambiance and the menu really seemed overpriced especially for the fish entrees.  Things started bad when they were out of the first thing I ordered. I then got a turtle soup and burger.  The turtle soup was actually good but I was never offered any Sherry so what's the point at that point so that was just an epic fail.  The burger was not up to par and especially for the amount they charged ($15) as it really didn't have much flavor and it lacked on all levels.  The shoestring fries served with the burger did not please me.  The service was inadequate as it took far too long to get drink refills.  So for around the same price as a fantastic lunch at Commander's Palace or Mandina's I got a mediocre burger and turtle soup with no Sherry offered with it.  So many better burgers in NOLA I can't see ever getting another burger here and  I just don't think this is making my rotation or even worthy of a return visit.

5 stars for the Tuesday night $2 beer pitcher special but other than that I'm really not a big fan of the food here.  There are much better pizza, pasta and sandwich options in the city.  I wish I liked the food here better as I really like the $2 beer pitcher special and I would love to support a local chain but I just really like so many other pizza joints so much better I just really never choose this place.  I only ended up at this location as it was one of the few places open during the recent ice storm around where one of my friends lives.  This location is probably about the most modern, hip and trendy of any that they have and I'm not a big fan of modern, hip and trendy most of the time so the ambiance here pretty much goes against my whole grain.  If not for the $2 pitchers of beer I would never have even allowed myself to be dragged inside this joint but hooray and 5 stars for the beer!

The food was around three stars and they keep expanding their menu and adding new items but they need a better organized menu.  This location is alright but nothing outstanding about the ambiance or architecture and it doesn't even manage any dive dank credibility so very three star there too.  The pricing  seems way out of line for the quantity of food you get and honestly I could make a better sandwich for a lot less coin.  For the price point here there are lots of better sandwiches and po boys in the area I'd rather eat.  Overall this place just doesn't float my boat but for those obsessed with high dollar grilled cheese I reckon you can find your bliss here but I also hear the grilled cheese at Delachaise is better.

I've eaten lunch here many times and dinner a few times.  They have good lunch specials and typically fast service (but I've had some slow service a few times even though I arrived before Noon).  I'm a strict omnivore leaning more towards carnivore and I must confess I haven't ever been  overwhelmed in complete ecstasy, like many people seem to be, by most of the dishes that I've had here.     They make a pretty solid and flavorful pho with a unique grilled chicken version that is much more flavorful than most versions of chicken pho (but they only serve it in a small bowl).  Everything I've ever had here has been good; just not better than other similar places I've eaten at in the area.  Everything is fresh and well prepared but it seems to be the same quality as some of the other Vietnamese places on the Westbank (but the menu is much more Chinese) but costs a bit more.  I've also had several times when I've attempted to order some listed seafood dishes and they were out of the main ingredients (and over the course of a year of continued attempts I finally gave up ordering them so my feelings might be hurt by that).  There are still some things I've yet to sample on the menu after eating there for many years (the salt baked items most notably) so when I finally get to those that MIGHT raise my ranking.    Overall a nice place and they have some dishes that you won't find at the other area restaurants.  It is a nice change of pace from many of the other more strictly Vietnamese places but it will cost you a bit more during dinner for that Chinese flair.

This is a solidly consistent place to grab some good food.  I rotate in here probably once every two years or so, as it usually isn't at the top of my list of places to go with all the other great options in the area, but I've brought a few out of town folks here when other places were super crowded and it has always been easy to access.  The service has always been pleasant and the interior space is much nicer than you might think from just driving past and looking at the exterior.  I've never had anything that disappointed me here but I've also never had anything that excited me either so this place is definitely a solid three star A-Ok in my book with potential to reach higher.

This is one of the nicest spots in the Warehouse district and I've always enjoyed myself here.  As the name implies they have a nice selection of wines while also offering a good choice in beer and spirits.  They have a comfortable bar along with table seating.  If your looking to escape the normal bar scene and want a more sophisticated and civilized location then this is your place.

The best offering here for my money is the fish and chips and that is also the largest serving offered on the menu and is in fact so large you could probably split it with someone.  The rest of the offerings on the menu run far more on the smaller side of things so you might need to order more than one of those other dishes to make a meal.  The service is usually adequate and friendly and the ambiance is alright with a tad much hipster vibe for my taste.  Booty's might just have the best and most authentic British version of fish and chips in the city currently.

This is a good spot for a quick lunch that also seems to serve as a neighborhood bar that probably would be nice for sports watching.  They have a limited daily menu of lunch specials.  The sandwiches I've had so far were a bit light on the meat portion while the lasagna was very good and other entrees decent sized.  They are right behind the post office and you just order directly at the bar before getting a number and sitting down so this is a great place if you need to do some postal business and then grab a quick lunch before going back to work.

I've been to several events here and it seems like a unique spot set off in the middle of a giant parking lot.  They have a nice patio in the back and the interior is spacious with a large bar.  I'm repulsed by hip hop music so that gets to be a big problem for me in this joint sometimes.  Friday is probably the most popular time for this bar as they usually offer free food.

Tommy's is a nice intimate dining environment with good service.  The lighting is a bit too low to read the menu easily so you might need to use some extra lighting. Everything but the sides served with entrees average around a four star here.  You start off with very nice complimentary bruschetta served along with bread and butter.  The baked oysters are one of the best things here and hover around a five star experience.  The appetizers here really shine as some of the best items on the menu.  The biggest disappointments I've had  here have been some of the sides served with the entrees.  The broccoli is served as a huge piece that has to be cut up into edible portions; the julienned sweet potatoes would be much better as mashed, the brabant potatoes were very dry and needed some butter or other sauce.  Another observation is that the coffee they serve here is among the weakest I've ever had and I really found it to be too weak for my taste.  Unfortunately for a fine dining experience this is also a very popular spot with the tourists and that has virtually eliminated any semblance of a dress code here so expect to see dinner guests wearing all sorts of extremely causal dress here.  Overall this has the potential to be a four or five star fine dining experience with just a few tweaks but at their price point I've got several other favorites I would prefer to frequent.  If you're in the area and want a convenient meal in a nicer environment this is an acceptable option.  Get the baked oysters and you will be happy.

This local chain does some New Orleans themed fast food relatively well.  Sadly I think this chain does better food than the consistently terrible "fine dining" Canon's that was at this location for many years previously.  When I have out of town visitors with children that only want chicken tenders and hamburgers this is where I bring them.  They also have some decent po boys (on my last visit my roast beef gravy was cold) and the hamburgers are a step up from the typical fast food place (and they offer multiple interesting combinations).  They also do some decent fried seafood platters and some of their other items are "ok" and might even be considered great if they were in any other city.  Unfortunately, they fail miserably with their gumbo, which is some of the worst I've ever had, so they certainly need to do some work on that.  They also have the largest selection of iced teas of anyplace in the area.  They have plenty of free parking behind the building and have an adjoining coffee and beignet shoppe for your dessert pleasure.  They also have a small bar area if you prefer drinking liquid alcohol concoctions to eating.  There are many better places to eat in the area but if you're in a hurry, dealing with fussy children, or have out of town guests that demand fast food this can be an easy spot for a quick bite to eat.

This is a national chain that caters to the niche of higher end men's barber shop that also offers a substantial selection of shaving items.  They offer all the tools, accessories and needed items associated with straight razors and safety razors.  They offer their own shaving products that include pure essential oils.  Their menu of options is as follows:  Royal Shave $55 Traditional Shave $35 Hair Cut $40 Head Shave $35 Beard/Moustache Trim $35 Royal Shave & Harcut $80 Traditional Shave & Haircut $65 Royal Shave & Head Shave $75 Traditional Shave & Head Shave $55  I've gotten shaves at many barber shops over the years and never paid such high prices so I might purchase some shaving tools and products here but I doubt I would find value with their barber services.

Lee's is a local Louisiana chain that has locations on the North Shore, Metairie, and Kenner.  Lee's makes some decent fast food burgers with a thick piece of meat compared to most other fast food joints that earns them a third star.  The fries usually aren't the best and their onion rings are usually a much better choice.  The burger is definitely the star of their offerings here and is probably one of the better one's you can get at a fast food joint.

I had been meaning to try this joint for many years but it never worked out over many attempts in the past but I finally forced the hand of fate to comply with my need to sample their food.  I was sorely tempted to try some of their goat dishes but instead I went with sampling their chicken pho and their example certainly passed the test with flying colors being very flavorful and satisfying.  It is an inconvenient drive from my work or home to get here so it will take some planning and luck for my next visit but I do plan on some goat here soon.

Tal's has a small little menu to match its small little space.  They only have bottled drinks, free water and iced coffee but no iced tea.  I really prefer Mona's and Lebanon over this place as they have a better selection of items and serve iced tea at those joints.  This place can work for a quick lunch spot and they have puffy pita's more like what I've had at Turkish places.  It's a little bit different than most of the other Middle Eastern style restaurants in town so if you are in the mood for that then this might fit the bill.

Jamila's is epically known worldwide for their excellent food they have been providing the hungry hordes for many years during Jazz Fest.  Less well known but even more delicious is what they prepare in their restaurant proper.  The Tunisian food here has influences that will bring memories of food from the Middle East and France while producing some remarkably unique and wonderful flavors all its own.    The hospitality here is legendary and offered in abundance by the husband and wife team that run this establishment.  The husband is frequently found to be sitting at the tables jovially conversing with customers while his wife will occasionally tell him to stop bothering people and, all the while, making it seem very much like you are part of their family as they go into great detail explaining the many wonders they have on offer for your dining delight (along with the best drinks to accompany each selection).  This is a truly enjoyable place to dine, drink, enjoy wonderful food, as you experience wonderful hospitality.

The Lakeview Pearl has a nice selection of specialty rolls here that are a bit different than other sushi joints in town.  The menu also offers a good selection of other non-sushi items for those that like to mix it up or don't want sushi.  The location is a bit strange as there are other businesses in the building with their signs facing Harrison but the Lakeview Pearl is the only one with their sign facing Canal Blvd. so it took a bit to figure out how to get inside.  The service was attentive and professional with drinks being refilled consistently.  This is the best sushi place in Lakeview so if you are in the area and craving sushi this is the place to go.

This is one of the best values on all you can eat shrimp, crawfish and crabs.  They have an extensive and affordable menu with a selection that will probably satisfy most people.  Seating is at large picnic style tables and it can get loud in here when its crowded.  Even though this place is on the Westbank its a really quick trip from the city and from Uptown its really faster to access than most restaurants in the French Quarter or Bucktown.  The biggest criticisms I have are that the shrimp are sometimes over cooked and when it gets busy service can sometimes take longer than I would like.    Overall this is a great casual seafood spot that is mostly a locals joint that will give you a lot of bang for your buck.

This place is much nicer on the inside than you would assume from its drab old strip mall exterior.  The food trends more on the expensive side for what it is with basic sandwiches, salads, soups, pastas and steaks.  They have a good burger that is nice sized but it comes with potato chips and fries are an up charge.  Cafe Fresca also has changing daily specials but many of them don't seem like good values.  The best value here is probably the 2 can dine for $20 deal and that's definitely the way to go if you plan on eating here.

This is a really great space and you can really just hang out in here like its a bar.  They have decent beer prices here that are far better than many other Warehouse district locations and it doesn't seem to draw the same crowd of douchebags and randos like some other bar locations in the area have.  The Phil's burgers are generally very nice and I like this location a lot more than their original Metairie space.  I never would've guessed it would've been so nice and actually so comfortable a place to just hang out and drink beer so I would suggest giving it a try.

This place has some of the most perfectly seasoned and spiced Thai food I've ever eaten.  Their Coconut Soup is the best version of that dish I've ever experienced and one of the best flavor experiences I've had in quite a long time.  Even better is that I had ordered a small cup of the soup but the kitchen made a mistake and they gave me a large bowel so that I was able to even more fully enjoy and lengthen my ecstatic gastronomic pleasure with that wonderful Coconut Soup.  I have really enjoyed every meal I've eaten here with the Tom Yum soup being very nice, the basil shrimp having great flavor and the noodle dishes all making my taste buds very happy.  This is DEFINITELY a place to eat at ASAP if you are a fan of spice, flavor, seasonings and awesome service which is all done at an amazing value for the great quality.

I've got some out of town friends that love this place... they love it so much that they demand to go here non-stop the entire time they are here regardless of what else is going on.  It can be Jazz Fest, Greek Fest, French Quarter Fest and all they want to do is go here.  From being dragged here incessantly I've grown to not like this place very much as I like my fests a lot more and I can only take Bourbon St. locations like this in very limited doses.  The big thing that really gets on my nerves and pisses me off after a few minutes in here is that the damn shot girls won't leave you alone and try to shove test tube shots down your throat no matter how many times you tell them no.

Bud's Broiler is a local and small New Orleans burger chain.  The typical Bud's Broiler experience is two stars for food quality (as are most fast food joints) but they have a few locations that stay open 24/7 that merit three stars but unfortunately this one doesn't which is strange as it is the one closest to Tulane and Loyola where you would think the most night owls would be.  Typically this location is filled by families enjoying their fast food fix.    All Bud's broilers have similar looking ancient menu's that have had their individual characteristics added over the years so that each has become its own unique piece of fast food heritage artwork.  Looking at the menu prices will quickly let you discover that Bud's is definitely more expensive than the usual fast food place.  This Bud's is located in one of the few strip malls within the city so it definitely doesn't have as much "personality" as the original one on City Park Ave. in terms of location and the building.  There is definitely better food out there and this place is located right next to Pyramid's Middle Eastern restaurant and very near Frost Top so 99% of the time if I'm in this area I'm heading to Pyramid's or Frost Top instead.  If they were open 24 hours, like some of the other Bud's locations, I would probably end up here more often.

Bud's Broiler is a local and small New Orleans burger chain.  The typical Bud's Broiler experience is two stars for food quality (as are most fast food joints) but they have a few locations like this one that stay open 24/7 that merit three stars.  I'm really a night owl and I like to stay up to all hours and since Katrina the options for 24 hour places have declined.  The great thing about the 24 hour locations is there always seems to be the kooky NOLA folks that always seem to be lurking around that always make a visit during strange hours all the more worthwhile and entertaining.  Bud's is definitely more expensive than the usual fast food place and along with their greater expense they also want tips for no service other than making your fast food.  The one thing that really pisses me off is that they don't offer free refills on drinks and they don't even fresh brew their own iced tea and use one of those fake "brewers" that have a hose running into it from some pre-made crap tea.  If I'm spending $10 on a burger, onion rings, and a drink I think they can spare the few cents it takes to give me a refill on some pre-made crap tea.    All Bud's broilers have similar looking ancient menu's that have had their individual characteristics added over the years so that each has become its own unique piece of fast food heritage artwork.  This is the original Bud's and it is probably the coolest one in terms of location and the building out of all of them.  The interior is really small and cramped but they also have some outside seating that is really cool.  There is definitely better food out there but there are few places that have as much character as this Bud's Broiler.

I've eaten here many times over the years and the food has just never impressed me and has never surpassed being simply average.  I'm sure this would be a fine establishment in most other places but we're very spoiled in NOLA and can demand more.  This can be a fun place to eat with a group and have a few drinks but this is probably one of the most mediocre pizza, sandwich, sort-of-Italian  places in the area.  The service is usually provided by Tulane or Loyola co-eds that provide varying levels of service and attractiveness that can add or distract from the quality of the dining experience.  The food is two stars while as a drinking establishment it  ranks around a three.

NOLA BBQEAUX works out of a food trailer and typically can be found at the Westbank Flea-market lot in Harvey.  They have some good brisket and very nice burnt ends served here with a tasty selection of three sauce options (regular, spicy and tangy).  Their sides are typical decent standard bbq joint fare with beans, slaw, grits and mac 'n cheese.  The BBQ reminds me a lot of Chef Ron's (formerly of many places but lastly of Central City BBQ) with the burnt ends being especially similar to his.  The folks running this place are very nice and you typically get your food very fast.  There is plenty of seating to be had around the area and lots of other food options to explore.

I usually just stop in here on way back from the Shooter's Club to grab a quick meal.  They have a decent menu selection and generally have good service that is sometimes a bit slow.  The food is typically good and they offer good value for their portion sizes.  They have good sandwiches, pasta, burgers and the seafood is typically prepared well.  I wouldn't go out of my way to eat here but it is a decent family restaurant if you find yourself in this part of town.

The food is decent and pretty authentic.  They don't have iced tea and I tried to get a Topo Chico water but they just gave me a plastic bottled water instead.  Sunday is a bad day to go here as they have VERY loud Mexican music blaring to the point you have to yell to understand the person right next to you.  The loudness of the music makes this place intolerable and unbearable on Sunday or any other day they choose to do it.  For just the food it is worth giving it a try but if you hear the loud music skip it.

This is definitely a dive atmosphere... a Metry strip mall dive that is.  They serve their po boys on Italian style bread with sesame seeds like R&O's does.  Their po boys run smaller and seem to have less meat than a lot of other places which I guess is to up-sell you on their "overstuffed" option.  The roast beef is alright and has some decent flavor and has some juiciness but not a whole lot of gravy deliciousness to it.  The seafood gumbo has some good flavor but the roux is a bit thin and watery for my taste.  I'm pretty disappointed they don't have fresh brewed iced tea here and only offer bottled drinks, beer, liquor, or fountain drinks.  The folks that work here will give you a good exposure the Yat accent and seem to be really nice people.  I would certainly recommend up-sizing to the overstuffed option when ordering a po boy as that makes it a much better value and sandwich. Certainly worthy of a visit on a po boy tour of Metairie but it probably wouldn't be my first stop.  If they just served iced tea and the prices/portion size were a bit of a better value this would be a three star joint.

Decent spot for some seafood or burgers.  They really like their fried catfish here but I'm not really a fan of most catfish and prefer trout and other fish for a seafood platter.  The seafood gumbo had quite a respectable amount of seafood in it and the fried shrimp were good.  I was rather confused over the lack of any hot sauce on the tables and wondered if I had been magically transported outta Louisiana?  The service was attentive and kept the drinks filled.  They close right at 9pm so that is a bit early for my taste but maybe it is what works in Westwego.

How strange I used to have a review for this establishment but AGAIN somehow YELP has made it disappear?    Golden Corral is a buffet joint and as is expected a lot of the food is of mediocre quality like most buffets.  Their grilled steak is probably the best item on the menu and is of a good quality that is above most other buffet joints items.  The biggest thing that makes this establishment a real winner is that they have a free dinner for military vets every year for Veteran's Day so as an army vet I would like to offer a sincere THANKS to Golden Corral for doing such a fantastic thing for vets.

When this place first opened it was AWESOME!!! Sadly they have been in a long, slow, steady, decline ever since.  The quality of nearly everything has gotten to be seriously lacking.  They now have a very poor selection of sushi and so many of the other items have just gotten plain gross as they are either prepared with such little care or are of such low quality.  I'm so sad as I used to so enjoy my time here but unless radical changes are made my time here is at and end :(

So the only other Kilwins I've been to is in Franklin,Tennessee and that one just fooled you into thinking it was a local gem while this location unfortunately reeks of corporate chain.  The service here was less than usually expected and really it just wasn't very friendly.  The atmosphere inside this location of Kilwins definitely doesn't invite you to order your treats and then kick back and stay awhile to eat them as the only seating is a very tiny area in a corner.  Overall I just likely will never return as I would rather go to Angelo Brocato's or Creole Creamery for a better experience other than the fudge they do have really good selection of fudge here.

China Doll serves some really large sized portions on their lunch specials so you get good value for your money here.  The ambiance is old school Chinese restaurant in a strip mall with attentive service.  The food in addition to being abundant is also rather tasty as well.  They do a large carry out business so you often need to walk past a lot of folks standing in the front waiting for their orders to get to the hostess for seating.  Overall this is a decent spot for some good and fast Chinese food on the Westbank at a decent price.

This was my first visit to this location of the growing local pizza chain of Theo's and they are certainly one of my favorite pizza joints around the area.  The thin crispy crust makes me a very happy eater.  I enjoy the wide range of interesting combinations they offer.  The Eccentric & the Spicy Mexican are two of my favorites but my usual fix is the Hippy with either chicken or meatballs added.  I always get a side of their tasty marinara to dip my crust into; although often it isn't needed I still love the sauce and will just drink it!  I also really like their meatball sub which is what I ate at this location and it was consistent with my good experiences at their other locations.

The R Bar is probably the best bar in the Marigny.  They stay consistent and keep doing what they do best.  It is a great basic dive bar where you can usually get fast service and enjoy yourself without a lot of hassle.  Usually this is a majority locals place and it rarely gets crazy crowded with a few notable exceptions like Halloween.  So far this place seems to have largely avoided being overrun by nasty hipsters like many other bars in the area have.  They also have a hotel here so you can camp out here if you want (I've never stayed or knew anyone that did so I can't comment on that).  They always have some interesting things going on but unfortunately around the same time the music at Bacchanal got shut down some other douche-bag damn Yankee carpetbaggers moved into the neighborhood and complained about their crawfish boils creating too much of a ruckus so those were curtailed for awhile too.  Hopefully all such losers will understand they have chosen the wrong place to live and will move to the suburbs where they belong and we can return to our normal pace of life without their unwelcome interference.    Tip:  This "complaining" happens all the time in all neighborhoods of New Orleans and I'm always hearing about it and it always involves Northern transplants so if you don't like music, boiled seafood, Mardi Gras crowds, people having fun then please don't live in the city and make yourself happy and go live in the suburbs as even there you will have plenty to complain about so do us all a favor and go "improve" those places with more regulations, laws, and complaints.  In my neighborhood of the Garden District one of my friends had a bouncy castle during Mardi Gras and damn Yankees that had recently moved into the neighborhood complained that the kids (who all lived on that street) were making too much noise on it (those people don't live there anymore).  Most Yankees are fine people but this vocal minority of complainers are NOT welcome so if you're one of those stay away!!!

Yelp Corporate jacked my previous review and deleted it as it was too politically incorrect for their little snowflake delicate sensibilities (and since that review was up for like years I'm sure it was due to advertiser dollars too) so here is my attempt at pleasing the First Amendment hating corporate overlords that despise colorful metaphors:  What The Frack (WTF in the SyFy Battlestar Galactica lame remake speak even though the original version was waaaaay better and Starbuck is always gonna be a cool fighter pilot dude to me) kind of intellectually disabled (updating to DSM V diagnostic criteria to replace "R" word but still with an IQ 70 or below) corporate menu planning for a BBQ place only has brisket one day a week (and on Tuesday of all days) but then has turkey daily? The Historic New Orleans Collection is many things and they describe themselves on their website as, "a museum, research center, and publisher dedicated to preserving the history and culture of New Orleans and the Gulf South."  The seven building complex has some good exhibits and often features interesting speakers on various historical topics.  The best thing about this attraction is that it's FREE.  They seem to do a good job with constantly changing the focus to different themes here touching on different aspects of history to ensure that future visits can be a different entertainment and educational experience than past ones.  They have a lot going on here and you never know what might be scheduled in the near or far future so you should check out their website frequently to see what is in the works.

This is a really nice looking space inside and half the space is dedicated to private events.  Much of the food seems to be very pork-centric so it was challenging to find items that left the pig fat out here.  For a distillery they also surprisingly seemed pretty stingy on their liquor pours and ALL the drinks my party sampled were what NOLA folks would call "watered down" and they just were not all that flavorful generally.  The food also was pretty bland and blah so again generally mediocre.  Service was also rather forgetful and inattentive.  There was decent live music so there was that.  There likely is a low chance I would return here unless they bam it up and add some actual flavor to things.

This is a nice easy spot to grab some great beers and decent food.  I like it more for the beer than food and they also have some good drink specials they run.  The crowd is a bit variable and it often seems to be more of a restaurant crowd than bar crowd a lot of the time but sometimes it does get more of a bar atmosphere.  They have a nice little patio out front that is nice to see the world of 12 South pass by. Overall this is definitely a pleasant spot to grab some great beer and have a good time.

$12.04 for a brisket plate with 2 sides and an iced tea is a great value.  Brisket was not so good while all the sides were great.  Among the best mac 'n cheese and cole slaws of the bbq joints in the area along with a very nice selection of different items that gives more choices than other local BBQ places

This is a comfortable coffee joint in Germantown that has a decent amount of both indoor and outdoor seating.  They have some food options here too but I only sampled the crack... I mean caffeine beverages and for those that care about such things they also make those fancy little latte art decorations in some of the beverages. When the weather is nice the outdoor area is a nice spot to enjoy some caffeine and get some work done or just enjoy the view.  There are some other business around here but you still get free parking around the area at the moment but things keep changing and growing so hopefully the free parking stays around.

This is a good Middle Eastern restaurant but it is the one that I eat at the least of any in the area.  This place is very often quite crowded and parking isn't always the easiest in the area so I usually opt for places that are easier to grab a quick meal like Pyramid's, Mona's, or Courtyard Grill.  The main factor impeding my eating here more often is the problem of its location in proximity to Jamila's, which is so close I will ALWAYS opt for that as my first choice over here, as I enjoy Jamila's so very much.  This place has a a nice ambiance and the energy level of the crowd usually seems to be high.  I think Lebanon and here probably seem to have some of the most jovial crowds having fun while they eat of any of the area Middle Eastern restaurants I've been to.  I've found all of the food to be good and I've always had great service.

Ok so they have repaired and put the giant mug back up and it is once again working.  They have brought back the signature Frostop root beer and use real glass mugs to serve it in.  They seemed to have gotten much more pleasant staff and the super bad attitude employee was not there.  The food is still the same and a bit overpriced for the fast food quality that it clearly is with a few local flavor and breakfast options that kick it up a bit.  They had a gross roof/ceiling leak dripping all over the place when I was there so they still have some work to do.  I hope they continue with their repairs and get this place back to the classic place it has the potential to be.

This is the same food you can get at the Byblos restaurants for a cheaper price and larger portions.  Some of the food certainly gets up to four stars but on average it is about a three star place.  It is also a market that has all sorts of interesting middle eastern grocery items that you can't really find anywhere else in the area.  It is like a cafeteria style dining arrangement where you order your food or you can choose things from the hot plates.  Most of the things I've gotten from the hot plates haven't been as good as in the restaurant so I usually go for one of the plate specials and those are almost always good.  The stuffed lamb plate was one special that I didn't care for as it was just lamb mixed with a bunch of rice and I missed my salad and hummus that comes with most of the other plate specials.  You get a lot of food here so it is a great value and an easy place for a quick lunch.  It is also right next to the Black & Gold store so you can grab some Saints gear and get ready for the game before or after lunch!!!  Byblos video review:  https://youtu.be/QUQbhgE0NRs

This is a combo candy store and wedding store.  I was just browsing the selection here as I was waiting for my tailor to finish something next door so I don't know anything about their wedding services. They have several types of candy available (with most of the focus being on chocolate) and offer fancy gift packaging.  They have a retail area with lots of gift and wedding items.  Overall it looks like a decent place to grab a gift or have some sweets wrapped up for a nice presentation and they have a lot of Louisiana and NOLA spin offerings.

Pretty generic as expected typical Mexican fare.  The food was on the more bland side and the salsa was more sweet with no spice.  The service was alright and they kept the drinks full.  They have a large parking lot and that's about all there is to say.

Sadly this formerly fantastic chain has been in a long slow decline and I believe this is the last one left standing in New Orleans (I think there is still a GOOD one in LaPlace http://www.laplace-frostop.com/index.htm).  The food and service have been on a drastic slide down ever since Katrina.  There is one employee that is just beyond any type of bad attitude and rudeness I've EVER seen anywhere.  They have some unique New Orleans and breakfast options available in addition what you might expect from their fast food burger selection.  They used to make their own famously great root beer served in a frosty mug but now all you get is Barq's in a styrofoam cup (I did hear they have recently started serving the old formula again but I haven't been back to confirm).  The last time I drove past it looked like they had even removed the long standing, upside down, giant, rootbeer mug.  I used to really enjoy the unique experience of eating here but after many attempts with all bad experiences since Katrina I just can't see going back to the miserable place it has become.

This is definitely a bird of another feather compared to the other spots on Broadway.  I first tried to visit on a Wednesday at 10pm and it was already closed so that really blew my mind and I'm still confused about that???  It seems more like a bar than a restaurant but with that early of a closing time is this place really more of a restaurant?  They have a fantastic view of the river from their rooftop and then each floor has a different "theme" of what is going on with food and drink.  It certainly seems to be leaning more towards the tourist trap destination while still attracting a fair number of locals.  It is overall a really awesome ambiance while the prices are a bit on the expensive side.  It is certainly a place that needs to be experienced and I will most certainly visit again.  I still have a lot to learn about the ins and outs of this joint as it is so complicated with all of the different things going on so maybe I shall come to appreciate more of the quirks of this place to enjoy it more.  Acme Feed & Seed video review of their Mardi Gras party:  https://youtu.be/mlFbv7G1Lxk

It is also right next to the Black & Gold store so you can grab some Saints gear and get ready for the game before or after lunch!!!

Outstanding old line New Orleans Creole restaurant!!!  Many people describe Antoine's as a "Food Museum" as so many of the dishes haven't changed since they were first put on the menu.  This also has the effect that many of the dishes are very old school French Creole preparations (with no new fangled light Nouvelle cuisine preparation, no light & heathy, no vegetarian, no Tex Mex spice rub, fusion anything, no molecular foams, and no vegan special requests) so expect lots of heavy sauces and piles of glorious flavorful butter!!!  This food (just like Galatoire's) might certainly not appeal to everyone but it is what it is and I LOVE it! Antoine's is also like a museum with all of the different theme rooms where you can see so much New Orleans history on display.  The traditions live and the restaurant is also still very much alive and granted there are some dead periods when it is not that crowded but other times of year it will be buzzing with locals doing what we do best and living life to the fullest.    I find it very entertaining to read other reviews complaining about the Oysters Rockefeller and how they think spinach is better.  Antoine's INVENTED Oysters Rockefeller back in 1899 and nobody else has cracked the recipe anywhere else; so all those other versions people have tried and base their comparisons are not real Oysters Rockefeller as you can only get the real deal at Antoines and they never had spinach on them!  I have dined at Antoine's many times and have almost always enjoyed my food and service.  I've only had one less than great dinner here when I attended a private group function once with a set menu and I found that the portions were far too small for me and I was still hungry but the quality was still excellent.  Often I will make a dinner simply out of several appetizers and find that a great way to introduce people from out of town to numerous treats that are available on the menu (without breaking any budgets).  I usually end my dinners here with the Café Brûlot Diabolique (which has a mean kick and will certainly get you ready for a night out on the town or a nap if you drink too much of it).  I also have enjoyed Antoine's new Hermes Bar where they have some additional lunch options and will allow you to order some things from their regular menu (but not everything).  Dress to impress and enjoy yourself!  Also see Herme's Bar Review.

This is usually my go to place for boiled crawfish, crabs, and shrimp.  They have the best boiled shrimp anywhere!!!  The crawfish is usually great depending on how and when in the season is they can be a bit small sometimes and I prefer to get the larger "select" premium ones when available.  They also usually have some great crawfish pies available.  They also have a good selection of other fresh & frozen seafood, gator, and turtle you can take home to cook yourself.    This is a market and they don't have anywhere to eat it once you buy it.  I used to always go across the street to eat my feast on the Bulldog patio but a recent change of rules has stopped that and I'm not happy about that!  You can still grab some drinks at Breaux Mart and go the park behind the grocery to chow down.

This is the spot I had my first taste of Middle Eastern food and I've been a fan ever since.  The combo kabob plate is huge and really enough for two people.  The inside and outside of the building doesn't really have any nice New Orleans "character" about it but they have done a nice job painting and decorating the space with a kooky Middle Eastern theme that makes it a much more fun space.  Many people bring their own wine to drink here (and I don't believe they have a corkage fee).  Service can range from excellent to terrible based on what waitress you get and how crowded it is and, as most of the servers are college aged females, they have a pretty high turnover.  Parking is also a bit tight in the area so you might have to find a spot a bit further away but it is very convenient to the streetcar.  I've always been very happy with my food here and it is certainly one of the best Middle Eastern places in the area.

So Ted's Frostop has been chugging along for several years since my last review and they seemed to have improved a lot of the challenges they were dealing with for so many years.  The front of house service has improved for putting your order in but they really have gotten to maintaining consistently  inconsistent hours and often just close early from what their posted hours are.  They seem to have gotten more popular for their breakfast and still get a decent lunch crowd while they just close before dinner really even gets started.  Their root beer mugs are now plastic instead of glass so at least they have mugs and the original recipe Frostop root beer back but it is so much better in a glass frosted mug than a plastic one.  Their Loto Burger are up to where they need to be and are good now while their roast beef po boy is really a disappointment for the price and the one I was served had stale poboy bread so there are plenty of much better poboys for the price in the area.  Speaking of prices those have REALLY gone up and the price of a meal combo here can get you a meal in a regular restaurant and many other fast food joints are not too far behind these days so really you can go to a full service restaurant for what you get here so that price inflation can't be good for business (with all the crazy  property tax increases and COVID-19 requirements eating into profits the prices are likely to just keep going up to make it so fewer and fewer folks can even afford the city anymore).  I hope they continue with their improvements and keep this place the classic place it should be but I have my fears about the direction prices are going and how anything (or most folks) will be able to ride out the inflation on so many things while at the same time so many folks are making less money or no money because of the COVID-19 situation.    My restaurant review video of Ted's Frostop is here: https://youtu.be/RZ4majqABqY

I usually only end up here after all the other groceries are closed as this is a bit of a longer trip from my house than most of the other markets.  This is a nice sized store and they have a good selection of items but don't seem to have as many local products as Rouse's.  They have a nice booze, wine and beer selection.  They're also big on using your Winn Dixie card and you can save some money if you get one and remember to use it.  They have later hours than any other grocery in the area so that really gives them convenience points. I do appreciate their later hours but I still miss the 24 hour grocery shopping we had in the area before Katrina.  What's a night owl to do these days at 3am when a sudden need to make groceries arises?

This is probably my favorite location of Mona's and they have an attached Middle Eastern market here.  They have a nice outdoor patio dining area and the inside has some unique design features that give you the illusion you could be off somewhere in the Middle East about to feast.  I'm a fan of the combo kebab plate, the fried kibby and the Mona's Special appetizer combo plate.  I also like their iced mint tea as it is quite refreshing.  Service typically seems to be much more attentive and professional here than the other Mona's locations.  This is the same food you can get at the Byblos restaurants for a cheaper price and larger portions.  Some of the food certainly gets up to four stars but on average it is about a three star place. It is also right next to the Black & Gold store so you can grab some Saints gear and get ready for the game before or after lunch!!!  Lebanon's Cafe video review:  https://youtu.be/QUQbhgE0NRs

The pizza reminded me of an exact taste copy of Chuck E. Cheeses while my meatball appetizer was a good experience.  The service was friendly but sometimes got so friendly with the other customers that service to my table got neglected and I was left without a drink refill for waaay too long.  Overall it is an alright pizza joint but there are lots of other pizza joints in the city I like a lot better so I wouldn't go out of my way to eat here while I wouldn't mind eating here again if I were in the area.

This place has been getting lots of hype of late.  Popeyes has nothing to fear from this chicken.  The biscuits are better than Popeyes though.  They have an interesting menu and concept but the food just is not all that great.  I've actually had far superior gas station chicken in many spots.  I might sample some other items eventually but I am not left with any strong motivations from the rather bland flavor of the chicken to hurry back.

Inconsistencies seem to be constantly building here and now to add insult to injury they have chosen to reduce portion sizes and then slapped us around more with the silly decision to eliminate one of the sides to the bbq "Pit Plates" along with increasing the prices for a last stab in the back and then finished me off as a future return customer by also removing the pickles.  The former bbq sauce bottles that were on the table have also been eliminated and now you have to go up to where the utensils and drink machine are to squirt sauce into little tiny dainty thimbles.    I now just will absolutely never return with the current menu as The Joint offers a MUCH better and CONSISTENT product in larger portions with 2 sides at a cheaper price.  Unfortunately Central City BBQ is just no longer even near being competitive, as the one edge they had was being open on Sunday, but at their current menu pricing with less food for more loot means I'm not doing it anymore.  I have to assume I will not be alone in my sentiments and unfortunately will have to predict this will soon be another joint that ain't dere no mo' soon if they maintain their current trajectory.  Hopefully they will step up to evolve and get more competitive in the market again.

Old school NOLA style eating establishment with traditional NOLA lunch items and traditional breakfast foods mixed up with some Louisiana accents.  They still offer a good value for your money here and you get your food fast.  The setup is a cafeteria style system where you go through the line of items on the buffet to select or make an order from the menu before paying at the register and then they call out your menu ordered items when ready.  The burger here is ok but certainly not in the top ranks of NOLA burgers so the po boys, daily specials and breakfast items are better selections.  The seafood gumbo is decent with generous amounts of crab and they do offer small and large options.  The seating is a bit tight and it can get crowded in here but it is a unique and interesting space worthy of a visit.  The main downside is this place is only open Monday through Friday from 7am til 2:30pm so if you don't work in the CBD it is rare you can eat here.

Mardi Gras World is an exhibit of the works and magic of Blaine Kern Studios who build the majority of the floats used in carnival parades.  This is both an actual workshop where they build Mardi Gras floats and an exhibit of the process and final results.  The Kern's are nice folks and they have put together a nice venue which is a  fantastic space for a party or event.  One of my favorite party areas is the cool-fake-Southern-plantation-garden room which is just entertaining to no end for some reason to me.  There are frequently fun events occurring here so make sure to check out the website and see what else besides just the tour is going on here.  Admission:  Adults: $19.95 Seniors (65+): $15.95 Children (2-12): $12.95

Zea Rotisserie & Bar is a local chain which has some of the top rotisserie meats in the Greater New Orleans area. Zea now has multiple locations across Louisiana and one location in Mississippi. Zea Rotisserie & Bar does offer a unique mix of blending rotisserie meats with some American, Asian and Cajun flavors which makes their food distinctive when compared to most other area restaurants.  I have eaten at Zea's for many years now and generally they have had good food but my most recent experiences have been less enjoyable than in the past.  They used to have a really great selection of rotating rotisserie meats but now they have really scaled the selection down and lamb doesn't even seem to be offered anymore.  I have also noticed a distinctive shrinking in the portion sizes.  I'm also very confused by their choice to only offer sweet potatoes "seasonally" as sweet potatoes are available all year round.  This was my first visit to the Zea's at this location although I had visited this location back when it was a Mexican restaurant.  Overall I enjoyed my meal but the portion size was not a full size meal for me.  My video review of this location of Zea's is here:  https://youtu.be/aiosBRDwek8

Sadly another dive bar that has raised the price of Abita Amber above what I'm going to pay for it.  The quality of the food service has been slipping and it just doesn't seem to bring in the crowds it used to so the ambiance has dropped.  Higher prices, less people and less fun...  Times are changing fast and not for the better in the bar industry of NOLA.  At least they still have the St. Patrick's day events but other than that I just don't find myself coming here anymore.

They did a nice job here and everything looks shiny and new so maybe too nice of job as we like our old school dive look in NOLA.  Unfortunately like most new places opening these days their drink prices are overpriced and I really didn't find the beer prices competitive to other places on Frenchmen.  They do have quite a selection of food so you can find something to satisfy your hunger here.  They have a nice upstairs with a balcony that can be entertaining for people watching as the crowds go past on Frenchmen.  Speaking of crowds there wasn't one here while the rest of the establishments on Frenchmen seemed to be jam packed this place was very sparsely populated which I would guess is due to their overpriced drinks not being competitive.

Edley's Bar-B-Que is really expanding all over while they seem to also be maintaining good BBQ quality at all their locations I've tried.  So far I've most frequently visited and enjoyed their 12 South location then I've also been to their Chattanooga location along with this one in Sylvan Park.  I didn't eat any BBQ here and I randomly ended up here simply due to the fact they stayed open later than the other joints in the area so after spending some time at McCabe Pub and Neighbors I closed out my night here.  Edley's certainly seems to have the largest selection of draft of all the spots I visited in Sylvan Park and there were quite a lot of folks in here enjoying themselves at a later time.  Overall I enjoyed myself here and Edley's has shown themselves to consistently be a great place to enjoy some fun times with good drinks along with good BBQ.

Junction is a dive bar that makes a good burger at a decent price.  They have a nice selection of options to kick the burger level up a few degrees.  They also do quite a very nice job on their fries here too.  The staff seemed to be enjoying themselves at work and took good care to make sure drinks were filled.  I actually still think the burger at Kukhnya in Siberia is a bit better though while the fries at Junction would win that throwdown.

I want an Abita Amber and I can't get one here it seems.  I loved the Bridge Lounge's mojitos but I can't get that either anymore.  I liked the Bridge Lounge's unisex bathrooms but now equality of bathroom rights has become segregated.  I miss the Bridge Lounge's dog obsessed atmosphere but that just is all gone.  The music volume is way out of control here and its hard to have a conversation inside its so very loud.  I'm always a fan of dead animals on the wall and animal hide rugs so that's an improvement.  There is more space but the new seating is far less comfortable than before.  Maybe I will grow to like this new place but until they add Abita Amber at a decent price it has slim chances of being a spot I frequent.

I believe this is the last remaining spot in the French Quarter that regularly serves calas which were once very prevalent in the Quarter but like so many things "ain't dere no more."  The interior space and courtyard areas are all French Quarter style that is hard to replicate or find anywhere else in the USA.  This joint does cater mainly to tourists these days but you will still find some locals inside.  The portions are more on the smaller side compared to what most NOLA eateries serve these days.  The breakfast, lunch and dinner items are executed well typically and they have specials.  The seafood gumbo is well stocked with generous amounts of shrimp and crab.  The corn & crab bisque is also equally richly flavored with generous amounts of crab.  The crab balls have a nice consistency to them and maintain good flavor throughout the exterior to the interior.    The service here can bit a bit playfully gruff with some attitude developed by some staff that seem to have been dealing with crazy tourists for many decades.  My last visit I got quite a sassing over ordering iced tea as they were almost out so the waitress informed me I could only have one refill and that was it as they were out and were not making anymore; after my second refill every time the waitress saw me she told me I better not be expecting anymore refills; on the way out of the restaurant our waitress was standing outside and again she told me "uh huh you still wanting another refill I know that look."  So the trick here is to understand this is more of game that is being played so don't get your snowflake feelings hurt and play along with it and maybe you might learn something about a different way people communicate.  Overall this is a bit of a tourist trap but it is worthy of an occasional visit.

This is a decent medium sized grocery that has some nice prepared foods.  They have most of the things you need at prices higher than you would sometimes expect.  They often have some surprising items here that you wouldn't expect along with typically good produce.  The parking is a bit limited for the location and getting in and out from Claiborne can be tedious.  Due to the location I rarely visit this place but before Katrina I used to really be a fan of the Robert's prepared food at their location in the LGD on Annunciation... so if they would just reopen that location I would probably be a more frequent customer of theirs.

This is a great dive bar with some amazing daily specials!  They have a great Monday night special with two lobsters and then steak night on Wednesday and Fridays.  Their regular menu food is also great bar food with huge burgers and flavorful tamales.  The drinks are reasonably priced and there seems to usually be a decent crowd of folks here.  Overall this is a cool spot with some great bar food and they serve later than many other spots.  My video review of Sportsbeat Pub & Cafe is here: https://youtu.be/TveQyQYthXc

Jack's Bar-B-Que has three locations in Nashville and this is pretty good BBQ for a local chain joint.  There was quite a line of folks waiting and the inside was packed full of hungry people during my lunch time visit so this certainly seems to be the case at all of the BBQ joints I've visited in Nashville so far.  I got a brisket plate and it was some good brisket although I certainly have had far better this is definitely some of the better brisket I've had in Tennessee.  For sides I had mashed sweet potatoes and turnip greens which were both delicious. I'm always VERY happy when a place has mashed sweet potatoes and the turnip greens are also a great side to my taste buds.  Overall this was a great spot to grab a decently quick lunch even with the line and although it was more of a fast food type environment as you just order at the counter and then you take care of yourself the staff were very nice.

Central Grocery claims they originated the muffuletta and they have been doing well ever since.  Unfortunately as their fame has spread and the lines have grown the quality has degraded.  The olive salad in particular seems to have had been "cut" with cheaper oils mixed into the recipe instead of being pure olive oil (the ingredient label now says "Canola and/or Cotton seed Oil" along with olive oil).  You can still get pure olive oil and much higher quality olive salad for a much cheaper price in NOLA (for example Rouse's store brand is far cheaper, much better quality, and FANTASTIC!  Rouse's also offers the Progress Grocery Muffuletta).
