I've attempted to enjoy myself many times in this venue but it just isn't my scene.  DJ techo/hip hop/rap music just isn't a form of sound that I find pleasurable.  The clientele here just doesn't seem to be the kind of folks I easily meld with but that might have a great deal to do with the fact that its usually so loud you can't communicate with anyone verbally.  It just seems like a cheesy place to me and I can't get into the groove this place offers.  It seems like the crowd is mostly folks from the suburbs and I don't know anybody that hangs out here.  When I've gone here with friends we never make it even an hour before we feel like we're getting our teeth pulled and we run out as fast as we can.

This is a bar mainly designed for cocktail drinkers and I'm mainly a beer drinker.  This bar is insulting to beer drinkers as they pour your TINY 4-6oz serving of beer in a baby stemmed glass and then don't give you the bottle unless you pay for a large wine size bottle of beer.  Of course they charge you the full price for the tiny shot of beer they serve that you would pay for a normal size bottle of beer!  As a general rule I'm not a fan of tiny and dainty coupled with inflated prices when it comes to what I eat and drink.  I had some decent Bourbon drinks here and sampled one of their "cobblers" but really it wasn't any better than any brand of Bourbon and soda would have been so I really don't see any point in paying a premium price for an average tasting drink.  The interior was nice for what it was but the main attraction for coming to this place is the fancy cocktails which really don't do much for me.  Overall it probably just isn't a place a beer drinker like myself would ever choose to frequent but if you like fancy cocktails you will love it here.

The new Metairie location of Massey's on Veteran's is much nicer and easier to access than their previous location.  The new store just has much better feng shui and is much better to shop in.  It also doesn't hurt that Mellow Mushroom is right upstairs so you can combine some shopping with some pizza feasting.  Massey's is definitely the premier local business to equip yourself for just about any sporting activity other than hunting or fishing.  They don't quite have as large a selection here as they do at their main store on Carrollton but this location still has quite a good inventory.

This is probably the nicest LOOKING sushi restaurant in New Orleans and there always seems to be a good crowd here.  The ambiance of the place is generally nice while being a bit too ultra-modern for the area and my old fashioned decor sensibilities.  This is also the most BLAH bland and boring sushi in all of New Orleans.  It is also overpriced and the service is often terrible.  I will only sit at the sushi bar as that is the only way you generally get acceptable service that still tends to the slow side.  They also have a tiny patio outside just past their small bar.  The best thing to do here is go for the sushi happy hour which used to be a good deal but I'm not sure they even offer it anymore.  They seemed to have been turning this into some sort of techno type club later at night with more of a bar scene on some nights so I'm not sure what's up with that either.  I very rarely come here anymore and do my best to avoid it as there are just so many better places with better prices that I've got zero motivation to return.

This is a cool little festival in the French Market and covers all things tomato and its FREE.  The Cajun-Zydeco Festival happens at the same time as this festival so you can also check out some great music at the Mint for that event.  The Seafood Festival used to also be held at the same time as this event but it got so big it branched off and became a stand alone event so that decreased the food options available for this day of festivities.  The biggest challenge of this festival is the HEAT so be prepared.

Three Legged Dog is where Running of the Bulls used to start.  There is nothing like getting three for one drinks at 7:00am in the morning before running with the bulls.  Maybe its always three for one happy hour here I'm not sure.  I have vague memories of food being here but I've never eaten any as I've been too busy with three for one drinking.  All I know is that this is a pretty small space and it can be a tight squeeze during crowded events but usually it seems relatively calm compared to the madness of nearby Bourbon Street.  Overall this is a pretty cool dive bar and three for one is always a kick-ass deal so I like the place.

So for my 1800th review the Exit/In is a worthy venue.  I saw my Oxford, MS pals the Kudzu Kings here and crazy Kudzu Dave, the bass player, virtually lives at my house in New Orleans about half the year and I've known the folks in the band from since and before the band started.  I was also glad to see quite a few folks from long ago that I hadn't seen in many years show up for the show so that made the whole experience even better.  The venue is spacious while not being too big to lose the ability to have a good view of the performance from pretty much all over the space so it was intimate without being cramped.  They also have an upstairs balcony level area that also adds some more good space to view the show.  The sound quality in the space was also of good quality which isn't always the case in some venues.  I was also happy to see that this space has hosted a LOT of famous and less famous quality bands and they have a pretty extensive list of them on the wall behind the bar.  The bar service was quick and easy but it did take the bartender's longer than average to remember my tab. The Tiki Bar exit that leads to their patio did not have a Tiki Bar but it does lead off pretty near to Cafe CoCo which is an awesome place to grab a snack and more beer after a show!    Overall this is definitely an awesome venue to watch a show in and it is just a perfect size place to have a great music experience.

This location keeps changing names but the awesome patio stays the same.  The waitress came to the table and said she could take food orders but not drink orders so that was rather unusual and I've actually never heard that before anywhere in New Orleans.  There was a decent two musician band playing and it was a very pleasant environment.  I didn't get food so I can't give any feedback on that.

I'm glad a new location of this Italian joint has opened near my house.  I have eaten at the Metairie location a few times but for lunch the Chicago Deep Dish was a bit challenging as it takes around 40 minutes to cook and then it is so huge that you always have some leftovers to deal with. The Chicago Deep Dish is completely delicious and is the best deep dish pizza I have even eaten and the only pizza I have been defeated by and unable to finish in one sitting.  They also have thin crust pizzas here but I have not yet had the opportunity to sample those yet as the deep dish is so great it is hard to deviate from.  They also have some delicious sounding pastas on the menu that also peak my interest.  The service is extremely attentive and on my last visit they provided really great service.  The ambiance is still the same of the former pizza place but it has a decent bar and they have a really great pizza oven in this place and this is certainly a HUGE upgrade from the previous pizza place that was in this space.  I think not many people even know this place has opened here as I didn't even learn about it until I saw a GroupOn for it.  They also have some lunch specials where you can get a slice of the thin crust or Chicago Deep Dish already prepared so that is a good upgrade from the Metairie location for those of us in a hurry to have to get back to work on the weekdays.  They have some really great food here so I would suggest you hurry up and eat here ASAP.  Pro Tip:  If you are getting the Chicago Deep Dish call ahead and put your order in as it takes around 40 minutes to cook.

I've been using this airport for many years, since I was a child, and seen it decline into a complete sorry state and then improve a bit into the transitory state it is in now as renovations are underway and all sorts of great promises of wonderful things to come are in the air.    Unfortunately while the renovations are going on we get to contend with, at least on my recent trip, only having ONE working concourse and on my recent last flight back home to NOLA only ONE luggage carousel was working so everybody from every flight was all mixed together.  There were substantial delays because of the limited number of gates available so hopefully this will be rectified soon!  The business options in the one working concourse area also have limited hours so if you are traveling at odd hours you will have no options for provisions or entertainment.  It is really shameful in the current state and I hope everything gets super improved and gives New Orleans an airport finally worthy of our great city.

I went for lunch and had one of their specials which was a grilled tuna steak with green beans (they were obviously of the canned variety and super salty) and a shrimp bisque.  The food really wasn't that good to me (I would give it 2 Stars) and overpriced for what it was.  It was also crazy crowded that day with some type of huge meeting going on with a lot of retirement home folks.  The service was very good and the people all seemed very nice so I will give them an extra star for that and maybe it was just an off day with such a crowd.  I would like to return when it isn't so packed to sample the burger but the location of this place is not very easy to access.

This is a high end cocktail bar in probably one of the worst looking locations anywhere in New Orleans.  From the outside this bar and the entire area look like they have barely recovered from Katrina and it looks mighty spooky.  Once you go inside it is like night and day.  They have done some substantial work making this a pretty comfortable space to hang out in with all sorts of activities like pool, darts, etc.  They also put out some pretty decent food with BBQ sandwiches and such.  When you are in the mood for some fancy smancy cocktails like they serve in Cure, Coquette, and Bar Tonique just save yourself a small fortune and come here to drink instead.

This is a very busy seafood joint in da parish that offers fresh, boiled and fried seafood.  They also have some nice items like crawfish pies and specials like crawfish bread and artichoke bread.  The crawfish bread is actually more like a crawfish pie and actually better than their crawfish pie.  The boiled crawfish and shrimp is alright but still not up the the maximum level that Big Fisherman brings to dominate that niche and remain king of the boil.  The fried food entrees are generously sized and come with a nice selection of sides with the crawfish fettuccine seeming to be the most popular one.  I am pretty grumpy that they add sausage to their seafood gumbo as I demand all seafood in my seafood gumbo if I'm going to eat it. Overall this is the prime spot for seafood in the area and it often has the line of waiting customers to prove it.

4 Stars for Happy Hour and for this bar having a lot of young professionals with most people dressing appropriately (I'm an old school preppy fellow and can enjoy the occasional sloppy night out but I think we need more preppy spots!!!).  They have a good beer, wine, and liquor selection.  The service can get pretty good when they recognize you here after several visits.  There are also usually some of the best looking women of most of the area bars that will pass through here at some point in the night.  3 Stars (generally) for later in the night when it gets more crowded and when they have music as the acoustics in the bar are HORRIBLE!  I even brought an acoustics specialist I know to offer his services and they said they were having someone "work" on it but obviously that hasn't happened yet.  You can't hear what someone right next to you is saying it gets so loud in here!!!  It also is a big negative that they add a $1 surcharge on all drinks when any live music is playing as the music usually isn't worth that amount and I would prefer to just pay a cover as that really adds up on the final tab (so I usually just don't go or leave when they have live music as the music quality, along with the bad acoustics, just isn't worth more than $3-$5).  Other than the acoustics the other big negatives are they also frequently run out of beer and the service can be ridiculously slow sometimes.  The food is "ok" but way overpriced for the very small portions (I'm not a fan of this small plate concept ya know!).  They also offer some good cheese plates which you would expect at a "wine bar."  The men's bathroom was obviously designed by women and needs some tweaking to be a MEN's bathroom as the stupid two way swinging doors and no urinals are a major pain.  During the weekends it also seems to sometimes become majority old people or cheesy people and that runs out the younger professional crowd elsewhere but when it is good it is VERY good in here.  When this bar is firing on all cylinders it is hard to beat but it definitely has some inconsistent qualities about it.  Happy hour and most weekends are usually the best times but those range from well attended to very sparse.  Thursday and Friday seem to draw the best Happy Hour crowds.  If music is playing or it is very crowded just don't expect to hear anything or better yet sit outside at one of the tables.

This Academy is alright and usually has a good selection of items and sometimes has some nice surprises in their sale racks.  They have gotten much better about stocking ammo and often seem to have more ammo than the other Academy locations in the GNO area other than the one at Elmwood.  They also have a great fishing section and have some decent sales on many fishing items.  They also sell hunting and fishing licenses so you can make sure you're legal before pursuing the sportsmen's paradise Louisiana offers.

For the price I really didn't find the experience and flavor to be a good value.  It just really seemed to be more of a gimmick that was OK for a one time visit but to me it just wasn't really worth the experience and I would have rather have had Brocato's or Creole Creamery.  You should come try it out at least once and maybe it will be a thing for you but for me... I did it and once was enough to last me forever so I probably won't be back.  If you like lots of stuff on your ice cream then you might be more into this joint than I was as I'm not into all that stuff contaminating my ice cream other than fruits and nuts.

They make a very large and tasty pizza but they have very limited toppings and only offer pick up service with very limited delivery and very very limited business hours of only Thursday & Sunday.  I hear they are maybe moving into another place with more regular hours.  It is a lot of pizza for your money but it is an adventure to acquire it if you don't live in the Bywater or Marigny.

This is a very large venue for watching live music and other events.  I've seen some great shows here.  It is a bit far off from everything but it has plenty of parking.  They seem to have bands I want to see rarely these days so I seem to end up here more for special events but they still book some good shows a few times a year here.  Certainly worthy of checking out if there is a band you want to watch.

This is a nice casual brunch, lunch, or dinner spot on Magazine St. in the Garden District.  They have a nice courtyard but sometimes the birds make it less nice so make sure the check your seat before sitting.  I really like their veal pot roast (ahhh they took it off the menu!!!),  sauteed shrimp & crawfish po boy, and their awesome burgers.  They have lots of other great things on the menu and they often offer some special cocktails.  The cocktails are sometimes hit or miss as I've had some great ones and some I didn't want to finish so maybe ask for a sample first.  They sometimes have live music and hearing M. Jackson's "Beat It" on the original fiddle is quite entertaining!

This is a combination sushi and Vietnamese restaurant.  The pho here is good but they are not very generous with the beansprouts, basil and cilantro.  The prices on the banh mi seem to be expensive but they are larger as they use traditional NOLA French bread instead of the Vietnamese French bread but I personally prefer the Vietnamese bread (which I find is actually closer to the real French bread in France).  The space is large and open and they have a combination sushi bar and alcohol bar.  Service was decent enough but my drink got left unfilled a few times a bit longer than I would have liked.  Overall a decent spot in the CBD for some Vietnamese at a bit of a higher price than many other Vietnamese spots.

The buffet is generally the way to go here and that will usually let you sample items such as the excellent fried chicken, shrimp creole, jambalaya, red beans, mac 'n cheese, green beans, and dessert.  The famous gumbo z'herbes is a dish that is usually just served once a year and that is a crowded and popular day at this venue that can be an intresting experience if you can get in.  The neighborhood that this restaurant is located in is certainly what most folks would call the ghetto so use appropriate caution.  They also have a really strange price structure for drinks so if you pay cash for a beer you end up with lots of pennies and nickels so a credit card tab will probably be an easier thing to deal with.  It is always a treat when Leah Chase is in the house and she usully makes a point to come out and say a few words to folks.    Hint: The fried chicken here is MUCH better to me than the what you get at Willie Mae's.  Tip: They are usually just open for lunch since Katrina but they are planning on Friday dinner service soon.

Ok the venue is still a cool place but after returning a few times to eat they definitely have some work to do with getting the food to where it needs to be.  Their burgers and chicken sandwiches really need some tweaks to their flavor and cooking.  I'm afraid they seem to really need some staff changes in the kitchen.  This is an ambitious and complicated idea they have and they really need to step their game up with their food if they want to draw a good crowd.

This is a pretty solid dive bar that is cash only.  This is a bar that you have to ring a bell and get buzzed in to enter.  I've seen some crazy things in here during Carnival time and had some very good times here.  They usually have pool tables but they often take them out during Mardi Gras time to make room for all the crazy people that take over.  During the rest of the year this is always a decent bar to go to and hang out at for interesting conversations and the bartenders usually have some interesting things to say.  It gets way too smokey in here for my taste and the lack of accepting credit cards discourages my more frequent appearance in this venue but it is always worthy of a visit.

They have a pretty awesome ambiance in here with lots of nice taxidermy with animal heads, birds and fish all over the walls that give it a nice hunter lodge comfy feeling along with generally nice looking waitresses.  The food sounds better on the menu than it actually tastes with much of it being pretty bland for my taste.  The service seems to be focused more on having waitresses that look good in skimpy outfits rather than giving great service but I'm a firm believer they could accomplish both.    On my last visit the service was barely adequate and they were somehow out of the meatloaf during lunch service so they definitely didn't impress me.  I'm also underwhelmed by the flavor of the pot roast but it is a nice portion size (although the vegetable side came with a lot of bacon in it that isn't included in the description of the dish).  This place seems like it could be a nice place to watch sports and have some mediocre chain food while enjoying the view of the mostly decent to good looking waitresses that are the main focus of this establishment.  I'm generally not a fan of chains but the dead animals on the wall along with the nice looking ladies working here certainly inspire me to feel a certain primal attraction to it.  Service and food still rate more of a 2.5 stars but the ambiance bumps it up.  If they would put a dash more of NOLA spice zing into their food it could really improve it so I would recommend they invest in a bit of Tony Chachere's.

This is a pretty cool dive bar off in transitioning part of town.  They have live music and usually have an eclectic crowd of people of majority hipsters eager to cut a rug.  I'm way too un-hipster to fit in very well here but the dive bar groovy elements are definitely NOLA classic and worthy of visit and when you add in live local music then it is certainly a hot spot to check out.  So even if you are un-hipster and will be too uncool for school here just say "hrumph" and get over it and make the hipsters jealous with real classic and vintage prep style like I do as I'm always going to dress like it's still the 1980's and sometimes like its the 1780's.

Hummm I've been going to this place a long time now.  I used to really enjoy the place in a prior incarnation when it was basically just a plate lunch type place with really great fresh veggies (but it was a bit on the dirty side).  When the place changed owners a little bit before Katrina they went for a much more upscale dining experience and it took them awhile, and going through some other owners, to find exactly what they needed to do but they have finally hit a good stride (I'm still not sure about that giant frying pan they installed outside).  This place has a great brunch, lunch and dinner but it does get crowded and the small space generally requires making reservations.  The ambiance is often ruined when they turn up the music way too loud.  They have also brought in the silly small and large plate trend (I look forward to seeing that trend end) and I would generally avoid the small plates and stick with the large plates.  It can sometimes be a nice change of pace from some of the other better known restaurants.

Oh yeah Let's Do the Time Warp Agaiiiin!!!  Cool late 70's to early 80's folksy  kitsch design makes this place AWESOME to just flash back and get into an old school vibe real quick.  The food isn't quite the equal of the ambiance but they do have some solid items and their burgers are pretty good.  I wouldn't recommend the BBQ brisket as really why waste your money or time on what they offer here when the Joint offers an entirely higher magnitude of better quality BBQ for around the same price so just skip that here and get something else.    Overall a solid spot for some affordable food that is mediocre to pretty good depending on the item and you can wash it down with some nicely priced beers offered at a decent value.

Ummm I pretty much absolutely hate this place and can see no possible way that I would ever return.  This place is just ridiculous.   I couldn't find anything redeeming about it.  The music is repulsive to me and the patrons make me want to run away and hide.

Ok this place probably has 4 or 5 star mixed drinks if you get a bartender that knows what they are doing (often you don't) but the ambiance is terrible in here to me.  The worst part of my last experience in this place was the horrible music they played (very loudly). Their beer "program" also makes me angry as they are too "cool" to carry Abita Amber.  I've been here several times so far and I've never gotten very prompt service and I just really haven't enjoyed myself in here so I have always left after one or two drinks. This place is just way too Hipster for my preppy soul and reminds me too much of a "gastropub" type place.  I'm sure I will get dragged here again by my cocktail snob friends so maybe I will eventually find a way to entertain myself here.  Maybe if I drink enough Jameson shots and start doing things with olives...

This place used to be a Little Tokyo and little seems to have changed since the name change to Ikura.  They have some good combo options and their sushi selection has a respectable number of choices.  The service could be improved as it seems that it runs slower than most other sushi joints I've been to anywhere ever.  Nothing really impressed me as above average while the food also didn't disappoint to below average so it really is just an average sushi and hibachi joint other than the below average service.

They have started doing a really impressive all you can eat experience here.  It is NOT a buffet but instead you get a special menu on which you can check off any of the items you want and do that as many times as you want.  Lunch all you can eat is cheaper than dinner and during my last visit one of my friends opted out of the all you can eat and ordered something off the menu BUT they ended up paying MORE than I did for the all you can eat option.  This is a really great deal they have going on now so watch out if it gets too popular.

Fancy new edition of the now pretty extensive Ruby Slipper chain that started in Mid-City.  They continue to execute with a reliable continuation that matches my experiences at the original and in some ways even exceed them.  I'm not a big breakfast person but they offer a decent array of brunch and lunch items for folks such as myself along with some rather well executed alcoholic beverages to add to the fun.  There was a bit of a wait as this location has grown quite popular so do plan on that if you are doing a visit during the weekend.

Mainly I recommend the super cold schooners of beer here along with the ambiance.  The menu probably has remained pretty constant since this place opened in the 40's so you can see what folks used to eat in NOLA dive bars.  Some of the seafood and semi-Italian dishes are decent to good but generally nothing is outstanding here.  The menu has some interesting items along with a selection of po boys and other sandwiches.  There is usually a pretty good collection of characters from the neighborhood here.  They only take cash so that is a pretty irritating inconvenience.

This event started off pretty slow and then picked up a lot more momentum as the night progressed.  There was good music aplenty and some great costumes.  The beer selection was typically terrible and disappointing as usual for the Sugarmill venue.  They definitely put a lot of time and effort into decorating the place and if you had to endure the Mayan apocalypse anywhere this was the best spot to do it in style.

This is a nifty little market space and food hall (reminiscent of a mall food court space) for multiple vendors just like the St. Roch Market and that should be no surprise as it is run by the St. Roch Market folks. There are selections of various foods and drinks available along with a few other interesting items. This is an interesting venue to visit if you want to try several different types of food all in one space. Long Chim, a Thai comfort food and street food vendor is probably one of the most interesting of the offerings here to me then it is nice to grab some dessert at Mac & Moon.  Overall this is a nice building that provides a good environment to enjoy some food and drink with a bit too much hipster, vegetarian and Vegan flair for my carnivore hunter soul.

Massey's is one of the best outdoor sport suppliers in the area for nearly any activity other than hunting or fishing.  This is their main store location and they have a great selection of clothing and equipment.  They also have kayaks for rent and sell new and used bicycles.  They often have some decent sales here and are one of the few local places or only local place you can find many outdoor items.  The only downside to this place is they have so much cool stuff you're always tempted to buy more than you intended whenever you walk inside.  Great selection, fair prices and good service make this one of my favorite places to equip myself for any adventure or just the adventure of daily life in NOLA.

This place was cool when it was on the lake and this new location doesn't give anywhere close to the ambiance the old spot had.  The food has always been inconsistent and generally you need to stick to either the fried or boiled seafood.  There are far better places to eat for the money but if you find yourself in Elmwood and craving seafood this is one of the few options in that area.

Giorlando's is a place you might quickly drive by and miss if you're not paying attention.  The parking lot takes a little getting used to and goes from deserted around 11am to packed by Noon.  They always have some good Italian food and I love the lasagna (and the chicken and veal parmesan).  They also have some very good po boys and the roast beef is very tasty here.  The service has always been friendly and quick and the atmosphere seems very family friendly.   I've only been here for lunch but this is a great spot for a quick and tasty meal.

This is a retro vinyl and local music record store of the likes that has nearly gone the way of the dinosaur.  They have quite an extensive collection so you can take up a lot of time browsing around.  Not a lot of music soundtrack stores of any kind left around most places these days with most everything having moved online so great thing NOLA moves at a different pace and lives in a different world than the rest of the world so we can still have a place like this.

I had my first taste of this marvelous place during French Quarter Fest.  I didn't realize how nearby it was to my usual haunt of The Old Absinthe House so I will certainly be returning the this very comfortable and well appointed hideaway from the nearby madness of Rue Bourbon.  The only thing I didn't like were the weird disco lights in the ceiling that seemed to clash with the elegance of the rest of this establishment's accoutrements.  I didn't have the opportunity to sample any of the wine and only had beer as I was in full festival mode so I look forward to returning for a more refined and vin amicable visit.  This will certainly become a popular stop after a long lunch at Galatoire's.

This was one of the most enjoyable dining experiences I had while I was visiting Nashville.  The old Victorian house really made the experience and ambiance really reach fantastic status.  If you are looking for the best biscuits in the area this place gets my vote.  The family style dining really helps you to meet other folks and then Monell's is really not letting any possibility exist you leave hungry from their table.  The only thing I would have seen as an improvement would have been if they offered some kind of pie or cheesecake for dessert as all we had was banana pudding and I'm not a fan of that stuff.  They also have a fantastic patio with great landscaping and have put a lot of effort into the flora around the building.  I highly suggest you do yourself a favor and enjoy a meal in this epic spot.

The menu here is a pretty confusing mish mash of dishes that are from all over the place.  Somehow they manage to pull off the widely diverging cuisines at a decent level. They have most recently added sushi to their selection of offerings.  This would be a place to go when you have a group that has people that all want different types of food.  In the attempt to be all things to all people Sun Ray ends up doing ok but not great food.   If they decided what type of restaurant they wanted to be they could probably pull off some great food with more focus as they obviously must have some serious talent to pull off such a wacky varied menu.

This is pretty much a tourist trap chain type restaurant.  The food isn't all that great but it is definitely better than the Las Vegas location.  I'm really confused why they can't seem to do drinks and food at least on par with the similarly themed but far better executed Bahama Breeze chain.  I seem to end up here about once every five years.  I like Jimmy Buffet and I wish he had higher standards for his restaurants.  The big bonus is you can get wasted away again in Margaritaville on  margaritas here but the bad news is they aren't that great here and I wish they had prickly pear flavored ones like the Z'Tejas chain does.  The upstairs is the best redeeming thing about this place so if you're going here make sure to get upstairs.

I've popped in and out of this place a few times.  Generally I find the space a bit too narrow and constricted for my taste when it gets crowded but usually it isn't too bad.  It does have a nice small courtyard in the back and a nice upstairs.   This place does seem much cleaner than a lot of the other Bourbon bars that seem to let their places just get all nasty and funky.  Overall a decent place to grab a drink if you're doing a Bourbon Street bar crawl.

This is actually a small local chain and they have two other locations in Bucktown and Covington.  The food has a slightly different flair than what you find at many New Orleans style food places and they have some unique items.  I've eaten at the Bucktown location often and only ended up at this location a handful of times.  The food is consistent and they generally do good food.  The Westbank can sometimes be a challenging place to find good lunch spots so this is a good place to have on your rotation when on the Wank.

Since moving into their permanent location this place has really flourished and achieved consistency in producing great pizza.  The space is pleasant enough to enjoy your pizza and the serving is large with the price being more than fair.  The topping selection is VERY limited but the menu selection has expanded to include things besides just pizza such as their stuffed rolls.  The crowds have grown along with their fame so this place does often get crowded on weekends.

The food and setup of the place just seemed exactly like Felipe's.  My chicken tacos were alright but I thought they were overpriced for what I got and I think more pricey by a tad bit than Felipe's.  So really not much else to say other than it is pretty much a slightly more coin version of  Felipe's with a different name.

3 stars for the food but -1 star for the price!  I had the Company Burger, which was a decent size burger, and the fires which were done very well but have to be purchased separately and were a very small size.  They have reduced the prices on their drinks from what was originally listed on their website menu and that has made this place a better value.  It still is a very pricey burger for what it is and I appreciate that they are using quality ingredients but it is still expensive even with that.  For what the burger costs here I can go to Whole Foods and buy enough grass fed beef to make a weeks worth of burgers!    The burger tastes very similar to one I get at an old food stand (that is on my way to my grandparents house in Mississippi that has been around since the '50s) and they have always used local grass fed beef and I can get their very similar burger for about $3.  You can also get a very similar and less expensive burger at The Camellia Grill or Clover Grill.  I might return but it won't be very often as at the current price level a Yo Mama's burger is a far better choice.  FYI the meat for burgers here comes from Creekstone Farms which is advertised as "all natural, hormone & antibiotic free" and is fed on a "vegetarian diet" but corn is a vegetable so they can still corn fatten the cows and meet this criteria.  So this standard doesn't mean the same thing as "grass fed" beef which is much healthier for you and has higher omega-3 fatty acids than fish!

Interesting place with a wide assortment of food items that seems to make it part restaurant, part coffee shop, part ice cream store and part grocery with a juice bar thrown in for good measure.  So with all that I was utterly confused they don't offer iced tea but they do have regular and sparkling water on tap.  The owner (that several reviews have complained about the service from) was working the front when I was there and she isn't the friendliest person I've ever met but she did fine taking my order as she was also very busy making food items so I think that is just her quirky personality which is fine with me but might be off putting to folks that need service with the big fake smile that aren't used to quirky personalities.  Seems like she is doing a lot of the work in this joint herself so she might just be exhausted too as running a business is a lot of work.   So I got the meatball parm sandwich and found that I wanted more flavor out of it with more herbs and more red gravy but overall it was an alright sandwich.  The fries that came with the sandwich were decent sized and quite a filling portion.  I finished my meal with oatmeal apple walnut ice cream although I couldn't taste any of those ingredients as the ice cream seemed to have too much ice content and seemed to need either more fat content or more churning or maybe both.  I think this place has potential and they have the ability to be good at some things but they probably need to focus more as they are a small space doing a whole wide range of things which makes it hard to focus on doing everything right all the time.  More work and possibly more training in the art of ice cream might be a good idea as there are some very creative flavors here that just need some tweaking.     I'd like to give them three stars just for being unique and creative but honestly there are better meatball poboys and better ice cream widely available in NOLA right now so I can't so I will just hope they will find their groove to earn extra stars on my next visit.

I really like the fun vibe and the ambiance of this place but I'm just not a fan of the whole Latin and Caribbean fusion style food into tapas concept.  I generally hate small plates and that is about the only type of plate you will get here.  I've eaten a few decent things here over the years since they first opened but really after several visits nothing has ever really knocked my socks off to motivate me to return.  They used to not have a corkage fee but the last time I ate there it was around $8 per bottle.  I can go to lots of other better places that serve much bigger portions of food at lower prices that don't charge any corkage fee.  I don't mind paying a corkage fee in a nice restaurant that already sells wine but this place is a far cry from fine dining and has no alcohol permit.  I love Spanish tapas but I just seem to strongly dislike Central and South American tapas as it seems I find most of it BLAH.  If you like this type of food you should be quite happy here but it just isn't my style of food... I think it might be because they don't use aioli and lack the power of enough GARLIC in their food!

Man I'm not sure what has happened here.  I don't know if it was a bad day or a pizza oven problem or maybe the heat of August, as the margherita pizza has always been good here, but the one I got yesterday was just AWFUL!  The pizza was tough as leather and dry as the Mojave dessert.  I had a friend that had never tried it that I talked into getting it with me and they were very unhappy with the choice.  I really hope it was just an off day but it was like a completely different pizza than I've ever had from Pizza Delicious before as it was plain awful!

Awful and slow service with mediocre food.  They threw bacon on my mac and cheese without even asking if I wanted it (which I don't) and when I dumped half the mac and cheese out onto the empty plate (they give you an empty plate with your silverware for some reason) with the bacon nobody ever asked if anything was wrong with it..  Getting a refill on my iced tea was a painfully long wait with no lemon given while closing my tab out was an unacceptably long wait when the bar wasn't even close to being half full during lunch (bar service should be faster than table service but not here).  This might be one of the best places to drink beer on the Wank but I wouldn't eat here again.  Bah humbug this place flaunts all the bad stereotypes of the Wank and creates new negative ones.

They open early at 8am for breakfast but I'm not much of a breakfast person so I've only been here for lunch.  They have a selection of entrees, sandwiches, po boys etc. of the standard NOLA fare.  They also have a decent bar but they close too early to have much of a bar crowd other than happy hour and Saints games (they do have a lot of TV's so this is a really great venue for watching sports).  I really only go here when I'm having to attend a training or some other type of event in the Quarter when I need to eat somewhere quickly and this spot usually gets me in and out fast enough to get back in time for when I need to be back.  If you're a breakfast person this place will probably be a good spot for you and it can work for a quick lunch or dinner.

This place is alright for the Westbank and for Mexican food.  It was just like nearly every other Mexican food joint with chips and items wrapped in some kind of tortilla.  I've had worse and I've had better.  Service was mostly on top of things and kept the drinks refilled in a timely manner.  The price was a bit more than I would have expected for the quantity of food.  The parking is kind of weird and a bit dicey exiting the parking lot the way it is setup.

This is a cool dive bar that draws a loyal local following.  Monday's usually feature Holly Tamale bartending and offering samples of her fantastic tamales.  In addition to the interesting patrons of the bar you also have the options of a pool table free jukebox for your entertainment pleasure.  As with many NOLA neighborhood establishments the patrons here come in all ages, styles and backgrounds so if you don't like that don't visit New Orleans.  It is a cash only joint so be prepared for that.

This location of Taqueria Corona seems to have a VERY different ambiance than their Uptown location even though the food and service is essentially the same.  The difference in ambiance might be one of the best examples of the difference between the city and burbs.  I find that the Metairie location lacks any charm, comfort, or fun vibe and I really feel crammed into this small strip mall space with their crowded seating.  The only thing this location offers that is better than the Uptown location is ample parking.  To sum up my feelings about the vibe of this place is that I absoutely HATE it and it is a typical strip mall BLAH place.    Most of the food here is similar to your typical Tex-Mex selection with some slight differences and offers some things most of the other area Mexican type places don't as the Honduran owners put their own slightly different spin to some things.  They have their "cebollitas" grilled green onion appetizer that is tasty.  They offer the usual taco, burrito, and other options wrapped in some type of tortilla like most Mexican joints do.  I usually opt for one of the entree platters to get a selection of several different things.  This is one of the few places to offer beef tongue as a meat option to stuff your taco or other tortilla wrapped entity.   Even though the food is nearly identical to the Uptown location I like it a GREAT deal less due to the very unpleasant environment.  The only reason for me to ever visit this place is that it is right next to an office I work out of and even then if I were going to eat Taqueria Corona and had time I would drive all the way back to the Uptown location to avoid having to be crammed into this uncomfortable space.  The Uptown location has a bit of charm and ambiance while this place makes me want to run as far away from the Satanic strip mall burbs as fast as I can.  Do you hear that sucking noise?  Its your soul being sucked up by EVERYWHERE else USA so fight it with all your might.

With the name Cochon you would expect everything pig to be fantastic here which I'm sure it is and so I have heard from many.  The problem I've got is I'm not really a fan of the pig so lots of things I'm not eating here like their signature andouille, boudin, or cochon de lait.  I've been here three times just to make sure I'm not a fan and I have now confirmed that they probably have the WORST and most flavorless beef brisket entree I've ever had in New Orleans (but remember the worst food in NOLA is probably better than most food in other places but I will grudgingly admit Texas is the all time brisket master champ) and the other non-pig dishes I've eaten have just been pretty mediocre with much better versions available elsewhere.  This food might be good to you if you never had a grandmother that cooked this type of food but mine could do ANY of these dishes far better.  What really confuses me is that the next door Cochon Butcher has much better tasting brisket and sandwiches so you probably would do better to just go there unless you worship at the high alter of all things pork.

Decent food in a decent new venue with prices that were a bit on the expensive side for what I ate.  This is a VERY casual restaurant and service seems a bit slow/disorganized/unprofessional/hipster with the waitstaff dressed in street clothes.  The menu somehow managed to be very large yet still didn't really offer a lot of options for main entrees so I guess maybe they are pushing more of a tapas/share appetizers type concept.  I had the salmon which came on a large bed of grits with a side of a few stalks of asparagus.  My friend, Da Goat, got the pork chop with mac n' cheese and green beans.  Both of us agreed the portion size was a bit on the smaller size for dinner entrees at the price point that was being paid and the food while decent just wasn't anything special.  The dessert menu prices were on par with NOLA's top tier fine dining restaurants so we opted out of that option.   Overall it was a decent experience but Da Goat and I agreed that we probably wouldn't make a return visit as there are just better options in the area for the price so Munch Factory probably should have stayed back in their original location.  Rating is 2.5 stars for the food and service while the location is very convenient and has a lot of potential.

I hate Ms Mae's and I love Ms Mae's.  I love the cheap drinks and some of the characters this place attracts but I hate the thick smoke produced by the nasty chain smokers that are attracted to this watering hole like moths to a flame.  Ms Mae's is also a very popular place for folks to get boozed up prior to shows at Tipitina's.    This place never closes so saying it is open 24 hours isn't really accurate as it is eternally open.  This is the place to seek when all others have called it quits.  So after you stumble into the bright and horrid sunlight when Snake'n Jakes kicks you out at dawn many of your fellow revelers will be heading to the eternal dankness of this high shrine to all things dive bar and boozed up.  They have several pool tables and other games to entertain the patrons as if the sheer ambiance of the cheapest booze anywhere isn't enough.  A fantastic place and a purgatory where you have no choice but to burn through the bargain booze that will cause such joy now and such hangover pain later.    They only take cash here and be prepared for anything as they have survived fire, hurricanes, car crashes through the front door and they still just keep going and going even with no ice and hot beer.  If a nuclear holocaust happened the two definite survivors in New Orleans would be the cockroaches and Ms Mae's.

This is a gas station that also offers po boys, fried chicken and other food items that are mostly fried.  They are open 24/7 so that really puts the "convenience" in their store.  This is one of the few gas stations convenient to the French Quarter and its usually easy to access with a nice selection of items.

VERY slow and disorganized service during lunch with no hostess so people just seated themselves but then some never got service (I saw a police officer arrive and take a seat for a long while and no staff acknowledged him so he finally got up and left looking pretty unhappy).  My food order took at least 45 minutes or longer to get out which is a really long time for the type of food served here.  Unfortunately the food itself really wasn't that great and it gets a 1.5 star for the tuna and burger (especially at the price point) as it really didn't deliver compared to most other places in the area.  I have always had good food at the Rivershack Tavern on River Road so I'm not sure what is going on here?  Granted it was really crowded here for just a Friday lunch and there were a lot of rowdy folks at the bar so maybe that was knocking the pace of service off?  The redeeming factors that raise the star rating up here are that this is a really cool bar that has some great features.  They have a nice outdoor patio with another rooftop deck patio on top of it with some great views.  I also have been a long time fan of the original Rivershack Tavern on River Road so I can't imagine the current state of unacceptable food will last long here as it has always been good at the original.  They also follow the original by having a nice schedule of live music.    Overall I was really disappointed in the food but impressed by the layout of the bar and the daily specials and happy hour that are offered.  I really hope they get better organized and get their food and service back on track.  This spot has a huge potential to be one of the great bars of the area and I hope they get things running consistently soon.  I definitely will return and hope for an improved experience next time.

I enjoyed the great fried chicken at Fiorella's in the French Quarter for many years and I'm glad that we now have the original family involved again making that great chicken at their new location in Gentilly.  The Fiorella fried chicken is legendary and it has been ranked by many as some of the best New Orleans style fried chicken in the city.  Fiorella's also has great Italian food options so you have a lot of great choices here.  I've eaten here several times now and I've enjoyed all of my food and I certainly will be making many return visits.  My video review of Fiorella's is here:  https://youtu.be/SXTJhJQJtfc

Haydel's Bakery has a great selection of King Cakes, Kringle Cakes, Wedding Cakes, Birthday Cakes and all sorts of other cakes and pies are made in abundance at this dessert wonderland.  Cookies, cupcakes, petit fours, fudge, cannolis and pastries are all available in abundance along with a fantastic selection of chocolate candies.  If you like delicious cakes, nice pastries, and other special desserts for the holidays Haydel's New Orleans cakes, cookies, pastries and other desserts are sure to interest you.  New Orleans has some very unique cakes with our Doberge cake, Russian Cake and King Cake that Haydel's does amazing versions of along with their great Christmas cake the Cajun Kringle Cake. If you need a custom cake for a wedding, birthday, anniversary or any other special event you can certainly get a great one done at Haydel's.  They also have a variety of other New Orleans themed gifts and food items.  This is a fantastic NOLA place to visit if you're in the mood for sweets and need to get your dessert fix.  They also ship many of their items if you want to spread some New Orleans sweet love to others that live outside of New Orleans.    My video review is here:  https://youtu.be/10IuqrsQH_s

This is a good dive bar with a sports bar ambiance that also has trivia nights and daily food specials.  They have steak day/night on both Tuesday and Thursday and for the price you get a decent filet and stuffed baked potato.  You might be curious as to why I call it a steak day/night and that is because their specials go on all day and they keep going til they sell out so if you want steak night for lunch this is your joint.  The barmaids are attentive and provide quick and friendly service.  This place is good for both lunch and dinner along with getting a bit of a happy hour crowd.  Overall this is a decent spot to grab some food or drinks or food and drinks in the area.

This is a generally good restaurant with several daily specials and a decent small bar.  Unlike most places they have MANY different daily specials.  I especially like the corned beef on Monday, the Reuben (made with the leftover corned beef) and lamb shank on Tuesday, the brisket on Wednesday, and the turkey on Thursday.  They have a pretty extensive menu and some good burgers, po boys, and other sandwiches.  They also make some pretty good fresh fried chicken here.  The big complaint I have about this restaurant is that they get most of their side vegetables out of a can other than their cabbage and potatoes.  It is so easy to get fresh (or at least frozen) vegetables that I find it so sad they don't choose to use fresh produce and doing so would greatly increase the quality of their food.  This is a solid choice for a quick lunch or dinner with many choices with consistently good food that could begin to get much better if they used more fresh produce.  Video Reivew Here:  https://youtu.be/CmBI-TRzWcE

This is a nice little neighborhood restaurant around the corner from Clancy's.  The building is a long rectangular shape that is on the smaller side and they have a very tiny outdoor dining space that you can request along with the inside lower and upper dining rooms that you will observe upon entering.  The "lower" room is adjacent to the bar while the "upper" room is entered by climbing a few steps.  Typically this establishment attracts a business casual attire crowd.   Sometimes the food is fantastic and sometimes it leaves something more to be desired.  One of my biggest disappointments with this place is that they have really small bowls for their soup and when you're paying $8-9 for soup you really deserve to get at least a real bowl and not some small ashtray looking vessel.  The burger here is a nice sized creation and has some good flavor profiles but it unfortunately tends to crumble apart far too easily.  The menu seems to have a great love of bacon as it seems to often figure prominently in many of their dishes.    Patois is probably best known for their amazing brunch and that is always a great choice here.  They can get a bit over the top with their desserts sometimes and they often have a good selection as an example on my last visit they had a white chocolate bread pudding with candy cane ice cream, creme anglaise, Herbsaint syrup, and macadamia. Personally I prefer the food at nearby Clancy's but this is always a nice option for a change of pace and different ambiance.

Mona's is always a consistent choice for decent to good Middle Eastern food.  This is probably my favorite location of Mona's and they have an attached Middle Eastern market here.  They have a nice outdoor patio dining area and the inside has some unique design features that give you the illusion you could be off somewhere in the Middle East about to feast.  I'm a fan of the combo kebab plate, the fried kibby and the Mona's Special appetizer combo plate.  I also like their iced mint tea as it is quite refreshing.  Service typically seems to be much more attentive and professional here than the other Mona's locations.  This is the same food you can get at the Byblos restaurants for a cheaper price and larger portions.  Some of the food certainly gets up to four stars but on average it is about a three star place.  It is also a market that has all sorts of interesting middle eastern grocery items that you can't really find anywhere else in the area.  It is like a cafeteria style dining arrangement where you order your food or you can choose things from the hot plates.  Most of the things I've gotten from the hot plates haven't been as good as in the restaurant so I usually go for one of the plate specials and those are almost always good.  The stuffed lamb plate was one special that I didn't care for as it was just lamb mixed with a bunch of rice and I missed my salad and hummus that comes with most of the other plate specials.  You get a lot of food here so it is a great value and an easy place for a quick lunch.  It is also right next to the Black & Gold store so you can grab some Saints gear and get ready for the game before or after lunch!!!  Mona's video review:  https://youtu.be/QUQbhgE0NRs

This is a classic New Orleans restaurant with strong Cajun influences that is a good spot for a relaxing lunch or nice dinner.  This was one of the first New Orleans dining institutions to start offering crawfish in a major way.  This is more of a fine dining restaurant with a bit of a casual feel but the prices are usually worth the quality of food that you get.  Lunch can get crowed but typically I've never had a problem getting in before Noon without a reservation but if you plan on a later lunch or dinner I would suggest making one.  The turtle soup, gumbo, crabmeat au gratin and all the dishes made with crawfish are great choices here.  Like many of New Orleans finer dining institutions the recipes here have remained largely unchanged for a very long time so the food might not be exactly what you were expecting so if you're unfamiliar with things you might want to ask for more details from your server.

The museum seems to be ever growing and they are adding more pieces to it all the time.  The main museum is located on several levels and it seems to contain a lot more Pacific theater items which is interesting as this establishment started as the D-Day museum.  They have lots of display cases with items in them and some written and interactive components that go along with each section.  I've been able to attend private party functions here and gotten to have the run of the place and they have a nice collection of items.  The one criticism I would have to give is that just like the museum's movie "Beyond all Boundaries" this place really over focuses on the U.S. to the almost complete exclusion of our allies and to watch the movie or tour the museum you wouldn't really know that the U.S.A. had allies during WWII.  A broader historical context would make for a much more educational and realistic picture of what WWII really involved and expand the "boundaries" beyond just the narrow view that America did it all.  The U.S. played a large role in WWII but so did many other countries and it is important to remember all those who sacrificed for their countries in those terrible times.

This joint was in my weekday lunch rotation when I worked in one of the nearby office towers and I hadn't been in a few years until a recent dinner.  I have eaten many more times at the location on Magazine Street but this location has been consistent with a some improvement in the service being needed at times.  This restaurant is a bit different from your typical Tex-Mex joint and offers some things most of the other area Mexican type places don't as the Honduran owners put their own slightly different spin to some things.  They have their "cebollitas" grilled green onion appetizer that is tasty.  They offer the usual taco, burrito, and other options wrapped in some type of tortilla like most Mexican joints do.  I usually opt for one of the entree platters to get a selection of several different things.  This is one of the few places to offer beef tongue as a meat option to stuff your taco or other tortilla wrapped entity.  Overall this is a decent spot for a lunch or dinner in the area but there are quite a number of decent choices around these days in this busy area of Metairie so make sure to sample as many as you can.

I had the most unusual experience of having a rock or some other weird type of road debris ricochet off my passenger side mirror and crack the door glass.  Broad Auto Glass was able to repair it like they do on a windshield and prevented the cracks from spreading.  There was a large crowd there on the Friday afternoon I got there and the workmen were gone a bit longer than expected so it took longer than it should have for such a simple repair.  They also do residential glass so they can also assist you with window repair or any other glass repair you need.

This place seems designed nearly 100% mainly for catering to the females.  That's a great thing as the ladies need more of their own spots besides just Phony Baloney (aka Bouligny) Tavern.  The Vintage actually has a few decent beers available for the gents while mainly focusing on the vino and bubbly to indulge the ladies.  The pesto meatballs here are a nice manly treat you can indulge yourself in here that are quite worthy of feasting on while maintaining your full masculine traits with no freu freu complications.  For those seeking beignets and coffee they also offer that but... seriously they sell booze and meatballs here so... maybe a coffee after lots of booze so you can drink more booze?  EXACTLY just add some whiskey to your coffee for the win!  A big plate of meat vs a petite plate of poofy floofy dough balls... ummm the plate of meat wins every time!   See it isn't that hard gents so go out and impress the ladies with your carnivore and ale quaffing skills.

The rooftop hotel bar trend seems to be taking hold in more and more spots with New Orleans catching up with the other cities that have had them for years.  My initial visit to this spot seemed to mirror my experience at most of the other rooftop bars with overpriced drinks to pay for the grand views.  There was live music and a free wine event during my visit but the patrons seemed be nearly all be tourists.  I actually came with a group of tourist friends that were in town for the U2 concert and we also tried their menu which seems to be tacos with chips and dips.  The food and service were attentive and the space was attractive for what it is but the space seemed way more Californian than NOLA style.  It just wouldn't really be on my usual rotation of places to go but I might take other tourist friends to check it out.

They are up and rolling at their new location.  The new space is a bit larger and more spacious.  The parking is a bit tighter than the old strip mall location but the building and location are much nicer.  Definitely an upgrade from the former location.  This is one of the BEST sushi restaurants currently in the area.  There were some others that came close but they seem to have dropped in quality while Kanno has consistently been excellent.  When I first heard about this place I was extremely skeptical as it used to be in a bit of a shady strip mall in Fat City and it didn't look that good outside or inside but once I tasted the food none of that mattered and now they have some upgraded fancy new digs.  They have an awesome blue crab roll and amazing soft shell crab spicy miso soup!    Elvis and his wife are the owners and work the sushi bar (and maybe you would guess there is a lot of Elvis artwork).  They have reserved seating for their VIP customers that eat there like twice a day as it is that GOOD!!!  You have to earn your spot in the reserved section so don't even try to sit in that area.  Everything I've had here has been outstanding and if you're really good they give you a tasty little frozen chocolate treat for dessert.  They are closed on Sunday & Monday and they take a long holiday back to Japan once a year so you might want to call to make sure they are open but they usually are and it is definitely worth a visit multiple times a week!!!

Bon Ton Cafe is being sold with their last day open under the current owners being Friday March 6th, 2020.  The new buyer plans a renovation and a late 2020 reopen.  Bon Ton has been a classic New Orleans restaurant with strong Cajun influences that was a good spot for a relaxing lunch or nice dinner.  This was one of the first New Orleans dining institutions to start offering crawfish in a major way.  This was more of a fine dining restaurant with a bit of a casual feel but the prices were usually worth the quality of food that you got.  Lunch could get crowed but typically I never had a problem getting in before Noon without a reservation but if you had planned on a later lunch or dinner I would have suggested making one.  The turtle soup, gumbo, crabmeat au gratin and all the dishes made with crawfish were great choices here.  Like many of New Orleans finer dining institutions the recipes here remained largely unchanged for a very long time so the food might not have been exactly what you were expecting so if you were unfamiliar with things you might have wanted to ask for more details from your server but now we have to wait and see what happens with the place.  Watch "Bon Ton Cafe... Closing?" on YouTube https://youtu.be/dF7r1edi3BE

This is a generally good restaurant with several daily specials and a decent small bar.  Unlike most places they have MANY different daily specials.  I especially like the corned beef on Monday, the Reuben (made with the leftover corned beef) and lamb shank on Tuesday, the brisket on Wednesday, and the turkey on Thursday.  They have a pretty extensive menu and some good burgers, po boys, and other sandwiches.  They also make some pretty good fresh fried chicken here.  The big complaint I have about this restaurant is that they get most of their side vegetables out of a can other than their cabbage and potatoes.  It is so easy to get fresh (or at least frozen) vegetables that I find it so sad they don't choose to use fresh produce and doing so would greatly increase the quality of their food.  This is a solid choice for a quick lunch or dinner with many choices with consistently good food that could begin to get much better if they used more fresh produce.

Went in here several hours before the LSU game and it was very very crowded with over an hour wait so I didn't get to sample the food here (but I've eaten at the one in Baton Rouge).  The tables around the bar are really cool with their own self-serve draft beer taps.  Looks like a decent place to watch sports and it is a nice space for a small group to watch a game together.  They probably should have made the actual bar a bit larger to accommodate more people sitting around it.  This place looks like it will be doing very well with the LSU crowd.

Fantastic food in a decent space with ambiance that tends towards more fun and casual than fine dining.  The downstairs dining room is a bit narrow and cramped with the tables rather near each other.  Service is excellent but not necessarily the most friendly and engaging.  The dress code is business casual but that rule doesn't seem very well enforced as it seems more tourist casual.  This is a very tourist heavy spot but it still has food that should appeal to the high standards of any local.   Certainly one of the top restaurant gems in NOLA that should be on your must do list for the experience of Paul Prudhomme's legendary cuisine.  Tip: The bread basket is great with carrot bread, corn bread, cheese bread and regular bread etc. with plenty of butter.

The French Quarter or  is the original core of the city of New Orleans.  Most of the original French buildings were destroyed by fire but a very few remain while the vast majority of the current Quarter was built by the Spanish.  This is where most tourists focus the majority of their time and there is a lot to experience in this area from world class restaurants to the wild debauchery of Bourbon Street.  Great events, such as the French Quarter Fest, are always happening and you would be hard pressed to ever be bored in this area.  The great thing about living in New Orleans is you can always be a tourist in your own town just by paying a visit to this part of the city!

This place often gets a bad rap as a tourist trap and it does, very often, have long lines outside of it along with tourist inflated prices.  I would never wait in line to eat here but they certainly can make good food.  They make nice roast beef, shrimp, and oyster po boys.  They have some decent gumbo and their crawfish etouffe has always been good.  When you walk in you have to go through a cafeteria style set up where you tell the staff what you want to eat, then you pay and then you find a table to wait for your food.  The interior of the place is much larger than what you might think, from just the outside, and there are lots of different areas with dark corners you can hide away and eat in this place.  There are too many other places to eat in the area for me to ever wait in line here but if there isn't a wait this can be a great place for a quick meal and I will often grab some food here before the Wednesday on the Square concerts.  I would never attempt to eat here on weekends!!!

This is really a small little spot that you might easily walk past and miss if you aren't paying attention but they certainly deserve your attention.  They have some good versions of items that not many other places in the area offer and then they offer some much better versions of items than many other Chinese places seem to push out of their kitchens these days which often seem like recently defrosted factory made food.  This place is similar to the quality and care in their food that Hong Minh and Little Chinatown put out except they are more expensive while also offering items those other establishments don't.    The dumpling selection here definitely has more of a house made and not factory made (then frozen and reheated) texture to it like many of the other Chinese restaurants offer so Dian Xin really seems to be putting out among the best available dumplings in the area now. Their Szechuan chicken was well spiced and was a large serving of mostly meat for the price but I would appreciate more vegetables in the dish.  Their hot tea selection includes items I haven't seen in a long time and it was quite nice to have some golden buckwheat tea again after many years without seeing it as an option around these parts.  The hot and sour soup was well flavored but I noticed there was no wood ear fungus in it which I consider to be pretty essential to a proper and HEALTHY part of any hot and sour soup.    The service was very attentive and kept the drinks refilled along with dealing well with my grumpy dining companion that was just all surly over several of the menu options being sold out already (do come earlier than later as they seem to often sell out of items these days).  The only big area of improvement I would argue for is that they could offer more dishes without pork as quite a large portion of the menu contains pork mixed in without even saying it is in there in true Chinese style but in the USA some more pork free options would be nice and accurately labeling the dishes with pork in them on the menu would be appreciated.    Overall I certainly look forward to more visits here to sample more of the menu.

This is probably the best steakhouse in New Orleans.  I might be slightly influenced by the fact I can walk here from my house but I frequently get requests from my friends to eat here.  Everything I've ever had here has been fantastic. The steak is usually the way to go but all of the other dishes I've had are great here too (especially the turtle soup).  This place changed ownership about 4 years ago so there have been some changes with the new owners.  Before Katrina I used to eat lunch here often and they had a great lunch menu (with some of the best meatloaf I've ever had anywhere) but with the new ownership they no longer do that menu and only have lunch on Fridays now.  I've always had a fantastic dining experience here with great service and excellent food and everyone I've ever eaten here with has thoroughly enjoyed it and demanded a return visit.

I've always had excellent food and fun times at Clancy's.  The only downside is that Clancy's is very much a neighborhood restaurant so parking is a bit challenging in the area and when it gets crowded it can get very tight on the street.  I'm also sad to have noticed that the dress code has pretty much disappeared and all sorts of people run around in blue jeans and all types of other uncivilized ruffian outfits.    It can get rather loud and boisterous in the restaurant at times and especially downstairs.  Some of my friends go to just hang out at the bar as they enjoy the social atmosphere so much.  The lunches I've had at Clancy's have always been a relatively calm affair compared to the night time fun with very few people in attendance.  Certainly a great spot to enjoy a great night of fun and excellent food.  The good news and the bad news is that it can be very difficult to find if you don't know where you're going so that is good news for locals that like to keep some of our secret spots to ourselves and bad news for tourists that will have a challenge finding it.  Please dress up a bit for traditions sake and come prepared for some great times and great food!

Russell's Short Stop is right at the intersection of Transcontinental Drive and Airline Drive and it gets very crowded at lunch.  The biggest problems here are just the sheer popularity of the place as it gets so packed and the lack of any good atmosphere.  The ambiance inside seems more like a fast food restaurant than anything else and everything involves standing in line to order at the counters.  This place is all about the po boys and lines are already forming by around 11:00am.  This seems to be the go-to place for po boys in this area and they also do a decent gumbo (seafood only available on Fridays).  I first ended up here as one of my friends told me it was the ONLY place she would eat a roast beef po boy from.  I certainly don't think the roast beef here comes anywhere close to the BEST roast beef po boy I've ever had but it is a good one and the other things I've sampled here have also been good.

Mona's is always a consistent choice for decent to good Middle Eastern food.  This is probably my favorite location of Mona's and they have an attached Middle Eastern market here.  They have a nice outdoor patio dining area and the inside has some unique design features that give you the illusion you could be off somewhere in the Middle East about to feast.  I'm a fan of the combo kebab plate, the fried kibby and the Mona's Special appetizer combo plate.  I also like their iced mint tea as it is quite refreshing.  Service typically seems to be much more attentive and professional here than the other Mona's locations.

King Cakes, Kringle Cakes, Wedding Cakes, Birthday Cakes and all sorts of other cakes and pies are made in abundance at this dessert wonderland.  Cookies, cupcakes, petit fours, fudge, cannolis and pastries are all available in abundance along with a fantastic selection of chocolate candies.  They also have a variety of other New Orleans themed gifts and food items.  This is a fantastic NOLA place to visit if you're in the mood for sweets and need to get your dessert fix.

This is one of the top spots in Metairie to get a snowball.  The good news here is the line and wait time is usually nowhere near to what you must endure at most of the spots in Uptown NOLA.  The bad news is the ice isn't nearly as exceptional and the flavors seem to taste commercial and not homemade.  It can still get crazy crowded here depending on your timing.  If you're in Metairie and need a snowball fix this is probably one of the more popular options but I'm much more a fan of Hansen's myself and you usually get faster service nearby at Casey's.

The museum has added a LOT more to their collection and it seems to be ever growing and they are adding more pieces to it all the time.  This establishment started as the D-Day museum and they actually still have two separate areas that cover D-Day in two different buildings which is a bit of a break in the continuity of the tour.  They have lots of display cases with items in them and some written and interactive components that go along with each section.  I've been able to attend private party functions here and gotten to have the run of the place and they have a nice collection of items.  The one big criticism I would have to give is that just like the museum's movie "Beyond all Boundaries" this place really over focuses on the U.S. to the almost complete exclusion of our allies and to watch the movie or tour the museum you would barely know that the U.S.A. had allies during WWII.  A broader historical context would make for a much more educational and realistic picture of what WWII really involved and expand the "boundaries" beyond just the narrow view that America did it all.  The U.S. played a large role in WWII but so did many other countries and it is important to remember all those who sacrificed for their countries in those terrible times.  I didn't see a single British/Commonwealth uniform or firearm in the collection while they do have a decent selection of the Axis powers equipment but they also don't really cover the many allies of the Axis powers either so they have a lot of important history to expand on.  They also seem to neglect to mention that National Socialist Germany and the USSR kicked of WW2 in Europe by invading Poland so they could each bring their unique brand of Socialism to the Polish people and then Western Europe declared war on Germany but somehow forgot the USSR's part in the Polish invasion and didn't declare war on them as well?  The museum seems to focus on WWII starting with Pearl Harbor for the USA but that really leaves out big chunks of WWII that deserve being included here and I hope they will continue to expand their collection to include those glaring holes in their collection and their story telling of World War II as history deserves to be remembered so we don't repeat it.  My review video is here:  https://youtu.be/6Nym77PW-cA

This place often gets a bad rap as a tourist trap and it does, very often, have long lines outside of it along with tourist inflated prices.  I would never wait in line to eat here but they certainly can make good food.  They make nice roast beef, shrimp, and oyster po boys.  They have some decent gumbo and their crawfish etouffe has always been good.  When you walk in you have to go through a cafeteria style set up where you tell the staff what you want to eat, then you pay at a cash register and then you find a table to wait for your food order that they bring out to you.  The interior of the place is much larger than what you might think, from the outside (so maybe Timelord tech is involved), and there are lots of different areas with dark corners you can hide away and eat in this place.  There are too many other places to eat in the area for me to ever wait in line here but if there isn't a wait this can be a great place for a quick meal and I will often grab some food here before the Wednesday on the Square concerts.  I would never attempt to eat here on weekends!!!  Overall a good spot to grab some NOLA food if the line isn't too long and they are one of the few spots to offer both a sliced roast beef and a roast beef debris as poboy options (the sliced roast beef has debris on top of it).  My video review of Mother's Restaurant is here: https://youtu.be/6zBhxGK352g

This is one of the BEST sushi restaurants currently in the area.  There were some others that came close but they seem to have dropped in quality while Kanno has consistently been excellent.
