When I first heard about this place many years ago I was extremely skeptical as it used to be in a bit of a shady strip mall in Fat City and it didn't look that good outside or inside but once I tasted the food none of that mattered and now they have been in a very upgraded location for several years and just keep getting better.  They have a fantastic selection of so many unique and creative rolls that are fantastically delicious along with an amazing soft shell crab spicy miso soup!    Elvis and his wife are the owners and work the sushi bar (and maybe you would guess there is a lot of Elvis artwork).  They have reserved seating for their VIP customers that eat there like twice a day as it is that GOOD!!!  You have to earn your spot in the reserved section so don't even try to sit in that area.  Everything I've had here has been outstanding and if you're really good they give you a tasty little frozen chocolate treat for dessert.  There hours have been more limited during the pandemic situation and during normal times they usually take a long holiday back to Japan once a year so you might want to call to make sure they are open and what the current hours are but they usually are and it is definitely worth a visit multiple times a week!!!  This is a smaller restaurant and with the pandemic lower capacity requirements you need to make a reservation to dine inside the restaurant.    My video review of Kanno is here:  https://youtu.be/1DgujQdCWDU

This is yet another location for the quickly expanding Mr. Ed's empire.  This is the nearest of their many locations to my house so even though I'm partial to their location in Bucktown I needed to give this one a try.  It was virtually deserted in here when I walked in for lunch on the weekend and the past history of failed businesses here might still be hanging a curse on this spot in some folks memories.  I sat at the bar and there were six TVs in the bar area along with one in dining room so this should make this a good game day spot.  Service was friendly and attentive (which as the only customer at the bar I would expect no less).  The gumbo was good and served with a lot of crab on top while my roast beef poboy was flavorful.    The price was a bit steep for my budget for a quick lunch of just a po boy and cup of gumbo so I probably won't be making this a regular stop on my lunch rotation but it is good to have another traditional New Orleans food option back on St. Charles.

Mama's Place is a fantastic neighborhood bar which for a small joint puts out far above average food for a bar this size.  They have great service, food and drinks along with decorating to the maximum for holidays. Mama's Place is known for having a really good bar food menu with some really nice choices that also include great burger options along with impressive daily specials and the best steak of any steak night I've tried at all the bars that offer steak night.  They also have a great off menu item that is sometimes featured as a special which is the steak sandwich which is a really nice item to sample.    Overall fun times, good food, great service and plenty of friendly folks make this one of the best bars in the area.  My video review of Mama's Place is here: https://youtu.be/uBjQDFDdfpg

I've eaten at other Gus's World Famous Fried Chickens and they were way more spicy and delicious.  The few times I've eaten at this location I just have found it strangely bland since we are in the birthplace of Popeye's spicy chicken so obviously we like spicy chicken in these parts!  So my last meal here a rat decided to run up behind me which NOLA has LOTS of rats so that really doesn't bother me as much as the lack of spice in the chicken.  I really enjoyed my Gus's chicken experience at other locations but sadly the NOLA location has constantly disappointed me in the flavor department.  My video review of Gus's World Famous Fried Chicken is here... watch for the rat!!! https://youtu.be/G3wwPjbnoJI

Decently sized bar in the CBD with decent drink prices that make it more competitive than many other spots looking to match New York City prices.  They have a lot of tables and in many ways it resembles a restaurant more than a bar.  Service is quick and friendly even when it is crowded.  The bathrooms are a bit small for when larger crowds are around but I'm not sure if that is a common occurrence.  The last time I was here there was also a band but I'm not sure how frequently that happens.

I end up here with a group several times a year prior to a long, fun lunch in Arnaud's and I also get here on my own as much as possible.  This is a fantastic old school NOLA bar and the only thing I dislike about it is that it can get very smokey sometimes.  As an old school bar there ends up being a lot of cigar and cigarette smoke here at times and I could seriously do without that.  Other than the smoke the ambiance is fantastic and they sling some awesome cocktails here.  This is definitely one of the best bars to enjoy yourself in the French Quarter and all of New Orleans.

COVID-19 has changed many things very fast in New Orleans but thankfully Clancy's is for the most part maintaining things as normal as possible.  It is very appealing to be able to have a bit of normalcy in this classic spot and it is one of the few bright spots still maintaining civilization in these dark times.  I've always had excellent food and fun times at Clancy's.  The only downside is that Clancy's is very much a neighborhood restaurant so parking is a bit challenging in the area and when it gets crowded it can get very tight on the street.  I'm also sad to have noticed that the dress code has pretty much disappeared and all sorts of people run around in blue jeans and all types of other uncivilized ruffian outfits.    In normal times it  can get rather loud and boisterous in the restaurant at times and especially downstairs.  Some of my friends go to just hang out at the bar as they enjoy the social atmosphere so much.  The lunches I've had at Clancy's have always been a relatively calm affair compared to the night time fun with very few people in attendance.  Certainly a great spot to enjoy a great night of fun and excellent food.  The good news and the bad news is that it can be very difficult to find if you don't know where you're going so that is good news for locals that like to keep some of our secret spots to ourselves and bad news for tourists that will have a challenge finding it.  Please dress up a bit for traditions sake and come prepared for some great times and great food!  Video Review Here:  https://youtu.be/u1vRkMxpVpo

This is a popular breakfast and brunch spot that often seems to attract a queue of people waiting to get in.  They have lunch during the weekday but the weekend is all breakfast.  The steak and eggs is probably the smallest portion of steak I've ever had anywhere for that dish and their hashbrowns seem closer to thick cut potato chips but everything is generally executed well.  I personally prefer veal grillades and here they do pork.  You can bring your own liquor or champagne and they have mixers to let you create your own Bloody Mary or mimosa treats.  Overall this is a good place for brunch or weekday lunch with friendly service but I wouldn't wait in line to get in.

I ate here soon after they opened and my food was very much not to my liking.  Some of the seafood dishes sound interesting but unfortunately I had the ropa vieja and I just completely didn't like anything about it.  I haven't been back since that experience but it sounds like from some of the other reviews that they have expanded their menu and added some good drinks so I might need to get back to sample some mojitos.  As a disclaimer I just really don't find most "Latin/South American style" food to my liking.

The New Orleans Museum of Art is beautiful space that rotates touring exhibits along with their own permanent collections set in the amazing venue of City Park.   I've got many memories of the Museum of Art with the earliest being making multiple trips to stand in LONG lines to see the King Tut exhibit and after many attempts FINALLY getting in.  Directly behind the museum is the sculpture garden which is a great spot to enjoy.  There are also frequently nice events and parties at NOMA and I've always had fun during these.  One ongoing event is "Where Y'Art?" every Friday evening at with activities and entertainment from 5 pm to 9 pm.  Check out their website to see the most recent information about exhibits.  This is a great place to visit!  Admission:  $10 adults ($8 with Louisiana ID) $8 seniors, active military  $6 children (7-17) Children 6 and under are free. University students with valid ID receive $8 admission. Wednesdays are FREE admission days for everyone

This is a pretty basic bar with circa 1970's decor in the usual strip mall type building on Veterans in Metry.  The beers were a bit more expensive than I would've expected for a dive joint like this on Veterans but I guess gentrification pricing is taking hold of the entire metro area.  They have a good selection of televisions so they live up to their sports bar name and provide adequate options for viewing the game of your pleasure.  I've never been here when much was going on but I could see how it could be a fun place with more folks around.

The PRC does a lot of great preservation work along with being a great resource for all things related to New Orleans historic architecture.  You can learn the difference between a Creole cottage, double gallery and shotgun house.  They also offer educational programs, home tours, and other events.  There are both permanent and rotating exhibits on New Orleans architecture and historic neighborhoods along with a gift shop.

This is probably one of the better places to both drink and eat Mexican in Mid-City but there are better Mexican places to eat at in the area.  The food is just like all the other Juan's locations in the area except they seem to have added a seperate brunch menu at this location which also probably has the most seating.  The bar layout here doesn't make it very good for watching sports and they only have small TVs that aren't easy to view.  The service here usually isn't as good as the Magazine location and the small parking lot is usually full.  This Juan's is much more restaurant than bar while the Magazine location is more bar than restaurant while the CBD location is still just working on getting the food right.

Very poor service from bottom service workers to the top of the leadership.  I ordered an Ultimate Chicken Sandwich and added cheese for 50 cents more along with a coffee.  It took over 30 minutes for me to receive my order and I first discovered my coffee was cold and then I found out they had left my cheese off the sandwich.  Well the receipt had a contact website address so I thought I could easily resolve this issue by using that so I logged in and submitted my details that I was owed 50 cents and displeased with the wait time and the cold coffee.  Every other situation in which I have made similar complaints I have at least received some sort of coupon and apology but Sonic simply sent me some automated response saying they appreciated my feedback.    I am still owed 50 cents!!!  I am also deserving of a hot cup of coffee and an apology for the excessive wait.

This is Deuce McAllister's restaurant and bar in the French Quarter that I'm guessing just pays Deuce a licensing fee for him to make appearances similar to what Harrah's does with Manning's.  Just like at Manning's where Archie can often be seen Deuce is often found here.  The food is a concise menu of interesting selections that are mainly Louisiana food.  The bar is large and is clearly designed to be a nice venue for watching sports. During the recent Ole Miss Sugar Bowl festivities this place was packed to the gills with Ole Miss folks including the new Chancellor.

This is a joint I mainly go to for buying gag gifts for "Dirty Santa" events and other similar parties.  They have a selection of naughty movies and adult themed "toys" and a few outfits that you can peruse.  This is probably a good spot for bachelorette parties to stock up on the naughty rando crap they like to haul around Bourbon Street.  It is located way off in the middle of an industrial park and can be a bit challenging to find as they keep a low profile of their building despite their many blinged up billboards.

I've eaten at this establishment several times and its got an interesting and fun interior design.  They have some interesting and decent pizza here but its nowhere near great and barely acceptable.  The crust is thick along the lines of a Pizza Hut pan pizza and I really prefer a thinner crispy crust.  They do have a buffet M-F but they have the WORST selection of any pizza buffet I've ever had with only pepperoni, veggie and cheese pizza as choices.  The beer here is also way overpriced so I can't suggest this as a fun boozing spot either.  I MIGHT return here just for one of their specialty pizzas but I won't be drinking booze or ever eating at their buffet again.

I love some kebabs and I was excited the website said they were planning lamb roasts every Sunday.  The chicken and falafel sandwiches are alright but the lamb pastrami is the best thing I've had here.  I could tell that they really take some time to use some quality ingredients in a lot of what they prepare but they still have a lot of kinks to work out.  One of their unique offerings is the young coconut they pop open for you to drink.    Areas that could use some improvement:  They didn't have any self-serve ice next to the drinks so that was a bit of a challenge.  They also got my tables order confused with a to go order so that caused a bit of mix up so they need to develop a better order system.  Something got burned and caused a really bad burned odor and fumes; so accidents happen but maybe a better venting system over the oven could help it from being so overwhelming a sensation when they do.    The website is a bit confusing with the hours listing being Friday-Monday  3PM-12AM and 3PM-12PM in different locations on the site so that needs to be cleaned up to fix the AM/PM confusion.  The environment was also a bit confused inside with half art gallery and half restaurant and I  don't think the art gallery did much for me other than limit my seating options.  The crowd consisted of a lot of really dirty unwashed gutter punks and other Bywater hipster types that gave off quite a bit of unpleasant body odor so just be prepared for the possibility that if enough of them are there you might want to just get a to-go order to avoid their retched stench.  I think the Bywater restaurants might want to start posting signs that say, "No shower no service!"    50 cent surcharge for using credit cards!  I completely understand how credit cards abuse business owners with their fees but you should at least post a sign stating that policy instead of telling folks after the fact or NOT telling them at all!  The specials board is very badly placed way over to the left where nobody will see it unless they know to look way over to the left above the drinks.  You need the specials right underneath the register where folks can see them as they are approaching to order so they know they are there and really you should hang a board above the register.  Overall there are just a whole lot of other Middle Eastern and Greek restaurants that have better food to me at this point in the city but I certainly see this joint has some potential if they get their act together as they are the only restaurant of this genre in the Bywater.  So I'm just going to wait and see what develops but I'm still going to go back to try the roast lamb and get another coconut.

I had the beef ramen and it was a good bowl of soup but it was a bit over priced at $10 as it was the same size as a small bowl of pho at most Vietnamese joints where you can get a large bowl of pho for less than $10.  The worst sticker shock was the $3.25 iced tea which I passed on and just had water and I was also a bit sad that they had no Abita Amber in their very small beer selection.  I had the blueberry & peach pie and I thought the crust was quite nice but it was a bit tough and I didn't find that I liked the combo of peach and blueberry as the flavor didn't really work for me.    The interior of this place has been made into a very bright orange so all the Tennessee and Auburn fans can find themselves right at home but I find it a bit glaringly bright.  The seating is not very comfortable and didn't encourage me to linger around and enjoy myself.  The music was way too loud and not very good so that definitely could have been turned down a whole lot.  This place definitely has zero New Orleans vibe about it and could have been ripped out of Austin or someplace in California or New York.  I liked the ramen but the rest of the scene was trying way too hard to be way too hipster.  I would definitely return for the soup but I'm not sure about the rest of the food and the ambiance is just not pleasant.    So in summary the ambiance is awful, the prices are a bit expensive, the ramen is really good and the pie has potential.

The Crunchwrap Supreme is probably the best thing I have tried here and it does taste quite similar to the Taco Bell version minus the stomach ache Taco Bell usually provides.  The burger is a bit on the salty side and for some utterly insane reason they don't have mustard and only offer nasty blasphemous ketchup (I HATE ketchup) so the only time I can eat the burger is if I bring my own mustard.  The tachos (tater tot nachos) just don't measure up to the amazing ones at 13 Monaghan so I probably wouldn't get those again.  Overall it is a decent place for later bar food at the Tchop Yard.

This is a Pakistani restaurant with a selection of American food.  They have quite a few goat dishes and also cater to vegetarians.  The food is ok but somewhat overpriced and they also don't have brewed iced tea available and only offer bottled drinks which is a pet peeve of mine.  There is no table service but the guys behind the counter seem friendly enough.  Personally I would much rather go to Nirvana than this place.

This is a nice hotel bar that just opened in the newly launched Hyatt French Quarter.  They have a small batch bourbon theme and since I like bourbon that might just float my boat.  They have some nice bar food and the ambiance and crowd is more upscale than you will typically find stumbling along on Bourbon Street.  This is definitely an easy bar to access right off Bourbon so it will definitely  be added to my list of civilized reprieves from the often barbaric hordes that overtake the French Quarter.

They have taken their sign down from the building and the website no longer works so it appears they have finally imploded from their lack of quality.  They started out so strong when they first reopened after Katrina and had lines out the door of people waiting like no other restaurant I've ever seen open in the NOLA area before.  Sadly they squandered that huge fan base with poor service and bad quality food.

The longest bridge in the world!  At least until the Chinese finish the longer one they're building.  This was and is an engineering marvel that opened up the Northshore to become a suburban mecca for many more people.  Personally it would be a living hell of a nightmare to me to have to commute over this long bridge to work daily and I respect the tenacity of those many souls that have chosen that way of life and I pray with all my might that I NEVER have to do such a daily commute unless it was in a Lear jet.  I already hate commuting from Uptown to Metairie for work and miss the days when I still worked in the city and had a commute time of about 2 minutes.  For those times I need to get to the Northshore I'm glad we've got this nice bridge but the speed limit of 65 taxes my need for 85mph speed but they always have lots of police waiting to give out tickets to those with superior driving skills and a need for speed so sadly Speed Racer is not welcome here.

This space has seen quite a few restaurants come and go in relatively short time spans.  I'm not sure this one is going to last either as they don't seem to quite be up to the standard needed to survive in the competitive restaurant scene of NOLA.    On my last visit I had their burger which at $10 was a fair price but it was served on quite a small slider size bun with a thick serving of meat.  The burger tasted decent but it doesn't come close to the amazing burger at nearby La Petite Grocery.  I was disappointed they didn't have Creole mustard and the french fries were limp and lacking much in the way of flavor along with actually seeming to be rather under cooked.  I ate at the bar and was given a water but somehow I never had my drink order taken so I would've ordered an iced tea but I never got the chance to order that.  My friend enjoyed the fried chicken they had so that might be a worthy item to sample.  Overall I'm not sure I want to return but there were some other interesting items on the menu so perhaps they will improve with more experience so I will wait and see for now.

This technically isn't a dog park but its 100% de facto used as a dog park all the time.  This is the best doggie paradise anywhere around the French Quarter and the dogs have a fantastic time here.  There are lots of plastic chairs in the park and a covered pavilion area with picnic tables.  There are many tennis balls strewn about the place and plenty of people hurling them for dogs to race after.  All size dogs are constantly running around and having awesome dog times.  If I were a dog I would really appreciate my human bringing me here for some serious dog time!  This place is also near Veri Marte and while it might seem tempting to grab some food and picnic in this park that's generally a bad idea as the dogs will go crazy over your food!!!

The french fries here were very good and some of the best I've had outside of duck fat or goose fat fried ones.  The burger was "ok" but it certainly seemed overcooked on the outside and it just didn't seem like anything I couldn't do better on my own grill.  The chili was good but for my taste it could have used a lot more spice and I wish it was served with some hot peppers.  For the price it really wasn't worth it and I would much rather have the burger at Chateau du Lac than here.

I drive past this restaurant often on my way back from work so I decided to stop in and try it.  The interior is very small with just one communal table and the rest of the seating being at the bar.  It seems to be going for a trendy and hip vibe and I was the only person in the restaurant as it was still a bit early for the dinner crowd.    I was provided with some nice complimentary bread served with pureed acorn squash and another condiment that I think was some type of fig preparation and that was a nice start.  The menu had some interesting items on it that seemed to be pretty unique and ultimately I decided to just get the lamb kabob entree.  I was sitting at the bar but there is a bit of raised area still between you and the server and you get served like a bartender would serve you so they kept my iced tea and water both full so service was efficient.  My entree was interesting with two ground meat lamb kabobs on sugarcane skewers which were then placed on a bed of salad mixed with various vegetables and pasta.  There were certainly some unique flavor profiles in the meal but when it came time to pay for my entree and iced tea the total with tip cost $31.16 which really made it a poor value as I didn't think I got very much food for my money.    Overall this restaurant has some interesting ideas going on but the location, ambiance and dining style don't seem to rate fine dining prices.  The desserts were surprisingly very standard with nothing very unique about them at all other than being as expensive or more so than most of the best restaurants in New Orleans ($6-$11) so I didn't even bother trying them. It is an interesting concept but I don't know how they are going to attract a lot of repeat business at their current cost structure.  It was interesting to try once but at the prices they are charging there are a whole lot of other better restaurants in town I'd rather spend that kind of money on.  For diners that are looking for something quite different than the usual New Orleans dining scene this will certainly give you a new experience.  I will give them 4 stars for their unique dishes but 2 for price and 1 for the dessert menu so let's call it a 3 star overall experience.

This is another location of Sun Ray Cafe group and the food is very similar to their Warehouse District location while the ambiance is completely different.  The Metairie building is smaller and more intimate than the wide open space of the Warehouse location.  This location is a bit hidden away behind some other buildings right off Metairie Road so you need to know where your going to find it.  The food at all Sun Ray's is very expansive and seems to include influences and offerings from numerous cultures and traditions from sushi to a mish mash of dishes that are from all over the place.  Somehow they manage to pull off the widely diverging cuisines at a decent level and there should be something for almost any taste here.

I ate a late lunch here for Good Friday and was one of two occupied tables in the establishment so I had very attentive and rapid service.  They have a small menu and I decided to try the French onion soup and the fruits de mer crepe as I still dream of the wondrous, spicy, delicious fruits de mer pastas I ate in the South of France.  The server brought some excellent French bread and butter to snack on while I waited for my food.  The soup was brought out very rapidly in a good portion sized bowl and was a tasty example of the classic.  When my main course arrived it consisted of two large crepes with a drizzle of sauce and the seafood inside was supported by a cream sauce.  While the dish was good and VERY filling I was a bit sad it gave me no memory of those marvelous seafood dishes I had back in France.  This place is BYOB with no corkage fee and the interior is quite nice so it certainly appears to be a great place to bring a date of enjoy a night with a group of friends.

I've eaten here at lunch many times and dinner a few times and always enjoyed nearly everything I've had here.  The one thing I didn't really enjoy was the burger but I've only sampled the burger at lunch once and it wasn't among my favorites (it isn't a bad burger it just doesn't compare to others in its pricey category).  They also make some fantastic cocktails and it always seems to be a fun place to enjoy a meal.  The biggest issue here is the parking which can be a challenge in the area.  I've always managed to get in without reservations but it might be a good idea to get a reservation for dinner.

Lakeview is one of the most modern areas of New Orleans and has a lower density of bars and restaurants.  This is one of the places where people move after they get married and have children so there are lots of families here.  There are some fun bars and restaurants in this area but it has a much more suburban feel than most of the other neighborhoods in New Orleans.  There are still many deserted houses here from Katrina and the area seems to be recovering slower than other areas but there are some fantastic deals on some nice modern houses that can appeal to many people.  This neighborhood also gives you the opportunity to live right next to Lake Pontchartrain and all the amenities that it offers.

This is a good Vietnamese restaurant with a pretty good selection of different dishes on the menu.  There is a selection of bubble teas but they have regular, and not my preferred jasmine, iced tea.  They have many different versions of pho and offer a seafood version which is nice.  This is probably my least favorite tasting chicken pho along the Vets Blvd (it isn't bad it just isn't as good as the other places) but it is also probably the cheapest (probably about $3 cheaper than other spots) so that makes it a great value!

I had previously only been to the original Sucre on Magazine and recently found myself in the area of the Metry location and decided to stop in and check it out for comparisons sake.  It definitely seemed to have more of a suburban feel to it than the Magazine location.  It seems much larger on the inside but at the same time less posh.  Overall I'm still loyal to my hood's Magazine location and prefer it but I can tolerate being forced to go to this one in a pinch as the desserts are all just as good as the originals while the service was definitely less professional/mature I would observe.

They have some really large lunch specials here that give you a lot of food.  The sushi has never seemed like the best quality but it has never been terrible either.  Nothing has ever really excited or inspired me here and it has all seemed pretty basic.  They do have a parking lot that is across the street and it can be a bit of an adventure crossing St. Charles at that spot depending on the time of day.  Overall a decent spot for lunch and a good value.  I live really close to this restaurant but I've only been for lunch so I can't comment on how this place is for dinner.

I didn't have very high expectations about the food (beyond maybe a good burger) going in for the first time but I was generally pleasantly surprised by the options.  The theme here seems to be a mash up of Hooter's, Twin Peaks, Walk Ons and Copeland's but with generally better food.  The menu is full of traditional New Orleans fare and a very respectable selection of seafood.  I had the gumbo and it was quite good with larger shrimp than you generally get in gumbo.  I also had the burger and it was a decent tasting larger burger but I probably wouldn't get it again as there are better burgers elsewhere and there are so many better dishes on the menu here that I want to try.  The service was far too slow many times so they still have some new restaurant breaking in to do but the food was all good.    The parking lot was completely full during my lunch visit so there is still the new restaurant initial run of crazy crowds going on here.  My server informed me that nobody has yet conquered their burger challenge which is to eat a 7 patty burger within 30 minutes (that burger is about $50 and your prize is you get to eat it for free if you complete the challenge).

This is a great outdoor space that is part of the fantastic City Park and New Orleans Museum of Art.  They have a nice selection of sculptures and the landscaped area is nice for enjoying the outdoor environment.  This exhibit has the exorbitant cost of entry set at FREE.

This is probably the most dive of dive bars in Mid-City.  I might even go so far as to say that if Snake 'n Jake's and Ms. Mae's had a baby then this was it and they abandoned it and kicked it out to live in Mid-City.  The biggest claim to fame of this place is the sheer dirt cheap prices of their drinks.  I think I would be completely accurate in saying these are the cheapest drink prices you will find anywhere in Mid-City.  The clientele in here seems to generally be intent on getting as completely wasted as possible so that has its good and less good points.  They have a really cool back area with all sorts of video games and other entertainment along with a lounge couch area that could be somebody's living room.  I'm also a big fan of the fact that they serve their draft in full Imperial pints making it an even better value.  This place seems to ALWAYS have people in it but I've rarely seen it really crowded.  This is definitely a place to experience just for the sheer entertainment of the wasted drunk characters imbibing in this place and the cheap drinks just add to the value of the fun.

Its a chain and its focus seems to be as a coffee and dessert establishment that also has some fast food French bistro options.  I've been dragged here for a few meetings and if you must go to a chain this is certainly a better one that offers acceptable quality.  It definitely isn't ever going to be my first choice but at least I know if I get trapped in some unfamiliar suburb in Texas and see another one that I can at least expect some decently edible food that won't be Tex-Mex.  This location ALWAYS seems to be packed and they are very busy here so parking can be a challenge.

They have some good prices on their daily lunch specials and do nightly dinner specials like a steak night and oyster night.  At lunch the service is very fast as I've never been here when there are more than a handful of folks here.  Definitely a spot to grab a quick lunch.  The burgers are decent and they have a good selection of other items to choose from but I find their fish dishes to be overpriced and on the very expensive side for the area.

This place deserves NEGATIVE stars!!!  I just had one of the worst meals of my life here.  They served me the all time worst brisket I've ever had along with some of the worst chopped beef.  My "roasted" corn was burned and charred black.  This was a seriously disgusting meal and the brisket looked and tasted atrocious!  I would not feed the brisket they fed me to a dog.  This place gets my vote for one of the worst restaurants in the NOLA area!

This review is mainly for the pool, patio, and bar area.  This is a fantastic spot, that not many people frequent, where you can grab a relaxing drink and just enjoy the outside when it is nice weather.  There is a great observation deck where you can get some great views of the city and watch the activity on the Mississippi River.  Really one of the great hidden venues of the city!  The hotel as a whole is a fantastic place with many fantastic features but the pool area is by far my favorite!

I liked the French Market a lot better when it was mostly a food market.  Now there is a lot less food and LOTS of tourist trinkets, souvenirs and clothing items.  There are some cool NOLA items here that would make good gifts for folks and that seem locally made but there are a whole lot of things made in China too.  Ultimately its certainly something most tourists will have to do but I wish we could make it a nicer and more food focused destination like traditional markets in other cities are.

The prepared foods here are four and five stars all the way while the grocery selection is more of a three star limited selection at higher prices.  The location is next to the Jewish Cemetery and its an old fashioned style smaller market with a decent assortment of produce and nice collection of local New Orleans foods.  The butcher and meat department really does some excellent work and this is great place to get your carnivorous needs cared for.  This place definitely has a lot of unique NOLA charm to it that you just won't find at many other larger stores.

This is the nearest coffee shop to my house and they have good WiFi.  I'm generally not the coffee shop type but they do have their occasional uses for me.  They don't have late hours so that makes it way less useful to me than the recently departed Rue de la Course that converted to being Ignatius the larger.  During daylight and early evening this is a decent place to get some work done but their closing hours of 5 or 6pm aren't conducive to my usual work patterns.

I think this is probably the nicest location of Slice but it can be really challenging to park as its so near to the parking madness around Whole Foods.  If all your in the mood for is one slice of pizza this is probably the best place to get a highly customized slice to fit your hearts desire.  The pizza here is ok to me and I like the availability of all the topping choices.  I still rarely end up here as when I'm in the mood for pizza I usually go to Theo's, Pizza Delicious, or the $5 pint and a slice deal at New York Pizza.  This is certainly a decent place for a slice but I always need more than one slice!

The ambiance here isn't my favorite as it has the restaurant crammed into a high rise office building feel.  The bathrooms are a bit of an inconvenient hike to access here and you have to go outside the restaurant and into the lobby past the elevators to reach them.  The bar doesn't even appear like it is really used very often.  I think this is mainly a lunch spot for folks that work in the building and dinner never seems very active.  The food is actually pretty decent here and probably is one of the better options in the immediate area but there are definitely better places not much further away.  Service is inconsistent and it often takes far too long to get your drink refilled or order another alcoholic beverage.

Its Italianish meets Middle Easternish food here with ok results at a decent price.  There never seems to be a lot of people in here so you usually get pretty quick service.  The location near City Park is nice along with having a nice patio seating area.  You can definitely get better Italian and Middle Eastern food at other restaurants in the area but I guess they must have something that they might do better here... maybe their salads are a bit better... maybe... sometimes.    Generally most things are ok and they have some interesting specials but I'm definitely not a fan of their lasagna.  Nothing awful here with many decent items (like pizza) but definitely not my first choice most of the time as it is mostly all a bit blah and bland here and there are just so many better options in the area for my taste.  The food here reminds me of a blander version of Fresco Cafe and Pizzeria on Maple Street.  The draft beer prices are crazy as draft beer should be cheaper than bottles but Abita beer bottles are like $3.50 while draft is $4.25 so that makes no sense.

Wham! What happened to the PJ's that was here?  Ok a new joint so I will try it out and not even read any Yelp reviews first as I just want some espresso or maybe just a coffee so how can that go wrong?  Bam!  The juice and coffee are expensive for the very small serving size.  This is the smallest espresso serving I've ever had anywhere in the entire world.  This is also the single most expensive wheat grass shot I've ever had anywhere.  The pastries and such food items I saw looked nice and all but I really don't care about those items for the most part and I just wanted some caffeine.  The ambiance and concept of the place are nice enough but the prices and serving size just don't make this a place I plan on making a return visit.    Overall I have to rate it a "No Thank you Ma'am" as the small serving size and expensive price for juice and coffee just don't work for me.  They also close at 7pm and as a night owl that's way too early for me and I need 24/7 spots.  After my experience here I promptly went down the street to New Orleans Coffee & Beignet Co. for a large dose of caffeine goodness at a fair price.    Wham-Bam-No-Thank-you-Ma'am!

This was an interesting spot that I visited for the first time on a Yelp pub crawl on a party bus.  I had driven by this place many times on fishing trips but hadn't really even noticed it was a bar.  I was impressed with the fact that I had to get buzzed in and that made me feel all happy as all the other bars I've ever had to get buzzed in are pretty cool places.  The bartenderess was very friendly and tolerant of our group (as most of us stumbled in with our outside drinks still in hand).  Most of what I remember in here was a frightening haze of red light that was much more intense than the red light in Snake 'n Jake's and when I was a child I used to have a nightmare about being trapped in a room with this same haze of red light.  I have finally discovered that my nightmares as a child were all about the Roaring 20's in that their beer selection doesn't have any local Louisiana beers or special beers at all beyond Bud, Miller, and Coors products... nooooo I need my Abita Amber!!!  Other than the limited beer selection and crazy red light this seems like a decent spot to experience on the West Bank.

This local chain seems to be spreading its octopus like tentacles all over the Greater New Orleans metro area.  Fortunately I like octopus so I can eat the tentacles.  With their many locations and large scale buying ability they seem to offer some good seafood options at decent prices.  While Little Tokyo isn't usually my first choice it is always a reliable choice for decent to good sushi and Japanese fare.    This is probably my least favorite location of all the Little Tokyo's due to the location in a narrow strip mall space.  This location does take a bit of a different spin on their usual formula and specializes in ramen, Yakitori (Japanese Shish kabob), and Shabu Shabu (Japanese Fondu) so if you're in the mood for something a bit different you might find what you need here.  The location is much smaller than their other spots and the service is inconsistent.  The music volume and choice is generally unconducive to my dining pleasure.  Overall the experience rates around a 2 star for me as they have often gotten my order wrong along with everything else.  They are open til around 2am so if you're in this area that does give it a bonus star for a late night option.  I also agree with the other reviewer that noted that the rolls here are frequently made far too loose.  I find this to be a Little Tokyo wide phenomena at all their locations and it is a real irritation and detriment that could be easily fixed.  The Mario painting on the wall terrifies me...

The festival itself is a 5 star experience but the ever increasing prices and crowds drive it down to three stars.  They have fantastic food and great music at this festival.  This is probably some of the best food you can find at any festival anywhere in the world!  I would love coming to the fest just to eat on all the tasty treats so the music is just a big bonus!  This is always an amazing event and it is hard not to have a great time here.  It often does RAIN and flood the fairgrounds so wear clothing/shoes that can handle water up to your waist.  When it doesn't rain it can get really hot so wear a good hat, use sunscreen, and drink lots of beer, liquor, and water.  The Brass Pass from WWOZ is a great thing to get if you're planning on going for all the days of the fest with the added benefit that you can leave and reenter.  I wish it was cheaper as the ever increasing prices have forced me to curtail my preferred everyday fest to having to be very selective about the days I'm going to attend.  They also offer some discounted packages for each weekend so you can get slightly cheaper tickets that way if you're planning on doing all the days on the first or second weekends... what other fest does so many days?  Jazz Fest just kicks the pants off all other fests!

I actually got dragged into the Westbank Victoria's Secret with a girl I was dating after we ate some Vietnamese food.  I had no clue that they had a Victoria's Secret on the Westbank so big surprise bonus points!  Hot lingerie with hot chicks modelling it and hot chicks trying it on all with hot chicks working in the place... What's not to LOVE this is actually a man's paradise!  I was a bit antsy on exiting the store when I noticed a rather grumpy looking man wearing Middle Eastern garb who was sitting at a bench directly in front of the store reading a Koran and looking a bit disapprovingly at us as we came out of the store... he didn't fool me one bit and I busted him and he knew that I knew he was there just to check out the ladies!

The same people that own Bulldog and Velvet Cactus own this joint and that used to be a great thing but now its all gone way too corporate for my taste.  The food here is definitely at a higher level than the Bulldogs but it used to be a whole LOT better and I would eat lunch here often but the quality and selection at lunch has definitely declined so I don't eat here anymore.  Similar to the Bulldog they specialize in good quality beer and I used to stop off in here during parades on Vet's (such as the the St. Patrick's/St. Joseph's).  This used to be one of the cooler bars for drinking beer on Vet's but I generally stay in the city and the beer here is expensive compared to surrounding establishments.

I love Theo's Pizza!!!  This is probably my favorite pizza place around.  The thin crispy crust makes me a very happy eater.  I enjoy the wide range of interesting combinations they offer.  The Eccentric & the Spicy Mexican are two of my favorites but my usual fix is the Hippy with either chicken or meatballs added.  I always get a side of their tasty marinara to dip my crust into; although often it isn't needed I still love the sauce and will just drink it!    I also really love their ice as it goes so well with their iced tea and I think it might be the best ice in NOLA and I want to find out what kind of machine makes it as I want one.  They also have good beer and wine specials.  The sandwiches are very tasty but maybe a bit overpriced for their size.  The salads have always been very good also.  I have heard a few negative reviews from some of my friends about the Canal Street location with their crust not being done properly but I've never had a problem at the Magazine Street location.

Remember that time at One Eyed Jack's?  Well if you don't this is a bar and entertainment venue that resembles an old fashioned theater.  On nights when they have performances you can still drink in the front area that has a bar without paying to see the stage side performance.  The front bar area is nice with some comfortable couch seating and bar stools.    The stage side has its own circular type bar that has some bar stools around it.  Additional seating in the stage area is available along either wall in booths and there are some stand alone chairs available.  They also have a small balcony area that will accommodate a few seats.  On my last visit I saw (for the first time ever in any French Quarter venue) a patron kicked out for being too drunk after he bumped into a table and knocked a bunch of beer bottles on the floor.  They are also noted for their Thursday 80's night but every time I've attempted to go to that there has been a long line and I'm not waiting in line for that (I hate lines and I won't do them hardly ever).   Overall this is a nice venue to see a show or just hang out in the bar.  The service is generally reliable and the drinks are acceptable.  The shows and performances here draw a mix of locals and tourists with generally a decent crowd of folks.  They often will get music and other performances that aren't generally featured elsewhere in NOLA so you can often find something interesting going on here.  So based on all these facts I think we can conclude that this fine establishment was actually named for the "road house" in Twin Peaks: Fire Walk with Me.

This is one of Dickie Brennan's fine dining establishments that is on Canal Street and  the prime location makes it a very popular destination for tourists and the beautiful interior draws and keeps locals.  There is multi-tiered seating that really is  unique in NOLA and the upper levels can really give one an interesting view.  In addition to the marvelous interior they have a small outdoor "patio" seating area on the sidewalk.  Unfortunately this restaurant's prime tourist location results in lots of sloppily dressed tourists that lower an otherwise upscale ambiance.    I've eaten at the Palace many times for lunch and a few times for dinner.  Generally I've enjoyed my meals here and had some good times.  Unfortunately the food can be inconsistent at times (especially when it is slammed full of tourists) and this is the only fine dining restaurant in NOLA I've ever had to send something back (a fish dish charred and burned black... not just the fish but the entire dish had a coat of carbon burn and it wasn't even blackened fish).  One of my friends was the manager on duty at the time so I was taken care of quite rapidly but I was just  amazed that they even served such an obviously burned plate of food to my date.  The other issue I've run into here, especially during lunch, is that it can sometimes take quite a long while to receive your food (If I arrive at noon when it is slam packed then I can understand but if I arrive at 11am when hardly any other customers are there I'm less understanding when I need to be somewhere).  If you aren't in a hurry and have time for a leisurely lunch or dinner then this will typically be a fantastic place to enjoy a nice NOLA style meal.  The food here is generally fantastic and seems to focus more on seafood.  The desserts have always been nice and the interior elegance of the space is pleasant to dine in.

They have a lot of stuff for all sorts of projects, crafts and hobbies along with toys.  The main problem here is finding anything as there is just so much stuff but fortunately the staff can usually direct you to what you need.  They seem to have some good sales here but some of the items seem a bit overpriced when not on sale.  It will be the main game in town for many items so I expect this will be a popular location.

In the spirit of full disclosure I have to say I honestly miss the previous bar at this location, the Mermaid (that was a super dive bar nearly on par with Snake'n Jakes for sheer shady dive awesomeness with the addition of cool live music a la Saturn Bar like).  They did quite an extensive renovation of this space and it looks all very shiny, new, and Warehouse Districty like now with none of its past dive glory remaining.  This is the headquarters of all things associated with the University of Alabama and they have nearly all their local events here.  During college game days this place will be at least 99% Alabama folks and a whole lot of them any other time.  They do have food here but I've never sampled any of it but it looked like some decent outdoor grill type fare.  They have a nice outdoor patio and it is great that they are non-smoking inside.  Parking can be very tight and often a pain in the area so I usually try to park farther away and walk a bit to avoid the congestion and crazy parking people do that often block other cars in.  So far I've had ok times here but nothing close to the fun I used to have at the Mermaid Lounge.

On arrival I was happy when they brought out a large decanter of salsa and a small container of bean dip with complimentary chips.  The salsa was rather unremarkable and sadly rather bland; while the bean dip was rather bean tasting.  My combo plate with a taco, burrito and enchilada all pretty much tasted interchangeably the same and uniformly bland.  It wasn't bad but it wasn't all that good either and just was an overall very bland meal experience.  I probably will not return as the food just lacked in the flavor department.

The burnt ends were tough and just not really well executed while my mac 'n cheese really lacked cheese along with the cheese biscuit also needing some work.  The BBQ plates here also only come with one side which is out of line with all the rest in the area that offer at least two with the base price.  The original Ugly Dog in the Warehouse District never had the best BBQ in the area but it is much better than this.  Nobody in my group enjoyed our meals so sadly this place really failed us and none of us are likely to return.  Now that The Joint is offering the top burnt ends in the entire state you better bring some serious game to play in the BBQ scene these days with burnt ends.  Leaving three hungry men with a bad taste in their mouths as they have to return to a hard days work did not leave a very good impression.  The staff were nice and attentive but the food just failed on all fronts so that is going to take some serious intervention to fix.

I haven't eaten here again since Gorden Ramsay did his makeover but I ate here several times before then.  Nothing here was outstanding but nothing was terrible.  This is an unassuming typical Metairie strip mall type of place with pretty mediocre food.  The seafood dishes often seemed to be lacking and I generally opted for their other options which were alright but not quite worth the price.  The only thing I really liked about this place is the servers were generally very friendly and authentic NOLA Yat-tastic.  I might check it out again to see if Gorden was able to make any lasting improvements in the joint but my prior experiences left me very unimpressed.

Fat Harry's is one of the first bars I ever went to in my younger days (back when the drinking age was still 18 in Louisiana ya know).  This has always been a great college bar that a lot of local folks also frequent.  They have always had pretty good bar grub with nice po boys, burgers, sandwiches, cheese fries, etc. and this is actually a great spot for a quick lunch.  The beer prices got a bit more pricey after Katrina and are still a bit more than you will find on most of Magazine Street.  This used to be my favorite bar in NOLA, that I frequented more than any other, but as I've gotten a bit older I've shifted to being at the Bulldog more as I think their draft beer tastes better (and it's closer to my house).  I've always been a preppy Southern fellow so I've always felt right at home in here and it probably is one of the preppier bars in NOLA so if you don't like Southern preppy folk this might not be your place.  The crowd certainly shifts to a much younger one during the weekends and sometimes that does bring in some stupid behavior but the staff is very good at handling those situations.  The bartenders are always on top of their game here and do a great job of taking care of large crowds.  They have some nice outdoor seating on the sidewalk for those nicer days (and now that it is non-smoking for you smokers to poison yourselves).  This place gets to its maximum crazy times during Carnival season and especially the weekend before Mardi Gras.

This is a bar and restaurant that makes fancy cocktails.  I like beer much better than cocktails and most fancy cocktail making joints have a beer selection that sucks but Melange has a good selection of beer.  I haven't had an opportunity to sample their food but now that I've established they have common sense with their beer choices I will certainly return to do so.  The inside really seems more like a bar than a restaurant to me but in this area of town that's certainly acceptable and sometimes preferable.  It pulls off being both spacious and intimate at the same time with the way they have arranged their seating so it has some good feng shui.  The location is just off Frenchmen so it can be a bit of a calmer place to relax and grab a drink during some of the more intense celebrations that occur in this area.

On a recent Friday night I finally engaged in the "Feed Me" menu here which was a nice sampling of various specialties of Chef Duke.  I am an experienced veteran of the "Feed Me" menu at Tony Angello's Restaurant so I had high expectations of an enormous feast.  My expectations were somewhat disappointed as Giovanni only has 6 courses for his "Feed Me" as compared to the 10 to 11 of Tony Angello's.  The courses were all good while the portions were all quite small and I was certainly nowhere near being as full as I typically am after most of my dinner experiences with fine dining in New Orleans.  The courses were: Oysters Giovanni, seafood caprese salad, ravioli, grilled fish, fillet and bread pudding.  I liked all of the courses except for the bread pudding as it was full of banana and I don't really care for banana bread pudding.  I'm glad I finally did the "Feed Me" menu here but ultimately I don't think it is the best value and I would stick with the other great things on the menu in the future but it certainly is worthwhile to do once.  The opera singers were in full effect and they always add an entirely new level of entertainment to any meal here so that is a huge value added for your dining pleasure here.

I've only eaten dinner here but they have started doing lunch so I still have to check that out.  I've had some very good food here and found this to be a great place to take dates.  It is probably one of the more expensive restaurants in New Orleans so I don't go frequently but every time I've been it has been a very enjoyable experience.  They have very good Italian food and they do some very good things with veal.  I also hear rumors that this is Martin Scorsese's favorite place to eat in New Orleans :)

The food used to be really great here but sadly the prices have substantially increased while the quality of the food and service have tanked.  I recently had the single worst fish dish I've EVER had in New Orleans here which consisted of blackfish on a bed of fried green tomatoes all resting on a huge slimy sea of tartar sauce.  The service, food quality and prices are all failures to me at this point.  The one high point was the live music.  There are so many restaurants providing such better food at better prices with attentive service there is no reason to bother with eating here and dealing with poor service.  The drink prices demonstrate that they have morphed into a tourist trap so when one beer costs as much as an entire six pack you are being gouged at rip off tourist prices.

This is the newest location of the local chain of New Orleans Coffee & Beignet Co. and it is a small counter space with seating in the hotel lobby.  The prices are fair for generous portions and the service was friendly and fast.  It actually took me a bit to actually figure out where it was as they have a sign outside and then when you walk inside you just see the Legacy Kitchen bar and it took me a minute to notice the little counter in front of the bar was the coffee shop and not part of the bar.

Ehhh happy hour... completely deserted.  They offer ONE beer, one red wine and one white one but they do have many $6 cocktails for those that want that.  The drinks outside of happy hour in general seem very overpriced for what you get.  This place calls itself a bar but is much more of a finer dining/fancy craft cocktail establishment.  They have some happy hour small plate snack food and then dinner offers a very small selection of items which are decently priced for some with a bit of an overprice for others.  I guess the main selling point is that there is not anything else really like it in this part of Nashville.  The ambiance and interior of the building is very nice along with their outside patio so this could certainly make for a good dinner date spot.  The staff here were just not very happy looking or very friendly during my happy hour visit.  For happy hour I just can't recommend it unless you want a really quiet time and I really had a whole lot more fun nearby at the Pharmacy beer garden.

This indoor range has been nicely done and everything is shiny and new.  They have one 50 foot rifle lane and the rest of the lanes are pistol only.  The range is well ventilated and the temperature is kept at a comfortable level.  There were very few shooters and no wait on my last visit as this place is still pretty new and not many people know about it yet.  The waiting/retail area is very nice and far more comfortable than any other area range I'm aware of.  The downside is that the prices here are significantly higher than other ranges and they could really mark out and define the distance lines for the targets more clearly.  The lane setup also makes it challenging to retrieve your brass if you want to keep it.  The location could also use a bit more exterior signage to make it easier to find.   They do offer memberships that decrease the range prices but none of the membership packages seemed to be a good option for my needs.    Overall the range and staff make this a four to five star location but the significantly higher pricing unfortunately makes this range a place I won't visit very often so it loses star power for lack of value.  You could argue that you get what you pay for but at their current prices I just won't be able to afford returning very often but I certainly will be returning occasionally as it is a really nice range.

I'm a much bigger fan of their St. Charles location but if you are in Metry this is certainly a good choice to get your Italian food craving taken care of.  They have a good selection of lunch and dinner specials.  This would also be a nice spot to bring a date or have a business meal.  The only challenges I have here are that the parking lot seems to often be completely full (even when there are not many people inside) and the service can be a bit slow at lunch when you need it to be a bit more fast to return to work.  Their pasta, seafood and veal dishes are all quite nice here but I'm always going to prefer the St. Charles Ave. location.

A chain in the suburbs in a strip mall what's not to dislike when you're used to NOLA proper?  Well if they at least had decent food there might have been some hope for them but unfortunately the food here is really disappointing even for the mass produced chain bar food that it is.  In any other metro area this might be acceptable but in the New Orleans area we're spoiled and used to a certain quality of food that this place comes nowhere close to reaching.  I just don't see any reason to ever return here again.

The story of this establishment's name is that it was offered as a residence to Napoleon in 1821 as a refuge during his exile but even after he never showed up the name stuck.  The food is "ok" with some items being better and some being a bit "blah" but the main draw here would be for the drinks.  They make a really nice and refreshing Pimm's cup and a proper Sazerac.  This can be a pleasant place to enjoy some good drinks and good company.  They have a nice courtyard to enjoy when the weather is pleasant and seating at the bar or at tables inside when it isn't.

This place has been around for a long time but I've only just gotten around to eating here today.  I've had very limited experience with Korean food and most of it, until today, wasn't very good or very authentic.  This is the finest example of Korean I've ever had, so far, and it was a completely enjoyable experience on every level for me.    I really enjoyed the spicy beef soup at lunch and everything comes with like 6 little bowls of an assortment of awesome pickled vegetables and rice!!!  I love spicy and I love pickled so this place hit my taste buds on all the right levels.  It was cheaper to eat here than at most Pho places and with all the side dishes it was a lot of food at a great value.  The ambiance is total 1970's faded glory that I really find groovy and the family that runs the place seems very nice.  I look forward to many further adventures in this place!

They have an alternative Chinese menu with more traditional and less Americanized versions of more authentic Chinese dishes.  Their lunch special is a really good value but even though their menu indicates some modifications can be made you can't substitute spring rolls for the egg rolls as I tried and got denied.  Many of the dishes here I find to be overly sweet and I'd prefer more heat and less sweet.  Overall it will work for a quick meal and during lunch it is a good value but I've certainly had better Chinese food.

I HATE it and I LOVE it!  The nasty smells and horrible crowds of uncouth acting people disgust me.  I thoroughly enjoy the wacky, wild, non-stop party and fun times.  There are amazing drink specials here and complete tourist rip-offs.  I enjoy a fantastic lunch at Galatoire's or another great Quarter restaurant with some fun times back on Bourbon Street.  I especially love lunch during the Friday before Christmas and Lundi Gras.  I get extremely frustrated with my out of town friends that always and non-stop want to do nothing but Bourbon Street all the time and refuse to ever sample anything else that NOLA offers.  There are terrible things and great things about this street but I'm glad I live in New Orleans so I can always choose to be a tourist and go on vacation here if I want.

I generally only end up here for special events and private parties.  Its an ok place and about the only place in NOLA that ever attempts any type of velvet rope.  I've never had a fantastic time here but I've never had a terrible time either.  This is definitely an "a-ok" place most of the time.  If it isn't a special event or private party I'm probably not going to be here and it usually doesn't get the music I like with a few notable exceptions.

Nice historic building that they did little remodeling too and fortunately preserved much of the historic nature of the old shotgun building.  Due to the historic nature of the building the dining space is quite small and intimate which could be a good or bad thing depending on what you're looking for.  The menu is very concise and the plastic chairs would be best replaced by some wooden ones eventually.  This is the first and only place I've had a hot shrimp remoulade salad and I've got to say I find I prefer the cooler versions.  They have a decent selection of items but its a bit on the pricey side considering the portion size.  They serve some nice bread and butter with your meal and the hostess seems to often double as the only server which leads to decent but not always quick service.    Overall this probably wouldn't be my first choice for a nice restaurant as it seems to often lack bang for the buck but it is one of the few nicer dining options in Mid-City.

This is a really great toy and bike store.  They have an excellent selection of items and you should be able to find a toy to make just about any age kid happy.  There were some toys that were so cool I had to resist the urge to buy them myself as I wanted to take them home and play with them.  They have some items I haven't seen since I was a kid that used to be carried by most of the toy stores in the French Quarter but you can't find them in those places anymore.  They certainly have a great selection and the prices are sometimes more than you will pay at the soul sucking chain stores but you also get great service here.  If you want to find some cool toys or need anything related to bicycles this is definitely an establishment to check out!

This place has some really good pho options and is one of the few local places I've seen a seafood pho option.  They have many other Vietnamese options but I generally rotate between the chicken, beef, and seafood phos.  They also have one of the finest examples of Vietnamese hot and sour soup that I've ever had; I've generally found this dish in other places to just be "ok" but here it is FANTASTIC!  They also go ALL OUT for their New Year's celebration and they had three dragons doing the dragon dance all inside and outside with lots of fireworks.  They have both jasmine iced tea and regular tea along with a large selection of bubble teas.    I've always had very quick and efficient service and find this to be a very reliable lunch spot.  They also have some really AWESOME hours as they stay open into the wee hours of the morning during the weekends if you really need a pho fix late night!!!

Intimate space run by the owner that is very passionate about his food.  He explained that he does more of a homestyle of Middle Eastern cooking than you find in the other spots in the area.  Definitely smaller portion sizes than you get at Byblos Market and slower to get your food but a lot more personable and friendly banter to be had here.

My recent evening visit was during a hectic busy time and things seemed to be pretty disorganized.  They have some self-order kiosks setup with ipads that are very buggy to work and the credit card part didn't seem to work so I had to bring my receipt up to the counter to pay so they still seem to have a lot of bugs to work out with that system so you might want to skip that for now and just go straight to the counter.  My "Pizza Steak Hoagie" gave me high hopes as it looked fantastic but on biting into it I was met with cold bread and a lot of cold interior marinara sauce.  By the time my friend who had ordered before me got their order I had already finished my sandwich but at least the late arrival sandwich was hot and much better than mine so I guess the trick is to stick with the "The Original" sandwich.  A guy did stop at our table and apologize for the chaos and delay in my friend's order and gave us some coupons for a beer discount.  Liberty Cheesesteaks just moved from their smaller original location into this larger location so I guess they are still experiencing growing pains and have quite a few kinks to work out.  I might give them another try in a few months to see if they have gotten their new ship sailing smoothly.

Decent new Korean spot that just opened that does a lot of carry out business.  They have a good value lunch menu and my lunch with tax before tip was $8.18 of course sadly they don't offer iced tea and I had to just drink the water instead but at least that was free.  I had the beef ramen and it was spiced well and the free side items were nice although smaller in portion than the other Korean places but the waitress did ask if I wanted more when I polished them off.  Overall this is a decent spot for a quick dine in or take out Korean meal.

This was a decent hotel that had a bar but no swimming pool.  The location of the hotel is fantastic and is right in a prime spot with a lot of great places around it.  The only negatives were that the toilet just didn't flush properly and they only had one ice machine that was located on the 4th floor.  The bar area, patio and lounge area seemed to stay pretty busy during my stay and then they also offered a decent breakfast spread every morning.  The "gym" was squeezed really tightly into one small space.  Overall location location location along with a better price than most of the other nearby hotels really makes this place stand out as a good choice in the area.

Funky hipster vibe Vietnamese place that has really done a nice job fixing this spot up inside.  The pho is a generous serving and they also offer a really super spicy hot sauce chili oil to go along with it that will certainly clear your sinuses.  The service is generally attentive and prices are reasonable except the bahn mi seemed too expensive but they were larger than most places.  This is one of the few Vietnamese joints also offering a full bar selection.  They seem to have created a popular reputation and stay pretty busy here which brings up the main downside which is their small and generally crowded parking lot which you need to be cautious when navigating.  Overall this is a pretty nice place to enjoy a good meal at a good price and its also a nice spot for social gatherings.

This place really does have the irritating aura of a chain restaurant but I do like the old school sci-fi posters on the wall.  The loud and horrible rap music they blare really detracts from the experience here and I was having to restrain myself from my strong desire to rip the speakers out of the wall and bash them to kill the horrible noises they polluted my environment with.  During my last lunch visit this establishment was nearly deserted so they certainly need to make some serious adjustments to what they are offering here.   The pizza here is rather bland and leaves me with thinking it is a fairly close match to a DiGiorno frozen pizza in flavor and consistency.  Just like DiGiorno the pizza here  isn't exactly bad pizza but there are many better pizza joints in the area.  One of the biggest pizza shortcomings is their red sauce which seems to just be plain tomato paste which could REALLY use some herbs and spices added to it along with being more generously applied to the pie.  The other food options available here bump their rating up higher as they do have a decent selection of other choices on the menu.  The small pizza is also quite filling as generally I can polish off a small size easily all on my own but I was left with two slices remaining with a full belly at my last pizza encounter here.  I think I will probably stick with with the sandwiches and entrees on any future visits unless they do some serious reformulating.

Cash only dive joint that invented and perfected the infamous "Nashville Hot Chicken."  So I got the hot level of hot chicken and I could have gone several levels hotter to maybe even the top tier of hot.  Being from New Orleans I'm no stranger to heat and spice but from the numerous warnings I played it semi-safe and just went with the plain old "hot" level instead of mediocre and bland "medium" to see if it would test me.  The heat does have a nice build up that slowly gets more heat in your mouth as you eat.  I found the exterior crust of the chicken to be really hard to an excessive amount for my preference.  The interior of the chicken was alright but nothing to make it amazingly juicy or flavorful and it didn't seem the heat was marinated down into the meat of the chicken and that the heat was all contained in the exterior crust.  I was also really surprised at how long the wait was and the very large number of people waiting at 3pm on a weekday afternoon in this small little space.  So I guess all the hype had me expecting more but really there are far more hot chicken wings out and about in the universe so all the warnings about the mouth heat are overdone.  Now what you do have to watch out for is that the oil or spice combo they use for the chicken is not very kind to your stomach and intestines so you do get a few days of discomfort from that "other" end of the eating spectrum.  Overall I guess it is alright chicken but it seems to be more of a gimmick than just really good fried chicken but you might as well try "Nashville Hot Chicken" at least once and I will try the top tier hot at some point just because I can.  Protip:  They let you call your order in ahead of time so that is the best most fantastic idea you can do for this process.

This is the biggest late night crowd to be found in the Warehouse District and they party til the wee hours of daylight the next day.  I generally don't find this to be a very enjoyable bar as it is crammed like a sardine can in here on the weekends.  If the crowd happens to be a lot of hot women that could be a potential fun sardine can but my last several visits there have seemed to be more dudes in here ruining the ratio.    The music is usually so loud I can't even remember what type of music they play as I can't hear myself think long enough to process what I'm hearing.  The wait for drinks has always been long and irritating to me.  Personally I would put this place at 2 Stars but the sheer number of people drawn here and the fact that they are the main late night spot in the Warehouse merits they get at least 3 Stars.

They did a major remodel of this joint after Katrina and it used to look a LOT more like an actual palace than it does now.  This certainly isn't one of my favorite Asian joints to eat at on the Westbank but it certainly is one of the more interesting.  They have an eclectic selection of scary Tiki drinks in notably vintage Tiki glasses.  The food is generally unremarkable but isn't terrible.  I occasionally stop in here to eat when in an extreme hurry without time to get to Pho Tau Bay or 9 Roses which is a very rare event indeed...

This is one of the best Brooks Brothers stores in the U.S.A. and they have some unique New Orleans items.  If you find yourself needing a tie in Carnival colors then this store can provide you with a nice selection.   I've always found the staff here to be extremely helpful (sometimes to the point of overkill).  I generally prefer to get most of my Brooks Brothers clothing at a significantly reduced price at their outlet stores (hooray we finally got an outlet in Gonzales) but some unique NOLA items are only available at this store.  I've always found the quality and fit of most Brooks Brothers items to be among the best quality.  If they would have outfitted both Southern and Northern officers during the War of Northern Aggression then I would give them Five Stars but I have to hold a slight grudge (and star) against them for only outfitting dirty Yankees.

This is a pretty decent dive joint way out in the Bywater.  Their biggest night is usually on Thursday when Kermit and the BBQ Swingers play.  It has gotten so miserably crowded with Treme tourist fans that now Thursday nights are much less fun as it takes so long to get to the bar or the bathroom (or just move anywhere).  Even when it is crazy crowded the bartenders do an outstanding job and the drinks are very fairly priced.  If you aren't familiar with the area you should certainly take a Taxi.

Not a brewery and not a bar but some interesting version of a beer store that is like a bar but with much cheaper beer prices than a bar.  Interesting concept that offers an interesting selection of beer and ciders along with some wines and spirits.  They also have the rare to find in NOLA phenomena of an actual parking lot.  This place lets you run a tab and operates pretty similar to a bar except they close at 9 or 10pm depending on the day.  A comfortable spot to try out some new drinks and relax for awhile.

This is the first big parade event that really gets the Carnival season into high gear.  This is a bawdy and satirical parade that is definitely intended for mature audiences but some people still bring their kids.  This is a walking parade with smaller and more old-school mule drawn floats.  There is a lot of "interactive" participation between the crowd and the krewe members.  The throws are more creative and often created by the krewe members.

Old school gun shop with a gun range down in the basement.  They had a pretty good selection of pre-owned and some mil surp firearms.  Most of their inventory seemed to be pistols.  The staff were helpful and attentive and then left me alone to look at their selection in the cases.  They did have some nice examples of notable mil surp pistols.

Pretty average to a bit below average overall for everything I've had here.  I've only been a few times and sampled different things and nothing has really stood out yet.  For purposes of full disclosure I need to admit that I LOVED the restaurant that was in this space prior to Katrina and I was really sad to see it go so maybe I have some unconscious resentment that Mondo doesn't have awesome oysters like the previous place (I might have a slight addiction problem with oysters).  I first came here for the burger that I heard was amazing but it was just "ok" but it really did look pretty (Lakeview Harbor across the street does a better tasting burger).  It has always been crowded every time I've been here and you're usually lucky if you can even find a seat at the bar.  This is such a popular place that it would be a great location just to hang out at the bar to people watch.  Mondo seems to be one of the busiest places in the neighborhood for the "more mature" crowd.  The recent opening of the Velvet Cactus has siphoned off some of that crowd and brought in extra so you could now actually have a pretty fun bar crawl going from Parlay's, to Mondo, to Velvet Cactus.
