Mondo would probably never be my first choice in the area to eat and I would go to the nearby Steak Knife or Lakeview Harbor before returning here but it might be worth a visit if you see something on the menu that catches your eye.

The new ramen menu seems like a better option for this location than their previous menu.  The chicken and oxtail ramen I have had here have both been good.  The "spicy" noodles really didn't taste any different or seem to have any spice difference than the normal noodles.  I didn't really find the shrimp dumplings to be worthwhile and I wouldn't get them again.  Overall I like the ramen soups for a change of pace from my normal pho options but at double the price of pho I probably won't make a regular habit of it.

Living in New Orleans with our numerous pot holes and random tire destroying garbage littering the streets you often get to spend lots of time changing tires.  Delta World Tire is one of the better places to have to take care of this unpleasant fact of life and they really do give great customer service.  They also provide other automotive services like oil changes in addition to their tire services.

Total dive place that only takes cash or personal checks.  They offer some of the best tacos I have ever had due to their fantastic tortillas.  Quick cheap and good somehow all are allowed to exist here at one time.  The only thing I might have wished for improvement would have been some kind of salsa and other condiments bar.  Definitely a top spot to get your taco fix on in the Nashville area.

I don't like doughnuts so this review is only for the Po-Boys.  I got a roast beef po boy and it was alright except for lots of inedible tough gristle that was all in the meat.  The first couple of bites tasted alright but then the meat was just of a terrible and tough consistency.  I haven't been inspired to return due to my gristly experience.  I really hope this was an off day and they don't usually serve meat of this quality.  They also close at 6pm so it is really hard for me to ever get here in time from work to eat.  I want the legends and stories to be true about how good the po boys are here so maybe I can force myself back for a seafood attempt but bad roast beef is a hard thing for me to get over.

Mexican street food is what they advertise and I suggest they leave it in the streets of Mexico as the food was terrible and extremely bland (unlike any other real Mexican I've ever eaten)!  It was also interesting that it seemed to be gringos cooking the food.  Awful service to the degree it was the worst service I've ever had as I saw the waitress when she took my order and not again until I paid my bill.  I first attempted to order an iced tea and they didn't have that so I got a water instead which was served in a tiny mixed drink glass.  In the hour it took to get my food my miniature glass was refilled once and thankfully I finally noticed they had bottled mineral water and I got one of those before I expired from complete dehydration. The bar looked cool and had a small patio in the back so they get one extra star for that.  They should really lose the extra star though as I could only find one unisex bathroom in the whole place but it does have a shower so you can wash off the angst that all the dirty hipsters crowding this place will leave on you.  They had some nice looking and smelling mixed drinks and I might have tried some if I wasn't dying of thirst and hunger along with having such a negative experience with the food and service.  My experience here left me with a feeling of all I wanted to do was escape.  Maybe they will find a way to improve but my experience was so bad  I doubt I shall ever return.  If you want real Mexican then Taqueria Guerrero (next to Brocato's) will give you some authentic options.

Penny's Cafe is a community staple in Violet, LA and it has quite a lot of local characters that frequent the joint.  They have quite a comprehensive menu along with doing occasional seafood boils.  It is about the last actual restaurant you will see on your way to the fishing grounds of Shell Beach, Delacroix or Hopedale so it is a good place to stop off on the way going fishing or the on the way back home.  They sometimes have a breakfast buffet and then a lunch buffet that seems pretty popular.  The menu has a selection of New Orleans' Creole fare along with some Italian and plain old fashioned American diner food.  The seafood gumbo has a decent amount of seafood in it with good flavor.  The entrees are decent sized and typically quite filling and the po boys and other sandwiches are done well.  The service is friendly and usually takes good care of you.  The only big negative is they have a two refill policy for their soft drinks and iced tea which is rather unusual for the area and I can't think of any other restaurants that do that.   Overall this is an interesting joint that has some decent to great food with a lot of local character.

I've been to many events, parties, and trainings here.  This is a nice hotel conveniently located on Canal Street and near to most things in the French Quarter.  All of the various event rooms I've been in have been set up very well and, as someone that frequently books spaces for trainings, I would say they offer above average service and meeting space.

This place is very much focused on being a cocktail bar and their very limited and tiny selection of beer and wine testifies to this fact.  The cocktails they make here are very extreme examples of handcrafted talent made with extreme precision, effort, and skill.  They are also very small and rather expensive on the New Orleans scale at around $10 but in any other major city these concoctions would probably be $25-$70.  I'm always disappointed they don't have Abita Amber so I never spend much time here and I only show up for a few cocktails and then leave to go find a bar with Abita Amber as I can only handle so many of these extreme cocktails at a time.  The food I won't comment on as it would be a conflict of interest due to my knowing people involved in the situation.

Ahhh its been an inaccurate liberal slanted rag for awhile now that sometimes has good stories with their few good reporters.  I've mainly been reading it online for years now so their transition to focusing more online and less on daily print doesn't disturb me that much except for the fact that we really NEED newspaper in New Orleans for our crawfish, crab and shrimp boils!  The online version really pisses me off with how they will selectively and arbitrarily delete posts in discussion threads when the opposing viewpoints are better researched and completely disprove their often inaccurate and highly slanted "stories" that are more opinion pieces.  They also did a design change to the online version that made it more of a blog format and the new format really is terrible.

They have created a nice intimate space here that produces a good environment for couples or groups.  Some of the food is priced more towards the fine dining scale while other choices on the menu offer more affordable options but overall this is currently the most expensive Middle Eastern food menu in NOLA.  You get a nice complementary bread serving brought to the table to start you off with a side of spiced olive oil.  The matzo ball soup (with duck meat) is probably the best value and a large serving that can be a meal itself while the lamb shank is the most expensive lamb shank I've ever had (and one of the largest I've ever seen).  They offer a selection of items for the table with prices starting at $12 for 3 small plates and going up from there for additions.    I think the best way to experience the food here is to do the small plates but I'm not sure why they do an entirely separate section for hummus which isn't included in the small plate selection.  The food here seems best suited for couples or groups to share so eating as a solo diner is a bit more challenging to get a good balance of food quantity here.  The biggest disappointment to me here is that they charge $6 for Abita Amber which just seems outrageous for a Magazine Street establishment.  My favorite thing about dining here is that the staff is really great and takes good care of you and Chef Shaya takes the time to stop by and check up on how you're enjoying your food.    Overall this is a great place for groups and couples while  more challenging for the solo diner.  They offer some unique spins on Middle Eastern food that aren't found at other restaurants and have the best space and service of any restaurant of this genre in the area but I'm not drinking here at their alcohol prices.

You have to get buzzed in to get inside this place.  They are fanatics about the Cubs and darts here and I really don't care for either but the bar is still a decent place to grab a drink.  For whatever reasons this bar seems to be one of my least frequented spots to stop in to booze Uptown; not that it is a bad place I just often forget that it exists.   The service has always been great and there always seems to be at least a small group hanging out (except during Mardi Gras time when it gets crazy after the parades).  This is certainly an interesting place to visit and have some fun times.

This newest of BBQ joints in the area is located inside a non-descript strip mall location that would be easy to miss if you didn't know where you were going.  It is a smaller no frills place currently and my first disappointment is they offered no fresh brewed iced tea.  I quickly decided on my staple of brisket to evaluate their BBQ offerings.  I was slightly excited by their selection of four sauce offerings in:   1) Vinegar  2) Hickory  3) Sweet and  4) Pineapple Bourbon    The sauces were all good with the brisket being tender while the mac'n cheese is good and the slaw is crisp.  The serving size was on the smaller side for my expectation in comparison to the Joint and the flavor, texture and overall experience was not as good as what I have come to expect from the Joint.  I will certainly give this place several more samplings but for now at least they are still behind their nearby BBQ competitor Très Bon Cajun Meats.

This is a classic old fashioned men's barbershop that offers classic buzz cuts and trims along with straight razor shaves.  You're not going to get any fancy modern haircut styles here and if you think you can walk in with a male pony tail and escape with it you would be very mistaken.  You can have your choice of any 1950's style haircut you want here as long as its short and neat.  Some of the barbers are getting really old and past their prime though so I'm very cautious about getting a shave here ever again!  The last shave I got here the barber's hands were mighty shaky and he cut me more than I've ever been cut before during a barber's shave!  Since that experience I've gotten all my shaves at Algie Hailey's on Metairie Road as I'm a big fan of not having my throat slashed open accidentally (or any other way).     Still a great haircut value if you like the buzz cut look.  I was in the army so I know how to look really sexy for the ladies with this hairstyle!

Very Americanized and bland food. The Lucky Rooster Soup had a decent mix of veggies but the chicken is the same diced stuff they use at Juan's and Slice. The soup was much improved by adding their Rooster Sauce but it just wasn't that great. The Cocoa Pot dessert was very small and nothing special as it was just peanut butter with some chocolate syrup poured over it with some chocolate wafer cookies shoved in it. I could have made everything I ate here in less than 10 minutes and for under $5 except mine would've been much better.    Lucky Rooster Soup with egg added $13  Iced Tea $2.50 Cocoa Pot dessert $6  So with tax, tip and metered parking lunch came out to $29.34! At that price I could've gone to Commander's Palace and had three courses with 25 cent martinis to boot!  Juan's and Slice are good values and good food but Lucky Rooster fails to deliver in either area. Noodle and Pie blows this place out of the water with both food and value.  They do seem to put extreme effort into their fancy cocktails here so maybe that's why women seem to like this place as they get all liquored up and then anything tastes good to them.  This place is all form with no substance and Lao Tzu says the Tao will not be found here. Sage advice I will follow.  Leave this place to the hipsters and fancy cocktail addicts!

This place has been around since the 50's and you can have a flashback to the olden days here.  The burgers are decent but certainly not great and fries come out hot but with salt on the side.  The po boys here are alright and probably better than the burger.  The real attraction here is the soft-serve ice cream and the desserts made with it.  They also offer snowballs here year round.  On my last visit they were out of Coke... c'mon you can't have a full flashback without any Coke!

I've always heard mixed reviews about this place with most being bad and so I've always been hesitant to try it.  Gorden Ramsay did a makeover of this place so I had hoped that would have improved the food but I continued to hear mixed reviews but not as many terrible ones.  This was one of the very few places open and the only place serving their full menu on the day after Hurricane Isaac landed so they get one extra star for that.  They also housed their staff above the restaurant during the storm so that also deserves credit for excellent planning.   The tail end of Isaac was still blowing pretty good when a friend and I decided we needed a nice post storm meal and this seemed to be our only option for a nice dinner so we decided to try it.  When we first arrived there was a line of folks waiting to get in but we were able to get to the bar and enjoyed an island of normalcy amidst the chaos of the storm.  The service was very organized and efficient in dealing with the many people waiting to eat.  Unfortunately the area where they really underperformed was the most important area and that was their food.  The best way to describe this food is that it's like Copeland's but a lot less good.  My friend and I ate multiple things and none of the items really tasted good to us.  The BBQ shrimp were the most edible things served.  The seafood gumbo tasted funky, the redfish was not fresh and had zero flavor, and sadly the cheesecake was the absolute worst I've ever had.  My friend and I agreed that the fried seafood options would probably be the best thing to get here in the unlikely event we ever returned in the future.    I really want to give this restaurant a good review as I'm very impressed with their superior planning and execution of their hurricane plan but the food really failed to deliver.  I would like to hope that the disappointing food was due to the chaos of the hurricane but they never lost power and they had a full staff so that would be a difficult argument to make.  I'm very thankful that they were open and I got to at least eat dinner as later in the afternoon I met a lot of folks that were hungry that weren't able to find anything to eat so the food here was definitely better than no food.  During normal circumstances and for the price there are much better quality experiences to be had all over the Quarter than this place but during a hurricane this might be your best bet.

Amazing value for your money and great lunch spot!  It has been a VERY long time since I got so much food for such a low price.  Very nice folks that run this place and they make a point to find out your name and remember it.  I had driven by this place a few times as it is near my office and I wasn't sure if it was a just a bar or something else but on closer inspection I noticed they advertised some really great lunch specials and they have a whole lot to choose from.  This place seems to have many repeat customers (so that says a lot about a place to me that has people that eat there so often that the staff know most people that walk in the door by name).  The location is not the most convenient (unless you work around where I do) or easiest to find but it has very easy parking.  I will be going back for lunch on a regular basis to sample all the tasty looking things on the menu and that will take awhile as they have different daily specials in addition to their already well apportioned menu.

I had a previous review and more pictures that Yelp has somehow lost...   The food ranges from really good to items you might get better elsewhere.  They have some unique items that I haven't seen at other Peruvian places in the area.  Their purple corn drank "Chicha Morada" is quite refreshing and very nice for a non-alcoholic beverage and the Inca Cola is pretty nifty too.  The seafood platter is the one item I would probably avoid as there are just much better versions at traditional NOLA seafood joints around town.  There other dishes are all pretty good and they have some nice soups.  Very nice folks working here and typically good friendly service that can be a little slow sometimes.  The restaurant can be a bit challenging to find as they don't have much of a sign to let you know this is a restaurant so it is easy to drive or walk past and not even notice.    Overall it is a nice place to try something quite a bit different from most of the other options available in the area.

A pretty good and faithful reproduction of the Parthenon in Athens with some other museum displays underneath it.  It is a really quick tour to see everything but it is a well done and cool space to check out to compare with the original bits and pieces of the original strewn about the world and in Athens.  I'm also hoping maybe they might consider building the rest of the Acropolis around it but then I guess they would need to raise it up on a reproduction Acropolis too...

I ate at their pop up inside of Milkfish and my table had the pickled tea leaf salad, papaya salad, ginger garlic chicken and amok fish.  It took quite a while for our order to be taken but once that happened the food came out very fast.  The salads really didn't impress very much as the main flavor was salt from the nuts that overwhelmed everything else and I didn't really seem to have all that many pickled tea leaves in my tea leaf salad while the papaya salad was the much better of the two and had a bit of spice heat to it.  The chicken didn't have very much garlic or ginger flavor and I actually found it to be pretty bland but juicy and the side of okra it came with was nice.  The amok fish was probably the best tasting item of the night and was done with catfish and I would've preferred another fish but it was the highlight of flavor for the night.    The service was really disorganized and slow and only got worse as the place got slammed and they had people lined up to get in.  They were giving 10% of the proceeds at this nights pop up to help Burmese children so it was a very well attended night so they should've been able to raise some funds to help with that.  Overall it was a pretty mediocre experience and nothing really impressed me much to inspire me to want to return other than possibly the amok fish if it were done with another type of fish.

I got dragged in here by some out of town friends and it is REALLY just a tourist trap.  There are so many places doing infinitely better food all over the place in New Orleans that this place is a waste of time.  The servers all seem miserable which likely happens as they know that their food is bad and they probably hear frequent complaints.  I wouldn't ever eat here again as it just doesn't compare to any of the many better places around.  Also it's a cheesy chain... Eating at a chain in New Orleans makes as much sense as eating at a McDonald's in Paris... oh wait I know people that have done that...  Tip:  Tourist Trap  Recommended Action: Avoid

They did an excellent job of renovating this location of the former Coyote Blues Mexican restaurant into a nice Italian wine bar and restaurant.  Sadly the food still suffers the same fate as the former Mexican restaurant in that it just doesn't taste all that great.  The food here is really lacking in flavor and I found that the lasagna and chicken Parmesan were extremely bland with great need of herbs, spices and garlic. The best tasting things I've had here include their bread (with oil and vinegar) and the veal soup was decent.  In the flavor department this food really ranks at the very bottom of all other Italian food in the area.  The service, ambiance and all other aspects are acceptable but the food just needs a serious makeover to add flavor.  Overall the wine is a great value so this is a place to come and drink but I can't recommend the food as nearly all other Italian/Sicilian restaurants in the area offer better tasting food in larger portions for a better price.

The BBQ brisket here isn't my preferred Texas style and is more in line with what you would find in Memphis (or Corkey's locally) and is more akin to pot roast the way it is served.  The brisket is tender and moist but it just doesn't give me the BBQ zing I love like the Joint does.  This style of BBQ brisket probably is better on a sandwich than on its own.  I'm also not a fan of the fact they give you BBQ sauce in a tiny little shot cup instead of letting you apply your desired amount from a dispenser of some sort (I always get a bit grumpy when sauce is dispensed like its gold).  The sides here are really good with the beans, fried brussel sprouts, cole slaw, tater tots and mac 'n cheese all being good choices.  There aren't a lot of BBQ options in this immediate area with the only other one that comes to mind being Boo Koo BBQ at nearby Finn McCool's.  I think Boo Koo's brisket is better than the brisket here and the Joint smokes them both but this food is certainly worthy of eating if you're in the area.

The ramen menu at Kin has earned this spot the top ramen destination in the area.  The chicken, brisket and oxtail ramen I have had here have all been quite good with most of my friends seeming to prefer the brisket as they find it more flavorful (although the oxtail has not made a showing in a long while now so many of them haven't tried that one yet).  They seem to have a constant changing rotation of dumpling specials and folks rave about their chicken wings. Overall I like the ramen soups here for a change of pace from my normal pho options that have gotten quite numerous in the city.  Nice folks that own and run the place with the only complaint is service can get a bit slow sometimes when it starts getting crowded.  The interior design of the place makes it a bit challenging for the servers to get around to all the customers easily too.  I wish they might start offering a few more vegetable selections to go in the soups and maybe a choice of eggs with adding duck and quail as optionis?

This is a cool French Quarter Hotel that often has some really great rates.  It has some nice architectural features with a lot of NOLA charm.  I've stayed in many places of all types of quality all over the world and this place generally gives you exactly what you pay for and often more in the range of prices in the French Quarter.    The rooms are not the most modern or best equipped but if you are planning on spending a lot of time in your room watching TV then I'm not sure why you came to New Orleans in the first place.  You really only need a place to sleep and a safe enjoyable environment in the hotel and you get all you need here.  They have an interior courtyard with a pool that is very nice and the location is far enough off Bourbon Street to get to the madness quickly and escape it when you've reached your limit.  The location is also near Canal Street and the streetcars.  Its definitely not the top tier in quality but its nowhere close to the bottom so if you want or need better then you need to pay a lot more.  For most people this hotel will meet or exceed their lodging needs while in New Orleans.

This is more of a dive restaurant with a bar.  They do a good sized menu (with rotating daily specials) with some decent seafood, steaks and a good burger that is similar to Port of Calls.  My biggest complaint about this place is that they use margarine and not real butter.  Service is adequate but usually a bit on the slow side.  There usually seems to be a decent size crowd in here but I've never had to wait for a table or space at the bar.  It is a good location for some quick food and worth a visit if you are in the area and is also one of the only spots in that vicinity you can grab some food later in the night til about 1am.

This is a gun store with a small firing range onsite that has been "under construction" for several years so I'm still not sure if it is even open yet and they mainly just use the Shooter's Club range which is nearby (FYI most of the reviews for the range here are really for the Shooter's Club and not the Jefferson Gun Outlet).  Some of the prices here can be much steeper than what you will find at Academy or online and the customer service can be lacking at times with some of the staff while the Shooter's Club staff are always pleasant to deal with.  They offer concealed carry classes, FFL transfer service and consignment for used firearms.  They also have a selection of accessories which include holsters and law enforcement items.

This place has an uber new and shiny exterior and interior.  It is even a bit out of place on Oak Street it is so fresh and shiny and looks like something out of California or Texas.  They have a good sized staff and they provide good service.  The chairs in this place, while looking quite nifty, are some of the most uncomfortable chairs I've ever sat in and you only get a choice of any chair you want to sit as long as it is one of these evil back breaking chairs.  They have a good sized menu and offer some things that aren't offered at other area sushi restaurants.  The fish all seemed to be very fresh and good quality.  I had a good toro (it was just very cold the coldest toro I've ever had), one of their special rolls, and their hot and sour soup.  The only iced tea they had available was green tea and it wasn't a very good green tea.  The price for my dinner was the most expensive sushi experience I've ever had in New Orleans and I probably would have been happier with a meal next door at Jacques-Imo's in that price range.  It was good but I've just had better in NOLA and it wasn't good enough to justify what I paid.  Overall I enjoyed my meal and will probably return for another visit but I'm still favoring Kanno as my local favorite.

The Presbytere is part of the Louisiana State Museum that features Mardi Gras and Hurricane Katrina exhibits in the building.  The Katrina exhibit is on the lower floor and uses multimedia and artifacts to document the disaster and that dark times that followed.  The Mardi Gras exhibit is on the upper floor and has a lot of costumes and artifacts documenting the history and traditions of the celebration in New Orleans along with a special section focusing on traditions in rural areas.  If you're looking at the front of St. Louis Cathedral the Cabildo is to the right of the church.  The Mardi Gras museum has been a favorite of folks I've brought to the Presbytere.  Admission: Adults  $6 Students, Senior Citizens, Active Military  $5 Children 12 and under  Free Groups of 15 or more w/ reservations  20% discount School groups w/ reservations  Free Purchase tickets for two or more museums  20% discount AAA membership discount, with card  10% discount

The food and service is exactly like Mr. John's which is to say quite excellent.  The ambiance I found much less appealing than Mr. John's.  If you can't get a reservation at Mr. John's come here but I prefer Mr. John's for the environment and its much closer to my house.  The turtle soup is always great and they had seafood gumbo as a special on my last visit that was quite nice too.  People seemed a bit more casually dressed here than at Mr. John's and there seemed to be a higher concentration of tourists (which I would have expected from the location).  Still a great place and probably the best restaurant in this section of the CBD.  Tip: I love everything on the menu here with the exception of the burger which just really disappointed me.

The outside of the place has a much better ambiance than the inside and I found the interior to be a bit cramped.  I ordered the shrimp creole which was, unfortunately, the worst version I've ever had in my life of this pretty simple dish.  I'm seriously hoping that it was an off day because the service really wasn't all that adequate either and I've rarely been in such a hurry to exit a restaurant as I just really didn't enjoy my experience.  They do have some items on the menu that intrigue me still so I might give this place another chance but as they are so close to Parkway Bakery they really have to raise the bar to inspire me to stop here instead of there.

This is good but not great German food (but probably the best I've had in New Orleans).  I've only eaten at dinner, always sat at the bar, and always experienced good service.  I generally find the food to be a bit overpriced for what it is but the portions are generally of substantial size.  They have a good selection of beer and they have far more things on the menu that I like than say Luke or Deutsches Haus.    The ambiance falls far short of what it could be and it is really more of a place just to eat.  It doesn't seem to lend itself to just hanging out enjoying beers and being sociable.  It is certainly worthy of a visit for a change of pace from the usual offerings in the French Quarter and offers some things not available any other place in the area.  I recently went here for lunch on a Saturday and spent about $33 with tip (I had the goulash soup, jagerschnitzel, and apple strudel) so it approaches the cost of a fine dining restaurant for lunch if you get multiple courses but is very affordable if you stick to just an entree.

You can meet many of your Mardi Gras throw, costume and decoration needs here.  This is a warehouse of Mardi Gras fun with all manner of interesting items on display that can be purchased in large or small quantities.  Definitely an easy to access spot off of River Road not far from the Riverbend.

This used to be a super goth/heavy metal type freaky place with secret doors and upstairs human torture cages with hidden nooks and crannies all over the place.  Now they have split the place up and ruined the whole thing.  Yet another place that just ain't there no more...

This convenience store/gas station is a decent spot to grab some quick gas station style food like fried chicken and other items that are mostly fried or otherwise battered up in some method.  They sell adult beverages as well so you can put together a little party of your own here to walk over to the nearby Bayou St. John and have a little picnic party.  This is also the area of Bayou St. John that hosts the Bayou Boogaloo fest and this spot is also near Parkway Bakery of po boy fame.  The customers here (or sometimes not customers but randos that just hang outside the store) can be on the sketchy side at times so I would just always exercise your appropriate average NOLA area caution when entering or leaving this joint.    Overall this establishment has some decent provisioning capacity to meet your food, beverage and fuel needs with about an average NOLA gas station level of sketchy.

I ate at the Mosquito Supper Club for their fais do do brunch and the music, energy and environment were all great.  The seating was pretty limited with small uncomfortable chairs as they really wanted to motivate you to hurry up and eat so you could get up and start dancing.  The food was fairly priced but I found the portion sizes to be too small for my appetite so you needed to order several things.  I really liked the shrimp and grits but I wasn't that crazy about the chicken and waffles or quiche.  I'm not much of a breakfast food person anyway so I would've liked to have seen more lunch type items on the menu.  The mixed drinks were limited but they had a nice selection of cocktails available.  Overall it was a nice event but I think I would like the food at the dinner events more so maybe they will do a fais do do dinner soon.

They have nice cougars that work here and daily lunch specials that seem decent to good.  They just seem to have gotten a bit lazy with some of their specials (as an example the Tuesday pot roast special comes with mashed potatoes and carrots so while the pot roast is decent they could really add another vegetable to make it a more balanced meal).  They have "ok" burgers and po boys with fries that are a bit small and short.  The bar seems like a three star joint at least with lots of televisions and it would probably be an interesting place to watch a Saints game but there were no other people in the joint when I was there.  The main thing I don't like about this joint is that it's in a strip mall and I just hate strip malls!  They have somehow managed to build a small little side courtyard even with their limited strip mall options but without further evidence I would have to say this a two star place to me overall.

The service and ambiance are all good here but the food and drink leave a lot to be desired.  The brisket tacos were served with the meat cold and the chicken enchiladas were on the smaller side along with only containing two per order without the normal sides of rice and beans that most other Mexican joints in the area serve with this dish.  The margarita pitcher was the smallest pitcher I believe I have ever seen so it really is more of a large glass than a pitcher while the margarita itself is very weak in the amount of tequila used.  Overall there are just many other better options out there which are of better quality and better value so I really don't see a need to return here.

This range is located on the edge of Jean Lafitte Park so it is a scenic drive to adventure out to this location.  The price is a bit steep at $20 and $4 for two targets but that is with no time limit and you can shoot from open til close if you want.  This range allows both pistols and rifles with the range going out to distance of 50 yards.  It was disappointing that the yardage distance wasn't marked out so you need to do a lot of estimating and that is a situation that could be easily fixed with a bit of paint.  During the weekdays this is really one of the few NOLA area options for shooting rifles and to get an initial zero this place will meet your needs.  I would suggest you double protect your ears by using both earplugs and ear muffs at this range as the sound is EXTREMELY loud when rifles are being fired.  The targets are set up on an electronic pulley system so it is pretty convenient to zero in a rifle here.  They have wire fencing set up underneath the shooting stalls so if you have any brass that goes over into that section you won't be able to retrieve it.  They also offer firearms classes, gunsmithing, paintball and airsoft.

This is a good local bakery that has lots of dessert options and breads.  They have lunch sandwiches and lots of breakfast choices.  I rarely get here as I'm not much of a breakfast person and they close at 3pm.  If you like your sandwich on fresh bread this is a great place but they have very limited sandwich choices.  This is a very small operation so they are often out of things so it is best to call ahead if you need something.  They have finally started taking credit cards with a minimum purchase (I think it is $10).

This place is ok and really more like a 2.5 star to me.  I've only ever ended up here after Wednesday's on the Square.  It is one of the few remaining real down and dirty dives in this area as most of the other places have gotten much nicer from all the Warehouse District development.  The crowd often seems a bit older than many of the other bars in this part of town.  I've never eaten here or known anybody local that did and I'm a pretty adventurous eater but I have no plans on eating here unless I hear a lot of great reviews from folks I know.

I sometimes stop off here on my way to or back from fishing.  They have some good po boys, muffulettas, and platters.  They give good size portions and usually have your food prepared very fast.  It has an ambiance more like a fast food place but they do some New Orleans style food well.  If you want some quick and tasty food this is decent spot to eat.

I can walk to this place from my house so that makes it a big bonus for convenience but they are only open for lunch so I can only make it in there on Saturday for the most part as I'm usually nowhere close to here while working.  The sandwiches here are alright but I don't think they are anything super great other than they press some of them.  I think it is a bit expensive and the portion size is a bit small for me.  I'm also unhappy they don't have fresh brewed iced tea and just sell things in bottles.  They do have one of the best selections of root beer of nearly anyplace around.  During Mardi Gras they set up a little outside window you can order at.  This place is ok if I'm in a hurry but it isn't one of my top spots for lunch or a sandwich.

This place serves pretty generous portions for a decent price.  The salsa was rather bland but you do get both a green and red salsa for free.  The best thing about this place is that its right next to the Rugby Pub and I'm an old rugby player so anything associated with rugby (or near to it) makes it the best thing always (the rugby pitch is nearby also and I've spilled my fair share of blood there so its sacred ground).  The most interesting thing about this place is that they use Time Lord Technology and just like Dr. Who's T.A.R.D.I.S (Time and Relative Dimension in Space) this restaurant is much bigger on the inside than it appears from the outside.  The parking lot can be slammed full of cars but inside it seems as if there is barely a crowd and there always seems to be more tables available.    The service can be at bit slow sometimes and the menu combo selections seem to lack a lot of variety outside of beef and I would like to see more chicken options included.  I wish they would put Mexican hot sauces on the table as the flavors of the food are way too tame and bland for me.  Overall this is a decent place to eat and enjoy some margaritas while basking in the glory of one of the Wanks most popular restaurant spots.

Middle Eastern food that serves later than most other restaurants of this genre in the area.  They have about half the seating inside and half outside on their patio.  The beer prices are more on the expensive side while the food is competitively priced.  Its hard to pay $5 for an Abita Amber here when nearby you can get a slice of pizza and an Abita for $5 at New York Pizza or get just the beer at Brother's Three for under $3.  Overall I would stick to eating and not drinking here unless you need fancy cocktails or fine wine which they do have some good options on here.

This restaurant is really like two separate restaurants in one.  It is located right next to Hong Kong Market so you expect that perhaps they will take advantage of the great produce right next door but I do highly suspect they use quite a few pre-made mass produced frozen items.  One side of this establishment is a buffet style restaurant that is often crowded.  The other side stays busy during the weekends and specializes in Dim Sum and this is about the only place in the area you will get the full Dim Sum experience.  Some of the Dim Sum items are definitely better than others but it is a decent enough experience to make the trek to the West Bank as you can also indulge in some Hong Kong market shopping all in the same trip.

Small little deep cover bar that also offers live music in a bit of an out of the way spot you need to know where it is to know there is a bar there.  During my most recent visit to Sidebar to hear some music there were folks of all ages (like most NOLA bars along with several dogs) inside all having a good time.   The back room where the band was playing was filled up with what I would consider a few too many chairs really to be able to navigate through that part of the bar or even dance so I probably would have been happier with fewer chairs but I would say the same for JazzFest and French Quarter Fest too along with making fun of the chair scene for the jazz performances at Snug Harbor.  Overall a decent little bar that still is a bit of a hidden spot for the moment.

I didn't want to write a review about this place as its one of my secret hide-aways (which I want to keep secret) but the cat's already well out of the bag. This is my favorite bar in this section of the Warehouse District as they always have cold beer at a fair price with attentive bartenders.  The food is generally good and they have one of the best shepherd's pies in the city.  Most of the crowd in this area seems to stay focused on Lucy's so you can either deal with waiting and standing over there or you can almost always find a seat in Vic's and get quick service.

This is quite an affordable and quite a large selection of food on a buffet.  The drink price will up the price of the buffet more than you might suspect so just be sure to double check your drink price before ordering one.  The food is overall pretty decent with a lot of canned veggies along side some decent proteins.  There is a little Chinese food thrown in with some things like Salisbury steak, fried chicken, chicken nuggets etc.    Overall a decent budget place for a variety of food.

Newish hotel in a rougher area of Canal that has been in the process of transitioning for many years now without much progress in the transition part.  Seems they have done some pretty extensive renovations and upgrades to the facility and the bar is really upgraded.  The "happy hour" prices on draft beer are the same price or more expensive than many other establishments regular prices so not sure how they have calculated their "happy" formula out but it doesn't make me so happy.

I'm not sure what happened to my previous review on here about Ben's Burgers (my pictures are still on here) as Yelp sometimes seems to randomly delete reviews for some reason?  Well anyhow this was one of the first of the Bud's Broilers to disappear but they did it in the unique way of just renaming themselves and keeping most everything else exactly the same with slight tweaks while many of the rest of the Bud's have just closed and disappeared.  They have maintained there dive style inside so that is also a bit of a bonus push for them as well.  Bud's... I mean Ben's food is about a 2 star on average to me BUT they are one of the very few spots open 24/7 in the area so that does bump them up an additional star as that is a very valuable thing to have in this area.    Tip:  This joint is still cash only so make sure to have some or you might have to use the ATM and pay the fee.

I used to read the Gambit all the time and it was a great source of information of upcoming events and music.  Since Katrina it has been much harder to find Gambits as not as many places seem to carry them or they seem to run out of them faster.  In the years since Katrina I've actually picked up a paper copy of Gambit only a handful of times and I've gone to their web version more frequently but still only on rare occasion.  My main exposure to Gambit these days is via "Gambytes" their weekly email newsletter synopsis.  Maybe I've just gotten older grumpier and much less cool but I get so many emails about events that my calender is often so full its hard to fit anything else in but I often miss cool things I would've liked to have known about that sometimes get missed in their newsletter.

Deanie's is generally more about quantity than value along with being a bit too much on the bland side for my taste.  There are a lot of other seafood joints in the area that do better tasting food at a better price.  There are also not many places that do as much volume as Deanie's does and they usually also get the fried food out really fast!  Everything is descent for the most part and there are certainly places that do worse food while nothing really stands out to excite my taste buds and all the fried food tastes very similar.  The boiled shrimp here is also 100% frustratingly overcooked EVERY time I have ordered it so now I've given up on even trying to order the boiled shrimp again.  Overall this is a place you can bring a big group and they will likely have something that most folks can eat along with being bland enough for the typical Yankee and others who have spice aversions.

This coffee shop is extremely frou-frou and I came here looking to see what the deserts were like.  The only two desserts here were brownies and sugar cookies at $5 a pop which seemed way too expensive to me.  The brownies looked like the better option but it was still just a brownie with some icing on it which didn't look worth $5 to me so I didn't get it.  I did get a coffee and it wasn't that great for the price either.  Overall I will just leave this place to the ladies as it is most DEFINITELY a space that should be reserved for them.

I've certainly noticed a decline over the years in the quality of the food here along with an increase in price (and the gumbo just doesn't seem worth ordering anymore to me).  Acme seems to have, unfortunately, earned the label of "tourist trap" for a reason but the oysters still seem to be consistently good and that should be the usual focus of a trip here.  The po boys or a fried seafood plate would also be a decent thing to sample in here.  The usual crazy lines at the French Quarter location make it a very rare thing that I will even attempt to eat oysters here as I hate lines but occasionally you can catch times without a line.  If there is a line I most often will be opting to eat raw oysters across the street at Felix's and I always prefer my grilled oysters at Drago's.   If you've never been you probably should visit but to me it just usually isn't worth the wait or the cost.

Delta Angel is in the St. Vincent's Guesthouse which is a cool place to begin with.  The restaurant is behind the main entrance and faces the interior courtyard.  The ambiance here is really cool and funky and they have fur wallpaper behind the bar.  They have 80's music videos they play for Saturday and Sunday brunch.  I don't care what you think about the 80's as I know the 80's were awesome and so much more awesome than the 90's and 2000's it just doesn't compare!  I love hearing REAL music again and remembering when there actually were such things as music videos.  The most awesome thing about this place is they are going to be doing poolside Saints viewing events.  Yes that's right they have a pool here so you can eat, drink, make merry, swim and watch the Saints on a giant inflatable screen.   When this place is crowded they quickly fall behind and don't seem to have enough staff to cover all the tables so service suffers.  When it isn't crowded here you get really friendly and good service.  The menu has a lot of interesting things on it but the sandwiches and salads seem to be the better choices.  They have a nice steak sandwich that has a lot of flavor.  The omelets are very large and have lots of stuff crammed into them but they seem to need a sauce or something extra added as they seem less flavorful than most other omelets I've ever eaten.  I was also disappointed they don't have a dessert menu as a place like this seems like it would have awesome desserts but they don't.   If they can tweak their menu to get everything up to the standard of their steak sandwich and get their staffing levels able to efficiently handle busy times this place easily has potential to reach four star status.

I used to enjoy eating burgers here at past businesses that were in this location. I also miss the old dive ambiance that used to be in here as they have done quite a major heavy handed renovation that has made this place look too bright and shiny new.  I had high hopes for a good burger here but sadly the burger just didn't deliver and it was really less good than a Burger King Whopper.  They have quite a lot of items on the menu here with a large selection of breakfast items and the breakfast seems to be what most folks enjoy here.  I think the burger needs a major revamp here and it definitely needs some major improvement.  Overall I definitely wouldn't get the burger again in its current configuration so I hope they upgrade it.  My video review of Streetcar Cafe is here:  https://youtu.be/GQd-bkbO-tE

Cool dive bar that has darts in the back to hone your skills.  Friendly and fast service from the bartender.  The big downfall of this joint is they still have smoking which usually kills a place for me fast but fortunately during my visit there was not much smoking going on but the smell was still strong.  They had good deals on beer and they had great music playing.  I also believe this bar is owned by Louisiana folks and is a good spot to watch the Saints.

This is a nice little Vietnamese cuisine spot right around the corner from Po Boy King.  They have the smallest bowl of pho I've had anywhere in the NOLA area (smaller even than that hipster joint Magasin Cafe) and that can be a good thing when you are not in the mood for a large or medium bowl (it is also priced accordingly).  They have a pretty concise menu and it is a pretty concise sized space but it seems to be a quick in and out joint for a good meal.

A more cocktail themed bar next to the MidCity Bulldog taking the place of several previous bars that have been here.  There seems to be a steady crowd of folks here and a lot of back and forth between here and the Bulldog.  They have a bit more upscale scene than Bulldog here but the beer prices at both here and Bulldog are expensive unless you can get a good special or happy hour.  You have a better wine selection and more cocktails here so that will bring in a bit of a different crowd than the Bulldog.  Overall this is a decent place to hang out but really I would rather just go to the nearby Mick's Irish Pub than either here or the Bulldog these days.

Its the best casino in the NOLA area... they also really need to step up and upgrade this joint to prime Vegas standards!  For what it is its ok and they know on average they will make about $75 bucks off all the suckers that walk through the door because they are in the business of gaming and not gambling as they make sure the house will ultimately always win and all games statistically give the edge to the casino.  Go here and enjoy the entertainment value of the gaming, the buffet, the restaurants, the shows and other attractions and you will be fine.  Go here expecting to change your life with your "winnings" and most likely you will be unhappy.  A very rare few can be professional gamblers but the only sure fire way to know what your profit margin will be is to own the casino.  Think you can work hard and develop card counting skills?  Card counting isn't illegal but if the casino catches you doing it they can and will kick you out and permanently ban you as they don't like giving up ANY of their edge!  As a privately owned business they can ban whoever they want for any reason.  Firmly grasping the statistics and odds I will still occasionally be a sucker myself and play roulette and craps here as who doesn't like beating the odds sometimes!  The buffet is always open so regardless of the holiday or virtually anything else short of a mandatory evacuation or shut down you can always find some food here.

This is a really fantastic sweets shop that offers a great variety of dessert treats.  They have a great selection of some quite flavorful ice creams with a marvelous texture.  They also have quite an impressive array of fudge flavor options to choose from.  They have quite an above average assortment of both commercial and their house made candies, chocolates and other creations on display.  The delightful display cases wind around to lead you throughout the store in an ever growing lust for the goodies on offer along with tempting you with free samples of many of their delicious offerings.  My last visit was during a cold snap and even the chilly weather couldn't keep large numbers of customers from waiting in line for the delicious items available here.    Overall no trip to Franklin is complete without a visit here.

Schnell's Restaurant & Bar Family Dining is a great old school restaurant with a nice rear area with two separate bars. This is the only bar I've ever seen that sells lottery tickets in the entire USA which I would guess there are more somewhere so if you know of any let me know. This is also one of the very few places in the greater New Orleans area that is open seven days a week for breakfast, lunch and dinner. Schnell's has good po'boys, fried chicken, burgers along with a wide variety of other good choices.  They also have some fantastic onion rings and a great selection of rotating daily specials each day of the week.  Their dessert selection is limited to just the one choice of bread pudding.  Before our current "situation" and "troubles" they would host live music which for now is on hold.  Overall this is a nice spot to check out especially for the daily specials.  My video review of Schnell's Restaurant & Bar is here:  https://youtu.be/av0cNXDBHPA

This is one of the more noted spots for a muffuletta in the area along with being a really awesome Italian market and deli where you can find some really great items to cook yourself, order a meal, get some wine or meet a dessert craving.  They have a special cannoli King Cake many folks crave around Carnival time.  My favorite deli item here is probably their Italian meatball hoagie covered in marinara sauce and Italian provolone cheese.    Overall this is a great spot to check out to do a little bit of shopping and a lot of eating.

This a cool looking spot right across the street from Neighbors bar that although it is called a pub it is much more restaurant as they close VERY early for a pub/bar.  I only had enough time to enjoy one adult beverage in here as they close so early you can't even get warmed up for a night out here.  In practice this place is much more of a restaurant that also has a bar which serves pub type food with some kicked up items.  The ambiance of the place is 80's fantastic and I really like the way the interior, exterior and outside patio look here so if you can start your party earlier this is a great spot to enjoy before they do their early shut down and then you can walk to some of the other nearby area bars that are open later like Neighbors, Edley's Bar-B-Que etc. This is a non-smoking location both inside and out which as a non-smoker I greatly appreciate the lack of cancer sticks in my operational area.  Overall this is a great spot that I just wish stayed open until a decent 2am hour or so.

This seems to be the only Dairy Queen location in the universe that doesn't have hamburgers... at first I thought perhaps a Hindu was the owner but they offer chili fries and hot dogs so that can't be the case.  I have been to this location a handful of times over the years and in the past they did have hamburgers so I'm not sure what happened to make them recoil from offering this staple.  They seem to have all the usual Dairy Queen desserts here so you can go for that but don't plan on getting most of the usual food items you find at all the other Dairy Queens in existence at this excruciating strip mall hell that is thankfully trapped way out in the suburbs so I don't have to be reminded of their chicanery.

I'm not sure what happened to my previous review on here about Ben's Burgers (my pictures are still on here) as Yelp sometimes seems to randomly delete reviews for some reason?  Well anyhow this was one of the first of the Bud's Broilers to disappear but they did it in the unique way of just renaming themselves and keeping most everything else exactly the same with slight tweaks while many of the rest of the Bud's have just closed and disappeared.  They have maintained there dive style inside so that is also a bit of a bonus push for them as well.  Bud's... I mean Ben's food is about a 2 star on average to me BUT they are one of the very few spots open 24/7 in the area so that does bump them up an additional star as that is a very valuable thing to have in this area.

The location of this restaurant is fantastic and it has a pleasing ambiance. This is a chain and this location is sadly not a very good one as I quickly learned.  The staff (on a Sunday at lunchtime) seemed really unhappy (maybe hungover) and service was not very good. The food was just... alright but really bland while the price was way too expensive for the quality and quantity of food so honestly I would MUCH rather eat at Mas Tacos Por Favor for many magnitudes of better Mexican food at a way better price.  I would rather have paid a bit more and just gone next door to Barcelona Wine Bar for a better experience than I had here.  Perhaps this is a fun place to enjoy adult beverages as the location is well situated and designed for that but eating here just doesn't seem to be an option I would wish to pursue again (even the adult beverages didn't look that appealing here so I would probably stick with beer if drinking here).

Cool dive bar that has darts in the back to hone your skills.  Friendly and fast service from the bartender.  The big downfall of this joint is they still have smoking which usually kills a place for me fast but fortunately during my visit there was not much smoking going on but the smell was still strong.  They had good deals on beer and they had great music playing.  I also believe this bar is owned by Louisiana folks and is a good spot to watch the Saints.  The Villager Tavern video review of their Mardi Gras party:  https://youtu.be/mlFbv7G1Lxk

Alright Vietnamese food with a few unique spins on some dishes.  The chicken pho was good and they do multiple versions of their bi chi tacos that are interesting.  I was really disappointed in how small the vegetable basket with the pho was and sadly that just seems to be a recurring theme of Vietnamese places in the city limits of NOLA (Wank and Metry joints give you a huge basket).  The prices are a bit more expensive than a lot of other Vietnamese joints.  The service is a bit scattered and inattentive.  There is a nice patio outside and the indoor seating has a nice view of Maple Street.  The lackluster service would probably detract from making me want to eat here on a regular basis.

I had a kilt made in Scotland and they made some very large promises of which they sadly failed to deliver on any of them other than delivering the kilt.    In stark contrast USA Kilts has exceeded my expectations with every order I have put in with them and their shipping is somehow both cheap, fast AND accurate.  I had a 5 yard kilt made in my family tartan in a different fabric than the "Deluxe 9 yard Hand Sewn Kilt" I had previously had made in Scotland (the folks that made that kilt removed that kilt option from their listing after I asked them why I didn't receive any of the promised services they offered but I never heard back from them).  The 5 yard kilt from USA Kilts I received arrived faster than my Scottish made one even though USA Kilts couldn't get the tartan fabric due to the Scottish mill being back ordered.  The quality of the 5 yard kilt is certainly the equal of the Scottish made 9 yarder with the USA Kilts leather fasteners of higher quality along with providing a better all around fit to the kilt.  The Scottish made 9 yard has a bit more swoosh in the pleats but really not that much more than the USA Kilts 5 yard version.  Where USA Kilts really dominated the Scottish maker in quality was in the Fly Plaid as I only got a piece of cloth that really was too short by a couple of feet for a Fly Plaid from the Scottish folks while USA Kilts did a proper sized piece of cloth with the quality addition of a pleat stitched into one corner to make it far easier to wear.    Overall USA Kilts has really outdone the competition offering excellent value for superior quality along with hitting excellent marks on time to completion and customer service.  USA Kilts also has a LOT of YouTube videos covering all manner of things related to Scotland, kilts, tartans and pretty much everything you might need to know about ordering, wearing and respecting the culture of the kilt.  If you have been thinking of ordering a kilt and think maybe you don't have a tartan well they have a great search feature to let you check out the possibilities of that and then they also have other options for you that they can help you with finding a suitable tartan so definitely contact these great folks.  This is definitely a great business to do business with and they go above and beyond to help out their customers and definitely earn your repeat business and the loyalty of their customers.

This is a pretty grungy dive bar and seems to get more smokey than the average dive joint.  They have a big clientele of pool and ping pong fans here.  There seems to always be an overly serious game of pool going on so you have to tread lightly when passing by the table.  Some of the drinks seem decently priced but then others seem out of whack.  I only seem to end up here when I get dragged by my friends as I hate the smokiness of the place.  There always seem to be an above average number of people looking really rough and grungy in here like they have been awake for many days.  So there are always some interesting characters in this joint that will be really happy to talk to you.

Service was excellent and the front of house was very professional and friendly.  The menu here really isn't a New Orleans style and seems more like some "contemporary modern" trendy something we say it is because we made it up of some type or other.  I also found the fish of the day to be very overpriced and I had been planning on ordering fish but at the price they were charging I know of far too many other places with better deals.  The food was just a total failure as both my dish and my friend's dish were just poorly executed and tasted of nothing but pure salt.  I enjoy my food being heavily seasoned and spiced but our food had no other flavor but just pure salt as if you had poured the salt directly into your mouth.  The only redeeming thing was the smoked fish dip that actually did have some good flavor that was able to get the overwhelming salt lingering in my mouth to diminish somewhat.  Due to this experience I just really can't recommend the pasta here.

They seem to generally only have the upstairs bar open most of the time these days.  I have seen this location change names and owners several times and I had just never actually made it inside as it always seemed deserted.  I finally saw some folks at this bar one night when I was out doing a pub crawl with an out of town pal so we stopped off in here and it was pleasantly surprising.  They do have an actual library study type ambiance upstairs along with a decently sized balcony patio.  The bar is a large one and they have a decent selection of draft beers.  Overall this is a nice spot but it still seems to rarely get a crowd.

The atmosphere here can get loud and boisterous at times and the design is a bit cramped with the maximum number of tables and chairs put into the space.  I think this restaurant is better enjoyed at a larger table and is somewhat less enjoyable at a 2 top.  They do make good drinks here and the restaurant is definitely a better experience when indulging in the alcohol beverages and having a social experience.  I recently made my first visit since the long reigning chef here, Sue Zemanick, departed so the food has certainly had some changes.  The beef tartare lagniappe and hamachi appetizer didn't really work for me to start off the meal.  Things drastically improved for the entrees with the veal cheeks and red snapper both being outstanding.    Reservations would definitely be recommended here and it is certainly one of the top fine dining restaurants in the area while being one of the few hidden away in the neighborhood it lives in.  This is not an old line Creole establishment so it does things many of our more famous restaurants don't do so if you want a break from the typical New Orleans traditional food this can give you some more variety.  Gautreaus's definitely takes some different spins on food in ways you will not find in other area restaurants which those spins sometimes work for some folks but not others but the ride is generally enjoyable.

Well Donkey Balls the new ownership got rid of the real pint glasses and gimped up all the decorations and moved them all around.... The menu is all fancied up and moved about but at least they kept my Radiator Special po boy...

Saint John is a new restaurant which has bravely opened up during the slow times of the ongoing pandemic.  For my first visit I went with a group of friends and we all enjoyed our food and experience.  They have a first floor that includes a chef table space and then a second floor with a great balcony overlooking Decatur Street.  The big food winner here was on their appetizer menu with their "Oysters Saint John" which is oysters served three ways with a selection of oysters poached in double cream then crispy fried oysters and finally oyster dressing in vol-au-vent (a pastry shell).  Our server informed us that the Oysters Saint John has been their most popular dish and some regulars simply order multiple servings of that dish for their meal.  I continued my enjoyable meal with hot shrimp remoulade, seared gulf fish court-bouillon and finished with a dessert of lemon iced box pie. All the other food that was ordered by my group was reported to have been thoroughly enjoyed by all.  The only leftovers were the two gents that had ordered the overstuffed poboys who took sizable portions home for later feasting.  Overall everyone enjoyed their meal and our first experience at Saint John. I have to say this was the best experience I've had with a newly opened restaurant as they had not even a minor hiccup or any other issues with all going absolutely perfectly for our meal.    My video review of Saint John is here: https://youtu.be/nPOZbQfiSZ0

The pizza and pasta are good and the service was generally attentive.  The pine nut caramel gelato is very good.  They have done a nice job vastly improving this former Popeye's and they seem to be building a patio addition on the front.  This is probably one of the better Italian restaurants in Harahan but I wouldn't make a special trip out of New Orleans just to eat here on a regular basis.  If I were in the area this would be a good choice but I think there are equivalent or better options in the city limits of NOLA proper.  The only real negative is that I find the fish options to be significantly overpriced.  Overall this is a nice addition to the area and gives the neighborhood another great dining option.

The only reason I ever go here is for the Thursday and Sunday steak nights.  You HAVE to get here early as they sell out of steaks FAST!!!  They also have a pretty decent menu of other things (like tuna steak).  The steaks have always been tasty, fairly priced, and you receive your order pretty quickly.  The bartenders have always been nice and efficient.  The location is completely strange off in the middle of a combination of residential and weird office spaces not far from Lakeside Mall...only in Metairie could you find a spot like this.

This was actually a pleasant surprise to find decent value good Tex-Mex in the French Quarter.  For many years I had avoided this place assuming it was just another tourist trap for pathetic Texans that refuse to eat anything other than Tex-Mex but they actually do very flavorful food here that can put many places in Texas to shame.  To be fair for many years Country Flame actually was a very sketchy tourist trap venue that didn't do much good but it has certainly evolved in offering quality flavorful food at a good value.  They also expand beyond the typical Tex-Mex options and offer a nice selection of other foods from Cuba and other parts of Latin America which are also executed quite well.  It is a rare thing in NOLA fo find a place that had descended so low in the myths, legends and lore of the Quarter to redeem itself and rise from the ashes to achieve delicious redemption.

They never seem to have the lasagna and that irks me a lot!  The pizza is "ok" but I think I could be fine with never eating it again and I think even the Dough Bowl is better.  The location is off Broadway next to the graveyard way off in the middle of a neighborhood and they keep the door locked so it makes picking up your food a bit shady and the building looks a bit run down and super slim shady.  They could do a little bit of work and make a much more pleasant outdoor dining area and with some more work they could probably even make some indoor dining space.  As it currently stands this place is only good for delivery or carry-out.   Personally I've given up on ever attempting to get the lasagna again and the pizza doesn't inspire me at all so I doubt I will ever return.

The ambiance isn't very good here and the selection is less than at many other sushi joints.  I've eaten at the "noted" Uchi in Austin and had higher expectations for a joint with the same name.  It isn't terrible here but there are just so many better options nearby.  They are quick though so if you're in a hurry this place can be a quick lunch in the often crowded section of this area of the Causeway.

First off big thumbs down for this place being in the Federal Building and being a weapon free zone!  I was in the army and got to bring plenty of weapons into Federal buildings when I was wearing a uniform and I'm very sure the 2nd Amendment applies to the Federal government so they are blatantly violating the Constitution with their dumb "rule" against weapons.  There are viscous insects in this place that are huge and hungry so I have a need to be armed with at least a fly swatter in case they escape and attack!  For being just a bunch of bugs this place is actually pretty cool and they have some interesting exhibits.  The Victorian bug collection room probably was my favorite spot in the whole area as you got to see the wide and wondrous variation of so many insects with their plethora of amazing colors.  The bug eating station was ok and I chowed down on some of the crickets and meal worms.  The movie was actually more entertaining than I thought it would be but you might want to make sure to wear a hat if you plan on attending.  The butterfly garden was ok but I think I was more entertained by the koi in the fishpond than the actual butterflies as alas I had much higher expectations and thought there would be a more extensive garden.  FYI if you get attacked by the butterflies they have a sign saying it's a Federal offense to mess with the butterflies or allow them to escape out of the garden and those critters do like to land on you so you gotta get checked out before escaping the garden.  If you have naughty kids I might suggest skipping the butterfly garden as with all the Federal regulations they might get in all kinds of trouble in there so just go watch the movie and the other giant bugs do their things.  Groovy fact:  I once went on the local TV news after Mayor Ray Nagin and before the African millipede.  Talk about a prime news spot...

I would say don't eat here just drink here except the drink prices are more expensive than Ernst right next door.  I wish I could say more positive about the food but just don't eat it!  I went to Ole Miss, I was in graduate school when Eli played for us, I grew up with Archie playing for the Saints.  I just think they need to start totally over with the menu.  The interior, patio and bar are a great places to watch a game and if just rating that this place is probably four stars but the food and drink prices really drop the ball here.

This is the BEST sushi restaurant currently in the area.  There were some others that came close but they seem to have dropped in quality while Kanno has consistently been excellent.  When I first heard about this place I was extremely skeptical as it is in a bit of a shady strip mall in Fat City and it doesn't look that good outside or inside but once you taste the food none of that matters.  They have an awesome blue crab roll and amazing soft shell crab spicy miso soup!    Elvis and his wife are the owners and work the sushi bar (and maybe you would guess there is a lot of Elvis artwork).  They have reserved seating for their VIP customers that eat there like twice a day as it is that GOOD!!!  You have to earn your spot in the reserved section so don't even try to sit in that area.  Everything I've had here has been outstanding and if you're really good they give you a tasty little frozen chocolate treat for dessert.  They are closed on Sunday & Monday and they take a long holiday back to Japan once a year so you might want to call to make sure they are open but they usually are and it is definitely worth a visit multiple times a week!!!

This place is definitely still open and still where it has always been.  They have a good selection of kosher grocery products and a deli with a decent selection of typical Jewish deli options.  They are very strict about the "kosher" part and won't even make a sandwich for you unkosher by putting cheese on your pastrami sandwich so don't bother asking.  The same applies to their hamburger as you won't get a cheeseburger here and the burger is "ok" but it is a bit dry and for the price I would MUCH prefer a Yo Mamma's burger!  They do give you a really large order of fries with all the grill items like the burger that come with fries.  So even though it is a bit pricey for what you get they can charge a preimium as it is one of the few places in the area that is kosher and that carries many of the items they sell.  For my deli needs I typically go to Martin's Wine Cellar but if I'm in a rush and in the area this place can do the trick as they also have some decent soup... I just often feel some pain in my wallet after a meal here.

The buffet here is more expensive with far less quality and selection than Nirvana.  I would never get the buffet here again.  They had all vegetarian dishes with two chicken only dishes that were all chicken drumsticks, wings and thighs.  The chicken wasn't very good and one of the chicken dishes was very cold.  I had reservations about eating the cold chicken on a buffet and they were well founded as my stomach wasn't right for the next three days.  The vegetarian dishes were alright so maybe this place will make vegetarians and Vegans happy.  Maybe the menu items are better but I was very disappointed in the quality and selection on the buffet.
$5 Abita Amber!  I'm outta here too many other places to drink the same beer cheaper!

I hate smoking but I've got to admit I have puffed on a handful of cigars in my life so if you want a cigar I guess this is a bar to get them at.  I still hate smoke so even though I've taken a few puffs on a cigar I still have no desire to be around them or any other smoke. They have a decent happy hour when there isn't music playing.  When they have music here there sometimes is an up-charge of $1 per drink and I don't like such a policy.  I'm all for supporting live local music but I greatly prefer a cover charge and would much rather pay $5 at the door or have a tip jar for the music and know what I'm getting into rather than a surprise up-charge at the end of the night.  Overall this is a good bar where you can probably find a spot to sit and relax and enjoy yourself and there is a nice patio out in the back.

This is very similar in many ways yet completely different to the Magazine Bulldog.  They have the great tasting selection of 50 draft beers (some of the drafts are different than at the Magazine location) and many more in bottles.  They have a much larger patio and more space inside.  The food menu is identical but the kitchen is much larger (and the cook looks much happier than the super cramped and hot guy suffering in the Magazine location's micro-kitchen).  They have even recently been doing different types of specials at this location and the one on Magazine so they have developed very different personalities.  Mid-City Bulldog generally seems to draw an older crowd on average but with the typical New Orleans mix of all ages thrown in all the time for good measure.  They have much more comfortable seating here and the bathrooms generally seem to be much cleaner than the Uptown location.  The parking lot does often fill up and getting out of the area can be a bit crazy when big events like Jazz Fest and Voodoo Fest are going on.  I still have a preference for the Uptown location as it is just much closer to my house but if I'm in the area I will certainly stop in.

The Mint is part of the Louisiana State Museum and houses the Louisiana Historical Center, The New Orleans Jazz Club Collections of the Louisiana State Museum, and a new performing arts center.  There is a small exhibit of minting equipment that doesn't take very long to get through and really isn't worth the admission fee.  The reason this location gets three stars instead of the two the mint exhibit deserves is that they have several nice little festivals here that are fun events.  Admissions: Adults  $6 Students, Senior Citizens, Active Military  $5 Children 12 and under  Free Groups of 15 or more w/ reservations  20% discount School groups w/ reservations  Free Purchase tickets for two or more museums  20% discount AAA membership discount, with card  10% discount

Ahhh it just doesn't do much for me.  I'm just not the food truck type of person I guess.  When I walked up to order the truck was surrounded by what looked like a vagabond band of gypsies but as I got closer it was just a bunch of nasty hipsters.  None of them seemed to be giving any business to Dos Jefes where the truck was parked and if I were a business owner I don't think I would like this ragged band of really stoned looking kids hanging around outside my place of business scaring off my customers.    I got the brisket and chicken tacos which for the price of $13 I could have gone to a sit down restaurant and gotten an iced tea, a table, and service along with my food.  One of the primary benefits of truck food I thought would be fast service but not so much as there was a decently long wait as there were so many hipsters waiting for their stoner fix munchies.  I thought the chicken tacos were ok while I found the brisket to be really greasy.  My favorite thing was the spicy habanero pepper sauce which gave a nice burn and flavor to the tacos.  When I think of a taco food truck I'm thinking of paying $2-$3 for some super spicy real Mexican tacos that take about 2 seconds to get as that's what I got all the time in Texas.   I'm all in favor of doing any sort of business we can in New Orleans so I'm very happy these food trucks are doing well and its great they make some people happy but they definitely are NOT my thing!
