This is one of the last remaining single theatres in the country and a fantastically fun neighborhood gem.  They do a LOT of variety for having just a single screen and often do special Midnight Events with unique and fun screenings with added pizzazz such as when they do Rocky Horror Picture Show with a live cast thrown in the mix that encourages audience participation.  They also have classic movie screenings so you can experience Casa Blanca and MANY other classics the way they were meant to be seen.  They have upgraded with the times and have a great digital video and sound system. I am also a big fan of their balcony seating area and depending on the movie/event this is often my favorite perch to experience things here.  The only slight negatives I could possibly think of would be the seats are the old school variety which are a bit less nice than the new super fancy movie chairs other places offer and parking is often a bit challenging as it will require street parking in the surrounding neighborhood. I can sincerely report I have had more fun and amazingly interesting experiences in this theater than any other place other than possibly the sadly departed HOKA Theater in Oxford, MS.

Some of the girls working here look nice in the kinky plaid outfits.  I don't think they have food and I didn't see anybody eating or any space for a kitchen.  They have nice large steins of beer available and the patio is decent.  The indoor section is pretty small so if it is hot enough to need air conditioning there isn't a lot of space.  When I went it seemed to mostly be people waiting for seating next door at super crowded Walk On's.  The servers seemed pretty confused so I guess they are still in training mode and getting the new place up and going.  An "ok" place but probably not my first choice for a watering hole as it was majority dudes and the few girls there seemed turned off by the kinky outfits of the servers.  This place is like a mini-Hooters but better outfits.

This place is "ok" for the Warehouse District which is probably my least favorite area of NOLA to go out in unless there is some type of event going on.  They have some "ok" food for a snack but I wouldn't depend on a meal here and the service seems "ok" most of the time.  I've never had a terrible time here but I've never had a good time and I've only ever had just an "ok" time.  So a perfect three star joint and all around average "ok" experience most of the time for a Warehouse District bar.  In relation to any other area of NOLA this place would probably just be a two star joint but the Warehouse is pretty different from the rest so for just that part of town they can get three stars until they get more of a fun crowd and get up to three in relation to all of NOLA.

This is the same good food brought to you by the fine folks at Pho Orchid as they are expanding their reach.  They don't have the full menu here but they do have some things that are a bit different than at the original.  The food is more counter service fast food style and the prices seem a bit cheaper than at the original.  You can really get in and out of this location fast and I also noticed quite a few people getting to go orders.  This is definitely a nice option to have when you have a craving for some Vietnamese but need a faster than the already rapid turn around on your food at the original Pho Orchid.  Definitely my favorite restaurant out of the several that have passed through this location in recent years.

If you're in the mood for fancy cheese this is one of the main places to go and most of the area restaurants that serve fancy cheese seem to get it from here.  They also offer sandwiches, cheese plates, and wine to enjoy along with your cheese purchase should you desire to eat it there instead of getting it to go.  The sandwiches are too small for my preference but everything on them is good quality.  They also have a nice deck to the side and another tiny one in the front that can be pleasant to enjoy when the weather is nice.  This is also one of my favorite areas in New Orleans on a nice stretch of Prytania Street with several nice options for eating and drinking.

This is cool bar that seems to attract a dedicated cadre of locals and here you can usually escape the tourist hordes of the quarter.  They make a mean burger with some good onion rings and ok fries.  The burger is on the larger side and has some juicy deliciousness but sadly I've yet to have an opportunity to try their pizza.  They also feature some changing specials I've also neglected to sample thus far as I'm usually opting for the burger.  This is a dog friendly bar as it is right next to the dog park and so it attracts lots of dog lovers.  The service is friendly and attentive along with often being entertaining.  The prices are generally affordable and not the typical tourist rip off many places in the quarter have degraded into.    FYI:  This is yet another of the bars that claims the notoriety of having had Lee Harvey Oswald as a frequent customer.

This is where many a late night through dawn all-niter becomes an all the next morning bender.  It is rarely crowded but there is always a crowd of characters in here.  Like most of Igor's many locations you can also do your laundry here in the upstairs area.  They also do a limited 24 hour menu of middling quality and are rumored to have one of the best Bloody Mary's in NOLA (I don't like those things so I can't confirm that). I've always had outstanding and highly entertaining service here and your bartender will also be your cook.  I've seen some very strange things in here and met some even stranger people.  I've actually even been an extra in a movie here that a friend of mine made portraying another person I know.  If you find yourself still awake in here after a long night out around 9am then you my friend have reached a new dark level of New Orleans party expertise.  I highly suggest only reaching such levels during Mardi Gras.  Remember eat a little, dance a little, and drink a little to keep your pace up!!!

This is a nice little locally owned grocery that has a good selection of local items and some things you don't generally find at other area stores.  The size of this place limits the selection but they generally have most of what you need if not everything you want.  They have good prepared foods focusing on local dishes and decent to good po boys that are very generous on quantity.  The roast beef po boy is probably one of the sloppiest gravy drenched examples I've ever sampled.  This Zara's location is more pleasant to eat at than their other location on Prytania and they have much more seating.  This is definitely a very unique New Orleans shopping experience that reminds you more of a place in the French Quarter or Europe than the larger grocery stores ever could.

Tulane has done a really nice job with this stadium and it has really revitalized the fan base and made games a lot more fun.  The Tulane games in the Superdome always seemed to be missing a lot of energy from the "crowd" which never seemed like much of a crowd but there is no lack of that here.  The facilities are top notch and this is a great addition to the area.  Tulane has done a great job managing crowds and traffic so there really isn't a lot of noticeable burden placed on the surrounding neighborhoods.  The only things I'm not happy with are that they don't allow kegs in the tailgate area and they are also following the general trend of being the PC police and blatantly violating the civil rights of citizens as they have rules that fly in the face of the First Amendment:  "Refusal to remove or turn inside-out clothing deemed offensive or obscene upon request by stadium personnel"  and   "Possession of any unauthorized banners or signs"  along with their "Rules of Conduct" that further outline restrictions on speech.  Any infringement on civil rights should be intolerable at any University and free speech, even when offensive, should always be respected and held sacred as the free exchange of ideas and language should be the basis of any place of learning.  We've had incidents in the news recently where people will find offense at almost anything so these restrictions on free speech under the guise of being afraid something will be deemed "offensive" are just ludicrous as you can find someone that will be offended by almost anything these days.    Overall this is a great stadium and Tulane provides a fun experience and they just need to escape the PC police nanny state attitude that is just un-American and allow keggers back where they belong at tailgates.

This joint is much more similar to the old Pancho's on Vet's than the terrible and short lived new one we got off of Airline.  The all you can eat option is a bit pricey for Mexican so unless you're really hungry you might want to just order from their non-buffet options.  They don't have the little flags to raise and instead have lights to turn on which just don't seem as fun as the flags.  Overall its a decent spot if you need a Mexican buffet.  Personally I don't see myself craving this buffet too often and would generally prefer other spots to eat Mexican but sometimes you just need to gorge on a buffet I guess.

Its much more of a convenience store than a grocery and the biggest sellers here seem to be alcohol and lottery tickets.  Its a bit larger than your usual convenience store and they do have some produce and food items that your usual convenience store won't carry but the prices are on the higher side.  I usually end up here for lottery tickets or during Carnival to grab drinks during parades.  They're typically inconveniently closed by 8pm and I would recommend going slightly further one block down to Zara's on Prytania for a better experience and better prices on most items.  You also typically get to deal with drunk bums panhandling outside this location.

This place makes good snowballs and assorted snacks at far better prices than many of the other more popular snowball joints.  The neighborhood definitely still has authentic Central City eccentricities with things like Ya Ka Mein and people banging on the window of the snowball stand yelling about money they think was charged wrong.  It is usually a really quick turn around and faster than many of the other snowball joints about town.

This is my usual cleaner and I bring most of my dry clean items here.  This is a family run business and usually members of the family are there working.  The prices are more expensive than most other dry cleaners in the area but they do seem to generally do a good job.  This is probably the best dry cleaner in the city but it certainly isn't always up to the level it needs to be.  I've had some stains on linen and seersucker suits that didn't get completely removed and you do need to point out problem stain areas if you want them to get extra attention.  I've also had some wool suits that started sprouting some sort of funky mold on them that Liberto's was able to wipe out.

I had an eggroll and the milkfish and unfortunately I just didn't like anything I ate here.  I was told my fish would be smothered in a sauce with shrimp and I got exactly one shrimp.  I found lunch here to be extremely over priced with the food just not to my liking and it is probably the first time I've ever eaten a fish dish I didn't like.  I don't eat pork and most things here are very pork centric so maybe that's what I'm missing here.  The space and service were all nice but unfortunately it just seems the food here is not for me.

This place has a small patio and small indoor dining space (and small to the point it can be a bit cramped).  The patio can be enjoyable when the weather is nice outside and they do have outdoor heaters for cooler times.  This place used to have more of a French Caribbean food theme (I didn't really like) but they have seemed to be going more towards a French Bistro concept over the past few years (and I like that much better).  They often do some good mussel dishes and the menu seems to change pretty often.  Generally good food but I've had few exquisitely divine dishes to stimulate my long term memory so far.  The patio is the main draw of this place and usually this wouldn't be my first choice for dinner but it is a pleasant spot on a nice day to enjoy lunch outside.

For the West Bank this place is totally four stars but it would be around 3.5 on the East Bank.  This is probably one of the finest dining locations that the Wank offers.  They also have made some great food for many events that I've attended.  They have some very good gumbo here and they also offer a nice choice of daily specials.  I particularly enjoy their Tuesday night all-you-can-eat crab special and the Thursday night half-price oyster (and ladies drink free) special.  I've actually even hung out in the bar here for a birthday party once and it seems to be a popular spot in the area.  I've eaten here many times at lunch and dinner and the service has always been friendly and efficient.  Most of their food is good with a few items being less than stellar but in general the majority of items are well done.  If I'm not in the mood for Vietnamese when I'm working on the Wank then this is probably where I will be going.

This is definitely not a "hidden gem" anymore and the word has gotten out and this place has become a victim of its own success turning it into more of a tourist trap.  When the usual wait time for brunch and lunch on the weekends is an hour then you can safely assume the secret is out.  There are far too many great restaurants in NOLA to wait around an hour anywhere to eat.    The food here is worthy of three stars and it is mostly plain and simple food with a Louisiana/Mediterranean flair made with fresh ingredients.  Everything here is "ok" but nothing jumps out as outstanding or must have other than they do serve really nice bread.  The ambiance in the courtyard is nice and the inside is quaint but you can find similar experiences all over NOLA without the hour wait.  This place is worth at least one visit but I highly recommend you do it during the weekday and not the weekend when the tourists descend in droves to drive the wait times up and the experience down.

This was a very cool venue with the upstairs beer garden area being especially a great place to hang out.  The guy running the line into the front door was really sociable and helpful with getting people educated and ready to order along with being entertaining.  The BBQ brisket was acceptable (I've definitely had way better) but the portion size was certainly on the smaller side for what I'm used to.  They have a respectable selection of sauces but they only give you a bottle of the vinegar sauce while the other sauces they bring in tiny little weak ass microscopic containers that make me really unhappy as BBQ places that dole their sauce out like it is made of solid gold unobtainium really hurt my feelings and cause me severe emotional and gastrointestinal distress.  Also service upstairs was not and getting a refill on a drink was never going to happen so I deeply regret leaving a tip as I sure didn't get anything approaching service.  Overall this is a cool place to hang out at in the beer garden but save your tips for the bartenders.  Pro-tip:  You can skip the tourist line and go order upstairs for a shorter line.

I had heard some good things about this establishment and finally got a chance to try it out.  When I arrived there was a good band playing and a few older folks sitting at tables enjoying the music.  The building has been nicely redone and the small patio outside is a nifty nook to hang out and the upstairs is a nice place to take a break from the louder music downstairs.  I ordered the bouillabaisse and an Abita Amber for dinner.  The bouillabaisse was decent and came with four large shrimp, several mussels and some slices of fish.  I've definitely had better bouillabaisse in my time and certainly less expensive as the bill with my beer came to $31 before tip.  The other strange thing I noticed is all of their beers from Budweiser on up and including Abitas were $5.  This establishment really feels like more of bar but the food and prices are more in line with a fine dining restaurant.  For the price I really could've enjoyed better food at a better restaurant.  The price of the beer here will really prevent me from hanging out here to enjoy the music.  This place seems like it will end up catering more to the tourist crowd than the local crowd so I hope they have success with that but I wouldn't mind if they offered some locals specials with more realistic beer prices.

This place is near my office so I will rarely pay a visit to it when I need some quick and cheap Italian.  Typically I'm going for the lasagna which probably merits at least 3 stars and is usually decent.  The pizza here really isn't very good and leaves a lot to be desired and when my office gets pizza delivered from Cafe Roma I'm really left with very unhappy taste buds.

This place has a good menu selection and the food tastes very much like homemade and eating at somebody's grandma's.  The crowd tends to be of the older grandparent type as well.    I have experienced some really slow service at lunch which isn't a big deal unless you need to get back to work (and I really did at one visit).  The red gravy is one of  my least favorites in the area and some of the food could have used a bit more spice for my taste.  The prices are a little above average on the specials and for some of the non-specials so it can get expensive to eat here but you generally get large portions and most stuff is "homemade."  Personally I think the seafood selections and non-Italian dishes are usually the better choice here.  They do have a pretty extensive menu with a lot of enticing selections.  There are still many things on the menu that I would like to sample (I've heard good thing about the fried chicken but that takes awhile to cook so you have to wait for that). This is a classic old New Orleans style Italian Creole place that you should certainly visit at least once.

This is a place for sugar addicts!  If sugar wasn't legal it would be illegal and the only thing that makes sense about all the good reviews here is that there are LOTS of sugar addicts in the world these days.  EVERYTHING here is disgustingly sweet and I'm not a sugar addict so this food just isn't good to me, I find it a poor value, and the portion size doesn't fill me up.  I've been here 4 times so far and I ate during the first two visits then just drank on my third visit, and on my (last) fourth visit I gave it one last chance.  The food is just not good to me at all (granted this is not my favorite style of food).  The first time I had the jerk chicken and found it to be SLIMY and not at all spicy.  The second time I had the tacos and found them bland, very very small, overpriced, and not at all filling.  The third time I sampled several of their drinks which were good but not outstanding and nowhere close to being worth the PRICE (and this was during happy hour).  I had heard recently that the food's flavor has improved substantially since they first opened but on my last visit the tacos are still very tiny and the lamb and scallop tacos were super sweet to the point of being gross to me.  The price for three micro tacos and an iced tea was $18!  It was such little food I had to buy three more tacos at a taco truck not long after for $8 so just double your order at the taco truck and you will still save money and maybe get a decent sized meal that doesn't taste like pure sugar.  This place gets two stars instead of one as it is a good place to people watch and it does bring in a large crowd (somehow, despite the mediocre food, that I just don't understand except it is between Juan's and Nacho Mama's so maybe people run from Nacho's to Juan's and then Juan's is too crowded so they compromise to go here).   I'm completely not  a fan of their food and thus regulating it to a place I might just occasionally grab a tropical cocktail.    Tip:  If you eat here on a regular basis you are going to have a much higher risk of developing diabetes as the sugar content of the food is sky high!

I LOVE Greek Fest and I go every year.  I do the race on Friday night and you get free beers, a t-shirt, and free entry for the entire weekend for the price of your race entry which ends up being a great deal.  I love the food, the music and most of all the fun people that are enjoying themselves to the maximum here.  This is a great family event with activities for all ages.  Beer, Wine, liquor are all in abundant supply and the pastries are decadently delicious so it is definitely a must do on the festival schedule.  Friday night has always been the most fun for me but I go all three days!

This review is just for their carry out pizza.  I had The Bird pizza and a cheese pizza.  This was some of the worst pizza I've ever had.  It was covered in some type of "crumbs" that I'm not sure if it was seasoning or quite what it was but it gave the pizza a really gritty texture.  There were not a lot of toppings on the pizza and the crust was thin but not in a crispy tasty way like Theo's.  Usually I get full after half of a large but I took down the entire medium Bird and then two more slices of cheese and probably was still a bit hungry.  It was Super Bowl Sunday so maybe that had something to do with it but I really didn't like the gritty "crumbs" and would definitely opt for Pizza Delicious over this in the Bywater area.

This is one quirky, kooky, cool place!  The have a lot of fresh produce and meats from the owner's farm and I really like that.  On Friday's they have an insane deal where you can eat almost everything in the grill, deli, and prepared food section of the store for $19 and they had raw oysters, bbq, steak, pizza, fish, and all manner of other things going on.  The Friday special is just  an insanely good deal!  The owner's farm produce looks fantastic too.  They have a very eclectic selection of all sorts of different products and this is certainly one unique store.  They even have a selection of Mardi Gras beads, masks, and boas upstairs.  This is definitely a spot you will ONLY find in New Orleans!

This is a very small and cramped space right next to Parley's Bar.  The location is really lacking as there isn't any easily accessed bathroom for customers here and I like to wash my hands before I eat.  The burger is good quality and they use "artisanal" buns which are also quite good and tasty.  The namesake Jaeger Burger is $7.95, which is a bit high for a burger but reasonable for the quality, whereas the plain fries are $2.95, which is outrageously high for simple french fries!  The fries here are simply boiled potatoes sliced and fried (that resemble a cross between a potato chip and a french fry) they also offer cheese fries, chili cheese fries, debris fries and poutine fries.  Honestly I wasn't that impressed with the fries and for the price I would suggest just skipping them unless you plan on going for some of the topped versions.  They also have hot dogs, roast beef debris sandwiches, fish sandwiches, shrimp salad and some "vegetarian" options.  They advertised "iced tea" on the menu but only had bottled versions of all drinks.  They do take credit cards but they certainly have to make a few tweaks to make the dining experience here more enjoyable.

When I first heard of Santa's Pub years ago I thought it would be similar to New Orleans own holiday themed dive, Snake and Jake's Christmas Club Lounge, but Santa's Pub is way more high class.  Mainly this seems to be more of a karaoke joint and they only serve beer with no wine or liquor so I couldn't do my mandatory Santa Jager shot or a Jameson like I do at Snake and Jake's.  Of course I have to say that currently Santa's Pub is way more entertaining than Snake and Jake's as ole Snake's has seen better days while Santa's Pub is killing it with some really great and entertaining karaoke fanatics that are backed up by an enthusiastic and supportive crowd of fans. The main downsides to this place are the smoking inside and the cost as I ended up spending more money(cash only) in this dive than in any other bar I visited in Nashville as there was a $5 cover and then beers were around $4 apiece,other than that poisonous PBR hipster crap that is only $2,  while nearly everywhere else I went in Nashville had some awesome 2 for 1 beer special or other great deal going on (I must have made Santa's naughty list). Certainly a cool spot that is certainly worthy of a visit if you can make it at a time with fewer nasty smokers.  I am also very confused about one thing with the karaoke?  They have a rule that you can't cuss while singing but what about songs with curse words in them?  Like what about "getting run over by a damn ole train" or some such cause you gotta cuss to sing the song?

They get some good music here but it isn't as much fun and its far smaller as compared to the YLC Wednesday on the Square.  They have a small selection of vendors to get food and drinks from.  Parking is easy and you can also take the ferry for a nice visit.  My only complaints are that there is no shade so you are in the sun the whole time and the beers are bit too expensive.

They have a decent fish and chips here which as they are inside of an Irish bar is pretty much a mandatory requirement.  The burgers here are also pretty dang good similar to Company Burger but better and are some nice bar grub.  Their fries/chips are also pretty nice examples and quite a bit better than most of the other bar's fries in Mid-City.  They have a decent selection of other food items that should make most folks happy for a snack or a meal so certainly worthy of a try.

I hate strip malls but I seem to end up at this strip mall more than any other.  They do have some useful stores in and around the Elmwood Shopping Center that make trips here a necessary evil.  There are some good bargains to be had here also.  We also can't neglect to mention the Elmwood Fitness Center that is located here which is one of the hugest fitness emporiums in the state.

Decent bar with a Winston Churchill theme where most of the folks that live around Metairie Road seem to congregate.  It seemed like more of a fun and happening spot before Katrina but it still gets quite crowded in here at times with a bit of an older crowd.  They had a fire and had to do some remodeling repairs on the inside and they also built a nice deck patio in the back.  The food is decent but the beer prices have been creeping up of late but thankfully they have finally gone smoke free inside.

This is a really cramped space and you really get no service after ordering.  The chicken pho here is not as good as Pho Nola or Pho Orchid's.  They seem to cook their pho very hot and fast here as they have the hottest broth temperature I've ever experienced from a pho and the chicken had an over boiled texture.  The food isn't terrible it just isn't nearly as good as other nearby Vietnamese places and for the same price I can actually get a little service and get my tea refilled at those places.

There isn't a lot of running at this event but there is a tremendous amount of drinking.  This event seems to get more crazy popular every year.  They really need to add more port-o-potties as the lines get out of control during this long debauched day.  So you wear a red dress, listen to live music, and drink beer from 8am till around 2pm when they feed you some Corky's BBQ and then unleash you to go on a pub crawl up and down Bourbon Street.  It is definitely a marathon of drinking and not a sprint so you need to pace yourself... even then you will need a nap most likely...  This is a great fundraiser and a crazy fun time.

This is your basic coffee cafe with desserts, salads and sandwiches that could be in Anytown, U.S.A.  They have some pretty good cheese cake and the iced tea and coffee are decent.  This just wasn't a place that appealed to me very much, it just wasn't my type of place, as I don't really like coffee shops to begin with but they can serve as good work spots but I can't see getting much work done here.  This place would probably be at least three stars to most other people but it just isn't my cup of tea and expensive for what you get.

Had a great time on Friday and ate way too much food.  The great thing about this festival is that it has food vendors that aren't normally at a lot of the other festivals so you get the opportunity to sample many new things.  I basically ate everything in the Italian area and a crawfish pie.  Lots of good local bands last night but it never got uncomfortably crowded so it was easy to get around and enjoy lots of space while enjoying the music.  One the great things about this festival is that it is spread out all over Gretna so you get to actually enjoy some of the local bars and restaurants in the area.

The good news is that this place has an extensive selection of authentic NOLA home replacement  parts to renovate and maintain your historic property.  The bad news is this is a graveyard of parts and pieces of historic homes we've lost.  The prices are also quite eye opening as many of the items are quite more expensive than you would think.  I fear such prices will further the looting of many of our abandoned historic homes and further deteriorate them so they become even less likely to be renovated.  Entire blocks of historic neighborhoods were torn down in the process of building the new Medical Center of Louisiana on 78 acres so apparently there are forces that would like us to look like strip mall everywhere else America at work.   I mourn the passing of so much of NOLA's history and charm but this is probably still the best place to get historically appropriate replacements and repairs to your historic NOLA architecture.

There is food from all over the country at this fest.  It is always VERY hot at the time of year this fest is held so that makes being outside a big challenge.  This is a good opportunity to sample a lot of things you usually wouldn't get to eat locally.  I love the Louie Mueller's BBQ brisket that travels to be in this sometimes but I'm always pissed off they don't have sauce and they say "our meats so good it doesn't need sauce."  Yeah but at your restaurant in Texas I've eaten at many times you got sauce and I WANT sauce so bring it dang it!  Overall its a decent event for a quick snack trip but the heat usually prevents long term enjoyment.

This is about the only sushi joint in this area of Jeff Hwy and its ok for what it is.  The rolls I ate didn't stay together as well as I would've liked and they were a bit over soaked in some sauce for my taste.  They have some decent specials and although the outside looks terrible the inside is acceptable but small.  It isn't going to tempt me away from Kanno anytime soon but if you're in the area its a decent option.

So some of the ownership and some of the employees of the Chart Room moved over here.  They have a nice little courtyard area where it looks like they have a stage where they can have some live music.  The bar is quite a large rectangular design which offers up plenty of seating.  The clientele seemed to be of the older variety when I was in there and it seems like a good spot to escape the crazy tourists of Bourbon Street.

I've eaten at Byblos on Magazine for many years and it is usually good with some consistent patches of less than good incidents.  My first experience eating here was terrible as I got the lamb sampler platter and everything came out burned black and crispy.  Fortunately that was the low point and things have generally been better since then.  Byblos does some things better than other Middle Eastern places but not as good as others in the area.  I generally find their beef kabobs are consistently outstanding while the quality and taste of the lamb is very inconsistent.    Byblos was a much nicer and larger restaurant at its former location and now its much more casual.  Usually a good place for lunch or dinner but sometimes some inconsistencies do pop up.  Overall I think the food was better at the old location and I just never really end up here very often since they moved.  I really like Byblos Market on Vet's the best out of all of their locations and I eat there quite often.

This is very basic and very likely pre-packaged Chinese food that gets a good reheating in the wok.  It is probably a bit less quality than your usual Chinese buffet but they do give you large portions and they are usually very quick.  Depending on the dish you order you might get more or less of the highly probable frozen pre-packaged ingredients in your food.  I have gotten food here a handful of times and while not bad it certainly didn't have the zing of fresh veggies and the sauces were just ehhhh not so flavorful and it probably rates among the most bland Chinese I've ever had.  Depending on the rotation of who is working the front they may or may not speak English so you might have to point at what you want on the menu.  You can dine in, get delivery, or take out but the vast majority seem to get take out or delivery.

This is a small local chain and they have other locations on the North Shore plus a Mexican restaurant in Metry.  Food was ok but nothing special really and just your standard Mexican fare more on the bland side.  Tacos are of the small variety and for the price I would MUCH rather go to  Taqueria Guerrero on average.  They do have $1 taco night on Tuesdays so I might go back and try more things then.  The server I had was really cool and asked if we had a Groupon and then let me use my phone to quickly buy the Groupon and use it for the meal.  This is a prime spot for Carnival parades so I imagine it will be busy for the season.

This is one of the all time worst casinos and draws a crowd of people that look like they are in terrible physical shape and might drop dead at any given moment.  The cliche of the person with an oxygen tank still smoking their cancer sticks is easily found here.  The place is very smokey and has an air of despair and depression about it.  I rarely go to casinos but I've been to many of them and this one is certainly among the worst I've ever seen.

WOW this place has probably one of the largest menus of anyplace in the New Orleans metro area!!!    They have shark fin soup, abalone soup, various versions of pho, Chinese, Vietnamese, and several other Asian dishes thrown in for fun.  The only complaint I've got is they don't offer jasmine tea like several other Vietnamese places do (maybe they do and I just don't know how to order it).  I see more Vietnamese people eating here than just about any other place I've eaten in the area so maybe that means this is a really good authentic Asian place.    I really enjoy the food here and it is a really good value and actually just a downright cheap place to eat with fantastic food.

This is a very convenient grocery to where I live but they are a bit on the smaller side and often lack many things you can find in larger stores.  The BEST thing about this grocery is they often have the cheapest prices on beer of nearly anywhere else in the city (cheaper than Walmart).  If I'm pressed for time and need to do a quick in and out this grocery is by far one of the easiest places to do that as parking is very easy and I've never had to stand in a long line here.

I usually eat these tasty treats from Debbie when I'm visiting 12 Mile Limit but darn it if the bartenders don't usually eat up all the salty balls.  I've also been to quite a few parties and events that were blessed with the yummy goodness of the baked goodness from Debbie.  You should stop in and try some if there is any left at 12 Mile Limit or just go ahead and order some items as they will be delicious.

I've eaten at the Magazine location for years as it is the closest to where I live.  I've also eaten at most of the other locations (my favorite location is the one on Banks Street that has their market attached to it).  All of the locations have been very consistent in quality and service.  It isn't the best Middle Eastern food I've had but it is generally good.  I really like their iced mint tea and I usually get the combo kabob platter.  I also like the Mona's sampler which gives you a selection of their appetizers.  I think they have the best kibby in New Orleans and I do enjoy munching on those.  I've nearly always had good service at all the locations of Mona's I've eaten at.  A little known fact is that you can bring in your own wine and they don't have a corkage fee so that can be a nice way to enjoy a pretty inexpensive fun dinner.

They have a mechanical bull made up to look like a killer whale.  They have 3 for 1 drinks on some things but not all things for some reason during their happy hour.  The same people that own this bar also own the Bourbon Cowboy right next door and they even share the same plastic glasses but for some illogical reason you get a smaller selection of 3 for 1 drinks in this place than you do at Bourbon Cowboy.  They have a large back patio area and it can be semi-entertaining to watch tourists ride the "whale."

This is currently some of the best pho around Uptown (at least until the two new places open on Magazine and better than Jazmine and maybe equal to a bit under August Moon but that still isn't all that great).  The prices were about $2 more than other places for a bowl of pho on the Wank or in Metairie.  They have a decent size menu of other Vietnamese food and they also offer delivery in a limited area.  They were stingy with the basil but very generous with the bean sprouts and peppers for my pho.  I can walk to this spot from my house so it will certainly be very convenient for a quick pho fix.  The service was polite and efficient.  So even though I prefer the better Vietnamese food at other locations (West Bank & Metairie) I will probably be returning often just for the sheer convenience of the place.

This is one of the best places in the New Orleans area to get a wide selection of freshly caught seafood options along with some live, frozen and prepared items.  This is basically a shopping mall of various vendors offering various selections of items mainly focusing on seafood with some having tamales and other prepared and frozen foods.  Mona Lisa Lounge is also a short distance away and they offer boiled crawfish when in season.  There is also a nearby dock offering Swamp Tours.

This is the nearest Chase bank to my house and its also my absolute least favorite Chase I ever visit.  There is invariably a line to use the ATM and frequently there are bums begging for money after you use the ATM.  Often the ATM is out of cash or broken for some other reason.  I do my best to avoid using this Chase branch and regret it nearly every time I do!  I much prefer the TWO Chase locations on Prytania right past Napoleon that have ATM's nearly directly across the street from one another.  This branch is in extremely sore need of more ATM's and they need to run the panhandling bums off!

This is the ONLY cab company I use in NOLA period!  United is the ONLY decent cab company in the entire city of New Orleans and I've always had consistently good service.  You can almost always schedule a pick up and even on extremely busy days with huge events going on they will answer their phone and tell you a pretty accurate wait time.  Almost every rare instance I've used another cab company they have tried to rip me off and do all sorts of crazy routes (or didn't know where they were going) so (especially if you are not familiar with New Orleans) ALWAYS use United Cabs!!!

Hidden in plain sight near the intersection of Tulane and Jeff Davis is an often overlooked Mid-City gem.  I had often driven past this bar without giving it much thought, as I hadn't heard about it from anybody I knew, but it turns out this is actually a very cool dive joint.  This is a much needed 24 hour spot for Mid-City that offers up live music and good food.   Sunday's are an awesome time to visit as they have $5 small plates so you can sample a wide range of their offerings at a reduced price.  They have different specials 7 days a week and the friendly staff and patrons make this a joint a pleasure to experience.  They have very good burgers with fresh fries that are among the best in the area (kudos to Yelpers Danon H. &  Charles H.'s reviews for informing me about the great burgers here).  The crowd here did seem to trend towards the older side so if that bothers you then go somewhere else and leave us grumpy old folks alone :)  Tip:  We need more 24/7 spots in the city and this is the only one I know about in Mid-City so lets get back to those pre-Katrina days when there were 24/7 joints all over!!!  Dmac's gets one extra star for being about the only 24/7 spot in Mid-City!

This is a decent little Brazilian store with a cafe.  They have some nice steak, chicken and fish plates that come with a large plate of rice and beans along with a less nice iceberg lettuce salad with some tomato slices on it.  I also had two of the meat pies and they were a bit bland for my taste but similar to most other items like this I've eaten.  They also have sandwiches and desserts along with a selection of Brazilian and other Central and South American drinks.  I was a bit sad they didn't have any iced tea though.

This dive joint is mostly a music and event focused venue.  The main thing that can be said about this place is that its red both outside and inside.  When it gets crowded the bartenders can get a bit grumpy and things can move really slow so they might need to hire more bartenders for crowded shows.  It can also get really hot when it gets crowded which when that displeasure is increased by the length of time it takes to get a drink the combination can make customers a bit grumpy.  This is a good place to watch music when it isn't packed but be cautious if it is packed as there might be grumpy people inside.  Every Monday is Bluegrass and Hi Ho is really the only place in the entire NOLA area that you can regularly enjoy that music form and that's my favorite time in this joint.

The brisket here has a nice smokey flavor that seems to build on itself and linger for awhile in your mouth.  The servings of brisket I've had so far seemed very lean and a bit on the dry side and I generally prefer mine a bit more fatty and moist.  The BBQ sauce was pretty tasty but doled out in a little container and as dry as the brisket is it NEEDS some sauce.  Overall I like the food but I'm just not a fan of the Barrel Proof bar this place serves out of as it is way too hipster for me.

The location is really run down and dirty.  The service is terrible.  The food is awful and probably the worst Chinese I've had in the area.  They do give large portions but when it tastes the way this stuff does in such a dirty environment you should fear eating it.  I wouldn't return!

NOLA-Q is a BBQ pop up that serves 6pm til around 9pm on Friday at Coulis Restaurant and Saturday at Pal's Lounge.  They offer moist and lean brisket, pulled pork, pork ribs, chicken and sausage.  They have some pretty decent sides which are a bit better than some other BBQ joints in the area.  The service at Coulis seems more restaurant style while the Pal's is more bar grub style.  The brisket is certainly among the best I've had in the New Orleans area but doesn't quite reach up to the level of the Joint but its the closest of any I've had.  They offer three BBQ sauces: mustard, St. Louis sweet and spicy chipotle.  I find I like to combine the mustard and chiptotle for my brisket eating pleasure.  Definitely some good BBQ and worthy of checking out!

In the Spring just prior to the ravages of Katrina Anthony Uglesich closed shop after 50 years of working in the restaurant his father opened in 1924 after immigrating from Croatia.  I only got to eat here a handful of times as it was only open for lunch Monday through Friday and then closed for the Summer.  There was ALWAYS a long line here so along with their hours it made eating here very difficult if you had a regular job.  The only times I got to eat at this famous dive were when I ended up having some time off which was rare for me during the days when they were still open.    Uglesich's was well noted for their fresh and always local seafood.  Their food was certainly good and it had a unique flair that made it different from any other area location.  I did enjoy my meals there but it wasn't worth a three hour wait to me and I would only venture to eat there when I could catch a day with a short line.  Sadly this is another NOLA institution that "ain't there no more" and I still miss it when I often drive past it on my way home.    The good news is that you can still get a piece of Uglesich's from their cookbook and they still occasionally do catering:  http://www.uglesichs.com/

The food here is interesting and the taste of most things is good.  I'm always a bit cautious about "fusion" places and this place combines Asian and Latin food but so far most of the food has turned out well.  The service is a bit inconsistent as it has been slow and inattentive sometimes.  The owner has been here every time I've eaten here and has made a point to ask about my meal and it seems he asks everyone in the restaurant how their meal is and he has also been eating the food every time I've visited so that's always a good sign.  For a "bar" they are still only open a couple of nights with most of their service being at lunch.  Compared to most other Asian and Latin restaurants the portions are a bit on the smaller size for the price and overall most things are not the best value here for the amount you're served so you will end up shelling out at least around $20 with tip for most of the entrees on the menu and an iced tea or other drink.   The curried noodles have a nice spice to them but I think I would prefer another noodle type than the udon they are served with as the udon seemed to get all the chicken to slide into the bottom of the bowl.  I think I might like this dish with udon noodles if it were made as more of a soup so the distribution of everything would be more even along with throwing in some more veggies.  The burger was very tasty but could've used some cheese and maybe an egg on it while the fries served with it didn't really do much for me even though they were mixed with cheese and seaweed which might have been nice on some thicker duck (or goose) fat fries.    Overall I like the space and the food while the service and prices would give me pause to regularly eat here.  I'm impressed with the owners hands on approach and I expect they will make course corrections as needed to get this place up to a fantastic place as they gain experience.

This Whole Foods is much smaller than most with a bit less selection and no prepared hot food bar area.  The unique location and reused space do give it some nice unique qualities.  You can often find grass fed beef here which you usually can't find in the Metairie location.  Whole Foods also has some of the best BBQ beef brisket in the area along with a good mix of local, organic, and non-GMO produce.  They also offer lots of high carb and high sugar baked goods that most "vegetarians" and "vegans" thrive on.  I look forward to one day meeting a "real" vegetarian or vegan that actually eats veggies instead of basically living off desserts and muffins :)   Parking is usually a painful experience here and it is DEFINITELY better to go in off hours as people act crazy about parking here.  After Katrina I lived next to Whole Foods flagship location in Austin so this is certainly a much less dynamic store but it usually serves its purpose.  Unfortunately during my last visit I'm not sure what was going on but there were the least amount of fresh fruits I've EVER seen at a Whole Foods.  I was going to get some grapes but there were none to be had???  One last review of ONE Star for all the LAZY people that leave their carts strewn all over the place in the parking lot!  If your going to eat healthy maybe take a few extra seconds of exercise to put your cart back and OUT of my way you rude, pathetic excuses for civilized creatures.  It is the utmost in poor manners and you are probably the same douche bags that zoom in and cut people off to steal the parking space that someone else was patiently waiting for.

This is probably one of the most unique and different dining options in NOLA.  It has a menu that is far different than almost any other in the area.  They do some very unique things with some of their food AND drinks.  I've been for dinner many times and lunch once and always found it tasty but sometimes the portions were a bit smaller than I would have liked and I found myself still a bit hungry after.  The seating area is very small and cramped inside with more space outside so you might make some new friends because you will be very close to others.  Describing most of the dishes and drinks here just wouldn't do them justice so you just need to get down to the quarter and try this place out.

I only seem to end up in this joint every few years.  They usually have some decent to good music playing in here many nights.  It has always been crowded when I've seen shows here but you usually can get drinks pretty quickly which is always a plus.  I've always had a decent time in here but nothing of epic proportions.

This is a really cool, old school, dive bar that has a fantastic atmosphere with wonderful service.  They have a loyal following and it is a great place to hang out  and enjoy yourself.  They have a great steak night every Thursday (just $10) and the prices on the drinks are always reasonable.  It is in a bit of a hidden location so you need to know it is there or you will probably just drive right by it.  This is definitely a great place to grab a drink and soak in some local ambiance.

This place is convenient to grab some food before or after a movie as it is adjacent to the AMC theatres.  They have some very nice soups here and the typical Americanized Chinese food is all good.  I did have a really nasty experience here one time when I was chowing down on an egg roll and suddenly noticed that there were lots of little specks in the duck sauce... as I looked back over at the duck sauce I saw lots of ants crawling up and down into it... ahem I had just eaten a large number of ants in the duck sauce on my egg roll!  Well at least I didn't get charged for the extra protein but when I brought up the fact to the waiter he acted like he really could care less.

I liked the old Saturn Bar a lot more because the "new" Saturn is full of hipsters and I don't like hipsters as any dude that wears those really tight jeans is just stupid and causing serious damage to their future reproductive capacity (but since hipsters should never reproduce anyway maybe that is a good thing).  Hipsters also don't know how to drink beer right and they are always smoking and I hate nasty smoke.  So I still make random appearances in here for old times sake just to see the freaky bands they have here and to demonstrate proper beer drinking skills.  The place has been cleaned up of a lot of the "clutter/art" that used to give this place more character but it is easier to move around inside now.  Definitely still has some great dive bar ambiance that is worthy of checking out if the hipsters aren't smelling extra funky bad that night.  The jukebox is still fantastic as it hasn't been updated since the 70's so all GREAT music and none of that modern rap hip hop crap with all that deep non-stop bass that hurts my head.

I've had the burger, fish'n chips, and a smattering of some of the other offerings here but I've still yet to sample the actual BBQ.  This is the main food that is available in Finn McCool's and most of it has been pretty good.  They have a very tasty and large burger available here and it came with fries that were also very good so the cheeseburger and fries is probably the best thing I've had here so far.  This is certainly a great place to grab a late night snack.

This a great French style bakery on a convenient section of Magazine street.  They have nice breads, pastries, sandwiches, quiches, and sometimes pizza and other daily specials.  This place seems exactly like bakeries I've been to in France and is a nice place to get your baked goods or grab a quick breakfast or lunch.

This place has some good brisket, great BBQ beans, and nice mac n' cheese.  Continuing the recent trend, that seems to be happening in the fast developing NOLA BBQ scene, they offer three distinctive types of BBQ sauce.  The brisket was very tender and flavorful but unfortunately lacked the hallmark of a distinctive smoke ring to really give the brisket maximum flavor.  The brisket was served with a side of horseradish sauce which was a welcome flavor addition.  The BBQ plates here are served with sweet potato "beignets" which seem more akin to baked muffins but still very tasty.  The BBQ options in NOLA continue to grow and improve and while this place certainly does offer some good BBQ and great sides the brisket at the nearby Smokin Buddha Bbqieux greatly outshines what is offered here.

The best thing about this joint is that is it is open 24/7.  The food ranges from good to mediocre while the drinks are mostly good and the beer is great.  The seafood gumbo isn't really worth the effort and the burger probably is one of the more unremarkable ones in the city so there are far better choices to make on the menu than those. They have a really awesome side of mashed potatoes with gravy and you should explore more of their entrees.     The crowd here often consists of strippers getting off shift or going on shift along with a motley selection of other locals mixed in with a fair number of tourists.  It is a bit more low key than most of the places on Rue Bourbon so you can be near the madness but escape for awhile here.  The staff is generally nice and the service is usually adequate and friendly.  There are better places and worse places to eat in the Quarter but in the realm of 24/7 joints we have fewer of those than we used to so this place gets to join a small elite group of the few remaining 24/7 eating and drinking venues left in the city.

I've eaten their burgers, salads, and a few other of their menu items. The fish tacos are really expensive and you can get much better ones at Sarita's.  The service has been a bit slow and I've sat with my drink empty for far too long on every visit so far.  The atmosphere is interesting with all sorts of folksy art, hipster groovy stuff meets gas station.  As a disclaimer I should admit that a lot of the (rather small) menu seems to be a bit too Southwestern influenced for my taste (nothing wrong with Southwestern except it just isn't my favorite style of food; plus I'm getting bored with the Mexican/South American/Latin "influenced" menu items at so many different places and it seems to be getting really overdone in NOLA).  I would certainly recommend Cowbell's burger over Tru Burger (the best burger in this area is probably still at G B's Patio Bar & Grill) and rather than eating any of the main entrees here at dinner I would head to Jacques-Imo's instead for a better meal at a similar price.    The food I've had here so far has been fresh and well prepared but nothing has really excited me so far.  It is a decent place to grab a quick meal at lunch but wouldn't be my first choice in the area for dinner.  It is a good spot for an occasional change of pace but I won't be  a regular here as it is a bit too expensive for what you get.

This is a uniquely New Orleans tiny grocery store.  They have all sorts of things that you just won't find outside of Louisiana (such as sausages made with things like shrimp, alligator, and crawfish).  They have a great selection of single serving entrees that really include a much wider variety of things than any other grocery with items like rabbit.  They even had a selection of canned escargot I noticed on one visit as I was browsing for something.  This location is a popular spot to grab drinks during Mardi Gras as it is close enough to the parade route to be convenient while being far enough away to not be crazy crowded.  Before Katrina this location had awesome po boys and prepared foods.  The roast beef po boy is still one of the sloppiest to eat anywhere and is packed full of goodness.  They still have a great selection of daily specials but the quality of the po boys and other foods seems to have declined in recent years.  This Zara's location always had much better food than the other one on Prytania and I largely credited that to the main deli guy, that doesn't seem to be there anymore, as that big guy really put together some good food and seemed to have a love of food (and always made sure you were going to be fed VERY well).  The portions are usually still huge here but just not as tasty.   I still think it is worthy of a visit but I just don't go here as often as I used to.

This is a great dive joint for 24/7 dining and drinking along with a fun Jazz Brunch.  The burger is ok and they have some interesting variations of it but the other items on the menu are probably better choices.  The back dining room is smoke free and a much better place to eat.  The front bar area allows smoking and can be VERY smokey where often even the bartender is smoking.  You also get a bunch of strange Quarter characters that seem to gravitate towards the front bar so if you're looking for Ignatius J. Reilly you might just find him here.

This is a relatively small bar by New Orleans hotel bar standards.  It reminds me much more of a restaurant's side bar than the main bar of a large hotel.  The Green Bar (I think I would rename it the Green Room as it is really more the size of a large room) is pleasantly appointed in dark wood and green colors so hence the name.   Due to its location and size, I would see this spot as catering mainly to the tourist crowd that would be staying in the Westin.  I imagine this might also work as a more intimate and private location for a small party or event as well.

This is generally a nice store and seems to have a wide selection of items and it is the best Dick's around New Orleans.  Unfortunately I've just never been able to find what I'm looking for here and always seem to just end up having to go to Academy where there seems to be a better selection of items on hand.  They do have some decent sales here sometimes and unlike the Metairie location they do sell firearms.

This is a decent venue for watching live music and other performances.  It retains much of its old theater architecture which makes things interesting with multiple levels.  The space really seems on the smaller and intimate scale so you can really get up close to things.  The single bar does seem to get a bit too crowded at times so maybe some ideas to add additional bar locations could be developed.  The drink prices are outrageous so I don't drink much here and they really need to bring the prices down to realistic and reasonable levels.  I like to drink beer when I watch live music so the drink prices here really discourage me from attending events at this venue as I refuse to pay rip off tourist prices.

I've ended up eating here many times as this is a great place to introduce newbies to the cuisine of New Orleans at an Applebee's like level and you can lead them further on from here.  The majority of the customers are tourists but they still have decent prices for the Quarter.  I think many tourists get recommendations for this place but then confuse it with the similar sounding Cafe Maspero which doesn't have food as consistently decent as what you get here.  The food at this establishment has always been done ok and they offer a good selection of New Orleans classics that most folks find pleasing.  This is also a very historic building where many notable events happened with probably the most significant being General Jackson planned the Battle of New Orleans here so that adds a bit of extra ambiance and makes your tourist friends happy that they have a story to tell about where they ate.

So during my college days one of my friends had a crazy group of Welshmen decide to come and visit NOLA.  "Ahhh I hope your ready for us as you yanks can't drink worth a damn compared to us Welsh" said one of the lads as we picked them up at the airport.  I looked slowly back at him and replied, "oh really now I think I've got the perfect place to test that theory."  So off to Bourbon Street and Tropical Isle I took them.  I pointed up to the sign they have posted where it described the record for consuming Hand Grenades was 11 and the Welsh lads all looked at each other and laughed and said, "what that's all we will knock that out in no time!"  So as they were about midway finished with their fourth Hand Grenade the whining began, "so what time are we going home now it does seem to be getting a bit late and we had a long flight you know."  I looked back at them coldly and said, "I thought you were going to drink us under the table and it seems I'm on #5 while y'all are still on #4?"  A few more minutes pass by and the Welsh begin to turn greenish and suddenly one of them vomits all over the floor and in quick fashion the rest of them all take turns running to the bathroom to yak.  They didn't want to do much for the rest of their trip but eat.    On another occasion I drove down from Ole Miss during Mardi Gras and met some folks I knew and one girl comes running up to me with her Hand Grenade proudly in hand as she began to hug me and suddenly unleashed massive amounts of green hand grenade infused vomit all over my brown Doc Martin Oxfords.  I used to think Doc Martin's were impervious to most damage but the vomit hand grenade mixture ate the polish completely off my shoes.    On another road trip from college we ended up drinking Hand Grenades and Horny Gators and all seemed fine until on the ride home the idiot in the front passenger seat decides he needs to vomit.  The dumb ass sticks his head out facing forward against the wind as I'm sitting in the back seat punching him in the back of the neck and head yelling for him to turn his head to face behind the car.  When the vomit is unleashed it all comes pouring back splattering the entire interior of the car along with my entire face and body.    Tip: Don't drink more than 4 hand grenades or you might get stupid and then vomit everywhere.  Don't be "that" person!

This is just a review of the rude behavior of Oxalis staff I encountered and not the food or otherwise as I didn't get to that point.  I attended a wedding in the area so my friend and I are all dressed up and decide we want to try Oxalis so we look at Yelp and it says they open at 4:00 but we go to Bacchanal first to have a bit of wine fun first.  So we arrive at Oxalis around 4:54 and walk right in and don't see a hostess but there is a bartender busy doing some bar things behind the bar so we just take a seat as nobody else is inside.    After a few minutes a lady carrying a box walks by and asks "are you waiting for somebody that works at the restaurant" so we indicate we just want a menu and some drinks.  The very unhappy box holder tells us that "the restaurant isn't open yet and the door shouldn't have been left open so you shouldn't be inside."  I asked what time they opened and the box women tells me, "5:00" so I look at my phone and reply, "it's 4:56?" so we get up and leave and go to Delachaise instead as there was no way we were waiting outside in the thermonuclear heat.  I guess they really hate seersucker suits in the Bywater as this was the most unprofessional and rude experience I've had at a New Orleans restaurant.    Geez box girl sorry you were having a bad day but that was just EXCEPTIONALLY rude and unprofessional to treat customers like that.  I don't care so much when people are bunghole whack-jobs to me as I will make entertainment out of them but the fact that this box girl was rude to my guest made me quite unhappy.  Quibbling over a mere 4 minutes in NOLA is ludicrous and cost Oxalis income that night so a firm application of a lesson in Southern manners is apparent as I assume box girl is some form of Yankee interloper unversed in our superior Southern ways and traditions of polite human communication.

This is probably the most dive Italian/Mediterranean joint in NOLA.  They have pizza, pasta and sandwiches.  The food is generally good and the service ranges from attentive to indifferent depending on who, what and when is going on.  The last thing I ate here was the pasta marinara with meatballs which overall was good except my meatballs were cold.  I probably wouldn't suggest this as an initial spot to bring a date but the prices are very affordable for NOLA and a bargain in the Quarter.

FREE music and often many FREE beer, wine, and liquor options!!! Ok so there are different groups that do it depending on the time of year and they try to call it different things but since I'm the boss of fun and proper English descriptions of things I'm mandating that they all just be called Wednesday at the Square as that is the best description.  What isn't to like about this Spring and Fall event that brings all sorts of fun loving people into Lafayette Square after work for a fun filled afternoon that usually turns into a longer night that leads to a bit of a hazy Thursday.  There are great food options, local vendors of all sorts of crafts and other goods.  Wednesday's on the Square is just like our own little old school Jazz Fest that we get to enjoy for nearly half the year at the great price of FREE :)

Tiny little coffee shop back behind Delachaise Wine Bar set in-between Prytania Bar and Aline Street Beer Garden across from Touro Hospital.  A few tables and chairs outside for seating with even less inside space to sit but most folks seem to just grab their items to go.  They have some soft drinks and other bottled beverages along with some cookies, muffins and a few other assorted food items.  Usually this is a pretty quick in and out place to grab some caffeine or other beverage.

Zea's has some pretty solid rotisserie meats and some interesting sides that are not very common at other restaurants in the area.  They are a bit pricey for what they offer.  Zea has very consistently good (but not great) meat and seafood.  I generally avoid chain places like the plague but this is a local operation and has quality far and above most other "chain" type operations.  I will go for the meat maybe about twice a year.

This is probably the nicest location of this local chain as it is located in a historic house.  They have built a nice patio and done extensive renovations to this location.  The food isn't anything fantastic but on average its good.  The service is adequate and they have a decent selection on their menu.  The lasagna portion is respectable but the flavors could certainly be bolder.  They frequently offer excellent drink specials at this location.

I've eaten lunch, dinner, and been to some special events at August.  I've certainly had some 5 star meals but on average I would say the experience is typically a 4 star for me.  The food has generally been very good with the portion size a bit lacking for the price at times.  Service has always been outstanding and I've always felt very well taken care of here.    The most interesting experience I ever had here was for a special lunch with the featured speaker being none other than that ass clown recovery czar, Ed Blakely.  This was very early in the Katrina recovery process and Ed explained to us his main plan for our recovery was centered on the fact that he was a vegetarian and people in New Orleans didn't eat enough vegetables so he believed our recovery should focus on building more green groceries in every neighborhood and riding our bicycles more.  At that time he was certainly putting the cart before the horse and I think we had a lot more pressing problems to focus on, like repairing basic services and infrastructure, so that probably explains why he was such a dismal failure.    Lunch has seemed to be a pretty simple affair and not at all crowded like some other well known venues in the city.  There also never seem to be any great drink specials like other places offer during lunch so generally I wouldn't really recommend this as a "fun" lunch spot but they do have a GREAT value with a $20 lunch special but I think to get the full experience dinner is my preferred meal here.

I really liked the CC's Coffee that used to be here so I didn't visit this place for quite awhile.  The coffee here is actually quite nice and it is an easy place to visit with the bonus of quick service which results in long lines being rare.  There are quite a lot of coffee shops in this area and so far I would say this is the best coffee I've had in any of them.  The interior area also has ample seating and has always had space available when I have visited.

Acropolis has been serving me great Greek food for many years out of their location on Vets and this new (and much larger) second location has taken over the former Wayfare space on Freret Street.  This new location also has a much larger bar area which should go well with the Freret Street scene.  The staff is still very new and getting their routine down but overall things seem to be running decently smoothly for a brand new restaurant.  I look forward to enjoying their delicious fish specials and other great food at this much nearer location to me.

They have great daily specials along with some good po boys, burgers, muffulettas, and platters.  They give good size portions and usually have your food prepared very fast.  I really like their meatball muffuletta and they make most of their food in-house which really improves the quality.  It has an ambiance more like a fast food place and while they do maintain some quality New Orleans style food the service can lack at times.  If you want some quick and tasty local food this is great spot to eat.

Ahhh another one bites the dust and I forgot to post this review back before they went outta business...  This is a corner grocery with a small selection of items and a nice selection of adult beverages and po boys along with other hot food.  This place has been around for many years under various names and it has largely stayed the same while the rest of Magazine Street has continued to gentrify.  If you want a quick and cheap meal that is still pretty good this  is a decent spot to investigate.

This is a Chipotle style fast food type of sushi/Poke Californian/Hawaiian type joint where you just pick your ingredients and get your bowl of food made based on your choices.  You get a decent sized bowl with quite a generous selection of ingredients.   The establishment seems to be very efficient and gets your food to you much faster than the average fast food establishment and maybe even faster than your usual Chipotle time.  The food seems fresh with good flavors available for toppings and sauce options.

Sadly I have to say my last Puckett's experience at this location was nowhere nearly as nice as my last one in Franklin.  I really have enjoyed the Franklin location and I had thought that I would most certainly enjoy this location but that was not the case.  I was disappointed they were out of the special of the day even though I arrived shortly after they opened as somehow "it didn't get made or something" according to my server.  So I rolled with the punches and decided to try the burger instead.  The food took a really long time to come out and the server kept coming back apologizing for the wait.  I started to get a bit nervous about the wait time as I had an important meeting coming up so my time was growing thin but finally my food arrived.  Unfortunately my order ended up being a less than good burger as it was too much on the burned crispy side.  I didn't have time to send my food back so I grimly crunched through the crispy burned burger patty and went off to my meeting in a less than happy state.  I KNOW Puckett's can do much better food than this so I'm not sure what series of troubles happened to result in my poor experience on this last visit but something was surely amiss in the kitchen that day.

This is probably the all around best Asian buffet when it comes to quality and selection.  They have some pretty decent boiled shrimp and they also do the right thing and pay a bit more to use Louisiana crawfish instead of nasty imported ones (which sadly enough probably can't be said about a lot of other places around).  This isn't really the place to come if you're looking for a hibachi or sushi buffet even though they do have a decent selection of sushi.  Any dish they have here is almost always better quality than any similar dish at any of the other buffets.  They have one of the largest selections of entrees and always seem to have a nice assortment of fresh fruits.  Even when Oki Nago was at its peak and super awesome this buffet was always good and had its place for things you don't find on most of the other buffets (like their large boiled shrimp) and they also have good roast chicken along with some other surprises not usually found on a typical Chinese buffet.

I love Oktoberfest and I also need to disclose that I'm also a member of the Deutsches Haus.  For the last weekend of September and the following three weekends in October the Deutsches Haus puts on a fantastic event full of German beer, booze, food, music, and fun!  I very much miss the Oktoberfest celebrations at the old Haus which was destroyed as part of the eminent domain takeover of property for the building of the new LSU Hospital.  The great news is the new Haus will be in a much better location and the plans for the new Haus look AMAZING!  In the meantime Oktoberfest is being held at Rivertown in Kenner Bra...

Wow total surprise of not knowing about this cool dive bar in the CBD.  I live on Carondelet Street in the Garden District so I gotta give some extra bonus points to places on my street.  I haven't eaten here yet but this is a popular bar that somehow I've never heard about.  The only thing I really didn't like about this bar is that they only have one unisex bathroom you have to get a key from the bartender to use. The crowd here is lively with an interesting variety of folks in here.  I'm certainly going to have to check out this place more often and eventually get around to sampling the food.

I dined here with a friend of mine and I've got to say that Tempt really didn't tempt us at all.  The Saint Hotel, in which Tempt is located, is an interesting place with all sorts of weird disco lighting and they seem to prefer a hazy blue glow.  The decor of the restaurant gives a different experience than the hotel with some impression of being open and breezy with lots of flowing curtains but unfortunately they also have one out of place long table with some really horrendous clear plastic chairs that seem very fragile and might break if you bump into them that are accompanied by some sort of embellished throne chair at the head of the table that looks very odd.  With curtains being everywhere they strangely left them off the large plate glass windows that look out onto Canal street.  The view from these large windows lets you experience the eclectic mix of people wandering down the street but they can see you too (and most of them looked pretty rough).  The menu is very small and really seemed pretty boring so I settled for the salad, gulf fish, and peach dessert.  The restaurant was nearly deserted and only one other table was occupied while I was there but it still took a very long time for the food to come out.  The food really wasn't to the level it needed to be to "tempt" me and I just didn't enjoy any part of my meal.  The portion sizes were also so small that I had to eat another meal later.  There was one guy working front of house that had to do everything and he seemed to provide the best service he could but the poor fellow had to run all over the place to get things.  Honestly I don't think I would ever want to eat here again and the main thing I felt tempted to do was get out of the place as fast as possible.

This is definitely one of the most neighborhood of all neighborhood bars.  It is just like a suburban house set amongst many other houses.  You won't be getting all rowdy and crazy in here but you can certainly have a calm and collected good time in here.  You definitely need to know where you are going to find this place and I've never seen it crowded.  When people move to Old Metairie and miss their nasty days at Snake'n Jakes they can come here for a clean and hygienic version of a hidden away neighborhood bar.

This is a dive seafood joint slinging boiled and fried delicacies from the waters of the area and beyond.  They seem to have a decent sized line most of the time here and you wait to get to the cash register to order and then you wait to pick your food up after if to go or sit down with your number at a table for dining in.  They are noted and very popular for their boiled crawfish and during the season that is probably the most popular item here.  On my last visit I had a fried trout filet which was good, a shrimp sandwich on bun that was good and fried oysters which were overcooked which made them too hard and rubbery.  The building Castnet is in also houses Walker's BBQ so you can double down with seafood and BBQ if you wish.

I'm not the biggest fan of chains but this is the only location in NOLA so that makes it unique to our area.  The other cool thing about this place is they actually serve you on actual plates and give you real silverware.  You also get semi-table service and your food is brought to your table.  I had to pick bones out of my chicken tacos so I wasn't exactly thrilled about that.  The grilled and fried chicken are really good for a fast food style joint.  The real treat here are the sides with plantains and yucca fries.  I'm going to return to try the empanadas.

The roast beef sandwich here has a good flavor but it took only one napkin to clean up after and it seemed a bit light on the meat.  The New Orleans style French bread from Hi-Do Bakery seems a bit different than most other breads used by po boy places and gave the sandwich a bit of a unique texture.  This place is very much out of the way for me so although it isn't a bad drive and the restaurant is located on a major Westbank thoroughfare it was still a long way to go for a sandwich.    The ambiance and location are not very stimulating as this place is located in a bland suburban strip mall and is saddled with all the stereotypes that brings while the inside appears very clean it doesn't convey much personality.  The staff seemed nice enough but the ordering experience just seemed more like a fast food place than a typical New Orleans po boy experience.  The menu also had some interesting looking daily specials that seemed worthwhile of checking out if you aren't in a sandwich mood.  Overall I really wouldn't ever go out of my way again to go all the way out here to eat but if I were in the area I would certainly return.

This is a convenience store with a little restaurant in the back along with being the Miami Dolphins Football Team fan headquarters for New Orleans.
