They also have some of the best pho broth I've ever had and make some good po boys.  Saturday is their big pho day so that's when I suggest heading here to sample some of that fantastic soup.

I have several friends that live near Oscar's in old Metairie so I end up here more often than I would otherwise.  The bar is the center of the space with seating on either side of it.  They usually have female bartenders working that give decent to great service.   There is usually a mix of all ages earlier in the evening but the later it gets the fewer people remain so this is definitely a place to visit earlier and not later.  My main complaint about Oscar's is that they tend to close early by New Orleans standards so I've had many occasions where we've just arrived and they shut the place down 5 minutes later so we have to relocate elsewhere (usually Winston's).  Oscar's does make a solid juicy burger (except for the Metairie St. Pat's parade when it is crap) and they have several other good looking things on the menu but over the years I've only eaten the burger so far.  The burger is comparable to Port of Calls (but maybe even a bit better with a lower price).  Oscars is a decent place to eat and hang out but if I didn't know people in the area I wouldn't have much motivation to visit very often.

This is probably one of the better sushi places in Metairie.  The regular rolls here are very small and the main thing that makes this place stand out are their specialty rolls.  Fuji has a larger selection and variety of specialty rolls than just about any other sushi place in the area.  If specialty rolls are your thing then this is your place.  Personally I prefer Kanno in Fat City.

I just really did not enjoy the food here and I was very sad I didn't go to Barcelona Tapas, Lola's, or Vega Tapas.  Maybe I ordered the wrong thing or it was an off night, as my food certainly didn't seem anything like what other reviews describe, but after two visits my tongue just said BLAH.  I also drank my fair share of Sangria here and found it to be pretty weak compared to other comparable establishments.  The service was non-existent and it took an insanely long time to get served.  Just not my kind of place and granted I do hate small plates at most places but if they are done the way Barcelona Tapas, Lola's and Vega do them then I LOVE them.  Unless something major happens I will probably never return to Cafe Grenada as there are too many other and far better choices.

This is a "higher class" dive of a diner with a Southwest leaning menu with some Italian and New Orleans dishes thrown in for good measure.  The menu certainly goes all over the map with its dishes and that seems to leave some less than excellent execution but generally they pull off "ok" food.  The burger and lasagna are decent and the Mexican style food is edible but not my first choice.

Ummm it is a hipster congregation spot with pretty mediocre food that consists of mostly breakfast items and sandwiches.  I'm not at all into breakfast so this is probably the worst place I could have ever chosen to eat.  I got a sandwich, it didn't make me happy, it took nearly an hour, it was expensive for what it was, and I was still hungry; so I went to go eat lunch AGAIN somewhere else.  I get very unhappy when that happens and want to unleash one star but I will give them one extra star just in case my dislike of breakfast and hipsters is clouding my senses.

I have gotten to deal with agencies like this in multiple states and NOWHERE else I have lived has anything to compare with what a large time investment is required to get things done in this establishment.  It has ALWAYS been packed crowded here every time I have needed to make a visit.  The new "REAL ID" currently can't be done at the private driver's license and title businesses that I would prefer to deal with to pay a bit more for a LOT less time waiting.  The state of LA really needs to make more things available to do online and to expand what the privately contracted businesses can provide.  The folks that work here are generally very professional and nice at dealing with the typically large number of VERY frustrated people that typically get crammed into this space. You get to here LOTS of complaining and unhappiness in this joint and sometimes you get to finally be called up to the window and discover you were routed to the wrong person and then you get to wait AGAIN.  For working folks this process will often require just taking the entire day off from work to get their business done.   Other larger areas do this process better so will Louisiana ever learn to improve messes like this?
Good jerk chicken tacos on Taco Tuesday, weird clear plastic furniture and awkward service.  Annnnd they are already out of business before I finished my draft.

A chain restaurant that ranges from decent food to Applebee's blah quality.  Consistency is a practice that seems to evade the food preparation and service.  Generally you can get an OK meal but far more often than acceptable you can get a less than enjoyable meal while on rare occasion it can actually be pretty good.  The service can be really slow to refill your drinks about half the time depending on the server but sometimes you really get a great server that takes first rate care of you.  Overall they really need to work on their consistency as they have demonstrated they can do things well when they are running on all cylinders but they have far too many hiccups to be rated as reliable.

This is an old school Nashville dive joint famous for their burgers.  From afar their neon sign might lead you to believe this is a dive bar instead of a dive restaurant.  The folks that own this restaurant and the folks that work in this restaurant are all really great people that take good care of you in here.  I had to get the cheeseburger and then I allowed my rebellious nature take over to get the hashbrown casserole for my side.  The cheeseburger was a good old school style delicious flavor and the rebelliousness certainly paid off as the hashbrown casserole was fantastic.  They have other sandwiches along with daily specials and other menu items that are worthy of trying as well it is just a matter of finding the time to try them as this place does have some limited hours closing at 3:30pm so no dinner service.  Overall this is a classic old Nashville place that is a great spot to visit and friendly folks that will take good care of you.  Bonus: They have BEER!!!

Food was alright but nothing really stood out to me other than the high price for lunch.  I was also pretty disappointed along with being rather shocked and insulted that I wasn't offered sherry with my turtle soup as that is a form of sacrilege in NOLA.  The lamb meatballs were ok but definitely not very filling.  The "drink specials" and "happy hour" prices seemed high priced even on special.  The space is interesting but the parking is limited in the area and I'm not sure this restaurant really fits in with the area.  The concept seems to be casual dining with fine dining pricing.  I actually had to go eat a second lunch after this lunch to fill up.  Maybe dinner is better here... sadly Spicer's restaurants just don't seem to ring my bell generally.  Overall there are just a great number of much better options at much better prices.

I love Oktoberfest and I also need to disclose that I'm also a member of the Deutsches Haus.  For the last weekend of September and the following three weekends in October the Deutsches Haus puts on a fantastic event full of German beer, booze, food, music, and fun!  I very much miss the Oktoberfest celebrations at the old Haus which was destroyed as part of the eminent domain takeover of property for the building of the new LSU Hospital.  The great news is the new Haus is at a much better location on Bayou St. John and the new Haus is finally finished (on the outside at least so for this year you still can't go inside as they are still finishing up).  Throw on your lederhosen and dirndl and come ready for action.  Prost!!!

The food here is generally quite mediocre and there are so many other more flavorful options around it just makes it rather hard to choose this place.  They have a really varied and interesting menu but the food lacks that important component of FLAVOR.  For example their Singapore Noodles dish is the most disappointing example of the dish I've ever sampled and the nearby China Orchid has a much better version.  They have some potential but they really need to concentrate on improving the flavors.

I'm very dissappointed in how they have been raising prices here and they are now the most expensive bar in Mid-City by far.  I really like the Bulldog but I'm not paying $4.50 for Abita Amber when I can get it for $2 and $3 at all the rest of the bars in Mid-City.

This place has some good tacos with better tortillas than many other joints in town. They pretty regularly offer special tacos that rotate randomly.  You can sit anywhere you want as long as you enjoy outdoor dining as they have covered and uncovered patio dining here.  The food is ordered at a counter and then you are given a number and they bring it out to you.  The food is usually brought out pretty quickly and I've never had to wait more than a few minutes for my tacos.  They have a couple of hot sauces and some water at a little station in the covered patio section.  They also sell booze and I have tried some of the drinks and they are alright but seem weaker than some others joints.    Overall this is a decent spot to grab a really quick meal and it is also really near Tipitina's for an added bonus.

This is one of the "must go to" places in New Orleans for classic food that hasn't changed in years.  You also must learn to listen to your waiter about what is good and if you go often (or know people that do) you will get to have a preferred waiter that will take very good care of you.  There are few things as important as having a good waiter at Galatoire's so take good care of one when you get one!!!  You must eat downstairs and preferably on a Friday for lunch.  I've always had a great time downstairs with excellent service and great food.  Upstairs I've had a great time and great service for private parties.  Eating upstairs with reservations I've had some very poor service and extreme attitude ONCE from a bad waiter (when he was tipped 15% instead of 20% for said poor service, and a sommelier that never showed up after repeated requests, the waiter threw a hissy fit until others at the table caved in and gave him his extra 5%).    I've had some fantastic dinners downstairs (my last visit I somehow didn't spend more than $50; even after drinking massive amounts of beer while with wine it can get much more pricey).  Generally the food is outstanding but sometimes it can be just good depending on many factors so it is important to ask your waiter what's good that day!!!    This is old line classic New Orleans food that isn't nouveau, trendy or quite to everybody's taste (especially if you have been on a diet of Applebee's or Tex Mex non-stop) but they have been doing what they have been doing for a long time so respect the tradition and have fun!

Service and food just really underwhelmed at every point.  Drinks had black particles in them that turned out to be coffee that had somehow been spilled in the ice.  Prices for the quantity and quality of food made it not a good value.  Service was very slow and frequently the waitress just disappeared for long stretches.  The food took quite a long time to come out for what it was.  This establishment definitely seemed to be disorganized and struggling to get into a functional mode.

Holly is a really cool lady and as a bonus she also makes some kick-ass tamales.  Holly's Tamales are usually found being sold out of Holly's purple tricycle that has a large food box on it from whence the delicious tamales are served.  The tricycle can generally be found in the Bywater, Marigny and Quarter areas but sometimes special requests for other locations can be accomplished.    Holly learned her tamale skills from her family and its a tradition that is several generations perfected now.  I've had the noted Doe's Eat Place tamales along with many other tamales around the country and Holly's are the best I've had as they are the perfect mixture of meat and masa with optimal moistness that add up to great flavor (as so many other places have tamales that I find are far too dry and flavorless).  The tamales are variable day to day but thus far I've known of them in the options of vegetarian, pork, beef and chicken with the occasional special creative flavor touches added for more variability.  Some days you get more choices than others so it just depends what's going on with Holly's schedule so if you want a specific type just talk to Holly and she will let you know what her plans are for her upcoming batches.    Well what are you waiting for?  Go get some Holly's Tamales!

This is a nice little mid-range Italian joint in the Quarter that leans towards a bit of a dive ambiance with a smattering of hipness mixed in with an obsession of all things Mona Lisa.  They have a good lasagna along with other nice pastas and pizzas.  They have decent salads and their house feta vinaigrette is very similar to the one at Vincent's Italian and is quite tasty.  If you're in the mood for Italian in the French Quarter this is probably one of the most affordable places that does consistently good food.  As an extra bonus they offer delivery throughout the Quarter and Marigny.

This is a pretty comprehensive pet and garden center that for my preferences is far superior to any PetCo chain type joint.  The staff is super attentive and helpful from the moment you walk in and they really provide superior customer service.  The aisle labeling could be a bit more comprehensive and descriptive.  They have live animals available for purchase as a pet (or in the case of the rabbits deep frying and passing off as chicken tenders; seriously fried rabbit tastes just like chicken; yes there are still places that serve rabbit in New Orleans and you should eat it).  They also have a great selection of garden essentials so you can multi-task here to shop for both pets and your garden so BAM automatically being a better option than PetCo along with being far more pleasant than a Wally World.  So go adopt some delicious bunnies and have a great delicious time and get some garden seeds to make sure you plant some nice side dishes.

I ate here soon after they opened and just now remembering to post the review nearly a year later so I would imagine they have improved most things by now.  The stuffed mushroom appetizer was good but a bit pricey.  The paella was decent but the shrimp had a bit of an off fishy taste that detracted from the dish.  The chocolate terrine dessert was just passable but it really wasn't worth the price while the tres leches was a bit better while still being too small a portion for the price.  The service was still getting up to speed and were not up to standard but I imagine it has improved by now.  This place is alright but I find the Spanish food at Lola and Barcelona Tapas to be more to my taste.  Overall my experience just was nowhere near what I typically enjoy at Lola's or Barcelona Tapas but I need to get back here again to see how things have developed as they have gotten good ratings thus far.

This is a really interesting spot located in Kenner's Rivertown historic district which has a lot of interesting things to see and some really good places to eat.  I have been attempting to visit Porch and Patio Wine & Beer Garden for awhile ever since they opened.  My timing was always off when I was in this area on past visits so I was never able to be in Rivertown when they were actually open but just from seeing this business from the outside it definitely looked like a cool spot.   So I finally resolved to plan a specific visit and call to confirm they were open to make a visit.    When I finally arrive for my long overdue visit I was even more pleased with the location than I thought I would have been from just seeing it from the outside.  They have a really cool back parking area along with an amazing outside beer garden area which also has an awesome outdoor stage. They have a unique practice here of "branding" the buns on their burgers and their poboy bread which I haven't seen any other place do so that is a unique twist.    There was no host or table service so it was a seat yourself type of joint and then you went up to order at the bar and then you also refilled your own drinks (except for beer and booze... it should be refill your own beer though yeeeesssss).  On pondering the menu I decided to sample their burger for my first visit, although they did have quite an interesting selection of other items on their concise menu along with a good selection of daily specials.  The burger reminded me of The Company Burger except you could get it dressed with lettuce and tomato.  For condiments they were using the tiny little mustard packets instead of squeeze bottles which those little packets always make me grumpy (and during these pandemic times some places use the packets and others use squeeze bottles so you never know what you will get).  The only real hiccup in my experience was I ordered an iced tea but they hadn't made any yet so I had to wait a bit for them to make some.  It probably was a terrible idea to get iced tea anyway though as they have an impressive selection of draft beer on tap here and the bar is really cool along with having quite a few big screen TVs along the walls for folks to watch whatever.   Overall my burger was good and the French fries that came with it were perfectly fried and seasoned.  I found the price to be a little expensive considering the size of the burger but EVERYTHING seems to be getting expensive in these crazy times.  This is definitely a joint you want to visit for the great ambiance but check out their music schedule and visit during the live music as I imagine that would really kick up the awesomeness of this cool spot.  Currently during the pandemic situation they are still a great spot for live music, good food and socially distanced fun for folks to enjoy some good times both inside and outside with their really great outdoor stage that is hosting live music.  Check out my video review of Porch and Patio to get a better idea of the great aspects of this spot:  https://youtu.be/3zBV5f00nUI

The boiled and fried seafood here ranges between a three and four star experience.  This place is also famous for being the folks that bring you the soft shell crab po boy during Jazz Fest.  The ambiance is pretty plain and standard Metry dive joint with the service being friendly and attentive typically except when it gets really crowded which is often.  The thing that knocks many people for a loop here are the prices and it is expensive to eat here typically.  As an example during a recent lunch visit I got the seafood platter with a soft shell crab, seafood gumbo and iced tea which resulted in my bill being in the range of a fine dining experience.  That is quite a chunk of change compared to the prices at most other seafood joints in the city where you could've engaged in some substantial alcohol consumption before getting your tab anywhere near that.  Now I will say the seafood platter is plenty of food for at least two people to eat and many other places have kept their prices lower but greatly reduced the quantity of their food.  The one item that I'm really not a fan of here are their crawfish pies which are tiny little things without a lot of stuff inside. As a general rule you will often find a bit of sticker shock for many items here and can often get comparable food at better prices at many other places.    Overall the fried and boiled options are usually always done well and if you're willing to put up with the premium pricing and often crowded environment you can satisfy most of your seafood cravings here.  This is also about the only seafood option like this on Metairie Road and they have a lot of fans from the nearby neighborhoods.    My video review of The Galley is here:  https://youtu.be/di6QH5Pw3w4

This is a great cafe located inside the Lakefront Airport.  The ambiance is fantastic and both the airport itself and the cafe are visually stunning and beautiful to behold in Art Deco glory.  The diner part of the cafe is open weekdays (Tuesday to Friday) and for brunch on Saturday.  On Sundays the diner is usually closed and they move service into the more formal Walnut Room where they sometimes offer special buffets for holidays like Easter or just the menu for regular Sundays.  The Walnut Room also has the added benefit of giving you a good view of the runway so you can watch airplanes take off and land.  The food offers many New Orleans traditional foods with brunch, lunch or breakfast food with plenty of seafood options and everything I have had has been done well.    Overall this is a definite place to visit to also combine a good meal with a view of the wonderful airport interior.

The ferry is a very convenient way to travel as a pedestrian from the Eastbank to the Westbank or the opposite.  The ferry has also saved me many times when I've been working on the Westbank and the bridge gets shut down for some reason and it has allowed me to escape the Wank to get back home without waiting for hours on end of backed up traffic on the Expressway for the same $1 price as the toll on the bridge would be.  The main thing I don't like about the ferry is that it stops running relatively early (by NOLA standards) so you can make a run to happy hour in Algiers but you can't stay out very late at all or at midnight you will turn into a pumpkin and have to take an expensive taxi ride to return to the Eastbank.  There are a few nifty bars to see in Algiers and it can be a relaxing trip to take in the Mississippi River.  You get some great views of the area that are impossible to get any other way during the ride.  For the price (FREE for pedestrians and $1 for vehicles) it certainly is one of the best values of anything you can do in all of NOLA.

Small grocery with a deli serving quick and cheap po boys, burgers, sandwiches, crawfish pies, meat pies, chicken wings, chicken tenders, meat gumbo, red beans, seafood platters (no oysters), salads and their famous fries.  The crawfish pies are probably my favorite thing here and the fries are alright along with being a huge portion size.  This is a take out only place as there is no seating inside or outside.

A new restaurant inside of a gas station... humm so it seems we are going all country style in NOLA finally which is fine with me as good food in gas stations is a great thing.    This place usually gives you a large amount of food for a decent price.  The first time I went I had enough food for three meals but the second time it was enough for just one, albeit very large, meal.  The only complaint I would have is that they don't have fresh brewed iced tea and you only have the fountain drinks or bottle drink options.  I also wish they did offer the hot chili paste sauce most of the other Middle Eastern joints in town offer but currently they just have Sriracha.  Most people seem to get their food to go here so even though there are some tables here I've yet to seem them used.  If you aren't in the mood for Middle Eastern food they also offer a menu of more traditional American food items.      Overall I've been pretty happy with my food here so far and they give you a good portion size at a fair price along with being very generous on the condiments they top the food with.

This is a new place to me that opened up back during the beginning of the pandemic situation and they seem to have a lot of new wait staff.  I made two recent visits in two days as I enjoyed my first visit so much.  As you might expect from a business named The Gumbo Krewe they do have some good gumbo here and I had the seafood gumbo along with a nice trout filet that was one of their daily specials and on my next visit I tried some crawfish etouffee and a cheeseburger.  I generally enjoyed my meal and experience here along with having fun with the fact the building the restaurant is in has an interesting round shape with a side enclosed patio.  There are still some teething problems here as the bill didn't come out right as the prices in the system didn't accurately reflect the price posted on the menu for one of my visits and on another visit I was never given the lunch specials menu and I was upcharged for getting a different side item without being told there was going to be an upcharge.  They also have been having live music and they have happy hour specials every hour so this seems like it might be a fun spot to check out for some music and happy hour fun.    Overall this place is still very new to me so I look forward to learning more about it and so far other than the few hiccups mentioned I think this should turn out to be a nice spot to pass a good time with some good food.  My video review of The Gumbo Krewe is here:  https://youtu.be/Q2VTbhskMMg

The ambiance is pretty plain and standard Metry with the service being friendly and attentive typically except when it gets really crowded which is often.  The thing that knocks many people for a loop here are the prices and it is expensive to eat here typically. Now I will say the seafood platter is plenty of food for at least two people to eat and many other places have kept their prices lower but greatly reduced the quantity of their food.  As a general rule you will often find a bit of sticker shock for many items here and can often get comparable food at better prices at many other places. So I used the website to change my mailing address and they closed my account!  I went back to the website to check it out and links to change your address and close your account BOTH go to the same page!  In addition to fantastic website design they also have let a small hole on the corner down from my house grow into a much larger hole that has been growing for TWO YEARS now despite repeated requests by everybody on the block to repair it!  These clowns want to raise rates!  The only way to fix this circus is to fire all these clowns and privatize the whole affair like they have in Jefferson Parish.  They have been stealing all the money that was to be used for maintenance for years and now they want to go back and make us pay more to fix what they were supposed to have been fixing all these years.  Out with the whole board and bring in competent people!

This is the long awaited re-opening of this spot that has had several incarnations over the recent years so expectations have been running high from recent media stories about this restaurant.  On entry the staff were all super motivated, friendly and excited to the point of almost overkill.  You were greeted and spoken to by multiple people both coming and going into this joint.  The decor has also certainly been Miami Viced 80's dayglo decorated out to the max.  My friends used to love bringing their kids to the Warehouse Grill that was here previously but I don't think they will enjoy this new Flamingo joint as it seems more like a bar than a restaurant and I know their little girl is going to be heartbroken they took out the claw arcade game she loved to play.    My main focus in this review is the food and I really didn't enjoy my food experience here.  During the initial ordering process I was very disappointed when I found out the "Gulf Fish" on the menu was actually Basa (AKA Swai) which is a cheap imported Asian catfish which sadly many restaurants these days seem to be passing off as a local fish when it most certainly is not.  My friend got the fried shrimp plate and was informed the shrimp was locally sourced (but I have my doubts after the Basa/Swai bait and switch) and the shrimp were executed decently with acceptable flavor.  After my disappointment in the fish I just got a burger but that led to more sadness as my burger just seemed like it was made with a bland mass produced patty except any fast food joint would have tasted better than what I got.    They are still pretty new so maybe they will get in stride and improve things but from my experience this place just seems like a tourist trap slinging some low quality ingredients masked as things they are not.  The Basa/Swai is unacceptable in any local restaurant and the burger patty needs serious work and doesn't compare to most other local joints.

This is one of my absolute favorite days of the year.  It is a non-stop fun and insane time that goes and goes and goes.  I have more fun at this parade than any parades during Mardi Gras.  There are so many side parties and other things going on in addition to the main parade that it is just non-stop fun that goes on late into the night.  Besides my name is Shannon so the ladies have to kiss me with an Irish name like that.

This is one of the hardest po boy joints to get into in New Orleans as they have such short opening hours.  Their operating hours are only being open from 11am to 1pm Wednesday to Friday with seafood poboys ONLY on Friday, so you need to be really nearby during the work week to sample this place, and it has taken me quite awhile to finally be able to fit a visit in.  This is definitely a dive type atmosphere and has the bones of an old grocery store with a random assortment of shelves and coolers that have things in them and others that are empty or ancient.  The roast beef po boy certainly doesn't rank up with my top choices in the area.  The cheeseburger wasn't terrible and it also wasn't very impressive so maybe a bit under a McDonald's burger.  The shrimp po boy is ok and probably the best option on the menu.  Overall this place has plenty of old New Orleans character but they just are not in the top tier of po boy joints.  Tip: Bring cash as you need it to pay here AND sometimes they close early.

West Marine is a nationwide chain that has most of the things you need as relating to boats and associated marine needs.  They often have some good sales online and you can ship your items for free to their retail locatins.  If you need some equipment or outfitting for most things relating to boating activities on the water they likely have what you need here.

This is a nice little breakfast and lunch spot and usually they close too early for dinner.  They are famous for their roast beef po boy and burgers but they have a lot of other good things on the menu.  The roast beef is really just "ok" to me, as there are lots of other places I like better for that, and it is rated only for 1 napkin as it isn't the sloppy and gravy dripping joy I love in my roast beef po boys but the meat has a good flavor.  The burgers here are large but they don't seem to have a lot of flavor and the buns are a bit on the hard side and I don't think I would get another one.  They also have some awesome looking steaks here that I've yet to sample and I look forward to that.  Unfortunately any old school ambiance this place had got washed away, like so many things, in Katrina and they now have a modern looking interior.  They also have a series of large screen computer monitors/TVs for their menu that kind of give the place more of a fast food ambiance so I'm not sure if those things wouldn't be better repurposed as actual TVs to watch instead of being wasted as giant menus.     The only really big complaints I have about this joint are 1) that they don't do fresh brewed iced tea and they use that God-forsaken fountain style iced tea that is just plain crap.  I'm a pretty reasonable and patient man with most things but I've got little patience with places that don't take the time to brew proper iced tea!   2) the bathroom is sort of nasty and they frequently are out of paper towls. 3) related to #2 they dole napkins out like they are made out of gold!  They don't have napkins out for you to use and you can only get them issued to you from the staff.  The care they take with lots of their other food is evident and they have even started serving on actual plates so it belies my sensibilities that they wouldn't take the time to brew their own tea!  Most of the food here ranges from three to four stars but the iced tea issue is like a negative three star but we will just act on the assumption that they will be rectifying this issue ASAP as surely it has to be an oversight.

This is a decent place to grab some late night grub when on Frenchmen.  I've only had the sandwiches and nacho style tater tots along with a mighty fine tomato basil soup... I really like that tasty soup!  So it is more like a bar that serves food than a restaurant with a bar which is perfect for Frenchmen Street.  The servers often seem to be a bit surly and grumpy but I guess that is the vibe they're going for here.  I don't think I would like the service in this place very much sober but for late night grub it will do the trick.

This hotel offers a great price for the area which is quickly gentrifying.  It certainly is an older place and a bit beat up in some areas.  It was a pleasant stay and was good enough for what I needed it for.  The only negative is I did get some kind of bug bites that might have been bed bugs as they definitely were not like any mosquito bite I've had before.  These days bed bugs are a hard thing to control and even the nicest of hotels get them so a few bites was worth the small hassle for such a great value on a room when nearly everything else affordable was booked up.

The crawfish were very overcooked making them tough and rubbery along with having lots of head only bugs.  The shrimp were about $1 more per pound here than at my other regular spots while being smaller and less flavorful.  The crawfish pie was shameful with being filled with mostly rice and maybe 4 crawfish in the whole pie.    The other prepared food is probably a better bet than any of the boiled seafood.  Some of the prepared food actually did look pretty good and the shrimp pasta was looking quite tasty but after the other unpleasant things I experienced I wasn't in the mood to eat anything else here.  I won't be returning here for any boiled crawfish or shrimp and the crawfish pie should be renamed a rice pie.  For an added bonus somebody had totally had massive stomach issues and splattered the entire bathroom with their diarrhea so washing the hands after eating the substandard seafood was a no go.  Tip:  Exponentially better boiled seafood at Big Fisherman and Schaefer & Rusich.

This is a nice 24/7 convenience store/Middle Eastern restaurant.  Most of the food takes a bit of a unique Egyptian tilt and they do some things that are similar but a bit different than many of the other Middle Eastern options in the area.  They offer a bit of table service but not what I would consider full service.  They only have a few drink options you can order and then you can choose other drinks out of the convenience store coolers.  I tried the Egyptian green tea and it was ok but still tasted like regular tea to me.  Good option in the area for when other places are closed and you don't want that gross Krystal burger feeling the next day.

My recent lunch at Galatoire's was a fantastic experience as usual with good friends, good food and good people... Yet it was VERY concerning as the restaurant was deserted except for one other gent eating alone and our table of four.  The French Quarter was also quite deserted and there are still too many places boarded up and closed down.  Our economy can't survive like this and the epidemiological data no longer justifies such strict shut down measures as at this point medical necessity in no way justifies this current situation.  Our veteran waiter has been working at Galatoire's for longer than I have been alive and he had been hospitalized and nearly died from COVID-19 and he also needs and wants business to return to as nearly normal as possible!  Other tourist destinations around the country are having economic booms (Gatlinburg, Pigeon Forge, the beaches of Alabama and Florida along with many other spots). Even Jefferson Parish has more going on than the French Quarter at this point.    The politicians need to STOP playing the typical corrupt Louisiana political games and instead use data driven epidemiological practices.  The data clearly shows that it is quite safe for most folks to return to nearly normal while high risk folks can continue to take elevated precautions.  Just my informed opinion of course as somebody that has seen the rest of the world and also has graduate level epidemiology courses on my university transcript along with a lot of experience with analyzing population health data.   Galatoire's is one of the "must go to" places in New Orleans for classic food that hasn't changed in years.  You also must learn to listen to your waiter about what is good and if you go often (or know people that do) you will get to have a preferred waiter that will take very good care of you.  There are few things as important as having a good waiter at Galatoire's so take good care of one when you get one!!!  You must eat downstairs and preferably on a Friday for lunch.  I've always had a great time downstairs with excellent service and great food.  Upstairs I've had a great time and great service for private parties.  Eating upstairs with reservations I've had some very poor service and extreme attitude ONCE from a bad waiter (when he was tipped 15% instead of 20% for said poor service, and a sommelier that never showed up after repeated requests, the waiter threw a hissy fit until others at the table caved in and gave him his extra 5%).    I've had some fantastic dinners downstairs (my last visit I somehow didn't spend more than $50; even after drinking massive amounts of beer while with wine it can get much more pricey).  Generally the food is outstanding but sometimes it can be just good depending on many factors so it is important to ask your waiter what's good that day!!!    This is old line classic New Orleans food that isn't nouveau, trendy or quite to everybody's taste (especially if you have been on a diet of Applebee's or Tex Mex non-stop) but they have been doing what they have been doing for a long time so respect the tradition and have fun!  My video review of Galatorie's is here:  https://youtu.be/HU1fGpnObik

This is a cool neighborhood bar in the Sylvian Park area with a nice vibe that seems very popular in the area.  They have a decent menu of bar food here but so far I've only had drinks here.  There is a nice patio space to enjoy outside when the weather is nice and plenty of interesting spaces inside. They are adding additional locations and sadly I have seen formerly great places lose a lot of their local focus and go corporately cold when they do that so hopefully they maintain their "neighborly" focus and don't forget their local neighbors are what built their business. The female bartender that was working during my last visit (back in 2019 prior to all the worldwide insanity) was certainly not skilled in the art of customer service and seemed to be in a really bad mood so that did kill some of the otherwise nice vibe of this spot. This area has a few other drinking and eating establishments nearby so you can do a bit of a pub crawl with food tasting as you enjoy this nice neighborhood space.

It's OK food but seems a bit pricier than other sushi options around Uptown for dinner although I hear they have good lunch specials.  Most other sushi places Uptown give you a lagniappe snack when you sit at the sushi bar but not here.  It rarely seems to have a crowd so I'm not sure this place will last much longer than the other series of restaurants that preceded it.  Honestly I doubt I will be back as I like my old regular sushi places much more.

This is one of the coolest zoos anywhere!  My earliest memories of this place are back in the days when you could ride an elephant and camel here.  They don't offer animal rides anymore but they have some really great exhibits and many activities for both adults and children.  The white alligators have long been a noted animal exhibit here.  You can even feed some of the animals and the most fun to me are the giraffes. My overall favorite animal exhibit is probably the orangutans as they really like to put on a show and sometimes they even get t-shirts that they play with in all sorts of kooky ways.  This is also the location of Monkey Hill which is one of the highest points in the city.  There are many enjoyable places to relax in between viewing the animals and other exhibits and I've always liked the sea lion pool.   Since this is a zoo in New Orleans they have good food and drink here all the time but they also have numerous festivals and events that are held here with some of my favorites being Zoo-To-Do, Swamp Fest and Asian Fest.  Most locals with children get memberships which end up being a great value for frequent visits and good discounts on events.  The Audubon Nature Institute also has the Aquarium of the Americas and the Insectarium that are downtown but you shouldn't attempt to visit all of them on a single day as the zoo is so large.  Since I only got to ride a one hump camel as a kid here I'm still anxious to ride a two hump version one day!

I've been to many private events here that have been enjoyable and I've also generally enjoyed lunch and dinner here.  I personally enjoy what some people call the "old fashioned" style of food here.  I'm not the biggest fan of breakfast and I don't really like bananas so those factors reduce the full enjoyment of the charms this place offers.  I do like some brunch items far more than "standard" breakfast fare and New Orleans breakfast items are usually much better to me than what exists in the rest of America; so brunch is far more acceptable than breakfast to me and I do love some good grillades.    I'm disappointed in how much they have allowed the dress code to slide in this establishment and unfortunately that seems to be a trend in too many places.  There are many other places that I enjoy brunch at more but Brennan's is an experience that is fun occasionally (but probably the most expensive experience of any brunch in NOLA).  I think lunch is probably the best value and a good way to experience some of what Brennan's has to offer.

I've eaten and purchased wine at Martin's for years.  I'm still sad they haven't reopened the deli Uptown again since Katrina but I still go  to the Metairie location often to eat.  They usually have multiple specials for lunch everyday.  Over many years I think there was only one special I didn't like and it was due to just a bad and tough piece of meat that was a fluke. I have to say I did an experiment with eating the "Healthy" lunch option for 3 months and I actually gained weight so it is healthy in a New Orleans dining sense but not for the size of the belly :)  They always have a great selection of wine, beer, and liquor with some very knowledgeable people to assist you.  They have an amazing deli counter with all sorts of tasty looking desserts and food choices.  They also have an entirely separate deli counter for a selection of some great cheeses.  They also have a great sandwich and salad selection.  Martin's also has pretty good & large burger that they fresh grind (so expect to wait at least 20 minutes for it) and they usually have a different daily burger special during lunch.  I also enjoy the Sunday brunch here with the only complaint that I've heard is that they usually don't have bloody Mary's.    The Metairie location has a decent size parking lot but it fills up fast around lunch.  On really crowded days it can be hard to find a place to sit and they sometimes run out of silverware so there can be a bit of a wait.  The best bet is to get there before the noon rush so you can enjoy yourself.

It is a really large and old oak tree that hosts weddings, picnics and just goofing around (not to be confused with the Dueling Oak in City Park).  It was here long before any of us were and will probably outlast all of us and maybe the next few generations after.  As a good strong and wise oak it would make all the ancient and modern Druids proud.  Respect the oak and do not break or otherwise harm the oak or despoil it with graffiti or the curse of the Druids will be upon thee and if I catch you doing it you will be wearing a wig of Spanish moss for awhile as this tree is under my protection and I will call you out for a visit to the Dueling Oak in City Park.

This is a cool little boutique bar with a German beer garden theme.  I really like the beer selection here and they have lots of German beers not easily found elsewhere.  They give a discount here to Deautches Haus members so that is really awesome.  They usually don't have a big crowd of folks here but they usually have a very friendly group of people here that will certainly make for an enjoyable visit.

This is a good dive type NOLA dining joint with LOTS of choices.  They have a rotating selection of multiple daily specials along with a good selection of sandwiches, po boys, entrees, salads, pizza, and fried chicken.  They have so many things to choose from that you're probably going to be able to find something to for even the most picky of eaters.  The food isn't great but it is certainly good and a good value.  You have to order and pick your food up at the counter and they don't provide any service, other than busing your table, but they still want tips so I'm always amazed by the ever expanding demand for tips when no service is provided.    I know the usage of the English language is constantly degrading and our education levels continue to decline but let's just quickly review a definition:  Tip:  A sum of money given to someone as a way of rewarding them for their services.  I love to tip for service and I think it is an insult to the hard working service industry folks that actually work for tips and EARN them by providing service for non-service providing staff to demand similar tips for doing NONE of the serving work and providing no service.  Overall this is definitely a decent spot to grab a quick meal in a classic dive type atmosphere.

This is a great bar for private events and live music.  The place is split into two long and narrow rooms with one half being the main bar area that has a cool ceiling shaped like a guitar and the other room being the stage area for viewing music.  I'm friends with the owners of this place and they generally keep things running pretty well here.  The main thing that gives me the "blues" about this juke joint is that some of the bartenders here are sometimes not my favorite as they seem unable to handle large crowds well and can be painfully slow while they also have some other bartenders that just seem to always be slow.  If it wasn't for the inconsistent to occasionally poor service this would be a four start joint.  They are still a pretty new establishment so they are still breaking in the staff so with time I would expect the service to improve.    I would come here more often except for its location, as I don't hang out in the Warehouse District that much, and parking is never easy in the area.  If you're looking to book a private party or event this is certainly a nice venue to check out.  As far as just hanging out here as a bar it is usually more fun on nights when they have a good band and they generally keep a pretty full music schedule.  One area where this bar seems to really excel is that they probably have some of the best and most spacious bathrooms I've ever seen in the area bars so that should be good news for all the ladies.

This is an "ok" Mid-City bar but it probably has the least personality of any bar in Mid-City (so far) as it is still very new.  I really liked the Dixie Tavern that was here previously a lot more.  This place attracts a lot of smokers and it is probably one of the smokiest places to go in Mid-City other than the Banks Street Bar.  I'm not a smoker so the often smokey nature of this place tends to make it much less appealing to me.They also don't have a kitchen here and will only occasionally bring food in for events like Saints games.  I've popped in and out of here several times but I just haven't found a "vibe" to it that would make it a part of my regular rotation.  As this place continues to develop it might find its "soul" as it gets more integrated into the neighborhood and starts to establish its traditions and gain fame for its unique characteristics.

They make a mean burger with some good onion rings and ok fries.  The burger is on the larger side and has some juicy deliciousness but sadly I've yet to have an opportunity to try their pizza but I reckon it will happen one day when I least expect it.  They also feature some changing specials I've also neglected to sample thus far as I'm usually opting for the burger.  The trend of duck fat, goose fat and poutine fries has really kicked up the fry competition in NOLA so the fries here might need to kick it up a bit.  They have a bit more of a selection than your typical bar grub fare so you might want to check it out.

This is a nice little coffee and deli space inside the Zeitgeist movie space that also has a hair salon upstairs.  They have been expanding their selection from some simple items like pastries and donuts to more lunch sandwich options.  There is a great deal of space inside to hang out or get work done and it is actually a comfortable spot that also provides plenty of meter free parking in the area.

Parkview Tavern (NOT to be confused with Parkway Bakery & Tavern) is a dive bar I've only been to three times, so far, but I've always had a good time.  I went once to meet a group of friends and one of them won a nice chunk of change on video poker so that resulted in some free drinks.  I also came here twice to recharge my beer meter during the Voodoo Fest.  There is usually a decent small crowd in here and the space has a unique "hand built" quality about it.  The drinks are pretty cheap and there are lots of TV's all over the place.  The biggest issue with this place is EVERYBODY seems to be smoking so even with the doors open it can be pretty irritating in here.  They do have a nice patio area outside that is comfortable to enjoy when the weather is nice.

This is mostly a tourist destination but it is well located in the Quarter.  The food is decent but there are far better places to eat.  I actually watched the Saints win the Super Bowl in this establishment with a large group so that was a memorable experience.  This does make for a decent sports bar as they have many televisions and have a lot of sports memorabilia on display.  This probably wouldn't ever be my first choice but its overall a decent place.

This is a good Greek restaurant with a Cajun/Creole flair.  They have fried seafood, gumbo and Mediterranean food.  The service is friendly and generally efficient.  the ambiance is decent except for the choice of programming on the TV which on my last visit was one of those appalling who's yo daddy DNA test shows.  They have some good sandwiches and gyros and quite nice salads.  Nice casual lunch spot but I've never been for dinner so I'm not sure if they change anything up.

This would probably be the most dive Indian restaurant I've ever been too, except for the fact that I've been eating their food from way back when they were downtown on Canal St., in a much better spot (in an interesting upstairs place that is now some kind of Asian wanky massage joint).  They probably used to have one of the best Indian buffets in the area with more choices on their special weekend buffets than anybody else (fish, lamb, and chicken dishes) and you still get to use their great huge metal plates to feast on.  The buffet now is a bit more inconsistent and they can be a bit unclear as to when they will be open to offer the super buffet on the weekends but they usually offer a weekday lunch buffet that consists mainly of chicken and vegetable dishes.      It appears to be run by one family and they seem like very nice people and they make good food (but maybe they aren't the best business people or had some sort of tragic financial or medical situation to have had to move to this way low rent location where you might feel a bit scared to exit your car).  It certainly does look run down inside (outside is apocalyptic) and during weekday lunch I've sometimes been the only person in there (so they certainly could use some more business).    I feel pretty bad for these people as I've seen how much they have had to downsize their business (for whatever reasons) but I think these folks are certainly capable of producing 4 to 5 star food they just need to get more people in the door and find a better location.  I was so sad when they left the Canal location but I was so happy to find them again so I certainly think it is worth trying out.

This is a shotgun single converted into a long bar with some outdoor seating located right next to the LSU/VA medical complex that swallowed up the old neighborhoods.  Most of the food is centered around burgers here but they also have a fish sandwich, sliders, vegetarian burger and offer breakfast.  They also feature a nice happy hour from 4-7 with half off wine and beer.  The burgers and fries here are decent and the service is typically fast and even better if you sit at the bar instead of a table.  It certainly isn't the best burger in town, especially for the price, but the happy hour is a good deal and it's a place you can watch football in Mid-City and still get a bar stool most of the time during games.

They violated all principles of Southern decency by being out of iced tea at lunch so i drank water with she crab soup $9 and curried goat $13 with my bill total being $27.80 so it seems i still got charged for my missing iced tea anyway. The soup was good while the goat was tough with little flavor so it comes nowhere close to the great curried goat my Vietnamese friends make. This is a nice facility as part of the Southern Food & Beverage Museum but at those prices I'm going for better food, better service and 25 cent martinis at Commander's Palace for weekday lunch.

Bayou St. John includes beautiful scenery from Lake Pontchartrain down to the "secret swing" to Holy Trinity Greek Orthodox Church (that is home to Greek Fest) going past City Park and the Fairgrounds way down to the current endpoint at Parkway Bakery.  There are festivals, kayaking, fishing, volleyball and all sorts of other activities constantly going on next to this body of water.  The biggest gem of the area are the many vibrant neighborhoods that flank the Bayou extending from Lakeview into Mid-City and give this area its uniquely New Orleans character.

They have "Ghetto Punch" (AKA Red Drank) what more can you ask?  17 flavors of wings, crab cakes, chicken tenders, fish strips and crawfish balls.  Where else in the world but New Orleans would you find such a place?  Let me tell ya:  NOWHERE!  Go Ghetto on the Wank and go to Wing Snack Express!

This place has improved steadily since their initial opening challenges.  They were one of the few options open on Mardi Gras day and seem to be working hard to run a good business.  They have a decent selection of items on the menu while the service is usually in the range of acceptable to very slow so they could be faster on refilling drinks.  Overall this is usually a decent place to grab some affordable Vietnamese food in the area.

The main claim to fame for this bar is their huge chair that seems to be the obligatory photo magnet.  The bar itself is nice but like many hotel bars it is quite overpriced.  I've never seen more than a handful of people in this bar and I usually walk past it without bothering to go in but when I have folks from out of town I will bring them here to get their big chair picture taken.

They have a discount cash price which makes a lot of the seafood a good value here.  The crawfish is usually the best thing here while the boiled shrimp isn't my favorite.  I still prefer the Big Fisherman on Magazine but if you find yourself in Bucktown this is a good spot to grab some mudbugs.

Great burger joint with an even greater and actually pretty awesome beer garden.  Our server was super friendly and seemed to be just having a fun time at work.  All of the staff seemed to be really happy and enjoying their day.  The only thing that was a bit confusing to me on their menu is that they only offered some of their beers in the full liter and when I asked the server there still just didn't seem to be any good explanation of why that was the case.  This might be my favorite outdoor spot in this area of Nashville.

I'm not a coffee shop person but I really liked using this place for their WiFi.  It was cash only which was a pain but I usually would only get an iced tea or sometimes an oatmeal cookie.  This place was near my house so it was great to have meetings with people who might not understand our NOLA ways of doing things in bars during work hours.  I do miss this place a bit as it was a good working environment with very convenient electrical plugs but many of the area neighbors are happy that its gone as they really didn't like the dirty hipsters that this place attracted.  My life has been made much more inconvenient without the easy access this place once provided.

Its about the only Western wear place on the Eastbank and they have a decent selection of boots.  They have quite a few shirts, jackets and jeans but on a recent visit I just couldn't find any shirts that really appealed to me.  The store seems to be about half men's and maybe a bit over half women's items.  Some of the prices seemed a bit expensive but many of the items are made in the U.S.A.

For my 1400th review I want to highlight this great neighborhood dive bar; so before I begin let's be clear that I don't want you complaining/progressive/whiny/PC/reformer etc. carpetbaggers looking to over regulate and redefine my city reading this review and invading this space so just stop now...  Yeah I'm talking to you so If you don't like go cups, 24/7 bar hours or music leave now!  This is probably my favorite bar in the Bywater as its still an authentic New Orleans bar without any pretentious hipster crap like a lot of the other area bars and restaurants are transforming into.  The drink prices are reasonable and haven't upsurged insanely like some of the "gentrification" businesses catering mainly to tourists that also love to rip off recent transplant locals.  I'm fine with fixing things up and making them nice but not at the expense of losing our local culture along with having to pay insanely inflated prices.    Tip:  Quick equation to determine if you're paying fair price.  When one beer costs nearly as much as an entire six pack of that beer that's insanely inflated and a total rip off place!

The BBQ definitely isn't the best I've ever had but the people working here were really great.  I stopped in here after a long day of fishing to grab some brisket and they were really nice folks.  The brisket was more on the lean and tough side while the sauce here was very sweet.  I might suggest going for the burger over the brisket here.

I'm afraid I find this statue of Ignatius a pale reflection of the character depicted in a Confederacy of Dunces especially as it seems to be in his earlier wardrobe.  New Orleans being the place that it is I think we deserve the more flamboyant Ignatius depicted towards the end of the story when he is bedecked out in his pirate attire!  Imagine the glory of a statue of Ignatius astride/beside his Paradise hot dog cart with his pirate sword held high!  Such a sight could compete with General Jackson's statue in Jackson Square and assuredly deserves an honored spot somewhere along the madness on Bourbon Street.  Perhaps a grand huge entry arch at Canal and Bourbon with the statue crowning it?  Something even grander like the Arc de Triomphe in Paris perhaps?  As our main business in NOLA is the tourism business we certainly need more grand landmarks for the tourists to ogle so let's get busy!

The prices at Mr. Gyro's are really high for what you get here.  The only reason to eat at this establishment is just for a gyro as the entree prices are just not a good value.  I much prefer Acropolis or Byblos Market, as the food and prices are both much better.  Mr. Gyros does do decent potato wedges but a lunch entree and iced tea will probably cost around $18 so for this type of food Acropolis is really a better value and better food.  If all you want is a gyro this is a decent place to grab one but beyond that I would suggest elsewhere.

$5.22 for one Abita Amber!!! Seriously that's almost a 6 pack across the street at Breaux Mart!  I can buy a keg of Abita Amber and the serving cost is around 85 cents for a large solo cup that holds more than the Bulldog pints so I would expect a bar could get a quantity discount for even less.  The price gouging corporate demon anti-NOLA culture to the MAX has fully taken over with that!!!    This is no longer a locals bar and now is firmly entrenched as a tourist establishment of ill repute that especially caters to Tulane students from the Northeast that are nostalgic about paying New York City prices in the Bulldog.  They need to open a bead and t-shirt shop next door as they Bourbon Street it up on this section of Magazine...  Bulldog ownership has totally lost the fact that volume is where you make profits and I'm certainly not drinking volumes of anything at their current prices where back when Abita Amber was just $4 a pint I would drink many on a daily basis here as I used to enjoy this bar.  They have completely driven off all their regulars here and all the staff that worked here for many years is gone.  This bar is dead to me now.  Abita Amber prices at other area bars:  $2 PITCHERS Reginelli's Pizza Monday, Tuesday and other announced times.  $4 Rendezvous Tavern ($2.50 on Wednesdays)  $4 Balcony Bar (cheaper for announced specials)  $3 Ms. Mae's  $2.75 Brothers Three  $5 New York Pizza for a slice of pizza AND an Abita Amber  Bourbon Cowboy 3 for 1 special works out to about $2.50 per beer for Abita Amber.

The outside of this place looks nice and the inside seems like more of a market with a butcher area and prepared food area.  The order area for prepared food is a bit of a strange setup and just a series of glass panels looking into the kitchen area with chalkboards listing the options.  I was unhappy they didn't have any iced tea but they did list Arabic tea as an option (I like my stuff unsweet and that stuff is way sweet).  The lamb I had wasn't the best but it was ok and the salad, hummus, and rice were all very good.  The salad had some really fresh tasting cucumbers, green peppers, and tomatoes in it.  They have a dining area in the back but they didn't have hot pepper sauce like they do at Byblos Market.  The guy working the front counter seemed very nice and laid back.  With a few minor changes this could be a much better place easily on par with Byblos Market.  I was the only customer in the place while I was there for lunch so it is certainly very quiet here.  The food might encourage me to get something to go here but currently I much prefer the environment at Byblos Market if I'm remaining to dine in an establishment like this.

This used to be where the locals went to enjoy live local music but the tourists have definitely found out about it so it often is majority tourists and hipster transplants around here.  There are still some decent venues with good drink prices but many places have certainly started charging tourist prices.  The quality of the music has also gotten a lot more variable so while you can still see some great shows there are also a fair number of mediocre ones.  Generally Frenchmen is better than Bourbon Street as it definitely smells better as the urine, vomit and horse poop are typically not present but you still have to deal with the body odor stench of the gutter punks and hipsters.  This is also the place to be during Halloween to see the freak show of costumes that will be out en masse.  I liked this area a lot more before the hipsters and tourists took it over.  Make sure to wear pleated khakis with a tucked in polo shirt like a local and the transplant hipsters will take it as a personal affront which is awesome to see their angst.

This is the closest gas station to my house and it has a great location at the intersection of Washington and Magazine.  They always seem to have the cheapest gas prices of anyplace in the Garden District / Irish Channel / Uptown area.  This store also assists me to look forward to achieving my life long goal of winning 100 million dollars as I frequently purchase my lottery tickets here. This place is also open 24/7 so it certainly puts the convenience in convenience store.  Maybe I will even purchase it one day soon when I get my winning ticket.

Seems to be a small family run establishment and the experience started out well enough.  The first disappointment was small portion sizes compared to other area Middle Eastern restaurants.  Second disappointment is that it just seems service totally disappeared and a drink refill never happened which as there were no other customers in the place just isn't acceptable.

The menu is a bit confusing as it isn't the best organized and be aware that most of it is in Spanish so you will need some time to translate it with Google or have a working knowledge of some Spanish food terms if you're not fluent.  The service is inconsistent and while friendly could be more attentive to details.  The food is decent and they have nice freshly made tortillas.  The prices for several items seem higher than the nearby Taqueria Guerrero.  They have a breakfast menu that could appeal to those who like indulging in that meal with a Latin flair.  Overall I would generally prefer Taqueria Guerrero except the fresh tortillas here are some of the best around.

This is probably the most affordable place to eat among all the new places that have opened on Freret St. and they have been there longer than most of the others.  They have many tasty options that are all very reasonably priced.  The only slight complaint I have about this place is along with the free chips you get some "queso" that tastes like the velveta cheese you get on Superdome nachos more than any real queso I've had (so they might do better just switching to salsa but it is free so you can't complain too much).  They also were having a half price drink special the last night I ate there so that was a GREAT deal for a Friday night.    Their tacos are all around $3, depending on the meat selection, and you then get to add additional toppings of your choice.  At my last dinner I selected a chicken taco, shrimp taco, and fish taco (they use flounder for their fish tacos) and I was quite satisfied with the portion size (with the chicken being exceptionally generous on the toppings).  They also offer "bowls" of various combinations of taco ingredients sans tortillas and then a few additional entrees with the most enticing to me being a steak.  This is certainly not the best Mexican type food I've had (and I'm not the biggest fan of this type of food) but I would definitely go here before Superior Grill, Nacho Mama's, Taqueria Corona, Maya's, Baru, Rum House, or Felipe's.  Overall a fantastic value for some good simple food with some great drink specials.

Crazy Johnnie's has some nice filet mignon and prime rib po boys for lunch and always good steaks.  They really offer a lot of value for what you get.    The only "beef" I have with them is that I would say they have absolutely GROSS iced tea (that I was told comes out of a fountain like Coke)!!! Seriously I think they could take the time to brew some iced tea, as it isn't rocket science, so the best bet is to stick to drinking beer.  The crazy potatoes are some very good examples of how to do some  tasty things with potatoes.  I'm also a big fan of their steak sauce and have been known to even put it on my crazy potatoes.  They also offer some good seafood and chicken options.  The gumbo and bbq shrimp are very nice things to start your meal with.  You generally get very good service and the food seems to always come out quick.  I prefer lunch to  dinner here and it is usually a great place to grab a quick and tasty lunch during the week.

This spot has some good Mediterranean food along with some great happy hour and other drink specials. The same folks that own Pizza Perfect next door to this place also own Kay Bob's Grill & Ale so you can get the food from both Pizza Perfect and Kay Bob's in both spots along with their drink specials. They have awesome daily happy hour specials and on Saturday when I last visited it was "Happy Hour all day featuring 2-for-1 pints ($6 minimum) and pitchers" and I had some really great craft beers at a fantastic value!!!  The food I would rate more at three stars as the quantity was rather sparse but the drink specials and awesome staff nailed down a four star for them.  The staff were really friendly and our waitress provided excellent service along with being super perky and totally on top of things.  This was a great experience and location with prices that made it a great value which make this a really great fun spot to eat, drink and make merry.

This place has ok food and ok pho but probably the most bland and unremarkable pho I've had anywhere.  I've been once and I probably won't ever go again as there are so many better options.  As a last resort if you need some pho and can't escape the river bend this will be your only option.

My least favorite Vietnamese place in the NOLA area so far.  They didn't bother to bring me my vegetable plate to go with my pho and they only had selections of beef pho with no chicken, seafood, or other options.  I've also heard this place is also a national chain so that seems a bit strange to me also.  They do take credit cards with a posted minimum of $10 but they allowed me to charge my $8 pho with no problems.  The service seemed a bit confused as there were two ladies that just served everybody haphazardly and then a guy from the back brought your food out to you so in all that chaos it is no wonder they forget my veggie plate.  The beef pho I had was good I just prefer other places with better ambiance, service, and more choices.

This place is a very traditional meat and three Southern cooking joint.  So far out of my Nashville experiences with meat and three joints this one is probably on the bottom of my list as I have enjoyed the food at most of the rest a bit more so far.  All of the establishments I've had the pleasure of experiencing thus far have been most worthy of a visit and Dandgure's is no different as you should definitely pay a visit here and experience it as they do some good food.  My challenge is that Dandgure's is so near Arnold's that I just have to generally give Arnold's the win as that establishment is just FANTASTIC and a definite cut above Dandgure's to my taste.  When the line is too long at Arnold's and I have to get lunch done in a hurry Dandgure's is a reliable backup plan.  Actually I would say Dandgure's is a much more traditional Southern style of cooking in many ways than Arnold's from my experiences growing up and travelling along with eating across all of Dixie for most of my life but personally I just prefer what I find is the "upgraded" experience of Arnold's most of the time but your taste might vary.  Overall these folks WIN at being the MOST friendly and sociable of any of the meat and three joints which is a hard contest in itself as most all of the joints have very nice folks so make sure to stop in and say hello and enjoy a good meal.

This is a decent Vietnamese restaurant that also offers some Chinese dishes.  Typically I get the chicken pho here and it is usually brought out nearly immediately after ordering it in a very large bowl.  You get probably one of the largest servings of pho here of anywhere else in the New Orleans area but you also get charged more than many of the other places that offer pho.  They also have a $15 minimum credit card charge that is inconsistently applied.  I've had it usually not applied during lunch but they get a bit belligerent about it at dinner.

This is a really nice park that has multiple attractions to lend in addition to its natural beauty.  There is a nice running track that meanders around the edge and at certain points along the track it has different workout stations with things like pull up bars.  There are tennis courts and equestrian stables.  There is also a golf course along with a well appointed club house that is open to the public.  The club house has a decent restaurant and it frequently hosts wedding receptions as does the Audubon Tea Room.   The park also encompasses the zoo and the "Fly" which runs along the Mississippi River and has athletic fields which are mainly used for baseball and soccer.  Besides the wildlife in the zoo there is the occasional alligator reported in the main lagoon along with lots of birds in the park and the most psychotically rabid squirrels I've ever seen anywhere... seriously these squirrels attack each other viciously and I've seen one bite the tail off another one.  There is definitely a lot to do and see in this park and it is a great place to enjoy some outdoor space.

Carreta's Grill is a small local chain with two other locations on the North Shore.  This place is often a madhouse during weekday lunch hours and is often crowded to capacity.  They have a decent menu selection and some good combos that let you sample many of their offerings.  Their enchiladas actually have some sauces with distinctive flavors so those are a good choice.  They really excel here with keeping you well supplied with complimentary chips and salsa for your entire visit.  Its a decently average TexMex place where you get what you pay for and will definitely not leave hungry.

AJ&J Asian Bistro has a bit of a long name for a restaurant but they have done some nice work sprucing this space up.  The food theme seems to focus on a mix of Thai and sushi with a dash of Chinese.  This is a really affordable lunch spot and they have some good deals.  I had the pad Thai that came with the chicken hot and sour soup.  The hot and sour soup isn't as good as other places I've had it but for the combo of the soup and entree it was far cheaper than anywhere else.  Dinner gets more expensive so you might want to cut your teeth at lunch to discover what you like here.

The coconut cream flavor I got was good but the ice is more gritty and chunky than Hansen's but less so than Sal's.  There aren't many other options in this particular area of Metairie to get an icy treat and the prices are significantly cheaper than what you will find in the city.  The line was one person in front of me and about three people arrived behind me with service time taking only a matter of seconds.  They also are heavy on the syrup pour if you like that.  They have a selection of other treats and quite a substantial parking lot.  They have cream flavors here and the ice and flavor selection here seems better than Sal's.  Like most snowball stands this one is cash only.

Great little halal market with various Middle Eastern groceries and an even better butcher and baker.  They offer fresh meats and breads that are all of great quality.  The fresh produce selection is a bit concise and isn't the main star here but they have a good selection of other needed grocery items and assorted dry goods.  This spot is also right next to Sahara Cafe so you can eat a nice meal and then make some Middle Eastern groceries after.

I've consistently heard that dinner here is fantastic but very overpriced and not really worth it when compared to other spots in town.  My experience at lunch was similar except that the food was just good and not fantastic.  I had high expectations but the lunch menu seemed rather limited on choices when compared to other fine dining restaurants in the area.  They really fell short here in the service department.  I was offered no sherry with my turtle soup and getting my iced tea refilled was really inconsistent.  I was especially displeased when my empty glass of iced tea was taken away and I was left with only water prior to my dessert course even arriving and was never asked if I wanted coffee.  I'm not sure if it is a training issue or what but the staff here all seem very overly obsessed with commenting about their house filtered iced water and they were so focused with asking if I wanted more house filtered water every time they were around they really forgot to take care of my iced tea and other service needs.  If the restaurant had been crowded I might have been more understanding but there were only a handful of tables when we arrived and only a few more as we left.  I had turtle soup (which was quite overpriced at $10), Gulf Fish and then the best part of the meal the chocolate cake for dessert.  Of course no inquiry was made if I wanted coffee with my dessert.  For the price, clumsy service and overall experience I just don't think I would return for lunch.  I would definitely consider returning for dinner as it is a nice space but probably only if somebody else was buying.    There are certainly aspects of this place I like but they really need to get the service aspect better organized as I really would have had a much better time and far more enjoyable meal by just turning the other direction on Bienville Street and going to Arnaud's instead.

It is pretty much like all the other Trader Joe's I've been to and while none of them really are my favorite places to make groceries they are ok for some things.  I find this to be a place with lots of snacky foods and a limited selection focused on their rotating seasonal items.  The wine and cheese can be a good value here and you can find some unique items but for general making groceries I find this place a bit limited and will prefer one of our local groceries or even Whole Foods for a wider selection of needed items.

I've probably had the most consistently good experience here of any other FedEx in the area.  They have a large parking lot in this strip mall complex that makes parking easy and unlike most of their other locations it also is free of city parking fees.  They have staff that are generally knowledgeable and helpful with getting your projects completed on time and on budget.  This is my preferred FedEx location in Orleans Parish and when attempting to use any of their other NOLA locations I've often regretted it.

This is probably the oldest Spanish tapas restaurant in New Orleans and they have been around long enough to know what they're doing.  I really like Lola's and they have some great food here.  I also really LOVE garlic and they make some great aioli here!  They offer their sangria in your choice of both a white AND a red so you can satisfy the most discerning wino.   The tapas and the entrees here are all excellent and they really excel with their soups and stews.  Their garlic soup isn't as good to me as the one at Barcelona Tapas but it is a close second.
