Their paella seems to be one of the weaker items on the menu for consistency as when it is good it is very good but when it is off it isn't so good so I usually opt for something else.  The restaurant itself is a bit small and crowded but somehow that just adds to the ambiance and it just occasionally makes you forget you're not in Spain as you enjoy your meal.  The prices are a bit high for what you get and the parking can sometimes be inconvenient but I've always enjoyed myself when dining here.

This is a cool bar with a nice beer selection with the 24 drafts on tap all coming out of the side of a Jeep Grand Wagoneer.  The service was efficient and friendly.  The crowd was pleasantly boisterous and everybody seemed to be having a great time.  They had a pretty nice looking menu and all the food I saw come out looked quite appetizing but I didn't get to eat as I had already had dinner (I ate at the nearby The Tavern which had 2 for 1 drinks that night and the bartender there had told me about this new spot that would be happening after they closed).  This is definitely one of the popular and fun spots in the Midtown area that you should visit.

I've only been here once for dinner and it was with the decided intent of sampling their "infamous" Elizabeth's Dream Burger, that usually comes topped with lots praline bacon (I don't like bacon so I ordered it without it).  My burger came and it was a very large thing and had plenty of praline bacon on it even though I had specifically requested it without it.  I was able to easily remove the offending bacon and fed it to my hungry dining companion who enjoyed it thoroughly.  My burger, on the other hand, I found to more than adequate on the size scale but definitely lacked in the flavor scale.  It was such a disappointing experience to have my burger dream shattered I've never been back but I've heard good things about their brunch.  If they were not way far away from my headquarters in the Garden District I might decide to make a run out there for brunch one day but my shattered dreams still make me reluctant :(  WARNING: there is one of those horrible and evil speed cameras right next to Elizabeth's!!!! I just got the "good" news in the mail... Greedy Bastards stealing my lunch money again!!!

Pretty interesting location for an ice cream joint and the ice cream is pretty good too.  They have some interesting flavors here and are happy to let you sample taste them.  The price was a bit on the expensive side for the quantity you get.  Parking was a bit of a challenge as this is a very popular area but a few blocks away street parking was eventually discovered.

The pizza here is very old school and traditional style.  The crust was very good but the flavor of the toppings left a great deal to be desired.  I had the margherita pizza and I found it to be very slack in the basil area.  I would have to say that this was one of the blandest pizza's I've EVER had but the crust was fantastic so that it evens out to about a 3 star pizza.  Pizza Delicious makes a far more fantastic and VERY flavorful margherita so I would greatly suggest that one over the version at Ancora.  The service was acceptable and my pizza came out very fast.  Ancora also makes all their cured meats in house but they seem to focus only on the pig to the exclusion of all other meats.  The price for their one available (and small) single serving size of pizza is way too much for what it is.  I would be willing to pay around $5 (like at happy hour at Domenica for very similar pizza) for this size and type of pizza and certainly not the $13 price.  I probably won't be returning here as I find it extremely over priced for the very simple, basic, and cheap food that it is along with the bland toppings (at least for the margherita).

This is probably the most fantastic fitness center anywhere in the state.  They have a huge array of equipment, swimming pools and a large schedule of classes along with several bars.  They have programs for all ages and abilities.  I've visited this place many times and I'm a fan but it is waaay to far out in the suburbs for me to ever consider joining it.   Maybe one day they will open a branch somewhere Uptown...

I finally made it here for lunch on a Friday and got the Squid-ink Cavatelli with tuna, cherry tomatoes, lemon, scallions, garlic & chili.  My lunch started well with the waiter bringing me some bread and herb infused olive oil with a few olives added for extra flavor.  When my pasta arrived it looked pretty but it, unfortunately, tasted very bland and it was the smallest serving of pasta I've ever had ANYWHERE.  The service was excellent (no reason for it not to be as there were only two other tables other than myself).  They did give me a menu for an upcoming special dinner that looked fantastic so I hope this establishment really does offer up more than I experienced on my initial visit (not to mention it left me still quite hungry and in need of a second lunch).  I would give the pasta I had for lunch two stars and the service and ambiance about a 3.5 but if the special dinner menu tasted as good as it sounded then this place could certainly be worthy of a higher ranking.

I like the fact they are all about organic and that you get lots of topping choices.  I thought the bun quality was good and they do give you a pretty hefty slab of meat on your burger.  Unfortunately steam cooking pretty much drains all flavor from the meat and ruins what could be a great piece of meat.  When I visited the place was nearly deserted so it looks like their initial crowd of visitors has spread the word that the food here just lacks the crucial element of flavor.  I was also a bit peeved that for a place that touts its healthy and organic options they didn't offer fresh lemon wedges for my iced tea and only had plastic packets of lemon juice.    This place really needs to install a grill ASAP to cook the meat in a way that will lock in the flavor.  For the premium price of $14.15 that I paid for my burger, cole slaw, and drink I really could have had a much better burger in a much nicer restaurant so I really expect a lot more.  All of my friends that have eaten here along with with 100% of their kids have also reported extreme displeasure with the price and taste of the food here and that they would never return.  Steamed burgers are good at Krystal but just don't work for the size of burger they do here.  Unless this place gets a grill I'm afraid it won't last long.  Poor value and poor flavor combined give me no motivation to ever return.

This is just an old school diner that has remained virtually unchanged since 1946; which is great because they don't need to change anything.  The only bad aspect of Camellia is that there is often a line to get in and sometimes that line doesn't move nearly fast enough, as you have to watch other people eat and smell the good food!  They serve up some classic burgers, desserts, and a good selection of tasty sandwiches.  I'm not a breakfast person but you certainly can get that stuff here too.  I've usually eaten here for the night time / early morning time and it really hits the spot around then.  The burger is comparable to those that they want to charge way more for at the newer places on Oak and Freret but you get a lot more food options here with a burger that really tastes better.

I used to work across the street from here and ate lunch here pretty often and I'm a bit sad I don't get to eat here as often as I used to.  Really the best way to describe Cafe Minh is as a toss up between a French restaurant with some strong Vietnamese influences or a Vietnamese restaurant with some very strong French influences that combines with some New Orleans Creole fusion magic to create some great things to eat.  This place also does a fantastic Bouillabaisse (possibly one of the best in the city).  The food has always been fantastically fresh and I've always enjoyed EVERYTHING I've ever eaten here.  The focus of the food seems to oscillate between Vietnamese, French, and Creole with the changing daily specials.  The interior of this place is far nicer (even borderline upscale) than the exterior would lead one to expect and I would certainly recommend this as a nice location for a date or other nice occasion.

This is a mostly locals dive bar in the Quarter that is right across from Pat O's and a few blocks off Bourbon.  This is usually a place I will escape too when I want to avoid the crowds of Bourbon St. or Pat O's.  I've never had a problem finding a seat at the bar here and there never seems to be a wait for the bathroom so this place gets three stars just for the sheer comfort of providing the basics that can sometimes be hard to find in the French Quarter.  The best thing about this bar is that it is very near Yo Momma's where I can always get a fantastic burger.

This is a great little restaurant that is noted for its courtyard.  The food leans more towards French with the occasional nod to Southern and New Orleans influences.  They also offer a simple Sunday brunch with a concise menu.  The bar is right next to the courtyard and offers a pleasant escape when the temperatures are nice.  My only complaint is that sometimes the portion sizes are far too small for the price.

Every time I've attempted to use this location it has completely failed me and they seem to chronically be out of supplies, boxes etc. so I always end up having to go down to the Convention Center location to take care of my business.  At this point I've given up on using this location.

I'm very surprised that I found the food to be as good as it was here as I had a bit of a bias going in because I'm not the biggest fan of Superior Grill's food (Superior Grill is a Tex-Mex place owned by the same people that opened this place).  I just sat at the bar and sampled a few appetizers with low expectations as they had so recently opened.  They have a nice looking raw oyster bar in here and the grilled and raw oysters really were fantastic and among the best I've ever had.  The crab cake seemed to actually be 99% crab and was great.  I also had ordered a gumbo and they accidentally brought me crawfish etouffe which was tasty but they quickly realized their mistake and brought me my gumbo which was good but not fantastic.  They make their own potato chips and some kind of dip and even those were good.  The location is perfect and this will certainly be a popular spot during Mardi Gras for parades.    They have done a fantastic job of renovating the old Copeland's space and it is both very comfortable and aesthetically pleasing.  I have eaten here several times now and the appetizers and oysters remain the stars of the show with the entree options being less pleasing.  If everything else can reach the level of the appetizers and they maintain standards I will be glad to have this addition to the neighborhood.  Tip:  They have a fantastic daily happy hour with 50 cent oysters, $3 draft beers, 2 for 1 frozen drinks along with half off glasses and bottles of wine.

So I had been to the Causeway location of this place a few times and found the snowball ice alright but I had never tried their "cheesecake stuffed" snowball before.  So I finally broke down on a rainy day and got the blueberry special.  Ahhh... well the snowball part was alright but the whipped cream I could have done without and then when I got into the "cheesecake" portion that stuff was just gross and I won't get that again (and I LOVE cheesecake).  As I was digging down into the lower parts of my snowball I was driving past Hansen's and there was ZERO line and I wept deeply for sinning against the mighty snowball gods and knew I must keep my Hansen's vigil more strongly and not stray to such sinfully aberrant things as a fake cheesecake stuffed frankenconeballs.

Yes... I confess I've been here and more than once.  During parades I've frequently gotten a daiquiri  here and sometimes after work I've zipped in for an icy cold refreshing beverage.  Drinking a daiquiri isn't the most manly thing but I've done it here often but they also have nice beer specials so you can pretty much get what you want.  This is probably the nicest New Orleans Original Daiquiri location I've ever been to and I've been to MANY.

If they ever rolled on time they would be four and maybe five stars but they get serious star points deducted for ALWAYS rolling late!  So great parade with krewe members of black, white and every other possible ethnic group or mixture painted in black face with their theme "throw" being highly decorated coconuts (but the actual coconuts are so large and heavy they can't throw them anymore and have to hand them out).  This is always a very popular and crowded parade VERY early in the morning for Mardi Gras Day right before Rex rolls.   Anywhere else in the world these days the damn PC police would be yelling for heads to roll because of the black face and other traditions.  Thank God I live in New Orleans where we can still poke fun at things, have satire, irony and all sorts of other complicated cultural disruptions while having a damn good time with it.

White Linen Night is an annual tradition every summer in the city's Warehouse Arts District on the first Saturday night in August. The occasion calls for wearing white outfits and some even wear white hats as they tour through the art galleries along Julia Street and the side streets.  The dress has gotten much less formal recently and there are far fewer white linen suits than in the past and many more white linen shorts and casual shirts.  Samplings of New Orleans cuisine from local restaurants are available along with wine, cocktails, and beer to enjoy as you go about your gallery stroll. The outdoor celebration also includes live entertainment provided by some of New Orleans most talented musicians.  The official post party at the Contemporary Arts Center is a great time with good music and an enthusiastic crowd.  504ward also does a fantastic party for this event at the Louisiana Children's Museum.

This newly opened "pho" restaurant actually has a very small menu and they had chicken pho listed but didn't have any ready!  When will the curse of new restaurant malfunction end?  They also have a vegetarian/vegan pho listed for all you super unhealthy eaters :) Selection includes egg rolls, spring rolls, skewers, four types of pho, six types of bun (noodles), six rice dishes, four banh mi (po boys), and two desserts.  The interior of the restaurant is spacious with comfortable seating but is still lacking much ambiance.  I was not happy when they didn't have my chicken pho and I didn't feel like a beef pho since I ate a pound of BBQ beef at the Road Food fest at lunch so I opted for a Bun and will have to return to give a pho report.  The price for pho is $6.99 for a small and $7.99 for a large.  To add to the inconvienace this place is cash only.  Ok seriously now what is the major malfunction!  I returned again to sample the chicken pho and they STILL don't have it.  They had told me on my first visit they would have it the next day BUT oh no now they say it "should" be available in a "few" days.  Why have something on the menu if you've never even made it?  None of the waitstaff had ever had it?  What kind of pho place is this that only has a selection of 4 types of pho but really only has three?  Excuse me I'm going to go bang my head against the wall and just go to the Westbank or Metairie for some pho...

Bulldog we've had a long sweet run but now once again you're raising your beer prices so we have to part ways.  I love you dear Bulldog but I will not let you rape me like this!  You first encourage me to bring in crawfish for YEARS then you slap me and tell me I can't!  You raise your prices not once, not twice, but THREE times in so short a space of time!  Breaking up is hard to do but in this case it ain't that hard as financially it makes perfect sense.  It used to be so much fun with you but now you've gone so corporate and sold your soul.  I can go to Blue Nile to watch music AND drink beer cheaper than I can just drink beer with you Bulldog and I can get $2 Abita Amber almost EVERY night along with better food at Bruno's!  I guess I will be at Tracy's or most of the other bars Uptown with all the rest of your former regulars drinking the same beer at substantially cheaper prices.

The music is always great at this festival while the food just frustrates the ever living hunger out of my belly!  They NEVER have enough BBQ vendors and the vendors are always running out of things.  The lines to get something to eat are ridiculously LONG!  It is literally quicker to drive out to the Bywater and eat at the Joint and drive back then to wait in the line for BBQ at the Joint booth at the festival.    Guess what?    For the last two years that's exactly what I've been doing and I just drive out and eat at the Joint before going to this fest and that's probably your best bet (until they add more vendors and provide some relief to the crazy long food lines).

I had heard many great things about this place and it took me awhile to finally meander my way out to try it.  Overall it is decent sushi but nothing really knocked my socks off and it was more on the expensive side.  Taking into account the distance I have to travel from the Garden District, the limited street parking and price there are lots of other sushi places I would choose before this place.  If I were already in the area and had folks that had a need for sushi I wouldn't object to returning but I wouldn't make a special trip just to eat here.

I really wish I could like this place.  The owners and staff are awesome and I LOVE the bar.  I really like the look of the entire building and the courtyard.   But I have to mention that I HATE the new "GASTROPUB" concept going on in New Orleans recently.  They don't have Abita Amber here and the food is way overpriced for the basic and often not so great food.  Just like all the "gastropubs" that are going on in New Orleans I just feel why bother when I can just go to a real restaurant or bar where you can actually eat a plate of food that will fill you up instead of being a snack and actually get a selection of more than 4 beers.  Did I mention I HATE GASTROPUBS!!!  I wish they would just turn this into a full bar where I could have a full selection of drinks!!!  The food is sort of ok but it... just is... well... Gastropub food and from painful experience that has been a genre of food that just doesn't appeal to me as I'm a DINER and not a SNACKER.  I wish they at least had Abita Amber and I might go to at least hang out and drink at that amazing bar but ahhhh it looks like that isn't happening.

This is a legit dive bar in a strip mall that seems like it would probably be a good venue to watch sports.  The drinks were fairly priced and the service was efficient.  The only negative issue for me, but one that kills it for me, is that this place is super smoke filled and 100% of all the patrons in this joint were hitting the cancer sticks like they were never getting to shove another one in their mouth.  Also on offer during my visit were some really hilariously awful karaoke performances going on; as chain smokers often have raspy crackling voices from all the years of turning their mouths, throats and lungs into a pieces of dehydrated shriveled meat like a ham hung in a smokehouse what else could you expect?  The space of time I was able to handle being in this joint was one beer and then the clothes I was wearing reeked of smoke for a week after until I got back home and could wash them.    One day if the practice of smoking finally dies off maybe I might return but likely the last kooky suicidal smoke inhalers will be lingering on in here for a few decades more.  So all you smokers have firmly established a strong home base in this establishment to fully enjoy exclusively to yourselves.

I don't really care for hot wings but this joint does sling some great burgers, chicken sandwiches and other nice items.  The prices here are also a great value and you get a large portion of food for a very reasonable price.  The main downside of this place is it really isn't built for dining at the location as they have very limited seating inside and a table outside.  They also only have bottled drinks and no freshly brewed iced tea which always saddens me.  Overall though for a large delicious burger with nice fries this is one of the best values in the area along with offering some surprises on the menu you won't find in any other hot wing place outside of NOLA.

I pop in here every now and then but it is a very tiny bar that quickly gets packed with a mix of tourists and locals (seems like more tourists lately).  They are also cash only which makes it a huge inconvenience and greatly decreases my imbibing.  I usually end up here while waiting for a table at Adolfo's which is right above this bar.  They often have decent to good music in here with the caveat that it gets so crowded sometimes you end up almost stepping on the musicians.

Decent bar that has invested some coin into their interior decor.  The bar dominates the space and there are side tables as well.  The food mostly was not to my taste and I found the mushroom flatbread bland and unworthy of eating and the chicken sandwich on naan was also not really to my liking and left me wishing I would have just gotten their burger.  The french fires were quite good so I was happy with those.  They were nearly out of iced tea so I didn't get to drink my fill of that and then they also seemed to be running out of mustard as the last bottle available had very little left in it.  I think I would probably focus more on drinking than eating here.  It was also very dead in here on the night I visited so it seems to be more of a happy hour spot.  The menu seems to need a revamp as it just doesn't really seem to be a good mix of items for the area and attempts a fusion of things that end up not working out too well other than for maybe Vegans and vegetarians.

I was very pleasantly surprised by this establishment and even impressed.  They have some great prices on food for the area and a concise menu with a nice selection of breakfast and lunch items with NOLA flair.  The seafood gumbo here has an impressive amount of seafood in it and I haven't been impressed in a long time so that was quite a pleasant surprise.  The Swiss Schroom burger was large, juicy and quite nice for the price with the fries also being good.  The lady behind the counter was the one that took my order and cooked my burger so it was similar to a diner style joint.  I was also provided excellent service for my entire visit even when more people arrived and the counter lady had to also wait on some tables.  They also have an impressive selection of beer, wine and other drinks in their wall cooler in the back.  This place will certainly be getting more visits from me in the near future.

I really like the food here and it is certainly kicked up several notches in the flavor department from other Slavic restaurants I've eaten in.  They have a nice beef stroganoff, tasty pierogi, some of the best kapusta I've ever had along with a mighty mean burger.  I couldn't even finish my stroganoff it was such a large serving and I can eat a lot!  This is a great little spot and I will certainly be eating here often.  The only downside is that it is located inside Siberia so it isn't the most convenient place to eat if a popular band is jamming.

This is mainly a law enforcement supply store but they have many items that anybody could find useful.  They have a large selection and this is actually a branch of a small national chain that has locations across several states so you can also check out their website.  The location is a bit out of the way on the I-10 Service Road and they only open 9am-5pm and closed on the weekend so you might want to call ahead to see if they have what you're looking for.

Ok I've just had one of the most delicious, tasty, and juicy burgers on the planet!!!  I got the "Dirty Burger" which is a burger topped with roast beef debris gravy.  I thought that it would be a bit oozy gooey and messy BUT it wasn't.  The debris gravy added a whole other dimension of beef flavor goodness to the entire experience that just kicked this burger up to amazing flavor heights.  The burger meat itself was outstanding and bursting with flavor with obvious tasty chunks of onion in the meat.  This is one of my all time favorite burgers hands down!!!  The only downsides were they sliced my burger in half (and I hate it when places do that) and the bun could use some improvement.  With the roast beef debris being so good on the burger you can probably guess that it is equally fantastic on a po boy and it doesn't disappoint as they really do a fantastic roast beef po boy here.  My main "beef" with this place is that they only offer their pizza at night and not their other delicious options.  The pizza looks fantastic and I will try it at some point but I'm still addicted to their beefy goodness contained within their Dirty Burger and roast beef po boy so I get sad when I can't get it at night.  They have lots of other sandwich and po boy options (and maybe some other stuff I'm not able to focus on as I'm still in a burger swoon) so I look forward to sampling other choices here soon!!!

Some very respectable brisket with plenty of smoke flavor.  They have a lot of other very delicious menu items that are also worthy of sampling such as their shrimp and crawfish.  This is a nice spot that you might just zoom past if you didn't notice the bbq smoker in front putting off a nice hint of smoke.  Very nice folks running and owning the place with a lot of obvious love put into decorating the place to honor their relative named Elaine that they started the business for in her honor.

Po boys, burgers, seafood platters and daily specials are served cafeteria style here.  You get in line and then order your meal but don't forget to grab a drink from the coolers, as they only have bottle drinks and beer, then pay at the cash register.  At lunch this place gets pretty crowded so you might have a wait to find some seating.  The food is generally good with some standouts.  An interesting and busy place with some friendly folks working there.  Cash or check only.

This bar has always been a consistently good place to enjoy yourself and I've been to MANY private parties and events in their upstairs venue over the years.  They food is decent and much better than most of the other bars in the Warehouse District.  They have a lot of tables set around the outside so it can be a patio like experience when it is nice outside and then they have a great balcony upstairs to enjoy for private events.  I've always found the bartenders here to be outstanding and they have always delivered extremely rapid service no matter how crowded and crazy the bar is (and this includes insanely crowded times like Running of the Bulls).  This is probably my favorite bar in the entire Warehouse District simply due to the consistent and excellent service.

This is where most of the live music has relocated from Bourbon street.  It generally smells better and is usually much cleaner than Bourbon.  Typically there will be more local folks enjoying themselves here but the tourists have definitely discovered this area.  There are numerous music clubs and bars here along with a few good restaurants.  Plenty of gutter punks park their stinky selves around the area and hassle you for money so please be kind to those of us that live here and don't feed them so maybe they will either leave or actually get jobs or maybe even finally shower.

This is the best venue to see music at the House of Blues.  They have it set up for standing room only for most shows so there usually is nowhere to sit.  You get a much better music experience here than you do in the HOB's main stage.  Some of the best shows I've seen in recent years have been here.  The drink prices are the same as in HOB and generally make me less than happy.

I decided to sample the lunch at this very new restaurant so this review is just for my initial visit and usually I like to eat at a place more than once before I review it but I was really impressed with some aspects of this place and thought it deserved some early comments.  When I arrived the owner was at the front of the restaurant as I walked in, as he was acting as host, and he was a very friendly person and seemed very passionate about his restaurant.   I had arrived for an early lunch around 11ish and I was the first person to arrive for their lunch service that day.  As I walked in I found the ambiance and location of this establishment to be a total five stars as it really is a beautiful building that has been renovated nicely and they also have a very nice courtyard.  I was dining solo so I requested seating at the bar and found that the bar is also very nicely done and it is a comfortable space.  I haven't been this impressed by a new restaurant's interior in NOLA barely... EVER so they have certainly created a wonderful space.  I received my menu and I found it a bit limited in choices but as a new establishment that is acceptable if everything is done well.  The thing that threw me off a bit was that there wasn't very much seafood on the lunch menu and the dishes seemed more like something for Fall than Spring.  After a short dicernement of my choices I decided to order the duck gumbo and rabbit stew.  The duck gumbo is a very rich and hearty dish with a very pronounced roux that shows no evidence of vegetables which seems more akin to the Cajun style gumbos in  Acadiana than the Creole gumbo style more often found in New Orleans.  The duck presents in large delicious slices and is extremely tasty so that this gumbo can nearly be a meal unto itself.  The rabbit stew the owner told me is based on an "old family recipe" and it is also a very heavy dish with the sauce being extremely flavorful (it also reminded me much more of a dish from the Cajun lands than typical Creole New Orleans flavors).  I found the sauce for the rabbit so tasty I was a bit sad that I didn't have any bread to sop up more of the flavor (they give you a flatbread here that doesn't work well for such attempts).  Although I was very full from my meal I decided to go all out and closed out my meal with their decadent chocolate dessert.  I ended up paying about $7 more for my meal here than I would for lunch at Commander's Palace (with the notable minus of the 25 cent martini bonus of Commander's of course so they might want to consider some type of drink special like that at Dijon).    Overall I enjoyed my meal but once again it seemed more like something I would prefer to eat on a cold Fall or Winter's night than a Spring lunch.  I certainly would like to see more seafood and daily specials on the menu.  The food was overall good with probably about a 3 to a 3.5 star rating for me when factored in with the cost while the ambiance was just fantastic except for the lack of people.  They are still a very new place and currently working on a new menu and I believe if they keep working on polishing what they are doing with their food they can certianly get this place up to a four or five star rating.  I really want to give them four stars but I just don't think the lunch is quite there yet.  Their lunch is currently priced at Commander's Palace levels but they aren't yet up to par with what you get for around the same price as Commander's but their new menu might be a totally new story.  Their dinner menu looks to have a lot more choices and I will certainly return to sample their new menu for dinner and I want to return soon just for drinks at their bar and patio.  On my next visit, when I plan to return with a group, I fully expect this place to be at a four star level at the least!

Their seafood gumbo is a bit watery and could use a thicker rue and more seafood.  The shrimp creole leaves the tail on which I've never had in any other version of this dish so you get to take those off (I'm fine with peeling my own shrimp but this isn't peel and eat shrimp).  They have a decent selection of NOLA style food with the majority of the seafood being fried.  There is a raw oyster bar so you can get your fix here.  The service is generally attentive and friendly.  Overall its a decent place for lunch if you are nearby and need a quick meal.

This is a great little dive spot to watch some good music.  Usually it is almost all local folks so this is still a little local gem that hasn't been overwhelmed by tourists...so far.  I've had some crazy good times in here and when there is a good band it can get pretty crowded and HOT.  The drink prices are very fair and the service has always been great.  It can get pretty gross and smokey sometimes depending on the crowd.  Parking in the area can also be a challenge on crowded nights.  This area is getting more trendy with all the development on Oak Street so places like this are getting to be an endangered species for the future as the $12 fast food "gourmet" burger joints creep ever closer.

This is a cool old school Chinese restaurant where they really go all out with decorating it like a Chinese restaurant which seems to be getting quite rare with new joints opening these days.  The lunch combo portions are very generous and it is unlikely you will leave here hungry.  The food here is the Americanized style that many folks grew up eating in the 70's and 80's and it hasn't changed much here so it is a blast from the past for many such individuals.  There is certainly more authentic Chinese food around these days and there are better versions of many Americanized Chinese dishes around these days but there are not a lot of joints left in the area that combine the old school Chinese ambiance style with such huge portions of generally decent food along with a huge helping of over the top fun make believe to almost make you think this place was transported out of the 1970's.

This is a great spot with some good food and a nice bar.  The prices are quite reasonable and the beers are a great value.  The only downsides are they are cash/check only, they used canned green beans and they only have a rotating gumbo and don't consistently offer an all seafood gumbo on the menu.  They do have changing daily specials and they offer a really good selection of New Orleans style food along with friendly service.  They also do quite a nice brunch on Sunday and offer some items you probably won't even find in the city limits of NOLA such as red velvet pancakes.    Overall this is a nice spot to visit that also usually provides a pleasant drive from NOLA so it is a worthwhile endeavor to visit and experience this joint (just make sure to bring plenty of CASH).

I've eaten at Byblos on Magazine for many years and it is usually good with some consistent patches of less than good incidents.  My first experience eating here was terrible as I got the lamb sampler platter and everything came out burned black and crispy.  Fortunately that was the low point and things have generally been better since then.  Byblos does some things better than other Middle Eastern places but not as good as others in the area.  I generally find their beef kabobs are consistently outstanding while the quality and taste of the lamb is very inconsistent.    Byblos used to offer some very consistently clean bathrooms but, for at least the past year, the men's toilet has been constantly clogged up and emanating a very unpleasant smell.  I've also seen some inconsistency with management where sometimes you are "allowed" to order some combination of things and other times you are not.  They also have been a bit confused on the menu with having gyros on both the dinner and lunch menus but then only on the lunch and then going back so I've seen several people get frustrated with that.  Byblos offers belly dancing on Thursday nights and this location can be a fun place just to hang out and drink as their drink prices are much cheaper than some of the surrounding restaurants (and even some of the bars).  Usually a good place for lunch or dinner but sometimes some inconsistencies do pop up.

This used to be a decent place to sample some New Orleans favorites and they offer some good combos but the quality of the food has deteriorated drastically over the years.  Essentially this is a tourist trap and although it does have a certain charm to it when looking at it from the outside along with a nice location it then declines quickly as the quality of the food does not justify the inflated prices.  There are far too many other places serving much better food at much better prices than this establishment.  Until they do some serious quality control and gain much more consistency and better value with their prices this is a place to generally avoid.

This place has been several different bars and this latest incarnation seems to vary from an older crowd for happy hour to a much younger crowd when they have music.  The music that I've heard blaring out of here has never really attracted me so I've only been here for happy hour.  This is a decent bar with an ambiance that slightly reminds me of a more run down Applebee's bar.  I don't like reminders that Applebee's exists so I really prefer the nearby Delachaise but I will pop in here occassionally.

This is like hanging out in a crazy old Victorian house that somebody decided to turn into a dive bar... wait that's exactly what it is!  They often have live music in here and it is a relaxing place to enjoy a performance.  You really don't have a lot of room for dancing but a few folks can make it work.  A big bonus to me is that they have gone smoke free and that always makes everything better.  It is a bit cramped and a bit of an unusual set-up for a bar with music but I've always had a good time here.

I've eaten here a handful of times over the years and generally it is passable but never anything notable.  This place caters mainly to the tourist crowd and it is very rare to see any locals inside.  The building and ambiance are nice and I've often made use of their bar to grab a drink to go.  Where they often fall short is in their food execution which often just doesn't live up to expectations.  In any other city this place might rate a three or four star rating but in NOLA there are just too many better places for food.  Generally your best bet here is to stick to the sandwiches or fried seafood.

This is an interesting dive bar with a more interesting and bit of a rougher around the edges crowd.  There are always some interesting characters in here and they always seem to have some good prices on drinks.  They also have an interesting patio in the back that seems to be rarely used (at least at night).  They have started doing food with a good sized menu and the kitchen stays open til 2am.  I've only eaten the burger and fries so far which are decent but not great with the fries being the better experience.  There are several types of games and pool tables that usually seem to be engaged by some really serious pool players that will get very grumpy if you get in their way.  The biggest negative here is the sheer number of smokers that seem to always be in this bar.  If possible I think Half Moon probably gets smokier than Rendezvous and often even the bartender is smoking.  The bartenders have always been very quick and efficient with their service and this bar has seemed to have gotten much more popular since Katrina.

Every Saints game is a HUGE festival in its own right!  When the Saints play at home it's like a mini Mardi Gras party all over the city.  When the Saints play away we bring some NOLA culture, food and fun to wherever we're at along with our demands that we be allowed to have go cups for our drinks!  We don't care about any silly open container laws as they are illegal and immoral to Saints fans and most places tend to adapt to us and just accept our wild and wacky ways.  Celebrating the Saints crosses more class, social, political, geographical and racial divides than anything else in New Orleans and the kinship fans feel over our team crosses more boundaries than any other celebration we have.  The Who Dat Nation are among the most creative and outlandish with costuming for games and you will be hard pressed to find a more dedicated, outlandish, eccentric and interesting group of fans.

Ale NOLA offers 30 beers on tap along with bottles, cans and liquor.  They have a small kitchen in the back slinging bar grub to hungry folks. A shared patio with its sister bar, Oak Wine Bar, makes for an interesting dynamic with some folks wandering back and forth.  Ale NOLA and Oak Wine don't have a shared billing system so you cant have a tab on one side and use it on the other.  The dimensions of this long and narrow space are equivalent to a shotgun single.

This is a really nice food court offering a fantastic variety of food.  They have optioms that should suit nearly any taste or preference at a decent price.   The biggest issue here would be the lack of any advertising outside the building to let folks know what all is inside to eat so it seems it ends up being mostly folks that work in the building or nearby that end up eating here.  There are certainly some food options here that more folks would like to sample if they only knew there was a food court here.  The other issue is this is mainly a lunch spot and closes comparatively early so folks who don't work nearby can't do dinner here.

As far as I know this is the only Peruvian restaurant in NOLA.  Very little English is spoken here but they do have a picture menu for those not well versed in Spanish.  They don't have iced tea and I attempted to order a Topo Chico mineral water but instead I received a plastic bottled water so I assumed they didn't have it until I saw it in their case.  The food is pretty good and there are some things that are a bit different than anything I've had before so this is certainly an interesting spot to check out for a little something different.  They do some nice things with potatoes here.  If you can find a friend that speaks Spanish you will probably have a better experience here.  They do take credit cards here.

Well some of the things here are done well but overall I just wasn't happy with my meal or the service.  The Vietnamese fusion approach here just didn't really work for me and I like the Vietnamese/French fusion food Cafe Minh a whole lot better.  I might give it a few more chances but the menu just doesn't really excite me and for the price there are a whole lot of other places I would rather go.

Ok I drink here more than anywhere else and I've been going here for quite awhile now.  I frequent the Magazine location as it is very close to my house but I get to the Mid-City location pretty often also.  It used to certainly be a 5 Star rated place for me but some changes over time have lowered it for me.  I have completed the infamous beer journey, of tasting all their draft beverages, more times than anybody else so I've got more experience with the bar than a lot of the current staff.  Most of my friends have seemed to have stopped going here either because they have gotten too old and grumpy or because they don't like the changes either.  They used to encourage folks to bring in crawfish from across the street and now they have suddenly banned all outside food and eliminated one of my favorite activities of eating crawfish on the Bulldog patio so BIG minus!!!  The food used to be outstanding with an amazing burger but as they have grown in size, consolidated ownership, and become much more corporate with multiple locations (Magazine, Mid-City, Metairie, Baton Rouge, Jackson) they have lowered the quality of the food and it just isn't what it used to be (most notable is the dramatic decrease in hamburger bun quality; they used to bake their own awesome ones and now they buy some that fall apart easily).  The Magazine location has also acquired a very bad behaving customer in recent years in the guise of a crazy old black dude (always wears a hat with lots of missing teeth) that gets hammered and just terrorizes women incessantly (some girls find it entertaining briefly so it keeps encouraging him to continue the behavior to extremes and this has resulted in many many young ladies getting the hell out of dodge to avoid being harassed; this has also resulted in many near brawls).   They have also eliminated one of the perks of doing the beer journey since Katrina in that they used to have an awesome Christmas party but they have stopped that (which irks me greatly as I greatly earned that perk multiple times)!!!  The Bulldog on Magazine used to be a great place to watch the Saints games but it seems to have just allowed that to die off and most people just seem to prefer the Mid-City location or some other bar now (lots of other places have free food during games so that siphons people off).  They have also had multiple price increases in the drinks which make it much less comparable to nearby establishments (I'm sure the yankee Tulane students from New York City, that frequent the Magazine location, making remarks at how they can't believe how cheap it is to drink in NOLA don't help keep the prices down either).  Might also be nice if the often cramped Magazine location took over Nacho Mama's (not a fan of their food) and knocked the wall down between them to make for more space.  They still have the best tasting draft beer in the area due to their care in cleaning their beer lines and it is hard to find a pint as fresh and tasty as they pour anywhere else on draft.  I love beer and so that is why I still frequent this place and pay the silly inflated price as it is damn good beer here (I just don't go as much as I used to).  I also get outstanding service (possibly due to the fact that I've been going to this bar for such a long time and I like the fact that they already know what I want and they always treat me well as I've been a mighty good customer over the years or maybe they just have kick ass bartenders).  The electronic trivia is also an entertaining bonus that is available to keep things interesting.  It is both a good and bad thing that the Magazine location gets packed: it is good when it is packed with girls and bad when it is packed with dudes!  The most fun to be had at the Magazine location is to be found on Wednesday nights for pint night (when you get to take home your decorated pints) and the Irish Channel St. Patrick's Parade (insanity fun).  Wednesday nights are still the most consistent good times for the most part (although I miss the funny smart ass pint glasses they used to give away before Katrina).    Overall always a great place on Magazine and Mid-City for a tasty cool brew but a bit overpriced on Magazine for the area and way overpriced in Mid-City.  BRING BACK CRAWFISH EATING on Magazine!!!

This is a chain of bars owned and located inside a real estate company's developments at multiple locations.  The Goat bar at the Nashville property is very nicely built and has been integrated very well in relation to this site location's pool with the bar patio merging into the nearby pool area with good feng shui along with the patio having impressive heat generation capability for cooler weather that might put a dragons breath to shame.  They have a nice looking menu but I haven't had  a chance to eat here yet but I was here during a football game day and it had quite a nice crowd that was of pleasant size where you could still find a seat while still maintaining an energetic vibe inside.  The only downside I found is they didn't have t-shirts for sale and since I've got a pal who is named "The Goat" I really wanted to get him a shirt but alas they had none on offer and simply advised perhaps in the future that option might be possible.

This is nearest Popeyes to my house and living in NOLA you always need access to some Popeyes for various events, feasts and moments.  This location probably gets more than its fair share of tourists but it always seems to have an interesting group of folks inside.  For the most part it is busy but service is still fast and efficient.

This is one of the top hotels in New Orleans along with having one of the premier entertainment venues with the Davenport Lounge.  You get comped parking for many of the events held here along with visits to the Davenport Lounge so the parking garage is quite popular.  If you want to dress up and escape the tourists on Bourbon Street this is one of the best choices for a nice civilized experience with some old fashioned glamour and elegance.

The Good:  This place has the look and feel of your standard Southern Diner (if there is such a thing as "standard" in Southern diners)  that you can find all over most of the South.  I got the pimento cheese burger with fries and the burger tasted exactly like one you would grill yourself on an outdoor grill.  The best things about the burger were that it used a good bun and I got it dressed and the veggies were extremely fresh.  The fries were very good and perfectly done with a nice crisp outside.  They had some interesting blackboard specials and drinks listed.  They also have a very large bar that you can sit and eat at and that is one of my favorite spots to sit when dining solo.  The Bad:  The menu was pretty small and they had a really limited selection of sides.  I love meat and veggie plates but I don't like fatback or bacon in my veggies and half or more of the few veggies on the menu seemed to have that in them.  Another bad aspect with the side veggies is you only get a choice of one with your meal and almost every other place across the South I've eaten in places like this you always have a choice of at least 2 or more veggies.  I observed other people's food and other than the sandwiches and burgers they didn't look all that great--just ok.  The service was also a tad bit slow on getting refills on my drink.  The Ugly:  The price for my burger and iced tea came to $14.82 (before tip) so that was a mighty expensive lunch for just a burger!  I could have gone to Yo Mama's or La Petite Grocery and gotten better food at that price.  There is also considerable sticker shock (which seems to have become the norm for new places opening recently) with the price of beer on the menu set at $6 and that price for an Abita Amber is outrageous for Freret Street and all of Uptown.  If I can eat a meal and drink beer at almost all the restaurants on Magazine Street cheaper than at High Hat then I have nothing to motivate me to return.  Unfortunately the food is just not a good value and at current prices I really can't see myself returning for a second visit as I have too many other choices that are better, cheaper, and closer to my neighborhood.  I really want a nice meat and veggie plate restaurant Uptown but sadly this isn't it but possibly with some adjustments it could be.

This is a well laid out library with some parking with it which certainly makes it easier to visit.  They have some decent meeting space and the interior of the building is nicer than I would have guessed from the exterior.  They have a lot of different offerings throughout the week so this is certainly a good resource for the area.  Overall a library is a good thing and a good library is a great thing so make sure to check out this library to see for yourself.

This place is slinging nice sandwiches and huge burgers.  The prices make this place a pretty good value for the amount of food you get and you will most likely get quite full on the food here.  This is a really casual spot with most of the seating being at the bar with just a few tables.  They do a slight Vietnamese bling to some of the food to give it a little extra BAM   of something a bit different.

As part of a week long "meat fest" (where a group of men are going around and eating at all the area steak houses before lent) I arrived here as one of the stops on our "meat tour" and we all decided to go with the tasting menu along with getting one extra steak (the skin on Entraña Fina con la Piel) and the sweet breads as additional appetizers.  I got the NY Strip as my steak and everyone else in the group got other types of steak.  The stars of the show were the Entraña Fina con la Piel, the sweet breads, and the filet.  My NY Strip I had ordered medium rare and it came out much more medium well (and too dry), another steak in my group had to be sent back because it was WAY overdone and the "Kobe" steak was an epic fail.  My group was also not happy having to share the empanadas as they were quite tasty but other than that we were quite gorged by the end of our meal.    The real low point of the evening was our server who was, unfortunately, pretty irritating and bossy (as she told us we couldn't pour our own wine and would periodically bang on things to try and hush us so she could make some announcement).  By the end of the night it got to the point we were just ignoring her and people were making jokes about how overbearing she was so she got more and more irritated with us.  Regardless both she and the restaurant made a lot of money last night as we cleared out several of their wine selections with seven of us running up our bill to $119.00 each (which has been the highest bill yet out of all the steak places we've eaten at so far).   For a return visit I would just focus on eating meat (as the sides just take up valuable stomach space that more meat could be crammed into) so make sure to get the sweet breads, the filet, and the Entraña Fina con la Piel.  I think I might enjoy just sitting at the bar to eat more than having to get bossed around and told I can't pour my own wine.  Overall a good experience, but I expected better, yet I shall return to sample La Boca again.

This place does look exactly like a camp and it seems to be quite a popular spot in the area.  I've been around this place several times as it is right next to Hillbilly BBQ and across from the pistol range but not much ever seemed to be going on during those visits.  I finally ended up here on a Wednesday for the very popular bike night and I'm not a biker so unfortunately I don't have lots of cool leather to wear thus arriving in my preppy work clothes made me stand out quite glaringly.  They had a really good band jamming out and everybody seemed to be having a great time.  They have a really awesome huge back patio area here that I had never seen before and that is quite an impressive space.  The huge downsides to me for this joint are that it was extremely smokey, it was almost all dudes and they were out of Abita Amber at only 9pm.  I would like to return when they have some events going on at the back patio where I can actually breathe.

This is a decent indoor range to get some pistol practice in.  They only offer hourly rates and with the price of ammo these days most people don't need that much time so it could be nice if they offered at least 30 minute rates.  They have pistols for rent along with eye and ear protection if you happen to forget your own.  They have a decent selection of ammo for sale if you don't want to bring your own.  This is often a busy place so you might have to wait a little while before a lane opens.    This is the first indoor range I've ever shot in as during my formative years and then during my time in the military I used all outdoor ranges.  In most aspects I think I prefer shooting outside but I really liked the automated target movement here which allows you to easily change distances.  The location is at the end of a dead end road so it isn't the most convenient place to access for me but its pretty near the Earhart Expressway so once you learn the navigation you can usually get there in acceptable time.    Nice folks running the place and I found signing up to use the range a relatively quick and painless process.  After you do the simple initial paperwork you get a "membership card" then sign up on a list and wait for a lane to open.  When space opens they call your name and tell you your range number so you can start your shooting and then payment is taken when you finish.  Eye and ear protection are mandatory and the deafening roar of so many weapons being fired indoors really amplifies the sound and there is a lot of brass bouncing around so bring your own or rent it!  Bonus:  They have many interesting and humorous paper targets for sale.  Yes we're talking zombies and clowns... and zombie clowns!   Damn I HATE clowns!!!

I'm really not the biggest fan of fast food and I'm definitely not a fan of chains.  Some chains do put out decent food and sometimes every few years I will indulge in some of it.  Chick-Fil-A was a place I used to love to eat back when malls were cool in the 80's.  I still think they have one of the most fantastic fried chicken sandwiches and the pickle they throw on there brings out some extra zing of flavor.  I also had my first experience with waffle fries here and those things are also pretty damn skippy tasty.  I once worked with a young lady that loved Chick-Fil-A so much she ate it EVERYDAY for lunch for the three years I worked with her.    I also think it's great the owner has values that he stands by and he isn't afraid to run his business by his values.  I'm glad we still have some semblance of a free market in this country and the right of free speech where people can agree or disagree and if you like nice fried chicken you can eat it or not.  God help us when the PC thought police lunatics take over and force us to only eat fried tofu and only engage in group think with anybody that disagrees with them being swiftly sent for "recycling" to fertilize more soybeans to make more tofu.  Remember kids PC is EVIL and being non-PC is way COOL!

This is a great Bavarian style beer hall meets American sports bar along with serving up some of the best BBQ brisket I've had in Nashville.  They have proper full size Bavarian Maß liters to ensure you get enough beer to wash down your food with and enjoy the Gemütlichkeit.  The only thing missing here are proper biermädchen which would really kick up the aesthetics of this joint. There is a great game day vibe here and the communal beer hall tables make for a fun time along with adding the challenge of finding an open seat during the more popular and crowded times here.    Overall this is typically just a great spot and a lot of fun can be had here.

The all you can eat deal is probably the way to go here as the rolls are pretty tiny.   I ordered the regular two roll lunch special that came with miso soup and salad and I was still very hungry and had to go to second lunch elsewhere to make a full meal of it.  The sushi wasn't terrible but it didn't get much above pretty mediocre at best.  It really didn't inspire me in any way that would really make me want to return.  A very average and bland kind of strip mall place like you might find in Anytown USA...  Have I mentioned I hate strip malls?

Generally I avoid this place like the plague as it is just chock full of tourists and aggressive shot girls attempting to choke you by shoving test tube shots down your throat.  Occasionally during their three for one happy hour I end up here with some of my friends that like to make fun of tourists or when someone in my group of friends has out of town people that for whatever deviant reasons love this bar and demand we visit.  Some of the shot girls are decent looking so maybe that is the draw along with the fact this place is usually packed with tourists and many of the female tourists are often wearing less clothing than the shot girls.  This place is tolerable in limited doses and I seem to end up here two to three times a year.

This is a pizza joint in a Metry strip mall that has been around awhile and is many folks favorite.  It isn't my favorite but they do make alright pizza here. This is a popular family spot and this spot draws a consistent clientele but I've never been here when its been packed.  Other than pizza the only other items available here are salad and spaghetti.  If you find yourself in Metairie and in the mood for pizza this is one of the better choices in the suburbs but there is better pizza to be found in the city.    Tip:  If you need Saints gear you can combine your shopping experience at the Black & Gold shop with your pizza experience as Tower of Pizza is in the same strip mall.

Pontchartrain Landing is a marina and RV park located on the industrial canal right off Lake Pontchartrain.  They have a good BBQ restaurant, good patio bar, little swimming pool and hot tub.  The swimming pool and hot tub are free to use.  They also offer camper trailers, "tropical villas" and permanently moored houseboats for rent so you can visit for a short time or just live out here.  There are a wide range of interesting people here both tourists and locals that you probably won't meet anywhere else.  This is still a relatively unknown place and not many locals seem to know about it so if you want an interesting new experience this place can be a fun diversion from your usual list of activities.

I was dining across the street at Monell's so being from New Orleans and a lover of all things fish and seafood I had to investigate this joint.  On walking in I was greeted with an impressive display case of numerous fish and then they had other seafood available as well.  This is a nice old school looking dedicated seafood joint but I didn't see any seafood offered for consumption on the premises or cooked and ready to go.  They certainly had some room to add some chairs and tables but none were placed as of yet.  I sincerely hope they will start offering boiled crawfish, crabs, shucked raw oysters and other such prepared items for consumption on the premises or to go if Nashville legalities allow such things.

I've been attempting to eat here for years but every time I've scheduled a meal here something always seemed to get in the way.  Well I was finally able to break my GW Fins curse last night.  This place always seems to be crowded and mostly with tourists and that was the case during my meal.  The interior of this place is very modern and "hip" and personally that's not my style so I didn't find that aspect very appealing.  It also gets pretty loud in here due to the crowd so that should also be a consideration when planning to eat here.  The food here is generally not New Orleans style food but they have a few New Orleans dishes splashed about the menu.   I ate here with one of my friends and we shared the fried lobster tail appetizer which tasted ok and exactly what I thought fried lobster would taste like.  I had the hog snapper for my entree and apple pie for dessert while my friend had the wood grilled grouper and molten chocolate cake.  The hog snapper was highly recommended by our server and it came with a very crispy sear/crust on one side that I didn't really like but the rest of the fish was cooked well other than being VERY bland and it  lacked seasoning so I had to resort to some Tabasco sauce.  Where this dish really fell flat was in the "sides" which were lobster and tomato risotto, sugar snap peas, and lobster butter.  The fish was stacked on top of a hint of about a tablespoon of  flavorless risotto and I was served exactly THREE snap peas.  In my book these don't count as sides but garnishes!  Vegetables are cheap and for the prices they charge you should certainly be served more than three peas (I love peas!) and a tablespoon of risotto.  My friend found the grouper dish to be very nice and that fish tasted much better to me while still needing a bit more spice.  I had no chance to sample the molten chocolate cake as my friend gulped it down and my apple pie was satisfactory but I've certainly had better.    If you're looking for a New Orleans type experience this is definitely not the place for either NOLA ambiance or food.  If you're looking for something very different and in the mood for seafood this is a good option for something much different than you will find anywhere else in the area.  They seem very concerned with artistic plating but that comes at the expense of stacking things on top of each other and I hate my food being stacked like that and it also results in them giving you very small portions of the accompanying sides.  I prefer function over form with my plate and the plating here definitely makes form the main focus with the result that eating requires unstacking the pile that has been served to you.  This is also a very tourist filled spot and very expensive for the portion sizes.  At these prices there are many other restaurants I like a lot more.  Overall this isn't a place I would frequent but it is on my list for an occasional change of pace.  They certainly have a very nice and constantly changing selection of seafood on the menu that you won't find in most other local spots.  If they would kick up the spice, serve decent portions of sides, and STOP the practice of stacking food on plates I would like this place a great deal more.

This is a great deli and a great po boy shop in addition to being a grocery!!!  They have a fantastic selection of available meals and sides in their deli counter and a large selection of various po boys and other sandwiches.  I don't know if I will ever be able to make it through everything they have on the sandwich menu much less the deli counter but I've made a good effort over the years.  Great place to grab some picnic food and head over to the dog park or river to enjoy the food and outdoors.  They also do some pretty good catering options I've had at parties as well (I really like their mini strombolies).  Verti Marte video review:  https://youtu.be/a8Q-y4jAXIk

So far this is my least favorite food of all the meat and three joints I have visited in Nashville but they give you a LOT of food for the price (and for being my least favorite in Nashville it is still better than many others around the rest of the country).  The service here is great and good old Southern friendly and pleasant as they kept my tea filled and made sure to check up on me to make sure if I needed anything.  Unfortunately my choice of the "beef steak" was just one of the least pleasing country fried/chicken fried style steaks I have yet sampled and it reminded me too much of some unpleasant school cafeteria meals I had as a kid so I just wouldn't get that again.  The vegetables were all great and I look forward to sampling lots of the other meats and vegetables here as I imagine I will likely enjoy those a lot more.  This is a fantastic dive type of joint as well (in every good way) which adds up to big bonus points to me and as they have kept most of it unchanged for many decades so there is a lot of old Nashville to enjoy inside this place.  Overall this is a decent spot to grab a hearty meal at a good price with pleasant folks working there.

Ruth's Chris used to be a local NOLA joint and they got props for that.  They then expanded and became a chain and as with many chains that did result in a loss of the quality they used to have.  They also relocated their corporate offices out of NOLA after Katrina so they get major negatives for that.  Generally the steaks here are very well done while the sides are good but not outstanding.  I have had occasions where my entire meal was burned, and I mean with black charring all over my steak and sides, so they aren't always perfect but at least 80% of the time they do a decent job.  This location is far better than the one in Metairie but there are usually other places I will go for a steak.  When Ruth's was a local place it was hard to beat but the ravages of going corporate and becoming a chain have definitely decreased the experience.

I've been going to this grocery location for years way before it was a Rouse's.  I really miss the 24 hour operations that used to exist before Katrina when this was a Save-A-Center as I like to do my shopping late after all the crowds are asleep.  The quality of the food and the design of the store has drastically improved since Rouse's took over and they have consistently upgraded things at this location.  There is a really good selection of local Louisiana products and some local produce featured.  They have a decent to good prepared food selection here along with the excellent Progress Grocery muffalettas and Rouse's house brand olive salad is among the best there is.    My biggest issue with this location is that there is almost always a line at the deli counter and I often get frustrated with how long it takes to order and check out at this location.  Another bone of contention with the deli is they will often advertise deli meats on sale but when you place an order for such a special they often forget to give you the sale price and this has happened frequently enough that I complained on their website but I NEVER heard back from anybody.  They still have the self-checkout machines left over from when this was a Save-A-Center but they don't use them for whatever reason and I wish they would re-activate them to speed the frequently slow checkout process at peak hours.    Rouse's constantly works to improve this location but it still has some weak points that chronically disappoint and there is still a lot of room for improvement.  Overall this is still a good spot to make your groceries at typically good prices.  The nice selection of local brands, products, and produce is certainly appreciated.

The location of this place is a bit challenging to find in Harahan and it certainly qualifies as a fantastic NOLA dive spot along with their next door seafood market.  The service here is very friendly and down to earth with the staff making sure that you have everything you need to enjoy your meal.  They have a large and fantastic list of appetizers that can become a meal into themselves (like the Eggplant Harahan, seared tuna, BBQ shrimp, the fried green tomatoes, and the crab cakes) and the only thing I'm not a big fan of is their seafood gumbo that they add sausage too (and that's just a personal preference that I don't like sausage in my SEAFOOD gumbo).  This place has some great raw oysters, good boiled seafood, great po boys and fried entrees.   I've always had good experience here and everybody I've taken here has greatly enjoyed it!

This place gets extra bonus points for being open 24/7 and they also have a good selection of daquiris.  The fried shrimp here was a bit on the hard/overcooked side on my last visit so they seem to have gotten a bit inconsistent with that unfortuantely.  They do have a large selection of food so there are plenty of other options.  If you find yourself late at night in need of some food with a side of daquiri this place can do the trick.

So my very first purchase at a Best Buy was here and I got a Sony Vaio laptop for my work.  I needed a DVD burner for the projects that I was working on so I ask the salesman specifically if he was definitely sure that this model had a DVD burner on it and he assured me that it did.  So I get home all happy and excited to get busy with my project and... what it has a DVD player but NOT burner!!!  So I jump back in my car and drive way back out to the burgs from Uptown to return this item I was woefully misinformed on.  I get to the returns department and explain my situation and they say they are happy to accept the return with a small $300 restock fee since I had opened the package.  I make it clear to them that such an arrangement was absolutely unacceptable so to placate me they offered to sell me an external DVD burning drive with some DVD authoring software at a "discount."  By this point I was so infuriated I accepted the "deal" as I had no more patience left and LOTS of work to complete.  So from that experience I have severe doubts that I would EVER purchase another laptop from Best Buy...

This is definitely a better tour with a car than doing it via Riverboat but the boat is a nice cruise.  This is the site of the historic victory over the British at the Battle of New Orleans which is celebrated in Jackson Square with the statue of Gen. Jackson.  That notorious pirate Jean Lafitte and his band helped out but the real star of the battle was the artillery that decimated the British troops.  Mostly this is just a big field with some signs along with a few historical sites and the graveyard.  My dad is a big history buff and he brought me out here often when I was a kid.  I haven't had a chance to check out the new visitor's center.

This is nice dive and diner ambiance joint serving up breakfast and New Orleans and American Diner classics.  Their hamburger steak and onion rings are quite nicely done with the hamburger steak seeming more meatloaf style.  Their seafood gumbo is well provided with ample seafood and has a good flavor.  You order and pay at the register so for drink refills you have to go back up to the counter.  Overall this is a decent spot for a casual breakfast or lunch.

The location of this place is a bit challenging to find in Harahan and it certainly qualifies as a fantastic NOLA dive spot along with their next door seafood market.  The service here is very friendly and down to earth with the staff making sure that you have everything you need to enjoy your meal.  They have a large and fantastic list of appetizers that can become a meal into themselves (like the Eggplant Harahan, seared tuna, BBQ shrimp, the fried green tomatoes, and the crab cakes) and the only thing I'm not a big fan of is their seafood gumbo that they add sausage too (and that's just a personal preference that I don't like sausage in my SEAFOOD gumbo).  This place has some great raw oysters, good boiled seafood, great po boys and fried entrees.   The only bad thing about this joint is they don't have fresh brewed iced tea and only sell bottled drinks.  I've always had good experience here and everybody I've taken here has greatly enjoyed it!  Seither's video review:  https://youtu.be/wOGgdOGiFZQ

This is a place to mainly focus on the fried foods and they have an "ok" gumbo.   They used to be out in Bucktown but after Katrina they moved right off of Veteran's.  The new location certainly never has achieved the same ambiance as the old one and I never thought the food quite came back to the same quality either.  Unfortunately I just read that today they are closing for good and will be added to the "ain't there no more list" that sadly keeps growing as our old New Orleans favorites continue to fade and more nasty national chains invade to chip away at everything that makes NOLA unique and special in the world.

Wow this place provides some decent food and offers some nice Cajun music but unfortunately charges New York City/London/Zurich/Tokyo prices with $10.50 for a tiny cup of seafood gumbo being really just extortion levels of rip off.  Their Crawfish Triple Play for $29.99 is putting me in the same price range of a nice Commander's Palace weekday lunch or a great steak at a fine dining establishment.  The beers going north of $7 is also just extremely out of line with other similar restaurant venues in the area.  Overall this is just a total tourist trap rip off that will never attract a local crowd with prices like these so it will be the nearly exclusive venue of tourists.  This is a sad state of affairs as they really could get more local folks eating here and enjoying the music if they adjusted their prices anywhere near the actual market prices other similar joints charge in the area.

Swett's is one of the best meat and three joints in Nashville and they put out some fantastic food.  They have a great old Nashville vibe and their building has decades of history on the walls.  Service is cafeteria line style like many of the other local meat and three joints along with the expected rotation of daily specials.  The flavor of all the meats and vegetables I have had here have all been extremely pleasing to my senses.  They are so proud of their food here they even put their name on their china.  They also are open for dinner and they have a decent amount of parking around the place so depending on the time of day you might actually avoid the crowds.  The folks working here are really nice and give full blown classic Southern hospitality to you as you go through the line and throughout your visit.  I could literally eat here everyday for two weeks (or longer) and never get bored and be quite happy as some of this food would even put my grandma's to shame and there is such an amazing selection of items.    Overall this is a definite stop when you are in Nashville for fantastic food and great service.  Pro Tip:  Many of the other meat and three joints in Nashville close after lunch so you can actually eat lunch at another spot then have dinner at Swett's if you want to do a double feature of Nashville meat and three Nirvana.

Well I had heard that this was one of the better burger joints in Nashville (which was concerning since it is a chain) but I was sorely disappointed.  After I ordered my food and drink I quickly learned they were out of iced tea.  When I finally got my burger the mustard bottles were all empty and to top it off I was served hard and cold French fries.  The burger itself was alright but really overpriced for what it was and 5 Guys is much better.  Service just wasn't and nothing ever got done to fix anything I asked about.  The only good thing I can say about the place is that they have beer.    Overall I definitely would NOT rank this as one of the best burger joints in Nashville as I have had plenty of better burgers.  This chain got its start in Austin, TX (I used to live there) and I would also say that it would NOT rank as one of the best burger joints there either.

Currently offering breakfast and lunch along with a happy hour starting at around 3 or 5pm.  Monday to Friday they offer a changing daily plate lunch or a burger option.  This establishment used to be quite noted for its fine dining but I was informed by the staff that although dinner will be added in a few months  it is unlikely for a return to fine dining to happen here so it will be casual dining.    This place offers a great value for their food and drink.  The historic building has a great ambiance with several dining rooms along with a nice back patio.  This is a nice spot to have an event and they do rent it out.    Overall this is a low key spot to enjoy some food and drink at a great price with good service.

Nice neighborhood bar that has gone through some ownership changes of late.  They sometimes have complimentary food and always seem to have a warm happy greeting for new folks.  During my last visit a lady that has been cooking on and off at this establishment was present and had lots of interesting tales to tell (she is right behind me in the photo of me scarfing down VERY delicious and spicy chicken mac 'n cheese).  I got some of my pals that are life long Metry residents to visit here that had never even heard of the place so it still seems to be a bit of an unknown mystery space even to folks that live as near to the location as around the Metry Road.

This is a pizza joint in a Metry strip mall that has been around awhile and is many folks favorite.  It isn't my favorite but they do make alright pizza here.
