It has shuffle board, dat games and more. The brew selections are attractive to people. You can have the $10 flight with four glasses of different beer. That way you can sample 4 different beer. Small dog is allow in there. They also have outside sitting. We have shuffle board challenge from the local. We have a lot of fun there. Grace got free popcorn for munchie.

If you cannot stand the heat, don't try this restaurant. It brings the heat of spicy food to the table. I would said it is about medium Indian heat. The keyword is "Indian heat". You know it is spicier than normal medium spicy.   When they have a word biryani in the restaurant which mean special Indian mixed curry rice. This type of food is normally seen in Muslim India, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Iran, Iraq, Kenya, Kuwait, and more. It is very colorful rice and some with meat like chicken, goat or beef.   The buffet here is a bit expensive. It does have the good veggies section with at least 10 choices. The meat section has 8 choices. It Clyde tandoori chicken, biryani chicken, curry chicken and more. The price is rather above average among the area located which is USF.   I like the sweet Mango Kesari. It is good dessert. The service is good. It worth the money.

I think about 3.5 stars. Mainly is the price and the offer of the material are not measure up. My review is only focused on the shave ice. Not the drink. The drink may be speak differently. But shave ice is at the high side in compare to the same area cafe along the Park Blvd.   We have the strawberry shave ice. Any topping will be additional cost. Which make this an expensive item for the initial price. We did add the rainbow jelly. The ice already has the flavor before they shave it. This is typical Taiwanese ice making process. It is delicious.   The place is popular now. May be they need to think about some offer now to keep the customers coming. If they do it, it will last a bit longer.

This restaurant we have came a few time I finally have a chance to try it. The first time we are here they have close during the day of the week, second time was too busy. The third time we finally have a chance to try their happy hour menu. Love it.   We started with Moroccan Spice Wing. The marinated or seasoning is special. Wing is good. The second dish is the tuna tartare. The tuna is fresh and well sauce. The wonton skin is crispy to accommodate the tuna. The third dish is the creole style crab cake. This dish has good meat burn side of crab cake. I like this method better. The quantity is small. The last item is the Korean St. Louis Rib. This dish I like the most. The rib is well prepared. Perfectly grilled. The sauce is beautifully done.   Overall our experience is great. Love the food. Chef has good technique on grilled. Very good use of sauce. Definitely like to try other things in the menu. The construction on the street make it difficult to get to.

I would said this restaurant is in the middle of the pack. May be their high star rating is due to the local favorite. The restaurant is located on the corner of the plaza. It also serves sushi. They no longer take yelp 15% off coupon.   We started with the Tom yum chicken soup. It has some flavor of Thai but not strong enough. Soup a bit salty. We have the chicken satay appetizer. I think this is their best dish. The entree we have pad Thai. I think they can do a better job on this one. The peanut sauce is not a lot. The noodle is ok. We also got the drunken noodle that not in the menu. But I am disappointed for not spicy enough when I have order the Thai hot. Second, they noodle in the wok seem like just a small BTU technique which I can do it at home. If I order this in restaurant, I expect high BTU wok with burn oil cooking. I cannot find it here. The last dish is the duck basil. The duck is filet. The dish is sweet. I would said is a ok dish.   Overall my experience is average. The dishes are  too Americanize. They need to paid attention to customers requests of how spicy the dish. Chef technique need to improve. I would said is take out quality.

Yelping 1900. Authentic Cultural Food No. 47. Center East Chinese Cuisine  This restaurant use to call Tao Asian Fusion. Recently has changed their name. The menu is also changed. This restaurant basically has Shandong and Peking cuisine. Very close to Szechuan cuisine. This area of China eat slightly different from other side of country. Since it is at the capital, the cuisine includes many area of China due to dynasty dining.   I like many items in the menu and the special of the day. It has an attractive menu. We got the sautéed pig kidney. The chef is skillful not to let the ingredients over cook. It is nice to see to serve this dish right. Our next dish is the beef noodle with pickle veggies. The beef is marinated and braised for some time.   We also got the fish with black bean sauce. This black bean sauce with chili is a nice combination. The fish is fried with whole fish no head. So you need to skill eater to order this dish. Our last entree is the Dong Po Pork. I love this dish when they prepared correctly. This is Pork belly with skin and braised in sweet sauce. It need to be braised over time to soften the tough skin and meat. Which they have done that. I would recommend this dish if you come to visit.   We order the beef pie from the special menu. It is special street food category. If they carry this dish. Order the pork pie. Overall experience is excellent. Enjoy the good cooking. We have been back twice.

Just like to agree with the rest of Yelper. 4 stars. It is good to have their weekday specials. It is $3.95 a roll. The special is about six pieces per roll. They also has the weekend special for 50% off on the second roll. The week end special are specialty roll.   The decorations of the restaurant is contemporary. I would give them a good effort for the bathroom details. During the lunch time, not too many people. We order the spicy tuna, spicy yellow tails, spicy scallops, Tampa roll, eel avocado, and the Boston roll. The food is good. The spicy scallops has the most tasty flavor.   Food is fresh. It take 15 minutes for six roll to make. The important is the rice. They do have the right ideal about the rice seasoning. It right amount of rice. Close out is good.

Rubio is a nicely presented new fast food with actually a comfort food of America with Mexican background. Are they true authentic Mexican food, probably not. But I can said it is fusion Mexican food.   We have order the Coastal Trio and Salsa Verde Shrimp two taco plate. It is order on the counter and the food bring to the table. The grilled fish and shrimp are average. Yes, they show grilled mark but grilled technique should be have smoke flavor or grilled mark burn meat flavor. The fried fish is good.   The main reason they are average is the food is a big blend. However they have good interior decoration. Place is very clean may be they still new. Salsa is more in liquidity stage instead of chop up process. This tell you fast food process because it is easy to produce liquid than chop up.

The restaurant location has been through many other types of restaurant before today Mediterranean Cuisine. I wish they doing well since they do have good food. Winning the support of the customers is important. Such as doing something different than other Mediterranean cuisine restaurant typically do. One improvement can be done definitely has all dinner or meal with multi sides to accompany. Currently they allow one side which I feel to little and not comparable to the near by restaurant has done.   I have chicken kabab and the lamb chop dinner. The chicken kabab I choose the baba ghanoush. The Baba ghanoush was delicious. The chicken was grilled with juicy meat and marinated sauce. It is a good dish to have. The lamb chop I have choose the yellow rice. The lamb chop was very nicely done. As I said above, for the price they have, they may want to include another side.

It one of good seafood place in Dunedin. This restaurant is about 4.5 stars. The reason they stay at 4 stars due to service during lunch time. They have one waiter and reception for the afternoon. I can see 6 table of customers but not enough waitress. Obviously this is a balancing act for the restaurant if they need to spend more overhead.   With that said. The food are excellent. 5 stars. We started with fried crab crawl. This is special of the day. $12 for about 20 crawls. The crawl is fresh with great coating. Love it.   Our main dish is oyster poboy and the blackened hogfish. They give a lot of oyster at the poboy. The oyster are great. My friend was not able to finish and take home. The hogfish blackened is ok. Not like the Cajun style. But the fish meat is good and tasty. It is good sandwich.   Overall experience is good. Hope they continue the good food.

Today the YBOR City have the 3rd annual snow parrade. We decided for dinner before the parade.   This restaurant is kind of away from the center attraction of the YBOR. It located at the 5th Ave and 17th Street. Two Avenue from central YBOR.   This is Argentina restaurant. They must have done their churrasco correctly. I have order a  baby churrasco and my wife have Mar Y Tierra (surf and turf). While we waiting for the food, we can see across building with the kitchen that pounding the steak.   Mar Y Tierra came with three grill shrimp, grill skirt steak low grade with a lot of tender. It also  has side rice and side salad. The shrimp is marinated and grill with perfection. The skirt steak also marinate and grill. This dish is yummy for the shrimp and the steak is tasty. No complain for the price of this dish $18.   The baby churrasco is 8 oz compare to the full churrasco 22oz. The price different is $10. Since I just want to taste the strip cut of the churrasco, I order a baby. When the steak came out, it is a whole piece like my wife dish not like the strip size cut. This is incorrect. It have a lot tendon. I did not say anything because I think this may be the way they have prepare it. So I have finish it. Then my neighbor table order the full portion and I can see there is different of the meat - strip size churrasco not like the flat piece. The correct churrasco should a strip cut no tendon. They should not use the word "churrasco" if they not serve you the Falda cut in Spanish. I am agree the seasoning for the taste is there but the meat material quality is not there. Argentine should know their meat.   The other thing is the waiter did not ask me how is my steak to be prepared and they came out well done. It was too late to change. The waiter also not attentive. My glass of the water was empty for long time and not come to refill. This restaurant waiter need to be trained.   With the above experience, I have to give them 2 star.

4.5 stars restaurant. Not yet 5 stars to my book. This restaurant has plus at back of the name. This mean they beyond just poke only. The restaurant also has the Vietnamese cuisine. So you can get poke and cook meal. I got best of both worlds.   I start with mixed poke. I got the base as rice and protein as tuna. They are generous for one scoop of protein. This is why they have 5 stars. I got all the mixed in ingredients and topping that have have no up charge. The sauce are poke sauce, eel and special ask for sesame oil. It was really good for mixed in. I would pre them to do mixed in ingredients and protein separately than added into the base then add topping. But they don't have this procedure. They do put the sauce over base then on top of mixed in ingredients. This area they can improve.   We also got the combination pho and grilled pork bun. Their Vietnamese side food also delicious. The grilled pork is well marinated and their pho is deep with herb smell.

#ThankYouThursday.   I have chosen Terra Gaucha for today visit for lunch dine in experience. Thank you for hanging there during pandemic. I think your restaurant has good high ceiling dining hall. No doubt the great Brazilian Grille in Tampa Bay Area. We were lucky to have you. Interior design is great. Good place for power lunch and bring the the client.   With that said. This is place for meat. Love it. Buffet style. People may be afraid of close contact because of buffet. Thank you to make it safer for people come to the table. Before each individual come to the buffet booth, each one need to put on the hand gloves. So the share spatula is not touch. The buffet table already have partial cover on top. But I think more cover or complete lid cover is better. We saw a few completely cover such as soup item is very good.   The meat bring to the table is well perform. Server wear gloves and mask. Definitely great to visit. Keep serving our community and we are looking forward to see you again.

Very close to 4.5 stars restaurant. I would said they are good enough in this area. In fact, they are better than most of the Japanese restaurant which serves by non Japanese chef. I believe many enjoy the food once they have the sashimi.   Restaurant is kind of tuck away in the plaza. Not visible to the Main Street. We got bento box special and the Arizona roll. We are kind of in hurry for a movie but we didn't tell them so. However, the speed of the serving, we were able to finish at 35 minutes.   I like my bento box. It has sashimi, sushi, California roll, goyoza, teriyaki chicken, tempura shrimp and veggies. Accompanying with salad and soup. I like the way they prepared the sashimi. The fish was glazed with sesame oil. Nice touch. The temperature is crispy and evenly spread of flour. I like they special made goyoza. The infill include meat and scallions. Very nice. All fish is in good size.   Overall very good experience.

Old Navy definitely is the most like by many people. Their clothing are made to American style and widely accepted by general population. Their price of the clothing is affordable that welcome by many consumer. This is one of my wife favorites store just to shop. May be she can find something she like.   It was always easy for us to visit when we have extra time before the cinema show. They very close to the cinema. It is obvious visit for close proximity. There have their fashion statement to fit the typical people who looking for.

It an interesting local produce place. The location of the store is actually close to the county line but not at county line. It is one street south of the county line at Hillsborough County.   They have good piece of farm property at Lutz. It is large enough for the farm, building and food truck. The entrance may need some fixed up for the big hole cumulate the rain water.   The produce they have is one of the kind. Basically have fresh veggies, home made drink, olive oil, soft drink and more. I got the cane soda. This cola made from sugar cane water. It is interesting. Their fresh fruit are store at the refrigerator to maintain freshness. This is the place I saw sell fresh blackberry juice.

Solid 4 stars. Very close to 4.5 stars. If they have more creative side, they probably 5 stars. This take out BBQ place is Riverview jewels. Many come here for the pickup food. The peach cobbler should not be miss. This is the item I recommend.   We have the family meal deal with three meat types and 3 sides and a peach cobbler as a deal. The meat are ribs, chicken and pulled pork. The best is the rib. I like the way the have the rib with seasoning stick to the surface. The sons is the chicken. The sides we have is the yellow rice, garlic potatoes and collard greens. The best is the garlic potatoes.   The deal is good for $25. It is in good quantity. The wait is good to order on side. Many call in. The smoke house just right outside.

Currently the restaurant are not open for public to dine in. It is takeout only. In order to attract customers and regularity, they push out several rewards systems. They have clover points system. 50 point cumulative got the free peach pudding with milk. 100 point got Tao Beef Burrito, 200 point spicy chicken and 300 whole grilled fish. Basically is 10% off item you cumulative as point.   The also run weekly half price promotions. Currently is the grilled lamb leg half price. You can choose spicy or salt and pepper. I prefer the salt and pepper. It is delicious. Other item include dong Po pork belly, fiery shrimp are among the best. You should try those dishes. The lunch special is comparable with and fast food outside with great value. It also includes a soft drink and make the deal sweet with about $8. Can beat that.   Call ahead is the key. They usually need 20 minutes to prepare. Food are very nicely seasoned and go with wine at home. Are you hungry now.

About 4.25 stars. This newly added location is similar to the one at River View. But I think they are better location in compare to the one they have in River View. I like open space compare to restaurants that previously here.   We were here since we know their sister company at the south. I have the Spaghetti Ortolano with grilled shrimp. I kind of changed the protein on this dish. It turn our very well. The ingredients included pine nuts, green bean, asparagus, broccoli, tomato. This pasta dish is harmony to go with grilled shrimp. We also got the Chicken Parmesan with pasta. The chicken is breaded. Both dishes are excellent.   The food is on time. We were lucky to beat the Sunday lunch crowd. Not much of wait. The restaurant filled up in 30 minutes. So go early on Sunday.

I have been to this house two year ago close to Christmas. The owner always has the fun to set up the Christmas light and attract a lot of visitors. The entrée is free but suggest for donations to keep up the cost.    The whole front yard is cover with Christmas light. They have good nativity scene with arc light over it. The trees is completely wrapped with light. Giant size snow man blow with air. Bubble fill with sky. Charles Stanley preached the sermon. These is the few set they do. The model train section with amusement park has a lot of moving part. The section with light show is dancing.  I like their North Pole penguin set up.   There many photo spot opportunity. We took many of that. They even have people direct the traffic to keep vehicles moving. Street side parking is available.

This food truck located a the empty land. The entrance is from Old SR 54 not the Wesley Chapel Blvd.  the map may take you at non entrance way. They do have pepinos, patacone, cachapa and more. Is is Venezuelan food. Price is at the high side.   I got the carne mechada (shredded beef). It look beautiful. The beef is a lot. I also like the fried patacone. It was crispy. The Venezuelan cheese is delicious. The sauce was well made.   From order to finish is about 10 minutes. I don't mind the wait to get the freshly fried patacone.

Review #2900. Rare ethnic food #70. Iraqi Cuisine.   This review go to our local unique restaurant. I have many Middle Eastern food but this one is different. If you come to visit, I would suggest get the Iraqi Masgouf fish dish. The restaurant has very interesting meat dish in the menu. All food is interesting.   We got the Iraqi Masgouf. This dish is not cheap but it has good quantity and quality. The entire come with marinated grilled fish. The side dish have Fries, green chili, butter bread, two mixed veggies, and more. The fish is delicious with bone. The other dish we have is the  dolce ribeye steak. This dish we select the rice. I like the spice up rice. The steak was well marinated. It is tasty to the bone.   The restaurant has a yellow bird. It sing for us while we are eating. The chai tea is complimentary. The soup was special complimentary. We got the lentil and the okra soup. Service is good. Love to eat there for good food. The bread is special with their own made butter.

Cinco De Mayo weekend, our office pick this restaurant to have the lunch before the week is over. This restaurant is hidden at temple terrace in a small plaza. If I don't have yelp, I would not have found it.   They have $5 lunch special and margarita special. I have order one margarita and it come with 32 oz glass. Giant glass!!! It almost cannot fit my face. I have asked the help from my friend to take a sip.   I have ordered the steak quesadilla, it come with lettuce and tomato. The steak is stir fried in flour taco. It is decent. Taste is good. I have added a dessert at the end with fried dough with cinnamon, powder sugar and honey.   Service is friendly, food came out fast, the atmosphere is great. This is about 3.5 stars restaurant. Please check them out. Definitely a very budget lunch.

A little above 4 stars. Because of the good flavors. They located at Seminole Height. Parking is at the side street. The seating is limited at interior but they do have the courtyard seating share with the chicken place next door.   They have vegan or veggies bowl. We got the surf and turf bowl. It is included the grilled shrimp and steak. I like it they cook your order. They grilled the steak right when you order it. Good seasoning to the steak and shrimp. The choices of the topping is by yourself. I like the broccoli and Brussels sprouts. Our base is the noodle. Every thing is great. Even the sauces are creative to be added on.   Not much service. The workers there are very friendly with a smile. Love the food and we will be back to try other item. A+ on the seasoning and the sauce accompanying it.

This is brand new Brazilian Steakhouse. It is a chain restaurant with well train staff to get this restaurant run smoothly at the first month. The lunch is cheaper than the dinner. The all you can eat steak also includes all you can eat buffet for other miscellaneous items.   The steak is awesome. Especially I like the lamb chop, chicken heart, skirt steak, top sirloin. All steak is well seasoning. Especially the chicken heart and chicken drum stick. The chicken drum stick is marinated in wine sauce. Very delicious. There are wave and wave of meat to cut. They also bring out big giant leg of lamb.   During this time on the brand new opening, they have 10% off the bill. On the buffet table, they have heart of palm, Smoke salmon, caramel mushrooms and more.   Tip - don't forget to ask for the steak sauce such chimichuri, hot sauce, mint jelly to go with steak and lamb chop.   Service is excellent. These include the speed, attention to detail, clean up, and frequently check on the table. Definitely 5 stars.

Yummy House is alway to go restaurant. My recent visit drop a stars. Mainly is the taste and quantity. They still hold good menu selections. But I think the menu is reduced items. During pandemic and inflation, the price did increase by 20%.   The main reason they deducted a stars from my previous review is the quantity of the protein is reduced and the price increase. They no longer the most economical restaurants. You can tell the customer also reduced during dinner time. Lunch time is still a lot of customers especially weekends due to dim sum.   I also feel their best chefs is no longer here. Food taste is a bit less than their branch at Ocala.

Kao Thai is in my bookmark for a while. Finally I have a chance to visit the restaurant. The restaurant is well decorated. I like the clothing napkin setup on the table like bold tide. They have different menu. One is their regular menu and the other is the Thai street food menu.   We Thee dishes from the Thai Street Menu. The first dish is the Yum Nam Kao Tod. This is salad dish with sausage, crispy curry rice that fried, peanut. To me, this dish is salty and sour to be eat along. The second dish is Hoy Tod. It s a mussels egg pancake and bean sprouts. It come with the dipping sweet chilies sauce. I like this dish. The third dish is my favorite. Kao Kook Ka Pi. This dish has seven combination items in one dish. The item I like the most is shrimp paste fried rice. I have this as Malay dish. But they carry it. This is the first I have in Tampa Bay. The dish also includes the caramelize pork belly, Thai sweet sausage, egg, onion, apple and string bean. It is well presented.   Overall our experience is good. I really want to come back to try their main menu dish. This restaurant is about 4.5 stars since each dish is well decorated.

Rare Authentic Food #38 - Florida own seasoning crab.   I am surprised Nick and Tina did not smell this one out since both of them love crab. This restaurant now is my number one store to go finger food for crab. It is king of the crab store. Best ever. If you want some finger food during this football season, this will be the one if you don't mind to get down dirty with finger for limited crab meat.   Today I got two types of crab. The garlic crab and fried crab. Both of them are excellently exceedingly my expectations. The garlic crabs are finger licking good. 3 crab for $7.50. I also got the seasoning fried crab for $11. Man!!! Those are good. The seasoning is deeeeeeeeep into the crab since the crab is minorly crack to allow the seasoning get into the crab meat. They have other item. But I think you should concentrate on the crabs.   Am I coming back. Hell yes!!!! Love the food. By the way this is just a take out store. You can order 15 minutes ahead so it won't be any wait. The crab is fresh. The fried crab is normally bigger than garlic crab. There is not sit down area. Only carry out.

Oh well, this is average among the restaurant over here. Marrow do have some Americans cuisine. However, what I take for this restaurant may not measure to the value you paid while other restaurant may be do better than them.   We were here to try their food first time. We have the Tavern 'slammin' steak sandwich. With upgrade side to grilled asparagus it is close to $20 dish. I expect this should be smashing dish. It turn out the meat is is just few cold cut on hot bun. I have give them with nice skirt steak. But it is cold cut. The upgrade asparagus only come in 4 strings.   The second dish is better. The chicken stack. It is grilled. Also about same price I have for steak sandwich. In compare to near by restaurant, I think the nearby restaurant may be better. I know the competition is tough. But I think they can do better.   Our service is good. Just some time they waitress not paid the highest attention to our table during meal. But when get paid, it was quick.

For the BBQ they are about middle of the pack in Tampa. Their combo compare to many place they are right portion not the generous portion.   We got the combo package with collard greens and sweet corn as side. The main meat is the hog feed and the rib and brisket. The hog feed is the pull pork. I think the rib is better. Brisket is just good. We also got the pork sandwich. Their food is good but not to jump out the seat.   Price is a bit in the expensive side. May be create something attractive to the side items will attract more business. I do like the choice of the sauce. We got the mango sauce and the guava sauce. It is interesting.

This is the restaurant we have visited sometime ago and finally I have sometime to write about it. Havana 86 is the restaurant may be open during pandemic. We visited two months ago. I like the restaurant because it has good Cuban cuisine. Especially this area has already many Cuban restaurants close. I am happy they open their door.   We started with Tostones Rellenos - stuff fried green plantain. We got the stuffing at lobster. It comes with 5 pieces and delicious to share. For the main course, we have Vaca Frita and Churrasco ala Cubana. The vaca frita can be a little crispy by pan grilled longer. The skirt steak is delicious.   Overall the food is good. It is close to 4.5 stars. Price is affordable. Hopefully they keep it this way. Service is ok nothing jump out.

If you come drink is good. If you come for food, this may not a good choice. World of beer surprise me that they serve food. However, the food come out of the kitchen is too slow. Menu do not have good choices.   I got one of the special mojito. But I feel the cocktail is too light on the alcohol percentage. The drink feel like soft drink. Unless you go with their draft beer or bottle beer. Other than that, I not recommend their cocktails.   We order three tacos for snacks, it take 30 minutes to come out. I think this area need big improvement. The shrimp taco save them one stars. If not it is 2.5 stars.

It is about 3.5 stars. The lobster is definitely better quality than most lobster roll I have. They do have body meat not like most restaurants mainly crawl meat and the body sold to other dish. The preparation is butter lobster. I actually like this way better because you can taste the freshness of the lobster.   They have three different size of the roll. 2 oz to 4 oz selection. You also go to mega roll foot long with 10oz to share. They also has the lobster fried or Macaroni to try. Other than lobster, hot, burger, fish sandwich also available.   The truck just park outside. You can order the inside the brewery and they will give you a wait table. Food is great. I would said a good lobster roll in Tampa. I would suggest at least 3 oz roll.

I would said above average restaurant. This is local favorite restaurant which get a high review. The choice of the restaurants are not much in Wesley Chapel. I would said they are one of the better one in this area.  We have the mixed grilled, lamb pita, and the appetizer. The appetizer has some sour material in it to create the appetite. This is a good start. The mixed grilled is decent. Meat may need a bit more heavy seasoning. It can improve the meat by sealing the juice of the meat.   I saw the price range has went up since other people review not long ago. They have been adjusting their pricing quite often. They are getting with competing with Greek fast food chain may lose this batter since they are in very remote area with less customer traffic. I would said for the current value, they are about 3.5 stars.

A good barrier island food off the Pinellas county gulf coast. Rick is look like back to normal after pandemic. The customer come back to enjoy the mixed cocktails and food. It is St. Pete beach area restaurant. I pick this place after my visit to my project.   I order the grilled grouper sandwich. It come with the side. And I got the deep corn on the cob. I have not have a deep fried corn in Florida. I have deep fried corn once at New Orlean. The corn is very delicious. I recommend this side order if you come here. The outward of the corn has apply a layer of salty coating. It match the corn sweetness. The grouper is fresh. Seem like fresh catch of the day. My friend has a he shrimp pasta. He like it and finish the entire bowl.   Overall the service is good. I did not try their cocktails. But the food is good and has some unique item.

This Kung Fu tea is in the middle of the pack. We got the coffee slush with boba and the winter melon milk tea. I agree with Vivian that they need to improve the mixologist of the tea. Somehow it do not have the taste of harmony. The ingredients is good. The honey boba is still very good. But the the tea bitterness need to tone down. Caffeine is well maintained but the the tea bitterness somehow need to reduce. Milk is a bit heavy compare to many milk tea I have tasted.   This restaurant has token ramen section. We did not try their food this time. But will plan next visit to try their hot food. I like the open kitchen with glass wall allow the customers see their food preparation. It has increased the interest of the food.

Yelping 1400 - Rare Ethic Food # 41  This one go to the local restaurant which is unique in many way. This Turkish kitchen offer many items I have never seen before. It is amazing to try them all. I would recommend friends to try this restaurant which is extremely good.   To begin, we start with oven baked Hummus with added Turkish sausage. This hummus is mixed with mozzarella. This dish come with lavash bread. This is my first time have this dish. It is huge bread. The bread blow up is actually made up of hot air trap inside that bigger than my head. It is interesting.   The main dishes include Levrek- Whole Mediterranean Sea  Bass. The fish is grilled. I like the crispy fish skin with the marinated sauce. The fish is fresh and great to enjoy. The second dish is Pirzola - marinated grilled lamb chop. It come with 4 chops. Very good flavor.   We end the night with special dessert. The Kunefe is one of the specialty of the night. It is string type Filo Dough stuff with cheese and sugar syrup. It was interesting to pull them apart. String dough make the this dessert unimaginable delicious.   Overall this is solid five stars restaurant. Good service.

There are so many poke place pop up lately. This is second poke island I have seen. I like it particularly is their choices of the protein. They have something that other poke place do not offer. The protein has eel, Tempura shrimp, tomago, squid. These items is not normally serve.   They have served a Yummy sauce which is spicy sesame is lovely. Mixed it with eel and poke sauce will make this perfect. I would said one part of yummy and poke sauce and two part of eel sauce is the way I like it. It you don't want it sweet, just use one part of eel sauce. I like the way they have the sauce on the rice first then pile all ingredients and sauce on the top. To make better, I would suggest sauce and ingredients mixed and put over rice. Then topping. This will increase the best taste.   Price is good. But more protein did not mean you get more food. I would suggest that more protein with more food.

Flames Indian Restaurant is one of the up coming Indian cuisine at south Tampa. The cuisine does tone down a bit for the local American. It is still maintained a good spice mixture that represents the Indian cuisine. The decorations of the restaurant is nice. While we eating there, there are some local come to pickup the take out.   We have the Phatthar Gosht Ka Saalan. It is a lamb dish from Hyderabadi Cuisine. This dish to me the spice is enough. However I think missing the heat of the spiciness. It has s still delicious.   I like the most is the Chicken Chettinad. It is a classic chettinad dish with great flavor. I like the sophisticated of the spice. It is great dish to go with rice.   Both dishes is good. Portion is a bit small. Service at the restaurant is good. If you not use to the spicy Indian foods, this may be a good choice. They do have good taste.

One of my best restaurant list in the Bay Area. I have been to this place many time and decide to give the a full review. The restaurant originally start at the Water Ave Armenia location. Then they build the Bistro at this location (Hillsborough Ave). Then they have open the Gainesville and Sarasota. I have been to all of them except the newly open restaurant in Ocala.   They have consistence tasting through out these locations. Tonight we have long distance friend visit us and we decide to take them here. Since tonight is January 1 no reservation. Usually the weekend and holiday they don't take reservation. We have waited 30 minute for our table. We have order the sizzling ginger scallion frog leg, crab and fish maw soup, steam snapper with ginger and soy source, duck raisin fried rice and the grouper egg plant hot pot and the appetizer of scallop in salt and pepper. The salt and pepper scallop is wet coated with flour and deep fry then stir fry with Garlic, pepper and salt. They did not over coat the ingredient and make the scallop soft inside. This is a delicious appetizer.   We have the main dishes of the raisin duck fried rice. The duck is roasted and the meat is chop in small pieces and stir fry with raisin, egg and long grain rice. The fry rice is fantastic. The egg and fish maw soup has make a good use of ingredient to create the flavor of the soup. Add an hint of red vinegar and white pepper, it will enhance the taste. The sizzling fog leg is a bit down today. The frog leg is coated and deep fried. However the chef make the coating too thick today. Usually they are good thin coating to keep the leg meat intact and stir fry with ginger and scallion source. The steam fish is perfect with fresh snapper and ginger in soy source and sesame oil. We have two pounder fish. We also have the egg plant and grouper hot pot. The egg plant is cook in the fish source and use the hot pot to braise and soften the egg plant fiber. The mix of grouper the the egg plant is a pleasant dish to eat.   Overall we are very satisfy with our meal and service. I wish they allow reservation to make the the restaurant more attractive.

It is good Italian restaurant at Dale Mabry. One thing make them high stars rating is their food. Good choices of menu selection. Sauce is great. Presentation of the fish also nice. We were here for the dinner. The interior is nice with wide open dining hall. One thing can improve is the seat cushion of the booth need to resurface because when we seat, the seat cushion is sink.   I have the scallops sambuca. The dish come with 4 big seared sea scallops. The pasta is the bow tie pasta. The sambuca sauce was accompanied well. The pasta also includes the shredded bacon. The dish is big with take home for next day. My wife has branzino of the sea. It is Mediterranean Sea bass. The fried the whole fish with checked score. It allow the interior of the fish fully fried. They also give a thought to stand the fish on the spinach bed and plum tomatoes. It is well presented. By standing the fish instead lay flat. It allows both side of the fish fully crispy while eating.   The pre-meal includes garlic rolls. It has good garlic butter oil on top. Our service is good. Our food definitely impressive. Love to come back for more.

It is about 4.5 stars. Onur is part market and part restaurant. This is a Turkish market for item like Turkish delight and all the Turkish goods such as tunas jam, coffee, spices, flour, marinated steak and more.   We got some of the cookies and milk drinks mixed and a kabab to go. We have the chicken kabab and it comes with veggies. You will not believe the kabab is good. Love the juicy chicken kabab.   The menu of the restaurant was easy to select. The price is affordable in compare to full middle eastern restaurants. The kabab was prepared in ten minutes. In compare to restaurants I usually waited for half hours. This is the plus to prepare the food quick and quality.

This Bento has great setup among many Bento I have been to. Set up is very nice with indoor or outdoor dining. The elevated outdoor concrete floor serve a very good view and away from the vehicles.   I have sushi box with yellowtail caliente roll and salmon roll. It come with California roll, goyoza, salad and spicy cucumber pickles. This bento box is fresh and good. The food do improve a lot from old day. My wife have bento box of chicken katsu. The chicken was two flat pieces. It also accompanied with noodle and brown rice. The salad and wonton skin also includes in the box.   There is not much of service. It is order at the counter and bring a number to your table. Food was delivered by your number.

Very close to 4.5 stars. This restaurant has potential. Newly open. It give good quantity of food. It is upscale fast food with good flavor. Menu is easy understanding. A three step process to select what you want.   First step is to choose the your entree. This includes burritos, quesadilla, bowl, taco. Next step is to choose your protein, it includes different types of chicken, pork, steak or ground beef, shrimp. Base on type of protein will determine the price of the items. Next step to choose your add on. They have good choices. I got the steak quesadilla. The add on was delicious. It take 10 minutes to prepare my thick quesadilla. It has good cheese. My wife have BBQ pork. The bowl is huge with add on. She like the taste of it.   Overall I said it is good value for the food we have. I like the good thick quesadilla. Enough steak in it. Good grilled steak.

This is our second stop happy hour restaurant. Malio is restaurant near Curtis Hixon park. If you happen to be there, you may want to check on their happy hour from 3 to 7 pm Tuesday to Friday. Their happy hour food item is great.   I start with their high west old fashioned. It is a double Rye whiskey. It has some kick into it. Good deal at happy hour. Our selection for the appetizers begins with filet tips it was grilled very well. Good to share with friend. Our next appetizer is Ahi Tuna Tartare. It serve with wonton chip and pickles ginger. Tuna was good. Our last appetizer is the Shrimp Theresa. It is grilled shrimp with ponzu crispy outside. I like this appetizer the best. It come as six pieces.   Overall we enjoy our time here. Service is good. Parking at the building is $6 if you want to park close. They do have coupons but still need to pay $6 for parking. I think it defeated the coupon.

My friend have a surgery here which give me an opportunity to visit this hospital. I was not aware of this hospital is located in the middle of south Tampa. It is convenient for the south Tampa residents to visit their love one if they need a surgery. I would suggest any short duration of surgery should be close to home. It allow immediate family care without traveling abroad.   This hospital is rather nice because there was plenty of parking space for visitors. Their park is just a walking distance. The hospital keep clean and comfortable for the patients. The recovery room for overnight stay is good. The only thing is need a bit of visitors chair. I am guessing most recovery room due to short duration stay, the room is designed for patients and family. They don't want a party in the hospital due to many visitors.

100 Montaditos is actually 100 items of montaditos. It is the bun with the tapas item insert. This is new concept chain restaurant from Spain. The first store in the bay area is start at the Wire Grass Mall. We have been here two nights and finally I can gather the fact for this review.  I won't say I have tried each of items but I have enough for the general ideal of the concept. Although they have 100 different montaditos but their main ingredient as follow: Serrano ham, chorizo (sausage slice), salchichon (cure sausage), Lomo (dry cure pork-best item), Chistorra (basque sausage slice), tortilla, meatball, shrimp, tuna, philly steak, blue cheese, mozzarella, ground beef patty, hot dog, chicken, BBQ pull pork, garlic pork lion (one of the best), brie cheese, goat cheese, smoked salmon, anchovies. With this combination, they created the 95 items. The remaining 5 are the deserts. Although they have two different bun and the cost start at $1 to $3. The best pick are the Serrano ham, Lomo, Garlic Pork Lion. The manchego cheese is the 3 month cure cheese from Spain is also available. They have bigger platter such as calamari, croquette, and chicken wing. You also can order the cured meat alone.  For the visit, the new opening attracts lot of customer during the lunch and dinner time. When they don't have line, it is best to order as little as possible to keep the food warm. Then order the next item as you need. Every Wednesday all the montaditos is $1. I feel that we have too much bun by the time we have finish the meal. Although they are filling but do not give me the sensation as Tapas. The service is great. The team of the waiter and waitress is almost like the bee group that work around you.

Our experience is about two and half stars. Below are some of the reasons why. First. The food did not sit well in the stomach. I have to go to bathroom twice. After almost $70 of food. I expect it to be high quality. Some how it has not meet the standard may be we are the early crow at 5 pm. Second, the soup is part of the all you can eat but the machine is broken, the soup is regular room temperature. I think this should be be prepared and ready all time. Third. Many time the waitress forget to bring our order. And the table was not check regularly and the 18% tip is added due to we have large crowds.   With that said. We enjoy our time there. Since we we have a large table. We were able to divide our group to different categories grilled or order. It was fun to grill with a group. It is not good for two people to be here. I would said need 3 or more person in order to enjoy it. More is the best.   One best thing is they have good ventilation in the restaurant. It is a plus. But still smell food after you walk out from the restaurant. I would suggest not wear any expensive clothes or leather product includes your hand bag. Because the food smell will stick.

If you like quality food, then you will like Turchetti's!  I went to the grand opening and was fortunate to get there just before the lunch rush.  It's located within the former "Marrow" space, so parking is limited to street parking in the area.  Inside, there is a window processing area at the front, and once you get into the main area, the order counter/cooler/bar are on the left side; the two-top tables are in the middle; and the 4-top tables are on the right with the curing meats in a windowed room beyond those.  While waiting to place my order, I noticed the menu boards for sandwiches, burgers, and sides posted above the cooler filled with packaged meats to go.  I picked up a pack of beef franks and one of beef summer sausage.    I was welcomed by the cashier who explained a few things to help make the visit informed.  I started with a double order of N'Duja Deviled Eggs (they come as half eggs) and went with the Pastrami (Reuben).  They also have a variety of beverages including Pepsi products, sparkling water, and a few beer selections.  After paying, they gave me a card to place on my table so that the server could bring out my order.  After a brief wait, the eggs were delivered.  Wow! The flavor was great.  I ate each half like it was an amuse bouche.  The yolks were flavored and though I can't tell you all the ingredients, the creamy texture and the light bite of the egg white added to the layered flavor (definitely an hint of vinegar & mustard seed).  They aren't filling and are worth a taste.  The Pastrami was delivered soon after and was excellent!  The rye was lightly crisped for that satisfying crunch.  Inside, they have the pastrami layered with Swiss cheese and "gardenkraut" topping and a bit of 1000 Island dressing for more flavor.  Simply delicious and it paired well with my Central State IPA.    The only negative I had was that the place was getting quite busy since it was opening day and the line was backing up.  I think once the cashier doesn't have to take time to answer a lot of questions about the place due to all the new customers, things out to go more quickly.  Still, the line was moving pretty well while I was there...maybe 5 minutes from door to placing your order.  Review #1265

New Day has been serving meads and ciders in Fountain Square for about seven years.  So, I thought it about time to stop in and see what I was missing.  The shotgun style shoppe has a serving room in the front and a gathering place/gallery in the back half.  The serving room is lined with tables on the left.  The right side is made up of a display area for merchandise and a long bar area that has blackboards for upcoming events, beverages, and menu items to enjoy while sipping your drinks.  Since it was my first time here, I went with a flight (6 selections for $8).  They hand you a flyer that you can fill out and indicate your selections.  On the back is a listing of custom cocktails that are available made from the house beverages.  Okay, I will admit that I had no idea what mead was other than something knights and commoners drank while roaring about their conquests.  So I asked.  Basically, it is similar to wine, but made with other fruits instead of grapes.  They can also use honey instead of sugars.  However, like craft beers, the drinks can have a variety of ingredients that can take them into a wide range of flavors.  My flight had three hard ciders and three meads.  The Gold Rush (6% ABV) is a dry, champagne like drink.  The South Cider (6%) is more of a gateway beverage for someone who is used to commercial apple ciders sans alcohol.  It is sweet with the taste of apples and honey.  I also tried the seasonal Barrel Aged JC (Johnny Chapman) that is deep in flavor due to the black strap molasses (12%).  This is a drink for those who like their drinks to kind of slap them in the face with flavor!  Surprisingly smooth, it is very complex and somewhat herbal in aftertaste.  The meads I tried had a variety of flavors.  The Washington's Folly (6%) is a cherry mead with fresh tart cherry notes.  The Shelby Blue Ribbon (6%) is made with Strawberry and Rhubarb.  The aroma of rhubarb adds to the enjoyment of this one.  My final selection is another seasonal selection called Breakfast Magpie (8%).  This is a black raspberry mead with a strong coffee (espresso) infusion.  The coffee taste is strong and dominates the raspberry flavors.  As for the rest of the business, the staff seems friendly and well informed.  The merchandise ranges from t-shirts to glasses and growlers.  There are several selections available year round, but the seasonals come in roughly each quarter, but last only as long as the supply lasts.    Overall, I really enjoyed my beverages and the experience here.  Review #251

Pancake house by day, steakhouse by night!  If you have read any of the other reviews (particularly for Gaucho Steakhouse), then you will see there have been a number of bewildered guests that have dined here.  The family that owns this brunch restaurant closes the place at 3, cleans up, and then reopens as Gaucho Brazilian Steakhouse at 5 pm.  Both restaurants use the same entrance and space, but the signs over the entrance make it look like the pancake house is on the left and the steakhouse is on the right.  Just go to the left, regardless of when you dine here.  Okay, so the space inside is not designed for clearing things up.  There are large murals on the walls celebrating breakfast and area sports teams.  And there are posters about steak as well.  The space is broken up into two shotgun style dining areas.  The one on the entrance side has a number of tables and a bar area towards the back.  The space to the right is divided by a mirrored wall that is lined with booth seating for the tables that are located there.  Pull out chairs sit on the opposite sides of the bench seating.     Anyway, I ordered my brunch selection and a bottomless cup of coffee and was generally pleased.  The "Original Benny" came with two poached eggs, a buttery Hollandaise sauce, English muffin halves, and Canadian bacon.  Pretty well executed and tasty.  On the same plate, some crisped hash browns came with the order to help mop up any of the sauce left over.  On a side plate, a colorful fresh fruit plate offered melon, red grapes, and orange slices.  The service was okay....efficient comes to mind.  Not a lot of interaction or welcoming attitude.  I could understand if it was a busy day, but the room seemed less than half full.  Overall, if you are hungry, the food is good and you just have to trust the staff to lead you to seating.  Don't over think it.  Review #503

My wife and I enjoyed good food and service in this quirky new pizza place.  I really liked the breadsticks and the Sidekicks Supreme pizza.      I was surprised to find street parking just around the corner at lunchtime on Saturday.  (Free is good!)  Anyway, we walked past two other restaurants/bars in the Action Bowl building and saw the sign/stand in front of the entrance.  (It still says Shelby in bold letters over the doorway.)  As we entered, we saw the sign to seat ourselves and our waitress noticed us and greeted us, echoing the sign to sit wherever we liked.  We chose a window seat so that we could see the fountains and people watch.    Our waitress was over promptly and maintained good service throughout our lunch.  She kept busy doing prep work while not attending us and managed to deal with carryout orders as well.  I noticed another sign that they now have Uber Delivery available.    While waiting for our food, I noticed they have pictures of sidekicks all around the restaurant. I recognized many of them. There is also a pinball game to help pass time.  A long bar is available for patrons to order one of the bottled beers or local brews (I think there were 8 on tap.)   Our breadsticks came out first.  We ordered 4 sticks which came with two choices of dipping sauces.  (Breadsticks can be ordered in 2, 4, or 6 and there are six varieties of dipping sauces to choose from).  We ordered the marinara and the nacho cheese.  The nacho cheese comes with red peppers diced into the sauce.  Both sauces were tasty and the sticks were flatter than I have had elsewhere, but that was a good thing.  They seemed to have a little more crispness than most I've tried.    Our pizza arrived and was very good!  This thin crust pie had plenty of mozzarella that stretched when I lifted each slice. The green peppers were cut large, but were cooked thoroughly, so that was a nice surprise.  Plenty of flavor.  The crust itself was crisp around the rim, but just a little soggy in the center which made it hard to pick up at first.  There was just a little grease from the pepperoni, but just enough to lick my fingers, not make a mess.  Overall, I would order this again and since there were 8 slices, I had to get a box for my leftovers.    I haven't tried their salads or sandwiches yet, but based upon my experience, I would gladly bring friends here to eat and maybe grab a brew.  Review #341  p.s.  This is the third restaurant I have been to in this location.  It is quirky here on its own, but seeing the same basic layout with new decor just adds to the oddness of the experience.

I noticed the sign for the business on the side of the building and thought I would check it out.  After all, a name like Fancy Fortune Cookies has a certain appeal to it.  Seemed like my lucky day!  The business, located on 65th between Allisonville Rd and Binford, is clustered with a number of small businesses that use a common entrance, parking, and are grouped into a few buildings.  This business has been around for about 30 years and makes fortune cookies for special occasions.    The entrance was colorful and featured a lot of gift ideas for presenting fortune cookies.  Once you walk into the center of the shop, there a small gift bags and sample bins of individually packaged cookies.  There were plain and chocolate covered ones.  There were flavored cookies in bright colors.  On the wall was a price list for ordering cookies (minimum order of 50) if you want to personalize the messages and the assortment you need for your special event.  If you are like me and are just looking to getting a package of a smaller quantity, they had plenty of options.  The basic fortune cookies (multi colored/flavored) sell for $8 per dozen.  The chocolate covered cookies go for $12 per dozen.  I have sampled some of each and can tell you that the flavors are fantastic!   Oh, and if you check in with Yelp while there, you qualify for a free sampler bag of the basic fortune cookies with a purchase on your first visit. Such a deal!    Review #389

The Stutz, much like the Circle City Industrial Complex, is one of those repurposed industrial complexes filled with as many twists and turns as shops and businesses.  If you want to visit the gallery in Stutz, I suggest street parking (southbound on Capitol).  You can either walk through the gated alley from the east side of the complex or from the 10th Street alley on the south side to the outside gallery door.      The gallery door lets you into another grouping of business, including a loading dock with an antique fire engine.  But if you take a right as you enter through the second door of the entry, you will find the gallery just passed the elevators.    The gallery itself has two show rooms connected by an annex that features other artists not part of the show.  The gallery is open Wed-Fri from 11 to 2 and is free.  It is also open on the first Friday that the new exhibit opens.  Most shows run a month, but it is best to check the website for specifics.      There are also open houses where most of the artist's studios (around 70) are open to check out and purchase art pieces.  The studios are located upstairs during the open houses.  The next open house will be April 28-29, 2017.    During my visit, the artist had pieces from five decades of work on display.  She had acrylics and watercolors, hand cast ceramics, and drawings.  Overall, the exhibit was interesting to view, though I wasn't moved to make a purchase.  Review #247

My wife and I brought some friends to Delicia for dinner on a Thursday evening (6-2-16).  We were the first to arrive, so we were immediately seated in the area across from the bar.  The restaurant was very stylish yet inviting.     We also had great service with a combination of friendliness and knowledge that I wish more restaurants had.  After all, the social aspect of dining with friends can be as key to enjoying the evening as the food.   After ordering our beverages, we were brought a small cup of Sancocho as an amuse bouche.  I am not familiar with the item, but the flavor reminded me of tasty bean broth.     We then shared a guacamole for the table.  Excellent flavor combination in the guac.  My wife, who normally doesn't care for avocado, even thought it was good!  The chips that came with the guac were light, but crisp enough to scoop.   I ordered the "De Palmitos" salad (hearts of palm, field greens, roasted walnuts, butternut squash, hibiscus-lemon vinaigrette).  It was my first time trying hearts of palm, so having all these other delicious flavors gave me confidence to try something new.  I was very pleased.   Finally, I ordered the Pescado Zarandeado (it comes without the fish head....I asked.)  The sea bass was colored/flavored with green and red achiote which made for a nice presentation.  Very tasty.  The fish came with black beans and white rice to fill out the entree.     With the great atmosphere, service, and food, it was plain to see why this restaurant was voted one of the Top 5 restaurants in Indy.  I look forward to my next visit.  Review #6

I had good food, beer, and service on a Sunday afternoon.  Stopping in for a late lunch, there was plenty of room inside and out.  There is a small parking lot for customers and some free street parking across the street on Cornell.  Inside, the pub is quite dark.  On the north end of the pub is where you can see the brewing tanks behind glass next to the bar.  I grabbed one of the smaller tables in that section and ordered a flight of their in house brews.  The flights are about 5 oz each and were only $1.50 each.  I opted for four:  The Cerveza de Sol (a Mexican style lager 5% 10 IBU); the Nice Weiss (Hefeweizen 5.25% 14 IBU) with a mild banana/clove taste; To Helles With It (German style lager 5% 17 IBU); and I Got Rye on It (a malt liquor 9% 28 IBU).  I enjoyed each of the samples and recommend trying the flights to get a sense of what you might like best.  I was drawn in by the Indy Burger Week promotion, so I went with the tasty Cheese Crock Bacon Burger with a side of brewpub "chips" and cole slaw.  The burger can be ordered to "doneness" and since I always order my burgers with a nice char, I was really pleased how great the kitchen did the grilling.  They then dunk the burger in cheese and serve it on a thick pretzel bun with bacon, lettuce, tomato, and pickle.  I have to admit that this was one huge stack of sandwich!  I ended up squishing the bun down to fit the sandwich in my mouth.  The taste was really good.  The cheese doesn't go on in a thick sheet like when a processed cheese is placed on top.  Instead, the heat of the burger melts the cheese so that you can see the cheese down in the crooks and crannies of the burger, but see mostly burger on the top.  Still, there was plenty of cheese flavor.  The cole slaw had a bit of a pungent taste.  I couldn't tell if it was the vinegar, but it may have had a touch of horseradish inside..not the heat, just something in the taste made me think of it.  It worked really well with bites of burger, but a little stronger than expected when eaten alone.  The brewpub "chips" are the English style thick sliced potatoes, not the crispy type we normally think of here.  I think there may have been a little bit of seasoning on them for additional flavor, but I didn't notice it throughout the batch.    This service was attentive and helpful.  Although my waitress had customers in other sections of the pub, I never waited more than five minutes once I finished a glass or my meal to have them cleared.  Checkout was fairly quick too.  As Indiana's oldest brewery, they have a number of quality ales to select from their own tanks.  They do offer a few other brewery/cidery options along with some wine and cocktails.    Overall, I had a very pleasant time at Broad Ripple Brewpub.  Review #324

I stopped in for lunch and had a really good experience.  The restaurant checks all the boxes for expectations from a local Mexican restaurant:  colorful interior, Hispanic music in the background, complementary salsa and chips (a little spicier than most places!).  In addition to these, I was greeted immediately and shown to my booth.  The chips arrived while I was perusing the menu.  When I put the menu down, my waiter made eye contact and came right over to see what I needed.    As soon as I finished my bowl of salsa, he brought out my entree and asked if I needed more salsa since there were still chips left in my basket.  Fast service and kitchen!  The entree (Fajita Quesadilla) appeared neatly plated on a 16" oval platter with the folded 10 or 11" tortilla stuffed with cheese, green peppers, onions, and my choice of beef (steak).  The rest of the plate was filled with shredded lettuce, sour cream, pico de gallo, and guacamole.  The steak was quite tender and had a nice flavor that went well with the other ingredients.  I quickly piled all the external ingredients atop the quesadilla and dived in.  Very tasty and filling.  The lettuce was thin cut (shredded) and not too long.  I appreciate when veggies are prepped bite sized.  Overall, as appealing visually as it was to my taste buds.  Really good flavor and great service.  Parking was free down the street and the atmosphere was clean and welcoming.  Though it has a lot of competition in the neighborhood for customers, El Arado is a strong contender!  Review #447

This combo candy shop and gift shop has some delicious confections to test your will power.  Though I noticed the variety of gifts and cards, I had my attention drawn to the chocolates counter.  (They have a variety of other types of candies including a jelly bean wall and some other fruity type treats.)  After looking over the displays a couple times, I asked and found out that you can buy the chocolates by the piece or by the pound.  I thought it best to go with individual pieces and limited my purchase so that my waistline stayed relatively the same size as when I started the day.  I decided to get a pecan snapper in milk chocolate (snapper = turtle), a cashew snapper in milk chocolate, and a dark chocolate covered pretzel.   Because the pieces are handmade, they are on the pricey side.  (After tax, it was nearly $8!)  The flavor was really good.  The snappers were fairly large compared to the ones you see in those assortment boxes.  They were filled with nuts and creamy gooey caramel.  The only problem was that since it was a hot day, I had a bit of a mess as the chocolate melted.  (Fear not, I am not above licking my fingers to savor the last bit of it!)  Overall, I would recommend this place if you have some will power or otherwise, a very deep wallet!  Review #1214

Once I walked in from the patio on the north side of the building, the first thing I noticed was a wall loaded with awards for the prize winning ales that this place has won at the Indiana Brewers Cup.  Since 2012, it seems Bier Brewery has had prize winners.  So the bar is set pretty high for your drinking experience.  I have had a number of their canned beverages around town.  They make a variety of brews including Special K (kolsch), Weizengoot (Hefewizen), and PDG ("Pretty Darn Good" American pale).  I have enjoyed them all!  The interior is dim and filled with assorted tables, chairs, and a lounge area.  The restrooms have been designated as Stouts and Blondes, so I guess that is understood to be gender neutral (I hope so since I am neither stout, at least not yet, or blonde!)  In the back corner is the counter/tap area with a list of the current taps artistically displayed on the chalkboard.  One thing I liked was that the counter has several laminated flip folders describing each of the featured brews.  I am still learning about craft beers, so I enjoy reading the details of each brew when available.  My only negative was that the brewery doesn't have flights of beer to sample.  Instead, they give free samples in small plastic cups.  In fact, you can try everything they have on tap!  But I found the samples too small (they said 3 oz, but they actually were only partly filled so about the size of a shot) to be able to distinguish the uniqueness of each brew, especially if you don't get a glass of water to clear the taste of the previous sample.  Of the four samples I tried, only the seasonal pumpkin ale stood out and the spices overwhelmed the beer and pumpkin flavors.    For me, I would prefer a legitimate four or five ounce sample to see how the flavors hold up to appreciate the nuance of each selection.  That's why I like the flights.  I don't want to buy a whole pint and find out that I may not like how the taste develops.    I know the brewery makes good beer, so even though I was disappointed with my visit to the brewery/taproom, I don't need to see the awards to know this place will continue on the right path.  I simply wish they would add the option of flights like so many of the other breweries around town.  Review #390

While on the west side, my wife and I decided to give Pho 36 a try.  I must say I agree with a number of reviews that mention that the service is friendly and pretty efficient (even though the owner/waiter was the only one covering the front including the cash register.)  The food we ordered, and we ordered a lot, came out pretty quickly and I enjoyed everything I tried.    I started with an order of Egg Rolls (3) that were nice and crisp and filled with ground pork, egg, long rice, carrots, and onions.  There were a couple types of veggie strips along side and a dipping sauce.  The sauce was on the thin side and didn't add a lot of flavor, but it was enough to add some depth to the taste.  I also had the Vietnamese Chicken wings which had five pieces of crisp breaded chicken drumettes or flat/tips and covered with a sticky "fish" sauce which tastes like a combo of sweet and savory flavors. (I didn't find it pungent, salty, or hot.  The flavors seemed like honey and sesame seed to me.)  My wife liked these too!  I also ordered the "Special" Bahn Mi - a baguette sandwich with sliced pork, pate, mayo, carrot, daikon, cucumber, sliced jalapeno, and cilantro.  My wife thought it tasted hot, but I didn't notice the heat at all.  The ingredients are served cold, but the flavors were refreshing and quite good.  The bread was very fresh too.  My wife was new to the cuisine, so she played it safe with the stir-fried chicken with mixed vegetables.  The dish was plentiful and the rice with chicken and shrimp stayed moist, not overcooked.  Plenty to eat for the money.  I also sampled a bowl of Pho - Chicken Noodle soup.  I noticed a small plate of sliced jalapeno, cilantro, and bean sprouts, but completely forgot to add them into my bowl.  The bowl itself was huge and was loaded with noodles and large (almost more than bite-sized) pieces of chicken.  The soup itself was on the bland side, like broth with just a hint of seasoning.  Maybe if I had remembered to add my side veggies/herbs, the flavor would have had more depth to it.    On the fun side, I ordered a strawberry bubble tea.  This was very cold and I did get a bit of brain freeze.  The bubbles are black tapioca beads that have the texture of gummy bears and were odd to watch slide up through my straw.  The flavor was exceptionally good and the drink stayed icy throughout the meal.  Overall, it was a fun place to stop and try another cuisine that is hard to find around town.  Although it has items that are similar to those offered at nearby restaurants, the business did a brisk business the entire time we dined there. it must be the service and food being a high quality.  p.s.  For additional flavor, they have Sriracha sauce and Hoison sauce bottles on the tables.  p.s.s.  Although the website leads me to believe this is a franchise of a chain, the ownership appears to be local and works in the restaurant.  Review #376

For lunch on Saturday, my wife and I headed to Irvington to try BitterSweet.  Having lived on the east side for eight years, we were really hoping that this restaurant would be another link in the restoration of the Washington Street area.  Sadly, we left a bit disappointed.  Arriving just after noon, we found parking behind the restaurant.  We followed directions and seated ourselves.  Our waitress greeted us and saw that the table needed a bit of cleaning, so she took care of that.  When we placed our beverage order, she brought my wife's iced tea, but forgot the lemon.  Then, my wife had to go ask for silverware so she could stir the tea. We noticed other tables correcting the service as well.  Little things, but clearly the lack of mature leadership on site let quality control slip.  After placing our orders, we took in the atmosphere of the place.  As described in other reviews, it is rather stark.  Also, half of the flourescent light fixtures were missing their coverings and a fair amount of those had bulbs burned out.  It just looked like it needed one good day of maintenance and decorating to be appealing.  After a reasonable amount of time, a different waiter took over and brought out our food.  He was much more attentive, i.e. experienced.  My wife ordered the Cuban sandwich, while I went with the Caprese Grilled Cheese and Mediterranean Orzo as a side.  The Cuban was pretty standard:  pork tenderloin, ham, swiss, dill pickle chips, and dijonaise on a pressed bollio roll (with seasoned kettle chips).  She let me eat about a third of her sandwich and we both felt the sandwich was rather bland.  The dijonaise was spread very thin and was barely detectable.  There were probably only two small pickle chips per half, so that many bites missed having the complimentary acid to round out the flavor.  The ham was far less in proportion than the tenderloin, so any saltiness that would be expected was reduced as well.  Simple adjustment to this sandwich could have made it delicious.  My Caprese Grilled Cheese sandwich was loaded with lots of cheese (provolone, fontina, and mozzarella) so that it had that oozing gooey texture that I expect in a grilled cheese.  It also came with roasted tomatoes (delicious!), fresh basil, and a touch of balsamic glaze on grilled sourdough bread.  Much better overall than the Cuban, but the bites of tomato were not evenly divided so that about half of my bites got no tomato at all.  The cheese and basil were fine, but the bites with tomato were fantastic.  So, what could have been a home run, was hit and miss depending upon the bite.  The Mediterranean Orzo side dish was served and upon the first bite, we realized that this was a cold salad, not something freshly cooked and tossed.  The salad came with spinach, sun dried tomato, red onion, kalamata olives, artichoke hearts, and feta cheese.  It was okay, but labeling it as a side instead of a salad led me to believe it would be warm.   I am giving the restaurant the benefit of the doubt since we didn't order any of the tasty cakes in the display case.  I hear they are delicious, so I will give them a third star for potential.    I don't think this restaurant would have much difficulty raising my rating with a bit of oversight and care, but I probably won't drive 45 minutes again to give them another chance.  If any of their regulars are on Yelp, please post if you see the management make an effort to fix up the decor and the service.  Review #94

I stopped in here for lunch on a Tuesday (4-12-16).  Although it is part of a strip mall with plenty of parking, the interior is anything but typical.  A wall sized mural and elegant tables await the diners.  I was a little disappointed that some items are available in the dinner hours, so I ended up choosing a couple other items and relying upon getting a to go box for what I didn't finish.  My first item was the Grilled Shrimp with Wild Mushroom Risotto, braised tomato, ratatouille vegetables, Broccoli and Crispy Onion.  This was a nice sized portion for lunch and the flavors were well suited for accompanying the shrimp.  I would definitely recommend this.  I also ordered the Chicken Almond Croissant with roasted rosemary chicken, toasted almonds, celery, onion, tomato, bacon aioli, petite greens and barbecue chips.  Again, this was a delicious combination.  (I saved half the sandwich so that I would have something to eat later in the evening.)    I plan on returning with my wife and friends soon to be able to sample some of the evening menu.  Review #31

After catching a quick bite for lunch on Virginia Avenue this Friday afternoon, I headed north to Shelby Street to try a flight of brews from Indiana City.  A few snacks are available at ICB, but mainly they rely upon using ClusterTruck delivery if anyone wants something more substantial to eat while sampling the local brews.  This was my first time at ICB, so after parking outside in their lot, I sat at the bar.  The flight ($7) comes with the customer's choice of four varieties.  Since I am not an experienced craft beer drinker, I went with some of the lower IBU options.  I selected the Sister City (Kolsch) as my first sample.  This was a great intro beer coming in at 4.7% ABV with only 20 IBU.  Very smooth for someone trying craft beers for the first time.  Next, I went to the Son of War (Blonde Ale) which was a very hoppy tasting Belgian style ale with a bit of citrus flavor on top of the hops.  Definitely a stronger flavor, especially after the swallow than the first brew. 4.5% ABV and 15 IBU  As my third selection, I sampled the Yacht Rock (Wheat Ale) with hints of orange peel, coriander, and fermented with witbier yeast.  The drink appears to resemble orange juice as a cloudy deep yellow color.  The taste was very pleasant though a bit higher in alcohol content than the first two choices.  6% ABV and 19 IBU.  As my final selection, I went with one recommended by the bartender based upon the information I had given her about what I liked.  She suggested the Shine (Dampfbier).  Dampfbier or "Steam Beer" is an effervescent ale brewed at warmer temperatures than most of the other ales.  This version had a hint of banana and was quite good as well.    The bartender was very friendly and was able to carry on a conversation between dealing with customers and posting info on the blackboard behind the counter.  ICB beers are available in cans at many liquor stores around Indiana, but not groceries.  There are also a variety of options for getting beers to go in growlers and bullets as well.  Review #93

The newest addition to the regular features of the Indianapolis Museum of Art (IMA) was very cool!  While checking out the spring gardens and greenhouse near the Lilly/Oldfield mansion, I stopped by the new beer garden.  The Beer Garden came to fruition as the first phase of the museum's plan to make the museum more approachable.  Sun King Brewery continues its support with the museum, first providing beer for last year's mini golf exhibit, and now by creating an exclusive Farmhouse Ale called "Among the Leaves" (5.1%, 23 IBU) for the Beer Garden.  The seating area is just east of the greenhouse on the north end of the IMA campus.  A pergola covers most of the seats.  There are additional tables out across the driveway for spill over crowds.    You place your order at the outside counter where a menu board lists the ale, a German Pilsener, and a dry Riesling wine.  There are also a Root Beer from Triton Brewing, a giant pretzel, cheese Dippy, and a snack mix available along with coffee, tea, bottled water, sparkling water, and lemonade.  I ordered the giant pretzel with mustard to go with my beer, paid, and took my number to one of the long tables.  Before long, my beer and pretzel arrived and I then had the choice to eat it there, or walk the grounds with my food.  The only restriction is that you can't take the beer into the museum or off the grounds.  The beer comes in a glass so if you do wander, you need to return it to the beer garden.  As far as the quality, I really liked the beer!  It was a clear amber color and had a full flavor that I expect from a Farmhouse Ale.  And the pretzel was easily big enough to share, but I managed to devour my warm and salted pretzel on my own.  The mustard is a basic yellow, not a spicy brown or horseradish style.  The only knock I have is that the selection is rather small.  I realize it is new and they are limiting their exposure while trying to offer something for a large range of people, but when I compare it with other beer gardens, it simply isn't on an equal basis.  Sure, it has probably the best surroundings of the beer gardens I have been to, but I am trying to be fair.    I will give them a pass on being a bit expensive since I realize the museum is trying to make money (I don't believe they receive any tax dollars, so I don't mind paying the extra amount.)      Note that the only way to get to the beer garden is to go to the museum first which now has a fee of $18 for non-member adults.  So, it isn't a place to go just for a beer.  But, if you want to check out a great museum and gardens, it's nice to have a casual option for grabbing a beer and a snack for strolling around.  Review #262

This is the third of the 5 local (soon to be 6 when the south side branch opens) Books & Brews I've been to.  Like the others, it has a book theme, a section for families to dine, and a separate bar area.  The have the five core brews on tap (also available in cans), and there are a number of smaller batch brews that come from the "mothership" location in Fishers.  So, this spot doesn't actually brew, but is a more like a pub than an actual brewery.  The staff seemed to be friendly and good at making conversation when they weren't busy helping customers or cooking.  And I must admit, the chicken wings I ordered were expertly cooked with a crispy outside and a juicy middle.  The price was a bit high for the serving size, but I found the serving to be right sized (8 pieces) for me when paired with the fries that come with the order.  (I had the "Where the Wild Wings Are".)  I like the clever names they have for their brews; all have some connection to a book title.  The available brews are posted on a chalkboard behind the bar and can be amusing to read through when seen gathered like that.  On my visits, I sampled a couple choices before ordering a Shogun Soba Ale (5.1%, 23 IBU).  It has a dark color from the buckwheat and has a somewhat buttery taste that paired well with the heat of the wings.
