Books & Brews is expanding rapidly in the Indy and Denver areas while looking forward to opening in Ohio soon.  They seem to look for spaces that are already set up for business (not new construction) and can keep their start up costs lower than from building dirt up.  Nothing wrong with filling an empty space with a place providing tasty beer and some food to go with it!  Review #645

Timing might be the biggest cause for my mediocre rating of this nature preserve.  I expected there not to be many flowers in February, but the recent rains really curtailed my enjoyment of exploring the trails.  So, I only visited the prairie side of the park.  There are lots of bird houses on poles throughout the prairie side.  There is a covered kiosk area near the pull-off (not really a parking lot as just a patch of gravel by the roadside.)  The kiosk had plenty of room to display information , but what was there looked aged and didn't really catch my attention.  So, I hope to get back this spring, after a dry spell, to check out the flowers and greenery as well as the back woods beyond the prairie while taking a long hike.  Review #610

Wolf Run has the potential to be a really great park on the south east side.  It is easy to find just off Thompson Road and has a paved parking lot near the shelter and playground.  There is a paved walking path oval around the park and basketball courts on the west end, away from the playground.  There is no parking/street access for the courts without hiking or biking, but it offers a distance which keeps older kids from the younger ones.    The playground has two sets of equipment:  one for bigger kids and smaller equipment for the tykes who might not be as safe on some of the bigger pieces.  They are conveniently spaced for parents who need to watch both.    There is a large lawn area for playing athletic games, but very few trees for shade.  Maybe future plantings can be arranged to offer a break when the hot days of summer approach.  Review #676

I was really surprised by how much there is to do at this park.  There are baseball and basketball areas, an aquatic center, a few shelters, a playground on the north end and a Play 60 Colts inspired playground/fitness equipment area.  But try as it might to be inclusive, the park needs some capital investment in basics like walkways that aren't broken and sadly, more surveillance in the parking areas.  I had been here before about a year ago to take photos of the Thomas Taggart Memorial.  Taggart was the Mayor of Indy from 1895-1901, became a Senator in 1916, and founded Riverside Park.  The Memorial was built in 1931 and was thought to be a treasure of Center Township, but has fallen into disrepair and has been closed off by fences to prevent further vandalism.  A study was done around 2005 to spend $1.3 million to restore the stability of the Memorial, but even now there is little evidence that anything is happening.  This could be a great location for all types of events if restored.  There is another building that hosts functions, but it seems rather mundane compared to the Taggart.  One of the newer additions to the park was the Play 60 inspired playground/training equipment that is on the 24th street end of the park.  Colts logos and colors are prevalent throughout the area since the NFL is behind the Play 60 (minutes of exercise/activity each day) program.  I will admit that most of the equipment and shelters appeared to be in pretty good shape.  But like I've seen mentioned in reviews of other city parks, the convenience of having parking lots away from busy streets can attract adults engaging in inappropriate activities.  As I was driving by on a Sunday afternoon, a group of men had gathered in one of the street side lots and their behavior was offensive enough to keep me from stopping.  There is no way I would have wanted to take my grand kids to the park after seeing that behavior.  I can only hope it was an isolated event, but the fact that none of the other men stopped the offending individual was deterrent enough for me.  I truly believe this park has the space and basics for becoming a really good park.  But in the meantime, a little more police presence might be needed to make the park a bit more family oriented.  Review #714

My wife and I stopped by for lunch on a Saturday and arrived just as they opened. One of the employees was still mopping the floor while we waited for our server to arrive to take our orders.  Since our order was first in line, we had great turnaround on having our food brought out.  We started with an order of gyoza (5 dumplings) which were crisped and served with lemon slices and a small amount dipping sauce.  The flavor was good, but the serving tray reservoir for the sauce was too small for the dumplings to be dunked in so about half the sauce went unused and too little got on the gyoza.  We each were brought a side salad before our entrees came out.  The iceberg lettuce was crisp and generally bite sized and loaded with the house dressing.  The flavor was quite good, but they could have used less dressing.  I also got a bowl of Miso soup which I found to be one of the best I've had!  As I stirred it, the soup went from a mostly broth like appearance to a more cloudy look.  The flavor had a more salty taste than most versions I've had elsewhere.  But then the entrees arrived and the disappointment arrived with it.  My wife ordered the Beef Teryaki and she might as well have ordered an ill prepared liver and onions.  The pre-sliced beef was served with a teryaki sauce on top, while presented of sliced white onions.  There was nothing about onions in the description, so she was surprised.  The beef was over cooked and dry, especially on the outer slices to the point it was tougher and chewier than it should have been.  The plate came with some unseasoned white rice.  I had ordered a Bento box and it came with more of the plain white rice, some orange slices, and my choice of roll (avocado), and meat (teryaki shrimp) served over the undisclosed sliced white onions.  The shrimp was also over cooked so that they were rubbery.  The flavor was good, it's just the texture was unappealing.  So, some of the apps were good, but both entrees were misses.  Having read some other reviews, I was expecting much better quality.    Note:  The approach to the restaurant out front could use some cleaning and the stairs were quite steep.  If you have trouble with stairs, I suggest approaching from the rear where the parking lot is the same level as the restaurant.  Review #771

This park is dedicated to the mountain bike riders of central Indiana.  Here, the riders have right of way on the 127 acres of park trails.  Seriously, if you are a hiker or walker, please find some place else.    The park is on the south side of 96th, immediately east (about 50 yards) of Hazel Dell Parkway.  (Hint:  It is much easier to find if you are approaching from the west so that you don't have to turn across traffic so close to a stop light.)  Inside the park, there is plenty of parking, some picnic tables, and a small shelter.  From what I saw, the trails are narrow and have some serious drop-offs along the way.  There are ponds and the river along the trail as well.   Please note that if the trails are wet, the folks who oversee the park want to avoid damage to the trails from ruts that harden and make the trail lose its accessibility.  So ride when the trails are dry.  Pretty simple rule to comply with.  I am encouraged by the information on the Indy Parks website that there are plans for a skill and challenge feature for developing the skills of the riders in a controlled environment before confronting those challenges on a trail.  Review #736

I generally enjoyed my visit to Deviate Brewing.  The interior is a bit crowded and dark compared to a number of breweries I have visited, but the bartender was friendly enough and mentioned a couple brews that were available even though they weren't listed on the chalkboard behind the counter.    I decided to go with a flight (4 five ounce selections) which have varying prices dependent upon the brews selected (anywhere between $8-14 for the four choices).  Lots of Stouts and IPA's are featured.  The four I chose were full flavored and I enjoyed 3 out of 4.  The PB&C, a peanut butter imperial stout was full of peanut flavor and was quite good as a special choice.  The Color Blind (blonde stout 7.8%) was another smooth and full flavored choice.  I also enjoyed the Kuppa Kopi (coffee porter 5.7%) for its smooth coffee taste without the bitterness.  I would drink each of these again!  My only choice that didn't taste quite so appealing was the Victimless Crime, an oatmeal stout orange zest.  Something about it seemed like an odd pairing the more I drank.  Even though it was only 5.3%, it seemed more boozy than the others to me, and the orange flavor when paired with the other flavors in the profile, just didn't appeal to me.  Still, 3 out of 4 ain't bad.    It can be a little tricky getting in and out of the parking lot since it is located at such a busy intersection (96th and Michigan Rd).  I managed to time traffic okay to head west on 96th to leave, but trying to get back on the interstate or to head east on 96th during rush hour would seem difficult due to excess traffic.  Enjoy the beer, but keep your wits about you when you head out!  Review #426

If you love disc golf, you may love this park.  The full 18-hole course is nearly a mile in length.  It has holes that are in the woods as well as ones on the open green space.  If you aren't a disc golf fan, there isn't much else for you here other than walking the course and a few narrow trails along the river.  There are a few picnic tables and grills, but no shelters or restrooms.  And if you're concerned about your car hitting potholes as you drive in, you may want to look elsewhere to visit.  The gravel road was in bad condition and made it challenging to get back to the paved parking lot...which has its own roundabout!  Review #738

I am not generally a fan of buffets and cafeterias.  Like most, Gray Brothers does tend to overcook a lot of their foods like the pork and roast beef entrees.  The green beans are also "well done" instead of al dente.  And their pies have several inches of rich meringue that overwhelm the otherwise delicious pies.  So, why four stars?  There are a number of items available that are really good!    I like to get the dark chicken for an entree.  Lightly breaded and seasoned, the chicken is tender, juicy, and lets the flavors of chicken and a bit of salt come through.  The light crunch of the breading is a nice touch.  They are generous with the portions as well.  I got 2 thighs and a leg for under $5.    I also like the pasta & broccoli salad.  Nicely balanced between spiral pasta and veggies, there is a sweetness to the side dish and the diced red onion makes a nice savory addition.  I definitely recommend this.   For a side, one of my favorites are the beets.  These small whole baby beets are cooked thoroughly and are bathed in a semi-sweet sauce.  There is enough beet flavor to avoid being masked by the sauce.  Give it a try!    The line workers are more efficient than friendly, but the staff attending the dining area seem to be a bit more welcoming.  Although you usually carry your own tray of food and beverages, the staff will clear your empty dishes, refill your beverages, and fetch a "to go" box if your eyes are bigger than your stomach capacity.      My wife and I don't usually dine in.  We prefer to go to the west end of the building where there is a carry out section.  It does have fewer options than the main restaurant, but most of the favorites are there.  The carry out is a great place to stop and get "home cooked" quality food without any of the fuss and dishes.  Review #445

Of all the parks I have reviewed, this one stuck in my mind that I needed to return to and see it once the flowers and greenery were peaking.  My previous review in February was when the paths were muddy and there was little sign of life.  Now that it is July, I found the trail wide and grassy (though still a little uneven under foot, so pay attention or you can stumble).  All around were wildflowers, birds and bees in motion, and a general sense that the prairie was alive and doing well.  I was able to work my way to the wooded area to the rear and right of the prairie. The path, sometimes mostly earthen, was narrower with a bit of an elevation change so that emerging from near the front required going up about a dozen steps to reach the prairie near the road.  Along the way, there were squirrels, a small creek, and lots of new forest trees that animals could be heard more than seen.  Though the day was hot, the shade and the breeze reached through the woods to make the journey pleasant and biting bug free.  The park is something that is well maintained and should be a point of pride for the community.  Rev. #35

I enjoyed my visit to Phan's Kitchen for lunch on a weekday.  The restaurant is tucked away inside Washington Square Mall on the wing nearest to Target.  There are a few decorations on the wall, but the general condition of the dining room was a bit worn.  (Hopefully the place will be successful and can invest in new chairs.)  There is a row of four-top tables on the left side of the dining room as I entered.  The order counter/grill are on the right.  I asked about seating/ordering and was told I could grab a menu and have a seat while I decided and then should return to the counter to place the order and pay.  During my visit, there was one guy handling the phones, the grill, and the cashier's duties.  So, even though I was the third customer, the order for my appetizer still took about 20 minutes (the entree came out much quicker as the boss arrived to help pick up the tasks.)  I started with the suggested Lao Beef Jerky.  Served on two green leaves, the jerky was tasty and had a nice chew, without being dry and tough.  Not exactly a Wow! moment, but still quite good.  I also ordered Pad See Ew which I've had many places that serve southeast Asian food.  I had read that this place can really crank the heat, so I played it a bit too safe and asked for it mild.  I think that robbed the dish of the fullness of flavor that I might have had if I had cranked it up just a bit more.  It was okay, just a little bland.  They do carry three sauces on each table, but I was afraid I would mess up what was a perfectly fine meal if I tinkered with it.  The only real negative about my meal was that most places I've had this dish use the wide noodles that are a bit thicker and shorter.  I checked and even the menu called for wide noodles.  But my plate arrived with what looked like very long egg noodles (maybe a half inch wide and much too long for my limited chopstick skills to securely tug out from under the beef, onions, and broccoli.)  The noodles just didn't have that texture and taste that I've enjoyed elsewhere.    Overall, the staff was pleasant and took care of my requests for a fork, more water, and even a to go box since the portion was huge!  I hope they continue to do well.  Review #701

You know, when your server greets you with a smile and goes about her job with a positive attitude, it can make your whole meal experience go well.  And when you top it off with a delicious sandwich and side, you earn a 5-star rating.  So it was with La Mulita.  I grabbed a spot in the lot behind the building and when I entered the restaurant, the sign directed me to seat myself, so I grabbed a spot outside the "bar rail" and sat in the dining area.  My server was busy delivering someone else's order and I soon realized she was not only doing the waiting, but running the bar too!  She went by dropping off a glass of ice water, apologized for the wait and said she would be back in a minute as soon as she delivered the drinks to the couple by the window.  She immediately returned and took my order.  Efficient and friendly.  In relatively no time, she brought out my Cubano and my side of sweet potato wedges served with a serrano aioli.  The first bite of the sandwich let me know the bolillo (bread) had been toasted with the crispness of the bite.  Then Wow!  The flavor of the combo was great!  There was a delicious grilled flavor in the ham & pork.  There was also a pickled tomatillo and Chihuahua cheese adding to the blend.    I then tried a sweet potato wedge which was lightly crisped and salted.  The sweet/salt combo was good.  Then I dipped one in the savory serrano aioli and that punch of flavor was all it needed to take the flavor to the next level.  Simple flavors, but in the right combination, can make for a nice surprise.  All too soon, the meal was devoured and I thanked the server for a great experience.  Review #682

As a fan of public art, I would like to point out that the outside of the Children's Museum has a number of pieces that are probably overlooked by most visitors.  The parking in the garage is free, so I took the opportunity to stroll around the outside.    Before you exit the garage, there is a 26' tall statue of Anubis overlooking the parking area.  This statue has been here before, but has traveled following a number of Egyptian exhibits.  Now, it is a permanent addition.  Once you cross Illinois St, there are a number of bronze statues of children playing and reading.  Two of the three are designated as memorials.  Each is a reminder of yesteryear when kids got outside to play or read a book.    Breaking into the top of the museum, a mother brachiosaurus lifts the roof allowing her offspring to climb in.  Purely fantasy in staging, the sheer size of the dinosaur is quite impressive.  As you work your way around the building to the south, there is a series of miniature recreations of the great architecture of the world.  Kids can play/climb all over these constructs or read about the originals on conveniently placed plaques.  The last is a tribute to Anne Frank.  Anne used to look out over a tree and dream of freedom as she wrote in her famous diary.  There is an art piece that features an open diary and a young tree grown from one of the actual nuts of the original tree outside Anne's window.  On the southwest corner, another grouping of dinosaurs (Alamosaurus) is seen escaping from the interior of the building.  Fantastic coloring and lifelike (as imagined) recreation of these beasts can be quite surprising as they appear to be running towards the street!  During certain festivals and holidays, these dinosaurs often are decorated with party hats of whimsy.  Often overlooked, Beyond Spaceship Earth shows a pair of astronauts working outside their point of entry (to the planetarium a located at the back of the main floor of the museum.)  I remember being fascinated by the spacewalks of the 1960's, imagining how courageous those early astronauts were, trusting their limited technology to keep them safe in the vacuum of space and to return them home safely.    On the north side of the grounds, there is a small mural on the building that shows a number of the exhibits within the museum.    Of course, I have been inside the museum numerous times.  I really appreciate that they continue to bring new exhibits to capture the imagination of visitors like Avatar, Transformers, and Hot Wheels.  But they also have a number of keepsake exhibits that keep drawing me back as well (Merry Go Round, the Trains, Beyond Spaceship Earth, and the Dinosaurs.)  Science and Fantasy...high tech and primitive...activities and quiet observation are balanced within.  And quality time with the kids that grow too fast can be as treasured as any of the exhibits.  Review #141  FYI: For a more complete list of Public Art in Indianapolis go to the following website:  http://www.indyartsguide.org/public-art/

I stopped by to see what this location had since I had enjoyed my stop at the Keystone at the Crossing location.  This place is noticeably larger with more room to move around.  The inventory seemed to be different here.  More focus on home decor (serving dishes, rugs, etc) and less of the cute stuff that I liked at KatC.  The price is upscale which is expected on this side of Indy, so I wasn't too shocked at anything.    They do have some whimsical items like the stuffed penguins & flamingos, but not much variety.   The man behind the desk greeted me when I came in but wasn't intrusive as I browsed, staying at the counter while I was there.    I didn't find anything to buy on this visit, but some things did catch my eye and made me pause to consider them.  Review #2022

I stopped by late in the lunch hour after roaming around in the January chill.  I wanted a simple cup of coffee and noticed an eye catching array of large muffins sitting on the counter.  So, a cup of House Blend coffee and a giant crumble topped apple (caramel?) muffin for under $4.  Very cool.  The shop was being manned by the owner and he was very pleasant and helpful.  We chatted a while since the morning rush had passed.  I headed upstairs and was glad to find the coffee was served at the right temperature to drink right away.  No scalding!  The house blend was a bit stronger than I usually like, but the flavor was deep and rich and I quickly adjusted.  Oh, and that muffin was phenomenal!  Light and cakey inside, but with chunks of seasoned apple inside.  And the top was crumble topped with a slight crunch and drizzled with a hint of frosting.  One of the best muffins I've had!  I'm not sure if they make them or buy them from someplace else, but I will find out the next time I return.    Review #2094

I enjoyed my visit to this clean and inviting place on 38th Street.  It is located on the north side of 38th between Moller & Georgetown at Kevin Way.  There's a stoplight making it easy to get across traffic and if you make an immediate right on Kevin Way in front of the Planet Fitness, you can drive straight to this bright yellow restaurant.  Although it is elevated with several steps to climb, there is a ramp for those who need it.    Inside is quite open and spacious.  I was seated at one of the raised booths (They do have some tables located in a section that do not require stepping up.)    The hostess/waitress was pleasant and efficient.  She took my order and within about twelve minutes, I had my small order of Jerk Chicken.  Wow!  The flavor was fantastic!  I got eight small wing halves served wet with lots of napkins.  The had a built in heat, but not overwhelming.  They also had a nice tangy flavor that was similar to a barbecue sauce, but with a bit of additional spice to lift it to another level.  Definitely try these if you visit!  I also tried a housemade sweet drink called Byssop that is made from hibiscus flowers.  The drink is very sweet for someone who doesn't drink soda.  Once I got passed the initial blast of sweet, I adjusted my expectations and noted that it was both fruity and floral.  The deep reddish violet color was appealing and the beverage, served over ice, was transparent.  Note that an order of the beverage does not come with refills.  My main course was from the dinner menu:  Oxtail stew which comes with a couple side courses.  The stew is made with tail meat which is "bone-in" and floats in a dark brown gravy with stewed carrot chunks.  The gravy can be eaten like soup, but note that you may get pieces of thyme stem as I found several lengths in mine.  The carrots were tender and tasty.  The beef itself was very tender, but because it is submerged in the gravy, becomes difficult to cut off the bone.  I suggest asking for an additional small plate that could be used as a cutting board.  Good taste, but not a "wow" combination.  The only real disappointment was from the sides.  I got the mixed veggies since my meal was meat laden.  The veggies were colorful, but thoroughly cooked, so they were limp and not as flavorful as I hoped.  The Jallof rice was served in great abundance, probably close to three cups worth!  The rice was a bit overcooked and had become dry.  I probably could have added some of it to the gravy from the stew, but I didn't.  The rice, though bright orange in color, was a bit on the bland side as well.  I believe they add tomato and onion (traditionally), but any pieces included were unnoticeable.  So, like many restaurants that are open all day, you have to choose carefully to get the best flavor for your dollar.  Definitely try the wings and if you like sweet drinks, get the Byssop.  Otherwise, read the reviews and see what others recommend to maximize your visit.  Review #487

I stopped by here on a sunny winter day and was amazed at how bright and cheerful the place looked.  I totally respect my friend Richard P's opinion that it doesn't match well with the neighborhood in colors, but I think the target audience, i.e. children, will love it!  It's very bright in primary colors and the play area is a checkerboard of padded squares that are slightly raised to help with drainage.  There is also a grill with some bench seating and a permanent ping pong table for folks who bring their own paddle and balls (the net is metal and stays up year round.)  The playground is located on the busy one way eastbound New York Street.  It is fenced to offer a bit of protection to keep the little ones from running out into the street.  The equipment is packed closely together which makes it easy for parents to keep an eye on them, but I can see it becoming congested if a lot of kids are here.    The playground has all kinds of unique pieces too!  I've not seen anything like the pieces here.  They still have similar functions for climbing, swinging, and sliding, but look different and less boring than most.  Parking is limited to street parking along the north lane of New York or along Jefferson.  The neighborhood is undergoing a transformation and the proximity of this park to Westminster Greenspace and a pocket park on Parkview is helping to make it more visually inviting.  Review #2302

This museum is truly unique and has a wonderful collection of paintings, sculptures, tools, and apparel from the "Wild West" to numerous tribes of Native Americans.  On each of my visits there is a balance of reverence for the determination of early settlers heading out into what was (to them) an unknown territory and a sadness for how shamefully our country has handled dealing with a proud people indigenous to the land.  Growing up in the 60's, I had an idealized vision of the west:  Good guys wore white hats and had a loyal horse.  Gun fights happened at noon but no blood was ever spilled, and only heroes took awhile to die.  So going into the first floor exhibits of the Gund Gallery and Art of the American West was very nostalgic.  Fantastic pieces of sculpture like "The Broncho Buster" by Remington and "Chief Crazy Horse" by Baur are masterfully crafted.  Paintings like "The Twins" by Hennings and "Crippled but Still Coming" captured the flavor of my memories of cowboy life.  "A Secret Cache" by Buxton and "Blessing From the Medicine Man" pay reverence to the native peoples of the land and their lives.  Fantastic vistas captured on canvas like "Mount Wilson Winter" by Chavez and one of my favorites, the triptych "October Suite, Grand Canyon" draw you in to a world where the land was majestic, not littered with highways and oil rigs.  It is truly unique to the midwest and worth seeing for these pieces on their own.  But when you get to the second floor, and enter the "Mihtohseenionki" (The People's Place) that reality replaces the nostalgia.  There is an extensive display with timeline boards that tell the history of the Native Americans, primarily the Miami tribe in Indiana.  There are numerous artifacts to see, but the recurring theme is the numerous treaties that were negotiated usually after some bloody conflict in which the settlement meant pushing farther to the west.  Compare the rich, lush landscape of the east with fresh water rivers and great soil for crops to the desert lands that have become the last resort for many and you will understand my impression.  The remainder of the second floor is devoted to the Native American Galleries displaying pottery, clothing, utensils, and religious artifacts of the diverse societies of the West.  From desert to the Great Lakes to the northwest and beyond, there are numerous examples of artwork in the everyday lives of the people.    The collection is truly remarkable and are fortunate to have access to it.  On a lighter note, there is a cafe on the canal end of the first floor, a family activity area on the canal level (lowest level), and for Yelpers who check in before paying, a $2 discount.  Also, parking in the garage is free if you ask for a validation pass at the time you purchase your tickets.  Review #202

I stopped in for a burger during the opening week.  This spin-off from St Elmo's/Harry & Izzy's is located on the street level of the Circle Centre Mall with access from Georgia Street, or from the south escalator if you are coming from the parking garage in the mall.  This is a full service restaurant, so they take reservations and have you wait to be seated by the hostess. They have multiple bartenders and have waiter staff.    The bar is in the center of the dining space, with four top tables lining the outer walls.  Multiple televisions play silently while you wait/dine.  Overall, I would rate the waiters/bartenders to be very good.  They were friendly and maintained my water glass throughout.  However, the kitchen was running behind for a place that specializes in burgers.  It took a full 30 minutes from the time I placed my order to get my food.  I get that it's their first week, but most folks working downtown cannot afford a lengthy wait on their lunch hours.  So, definitely room for improvement there.  As far as the food, let me suggest ordering the Zucchini Straws.  Yum!  Long strips of zucchini are lightly breaded and fried to a delightful crunch on the outside with a light airy filling on the inside.  The aioli dipping sauce is perfect for the side.  I decided to try the pricey Prime Degree burger, which is basically a burger with BLT ingredients and cheese (plus an aioli sauce for a condiment.)  The flavor was good.  My burger was a little more done than I ordered but close enough to not take points off.  Now here's the takeaway:  I don't know if their beef is that superior to other high end burger places, but at the end of the day, the more ingredients you add to the sandwich, the less burger flavor comes through.  My burger had a nice char flavor (as requested), but when all the other flavors were added, I couldn't really taste a difference.  I can't recommend spending $19 for a burger (without sides).   Review #399

This park is a truly great park on the near east side for anyone who wants to take time to visit.  It is conveniently located on the south side of Washington Street (a turn lane is there for anyone who has to cross traffic.)  I used to drive by this when I lived on the east side and drove local streets to downtown.  I wasn't impressed.  But in the time between my last visit and now, the park has undergone a half million dollar makeover (Wow!) that has made it a go to place.    Do you want a place with shade and a shelter with picnic tables, quiet places with benches to relax, open space for activities on the far east end?  They got it here!  Do you want basketball courts, an aquatic center, and a cool playground right near the shelter?  They got it!  The park has a lot of paths (grit based) to travel on your way to the different amenities.  The playground and aquatic center (pool, slides, splash pad) are separated by the common parking lot so that the end of the lot fill faster than the center.    Note:  There is also a memorial to Sylvia Likens on the southwest edge of the park.  If you are interested in learning more about the memorial, there is a great review by Richard P that has all the information you would like under the Sylvia Likens heading.  Review #678

This new shop in Mooresville looks like it's off to great start with a beautiful collection of house plants and artisanal pots/accessories.  For a small shop, I was impressed with the variety they offered.    In addition to the house plants, the office part of the shop carries Indie Coffee Roasters coffee (Carmel) and a selection of oils, including CBD oil.  They have a few parking spaces out front and some additional spots behind the building.  Unfortunately, the current business hours are limited to a lunch time window three days a week and only extend into early evening hours on Thursdays.  Hopefully, they will be successful enough to expand the store AND the hours if they want to compete with all the big box discount plants in the area.  Review #2109

What a cool venue!  My wife and I stopped by for lunch on a Saturday and the place was pretty quiet.  We sat in the bar area on the left (there is a larger seating and lounge area to the right).    Before eating, I browsed some of the A J Foyt Memorabilia gathered along the walls and an actual race car over in the lounge area.  I then tried a flight of the white wine samples:  Riesling, Sauvignon Blanc, and Chardonnay.  You only get a small pour of each, but enough to get a few sips.  I really liked the Riesling (my favorite of the three).  Our lunch arrived and I got the BBQ Chicken Flatbread while my wife ordered a salad with an upgrade of chicken strips added.  The salad was large and only loosely chopped, so she did need to cut it into smaller, more bite sized, pieces.  They also brought her a couple types dressing on the side since they didn't have exactly what she wanted.  She enjoyed her meal and there was enough for a to go box.  My flatbread was about 8" x 12" cut into eighths.  The BBQ sauce was sweet and tangy and the chicken was cubed, still moist, and warm.  The flatbread was also topped with sliced red onion and cheese.  Very good!  I thought the crust had just the right amount of crunch and held its shape despite the toppings.  Definitely recommended!  Overall, we had a fun time and enjoyed our meals and the wine.  Be sure to check their hours since they are somewhat restricted.  Also, be aware that the space is sometimes reserved for private parties that you may not be aware of until you arrive.  (Hopefully they can add a calendar to their website to show blackout dates.)  Review #2138

The City Center Park is a great playground area for children.  It is located just a block south of Main Street between US 31 and Madison.  You can tell it is well maintained and has a lot of great ideas built in.  For instance, the playground areas (one for toddlers, one for older kids) are elevated and have padded squares underfoot that provide good traction and a soft cushion if a little one happens to tumble.  The elevation allows the runoff water to go to good use by collecting in a couple rain gardens.  The trails/walkways are all paved and even though I visited on a rainy day, the paths were puddle free.    There are several seating areas for parents to stay close to the playgrounds without having to stand the entire time.  There is also a permanent restroom and water fountain area, so no port-o-lets on site.  Parking is located along the north side of the park and there seems to be plenty.  In summer months, a splash garden is also available and tennis courts are fenced in to keep stray shots from traveling too far.  Overall, I think it is a great addition to the local parks in Greenwood.  Review #504

I enjoyed browsing through Papyrus inside the Nordstrom wing (east hall) of Keystone at the Crossing.  They had a really nice window display with painted wooden holiday items that caught my eye.  Inside, they had a number of greeting and holiday cards, some games and books, and accessories for wrapping. There were even some small gift items too.  The shop was full, but not too crowded on a weekday.  Seems like a great place to grab some last minute cards/wrapping paper if you did some shopping in the mall without having to stop someplace else.  Good location!  Review #1963

I've been meaning to stop by Mudbugs for quite awhile, so on a rainy Saturday, I finally made it.  Inside, the dining area is filled with color.. bold color.  The walls are covered with images and decorations to make you think of Mardi Gras.  A small tv in the corner was playing an episode of "Swamp People" that was a bit creepy for me to think that people make a living, by choice, to hunt snakes and crocs for income.    Anyway, there is an order counter with a chalkboard menu to the left.  There are a variety of entrees, sides, Po'Boys, and a combo platter.    I decided to give a Chicken Po'Boy a try.  It comes with a choice of hush puppies or potato salad (I went with the potatoes).  They have some bottled beverages, but there is also a self help soda fountain to the right.  I grabbed a 2-top after being given my order number to set on my table.  The food took about 10-15 minutes to be brought out.  The flavor of the chicken sandwich was really good.  The chicken was moist and had a crispy crunch batter.  I also liked the cajun sauce that was added for a perky flavor.  The lettuce was crisp and added another bit of crispness.  Really tasty sandwich!  The potato salad was topped with paprika and was fine.  It was generally cubed potato with a mustard based cream.  A little on the dry side, but okay.  I've had similar texture from grocery brands that were also chilled.  I've not been to New Orleans, so I can't comment on how it compares, but the meal was modestly priced and had a pleasant flavor.  It's a nice alternative to the burgers, pizza, and Mexican restaurants that fill the area.  Review #2494

This place was by far the busiest of the three gift shops on Mass Ave that my wife and I explored.  With a name like Silver in the City, she expected it to be more of a jewelry store.  When she passed by that section of the store, no one asked if they could help.  There was a lot of stuff, a wide variety actually, but the place felt cramped and crowded with a line stretching back from the pay counter like you would see at a department store with kids waiting to see Santa.  Either not enough help or enough registers...not sure, but I found the experience difficult to maneuver and actually look at the goods.  Maybe I will have better luck on a weekday when the crowds aren't so large.  Review #1834

In the passed year, I have been both a patient and the designated driver for a loved one undergoing a procedure at St Francis/Franciscan Health Indianapolis Hospital.  In both cases, admissions made the process easy and the staff were friendly and helpful.  In my case, I had to transfer from a smaller satellite hospital that was unable to handle my needs.  This location got me in immediately and although I needed to stay overnight, was in fine shape to take off the next day.  When I compare the procedure I received to those of friends who had it done 15 years ago, mine was minimally invasive and required a minimum of pain relief in the following days.  In the case of my loved one, she had undergone the procedure at another facility and was dreading having it again because it is quite painful and requires the patient to be awake.  But this time, the process was greatly improved with far less discomfort.  Good quality surgeons and specialists to handle the procedures go a long way in the healing process.  I also found the waiting areas of the hospital to be clean and open, not cramped and uncomfortable.  There are even places where you can walk inside to stretch your limbs if the procedures run a few hours.  That was a relief to me!  I have had great results when dealing with this location.  Review #2274

What a great place to get out for some exercise and to reconnect with nature.  The park is 127 acres and has multiple foot worn trails that total about 2.25 miles!  The northwest corner of the park is a state nature preserve which is densely wooded  with most of the trails.  It features numerous small creeks with small footbridges over most and a few larger ones when necessary.  That doesn't mean you won't get mud on your shows, but at least you probably won't need to change your socks!  The rest of the park is under DNR oversight and features prairies, wetlands, and a swamp!  I really appreciate that parks don't turn everything into a lawn.  Creatures need habitats that they are used to, so when there is space, I applaud efforts to provide sanctuary to them.  The trails in those areas are limited and the wetlands have an observation platform to make it easier to see what surrounds you.  There is a grit packed pathway that leads from the parking lot to the two shelters which are less than a quarter mile from the parking lot.  There are permanent restrooms that are maintained as well.  If you are going here to hike, I highly recommend stopping by the little building at the parking lot and grabbing a pamphlet about the park.  Within it, there is a map showing color coded trails and lists how long each trail is.  This can be really useful since the trails seldom go in straight lines.  Each trail intersection has a post with a sign showing which trails head in the corresponding directions.  That is great for first time visitors like myself.  Note that the trails wind through the trees, so roots may become tripping hazards if you are looking up all the time.  There is also a limited amount of elevation change especially on the Creek Ridge Trail.  That's a good thing or else the park would flood out.  At least the wooded and prairie areas stay mainly dry.  Review #801

I stopped in this new sandwich shop which is part of a three business cooperative located midway along a row businesses in an industrial area on 79th, just east of Zionsville Road.  There are two doors leading from the parking lot:  The left one opens to Wabash Brewing; The right one opens to the adjoining space and holds Liberation Roasting Company (coffee) and this aptly named restaurant.  Note that this place is open to all ages (only the brewing area is off limits to minors.)  They have a menu board and table pamphlets to help you choose your food items.  There are sandwiches, salads, and flatbreads which are made fresh when ordered.  On this visit, my wife ordered a wedge salad while I went for the Peppa Pig flatbread and a half house salad.  While we waited for our food, I strolled over to the brewery to pick up a beverage.  My wife decided to go with a Coke which was only $1 and served in a chilled can.  No ice is available yet, but they do offer cups and straws if preferred.  Before long, our food came out and the portions were quite generous!  My wife's wedge was a full quarter head of iceberg lettuce topped with tomato, bacon bits, and a Gorgonzola cream.  Everything was fresh and crisp.  She thought the size was almost too much and that if they continue to use a full quarter, then more cream would help.  She also thought a bit of bell pepper would perk up the flavor as well.  I went with the half salad and was surprised that it was as large as a full salad most places.  I went with the Balsamic Reduction as my dressing and it was delicious!!!  It had a great combination of savory and sweet flavor along with the mixed greens, grape tomato halves, and shredded cheese.  The Peppa Pig flatbread features peppered bacon, garlic aioli, small tomato slices under the cheese, loads of fresh mozzarella, and topped with chiffonade basil.  The flavor was nicely balance and the cheese was pleasantly gooey.  My only negative was that the scratch crust was a little on the soggy side and could have used just a bit more crispness to give a nice texture to support the cheese.  Overall, the food was tasty and reasonably priced.  One of the three sister owners was on hand to greet, prepare, and serve us.  I like being able to support new businesses, especially where a family is so active in running the place.  Review #498

My wife and I stopped in for an early dinner on Tuesday evening at this hotel restaurant.  After a short walk through the lobby, the open sided bar/restaurant was easy to spot.  Since it was early, we had our pick of seats.  We selected a small table for two instead of a booth, bar seat, or large communal table.  After placing our order for a couple drafts (includes local craft brews), we placed our order for burgers and sides.  My wife went with the BT House burger and a side salad.  I opted for the Uptown Burger and cole slaw.  Both of us liked our choices.  Her burger came with American Cheese, grilled onions, lettuce, pickle, and a tasty house "KGB" sauce.    My burger was seared nicely and had grilled portabello mushrooms, carmelized onions (kinda sweet), Swiss cheese, and roasted garlic mayo.  Very good!  Although the burger was 1/3 pound, it maintained its juiciness even with the searing.  The cole slaw was creamy and used red cabbage which created a pink color.  The taste was fine, but I can't say I have ever seen pink slaw before.    Service was fine and we didn't have much of a wait between any of our dealings.  A bit on the pricey side, the flavors were comparable to high end burger places.  Thankfully, the fresh quality held up.  Review #155

As I get older, I have trouble keeping up with all the fads in dining.  So when I heard about a "Paleo" diner, I wasn't sure what it meant.  But, being a fan of good food, I thought I would give it a try.  Nook has expanded their hours to include lunch, so I went the day after their first lunch serving.  As my waiter arrived, he explained how people should eat like "cave men":  no artificial sugars, no gluten, and no dairy.  Now, I have no animus against any food group, believing in the basic food groups and moderation to be my golden rule of dining.  But any given meal for me may step out of the pyramid.  So I gladly accepted the complementary sip of olive oil to start my meal.  It is supposed to be good for digestion.  I noted a hint of peppery flavor which was actually rather pleasant.  I started my meal with a beef broth bowl.  The bowl is huge!  They start with 200 pounds of beef bones and slow cook it down to extract the rich flavor from the marrow.  The broth has daikon radish, shiitake, shredded beet noodles (yellow), onion, shredded cabbage, and topped with fresh herbs.  Yum!  Note:  You can make this a full meal by adding beef to the bowl for an additional $7.  I also ordered a side of Brussels Sprouts which are shareable in size and un-shareable because the flavor is so fantastic!  I devoured the whole dish by myself.  The sprouts are halved and are grilled with shishito peppers, candied (turbinado brown sugar) bacon, and topped with a smokey paprika aioli.  The flavors were nicely layered and makes me wonder if people who say they don't like Brussels Sprouts had any idea how much they are missing.  As an entree, I ordered the short rib taco.  Instead of a flour or corn tortilla, they use ground almond which adds a nice flavor and a bit of crispness.  The short rib beef was juicy and tender, but maybe a tad under seasoned (they do have salt and pepper on each table, but I refrained from using it since I wanted to see how the flavor combos worked without it.)  The taco also has scallions, shredded napa cabbage, teriyaki, and sriracha (not very hot with all the other ingredients).  They also added shredded carrots and herbs on top.  The herbs were fresh and gave a pungent fragrance as I folded and lifted the taco for a bite.  Note:  although the tortilla holds up to the juices, some will drip out onto your plate with the orange color of the sriracha....be sure you have your napkin in place so that you don't get stained. (Whew!)  The staff was very friendly and even though they left an iceless carafe of water on the table for me, frequently did the pouring when they passed.  The front manager stopped by to see how I was enjoying the meal and even the owner came by.  I like when the folks who are supposed to be overseeing the operation actually care about listening to my feedback and don't just go through the motions.  Everything ran smoothly and the waiter even checked on a couple things for me with the kitchen to answer my curiosity.  (Note:  I go at non-peak times, so staff may have a little more time to answer.)  I doubt I will switch over to becoming Paleo.  But I will definitely be back to try some of Nook's other options soon.  Review #689

This is one of the better parks on the near southwest side.  There is a really great playground and splash area for the kids.  There is a paved pathway for walking around the prairie area and a basketball court for older kids.  They have a shelter and picnic tables close to the playground too.  Though everything looks to be in pretty good shape, the park doesn't have much parking of its own.  There are a handful of spaces on the south side of the park, but I imagine some folks park at the nearby elementary school and walk over.  The park could also use some tree plantings for shade and some benches around the playground/splash areas so that parents don't have to stand the entire time the kids are playing (especially if the shelter is rented by someone else).  It is bright and colorful and looks like a place kids could really have a fun time with equipment that isn't just the same old, same old.  Review #667

I stopped in for a bite and brew after a morning of hiking around Central Park in Carmel.  Since I was dining alone, I grabbed a spot at the bar and was impressed with the giant row of taps behind the bar.  The menu for drinks is large and two sided with all the fun stuff about the craft beers that I like:  ABV, brewery, location of the brewery, and sorted by beer type.  And I also like that they offer flights of 5 oz beers just like a number of breweries do!  So, that was the route I headed.  I also wanted to get something to eat and saw the Crab Cake Melt listed under the sandwich section.  Served on an oversized English muffin, the crab cake is covered with melted Gruyere, arugula, crispy onion strings, a tabasco mayo, avocado, and roasted tomato.  And though it looks like one of those giant monoliths that you wonder how you can fit it into your maw, relax....you can simply smash/squeeze the sandwich down to a smaller size without it shooting out the sides.  Oh, and the flavor was fantastic!  I was really surprised by how well the flavors worked together and the tabasco was tempered by the cool of the avocado.  Just lots of layers of flavor.    With so many beers to choose from and a few hard liquors for those die hards, this is a great place to sample a large number of brews from around the state and around the country.  And the food was even better!  p.s.  The service was very pleasant and efficient.  Even though all those working in the bar would disappear at times, there was always someone back within a minute or so to make sure nobody was left unattended.  Review #944

I think I took more time making up my mind than this restaurant took to make my lunch!  When you walk up to the booth, there are banners with food (mostly sandwiches) listings along the entire length of the booth.  There is also a substantial salad bar along the north side of the booth which can be tempting too!  I finally settled on the Cubano sandwich (Pork, Ham, cheese, mustard, & pickle) with a side of cole slaw.  I grabbed a napkin from the counter and went to the south end of the booth to A) get out of the way of the new orders, and B) find the pick up counter.  Before long, they called the last two numbers on my ticket I received after paying.  A plastic fork was included in the styrofoam container.  Note that they have a self serve soda dispenser that you can do while waiting too.  I took my order upstairs and grabbed a spot in the balcony of City Market.  The sandwich was about 6" overall and sliced on a slight bias, wrapped in deli paper to keep the handling clean.  I thought the bread and sandwich ingredients were quite good, but not the best I've had.  They used sliced ham and pieces of pork not uniformly carved to make the meat of the sandwich.  The bread was fresh and had a nice bite texture without being toasted.  One thing I particularly liked was a surprise in the slaw that it had some heat to it.  I'm used to slaw being either tangy from a vinegar/sugar base or being creamy.  This was on the less creamy side and the bit of heat was a pleasant change from the usually cool taste I get from slaw.  I definitely recommend it if you like trying something different.  Overall, efficient service and good food without taking up your whole lunch hour to get your food.  Review #1966

After taking photos on the Monon, I stopped in for a late lunch at Bub's.  I liked that they had a patio with a view of the Monon and inside, colorful small rooms create more private dining experiences than the big open air dining places elsewhere.  And the service, though quite active, managed to be friendly and keep delays to a minimum.  The only problem was the lunch was nothing to rave about.  I ordered a pot roast sandwich that comes with potato salad.  The meat was tender, but only lightly seasoned.  There is a house horse radish sauce, bacon, cheddar, and pickled onions on mutli-grain bread.  First, the onions were very tart which threw off the balance of the sandwich for me.  Nothing exactly wrong, it just didn't appeal to me.  There was also a texture problem.  The bacon was thick and chewy while the rest of the sandwich was tender.  So, biting through the bacon was awkward.  I often pulled the bacon part way out of the sandwich while eating.  Maybe a little thinner bacon would work better here.  The potato salad had bacon pieces in it and was okay on flavor, but the consistency was too thick/dry.  I like it a bit more creamy and less clingy.    To be fair, this place specializes in breakfast and I just don't get up to Carmel for breakfast very often.  If I do, I will give Bub's another shot.  But, at least on this visit, the food left me without anything to rave about.  Review #3125

After having such a pleasant experience at the Mass Avenue store where we made some purchases, my wife and I made a point of exploring the Nora shop to see what else we might find.  Sadly, this store doesn't have nearly the diversity of items that the other store has.  And though there were three staff working (two were behind the counter without customers) and one was doing inventory), it wasn't until we were getting ready to leave that the one doing inventory greeted us.  So unlike the store on Mass Avenue where they asked if we had shopped their before and took the time to explain the fair wage system that they use, we could have come in and never known anything about the items on display.  I will stick to the Mass Ave store.  Review #2051

I stopped in this brewery nestled in the heart of the West Clay area of Carmel.  Great location with parking out front and a patio on the side with garage doors that open during nice weather.    Inside there is an industrial look to the place with an open view of the brewery (not behind glass like other places).  There are lots of different tables heights and sizes to choose from as well as individual seating at the bar.  I was greeted by the bartender (Josh) who introduced himself and took good care of me, answering some questions I had about the beer and my flight options.  Flights are normally 4 pours ($8) with 6 pours also available.  I went with four house brews though they do carry about as many outside beers as well.  Overall, lots of choices here!  I picked the Pub Scout Bohemian Pilsner, and Ginger Witte Urban Wheat to start with.  Both were okay, but nothing I would recommend.  I then progressed to the Holy Water Stout that had a deep taste with hints of chocolate.  My last selection was the Fist of Fury Blood Orange IPA that was good.  Nice balance of orange and hops for an enjoyable, refreshing beer.  Josh made some recommendations that he provided samples of and both were really good.  I normally am not a fan of Brown Ales, but the Mac Daddy Scottish Ale was really good!  We also talked about the Johnny Ringo Ghost Pepper lager made with real Ghost Peppers!  Don't be scared of trying this one.  The beer to pepper ration is high, so the pepper adds a nice edge to the flavor with only a mild tickle at the back of your throat.  I can't say if the heat gets stronger if you order a pint, but it is worth trying if you stop by.  I know it will be on my list the next time!  I didn't see a food menu while there, but I hear they have some things in house.  Check out the website to see what they offer.  Overall, a solid offering of beers and may have been an even better rating if I had tried just the ones Josh recommended.  Review #3166

My wife and I stopped in for an early dinner during the week and were seated right away.  There is plenty of parking in the shared lot and the interior is brightly lit with colorful decorations and a high ceiling.  Mexican music plays in the background at a level that is heard, but not restrictive of conversation.  We received complementary salsa and chips to start the evening.  I thought they tasted fine, but my wife thought they needed a bit of salt. Before long, we received our orders:  she got a beef filled chimichanga with a white cheese sauce, rice and beans, and a number of toppings including sour cream, lettuce, pico de gallo, and guacamole.  She thought the flavor was really good.  I ordered the Tacos decarne asada (strips of steak in flour tortillas) with lime wedges, rice and beans.  I was a little surprised that there was no additional toppings, but decided to just try them with the lime juice.  Very Tasty!  Although I enjoy all the other toppings that usually come with midwestern tacos, I have to admit that the bit of lime really brought out the steak flavor!  Our server was friendly though he seemed to be harried trying to keep up with the inflow of new customers.  But in the end, he made an effort to expedite our requests and process our bill since we had a grandchild's concert to attend.  Good food with easy access to the plaza on the northwest corner of US 36 and Dan Jones made it a nice choice for us to grab a quick bite.  Review #3338

This park is nicely maintained and has a shelter and playgrounds with some open spaces for active sports.  It is on a hiking/biking trail so it makes for a decent rest area.  But it is a cookie cutter park lacking restrooms and running water that visitors (both park and trail types) could benefit from.  The mature trees are at the perimeter and so shade is limited to the shelter or sitting in your car.  Not much for older kids to do unless they have enough for a team activity.  Review #768

I really like this park.  Not only does it have a lot of greenery (both trees and gardens), but it is filled with fountains and statues too!  Back in 1821, when Alexander Ralston drew up the plat map of Indianapolis, plat 25 was designated as University Square.  Over time, the name has changed slightly to become University Park.  In 1887, a statue of the first Vice President of the United States from Indiana, Schulyer Colfax was placed.  Colfax was the 17th VP who served under the 18th President Grant (Andrew Johnson was the 17th President after Lincoln's assasination and the VP position was left vacant during the remainder of Johnson's term.)  On the side of the statue's base is a relief of Rebecca and Eliezer at the Well in honor of his establishing the Rebekah Degree organization.  In 1908, a statue of Benjamin Harrison, our 23rd President and Indiana's only one, was placed.  The sculpture was created by artist Charles Henry.  In 1914, the park was redesigned by George Kessler (yes, that's the same Kessler that the boulevard is named after).  The Depew Memorial Fountain was centered in the park in 1919.  The surroundings of the fountain were designed by Henry Bacon.  In 1923, the original "Pan" and "Syrinx" sculptures were installed by famed local artist Myra Reynolds Richards.  Sadly, both original statues were stolen later.  In 1934, "Seated Lincoln" was created by Henry Hering whose work can also be seen on the obelisk in Veteran's Memorial Plaza (two blocks north) and adorning the Indiana World War Memorial on the block immediately north.  He created the relief figures at the top of the memorial as well as the "Pro Patria" statue on the southern steps.  In 1973, artist Adolph Wolter created replacements for the Pan and Syrinx statues, but used his own designs instead of following Richards' originals.  Sadly, the Pan was stolen again and has been replaced by a third Pan by Roger White in 1980. Then after it was stolen, White created a fourth Pan in 2005.  What is it about small sculptures that thieves keep stealing them?  Anyway, the park is easily within walking distance for most downtown workers who can pry themselves away from their desks long enough to enjoy the setting.  Review #1864

When I used to live in Greenwood, I would stop at Phillips Produce to pick up some fresh fruit/veggies.  And during the fall season, they sell pumpkins and bales of straw for decorating.  But we moved, so it had been years since my last visit.  I finally stopped in and am I glad I did!  First, they are easy to find with a location at the corner of Southport Rd and Meridian.  It does make it a little difficult to get in and out of when traffic is heavy because it can back up and block the entrance if you are having to cut across.  (So plan avoid rush hour or plan to arrive from the west on Southport!)  I started browsing and was greeted by the staff.  He suggested grabbing one of the carts which is cool because they have a small ramp that you can tow the cart inside to pay without having to unload.    There were all the items you might go to an orchard to find:  pumpkins, apples, gourds, mums, and more.  I found some purple mums for $8.50 that had blooms spreading nearly 2' across!  There were some cool gourds five for $5.  Another good deal!  The staff, though busy unloading and arranging things by one of the sheds, saw me go into the store and immediately came over to ring up my order.  That is good customer service.    Now that I've returned once, I'll have to make it a point to swing by this way more often.  Review #3155

On our way home, my wife asked if I would stop at this local alterations shop to pick up a garment she had adjusted.  I will be the first to admit that I don't personally know much about sewing and alterations, but my wife does and she couldn't say enough about how reasonably priced this place is.  The woman who does the alterations is very friendly and my wife has been very pleased with the results.  Understand that you can't usually drop off some intricate garment and expect her to drop whatever she is doing to fix it.  But my wife was in no hurry and the garment was ready in a couple weeks.  There are a couple changing/dressing rooms for visitors to try on their garments for marking and reviewing.  Note that the owner only accepts cash or checks, NO Credit Cards.  My wife found the place through the local grapevine, so when I saw it was already reviewed on Yelp, I was pleased to see the reviews echoed my wife's opinions.  If you are in the area, stop by this small shop just south of the Casey's at the intersection of Bridge St and Indianapolis Rd.  Review #3653

It's hard to believe that I hadn't stopped by here before, but after buying a "healthy" lunch at Duos, I thought picking up a slightly indulgent snack for later was a good idea.  Located on the main intersection of the food hall at City Market, I browsed the display counter of available cookie options and narrowed down my order to an oatmeal raisin, a chocolate chip, and a peanut butter cookie.  I was a nice guy and shared them with my wife when I got home (which was an accomplishment that they made it that far.)    The cookies run just under a $1 each and have decent size to them.  I found most had a little bit of bite/crunch to them with the oatmeal raisin have a bit more of a chew factor (all of which I expect and appreciate.)    I was glad that they allow credit cards for orders as small as $3 since I had used up my cash the day before.  Fortunately, the tax put my order over the minimum and I didn't have to sacrifice my treats.    If you are downtown and like picking up a small treat for yourself with minimal wait, check out this shop in the market.  Review #3606

I stopped in Wednesday morning for a quick cup of coffee and a scone.  After a short wait in line, they took my order.  On the coffee, they asked if they needed to leave room for cream or if they could top it off.  On the scone, they offered to heat it (microwave).  It definitely added to the flavor to warm it up without making the scone chewy.    Be aware the coffee is extremely hot and will take awhile to cool down.    I was able to meet a friend and we were able to sit and chat without any pressure to move on as it seems to be a popular place for folks to log on and work while they sip their coffee.    Overall, it was a good experience and the prices seemed reasonable for a bistro.  Review #156

I should have read the reviews before going.  I had a general sense that Indy Reads Books was an independent book seller and that they had some literacy program affiliation.  But I was unaware of all the events and activities the non-profit side of the business participated in.  Since I am not that familiar with them, I base my experience upon my visit as someone just stopping in.  The shop is located at the bend in Mass Avenue across the street from Rooster's  and Black Market.  Parking is limited in front of the store, but there is street parking available if you don't mind the walk (some is metered.)  Inside the shop, the checkout counter is located near the front and also acts as an information booth.  To the left is where you will find cds, dvds, and some books.  Throughout the store, you will find a mix of used and new books by general categories.  I found it interesting that there were a few nooks where seating was available.    In the back on the left is a children's section that is loaded with affordable options.    The shop is filled with a diverse selection that apparently has a lot of turnover, so if you don't find something while there, just ask to see if they may have it or can get it for you.  The place feels more like a library than a bookstore with its hardwood floors and inviting atmosphere.  Definitely worth a stop when exploring Mass Ave.  Review #3464

I went on a Sunday afternoon to this beer garden in Irvington.  There wasn't any special event going on, so there wasn't any food available, or entertainment like a party or movie.  Just a nice open space with pergolas, a variety of tables, and a fire pit.  I will also say that going by myself didn't help any since there was nothing going on but people with their dogs drinking beer.    Getting here is also odd.  You can see the venue from Bonna Avenue, but you can't drive straight back to it.  There is a fenced off private parking lot directly north of the garden, so you have to enter on the gravel (and somewhat bumpy) driveway on the east side of Coal Yard Coffee and then drive back behind that building to use the gravel lot east of the garden.  There is a metal ramp to get up to the garden level and then most of the patio area is a wooden deck.  I did find it odd that the area by the fire pit is not level with the deck and has a different base.  I wasn't watching and nearly stumbled when I stepped off the 1 1/2" drop while going towards the pit seating.    During my visit, I didn't notice any wait staff, just a guy sitting inside the building behind a counter.  I couldn't read the handwritten names on the taps, so I had to ask what they had available.  After I learned that they don't do flights, I settled on trying their Oktoberfest (a German Marzen ale).  They serve in plastic cups and I noticed a number of covered trash cans around the patio for convenience.  The beer was okay, but not my favorite.  The patio was nice, but I could sit on my own porch and drink a beer.  I thought the bartender would be a little more welcoming when I mentioned it was my first visit and when I asked about flights, he said I should just go to the regular brewery on Washington Street.  They had no intention of serving those here.  My advice?  Watch their Facebook page for an event.  Go with some friends and bring your own food to snack on.  Otherwise, it is just a nice place for the locals to hang out and gather with their dogs.  Review #3178

Plat 99 is the house bar and coffee lounge for the Alexander Hotel. It sits on the second floor overlooking the activity of CityWay.  From early morning until 3, it is a coffee and pastry shop.  Only after three does it begin offering cocktails and the menu items listed on their webpage for customers to get a side dish or something from the kitchen.  Plat 99 has a gorgeous interior which was designed by artist Jorge Pardo who also created all the beautifully shaped and colored lights that hang inside and out into the lobby/stairway that leads up to the lounge.  (Note that elevators are available on the other side of the lobby.)  Inside the lounge, the bar area forms a central rectangle with a number of small tables all around for guests to nestle into.  Note that there are no bar stools and no waitress service (at least during the coffee shop hours.)  The woman behind the counter was very pleasant and was able to converse while getting my Tinker Coffee (ready to drink!) and offered to heat my cranberry muffin for me.  Both were excellent!  The atmosphere was very open with windows all around the lounge.  Quite different than a lot of closed off coffee houses I've been to.    I will definitely have to come back during the evening hours to check out the bar for their house cocktails.  I've had some at their annual Miracle on South Street pop-up and enjoyed those.  Note that there is affordable metered street parking available or a somewhat more expensive parking garage on the north side of the hotel.  Review #3334

Location, location, location!  That's what makes this park hold its value.  It has a hill in the center of the park that offers one of the best views of downtown available from the east side, i.e.  for watching the sunset or fireworks.   Other than that, the park does have some nice paths to walk, plenty of large trees for shade, a playground with swings, and a shelter with a grill.  Unfortunately, it doesn't have a dedicated parking lot (street parking is free if you can find it.)  It also has no restroom facilities or running water fountains, so plan accordingly.    The park seemed fairly well maintained, but I hear it gets crowded during celebrations.  Review #512

I decided to give Barbecue and Bourbon a try one Saturday for lunch (4-23-16).  I was glad they had several parking spaces right next to the building since the street parking was getting full.  I walked passed the outdoor seating and entered the shotgun style building.  I was greeted quickly and shown a seat by my waitress.  I looked over the menu and was thinking about the slow roasted brisket, but decided to ask my waitress for a recommendation after telling her which way I was leaning.  She mentioned that they were running a lunch special "7 for $7" (Seven types of hamburgers for $7 each).  She recommended the Beef and Cheddar Burger - a nice sized burger with roasted beef (brisket?) pieces on top and then smothered with Cheddar.  Sounded like the best option.  I also ordered the onion rings and cole slaw and a beverage.  After a short wait, she brought out the burger and chips in one basket and the other two sides in another.  My little table was full!  The Good News:  The Beef and Cheddar Burger was fantastic!  One of the five best burgers I have had this year.  The flavors were spot on and blended so well together.  (My pet peeve is trying fancy burgers that I can't even taste the beef.)  I highly recommend this meat lover's delight.    I also really liked their cole slaw.  It wasn't smothered in mayo....even though there was some liquid left in the bottom of the bowl, the cabbage was flavored but not masked.  Really good!  The Not so Good News:  The Onion Rings were a train wreck to look at.  The flavor was okay, but the cook/chef skipped a step in separating the inner membranes from between the onion rings, so there were a number of rings that the membrane pulled away during cooking, which makes the coating pop off or look deformed.  Okay, they are just onion rings, so not that big a deal, but it was a missed opportunity to have a completely fabulous lunch.  I plan to return with some friends in the near future.  Review #24

Although I still have my concerns about noise levels and parking, the food and service at this restaurant are so good that it is worth the inconvenience.  We went at 5 and were able to find street parking on Mass Avenue ($3 for 2 hours).  Because it was a warm spring day, the restaurant was able to open their windows wide and allow a nice breeze into the place.  Because the windows were open, the noise level dropped though the background music was still a bit louder than I would have liked.  The outdoor patio on the second floor is now open and is accessible by stairs or elevator for those who may need assistance.  Our server (Justin) did a great job and had a pleasant attitude while taking car of us.  He managed the wait time between courses so that we weren't waiting long periods between our dishes.  And the food was delicious!  Not only did it taste great, but the presentations were as colorful as they were tasty.  (See photos)  We started off with the Street Corn (we had it served off the cob in order to share it) and the Brussels Sprouts.  Both were topped with Cotija cheese and cilantro with lime.  The corn also had a nice chipotle mayo that added another layer to the flavor.  I decided to go with the Red Drum (white fish) that was grilled enough to bring out the grill flavor while staying moist inside.  Beneath the fish were sweet plantains and yuca fries.  The fish was topped with a tasty chorizo chutney.  Excellent!  The ladies went with the Taco Salad.  Although they thought there was a heat element in the salad, I didn't find anything spicy in the mix.  The salad had beef, poblana crema, guacamole, lettuce, roasted tomato, and black beans.  It was topped with some crispy yuca chips that they also enjoyed.  For dessert, I went with the Tres Leches.  The gals went with the Apple Flan.  All were really good.  My only suggestion is that since both come with coffee ice cream, it would be nice to offer vanilla ice cream as a substitute since neither of the gals drinks coffee.  (More for me, but a little disappointing for them.)  If you want an enjoyable evening of dining and can get here before it gets too crowded, Livery is the place to go!  Rev. #26

This small Asian restaurant is tucked away in a stripmall on the north end of the International Marketplace.  I found plenty of parking out front and entered for lunch just before the place started getting busy.  The restaurant offers Vietnamese and some Chinese food items.  I decided to go with the Yelper recommended Bun Bo Hue (Spicy Noodle Soup) with lots of long thin noodles, beef, "beef tender" and pork.  While waiting for my entrée, I ordered a small batch (3) of Crabmeat Rangoon.  The rangoon came out soon and were still steaming hot inside.  Although the wrap was generally crisp, there was a slight chewiness to it.  The flavor was quite good, but the chewiness was enough to detract my attention from the flavor.  Before long, the soup arrived and Wow!  What a huge bowl!  The bowl was a full 9 inches across three inches deep.  It was filled with a spicy broth, long thin noodles, and cuts of beef, beef tender (?) and pork.  On the side comes a small plate loaded with bean sprouts, a lime wedge, sprigs of purple basil, and sliced jalapeno peppers with seeds.  I asked the waitress and she said to squeeze the lime into the broth first, then add the sprouts, basil (leaves only), and pepper a little at a time to allow them to cook/infuse more flavor.  The Positive:  The broth, once it cooled a bit, was excellent!  It had a bit of heat that I would rate about medium, so a bit spicier than I normally get.  The noodles were tender like the noodles you get in canned soup.  The noodles also didn't have much flavor on their own.  The sprouts added a bit of savory and the basil seemed to take on a bit of licorice flavor.    The Negative:  In their defense, the waitress asked me if I minded that the pork was fatty.  I figured that the fat would add flavor to the broth.  However, the pork was thick cut and not only had fat, but also had the rind (skin) which was tough and chewy.  I basically chewed the pork meat from the fat and set the fat aside on the side plate.  That was manageable once I realized that every piece of pork was like that.  What was bad was that the pork and the beef pieces were completely overcooked and tough to chew.  And, instead of picking up flavor from the spices, seemed blanched and flavorless.  So, I'll settle on an average score for the excellent broth and the disappointing meats.  I hadn't seen any comments about the texture problems of the meat in any of the positive reviews of the dish on Yelp. Maybe it was just a bad day in the kitchen.  Review #569

I can't believe I don't have a review for Chatham Tap on Mass Ave until now.  I remember going here for lunch and enjoying the English Pub atmosphere even when there wasn't a soccer game on television and I wasn't having a beer.  I remember good service and some tasty food.  When some recent developments in my life necessitated my being downtown near lunch time five days a week, I remembered that Chatham Tap had some really tasty "Prince Dean's Angel Wings" that seemed to be calling my name.  Despite the pandemic and the blocking of Mass Avenue to through traffic, my wife found a spot to park and wait nearby while I walked over to pick up my carry out order (twice in the last couple weeks.)  Sure, you may find less expensive wings, but I'm telling you that you can order the wings in different quantities and they do offer different flavors for the wings including teriyaki, BBQ, Indian Curry, or chipotle-apricot, but I went with the house flavoring once and a split between the signature sauce and some teriyaki.  The wings were excellent and the staff, despite the social distancing on my recent trips were efficient and friendly when transacting our exchange.  Sadly, I forgot to get photos of these tasty treats, but I encourage you to stop by and see/taste for yourself.  Treat yourself to something remarkable and try some wings for yourself.  Review #3765

When I dine out, I usually support independent/local businesses.  But when it comes to ice cream, I bend that rule a bit.  Sure, Greenwood has a local favorite, but the lines tend to be long.  I was hoping to find some ice cream and another local spot in the mall looked like it had gone out of business, so I got on Yelp and found this place just across the street!  This is the third Cold Stone Creamery I've been to in the metro area and I will say they have a consistency of quality that I appreciate.  After grabbing a parking spot to the side of the building, I was greeted (as were all subsequent customers) when I entered.
