There is a large display counter with buckets of flavored ice creams and menus with lots of pre-determined combinations.  You can also build your own (they build it according to your requests) with a wide variety of flavors and toppings.  I decided to go with the Founder's Favorite made with Sweet Cream ice cream, pecans, brownie, chocolate fudge syrup, and caramel.  Yum!  I chose just a small serving in a cup after seeing the calories skyrocket as the servings get larger.    I like that there are combos already determined.  Sometimes, there are so many choices and not everything I pick seems to work well together.  This is the third different combo I've tried and they all seem really good.  Fortunately, someone came from the back of the business to help out as the hot day was making the line grow longer.  The two employees seemed to work well together and soon had the line handled.  Not the cheapest ice cream around, but because of all the ingredients and the "hands on" approach of mixing the ingredients together instead of just layering them, I don't mind occasionally stopping by and getting something tasty.  Review #2729

I'm trying to figure out what the big deal is about another franchise coming to town...especially one that specializes in hot dogs. SMH  I've heard people rave about the original in Chicago and about the crazy lines in Fishers, so I decided to avoid the things that make for a bad experience (long lines, long waits, no parking) and come for lunch during the week well after their grand opening in Avon.    There seemed to be plenty of parking here and we were pleasantly greeted by a man passing out menu flyers so that we could look over their selections while we waited in line.  It looked rather long, but to their credit, the line moved quickly.  By the time we reached the bend, we had our selections in mind and another employee asked us what we wanted.  She wrote our order on a paper bag and when we got to the counter, gave the bag to the cashier who repeated our order and asked any pertinent questions related to our order so that we knew what our options were.  We paid and were given an order number on our receipt before being directed to the other end of the building to pick up our lunch.    I suggested my wife pick out a spot to sit while I waited about ten minutes for my order number to be called.  There was a slight mix up, but it was corrected in less than a minute, so overall, things went pretty well.  I stopped and picked up my napkins, straws, ketchup, and salt at a counter near the entrance and then hunted down my wife to join her with our meal.  She picked a spot, but it hadn't been wiped down completely between guests, so we sat to the other side of the table (4-top).  She ordered the Jumbo Hot Dog which it truly was.  It came with a host of toppings including mustard, relish, celery salt, chopped onions, tomato, a pickle spear, and sport peppers on a sesame seed bun.  She liked the flavor of the dog, but thought the onions a bit strong and wasn't sure why the relish was a bright green....had to be some artificial coloring since I've never seen pickle relish that color.  Okay flavor, but not something she would order again.  I got the Italian Beef (I went with the standard presentation) and selected the sweet peppers.  I also ordered a small fry.  The fries were good and salted ahead of time.  No problem there.  The beef was juicy and very tender, and had a decent amount of meat in the French bread bun.  The pepper was very mild as was the beef flavor.  I kept wondering what I was missing....it just didn't have much flavor.  I think everything was cooked properly, but there wasn't any "wow" to the sandwich....just very ordinary.  So, back to my original question....why all the fanfare?  I doubt I will ever understand it.  Review #1355

My wife and I are big fans of Holcomb Gardens; so much so that we were married by the gardens back in '83.  Over the years, the park has maintained its basic appeal with long rows of gardens & hedges, art sculptures,  a pond/fountain, and benches with words of wisdom from philosophers and writers.  There is a roundabout with parking along the edges once you've descended the hill past the pond and observatory.  A small waterfall and springs is on the right as you near the parking.  The gardens have a gazebo and a permanent shelter that can be rented in case of inclement weather.  (We had our reception there.)  The park is also located along the canal, so if you want photo ops or are looking for a start finish spot, this might be the place for your adventure.  Review #1174

I made my first trip to this buffet after having lived in town for over six years and I will say that the food is pretty good, at least it's as good as the stuff you can buy prepackaged at the grocery (from the freezer section.)  I was surprised at how large the dining area was and how many buffet lines (five in total) were available to choose from.  But I found the staff a bit difficult to communicate with and maybe it's just a cultural thing, but they don't interact with the customers any more than the minimum.  When I entered and let the hostess know I was by myself, I was directed to follow a server who showed me to a table.  She provided my napkins, utensils, and asked my drink order.  After bringing my drink, she then disappeared.  I have been to restaurants that have buffets as an option, but also allow you to order from a menu.  No menu here.  I've also been to buffets where they charge you by the weight of your purchase.  No scales here.  And in almost every case, the server/hostess has directed me to help myself when ready or at least asked if I had any questions.  I tried talking with the server and she thought I was asking her to get the food for me.  Again, difficulty in communicating.  So, I helped myself to one of the five buffet lines.  I started with a salad.  When I finished, I left my used plate on my table and grabbed another plate to try some Chinese foods, including the egg drop soup (help yourself to additional plates and bowls as needed.)  By the time I got back to my table, my old plate was cleared.  Yeah!  What surprised me was that none of the other reviews have mentioned that there are quite a few American dishes to eat here:  pizza slices, fish, chicken wings, Texas toast, and a separate line devoted to desserts.  Who knew?  It appears that you can continue going to get more food until you pop or decide you've had enough.  All for under $10.  Just amazes me how people think it's too expensive.   Anyway, now that I know they have a wide variety of food options and that you help yourself whenever you are ready, I would probably have a better experience on a return trip.    Oh, I also recommend flagging down your server when you are ready so that she can bring your bill.  You pay at the front desk when you are finished.  Review #1992

Opening day of this new coffee franchise (from Iowa) saw long lines in both the drive thru and walk up counter.  The line was constant from 6 a.m. to when I got there around 10:30.  Yet everyone, staff and customers, seemed in a good mood.  The line moved along and allowed plenty of time to see the menu of beverages, pastries, and sandwiches, both breakfast and lunch.  While waiting, one of the staff asked customers if they wanted to be part of the rewards program offered.  I noticed there was a small dining room and another beyond that.  Since both were full I decided to get my order to go.  I placed my order for a short medium roast black coffee, a mixed berry biscuit, a #1 breakfast sandwich with egg, sausage, and cheese, and a #5 Cabin Club turkey & ham on marbled rye.  After paying and giving my name, I took my drip coffee and waited with those ahead of me who were also getting food and/or a special beverage.  I must say I really liked the breakfast sandwich that was served on a plain bagel.  Nice flavor without needing any seasoning.   The mixed berry biscuit was just a bit dry on the outside, but when eaten with the tasty fruit in the middle, was also quite good.  The Cabin Club had a thick layer of folded sliced ham and turkey along with tomato and lettuce on marbled rye.  Nice flavor but since it didn't have any condiments, it seemed a bit dry.  I don't recall seeing packets while there but it would have been nice to be asked if I wanted any condiments or directed to them by the staff.  Fortunately, I had them at home and made the sandwich taste better.  Note:  Though the meats were layered thick in the middle, they were not layered evenly across the entirety of the bread.  And the coffee?  Served so hot that I couldn't hold my cup even with the insulator.  I waited at least 5 minutes before trying to sip it and still burned my tongue.  Eventually, it cooled enough to drink.  It had a slightly burned taste that kept it from being a satisfying brew.  Overall, the food was enjoyable and reasonably priced.  I would encourage them to reduce the coffee temperature after roasting it so that folks who drink the coffee straight can enjoy it without waiting a long time to determine if it is burned or not.  Review #2608

Although I don't stop for ice cream often, I will say that this chain has some of the better options available.  This shop was clean, had plenty of free parking in the shared lot, and it looked like the ice cream tubs/barrels on display were maintained and full.  (I hate looking through a long list of options only to find out the place is out of my first choice!)    The ice cream is fairly rich tasting and the flavors seem true to the description.  Not the cheapest place around, but that's okay as long as the quality is good and the wait isn't too long.  Prompt service and we were on our way!  Review #2626

This was my first visit to this shop on the east end of the fashion mall.  I didn't realize it was a part of the Pottery Barn/Williams-Sonoma business group.  The space was very open and easy to move around without feeling cramped.  Yet, despite the high ceilings and open space, it still felt cozy due to all the soft touches that were in each room.  Generally speaking, each section of the store featured an area of the home and items to consider adding to your own.  There was a section for bedding, one for dining/kitchen, and several for family areas or something to accessorize your bedroom.  Lots of cloth items and some plants (mostly small cactus in pots), and some knick knacks.  Although there were visible employees working the counter or stocking, I was not greeted or offered assistance by anyone while I browsed through the store.  That didn't stop me from looking around, but would have been more likely to encourage a purchase.  They do have some nice looking items that if I was looking to replace something in my home, would definitely consider coming back for.  Review #3301

I took my wife to "that place where they have you try on shoes and then walk on the treadmills to make sure you're walking right."   It took me a while to remember it (I had ducked out to the pastry shop the last time), but when we got close, I remembered that this shop on the south end of a strip mall just south of old town Zionsville helped her find some really good shoes.   We pulled into the small lot behind the shop and entered into this split level shop (Note:  They do have a ramp for accessibility between the levels.)  Before long, we were greeted and my wife was assisted in finding some new shoes.  While there, another customer arrived in running gear and the other worker helped her find shoes, let her run on the treadmill to try them out and filmed the running to show the customer alignment issues that could be corrected by shoe adjustments.  Very cool!  But since my wife's running days are passed, the walking sufficed and she was able to pick up a pair that felt really comfortable and order another pair in a different color since they only have certain colors in house.    My wife also liked that she was able to donate her older shoes and received a discount on her purchase (Note:  I'm not sure how that program works, but it is worth asking about if you are someone who replaces their athletic shoes every six months or yearly.)  I will say one last thing...the store only has a couple working at a time, so if it is busy, you may have to wait awhile because the staff focus on the customers they are with.  They did acknowledge the new customers, but some did get tired of waiting and leave.  Plan accordingly.  Review #2135

My wife and I brought a friend to Delicia for her first visit on an early Tuesday evening.  We were seated promptly and had great service throughout the evening.  The complimentary Sancocho soup was a big hit.  In fact, our guest wished that it was a menu item!  We sampled the Guacamole and the Salsa Trio:  Salsa Fresca (mild); Sikil Pak (roasted pumpkin seed);  and Tomatillo (spicy, but not hot).  My wife and our friend liked the salsa Fresca and the Guacamole, but were not fans of the other two flavors. (That meant more for me!!)  Our friend ordered the Short Ribs with Ancho Salsa - braised boneless short ribs, ancho salsa, roasted vegetables, white sweet potato mash.  Although she was fond of the sweet potato mash that was underneath the ribs, she found the flavor of the short ribs to taste more like a roast beef sandwich than like ribs.  Good, but not what she was expecting.  My wife ordered the Tamal Corn Cakes - barbacoa beef, pico de gallo, crema, queso fresco, herb green rice.  She did enjoy the entree cakes, but found the side of green rice too heavy on the cilantro flavor.  I assume they use that much herb to achieve the green coloration, but the flavor of the rice was overpowered by the herb.  I decided to push my boundaries by ordering the Cazuela de Mariscos - mussels, calamari, scallops, shrimp, rice, white wine-saffron sauce, and two grilled baguettes.  I enjoyed the flavor of the various seafoods (my only previous experience with mussels was a bad one at a famous downtown seafood restaurant chain.)  There was a lot more sauce than I expected, making the dish seem almost like soup.  However, the rice had excellent flavor and paired very nicely with the sauce.  The sauce was spicy, but not spicy hot.  I did think some of the seafood got a little rubbery from sitting in the hot (temperature) sauce, but not to the point where it was a problem.  Overall, the flavor was delicious.      Overall, I have enjoyed both of my visits to Delicia and have found my food and dining experience to be quite good.  But I feel I can't ignore the opinions of my guests who were less  than "wowed" by their experience.  So only four stars this time.  Rev #3

There is a new Chinese restaurant in the Town Center Plaza that is giving it a go.  I believe it to be an independent restaurant, but has all the standard chain offerings that seem to be pretty popular in the area.  As part of a strip mall, there is plenty of free parking in the lot.    Inside, they have done a complete makeover of the lobby and small shotgun style dining area.  Warm yellow walls, black and white flooring and wainscoting, and teal benches make for an inviting interior though it was kept rather dimly lit.  I decided to get my order to go and after placing my order and paying, grabbed one of the chairs in the lobby by the window.  I didn't see any wait staff, so I believe you are supposed to grab your own supplies from a counter where you pay if you are going to dine in.  Otherwise, you should have all the napkins, sauces, and plastic utensils inside your to go bag.  I was ordering for dinner, so I selected Egg Drop Soup (thick and yellow, but not much seasoning), crab rangoon (6 in an order and quite crisp with a sweet red sauce), and the peppered steak entree that comes with white rice.  The flavor was mild and okay, but the peppers were cut into too large of chunks to be bite sized and I wasn't supplied a plastic knife (which probably wouldn't have cut the peppers).   Fortunately, I was able to dump it out onto a plate at home and take care of it.  But if you were trying to eat directly from the little white box, you would have some challenge.  My wife sampled my dinner and thought that it was okay, but not anything special other than if you simply wanted a quick Chinese to go dinner.  I will say that the lunch specials are priced at only $5.50 and include fried rice and your choice of an egg roll or crab rangoon.   There are 25 lunch special options listed!  Anyway, the food was good, but nothing unique.  The service was efficient and easy to communicate with.  It's nice to have another option for dining in the area.  Review #2574

This long time coffee shop has found a way to do a lot of things right!  First, though they are in Broad Ripple, they managed to carve out a small parking lot in the back of their shop that if you are lucky, you can enter via the alley next to the shop.  Next, they provided a handy rear entrance to the shop for those lucky souls, as well as a nice front entrance that is a bit more welcoming.  Both entrances have spots for visitors to relax and check their devices while they enjoy their purchases.  For folks like me who still like drip coffee, they have multiple options to try each day.  I went with the Choo Choo Brew which was a rich black coffee, full of flavor, but not too strong.  As the barista stated, this is the coffee that launched the business.    I also picked up a tasty wedge of coffee cake that was sweet and had a bit of cinnamon and some crumble on top for a little more texture than the main cake body of the wedge.  Very tasty too!  The servers behind the counter were keeping everyone satisfied and were quite helpful with answering questions.  Seems like a really nice place to relax and if you have to, get some work done.  Note:  I love that they serve the drip coffee at ready to drink temperatures!  That's the only way a coffee house will be considered for a five star rating from me.  Review #2105

Some things just make sense.  You want good steak?  Go to a steak house.  You want a good burger?  Go to a burger place.  (I hate reviews that order some obscure menu item and then complain that it wasn't the best they had ever had.  Really???)  So it seems to make sense that if you are a meat eater, but want to try something Vegan, then go to a place that specializes in Vegan foods and has a lot of options for you to try.  That was the case for my visit to Three Carrots' new sit down restaurant on Virginia Avenue, on the Fountain Square side of the interstate overpass.  My visit came during the first week and the sign wasn't even up on the outside and the roof was being worked on.  It may not look open if you drive by, but trust me, it is and ready to serve!  So, after finding free street parking, I entered into the newly refurbished building.  The interior was a mixture of artistic ceiling lanterns and art work with bare concrete floors and unadorned tables.  There were a number of two-top and some longer tables, and in the back on the left side, some bar stool seating.  I was greeted promptly and sat at one of the two-tops.  The waitress brought me a menu of lunch items as well as beverages (including alcoholic types) to choose from.    Being curious and having had little exposure to Vegan cuisine, I thought it best to order something that had meat and dairy counterparts out in the restaurant world.  I started with the "Mac and Cheese Croquettes" and then ordered the "Seitanderloin" as my sandwich.  The croquettes are made from what looks like mac and cheese, then rolled in breading, and deep fried.  I got five croquettes, somewhere between the sizes of golf balls and tennis balls, and my choice of BBQ or Buffalo sauce.  Too big for even my big mouth, I cut each croquette and dipped them into the sauce.  Wow!  Very nice texture and flavor.  The BBQ sauce had a little bit of heat (mostly in the aftertaste) and really complemented the M&C.  I still don't know what binding agent they use instead of cheese, but whatever it was, it did a fair job of looking like cheese and mostly held the croquette together.  Note that once you break the outer breading, there is enough moisture inside that the noodles may not stay in place.  At least they weren't dry and pasty, so chasing a stray noodle wasn't too much to accept.  Moving on to the sandwich, it also did a fair job of taking on the look of a breaded tenderloin, even extending beyond the bun as all good tenderloins do!  The sandwich comes impaled with a steak knife for those who like to slice their sandwich in half.  Here I encountered one of the negatives.  The "meat" part of the sandwich was a bit overcooked and made slicing through the sandwich neatly a bit difficult.  The sandwich also comes stacked with tomatoes, lettuce, red onion, mustard, and garlic aioli, and maybe some pickle (I don't recall seeing them, but they are listed on the menu.)  I ended up toppling my sandwich halves during the carving, but quickly reassembled the halves and took my first bite.... and I liked it!  The bit of overcooking made for a delightful crunch which my teeth had no trouble cutting through.  The flavor was very similar to a seasoned breaded tenderloin and provided a satisfying chew.  (I've had an under cooked bean burger elsewhere before and it fell apart, so I recommend erring on the side of crispy, not soggy.)    The sandwich also came with blue chips and salsa on the side.  The chips were crisp and the salsa a bit tangy, but served in a very small round dish.  Since the salsa was not thick, it tended to fall off the pointed end of the chips.  I ended up breaking my chips into smaller pieces to better scoop out more salsa.  Hopefully, the mgmt will figure out a better way to make salsa dipping easier.  Service was friendly, welcoming, and prompt.  Water was iced in pitchers and was topped off during my meal.  Noise level was moderate with a mixture of music styles playing over the speakers.  Overall, even if you aren't a Vegan, they have very approachable options that are available if you want to expand your palate exposure.  I did, and I liked it!  Review #461

I stopped in during the week around 5 and was able to take a spot at the bar where I was greeted by Jesse who was one of two people working behind the counter.  Even though the place had just opened, there was a smooth flow of activity...no dawdling around.  While providing water and utensils, we discussed my options for selecting a wine flight to go with the food choices I was leaning towards (the Brussels Sprouts salad and the Crab & Lobster Cakes).  Note that I could have had a single wine or taken advantage of the 9 oz carafe for a discounted price on Wednesdays.  But having looked over their online menu, I was aware of their extensive list of wines and particularly, wine pairings to create three 2-oz tastings that would allow me to sample more wine without having too much to drink.  We agreed upon the Amelia Earhart flight (pun intended...I think) which is three types of Chardonnay arranged in a specific order.  What I will say is that the selection from Chablis FR that started off the flight was my favorite.  Maybe it was due to being the first one I sampled while waiting for my food, but it was excellent to my palate.  As I was finishing the first sample, my Brussels Sprouts salad arrived.  It was a large serving which would normally be shareable, but I am no piker when it comes to eating large amounts if I want to, so I gladly devoured these.  I will say they weren't the most appealing looking dish I've had, but made up for it in skill and flavor.  The sprouts were done to a level of crispness that I really enjoy where there is almost a chip like crunch on the outer leaves and a satisfying chew to the rest.  They were dressed with a chili and sweet potato (diced) salsa and a lime vinaigrette for the acidity to balance with the savory veggies and spice from the chili.  Great start.  Before I finished the large plate of sprouts, my duo of Crab & Lobster cakes with lobster curds and pea sprouts arrived.  Although there was a faint hint of sea smell, the pairing of the pea sprouts, the creamy sauce and the cakes was delicious.  I will recommend using a knife to cut the pea sprouts because they are a little too large to easily fit into your mouth, particularly if they have the sauce on them.  I was simply using my fork for the tender cakes and realized I was not being the most elegant trying to fit the uncut stems into my mouth.  Thankfully, I was dining alone and no one saw my clumsy attempts.  All too soon the food and wine where gone, so I asked for a dessert menu and selected the Chocolate Chip Beignets which come coated in sugar, on a plate decorated with a bourbon chocolate ganache and berries, with a small dipping cup of Anglaise on the side.  The four beignets were bite-sized for me, but some may prefer to cut them.  I was able to spear each, dredge them through the chocolate, spear a berry or two and then dip.  Yum!  Delicious!    As you can tell from my description, this wasn't a cheap place to get full, but rather, an elegant space with a very professional (helpful and friendly) staff, and food that is generally small plate in portion.  The price for the wine flight is what seemed to raise the price quickly, but I knew the prices ahead of time (their online menu lists all the details, so nobody should be surprised by the cost.)  Of course, parking is always a challenge on Mass Ave where there are pay spots and that horrendous straight in parking that makes patrons have to back across both lanes of traffic just to get their vehicle clear of the cars next to them.  I'm hoping the business owners will demand it go back to the angle parking!  If you are looking for a fine dining experience on the north end of downtown with lots of options for wine, give this place a try.  Review #2427

Having tried Tinker Coffee at quite a few local coffee shops, I decided to finally head downtown to the source of those fine brews to get some for home.  The location does not have a "fresh pot brewing" for you, so if you are thinking it's a coffee shop, you would be mistaken.  What it does have is the source beans and a large roaster and the end product sold (as whole beans or ground) in 12 oz. bags.  When I entered, I was greeted and the man asked what kind of coffee I liked, what I used to make it, and then made recommendations for the coffees that best fit that description.  I picked up a couple of the resealable bags:  One was Muheres Cafeteras  (Coffee Women) which is medium coffee from Colombia that is from a collective of over 300 female coffee producers.  It has hints of Granny Smith apples, cinnamon, and jam.  I don't have the best equipment at home, and may not have made it quite strong enough, but the flavors were very subtle, but nice.  I also picked up a Finca La Aurora (Villa Aurora) from Nicaragua which is another medium blend with hints of chocolate, shortbread, and red apple.  This one was my preferred flavor as the accents came through a little better on my equipment and balanced out quite well.  Neither of the choices had the bitterness I've found in store bought coffee.  Yeah!  As I wrote earlier, there was a balance in the flavor so that though there is probably some bitterness, it didn't dominate the flavor.  For those who are interested, there are occasional "cupping" events on site that cost $15 for a class (90 to 120 minutes) held on select Saturdays.  You do have to reserve a spot on their website to attend since they limit the class size to make it manageable for the staff and enjoyable for the visitors.  I hope to make one of the upcoming classes soon so I can learn all about the finer points of appreciating coffee nuances.  Until then, I will simply enjoy what I have just purchased.  Review #2133

After catching a film at the local Showtime Cinema that started at noon, I was looking for something to eat and realized I had never stopped in at this franchised pizza place on my way home.  It is tucked away down a frontage street near the Walgreens and because of the mid-afternoon time frame, I had the place to myself.  I entered and after just a moment, I was greeted and I explained I would like to get a personal sized pizza and some garlic breadsticks to go.  She showed me where the menus were and I was able to quickly decide upon a Hawaiian style pizza with my choice of thin crust.  I also decided to go with a marinara dipping sauce instead of the cheese option for the bread sticks.    What is nice is that they have an open view to the kitchen and they got right on my order (as well as some to go orders that had been called in.)  In about 15 minutes, my order was ready and I was on my way.  The price was less than I expected and the flavor was really good.  I had never had a Hawaiian with the additional flavors this one had.  Sliced almonds and Cinnamon powder were added to the shaved ham and pineapple.  Really tasty!  The breadsticks were soft and warm and not too overloaded with garlic.  I like that I could pick up the breadsticks without getting butter all over my hands.    Overall, I enjoyed my meal and the prompt service I received.  Review #3461

If you like Sun King, then this is a must visit spot for you.  I was able to attend a soft opening at this new location and even though they were still supposed to be working things out, I couldn't find anything that they needed to work on.  First, finding the place is pretty easy.  It is located in the former Thr3e Wise Men location on Broad Ripple Avenue.  It's in the first plaza on the east side of where the Monon Trail crosses.  What makes it even better is that there is a parking lot right next to the building, so that makes it even more appealing than some of the other spots in BR.  The interior is arranged very similarly to the previous brewery with the bar to your left and dining/seating area with tables to your right.  A private party room is also available back towards the kitchen.  I ordered a flight from a fairly large list of brews.  Note that they have cocktails and wine here too, though I didn't spend much time looking at the menu.  Note that all the menus should expand once they have their Grand Opening.   If you have the munchies or even desire a full blown meal, that will be offered by their chosen in house restaurant, Offshore Broad Ripple.  Offshore is run by Pier 48 which just opened a seafood restaurant downtown.  Offshore will be more "farm to table" than seafood.  One of the things I noticed about during the soft opening is that I was able to pay both Brewery and Restaurant on the same bill (which is different than the other Sun King locations.  I hope they keep this convenience.  And the beer?  I like trying beers from across the board.  I will say my favorite today was "Probably an IPA" New England IPA.  Great balance!  And though I thought the "TrollStorm" Porter (11% abv) started a bit over the top, the more I drank, the better I adjusted to it, especially when eating my flatbread.  By the bottom of the flight glass, I was sold!  Service was friendly and frequent enough to keep us from waiting for anything.  Check out was right at our table with one of those hand held electronic readers which meant my card never left my sight!  Another plus!  If I had any negatives, it might be that the prices were on the upper end.  $10 for a flight of four isn't outrageous, but it definitely is on the high side of brewery prices in the state.  If you like Sun King products and want to try them in a new setting, check this place out when they open!  Review #3170

Back when our daughter was little, my wife and I got into building and furnishing dollhouses.  Though I never was very good at it myself, there was something about the miniatures that held my fascination.    So visiting this museum devoted to keeping some amazing dollhouses maintained and then shared with visitors young and old was a fun way to spend some time.  The houses and displays of miniatures are on the floor of the building that is up a small flight of stairs from the entrance.  Note that they do have some parking south of the building, and there is a free public lot across the street to the southwest.  The fee for viewing the museum for adults was $10 which includes getting an electronic device that allows you to hear more information about key houses in the collection by entering the number next to the piece onto your device.  Many also have written information that is different from what you hear.  To its credit, the museum has a wide variety of miniatures.  They have the beautifully ornate pieces which I like.  They also have really old pieces that were hand crafted.  There are some "kits" that were mass produced after WWII made out of metal.  One of the large pieces is even displayed on a turntable so that you can see inside and out.  In addition to the houses, there are some individual rooms that represent works of fiction (Twelve Dancing Princesses, 221b Baker Street, etc) and some that recreate period pieces with furniture that took hours to create.  Chairs that have caned seats and spindles that are hand turned must have been extremely difficult to recreate because they are so small and delicate.  If you like this sort of imagery, then definitely take time to visit.  It is a very nice collection worth the price of admission.  Review #1114

This is an interesting shop to check out while visiting Irvington.  I was surprised to see it open late on a Sunday afternoon (their website says they aren't usually open on Sundays) and decided to stop in.  I'm not a religious person and don't believe in spells and potions and that sort of thing, but I do have respect for other individual's beliefs.  So wandering into here was something new to me.  They have lots of books and hundreds of herbs, they have incense and candles, lots of plants in the front window (not sure if those are for sale), and a room in the back for reading and classes.  They have bumper stickers with spiritual comments, sometimes humorous.  Basically, there are a lot of items to browse through that aren't like what you find in other places.  Apparently there are 50 artisans who provide their wares to the shop.  Review #1990

This is the first Mexican restaurant that I've been to that when I ordered Asada/Steak (plug in any kind of meal), that it tasted like steak!  Seared flavor without being dried out and chewy for a reasonable price.    Back story is that I've driven by here many times and it always looks busy.  I had been there mid afternoon just a few days ago and people were lined out the door (not that it takes many to do that at this tiny shack),  So, while in Speedway and my first two choices being unexpectedly closed that day, I headed north on Highschool Road to give Tortas another try.  I couldn't believe it.  No line!  Only one guy waiting on his food.  I quickly ordered two Asada Burritos to go (There were only three stools inside and one of those was held together with twine.)  While waiting, I could see that they were (a) getting lots of phone orders; and (b) that the shack could use some attention as it is "well worn".  But with the constant barrage of customers, I frankly don't know how they could turn customers away to take care of the repairs.  Before long, I picked up my order and was off.  The "to go" burritos are wrapped in tortillas and then a paper liner and foil to keep them warm.  They are sliced across the middle to allow them to fit into a styrofoam box with sliced jalapenos on the side.  Different sauces were also put into the bag, along with plastic utensils and napkins.  When I got home, I opened my first box and took a bite without adding any of the sauces or peppers.  Wow!  Delicious steak flavor with a bit of cheese, tomato, lettuce, etc.  I don't care if this is authentic or not.  It was delicious and that's why I keep trying new places:  You never know when that next "Wow" moment will come.  I devoured the entire burrito while standing at the counter as my dogs looked enviously on.  Reluctantly, I saved the second burrito for my wife who wouldn't be home for a couple more hours.    When she arrived just after 8, she was hungry and when I told her that there was a steak burrito for her, she gave it a try.  Even a bit cold, she couldn't believe how great tasting this meal was.  It was filling enough we didn't even need sides.  She was brave and ate on the couch as the dogs tried their most pitiful looks to try to get a bite.    If you can find an opening in the line, give this place a try.  It gets two thumbs UP (and a couple paws too!)  Review #2585

Note:  I ate from the lunch menu, not the all you can eat sushi menu.  When I pulled into this strip mall at 111th and Allisonville Road, I was surprised how many restaurants were clustered together.  I was able to find a space out front of Kasai and since it was around 1 pm, I was able to get a seat right away.  The waitress/hostess brought two separate menus:  The first was for ordering from their wide variety of items and included some lunch specials at the back; the second were some laminated checklists for the all you can eat program.  You have to choose before you order....crossing in and out is not allowed.  So, you will have to read some other review of how they thought the all you can eat menu compares.  I didn't need to get stuffed, so I simply went with one of the lunch specials.  So glad I did!  The lunch special comes with a bowl of Miso soup and a side salad with Ginger Dressing (note that they dress it for you and could scale back on how much they use.)  I upgraded the Miso to a Hot and Sour Soup for an extra $1.  I also got to choose two 6-pc rolls:  Eel Roll and Spicy Crunchy (crab) Roll.  The salad came out first and was a true side salad:  mostly iceberg lettuce (crisp) and some small colorful ingredients like a cherry tomato, carrot and red cabbage strips.  The ginger dressing was really good, but I left a lot of it on the bottom of the bowl.  The waitress asked if I preferred a fork which I did, and she brought it over right away.  When the soup came out next, I was surprised how large the serving was.  I'm guessing it was two full cups and it was steaming hot!  I kept stirring it to cool it down because the waitress cautioned me that it was hot.  So, I drink some green tea while waiting.  Before I had made much of a dent in the soup, the two rolls arrived.  So I alternated between bites of the soup, bites of the rolls, and some pickled ginger.  The soup was just thick enough to give it some heartiness.  It had strips of veggies and mushrooms and just a bit of spicy heat on the back of the palate.  Very manageable for me, but maybe a bit too hot for what my wife would want.  I found it perfectly spiced for me.  The crab filled spicy crunch roll had a really nice balance of flavors, especially when dipped in soy sauce.  The eel had a bit more sweetness from the eel sauce, which was again balanced by the salt in the soy sauce.  I found both very fresh tasting, not a hint of fishiness odor or taste.  Good stuff!  The pieces were bite sized, not some over stuffed roll that you can't fit into your mouth.    I've begun eating my sushi without using chopsticks.  I read somewhere that it should be "finger food" and so I've eliminated the frustration of trying to pick up a piece (intact) with chopsticks.  If you struggle with chopsticks like I do, just pick it up and eat it.  It's your food...it's okay!  Very pleasant service without being intrusive.  I would gladly go back!  Review #1876

After making the 50 minute trek to Broad Ripple, we found some paid street parking about a block north of the restaurant.  The store front has limited outdoor seating on the sidewalk in front, and a small amount of "bar" seating by the counter.  Fortunately, there were tables and picnic tables available in the side room, enough to handle the Friday crowd.  We placed our order and paid at the counter, then gave our name for them to call out when they delivered the food to our table.  My wife and I both ordered the smallest of three sizes available for the Cuban, the "mini".  I also ordered the three option Veggie Platter, selecting the Borracha Bean Soup, the Seasoned Yellow Rice, and the plantains for us to share.  We picked a standard table in the festive dining area, Cuban music playing and lots of colorful posters and unusual decorations which made it interesting to look at while waiting for our delivery.  They have paper towel dispensers instead of napkins available and along one wall, additional plastic ware, condiments, toothpicks, and more paper towels were available to "self-serve".  Before long, our food came out and we dug in.  The Cuban which is served in an authentic way with ham (not over salted like American hams), roasted pork, Swiss Cheese, mustard (yellow I think), and pickles all served on the tastiest Cuban Bread!  The bread alone is worth ordering with the thin crispy crust and feather light inside.  The flavors were full and the meats were moist.    The Borracha Soup (Drunken soup) was moderately spiced with just a little heat.  The main flavors were the bean and what tasted like ham to me.  The rice was prepared in chicken broth (turning it yellow) and was seasoned somewhat like a dirty rice if you are familiar with Cajun cooking.  Not sure what spices were used, but again, it had a full flavor, not bland like plain white rice.  The plantains were carmelized and served with a slightly tacky texture on the outside.  The flavor was sweet with a banana like taste.    Since it was our first time, the owner offered us a free sample of their award winning house "coffee".  Although only about the size of a shot, there was a burst of flavor that was more like an after dinner drink than a "morning wake me up".  Really good!  The staff was friendly and were hustling to get the food out.  Be aware that other than bringing out the food, they expect you to help yourself to the drinks, utensils, and to bus your own table when finished.  Just wish they had a way to add tips on the bill instead of using a tip jar.  Too bad this is so far away.  I would like to return again soon!    Review #298

My wife and I stopped in for lunch in this restaurant located on the end of a mini strip mall along US 36, just west of Ronald Reagan Dr.  Plenty of free parking in the lot outside this shotgun set up restaurant.    We were seated promptly and had good service throughout the meal.  We had very small wait times between courses, the table was cleared quickly and water refilled.  The service was really good and kept the rating from going into the negative zone.  Some of the food was really good.  Although they use imitation crab, the crab rangoon which came with a crushed peanut dipping sauce was the best I have had!  It was filled with a generous amount cream cheese and a blend of flavors that made for a great start to our meal.    The edamame, however, was a little under cooked and needed a bit of work for the beans to "pop" from the shell.  They were also salted heavily on the top, but not much on the pods lower in the bowl.    My wife's Thai Dumpling were made from ground chicken and shrimp which were on the bland side when compared to the flavorful pork options I have had elsewhere.  The Ginger Soy Sauce that accompanied the dumplings was a thick sauce that helped, but my wife is not a big fan of ginger, so she wasn't thrilled with the selection.  The soup course (clear chicken noodle for her, Miso for me) was okay.  Since I ordered a Bento Box for lunch, my soup and a salad selection came with the Box.  I ordered a Mixed Seaweed Salad which was more salad greens than I have had elsewhere that features the seaweed in a thread like prep.  The seaweed here was in thin ribbons atop the field greens and dowsed in a salty soy and ginger dressing.  Can't recommend this.  The Bento Box came with a choice of about a half dozen sushi rolls (8 pcs), Seafood Tempura (4 pcs), and a choice of a sashimi or nigiri option.  I went with the really good "Philly Roll" with cream cheese, avocado, seaweed, and a choice of meat (I chose eel) wrapped in a sushi rice.  Very creamy and tasty!  The seafood tempura had two pieces of breaded shrimp and calamari that had a rather bland coating.  I went with the Salmon Sake Sashimi which came with three pieces of salmon served on what I think was chilled radish threads.  The salmon was fine, just not on the same level of what I have had at my favorite places.  This is a nice place and I have not had a chance to try the Thai side of the menu.  However, when it comes to sushi, I cannot recommend this as my first choice.  Review #306

This auto car wash is the closest to my routine journeys, so even though I thought it was supposed to rain, I needed to get my car clean from the road salts that had accumulated and were making it difficult to see my mirrors clearly.    Frankly, I've had some hit and miss dealings here.  They have a fair priced selection of cleanings to offer through their standard pull up/place gear in neutral/hands of the wheel until finished operation.    What makes the difference is how much prewash scrubbing the attendants do before going through.  On this occasion, the guy did a really good job and my car came out looking clean and shiny.    However, on some visits, the attendants didn't do much, particularly along the rear license plate area and I've come out with grime still there because of the shape of my car and the inability of the scrubbing machines to reach there.    So, if you are in a hurry, the place can get your car generally clean, but you may need to do a bit of touch up at one of the stations alongside the building to finish.  Review #1976

Based upon my lunch time visit, I was expecting a fabulous dining experience with my wife and our friend.  Sadly, all our entrees were improperly flavor balanced.  Maybe it was the chef's night off.  We arrived on Thursday evening and were seated promptly.  The room was very dark, relying mainly upon the natural light at the front of the restaurant and some dimly lit hanging lights that were more ornamental than functional.  Our service was friendly and efficient throughout the evening which started off well.  We put in an order for the Bacon Wrapped Apricots - tequila soaked apricots, hickory smoked bacon, jalapeno kumquat honey glaze.  These were tremendous!  There was a bit of sauce on the side that added an extra layer to the flavor!  Definitely get these!  We also shared the Foie Gras - sauternes, charcoal honey, espelette jelly, pistachios, country bread.  I really liked this, especially the bites where I got a whole pistachio.  The ladies thought it was good, but thought it a bit light on flavor.  I then ordered the "Toad in a Hole" - toasted brioche, egg, asparagus, prosciutto, roasted peppers, poached pears, shaved brussel sprouts, brie, truffle mushroom puree.  The way it was served, I ended up cutting up the entire serving first so that I could get multiple flavors in every bite.  Otherwise, there would be some bites that were mostly bread.  If you look through the ingredients, you can easily see that lots of flavor combinations made this a delicious meal.  My only complaint was that the tableware knife was too dull to cut through the prosciutto.    Our friend ordered the Harvest Salad - endive, roasted beets, goat cheese mousse, portobello, blackberries, buttermilk vinaigrette, pistachio granola.  She raved about how good it was.  My wife agreed.  They both thought it the high point of dining.  And then the entrees came out.    There was no balance to my Pork Belly - red chile glaze, bacon braised swiss chard, smoked onion rings, white bean puree, sweet corn relish, peach coulis, arugula salad.  Again, I needed to cut the meal completely because the plate was stacked high.  The pork was very salty.  The chard and arugula were clumped and had a more intense flavor than expected, overwhelming the rest of the ingredients.  The bites without the greens were overwhelmed by the saltiness.  It just didn't work.  I could see promise in that the pork was cooked tender and the plate looked rather nice, but the balance was wrong.  My wife had the Beef Brisket - sweet corn pudding, roasted creamer potatoes, heirloom tomato puree, baby carrots, hickory gastrique, pickled mustard seeds.  She found the brisket on the dry side.    Our friend ordered the Fettuccini - crushed tomato sauce, roasted garlic ricotta, pancetta.  The restaurant does offer meatballs for another $3.75, but since our friend is usually a light eater, she passed and just went with the basic plate.  Sadly, the flavors were basic.  She thought spaghetti at home had more appeal than what she was served.  I get it:  If you want spicy, get the meatball.  But if they are going to offer a meatless version, then the flavors should stand on their own.  We finished sharing a creme brulee with pear sorbet and candied rice krispies.  The brulee was good, but the sorbet was teeth chilling cold (I wonder if they used liquid nitrogen?)  Uncomfortable to eat, and then it tasted like juice.  Not much flavor complexity.  I don't like writing negative reviews or down grading from excellent ones.  But I could see the disappointment in my guest's faces.  Since we traveled nearly an hour to dine, it is unlikely we will be back any time soon.  Maybe we were just a few years late catching this place when it was one of the best in town. Rev #17

Delightful food, good service, and an enjoyable experience in a cool new restaurant are what I enjoyed in the company of my wife and friends on an early Friday evening.  This small plate, Latin American inspired restaurant is the newest in the Cunningham Dining Group family of restaurants.  The restaurant is located downtown on College, directly east of Mesh on Mass.  Like Mesh, it shares many of the same strengths, and unfortunately, some of the weaknesses that come with locating in a hot spot for dining.  First, the good:  The look of the restaurant is beautiful.  There is a long walkway from College on the north side of the building that leads back into the restaurant.  I noted there is an outdoor stairway that in warmer seasons, could allow someone access directly to the upstairs patio outside the second floor bar.  Lots of earth tones and deep blues inside with numerous paintings and some sculptural decor and lighting make the eyes dart to take it all in.  And be sure to check out the Justin Olson mural on the south side of the building:  very cool and clever use of lighting!  The service was top notch all evening.  Even though our waiter (Josh) was training, he never missed a beat when it came to attending us first.  He was very good at explaining the layout of the menu and made recommendations for each grouping.  He pointed out some of the unique house brand options from the reverse side list of beverages.    To start, we ordered a variety of the "Primero" options.  The Brussels Sprouts are prepared beyond the typical al dente. Instead, they were soft, almost creamy in texture and when paired with the cilantro, lime, and cotija cheese, had a delightful flavor.  The Patatas bravas were fingerling potatoes trimmed to bite size pieces and served with fire-roasted tomato, Spanish soubise (think onion based bechamel white sauce), scallions, and topped with crispy shallot rings.  My friend and I found the flavor full and savory, while the ladies seemed to prefer the Yuca fries, also served with the Spanish soubise, and Chihuahua cheese.  The yuca is prepared with a crisped exterior while staying moist inside.  The yuca has a mild flavor on its own, so the additions tend to lift the flavor profile.  For our "segundo" plates, the ladies ordered the Pork pastor which was generously portioned and included cilantro, onion, pineapple, green cabbage, lime crema, and served over a tasty sweet corn cake.  The flavors were savory, not spicy and would be a recommendation to anyone who is a fan of local Mexican cuisine.  My friend ordered the Skirt steak that was sliced and served medium rare with browned butter, griddled polenta, spicy chimichurri (not too spicy), and baby carrots on the side (real ones, not the artificially cut down to size ones.)  He found the flavor to be satisfying and even the ladies agreed it wasn't too spicy and worth ordering on our next visit.  We also ordered an additional "primero" seasonal vegetables as a side dish to share with our meals.  Tonight, it was sweet potato, beets, and turnip.  Our desserts were also really good.  We ordered an apple flan served with vanilla bean ice cream.  We also ordered a bowl of churros with dulce de leche.  Although it was difficult to get to the cream on the bottom of the bowl, we figured out that by using the extra serving plates, we could divvy up the churros and then spoon out the cream or dip into it more easily.  Both are delicious.  So, overall, we really enjoyed our visit.  There were a few things that I think are worth pointing out and contribute to the missing fifth star.  I understand that the items in the "segundo" portion are also small plate servings and the prices are substantially cheaper than "entree" portions at comparative restaurants.  But when I ordered my scallops, I was disappointed that there were only two small scallops on my plate.  Compared to the amount of food each of my companions got, I would have rather paid more and got at least one more scallop or have had an option listed to get additional scallops for an upcharge fee.  The flavor wasi fantastic!  It's just that I didn't get very much.  By the time I was aware of there only being two, I didn't want to wait on an additonal order.  Parking in the area is very limited.  Now that their lot is shared with Mesh, there is even less.  So, unless you like to walk, count on getting over into the left lane on College and paying the Valet to park your car ($8).  I'm not sure if valet service is available every night, but it is an option most nights.  Also, like Mesh, the noise can get ridiculously loud and nearly impossible to converse.  The walls are mostly brick and the ceilings are bare.  Sound reverberates around and can defeat any sense of relaxation at meal time.  Fortunately, we finished early, but by 7, the place was full and buzzing.  That may be fine for a bar, but for dining, I wish they would follow Vida's lead and make a place to converse.  Review #201

I have dined at Milktooth twice and now understand why this restaurant gets such high marks from diners and Indpls Monthly (rated #1 in Indy).  My first visit was a solo visit (3-14-16).  I thought I would sample a few of the items.  The Macchiato looked great, but was quite small and rather bland...not a great start.    But then my main dish arrived, the Smoked Swiss Cheese & Ham Dutch Baby Pancake.  Upon the very first bite, I was hooked!  The apricot mostardo was brilliantly paired with the savory tastes of the ham and cheese.  Totally delicious!  I wasn't a big fan of the green sprouts taste, but they definitely added visual appeal to the meal.  I also ordered a cinnamon sticky bun to go...this too was a little disappointing since it had dried out a bit since baking earlier in the day and I could taste a bit of burned flavor which detracted from the taste.  So, I left with a mixed feeling about the restaurant, but thought I would give it another chance.  My second visit (4-22-16) was with my wife and a couple friends.  We grabbed one of the few remaining parking spaces and were seated promptly.    This time, everything I ordered was fantastic!  I even sampled a few bites of some of the other items ordered by our table.  Everything was good.  I started off with a cup of Holy Basil Tea.  This might be my favorite hot tea ever.  I will definitely order this again.  I then ordered the Ham & Egg Croissant with pesto AND horseradish (spicy brown mustard).  This was absolutely delicious.  Now, when I make ham and eggs at home, I always add both pesto and brown mustard.  This is one more reason I go out to eat...to find new flavor combinations of things I never would have thought to put together on my own.  I also got the Potato & Celeriac Latke with curried cauliflower puree and onion marmalade, and a spring surprise of fiddleheads (fern sprouts).  This savory wonder was also well made and worked well with the croissant (but the combo is quite filling!)  My only regret is that I can't find celeriac at any of my local grocers to try making this at home.  So much better than just plain potato latke.    I have read there is often a long delay getting in here to eat.  Just one more reason to take advantage of opportunities to break the routine and get out to a wonderfully elevated dining experience now available in Indy.  Review #34

Although the shop carries additional sweets (like B Happy Peanut Butter), I was only interested in getting some ice cream.  The shop is located in a stripmall on the south side of the highway, so access is somewhat awkward.  You can enter from the stop light and work your way over, or turn on the east side, but have to go all the way back and come forward again.  Weird that they don't have a direct access to the side road there.  Anyway, I was hunting ice cream and as soon as I finished parking in the shared lot, I noticed the "Fat Elvis" ice cream listed on their menu.  Made with a banana ice cream base, they add peanut butter bits to provide the flavor combo that mad Elvis into Fat Elvis.    Undeterred by the calories, I ordered a single scoop in a cup.  It is on the expensive side (around $4), but they sure don't skimp on flavor.  This was so good!  Very creamy ice cream, not icy or dry tasting.  Just lots of melt in your mouth flavor.  Look, if you want plain vanilla or chocolate, you can get it here, but what makes a place like this special is the combinations you don't find at the grocery store.  Check them out!  Review #2874

I've been buying Soma products as gifts for my wife for quite a few years.  They make high quality clothing and I appreciate that their sleepwear has a wicking capacity that allows her to get a good nights sleep without feeling too hot or clammy.  Just a comfortable night's sleep.  So now that she has accomplished a significant weight loss, it was time to get something new.  I've always purchased items online before, but since we were at KatC, the location of the store seemed to be kismet.  She was free to browse around the store and check out the different styles, but like most places, not everything is in the right size.  Fortunately, she didn't give up and she happened to check out the clearance items and found just what she wanted on SALE!  The staff was friendly and wasn't pushy.  My wife was able to get her items quickly and they looked great on her as well as made her feel comfortable wearing them.  As long as they keep making quality products, we will keep purchasing these products.  Review #2463

This was my first "Taste of Speedway" event which was held at the Dallara IndyCar Factory.  I was impressed by how much food was available.  At first, you might think that the portions are really small, but by the time you visit over 30 places to try what they have brought, you get pretty full!   I am particularly fond of the Main Street restaurants.  I enjoyed the food from Dawson's, Big Woods, 1911 Grill, Tacos & Taquila, Daredevil, and many more.  And not all the vendors were restaurants.  There were a wide variety of businesses in Speedway that brought food too.  Some were apartment complexes, or realtors, while others were promoting fitness and healthy living.  There was a lot of variety from snacks and donuts, to ribs, chicken, pastas, and desserts.  The price was very affordable with tickets bought in advance being only  $10, while they were $15 at the door if you held off.  As my wife and I entered the building, it appeared that the room was pretty full with visitors already.  There were a few tables for people to be seated, but not nearly enough for everyone, so it was important for people to clear their own trash before leaving (sadly, there were a few who weren't so considerate.)  Trash cans were in short supply especially since there were lots of small plates and cups being disposed.  What I didn't realize right away was that there were more vendors on the north end of the building.  There was a bit of a bottleneck where some large displays blocked a view of the numerous vendors on that side.  Because a vendor was right by the bottleneck, it was hard to tell if people were waiting in line or waiting to get through to the other side.   Fortunately, everyone seemed to be in good spirits and enjoyed the evening.  Hopefully any future events can address the trash and table issues and be mindful of the bottlenecks created by displays.  Review #2490

What a nice surprise finding this shop filled (I mean packed!) with collectibles.  I'm not talking about the latest and greatest highly marketed items, but those kinds of things I grew up liking or buying for my kids when they were growing up.    They had Star Wars, Star Trek, GI Joe, Marvel and DC figures, Barbies, sports figures, and so much more.  Lots of vintage comic books too.  I've been to comic stores and to a somewhat similar place in Fishers, but this shop, though packed, seems more organized and easier to get around in.  There were lots of items I remember seeing 20-30 years ago.  Some were still in the packaging, but there were some just in plastic bags that were really affordable if you are looking for toys that kids can play with.  (Why pay for the packaging?)  But they had some items that, although maybe not in mint condition, were unique.  How about a life sized inflatable Jabba the Hut!  Or helmets of storm troopers or Boba Fett.  Ora cooler that looks like R2D2.  Yes, they had them!  The guys who work there were friendly and easy to talk to about the items.  Although I didn't make any purchases this day, I got some ideas I may pass along to my family for my birthday/Christmas.  Fun stuff!  Note that this location is a little awkward to get to from the south.  I highly recommend cutting across Troy to Brill Street and then heading north from there because Madison angles and would be difficult to turn onto Brill from the south.  Southbound on Madison is no problem though...just watch for the street sign.  Review #3305

Truth time:  I didn't make a purchase, so I can't say how the service is.  What I can say is that for being a Movie and Music store, I was surprised how much of the store is devoted to other kinds of merchandise, like t-shirts.  I remember going to the mall and buying CD's and movies and having tons of options.  Maybe it's because so much streaming / downloading is going on that these types of stores need to carry items that aren't electronic.    But I can only base my review upon what I know has gone before and though they have a nice selection, I wasn't impressed.  It's Okay, not anything unique or enticing.  Review #1907

When I am looking for a restaurant that will be a new experience for me, I only look at places that are 3.5 stars or better.   That usually translates to a good experience and with that, come high expectations.  So, when a place exceeds my expectations, you will generally see my review giving 5 stars.  At 3 Sisters, my expectations were exceeded!  In all honesty, I had tried to come here late on a Saturday morning, and when I saw the line all the way out the door, I decided to go elsewhere.  Bad for me, but good for business.  This time, I picked a rainy Tuesday to try again and after parking in the small lot on the north side of the building, was able to get seated immediately, being greeted with a smile and a welcome.  After being served a strawless glass of ice water, I picked the Salmon BLT from the sandwich part of the menu and went with the potato salad as my side.    Before long, my plates arrived:  The sandwich was stacked high and was sliced with a couple pickle chips between the diagonal halves.  The potato salad was served on a separate dish.  The salmon, served atop toasted sourdough, came with bacon, avocado, tomato, arugula, and mayo.  Wow!  The saltiness of the bacon worked very well with the savory salmon and the cool creaminess of the avocado.  The arugula (peppery) and tomato also added to the fullness of the flavor.  I definitely recommend this!  The potato salad was served chilled and was more American potato salad than mustard style, though I didn't recognize all the flavors.  Still, it made for a pleasant side to pair with the sandwich.  Though the sandwich was voluminous, the simple joy of the flavor let me power through devouring the whole thing.  Sadly, it didn't leave enough room for dessert.  The waitress was attentive and seemed to listen well, adjusting her responses to reflect the tone of the visitor/guest.  I was very pleased with how quickly the ordering and checkout processes were completed.  To enjoy this place (which does have seasonal outdoor seating available), go for times that aren't peak so that you can enjoy your meal without having to wait in line.  Review #828

Really high quality items in a small space with friendly folks there to assist you.  My wife and I enjoyed browsing around the shop on a Saturday afternoon and met one of the owners.  The shop was filled with unique items of furniture, accessories, candles, and other scent related items to create a sense of home.  Though they didn't have the specific thing my wife was looking for, they suggested taking a photo of the room/materials and sending them to the shop so they could help find something that would coordinate with our stuff.  Nice!  Very pleasant experience and we look forward to stopping by when we are next in the area.  Note:  This is another new business that opened in 2018.  Review #2154

I had heard about the expanded bar/restaurant and as I walked along Virginia Avenue, I thought it might be cool to sit out and people watch.  Unfortunately, there was only one person working the lunch shift and she couldn't cover both sides of the business as well as watch the patio.  So make a note that dining outside is an evening option.  Inside, the bar is dark with lots of tv's going (only one with volume on.)  I grabbed a spot at the bar and waited for the waitress to return to the floor.  It wasn't too long (a couple minutes), but felt odd until I realized she was the only one working the front of the house.  Anyway, I ordered a breaded tenderloin and a side of tots.  They were ready in short order and the portions were large.  Lots of tots that were lightly seasoned and had a nice crunch.  The tenderloin was a decent size and not pounded thin, so it held its moisture.  The bun itself was a bit buttery or maybe had a slight oil coating from being on the grill which necessitated using my napkin frequently.  The flavor was really good though, so I didn't mind too much.  Check out was fairly quick but there was a bit of a mixup on the change.  Not a big deal, but just something to be aware of when you pay.  Good good with large portions and prompt turnaround times.  Hopefully I can check out the patio on my next visit.  Review #2882

I only stopped in for donuts, so I can't rate their sandwiches or beverages (both hot and cold).   The donuts I picked though, were quite tasty.  I picked out an apple fritter (nice flavor, but not as much apple as other places), a chocolate covered-cream filled long john (filled from end to end and VERY sweet), and an Old Fashioned glazed cake donut that looked like an exploded ring (much lighter than a lot of cake donuts I've had.)  The staff who was working during my visit were attentive and friendly and that is always appreciated.  Whenever I order donuts, I try to let them know if it is going to be a lot (that would need a box) or just a few so they know how to arrange them as I select.  It requires a lot less handling that way and the donuts keep their appearance longer.  Note that this store is on the end of a strip (across an access road to the east of the Kroger.)  Even though it is on the corner, they do not have a drive thru option.  The large parking area for these shops is only accessible from near the storefronts.  You can't enter closer to the road and drive back for some reason.  I can't blame the shop for this inconvenience, but I point it out to help other customers avoid driving to the far end only to see it has no egress.  Good donuts, friendly and efficient staff make for a winning combination if you are looking for some variety in your morning choices.  Review #3741

Some orchards are out in the middle of nowhere and promote themselves by adding festivals, playgrounds, corn mazes, etc.  Otherwise, why would you travel there.  But Adrian Orchards is an Urban Orchard.  It's nestled into a neighborhood that grew up around it.  Did you know that this orchard has been going for 95 years?  That says they must be doing something right!  So, don't come expecting lots of fun things to entertain children.  They have a pumpkin patch, an apple orchard, and a store.  The good news is that keeps the crowds down so you can get in, make your selections, and not wait long in line.  I pulled into their paved parking lot (another plus!) and browsed around some of the display they had outside their store.  They were selling beautiful mums for only $8 that were ideal for planting (I did!)    Inside the store, there was a wide range of produce, apple cider (already cold), Indian corn bundles, and an area decorated with festive autumn and Halloween items.  They also had jams and jellies, and other canned goods for fruits that were out of season.  Staff was friendly and offered to help find items.  Checkout was quick and easy too.  If you want all the perks of going to the orchard without having to fight the crowds, then consider Adrian!  Review #3156

Let me fully disclose that we met some long time friends for dinner and we had a great time visiting as well as enjoying the friendly service (great job Andrew B) and tasty food.  We had such a fun time that I am sure it puts a positive light on my rating and review.  There are a few minor things to be aware of that would make for an even better experience.  First, if I hadn't known from other reviews that this bar bistro was in the former Black Market location, I might not have found it.  The building still says Black Market and I couldn't see anything about Bodhi until I went to the front door.  Another thing to note is that this location suffers from the lack of parking that every other business on Mass Ave has.  We got to the restaurant when it opened at 5 pm on Monday, but their tiny lot was almost full already (we got the last spot.)  I suppose we could have paid for metered parking somewhere along Mass Ave or parked at the parking garage at Bottleworks and walked over.  But be aware that if you are meeting someone, be sure you allot time to find parking.   Our friends arrived a few minutes ahead of us and were able to get a table for four by the windows.  (No reservations are available here.)  For us old folks, having lots of natural light to help read the menus is a plus.  They do have patio seating open but it felt a bit too chilly for us, so we stayed inside.   Our waiter was upbeat and eager to serve and stayed in a positive mood throughout the dinner and cocktails.  I was the only one of our party who was familiar with Thai cuisine, so we needed some time to pick.  We started with our beverages (I got the Emerald Buddha (fresh and crisp cocktail) to start.  They also have a nice lineup of local craft beers on hand.  coke products too.  They didn't have any ice tea made other than Thai tea, so my wife couldn't get an Arnold Palmer drink.  A little disappointed, but not a big deal.  We moved on to some starters/shareables.  I ordered the Crab Puffs (think crab rangoon) which my wife declared she would get an order for herself next time and not share.  Served with sweet chili sauce for a sweet heat.  Probably the best rangoon we have had in town!  Highly recommended.  Our friend wanted a cup of Tom Yum soup, but was told it only was served in a large pot that was shareable.  I agreed to help her eat some.  Seems like minor change could be made to accommodate a single consumer.  The waiter said our friend could add a protein and make it her meal as an option, but enough of us agreed to help her eat it and we were brought out bowls and shared it.        My friends like spicy hot food, so I wasn't too concerned, but the website clearly states to not go too hot when ordering.  They can always add more spicy heat (they brought out chili flakes for our friends to add), but can't take it out.  If you order it hot and can't take it, too bad...no refunds on your mistake.  I like that they disclose this ahead of time and encourage people to not overdo the heat request until they are used to the standard heat levels served here.  Having said that, I ordered my items mildly spicy or at most, medium.  Our friends ordered their items medium and requested the pepper flakes, but didn't need many.  Be wise and aware of your options and responsibilities (you pay whether you eat it or not because of the heat level.)   I ordered my standard Pad See Ewe which I get at every Thai restaurant on my first visit so I have a point of comparison between restaurants.  This was delicious and though on the pricy end of the cost spectrum, there was plenty to get a take home box for a second meal.  I've tried making this at home and just the ingredients I purchased on my own make me wonder how a restaurant can charge as little as they do.  I really appreciate great flavor without having to do any of the work myself.  Thanks to the ladies who run the kitchen at Bodhi.  Excellent flavor!  Our friends and my wife ordered different entrees including various stir fry and the drunken noodles.  All reported they enjoyed their meals.  Everyone got take home boxes too.  If you leave her hungry, you must have shared everything or just didn't sample enough of what everyone else ordered!  Because I finished my first cocktail while visiting and eating our appetizers, I ordered a tasty Francoise & Etienne cocktail to go with dinner.  It was so good I even ate the orchid and the tangerine ice cubes.  Yum  Hopefully they can find a way to manage parking.  A new hardware store just opened a few weeks ago across the parking lot, so that is going to make parking even more challenging.  If you are young and healthy, I suggest street parking along Mass Ave if you spot a space.  I was hopeful there would be some handicap reserved spaces, but didn't see anything nearby.      I look forward to returning in the near future to try some of the other goodies on their menu and cocktail list.    Review #3904

I have been to this Fleming's Prime Steakhouse twice and have had excellent service and delicious food on both occasions.  The last time I went was during the Devour Northside promotion.  I had the Fleming's salad (iceberg lettuce with candied walnuts, craisins, tomatoes, onion, and herbed crostini); Filet Mignon with porcini rub, black truffle butter with gorgonzola cream; and rice pudding with blueberry sauce.  All were cooked properly and were worth recommending.  We did have a few delays that seemed to get us off to a slow start. Most of that delay was while our server was chasing down an answer about a unique alcoholic beverage type by one of my party.  But once we got our orders in, everything seemed to go well.  If this restaurant was closer, we would probably attend more often.  It takes an hour during the week to get to this side of town.  We usually wait until there is a promotional event that makes the great food more affordable for those of us on a budgeted income as well.  p.s.  The room has very limited lighting which makes reading the menus a bit difficult, so we look online to get familiar with the menu.  Just a little brighter would help.  Review #46

This place is huge and has plenty of parking so that if you make a purchase, you won't have to haul it very far.  This was my first time visit, so after entering the spacious lobby/checkout area, I chose to go to the right to check out the "Decorator Mall" side of the place.  Here was a variety of knick knacks, wall hangings, and seasonal items to add a bit of style or flair to your home.  The aisles were clear, but I did need to say "excuse me" to get around clusters of shoppers who tend to forget anyone else is browsing.  The other side of the place (even larger) is the Antique Mall.  This was a little less organized, but manageable.  Here were more collectibles and antiques than I saw on the other side.  Some of the stuff made me scratch my head why it was there (an empty Sun King can for $3?), but other items looked like the type of stuff you could pick up for your collections.  Lots of dishware, books and music sources, and quite a bit of nostalgia items that I remember (mid 20th century items), but not in the best of condition were noticed.  Plan to allow yourself plenty of time to browse since just the walking will take you awhile even without stopping to snoop.  Review #1958

My wife and I stopped in for lunch on Saturday and were lucky enough to grab a parking spot in the lot behind the restaurant.  The entrance to the restaurant has moved to the south side of the building instead of out front where a previous establishment had used.  There is still a patio on Delaware with a small fence around it for patrons who wish to enjoy the sun.    Inside, the look is festive without the over the top gaudiness of some places.  A long row of bench/booth seating runs through the middle of the dining area with 4 top tables making up the rest of the seating.  The cantina looked stocked with rows of tequila behind the bar.  I can't comment on the cocktails since I passed on them this visit.  For lunch, my wife ordered a Taco Salad with chicken.  She thought the flavor of the salad was quite good.  She liked the crisp flakiness of the shell as well, but thought the shell held an aftertaste of the cooking oil that she didn't care for.  The portion was large, so she ended up getting a to go box for the rest.  I went with a Chimichanga (ground beef option) which comes with lettuce, tomato, guacamole, refried beans and Mexican rice.  I found the taste to be quite good with the beef being seasoned and providing a lot of beef flavor to stand up to all the adds on the plate.  Oh, and we got complementary chips and salsa.  The chips were a bit broken and had a similar cooking oil taste to them, but it wasn't as noticeable with the slightly spicy salsa.  Service was friendly, kept the orders moving, and bussed the tables quickly.  Overall they did a good job.  I didn't see anything unique or outstanding on the menu, but what I had was good.  Now if they can just get that cooking oil taste resolved....  Review #1116

I give credit to a company that realizes the product line is changing, so it adapts to become useful in other ways to keep its customers returning.  As more readers grab books online, the need for giant bookstores might become a convenience rather than a primary source.    So this chain has added lots of departments that aren't too far of a stretch from reading to appeal to customers and continue to bring them in.  Besides thousands of books, there was an artists supplies area, a video area, a toys and games area, periodicals, young readers, and a cafe!
