Throw in convenient parking (free) out front and you could spend a lot of free time browsing the store, finding something of interest, and then grabbing something in the cafe so you don't have to wait to start reading!  Well kept and plenty of staff even on a Monday evening to assist customers find what they wanted.    Review #2160

I've noticed this restaurant on several occasions because of the colorful public art murals painted on the sides.  So, I decided to stop by and give it a try.    The restaurant is located near the corner of Rural and Washington St, so if you are looking for free parking (no street parking allowed!), head north on Rural to the alley and take it across behind the library and a small Mexican restaurant and you can pull into small lot on the east side of the building.    Inside the restaurant, you quickly notice a colorful street mural painted on the dining room wall.  There is also a cool tree sculpture rising above the dining tables.  On the left is the counter for placing your order and a display of baked items available for purchase.  The left wall has a blackboard menu with items, including ingredients in each, and prices.  I decided to go with a strawberry smoothie (very good!) and went with the house special, the Pia Sandwich (I also picked up a bag of chips.)  After paying, I took a seat and within minutes, my meal arrived.  The Pia is a fantastic flavor combo.  I chose the baguette (bagel is also available) for my base and the owner/chef/cashier/waitress put together the hot sandwich with turkey, egg, avocado, tomato, greens, pepperjack cheese, and pesto.  Wow!  What a great sandwich!  She even sliced the sandwich in half to make it easier to handle.  When I was done, they have a trash can near the door and a small gray bin on the shelf beneath the menu board to place your plastic serving basket.  I forgot to mention that napkins are available in the center of each dining table.  I didn't mind busing my own table seeing how many jobs the owner was doing.  All the while, she had a great demeanor and made sure to invite me back to try something new.  Sounds like a great idea!  Review #534

Although I don't eat here regularly, I have been dining  with this Harry and Izzy's for ten years.  I used to come over for a nice lunch when I worked on the circle and really appreciated that they have a special lunch selection that makes it easy to get in and be fed without being late back to the office.  Now that I am retired, I just don't get downtown for lunch as often, so it required a planned visit to get reacquainted.  Surprisingly, I had never reviewed this place before. It has been well maintained and while convenient for lunch, it still has all the finery that makes for a nice evening meal with the white tablecloths and black napkins.  I don't feel I have to dress up to dine here, but would feel comfortable in a suit s well.     We parked inside the convenient parking garage of the Circle Centre Mall although there isn't any signage in the garage telling you were to go to find the restaurant.  There are some stairs and escalators involved, but we managed to arrive and because it was a weekday lunch, didn't need reservations for our party of two.  A moment's wait and we were shown to a table that had a nice view of the restaurant as well as windows for viewing outside.  Our server Maggie did a fine job of getting our orders placed.  They do use that Rorshach looking doodle to scan with your phone (hate those) but did have a printed lunch special menu that I found very useful.     My wife and I got very similar meals, both opting for the filet sliders (extremely tender and well seasoned bites) served on Hawaiian rolls.  The sliders came with a horsey dipping sauce that wasn't overpowering, just nicely balanced.    One of the odd things was that the "side" included a cup of soup.  Because it was a side, the soup wasn't brought out early, but served with the sliders.  I would have liked to have had it early.  The soup was a tasty Tomato Basil, with croutons which I really enjoyed, but my wife found to to be too heavily seasoned.  She upgraded her salad to a wedge salad while I went with the a delicious Hearts of Romaine salad with candied walnuts and a rosemary vinaigrette.  We both enjoyed the salads a great deal.  Then to finish off the meal, we also had a choice of desserts.  She went with the fudge brownie with ice cream and whipped cream while I chose the creme brulee.   Again, excellent choices and left us feeling very pleased with our decisions and glad we made the trip downtown to get out of the boring routine of summer holiday BBQ and pizza.  I'll have to make a point to not wait so long between visits next time.  Review #3919

When is a brewery not a brewery?  This was the fourth Upland location I've visited and the place is surprisingly large inside, like it could hold a brewery in there.  But this is simply one of their tap house extensions that carry most of the Upland drafts brewed in Bloomington and a large number of the bottled sours (I believe that was what I saw on the shelves by the bar.)  Anyway, I simply wanted to grab a quick brew and check out the place.  Grabbing a seat at the bar, I was greeted by the bartender who asked if I needed a food menu, but then directed me to the chalkboard list above the bar if I wanted just beer.  I decided to go with a Saison that I had previously in a flight called the Life Exotic (5.2%, 18 IBU).  Lots of herbal layers in the taste, not just a simple brew.  And on Sunday, the pint was only $3!  Such a deal.  While there, it seemed that most of the employees were in constant motion checking on customers, bringing out food, etc.  Although I didn't eat, I sat close enough to folks to hear them complimenting the food orders they had, so it sounded like they were enjoying it.  Solid first impression for me.  I like that they have convenient parking in the lot behind the building since there isn't any place on 116th to park.  Review #2416

Why five stars?  I can honestly say that I liked the food I ordered more than I expected to.  The server behind the counter was very helpful asking if it was my first visit as I entered, then proceeded to walk me through the steps of building my own Indian food experience.  Where some places throw authentic Indian food into a buffet and expect the customer to know what they are getting, here is a place that helps people like me to overcome my lack of knowledge/palate and bridge to a delightful (if somewhat Midwestern-ized) meal.    First, you have to find the place.  It is important to note that 10th street is a one-way street heading east.  The easiest way to direct someone not familiar with the area is to come from downtown, then northwest on Indiana Avenue until you reach the 3-way intersection with St Clair and Paca.  Head straight north on Paca and about a half block before reaching 10th St, pull into the shopping plaza on the left.  Tandoor & Tikka is part of a building that has an Arby's and a sushi place next door. (I tried google maps and the place is so new that it isn't on it!)  There is lots of free parking in the lot.  The ordering process is much like I've encountered at Poke places:  You go to the counter and the menu behind the servers tells you the order you need to follow to build your meal.  I went with a "naanwich" style that basically takes the disc of baked leavened bread as a base.  I then picked from five proteins (I had the tandoori chicken), and then moved onto selecting a curry.  I really appreciate that the menu board has all five types of curry options listed which include spicy heat rating as well as a general description of the ingredients.  (That's worth a star by itself!) I asked the server for a recommendation of what she thought would go best with the Tandoori spices and she let me put Tikka Masala (blend of tomatoes and yogurt) on one side, and the Saag (leafy greens and spices) on the other.  I then got to choose from the colorful bins of fresh toppings that are too numerous to itemize here, and there is not limit or extra charge for your selections!    Finally I got to choose from the sauces and got three:  a blanco chutney, a mango chutney, and a Tangy Tamarind chutney.  They then folded my naanwich in half and placed it in large press to cook it like an oversized panini.   While waiting, I also ordered the Masala (collection of spices) Samosa (deep fried dough-wrapped spiced mix that I believe has potato as the base).   I also tried a Berry Lassi (berries and yogurt) drink.  Before long, my order was ready and I went to the side counter to pick up napkins, plastic ware, and a straw.  I was surprised at how large the serving was.  The naanwich was sliced in half so that it was generally like eating a large taco:  you hold the folded side down to avoid wearing the spiced colored juices.  Since I picked the ingredients, I couldn't help but enjoy the flavors.  The curry was mild and didn't overwhelm the other flavors.  I must admit I enjoyed the Tikka Masala more than the Saag.  The Masala Samosas was okay, but not my favorite.  I tried some of the dipping sauces and those helped lift the flavor to a higher level.  The lassi was smooth and creamy and generally had a pleasant berry flavor.  I bused my own table when done (the trash and used plate counter is on the opposite side from the napkins counter and was a little difficult to see at first.)    Seating is available at long counters along the windows with backless chairs or in unique booths that look like some sort of converted carriages.  Note that for the carriage seating, you have to step up and then your knees raise high while you dine.  It was a little awkward, but not cause for any discomfort.  Overall, I was pleased with the quality of food, the quality of service, and the overall business operation making a foreign food become approachable.  I would gladly recommend this place!  Review #1150

Although I'm an omnivore, I still enjoy visiting Vegan restaurants to see the chefs use their skills to create tasty dishes.  10th Street Diner has a variety of meal options including soups, salads, and some entrees for folks to try.  After parking in their large gravel lot at this corner spot, I noticed the "Order Here" sign above a menu board.  The host/waiter/runner greeted me as soon as the folks ahead of me were finished.  I decided to try one of their sandwiches, a Seitan Reuben and added a side of Brussels Sprouts instead of the chips (upcharge).  They have a variety of beverages including beers, but I went with chilled water from a dispenser by the front entrance.  The seating area is on the visitor's left and the grill which has bar style seating is also on the left against the south wall.  I grabbed one of the bar stools and watched as my meal was prepared.  Let me say that the Brussels Sprouts, which are grilled crisp and coated with a sweet Balsamic (house blend) glaze were fantastic!  I gobbled those down rapidly.  Note that the portion size is for a single, not meant to be a shareable portion.  The Reuben has marbled rye, dressing, and a tart and tasty sauerkraut that evenly covers the bread.  It appears that the bread also is basted with a margarine to add a bit of flavor and crispness under the press.  The seitan was sliced thin and was very tender.  Pretty good flavor for a sandwich.  However, if you are someone who really likes the flavor of corned beef and Swiss cheese, the seitan doesn't match those deep savory flavors or provide the same texture.  So, do I compare this only to Vegan places, or to all other Reubens?  It's a tough call.    From my point of view, I have to compare it to all diners, not just Vegan because my diet isn't restricted.  But if you are also a meat eater like me, don't miss giving this place a chance just because it may be different.  Good flavor and good/pleasant service is always appreciated.  Review #2610

I took advantage of a Yelp promotion this week to stop by this new shop in Fountain Square.  They serve delicious chilled juices that avoid all the artificial additives so many commercial brands have.  Cold-pressed ingredients that aren't pasteurized let the true flavor come out in these drinks.  The shop is located on Shelby in a shared building between the Conoco and the My Pet Carnivore shop.  There is angled parking along the south side of the building and when you exit, you simply head to the alley to get back to the streets.    Inside, the shop has concrete floors and an industrial vibe.  The left side is filled with 4-top tables with outlets.  Wifi is available if you want to hang out like you would at a coffee shop...only with something more healthy!  Towards the back is a refrigerated case where you can select which of the flavors interests you.  If you aren't sure, just ask the staff behind the counter if you can taste them first.  The juices (currently four combinations) are available in 16 oz containers (considered 2 servings).  I tried two of them while there and enjoyed them both.  I settled on the sweeter "Carrot Bliss" though I liked the slightly salty taste of the "Pure Greens".  Each 16 oz beverage has about 2 pounds of fruits/veggies.  Wow!  The Bliss has roughly 3 carrots, 3 oranges, 1.5 apples, 1 lemon, and some light tumeric root.  And water.  That's it!  I found it really refreshing and could see having this as a breakfast drink.  However, I drank it all in one sitting!  It was hard to stop since it tasted so good!  Although the price is higher than the teas, coffee, and Kombucha which are also available here, there is a lot more health benefit from the juices than those other options.  At only 100 calories per serving, you won't have to worry about busting your caloric intake targets either.  The staff was welcoming, helpful, and knowledgeable of the juices.  What more could you ask for?  Stop by here soon.  Who knew being healthy could taste so good?  Review #2806

My review is for a walk in purchase of pastries.  I haven't ordered a cake or tried lunch yet.  Wow!  Even after lunch there was a wide range of pastries available.  Many of them had a seasonal appeal that was artistically done.  After pulling into their private lot, I had to enter the door on the lot side, not the one closest to the road.  Once in, I saw a row of tables for diners to enjoy selections from their lunch menu.  Straight ahead was the order counter with three full cases of pastries.  The first was filled with donuts and breakfast type goodies.  The other two had cupcakes, cake pops, and small cakes that were colorful.    I noticed they also make a variety of coffee items as well from a list posted on a blackboard.  I ended up selecting a snowman and a Christmas tree cake pops, two varieties of cupcakes (a snickerdoodle flavor and a cookies 'n cream, both with a nice cake to icing ratio), some salt & sweet party mix, and a large crispy breakfast cinnamon disk.  Everything looked and tasted terrific!  I can't wait to go back and try one of their sandwiches on a croissant!  Review #3430

The park is huge and clean and has lots of parking that allows the visitors to park near whatever area of the park grabs their interst.  Near the entrance on the east end, there are trails through wooded areas and gardens with benches.  The trails are paved and wind along the perimeter of the park.  The roads wind through the park where there a numerous shelters to choose from.  And the four half court basketball courts are in their own area away from the little kids playgrounds.  On the west end are more shelters, a small playground for littler kids, and a splash park.  All seemed to be in good condition.  Since it was a cool, sunny day, only the playground was in use, but the splash park looks like it is the only one in town, so I bet it gets plenty of use.  In the middle of the park is the playground I have read about and heard about:  The Blastoff!  It has all kinds of fun activities for kids to do (See Nicole S's review for details) and the playground is within a fenced in area so that they can run and climb and slide without getting too far away from parents who are resting in the attached shelter area.  I did have one small problem with the park.  Since the Blastoff appears to be mostly wooden, a number of the peaks of the fortress were losing paint and fading.  Hopefully a spring paint job will revive the appearance.  I'd hate to see the wood go bare and possibly splinter for the kids' sake.  Review #651

Look, as a rule, I don't usually give 5-star ratings to franchise restaurants.  I want locally owned businesses/startups to thrive.  Though a franchise, this location is locally owned (and expanding to Fishers - The Yard, and Westfield near Grand Park) and continues to exceed my expectations.  I first had the pleasure of trying a blueberry bliss at a recent Yelp event.  Not only was the smoothie cold, fresh, and delicious, but I could tell the owners were proud of what they had to offer.    As another rule, when I find something that I like at a Yelp Event, I bookmark the business and make a point to see if it was as good the second time as the first.  Well, it was!  My wife was with me on a trip to Carmel and since we were so close, I suggested we stop by and pick something up.  She decided to go with the Beach Bum Smoothie which has a combination of chocolate, strawberry, and banana flavors. Think banana split.  Think tasty!  They only offer one size for adults and it was plenty.  (I believe they use a powder for the chocolate flavor, but I didn't ask.)  She would have personally liked a bit more chocolate, but who doesn't?  I went with the Acai Berry Boost smoothie that was recommended when I mentioned I had liked the blueberry.  The Acai comes with acai, pomegranate, banana, blueberries & strawberries.  It was fantastic.  Just a hint of tartness to keep it from being too sweet.  Very refreshing.  While we sat there in the dining room trying to not get brain freeze, I decided to pick up a sandwich to go since I hadn't set anything out for dinner.  As a rule (lots of rules I live by but sometimes break), I usually don't order sandwiches from places that specialize in treats/desserts/etc.  But I have to say, I thoroughly enjoyed my Pressed Chicken Caprese sandwich.  The chicken was moist, the tomato and lettuce fresh, the Parmesan and Mozzarella were oozy, and the balsamic glaze's sweet/acidity stood up to the pesto savory for a great blend.  The sandwiches also come with the customers pick of sides which are self-serve next to the counter.  They had chips and fresh fruit options.  And the owner, the same guy I had met at the Yelp Event was thrilled that I made the trip from Mooresville to stop by.  He was so gracious and helpful.  I saw him open a door for a customer.  It's nice to see someone who is thankful for customers and treats them as guests.    This may be a franchise, but you would never know it without research.  Quick friendly service with delicious food options.  5-stars!  Review #2858

Basically, if you are looking for something healthy to eat or drink, the franchise offers a variety of options.  Tucked away in a strip mall along with other restaurants and shoppes, I didn't see this one right away.  Fortunately, they have convenient parking out front and I was able to go right in and pick up a bottle of "Red" juice.  They have a number of flavors with colors as names available that are chilled in a cooler across from the order/food prep counter.  I had already made plans to dine elsewhere, so I can't comment on the quality of the flavor on their menu items.  The "Red" juice is made from Apples, carrots, beets, and lemon.  Although the first sip is unusual (at least to my palate), I quickly got used to the taste and now think of it as quite good.  The only negative for me was the pricing.  I found the price of $10 for a single bottle to be 25% higher than what I can get a similar product from a local producer (317 Juicery) in Fountain Square.  For me, I'd rather save money buying local than from a franchise.  Neither one is close to my home, so I can't say convenience is a factor in my decision.  Review #3353

I really enjoyed this marvelous collection of lighted images at the fairgrounds.  I picked a weeknight when the air was cool (not freezing) and the crowds were small (and parking was easy), so I was able to take my time and enjoy the presentation.  Each of the exhibits has a sign that you can read to learn about the lanterns in that grouping.  I am not very familiar with Chinese history, so I found the info to be concise and useful.  Scattered among the images of Chinese culture, there were lots of animals from around the world (land and sea!).  Certain lanterns had small movements built in (like the lions near the entrance).    This is a great exhibit for capturing photos, but be aware that if you go on a crowded day, you may have to use more patience to wait for people strolling through your shot.  Fortunately, the small crowds on a Tuesday evening allowed for quick snapshots.  Overall, I took about 45 minutes to go through the exhibits.  Some were tucked away by the DNR building or to the north of the food trucks/stage area, so don't rush.  I particularly enjoyed the figures of the Chinese Zodiac which has a sequence of twelve animals rotating each New Year.  The characters were colorful and delightful.  (My favorite is next year's Dog which is also the year I was born in.)  Although not particularly a Christmas event, it fits in with the light show theme and I liked that it was unique.  I didn't stay long enough to catch the performances on the stage, but there was pleasant Chinese music in the air as I strolled along the pathways.  Be sure to dress warmly and wear your walking shoes!  Review #477

This place has so much stuff that I'm still trying to remember where I saw everything.  The building, mostly one story, is seemingly endless!  I knew it was a lot bigger than what it appears from the front when I saw floor maps posted and phone numbers posted for assistance (I assume for help if you get lost too! ha!)  Anyway, they have lots of parking and there is no single best way to explore.  Some of the wider rooms have rows of glass cases laid out so that you don't have to rubber neck back and forth.  I liked that!  There were other booths and rooms where you simply walk in and look around.  But even here, there are places where you think it may be a closed room but it leads to another section of the building.    I was impressed that there was a lot of cool antique furniture scattered throughout the complex.  There were also a wide variety of antique collectibles too.  I know they have some lower quality stuff, but I found the percentage of cool things to junk to weigh heavily on the cool side.  Just be sure to allow yourself lots of time to wander through.  Note that the floor isn't the most even as you go between buildings, so watch where you walk as you browse.  Review #1906

I get it...not everyone likes art.  Not every piece will appeal to the observer.  But consider this:  Civilizations come and go, but with luck, the art survives to tell us something about the people who lived in those distant times and/or locations.  I really enjoy going through the art museum.  So, when I got a chance to take my wife to the mini-golf Bi-Centennial exhibit, I knew I could indulge my art envy as well as have a fun time.  On the second level terrace, a full 18-hole mini-golf course has been set up with Indiana themes on each hole.  As you start each hole, a description panel tells about the hole:  the Indiana connection, who built it, etc.  And then you get to play the par 54 course.  Some are pretty difficult holes to par.  Some are easier to birdie.  I couldn't help but appreciate all the different ways artists thought of Indiana and the things that make us Hoosiers.  After lunch in the IMA Cafe, we went through the "19 Stars of Indiana Art" exhibit.  Representing numerous fields of art and fashion, Indiana has a strong connection to the arts.  One of my favorite clips on a monitor showed how the US Army made inflatable tanks to fool the Axis about the true number of weapons were facing them.  (It was pretty funny seeing the artist and a few friends hide inside by lifting up the tank and walking to make the tank seem to go forward!)  I also was amazed at the craftmanship and design of a tea serving set called "Tea & Coffee Piazza".  Absolutely beautiful....not sure how anyone could ever use it without being afraid of damaging the fine work.  I also took a short walk around the Oldfield Gardens to appreciate the views of the lawn and woods, which were populated with numerous outdoor works of limestone, bronze, and painted aluminum.  Great diversity that lent a feeling of surprise as to what I would discover next.  Although I don't get out to the IMA often, there is truly something special about the place.  Inside and out, the exhibits and pieces get my creative juices flowing and makes me wonder, "What might I be able to do?"  Review #136  FYI: For a more complete list of Public Art in Indianapolis go to the following website:  http://www.indyartsguide.org/public-art/

I wish I made salads this good!  At home, my salads are kind bland and boring.  But not here!  I stopped in the City Market and went to the north end of the first floor (where Gomez BBQ used to be) and took in the menu.  They have some imaginative combinations of salads to choose from and after reading through them, I decided to go with the Smokehouse Salad.  Served in a deep 8" bowl, I was given my choice of spinach or mixed greens as my base.  Note that leaves are generally uncut, so be sure to grab a knife when you grab a fork from the counter.  I went with the mixed greens to go with my marinated chicken, herb roasted tofu, grape tomatoes (halved), blue cheese crumbles, sweet corn (yes, they added corn to a salad), smoked almonds, cooked farro, and crispy onion straws.  They top it off with a Hickory Honey Mustard dressing that was perfect!  For days when you aren't interested in just a salad, they have panini, mac & cheese, soup, and combos of those items.  Note that they have Broccoli and Cheddar soup that is Vegan.  The staff were welcoming and the wait time for my salad was so short that I've waited longer for fast food.  They also have a rewards program (Golden Tongs Club) where the 10th salad or panini is free.  As stated above, the salads are huge, so I was glad they come with a lid so that I could save the other half for dinner.  Review #3754

When I saw the great reviews for this Food Truck/now four day a week dedicated to the Metazoa parking lot business, I had to stop by and pick up something for dinner.  Let me say up front that if you like your barbecue to have a smoky flavor that doesn't need a lot of sauce to be enjoyed, then this is your place.  They do have some tangy sauces too:  mine came with a Carolina mustard type and a sweet sauce.  Although it is apparently popular in Texas to throw all the ingredients on a paper lined tray, I am not a fan of that style of serving.  Fortunately, I got my order to go and they have some really nice coated boxes that make for easy transport and kept the food warm until I got home.  Note that they have a variety of meat options and that if you choose one, you will get a measured 8 oz serving.  There are also combo meat platters with smaller portions of each meat but come with 2 small sides in the price.  That is important to know if you are picking up food for two people.  I mentioned that I wanted an order of the pulled pork and an order of the pork ribs.  I also wanted a small side of potato salad and one of coleslaw.  Sounds a lot like a 2 meat platter, doesn't it?  So, when they repeated my order, they called it a 2 meat platter of my meats, not 2 individual orders.  I paid the combo price, took my order and since it came in two boxes (plus the sides in their separate containers), I didn't inspect it until I was home.  So, when I saw there was only enough meat for one person, I was initially disappointed and confused.  2 ribs and just under 4 oz of pulled pork wasn't much to share.  I was charged properly, so no problem there.  But it is important to be specific when ordering that you want the full 8 oz of each if that's truly what you want.  You won't get the combo price, but you will get enough to eat.  Now that I know, I would gladly return and if time allowed, stop by Metazoa to enjoy some tasty beer with my food.  I particularly liked the Carolina mustard with the pork options.  Review #2493

This was my first visit to this Caplinger's location.  If you have been to their other locations (mostly on the north side of the metro area) then you will pleased that they offer the same high quality food and also have the meat counter to get sea food for your own home preparation too.   Although the food I ordered (The Caplinger's special sandwich with a side and beverage) was really good, I will have to wait until they can open for inside dining to give them a higher rating.  When you walk in, you notice a sign about having to wait for your meal in your car since they do not have indoor seating during the pandemic.  The sign suggests they will bring your order out to you, but instead, they give you a pager to let you know when to come back in to pick up your order.  Not the most efficient way to minimize contact with trips inside and handling of pagers.  Fortunately, we carry our own bottle of hand sanitizer to clean and stay safe.  I just have no idea how often they clean each pager.  The space is quite small and so I see why they don't offer indoor seating though it will be right across from the seafood deli.  I really enjoy their breaded white fish and they don't skimp on the toppings which were all fresh and tasty too.  For beverages, they carry Pepsi products which they dispense for you.  Although I tend to get the special when I visit their locations, I can say that the side dishes they offer are worth the small upgrade price which includes the beverage as well.  They are known for their collard greens, but when I saw they offered corn on the cob with Old Bay seasoning, I had to give it a try.  Too bad they don't offer Cotija cheese to go with the corn because the cheese, corn and Old Bay seasoning is a summer staple at my house.  The corn wasn't seasonal, so it was a bit chewy, but was still flavorful.  The only real problem I had was that all the seasoning was clumped in the middle instead of being distributed equally over the cob.  So, some bites had a lot of seasoning, while others had barely any.  A simple thing to fix, but worth noting to be aware of it.  My wife and I ate in our car which got to be a bit chilly since this isn't fast food.  Depending upon what you order, you may wish to get extra napkins to avoid making a mess in your vehicle.  I am so glad to see one of these restaurants on the south side (finally!), but unless you live close enough to be able to get it to go and eat at home, it is a little awkward and I am not a fan of cold seafood if I wait to get home first.  I look forward to warmer weather and healthier communities, so that I can try indoor dining and just enjoy the food without all the distractions.    Note:  Our to go bag came with plenty of napkins and plasticware for utensils.  Review #3867

Recent events got my wife and I to start thinking about making our final arrangements for the time when we no longer are around.  We had planned our wills a few months earlier, but had never formalized what we wanted done once we passed away.  One thing we agreed on was that we wanted to cause as little disturbance in the lives of our kids and grandkids so that they could simply grieve our passing.  We also knew we wanted to be cremated since our family isn't known for visiting cemeteries after the initial burial.  So, no sense buying plots or fancy caskets or even expensive urns to house our ashes for eternity.    We had heard lots of good things about this local funeral home which has the only crematory in the area.  We had attended funerals at this facility before and thought they had handled the proceedings quite professionally.  So, my wife made an appointment to sit down with one of their staff to discuss our plans.  From the outside, the building looks like a very nice older home with the entrance to the parking for the facility on the left side of the building (one way traffic around the building to minimize accidents.)  Inside, the look is less small town and looks quite professionally designed.  We rang the doorbell and were greeted, then taken back to one of the rooms in the back that would allow us to talk details for planning our own procedures while surrounded by samples of options.  Our hostess (Cindy) made us feel welcome and did her best to explain all the different features that came with each package.  I was impressed that she didn't try to press us into any certain package.  She did show us some options when we said we were uncertain or had not realized there were options.  We let her know about what we were looking for and then once we had made some decisions, she provided estimates for each of our services.  She also offered some long term payment options that would lock in the pricing.  The only negative is that they did NOT accept credit card payments here.  My wife ended up writing a check for my services and another down payment for what is like an insurance policy that guarantees a lock on the cost of her services.      We decided to go on the lower end for some of the options, but instead of going with the minimum, I urged my wife into upgrading to let the staff here help with handling donations, flowers being sent, handling phone calls, and generally coordinating things according to our wishes so that our kids didn't have to be hammered by all the phone calls from friends and family outside the area.  For me, it seemed worth the extra costs to let the staff handle all the details.  Although they have beautiful options for caskets, vaults, and urns, we decided to go with a modest casket for each since it would be burned in the crematory.  Couldn't see spending a fortune for the thing to be torched!  We also thought our kids might want to spread our ashes, so instead of a fancy urn and a spot at the cemetery to buy, we opted for some decorated cylinders that our kids could transport our ashes to wherever they wanted to spread them.  They also have jewelry and keepsakes that ashes can be inserted in.  It doesn't appeal to me personally to carry someone's ashes around with me, but one of my kids expressed interest in it, so we thought we would at least inquire about it.  Lots of options here.  We also learned that the staff handles getting the death certificates for the survivors to send to financial institutions, Social Security office, and other places that may need to know (life insurance policies).    Throughout the meeting, we were treated with respect and felt no judgment regarding our choices.  Very professional.  I feel at peace with our decision to go with Carlisle-Branson.  I hope our kids will use the staff's availability to negotiate through all the difficulties of losing a parent and closing their estate.  Review #3783

One of the success stories of the Fishers Test Kitchen at the Yard is that there has already been a transition from one of the businesses to a replacement.  One Trick Pony has stepped into the last kitchen area in the row of pop up test kitchens next to Sun King.  I got a chance to talk after my lunch with the man running the restaurant.  He has grand hopes for franchising his concept across the whole country to maybe 1200 businesses!  Talk about ambition.  The key to that is finding out how your first business is received and ironing out any problems before you go big!  I must say that this is an impressive start.  First, the name:  "One Trick Pony" refers to their logo which states "We do one thing really well.  An that's hot, fresh, smashed burgers that are diner style, made to order, & pressed on a hot griddle".  That is definitely true.  I ordered a double burger and each of the patties (about a quarter pound) was individually seasoned and seared to bring out the deep beef taste.    Know that you can order a single, double, or triple burger.  Instead of telling them what you want on your order, they have "Styles" of toppings you can select.  I picked the Old John style which has shrettuce (shredded lettuce), pickle, onion, tomato, mustard, mayo, and American Cheese.  There are several other styles you can order and if you need other condiments, there were some packets near the cash register, so be sure to look if your "style" doesn't come with a particular one.  I also ordered a side of fries.  You can get just plain fries or onion rings, but you can also order them with many types of sauces/cheeses (basically a poutine).     Let me say that the first bite of my burger had a great crunch to it!  Crisp toppings (pickle, onion, tomato) and a crisp sear to each of the burgers was a pleasant surprise.  That's the way I like my burger and although there was a lot to eat, I didn't feel like I had any trouble fitting these smashed burgers in my mouth.  (Much different than eating the half pound Big Mouth Burgers that are usually underseasoned and rely upon the toppings for flavor.  If anything, by seasoning each of the burgers, they were almost too salty by the end, but they didn't get too bad because of all the toppings on mine.  The cheesy style fries were okay.  The cheese reminded my of the creamy smooth Cheez- Whiz style so that it could be pourable/dip-able.  I noticed that the cheese was poured directly onto the fries and by the time I got to the end, the fries were getting soggy.  After lunch, I stopped by and asked if the owner would like any feedback.  I suggested they pour the sauces/cheese for the fries into a small cup and let the customer dip the fries.  He said he really like that idea and thought it would be really helpful for carryout orders.  So if you get fries with a topping and don't want to eat them first, simply ask for the sauce on the side!  The stand along fries seemed crisp and already salted, so my wife grabbed some ketchup packets from the counter for hers.  Overall, we really enjoyed our food and interaction with the owner.    One thing you should be aware of if you go in for lunch:  Sun King doesn't open until the middle afternoon, so you will need to order a beverage from the restaurant, or wait until later in the day if you want a beer with your meal.  Don't blame One Trick Pony if you can't get a beer.  This business is not associated with Sun King in any way other than sharing the same dining room.  Note that like the other food places in the Test Kitchen, you pay when you order and they give you a buzzer that lets you know your food is ready to come pick up.  That way you can stake claim to one of the seating places in the common seating area.  Also note that napkins and plasticware are located at stations near the entrance.  Down below is the place you can throw away your trash.  (I believe Sun King busses the tables later in the day.)  Near those stations, they also have sanitizer and cloths you can use to spray your own table and chairs before sitting if you are uncertain when the last time it was sanitized.    It's nice to see a new business looking successful during these difficult times.  We enjoyed our experience and would gladly return to dine again!  Note that it isn't a cheap burger place like the fast food places, but depending upon the number of burgers you stack on your sandwich, the price can climb fairly fast.  But the prices are clearly posted.  Just pay attention before you order and you will be okay!  Review #3816

My review is based solely upon my experience getting my two Covid vaccine shots.  I have not needed any other services at this facility.  When my age group finally became eligible for the Covid vaccine, my wife was thoughtful enough to search local facilities and even though I am not from Hendricks county, she was able to schedule an appointment within a couple days and I was pleasantly surprised at how quickly and efficiently the staff was able to process the group of patients through their set up.  I was greeted upon entering the hospital and though there are lots of signs, many of the staff asked if I needed help finding my way to the vaccine area.  Everyone was masked and there were plenty of signs on the floor to let you know six feet distancing.  After checking in, they then directed you to a waiting area and the staff who administered the shots were set up in booths separated from each other by drapes that went to the floor.  The nurse who administered by first shot did probably the best job I've ever experienced as she gave me the injection.  I barely noticed the shot.  I am not squeamish about shots and usually watch while getting them.  If I had reviewed upon this injection alone, I would have given five stars!  I waited the suggested fifteen minutes to see if I had any reaction to the shot.  I had none.  While there, they even took care of scheduling my follow up visit for my second vaccination three weeks later.    This time, I knew where to go and checked in at the vaccination station and then stood in line (but I was the only one there, so even though I was ten minutes early, they didn't make me wait.)  As soon as the next station was open, the waived me over and after a few questions, I rolled up my sleeve.  I wish this nurse had as much skill as the one on the first visit.  When I literally saw her hold the syringe in her fist with her thumb on the plunder, I was surprised when she used a "tomahawk chop" style of injection.  I felt the impact and was surprised!  Never had a shot delivered at fast forward speed before.  Fortunately, I don't freak out over such things, but someone who is squeamish may have been a bit more vocal about it.  Anyway, I am one of the fortunate people who don't have reactions.  I will say there was a little tenderness the next morning in the injection area, but other than that, no problems with the serum.    Other than the unusual technique on the second visit, I have nothing but praise for how I was treated by the staff.  Very efficient and no long lines when I visited around noon on Friday.  Now I just need to wait a couple weeks for the antibodies to build up my immunity.  Review #3891

I can't think of any other restaurant I've been to lately that my rating could range so widely.  It all boils down to why you are dining out.  Do you like trying new places?  hot spots? good food, strong drinks, excellent atmosphere and service?  Does there need to be loud music, or quiet spaces where you can carry on conversations with friends?  So, if you are looking for good food and good drinks, decent service and something a little quirky, I suggest giving Revolution a try.  This rating is based upon our first visit with friends that we frequently dine out with.  After driving around trying to find some parking without time limits and towing warnings, we lucked into a spot that opened just in front of the entrance.  It was a warm/hot evening and we were surprised we couldn't dine inside in the a/c, but had to head back through the bar to through the double doors hat lead to the Tiki patio in the rear where it was hot and humid.  Though we asked about dining inside, we were told that inside seating was only available if it was raining.  Seemed odd.  I realized they had a small staff and would have trouble covering both the indoor and outdoor customers, so we were gateful when the sun went down and it became more pleasant to sit outside.   There is no direct way to the patio, so we were up and down and walking around numerous tables and doorways to get to our table.  Turns out that even with wait staff, the table drinking water is still self-serve which I found odd.  The wait to place our beverage orders was not too long and though there was the lone bartender on the patio, she seemed to keep up pretty well.  Background music was light so we could hear he music, but still carry on our conversation uninterrupted.   I went with the unusually named Lardy Laddle double smash burger since I was hungry.  Quite good, but nothing that was outstanding or so challenging that I couldn't make it at home.  The other three in our group all went with Burritos, one pork, one chicken, and one Teriyaki chicken with pineapple bits for a Hawaiian influence.  All seemed pleased with their choices and portion sizes (Large) One negative for me was that a neighborhood cat was stopping by many of the tables while we were dining and it looked dirty and needing some care.  While sympathetic to its thirst and hunger, I didn't feel the staff should be encouraging it during the dinner course.  Surely some health code must regulate this sort of thing.  Fortunately, the feline stayed down and didn't get on the tables.  It was just an unusual experience that may upset some diners.  I will summarize by saying the food was good, the drinks were generous and the staff friendly even if not ambitiously focused on the customers.  The place is looking a bit run down and if the owners can spruce the place up and eliminate some of the weird and unusual rules, this could be a nice place to give a higher recommendation to.  Bottom line-- every one in our group said they would return for the food and drinks.  Review #3947

For those of you who are familiar with my reviews, you know I try to capture the first time experience of visiting a business with an optimistic point of view.  Unfortunately, this review takes a hit to the rating because of some confusion that I was unable to clear up as well as taking place during the recent pandemic which I am certain affected product availability as well as customer service since everyone was practicing social distancing.  When employees are not actively seeking out customers to make sure they are finding what they need lessens the shopping experience for me.  I had become a bit of a hermit during the pandemic and when my wife heard a news report about this nursery becoming a part of the Sullivan's Hardware family (I really am a big fan of the main Sullivan's store with all its offerings and great service), we made the trip from the opposite side of the metro area to check out this business.  I had read several articles online that Sullivan's had purchased the business, but when we arrived, we found no signage (not even on the receipts) that indicated Sullivan's had anything to do with the business.  In fact, if there hadn't been the Big Green Egg ceramic section of the store, I might not have any idea there could be a connection between my high hopes and what I found here.    The feel of this place, though it does offer a variety of interior decor items and plantings as well as having a large outdoor showroom of plants that include shrubs, annuals and perennials, didn't carry the hardware options and definitely lacked the charm of the main business.  This was more of a help yourself location.  If you are already knowledgeable of plants, it was fairly well marked to find what you are looking for, but if not, then a sense of bewilderment and frustration sets in.  My wife wanted some specific plants and just couldn't find them.  She did end up making some purchases of floor mats and checked out some of the wall hangings which she found many that lacked prices and others that were hung too high to read.  I was looking for a new rain gauge instead of just ordering one online but the selection was disappointing.  Unfortunately, since this business is so far from my home, I am not likely to return to update my review any time soon since there are probably a dozen other lawn and garden centers between my home and this location.  Without the special charm and service that I expected, I can't say that driving all the distance was worth the pay off at the end.  Review #3763

It's not easy to get to, but worth the effort!  This pioneer coffee shop was an early arrival in trying to help the near east side make a comeback.  Located across from the east end of the rejuvenated Willard Park on Washington St, the coffee house/event center shares space with Ash & Elm Cider in a very cool space.  Lots of brick on the interior and antique coffee making/measuring equipment makes for a cool vibe though the business isn't that old!    There's a dining area in the front of the shop and more 2-top seating along the center wall between the businesses.  Note that the wall between the two businesses has several open areas (no doors) that make it easy to bounce back and forth between them.  That's a good thing since the restrooms are down the hall on the Ash & Elm side.   Note 2:  You need to borrow the keys for the restrooms.  The keys are kept at the end of the pickup counter in Neidhammer and on a merchandise table at A&H.  The staff was very friendly and helpful and I was soon enjoying my medium roast drip coffee.  I also devoured an almond croissant (via Circle City Sweets) that was on display at the order counter.  Like many coffee shops, you should expect to bus your own table when you finish with the return near the front entrance.  The only real negative for me is that there is a minimal amount of parking on site.  Most guests park across 5-lane Washington Street and try to time crossing  where there is no designated cross walk.  You also compete with traffic trying to pull onto Washington from Hamilton on the west side of the building.  Street parking on Hamilton is fine if you come from the north, but know that you can only park on the west side of Hamilton.  I hope that the business can at least get a crosswalk and maybe a caution light to let drivers be on the lookout.  Review #2301

The food is pretty good here and the setting was really nice, especially the patio.  Service was friendly and prompt too.  Plenty of parking out front during lunch.  There were just a few minor issues that kept this from being better rating.  My wife and I ordered non-Alcoholic milk shakes and though the taste on each was delicious, the shakes were very thin, almost milk like.  I like my shake to be cold and more than chocolate milk in consistency.  We both noticed and I don't think that it had to do with it being a warm day on the patio.  We drank them fast.  The straws they provide are standard skinny straws so if you order a shake that has any cookie crumbs or fruit, you may have trouble getting those.  We asked for spoons to grab those bits.  Maybe they should look into getting boba straws while making the shakes thicker.  Skinny straws would be really tough to use if the shakes get thicker.  I broke one of my own rules by ordering seafood at a place that specializes in burgers.  I had one of their signature burgers at the Carmel Prodigy, so I decided to try the Teryaki Salmon just because it sounded good.  I devoured it and it was cooked perfectly.  Remained light and flaky and the sauce was tangy.  The steamed broccoli was a little bland (kind of expected), but some lemon pepper would go a long way to making it more tasty. My wife ordered the Hoosier Daddy Tenderloin and like most places, the meat greatly exceeded the bun size making it necessary to cut the tenderloin and stack it to get any condiments and topping with the meat.  Much of the meat was cooked okay, but parts were really dry and tough to cut through with the table knife.  The breading was okay, but could have used more seasoning as well.  just a bit bland.  The house chips were crisp and crunchy, but the oil had a slight burned taste even though none of the chips were burned.    Everything was fine to eat, but no wow factor.  The Asian slaw that also came with my meal could have used just a bit of sweetness to offset the vinegary taste.     The restaurant looked very nice and clean and the patio is smartly styled with fresh flowers and plenty of umbrellas for the tables.  This place has a wide variety of foods available including cocktails and some craft beer (provided mainly by BrewLink).  I will gladly return to try some other items.  Good service throughout the meal.  Review #3937

On my lunch time visit, I got great food, quick service, and affordable price!  I grabbed a parking spot in the lot in front of the entrance and was greeted and seated pretty quickly as they were opening the restaurant.  I had looked over a number of Yelp reviews, so I had a good idea what I wanted to try.  The waitress provided a lunch menu as well as the full menu, so I opted for the items that were recommended/caught my eye ahead of ordering.  To start, I ordered the Chicken & Crab rolls and the Crabmeat Asparagus soup (cup).  The two items arrived at the same time, so I decided to let me soup cool just a bit while I dug into the crispy rolls of goodness.  The finger sized rolls had a drizzle of a creamy sauce as well as a sweet & sour dipping sauce on the side.  These were fantastic!  The flavor was similar to that of crabmeat rangoon, but the crisp narrow roll reminded me of those expensive cookies that look like chocolate filled straws.  Perfectly cooked, crispy outside with a tasty moist inside.  Definitely order a set for yourself!  The soup was pretty good too.  It had two kinds of meats as well as bits of asparagus.  It looked like the consistency and appearance of an egg drop soup, but with bits of meat that looked like imitation crab strips and of real shrimp.  (The menu doesn't list details, I'm strictly guessing here.)  Before I finished my soup, my colorful Vietnamese Sandwich arrived.  Served on fresh French bread, my Banh Mi came with Vietnamese ham, long sliced cucumber, shredded carrots, what tasted like pickled daikon, pepper slices, and topped with fresh cilantro.  It also came with a knife to cut the 8" sandwich down if it was too much to handle.  The flavors were very fresh and delicious.  It was a bit difficult managing all the ingredients so that they stayed between the bread halves, but not too bad.  Well worth ordering!  I appreciated the "team" assisting to clear my table and bring my check to minimize my down time.  I was in and out in about a half hour.  Really good first experience!  Review #500

I've had my eye on stopping here for quite awhile, but I seldom find myself in the area after dinner, so when I had a chance, I made a point to drop by.  The shop is in a small shopping plaza east of Michigan on 86th (north side of the street).  They had plenty of parking out front too.  Because of the rainy winter weather, I was the only customer when I stopped in.  But I was determined to try some ice cream.  Now if you've read any of the other reviews, you will know that this place has created ice cream filled doughnuts, sandwiches, and froot loop wraps for their ice cream.  They also offer a free first topping for their scoops as well.  But I wanted to keep it simple since my metabolism isn't as fast as it used to be.  So I got to sample a few varieties and settled on the Graham Central which has bite sized chunks of graham cracker (maybe more crust like than cracker).  Excellent taste and texture.  The staff working were very helpful and friendly and there was no rush.  There is a small amount of seating inside the shop too since I got my ice cream in a bowl and didn't want to eat it in my car (or while driving!)  I found it was their 6 month anniversary of being open on my visit.  If they keep their customer service and ice cream quality this high, they should be around for a long time!  Review #2162

I'm not sure what has happened to this location.  Maybe they are struggling during the pandemic with help or maybe there has been a change in management.  This used to be my wife's favorite place on the southside to grab a burger when in a hurry.    But on our most recent visit, we both were disappointed.  I ordered a mushroom burger with curly fries.  Both were quite bland tasting.  I did eat my fries, but only finished about half my burger.  My wife just ordered a burger and it didn't stay together and made it kind of messy to eat.  She also thought it not as good as usual.  As we pulled in to place our order at the machine (which did work and we could hear clearly), she noticed that the lot surrounding the building had not been cleaned in some time...trash, mainly from customers, was all over.  Just makes you wonder if the inside is maintained any better.  We didn't go inside, so we can only wonder.  We both used to enjoy this location when we lived in Greenwood and lived much closer.  But over the passed five years or so, something has happened.  The woman who took our order and got our food was courteous and efficient, so no problems there.  The wait time was not that long either.  She even remembered to offer condiments which so many places seem to not think of on to go orders during the pandemic.  Here's hoping that this place can find the magic in the kitchen to make their food taste good again.  Just very disappointing, though quite filling.  Review #3788

My wife and I were running late, so we wanted something  tasty and not take too long since we wanted to get going and not push our meal into dinner time since we had plans with friends to dine out that evening. I had ice cream on my mind but wanted a hot meal too.  Culvers came to mind as a place that could satisfy both needs and it did.  We parked in they free lot outside so we could dine in.  we were directed to choose our own booth or table and then placed our order a the count where we paid, and fine tuned the accessories to our meals  (sides, condiments) and we were given a number for our table.  Our food was brought out quickly.  Some condiments were self serve as were extra napkins.  Dine in was mostly full service, but since you walk by many of the self serve stations, it was easy enough to avail ourselves of those items instead of waiting for the understaffed servers to get back to us.    We were able to get our left over food bagged so we could get on the road without much of a wait.   Price was a bit higher than the fast food places, but the quality made up for the difference.  If you want a tasty meal at not a lot higher price or time, stop in at Culvers.  Review #3960

There's a great little shop on Pine Street that has a wide variety of pies, sold by the slice or whole.  There are more than 3 dozen varieties available, many in either lattice crust or Dutch oven style.  (Note:  if you want a whole pie for a special occasion, they suggest calling at two days in advance.)  On my visit, I had to try the Dutch Red Raspberry "Kisser" pie.  Wow! Excellent flavor with a bit of sugar on the crust.  Did I say Wow!?  The pies are very affordably priced compared to the price of ordering dessert in restaurants ($4 here).  Whole pies are mostly in the $23-32 price range which is very reasonable if you have tried making pies yourself.  And they do all the work for you!  Great food, great and friendly service and they even have their own parking spaces next to the building.  For those who aren't in a hurry, there are a few tables inside and they have a few beverages available too.  Seriously, if you like pie, do yourself a favor and stop in here!  Or St Elmo's or Harry and Izzy's or any of numerous local places that carry their pies!  Review #427

Sometimes, it takes a bit of luck for a business to be successful.  When Pearl Street first opened, it was located on an alley downtown between Circle Centre Mall and the former Jefferson Plaza on Penn.  What was lucky was that a large open parking lot was across the street which kept the natural light available and made the alley feel open, not creepy.  I find it hard to believe that with all the development downtown that this same lot is still undeveloped after ten years!  It allowed the place to be seen and develop a following when it could have been easily forgotten.  I hadn't been back in a long time, so I decided to stop by and grab some lunch.  They were packed on a Thursday!  Note that you have to enter the building through a door west of the pizza place and enter through a hallway and step up in through another door to the dining room.  Once there, the sign suggests to seat yourself.  I saw a few counter seats by the window across from the bar.  That may have been part of my problem.  Nobody realized I was there.  My back was to the bar, but I wasn't at the bar, so was one of the dining room staff supposed to wait on me or one of the bartenders?  They were packed, so it was hard to get anyone's attention so I stayed facing the open area and tried making eye contact.  After about five minutes, one of the staff who eventually became my waitress saw me and made a point to come over.   I will recommend not selecting this location if possible since I was surprised by a waiter who came up behind me to refresh my water.  And it took awhile again to get my check.  Sit at the bar or at a regular table in the dining area to get more timely service.    I ordered a personal sized pizza.  They have lots of suggested options and a build your own option too.  I went with an 8" size and chose the hand-tossed option.  The Mad Greek happens to be meatless, but sure comes with a lot of flavor.  Although I left off the banana peppers, the combo of flavors, especially the cheeses with the assorted veggies was delicious!  Even the crust which had a crispness to it had an excellent flavor with a hint of salt.  I would gladly recommend that choice.  The wait time was pretty short considering how busy the place was.  If they are this busy during the week, they must get crazy busy during ballgames.    Note that they do offer a Yelp 10% discount on food items.  Review #2704

This small Chinese restaurant has low prices and quick service.  Their small shop is in a strip mall just south of Main St on SR 135 in Greenwood.    What I liked:  Convenient parking, quick service, and low prices.  The crab rangoon was crisp and had a fair amount of crabmeat inside.  The sweet dipping sauce was tasty without making the rangoon loose its crunch.  The Beef with Broccoli had a nice flavor.  The beef was tender.  What I didn't care for:  Their is an $8 minimum purchase to use a credit card.  Not bad, just awkward to find something to add since I was low on cash.  Their plastic ware is flimsy and made cutting the hot, but barely tenderized broccoli difficult.  I couldn't spear it through the stalk with the fork.  I ended up stabbing the crowns of the stems.    Problem:  I got an order of egg drop soup.  It was generously sized and served piping hot!  However, the flavor was generally bland, even for egg drop soup.  And there was a trace of soap/chemical in the soup.  I would have mentioned it to the staff, but since I paid at the time I ordered, I didn't see anyone after they brought my food out.  No follow up on their part and no opportunity for me to call attention to it.    Rev #395

Convivio provided a nice upscale dining experience.  Located in the shops on the north side of Market District parking lot.  I was able to grab a spot right outside the restaurant and was seated promptly.  I opted for bar seating which was quite comfortable, having plenty of leg room beneath the dining surface.  The bar has a full liquor license offering cocktails, wine and several beers on tap (maybe 6).  I started with a Caesar salad that was surprisingly large for lunchtime.  The plate was 9" square and was fully covered with Romain, cheese, and garlic croutons.  The Grana Padano was shaved, not shredded.  The dressing was full flavored and delicious.  The romaine was fresh and crisp.    While waiting for my entree, a small cutting board of focaccia bread with seasoned olive oil was brought out.  The bread is made in house.  The oil was okay, but most of the seasoning sat on the bottom and the bread didn't really absorb the oil, so I left a lot of the flavors in the bottom of the dipping dish.  My entree soon arrived:  Tagliatelle al Convivio.  This pasta dish arrived in a giant dish that had a cereal bowl sized serving of the pasta/chicken dish.  The house made pasta is red bell pepper-infused in a red bell pepper cream sauce and topped with grated Parmiggiano cheese.  It had good taste, but the flavor was described as zesty, but was only mild.  I was expecting the flavor to be more robust like the salad, so it was a bit disappointing to discover it on the bland side.  Service was great, being both friendly and efficient.  Overall, the meal was enjoyable and is someplace I would recommend for folks wanting to dine where they can carry on conversations without a lot of background noise.  Review #448

This brewery does things right.  Sure, they make great beers, but they also add the things that make the customer experience better.  First, they have regular hours so that you don't have to memorize which day of the week it is to know if you can stop by.  They open at 11 so you have a choice of stopping before dinner or after, or in this case, stop for dinner. Yes, they have a nice menu of sandwiches, spaetzle, poutines, sausage, and shareable appetizers to take care of your hunger.  The service was attentive and seemed well trained in using their electronic ordering tablet so that they don't have to rely on memory alone.  Also, your credit card is processed at your table, not back in some obscure place.  I ordered a flight of four ounce beers.  They have a rack for holding four selections, but since each beer is priced separately, you can get as many or as few as you like.  I went with five and found all them quite good!  I started with a Rauchbier (5.5% 25 IBU) which was a smoky German Style lager.  I then had the Negra Mexican Dunkel (5.4%, 20) which was smooth and refreshing after the Rauchbier.  Next was the JWP American Stout (8.2%, 65) that had a chocolate espresso flavor.  I moved on to the Vacation Kolsch (5%, 20) that tasted very light but still flavorful even after the stout.  I finished off with the NEX #7 Hazy IPA (8%, 80) which was full of hoppy flavor.  All were good to great!  The food was also very good.  I started with the crispy Brussels Sprouts which are grilled with cherries, and add melted pecorino cheese and whole seed mustard for a bit of acidity.  I also enjoyed the Brewer Steak Sandwich with unseasoned frites (they have salt, pepper, and ketchup at the table).  The steak was sliced into bite sized bits and had a nice char for flavor.  It was garnished with a bit of lettuce, onion jam, horseradish aioli, and diced cornichons (sweet pickle).  I couldn't help but think of the flavor reminding me of a really great chargrilled burger but with the texture of a Philly steak.  Pleasantly surprising!  The frites were cooked properly, but definitely needed the seasonings/condiments to perk them up.  Service was pleasant and kept my empty glasses/dishes removed.  Everyone was in an upbeat mood which you would hope for a new business.    Overall, a very positive experience and a place all new and competing breweries should be aware of.  This was five star all the way!  Review #2161

after finding convenient parking in the shared lot in front of the restaurant.  We entered a spacious dining area with lots of tables, but only one server working the floor.  While pleasant, there were noticeable gaps in interaction. our order was taken and placed but it wasn't until we were seated that this restaurant did we realize it did not serve margaritas,  Mexican beer with sliced lime was as festive as it got. I ordered the street tacos which are served on small corn tortillas, I don't know if they offer flour which I prefer.      y wife ordered a burrito that had a side of rice packed inside.  It looked rather plain without any sour cream, cheese on top, or pico de galo.  Seemed like an incomplete meal compared to other local restaurants.  It wasn't a big deal to me but my wife commented that chips and salsa were not free.  $1 per order. There are numerous Mexican restaurants within a short driving distance, so in order for this place to make it.  I think it needs to raise its game on many levels.   Review #3976

Okay, I'll be that guy...you know, the first one to give the place less than 5 stars.  I applaud that the place is providing a need for the community and provides dairy free and gluten free products for those who have allergies or have decided they don't want those things in their food.  But as a guy who has been eating baked goods for nearly 60 years, I have to admit that the taste of some items came across as kind of funky to me.    I bought a chocolate chip cookie and that was crisp and tasted pretty good.  I also snapped up a discounted day old lemon cupcake that had a delicious, creamy icing. The cake part was a tad dry, but that was kind of expected since the manager informed me about it being a day old before I made the purchase (hey, a cupcake for a $1 is a good deal!)  The peanut butter brownie was the one that I wasn't a fan of.  The brownie was very moist and gooey and the topping had large pieces of nut along with the creamier topping.  But the flavor just didn't come close to what I imagined in my mind.  Maybe it was an off batch, but it was probably more that some ingredients were substituted for those I like.    Still, two out of three is pretty good.  I hope the place does well, it's just not the first bakery I would go to if I wanted to pick up something to snack on.  Review #945

I brought a friend to lunch on a Thursday morning (6-2-16) to BRU Burger downtown.  We were able to find some street parking just west of the restaurant on Alabama St.  Because my friend is a regular at the restaurant, we were greeted by several of the hostesses and quickly seated outside on the patio.  I noticed that a permanent awning was now installed for the patio area instead of the original umbrellas for each table.  It allows lighting and heaters to be used on days when the weather is just a bit too cool for sitting outside otherwise.  I understand why they made the investment, but having been here maybe a half dozen times in the past, I feel the "atmosphere" was a little dark and lost some of the "European" appeal that the open air patio had.    I ordered the Farmstead burger - shaved Brussels sprouts, Prosciutto, truffle aioli, apple mostarda, and Farmstead feta cheese; and onion rings. The burger was cooked to my "doneness" level correctly and in a timely fashion since my friend needed to get back to work.      Although the flavors sounded appealing to me, I found the pungent flavor of the feta overwhelmed the other flavors, including the beef.  I like trying new ideas for familiar sandwiches, but for me, I need to have the other ingredients support the flavor of the burger, not make the burger get lost underneath and become filler.  I'm not saying the burger was bad, it just didn't satisfy my expectations for the meal.    The onion rings were excellent and the house ketchup has remained consistently good.  The service was efficient and attentive.  Just wish the burger wasn't lost in the toppings.  Review #8

The park has a lot of nice shelters, a playground with a variety of equipment, and a paved hiking trail.   The parking is spread throughout the park, so if you have a specific part that you prefer, you can drive right to it (which I saw some parents with small children seem to take advantage of.)    I chose a shaded spot for my car and did the shortened route for my hike.  It was on the lower level of the park and required walking across a very cool looking foot bridge that was easily wide enough for strollers.  However, as I was on the last part of the .8 mile hike, there was a large tree on the ground across the path.  It wasn't a big deal for me, but for the lady ahead of me who was pushing a stroller, it was a pain.  Then, where the water was standing on a 20 foot section of the pavement (with muddy ground on either side), it was a challenge to get around without getting wet or muddy shoes.  Look, if it's a nature trail, I kind of expect that can happen.  But when it's paved, I expect it to be maintained, especially for parents bringing little kids who don't particularly want their kids being wet and muddy too.  Overall, I liked the park and think it is a definite asset for the community.    Note:  At the time I went, there is a massive construction project on both sides of Green Street which limits the only road going by the park to one way north.  If the park would have been more busy, I could see this single route being a pain to deal with if you were in a hurry to get home.  Review #649

This small shop is just south of Main Street and I actually missed seeing it and had to turn around and come back for it.  As I stepped inside, I realized this is more of a "to go" place with a small display counter of pizza slices and desserts and another counter for checking out.  Since it was late in the lunch hour, there weren't a lot of ready to go options, but I decided the sausage and pepperoni would meet my needs.  The woman behind the counter threw in the sausage slice as well since she didn't think it her best "looking" piece and wouldn't want to sell it.  So, I got two slices of pizza for the price of a single $2.17 (tax included).  Can you believe it?  I spent less time in the shop than I would had I gone to a fast food drive-up!   And the flavor was good!  The thin crust slices were a little flimsy and flopped if I didn't use two hands or do the fold method, but they were definitely cooked and had really nice flavor.   Okay, not complex and layered, but with minimal toppings, that's hard to achieve.  Tip:  If you are near here, go to Brew Link Brewing across the street and bring a favorite slice from CJ's with you.  Review #605

This park is the ever ready bunny of parks on the west side:   It keeps on going!  I pulled in the park from US 36 at McClain Road and saw the dog park on the west side and the playground on the east.  I thought it would take a few minutes to see all the park had, but was I surprised.  There is a nice sized parking lot on each side of the entrance, so I chose the playground side and immediately noticed trails leading off into the woods along White Lick Creek.  There was also a nice playground, a story walk where kids can read a book as they move along the park, a basketball court that is transformed into an ice rink during cold spells, and shelters.  By one of the shelters is a large hill that can be used for sledding.   And then I saw signs that made me realize I was only on the north side of the park.  So, I hopped in my car and drove around to the other end.  There, I found another playground, a splash park, a community center, and an amphitheater.  There was also an exercise station along one of the trails.  The park has a bit of something for just about everyone.    Not all the parks are paved, so they can be challenging.    The dog park is basic and doesn't have any special training equipment, but there is a shelter inside the park fencing that allows the humans the rest while the dogs romp.  Overall, I look forward to returning to explore more of the hiking trails.  Review #725

I'm glad I gave this place another try.  This time, I ordered the lunch special "Squealers Favorite" which is the shredded pork topped with cole slaw and served with chips.  The pork was moist and had a nice smoky flavor.  The sandwich came with sliced onions, dill pickle chips, and a choice of barbecue flavors.  The cole slaw had a strong vinegar taste when sampled by itself, but when combined with the pork and all the sides, it gave the sandwich a full and well balanced flavor.  The sandwich is loaded with meat and slaw, so be aware that you may need all your napkins and the fork to get all of it.  Review #315

I was downtown at Gallery 924 and decided to drop by the Taco Shop since it was only a half block away.  If you haven't been to this restaurant before, it is conveniently located on the northeast corner of the block of the City Library.  There is limited street parking on the one way streets on the north and east sides of the restaurant.  I went early in the lunch hour, so I had no problem with items to select from.  It was basically a "Which type of taco do I want" menu.  I went to the counter near the entrance and ordered, paid, and gave my name for them to identify the order when it was ready.  I opted for the Carnitas and the Polbmole with a side order of guacamole.  Because I was mindful of my parking time, I decided to get my order to go so that I could move my car if needed.  My order only took around five minutes to be delivered to a side counter.  The tacos were boxed together (open faced, not rolled), and the guac was served in a covered container (a bag of nacho chips was also provided.)  They have some silverware, napkins, and self serve water in between the counters for customers.  I did see some bottles of sauce, but since it was my first time, I didn't think to check out those flavors or ask if any were recommended for the types of tacos I ordered.  So, I passed on the sauces and went with the basic tacos that come with white onion, cilantro, and a very small half wedge of lime to use on both tacos.  And as much as I hoped the tacos would be special, I was disappointed.  It's obvious that these were fresh and the quality of the meat seemed fine.  It's just that there wasn't much flavor.  Maybe it was the type I ordered, but I am used to tacos with a blast of flavor and being more moist.  There really wasn't much flavor to comment on.  Sure, the onion and cilantro added a nice flavor complement to the meats.  The mole sauce on the chicken taco added an extra layer of flavor that the carnitas taco seemed to miss.  It's just that there wasn't anything in the tacos that made me want to make a return visit as a destination....maybe as a convenience, but not a go to place.    I will say that the guacamole and chips were quite tasty.  The red onion in the guac gave the mix a nice punch of flavor.  But even the guac wasn't mixed very well.  I found a quarter avocado buried in my bowl that was too firm for the chips to break apart.  It tasted all right, but it was necessary to make it finger food to continue eating my lunch.      I understand the change in thinking that Plow and Anchor was too pricey for the walk up neighborhood business to survive and that tacos might be a better business decision.  It simply felt rather sterile in atmosphere and lacked any of the fun of the culture that inspired the menu.  Review #363

My wife and I were taking our grandson to the duckpin bowling next door and decided to stop in at this restaurant for convenience.  I liked that they had a lot of options that our grandson could choose from.  So after we found some free street parking down the street, we were directed by the waitress to choose a spot and she would bring our menus over.  They have lots of barbecue options, as well as burgers, some fried fish, and a different daily lunch special.  Our grandson selected the Thursday special, beef manhattan.  When he saw the platter (not just a plate), he couldn't believe it!  Lots of sliced beef topped the bread and then real mashed potatoes were nestled in the middle with gravy.  He loved the flavor, but he didn't come close to finishing the food.  (Fortunately, they have large take home boxes too!)  My wife ordered a beer battered fish (cod) sandwich that had about 6 ounces of meat.
