Thick sliced, the sandwich was a challenge to eat because of the height which included tomato, onion, lettuce, and tartar sauce.  She ordered the sweet potato fries with a dipping sauce as her side.  She thought the sandwich very satisfying...not amazing, but better than expected.  I decided to go with the beef brisket sandwich with the krinkle fries.  I had my choice of several sauces to put on the meat, choosing a raspberry chipotle.  The meat was thick sliced (about 3/8") and though it wasn't piled high, was plenty to eat.  The meat was nicely flavored from the slow roasting but did have a slightly spongy texture.  It was moist and mostly tender, but did make for an unusual bite.  But overall, it was a good sandwich too.  Note that the fries were unseasoned, so I helped myself to the table salt shaker.  I honestly have to say I had my expectations exceeded considering the average rating of 3 stars the restaurant has at the time of my review.  It has a nice vibe of late 50's to 60's era music and drive in posters on the wall.  Service was friendly and fairly prompt.  Portions were generous for the prices.  A solid four if you like a bit of nostalgia with your lunch.  Review #420

I have had the pleasure of lunching at Patrick's twice recently.   My first lunch was on a warm Monday (4-18-16).  Although there was room in the inviting patio area, I wanted to inside to see what the restaurant looked like.  I was seated promptly and had attentive service.  I choose to go with the Bayview Crab Cakes - Pan-fried blue crab cakes served on a bed of greens, with red chile mayo and basil aioli.  The crab cakes weren't huge, but seemed appropriate for lunch time.  I like the flavor combo with the condiments.   I also had a delicious House Salad - Mixed greens, dried cranberries, sliced toasted almonds, crumbled gorganzola, and house vinaigrette.  Nice and light, with lots of flavor.  Overall, very satisfying with good flavor.    I liked the restaurant so much that when my wife asked me where she could meet a friend on the northside of Indy, I suggested she head to Zionsville to Patrick's.  I was glad I was invited too!      We met on a rainy Tuesday (6-14-16) and after a short stroll from a side street where we parked, we met our friend inside.  I started off with a local craft brew and then ordered half and half lunch option:  side salad and half a sandwich.  My wife and friend ordered one of the specials for the day:  The chicken Quesadilla which both thought was a good choice.    Because I liked the salad on my first visit, I chose it again this time.  I then chose the Spinach Melt - Spinach blend with cheddar cheese, tomato, and bacon grilled on multi-grain bread.  This had a nice flavor and because the spinach was cooked, it didn't seem too much along with the spinach salad. I would order it again.    The food came out fast again, the only negative in both visits is that the salads and entrees came out at the same time.  So, next time, I will ask if the salad can be brought out ahead of time.  I chose to eat the entree while hot...it just seemed a little weird to the salad last.    Anyway, my wife wanted to try the Chocolate Volcano dessert which we split three ways.  It was a personal chocolate cake with a "molten" center with a couple scoops of vanilla ice cream.  The flavor of the cake was good and the center was moist, but there wasn't anything "molten".  We didn't get too disappointed, but it didn't fit the description.    Much like the revival of Main Street in Speedway, Zionsville can be proud of the number of quality restaurants and shoppes opening up there.  (I still love the brick streets!)  We're looking forward to our next visit....maybe brunch?  Review #20

Wow, this place may be known for its beer and burgers, but their Sunday brunch is one of the best I've had!  My wife and I headed out to an early brunch and found convenient parking (free on Sundays) along the street. (They open at 9 a.m.)  Since it was sunny and very comfortable outside, we chose to sit on the patio overlooking Mass Avenue.  Our server was very attentive and upbeat throughout our breakfast.  After she brought our beverages, it didn't take long for our meal to be delivered.  Overall service was excellent!  My wife opted for the Eggs Benedict Sandwich - two slices of thick-cut ham, fried egg, smoked gouda, with a house-made spicy brown mustard on a pretzel bun.  She chose the sweet potato waffle fries with cinnamon butter ($1 upgrade) as her side.  When the waitress set her plate down, we did a double take at the size of the sandwich.  I got to sample a bite of the sandwich and we agree that it was delicious.  The ham was full of flavor and the mustard and pretzel combo really added depth of flavor to the meal (much like it does on the Ralston burger.)  She needed a "to go" box for half the sandwich!  She also enjoyed the sweet potato waffle fries.  They normally come with house ketchup, but she opted for the upgrade and was glad she did.  Delicious!  To go along with my giant cup of coffee, I chose two entrees:  French Toast and Bananas Foster (which comes with two slices of bacon) and my side of mixed fruit; and the Ham and Brie Crepe with a side of yogurt and blueberries.  The French Toast was huge, nearly two inches thick and had a cake like texture inside the crispy exterior.  Cinnamon syrup, powdered sugar, and plenty of bananas covered every bite of the the toast so that each bite gave full flavor.  No alcohol flavor was detectable on this version.  The crepe was light and had folded slices of ham wrapped inside with gooey cheese.    All the items we ordered were prepared well.  If there was any negative at all, it was that the bacon was a little bit soggy and cooled, but still delicious.  I hope some friends will read this and want to join us the next time we go out for brunch.  5 stars all the way!  Rev #8

My wife and I went with another couple early on Tuesday evening to the local A1 Japanese Steakhouse and Sushi bar.  Three of us like sushi, while one of our group is not willing to eat any seafood, so we were glad he had plenty of items to choose from as well.    There is plenty of parking outside the front door, but if you need handicap access, there is an easier ascent along side the building. Unfortunately, it still requires a small step up since there is no sidewalk connecting the parking lot and the ramp access on the front of the building.  Once inside, we were quickly seated and were able to get a table instead of a booth.   We ordered a couple appetizers:  Edamame (steamed soybeans, but these were not salted on the outside), and Gyoza (pan fried "potstickers" with pork inside the noodle wrap) with a dipping sauce.  The Gyoza was really good, but the edamame was a bit disappointing since we have had the pods salted at other restaurants which is the way we prefer them.  For our dinner, my wife had the Spider Roll (Fried Soft Shell Crab, cucumber, lettuce, avocado w masago & eel sauce).  It was served Maki style (wrapped in seaweed or soy paper), and was okay compared to other restaurants, but not her favorite.  I placed two orders.  First, I ordered the Dragon Roll (Tempura shrimp, cucumber, avocado, eel w eel sauce).  It was very delicious, especially with a bit of soy sauce for dipping.  I believe it was 8 pieces.    I also decided to try the "Salmon Sushi" based upon the recommendations of one of the Yelpers I follow.  I went for the Nigiri style, which means raw salmon over a ball of sushi rice.  I ordered 6 pieces (or three orders since there are only two per order when ordering with rice.  Three pieces of salmon per order if you forego the rice and get it Sashimi style).  This was the first time I have tried raw salmon and the Nigiri style.  It was absolutely fantastic!  The salmon was so fresh that there was no hint of fishy taste, just a subtle salmon flavor.  The texture was softer than marshmallows.  I didn't try dipping them in soy sauce since the flavor of the salmon and rice worked perfectly together.  And the rice is absolutely delicious.  It was almost buttery in taste.  I will definitely order it again.  So, three of the four of us really enjoyed our dinners while my wife was a bit disappointed (see edamame and Spider roll).  Our friend really liked his beef appetizer (not sure what it was called) and his beef and chicken entree.  As far as service, it was okay, but could use a bit of improvement.  Communication was difficult.  She spoke very softly considering the background music and chatter of conversation in the room.  I had to ask her more than once to repeat herself just to be sure I understood.   We had to ask where our guests' appetizer was since it didn't come out at the same time.  (It did arrive soon, but if she had explained that the beef takes longer to prepare than the gyoza, we would have understood.)  Also, I am not sure why my wife's entree was put on the same platter as my two entrees.  No additional plate was brought out after our small appetizer plates were collected.  I don't think we realized that the small entree was even on my platter for a few minutes.  I'm pretty sure she mentioned it, but apparently, I wasn't listening close enough.  It just seemed odd that the other couple got separate plates, while we were supposed to share.  So, if you want fresh and delicious Japanese style food, definitely give this place a try.  However, understand that communication may need to be initiated.  Review #70

I was downtown Monday and a friend recommended stopping in at Oso's for lunch.  From the look of the place, it seemed like it must be new and is still improving the decor.  A large notice on the front window (I assume they are awaiting a license for drinks) made me think they were closed initially, but they do have a neon sign saying when they are open.  So, I went on in and grabbed a seat.    I was greeted promptly and given a menu.  I explained that it was my first time here and could use help picking something from the Honduran/Dominican menu.  The host was very helpful and explained that they have a list of foods from both nationalities as well as more Americanized items like Cuban Sandwiches.    With his help, I went with the Pollo Guizado with moro and salad.  The Pollo Guizado is described as Chicken Stew.  The moro is a traditional rice and bean side dish that took on an orange color from the seasonings.    When the meal came out, the chicken and rice/beans were mixed together.  The chicken stew did not come with a broth, so it was more like a slow roasted dish.  Please note that to enhance the savoriness of the flavor, they use the back bone/neck of the chicken in the roasting.  So, watch out for small vertebra and cartilage pieces before chomping.  I assume the hoofed proteins don't have to carry this caution.  The flavors of both dishes (since I ate them together on each bite) were deep and savory without being overwhelming.  The heat level was low (intentionally).  The host mentioned that certain items can be made "hotter" with additional spices (such as the stir fry items), but that they want to appeal to more palates with their basic recipes.    The portion size was reasonable and quite generous for lunch.    The salad was a nice side salad size with crisp lettuce and red cabbage.  The dressing was already on the salad when served.  Fortunately, there was a correct amount of dressing to add flavor without making the salad drenched.  I also tried a Guava natural juice with lunch.  It had a bright sweet/sour flavor with a bit of tangy kick.    Overall, I enjoyed my experience.  I think it could use a bit more decor work to make it more visually appealing.  The customer service was polite and generally good, but could pick up a few pointers like offering glasses of water to the customer and bringing out the silverware/napkins ahead of time.  Little things to make the experience more appealing.  I definitely preferred this dining experience to my first Honduran meal at a north side restaurant.  Review #160

We stopped by Sun King and thought we would check out the new Oca restaurant/shop inside.  Oca, meaning "Goose", is a spin-off for Goose the Market that opened inside the public area of the brewery.  Although they hadn't "officially" announced they were open, I heard that they were open in the evenings and working through a soft opening process.  So glad we stopped by!  My wife and I both tried one of the bundled French Bread sandwiches.  Tonight's featured City Ham and Gruyere with Dijon mustard, tarragon, and mini sweet pickles (cornichons).  I placed our order at the counter, paid, and gave my name.  They asked if I wanted the sandwiches toasted (yes!) and that allowed me time to pick up a couple drafts at the Sun King counter.  As soon as I was making my way back to our table, the Oca staff called out my name and I was good to go.    I loved the crispy crunch of the bread and the toasting brought out the flavors of the ham and cheese.  Excellent pairing for the spices too.  Can't wait to come back to try some of the sausages and charcuterie.    As if I didn't have enough reasons to stop by Sun King already, now I can get great quality sandwiches while there.  Note that Oca sells packaged meats to take home if you stop by to fill your growler.  Tech stuff:  They are open generally the same hours as the brewery. Parking is free in the Sun King lot.  You do need to bring your I.D. since everyone entering the premises must by 21 and over.  A number of platters are meant for 2 to 4 people, so bring friends!  Review #439

On Friday evening around 7, my external hard drive crashed.  Fortunately, the "Geek Brigade" (soon to be called IT Indianapolis) had someone on hand until 9 that night.  I was able to drop the old drive off and explain what I was hoping could be done.    By Monday afternoon (unfortunately, they are closed weekends), I received a call that my data was recovered.  Because my old drive was seven years old and had run continuously, it simply wore out and appeared to me that all my data was unretrievable.  Fortunately, these guys are Wizards with computers and through some magic, were able to retrieve the data and transfer it to a new drive about the size of a phone.  The new drive only runs when the computer itself is running, so it will get plenty of rest.   Even though this company can serve businesses, it is great to know that they still are able to fit the home users into their schedule without making us wait without our electronics too long.  I will be ordering a new computer to replace the old laptop I currently have, and I will continue to use their antivirus protection which they will set up for me.  (They can even do it remotely if that is more convenient.)    Great people who don't look at you crazy if you aren't computer savvy.  I appreciate that!  P.s.  They have $10 discounts if you "check in" when you arrive.  There are also Yelp discounts of $50 worth for $30 (I didn't use that, so I can't tell you how smoothly that works.)  Review #134

I stopped in to place a "to go" order before heading home.  I was the only customer in the place and no staff was behind the counter.  The music was very loud so that I had to yell back to the kitchen to let someone know I was waiting to place my order.  If you haven't been here before, they have a number of bags on the wall which contain lists of sandwich options by categories.  You are supposed to grab a bag for each sanwich and mark your selections before handing the bag to the cashier.  Fortunately, the cashier was helpful and grabbed the correct bags for me and with a couple quick questions, filled out the bags for me.  I paid and waited for the sandwiches to be made.  A second employee made his way out of the back kitchen and began assembly.  The wait was minimal, but because neither of the employees thought the music too loud, I couldn't understand what the "assembler" said when my order was ready.  I basically heard a mumble and saw his lips moving, so I figured that the eye contact we had meant my order was ready.  Makes me wonder why neither one of the employees gave a thought to turning the music down to a lower volume....  I liked that the sandwiches came double wrapped.  A paper wrapper held most of the ingredients in place.  Then, a foil wrap was added to help keep any juices from escaping.  Anyway, I got the sandwiches home and shared them with my wife.  The Philly Beefsteak was a nice sandwich, but the thin sliced steak was a bit dry and chewy.  There was also an absence of any condiment noticeable on the sandwich, so it came across as being at best, two dimensional in taste.  The onions and peppers were good, definitely better than the beef.  The other sandwich, the Ultimate BLT was by far our favorite.  Lots of smoked bacon and some avocado made this a BALT that was quite good.  The baguette was sliced on the bias which made it easier to handle, though the chopped lettuce managed to work its way out when the sandwich was held too tightly.    Overall, the service and sandwiches were okay, just not anything worth making a point of going out of my way for.  Pretty typical chain store fare.  Review #394

I discovered Graeter's Ice Cream on the menu at Mesh on Mass a few years ago and that's when the waiter told me that they were carrying it at Kroger's.  When I heard Graeter's was opening a shoppe in Broad Ripple, I had to make plans to stop in.    So glad I did.  The Black Raspberry Chocolate Chip is my favorite.  I only wish I lived closer so that I could try more flavors more often!  Review #35

Wow! What a great addition to the neighborhood!  This park used to be a lot smaller and frankly, the neighborhood was not that inviting.  But in the past few years, there has been a major reconstruction of 38th Street from the fairgrounds towards the Art Museum and this block in particular is looking much better.    There still is the small playground and shelter on the north end by the parking lot off Illinois.  There is a basketball court and lots of open ground for playing and running.  But the southern half of the park has the rec center and ultra cool playground with the spongy padded rolling hills that allow kids to climb, play music, jump, swing and go wild!  Oh, and there's a spray park between the parking lot and the rec center and some half court basketball courts to the east.  They even added some additional parking on 39th for convenience.  I would really love to see this area of town see a revitalization to the glory that once marked the near north side.  If this park is an example of the city's commitment to making a difference, then things will be well on their way!  Review #716

The park is a greenspace in the old downtown of Greenwood.  Located just north of the city library, it is a flat area alongside Pleasant Creek which runs along the north side of the park.  The main lawn of the park does have a pair of football goals but no lines to mark the boundaries.  On the east end, a pair of tennis courts also sit near Meridian Street.  There is a cluster of mature trees and a small play area in the southeast corner of the park.  For crossing the creek, a footbridge seems in good condition for traversing from Machledt Dr to the paved path leading to the courts.  The main function of the park appears to be for hosting city events due to its location and the availability of parking spaces at the library and at nearby businesses.  Review #665

We stopped by Sun King and thought we would check out the new Oca restaurant/shop inside. Oca, meaning "Goose", is a spin-off for Goose the Market that opened inside the public area of the brewery. Although they hadn't "officially" announced they were open, I had heard that they were open in the evenings and were working through a soft opening process. So glad we stopped by!  My wife and I both tried one of the bundled French Bread sandwiches. Tonight's featured City Ham and Gruyere with Dijon mustard, tarragon, and mini sweet pickles (cornichons). I placed our order at the counter, paid, and gave my name. They asked if I wanted the sandwiches toasted (yes!) and that allowed me time to pick up a couple drafts at the Sun King counter. As soon as I was making my way back to our table, the Oca staff called out my name and I was good to go.   I loved the crispy crunch of the bread and the toasting brought out the flavors of the ham and cheese. Excellent pairing for the spices too. Can't wait to come back to try some of the sausages and charcuterie.   *****update****** I made it back one evening and decided to try the Choucrote Garnie which may as well translate to "meat lover's dream!"  Actually, it's a "traditional dish of France's Alsace region bordering Germany" and the Choucrote is fermented cabbage while the Garnie means it is dressed with Riesling (white wine), herbs, potatoes, and charcuterie.   This huge option is brought out in a roasting pan.  My eyes started to glaze over at all the meats.  In the center was a large peppery Knack(wurst) nestled over a large serving of the Choucrote.  To the left was a thick (a full inch) smoked rib chop that was the most tender pork chop I've had.  In the upper left corner were two Nuremberg sausage (technically much larger at about 5 inches instead of the 9 cm traditional).  The Nuremberg have a thicker casing and more in the Bratwurst family.  To the right of the Knack were a couple slices of Pancetta that looked like American bacon, but have a higher salt content.  Just below that, there were two Strasbourg frankfurters.  Oh, and there were two potatoes that were halved and roasted.  The Choucrote itself was a great surprise at how much I enjoyed it.  My mother used to make a really nasty version of sauerkraut and dressed it with white vinegar.  I hated it!  But here, the pungent odor of vinegar is replaced by the pleasing notes of the Riesling.  The sour of the dish is tempered as well, so the overall taste is quite pleasing, especially since it is warm and served thoroughly tender. (I am not a fan of the sometimes rubbery and tough texture of raw cabbage.)  The portion size suggests it is for two to four people.  They mean it on this dish!  I made really great headway on devouring the dish, but common sense struck me before I was stuffed and decided to get a to go box.  Not for the picky eater, this is a dish that goes great with a dark beer (I went with the Sun King "Stuck in the Middle" Milk Stout option. Yum!)  *****back to the original review*****  As if I didn't have enough reasons to stop by Sun King already, now I can get great quality sandwiches while there. Note that Oca sells packaged meats to take home if you stop by to fill your growler.  Tech stuff: They are open generally the same hours as the brewery.  Parking is free in the Sun King lot.  A number of platters are meant for 2 to 4 people, so bring friends!  Review #439 Rev #30

The lunch special is only $5.50 (before tax and tip) and includes a variety of options.  You also get an egg roll, your choice of Egg Drop or Hot & Sour Soup, and your choice of steamed or fried rice with the lunch sized entree.  On my visit, I opted for the Pepper Steak (bite sized chunks of Green Bell Pepper and slices of onion) entree, the Egg Drop, and the fried rice.  The Egg Drop soup was delicious!  Just a bit of thickening and a little green onion for extra flavor made this one of my favorite takes on the soup.    The rest of the lunch came before I finished my soup.  The portions may be a little smaller than at some other Asian restaurants, but the price was also smaller and included the sides.  The beef and veggies were tender with maybe a bit more veggies than beef, but if this isn't for you, there is always the regular menu to select from.  The only negative I had was the fried rice had a slightly spongy texture, but it did not affect the flavor.    The service was friendly, prompt, and communicated clearly.  When I entered, I approached the counter and was shown to a table.  A menu was brought out and my order taken.  In fact, everything seemed to be full-service from the wait staff with the exception of payment.  When I finished, I simply went to the counter (without having received my bill) and checked out then.  I am not sure if they ever bring out your bill to your table.  I simply followed the lead of the other patrons.  Overall, a very positive experience on my first visit and with the tasty flavors, I recommend it!  Review #462

I stopped by this downtown drafthouse on Mass Avenue for lunch on a rainy Wednesday.  The good news was that the rain kept the crowds down, so I was able to find street parking.  The bad news is that the patio was unavailable due to the rain.  I remember when this used to  be Agio's restaurant...a great place to sit out and people watch while dining.  I was seated right away and looked through the lengthy list of craft beers.  The selections I had scouted on their website had dropped off the list, but because the beer list has so much information, I was able to find a tasty substitute without any trouble.  Based upon a recommendation from a fellow Yelper, I decided to go with the Recession Burger and Lemon Grass Cucumber Slaw.   The Recession Burger was fantastic!  It is definitely one of the best burgers I have had all year!  I really like combination burgers that mix other foods into the patties before grilling.  This burger has shredded potatoes mixed with ground beef seared on a flat top grill, topped with aged cheddar, bacon, mixed greens, and house-made ketchup and spicy mustard on a pretzel bun.  The mustard had fresh horseradish, so a couple times I got a mild sinus blast!  What I really like about the flavors is that I am a fan of pretzels and brown mustard.  This combo really worked well with the burger and bacon.  Yum!  Oh, and even though the burger was well done, it retained enough juices to keep it tasting fresh.  There was a really nice sear on the burger to bring out the flavor of the beef as well.  If you are a fan of lemon, then definitely try the slaw.  It came with lettuce instead of cabbage, tomato strips, peeled cucumber slices, and red onion.  The lemon marinated the vegetables nicely to bring a tangy/tart uniformity to the different flavors.  I would definitely order this again.  Good service, good food, good selection.  I look forward to bringing some friends here soon!  Review #71

Although I didn't show up until nearly 11 a.m., I was pleased that there were still a variety of donuts to choose from.  I selected the Maple Bacon donut and the Cookie Butter donut as my choices of the day.   The Maple Bacon has the top of the pastry (no hole) covered with maple glaze and then crisscrossed with a couple slices of crispy bacon.  Great flavor combo!    The Cookie Butter is also a round (no hole) pastry that has a creamy & buttery spread on top and dusted with crumbled cookie crumbs.      Both were quite yummy and still reasonably fresh considering how late in the day I ate them (without benefit of being covered or with any type of beverage.)  I can only imagine the quantity of pastry available early in the morning.      As far as the building, it is rather non-descript...something you could easily drive right by without benefit of a sign along the roadside.  There is a sign along the roofline of the building with the shop's name spelled out.    One of the benefits of the location is that it has its own parking lot on the north side of the building.  However, there is no entrance from the lot to the store.  You have to walk down several steps to the side walk to find the entrance.  For those who like a beverage with their pastry, have no fear.  They have a variety of hot an cold options available too.  Review #847

The park has been a "go to" destination for Indy residents for generations.  What started out as a private residence, the park has undergone many additions and changes over the years.  In 2017, "The Ruins" had a major transformation:  the pool/fountain was removed and the splash area was added to the east side of the wall.  But unlike other splash parks, this one has "ruined" statues and animal sculptures that represent some of the wildlife in the park.  Beyond the ruins, there is a huge playground near the south entrance.  There are so many places for kids to swing, climb, and slide that they may wear out just running between them trying to use them all!  To the east, a nature center is on the north end while lots of nature trails lead off into the woods and towards the river.  Note that the trails have a fair amount of elevation change which may be challenging.  Overall, this 95 acre park has a lot to offer for those who want to enjoy nature and have kids that like to be active.  Review #732

I continue to be impressed with the quality of food at Ralston's.  This is the fourth time I have been here and I have tried something different each time.  Good food, good atmosphere, and good service each time.  I stopped in with a friend on Tuesday for lunch.  We selected a spot on the open patio to dine.  Although the music was a bit too loud, it was a great spot to people watch.  My friend went with my suggestion of the Recession Burger.  She was very pleased with the sandwich's excellent combination of flavors:  Seared ground beef and potato in the burger, bacon, house mustard and ketchup and cheddar on top.  Delicious!  I went with the Sauced Duck: Pulled duck, spicy peach chipotle sauce (Yum!), gorgonzola, toasted almonds, and greens all wrapped in a flatbread that was light as a pancake.  Although the duck itself was a little dry, it was delicious when combined with all the other ingredients.  The peach chipotle sauce, with chunks of peach, was a perfect balance of heat and sweet.  The greens added a bit of crunch that gave the roll-up a variety of textures.  Great sandwich!  I double upgraded my side dish.  I selected the Sweet Potato Fries ($2) which comes with the house ketchup, and added the Cinnamon Cream Cheese dip ($1).  My friend said it best, "This tastes like dessert!"  If you haven't tried Ralston's yet, make a point to stop in.  I highly recommend their weekend brunch selections as well as their lunch time sandwiches.  Rev #15

Although there are plenty of flower and shrub places closer to us, my wife and I still find ourselves returning to Butler's just to make sure we don't miss something special.  Even though many places were picked over after Mother's Day, we still found plenty of quality hanging baskets and flowering shrubs at Butler's.  The friendly owners are on hand every time we go and answer questions about caring for the plants we buy.  Looks like we will continue coming back next year too!  Review #295

I had an enjoyable meal at Nickel Plate.  Located on the north side of 116th, there is a decent sized parking lot on the east side of the building.  Note that since the lot isn't exclusive, it can fill up fast.  I was greeted at the door and taken to a seat promptly.  The waitress did a fine job in taking my order, bringing out the food and checking on my beverage, and handling the bill payment.  What really surprised me was how swiftly the kitchen turned around my order.  It was less than 10 minutes from the time I placed my order!    I decided to go with the namesake Nickel Plate burger which was a juicy burger topped with cajun spices, grilled onions, and hot pepper cheese served on grilled Texas Toast.  The burger came lettuce, tomato, pickle and mayo on the side.  My first bite was without the side items and I was a little disappointed there wasn't much heat to the "hot pepper cheese" and the cajun spices.  I chose to add the side items and the flavor was improved.  It did make for a big bite due to thickness, but the toast was soft enough to allow for some squeezing to make it more bite-sized.  Overall, it was a pretty good sandwich.  If you order it, be aware that the bread is grilled with butter, so when you pick it up, your fingers will get a little messy.  (May need to ask for an extra napkin - they use paper ones.)  For a side dish, I went with the cole slaw.  They make it light, but a little bit creamy.  Pretty good option.  Some of the shreds of cabbage were a bit long and made it a little harder to fit on a fork.  But the flavor was fine.  Overall, I was pleased with the service and satisfied with the food.  I appreciated their effort in getting me taken care of so quickly.  Good job!  Review #433

My wife and I stopped in on Wednesday morning to pick up some locally made apple cider.  During the week, the crowds are down and the parking is much easier to find near the store portion of the property.  Unfortunately, the elephant ears and some of the menu items that make this place a treat aren't available until the weekend.  Outside the storeroom, there were rows of pre-picked pumpkins arranged by size and ready for purchase.  It makes it much easier for little ones to spot one they like that is already ripe.  There is also a play area with a playground and piles of baled hay for the adventurous to climb on.    Inside the storeroom, there are numerous varieties of apples bagged in various sizes like bushel, half bushel, and peck.  So, even though some folks enjoy the U-pick option, you can always let someone else do the picking and simply select the size and variety of fruit you want.  Note that the bags used for these pre-packaged fruits are "see through", so you can tell that there aren't any spoiled or damaged ones!  Further inside, there are a number of canned and refrigerated goods for purchase.  On this trip, we picked up several jars of preserves, a tasty pumpkin cake log, a taffy apple with peanuts, and our jug of apple cider.  Everything we have tasted so far has been excellent!  As a word of advice, before you go, be sure to check the website.  Because all the fruits are grown locally, the growing season determines when certain types of each fruit are available.    So, why not five stars?  Well, a while back, bad weather damaged a number of the heirloom or hard to find varieties.  The owners decided not to replant those, so the types of apples are just not as plentiful as they used to be.  (I used two specific types in the pies I make, and now I have to use replacements that just don't have the qualities I look for in baking apples.)  Honestly, it was the uniqueness that brought me to the orchard more frequently.  Many varieties they now offer are carried in chain store groceries.    And while there today, the staff seemed more interested in talking to each other than greeting us.  There were four clerks behind the counter and when I placed all our goods on the counter to check out, not one stepped forward or even greeted me to ask if I was ready.  I basically had to initiate the conversation to get one's attention.  Just not 5-star service.  Review #143

Although I don't get over to this side of town as often, I have to admit that when I think of buying something for my home, this place is one of the first places I think of.  Sometimes, it may be an outdoor decoration.  Maybe it's a holiday gift box (I hate using wrapping paper!)  The point is that they carry items that aren't like all the big box stores and this warehouse sized business has a huge variety to look over.  Sure, it's not fine art, but it is affordable and allows me to go with a style for a while and then, if I change my mind, not feel like I've wasted money when moving on.    They also have a large variety of glass and kitchen wares, floral arrangements (both assembled and components for when I feel artsy), and lots of holiday themed knickknacks.  Even when I don't make a purchase, I find it enjoyable to browse the variety of objects they carry.  Review #245

I cannot wait to go back to this park!  It has so many amenities on the east side of the park and great hiking trails on the west.  I didn't even get to appreciate all the colors that come in spring or fall, just the drab color of winter, and I still loved this place.    Okay, so there is lots of paved parking with multiple lots so that you can get to the shelters, or the playground, or the splash park without having lots of walking.  But if you feel like walking or biking, there are paved paths that appear to be mostly dry and if they aren't long enough for you, they are connected to trails that lead all around Plainfield!      After checking out the east side which was clean and seemed to be in great condition (yes to water fountains and restrooms), I crossed over a bridge which spans White Lick Creek and had the option of two trails:  The Blue Heron Trail that leads south passed the Blue Heron Lake (about a mile long); or the Cottonwood Path which heads north across another bridge to loop through the trees (about a quarter of a mile).  Both trails were paved with a dividing line to encourage people to stay on their side and reduce bike & pedestrian collisions.  The Blue Heron trail can be accessed from the county road to the south of the park as a starting point as well as from crossing the bridge from inside the park.  I did notice one spot near one of the many small lakes/ponds that the trail pavement was a little slippery from an overspill from the heavy rains recently left a light smear of mud.  Not bad, but it was probably very slippery a day earlier.  I also liked that the trail had markers every tenth of a mile.  There were also a couple location guides in the park that showed the general layout of the park.  I snapped a quick photo and used it on the trail since there were a couple offshoot trails that weren't leading any place I was interested in going.    There is a third trail which loops around the east side called the Red Maple Path and from the pictures I've seen on Yelp, there are lots of spectacularly colorful trees that warrant a stop in autumn.  I'll be back.  Review #612

I stopped in and must admit, the food I had (carnitas burrito) was generously portioned and quite tasty.  I liked that it was made to order and the line moved quickly.  I really liked that they steamed the tortilla before making the burrito so that it was soft and warm and held its shape without breaking like I've had at other places.     They do have convenient parking and some tables inside for dining, but most of the folks were getting their food to go.  The line starts at the counter end by the door and you work your way down the line and the servers build your meal as you go.  (If you have been to Chipotle, then it is handled the same way.)  They do have some beer available, but I passed on these since I got my order to go.    Although there were some basics like burritos, quesadillas, and tacos, there was not as much variety as a number of Mexican based restaurants as I've dined.  So, if you want one of the basics, you can have it made to order here.  If not, then you may want to try someplace else.  Review #346

Bring a friend...the servings are HUGE!    I had lunch on Wednesday and was lucky enough to street park in front of the patio of Taste.  I walked around the central indoor seating area and approached the pastry counter and the giant white board of options.  Fortunately, I had pre-selected what I wanted by reading other Yelp reviews, so I quickly placed my order and took a number to a table I selected by the front.  The wait was fairly short.  Since I only wanted water as my beverage, I was directed to a central station where chilled water with lemon was ready for self serve.  (Utensils, iced tea, and other items were there too.)  Because I ordered several items, the staff behind the counter asked if I wanted the items delivered as courses or all at once.  I went for the courses.    Before long, my eyes nearly bulged out as my V-8 Salad was delivered.  A 9-inch bowl filled with lettuce and 8 other vegetables was easily enough for two.  (I think there were about 5 cups of vegetables in that bowl!.)  The veggies were tossed in a generous amount of honey tarragon vinaigrette (maybe a bit heavy handed on the application).  The salad took on a sweetened taste that complimented the wide variety of flavors.  I think the corn and red onion  were my favorite bites, but the other bites were also tasty.  This was one of the best salads I have had all year.  (Take home box....yes, please!)  About half way through the salad, my B.A.L.T (A is for Avocado) with basil aioli and my Pomme Frites (with more basil aioli in a cup on the side) arrived.  The sandwich was served on a hoagie bun (about 8 inches total, sliced in diagonal halves.)  The frites were seasoned with Kosher salt and a light amount of cracked pepper.   The B.A.L.T. had a nice crunch to the bread and a bit of saltiness from the bacon.  I am not sure what component gave the sandwich a bit of tartness that I wasn't expecting.  It was a little distracting from my overall enjoyment of the sandwich.  The frites were served wrapped in a paper funnel stuffed into a metal cup.  I would guess there were more than two cups of frites served hot and tasty.  Just enough salt to perk up the flavor without overwhelming the potato taste.  Excellent job.  The dipping aioli added a nice complimentary taste, but I used it sparingly since I was already eating a huge meal.  (Half of the frites made the ride home too!)  I found the staff to be friendly and helpful.  I was made to feel welcome without their need to hover.  I would definitely be willing to return for more, possibly to try a selection from the lengthy breakfast and dessert options.  Review #89

What a perfect day to sit outside on the shaded patio of Vino Villa!  Tuesday morning, I headed over for lunch and grabbed one of the parking spaces behind the restaurant (about a dozen).  Since it was my first time there, I toured the inside noting a store and wine room on the first floor; rooms to dine on the second.  Because there was only one waitress on duty, I was asked to sit out on the patio since the weather was perfect.  I grabbed a table under the largest shade tree.  From there I could see a gazebo with additional seating as well as the patio which is undergoing some beautification.  After a slight wait for the waitress to chase down a question from one of the other customers, I was brought a menu and water.  I started off with a Chardonnay before placing a couple orders.  First, I ordered the Caprese Salad to take advantage of tomato season.  Four slices of a Mozzarella ball were covered with basil and tomato slices, red onion and a house vinaigrette (olive oil and balsamic vinegar?)  Absolutely delicious!  I also grabbed the "Asparagus in a Blanket".  Six blankets of asparagus with prosciutto and Gruyere cheese wrapped and baked in Phyllo dough to a crispy crunch!  On the side was a pattern of ornately arranged peanut, sriracha, and wasabi sauces that added as much color to the plate as the flavor did to the rolls.  Definitely would order this again!  And since I was anxious to try more, I settled on the Muffuletta:  a grilled hoagie bun with mortadella, salami, capocolla, olive salad, & provolone cheese.  The sandwich was pressed to a crunchy crisp outside but was nice and moist inside from the olive salad and juiciness of the meats.  The sandwich was cooked perfectly, but because the olives had the strongest flavors, the meats tended to blur into one common flavor.  Okay, but not phenomenal.  (Served with kettle chips.)  Total lunch took just over an hour, probably a bit less if I had decided on the sandwich earlier.  Still, it was a good decision so that the sandwich was nice and warm when I was ready to eat it.  I look forward to returning on another beautiful afternoon.  Review #88

I stopped in with some friends while on the north side.  This outlet store sells caramels, chocolates and knick knacks for a family owned business based in Hagerstown, IN.  The founders (the Abbott's) started making caramels in 1890, and chocolates around 1910.  Although, the business was sold to others in 2012, the original recipes have been maintained for over 100 years.    And you can taste the quality in the products.  The caramels are melt in your mouth delicious!  The chocolates I purchased came in a variety of mostly bite sized samples.  Excellent options are available, some with milk chocolate, and others with dark.    Most of the candies are made in Indiana.  You can tell which are locally made by the title plates for each variety.  Other hard candies are available on site, but those, along with the knick knacks are produced elsewhere.    Besides the knick knacks, there are some gift packages available.  Some are strictly chocolates.  Others are chocolates formed into shapes to help celebrate different occasions.      Although the chocolates are on the pricey side, the quality is really good and worth checking out when you are looking for some instant gratification for your sweet tooth.  Review #355

If you like small chocolate bites, assorted truffles, and even barks and toffees, then you will not be disappointed by the variety and quality offered by Ganache.  I stopped in (street parking is free in the area) and decided to get a few items to go.  I like that most of the chocolate bites come in milk chocolate and dark chocolate options, and some even come with white chocolate too!  The truffles show artistic skill as well.  My only negative is the pricing.  Some chocolates were $38 per pound!  I've had delicious chocolates from "mom and pop" confectioners that were less than half that price that were equally tasty.  I picked up six pieces of candy for over $8.  Truffles run about $3 each.  If you have a sweet tooth, this place can take care of you.  Just be sure your eyes aren't bigger than your wallet.  Review #428

I stopped by for lunch Wednesday afternoon.  I hadn't been to this restaurant for a long time, so I was pleased to see the changes in this location compared to the old one across the street.  The new place has a lot more light and more outdoor seating which is nice for days like today.    For the lunch crowd, the primary choice is to select from one of four types of pizzas that are fired up continuously and sold by the slice.    I added a side salad with my choice of dressing on the side.  Very reasonable price.  Unfortunately, the sliced tomato was lacking color and flavor.  I selected one of the special slices.  My choice had bacon, sun-dried tomato, fresh basil, and onion on a cracker crisp crust. Nice flavor combo!    Overall, I thought the food pretty good and the idea for offering pizza by the slice improves your chance for a quick meal during your lunch hour.  Review #157

My wife and I stopped in for lunch and had a really nice meal.  We grabbed a pull-in spot in front of the store and decided to dine in rather than sit on the patio in front.  Inside, soothing music played and a beautifully decorated room awaited.  There were a lot of dark wood booths and walls were accented with Japanese items including instruments and a kimono.  A full length sushi bar was on the right, and another dining room was behind the first.  After our beverages, my wife went with the lunch special Chicken Teryaki which was perfectly cooked.  The chicken had hints of grilled flavor and the sweet & savory combo of the teryaki was delicious.  I ordered from the sushi side, starting with sake (salmon) nigiri (raw over rice) and ordered a huge Las Vegas roll with barbecued eel, avocado, cream cheese, tempura fried, and topped with spicy mayo and unagi sauce.  Wow!  The roll was thin sliced and was delicious without adding any soy from dipping.  I will say the nigiri was a little odd tasting...I think from the rice.  Not sure why, but the flavor wasn't as delicious as the other items.  The edamame that was ordered as an appetizer was a little under cooked and made it harder to pop the beans from the pods.  They did have a generous amount of sea salt that was evenly distributed, not just on the top.  Just okay.  The service was quietly gracious and efficient, very much as you might expect from a proper Japanese restaurant.  We had no trouble communicating and wait times were minimal.  Overall, a very good experience that I would recommend for both the sushi and grill sides of the bistro.  Review #1151

I stopped in on an early afternoon to sample the beverages generated by this small brewery just southwest of 96th and Hague Rd.  It was a little hard to find it, but well worth the search!    I pulled up out front and when I entered, I could tell that the front area was for dining and placing orders for food items, but a sign over the back doorway directed me to the brewery as well as the areas for over and under the age of 21.    In the bar area, the staff were really helpful and pleasant to deal with.  It was my first visit and they all wanted to make a good impression.  I ordered a flight of house brews (four 5 oz choices for $8.)  For being a small brewery, I had no problem selecting my four.  I went with Cream & Punishment (a cream ale 4.8% 16 IBU),The Man in the Big Yellow Hefe (Hefewiezen 4.7% 11 IBU), Charlie and the Chocolate Stout (6.3% 23 IBU), and The Hound (a sour 7.0%, 18 IBU).      Of these the stout was my favorite with a milk chocolate overtone that was delicious!  I also really liked the cream ale.  The sour surprised me with the sour being so prominent on the first sip.  The hefewiezen was a little mild compared to other breweries...not as much banana and clove flavors.    They also let me get tastes of three other options:  Shogun Soba Ale was buttery smooth; Clifford the Big Red Ale was fresh and tasty; and A Beer Called Ove was a really nice Belgian Ale.  All were good.    If I am back on this side of town, I will have to stop by and sample the food items on the menu.  I am sure I will find a nice beer to go with what ever I order!  Review #348

Stopped in again for dessert after dining in Broad Ripple.  I got a bowl of Black Cherry Chocolate Chip ice cream, while my wife got a waffle cone of Black Raspberry Chocolate Chip.  Both were fantastic!  Our friend wanted to get a gelato, but they were out at the time.  Although a bit disappointed, she really enjoyed a child sized Banana ice cream cone.  Great flavors all around.  Rev #2

I stopped in during their soft opening period (the grand opening is planned for May) to sample a flight of their brews.  They had five house brews listed on their chalkboard behind the bar, so I selected my four (5 oz each for $8 total).  The Blonde Ale (4.7% 17.7 IBU) was fine and had a mellow taste, about what you would expect from the light end of the beer spectrum.  I then tried the Schwarzbier (5.1% 17.5) which is a dark beer.  It was another fine beer, but didn't particularly "wow" me.  Then I had the Carmel Apple Stout (5.4%, 35) which had a fantastic aroma of apples.  I thought this would be the best by far, but the taste didn't quite live up to the aroma.  It was again, a good tasting beer, but just ran middle of the road in taste.  And then I tried the Hoppy Pale Ale (6.7% 67) and got my "Wow".  I am not usually an IPA fan, but the flavor balance of this brew was delicious!  Maybe my tastes have changed or my palate was a little off from normal, but the hoppy taste of this brew was the best I had on that spectrum in a long time.  I definitely recommend this one if you are ordering a pint.  One of the owners was behind the bar and seemed very friendly and was interesting when engaged about the plans of the brewery.  The plans sound great if they can get all the required permits.  There is parking on their private lot on the north side of the building.  Food offerings will be available.  I think I read that it will be a limited offering with items like 10" pizzas, hot dogs, and snacks.  Hopefully, the grand opening will help them successfully launch this welcome addition to the neighborhood.  Note:  Check out the cool mural on the south side of the building.  Review #772

This local bakery has a tasty array of donuts, rolls, fritters, and cupcakes.  They even have full size cakes available too!  The prices are great.  I got six rolls & fritters for about $6.  The service was friendly and quick.  If you have a sweet tooth in Mooresville, this place has hours that accommodate customers.  Review #444

I am not a "hands on" kind of maintenance guy...I usually make matter worse than better.  Having confessed that, there are some tasks that even I can do.  And when I need a tool or piece, I always go to our local Lowe's.  The folks that work there are helpful and aren't hard to find like in some other big box stores.      They usually have the items I need, but if they don't, they are willing to order them for me.  I don't spend a lot of time waiting in line either.  They have plenty of room in the aisles and they have a complementary lawn and garden center that has a nice variety of plants and veggies.    Review #255

I had the pleasure of dining here on their first day and was very pleased with the atmosphere, the staff, AND the food.  Conner's is located inside the newly renovated Marriott and is the first of what is planned as a new series of restaurants for the hotel chain.  The restaurant has two entrances:  Street side is the main entrance where the sports bar "Champions" used to be (though you probably wouldn't recognize it now); from inside the hotel on the first level (if you use this one, you have to walk through to the street entrance to the reception desk to be seated).  Dining alone, I selected a spot at the front bar (yes there is a second one near the hotel entrance.)  I was greeted promptly and welcomed to the restaurant by the bartender.  The menu is designed for breakfast, lunch, dinner, and even brunch.  I was given a lunch menu to peruse and made a couple choices.  My appetizer (which is shareable) was the "Sticky Brussels Sprouts" which aren't crisped, but are large and halved served with apple bacon caramel (the sticky!), whole smoked almonds, and sprinkled with crushed red pepper.  The taste was layered and yummy with the sweet, smokey, nutty flavors and a heat chaser.  I recommend these!  For my lunch, I went with the Grilled Salmon.  The salmon was cooked perfectly.  Moist and flaky and topped with a brown butter mustard glaze, roasted mini bell pepper slices in three colors, chopped snap peas (cut on the bias), and served over a tasty quinoa pilaf.  YUM!    Sure, the prices are on the high end, but considering it is located in a hotel, I kind of suspected the prices would be.  At least you can get great food for your money.    I didn't get to try any dessert since I filled up faster than expected.  They look like they have an extensive alcohol collection which even had some local distillery items (from Gnaw Bone!) on hand.  I parked at the mall for a buck and walked the winding way to the restaurant without having to go outside.  I think street parking is rather limited, but their is hotel parking.  I don't know if they validate you parking for dining though.  I hope someone thinks to ask.  Review #813

While in Speedway, I decided to stop by this antique mall on Main.  Although it looks kind of small from the front, the mall becomes a split level shop about half way back.  The front half has a central room with smaller rooms off to the left and right.  I was pleased to see these were arranged nicely, in some cases, like someone's living room.  It made it very easy to move around and to view the items in the context of how they may look in my own home.  In the back half, the shop is more rows of booths than rooms.  Things are a little less formally arranged, but still good for browsing.    Due to the proximity of the track, there were quite a few booths featuring racing and car memorabilia, so if you are a fan of those, this is a definite place to stop by.  Review #1973

I stopped in for lunch on a Sunday back in March.  Construction was still going on for the new outdoor seating, so I took a seat near the front of the restaurant.  This sister restaurant to Bakersfield (just a few doors down on Mass Ave.) had minimal decor making me wonder if the main restaurant was still being worked on or if it was their choice.  Based on the waitress' recommendation, I went with the fried chicken, cole slaw, fries, and an Abita Root Beer.  The food was brought out quickly and I began dining.  What I was immediately aware of from the first bite of the plentiful chicken is that it was very salty.  I found out afterwards that the chicken is brined before deep frying.  That saturates the chicken with salty taste instead of just on the surface.  So, I was surprised at how salty the breading of the chicken was too.  It was just too much salt and overloaded the chicken flavors.  I tried eating the chicken with the cole slaw and/or taking a quick sip of the root beer, but all that did was make them salty.    I can't comment on their evening atmosphere or beverage options, but based upon my lunch experience, I probably won't be back for the chicken.  Review #50

Red Line, named after the subway train that runs from the north side of Chicago through downtown on down to the south side of the Windy City, is a train themed, self-serve frozen yogurt and treat shop.  Throughout the inside, there are authentic train seats and doors from Chicago's subway system.  There is a central dining room with the self-serve stations at the back and far right side.  You start by deciding on a cup or cone then go to the wall of frozen items where you lift up the handle on the flavor you like to dispense it.  Some stations allow you to use the middle handle to get a mixture of both flavors at that station.  I went with an Orange Creamsicle and Vanilla Cream mix into a bowl.  They then have a crunchies and sprinkles tower that you can spoon additional flavors onto your dessert.  Finally, they have a bar of chopped fruit, nuts, and other goodies to finish off your masterpiece.    And that's where you may wish you had some self restraint because pricing here is based upon the weight!  I used some ground graham cracker on mine and because it didn't weigh much, got my dessert for well under $4.  But if you load up on lots of candies and fruit and chocolate, you may go into sticker shock faster than you can say "brain freeze"!    For those who have some modicum of control, this is a great place to get a cold treat.  All others....beware!  ha!  Review #1929

If you read the other reviews, they can tell you about their favorite types of tea and can speak about tea quality.  What I want to point out is the quality of the help I received from the staff.    After the New Year started, I went in to buy an infuser to replace what I had at home.  I saw they had them listed at $12, or two for $20.  (I've seen them online for anywhere from $11 to over $40! plus shipping.)  When I got to the checkout, the pleasant woman let me know that they had some Christmas mugs on sale that came with the infuser, identical to the one I had selected, for only $8 as a reduced item package.  Not a tough decision to get what I wanted for less money AND a mug too!  She pointed out where to find them on the long wall of accessories and I was able to complete my purchase promptly.    She also pointed out that they have a rewards program for return customers that apply to their online purchases as well.    Overall, the experience was pleasant and I left feeling like customer service is alive and doing well at this store.  I will definitely return when I'm ready to acquire my next batch of tea!  Review #2074

Although we don't need these types of supplies regularly, it's nice to have a place that offers a variety of items to meet our needs.  My wife needed some materials and we were able to find them within a few minutes.  Checkout was breezy too.  My only negative is more the condition of the store:  looked rather dirty and trashy by the entrance (particularly just inside) which made an immediate negative impression.  Come on folks, pick up the debris and push a broom.  Review #2293

As it started snowing, one of the men inside the restaurant told me that when it snows in China, it is seen as a sign of good fortune.  Well, my good fortune started when I took my first bite!  This locally owned restaurant has a variety of sushi options as well as dishes from China, Japan, and Korea.  I stopped by for lunch and was impressed with the number of lunch options.  Many of those come with a complementary bowl of Miso soup and a small green salad with ginger dressing.  The soup uses large pieces of seaweed to add extra flavor during the cooking process.  The salad is fresh and is dressed only on the top, but with enough that you can add some flavor to each bite.  I started with the Sashimi (10 pcs of assorted fish).  My colorful plate arrived shortly after I finished my soup and salad.  There were five varieties of fish/seafood arranged over fanned cucumber slices and shredded white carrots.  It also came with lemon slices and an orchid (which is also edible!)  The fish was very fresh and in most cases, very tender.  I think it was the first time I have tried pink tuna, white tuna, and yellowfin tuna at the same sitting, so it was interesting to note how significantly they varied in taste.  The sliced octopus was much tougher to eat (I've never had it raw before) than the tuna probably because it was from the tentacles which are quite muscular.  Still, with a bit of soy sauce, the flavor was quite good.  I finished the platter with the salmon.  Rich and bright, the fish nearly melted in my mouth.  I will definitely get more salmon at a future date.  I also wanted to try a sushi roll and went for the Green Dragon.  This 7 pc roll comes with cucumber and cooked eel inside, and is topped with avocado slices or cooked eel.  Each piece also has a drizzle of "eel sauce" (sweet, salty, and savory) under the toppings.  Wow!   This was fantastic!  Highly recommended.  And if you are someone who appreciates a chef's artistry, the plates are so appealingly decorated.  The chef creates Japanese inspired art with the colorful array of sauces at the sushi counter.  The staff/hostess were all very welcoming and checked by during each course to make sure I was enjoying my food.  Nice conversation without being interrupting.  Service was prompt and checkout was a breeze in this full service establishment.  They do have a few non-seafood options available for your friends that may not like traditional seafood or sushi.    I will mention that the prices are higher than most lunch options in the Greenwood area.  This stand alone business can't get all the discounts of the massive chain restaurants in the area, but the quality is phenomenal and worth treating yourself to.  The atmosphere of the restaurant is tastefully integrated into the industrial strip mall space.  The noise level was in the quiet to moderate range.  Review #463

As a customer for around 16 years, I can truly say that I believe the staff at Greenwood Family Dentistry cares about making my dental experience the best it can be.  Dr Willman has gotten to know me and isn't in the practice for short-term needs:  He is looking out for the long-term care of my health.  I had poor dental hygiene growing up and by the time I was an adult, needed a number of teeth repaired or spaces bridged.  I have never felt pressured into seeking a treatment that was questionable.    Although the pricing may be higher than some other dentist's office or "quick fix" dentist places, the staff was able to make recommendations for plans that are similar to insurance since I no longer have a "dental plan" after retiring.  The prices for the procedures are now very affordable for the work I need done.  As part of their long-term approach, the staff may occasionally suggest options like trying a different type of tooth brush, getting a flouride treatment, or an oral cancer screening.  I may not want all those options, so as an adult, I have no problem telling them I may not be interested.  I never felt that it was "high pressure"....it's just a matter of being given the benefit of their knowledge.  If you are looking for a dental experience with friendly and caring people who will take time to be thorough for your long-term health care, I highly recommend giving them a try.  Review #846

Blooms by Dragonfly is a small business in the heart of Old Town Zionsville that is a florist shop as well as Home Decor and Gift items.  In addition to coolers with flower arrangements, my wife was quite impressed with the live plant offerings; so much so that she ended up making a purchase claiming the peace lilly was a fraction of the cost of some other large/chain florists she has shopped.  The staff was very friendly and helpful.  We were able to get advice on how best to maintain the live plant as well.  The rest of the store has stuffed animals, inspirational messages on items, and general things to use as knick knacks or wall hangings.  Cute shop!  Note that upstairs is another business where you can get personalized signs made.  Since I didn't find anyone to talk to up there, I haven't set it up as a new business.  Review #2642

If you are hungry for pizza, but want to try something different, then give Pies & Pints a try.  The combos they have assembled are unlike most places:  you don't see Cheese pizza, or meat lovers here.  They have unique combos like the Grape and Gorgonzola, the Mozzarella Caprese, or in my case, the Pine and Swine.  My pizza comes on a thin crust with fresh pineapple cubes, red onions, applewood smoked bacon bites, feta cheese, and is served on a tomato sauce.  It wasn't listed, but it sure tasted like there was quite a bit of garlic as well.  First, I loved the crust.  Thin enough to let the toppings add the most flavor, but thick enough (and cooked well enough) to not go floppy in the middle and stick to the cardboard box I got on my to go order.  I also like that the kitchen cut the ingredients into bite sized pieces.  Some pizza places are lazy and give over sized pieces that don't cook properly in the brief heating period which makes the taste inconsistent.  This place did it right!  I also like the setting/decor of this West Virginia based franchise.  You'll notice a white elephant (Irene) throughout the business.  There is a family dining area near the entrance.  There's a bar area and another dining area beyond the bar.  There is a patio section that they put up clear plastic to add more seating in the winter, and take the plastic off during nicer weather.  There is also an extended open area without seats, but that has a fireplace going for people to stand around.  When I first arrived, an employee came in from outside and walked right by me, did something at the check in place and walked away without acknowledging me.  Not  a great first impression.  After a few moments, I was able to get the bartender's attention and he welcomed me to sit anywhere in his area.  I let him know I wanted my order to go and he was glad to take my order and suggested grabbing a spot at the bar while I waited.  The pizza took about 15 minutes to come out (Sunday late afternoon) so I was really pleased it took as long as I was told.  If you are fixed on your pizza and only want the same thing every time, then don't come here.  Sure, you could probably build your own ingredient by ingredient, but that isn't what this place is about.  I suggest that coming here is an opportunity to try something new.  Just read through the ingredients and see what appeals to you.  Not every pizza place has to be the same.  Pies & Pints stands out in the crowd....like a white elephant.  Review #2419

This is a decent pet shop with friendly workers, plenty of space in the aisles, and a nice selection of items.  There are larger pet stores around the metro area, but this one focuses on having pet supplies, not all the ancillary services that those may have.  In addition to the supplies, they did have a few live animals:  2 cats, a bunny, budgies/parakeets, and some small furry critters too.  (Note:  I did not see any part of the store set up for selling dogs, so those early negative reviews may have contributed to a change.)  If I lived in the area, I could see coming here regularly to pick up supplies.  Review #2142

I had seen some friends had reviewed this place and since I know my wife really likes crispy Mexican pastries, I persuaded her to ride with me to try it out.  She headed on in while I was still in the parking lot.  She grabbed the standard tongs and metal tray (standard for a Panaderia anyway) and was soon hunting the shelves for her favorites.  Most are behind sliding glass doors, but some were still sitting on racks waiting to be added.    Check out had a slight delay, but was minimal.    They have a wide variety of pastries to choose from including some I was not familiar with.  They also sell hot coffee, beverages, snacks, and do have whole cakes as well.  As far as quality, the flavors were really good.  Maybe because it was late morning, the texture was a bit chewy.  The crispy ones were still flaky, but there was a definite bite required to get through them like they had been sitting out a bit.  I also ordered one with jelly and the jelly that was visible on the outside was the only jelly the pastry had.  It may be standard, I don't know.  But it was disappointing.  Overall, good flavors just not quite as good as the one about ten blocks away.  Review #3116

What a pleasant surprise!  I decided to stop by for lunch and after pulling into their private parking lot, was greeted and shown to a table in the dining room.  The dining room was basically divided by a center row created from the backs of the booth seating for 4-top tables.  Another row of tables was available for standard table seating by the windows on each side.  I went with one of the $9 lunch specials and a large cup of Jasmine tea.  The specials come with a bowl of lightly spiced soup (I believe lemongrass) that was quite tasty!  Nearly as soon as I finished my soup, my entree and remaining sides were delivered.  The lunch special also includes a small side salad with a ginger based dressing and a crispy spring roll (veggie) that comes with a sweet dipping sauce (not too thick, but not runny either.)  Both were pleasant tasting without any heavy or dominant flavors.  The sides were included on the same plate as the main course, the Pad See Ewe.  The plate was a full 12" across, so I'm talking about a lot to eat!    The Pad See Ewe was cut into large pieces (no knife is included in the initial tableware delivered at the time of seating.)  Fortunately, I have a big mouth and was able to devour the lunch without requesting a knife, but either they should cut them a bit smaller or you may have to spear and bite or ask for a knife.  I got my choice of protein with the Pad See Ewe, and went with the pork option.  There was a generous helping of meat that was right on the edge of being a little too done, but when combined with the large flat noodles (Yeah!) and the veggies, the meat was fine.  I also like that they include colorful veggies in the mix:  Bright orange carrots, deep green broccoli, and some light green cabbage (I was surprised how delicious the cabbage was with the sauce they include in the dish!) I've seen Pad See Ewe other places that came out a dull brown color.  This dish looked as appetizer as it tasted!  I also was given a choice of spiciness, and went with the "Medium".  That level is one where you taste the heat immediately, but it doesn't escalate from there as you eat more.  Yes, the sinuses got a good workout, but I didn't feel there was any need to drink something after each bite.    The service was friendly, but not intrusive.  They checked in on my after I received my entree and had a chance to eat some before asking how I liked it.  And the check was collected and processed quickly too.  I could easily have dined here during a lunch break.  Overall, a really good place to dine and a lunch offering that is competitive with the best Thai places I've tried in the metro area.    Review #1320

Went back to BRU Burger during the Indy Burger Week promotion and tried their petite size (4 oz beef) Baja Burger and the Gorgonberry Pecan Salad for lunch.  So glad I did!    After finding street parking on Alabama, I arrived just after 11 and choose to dine indoors.  Soon, my "small" sized salad arrived covering most of a 9" square plate!.  Excellent flavor combos between sweet and savory with the gorgonzolla cheese crumbles, crisp bacon pieces, sweet dried cranberries, and candied pecans.  I've had it in the past when they added lots of red pepper flakes, but I prefer this much better.    The sandwich was grilled to order (medium well) and the grilled flavor of the beef was the star of the meal.  I really enjoyed all the toppings that seemed to work well together.  My only complaint was that the Queso Fresco appeared to be scooped in a ball shape in the middle of the sandwich making it especially thick and unevenly distributed.  A couple extra seconds was all that was needed for me to break it down and spread it across the sandwich, but it really should have come out of the kitchen that way.  Anyway, I really liked the flavors of the Queso, the black beans and edamame, dill pickle chips and pea shoots.      I asked the waiter and he suggested that all the beef burgers are available in the smaller 4 oz sizes at a reduced price from the full 8 oz standard burgers.  (I think most are $7 instead of the $10 range for the full size.)  So, if you or someone you know doesn't like eating a half pound of burger, you can get the same great flavors without filling stuffed.    Good service and pleasant atmosphere made for a quick and enjoyable lunch.  Rev #27

This is the place to go if you want a sense of Indy (other than the track in Speedway).  The heart of Indy is found in this circle that was originally intended to be the site of the Governor's Mansion until the then Governor's wife said she would never live there because everyone would be able to see the family's laundry!  All the streets in downtown use this as the focal point including the angled streets Massachusetts, Virginia, Kentucky, and Indiana.  Eventually, a new use was decided and this monument was erected as part of our State's collection of War Memorials (second only in number to Washington DC).  There are numerous websites that talk about the art and sculpture of the circle. (I suggest https://www.indyartsguide.org/public-art/soldiers-and-sailors-monument/ ).  On my most recent visit, I headed into the gift shop at the top of the stairs on the south side of the monument.  Inside is a collection of items with Hoosier logos and commemorating the monument and Indy.    You can also go to the observation deck of this 284' structure for some of the best views in the city.  You can buy an elevator ticket in the gift shop for a small fee, or you can choose to climb the 330 steps to the deck.  Knowing I am not getting any younger, I decided to re-enact the climb I took back in 1963 on my family's visit to Indy while I still could.  I paced myself and eventually made it to the top without passing out as the stairway spirals tighter and tighter as you climb.  Once up there, it is a little difficult to get around the structural girders, especially if there are other people in the small space.    If you haven't been here, it is something to put on your bucket list, even if you have to ride the elevator to do so.  For those of us who love this city and are amazed at the transformation that has occurred here, you can see how beautiful the city has become with all the green spaces that have been preserved.  I love when tourists ask about the city and was glad to share a bit of history and show them points of interest while up there.  Tip:  Regardless of whether you walk or ride to the top, you can ride the elevator down.  Hint:  If street parking is limited due to construction or just regular traffic, you can just about always park inside the Circle Centre Mall for a few hours for only $3.  This remains my favorite spot to visit in the City.  Review #2582

One of the joys of Yelp! is when you give a business a second chance to redeem their reputation after a disappointing service.  The Eagle stepped up big time and I can now see why they are getting good reviews.  I stopped in for lunch on Monday and was seated promptly.  My server was very pleasant and made sure he kept an eye on my water glass and empty dishes.  Nice personality and able to spare a little time for chit chat to make me feel welcome.  I ordered the quarter (dark meat) of the brined Amish chicken with a side of collards.  The collards which were done right, are becoming one of my favorite comfort foods.  This version had a generous serving with a good balance of greens and shredded ham with just enough onion (I think) for flavor.  I would definitely recommend the greens.  The chicken is nicely breaded and because it is brined, the salt in the brine creates a reverse osmosis which initially draws moisture out of the chicken, but then back in at a greater level.  The result is extra juicy chicken which can stand up to the high heat of frying.  I have to admit this is some of the most tender chicken I have had.  My only negative is that they brine for about a day (according to my waiter) which makes the chicken significantly more salty than I am used to.  I home brine for just a couple hours to get the benefit of the moisture intake without as much saltiness.  While my first piece of chicken was really tasty, each subsequent piece tended toward becoming more salty...kind of a cumulative effect (reminds me how some spicy flavors become more "hot" the more you eat.) Maybe I have a lower salt tolerance than most (based upon reviews), but for me, I would prefer a shorter brine time.  The patio and bar areas are great this time of year when the weather is perfect for sitting outside and people watching.  Plenty of drink options are available as well.  Although the reputation of The Eagle is based upon their chicken, I think I would prefer to try one of their other sandwiches/entrees the next time I stop in.  Rev #19

I was able to take my wife to opening day of this new fall festival at Newfields.  The fifty acres of grounds have around 5000 pumpkins transforming the museum grounds into a colorful gathering spot for visitors.  With the aid of a donation from the Lilly Foundation, the museum is making an effort to de-stigmatize the notion that art museums are stuffy.  This was a family friendly event.  Not only are there pumpkins, but there is a kids play area with a pumpkin orange bouncy pad that is huge, a mini straw maze, pumpkin painting, and a petting zoo from McClure's Orchard.  There are photo ops (I spared you by editing my shots for uploading) throughout.    There is also the beer garden.  Sun King is on the south end and has a nice tent and seating area.  The north end has several other beer and cider vendors from around town.  There is also a food alley that has Sahm's, Goose the Market, some other non-food vendors, Oliver Winery, and West Fork Whiskey.  There was live entertainment in the food tent/dining area and a DJ was playing music across from Oldfield's.  A schedule is online at the Newfield's website for the entertainment over the four day event.  And if you didn't get enough from all those things, your ticket gets you in to the museum to see "Infinitely Kusama" on the 4th floor of the art museum.
