Note that even if you have online tickets to get into the festival, you will need to check in at guest registry in the museum to get a time ticket for when you can enter to see this unique exhibit by artist Yayoi Kusama.  Even with a time ticket, you may need to wait awhile (about 20 minutes for us) to get into the exhibit.  Note that you only get to spend 45 seconds in the room with the art installation and only two people can enter at a time (children and babies count as full adults, so be aware.)  You also have to check your purse/bags outside the exhibit.    Inside, the artist has created numerous lighted pumpkins with black polka dots in a room filled with mirrors on top and all the sides.  When I first walked in, I was a bit disoriented because the tiny room looks enormous once inside.  Very cool and something worth the wait.  I highly recommend getting tickets online to save money.  Also, becoming a member will also save you serious dollars.    I hope this event continues to grow/evolve over time like the Winterlights festival has.  I am curious to see what else they can add to make the fall festival even better.  Review #3124

The House is a convenient cafe for stopping by to get soup, sandwiches, and a few treats if you are in the Mooresville area.  The folks who run the place seem really upbeat and want you to have a positive experience dining here.  I stopped in on a rainy winter day and wanted to try some soup.  Lots of choices, but I went with the broccoli cheese, a bowl of chili, and got a chicken salad croissant (two smaller ones, actually) to go so that my wife could share lunch with me.  The highlight of the selections was the chicken salad croissant (s).  The two small pastries were light and sliced with a decent helping of a sweet chicken salad with sliced grapes.  The salad was moist but generally stayed within the sandwich.  No dripping here!  The chili was a very mild style.  I had them add onion and shredded cheese on top and recommend adding those.  It could use a bit more seasoning for my tastes, but was still pleasant.  The broccoli cheese was VERY cheesy with small bits of broccoli.  I would prefer a little higher ratio of veggie to cheese, but again, it's a matter of taste.  (I like to pan sear my broccoli before adding it into the cheese soup at home.)  The food was very moderately priced.  There is a small parking lot out front and a small dining room inside.  Review #2108

My wife was in the mood for a tenderloin, so based upon fellow Yelper Rick (Mr Tenderloin) G's recommendation, we headed on over to this west side pub.  The pub is located near the west end of the shopping plaza so we grabbed a spot in the common lot and headed on in. We were able to pick our own spot.  Note that they have separate entrances for the bar and the dining areas, but there is an open space between them so you can change your mind.  We were greeted by the Bartender/waitress who was really pleasant and did a good job checking in, clearing away used plates, and getting our check out.    My wife went with the smaller of the two tenderloins.  It was listed as only 5 oz, but was thick and still larger than the bun.  Good flavor though it was just a tad over cooked which made it a little less tender than ideal.  Good flavor on the breading as well.  It came with crisp, lightly seasoned house made chips.  I started with the Rarebit appetizer which is supposedly an Irish staple.  It's basically white bread (lightly toasted?) with a white beer cheese sauce and chopped pickles.  It was good, but as you can tell by the description, not fine cuisine.  I also ordered the chicken wings off the appetizer menu as my main course.  I ordered them with Teriyaki sauce.  There were six large sections and they were served hot!  Very tender with just a hint of crispness for a nice texture.  They were just a bit over salted for my tastes, so I wasn't sure if it was the sauce or the chicken.  I would recommend getting the sauce on the side if you can.  No finger towelettes were provided.  The wings also came with celery sticks and a choice of ranch or blue cheese for dipping.  Nice friendly vibe as folks gathered to watch the ball game.  Good service.  Near misses on the food, but still good flavor.  A nice place to grab a bit, a beer, and watch a ballgame.  Review #3118

First time visit and I stopped in to get a to go order.  I picked up the lowest heat level "Southern" for an order of white meat and one of dark meat.  I picked the single side option for both and grabbed the slaw for one and the mac n cheese for the other.    I was surprised at how large the dining room was and it was kept very clean.  I ordered and even though it was to go, I was given a number on a stand so that they could bring my order out to me.  When I got home about 40 minutes later, the food was still warm.  I found my dark meat to be crisped on the outside and moist/tender inside.  Nice flavoring in the breading too.  I also tried some of each side and thought both were good.  The slaw was the vinegar based, non-creamy style.  A little spice, not much sweetness, but a nice balance.  The mac n cheese was creamy, not gooey, with a nice amount of cheese taste.  My wife wasn't as big a fan of the seasoning on the chicken.  She isn't a fan of spiced heat and though this was minimal, she just thought the flavor wasn't as good as some of the chicken places we have closer to home.    Overall, though, I thought the food was reasonably priced and liked that the sides were tasty, not just an after thought.  I'll have to try some of their more "hot" chicken on future visits.  Review #3551

Across from the pay parking on Westfield Blvd is a tiny shop that is literally on the alley.  During warmer months, they even bring some of their items out into the alley during store hours.  Inside the shop, you will find nice quality items like furniture, paintings, and some knick knacks.  During the winter months, the business is making the most of some available space at the corner of Westfield and Guilford.  In that annex, there are lamps, clothing, and more small items that might work in a collection or as a gift.  The only negative is that the supply is rather small compared with other antique shops.  I'm not sure how quickly the inventory turns over, so you'll just have stop by to see whether they have what you're looking for.  Review #2279

There are lots of great arrangements available, especially during the holiday season.  And as the clerk told me, the savings should get bigger as it gets closer to the big day!  When I first walked in, I was impressed with the beautiful display of color making me feel more festive just by walking through.  A number of the arrangements are made in house.  There were also Christmas trees from small to fairly life sized already decorated and ready to go.  Other items like ornaments, stuffed animals, and characters of assorted sizes were around.  The west side of the store was still dedicated to floral and bridal accessories, but I didn't spend much time on that side.  Hurry over if you want to pick something new to make your home more festive...and save some big bucks!  Review #1928

For my second visit to Repeal, I brought a friend to try out the lunch menu.  We found a parking space through the maze of side streets north of the building that led to a small lot next to the restaurant.  Once inside, we were asked to seat ourselves by the bartender/waiter.  The owners could be seen taking care of other tasks about the dining room as we sat across from the bar seating.  Because my friend needed to return to work later, we both settled for water, so I can't recommend any of the numerous cocktails that are made with the liquor distilled right next door at the 12.05 distillery (visible through a picture window in the dining room).  I started off with a side of Brussels Sprouts which were plentiful enough to be shareable.  The sprouts were cooked perfectly...just enough crunch to be appealing and cooked enough to bring out the flavor.  The sprouts were prepared in duck fat and white soy vinaigrette and topped with sesame seeds.  They had a great blend of savory, salt, and acid.  Highly recommended for a party of two or more.  For my main meal, I ordered the Grilled Cheese made with smoked Gouda, apple, and mustard.  The hearty bread slices were extra crispy on the outside while the inside was tender.  It wasn't enough cheese to ooze out with each bite, but was thick enough to give a nice chew.  The flavors were more subtle on this sandwich, so maybe a little more mustard or  a more tart apple might pick up the flavor level.  I upgraded from the chips to a side of fries and they were worth it! ($2 more).  The fries were extra crispy and had a layer of crunch like they were lightly breaded.  A nice amount of salt complimented the flavor to make these some of my favorite fries ever!  I definitely recommend ordering them.  My friend ordered the Alabama Brine Pullled Pork sandwich with chips.  The slow roasted pork had a hint of smokiness in the flavor.  Although tender, the pork was a little bit dry, so using one of the table side sauces is highly recommended.  My friend chose the hickory sauce over the Carolina Mustard or the hot sauce options that were there.  Service was fine even though there was just the one guy working the bar and the tables.  When we saw that he was working the floor alone, we let him know that we had a time limit to watch so my friend could get back to work.  We quickly got our orders and had time to eat them, and still got our bill brought out with 15 minutes to go on our deadline.  I definitely appreciated that!  The next time I return, I hope to try the dinner options.  Review #101

Kaffeine Coffee is hidden in the wedge shaped neighborhood between Mass Avenue and the I-65/I-70.  The shop has a small sign out front and a few parking spaces in front, but other than that, you have to find a spot where street parking is allowed.  I was lucky and got a spot directly in front, so I entered the shop mid-morning.  The shop is rather dimly lit with strong backlighting from the windows.  The interior has some nice decor, using books and giant world mural as the most noticeable.  The place was pretty full, so I got my order to go:  A Kaffeine special blend coffee (12 oz was my size) and a couple muffins.  They have a list of all the coffee options on a small clipboard along the right hand wall (near where the napkins, creamer, sweeteners are.)  They have a lot of flavors, so there should be something for about anyone who likes coffee.  The pastries are kept under glass at the central cashier's counter.  I went with a blueberry muffin and a carrot cake muffin, which I saved for later.  The Blueberry had a good flavor, but was less sweet than most store bought varieties I have tried.  It had a slightly denser texture than I expected as well. (The Carrot Cake is also less sweet than I have had and does not have any icing like most I've tried.  The carrot is really pronounced in flavor.)  The only knock I have here is that like most coffee places, the coffee is kept so hot that you can't drink it straight for ten minutes without scalding your mouth and ruining the ability to taste the flavor.  So, I didn't think there was much flavor in my early sips, but as the coffee cooled, the flavor improved and was more satisfying.    Review #653

There is a lot to enjoy at Lion's Park.  First, it has a great location that is easy to get to from either the south or east side of town, located near the old Zionsville downtown.  Although the park is quite a bit lower than street level (it is near Eagle Creek), the city has built a really impressive stair/ramp system to allow folks to be connected to the shops in old downtown.  The ramps have a manageable slope as they zigzag first to the south then back again to the middle halfway up, continue to the north and return to the middle at the top.  Great planning!  Between the baseball parks, there is a central gathering point which features a gazebo, lots of playground equipment, and what appears to be a concession stand (I went in March, so it wasn't open).    Beyond the central area, there are other amenities (I didn't go through the entire park but could see basketball courts.  What I didn't see were any shelters where you could rent for a family picnic/gathering.  Not sure if I missed them, but they weren't apparent from the center of the park.  There is a large parking lot on the south end of the park.  As with any low lying property at creekside, I can imagine you need to watch the weather if you are planning on hiking around here after heavy rains (the last major flooding was in 2013).  The trails are paved for conservation purposes, hoping that hikers will stay on them.  The park is not part of the city's park system, but ran independently by the Lion's Club.  Still, it is a welcome addition to the areas green spaces.  Review #710

I stopped in Jack's for donuts after discovering them tucked away in a shopping center on Stafford Road (east of SR 267) the night before.  The shop is located on the east end of the shopping center and so it has a drive-thru available, but I decided to simply park in the abundant lot and walk in passed the outdoor patio.  The interior had lots of room for customers to wait in line or grab a small table.  The majority of the donuts were in glass cases between the customers and employees so that customers can get a good look at the donuts.    They had a decent selection with many having a flavored glaze/icing (chocolate, caramel, or sugar glaze) within the donut category.  The donuts, especially the twists and long johns, were large enough they could be shared (but does anyone ever share a donut?)  I ended up purchasing a Tiger Tail (glazed two toned twist), a Carmel Apple (filled bismark with icing), and a Chocolate Nut Stick (unfilled, but with chocolate icing and chopped peanuts.)  The Tiger Tail was light and very sweet.  I couldn't tell any difference in the flavor of the two shades of the twist.  The Carmel Apple had filling in each bite, though not a enough to drip out.  The Chocolate Nut Stick had good flavor, but the longer the nuts sit on the chocolate, the more moisture they absorb.  I didn't eat this one until the following morning and the nuts became chewy.  So, for maximum enjoyment, eat it right away.  It's good to see a local business (New Castle, IN) be so successful and to continue bringing good quality as it expands.  Review #3480

My wife and I decided to stop for a late lunch while in the area.  We were able to grab a spot right in front of the building which has its own parking lot.    When we entered, we were asked if we wanted the Hibachi side or the "regular".  We weren't that interested in a chef show, so we opted for the regular which also has the bar alongside the dining.    Our waitress showed up promptly to take our beverage order and give us time to review the menu.  They also had a list of daily specials near the bar, so my wife decided to go with one of those, the Orange Chicken bowl.  I ordered a side of gyoza to share and also the Chiku Bento Box.  I also ordered a pot of hot green tea.  Although it was served at a great temperature for sipping, the ceramic cup I was given did not have a handle, so it was very uncomfortable to drink from because the cup got too hot.  I ended up using a napkin as insulation between the ceramic and my skin.  Good tea, but gut some regular cups or mugs with handles please!  After a short while, our gyoza arrived.  The flavor was good, especially the dipping sauce.  However, the gyoza were only lightly browned on the bottom.  Maybe that's the traditional way (?), but I brown mine at home all over and to a bit crisper texture so that there is a pleasant crunch to the outside while the inside stays tender.  Just a personal preference, but it was noticeable enough that my wife mentioned it to me.  After our plates were cleared, our entrees arrived.  Her bowl of chicken arrived served over her fried rice upgrade.  It was okay, but lacked any noticeable seasoning other than the orange sauce on the chicken.  She was disappointed that it lacked any depth of flavor.  However, my bento box with my choice of salmon was mostly really good.  The slice of salmon is rather thin, so it was cooked thoroughly but not too overcooked.  It had a tasty glaze on top that was very enjoyable.  It came with a couple types of dipping sauces, half of a California sushi roll, two veggie egg rolls, some more gyoza, and some tempura veggies that had a nice crunchy outside, but lacked any seasoning inside.  It also came with a cup of brown rice on the side.  Overall, it was quite a bit of food especially when you include the small side salad we each got with a bit of a citrus dressing rather than the expected ginger based.  The restaurant itself appeared clean and very tastefully decorated.  Due to the time of day, it seemed very quiet during our visit (we didn't see anyone else in our section.)  The food and service were good, but nothing was remarkable enough to make this a destination for a road trip passed a handful of other teriyaki places closer to home.  Review #2505

We used to live in Greenwood and go here often.  We always counted on this place for a really good quality dinner.  Now that we have moved, we only get back here a couple times each year.  The quality is still here.    My wife and I like going before 6 p.m. to take advantage of the "early bird" specials:  Slightly smaller portions or a small change to the menu, but really good food for a lower price.  My wife likes to order the Shrimp special which comes with fries and cole slaw.  She gets it every time, so I am pretty sure she is a big fan!  (She also likes to order this at all the Stone Creek locations since she says it's pretty consistent across the franchises.)  My favorite is the Blackened fish (Mahi Mahi from the regular menu, some other white fish for the early bird).  It comes with a cajun spiced dirty rice with black beans and avocado.  I really like this...just the right amount of heat to round out the flavor without becoming distracting.  The cool of the avocado is refreshing and keeps the heat from building too much.  They have recently remodeled and have made the place a lot more up to date.  I think the Greenwood location was one of the first restaurants in the Cunningham Group, definitely before the explosion of different spin-offs downtown and in other cities.  So, I have to admit I was a bit disappointed that even though they have a stand alone building, that this location still doesn't have outdoor dining like every other Stone Creek.  And they still don't have lunch hours, so we end up going to the Plainfield restaurant more often now.  I understand that the cost of adding both options might be a bit of a risk, but it reinforces the stereotype that the south side can't support good restaurants.  Sure, there are lots of folks who still clog the chain restaurants thinking that quantity is the primary source of a good rating.    But for those of us who appreciate quality ingredients and a pleasant dining experience, it would be nice to have more options than the handful of upscale restaurants that are here.  I will still come to enjoy my dinner, but it would be nice to enjoy a warm spring lunch or an outside beverage.  Review #257

My wife and I were on the southeast side of Indy and decided to stop by Beech Grove for lunch.  There is a really nice 3rd generation Italian restaurant right on Main Street and I am glad we stopped by!  We grabbed one of the free spaces in front of the building and stepped in.  There is a hostess desk that has a sign asking for customers to wait.  We were greeted almost immediately and escorted to a table in the dining room next to the bar.  The bar is divided from the dining area by a wall with arches and murals of Italy.  The bar is also a couple steps lower than the dining area.  The dining room is filled with mostly 4-top tables and covered with black tablecloths.  The room has a faux plaster over brick finish where the brick sporadically appears through the light plaster.  The east wall has a large mural as well.  Our server was friendly and did a good job of keeping the food coming out in a timely fashion.  No long waits here!  After our beverages were served, we received a complementary basket of tasty bread.  The bread had just a little bit of crunch on the edges, but was soft and warm inside.  The only negative is that the butter packets were served cold and unspreadable on the soft insides of the bread.  (Maybe some could be allowed to get to room temperature in time for lunch.)  My wife got the 1/2 sandwich/salad combo while I got the Ravioli alla Reggiana with a side garden salad.  The salads came out first and had predominantly ice berg lettuce as the base, but there was also some radicchio, and purple leaf lettuce, some thinly sliced red onion, diced tomato, and carrot matchsticks.  The dressing came on the side and we both had the house vinaigrette.  Very tangy flavor on the dressing which was complex and really perked up the flavor of the salad.  (They also sell it in jars for anyone wanting to buy it!)  My wife's sandwich came with ham, salami, provolone cheese, and was lightly toasted before serving.  It also came with lettuce and tomato and more of the house dressing for dipping.  She thought the toasted salami was fantastic since it melted the fat that can be distracting from the flavor.  The ham did get a little dry from the toasting, but when all the ingredients were combined, the taste was quite good.  I got the choice of stuffing for my ravioli as well as one of three sauces (beef stuffing and meat sauce for me.)  The lunch portion comes with three large ravioli topped with the sauce and when combined with the bread course and salad, was quite sufficient.  The flavor was good, but not with a lot of layers.  Basically, the first bite and the last were the same.    The only real negative comment my wife mentioned was that the restroom did not have a handrail in the handicap stall to assist standing.  If you've ever had lower body pains or surgery, you know how much those hand rails can make a difference in getting back on your feet.  She managed but made a point of pointing it out to me.  Otherwise, the meal was fine and enjoyable.  The noise level was moderate even with background music playing.  And the total time we were there would easily fit into a lunch hour.  Definitely a nice dining experience!  Review #1310

Cozy coffee shop with an assortment of drip coffee options, pastries, juices, and specialty drinks.  After street parking along 52nd, I walked past the patio entrance and in through a lobby (it keeps the cold out of the main sitting area.)  The order counter is towards the back with pastries and juices in the counter display.  Behind the narrow waiting area is the drip coffee station with multiple types/strengths of coffee available self-serve after paying.  The interior is broken into a cluster of small areas where visitors were either chatting or working/playing on their electronics.  There wasn't a real line due to the slightly crowded space, but I knew who was ahead of me and looked over the goodies while I waited.  I ended up ordering a drip coffee and a Raspberry Danish.  I was given my choice of a paper or ceramic cup for the coffee and my Danish was taken to the backroom for heating.  (I think they have an oven since I didn't hear any hum from a microwave and the Danish took a little longer than I anticipated, coming out crisp and flaky instead of chewy.)  My coffee selection was hot, but not scalding, so I was able to enjoy it right away with my Danish.  The space also has a downstairs that has a fire place, a children's play area under the stairs, and seating around the perimeter.  The only negative is that at the bottom of the stairs, as you reach the landing, there is a small (2 inch?) drop off to the floor that has lights that are identifiable from the basement, but I didn't notice coming down as I stepped into the room and nearly stumbled.  They could use a yellow strip to call more attention to it.  Be careful!  Friendly staff and quiet work space with light music in the background.  They ask that you bus your own dishes with cups being returned to a tray at the counter.  Review #3437

I have enjoyed smoothies from this locally owned smoothie franchise at their Carmel location and at a Yelp event, but this was my first visit to the new Fishers location.  Like the other, there is parking out front, an order counter, and tables to dine and/or wait for your order to be served.  The list of options (including calorie count) is overhead behind the counter.  After ordering, you pay and give them a name to identify the order.    I selected a Blueberry Bliss smoothie.  Note that they only have one size for their smoothies and they seem quite large to me.    I really enjoyed the fruit forward flavor.  Note that although they don't seem super cold, I did get a bit of brain freeze from drinking it too fast.  My only complaint is that there was some loud equipment running near the order counter, which when combined with the background music,  made hearing the staff's questions a bit difficult.  Review #3410

The Rustic Root is a combination Antique and Gift Shop as well as a tea room.  The main entrance leads into the shop where there are groupings of items including candles, gifts, and some smaller items, including packaged teas.  To the right of the entrance is a somewhat enclosed area called the Garden.  This area has a few small tables for additional seating of the tea room.  Behind the check out counter (which is centered in the shop), is a partition where some additional seating is lined up for customers of the tea room.  To the far right of the entrance is the actual tea room area which includes a dining area and a dessert counter area where additional displays of tea are for sale.  Normally, reservations are encouraged for dining (especially for one of the tea parties), but because I was by myself and was only interested in lunch, I was seated promptly in the area behind the counter partition.  The table was tastefully decorated.  The waitress was hustling since she had to serve people in a lot of different rooms which makes it difficult to keep an eye on everyone.  I could have ordered from the brunch menu, but decided to go for the 1/2 sandwich (turkey panini) and soup (potato) for my meal.  Both were quite good and reasonably priced around $11.  I also wanted to try the Dragonwell Green Tea which was listed on the menu under the 1-2 minute section.  The menu listed the steep times of each tea, so when the waitress dropped of the tea pot and poured the first cup of hot water over the tea bag, she started the timer.  The shop also provides a small tea pot shaped dish to rest the tea bag in between steeps.  Very well thought out and fine if you are dining by yourself, but note that the small tables for two could get really crowded surfaces if both parties order tea and a meal.    Overall, it was a nice shop with good food and service.  If you are a fan of tea rooms and are interested in browsing the shop, plan a stop here to give it a try.  Review #1234

Since I retired, I've spent a lot of time checking out public art, historic buildings with cool architecture, and visiting most areas of the city just to see what I've been missing.  So, I couldn't believe I took so long to visit Coat Check Coffee.  And, I wasn't even planning on it.  I was taking pictures of a new art installation on the west end of the Athenaeum.  So, imagine my delight when I stepped into this massive building (b. 1893) that is filled with beautiful woodwork throughout the entryway.  But, in case you were thinking this would be some stuffy, highbrow place, a vividly colorful mural is painted on the east wall of the stairwell and wraps around through the entry.  Once I got up the stairs to the main floor, the space was transformed into a modern and stylish meeting space with lots of guests plugged in to their computers in small groups sipping coffee and noshing on munchies.  It was a little confusing since there wasn't really a line for ordering...lots of folks just standing near the order counter.  Still, the server behind the counter called out to me and said she would be with me in a moment.  And she was.  That gave me time to look over the counters of food on display.  They don't have a lot of food to choose from, but I'll take quality over quantity any time!     I wanted something sweet, so I picked a Blueberry Cheesecake Macaron.  Wow!  Fresh and tasty.  I wanted something savory, so I picked a Ham and Cheese Croissant.  Fresh baked, warm and buttery.  Another Wow! And when it comes to coffee, I have simple tastes:  a cup of black coffee that isn't scalding hot and has a rich flavor.  Tinker Coffee took care of that and I could drink it as soon as I picked my spot to enjoy it.  No burned tongue to make the food (and coffee) become tasteless.  Everything from service to taste to environment was good and felt relaxed and inviting.  On the technical side, you hover near the counter and step up when you see an opening.  They take your name and call out to you when it is ready.  They didn't seem to have trays, so be aware you may have to juggle a bit if you order a lot.  Coffee is served in real mugs, not disposables.  That means, you need to bus your own space (a collection bin is near the place to get napkins on the main floor.)  And parking isn't free.  Hopefully, you can find a metered street spot close by.  They just celebrated their first anniversary in this space at the time of my review.  Don't wait for a reason to go...just go!  Review #589

Our daughter had recently purchased a table and chair set from Urban Styles and had a positive experience here, so my wife wanted to check out the store since she liked the style.  Although we didn't make any purchases, we were amazed at the unique and stylish pieces we saw here.  Whether it was furniture or accessories, the items were different from anywhere else.  The prices do tend to run on the expensive side, but there were sales going on to bring the prices down to a more affordable range.   When we entered, we were greeted and asked if we were looking for anything in particular, and then given his name if we had any questions.  We then browsed around the different spaces set up like rooms or collections for a good half hour.  Everything was really cool.  The only negative was that when my wife had some questions about one of the sets, she went to the guy who had greeted us after he had gotten off the phone.  But instead of coming over, he made another phone call.  After awhile, we gave up and left.  Lost sale.  waugh waugh!  Review #2048

I normally don't frequent chain restaurants from out of state, but after trying some of the food items offered by Taziki's at one of the recent Yelp Elite Events, I thought it worth making the trip to the northeast side of the city to try a full meal there.   As you can tell by my rating, my expectations were exceeded!  Adding to my pleasure was the fact I had a free gift ticket that allowed me to have the special of the day which includes a free side M-Th.  What did I have to lose?  Note that this restaurant is on the south side of 82nd where the street is divided by a median.  So if you are east bound, it's not a problem.  If you are west bound, you will need to turn mid-block where there is a break in the median and then head passed a couple stores to the entrance of the restaurant.  Inside, there is a large dining area with the food prep/order counter on the right.  You walk passed the food prep to where a sign "order here" hangs.  There they have menus to look at to help you decide whether you want a bowl or a sandwich.  After ordering and paying, they give you a number to put on your table.  A beverage bar is not visible from the order counter, but it is just around a corner that is behind you (another sign hangs on the corner for beverages.)  Utensils and napkins are on each table.  After a short wait, the cashier brought out my tray with the Monday special, a Chicken Portobello Sandwich with my choice of a Tomato-Cucumber salad and chips.  I started with the salad and it was delicious (I highly recommend it!)  The veggies are sprinkled with Feta cheese and seasoned with a vinaigrette. (Similar in taste to a burrata.)  The sandwich was also very tasty with a grilled chicken breast served on a kaiser roll with Swiss Cheese, red bell pepper slices, sliced portobellos, and a mushroom butter.  Really good, though the sliced mushrooms tended to fall out sometimes.  The only negative was that there was a lot of "juice" on the paper lining the tray.  It wasn't greasy, just wet which made my fingers need to use the napkin more than expected.    You don't even need to bus your own table here.  They do that for you.  Someone even stopped by to make sure I was enjoying my meal.  Although not full service, I thought the staff did a fine job.  Overall, I would recommend this place if you are interested in trying a tasty Mediterranean meal while in Castleton.    Review #2680

The service and selection of healthy items for your dogs is top notch.  I walked in after finding a free public lot a half block away and was surprised by how many products I had never seen before.  There are treats and chewies galore.  They also carry dental treats as well as bags and cans of quality food items.  There is a table near the front of the store that is filled with what I would consider the "freak show" of chewies for your dogs like necks and heads, and other body parts.  Nice that they aren't wasted, but a little gristly to think about. :)  Of course, there are some pet supplies, but this place focuses on the treats and food items.  There is even a table of baked goods made in Greenfield specifically for dogs. You find those by the check out counter at the back of the store.  The man working during my visit was friendly and asked about the type of pets I had so that he could make suggestions appropriate to their sizes.  I ended up getting some meaty treats: Duck tenders and Chicken Apple sausage.  My dogs loved them!  Be aware that these are not mass produced pet industry items, so prices are going to be higher due to the lack of scale for the producers.  So, be judicious on how many treats you give out unless you have unlimited funds.    Friendly and helpful service and a wide selection of items to treat your dogs.  Review #2881

If you've been to any other Pier 1, then you will be familiar with the types of items you'll find here.  They have a candles section, an art/wall decor area towards the back, lots of stuff for you kitchen and dining room decor as well.  They also carry a limited amount of seating/furniture scattered throughout, but mainly the middle section of the store.  The checkout counter in this one is set right in the middle so if you have questions, you don't have to waste time searching for someone to answer.  They maintain a nice balance between seasonal and everyday time items as well.  Although we didn't make a purchase on this visit, the store carries a variety of quality items that would warrant a return visit when in the area.  Parking is shared with other shops in the Willow Lakes plaza.  It fills up fast on the weekends.  Review #3321

I stopped in for lunch while my tire was being repaired at a nearby business.  I immediately noticed that the handicapped parking area now has a ramp up to the sidewalk!  Thank you to the business for getting this taken care of!  Inside, the setting was rather dark, but still light enough to read the menus.  I was quickly seated and brought my utensils and had my beverage order procured.  Since it was around 1 p.m., I asked if I could order from the full menu or had to go with the lunch menu.  I was told I could order from either menu, so I skipped the lunch combo.  Instead, I decided to go with 3 servings of Nigiri Salmon (6 pcs total) and a side of seaweed salad.  This being my first time ordering a seaweed salad here, I was hoping that it would be as good or at least close to the seaweed I had at Union 50 a few weeks earlier.  I was not disappointed!  There was a mounded salad of shredded seaweed over iceberg lettuce pieces.  Over the salad were sesame seeds that gave a savory flavor to the dish.    The nigiri salmon, while fresh, seemed to lack the superb taste I remembered.  Still, the salmon was good when eaten with the rice.  The ginger on the side was perfect as a palate cleanser between pieces.    Overall, the service was prompt and efficient.  I will continue to return here for my sushi fix if they continue at this level.  Rev # 13

I stopped in for lunch and Wow! What a great meal! Twenty Tap recently reopened and they must have been fine tuning their service and food prep the whole time they were going through the remodeling.  I had never been here before, but lured by the Yelp Top 50 designation (2017), I thought it worth the trip from the southwest of Indy to drive here.  First, know that there is no parking lot, so you need to find a spot on the street.  Mine was a couple blocks away.  There is a small front patio area (covered) for outdoor dining, but I wanted to see the inside and waited for the staff to find a table for me.  Service was prompt throughout my meal.  Water brought out, extra napkins and a bottle of ketchup delivered without asking, and quick turnaround on getting my bill at the end.  The wait on the food and drink were short too.  Like I said, good all around!  I started with a draft local (Bloomington) and got the full pint for $5.  That is less than I am used to for craft beer, so I counted that a win.  (The beer was cold and tasty too!)  I ordered the Short Rib Grilled Cheese sandwich with a side of seasoned fries.  YUM!  The sandwich, served on Texas toast, was one of the best I've had all year! The short rib meat was juicy and when paired with the smoked gouda and Havarti cheese, made a winning combo.  The cheese was completely melted and gooey, so it held most of the ingredients together (although a bit of meat did drop a couple times.)  There was also a cherry bourbon glaze on the meat and a jalapeno marmalade along with the carmelized onion and arugula.  What surprised me was how sweet tasting the sandwich was.  The marmalade had just a hint of pepper flavor, not any detectable spiciness.   And the fries were so good!  I couldn't really tell what seasoning they used, but they reminded me of fries I've had that were cooked in Duck fat.  Almost buttery tasting while being crunchy crisp on the outside.  Nearly perfect fries!  Overall, a really positive first visit to this place.  Can't wait to return to try one of their house burgers!  Review #381

What a nice addition to the Greenwood area restaurants.  Conveniently located near the Greenwood/County Line Exit of I-65, the restaurant had a nice makeover from the previous tenant.  There is still the same ample parking and a spacious patio.  But now, there is a solid row of televisions stacked 2 high all the way around the bar/large dining room.  There is a stage in the North East corner of the room as well.  Seating is mainly high table 4-tops in the bar room.  After checking in at the hostess desk, we were able to seat ourselves for lunch and grabbed one of the tables.  Service was great throughout.  They have a nice line of craft beers available, both local and national.  I was able to get a sample before choosing Metazoa's milk stout to go with my Black Jack Burger.  The burger was cooked to temp (I like a nice char on mine, so medium well on a thick burger.)  It came with cajun spice, bacon, pepperjack cheese, and tomato, lettuce, onion, and pickle on the side.  Excellent choice!  Note that this is a BMB (Big Mouth Burger that is hard to eat without a bit of scrunching).  My wife ordered the breaded tenderloin with a side of orange slices.  Although the meat was thick, tender, and cooked properly, the breading was less than expected.  It reminded her (and I agreed on what I tried) of a pre-breaded tenderloin that was thawed just before cooking.  Just didn't do much to wow her.  The portion didn't appear as large, but because it was so thick, it was really filling.  We really like the look of the place, though the music was a bit loud for lunch time dining.  Fortunately, the televisions are on mute to keep from adding to the din.  Although my wife misses the fire cracker shrimp of the previous business, I can see coming back to find a new favorite.  Review #2812

When I go to a deli, I go for the food.  Sure, if they have great customer service that can add a fifth star to a review.  Convenient parking behind the shop with access through the back of the shop into the deli is great too!  Oh, and a variety of sides that if you are heading home, you can whip into something a little more than just chips.  That's good too!  So my wife and I decided to stop by Main Street in Carmel and managed to get there before closing at 5 p.m.  We were greeted into Joe's Butcher Shop/Joe's Next Door.  The east end of the shop is lined with butcher shop selections.  In the middle of the shop are rows of unique items to enhance your home cooking flavors.  And on the west side of the shop is the deli where you can order some great hot and cold sandwiches.  Going around 4:30, there was no line and my wife and I selected the Roast Beef and Cheddar  while I went with the highly recommended House BLT.  Although we had the sandwiches sliced in half for easier sharing, I think we both preferred the BLT because it was on a completely different flavor level from anywhere else.  The BLT is comparatively thin to the other sandwiches served at Joe's.  The bacon is sliced just a bit thicker than most commercial brands and undergoes a marvelous transformation during their house curing process.  While retaining a bacon flavor, there is a sweetness that was unexpected in the sandwich that I cannot attribute to any of the other listed ingredients.  The sandwich comes with a sweet butter lettuce, a generous slice of heirloom local tomatoes, an entire sliced avocado, roasted garlic aioli and served on toasted sourdough.  This is a two fisted sandwich because the avocado makes it hard to hold together with one hand.  Absolutely delicious!    The roast beef was piled onto the stirato roll and topped with aged white cheddar, house scallion / horseradish cream, and romaine lettuce.  I thought the sandwich well balanced, while my wife thought the beef just a little bit dry.  The flavor was really good in both our opinions.  We only waited a few minutes for our sandwiches and then went to the register near the front of the shop to check out.  There are a few small tables out front of the shop where you can eat and people watch when the weather is suitable.  Unfortunately, there isn't any room inside for seating.  Great food at reasonable prices for high quality ingredients.    Review #310

Somethings were good, somethings not so much.  My wife and I stopped in just after noon on Sunday and although we generally liked the food, there were several glitches on the service side that left us bewildered.  When we checked in at the front desk and asked for a table for two, the host took off faster than we kept up and he went toward the kitchen and started a conversation, leaving us wondering what was going on.  He realized that he had forgotten to seat us and apologized.  The room we were seated in was quite full and was divided between two waitresses.  Unfortunately, it wasn't divided equally.  Our waitress was courteous, but she was hustling much more than the other waitress.  So, we had waits between ordering a beverage and receiving it.  Long waits on water refills.  We noticed that she seemed focused on one task at a time and forgot things like taking used dishes away, asking about more chips and salsa until we had already received our entrees, and when I asked if the tacos came with cheese, she said "no".  I asked if I could get some and she said "no" again, which I found odd that a Mexican restaurant doesn't offer cheese with tacos.  I was puzzled.  The free chips and salsa were pretty good.  The chips were crisp and the salsa had a little hint of heat that accumulated, but not too strong for me.  My wife said the Taco Salad with chicken was really good.  The chicken wasn't dry and was generously portioned.    Despite not having any cheese for my tacos (nor sour cream), the tacos were pretty good.  Some of the beef was tough (like gristle), but most was okay, though not really tender.  Good flavors though.  It was just a drawn out meal and though the flavors were good, just not a place I would go out of my way to go to again.  Review #1843

This beautiful park is more for adults than children.  There is no playground, just a large lawn with a paved loop that runs into the woods that buffer the space from the river.  There is a large hill that kids could run up and down or sled if the weather provides snow, but otherwise, it is a calm and peaceful place.  There is a large shelter on the hill and several extra picnic tables for looking over the grounds.  The site is named for the West-Harris House or "Ambassador" house which is on the list of Historic places.  It is used for receptions and events and has a beautifully landscaped garden and a paved flat area to the side that tents could be set up during warmer months.  The history of the place dates back to the original log cabin in the 1820's of the West Family.  Although the original house is gone, the site remained valuable.  When the home of former Ambassador Addison Clay Harris (served under McKinley as ambassador to Austria-Hungary) was being threatened with demolition, the town bought the house and moved it to this current location in 1996.  A second stone house was moved the following year but I haven't found any information about it.  Although the house is set up for rentals, there are separate parking lots for guests of the house and for the park, so park visitation should not be limited by events.  Note:  Access to the park is restricted in 2018 due to reconstruction of 106th Street which is the road that the park's entrance is located on.  Although the entrance to the park remains open, there are numerous detour signs that may discourage visitors from thinking you can't get through.  You can from the north or south on Eller Road by driving around the barriers which state open to local traffic only.  Review #800

I met some friends for lunch on a Wednesday back in March.  It was our first time dining at Nada.  The atmosphere of the restaurant was warm and inviting.  The cantina at the entrance was brightly colorful and looked like a great place to sample the tequila collection.  But, since most of our party had to return to work, we sat farther back in the dining area and began sampling the numerous items on the menu.  First, let me say that the salsa and chips are delicious.  Yes, you have to pay for these (unlike some Mexican food chains that give them away), but the quality and freshness/crispness were superior to any other I have tried.  We shared the mild and medium heat options, the latter have a pesto base.  Excellent choices.  I ordered the crispy pork belly taco (I added a fried egg), the pickled cucumber salad, and the  Senor Mu Shu braised pork taco (Asian cuisine influenced). The tacos were double tortillas so that the ingredients did not slip through.  Although my choices were okay, others in my group raved about how good their choices were, so I will need to be a little adventuresome and try more mainstream choices upon my next visit.  Also note that if you add the friend egg to your taco, it will run so you may choose to use knife and fork instead of picking it up to eat.  Between the five us, we sampled ten different options, including soups and salads.  Everyone enjoyed the experience and planned on returning.  Note:  There are numerous fun items hidden throughout the restaurant.  Be sure to look around the decor to catch all the fun.  Review #52

I stopped in to check out this combination Hallmark/Pandora/gift shop after having enjoyed the one in Vincennes.  Like that other shop, this had a wide variety of items including the cards and women's wear/items, toys, puzzles, and lots of small items that would make for pleasant gifts.    Like all Hallmarks, there were still some marked down Christmas items hoping for someone to pick them up.  The only difference between this store and the one in Vincennes version is that the other greeted me as soon as I entered and made me feel welcome.  Here, the woman was busy changing out inventory and didn't acknowledge any of the customers browsing in the shop.  Review #3632

Now that the construction on College is out of the way, I finally made it to Captain Sushi.  I found paid street parking along the canal and strolled the short distance to this restaurant.   The left side is the main dining room where there is a sushi bar with chairs at the counter as well as the Japanese benches and low seating in the dining area.  The right side is a bar area that was closed during lunch, but has very cool anime characters painted on the wall.  I was greeted upon entry and grabbed a spot at the counter.  After browsing the menu, I went with the Japanese Spring Rolls, the Fresh Salmon Nigiri, and an Eel Avocado Roll.     I was surprised at how quickly the food was ready.  The spring rolls were light and crisp with a flaky layering (like phyllo dough).  The insides were filled with pork and veggies.  There was also a sweet dipping sauce and julienned carrots.  Really good and highly recommended.  Note that the insides are still pretty hot when they arrive, so be sure to avoid biting in too soon.  The salmon and sushi roll arrived at the same time.  The salmon, served over a ball of sticky rice, was excellent!  Very fresh tasting and brightly colored.  I didn't use any of the soy sauce, but did try a bit of the sliced lemon. Wow!  Really good. (I was surprised that they had been frozen with such a fresh taste.)  The eel-avocado roll was 8 pieces and came with an eel sauce mini bowl for dipping.  The roll was very good, but the eel sauce was a bit more savory than sweet with a taste that leaned towards tasting like molasses than the sweet/salty/vinegar taste I am used to.  Okay, but not my favorite.  The server was very personable and welcoming.  The service was quick.  The price was very reasonable.  I would gladly recommend stopping here if you are in the mood for sushi!  Review #2867

After catching a movie at the local Showtime Cinema, I was hungry and decided to stop in at Marco's Pizza.  They have a shared building/parking lot with Family Video, so it was easy to find and park.  The lobby is small with a few chairs for waiting and some along the window where you could eat if you wanted to, but this is more of a "to go" restaurant than "dine in".    I saw the menu listed above the order counter and went with a medium Deluxe pizza (8 pie slices).  The woman who took the order was efficient and let me know that it would take around 10 minutes.    The pizza was ready after the short wait and was quite tasty.  The dough was soft and thicker around the rim while the center was a little flopsy.  The cheese was plentiful and stretchy.  The crust had a nice flavor on its own that I enjoyed too.  The ingredients seemed to be fairly well spaced though not the most generously loaded that I've had.    The place also sells subs, salads, and sides.  It appears they also have discounts with the video store next door if you spend a certain level on pizza.  Review #3638

My wife and I stopped by to check out this fabric store near 96th and Hague.  Since we live on the southwest side, it was our first time discovering this place.  My wife is a very skilled quilter, but doesn't consider herself much of a seamstress.  She can fix things, but rarely creates her own clothing from patterns.    Well, the shop has the two types of fabrics separated!  Note that this isn't a big box store, so the space is somewhat small.  (There is a workshop area in the back that I've read they use for classes.)  What is appealing is that you don't see the same stuff you find at the big box places.  There were lots of high quality bolts (my wife found one that was $85 per yard!) that a skilled seamstress/tailor could have used to make a suit.  But because the supply is limited, my wife didn't find anything on this occasion to purchase.  We also did not see any "sale" items as mentioned in another review.  The shop also has some yarn, thread, buttons, patterns, and sewing related items for sale too.  If you are looking for high quality fabrics to complete your project, check out this shop before jumping in.  Review #3330

I had a nice late lunch (around 1 pm) where I was able to find free street parking and no wait to be seated inside the restaurant.  On my previous trip, I had a bit of a walk and wait even early in the lunch hour.  This colorful and mostly quiet atmosphere made for a pleasant setting to enjoy my meal.    I was quickly greeted by my waitress and because I knew what I wanted before arriving, was able to put in my order from the lunch specials at the same time as my beverage order.  That really helped my total time (about 20 minutes start to finish!)  I started with a pot of Ginger Tea. (Complementary water was brought as well!)  The tea had a wonderful flavor with a bold ginger flavor with a bit of sweetness.  I was surprised their seemed to be a bit of spicy heat on the swallow.  It was not a bad sensation, just unexpected from tea.  Good taste though!  Because I ordered one of the lunch specials, I got a cup of Thom Sum soup and a crispy veggie spring roll.  The soup was quite spicy and definitely built upon the tingling at the back of my throat from the tea.  Lots of flavor too!  The spring roll was crispy on the outside while allowing the julienned veggies to retain their crispness.  No dipping sauce here for the roll.  I ordered my standard Pad Seuw for Thai restaurants I haven't been to in awhile.  (It helps me compare restaurants and is a dish I have found that I liked on most visits.)  This serving was presented on an oval dish about 11 x 7 in.  The presentation wasn't the most colorful I have seen (lots of places add some carrot or more broccoli crowns.)  However, the veggies were al dente and had an enjoyable crunch without being too tough.  The flavor of the sauce was quite good, but the chicken (I believe all sliced white meat) was just a tad overcooked.  Good flavor overall.  Another solid restaurant option for the Fountain Square/Fletcher Place area!  Review #406

While other businesses seem to struggle through the challenges of the pandemic (including supply, social distancing, and customer service), I was thrilled with my visit to McCammon's Irish Market in Brownsburg.  My wife and I recently added some flower beds to our home and were looking for some specific plants which we could have ordered online, but would not have received until fall which would have given them less time to establish before the colds of winter.  When we arrived at this spacious garden center, we were greeted throughout the visit by employees who made sure that we found what we were looking for, helped us through their checkout process, and even helped transfer our purchases to our vehicle.  Such a positive and easy process that it was the best of the garden centers that we have been to during these trying times.  My wife was able to choose from several varieties/colors of the flowers she was looking for.  In addition to the plants, they also carry some of the hardware related to gardening and some other summer items (like grilling) that make for a convenient stop.    In a time when every business seems just a little different when it comes to how they handle the pandemic, I can assure you that it makes a big difference when someone is able to walk you through their process and actually serve the customer.  It was like a walk in the park!  Review #3764

When I look for a movie theater, I look: at what's showing; are the times convenient; and does it have prices that are reasonable.  Well, I was looking for showings of some independent films and found them at this Regal.  Located near Greenwood Park Mall, I found one playing on a Tuesday around lunch time, and on the following Sunday in the morning.  I was pleasantly surprised that I got great prices both times (under $7).  When I went, the lines were really small and the service was prompt.    The theaters have the "reserve" seating feature and the fully reclining seats available.  So, I was able to get great seats at both movies and could adjust my position easily during the films.    The theaters were clean and the restrooms were well lit and had been maintained.  Based upon my positive experiences, I have added this location into my "go to" options to see first run films.  Review #475

At 108 acres, this is one of Indy's largest parks.  There is a lot of room to spread out and to hike.  There are hills for those who like a challenge (or sledding when there is snow!)  There is a community center, five shelters, several playgrounds, an aquatic center, and ball fields and tennis courts.  The park was built in 1898, so there are lots of mature trees that provide shade for the benches/picnic tables around the park.  There is also a lot of open space for playing frisbee as well!  At the time of my review, a large construction project is taking place on the western end of the park to fix the rain runoff/sewage problem that contaminates Pogue's Run whenever more than a quarter inch of rain falls.  The construction is scheduled to go through the fall of 2019 which will then include restoration of the lawn and planting of new trees (and re-establishing the full disc golf course).  But the park is large, so there is still plenty to see and do and the construction doesn't cause any traffic problems for visitors.  Note:  While in the area, there is a lot of public art across the south parkway from the park.  If you don't mind the walk, take a stroll to check it out!  Review #626

What a fun way to kick off the Christmas season.  Having some German ancestry and with my wife who has LOTS of German ancestry, we both enjoyed seeing the shops with items that we both had in our homes as children.  There was a skating rink (we thought it best not to end up in the Emergency Room due to our age and lack of balance!) and polka music...and I didn't even mind it!  The music fit the setting though I would have preferred not having a speaker located right by the place to order raclette cheese sandwiches.  The volume made it difficult to hear names called out since there was only one guy making the sandwiches during the dinner rush, so people were clustered without any order to hear their name called.  At least a guy finally showed up after awhile, but count on a wait if you order one.  There was also mulled wine, a wurst haus to get a variety of sausages, and places for coffee and hot chocolate.    I liked that they had heaters both high (to warm your ears) and low (to warm your...well, you know!)  The planners did add some mats to help keep visitors from getting all muddy, but for those who may be mobility challenged, be aware you can stumble on these as well because the edges don't stay level.  There are also numerous places where there are a couple inches in drop offs or ridges which are easy to miss if you are staring at all the lights and things on display.  Not sure why some of the ridges were built into the plaza, but they are.  So, be aware as you move about.  Overall, it was fun and we enjoyed visiting before our concert at the Palladium.  Be aware that while free to visit, the items run on the pricey side.    Parking is free along the street and in the Center Garage to the south of the Tarkington Theater.  Review #1828

I enjoyed my lunch at Sakura.  The parking lot was nearly full, but I grabbed one of the last spots and I was still able to find comfortable seating in the dining room.  Although there were a number of lunch specials, I ordered two rolls for a very reasonable price.    My first option was the Sea Eel Roll (4 pc).  This large (thickness) roll was wrapped in seaweed with the rice and eel inside.  Though it was large, it wasn't too big to challenge my "bite sized" limits.  The flavor was fine.  I didn't see any list of ingredients for the rolls, so I assume it was eel sauce adding the dark brown color to the top of each piece.  I am used to a bit more sweetness/acidity in eel sauce from other restaurants, so this was a bit of a surprise.  Still good, just not as layered in taste.  The shrimp tempura roll (6 pc) was more tightly wrapped with the rice on the outside.  Two of the six pieces had ornamental shrimp tails protruding from the top of the pieces.  I ate those two with my fingers.  If you are a stickler for using chopsticks to pick up sushi, then you would have trouble with these shelled pieces.  The flavor was very good with a bit of wasabi and soy sauce.  Overall, there was a quiet atmosphere in the restaurant despite being nearly full.  The lighting was on the dark side and the decor looked a little dated, but seemed to be true to an authentic Japanese restaurant.   Review #416

Although I don't know much about gaming, I stopped by this shop across Meridian from Circle Centre Mall to see what kind of games they had.  The shop is long and narrow with the displays of games up front by the check out counter and entrance.  The back half of the store is set up with lots of tables for groups of players to be able to enjoy their purchases.  I can't tell you if the arrangement of the tables is conducive to playing all types of games or not, but I'm sure the staff can help meet your needs.  I was also glad to see that they did carry some more "old fashioned" board games that are self contained and suitable for most levels of family to play.  They also had puzzles and a selection of Monopoly games that had unique themes I hadn't seen before.  Oh, and don't let the downtown location make you think you are paying too much.  I checked some pricing compared to that certain online giant that delivers to your home and this place was within 10% of the online giant.  I like supporting local businesses, so when I can, I buy from actual stores and save the online for things that I just can't find elsewhere.  Overall, I came away with a favorable impression of this store.  Review #1968

I stopped in for lunch and was pleasantly surprised.  The food and service were good throughout the time I was there.  After parking in the shared lot, I went to the hostess stand to the right as I entered and then was seated at one of the colorfully relieved booths.  The colors are vibrant and almost demand that you check them out.  I quickly placed my order and while I waited, began digging into the complementary chips and salsa.  The bowl of chips was huge (way too much for eating by myself if I wanted to save room for lunch.)  The salsa was tasty and had a hint of heat that became more noticeable as I continued, but never too spicy for me.  Before long, my entree of Tacos de Asada with rice and beans arrived.  The three double shelled tacos (soft corn shells about 5 to 6 inches across) arrived with diced bits of beef, onion, and topped with cilantro.  There didn't appear to be any taco sauce of any kind on them, but the waitress did bring out a green sauce in a bottle.  It was okay, but the sauce didn't add a lot of depth to the flavor.  They tacos were definitely savory, but a little dry and especially filling with the double tortillas.  I am not a hot sauce guy, but they do have a couple brands on the table if that is something you like.  The beans were thinned so that they didn't clump like some places and they were topped with some melted cheese.  The rice was pretty good too and had small vegetables chopped into it for additional color and flavor.    I decided to not over stuff myself and decided to get a to go box.  The waitress brought the check at the same time and I was quickly processed and on my way.  Seemed like a nice place to try out if you are in the area.  Review #2179

Sometimes, you have to check a place out for yourself.  Generally, I can count on the Yelp ratings for a good feel for how I will like a business or event.  But in this case, I get the feeling I don't fit into the target audience of this festival.  The festival itself seemed to be loaded with businesses, both inside the BASH Event space, and outside under the tents.  Check in was easy and reasonably priced($7 in advance, $10 at the gate).  I was also to find a free parking space after just a bit of driving and a short walk.  It's just that even though I like shopping local and supporting small businesses, I didn't find much that I wanted to spend money on.  I already know where to get Goose the Market or Newfangled Creations when I'm in the mood.  And though there were dozens of women making their own "crowns" from plants and flowers at the numerous tables provided by the Tipsy Gardener, I couldn't see myself wearing a crown around the festival, let alone once I left.  There were also lots of places carrying women's products/cosmetics, jewelry, pottery, hand made cards, sunglasses, etc.  The problem is that if I wanted to get something as a gift and the person wanted to return it, where would they go?  So, even gift buying was not as appealing as it could be.  Frankly, I thought the festival would be more local than it was.  I thought it would have more artisan foods than it did.  I thought there would be more than one food truck to choose from.    Although I am glad I was able to go via Yelp, I can't say I would return.  I think it best left to those who enjoy shopping in crowds for themselves.  Review #2657

They're Baaack!  After a brief time without an active storefront for customers to make purchases, Hoosier Brewing has now set up on Madison Avenue in downtown Greenwood, across the street from Planetary Brewing.  The beer is better than ever!  So, there isn't any onsite or street parking, but a free public lot is available a half block to the south (southwest corner of the intersection of Madison and Main).  Another city lot is just a short stroll to the north as well.  At the time of my visit, the brewery still didn't have their sign installed out front, but that is coming soon!  The city has been fixing up some of the storefronts in the area, so the brewery benefited from that upgrade.  Inside, the brewery tanks are located to your left, the order counter/bar and tables are in front of you, and the axe throwing "Tap & Axe" is to your right.  I decided to go with a flight which comes with three 5-ounce beers priced at $2 per mini beer.  They have about a dozen brews on tap, including their first sour, and they have kombucha for those who aren't beer drinkers.  Note that they have a three way liquor license, so your friends who like basic cocktails can enjoy those here as well.  I tried the Harvest wheat (5% ABV), the Choco-Bomb Stout (7.3%), and the Hoosier Hospitality American IPA (7%).  I really enjoyed all three!  The latter two went really well with the food I ordered as well.  And speaking of food, it tasted really good.  It is pricey, but the quality was enjoyable.   When you place your order, they ask for your phone number and text you when to pick it up. The pizza, sold by the slice, was just a basic pepperoni (a little greasy on top, but a quick dab of a napkin took care of that!)  The crust was on the crisp side, but still could be folded.  Note that it runs $5 slice, so keep that in mind.  The wings (half wings) come in 4 or 8 packs with your choice of four different flavorings:  dry rub, barbecue, teryaki, and sweet chili.  Sorry if you are a hot wings fan, they don't offer those (Not sure if you can get some hot sauce or not.)  I ordered a 4-pack of teryaki and another of sweet chili wings.  Each pack was $7, so again it isn't the cheapest meal around.  The wings were cooked perfectly:  just a hint of blackening to bring out the flavor and crispness while staying steaming hot and juicy inside.  Some of the best wings I've had!  They also serve breadsticks.  No vegan or vegetarian offerings as of now, but who knows.  It's bar food, but really tasty!  There are plans for an outdoor patio in the spring.  They are also expecting their copper still soon to start working on their own bourbon.  Stay tuned!  And then there is Tap & Axe which has six stations available.  Be aware that if you want to throw axes, you can't have had more than two drinks if you want to throw.  So, throw first, then drink!  They charge $30/person per hour and require you to go through a brief tutorial so that you are not risking harm to yourself or anyone else.    I interacted with three of the guys who work there and each one was friendly, was excited to talk about the brewery/axe throwing, and made sure I was enjoying my food and beer.  With this kind of devotion to their products and customers, they are bound to be a hit.    Note that they are open for lunch on Fridays and weekends.  Future plans may allow for private parties in the brewing area, but that is still in the works.  Welcome to Greenwood guys!  I look forward to returning soon!  Review #3590

I stopped in to see the newest mural by Jules "MuckRock" Muck that was added to the interior of the shop in Aug 2019.  The mural "Bowie Kitty" shows a large white cat with the Ziggy Stardust makeup made popular by David Bowie.  Very cool with a sense of whimsy.  The shop also has a lot of vinyl available by alphabet within genre, pretty standard set up.  Unfortunately, like many vinyl shops, finding what you are looking for is hit or miss.  I found a lot of artists I like, but not the particular albums.  There is also a coffee shop in the back on the left.  I must have had bad timing because nobody was there to pour coffee or ask questions about the availability of albums.  Most of the people seated there were zoned in on their computers and I walked through the entire store without being acknowledged by anyone.  A guy did come in as I was about to leave and made a comment about the gathering of homeless individuals hanging out front (they moved on though).  Not sure if the guy who came in worked there or not.  So, if you like browsing without being interrupted, maybe this is a place to check out.  Hopefully, if you find something, you can have as good of luck finding someone to pay for it.  Review #2863

My wife and I have dined here several times, usually during the Devour North promotional event.  Each time we have received excellent service and delicious food.  During the most recent visit, we brought a friend for the first time.  We each ordered a different entree from the menu and everyone enjoyed their meal.  I ordered a house salad and was able to substitute blue cheese for the goat cheese that was listed on the menu.  When you know that something just doesn't suit your palate, it is really appreciated when you can make a change to something like a salad.  I then tried the Teryaki Salmon with shiitake sticky rice and soy butter sauce.  This was delicious.  The julienned mixed veggies on top added a nice crunch and taste.  I would definitely order this again.  Finally, I finished off with a refreshing raspberry sorbet.  Not only was it tasty, but it served as a nice palate cleanser to finish off the evening.  Note:  If the weather is nice, there is open air seating in the bar area that can be very pleasant.  Review #54

If you are like me and like your beef cooked at a high heat to add a bit of a charred flavor on the outside while staying moist and tender on the inside, then this is the place to try!  I stopped by in the late afternoon to grab a few beef tacos to go.  They give you the option of corn or flour shells (flour for me thanks!) and once the meat is ready in the kitchen, the server brings them out to the area behind the counter and he dresses them with the toppings that you want.  I was surprised at how many options they had and picked about a half dozen for my tacos.  I also had a choice of sauces (a spicy red or a cool green) which he offered to put in a small cup to make the tacos transport better without making them soggy.  And though the tacos became jostled during the trip home, it did nothing to affect the flavor which was fantastic!  Even with all the toppings, the beef flavor was prominent and the other flavors complemented the taste instead of masking it.  The tortillas were also fresh and light though sturdy enough for a single layer to hold the ingredients.  Great first visit and since this place isn't too out of the way from the road to my grandkids' house, I may be seeing this place again soon!  Review #1215

Although the business has had mixed reviews, I decided to stop by for lunch to see for myself.  I was surprised at how packed the place was with a definitely older crowd.  After finding a spot in their private lot, I entered and was greeted.  When I let them know I was dining by myself, the hostess mentioned they had open seats in the bar area with no waiting, so I followed her to one of the tables next to the bar.  I wasn't sure if I would be served by one of the waitresses in that room or not.  A couple minutes went by and since nobody stopped by, I grabbed a menu off the bar and at least figured out what I wanted to eat.  After a few more minutes, I realized that the bartender, who was swamped with customers sitting there, finally noticed me and before long, I was back on track.  I ordered a Reuben sandwich with a side of potato salad.  Both were good.  The portions were okay (I've had Reubens piled high with kraut and corned beef elsewhere).  Although not loaded, the sandwich seemed a nice size for lunch.  The atmosphere has a mixed theme of celebrating veterans in one area, and nostalgic memorabilia in others.    Although it doesn't have the feel of most upscale steakhouses I've been to, I think this is a place you can get a decent meal.  Review #3565

I was on the go and didn't want to order a full pizza, so I decided to get an Italian Beef sandwich.  It comes with your choice of dry, dipped, or wet (wet for me).  You can also get hot or sweet peppers on your order.  The sandwich is about 8" long and comes with chips & additional dipping sauce if you want it, so it is a whole lotta food for the price.  The wait time was less than ten minutes from the time I ordered.  The sandwich was double wrapped so it stayed hot the 20 minute drive home and didn't leak all over despite being wet.  They have their own parking area and a small outdoor patio with umbrellas on the tables in season.  Note that if you are approaching from the north, do NOT pull into the driveway off SR135 on the north side of the restaurant.  It is for the buildings next to the restaurant and is blocked to through traffic.  So pull into the south side of the restaurant that is shared with that large chain burger place.  I will say that the beef was still hot and had nice flavor on its own.  However, the dipping sauce/wet sauce had a bit of spicy heat to it.  Most places, I don't notice that.  Nothing wrong with having a bit of heat, just be aware of that if you are sensitive to spiciness.  Review #3160

I went in thinking this may be another antique store (per Yelp listing), but it is really more of a salvage/restoration piece store.  After street parking, I entered and found the place to be filled from floor to ceiling with all kinds of salvaged goods.  The aisles are narrow and because the stacks go so high, it was a bit dark and gloomy wandering through.    The people who worked here were friendly and offered to help, but I was browsing since I had been by here numerous times and decided to stop in when they were open for Small Business Saturday.  They do have lots of hard to find pieces.  Maybe you need some unusual thickness wood to match a damaged door frame.  Maybe it's a column to add support or replace what you had.  Door knobs and other accessories of architectural / functional nature are also spread throughout.    So, if you are looking for salvage items, you will probably lean towards a higher rating.  But as the owner of a relatively new home, there wasn't a lot here to hold my interest.  Note that they do have a large space outside that I believe you can find yard items as well.  Review #3367

Even though I stopped in about ten minutes before they closed, I was greeted and welcomed to this shop at 25th and Central.  I was surprised how full the parking lot was, but did manage to find one.  The entrance is on the south side of the north wing of the building.  Inside, there is a surprisingly large dining area with the order counter on your left.  Although they offer a wide variety of coffee based drinks, I noticed they also had a nice selection of chilled beverages and hot teas as well.  On the counter was a display of some tasty baked goods that were tempting too.  I picked up a cranberry pecan oatmeal bar to go along with my black coffee.    I got everything to go so I can't say how good the wifi is or how comfy the chairs are, but I can say that the coffee was good and ready to drink which was great since the baked bar I had was thick, dense, and went really well with the coffee.  The bar had just enough crunch from the pecans to pair well with the chewy oatmeal and cranberries inside.  Very friendly woman behind the counter didn't rush me and welcomed me to return again when I could stay longer.  Review #3757

On the north end of Mass Ave (before reaching the interstate), you might miss this small shop filled with goodies for your dogs (and cats too!)  It has a small frontage located between the Best Chocolate in Town and Rooster's Kitchen, so if you are hungry, your brain might just miss this pet store.  Mine did for too long!  But my wife and I were out shopping on Small Business Saturday and I had bookmarked this place on Yelp to be sure to stop by.  I had been to the locations in Fountain Square and Speedway, and since this was the closest to the other east side shops I was planning on visiting, I finally made it in.  The place is locally owned and cared for by people who love animals, particularly dogs and want them to be healthy.  So, if you like buying the cheapest thing you can for your dogs, you may be surprised by the items offered here as well as the prices.  It isn't cheap, but the quality is unmistakable.  When I brought home the human quality products (no preservatives or crappy scraps of animals), my dog tore into the treats.  She turns her nose up at the remaining over-processed, over preserved treats that I had from the grocery.  My pup knows good stuff!  The hardest thing about shopping here is that my pup seems so thrilled that I have to resist over feeding her.    The only negative here is that the store seems smaller than the other locations which carry more variety and have more space (or so it seems to me.)  Give this place a try.  Your dog(s) will thank you!  Review #3371

Although the store is clean and bright, I couldn't help but feel like something was missing from this store that I've experienced at the other Pier 1 stores in the area.
