This one has lots of furniture and accessories for decorating your home and the quality appeared to be there too.  However, there didn't seem to be as much of a candle selection as other shops.  There didn't seem to be as many international themed items as other stores (unless I just missed them.)  I am not sure of the status of this store as my wife tells me the parent company is having some financial difficulty.  Maybe the inventory was reduced, or maybe it's just the manager's priorities.  If I hadn't been in numerous other Pier 1 stores, I may not have noticed, but this store is fine for most home decor items.  Just didn't quite have the appeal of some of the other locations.  Review #3669

Full disclosure:  I don't have any food allergies or self-restrictions when it comes to dining.  (Calorie counting is my only limit.)  So, while I appreciate that this new shop offers a variety of breads (including a sourdough baguette) to folks who are searching for a tasty source for their gluten free, or dairy free, or sugar free (the list goes on), I am rating them based upon how they compare to all other bakeries.  So points for serving an under served corner of the market.    The shop is located in a plaza on the southwest corner of Allisonville Road and 96th.  There is plenty of parking and I like that there is a stoplight that allows you to have easy access back onto Allisonville.  Inside, the shop has a small reception area where there is a seating area and a display/purchase counter.  There were four types of bread (they had sold out of a fifth type) as well as the baguette.  I kind of expected more items based upon some of the reviews, so that was a bit disappointing.  The woman behind the counter said they are working on adding some more varieties including their take on a rye bread.  The shop is only open on Thursdays and Saturdays, which has also caused me to cancel plans to stop by while in the area (it takes between 45-60 minutes to get here from my house.)  The rest of the days, the staff is baking bread in the large area behind the counter.  So, no immediate plans to expand the retail shop hours soon.  And the bread itself?  Well, because they are substituting so many ingredients, it isn't like bread you find at a lot of bakeries; especially like the breads you buy in a grocery.  I'm not saying that is bad, but since they didn't have any free samples to try, we found both the seeded boule and the cinnamon raisin to be very dense and heavy.  There is a lot of chew compared to other breads we purchase.  The flavor was quite good which is why they are getting four stars from me.  But for my wife who likes bread with a crispy outside and a soft and much lighter inside texture, she was disappointed.  The loaves were selling for $9 each, so for us, having some free samples would have been helpful.   The bakery is run by three women and we were greeted and provided information about the products and business.  They even have a plaque that tells you how best to preserve your bread if you aren't consuming it in one day.    So, overall, a good tasting bread which fills a niche in the bakery market is now available.  If you really like bread, but have restrictions on what you can intake, this may be your favorite new place!  Review #3311

Here is another upscale restaurant for the Yard!  I stopped in for lunch and grabbed a spot in the mini lot they have in front of their entrance.  The interior is richly designed with high ceilings and lots or wood, brick, and plush booth seats though the regular table chairs were comfy too!  I was greeted as I entered through a door that kept the cold out and was escorted to a seat near the bar.  You can see the kitchen through the glass display shelves of the bar if you dine there.  My waitress was friendly and did a great job of making recommendations and keeping an eye on my progress.  Minimal waits during the dining experience.  Several staff stopped by to make sure everything was good.  I went with one of the Christmas ales after asking for a couple samples to try.  I also went with Seared Sea Scallops (4 decent sized!) served over three roasted fennel risotto cakes (they look like deep fried potato cakes) and those are nestled over a bed of shredded Brussels Sprouts and micro greens with a red wine butter sauce encircling the dish.  Really good flavor!  The sauce was very tasty.  The scallops were large and tender, though could have used just a bit more searing to bring out the flavor.  The risotto and greens/sprouts were excellent, especially with the butter sauce.    Note that the scallops are an entree, not a reduced lunch portion, so the price was what you would expect for a dinner.  But the quality was really good and I was glad I ordered it.    I didn't have room for dessert, so I will have to save room for my next visit.  Review #3440

Location, location, location.  We were boating and were able to find a spot along the dock outside of Wolfie's to pull up to and walk up the ramp to the restaurant.  It was a busy day on the water and so the restaurant was pretty full, especially the outdoor seating which we managed to get one of the last tables.  We were seated promptly and our wait staff did a good job of bringing out the beverages right away.  When our appetizers arrived, they came with extra mini plates so that the appetizer could be shared.  The Brussels Sprouts looked appealing, but were definitely undercooked (which gives them a funky smell.)  I like mine crispy with a bit of crunch.  These were chewy.  So, no five from me.  The main courses were pretty good, but my pan crusted chicken was very thin, which made it a bit dry.  Could have used some additional seasoning which the outside tables didn't have.  But the portions were generous and there were lots of options to choose from.  So, nobody left hungry, but just a tad underwhelmed on the flavor.    Great view of the reservoir from the patio so you get the benefit of being on the water without the rocking motion! ha!  If you are looking for a place that will have something for everyone, Wolfie's is worth checking out.    Review #3798

The Oasis Diner is a place with good food and for those of us who are old enough, to recapture the feel of the old style diners of our youth.  I have been there twice recently and enjoyed the dining both times.  The first time I went (4-26-16), I stopped in by myself for lunch.  There seemed to be a pretty good sized crowd for a Tuesday.  I grabbed a seat at the counter and took in all the details that seemed to be faithfully recreated.  I placed my order and also placed a "to go" order for my wife who was unable to go with me.  For myself, I ordered the Grilled Pork Tenderloin and cole slaw.  Now I know that Indiana is known for outrageous sized tenderloins, but I prefer good taste to mass quantity every time.  I ordered the tenderloin grilled and was very pleased with the taste and texture.  The cole slaw was good too.     For my wife's order, I picked up the pulled pork sandwich with cole slaw and sweet potato fries.  I managed to sneak a sample of the sandwich and fries and both were really delicious.   My next visit was on 5-13-16 for lunch again.  This time, my wife was able to join with me and she really seemed to enjoy the look of the place as well.  The service was friendly and timely too.   This time, my wife ordered a strawberry milkshake which the waitress was kind enough to split into two fountain glasses.  Really tasty!  She also ordered the soup and sandwich combo:  Tomato bisque soup and the Club Sandwich half.  No stingy portions on the sandwich.  She seemed quite content.   I decided to try the Oasis Burger (1/2# beef, pulled pork, barbecue sauce, bacon, cole slaw, pickles, cheddar cheese, garlic mayo on toasted bun.)  This is a meat lovers sandwich!!  And if I didn't get enough cole slaw on the sandwich, I got another side of cole slaw too.  (Can you tell I like their slaw?)   All in all, it isn't a fancy place.  It's a diner with good food.  There happens to be a city park right behind the diner to walk off some calories if you find yourself indulging too much.  There is also outdoor seating for nice days.   If you want a bit of nostalgia with your meal, give the Oasis Diner a try.  Review #17

Wow!  Does it feel good to write another review after this horrible slow down.  I had the opportunity to join a former coworker and her husband for a beer/lunch and we decided on the newly opened Nigh Brewing Company.  I am not sure of the connection, but there is definitely something linking Nigh to Plainfield's other main brewery BrewLink.  Many of the BrewLink brews are available here too!  On the site of a former brewery, this new one has easy access off SR 267 and Hadley Rd (There's a stoplight to help you get in and out of the retail area.)  They have plenty of parking on a couple sides of the building and the east end has a patio with a partial overhang for shade.  The seating outside is metal and heavy, but I found it comfortable enough.  Inside, the space is newly refinished and looked clean and spacious.  But since it was noon and in the low 70's and because the patio wasn't nearly full, my group of three chose outdoors.  But that didn't affect service at all.  The crowd was small due to the pandemic, so having only one woman handling the waitress duties and the hostess duties never became a problem for us.  She hustled and remained friendly throughout the meal. She had her mask and they have hand sanitizer dispensers around for patrons by the doorways.  I was pleasantly surprised to see they have now added flights of four beers for $8 even though some of the early reviews said they didn't.  So if you like trying lots of beers on your first visit, you can do that here!  I went with a variety of beers:  The "Nigh P.A." is an IPA (6.8% ABV) that had an approachable level of hops.  Not overpowering, but a very drinkable beer that won't cause all your other flight choices to taste weird.  I then moved on to the "Common Grounds" which is a Dunkelweizen with coffee flavor (5%) If you are someone who likes iced coffee, I would recommend this one.  I then chose the "Cordially Yours" Creamy Milk Stout (6.8%) that had bits of chocolate and assorted flavors that reminded me of my youth and sitting around eating a sundae.  Very tasty.  Not the kind of beer you would slam after mowing the lawn, but just very enjoyable flavor!  And I finished up with the "Rico Guavae" Milkshake IPA (7.7&) made with strawberry, guava, and vanilla flavors.)  It looks similar to grapefruit juice but has a nice blend of sweet and tart flavors with just a hint of bitter like you expect from an IPA.  I enjoyed all four beers without leaving the Nigh collection of brews.  They do offer BrewLink and other beers from around the state too.    And the food was above my expectations!  I ordered a grilled blackened salmon Caesar salad.  It was plenty of food without me ordering any sides.  The plate was covered with cut romaine lettuce (mostly bite sized, not giant leaves that require additional cutting).  It came dressed with Caesar dressing already on, but I suppose you could ask for it on the side.  Lots of croutons for a bit of crunch and thinly shaved squares of cheese too.  The salmon was light and flaky inside.  The blackened side was also the grilled side and offered just a hint of crunch from the searing.  Some of the best grilled fish technique I've had!  That alone was enough for an impressive rating.  My friends tried wraps and mac and cheese and enjoyed their meals.  I didn't get photos of their plates since it was our first meal together.  I like going with folks who know me and aren't put off by me asking them to wait until I get a picture of their food.  Hopefully next time we go out, I will be a little bolder and ask them if I can grab a photo before it arrives.  I don't like being rude.  Meals are meant to be enjoyed together!  And to make the day even better, my friends picked up the tab!  No waiting around for the bill to arrive.  The waitress efficiently asked how the checks were to be grouped/divided and before I could react, my friend said one bill for the table and to her.  I offered, but I have to admit that I do enjoy being treated once in awhile instead of being the one who always picks up the bill!   Very nice meal and beer selections.  Plenty of seating during the day and I can only hope that once the pandemic passes, more people will support this and other local breweries/restaurants.  It wasn't just a meal...it was a memory that I will enjoy.  Review #3779

For good food and a bit of nostalgia in a beautifully ornate setting, give Lotus Garden a try.  The last remaining restaurant (this one opened circa 1965) of the three original Lotus Gardens, was part of a group that pioneered Chinese takeout in the Indy area.  Although the original owner sold the business, the Tam family has maintained the charm and mystique of the original restaurant ever since purchasing it.  Inside, the walls and ceilings are festooned with large murals and carvings, some covering entire walls.  Dragons hold decorative lanterns over the booths in the main dining area.  The dining area consists of two areas, the main room is television free and is filled with pleasant music, however, not of Chinese origin.  The back room which has the murals does have a large screen television which could be beneficial, but looks out of place in the setting.  The food is made to attract American tastebuds with a number of very approachable menu items.  There is a large menu of dinner items to select from (I highly recommend ordering from the menu over going with a buffet option.)  For lunch, there are both "specials" and "combos" for under $9.  For only $.50 more, you get a chicken wing and crab rangoon added to the special.  The special includes an out of place dinner roll, fried rice, egg roll, and your choice of hot tea or coffee to go along with your entree.  I really like that they don't bring all the food out at once which gives you time to eat each grouping while it is hot.  I must echo my friend Erin's recommendation of the Egg Drop Soup.  They make fresh chicken broth every day to use as a base and you can tell the flavor is deep and rich and well seasoned.  If you have a soup choice, start with this one!  As much as I enjoyed the pleasant and efficient service and the very affordable prices, I must say that the food was quite ordinary during my lunch time visit.  Other than the soup, there wasn't any "wow" moment.  Just good food, maybe a tad over cooked, but definitely not dry.  I find it odd that they serve a warm, fresh baked dinner roll and packages of crackers while you wait.  It seems out of place, especially when the entree is coming with rice.  The rolls are baked in a pan together so that they have that square shape you see in commercial packaging.  Still, the roll was light and fluffy.    The tea was served from a metal tea pot which had an actual spout, so I appreciated that the tea poured evenly without dribbling down some rounded porcelain spout.  Very nice flavor to the tea, with a wedge of lemon served on the side.  Overall, it was a nice return visit to one of Indy's oldest remaining restaurants.  If you haven't been in awhile, treat yourself to a nice meal here.  I was in and out in about 40 minutes.  If you have never been here, make sure to take time to appreciate all the fine artwork inside.  Review #497

The next time I come here, I will either come early to have a better selection of fresh pastries, or will come around lunch and grab a soup/sandwich combo.  I had already eaten elsewhere thinking this was just a bakery since that was what I was looking for on Yelp.    Note that the cafe is located on the first floor of a highrise building on the southwest corner of Ohio and Illinois.  The cafe is to the right of the elevators and down a short hallway (enter the cafe on the left).  There isn't a large dining area, but the place didn't seem too crowded.  A salad bar is on your left as you head towards the order/pastry counter in the back.  A soup bar has a couple options on the right.  Menus are written on a whiteboard over the salad bar so that you can choose before ordering.  Because of my circumstance, I only ordered from the pasty counter which was somewhat depleted by the time I arrived.  Still, the pastries I got were very tasty.  The apple fritter was a reasonable size and had nice flavor and wasn't oily.  The small cherry pastries had a croissant like wrap around the filling and were good, but had lost their crispness due to the humidity.    I also noticed that they offer a free drink with a lunch order for Yelpers!  Be sure to check in!  The folks who work there were friendly and said they had been open for five years.  That's saying something for a place to survive without much advertising and minimal sidewalk visibility.  I hope to get back soon to try out their lunches.  Review #2705

I decided to head downtown on a Sunday, just after noon.  When I entered this restaurant on the northeast corner of the Central Library block, the woman behind the counter let me know that they have a different menu for brunches that I should use to order because of the time and date.  They still have the same beverages available, but food choices change.  I placed my order and couldn't help but notice the eclectic mix of colors and styles inside.  One wall near the restrooms had comic book covers that featured rappers dressed as superheroes.  There were miniature chefs (ceramic?) on the wall dividing the waiting area from the order counter.  There were also some red chairs there that reminded me of stadium or bus seats (they were linked together).  The rest of the place had an industrial look with concrete floors and pastel colors, but with deeper red accents.  My coffee arrived first and was served right on the edge of being too hot to drink, but just cool enough that I didn't need to wait long.    When my order came, I was pleased how appealing the chef had made my order.  I went with the Comida Taco which is served on the red and white checkerboard paper on a metal tray.  The taco was made with a chive tortilla which is a bit darker in color, but has an enjoyable flavor when combined with all the other ingredients.  There was Char Siu pork (looks like thick bacon, but is tender with a sweet/tangy/savory combination of flavors), scrambled egg, sauteed onions/peppers, and shredded carrots for color.  I chose to eat it with a knife and fork though I suppose I could have risked picking it up.  The ingredients were already spilling out the front so I went with utensils.  Note that the knife did cut through the red and white paper, but it didn't get soggy and stick to the food, so no risk of eating bits of paper with your taco.  I felt the eggs could have used a bit of seasoning since there wasn't any special sauce on the taco.  They had poodle shaped salt and pepper shakers on my table, but I decided to eat it just as served.    I usually don't comment on price since I figure it is relative to the person spending the money to decide, but I will say that for $5, that was a lot of taco!  Very affordable with a lot of good flavor to ingest.  Parking is always hit or miss in the area.  The library offers the first 30 minutes free in their garage and it's only $1 for the full hour.  Street parking (mostly metered) is also available if you can find a spot.  Good food, good price, good place to eat with an assortment of things in house to look at while waiting for your order.  Review #2415

What a pleasant surprise dining at this Eastern African restaurant.  The place was not crowded for lunch and I was able to grab a parking spot out front and a table by the window.  I started with an appetizer called Lentils Sambussa.  These three triangular puff pastries were filled with beans, onions, and herbs.  They were served hot and crisp.  The insides were a little bland on their own, but they come with a red chile and green chile sauce option.  Both sauces have an initial heat kick, but fortunately, the heat wasn't the kind that grew stronger with each bite.  What I found was adding a bit of green AND red to the pastries really added a lot of flavor making these quite tasty!  For my entree or large plate option, I ordered from the beef section.  I went with Ye-Siga Alicha (mild) as my option.  The 16-inch plate comes with a somewhat spongy brown pancake  like base called an injera.  It looks like it is poured over a hot skillet and allows the heat to create "bubble craters" on the surface until done.  Then, a stew like mixture including onion, potato, carrot, tumeric, and tomato is placed in the center.  There were also a variety of seasoned vegetable mixtures and a small salad placed on the injera as well.  On a separate plate, another injera is quartered and folded.  To eat this finger food, you tear a patch of injera and use it like a napkin to grab the food from the other plate.  The flavors were delicious!  Nothing I tasted was "out there", but seemed somewhat familiar with an additional spice or two to give it a twist.  If you are at all trepidatious about new foods, I highly recommend this selection.  The menu comes with a number of chicken, seafood, and vegetarian options as well.  Review #291

This corner bake/cake shop is easy to miss in a strip mall on the northeast corner of Madison and Stop 11.  The shop is small and when I entered, I didn't see anyone working, but I grabbed a serving tray and tongs to the right of the entrance and began shopping.  They have a large number of breads, pastries, and cookies available, but none were labeled, so it required a bit of guessing on my part.  At some point during my shopping, a woman quietly appeared at the cash register.    My wife is a big fan of the large, crispy pastry that looks like the dough is rolled out then the lengths get folded a couple times to spread out across the bake sheet.  Some places add a bit of sugar to make a glazed/sweet layer.  This place had just a light coating.  However, she still enjoyed the crisp crunch of the treat.  I also picked up a horn stuffed with a vanilla filling, a long roll with a berry jelly filling, a large cookie (like a sugar cookie, but not much flavor), and a triangle filled with pineapple filling (I thought it was lemon when I bought it.)  My favorite was the large triangle.  The horn was more like bread than like pastry.    The prices are low and I got all six items for less than a $6 ($0.89 to $1.25 each).  It's nice to know I don't have to drive all the way to 38th Street on the west side to pickup Mexican pastry.  I have a feeling my wife is going to want to visit here again.  Note:  This spot is adjacent to a Mexican grocery/restaurant so you can take care of getting all your Mexican food shopping/dining without moving your car.  Review #2699

I was looking for a bakery on the west side when this place popped up on Yelp!  Better than "just a bakery", this place has breakfast sandwiches, lunch sandwiches, and smoothies in addition to the bakery section of bagels and muffins.  Located in a busy strip mall on the southeast corner of Dan Jones and US 36, the biggest challenge is pulling in and out of your parking spaces.  (Lots of traffic and it is hard to back out, so skip the places right next to the building and choose a place you can pull forward to get out!)  Well, we found a spot and saw there were a number of tables (different sizes) for customers to choose from.  My wife grabbed a table while I placed our order at the counter.  On the left of the counter, I noticed the "Bakery" section and chose a Banana Nut muffin and a Peach Pecan muffin (to go).  I also ordered off the menu over the counter a Big Apple Club on whole wheat (get it toasted!) for my wife and choose a Tuna Salad on my choice of bread/twist:  the Monterey Cheese twist.  Since the business was nearly full when we got there, the wait was about ten minutes.  They had asked for my name when I paid and then delivered the sandwiches on actual china.  (Note that the drinks and utensils are self serve from a counter to the right.)  Both sandwiches were fresh and tasty and I would gladly recommend them.  I like that even if you choose the same basic sandwich on a return visit, they have a wide variety of breads to choose from which can tailor the sandwich to your own particular tastes.    This national chain has been around since 2007 and seemed to have a steady following in the Avon area.    Review #474

While traveling along Kentucky Avenue, I saw the sign for Mickey & Bill's Pizza, so I slowed to turn and go over the railroad tracks to get to this small shop.    They have a small lot along the building and the entrance is on the northeast side.    As I entered into the lobby where the order counter was, I noticed a very small dining room to my left and a few chairs to sit at if I needed to wait.  I was greeted and the woman behind the counter was very patient and helpful in describing the ingredients in the uniquely named pizzas.  (Note that they have flyers off to the left side of the counter which I hadn't seen when entering.)  The less specific menu is listed overhead behind the counter.  I hadn't called ahead, but since it wasn't a busy time, they were able to make my small pizza in about 15 minutes.  I got one called "The Works" which had 8 party cut pieces and is similar to Supreme pizzas elsewhere:  crumbled sausage, mushroom, green pepper, onions, pepperoni, and two kinds of cheese on a thin crust.  While waiting, I noticed they also have wings and breadsticks, salads, and some sandwiches to choose from.  They also have an option called "Take & Bake Pizza" that you get your pizza freshly made but finish baking it at home.   And I recommend grabbing a flyer since they have a list of discounts available on larger orders.  And the pizza?  Well, my wife and I like a crisp bottom crust so this was very enjoyable.  The ingredients were also piled high with just enough sauce and cheese to balance the flavor.  The firm crust allowed the ingredients to stay on the pizza without falling off.  That's a plus for me. (Not so much for my dog.)    I don't know if I like pizza (any pizza) enough to drive out of my way for, but if you are commuting along Kentucky Avenue or live in the area, I suggest you will enjoy your food from here.  Review #3608

During my visit to the new Test Kitchen at Sun King in the Fishers District,   I ordered some food from Korave.  This restaurant is run by the a pair of brothers (John and Kim) who left South Korea for culinary school in Utah, and then ended up with a food truck in central Indiana.  Their main focus is on Korean BBQ in this new location.  Although they are known for their rice bowls and poutine, I decided to go with the Street Taco medley and a side order of Mandoo (fried chicken dumplings.)  The tacos were fantastic.  I wasn't sure which meats were included in the medley, but each one tasted delicious!  Soft shell flour tortillas come with mixed greens, some pickled items, and sauces that bring out a complex layering of food that is easy to eat.  I didn't have a favorite:  they were all good!  The Mandoo comes with five dumplings that are nestled over some fresh shredded veggies and lightly coated with a sauce.  They were crisp and the ingredients were tasty, but I am used to having a dipping sauce for my dumplings.  So even though I asked, they didn't have anything to dip in.  That would be appreciated.  The portion sizes were fair for the prices.  Not too large.  I was easily able to eat the three tacos while my wife ate most of the Mandoo.  Basically, you go to the specific counter for the restaurant, place your order and pay, and are given a sensor that will buzz when your order is ready.  That allows time to find a table and place a beer order from Sun King.  (Note that they do sell non-beer beverages here too.)  When done, the wait staff of Sun King will clear off your trash for you.  The Test Kitchen is very popular, so finding seating is a challenge.  If you aren't successful on the main floor, you may find some room upstairs.  The overall environment is quite loud, though there are places that are family friendly (just not near the bar of Sun King.)  Parking is at a premium.  We grabbed one of the last street parking spaces just north of the brewery.  They do have parking garages available, but I don't know if they charge or if they are free.  Hopefully someone else will post that soon.  Review #3635

I am a big fan of this place.  There are so many positive stories behind the scene of how this place came to be and the service it provides the community.  But ultimately, it will need to succeed on its own merits and quality to be sustainable.  When you drive along MLK Jr, there is a small parking lot on the north side of the building.  Just look for the giant mural featuring photo real images of key individuals in the history of food production and Flanner House to our city.  On the east end of the building is the cafe.  On the west end is the grocery; Same building, but different entrances.  My wife and I only visited the cafe which is bright and clean and looked like something you would expect at a coffee shop with lots of folks working on their computers.  There are a couple pastry display cases next to the order counter where we were greeted by a pleasant woman. My wife wanted to try a strawberry croissant while I was in the mood to try one of their smoothies.  They even heated the croissant since we were dining in.  While I waited on my smoothie, I stepped outside to check out the pergola covered patio deck and the new Flanner House Orchard Greenspace to the south.  Great view to have an orchard and garden growing next to the patio.  By the time I stepped back in, my Banana Berry Smoothie was ready.  It was a little bit tart, and definitely cold, so I advise drinking it slowly at first.  Because of all the fresh berries, there are a lot of tiny seeds, so be aware of that if you aren't a fan of those.  You can also build your own with up to five ingredients.  My wife thought the croissant was good, but said that most of the filling was on one end.  So, if they could just be sure to fill them a bit more evenly, then she would have given it higher marks.  So glad to see the neighborhood have a place for stopping in to get groceries and a light snack/pastry/beverage.  It was cool to see all the kids in the neighborhood working on the garden/greenspace next door.  With this much involvement, it looks like Cleo's is on the right path.  Review #2732

When I was younger, I saw the classic animated Disney feature "Fantasia" and was amazed at the synchronization between the images and the music.  Watching the dancing lights on the lawn of Oldfields (The Lilly House) at Newfields brought back all those wonderful memories.  The lawn, the trees, the shrubs, just about everything has lights that are synched and really are enjoyable.   Not only is the light show great, there is a snowflake bridge and a kissing arch (it's a little off the beaten path!). There are places to get warm beverages and s'mores, and a self-guided tour of the Lilly House which is bedecked with poinsettias and Christmas lights/villages inside.  Parking was easy and free during the week.  Tickets sell out in advance for weekends, so it's best to save money by buying online at the Newfield's website and not taking any chances.  There are two blocks of times:  5 pm and 7 pm.  Certain dates even have a costumed fella in a red suit show up!  Very nice addition to the IMA and Indy's winter celebrations.  Review #468

I almost gave this restaurant five stars just for being a business in Broad Ripple with its own parking lot!  You do have to put up with bits of traffic problems with the work on College Avenue's Red Line and the median allowing access only from the south, so it's not a perfect setup.  And don't let the rather drab, strip mall looking exterior keep you away either.  Inside is an elegant setting with high quality food and beverages.  It always amazes me when I look at how much time passes between my visits to restaurants (I am not the ideal customer for business owners).  It had been quite awhile, so I decided to take advantage of this business being open on Monday nights (that's fairly rare in town).  With their opening at 4, I was the first customer about 4:30 and had my choice of seating.  I was shown to a small table in the bar area with a view of the tv screens over the bar (they are partially obstructed by the hanging light shades though.)  My server was very pleasant and she did a really good job throughout the evening as I ordered, dined, and checked out.  Plenty of water refills and the always appreciated check in on how everything tastes after I've had a chance to take a few bites makes for a smooth flowing evening.  I started off with a cocktail which tend to run in the $10-13 range.  The Strawberry - Basil Martini is excellent!  The brightness of the berry flavor with a hint of tarty sweetness was balanced by the aroma/flavor of the basil which added a savory element.  I barely tasted the alcohol, so it's a good thing it was pricey...these could sneak up on you fast if you kept drinking them.  Excellent for sipping and savoring the flavor.  Since I was dining alone, I passed the appetizers which generally are portioned to be shareable.  I went directly to the entree which was a tough choice (quite a few of the items sounded really good!)  I went with the Smoked Apple Butter Ribs (comes in a separated half rack) with two decks of Potato Gratin and garnished with braised red cabbage for a bit of acidity.  I was very pleased with the flavor and color of the cabbage which accomplished enhancing the meal with both attributes.  The ribs, though not quite 'fall off the bone' done were still very tender and were easily removed with a little knife work.  The smoked apple butter added depth to the flavor of the pork ribs and when combined with bits of the chopped cabbage, delivered a well rounded taste.  Serving them over the potato gratin, I had to move the ribs out of the way to realize the deck shaped potatoes were underneath.  The potatoes are sliced about 1" wide and about 3" long, then turned on their side to form a deck sized block.  This made it easy to use my fork to separate the slices into bite sized sections.  Bites of the ribs, cabbage, AND potato were the best.  Well done!  I also ordered an additional side (sauteed green beans) that were easily shareable, but I managed to eat them all.  They were served fresh and bright green from the al dente prep.  I personally prefer them done just a bit more, but I realize this is how a lot of upscale restaurants serve them.  Just a matter of choice.  They could have used a bit of seasoning or maybe a hint of lemon juice...something to bring out the taste.  Overall, it was a very enjoyable meal and experience.  Counting tax and standard tip, the meal (with cocktail and extra side) was just over $50, so not a cheap night out.  But if you want to try something that tastes good AND is filling, then check this place out.  Review #2433

I have driven passed this place many times on my way home from our daughters house, but neve around breakfast time.  Note that they do offer other items suitable for other meals, but I suspect it makes its main business at breakfast with "Pancake House" in the business name.  So, when my wife asked if I felt like going out for breakfast and didn't mind if we drove a bit to get there, I remembered seeing this place and that it had a solid Yelp rating, so I suggested here since she wanted eggs and hash browns, not just baked items or donuts.  The place appears relatively new and it was clean and in good shape.  Much nicer than a lot of breakfast places that I've found to be hole in the wall or dive places.  It's not a fancy place, but seemed well maintained and since they had plenty of parking, we grabbed a spot right by the entrance.  Apparently a lot of folks who go out for breakfast tend to sleep in, so we had the place pretty much to ourselves.  That translated to great service and minimal wait times on our order.  I particularly liked that the black coffee I ordered was hot, but not scalding, so I could drink it right away!  (other places take note!)  Our waitress was personable without being intrusive and she made sure to ask before topping off my cup throughout my meal.  My wife ordered an omelet which came with lots of sides, but she only wanted the hash browns.  She felt the omelet was a bit underseasoned and a bit overcooked.  (3 out of 5 for her)   Fortunately, each table has its own salt and pepper shakers and ketchup bottles, so we had no wait for any of those items.  My Eggs Benedict were really good!  I was surprised at how deeply yellow orange the Hollandaise sauce was.  Maybe they used extra yolks or maybe even a hint of mustard to get the color.  They used real English Muffins and provided a steak knife to be able to slice through the muffin and Canadian Bacon easily.  (I hate when places expect you to cut your breakfast with a dull table knife that fails to slice.)  Other than flavor, what makes a good eggs benedict is when the yolk of the egg is soft and spills out over the hash browns.  This serving had two eggs on top and both flowed smoothly.  Just wish the hash browns had been a little crisper.  Check out was fast and easy too, so an overall good experience for us.  Just need to fine tune the hash browns and cut back on the omelet times.  If you want to try something tasty for breakfast other than pastries or donuts, stop in Ricky's.  Review #3822

Although this place has an address on Cornell, it is set so far back from the street that it might as well have an address on Coil (it is across Coil from Fire by the Monon.) Regardless of how confusing the address is, it is worth taking time to find this tasty bakery in the small blue violet house.  The entrance is on the east side and once inside, it can get crowded quickly.  The display cases are near the door and I was glad to arrive when I did since there seemed to be a line of folks behind me!  Fortunately, I was able to see the variety of pastries available and with a bit of challenge, was able to pick up a nice variety.  (There is very little labeling and some of it that is there faces the server, not the customer.)  There are so many tasty looking choices that it is hard to decide.  I picked up a crowned cherry bread pudding, a raspberry chocolate tart, and three kinds of macarons to go.  Note that there are a couple small 2-top tables outside the building, but there simply isn't room to sit and relax.  Think of it as a "to go" bakery.  Yes, the foods taste as good as they look.  I liked that the macarons melt in your mouth as you bite them.  I got the banana, the blueberry, and the chocolate raspberry flavors though they had twice as many options.  It isn't a cheap bakery like a donut shop.  But understand that these aren't the type of pastries that get mass produced.  In fact, the building is so small that they aren't capable of mass producing this much variety.  And that's okay!  There's a nice selection of pastries to choose from and it is always nice to try something new to break up your morning routine.  Review #2868

I recently had the pleasure of attending the VIP & Media Event soft opening (2019) of the Carmel Christkindlmarkt.  And I will freely admit that plying my interest with loads of free samples of food and beverages may have influenced my enjoyment of this event.  But despite the cold, walking around the campus built around an ice rink did wonders for getting me in the Holiday spirit.  First, there was plenty of parking in the neighboring garage on Veteran's Way.  There are also nice restrooms and a chance to get out of the cold at the Tarkington Theater lobby.  And all around the rink there are fire pits and large space heaters (though the windy conditions minimized the warming that took place.)    There are dozens of wooden shelters that house food and gift shops all with a German theme.  There is also a stage for live performers and announcements.    I was fortunate enough to meet up with another Yelper (Joey "Zoe" C) and her friends to visit the shops and grab the tasty treats.  And there were lots of treats:  Schmalzkuchen (powdered doughnut holes); Schnitzel w Red Cabbage and lemon; freshly skimmed hot Raclette cheese over roasted potatoes; a pork sausage sample from Wurst Haus; a pretzel bite, coffee, and hot chocolate too!  So glad I only got sample sizes!  I didn't stay around for the ice skating (I bruise too easily and take longer to heal than in my youth!)  I'm sure it is fun for most folks, but I'm too out of practice to venture onto smooth ice.  The event was a lot of fun and thank you to Yelp for getting passes to see this Winter Wonderland with a German twist.  Rev. #51

Although this grocery store is fairly close to our home, we seldom shop here unless my wife needs to pick up something from the pharmacy (which is closed on Sundays).     This is an older store and you can tell by the large cracks in the floor and lack of brightness inside.  It seems small when compared to the superstore groceries in the area.  If you are familiar with this layout, I suppose you can get around quickly, but since it isn't our "go to" spot, we always struggle trying to find specific items that may not be listed on the aisle signs.  I found cashews for my recipes in the snacks aisle and again in the produce section, but it was more luck than anything that led me to them.    The parking for this place is always tight and even if you find a spot near the entrances, the lot has angled spaces so you have one way traffic but it seems tight and I don't like parking too close to the building because it can get crazy in the parking area.  Before I moved to town, I was warned by a long time resident that this place is unusual and they had stopped shopping at this place because of the awkward parking and lack of items you can find at the much larger supermarkets in the area.  Maybe you won't have any problems, but I will continue to use this as just a convenience shopping location if we have to pick something up in the area.  Review #3866

I enjoyed my meal at Pit Stop!  I was with my wife, our daughter, and grand daughters for a midweek dinner and we had plenty of space dining inside.  We were seated in a large dining room that has an exhibit room with lots of auto racing memorabilia.  We did not check out the Pit Crew Lounge since our granddaughters where with us and it is for 21+.  We were greeted as we entered from the parking lot and when we said we preferred dining in, we were taken to a dining room back away from the front door so we were plenty warm enough even on a cold winter day.  Let me say that I really enjoyed my meal and if it wasn't for the opinions of the others in my group, I might have rated this higher.  I ordered the Brisket Meal which came with 2 sides.  I went with a side salad and a dish of applesauce.  The meal comes with a diagonally sliced white bread which isn't large enough to hold all the meat that comes in the meal.  The Brisket was about a half inch thick, was moist, and very tender!  They only had two types of BBQ sauce on our table (original and sweet).  I forgot to ask if they had anything else.  I found the original had a nice balance of flavors and would recommend it for a good pairing with this dish.  My granddaughters ordered and seemed pleased (especially with the mac and cheese) but they aren't really picky eaters, so I didn't expect any problems there.  My wife thought her nachos with pulled pork were just okay.  She found the pork a bit dry on its own but for some reason, she didn't pick a sauce to help.  Oh well.  As I alluded to earlier, I didn't try any of the adult beverages, so I can say how good the cocktails or beer/wine selection is.  But, for a decent meal on the east side of Brownsburg, I think you can find something you'll like at Pit Stop.  Review #3877

Located on the north side of the Fountain Square Theater Building, the Atomic/Action Duckpin Bowling was a fun way to spend an hour.  The Atomic Bowl (1950's era decor located in the basement) was closed.  However, the Action Bowl (1930's era located on the fourth floor) was open and had plenty of lanes for our early afternoon enjoyment.    Basically, once you find a place to park (street parking is usually not too bad depending upon time of day), you enter the building on the north side and take the elevator up to the fourth floor.  Once you pay your money, you get a lane for $40 for the hour.  You don't need to rent shoes which is a plus since street shoes are fine.  Since just two of us were bowling, we got three games finished in our time and that was plenty!  Although the balls used are much smaller and lighter than regulation bowling, the balls do not have finger holes and can be difficult for smaller children to hold in one hand.   I had no trouble rolling three games, but going through that delivery motion made my legs start to feel a "burn" from the continuous bending.    Also note that scoring, though the same for strikes and spares (as if you will make any!), you do get a third ball on every frame that pins are left standing.  If you manage to knock all remaining pins down on the third roll, you simply get ten points instead of a spare.  This is a game that is very challenging if you are someone who likes high scores and rely on technique.  The small size pins make it very difficult to get pin action and I've seen balls thrown down the middle only get a 5!  So, if you are thinking about going, go in with a good attitude and with friends that are there for a social gathering, not worried about how high their scores are.    My only negatives are that the building is very difficult to navigate if you have mobility issues, and the lanes and balls are in need of attention, showing marks and nicks and could use some attention. (I could hardly see the guide marks that were out on the lane.)  Hopefully, the management will be able to do some renovation to make the experience a bit more user friendly.  Review #421

It had been over ten years since my last visit to Fujiyama.  Not that I ever had a bad experience, but that I hardly ever get to the southeast side around dinner time.  So, I set out to try lunch instead!  I was surprised to see how full their parking lot was already!  For the lunch crowd on a Saturday, most of the customers were dining on the Hibachi side of the restaurant.  I could here the slapping of the tools on the hot grill and the shouts of excitement.  But since I had never tried their sushi, thought this would be an ideal time.  I ordered several items including the Egg Rolls, the Tiger Roll, and the Magic Salmon Nigiri.  I placed my order for all three items at the beginning, so I wasn't of the order they would arrive.  The egg rolls arrived first.  There were two per order and when they were delivered, I was surprised!  They were larger than any I've had elsewhere and they were sliced on the biaz over a bed of shredded cabbage and carrots (& topped with a little green onion).  The dipping sauce had a large opening to allow the roll to be dipped easily.  The taste was the best I've had!  The sauce was a combination of flavors that had a bit of sweet, a bit of heat, and brought the crunchy rolls to life!  Definitely recommend these.    Before I was finished, my Tiger Roll arrived.  It looked impressive in size and height, but I realized that the shape of the roll was not round like most places.  The roll was thin compared to the height which made me think it must have been intentionally shaped that way.  Unfortunately, it made the roll lose its integrity for holding the ingredients in.  The flavor was pretty good and the sauces (eel sauce and spicy mayo) were tasty, but the roll was difficult to maneuver.  There was a slight hint of fishiness on the first bite as well, but that may have been from the tempura shrimp on the end since I didn't notice it on the rest of the roll.  My meal ended with the Magic Salmon Nigiri which is a popular item, but doesn't come with a very good description.  I expected 2 pieces of nigiri where the raw salmon would overlay the ball of rice.  What I received was two pieces of cooked salmon over rice with lemon slices between the pieces and topped with a sauce.  I was so bewildered, I didn't know what to say before the waiter moved along.  So, I tried it....and it was delicious too!  No wonder it is popular.  I enjoyed the flavor of the sauce and the three lemon slices were also baked, so they were juicy and added that acidity to the dish that lifted the flavor profile.  Still, it would have been nice to know that was how the dish would be prepared.  The waiter accepted that he should take that responsibility since the menus aren't clear.   Overall, it was a fine meal and the service was generally attentive and quick.  I think my next visit will be to try some of the steamed buns that are available on the dinner menu.  Review #1335

My wife and I arranged to meet our daughter downtown for lunch at the newly opened restaurant.  Set at the corner of  Market Street and Meridian, the main entrance is found on Market about half a block west of Monument Circle.  For long time Indy residents, you may recognize the former Blocks Department store.  The restaurant only uses a small portion of the once huge department area.  The scale here is much smaller without the opulent decor of the previous tenant.  Upon entering, you see the small dining area and bar.  Additional seating is outside on the expanded sidewalk area.  There was table side service, but the waitress was also the hostess and worked behind the counter too, so there were some times when it was difficult to find any staff in the dining room if we needed assistance.  We noted the the music was cranked way too loud for the small dining area though I will compliment the staff for making an adjustment suitable to make our dining conversation possible.   Despite the small number of staff working, I will say the food was delivered properly and without much delay.  I thought it was seasoned well, but did find that the two dishes ordered with chicken were cooked too long and seemed dry.  I was able to try some of my daughter's shrimp skewer and enjoyed IT.  Not rubbery, just a pleasant bite.  The prices were higher than most of the downtown options) nd the wait  could be improved to be competitive so that diners aren't pressured to leave just to make it back to work on time.  If  you are downtown within walking distance, I recommend  that option on nice days.  Some street parking was available and some parking garages aren't too far away, but on the day I went the doors to the garages  in the building weren't working.  So allow plenty of time for traffic and finding a spot.  I am glad that a landmark building is finding some continued use.  Hopefully this restaurant will fine-tune some of the items I pointed out and will be successful in drawing customers back o this once popular spot. Review #3963.

Let me qualify my review by saying that our eldest grandson is employed here and my wife and I wanted to check it.  Since it was his day off, he was able to take time to show us around the business without worrying about taking too long with us.    I think I had been here maybe once before when our son was a younger man (before our grandson was around).  It seemed quite familiar and I like that it felt spacious.  All the games and activities were functioning, so I didn't feel like we were missing out just because the place had just opened about an hour earlier.  I can't comment on how good the food and beverages are since we had already eaten before arriving, but as soon as we stepped in, there is a whirl of lights and sound (but not blasting so loud that we had trouble communicating.)  They keep the food and beverage seating near the entrance while the farther back you go into the arcade, the more chaotic and fully immersed you become in the arcade (state fair feel).    They have a lot of interactive games, some for individuals while others allow you to compete with other players.  Over on the south wall there were a number of skee ball lanes and some hoops shooting places.  So, you don't have to have great skill or knowledge of games to have a good time here.  Just relax and have a good time.  They have some packages for different price levels depending upon how many people want to play and how long you want to stay.  I didn't want to dive into that, so maybe someone else will review this place and provide better details.  We just tagged along my grandson as he explained some things.  Looked like a fun place if you are into games and maybe a competitive sort.  Review #3883

The restaurant, bar,brunch place is worth the effort it takes to get through all the downtown construction and parking challenges.  My wife and I wanted to get out and this newly opened spot. Had caught my eye.  Located on the site of the former Kruger's on Delaware next to Stouts Shoes with additional access from Mass Avenue.  The industrial interior has retained much of the noteworthy artwork of the former restaurant but has added a nice soft lounge area in addition to the tables and bar seating.  There is also additional outdoor seating on the patio along Delaware.  So if you avoid the busiest of times, you should be able to find some seating suitable for you.  I have read some reviews that thought it too loud,but our inside dining at lunch was tolerable for conversation.   While there we chose to order a dine in meal and we also ordered beverages.  My wife got a local craft beer while I opted for one of the house cocktails. Both very enjoyable.  If you like good food, food service, and good beverages, make some plans to check out Oakmont,  Review #3922

When I first thought of the concept, I was a bit skeptical that this was a viable restaurant.  But  then I started reading the reviews and decided to give it a try.  Sure you can make a good pbj at home, but this place has such variety of PB, some I had never heard of.  I decided to go unconventional and really enjoyed my sandwich.  My only regret was that they had run out of he jelly flavor that was my first choice.  I guess I will have to return.  Service was friendly and the wait was short.  The sandwiches ran about $7 so be aware the bill willgrow quickly.  Review #3978

Maybe it's the perfect day to sit on the shaded patio each time I dine here.  Maybe it's the friendly service, or the beautiful presentations that make me hungry before I taste the food.  Maybe it's the gorgeous woodwork in the restored mansion.  Those are nice, but the food is down right delicious!  Ya, it's the food!  I don't know exactly why it took me so long to dine here, but I am so glad I did.  I took my wife on Wednesday for lunch and we knew immediately that we wanted to sit outside on the patio.  We could have selected the gazebo, but the wrought iron chairs and tables looked comfy enough.    We were greeted immediately and quickly had our drinks served.  After a few minutes, we placed our orders.  My wife opted for the Prime Rib Sandwich with Kettle Chips.  The sandwich was served on ciabatta bread with white cheddar and carmelized onions. On the side were three cups:  one was an au jus; one a horseradish dipping sauce (think spicy brown mustard); and the third was a white creamy sauce (maybe a mayo).  The beef was served "cold", but was actually warm and juicy.  The cheddar was melted and soft, but not stringy.  The onion was cut into large pieces that added a nice sweetness to go with the sharp taste of the horseradish.  Very tasty!  I opted for the Maryland Crab Cakes.  Each of the four cakes was served on a warm lemon slice.  An ornamental pattern of three colorful sauces highlighted the visuals of the plate.  The sauces were made from peanuts (light brown color), sriracha (red color), and wasabi (light green color).  The flavors worked incredibly well together with the crab.  I didn't consider the sauces too spicy although my wife thought they had some kick to them.  Highly recommended!   I also couldn't resist ordering the Asparagus in a Blanket which I thoroughly enjoyed on my previous visit.  The asparagus (thin pieces, not giant tree-sized pieces) was wrapped in Filo dough with prosciutto and Gruyere cheese.  These are baked to crisp the dough which adds a wonderful buttery flavor to the mix.  The blankets are criss-crossed like lincoln logs and have a decorative splash of the same three sauces as the crab cakes.  The flavors worked exceptionally well here as well.  Delicious!  So glad they didn't take it off the menu.  Sure, it is a bit pricey for a lunch, but the menu items are the same size as what I could get at dinner, so I don't put artificial price restrictions when it comes to time of day.  If the food is 5 star, I am willing to pay for 5 star.    Oh, and they have a large variety of wines  (hence the name).  The wines are available from the store (to go) or can be purchased for dinner.  Note:  Since the same type of wine is available in both the store and the restaurant, there is a separate line item on your bill if you purchase an entire bottle for your meal.  I fully understand that most places just tell you a price without the breakout.....I've always paid more for beverages at a restaurant than at a store.  Don't let the extra fee surprise you and ruin an otherwise fantastic dining experience.  Rev #20

Overall experience was fine.  I had tried stopping here before on a weekend and the place had customers lined out the door, so I passed.  This time, we decided to go a round lunch time on a Friday and though the place is rather small, we were able to see some tables just waiting to be bussed before we knew we could stay.    Like many places I've been to eat after the pandemic, this place was short staffed and just trying to get a hostess or waitress to seat us took awhile.  My wife flagged a woman down and she cleaned a spot for us and gave us real menus to look over. Once we had her attention, we quickly got our orders taken and beverages brought over.  I ordered from the lunch menu (a yummy breaded tenderloin that remained moist and tender and mostly fit the bun.  I asked for it loaded and even got some yellow mustard which she brought over without delay too. The breading had a nice seasoning too.  Since I was eating, I also upgraded to a side salad  that wasn't all weeds with a vinaigrette dressing.   My wife ordered from the breakfast menu getting a waffle with strawberries and bananas.  Not quite crisp enough for her preference, but a decent flavor.  Her comment was that it could have been raised a level with some whipped cream on top.  I suggested she ask but she didn't.   Food was a little slow coming out of the kitchen compared to most local brunch spots I've been to lately.  But manageable.   One of the perks of this spot is that even if you have to wait, there are so many Indy 500 photos and collectibles inside that it is like a mini museum adventure looking around.   Plenty of food options, plenty to see, just allow a little time.  Convenient parking in the side lot and some street parking out front. Reasonably priced for what you get too!  Review #3927

I'm going to give this new location a five on potential, but understand that there are a few things that can be improved.  Sun King used to have a small batch location 20 blocks to the south.  Now, they are part of a vibrant food destination in Fishers District (aka "the Yard").  The facility they are in has a 2-story public area with additional outdoor space in nicer weather.  The main floor has the brewery in the back, the bar area in the center, and family seating up front.  To the right is the location of the Test Kitchen that features three independent restaurants that are either start ups or upgrades from food trucks.  Sun King handles the beer, the restaurants handle the food, so if you come here, don't blame Sun King if you don't like the food.  Got it?  The seating is mostly long communal tables, but we were able to grab one of the few 4-top tables at 5 pm.  Yes, the place was packed by then on a Friday night.  It is an industrial type space, so the place gets VERY loud, so hanging around to chat over beer and food requires a lot of effort.  Not a place I normally go because we like the social aspect of drinking.  It should be an easy fix, but be aware that the walls just bounce sound.  I did notice that the upstairs was a lot quieter.  However, there is very little seating considering the size of the space.  They did have cornhole and a few other games inside which took up a lot of space.  Hopefully the cornhole will move outside in nicer weather and they can get more seating.  They do have an elevator to go upstairs, but it was not operating yet.  If you want a growler refill, it appeared the folks at the entrance were directing customers upstairs since the bar there was less busy than on the main floor.  Sun King does have waiters/waitresses to come around and take your beverage orders.  Our waitress (Deb) did a good job of getting our beer orders to us despite the place being packed.  I am not sure if they will place food orders for you.  Everyone I saw getting food was going to the specific restaurant counter and ordering/paying and getting a vibrating sensor to let them know when it was ready.  They need to differentiate the sensors to match the restaurants as several in my group ordered from different restaurants.  And the beer?  I got a flight which was priced upon the selections.  I really enjoyed the beer, but I always have.  They have a really large variety of beers so it was nice to find a light cream ale for my wife while I ordered several IPAs and a Stout to pair up with the food.  Note that if you want to see what beer is on tap before visiting, be sure to go the the Sun King website and look under the tab "Locations", not "Beer".  I didn't realize that the Beer tab listed everything they can at Sun King and many where seasonal and not available.  However, if you go to the Locations tab and look under the Fishers destination, they had that current listing updated as of that morning.    Parking is at a premium.  We grabbed one of the last street parking spaces just north of the brewery.  They do have parking garages available, but I don't know if they charge or if they are free.  Hopefully someone else will post that soon.  Good beer with a nice variety of food offerings in a large space that could use some sound mufflers and more seating.  But if you like your bars loud and packed, then this is the place to be.  Review #3654

The inventory of this place is amazing.  There are so many gaming and action figures that my head was spinning.  So many cool things for collectors of fantasy themed pieces that I have to admit it is the largest collection I've seen.  However, it looks kind of like a teenager's room when you walk in.  Boxes of stuff clutters the walkways and the place could use a good cleaning.  Maybe that appeals to the normal clientele, but I found it distracting.  I wasn't able to discern any sense of grouping for some areas of the store.     This place could be so much better with a bit more effort to making it organized and maintained.  They have a great collection...it just doesn't look like it.  Review #2082

I stopped in for lunch and had a really good sandwich.  This place is really spacious as I found out by entering from the street level through the Circle Centre mall.  It seemed odd that there wasn't any sign directing me to go to the outdoor entrance on Meridian, but I wandered passed a bar, a billiard/library, bowling alleys, bocce and corn hole areas, arcades and ping pong areas.  I then turned the corner and went passed another bar, dart boards, and finally to the main dining area.  There I was told that I could sit anywhere and the server would find me.  Since I was by myself, I chose not to take up a booth at the main lunch area, and selected a small table in the nearby bar.     For some reason the two people attending the bar seemed more interested in stocking the bar than assisting me, so I wasn't sure if any staff was assigned to take my order.  Finally, someone I assume was a manager came over and took my order and told me the bartender would take care of me from then on.  Within minutes, a waitress stopped by to make sure I was attended to and the next time she stopped by, she said that she would take care of me the rest of the time and she did.  No other problems after that.  It just made me think that I should probably sit in the main area at lunch time if I was in a hurry.   That minor observance aside, the "A La Bama Chicken Sandwich" was delicious.  "Top Chef"'s Hugh Acheson put together the menu and the flavor greatly exceeded my expectation.  The flavor of the white BBQ sauce really accented the sandwich as did the Bread 'n' butter sweet pickles.  The pickles really complemented the chicken far greater than any dill might.   The only negative on the sandwich was that it used shredded lettuce that made the toppings (incl. tomato) a bit difficult to hold together.  The chicken was so moist that the breading it was cooked in steamed loose on one end.  The breading was good on its own too!     The sandwich came with house cut fries that were quite tasty, but maybe a little limp.  Good flavor though with just the right amount of salt for me.  Not sure if they have alternate sides for the lunches.  Note that the fries are served in a cast iron skillet along with the sandwich so I wasn't sure if the pan was hot (it wasn't).   Overall, there were a few minor things that they can do to tweak their service/presentation, but those can be worked out as the staff becomes more familiar (this place opened in late 2016).  The flavorful food was really good and I would gladly return to try some other items on the menu.  Review #218  p.s.  On a return visit, I tried the Sunday Brunch.  Although there aren't a lot of brunch options with independent sides, the options they have were enjoyed by our group.  If you want something light and not as filling, I recommend the Avocado Toast.  Otherwise, you may need a "to go" box to hold your leftovers.  And the service was greatly improved when we sat in the dining area by Meridian Street.

I am relatively inexperienced when it comes to dining on food that originates anywhere between the Pacific Rim and the Mediterranean, so if you are looking for tips on what to order, read Mike F's excellent review.  If you are a newbie like me and want to know some of the basics, then stick around.  I'll try my best!  First know that Lafayette Road is a divided highway north of 38th, so to get to this place is easy from the north, but a bit more challenging from the south.  I suggest heading north on Lafayette Road to Office Plaza Blvd (turn left) and then left again into the strip mall from there.  A frontage road will wind around to the parking lot for Bamiyan Kabob.   Once inside, you can seat yourself.  The waiter was soft spoken and I felt like I had to take charge of figuring out what to do by asking a lot of questions even after letting him know it was my first visit.  I also decided to go with the buffet (which I normally avoid) since it would be the best way to experience a bunch of flavors without committing to a single item.  It was early in the lunch hour, so I felt the food would still be fresh.  (Lunch buffet was about $13 pre tax and tip, but I was able to eat a sample of everything requiring 2 plates and a bowl.  You won't go hungry if you like the food at all.)  I let him know I was going to eat from the buffet and wanted a water which showed up at my table along with a basket of naan (flatbread that was quartered and is used to assist eating some of the saucy items in the buffet.)  Comparing the photos on Mike's review along with the items I found listed let me know that they have a lot of options here and so you just have to go and see what's available each day.  I grabbed a plate and utensils and decided to work my way down the buffet (I took pictures of the food and names above the trays to help me identify them.)  I got about half way through the buffet when my plate was filled, even with smaller portions.  There is a LOT of food here!  I noticed that some of the food was quite familiar, while others were completely unique to me.  Some had potatoes, or beans, or peas with chicken or rice.  Others were just sauces or purees that were a bit harder to identify.  What I will say is that everything had a lot of flavor.  They aren't afraid of using spices here and a wide variety of them.  What I really liked was that I didn't find anything that was overwhelming with a singular spice;  Nicely balanced dishes that I was able to enjoy, sometimes by tearing off pieces of the naan to mop up the plate.  I won't make recommendations other than to suggest just trying them for yourself.  I went back and got a second plate from the stack and nearly filled it too. My first plate and silverware were removed while I was at the buffet, so be sure to grab more napkins and utensils while up there.  My second plate had more of the meaty selections.  The "fried chicken" item had good flavor, but did get a bit dry.  I also wasn't a fan of the Goat Kata-Kat (Liver).  I could tell it was liver even without reading the sign since it had that dry texture that liver can get unless prepared by some master chef.  I wouldn't try that one again.  Of special note is the rice.  They have three kinds here and if you settle for just the plain rice, you will be missing out.  Both the Afghani Pulao and the Sindhi Biryani (both with chicken) were delightful and looked so colorful that the plate just looked more appetizing.  I also tried small samples of two unidentified desserts that were on a side buffet.    When finished, I wasn't sure what to do, but just walked up to the counter and the waiter rang it up promptly.  This is probably my most enjoyed buffet that I've been to.  I was surprised by how many items I liked.  If you want to dive into experiencing a new cuisine, give this place a try.  I was able to get in and out quickly, so don't let time be a constraint on checking in.  Review #2627

For fans of the distillery side of the Quaff on/Big Woods business, it is nice to see this expansion of the ultra cool Hard Truth Hills in Nashville, IN have a place to distribute both the liquors produced as well as the brewery items from the same location downtown.  Since our state is not very good at making the alcohol industry beneficial to the companies that make beer, wine, or liquor.  Archaic Rules, some dating back as far as Prohiition, impede the progress of new businesses.  In this case, customers can get tastes of beer, or liquor, but they can't get anything to go!  They have to get a special license to be able to sell bottles of liquor to customers who would prefer to drink in the comfort and safety of their home, instead of drinking on site and then calling for a ride.   I have several bottles of the Hard Truth liquors that I find quite good (from the main campus in Nashville, IN).  However, after sampling a taste of one of their newer products, I was unable to make  purchase to take home until their license comes through.  I thought we were supposed to be a "pro business" state, but you can hardly tell by all the red tape out puritanical "leaders" haven't bothered to address.  Not like businesses have had it tough the past year on their own, but when an existing business has already been licensed elsewhere in the state, it seems ridiculous to tie things up requiring more licenses.  Oh, well, I guess I will have to head to Nashville to pick up the new flavor.     Other than the inconvenience of not being able to make a carryout purchase yet, I will say that the gentleman behind the bar was very courteous and helpful.  The beer I tasted  was also quite good.  If you have patience, you can wait until the paperwork comes through for carry out sales.  But if you are able to enjoy a beverage on site, they do have plenty of beer and an impressive list of cocktails using locally produce liquor.  Although they don't have food on their own, there are plenty of vendors set up in the neighboring stalls of the Garage Food Hall.  Review #3843

My wife and I decided to get out for lunch to a  new franchise restaurant that opened Avon.  Not only do they carry a wide range of wines and flights to chose from.  They have delicious options for lunch and dinner.  The interior is spacious with table eating and bench seating.  Rev #3984.

I have been working my way through the Yelp Top 50 and decided to take a road trip to Fishers to give this restaurant a try.  So glad I did!  I stopped in for lunch and ordered a couple appetizers (Gyoza and Egg Roll) to go along with my entree, the Hibachi Scallops.  The entrees come with a choice of Miso soup or salad, loads of fried rice (with yum yum sauce), and lots of colorful grilled veggies.  The soup came out first and I must say this was the most delicious Miso soup I have ever had.  Many places serve a bland Miso that does not add to the experience.  Here, the soup had another level of flavor that I can only describe as being a somewhat acidic layer that reminded me of how fresh pineapple can add a layer to country ham.  Whatever they did, it was great!  Soon after I finished, my gyoza showed up.  Though smaller than some other places, this chicken stuffed noodles were just about bite sized (okay, a big bite and some folks might cut them).  The dipping sauce was a great complement to the taste.  I would definitely order these again.  While eating the gyoza, my egg roll came out.  Of course, it was deep fried and the ingredients in the middle held quite a bit of heat, so it was good to let it sit a little while before dipping it and giving it a try.  Interestingly enough, there was a little bit of ground beef inside the roll to go along with all the veggies.  The plates that they use have a little corner that holds the special dipping sauces and are a little small to fit the end of the roll into, but I managed to get enough sauce by angling the roll to get enough to taste.  The scallop entree was generously filled with 6 scallops on my visit.  These were seared on the flat ends while staying light as a feather in the middle.  A light sauce (like a teryaki) added a nice flavor element and a bit of saltiness to the course.  Very good!  I was surprised that there was only one waitress/cashier running the front end of the restaurant.  That meant covering the tables outside as well as in.  This gal was hustling from the minute I stepped in and did a great job of not making anyone wait too long.  Positive attitudes from both her and the chef who was working on some sushi across the counter from where I was sitting made my solo visit much more enjoyable.  I have been to some restaurants where they had a more traditional Japanese decor, but maybe this reflects contemporary Japan more than a Midwesterner's perspective of Japan.  I also was a little surprised that nice bowls and dishes were used for the appetizers, but paper plates were used for the entrees.  The paper was sturdy enough to do its job, it just looked a little odd.    So, if you are in the Fisher's area, know that you can get a tasty and hearty meal with very little wait time from this restaurant.  Review #362

I took my wife to Brugge on a Thursday morning for lunch.  We found a parking spot on the north side of the building and because it was early, we were able to pick a spot.  We decided to choose the patio, which is shaded.  What became apparent immediately was that the patio didn't fit my expectations of a "French" restaurant.  Instead of having a certain flair, we sat at a wooden table on a bare concrete slab.  The supports for the upstairs balcony were rusted and needed painting.  Not that it affected the food or beverages, but it was a bit disappointing.  Anyway, we had pleasant interaction with our server.  Our food was brought out in a relatively quick manner as well.    Since it was my first time here, I decided to go with a flight of Outlier Beer to get a sample of what the brewery side of the business had to offer.  I ordered the Madeline la Frambiose (brown ale), Mayfly Farmhouse (Saison), and Pooka (American Wild Ale).  All seemed to have a good deal of flavor, but the flavors weren't my favorites.  There are other breweries around town where nearly anything I have tried is something I would try again.  Maybe it was my choices, but all seemed a bit too sour for my tastes.  My wife ordered the Scrambled egg crepe with roasted tomato, beer glazed onion, & Swiss Cheese.  It was generous in size, but the roasted tomato was a lesser player in the flavor.  In general, the crepe was rather bland.  She asked for salt about half way through, and that seemed to help.  Still for $11, you expect a crepe to have more "wow" factor than what you can get at a brunch.  I went for the Duck Confit - dried cherry, lambic compote, spicy mustard, crispy fried leek with a side of Frites.  I selected the garlic aioli sauce and the "Popular and Dijon" sauce for dipping.  Like my wife's entree, I thought the sandwich lacked much flavor.  The Duck was tasty and moist.  The bread had a nice flavor, but the additional components were barely noticeable.  The bread was thickly sliced and masked the mustard and compote.  The leeks were not crispy.    The highlight of the meal was the frites.  They are as good as everyone else has posted.  They come with a sea salt and black pepper seasoning that finally had "wow".   I also thought the dipping sauces were very tasty.  The "Popular & Dijon" had a sweetness to go with the savory of the dijon.  I added some of the sauce to the last half of my sandwich and that made a huge difference.  I wish I had figured that out sooner in the meal.  So, although the food was okay and the service was attentive, I can't say I would drive 45 minutes again.  Review #76

Although it was one of the few nice days we've had this winter, the line waiting to get into the car wash was managed well.  This place has four lanes leading to the car wash that have what looks like a "toll booth".  Before passing into the single lane feed, you make your wash option selection and pay and then proceed to the toll gate.  When it's your turn, your gate goes up which eliminates the bottleneck of merging from four lanes down to the one.  Great idea!  Before long, I snaked my way around the south end of the building and was soon going through the car wash.  I like that they take time to do a bit of prewash and scrub before entering the actual process.  Pretty much standard operating once you enter:  Steer onto the track, throw it in neutral, and take your hands off the wheel and feet off the brake.  Before long, I emerged when I got the green light at the end where I could then either leave the site or pull into one of the many vacuum areas for cleaning the interior to match the outside.  It's not cheap, but it is a time saver and although my car wasn't completely spotless, I knew I felt safer on the streets having clear views out my windows.  Review #490

This regional bar & restaurant chain has a little bit of everything:  It's a bar with two separate dining/bar areas; games for groups of friends to play; and a menu with burgers, sandwiches, sushi, and even stuff for kids.
