I stopped in before catching a movie and decided to keep my meal light.  So, I ordered edamame and an eel roll from the front bar.    The edamame was generously portioned and still warm, but the salt was only sprinkled on the top layer.  So, some of the beans had more flavor than others.    The roll had eight pieces and was delightfully good.  They offered soy sauce and chopsticks as options with pickled ginger and wasabi on the side.      Everything was brought and cleared in a timely manner, but as I was finishing, the bartender disappeared to the other room and when she returned, I couldn't get her attention even though there were only two others seated at the counter.  I finally made eye contact and was able to get processed promptly after that and was able to catch the start of my movie.    They have a nice parking lot with lots of room for customers and when traffic is heavy (as it often can be near KatC), there is a traffic light to make pulling in and out of the lot less stressful.    I liked having the option of grabbing a light meal with a relaxed atmosphere and the option for grabbing a drink if I choose.  Review #568

Wow, what a difference the addition of a remodel and picking up a new chef can make!  I hadn't been to Cobblestone in five years after having an unremarkable dinner.  Other than the patio (very nice dining feature), there wasn't anything to draw me in.  So when I heard it got a much needed makeover on the inside and added Chef Jeremiah Clark (Stone Creek - Noblesville and Mesh of the CRG family), I decided to take my wife out for lunch while shopping in the area.  The interior is now cool and sleek instead of the out dated crowded place of the past.  They kept the patio option too, though it was a bit chilly on our visit to sit there.  More room and excellent service made this an enjoyable visit.  As for lunch, my wife went with the Chef's Special of the day, the pork tacos.  Three tacos were served with green tomato salsa, cilantro, onion, and limes.  Nice flavor and plenty to eat.    I went with more traditional Hoosier fare:  the Breaded Tenderloin.  My serving wasn't gigantic, but plenty for a sandwich.  I thought the toppings were fresh and really paired well with the meat.  However, the meat was a little over cooked and one end was noticeably tougher than the other.  The breading had a nice crunch to it, but was either unseasoned or only lightly seasoned.  I could taste the pork as the dominant flavor on the bits that extended beyond the bun.  So, it was a different initial taste than I have come to expect since most places add lots of salt.  I will say that once I got to the pork that was on the bun area, the flavor combo with all the toppings and the increased tenderness was really good.  (Seasoned sweet potato chips came as the side and tasted almost like barbecue chips.  Overall, it was a pleasant experience with the friendly staff and good food.  I definitely had a much better experience than my previous visit.  Review #419

I was pleasantly surprised when I returned to the Aristocrat Pub & Restaurant after a long absence.  On a cold December morning, I found a convenient parking spot in the lot behind the building (yes, a private lot in Broad Ripple!)  The seasonally closed front patio was festooned with lots of holiday decor.  Once I stepped inside, the warmth of the place took the chill right out of me and I felt welcome.  I decided to go to the pub side of the business.  Lots of rich wood and posters and paintings from years gone by gave the place the feeling of an old British pub.  Above all the decor, several silent televisions had mostly sports themed programming on air.  I decided to keep my order simple by going with "The Aristocrat" burger and selecting the coleslaw instead of chips as my side.  The burger was one of those thinner patties (probably 4 or 5 oz) and I was asked how done I wanted it.  It came with my choice of cheese and I could also get mayo, tomato, red onion, and pickle.  There are bottles of ketchup and yellow mustard on the table as well.  The coleslaw was a lot like my Mom used to make:  Somewhere between sweet with a bit of juice and the creamy style.  The slaw looked to be about a half cup serving.  The burger was very much to my liking.  It's the kind I usually prepare at home.  So, fine execution of the dish, just nothing available to make it unique or inspiring to my taste buds.  As I said before, I felt welcome in the nostalgic atmosphere where it was so quiet that I could actually think and hear the murmur of other diners in the pub.  The background music was at a level that was pleasant, not intrusive.  Service was friendly and I was able to get my water topped off and my bill processed quickly.  Nice to know that somethings hold up even after several years between trips.  Review #470

At a local gathering of food trucks this morning, I split an order from Serendipity Mobile Catering with a friend.  She ordered the "NorthEast" which is two crab cake minis with roma tomato, red onion, romaine lettuce, and topped with a roasted red pepper aioli on toasted gonella buns.  The sandwich should have been called a "slider" because there was enough aioli to cause the ingredients to slide to the side while being carried to our seats.  All kidding aside, the flavors worked really well together.  The crab cake was moist, though I have had some elsewhere that the crab was more prominent in flavor.  Still, because the flavors balanced so well, I found the sandwich quite tasty!  Review #85

This new addition to the ever growing collection of Mass Avenue eateries is one you should check out.  Don't be scared off by the construction going on next door.  The food is worth any difficulty you may encounter finding parking on one of the neighboring streets.  The restaurant is just north of Bakersfield and immediately you will notice they have built out a patio in the area that wasformerly three parking spaces.  That should add to the number of customers who can be served as well as giving another option for enjoying your dining.    I sat at the central "bar" where smoothies are made and lots of pastries are on display.  I was greeted immediately and found the staff to be very personable and informative.    I selected the 'tucky sandwich.  The menu only mentions a sandwich, but mine came with a house salad and a "hash brown" which looked like a mashed potato ball that was deep fried (it was browned all the way around.)  So, although the price looks a bit on the high side of price, you get a whole meal.    The sandwich itself was totally delicious!  The 'tucky is generally described as a ham and cheese.  The ingredients lift this sandwich to another level.  Yes, the country ham is thin sliced and plentiful.  Yes, the baguette (conveniently cut in half) is fresh with a perfect balance of crunch and chew.  The pimiento cheese adds a richness of flavor that pairs well with the ham.  It also comes with chow chow, pickled mustard, and collard greens.  If you like the taste of sweet pickles, these other ingredients will remind you of that combo of sweetness and acidity.  The collards also lay flat instead of in chunks like pickles, so the sandwich isn't as tall and becomes easier to eat.  Although the sandwich is loaded with flavor, it isn't overloaded like some places where the ingredients fall out, i.e. messy.    This is a place I will definitely bring friends to try out.  I was in and out of the restaurant quickly enough to fit into a designated lunch hour (if I still had those!)  Review #248

While waiting on the west side, I stopped in to pick up lunch, wanting to be sure I had enough in case my wife wasn't able to catch lunch that day (4-28-16).  I noticed a few seats available in case I wanted to eat while there, but decided to place an order of Broccoli Beef and fried rice to go.  I also asked for orange chicken and for an order of crab meat rangoon with sweet and sour sauce.  After a brief wait, my order was delivered.  From the counter, you can see each meal freshly prepared.  The portions were generous and the taste was pretty much as expected...an Americanized version of Chinese food.  Very agreeable flavors for traditional palates.  I didn't order anything that would let me discern a difference from this restaurant and one of the chain restaurants like Panda Express.  So, for me, I would say the two restaurants are interchangeable unless you have a desire for something more exotic.  (I did notice a much larger number of options available from Peking.)  Review #18

I dropped in for lunch on a Thursday (4-14-16) after seeing Tropicalismo make the Top 15 new restaurants of 2015 in Indpls Monthly.  The restaurant is located on the north end of a strip mall, so there was plenty of parking, but minimal effort of creating any atmosphere.  Basically, some music and a large mural were the most significant contributors.  As I walked in, I couldn't see anyone in the place except working back in the kitchen.  I finally was able to get someone to greet me who seemed to have very little command of the English language.  So, I sat myself and received a nod.  I placed an order for Empenadas to start with and then the Costillo a la BBQ which came with white rice, a small salad, and beans.  For an appetizer, there were three Empenadas (enough for an entree) along with some delicious, but unidentified dipping sauce.  The turnovers had a pulled pork center and the dipping sauce was very complimentary to the flavors.  The ratio of pastry to meat was a little heavy on the pastry side.  The barbecue was okay, but nothing unique or especially tasty.  The beans were heavily seasoned (more than I would like) to the point where the bean flavor was minimal.  The salad and white rice were basically flavorless.   To sum up, I was hoping to experience some unique and delicious flavors of another culture.  I came away disappointed and wonder how the restaurant was staying afloat.  During the entire lunch, not a single customer came in for seating.  Only a single person came in for an order to go.  Review #29

I stopped in for a late lunch at this first franchised expansion of a restaurant based out of Trafalgar.  As the name suggests, there is a rustic/southern decor in this narrow place.  There is a small patio with seating in front of the restaurant, a small dining and order counter in the front, a row of bench seating tables along the left side and the kitchen along the right.  An ice cream display case is located near the kitchen.  I placed my order at the counter on the right.  They have a menu overhead to assist in making choices.  I went with the breaded tenderloin on my choice of bread, paid at the counter, received a receipt with an order number, and seated myself in one of the booths.  Before long, my number was called and I picked up my plate at the order window about half way back on the bench seating side.    The good:  The tenderloin was a decent size and thickness.  It was mildly seasoned with a nice flavor and served steaming hot.  The fries were hot and plentiful too.  The table had salt, pepper, catsup and mustard, so I was able to apply those myself.  The odd:  My tenderloin looked more like a pork chop and had a chop type texture instead of the normal tenderloin that has been pounded for tenderness.  I kind of liked the texture, but it was noticeably different than any other tenderloin I've had.  The disappointing:  The cook didn't take enough time to drain the vegetable oil from the tenderloin because there was a small amount pooled on top of the meat.  I used one of my napkins to remove that so I was glad that the sandwich was served with the top on the side otherwise I might have missed it.  Also, the tomato was not ripe and was sliced too close to the stem end which left the center hard and white.  I cut the center out and the rest of the tomato was okay.  My sandwich was the only order at the time, so it wasn't a case of the kitchen being swamped.  It was simply an oversight that a chef would have caught before serving.  So, although the food was pretty good, I will have to rate them three stars for the oversights that came from the kitchen.  Note:  They don't have tap water available, so if you want water with your meal, it will cost you $2.49, the same as a soda.  Review #1091

This enormous city park seems as large as the other 150+ parks in the city of Indianapolis combined!  With a history that goes back to early in the previous century, the land has passed through numerous owners including Purdue University, the Lilly family, and eventually the city of Indianapolis.  This is the only city park in town that charges an entrance fee (less for Marion County residents than for other visitors).  The original vision of the park was that it was supposed to be self-sustaining because the city could not afford to take on the cost of maintaining the park at the time it was donated.  On my most recent visit, I decided to hike the three mile Blue Trail which loops around the north end of the park.  The trail was voted the best nature trail in Indianapolis by Indpls Monthly magazine.  About half the trail is through the woods.  The elevation change is relatively mild and it makes for a pretty easy hike for that distance.  Along the way are some exercise stations along the northern side of the trail.  The wooded path is generally broad and easy to navigate, though there are a few small sections where erosion has affected some of the footing.  About midway around the trail, it passes Lilly Lake and several shelters and playgrounds.  I found a living tree that had a dead center and made it possible to see completely through the middle.    Crossing one of the roads on the second half of the trail leads to a more steep ascent to overlook the reservoir.  The trail markers are not as reliable here, so I highly recommend picking up a map from the guards at the gate to help you stay on course.  The red and blue trails work their way down to near the reservoir and traverses a narrow section of land between the reservoir and a lake that is a bird sanctuary.  The path isn't very wide and during my visit, was only about a foot higher than the water levels, so be advised that passage may become difficult after heavy rains.  The only negative was that the north end of the path above the bird sanctuary is rather boring as far as scenery.  The path is wide and may have served a different function at one time from which it hasn't recovered.    The hike was relatively easy other than the one section and since it was a beautiful day, made for a pleasant trip seeing forest and bird sanctuary in one trip.  Review #833

This theater is undergoing changes that I hope will make the experience of going out to watch a movie more enjoyable.  Although the construction/remodeling is ongoing (temporarily cutting the number of theaters to 9), the completed half is noticeably improved.    Theater 5, for example, has reduced the number of seats, but several rows of recliners that allow the patron to select the amount of incline for comfort.  They have installed half walls between the landings so that those who recline may do so without affecting the people behind and above them.  Also, there is enough room to get passed anyone who is already in the fully reclined position (unless someone has extremely long legs!)  The restrooms have new signs and have installed dividers between the urinals for more privacy.  Also, the paper dispensers have been replaced by hand dryers.  This keeps the floor clear of paper towels from patrons too careless to properly dispose of the paper.  They have added multiple (6) automated ticket dispensers positioned on the counters that are fairly simple to understand and use if paying by credit card.  Yes, they still have a live person dealing with their club (Stubs) members if those movie goers want to interact with humans instead of machines.  We really enjoyed the experience.  So why do they only get four stars?  Because in each of the last two experiences when I first became aware of the new ticket dispensers, the human failed to advise people standing in line that the ticket procedure had changed and they could help themselves. It took a manager to come over in the first case to make an announcement.  The young man who was running the Stubs desk failed to say anything which I found to be completely irresponsible.  They have also removed the person who used to take your ticket and direct you to the correct theater room.  You have to wait a second time for the human to stop dealing with the Stubs customers so that he can tear your ticket.  Poor communication at the start of your movie experience is enough to make customers dislike the changes.  Fortunately, I went during off peak times when the wait wasn't that long.  But they need to train their remaining employees on customer service or have an additional person taking tickets and advising the folks in line.  There are too many options for theaters to put up with poor customer interaction.  Review #188

The Art & Nature Park is a nice place to go to go for a hike or spend a little time with nature.  The hiking loop is about 1.5 miles around and is fairly level.  The only challenge is whether the water level (the park is a retention pond for runoff from the interstate) floods out part of the trail.  The park is a bird sanctuary as well.  In the middle of the eastern most pond, there is an island that is off limits to park visitors, yet close enough to be seen from the shore.  There is art scattered around the trail, but none of the pieces has information about the name of the piece, the artist, or when it was added to the park.  It seems that if you want to be an art park, there should be some information provided.  The parking lot is on the east end of the park and seems to be plenty for the number of visitors.  Note:  Watch out for the speed bumps on Dequincy as you head north from 21st St.    Review #575

There are some wonderful options available for satisfying your cravings for pastry.  On my recent visit, I avoided the long lines by arriving around noon.  There were plenty of options left to choose from.  So, while I waited, I made mental notes of some of the pastries I was interested in.  Before long, I was helped by one of the staff who walked along the opposite side of the counter with me after I let her know I wanted a small box to go.  My selections included an apple crisp (nice bite-sized pieces of apple inside), cherry crisp (both crisps were glazed with a white powdered sugar based icing), an apple fries roll (more cakey with a cinnamon apple flavor), an iced lemon danish (large with a generous tart lemon center), and a couple of glazed yeast donuts (just because I knew my wife would appreciate them.)  All were quite good!  So, why not 5 stars?  Well, a few things were noticeable.  First, this is a cash only business.  I understand that most of the regulars know that, but I will admit I was trying to keep a running total in my mind on my purchase because I only had so much cash on me.  I could see this being a problem for an early morning customer who was short on cash.    Second, the parking is available in a lot that is on three sides of the business (I think), but the space on the front is kind of tight for backing out, especially if any cars are passing behind.    Finally, the options here seemed to be mostly standard donuts and pastries, with some cakes available.  Compared to some bakeries like the Heidelburg Haus or Gallery Pastry, there options were basic.  Think of it as the difference between a steak house and a burger joint, or a chef and a cook.  Both can have good food, just on different levels.  This place is great at the basics and has very affordable options.  Review #301

I stopped in this new brewery after receiving a text from a friend about how much he liked the IPA here.  He also mentioned great food too, so I was curious.  Imagine my surprise that a brewery that had been open for three weeks wasn't on Yelp!  Well, it is now!    This is a family business with two pairs of related husband/wife teams managing the duties (and also one set of parents too!)  One couple handles the front of the house business while the other couple handles the brewing and the marketing functions.  Although they have a small storefront in one of the industrial strip centers on the southeast corner of 86th and Zionsville Road, the brewery is surprisingly spacious inside.  There are tables near the door and the bar is on the right about half way back.  The house beers are posted on a large blackboard behind the counter and are large enough to read without glasses!  I asked and they have flights of 5 oz beers available in 4 or 6 selections.  They currently have six house brews, 3 are planned as regular/year round brews, while the others may be seasonal or limited editions.  I ordered a short flight of 4 and was happy with each one!  I started off a Marlo (5.1% 27 IBU) amber ale which was deliciously rich in flavor.  Very smooth and yummy...not many beers can say that!  I moved on to the Patersbier (5% 28.6).  This beer was very sweet tasting and was really surprising how much I liked it.  This may be a limited offering, so get there soon!  I went to one of the regular offerings, the Building One (5.8% 34.4) pale ale.  It was very hoppy without the bitterness that some IPA's have.  I call it a great transitional beer if you want to eventually add IPA's into your range of beers.  My final selection was the Kiss my, I'm Roasty (4.2% 29) Irish Stout which was filled with a deep coffee flavor.  Seriously, if you like your coffee strong and black, even when it's cold, you will love this beer.  If you don't like coffee, move along to one of the other options.  The good news is that whenever Traders is open for business, Mad Max Smokehouse Food Truck is ready to serve food to go with your beverages.  The stout went really well with a sweet brisket sandwich I ordered while there.    The staff was really friendly and I got to meet and talk with many of them on my Saturday afternoon stop.  If you want to try beer that is full flavored and very pleasant in its taste, give these folks a try!  Review #803

Although there are four locations in this locally owned restaurant group, I choose one of the farthest from my house to try out first.  At first glance, it struck me as being fairly similar to most large breakfast chains...crowded tables, pastel colors, open dining area.  What makes me have a higher than normal opinion of the experience was the combination of good tasting food and pleasant servers.    The "hotcakes" option that caught my eye was the "Hawaiian"; three fluffy pancakes with butter and sprinkled with powdered sugar, pineapple chunks, and shredded sweetened coconut.  Very good!     My wife got the Western Omelette with hash browns, and as you might guess, the portion was quite generous and though she enjoyed it, had to request a "to go" box since she was full about half way through.  Good food, and as I said, the pleasant service was enjoyable.  The server filled my coffee and offered to go cups for my coffee and my wife's soda.  She was also experienced to bring our bill along with the requested to go box.  Note:  You pay at the front, not your server directly.  One other bonus:  There is a playful mural on the outside west side of the building.  There is another one near the kitchen on the interior.  I like breaking up the plain walls and supporting local artists.  Now, I'll have to check out the places closer to home.  Review #609

I stopped in for lunch on Saturday since I was in the Greenwood area.  Since it was raining, I decided to eat in the comfortably spaced dining area.  Since there was only one person running the front of the business, I placed my order at the counter instead of waiting for her to come to me.    I selected several appetizers as well as an entree.  To start off, I went with the Won Ton Soup (smaller size).  It came with three slightly larger than comfortable bite sized won ton in a clear soup.  The soup itself was delicious, with a bit of saltiness to perk up the flavor.  The noodles were tender and had a pork sausage wrapped inside.  The pork itself was rather one note in flavor...i.e. bland.  It had nice visual appeal and overall good taste, but didn't have any "wow" factor.  My second appetizer was the "Dumplings" which I have ordered elsewhere as Gyoza or "Potstickers".  I went with the pan fried choice because I like how the noodle portion takes on another level of flavor when crisped.  The inside of the dumpling had a combination of a more spicy pork than the soup and some shredded vegetables.  Oh, and the dipping sauce was delicious with its multilevel flavoring.  Highly recommended, this appetizer comes with seven per order.  For my entree, I went with the Broccoli with Beef (I got a free side of white rice with the order). The plentiful portion had nicely cooked broccoli that had a bit of crunch, but was easy to chew.  The beef was thinly sliced and generously sized.  Maybe a tad overcooked, but not beyond reasonableness since the beef always keeps cooking when surrounded by hot veggies.  The sauce was sufficient enough to coat all the meat and broccoli, but was just okay in flavor.  Nothing really stood out about the coating.  The service was courteous and efficient.  The front end of the business was well maintained and clean.  Rev 9

There are a lot of things to like about this place....great movie selection, food and beverage options, plenty of parking.  However, the new "automated" machines that are supposed to allow the patrons to select the movie and the seats of choice, including reclining or standard, have had problems on several visits lately.  From not being able to read any of my cards, to locking up and making me have to find someone to assist, to not having anyone explain the that I should use the machines instead of waiting for a person to help me when they first converted, it just doesn't work very smoothly.  Maybe that's why they run 20 minutes of trailers so that you can be late and still not miss the start of the movie.  I go to a lot of movies and I appreciate that they are trying to bring first run movies, including some "Indies" to my area of town.  I also appreciate that the new improvements in the restrooms and seat selection (in theory) are better than what was there before.    It seems the prices are generally higher than before, but that may be because of the selection of seats I grab. Anyway, I will probably continue to go for the movies that have convenient times that fit my schedule when I am on the south central side of town.  Otherwise, I may just opt for the old fashioned places that have people who can deal with the mechanical difficulties instead dealing with them myself.  Review #219

My wife and I have been stopping in at Kirkland's for years.  I remember seeing this cool store when it was inside the Greenwood Mall.  Now, it has its own space in a strip mall with parking in front and a pick up door for large purchases out back (i.e. no more hauling things through the mall!)    We stop in here for a number of reasons.  Whenever my wife wants to change the decoration in a room, she usually stops in just to see if they have a piece or two that may finish the look, add to the appeal of the room.    On other occasions, like today, I was in the area and realized I hadn't been in for awhile.  They turn over the inventory frequently, so it seems that there is always something new to look at.  Yet there is still a familiarity when I walk in.  There is a lamp section, an art section, pillows and candles and lots of knick knacs and clocks.  There are also groups of unusual things, some of them seasonal that are new each time.  I guess the appeal is that no matter how often we go, we find something new.    And even though we don't make purchases with each visit, it always makes us consider the possibilities.  Review #328

The tap room opened late in 2016 and looks great! There is a space theme that perks up the industrial look of this shotgun style building.  Although there is no food sold in the taproom, there are some tasty options in the area that you can grab something on your way here. Free parking is available about a half block south of the taproom in the municipal lot.    The beer options in the taproom had five Planetary brews available and three guest taps.  The flight of six options has a great price of $10.  I enjoyed all the brews in the flight.  The Chemtrails Cream Ale (5.6% 16 IBU) was a nice starter to ease into the flight.   The Strange Planet Java Mint Stout (5.8% 24 IBU) was full of chocolaty flavor. I am a big fan Belgian Tripels, so the Hovercraft (8% 34 IBU) was my favorite of the flight. The Vostok 6 Russian Imperial Stout (8.5% 64 IBU) was robust and had lots of flavor to temper the higher IBU. Although I am not a fan of IPA's, The InterPlanetary Ale is an English IPA (6.5% 60 IBU) so the hoppy flavor comes through without the smack in the face you can get from American hops.  I also tried a guest selection from Burn 'em Brewing in Michigan City.  Their 21 N9NE Citra/simcoe Session IPA was a tasty sour/bitter combo.  Overall, the selections were very tasty and the atmosphere was pleasant and during the day, easy to carry on conversations.    Note: The business will expand to include the building to the north, possibly adding a simple grill along with bringing over the small tanks from the original location.  A new 7 tank system will be going in their old brewery site.  Review #281

I enjoyed stopping by this local toy store.  Instead of the towering stacks of over marketed items that try to get kids to buy them through marketing, here is a store that is built with the focus at kid's level.  Kids are encouraged to explore and see what attracts their own interests.  Some items are unique.  Some may remind you of something you had as a child.  There are so many types of toys and games that you wonder how they fit in this shop.  Stop by if you have a kid that is inquisitive or if you want to find something that will encourage your kid's imagination.  A great store!  Review #1175

I stopped by late in the lunch hour and was glad I was by myself so that I could grab the last remaining table:  a two-top.  This place gets points for originality as well as for tasty cajun food and friendly service.  Each table has a tall stand where you can place a laminated card to indicate that you are ready to order.  I was given a menu when I went to take my seat and I saw the card on my table.  It has a list of FAQ and answers to help explain the way service works.  So, read it!  Smooth sailing after that!  The seating is definitely tight so be prepared to squeeze through to find a table.  The tables are secure and I was glad since it would be easy to topple a regular two-top.    After looking over the menu, I placed my card and was promptly greeted by my server who took my order and brought out my drink.  I decided to go with a Po-boy (Breaded Crawfish) and selected to have it served over rice.  (You can also have in on French Bread, in a tortilla wrap, over cornbread, over nothing, and for an extra buck, over a 3 egg omelette!) The Po-boy comes with a house sauce and cole slaw on top unless you specifically request not to.  (Go with it if you love great flavor!)  Mine was fantastic!  I now wish I would have ordered a separate side of cole slaw because it was that good!  The Po-boy comes with three sides of my choosing or for $3, I could get unlimited sides (for dine-in orders only).  I went with the Etouffee (with a little more rice in it), with French Bread (to sop up all the remaining sauce  in the Etoufee), and the bread pudding.  The sides were brought out early so I really liked the Etoufee, but found the bread a little supermarket like.  Nothing special there.  The bread pudding, saved as dessert, was tasty, but was really soggy and spongy.  Not sure what was going on there.  Overall, you have to see the place to appreciate how unique it is.  Give this local place a try!  Review #631

I have stopped in twice in the last three months because I have a knack for finding nails to run over.  In both cases, service was given in less time than than the initial estimate was projected (the business was very busy on both occassions.)    Even though I am still driving on the original (dealer) tires, my tires were filled and repaired for NO CHARGE!  Talk about paying it forward to the customers!  Earlier in the week, my wife needed new tires for her vehicle and she was very pleased with the quality of service and the wait time for the installation.  She has raved about how smooth her car now rides with the new tires.  I am very pleased to support this neighborhood business that provides quality materials and service to its customers.  Review #121

I stopped for lunch in this restaurant in the relatively new Kroger shopping plaza south of Greenwood.  Plenty of parking makes it easy to get food to go or dine in.    The space is relatively open with dining on each side of the entrance and the counter to the rear.  They have lunch specials as well as sushi rolls and entrees, Chinese specialties, noodles and fried rice, Hibachi, and Teriyaki options.    I opted for a lunch special of 2 (six piece each) sushi rolls for about $8.  They have 18 types of rolls to select from.  For me, the Eel Avocado roll and the Godzilla roll appealed the most.  After paying at the counter, I grabbed my chopsticks and napkins from a stand on the right side and helped myself to the beverage dispenser.    After about ten minutes, the staff behind the cash register brought out my order.  Very colorful and full of flavor.  No skimping on the sauces and toppings.  I especially liked the Godzilla.  It was huge in circumference which always causes me to have the dilemma of looking awkward fitting each piece in my mouth or biting it and loosing the structural integrity of the wrapper.  Just a hint of heat even without the side of wasabi.  The Eel Cucumber roll was a much tighter roll and easy to pick up with the chopsticks.  The ingredients were fresh and I liked the addition of soy sauce for dunking to add a bit of saltiness to the roll.  Overall, a very solid lunch option for those who want made to order sushi!  Review #412

My wife and I decided we wanted to go out on Thursday evening, so we decided to make a short trip to Greenwood and stop in this restaurant that is tucked away in the middle of a strip mall.  Parking was available right outside the entrance.  We were seated in the colorful dining area and an employee brought over our menus and brought our beverages promptly.    We ordered several appetizers to get started.  The Egg Drop Soup was really good.  I don't have a lot of experience ordering this out, but this was the best I have had.  It had a thicker consistency than I am used to and had plenty of egg flavor.  (The negative is that the menu lists pint and quart sizes available, while our "pint" looked more like a "cup" sized portion.)  I also ordered an egg roll which was crisp and filled with savory sweet cabbage and carrots. I tried the "Duck Sauce" from the table to brighten the flavor of the outside, but it was rather tasteless.  Finally, we split an order of Crabmeat Rangoon (7 pcs) which were, again, the best I have ever had.  Plenty of crunch on the outside and surprisingly gooey on the inside.  It came with a small cup of sweet sour sauce for dipping.  Before we placed our order for our entrees, the evening rush of patrons arrived who had phoned in their orders.  It was at this point where we became aware of how few employees were on hand to handle the phones, register, bussing the tables, and serving the "dine in" customers.  So, after a few minute delay, our server came back over and took our orders.  My wife asked about the Mongolian Beef which had a "heat" designation beside it.  She asked if the heat could be adjusted and the server stated they could make a "mild" version.  So she placed the order while I splurged on the Seafood Combination plate.  Once our orders were in, the kitchen turned them around pretty quickly.  My Seafood combo was hit and miss.  Some of the seafood were a bit rubbery, while other bites were really good.  The mushrooms and most of the veggies were really pleasant tasting, but the mini corn ears had strong flavor that didn't seem to blend well.  The broccoli was oversized.  Since we didn't have knives in our tableware, I resorted to stabbing and biting the broccoli.  (Not my classiest move!)  And, unfortunately, my wife's Mongolian Beef, even on their mildest setting, was too spicy for her to really enjoy.  She liked the flavor, but the "heat" made her throat burn, making her eyes water.  Granted she probably has lower tolerance for spicy heat than most people I know, but there is no way I would describe this as "Mild".  Next time, she will know to avoid anything with the "heat" stamp, regardless of their ability to adjust it.  So, it was a nice, quick meal that I think would probably fit our lunch schedule better.  They do have plenty of $5 lunches and some $7.15 combos that looked very competitively priced with some of their competition.  Great apps and soup, but could use a bit more front of the house help and fine tuning of the entrees.  I toyed with the idea of only giving a 3 star rating, but the apps were so good that they are worth coming back for.  Review #80

Four of us who like to try new restaurants at every Devour event selected the newest steakhouse addition to downtown.  This is the second Cleveland based franchise to open in the last twelve months (Hyde Park being the other).  Located on the north side of Maryland street between Illinois and Meridian Streets, the restaurant offers patio seating for those who like to people watch, main floor/bar area seating, and additional seating on the second floor.  Parking is usually available for $2 in the Circle Centre Mall if you don't mind the walk, or $10 for Valet service.    As you enter the restaurant, you are greeted by the host/hostess and will be shown to your table.  This is a dress-up restaurant befitting the upscale pricing.  The tables are covered with white tablecloths.  The restaurant has a level three liquor license so you can get cocktails as well as choose from a lengthy wine list.  The interior is very polished and contemporary.  Maybe that appeals to younger patrons, but I prefer the opulence of more classic steakhouses.  Our staff was pleasant and knowledgeable but somehow, did not convey the welcome that I receive from other top end restaurants.  When we go to a restaurant of this level, we prefer when staff finds out if it is our first visit, and if so, guides us through the options.  We were asked what we wanted and once we mentioned we were there for Devour Indy, there were no suggestions about other options.  When we experienced Devour at Hyde Park in January, that location made it known that anything was possible.  There might be additional charges, but we could feel free to add regular menu items.  Here, when my wife mentioned she would like creme brulee for dessert when all that was offered on the Devour list was doughnut holes, the waiter didn't even respond.  We would have paid extra, but being ignored is not good for sales.  The food:  The Devour list was very limited in options. We were given two options for appetizers (Caesar salad or a stuffed hot pepper), three entrees (they did have a couple upgrades listed for steak toppings), and a single dessert.  There was a starter bread course with a fine grated cheese topped with olive oil.  The little plate for the oil was shallow and came with a small spoon which was pretty useless.  Everyone basically had to dip into the same small plate.  The Caesar salad was a nice size and looked pretty standard.  There were no large anchovy pieces visible and the black pepper was added in the kitchen, not at table side.  My friend who loves black pepper thought the salad was great.  My wife, who does not, ended up picking at her salad and offering the rest to me.  Seems like a simple thing to let people get their pepper at table side.  Maybe it was because the booth we were seated in made it necessary for the waiter to reach across the table (he frequently had to ask the couple against the wall to pass their water glasses for refills.)  I really liked the "Brad's Stuffed Peppers".  They use a hot pepper stuffed with house made sausage and covered in a tasty red sauce.  I noticed the heat from the pepper right away, but did not find it too hot.  My friend's wife, however, thought it very hot.  I did think that the sensation accumulated the more I ate.  If heat is not a problem, then I definitely recommend this appetizer.  (The waiter mentioned that the heat is variable depending upon the growing conditions.)  Because we were doing the Devour, I noticed that our entree came with two sides.  Normally, the side dishes are a la carte.  One of my pet peeves with Steakhouses is that some serve the steak naked on a scalding hot plate.  Here, regular plates came with the sides balancing out the steak on the plate, offering color appeal and removing the necessity of spooning from a communal dish.  The steak itself was a really nice sized 8 oz Filet, not some 5 or 6 oz Petite that other places offer.  It had a topping of seasonings (I wasn't able to determine their specifics) that complemented the taste.  My steak was very tender and delicious!  My wife thought hers a bit overcooked from her medium-rare selection, but not so much as to send it back.  For dessert, we were each given two large powdered sugar doughnut holes topped with a drizzle of chocolate ganache.  The flavor and texture were very nice, but seemed an odd pairing following a steak dinner.  (Hence, my wife's inquiry about creme brulee.)  Although the food was generally enjoyed and the service was fine, the experience was not at the same level as our favorite restaurants.  I found it odd that the restrooms are located on the second floor.  When my wife asked, the waiter didn't mention any elevator option to facilitate her access even though she entered with a cane.    Note:  Be aware that a "service charge" (20%) is added to your bill.  Then, if you use a charge card, the receipt will have a line for a gratuity without itemizing the already included charge.    Review #373

I stopped in for lunch (6/18/16) on a Saturday afternoon.  After parking in the lot on the north side of the brewery, I took a seat at the bar.  Although I considered ordering a flight, I decided to go with the seasonal ale "Blond James Blond".  I also ordered the "Biddy" which is an oven roasted chicken breast, bacon, provolone, sliced tomato, mayonnaise, local greens and avocado on baguette with a side of cole slaw.  The sandwich was good although it was tough keeping all the ingredients in between the buns.  The odd shapes of the chicken, tomato, and avocado kept me busy restacking my sandwich (my napkin got plenty of use!)  The cole slaw was sweet and creamy.  Nice flavor when paired with the sandwich.    My timing was bad as I arrived just before a group on a beer tour arrived, demanding most of the bartender's attention.  So, I'll give the service a pass.  My sandwich order came in ahead of the rest, so I didn't wait very long to get my meal.    Overall, the experience was a positive one.  I can see this being a place to bring some friends who can get away for lunch and a visit for awhile.  Review #44

I hadn't been to Yard House for awhile, so I decided it was time to make a return visit when business brought me to the downtown area.  I found convenient parking in the Circle Centre Mall and then made my way outside to the restaurant located on the south side of Maryland Street just east of the mall's overhead crosswalk between blocks.    The staff was very pleasant since the frigid weather kept a lot of customers indoors, so the staff was glad to have us.  The interior was rather dark since they pulled the shades to help keep the heat inside.  They even had enough courtesy to seat us well into the restaurant so that we didn't feel the draft from folks coming in.  Our waitress (Amber) did a fine job of keeping an eye on our water glasses, bringing special requests for lemon & sweetener for my wife's tea, and even making a condiment run for mayo for my wife's Turkey Melt sandwich that was a bit on the dry side.  Note:  When my wife mentioned the dryness of the sandwich, Amber alerted the manager who promptly came over to apologize for the problem and was going to notify the kitchen.  She also offered to replace the sandwich (my wife passed and decided dessert was a tastier option!) and then removed the charge for the sandwich.  That is caring about the customer having a pleasant experience and why I mention it.  It is nice to support places that hire good people to run their business.  I opted for the lunch combo 1/2 sandwich and salad/soup.  My choice was the Roast Beef Dip (au jus) and a Ranch Salad.  The flavor was fine on both items and hit the spot.  Other items we had were the Crispy Brussels Sprouts and Potatoes which came with a delicious Malt Vinegar Aioli.  YUM!!!  I love the roasted flavor and the aioli took it up a notch.  My wife chose the Clam Chowder to go with her sandwich half, and she thought it was very good too.  And her dessert option, a mini creme brulee with banana slices tasted good, but didn't quite get enough searing of the sugar to make a nice crust on top.  (My wife loves that crunch of the sugar paired with the creamy goodness of the brulee.)  So, great service and just a few minor problems with the kitchen reflect a 4 star rating with just a little room to improve.  I would gladly return again.  Review #482

I combined my visit to the Nature Center with one of their frequent tours.  If you check out the park's FB page, there is a listing of all their upcoming events.  I wanted to be able to explore the park (Sanctuary) area that is affiliated with the center, so I selected a walking tour about wildflowers.  Note that the current nature center is on the property of an elementary school, so the center is only open on weekends and select school holidays. However, the park area is open everyday and if you look at the parking lot on the north side of the school, there are three spaces reserved for the park guests.    So, I arrived a little before the tour was scheduled and browsed around inside the center.  You can tell it was formerly a home: lots of small rooms, each with a different function.  There are some with live animals like snakes, a bearded lizard, turtles, & salamanders.  Others have displays of stuffed animals that live in the area.  Some have interactive pieces that the kids can hold and check out.    The staff was really friendly!  Mindi, the county's Park Naturalist was conducting the tour and did a good job of engaging people on the tour and encouraging us to be active participants in the search for emerging plants.  We were throwing all kinds of questions regarding plants, birds, park developments, and anything else nature related and she was able to answer most right off the top of her head.  Very impressive!  The hike/tour was fun, but was slightly altered due to recent rains soaking part of the trail.  We were still able to see most of the loop and get to understand the general layout of the property.  There is a retention pond with a shelter built over the water in the middle of the forest.  How cool is that!?!  There is some elevation change on the trail, but nothing too physically demanding.  Note that the trails are foot worn, not paved.  Overall, it was a fun visit/tour.  I look forward to seeing what else they have scheduled in the coming months.  Review #802

I've been meaning to stop by this place ever since I first heard about them at a Yelp event (which unfortunately was cancelled).  When I had the opportunity to stop by this business just east of Zionsville Road on 79th Street, I jumped at the chance to check them out.  When you park, there is a shared entrance to a cooperative of three businesses here.  The left doorway is for those 21+ and leads directly into Wabash.  It has a few tables and some other seating between the door and the counter to the left.  A nice taplist of house brews featured a full dozen choices this day.  I decided to go with a flight since this was my first visit.  The flight comes with four 5-oz servings for $7.50.  I grabbed my flight and started drinking while waiting on my flatbread from Between Brews Foodwerks on the other side of the shared wall.  I started with the Whitewater Wit (5.2%, 15 IBU).  Nice and light with very pleasant, almost fruitty taste.  Very pale in color.  I followed that with the Mugga Cherry Blonde (4.8%, 14).  This red colored ale had hint of tartness at the start and ended with a nice cherry flavored finish.  Very pleasant.  I moved on to the Working Girl Belgian Blonde (5.6%, 26).  This was the first I sampled with the flatbread and it went quite well.  I am a fan of Belgian hops, so this was another pleasing choice for me.  My final selection was the BaconFace Brown (6.0%, 27).  This was a very solid brown ale, but I was a bit disappointed that I couldn't taste any notes of bacon.  Maybe it was because I had begun eating, but my taste buds were just not able to taste much other than the basic brown ale.  Okay, but not up to the expectation of a name like BaconFace.   So, overall, I was glad to sample so many pleasant drinks in one flight and look forward to my next visit where I can explore some of the dark and bitter options.  I hope that they can eventually upgrade to glass drinking vessels from the plastic cups used in my flight.  Something about the plastic seems to signal a cheaper product than the fine quality I tasted.    Review #499

I stopped in for lunch and didn't even have time for all the fun stuff outside!  But I did have a chance to get something from the new menu and sample a few sips of house brew.  I was very pleased indeed.  I chose the bar for seating and found the bartender to be helpful in making selections.  I tried the hoo-hoo honey ale, a pilsner, and a peach ale, all of which were full of flavor.  I settled on the house pilsner.  For lunch, I opted for the grilled cheese with the sauteed green beans as my side.   The beans came in a light sauce that was delicious and lifted the taste of the beans to another level.  The triple cheese was grilled with a buttery crust which gave it a bit of chew and goo that makes for a fine sandwich.  And the smoked tomato bisque I ordered as an additional side added great depth to the meal.  Besides the smokiness, there was a taste of oregano (I think) that kept the soup from tasting like something out of a can.  Tasty!  Good food and service made for an enjoyable lunch.  Review #181

I had good food and service at lunch midweek.  Due to the inclement weather, the crowd appeared to be rather sparse, but a little wind didn't deter me from parking in the Circle Centre Mall garage and crossing over Meridian St to this new franchise.      I was greeted at the door and given a booth at the front of the restaurant/sports bar.  There is plenty of seating at the lengthy bar and additional tables in the main room.  During the nicer weather, an equally large outdoor seating area is available.    I ordered one of the local draft beers (nice selection) and then went for the "Kalifornia Burger" with a side of cole slaw (chips is the other regular option).  I found the burger to be quite tasty!  Although the avocado, avocado aioli and lettuce have mild flavor, the pepper jack cheese and pico de gallo added just enough flavor to perk up the flavor without overshadowing the flavor of the beef.    The cole slaw was light and had a balance between sweet and vinegar.  It seemed to go well with the burger.      Overall, I would recommend this restaurant and would like to try some of the other options:  Sharable appetizers, wraps, gourmet burgers, and sandwiches.  They have a few desserts and salad options as well.  Review #209

Even on a cold and blustery day, I couldn't help but enjoy my time at this unique gem of a park on the far east side of Greenwood.  Just over a mile east of I-65 at the Greenwood exit, this park is nestled in a neighborhood and has lots to offer.  On the north end, there is a nice lawn area with a paved walking path that I would estimate to be about a quarter mile.  There are very cool looking pergolas on each side with benches near by for resting.  On the west end is Chandler Amphitheater with a stage area on the outside of the path and stone seating terraced into the landscape inside the path.  A few trees have also been planted/dedicated on the southwest end of the lawn for future shade.  To the west of the lawn is new pond for runoff from the neighborhoods that border the park.  South of the pond is fenced dog park with equipment for dogs and owners who want to train them.  And there is a shelter inside the dog park for owners who want to rest while the dogs run to their hearts content!  There is a wooded area with a barely noticeable path along the dog park fence.  It looks like there is every intention of keeping the woods natural.  But hidden within the woods (there is a driveway that leads back to a small parking lot) is a court for basketball and the Big Elm Play Area.  The play area is different from the other parks I've visited.  Sure, it is similar in that it has an elevated area with slides and things to climb on, but it reminds me of a two-angled fort.  There are swings too.  Of course, lots of shade is nearby from the trees surrounding the park just a short distance away.  The park is in great shape (with the exception of the information kiosks which have not weathered well).  This looks like a great addition to the neighborhood and I bet they are keeping it quiet so that they can have free run of the place!  Review #721

I stopped in to sample a "tasting" of the wines on a Friday afternoon.  The tastings consist of five (house selections) samples of both whites and reds for $10.  They also offer "Flights" which are three half glasses of Red ($16) or White ($14) that are pre-selected by the house.  At the time of my visit, the host mentioned that he felt they were still a couple weeks from having all the interior arranged and outfitted like he envisioned.  It felt pretty cool already with a large seating area where the oval counter was located, a small room in the back (east end) and a private room for parties in the middle.  I was told that the intention was to keep the place friendly and comfortable and never become a "bar".  There is no intention of serving food here, but patrons are welcome to bring food in with them or to order delivery.  The winery is actually located in California, but the two local tasting rooms (Carmel has the other) sell exclusively from their own line.  I started with the "Bliss" a Napa Valley Sauvignon Blanc (it turned out to be my favorite, so I picked up a bottle for home!).  I also got to try "Soulful" an oaked Chardonnay; "21 Windows" a California Red; "Grateful Red" a North Coast red blend; and "Zen" a Howell Mountain Zinfandel.  All were vintage 2015 and they offered a nice variety of flavors.  They are still working on permitting for displaying an outdoor sign, so just know that they are on the southeast corner where College and St Clair get bisected by Mass Ave.  Parking is left to street parking (paid), but I was told that a number of patrons Uber or live in the neighborhood and walk over.    One last thing:  Half the profits are donated to charity.  At the end of your visit, they give you a token to place in one of the eight charity buckets.  You can add your own cash to any bucket as well, but it is not pressured.   Review #680

I stopped in for lunch after working up an appetite hiking around downtown.  I had read some positive reviews about Mimi's so I decided to give it another try.  I really like the location and the restaurant has a cool interior.  I have also enjoyed dining on the sidewalk patio which is great for people watching.  I was seated promptly and provided a menu and markers for checking off the combinations of meatballs and sauces, as well as any other items I might want.  They also have a brunch on Sat. and Sun. mornings with another menu, but I decided to stay with the main option.  After asking for some time to review the options, I mentioned that I really wanted to try the Brussels Sprouts and was looking for something to go with them.  My waiter suggested that I go with the special which was a beef meatball that has Bourbon BBQ Sauce as the recommended pairing.  I chose to go with 2 slider versions of the special.  The Brussels Sprouts were very good.   They were nicely crisped on the outer leaves and al dente for the rest of the sprouts.  There were salt and butter flavors to balance the fried veggie taste.  I definitely recommend ordering them.  The sliders were okay, but not like I make at home.  The bread and sauce were fine....it's just something about the texture of the meatballs themselves.  Without any way to tell what the ingredients are, I can't say if it is something in the ingredients or in the way they are prepared.  I have seen several reviews claiming the meatballs were dry.  I think they were extremely lean and lacked any juiciness that a traditional hamburger based meatball has.  Without the juices, my appreciation drops a point. So, even though the taste is good, I just felt that the meal was shy of satisfying.  I have waffled between a 3 and a 4 star rating, but since I really liked the ambiance, the staff, and the side dish, I am going with the 4.  If they can only find some way to keep some juiciness inside, then they could get a higher rating.  Review #123

I recently returned to campus to explore their impressive collection of public art.  Having been a graduate of the university back in 1980, I was amazed at the transformation the grounds of the school had undergone.  Back then, most of the art was confined to the classrooms and to exhibits that were put on by the art department.  Now, there are green ways and a water installation as well as nearly two dozen art installations.   As a fan of bringing art to the masses, I believe the school should be commended for its devotion to the arts.  Only the campus of IUPUI has a more expansive collection than this private school.  In fact, U of I has published a walking tour of the numerous pieces.     If you are a fan of art, plan a trip to visit this campus to appreciate the creativity and artistic expression on campus.  Review #158

There are a lot of things to like about West Fork Whiskey.  As a business, they are adding to the investment in a neighborhood which had seen its hey day come and go, but is now transitioning into something revitalized with lots of new and remodeled homes on every block.  They have remodeled their own building and have provided their own lot in the back (street parking is still available, but the streets are quite narrow.)  Being a distillery, they cannot serve food, but they have a great relationship with Cannonball Brewing across the street and even feature CB's food on a menu.  You can bring your food in as well or have something delivered.  I had read great reviews of the place, and though I am not a whiskey expert, wanted to check it out.  I ordered a flight of three whiskeys so that I could sample the quality of the basic product without depending upon a "product use specialist" to influence the taste.  A flight of three shots runs $8 + tax and tip.  The Colonel is a wheated bourbon and I found it to have a pleasant taste.  All or Nothing is an aged corn whiskey that seemed one dimensional and just not that appealing to me.  3rd Degree was a specialty whiskey infused with cinnamon.  This reminded me of "red hots" candy with the rich aroma and heat from the alcohol.  I could see this one being used in all kinds of tasty cocktails.  The interior of the place was irregularly shaped and has a separate room behind the bar that has a garage door that opens to the outside during nice weather.  During my visit, that room was reserved for a private function, so the surprisingly large number of visitors early on a Saturday afternoon were packed into the front of the bar area which has about a dozen bar stools, and the small public area with a small number of tables.  So, a large number of folks were standing in the walkways between the bar and the tables.  There was a single server behind the bar and he was doing his best to keep up with the flow, but this obviously caused a wait to be served.  In fairness, most people there seemed to be having a good time.  But I am not a fan of densely crowded places, so I don't go to bars after 8 and I don't show up at restaurants on weekends after 7.  Being retired, I like to sit when I eat or drink and don't like being crowded.  I had to wait for a place at the bar to be cleaned before I could grab a spot.   I wish this place well, but it just doesn't appeal to me.    Review #686

Although the number of vendors wasn't large, there were quite a few items that I purchased on my visit.   I found a number of cheeses from Shipshewana.  There were cobblers and pies from Generations Pie Company in Fishers.  I also picked up a loaf of fresh sourdough bread from Circle City Sweets located inside the Indy City Market.  It didn't take long to browse through the place to see what was there, and because of that, the lines were short as people were coming and going the entire time.  That made parking available too.    If you are looking for local products, but don't want to spend all morning doing it, give the winter market a try.  Review #2018

As proud as I am of the city Indianapolis has become in my over forty years living here, I must admit I am humbled by the City's namesake ship and the men who will always be connected with the ship.  While many have heard of the horrendous tale of the sailors who first survived a submarine attack only to fall prey to denizens of the sea, there was also a mission that was completed.  The USS Indianapolis delivered the atomic bomb successfully to a location that was within bombing range of Japan.  That mission, though devastating in its own purpose, saved an estimated 2 million lives that would have died if an invasion of the islands were needed to end the War.  Because of the secrecy of the mission, radio silence prevented immediate help to the damaged (soon sunken) ship.  For five days, men survived as best they could without food, water, and cover from the sun, and shark attacks from below.  The memorial, somewhat shaped like the vessel, includes panels describing the ship on the north side, and the tale of survival on the south.  There is also an etching of the ship on the north side.  Review #1611

This gallery features a different artist or collection beginning each month with the IDADA First Friday gathering.  The gallery shares the south end of the building that houses the Arts Council of Indianapolis (ACI).  ACI coordinates the exhibits which are free to explore during working hours of ACI as well as the evening hours during the First Friday gathering.  (There is limited parking in a lot on the south end of the building and street parking.)    I first became aware of the gallery in late 2016.  As someone who is not schooled in art, but has relied upon my own reaction to whether I like something or not, I have to say that I have had mixed feelings about the shows here.  The gallery is relatively small compared to a number I have been to.  The focus of each show is narrowed, so maybe that is why the theme changes so widely from month to month.  If I had to put a label on what I have seen, I would say that it has been contemporary with some local connection.      Although I still find my interest drawn to art that I relate to (realistic landscape paintings and images with bright color palettes), I will admit that the more galleries I visit, the more I appreciate artists that push the envelope of art.  There was a time when I didn't like street art, but have grown to see that there are grades of quality.  Now, sculpture is one of my favorite types of art when it comes to contemporary design.    The point being that it is easy to dismiss art when you don't take time to actually look at it.  I did my time in the corporate world, and now that I have retired, I want to make time for the creative and positive.  It is easy to destroy, but takes effort and conviction to create something and risk being criticized.  I can appreciate the effort even if I don't like the individual piece.  And that is why I like to visit Gallery 924.    Review #246

This shop has an eclectic mix of gifts, toys, and women's clothing.  Located along Washington Street, there is street parking out front and a shared lot behind the row of businesses.    I found the variety to be more unique than most gift shops I've been to, but familiar enough to be appealing.  Although the shop is relatively small, I didn't feel like it was overstocked and restrictive for movement.  Though I didn't have anything in mind when browsing, I did stumble upon something I had been planning to buy and at a price that was very affordable.  Double win!!  The staff was friendly and checkout was quick and easy.    Review #1121

Here is a nice Chinese restaurant with a wide selection of items at a very affordable price!  I got a pot of green tea, a spring roll, a bowl of Egg Drop soup, and an entree of Sweet and Sour Pork for under $10 (excl tip).  Nice sized portions that were perfect for lunch (and some might want a to go box).    The tea was piping hot and was served in a large pot.  (I didn't finish!)  The egg roll was crisp and hot and had a nice taste.  I didn't ask, but this wasn't like the all veggie egg rolls I've had elsewhere....It looked like it had some meat inside.  Good flavor, but it could use some dipping sauce (I used some of my sweet and sour sauce from my entree.)  The egg drop had an orange color which surprised me since I am used to it being yellow at most of the restaurants I've had it.  The flavor was good and I couldn't discern any spice that affected the color.  The green onions on top were fragrant and definitely gave the soup a savory depth.  The pork was breaded before frying and was topped with the sauce after cooking.  The pineapple chunks were good and the green pepper chunks were served raw instead of sauteed.  Different from most places I've been, but sweet enough not to detract from the flavor.  I went with the noodles as a side instead of rice.  They were light and not too filling.  The waitress was hustling to keep up with all the customers since she was managing the register as well.  She did a great job and had a pleasant attitude the entire time I was there.  She even managed to chat a bit with regulars of which there seemed to be a high percentage of guests in that category.  I was able to easily place my order, dine, and check out in what would be a lunch hour for working folks.  Review #1938

I stopped by here, not because I had read other Yelp reviews, but because it caught my eye when I was heading from Circle Centre Mall towards the Circle.  Because I had already eaten lunch and was unaware that they had paninis and crepes inside, I went in for a smoothie.  I was surprised that there were only a couple patrons seated and only one person waiting to the right of the cashier for her order.  So, I was able to place my order and have it prepared in just a couple minutes.    I decided to enjoy the smoothie called Tarzan and Jane (Banana/Pineapple) while sitting in a lounge area by the cashier counter.  They do have two dining rooms with conventional seating as well.  As I looked around, I saw that to the west (left) of the counter was a hallway that was lined with frozen yogurt dispensers and across the aisle, a bank of crunchy topping dispensers.  I assume they charge by the weight of the finished product.  So, I will settle with a four star rating based upon the smoothie and somewhat low energy of the place.  Next time, I will have to get either a meal or build a bowl of yogurt to see if my rating can improve.  Review #1967

I enjoy going to Pier 1, especially at the holiday season.  Everything is marked down and the store if filled with Christmas accessories throughout.  Beyond the candles, runners, dishes, and stuffed items, they still have some of their furniture and household items making up the remainder of the store.  The staff was friendly and advised me of a further discount I had missed seeing.  Good salesmanship and good savings for me!  Review #1924

I stopped by this new addition to the Carmel Arts District food options for lunch.  Lots of food for the money and everything seemed to be made fresh!  I ordered a gyro on "bread" which came with a choice of fries, or in my case, Greek Salad.  Both were generously portioned and I saved part of what I ordered for later.    I decided to get my order to go although I had originally planned to dine in.  I got there about 12:15 and there was already one couple standing waiting for their food and a place to sit.  The dining area is very small with maybe four square tables.  There are some individual seats across from the prep counter, but those were filled with folks waiting to eat too.  So, I was helped immediately in placing my order but had a roughly 15 to 20 minute wait for it to be ready.  I think part of that is my bad timing, but it is a long time to expect customers to wait without a seat.  I know of one couple that saw how crowded it was and left without ordering.  My advice is that the food tasted good and was a good deal, but try to avoid the peak rush times, like right after noon.  Review #1962

After lunch in Broad Ripple, I looked across the street and saw Nicey Treat.  I recalled several of the Yelpers I follow/befriended had given it great ratings, so I headed over to give it a try.  They have a variety of uncommonly flavored popsicles that can be dipped in milk chocolate or dark chocolate for an additional charge.  I chose to splurge and go with the Strawberry Cream and have it dipped in dark chocolate.    The flavor was quite good.  I believe the dark chocolate has a coconut oil added that helps it solidify.  I could definitely taste the coconut flavor in my treat which surprised me that it was nearly as strong a flavor as the chocolate and strawberry.  Fortunately, I like coconut and the flavors I chose paired well with it. I mention it only for those who choose one of the more exotic flavors that may not pair well.    All in all, it was good, and probably a lower calorie treat than nearby Brics or Graeters.  Unfortunately, I devoured it much quicker than one of the competitor's much larger scoops.  So, for the price, I personally prefer the cone over the stick.  Review #111

I expect a place that specializes in TEA to have flavorful options.  What I didn't expect was a delicious soup, sandwich, and dessert as well!  After driving up the alley from 62nd Street to access the free parking behind the store, I entered the rear of the building and proceeded down the hallway to the back entrance of the shop.  I noticed quite a few racks of shop items and assorted "gift ideas" on the south side of the dining area.  There was also a comfy couch section and a couple dining areas.    The menu consists of breakfast and lunch items, numerous tea and beverage options, and a number of desserts (located on the north wall near the order counter).  I placed my order for a lunch meal which includes the sandwich and a small tea (chips are available.)  I decided to go with the BST (Bacon Spinach Tomato) sandwich on an "everything" bagel.  Everything was fresh and the veggies were colorful.  The bagel was thick and chewy, but not so much as to be difficult to eat.  Just a nice texture that complemented the crispy thick bacon.  Excellent!  I also ordered the soup of the day which was a Loaded Baked Potato:  Wow!  It was so dense that I thought it was potato salad, but was loaded with flavor like a great soup has.  Definitely get this if you go on a cold winter day.  Since I was Yelping, I asked for my free macaron as well.  I chose a Hazelnut that was fresh and tasty too.  Are you seeing the pattern that all the food was great?  And I did try a White Chocolate Blueberry tea that was served in a simple cup on a saucer, but even though it didn't have the color and visual impact of the food, the flavor was great.    The staff was friendly and helpful.  I paid for my order at the time I placed it at the counter and since it wasn't busy, they delivered it to a table I picked out.  Otherwise, they have a pick up area on the other end of the counter.  The napkins and silverware are self help at a small table on the south wall.  Patrons are expected to bus their own tables when finished.    Overall, a delicious meal in a quiet and comfy surrounding.  I definitely enjoyed my visit.  Review #479

This was a nice collection of booths and rooms for browsing.  It isn't as big as some of the mega antique malls I've visited, but it does have a nice variety of items, including furniture, inside its walls.  I was greeted as I entered and did see some things of interest, but didn't make any purchases this day.  It was a a little odd seeing several antiques that I remember having in our home as I was growing up in the 60's...items that were considered old even then.  A bit of nostalgia may have influenced my opinion, but I liked stopping by.  Review #1911

This is a nice shop that carries most of the supplies your pet would need.  What I noticed right away is that it seemed like everything was on sale.  However, what I figured out later (and isn't really mentioned on their website) is that if you become a "member" on their website (sign up for member emails), you get the lower price.   If you don't, you pay full price.  I don't live in the area and there isn't one near me, so I didn't want to give out my email address for a one time purchase.  So, all the items that I thought might be at a really good price were no better than I could get at lots of other places.  If it's convenient and you want to join their club, you will probably like this place.  Otherwise, it's not worth going out of your way for.  Review #2137

It had been far too long since my last visit to Fort Harrison State Park.  Much like I remembered, the park has an easy to follow paved trail that loops around the north end of the park from Delaware Lake to the Duck Pond.  Good for hikers and bikers, the 2.75 mile trail does have some elevation changes, but otherwise, is easy to traverse.  Much of the trail goes by the golf course that is the neighbor to the park.  Being a little more adventurous, I opted to take the Fall Creek Trail from the Delaware Lake parking area.  This trail wanders through the wooded area along Fall Creek with wide footpaths that are mostly worn down to soil, so taking this path is great on dry days, not so good after rains.  The trail winds for 1.1 miles to the north through the Warbler Woods Nature Preserve section of the park.  At its northern most point, there is a series of scaffolding and stairs called the Fall Creek Boardwalk and Observation Deck.  If you don't have trouble with stairs, this makes it easy to stay near  Fall Creek with sure footing.  If you don't like stairs, you should stick to the paved Harrison Trace path.    Fall Creek Trail ends at the Duck Pond on the east end of the park, so if you want to return to the place you parked, then you have to choose between the paved trail or find one of the other trails (Camp Creek) to take you back.  However, if you don't have a trail map with you, finding the unpaved trails is not that easy.  I saw some unpaved trails, but they had no trail markers identifying them (at least none visible from the paved trail.)  I played it safe and stayed on the paved trail, but would probably take the unpaved on my next visit just to be more enveloped in nature.  Although I didn't hike any other trails, the park has an easy 1.0 mile trail (Tree ID Trail) on the south side of the park near the Camp Glenn picnic area.  For those who like more of a challenge, there is a 3.6 mile Lawrence Creek trail loop that explores the southwest area of the park through the Lawrence Creek Nature Preserve section.  The park also features five shelters, multiple picnic tables with grills, playgrounds, a saddle barn, and on the north end from its own entrance, a dog park.  Fishing for those with licenses is available at the well maintained Delaware Lake which features a deck that extends into the lake for reaching deeper water fishing.  The 1744 acre park (including golf course) also has a visitors center, a museum of 20th Century Warfare (both near the saddle barns) and sledding/cross country skiing in the winter months.  Review #831

Located on the north end of the block on Mass Avenue across from Salt and Goodfellas, this place makes a big first impression:  big room, big colors, big sound.  The room has high ceilings with the dining room first and the bar in the back.  Lots of four and six people tables fill the dining area while the bar is set up for smaller groups & individuals.  The walls of the place are covered in street art/comic advertising type murals that are bright and bold in color.  And the sound was cranked pretty loud even at 2 in the afternoon.  Fortunately, I was dining by myself, so I only had to try conversing with the server for my table.  I ordered a blackberry margarita which comes served in a glass jar with lime slices.  They didn't put any "rim" on the drink (not sure if any of the flavors offer salt or sugar rims).  The drink was really good and I would definitely recommend it.  It wasn't made too strong but had a nice flavor balance.  My waitress helped me understand my dining options.  They have multiple menus which can be a bit confusing until you understand.  There were two menus just for the beverages which were already laid out on my table.  Each table has at least one "station" that stores paper towels (napkins), pencils, and the food menus.  If you choose to go with the appetizers or the "suggested" taco combinations, you simply tell your server.  However, if you decide to "Build Your Own" (BYO), it is more like filling out a test:  you put your name on the top of one of the paper menus, the quantity of each type of taco you want to build, and then fill in the circles next to the line item you want to include.  Note that you can build two types of tacos on each sheet.  So, I chose the BYO and wanted two different kinds.  I first selected the type of shell I wanted (you won't believe how many they have until you see the form!).  I then picked the protein and anything special like beans or rice (those are extra).  You then fill in your toppings, cheeses, salsa, and sauces.  The toppings are unlimited, but the others suggest you only get one per taco.  Note that if you aren't sure how a sauce will taste, you can order it on the side by writing SOS (Sauce on Side).  So, basically, when they use such fresh made ingredients, if you don't like the flavors in your taco, that's a You problem since it is what you ordered.  And this process explains why even at 2 in the afternoon that it took just over 20 minutes to get my food.  Most places have set options, so the kitchen can crank those out.
