Here, the kitchen has to read every line of your form (without confusing the two columns) and hope that you filled it out clearly (no partially erased circles or overlapping check marks).  They can't get in a rhythm like other places, so know that this isn't going to be a place to go to if you are in a rush.  Sure, they may get faster over time, but it just won't be as fast as places that don't let you pick.  Fortunately, I wasn't in a rush and the food was worth the wait!  I tried one with the Tequila Lime Steak and chose a fairly loaded taco.  The other, I went with the Sweet Lucy shell (one soft flour outside a corn hard shell with queso and guac for $1 upcharge) and the Tex-Mex ground beef base that was also quite tasty.  It was so tasty that I was nearly finished before I realized that my SOS sauces hadn't come with my meal.  Mark it down as an opening day mistake, but it tells you how good the tacos were that I didn't think them dry or tasteless without the sauce.  That is something I probably wouldn't say at many of the other taco places around town.  The service was hopping even in the early afternoon and was quite welcoming.  Note that if you sit at the front, the kitchen is clear to the back by the bar, so your server may disappear from view for awhile, but that is usually for just a brief time.  They are constantly moving when they aren't taking your order:  checking on the kitchen, refilling water, checking to make sure you don't need anything else.  They had that down.  But the food was brought out by someone else and I didn't see my order form after I sent it with my server, so it was hard to do a check to see if all the ingredients were there.  Overall, I really enjoyed the food and beverages and liked the look of the place.  Just know that it will be loud and the wait will be longer than you would have at other taco places, so plan accordingly.  Review #2465

The Indiana Medical History Museum is a worthwhile field trip for anyone interested in history, medicine, psychiatry, and, to some extent, the macabre.  On the site of what used to be an 160 acre campus that housed 2000 patients with a variety of "mental illness", very few of the buildings escaped the wrecking ball.  Now, the tour concentrates on the Pathology Building which was the center for instruction as well as supporting the testing and autopsy of the patients on campus.      Tours start hourly.  Because there is limited volunteer staff available, the doors are locked between tours. So plan on arriving a few minutes before the start of each hour or you will have to wait outside.  I am not sure if they can take credit cards, so plan on having $10 per adult on your tour.  Know that this isn't something for juveniles since most items are not to be handled.  Cameras are welcome, but the tour guide will tell you about places where cameras are not allowed due to privacy of the former patients' records.    After a brief wait, our group proceeded into the Amphitheater.  This large room served as both a lecture hall and taught through the autopsies performed in the spot where the lecturer would stand.  Students from the Indiana Medical College and from the Central College of Physicians and Surgeons received instruction.  In 1907, these two schools merged with the Ft Wayne College of Medicine and the IU School of Medicine.  By 1910, the autopsies were no longer conducted in the large room since the spread of tuberculosis affected nearly all of the physicians doing the autopsies and contaminated those who sat close to the dissection table.      Of interest in the Amphitheater is the original ice fed water fountain so that the lecturers would be able to get a drink.  Note that students were not allowed to have a drink from the fountain.  A large block of ice was loaded into a cabinet on the back side of the wall and as it melted, made fresh water available in the lecture room.    The next stop on the tour led to the smaller autopsy room.  A smaller room at the entrance held a "body cooler" while the surgeon prepared for the autopsy.  The larger room was sparse for easier cleanup and contained a metal table, a floor drain, weight scales, and a speaking tube where the surgeon performing the autopsy could speak into and have another surgeon on the floor above transcribe the notes.  Each autopsy had four pages of documentation per corpse.    The autopsy room has become a bit of a storage room now.  In there now, you will find donated equipment like an iron lung for youths, an old wooden phyician's chair, assorted wheel chairs of many years, and an odd collection of items that children/people had swallowed and had to have surgery to remove.  In the drawer we viewed, there were mostly an array of buttons and safety pins.  Other drawers had a collection of just about anything small enough to be swallowed.     The next room was the Anatomical Museum where a number of glass jars housed sections of brain traumas and abmormalities.  We were given time to wander through the exhibits and ask questions.  Of note was a "Brain-Slicing Machine".  Wow!  Another point of interest were a student's project of removing an actual nerve system from the spinal cord down to the fingers.  At first, it looked like a sideways tree, but upon closer examination, I could see it was real and had small labels identifying where the nerve sensations would originate.      The tour advanced more quickly through the remaining rooms.  On the rest of the first floor, there was a Chemical Storage Room, a Bacteriology Laboratory, and a reception area. The story of how syphilis was treated before the discovery of penicillin was discussed.  Syphilis' third stage could lead to insanity, so there were many patients on campus who were there due to this disease. Tests were developed there to help physicians identify the disease.  Early treatments included giving Mercury to patients.  That was replaced by Arsenic!  One of the last treatments before  the availability of penicillin was to infect the patients with malaria where the extreme fever would kill off the STD in about 30% of the patients.      The upstairs (sorry, no elevators available) houses the library, Histology Laboratory (microscopic tissue study), Clinical Chemistry lab, Photography lab, and patient records (where the autopsies were recorded from dictation below.)  In these rooms you will hear stories about advances in patient care and perception.  Mental patients were often shackled or kept drunk in the early days of treatment in order to manage their behavior.  Eventually, knowledge and acceptance that these illnesses could be treated and that patients should not lose their dignity and rights as humans prevailed.    The tour lasted about an hour.  In the spring, the tour expands to include the former morgue (repurposed as a 1950's doctor's office) and an herbal garden.  Review #212

Having already sampled Titus donuts (see another review) which supply the donuts to this shop, I decided to try their own baked items including the cinnamon rolls, the cherry fritter, and a small loaf of pumpkin nut bread.  The cherry fritter was huge and really good.  It is definitely shareable and only those who aren't concerned about calories would even attempt to eat it in one sitting.  Just enough cherries to give flavor without making the inside soggy.  Well done!  The cinnamon rolls, which the server said is the house favorite, was large and moist (even on the second day) and had loads of icing.  Though good, I found the icing a bit too thick and overwhelmed the cinnamon flavor.  I also tasted a bit too much salt which was unexpected in a sweet roll.  Sure, some salt adds depth and contrast, but the balance didn't seem right.  Finally, the pumpkin nut bread seemed to be a bit over baked and a little dry.  There wasn't that deep savory pumpkin/spice flavor that I get when I bake it at home.  More bread tasting than dessert.  Just okay.  The store does have a small sampling of artisan products available which was nice.  I picked up some seedless raspberry jam at a reasonable price that I am looking forward to trying later.  Maybe it was just an off day, but the baked products that were made in house just didn't excite me to a higher rating.  Review #1396

Small shop to get a quick deli sandwich on your choice of bagel...pretty simple concept that seems to work pretty well.  My wife and I found metered street parking across BR Ave. and enjoyed our selections.  The shop has a shotgun set up with the order counter on the left and a limited number of 4-top tables on the right.   The extensive menu is on blackboards behind the counter, so when you enter, make your way passed the menu and place your order when you are ready at the far end (there is a sign that says "Order here".  Note that you may have a wait to be acknowledged because they only work on one sandwich at a time.  Just be patient.  When they look up, let them know you are ready and they will get to you.   The menu boards are extensive and have a list of ingredients that they recommend, including the bagel choice.  They have about a dozen bagel varieties which are not listed on the board, but are in labeled bins just below the boards.  When you place your order, let the preparer know of any modifications you want at that time.  Also, since they have clever names for each combination, you HAVE to remember that name because when it is ready, they call out the sandwich name, not yours, not a number, not the ingredients.  Just the sandwich name.  Got it?  While waiting for your sandwich to be made, you can go back towards the front to where the cashier's spot is to grab some chips and, after paying for your options, fill your beverage.  You can go ahead and grab a table then or stand by if you are getting it to go.    I had a Riviera Reuben which is pretty standard for a reuben with the exception that it is on a bagel.  The sauerkraut does have a bit of tartness to it.  The sandwich was good and plenty filling.  My wife had a Ned's Gold Turkey sandwich that she thought was good, but felt the horseradish was too hot/too much for the sandwich.  She isn't a big fan of heat, but likes the horseradish flavor.  So, it may not be too hot for most folks.  They carry Coke products from the fountain next to the cashier's area.  They also have some bottled beverage options along the wall on the right side of the entrance.  Overall, a pretty good meal for a fair price.  Definitely a place we were able to get into and out of in during a lunch hour.  Note to owners:  The ordering process may work for you and for regulars, but from reading a lot of reviews, your process is confusing.  You would probably get higher reviews if you considered making it more normal.  Review #1702

I usually dine at the Jockamo's in Greenwood, but decided to travel to the east side today and grab lunch at this one instead.  The place has a front and rear (parking lot) entrance and is divided into several rooms including the main ordering counter/dining room, and a large bar area to the west.  Since I was dining by myself, I opted for the no waiting seating in the bar where they have some 4 top tables besides the chairs at the bar counter.  I was greeted and had good service throughout the meal.  I went with a lunch special since I wanted pizza (I usually get sandwiches in Greenwood) but not an entire pie.  The daily special was a tasty bacon cheddar slice that was really good.  Because it's thin crust, I was able to fold it, but did have trouble keeping the chopped tomatoes in the fold.  Still, the flavors were nicely balanced and when combined with a small side salad, made for a filling lunch.  Checkout was quick and easy and almost made me wish I didn't have to worry about calories since they have a great assortment of sandwiches and whole pizzas.  Review #2287

I stopped in and enjoyed the three house brews I sampled in my flight.  Being a micro brewery, less than half of their taps were house options.  Since I am not an IPA fan, I went with three house and one guest tap, the Breakfast Magpie by New Day Meadery.  The Dry Hopped Blonde called "Han Shot 1st" was hoppier than most blonde ales (5.2%).  The Scotch Ale was dark and rich (6.3%).  The Gose (4%) was tart and would pair well with some of the food options they offer.  They do have Cuban food available, but since we ate before arriving, we didn't sample it.    There is plenty of free parking in the lot on the south end of the building  (2200 block of east 46th street).  The entrance to the Brewery is on the south east corner.  A ramp is available as well as stairs.  Review #299

If you are looking to try something new that is both tasty and affordable, I recommend stopping by here.  Located in a strip mall on the north west corner of Main Street and Emerson, there is plenty of parking in front of the building.  During the week, they have lunch specials for about $8 and though the portion sizes aren't enormous, there are so many sides that you won't go hungry!  For folks who like to dip their toes in the water, there are numerous options that are familiar if you have sampled other Asian cuisine.  But if you want to jump right in, then they also have some authentic Korean dishes that may be quite different from anything else you have tried.  Since this wasn't my first visit to a Korean restaurant, I went with a dish called "Bulgogi" which consists of broiled, marinated tender beef with vegetables (onions) over rice.  The onions were sweet, the beef was truly tender and both were sliced small enough that they were easy to eat with chopsticks (forks are available too!).  What seems really unique about this experience is that my waitress/owner also brought out twelve small dishes, colorful and arranged in a rectangular pattern beyond my entree.  The dishes consist of a variety of flavors, colors, and heat.  Three items, including Kimchi, were spiced for more heat.  Others, like pickled or prepared vegetables, were served cool and tasting more refreshing.  Some were recognizable, while others were beyond my familiarity.  I ate them all!  The only one I wasn't a fan of was the seaweed dish which was a bit chewy and not that pleasant.    Service was polite and efficient, but not intrusive.  The food was served promptly and I frankly finished dining before running out of ice water, so there was no need to top it off.  There is plenty of room in the spacious dining room.  They have tastefully decorated the walls, a central garden, and the dividers between tables have small characters depicting a variety of jobs.  The restaurant made a very good first impression and I would gladly return to try some new dishes.  Review #830

When we first walked in on a Saturday afternoon (they open at 5 on weekdays and noon on weekends), we loved this place!  It is filled with Christmas lights and decor, lots of fun things to look at, and even the cocktail list looks like a Christmas card.  The space is a wrapped tent with warm air blown in from the west end.  Inside, there are stand only tables, seated 4 tops, and a comfy lounge area in the center.  As you enter, the hostess gives you a menu of the cocktails and another sheet with beer, wine, and snacks.  Note that when you are ready, you go to the counter and should count on an 18% gratuity that will automatically be added to the prices listed as you order.  Once you've paid, they give you a number so that they can deliver your items when they are ready.    While we waited, we looked around at the variety of Christmas items.  There is a "Throne of Lies" for Santa so you can tell him you've been good, though Santa wasn't there when we stopped by.  The cocktails are all listed at $12 and have Christmas themed titles.  I ordered a hot cocktail called the "Bad Santa".  My wife ordered a Snickerdoodle Blondie that wasn't huge, but rich, so it was easily shareable.    The one negative was that they don't have any hot chocolate based cocktails on the menu, though I will give them credit for creating one back at their Plat 99 base bar and running it over.  Although it was a nice try, it didn't really work since the hot chocolate tasted like instant and just didn't work well with the booze.  Nice effort, but if they do this again next year, I hope that their mixologists will work on something ahead of time so that it can be offered on the menu.  Even with that, we still had a fun time.  My advice is if you are planning on stopping by, go early.  They do limit the number of people admitted at one time, so unless you want to risk being left outside in the cold waiting for someone to leave, go early and grab a spot!  It's unlike anything else I've been to around town!  Review #1836

In a clever play on words, Victory Rolls and Baked Goods is a bakery with a distinctive 1940's flair.  From the music playing in the background to the hairstyles (called Victory Rolls) worn by the staff, the atmosphere is a throw back to 75 years ago when winning the Big War was a unifying movement in the USA.  And though they don't serve rolls on their list of baked goods, the name certainly is a short stretch to a reference to the pastries and cookies sold here.  The goods are quite tasty.  I picked up a variety of cookies and Danish, and an apple fritter too!  All were fresh and tasty and moderately priced.  I liked that the cookies can be bought individually and not in a batch of three or more.    To be honest, I forgot to check to see if they sell a cup of coffee to go with the pastries.  I got my order to go and didn't think to check while there.  Parking was easy on each side of the street.  I had no trouble finding a spot especially on a Monday when several of the neighboring places are closed.  I thought there were plenty of options to choose from though the display case is far smaller than some places I've been to.  Stop by and give them a try!  Review #1119

While the outside of the Indiana World War Memorial (the "World" is often left out) is being renovated, it seemed like a good time to visit and check out the inside.  The only entrance now is on the north side of the building at the top of the stairs.  Upon entering, there is a beautiful entryway that has a replica of the Liberty Bell.  Just beyond that is the entrance lobby where you can ask questions at the desk or head down the west hallway to enter the museum.    Along the way, there is a beautiful auditorium that you can look at, but not go on the stage. The detail is gorgeous and shows a level of craftsman that is easy to appreciate.  The museum is now designed to walk you through the lower level of the building, beginning with the battles in the Indiana Territory and progressing chronologically up to the present conflicts.  There are lots of weapons and flags and tie-ins to Hoosier history in each of the sections.    Highlights for me were seeing the recreation of a section of a trench that was key to the battles in WWI; seeing a full sized Cobra Attack Chopper from the Viet Nam War, and seeing numerous Hoosier Heroes.  My only complaint is that the building was originally created for remembrance of World War I, so with every new war, space is appropriated to make room and in my opinion, leaves less for the older wars.  Kind of lost history.  I understand being inclusive and respectful, but lots of small tributes doesn't make it better than one clearly defined subject.  It is still an interesting museum, just not what I particularly would like to see focused on.  Review #1965

For those looking for the Museum at the Soldiers and Sailors Monument (middle of Monument Circle) to find this museum, you are looking in the wrong place.  Back in 2018, the collection was moved to the Indiana World War Monument (431 N Meridian) to provide more display space and to do repair work under the Soldiers and Sailors Monument.  As of the time of this review, the collection has been moved for over a year and my thoughts are part of the review listed on that location.  According to the staff working in the Soldiers and Sailors gift shop (located on the south side of the monument at the top of the steps), something new will occupy the space under the monument once repairs have been completed.  It has not been released what will go in the space.  Review #2581

In the basement of the building just north of Litre House, there is a delightful collection of antiques, vintage clothing, house wares/decor, and vinyl.  The space is very inviting and the owners, including the house Pug will greet you when you arrive.    There are numerous open booths where you may find some beautiful furniture or crystal.  There may be china sets or old toys that you haven't seen in years.    If you are in the area, you can find free parking on the north side of the building.  Fun place to check out!  Review #2157

I read all the great reviews and was really looking forward to trying some pastries here.  I've been tasting pastries all around the metro area lately, so I had high expectations seeing 5-stars.  Frankly, the flavors and textures on the items I ordered left me a bit disappointed.   I stopped in and picked up an Oreja (flat, usually crispy heart shaped pastry), a Peine (a cream cheese filled usually flaky rolled pastry), and a Strawberry Ocho (a double sided spin on a Danish with strawberry on one side and cream filling on the other side.)  What I noticed in the Peine and Ocho was an unsweetened breadlike (think dinner roll) flavor that was a little bit chewy.  The filling and the appearance were great, but the payoff with flavor was the pastry itself being more savory than sweet.  I picked up the Oreja for my wife who loves when she bites the pastry and gets a crunch.  Unfortunately, the one I got was light in color and crunch.  Very little sweetness here as well.    I'm not sure if I caught them on an off day or if this is just their recipe for pastries.  But if I'm on the west side, I think I will drive a little farther to Mama Ines for 5-star pastries.  Review #1472

I've had really good tasting Thai food before, but when you add great service and a fair price, that calls for a five-star review!  When I first got to the restaurant, I had this sense of deja vu...the strip mall has lots of food places including Pho 36 which I have already reviewed.  Because of my timing (lunch on Sunday), there wasn't too much of a crowd and I found parking near the entrance.  Note that if you approach from the east you will have to turn onto the side road just passed the restaurant to pull in since a median divides the heavy traffic on US 36 where the restaurant entrance is located.  Inside, the restaurant looks a lot like many other strip mall places, but the owners have tried to add a sense of Thailand with numerous wall hangings and photos, and some tastefully arranged table flowers.  The tables are glass topped with tablecloths underneath.  I was greeted and informed I could choose my own table going with a 2-top along the left wall.  There was one woman covering the front end of the house and she did a great job:  greeting customers, bringing water, taking orders, checking on the kitchen, and just about anything else that needed done.  I ordered the small sized Egg Drop Soup and my 'go to' for ordering my first time at a Thai place:  Pahd See Ew (or something spelled very much like this since it is different everywhere I go!)  The 'small' soup bowl arrived in a covered dish about the size of a softball and must have had about a pint of soup!  It was served steaming hot, so I had to stir it quite awhile before tasting it. (I find this a common mistake of most restaurants having the soup way too hot to eat right away, especially when most customers want to eat and finish the soup before the entree arrives.)  The soup was not as thick as I've had elsewhere, but truly more soup-like, especially with the veggies, tofu, and mushrooms added.  Still plenty of egg, with a slightly different, but very delicious flavor than expected.    It wasn't long after finishing the soup that my square plate of ornately presented wide noodles arrived.  The plate was about 10" across and was filled fairly close to the edge for a fair sized serving.  In one corner was a "garden" of shredded cabbage and a 'flower' made from a raw carrot.  (I ate them all!)  The entree was ordered with chicken as my protein and at medium heat.  The first few bites definitely were tingling the back of my palate as I adjusted to the spice level, but it didn't get hotter as I ate and I knew I had the right level for me.  What I appreciate was that the flavor of the food didn't get masked by the heat.  The thick, wide noodles were fork tender and were coated with that somewhat sweet and savory sauce that I love in my Thai food.  There were chopped cabbage leaves, slightly larger than julienned carrots, broccoli florets, and 1/8" thick slices of chicken throughout the plate.  Truly some of the best Pahd See Ew I've had!  When I finish a meal, especially when on my own, I usually set my finished plates to the other side of my table and grab my wallet.  The woman who was running the front end immediately brought over my check and since she was paying attention that I was pulling out my wallet, she waited instead of running off so that she could process my bill and reduce my wait time.  I couldn't help but compliment her on how much I appreciated her paying attention.  Truly, great service!  A very satisfying lunch that makes me want to return with guests next time!  Review #2518

I was pleasantly surprised at the amount of items this place had.  There were lots of hobbies represented here.  I think it unfairly categorized by some as a guy's place, but guys definitely can find a lot of interests covered.    Since I am not into all these hobbies, I can't say if the selection is the best, but at least they have items on hand and may be able to help you track down what you are looking for.    I was also glad to see they carried board games and supplies/tools for working on assorted hobbies.  A nice place to browse around and to get ideas if you are looking for starting something new!  Review #1925

My lunch at George's was very pleasant.  I found parking in the shared lot of this strip mall restaurant and was greeted at the hostess' desk.  I was taken to a booth in the dining room (they also have a separate bar area and a private room available).  They seem to have a row of booths in the dining room with many four top tables in the center.  After taking my drink order, I was able to place my order for a Chicken Caesar Wrap (I chose grilled over fried) and a complementary side (potato salad).  The wrap was rolled thick so I needed to squeeze it a bit to get a good bite.  The chicken was in large chunks and stayed moist.  The lettuce was crisp and had just enough seasoning to keep it tasty and bright.  There was a hint of grilled flavor to the chicken which only made the wrap better.    The potato salad is highly recommended!  Instead of thick and pasty, this was light and creamy with bits of red potato and celery which added a nice crunch texture to the side.  Just a hint of sweetness to go with the savory and I will say this is one of my favorite potato salads I've had!  (The meal also comes with a dill pickle spear.)  The service was friendly and offered to refill my drink and got my check processed quickly.  Although there is a lot of space, I will say that I wasn't a big fan of the ambiance of the dining room.  I wouldn't consider it as a place for a romantic dinner....it's rather plain and felt like something you would see for a cafeteria.  It could definitely use a makeover.  I also noticed that the lunch crowd was a lot more senior than most restaurants I've visited.  I'm 60 and I felt young compared to the crowd.  That's okay, but seems to support that the vibe was not "hot and new".  Review #2141

I was walking along the Monon when I noticed this bakery shop.  Now that most of the construction on the Monon is south of them, I was glad to see the shoppe had survived and was open.  The shoppe faces south and is in a row of suites, this one a pastel pink with a pair of wings painted on the garage door by its patio seating.  Inside, there is a small seating area with a couple small tables for customers to enjoy a beverage with their baked purchases.  There is an order counter with displays of what is ready with menu boards overhead with beverage options and prices for the baked goods.  I was greeted and welcomed to the shoppe as the woman emerged from the back room where I assume most of the baking is done.  Very personable and waited patiently for me to decide.   I opted for some macarons (only 3 flavors were available during my visit) and then a cylinder of carrot cake.  I decided to get my order to go.  I was a bit disappointed with the texture of the macarons.  They weren't as "melt in your mouth" good as some others I've had around town.  These were more crunchy and I wasn't expecting it.    However, the highlight of the visit was the carrot cake.  Wow!  I chilled it when I got home and have been eating it just a little at a time since it is a generous serving.  Very rich and creamy icing.  Great spice combo in just the right proportions to be very satisfying.  I had mine with a bit of coffee to offset some of the richness and highly recommend that to other customers.  I'd like to try their pumpkin bread next.  Very friendly service, good/great flavors, and now, an easy to get to location.  Make a point to check this place out when you next are on the trail.  Review #3126

Nice little restaurant on the first block north of the underpass on Meridian.  Though a little bit of a hike for folks working on the circle, it is still close enough to catch some of those customers as well as those visiting the Convention Center.  I stopped in for lunch and they have appropriately sized portions for about $6 which includes sides and complementary chips.  I ordered the Classic Chimichanga with Ground Beef, but was surprised when it came with shredded chicken.  My waitress didn't stop by until after I had decided to go ahead and eat it, so I didn't bother complaining.  The chimi was about 6" which when combined with the beans and rice, was plenty for me.  Good taste and the chicken was moist and tender.  Just enough spice for flavor, but not much heat.  Decent food for a good price (especially for downtown).  Just need to get the staff to check in on customers more frequently.  Review #2583

If you like Caesar Salad, then I highly recommend the Grilled Chicken Caesar Wrap!  Great grilled flavor of the chicken paired really well with the mini salad (including a few croutons!) inside the wrap.  And the portion was generous too!  If you need more than this, they do have some sides, but I haven't tried those yet.  Located in the south east corner of City Market, there is an order window with some of the entrees written out on small black boards.  They also have printed menus on the right of those.  When it is your turn to order, they take your payment, give you a number, and then you wait for it to be called.  I grabbed one of the bar stools nearby that looks like it is from an unused kitchen (maybe they have classes or demonstrations there.)  For dining, you either take your selection to go or haul it up the stairs to the seating that overlooks the market.  This is a place I would gladly return!  Review #2297

I stopped in at Crown Liquors while out shopping in Fishers.  I wanted to get a bottle of Hendricks Gin as a present as well as check on different flavored mixes for frozen cocktails.  This corner store has its own lot and was easy to get into and out of.  Inside, there is a lot of space and I was able to quickly identify the sections I needed.    Not only did they have two sizes of his favorite, they also had a limited edition with more botanicals that was an option.    I also found some flavors of mixes that my local stores didn't offer.  Checkout was quick and smooth.  I don't buy frequently enough to say how their pricing compares to other stores, but I liked the variety and service.  Review #3441

I really liked this new coffee house in Fountain Sq.  Although it is small, it is laid out well and maximizes its seating without feeling crowded.  Lots of windows with live plants overlook what will become a shared patio with Three Carrots in the spring (April target).  Inside, there are bar style seats in the front windows, one communal table for 8 (right by the silent large screen tv), some counter seats where you order, and a smattering of 2-top tables along the window side.    The have paper menus on the order counter for you to peruse.  They also have a small selection of pastries/goodies.  I ordered a croissant (from Gallery Pastry) and noticed they also had rice krispie treats that are made in house.  They also have a sandwich of the day and a smattering of appetizers including a cheese tray.  The array of beverages is impressive. There are beers, wine, & cocktails.  There were Kalita and Carafe coffees, Kaija teas. I wasn't familiar with all the varieties, so I opted for the Cinnamon Plum tea.  After paying, I took my croissant to one of the window tables and waited for my tea to brew.    There was light conversation in the place, otherwise it was generally quiet with the exception of the service taking place behind the counter.  I devoured my croissant too quickly so that it was gone before my clear pot of tea arrived.  It had a bright plum color and had a pleasant fragrance.  The plum was probably a bit more dominant than the cinnamon flavor, but it was quite enjoyable.  I wasn't sure about bussing, so I took my mini tray with the finished pot and cup to the counter when finished.  I think they are still catching up with being a newly opened business.  The menu doesn't appear on their website (I've included photos of what it was during my visit.)  I would also like to see them develop a couple staple sandwich options so that visitors could plan on having lunch there instead of arriving and deciding they may not like the single daily option.  The staff were friendly and did a good job of clearing used dishes and would have cleared my dishes when I left, but I don't like leaving my used dishes on the table..with limited seating, I want to make sure the next customer can find a spot.  They also brought out the tea as soon as it had finished brewing.  I like that they delivered it without calling out my name or a number.  (That's a perk of being small!)  Seems like a nice place to stop by for a beverage and something light to go with it.  Review #2296

Here is another nice park for the folks in Broad Ripple.  This one features tennis and volleyball courts, a splash park, a playground for kids, and a small swing playground for toddlers.  There is a shelter with picnic tables but I didn't see a grill.  There are restrooms and a water fountain available during park season.  There is shade for adults who might not be participating in the splash park.    Note:  I thought the tennis courts looked like they were in really good condition compared to many I've visited.  Review #595

I've been watching this business grow since my first visit to the neighboring Liter House and I must say it looks great!  I also really liked the food.  But I'm not a fan of the ordering process and the deconstructed sandwiches.  First, the space is huge.  It has two stories, each with it's own patio area for when the weather cooperates.  The space is bright with natural light and the first floor (family area) dining had a large fireplace going to make it feel comfy.  The entrance to the restaurant is on the south side of the building around back.  (Note that Liter House is no longer open for lunch, so you can't cut through from the street side.)  Upstairs is for 21+ only, but during the day, nobody sits there.  Country music fills the air and  Willie Nelson photos haunt the restrooms.  (I know he's not dead, but just looks that way.)   Next, the food tasted really good.  I started with the smoked wings (Memphis Style spices) which come with ranch.  I got the small order (6 pcs) and the meat was right on the edge; so done that the meat fell off the bone, but some of the meat was a bit dry.  Great spicy taste, but not spicy heat.  So, points for lots of flavor!  I also got the house salad which comes with a choice of meats, but since I was loading up on meats with the rest of my order, I went without any.  They use a house dressing (I didn't see any other options listed) that was okay.    I also ordered the 1/4 pound chopped pork from the smoker (the meats are available until they run out since they all are slow roasted.)  The meat was still moist even without the addition of sauces (only Carolina Mustard and Bourbon & Cola flavors available) which is a good thing!  What I didn't like was the way it was served.  My tray was lined with a paper liner and a single slice of white bread was on the paper.  Half the meat was on the bread, the other half spilled over onto the liner.  The pickles and pickled onions were on the liner too.  Why?  I sliced my bread, rebuilt the sandwich and added the sauces.  It tasted great, but if I wanted to make my own sandwich, I would stay home.  My only problem with the place is the "unique" ordering style.  You pick a table first then read a brochure about how to order.  Really?  When you decide what you want, you remember your table number and stand in line to place your order and let them open a tab for your table.  You also have drink order cards on your table that you attach to the "t"-shaped rack with the number on it. (There are pens on the ends.)  When you are ready to leave, you mark the box for bringing your bill and attach it to the rack again.  The rest is a regular checkout where they bring your bill for you to sign.  But what if you pick a table, and while in line ordering, someone else takes your space?  I was by myself, so I left my jacket on the table.  What if you send one person from your group to place the order and they ask a question you don't know?  Are you supposed to flag down the other members of your table for an answer?  Just seems like they could run the ordering like thousands of successful restaurants/bars and not have to explain the system to everyone who comes in.  Despite the ordering process, I thought the service was friendly and the wait times were minimal.  I can see this place being very popular on summer nights with the half liters of beer flowing and tons of barbecue options to choose from.  Review #2289

We really enjoyed our experience at Blu Moon Cafe.  The staff was very helpful in selecting our orders which were paninis and sides.  I went with a spicy Grinder (hot ham and salami with provolone and giardiniera) and a side of smashed potato salad.  The heat from the sandwich surprised me, but it wasn't too hot.  The bread was perfectly toasted, but I will say that the sandwich got a little messy since the giardiniera dripped quite a bit causing the garlic mayo to get on my fingers.    My wife ordered a half tuna melt and thought it pretty good as well.  She got a side of chicken soup with large cubes of chicken, but no noodles.  It was spicy as well.  (She doesn't have a tolerance for heat so she left it unfinished.  I thought it was pretty good, but the chicken definitely got overcooked.)  When you order, they give you a number for your table and bring it out to you when it is ready.  I didn't see anything for busing the tables when done, so I assume they do that for you.  Overall, the staff was great, the food tasted great, though a bit on the spicy side and a little messy.  If you don't mind licking your fingers or using a second napkin, then this is a place to try!  Review #2024

Also known as the Carmel Arts Council Gallery, this tiny building (actually 2 small buildings front to back) sits on a prime space on Main Street.  The front room as you enter is filled with thematic artwork arranged in groupings from local elementary schools.  Periodically, the work is changed to showcase the work of a different school.  The back room is for the middle and high school artwork.  Where the front room is filled with images that feature the combined impact of the themes, the back room has less artwork, but more advanced in technique, allowing the individual pieces to become the focal point.  Some of the artwork is very skilled and you really see the progression as you step from the front to the back room.  The gallery has very limited hours, so for all my visits to Carmel, this was the first time I've seen the gallery open.  Still, I like that it gives the kids a chance to see their work showcased and encourages art in the curriculum.    The gallery has an arrangement with two sister cities, one in Japan and one in China.  The artwork gets shared and at those times, the students can check out how their counterparts view themes as well as know their work is being looked at in a foreign country.  Very cool!  The gallery's small size makes for a quick visit, so if you catch them when they are open, then stop by.  Review #2495

My wife loves this store (I like it, but not as enthusiastically).  She loves browsing through the items and enjoys seeing how they make arrangements so that she can take some of their ideas and use them at home.  On this stop, she noted some table lamps and a couple paintings that she is keeping an eye on.  She's a smart shopper and knows that there will likely be a sale soon, so she wants to go back in the near future.  I enjoy seeing the variety of items and if our home was larger, things I would add to my den/computer room/workout room.    We will be return!  Review #1953

In a state with 50+ covered bridges that are over 130 years old, it makes sense that the State Fair should have one of its own.  But since moving one of these treasured bridges is too expensive (and may cause some hard feelings), the state built a new one back in 2008.  The placement and function are perfect as it spans 90 feet over the west entrance to the infield of the fairgrounds.  Not only does it serve as a road, but it has also been setup as the entrance to events like the Chinese Lantern Festival back in 2017.    The cool thing about covered bridges is that as you walk through, you can see the intricate design and woodwork needed to support the structure.  This burr arch truss style bridge is one of the most common in the area.  I like that this bridge also has windows that let you look out as you cross.  Just another thing to take note of when you visit the fair.  Review #2857

If your kids are old enough to enjoy climbing and sliding (and bouncing around on a spongy surface), then they may love this new park that opened in Nov 2018.  It's located just north of the USS Indianapolis Memorial on the canal.  I also found some affordable street parking during the week on Senate by Walnut Street (about $1 per hour) that is just a short distance away.  The park has a blue theme due to the involvement of the Colts supporting the park.  There is a lot of emphasis on getting outside to play, so I understand the endless varieties of webbed rope paths around the park. They also have a couple slides and a fortress to climb up into.  There are some swings too.  I didn't see any kids playing during my weekday visit since it was so cold, so I am curious how the kids will play on the elevated tarps and sections of tarp that are stretched between tubular rails.  Are the steps?  Are they seats?  They are spaced about a step apart, but since they are elevated several feet in the air, I was puzzled about how kids will interpret what to do with them.  I'm pretty sure most kids will walk on them and inevitably, some will fall through.  Oh well, sports can be challenging!  I would have really enjoyed this as a kid.  I hope that visitors to the canal will take time to check it out.    Note:  They do have a large stretched tarp for shade since the trees in the area aren't big enough yet to offer shade.  Note 2:  There isn't much for little kids who would have difficulty climbing the ropes.    Note 3:  Restrooms are not on site, but are open to the public a few blocks away.  Review #1714

My wife and I stopped in on a cold and rainy winter day and were welcomed into this restored house/shop, filled with china and all the accoutrements you would expect from a tea shop.    I immediately ordered a hot pumpkin spice black tea.  I did notice that they didn't bring a timer to help me know when my tea was steeped properly like some other tea shops.  Still, I was able to approximate the four minute suggested time they gave me (I usually prefer five minutes for black tea).  The tea was tasty and the teapot had enough hot water that I could get several small cups worth, though the water cooled significantly over the course of my meal.  My wife went with a quiche of the day which came with chicken and mixed veggies including spinach that she found really tasty.  The plate also came with a small side salad with house dressing (no choices offered), a small bowl of fresh fruit, and a house baked scone.  I went with another daily special:  a Monte Cristo served on raisin bread with ham and cheese inside, and dusted with powdered sugar.  I also added a bowl of delicious Apple Butternut Squash soup.  My meal also came with the salad, fruit, and scone as well.  So, a lot of food that was quite delicious.  We found that the place also has a couple rooms upstairs that can be reserved for private tea parties.  There is also a generously sized patio on the south side of the building for warmer days.    For customers who enjoy murder mystery dinners, they have a frequent offering of those on their website.  Each table holds six customers during the dinner, so if you sign up for that, either bring your party of six or know that others will be seated with you for those activities.  The more you bring, the better the pricing is per customer.  We also ordered some food to go since we were heading directly home.  Why not get something for dinner?  So, my wife ordered a Salmon Strawberry Salad (the salmon is thoroughly cooked and was bland and just a hint of fishy taste.)  I ordered the Turkey Asparagus Wrap which was huge and had a nice taste (I only ate half during my dinner and saved the leftover half.)  We also ordered a couple desserts:  my wife got the Valentine's Cake (marbled chocolate and white cake that was okay, but not very chocolaty) and I got the Lemon Blueberry cake that I really enjoyed.  Moist texture and whole blueberries paired well with the lemon cake and sweet/creamy icing.  Overall, we had a good time dining here.  If you want a personal touch, I recommend going at lunch during the week when there is less of a rush.  Review #2202

I give 5-star ratings when a place exceeds my expectations.  I remember when this place opened that it took a beating due to some lackluster performance during the 2018 Devour, but the ratings have risen to a solid 4-star despite the rough start.  So, when the opportunity to dine here presented itself, I made a point of heading over.  The location is the upstairs section of the building shared with sister company Brugge.  Yes, you have to climb stairs to get in here, but if that is difficult for you, there is the option of seating in Brugge and asking for the Txuleta menu.  (Know that your food will have to be run outside via the stairs to be delivered.)  The inside is rich with dark woods and deep colored walls.  There are lots of mosaic inlays on the walls and by the bar.  Very elegant in places, but with a casual feel.  I started with a flight of the ciders.  Two are house made:  the Sidra Naturala and the Frambuesa (raspberry), both of which are on the dry side and quite tasty.  They also have a McClure's award winning cider "Bon Bon" which is a light and crisp apple cider that is delicious.  Most of the large plates and sides are shareable here.  However they do have the Pintxos menu of hot and cold items that are small plates.  Since I was by myself, I focused on the smalls and still felt there were a lot of options to choose from.  Know that unless you order one thing at a time, you have no control of the order your food will arrive.  It is delivered as soon as it is ready.  So, I ordered a couple small plates and ate them in the reverse order of what I would normally get from a standard restaurant.  My entree was the Smoked Trout.  I received a beautifully arranged plate of the smoked fish nestled on two separate slices of bread (like a bruschetta).  The fish was topped with a berry relish (berries and fish go great together!) and a bit of herb that was chiffonade into green ribbons.  All of this was served over a plate with lines of creme fraiche.  I've rarely eaten cold, smoked fish, but this was as good as I've ever had.  (I am curious if it might even taste better served warmed to unlock more flavor.)  The flavors were well balanced, but it could use just a bit more berry relish so that I could taste it in each bite.  (I would say 3 or 4 bites per bread slice.)  Before long, a beautiful vegetable plate arrived with two colorful veggies served on the bread also.  One was a shredded orange carrot with fennel and avocado.  The other was a deep reddish-purple shredded beat with grapefruit and greens.  Both were seated on a drizzle of a spicy jam that had a bit of unexpected heat that layered nicely with the flavors.  And the macadamia nuts were an excellent pairing; be sure to try those with the sandwich bites.  You're welcome!  The service was very personable and welcoming and offered some insight into how the food was presented.  I learned about the ciders and about the sizes of the different options which helped me make my decisions.   Overall, I would gladly return with others so that I could share the large plates and sides.  (I didn't have enough room to try the 26 oz bone -in steak!)    If you have had your doubts, ask yourself if you want to try something that is different from what you normally have.  Don't get me wrong..they still have steaks and chicken, but it may not be served like you are used to.  But if you appreciate new flavor combinations and a meal that is as beautiful to look at as it is to eat, then make a point of stopping by here.  Review #2292

Small shop to get a quick deli sandwich on your choice of bagel...pretty simple concept that seems to work pretty well.  My wife and I found metered street parking across BR Ave. and enjoyed our selections.  The shop has a shotgun set up with the order counter on the left and a limited number of 4-top tables on the right.   The extensive menu is on blackboards behind the counter, so when you enter, make your way passed the menu and place your order when you are ready at the far end (there is a sign that says "Order here".  Note that you may have a wait to be acknowledged because they only work on one sandwich at a time.  Just be patient.  When they look up, let them know you are ready and they will get to you.   The menu boards are extensive and have a list of ingredients that they recommend, including the bagel choice.  They have about a dozen bagel varieties which are not listed on the board, but are in labeled bins just below the boards.  When you place your order, let the preparer know of any modifications you want at that time.  Also, since they have clever names for each combination, you HAVE to remember that name because when it is ready, they call out the sandwich name, not yours, not a number, not the ingredients.  Just the sandwich name.  Got it?  While waiting for your sandwich to be made, you can go back towards the front to where the cashier's spot is to grab some chips and, after paying for your options, fill your beverage.  You can go ahead and grab a table then or stand by if you are getting it to go.    I had a Riviera Reuben which is pretty standard for a reuben with the exception that it is on a bagel.  The sauerkraut does have a bit of tartness to it.  The sandwich was good and plenty filling.  My wife had a Ned's Gold Turkey sandwich that she thought was good, but felt the horseradish was too hot/too much for the sandwich.  She isn't a big fan of heat, but likes the horseradish flavor.  So, it may not be too hot for most folks.  They carry Coke products from the fountain next to the cashier's area.  They also have some bottled beverage options along the wall on the right side of the entrance.  Overall, a pretty good meal for a fair price.  Definitely a place we were able to get into and out of in during a lunch hour.  Note to owners:  The ordering process may work for you and for regulars, but from reading a lot of reviews, your process is confusing.  You would probably get higher reviews if you considered making it more normal.  Review #1704

I felt like an adventure in cuisine, so I decided to try a relatively new place on the south side of Indy that features Asian Fusion (I believe Burma, Chinese, and Indonesia flavors but I'm not certain.)  I had read a number of good reviews on the Pan Mee (Dry) entree, so I decided to go with that.  The Pan Mee (Dry) is served as a stir fry.  Otherwise, it is part of a broth/soup.  The Pan Mee (Dry) is listed as a spicy dish, but for my palate, it was noticeably spicy, but not anything too outrageous.  Note that they do serve a spicy hot sauce with the dish if you wish to add more. (I passed on it.)  The dish comes with your choice of pork or chicken as the protein, and also comes with some veggies, the noodles (think thin spaghetti like), mushrooms, "black fungus", and topped with a few crunchies.  There is a bit of sauce underneath.  I tried eating it with the chopsticks, but my server noticed I was not making much progress and brought me a fork.  (Much easier!)  The flavor was really good.  It is hard to describe what it reminds me of since I have not had it before, but there was a savory and spicy combo of flavors along with the familiar Asian veggies, pork, and mushroom flavors.    The dish also comes with a broth/soup that when I asked about it, was told "fish".  There was a small amount of fishy taste on the first spoon, but after that, it was a pleasant broth.  The dish also comes with a small bowl of tiny dried anchovies.  Yes, they have heads and are intact, but are only about 1 1/2" long.  I tried a couple and found the crunch very pleasant, but there was a bit of a powdery residue after the crunch that wasn't very appealing.  And there was a definite fishy aftertaste that was a deal breaker for me.  Thankfully, it wasn't automatically added on top of the entree.    Although I enjoyed my meal, the atmosphere of the restaurant needs a lot of work.  There was an unpleasant aroma when I sat at the bar.  Kind of a stale air smell even though they had the ventilation going.  And while sitting at the bar, I could see a number of minor repairs that need to be completed or redone (wires, missing sides to cabinets, etc.)  I think they opened keeping their costs down, and it seemed to be clean, but just looked more like a dive than a nice restaurant to take someone out to.  So, I enjoyed the food and the service (even though only one person was working the front of the house), but not the atmosphere.  Note:  The parking that surrounds the building is angled, so I suggest entering on the north side of the building and then driving around to find parking.  (Entrances on both the north and south sides of the building.)  Note 2:  They also share the front part of the building (street side) with another business than doesn't look like they've put much into fixing up the outside of the place.  Review #1679

Although I have had a few lattes and fancy coffee drinks in my days, I still enjoy a simple black drip coffee.  Not too bitter, but full of flavor.  Not sweet and foamy, but immediately drinkable without scalding my palate and tongue.  So, when I go to a coffee house for the first time, I always get a black drip coffee.  If they can do that right, then they are worth coming back to.  If not....  So, I knew I was going to be around the canal updating my reviews of public art in the area.  Quills was the first coffee place to show up on Yelp and though it was all the way up on 9th Street (just passed Burgerhaus), I  grabbed some free street parking on Senate and headed in.    Very nice interior, music playing softly in the background with a murmuring of conversation as most folks sat at 2 and 4 top tables.  The order counter is on the left if you enter from 9th.  There was a nice selection of pastries in a display on the south end of the counter.  I went for the drip coffee and snagged one of the Cranberry Orange Scones to go with my drink.  A small white cup was used to serve the coffee and though it wasn't the best I've had, it was good and passed the "sip-ability" test.  No scalding!    What stole the show was the scone.  The pastry was large, but not ridiculously so.  It was light and the cranberries still had a fresh texture, not some hard craisin type fruit.  The hint of citrus helped brighten the flavor as well which paired very well with the hint of bitter that drip coffee usually has.    The place was nearly full but there were a few seats left by the order counter as I grabbed the 2 top closest to the door.  It did get a bit chilly as folks entered, but not too bad.  The rest of the space seemed to be quite inviting.  The wifi worked fine for my limited stay.  The service was friendly and because of my order, was very swift.  Note that like a lot of coffee places, patrons are expected to bus their own place when finished.  Having passed my first visit test, I can see coming back here whenever I am in the canal area and need a mid morning boost or a break from a long walk.  Review #2491

So good, I can't wait to bring my wife the next time!  I stopped in during the week, closer to lunch time and grabbed a seat at the counter (though there were plenty of tables in the main and auxiliary dining rooms.)  The young man who was working the counter promptly brought out my beverage and a menu and suggested the special soup of the day, a beer cheese, as being particularly good.  So, I ordered it and he was right!  Not just a simple yellow bowl, but bits of roasted red pepper and topped with unmelted shredded cheese, served in a bowl with a doily and colorful plate.  It looked delicious and was!  I also ordered the Eggs Benedict which came out just after I finished my soup.  I've had EB lots of places, but this was the best presentation/flavor combination I've had!  Instead of leaving the Hollandaise sauce a bland looking yellow atop the English Muffin/ham/poached egg combo, the sauce was sprinkled with paprika and parsley flakes, adding a festive look.  The eggs were made to order (soft/easy poaching) and served with additional bits of flavor/color in a strawberry and orange slice twist.  This was a splendid breakfast.  Service was excellent throughout the meal and I will return to try some of their other options.  Review #2101

My rating is for my current experience with the hospital which has been limited to the folks who greet you, who check you in as a patient, and who work in the lab.  I have some other history that goes back ten years when my wife had double knee surgery here and a couple years ago when I had need of assistance when passing a gall stone.    So, let's focus on the positive.  The hospital has plenty of parking out front and a dropoff/valet service (when non-covid conditions are in place).  They have automatic doors that revolve or doors that open with the push of a button to minimize physical contact of surfaces.   Just passed the entrance a group of ladies at a table have hand sanitizer dispensers that you must use to proceed.  They also have a thermal temperature that they use on some patients, but not all.  They ask what you are there for and then direct you to the proper spot.  I always am given a  "visitors" sticker with the current date on it and then I head down to the area to check in.  I have a standing order for weekly blood draws while I am under doctor's care, so the staff is always friendly and it seems many recognize me from week to week.  The check in process is efficient and the amount of time depends upon how busy they are, but there are plenty of seats with signs directing you to be socially distanced.  Once I check in, they give me a wristband with my information/identification on it and my paperwork to give to the lab.    The lab is just a short stroll down the main hallway.  I hand my paperwork to the office and they call my name when it is my turn to go back.  Again, the wait is dependent upon the time of day and number of patients.  From arrival at the hospital to driving off, my visit is usually about a half hour.    The staff are friendly and personable because so many people are squeamish about blood draws, but I have no problems.  I think they do a good job finding my veins and usually get the amount they need on the first try.  Only once did they require a second stick and cause a small amount of bruising.  Usually, they nail it on the first try and it doesn't bother me at all to watch them go in.  Seems like they have three rooms in the lab for patients to be worked on, but sometimes, a single person or maybe two have to cover all the rooms.  Overall, I am very pleased with this part of the hospital's services.  A few years ago, I awoke with a significant pain in my back that turned out to be a gall stone that was having difficulty passing.  This hospital didn't have the staff to do the suggested surgery, so they sent me to the main campus of St Francis over on the East side of Indy where my gastroenterologist was.  Although it was inconvenient to have to travel across town, the local staff was able to ease my pain so that the trip was not too painful.  Turns out it was the right call because the sister hospital took care of removing my gall bladder and the stone which had already passed through by the time of surgery.  Yes, it may have been an elective surgery, but since my doctor whom I had known for about 20 years stated that the gall bladder wouldn't be missed and if I didn't have one, I would get any more of the gall stones!  And I haven't!  11 years ago, my wife was a patient at the hospital and she chose this hospital and joint replacement service because they were one of the few places that would allow both knees to be replaced at the same time.  The surgery itself went fantastic and we did physical therapy with a sheet they sent home with us and  she was walking without a cane or walker in the doctor's office and was able to bend her knees to 70 degrees, much more than the expected 110 that the doctor had expected.  Great doctor and surgery team and great results.  The only problem was that post surgery, she was in quite a bit of pain and  the nursing staff at that time seemed unsympathetic.  They were complaining about being understaffed for the weekend.  I told them that my wife had undergone many surgeries and wasn't a whiner.  I knew something wasn't right and the nurse gave me more attitude.  I flagged down the doctor who noticed that she was showing symptoms of having too much blood loss.  She had donated blood a few weeks earlier and it was at the hospital in case she needed.  I tried telling the nurse that she already had matched blood on hand but was given the run around about hooking it up to an IV so that my wife would feel better.  I ended up having to reach out to the doctor again and he "ordered" the blood be given to her right away.  The staff complied and the pain went away.  Just sad that the nurse wanted to waste time arguing instead of helping the patient.  We stayed away from the hospital for years after that and chose other hospitals that were farther away  because of poor attitude.  Seems like someone got the message (probably via the doctor) and there is a much more positive attitude now.  Ten years ago, the rating would have been low.  Review #3826

Great food and nice atmosphere await at this restaurant/cake shop.  I really enjoyed my lunch here.  I found some free street parking across the street and though there was a line waiting to be seated, I was told by the hostess that if I wanted to sit at the window bar seats, I could get in right away.  She showed me to my place and I was greeted by my waitress in after a brief wait.  The space was packed and because of the glass walls (actually, some are garage doors that appear to be functional) and concrete floors, got to be a bit louder than I had expected.  Still, it was manageable.  The menu has lots of tasty items to select from, so I went with a Crab Corn Cake appetizer (two cakes) and the Gobble Turkey Sandwich (comes with your choice of kettle chips or side salad).  The appetizer is supposed to have lump crab meat and sweet corn in a "cake" that is pan fried, and comes with Old Bay mayo (a little bit of heat too) and a cilantro & lime salad that had a chewier texture than lettuce salad (not sure what the base was, but it was either a shaved Brussels Sprout or cabbage type green).  Good flavor, but not much crab.  Very mild crab flavor with a nice corn taste.  Definitely use the mayo for another layer of flavor.  The turkey sandwich was fantastic!  It was made with a thick slice of breast meat (about 3/8" thick) and was topped with a delicious spicy raspberry jam and a cream cheese spread with lettuce.  I am going to try making this one at home!  So why not 5 stars?  Well, even though I got there 75 minutes after opening, they ran out of my first choice of appetizer.  Seems odd that the item is listed on both the lunch and dinner menu and to run out of it so early seems like they need better planning by management/chef.  Fortunately, they have a lot of nice items that sounded good, so I was able to enjoy my options.  Over on the dessert side, they list about a dozen options, but at least there they mention that not all items may be available every day.  Sure enough, my first choice was out that day too.  Again, it seems like if you are going to list it, then you should try harder to have it every service or come out with a daily list of what is available so that customers aren't disappointed.  Overall, the service was fine and I thought it quaint that all the servers wear aprons.  There is a very pleasant atmosphere and I can imagine that if they open the garage doors during nice weather, this place could be a really great spot to sit outdoors and overlook the Lions Park across the street.  Nice location.  Review #424

My wife asked to stop at a nearby hardware store while we were on the west side of Indy, so this one popped up on Yelp!  After winding around the maze of patched roads that lead back to the store near 10th & 465, we grabbed a spot and headed inside.  One of the features of big box businesses is that they tend to have only one or two layouts, so we soon found our way to the outdoor area that is still inside the building.    Ultimately, after asking for assistance, we were directed to the outdoor area on the outside where the store carried what we were looking for at an affordable price.  They had some higher end options as well, but we were able to make do with the ones with the lowest prices.  The only knock, and I see it at a lot of hardware stores, is that there tend to be clusters of employees talking away right in the middle of an aisle, not paying any attention to the customers.  If you don't butt in and say, "can one of you please help me find this item", they ignore you.  Fortunately, my wife stopped one individual as he was walking from another area and he looked it up on the computer for us.  Once we got to that area, another employee pointed it out. (I wouldn't have guessed at that location, but it made sense to the store.)  So, some employees are helpful that's why I bumped the rating back up to a 4.  Review #3352

Even though this place is about a half an hour from our home, it is worth the drive to find those hard to find batteries that are sometimes difficult to replace yourself.  And when you need a specialty bulb, they are a good place to stop too!  Over the years, we have picked up batteries that have been for a wide variety of devices.  On our most recent trip, my wife wanted to replace a watch battery and wasn't sure of the type she needed.  She also didn't want to risk scratching the back to open it.  So she brought it here and let them do it.  She had an option:  Either simply buy a battery or, for a roughly 50% mark up, get a lifetime replacement battery.  They put a small insert into the back of the watch to let them know you've purchased the lifetime option and so you don't have to remember to bring in paperwork as proof the next time.  Nice option if you love your watch and plan on keeping it for a long time (no pun intended).  The guys who work here are customer oriented and though you may have a bit of a wait, they are trying to make sure each customer is satisfied before moving onto the next one.  Fortunately, the man who was doing repairs was able to assist in sales to keep the line moving.  Good service with hard to find items and replacement.  That's why we keep coming back.  Review #3485

While out shopping with my wife, we stopped into this Broad Ripple Shop that sits high above street level along Cornell (I forgot to check if there is an easier access from their parking lot on the west side of the building.) After climbing the stairs to the front porch, we entered into the shop.  To the left of the shop is a row of dressing rooms for visitors to try on the women's clothing offered within the shop.  To the right are several rows of clothing that extend to the back of the shop.  To the immediate right of the doorway are accessories, party games, greeting cards, and other small gift items.  Based upon my wife's opinion, the clothing seemed to be high quality but also came with a higher price tag than what she was used to paying.  She found a gorgeous necklace almost immediately, but the nearly $400 price tag scared her off.    The ladies working were welcoming and offered to help find something if needed.  Review #3329

What a delicious lunch I had at Tlaolli!  The Pork Carnitas over rice was so good!  I stopped in for a quick bite after hiking around Pogue's Run Art & Nature Park on the East Side.  I had driven by Tlaolli a few times and remembered all the great Yelp reviews, so I found a spot in the area and headed over.  They have done some remodeling, so be sure to enter from the east side of the building.  The "front door" on Washington is locked since that is where the kitchen is now.  When you enter the correct door, the order counter is on your left, the dining and restroom are on the right.  On the wall next to the order counter is a menu of their available items.  The gal behind the counter was very helpful since it was my first time here.  She asked if I was looking for Vegan or Vegetarian (I wasn't), if I wanted one of the specials, or some of the selections on the board that come with options.  I let her know I wanted the meal to go and after paying, she directed me to where to get my beverage and to have a seat until my food was ready.  She brought out a six inch aluminum dish with a top on it and some corn tortillas wrapped for some of the carnitas ingredients.  (Note that the two tortillas won't be enough to hold the rice in the bowl, but should hold most of the meat and toppings.)  When I got home, I dug in and Wow!  The rice was moist and spiced (I chose mild spice, but it was full of flavor!)  The pork was tender and the remaining ingredients worked well with both.  I only regret that the lid smashed the appearance of the meal during transport, so I couldn't share a photo of the order without it looking messy.    Really good food available here.  Now, if I can only get passed not being a corn tortilla fan...  Review #1577

While traveling between Brownsburg and Zionsville, we stopped in the Whitestown version of Flamme Burger.  (Note that if you are east bound on the parkway, you can't pull directly into the parking lot.  You have to go to one of the intersections where the center median is open.)  My wife and I found a spot out front and when we entered, we noticed a large, open dining room with mostly 4-top tables and every time the door opened, cold air seemed to spill into the area.  So we knew we wanted to sit as far away from it as possible.  Along the left wall, there was a corridor that we walked along to place our order at the counter.  The wait was short and once I ordered and paid, I was given my receipt and a number to post on a stand on my selected table.  Each table has a pen so that you can fill in the tip amount on your receipt after you finish dining.    After a short wait, our food was brought out with napkins and utensils (we had filled our own beverages at the fountain to the right.)  My wife ordered the BBQ Burger sans serrano peppers and an order of fries.  I went with the Flamme Burger and fries as well.  What we immediately realized was that we could have shared an order of fries and were going to need a "to go" box which was brought out upon request.  They serve the burgers on wooden trays and they come with steak knives.  These are BMBs (Big Mouth Burgers) and having a sharp knife and a cutting board was really appreciated.  (I hate those paper lined trays you find elsewhere that get soggy and stick to the bun.)  The burgers were cooked to temperature:  we both ordered medium-well to get a good char on the outside while allowing just a bit of juiciness inside.  Really good taste too!  The other ingredients were proportional to the burger in both size and flavor, so we both enjoyed our choices.    The fries seemed a bit under seasoned at first, but became very salty by the end.  I am not sure how that happened, but be advised before you add salt knowing what I experienced.  (Ketchup is in a bottle on each table.)  Our waitress did check on us a couple times and cleared our plates when we were finished.  (No self busing needed.)  Overall, a hearty and tasty meal.  The prices were comparative to other specialty burger prices, but if you are used to fast food burgers, you may be in for sticker shock.  I think you get what you pay for.  I choose quality and local.  Review #3377

Very pleasant staff in this tightly packed restaurant.  I grabbed a seat at the bar in the back of the restaurant and after a moment, was greeted by the staff behind the bar who then proceeded to get me water, my beverage and take my order.  The staff impressed me with how often they checked on me to make sure I was enjoying my visit.    I ordered a Chicken Salad Tartine along with a small orange juice.  The tartine had a generous scoop of chicken salad that was served with aioli over a toasted half slice of sourdough boule and some tossed greens.  A slice of cucumber was folded over the top.  The boule had a tasty flavor, but the crust was so hard that the table knife barely cut through.  I managed but would recommend asking for a steak knife if you order it.  Still, the flavor was really good!  The salad was mildly seasoned and was a mix of ground and small chunks of chicken breast.  It made for a pleasant lunch.  The greens seemed lightly dressed (I'm not sure what type came with it.)  My only real negative was that the back room seemed a little stuffy without any windows or proper air flow.  The bar stools were tightly packed together but fortunately, nobody was seated next to me or it would have become uncomfortable.  Not sure they can do much about it other than maybe a ceiling fan (?).    Overall, I enjoyed my meal and the interaction with the staff.  Maybe next time I can grab a spot on the front patio.  Review #1179

If Yelp had 3.5 Stars available for ratings, you would see Murphy's as an example. Somewhere between "Yay! I'm a fan" and "A-OK", they do a lot of things right, but there are bigger issues down the road that are going to take a major makeover to keep the place in business.  The 4-star stuff:  The food was really good, surprisingly so, and reasonably priced.  I ordered the chicken wings (small batch) and though the skins weren't crisped at all, the flavor (BBQ for me) was delicious and the chicken was really tender.  I also had a Reuben and house chips.  The Reuben looked like it was going to be really dry, but surprisingly, it was moist and tender and tasted really good.  The chips were house made and had a lot of crunch, but were unsalted, so pretty good.  My wife ordered the tenderloin (it comes breaded) and it was moist and tender with just a light amount of seasoning to keep it from being bland.  The 3-star stuff:  The service was obviously understaffed, though the folks working were hustling the entire time.  We had a tag team of servers trying to cover our table as the place was crowded on a Tuesday lunch hour.  The staff was pleasant and though they would occasionally disappear from the floor, did a serviceable job on keeping the wait times down.    The 2-star stuff:  The place looks like it will be out of clients in ten years.  I am 60 years old and was the second youngest diner they had....by about ten years!  This place does not draw younger patrons because of the way it looks.  The interior is wood paneled with dim lighting and has the suspended ceilings that went out of style a long time ago.  If they don't do a major makeover, they will gradually lose their clientele due to attrition.  They also need to update their website name (www.murphyssteakhouse.com) and Yelp name to reflect that they aren't an upscale Steakhouse.  There is nothing elegant here...it is a casual restaurant with sandwiches and soups, and yes, they sell steaks too.  No white linen tablecloths here.    So, if I could, I would give them a 3.5 Star rating.  I'll be nice because the food was better than I expected and the understaffed servers were trying hard....4 Star rating from me.  Review #2351

I am so glad I stopped by this shop on Small Business Saturday.  It is filled with so many cool toys and collectibles that it was hard to keep from smiling as I explored.    The shop is located in a shopping plaza on the southeast corner of the intersection.  The entrance faces Madison and is set back from the road quite a bit.  But there is plenty of free parking in the lot which lets you browse as long as you like.  The main entrance is filled with action figures, pops, and so many toys/collectibles that I remembered buying for our kids when they were little.  There were even some that went far back enough that they were something I had too.    The north section of the shop (a separate room) is filled with Lego pieces and kits.  I wasn't into those as a kid, but the place is packed, so if you are a fan, you need to check this place out.  Now that I am old(er), it is a little easier to resist making large purchases, but if you want to see your kids smile, bring your wallet when you bring them in.  It's like Christmas!  Review #3373

I decided to try Chef Mike's Charcoal Grill one Tuesday for lunch (4-19-16).  As some others have commented, there wasn't much front in help working, so I waited to be seated because no staff was immediately there to greet me.  But without too much delay, I was taken over the the seating area across from the bar.  There was a good crowd for lunch which was encouraging.  After another short delay, I was able to order and went with the Charcoal Grilled Bourbon and Chive Burger (6oz) with Swiss cheese and a tossed salad as my side.
