I selected it since it was indicated on the menu as one of their most popular items.    The burger was an absolute delight.  This was another one of my top 5 burgers this year.  All the flavors really worked well with each other and the grill flavor on the burger was perfectly balanced with the lettuce, tomato, and mayo accents.    The waitress was mostly efficient, but lacked the welcoming personality that I get from the best staff.  I wonder if having more front end help would have helped her attitude.  Anyway, based upon the food quality, I recommend giving this place a try.  Pick a date when you don't expect the crowd to be at its peak and you can relax to enjoy your meal without feeling rushed to get somewhere.  Review #25

Note:  This review is for the previous location only.  I felt like an adventure in cuisine, so I decided to try a relatively new place on the south side of Indy that features Asian Fusion (I believe Burma, Chinese, and Indonesia flavors but I'm not certain.)  I had read a number of good reviews on the Pan Mee (Dry) entree, so I decided to go with that.  The Pan Mee (Dry) is served as a stir fry.  Otherwise, it is part of a broth/soup.  The Pan Mee (Dry) is listed as a spicy dish, but for my palate, it was noticeably spicy, but not anything too outrageous.  Note that they do serve a spicy hot sauce with the dish if you wish to add more. (I passed on it.)  The dish comes with your choice of pork or chicken as the protein, and also comes with some veggies, the noodles (think thin spaghetti like), mushrooms, "black fungus", and topped with a few crunchies.  There is a bit of sauce underneath.  I tried eating it with the chopsticks, but my server noticed I was not making much progress and brought me a fork.  (Much easier!)  The flavor was really good.  It is hard to describe what it reminds me of since I have not had it before, but there was a savory and spicy combo of flavors along with the familiar Asian veggies, pork, and mushroom flavors.    The dish also comes with a broth/soup that when I asked about it, was told "fish".  There was a small amount of fishy taste on the first spoon, but after that, it was a pleasant broth.  The dish also comes with a small bowl of tiny dried anchovies.  Yes, they have heads and are intact, but are only about 1 1/2" long.  I tried a couple and found the crunch very pleasant, but there was a bit of a powdery residue after the crunch that wasn't very appealing.  And there was a definite fishy aftertaste that was a deal breaker for me.  Thankfully, it wasn't automatically added on top of the entree.    Although I enjoyed my meal, the atmosphere of the restaurant needs a lot of work.  There was an unpleasant aroma when I sat at the bar.  Kind of a stale air smell even though they had the ventilation going.  And while sitting at the bar, I could see a number of minor repairs that need to be completed or redone (wires, missing sides to cabinets, etc.)  I think they opened keeping their costs down, and it seemed to be clean, but just looked more like a dive than a nice restaurant to take someone out to.  So, I enjoyed the food and the service (even though only one person was working the front of the house), but not the atmosphere.  Note:  The parking that surrounds the building is angled, so I suggest entering on the north side of the building and then driving around to find parking.  (Entrances on both the north and south sides of the building.)  Note 2:  They also share the front part of the building (street side) with another business than doesn't look like they've put much into fixing up the outside of the place.  Review #1679

Although it probably sounds like I go out for every meal, I do enjoy a yummy dish at home too.  So, when I was walking along Main St in Carmel, I was drawn to this combo Olive oil/Balsamic vinegar/spice business at the corner of Rangeline.  This is the third store in the Midwest and I was totally impressed with the quality of the items offered.  I was greeted by a man who was running the counter and he explained how the different "islands" were set up:  The first (closest to the door) had a dozen tanks of flavored Balsamic Vinegars.  Each stainless tank had a small spigot on front that allowed you to pour a small sample into the handy mini paper cups for a tasting.  Wow!  There were so many great flavors that I was hard pressed to decide.  (I ended up selecting a small bottle of Red Apple Balsamic and a White Peach Balsamic.  Yum!)  The second island was set up the same as the first, but held savory olive oils.  Again, it was self help for tastings and here I found most had combinations of herbs or citrus.  I selected a bacon infused oil that I can't wait to try with either salads or as a base for frying a burger.  There was also a third island for unflavored olive oils that were from different varieties/locations to choose from.  The wall had shelves lined with spices and salts that also was setup so that you could taste them.  Great idea!  I ended up with a shaker of Tuscan spices that I've been looking for.  When I made my decision, the manager (?) filled bottles for me from the same steel containers as my tastings.  He then sealed the bottles (I didn't pay close attention to see how he did that since I was still browsing the spices.)    This is a specialty item store with a product that takes time to prepare and is also perishable.  So don't go in thinking you are going to get cheap grocery store prices for these things (even groceries aren't cheap.)  However, if you take your time and sample the flavors, I am sure you will find something unique and delicious to add to your pantry.  (Be sure to keep the oils in the dark after opening to avoid having sun damage.  Fortunately, the bottles are made of colored glass to help preserve the quality inside.)  I found the service to be quite knowledgeable and friendly.  No sales pressure at all.  I was advised that they have a points program that offers rewards after certain totals are achieved.  That might appeal to someone who was cooking more often and lived much closer than I do.  Review #2516

Just when you thought the Children's Museum couldn't be any better, they add this new 7.5 acre amusement park/art museum/collector's showcase to draw in kids who would rather be running around and playing than looking at things inside a museum.  I would guess the target ages for the park are probably 5 on up to pre-teen, though there are some activities that older kids and grown-ups can participate in too.  The official name is the Riley Children's Health Sports Legends Experience and that covers the amazing outdoor complex, the National Art Museum of Sport (Namos), the History of Hoops, and the World of Sport exhibits on the inside.  The park is part of the Children's Museum and is included in your Museum entrance fee. (No plans for separate park fees at this time.)  The good news is that you can still park in the museum's lot/garage and see all the fun stuff in the museum if you want, and then head over to the park through the central lobby when the kids start getting anxious to run and play.  Once inside the lobby, instead of turning right (south) to enter the museum, you turn left to go into the indoor exhibits.  (Note:  Save your tickets, paper or digital, because you will need to show them each time you enter the museum or the park sections.)  The indoor Hoops and World of Sport areas have items to look at, many with Hoosier ties.  There are even some activities to participate in like broadcasting or trying to match Reggie Miller's crazy scoring binge against the Knicks during the playoffs.   The Namos area has a lot of paintings and sculptures with sports themes.  Each stop has information about the art and artist who created the pieces.  And finally, I hit the outdoor area and was amazed at all the color and fun things to engage in.  The main path through the park is the Avenue of Champions which runs to the north end of the park where it reaches the massive Tree of Sports.  The tree appears to be a giant tree with large sporting equipment emerging through the bark.  Inside, you can climb 25 feet in the air and look out over the park.  The lower levels have slides that you can use as escape route (Note:  The slides are designed for kids.  I was having to bend my legs in some crazy ways to keep sliding through!)  On either side of the Avenue, local teams have their logos on each of the sport centers.  Pacers and Fever have multiple basketball goals and some exercises to sharpen your skills.  The Colts have a mini field where you can run through tackling dummies and practice catching passes.  The Indy Fuel have a street hockey version of their rink while the Indians have a home run derby area.  The Indy Eleven have soccer skills, and the Indy 500 and the US Nationals Drag racing have pedal cars to allow kids negotiate those types of race courses.    Around the different sports are three lanes of track.  One is for walking.  One is for running.  A third (the inner track) has stops along the way where you are challenged to complete certain exercises with the equipment on hand.  On the far end of the park is the golf complex.  There are several 9-hole courses to play including one for toddlers, one for instruction, and two Pete and Alice Dye signature courses that are inspired by real golf course holes.  I played the Red Signature Series B course and let's just say I won't be joining even the Senior tour anytime soon.  For safety and fun, you use oversize plastic ended putters and a tennis ball to play.  Each hole has different colored astro turf (different thicknesses too!) that represent the fairways, rough, sand traps and water.  Of course, the ball rolls through the sand traps and water easily enough, but the course still is challenging.  I noticed two of the nine holes were 90 feet in length, so you do have to put some "uumph" behind the strokes to get the ball to the hole.  The park has concession stands, restrooms, and water fountains without having to go back into the museum.  There aren't a lot of shaded areas, but that wasn't a concern in March.  So, if you have kids (or want to play like one) who love trying new things and enjoy the physical activity of playing, this park is a Home Run (or Touchdown/Three Pointer/Ace/etc!)  Review #715

Greenwood finally has one of these tasty bundt cake bakeries of its own!  Just like the other locations around town, they sell a variety of bundt cakes in three sizes to meet your personal or party needs.  The shop can be found in the outlot north of the Home Depot.  It is a little tricky getting into and out of this lot because of the medians along Smith Valley Road and SR 135, but if you are patient, you can get here...it's worth the wait!  Not only do they have bundt cakes, but they also have some gift ideas on display as well.  And be sure to try the free samples they have...you may find a new favorite.  I found the cakes to be moist and light with just enough icing to pair with the cake flavors.  Even the smallest of the cakes is shareable, but not so large that you will feel like any is being wasted.  I picked up a Lemon Cake and a Carrot Cake variety.  Really good cakes that you can now get on the south side without having a long drive.  Review #3616

What a nice addition to the area!  Chef Tia's offers a small but varied menu of dishes including wings, sandwiches, and some noodle dishes to help you get your cajun/creole fix.  There's also a kid's menu for those who need that.  First, know that even though the address is for Washington Street, you actually have to turn onto S Auburn Street.  There are a couple buildings at the corner of Washington and Auburn and you pull in the second driveway on the left to find the restaurant.  The second building is a strip mall and Chef Tia's is the farthest east.  There is free parking right in front of the restaurant.  Inside is a small dining room with a geometric pattern on the far left wall.  There is an unfinished hostess stand where you can pick up called in orders or will be greeted and seated for dine in customers.  I was seated at a 2-top along the wall and was brought my water and utensils/napkin.  The menu is grouped into to help you decide.  I started with the cup size Chicken and Sausage Gumbo which comes filled with white rice.  Even though it is the smaller size, it was a hearty soup with lots of savory flavor.  I wouldn't consider it spicy, more that the flavors tasted slow cooked and built on each other.  There was a bit of heat from the andouille sausage, but it wasn't the type that keeps building.    I also selected from the sandwich section (which comes with house cut fries) a Blackened Chicken Sandwich.  It came topped with lettuce, tomato, Pepper Jack cheese, and a cajun aioli on a brioche bun (more like a submarine bun).  The sandwich contained a chicken breast that was cooked to perfection.  Clear juices were running from this.  (That requires perfect timing to accomplish.)  The only problem was that because of the shape of meat (thick on one side,thin on the other), it was placed thin side into the fold of the bun.  It looks great, but as you bite into it, the open side is filled with chicken and toppings, while the folded side has very little other than bun and aioli.  I tried to get a bit straight from the edge, but because it is so thick, I wasn't able to adjust and was stuck with the "all or nothing" alternating bites.  Maybe if they let the chicken rest a minute and then sliced it and placed it into an open, not folded bun, the bites would be more uniform.    The sandwich was good, but the difference from bite to bite was noticeable.  Mild flavor for a blackened dish compared to other locations I've tried.  I would prefer a little more seasoning as served.  The service was friendly and made sure my water was managed and brought the food out as courses so that I didn't have to rush.  Oh, and for you Yelpers, first time visitors get 20% off their bill.  Just be sure to tip off the full price to thank your server!  Review #3247

I was very disappointed with my most recent dining experience at the new location of Chef Mike's.  I had enjoyed my visit when it was in that hard to find location, so I thought having this new location would help business bloom.  Sadly, everything was disappointing.  From the sign out front painted over the still legible Abuelo's (the former occupant) to the cone in front of the door (Why was that in the way?), we questioned whether the place was really open for lunch.  Inside, the place still looks like a Mexican restaurant but with a few flags and football pictures on the wall.  And my wife and I were the only ones n the dining room at noon.  That didn't say much for such a huge place.  Our server did a good job of getting with us, but the kitchen let us down.  First, they didn't have the fish (trout) option available.  So I ordered a Mandarin Salad and a tenderloin.  The salad lettuce was brown around the edges (which I removed) and just lacked freshness.  The tenderloin was seasoned well, but the first bite I took was a glob of sinewy fat. YUCK!  Nothing like having to remove food from your mouth and stash it on the side of your plate.  Fortunately, the rest was pretty good.  When you are the only dining customer in the place and the kitchen sends out food that is sub par, that means somebody isn't paying attention.  I can't see coming back after this disappointing experience.    Rev. #50

I stopped in High Velocity to celebrate "Tax Day" since there was a promotional event set up that had a Tax Day tie in:  a Taxman Beer and wings for $10.40.  Unfortunately, that didn't happen.  After parking in the JW Marriott's parking, I took my ticket with me and had it validated (the first 1.5 hrs will be free if you eat at one of the restaurants) at the front desk of High Velocity.  I was dining alone, but instead of sitting at the bar, I was taken to the back dining room where I was one of 2 people.  Not near a television although there were more than I could count, I was glad I had good eyesight so I could read the streaming underneath.  (I realize I could have requested a different spot.)  But I wasn't there for the sports.  I was there to grab the special...and the waitress knew nothing about it.  So, she went to check.  And she was told that I could only get a regular commercial beer instead of a Taxman craft beer.  I prefer to drink craft beer to support local breweries, so decided to go with something else for dinner.  I ordered a Metazoa Hoppopotamus with the Salmon BLT (which comes with house fries and a dill pickle).  No tax day promotion, but it looked like the best I would do.  After my order, my beer was delivered and then nothing.  I didn't see my waitress for a long stretch.  No water.  Someone else delivered my food and was gone.  The food was okay.  The fries were under cooked and on the limp side of being done.  The salmon was cooked properly, but the flavor of the condiments they put on the fish was underwhelming.  It was an okay sandwich.  As I was down to the last 3 bites, the waitress showed up to see how it was.  And then she was gone again.  Fortunately, there was one guy working who was really paying attention and even though I wasn't his guest, he noticed I had pushed all my plates to the far side of my table and was sitting there with my wallet in hand.  He cleared my plates and went to find my waitress.  She arrived and from then on, did a good job of getting my bill processed.  The food was okay.  The server was okay, just not present very often.  Would I return to try another meal?  Maybe...  Review #2472

Back in 2002, I stumbled across a recipe for "Beef and Bean Chili" in Bon Appe'tit Magazine (Sept issue).  Imagine my surprise when the source was Ralph's Great Divide in Indy!  So, I knew I had to go to this restaurant to see how my effort at following the recipe compared to the original.  (Mine was good, but it's worth trying the original for yourself!)  Okay, so this restaurant is tucked away on the south side of New York Street just before you reach the underpass for I-65/I-70 going into the north split.  New York is one way east and the block Ralph's is on is cut off from local traffic from the south by the off ramp.  So, to get here, get on New York, watch for Davidson (the last street before the underpass), and turn right and as soon as you round the corner (watch out for the bike lanes and concrete dividers!), look for the alley that runs behind Ralph's so that you can reach their parking lot.  (Note that if you miss the alley, you can go around the block and come up from the south on the west side of the building to get to the parking.)  I know this sounds like a lot of time wasted on finding it, but it is the most confusing location I've encountered.  (One last note:  You can only exit to the east when you leave and will have to go through the underpass.  If you get to the left right away, you can head north on Pine up to Michigan Ave to return to downtown. Whew!!)  So, the chili is really good.  I get it with added cheddar and red onion on top.  Served rich and thick, it has just enough heat to make it interesting, but not enough to put the weak at heart off.  Just really good chili.  I also got "The Lucy" on my most recent visit.  They have some fantastic home sliced cuts of ham (not some paper thin slices!) with Swiss on toasted Rye.  You have to ask for lettuce, tomato, and condiments (mayo for me).  Excellent tasting sandwich!    The restaurant, assuming you find it, is small and broken into three areas:  The front dining room where you enter, the bar area, and a smaller back dining room.  I sat at the bar since I was dining solo.  Although there was some leg room under the bar, I was not able to sit close to my food which can be a little bit challenging when you have soup/chili.  The staff was friendly and seemed to know the orders of some "regulars" upon seeing them.    The noise level was modest with light music in the background and all three televisions in the bar muted.  The walls are covered with memorabilia and writings/sayings.  Kind of quirky, but nothing too outrageous.   The seating is a little crowded, but since the crowd for lunch was light during my visit, it didn't seem too bothersome.  Review #507

After shopping at the Backyard Birds store next door, that employee recommended stopping for lunch at Pawn Shop Pub as a good, neighborhood cafe/pub.  The place didn't look too promising with lots of faded paint on the exterior, but the lot was in good condition and the ramp up to the entrance was in good repair.  I entered (there are two doors on the south side and one on the east) to a pub with a central U-shaped bar (open to the kitchen) with stool seating and a row of booth/tables on all sides of the bar.  The interior was festively decorated for the holidays as well as having a sports theme.  Lots of TVs all tuned (silently) to ESPN.  I grabbed a spot at the bar and was greeted and asked if I needed a menu.  I did and while looking through, I heard one of the waitresses mention a daily special to one of the folks seated behind me.  I decided to go with the special which included a cup of beer cheese soup (& crackers) and 1/2 breaded tenderloin (with chips).  The wait was very brief and soon I was enjoying my meal.  The soup had diced potato in the cheesy soup.  Not especially thick, but still hearty.  (I passed on the crackers.)  The tenderloin was literally cut in half, not just a half portion of meat on a bun.  I really enjoyed the flavor where all the toppings I ordered where in every bite.    The place seemed to have a bunch of regulars that knew the staff by name.  Kind of a quiet place with conversation murmuring instead of blaring tv's/music.  The crowd was definitely weighted towards older folks.  I got my bill after tax and it was just over $7!  I had plenty to eat and enjoyed the flavor, so I was generous with the tip.  Check out went quickly too!  If you want to try something different, while staying affordable, stop by the pub.  Review #3468

Having enjoyed dining at the new Pier 48 (seafood) earlier in the week, I was excited to try their "farm to table" restaurant located inside the new Sun King Broad Ripple.  Though they only had a limited menu during their soft opening when we dined, there was still plenty to choose from.    There were salads, appetizers, flatbreads, a few entrees, a kid's menu, and desserts!  And though there were just a few of each, they will be adding a lot more once they have their grand opening.  Offshore is located inside the former Thr3e Wise Men building which sits in the plaza just east of where Broad Ripple Avenue crosses the Monon Trail.  There is free parking in the plaza lot, though it could fill fast if this place is as popular as I expect it to be.  We entered from the parking lot and were greeted right away.  They have a bar on the left, a variety of dining tables on the right, and there is a private room available for special occasions.  We grabbed a short table and our waitress was prompt in checking in.    After ordering a flight of beer, she took our order.  My wife went with the Angus Beef Sliders that come with some seasoned chips (BBQ is the closest I can describe them.)  The two sliders were topped with white cheddar, "melted" onions, and spicy aioli.  Really good!  I went with the Honey Truffle Flatbread which had a thin crisp crust topped with tellegio, smoked provolone, truffle honey, olive oil, and pistachios.  Though it looked like a pretty large serving, it was light and didn't make me feel stuffed.  Nice balance of flavors with the sweet, nutty, and savory flavors.  Just enough chew in the crust to make me slow down or else I would have devoured it too quickly.  Note:  Be careful how you hold it so the pistachios don't roll off!  Service was attentive without being intrusive.  It seemed like she was looking forward to the expanded menu coming soon as well.  Payment was prompt and at our table with an electronic card reader.  Nice!  Although I didn't try any desserts today, I know that they are offering some of the same ones that Pier 48 has and those were delicious.  Sounds like more sandwich and salad options are coming with the expanded menu.  Watch for their grand opening soon.  It is a bit pricey, but the food quality is high and the flavors go really well with the beer at Sun King.  Review #3171

Although I still believe what I wrote in my first review to be true, I think it fair to upgrade my score based on the quality of the cocktails and getting to know the staff better at a private Yelp event.    After trying the Old Fashioned and seeing the quality of the ingredients they use to complement their cocktails, I was impressed!  No skimping on quality here!  During the tour, I learned that this place will be undergoing a major production expansion to increase their output 6 fold!  That is huge!  The space that they currently have will be undergoing some construction and the storage/aging of their product will move off site to free up some additional space for distilling.  I didn't ask if the tasting room will expand but I don't believe that was announced.  It still can get a bit crowded since the capacity of the room isn't that large.  Whiskey is the only product they make here.  They do have some varieties to choose from, but don't expect beer, wine, or other liquor....it's a distillery, not a bar.  They don't make food here, but have a good relationship with restaurants in the area (especially Cannonball across the street).  Good folks and good whiskey.  What more can you ask from a place called West Fork Whiskey?  Rev. #38

Mind over Mash has been open for about three months at the time of my review.  They have a huge space in an industrial park and everything here looks new!  Plenty of space in the extra "guest" room on the east side of the taproom.  The taproom has lots of table seating as well as a row of bar seats which seemed the most popular.  All the beer offerings are brewed in house with a heavy balance of IPA's (4) and Brown Ales with a sampling of other types.  They also have some versions that come Nitro.  On my visit, I started with "Bobby's Brownsburg Ale" (6.0% 51 IBU).  I thought it had a pleasant flavor with a hint of nuttiness. I moved onto the "OSO" Pale Ale (6% 60) and then the "Covetous" IPA (6.5% 63).  Of the two, I definitely preferred the IPA.  I am not an expert on the beer type, but thought the flavor was hoppy without too much bitterness and had a pleasantly smooth flavor & swallow.  My favorite of the bunch and one of the best IPA's I have had.  I finished off with the "Cloudy Ass" New England IPA (6.2% 70) which has 20% citrus hops.  It was okay, but I had a hard time identifying the flavors.  I guess my palate was cloudy too!  There are currently no dining options provided, but a list of local restaurants is handy and of course, you can bring your own food in.  There is information on their website that mentions future growth will add a kitchen to the site.    The bartender was friendly and knowledgeable about the brews offered.  I hope that as the brewery becomes more established that they will expand their offerings to include more stouts, porters, and maybe even a Hefeweizen.  Till then, go with IPA.  Review #1180

I really enjoyed my visit to the Hall of Fame Museum.  Having lived in Indiana my whole life, I knew quite a few of the names of the cars and drivers which made me recall many pleasant Memorial weekends watching the races on television or listening on the radio.     The museum itself has three main showrooms of vehicles with paintings and trophies throughout.  I really appreciated that the north and east showrooms had each vehicle identified with a story on the plaque.  Unfortunately, it looked as though the west showroom was undergoing a transition so a gallery called Indiana Cars was closed off and the remaining cars outside the gallery were just lined up without any information.  That was disappointing because I can only imagine that each had a story worth sharing or why else keep the cars in the museum?   There is also a theater for watching a film about the track's history and two gift shops at the entrance for buying anything race related like clothing and toys and collectibles.   I was pleasantly surprised at the number of race winning vehicles were on display.  The first 500 winner the Marmon Wasp is on hand.  The most recent champion on my visit was the 1996 Reynard Delta Faucet Ford (Cosworth XB) driven by Buddy Lazier.   Something I had not expected was the nice representation of Indiana built passenger cars, primarily located in the East Showroom.  Having watched numerous black and white movies, I couldn't help but find these passenger vehicles very cool, even without all the modern conveniences like seat belts, radios, and heaters that work!   If you haven't stopped by the museum in awhile, I recommend stopping by 16th Street to spend an hour or two exploring local history.  It was fun!  Review #266

For ice cream fans who like to try something new, I recommend stopping by Mandy's in the Main Street Shoppes in Brownsburg.  Mandy's is a locally owned ice cream shop that has a new name and location just a few shops down from its previous incarnation as Wylie's.  After parking in the shared lot, we entered the brightly lit shop.  Small tables for guests run along the left side of the shop.  The L-shaped order counter has a nice variety of ice cream on display through glass cases.  Samples are available to try before purchase which comes in handy since the names don't always give an immediate idea of the taste.  Fortunately, the shop has fuller descriptions underneath each title.  (Yeah!)  We found out the young man working was the son of the owner, who used to work at Wyliepalooza when it was in Brownsburg, then bought the franchise and renamed it Wylie's.  When the opportunity opened up for the shop closer to US 136/Main St, she decided to change the name to her own when she moved.  My wife and grandson both got small servings of "This $&@! Just Got Serious" ice cream which is a salted caramel with fudge and cashews.  Both really liked their selection.  There are five sizes of cups available to choose from and I went with the middle size (called Single) for my Raspberry Rhapsody which comes with Moose Tracks chocolate chunks inside.  Wow!  Excellent flavor.  They do have cones available, but I didn't check them out for options.  My wife kept commenting at how unique the flavor combinations were compared to other ice cream shops she has been to.  She normally just goes to the local DQ near our house, but I agreed the number of unique flavor combos was comparable to most of the larger ice cream shops in Central Indiana.  If you are looking for a delicious treat, don't wait until summer to start thinking of ice cream from Mandy's!  Review #3738

This coffee shop is setup in a former house just a few blocks east of the Main Street shops in the Arts & Design District.  They have a friendly staff and black and white sleek interior with lots of windows for folks who want to stay awhile.  I grabbed a spot along the street just a few spots down and climbed the stairs into the shop.  The order counter is straight back with a menu on the wall to your left of the counter.  Seating is available for groups at 4top and long tables.  They also have a couple comfy chairs, but mostly, it is laid out for folks who need a table to work on.  I always get a simple black house drip coffee whenever I go for a first time, and this one did not disappoint!  I found the coffee very flavorful without too much bitterness.  And the serving temperature was perfect for drinking it right away (which I did since it was a cold January day!)    I will also give them credit when I realized I needed to change my order from in house to "to go" about five minutes into my visit.  No problem.  They transferred my coffee, topped it off, and directed me to the stand to the right where I could get a lid, napkins, etc.  Good coffee!  Good service!  Good space!  Seems like a place that gets what it takes to succeed!  Review #2099

I've had this place on my radar as a spot to take one of my wine drinking friends, but for whatever reason, I had not made it in.  So, I decided to stop by myself and check it out.  The space is rather small with a wall of wine on the left, a display of bottled beverages (including spirits and beers) centered towards the front, and booth seating on the right.  The order counter is just beyond the centered display with a chalkboard menu overhead.  They have a small food prep area beyond the counter, so I waited as the lone employee prepared a charcuterie board for one of the other patrons.   After the short delay, the employee greeted me and poured a flight of port wines for me:  three 2 oz. samples.  One, a lighter port was from France.  I followed that with one from Portugal and ended with a fruitier California variety.  I enjoyed them all as I sat at one of the tables (one side is a long padded bench while the opposite side is chairs.)  Pleasant pop music played in the background as I relaxed, enjoying my wine.  This is a place you can get a meal including sandwiches and pizzas, but don't expect them in a hurry.  I'll have to come back some time to give their food a try.  Review #3470

Even though I live in Mooresville, I was the Duke of the Zionsville home location of this business.  So, when I heard that a second location was opening on the south side inside the Greenwood Park Mall, I was thrilled!    My Sugar Pie sells pies, scones, and other baked items in small sizes, and even whole pies!  I usually just pick out individual slices so that I can sample lots of flavors since I don't have a favorite.  On this trip, I picked up a Peach Lattice, a Cherry Lattice, and a Mixed Berry.  I've had them all before so I knew I would be happy with these selections.  The shop is located near the entrance of the mall by the outdoor shops across from the Thai Ice Cream place.    This location also has round tables for friends to sit at while enjoying their selections.  There is also a wall of merchandise to browse while you are there.  I didn't see any beverages for sale, but I am not certain about that.  But because of the way the slices are packaged, there isn't any concern about transporting them.  If you like pies, make a point of stopping by!  Review #2181

It doesn't look like much from the outside with it's bright yellow exterior and drive-up window.   Even on the inside, you place your order at the counter where there is a huge list of available items like a fast food restaurant.  Not only gyro's, but hot dogs, burgers, french fries, and Philly sandwiches are available too!  So, even though the menu is filled with choices, a white board with the daily special for about $8 caught my eye:  Gyro dinner with my choice of fries or Greek salad and a beverage.  I went with the salad and helped myself to the self-serve soda dispenser.  I selected one of the booths on the side of the dining area (a number of 2-tops were available and some where grouped as 4's and 6's).  Within a few minutes, they called my number and I was ready to dig in.  (Note that they have plastic ware and napkins near the soda dispenser).  I started with the side Greek Salad that had fresh iceberg lettuce cut to bite-sized pieces and topped with feta cheese, tomato, white onion, and dressing.  Olives and a pepper where also included (both had seeds inside).  Really nice taste and just enough dressing to coat the salad with flavor without being too much.    The gyro was served on a styrofoam plate with an 8" pita as a base.  The seasoned beef and lamb gyro meat was tasty on its own without being dry.  The gyro came with a house sauce and was also topped with more tomato slices and white onion.  Excellent!  I'm not an oficianado when it comes to Greek and Mediterranean food, but this tasted great and I would gladly order it again.  So tasty that I made a point of telling the manager how much I enjoyed it.  So, I'm not sure why they offer so many other items when they make such a great gyro.  They obviously know that they are good since they put Gyro in the restaurant name.  My advice would be to drop some of the clutter from the menu and make sure the gyro's are prominently featured on the menu.  Review #489

Okay, I am not a night "crawler" and I didn't stay late enough for the live music to play or even for the food truck to show up (around 6-6:30).  But what I did see was a very cool bar located next to a cool Cajun restaurant SotSot.  There is a definite 'throw back' feel to the place that captures a feel for the days of prohibition and silent movies were the talk of the town.  While I was there I walked over the plexiglass floor at the entrance to where you can see the "speakeasy" scene recreation in the basement.  There was a silent Charlie Chaplin short playing on a tv in the corner.  The main seating is at the long bar where they serve beer, wine, and some house concoctions that looked inviting.    I asked about the garden/patio and the bartender took me to the east end of the place where an open air patio hides within the walls of the building.  Seriously, you can't see it from the outside, but there were tables with umbrellas just waiting for warm weather to be put to use.  Looks like it could be used for fun activities when weather permits.  The staff seemed really friendly and said that since the business is owned by the same guy that owns SotSot, they are looking into how best to address the desire for food.  For now, it will be food trucks.  But maybe it will be ordering through SotSot or maybe a separate kitchen.  Nothing set there yet, but something to keep an eye on.    Check it out if you are in the area between downtown and SoBro.  Review #472

I decided to stop in for an early breakfast and was surprised that the place wasn't more full.  Often, the place looks like it has a large crowd.  After parking in their private lot, I entered the checkout/waiting area and saw the sign to seat myself.  I grabbed one of the many tables in the open dining area and was soon greeted by my waitress with a pot of coffee and a menu.  I was pleased to find the coffee was ready to drink without searing (yea!)    While I looked over the menu for breakfast, I noticed that my table was loaded with items like packets of butter, jelly, sweeteners, creamer, ketchup, and seasoning.  Seriously, when she dropped off a pitcher of syrup at my table, I was glad I was dining alone.  The entire center was filled with items to add to my meal.  I started off with a 12oz orange juice and water and ordered the Eggs Benedict which comes with hash browns.  Although they had three varieties of benedicts, I went with the traditional.    After just a short wait, my meal arrived:  Two poached eggs over Canadian Bacon on an English muffin and topped with a hollandaise sauce.  The eggs were still soft in the middle (perfect) and the sauce was smooth and creamy.  The muffin halves were lightly toasted and the bacon was thick sliced and just a tad bit chewy.  Still, it was a really good meal.  The hash browns, unbeknownst to me before arrival, were seasoned with a house blend of spices. The serving was generous, but just a little bit under cooked.  Some were closer to al dente.  I prefer my hash browns crisped and tender inside.  Also, the seasoning had a different flavor than I've had before.  It reminded me of a celery salt or similar to Old Bay, but not quite the same.  Once I got used to the difference, I liked it!  It did mix well with the sauce from the benedict.  I am not sure if you can order the hash browns unseasoned or not.  My waitress was quite attentive and made sure my coffee stayed filled.  And it always stayed drinkable, even without any creamer.  I let her know I was ready for my bill and she told me that I should pay at the counter by the entrance instead of paying her.  No problem!  The woman behind that counter processed my bill promptly and I was on my way.  Although there are other Blueberry Hill Pancake Houses in Indiana, I am not sure if there are more elsewhere or if they are connected.  I haven't tried their evening/lunch options, but overall, I was generally pleased with my meal and service.  Review #3508

Despite being downtown often, I had never stopped in for gas at this place.  I like that you can access this spot from both West Street and Kentucky Avenue.  There are lots of bays that are stacked 2-deep and the roof that covers the filling bays reaches all the way to the convenience store so you don't have to get rained on when you need to run inside.  The equipment seemed to work very well.  I had no issues at my pump and was able to get a receipt.  The other bays seemed to be nearly full too, so I guess that means they were working as well.  Out front, they carry ricks of fire wood, windshield washer, and I think I recall seeing ice (no propane tanks though.)  Since I don't buy things at gas station, I can't comment on customer service.  The only negative I have is that the space is packed, so there isn't a lot of room to turn around your vehicle when the place is busy, especially if you have one of the outer bays.  Review #3758

I wasn't sure what to expect when I heard about a new restaurant opening in Washington Square Mall.  The facility is pretty run down and you risk needing new shocks just driving around the place.  The good news is there is plenty of free parking by the mall entrance just north of Burlington.  Once you walk down that corridor to the main spur of the mall, take a short right and look across to the inner corner for the turquoise shop.  It's like a gem among the coal.  The shop offers breakfast scones and muffins and has a walk up window for those in a hurry.  But if you wander inside, you will be transported back 50 years to a "modern" style decor with Motown music in the background and some wild color patterns on the furniture.    Okay, if you are still reading this, the food I ordered totally surprised me with how delicious it was.  I ordered an Iced Chai to start with and that was tall and cool.  In just a short while, my Pesto Chicken Panini arrived with my side selection of fresh fruit (yes, the strawberries and blueberries were totally fresh!)  The sandwich was pressed to a light toasted crunch on the outside while the chicken stayed moist and tasty.  The pesto aioli paired well with the roasted red bell peppers and red onion and the Provolone cheese got just a little melted for an additional texture.  Great Sandwich!  The guys who were working there were really friendly.  If you decide to go inside to dine, just go to the counter to place your order and pay, and they will bring it out to you.  Be sure to take in all the design choices while there.  They will keep you busy browsing around while you wait on your food.  Note 1:  There are a couple small steps (about 3") that may trip you if you aren't paying attention, so watch for them or you may end up on the shag carpet.  Note 2:  There aren't any restrooms in the shop, so the nearest one is at the end of the mall spur which is a pretty decent hike.  So, wash up before you arrive!  Great little place.  I hope the Simon's put some of their wealth into fixing it up for those small businesses that are keeping the place from being boarded up.  Review #2573

After discovering a new pocket park on the near east side, I stopped in at KIB to find out more about the park.  Did you know they have about 200 projects per year?  Inside their lobby, there are sign up sheets for projects that are being planned right now!    When I was working, my company planted over 40,000 trees in the Indy area.  KIB was right along side our volunteers.  We would often have to clean up areas before planting so that the trees would have the best opportunity to thrive.  Overall, it felt good to volunteer on these projects to see how much better a bare lot could look cleaned up and newly planted.  For a list of opportunities that you can become involved with, check out the KIB website.  Review #2304

Disappointing.  I brought my wife here after seeing the great rating and had pretty high expectations.  And although the service was good and the restaurant was clean and spacious, the food was a big let down.....bland. Understand that I like flavor, not especially spicy hot flavor, but I like when a food has more than a simple "one note" taste.    When we arrived, our waitress brought us salsa and chips.  (She didn't ask if we wanted them and there was NO charge for them, so maybe they have changed their business plan and are giving them free like the competition does.)  The salsa was thin and quite mild.  Not bad, but I was surprised when my wife who prefers less spicy food made the comment that there wasn't much flavor.  We then ordered the Street Corn which was wonderful!  It is on the pricey side ($7.50 for 3 half ears of corn) but it was the best thing we tried.  My wife ordered a Taco Salad and apparently, she must not have read the description very carefully.  Instead of a crunchy bowl filled with lots of flavors, she got a plate with the ingredients spread out with a few crunchy tortilla strips on top.  If you like the crunch, then this is disappointing.  And the flavor was lacking.  I went with the Carne Asada which I had read was excellent, but this was the least favorite.  The steak is sliced into three thin slices, cooked well done, but without any char.  Very little seasoning.  I will concede they do give a lot of meat (each slice is larger than the corn tortilla), but it comes with lettuce, about a quarter cup of pico de gallo, and two roasted green onions.  Nothing else.  No sauteed peppers or guacamole, no sour cream or cheese, and very little seasoning. I can't say that the food was bad (I did eat them) but I can't figure out how this was supposed to be a great meal...did they forget to bring something?  For anyone still reading this, they do offer first time Yelpers a 10% discount.  That is a nice perk which was appreciated.  Overall, with all the Mexican places that I've really enjoyed dining at, I can't say I will stopping in here again.  Review #2097

I may be a bit biased after having such a wonderful Yelp Event here a few weeks before.  The owner is so welcoming and helpful and goes out of his way to make sure you understand your options.  He's even posted a "How to Order" sign over the counter that you should familiarize yourself with before stepping up.  If not, you will have to run through the questions for each.  Fortunately, the owner has included most of the answers right there!  I ordered a small tiramisu milk tea with boba, quarter sweet, and less ice.  They drizzle chocolate along the inside of the cup and top the drink with cocoa powder and chocolate nibs.  It wasn't as cold as I expected because of the less ice, but the flavor was excellent.  The boba is made in house and is sweet, so I was glad I ordered my drink only quarter sweet.  I also ordered a large peach smoothie to go.  Delicious!  And the large boba straw makes it easy to drink.  They do have a rewards program for return visitors that sign up.  They also have discounts for customers who save their cups and bring them on later visits.    I can't wait for the full opening so that I can try some of the sweet snacks they will offer!  Review #3110

This small shop on Main Street is part furniture store and part home decor (there seems to be items on just about every surface in the place!)  It has a farm house style for a lot of the items; there's even a mounted deer's head on the wall.    It has a different sense of space than most home decor places.  There are definitely lots of furniture pieces that take up most of the floor space.  But if you decorate in this style, it pays to look at all the shelves since they are loaded with goodies that you don't see in the big box places.  Note:  If you stop by, there are some cool historic photos of old Plainfield on the walls.  Pleasant shop with friendly service that doesn't bother you while you browse.  Review #2601

Having been to a couple of the other Public Greens locations around Indy, I was pretty sure that this was going to be another quality dining experience.  Check!  From the moment I walked into this new restaurant, I was greeted as one of the employees made a point of walking over to ask me if I had ever dined with them before and if he could explain how the ordering process works.  He could have just hollered from across the room, but instead, he came over and chatted.  Check!  You see, they have lots of items for sale.  The food is grouped as "Salads" (both pasta and veggie), "Snacks" (you just have to look at the menu because they are varied), and "Proteins".  You can pick one item, or any combination of two or three with the price adjusting based upon how many are included.  If that is overwhelming to you on your first visit, then they have some pre-selected "Full Plates" to pick from as well.  My advice is to look over the menu ahead of time (online) so that you aren't going into brain freeze over the possible combinations.    For those who need to know, they ask about food allergies before you place your order so that they can alert you to any problems with your selections before making it.  Check!  Seriously, the folks working there were really helpful and upbeat.    After making my selection and paying at the counter, they gave me a number to put on my table so they could bring it out when it was ready.  They have pitchers of water available that you can help yourself to at a central bar while you wait on your food.   Before long, my pesto pasta with grilled chicken was delivered.  The pasta is served cold while the chicken is still warm from grilling.  The flavor was good, but not remarkable.  The pasta gets a little chewy from being chilled.  The chicken was cooked properly without becoming tough, so once you move it off the top of the nestled pasta, it was easy to cut with the real silverware.  When you are finished, the staff bus the table for you.  I asked if there was a place to deposit the real plates and utensils, but they let me know to not worry about it because they take care of it.  And they did.  This is another fine example of great customer service lifting the whole dining experience.  The food was okay, but that may have been due to what I chose.  There are so many combinations that it should be easy to find something that suits me no matter what I'm hungry for.  Review #2683

Thunderbird is the perfect example for why you give a place another chance.  We hadn't been here for a few years after our initial visit (I think it was just a bar then, no food when it opened.)  But when we were hungry on a Thursday evening during a snow storm and our first choice for dinner was closed with no sign or notice on their website, we found ourselves in the area of Thunderbird and I checked to see if they offered food and they did!   We pulled into the small lot behind the building (free parking!).  Maybe because of the weather, or because of the pandemic, or because it was only 5 on a Thursday night, we had the place almost to ourselves.  We were offered a choice of seating and so there were several booths between us and the patrons on either side of us.  More than adequate spacing!     The bar had low lighting but it was bright enough to read our menus and the music was loud, but not aggressive, so we were able to carry on a conversation without any problem either.   Okay our server and the bartender were friendly which always helps, but the star of the evening was the food!  My wife is a little more restricted in what she likes but she gave the food a 7 out of 5 for what she ordered! ha!  The only thing she would have changed would have been to get a spicy sauce for her chicken pot pies on the side, so that she could not get too much heat.  But it was manageable and she devoured her meal despite it being a bit spicier than she prefers.  Instead of a pot pie, the ingredients for the pot pie were served in five wontons which were crispy and came with a sauce/gravy like you would expect to find inside a traditional pot pie.  Some flavors and a new presentation.     She also isn't much of a cocktail drinker and is particular about her beer, but they offered a Virtue Rose Cider and she was given a tasting sample before ordering a glass.  She loved it!  She also sampled a local beer, but went with the cider only.   I ordered the side of Brussels Sprouts that were some of the best I've ever had.  They cut the sprouts smaller and add a char to them.  They also add dehydrated green apple slices (a little chewy, but nice flavor), barbecue sauce, and pomegranate.  The serving size was just smaller than a breakfast bowl, so I was able to finish off the entire side by myself, but it could be shared by 2 people.   I also ordered the beef sliders which were on the smaller side of sliders around town. They are stacked high, but are less than 2 inches across.  They are served with a little onion, a pickle chip, and some beet ketchup.     After a local craft beer, I noticed that there was a gin cocktail that sounded appealing and was quite different from anything else I've tried, but was really good.  The "Toxic Avenger" had a lavender gin, sloe gin, and several layers of flavor, was very aromatic, and yummy.   My wife decided she wanted to try the weekly special dessert that was carrot cake.  It comes served with a pair of pecan tuiles that are thin crispy wheels that add a crunch that she loves.  She loved it so much she asked if they sold whole cakes (sadly no) and it may not be available since they menu and desserts rotate to keep it interesting.  She did order an extra slice to go.   So, despite being shut out by a neighboring restaurant, we were glad that our patience led us back to Thunderbird.  I am sure it won't take long to make a return visit.  They also have a small patio seating area for whenever the warmer weather returns.   Note that by ordering lots of beverages and courses of meals, the bill can creep up quickly, but we enjoyed everything we had and the service was great all night, so I didn't mind the price tag.   If you can go during the week to avoid the crowds, I highly recommend trying Thunderbird for a nice night out.  Review #3868

I shopped here just over a month ago and then again yesterday.  What I became aware of is that with so many home decor places in the area, these stores need to keep up with the competition.  Not counting online shopping, there are so many home decor shops along US 36 that I can't keep track of them without checking my receipts to see which ones I liked enough to make purchases.  On my first visit, I was looking for some seasonal items that would help turn our guest bathroom into something more fitting and welcoming to our guests.  That visit was a very positive adventure and I found a number of things that appealed to me and therefore, I spent some dollars.  Not a cheap place, so you do have to watch your totals as you shop.    But I felt the quality was good, so I wasn't too hesitant to part with my dough!  The only negative thing I experienced here is  the "one way signs" they have on the floor to encourage social distancing.  Unfortunately, who ever placed the "one way" arrows on the flooring wasn't paying attention as there are times you have to ignore the directions or else you get stuck in the back of the store or a corner.  The aisles are a little narrow for meeting another customer, so I understand that they want to create a flow, but it felt like I was paying more attention to the floor signs than actually shopping.  Nuts!  The second visit (just a day ago) I wasn't able to find as much stuff that appealed to me.  I was tired of all the holiday decorations I had up, so I was looking for items that would be more like Spring time.  I didn't find any "wow" factor in the stuff I was looking at.  So, a bit of disappointment.    If I had written the review a couple months ago, I would have leaned towards a 5 star, but as the saying goes, you're only as good as the last visit.  So, because of the distracting one way signs and the lack of items that had that instant appeal, I will knock a star off for this review.   Service folks were helpful which helps with the good rating, but no sale this day.  Review #3864

I wish I would have kept my photos from the early 1980's of what this part of town looked like.  Before the renovation which took more than a decade (finished in 2001), this close to downtown was considered risky with known "houses of ill repute" operating where the Eiteljorg Museum now stands.  There was no concrete base or any sidewalks along the water.  It was just an overgrown ditch with lots of trash and abandoned property that seemed like every other lot.  I worked on the circle and when the construction started, there was a buzz in the city.  I would walk to the area at least once a week to watch the massive construction.  Bridges were redone.  Tons of earth were removed as well as the trash.  A flat concrete bed that looked like a runway stretched from south of New York to nearly 10th Street.  Then they added the angled sides up the four feet between the canal base and sidewalk level.  Finally, they added the wide sidewalks that would allow walkers and bicyclists to share the space.  Buildings started going in and the empty spaces started filling in with condos and a few places to eat.  They didn't stop there!  The canal had pedestrian bridges spaced so that visitors didn't have to walk the entire way.  Fountains were added.  On the south end, the canal passed under West Street to enter the new White River State Park and flowed passed the Eiteljorg, the new State Museum, the Congressional Medal of Honor Memorial, and the NCAA headquarters/Hall of Champions before turning again to head to a small waterfall drop towards the White River.  All along the way, landscaping was added to offer a break for all the concrete.    Jump forward ten years and Indy was selected to host the SuperBowl #46 in early 2012.  So, the Arts Council of Indianapolis put together the "46 for XLVI" mural program which would add 46 murals around town...many of them under the bridges of the streets crossing over the canal.  The plain was now colorful (and it kept graffiti to a minimum!)  Over the years, there have been new additions in types of transportation (Gondola rides anyone?), new businesses, and numerous events like concerts, boat races, and foot races around the nearly 5K walk.  And the place has been maintained.  Sure, there is the occasional mess from the ducks or stray pup, but the condition of the canal has kept the feeling of being a family friendly place.  The murals could use a touch up too, but still are intact with little defacing which is further evidence that the place is meant to draw people.  Sometimes, we take it for granted that we have this amenity in our city.  Just today, I was having lunch at Burgerhaus and a family from out of town asked if the canal had been there long as a public space.  I answered and couldn't help but feel proud when the mother said "It's beautiful.  Truly beautiful."    Well done Indy!  Review #1615

This was our first visit and we met friends for lunch.  The place was clean and new with plenty of parking.  We walked in the front entrance and saw multiple display cases of baked goods including pies, cakes, buckeyes, and cake pops.  around the  corner of the counter was where you could order sandwiches,   combos and beverages.  At he far end of the counter was the place to order ice cream.  When you pay for your order, they give a number for your order and bring out to the table you choose (even if it is outside.) Like many restaurants, they were a little short of staff, but none of our waits were too long.  The manager made sure to let us know our orders would be coming out soon during our visit.  I had orders  for a meal, ice cream and baked goods. I liked being ale to  consolidate hem instead of having to pay at each station.  My favorite items were the Chicken Croissant combo, the buckeyes, and the chocolate cake pops.  Everyone in our group of four seemed to enjoy their orders.  They don't have an infinite variety of flavors, but plenty that most customers should find something of interest.  Th ice cream wasn't as creamy as some places  and had some ice crystals for a bit of crunch. Good flavor on my selection.  I would gladly return and hope they open a spot closer to where I live. Review #3970

A friend let me know about this new restaurant on Washington Street.  She recommended the "Chicago" hot dog and to get it charred style.  Thank you! She was right!    Although I have to admit that I haven't had a hot dog with the mix of ingredients this had, I cannot deny this was the best tasting hot dog I remember ever having!  The Vienna hot dog gets cooked extra long to bring out that deep savory flavor that a great hot dog can have.  No, it wasn't campfire blackened, but the flavor when paired with the chopped (not diced) sweet onion, sweet pickle relish, yellow mustard and tomato with a dill pickle on top of a poppy seed bun was fantastic.  (It also comes with a couple peppers which I didn't try this time.)  The owner of the restaurant has decorated the dining area with Chicago images including the skyline and Cubs (he's a northsider).  There is an order counter and since I got mine as a carry out, I'm not sure how he keeps track of each order since I went around 2 and was one of just a small number of people eating that late.  There is free parking next to the building and possibly behind it (a delivery truck was blocking my view.)  I will say that when I opened the wrapping, I was a little disappointed with the appearance.  The buns are delivered fresh from Turano Bakery and they taste great, but mine looked smashed like it had been handed down a line of Cubs fans at a ballgame.  And the fries were lightly salted and tasty, but were a bit limp.  The only reason I didn't give this an overall five is that my "to go" meal didn't include any napkins, catsup or salt for the fries.  I managed to find napkins in my car, but had to go without the other items.    Note that the Hot Dogs come in regular and Jumbo sizes.  On my next visit, I am bound to try the Italian Beef (they also have burgers, chicken, salads, grilled cheese and other items.)  If you want a hot dog, I would gladly recommend this place over that chain restaurant that blew into town a year ago.  This was relaxed and comfortable and just filled with flavor.  Review #2659

I decided to check out the brunch at HC Tavern just before noon on a Sunday.  What a delightful experience.  First, there was free parking available by the restaurant (additional spots can be found across the entry to Fishers District.  As I walked towards the entrance, I was impressed how nice the detailing of the entrance was.  Upon entering, I was greeted and because I hadn't made reservations, I was pleased that at that time and date, there were plenty of openings both upstairs and down at the bars (yes, there are two).  I decided to head upstairs and though grabbed a chair along the counter.  Let me say this:  From start to finish, the bartenders did a fantastic job of taking care of me.  There was teamwork and communication among them, so they were taking care of the walk up customers just as promptly as the folks who were seated there.  Menus were already in front of each seat, so I was quickly able to decide upon my order.  I started with a Deep Eddy Peach Mimosa which was full flavored and I recommend if you like peach.  I also decided upon the Crab Cake Benedict which swaps the country ham for crab meat and was delicious!  The English muffins weren't toasted, which I believe was a chef's choice.  They offer very sturdy silverware here, and my table knife was able to easily cut through the stacked muffin without disrupting the nestled shredded crab meat.  Who wants to feel any crunch while eating crab meat?  Not me!  I did notice that one of the eggs seemed to be a little more done than the other, but that may have been because I didn't cut through it until after finishing the other half (retain heat can do that.)  So, I suggest breaking the egg on both halves if you like the warm, flowing yolk.  The asparagus stalks were also lightly grilled and seemed to have a bit of a sweet glaze on them.  They were cooked somewhere between al dente and completely done which allowed them to keep their shape while being very tender to cut.  Overall, the food and service was excellent.  I also want to comment that the restaurant is beautiful!  There are lots of window seats on both floors.  There is an elevator near the entrance, so customers can easily get to each floor.  There also is a small wine room upstairs near the entrance.  This is an upscale dining experience, so you won't find any bargain meals here.  But even though it was on the pricier end of restaurants in the Fishers area, I didn't feel like I was out of place going casually dressed.  I look forward to returning with friends to try their dinner menu.  Review #3686

Broad Ripple has always been a neighborhood, but now, public art is bringing one small area even closer together.  Broad Ripple Flower Alley currently features four painted garages between 61st  & 62nd streets that use the alley just east of Carrollton.  In August 2019, international artist Jules "MuckRock" Muck was contacted by Deborah Jacobs (BRU-SFO design) to paint the garage at the back of her home/studio.  Jacobs had a dream of creating a "Flower Alley" and convinced her neighbors to go in on the idea.    So Jules and her assistant (and faithful dog Dada) began painting.  The neighbors started showing up and that evening, there was a block party as neighbors gathered to chat and watch Jules transform for large spaces with colorful flower themes.  Each of the buildings/murals was given a name as well.    From the south end, the murals are: Be Love which features red roses. Be Joyful which features yellow sunflowers Be Free which features red poppies on a white background Be Authentic which features purple morning glories on a rustic barn structure.  I happened to arrive the next day as Jules was working on the ladder painting some of the morning glories.  Deborah and her husband were also there and everyone was so gracious with their time and stories.  It is hoped that several other neighbors will be moved to continue the flower theme down the alley before Jules has to move on.  But either way, a neighborhood within a neighborhood has come together to create something rare in the metro area.    The next time you are in Broad Ripple, be sure to check out this new addition to the city.  Review #2877

Although it was cold out, it was a sunny Sunday in October and I took my wife out for lunch at 3UP.  This place is amazing!  All four dishes we shared were delicious!  The decor was cool and comfy, and the bright sun, combined with the fire pits, kept us warm as the building blocked the wind.  I wasn't sure about the parking, so I grabbed free street parking across Main Street.  I found out that there is free parking in the attached garage south of the restaurant/bar.  (Take the alley on the west side of the building to reach it.)  The front door isn't marked very well other than a small stand.  Just look for the entrance to Anthony's Chophouse and use the doors to the right.  Once inside, take the elevator on the right side up to the 3rd floor.  The bar and dining areas were very cool and comfy.  The east wall is all windows, one large section even opens to let in the fresh air.  But what sold us was the great atmosphere of the patio.  It truly sets this place apart from most bars.  The south wall is a vertical plant wall with over 1000 plants during growing season.  The patio furniture is set up in several groups.  We selected one with a fire pit.  They also have couches with big pillows as well.  Our waiter (Vanand!) did a great job of keeping an eye on us and made some good recommendations.  What we found out was that nearly everything on the menu is large enough to be shared.  So, ordered three items (they all came out at the same time, so if you want to pace your food, let the waiter know.)    I started with the Burrata.  Wow!  So good!  A large dollop of burrata cheese, over tomato chutney with pearl onions, colorful and crispy arugula, and slices of toasted garlic bread.  Great flavor and textures.  Be sure to eat with the arugula on top.  This may have been my favorite dish.  I also ordered the Shaved Brussels.  These were so good that my wife even ate them!  They shave and cook the sprouts and then add candied bacon, walnut, raisins, and top them with a lemon poppy vinaigrette.  So many flavors and they all worked.  Just a bit of tartness from the dressing, and sweetness from the bacon and raisins.  Lots of savory too.  Any the plate was really large....definitely too much for one person.  My wife wanted to try the UP Nachos which come out on a 15" oval platter!  They include braised short ribs (just a tad under seasoned), white cheddar, queso, sliced raw serrano peppers, green onion, cherry tomatoes, beans, and lime sour cream over house made potato crisps (chips).  The meat was tender and bite sized.  Some chips got a little soggy, but I was surprised how crisp most of them stayed.  The other flavors all worked together too!  I had to try one of the desserts, so we split the Apple Pie Rangoon which comes with six rangoon stuffed with spiced apples that were steaming hot.  And they come with a caramel dipping sauce that is warmed so that you can actually dip your treats without them sticking or breaking.  So good.  Did I mention they have powdered sugar on top?  Get these!!!  They also have a variety of cocktails, beers, and wines.  We will have to explore those the next time.   Review #1583

Everyone who is old enough to remember their feelings on that horrible day in 2001 will have some connection to this landmark along Indy's canal.  Though the location is surrounded by traffic (both vehicles and people), there is a sense of peace and quiet, of reverance, here.  The park was dedicated on the 10th anniversary of the event.  The memorial was designed by Bill Cotterman.  The eagle that is perched atop one of the beams was made by local firefighter/artist Ryan Feeney.  If you have an interest in the story behind the scenes, let me direct you to Wanda's review.  It is a fascinating read.  Review #1188

Although the signs on the side of the building call it Taylor's Pub II, the owners have this one set up as Taylor's Pub.  Set in shopping plaza at Woodfield and 86th, the place looks rather drab from the outside parking lot.    Inside, the pub looks very nice.  The interior is a bit dark which you might expect from a pub with bar seating on the right and additional dining tables and booths to the left.  Televisions show multiple shows, mostly sports, but some movies.  Sound is only on one.  I stopped for lunch and grabbed a spot at the bar and asked for a menu.  They have a standard pub listing of appetizers and burgers, but also have a few extra items that they list as specialties.  I went with the Railsplitter Fish and Chips made with Railsplitter beer in the batter.  Turns out that was an excellent choice.  I received two crisply battered pieces of white fish served over fries and with a cup of creamy coleslaw.  The fish comes with small cup of tartar sauce and a bottle of malt vinegar on the side.  The fish was cooked about as well as you can do it.  I liked the crunch and the light flaky insides.  No doughy texture or oily coating.  Just a nice bite of fish.    The fries were a little soggy from having the hot fish placed over them.  Not bad, but enough to keep them from being the best.  Some seemed unseasoned while other were salted. (note that no salt shakers are on the counter.)  The coleslaw was nicely chopped/sliced and the creamy but somewhat acidic/tart vinegar seemed well balanced in flavor.  My server/bartender was friendly and clearly knew the regulars by the ongoing conversation.  Wait times from the kitchen was minimal and checkout was quick too.    Overall, a good meal and good service.  Review #2902

Have you ever walked into a restaurant and found it had a completely different atmosphere than you expected?  I was pleasantly surprised when I wound my way through the parking lot to this restaurant near the corner of SR 135 and Main St.  Yiayia's, which means "grandmother's" in Greek, has a much more elegant decor than your typical breakfast place.  Stained glass in the light fixtures and original paintings on the wall go along with a clean and well spaced dining room.  I picked an off peak time (10 a.m. on a Monday) so I was seated immediately at my choice of a booth (4 top tables are also plentiful.)  They have a nice variety of breakfast and lunch items, leaning more heavily on the breakfast side.  While flipping through, the Blintz heading caught my eye.  So, I ordered a Blackberry Blintz plate with sides of hash browns and an egg over easy.  It had been a long time since I ordered a blintz, but the description of "golden brown and dusted with powdered sugar" had me hooked!  In very little time, my plate and sides arrived.  The blintz was thin, somewhat flat rolled soft shell stuffed with mascarpone cheese and topped with about ten blackberries in sauce.  The blintz were fork tender and the flavor was very good.  The only problem was that they weren't anywhere near golden brown and they forgot the powdered sugar.  Still the flavor was really good.  My sides were served as I had requested:  the over easy egg served atop the hash browns.  I think my favorite breakfast combo is the taste of egg yolk over cooked potatoes and the flavor here did not disappoint.  I really liked alternating between the sweet taste of the blintz and the savory taste of the sides.  Really good!  But like the blintz, the hash browns were done, but had no crispness.  I like a little crunch to my hash browns.  The service was friendly, and very efficient.  I was down to my last swallow of coffee when my server showed up without any signal.  He said he looks for steam coming off the cups ordered by customers.  When he can't see steam, he thinks it time to check in to see if more coffee is desired.  It worked perfectly!  Overall, I really enjoyed my meal and if they could have let the blintz and hash browns go just a little while longer, it could have been a perfect breakfast.  I definitely recommend dining here if you can find time when folks aren't backed out the door like I did.  Review #393

I felt like getting out and thought it was about time to give HopCat a try.  They are right at the corner where the "always under construction" College Ave meets Broad Ripple Avenue.  I managed to get by all the construction cones after parking along the canal and walking over.  Inside, the place is huge and on a weekday for lunch, it seemed rather empty.  Signs said to seat myself, so I grabbed a spot at the bar.  (Note that this isn't a great place to dine since the ledge of the bar doesn't let you bring your plate close to the edge which if you get something sloppy to eat, can make a mess.)  Anyway, after a short while, the bartender arrived and he made some recommendations when I said I was looking for a burger.  I ended up going with the Original Bar Zee Stuffed Burger.  It comes with an onion ring, pickled jalapenos, lettuce, tomato, and something called bar cheese.  Know that this is going to be one of those "big mouth" burgers that needs a bit of squishing to be able to take a bite.  Watch out for the cheese and jalapeno slices that may fall out on your clothes.  The burger comes with Cosmik (peppered) fries and dill pickle slices.   I generally liked the sandwich, but wasn't a big fan of the "bar cheese".  Something about the taste didn't appeal to me.  I would have liked a simple slice of American or Swiss to go with the sandwich instead.  The fries were good if you like black pepper (and a bit of salt).  I do, so I enjoyed them.  Wait times were minimal and my server was pleasant and helpful.    Pro tip:  If you have time to kill while waiting on your meal, walk around the bar and dining room and see how many of the Rock and Roll HoF'ers you can identify.  They are painted on black velvet.  Review #2702

What a delightful little restaurant with some tasty options for those looking for something familiar, but with a twist.  Reading through their list of ingredients left me thinking "Why didn't I ever try that at home?"  And they are best known for their take on Botha Chai tea which is spiced and mixed with soy milk, served warm and with a frothy top.  Very nice indeed!  Of course, Broad Ripple presents its challenges for finding parking, but we were fortunate to arrive as someone was leaving from behind the restaurant.  We got the ONE parking space designated for the restaurant.  I'm afraid you can't bank on getting that, so street parking along College or back in the neighboring area are your best bets.  The entrance to the building isn't very noticeable from College, but just look for the bright orange paint on the building at the south east corner of College and 52nd.  There is a single dining room where we were able to select our own space after being greeted.  Our visit was about 10 a.m. on Sunday before the crowd started getting large.  So, we were able to place our beverage and food orders and be served right away.    I went with the spiced Botha Chai tea and it was wonderful!  My wife normally avoids hot tea but after some coercion, even she admitted this was quite delicious.  A bit of cinnamon taste stood out, but I won't even guess at the other spices.  Nearly perfect on a cold winter day!  My wife ordered from the dessert menu:  "The Golden Monkey" or a crepe thin Dutch pancake (Pannekoeken) wrapped around housemade peanut butter and sliced banana, and drizzled with honey!  Lots of PB and the banana was ripe.  Very nice taste, though the PB does get a little thick when rolled, so be sure to have a beverage handy to help unstick your palate!  I went with a brunch item, the Bacon Skillet.  It is served in an oven hot iron skillet on a coaster with a pad over the handle to keep from touching it.  Fortunately, the skillet cools faster than the food, so I was able to dig into this big breakfast dish which was so good, I didn't want to ask for a "to go" bag...I wanted it right then!  Served over a bed of sliced potatoes, the grilled onions and peppers turned sweet to go along with the eggs, cheddar, bacon and ham.  Very colorful and flavors just as bright.    The staff was quite friendly and took care of us even as the place got busy.  Oh, and if you are a first time Yelper, be sure to check in and get 10% of by showing your discount on your phone.  I'd give this a 4.5 if I could.  Review #2057

Sometimes, a new restaurant seems to feel like it's been part of the neighborhood for a long time.  Whether its tastefully preserving an old favorite building, or offering classic food but with a little twist to make it their own, Maialina seems to belong here.  After using a public lot about a block away, we strolled down Shelby and entered through the doors on the corner next to the fountain.  The restaurant is relatively "L-shaped" with the bar and central dining area on the left, and additional dining and private room to the right.
