A high, dark olive ceiling and intricate patterned floors may be the first thing you notice as you are seated at some high 4-top tables or some standard 2-tops.   The bar is made with dark wood to make the place feel timeless.  We were greeted and had our water poured from a decanter on our table.  The waitress really enjoyed working there and had obviously tried a number of the dishes since she was able to identify her favorites.  And the things she didn't know, she checked with the kitchen to find out!    I started out with one of their house cocktails, the "La Dolce Vita" which comes with gin, cucumber, lime, mint, and simple syrup.  The taste was really good.  Even my wife seemed to like it and she doesn't normally drink gin.  I only wish that they would list the prices on their cocktail menu. (Mine was $12 which seems to fit the going rate for downtown.)  Although each individual course is reasonably priced, with the entrees averaging around $20, the cost can run up quickly if you are like me and like to sample a lot of courses.  Not to scare anyone off, but to be aware as your eyes start taking in the options.  I started with "Nonna's meatballs" which comes with three baked meatballs in a house red sauce and served with a slice of crisp grilled bread (slightly charred).  Each meatball is roughly doorknob size (if rounded out) and is lightly spiced.  The meat is moist, but not juicy/greasy.  I definitely recommend adding the shredded mozzarella.  My wife particularly enjoyed the sauce which is a sweet tomato base, but that you can tell is not store bought.    For insalata, we opted to go with the Caprese.  This is the only salad that isn't offered as full/half size.  Our beautifully plated slices of mozzarella and red tomatoes was surrounded by a ring of basil oil and served over a glaze of white balsamic.  The colors of Italy's flag make the dish look quite tasty.  One of the owners stopped by while we were eating and our only suggestion was that the tomatoes could be just a bit thicker. They were sliced the same thickness as the cheese, but don't have the same amount of flavor at that thickness, so we thought the balance would be a little better with more tomato.  The oil and vinegar were excellent!  My wife ordered the Shrimp Vesuvio which comes with a side (green beans served al dente).  The shrimp (6) were served with tails on over warm bread with lemon, spiced butter, and garlic.  They were just a tad over cooked (spongy, but not rubbery) and leaving the tails on required either more knife play to remove them, or slippery fingers if you picked them up to eat them.  My wife would have preferred the tails to be separated before serving.  The flavor was good.  Note that the flavor is mild, not volcanic from spicy heat.  I went with the Ravioli which came with six large squares stuffed with spinach and cheese and topped with a light green pesto cream sauce.  Very nice flavors.  I could see ordering this with the meatballs on the side for those meat lovers out there.  Each ravioli was nearly 3" across, so we are talking about a substantial amount of food on this serving.  Fortunately, I can devour a lot of food, so I had no trouble finishing all my courses.  And though I didn't have any "jaw dropping" dishes, I really enjoyed them all.    And I can't say enough how nicely we were treated by our waitress (Heather) and the owner.  They seemed like really nice people who were trying to provide a pleasant dining experience.  The vibe of the place was quite casual, though I could see someone coming here on a date night, talking while sharing courses of food.  I can see bringing our friends here to try even more options.  Review #2799

After lunch, my wife and I decided to treat ourselves to ice cream for dessert.  Fortunately, there was a Cold Stone Creamery two doors away!  I usually don't go to chain restaurants for ice cream, but since we were mere feet away, it seemed okay to give the place a try.  The entrance has some small tables between the door and the order counter.  Where the line begins is a nice display board that lists the favorite combinations along with ingredients and photos.  That sure helped!  The ice cream is displayed in stainless steel bins instead of the round paper cooler/barrels that I've seen at most homemade shops.  What I liked was that when I placed my order for the Banana Caramel Crunch, the server grabbed a scoop and smashed it on a chilled prep surface, then proceeded to add the chopped banana, drizzle the caramel and add some crunchy stuff (???) before folding it together to mix it up....right there in front of me!  I went with the smaller size in a cup and it was really good.    My wife went with the Strawberry Blonde option and liked having real strawberries added to the base ice cream, graham cracker, caramel, and whipped cream.  She thought it her favorite ice cream ever from a chain...another league than DQ (and of course, another price range.)  Sure, you can have ice cream at home, but this was really good and creamy in texture and the flavor combos make me think I should put a little bit more effort into treating myself to the sweet things in life.  Review #1152

On our way to shop in Brownsburg, my wife wanted to grab something to eat before continuing.  We hadn't been to Flap-Jacks, but after seeing they were more than just a breakfast place, we decided to stop by.    They have a parking lot and we were able to grab a spot not too far from the entrance on the west side of the building.  As soon as we entered the double door entry (good for reducing drafts), we were hit by a strong cleaning fluid smell.  Not a good thing for our appetite!  (It was still there when we left.)  We were greeted and seated at one of the side tables.  There is basically one large dining area, and some additional seating (stools) near the pay counter.  Although someone took time to decorate the place for the holidays, I got the impression that they should spend more time taking care of the actual business than the cosmetics.  The place screams franchise.  Nothing about it makes it memorable in a good way.  The side salads we ordered were thrown together and had little flavor.  The Ham, Turkey & Swiss Croissant, while made with good quality items, lacked any condiments or toppings.  None.  Why didn't the waitress ask if I wanted anything on it?  Bland and dry.  My wife ordered the Chicken Fajita on Pita and it comes with fries.  Generous portion, but again, lacking in flavor.  From what I can tell, this is a place to get a large serving of food.  Service was mediocre and the food forgettable.  It isn't bad, it's just not something I would return for.  Review #3403

Five Star meats and service.  I really enjoyed the different meats I've had from Moody's.  My wife makes a crock pot dish using the thick cut boneless pork chops (with pork stuffing and no sugar apple pie filling) that turns out fantastic with the meat having a great savory flavor.  I also picked up some of the breakfast sausage that is not too spicy, but with enough flavor to wake up your taste buds!    The folks behind the counter were very helpful and freezer wrapped everything I ordered.  No waiting all day for service either!  And when I mentioned it was my first time shopping at this location, they told me to pick out a FREE package of bacon!  I don't know if they do that for all first time guests, but I hadn't even made a large purchase.  I was very appreciative!  So why not five stars on my rating?  Well a couple things.  The place just needs a makeover.  It may seem a bit trite to knock off a star for appearance, but if you have been to the Zionsville location, that place is beautifully laid out with far more options on displays that are neat and clean and filled with artisanal items that might go well with your purchase.  That store sets the standard for all meat shops!  So, even though this place sells the same quality meats and the folks are nice, it just doesn't draw you in like the place to the north.  And the location is a bit of a problem for visitors who want to turn left out of their parking lot.  The shop sits next to a hill that has definite blind spots for traffic coming from the north.  I had to have my wife watch to the right while I waited for an opening in traffic from the left.  Lots of traffic with no center lane to pull into.   So, if you want high quality meats at very reasonable prices, stop by here....and maybe get some free bacon!  Review #2267

I went in with moderate expectations and came out with many of them exceeded!  I met a friend for lunch on a Tuesday.  There was plenty of parking in their adjacent lot.  Although they had seating available on the patio with umbrellas, it was getting humid out, so we opted to sit in one of the booths.  The inside is long and narrow which fits since the building used to be a laundromat, and more recently, "Nourish".    The restaurant is a family owned business and claims to have authentic Mexican food.  I am no expert on Mexican cuisine, but the flavor was abundant and delicious!    We started off with a complimentary bowl of chips and salsa.  Nothing fancy here....the salsa was a thin red sauce with a few chunks, but mostly tomato based.  The chips were nice and crisp and substantial enough to hold the sauce without dripping.    The star of the meal was the lunch special "Tequila's Quesadilla Fajita- marinated steak (or chicken), with tomato, bell pepper, onion, and cheese.  Served with lettuce, pico de gallo, guacamole, and sour cream on the side.  Excellent flavors.  The fajita was folded once and sliced to make it easier to handle.  They were juicy enough that it made my fingers a little slick, but they didn't feel or taste greasy.  The fajita didn't get too soggy from the juice either.  Inside, there was plenty of meat, but not stuffed to where it fell all over the plate.  And the veggies were chopped smaller than bite sized, but bigger than a dice.  The sweet onion and peppers were large enough to give nice flavor bites that complimented the steak.  The cheese helped seal the fajita to keep the ingredients inside.  I also liked the fresh flavor of the sides.  I didn't want to overstuff my fajita, so the left over sides I ate as if it were a salad.  Very good on its own.  The lunch pricing makes it very competitive with the fast food Mexican chains.  The service was prompt and efficient, but a little quiet making it a little hard to hear over the background music.    I would gladly return to try some more items on the menu.  Review #78

Well, I finally was able to purchase a milkshake from this expansion of Gordon's Ice Cream on the east side.  I will say that the flavor was good on my Salted Caramel Gourmet Milkshake and the staff working during my visit were friendly and quick to make my order.  But, I have had some issues here.  First, the milkshake didn't have that thicker texture that is a perfect balance between liquid and frozen ice cream.  My shake was really thin tending more toward cold flavored milk than a shake.  I also have to say this wasn't my first time trying to stop here.  On two previous occasions, I stopped by and the business was closed.  The hours on the door said they were supposed to be open, but the doors were locked.  That's frustrating.  There should be some sort of explanation on the front door saying why the business isn't serving customers.  Maybe it was a trouble experience when opening a new business.  Maybe it was some mechanical failure or some personal problem, but the owner owes it to the customer to at least post a sign if they aren't going to be open when scheduled.  I get that nobody is twisting my arm to purchase an $8 milkshake, but I like supporting local independent businesses.  But there is an expectation that the quality will warrant the price for an item that I can get dozens of other places (at least something similar).  I hope the management steps up soon, or else there could be more empty space available on Mass Ave.  Review #3612

Not your traditional florists:  this place is filled with live plants and accessories for the plants and your home.  I couldn't get over how many live plants, all tastefully hanging or arranged, there were.   And they also had displays of stationery, artisan products, and an area that had macrame that could be used for supporting your purchases.  Small space, but with free street parking along the cross streets, and such a nice assortment, it is worth stopping by to see what might fit your own home.  Review #3369

While exploring the south side of Indy, I found myself in the land of chain restaurants where Shelby Street meets US 31.  I decided that BBQ sounded like a good option and since I enjoyed the franchise on the west side, I decided to stop in here.  The free standing building had wrap around parking so it was easy to find a good spot.  The patio was closed due to the time of year, but looked like it might be a decent option in warmer weather, though it doesn't have much of a view.  Inside, the dining room with additional window seating is in front of you as you enter.  The order counter/pickup counter is to your right.  You simply get in line, pick what you want from the overhead menu board behind the counter, and pay.  Your food, when ready, will be prepared and set out along the counter where you see it being prepared.    Once my order was ready, I grabbed my tray and headed over to the accessory station in the dining room (along the right wall just before the restroom hallway.)  There, I was able to get silverware, small cups of sauces, pickles, jalapenos, and my beverage.  They don't use napkins.  Instead, each table has a roll of paper towels available.  I ordered Lolo's Pulled Pork as my sandwich and also picked a side of collard greens.  The pork had a mildly smoked taste and the portion was fine for a lunch sized sandwich.  I tried a couple sauces to see and though I generally like a Carolina mustard, I wasn't a big fan of their house mustard.  I also tried their original sweet sauce and it was pretty good, but had a bit of a molasses taste to me.  So, it was good, but not great.  I really liked the collard greens.  The leaves were cut to a manageable size and were cooked with bits of pulled pork for flavor.  Highly recommended if you want to order a side and aren't restricted to a veggie based diet.  When done, each customer is expected to bus their own table with the clean up station near the entrance.  Service was friendly at the counter and they seemed to handle the large group of customers that arrived after me pretty well.  Review #3702

I had a great time with my wife and a friend when we had lunch at Blue Sushi!  Great service and even better food make this a 5-star review.  We pulled up to the Iron Works Hotel and had plenty of free parking.  (They do have valet service as well.)  After being greeted, we were given the choice of dining inside or on the covered patio.  So we headed through the Gojira dining room to the origami bird dining room, and out onto the patio.  Perfect (a little noisy from traffic, but we managed.)  We started off with some sides like the edamame and the Cucumber Sunomono.  The edamame was pretty standard, but the cucumber was marinated and seasoned to bring out the acidity and the toasted sesame seeds on top added a delicious savory element to what some consider a rather bland vegetable.  This was the best cucumber salad I have had!  My wife ordered the Mango Crab Rangoon.  Not only was it colorful, it tasted just as good as it looked.  Five pieces per order.  The mango was used inside the rangoon and also in the sauce.  Another winner!  She also got the Lettuce Wraps which use butter lettuce leaves for you to stuff your own with the sauteed chicken, garlic, ginger, cashews, and peanut sauce.  It also comes with the cucumber sunomon, sesame noodles, carrots, crispy rice noodles, and sweet chili sauce on the side.  A little spicy for her, but good flavor.  I got the Nigiri Sake (salmon) and was pleased with the serving size, the freshness of the salmon, and that the sticky rice held together.  I tried one without any soy sauce and thought it just as good as the one with the sauce.  This is definitely finger food...chopsticks get in the way!  But my favorite dish was the Maki "South Pacific".  This 8 pc roll is stuffed with eel tempura, cream cheese, fresh pineapple, and topped with eel sauce (on the sweet side) and sliced scallions.  Wow!  I could not believe how delicious the pineapple was when paired with the crisp tempura and the salt/sweet sauce.  My new favorite roll!  Check out was a breeze.  Throughout the service, we were looked after (refills on beverages, used plates cleared, next order brought out) so 5 stars for that too.    I know this is a chain out of Nebraska, but I cannot lie...I am impressed with the food they prepare.   Review #962

I stopped in this south side ice cream shop and immediately noticed how bright and clean the placed looked.  They also have outdoor seating in front of the shop during the warmer months.  Inside, there are several small tables that 2 or 4 folks can sit and enjoy their selections.  Over the display cases of ice cream are menu boards that show lots of colorful ice cream concoctions as well as smoothies.  However, I opted for a simple scoop of Queso ice cream in a bowl (I know, not a very bold choice.)  The staff were friendly and quickly put my order together.  The ice cream had really good flavor.  It's hard for me to describe what queso tastes like, but it is sweet and tasty.  The only negative I had was instead of a creamy smooth texture like I've had at other Mexican Ice Cream shops, this reminded me of the texture of cookie dough.  It did melt (mostly) as it warmed, but there were small bits of curd, like in a cottage cheese.  Those were few in number, but they weren't what I expected.  I asked the ladies who worked there and they said it was from the added ingredients.  Since one was translating for the other, I decided that was the only answer I would get, right or wrong.  I'm not sure if it was that particular flavor or if all the ice cream takes on that texture.  Whatever the case, the flavor was good.  I think that ordering one of the more complex options would minimize any textural differences.  Review #2349

The restaurant has a solid assortment of sushi at a reasonable price.  Lunch specials are very affordable and on Sundays, there is a half price special.  However, one of the pros for this restaurant is that they have quality options for non-seafood fans.  We have a friend that has tried a number of the other options and has always given them a thumbs up rating.  On our latest trip downtown, my wife and I found some lunchtime parking right outside the door.  We were greeted immediately and had prompt and friendly service throughout the lunch.  I only wanted water with my lunch and was pleased that it came with ice.  I definitely prefer my water that way and don't understand why more places have discontinued cold water!  My wife and I both started with a bowl of soup.  I went with the Miso with tofu and seaweed.  My wife went with the soup du jour, a chicken rice with veggies.  The flavor on the miso was not my favorite.  I can't quite put my finger on what was different, but it just seemed a little flat.  My wife's soup was full of flavor, but it had red pepper flakes which added enough heat to the flavor that it wasn't long before it affected her sinuses.  It would have been nice to know it was spicy before ordering.  The edamame bowl was generous and had an ample amount of sea salt which we really enjoyed.  We ordered the house FortyFive roll and an Eel roll for our entree.  Both were excellent.    The highlight of any trip we make to FortyFive is the dessert!  The Cinnamon-vanilla roll was an early find for us and I have ordered it to share with friends probably a dozen times.  It is one of my favorite desserts in town!  I was a little disappointed when they removed the raspberry syrup from the combo, but this still remains a dessert to be experienced.  Sweet rice is shaped around vanilla bean ice cream and topped with a caramel sauce and toasted sliced almonds and cinnamon.  It is a bit difficult to eat because each slice of the roll is quite large and when you slice them in half, they don't hold together well, but I manage to stuff them in my mouth anyway!  Oh, did I mention they are topped with a tasty whipped cream?  It tastes even better than it sounds.  As with any Mass Ave restaurant/business, parking is a challenge.  Sure, I found a spot, but backing out from a spot that isn't slanted in the angle of oncoming traffic is always an unpleasant way to end an otherwise enjoyable meal.  It is impossible to see if a large vehicle is parked next to your vehicle and because of the perpendicular parking, you have to watch both directions since cars are longer than lanes are wide.  I hope someone in the neighborhood can address this issue.  Overall, I recommend going here, but if you don't mind walking a block or two, save yourself the stress of being blocked in by traffic.  Review #205

I think my rating sums it up pretty well.  Nothing surprising here with "wow" moments in the food, but it was prepared well and our group seemed to enjoy the dining.  Our service was attentive without hovering and attended our needs for real menus, not those tiny phone versions.  He also was able to retrieve our bill when the "automated" payment machine had run out of paper and cleared so that I couldn't take a photo as an alternative to a paper copy.     Surprisingly there were a lot of guests for late lunch on a Friday, but we found parking in front of the building and we seated promptly.  I ordered the Herb-Grilled Salmon with broccoli on the side.  I got the side salad instead of soup and a breadstick which was forgettable.  My wife and my oldest grandson each ordered the Four Cheese Stuffed shells and thought it was good, but not great.  My broccoli was really tender and the salmon had a nice flavor and was cooked through but not overcooked.     This is one of those places that your bill can run up quickly depending upon the number of sides and beverages you order, so don't think that just because it is a franchise that it will be inexpensive.   We chose this place since it was near the movie theater we were heading to afterwards.  It was a solid choice, but no wow moments, so only three stars from me.  Review #3898

My wife and I are fans of the HGTV home improvement/flipping show "Good Bones" that is based in the Bates Hendricks and Fountain Square districts.  Not only do the ladies who make up 2 Chicks and a Hammer save dilapidated houses that would otherwise be torn down or just be a blight in the neighborhoods, but they also stylishly decorate the homes they remodel. They now offer a lot of the items that they use to decorate in this brand new home decor and sandwich shop.  You can get snack packs and sandwiches as well as Bier craft beers and an assortment of wines to enjoy onsite.  It may sound like a weird combination, but say a couple arrives and one isn't into shopping for a variety of home goods, they can grab a sandwich or something to drink to pass the time while the other shops!  While browsing the store, Mina Starsiak-Hawk and her son Jack were mingling with customers welcoming them to the shop.    There is a wide variety of items from quaint little gifts, to products that promote the District Company or the Mother Daughter renovation team that goes by 2 Chicks and a Hammer (Mina is the daughter)  Because it was opening week, there were cars lining the street, but my wife was able to find one of the few remaining spaces in the lot behind the building.  Fortunately, we missed the opening weekend rush, so we didn't have to wait in line, but we did see this was a busy shop.  They do ask customers to wear masks during the current phase of the pandemic because in a small shop like this, it is hard to maintain social distancing all the time.  No problem for me since I'm not an inconsiderate whiner who has nothing better to do but complain about being inconvenienced.  I have real problems to deal with.  Inside, there is a wide variety of home decor items for just about every room in your house.  My wife thought some of it was pricey (the Turkish rugs), but thought it looked like good quality.  We ended up getting a few items we had never seen elsewhere for future gifts.  I got a 2 Chicks and a Hammer ballcap to keep my balding head to keep from becoming more sunburned.  The staff was very friendly and my checkout was quick and easy.  My only negative is that although the menu board lists all the beverages, it only lists the food as sandwiches, small packs, or large packs and the prices.  It doesn't tell you what type of sandwiches or what's in the packs.  I even checked their website and could not find a menu list of foods.  Maybe they aren't set on which foods will be offered, but because it was busy at the order counter, we didn't hear what the people behind the counter said was available.  So, we didn't get a chance to sample the food while there this visit.  (My wife had to be somewhere, so we left without eating.)    So, I give them a good rating for customer service and for the products they carry.  Just wish they would provide more menu details on the boards or their website to help customers decide while they shop.  If you have never watched the HGTV show, the new season just started a couple weeks ago.  It is so cool to see Indy portrayed in such a favorable light.  I recognize a lot of the places that they crew visits.  Review #3770

comfortably located midway along Main Street in Speedway, the former 1911 Cafe has been converted to Brozini pizzeria.  Free parking out front and both indoor/outdoor seating are available at this location.  There is family seating outside the bar areas and +21 only for those times you need to get away from children and just want a beverage and pizza.  We stopped by before heading to a friend's place on the west side.  I had no idea how hungry I was getting and fortunately, this place has generous portions.  Almost  too large.  I would definitely recommend their salads as shareable or could be halved for lunch.  I ordered a Caesar and my wife got Chef's salad and neither of us could finish our 12" plate full.  Definitely need a to go box.  Really good flavor and fresh ingredients.  Just too much. I also ordered a 6 pc bone in Teriyaki wings (They came already glazed with my choice of Ranch or blue cheese on the side for additional dipping.  And just to get a thorough tasting, I also go a NY slice of Sausage and mushroom pizza.  The slice comes with a giant/crispy breadstick which my wife grabbed before I could get much of it.  Everything I tasted I enjoyed though I must say I should have spaced the items out over more time so that I didn't get too stuffed.  If you are in the area and have a hearty appetite, be sure to think of Brozzini for a nice selection of food options.  Review #3953

When I used to live in Greenwood, I did nearly almost all my grocery shopping at this older store.  It has undergone some renovation and has a nice variety, though not necessarily the largest selection, of food items.  Like a lot of the Krogers, this one has a really nice produce section, has added some special "shops" for sushi and deli products, and has a large beer/wine section which includes a fair selection of local products.  They still have a number of the folks working there since I moved seven years ago, so I'm sure that if you ask anyone for some help, they will know right where to direct you.    My only negative is the same one as when I shopped there all the time:  They place displays at the space I usually stand to unload my cart from the side, so I have to squeeze in next to my cart in the narrow checkout aisles.  Don't the managers understand that people need room to reach into their carts?  I've talked to the checkout staff in the past and they agree that it would be better if they gave the customers room to stand there.  Oh well, it's not the biggest deal while shopping, but is something that is less appealing than my competitor grocery that I shop at now.  Note that I like the convenience of buying what I am looking for at one place and don't chase bargains all over town or buy a bunch of things I don't want just because they have coupons.  I think the prices are fair and the service was friendly.  That's good enough for me!  Review #2027

I never enjoy writing reviews where I drop my rating (especially from a 5 star down to just a middle of the pack rating.)  To be specific, the food and drinks that they offer are still delicious.  The problem is lack of proper management.  When a patron wants to plan a gathering (our group had 3 couples who had to travel on average 45 minutes to get to Thunderbird).  It was the first visit for four of our six people and we had looked at the website menus and came up with our food and drink selections based upon what was listed on their own website.  I also looked at my review from 2 months earlier and some wanted to try the items I had raved about.  But SURPRISE!  The bar had changed all their cocktails and the restaurant had changed all their food items.  None of the items we had enjoyed were available.  None of the items on the website were available.  Management allowed the changes to the in house menus, but failed to let anyone know what the options had changed to by updating their website.  I've been burned in the past by relying on third party menus or photos of menus, but when a business intentionally changes their offerings regularly, then it is up to management to make sure the social media (especially their own website) is updated.  When the waiter (who should wear clean shirts to work because my wife pointed out how sloppy his appearance was) kept insisting that we couldn't rely upon the website but had to use the existing menus at table side, he showed his lack of appreciation that we had come with one set of expectations and he seemed clueless that four of the six stood up and were ready to leave.  I had to calm them down with the realization that a group of six finding a table without reservations would be unlikely by just driving and stopping elsewhere.  So we stayed.   As I mentioned in my earlier review, music in the background is okay, but we were seated right underneath a speaker at 5:30 in the evening.  It was so loud we asked for the music to be lowered so that we could talk and discuss what we wanted to order and share.  The place had barely any other customers that early and nobody was dancing, so why do you need the music blasting so loud at such an early hour?  One waitress acknowledged our request, but no discernable volume change occurred.    The only reason this rating is not lower is that the food we settled on was tasty.  We tried different items and different cocktails that originally planned.  So the bartender and chef can be thanked for the okay rating.    And another problem....they only have one dessert available.  It included a gluten free cake that was dry and left an aftertaste of some unexpected flavor for several of our diners.  Seriously, if you can't offer more than one option for dessert, that is a poor decision too.  I ended up ordering an Arugula salad that had a lemon based vinaigrette and got fried chicken strips added for a protein.  The lemon was so sour that it overwhelmed all the other flavors.  I like "lemon pepper' seasoning, but the lemon from the Pink Peppercorn dressing overwhelmed the pepper of the arugula and other salad ingredients.    Sadly, I don't think I will be bringing any more guests here and recommend that management get busy and maintain their website menus.  It was very disappointing for our night out with friends.  At least some of us finely were able to carryon some conversation on the ride home.  Rev #60

This is the latest location for local Hardware chain Trust to open.  I wanted to set them up so that yelpers could find the business.  I think Fusek's True Value is the only other hardware store in the downtown area, so for those who reside near here (especially those who own homes with lawns downtown), there is now another option.  It is located across the parking lot from the new Bodhi Cocktail Bar & Thai Bistro in the site formerly home to Indy Reads (which moved to Fountain Square.)  Before you read any further, know that because I don't live downtown, I didn't engage in any transactions while here, so I hope others will soon add more detailed shopping information than I can.    The shop is especially prepared for home owners in the area.  Lots of items for outdoor work as well a the standard aisles of small items do it yourselfers need and can't find elsewhere.  Note that when we visited, a "house" dog was lounging near the counter.  So, I would advise not bringing your pets with you to shop since I don't know how they might interact.  The dog did not move during our entire visit.  Seemed well mannered.    One of the benefits of shopping here is that they are open 24 hours a day.  My wife asked and yes, they do get shoppers throughout the night!  I am glad I'm too old for those all night projects now, but realize that when you get started on something, you sometimes just want to get it done and having a place to get the supplies you need is a huge benefit!  The one negative that keeps this from an even higher rating is that the parking is very limited and if you wanted to bring a big truck for hauling larger or multiple purchases, you may have some difficulty in the small parking/loading area compared to most hardware stores I have frequented.  But, the store did have a lot of needs covered.  I think they are supposed to be a paint supply specialty shop as well.  But I didn't realize that until I got home and read some info on their website.  If you are downtown for some excellent food, stop by and check Trust out.  It might save you a trip to one of those big box stores later.  Review #3905

For perspective, we met dear friends here for dinner and cocktails and that always makes for a better time at a new business.  The wait staff were friendly and because we arrived at opening during the week, we were able to select our own table.  It was a beautiful spring day, so we sat out on the covered patio (to block the wind) and I am glad to say the service was fine throughout the dinner.  Sometimes patios are forgotten, but not here.  We had several courses of food to choose from.   Our two couples ordered the bread sticks with gin cheee and spicy brown mustard and the baked Brie with a fruit sauce (It tasted like blueberry to me.)  The only negative was the bread served with the Brie was a bit chewy.  I would have preferred it a little crisper. Two of us decided to order house cocktails while two ordered local craft beer (available only in cans).  The beer drinkers were a little disappointed, but the tow of us who ordered the cocktails were pleased.  The drinks tasted as good as they looked.  My friend tried the Gertrude Berrymore which came served with an edible orchid.  I ordered a playful Gin based drink called "Magoo Done Done It" which was served with a slice of muddled lemon rind which gave a wonderfully fresh aroma before drinking.  It was sweet and multilayered in flavors that was very pleasant for drinking.  MY wife thought it a little strong, but I told the waiter it was dangerous( ha!) because I didn't even blink while drinking it.  So smooth!  I held back from drinking an armfull of them!  Really delicious!  I was also delighted that the food was so tasty.  I've eaten at lots of breweries and distilleries and generaly found they offered food just to tide the customer over (so they don't leave!)  But this food was good enough that we scrapped going out to dinner afterwards and just ate from their offerings.  My wife ordered the Chicken Bacon Nachos as a main meal.  Our friends ordered the Pork Bacon Nachos for theirs.  The only negative our friends made was there could have been more pork...definitely not enough for sharing.  My wife liked her nachos too, but needed to ask for more sauce. I ordered the Duck Wings and there were about 10 pieces that had a spicy sweet sauce and came with dipping sauce, and a cut celery stalk.  The heat was just enough to balance the sweetness in the sauce and the umami of the meat.  I would gladly order them again.  Even though there was a slight mistake on splitting the bill, (one bill instead of two) I caught it immediately and the waiter fixed the bill right then.  The new order was exactly split the right way and I felt confident in the numbers.    For folks who go for the ambiance, it doesn't have quite the charm of the Fountain Square location.  The fireplace is inside is not made from stone here.  But this place looked to have plenty of places to sit (I prefer it to the FSq location especially during the social distancing times.  They have a tent like structure over the patio that keeps the wind at bay while still allowing for some sunlight and fresh air.  Also, parking is easy here with a large free lot in front of the building.  I hope more friends want to go here.  I will gladly return!  Review #3906

Although this was my first visit to this location of Jockamo, I knew from my visits to the other locations in town that there was a good chance of finding something really tasty to eat!  I chose to bypass a small pizza and opted for the Italian Beef.   I don't know if it is the most authentic, but it sure is delicious.  Not only does it come with a thicker dipping sauce than most restaurants, but inside the sandwich were peppadew peppers that added another burst of flavor with each bite.  Really good.  My wife enjoyed her side salad and an order of breadsticks (3) that came with parmesan dipping sauce.    Review #3968

One of the newest places to eat inside the AMP is the latest expansion ofCaplinger's fresh catch seafood.  I Was there briefly to order their special  of fish and chips along with a side.  My favorite side is the collard greens.  It seemed the breading on the fish wasn't quite as crispy as l had desired.  The breading seemed more crumby and so I rate this location lower than some of the sites.   Seating is plentiful inside the AMPs food court.  Parking is still random while the garage is under construction.   For a change of pace from fast food lunches stop by here.Review #3981

I stopped by for a tour and a wine tasting on a Saturday.  I was able to grab a parking space in one of the nearby lots and hopped on one of the tours.  The business is a production facility for the wines as well as a showroom, so tours are only conducted on weekends for safety reasons.  The tours are free and only take between 15 and 30 minutes, depending upon the number of questions people ask along the way.  During the tour, you see the machines used from receiving the grapes, through processing and fermentation, to storage and bottling.  It's pretty interesting, but lacks a "wow" factor since they aren't running the machines during the tour.  I also tried the "tasting" of seven wines for $5.  I had to sign up for the tasting and wait for the appointed time.  Fortunately, since there are three counters running at a time, tastings start every 15 minutes.  I liked that they gave me a checklist that describes the options in each  "barrel" (round) and I was able to pick from either of the columns.  The guy behind the counter was friendly and seemed pretty knowledgeable of the wines, giving even more information about each of the choices before serving.  The tasting started off with some dry options and moved through semi-sweets and sweets, ending with the most popular "Reggae" line of wines.  If you are interested in picking up bottles of wine you enjoyed during the tasting, they sell both chilled and at room temperature.  For those not wanting to wait, a patio with umbrellas is just outside the entrance and makes a nice place to enjoy your purchase.  I am not sure about the arrangement for glasses and if any food is available to munch on while sipping.  Overall, I enjoyed most of the wines that I tried during the tasting.  I think for its size, it is a nice business, one of Indiana's oldest wineries.    Review #268

I stopped in for a quick lunch at this brewpub located in a strip mall just off of highway 267 between I-70 and Washington St. in Plainfield. Since it was a Monday morning, the crowd was rather sparse.  I chose a window seat at a high top table and was immediately greeted.    Although my waitress had only been employed there a short while, she had a service first mentality and was willing to answer all my questions about the beer options and the food.   I decided to go with the "Turkey apple brie" sandwich with a side salad.  The sandwich came with plenty of turkey, sliced Granny Smith apples, brie, candied bacon, and chipotle aioli.  The flavors worked really well together.  The only knock was that the aoili was more plentiful on the second half of my sandwich than the first.  Definitely raised the taste having it on the second half.  I also enjoyed the salad with apricot vinaigrette and croutons.  Just enough salad to give plenty of flavor, but not fill me up before the sandwich.  (Note:  they arrived on the same platter.)  For my beverage, I chose the Hefeweizen, which had a nice hoppy flavor without the bitterness.  The ale appeared cloudy, but the flavor was really light with just a hint of kick at 6.4% ABV.  I also sampled a Blonde ale which was okay, and a Chile Stout which had a chocolaty taste with a bit of heat in the aftertaste.    My waitress also mentioned that there were a few other interesting items on the beverage list including a guest tap cider and a wine like concoctions well over 10% ABV.    Overall, between the pleasant and attentive service and the great tasting sandwich and Hefe, I am looking forward to returning to sample the dinner menu.  Review #82

Note:  This review is for the original version of the Vanguard before they reopened in late 2018.  More restaurant than bar, our party of three had an early dinner during the week.  We were fortunate to find the last street parking spot (metered) nearby and headed on in.  The interior space is set up as two spaces with dining straight back from the entrance and the bar and additional dining to the left.  We checked in at the front counter and were able to pick our own seating due to the small crowd at that time.  There are a number of booths and some two top tables.  There were some other large tables for groups, but I didn't see any four tops.  Our waiter was personable and did a fine job of making recommendations, keeping the water glasses filled, and getting our check processed.    There are two sections of appetizers (think small plates) grouped as Cold and Hot.  I selected the Beef Carpaccio from the cold and the Pork Belly from the hot.  Our friend selected a huge Arugula Salad, while my wife opted for the soup of the day, a cream of broccoli option.  Note that we were asked to pick our entrees at the same time as ordering our appetizers.  The beef was fork tender, sliced thin and served with pickled quail egg, sweet potato capers, and shaved Parmesan.  Although good, I thought the beef had a somewhat unexpected flavor, like it had been marinated.  Not sure what caused it.  It was okay, but not fantastic.  However, the pork belly was exceptional!  The outside was crispy and full flavored while still tender inside.  It came with red beans, braised cippolini, kale, and pickled mustard seed.  Each bite was fantastic and my dining partners were eager to grab another bite!  For our entrees, the ladies went with the Ribeye steaks which come pre-sliced and arranged upon a bed of gratin potato with swiss chard, garlic, and sunflower seeds.  The steaks were ordered medium, but came out far more rare than described, but close enough not to order a reheat.  The flavor of the steak was really good to our friend and to me.  My wife thought it a bit heavy on the pepper seasoning, but continued eating because the steak was very tender and balanced the seasoning of the potatoes underneath.    I ordered the duck breast and it was very tender.  Not too fatty like some restaurants.  However I wasn't a big fan of the side dish pairing.  It came with spaghetti squash, tomato & pepper confit, on a smear of caramelized carrot puree (more brown than orange).  The confit took on a bit of a tart flavor which was very different of a flavor pairing than I am used to with duck.  I normally get something sweet or sweet/acid based and served with some type of glaze.  This was roasted without any sweetness or glaze.  Good duck, just not my favorite pairing.  Our guest treated us to one of the evening's desserts, a butterscotch pot de creme.  Wow!  This small pot was accompanied by a crumbled almond cookie and a whipped cream like topping on the plate.  All together they made for a full flavored bite!  Overall, I was pleased with the quality of the food and service.  Entrees were priced mainly in the $20-30 range.  Your bill depends upon how many appetizers and beverages you add to the order.  Review #409

If you are in the mood for a simple meal and want to support local, you may really like this place.  If you want a burger and don't want to pay over $12 for it, you may like this place too.  If you want to get away from the corporate restaurants and like the idea of going to a place that is celebrating its 100 year anniversary doing the type of food they've always done, then this may be one of your favorites.  So, since I hadn't been here in a long time, I thought I would see how the food and experience held up in my absence.  I remembered that they were packed before, so I decided to target around 1:30 to avoid the lunch rush.  The parking lot was still full!  When I entered, I was a little surprised that there were plenty of seats at the bar or at one of the many tables inside.  There wasn't anyone greeting me at the door, so instead of standing there waiting, I headed over to the chairs at the bar.  (Note that the restaurant is for 21+, so they don't have to segregate the bar from the dining area with some faux railing/wall.)  Before long, I was greeted by the server behind the bar and after asking if I had been there before, she made sure to remind me that it was a "cash only" operation.  With that out of the way, I went with a simple single burger with cheese, ketchup, mustard, tomato, and lettuce and an order of fries on the side.  Before long, my plate was ready.  The burgers are small compared to most restaurants.  They are served very thin so they can get a crisp char on the edges (I like my burgers with a tasty browning to bring out the flavor.)  The toppings are also served inverted.  The tomato was on the bottom with shredded lettuce next, then the burger and melted cheese were next.  The problem here is that the cheese sticks to the bun, so the self serve condiments require lifting the cheese and burger off to apply the sauces.  Without lifting the burger, I wasn't sure if there were any condiments on the sandwich until I took a bite since the server hadn't mentioned they were self serve.  Overall, the burger was cooked nicely, but was under seasoned.  Yes, they do have salt and pepper shakers on the bar, but I'm simply stating that I have expectations that my food will be seasoned when delivered.    The fries were crisp on the outside and tender inside.  Very good!  But again, they were unseasoned.  I did add salt to them and used the ketchup bottle to add flavor.  No problems there.  Overall, it was a decent burger, maybe a bit unique in its presentation and preparation.  But honestly, I can make this meal at home without having to drive to the near west side.  And I don't have to worry about having enough cash.  Review #775

My wife and I headed to the north end of Mass Avenue downtown for lunch on Thursday.  We found a spot to park in the mini lot on the south side of the Black Market building.  Although there is plenty of outdoor seating, we choose to sit in the shotgun style interior.  The interior is dark and intimate.  Black Walls and communal seating are the first things we noticed.  The bar runs along the west (left) side of the room.    We chose a table for two along the front window and got our beverages.  Although they are known for their rum selections, I chose one of the local craft beers.  My wife selected the Egg Salad on Texas Toast with green salad (arugula) and pickled beets.  I got to taste a bite and confirmed that the egg salad lacked any punch of flavor.  Okay, but not delicious.  I ordered a Pork Tenderloin with BBQ slaw, red onion, and a spicy mustard mayo mix on top of Texas toast.  It came with a side of bread and butter pickles which I spread over the top as well.  The breading appeared a bit dark, but the meat was cooked correctly.  Although the tenderloin easily out-sized the bun, it wasn't so large that it became difficult to eat.  I did slice mine in half though.  The acidic and sweet flavors of the pickles with the savoriness of the onion and spicy mustard mayo really gave the tenderloin a nice balance.  One of the best overall tenderloins I have had.    I upgraded my side to fries which my wife and I split.  She thought them a bit salty, but I found the seasoning (with a touch of black pepper as well) to be just about right.      Fortunately, we saved room to try one of the desserts.  We opted for the Peach & Blackberry Cobbler with sweet basil and whipped sour cream.  The crust was sweet and sugary in flavor which offset the tartness of the berries in the cobbler. The fruit tasted like lemon juice was used to add brightness.  This is one of those desserts that the sum is better than the individual parts.  When I got fruit, crust, and cream in one mouthful, this was delicious!  I would like to come back again to try some dishes on the evening menu as well.  Review #90

I was looking for a pair of Men's black dress shoes and stopped by this location.  This vast space had helpful signs posted above the aisles to help me quickly find the area of the store I needed to search.  The aisles here don't go to the ceiling, but stay below eye level, so it was easy to view the entire store from any location.  It also eliminated the need for climbing steps on a ladder to reach any shoe.    Being that I had a clear view, I quickly realized that this was a self-serve business.  (If anyone was helping customers out on the floor, they were not quickly identified.)  So, I headed over to my section and saw a variety of options to meet my needs.  Below each pair of displayed shoes are the boxes of that type with the sizes on the end of each box.  Surprisingly, most were ordered from smallest to largest!  Unfortunately, the size I usually get wasn't available in all the varieties. However, since it was so easy to scan the sizes, it only took me a few minutes to find a pair that met both size and style requirements.    The aisles are also wide enough that I was able to comfortably try one of the fitting benches that allowed me to sit and put on the prospective purchase without being nudged by other shoppers in the same aisle!    Upon making my selection, there was a bit of a wait for the next open checkout register.  Only two were open since it was a Wednesday morning.  The clerk was cordial and asked the customary questions about my interest in receiving emails about sales.  Nothing too intrusive, so she quickly determined I only wanted my shoes and she expedited the process.  Overall, I would say good selection at a nice price and polite service.  That's what I was hoping for.  Review #321

This was an interesting historic site to visit on President's Day since Benjamin Harrison was our nation's 23rd President and the only one from Indiana.  He was also the grandson of the 9th president, William Henry Harrison (from Ohio).    The tour started in a welcome center at the back of the property and then the group walked around to the front entrance of the home to meet "the Butler".  He informed us that we were no longer living in the current time, but had traveled back to when Harrison was on leave from the White House for a short visit.  Several of the rooms in the home had character actors playing the roles of Harrison, his wife, and a grouchy cook.  We also had a tour guide walk us through the rest of the rooms.      We were informed that about 75% of the furnishings were original, while the rest were procured to fill in for missing pieces.     Overall, I found the tour informative, but seemed targeted towards the children in the group more than the adults.  I would also have liked it more if there were brochures or something with more information about the house and its residents were available.  Sure, I can look up the website, but as I am going through a place, I like to see something that might help me retain more about the information passed along by the tour guide.  (Note:  They do have a timeline of events and something about the size of a large bookmarker, but not much about the pieces inside the home.)     Also, parking can be a problem and I don't believe the building has been retrofitted to make it handicap accessible.  So, no fifth star for these issues, but still, it's a pretty interesting way to spend a little over an hour.  Review #229

This park is going to be so cool when it grows up.  Developed in 2017, the park has a new Amphitheater, paved walkways, two bridges that span Pleasant Creek which now handles more water (it's deeper and wider), a firehouse themed playground, and a gazebo.  Parking is conveniently located on the south.  From there, you can walk down the broad steps to the main level of the park or take a slight detour to the paved sloped trails which lead from the west end of the parking area.    The only knock I have is that the grass and the plantings aren't ready for all the activities the city wants to put on here.  I hope that whenever they have festivals and activities, that the plants will hold up to the foot traffic of all those who don't stay on the paved paths.  But once the plants get established, this should be a beautiful addition to the city's park and trail offerings.  Review #776

Grandma's Oven has opened a bakery in Camby after running a successful business in Plainfield.  I was driving down SR 67 near the entrance to Heartland Crossing and noticed the bakery's sign right next to the Subway shop (you can get to it from the entrance for Meijer.)  After parking in front of the store, the owners greeted and welcomed me to look around their facility.    The new place has "right sized" to being a bakery choosing to no longer offer sandwiches.  They now concentrate on offering fresh baked cookies, brownies, cupcakes, large loaf and fruit breads, and coffee cakes.  While browsing, I noticed they also offer some Indiana Artisan food items, some home goods, and have a nice size area on the back half of the store for groups to rent.    I decided to select three types of cookies from the large self-serve case on the right hand wall.  I went with a chocolate chip, snickerdoodle, and a peanut butter cookie.  They also have seven other types of cookies to select from.  All the cookies are $2, or 12 for $20,  These are some nice sized cookies too!  The chocolate chip was about 4" across and about 1/4 inch thick.  The cookie was crisp and loaded with lots of semi-sweet chocolate.  The snickerdoodle was about 3.75 inches and about a half inch thick.  This was a little softer cookie and had plenty of cinnamon and sugar on top without overwhelming the cookie taste.  The peanut butter cookie, though only 3.25 inches was a full 3/4 inch thick.  Nice peanut buttery aroma and a nice flavor.  Not quite as strong a peanut butter taste as some of my homemade ones, but the flavor intensified as I got closer to the center.      I also got to sample a bit of fresh baked pumpkin bread and of course, bought a loaf for home.  The loaf is a pretty good sized 9" x 3.5" and what I really liked was that the outer crust had a bit of crispness that kept the inside nice and moist.  (My wife loves the crust and ends!)    The owners said that the breads can be frozen for extended periods by wrapping them in aluminum foil and placing in a ziploc bag.  They do not use preservatives, so they recommend refrigerating any baked goods if you aren't consuming them right away.    Overall, I got great service and really good baked goods.  And if you have any guilt for trying them, there is a gym around the corner of the building! :)  p.s.  They offer coffee and I think they may have some tea as well.  Review #314

My wife and I stopped in for lunch on Sunday and had really good burgers provided by pleasant staff.  We took advantage of the free street parking instead of pulling into the private lot on the north side of the restaurant.  We were greeted before we entered the building and when asked if it was our first visit, received an explanation about ordering.  Basically, take a menu, figure out what you want, place the order at the counter, take a number back to your table, and let them deliver your meal to your table.    I must say that although we were told about 8 minutes for our burger to be prepared, I think it may have been even less!  So, not really fast food, but a lot faster than most higher end burger places I have dined.  Yes, the burgers are expensive, but that is because the beef is grass fed.  I was impressed that even though grass fed tends to be leaner, the beef was cooked through without becoming dry.    My wife ordered the third pounder with cheese.  It is a large sandwich and comes with a build your own holder to reduce the amount of juice dripping down your arm.  She needed a to go box.    I went with the C N Cheese burger that comes with cheddar, truffle mascarpone, parmesan, "salad" (Lettuce and lots of it!), and batch brewed tomato relish & aioli.  I thought the flavor was really good!  Even though there were lots of flavors, they didn't hide the burger taste which is essential for my burger dining requirements.      I ordered the Kumara Fries which are a type of sweet potato fry:  Less salt, but a nice dipping house "BurgerFuel" aioli.  They were okay, but the fries are not very appealing to look at.  They come out dark, appearing nearly black in places.  The flavor was okay, but again, they don't look that appealing.    I passed on trying one of the alcoholic beverages and opted for a chocolate shake.  The flavor was deep, more like a chocolate chip/semi-sweet taste.  Really good and thick too!  Still, it seemed a bit high priced (about $5) for a shake in a paper cup.    Although the music was pumping, we had no trouble carrying on our conversation.  Maybe it was due to all the windows being open instead of being closed.  Glad to see that management was listening to the suggestion to keep it at a reasonable volume.    Overall, it was a good first visit.  I wonder if they will eventually add more selections to the menu.  It did seem rather limited for folks wanting to try something different without going into veggie burgers.  The quality is good, but expect to spend at least $10 per person.  Review #342  p.s.  This is one of those places that doesn't offer putting a tip on your card.  If you want to tip, you need to bring cash.  Not sure why businesses don't offer that convenience.

Although I used to live in Greenwood, I never took time to explore this park.  From Main Street, which is the entrance you can drive through, it appears to be just a baseball diamond.  But when you slow down and enter the park, you see all kinds of things to do.  Beyond the initial parking lot, a lane winds its way back toward a creek that runs through the middle of the park.  Additional parking near the creek is convenient to reach the tennis and basketball courts, the multiple site playgrounds, the shelter and restrooms, and even the dog park!  If hiking is more your source of fun, you can walk over the bridge spanning the creek by the parking lot and get a good work out.  To the right, you wind between the creek and a clean dirt landfill that has elevated the ground about ten feet (the area is fenced in for safety reasons).  If you go straight after crossing the bridge, it leads you up a hill.  If you stay to the left, the trail leads you towards the entrance of the park.  I don't think the park has a loop to bring you back without retracing your steps.  I look forward to checking the park out once the weather is warmer and the foliage is in full greenery.  Review #544

Nice atmosphere, good food and service, and a reasonable price for the quality. On Thursday, I stopped by for lunch after parking out front on South Street.  (There is a parking garage just north of the Alexander Hotel that has a sky bridge connecting to the building.)  Since I was dining alone, I sat in the bar.  Having dined at the restaurant a half dozen times before, this was the first time I was seated in this area.  The area over the bar is a giant curved white board that is decorated with a mural and a list of some of the bar specials.  The lunch menu is easier to read than it was when the restaurant first opened.  Now, the lunch entrees are listed on the top of the small sheet and the sides are listed below.  The entrees come with one side per order.  For those with more of an appetite, you may order any of the entrees in a bento box which has the entree and your choice of three sides ($6 upgrade).  You can choose three of one item, or three individual items, or any combination that reaches that sum.  Today, I went with the Brie BLT entree and opted for the standard single item:  Spicy Peanut Noodles.  The sandwich comes out on a square trimmed bun (very soft bread) and has a generous slab of softened brie with heirloom tomato, arugula, and a surprisingly salty layer of bacon.  Although the bacon was saltier than I normally like, the rest of the sandwich worked to tone down the effect.    The side dish was a spaghetti type noodle in an orange sauce.  The menu mentioned napa cabbage and shaved carrot, but I didn't really see anything resembling them in their natural state.  The noodles were also served cold which was a surprise as well.  After my initial reaction, I did adjust quickly to the cool pasta as the flavor jumped to the forefront.  Definitely a nice peanut taste with a bit of spicy heat, but nothing too strong for anyone who eats spicy wings or Asian food.    Overall, it was an enjoyable lunch with pleasant service.  My waitress mentioned that some new items were being tested and should hopefully roll out soon.  Review #186

I enjoyed my experience and the food here.   I think that if I had done a bit more research before stopping in, I would have enjoyed it more.  I knew this place was getting a buzz on Yelp, so I decided to stop by.  I had heard of "Bubble Tea" but other than it being something like tapioca, I really wasn't sure what to expect.    The shop is very bright and colorful right on Broad Ripple Ave (62nd St.)  In the window next to the door is a simulation/installation of the types of crepes that are available.  Inside, there are a couple posters that provide some information about traditional Boba and "Popping Boba".      There are also a number of pamphlets available inside the shop that list the menus.  When I had a chance to look over the options, I decided to try the "Merry Berry" Hot Crepe and a Fruit Tea "Peach" (bubble tea).  I placed my order for in house dining (there are a number of odd sized stools and tables to choose from and a bar with seating along the west wall).  To the left of the area where I placed my order, additional napkins and plasticware were available.    After a few minutes, my chilled drink and hot crepe were brought out to me.  My server pointed out that there was a plastic lid/film stretched over the top of the bubble tea and that the over sized straw provided had a pointed edge on the bottom to be used to pierce the lid.  The over sized straw is necessary because the boba inside, along with ice and the flavored tea, swells and cannot be drawn through a standard sized straw.      I found the tea to have a really nice fruity flavor and when I got my first boba, it was a bit of an odd sensation.  The texture is like chewing a small rounded gummy bear.  It is supposed to be sweet, but I couldn't really taste much flavor due to the other flavors already in the tea.    The hot crepe I selected was really delicious!  The crepe was wrapped around a combination of blueberries (which tended to settle in the bottom), banana strips, nutella, and custard.  The crepe was rolled into a conical shape and then flattened and served in a paper and plastic wrapping.  I wasn't sure how I was supposed to eat the crepe since the wrapping was designed to slide off the bottom, not the kind that can be peeled a little at a time.  Also, the paper plate that is provided is too small to hold the over sized crepe, so I wasn't sure that if I slid off the wrapping that I could cut the crepe without it leaking all over.  So, I grabbed a couple extra napkins and used those to hold the stripped crepe while I nibbled it from the top down.  Once I figured out a method, I was able to really enjoy my selection.  Maybe someone has a better way than what I found.  Now that I have an idea of what to expect, I can imagine my next visit will require less distraction and more time to enjoy my choices.  Review #323

Just west of the business district on 116th street is Park Drive which leads you into a circular 34 acre park.  The park has so many activities that it doesn't matter your age, you might feel like a kid again!    There is plenty of parking on the south side of the circle (it is the only side for entrance).  In the middle, there is a building that has the restrooms and water fountains.  To describe the park, imagine the park as a clock with the park entrance being where the "6" is on the clock.  On the outer perimeter at 7, there are a couple basketball courts.  At 8 through 12 is a baseball park with its own concession and restroom stand.  From 1 to 3 is a wooded area with its own shelter and picnic tables.  And from 4 to 6 is a soccer field.  There is also a large perimeter sidewalk for hikers to loop around all these features.  But if you have little kids, you may not even notice all those activities I just listed.  Right next to the central building is the playground.  It appears there may be a flat water feature on the approach to a shelter.  (The water wasn't present during my early April visit, but there are holes that look like they could be either water jets or collection points.)  Beyond that is a spectacular playground with lots of vertical pieces which make for long tubular sliding!  But if your kids are afraid of heights, there are still many other pieces including swings and other climbing features.    The most unique piece I found looks like an elevated and enclosed seating area with two benches facing each other.  There is a ramp that leads into the center of the piece that allows wheel chair access.  I couldn't figure out what the piece was at first, and then I saw the flaps behind the benches where friends could stand and use their weight to rock the seats in between.  Sure, you need friends to play with, but with all the kids in the park, it didn't seem like it would be hard to encourage others to play here.  (See my photo to help you understand what it looks like.)  The equipment is pretty new having replaced the original equipment of the park.  The landscaping and maintenance of the park was maintained as well.  This park is a great addition to the Fishers park system.  Review #797

Despite the sterile colors of this new home for the restaurant, the staff made us feel welcome on our lunchtime visit.  There was plenty of room to grab a chair (seat yourself style).  Our hostess/waitress swiftly brought out menus and our drink orders.  We even got to place our orders quickly.  However, there was a longer wait than expected for lunch.  But the food was reasonably priced and the taste was really good!  My wife ordered a low cal plate and opted for tuna salad as her main item.  The large plate came with a sliced hard-boiled egg, tomato slices, a cup of peaches, another of cottage cheese and some cheese slices with crackers.  She said it all tasted fresh and was quite filling.  I ordered the lightly breaded cod (sandwich) and was able to pick the toppings I wanted.  I also got a side of onion rings.  The cod was cooked just right and was moist with just enough flavor in the breading to complement the fish.  It was served on a fluffy white bun that managed to keep all my toppings held within.    The onion rings were lightly battered as well and although a little "juicy" inside, the flavor was sweet and yummy.  They could have gone just a little longer to crisp the outsides more, but I preferred these to being burned.  The onion itself was very tender.  Overall, I like the new location and can see stopping by here again to try some of the other options (including breakfast fare.)    Review #282

A variety of flavors awaits!  Whether it's a salad, appetizer, or a sandwich that interests you, there is plenty to choose from.  My wife and I brought our good friends with us to lunch on Tuesday.  After being greeted and seated, we began ordering a number of tasty items.  For appetizers, we selected the small order of Duck Wings, Pat's Philly Pretzel Nuggets, and the "Grilled Bloomy".  We selected the Korean BBQ style for our wings.  The small order has 3 pieces and was served crispy over a bed of arugula.  The Korean style was delicious with a hint of heat and a bit of saltiness.  We got another small sample of the hot sauce ($1 for the extra flavor) and found it disappointing.  Not much heat and some odd bits at the bottom of the cup.  The Pretzels were generously stacked and came with a piping hot bowl of beer cheese.  The flavor of the pretzels and cheese were good, but the sauce was a bit thin and didn't stick to the pretzels other than as a fine coat.  However, once the cheese cooled a bit, we found (after most of the pretzels had been devoured) that the cheese stayed thicker and delivered more flavor.  The pretzels were more soft style than crispy throughout.  And the "Grilled Bloomy", which comes with a rotating variety of accompanying items, was a warm brie cheese.  This time, it came with Granny Smith apple slices, a jellied fruit, and unsalted crackers.  The best flavor came when all four items were combined into a mini sandwich.  Lots of crunch and gooey texture of savory, tart, and sweetness.  For salads, I highly recommend the "Buttah" if you like salad that is sweet and refreshing, and the "Romaine" (which was good, but not as delightful) for a more savory style.  The "Buttah" featured butter lettuce, strawberries, white onion, feta cheese, and white balsamic dressing.  Every bite was full of flavor and is something I could order again and again.  My friend ordered the Romaine which came with asparagus, radish, sliced hard boiled egg, capers, Parmesan, lemon & olive oil.  He said it was pretty good too, just didn't have that "wow" factor.  For our entrees, we got the "Bacon", "Hoosier", "Blue Bison", and "No Meatloaf".  Three out of four got great reviews.  The "Bacon", a BALT was loaded with oven baked bacon and came with Aji sauce on Sourdough.  Our friend likes the bacon less crisp than I do, so he loved the way the bacon produced a chew.  I'm talking about a half inch worth of sliced bacon on the sandwich!  He said he would gladly order the sandwich again.    His wife ordered the "Blue Bison" burger which came with a nicely portioned bison patty, with blue cheese, bacon, and topped with onion straws.  The burger (she went with medium) had a nice browning flavor that came through without being buried in the blue cheese flavors.  Note:  the bison meat is very lean, so it can seem a little dry, but the bun was quite fresh and although the sandwich lacked the juiciness associated with beef burgers, the flavor was great!  My wife went with the "Hoosier" pork patty with Granny Smith apple slices, smoked Gouda, and hickory dijon (she left off the arugula).  Having ordered this the first time we dined there, I knew she would enjoy it.  She did!  Definitely would recommend this to first timers.  Finally, I had the "No Meatloaf" option since I had seen a number of folks speak well of it on Yelp.  Sadly, I must be too much of a carnivore to appreciate the vegan offering.  Although the plate looked like meatloaf with gravy over mashed potatoes, with green beans and onion crisps, the comparison to meatloaf ended with appearance.  The consistency of the loaf reminded me of dressing and had a strong spice flavor that I can't quite identify.  I thought it was okay, but none of my dining mates liked it at all.  I would not order this again.  Oh, I also ordered a side of Mexican Street corn.  This was an entire ear of corn (still on the cobb), partially charred and coated with (I'm guessing) cotija cheese and paprika.  Very colorful presentation and a wonderful blending of flavors.  I highly recommend it.  So, with a few limited misses, we all left with plenty to eat and enjoyed the offerings at Shoefly.  Seriously, bring friends who don't mind sharing so that you can get bites of many different things.  It's worth it!  Rev #10

Although a lot of the park is open green space and lacks much character, I love the look of the playground and main pavilion area.  If I was a little kid again, this is the kind of playground I would have totally enjoyed.  Instead of the run of the mill playground like most parks, this place features "rocks" and sand trails.  I loved climbing and digging as a kid.  When you add the hidden surprises formed into the rock piles, I couldn't help but start searching for more (and there are plenty!)  The pavilion is large and has lots of shaded area and tables to relax while the kids play close by.  The grounds looked well maintained and the parking lot was just a few steps away if you needed to get something from the car.   Review #740

This 16 acre park is located on the east side of Carmel on Main St, nestling back into a neighborhood.  The front of the park has a lot of open space which turns out to be a mini disc golf course.  It has only 9 holes and the distances are on the short side compared to other area parks.  (Kid Sized?)  The entry road has parking spaces all along the way as it bends around the splash park, the large shelter, and back towards the woods where a small playground tower is nestled in the trees.  One side of the tower has wind chimes that vibrated along the rails of the tower while I was there.  Nice touch!    You could take a short hike through the woods, but because of the small size, you are within viewing distance of the nearby houses behind the park.  If you are looking for hiking, I would suggest other parks would offer more enjoyment.  The park seems to be well maintained and looks like a fun place for kids during the summer.  Otherwise, it's kind of limited.  Review #741

After lunch, I made a few stops and found myself in the neighborhood of this family owned business. (They own a shop in Florida as well.)  They are located between the Starbuck's and the McAlister's on SR 135, so there is plenty of convenient parking.  I was surprised at how many options were available for customers.  They have a wall display that shows the options.  They have pre-assigned scoop amounts for the different sized cups and cones.  Since I had already eaten and was only interest in a single scoop, the server suggested the "kiddie" size bowl which worked out fine!  I really like ice cream, but ever since Cafe Nonna closed in Fountain Square, I have been looking for a place to get gelato.  Ta da!!!  I was able to get a Cinnamon Apple Pie Gelato and was I happy!  Saturated flavor with a nice balance of cinnamon and apple flavors.  Nice texture that didn't melt before I could finish it.  Delicious!  And all their servings come with an animal cracker on top just to make it fun.  I got a lion, so hear me roar!  This is good!!!  Review #396

First, a place in Broad Ripple that actually has on site parking gets a star for that!  As it was, we grabbed one of the last places even though it was around 5 pm because a huge wedding party was filling one of the rooms.  Fortunately, the dining room we were seated in was much quieter and we got our choice of seating.  The menu is modest in size and has a few weekly specials as well.  I was in the mood for an appetizer and went with the crab cakes.  Wow!  Two decent sized patties, pan fried and served with Poblano Pico (with a bit of heat), Chipotle crema, and Cilantro.  Totally delicious!  My wife wasn't as hungry and went with the Hawaiian Turkey Burger with a side of waffled sweet potato fries.  The fries were crispy on the outside and tender inside.  The sandwich meat which may have been a bit dry on its own benefited from the teriyaki sauce, grilled pineapple, and garlic aioli (and Swiss cheese too.)  She asked for honey mustard and they gave her some honey mustard dressing and she said the flavor was really good.  I was a bit hungrier than her, so I went with the Filet Forestiere - 8 oz filet cooked to order (medium rare for me!) and served with Burgundy Mushroom sauce, mashed potatoes, and sauteed Spinach.  The dinner was served stacked which made it a little awkward when the meat sunk into the potatoes while cutting, but I soon adapted and before long, was enjoying a really tasty combo.  The burgundy mushrooms had a great savory flavor (not too salty like some places I've been) and it paired well with the other items.  I also liked that the sauteed spinach was not mushy and the bright green color kept the meal looking appetizing, not like a large brown mound.    In spite of there being a large party in the other room, we did not experience any delay in getting our food delivered.  We had just a few minutes between the time we finished the appetizer and started the entrees.  Good timing!  It had been a long time since my last visit.  I am glad I made a point of stopping back and hope to get back again soon.  Review #580

This is a really nice park west of Greenwood near the Center Grove Schools.  Although electric transmission lines run over the eastern edge of the open space (including the driveway as you enter), the playgrounds, shelters, and most of the park are far enough away to make the wires and towers nothing more than an eyesore.  As you drive the winding blacktop road up to the top of the hill, you get a good view of the open area where there is a hiking trail that has some physical workout stations along the way.  At the hilltop, there is a parking lot that surrounds a central shelter.  A restroom building is to the right of the parking lot.  Beyond the central shelter, there is a large playground that has equipment for bigger kids separated from the pieces designed for the littler ones.  There is a mini basketball court beyond one of the most diverse swing set collections I've seen in Central Indiana.  There are swings of all sizes and configurations so that infants and kids who need wheelchairs can enjoy a good swing!  Beyond the swings is also a music area where kids can bang away on a variety of "instruments" to make music...or maybe just noise.
