Each end of the playgrounds has another shelter and across from the south end shelter is a full sized basketball court that seemed in good shape.  I did notice that a number of the large shade trees that line the north and west edges of the park have been cut down since my last visit.  Still, there is plenty of shade surrounding the playground, but none directly over the equipment.    Dogs are welcome as long as they are on a leash and the park generally has hours of sunrise to sunset.  Now that school is back in session, the park has few attendees during the day.  But during the summer, it can get crowded quite rapidly, so plan accordingly.  Review #1356

The former Northeastway Park shares an entrance with the golf course/driving range on the east side of the road.  The main feature of the park is the 20 year old aquatic center which has two sizes of swimming pools, a spray park, a large water slide, and a zero depth entry pool.  Outside of the summer attraction, there are numerous shelters, tennis courts, basketball, sand volleyball, and a playground.    Although there have been some reviews that refer to this park as "little", the park has over 85 acres which is enough for a disc golf course and some wooded hiking/running trails.  Parking is spread over a great length of the park, so you don't have to park far from where your main interest lies.  Review #735

I stopped in for lunch during the week and after backing into my street parking spot (yes, that is how you have to do it on this one way street!), I grabbed a seat at the bar.  The place was fairly packed and they had some ballgames on the big screens over the bar.  I decided to try the Italian Beef (sliced with spiced au jus, giardiniera & peppers on an Italian Roll) with a side of house-made slaw.  For being busy, the sandwich and slaw came out pretty quickly.  The sandwich was really large.  The roll was bun was thick and was filled with the beef and fillings.  The peppers were draped over the top and then potato chips were placed over the whole thing.  The slaw was served in a separate paper bowl.  The flavors on both were okay.  Nothing wrong with them, just not much wow factor.  The slaw was very creamy without much sweetness.  The beef was thin sliced AND cubed.  The cubed pieces were a bit on the chewy side.  The flavor was okay, but the beef itself didn't have much flavor.  Mainly, the giardiniera added the flavor and a bit of heat from the peppers.  So, why not better than 3?  Well, the sandwich was really hard to eat because of the diameter.  I have a big mouth, so I was able to cram it in there, but it required some compression before biting.  The chips being served on top also added volume, so I had to remove them from off the sandwich as well.  Juicy? Oh my!  When I picked up the sandwich, I could tell that the soft bun was soggy on the bottom and the juice ran down my wrist onto my shirt sleeve before I could set it down to grab a paper towel off the roll that was set in front of me.  I am glad the beef was juicy, but I shouldn't have to wash my shirt from the juice!  Oh, and the chips that had fallen off on their own were soggy too.  So, one point off for no 'wow factor' and another off for the difficulty handling/soggy issue.    The service was prompt and courteous.  The flavor was fine.  So, maybe the next time I would try something else and not have an issue with the au jus.    Review #240

Keeping it simple, I really enjoyed the flavors of the food I tried.  I went with a Combo Special that came with a side of fries and a jumbo drink.  I don't know enough about the cuisine here to tell you what kind of meat it had (some lamb blend, I would guess) or what the white sauce was (it was delicious!)  All I know is that the kitchen is openly visible and I could see one of the staff shave the thin layers of meat for my meal right after my order.  The veggie toppings I had him add were all fresh and tasty (even if the tomato was on the pinkish side).  And the base of the gyro (Naan?) was light as a pancake, sturdy enough to be picked up and eaten that way, or tender enough to be easily cut through with the self serve plastic ware.  There is a very strange vibe here mixing what could be a very nice dining experience with the inner workings of gas station.  The seating is not near  the order counter (not even in the line of sight) which makes it weird to sit while waiting for your order to come up.  Even when I mentioned it was a "to go" order, I had to ask about napkins/plastics and forgot to get any salt packets for my crispy fries which were basically salt free.  If they could work on customer service a bit and make the restaurant part fit together with the seating they could be a five star experience.  Right now, I would only recommend orders to go.  Review #825

If you want to escape from the crowds at the Indianapolis Zoo, take comfort knowing that your ticket gets you into the White River Gardens as well!  The Hilbert Conservatory is where you will find indoor and tropical plants.  As a bonus, the Butterfly Kaleidoscope has returned this year (into September) where you can watch butterflies released from their incubator.  There are plenty of colorful butterflies winging their way throughout the two story structure.    The outside gardens were just beginning to show color during my visit.  Although the water works had not been activated yet, I can imagine that the gurgling sound of water splashing in the fountains will combine with the breeze to make this area as calm as it is beautiful.  Even without the water (mid April), I could see that the numerous fountains and ornamental statues would be the foundation for some great photos.  The addition of colorful flowering plants, shrubs, and trees will surely create a space that is worth stopping by.    Note that to enter the outdoor gardens, you must first go into the White River Gardens Building and after showing your ticket, you will pass into a small room where one door leads to the indoor garden and another on the left leads to the outdoor gardens.    The outdoor gardens are arranged into a variety of styles.  Each of these areas has the name of the garden written in the footpath as you stroll along.  Lots of artwork (mostly limestone) can be found in the Knot Garden and along the wall of the Ornamental Allee (not a typo!)    I look forward to returning in the summer to see how much the view has changed.  Review #269

I stopped in at the brewery after sampling some of their beers in bottles or on draft elsewhere.  So, after parking in their lot on the south side of their building, I opted to sit at the bar so that I could get a good view of the beer options mounted on the wall.  The bartender was friendly and explained that they had options for flights.  I went with one that featured five standard house beers and because they were out of the sixth (Hefeweizen), I was able to substitute from the seasonal side of beers as my sixth.  The flights serve 3 oz glasses for $7.50 for all six.  I was pleased with the flavor on all the beers.  I remember trying some of them in bottles I bought at a store when I was first starting to drink craft beers.  I am so glad I gave those a second chance to redeem themselves.  They really did.  I think the standout for me was the stout which had a deep flavor that was somewhere between a coffee and a chocolate taste (at least to me.)  The IPA was also good without being so hopped up that the bitterness was overwhelming.  Good beers, friendly staff, and lots of games/art to look at.    They also have outdoor seating that is covered by the overhanging roof.  There also appears to be a stage on the west end of the parking lot for entertainment.  Review #1010

Okay, I will be the first to admit that when it comes to all the fancy coffee drinks, I am no expert.  But for a cup of black coffee that you can drink when it is served (and not burn your taste buds), this place gets a top score!  Nice flavor and prompt service are always in style.    I also ordered a tasty blueberry muffin which the staff offered to heat for me.  Quite good without being soggy from too many blueberries.  Just right.  I appreciated that I was notified that some additional baked goods were just coming out of the oven, but I thought the muffin enough for my morning.  Still, it is nice to think the staff is aware of what's going on in the backroom and making sure the customers are kept informed.  There are several spots along Johnson for street parking (which is a one way street).  The interior is bright and has modest decor with consignment art on the walls and a nook filled with books right near a pair of comfy chairs.  Most of the seating is standard table and chairs.  The menu is on the blackboard behind the order counter.  Pastries are under glass at the counter so you can see what is available.  Overall, a well thought out place to stop for a coffee and a bite.  Review #1120

Note:  Review is for the mural on the outside of the building  One of the keys to having a successful business is getting people/customers to notice you are in business.  What better way than to put a bright and colorful mural on the side of your building which is clearly visible from a main thoroughfare like Keystone Avenue?    In 2016, the business owners commissioned the FAB Crew (Fantastic Aerosol Brothers) to create a full sized mural for their location.  Done in deep colors of purples, oranges, and greens, the mural has a huge face with lots of swirling shapes and highlights that seem to have an electric quality to their appearance.  I'm not very good at determining if the shapes are meant to be letters and spell out words, I guess I spent too many years being a dull accountant to be able to pick the letters out correctly, but if I had to guess, I would say that the symbols spell out "smoke" and "vape" based on the nature of the business.  Or, I could be totally wrong. Oh well!  Review #1585

Great food and beer are available at this brewpub.  I stopped in on Friday around noon and took a seat at the bar.  The bartender was putting up the latest menu detail on the blackboard behind the bar.  A warm greeting and an introduction to the taplist and menu became his priority.    After a few minutes review of the options, I went with a flight of four brews.  My choices were: the Whimsy (Summer Saison); Maibock; Dunkel (Brown Lager); and Muse (Strong Golden Ale with a 9% ABV).  Based upon our discussion, he threw in a sample of another beer that he thought I might enjoy (The Vacation Kolsch).  Overall, the flavors were unique and very tasty.  Because I am new to craft beer, the Whimsy, Maibock, and Vacation were beers I would order again.  The other two, although tasty, were something that might appeal to those with more experience.    The taproom welcomes food deliveries from nearby restaurants to be consumed in the taproom and on the spacious patio, however, they have some very delicious sounding items made in house as well.    For lunch, I went with the House Sandwich "Volume 5" with chips.  This isn't your stereotypical "bar food"....this sandwich was fantastic!  First they start with Semolina bread from Amelia's Bakery in Fountain Square.  They also add 6.5 ounces of Cotto, Saucisson Rouge, & Lomo Ham from Smoking Goose Meats.  They add farmstyle cheese (Haymaid's) and Sun Dried Tomato puree and sour cream.  All these items are stacked on the grill and pressed so that the bread gets toasted and crunchy.  On the side, they provide arugula and pickled red onions, which my bartender recommended putting on the sandwich as well.  My only complaint is that this sandwich will only have a limited run of availability before a "Volume 6" replaces it.  (They have salads and tasting plates as well.)    I can't say how the place is during "drinking hours", but if you want a tasty pairing of food and ale, try this brewpub for lunch or dinner.  Review #72

The good news is that the food was tasty and the service (lunch time) was pleasant and prompt.  I arrived a little after they opened on a Saturday and was a little confused about where to park since there aren't any painted lines.  They do have a section for wait service on the north side, but nobody was parked there.  (The waitress said that when they are open, they do provide curb service.)    So, I found a spot around the south side of the building and walked up to the "order window".  There are a variety of options for burgers, dogs, and pizzas.  They also have a number of ice creams, sundaes, and shakes available too!    I selected the single "Suds Burger" which comes with a slice of processed cheese, shredded lettuce, dill pickle chips, and "special sauce".  I also ordered the onion rings and a root beer float.  The burger had really good flavor, but I did notice that the bun felt cold.  A little time on the grill or even a toaster would have made a better first impression since the sandwich felt cold.      The onion rings were lightly breaded and had a nice crunch in each bite.  The onions were sweet and the breading stayed on the onions, not falling off like some places.  The lightness of the breading kept them from being greasy and allowed the flavor of the breading to come through without overwhelming the onions.    I did find the root beer float to be the most disappointing.  Although the flavor was good, the presentation in a styrofoam cup with lots of that off brown foam being all that was visible was not very appealing.  There also was just a single scoop of ice cream in the root beer, so it was gone well before the root beer.  I think they may have mugs, but they were not chilled that early in the day.  Not sure if they would have used a mug for the float or not.    At the time I went, there were no car enthusiasts on site.  This place is run by classic car enthusiasts and draws them in during the evening hours.  So, even though there are times when you can go to check out the cars, lunch time was not one of them.    I appreciated that they kept a lot of the nostalgic look and even some of the equipment from an old drive in diner.  But even with the "oldies" music playing on the speakers, I didn't capture that feeling from my boyhood when going to the local drive in was a big deal.  I applaud the effort, if not the result.  Review #316

I stopped by for lunch today and ordered the brisket sandwich with a side of charred carrots and an additional side of mac & cheese.  Good food and overall, a very positive experience.  The staff was very friendly and welcoming.  I appreciated when my waitress brought out my meal and mentioned that the giardiniera is great when it's put on the sandwich instead of leaving it as a side item.  She was right!  There is a lot of bread making up the bun and by the time you add several thick cuts of brisket and caramelized onions, there isn't much room to add anything else.  But the acidity of the pickled veggies and the slightly bitter and salty olives add levels of flavor.    The meat itself is thick and moist, reminding me of stewing beef without the deep charring.  Still, the flavor was good.  The charred carrots were a nice surprise for my side.  Just a hint of sweetness released from the carrots.    The mac & cheese side comes with one veggie and one topping.  I decided on the broccoli and cheddar ritz topping.  The mac and cheese uses a light and creamy bechamel that doesn't bind the pasta into clump.       I would recommend giving this place a try!  Review # 175

I stopped in for lunch midweek and enjoyed great food and good service.  I was seated right away after finding a spot in the lot outside.  They have indoor and outdoor seating when weather permits.  I chose inside to beat the heat.    Since I knew what I wanted, I was able to place my order and had a very short wait before a small Greek Salad arrived.  Very good with lots of cheese over the ice berg lettuce.  There was a single olive and pepper, and a couple small grape tomatoes.  Overall, the flavor was very good but could have used an extra olive or two.    Within a couple minutes of finishing my salad, my Gyro Platter arrived.  It was loaded with a lot of items.  Besides the "gyro meat" strips, there was an oven roasted potato, really delicious green beans (with onions) over rice pilaf, Tzatziki sauce, onions, a small tomato, feta cheese, and pita bread triangles.  I was pleased the meat was seasoned and though thinly sliced, remained moist.  I made combinations of the different items on the platter and everything seemed to pair well.  I definitely recommend the platter.  It was also quite filling!    So, for a first visit, this was an enjoyable place to grab lunch.  From the delightfully Greek inspired interior with photo and painted murals to the pleasant demeanor of the staff, this is a place I would gladly bring guests.  Review #353

I stopped by this small brewery in the corner of a strip mall located next to the Monon Trail.  Plenty of parking space and a nice outdoor patio area with a pebble base that may not be the easiest surface to negotiate if you have had a few too many.  Inside, there is a small room with an L-shaped bar that was filled with patrons even at 5 p.m. on a Monday.  The location under the sign that says to "place beer orders here" was already occupied.   I had to nudge my way in between the bar patrons to place my order which didn't endear me to the guys on either side of me.   I asked about getting a flight and here you can get as many samples as you like for $2.50 each.  I had a list of four that I copied from their website, but none of the four were available.  I usually prefer lighter beers and fewer hops, but all of the six house choices were either dark or IPA's.  Not a great start!  Fortunately, I was able to get three selections from the dark beers that were pretty good.  The Fred's Red Session IPA wasn't too hoppy and was pretty good (4.4% 50 IBU).  The Hally's Hoppy Brown Ale (6% 42 IBU) and the Double Diffie Imperial Stout (9% 32 IBU) were my other choices. The Double had a chocolaty almost smoky taste to my palate.    The brewery doesn't offer any foods, so my wife and I brought in some food, including jerk chicken from Jamaican Reggae Grill next door.  I assume that the intense spicy heat from the chicken made me perceive all three beers as being sweet.  I can't imagine that they are this sweet to everyone else, but be aware that if you grab something from the Caribbean restaurant, your palate may affect the taste of your selections.  Although the beers were okay and the bartender got to me fairly promptly, I definitely prefer a place with a bit more room.  The interior was dark and reminded me of an old dive bar.  I much preferred the spacious outdoor area that had plenty of tables and a fire pit that was going even when it was in the mid 80's temperature wise.  There is also a self serve water dispenser that is available near the back door.  It doesn't have any directions on which buttons to push, but I figured out there was a hot and a cold option without much delay.  If you are in the area, this is probably a fine place to pick up a dark beer or IPA.  But for my tastes, I prefer a place that keeps its website up to date, has a bit more room near the bar, and offers a variety of brews.  Review #312

I used to shop at the Kroger's a few miles north when I lived in Greenwood; Either that one or the Marsh that has become defunct.  Recently, this "new Kroger" was built on the southeast corner of SR 135 and Smokey Row Road and it is far bigger than either of the two I used to shop at.    This Kroger has a huge selection of produce to your right after you enter the prime shopping area.  Beyond the produce, there is a Bistro that has window seating (view of the parking lot, but hey, at least it's sunlight!)  The south end of the store also has a bakery and a butcher shop in the back that had three butchers working during my visit which made it easy to get my order wrapped and ready to go promptly.  Between the bakery and the butcher/deli areas, there is an extensive selection of local and commercial beer and wines.  I was surprised how many craft beers that were available to choose from.  The middle of the store seems to be two halves filled with groceries with numerous rows running east to west.  I like the idea of a central aisle down the middle of the products, but it does make you slow down to look at what's on each side of that aisle and makes you have to watch for carts pulling out into your way more frequently.  Of course, ever store seems to be set up a little differently, so unless the specific item you are looking for is listed overhead at the start of each aisle, you may be wandering around looking for help.  Seems like there are always people stocking shelves, but those more often than not aren't Kroger employees, but someone from a supplier.    The north end of the store carries a lot of non-food items and the back corner has the seasonal items which I rarely bother with while shopping, so I am glad it isn't in the way.  I was a little disappointed with the check out though.  Only one line was open for processing other than the six self help stations.  One of the stations was non-functioning, three had customers, and two were tied up with an employee trying to help another customer.  The customer was asking about a charge and had pushed her cart in front of the other only remaining checkout.  That's where the employee and the customer stood discussing some charges while not clearing the one that still had the customer's charges registering.  So, I still had to wait in line for one of the machines to open since the discussion seemed like it was going to go on.  Finally, I was able to get one of the machines and check out.  I will say that I found that each time I moved one of my bags off the "finished" area to make room for the next item, I found it irritating that the machine told me to put the bags back.  "Hey, give me room to check out my groceries or be quiet!"   You can't reason with machines any more than with employees. Sigh!  Checkout seems like that was probably a one-time problem, so I will give the store a pass and not ding them too hard.  Still, any employee stationed to help at that area needs to be aware of all the machines and to keep things flowing smoothly.  Review #2514

I know how good the food is at the deli side of the business, so I made a point of heading downtown to Fountain Square to pick something from the butcher shop that recently opened.  There are a few street parking places (west bound) and I was able to grab one right in front!    Inside, I was impressed at how clean the place looks.  Display cases of packaged goods for those items you might want to store in your freezer were stocked.  Displays of artisan chips and sauces/condiments were offering items to accessorize if you were going to get something to make your own sandwiches (they even had buns!)  There were glass display counters for you to be able to see cuts of meat and sausage/cold cuts all below eye level so that you could easily converse with the friendly staff who were there to assist in filling your order.  I also liked that they had some cooked samples of some of the sausages so that you could try before you buy.  I ended up buying both the cheddar brats and the hot Italian sausage.    Now understand that this is not some giant chain that can offer cheap cuts of meat at discounted prices.  This place is all about quality cuts and assisting you to get the right meat for what you want to prepare.  So, $10 a pound may scare off someone who wants to buy brats for a cookout (about 3-4 brats per pound).  But if you are like me and don't mind firing up the grill for just a couple people, you can get high quality meats where they don't skimp on flavor.  Unfortunately for me, I don't live anywhere close to this shop, but if I know I am in the area, I can pencil in making this stop last on my "to do's" and pick up something before heading home.  It's that good.  I hope that as the business grows, there will be a greater selection on display.  I assume a butcher shop will work with customers who call ahead to get special cuts, but for now, you only see certain types of meats.  Review #2765

Wow!  I was totally surprised by how delicious the Ram Dunker Burger was.  I was drawn in by the Indy Burger Week promotion and decided to try this $5 selection.  It's a 7 oz burger grilled to order (I like a nice char on mine, so medium-well!) and topped with cheddar jack cheese and served on a pub roll with au jus dipping sauce.  The burger tasted like steak!  The  char was just enough to bring out the full beef taste and the au jus had just enough saltiness to complement the flavor like an expensive cut.  While everyone else is trying to create flavor combinations that will be the next big thing, it is great to find a place that strips the sandwich down to the basics and lets the beef take center stage.  Great job!  I added the sweet potato fries as a side and the flavor of them was very sweet.  They may have been a little bit undercooked, because they broke when I picked them up instead of being crisped, but they seemed to melt in my mouth.  Again, another great choice!  I also tried the shorty flight to sample the beers.  Here you get three 10 oz selections of house beers for $9.  All three were good or better.  My favorite was the Hefeweizen that had a great balance of banana and clove flavors (5.2% 15 IBU).    I won't wait so long between visits to come back and try some more options.  Review #319

I stopped in for lunch on Tuesday and ordered the special of the day: fish and chips.  Prompt service and a meal that was exactly what I was looking forward to.  The quantity of food was just right for lunch and the price.  The fish was lightly breaded and fried enough to have a nice crunch while staying moist inside.  The fries were equally impressive.  Nice and crisp on the outside and steaming hot inside.  The fish was slender in profile, so it was fine as finger food not requiring utensils to cut it first.  With a pickle spear on the side, I had plenty to eat for under $10 (excl tip).  At lunch hour, there was a flow of patrons stopping in, but sitting in the bar near the entrance did not get too loud.  Overall, I enjoyed my meal and the ambiance of the state's oldest bar.  Review #203

Hey Guys!  Yes you guys out there who may be thinking this is a ladies only place for gals to hang out.  This is the perfect spot for you to pick out some great scents for your den or man cave!  Sure, there are lots of perfume-y options to choose from, but there are lots of scents for even the manliest of men.  And since it takes about an hour to go through the smelling, selecting, and actual making of the candles, you get to have an ice breaker/conversation with any lady you might take with you.    If you are with someone who wants to make a candle with three scents, they will usually need a helping hand to squeeze the third bottle of oil scents so you get to be the hero by literally lending a helping hand.  Once you've poured your candles, they have to sit for 90 minutes so that you aren't trying to haul around hot liquid wax.  So, the location is perfect for you to walk to one of the many restaurants along Mass Ave, grab a bite to eat or a cocktail, and then swing by to pick up your candles before you go.  Note that they will give you some final instructions for optimizing your candle's success when you pick it/them up.  I also like that if you buy 3, you get a fourth one for free.  My wife and I had only made 3, so we picked one of the single scented candles as our fourth.  As I write this, I am enjoying my Coffee/caramel/pistachio candle in my den.  It smells great!  This would make for a great date idea as well as a fun thing to do with a small group.  They also serve beer and wine, though I would suggest not getting too thirsty since you are dealing with intensely scented oils and hot melted wax.   Just follow instructions and ask for help if you aren't sure about what you are doing.  The staff is friendly and very knowledgeable about combinations if you have trouble coming up with anything on your own.  Just know that they can get really busy with only a limited number of staff working when there is a room full of customers.  Review #2733

From what I can tell, this is a locally owned restaurant.  So, if you are looking for a typical, but good, Chinese-American menu, give this place a try.  All the usual favorites are there.  We ordered broccoli beef, orange chicken, fried rice, fried pot stickers, and crab rangoon.  We also got a small serving of egg drop soup which is shareable too.  Wait times vary depending upon how many call in orders are ahead of you, but I got my walk up order about fifteen minutes after placing it.    There is an order counter that you use regardless of whether you are dining in or taking out.  They simply call out the order when it is ready, so paying attention to what you ordered as well as the cashier is important.  Like a lot of competitor restaurants, the seasoning is simple and not too spicy.  But the ingredients seemed freshly made (pot stickers, veggies) and everything stayed hot despite about a half hour difference in getting my order and sitting down at home to eat it.  They use excellent/reusable cartons instead of cheap styrofoam.  (I can always use those!)  The cashier was efficient and other than being a little soft spoken, was easy to deal with.  Review #2850

Whether your dog is big or little, you are sure to find something here that will allow you to spoil your buddy with something special.  Maybe it will be one of the in-house baked goods.  Maybe it will be one of the myriad of rawhides.  Maybe it's a packet of training snacks or new toy from the wall of colorful items.  I picked up some smaller treats from the baked goods counter I my dogs devoured them.  Just wish I would have picked up some more for the next day.  The folks who work there were friendly and seem like they are dog lovers too!    If you are in the old town village, stop by and pickup something for your special pooch!  Review #2217

One of the free parts of the Newfields (IMA) offerings is the 100 Acres Art and Nature Park, just west of the art museum.  This island is cool for hiking, checking out public art, and appreciating nature.  In the middle of the island is a large lake too!    The park has a number of art pieces that were installed in 2010.  A few of the pieces were temporary and have since been removed.  Disappointingly, those pieces have not been replaced by new pieces which would make return visits more interesting.  The park trails are generally flat and most are accessible in all weather.  However, during my visit, part of the northern trail around the lake had been closed for conservation purposes.   I appreciated that signs were posted advising of that closing before getting all the way to the spot where the trail ended.  Still, even with this limitation, there are plenty of paths to hike.   On the east end of the park, there is a visitors pavilion with restrooms and seating for resting if you wish to take a break or are getting too hot from hiking.  A series of bird feeders are located in front of a large window in the pavilion for those visitors who wish to bird watch.  The park was blooming with wildflowers and redbud blossoms during my early May visit.  Even though I was close to the traffic on 38th street, I couldn't hear any traffic, just the sound of multiple birds and the wind through the trees.  So close to town, yet it felt like I was far away.  The park is accessible for free from west bound 38th street. For those who are also visiting the art museum (fee required), you can cross the Waller Bridge that connects the Newfield grounds near the Lilly House to the 100 acre park.  Review #845

The new distillery/brewery from Sun King is open!  The building is spacious and has a lot of cool features to make the visitors happy.   First, despite the construction, you can get here from the east or west and park for free inside the new Midtown Parking Garage (located on Veterans Way).  Be careful of construction workers if you cross the Monon Trail, but you can get through!  Second, there is a new plaza being built right in front of the building, so Sun King has provided a nice sidewalk to skirt around the construction on the east side of where the plaza is going in.  That should add to the view of the location even more.  Next, the building is very cool.  Two stories of contemporary design with lots of wood (patterns on the walls, stairs, and a flag on the second floor) and lots of gray tones for a somewhat industrial look.  Note that this building doesn't look like a warehouse.  Also, a second floor patio is located on the west end of the building just outside of one of the bars.  Behind the second floor bar is a private room that can be reserved for parties.  Speaking of bars, there is one on each floor, both on the west end.  You can place your beverage orders directly at the bars and grab a seat there, or in one of the many seating areas.  However, you can also flag down one of the roving servers and they will take your beverage order and deliver it to you.  Each table top has a full menu of the liquors, the cocktails, the beers, and even a list of all the food items from each of the food vendors on site.  As far as food goes, three of the four food vendors were operating on day 1.  On the main floor, Oca has a shop in the center of the building, beyond the staircase.  They sell food to eat and packaged items to take home.  Also on the first floor is La Margarita (from Fountain Sq) serving Mexican dishes.  There is room for another restaurant to the right of La Margarita.  On the second floor, you can get pizza from Pi (which also has a food truck in Indy).    For all of the food vendors, you simply go to the counter, place your order and pay and then wait for your food.  I tried the personal sized pizza and only had to wait ten minutes on opening day.  Note that you pay for food at the counters and the beverages on a separate bill unless you are getting a soda from the vendor.  I took advantage of the wait to select one of the cocktails on the menu:  the Matcha Bird which is made from a collaboration of Sun King and Cardinal with a Bird Royale Spirit, Matcha (tea), honey, passion fruit, Topo Chico (bottled water) and Sumac Sugar.  It was delicious!  The server brought my drink to the second floor dining area I selected and the drink went well with the pizza.    The only negative beyond the construction is that the distillery is about a month away from producing their own line of liquors.  In the meantime, they have invited a number of local, state, and regional distilleries to collaborate on some liquors.  As the Sun King brands become available, they will eventually phase out the other items and go solo.  Some of the collaborations are in short supply and may not last long.    I really enjoyed my experience and was welcomed by the staff which encouraged me to browse around so that I could make up my mind.  I look forward to my next visit.  Review #1039

I stopped by on a weekday at the end of August to enjoy some ice cream.  There was no line to speak of, just ropes for forming lines in times of demand.  I was surprised that for having such a large building, there was no indoor dining/ordering area.  It was simply a series of windows for ordering from the outside.    There is a large menu posted behind the glass which can be a little hard to read when the sun is shining, but what is apparent right away is that they have lots of flavors and arrangements for consumption (floats, shakes, bowls, cones, etc.)   Now when it comes to ice cream, I prefer places where you can see the ice cream before making a selection...maybe even get a small sample.  Here, I am not sure if you can get small bites or not, so I simply let a flavor jump out at me off the large list.  I went with banana cream pie probably because it was one of the first listed.  Good to know that it was delicious and I had picked a winner.  I decided to go with a bowl because I wanted to keep walking and not worry about it melting.  Note that there are some benches on the east side of the building and a pocket park with shade is just across Morse Street.  The flavor was really good.  The ice cream was creamy and cold, but not so cold as to cause brain freeze.  The banana flavor was true to expected.  I also liked that the texture had small lumps like I was getting a bit of pie crust along with the filling.  Very good.  If you can time it right, like I did, you can have a wonderfully delicious treat at a reasonable price without a long wait.  Review #1290

This is the 2nd Festival of Trees I've been to at the Indiana Historical Society.  Each year, they seem to add more trees and encourage you to explore the IHS while you look at the trees.  They have both conventional and unusual trees decorated by local businesses, organizations, and societies on display on the ground level, 2nd floor, 4th floor, and canal level.  Some are absolutely beautiful.  Others make you scratch your head and wonder "What were they thinking?"  Overall, I felt the festival in 2016 had a bigger "Wow" Factor than this season's.  Some of my favorites were #24 Bumbles Bounce, #36 Visions of the Sugar Plum Fairy, #52 A Traditional English Christmas Tea, and #41 Yelp, Actually!  Nice job!!  For those who have trouble with stairs, they have an elevator right across from the coat check/closet area.    If you park in the IHS lot, be sure to have your parking ticket validated at the time you buy your ticket.  It's free to park when validated.  Review #1858

Leonard Park has a wide variety of things to do for children, big and small, and adults too!  There is a really nice playground with lots of climbing equipment and a smaller version for little folks.  There are also two baseball parks, several tennis courts, lots of horse shoe pits, and paved walking paths.    For those who want to have "get togethers", there are a couple nice sized shelters and a permanent restroom building.  There are lots of shade trees throughout the park.  I also found parking on the east end as well as along the street.  Not sure if there was parking on the opposite end by the second ball field.  There were a quite a few benches around the playground for adults to relax on including several under the blue shade tarps to escape the sun.  Note that the playground is in full sun, but only a short distance from places to take a break in the shade.  The park was clean and maintained during my visit.  Generally, it looked like a fun place to get some outdoor time.  Review #1373

Just off the beaten path in Irvington is this quirky little shop that sells a variety of coffee products and a few pastries to nibble on.  The place looks like it's been around for awhile and maybe had several lives/uses along the way.  There is a small front patio next to Bonna Ave.  Inside, there is an art filled entry room, and then a couple lounge rooms by the order counter.  The eclectic mix of art and figures (including toy soldiers) make for an interesting browse while you wait on your selection.  I was greeted and though they carry a drip coffee, they only had a dark roast available.  So, in a relatively rare occurrence for me, I decided to give something else a try:  A Dirty Chai.    Before long, I got my drink and gratefully, was able to drink it right away without being scalded. (Yeah!)  I loved the flavor of the drink though it wasn't what I was anticipating.  When I was a kid, I used to come home from school and make a cup of tea with milk and would dip ginger snap cookies in it.  (Hey, I was a kid....mom was glad I ate anything!)  This drink reminded me of this forgotten memory and it made me feel happy.  I'm not sure if that flavor is what the shop intended, but it was a great choice for me.  So even though I didn't get my medium black coffee, I left with a positive experience.  Note that there is parking on the westbound side of Bonna (free).  You can't park on the east side of Coal Yard's building, but if you drive down the lot and circle back around the building to the west side, you can park there. (There is a small ramp from the street to the lot, but the bricks are falling away and I was discouraged from using that.)  Review #2606

I usually avoid going to restaurants with large groups.  It almost always brings out the flaws in planning and service, and sometimes, the kitchen.  If this were a small business, I wouldn't even review the place.  But because my grandson wanted to have his birthday party at the Cheesecake Factory, his parents planned for about a dozen of us to meet and dine there.  I hold these large national chains which host groups to a different standard.  They ought to know how to do it through experience.  So when they seat a large group with half the people seated on benches, the other half on chairs, that means the servers have to reach over the chair people to place the food and fill the water of the bench people.  I must have been banged into or had the waitress put her hand on my shoulder half a dozen times during the meal.  And I wasn't the only one.  I don't really blame her because she had to serve and didn't want to spill the food.  But she could have asked for help passing the food or excused herself for the contact.  It's a bad set up and the management is to blame.  Of course, with a large group, you always have someone get a foul up on their meal and so my son's meal had to be replaced meaning he didn't eat until nearly everyone else had finished.    The portion sizes on some of the meals are ridiculously large.  You can tell by the number of take home bags that this is a strategy of the company to get advertising from the colorful bags that they wrap the take home food in.  At the table next to us, every single person had a colorful bag to carry around the mall property after their meal.  The only thing I enjoyed about the experience was that my meal was actually quite good.  (I asked and got mixed reviews from the others dining with me.)  I ordered the Chicken Riesling and thought it had a really good grilled flavor on the chicken and the wine sauce (with onions, garlic, and mushrooms) was delicious.  Apparently they have a "skinnilicious" menu for folks wanting to watch their calories.  According to my wife, they were still quite high in calories.  Again, the portion size is priced in the $mid-teens for most items so you just don't eat the food you pay for if you want to not gain weight.    Sorry, I can't recommend this place unless you go in a small group and have a huge appetite.  Review #1118

I was hoping there would be a lot to find in this over-sized warehouse, but I found the place to be congested and messy with the quality of items you might find at a garage sale, not an antique store.  Lots of booths were in disarray, over packing their space with everything they could instead of trying to showcase their best stuff.  I walked through the entire building (except for the food and electronics places on the periphery) and felt there was little stop and look at.  I did notice that the back and east side of the floor space seems to feature more large pieces of furniture if that is of interest to you.  I probably won't return.  Review #2055

My wife treated me to a nice Monday night (6/6/16) dinner on the patio of the Stone Creek in Plainfield.  We have been customers of most of the Cunningham Dining Group restaurants and often turn to the Stone Creeks since they are the closest to us.  We wanted a light dinner since it was rather warm outside, but the shaded patio had a nice breeze and was perfect for dining.  After placing an order for beverages, we each got a wedge salad and I also ordered the battered shrimp, with french fries and cole slaw.  While we waited, we were brought the trademark Stone Creek freshly baked bread with the roasted pepper dipping sauce (take home bottles are sold if you ask at the counter.)    As we sat, our appetites picked up and we also split a brownie/ice cream dessert that was delicious.    The service, although personable, was a bit slow as it seemed there was a large party going on in the upstairs part of the restaurant.  But because we were enjoying the evening, we weren't too upset with the delay.  Still, it is worth mentioning in case it becomes a problem.  (It's the first time we have encountered delays in multiple visits to the restaurant.)  I recommend the restaurant for lunch or dinner.  It is nice to find a place that has good food open on a Monday.  They also have a nice selection of locally brewed beverages to choose from.  We also like that they have a points program that crosses over with all of the other CRG Dining restaurants in the area so that we can earn a $100 gift card over time.  We will definitely be back again.  Review #3

About midway along the CCIC is a small, but very cool gift shop for those looking for items locally produced and affordably priced to give as gifts.  I have been by a number of times, but hadn't stopped in until today.  The shop itself is has a small area for items on display (though there is an open area in the back with tables..not certain what that is used for.)  But in the display space, they manage to arrange a nice collection of items plants in cool pottery, small prints, incense and CBD items, DIY embroidery kits, and jewelry.  Just lots of stuff to browse through in a small space.    My advice is to go during the week when crowds might be smaller so that you can take your time without bumping into other shoppers.  Review #1944

This is a nice sized nature park that happens to have a sprawling lawn and shelter by the entrance.  The random trails roughly loop to bring you back to the starting spot, but it's mostly foot paths worn from years of hikers.  So, if you encounter tree roots sticking out of the ground or a fallen tree, you have to pay attention instead of looking all around you.  And that is not easy to do with all the mature trees and a few sudden changes in altitude.  This is one of the more challenging hiking trails around the city parks, so I'll give them credit for that.    I nearly gave the park a five star rating, but there are a few things that held me back.  First, all dogs are supposed to be on leashes.  Seven of the nine dogs I met were off leash and when two big labs rushed me, I was able to keep them from jumping up on me.  If they had come up from behind, I might not have heard them in time.  Seriously, there are dog parks all over town for people to let their pets run loose.    Also, part of the river walk is closed off for conservation (the river bends there and I assume erosion is taking its toll.)  Good for the park overseers, but the lack of notice makes you have to double back the way you came.    Still, it has about a mile of trails to get a good workout and the noise from College Avenue is somewhat quieted by the dense forest.    Review #587

This small shop has a variety of baked goods with focus on cupcakes and chocolate covered items.  Along the sides of the shop are packaged items that are priced individually like chocolate covered oreos decorated in themes like superheroes or winter.    There is also a display case at the order counter where you can see a variety of cupcakes, some cookie options, and more chocolate options.  The staff were patient and helpful and we were soon able to make our selections.  It isn't the widest variety of baked goods around.  I didn't see a lot of pastries here.    Also, at the time of my visit, there were only a couple of each type of cupcake on display.  Don't worry, they have plenty in the back if you want more of a specific type.  If you have a sweet tooth, stop on by to see what may grab your interest.  They are located in a stripmall so there is plenty of parking available close by.  Review #3497

After a bit of shopping that carried late in the lunch hour, I decided I wanted to grab a meal before heading home.  I had never stopped by Nonna's though I had driven by it numerous times.  So, I pulled off the highway and took the frontage road (Cambridge Way) to this restaurant.  There is a separate entrance for pulling into the parking area which allows you to drive around to the front on the west side.  I noticed there is quite a bit of patio seating with a pergola covering the space.  The double door entrance helps keep the climate controlled inside.    I was greeted at the front desk and noticed the seating was arranged around the outside of a central room that was basically an underused coffee shop.  That space is generally available for a party to reserve, but customers can choose to sit there when it is not in use.   I was okay with being seated in the regular area which relied heavily upon natural lighting (it seemed a little darker than I expected inside.)  The hostess also acted as my waitress and since it was just after 1 pm, I was the only customer, so I got prompt service.  Even as other guests arrived, I was unaffected as my food was soon ready.  I started with a house side salad and was pleased it came out while I waited on my entree.  The salad was fairly large and came with the dressing on the side.  Their side salad is mostly iceberg lettuce with red onion, black olives, tomato slices, and cheese.  All the ingredients were fresh and their house made dressing was tasty too.  Soon, my Stromboli arrived.  Really well made, the outside was lightly crisped and dusted with a bit of garlic and other seasoning.  It came with a small cup of dipping sauce that was a great addition.  I will say that they loaded the stromboli from end to end with lots of gooey cheese (mozzarella and provolone).  No bite was just dough, so I appreciated that.  However, the other ingredients like the meats and veggies were a little scant, so some bites were only the bread and cheese.  That's the only thing that kept this from being a five star review.  I will say that my wife had been here before with a large group and she had commented to me that she was very disappointed.  I think that is pretty common for large groups at most restaurants, so I was glad I gave this place a visit on my own.  Completely different experience than my wife had.  I took some of my food home and my wife tried it (actually finished it) and so I think I may have changed her mind about the restaurant too.    Overall, the service was good and so was the food.  Quite a bit for my money too, so I felt it was a good value.  Review #3683

Not sure which I liked better:  The food or the people who worked there.  Does it really matter which?  Both were great!  I saw this restaurant pop up on the "hot and new" feature on Yelp, so I decided to give it a try.  It's located along Keystone just south of where Fall Creek crosses, so it is very close to the trail that runs just passed it.  It looks like it may have been a drive in at one point with the large awning that covers most of your car on the south side of the building.  Seemed like there was plenty of parking.  Inside, the place is filled with delightful island music and filled with color.  The dining room has Jamaican Breeze painted in floor to ceiling letters (except for where the windows interrupt it).   The bar is on the left as you enter and runs at a right angle to the dining area.    I stepped up to the order counter and after receiving a hearty welcome, I decided to go with the Jerk Chicken quarter (dark).  They have several sides you can order for an additional $3, but the lady behind the counter pointed that I would already be getting some rice and peas (looked like beans to me), cabbage (they had a little bit of acidity like they were lightly  pickled), and two slices of grilled plantain.  That was plenty, so I went with just the entree.  I also got to choose my sauce (which comes on the side).  I went with the sweet (with a bit of tangy flavor too) over the mild or spicy sauces.  She took my name after I paid and told me it would be a couple minutes.  Sure enough, she called me for my order in about five minutes and it was great.  I went to pick up the drumstick and the meat started falling off the bone!  I simply used my fingers to tear the meat apart and dip it in that delicious sauce.  So good!  The rice did its job of getting me full while the cabbage and plantains rounded out the flavors with the acidity and sweetness to go with the savory chicken.    Note:  If you go, you HAVE to eat the skin even though its blackened.  It is so full of flavor, you can't pass it up.  Run extra miles if you are worried about calories.  This is worth it.  I'm getting on the treadmill right after writing this!   Hint:  Traffic can get kind of crazy with construction and rush hour, but don't let that stop you.  Try to find a time when you expect traffic to be reduced to help you get here.  It's worth it!  Review #2350

I had a really good meal from Subito today.  It was a nice weather day, so I didn't mind street parking a couple blocks away down Virginia Avenue and walking to the shop.  It was 12:30 on Wednesday, and I noticed the line was backed up to the door.  At first I thought it might be a long wait, but once you see how small this place is, you realize why there is no seating.  You also realize that five people ahead of you fills the entryway!     The good news, is that these guys are efficient!  The man at the counter was friendly and knew how to keep the line moving, keeping the orders flowing back to the three guys in the back.  If you haven't looked at the menu online (or grabbed one of their monthly soup charts), you can see what sandwiches and sides are available on an overhead whiteboard.  The drinks they have are chilled in a refrigerated unit next to the counter.  The soups available for the day are on a sign in the corner.  Anyway, once you order and pay, they ask your name and you step to the side where you can see your order made.  Even though I started on the outside, it was less than ten minutes until I had my order in hand and was out the door!  Wow!  I've waited at fast food places downtown longer than that!  I ordered the Chicken Caesar Wrap - crisp Romaine lettuce, chicken breast, tomato, aged pecorino Romano with scratch-made Caesar dressing on a tomato-basil wrap; housemade macaroni salad (with onions, celery, roasted red peppers, and herbs/spices).  Both were excellent.    Note:  If you are interested in the soups of the day, you can ask to have a sample of each to help you make up your mind.  Sure, it would be nice to have parking available.  Yes, it would be nice to have a table to sit at close by.  But the owner/chef of this business has a plan to make a go of it counting on folks who work downtown and plan to head back to their office or to one of the nearby parks to eat.  Once you understand that, it is hard to take away stars because of the "inconvenience".  If you are downtown and want some fresh and tasty food, treat yourself to Subito.  Review #67

I recently grabbed a lunch "to go" from Between the Bun(6-6-16).  Fortunately for me, it was during the week and there wasn't much of a crowd, so I was able to get my lunch and head back out on the road within 15 minutes.  I really appreciated the quick turnaround since it is posted inside the restaurant that they don't precook the burgers.    This was my second visit to the restaurant, so I wanted to try something different.  I went with a relatively new burger, The Liberty Bell Burger which is their take on a Philly Cheese Steak.  I found the burger full of flavor and was nice and juicy.  I chose the french fries, which are seasoned with a bit of heat and spices.  If you aren't a fan of spicy heat, you may want to choose another side for your burger (my wife does this).  If you don't mind heat, then the fries are very flavorful.    My only knock on the meal was that it was rather bland in appearance compared to the flavors inside.  I like that "wow" factor when I get a great meal.  The decor inside the restaurant is fun and quirky by choice, so it is hard to fault the owners for that.  Still, it isn't a place you would go on a romantic date, but could be a fun place to go with friends.  Review #4

I am relatively new to the world of public art.  Sure, I checked out some of the art displayed downtown in Indy when it was there.  And I checked out the murals that went up for the Super Bowl (XLVI for 46).  But, other than that, I hadn't really noticed.  I don't think that I'm the only one who walks or drives by ornate buildings and sculptures, murals and graffiti without taking time to see what is there.  So, now that I am retired, I have the time to slow down and look at the world around me.  When I saw that Carmel had an extensive collection of public art, I hopped in my car to check it out.    The area designated as the Arts and Design District (and the area to the immediate south on Rangeline Road) is filled with artistic sculptures and fountains.  There are murals and private pieces of art as well.  And there are numerous shops in the district to appeal to anyone looking to acquire something for themselves.  My focus on the day I traveled was to find the pieces by J Seward Johnson Jr.  The city has acquired 15 of his bronze lifelike sculptures and placed them in places that are likely to be noticed by anyone in the area, but are so real looking that you may be surprised they aren't fellow humans.    I started out my journey just south of the district at the Carmel City Center.  The first piece I found was "My World" (1992) where a little girl sits reading a book on south Rangeline Rd.  The next piece was "Big Sister" (1987) at Hanover Place in the area behind Divvy Restaurant.  The piece depicts a young girl receiving help in tying her shoe from her big sister.  I then headed north to Main Street and parked on the east side of the district.  As I walked along the north side of the street, I found "Who's in Charge" (1991) at 30 N Rangeline.  It shows a boy sitting upon his father's shoulders.  The next piece I found was "Sidewalk Concert" at 22 W Main, right in front of a music store.  A statue of a violinist playing for tips is the focus of this piece.  Further down the street at 40 W Main (on the corner of 1st Ave), "There, Now You Can Grow" has a little girl with a watering can placed next to some live flowers.  From that location, you can also see a large Mural painted by students at Carmel in 2007.    Across 1st Avenue, I then saw "Ambassador of the Streets" (1993).  This woman in a red dress is walking her dog.  The dog has other things in mind than walking in the direction the woman wants to go.  A little farther down the street and I found "One Man's Search" (1996).  It shows a man (in a Carmel HS jacket) sitting on a bench reading a book.  Across 2nd Avenue near the Monon Trail is "Oh, It's You, Welcome!" (1997) portraying a policeman named W Carey.  Further down the street is an oversized bronze of a dancing woman by Jerry Joslin titled "Eternal Spring" (or Spring Eternal).  And finally, near the roundabout, an artist is painting the fountain in the middle.  This piece is called "The Right Light" (1983).  I really liked that this piece not only shows off the sculpting ability, but the painting skills of the artist as well.  Working my way back to my car on the south side of Main Street, I soon noticed the piece "First Ride" just a short way down the Monon Trail.  This piece is a bit dated, showing a father helping his daughter ride her bike before the days of safety helmets.  Interestingly, the city put a plaque that the use of a helmet is not to be ignored just because of the statue!  The next block shows two pieces.  The first is "Confirming Predictions" and shows a man on a bench checking his stocks in the morning paper.  The second is a woman coming out of a butcher shop called "Holding Out".  Sadly, the plaque for this piece is missing, so there was little information about it.  As I crossed 1st Avenue, there was another colorful mural on the east side of the street.  As I got to Rangeline, I turned south and saw a couple holding an umbrella called "Elemental" (1993).  Although it seemed a bit out of place on this sunny day, I can imagine it seems very realistic on a rainy day.  I crossed the street and at 1 S Rangeline found "Things to Do".  This piece has a business woman seated on a bench making out a list of things to do that day.  By the look of things on the list, she seemed rather ambitious!  The final piece was found at 19 E Main St.  This statue reminds me of several photos taken after World War II ended as a returning sailor plants a kiss on a willing lady.  The original title of the piece was "Unconditional Surrender" (2004), but is also known a "Embracing Peace".  Overall, the pieces are very lifelike, although some have become dated.  Still, I appreciate the nostalgic feel that made me feel welcome.  After the walk, I was able to try out one of the numerous restaurants in the area.  There is a great diversity of shops along the path as well as places to acquire art.  It was a fun way to spend my morning.  Review #154 indyartsguide.org/public...

I've been a regular visitor to Fishers for a couple years now but even though this place is just south off Lantern Road, I had never heard of it.  Thanks Yelp for letting me find it!    The natural area is pretty much that.  There is a narrow wooded area that widens and has a small lake in the middle.  The trails through the woods are natural, so after all the rains we've had in June '19, it was reasonable to expect some muddy patches.  Most of the fallen trees have been cleared.  Over by the lake, there is an observation deck out over the water.  However, the entrance was below water and meant getting out onto the deck would require getting my feet wet up to my ankles.  Maybe another day?    One of the well planned benefits of this park is that the Nickel Plate Trail runs along the outside of the park.  That trail is level and paved and because it is not directly in the woods, cuts down the risk of mosquitoes and ticks (they seem to be everywhere this year!)  What I like is that there are several access points between the park's trails and the bypass.  You might even find a park bench there too.  Because the heat index started soaring during my hike, I cut my trip short and didn't go all the way around.  As I got past the deck area of the lake, the trail became very narrow as the shrubs/brush/trees were overgrowing the path area and it became more "buggy".  So, choosing to not push my luck, I exited to the paved trail for the return trip.  I will definitely mark this park as one to return to in the fall for further exploration.  Review #2718

Although I didn't stop by for lunch, I did have an enjoyable time on a cold winter afternoon trying some tea and a scone.  This house turned business has its own parking along the south side of the building.  After a few steps up into the place, I found a boutique of jewelry and home items as well as some teas.  They even have more upstairs!  I was greeted and asked if I wanted to dine (Yes!) and they asked my name.  When I had finished browsing, I was led back to a table with a small bell/ornament with my name written on it.  The table was a 2-top though most in the room were 4 tops.  The room was filled with ladies chatting away while munching on sandwiches that looked colorful and tasty, with what may have been croissant breading, but I'm not certain since most were partially consumed.  I had already eaten, so I perused the tea menu and the waitress/hostess suggested a scone.  I selected one of the three available on that day, an apple cinnamon scone.  For my tea option, I went with a black tea called "Cranberry Autumn" with the tart berry and some orange flavors and aromas in the tea.  The tea was brought out dipped in a white pot and with a timer that was counting down how long the tea needed to steep.  I asked and didn't need to remove the tea bag from the pot, but it was suggested to wait until the sands had dropped to assure that the tea was ready.  Delicious!!  I began on the scone which was served with a warmed whipped ball of butter in a small dish.  The scone was only about 4 inches in length and maybe a couple wide at the outside end.  There was a light drizzle of cinnamon icing on top.  The scone was fresh and tasty, even in the afternoon!  Points for that!  The hints of tangy and citrus in the tea paired well with the sweet and savory of the scone.  I love when the beverage and food enhance each other's flavors.  Very courteous and welcoming staff made for a pleasant visit.  They do have afternoon teas with a large selection of food items which priced out about $32 each, but my pot of tea and scone were just over $5 excluding tip.    If you are wanting a great way to escape the chill this winter, stop by here and treat yourself to a delightful experience.  Review #1877

It had been awhile since our last visit to La Trattoria along the newly completed Madison Avenue of Old Town Greenwood. (Yes, folks were actually using the new bike trails!)  So, my wife and I stopped in after grabbing a spot in the adjacent parking lot.  They had outdoor seating available, but I wanted to see what the inside was like.  It hadn't changed noticeably in my absence:  Still a comfortable house with two rooms set up as dining areas with mostly 4-top linen covered tables.  (My wife pointed out that they still had the fall candles on the wall and decorations on the tables.)  It's not a fancy place, but a somewhat upscale restaurant with a menu split between pasta dishes and steaks.  Most of the pastas are under $20 with a side salad and bread/dipping oil included.  The steaks start around $30, come with choice of baked potato or new potatoes with veggies included as well as the salad and bread mentioned earlier.  They also had a decent variety of beer, wine, and cocktails.  I decided to go decadent with the Triple Chocolate Truffle Martini and it was delicious.  My wife thought it had a hint of coffee flavor, but I noticed the rich chocolate flavors and a sweetness unlike most martinis.    After devouring the sliced bread (all but the bottom which you have to tear or cut through) and the pepper flecked oil, our salads arrived.  They mainly use iceberg lettuce as the base and have typical shredded veggies added along with cheese and croutons.  I liked the house balsamic vinaigrette:  Thicker than I expected, but not clumpy.  I was pleased to see my colorful steak plate arrive.  I appreciate when a steak is served with colorful veggies and potatoes instead of just a lump of meat.  It just looks more appetizing (a makes for nice photos too!)  The steak was seasoned (mainly salt) and was cooked to a tender medium rare with a nice char on the outside.  Really good deal for the 8 oz. and plenty to eat.  My wife had the Chicken Alfredo, and as I suspected, it was a bit bland.  The chicken was cut into bite sized pieces and had a nice grilled flavor without becoming rubbery.  But there was a very high noodle to chicken ratio and she struggled getting the noodles to stay wrapped around her fork.  The serving was large, so she had to get a "to go" box.  Our service was pleasant and though the room was a bit loud, we could still carry on a conversation.  Check out was smooth and prompt.  Overall, a nice dining option without a lot of pretense, just good food and service for well made food.  Review #2681

I was glad to see that the old town section of Zionsville has a new chocolatier after the Ganache shop closed down.  Located in the same little row of shops on East Pine, this shop features hand crafted truffles, creams, turtles, barks, and assorted other styles of chocolates that the owner makes herself.  I picked out a nice variety and though they can seem pricey if bought by the pound, I was able to pick up a selection of truffles, a milk chocolate turtle, a blueberry cream, and another selection for about $11.  You can see the skill level in how decorative each piece is on display.  I also like that they have a pre-printed card that you can take with you to identify the truffles once you get them home.  Very helpful!  The flavors were really good!  The turtle which I bought for my wife had a nice balance of milk chocolate, pecans, and caramel.  Not the largest I've seen, but a reasonable size that was quite tasty.  They do have a stand with some bulk chocolates (like covered peanuts) that you can pick up, but I think the beautiful colors/craftmanship of the chocolatier will draw you right passed those small bags, which frankly, you can get lots of places.  But, if you like exploring the world of chocolates, go directly to the display counters.  You will find lots to choose from.  Review #3691

"I don't fly often, but when I do, I use Indianapolis International Airport."  That may sound a bit over used, but it's true.  I get that this isn't a major hub and that because of its size, everything is easy to reach.  It also helps that it was planned from day one instead of being put together as a series of expansions.  All that helps to make it such an easy airport to get around.  What impresses me is that compared to other markets, how much I noticed how well Indy did.  Arrival and check in was easy.  A short stroll through the central concourse filled with food and shopping options led to going through security which was the fastest we encountered on the round trip.  And the waiting areas in the secure areas/terminals had enough to do that we weren't hungry or bored while waiting for our plane.    If I knew flying was this easy, I might have gone on my vacations!  Great job, IND.  Keep it up!  Review #2392

During my visit to the new Test Kitchen at Sun King in the Fishers District,   I started my dining with some food from Natural State - Provisions.  This southern influenced restaurant is brought to you by the folks who founded King Dough (originally in Bloomington, now on the near east side of Indy).  What to expect?  Large portions of tasty flavor combinations that you probably hadn't considered yourself, but somehow, seem familiar like comfort food.  I ordered the McSunKing sandwich which surprised me at how large it was.  Start with a large buttermilk biscuit, sliced and filled with bacon, egg, american cheese, and though it mentioned red eye mayonnaise, I found a lot of jelly as the main color/flavor influencer.  My wife ordered another sandwich and started eating mine while I was away from the table.  I only got about a quarter of the sandwich and it was really good if you like breakfast at dinner.    I also ordered a side of collard greens which come with house pickled tomato and onions, and smoked ham.  Really good and a decent size serving, which could be shared.  My wife ordered the Momwich that is an even larger sandwich that includes turkey, provolone (ours was missing the cheese though), lettuce, chips, sun dried tomato spread, & dijonaise mustard on Texas Toast.  We were too full from all the food we ordered (from the other places too) so we saved this sandwich until the next day.  Even without the cheese, the sandwich had a really good flavor.  I wasn't sure how I felt about having potato chips in the sandwich, but they were crisp and had more seasoning than just salt, so they added texture to the sandwich as well as flavor.  My friend ordered the Soda Jerk, which is a root beer braided pulled pork with pickled onion and cucumber on a sesame seed bun.  He enjoyed it, but didn't share.  Basically, you go to the specific counter for the restaurant, place your order and pay, and are given a sensor that will buzz when your order is ready.  That allows time to find a table and place a beer order from Sun King.  (Note that they do sell non-beer beverages here too.)  When done, the wait staff of Sun King will clear off your trash for you.  The Test Kitchen is very popular, so finding seating is a challenge.  If you aren't successful on the main floor, you may find some room upstairs.  The overall environment is quite loud, though there are places that are family friendly (just not near the bar of Sun King.)  Parking is at a premium.  We grabbed one of the last street parking spaces just north of the brewery.  They do have parking garages available, but I don't know if they charge or if they are free.  Hopefully someone else will post that soon.  Review #3634

This large warehouse is pet friendly and has plenty of room in the aisles to let you browse for your pet needs.  They also have a mini pet hospital, grooming area, and adoption center inside the store, but I haven't used those.  I have spent time looking through the wide variety of options they have for toys, healthy snacks, and items meant to make my pet's life better.    Note that they often let animal rescues to set up inside the store or on the large sidewalk/parking lot out front.  I won't get into the debate about where the pets come from...every pet should have a home.  I've seen lots of mutts available here, so I have a good feeling about it.  On my last visit, there were a number of greyhounds that were needing homes.  Overall, when I am in the area, I like to stop by and see if there is something I can pick up for my two dogs.  Review #1955

My wife and I stopped in for lunch on Sunday afternoon and took our seats at the outdoor patio tables on the east end of the business.  Our waitress (India) was excellent with her attentiveness to our needs even though she had a large group near by.  Even though there was a bit of a delay getting our food delivered from the kitchen, it was a nice enough day to relax and enjoy our beverages.  My wife order a Basic Brewpub Burger with a 1/2# of angus beef.  She upgraded to include cheddar to go along with the garlic aioli, lettuce, tomato, and house made pickles.  Excellent flavor, but too much for her to consume in one sitting. She went with the fries as a side.  Although fries can be ordered with a number of seasonings, she opted to ask for the basic salt on hers and said they were great.  I tried the Korean Fried Chicken sandwich. The breaded boneless chicken was topped with a slaw made with a sesame teriyaki sauce that was delicious on a brioche bun.  The only negative was that the chicken were thick "nugget" sized pieces that made it difficult for the slaw to stay inside the sandwich due to the bulky shape.  The chicken itself appeared to be chunks of breast meat, not some cheap composite like fast food places.  The brioche bun also added to the height of the bite, so I ended up mashing my sandwich when trying to fit it in my mouth.  The bun crumbled a bit and I ended up getting some sauce on my fingers, but it was delicious!    The side for me was the grilled Brussels Sprouts.  Excellent with just a bit of char to round out the flavor.  Highly recommended!  All the food was great.   I also ordered a flight of 5 samples (about 2 oz each) for $4.  I really enjoyed the Tripel (9% 35 IBU), the Cherry Oat Ale (5.8% 10 IBU), and the Salted Caramel Wheat (6.4% 10 IBU).  The Mai Bock and the Mandarina Farmhouse Ale were okay, but weren't as distinctively memorable as the others.  Most of the beers I have tried, particularly on the less bitter end, have been enjoyable and I would consider ordering as full sized pints.  If you aren't in a rush, drop by and enjoy some of the food and beverages.  It's just north of I-70 on the west side of SR 267.  Good stuff!  Rev #25

If you want to try this new restaurant, I suggest going during the week and going early!  My wife and I arrived without reservations on a Tuesday around 5 pm and had no trouble being seated.  The restaurant is beautifully adorned and definitely feels like an upscale restaurant.  Although I didn't see any dress code, this is a place everyone who came in seemed to be dressed for a nice dining experience.  Service was also very inviting as well.  From the hostess that seated us in the dining area (it has a view of the kitchen) to our server (Briana) who had an upbeat attitude, we were taken care of throughout our stay.  Even when there was a miscommunication on my wine choice, there was no hesitation to fix the situation without any problems.  We started with a complementary bread course which comes with a few slices of crisped bread.  They have a bottle of flavored olive oil at each table and individual small plates for customers to use.  This location did not have balsamic vinegar and I didn't bother to ask if that was an option.  We skipped the early courses of antipasta and salads (they don't have a small side salad option, just larger ones that you can share) and went directly to the entrees.  I was a little disappointed that this location didn't have a filet option like the Iron Works location used to have.  But my wife and I were both pleased with our colorful selections which each came with the option of shredded Parmesan served by the waitress.  My wife chose the Tortellini alla Effie which comes with shrimp and spinach in a vodka tomato sauce.  I went with the Linguini Bosco Mare which also has shrimp and Shitake mushrooms in a garlic olive oil.  Both meals were really good.  The dessert options were chocolate cake, tiramisu, and cannolis.  Sorry, if you are fan of the bombas that the Iron Works location offered, they don't have them here yet.  (HINT HINT)  The only other suggestions I would offer is that the waitress and staff need to project their voices a little more.  I had to ask for something to be repeated over the background music and my wife asked me what was said one time as well.  And the miscommunication on the wine was probably due to volume level as well.  Review #3718

I've been in the area a few times, but had not stopped in before.  This small coffee shop is tucked into a little neighborhood by Rolls-Royce which is cut off from downtown by all the road construction on Meridian Street, so I suggest approaching it from the south and finding some metered street parking out front or to the south of the building.  I didn't see any handicap accessibility ramps, so entrance is via some steep stairs up to the lobby of the cafe.  The cafe is just beyond the lobby at the entrance.  The left side is where the prep/order area is with some limited seating.  To the right side is more of a place to set up for chatting with friends or doing some work on your devices.    If you want to place an order, you go down the middle and wait your turn at the counter.  There is a cooler of non-coffee drinks as well as a limited food selection.  I was there for the coffee and ended up getting mine to go.  I was fortunate that because I take my coffee as a simple black drip, I didn't have to wait for all the specialty drinks ahead of me.  Thanks!  They had a couple flavors of drip coffee to choose from and the barista let me know the characteristics of each so that I could get the one best fitted to my tastes.    And the coffee, while still hot, was not scalding.  I was able to drink it right away though I was careful not to take big gulps at first.  I really appreciate when a coffee house gets the temperature right.  I think if I had wanted to stay awhile and set up a workstation, I might have appreciated this place more.  As it was, making a special stop, paying the meter, and then climbing stairs to get into the place seemed like a lot to expect for a cup of black coffee.  So, go with an intention of staying if you want to get your money's worth from the visit.  Review #3316
