Indy has a new park (Fall 2018) that opened on the south side of the City-County Building on Washington Street.  The plaza is a makeover of the former concrete sidewalk/patio that was boring and unattractive.  Now, the out buildings have information about the city's history.  There are colorful pastel tables and chairs for those wishing to bring their lunches.  There are even bench swings on the west end for those who wish to spend their time having a little more fun than the rest!  The old sculpture that was on the corner didn't survive relocation, but a new art installation has been added.    The plaza is supposed to hold up to 1500 people for gatherings downtown.  Looks like just one more perk for folks who don't want to feel chained to their desks at lunch time!  Review #1752

Jimmy's Diner is a place with good food and from what I could tell, a loyal following of regulars from the neighborhood.  There seemed to be a lot of interaction between patrons so this is apparently a social destination as well as a place to get some decent food.  My wife's tenderloin was flavorful and juicy.  She liked her onion rings as well.  I went with the 3 Beef Slider and fries.  Both could have benefited from a little higher cooking temperature since there wasn't any char on the burger and the fries were done, but without any crispness.  The place was packed and there was only one waitress taking care of orders and one guy handling busing.  So, the wait was a little longer than expected, but understandable for being so busy.  The negatives are just to let "outsiders" know that this isn't a place for ambiance or any cool retro vibe like some diners (like Oasis).  There just isn't any effort into making the place look inviting.  Although the cook/owner acknowledged us upon entering, it was at least five minutes before we even saw a waitress and a menu.  The seasoning was mild with nothing different than I could make at home.  The walkways between seats are narrow and feel crowded.  It just doesn't lend itself to being a place I want to return to.  I haven't read any negatives about the place from others, but having dined at over 400 restaurants in central Indiana, I can say there are lots of other options to choose from if you aren't one of the regulars.  Review #236

I'm not sure why this place is getting such a good rating.  It is difficult to get into if you are westbound on 82nd, it looked a bit picked over, and even though my wife and I were the only ones in the shop, the two clerks were busy eating (3 in the afternoon) and didn't speak to us or even acknowledge us as we browsed through the store.  There were some witty little pieces, some animal slippers, and most items seemed reasonably priced.  But they have arrows that encourage you to look in the restroom for savings and they have a large display of candles that aren't for sale.  What???    After having dealt with businesses earlier in the day that made sure to offer help and thanked us for coming in, we both agreed that this place won't be a place we will return.  Good day, Sir!  Review #2050

Wow!  I really enjoyed my lunch here!  I am not very familiar with Korean food having only had it maybe three times before today.  I love that with my basic lunch order of Bulgogi (shredded beef in a somewhat sweet sauce), I got an entire bento box of rice, cooked veggies, and two pieces of avocado sushi.  AND on the side I got four more dishes that I'm guessing were sprouts, somewhat sweet cucumbers, potatoes (in a thick Teryaki type sauce), and chopped white radish (Dongchimi?) that wasn't spicy.  Add to that a side salad with a mild ginger dressing and a small bowl of fruit pieces for after dinner, and I was a happy camper!  Oh, and the cup of Green tea was probably about 24 ounces!  Nice flavor with little bitterness.    The greeter and the server were both friendly and did a great job of clearing my used plates, offering me a fork since I am a dork with chopsticks (would probably starve with anything requiring actual skill), and bringing out the bill and processing it when I was ready.  Highly recommended for anyone who wants a great meal to get introduced to Korean cuisine!  Review #2083

It had been a while since I my last visit, so I decided that it was a perfect place to go when I had a "bachelor" dinner night.  So glad to have my expectations exceeded!  I went early on a Thursday evening and after parking along the street (free), I grabbed a spot at the bar.  The waitress/bartender was friendly and offered a dinner menu when she asked for my drink order.  They carry Abita beer in bottles and on draft.  I opted for the Amber draft and it was excellent.  I asked if they had flights to sample, but they don't currently.  They do offer small samples if you have trouble making up your mind by just reading the names.  Excellent choice #1.  I placed my order and was offered a bread course.  I gladly took the warm sliced bread (completely, not the kind you have to tear) and spread a bit of whipped butter (room temperature, so very spreadable).   I then used the squeeze bottle of house sauce featuring Balsamic vinegar and a cajun spiced mustard.  Wow!  I was offered another basket, but had to decline since I wanted to save room for dinner.  I started off with the Maque Choux (Mock shoe) which is a seasonal offering that captures local corn at the height of flavor and makes it the key ingredient in spicy (flavor, not heat) chowder.  Lots of corn in the decent sized serving, topped with additional seasoning and diced green onions.  It was thick enough to eat with a fork, but not clumpy or gravy-like.  Excellent choice #2!  With perfect timing, my entree, the Barrone Street Shrimp came out.  The large plate comes with about ten butterflied shrimp (sans tail shells) and a plate full of red potato chunks in a sweet spicy red sauce.  The potatoes were bake thoroughly to be tender.  The shrimp were served hot, but even though they stayed hot throughout my meal, they didn't overcook to rubbery. Fantastic!  They use a house mix of seasoning in the sauce which leaves a bit of Thyme flavor after the initial barrage of flavors.  Again, there is a lot of spice flavor, with just a hint of heat.  Perfect for me!  Excellent choice #3.  Service was prompt throughout the dinner and maintained a friendly disposition throughout, even inviting me to return with my wife on the next visit to try something new.  Not sure if I can talk her into trying cajun, but I will gladly  return!  Review #398

Although the majority of the business has a variety of items for purchase (quite a few vintage), in the back is an ice cream parlor which drew me in.    With a few small tables for customers to dine inside, the parlor has large display cases filled with two dozen varieties of ice cream.  After sampling a couple varieties, I settled on a Key Lime Pie ice cream.  The flavor was quite good and the scoop even had bits of graham cracker to add the flavor of a crumb crust.    The parlor also sells a few other items like hot dogs and nachos.  The staff/owner was very pleasant and helpful, as well.  Review #868

I had heard and read good things about this chain restaurant near County Line in Greenwood, so when our shopping brought us to the area, my wife and I headed into the restaurant.  Near the order counter is a large display with lots of options for your order, including pairings of sandwiches and sides, soups, and pizza.  We both selected a half sandwich combo, hers with soup, mine with fruit.  We paid and took a number to an empty table and filled our beverage glasses at the counter in the rear.  Napkins, salt and pepper shakers are located at another counter closer to the place we ordered.  Before long, our orders arrived.  I will say that the woman who brought out our food was very friendly and courteous.  She was doing a good job.  I was surprised that when I paid, my receipt didn't have a way to allow including a tip on my bill.  I found that odd that a place that provides service doesn't make a spot for tipping on the receipt.  I guess if you want to leave a tip you have to bring some cash.  IDK  The sandwich halves were about 3" in length, so if you are used to a competitor's half sandwich, you will probably feel you didn't get as much, but this place throws in your choice of side with the sandwich.  It just looks smaller than what you might expect.  It was still plenty to eat, just something about the small size surprised me.  Our food was okay.  Her soup (corn and crab chowder) was loaded with pepper so much that I smelled the pepper across the small table.  Yes, even before I smelled the crab meat.  Then, her grilled chicken was so bland she needed to grab the salt shaker from the station to see if she could perk it up.  A bit on the dry side too, so not a very enjoyable meal for her.    My fruit was fresh and cut small enough that it was bite sized.  The sandwich was okay, though I missed that it included goat cheese (my arch enemy!)  I managed to eat my sandwich though the cheese is not pleasant to my palate.  It's my fault that I ordered it since it is listed on the menu.  I simply haven't had it paired with a pesto chicken sandwich before and didn't notice it.  Lots of strong flavors when you include the basil and garlic from the pesto.    So, we didn't have a bad experience, but other than the service, there wasn't much that we really enjoyed either.  It's okay, so 3 stars for us.  Review #2530

I stopped in for a quick cup of coffee late in the afternoon and was very pleased.  Not only did the shop have plenty of free parking outside their door, but inside, the place looked inviting and well kept.  Very quiet vibe so that if you wanted to spend a little time working here, it seemed like you could go undisturbed.    Although they offer a lot of pastries (and sandwiches until 3 pm), I simply wanted a nice black coffee that was drinkable without burning my tongue or tasting bitter.  I received a really fine tasting coffee that was hot, but ready to drink and I was happy!  The man behind the counter was friendly and we chatted while he got my coffee for me.  So nice to have baristas who can make a customer feel welcome.  If you are in the Geist area, make this your quick stop for a good cup of coffee.  Review #3672

Guess who was the first customer at the new location for Between the Bun - Burgers, Dogs and More?  I even beat Liz Biro to the place!  Tired of fighting all the mechanical and road construction problems of the Greenwood location (and lack of accessibility, parking, and no patio), the owners of BTB decided to take over the former Teddy's Burger joint at Southport and SR37 (about a block west on Southport behind the Anytime Fitness).   The space is huge and is so much better than the old space.  The benefits now include:  Lots of outdoor seating with picnic tables; loads of room inside the building including an indoor fireplace that will be popular once the weather cools; lots of free parking on the west side of the building; no stairs to climb to get into the place!; lots of windows so that you can see the sun on nice days; high ceilings to make the place feel open and not so crowded; spacious restrooms; and in development, a party room that will be available to reserve in the near future.  But fear not!  Even with all the changes, the burgers are still great!  I tried the Brickyard Burger and it was delicious!  I will caution you that if you are a small-mouthed eater (Nicole, I mean you!), you will struggle with this burger.  It is huge and piled high with flavor!  It comes loaded with a half pound burger that is hand made and marinated in their own seasonings (dipped and deep fried), and topped with cheddar cheese, Wisconsin White cheddar curds, smoked crispy bacon, lettuce, tomato, a thick white onion slice, a dill pickle slice, and topped with their spicy Spitfire Ranch sauce served on a Pretzel Bun!  Whew!    I also ordered a side of Tots which come spiced unless you ask for them to be just salted or unseasoned.    And if you aren't into burgers even at this award winning burger place, you can order any of their flavor combos and substitute a veggie burger, a turkey burger, or chicken breast at no additional cost.  That is very cool!  There are also a variety of hot dog combos available and other sandwiches, sides, and salads.  No reason to go hungry here!  Great new place with the same great flavors.  I like it!  Rev. #37

As I walked towards the new The District Tap (TDT), I couldn't help but notice the giant open window space right on Meridian.  It seemed like it was drawing me in.  I was so busy people watching that I missed the entrance which is just north of the window.  (Note that there is actual outdoor seating on the south side of the building.)  When I entered the space, I turned to the right and was immediately greeted with a smile and a welcome at the hostess table.  I can't tell you how many times that makes a difference, but making customers welcome is always a good start!  Although I often sit at the bar when dining alone, I was taken to a small four top over to the side.  There were tons of televisions (on mute, but with closed caption).  So, the sound level of the place, even with a large crowd was not too loud.  The room was also a bit dark so that the screens could be seen clearly, but I had no trouble reading my menu.  Seemed like a really nice balance of light and sound.  The menu here is large and carries lots of favorites.  I noticed a couple Mahi-Mahi options:  One was a sandwich while the other was a taco.  I asked and was able to get the tacos on lettuce instead of a white corn tortilla.  The fish is blackened and served with avocado salsa, citrus slaw, and topped with mango salsa and cilantro.    It also comes with a side of rice pilaf.  Though the fish was cooked properly, I did find it a little under seasoned for what I think of the spice level on blackened fish.  The salsas were tasty though and it was still enjoyable.  (I wonder how some cajun spices would have perked that taco up!)  My server was friendly and attentive and I thought she did a great job of keeping available without being hovering.  (Shout out to Kari!)  Parking is always a challenge especially with Georgia St having eliminated the street parking and a loading zone in front on Meridian.  But there are some side streets with metered parking or you can park inside the mall for $3 for three hours and just walk over.    If you like TDT on the north side, you will like this first expansion downtown.  Review #3060

It had been awhile since I attended Penrod, so I was determined to make it this year.  (I had a ticket last year, but the downpour of rain dissuaded me from going.)  I remembered that parking at the actual Newfields site was both limited and expensive, so I grabbed a spot just before lunch over at the Cycloplex (Velodrome) and take the free shuttle.  Note:  Unless you plan on buying something big, taking the shuttles is a fast and easy way to avoid the traffic headaches and save a bit more money that you can use for food and art at the event.  Check-in was easy and quick and soon I was wandering the grounds which are divided into color stations with food vendors at each one.  Live performances were far enough apart that I could hear each clearly without competing music interfering.  I particularly enjoyed the singing of Sy Smith whose voice was skillfully woven through the nearly Autumn day with the occasional whistle voice demanding me attention.  Wow!  The grounds are covered with white tents housing artists from around the country.  One of the first large shared tents I entered was for the Stutz artists.  All kinds of art was there.  I thought it was cool that one of the Stutz vehicles was there for visitors to see as well.  Also note that food lines form early and seemed to take awhile to get through.  The ones I stopped at were taking 15-20 minutes to place your order, so choose wisely.  The lines can block some of the walking paths, so be sure to bring your best manners to facilitate getting through.  And the art was really good.  I saw piece after piece that caught my attention.  Problem is that I've downsized my home twice now, and I can't imagine where I would hang the pieces.  Even table top space is limited at my place now, so I am not the ideal customer.  But I still enjoy looking at the art.  I will say that moving around the campus is a lot easier than at Talbott Street's Art Fair.  And though I have seen some folks complain about prices, that doesn't seem to affect the crowd since there were thousands of folks wandering around.  I can't see much that I would improve about the day, but if you are going with making a purchase in mind, the process of picking up your purchase with your vehicle or having to make plans for your purchase to be shipped is a bit discouraging for me from buying.    Review #2990

From the pleasant phone call to schedule the glass repair to the moment I drove off with the repair completed, I found the experience of dealing with this business very positive and affordable.  Since I took my car in before the windshield started to "spiderweb", I didn't need the full windshield replacement.  In less than a half hour, the repair was completed.  I really liked that they advised me that if for some unforeseen reason the window cracks or I am dissatisfied with the appearance, they would apply the cost of the chip repair towards the installation of a full window replacement.   After leaving, I went out and got my car washed with confidence.    Review #579

I don't go out for ice cream very often, but when I do, I like to support local businesses over the big franchised chains.  So, while in Avon, I made a point to stop at this place to give it a try.  Although they have convenient drive thru, I parked in the horse shoe parking lot that surrounds the building and walked up to the order counter.  Overhead, there are menus for a few meal items as well as the large list of flavors for the ice creams available.  You place your order and pay at the window on the right and pick up your order at the left window.  I decided to go with a sundae (strawberry) over an ice cream cone or frozen custard cone.  I saw the listings for waffle cones, but didn't see any pricing for getting a scoop in a bowl which is what I have been doing lately.  So, the frozen custard sundae was soon ready with plenty of yummy strawberry/sauce topped with whipped cream and Maraschino cherry.  Although provided with a plastic spoon and napkins, I must say the spoon was very flimsy and bent a little even with the soft serve custard.  I wonder if it would have held up with the firmer ice cream selections.  Anyway, the flavor was quite good and the price was reasonable.  Service was friendly and pretty swift.  I enjoyed my sundae and was soon back on the road.  Review #2521

I've been watching this location for a while and decided to take advantage of their new lunch time hours to stop by.  So glad I did!  After pulling into their small parking lot at the back of the building next to their back patio (they have street parking nearby too), I passed the bike racks along the sidewalk and stepped into the cozy dining room of Mayfair.  I was immediately greeted by one of the owners who wished me a Happy Halloween.  I decided to step to the left (west) half of the room which is the 21+ bar area and grabbed a seat at the stylish bar.  The other owner brought me a beverage menu and a food menu to look over after greeting me.  Talk about personality, Hilary was running the bar while co-owner Eric was taking care of a lot of the behind the scenes tasks.  I felt welcome right away and found the setting to be quite comfortable.  The lighting was warm and bright enough to read the menu.  I decided to try one of their many drafts, most of which are local craft beers.  I also chose the Turkey Melt with a side of Sweet Potato Fries (they also have a shareable appetizer with a sweet potato fry base, but I got the smaller 'stand alone' fries as a side.)  The food and beer were served promptly and I was very pleased.  The Turkey Melt comes with both American and Swiss cheese and they top it with their own house made Russian dressing.  (Eric's friend runs the kitchen and developed the flavor combo for the sandwich.)  The sandwich was sliced diagonally and was lightly toasted (grilled) to give a little crunch texture to the bite.  Excellent flavor with just a hint of heat in the dressing.  The fries were large and done just right...soft inside but no signs of grease or sogginess.    Hilary took time to tell me the history of the building which is over 100 years old and has housed many businesses dating back to the jazz era in Indy.  Fortunately, the new Mayfair Taproom owners were able to salvage the building (some work is still happening by the back door) and turn it into a beautiful local pub.  The old Mayfair Tavern had a really long run at this location.  I wish the new owners just as much success!  Note:  They have gender neutral restrooms with assistance rails and changing tables inside.  Review #1641

My wife and I decided to head to the near north side for lunch one Friday in February.  We appreciated the free parking in the lot north of the restaurant.    The atmosphere was clean and a colorful with a long row of tables by the windows and a huge amount of seats next to the bar counter.  We were seated promptly at a table.  After looking over the menu, I decided to go with the Hoosier sandwich (pork patty, apple, arugula, smoked gouda, and hickory dijon) and Yucca fries.  The sandwich flavor was excellent!  I highly recommend this to anyone who is a first time customer.  The yucca fries came with a dipping sauce, were huge in portion, but without the sauce, were rather bland.  I probably wouldn't order them again.  My wife and I decided to share the white chocolate & raspberry bread pudding.  This was a tasty item as well.  This is a place I would definitely return to.  Review #57

My wife had scheduled a fitting for new intimate ware after recently losing 25 pounds.  The foundations she had at home just didn't fit.  She had tried finding something on her own and decided that wasn't working, so she turned to the business that specializes in getting the measurements and fit matched to the body type.  She also wanted something that would look attractive instead of something boring or plain.  Although they do take walk ins, the staff advises customers to schedule ahead of time so that you can have their undivided attention in finding something that will make you happy.  Having gone through a fitting before, it amazed my wife how poorly a woman can know her own requirements for a proper fit.  So, she knew that getting an appointment would solve her dilemma...and it did.  My wife found several items that she was very pleased with in both fit and style.  She commented on how the owner helped turn what might be an awkward or embarrassing situation into something that was positive.  Based upon my wife's assessment, the store and staff get 5-stars!  Note:  They do have comfortable chairs out front for those waiting on the customer to be fitted.  They even offered coffee and chocolates!  Review #2020

This place must be doing something right.  I stopped in around 2 on a Friday and the place was packed!  Some folks were working on their devices, but most seemed to be chatting with friends, both seated and standing.    I was able to stop in for a quick cup of black coffee and grab a spot off to the side.  I like to try something simple when I try a new coffee shop since  it's a good way to see how the base ingredient tastes.  I found the drip coffee to be full flavored without too much bitterness.  And I love that they serve it at drinking temperature so I didn't have to waste too much time waiting for it to cool or burn my tongue.    The staff was friendly and got my coffee right away.  Note:  This spot is a self busing place with a bin for your dishes/mugs right by the door as you exit.  Review #2088

After a morning of hiking around downtown, I decided to quench my thirst at YoguLatte.  It was Sunday morning, so the business was open but only had a few other customers. I was able to place my order directly at the counter: Italian Cream Soda with whipped cream on top.  There were eight flavors to choose from, so I opted for Raspberry.    The beverage started with a bit of cream soda in the bottom, then ice was added and cream to augment the bubbling nature of the soda.  The whipped cream was added to the top.  I only ordered a small serving, so I was able to hit the bottom quickly.  Well, bottom is a relative term.  There was plenty of ice and whipped cream left inside.    So, overall, the flavor was really good, but since the ice didn't do much other than act as a filler (okay, there was some chilling that occurred), I find it hard to give a 5 star rating.  The next time, I will have to try one of the frozen custards.  Review #122

My wife and I had an early dinner during the week at this restaurant, so the hostess/waitress seated us at a four top in the central dining area.  Overall, we found the food and service good.  Though similar to many of the other restaurants serving Mexican food, we did note a few items that were different.  Our first impression was that this restaurant was a bit more "classy" than many of the others we have been to.  Though the color of the dining room was a vivid green, it was tastefully decorated without all the over the top colors of some of the other places.  This looked like a restaurant for adults, though I am sure kids are welcome.  My wife ordered a strawberry margarita and thought it very good.  A very pleasant surprise was that it was only $3!  Not huge, but still, a very good price.  I would think they would have a sign up if it was on special and if that is the everyday price, I would be shouting about it!  She also ordered the Fajita Taco Salad with steak.  The steak, though well done, was still juicy.  (Yea!)  However, it was cut into thick four inch strips which made it difficult to cut since the shell filled the small plate. If you order this, ask for a second plate to be able to cut the steak on.  The serving size was large, so she requested a "to go" box for about a third of it.  I went with a Chimichanga with ground beef as my meat option.  It came topped with cheese and sides of rice and beans.  Also on the side were toppings of greens and sour cream.  There was supposed to pico de gallo (according to the menu), but none was visible.  Inside the chimichanga was packed with seasoned ground beef and what I think were small potato cubes (they were thoroughly cooked and soft).  What was missing were any bell pepper or onion like I am used to.  Not knowing what is authentic, I can't really say whether this way of serving a chimi meets "authentic" criteria.  I just know that I was expecting something different based on other dining experiences.  In fairness, the meat filling was generous and probably more expensive than filling the tortilla with veggies, so I am not complaining... just pointing out a noticeable difference.  The service was pleasant and checked in a few times to be sure we were doing okay.  The restrooms were well maintained.  The table has a canister with napkins and metal utensils.  There are several televisions with either muted sports programs or Hispanic news with Spanish subtitles.  Overall, the experience was positive and enjoyable.  I would suggest it was a little more upscale than most Mexican restaurants and the price was maybe a little higher, but not to where they aren't competitive.  p.s.  The restaurant is in a strip mall on the southeast corner of Raceway and US 36.  Due to the construction, the sign is down and only a small banner near the doorway lets you know you have arrived.    Review #919

It had been a long time since I had dined at the Rathskeller, so while downtown with my wife, I decided to treat her to lunch at this iconic restaurant.    The Rathskeller has so much history that I can't even begin to do it justice in a food review, so suffice to say, a long history of German culture has shaped the building, the restaurant, and the food.  We were greeted and seated in one of the downstairs dining rooms.  Note that they have some massive rooms for parties/festivals as well and a bar that is huge (complete with mounted trophy animals.)  Our room was lined with steins of all sizes and figurines that were plucked from literature and German lore.  We were seated in a corner at a glass covered table.  The room was rich in dark wood, very ornate, and proudly showing its craftsmanship.  We quickly selected our meals and while we waited, we were brought out a tasty hot pretzel with just the right amount of salt.  They also brought out a dipping mustard that would probably rival St Elmo's cocktail sauce for the amount of horseradish.  I didn't mind the flavor going down, but the burning sensation that filled my sinuses with even a little amount ruined the flavor for me.  I had to eat the pretzel without the sauce because it made no sense having it that strong.  (Note:  Aging the horseradish two days will allow the full flavor to come out without the unpleasant sensation according to one of my food professional friends.)  Anyway, our appetizer of stuffed mushrooms soon arrived.  The texture of the mushrooms stood out (very fresh!).  Cream cheese, bacon bits, chives and two kinds of cheese made for a nice start.  My wife went with a Chef Salad that was huge.  Strips of ham on top and her choice of dressing made for a nice meal.  However, the plate is so full that cutting the pieces down to bite sized made some of the salad fall off the plate to the table.  (They should be using a bigger plate, or smaller portions, or cut the lettuce into smaller pieces.)  I ordered the Kassler Ripchen which is a smoked pork chop topped with cooked apples, golden raisins, and walnuts to make a light sauce.  The flavor was very nice and the the components complemented each other.  It came with a slightly tart sauerkraut (good!) and German potato salad with much larger potato pieces than what you find in any type of American version.  No mustard here!  My wife wanted to split a bread pudding dessert which comes topped with a raspberry sauce and whipped cream and a cream base underneath to dip each bite in.  Very good!  Although our service was polite and generally good, she did miss noticing that my water had run out, that we could use more silverware, and she didn't pick up that we might want to share the dessert (most upscale places ask if we want to split a single dessert when ordered.)  Just things that we ended up taking care of ourselves, but for a $60 lunch for two without alcohol, I expected a bit more attention.  Overall, a good meal especially in October.  Review #3202

Growing up in Northwestern Indiana, our family frequently visited our Dad's best friend's family farm.  Our family knew that the others worked hard and long hours, but we kind of took it for granted since we got to eat all the great food and enjoy the animals and open space without having to do anything but go.  And so the State Fair was easy for me to take for granted too.  It's there every year and sure, a lot of the exhibits and animals are pretty similar from year to year.  My wife isn't a big fan of walking around crowded places, so I decided to take advantage of a pair of complimentary tickets I received from a Yelp event and go by myself.  As you may have read in many other reviews, there are lots of great opportunities to be entertained by concerts and competitions in the evenings.  They have a main midway and a smaller one intended for the smaller kids.  You can see some of the best arts and craft down in the exhibition hall.  And if you like looking at livestock, they have lots of it!  One of the favorite draws for the fair is the food.  Part nostalgia, part indulgence, the food covers a wide variety of options.  Many of the vendors offer meat items made from the animal types in the pens and stables.  Other vendors feature dairy and/or vegetable items from the state.  And then there are those items for the adventurous who want to try anything deep fried.  I noted that there are some vendors who try to provide healthy options or vegetarian items, but you have to search for those since most are selling the popular items.  I went three times (counting the night before event) this year and was glad to see many things were familiar.  There is a reassurance that not everything in our lives has moved into the fast lane.  So why not 5 stars?  I definitely enjoyed myself.  Well, there were little things that I thought could be improved upon.  For instance, when looking at the livestock, many of the pens/stalls didn't have any species identification.  If the owner wasn't on site, then there wasn't anyone to ask.  It seems like a simple thing to do and an opportunity for visitors to learn something new.    Also, in the DNR building, the cool water fish tanks were covered with foggy condensation.  Why put together the large tanks and transport the fish if you aren't going to keep the tanks visible?  Not a paper towel or squeegie in sight.  Again, it seems like a simple thing to fix, so why didn't anyone of the many folks working in the building take care of it?  Because the fair lasts for 17 days, it definitely requires some planning on what you want to see before selecting a date.  Not only do you need to be aware of large crowd days and not so pleasant weather days, but you also have to determine which livestock you want to see.  Most don't stay there for the entire run of the fair, so on one trip, I got to see almost everything but my favorites, the draft horses.  I did make a special trip back to see them on my third visit of the year but by then, I didn't feel like returning to many of the exhibits I had already been through before.  Overall, I am glad I went and I hope that the fair continues to find ways to make the experience better each year.  After all, I am sure they don't want folks to take them for granted.  Review #366

After grabbing lunch on Friday, I stopped in at Redemption to sample a flight of their house brews.  There was plenty of parking in the lot and even a few benches available for outdoor seating in front of the brewery.  I opted to sit inside the spacious taproom/bar area.  After discussing my options with the bartender (excellent service and a great source of information about the beer and food), I went with a flight of four 5 ounce samples.  Being new to the world of craft beers, I like to rely upon the staff for advice on what to sample and in what order to drink them.  To start with, I selected  the "Four Fathers" cream ale (5.2% 23 IBU).  As expected, this great intro beer for newbies in craft beer drinking was delicious and smooth.  If you know someone who only drinks commercial beer, this is one to let them try.  My next selection was the "Smash Blond" blonde ale (4.8% 17 IBU).  This had a bit more bite to it than the cream ale, but was still very smooth.    The "Daytripper ESB" was my third choice (5.2% 36 IBU).  This was my first experience with ESB (English Style Beer or English Special Beer, depending upon who you ask.)  Although this had a higher bitterness (IBU) quotient than the first two, there was enough other flavor in the drink to mask some of the punch.  By this time, I had ordered a couple tacos (see below) and the bitterness virtually disappeared when paired with the flavors of the tacos.  Finally, my final selection was the "Reclamation Nitro" Vanilla Porter (5% 27 IBU).  This was my first Nitro beer.  Nitrogen is added instead of carbonation, so there are far fewer bubbles, producing a completely different feel to drinking than the other beers.  This dark porter had lots of flavors, reminding me of dark chocolate.  The taste when paired with the smooth texture of the drink reminded me of drinking a chocolate milk (only much less sweet).  It slid down easily.  Not my favorite, for sure, but worth trying for the experience.  As mentioned before, since I had already had lunch, I didn't sample any of the sandwiches or desserts.  However, since it was Taco Tuesday where tacos are only $2 each, I thought I would give them a try.    First, I tried the "California Love" street taco with Shredded Adobo Chicken in a corn tortilla with melted cheese, roasted corn salsa, roasted red pepper, lettuce, pico de gallo, and cotija cheese.  I also sampled the marinated diced Steak on a flour tortilla (with the same extras) and a side of Street Corn which comes served in a cup after being grilled with jalapenos, green peppers, and onions.    Although the service and the beers were great (5 star), I found the tacos and the street corn a bit overcooked, which took away from the overall appeal of the food.  They were okay, just not to the level of some other breweries that have in house chefs.  So, probably a 3 star score on the food.  Review #97

There is a lot to like about this place.  They have some really good food that reminds me of the type we had when families ate meals together on Sunday afternoons.  They have carryout service and an Early Bird special for only $14 instead of $22, but was still more food than I could finish.  There are cool murals and art, a great soundtrack of classic lounge music (Martin, Sinatra, Bennett), and friendly staff.    I arrived at 4 pm after watching a movie at KatC and went with the Early Bird.  You can't imagine how much food there is until you see it sitting on the table in front of you!  First there is a salad (enough for three?) in an elongated dish that you transfer to your serving bowl.  It's mostly iceberg lettuce (nice and crisp, but with a few edges that were a little wilted), julienned carrots, and cherry tomatoes.  They have a house dressing that is on the sweet side as the dressing.  (I didn't ask if they have other options.)  Pretty good!  They also brought out a pair of fresh baked biscuits with butter and apple butter on the side.  These were light and tasty, especially with the apple butter.  I didn't need the butter served in packaged pats.  There was also a bowl of pickled beets that were of different sizes.  I must admit these were some of the best I've ever had!  Very tasty and just the right balance of sweet, vinegar, and beet flavors.  Before very long, my entree came with my choice of two of the three house veggies.  I had the mixed fried chicken with green beans and mashed potatoes with a lighter gravy on the side.  The restaurant has been given awards for its chicken and I will admit there was a delightful crispness to the skin.  The thigh meat was hot and moist; cooked to perfection.  The breast meat was just a tad overcooked and parts were a little dry, but not too much.  I simply used a little of the gravy to perk that up.  I have to admit I was a little disappointed that the crust of the chicken lacked any noticeable seasoning.  I've had super salty brined chicken at the Eagle (too much salt!) and peppery flavored chicken from that large chain, so to eat this was a little underwhelming.  The meat was fresh and fine, just add a little bit of salt and pepper to the breading please!  The table condiments won't stay on and don't really help.  The mashed potatoes tasted real (a few lumps are good!) and the gravy had a complimentary flavor.  I had no trouble devouring this!  The green beans are prepared like I do at home with them being cooked thoroughly, but not mushy, with a bit of onion and tiny pieces of either ham or bacon.  The flavor of the beans were delicious and added to the comfort food theme.  They also offer a serving of ice cream with toppings which I had to pass on since I was stuffed!  I think one of the things that has harmed the ratings of this place has to do with the mixed signals you get from the decor.  There are really nice touches like the murals and paintings, but the tables have a distressed, almost scraped look that isn't appealing.  The carpet is probably clean, but has a color that looks drab and dingy.  I can't tell what type of experience they are going for.  The server was friendly and kept up with the growing crowd as people began filing in.  Nice personality and easy going.  The only negative was that to enter the orders, he would disappear from the dining room and as the only staff on the floor, it made it necessary to be patient to get his attention when I was ready for something like a refill on my tea or to get the check.    Overall, I thought the food was good and the price was exceptional, especially at the Early Bird amount.    Review #2075

The Indpls Firefighters' Museum and Survive Alive is located on the first and second floors of the new building on the corner of Mass Ave and St Clair.  It is a free museum but will gladly take cash donations in the contribution boxes on both floors.  Within the museum, you will see historic fire trucks, equipment, collections of toys, plates, and all things firefighter related.  There are photos and videos of routine and extraordinary events that firefighters have had to deal with.  Note that there may not be anyone to talk with about what you are looking at.  There is usually some metered street parking available on Mass Ave and possibly some free parallel parking on St Clair (east bound only) if you are lucky.  The entrance to the museum is on the north end of the building; the same entrance as if you are going into the union.  The exhibits are to the left across the lobby though a sign by the elevator directs you to the second floor.  I decided to head into the first floor exhibits and later, used the stairs on the south side of the building to review the second floor items.  If you are interested in history, like firefighter related memorabilia, or are an Indy buff, there is bound to be something of interest for you.  Review #1377

I think this is a park that targets younger children while offering a quieter setting than Hummel Park down the street.  There were lots of stand alone pieces for kids with imagination or those who can't resist climbing on things.  Lots of the equipment was made to look like something else like an ant, a wagon, etc.  They also have a younger kids/toddler playground separate from the bigger kid equipment, yet close enough for a parent to see both.  There is a shelter and the side street (which has a sign making you think it is a utility road) has angled parking in the shade so that your car doesn't get too hot while you're visiting.  There is a school across the side street, so I'm not sure if the ball fields are part of the park or school, but even if they aren't for the park, there is still a lot of room to run around beyond the playgrounds.  Review #614

When I lived in Greenwood, I made it north of the County Line regularly to visit Michaels.  Back then, I used to like it more than the Hobby Lobby next door; more things I liked and less crowded.  I always used to find lots of stocking stuffers for the grandkids during the holidays.  I also used their framing for posters or shadow boxes.  And they had lots of fun crafts for the grandkids to work on when they came over to visit.  But upon this visit, the place just looked different.  It was brighter, but seemed somewhat empty.  Maybe I should have stopped by earlier in the Christmas rush (like October or early November), but just two weeks out from Christmas, there just didn't seem to be that much to choose from.    They still had the framing station in the back and quite a bit of craft related items, but it seemed like there wasn't much that caught my attention like in the past.  Review #1930

My wife's CRV is often used as a food transport, bus for grandkids, and a restaurant for when she can't wait until she reaches home to start eating.  She also likes to take our little dog with her when she drives, so we also get dog hair stuck in the tiniest places in the car that our vacuum  cleaner just can't seem to get to. We have seat covers over the front half of the interior, but not the rear seating area and luggage area.  She asked if I would get her car detailed  for a birthday present since I am not nearly as able to get out and shop as I was before my illness.  She called and made an appointment because the place is just too busy to drop in and get service.  She got a time when our neighbor could pick her up and then when the car was ready, out neighbor could return my wife to the shop. The only disappointment I  had was I hoped it would have the new car smell since the interior was so clean that it looked like brand new.  Not a big deal.  We had only arranged for an interior detailing, so when she got home, I had to check out the final condition and was very pleased.  There was one oil based stain on the seat cushion in the rear that they tried several times to get out, but because the cushion was holding the oil, every time it was cleaned, the seat got a new stain.  So instead of trying to cut out the foam, we have decided to order seat covers to avoid having anyone sit on the spot.   Service took a few hours for the detail and my wife said her interaction was friendly throughout the day.  The cost is not cheap, but if you are older like we are, bending and reaching to clean all the spots is hard work that neither of us wants to attempt, so I gladly paid for the service and see my wife's face light up every time she climbs in her clean car is worth the cost.  I particularly was glad to see any "film" that was on the interior side of the windows was gone.  No streaks.  I struggle to get those windows clean when I try it, so this was a definite plus.  We did have to wait more than a week to get an appointment but that allowed u time to coordinate a drop off and pickup with our friend since I no longer can drive and sold my car.  Tis locally owned business did a fine job on the car and an even better job of treating my wife.  Sometimes, it's okay to spend a bit of money on yourself to get a task done that you would hate having to do yourself.    Review #3917

I stopped in this Brewery after reading the positive reviews and I agree:  This place has great beer!  Located in a strip mall in downtown Plainfield right on Main Street (US 40), it was easy to locate and grab a parking space in front of the shop.  The outside windows and the interior have a whimsical art style contributed by the wife/co-owner/bartender.  Inside there is a lounge and foosball table on the east end along with merchandise.  On the west end is additional table seating to go along with the bar seating on the north end of the room.  Since it was my first visit, I went with a flight of four 5 oz servings for $10.  There was a wide variety of options to choose from, so I was pleased to be able to get a lot of different flavors.  I started with the "Murphy's" Blonde Ale (4.5% 19 IBU).  It was crisp and clean and had more flavor than a lot of blonde ales.  My next selection was the "Ronaldo's Hefeweizen" (4.8% 13).    It had a nice aroma and delivered on the herbal taste I was expecting.  The "Ivory" (4.8% 19) was a white stout that had a tasty vanilla flavor.   This was really good and was a nice change of pace.  I finished with the "Ebony" (5% 25) Oatmeal Stout which had a full chocolate flavor.    They do not offer food here, but you are able to bring in your own if you desire.  I really like that they are open at noon everyday but Monday.  So many breweries don't open until 4 and miss out on the lunch crowd.  I don't like dealing with rush hour traffic, so I really appreciate being able to get in for a taste or get something to go while everyone else is working.  I love retirement! :)     When I talked with the bartender, she said that they are rolling out new beer every few weeks so that I should stop in frequently to see what has been added.  Her husband did a great job of maintaining the website since all four options I wanted on line were available on my visit.  Review #318

Although I have been to this location at least twice (once last week), I had nor written a review.  As far as nationwide (?) delis go, this is one of the better ones I've tried.  I find I am a consistently a fan of their soups.  I've not tried any entrees, but I usually get a sandwich or as in my most recent visit, a combo half and half.  The spicy Chicken soup was really good.  Not super spicy, but with enough flavor to wake up the taste buds.  I also had the Spicy Southwest Chicken sandwich which also had chicken and some avocado and a bit of spice was just a little underwhelming in flavor.  Nothing bad, just no wow factor.  My wife had the grilled chicken Caesar and the broccoli cheddar soup combo.  Both were good, but she didn't rave about them.  The soup comes in what I estimate to be 1/2 cup portions in the combos.  The sandwiches are half sized, but still plenty to eat.   We were undecided about where to eat since it was nearing lunch on a Sunday.  All the brunch places were packed, so I remembered McAlisers was nearby and instead of phoning ahead to save time, we just arrived, placed our to go order at the counter, and waited in a designated area that had plenty of spacing.  Plenty of hand sanitizers in the area too.  So, although it wasn't a fast turn around do to the lack of phoning in on our part, the wait wasn't too long.  We decided to take our order out to our car instead of sitting on the small patio area which needed some busing of the tables.    It was an affordable meal with plenty to eat, and plenty of options to choose from.  Not fast food, but not top flight either.  Plenty of parking too!  Review #3787

Wow!  Great food, friendly service, nice atmosphere, and get this....they even have a small parking lot....in Broad Ripple!!!  The building is on the small side, so I could see the place getting crowded, but for lunch, I had no trouble.  Since I was dining by myself, I thought the bar dining a better fit.  The atmosphere is a little dark there without windows, but felt comfy.  The bartender, Mike, was friendly and helpful.  After ordering a beer (they have a few to choose from, but have lots of distilled spirits on hand), I was looking over the menu and decided to go with a couple items that Mike recommended as house favorites:  The Sopa Azteca and the Bison Quesadilla from the starters section.  The Sopa (soup) is thick and loaded with flavor.  It's more like a stew since there is so much shredded chicken inside, and it is topped with diced onions, sliced radish, and cilantro.  I stirred mine together and was amazed at how good it was.    Soon after, the quesadilla arrived and it was appropriately sized for lunch.  Four quarters with moist and well seasoned bison and topped with more cilantro and crema with a hint of tartness to it.  Lots of flavor layers which made the overall flavor great.  Bravo!  I am already making plans for returning with friends to try more items on the menu.  Note that they don't have a huge selection and it's not a place with huge portions.  But if the sampling that I tried is any indication, I think I will have no problem finding something to order.  Review #596

After some research by my wife, she found this was the nearest location for us to receive our booster shot for Covid 19 and although the processes was a little confusing   because we had three insurance companies for the pharm tech to sort through, She managed to keep the line moving.  When it was time to get our shots, we were able to get our booster AND our Flu shot  in  a single injection which was very convenient.  Like a lot of places these days,  it seems they could use a bit more  help around lunch hour when demand is high.  Review #3979

What a trip through my musical past!  This two room shop has used vinyl and books at reasonable prices.  The albums are grouped by genre and then alphabetically within that grouping.  Most of the ones I looked at were in the $5 to $10 range.  There was a wide variety of artists as well, though they didn't have complete discographies.  Still, any place that has Mountain's "Nantucket Sleighride", "Ten Years After Recorded Live", and lots of early Genesis (with and without Peter Gabriel) is okay in my opinion.  There were a lot of books too, but I didn't see any clear markings on the shelves indicating the categories like I did on the albums.  There was a general order to the books, but I found it confusing to find anything specific on my own.     I appreciated that I had the opportunity to browse even though I currently don't have a record player.  But walking through here made me consider it might be fun to pick one up.  The sound playing on their system was so much better than what I have now.  Ah, the good ole' days!  Review #1122

Pretty good food with just a twist on spices from what you might expect.  I went with a fried chicken special on a Sunday which came with 2 pcs of chicken, fries, and a "mac" and cheese side.  I also picked up a malt vinegar slaw to go with my meal.  My wife went with the Carmel Tenderloin slider.  The slider is just that:  one of a variety of options for mini sandwiches and hers contained a tenderloin with a small garden of veggies on it.  She thought it was pretty good.    The chicken was tender and moist and had an unusual breading that was quite tasty, with bits of rosemary seasoning in the mix.  The Mac and Cheese was made with the spiraled rotini pasta and had a spiced flavor that was good, but I couldn't place a name to the alteration.  The cheese flavor was definitely secondary to the spices.  And the slaw definitely was unique due to the malt vinegar flavor of the slaw.  I like malt vinegar, but if you are a fan of creamy slaw, this may not be for you.  If you like your slaw sweet, this may not be for you.    I applaud that the kitchen tries to give the customer something out of the ordinary.  What knocks the star off is that even though I arrived just after opening on Sunday, they were out of all the barbecue options (pulled pork, ribs, and bbq sliders) due to a rush on Saturday night that slammed them.  I get it that it takes a long time to make ribs and BBQ, but you it is your business to anticipate plans for high demand.  I'm glad you created a special with the fried chicken, but I'm guessing it was going to be a long day for the guy behind the counter who had to tell each customer that there wasn't any bbq.    Review #1721

This is one of the toughest reviews to write.  I want this place to succeed, but they need to make some improvements to their execution or else they will not get many repeat customers.  Beer:  5 -Star.  I've tried nine of their 23 house beers and have liked them all.  And for folks who don't like craft beer, they have some domestic commercial brands available.  Food:  4 -Star.  On my second visit, I ordered an Avocado Chicken Wrap that was really good.  My wife ordered a Taco Bowl with chicken, but was given chicken tacos instead.  Not much flavor but okay.  Execution/Service:  1 -star.  Okay, I get that they have only been open a week but that's why you have soft openings with folks who aren't your friends who will tell you the truth.  And I understand that they went from a location where you could easily bring in your own food to a place out in the country where they feel they need to provide food.  But the execution and management of issues brought to their attention just FAILS.  First visit:  Tuesday, second day of business:  We arrived at 5:45 and were told at the host desk that there would be about an hour wait on food because they were slammed with three large parties just ahead of us.  We said we were okay just going with beer.  They seated us and we waited for a waiter to show up. I asked for a beer menu and was told they didn't have enough for each table because some tables took more than one. (They are a brewery and don't have enough menus for customers to look at and drink while waiting.)  After fifteen minutes, I went to the owner/manager and asked for a beer menu and he managed to get one to me.  He thought he could help out and take my beer order of a flight.  He wrote it down and turned it into the bar.  After ten minutes, they brought out the wrong flight.  After another five minutes, I flagged down another staff member who told me they discontinued doing flights due to the high volume.  We got up and left very disappointed.  Second visit:  Friday, fifth day of business:  We arrived at 11:45 am and were greeted and told we could pick any seat we wanted.  We had menus and gave our food and beverage order.  So far, so good, though the music is loud and the room is all hard surfaced so the volume even with a dozen people in the dining area makes it difficult to hear.  Our waitress brought out my wife's iced tea and my flight and took off.  I looked it over and realized that one of the beers was a sour instead of an IPA.  (Note that they don't have the beer menu arranged in best drinking order and don't make any effort to arrange them that way when served.  I pointed it out to the owner/manager that it would be helpful and was told he didn't have anything to do with that....Really?  It's your business.)  I drank my other three beers in the best order, loving each one and hoping that the waitress would return.  When she finally brought out our meals, I pointed out that there was a mix up on the beer and they made it right.  She either was distracted or couldn't hear very well since the IPA and sour have similar names.  Note that it took about 25 minutes from the time we ordered until our meal was delivered.  For a slow time, seems like the kitchen isn't used to cranking food out.  My wife also had ordered the Taco Bowl with Chicken, but was brought a tray of Chicken Tacos.  The owner and waitress said not to worry about paying for the meal (thank you!) but they would make the taco bowl if my wife still wanted it.  They took away the tacos and that's when the owner said that there were several orders ahead of my wife's in the queue.  Seriously?  If you screw up someone's order and have already delivered the food to others at the same table, you expedite the missing meal to the front so that the folks have a chance of eating together.  That's just basic Restaurant Etiquette 101.  My wife said to bring the tacos back so that she could at least have something to eat.  The waitress said fine and that she would bring the taco bowl out in a "to go" box when it was ready.  We finished eating and asked for our check.  The taco bowl hadn't been started yet, so we told them to just forget it.  I was stunned at how clueless this place was.  When the guy running the front end of the house seems unaware of how a restaurant should operate, that suggests they need someone else to manage that side of the business.    They have great beer and the food was pretty good.  I have hope that they will get the execution fixed if they address the issues that cause mistakes and delays.   Review #2723

I stopped in for a cup of coffee on Sunday.  Note that the coffee shop is located south of the roundabout at 106th and Lantern Road, not along 106th like the address suggests.  They have free parking in front of the shop.  Inside, the shop was bright with a variety of seating options towards the front and along the walled mural on the right.  The order counter for coffee, pastries, and sandwiches is on the left.  Although the pastries, including croissants, looked great, I passed on those and went with my standard black coffee.  They were out of medium roast, so I went with a light roast instead.  I was surprised that even though the coffee was a simple order that they took my name and told me I could pick it up at the other end of the counter.  I've been to other places that either have self serve on black coffee or expedite the simple orders to reduce the wait times/line waiting for pickups.  As it was, I grabbed a seat by the window and did not hear my order called, so after awhile, I looked over and made eye contact with the person at that end and saw my coffee waiting for me.  The coffee had good flavor and was right on the edge of being too hot to enjoy, but it cooled just enough that I was able to enjoy it with minimal searing.    The service was friendly and though I had to wait a bit, felt that they were doing as well as their system allowed them to get their orders out.  Just wish they were a little more vocal when calling out the orders.  Review #3687

While I finished up at the neighboring dog bakery, my wife headed into Lesley Jane to check out the beautiful prom dresses in the window.  Did you know that if a student selects one of the dresses for a Zionsville event, the owner of the shop won't sell another one of that style to anyone else who is going to that event?  The owner doesn't want to have two girls showing up in the same dress.  I bet you don't get that service in a big box store!  My wife thought the owner was very pleasant and enjoyed talking with her.  The clothes tended to run towards that young woman/high school student age group, so my wife didn't find anything for herself.  But she liked the quality and variety that she saw.  I will say that for a place that sells formals, I was a little disappointed on the type of displays that were used for presenting the clothes.  I expected it to look more upscale to match the quality.  I understand that prom clothes are only part of what they offer, but some of the displays could have been set up a bit more elegantly.  Overall, my wife thought this a place she would definitely shop if she were in the need of a formal gown and accessories.  Review #2218

I stopped in for the lunch special and had a nice experience.  The special was one of their lunch items paired with a complementary serving of soup (noodle), small salad (ginger dressing), and a veggie spring roll with dipping sauce for about $8.  Good value and good flavor!    I noticed a sign at the entrance promoting the restaurant being a wine and martini bar.  I had to admit, this was probably the nicest decor/ambiance for a Thai cuisine restaurant I have been to.  And after being seated, I knew the place had class when it put on Diana Krall's "The Look of Love" cd.  Very nice and worth a star or two just to be able to listen to such great music while dining!    As I usually do, I ordered Pad See Ew on my first visit to a Thai Restaurant.  As I mentioned earlier, there was the full complement of sides that were as good as any I have had in the area.  The Pad See Ew comes with a choice of meat  and of spice/heat amount.  I went with a pork option and a mild seasoning which was on the sweet side. (Probably should have gone with the medium.)  The flavor was good, but the pork was a little on the tough side of done.  I also didn't receive a knife with my flatware, so having a generous strip of pork (over four inches) necessitated spearing it and folding for another piercing so that I could eat it without wearing the sauce on my face.  Not a big deal, but if they kitchen is going to send out large pieces, they should coordinate with the servers to make them manageable.    One other small item of note:  I ordered a pot of Jasmine tea and was able to get about 2.5 cups from the pot.  Unfortunately, the spout of the ceramic tea pot was made with thick rounded ceramic instead of narrowing to a thinner point which meant that instead of being able to do a slow pour into my cup, quite a bit of tea ran down the lower edge of the spout onto the table.  Physics is what it is, so be aware that if you order tea, you may need to request extra napkins.  Review #351

First, let me give a thanks to the management that honored our reservations on a Saturday night even though we were nearly 25 minutes late due to traffic.  I did call a few minutes before hand when I realized we were stuck on I-465 and they were understanding.  We arrived and were seated promptly.  Thank you for taking care of us!  Thanks next to our hostess & waitress.  They understood we were running late and had to make an event.  Fortunately, my wife used their website to read off the menu while we had been delayed and so we knew what we wanted by the time we got there.  We were able to put in our order at the same time they took our beverage order.  Our food was out quickly, though not at the same time, and we made our deadline by asking for the check right away too.  Now, as mentioned above, we placed our order at the same time, but with tapas, it seems standard that plates are small portion and arrive when ready.  People often share their plates and so it isn't as important as a formal dining arrangement where the expectation is that all meals come out together.  Apparently my wife wasn't familiar with that concept since she doesn't go to many tapas style places.  So, when I got my order of tasty Seared Scallops served over fried green tomatoes and a maple mustard sauce with shaved Parmesan on top, she passed since she isn't a scallop fan.  I really liked the flavor combo, but thought the scallops were a bit small even though there were four of them.    Soon, her Crab & Lobster Cakes arrived but the plate looked rather empty when the two small cakes arrived with only a lobster sauce and pea shoots.  No real side since those are sold separately.    I also ordered a beer and she a soda, so counting tax & tip, our bill was $47.  Seems a bit pricey for the meal.  I really enjoyed mine, but my wife thought the cakes were very average to what she's had around town.  The problem is that it takes just as long to prepare small plates as large and so lowering the prices isn't much of an option.  So, just be aware that the $12-$20 plates can add up quickly if you are hungry.  Aside from the price point, I really enjoyed my experience and would go back now that I have a better understanding of what to expect.    Other stuff:  I grabbed some free parking on the City Hall plaza.  I think there is a parking garage across the plaza, but I'm not sure if there is a cost.  The interior (including the restrooms) were very clean and in good condition, so that is another thing they have going for them.  Review #3115

I've only been once for lunch, but I generally enjoyed my visit to Big Lug.  First, once you get there, they have a great location in a strip mall (a parking lot outside their front door) and next to the Monon Trail (with a patio out their backdoor!)  There are bars and dining areas on both floors as well.  We came in from the parking lot and noticed that the tanks are elevated to the second floor allowing more room downstairs.  It has an industrial feel on the floor and ceiling, but the walls are filled with murals and art/posters to give it a bit of life.  The staff was friendly and kept a pretty good eye on us even though there were a number of people at the bar during our visit.  I also thought they had a tasty fish and chips meal (with house tartar sauce).  The "chips" were hand cut fries that held the salt and tasted like they were lightly seasoned too!  The flavor was really good.  The fish had a crisp batter outside while staying moist inside.    While my wife enjoyed the fish, I ordered the "Kevin Kline" burger as part of the "Indy Burger Week" promotion.  I've had bigger beef patties and ones with a more memorable flavor, but the burger was topped with fresh, crisp lettuce and onion, a tomato slice (probably better when in season), and served on a warm toasted bun.  It also came with mayo and two kinds of cheese.  When ordered with the fries, it was enough to be satisfying without making me feel stuffed.  I do wish they offered beer flights since it was my first time there.  They do offer 7 oz. servings as well as small samples, but it's really hard to evaluate how a beer will taste on just the small sample size.  So, I went with a pint of the Creme Fraiche (Cream Ale 4.7% 14 IBU) which was okay, but didn't really do much for me when paired with the burger.  I should have grabbed something a bit more robust.    So, I defer to other Yelpers about the night life and beer side of the business.  The food was good and portioned well for lunch.  Review #317

This was my first visit to this fast growing local cupcake chain.  After parking in the shared lot (across the lot from Bed Bath & Beyond), I entered the shop.  There is a small seating/dining area by the entrance with the order/display counter towards the back.  By afternoon, the cases weren't as full, but there were still about a dozen options of cupcake in different sizes (priced by size).  I selected a Dirty Chai and a What's Up Doc? to go.  The Dirty Chai was a very large sized yellow cake with a pile of creamy icing sprinkled with seasoning to give it a chai taste along with lots of sweetness.  The cake was okay, but a little dry.  The icing was nicely flavored, but I could have settled for about half as much and still been fine.  The What's Up Doc? was a smaller carrot cake that was decorated a bit more ornately and because of the ingredients, I found it a lot to have a lot more moisture along with a bit of nut/carrot crunch texture.  I really liked this one and the icing, though still thick, was balanced with the cake part.  The staff working behind the counter was really helpful and friendly.    Overall, I would recommend coming here for a specialty cupcake.  Review #3523

When I review a restaurant, before I give it a rating, I consider what my expectations are based upon the type of food they specialize serving.  So, if a place is an ice cream shop, I use different standards than if it is a steakhouse.  It isn't just the price, but the level of satisfaction I get compared to my expectations.  When it comes to the Legend, I knew ahead of time what I was going to order so I had a pretty clear set of expectations, especially since I had dined twice previously at the restaurant. I ordered from the lunch menu a combination of foods that was highly recommended on Yelp!  Upon entering, I asked to sit at the bar since I was by myself and didn't wish to tie up one of the few remaining tables.  I was brought a menu quickly and since I knew what I wanted, I placed my order for "Maybe-your-mom's meatloaf". I selected my two sides of Garlic Mashed Potatoes and Cole Slaw.    Since meatloaf isn't one of those things that needs to be cooked by individual order, I was hoping that my meal wouldn't take long.  SEVEN MINUTES!  That's all!  Even though the house was full, my food was brought to me in only 7 minutes.  Talk about surprised!  The meatloaf was moist and served with a beef gravy on top.  It's made with lean ground beef mixed with sauteed onions, oatmeal, eggs, and spices.  The oatmeal adds a slightly different texture to the meat while keeping the beef from becoming too greasy.  However, the oatmeal didn't seem to change the flavor.  There was just enough salt to bring out the meat flavor.  Overall, it was pretty tasty!  The cole slaw was of the creamy type.  The veggies were still generally crisp, but because of the creamy coating, weren't as crisp as some of the other slaws I have had elsewhere.  What elevated the whole meal was the garlic mashed potatoes.  I expected they might have a strong garlic taste, but these were more buttery tasting.  There were bits of potato skin adding a nice rustic savory flavor to the side.  I like my mashed potatoes to have chunks of potato intact, so I wasn't disappointed.  The potatoes where whipped just to the point that the body of the side was creamy to the edge of becoming gummy, without crossing the line.  It's like they were pushed to the limit without crossing the line.  Excellent.  And they were great for mixing with the extra gravy that had been ladled over the meat loaf.  Highly recommended if you like lumps within your potatoes.  So, my expectations were to spend a lunch having a meal that might remind me of "home made".  And that's what I got.  But with the expertise of execution, friendly service, and efficient delivery, my expectations were greatly exceeded.  Review #149

This delightful shop on the southwest corner of Audubon and Bonna Streets is laid out like a house where you wander from room to room, each with its own sense of style.  So, just because you see something in the front room where the host is seated, you may find something quite different as you wander on back and around.    I went towards the end of the year, so there were lots of holiday items on sale.  There also were lots of knick knacks, some jewelry, pottery, unique ornaments, and even an autoharp!  It's an eclectic gathering of items so take your time to browse.  You never know what cool thing you will find next.  Review #1989

Much like the other Caplinger's on Shadeland and in Noblesville, this location has great seafood.  Even though they have other items, this place is where you should get seafood.  If you go and don't get seafood, then that's a you problem for missing out on the Caplinger's Special and you can deduct a star from your personal rating for being foolish.  They still have the best seafood sandwich in the metro area.    But unlike the other two locations, I had problems with this one.  First, when you walk in the door, it looks like you could walk up to the counter to read the menu and place an order.  But there is an unmarked aisle on the left side which you are supposed to go to.  If people ahead of you are blocking the aisle making up their minds, you have to ask them to step aside so you can place your order.  Second, the guy behind the counter didn't do a good job of communicating.  I got combo lunches which come with beverages.  He handed me two cups, but didn't give any directions about where to find the beverages.  The ice is near the entrance by the tea dispenser.  The sodas are kept to the right of the counter in cans inside a refrigeration unit.  He also didn't ask what I wanted on my wife's sandwich, so it came with nothing.  I assumed, since it was a special, that it came with at least something like lettuce or tartar sauce.  He asked about what I wanted on my sandwich, so I don't understand why he didn't ask about hers.    I also had to ask where the napkins and condiments were.  (Again, they are located near the front of the place instead of near the counter.)  Oh, and if you need additional tartar sauce, they keep that at the counter, but all the other condiments and sauces are at the front.  I assume the tartar sauce is chilled and house made while everything else is in shake bottles or packets.  Still, why aren't they available near the counter?  A little communication would have helped.  But those problems are fixable.  What is left is fantastic seafood.  I have tried the Caplinger's Special (a Vietnamese catfish that is a vegetarian, not a bottom feeder is the species used.)  It was fantastic!  I have had the Blue Crab melt and that was amazing.  Here, I have had the Salmon Filet and it tasted great, but understand that it is a thick slice of fish that is somewhat narrow and you may get bites of sandwich without the fish.    I usually get the collard greens and they are quite tasty.  My wife ordered the baked beans and gave a thumbs up on those too.  So, there are numerous options and we wish that if these group decides to expand further that they may head southwest so we don't have to travel so far to try them.    Go for the food, but either do your research or go with a friend who knows their way around to make the most out of your visit.  Review #481

Great ingredients are necessary for great sandwiches.  At Sub 16, the ingredients are both fresh and full of flavor.  I ordered the roast beef which was served medium rare and had a moderate amount of seasoning.  The Swiss cheese I ordered was sliced from a block of cheese while I waited.  They have a number of size options and allow you to select your toppings and condiments.  I like that they offered toasting for the sandwich for that extra bit of crunch and aroma.  And the taste was so good!    Review #451

This is another store my wife and I frequent when browsing Perry Crossing.  They always have some cool items to check out (even if you didn't think you needed it!)  Most of the items are smaller and could find room in your home, but I noticed they are carrying some larger items like chairs, so that will be interesting to keep an eye on.  They have a lot of holiday merchandise as well as their assortment of home decor.  Prices are typical for mall franchises, but not unreasonable.  And they often seem to have sales to help with that.  Staff usually lets you browse but seem helpful if you ask.  Most of them are running the cash registers since this place always seems busy.  Review #1950

I met friends on Monday for lunch at Iozzo's.  After parking in the side lot (north side of the building), we entered through the plexi-glass entrance into the richly decorated dining area.  Large pictures decorated the area.  The bar was situated off to the left.  We decided to head to the back of the building which leads out onto the cobblestone patio, sheltered between two shotgun style buildings.  Each table had an umbrella and was stationed between fountains and plants that made it seem much more inviting than the location might suggest.  The only negative of being outside was the sound of traffic from the nearby interstate that is not too far away to the south.  After placing our orders, we received a complimentary basket of bread with butter and a small plate of chopped tomato nestled in olive oil.  This was okay with the bread, but lacked any wow factor.  Maybe a bit of balsamic vinegar or pepper may have perked up the flavor.  My entree came with a side salad that I paired with the balsamic vinaigrette.  Excellent greens and the dressing was somewhat sweet.  Very tasty!  I started with an Orzo Portabella entree.  This comes with sliced mushrooms, sun dried tomatoes, basil, and scallions tossed in thick tomato cream sauce.  Other than the sauce being a little bit thick, the flavors were terrific!  There was a hint of tartness to the meal which added a nice layer of flavor to go with the pasta and savory mushrooms and tomatoes.  I also ordered a Caprese Panini with a side of house chips.  The house chips were really delicious with a dusting of seasoning that seemed to have a hint of sweetness.  It also came with a nice side of a whipped dip.  (Definitely try these!)  The Panini had a bit of pancetta, mozzarella, basil, greens, and basil pesto aioli.  I was a little disappointed that the tomato wasn't as flavorful as some of the caprese I have had lately...maybe the peak for fresh, ripe tomatoes has come and gone.  The rest of the sandwich was okay, but I couldn't really taste the pancetta.  Just a bit bland.  One of my friends ordered the Stuffed Portabella Mushroom appetizer as a meal.  It came with three nice sized mushrooms, and filled with spinach artichoke dip and mozzarella cheese.  She thought it was perfectly cooked and that the flavors were well balanced.  (I think she was inspired to try making this at home!)  Definitely would recommend this item.  My other friend opted for the Chicken Diavolo.  This came with a bed of spaghetti under the chicken and topped with spicy marinara sauce.  It definitely had more heat than any of the other items we ordered, but it wasn't overly hot from the spices.  He mentioned that the chicken (cut into strips) retained its moisture and was good as well.  Overall, the service was attentive and efficient.
