Good job in getting my friends in and out so they could return to work.  If you haven't been to Iozzo's in a while (or ever), I recommend making a point to stop in the next time you are downtown.   Review #130

One of the perks of being older, my group of six people had all received their Covid vaccines and were ready to get out for some social fun.  We selected Penn & Beech in Carmel since my wife and I had enjoyed the candle making at the Mass Avenue place so much, but realize parking (especially while the NCAA tournament downtown made it less appealing than this north side location).     The  Carmel location is located in one of the first floor shops of the free parking garage just south of the Sun King Spirits and park along the Monon Trail/Boulevard where Elm Street crosses.  (if you are traveling north/south on Rangeline road, just look for the roundabout with the Brad Howe sculpture Reckon (2019) in the middle and that is Elm Street.  Head west towards the Monon and pull into the garage next to the entrance.  Who doesn't love ample free parking?     Once you find it (reservations are recommended for groups, but walk ins are accepted if they aren't too busy.)  During your visit, you will select from hundreds of scents.  After filling out a list of your favorites, you will be taken through the process by the hostess to show you how to mix the scented oils that will give your personalized candle your own preferred scent.  You pick a vessel (you get to keep it) that your candle will eventually be poured into.  Through a series of sniffing and stirring, you mix the oils to get your optimal scent.  The process of mixing takes about 90 minutes.  The hard part is then waiting another 2 hours for the hot wax to solidify in your selected vessel with a wick.  The 2 hours is pretty much needed to avoid having your candle spill during transport and if you've ever touched hot wax, it can be painful.  If you've ever tried to get hot wax out of your clothing or car seat, you know it is worth waiting the 2 hours to avoid any problems.  The good news is that downtown Carmel has a lot to do while you wait.  You pay when you finish making your candle and create a label that identifies it.  After two hours, you can return to pick it up.  They do have wine and some beverages to help you pass the time if you decide to wait it out on location.  We chose a nearby restaurant and had a nice afternoon/early dinner all in the same trip to downtown Carmel.   Note that there are hundreds of scents so it does take time and to be honest, by the end, I was glad I had lost some of my sense of smell as having so many people in our group all mixing at the same time made it a little hard to discern the final scent of my own because I just don't encounter so many scents at one time usually.  But I trusted my initial choices and the help of the hostess to help select fragrances that were complementary to my favorites.  Today I am enjoying my candle as I type:  a mix of pear, teakwood, and mahogany.  None of my scent choices was overpowering, so my den is filled with this nice, fresh aroma of pears and wood.   If you have time and some $, this is a great socialization activity where you each leave with something that suits your own tastes and you share in the experience with friends.  There is no minimum age posted, but because there is hot wax and the scented oils are not something you want to spill all over, I wouldn't suggest it as a child's activity.  But great for adult friends to get out and do something individually, but able to socialize while working. Great staff were friendly and knowledgeable.  Review #3893

Well despite the struggles this relaunch of Brew Link experienced, I didn't give up on them.  They simply have a great line up of tasty beers.  I continue to be impressed with the flavors that they seem to create.  I also like that they seem to have enough trained staff to reduce wait times.  On my most recent visit (Sunday lunch), I was able to order a flight of beer and a sandwich/side with my total time at the place just over a half hour.  Huge improvement and sitting in the bar seemed much quieter than in the dining area as well.  I ordered a pulled pork sandwich which was tasty (a bit on the salty side) with a house barbecue sauce.  Sure, I would prefer to pick my own type of sauce, but what they had was pretty good.  The slaw was also good with a lighter, less creamy texture.  They still serve flights in the order you tell them instead of arranging them in best drinking order (the same way with the beer menu.)  This is one of the few breweries that doesn't arrange the beers to optimize the flavor for guests.  Not a problem for experienced flight drinkers, but for someone new to craft beer, it is an unnecessary risk.  I even asked the server which order she would suggest, but the answer showed a lack of understanding of how sours and IPA's can throw off the taste of lighter beers.  Oh, well, I've mentioned it more than once.  I can now fully recommend going here.  So glad the management took steps to make the experience better for the guests.  If you were one who experienced their rough start, I say give them another try.  If you haven't been here before, I'll ask "What are you waiting for?"  Rev. #46

This review is strictly for the exterior garden and art.  I have not taken classes here.  On a beautiful afternoon in August, I had the time to wander about the gardens of IAC.  There are numerous terraces & gardens, a mural, and many large installations of outdoor art placed around the paths as I wandered.    In addition to all the art and nature trails, there is a scenic overlook of the White River that comes equipped with a ramp so that anyone can enjoy the view.    Overall, the tranquil setting allows for individual contemplation on what was the artist of each piece trying to convey.  So glad I was able to find time to return to this pocket paradise along the Monon in Broad Ripple.  Review #110  FYI: For a more complete list of Public Art in Indianapolis go to the following website:  http://www.indyartsguide.org/public-art/

One of the newest places to tempt you on Mass Avenue is a delightful ice cream and candy shop out of Petoskey Michigan.  From the moment I stepped in, I felt like I was going to struggle making a decision:  So many candies, taffy apples, fudges, ice creams, and candied popcorn that it is hard to know where to start.  Fortunately, I was snapped out of my overload by the staff who invited me to come over and sample some fudge.  I also sampled some of the ice creams before making a purchase there too!  I think having the samples was enough to clear my head and allow me to feel satisfied with just a half slice of fudge (saved for later) and single cup of ice cream.  Yes, the place is more expensive than the fast food soft serve places around town, but even though it is a chain, it isn't as mass produced as some places.  They actually make the candied popcorn in the back as well as quite a few of their items.  But here is the one thing I noticed that keeps me from giving this place a 5-star rating:  Some things I picked to sample didn't taste anything like what I expected.  I really loved the Sea-Salt Caramel fudge, but the peanut butter fudge wasn't very sweet and tasted a little "earthy" to me....maybe like unsalted peanuts.  I also really liked the Turtle ice cream (with just a hint of salt to offset the sweetness), but was surprised that I didn't like the Banana Fudge Pie ice cream....it tasted like artificially flavored banana.  I don't know if they use real bananas or not, but the taste was just different.  My advice:  Try everything before you buy.  You may find some items that you really love!  But, you may be disappointed if you buy something just on the name.  The store is glad to let you sample the ice creams and fudges, so try them.  They don't want bad reviews any more than you want to dislike your purchase.  If you are disappointed, it may be your own fault.  Review #2466

My wife and our friend joined me for dinner on Thursday evening for dinner.  After parking in the lot on the north side of the restaurant, we were seated on the canal side of the building.  Unfortunately, it was already dark so the view wasn't a factor.  After placing our drink orders, we were served complimentary pita and herbed\spiced olive oil.  Very tasty for our friend and me.  We also ordered the flaming Saganaki and the fun of yelling "Opa!".  After the flame subsided, the cheese was warm throughout and the exterior that crisped added another level of flavor and texture to the softened cheese.  The chew of the firmed cheese seemed to unlock flavor as we consumed it.  Definitely order this if you enjoy cheese!  I ordered the Grilled Salmon which came with a house side salad (delicious!) and rice (I think it was jasmine).  The salmon had a bit of a char on the bottom which gave it a real grilled flavor.  It came with lemon, tahini sauce, pickled onions, and house pickles.  Very nice combo of flavors.  Our friend ordered the Fattoush salad and it had a pungent flavor that was aggressive, but tasty.  I sampled a bite and noted there was definite salinity to the flavor, but it was balanced by the other flavors.  The crisp pita chips added a nice bit of crispness to the salad.  She also ordered a lamb gyro that also had a saltiness to it, but she loves salt and thought the gyro "delightful".  She ended up needing a to-go box for the second half of the sandwich.  My wife isn't a big fan of powerful herb and spice flavors, so she went with the Shawarma beef which comes in a wrap.  This was the only disappointing flavor of the night.  There was a dominant spice (not sure if it was allspice or nutmeg or something in that range) that stayed as an after taste for quite awhile between bites.  The beef, although tenderloin, was overcooked and chewy.  So,she was disappointed with her meal.  Fortunately, the wrap came with fries to munch on.  I would suggest the restaurant put curtains on the north side.  As we walked in from the lot, we could see into the kitchen and it wasn't the most appealing view.    I would also recommend that they paint yellow on the step up into the restaurant.  Since the step is set back about a foot from the sidewalk, they filled in with a sloped bit of concrete, but left about a one inch "lip" of the step overhanging the slope which could easily trip someone not watching closely.  Review #197

This full service bakery has a large variety of pastries, both Mexican and traditional American.  There is plenty of parking in the lot for this business at the end of a strip.  Once you walk in, you will see walls of display cases filled with assorted pastries and cookies that don't run out early.  Making selections is self-serve, so you should pick up a large metal platter and pair of tongs near the entrance to take with you as you move around the store.    I picked up a mix including double flavored danish, strudels, churros, and some crispy versions of twists and elephant ears.  My wife loves the crispy styles and is already planning our next visit.  When I made my selections, I took them to the central counter and was pleasantly surprised how affordable they were.  The staff was friendly and had offered to help if I had any questions.    If I could make any suggestions, it would be to maintain the labels on the display cases.   Review #501

The Commodore is the newest attempt at a speakeasy style bar in Indianapolis.  Although it isn't quite as clandestine as the prohibition era speakeasies, the bar does a good job of masking their location.  Even if you know which building it is in, they don't have any signage pointing to their entrance and no sliding panel to knock on to give a password.  Fortunately, you don't need a password to get in here, but it does take some patience to find and helps to have good word of mouth from someone.  As a matter of fact, the bartender doesn't want anyone to set this up on Yelp because he's afraid it will become just like any other bar.  He wanted to maintain the secret place which is why I haven't given any specifics about how to find the entrance.  They have a huge instagram following, so I don't see what problem Yelp is going to add.  If you are in the area, stop for dinner at one of the local restaurants and ask for assistance finding it.   Inside the bar is rather dark but with mid century furniture grouped in the open space before the bar.  The bar (mainly cocktails) is along the back wall and when we first visited, my wife and I were told to just grab a seat at one of the tables.  It was 5 pm on a Thursday evening, so the place was rather empty.  Lots of room at that time for social distancing.     The bartender came over with actual cocktail lists that made it easier to determine what we wanted to order.  I prefer gin drinks, so I ordered the "Corpse of New Orleans" which is served in a small Peychauds bitters bottle with a metal straw.  My wife isn't much of a cocktail drinker, so she described what she liked and the bartender made her a "Clarified Milk Punch" which she really enjoyed since she likes the flavor of margaritas most places, this was closest to what they had available.     There isn't food available, but since Maialina is on the same floor of the building, we came back the night before Halloween with two other couples, dined Italian, and then headed over to the Commodore entrance for cocktails.   The bar was decorated for Halloween and was very dark inside with only some purple lights (possibly black lights).  We grabbed some lounge seating just large enough for the six of us.  But no menus were offered, just Ouija boards with the cocktails etched in with small red letters.  Nearly impossible for us to read in the low lighting.  If that's all they offer you, just ask for a real menu to make it easier on yourself to figure out what the house specialties are.   The place was much more crowded the second night since it was a Friday and a little later in the evening.  They had the music turned up a bit too loud for conversation which I don't get.  There is no room for a dance floor, so why so loud?  We got them to turn it down enough so that we could enjoy our visit with each other as well as the ambiance.   I wonder if this place that opened during the pandemic and chooses to hide deep inside a building with no signage to let customers know where to find them, AND discourages social media will make it.  It's a cool place for folks who like cocktails, but if you are just a "dive bar" kinda patron, you probably won't like the limited offerings and high priced drinks.  I doubt they carry bud light, but I didn't ask.   I will say that everyone in our group who ordered a cocktail enjoyed what they had.  Our friend who only drinks straight rye was pleased with their selection.     Unless this place gets a following of "regulars", I think the lack of attention will make it fall victim to poor cash flow like so many other places.  The novelty of the place is in finding it.  Once you are here, it seems just like any other bar with tasty cocktails.  I don't know if that is enough to continue bring folks in.   Review #3841

On my first visit, I choose to stop inside the business instead of pulling up to the drive through lanes.  In the lobby, there is an open area in front of the counter where you can see the over-sized menu boards, grab some Torani flavors for your coffee, or have a seat while you wait (no tables though.)  I had looked over the menu online for this Kokomo based franchise before arriving, so I stepped up and got a house black coffee to sip on while I waited for my 6" sandwich called the "Deluxe (Supreme)" which is basically all the ingredients you would get on the pizza by the same name, but on a tasty and toasted submarine sandwich bun.   Surprisingly fast, the sandwich was ready to go!  The sandwich comes wrapped in foil within a nice little paper, logo bearing, bag.  Note that I forgot to grab a napkin and they don't put one inside the small bag, so be sure to grab some before you take off.  The sandwich must be cooked at a high temperature because some of the cheese was burned and stuck to the foil.  But the sandwich itself was fine and unaffected by the cheese.  The bread was lightly crisped and was really tasty and light inside.  (Best bun award!)  The ingredients of the sandwich were fine, but nothing that blew me away.  The cheese was generously applied and had a soft, pillow-y bite.  The ground beef was lightly seasoned and truly ground into small bits.  The onion and peppers were well cooked and the tomato paste was ample, but lacked the deep flavors of a really good Italian sauce.    The 6" version I ordered was plenty for lunch and I give them credit that the sandwich and most of the ingredients stayed in place though there were a few bits that fell back onto the foil.    I also appreciate that they were willing to put together a lunch before 11 a.m. since I was there about 20 minutes before then.  It fit my schedule perfectly on this day and contributes to my solid rating.  They have lots of fancy coffee based drinks for those who like them, but it's nice to know that they make a good cup of rich dark coffee that is served hot, but not scalding, so that I could enjoy it right away.  Overall, a good first visit and I would gladly return when I am in the area.  Review #2026

Nice little shop for all your sweet cravings when visiting the marina/Geist Reservoir.  Tucked away on the north side of the reservoir in a small strip mall filled with mostly restaurants, this is the place to pick out your hand dipped ice cream, get house baked cookies, and some packaged items like honey, popcorn, or some candies.  The staff was helpful giving tastings before purchase if you are debating between flavors.  I went with a Dark Chocolate Raspberry Ripple which had a deep flavor.    There is convenient dining both inside and out (weather permitting) for enjoying your purchases.  Parking is shared with other businesses in the strip.  They don't have the largest selection of flavors in the metro area, but all in my group seemed to enjoy their choices.  Review #3637

Having seen some Yelp reviews for 'Frittle Candy", I soon learned that the business behind the candy was called Newfangled Confections and it's just a stones throw off Mass Avenue on North Street.  I stopped by the simple green house and grabbed a spot in the parking lot next door.  There's a small sign in the window that has the company name and I saw they were open, so it was time to experience the amazing treats for myself!    The owner/creator of the candy was there and she was packing a lot of samples to take to a trade show, but took time out to greet and help me pick out a package of Sweet & Spicy Pecans and a box of Frittle.    The pecans are coated with both brown sugar and sugar, butter, and a combination of spices that add a little savory flavor to the initial taste.  Then, there is a surprise as the spices kick in a bit of heat on the aftertaste.  Quite tasty!  The candy that seems to draw the most attention (well deserved!) is the Frittle.  I've seen reviews try to describe it and the best I can offer is that it is a sweet peanut flavored candy that is cut into small flat squares.  The texture is somewhere between that of peanut butter fudge and peanut brittle.  There is a little bit of crunch, but much softer than I expected.    I've done a lot of candy making on my own and know it is quite labor intensive and can be very unforgiving if the temperature isn't right.  Heat it too slowly and the moisture steams off.  Heat it too quickly and you run the risk of burning the sugars on the bottom of the pan (it can ruin a whole batch!)  The ingredients swell and bubble and to the untrained eye will look like it will be done, but you have to keep stirring and watching.  It's no wonder that the small boxes sell for about $5..not for the ingredients, but for the time it takes.  And it will be $5 that you won't regret spending!  Review #1378

Okay, when I complain about there being little things that keep me from giving a 5-star rating, and the place fixes those, then it seems fair to update my review and give out that fifth star!  I had complained about there not being a way to identify all the unusual species in the rabbit and fowl building.  This year, the rabbits had signs over their cages and there were three posters filled with the names and images of the unique fowl that was on display.  I just took pictures of the ones that caught my attention and looked them up on the posters.  Check!  I also complained that the condensation on the fish tanks over at the DNR building made it impossible to see the fish clearly.  This year?  Not a bit of condensation.  Great visibility.  And the outdoor viewing of the fish was improved (and labeled too!)    Sure, there are lots of things that will quickly bite into your wallet if you try to do everything, especially with a family.  But there are discounts and special days for more discounts, so it simply requires some planning and some self-restraint to avoid running up a huge bill.  I didn't find it that hard to keep my costs down and still got a nice taste of the fair.    And there are lots of free exhibits to check out too which gave breaks from the heat while entertaining.  Thanks State Fair for continuing to improve the experience of your guests.  Rev #47

When it turns out that your first choice for lunch falls through, It is nice to know that a dependable alternative is in the neighborhood.  My wife and I were out to try some new local place, but found it did not have an actual sit down location and it's sister business was experiences a loss of its kitchen equipment/fryers, so we decided to switch to plan C and since we have had good experiences at other McAlister's in the past, we pulled in and grabbed a bite.  There was a lot of indoor seating, but the air conditioning made it quite chilly, so after ordering at the counter and being given a "Number card" to place on our table, it wasn't long before the servers found us and brought out our beverages.  (these are huge!  It also was just a short wait until our meals were also brought out.     I ordered a really good Reuben with plenty of corned beef and a nice amount of sauerkraut.  Really nice pairing of flavors.  Unfortunately, when they made my wife's sub wrap. it had no condiments on it.  She was given a condiment packet that was not pressed properly for easy opening.  I was able to force a fork through the plastic and she was able to get a little mayo for her sandwich, but it would be nice if they could ask if you wanted any before they sent the sandwich out to the dining room.  The utensils they give simply aren't sharp enough to open the packets neatly.     She also upgraded her side to a tomato bisque soup for a small charge and thought it had a nice flavor, but was so thick that it reminded her of tomato sauce, not soup.  Overall, we enjoyed our food, it's just the little things that kept this from being a really enjoyable meal.  Review #3933

Since so many of my friends have already done great reviews of the overall restaurant, I will focus on the Savor Downtown special that the brewery ran.  My wife and I street parked on Delaware and seated ourselves in the main dining room.  Note that all the seats there are high top seats.  The only ones with backs are at the bar. (There may be some lower tables in one the back dining rooms, but I did not grab a spot there.)  Before long, our waiter arrived with menus, tableware, napkins, and got our drink order.  Although the beer menu (quite exensive) says that flights are $7 for four samples (about 5 ounces each), they actually are priced individually.  Many combos will be $7, but one of my selections was a dollar more bringing the total to $8.  If that matters to you, you should ask if any of the prices are higher since it wasn't indicated on the menu.  I selected the David Hasselhefe - Hefeweizen (4.8%, 11IBU); the Midnight Fuel - Coffee Stout (6.3% 50); Satsuma Pop-Star - double hopped Imperial Milkshake IPA (11.2% ?); and the Nefarious Nectar - Belgian Golden Ale (9.2%, 29).  The Hefe was okay, but a little lacking in clove punch.  The Stout had a deep roasted coffee taste.  The Imperial was surprisingly smooth without a punch of hops.  Maybe it was due to eating food while drinking, but I was very pleased with the taste.  And the Golden had a fruity (think peach) flavor that also was quite tasty.  For the Savor Downtown special, we got one shareable appetizer, one entree each, and one shareable dessert.  We opted for the Fried Dill Pickles which are served in a conical basket with a dipping sauce.  A nice combo of tart and creamy/savory flavors.  My wife had the Indiana Tenderloin which was a bit overcooked and dry, but passable with the spicy mustard served with it.  I went for the Beer Cheese Burger (1/2#) topped with bacon and lots of garden stuff.  It was cooked medium and was quite juicy.  Both our entrees came with seasoned fries that were also cooked just right.  They were topped with cilantro and paprika and also had a sauce for dipping.  I really enjoyed the dessert:  Key Lime Pie!  It looked fantastic and I loved the flavor too!  Not only did it have all the standard key lime elements (light and creamy filling, graham cracker crust), but it was drizzle with a bright green sour apple glaze (think melted Jolly Ranchers) that took it to another level. My wife wasn't a fan of the addition, but I loved it.  Service was friendly at the lunch hour and we were in and out in well under an hour.  I can see returning to try more of their house brews in the future.  Review #1148

Although there is some stiff competition for top ice cream spot in Broad Ripple, I believe Wyliepalooza is right near the top!  The shop is small, but has a great location on 54th at the Monon.  Though small in size, they  have big flavors and I recommend the Banana Cream Pie Ice Cream.   Plenty of creamy texture and such delicious flavor!    They have some lawn chairs out front for relaxing and a few area lots will let you park and go.  If you haven't been here yet, make it a point to check it out the next time you're in Broad Ripple!  Review #2800

If you are looking for a fun and inexpensive way to escape the winter weather of Indiana, then consider heading over to Indianapolis' oldest city park and explore the Garfield Park Conservatory.      This park is conveniently located off I-65 taking the Raymond Street exit west to Shelby Street, and just a couple blocks south from there.    Once in the park, the conservatory and Sunken Gardens are the first points of interest on your left.  There are two free parking lots on the north side of the Conservatory.  The building and gardens are also handicap accessible.    There is a lobby where you can hang a coat and pay your $2 entry fee.  Brochures for a self-guided tour are at the counter and if you have any other questions, the staff person can answer them for you.  On the day I went, I had questions about two plants that I was unsure of their names, so that was determined quickly.    The first room beyond the lobby holds a large gazebo.  This makes a great room for the Conservatory's exhibits of bulbs and art throughout the year.  The gazebo looks like it would be a great for a photo shoot (Special photo shoots require advance approval from the Park.  See the website for details.)    From the moment you walk into the lobby and the actual conservatory, you will be aware of lots of foliage encased within a glass and metal housing.  This allows lots of sunlight for the plants within, but can make photography a bit challenging.  I was fortunate that I selected an overcast day which made my picture taking experience much easier.    The Conservatory has a pathway that loops through the entire length creating a center "island" that has additional plants and an artificial waterfall with a Koi pond on the south end.  The self-guided tour encourages the visitor to travel clockwise around the path.  You will notice that there are label markers at the base of the plants that include the common and scientific names and the country or region where the plants are from.  Twenty Two plants have been selected as representatives of the collection and have additional information within the brochure.  These representative plants have numbers on their markers that match the brochure for easier identification.    The numbered markers are not always easy to find.  Generally, the numbers alternate back and forth across the pathway as you proceed.  The brochure will help you know what to look for as you travel by giving a description of what to look for.    About a third of the way on the southward leg of the loop, there is a side hall that leads to another building that is for the staff.  This hall is where a restroom and some live animal tanks can be found.  I recall there being a frog, snake, tarantula, and green anole as well as a fish tank.    As you walk, you will see a number of flowering plants and brightly colored foliage.  Bromeliads and orchids are two of the most populous varieties.  Bird of Paradise plants are also quite colorful and one extremely large plant is near the end of the loop, but unfortunately, wasn't in full bloom at my visit.    There are also a number of trees maintained within the building.  A number of fruit bearing and varieties of palm trees can be seen on the trip.  Other trees produce seeds that are used in making gum, cocoa, perfume, and spices.    On the southern end of the loop, a large artificial rock formation fills the southern part of the loop.  A nice waterfall feature drops into the koi pond.  The sides and back of the rock formation are covered with orchids and other flowering plants.    Overall, the park does a really good job with the space they have.  They try to add variety by hosting bulb shows and orchid shows, but generally speaking, the plants are the same each visit.  At different times during the year, the plants will be in different stages of blooming and fruit bearing, so when combined with the plantings in the Sunken Garden, there will be something new to see on a return visit.   Review #214

There was a time that JC Penney was our first choice for buying clothes.  It was one of the few national brands that was available in the Midwest.  Now that I'm retired, I don't need "dress" clothes as often, but I wanted to pick up a nice short sleeved shirt for nights out with my wife when we go to upscale restaurants.  Immediately, JCP came to mind.  On this trip, the escalators to the second floor of the store were shut down, so I had to find the elevator to gain access to the Men's department.  Once there, I noticed a couple employees processing some inventory in the checkout area.  I looked and looked, but wasn't having finding short sleeved shirts;  all I saw was long sleeved.  So I asked and finally the gentleman took me over to one small section and pointed towards another section that seemed to only carry slim cut clothes (my slim days are passed.)    I was a bit disappointed that they didn't have much in my size.  Lots for guys either heavier or more muscular, but not much for me.  Fortunately, I only needed one and made my purchase.  They still ask if it will be on a Penney's card and if I wanted to sign up for a rewards program, but I would have liked to have had as much effort put into someone helping me find options.  It just wasn't the same level of help I used to get in "the old days."    I got a suitable (no pun intended) shirt for my purposes, but between the inconvenience of the equipment failures and the lack of inventory and eagerness, I can't say it was anything more than just "OK".  Review #2579

They have lots of options for caffeine and and non-caffeine drinks, smoothies, juices, and even some pastries.  Honestly, as someone who usually just drinks a straight black coffee, the options are seemingly endless.  Still, the staff behind the counter was patient and took their time to make sure I knew all the options available when I decided to try one of their specialty lattes.      The drink itself was pretty tasty.  I also enjoyed the Coffee Cake muffin which was reasonably priced at $2.50.  Service was fast and helpful.  They have drive-up service too.  Review #496

It had been a long time since I had been to Kabuto.  I had tried the hibachi style dinner with a show from the chef.  It was okay, but not amazing.  This time, I decided to try the sushi side of the business for lunch.    After parking in the spacious lot out front, this strip mall restaurant had the drapes closed which made me wonder if it was open.  It didn't look inviting.  I saw the open sign and decided to head on in.  After passing through a couple of entrance doors, I was greeted by the hostess and after asking if I wanted hibachi or "other", she directed me to seat myself in an enclosed area with a drape across the entrance and half walls containing six 4-top tables.  From there, the service was pretty good, though most folks were in the hibachi section, so I did go awhile between seeing any waitresses.  Fortunately, they didn't forget about me as the lone diner in the sushi section.    I ordered a hot green tea and though it tasted good, they left the leaves in the bottom of my cup.  I thought I saw a couple floating pieces of tea leaf along the edge of my cup.  It wasn't until I got near the bottom that I couldn't drink any more without getting a mouth full of chopped tea leaves.  Why don't they use a strainer or poultice to contain the leaves?  No refill was requested.  I ordered a side salad which is mostly iceberg lettuce and a few shredded carrot strips topped with a ginger dressing.  It tasted like it was peanut based so much that I had to ask if it had nuts, but was assured it was simply ginger based.  I really didn't taste the ginger at all.  And they salad was drenched in dressing which left a lot of it at the bottom of the salad bowl.  Soon, by Salmon (Sake) Nigiri salmon and my Dragon Roll (avocado topped Eel Roll) arrived.  The portions were large.  The salmon was big enough that it required two bites for each of the pieces.  It wasn't a chilled as some other places, but still at an acceptable temperature.  Nice flavor with/without the low sodium soy.  The Dragon Roll was a bit disappointing.  It was technically correct, but lacked any of the artistic flair I see at other sushi restaurants that go the extra distance to make the roll worth the $11 charge.  The meal was fine and the service was fine.  It just seemed like there wasn't any life in the place or the food that made me want to return soon.  Review #2660

I've been nicknamed "Mr Parks" because of my numerous park reviews, so when I read Brady R's review of this previously unvisited park, I knew I had to go.    What I found after parking right next to the entrance along Virginia, was a greeting in the sidewalk quoting a John Lennon song.  There were numerous shrub plantings that were full of fall colors. Those were just tall enough to block the view of what lie ahead in the park other than a narrow gravel trail.  As I walked along, there were numerous benches, many of them with quotes from different authors and/or faiths.   And finally, the path opens up to a small park setting where a triangular tarp offers shade over three rows of baseball seats from the Indpls Indians former stadium.  The tarp is anchored by several gabions which counterweight the tarp to keep it from blowing away in the wind.  The space beyond the seating is landscaped with mulch and small plants.  A small fence blocks the visitors from wandering any farther down into the greenspace which lies between the lanes of interstate traffic down below.  And that's it.  But that's when it struck me:  I'm retired and I enjoy getting out and doing whatever I feel like on a given day.  While thousands of people are rushing here and there in Indy each day (like the interstate), I get to simply take my time to explore, eating and drinking my way around central Indiana.  I have a blast!  And in this location, I see the metaphor for retirement...taking time to appreciate that I've made it this far and no longer have to do the rushing.  I can sit and watch everyone else rush about and be glad they do so I don't have to.  There is a steady murmur of sound like white noise that I found surprisingly relaxing.  I could see grabbing a bite of food or a beverage from one of the dozens of local places and coming here to relax.  Review #1655

This was our second trip to the Tile Shop on the southside.  Our first was to select tile for a backsplash in our kitchen.  Nearly ten years later, we were able to find the same tile and the complementary smaller trim tiles to replace the damaged ones we had when we changed counter tops through a different company.  I won't guarantee that if you make a purchase, and need more at a later time they will have it, but it definitely influenced my rating.     Like the other reviewers, the customer service could be more welcoming.  We wandered the spacious store looking for something to go with our tile and when the small staff did not greet us, my wife simply took matters into her own hands and asked one of the staff (when she finished on the phone) if she could help us.  They just don't have many folks on the floor to assist.  Maybe if they shifted priority to helping in house customers instead of dealing with other tasks, they would have a better overall rating.   The most frustrating thing my wife encountered was that they didn't have the boxes for the items you wanted stacked nearby.  So, we couldn't tell if the items were available in the quantities we wanted without asking.  Again, not having many people working means there may be delays in getting answers.  Fortunately, they weren't that busy during our visit and my wife was able to get the small quantity of items packaged and ready to go in just a short visit.   Overall, they have a lot of beautiful displays to inspire customers for future projects.  I thought the prices reflected the different quality of materials, so you have a lot of control over how much your renovation can run based upon the materials you choose.  We had good service and liked our materials we selected.  Review #3871

I was in the KatC area getting ready to watch a movie, and decided to stop in at Piada to grab a quick bite to go.  So glad I did!  I had read that the experience is not as quick as fast food, but I must have timed it right and was in and out in just over five minutes.    I found a spot in the shared parking lot north of the building and once I entered, I figured out that I should walk down the hallway on the right down to the food counter.  There, I picked up a copy of the menu and quickly  was able to spot something I wanted to try (I like variety, but sometimes, keeping the menu simple is a benefit!)   I opted for the seasonal Summer Avocado Piada.  I had never had a piada before, but it's basically a wrap or an Italian tortilla used to pack all kinds of flavorful items in a portable bundle.  The basic piada has roasted sweet corn (YUM!!!), cherry tomatoes, avocado, arugula, mozzarella, crispy pancetta, and a basil aioli.  I upgraded and added some chunky chicken for a small fee and had one heck of a tasty meal!  Great flavors.  A little spicier than I would have guessed, but just fine for me.  Plenty to eat too!  The piada was about 7-8 inches in length.  They built the piada right in front of me, so I could see all the fresh ingredients going in.  If you have any restrictions on what you want included, you better let them know up front....the line staff was quick and had the piada rolled and passed down the line to the cashier in seconds!  I couldn't believe how quick they moved.    Even with the added chicken, it was less than $10 before tax and tip.  Really good taste, friendly and efficient service.  I can see why there was a nice crowd of folks enjoying their meal in the generously sized dining area.  Review #377

Forget the over-hyped chain that blew into town trying to be Chicago.  This locally owned restaurant loves Chicago sports teams (Cubs and Bears), and brings the food that is associated with that area.  They also have an open new space with lots of windows and also have a 3-way liquor license.  I was in the area and stopped by to grab a quick "Chicago Dog" and some house made chips.  The hot dog came loaded with all the colorful ingredients that makes it Chicago, but that most Hoosiers just don't bother to add.  The flavor was great, the bun soft, but solid enough to hold the ingredients in, and the Vienna hot dog was good enough that you could eat it plain, but why would you?  The house chips come in two sizes, and are crisp with a bit of seasoning (not much salt though).  Since my daughter's family lives in Brownsburg, I can see stopping by here again.  Maybe I'll even catch a ball game on the big screens.  Note:  They don't have their own parking and street parking isn't allowed.  So, there are two surface lots on the west side of Green Street and the parking garage on the west side is also available.  Don't use the parking garage on the east side of the street since it is for the residents only.  Note 2:  At the time of my review, Green Street is still closed on the south end of the complex, so if you are coming from Avon or the south, you will need to go through a few neighborhood streets to get here.  Otherwise, from the north there is no difficulty at all.  Review #2426

Pleasantly surprising food from this little corner shop of City Market.  Although I arrived after five, I ordered from the posted lunch menu:  small tomato basil soup and half a sage aioli chicken salad on french bread.  All for only six bucks!  Service was quick and they offered a choice of a slice of french bread or corn bread as well.  The soup had a lot of flavor with a slightly salty leaning.  Although it was good, I found the basil was only a minor flavor leaving a mostly tomato taste.  The chicken salad was generous in size and was fresh and moist.  I liked that they added pistachios to the salad for a bit of crunch.  The sage was very subtle like most of the flavors.  Not exactly bland, but not screaming with flavor either.    Overall, a quick and satisfying meal for a low price.  Review #183

I stopped in for lunch and was pleasantly surprised at my surroundings.  After finding free street parking across from the entrance, I noticed they had some umbrella covered dining in front of the building.  But since it was about 90 by lunch time, I headed inside for the air conditioning.    Inside, there is a small lounge area (the Rhino Lounge) to the left and then a "to go" order counter just ahead on the left (the kitchen is behind that area.)  That leaves a long and somewhat narrow dining area with a row of 4-tops along the right wall and a row of 2-tops running parallel across the aisle.  Nice that none of the chairs open into the walkway!  Inside there is art work everywhere.  Paintings, murals, and comic murals of Rhinos doing human things like grilling pizza are painted on the bathroom wall.  (The family name is phonetically close the Rhino, hence the family's affinity for the large mammals.)  I was greeted and was directed to pick a spot since the place wasn't that crowded.  I grabbed a 2-top about midway back.  The waitress brought out a menu that was fairly quick and easy to negotiate with there being some apps, some salads, some sandwiches, and then lots of pizzas.  Still I was able to make a quick selection and got my order into the kitchen.    I browsed the paintings for a few minutes and my Caesar salad was ready.  For a small, it was still a pretty fair size.  The flavor was really good.  The Romaine was fresh and crisp.  The cheese was shaved, not some prepackaged stuff.  The croutons were large and house made.  Not overly crunchy like store bought, but with enough to add texture.  Very good for $6.  I also ordered a small pizza (about a 10" or so.)  I went with the "Big Momma" which comes with the house sauce (?), pepperoni, sausage, and mushrooms (cut on the large side).  The crust is ultra thin and when grill fired, gets a bit blackened to a crispy crunch.  This isn't one of those fold your pi places.  It would snap before you folded it.  I must admit I liked the thin crust especially since I didn't want to feel full from eating lots of dough.  The rest of the pie was just a little bit of a mystery to me.  I have eaten lots of pizzas with similar ingredients and was expecting something like that from the toppings.  But there was some flavor on the pizza that I just can't identify, tasting familiar, but unexpected in a pi.  (I never have figured out what spice or herb it was, but guess it might be something in their house sauce.  I dunno!)  So, the flavor was fine, but wasn't necessarily my favorite combination.  I hope that makes sense.  They offer different sauces on different combinations on their menu, so maybe it was just this one combo that befuddled me.    Anyway, the service was fast and friendly and I had no trouble time wise fitting the meal into a lunch hour (if I had a lunch hour anymore! ha!  Gotta love retirement!)  This is a place I would gladly suggest to someone who wants to eat pizza without worrying about feeling guilty over carbs and calories.  Nice place, nice people, and nice food.    Review #1300

My day of exploring Broad Ripple continued with another great find:  Upland Brewing's new expanded Tasting Room.  After grabbing some convenient parking in a lot across 49th, I entered the dining area, but decided to head into the bar area since I wanted to sample some of the sour beers that Upland has become known for.  After sampling a few of their options, the bartender Carson suggested one called "Petal to the Kettle" (6% 5 IBU) based upon what I had tried.  That was the winner!  I settled in with a pint and enjoyed the mildly tart ale with hibiscus, rose petal, and strawberry puree.  Very refreshing!  I could see sipping this one pool side (if I still had a pool!)  They do offer meal options and the dining room appears to be open to all ages, though I think the back area may still be an adults only section.   The only request I have is that when they offer flights (6 for $7), that they would have a sours option...I don't mind if you have a different price.  I just don't live close enough to visit Upland that often (halfway between Bloomington and Broad Ripple makes for a drive either way.)  I look forward to returning!  Review #2103

If you are looking for a variety of options for breakfast/brunch, stop in at this location of this family owned and operated restaurant.  I ordered the Eggs Benedict with a side of hash browns and found them to be quite good.  The coffee was also good; not too bitter, not too hot.  The only place they could do a bit better is on the service.  Although there is no sign about waiting, there isn't a sign saying to seat yourself either.  So, I waited even though one of the cleanup staff saw me without thinking to mention it to the the wait staff who were back by the kitchen counter.  Eventually, someone in the back saw me and mentioned it.  Once I was seated, I had pretty good service though my waitress wasn't the most efficient I've had.  With a little more awareness (keeping coffee filled, watching the front), the service could be really good.  Review #3617

My first visit to a Tiki Bar won't be my last!  I had been looking forward to the opening of the Inferno Room (I like trying new places) and went in the late afternoon on Wednesday.  I got there early enough to grab one of the spaces in the lot behind the restaurant.  There is some free street parking along Virginia also.  From the moment I walked in the door, I had a feeling I was a. going back in time, and b. to another place!  Bamboo, carvings, plants, and music all work together to create a feel for being at a bar in the South Pacific.  The lighting is low and in the afternoons, the entire second story rooms (Kahuna and Luau) are bathed in red light as the sunlight streams through red glass.  Everything is red.  It's really mind bending.  Upon entering, I was welcomed by the host and told a bit about the bar.  I asked and was told I could roam through both floors of the place before grabbing a seat at the bar.  There are authentic pieces imported specifically for the bar and those that are not, were commissioned by an artist to create them.  No trashy pseudo pieces here.  You can feel the vibe immediately.  The bar is filled with skulls and carvings and palm fronds.  The staff is friendly and glad to talk about the concept behind the theme.  The menu is based upon foods that are available in the South Pacific but with a bar twist.  There is an assortment of kabobs and sliders, and other finger foods.  This isn't a place to eat salads....sorry, not available.  In fact, there aren't many veggies available in traditional form (Yam kabobs!)  But you don't have to go hungry.  There are lots of drink options and plenty of small plates to choose from.  I ordered a Crab Rangoon which is made with REAL crab meat.  Deep fried and filled with crab, cream cheese, and seasoned with tarragon, they come with a tasty dipping sauce (I got 4 in my serving.)  Very good!  I moved to the Pork Kabobs, which were three skewers of bite sized pieces and seasoned with a sweet soy sauce and sesame seeds and served with marinated cucumber slices.  Good flavor though one of the skewers was a bit more done than the other two, which made it a bit tough.  But otherwise, a yummy flavor profile with a variety of flavors.  I talked myself into trying the Jerk Chicken sliders as well.  Two small sandwiches of spiced and juicy chicken between two pillowy buns that had a texture very similar to steamed buns.  (I was told that the chef at Rook worked on the menu here.)  The flavor was good, but note that the buns mute the spicy taste a bit, so you may want to do the Kabobs instead for full spiciness.  For dessert, I went with a Chocolate Huapia Pie which is served in a glass and has a custard like texture.  Chocolate flavor on the bottom and topped with crushed Macadamia nuts = Yum!  Just get this!  And if you are still reading this, you've got to try some cocktails.  I had my first Singapore Sling which is a floral covered rum drink that was great.  I also noticed they have a couple slushy machines.  I asked and was told one of those (not listed on the bar menu) is called the Missionary's Downfall.  Less complex in flavors, but a refreshing way to end an evening (like dessert with booze!)  You won't find a list of ingredients to the beverages here.  It's part of the Tiki culture to not worry about that sort of thing....just trust the bartender and hope for the best....like finding yourself stranded 50 years ago in the South Pacific and surrounded by new friends a few bar stools down.  It's an experience as much as a meal and drinks.  Just be careful that the cost will creep up on you if you keep ordering.  But it was worth it!  Review #1327

While my traveling companions stood in long line at that "coffee chain", I walked over to Shapiro's and grabbed a bacon, egg, and cheese bagel and a cup of coffee.  The sandwich was made to order except for the bagels which were offered in a variety of flavors.  I finished my yummy breakfast just as my companions were getting their frothy beverages.  I think my choice suited me better for a day of travel than theirs.    They are on the pricey side being located at the airport but I got that impression from all the businesses.  The only negative I had was that I was going to get the sausage instead of the bacon but they were out at 7:30 in the morning.  You can't let that happen at a breakfast place.  Review #2353

Maybe because they have only been open a week or so, I won't rate this one quite as high as some of the Arni's I have been to.  It was clean and the food was okay, but for our Friday lunch, the wait to be seated was a half hour and growing while we waited.  They take your phone number so they can text you when a table is ready, I assume they want you to wait in your car, but we decided to wait with our masks on to keep in touch with how long the wait was going to take and that nobody was getting seated before us.  Right around the estimated time, they just told us since we were near the entrance not far from the host desk.  Everyone was in masks, so though it got crowded when more people entered, many walked out due to the long wait.  Most folks have to get back to work, so half hour waits will have to be improved on.  My wife asked and didn't get a satisfactory answer why they were so backed up.  I asked if we could at least have a menu to look at while we waited so that we could place our order right away.  That was helpful.  One thing I didn't anticipate being a surprise was that the beverages didn't list prices, so that when my two granddaughters and I ordered milk shakes with our meals, that was $18 for the 3 drinks!    Even though we weren't seated by the front door, it was quite drafty and my wife and one granddaughter didn't wear their jackets and were cold for most of the meal.  The noise level wasn't bad for as crowded as they were.  We could carry on a conversation easily.  Our food came out fairly quickly, but the waitress forgot to ask if we wanted water in addition to our milkshakes which took a lot longer since she had to get someone to help her make them.  Water would have been nice.    The food was plentiful which I usually don't mind, but lunch sized portions would have been nice to offer on my wife's Southern Fried Chicken Salad with Honey Mustard dressing.  Good taste, just way too much.  Our granddaughters aren't so little anymore, so they ordered a cheeseburger and the other a hamburger.  The tater tots were definitely preferred.  More crisp than the fries.    I ordered the Breaded Tenderloin which was thick, but a little dry.  It was almost too tall for my big mouth to take in.  They only had a dill spear, not dill slices on the sandwich and the mustard was in packets.   I also got the side of Brussels Sprouts for $1 upgrade over the fries offered with the sandwich.  They had a good, but not readily identifiable flavor, but were a bit undercooked which made them chewy.  I like mine grilled until the outer leaves turn crisp and maybe a little blackened.  This was just a jaw workout.  Probably won't order those again.  The  service the rest of the time was good and the wait time for our food and upon request, the bill, was minimal.  Hopefully, the restaurant will iron out the delays and fine tune the portion sizes and cook times.  I think I will wait a bit before heading back, but it was good enough that I don't regret going.  Review #3895

I don't go out for pizza very often, but when I do, I will look for a nearby Greek's!  This Hoosier chain is consistently good and the Greenwood franchise was just as great of an experience as I've had at the others.  From being greeted at the door, to the pleasant conversation with the bartender about soccer and craft beer, to the excellent salad and pizza, everything was enjoyable.  The location doesn't allow for much foot traffic, so the hours are mostly evening except for on the weekends.  But that also is good for customers since it wasn't as crowded as some pizza places I've been.  I was able to find parking in the lot outside the front of the restaurant and was the only one seated in the bar area.  Note that I had plenty of leg room at the bar too.  Didn't bang my knees or have to sit awkwardly to reach my food.  I didn't realize they had flights of beer, and though I only tried one of our state's offerings, all that I tried were really good.    I started with a simple side salad which looked like an homage to Italy with red tomatoes, white shredded cheese, and green shaved bell peppers across the top.  Very fresh and delicious with my choice (balsamic vinaigrette) of dressing.  And not soon after I finished the salad, the small Gourmet House Pizza (6  small wedge shaped, thin crust slices) arrived.  The house Italian sauce (somewhat sweet to me), onions, blended cheeses, mini meatballs, sliced black olives and Feta cheese made for a tasty combo.  No folding required to pick this one up.  Note that it was steaming hot when it came out, so I took a few more sips of beer before eating to avoid that dreaded roof of mouth burn.    Great beer and food, pleasant sports bar atmosphere, nice open dining area, and friendly service made for a much better experience than I had anticipated.  Give them a try!  Review #2727

Due to a change in my circumstances, I've found opportunity to be out and about even during the pandemic and have made it a point to swing by Between the Bun on the Southside (SR37 & Southport roads).  I simply phone in my carryout order and by the time I get there, my order is usually bagged and ready once I pay.  My wife is my transportation provider, so I had to do a bit of convincing her since she doesn't normally need a BMB (Big Mouth Burger) that weighs in around a half pound for lunch.  But Between the Bun is not only a great place to try some delicious and creative (no ruts here!) flavor combinations for burgers, they also have award winning hot dogs...and the big dogs are deep fried for a little bit of crunch factor.  (Try the Windy City Dogs!)  Look, you can make a nice burger at home and put on your "usual" toppings.  Why pay more for something you can get at home?  But the folks behind Between the Bun think outside the box and I can't tell you how many different flavor combinations that I've really enjoyed here.  You get a lot of food and even more flavor when you are willing to break out of your rut and try something.  They have regular and spicy fries too!  My latest "go to" burger is the PBJ burger.  Yes, the PB is peanut butter spread over the top of the massive burger.  But the J is for jalapeno slices that add that extra layer of depth to the flavor profile.  And to temper the heat from the jalapenos, they add a maple syrup, bacon, and pepper jack cheese.  There is so much flavor that your mouth has a party whether you want it to or not!  It's no wonder this place does so well in burger competitions and comes home with so many awards.  If you are a dull and boring person, you may complain that it's expensive for a regular burger.  But if you are someone who appreciates flavor and treats yourself to something nice when you have the chance to go out to eat, swing by BTB for one of the tasty burgers, a hot dog, or do like me, and get one of each.  I'm usually so full by the time I finish I don't even need dinner!  Pleasant staff, plenty of outdoor seating and parking, and they are starting to open up to socially distanced inside dining as well.  Once they get back to normal, they will be offering local music too.  Lots of craft beers available here too.  Revised #53

For point of reference, I am not a Vegan or Vegetarian, and really don't plan on becoming one.  But I am open minded when it comes to food and I decided to give this place a try.  As I looked over the colorful menu board mounted over the counter to the kitchen, I struggled to find anything that appealed to me.  However, the Nacho Mama Bean Bowl seemed like something that would be both tasty and satisfying.  Good news....I liked it!  It was served with pinto beans over greens, plenty of quinoa (done to the right level of chew), some sprouts, avocado slices, fermented veggies for a bit of acidity, pumpkin seeds, and topped with a cashew nacho cheese.  The serving was large enough and the beans and quinoa were filling enough to be satisfying.  The flavors blended quite well and I would recommend this to anyone who, like me, is new to this type of cuisine.  I will also commend the young man running the order counter.  He was very polite and helpful and even brought my food out to me when he saw me take a seat along the order counter.  Normally, you have to gather your own napkins and utensils if you are a 'dine in' guest, then bus your own place setting when finished.    On the negative, the space is quite small for those wishing to stay and due to the frequent use of a blender for making smoothies, the room gets quite loud (especially as you get closer to the kitchen).  There is a covered patio that adds a bit more seating and distance, but that only helps to a degree.  Because this is Broad Ripple, you can hope for a bit of luck finding parking.  There is a small parking lot next to the restaurant for just a few cars, but your best bet is to prowl the streets of BR.  (Note that Ferguson is one way southbound.)  So, this was a generally positive experience and meal.  I'm not sure how often they change the menu.  Right now, I would have to say that Three Carrots downtown has more appeal to me than Ezra's.  But both served high quality food and what I've tasted in both places was fine.    Review #2430

Hidden away on country back roads in southeastern Hendricks County is a fairly new nature park that is very accommodating to visitors.  The park, located to the south of the Indianapolis Airport expansion was created to provide a habitat for the endangered Indiana (mouse eared) bat (Myotis sodalis) whose previous habitat was displaced by the airport and Ameriplex expansion.  The park is filled with new growth plantings of native Hoosier trees like ash, elm, persimmon, walnut and others.  There is also an old growth section, a pond, and wetland areas.      At the park entrance, there is plenty of parking and restrooms where a kiosk of park brochures can be found.  The brochure is filled with information including a map showing the five trails (including distances) within the nature preserve.  The trails are located on the south side of the pond and have markers at each intersection which help the visitor to identify where they are on the map.      On my visit, I started with the longest trail, Oak Trace which extends 1.2 miles to the far side of the preserve.  The trail is mostly a grassy trail, but does have a few leaf covered stretches which can be a little muddy.  The trail is fairly level, so it is an easy hike.  Along the way, you may check out display panels that contain information about the wildlife living in the preserve.    At the trails end on the west side of the park, you have the choice of returning the way you came or heading through the woods on Bat Haven Trail (0.7 miles).  This trail is less expansive and winds through the trees as a leaf covered path.  On my visit, the leaves were slick from a recent rain and I would suggest a walking stick and boots that you aren't afraid to get muddy (I maintained my balance but slipped a few times and got mud on my shoes and pant legs.)  The Bat Haven trail does have some elevation changes, but none are too drastic.  There were a few fallen trees that I needed to step over.    As Bat Haven ends, the Beaver Ridge trail (0.6 miles total) offers a north or south path that loops around the eastern woodlands area.  I chose the north side of the path which offers a view of the pond area before reuniting and leading back to the early part of Oak Trace trail so that I could return to my vehicle.    For folks who want to enjoy views of the pond, to fish, or picnic, a paved path exists to walk along the north side of the pond.  There is a single shelter, but are numerous picnic tables, many with grills, that are set on round concrete slabs so that the footing is level and dry, not trampled.  More information panels are located around the picnic area.    My only caution is that since the preserve is meant to provide a safe haven for animals, there are no facilities/equipment along the trails other than an occasional park bench.  You will need to pack your own water and will need to carry any disposable trash with you back to the entrance.    The preserve is a place where you can get in touch with nature to the level of your own choosing.  Since it's only fifteen minutes from my home, I am sure to be back again soon!  Review #550

I recently went to the "Festival of Trees" at the IHS with my wife and friends.  Since we chose a Tuesday evening, there was a choir (Encore Vocal Arts) singing Christmas music while we strolled through the collection of 72 Christmas trees.  Each of the trees had a unique theme.  Some were devoted to a particular state university, while others were from state businesses or charitable organizations.  The rest of the building also had some holiday decor as well.      The trees are located on the canal level, the first and second floors, and on the fourth floor which is only accessible via the elevator.  So, there was some delay waiting for the single elevator to transport people to and from the different levels.      Although we didn't take time to explore the interactive exhibits with live period characters, we did stroll into the Cole Porter Room which also had live entertainment performing during the time the carolers were taking breaks.  It looked like a cabaret from the Waldorf-Astoria.  Not sure if they serve beverages in this barroom setting.    There is also a cafe on the canal level that is open during the day (10 to 4) and concerts on the canal during the summer.     One of my favorite things about the IHS is that they have an immense archive of historical photographs that you can view from your home computer.  As someone who worked downtown over 30 years ago and witnessed the amazing transformation, I really enjoy seeing images from a time before urban blight had brought the downtown to its lowest point.  (So glad it is finding a resurgence!)      If you have any interest in history and enjoy interaction, this is the place for you.  If you are someone who simply likes to look at pieces and read about them, then you will probably want to wander over to the State Museum a block away.  Review #206

Although a lot of people use the park for the baseball and soccer fields, the park is located next to a horse ranch that allows horse riders to use the park just like the hikers and bikers do.  There are some different trails for the bikes and horses, but they do overlap in the easiest trails, so everyone just has to share those spaces.  As far as hiking goes, the blue trails are supposed to be the easiest.  However, there are a few stretches that the markers indicate blue that have some pretty sharp changes in elevation, so my advice on first visits is to take it slow and steady until you get familiar with the park.  I read that the elevation changes roughly 80 feet on the trails so the green trails are rated as moderate.  I personally like that I can get a good workout without having to head to one of the southern state parks.  My only negative is that there are still quite a few intersections of trails that don't have markers, so you have to assume you proceed straight ahead.  On my first visit, I couldn't find a marker for the green trails and got sidetracked to a blue trail which went an extra mile before returning to the starting place.  I didn't mind the workout, but it would have been beneficial to help me plan my visit.  If the parks department would simplify their maps with basic loops and place color coded markers for each loop at the intersections, I think this would make navigation easier.  As it is now, the map at the kiosk shows all the possible paths and it is simply confusing.  (Particularly the challenging section coded the same color as the easy made me question their system!)  Now that I've been there, I have a better sense of the park and look forward to returning when the foliage is back.    Review #713

Just a few blocks south of the fountain on Shelby Street, another Mexican Restaurant (this one with parking access from the alley east of Shelby, on the site of the former B's Po-Boy.  Like its predecessor, there is still plenty of outside seating and still the fun games to play like bocce and large jenga. Much of the patio is covered for shade and inside, there were plenty of tables as well as bar side seating.   A friend and I decided to give this place a try and we really appreciated that they had actual menus to read  their lengthy list of options.  We were greeted promptly and the only service issue was that I ordered a side of hot shelled corn that didn't arrive until asked for.  My friend ordered a trio of tacos which he liked.  I ordered a steak Burrito which was huge though I managed to devour it in one sitting along with the corn, rice and pico.  Very good sides but the steak itself was under seasoned.  Just a bit bland.  Decent portion sizes for the prices. We were brought out salsa and chips, but they only offer one heat of salsa, so if you want it hotter, you have to add hot sauce to your dipping bowl.  We each got our own salsa, so I didn't mind the milder stuff.  Once my friend added the hot sauce, he was satisfied.  Check out was handled well and no problems.  Everyone was pleasant on the staff which made us feel welcome. I know there are lots of Mexican  restaurants to choose from in the area, but if you like the bonus of nice outdoor seating and games while you wait, consider stopping by Fountain Burrito for someplace new.  #3923

If you like a restaurant that has well prepared food, a nice atmosphere, and good service, then give Capri a try.    I stopped in for lunch and although the outside is looking a little weathered, once I stepped inside I realized that this was a place that had style!  The dining area that includes the bar is decked out with numerous photos of famous actors and musicians.  The background music was very pleasant and having white linen on the tables added to the feeling that this place knew how to entertain.  A basket of two bread rolls was served steaming hot.  The huge slab of butter was a bit cold and made me glad the bread was especially hot so that the butter melted quickly. For my meal, I went with the soup of the day:  Cream of Asparagus.  To this, the waiter added grated cheese and ground black pepper.  The flavor highlighted the asparagus flavor, but I couldn't help but wish there would have been some small pieces of asparagus within.    For my entree, I ordered the Fettuccine with Meatballs (Veal) in a Red Wine Tomato sauce.  Again, the flavor was very good.  And this is where I struggle...the flavor is what you would expect from a nice Italian restaurant, but there was no "wow" moment.  No twist.  No surprise.  Just fine tasting food.  Frankly, other than being served, I cannot say that there was anything that different from the same dish I prepare at home.    So, I don't have any negatives about my dining experience.  If you are someone who knows what you like and that includes traditional Italian dining, then give Capri a try.  Review #185

I really like browsing through Williams-Sonoma.  The store is arranged into groupings of food and kitchen related items.  I can't help myself from picking up a utensil that I've never seen before or some food item "starter" or additive.  In fact, if they weren't charging mall prices on everything, I would probably buy more gadgets.  Over the years, I have picked up a number of items and they all seemed to have high quality.    On my most recent visit, they had samples of barbecue sauces with some freshly cooked meatballs for dipping.  End result?  I ended up buying a sauce that I had never heard of before and probably wouldn't be able to find anywhere else.  (I ended up making dinner that night with the sauce as a key ingredient.) And that's the point.  Williams-Sonoma is a place to find quality products that can either make your home food preparation more simple or add to the flavor profile.  Fight the routine!  Try something new.  Stop in at W-S for a change!  Review #332

If you are looking for a unique experience in coffee houses, then give this place a try.  There are lots of restaurants/patios that are pet friendly, i.e. bring your dog.  But here is a place you can grab a cup of coffee (lots of options with cat names available here!) and either watch the cats through the big windows or, if you make reservations, can sit with and play with the cats for a small fee.  Funds from the visitations go to taking care of the felines.    I wasn't shopping for a new addition to our household (adoptions are available from the "showroom" for cats!), but thought I would like to see what the place was like.  Since it was cool and drizzling, I decided to try their Hot Chocolate made with dark chocolate for a rich, deep flavor.  What was nice was that this didn't have the normal bitterness you get from straight dark chocolate, so it was very smooth tasting.  I especially liked that it wasn't served scalding hot.  I hate burning my tongue on the first sip or having to wait ten minutes for it to cool down like some places.  They also have pastries if you have the munchies, but since I had just eaten, I passed, though I will admit they looked really good!  The cats were rather inactive while I was there, but from the looks of the room, there was lots for them to do and to climb with many elevated nesting places.  If I was a cat, this would be a cool place to hang out!  Review #407

As several of he AMP's businesses struggle to find employees, so that they can be open during their posted hours, I was pleasantly surprised to find this newer business open on the  back wall  along the west end (to the left).  The restaurant specializes in burgers and "bites(sides)" with a number of chef designed combos or options that allow you to dress your burger made to order (within reason.  The wait was short and the sandwich warm.  I chose the Bottom dollar burger that came with sauteed onions and cheese.  Really tasty!  I chose the fries which appeared and tasted to be made from Yukon Gold potatoes.  Excellent flavor, but just a little soggy by the time I ate them. The special came with a soda but the soda  is self served.  At the counter they give you a cup and straw, but you have to walk to the dispenser located at the far end of the AMP along the east wall.  Seems inefficient since you have to return all the way back to the shop to pick up your meal order. If you want your order bagged for carryout, be sure to mention it and ask for any utensils you might need for your sides.  Reasonably priced and moderate wait. Review #3964

I don't drive by this part of Greenwood very often, but when I happened to notice this charming business on the north end of what is becoming a restaurant road, I made plans to check them out.  So glad I did!    The restaurant only has lunch service for customers to drop by, but if you are interested in experiencing a "High Tea", reservations can be made.  High Tea starts at 2:30 p.m.  I forgot to ask about minimums/maximums of parties, but they do have two levels of "teas", including tea, scones, sandwiches, and treats.      This place is a beautifully decorated house that has the front area converted to the dining area, the middle of the house is the gift shop and lobby, and the back of the house is used for the kitchen.  They have parking in the rear of the house and a long, low rise ramp for anyone needing it to reach the entry porch.    Once inside, I was given a table by the fireplace.  The room is laid out with water goblets, flowers in tea cups on every table, and silver chargers at each place setting.  I was initially concerned that I was under dressed for the lunch, but even though it looks classy, casual is welcome.  Whew!  In fact, the whole experience made me feel like a guest in someone's home.  Very personable and no pretentious behavior.    I started off with one of the house teas.  I went with a Cinnamon Orange Spice that had a wonderful aroma.  A china tea pot of hot water was brought out so that I could refill my cup as needed.  Very tasty!    When my waitress mentioned that they had LS Ayres Chicken Velvet Soup, I said "Yes, Please!" and it was brought out almost immediately.  Wow!  I forgot how good this soup is.  The creamy, yes velvety, consistency of the soup with diced chicken and lightly topped with herbs was so good!  It is served quite hot, so be aware before your first spoonful.    I also ordered the Sassafras Club Panini which comes with a side salad and a small scone.  The Panini was generously stuffed with ham, turkey, provolone, spinach, bacon, and basil mayo.  The ham was thin sliced but retained the cured ham taste with just enough salt.  The flavors worked well.  The salad, mostly field greens, was topped with Raspberry Vinaigrette that was excellent!  And the scone, though smaller than most I have had, was a moist blueberry with whole blueberries inside.  It was one of the best I have had!    I was filling up, so I passed on the desserts, but I plan on returning soon to give more items a try.  They have a limited number of options, but they do have sandwiches, soups, quiche, salads, and desserts.      If you are near downtown Greenwood (Madison and Main area), why not break from your routine and give this place a try.  It is filled with charm and a bit of nostalgia, and lots of great food!  Review #330

Our friends asked us to try Cooper's Hawk for the Devour Northside on a Saturday evening.  Thankfully, we had reservations and were able to walk passed the overflow crowd in the lobby/wine tasting area that spilled out onto the sidewalk.  Note:  Weekends and promotional events cause lines....if you don't make reservations, blame yourself, not the restaurant!  The restaurant seemed much larger inside.  The lighting was dim which may be romantic, but I need at least enough light to read the menu and to see what I am eating.    I had reviewed the menu online so I had a good idea what I wanted to try.  I decided to order from the menu and skip the Devour promotion.  I went with the Brie & Fruit Bruschetta (excellent flavor...just wish I hadn't offered any to my friends to share!).  For my entree, I selected the Pistachio Crusted Grouper.  This was a fantastic choice as well.  The food appealed to all of our group.    The only downside to the evening was the waiter seemed distracted.  He would disappear from our area for long periods of time.  We initially thought it was that he was busy, but then we noticed him standing around talking with other waiters and not even looking in our direction so that we could get his attention.  I don't understand why it took so long to get the bill after we have had our dessert or said there would be nothing else. It seems like they would want to help us finish so another guest could be seated.  I do plan on returning for the food and wine and hope that it was just an off night for service.  Review #51

Unlike most big box hardware stores, this True Value is part of an existing building.  The good news is that it is convenient for downtown residents and visitors who need to find something that they just don't find elsewhere.  The bad news is that they are limited in space, so the aisles are narrower and the stacks of inventory aren't as high.   This place does have a paint department as well as most of the items you would shop for at a hardware store.  I was looking for a smaller watering can than the one I have.  I was able to find them in three sizes at reasonable prices, so I gladly made my purchase.  Another benefit of having a smaller store is that if you have any questions, it isn't hard to find someone to help.  I was directed to the specific aisles right after being greeted when I entered.
