If you like having service as well as supplies, then consider stopping here when downtown.  Review #3755

By now, many of my fellow Yelpers have heard about my recent battle with brain cancer.  I had no idea that I had a fist sized tumor in my right temple until I had a massive seizure that caused me to throw myself to the flow, striking my side table next to my bed so hard with my jaw that I broke the legs off!  I don't remember any of that but remember waking in the hospital with a breathing tube in my mouth and feeling somewhat confused.  Within a few days my surgery was scheduled and they successfully removed a small high grade tumor as well as the massive low grade tumor.  I spent nearly a week in the hospital and must say that everyone I came into contact with was friendly and caring and encouraging, so I felt the care I received throughout my stay (and my recent follow up visits) has been excellent.  Even the food from the cafeteria was pretty good.  Not high cuisine, but palatable and with enough diversity that I felt like I had decent choices for each meal.  In fact, my only complaint is that they could boost their WIFI since over the course of the week, there wasn't much I could do other than take naps.  Streaming on my phone was not very successful.  But honestly, I probably needed the naps to recover from the huge surgery (42 staples needed) more than I needed to watch some episode of a tv show.  I feel like the staff was so upbeat and supportive including helping my wife and I find our way around the hospital.  If anything, they may have given too much information upfront since I am not well versed in medical and medicinal terminology.  Fortunately, my wife takes great notes and was able to coordinate all my follow-up appointments for me and to fill my pill box so that I took the right pills at the right frequency.  When I met with the surgeon and oncologist, I felt they explained things in terms I could understand and they prepared me for the upcoming challenge of the multi cycle treatment plan which starts next week.  I understand what each phase is supposed to provide and with so many ways of attacking my disease, I am confident that I will one day be back to my independent self.  It won't be easy, but I felt each doctor and nurse I dealt with cared about me and did their best to make sure I knew they were in this fight with me.  On my follow up visit where I was fitted with a radiation mask, I met a completely different set of staff and each of them was equally helpful whether it was on getting registered, or someone escorting us to the right department for our appointments.  Just wonderful people who are doing their best to help the patients in their care.  What more can a patient ask for?  I am thankful for the good folks at Methodist who literally saved my life.  And despite having an initial prognosis of only having 15 months if I don't continue with treatments, their support and plan gives me hope that I will one day be back to writing more reviews as I explore our state, one county at a time.  Methodist is a great place and benefits with its connection to the greater IU Health organization including the Goodman Hall Neuroscience center across the street.  Thank you to all the staff who took care of me.  Review #3760

With so many Mexican restaurants to choose from, this place needs to step up its game to make it a destination for anyone other than a local.  It is set back in a shopping center which is easy to miss if you are traveling at speed north on Emerson Avenue just inside I-465.  We drove by, but turned east on Churchman and drove back through the shopping center to the restaurant.  My wife's fist comment was that the parking lot was trashy and needed a good sweeping near the restaurant entrance.  Once inside, The initial appearance was better maybe because of all the festive colors.  (Not too loud either.)  But the flooring and the blinds on the windows looked like they could use some repair/deep cleaning too.  The restrooms didn't have a light switch so it took a moment to figure out it must use a motion sensor to turn on the lighting.  I found this uncomfortable until the light finally came on, I didn't close the door behind me.   We were seated at a bench, but because my wife felt she was so far away from the table, we were able to move to a different table.  Our order was taken promptly, but there were some miscues.  My wife ordered a beef Quesadilla, but it arrived as chicken.  This after the waiter had already checked back once to be sure of the meat.  She also ordered a strawberry margarita and there was a miscommunication.  She likes them frozen, but I think she might have said icy.  The liquid had a few ice cubes floating in it and was otherwise just not that appetizing in appearance.  I ordered the lunch burrito beef which was ground beef and sides of really smooth beans and rice, but no pico de galo or sour cream on top.  Okay flavor, but just so so.  Having had a similar meal elsewhere last week, this was a distant second in both flavor and texture.  Forgettable.  The meal was okay at best and filling.  If we hadn't been in the area, I don't think we would have ordered here.  Review #3926

I recently enjoyed a return visit to the State Museum featuring a state bicentennial salute "Indiana in 200 objects".  Sadly, the exhibit is only temporary, but in the time I spent wandering through, I couldn't help but wonder why the pieces selected were chosen over countless other items.  There were six general categories for the pieces representing 200 years.  Some of the pieces were clearly historical items with strong Indiana ties, while others were somewhat obscure, making me wonder why someone pushed the committee to chose that particular piece.  Either way, I still learned things that were outside of my normal education and media based information.    In previous visits, I randomly wandered, looking for items of interest....natural history with bones of beasts; old cars that were unique, not looking like every other vehicle on the road; and artwork by local talent.  Those items are still here and I enjoy relearning about them.    However, some of the permanent exhibits could use a little re-imagining.  The "Birth of Earth" and "The Native Americans" galleries on the canal level are two that come to mind.  I understand that the Eiteljorg is next door, but the quality of actual Native American artifacts is slim.  The Birth of Earth was a spacious dark exhibit where there wasn't much to do other than touch big pieces of rock.  Maybe the galleries could switch exhibits and improve both.    One of the positives about the museum is that it is always bringing in new exhibits on the third floor to offer something new to the visitor.  So, you may sometimes visit when an exhibit gallery is off limits due to the setup time required.  (Such was the case upon my visit in early January.)  Fortunately, there is a solid website that tells how long current exhibits are running as well as some of the upcoming exhibitions so that you can plan more effectively.    Another positive is the location.  The grounds and museum are beautifully located along the canal.  Outside, you can find an artistic interpretation of each of Indiana's 92 counties with a mini-narrative about what each art piece represents.  (Note:  Some of the plaques are missing and hopefully, the museum will replace those soon.)  There is also the famed Steam Clock that plays music periodically throughout the day.      If you visit during the warmer months, be sure to take in lunch at the Farmer's Market Cafe.  Outdoor seating is available so that you can overlook the canal and people watch.    Access to each floor is available via elevators for those who have difficulty climbing, but additional stairways are available on the east end as well centrally located.       Overall, the museum can be an entertaining way to spend an afternoon.  If time allows, you can stop by the NCAA Hall of Champions, the Eiteljorg Museum, or wander along the canal and the Washington Street bridge to see the public art collection.  p.s.  The drive up to the front entrance has nineteen circles on the sidewalk arranged in order of statehood, ending with Indiana at the front door.  Each circle has the shape of the state and a corresponding number of stars for each position.  Review #208

The nature park has been shaped as roughly an oval that extends from the parking area east to Eagle Creek, then follows along the creek to the west before returning.  Inside the oval, it is densely wooded yet the oval is narrow enough that can still sense, if not see, the other side of the trail.  On the south and east side of the oval is Eagle Creek and there are many places you can stop to watch the water flow or if you are interested, to go off path to get a closer look.  On the north side of the trail, there are picnic tables for anyone wanting to rest or dine in the park.  There is a small patch of woods between the trail and the busy street, but the entire north walk includes the sounds of traffic.  So, I applaud that anyone who wants to reach the creek in a hurry can take the direct path on a paved trail, but it loses some of the "feel" of nature with all the traffic noises.    I would also like to see more information about the park on site.  A trail map (with distance) would be helpful.  The oval also connects on the northeast end with another trail which shares the creekside and continues to the southwest for series runners.  I wasn't that ambitious to see where that trail leads, but it might be helpful to know where I would end up if I took one of those paths.  The park appeared in good condition, but unless you are someone who is going strictly for a short hike, there isn't much to draw you here that helps you feel like you are escaping the sounds of the city.  Review #711

I went to Broad Ripple to try "The Garden Table" for brunch on a Monday morning (6-1-16) after seeing the restaurant make the "Top 25" listing of Indpls Magazine for 2016.  Although I was tempted to sit outside on such a beautiful day, I wanted to capture the feel of the restaurant by sitting inside near the front windows.    The restaurant has a quirky feel to it, with lots of information about their food and products written on blackboards around the seating area and behind the counter.  Lots of folks appeared to have arrived before me and had set up "camp" working on their computers or meeting with friends to chat.  Nice Vibe!   The restaurant is one where you approach the central counter and place your order.  They bring out your food when it is ready.  (Meals are paid for in advance.)  I ordered some coffee to sip while I waited and was pleased to see that a local Indy small business (Tinker Street) was the supplier of the coffee.  They have a number of additives for those who like to make their coffee taste like dessert, but I like my coffee black and was pleased with the taste.  I ordered the savory "Garden Benedict". (Mashed avocado toast, topped with poached eggs and basil hollandaise.) The toast was full of nutty and seed flavors, but a bit hard to cut through with a regular table knife. The basil flavor was the dominate taste, but was mellowed by the poached egg soft yolk.  I would definitely order this again.  I also tried the Broiled Grapefruit drizzled with local honey.  This was a bit disappointing since I couldn't taste or see any signs of the honey.  The grapefruit was ripe, so it was still tasty, but didn't seem to live up to the description.  If you are ever in the village area and would like something good to eat while you people watch folks go by, then the Garden Table is worth stopping in.  Review #9

I hadn't heard of Happy Dragon (although it is a chain with several locations in the metro area), but when another restaurant was backed up with customers, I decided my time was worth more than waiting in line and headed down the strip mall to try out this Chinese restaurant.  The overall appearance was very typical of strip mall restaurants...white walls at the front with lots of pictures of food and preprinted menus available for ordering take out.  In fact, I got the impression that most of the orders were for take out.  As one of the only dine in customers, I didn't have to wait long for my lunch special.  I ordered a Chicken Chow Mein lunch with fried rice and an egg roll as my complementary sides.  The flavor was really good and the bowl was quite appetizing to look at.  I did find the fried rice to be a little flavorless but the white sauce did well to make up for it.  The egg roll was a vegetarian type and had a crisp outside.  I did find adding one of the sauces added to the flavor.  Although I usually prefer to support independent restaurants, it's nice to know that I can still get a decent meal even if there aren't any "wow" moments.  Review #726

I have been here two times for lunch and had wildly different experiences on the two occasions.  My first visit (5-12-16) was a solo venture for me.  I sat at the bar and was able to ask the bartender questions about the business and the brews available including asking them to identify the local breweries on their menus. (Which they now do!)  I ordered the triple play and was pleased with the quality of all three items:   Prarie Organic Gin Creamy Tomato Soup - Sauteed Crimini Mushrooms, Red onions, leeks, Julienned carrots , and garlic. Deglazed in Prairie Organic Gin with Tomato soup stock, topped with Sour Cream and chives.  Unlike most soups that look like they are out of a can.   Crispy Southwest Chicken Wrap - Crispy chicken fries wrapped in a tomato basil tortilla w/chipotle ranch sauce, roasted corn, roasted red peppers, red onions, Pico de Gallo, black beans, lettuce and colby jack cheese.   Chop Salad with Balsamic Vinaigrette dressing - tossed w/Mozzarella, heirloom tomoatoes, red onions, pine nuts.   No problems and good service.  Probably would give them a 4 star rating.    However, my second visit (5-20-16) had a friend meet my wife and I for lunch.  We liked the plentiful parking and that they have a small outdoor patio, but the weather was a bit cool that day.  The interior of the dining area was large and allowed plenty of room between tables.  And my friend thought the Bloody Mary was excellent!   But....that was about the end of the niceties.  I ordered a round of Porter battered jumbo onion rings, dipped and dredged in seasoned cracker crumbs and crisp fried for the table.  The onion rings were drizzled with porter beer BBQ sauce, served with jalapeno ranch dipping sauce.  The serving was pricey for an appetizer until I saw the quantity.  There were 12 rings that seemed huge as tennis balls.  The first bites were fine, especially with the BBQ sauce.  But too much of a good thing is too much.  The cracker breading sat heavily in our stomachs and some of the rings were a bit under cooked which left a pasty taste.  We only finished half of the rings and didn't even want a take home box because the crumbs were beginning to hold the cooking oil.  Nice try for something unique, but just too much.  I also ordered the stout pork belly BLT with Stout beer and kosher salt brined pork belly, seared and oven roasted, served with baby bibb lettuce, beefsteak tomatoes, and homemade apricot onion jam on grilled garlic shallot bread with garlic parmesan chips.  Again, this sounded like a delicious combination to try, but the execution was very disappointing.  The thickly slice pork belly was more like jerky.  Because it was plentiful, it was stacked one slice upon another.  As I bit into the sandwich, the pork slid across the lower layers, resisting my bite.  I have read other reviews where the pork was melt in your mouth smooth, but others have also complained about the jerky quality.  The only thing that will save this option is getting the consistent tender or lightly crisp texture.  It was so distracting and difficult to chew, that it was hard to enjoy the flavors.  My wife and guest also had some problems with the flavor combinations on their food, so we left disappointed.  I hope that the kitchen manager can get some consistency soon so that this promising concept doesn't disappoint very often.  Review #16

I stopped in this breakfast/lunch franchise located in a northwestern outbuilding of the Walmart plaza on South US 31.  It was a little challenging to find the spot since there weren't any signs on the back of the building as I approached (the sign is visible from the highway, but it faces away from the Walmart).  Once I found the restaurant, I noticed there was a lot of nearby parking.  It was my first time in one of the Metro Diners which is a chain originated in Florida.  It was bright and clean and had plenty of seating.  It is a full service restaurant, so I was greeted at the entrance and taken to a seat near the back.  My waitress did a fine job when I told her I was under a time constraint and she assured me that I should have no trouble dining in the amount of time.  When she brought my coffee, she took my order and within 10 minutes, I had my meal.  I opted for the Crab Cake Benedict which came with two poached eggs topped with a creamy Hollandaise nestled atop the crab and English muffin halves.  The flavor was fresh and about what I expected.  No creative flourish to set it apart.  It came with a large serving of hash browns that were crispy on the outside and tender in the middle.  During the meal, I was offered a refill and even a cup of coffee to go.  My check was brought out and the waitress explained that she thought that since I was in a hurry, that she would make it available, but that I could take as long as I liked.  I gave her my payment just to expedite the time and was finished with my whole meal, from entrance to exit, in twenty minutes!  I thanked the waitress for taking care of me as I finished my meal.  Overall, it was good service and good food at a reasonable price.  I don't go out for breakfast often, but when I do, I appreciate that they offer something that I don't routinely make at home.  Review #367

The restaurant had a cool vibe while giving a warm reception to us on our late lunch visit on Wednesday.  We found some street parking on College and were offered our choice of a seat near the entrance or back in the bar area.  We opted for the back and were promptly met by the bartender.  Although they have a variety of coffee drinks and exotic teas, my wife would have liked a simple soda which wasn't on the menu.      Instead of a standard lunch menu, there is a brunch menu with some tasty options.  My wife opted for the Croquetta, a crab cake with two shrimp, two poached eggs, an herb salad with chipotle Hollandaise, and potatoes La Luz.  I selected the Bisteca which is a blackened petite filet with bacon and all the same sides from the eggs to the potatoes.      Although the steak came well done and didn't come with a steak knife, I found the flavor to be really delicious.  The eggs had warm flowing yolks that pared well with the steak and bacon.  The potatoes La Luz were really good:  cubed potatoes with red bell pepper and onion strips, cherry tomatoes, and seasoning.  All these came with a variety of herbs leaves which I enjoyed.  There was a bit of licorice like flavor which was a little odd, but not enough to ruin the effect.  (My wife would disagree as she passed on eating the greens.)    The crab cake and shrimp meal also tasted good, but the portion size of the crab was a little sparse.  She also liked the potato mix.  Her comment that it would be nice to have a slice of bread or a roll to gather the remaining egg yolk left on the plate is a great suggestion.  Who likes leaving that much flavor on the plate?       Overall, our service was prompt and friendly.  Our wait was short and we were in and out in less than 45 minutes.  I don't know if they rotate the menu seasonnally, but they offer a different dinner menu as well as an assortment of baked goods to give you options.    Review #200

On the south wall of the Central Ace Hardware building, local artist Carl Leck has created a giant mural (2012) that ties directly to the hardware store.  The wall features a giant screw and screwdriver that are painted with 3D shading to make them look real.  Behind them, the background has vertical shades of gray with white silhouettes of other hardware items routinely found inside the store.  This is one of Leck's earliest public art murals.  He has done both commercial and independently themed pieces around town, including several for the "46 for XLVI" Superbowl project downtown.  Review #1344

I drove to Broad Ripple and parked across the street from Public Greens for lunch today (6-16-16).  Because of some advice from other Yelpers, I looked over the menu on the Public Garden's website to see what items I might like to try.   NOTE:  The menu changes monthly now, not weekly.  Upon entering, I saw a few people who were waiting in front of the display, but not standing by the counter.  So, I headed on by them and was greeted and asked if I needed any help deciding.    Since I knew what I wanted to order, I told them I would like one of the Large Plate items, the "BBQ Grilled Walleye" with KC Style BBQ, Slaw, & Early Summer Chow Chow (pickled vegetables).  I also wanted to try the snack "Public Gardens" - Southern Style Braised Micro Farm Greens and Smoked Pork.  While I waited, I was able pick up a local craft brew on tap to sip while I waited.  I took my beer and a number to one of the tables outside on the patio facing the Monon trail and across from the gardens that many of the greens are gathered from.  As I sat there enjoying the great weather and people watching, the Chef came out to let me know that my fish was on the grill and that it would be out soon.  It hadn't been that long, so I was surprised that he took the time.  It was greatly appreciated.  While he was there, I asked about why the collard/mixed greens were given the "Public Greens" name, in essence becoming the namesake of the restaurant.  He said that it was one of the first dishes that the restaurant had developed and that all the leafy greens were initially grown on site.  Due to the demand for this dish, they decided to keep it on the menu (while everything else was being changed weekly).  They decided to change the dish name to Public Greens at that time.  Soon after, both dishes were brought out by the friendly staff.  The greens were perfectly cooked.  The leaves were tender, but not soggy.  The bits of stalk were cut into bite sized pieces and gave a nice crunch.  The smoked pork was shredded and balanced the other flavors.  Definitely worth ordering!  The walleye was accompanied by, what in hindsight (to me), was obviously a great pairing.  I mean, if this was a pork BBQ, it would seem natural to have some slaw and/or some pickled side.  So why not swap out the pork with a nice portion of fish?  There were two pieces of walleye, about 6 oz total. Full grill marks, a little bit of char on the outside, and moist fish inside.  The flavor combo worked!  If you aren't adventurous enough to try one of the many salads or "snacks", I highly recommend the BBQ Walleye.  Rated one of Indpls Monthly's Top 25 restaurants in 2016, this meal lived up to its billing.  Review #38

This review is based on a Saturday early afternoon visit to have lunch.  I have driven by the Blind Pig for years, but like much of downtown Greenwood, it just didn't look that welcoming.  With the new face lift that the downtown is getting, and being small business Saturday, I decided to finally stop by and see for myself.  The outside is looking great with the exception that they don't have an official sign mounted yet.  The place looks great from the outside and has all new windows that should be able to brighten it up and bring in plenty of fresh air  Previous reviews mentioned the bad smoke smell, but the place underwent a deep cleaning including the heating and cooling, so that I didn't detect any odors that were offensive.  So disregard any reviews that give negative comments about that.  The inside is still pretty simple without much investment in decor.  There is an old stage to the left of the entrance.  To the right is the section for pool tables.  Overall, the place is much larger than I had imagined based upon the prior store front.  A large bar runs from the entrance towards the back where the kitchen is.  I reviewed the menu for awhile and the bartender suggested that the pizza was their specialty.  It comes as an 8-inch cheese pizza with additional items upgrading at $.50 per item.  I went with the mushroom, pepperoni, and sausage upgrades.  What I got in return was a whopping deep dish pizza that I was able to take part of home.  Sure, I could have finished it at the bar, but half of it was plenty without stuffing myself.  Really tasty and lots of cheese.  The crispy crust on the bottom was a bit oily on the fingers, but didn't detract from the taste.  The pie held its moisture too.  Overall, pretty good pizza!  Note:  The sausage is rather mild, so if you like your pizza spicier, they do have the red pepper flakes available to take it up a notch.    So, if you are looking for someplace new to try, give the Blind Pig a try.  I'll let someone who is more into nightlife review the late hours scene.  Review #193

I like that Plainfield has created a series of parks that target different needs and has connected many of them with trails.  For visitors who want a tranquil place without the long hikes of a nature park or the bustling of little kids at a splash park/playground, Friendship Gardens has numerous benches and some gazebos to sit and enjoy the outdoors, maybe to even reflect and remember.  As you go through the park, you will see a lot of dedication plaques.  Some are by trees.  Some are by fountains.  Some are on benches.  I am not certain who determines what gets a plaque, but it is a sign that people wanted to create a place where visitors are encouraged to appreciate the beauty of the space.  There are several larger memorials.  One is to honor those who served in the military.  Another sculpture called "American Family" (Connie Scott 2003) depicts a bronze family (even a dog!) that honors "family values" and their importance in the community.  Review #615

I went with friends early on a Friday night (4-29-16) to celebrate their anniversary. I had suggested going to Marrow based upon the Top 25 rating in Indpls Monthly for 2016.  I had also read a number of good reviews, so we showed up around 5:30.      I really was hoping for a great evening of inventive and delicious food, but we got off to a strange start.  First, I thought I knew where the restaurant was, but there wasn't a sign that spelled out "Marrow".  Instead, there is a shingle with an artist's interpretation of a bone with marrow hanging over the front window.  When we went to the door which did have the name, it was locked even though the restaurant was supposed to be open for a half hour by then.  We saw customers inside and through hand gestures, figured that we were to wait.  After a few minutes, the door was unlocked without any explanation.  Very strange start indeed.    We sat about half way back in this shotgun layout restaurant.  The lighting was very dim and somewhat difficult for reading the menu when your eyes aren't as young as they used to be.  Still, Charlie our waiter was very attentive and welcoming and turned the initial impression around.  He seemed inviting and very knowledgeable of the dishes and beverages.  Now part of the problem was our own....I had read that it was best to come with friends and share the dishes.  Unfortunately, each of us wanted to try something different so we ordered way too much food!  I started with a Smoked Deviled Egg...not a whole one, just a half...and I shared it with one of my friends.  The flavor was delicious and I didn't want to fill up on appetizers...Still, I would have thought one whole egg for $3 wouldn't be asking too much.   One of my guests ordered the "Pickles" which was a play on words for five different pickled items.  Some were delicious, others were just okay to my palate.  I had read a number of reviews raving about the Shells & Paneer and the Fried Tandori Chicken and Rice Grits.  I thought the Shells were pretty good, but I rarely eat curry flavored dishes, so the cumulative effect of eating that much (probably two cups of noodles were in the bowl) even after sharing, was a bit too strong of a taste for my palate.  And quite filling too.  The Chicken was good, but the grits were not memorable....more filler.  One of my guests ordered the Hillbilly Cassoulet and she absolutely loved it.  I thought it pretty tasty too.  She also ordered the corn muffins with sorghum and miso-honey butter.  Again, that was a hit.  (She was the most satisfied with her selections of all of us and would probably give a higher rating.)  Her husband ordered the spare ribs after his appetizer.  He thought they were pretty delicious, but when he offered his wife a bite, she made an unpleasant face because she thought it was far too spicy hot.  I thought the heat was fine, but only had a small sample and didn't get a cumulative build up that the husband did.  He likes things hot, so he was satisfied.     I applaud the creativity and appreciate the effort to go "family style" on portions to encourage guests to sample and share.  And the visuals of the dishes were generally very appealing.    My advice is that if you plan on dining at Marrow, take time to look over the ingredients instead of just trusting other peoples opinions.  Everybody has different tastes for what appeals to them. I will need to follow my own advice the next time I plan a visit.  Review #21

This is a very nice neighborhood playground/park.  Set in an area with mature trees, the park has two playgrounds (toddlers and older kids), and a shelter with a picnic table and a grill.  The play area has drainage to avoid puddling which is good since the playground uses recycled rubber to soften the footing.  There is also a water fountain and a lending library too!  On the negative side, there is no designated parking, but the street parking is free in the neighborhood.  I also did not see any restroom facilities.  Review #513

This quirky grouping of bronze sculptures is actually 3 sculptures that were on the site during the 2005 Art Strategies public art promotion with sculptor Tom Otterness.  Back then, 25 bronze sculptures were placed primarily along public ways in downtown Indianapolis.  The Otterness collection was one of the first of several annual public art initiatives sponsored in Indy.  The largest of the three sculptures is titled "Free Money" and was sculpted in 2001.  The dimensions are 107.5 x 69.5 x 84 inches.  I wonder how many tourists observe that the base of the statue is a bag of money?  The smallest of the sculptures is titled "Male Tourist" from 1999.  Its dimensions are 27 x 21 x 10 inches.  The male is left holding the bags for a third sculpture.  The third piece is titled "Female Tourist" and is a slightly taller figure taking a photograph, apparently of the "Free Money" sculpture.  The third figure is 34 x 16 x 14 inches.  If you look closely at one of the attached photos, you can see the spot where the third figure stood before being removed due to an act of theft/vandalism.  However, the statue is restored and completes the three pieces again.  What impressed me the most about the collection when it was in town was that the figures often appeared benign, almost childlike at first glance.  However, several made dramatic social commentary.  My favorite was "Big Big Penny" which was located on the steps of the War Memorial along with "Educating the Rich on Globe" and "Miser".  I recall having several interesting discussions as people stopped by and began noticing the details of the sculpture and how they related to the role of money, power, and the social classes.  Review #117  FYI: For a more complete list of Public Art in Indianapolis go to the following website:  http://www.indyartsguide.org/public-art/

Although the place was packed when I arrived, I was greeted and seated promptly.  I took advantage of their low priced lunch options getting free salsa & chips, and a lunch sized Chimichanga with lots of options for $5.99.  I liked that the Chimi came with my choice of soft or fired tortilla, with beans or rice, and I could add cheese sauce or red sauce.  The Chimi was definitely smaller than most places, but since I knew it would be, I was fine with that.  (My waistline probably is too!)    The salsa was a little bit spicy and has nice veggie chunks.  Very nice!   The service was prompt and even check out was quick too.  (You can have the staff run your payment like a regular restaurant or take your bill up to the front and pay yourself.)   The only negative was that there wasn't much visual appeal to the meal or setting.  The sour cream was mostly liquid and the the interior of the place looked rather dated and broken into lots of small areas.     But the food tasted quite good and is worth stopping for.  Review #495

I had an early lunch at the downtown Napolese Pizzeria, just outside the Circle Centre Mall.  After parking in the mall and making my way outside to Meridian St, I was one of the first to arrive for lunch.  I chose to sit at the bar since I was dining by myself.      Within a few moments, I was provided a menu and water and had the basics of the restaurant explained to me, as well as the day's specials.    I selected the Meridian-Kessler Pizza - Italian Sausage, provolone, mushroom with tomato sauce and one of the canned craft beers.    While waiting, I was provided a small dish of Mixed Mediterranean Olives which were tasty;  more salt than bitter in flavor.  (3 kinds, all pitted for snacking)    The pizzas are "individual" sized, coming out on a 12" plate.  My pizza was a bit oval and overhung the plate about an inch on two of the sides.  All the pizzas are sliced into 6 pieces just before being served.  Individual slices are not sold since the pizzas are made to order, not left sitting around under a heat lamp.    The flavor was pleasant, but not remarkable.  As other Yelpers have commented, the center part of the crust was a little flimsy, but done enough to allow the slices to be hand held without dropping the toppings.  The mushrooms had a really nice flavor.  I guess I am used to a bit more sauce on my pies.    The service was good as well.  Since I came in around 11 a.m., the waiter was juggling attending my needs as well as helping get set up for the lunch service rush.  I never had to wait long especially since the pie was ready within 15 minutes.  And when I was ready to go, I simply signaled him while he was at the register and he promptly came over with a "to go" box and my bill.    Now that I have sampled the pizza, I think I am likely to sample one of the salad meals or sandwiches the next time in to get a better sense of the menu.    p.s.  They have both indoor and outdoor seating when the weather cooperates.  Review #65

I stopped by on an early Monday evening and was surprised that there wasn't much of a line ahead of me.  After parking in the rough lot behind the store, I walked around the building and was helped fairly quickly at one of the windows.  I hadn't been here in a long time, so I decided to treat myself to a banana split.  All the expected flavors (pineapple, strawberry, and chocolate) were there along with whipped cream and a cherry.  I also had them add the chopped nuts (under the whipped cream) along with the banana halves.  All the flavors were on point and reminded me of the splits we made at home when I was a kid.  Great bit of nostalgia as mentioned elsewhere.  The only reason I don't give this a five star is that there aren't that many different flavors of actual ice cream.  They rely upon adding a lot of items to make flavors, but unlike some of my favorite ice cream shops, they don't have a lot of buckets of colorful items to tempt the visitor.  In fact, about all the ice cream you can see is the word "ice cream" on the menu.  No windows to see inside or get a glimpse of what you might be selecting.    What I ordered tasted good.  I can't knock them for that and the price seemed fair.  Just wish I could see what I was ordering before it was handed out the window to me.  Review #289

If you want to get a good work out while escaping the daily grind, consider going to Skiles Test Nature Park soon.  There is a nicely paved path that winds up a steep hill at the beginning (there are about five rest areas along the way if you need them!).  Once it crests the hill, it leads to the north end of the park which makes it about 3/4 of a mile from the parking lot.  On the east side of the park is a reclaimed prairie area.  I was a little surprised that the grasses had been cut before winter, so it didn't look much like a prairie as it did a giant lawn.   On the west side of the path is a densely wooded area with one primary side path that loops through the forest.  It is mostly well maintained, but is not paved like the central path.  And for those a bit more adventurous, there are numerous less traveled paths that wind around.  I took one of those on the northern end and had to negotiate my way across a shallow stream about six feet across by using stones in the floor of the creek.  As I rose up the bank on the other side, I noticed the tracks of the deer that had recently used the path too.  There are no path markers or any pamphlets in a kiosk at the beginning.  No restroom and water fountains are on site either.  But if you like being out in nature and don't mind the challenge of a steep hill, then Skiles Test NP may be perfect for you!  Fun Fact:  Skiles Edward Test was a local business man who is connected to the Indy legend of the "House with Blue Lights".  Review #592

I echo Kara W's review about this new restaurant that opened around Independence Day:  Lots to like about the beer, the staff, and the surroundings with a slight noise problem.  I stopped in on a Saturday afternoon and saw there was a good crowd.  I like that they have onsite parking, a covered patio with picnic table seating (well behaved dogs are allowed!), and a garage door window area (it was closed due to the high heat, but is a nice option.)  There is a split counter area at the back of the building with a spot that suggests to place your order there.  There are some bar seats, but most folks were opting for the tables inside.  On the left behind the bar is the big board of beers that lists beer options/types/ABV/flight cost/pint cost/ and IBU.  On the right is a board with snack options which include soft pretzels, chips, charcuterie board, and info on Cluster Truck.  I decided to grab a flight of four 5-oz drinks (but could have gotten a flight of all seven house beers.)  My choices included the Red Line American Red Ale (5.3%, 33 IBU); Jorts Day Dry-hopped American Wheat (5.3%, 23); Hervey Street Hefeweizen (4.4%, 15); and the St Catherine Sienna Lager (5.2%, 22).  I liked them all!  The Red Line was deeper and richer than I expected.  The Jorts Day had a nice amount of hoppy flavor without being too bitter.  The Hervey Street (named after the cross street to Shelby) was a solid Hefe flavor with nice aroma and taste of the clove and banana flavors that I look for in a Hefe.  And to close out, the St Catherine was another full flavored beer that took on different flavors as I sipped more.  All the beers were cold, so any problems that other reviewers had must have been dealt with.  The folks behind the counter were friendly and could carry on a conversation while getting the beers.  There was no "wait staff" so customers carry their choices to their preferred seating and return the empties to the counter.  Seemed easy enough!  I liked that they already had two new beers announced, so I may have to return to the southeast side soon to check those out!  Review #1117

If you are looking for a quiet place, or a local place to get a good workout from hiking, then Glenns Valley is a place for you.  They have a parking lot at the entrance.  From there you can head in several directions on unpaved trails that have numerous branches.  I was surprised at how steep the assent was on some of the paths and really got my heart pounding!  There is a mix of evergreens and deciduous trees along the way and lots of wildlife could be heard scurrying about.  With so many winding trails, I will need to return to explore more of the paths.  Note:  There are now signs posted that sledding is prohibited in the park.  Review #688

On a Wednesday, I stopped at a downtown cafe and picked up a lunch to go.  Food in hand, I headed over to Metazoa to sample some of their craft brew and take advantage of their spacious seating including two outdoor patios.  They currently open at 1 on weekdays, so I was able to order a beer flight to go with my meal.  They were very cool with bringing in my own food since they currently don't have a permanent food option on site.  I chose a flight of only 4, but could have tried 6 or 8 different ales.  Unlike some other brewpubs/taprooms, I got to actually pick the four beers that I wished to sample.  What is apparent by the names of their ales is that this business cares about wildlife.  (Check out their website to see all the contributions these guys make!)  The four beers I sampled were: Nap in the Hammock (cream ale) 4.7% 17 IBU Kinkajou (honey weiss) 5.2% 7 IBU Dormouse Dubbel (Belgian) 6.5% 24 IBU and Red Devilicious (Cask) (Irish Red) 5.2% 20 IBU  As experienced craft brew afficianados can tell, I didn't sample any of the IPA's or darker beers since I am new to the tastes.  So, I cannot comment on those others.  Of the ones I tasted, my favorite was the Kinkajou.  The flavor was delicious. The honey aftertaste was bright.  My next favorite was the Nap in the Hammock.  The NitH would be considered a transitional beer for someone who has only experienced the big corporate beers.  The flavor was fresher than those mass produced competitors.  The Dormouse was okay, but I tasted more of the alcohol than any other notes of flavor.  Maybe the food I was eating didn't pair well with it.  Hard to say. The Red Devilicious was the first cask beer I have tried.  The bartender explained to me when I ordered that the cask beers create their own CO2 inside the cask (as opposed to the other beers that have the CO2 injected into them.)  The cask beers are roughly 15 degrees warmer than the others which allows their flavors to be fuller.  I agree it definitely had more taste than the others (the malt tasted chocolaty, almost like a coffee to me).  However, it was so different than any other beer I have had, I would say that my taste isn't experienced enough to appreciate that style yet.  Note 1:  There was plenty of parking on site for a lunch crowd, but there is some street parking on College (which is one way North at this location so approach from South Street.)  Note 2:  Plans are being considered to bring a permanent food option to the brewery which would facilitate opening a couple hours earlier to make lunch an option for the neighboring businesses as well as driving customers.  Currently, food trucks and delivery are the only other options other than bringing your own.  If you like trying new beers and knowing that some of the profits that you generate are going to support wildlife (mostly Indiana facilities), then give Metazoa a try.  I will be watching their website for more news and look forward to trying their food.  Review #68

The food at Noah Grant's is delicious.  My wife and I tried mostly items from the seafood side of the menu and a salad, and we enjoyed them all.  The items I would suggest are the shrimp and crab bisque, the Strawberry Fields (salad), the Maryland Crabcakes, and the Seafood Risotto (Scallops over Crab risotto).    My wife and I also liked that the building and interior decor are very classy.  They have the tin stamped ceilings.  The bench seating has lots of comfy pillows for back support if your legs aren't long enough to allow you to sit all the way back against the back of the bench.  The lighting is imaginative with some lamps look like jellyfish, others are surrounded by crab traps.    But despite these very positive points of atmosphere/experience, there is a definite identity problem for this restaurant.  Is it an upscale fine dining restaurant or is it a casual sports bar?  The food quality, the appearance, and the pricing suggest fine dining, so we dressed accordingly, thinking it would be like a fine steakhouse atmosphere.  But the staff were in jeans and shorts (in March) that weren't even ironed and other than our server who seemed pleasant and dressed nicely, there wasn't any warmth in the welcoming or exiting from the hostess station or others.    And to make matters worse, even though we ate during the week at 5 p.m., the open space between the bar and the dining area is wide open, so the revelers at the bar who were watching the NCAA tournament were clearly heard yelling.  Within the first five minutes, we were hearing F-bombs and S-bombs at full voice from individuals who thought they were at their own home or at a low end sports bar.  From what I could see, no management asked them to watch their behavior.  Fortunately, it must have reached halftime, so the noise level started to come down, but if this noise problem isn't fixed, I'm not sure there will be ratings anywhere near the level of the food and decor.    What was supposed to be a nice evening dining with my wife was certainly less than that.  We chose not to stay for dessert because of the noise.    Note:  My wife liked the food very much and thought we might give it another chance on a night that didn't have sports activity.  But the lack of management's stepping up to take care of the problem looks like there is more at fault here than lack of noise suppression.  I feel bad for the server and the kitchen.  Review #712

This mammoth store has large sections devoted to flower arrangements, fabric, hobbies, and Christmas items.  In the middle, you can find baskets, knick knacks, small furniture pieces, and plenty of other things for your home.  The stuff isn't of the high end quality, but they do have some neat items that you don't see elsewhere.  And if you are trying to decorate on a budget, then it may be your favorite place to start.  Still closed on Sundays, so plan accordingly.  Review #1931

This restaurant is fine..it's okay.  I like that they have some familiar Chinese food and make it to order instead of having it sit out on a buffet.  And I liked that the entree I ordered didn't take too long to make.  The Beef and Broccoli was cooked properly with the beef being very tender and the broccoli having a little bit of bite to it.  Oh, and the spring roll that I got was pretty tasty and larger than most places I've gone.  But the place is as sterile as can be.  They have a minimal amount of decor and the dated bench style seating looks like a typical fast food place.  Not much to make you think China.  The staff behind the counter was efficient, but not really welcoming.  The photos they have the food behind the counter don't look that appetizing.  It just isn't a place that says "Hey, stay here and eat."  So, I got my order to go.  What I will say is that the food was nice and hot and stayed so all the way home.  What that did though, was overcook the rice by the time I got to it.  The meat, though tender, relied solely upon the sauce for flavor.  No flavor from the grill (browning) at all.  And the egg roll, though good, didn't have any dipping sauce options, so I simply used what was on my entree to perk up the flavor.   Nothing here to set it apart from lots of chain store Chinese restaurants and certainly not a place that feels inviting to dine in.  It's probably a good enough place for locals to grab something quick, but not a place I would go out of my way to return to.  Review #1960

For a park without much space and limited access to the nearby river, this park is amazing.  There are festivals and concerts here.  There is a state museum, a sports museum (NCAA), a western museum (Eiteljorg), a zoo and botanical garden, and a former pedestrian bridge that now hosts temporary art installations.  Oh, and there is a beautiful canal that wanders through it designed for handling lots of folks using different modes of transportation.  It has a large underground parking facility and is just a short walk from the IUPUI campus, the convention center, Victory Field, and downtown.  Could there be a better location for this place?  The only negative I have is that it doesn't really promote itself as being a collective park.  There are lots of things to do here or very close by, but I don't see a lot of promotion saying "come to White River State Park".  But people still come here for all the individual activities.  Imagine if these activities/events all coordinated instead of doing their own thing.  This could be a next level event!  Review #1616

I've stopped in twice recently and enjoyed my meals both times.  On my most recent visit, I stopped in to try the Burger of the Month:  Nice Burger.  The Nice was a juicy half pound burger (even when served medium-well!) and topped with Brie, shaved apples, fig aioli, and caramelized onions.  The flavor was sweet and savory.  The burger also came with Truffle Tots which were crisp and crunchy.  Nice flavor on both.  The bartender was very personable and let me sample a couple tastes of brews on tap before I settled on a seasonal pumpkin spice brew.  Also, the burger was ready right away so I didn't have much of a wait.  Overall, it has a great location with the outdoor seating, but because it was cold outside, I finally dined inside for the first time.  There is plenty of room but it did feel like the ceiling was a little low.  Maybe it's just me, but I guess I'm used to a lot of pubs/restaurants with higher ceilings than here.  It wasn't claustrophobic, but noticeable.    Tip:  If you park in the garage just off Senate, they will validate your parking for you!  Rev #39

It had been awhile since my previous visit, so I decided to return to Bakersfield for a late lunch.  Fortunately, since it was after 1 p.m., I had no wait and the noise was moderate to light.    I ordered the short rib tostada which comes with a fried egg (sunny side up), black beans, Bakersfield hot sauce, queso fresco, shredded romaine, chives, and cilantro buttermilk dressing on two layers of crispy tortillas (about 5 inch each.)  The tostada also came with several lime wedges on the plate which added a nice acidity to the flavor balance.  I was also brought a Salsa Verde and a Salsa Roja which I used alternately.  Both worked well.  The crispiness of the tostada caused the meal to break into irregular shapes when I tried cutting through it.  Although it looked like a bit of a mess after cutting, the tostada was delicious and worth ordering again.  The heat was noticeable but balanced out by all the other flavors, so I wouldn't say it was too hot.  For me, it was just right.  The service was okay, but little things like not offering a glass to go with my can of beer (corrected when delivered) and not providing tableware until I asked for it means there was room for improvement.  Remember, the place wasn't hopping at this time of day.    Another item that I would appreciate was that having had the appetizers before, they are of the size I would consider shareable, so as a lone diner, I felt like I would need to either over eat or get a to go box if I wanted anything more than just an entree.  When I have to pay for salsa and chips, it would be nice if I could get a portion that was tailored to a single guest.  Overall, it was good food and a cool environment with decent service.  Like all Mass Ave businesses, the opening of two more new restaurants on the block later this year is going to make finding a parking space even harder.  But if you are lucky enough to find one or are within walking distance, then I would recommend Bakersfield for a nice option.  Review #333

I had been to quite a few breweries in the metro area, but had never been to one for Central State Brewing.  I looked it up and found that Koelschip is their pub that sells mostly their products.  I grabbed free street parking just down from the entrance though there is a gravel lot across Delaware from the bar.  Upon entering, I was immediately greeted and welcomed.  I'm not sure who was working when some other Yelpers took points off for bad service, but I must say that my experience was great!  The bartender introduced herself and asked my name.  As regulars started showing up, she introduced us and encouraged everyone to join in on the conversation.  Very friendly.  Very inclusive even though I wasn't a regular.  The space is long and narrow though they own a basement and an upper level.  So, no plans to add any in house food here.  Oh, and the decoration has empty frames with words instead of art like "couple with pitchfork" or "dogs playing poker", or simply "art".  It's kind of funny to see them all grouped like real paintings.  I decided to try a flight which is a bit higher priced than most others I have tried.  Here, most of the 5 oz tastes are $3 each, so $12 for four.  I had tried three of their ales before, so I decided to pick from the remaining flavors.  Note that they had about a dozen house ales/ciders on tap.    So on this visit, I went with the Halsurchschlag (mispronunciations are accepted, but you can just point to it on the menu!) which is a Meyer lemon Berliner Weiss (3.9%); the Bashi Barleywine (10.5%); the Hickory Ridge Farmhouse IPA (6%); and the Lazer Raptor Cranberry, Lime, Sea Salt Gose (5.9%).  My favorite was the Hickory Ridge.  This IPA was full flavored and multilayered which made it balanced, and though it had bitterness, it was balanced.  I also really liked the Lazer Raptor which was a very light and clean, call it refreshing beer.  But, the tartness of the fruit was replaced by a slightly salty aftertaste....think margarita for the closest taste.  The Halsurchschlag was a slightly tart beer that was a great starting beer.  It has a bit of a palate cleansing effect though it has a low alcohol content.  My least favorite was the powerful Bashi.  The high alcohol taste came through though it was partially offset by the pitted fruit, sugars, and spices that reminded me of a molasses taste or a weaker version of Grog.  Maybe if I was eating something, the flavors would have balanced out the meal, but alone, it was just a bit too heavy tasting.  Great service, friendly atmosphere, and generally good beer with a bit of emphasis on the sours make for a fun time at Koelschip (Coolship).  Fun fact:  though they brew their own sours at 26th & Sherman, their standard beers are brewed by Round Town Brewing using Central State's recipes.  Review #2134

Look...any place that brings in my favorite recording artist is going to get a great rating.  Truthfully, the food and venue are really great on their own!  So, when I saw that Jim Chappell was going to be performing on a Sunday night, I immediately bought a ticket online.  There is a handling fee and you simply check in the night of the show after 5 but at least a half hour before the show starts.  The main dining room that can see the stage (a very intimate setting) only seats about 100 guests.  I got to the area about 5:40 and actually found street parking on College!  Check in was at the main entrance and even though I was alone, I had no trouble getting a really good seat.  There is additional seating in the lounge where you can listen, but not see the performance.  I think those get a reduced ticket price.  Oh, and the lighting is low and mostly red.  Photos of food don't turn out unless you use lighting on your phone before the concert.  The photos of the stage don't seem to be affected.  Obviously, flash photography and cell phone conversations are discouraged so that guests can hear the music, not your chatter.  The staff and host were very welcoming.  I was seated and got my drink and placed my order for food, dined, and even ordered dessert before the show started at 7.  The servers are very quiet once the show begins, but still circulate to see if guests want anything else.  They then bring out your bill with about a half hour left in the show and you settle then.  Know that if you come here for a concert, you will have two bills:  one for attending the concert; and one for what you eat.  There is a minimum of $15 per person for food and beverages to make it worth while having servers on hand.  The concert tickets are based strictly on what the artist is charging.  But know that if you buy a ticket, you are going to be right there!  I was at the third table from stage and the sound was fantastic.  The food was also delicious!  I ordered the Crescent City Crab Cakes which comes with a side (I chose the Sweet Corn Maque Choux).  There were 3 breaded crab cakes (a little on the small side) that were cooked just right and came with two dipping sauces:  a cajun mayonnaise and a cocktail sauce.  The mayo was creamy and lightly spiced.  The cocktail sauce definitely had horseradish, but for flavor, not the ridiculous burning pain.  The "mock shoe" wasn't as creamy as I expected, but had a nice spicy taste that went well with the crab.  Oh, and the White Chocolate Blueberry Bread Pudding was fantastic!  It comes with a bourbon glaze caramel, a light cream, and topped with fresh cut strawberries.  Wow!  And the concert?  Simply amazing.  I love when a musician can play moving music acoustically.  Sure, big productions and great combos are fun too, but to show your talent with nothing but a piano is for a true master.  I've had the pleasure of seeing Jim Chappell once before when he came to Carmel (I even attended a workshop he gave that morning and had lunch with him.)  Both times, he has someone come out of the audience and play three notes (or in the first show, three different people pick a note).  He then creates a melody based on that pattern.  I am amazed every time how quickly he can create something so personal and emotive.  I have already scanned the upcoming schedule and found 3 or 4 more concerts I would like to go to this year.  If you want to go, get your tickets ahead of time to assure your place.  Once they are sold out, you won't get in.  Review #1228

Note:  I have not rented this facility for a private reception.  My review is based upon taking a tour in my first visit (when it reopened) and most recently, to view an art exhibit in the Rapp Family Gallery.  When Indiana Landmarks Center opened after a previous life as a Methodist Church, it became a symbol of why there is such interest in saving buildings from days gone by.  The building is fantastic in scale and beauty.  Woodwork, stained glass, and a giant pipe organ that looks more like an art piece than just an instrument are gorgeously preserved.  The $19 million renovation restored this 19th century Romanesque Revival church to a new purpose.    Once I checked in at the receptionist's desk, I started my most recent visit in the gallery on the lower floor.  There were 70 paintings by a local landscape artist who focused on the state parks as subject matter.  Wow!  It was fun recognizing some of the locations from my visits to the parks.  I am not sure how often they swap out the paintings, but I thoroughly enjoyed viewing these.  After the gallery, I was able to wander through the Grand Hall, the Cook Theater, and the board room to check out the superior restoration that was accomplished.  I can only imagine how great it would be to see a performance on either of the stages.  There is just something special about being around such fantastic work by artisans, both from the past and in the newer work to restore the grandeur.  If you are interested in renting the facility, know that the Grand Hall holds 550 when you include the balcony.  The Cook Theater can seat 350 for dinner when you count the mezzanine.    Tours of the building are free on evenings that First Fridays are scheduled.  Otherwise, group tours can be arranged for a fee.  If you have an interest in architecture or local history, this facility is a must see.  Review #243

After hiking around downtown on Tuesday afternoon, I decided to drop in Café Nonna to enjoy something cool and refreshing.  Mission accomplished!  Located in Fletcher Place, Café Nonna has a nice selection of Gelato and Sorbetto (non-dairy) items that can be ordered in a cup or a variety of cones.  After sampling a few, I decided to go with the Mango Sorbetto.  Although I am not a fan of fresh mango (at least the kind we get locally), the flavor was a blend of sweet and tart and altogether delicious!    While there, the cashier asked if I would like a sandwich and I thought, "Why not get one to go?"  So I did.  I selected the Baked Ham Sandwich on Marbled Rye with lettuce, tomato, house pickles, and house spiced mustard.  Okay, I have had a lot of ham sandwiches in my life, usually with some variety of cheese.  Since this sandwich didn't have cheese, I was expecting that the ham would need a lot of flavor to fill out the flavor profile.  It did!  There was over an inch of thick sliced ham on the sandwich!  No kidding, there were six slices of ham that had a hint of clove (?) seasoning that I go for whenever I bake a ham at home.  The house pickle added another level of flavor, not dill and salty, but a variety of spices that worked well.  When I added the spiced mustard, it was at another level.  I definitely recommend this sandwich if you have a hearty appetite, or feel like sharing, or want something for later.  And for only $6, you can't beat it!  Although the café is located in Fletcher Place on Virginia, it does have its own parking lot to the southwest of the storefront and patio.  Unfortunately, you can't turn off Virginia to get to the lot since the road is one way the opposite direction.  So, I headed down to McCarty and came back up to Virginia via the side streets.  The streets are a bit tight, so be careful as you approach.  It is worth it!    I plan on returning soon to try the sausage sandwich as well as some other flavors of the dessert.  The sausage is made in house and was recommended by the person who first told me about Café Nonna.    Review #131

I am a movie fan....a HUGE movie fan having seen all but 9 of the 528 movies nominated for Best Picture by the Academy.  So, when I want to see an indy film that is simply not available any place else in Central Indiana, I drive the 45 minutes necessary to see it at the Keystone Art Cinema.  Their selection of films is unmatched, ranging from the smallest Indy film all the way up to the blockbusters.  Sure, some films I can wait until they come out on DVD or an online service, but when I can figure out a movie time that works well with catching a lunch on the north side, then I am all in!  In addition to the best selection of movies, they have the basics for snacking.  They also were one of the first places around town to offer alcoholic beverages to enjoy while watching the movie.  Comfortable seating and good sound systems work well for enjoying films.  Prices, while on the higher end, aren't outrageous compared to most other movie theaters.  The only negative for me is that their parking can be limited due to competing with all the Keystone at the Crossing Mall customers.  Sometimes, you just have to walk farther.  Review #104

Wow, what a difference from my first dining experience.  This was great from start to finish! If you are reading reviews (like my old one) that write about Asian Fusion cuisine, you aren't getting the new picture.  According to my server (Matt was tremendous!), the chef likes to hop from continent/culture to a different one every couple months.  In May, I went and enjoyed the Central and South American (Latin) cuisine.  Although the interior has remained the same (and could stand just a little better lighting for us older folks to read the menus), the menu was completely new!  I decided to order one cold appetizer and then one served warm instead of going with an entree.  I started off with the Cocktail de Conservas with crab, sardines, mussels, concha, and octopus served in a cocktail glass with a liquified jalapeno cocktail sauce with saltines and lime wedges on the side.  I think there may have even been some small avocado slices in the mix. The variety of seafood was chopped into small pieces that made it hard for me to identify any except the sardines before tasting.  The variety of meats provided different textures...some with a little chew and others quite tender.  The lime added a nice depth to the flavor and the cracker served to revitalize the palate between bites.  And I really liked the bites where the cilantro leaves brought that familiar Latin flavor to mind. This starter was easily consumed by me and although it could be shared, I would recommend everyone getting their own.  My other item was the Oxtail Chilaquiles - small tortillas softened by the salsa rojo and topped with cubed oxtail, scrambled huevos, black beans, shredded cabbage, guacamole, cotija cheese with lime on the side.  The tortillas were sturdy enough to need a knife to cut through and had a pleasant flavor and chew.  The oxtail was juicy, tender, and had a great beefy taste.  The rest of the ingredients were distributed over the top, so each bite had a slightly different taste combination.  All were delicious!  I would definitely recommend this for someone who is less adventurous and is a steak fan.  I am so glad I gave Marrow another chance to win me over.  I am looking forward to returning and exploring some other continental cuisine.  Rev #23

Arni's used to be our spot when we lived in Greenwood.  We got to know the waitresses and had our favorite dishes.  My wife particularly loved the Southern Fried Chicken Salad and I was fond of the mini Cheeseburgers.  We always ended our dinner by sharing the Oreo Brownie Blast which we still use as a standard to rate desserts by.  So, when I returned in my first time in about four years, I was surprised that there was very little change in the layout/decor:  Still plenty of parking around the building, a front dining room that can be used as a small event space, a separate bar, and a large dining area form the layout of the space.  But the space felt different.  My waitress was friendly, but seemed a little forced as she hustled trying to keep all the tables.  She did a good job getting the order in, keeping ice water handy, and processing the bill.  The food, I ordered the Arni's Club, was fine.  Generous amounts of turkey and ham, with bacon and two kinds of cheese, and a little bit of mayo made for a hearty meal....just nothing exciting.  Maybe some kind of condiment with a bit more spice would perk it up.  The cole slaw I selected for the side was pretty good.  It was on the sweet side.  Overall, it was a lot like many pub food restaurants.  Good taste, but nothing you couldn't make at home.  They simply provide the convenience.  Review #2111

I was pleasantly surprised at the size and selection in this two story antique store in the middle of the Main Street shops.  The store is arranged with orderly booths with plenty of room to pass.  There are lots of collections including furniture, books, table settings, comics, vinyl, coins, and just about anything else you can think of.  Towards the back, there is a large staircase that leads upstairs to even more items.  Cool selection well worth checking out.  Review #2100

When you get great pizza, a selection of local craft beers, some tasty "shells" (calzones), and throw in a big welcome when you arrive, it's hard not to give the place a 5-star rating!  Throw in a few murals outside, more murals inside, paintings that are for sale, and decoupaged chairs that each have a unique theme, then there will be plenty to look at while you are waiting for your pizza to be made for you.  They have a small lot on site and free street parking along 16th and along Columbia.  There will also be outdoor seating at the picnic tables on the east side of the building.  Inside, the place is a little small, but cozy.  They have a pair of unisex restrooms: one is small (the door says "Lil Jon") and one is large (the door says "Biggie").  While waiting on our food, the owner let me know that the beer I ordered, "Insurance Sucks" (5%) is a collaboration between Centerpoint Brewing and the pizzeria owner's friend who is a home brewer.  The owner also has an insurance business, hence the name.  Though Greek's Pizzeria is a franchised business, it is based out of Muncie and each store is individually operated with a minimum of intrusion from the parent company.  The dough is made on site by the shop but has to use the parent recipe.  The secret pizza sauce is delivered from Muncie.  Other than those two required items, the owners have license to decorate the premises and adorn their pizzas however the want.   I went with a personal pizza, the Gourmet Meat.  Sliced into sixths, they have a firm crust and very little grease.  They use a type of pepperoni that doesn't produce a lot of fat and if you order double pepperoni, they sop up some of the excess so that the end result is more flavor, less greasy taste.  The pepperoni got crisp like bacon and my wife kept taking them off my pizza when she thought I wasn't looking!  She ordered a "Shell" of Ham and Cheese with a pickle spear.  The shell was huge, nearly a foot long and she definitely needed a "to go" box.  The shell did not come dressed in sauce like a lot of calzone other places.  Instead, she asked and received some spicy brown mustard to go along with the meal.  The folks behind the counter were friendly, but mainly let the owner greet and say farewell to the customers.  If desire has anything with making a business a success, then this place will do well.  Highly recommended!  Review #1814

My wife and I had an enjoyable lunch at Taylor's.  There were lots of options including some daily specials that looked pretty appealing.  I went with the Parmesan Encrusted Pot Roast on my choice of Rye bread.  Plenty of meat and mildly seasoned with a few sauteed onions and the bread lightly coated with the cheese.  It came with a side of house pretzels which were crisp and garlicky.  The dill spear was a nice touch too!  My wife passed on the regular chili and went for the chili 3-way which includes cheese and pasta noodles.  She thought the flavor fine, not too spicy, but found the bowl a bit dry (possibly the noodles sucked out some of the moisture.)  The serving was large and she left mostly noodles sitting at the bottom.  Probably should have just got the regular chili.  It also came with a peppery breadstick which she gave to me since I enjoy pepper more than her.  It was robustly seasoned, so be aware of that if you order them.  Our hostess/server was friendly and checked in on us regularly.    I could see why so many folks who visit here are regulars.  Lots to choose from and the flavor combinations are just a little different from all the other places.    Review #2294

My wife seems to enjoy looking at jewelry and estate items, especially when they are displayed as nicely as they are here.  The shop is laid out like an "L" and has both estate items as well as new that cover a wide range of collectibles, jewelry, and watches.  The staff was very helpful and assisted my wife who was checking out the watches on the west end of the shop.  While she was engaged, I browsed the store and couldn't help but notice the beautiful furniture and decor used inside.  There's a grandfathers clock, an ornate display cabinet, and even a beautifully maintained salt water fish tank that make the place seem special.  My wife says the prices are good to great for the items she checked out.   That's a good enough recommendation for me!  Review #2213

There is a lot to like about Flat 12.  They have a wide variety of beers to choose from.  They have a large patio with plenty of spots to sit in sun or shade.  They share a space with Hoagies & Hops, so you can get really good sandwiches without having to bring it with you or wait for a delivery.  There are lots of televisions to catch the latest games/events too.  Basically, it has about all you would want for a relaxing location to sip a beer and enjoy being with friends.  I won't say it is my favorite brewery, but I definitely enjoy coming here.  Like a lot of places, parking is somewhat limited to street parking.    Note:  Dorman is one way northbound, so head east on New York St to get here.  Review #984

My wife and I were invited here by our daughter's family for lunch, so we met in the business's private lot and headed on in.  I had read some reviews, but those were somewhat dated as the menu board I saw in front of me had fewer options than some photos on this business's Yelp page.  I had planned on getting a Carolina pulled pork which comes with the cole slaw on top, but that wasn't offered.  Instead, I went with a "naked" brisket and added two sides:  cole slaw and green beans with bacon.  The place has an order counter to your left as you walk in and then a number bench/tables (ours rocked every time someone leaned on it) and some 4 tops in the dining area.  You place your order and then pick a table.  When it is ready, you go retrieve it from near the order counter.  Sauces and sodas are around the corner from the ordering area, so I grabbed a couple sauces to try them out.    I didn't see my favorite sauce:  a Carolina mustard.  I grabbed something similar in color and a Cherrywine sauce for something new.  The yellowish sauce didn't have any of the mustard flavors and was disappointing.  The Cherrywine simply didn't pair well with the brisket.  Be aware that if you order your sandwich "naked" (no bun), they don't have table knives sitting out by the forks.  So, you have to spear it with your fork and bite it or use your fingers.  There isn't any service on the floor to even ask if they have knives available.  The meat did have a smokey taste and stayed moist on its own.  It was generally tender, but not "fall apart" tender.  The green beans with bacon was peppered and salted and had an overall pleasing taste.  The beans are cooked thoroughly, not al dente.  Although I liked them, my wife thought they had too much pepper.  The vinegar based slaw was a pleasant surprise.  It had more crunch than I expected and had a bit of tartness instead of being overly sweet like some places.  It was sliced much larger than most places I've been too, so it didn't look like it would work as a traditional Carolina topping.  My wife seemed to like her food better than I, so I might give this another 1/2 star based on her experience.  But for me, there was not a single thing that stood out to draw me back.  I have several independent barbecue places closer to my home that I have enjoyed more.  Sorry City BBQ.  Review #1795

We don't have a Trader Joe's on our side of town, so it isn't practical to shop for perishable foods here.  But when I am in the area, it is a place I stop by to see what food items are out there that I hadn't discovered yet.  In some cases, when I am about finished with my business on the north side, I actually make purchases that I can trust to stay fresh on the drive home.    Such was the case on my most recent visit.  The vibe was inviting and friendly,  not like the big box stores that have every item you need and more that you never will.    Here they have variety and that in itself is interesting.  And the prices, while maybe not the same as the giants, is reasonable and worth the quality.    Now that Marsh has closed its doors, I wish we had a Trader Joe's on our side of town to find those items that the big stores don't carry.  Review #329

I'm going to have to return soon.  I was in a bit of a hurry and when I walked in, the menu board listed Root Beer Float and I honestly didn't look any farther.  The gal behind the counter immediately asked if I wanted to go with the traditional vanilla ice cream and then began scooping the frozen treat into the cup.  A&W Root Beer was then opened and poured over the ice cream for that not so pretty foam that tastes delicious.  She even gave me the rest of the can of soda to go with the dessert.  The space is easy to spot from the highway, but requires turning into the shopping center (the one with the movie theater) and then driving behind the frontage buildings to about midway down the row.  An alley area leads passed the outdoor seating (located underneath a former drive through area for a bank) to the parking and entrance.  Inside, there is a party room on the right and a play room on the left of the entrance.  Beyond those, there is dining on the left and the order counter on the right where they have lots of barrels of ice cream and a variety of other sweets.  Service was fast and friendly and before long, I was out the door.  I'll have to go after lunch the next time so that I take more time to see what else they have available.  Review #2722

The Small Mall is a single story shop that has relocated its collection of furniture, antiques, and home decor from the former Mass Ave location to the one in the strip mall off 62nd near Binford.  There is a lot of furniture that seemed reasonably priced to me within the shop.  I also found a bunch of cool home decor items like paintings, wall hangings, mirrors, and some antique knick knacks.    There are some arrangements that help you visualize what a room might look like with the piece you are interested in.  There are also open spaces that have been setup as rooms, but without the walls.  Traversing the length of the shop is easy with plenty of wide and clear aisles to pass along.  The quality of the pieces appeared to be on the nicer end, not flea market stuff.  The person behind the central desk was friendly and greeted me when I entered and offered to help if I was looking for something specific.  Overall, I enjoyed looking through the shop though I didn't make any purchases on that day.  Review #2140

Having tried about a half dozen Thai places around Indy, I can heartily endorse dining here.  We stopped in for lunch (about $8 each) and got the entree, a small bowl of soup (coconut milk vegetable soup on our visit), a crispy phyllo dough wrapped spring roll with a sweet sour dipping sauce, a small salad with ginger dressing, and of course, the choice of meats and spiciness level for our entrees.    We were greeted as we entered and service, while maybe a little understaffed due to a nearly full house, did a pretty good job of keeping up with our needs.  Complimentary water was brought out in addition to our beverages.  I ordered a small pot of tea and got just over 1 1/2 cups (a little on the low end compared to other places.)    My wife does not do well with spicy foods, so when she ordered the Pad Piew Wan with pork and low spice level, she got a large meal with a tasty sweet and sour sauce that suited her well.  She was very pleased with the taste and the comfort level of the spice.    I went with my standard Pad See Ewe (I like to get this the first time at any Thai restaurant which makes it easier for me to compare for ratings.)
