I opted for the chicken and a medium level of spicy heat.  The chicken was moist and had a pleasing taste on its own.  The spice level was one that seemed low when it started but eventually raised as I ate more.  I would say it ended on a medium level which was fine.  Strange how some places build the heat while others deliver it from the start without getting hotter.  Not sure what different spices each place uses. The noodles were slippery without being slimy.  The taste was very pleasing.  The veggies were cooked just beyond al dente, so there was texture without being tough.    Overall, I thought this was a great value for lunch (and maybe some leftovers for light eaters.)  I would gladly return to try more entrees.  Review #343

Pretty much a "to go" only coffee place with just a couple small tables outside during nicer weather days.  Didn't see any indoor seating.  The place seems like it is a beverage only shop as well since I didn't see anything on the menu to munch on.  I simply got my standard black drip coffee and it was okay, not fantastic.  It was served right on the edge of being to hot to drink, but I managed to not burn my tongue, so they get a good rating for that!  Friendly and quick service around lunch time, so good ratings for that too!  Review #2584

While shopping in old town Zionsville, my wife wanted to stop by Green Apple to see what type of boutique it was.  So glad we did!  The shop is small, but makes the most of its space with displays and wall hangings of fashionable athletic wear.  There is a small office with a cutout window that the shop owner, Shelly, can welcome customers.  After just a few minutes of shopping, it was clear that Shelly has a real passion and knowledge of her products and the customers she hopes to serve.  My wife kept finding items she liked and Shelly was able to tell her whether the brand ran large or small, was able to show other pieces that would coordinate with the piece, and some other products/accessories that might be useful.  One of the cool options is that she has a customer list that you can sign up for online to periodically receive gift boxes selected for you based upon the profile you provide.  You have the option to select frequency, dollar limits, piece limits, etc.  You keep what you like and pay only for those and send the undesired pieces back.  You can stop by anytime to meet with Shelly to fine tune your choices.  Some folks even do this as a gift option for friends/relatives.  One more thing:  They do have a small selection Matilda Jane children's clothing that you can browse inside the shop.  If you want to find quality clothing for your athletic endeavors that will easily transition to stylish wear "on the go", stop by and check this out!  Review #2199

When my wife walks into a sports bar and immediately says she likes it, That Place is going to get a good review.  She thought that it was spacious, not cramped.  It was clean, not dingy.  It didn't smell like some old dive bar.  She notices those things more than I do.  They also have lunch specials which she took advantage of getting the Taco Bowl.  No shell outside, just frito type crunchies underneath.  The flavor wasn't spectacular, but satisfying.  The portion was plenty for a lunch without her having to get a to go box.  I like paying for what you eat at the restaurant without having to eat leftovers to get your money's worth.  I went with the house special sandwich:  "That Sandwich".  It's made with a German Bologna, grilled onions, pepperjack cheese, and sweet pickles on grilled marbled rye.  If you like Reuben sandwiches, then you will probably like this.  There are lots of similar flavors here that work really well together.  I would definitely recommend it.  The sandwich comes with house made crinkle chips that were large and crisp; maybe just a tad over cooked and they would definitely have benefited from salt being added when they were finished cooking.    The place supposedly gets busy in the evenings and weekends with live music added.  For lunch, it was relatively quiet with all the televisions on mute.  Service was okay since the bartender had to run the whole front end by herself.  So, she made it over when she could and kept a pleasant disposition despite the lack of help.  Review #2706

I dropped in for lunch on Tuesday and took advantage of the flight (4 beer samples for $8) and the combo lunch special for $7.50.  Fantastic!  After parking on nearby McCarty Street, I grabbed a spot at the bar where Anna, the bartender/waitress was running the entire front end of the house.  She was impressive in that she handled all the customers and still had time to be pleasant and efficient.    I had pre-selected some food items from the online menu, so I thought I would put my food order in first and make my flight selections later.  Seeing that I wanted a salad and a wrap, she pointed out the "Take 2" lunch special (available Tues - Fri).  Since the wraps weren't part of the special, she suggested getting the ingredients on a ciabatta bun instead.  Turned out it was a great suggestion as well as a cost savings to me!  For my salad, I went with the Chick Corea Salad.  (Chick Corea was a jazz fusion artist I listened to in high school as a solo artist and with Return to Forever.)  The salad came with Chick Peas, spinach, quinoa, sun dried tomatoes, and feta cheese.  I went with the apple cider vinaigrette (it comes on the side) as my dressing.  Excellent!  I highly recommend the cider/salad combo of flavors.  The wrap choice, now a panini style sandwich, was the "Travelin' Light".  The ciabatta bread was crisp and tasty and held up well with the roasted red pepper, provolone, spinach, quinoa, and sweet chili sauce.  Not too spicy, but a nice balance of flavors.  Truly a pretty sandwich to view with the bright red pepper and deep green from the spinach.  Just enough cheese to get a little gooey, but not sloppy.  (I'm not exactly sure of the musical tie in on this menu item.)  After asking a few questions about the flight, I selected some of the lighter house beers on tap:  The "Built to Last" Pilsner (4.7%) was delicious.  It seemed to almost have a fruity taste on the first sip although no fruit is listed in the description.  Very tasty! I then moved to the "Chilly Water Lager" (5.8%).  This was another fine, very smooth flavored beer.  I also had the "Maggie's Farmhouse Ale" (6.9%) and the "Loose Juicy" Pale Ale (5.6%).  Every one of the beers tasted good on its own and with my lunch.  I tried a sample of the "Charlie Brown" American Brown Ale and wasn't a fan of that, but that was more for information purposes that I tried it.  Since I still had room to eat, I didn't want to pass up the chance to try the dessert featured at Chilly:  "Skip's Balls"!!  These golf ball sized desserts are made with cookies and cream cheese, then dipped in your selection of one of the available sweet coatings.  I selected the dark chocolate coating which forms a crisp outer layer of the treat.  (These are hand held, not a knife and fork type of dessert.)  The cookie filling was very light, maybe a little denser than a cupcake.  Reminded me of the taste you get from the outside cookie on an oreo.  Sometimes, different flavors are added inside as well as to the shell.  I believe Anna stated that they currently had white chocolate and peanut butter shells on hand.  Loved this so much I got a couple more to go!  Great food, great beer, and great service lifted this brewery beyond my expectations.  5 Stars from me!  Review #126

I had a nice cup of black coffee and a really tasty almond croissant at Provider.  The staff was very friendly as I ordered my coffee at the counter.  He asked what I liked and recommended a brand of black coffee for me.  It comes with a second cup at no extra charge.  I mentioned I would like a croissant (almond) as well. I was able to help myself to one from the display case behind me (across the aisle from the counter).    The croissant was very tasty!  Light and flaky outside, creamy almond paste inside, and topped with crispy baked almond slices made for a delicious pastry.  I was able to grab one of the high top chairs at a table.  I felt like the only person not working on a computer while drinking my coffee.  Seems like most of the folks were there for a lot more than just the coffee which filled the shop's seating and table space.  Although there is plenty of space outside, I didn't see any chairs for enjoying a nice morning in the sun.  My only negative is that the actual menu doesn't list much detail about drinking options.  Coffee is simply listed as coffee.  I can't remember what type I had and can't look it up on a website.  It looks like many of the beverage options (other than the lattes) are listed by generic group.  I looked around the shop and didn't see any boards with lists.  Maybe I missed it, but I don't see it any of the interior photos posted on Yelp either.  Hopefully, they will put together some kind of list (paper or board) to let customers see what options are available.  Although there are quite a few parking spaces between the buildings, most looked taken, so I was able to pull into a spot across the street (facing the Monon).  Review #960

I had heard about Punch Burger when it first opened, but since I had heard it was always packed at lunchtime, I put off going.  But when I knew I was going to be downtown this evening, I found a review of Punch Burger and it mentioned that this was a local business, not another one of those giant burger chains (thanks Brittany S!)  So, I stopped in.  First, I liked that they had 20 minute free parking in front of their business.  I was able to pull up, order, and get my sandwich to go in far less than that time constraint.  I liked that they have a group of named burger options to choose from or an extensive list of ingredients to Build Your Own.  I was instantly drawn to the Thai Burger and made that my choice.    When I got my order out to my car, I had to take a bite before heading home.  Wow!  The flavor was so good!  If you have never tried a peanut butter and burger combination, then you are really limiting yourself!  This burger also came with some red onion, chili sauce, and Asian slaw underneath.  Strong flavors with a great balance.    I also liked that the burger was a moderate size (I'm guessing a 5 or 6 oz burger) since it wasn't as massive as a lot of burger specialty places.  I could actually take a bite without having to squeeze the burger to eat it.  That's a good thing.  I hope I won't wait so long to return to try another one of their flavor combos.  Review #1747

I stopped in mid-morning, missing the morning breakfast rush and grabbed a seat in the dining room.  The waitress/hostess was pleasant and brought a menu and took my beverage order promptly.  Since it was my first time here, I wanted a little more time to look over the menu.  She did a great job of watching to see if I was ready.    Since it was nearing lunch time, I decided to forego a traditional breakfast option and went with the Southwestern Skillet.  It was served in a mini skillet filled with onion, bell peppers, avocado, sausage (they were out of chorizo) and cheese.  They also threw in some red potato quarters.  The meal came with 2 eggs on top (over easy for me) and 2 biscuits and gravy on the side.  Quite a meal!    The seasoning was minimal, but each table has salt and pepper shakers so I was able to adjust the seasoning to my taste.  All the veggies were cooked thoroughly and the sausage had a nice browning for full flavor.  The only negative was the eggs were just a little over cooked, most likely from sitting on top of the hot skillet of food.  The biscuits were country style and were very light, much lighter than I expected.  The gravy was served on the side so I could add as much (or little) as I wanted.  Nice flavor all around.  Plenty of parking outside and inside, the place was clean and tastefully decorated.  There's a colorful mural of an Indiana sunset by the door.  Good service and good food for a price that reflects the quality of the ingredients.  I was stuffed by the time I finished with a smile on my face.  Review #2738

I have had this place bookmarked for the entire time they have gone through construction.  I remember seeing the livery being put up on wheels and moved to this spot next to the train tracks just south of the Fieldhouse.  So when I heard about the grand opening from one of the staff up at the Fortville location, I made plans to be here at 11 a.m.  The good news is they have all the great beers that you get at the other two locations.  They have a beautifully restored/transformed building that is two stories tall (an upstairs bar holds about 50 more people.)  And the folks working there were so proud of their place that everyone of them seemed to be smiling.  And it only looks to be better in the spring when the large outdoor patio can have nicer weather to entertain customers.   The location looks to be promising too for fans who go to a basketball game just up the street.   I was greeted in the main lobby and given a preference of bar seating or table and though I usually go for the bar when by myself, I was given a table in the bar since I was ordering a flight and didn't want to be crowded  once my beers and food arrived.  There are lots of house beers to choose from including their seasonal and reserve vault series.  They even have some additional ales in bottles.  I tried four new seasonal ales ($2.50 for each mini so you build your own flight size.)  I was definitely awake with the Tax Holiday 10% ABV.  Wow!  That is one potent dark ale!  I decided to go with the CityWay Smash Burger, a double patty with a somewhat simple ingredient list of American Cheese and "Fancy Sauce".  The burgers were good and juicy while being thin.  However, I would have liked it more if there were more flavors (tomato, onion, lettuce, anything) than just the sauce.  Hard to describe what was in the sauce since I didn't really taste it on its own.  I'll probably try something else the next time unless they add some toppings to the burger.  The fries were long and done perfectly with a bit of salt.  It came with a small cup of catsup for dipping and I was sad when they were all gone.  Excellent!  The service was great during my visit.  I had my own carafe of water, and whenever I finished one of my mini glasses of ale, the empty was promptly removed.  I was also checked on to make sure I didn't need anything a couple times during the meal too.  Really good job.  So, there are some things to be aware of when you visit here.  Note that there is construction on both Delaware and South Streets.  That means there is VERY LIMITED street parking in the area.  You can park in the Alexander Hotel's parking garage but that's pricey.  The other CityWay garage is for residents only.  The hostess also recommended parking at the Fieldhouse garage or the Circle Centre garage which are a couple blocks away.  Note that if you park at those, you will have to go through railroad underpasses and unfortunately, Taxman has no control over the lighting and the number of homeless people located there.  I really wish they would have had their own lot.  My advice is to park south of the brewery along Delaware or South Street to the east of Delaware.    Note too that if you sit along the brick wall in the bar, the air is on the chilly side this time of year.  I noticed it first and then heard one of the ladies at the next table ask her group if anyone else felt cold.  No insulation between the outside and the brick.  So, if you are sensitive to the cold, sit more in the middle.  I don't want to sound too negative.   I really like the space and the food/beer/service is the high quality I expect from Taxman.  Maybe some of the other issues of the area will be improved by the time the patio is open.  Review #3313

For a slightly different experience with Mexican/Taco dining, stop by this strip mall restaurant just west of the Uof Indy campus.  Upon entering, my wife and I noticed the colorful, but tastefully decorated interior.  We were greeted and told we could pick our own seating.  There is a small bar area on the rear left, booths along both walls, and a row of tables down the center.  Before long, our waitress stopped by to get our beverage order and deliver the menus.  Although she mentioned they had a "salsa bar", she didn't really go into any details which would have been useful for a first time customer.  Basically, if you order tacos (or another entree but want more toppings), the tacos are basically the tortilla (corn or flour) and the meat.  You then head over to the free standing salsa bar where there are three types of taco sauce and eight toppings including cucumber, radish, onions, peppers, limes, etc.  They do have small cups for carrying your sauces, but there aren't any small plates to hold your other ingredients, so you have to bring your entree plate with you.  Note that I didn't see any lettuce, tomato, or sour cream at this station.  I saw someone get a small plate with lettuce and sour cream, so you may have to ask for that.  Never did see any tomatoes.  I ordered the Carnitas which is a delicious braised pork dish that is made with a family recipe.  Excellent flavor and the pork was juicy/tender.  It comes with three tortillas and sides of beans and rice.  Highly recommended!  However, my side order of Elote was disappointing.  It looked really good, but was heavily salted which made it difficult to enjoy.  I expected the spicy seasoning, but somehow, I barely tasted that.  The salt was just overpowering of the other flavors.  It's a shame because the corn had a nice bit of char to bring out a deep rich flavor, but it was barely noticeable.  My wife went with a chicken burrito which is huge!  It comes sliced across the middle for easier handling.  Although it lots of ingredients, she found that only the chicken was spread across the length.  Most of the items were dolloped in just one spot, so one bite may be chicken and lettuce.  Another might be chicken and sour cream.  It would only take a brief time to spread these ingredients and make for a better overall flavor for the customer.  She also found the seasoning on the chicken (it had a bit of an orange color) to not be to her liking.  I tried it and thought it tasted like celery seed.  Not what she was expecting, so she was disappointed even though the chicken was tender.  Note that if you don't eat it fast, the tortilla will hold in the heat and continue to cook the chicken.  So, I enjoyed my entree, but not the elote.  My wife liked the chicken burrito, but not the presentation or the sauce it had.  The waitress was friendly and did a good job of checking in and processing our bill.  So, 3.5 for our experience, but I'll round up hoping that they will get some of the issues I pointed out fixed.  (I mentioned the salty elote to the waitress and she said that the corn can be ordered with low salt.)  Review #2616

I've been meaning to try the beer at Triton on draft instead of settling for bottled, so when I read that they opened a new bistro as part of the brewery, I decided to take the 45 minute trip.  So glad I did!    Now if you aren't familiar with this relatively new development just east of Fort Ben, be aware that street signs are hard to find.  Fortunately, if you have a good map or GPS, it will get you close enough to see the giant metal tank with the Triton logo sitting in their parking lot.    I must admit my first impression wasn't very positive.  I walked in and had five people wearing black Triton t-shirts look at me and then ignore me.  I was the only customer and it was during regular business hours.  After a few moments, my waiter appeared and greeted me.  The service from then on was spot on.  Isn't it amazing how the quality of interaction with staff can affect your whole experience, regardless of food and beer quality?      Since I had looked over the menu and beer list ahead of time, I placed more order and was pleasantly surprised how quickly everything arrived.  First, I started with my two half pints of beer:  Hometown Hero Ale (4.5% 16 IBU) and Barn Phantom Gose (4% 10 IBU).  The Hometown is a Golden American ale and had a fuller flavor than some I've had.  The Barn Phantom was a sour that was just tart enough to keep my attention without throwing off the flavor of my food.    For my lunch, I went with a Breaded Tenderloin and for a small upcharge, added deep fried Onion Rings.  The Tenderloin was great.  It was larger than the brioche bun, but not gigantic in area.  Instead, they left the meat thicker which allowed it to maintain its moisture and ultimately, more satisfying.  The meat & breading could use a little more seasoning for my tastes, because I used the full complement of toppings which tend to dull the seasoning.  I want to make special note that the house made pickles, which include beer in the process, were delicious and I appreciated that it wasn't just the typical sweet or dill flavor you get from store bought.    The onion rings were small in number (4) but huge in size.  They were stacked into a "tower" and frankly, I didn't finish them all.  The onions are thick sliced rings (at least a half inch) and then heavily breaded.  Although the first two were crisped and tasty, by the time I got to the third and largest of the ones I ate, they had cooled and the breading held onto some of the cooking oil making the taste a little less appetizing.  I'm not sure if they could thin the batter and still have it coat evenly, but when pairing the breading of the onion rings with the bread in my sandwich, I was filling up fast.  I would suggest sharing an order.    I like that the beers are available as pints, half pints, and flight sized 5 oz. and all the prices are shown on the menu.  They also have some small batches which I would like to come back for including existing beers with fruit flavors added into the brewing.  Key lime beer anyone?    I recommend giving the place a try and hope that you get the server I had so you can enjoy your meal and beverages.  Review #567

My wife and I stopped if for lunch and had a really enjoyable experience.  Our waiter (Tyler H) was welcoming and took care of us throughout the meal.  We were seated on the patio which is so close to Eagle Creek that you can hear the flowing water from the deck.  Very comforting!  My wife tried the Mahi Mahi without the bread and seemed to enjoy it.    I tried the 1/4 pound "Settle for Less Ugly" ELK burger.  I may have had elk before, but it must not have made much of an impression.  This time did!  The patty was liberally seasoned with a variety of spices that you might find on a steak and with the nice char from a medium well temperature, the taste was really good!  (Lots of spices which were well blended..not salty at all!)  I also got a small order of the Sloppy Waffle Fries to share.  I liked the light, but mostly crisp fries.  Each one was enough for a couple bites.  The bacon bits and sour cream were find, but I wasn't a big fan of the mystery "Cheez Whiz" type cheese that was dolloped on top.  I can't place the taste.  Okay, just not my favorite.  Let me point out that this location seems to be a lot more spacious than the Carmel location which I found cramped too closely together.  Also, the trend on reviews seems to have rebounded from a mediocre period a couple years ago and settled into a generally favorable recommendation.  Give this place a try the next time you want to try a tasty burger while keeping the dollars local.  Review #2640

Did you ever have one of those places that seemed to keep popping up in articles you read or heard discussed, but had never found time to visit?  Well, the Harrison Center was becoming "that place", so I decided to visit on a winter day.  I contacted them ahead of time to arrange for a guided tour (free) since I have heard that that there is a confusing floor plan that may baffle first time visitors.    I pulled in off 16th Street into the mid-block parking lot between Delaware and Alabama.  Parking is limited when lots of artists are in their studios or the Center is having an event, but because I was going on a chilly afternoon, I was able to grab a spot.    Be aware that the Center is made up of three buildings that are linked by basement hallways and multiple stairwells.  Some floors are split level (the Gymnasium for example), so if you have mobility concerns, you may need to limit your visit to the two main galleries in the southern building:  City Gallery and Speck Gallery.  The Harrison Gallery and the Gallery Annex are on the first floor of the northern building, but do not have a ramp to make it up the three steps.  If that is not too much climbing, you can approach the northern building via the sidewalks in the courtyard area (exterior).    If you want to experience the full exposure to the galleries and studios, take the guided tour.  The guide will take a large set of keys which will open the individual studios of the artists so that you can appreciate how each individual arranges their tools of the trade.  Note that artists are free to decorate the inside of their studios as they wish and frequently use the wall space in the hallways outside their studios to hang their works, many of which are available for purchase.      Since there are many artists with preferences for working all hours of the day and night, you are bound to run into some artists working in their studios when on the tour.  If you catch them at an appropriate time, you may be able to engage in a conversation.  Just keep in mind that they are there because it is their work time, so brevity is in order.  I was able to chat with several, including resident curator Kyle Ragsdale, who has a retrospective featured in the Speck Gallery.    I also met William Rasdell, a photographer and digital artist who uses his art to study the effects of migration on culture.     Artist Chad Campbell took time to explain his motivations and background leading up to his work with found materials and the use of the familiar to make his art relatable. There were numerous wire art forms arranged outside his studio on the basement level.    If you plan on taking the guided tour, please allow yourself time to go back and visit the galleries in greater detail or maybe engage in a conversation or two.  You can easily extend a visit from an hour to several if you explore on your own.  Review #210

The first time I brought my wife to Burgerhaus was during the winter.  We had a wonderful meal and absolutely loved the giant Belfast onion rings.  I really enjoyed the Tuscan Burger as well.    More recently (6-3-16), my wife and I brought another friend who was visiting for the first time.  We got there early to beat the dinner crowd and were able to sit outside on the patio overlooking the great view of the downtown canal.  Nice breeze, a cool beverage in hand, and the expectation of another great burger.  This time, I tried the Monaco burger.  Although it was cooked properly and quite juicy, I was a bit disappointed in the flavor combinations.  I feel like the toppings hid the flavor of the meat, which made the beef seem like filler instead of the key ingredient.  The fries that came with my meal were seasoned nicely and not too salty.  The order of onion rings that came to the table were once again delicious.  The only real negative was that there was a communication problem for our friend's burger.  It was so rare that the reddish juice from the burger had made the bottom half of the bun soggy.  She thought she ordered the burger medium.  Our waitress quickly removed the sandwich and within a short while, brought a replacement that was cooked properly....at first we saw the juice dripping from the second attempt, but realized that it was clear in color and soon stopped dripping.    Our waitress was very welcoming and understood that we were a group enjoying the evening on the waterfront.  She picked up on our festive mood and did everything she could to keep our spirits light.  I look forward to returning and trying some of the other options and being able to review with a higher score like I had experienced upon our first visit.  Review #5

I've been to several UPS stores in the area and based upon the amount of services and supplies this location has, I would say that it warrants an average rating.  It doesn't seem to have as much to offer as the Greenwood location, but is laid out better and offers more than the Mooresville location.  So maybe  3.5 star?    I do like the layout with the counter area to the right which allows people to come in and move about without waiting in a long line by the door.  However, the amount of supplies for shipping on display near the front seemed somewhat limited.  Still, if you have your items already boxed and ready to go, the staff seemed to be intent on getting everyone helped.  Review #3482

Though you could hardly tell from the outside of this strip mall restaurant, inside is a tastefully done escape to Japan!  The inside is kept somewhat dark with down lighting over each table.  There is also a sushi/alcohol bar located in the middle of the restaurant with seating available too.  I was greeted and seated promptly and went with a booth style table in the dining area.  I ordered hot green tea which is served by the cup (though you do get refills) instead of them bringing a pot which can take up table space.  Nice flavor that tasted of tea, not diluted or affected by the chemicals in the water like some places I've had it.  I ordered a lunch special roll (Eel) that comes with 2 chef choice Nigiri, a small bowl of Miso soup, and a small salad with their house dressing.  I also ordered an appetizer of Tuna Tataki to come out after my soup and salad, and before my sushi platter.  The soup was one of the better Miso soups that I've had.  Though thin, it did have a bit more salt than comparative bowls I've had.  It also had bits of seaweed and a little tofu, but minimal.  Nice flavor overall.   The salad was primarily iceberg lettuce in generally bite sized pieces with a few small vegetables pieces added.  The house dressing was good, but it was applied a bit too generously so that a liquid formed in the bottom of the bowl.  The Tataki Tuna was lightly seared around the edges before being sliced and served over a crispy bed of noodles (not sure, but maybe rice or glass noodles?) and dressed with a teryaki sauce and sliced green onions.  Very good and exactly what I was looking for in the dish.  The 2 nigiri added a bit of color to the platter when it arrived with my sushi.  One was a filleted shrimp over rice and the other may have been a length of crabstick secured to a ball of rice by a seaweed wrap.  Both were good with a bit of soy sauce.  The Eel roll was a 6-pc portion and drizzled with eel sauce for that sweet, salty, and savory combo taste.  Very good too!  Wait times between courses were minimal and even checkout was processed swiftly.   If you are going to have a franchise of a chain restaurant, this is the way to run it...good food, good service, clean space, nice ambiance.  Review #2534

I must say this is one impressive park!  It is well thought out having room for a huge playground, a splash park, an amphitheater (overlooking the lagoon), a prairie (restricted access), a woodland garden with trails, and plenty of parking!  There are multiple shelters near the playground and a larger shelter/pavilion with restrooms between the splash pad and playground areas.  Ramps grant access to the upper level towers of the playground equipment and the surface of the play areas is cushioned to reduce the risk of getting hurt from a fall/slip.    There is a paved trail that travels the west, south, and east perimeter of the park and more trails that weave through the park.  There is even a "Prairie Trail" that can be walked along the northern side of the park to the Monon Greenway and cross over into the Central Park East Woods which extends all the way to Westfield Blvd!  The only thing about the park that I didn't like was that you can't drive through the park and get to the east side of Central Park.  You have to exit the park and get there via Westfield Blvd.  The maps on the website don't show that the only road between the two parks is for authorized vehicles only.  p.s.  There is a skate park near the aquatic center that I completely missed seeing on my visit. So much to do!!  Review #942

I am generally not a donut fan.  I tend to go for the more fringe pastries that catch my eye.  So when I had a mid-morning craving, I decided to stop by this small shop in a strip mall on the southeast corner of County Line and Meridian (SR 135).  By the time I got there, there was only one case with choices left.  However, the options were quite varied, with donuts being one of the more picked over items.  What struck my eye immediately was how large the fringe pastries were.  I picked up an apple fritter that was probably 8" across.  They also have the "pine cone" which is shaped like a "Bloomin' Onion" of pastry.  Nearly 9" across, this one is definitely shareable and the protrusions make it easy to tear off bite sized bits.  I took it home and my wife thought it her favorite.  Lots of very rich icing coats the cone.  And even though these two items were large, none of the pastries I picked were over $1.75.  I didn't see prices listed on the display counter, so I don't know if I missed a price list in the shop.  The receipt didn't display names of the individual pieces, just the cost.    Overall, the pastries tasted fresh.  My only knock is that they were so sugary in taste that I could quickly reach my fill of sugar before being full from the pastry.    Review #459

I've noticed this tiny house next to the Monon many times.  It's brightly colored and I always see it when I look to make sure nobody is ready to cross 54th on the trail.  I hadn't noticed there was a tiny driveway with some parking between the house and the trail until last night, so I pulled in and grabbed a spot.  There is a tiny patio with a bench for visitors to sit and enjoy what they get inside.  The inside has a tiny lobby, so hopefully, you time it when there isn't much of a crowd.  There is a tiny display case of ice cream and sorbet, and a set of menu boards on the east wall that tells you about the types of items you can choose from or have made (sundaes, floats, etc.)  I sampled a couple of the choices:  A lemon cheesecake ice cream and a raspberry sorbet.  The ice cream was very tart that nearly gave me a "pucker punch".  I was expecting it to be a more subtle, complementary lemon flavor.    The sorbet was delightful with a fresh taste of the berries and became my order.  Very enjoyable on a warm 70+ temperature day.    Service was friendly and prompt.  Know that if you pull in the driveway, you will have to turn around to exit out onto 54th since there is no rear exit.  And as always, be careful if you have to head west so that you don't run over the trail folks!  Review #2434

I stopped by this park on Monday morning after having driven by it upon a number of occasions.  Not knowing much about this park before hand, I was pleasantly surprised to discover that there were several sections designed to appeal to different ages, and different uses.  The two I spent most time exploring were the children's playground area and the decorative bridge and amphitheater.  The playground had plenty of places for the kids to run and hide..and learn.  Each of the playground pieces had an information station that told about the piece.  I read several and was glad to see that they were concise and understandable so that even if a child wasn't able to grasp everything, at least the parent should!  There were tunnels, and places to play in the sand.  There were echo walls and a sundial.  The kids who were there were running and laughing and entertaining themselves while the parents were able to stop and relax.  I then walked over to the bridge called Campbell's Crossing.  Decorative fences depicting families on each end contained additional art work on the bridge.  Beds of flowers and shrubs and grasses softened the cold stone/concrete of the bridge.  At the southern end, a pergola shelters the statues of the founders of the park, Jesse and Beulah Cox.  Their figures overlook a cascading water feature that descends into an amphitheater.   All the grounds were beautifully maintained and made me appreciate that someone had the forethought to set aside this space as neighborhoods and businesses spring up farther into the countryside.  I can see this place being useful for special outdoor events and concerts, and everyday use for long walks and letting children play.  Review #152

Quick comments:  Really tasty food.  Good beers but mostly IPA's and fruit based flavors.  I stopped in opening week and appreciated that there was some free lot parking to the west of the building.  I noticed as I entered that there were small tables for outside dining/drinking along the north and east walls.  Inside, the place is quite large and industrial looking.  The far south end has a brightly colored mural painted, while much of the walls are bare concrete blocks.  Some plywood was left exposed for making the booths as well.  Otherwise, there are numerous tables and some comfy seating for those who wish to play one of the many board games they have on hand.  My waitress welcomed me and let me know they have samples of their beers (free) as well as the option of getting a flight of four 6-oz pours (priced upon your selection.)  The flight appealed to me (I was able to add a 5th choice for an upcharge.)  I ordered a Fast Joe Burger which is a BMB (Big Mouth Burger) that requires some finesse to avoid wearing it.  I squished it down enough to get a good bite and was pleased with the flavor.  Think of it as a basic double cheese burger (loaded) but with beer based bacon jam for additional savory flavor.  I also ordered the Fall Bacon Sweet Potato Salad.  This looks a lot like what you would expect if you substituted sweet potatoes for reds, but the flavor took on an interesting roasted flavor from the strips of red bell pepper and the sliced green onions added to the basic recipe.  I was surprised that my meal was served with some tasty fries (thin, salted and with a hint of pepper).  I didn't order them, but my waitress told me they come with every burger.  It doesn't say so on the menu.  So, I would suggest to customers that they ask if the burgers include fries in the pricing.  I encourage the owners to let people know if the burgers know on the menu.  The house beers that I sampled were from a selection that was heavily weighted with IPA's and fruit based flavors.  They were good, but a bit of diversity in the beer lineup would be appreciated.  Review #3051

I stopped in just because I wanted a cup of coffee.  I noticed they had a "coffee order" place along the counter and after just a brief wait for the order ahead of me, got my order of black drip coffee. I gather that they change the flavor of the day and didn't mention what the flavor was, but it was deep and rich and only just a little too hot to drink right away.   Even though I got a little singe to my taste buds, the flavor was good and service was quick.  Review #2021

3.5 stars rating.  The service was really good.  The bartender was running the entire front end for the Sunday lunch crowd and she did a great job of keeping up and keeping us informed on our food progress.  The problem was that the food entrees were disappointing.  The breadsticks came out first as an appetizer (5 for $10).  Sure, they were on the high end of prices, but these were delicious and baked perfectly!  The cheese sauce that came with them was also quite good.  We were off to a good start!  My wife wanted the grilled chicken taco but not the taco shell, so they accommodated her request and put it on a plate.  It looked appetizing and had a nice amount of veggies to go with the chicken.  The problem was that the chicken was really dry.  I tried a bite and agreed with her assessment.  For my entree, I went with the Reuben and the Sidewinder fries as a side.  The fries were perfect!  Really liked those thick cut swirls of potato.  But the Reuben was disappointing.  First, the cheese they use had the same smell as the Kraft Parmesan cheese.  I know it was Swiss and tasted okay, it was just this musty smell every time I lifted the sandwich up to take a bite.  And the corned beef was just not cooked long enough.  I knew it was okay to eat since beef goes through the curing process, but the beef was tough and had no juice.  I've had really great Reuben style sandwiches at Turchetti's and the Bloomington Sandwich shop, so I know what a Reuben should/could be.  It wasn't a bad sandwich, just not anything I could recommend.  So, because the service was so good and the sides were excellent, I will round up to a 4 star.  But I would probably order something else the next time.  Review #1623

When I stopped by for lunch, I thought I would try something new.  So, when I saw they offered a BB-Cuban sandwich, that became my choice.  The sandwiches are made to order and within a few minutes, it was ready to go.  The BB-Cuban features pulled pork, sliced ham, bbq sauce, pickles, Swiss cheese, whole grain mustard and comes served on a Circle City Sweets bun.  They also offer coleslaw either on the side or on top.  Note that the coleslaw isn't the sweet kind; it's more tart/acidic, so my advice is to put it on top of the sandwich to blend the flavors.  Or, you can use one of the plastic forks to put a bit on each bite since this sandwich is THICK!  I had a hard time fitting the thing in my mouth and usually don't have problems.  So, you get your money's worth here! They also add some house chips on the side.  You can get your order to go or for dining in the upstairs seating of City Market.  They also have some sides and beverages available here, so you don't have to go to one of the other market vendors to fill out your meal.  My only negative was that there is a lot of grease that comes off the BBQ. My paper bowl was pretty coated on the bottom by the time I finished and I recommend grabbing one of the packaged hand wipes at the counter before dining so that you can clean your fingers.  (Not a major problem, just kind of messy.)  The flavor was good, but if you want, you can add more flavor options from the bottled sauces on the counter too.  Overall, a hearty lunch with good flavor.  I'd like to try the standard pulled pork and the brisket options in the future.  Review #2347

What I like about Crate & Barrel is that they have items for your kitchen AND your living space.  With so many open kitchens, sometimes it's better to be able to match colors, patterns, styles from room to room, so when I pick up something that may sit out on the counter or be visible, it's nice to know how it will look.  But even if you aren't coordinating, the staff was quite friendly and wanted to point out that they've added a kids section and a design section to the store.  Most of the downstairs seemed to concentrate on the kitchen items while the upstairs was for the living spaces.  I like when a shop arranges their furniture in groupings with accessories...it's great for ideas and possibilities I hadn't thought of.    The store has a lot of space and was uncluttered making for easy browsing.  That also allows them to have a large variety in store that you just don't see at some of the smaller boutiques.    Overall, I enjoyed my visit to the store and dealing with the employees.  Review #2189

If you live on the east side or downtown, it's nice to know you can check out a McNamara Florist in your area.  However, note that this is the prime warehouse location.  The building is huge, but most of it is off limits. However, there is a smaller store/showroom available on site.  I think it is surprisingly limited compared to the other McNamaras around the metro area.  First, getting here is a bit of a challenge if you aren't familiar with it.  If you take Mass Avenue northeast of downtown to 18th Street, turn north and go over the tracks to Ludlow (the first and only cross street).  Turn right and follow the signs to the entrance of the shop where there is plenty of parking in their lot.  Inside, there may or may not be anyone to greet you immediately.  A bell sounds to let the folks working in the warehouse/offices that someone has entered.  We were greeted and were encouraged to look around and ask questions if we had any.  The woman said to shop around and ring the bell on the counter if we needed anything, so she headed back to her regular job.    Since we were the only ones shopping on Small Business Saturday, I can see why she went back to her regular job.  I don't think they get that many customers.    I guess I don't understand why this shop is smaller.  The building is enormous and it seems like they could easily expand into an adjacent room with more items.  As is, it just can't compete with the other McNamaras around town.  Review #3364

4.5 Stars out of 5   Great tasting pastries, clean and open space to sit and eat donuts without being in your car, and friendly/helpful service.  After pulling into this location on the west side of the second building back in the plaza (north of Steak and Shake and next to Between the Buns), I popped into this roomy new bakery.  The selection isn't the largest, but everything I tried was fresh and really good.  Nothing stale.  Nothing skimped on.  Just really good flavor and satisfying.  They also offer drip coffee which a lot of bakeries don't, but I will say that it is served WAY TOO HOT.  (I drove to my hair salon, got a haircut, and the coffee was still hot 45 min after being served!)  I appreciate that they offer the coffee, but I want to be able to drink it with my pastries without scalding my tongue.  There seems to have been a change in hours from what Yelp has listed (I sent a request to update to Yelp HQ.)  That makes it a little confusing.  Safe to say that they aren't open passed noon, so if you are thinking about grabbing some on your lunch hour, go here first before grabbing a burger next door.  No long line at mid morning.  They accept credit cards.  Frankly, I can't see driving another 15 minutes to that "other bakery" on Southport Road when I can get what I want here and not have to stop at an ATM machine first.  Glad to have this new bakery on the south side!  Review #3158

The bakery is mostly a place for donuts, cookies, and some pastries.  Pretty standard fair with the exception that these taste fresh.  I've been to many bakeries and donut shops around the metro area and must admit that I didn't see anything here that had that "wow" factor...just plain and simple stuff.  I prefer pastries to donuts, so I did pick some Danish and a sampling of the cookies (they make theirs the soft and chewy variety, not the crisp or thick kinds.)  The flavors were fine.  Just nothing to get excited over.  It's nice that they have long hours and are open before and after work.  I was surprised when I saw the sign on the door that they are a cash and check only business.  I've seen other places do that unless the order was large, but it seems like an inconvenience to the customer to have to stop at an ATM if they need a large order.  The competition has gone tech, so I wonder how much business they are missing out on.  Oh well, if you are in the area and have some cash on you, stop by and support local to assuage your sweet tooth.  Review #1321

I stopped by for lunch and ordered a couple slices and an order of breadsticks.  The slices are huge (1/6th of a 20" pizza = 10" long and about 9" across!)  They have the pizza slices sitting out for you to select the type and then they do a quick reheat in the ovens to make sure it is warm when served.    After prepaying, I grabbed a seat in the dining room which looks bigger and cleaner than on my previous visit a few years ago.  It probably isn't any bigger, but it felt like there was plenty of room.  Before long, my order was ready and I went back to the counter to pick it up.  I grabbed some napkins and utensils in case I needed them from a counter to the left of the order window.  They also have a beverage dispenser to the right.  The slices were served individually on their own plates.  I started with a supreme pizza that I believe they call the Southside Special.  It comes with pepperoni, mushrooms, olives, onions and peppers.  After a quick dabbing with my napkin to get the excess grease from the top, I noticed the the green peppers and the onions were in large clumps.  The cook had sliced them, but not all the way across, so I had to manually separate the pieces and spread them across the pizza so that I could have some in each bite.  And when I tried to lift the pizza to eat it, the center was so soft that it drooped and spilled the topping onto the plate.  I understand they may want their pizza slices to be folded, but this was just soggy and disappointing.  Fortunately, the flavor was good.  If they could just crisp the crust a bit before so that centers got done, it would improve the customer satisfaction a star or two!  I moved on to the sausage and pepperoni slice and it was in better shape, but still had a lot of grease on top.  I guess I should have left it since the sausage was so mild that it barely had any flavor.  The pepperoni were okay and the crust had a nice crispness to the bite while still being able to fold it.    It is sad that a local restaurant can't get the consistency down so that customers want to keep coming back.  As it was served, the pizza wasn't any better than a reheated frozen pizza I can get at the store.  Sure, the portions are generous, but I will pay for better quality if I can count on it.  Review #2001

Although I have driven by this restaurant numerous times, somehow, it never really caught my attention.  Maybe a different, more enticing name would draw people in.  Maybe a higher profile store front other than a bland strip mall exterior would help.  And even those things don't fully explain how this place has missed my radar.  When I searched Yelp for restaurants in the area, this only popped up as the 71st option!  So, it wasn't just me.  What I will tell you is that if you want a good quality lunch with a number of recognizable/traditional food options, maybe an alcoholic beverage, and being able to sit outside under an umbrella, then this is the place to bookmark.  After grabbing free parking in the lot, I entered into a clean, but a little bit static restaurant.  Their dining area was near the front, bar area towards the back, and lots of windows brought in natural light from the front of the space.    I was greeted at the door and taken to a booth along the wall in the bar area.  I was immediately drawn to a salmon sandwich that comes on a brioche bun with lettuce, tomato, pickle chips, and a spicy tartar sauce on the side.  I also upgraded to include grilled asparagus as a side.  After a brief wait, my meal arrived.  I built the sandwich that was quite tasty.  The portion was just right for lunch and the salmon was cooked to the proper temp for my selection.  The asparagus had a grilled/char taste that I really like.  Overall, a really delicious lunch.  Checkout went smoothly too.  So, if you like a quick meal, but not fast food, give Smee's a try.  Review #2808

During 2018, I am trying to get back to at least one restaurant per month that I used to enjoy, but for some reason, hadn't been back to in a long time (a decade or more.)  So when I saw an UYE at Shapiro's, I knew that I had to stop in.    The place is much as I remembered it:  plenty of parking on the outside; lots of tables for groups or families; well lit interior; and a cafeteria line like I used to go through at school, but with food I actually looked forward to eating!  And for as many folks who were dining there, a relatively quiet atmosphere, great for conversations.    Although the line nearly reached the entrance, it moved efficiently well and soon I was standing before cases of desserts, followed by cool sides, then progressing on to entrees and warm sides before reaching the cashier.  Behind the numerous staff working the line is a menu board to help you make your decision while you approach.  If you want a beverage, they are around the corner (self serve) where they also have "to go" boxes available (great idea!!).  Once you have your food, you are free to pick out you own spot.    I was there to meet some fellow Yelpers and we got to meet one of the 4th generation family members (Sally Keck Shapiro) who spent time with us filling us in on the family/deli's evolution through the changing restaurant scene in the 100+ year history of the business.  It's great to see a family owned business succeed and have such devoted followers.    Oh, and lest I forget, the food was delicious!  The Brooklyn Pastrami on rye (baked in house from a recipe a former neighboring business passed along to them) with Swiss and a bit of spicy mustard was loaded!  I couldn't get over how much meat was on the sandwich (served halved).  A tasty pickle spear was included with the sandwich too.  I also ordered the chilled mustard potato salad that had just enough kick and the spice worked really well with the sandwich.     "Cook Good; Serve Generously; Price Modestly; People will come."  That was the founder's motto and it still holds true today.   Sometimes, you just shake your head trying to figure out why it takes so long to get back to a place that is so good.  I'll be sure it won't take nearly so long for my next visit.  Review #826

Although this place is literally known for their meatball combinations, I decided to go with something different on this visit (I have been to the Mass Ave location previously).     I decided to go with their Skuna Bay Salmon with Honey Garlic Glaze.  It comes with a side salad topped with a sweet vinaigrette and a choice of a side.  I picked the Mac n Queso though I was surprised it was definitely shareable in size.  The salmon was uniformly light pink throughout and easily flaked even though they managed to put a light crispness to the top.  The glaze, which was served on the side, added a nice complementary flavor depth to the salmon.  I even added what I didn't use on the salmon to the mixed greens of my salad.  I enjoyed both.    The mac was actually made with larger noodles (penne) and served in the light queso sauce with a bit of gooey cheese on top.  It was fine, but was rather bland, so it didn't do much overall for the meal.    The restaurant is on the south side of the mall in the food court and is accessible from both the court and the exterior.  Parking is free, but how close you get is dependent upon how busy the mall is in general.  The interior of the restaurant is tastefully elegant and is a place you could as easily dress up for as going casual.    I was greeted at the door for seating and had fine service throughout the meal.  Note that water is served via a chilled bottle that is brought to your table right after being seated.  No ice is included and self-serve on filling/refilling as needed.  Overall, it was a fine meal with good service and flavor.  They do more than meatballs here!  Review #3615

Although I am no longer a collector, I still enjoy checking out comic shops when I find them.  This may be the largest comic shop I've found so far!  Lots of well organized/neat rows of merchandise, many reaching higher than my head, make it easy to find sections of interest.  One of the things that make this place great is that with enough room, they are able to place recent issues behind the most current release, so if you find a title you want and it's on issue #5, there is a good chance that they will have copies of #1-4 right behind it!  Very nice!  It took me awhile to figure out the sorting.  My first impression was that it was sorted by comic company (DC, Marvel, other) but the more I explored, I found independent comics also and it was alphabetical.    They also have gaming rooms in the back and low stacks of older comics, though that section wasn't as well stocked as some places I've been.  Their collection of graphic novels was huge, so that is a definite benefit too.  They also have some merchandise, but I didn't think it was as diverse and large as some I've been to.  Still, there is a good chance they will have something you are looking for.  Overall, an impressive place to check out comics if you are the kind of reader who is a collector.  It will be interesting to see how the online services for digital libraries impact this business.  Review #3700

When I go into a restaurant for the first time, I set my expectations upon the style of restaurant and the ratings everyone else has given it.  So, I had some pretty high expectations with the lofty rating that Samano's had.  When I give a five star, that means my expectations were clearly exceeded.  Such was the case here.  After parking (there is a parking garage as part of the complex or a lot across the street), I entered into a somewhat expected vibrantly colored dining room.  But instead of being overwhelmed by images packed too close together and every color in the rainbow, this place is tastefully done in reds and oranges with dark accents.  There is a large mural in black and white on the west end of the dining room too.  It looks more upscale.  When you walk in, the order counter is directly ahead and while there, you order, pay, and are given a number to take to your table/bar stool to wait.  They do have self serve soda machines where you will also find your utensils and other items.  Napkins are dispensed at every table.  For lunch, I decided to go with a couple taco options and a side of beans.  The Spicy Grilled Chicken taco was served on double 5" soft corn shells.  The chicken wasn't particularly spicy, but was diced into small cubes along with the onions.  I added a squeeze of lime juice and was very pleased with the overall flavor. (That's significant because my palate is more geared towards flour tortillas than corn).    What really blew me away was the pastor offering, the "Marinaded" Pork.  Instead of what I expected, this took on a Hawaiian flavor with grilled pineapple in with the spiced meat.  Delicious! It came served on a single 5" shell and though I wanted to savor the flavor, I devoured it.  Just enough onion and cilantro and a spritz of lime juice made for a great combo.  Instead of the rice and beans, I simply ordered the beans which arrived in a small bowl and looked like soup.  However, there was just enough liquid to cover the beans.  Make no mistake, the cup was mostly beans, but just enough of the tasty liquid to make you wonder if they might not make a yummy soup option.  The only negative I experienced was that when I arrived around 1 pm, there were a few tables that hadn't been cleaned and some ingredients had fallen to the floor.  I was about to mentally knock a point off, but before long, one of the guys in the back came out to start cleaning.  I also realized some of the messes were by patrons still seated, so it wasn't the business's fault that they hadn't cleaned.  Who likes somebody sweeping right next to them?  It appears from the menu that they have a lot to offer beyond the tacos listed first.  With such a positive first visit, I would gladly return to taste some more!  Review #2499

What a great setting to enjoy a beverage before an evening event downtown!  The second floor cocktail bar is located within the Hyatt Place that newly opened on Pennsylvania across from the Fieldhouse.  After climbing a stairway surrounded by art installations (elevators are just beyond), the bar is located to the left of the check-in counter.    During the day, the space is open and anyone can walk around to check out the stylish bar area.  What is very cool is walking out onto the balcony that provides an elevated view of the fieldhouse and the surrounding downtown area.  There is a fire pit for when the weather gets chilly.    Once the bar opens at 3 p.m., it becomes a 21+ space only, so don't bring your kids before a Pacer/Fever game.    I sat at the bar in the early afternoon and had a very pleasant experience.  I ordered one of the house drinks, a "Cool as a Cucumber" cocktail that was delicious.  Count on prices to be on the higher end as you would expect from a business located within a hotel.  The bartenders were pleasant and prompt.  Parking in the area is always a challenge, especially on game nights.  There are a few pay street parking spots on the alley between Penn and Meridian.  I simply chose to park in the mall garage ($3 for 3 hours) and walk the block to the bar to avoid driving around looking for a spot.  This is a great location and should become even better in a few years when the new plaza goes in across the street, north of the fieldhouse.  In the meantime, enjoy the elevated view and the cocktails.  Note:  They do offer a limited meal selection though they shouldn't call it Lunch and Dinner when they clearly don't open in time for lunch.  Review #2714

I went on a Monday evening and found the place was fairly busy, even before 6!  I had my concerns after all the negative comments in the early weeks about delays, but let me address some issues first before I talk food.  #1- Long delays - The owner heard the complaints and the chef has been removed.  A new kitchen manager will start this week.  I caught them in transition and there was a mistake on my order, but the manager had the young man doing the cooking come out and listen to my comments (i.e. not all the ingredients were on the burger).  We agreed on the solution and I was happy with that.  From the time I placed my order until the time it was in front of me was about 15 minutes.  A steady stream of platters were coming out of the kitchen while I was there.  #2 - Inattentive management - The owner didn't know me, but came by and introduced himself and told me that if there was anything he could do to make my evening better, to let him know.  After my meal arrived, he came by again and that's when I mentioned the missing ingredients (I had let the bartender know first and maybe she signaled the owner...not sure.)  Anyway, it was a teaching moment for the kitchen and I was adult about letting him know of the problem.  We resolved the problem calmly and to my satisfaction.  He genuinely seemed interested in helping.  Okay, since this is a Scottish bar, I thought I would treat myself to a Rob Roy cocktail ($8 for standard house cocktails).  Not overly garnished, there was enough booze to give it some kick, but not too much to be aggressive.  The bartender did a fine job (covering the waitressing part of the job too.)  Continuing the Scottish theme, I went with the Robert the Bruce burger which is listed as having the burger, spicy pepper jack, sauteed onions and mushrooms, peppers, and romoulade.  Mine was missing the peppers and romoulade, so it was on the bland side.  It definitely was better after the adjustment.  I also got a small fry which comes with a choice of seasoning or sauce, so I went with the Garlic Parmesan seasoning.  They were fine and maybe just a bit more garlic flavored than I would prefer, but that's just me.    Overall, I got the impression that the management was making adjustments to correct the early flaws.  The restaurant definitely had a cool vibe with lots of sports on the numerous screens but the volume was down on them so that conversation was still possible.  Note:  They have a nice area for dining when the nicer weather finally arrives!  Review #2285

I took my wife to this new restaurant on Main Street and thought they had done a lot of things right.  I was a bit disappointed in the flavor, but I think there was a reason.  I'll get to that soon.  The restaurant is just east of the Arts District and kudos to them for having a small lot on their east side and a public lot directly north of the building without having to cross a street.  That is very helpful!  The place looks really cool too.  There is a large pergola covered patio and the tables have large umbrellas that with their ability to be tilted by the staff, did a pretty good job of keeping us comfortable dining outside even when it was nearing 90!  The staff was also very helpful.  Kind of a team concept and doors where held open for us and water was kept filled.  We were able to get our beverages and place our order promptly.  And when the food arrived, the orders were very generous is size.  My wife ordered Mae Mae's Meatloaf and it had probably two cups worth of meat!  There were also real mashed potatoes (with some chunks left) and a combo of collard and turnip greens that had a bit of seasoning (probably 1.5 cups worth!)  So, a lot of food.  My wife had to be coaxed to come her so I could try it, so it wasn't a big surprise to me she wasn't a fan of the greens.  I tried them and thought they were pretty good.  I ordered the salmon and it also was a large portion with a tasty coconut rice, citrus black beans, some buttery asparagus, and pickled red onion.  I was eating it and just thought it seemed lacking in flavor.  The salmon was cooked through, but not dry.  It just tasted like plain salmon.  I finished eating it with bites of my sides and it wasn't until I got home that I remembered it was supposed to have a chili lime butter.  So one of two things happened:  either they only add just a minimal amount, or they forgot it completely.  I couldn't taste it.  If I would have made the connection (they take away the menus when you order), I would have said something to give them the opportunity to fix it.  So, I will give them a 4 instead of what I was initially thinking was a 3 star meal.  Maybe the owner will read this and be able to tell if the chili lime flavor was there.  I just couldn't taste it.  We ended up getting a to go box for my wife's meal and got a round of Key Lime cake that was quite good (to go too!)    So, generous portions at the $15-25 range for entrees.  Hopefully they will dial in the flavors of the food as it goes out to customers.  Review #3050

My wife and I stopped by for a carryout lunch.  We noticed that there is some outdoor seating for warmer weather, but inside, there really aren't dining tables, just benches.  Over in the bar area which is 21+ only, there seemed to be a few small tables, but during Covid, everyone is expected to grab and go.  They do have menus at the counter to look at and the staff were really courteous and helpful.  To the right of the order counter is a small display of the days sweets.  We were focused on lunch, so I got a Chicken Salad Sandwich and my wife ordered a breakfast sandwich with egg&sausage.   I upgraded my sandwich to be served on a really tasty croissant.  The chicken salad was a little dry when served on the croissant.  Not sure if it was a bit overcooked or just needed a little more mayo/salad dressing to make it more appealing.  It's a fine line because if it gets too moist, the croissant would lose it's crispy flakiness, so have an idea if you are going to eat it right away or leave it in a to go box for a ride home to eat.  The flavor was good, just need to solve the moisture problem.  My wife liked the flavor of the breakfast sandwich with cheddar and sausage.  She thought the egg was overcooked, but otherwise the rest was fine.   One thing I really appreciated was that my order of a house coffee (served straight) was hot, but not scalding.  I could drink it promptly after ordering it.  My pet peeve is coffee served too hot.  This had good flavor and helped with the flakiness of my sandwich.  They also serve alcohol but I didn't explore those options during my morning visit.  This place just opened in Oct 2020 (I believe that was when) and they are hopeful  that the warmer weather will continue to allow them to fine tune their dining experience.  The place was clean and because of the carry out service, there was no issue with social distancing.  Review #3851

I found this Michaels to be arranged very similar to the one in Castleton, so I assume this is the standard layout for most of the franchises.  (I think the one on the south side is a little different, but similar.)  So, I was able to find my way around the store to the areas of interest quickly.    I was also pleased that this location had lots of staff working the floor during my visit, so if I had any questions, there were plenty of people to ask.  The staff here wasn't as outwardly friendly as the Castleton location, but there wasn't anything negative in my visit.  The store was clean, orderly, and well stocked...pretty much what you would want from a hobby and craft store.  Review #3682

I really enjoyed my first visit to Boyden's.  I'm more of a pie than a cake guy, so seeing a large variety of fruit Danish right as I entered the door was great sign.  The staff was friendly and I was able to get my order promptly.  They have a nice variety of pastry options and have a limited amount of coffee available too.  The Danish have a light texture and the icing is very sweet.  They also have a fair amount of fruit filling, more than I have found in most bakeries.  Review #1972

This garden center nursery has been a staple on the south east side of Indy for a long time.  Although it is quite a distance from our home, my wife and I were on a road trip and were searching for some specific plants to grow along our new trellis.    The folks here had a great supply of plants and were quite pleasant.  Not only did they have a wide assortment of colors and types of plants for my wife to choose from, but she was also able to pick up some bird seed and some top soil which the staff helped her load (she knew I could unload it once I got home!)    Good selection and good service makes for a good rating.  It has easy access off Emerson to the Interstate (465) so even though the distance was a little farther than we would normally consider, the drive was easy and pleasant (as long as you avoid rush hour.)  Review #3769

I've been here a few times, and though I haven't shopped here on a "regular" shopping day, I have stopped in when in the area and picked up a few things so that I wouldn't have to make a special stop elsewhere.  They have convenient parking (rare near Mass Ave) for up to 2 hours.    Inside, they have most of the departments that the big box stores have for groceries:  Deli, cheese, sushi, produce, salad bar, and the standard boxed goods.  Note that there is also a small pastry shop on the Alabama Street side where you can get some additional goodies/lunch.  I just needed a couple items and so I was able to quickly find those and go through the self checkout.  It wasn't too hard to figure out and soon I was on my way.  They don't have all the options that the giant stores have, but they have the basics covered here and for most things, you can pick them up without having to go to the suburbs.  It will be interesting to see how this franchise fares now that there are more options popping up downtown.  Review #3756

Overall, we had a good impression of the Good Feet Store.  We had stopped by here about a year ago and because of my wife's (then) recent hip surgery, they let us know that they couldn't help us until she had more time to recover.  Once stabilized, they could then proceed to a fitting.  Note that we had been to visit the insurance approved doctor who was getting paid hundreds of $ to simply glue attachments to the bottom of your own shoes!  Ridiculous!  So, my wife had made due with "home improvements" to her inserts until enough time had passed and she was getting more problems.  So, we recently returned.  This time, we were able to go through their house program which she will continue expanding over the next couple weeks until she can max out the times on the different inserts.    Basically, they take an imprint of how your striding foot contacts the ground.  Ideally, your entire foot should make an impression with the exception of the inner arch area.  What we saw was the foot that was giving the most pain in her hip was very irregular on weight distribution.    So, the person who was helping us went into the back to grab a box of three types of inserts that are worn during their process (individually, not stacked.)  The idea is to reshape the bottom of the foot over time to force the placement to be redistributed more evenly.  Honestly, I don't know if they match the inserts to what your foot is doing or if it is a one style fits all, but they do match the inserts to your shoe size and then work with explaining what each is meant to do and give you a schedule for how long to wear each insert per day.  They also stress NOT to walk around without shoes/inserts as that undoes the benefits.    So, my wife is early in the process and I hope that getting a regular stride that makes her foot strike properly will help ease the discomfort she experiences.  I strongly believe in body alignment and letting the body work properly (shoulders should be level, feet should face forward at all times, strides should be long and steady, etc.)  I've been alive over 60 years and learned about proper mechanics about 40 years ago and have hardly ever had aches and pains and have never needed a message or chiropractor.  I hope that the process the folks at this store help bring some of that relief to my wife.  It would be worth the price.  Review #3416

If you are taking the time to read my review, be sure to check out the photos of this place.  The upstairs lounge has a speakeasy feel with overstuffed couches, lots of wood, a faux fireplace.  It is beautifully done for a space that was hurriedly put together due to the fire at the Irvington location at the end of 2019.    Contrast the beauty of the interior with the almost hidden entrance (look for the wooden crow over the door in the alley to the west of the City Market.)   Other than the crow and a small, free standing sign, there isn't much attention being called to the Loft.  The owners intentionally wanted this place to have a somewhat secretive entrance to be reminiscent of the way speakeasies were a hundred years ago during Prohibition.    When I found the right door, I entered a stairwell that looked like the place was going to be condemned.  But then I noticed the Black Acre sign at the top of the stairs.  The contrast between the stairwell and the Loft is dramatic!  There are two rooms:  The bar area has lots of comfy furniture to the right while the bar is on the left.  A second room with more tables is beyond the barroom.  I was greeted and immediately served at the bar.  I went with a flight which you can order as many small sized drinks as you desire and priced accordingly.  I went with my usual four and really enjoyed them.  I had a funky farmhouse ale (Storm of Memories), a stout (Widower's Debauchery), and a couple IPA's (TV Wolf and No New Money).  I liked all that I tasted.  Note that Greek's pizza occupies the space below the Loft, so you can get food from Greek's menu by ordering at the bar.  Surprisingly, even though Greek's isn't open as a business on weekends, they will make food for the Loft customers.  I hadn't realized that before arriving.  Great bartender (Lindsey) and great space with an unusual mix of tunes playing in the background.  Since I went around lunch time on a Saturday, I don't know if it gets loud or crowded.  But when I went, it was just a cool place to hang out and chat.  Parking is always a challenge downtown, but I found metered street parking on the other side of the City Market.  Review #3685

Nestled in a corner of what seems like a private strip mall (it houses Northside Social on one side and the Northside Nook on the other), there is convenient access and parking from College and 65th.  The space has a counter near the entrance and the rest of the room is made up of 2 and 4 seat tables where you are supposed to wait to be seated.  I opted for a 2-top and was glad to be seated away from the cold air near the entrance.  Service was attentive without being intrusive.  The only negative was that when I ordered a half sandwich and a side salad, with an additional cup of soup, all were brought at the same time.  I would have preferred being given the option to have either the soup or the salad ahead of time.  As far as the food, I ordered the Crusty Grilled Four Cheese sandwich which was quite crispy; the bread much darker browned than I've had elsewhere.  Although there was plenty of cheese inside and it was mostly melted, there wasn't much flavor.  Maybe a bit of butter on the grill instead of oil would have elevated the flavor which was pretty much monotone in flavor without any condiments.   The side was made up of colorful greens and diced veggies.  All were quite fresh.  However, I ordered a raspberry-honey vinaigrette and was brought out a yellow, almost watery dressing.  I didn't notice it before the waiter left the table, so I decided to go with it.  Surprisingly, there was a lot of flavor in the dressing despite its liquidity.  It complemented the salad greens and saved what could have been a disappointment.    The highlight of the meal was the soup of the day, a Lobster Chowder.  The flavor was rich with lobster flavor though there weren't any large chunks.  The soup was served hot and had chunks of red potato as the most noticeable accompaniment of the lobster flavor.  Good taste!    It appears that they get a good deal of carryout business as well as dine in.  They open early and also have breakfast options available even through the lunch period.  It was an enjoyable lunch, but didn't have any "wow" moments.  Review #486

I convinced my wife to make a drive downtown to Tech 16 so that we could try some of the new places inside the AMP.  We have been watching it via its website and this was our third visit.  Since it was approaching lunch time, we each picked a spot that appealed to us and I selected Azucar Morena, a Venezuelan inspired restaurant.  It can be found on the north end of the AMP (near the stage and restrooms)  The business opted for one of the finished restaurant stalls as well as the standard transport stalls, so there appears to be lots of room for the staff to set up a food line.  The order counter is about midway along their space and has an information board nearby on how to order an Arepas that you pick the items.  I decided to play it safe and go with one of the predetermined combinations which was called the Reina Pepeada which means "Curvy Queen".  The sandwich is served on a rounded white cornmeal biscuit with shredded chicken breast, cilantro and avocado as the primary flavors.  The selection came with a side.  I opted for the house pico de galo which I then added as it fit onto the sandwich.  Really yummy and I found that the chicken, though only lightly seasoned, was good.  I picked a sweetened tea which was huge as my beverage.  They have a lot of juices available too, but decided to try those on another visit.  The sandwich flavors are mild so very approachable to someone unfamiliar with the cuisine.  No "heat" worry here.  The wait time was about ten minutes, so not too bad.  They give you a number with your receipt so you need to stay fairly close to hear them call it out so you can pick up your order.  Once you get it, you can sit anywhere in the AMP.
