Try something different today and give Azucar a try!  Review #3934

The more I try poke, the more I am glad we are getting these businesses all around town.  If you haven't tried poke before, it is a "build your own bowl" of Hawaiian origin that emphasizes fresh and healthy options to build your meal.  Located at the top of the stairway on the southeast corner of City Market, Poke Guru has a food stand that you start by picking your bowl size, then whether you want greens, white rice, or brown rice as a base.  Next, you decide if you want a protein (they come plain or marinated), and then work your way down the line adding toppings.  Finally, they have a variety of sauces to have added to your bowl.  They also have some beverages in the cooler to your left as you pay.  Note that the toppings get added in sections that may or may not overlap.  If you want a bit of avocado along with your cucumber or Korean radish, you will have to use your wooden spork or chopsticks to mix them yourself.  I went with a marinated ahi tuna with a teriyaki sauce over my toppings.  Very fresh, colorful, and best of all, tasty.    Service was prompt and friendly.  It isn't the cheapest meal you'll find downtown, but it is reasonably priced considering how fresh the ingredients are.  Review #3207

I enjoy checking out small, independent bookstores to see what they have that allows them to compete with the big stores and online sellers.  This shop is not a place to go for the latest trending books.  Instead, it's where you search for that book you read as a child or the classic that may be an early edition.  Whatever it is, somehow they manage to keep going.    Not only do they have sections that you will find elsewhere (fantasy, fiction, children's, etc) but they also have groupings/collections that make it easy to pick up multiple titles in the same vein.  I noticed a section devoted to Dickens, one for the Wizard of Oz, and another for the Winnie the Pooh books.  There are also groupings of local authors too.  I didn't see any big black dog on my visit, not sure if that's still possible, but the dog bowl of water is still out front and there were some play toys on the floor in the main room, so maybe I just missed the dog on my visit.    Anyway, the store is one where you can browse and if you are lucky, find something that you won't find at those big places that are interested in the latest hot item.  Review #2216

My wife and I met my son's family for brunch on Saturday around 10 a.m.  The restaurant, located in a strip mall looked to be quite busy by the look of the parking lot.  Upon entering, we realized that the waiting area was much too small for busy times, but we were able to get our name on the waiting list.  Much to our surprise, the restaurant did a great job of getting the crowd seated inside the restaurant and we were taken to our table after about a ten minute wait. They have some lobby seating available, but it gets a little congested with people waiting to pay (one register) and people waiting to get their name on the list.  Other than the congestion at the front, everything else with the brunch went smoothly.  Everyone ordered something different, with some even making special requests.  I went with the Original Eggs Benedict which comes with hash browns but allows for home fries to be substituted.  I stayed with the hash browns and was glad I did.  I love the flavor of warm egg yolks running into my hash browns.  Real comfort food!  The Canadian bacon was tasty but could have been served a little more generously...Hard to see under the poached eggs.  Basically, you get a sliced English muffin (both halves), each topped with the Canadian bacon and a poached egg.  The hollandaise sauce was thick and rich and elevated the biscuit flavor along with the rest of the hash browns.  Overall, I highly recommend this option.  The coffee was rich and hot, but not scalding, so I was able to enjoy it right away.  I prefer it black, but they do have creamers and hazelnut flavor additives as well as a variety of sweeteners.  I hate coffee that is served piping hot and scalds my taste buds....maybe a certain chain serves it so hot so you don't taste their food! (?)  Anyway, I found the service good-natured and welcoming without the condescending "sweetie" or term of endearment that some places have.  Our food was out quickly and our table was cleared with a minimum of interruption.    Overall, I would advise not to be scared off by a busy looking parking lot and entry.  We received a quality product with a reasonable price.   Review #242

I rarely eat fast food because a: I like supporting local, and b: I prefer eating something that is more healthy.  But for Captain D's, I decided to step out of my boundaries and give them a try.  I have lived on the south side for nearly 20 years and something about this place keeps it going despite the difficulty getting into the parking lot (more later).  It appears to be the only one of this chain in the metro area (according to the website locator).  Yet the ratings stay high while many other fast food places get poor ratings.  So, I stopped in for lunch.  Okay, if you are heading southbound on the divided highway US 31, you can pull right into the lot which has a loop around the building for drive through service.  But even the lot has a large dip for drainage.  However, if you are heading here from the south, you need to turn onto the side street before reaching it and then take a right onto another side street that has sandbox sized potholes by the lot which you have to navigate around.  And getting out of here, you have to head south and turn at the stop light to get headed back to the north.    So, I took the side street route to get here and found some parking, entering on the highway side.  The place has a clean dining room at the entrance with the order counter on the back left.  The menu is listed overhead and when you are ready, place your order.  I was surprised at how quickly my order came forward form the kitchen in the back.  I hadn't even finished paying yet (they don't make you sign your receipt here even though it says Merchant's Copy....I asked) when my tray arrived with Fish and Fries.  I was given a cup for my beverage to fill at the station to the right.  I also stopped to get some sauces including ketchup and tartar sauce.  Unlike their nearest competitor in the industry, I didn't find malt vinegar anywhere.  I had also been given a wrapped plastic fork at the counter to use.    I was pleasantly surprised that the fries were really long and still hot and had already been salted.  Very nice!  And the fish (2 pcs) were long and crisped though once cut, the breading sometimes fell off from the steam of the fish.  Again, the fish was good without any "fishy" scent.  That's a good sign!  The plate also came with a couple hush puppies.  Overall, I would say that if you are a fan of this type of meal, the quality is as good as any fast food place I've been.  Now, if they could just do something about the parking lot.  Review #3521

Although I didn't make a purchase on my visit, I was pleased with the quality of home decor and furniture I saw in the store.  There was no hassle but plenty of staff on hand if I had a question.  The store was set up with many "rooms" of arrangements and then shelves of accessories along the side walls.  I liked the openness of the store which allowed me to wander without feeling like I was tripping over displays or other customers.  Review #2187

If you like relaxing in a dark lounge, not too noisy, but not too quiet, then stop by the Ball & Biscuit.  After taking photos for the Arts Council, I found myself downtown and saw the opportunity to finally stop by here.  I grabbed some metered street parking on Vermont and walked the short distance down Mass Ave to the shop.  I noticed they have patio seating, but being a cool day in Autumn, decided to go inside.  They have a couple seating areas, the one by the front window was much brighter.  I was by myself and decided to grab a spot at the L-shaped bar.  The menus for food and drinks were already on the counter, so I leafed through and decided to order the Cuban Pork Belly Sliders and the Pearl Jam Cocktail.  The bartender was on the quiet side, but quickly brought a water and then made the cocktail.  Served with a slice of orange, the drink uses Pearl Plum vodka, Falernum (a spiced syrup), and Ruby Red grapefruit juice.  Delicious!  Not too strong, but not watered down either.  Really good!  Note that the price was $12 which isn't out of line for downtown.  Before long, my three sliders arrived with sweet pickles on the side, on a bed of arugula.  The taste was really good, especially with the arugula added to the sliders.  They also had a crispy toasting on the buns that added an unexpected crunch to the bite.  The only negative was that when I first bit into the sliders, there was so little meat that I thought that they may have brought me the wrong dish.  Even though there was very small portions of meat, the flavor was still excellent.  But when you are charging $13 for three small sliders, you can't skimp on the meat.  Check out was quick and overall, I enjoyed my meal and drink.  Review #3282

I really like coming to this Stout's Footwear (formerly New Balance) store.  I have learned so much and found the staff to be very helpful.  Here's some reasons why: 1.  I assumed my feet stayed the same size.  They measured my feet and because they had flattened over time, I went from wearing a size 10 1/2 to a 12.  Talk about improving my comfort!  2.  I had intentionally bought shoes a little small because I have those type of heels that shoes  slide off the back.  When I mentioned it, they showed me how to tie the Runner's Tie on my athletic shoes and eliminated the problem.  3.  I used to run a lot, but switched to walking to ease stress on my old bones.  I assumed I needed a walking shoe.  But when I talked about the quantity of steps I was taking, they directed me back to something closer to a running shoe support which made a big difference in my comfort.  4.  I used to buy shoes when they started to look worn on the outside, never really thinking about the inside.  When I was suffering from arch pain, they taught me that every day shoes wear out faster on the inside where the arch support is needed.  So, ever since I started buying new shoes every six months (regardless of how good they may have looked on the outside), I have not had any arch pain or ankle pain where my old running fracture had been.  I mark the 6 months on my calendar to remind me.  Being pain free is worth the cost of a pair of new shoes.  Sure, the New Balance line is on the expensive side for someone like me who is retired, but they tend to have special sales and/or coupons for discounts if you watch for them.    Gone are the days when new shoes had to be "broken in" to feel right.  Now, I wear my new shoes right out of the store.   Review #637

Wow!  What a wonderful addition to the metro west side!  Although it isn't the easiest shop to see, this little candy shop is worth taking a drive west of Avon towards Danville located in a small strip mall in another building next to Cabin Coffee Company.  The shop is on the south end of the building closest to the highway.  They even have a stop light to help you in and out of the access street (Main) to get back onto US 36!  Even though it was opening day, the shop wasn't too crowded and I liked that they had someone manning the front door so that you could walk right in (masks are preferred since it is food) and hand sanitizer is also available.  Fortunately, they have multiple samples of fudge in individual sealed cups for visitors to try.  I ended up trying a peanut butter fudge (very smooth and creamy) and a cookies and cream fudge that I also bought when I checked out.  To your right as you enter is a merchandise room.  To the left is where you find other candies like Pez. They also have individual chocolates in a display counter.  The check out is right in the bend of the service counter and one person handled all the money exchanges.  Other folks assisted in boxing your orders of fudge (using tools, not touching your purchase.)  If you walk straight into the shop, there are some more packaged candies ready for purchase including taffy, and my wife picked up a package of Milk Chocolate English Toffee w/Sea Salt.    Everyone there was friendly and helpful.  Each sample I tried (including the toffee which I didn't get to sample but ate a piece after purchase) was delicious.  They even have some sugar free candies too, but those aren't my style! ha!  As someone who has made fudge for nearly 40 years, I understand how time consuming and exact a science it is to get fudge to turn out this great.  It is extremely temperature sensitive.  I don't like grainy fudge and I don't like hard fudge (too much like rock candy).  But this stuff is great!  And for anyone who wants to complain that fudge costs $16 per pound, I question if you have ever made it yourself.  First I couldn't eat a whole pound in a week, so they serve it in smaller servings.  I got two kinds at a quarter pound each.  The ingredients alone are expensive and it isn't something you can ignore once you start it.  Before anyone complains about pricing, try making it yourself and see if you can make it turn out anything like fudge.  This place delivers a high quality product and saves you all the time and clean up for a very reasonable price.  They have lots of flavors available, so I can see making return trips to try other flavors.  I can imagine this place being really popular during the winter holidays when a few extra pounds help keep me warm!  Give this place a try!  Review #3781

As a somewhat frequent visitor to the AMP, I've been keeping an eye on this place because it looks so tempting!  My wife and I finally got to buy some treats now that they are open!  I've heard their cheesecake is really good, but both of us were smitten by the giant Granny Smith apples that are served like taffy apples, but the variety of flavors is wonderful.  I ordered a Pecan Caramel apple while my wife ordered a milk chocolate Turtle apple.  Each was served in its own container to make it easier to transport home.  The only 'negative' is that these are huge!  They are nearly impossible to bite into without knocking off some of the topping/nuts.  When we got home, we sliced them which made it much easier to enjoy the blend of flavors in each bite.  The apples grabbed our attention that we didn't really check out all the other goodies available.  My wife was interested to see if they had actual pies available but not at the moment.  They were out of one sort of apple combo and offered to make one for us if we could wait on it.  We made time!  Between this shop, Circle City Sweets, and Boba & Everything, you are sure to find something sweet to satisfy your cravings!  Fresh and crisp apples for our treat and excellent pairings of flavors.  Worth indulging on the price.  Review #3939

This is a nicely organized shop with primarily consignment furniture.  They do have some accessories like lamps and wall hangings, but the majority of space is furniture.  Like most furniture places, the items are packed pretty close together but with a little effort, you can get to all of them.  The shop is on the end of a strip mall, so there is lots of free parking and the site makes it easy to load any purchases you wish to take with you.  The staff were all busy helping shoppers, some making purchases, some loading stuff in their vehicles.  Seems like everyone was focused on the customers.  They do have several business spaces connected with the main purchase desk on the far west end.  Note that they encourage folks to browse and have free popcorn in the back in the show area behind the counter.  Review #2089

This nature park is so close to getting a five star rating that I hope a future visit will convince me to raise my evaluation.  There are a number of things I truly liked here.  First, there are well marked trails with a very readable map posted throughout the park showing where the trails wander and if you decide to change your mind, where the next branch is to alter your course.  For safety, there are signs with specific numbers posted so that in case of an emergency, you can use your phone to call 911 and give the specific location of the park to get help if needed.  As far as nature, as soon as I descended into Trail 1 I began hearing the sounds you only find in the countryside:  the flap of the pileated woodpecker and then the staccato tapping after landing; the higher pitched croaking of small frogs coming from a pond of still water surrounding a small island that has a man-made bridge for access; the rustling of leaves as squirrels and chipmunks scurry across the forest floor.  The park runs along a length of Eagle Creek, the actual creek that feeds into the reservoir.  I was surprised to see how large and full the creek was.  The recent rains had turned the water brown from the runoff and its rapid flow caused disturbance at every bend it encountered.  My hope is that some maintenance on the trails will take place soon.  There were a couple places where the flow of water had turned the walking paths into muddy stretches.  Maybe some well placed logs or stones could keep the casual hiker from returning with wet shoes and mud spattered clothes.  My biggest concern is for the stair steps on routes 1 and 3 due to safety.  Rail ties were used to secure even footing from the parking area down to the trail floor.  But erosion has caused the steps to pitch forward which could lead to a severe fall if the steps were wet or the visitors shoes were slippery from mud on the trail.   Be aware the rise and descent is not for the physically challenged.  Maybe a more sloping side to side descent could be built into the hillside to reduce the risk.  Review # 646

This is the fifth Thai food restaurant in Hendricks County that I've tried and overall, I will say that the food is tasty, the restaurant is more elegant, and the service was friendly.  However, I didn't catch them during the weekday lunch specials, so the servings AND the prices were higher than the other places.  Unless you get the weekday lunch special, the entrees are a la carte and I'm guessing, the servings are much larger (at least compared to the meals I've had elsewhere during their lunch specials.)  After parking behind the restaurant (no street parking is available, but a large lot and even a free parking garage are nearby), we entered through the back which you take several twists and turns to reach the front where we were greeted and seated.  We were taken to a booth though they do have some tables available too.  The booths are easy to get into, but sit back from the table which made us have to sit forward to comfortably eat.  Also note that there is a small step up into and out of the booth.  I forgot and nearly stumbled into the table next to me! Yikes!  I ordered a small bowl of Tom Yum soup when we placed our beverage order.  It took much longer to come out than I expected.  It was also much larger (maybe 2 cups?) than I expected for a small serving.  I got it with chicken and medium spiciness which was hot enough to feel the tingle in the back of my throat, but not so hot as to become uncomfortable.  The soup (lemongrass based) had large vegetable chunks as well as the slices of chicken and was very tasty.  I would definitely recommend it.  Our entrees started coming out after a longer expected wait.  First, my wife's Sweet & Sour Saute (pork/mild) came out.  The serving was large and came with a heart molded serving of white rice (just over a cup).  She seemed to like the flavor quite a bit and said the mild still had a lot of flavor.  After a couple more minutes, my grandson's Orange Chicken (w Rice) came out with my Pad See Ew (pork/medium).  The Pad See Ew was delicious and had the same level of heat as my soup, so I thought it really good.  My grandson ate some of his lunch but didn't finish; Unusual for a teenager.  I tried a taste of his chicken and found it was completely chewy from being over cooked.  If it had been me, I would have asked for a fresh batch, but since he hadn't mentioned and ate over half, I didn't think I should order more since my wife and I had already finished.    So, the flavor was good, the delays in the kitchen (time wise and not serving all entrees at the same time) could use some work, and if you are concerned about prices, go during lunch on a weekday.  If you don't mind the larger portions and prices, this is the most opulent Thai place in the area and would make for a nice date place.  Review #3736

I can't believe this was my first visit to this little shop on Madison.  I've been across the street at least a half dozen times, but had never made it in here.  I won't make that mistake again.  The business was a two-story house turned into a florists and home decor shop.  The front door is kept locked, so be sure you go around to the north side of the building to enter.  The main parts of the building within your sight lines is filled with home decor.  At the holidays, there was Christmas stuff from top to bottom!  Even upstairs they have a room with more items.  Behind the stairs is the cooler area for fresh flowers and to the left of the counter (seen as you enter) is more space for the employees to put together arrangements.  I decided to pass on fresh flowers and instead found a seasonal spray hanging on the wall with lots of festive ribbon and greenery.  It looks nice on my front door.  Very pleasant people to work with and a nice variety of items (and colors) to help you decorate.  Review #1912

My wife and I stopped in for a late lunch during the week and were pleased with our experience.  The shop has parking on three sides, so there were plenty of spaces.  We entered from the west entrance which is where you will find the order counter and where folks who are getting their orders "to go" wait for their food.  The order area isn't much wider than a hallway, so it is a little hard to read the overhead menu, but fortunately, they have printed menus on the counter.  We decided to get our order for dining in, so my wife ordered a chicken burrito.  I ordered a pair of Asada (beef) tacos and an Elote.  The tacos were the small 5" shells made of corn and doubled so that the contents stayed inside.  Note that they don't come with any sauces, so you will have to add some from the dispenser bottles at the pick-up counter.  The Elote was a large ear of corn covered with a mix of mayo, chili powder and Cotija cheese.  It was steaming hot when served so it took a little wait to be able to enjoy it.  However, it tasted really good and I would gladly recommend it.  Note that I didn't see it listed on the menu, but asked and they had it.  My wife thought her burrito was fine.  It was a huge rolled serving that was halved by the kitchen.  She liked it, but as served, could have benefited from a sauce.  She ended up taking half of it home.  The dining area is where the south and east parking lot customers enter, so we got a bit of chill each time someone came in that way.  There is a station for customers to clear their own tables when finished.  Overall, good tasting Mexican food at a reasonable price.  Wait times were short.    Review #3727

On a cold and snowy night during the brewery's first week, with construction all around the place making it difficult to park, I still had a great time at Ellison Brewing!  Despite the challenges, the staff were in good spirits and welcoming.  The crowd was light early in the evening, so I was greeted and helped immediately!  The brewery is the first expansion out of state (Michigan) for this company.  It's located in the former Tow Yard location where Meridian Street angles to become Madison just south of South Street.  Fortunately, they have been told that the road construction should end in about a week, so that will open up access to more parking in the area.  At the time of my writing, there were a few spots along Pennsylvania and a pay lot just north of the business with access off South Street.  Inside, there is a seating area with its own bar to the right as you enter from the elevated entrance on the west end of the building.  There is another bar with seating on the left by the brewing tank area.  That leads back to the second seating area with a view of the kitchen and away from any potential drafts from the entrance.  I chose to order directly from the bar in the first seating area (they do have table service, but I thought I would be more direct.)  I usually order flights of five ounce drinks.  Here, there is no set number in the flight.  All the tap beers were $2 (very good price!) per shorty.  (Note that you can get samples before ordering as well.)  Although they had nine beers to choose from, they had a really nice mix of ales represented.  I started with the Amber Ale (4.7%) which was full of flavor and had a surprisingly darker color than most I've tried.  Full bodied with a very approachable taste.  A great starter!  I moved on to Crescent Fresh IPA (6.2%).  Normally, I don't drink IPA's this early in the flight, but based on what I ordered, this is what my server suggested as next.  The IPA was also a solid, clear choice.    The third beverage was unlike anything else I've tried locally.  The We've Been Jammed "Fruit Beer" (4.5%) is one of those "dangerous" drinks because it has so much fruit flavor that I didn't notice the alcohol.  It has a nice balance of sour and sweet with a bit of vanilla.  It was refreshing and delicious and is something I would recommend to anyone who isn't a beer drinker in your party as a starting point.  I finished of with the Tiramisu Coffee Stout (8%).  Though not as sweet as the dessert, it had a deep dark chocolate/coffee taste that was really good.  I can imagine pairing this with dessert.  I was going to a catered event immediately after my visit here, so I didn't try any of their food items.  They do offer a variety of appetizers, some entrees, and pizzas.  Hopefully, I will get to check those out on my next visit.  Review #3323

Having tried the Noblesville location, I thought I'd swing by the City Market's version even though it was getting later in the day.  Fortunately, they still had about nine varieties of doughnuts and bismarks available.  If you've not had their pastries, then you're in for a treat.  These are big donuts!    I will be the first to admit that I am not the biggest donut fan, but I've still eaten my fair share.  So when I tried their Boston Cream, I was impressed!    Some places are really skimpy when it comes to the cream in the middle.  Not here!  The Boston had just the right balance of chocolate icing on top and cream in the center.  Really nice flavor too!  I know it's called Rebellion Doughnuts, but I have to admit I would would love to see more bismark options, or maybe Danish.  But that's just me.  The flavors are really good.  Review #2346

Really nice atmosphere.  When you step in the front door, there is a pair of doors to go through:  The restaurant on the left; the 21+ requirement for the bar on the right.  They do have a wall between the sides of the place but they share the same roof.  (and the wall only goes part of the way back to allow staff and patrons to pass back and forth.)  I decided to order the fish and chips but based upon recommendations, I was able to substitute the "neeps" for the chips.  I have to admit that I had no idea what they were, but that they were worth ordering.  The waitress described them as turnips that were cooked down and mashed.    Before long, the plate arrived with the three fish strips and a large serving of tartar sauce and lemon on the main plate.  The neeps were served separately and looked to be enough for two servings.  The fish was tasty with a slight crispness.  I tried them with both the tartar sauce and the malt vinegar that was tableside.  I found the tartar sauce and lemon combo to be quite tasty.  The vinegar and lemon was okay, but I definitely preferred the other combo.  The neeps looked like a slightly orange/yellow mashed potato with about the same consistency.  The side order of neeps describes them as "Sweet Peppered Neeps".  I did find them with a bit of sweetness, but couldn't detect any pepper flavor to them.  I'm not sure if they only pepper the side orders or if you have to ask for the pepper, but mine was not noticeable.  Okay flavor, but not quite the flavor I was expecting.  The waitress was very welcoming and friendly without being intrusive.  Water was refilled and the bill was brought out upon request.  Good job!  Parking is a challenge here, but I was able to street park ($1.50 per hr) a couple blocks away and enjoyed the nice walk since it was sunny.  Review #679

On a warm day with a breeze, we found this brewpub in downtown Fishers and were pleased to see it had a huge patio.  After parking in their lot on the west side of the brewery, we checked in at the hostess stand and then headed out to a table in the covered area of the patio.  This place is clean, spacious, and has a welcoming vibe like being invited into someone's home....a very big home!    Since we had lunch before arriving, I decided to order four of their 5 oz brews ($2.25 each) to make a flight.  I went with the Coffee Blonde (4.8% 20 IBU), the Blood Orange Blonde "BOB" (4.8% 20 IBU), Brick Arch Porter (6.5% 30 IBU), and Mofo Risin' Stout (4.8% 27 IBU).  Of the four, the "BOB" was the most memorable.  I really liked how the citrus flavor of the Blood Orange seemed to blend with the blonde flavors of the ale.  I would definitely order a pint of this!  The others had a lot of coffee and/or chocolate undertones.      My wife decided to skip the ales and head straight to the dessert menu.  She ordered an ice cream cookie sandwich.  This week's combo was a peanut butter cookie filled with chocolate ice cream and drizzled with chocolate syrup.  The best part of it was that she shared!  It was really delicious, and fortunately, the last two beers on my list had chocolate notes already and paired well with the dessert.    There are lots of added touches to the place.  A cool mural on the west side of the building has a railroad theme.  The chairs and tables on the patio were matched and felt very comfortable.  In the center of the patio is an "island" table/bar with the center of the island filled with stone and oil lamps.  There was even seating on the east side of the building where the brewery tanks are located for those who want a more industrial vibe.    Although we live on the other side of the metro area, my wife has already mentioned taking friends with us on a return visit to try out the dinner menu.  Review #326

I really like the idea of having a Test Kitchen in Fishers.  I am somewhat surprised that nobody else opened one before.  Sure, there have been food courts that have had a wide range of success, but I can't think of any place that specifically was designed to encourage new chefs to come up with an idea, or for food truck chefs to take a shot at a brick and mortar restaurant, or an existing chef to try out a new idea without the prohibitive costs of start up.  Although there is only limited time each restaurant can be in the Test Kitchen (I think it is one year), it seems like a fair enough time for each business to determine if the customers like the offerings.  There is a special room called the Signature Table which can be reserved for special events like private parties, cooking lessons, & chef demonstrations.  There are spaces for three restaurants at a time in addition to the Sun King Brewery which occupies the majority of the space.  The individual restaurants don't need to worry about getting alcohol licenses which can be cost prohibitive for start up places since Sun King is on site with their range of beverage options.  The three restaurants onsite when I visited were "Natural State" (southern), "Korave" (Korean BBQ), and "Lil Dumplings" (global street food),  See individual reviews for these restaurants and Sun King.  The Test Kitchen is very popular, so finding seating is a challenge.  If you aren't successful on the main floor, you may find some room upstairs.   The overall environment is quite loud and there are places that are family friendly (just not near the bar of Sun King.)  Parking is at a premium.  We grabbed one of the last street parking spaces just north of the brewery.  They do have parking garages available, but I don't know if they charge or if they are free.  Hopefully someone else will post that soon.  #3647

I enjoyed browsing through the shop.  It's filled with art, jewelry, clothing (both serious and whimsical), and an eclectic mix of items for you and your home.  There are several rooms on each floor that have their own unique collection of items.  The shop has its own parking on the east side of the building.  It does have it's challenges if you aren't okay with steep stairs, but other than that, the space is laid out well.  The staff was friendly and welcoming.  If you are looking for something unique for a gift (for yourself or others), stop by and give this place a try!  Review #2087

During my visit to the new Test Kitchen at Sun King in the Fishers District,   I made my last stop for food at Lil Dumplings.  The restaurant is the next venture for Carlos Salazar who gained fame locally for Rook on Virginia Avenue (in Fletcher Place).  This newest venture is for Global Street Food.  It's like hopping around the world of cuisine without the mileage!  Since I was already pretty full, I decided to pick just one item which was the Szechuan Hot Chicken Steamed Bun which comes with pickled cucumber and honey mustard.  I love the steamed buns (my first tasting was at Rook) and so when given a choice, I pick food with these pillow-y soft bread.  The chicken gleamed with the breading, seasoning, and glaze that made it look as delicious as it tasted.  There was a little bit of heat, but the bun kept the heat moderate and allowed some of the sweet and spice to come through.    I will definitely have to stop by again to check out more of their menu.    Basically, you go to the specific counter for the restaurant, place your order and pay, and are given a sensor that will buzz when your order is ready.  That allows time to find a table and place a beer order from Sun King.  (Note that they do sell non-beer beverages here too.)  When done, the wait staff of Sun King will clear off your trash for you.  The Test Kitchen is very popular, so finding seating is a challenge.  If you aren't successful on the main floor, you may find some room upstairs.  The overall environment is quite loud, though there are places that are family friendly (just not near the bar of Sun King.)  Parking is at a premium.  We grabbed one of the last street parking spaces just north of the brewery.  They do have parking garages available, but I don't know if they charge or if they are free.  Hopefully someone else will post that soon.  Review #3636

I enjoyed my visit to Daniel's Vineyard.  The facility is pretty new and has a great looking event space on the second floor of the winery that looks over the vineyards.  The tasting room servers were very pleasant and able to share information about the wines that I sampled (4 tastes for $5).  Of the four, my favorite was the Winzer White.  Winzer (the family dog) White is described as having "tart yellow apples, bartlett pears, and lemons; off-dry estate white blend with a moderate acidity, light body & a quick finish".  I found the taste refreshing and delicious; by far my favorite.  I also enjoyed the Chardonnay 2015 and the Sangiovese 2016.  Both were good, but didn't have that "buy me" impact from the limited size tasting.    Normally, there are food options available on the weekends but the chef was out during my visit, so I can't comment on how good the food is.  The place has two stages for entertainment.  The outdoor stage is northwest of the winery (short walking distance).  There is also an indoor stage available as well.    The one thing I found a little odd was that the parking was quite a distance from the entrance, especially when the entrance isn't on the south side facing the lot.  They do have about a half dozen handicapped spaces available much closer, but the general parking is separated by a lawn area from the winery.   Generally, I enjoyed my visit and the tastings enough to bring a bottle home.  I would like to come back sometime when the weather isn't so hot so that I could sit outside and overlook the vineyards, maybe listen to some music, and grab a bite to eat with my wine.  Note:  Though the address is 9061, the entrance to the vineyard is just north of 86th.  The drive heads east and then angles north to the higher address.  Review #1037

I normally avoid chocolate shops because I usually buy way more than I should and watch my waist get fatter as my wallet gets thinner.  But life is short and I can't take my money with me, so why not support a local shop so that I can feel good about my indulgence.  And when I tasted my purchases, I knew I had done well.  Whether it was the dark chocolate covered pretzel with just enough salt to contrast with the sweet; or the milk chocolate almond clusters that have a distinctive bite/break when you try them; the chocolates were some of the best I have had.  I also saw a vegan and gluten free Toffee Peanut Butter Cookie that I would have normally passed on, but the flavors are some of my favorites. So I bought it.  Wow!  I've had just enough lousy V/GF cookies and baked goods that I was leery that this would be a brick.  But it wasn't.  It had just a bit of crunch and didn't sit heavy in my belly.  And the flavor was just what I had hoped for. It was a darned good cookie!  On my most recent visit, I decided to get a 6 pack of chocolate truffles.  They had some preselected options, but I chose to build my own.  The problem is that once I get them home, I have trouble remembering which truffle is which.  So, the clever person on duty pulled out a card and drew 6 squares and wrote down the names of my selections in the order that she placed them in the box.  So, as long as I didn't spill the box, I could identify them.  I only had one white chocolate selection in my order so that made it easy to orient and choose a flavor I wanted to start with.  Treat yourself right today and you can spend the rest of the week walking it off.  That's my plan and I hope I stick too it!  Review #3854

My wife wanted to stop for dessert and since we had not tried a Rita's franchise before, we headed over to this spot on 96th to give it a try.  Plenty of free parking in front of this stripmall shop.  Inside, there is a little bit of seating on your left and the order counter extends back along the left wall.  The place to order is at the far end with a rope line separating the people waiting in line from those who are ordering.  Fortunately, the line was short and we placed our order.    There are flavor and menu options listed behind the order/display counters.  My wife liked that estimated calories were listed by each option as well, so she decided to go with a 2-flavored Italian Ice.  I decided to go with a Candy Apple Gelati which came with half Italian Ice and half frozen custard (I went with vanilla) in the same cup.  I thought the flavor of both was really good individually, but even better when I scooped a bit of each on my spoon.  I also appreciated that they had a Tuesday special of Italian Ice for only $2!    There are lots of flavor combinations available and also, toppings can be added for an extra cost.  Something a little different from the standard ice cream shops in the metro area.  Review #3719

You can read it in the owner's statement.  This is a family owned business that primarily caters and makes special order cakes and related baked items for just about any occasion.   But even though the statement refers to the six family members who work here and are owners, the meaning of family runs much deeper than just words.  I had the pleasure of being introduced to Marsha Q and her mother at a recent Yelp event (Yelp's 15th Birthday Bash.)  After a brief introduction about herself and her family business, we all got to ask questions.  I asked about being able to walk in and buy fresh baked items and was told yes, I could stop by, but that there would only be a limited supply of things for sale to the general public.  However, if I wanted to get something specific, to be sure to call in advance to make sure they had the availability to complete an order.  The owners were gracious in their demeanor and the treats they brought to the event were quickly devoured.  One of the things I try to do is make a follow up visit to vendors who provide free goodies at Yelp events as a way to say thank you for their stories and generosity.  So, with my wife and three of my grandchildren in tow, we stopped by on a Wednesday morning and both Marsha and her mother were working that day.  I let them know that I appreciated their participation in the event and they seemed genuinely flattered.  Each of the grandkids picked a Halloween cake pop and though there wasn't much else set out, Marsha let me know she had just taken out a batch of sugar cookies and some cupcakes.  I asked for some of each.  She even asked what type of frosting I wanted on the cakes (butter cream).  She went in the back and prepped them and boxed them for our trip home.  While she worked in the back, her mother shared stories about the display cakes that were in the front of the space.  She also reminded us of how they once made 8000 cupcakes for when Indy hosted the SuperBowl!    Just a note:  The bakery isn't set up as a standard bakery retail place with large counters of items on display.  Rather, it is a little random with items over here, and some over there.  But you just have to ask what's available.  If you are willing to take a chance, then drop in.  Otherwise call in advance.  Before I wrap up, I mentioned how family was mentioned in the owner's business statement.  When I walked in, I was greeted and made to feel like I was part of the family.  They obviously love what they do and wanted to make sure that my family was happy with the items we chose.  That's something you don't see in a lot of places.  Certainly not in the big chain bakeries or the ones who are living on their reputations.  Marsha and her family bake with love and it shines through in every bite.    Review #3249

What a delightful shop in Plainfield!  If you are looking for pastries/baked goods, chocolates, popcorn, salsas and mixes, and even coffee beans, this is worth checking out.  If you are looking for a gift for a friend who spends a lot of time in the kitchen or likes trying new mixes, check it out.  This new business is located in a strip mall just west of the Krogers and has plenty of parking out front.  Inside, the front of the shop is filled with shelves of ceramics, mixes and food stuffs.  The back of the shop has two counters.  One is filled with slices of cakes and pastries.  The other is filled with chocolates.  I picked up a bag of coffee form Noble Coffee & Tea Company.  I also got a popcorn mix from South Bend Chocolate Company.  And of course, three kinds of cake including a carrot cake, a double crunch apple, and a  lemon berry mascarpone slice.  The owner and her mother were working during my visit and were very friendly and helpful.  I've been to a lot of places like this and I enjoy finding independently owned places that offer items from other artisan businesses.  Understand that this isn't a cheap donut or cupcake shop.  I don't recall seeing either of those items.  But if you want to try something different and enjoy good quality products, stop by.  Review #2999

Great brunch for hungry morning people....it is easy for your eyes to want more than your stomach can handle!    On a Sunday morning about 10 a.m., my wife and I found some street parking (free on Sundays) and walked along the CityWay businesses (Cerulean, Market Table, etc.) to go to Yolk for brunch.  Yolk is a franchise of restaurants originated in Chicago, with Indy and the Dallas/Fort Worth areas becoming their expansion cities.  The inside is a mix of diner and industrial styles with a deep blue, white, and yellow-orange color palate.  There is plenty of indoor seating, some with views of the kitchen.  Additional outdoor seating is available in front and along the side on a patio under table umbrellas.    We were seated promptly and given our menus, table ware and had our beverage orders taken.  I noticed that a tray of coffee adds (flavors, creamers, sugar varieties) were already there to reduce the delay times that sometimes go with being dependent upon the waitress for everything.  My wife ordered the corned beef hash that comes with two eggs, diced potatoes, green pepper & onion, and a side of bread option (she went with rye toast - 2 slices).  She was pleasantly surprised that the entree was made with real shredded corned beef.  She was expecting something more like the packaged stuff you can find on a grocery shelf, so this was a definite point were the food exceeded her expectations.  She did find the potatoes a little tougher than she prefers although I think they were technically al dente...just not her preference.  I went in with a big appetite, but I had no idea that the portions of the restaurant would be so substantial!  I ordered coffee and Eggs Benedict for my savory entree and also the Apple Blintzes from the sweet side of the menu.  The Eggs Benedict was pretty standard (i.e. delicious!) with two halves of an English muffin, Canadian bacon, 2 poached eggs, and sides of diced red potatoes and fruit.  The fruit was all fresh.  This day, there were watermelon, red grapes, pineapple, and orange slices.  My potatoes were done to my liking and were tasty with the spill over Bearnaise sauce and soft egg yolks.  The only negative was that the egg whites were a bit "runny" (not my favorite), but with all the other flavors, was not so noticeable.  The Apple Blintzes were HUGE!  Three crepes were folded into multi-layer squares filled with "Special Cheese" (looks like a ricotta or cottage cheese) and topped with sauteed cinnamon apples.  On the side were whipped cream & cinnamon, sour cream, and syrup.  The food was overall pretty sweet tasting.  Because these were blintzes, the cheese was inside and the crepe was thicker than expected to hold together with the moisture.  I am used to crepes where the fruit is inside instead of piled on top.  Overall, the taste was pretty good, but it was really heavy and filling.  I ended up having to get a "to go" box simply because I was full.  I alternated between bites of the savory entree and the sweet to avoid having a sugar rush from all the sweetness.  The service was attentive and efficient.  Water and coffee were refilled and a second Iced Tea was brought without asking.  When we requested the check, it was brought promptly and we were instructed that we pay the cashier on our way out.  This sped up our overall experience because we didn't have to wait on a busy waitress to make trips back and forth.  We also didn't have to part with our credit card, which is also a plus.  Overall, we ordered, ate, and checked out in less than 45 minutes.  Entrees ran in the $13 range each, so it is pricey for breakfast, but comparable with quality restaurant pricing instead of dives or fast food breakfast places.   There are plenty of options on the savory and sweet sides to choose from.  They even have some sandwiches if you are leaning that way.    Note:  On Sunday morning, we saw that by the time we finished, there was a line of folks waiting to be seated.  So, get here early on the weekend if you don't want to have to wait.  Review #114

While on the west side of the Metro area around lunch time, I talked my wife into stopping here since I hadn't been here before, but thought it looked like a nice alternative to the sandwiches, Mexican food, and pizzas we had been sustained on during the pandemic.  Located in the former Metropolis shopping area, we were able to find some convenient free parking just outside the front doors.  We had just come from an appointment and hadn't called our order in, so we entered the bright and clean space where you have a long order counter where you can see the ingredients as well as see suggested options on the easy to read wall menus behind the food prep area.  We both opted for salads on this visit, but could have ordered wraps too.  Even if you select one of the salads listed on the wall, you can make changes to the order when you   place it at the cashier.  I replaced the kale in my "The Forbidden Fruit" salad with Romaine lettuce and kept the chicken protein.  My wife ordered the GD Special salad adding black olives and selecting iceberg lettuce and romaine.  You can also add proteins.  You can select salad dressing (over the top or on the side), and finally, you can order how finely chopped you want the ingredients.  The salad ingredients when rough cut were quite large and I think most folks would need a knife to fit the pieces in your mouth, so we ordered the fine cut on our salads.  We got our order to go and I was pleased at how fresh tasting everything was even a half hour later when we got home to eat.  (Note they do have some inside spaces, but are limited and don't have ideal locations with customers walking passed to place their orders.    I really enjoyed the flavor of my selection.  But there were some things that weren't up to our expectations.  My wife's order was supposed to be topped with crisp tortilla chips, but the preparer didn't add them.  I also expected to be able to see my protein (the chicken) in my salad.  I could taste the chicken but it had been finely cut/diced down to bacon bit  size.  It was okay, but because I was expecting there to be bigger pieces (something closer to bite sized) I was initially disappointed.  But the chicken was there, just finely cut as per my order.  The portion size was plentiful and my wife saved nearly half for her dinner that evening.  I had no trouble devouring my bowl of salad in one sitting.  I have seen some people complain about pricing, but making salads is a very labor intensive item, especially if you are getting orders made to order.  My wife's comment was that she would eat salads every day if she just had someone make them for her.  I try, but not daily! ha!     I thought the food was really tasty and the folks were pleasant but weren't chatty or particularly welcoming.  It's hard to tell if someone is smiling at you when wearing a mask, so if they could use their voices to be more welcoming, that would help too.  If you want a salad and just don't feel like doing all the prep work yourself, definitely give this place a try.  I hear they have shops all around the metro area, so keep your eyes open as new ones set up or check online to see their locations.  Review #3890

This shop has women's clothing and accessories, primarily for younger women who want clothing that looks both professional and fun.  The shop is much larger than it appears from the front since it extends across the entire block.  There is plenty of room for the merchandise to be displayed and there are nice dressing rooms about 2/3 of the way back.  The woman working at the desk was friendly and seemed to manage several customers at once.    Note that there is a small floor level change for those who have mobility challenges.  Review #2215

This brand new addition to "the Yard" in Fishers was a pleasant discovery.  After parking in front of the building on the east side of the north-south access road, I entered the shop portion of this meat shop.  There was a rack of food items by the door.  There is a U-shaped meat counter with multiple staff available to assist.  In the center, a 2-sided cooler has packaged meets and food items.  I decided to get some bulk Mild Italian Sausage, some sliced Jalapeno Colby Jack cheese, and after getting a free sample of their house made Ham Salad, decided to get a pound of that.  The ham salad was fantastic and I've already tried some on crackers with the cheese. Yum!  Very friendly, helpful, and timely assistance from the staff.  I wish I lived closer.  I could see becoming a regular customer here.  Review #3409

A place in Broad Ripple that has its own free lot!  The site of the former BurgerFuel restaurant has a fantastic new restaurant and its own parking lot on the north side of the building (pull in off of Guilford).    My wife and I wanted to treat our oldest grandson to dinner and this was fairly close to his apartment.  Since it was new and getting lots of great reviews, I combined my love of good food with the opportunity to spend time with my eldest.    The place still needs some work on the interior, (concrete floors need a good cleaning), but the kitchen appeared bright and clean, all the staff had masks worn appropriately.  They have the menus that you can pull up on your phones if you have the right app, and even though they didn't have any outdoor seating for the cold weather, the tables were spaced far enough apart that we felt comfortable dining in.  This is Texas style BBQ and they offer a variety of meats including ribs, pork shoulder, chicken, and brisket.  They also offer a couple varieties of chili including the Hillbilly Chili that my wife selected.  It has a Trinity of meats including pork, brisket, and sausage served over fritos along with jalapenos, sour cream, pickled onions, etc.  She thought it spicy, but not too strong.  I don't know if they have any vegan or vegetarian options, frankly because I didn't look.  I was there for BBQ!  I ordered the pulled pork shoulder which had an excellent taste.  They have multiple sauces available.  I went with their mustard, pickles, and onion on my sandwich and it was delicious!  The only negative I had was that the buns felt a little greasy to the touch (you can see the shine in the photos).  Not sure what caused that.  Note that all the sandwiches are ala carte, so it can get expensive if you start ordering sides and a full size sandwich.  Most sandwiches offer a choice of full pound or half pound servings.  They also have some family size meals or shareables, but these still can get a bit pricey if you aren't used to going out to nicer fully smoked BBQ houses.  To my knowledge, they do not have a liquor license, so I believe most of the beverages are sodas or bottled waters.  This place would be fantastic if they could get the right to serve craft beers with their BBQ!    My grandson got the mac and cheese and my wife was able to get a bite and said it was delightful.  I ordered the baked beans as a side and they were fantastic!  Lots of brown sugar, and a bit of brisket in with the beans made it almost a meal in itself.  Lots of layers of flavors and all worked well together.  Highly recommend them!  The staff were friendly and waited us at the table.  We were provided napkins and plastic ware so we didn't need to wander around looking for any of that.  I look forward to visiting them again and hope to try the ribs.  If they are anywhere as tasty as the sandwiches and chili, it will be well worth the trip.  Review #3863

Have you ever wanted to have a nice selection of Mediterranean food but didn't want to sit through a long wait/formal lunch?  Have you ever wanted to grab something quick, but were tired of going to the endless chain restaurants?  Then Lava Express is a place for you to try!  Tucked away near the west end of a strip mall on 116th, this small shop offers a solid, but limited menu of food that is made fresh in the open air kitchen while you wait.    After parking in the shared lot, I entered the restaurant where one of the employees was providing information to a small group that was trying to decide what they wanted.  I bypassed all those folks (walking between the food prep area and the dining area) towards the back of the restaurant where the order counter is located.  (They have a menu there too.)  I was able to order a gyro combo which comes with seasoned fries and a self-serve beverage.    I let them know I was dining in and paid, taking my cup to the front of the store where the beverage dispenser and busing station are located.  (They carry Coke products.)  I grabbed a seat at one of the tables and waited for the food to be brought out to me.  They don't use numbering or naming systems.  They look at your face and bring the food to you!  The gyro was generously portioned in two halves.  The lamb/beef had a nice flavor on its own, but when added to the pocket full of ingredients, it was really good.  They also provided a small cup of giardiniera for a bit of heat and acidity which was perfect for the dish.    The seasoned fries were good, but the seasoning wasn't distributed evenly throughout the fries (mainly just the ones on top.)    The staff was friendly and efficient and were bringing out small samples of their smoothies to try.  I didn't buy one, but I thought the honeydew smoothie was particularly good.  The cold, slushie style treat was a nice palate cleanser after the meal and was really good.  There is also a small outdoor dining area in front of the store that is available on nice days.  Overall, I had a really good meal and was in and out in about a half hour...perfect for most lunches!  Review #2715

After being in business for awhile, this place became Harold's Steer-In over 50 years ago (1964).  It has gone through some structural changes and though it no longer offers drive-in service, the business keeps serving traditional foods (including breakfast) to folks on the east side.    I parked under the shade of the former drive-in canopy and entered through a small entryway into the restaurant.  It has a fairly plain interior showing signs of becoming dated while still loyal to the local school teams that have pictures and memorabilia on the walls.  I followed the sign and seated myself for lunch.  I was greeted and brought my beverage and a menu.  I noticed a sign on the wall that they had won awards for their tenderloins, so that seemed like the way to order!  I picked coleslaw instead of fries and waited a short while for my food.    The tenderloins come either grilled or breaded (breaded for me) and topped with onion, mayo, and tomato.  I also added some mustard (upon request) and was soon enjoying this normal sized meal.  The sandwich comes on a toasted bun for a little more crunch and the breading, though a bit darker than expected had a nice flavor and the meat was still moist.  Good sandwich!  The slaw was cold and sweet (not creamy) and was finely shredded.  The taste went really well with the sandwich.  I did have to flag down a waitress for utensils and napkins since I wasn't given them earlier.  But that was easily resolved.    Unless you like your tenderloin the size of road kill, you won't be disappointed with the fine tasting sandwich.  Easy to see why they won awards for it.    Nothing fancy here, just good food at reasonable prices.  Review #2769

I decided to venture just a bit north of the heart of Fountain Square up to this local bar at the corner of Fletcher and Shelby.  Although there isn't parking outside the door, there is a row of angled parking across Shelby along Fletcher.  I crossed the street and up the steps into the bar.   The interior is a shotgun style place with the long bar w/seating on the right, a center row of standing islands to rest your beverages on, and then some additional seating fitted wherever it doesn't get too crowded (at least until the place gets really busy.)  In the back is a small grill area where they prepare the food.  I also noted that there is a covered patio area of the right rear of the building that was enclosed to offer some protection from the cool winter.  Not sure if it stays open all winter or not.  The man working behind the bar/running the grill/taking orders may have been the owner.  He was doing it all during the lunch hour.  It wasn't too crowded during the week so wait times were minimal.  I noted that he was dialed into the music playing, making sure it wasn't too far out there for customers.  (I can't tell you how many places have it either too loud to carry on conversations or have profanity laden lyrics that I have outgrown.)  It seemed the guy was really focused on getting everything done, especially as more customers started showing up.  Just able to carry on conversations too.  Great job!  I ordered one of the lunch specials:  a Philly Cheese Steak with chips and a beverage.  While I waited, I browsed around the bar.  There are Sports Illustrated covers framed all over the walls.  Lots of sports items with a couple silent, but captioned tv's playing over the bar.  I also noticed that they carried a number of beers on tap including a mix of national brands and local craft selections.  Hard liquor was also available.    The sandwich was good.  Crispy crunch of the bread and large chunks of green pepper and onions inside with the cheese and meat.  Good flavor, but could use a little higher ratio of meat to veggies for my tastes.  Still, a good sandwich, but not what I would consider a traditional Philly.  Although this is a well established neighborhood bar, I didn't feel any negative vibes during the lunch hour.  In fact, the staff was easy going and welcoming.    It's nice to see a local place still making a go of it even with all the change going on in the area.  Review #3308

Hit or miss.  I really liked the pupusa, but wasn't a fan of the curtido (slaw like side) or some of the accompaniments to the Tipico Casamiento.  I'm not sure if I caught them on a bad day or not, but my pork, cheese, and bean pupusa was grilled so long that my table knife wasn't sharp enough to get through it very easily.  Still, the flavor was really good, especially when paired with a couple of the bottled sauces brought table side.  The casamiento is a tasty bean and rice dish; by far the best part of the entree.  I also liked the eggs and fried plantain with sour cream.  But the cassava (yucca) and Chicharones (fried pork chunks) were woefully under seasoned and somewhat overcooked as well.  I tried pairing bites of each with the sour cream and with some of the sauces, but just couldn't find a flavor combination that I could really enjoy.  The curtido looked like a cole slaw, but had a dominating herbal flavor (oregano is my best guess.)  It was an unexpected flavor to me, so although I ate it all, found it didn't go well with the pupusa (at least to my palate.)  My dining friends seemed to enjoy their pupusas, but neither raved about them either.  If I were to come back, I would definitely go for another pupusa (only $2), but would probably look towards trying something different as an entree.    Review #829

Authentic Mexican food recipes that were passed from family and tweaked by the former Sous Chef of Tinker Street await the customers of Festiva.  This restaurant is pioneering the redevelopment of east 16th Street, just across the Monon.     There is a lot to like here.  First, they have their own lot on the east side of the building, but since those will be gobbled up fast, they do have street parking on 16th street once they open.     For Margaritas, although they aren't huge like a chain restaurant, they have excellent flavor.  My guests highly recommend the Margarita Estacional made with fresh pressed juices and agave nector with Maestro Dobel Silver tequila, Blood orange, habanero, hibiscus, and citrus with a salt rim.   The quacamole is fresh with chunks of avocado in with the mix, and topped with sweet pomegranate, thin sliced Jalapenos, and cilantro.  This went really fast for our group of four, so you will probably want a second order or consider another appetizer to start.   We went with Chicken tamales, mole pablano.  The chicken is especially tender and the tamale is fresh, removed from the husk, and covered with a tasty mole sauce.  Not much heat, but good flavor.    One of our party tried the Tender Cactus Leaves with Guajillo (a mild chili pepper) Vinaigrette as a salad.  The cactus is diced and cooked just a bit past al dente, so it has an easy bite.  It comes with red onion, fresh mild radish, and a bit of cheese (not sure, but it may be cotija).  Nice flavor and would be ordered again upon our next visit.   For entrees, in an unusual move, three of the party ordered the Arabes Al Pastor: Slow spit roasted pork (served in a separate bowl) with Cumin, several corn tortillas, and onion, and cilantro on the side.  It comes with three sauces so that you can select your heat level.  Note:  one of the orders came with a large hot pepper on the side.  The other had the hot pepper on top of the meat and the ladies in our group thought it very hot and unpleasant.  Once they got to the lower levels of the meat, the heat was unnoticed in the meat.  So, be aware to look for where the pepper is placed.   I went for the Pescado, a grilled whole (but no head) Mediterranean Sea Bass, with salsa Rodrigo on top.  It also came with corn tortillas and roasted sweet cherry tomatoes which worked really well with the salsa and fish flavors.  I only wish that they offered flour tortillas since I prefer those to corn based.     For dessert, two preferred the pound cake which doesn't look like pound cake you're used to.  It is served in a swirled pattern with a fruit salsa and got good reviews.  My wife and I went with Mango Gelatina which has the consistency of a flan and is topped with chopped kiwi and a creme fraiche.     The only negatives for the evening were that the seats are really close together, so it was hard not to overhear the neighboring table.  They also have built a temporary wind breaker for the front door which makes it very difficult to see on coming traffic from the west.  Fortunately, it was dark when we left and could pick up headlights, but it could be problem in the summer. Oh, and if they can offer flour tortillas as a choice, I would be really happy!  Review #207

I stopped by on a cool Sunday morning just after they opened. Free parking on Indiana Avenue (love the free weekends!) for a short walk down the stairs to the canal side location.  No lines!  I ordered a half Italian Beef sandwich and added the pay options of Mozzarella Cheese and Giardiniera.  I also liked that they let me select how I wanted my au jus.  I got it in a cup instead of drenched over the top.  I can't stand a sandwich too soggy to be picked up, so this option with the cup wide enough to dip the bread was appreciated.  The standard side is a bag of chips.    My sandwich arrived in minutes and was loaded with flavor.  Their beef is finely shredded instead of sliced, so a few globs managed to drop into my serving basket.  The beef stayed moist and seemed evenly balanced throughout the sandwich.    The location is great (as long as you don't mind the stairs) and they offer pizzas and dessert options as well.  It is worth noting this is a seasonal location from April through the end of summer. Then, the business transfers back to the original Lockerbie location.  Review #280

I had lunch here on Monday and had good food and prompt, courteous service.  There was a decent crowd for late in the lunch hour.  Although there is a parking lot out front, I was lucky to grab one of the last spots near the restaurant due to the lot being shared with several other businesses.  Since I was running a bit late, I appreciated that my waitress stayed within eye sight and took my order as soon as I was ready.  I opted for the crab cake appetizer and asked for my blackened tilapia to be brought out later.    I didn't read the menu closely and was surprised by how flat the cakes were.  Very moist with a good flavor, the cakes were a mix a crab and tilapia.  Although the flavor was pleasant, the texture lacked a crusty outside that I have had at other restaurants.  Not bad, but not quite what I expected.  The blackened tilapia was served in my choice of a wrap:  corn or flour.  I went with the flour and it was grilled to give the wrap a crispy, firm base which was appreciated because the fish and accompianing pico de gallo would probably soak through otherwise.    The fish came with avocado slices and a pineapple-habanero sauce which gave the wrap a sweet and spicy-hot combo.  The flavors weren't quite balanced, or maybe the distribution wasn't even.  My first of the two wraps had plenty of heat but was a bit underseasoned with other spices.  The second wrap seemed to have more balanced flavor, as the pineapple flavor seemed more prominent than the habanero.  Still, the flavor was a bit under seasoned and could have used a bit more salt.  Again, not bad, just not 5 star.    Review #199

I don't buy a lot of athletic wear, so I can't really say how this shop compares to the big box places.  But what I do know is that they provide a service to Avon and the neighboring community when it comes to personalizing band/athletic clothing.  My wife has a lot of sewing equipment at home, but even she prefers to come here when it comes to having our grandsons' letter jackets embroidered.  She can get the jackets in the school colors here, and have them embroidered with the school name (official logo) and personalized with our boys' names.  And as they earn patches for competitions they perform in, my wife is able to have them added to the jackets in a reasonable time frame.  It isn't a cheap place, but it is done well and looks professionally done.  Our oldest grandson's jacket has held up well and we haven't had any problems with the patches becoming loose.  We recently picked up our next grandson's new jacket and it turned out great.  We are looking forward to continued service from this business as our grandchildren progress.  Review #3363

My review may be a little biased on the high side because whenever I gather with friends to share a meal, I tend to have a more enjoyable experience.  Although there is a small parking area reserved for customers behind the restaurant, it does fill up quickly and it is easy to miss if you are in a hurry driving along College.  The alley behind the lot can sometimes be blocked by vehicles parked in the way, so I suggest slowing down and keeping your eyes open for the driveway back to the lot.  The restaurant has indoor and outdoor seating (including a patio on the back.)  The indoor also has garage doors that open to let the fresh air in.  It does get loud inside with the music cranked, lots of conversation and the noise of vehicles from College Ave.  The six of us shared a table where we could see by the natural light coming in through the front.  They have lots of choices for beverages, including many craft beers.  Sadly, I ordered an iced tea that had no flavor...I thought it was just water.  Almost that clear.  Our table ordered a variety of sandwiches and sides.  I wanted the Reuben but was a little hesitant when I saw it was house smoked.  It was really tasty and I chose it because the Pastrami and Corned beef did not include sauerkraut which I wanted on my sandwich.  I made the right choice and was very pleased with the taste.  The fries that someone ordered were seasoned and I really enjoyed them. I think the consensus of the group was that they enjoyed what they ordered and other than it being too loud, enjoyed dining at FD.  Review #3942

Although my wife and I enjoy trying new restaurants and bars, I don't think we fit the target customer well for the Saint Shack because we are older.  The food and cocktails we tried were tasty and reasonably priced.  The hostess who greeted us was friendly too.  Located on the west side of Meridian Street between the mall and the Slippery Noodle restaurants, you can pay to park in the mall or use the metered parking along Meridian if you are able to find a sot. Fortunately, we went early and grabbed a spot right in front of the bar.  The Saint Shack is located on the street level and because of that, I was approached by someone asking for cash even before I got inside the bar.  That happens way too often near the Fieldhouse  anymore.  Inside, even after just opening, the music was thumping loudly which I guess is okay if you are here to mingle and like the music style, but if you are there to grab a bite to eat and talk with friends, it becomes a bit more difficult.  The  volume caused the bar tenders to shout loudly which was distracting while my wife and I ate. One of the bar tenders has a very shrill and piercing laugh that was off putting to hear throughout our meal. I'd say the frozen slushies were the most appealing part of our experience.  No waiting to be served at the bar.  The hostess got them for us and even took our food order, so we rarely saw any wait staff throughout the meal, though our food made it to our table in relatively little time.  Don't expect a glass of water ;with your meal or follow up attention. Fortunately, the food is served in boxes you can use for "to go".  It did okay for a bar, but service wasn't quite at restaurant level.   My wife enjoyed her Indy dog, but  passed on the jalapenos.  I ordered a regular corn dog after my attempt to order an andoullie corndog failed. I also placed an order for tots (crispy and plentiful. Finally, I ordered Boudin Balls (4 per order).  These were coated with crispy crumbs and served with a spicy brown mustard to add a bit of heat flavor.  Since these meatballs are made with crumbs inside to help keep the sausage from becoming tough and binding, they tend to break apart quite easily which made dipping them a little messy.    One of the things I failed to find was a way from the restaurant area down to the bar in the basement without having to go outside to the front of the bar.  Seems the mgmt should have addressed this during he build out.  If here is a way downstairs, it definitely needs better marking for patrons to find.  I understand that these may be two separate bars, but are decorated like they are one.  JUust a little more confusion.  Well, if you are a fan of frozen/slushie type cocktails, swing by here and give them a try.  We really enjoyed the ones we tied.    Review #3954

First let me state I am not an afficianado of bubble tea and my wife is even less so.  This was her first time ordering one and although what she ordered turned out really tasty, she was a bit bewildered by the numerous steps in ordering. She ordered a dairy milk option, not a tea option.  She ordered a strawberry flavor which was delicious.  And when it came to the boba, she got popping, not the beads.  Since I got to try half her drink, I was quite surprised by the popping since I had never had it before.  I was used to the beads that were more like tapioca/gum drop chewy.  Instead, as the poppings slid up the straw, they burst with a squirt upon first contact with my teeth.  I found it quite pleasant and the immediate flavor release was also pleasing.  I found the ordering menu on one end of the stall,so a second one would be beneficial in case customers were blocking the view of the options. These beverages are more expensive than sodas or iced teas, so keep that in mind if you are ordering a double digit sandwich for lunch.  Just look for the bright colored stall about halfway back through the AMP to give them a try.  Review #3936

If you are looking for something to breakup the day to day routine foods like burgers, pizza, wings, then I recommend giving one of Chicken Salad Chick restaurants a try.  They have expanded the number of locations around the metro area.  Since we were meeting friends on the north side, we chose this location near the pyramids  at 87th and Michigan Rd.  They share a parking lot, so we were able to find free parking with just a short stroll around to the front entrance.  My advice is to go online and check out the numerous options and combos available.  That way you can select which of the multiple flavors you want.  The salads have been given short names so you don't have to rattle off every ingredient.  It's very helpful!  you can choose to simply have a scoop of the chicken salad, or have it on one of their breads or croissants.  If you are hungry and wish to have more than one scoop, they have meals like the duo or trio where you get chicken salad, sides (like M&C or fresh fruit), a small side salad or soup of the day, and with every meal, a small lemon cookie and a tart dill pickle spear.  Mine also came with a beverage too.  So you can imagine how knowing the menu ahead of time will make it easier to order.  Try not to get behind someone who has no clue because you may be in line for awhile.  I ended up ordering a trio and really enjoyed the chicken salads.  I was a little disappointed that grilled bread I had two selection put on were over done and the slight burned taste took away from the sandwich.  I'll go for the croissant next time or just the salad in a cup.  I was impressed that the restaurant was so bright and clean.  This appeared to be a new building and everything about it, including the parking area  was taken care of.  Try something new but may remind you of younger days.  Stop in for chicken salad soon! They also have larger packages of salad you can take home for the family  which are ready to go! My favorites were the Fancy Nancy and the Sassy Scotty.    Give it a try  for a fresh taste on a a time-tested idea.  Review #3965

I've had this place bookmarked for awhile, but since we live 45 minutes away, I don't get over this way very often.  I'm so glad that when I had an appointment downtown, I asked my wife to head east and we found this place for lunch.  It is so nice to see some of the vacated shops in Irvington have new businesses jump in to keep this mini strip at the intersection of Audubon and Bonna Avenues stay full and doing good business. This location has its own parking lot in front and used to be home to Tyner Market and The Mug. Now, along with Landlocked Baking and Strange Bird, the space is filled with food and beverage places and has become a destination for the historical area that is vibrant and current!  Come on Irvington!  Support your local shops.  There has been way too many closures of cool places even before covid.  This is another spot that could use a nice sign on the building front to let you know you were at the right location.  They do have a sign by the street, but even when we walked in, we were asked "Are you looking for the Mug?"  I thought it an unusual greeting for a new business to ask for their first question.  We said, "No, we were looking for you!"    I relied upon some of my friend's reviews for what to try when here.  My wife ordered the Chicago Dog and an order of Golden Fries (but without the black pepper).  I ordered the Breakup Burger which has to chargrilled thin patties on Hawaiian Rolls with lettuce, mustard, American cheese, kewpie mayo, and dill slices.  The charring on the burgers brought out a great balance in flavors.  Highly recommended by me!  It wasn't a BMB (Big Mouth Burger) like some places, but was delicious.  The fries were tasty and were large enough to share between us.    My Chocolate Shake was a little different than I expected.  It was more like really cold chocolate milk with a light whipped cream topping instead of the icy milk shakes I am used to.  Great flavor though.
