Nice that I didn't get a brain freeze as I drank it!    It did take a little longer than the fast food burger joints, but the taste was well worth the wait.  We were able to dine inside with plenty of spacing and our food brought out to us.  They do have outside seating for days just a little warmer than upon our visit.  If you haven't been here yet, and like traditional food, you are sure to find something here to like.  Review #3886

After visiting our eldest grandson and his new apartment on the west side, we decided to take him to lunch.  Mexican food was agreed upon by all of us and w decided to give La Hacienda a try.  It can be a little difficult to find since it stuck in an inner corner of a large building.  We ended up driving all the way around just to find it.    Although the parking lot needed some cleaning and pot holes filled, Once we pulled up to the restaurant, we found the interior to be clean and lively.  we were given our choice of booth or table and we chose a section where the music was not too loud.  All three of us ordered something from the lunch menu which was fairly large serving for the price.  Our food came with chips and salsa.  The salsa was very thin with just a hint of heat to it.  The chips were light and crisp...good  enough to munch on even without salsa.  Our entrees came with beans and rice as well, so a full meal. Service was pretty good and the wait time on the kitchen was acceptable.  My wife decided to add a frozen strawberry margarita and thought it needed more mix (not enough berry flavor.)  The waiter brought us our bill and I paid at the front counter.  Overall, a pleasant meal and experience.  #Review 3966

After an awkward search trying to find the restaurant, we realized that if we had stayed on Michigan Road and turned east onto 106th, our journey would have been much easier.  The signage is small  on all other sides of the building so, we would get glimpses of where it was and then ran into a bunch of  curved streets and blocked access until we got out onto 106th again.  Fortunately, my wife's diligence and patience paid off as we both enjoyed our meals here.  It was a beautiful day to sit out on the front patio.  Our service was good throughout the lunch and wait times were fine for our time schedule.  I liked that we had real menus to use which is helpful because there is a lot to choose from.  Although they specialize in smash burgers, you can get lots of other items like tenderloins, dynamite shrimp (my wife's choice).  And just because they smash the burgers flat to get more sear area for that wonderful char flavor that makes a burger a burger, my selection came with the burger doubled so that it was still challenging to fit it into my own big mouth without a little smear of condiment on my lip or cheek! ha!  Just another reason to take a friend whom you can trust to tell you! The only negative I have is that if you are tempted to try lots of things (much is ala carte) the bill can grow quite rapidly.  I was famished when I arrived but was quite content by the time I left.  But counting tip and tax, the two of us ran up a bill (without alcohol) of $50  for lunch.  Nobody's fault but mine, but I got iced tea, we each got an order of house fries (worth every penny!) and my wife tried one of their non-alcoholic milk shakes.  Her strawberry surprise was like it had strawberry jam/jelly instead of fresh strawberries, so it was quite sweet for about $6.   I have been to most of the 1/2 pound specialty burger places in the area, so I don't feel this place is priced too high for the competition, but if you just like a plain burgers, this type of restaurant probably isn't your best choice.  I go for things I don't make at home.   My wife's Dynamite shrimp had a really nicely balanced flavor and was breaded with a doughy coating with nice seasoning.  The problem from so much breading is that the shrimp got a little over cooked and was a bit rubbery in texture.  since she wasn't able to finish her lunch in one sitting, I was able to grab a couple of he shrimp and it made me wonder what was "dynamite" in the name.  I found it very mildly flavored even with the sauces drizzled over it.  Maybe the name comes from the size of the shrimp.  They look like they exploded they were so large!     When I got home, I found that they have either added more locations already  or are in the process of adding some closer to where I live.  I will have to check those out to see how the flavor and service compare to this location which takes at least 45 minutes for us to get here.   Good food, good service, minor wait times.  Review #3929

My wife and I recently scheduled lunch at "The Loft" (6-9-16).  We went on a day that the weather cooperated, allowing us to sit out on the balcony and enjoy a great spring day while dining.   Although we didn't have reservations, we were seated promptly and without much delay, were brought water and asked about our beverage selections.  We informed our waitress that we had about an hour before we needed to leave for another appointment, so we went ahead and placed our order for our meals at the same time.   I selected the Lake Trout on a bed of millet and mustard aioli, along with asparagus, shallots, and almonds.  The skin of the filet was crispy.  The flesh of the filet was moist and tender.  So, excellent marks for preparation.  I also thought the flavors worked well together, although I am not a big fan of millet.  Still, the food was served timely, and tasted delicious as well.  I also ordered a bottle of Ginger Beer which was quite tasty.   My wife ordered the house burger after ordering a root beer float.  She liked both, but needed a "to go" box for the remaining half of her burger.  She ordered the Kettle Chips as a side, but she wasn't a fan of the salt and pepper flavor combination on the chips.  (I tried them and found them quite good, but couldn't get passed the notion of some other herbal taste there as well.)   All in all, the service and food were good, but we didn't have any "Wow!" taste moments, so that is the only reason I didn't give a higher rating.  Review #1

On our second visit to the Garage Food Hall, we decided to try something different.  There were three in our group and we decided to go with Gaucho's Fire since it offered food that everyone was able to find something that appealed to them.  I saw in the business's comments that they recommended the Brazilian Steak Sandwich and the Grilled Beef Chimichuri.  One of our group ordered from that selection while I ordered the Grilled Chicken Salad.  We waited briefly before ordering and paid before finding a seat in the general seating area shared by the food hall.  (It was quite spacious).  Our receipt had an order # and one of our group stood within range of hearing the cashier call out the number for pickup.  The meals came with napkins, plastic ware and a tray to carry it all on.  The wait was about five minutes for our order to be put together during a weekday lunch.  Our friend ordered the Brazilian Steak Sandwich and said it was really good.  My wife ordered the Grilled Beef Chimichuri and said the beef was chewy.  I tried it and thought the meat was tender enough, but with a bit of chew.  I was disappointed in the chimichuri seasoning.  I've had it elsewhere (maybe not authentic elsewhere) but I definitely was not drawn to the taste and wouldn't recommend it.  I ordered a large Grilled Chicken Salad that had bite sized pieces of chicken that were tasty and held some moisture despite the grilling.  They offered a choice of dressing (Ranch or Blue Cheese) and layered it on fairly thick.  It is served over a bed of greens that are cut, but not quite small enough to be bite sized.  With the dressing, I struggled keeping my face free of dressing as I tried to fit the lettuce/chicken/toppings into my mouth.  I have a fairly large mouth, so I was surprised that the lettuce needed additional cutting with my plastic ware for me to fit the "bites" cleanly into my mouth.  If they would cut the lettuce into just a little smaller pieces, I wouldn't have been wiping my face after each bite.  Little details could be improved and earn a higher rating, but I have to base my review on what my/our experience was, not could be.  Most meals offered where in the $8-10 range.  Extra sides and desserts and beverages are add ons.  Be sure to hold onto your receipt to get a discount on your parking fees if you stop at one of the internal machines marked by small murals that help you locate the place to get discounts on your parking.  We got our first hour of parking validated for no additional cost.  Review #3872

Although I don't grab coffee  to go while I am out exploring (not very often) I wanted to support one of the coffee shops and pick up a bag of freshly roasted and ground beans for my home use and talked my wife into heading passed all the downtown construction to try out Command.  Instead of using the drive rhru, She parked in one of the spots out front.   Once inside, I found the area small, bright, and clean inside.  Some patrons seemed to be enjoying the limited seating with plenty of spacing that I didn't feel like I was intruding on their space/conversations.  There is an order counter with some display cases  and menu boards along the wall with most of the pricing and options.  Unfortunately, by the time I arrived, (mid morning) I didn't see much to order/choose for dining other than the liquid side of the menu.   As I entered, I saw the bags of beans ready for customers to use at home.  Unfortunately, Command only makes light and dark roast while I prefer medium roast.  I asked (just to be sure I wasn't missing something) and the staff confirmed they only have the two options on their beans.  Fortunately, they offer complementary grinding and so I chose the dark and found it not too strong this morning when I made my own cup at home.  Nice flavor on the Colombian Supremo.  no bitterness.    As far as food items, all I saw were some cupcakes and some 4 Bird cookies which I selected two.  (Too bad the FS storefront of 4 birds doesn't sell retail ( at least not whenever I have stopped by.)  Fortunately, Command had a small selection of cookies right at the counter and I could easily check them out in time to place them with my coffee order.    service was quick and friendly, and helpful, but again, I was just getting the coffee, nothing else to eat besides the cookies, so I would say that the wait time was what I would expect. Not sure using  a drive thru would have been any faster.    I was pleased that access in and out of the lot was not a problem despite this location being at a busy intersection along Fall Creek & 29th.  Just keep your eyes open when looking for the entrance and you should be fine.    Review #3955

Once again, my wife and I enjoyed ice cream at this wonderful old depot on the Monon Trail.  This time, I went with the Broad Ripple Blackberry ice cream in a dish.  We sat out on the deck beneath the table umbrella to watch folks go by on the trail.  While we sat, the server brought out water to help quench our thirst since it was nearing 90 degrees.  It was a nice touch that wasn't expected....just good customer service.  Some places get it...some don't.  Rev #5

Excellent food, atmosphere, and good company made for a fun evening on Friday night!  My wife and I invited our friends to join us during the Devour Northside promotion, but none of  us went with the 3 course options.  Instead, we sampled a number of options from the regular menu.  After ordering drinks, we requested a bread course (no charge, but only brought out by request).  Four kinds of bread were served with an herbal butter spread.  All received good ratings.  We started with several small plates:  two orders of Crispy Deviled Eggs - 1000 Island Dressing, House Giardiniera, Nduga Sausage (4 halves per order = Delicious!); and a Shaved Brussels Sprouts Salad - Sieved Egg, Smoked Almond, Parmesan, Citrus Vinaigrette. The sprouts were prepared raw so they had a bit of a chewiness to them and a flavor similar to cabbage.  The other elements of the plate worked well with the flavor, especially the almonds.  For dinner, my wife and friend ordered the Pork Chop with Baked Beans, vinegar Peppers, Bacon marmalade, house Kraut.  My friend thought it was exceptionally good.  My wife enjoyed the flavors as well, but found the chop a little tougher than expected.    My friend's wife ordered the Wild Coho Salmon - Potato Gnocchi, marinated zucchini, rainbow chard, aleppo pepper.  I got a taste of the salmon (served medium done) and was pleased with the robust flavor without the fishy taste.    I decided to step out of my  comfort zone and went with the Rabbit Biscuits and Gravy with baby carrots, Shitake mushrooms.  I figured I may not have another chance to try rabbit in the near future, so I rolled the dice and trusted the chef to surprise me.  First off, the biscuits and gravy were really good on their own.  There was a sweet component to the combo, and maybe a hint of wine ???  The Shitake mushrooms were tender and seemed to pick up the flavors of the gravy.  The rabbit was very tender and had a mild flavor...no gaminess at all.  I assume the rabbit was farm raised.  There wasn't a lot of rabbit on the dish, but what I had was enjoyable.  For dessert the gals split the popular Sticky Toffee (with vanilla ice cream) and my friend ordered the Chocolate mousse which came in a sundae glass with whipped cream on top.  Everyone enjoyed their desserts as much as their dinners.  Overall, everyone was very pleased with their dinner and would recommend dining here.  Sometime, we hope the weather would cooperate so that we could dine out on the vine covered patio.  Very cool!  p.s. If I had to point out any negatives, I would say that the service could have done a better job of clearing the table of finished plates.  It seemed they were trying to clear at the same time of placing the next course and got in each other's way.    Rev #18

After dining at one of the upscale restaurants in Broad Ripple, the group of friends I was with headed over to Brics to enjoy an ice cream dessert (6-2-16).  It was a great night to sit out on the patio and people watch the folks and pets on the Monon Trail.  I ordered an Apple Crisp ice cream (single serving) in a waffle cone.  It was huge!  After having dinner, I was glad I didn't splurge on a double dip....can't really get a to go box for ice cream! :)  Excellent flavor.  Generous portions.  Great location for people watching.  This is a really great place to go for a dip!  Review #7

I stopped in for lunch and had a really tasty Cuban sandwich with a Vegetales Mixtos side.  The staff were very friendly.  The Cuban surprised me when it had ground ham and pork instead of the sliced meat I've had elsewhere.  They also add mayonnaise and butter to the standard sandwich (Swiss, mustard, sliced dill pickle) which kept the meat moist and tender.    The mixed vegetables were bright and thoroughly cooked, but not to the point of being mushy.  Light seasoning let the flavors come through.  (They do have salt and pepper on each table if desired.)  If I could suggest anything, it would be that the service was just a bit slow.  I was the only dine in customer around 11 a.m., so I was surprised it took awhile for my water to come out and about 20 minutes for my sandwich.  There were a couple "to go" orders ahead of me which I'm sure made a difference, but I can imagine that the wait could grow longer if it was crowded.  Friendly, and did a good job clearing my plate and bringing my check so that I was able to get out smoothly.  Overall, a nice meal.  They do have three lunch specials as well as some soup options that might be worth checking out the next time.  Review #502

Very nice sushi restaurant with enough Asian options for those who aren't huge sushi fans.  This strip mall restaurant was quiet and had easy to find parking right outside the entrance.  We were greeted right away and given our choice of booth or 4 top seating.  After our order was taken, it wasn't long before our soups (Egg Drop for my wife, Miso for me) arrived.  The egg drop was on the thin side, but had a full flavor.  The Miso also had a lot more flavor than some Asian restaurants I frequent.  Good overall.  My wife got the sweet and sour chicken which has a large number of puffed batter chicken that was very tender.  The chicken itself wasn't seasoned much, so without the dipping sweet & sour sauce, there wasn't much flavor.  She really liked the moist bites and thought the sauce had a nice balance between the two tastes.  She thought the chicken was the most tender she had ever had!  If only they had used just a bit more seasoning to fill out the flavor.  Note that the complementary fried rice was a bit on the dry side like it had been prepared ahead of time had been kept warm.  I got a serving of Gyoza which I found very light (non-filling) with a crispy crunch to the bottom.  Very good!  I used the dipping sauce and the savory/acidic tastes paired well with the dumpling.  Very good!  My main course was the Fancy Dragon, an 8 pc roll with eel, kani (imitation crab), cucumber and topped with avocado and eel, and eel sauce.  The roll was sized right making the pieces more bite sized than some oversized rolls I've had elsewhere.  The only negative was that the wrap of the roll wasn't overlapping enough, so each piece tended to split on the bottom when picked up (I tried both chop sticks and with my fingers to keep the ingredients inside the roll up.)  If only they had allowed that bit of overlap, I wouldn't have had to pick up as much out of the dipping bowl.  Soy sauce can leave quite a stain if splashes come from dropped ingredients.  The service was friendly and welcoming and even checked us out promptly, but didn't stop by to check on our water or iced tea.  Wait times were minimal between courses.  Overall, a very nice place to dine with lots of Asian and sushi choices....just like the title of the business.  Review #492

Wow!  I ordered a Cubano (regular size) and this sandwich was huge!  So many layers, so many meats!  I heard some guy ordering Vegan and thought he might choke when he saw my order.  Seriously, I think I could have ordered the "light" version and it would have been plenty.  I found some street parking down the street and strolled in for lunch.  This place has been in business for over 50 years and I thought it time to give it a try.  There are two little rooms for dining (some outdoor seating on Virginia when weather permits).  There was only one guy handling the tables and the counter....he was hustling, but had a great attitude.  When I looked over the menu, I saw that the salsa and chips were a menu item and come in three different sizes (starting at about $2).  There are about two dozen tortas that are named after celebrities.  It's a little odd seeing so many faces staring back out of the menu!  As I said, I ordered the Cuban expecting it to be similar to ones I have had elsewhere, but this is by far the largest I've eaten.  Somehow, the layers stayed in place, which I found to be an engineering marvel.  Overall, it was a good lunch!  Okay, I know I said the guy out front was hustling, but it did take around 20 minutes for my chips & salsa as well as my sandwich to come out. And the flavors of all the meats were okay, but not a real culinary masterpiece.  So, I'm going to settle on a four and hope that by my next visit that they will have enough help to keep the food flowing.  Review #267

I was pleasantly surprised at having my expectations exceeded with this restaurant!  I have had limited exposure to Indian cuisine (mainly overcooked buffets that were disappointing).  But because I had read a number of good reviews, I decided to give this little shotgun layout restaurant a try.    First, it is located near the intersection of Virginia and McCarthy, just west of where Virginia crosses over the interstates downtown.  I found parking along McCarthy since there isn't a separate lot for customers.  There is a sign (shingle) hanging out above the sidewalk that is pretty visible, but I found it a little confusing since the first name on the door is for the business next door.  (The doors have the emblem of Spice Box appear as a white decal on the glass.)  Once you enter from the outside, take a left to enter the narrow walk to the counter.    Spice Box began as a food truck, so they learned to operate in a small place.  There is a limited number of seats inside the restaurant so they asked if I was getting something for there or "to go".  The food items are located on a blackboard at the back of the counter area.  Chilled beverages including beer, sodas, and bottled water are off to the right.  I got a hint of the Indian pop culture when I looked up at the ceiling where posters of Bollywood movies brightened up the otherwise dark interior.  There isn't really a wait staff;  mainly, you walk to the counter and give your order.  They call your name once your order is ready...in my case, less than ten minutes.  Still, the owner's husband was running the counter and had a very inviting personality and was willing to make recommendations if customers were first timers.  (He recommends the Indian Tacos as the best intro selection.)  Having read several reviews, I went with the Palak Paneer and upgraded to the Spice Rice as my side.  It also comes with Naan (a flatbread) as an additional side.  The Palak (Spinach) Paneer (cheese) was delicious!  The spinach was light and flavorful, but without the overpowering curry flavor that some Indian foods have.  Very light.  Very tasty. The Paneer lent a nice texture with a slight chew.  The Spice Rice had a little bit of heat and a touch of cilantro which complimented the spinach as well.  (I frequently had spinach and rice on each forkful.)  This was a very pleasant meal for someone new to Indian cuisine.  It tasted fresh and the staff was easy to communicate with and very willing to introduce their customers to their cuisine.  Check them out!  Review #91

I stopped in for a quick dinner one Saturday night (4-16-16) right as they were opening.  I had been meaning to dine here for quite some time, especially since the restaurant once again made the Top 25 list in Indpls Monthly.    Being mid April, I noticed the patio was open, but the greenery wasn't in color yet, so I filed that notion of coming back later in the summer to take advantage of the seating out there.  I decided to sit in the bar area at one of the tables.  Since it was early and the dinner crowd hadn't started making a lot of demands, I was able to get a craft beer recommendation from the bartender without having to wait for attention.  I also was able to get my dinner order in to beat the rush as well.  I decided to go with the Pork Chop (10 oz?) with baked beans, bacon marmalade, house kraut, and vinegar pepper.  This thick cut chop was cooked perfectly.  I haven't been a big fan of kraut until recently, so this combination with the other items encouraged me to try it even more often.  Delicious.  I am looking forward to returning soon with my wife and friends.  Review #26

I used to live in Greenwood, so I was a regular customer for ten years.  A few years ago, I moved to another town, but find myself returning to this location for my oil change.  I really like that they keep my maintenance history on their computer so that I can see what is recommended due to mileage.  It gives me confidence that I am only paying for needed services.    I know some people feel places are pushy and try to sell them new equipment.  I find that simply saying "no" and not making a big deal about it has worked when I am asked.  Having been a customer for over 15 years, I have always been treated with respect and never noticed any pressure to purchase on me or others who are getting vehicle service while I am there.  I trust this place to do the work quickly and correctly.    I think there are other places that have cheaper prices, but with the money I have invested in my vehicle, I don't want to go to some fly by night shop or have to leave my car all day just for fifteen minutes of work.    Review #437

What a fun place to hang out to grab a fix for your sweet tooth!  This brightly colored shop is staffed with folks who seemed to enjoy their job and were really glad to engage with the customers.  They have a nice variety of cookies, brownies, and similar treats that looked as appealing as they taste.  There are teas and coffee type beverages and even some alcohol based options too.  Though it is located on the outside corner of a group of shops, you can park in the lot behind the shop and enter through a back entrance.  Note that the entrance didn't seem to have a large sign to call your attention to it, but if you pick the door near the corner, you can walk right in.)  These aren't your mass produced store bought cookies, so expect to pay more.  I think they compare favorably with a number confectionery shops around town.  Good quality.  Friendly staff.  Flavor worth the calories.  Review #449

I stopped by MashCraft on Friday afternoon at the urging of a friend who is a big fan.  MashCraft is nestled in the corner of a strip mall off SR135 (Meridian to those in Marian County).  After finding parking in the lot, I entered the main room of the brewery which has an L-shaped layout to the bar area with the actual brewery deeper into the building behind the bar.  Although there are some tables to the left, I selected a spot at the bar and inquired about my options for a flight.  Most of the flight selections are 5 oz each and since each sample is individually priced, I could select as many beers as I wished with the price floating along to match the number.  Most of my selections were very reasonably priced at $1.50 each while one was $2.    The staff was very friendly and informative and brought out my selections in the order that they are arranged upon the menu.  Being relatively new to craft beers, I tend toward the less bitter ales.  My selections were as follows:  MashCraft Gold - American Blonde (5% 25 IBU) was very smooth and a great intro to their brews.  Sunday Funday w/Grapefruit - Table Saison (Collaboration with Central State brewing) (?% 23 IBU) was far less tart than I expected from the grapefruit.  It definitely had a fruit tartness (with peppery undertones) but wasn't overwhelmingly tart like some other sours I have tried.  Attilla the Hunny - Honey Ale (5.3% 10 IBU) Wow, after the tartness of the previous ale, this beer seemed like a smack in the face sweet drink!!  The transition from sour to sweet was almost too much, but on it's own, has a nice flavor.  I had eaten before stopping by, so I don't know how this beer would pair with a meal.  The bartender suggested that it would be a beer for someone who liked sweet wines to sample as an entry to craft beer.  I agree!  Tart Bruin - Tart Belgian Brown (5.9% 22 IBU)  This tasted as described on the menu, but was my least favorite of the bunch.  I may be old fashioned, but I prefer my chocolate in a dessert, not in my beer.  I appreciate that brewers push the envelope with tastes far beyond the range of commercial big box breweries.  It's just that the farther you get from the "normal", the fewer palates it will appeal to.  So, overall, I enjoyed my sampling.  I would recommend bringing your own food or ordering something and having it delivered.  Choose something that you normally like with beer and see how the house ales pair.  Review #129

This new addition to the Zionsville food scene is a definite hit!  After finding street parking, my wife and I were greeted and shown to our seats in the bar side dining area.  The space is large with high ceilings and hard wood floors.  The walls are decorated with colorful art.  Our waiter did a fine job of explaining the daily specials and was good at letting us know options.  After placing our drink orders, a complementary bread and seasoned oil/dip course was brought out.  Very tasty, but the high sides on the rounded dipping bowl made it hard to get much of the sauce onto the bread.  My wife decided to try the Casarecce alla Genevese pasta dish.  It comes with shrimp and a pesto/cheese sauce.  She normally isn't a fan of basil, but the balance of flavor on this dish was very enjoyable to her.  I decided to go with one of the evening's specials, the seared halibut with asparagus and roasted red potatoes.  The fish comes with a kalamata lemon butter sauce which I mentioned to the waiter might be a deal breaker for me since I am not an olive fan.  He offered to substitute a sauce or put it on the side.  I wanted to taste the flavor combo, so I went with having it on the side.  So glad I did!  The sauce had a tasty blend of flavors which didn't overwhelm the fish with the olive taste.  Sometimes you just have to trust the chef!  The halibut was gleaming white inside and very moist and tender while the top had a golden sear.  Very good!  I will say that because they have such large rooms, the air conditioning blows hard and though we looked around to see if there was another table we might move to in order to avoid a chilly draft, there didn't seem to be a place that wasn't in line with the vents.  The lights were swinging (gently) from the force of the A/C, so it was pretty easy to tell it was breezy everywhere.  That made it a bit uncomfortable to sit for a long time.  Overall, it was a fine experience and I look forward to trying the outdoor seating when the temperatures cooperate.  There is a section of the menu that will rotate to different areas of Italy each season, though some of their standards will remain.  Review #1031

The food here was by far the best Indian food I have had from a buffet style restaurant.  As mentioned in other reviews, don't let the buffet setting discourage you by thinking it will be dry and overcooked.  On the contrary, the seven items I sampled were all full flavored and moist, with enough spices to let you know this was Indian, but mixed with enough familiar flavors that my palate was able to relate to it.    The staff out front was friendly, but did have a heavy accent which I struggled with understanding.  So even though I repeated my question about my dining options at lunch time, I am sure I looked like a deer in the headlights upon hearing his answer.  I decided to go with sampling the buffet, but I wasn't given much direction about how to proceed.       I wasn't sure if I was supposed to wait at my table or simply grab a tray and start helping myself (I helped myself like the other newbies ahead of me).  I could see staff milling about behind the buffet line, so I wasn't sure if I was supposed to have them serve me or use the spoons myself (I served myself).  I did find it awkward having to bend over to reach beyond the wall to clear the low overhang.  I could see most customers were expressing some concern about reaching over the hot trays to spoon foods from the second row of entrees.  It was interesting to hear the comments as I sat at the table nearest the food line.  It was easy to tell first time customers from regulars.  I also didn't get a bill when I finished, so I walked up to the counter and initiated the payment process.     And that is the difference between running a restaurant and a food truck.  Expectations are higher at restaurants when it comes to service and for folks who are new to a restaurant, having someone work the front dining area who can clearly direct customers is a must.    Review #347

While in Brownsburg to celebrate my birthday with our daughter's family, we decided to head over to the local CRG Dining facility, Boulder Creek.  Even though it was noon on Sunday and quite busy, we were seated promptly.  Although the time period is included in their brunch range, we opted to eat from the regular menu.  Our granddaughters were able to find items to eat from the children's menu which included a number entrees and sides.  Of course, they offer the trademark fresh baked bread and roasted red pepper infused dipping oil.  If you enjoy warm bread with lots of flavor, it is a must try.  I discount any review that doesn't factor this fabulous course in the ratings.  The menu includes a number of items similar to the Stone Creek franchises of CRG.  I opted for one of my favorites:  blackened mahi mahi.  Not only did I get a thick cut of nicely cooked fish, but it comes with dirty rice and black beans and is topped with a citrus guacamole. Highly recommended!  Other items that our group selected included a breaded shrimp entree with a large baked potato, a chicken salad, and a breaded tenderloin sandwich.  All were rated favorably.  For dessert, they offer a large chocolate brownie and ice cream dish topped with whipped cream and a cherry.  Excellent!  The only negative is that the dining area gets rather loud when the room fills.  I like to be able to engage in conversation while dining, so the addition of some sound baffling could help.  The menu remains pretty stable in this branch of the CRG family.  Although I love the creatively delicious options of the upper end of CRG, it is nice to have an option to have a favorite remain on the menu so that I can enjoy it time and again.  Review #187

Some times you trust your gut....some times you trust the skill of the chef and let him/her work the magic.  Tonight, I went with my gut and did my gut deliver!  And so did the chef!  For anyone who has not been here, Recess has a new menu every day.  To know what your dining options are, you have to wait until 2 or 3 in the afternoon to find out.  That makes it tough for me to plan a trip when: a. I live nearly an hour away; and b. Getting my wife and friends to go is tough to coordinate so that everyone is set up for an enjoyable evening of dining knowing their likes and dislikes as I do.  So, tonight while my wife was at her charity gala, I had a chance to try my only missing restaurant on the Indianapolis Monthly Top 25.  (I still would like to go back to Cerulean to make all 25 in the last 8 months.)  Recess has two dining options nightly.  You can order a flight of food for $68 (wine pairings are extra) where you get a four course meal, including dessert.  Your other option is to pick and choose the courses you want. Tonight, my two dining kryptonites were on the flight menu.  So, I had to go with my gut and resist trying the flight.  Once that was decided, I sat back and let the chef do the rest.  I started off with the sashimi salmon.  It was light and fresh and was served with shaved cucumber sprinkled with roasted sesame seeds and a splash of seaweed powder on the side.  I also was given some soy sauce as an option.  Very savory flavors for the fish and veggie and the times I dipped into the soy sauce, the salt complimented the flavor as well.  My second course was a Coconut sweet corn & rice soup, shaved beef, celery, and napa lettuce.  The coconut flavor didn't dominate the other flavors.  Instead it worked with them as well as the spices to form a subtly balanced dish.  At first, because it was served steaming hot, I was eating off the top and thought it mostly a vegetable soup flavor.  But once I stirred the soup, the heavier ingredients like the beef and corn made their way into the flavor mix and completely changed the emphasis of the flavor.  To the credit of the chef, I liked the soup both ways!  With my third course, I got a glass of Chardonnay to pair with my entree:  Judith Point Scallops, with broccoli, carrots, spinach, and celery root puree.  Even though there were only two scallops, these were thicker than most places I have had them...nearly an inch thick.  Again, the execution of the meal was flawless.  The scallop was tender and had no hint of "fishiness".  The carrots and broccoli were al dente and gave the meal a bit of crunch to compliment the tenderness of the scallops and spinach.  Nice flavors!  Finally, I went with the Maple Glazed Pecan Truffles (with a hint of coconut inside), served with apple butter and shaved honeycrisp apple roll ups.  The glaze created a thin but solid shell around the mini cake like truffles.  The pecans where chopped small and the apple butter (looked more like sauce than butter) was underneath.  The three mini cakes were just a bit too big to be bite sized, so I broke them in half before eating.  The cake part was fresh and light while the coconut strings added a bit of chew to the bite.  The crunch of the pecan pieces also worked well with the other textures and flavors.    The service was friendly and pretty efficient too.  My server Josh was personable and didn't seem  bothered by my questions about the food (I had several.)  From the moment I entered until I was out the door, my evening was five star!  (I even got one of the few parking spaces directly in front of the store since I dined when they opened at 5:30.)  Rev # 140

This huge park (82 acres) has so many amenities that I am already looking forward to my next return.  The appeal of the park is more as a nature and activity site than as a standard park.  Sure, there is a dog park and a playground, but the park is divided by a creek and has lots of trails that you can hike if you bring the right footwear or wait until the trails are a little more dry.    There are a two shelters on site and a paved parking lot well into the park so that you aren't stuck at the south end.  There is a lot of lawn space on the higher ground so visitors can engage in activities they may not have room for at home.  And one of the coolest features is the steep (!) hill that is next to the parking lot.  After a heavy snow, this becomes a great hill for sledding.  It has a nice level are at the top so that everyone can line up where they want to launch from.  I guarantee your can get a great workout from climbing the hill a half dozen times!  I like that you don't have to worry about hitting anything at the bottom or worry about traffic like when I was a kid and we used the streets to sled.    Review #632

This park is loaded with activities for visitors.  The park is called the Sarah T Bolton Park and serves not only as a spacious area of greenery for walking and outdoor activities, there is a war memorial on the south side of the park, a playground, a dog park, and a baseball park across the creek.  There is a lot of paved parking spaces and many mature trees.  All the roads are blacktopped and seemed well maintained.  Review #618

Our friend was visiting from out of town and we decided to take her to brunch.  Since it was Sunday, street parking was free.  Because it was around 9:30, we didn't have any trouble finding a spot.  Still, when we walked into the restaurant, there was a ten minute wait.  They gave us a hand held buzzer that alerted us when it was our turn to be seated.  (Note:  There are paper menus available at the reception counter to review while you are waiting to be seated.)  The room is colorful and very clean looking.  Plenty of space between the tables too.  Noise level for a full house was still very reasonable, i.e, we could easily carry on a conversation at our table.  Our waitress took our beverage order while we continued perusing the menu.  I had the coffee and the fresh squeezed OJ which comes in a huge water glass (maybe ten or twelve ounces!)  Very tangy OJ, not overly sweet like reconstituted OJ served elsewhere.  For some reason, my OJ didn't show up when our guest's OJ was delivered.  I mentioned it to our waitress and it was quickly brought out.  The coffee was delivered with it's own pot that allowed for at least three full cups at my convenience.  After a bit of a wait (by this time the place was completely packed and the line was out the door), our breakfasts were delivered.  My wife ordered the Belgian Waffles with whipped butter, powdered sugar and maple syrup.  She prefers them a bit crisper than most folks.  Nothing fancy, but nothing wrong either.  Pretty standard fare.  Our friend felt adventurous and went for the "Crabby Patty Bennie".  It was made from lump crab meat that was topped with fresh herbs and poached eggs on a toasted English muffin with lemon hollandaise sauce.  Excellent fresh crab flavor, brightened by the tart lemony sauce and complimented by the savory eggs and muffin.  On the side were a good sized portion of skillet potatoes and an Everything Muffin (Savory instead of sweet.  Made with garlic, onion, and poppy seeds.)  I would definitely order this!  I was quite hungry and got two orders:  First was the "Mr. Potato Head Casserole" with a layer of hash browns (could have been a little crisper) baked with sour cream, diced onions, spices, and cheddar-jack cheese.  These were topped with bits of breakfast sausage, diced tomatoes, poblano peppers, and roasted mushrooms.  Around the side was a nice ring of queso fundido creamy cheese and an egg (mine was ordered over easy) on top.  Excellent Mexican flavors that were spicy, but not spicy hot.  (Two bottled hot sauces were available on the table for those inclined to add heat.)  I also got the "Sweet Home Apple Bourbon Crepes" served warm filled with sweetened cream cheese, apple bourbon compote, chopped candied pecans, sorghum, whipped cream, powdered sugar and cinnamon.  More like dessert than breakfast, this beautifully plated dish was as tasty as it looked.    The service was adequate, but not exceptional.  I think there are just so many customers for the kitchen and servers to deal with.  Still, with all the running around our waitress did, it is hard to find fault, especially knowing that Sunday mornings are probably the busiest time of the week.  Sure the price is high compared to a lot of other chain breakfast places...but you get what you pay for.  If you want routine breakfasts that you can make at home, then this may not be worth your time.  But if you like trying new flavor combinations and food that whets your appetite before you take your first bite, then give this place a try.  I believe they have a franchise in Carmel as well.  Review #87

I stopped in at the Circle City Industrial Complex (CCIC) after lunch on Friday and was pleasantly surprised to see they have added a new parking lot on the south end, right outside the entrance of Centerpoint Brewery.  Seemed like a great place to start my exploration of the CCIC.  The open space had two main public areas:  The tasting room and to the left a separate room with tables.  Most customers selected to be seated at the long bar since the only wait staff was the bartender.  Like most places, the menu is on a board to the left side of the large decorative tap display.  They also have printouts with the current brews with a description including % alcohol, IBU, and a write up of the flavors.  I asked about flights since it was my first time here.  The flight portions are 5 ounces each with a minimum of 4 selections, but as many as 7.  (I got the 4 for $9 option.)  The first thing I noticed was that the names were pretty straightforward which made it easy to get a feel for the type of beer without reading much.  My selections were the "Gold", "Black", "Dopplebock", and "Winter Wit".  The Gold was a Kolsch (4.6%, 24 IBU) that had a really light flavor that I could see paring up with a meal.  Definitely the gateway beer for newbies transitioning from commercial beers.  I really enjoyed the smooth flavor.  The Black was a Porter (6.5%, 34 IBU) with a rich dark color and a chocolate flavor malt.  Again, this was a smooth flavor without any strange side tastes.  Pretty good overall.  The Dopplebock (8.0%, 21 IBU) had a bit more complexity than the other two.  It took on a roasted flavor with a little bit more kick since the alcohol content was increased.  Finally, the Winter Wit was a Witbier (5.0%, 48 IBU) that had a definite herbal aroma of coriander and cilantro which carried through on the flavor on the initial taste, but kept from building and avoided becoming overpowering.  This kept the bitterness in check from the higher IBU content.  As I drank more of the serving, the citrus flavor became more noticeable.  Very nice option for someone wanting to expand beyond the basic commercial beer/pilsners.  The bartender was busy, but had a pleasant demeanor and was able to answer questions about the beer, the company, and the CCIC. I found out that a restaurant was being planned across the parking space but since it was early in construction, hard to say when it would be available.   Since they don't make their own food, Centerpoint has a rear entrance where food trucks can drive into the building and run on building utilities instead of having to run a generator or their truck to power the food line.  So, no having to go outside to grab a bite during winter months.  The bad news is that the food trucks are only there part of the time.  You may need to contact the owners of Centerpoint for a better idea of the schedule.  Otherwise, you can bring in your own food options.  Overall, I was pleased with the beer and the service.  If you haven't stopped by the CCIC in a while, take Mass Avenue just north of 10th Street and find free parking there.  Review #241

Our group found our way to this restaurant near 56th and Post.  It was a little odd finding our way in.  The front entrance is located on a one way loop, but even if you go that way, there is a parking restriction.  So, you have to find the one way road east of the loop to come up to the restaurant from the rear.  Of course, there are no street numbers on the back side, so you have to look for the "Open" sign in the window to know where to go in.  The front of the restaurant is undergoing reconstruction which blocks entry.  This restaurant requires patrons to climb stairs to get to the lower level to place your order, so be aware that if you have physical restrictions, you will be challenged.  We wandered around the restaurant and enjoyed the numerous book shelves and local consignment art.  Not seeing the counter to order on the upper floor, we took the spiral staircase to the basement level and picked up menus.  There was seating both upstairs and down, but we were able to find a table not too far from the counter after placing our orders.  This is a restaurant where you place your order at the counter and then wait until they bring your order out to you.  No number system, so we felt it better to stay in the vicinity to be sure they found us.  All the sandwiches have author names or famous book titles.  My wife and friends all went for the popular Vonnegut sandwich with Broad Ripple chips.  Their sandwiches came with city ham, smoked turkey, kosher pickles, Swiss cheese, slaw (raw red cabbage) dijon, and garlic/pepper mayo.  All thought their sandwich was pretty good.  I went with the Dumas:  City ham, melted brie, molasses dijon, on a grilled cinnamon brioche.  The brie was gooey good and the dijon and cinnamon gave a complementary fullness to the savory flavor.  Our friends also added one of the salads and a macaroon.  The macaroon was large, but didn't make it to the car!    Overall, I think we all enjoyed the food and the atmosphere.    Review #273

Revery is our favorite restaurant on the south side.  We get consistently good food and whenever we wish to shake things up, there are enough options to break away from the humdrum fare of other places  My wife and I have tried their dinners, their lunches and even their Sunday brunches....and the flavor has been consistently good.    This morning, we decided we wanted to try out the back patio.  Island music was playing in the sheltered area with a live tree growing within the confines. Umbrellas were open at each table.  We grabbed a nice spot by the tree and could still smell the fresh cedar of the nearby fencing.  Today, my wife ordered the Pork Tenderloin and fries.  It was a respectable sized tenderloin (much bigger than the bun), but not so ridiculous as to be wasteful or decadent.  The flavor was good and simple as the Indiana unofficial sandwich is expected to be.  The fries were a bit salty for her tastes.  I sampled them and liked them, but agreed they were a bit heavy on seasoning.  Our waitress said that in future meals, we could request them to be less seasoned without any problem since each batch is seasoned independently.  I ordered the Chicken Salad Croissant with a side of seasonal fruit.  The croissant was buttery good and the flavors of the grapes and sliced almonds complimented the flavors.  I would definitely recommend this sandwich to anyone stopping by.  It was an absolutely beautiful day to sit outside and enjoy the warm breeze, good food, and great company.  So glad that Revery added this dining space to their location (downtown Greenwood at Main and Madison).  We will continue to have this restaurant in our "go to" places.  Review #41

It had been a long time since I had stopped in at Joe's...probably back when the restaurant was in its original location.  So, I was glad to see a lot of familiar images when I walked in.  I was greeted and seated promptly.  The place was about half full so my waitress did a great job of keeping an eye on me.  They have a team of folks who bring out complementary chips & salsa, clear old dishes, etc.    I selected the Mis Tres Amigos from the lunch menu.  While waiting, I munched on the extra crispy chips and real salsa.  Although the salsa ran out long before the chips, they have Joe's "original" salsa which is pureed  enough to be dispensed from a squirt bottle (conveniently located on the table).  It's rather sweet and has a bit of heat on the back end, but the recipe dates back to a time when there were few Mexican restaurants in Indy and the salsa had to conform to Hoosier tastes.  Soon, my lunch special arrived.  The "hard" taco was loaded with lettuce and cheese in a crisp taco shell with a seasoned ground meat base.  The "Joe's style" taco was a small rolled tortilla with the same ground meat inside and topped with a dark sauce.  The enchilada was another rolled entree but had a cheese sauce instead.  There was also a large dollop of sour cream on the plate to go with the three choices.  The flavor was okay, but kind of one dimensional like something you could get from a frozen food section.  Okay, but not anything "Wow!"  Of course, since it was lunch time, I got to hear Kate Smith's "God Bless America" piped through the restaurant's sound system.  The paper place mats tell the story of Joe's journey to Indy from Mexico and why he loves this country.  If you like nostalgia and Indy's history, then this place earns an extra star.  Although the service was fine, the food is best described as convenient rather than delicious.  Review #563

Just a few blocks west of Keystone (around 73rd) is a 11.6 acre park that is mostly open fields used for soccer and lacrosse.  However, in the southwest corner, there is a splash park and playground for smaller kids.  Conveniently, there is parking right near the children's area.  There are a few trees for shade and a single shelter.  During the "season" for Indy Parks, there is a permanent restroom on site with water fountains on the outside.  If you have small kids and live in the area, this could be a really nice park.  Otherwise, there isn't much to draw you in.  Review #734

First, let me say that having a Martinsville address for this location is very misleading since it is north of SR144 between Mooresville and the Center Grove section of Greenwood.  (Much closer to Indy).  I stopped in for lunch and enjoyed looking at the overload of memorabilia of "days gone by" that cover the interior of the restaurant.  I ordered the grilled tenderloin sandwich which was pretty tasty.    Service was okay and the food was enjoyable, but there wasn't much about this restaurant to distinguish it from other restaurants beyond the decoration.  Pretty much a standard menu of items.  Review #42

Excellent food!  Cunningham has another winner with Rize inside the main floor of the new Ironworks Hotel.  Like the sister restaurant Provision on the second floor, Rize shares a large parking lot with valet service available.  The restaurant is rather small and on the opening day, had a good crowd with just a few bar type seats and one table available after we were seated.  We were welcomed at the door and seated by the hostess.  Before long our waiter arrived to highlight a few items on the menu and take our drink orders.  They don't have sodas, but they do offer a fresh pressed juice combined with sparkling water called a Fizz.  (I liked the Strawberry & Mint.)  There are also different teas and coffee options, along with some alcohol based cocktails.  We brought our appetites, so my wife ordered the Cinnamon Roll and the Farmhouse Waffles.  The roll is huge, nearly six inches across.  Very shareable!  It is a brioche topped with a citrus glaze that is quite tasty and offers a nice layer of flavor over the plain icing you get elsewhere.  The farmhouse waffles were nicely presented and topped with a combo of maple whip, brown butter crumble, maple syrup, and sea salt butter.  Great taste with sweet and salty toppings and the whipped nature of the toppings made them very easy to spread over the entire waffles.  (She needed a to go box for much of the roll.)  I wanted to sample the sweet and savory options, so I started with the Potato Waffle.  The crispy grilled waffle sat in a base of truffle fondue, with a sunny egg, greenhouse greens with julienned radish, charcuterie, and Gruyere cheese.  Excellent flavor combos.  I was really surprised how well the greens paired with the waffle and fondue.  Definitely something to consider!  I also enjoyed the Honeycrisp  Apple Toast.  The toast is thick and was a bit tough to cut through even with the sturdy flatware.  But after a little effort, the combo of honey, peanut butter, chia seed, and bleu cheese were excellent.  It also came with greenhouse greens on the side which had a light saltiness to them which paired with the sweet and savory toast.  The apple was presented two ways and completed the fine taste.  So why not five stars?  Well, the service was a little below the level I expect from the non-traditional type restaurants in the Cunningham group.  I get that it was opening day, but the waiter forgot to check in after my drink was long past empty.  (He did ask as I was finishing my meal, but failed to bring my water.)  He also forgot to bring a couple small plates for sharing that I asked for when I placed our order.  A bit of training and experience should iron the service out.  What really got me was the noise level.  Much like Mesh, this place can be deafening once the crowd gets started.  My wife and I had a tough time hearing each other due to the hard surface floors, walls and ceiling.  Very industrial appearance at the ceiling.  At one point, a table of six had people literally yelling to each other just a few feet from us.  If Mgmt would add some dampers above, the experience could be greatly improved.  This is another great cuisine option in the Indy dining options.  The prices are on the high side for breakfast/brunch, but you are going to get flavor combos that you just don't find at the generic chain restaurants.  This place could rival Milktooth for the best breakfast before long!

I finally found time in my schedule to check out the new pasta/pastry restaurant on the resurrected Main Street of Speedway (6-7-16).  Rolling in the Dough is only open from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. Tuesday through Saturday, so unless you are in the area at lunch time, it requires some planning.  I took my wife and another couple with me to check out the restaurant.  It has a counter at the back of the seating area where you place your order and then receive a number for your table so that the staff can bring the food out to you (you pay in advance.)    I choose to go with the specialty of the restaurant, the Pasta Bowl.  I was a little disappointed that there was only one type of pasta available on the day I went (spaghetti), but since I was getting the marinara and meatballs, I wasn't put off by the lack of options...still, a pasta place should have been better prepared.  The spaghetti was freshly made and although I don't know if the marinara and meatballs were made in house, they sure tasted delicious.  The marinara was fairly simple in flavor, but had a bright taste that worked well with the lightly seasoned meatballs (tasted like some sausage seasonings in what appeared to be ground beef base).  Overall, the bowl was a great size for lunch.    My wife tried a half and half option:  cup of tomato bisque soup (thumbs up!) and  a half ham salad sandwich.  The ham salad was bright pink in color with bits of green pepper spread evenly throughout.  She said the taste was quite good.  Because of the perfect weather on the day we went, we chose to sit outside on the front sidewalk under the table umbrellas.  From our table, we could clearly see the southwest corner of "The Speedway".  For visitors outside of Indy, it could be an eye opening experience to see the enormity of the track.  Just an extra perk of the location of Rolling in the Dough.  I don't know if locals take time to really appreciate the amenities that are around us.  Our food did come out in waves, but the wait wasn't enough to upset any of our party.  I did finish first, so I chose to go back in and pick up a chocolate covered strawberry scone, which I ended up sharing.  I have had a lot of bad (dry and pasty) scones in the past, but this was a delightful change.  I could taste the freshness in the portion I was able to keep for myself! :)    Overall, I was very pleased with the restaurant and have recommended it to others.  They definitely need to have more pasta options available for customers and if they could have any pasta to go available without pre-ordering, that would be helpful too.  Review #2

I get that they have a lot of state brews that are hard to find around Indy.  And the service was fine and helpful.  There's just something about a bar with only one wall that left me with an odd feeling about the place.  It gave me the impression of the type of gathering at a wedding reception of a bunch of people sitting around talking in an open area.  There is a historic building, but other than being old, not much to see there.  Maybe it would have felt different sitting at the small bar, but if you sit just a short distance away, you might as well find a cafeteria to sit in for ambiance on par with this.  I like a bar to have character.  This comes off as rather bland.  I do appreciate that it was convenient to be able to grab a beer after ordering something to eat downstairs.  But if I wasn't already at the market, I probably would head somewhere else.  Review #184

Note:  I've never ordered flowers here.  This review is based upon the home decorations.  My wife and I love coming into McNamara Florist.  The store is like a showroom for decorating ideas and always carries something unique that I've not seen in other stores or online.  I'm not talking about country style knickknacks.  I mean beautiful accessories for the home, often seasonal, as well as candles, lighting fixtures, live plants, and elegant pieces you would be proud to set out.  And when it comes to seasonal, they have a Christmas celebration the first weekend of November.   That is when they have finished decorating the entire store and if you don't mind crowds, it is like walking through a Winter Wonderland.  Truly amazing things to see and grab a cookie or two!  Sure, the prices are relatively higher than other south side shops, but the quality is top notch....and I find you usually get what you pay for.  Don't be afraid to stop by and look.  You may just find something you didn't know you needed!   Review #1437

I found this restaurant when one of my Yelp friends wrote such a detailed review that I bookmarked it and decided to drive the 40 minutes to get here.  (Thanks Wanda!). She nailed the review, so I wasn't sure what I could add to her observations.  Where Wanda has had experience with Cajun and spicy foods, I am someone who has had limited Cajun exposure and prefer my foods to be full of flavor without too much heat.  SotSot came through!  I tried the Pick 2 lunch special selecting the Jambalaya and the Crawfish & Shrimp Etouffee.  Both entrees had enough flavor, especially the Jambalaya that was saturated with flavor from the smoked sausage. The rice tends to cook completely during the slow cooking process.  Yes, it still looks like rice, only it is more brown and very tender (smooshie comes to mind.)  The Crawfish and Shrimp Etouffee is also somewhat thick, but in this dish, the rice is cooked separately, so it is used as a bed to be ladled upon.  The rice takes on a more familiar taste with a bit more bite/chew...al dente.  This was the first time I had eaten crawfish and I honestly didn't recognize the pieces.  Everything blended well together.  (Note:  I was able to recognize the shrimp without any trouble.)  It was a much lighter dish than the other.  The entrees were served in a bowl next to one another along with a couple slices of buttery garlic bread.  The bread was fantastic!  Although the restaurant is undergoing some renovation, there is enough finished decor that I could get a sense of where the ambiance is headed.  Very cool jazz was playing at the volume where I could discuss the restaurant with the staff or just sit back and listen.   So, if you are new to Cajun food but have been a little hesitatant due to heat or flavors that you think unfamiliar, rest easy.  There is a depth of flavor in the smoky Jambalaya that is as familiar as any comfort food on a summer's day.  Review #132

As a second part of my Saturday lunch time excursion, I headed over to Ash & Elm Cider Co.  It is located on East Washington Street, two blocks west of Keystone.  The Cidery shares a building with a coffee company and has parking available across Washington Street.  (Sorry, no cross walk is marked, so it pays to be vigilant crossing the highway.)  This shotgun style setup is smartly designed with lots of brick and exposed beams.  I selected one of the seats at the long bar and ordered a flight of four ciders to sample since I have not had much experience with hard ciders.  The owners, Aaron and Andrea, were both working and were very friendly, seeming to enjoy my questions about their business and cider offerings.  I learned a bit about the history of cider in America while we chatted.  I also learned about the challenge to come up with a name for the business, that was unique, and not already trademarked.    Aaron set up the ciders in order of dryness-sweetness for best enjoyment:  Dry, Headlong, Semi-Sweet, and Idle Summer.  I must admit, I liked the Dry version best.  It was a nice cross between the familiar NA apple cider and champagne.  Really light and tasty.  The other selections took on additional flavors that ranged from Hoppy to citrus.  I thought they were all pleasant tasting, it's just that the familiar was closest to what I expected going in.    I also sampled the Sweet & Smoky Nut Clusters (mixed nut brittle, adobo, & cayenne).  This was very tasty and I loved the complexity of flavors.  Although not quite set at brittle stage, the flavor was still delightful.    I think the next time I return, I will sample one of the sandwiches or salads which are available in limited options.  Review #81

I have to admit that I had no idea what to expect from Three Carrots other than a handful of recommendations from Yelp.  Having found street parking a block away, I entered the main hall of the City Market and began looking for the Three Carrot sign.  Turns out that I had walked by it once!  The restaurant is located on the main floor of the hall on the south east end of the center aisle.  (The sign is hanging on the south end and is a simple banner stretched across the top.)  Once I found it, I was pleased that there was no wait to place my order.  They took my name and payment and had my order in about 5 minutes.    I am very limited in my exposure to Vegetarian dining, so I wasn't sure how I would like a soy substitute for meat.  I ordered the Seitan Banh Mi which came with blue chips and salsa.  The Banh Mi can be eaten like a sandwich (it is a little tough to cut with the plastic ware that is available.)  It came with "Seitan Shredz" which are marinated in soy sauce, ginger, and garlic and takes an appearance that could pass for a processed meat.  The flavor of the Shredz had a mildly spiced flavor which was pleasing.  The sandwich came topped with pickled daikon  and carrots, avocado mayo, cilantro, cucumbers, and jalapenos.  The mayo is very creamy and can be a little messy, but it works really well with the heat kick from the sliced raw jalapenos.  There was far more flavor than I was anticipating.  Really tasty!  (The menu indicates it will be spicy.)    There are sides available for an upgrade price, but I went with the standard blue chips and salsa.  The chips were crisp (except for where the mayo got on them) and the salsa was spiced and sweet.  Again, the flavors complemented each other and the banh mi.  Overall, if you are in the area and can find a parking spot, give this place a try!  Review #350

Nice variety of cakes, cupcakes, cheesecakes, and mini-pies.  There are even quite a few large cookies!  They have convenient parking in their lot on the east side of the building.  You can even order special event cakes, but I strictly stopped by for something sweet to eat right away!  The cupcakes were running about $3.75 each, while the pies and cheesecakes were a bit higher.  It's not cheap, but it isn't standard grocery store baked good either.  Good and fresh with lots of flavor.  The adage "You get what you pay for" applies here.  The service was friendly and efficient and the store was spotlessly clean.  Review #1703

My wife and I brought a friend to dine with us on a Wednesday evening in February.  We had an early reservation time (which worked out for us as a freakish snow storm hit Indy).    We were able to find street parking directly in front of the restaurant which was another benefit of dining early.  The atmosphere is cool and industrial.  Unfortunately, our seats near the windows were metallic and chilly as well.  The staff turned up the heat for us, but there was the initial discomfort.    I ordered the scallops and they were good.  The ladies ordered a steak cut which surprised me that they didn't choose a seafood option since this restaurant is primarily known for its seafood.  I am not sure if the staff was concerned about the weather, but since we were the only ones in the restaurant, it was not a good sign that one of the steaks was under cooked (ordered medium rare).  They also had run out of the wine that was on the menu that our guest ordered.  Just not a great first impression.  After we left around 6:45, they turned off the lights.  I think that this could potentially be a good place to dine, but we must have caught them on an off night.  Review #56

I stopped in for lunch while downtown and have to say that the food was really good!  I went with the Chicken Club sandwich which comes with Kettle Chips.  The kitchen did a great job of making the chicken tasty by using a cajun rub (I think) and getting a charcoal grilled flavor on the sandwich, while keeping the meat juicy!  That alone is worth kuddos!  The sandwich comes on a multigrain bread (sliced diagonally for ease in handling and eating).  There was also fresh lettuce, tomato, mostly crisp bacon, and mayo.  The sandwich was a little juicy so between the juice and the mayo, I was using my napkin more than most places.  Still, the sandwich stayed stacked without falling apart.  Again, kuddos!  The service was efficient.  I was greeted, brought a menu, had my order taken and delivered in a reasonable time.  I didn't need to ask for a water (with ice!) refill.  And I even got my bill promptly.  Good job by Bryce.    The only thing keeping this from 5 stars is that the atmosphere of the place is a little unfinished.  Maybe it is still being decorated since it just opened in January.  I like the Kyle Ragsdale art on the walls, but between the gray interior paint and benches and the dark paintings, there is a somber feel to the place.  The music was something I wasn't familiar with as well, so it wasn't an atmosphere that says "I want to hang out here."  Maybe some cushions on the hard wooden bench seats or a little color might make it more inviting.    Anyway, if you want to grab a quick lunch and have some really good food, bring a friend to talk to while you eat and you should have an enjoyable time.  Review #235

I must say this is one of the best shipping places I have been to.  Even though there is one in my current home town, I prefer going to this location (about 10 miles away) if I have errands to run.  They keep enough people on staff to help (although I still may have some wait, it was reasonable.)  They also keep the place looking like a professional business and have a variety of services to help for those things you may have forgotten if you packaged the box yourself.  No pressure sales, but just friendly suggestions.  The only negative is that they have a location that makes getting in and out a little iffy when it gets busy.  The lot entrance is very near the entrance of the shopping plaza and if someone is following too close or if a line is waiting to exit, you may not be able to get pulled in without risking a fender bender.  And they also allow parallel parking behind the pull in parking which doesn't allow much room for your car to back out.  Probably can't do anything about that unless they relocate, but it is one thing I would have done differently if I was setting up the business.  Review #1761

I was in the mood to try something new.  I had noticed this ice cream shop listed on Yelp and decided to stop in.  They are located in a big shopping center with lots of parking.  The dining area and the order counter are quite large, clean, and colorful.  It's a lot to take in before being greeted by the owner.  I noticed that most of the labels were written in Spanish which I am not fluent in.  Fortunately, the owner was quite conversant in English and able to walk me through my choices.  I decided to try something called the "Mangonada" which is something I would call "Fire and Ice".  The frozen fruit drink is made with mango sherbet, lime juice, Chamoy sauce (made from pickled fruit and peppers and has a sweet, sour, salty, and spicy flavor combo), and chili powder.  There is also a Tamarind straw as well as a long plastic spoon for digging out the chunks of mango in the "drink".  The flavor was so different from anything I have had, that it did take a while to decide what I felt about it.  It wasn't bad, but it was just such a different flavor that I don't know if I ever truly appreciated the quality.  There were some bites where the chili powder landed squarely on the back of my palate and was hot enough to make me cough lightly.  There were bites where the mango was dominant and cool/soothing.  I mixed up the contents and when balanced, the sensation was fine, but I don't think I am a big fan of the combo.  The tamarind straw is another unique feature of this choice.  Tamarind is a tree based bean that when ripe, has a bit of sweet and sour taste.  The processed pulp clings to the plastic straw that is dipped into it (think of how a corn dog batter sticks to a skewered hot dog.)  The texture of the tamarind is a bit chewy (like eating a fig newton).  Also note that the bottom of the straw is covered and partially filled with the tamarind so you probably won't be able to suck the liquid through the straw until you eat the tamarind off the bottom.  And be aware, the chili powder and Chamoy sauce are what you will most likely suck through the straw on the first try, so be prepared for a blast of spice!  I would also like to note how generous the portions are.  I ordered a small and it came in a 12 Fl Oz cup with a rounded top that was filled to the rim of the cap.  I measured at home and realized this was a 20 ounce serving and was considered "small".  Yikes!    If I go again, I would probably play it safe and try one of their numerous types of ice creams or popsicles. But, it was worth trying something new so that the next time I experience a spicy and sweet combo, I will be better able to enjoy it by having a better sense of what to expect.  Review #1810

What a fun place to go with friends!  Our group of four dropped in for lunch on Friday and explored the main floor deli and the downstairs "Enoteca" wine cellar.  Food for lunch is available in both places as are take home items. What I found especially helpful was that you can pick and choose what you want throughout the place; maybe some soup and sandwiches from the deli, and some plates/drinks from the cellar.  You only pay as you leave, so you don't spend all your time at the register.    We had placed our order for some deli  items and then wandered down to the cellar and browsed around.  We grabbed a place in the Enoteca portion at a communal table and waited for our soup and sandwiches to be delivered.  Our group decided to go with the two most popular sandwiches and split them in halves. The Batali comes served on hearty bread with coppa, soppressata, capocollo, provolone, romaine, house-marinated red onions, spicy giardiniera, mayo, and tomato preserves...lots of spice and a bit of heat.  The Goose (named after Mollie the co-owner's nickname) has the same bread with La Quercia prosciutto, rossa, fresh mozzarella, basil, EVOO and black pepper. This is a classy ham and cheese style sammie, much milder flavors than the Batali.  We also each got a medium cup of soup.  The flavors of the day were Broccoli Cheddar (great taste, but the broccoli must have been pureed because the flavor was there, but not any pieces), and the Beer Can Chicken soup.  This was a hearty, denser soup with more of a kick than the other soup.  Both were quite good.  We also got some plates to go with our entrees.  The Nuts (almonds) were delicious and had a nice crunch.  The Olives came in a wide variety of shapes and colors.  Both were very reasonably priced and delicious as well.  I also picked up an unusual beverage:  The Raspberry Beer Float.  The float is made with two small scoops of raspberry gelato that are combined with New Planet's Raspberry Ale.  At first, the gelato was too cold to have much affect upon the ale, so I mostly tasted beer.  But as the gelato began to melt, it began to foam as I added the remainder of the bottle.  This took on a whole new level of raspberry flavor.   So, my advice, is to let the gelato have a bit of time to warm enough to create the best combination.  Everyone who helped us was friendly and efficient.  Several offered us free samples:  Today we were offered Chai, Tasso ham, and Muscat wine.  They appear to have frequent early evening free tastings as well.  So, from the moment we entered as bewildered guests to the moment we left feeling like welcome friends, the experience and food was great.  Bring friends to share the fun!  Review #119

I really liked this park.  There is a private parking lot (paved) that is an easy stroll to childrens' swings and two playgrounds, to a pavilion, and to adult swings, as well.  There are two shelters on the west side of the park and lots of mature trees for shade.  There are paved walking paths and for older kids, there is a climbing rock that has "fossil" imprints made in the surface.  The park is nicely spaced with nothing seeming too far away, but allowing the features to have their own space.  There is an elementary school as a neighbor of the park, so that offers even more greenspace to the setting.    Review #573

I had intended to try out the food trucks each Friday during the summer that locate on Georgia Street, so even though I was running late in the lunch hour, I noticed there were still about a half dozen options lined up serving customers.  After finding some metered street parking near Union Station, I walked the block over to the trucks and decided to try out NY Slice (it is based out of the south side restaurant).    I saw there was an Italian Sausage Combo option available and went with that.  The menu states that the sausage comes topped with peppers and onions, as well as with a beverage, chips, and a cannoli (all for $11).  So I placed my order, paid, and waited a few minutes for them to call my name.  In fairness, it was after 1 pm when I placed my order, so it is possible that there had been a run on that choice.  But for whatever reason, instead of telling me they had run out of peppers and onions, someone in the truck decided to add the chili sauce instead.  I carried my meal when called back to my car and realized that I didn't get what I asked for.  I understand that if they run out, they can't go get more, but they should mention it to the customers.   Otherwise, you get bad reviews.  See how that works?  The sausage itself was fine.  Not very spicy.  Just enough to tell it wasn't a hot dog.  But without the blend of flavors that the peppers and onions would have provided, the sausage was disappointing.  The chili sauce was supposed to be spicy as well, but it wasn't.  And the flavor was not the great when paired with the Italian Sausage.    Overall, just a disappointing meal for the price.  Review #2864

If you want a lot of info, read my friend Libby B's review.  There's a lot of cool stuff on her write up.  I also had a great time with one of my buddies at 12.05.    We found free street parking on Virginia Avenue and on College.  We met for lunch at Repeal (next door to 12.05 and owned by the parents of Nolan, the owner of 12.05).  After lunch, we headed next door to 12.05 for our scheduled tour/tasting.  Their website makes it very easy to schedule on Thursday through Sunday.  There is a $5 charge for the tour/tasting, but they are cool enough to apply that charge against any purchase of cocktails or bottles of spirits you decide to pick up after tasting.  (Note that you can ONLY tour by appointment.  However, you can make a purchase during their normal hours without having to schedule a tour.)  The tour itself is brief since the space is small, but efficiently organized.  I was impressed that they were able to answer very technical questions as well as speak in familiar terms when our questions weren't so detailed; i.e. they didn't make me feel dumb for asking the question! :)  As for the spirits, I am a novice at hard liquors, so I really liked the Rhubarb Liqueur (40 proof) with a great balance of tart and sweet without a strong kick.  I also enjoyed the New American Gin which is less piney than a lot of gins on the market.  They have recipes for cocktails on their website (including a Garden Daiquiri that combines the gin and liqueur with lime juice and simple syrup.)  When spirits can pass the taste test without all the cocktail additions, you know you are dealing with quality.  So good, that I bought a bottle of each!  Virginia Avenue is really blooming with great new places to eat, drink, and have fun.  12.05 is a fine addition to the group.  Review #478

There's a lot to like about Sahara.  The interior is very stylish and uses relief art on the walls that complements the rest of the decor so that you feel like you aren't in Hoosier country.  The food was also very good and was ready in a very short time.
