And even the tea set looks like something out of Aladdin with the fine details and a bit of rose water from an ornate dispenser to enhance the experience.  I started with the Tahini Salad which tasted really good with all the fresh vegetables.  The salad did have way too much sauce though, as there was a pool of sauce at the bottom after eating all the veggies.  Great taste, just a bit too heavy handed on the application.    I also ordered the Falafel sandwich which was served halved and wrapped in foil.  It was served warm, so I don't know if these are made ahead of time and then reheated or not.  The flavor was quite good, but because the sandwich was layered, there were some bites where I got the falafel and others where I got just the accompanying veggies.    One thing that I found different about the experience is that I was never given a check when I was finished.  I asked the owner/man behind the counter for my  check and he motioned me to come up to the side of the counter to pay there.  I did see a bill before paying, but found it weird that there was no communication ahead of time to tell me that I was supposed to go back there to pay (I expected to see my bill before heading there like most places that ask you to pay at the counter.)  Odd way of doing things.  To me, if you aren't going to conform to standard business practice, then you need to let your customers know.  I could have been sitting there quite a while waiting for the bill if I hadn't seen other customers head back to the counter on the side of the central area.  Of course, parking is always a challenge in Broad Ripple, but if you are lucky, you can street park for a small fee, or find a space a block or two away for free.  Review #2281

It's nice to have tasty food options in Mooresville.  Although I wish this was a stand alone business instead of part of a chain, that doesn't diminish that having Greek food available in town is a plus.  This is a walk in/drive up operation with an ordering process like a fast food place.  You order and a number is listed on your receipt that they call out when it is ready.  There are lots of seats inside with a small patio out front that could possibly hold additional seating in better weather.  I ordered a couple items to see how they stacked up.  The Gyro with Feta  was a pleasing option.  I ordered it with their standard options which include tomato slices, onions, and lots of creamy white dressing that can be a bit messy.  The bun is thick and a bit chewy, but generally tastes good.  The gyro meat was pretty good too.  Overall, a nice option, just not quite the quality of Mr Gyros on 38th Street.  I also ordered an Italian sausage with my choice of pepper options.  I went with the sweet over the hot.  I was surprised the cashier didn't ask what else I wanted on it, so when I got home, I realized it was just the sausage and peppers.  No condiments.  I tried that way and could tell the sausage was a bit dry with most of the fat cooked out of it.  I added some of my own condiments at home and seemed to enjoy it better, but must admit that it was definitely less enjoyable than the gyro.    Note that they do have burgers, fries, and even grilled chicken sandwiches for Hoosiers who are too afraid to try something different.  Can't say how good they are, but seriously, why even come here with a million other places to get burgers and chicken?  Come for the gyros and enjoy a nice tasting meal.  Review #1827

I was fortunate enough to be invited to a special luncheon at Prime 47 and had excellent service and food!  Although the menu was fixed for the event, I found the food to be flavorful and plentiful.  I started with a field greens salad that was enhanced by strawberries, candied walnuts, bleu cheese crumbles, and an apple cider vinaigrette, lightly applied, but enough to add the acidity to the salad.  Very sweet and yummy!  The main course was an 8 oz filet mignon that was excellently seasoned and though it looked to have a dark char on the outside (almost dry looking), the inside was a beautiful pink medium rare.  Very tender and delicious.  (Much more tender than the steaks I get at the market.)  The steak came with three nice sized grilled shrimp, russet mashed potatoes, and large grilled asparagus with Hollandaise sauce.  The shrimp were seasoned and had a nice grilled flavor that came through.  The mashed potatoes were mostly creamy and had several at our table oohing and aahing.  The asparagus were firm, but cooked through (maybe a little more than al dente, but not mushy).  I drizzled the Hollandaise and was glad I did.  I also grabbed a wedge of lemon and that rounded out the flavor to were it was another great moment in the meal.  The dessert of the day was a chocolate and cinnamon bread pudding with a dollop of fresh whipped cream on the side.  The pudding was just a little over baked making the sides a little tough to cut through with my spoon, but the flavor was good again (the chocolate seemed to be more noticeable than the cinnamon to me.)  Overall, it was a fantastic meal and experience.  It was only a short block away from the parking at Circle Centre mall, although I think they do offer valet service at times.  Street parking is metered and is tough to count on.  The interior of the restaurant is upscale and elegant. Substantial silverware is a good indication that this place doesn't cut corners.  Although pricey, I think the menu is in line with the other downtown steak houses.  Review #457

Check in before ordering:  You'll get five free breadsticks!  I was in the Brownsburg area and saw the great rating, but wasn't really hungry for a pizza.  So, I decided to go with a lunch special and got the Chicken Bacon Ranch sub with 2 bread sticks and a soda for about $8.  The subs come with a choice of wheat or white.  The breadsticks come with a choice of marinara or cheese.  Sodas are refrigerated bottles and they have a decent selection.  While I waited, I checked out the album and music related items that line the walls of the dining area.  There aren't a lot of seats, but I found the dining room larger than some reviews suggested.  Before long, they called my name and I picked up my order from the counter.  The bun was crispy as I bit into the unsliced sandwich.  There was just enough ranch to keep the sandwich from being dry.  There was a definite taste of black pepper which surprised me, but in a good way.  If you aren't a pepper fan, I would suggest looking at something else on the menu since it is prominent.  The breadsticks were fresh and had a little bit of doughy texture (again, a positive for me).  The marinara sauce was a bit disappointing....mainly bland without the spiciness that I was hoping to get after taking a bite of the sandwich.  Now, if they could take that sauce up a notch, it could be really good.  I didn't try their pizza, but watched them making them fresh to order.  They looked really good and I suspect the slices could be pretty generously sized on their larger pizzas.    I liked what I ordered and if I am back in the near future, I will have to give one of their pizzas a try.  Review #648

Downtown Mooresville has a beautiful shop on Main Street, Bud & Bloom Florist.  I was walking by today and was surprised at all the items I could see through the window besides flower arrangements, so I stopped in.  The shop is tastefully arranged with live plants on the right near the entrance, and the rest of the shop with zones for different themed home decor accessories.  There's even a table area with seating if you need to rest while shopping.  The arrangement counter is in the back so if you need help with picking out something in the front part of the shop, or need an arrangement put together, head on to the back to be helped.  Review #1935

It had been more than ten years since I last dined at Bynum's.  Then, I went with a company luncheon and the placed was packed, the interior was a bit dated, and the service was okay.  It wasn't some place I was eager to return.  However, on my most recent visit, I came away with a much better impression.  I returned for lunch again, and was surprised that the place was relatively empty.  Bad for them, but excellent for me as I had attentive service throughout.    The interior is all wood:  benches, wall coverings, beams (though they do have some interesting quotes written across them in gold).  It was rather dark since there are no windows to bring in light.  As I entered through a waiting area and then into restaurant, I veered to the right to find the hostess desk.  There is a bar area with televisions on the right, but I was directed to the main dining room.  The booth was formally set with black napkins and a small oil lamp.  Instead of going with the lunch special, I decided to go with their Signature Steakburger and fries, ordered medium well to get a good char. Before long, my meal was brought out:  A half pound of beef, charbroiled (great taste) with mozzarella cheese, sauteed mushrooms, and tomato, lettuce, onion, and pickle slices on the side.  The fries or potato wedges were hot and had a slight crunch to the outside, but were soft and steamy inside with just a hint of seasoning.  The burger, maybe a bit closer to well done, still retained its juiciness.  The flavors (except for the pickles which I ate separately) blended quite well and the burger was something I would gladly order again!  I'm not sure why the place wasn't busier except that I know a lot of southsiders think spending over $10 for lunch is a sin.  Their loss.  This was a nice spot to grab a quality meal in an area swimming with fast food and chain restaurants.  Review #2093

This shop is filled with items to spruce up your home.  Whether it's colorful candles, or original paintings, or maybe stones or table top items, there is a lot to check out.  Although it is located on 54th, they have a small parking lot in front of the building which makes it pretty easy to stop by.  Inside, it looks like an older building that had log columns in a previous use that are now mostly covered by a softer appearance, with a few columns left for support and visual interest.  My wife and I browsed the store, enjoyed our conversation with the clerk, and found quite a few items that would work well in our home.  We ended up picking up a candle in a colorful watercolor style jar.  Very cool!  The items I found here are familiar, but still unique to this shop.  And if you are interested in local art, they feature artists Kyle Ragsdale and Nathan Foxton (check out more of their works at the Harrison Art Center at 15th and Delaware.)  Review #2158

Lots of reviews from my friends have summed up all the pertinent details.  Let me just say that I enjoyed each of the "bites" that I sampled and got a hot cup of coffee that made for an excellent first visit.  The sizes of the confections are literally bite sized (at most two bites if you are trying to make them last!)  I sampled one of the chilled "shooters", the Banana Pudding.  Excellent!  I also picked up a couple "cream pies" which were oatmeal raisin cookies with lots of vanilla icing in the middle.  (Double yum!)  And I liked the fresh macarons in their bright colors and unique flavors.    They also have a variety of coffee and non-coffee options.  I like my caffeine simple:  black coffee.  It was served hot and they even asked if I needed to save room for cream, which I didn't, so they filled it up.  I don't care for scalding hot coffee, so I was glad mine had a decent temperature, but not so hot that I would need to wait until after lunch to drink it?  (Seriously, do some places serve it so hot in order to scald your taste buds so that you can't tell how it tastes?)  Service was welcoming and friendly throughout my purchase experience.  I would definitely recommend stopping here and expect to stop again the next time I am in the area.  Review #418  p.s.  I know coffee and tea have to be heated to certain temperatures to unlock the flavor, but once there, it doesn't need to stay that hot.

After some appointments early in the morning, my wife and I decided to check out this restaurant that was in the vicinity.  Their sign along 86th Street is hard to read (kind of brown with black letters outlined in white) but we saw it and finally figured out which entrance to pull in since there are several strip malls east of Ditch, but they aren't connected.  But once we got there, we were pleased with the place.  The interior was a bit dark, but seemed clean, not too loud, and we were greeted by a host who offered a selection of seating options and let us know who our server would be.  There was a wide range of food options with prices that are a bit higher than an "average" lunch, but lower than dinner.  We had heard that portion sizes ran large, so we passed on the appetizers and went straight for the meals.  My wife has been on a Mexican food kick lately and decided to go with a Taco Salad.  It is interesting to me to see how many different ways these are served.  In this case, she got a 12" plate with a thin shelled tortilla and all the usual ingredients were arranged as you would expect on a pizza.  When it was delivered and my wife was asked if she needed anything else, she immediately said "a to go box!"  And she did.  Good flavor, just a whole lot to eat at one time.  I decided to go with something different from the patterns I've been in lately when trying to compare one place to another.  So, I got the Baja Fish Tacos which come with a serving of Cuban black beans and rice (same bowl, but with the beans on top.)  The tacos were very lightly dressed with an avocado lime drizzle for acidity.  The fish was made with a delightful blackened spice that contrasted the shredded green lettuce (listed as green cabbage on the menu) and the pico de gallo.  There were three tacos in the meal.  Very tasty and I would gladly recommend them.  Overall, the restaurant and our service were quite good, with water refills and checkout in timely manner.  The staff was friendly and it made for a nice respite after a busy morning.    Review #2264

I met a friend for lunch on the south side of Indy at Thai Recipes.  It's located at the first intersection as you exit I-465 at the US31 exit in a strip mall on the right hand side.  There was plenty of parking out front, so I entered and waited for my friend to join me.  While waiting, I ordered the Chang Pilsner Beer from Thailand.  It has won awards for Asia's best beer and is served chilled in a bottle at the restaurant.  Very tasty for a pilsner!  (Note:  Chang means Elephant.)  My friend soon arrived and we placed our orders.  The restaurant has 13 lunch specials that make it easier for those unfamiliar with the Thai language to place orders.  All the lunch specials come with vegetarian Thom Yum Soup (somewhat spicy hot) and vegetarian Spring Rolls (deep fried and crispy).  Most of the entrees come with your choice of beef, pork, chicken, shrimp, or tofu as your protein.  They also come with your choice of "heat" as mild, medium, hot, and Thai hot!  Finally, some of the entrees also come with steamed Jasmine rice, but apparently only the ones that don't come with big noodles.  (I found it a little confusing on the menu when I didn't get the rice, but my friend did, so I asked the owner.)  For an additional fee, you can get brown rice and fried rice as well.  For my lunch special, I went with the #2 Padd See Ew with beef (medium heat for my first try here.)  The entree comes with large, slippery tasty noodles, small pieces of beef, egg, carrot, broccoli, snow peas and covered with a sweet soy sauce.  The plate was also garnished with decorative shredded carrots and red cabbage that fit in well with the other food items.  The fresh veggies were cooked al dente, so there was a nice crunchiness to go along with the tender noodles and beef.  Everything on the plate blended well together.  I highly recommend ordering this if you are new to Thai Food.  The "medium" heat was enough to feel on my throat without any burning sensation.  My friend opted for the #12 Massaman Curry with Chicken (medium heat).  The Chicken came in a bowl with coconut milk, massaman curry paste (yellow), potato chunks (slightly larger than bite size, but tender enough to cut with a fork), carrots, peanuts, and topped with cashews.  I got to taste a bit and would say the curry is the most dominant initial flavor, but that the nuttiness of the peanuts/cashews definitely came through.  Pretty good, but since I am a novice with curry, I think I preferred my dish more.  It's a clean, bright restaurant that is much larger on the inside than it appears by looking at the storefront.  It is a family run business and the owner was on site to answer any questions.  The service was attentive, frequently filling our water and my friend's ice tea.  Counting the beer and tip, my lunch was only $16.  Definitely worth returning to!  Review #113

Another solid addition to the Greenwood dining choices arrived last December at the former location of Louie's.  The new place has covered outdoor dining, plenty of parking, bar area seating and a separate dining room area that is kid friendly.  They have a full service bar with a nice selection of drafts as well as a large number of bottled/canned craft beers.    I stopped in for lunch and started with the Crispy Brussels Sprouts.  These were halved and deep fried with a bit of salt seasoning and a house mustard sauce for dipping.  Excellent!  The serve them in a brown paper lined dish that really soaks up the excess oil to keep the sprouts from becoming too messy.  The portion could be shared, but I had no problem devouring it myself.  I also had the Indiana Tenderloin with fries.  The tenderloin can be breaded or grilled.  The fries can be substituted out for cole slaw, or several other sides.  My tenderloin was a reasonable size, not some ridiculous slab.  The bread and toppings were good, but the breading of the tenderloin itself was under seasoned.  So, the bites beyond the sandwich portion were bland.  Still, the meat was served hot and moist inside, while the breading was cooked properly to add a little crunch.  The fries were a bit on the salty side, so eating the combination of tenderloin and fries together worked out well.  The service was friendly and brought any thing I asked for promptly.  I think on my next visit I will go for one of the house burgers that seem to be their specialty.  Review #260

Delicious food option that can be as good as your ability to blend flavors.  When you enter (after pay street parking), there is an order counter with menu checklists that walk you through how to have your poke built.  Simply start at the top and check the boxes that you want (each section tells you if you can pick more than one item in that group or if there are fees for adding more.)  I started with a base (Burrito style for me, bowl for my wife, and a third option for a salad bowl.)  Then I chose a type of rice or noodle, then a type of green to add (spinach for me).    You can add your protein next with different pricing for 1, 2, or 3 proteins (Tuna for me!)  Step 5 has Mix-ins (as many as you want).  Step 6 adds flavors (sauces and condiments), and Step 7 adds crunchies and toppings.  Finally, you indicate take out or dine in and put your name on it.  Tell the cashier your beverage preference and pay and they give you a buzzer that will let you know when to pick up your order.  The interior has a blonde wood throughout that looks fresh and new.  The interior is small, but feels spacious.  They have two gender neutral bathrooms, but be aware one has the light switch on the outside.  Before long, our orders were ready.  We both really enjoyed our lunches and found them quite satisfying.  My burrito style came sliced and wrapped in white paper, which once removed, revealed what looked like a seaweed wrap holding my order together.  The sauces/condiments were evenly distributed so that I got those accent flavors throughout the meal.  I did find the open ended burritos a little messy since some ingredients and sauce fell out the bottom.  I let the folks behind the counter know that it was that way and hope they begin wrapping the ends to make the meal easier to handle.  Overall, both of us enjoyed our meals and would gladly return and recommend it!  Review #1832

Although I hadn't tried their pizza, I decided to go with a sandwich and a salad since I was dining solo.  This chain restaurant from Atlanta opened their first area franchise at 116th & Keystone.  After parking in the spacious lot, I entered this large restaurant filled with colorful murals.  Turns out they have created a cast of animated characters based on mushroom themes and can be found throughout the store.  I entered and saw some folks working but nobody greeted me.  Since there wasn't a sign to wait, I simply headed over to the bar area and grabbed a spot at the counter.  I asked the first person I saw for a menu and received three:  a food menu, a beer/beverage menu, and a daily special menu.  I decided to go with a little Greek Salad and half an Italian Hoagie.  The salad arrived quickly with the dressing on the side.  The ingredients were fresh and the lettuce (romaine and iceberg) was crisp.    The hoagie was fairly loaded with meats and greens.  The meats were placed on the bun and the garden and dressing were laid out on top.  I was able to fold the bun and with a bit of tucking, was able to keep all the ingredients in.  My first bite was meat and bread, and though okay, it didn't do much for me.  But the next bite, I got the herb vinaigrette and some basil and the flavor went to another level.  I really enjoyed that sandwich.  Though I was thinking there appeared to be quite a bit of bun, I didn't feel too full after my meal.  I was able to get my bill paid and processed in a timely manner.  The staff behind the bar did a good job of paying attention to my water levels and seeing if I needed anything.  Overall, it was an enjoyable experience.    Note that they have a decent assortment of brews on tap if you enjoy having a sip with your pizza.  Review #2523

I could ramble on about how tasty the freshly made to order sandwiches were that I had.  Or get into detail how I really liked the tubs of side salads they carry in their coolers.  I could even mention that they had lots of local food items that many folks saw at the recent Yelp's Totally Bazaar.  But let me just get to the point that if you want to get something to eat that you can count on quality, freshness, and tastiness, come to R2Go!  They have some free parking on the south side of the building and I was helped right away by Chef and the staff.    So glad I found this place!  Review #473

I've been going to the City Market for nearly 40 years now.  In that time, there has been a major shift in focus on making the place vibrant and an asset to downtown.  For years after Market Square Arena was demolished, that side of the Mile Square was tied up in development plans that showed promise, but failed.  Finally, there is new life in the neighborhood and with it, the City Market has undergone some renovation and transformation to make it a great place for workers and visitors downtown to grab a bite to eat from lots of small businesses that occupy the central food hall.  Some have been there a long time.  But thankfully, there are some new places too!  Lots of ethnic foods, some vegan/vegetarian options, and some tasty snacks/pastry shops as well.  The building itself has a rich history that is too lengthy to include here.  If you have time on a Saturday morning, schedule a tour of the catacombs underneath (see a separate business review).  Outside, there is a plaza which frequently holds concerts and festivals on the west side of the food hall.  On the east side is a lending library, bocce ball, corn hole boards, and standing tables for people who want to get outside with their food purchase.  Now, if we can just get some more of the vendors to have evening hours, that would be great!  Review #3206

I stopped in to try their sushi and had a really nice meal.  After parking in the large lot, I was surprised how the interior transformed into a nice Japanese Restaurant from the plain and boring outside of the strip mall.  Lots of nice touches to make the place feel classy and still welcoming.  I was seated in one of the booths and immediately began looking through the long list of sushi options.  I decided to go with the Zionsville Roll which is an 8 piece roll with Eel, cucumber, topped with spicy tuna, avocado, and eel sauce.  I also ordered a Salmon (Sake) sashimi and a bowl of egg drop soup to get things started.  The egg drop soup was quite savory with a nice broth that wasn't too thick, but still had lots of egg/chicken flavor.  The color was pleasant and the egg was nicely distributed in small swirled pieces throughout the soup.  Definitely one of the better ones I've tried.  The Salmon came with three slices nicely displayed on the same plate as the sushi roll.  The salmon was bright and fresh, quite tasty even without soy sauce.  Nice texture.  Definitely good quality.  I usually get nigiri style (over rice), but didn't see it in my quick perusal of the menu.  The Zionsville roll was wrapped tightly so I had no trouble picking up each piece intact and fitting them into my mouth as a single bite.  There was a nice little crunch from some of the ingredients and the eel sauce added a nice blend of sweet, salt, and savory.  I usually get a dragon roll or something with eel, so I was glad to try something similar with just a little variety on my first visit.  Service was efficient and a bit on the quiet side, but pleasant.  Check out was timely as well.  Overall, a very positive experience for the sushi side of the business.  I would gladly dine hear again.  Review #1393

I stopped in for lunch and what a difference I noticed.  In my earlier review from opening day, the noise was overwhelming.  This time, the sound was at very acceptable levels while I waited for my "to go" order.    The hostess directed me to the pay counter to place my order and then after paying, I was encouraged to have a seat over near the "chef's" bar.  The staff was very friendly and put together my meal in about ten minutes.  And what a delicious option!  I ordered the Roasted Chicken Salad with an upgrade to the fresh fruit side.  First, the Chicken was so good!  I could taste the roasted flavor of the chicken along with the curry, roasted almonds, balsamic reduction, and julienned apples served on sliced cereal bread.  It also comes with a small greenhouse green salad that was tasty too.  The fresh fruit was truly that...a wide variety of berries and melons served in small bite pieces that were ripe and colorful.     If you are looking for good tasting food and want something different from the generic options served elsewhere, give Rize a try!  Rev #29

Let's see...they had everything I was looking for, they offer a 10% discount for 1st time Yelpers, they gave free advice on planting and care of my purchases, and they have a pair of mini donkeys out back!  Expectations exceeded!  The garden center is easy to find on 71st near Michigan Road.  The parking lot is gravel and out front, they have a lot of outdoor plants and a couple green houses. There is a large building for gardening supplies and a smaller building (climate controlled) for all their house plants and accessories.    Out back, there is a small barn with a couple mini donkeys and a quiet, shaded area with a gazebo and a small creek running by.  Very quiet and relaxing when you want to take a break from your daily routine.  I had some questions about house plants and about best times and conditions for planting some perennials.  The owner and the staff working were all pleasant to deal with and I left confident that even I could make the plant grow!  (Wish me luck!)  A very positive, personal experience that you just don't find at the big warehouse garden shops.    Review #2906

If you want any of the popular Asian dishes for lunch or dinner, give Tian Fu a try!  They have multinational offerings from the Pacific Rim including Chinese, Japanese (both Hibachi and sushi), and Thai.  They have numerous lunch specials and if your group orders over $45, you get a $5 off Yelp bonus!   I stopped in for lunch with my wife.  We entered the regular restaurant (they have another door for the all you can eat sushi) and were seated in a booth in the main dining area.  The lunch menu didn't list everything that I saw online, but we found that if you want something, just ask.  They may just have it!  We looked in the menu and didn't see a soup section so after ordering the lunch special sushi (two 6-pc rolls with Miso soup), I asked if they had egg drop soup that I could exchange for the Miso.  Yes!  Speaking of the egg drop, it had a pleasantly thicker consistency and some al dente vegetables in the soup.  The taste wasn't quite as "eggy" as some places I've tried, but it was a pleasing taste and my wife especially enjoyed hers.  I tried the Eel avocado roll (cooked) and the spicy crab roll (raw) for my lunch.  The spicy crab had a nice flavor with just a bit of heat, not too much.  The rolls were tightly packed and held together even when dipped.  The eel roll had a tasty eel sauce (I love eel sauce!) but the fish had a slightly stronger taste than other places I've enjoyed.  Okay, but not my favorite.  My wife went with a Stir Fried Chicken which comes with a soup choice, a filled wonton, and a fried egg roll (veggie).  She thought the meal was just okay, her primary problem was the chicken was lightly breaded and overcooked to give it a bit of chewy texture.  The roll and wonton were okay, but nothing to rave about.  Standard fare.  The staff was generally efficient and courteous, but not very outgoing and welcoming.  The atmosphere was rather dark with the shades down at lunch time which didn't help the experience.  Overall, I would eat here again, but wouldn't make a special trip as a destination meal.  Review #1809

Overall, I enjoyed the food (stromboli) I ordered from here.  I stopped in for lunch (to go) and after a short wait at the order counter, I was able to place my order.  This Greek's is much smaller than most of the franchises I've been to.  They don't have a featured bar area like the ones that I've given 5-star reviews to.  In fact, there are just a few places to sit with most of the seating at long tables.  Seems like this one prefers to be a carry out restaurant.  It took just over 20 minutes to get my order.  The stromboli is served as an open face sandwich with the meat on one side and the veggies on the other.  Both had red sauce.  The bread was crisp on the outside and not so thick that when I placed the halves together that it would cause any trouble eating it.  The flavor was good, but a little mild.  No punch to it or anything to get raves for.  The sandwich also came with a side of chips in the listed price.  Overall, it's a good place to get some pizza or sandwiches, but not a destination place to dine in.  Review #3165

On Bluff Road (just south of I-465 on the southwest side) one of the remaining retail greenhouses is still doing quite well.  Even at midday Tuesday, the lot was filled with folks selecting from the annuals, perennials, and vegetable plants from the numerous greenhouses on the campus.  There is a limited parking lot that is located by the front greenhouse which also serves as the checkout center.  A driveway on the north of the building is the one to pull into and allows you to head along the rest of the  buildings where you can park by pulling into the angle parking or using the larger lot near the rear.  (Note that there is a small drive between two buildings that allows you to turn to the south drive to exit.)  There are flatbed wagons that you can use to load your plant selections on while you browse through the sheds.  If you are getting more than one of an item, you can make use of the plastic shipping trays to load your choices so that they are less likely to fall off your cart.  Generally speaking, you will find veggies to the north of the first shed, perennials in the next few, and annuals towards the rear.  The plants we have purchased over the years have looked very healthy and well cared for.    The staff is generally helpful in finding a specific type of plant, but even they can be stumped sometimes and may need to ask one of their coworkers.  Still, they have good teamwork and are willing to help you find what you want.  All in all, a nice selection of plants.  Not the cheapest around, but they seem to be in better condition than what I've found at the big box stores.  They also seem to have a better selection too!  Review #2543

We stopped in after making reservations for an early Saturday evening dinner.  Overall, we had good food, generous portions, and a pleasant server.  However, there were a few things about the place that could use some attention.  After parking in the Circle Centre Mall, we strolled down Meridian and entered.  The interior of the restaurant is broken into lots of small rooms and a bar that you can partially see from the entry.  There is also a Host lectern that was unmanned, so we waited a couple minutes for anyone of the staff to greet us.  I don't understand the point of having a station for a host and not having anyone there.  But since we had reservations, someone eventually arrived and seated us to the right in one of the small rooms.   We waited a few minutes and our waitress arrived and took our beverage orders.  We watched as two other couples arrived and left because no one was there to greet them.  Some other people arrived and seated themselves at the bar.  It was becoming a pattern of confusion about seating.  After our beverages arrive, we quickly placed our orders to make sure the food was put in the queue.  Although we never had that long to wait, we rarely saw any staff during the visit because of our secluded room.  It felt odd.    By mid-meal, we noticed that one of the male servers was telling guests that there was a 30 minute wait.  We had a 6-person table in our nook that was unfilled and I could see a 4-person table unused across the way.  Did they simply not have enough staff to man the tables?  Again, it seemed like a lost revenue opportunity for the restaurant because ALL the customers who were told of the delay left.  Fortunately, our food arrived in a timely fashion and it was quite good.  I had a starter cup of Guinness Onion Soup that had a delightful flavor.  There wasn't any actual broth since their version has garlic bread cubes in the soup that absorbed all the broth.  The onions were so cooked that they were there in flavor, but not visible (they must have completely broken down into the broth.)  The cheese topping was melted and easy to dig through with a spoon which made eating the soup very easy.  Really good flavor.  The only real negative was that the house bread was a bit dry and without any broth to dip it in, it was less than I had hoped.  I also ordered the fish 'n chips.  A large single piece of battered white fish came with lots of seasoned potato wedges, cole slaw, and tartar sauce.  Good flavor without being overcooked made for a filling meal.  Note that they do have malt vinegar on the tables for those who prefer it to tartar sauce.  My wife got the Paddy Mac Sandwich with the corned beef replaced by smoked turkey.  It comes with cole slaw on the sandwich along with Swiss cheese, 1000 Island dressing and served on marbled rye and a side of the potato wedges.  She thought the flavor was pretty good but though the ratio of turkey to cole slaw was light on the turkey.    As I mentioned above, we enjoyed our meal and found our server to be pleasant though some small delays occurred.  I hope they can use this review to address the lack of a greeting to customers who are coming in out of the cold and have nobody to talk to.  Review #3332

I really enjoyed this restaurant.  I had mistakenly thought it was another chain Japanese restaurant, but this family owned place is located in an old house in old Greenwood.  There is parking in front, on the south side, and behind the restaurant, with a municipal lot about a block north.  There are steep ramps that help provide access, hopefully they are manageable.    There didn't seem to be a lot of seating, but since I was dining by myself, I sat at the sushi station.  The "bar" was at a higher level than most dining tables, but it worked out okay since anything that fell off my chopsticks didn't travel as far!    I started off with a seaweed salad.  This was brought out promptly and was both colorful and full of flavor.  There was a great sesame flavor with a hint of sweetness.  The seaweed had a nice texture without being chewy.    Before I could finish my salad, my Tuna Tataki arrived.  Six slices of seared tuna with crushed peppercorns are served with the chef's special sauce over a bed of crisp iceberg lettuce.  The lettuce and sauce have a bit of a salty flavor that pairs well with the seasoning on the tuna.  Excellent!    And before I could finish either my salad or tuna, my "Hawaiian" sushi was ready!  The 8-piece roll was one of the best I have had!  Eel with avocado, cream cheese had a creamy, buttery flavor.  Topped with Eel sauce, the combo was something I would recommend for someone who isn't a big seafood fan since the other flavors were so approachable.  (They would just have to get passed the word "eel"!    The only negatives I can mention were that the sushi was on the higher price end compared to other restaurants.  Excellent flavor, but it is pricey.  And the television in the sushi room was tuned to "the People's Court", not exactly what I expect while dining on sushi. :)    Review #288

Instead of telling you all the details about parking and ordering, I'm simply telling you that this is great ice cream with wonderful flavor options.  I first tried Graeter's eight years ago and it is my favorite chain of ice cream shops....also it's available at my grocery store.  If you have put off trying this, that's okay.  It just leaves more for me!  Review #1722

Solid four stars, maybe 4.5!  I stopped in on a Saturday for a lunch and was impressed with the service and the food.  I was greeted and seated in the back dining area.  There was only one woman running the front of the house, greeting, seating, waiting, and cleaning.  I don't think she ever stopped moving!  I ordered the Italian Club sandwich that came with a side of chips and a pickle spear.  The sandwich was sliced in half for ease in eating (and for saving if you only want part of it then.)  The crust was crisp and not too thick.  So, it was firm enough to hold the ingredients without making the bite too large or leaving me with a lot of bread like some other restaurants do.  The flavor was really good with the four kinds of meat blending with the banana peppers, olives, and mozzarella.  The chips and pickle were just okay, nothing special.  They do offer beer and wine here and they also have a salad bar and pizza bar, but I am not a fan of picking up pizza that has set out for awhile.  I definitely think I made a good choice with the sub.  Normally, the waitress brings your check and you pay at the counter between the front and back dining areas.  Unfortunately, a small wall blocks the view of the back dining room when the waitress is manning the cash register.  So, I simply walked up to her and let her know I was ready to check out.  (Something that isn't too confusing when there is only one employee in the front.)  Check out was cordial and swift, and soon I was on my way having had an enjoyable dining experience.  Review #3294

Like many antique malls throughout the metro area, this shop is much larger than it appears from the outside and the amount of enjoyment you get shopping here will probably depend upon how your personal search lines up with the booths inside.  I did find that a number of the products seemed to have a decent quality though pricing is always subjective.  The owner of the shop greeted us as we entered, but otherwise let us browse on our own.  There are numerous small rooms towards the back of the mall, but otherwise, there is a long room with booths on the left, glass displays on the right.  Some of the rooms seem to have themes, like books, or clothing.  Note that the building shares space with a fireplace shop on the south side of the building, but they are separated inside by a wall.  They share a common lobby, but that's it.  Review #2201

I enjoyed my lunch here.  The place shares a large parking lot with several other businesses north of the local Kroger, so it was easy to find a spot.  The restaurant is huge!  Very large dining area with lots of spacing between tables (though the booths seem a little bit crammed together).  The interior is the bright and festive collection of images that makes it feel like there is a party going on.  I entered in the door they suggested and then walked across an expanse to where the cashier/check in stand was. (Seems like they should have the closest door be the entrance, but maybe they get too cold during the winter.)  We then walked back towards the entrance to get a menu.  (Seems like those could be kept by the cashier.)  Anyway, I was seated in one of the booths where I squeezed in.  Before long, I knew what I wanted to order and my waitress arrived.  She soon returned with a bowl of chips and salsa.  I really appreciate that the salsa was in a large bowl so that the large chips could actually scoop the salsa without being broken.  (I wish other places would realize this.)  The salsa was mild in flavor and had nice chunks of tomato.  The chips looked as though they were either made in house or at least had been heated before serving.  Nice and crisp.  Before I finished my chips, my lunch sized Chimichanga arrived with an array of toppings including a white sauce, lettuce, guacamole, pico de gallo, and sour cream.  Sides were rice and beans.  The portion of the chimi was fine for lunch.  Roughly 6-7" in length without huge folds of flour tortilla on the ends.  I got a lot of diced steak from one end to the other as I ate.    Good flavor, but without much heat.  They do have hot sauce on each table for those who like it.  Seasoning was tastefully done without overwhelming the flavors of the ingredients.  I finished quite quickly and my waitress had left the floor, but I was able to get the attention of one other waiter and he went back to get her.  So, good teamwork to keep my wait short.  I paid at the checkout cashier by the front and was soon on my way.  Note that they do have a 3-way liquor license and there is a bar at the rear of the restaurant.  However, I didn't try any of their cocktails/frozen drinks.  Review #3435

I stopped in for lunch after seeing Chapati listed in the top 10 of Yelps 2017 Best Restaurant list.  Tucked away in a corner of a strip mall at I-65 and Lafayette Road, there was plenty of parking in the lot for this shotgun style restaurant.  The interior is vibrant with bold colors and has several sections:  a lounge and game area, a central dining area, and an elevated row of tables (the large black markings on each table top are numbers 1 through 8 beginning at the door.)  As you enter, there is a stand on the right hand side where laminated menus are available to browse as you pick your seating.  Once you make your selections, you approach a counter towards the back of the restaurant and place your order.  The staff were very friendly and helpful, so if you aren't familiar with the cuisine or dining customs, feel free to ask.  I selected the Beef Bahari for my lunch.  The beef was marinated and then after allowing the flavor to settle in, a second wet rub is added before grilling.  It has a mild (or no additional spice) option and then three more levels of heat for those who are into it.  I usually like some heat, but find excess heat detracting from the flavors.  I was able to get a selection somewhere between the mild and first level of spicy and that was plenty!  I immediately felt a slap of heat on the back of my throat on the first bite, but fortunately, the heat didn't continue to grow with each additional bite.  The beef was fork tender and retained its moisture, so it was perfect!  There were two chapati flatbreads on a second plate.  I was told that I should tear a piece off and then fold it over the beef, adding some sweet onion and sliced tomato as well.  Before eating, I used the chutney (dark green sauce) for dipping.  Great flavor combo with multiple layers of taste.  The rest of the serving plate (9 inch) was filled with colorful basmati rice.  There was a light green yogurt dipping sauce available which I drizzled over the the rice.  Again, the sauce added a delicious layer of taste to the rice.  Note that they add some food coloring to the rice to make it appear more festive on the plate.  I appreciate that they pay attention to making the meal look as appetizing as it is.  Great food and service.  Attention to details.  Lots of thought put into making the meal enjoyable.  Treat yourself to something different if you haven't been here before!  Review #287

There's a new coffee shop across from My Sugar Pie in Zionsville.  The shop is bright and cheery, but a bit small.  The white walls have some whimsical murals on them.  The order counter is centered along the wall to your left as you enter.  There is single seating for those liking a view along the windows, some tables of different sizes, and a couch in the back corner without a table.  The staff behind the counter were very friendly and upbeat (always appreciated by me in a coffee shop!)  There is a menu on the wall behind the counter with the offerings they have.  The counter also had a sampling of pastries available, and beneath the counter were shelves with board games and packaged coffee available for purchase.  I decided to go with my usual black medium roast coffee and I was pleasantly surprised to hear I had a choice of one with hints of chocolate or one a bit more seasonal for fall.  I went with the seasonal which was ready right away.  It was just a slight bit too hot to enjoy right away, but I was able to take the lid off and it cooled to an enjoyable temperature within a couple minutes.  I'm not sure it was my favorite coffee, though I appreciated that it had the hints of fruitiness.  I would probably order the chocolate option on my next visit just to see how it compared.    The place seemed to be doing well with lots of folks camped out.  Some were working on computers, others were just chatting while others looked like they were just waiting for their "fancy" coffee beverages to be ready.  If you are in the mood for a coffee or need a place to get off your feet and relax after shopping in Zionsville's Main Street district, stop by this shop.  Review #3295

I really enjoyed my first visit to the newest Brewery in Carmel!  Not only were their beers tasty, but the food and service was good too!  Note:  This is one of those places that once you know where it is, it is easy to find.  But they don't have any permanent signage on Veteran's Drive since the entrance of the restaurant/brewery is on the back of the building.  I suggest parking in the midtown garage and when you come out of there, head toward the plaza that is in front of the Sun King Spirits.  Look to your right (east) and that's where you'll find Fork + Ale.  Looks like the plaza may actually get completed this summer!  As you walk by the windows of F+A, you notice that they are garage doors that will open the space up with fresh air once the weather turns a little nicer.  The entrance is towards the north end of the plaza and has a colorful and inviting lobby.  That's where you are greeted and seated by the hosts.  The bar is lined with numerous large screen tv's and has mostly high stool seating, though there was a single row tables (I think they were 2-tops).  The dining room is arranged with stand alone tables (4's) and conventional seating (no booths).  High ceilings and the aforementioned windows allow lots of light into the room.  More large screens are silently playing in the dining area but not as densely packed as the bar side.  Since this is a new brewery/restaurant, I decided to try a flight of their beers:  four 5-oz drafts for $5.  Great price!  Unfortunately, they only have three of their beers ready for opening.  But they offered a selection of any of their guest drafts (about a dozen or so to choose from) as an option to fill out their flight.  (Making the most of a disappointing circumstance).  The good news is that I enjoyed all three of their house ales!  I started with the Beehive Blonde (4.7%, 20 IBU) that was full flavored, not watered down like commercial beers.  Next was the Winking Cedar Brown Ale (5.2% 23) which had hints of chocolate.  My last house beer was the Hopping Around IPA (5.9% 63) which had lots of hoppy flavor but wasn't as bitter as many I've had.  Great gateway ale for those who want to try IPA's for the first time.  They are working on perfecting a Wicked 7 Wheat (not sure how soon that will be ready.)  The food side was also enjoyable.  I opted for one of the "hand held" options instead of a salad/soup/pizza.  The Beer-Braised Beef is served on a fluffy Hoagie Roll with thick chunks of beef, giardiniera peppers, fried onion crisps, fresh arugula, mozzarella, and topped with a creamy horseradish condiment (not too strong).  Make no mistake, this is what I call a "Big Mouth" sandwich.  It's served open faced, so you could use your knife and fork, but since it was listed as hand held, I took the challenge.  After a bit of squishing the bread together, I was able to fit the food into my mouth.  I wish you luck!  The flavor was really good.  The peppers added just enough acidity to balance out the savory meat and cheese flavors and not be lost by the taste of the bun.  Well balanced and worth ordering.  I let them know that I did feel the beef cubes were cut just a bit too large since they occasionally fell out of my sandwich.  I suggested cutting them just a bit smaller when compiling the sandwich so that it wouldn't be so bulky and prone to roll out.    The sandwich came with free fries that looked like they had been crisped in duck fat.  I really like that bit of crunch that goes with the crisper outside and a soft inside of the fries.  Not sure about what oil they use, but that's what it appeared to be.  Since it was only their second day, I had numerous staff/manager stop by to see if I needed anything or had any thoughts.  Seems like they are trying really hard to get off to a great start.  FYI:  This is an independent business.  It is not a chain brewery out of PA that has a very similar name.  I was told this business was started by the same folks that started the Stacked Pickle, a local (Indiana) restaurant chain.  Although I would like to see more house beers available from a business listed as a brewery, I will say that my visit (though crowded) was enjoyable and that I liked the beer, food, and service.  I hope they can continue to develop more options for customers to sample from their brewery side.    Review #2515

Each Wednesday during the "summer" months, there is a pop-up event where vendors block off Market Street between Delaware and Alabama Streets.  Some of the vendors are farmers with fresh produce.  The majority are selling anything from flowers to soaps, to sweets.  Just about anything they can sell from a tent and table, it's here.  What surprised me was the different approaches taken by the vendors.  Some were greeting folks as the passed.  Others were buried face first into their phones.  Guess which ones were attracting customers!  Seriously, if you aren't going to engage potential customers, why show up?    Look, you can find this stuff at your local grocery or on line, but if you want to change your routine and are anywhere close to the downtown event on Wednesdays, swing by and check it out.  You might find a fresher quality item or find something that you haven't noticed before.    Review #2682

My wife and I have been coming to this little framing shop in Greenwood for several years.  I recently was gifted an art sketch from a local artist and wanted to make sure it was preserved.  When I walked in, I was greeted by the staff and we talked about my options.  Not only did they listen to what I wanted, but they offered to show me some options that would really complement the colors within the picture.  They even suggested UV glass to keep the colors from fading.  They had a lot of options for mattes and for frames.  But understand, this isn't a place with a bunch of frames and they just slap your picture inside.  Instead, they have a lot of frame and matte options that are custom built to fit your picture exactly.  Having custom built frames does add to the cost, but if you have a keepsake that you want protected, this place does it right!    Although I was originally told it may take a couple weeks due to the slow down from the pandemic, I was glad to get a call that it was ready in only one week.  I was very pleased with the result.  It was easy to hang when I got it home and I know that the UV glass will preserve the quality of the picture for much longer than if they hadn't suggested it.  Not the cheapest place, but you don't wait in line for ever like at those big box places for someone to help you.  They aren't cheap either.  But this was a once in a lifetime gift, so I wanted to be sure it was taken care of and framed right!  Review #3794

Whenever I shop in a home decor/gift shop, I try to get a sense of how the owner is hoping to brand their business.   I'm looking for that "Why would I come back here?" appeal that makes a business a destination instead of simply going to a big box store to get something.  So when I stopped in after seeing a friend's photos of the shop, I first noticed that the staff was personable and inviting.  I really like when a place that is offering things for your own home makes you feel welcome in their business.  It sets a tone.  As I browsed through the different rooms in the shop, each was a little different.  There are some standard items like candles, knick knacks, some women's jewelry and accessories, and even a few toys.  But what I sensed was there were two themes that seemed most apparent.  First, the store is loaded with holiday items.  I came here just a few days before Christmas and the place was loaded with unique items that were affordable (though not cheap.)  There were ornaments (marked down by 40%), table items, and things you'll just have to come in and check out for yourself.  I also noticed a second theme that was promoting downtown Indy.  They had pillows with the names of neighborhoods on them.  Those would be great as house/apartment warming gifts.  Even the candles mentioned earlier had neighborhood names on them, though I am not certain who determined which scent represented them.  (Note that all the fragrances were pleasant, not some actual scent you might smell outside!)  And the staff were friendly and welcoming.  That goes a long way.  Although I didn't buy anything on this visit, now that I have been here, I will add it to my shopping list on small business Saturdays as well as when I stop on Mass Ave.  Review #3463

When I first became aware of this garden supply/nursery, I thought it was just a "pop up" shop located in a space along SR 135 that looked like it might have been a drive in restaurant.  The actual space extends beyond the paved surface and they have a nice collection of plants and shrubs available.  The business also has a very nice location in Brownsburg which may have a little better selection than this one, but my wife was looking for some specific plants and enjoyed wandering around while I mostly stayed by the car.  Unfortunately, the type of plant she wanted was sold out by the time she got there, so her trip was a little disappointing, but she thought the folks helpful and from what I saw, they had a large variety of things to choose from.  Just not the specific that we were hunting for.    Note that it is located on the east side of a busy stretch of SR 135 across from a fitness club, a Jiffy Lube, and a Mike's Car Wash.  So, getting in and out requires you to pay attention since there is no light to make it easy.  There is a central turn lane down SR135, so you can pull out there, but be aware that other traffic may pull into that lane while you are pulling out.  We simply turned with traffic to avoid having to make a mad dash across.  So, my tip is to be aware of time of day and traffic flow to make access easier.  If you are in the Greenwood area, give this place to try for your garden needs.  Review #3768

Note:  I only ate at the restaurant without shopping at the grocery.  I didn't realize until I started working on my review that there are Tiendo Morelos restaurants/markets all around town.  I don't usually shop at a Mexican grocery unless I am looking for cotija cheese for making elote.  However, I entered the grocery because the sign in front of the restaurant entrance said it was closed.  I clearly saw people working at the food counter and a customer standing there, so I went through the grocery to see what was going on.  Apparently, nobody had removed the sign and left a "caution" cone blocking the door.  Anyway, after the weird start, I enjoyed my experience.  The colorful dining room has lots of festival streamers hanging from the ceiling and loud Mexican music playing.  (Note that the grocery has an equally loud sound system playing something completely different so you get a weird stereo effect that is hard to tune out.)  The dining booths go about half way back into the restaurant on both sides.  Beyond the left side is a cooking area with a large menu posted over the top.  Even though there is a counter at the cooking area, you don't order there.  Behind you on the right near the back of the restaurant is a smaller counter with a cash register and a menu booklet that you order from.  Once you place your order and pay, you wait and they will bring it out to you.  Note that any beverages are sold in bottle form and are self-serve from the cooler next to the order counter.  The wait was fairly short considering they prepare the entrees to order.  I went with a couple tacos (with the cilantro and white onion) and ordered rice and beans.  Apparently the cashier had a little trouble understanding me when I ordered the Asada and Pollo tacos.  I was brought out the Asada and Lomo instead. (I was the only customer at the time.)  But, instead of sending it back, I like pork loin as well as chicken, so I simply added some green sauce (mild) and a few drops of red (supposed to be hot, but I didn't think it was that hot.)  The tacos were excellent.  They were served on double layered corn tortillas.  I usually prefer flour, but wasn't given an option here.   These were the best tasting corn tortilla shells I've had.  And the ingredients inside were delicious with the added items being colorfully fresh.    The side of beans and rice were forgettable.  Not bad, just lacking much texture and flavor.  Very bland and not much other than filler when compared to the robust flavor of the tacos.  The staff was friendly and the restaurant was pretty clean looking, so given the high quality of flavor, I would recommend stopping by to quench your Mexican food cravings.  Review #2698

When I lived in Greenwood, I used to frequent this place often.  But now that I live elsewhere, I was glad to see that the place has maintained the quality that used to draw me in.   The aisles are clean and orderly and generally, are labeled to assist you.  However, I didn't see anything specifically called "shelving", so I took a guess and headed back to the interior lumber area.  Success!  I like shopping in the digital age, because when I found a board I thought ideal for my new shelf, it didn't have a label on it.  So, I simply took a photo of the bin label and had it handy at checkout.  Easy peasy!  They also measured the board since it was priced by the linear foot.  Also easy!  I grabbed some support brackets from the facing aisle of the wood and was pleased that the man who worked the checkout counter was pleasant and efficient.    It looked like there was plenty of staff on the floor as well as at the customer service and checkouts.  I hate going to some hardware stores where you can't find anyone to help.  Looks like Home Depot understands!  Review #3703

I had tried a couple bottled varieties of Scarlet Lane when I first started trying craft beers and because of the strong flavors, I wasn't originally a fan.  Now that a couple years have passed, my tastes have evolved to where I enjoyed every one of the beers I had on my recent visit.  I was in the McCordsville area and was glad they had signs for the brewery since the street signs are hard to read while zipping along US36.  The entrance to the brewery is actually on a small road called Depot that takes you from Railroad St west to the back side of the warehouse.  The lot is gravel and so you park where you won't block doors to the other buildings and hope you don't get blocked in.  Since it was around lunch time during my visit, I had no troubles.  As I approached the main warehouse, I noticed a fire pit and some chairs for those who stay later in the evenings.  When I entered the warehouse, the bar was on my left with counter seating and then tables beyond the bar area.  On my right was the production part of the warehouse.  There were giant fans blowing to keep the place cool on a 90 degree day, so they were loud as was the music.  Fortunately, the bartender had great hearing so I didn't have to repeat myself as she pulled together a flight of four 5 oz drafts for me.  (I believe the flight cost fluctuates depending upon your choices.)  The four choices I made were all delicious!  I tried the Laughing Water Australian Sparkling Ale to begin with (5.5% 35IBU).  Clean and crisp.  Quite nice.  I followed with the Clown in the Window with Blood Orange.  This citrusy ale was based on my first beer but brewed with the oranges.  Another clear and tasty brew.  I moved on to the Salem Pale ale (4.2%, 40) which had a definite hoppy taste without being too bitter.  Great for my tastes. (Note they do have much higher IBU choices on tap.)  I finished off with a Dorian Coconut Stout (5.0%, 35) that was one of the tastiest stouts I have ever had.  Rich and dark in color, I was floored by the great coconut taste that was really prominent in the after taste.  Coconut sweetness without the chewy texture that keeps a lot of folks from enjoying coconuts.  Definitely worth a try!  I am really glad I made a point to stop by to give this brewery a chance.  The service was friendly and I didn't have to wait for my checkout.  If I could change any thing about my experience, I would have liked the music just a little less loud for that time of day.  The fans had already made it noisy enough.  Review #1036

I stopped by this deli with my wife after a morning of shopping in the old town section of Zionsville.  This place is a short drive from there on Oak Street, located in a shopping center on the south side of the street.  Plenty of free parking out front!  We were greeted and directed to the menus that were spread (each was the same) across the counter.  The woman who greeted us mentioned that breakfast items were on the left, lunch on the right to save us some time.  She was very helpful when my wife asked for the Chicken Bacon sandwich without bread, offering lettuce instead.  I went with the Reuben sandwich and a side of Taco Pasta Salad (and a complementary dill pickle spear.)  After paying, we were directed to pick a seat (we were dining in) and told she would deliver it too us.  The food arrived in just a short while and I found it to be really good.  My wife thought the chicken just a tad overcooked, but with good flavor.  My Reuben was served warm with a nice tart sauerkraut and tasty cheese on a marbled bread.  There was also a small cup of sauce to add to the sandwich that added even more flavor.  The only thing I would suggest is that the meat (sliced) was clumped in the middle before being sliced diagonally.  That left very little meat in the corner bites while I was grateful to have a big mouth for eating the center.  I did rearrange the meat on my own on the second half, but it seems like whoever makes the sandwich should have done that for me.  Although we enjoyed the food, my wife pointed out that the place could use a good cleaning (easy to do) and was due for an overall makeover.  I noticed our table hadn't been completely bused before we were seated and she noticed the carpet runner in front of the counter needed vacuuming (someone left a cigarette butt on the floor even though they don't smoke inside.)  And when you walk up, the front window that allows you to see in the restaurant was partially blocked by carts with soda and packages that hadn't been put away.  The place has been in business for nearly 20 years, so maybe if they looked at it with fresh eyes like mine as a first time customer, they could see the clutter instead of just being used to it.  Review #2214

What a wonderful spot to pop in for a savory pot pie or to grab a fruit pie/slice to go!  They have a different pot pie each day (some days have vegan options) and the fruit pies and galettes available every day they are open.  Half the business is the bakery which can be seen through the front window or the cut out wall that separates the customer side of the business that features a handful of seats for those who wish to eat immediately without having to wait.  I ordered a slice of Apple Crumble pie and the Sugar Creme Brulee pie as well.  Tasty crusts.  Yummy fillings.  And you don't have to make a mess in your kitchen trying to get something this fresh.  (They do all the hard stuff for you!)  I will have to stop by more regularly now that I know where they are!  Note:  There is limited parking in front, but an empty lot across College is easy enough to use.  Review #2102

If you want a quality sandwich, you can count on Shapiro's!  They have delicious meats, delicious breads, and generally, friendly folks to help you.    This location is on the north side of the food court inside the mall.  There are tables at the entrance and a large "L-shaped" counter that displays the meats and desserts.  On the right side, you place your order when ready.  (There is a menu board overhead.)   Once you pay, they give you a paging device that will let you know when you can pick up your order at the other end of the counter.  It is a little confusing since there didn't appear to be a sign tell you where to order.  It could also be a lost opportunity if you are hanging around the pick-up side and realize you have to have one of their pastries.  Do you get back in line to order or go without?  I decided to pick up a couple sandwiches to go.  I ordered a turkey and Swiss on house rye with lettuce, tomato, and mayo.  Good sandwich, but they forgot the mayo (or put so little on it that we didn't see it or taste.  And the lettuce didn't look fresh...somewhat wilted (should have been caught at the food line.)  Fortunately, we ate at home and had our own lettuce on hand.  Definitely something to be addressed.  I went with the Reuben which was delicious!  There was a lot of meat and the sauerkraut had the perfect combination of sweet and tangy/sour to match.  The sandwich had been heated to melt the cheese and I loved the crisp bite of the bread...even after the trip home.  The only suggestion here is that the kraut was all in the center like it was dolloped with a scoop instead of being distributed across the entire sandwich.  (I fixed that at home too.)  So, 5 stars for the taste, 3 stars for the execution which should be easy to fix with a gentle reminder from the manager.    Prices are higher than the fast food delis/sub shops, but the portions are generous (they have half portions on most sandwiches).  And the meat and bread quality are some of the best in the metro area.    Review #2802

I hadn't been to this restaurant/pub for a few years, so I decided to stop in for lunch to see what was new.  In short, not much.  They still have plenty of outdoor seating for visitors to enjoy during nice weather.  They still have a small table seating area with about a dozen seats at the bar (3 way liquor license, so you can get the hard stuff.)  They have a music machine and a pull tab dispenser near the door.  I was by myself and chose to sit at the bar since the only other customers were there too.  They do have table service, but I figured it was easier and would get better service if I was conveniently seated.  I did get a menu and my beverage promptly.  And the woman who took my order got the order right and processed quickly.  So, after just a short wait, I got my mushroom burger with an upgrade from chips to fries.  The sandwich came fully loaded as ordered and the mushrooms were generously portioned.  The other ingredients were also fresh.    But the burger was not that great.  It was roughly a half pound burger, which would normally allow for the grill to get nice and hot to provide a tasty char to the outside.  And some of the middle was still pink which can be risky depending upon the place you get it.  And with all the ingredients loaded on the sandwich, I didn't think I would be able to have it re-fired.  The shoestring fries were plentiful, but were unseasoned.  So, by the time they arrived, the salt I added from the shaker fell off.  I had to season my ketchup to get more flavor.    Overall, it was an affordable meal that was generous in quantity, but a bit underwhelming in flavor.  The service was thoughtful and attentive without being intrusive.  So, just an A-O-K from me.  Review #3740

I've been meaning to stop by here, but always seemed to drive by on days they were closed.  Today, I made a point of stopping in and I'm glad I did.  The shop is small and has a display case with a few types of cupcakes, cake "balls" which are wrapped in chocolate, brownies, cookies and Hello Dolly treats.  I picked up a variety and all had really good flavor.   The cupcake was a little dry, but the icing was perfect...not too sweet, no greasy aftertaste, just lots of tasty flavor.  The chocolate wrapping on the strawberry ball reminded me of the texture you get when eating a cordial.  The strawberry cake inside was great!  The service was friendly and kept up with the steady flow of customers.  I look forward to my next visit!  Review #1934

I stopped in for lunch at this nicely decorated Thai restaurant.  It is located in a strip mall on the south side of Whitestown Parkway on the western side of Zionsville.  Plenty of parking and plenty of seats inside.  I was greeted at the front an taken to a table.  They have multiple 2 & 4 top tables with one side chair seating, the other side a padded bench.  There is also solo seating at the bar that primarily features wine.  Since it was my first time here, I went with my go to for Thai:  Pad See Ew.  I ordered it with pork as my protein and medium on the spice level.  The entree was one of the lunch specials (about $9) and was preceded by a complementary broth/soup that had a surprising amount of flavor.  It had a few noodles which were difficult to maintain on the soup spoon, so I had to resort to using my fork to wrangle them.  Very good!  The entree arrived shortly after I finished the soup and it was served the same as I've seen many places around the metro area with a small side salad and a crispy spring roll with a dipping sauce.  The noodles were wide and soft and the heat level was fine for medium.  No real burn factor, but lots of flavor.  The pork was cut just a little thicker than most places and it was a little more chewy than I would have liked (probably just a bit overcooked.)  The salad was already dressed with a yellow sauce that had a hint of horseradish that I didn't expect.  Still good, but a little different taste than what I've found elsewhere.  Service was friendly and prompt.  I didn't wait more than a minute or two at any time during the meal for the next course, water refill, or processing the check.  Overall, a nice restaurant that is competitive with all the other Thai places in the metro area.  Maybe not #1, but a place that I would recommend for those in the area.  Review #3689

The library was a steady source of reading, audio, and video entertainment when I lived in Greenwood.  The staff are very helpful and I have gotten to know several on a first name basis.  Even after moving to Mooresville, I maintained my membership even though I now have to pay an annual fee.  In addition to the stock of materials on hand in the local branch, they can transfer materials from any of the JCPL branches at no additional cost.  I also use the digital download Hoopla to borrow electronic media without leaving my home.    Finally, I can reserve upcoming new releases so that I don't miss any of the entertainment that is of interest.  Review #63

My wife and I brought a friend to dinner which says something about the quality of this place since we drove from the south side....my third time dining here in a year.  My first two experiences were fantastic and well worth the middle to upper price range of Indy dining options.  So, it is never fun for me to write a review update on the downward trend.      Sure, most of the items had really good flavor (I recommend the Minneapolis Potatoes as a shareable side and the Sticky Toffee Sundae made with dates.)      But it seems like the items on the menu are the same as both previous visits 6 months ago and a year ago.  Don't get me wrong; a few favorites are great to keep customers coming back.  It's just that I expect a higher end restaurant to keep tinkering with the menu, taking advantage of different cuts of meat and sides to pair with them.  When I compare my dining notes to earlier ones, I just don't see anything different in the menu.  And maybe that's speaks to a lack of effort.    Our friend's steak, asked for medium-rare, was pretty brown with very little pink.  She ate it without speaking up, but I could see from across the table that it was at least medium, if not medium-well.  My wife, who loved the pork chop six months ago mentioned on the way home that the pork was much tougher than she remembered and didn't have much seasoning on its own....it just relied upon the bacon marmalade topping.  That is such a missed opportunity for building a layered flavoring that I expect from a chef.  I can make overcooked and under seasoned meals at home!     I feel comfortable letting the chef/staff know of problems with my food and try to do it in a nice way.  But not everyone does, and I don't feel it my place to make my guests feel awkward by calling out a food problem without their consent.  Sometimes, I don't know about the problems until after we are in the car.  I get that the chef can't do anything about it if we don't speak up, but that doesn't make the problem any less real.    So, I hope that this was just an off night and that some new offerings will be available soon.    Rev. #22

This restaurant is worth checking out for the friendly/swift service and the fresh foods.  Located at the north end of a strip mall near 136th and US 31, there is plenty of parking conveniently located near the entrance.  Upon entering, you make your way to the left wall and can a) use the hand menus, b) read the overhead menus, c) read the descriptions on large number of sides and toppings, d) ask the friendly folks behind the counter, or as I did, e) any combination of the above!  The first choice is whether you want a bowl item or a taco.  (I went with a bowl).  If you go with the bowl, then you decide between the white bowls (cold) or stone bowls (heated which will add a few more minutes to your prep time.)  You also need to decide if you are dining vegetarian or as an omnivore.  (I went with meat.)    The entree I selected was the Bulgogi Beef Bibimbap Bowl!  (Try saying that once is hard enough.)  Bulgogi is the name for the beef.  It is cooked thoroughly, sliced fairly thin and is relatively unseasoned.  I got to select from white rice or fried rice and then my 5 selections of cold/pickled ingredients to go with the entree.  I opted for carrots, zucchini, spinach, soy seasoned sprouts, and tangy cucumbers.  (They have a number of spicy ingredients including three kinds of Kimchi available as well as other tangy items.)  Since I was getting my entree heated, they top it with a soft fried egg and my choice of five additional finishing flavors.  I skipped the traditional hot spicy sauce and went with sesame oil, sesame seeds, green onions, and seaweed strips.  Once the bowl was brought out from the kitchen, I was then able to add additional sauces like soy sauce and "BBQ" from the area where you grab your utensils, napkins, and beverages.    I also sampled the Jujube tea which comes with a pitcher of hot water.  The tea is made from adding a spoonful of concentrated dates in the bottom of your mug.  You let the heat of the water breakdown the concentrate, or you can stir it a bit.  Note that you only get the one teaspoon of concentrate, so if you want more than the one cup, you need to resist breaking down the entire spoonful on the first cup.    Overall, the food was prepared well and fresh.  I think to fully appreciate how good this place can be may take multiple visits for you to dial in your perfect flavors.  Some items worked together better than others for me.  I also didn't try the kimchi in my selections (though I did get to sample them separately.)      Tip:  The food is served with the toppings clustered in small batches around the bowl.  It's hard to tell how much rice and beef are included under the ingredients, so I recommend stirring the whole thing together to get a nice mix of flavors in each bite.  You can always add the sauces you like a little at a time to taste test the combination you prefer.  Review #357

This is one of the better Thai restaurants in the metro area.  The service was welcoming and efficient in getting the food out, clearing away dishes, and bringing the check.  The portion for the main entree was perhaps larger than the better places I've been on the south side, but here, it only comes with a choice of soup, salad, OR spring roll;  Not all three like some places, or at least two.  I went with my standard Pad See-Eiw (spelled differently at about every place I go!) which only comes with chicken (at least at lunch).  The portion filled the plate and had large flat noodles, though they didn't look the same shape as the noodles I've had elsewhere.  They come in a sweet Thai soy sauce with broccoli (thoroughly cooked and bite sized florets), small bits of cabbage and egg.  I was able to select the heat level for spiciness and medium seemed to be a great choice for added flavor without making the meal uncomfortable.  I could definitely feel the tingle from the spice, but the hot tea I ordered did a good job of resetting my palate.  The flavor was wonderful!  I would gladly recommend this dish.  The chicken was moist and sliced into bite sized pieces that was nicely balanced with the rest of the dish.
