I ordered the soup as my side and it was a mild broth filled with diced vegetables that tended to pool at the bottom.  The flavor was pleasant, with more intensity than a Miso, but less than a Thom Yum.  Think vegetable soup to get an idea.  Overall, a very enjoyable experience with good service and flavor.  It's a bit more pricey than what you find at the better places on the south side, but offers the north side an excellent option.  Review #2073

First, let me say that I have dined at several of Chef Hardesty's restaurants over the years and always had a good impression of the food and dining experience.  In fact, when you enter this small shop across the Monon from Mama Carolla's, you can see a full kitchen set up for one of his intimate dining experiences.  But, being simply drawn in for a cup of coffee, I have to say I was a bit disappointed.  I've read the other reviews and believe I must have simply stopped by on a bad day.  The coffee was too hot (burned tongue) and quite bitter.    The shop doesn't rely upon labels either.  The hot coffee was from an unmarked dispenser so I couldn't tell if it was a medium or dark roast before purchase.    The best thing about the visit was the maple pecan cookie (the only type offered.)  The cookie was delicious with a great balance of crispness on the outside and soft, yet chewy center that was very pleasing.  This isn't the type of coffee shop that you come into to set up your laptop.  I was a little disappointed that the interior seemed a bit austere.  There were a few tables with chairs, but there was no invitation to come around the counter and grab a seat.  So, for me, it seemed like it was for "to go" orders only.  I'm not sure what the chef's desire is for the coffee shop part of the business.  His baking skill produced a tasty treat, but I can't say that I would be drawn back to a spot for just a cup of coffee and a cookie when there are so many other places in the area that offer more variety.  Review #3640

While on the east side hunting street art, I decided to take a break and stop in Wyliepalooza for a cup of ice cream.  This brightly (almost to the point of gaudy) colored place clearly targets youth, but a friendly greeting by the staff and one of the owners let me know I was welcome too!  They have a menu board on the wall that gives you an idea of what is available.  They also have signs on the shield glass identifying the tubs of ice cream.  I decided to go with the Cherry Amaretto Fudge ice cream.  Large chunks of black cherries were visible even before she started scooping.  The fudge and amaretto flavors were there too, all nicely balanced.  The serving size was pretty large for the price compared to some of my other favorite frozen treat places.  While talking to the owner, she mentioned that she started the business with her mom and have an another parlor in Brownsburg.  When asked about the name of the business, she replied it was a combination of her daughter's name and a slang term for party.  So, the youthful theme makes more sense.    I appreciate family run businesses that are willing to take on the big corporate franchises.  Keeping the dollars in state is helpful, but I mainly like supporting places where the owners are in touch with the customers.    Review #150

Maybe I should make it easy to review and simply tell you to read Nicole S's excellent write up.  She has a gift with words!  But just in case you are still reading, I will let you know that this park is located near the White River and so there are areas of the park where it is either a large lawn (used as a football field) or prairie with paved walking trails.  Unlike most waterfront parks, the elevation of this location seems to be raised well above the flood plains that many parks are captive to.  The sprawling 62 acres is fairly divided between the halves with the entrance road and parking lot also being centered.  There is a permanent restroom and water fountain building on the east end of the lot.  If you have kids, there is a truly unique playground which pays homage to ancient native american culture including a climbing mound and an archaeological digging area with plastic bones to discover.  There is also a small building that you can walk through that has an interactive area where you push buttons to hear about the daily routines of these early people.  There are also artifacts behind glass to look at and read about.  The trails walk through the large prairie area with enough spacing so that you can still feel outdoorsy without losing site of where you parked.  The prairie is also large enough that it could easily hide small critters and birds that may want to make the place home.  They do expect you to keep any pets you have on leash so that they aren't hunting down the critters.  You may not want to make this your exclusive park to visit, but it definitely is a place worth checking out for a unique play experience or a peaceful hike.  Review #798

After finding a spot for free street parking, I strolled down Virginia Ave to have lunch at Red Lion Grog House, located within the former G C Murphy building.  Because of the unusual layout of this former department store, many of the businesses with storefronts have a double entry, i.e. go in to a small alcove and then find the door into the business you want to visit.  Fortunately, this one has a large shield emblem on their door.  Once inside, you will see (barely.  It is kept quite dark inside) that the bar is a long, narrow shotgun style pub.  There is a small window seating area with a few 4 top tables, but the rest of the seating is at tables along the west wall.  There are a handful of seats at the bar halfway back in the room (about eight I think).  I grabbed one of the spots since I was dining by myself.    Since it was lunch time, I referred to the lunch special menu (note that a full menu was offered if that was preferred.)  The lunch specials are $8.49 and can be upgraded to a combo (soda) for $1.50.  I decided to go with the highly touted Fish and Chips, but upgraded my chips to cole slaw for an extra $.50.    After a short wait in which my beverage was presented, a basket with my fish (deep fried breaded Atlantic Co) arrived with a small cup for tarter sauce and another cup for the cole slaw.  The fish was fresh and thicker than I've had elsewhere, and was bright and flaky. The breading was crisp, but did tend to get a little soggy from the steam off the fish by the time I finished.  Nice flavor, especially with the tartar sauce.  The cole slaw was a nice blend of vinegar based and creamy.  The slaw was shredded to thin cuts and not too long to easily remain bite-sized.  Overall, a great choice to pair with the fish if you want to have a little color on your plate and keep the meal from feeling heavy.  For having only the one bartender/waitress working at lunch, I was surprised how quickly the service remained.  Sure, there was a bit of a wait as several tables decided to check out just before I finished, but it was understandable and not too inconvenient.  Overall, it was an enjoyable meal that had effective service.  If you are looking for something different from the run of the mill burger and taco places, try this British pub for something different.  Review #442

This was the first time we used FastPark and it was great.  My wife knew it would get busy around spring break, so she reserved a space.  Then, on the day of our departure, she drove up, used the email image on her phone to get in, and was told which spot to park in.  The ticket they gave her had the space location AND the instructions for where to go when at the airport to be retrieved.  Fair price, great convenience.  The shuttles are numerous and run frequently.  Highly recommended.  Review 2389

I love when a local business is successful enough that it can try something new without screwing up the place that first attracted the customers.  By now, most interested folks have heard of and maybe even tried Sun King's main line of ales.  With that success, they opened this second location to develop "small batch" beers (7 barrels of capacity for each type.)    The main location frequently gets some of these beers to mix into their line up of taps.  But if you want to try the newest items, some that haven't even made it to the main location, then this is the place for you!  I've tried over 30 of the Sun King flavors, so when I stopped in here, I just asked "What's New?"  The bartender directed me to two of their newest, and after a quick sampling, I decided to go with a "Brite as Helles" German Lager (4.5% 20 IBU).  It was balanced and had a combo of malted, toasted flavors and a floral hop.  Quite tasty!  The space was clean and open with a clear view of the vats in the next room and a long bar where you can grab a spot to enjoy your brew.  They do have some Oca sandwiches and cheese boards on hand.  They also include menus for order in food from nearby restaurants.  Note that this location is only going to be open for a limited time.  Once the mega-development "The Yard" (116th Street) is finished later in 2019 (fall estimate), Sun King will close this location and move to the new spot.  Once there, it will have a large variety of restaurants to grab food from.  Review #2143

If you like your barbecue moist and juicy instead of dry, then you have to try this place!  I ordered the pulled pork and was surprised how moist it was even before adding any sauce.  If you are coming from the east on Raymond, you won't have any trouble pulling into the lot just before you get to Keystone.  However, if you are coming from the west or on Keystone, know that Raymond is a divided highway (median) so you have to go down to Churchman and head north.  You can cut through the Burger King lot and get to the Pull Up lot or find a spot to turn around and come back from the east.  Got it?  Once inside, you place your order at the counter.  They have overhead menus as well as printed paper ones.  I ordered the pork along with a couple sides (coleslaw and potato salad) and they gave me a deal as "dinner meal" that saved me a buck.    The slaw is unsweetened and was surprisingly refreshing.  The potato salad had a creamy texture along with the diced potatoes and a bit of sweetened vinegar and chive flavors (reminded me of my Deviled Eggs flavor.)  Service brings out your order for dine in customers (they call out your number to see where you are seated).  To go customers like me can save time by meeting them at the counter.  The only thing I would have liked better about the sandwich was that the pork didn't seem to have any blackened sear on it.  None of that deep roasted flavor.  But it was still good.  I also didn't get any sauce in my to go order.  I thought the woman behind the counter asked me if I wanted toast, but maybe I misunderstood her.  They do have bottles on the counter of several flavors, but I'm not sure how they handle to go orders.    Anyway, it was good food at a reasonable price with pleasant service.  Sounds like a good recipe for success!  Review #2605

What a delightful little shop in downtown Plainfield!  I went on their second day as a brick and mortar shop and timed it when the line was fairly small.  The only problem with their layout is that it is hard to see the actual goodies while you wait in line (note that you can see the menu board which helps.)    The shop is arranged with a bank of high stools / bar along the window, the goodies / order counter on the left, and the payment counter / coffee supplies on the right.  The menu consists of mostly desserts.  They have cookies, cupcakes, brownies, cobbler, pie, and cheesecake.  They also had one kind of cake when I stopped by.    I found it interesting that the window shows the time they open, but not closing times.  I think they go until the food is gone.  In fact, by 10 a.m. the brownies were sold out!    I decided to go with a blackberry cobbler (large serving!) and a slice of apple pie.  The cobbler had a delightful flavor, but instead of most cobblers I've had, this had a pillow-y dough.  Not simply under cooked...it was lighter than most doughs.  Not what I expected.  The pie had a nice tart apple which was less sweet than most I've had.  The crust was more crisp than the cobbler, but still not as crisp as I prefer.  The bottom got a little soggy.     So, good flavor, but just the dough part isn't my preference.  The coffee had a really rich, delicious flavor.  Unfortunately, the temp it was served at was simply too hot to drink right away.  Four hours later and my palate is still tingly from that first sip.  This place is a nice addition to the downtown Plainfield area.  The flavors are really good.  I would just prefer a few tweaks on how done the crusts are and the coffee temp.    Great service and fair pricing.  Review #2599

Scarlet Lane has some really tasty beers, with a great number of them in the IPA and Stout categories.  This is the second of two tap houses to open around town in recent months in addition to the home McCordsville brewery.  Although no food is available at this location, they are across the street from Next Door and share the same building as a future Top Chef operated restaurant (I think it will be called Stiltsville), so getting food should not be a problem.  The interior is some what industrial but has a couple large murals to keep the place from becoming sterile.    The staff was friendly and even though the bar seating was full, the staff managed to notice my wife and I, bringing water and taking our order.  I went with a flight of ales over a wide range of the beer spectrum.    I started with the Fragile Reign Brut IPA (4.7% 23 IBU) which was a delightful way to start.  I moved on to the Resilience Butte County Proud West Coast IPA (6.3% 64) that is cool in that sales proceeds are donated to help victims of the Camp Fire destruction in California.  I then moved on to the Maya Milk Stout (5.0%, 5) that is a comfy stout without the high alcohol content that has hints of vanilla and cinnamon with a bit of coffee taste.  I really enjoyed that one!  And finally, I went with the Kanin Kolsch (4.5%, 27) that has hints of banana paired with the hops.  Another winner!  Overall, it was a great way to check out a lot of their flavors in an easy going setting...and a lot closer to me than McCordsville.  Review #2159

Short and sweet review:  An independent coffee shop is conveniently located at Perry Crossing that serves a tasty black house blend at a temperature that is hot, but doesn't scald.  So, you can drink it right away!  The shop has convenient parking out front, but if those are taken, there are spaces in the larger lots beyond the main drag.  Inside, the shop is spacious and bright with a large central seating area, but with a couple nooks toward the front.  One has a large checkerboard set up and the other is a mini library.  The counter is towards the rear on the left.  There are the usual coffee options as well as sandwiches and sweets.  Bottled beverages are chilled too.  On the right is an assortment of Popcornopolis popcorn is available as well.  And the service?  Just a friendly man who had a lot of personality and seemed glad to have customers coming in.  He greeted everyone with a smile and a positive attitude.  I wish all coffee shops would do that.    The next time I am at Perry Crossing, this will be the spot I go to for coffee.  Review #2849

The shop has a convenient drive up window, but it's the inside that makes this coffee house worth stopping by.  There is a lot of space, but it feels like it is warm and cozy inside.  They have a variety of beverages here, but are somewhat limited when it comes to finding something to eat.  They receive their pastries from another company, so depending upon the deliveries, they can have a swing in available options.  One thing I like is that the plain black coffee has a rich flavor and is served at a drinkable temperature without having to wait for it to cool down.  Another was that the barista was friendly and got the orders ready promptly.  While I sat at the counter with my coffee, I noticed he kept the line to a minimum so that folks could go about their business.  Review #2000

This review is for the Ice Cream only since I did not try any of the Mexican food.  I found this restaurant with an unusual combination of specialties through Yelp!  Located in Nora just a bit west of North Central HS, I was able to grab a parking spot in the communal parking area south of the restaurant.  The big square dining/serving area has plenty of room and many tables for guests.  The ice cream selections on hand are posted on a board behind the counter.    Several of the selections have names that were hard for me to guess the flavors, so I asked for a sample and that made a big difference.  As a result, I went with the White Russian and with the Mamey combined in a bowl.    The White Russian is mainly a chocolate base but it seemed to have hints of mint and coffee as well.  When I asked the owner, he said think Kahlua and it made more sense (I have never had a White Russian cocktail, so it never hurts to ask.)  Very tasty and smooth.  I also had the Mamey.  This one reminded me of a creamy cookie dough.  Boy, were my taste buds off.  The Mamey is a tropical fruit that has a subtle flavor that I have read described as a baked sweet potato.  It was delicious too!  The texture was just a little different, so that is probably where I got the notion of cookie dough.    When I discussed the ice cream with the owner, he mentioned that all the ice cream is made in house, not through some outside vendor.  Credit for that!    For two large scoops in a bowl, I still spent less than $5 including tax.  Great price and even greater flavor!  Highly recommended.  Review #103

I had a recommendation from a friend to try Bub's Burgers when I was in the Carmel area for lunch (4-13-16).  I was able to grab one of the few remaining parking places in their lot....it seemed obvious this place was popular even during lunch hours.  The claim to fame for this place is for patrons to eat multiple "Big Ugly" burgers so that they can get their pictures on the wall of flame.  That usually signals an interest in quantity over quality.  In fairness, I was seated quickly and the service was prompt and efficient.  I ordered the "Settle for Less Ugly" burger (a step down in size from the specialty) with Pepperjack cheese and selected cole slaw and sweet potato waffle fries as my sides.  I will admit the burger flavor was good.  It was also juicy, but there wasn't anything about the flavor that I haven't had at home or numerous other burger joints.  The cole slaw was okay and the sweet potato waffle fries were plentiful, but nothing delivered a taste that made me want to go out of my way to return.  Sure, it is a lot cheaper than most of the burger specialty restaurants, but sometimes, you get what you pay for.  Review #30

Knowing how difficult it can be to maintain a good looking lawn, I marvel at the places like Avon Gardens that not only design beautiful landscapes, but maintain them!  The grounds are worth visiting even if you aren't making a purchase from their large selection of plantings and garden architectural features.  Probably more than half of their property is designed and you can walk through to get ideas for possibilities.  Doesn't matter if it is for a water area or a wooded area, maybe just something around your house.  They have beautiful options on site to inspire you.  And the pricing on the pieces of garden accessories I was looking at seemed very reasonable.  There was a wide array of plants too, but I usually don't like setting things out until May, so this was more of a reconnaissance trip to see what was there.    Sure, you can get cheap plants at the big box stores and watch the spindly things struggle to look good.  But why not talk with the folks here and get expert advice and high quality plants that give you the best chance of doing it right the first time?  Glad to have this place on my radar!  Review #2520

I enjoy shopping local, especially when the independent shop carries mostly local artisan products.  Such is the case with the Hayloft, tucked away in a corner of the Main Street Shoppes on US 136/Main St east of Hornaday Road.  The shop doesn't have a lot bright colors to draw your attention so I drove around a bit just to find it.  I also thought the store front a little dark (my wife thought the place was closed), but once inside, the two room shop was much brighter and appealing.  The main room you enter has the order counter in the rear with coolers filled with meats, eggs, and other food items on the right.  There were also lots of mixes, snacks, and other items.  The room to the left carries coffees, sweatshirts, gift bags (?), and more canned goods.    I ended up having a bag of coffee beans ground for me and picked up a mix for baked mushrooms.    The woman behind the counter was friendly and answered my questions while she ground the coffee (no extra fee.)  While we chatted, I noticed the order counter had lots of baked cookies and a display of cupcakes, but since I was going for ice cream after my visit, I passed on the treats.  A nice shop for finding quality items while supporting local (90% of the items in store are locally/Hoosier made).  Review #3737

I really liked the wild berry smoothie and the Kurt V sandwich I had here.  Both were ready in a matter of a few minutes and were full of flavor.  The smoothie was super cold and almost gave me brain freeze upon three different occasions!  It was so good which was so tempting.    The sandwich was grilled with portobello, provolone, roasted red peppers, fresh spinach, and garlic aioli.  Very tasty and with a bit of a chew getting through the different textures in the sandwich.  Very colorful sandwich, as well.  I definitely recommend this!  Since I am in the neighborhood about once a month, I would probably stop in again, but even at lunch time, there was little to no conversation.  Nobody smiling.  Maybe that's just the way restaurants / coffee shops are now.  Everyone is on their phone or laptop and many have earphones in.  Sad that conversation seems to be non-existent in these types of places.  I remember "in the olden days" when these types of places were great for discussion on world problems, without getting into name calling.  Different times.  Oh, back to the review:  This is one of those places where the menu is on a chalkboard and you pay up front and wait for your order to be set on a counter when the staff calls out the order.  No names are taken, so if you want your order as soon as it is placed on the counter, you have to pay attention.  The staff just call out what is on the counter and I don't know what happens if two people have the same sandwich.  Not a great business model, but I guess they make it work.  I had to ask what the staff said because I wasn't paying attention when they shouted.  (I only caught part of the description.)  Maybe if they said something like "order up!" before announcing the items it would give more time to redirect my thinking.  Oh well, nobody else seemed to mind.  I'm glad there are still options that go that extra step.  Not so much here.  So only a four.  Review #313

This new automated car wash can be found in the outlet of the south side Kroger.  There are three lanes for pulling in:  The left and center are for non-member cash and credit customers; the right lane is for members who get a Quick Pass to use.    There are several options for how thorough a car wash/cleaning you can select starting at $10 and going up to $21.  I was in the left lane and dealt with a human rather than using the automated machines on the other two lanes.  I selected one of the middle priced options and pulled around to the west end entrance of the wash building.  This wash uses a belt system that you are directed to pull onto, throw the car into neutral, and take your foot of the brake.  Pretty standard car wash with soap and spray, spinning brushes and hot air blowers.  At the end, the green light comes on prompting you to pull the car forward..standard stuff.  To the right (south) is a long row of vacuum stations where customers can clean out their cars.  I believe the vacuums are free.  Everything is in great working order as expected for a new business.    But, like all belt driven car washes I've been to, the brushes failed to clean around my car's license plate where the brushes aren't able to reach.  Even after spending $18, I still had to finish cleaning the nooks of my car's body.  So, no 5 star review from me.  Review #3623

Having been to several Mexican restaurants this week, I feel I have a good perspective on what's available for lunch in the market.  If I had been the only diner on this trip, I would have probably given a 5th star because the flavor for my lunch sized Chicken Burrito was delicious!  Nice portion and it came with Pico and sour cream without an upcharge.  Just really tender chicken that was full of flavor.  My wife's ground beef burrito came with plenty of stuff on the side (incl. beans), but the entree was very dry inside.  Overcooked beef and not much seasoning.  The portion was generous (she brought some home) but will probably add some more sauce or flavoring.  So, I had to take a star off for the disappointing beef.  Didn't see steak offered as an option, just the chicken or ground beef.  They had some beers incl. Mexican and some local, but I passed on the choices.     Plenty of parking outside and a large lot behind the restaurant too.  all free. Review #3928

When we lived in Greenwood, this was our Go To spot for car washes.  Located conveniently next to a Jiffy Lube, I seemed to grab a wash right after getting the inside of the car taken care of.  It looked and ran like new.  Now that I live in another town, I just don't get to this location as often.  I've tried several local places near my town and they aren't as friendly and don't do as good a job of getting my car clean as this location.  So, other than the fact that they aren't convenient for me anymore and that getting in and out of the lot is challenging when SR 135 has a lot of traffic.  There is no traffic light to assist with access and egress from here.    They usually have a couple lines set up to get the cars marked for going through the automated system.  I've never had any problems with damage here and as I mentioned earlier, our cars looked great after each service.  They can get quite busy because of the lack of competitors in the area, so if you have a bit of patience, the service is what you are looking for.  They do have some additional services for you to do touch up work and vacuuming when you are finished.    Review #3880

So, just in case you missed the big Yelp Bazaar, fear not!  There is still the weekly (Saturday morning) Winter Farmers Market over at the CCIC.  All the road repair is finished on Brookside and there is plenty of parking in the common lot if the small lot by the entrance is full.  The Farmers Market is located on the south end of the CCIC and there was plenty of room to roam through the aisles as you check out the vendors.  They even have a map inside the entrance to show you were the vendors are located.  I found a number of produce vendors, but this was more than just fresh vegetables.  There were a number of locally produced items from vendors who may not have a physical storefront, but are becoming well known through the area.  One of my favorites was Tulip Tree Creamery which had lots of samples to taste and purchase.  These cheeses are used by lots of other businesses and I felt I needed to pick up some to lift my home cooked meals.  Circle City Kombucha was being manned by one of our own Yelpers, Brady R.  I hadn't tried kombucha before, but after being told about it at a previous Yelp event by my friend Kristie K, I had to try it.  There were a few flavors available and I found it effervescent and tangy.  Ended up grabbing a growler of that too!  There were lots of fresh bread and baked goods vendors like Amelia's, Muddy Fork Bakery, and others.  I grabbed a pretzel croissant from MFB that I thought might pair well with some of the cheese I purchased.  There were a few places to get hot food and some seats to take a break if you ran out of steam before you ran out of vendors.  I was pleasantly surprised at how many options were there.  I shall return!  Review #1945

All the best qualities from the Pendleton location (food is delightful!) but add plentiful parking, a beautiful setting with plenty of room, and nicer restrooms and when we went, a front room manager and waitress who made sure things were going well from start to finish.  I definitely recommend coming to this Catellos if you want to have an upscale night out that can easily be dress casual, while offering top quality food.  If you are a fan of cheap spaghetti houses, this isn't your place.  But if you like authentic Italian food with options that are coastal (lots of shellfish and fish options), lots of pastas, and a nice selection of salads, sides, and though we were too full to try them, desserts too.  We made lunch reservations for our group and were comfortably arranged near the front windows which provided plenty of light (I am not a fan of very dark restaurants that make it difficult to read the menus.)  Our waitress did a good job of keeping the orders straight (even through the final bills.)  Our group ordered from all over the menu (seafood pasta, paninis, spaghetti, lasagna, salads, and wine.)  Everyone seemed quite pleased with the flavor combinations and portions.  While we waited for our orders to come out, we were served sliced loaves of bread with olive oil for dipping.  There were multiple oil plates so that none of us had to pass them...everyone was able to dip their bread individually.  If you want butter, you will need to request it.  The butter is cold and unseasoned, so if you like salt (and pepper), you will have to request the waitress to bring some to the table and grind it for you (due to Covid measures).  Our group was very pleased.  I'm not one who complains about lunch prices when the quality of service and food options are the same as dinner.  For me, who cares what time it is?  I care about having a dining experience and Catellos provided a nice venue and meal for our group of 6 to gather.  It is a long way from my home southwest of Indy, but I would definitely consider returning with friends for another visit.  Review #3846

My wife and I stopped by for a  tasty lunch earlier in the week.although there was plenty of parking but limited spots to transfer from the lot to the sidewalk. No automatic doors either.  Fortunately, we were able to get my wheel chair in and situated at one of the dining room tables.it seemed chilly since the outside air was unobstructed-from the dining room.   You place our order at the counter and help yourself to  utensils and napkins.  There are many-options  iicl. soups FYI Bigger spoons would be be helpful, salads, lots of appetizers and sushi options.entrees  are diverse and several proteins are available.  Rev #3985

This was my first time shopping at this meijer.  We normally shop the one in Camby, but since we had our grocery list with us on our way home from running other errands, we passed this meijer and decided to stop in since we were already here.  Plenty of parking, so we grabbed a space fairly close to one of the entrances and appreciated that the rows for parking had letters to help us remember which row we had chosen.  One thing that is weird is that meijer stores are not set up identically, so from my perspective, we had to figure out where everything was.  We would have probably shopped faster driving on to our local store and just picking up what we needed.  I'm a bit of a speed shopper because I know my own store layout so well.  Trying a new one is always a bit frustrating.  I wonder why they don't lay out the stores which are usually built from the ground up the same?  Not that this store is to blame, it is more of a complaint about meijer in general.  The store is huge and they do have a lot of items to choose from.  I also like that there seemed to generally be wide enough aisles for people to pass with carts.  There were shortages on some holiday items and paper products probably due to the hoarding mentality that has taken hold of our nation.  You can't even mention snowfall without stores noticeably being depleted.  I was looking for a canned good for Thanksgiving and the store had it set up on the bottom row.  Unfortunately, the rows are deep and from a standing postition, it was hard to read the label for the items which were shoved so deeply into the row that the labels on the cans were not readable.  I literally had to get down on my knees to read the small print and then look through the row to see the canned goods lined up single file at the back of the shelf.  Good thing I am still flexible and have long arms.  I don't know how many people would go to my effort to get what they needed.  So, someone on the staff should be bringing the items forward for the customers, especially in the areas where obvious attrition was occurring.  Maybe they could check in the back to see if there were any more inventory in stock to help shoppers.  I can't have been the only shopper frustrated that it was difficult to find common items in the store.  I also noticed that the shelves seemed high and that made it difficult to read some of the aisle signs.  My wife was looking to find the pharmacy and it took awhile to spot it.  She didn't say whether she found the item she was looking for or not.  I understand these aren't ideal times for first visits to stores, so I am giving them the benefit of the doubt with a 4 star rating.  But customers will only put up with shelves that aren't maintained for so long, especially if they can find a better shopping experience elsewhere.  We ended up using the self check out counters since the regular customer lines were all backed up.  Fortunately, I've grown pretty good at scanning over my lifetime of grocery shopping.  I prefer using the limitless lanes because they have more room than the limited number of item check outs.  I could scan and set my stuff on the larger area without having to stop and bag part way through scanning just to make room.  Review #3821

It's too bad that I'm watching my weight for the holidays.  There were so many kinds of candy and soda in here, that I was really tempted.  Whether its some old fashioned candies like salt water taffy (bins of them) or candy cigarettes (yes, that is a real thing!), or chocolate covered malt balls, there was a sense of nostalgia and childhood memories regained.  And the sodas were mostly small company brands with names that made you wonder what the manufacturers were thinking!  Although they don't have every type of candy that I remember, I will say that if you grew up a half century ago, you will probably find something to bring back pleasant memories.  And if you are younger, you can find something for the first time to try.  Review #1975

I will freely admit that I am no expert on Malaysian food.  This is probably the first experience I've had with this type of food.  I've had lots of similar flavors, but nothing else particularly identified as this.  What I found wer generous portions, a casual dining experience with very little English being spoken, and food that tended towards being over cooked.  The nondescript business blends into a strip mall that sits back from SR 135.  There is plenty of parking and the place looks dark from the outside.  Inside, the dining room is much brighter with a bit of ornamentation and television playing (volume on) in one corner.  (It was playing some music video with a non-English wedding until one of the patrons turned it to something like MMA fighting.)  One woman was handling the front end of the business.  She hadn't bused all the morning dining tables yet, but made sure she cleaned one before I was seated.  She brought me a menu and a free glass of hot tea.  Note that they don't use any kind of strainer vessel for their tea.  The leaves float around and for someone who is used to NOT having tea leaves in my sips, it was a bit odd spinning my glass around to avoid leaves and stems.    I ordered a small Tom Yum Soup with noodles but wasn't asked if I wanted it chicken or vegetarian.  Mine came with some tofu looking lumps and some shrimp with the tails still on.  Again, maybe that's traditional, but I'm not a fan of it.  The spice level was decent..not too hot, but enough to make my sinus react.  And though it was the small version, this was a huge serving for a single person, probably well over a pint.  I had expected something more like a breakfast bowl or smaller.  This could be someone's meal.  The flavors were fine, but the soup was served steaming hot.  The shrimp had become rubbery and it was a necessity to blow on each bite to make it cool.  I liked that they included a fork and a large table spoon for grabbing the noodles and veggies.  They also provided an Asian style spoon for the broth.  Good flavor, just over cooked.  Before I could finish, my IMBI Beef arrived.  Again, it was a large portion covering a 9" square plate.  The beef was sliced to bite size and came with ginger, oyster sauce, and 3 inch pieces of green onion that were a bit chewy in texture.  They offered chili peppers with it, but I passed.  The flavor was good, but again, the beef was completely overcooked and took on what was becoming a familiar rubbery taste.  Maybe that's the way the regular customers like it.  When I finished, I was stuffed and paid at the counter (I wasn't brought a bill but the woman was sitting at the order counter not recognizing I was done.)  As my rating shows, the food was okay, but nothing that I would rush back to try again.    One last note to the owners:  For only being open just over a year, there is an unusual amount of discoloration on your carpet from foot traffic.  It makes the place look dingy and should be replaced or at the very least, deep cleaned.  That does not appeal to Hoosier patrons if you are looking to expand your clientele beyond those who currently stop by.  Review #2728

Wow! What a cool experience right here in downtown Indy.  As a local, I've heard the Vonnegut name for most of my life, but wasn't that familiar with the author's work until recently.  Having just read "Slaughterhouse Five" and a collection of short stories "Welcome to the Monkey House", I got an appreciation for how imaginative and engaging the author was.  The museum is open for visitors to view with three floors of items and artwork, a book store, and soon, a coffee shop.  But if you want to get your money's worth, contact the museum to find out when the guided tours are...they make the experience so much better.  My tour guide was very knowledgeable and had a sense of wit that complemented the author's.  The museum has several sections which are interesting for different reasons.  One section has a collection of banned books and I just can't get over that some narrow minded communities think that ideas can be shut down.  Hint:  There's a thing called the internet and people will get whatever they want, so don't be an * about it.  There are also books that are by authors that inspired Vonnegut or fit into the styles of writing that the author liked.  Note that members of the museum can take advantage of the lending library here.  Up on the second floor is a gift/book shop where you can find items to purchase related to the author.  On the third floor, there was a Slaughterhouse Five exhibit that features a lot of text and imagery from the author's time as a prisoner of war after the Battle of the Bulge during WWII when he was forced to march to Dresden and kept in an underground slaughterhouse.  Also of note is that if you go online at the station on the second floor, you will find a wide variety of information and images about Vonnegut for you to explore.  For those who have trouble negotiating stairs, there is an elevator available.  I highly recommend this museum for adults who consider themselves free thinkers.  I don't think this is a place that children would appreciate simply because they probably won't have had enough life experience to understand the ideas and concepts the author wrote about.    Parking is free in the mini lot that surrounds the building with access off Indiana Avenue as well as West St/MLK Blvd.  Metered Street parking is also available on Indiana Ave.  The tour lasted about 40 minutes (mine started at 11 a.m.)  Definitely worth checking out to get a fuller experience from the museum.  Review #3604

If I could give another half star, I would.  They almost get 5 stars because you can grab good food and some beer on a Monday when a lot of places are closed.  After a doctor's appt which ran more than an hour late, it was nearly 3 by the time we got here for lunch.  Brewlink was open in the spot that was formerly TwoDeep Brewing.  Still looks similar and has the convenient parking on the north side of the building, with easy southbound access on Capitol Ave.  I decided to go with a flight of 4 (most are $2 per small glass).  Each of the brews I have had at their other locations have been good, so I didn't even ask for tastes, but just made my decision off the tap list menu description.  I was quite pleased with all four choices.  And they had a nice lunch menu to select from.  My wife got a Beer Mac n Cheese with Chicken that had a good flavor (but the chicken was a little dry if not dipped in the creamy sauce.)  I ordered the Beast Burger which has Bison, Elk, and Wagyu beef which kept it from being dry.  The fries on the side were really good too.  So a solid 4+ on the food.    My wife has some mobility trouble and even though there were just a few steps down, they don't have a central handrail for stability which would be a great addition. (they do have one along the wall though.) I didn't ask about ramps though, so I don't know what their plan is for people who have even more mobility issues than we did.    Overall, we really liked the place and would recommend it if you want to avoid the crowds of downtown and near the convention center but not be too far away if you were going to do something later.  Looks like they may have some outdoor seating in warmer weather too.  Give them a try if you don't feel like driving all the way to Plainfield to try their beer.  Review #3892

In 2016, this local eye care business hired artist Justin Olson to create a colorful mural on the outside of the business.  The artist depicted the face of an eye glass wearing person on three sides of the building.  To fill out the rest of the space, vibrant colors are swirled including silhouettes of eyes.  As you drive by this place on Shelby, the colors draw your attention to the building...that is if your vision is good enough.  If you have trouble seeing it, maybe you should stop in....and maybe somebody else should drive! ;)  Review #1890

This is the 30th barbecue restaurant where I've dined in Indiana and I have to say their barbecue is one of the best!  The price is affordable and the meat is piled high on the sandwiches (no skimping!)  They also have four flavors of BBQ sauce (with descriptions of the taste) available in condiment bottles on the interior tables.   Because my pulled pork sandwich was so tall, I pulled some of the meat off to the side and tried each of the sauces to see what I liked best.  They are all good and accurately describe what to expect.  The restaurant is on the south side of US 136/Crawfordsville Road, just a short distance east of Raceway.  There is a narrow driveway on the west side of the building that will lead you to the lot in back of the restaurant.  Sorry, you have to walk around to the front to enter the dining area.  The business is located in a small ranch style house that has a couple rooms set up for dining.  There is an eclectic mix of decor with a large part featuring racing, though there is a pinball machine (Star Trek) in the corner.  Tables mostly seat four people and there are picnic tables with umbrellas outside.  Large blackboards with menu options are to the right as you enter and the order counter is mostly in the center.  You order and pay and they bring the food out to you.  If you get a beverage, they have a self-serve station for you.  Note:  For anyone who is uncomfortable in going into a house turned restaurant, note that at the time of my writing, this place has a PERFECT Health Score (100 points!)  That is impressive and requires a lot of effort and know how from the owners/staff.  My wife wasn't as hungry as I was, so she ordered the pulled chicken  (nicely seasoned) without a bun and mainly just picked bites from my pulled pork combo.  My combo came with choice of two sides.  I went with the mac 'n cheese (creamy and good, but a bit bland) and the green beans which are cut and thoroughly cooked with a bit of cubed ham.  Again, there isn't much seasoning (I would love a bit of onion in there.)  Fortunately, salt shakers are on the table.    The meat was generally moist and shredded.  I have to admit that it looked rather sterile when served on a plain white bun without any sauce.  But that's okay since I did my taste tests with all the sauces.  I settled on the Carolina which has a vinegary punch to it for deeper flavor.  Although there isn't much atmosphere for dining in, the food quality was high and the taste of the sandwiches was good.    If you are in the area, give this place a try for you barbecue cravings.  Review #2766

There is a good reason that Iaria's has been in business for a long time: they serve a good meal!  I stopped in for lunch after parking in their private lot on the north side of the building.  (The doors are somewhat tough to open due to vacuum pressure, so pull hard!)  At the doorway, there is a hostess station sign asking you to wait to be seated.  To the right is a hallway that leads to the bar area.  I opted for the dining room since the bar looked somewhat cramped and packed.  The dining room has a wall of mirrors on the far end to make the space seem more open.  There are 4-top tables with chairs and some booth style seats.  The booths look padded, but be careful to not sit too hard.  The "padding" doesn't do much to protect you from the hard, uneven seating underneath.  (I tried scooting in to a corner and caught a raised joint where the benches were together.)  The waitress was pleasant and though handling a large group at the tables next to me, minimized the wait between interactions.  My water was refilled and my check was processed in a timely manner.  I went with one of the lunch specials, the beef lasagna.  It came with a side salad as part of the deal.  First, I received a complementary basket of sliced bread and crackers.  The bread came with room temperature margarine and there was already a bottle of olive oil on the table.  The salad was next and the Italian dressing I ordered was in a cup on the side with a spoon to allow me to put as much as I wanted over the salad. The dressing was really good and may have been made in house.   The salad plate was 8" and was made using iceberg lettuce that was mostly cold and crisp.  However, some of the ingredients didn't look quite in top shape due to possibly too cold temperatures.   The lasagna was served unadorned in a bowl that allowed extra sauce to be held in reserve for when needed.  The noodles were very tender and the beef was lightly seasoned.  The flavor was good but not layered like I've had other places.  The sauce worked quite well with the beef and noodles.  The portion was appropriate for a lunch portion too.  I was satisfied without feeling stuffed.  Overall, I enjoyed my return visit to Iaria's.  Lunch was quick, service friendly, and reasonably priced for the meal.  Review #1033

Whether buying a new car here, or bringing my car for a bit of maintenance, I continue to be impressed with the quality of service and positive/friendly service I receive.  I'm one of those customers that doesn't buy a new car very often.  I drive them until the maintenance becomes too expensive/frequent that I buy a new car as a better financial decision.  So, it would be easy for them to not be welcoming.  But I never have been treated poorly in the seven years I've been coming here.  My car usually keeps humming along (my previous one lasted ten years) but every once in awhile, something happens and being that I am mechanically challenged, I take it in.  Sometimes, the warning light isn't a big deal, so they suggest trying a few things first before bringing it in.  But when what seemed like a small problem (amber light) suddenly turns to a bunch of red lights on my dash and warnings on my car's computer screen, I make sure to take the car in and have it looked at.    Normally, when I take it in, I get a courtesy call that lets me know what the maintenance guys have found and get an estimate.  But this time, I didn't.  The man on the phone knew he hadn't called when he called me to let me know the car was done.  Before I could panic that it would be some huge bill, he let me know that even after five years, the part was under my warranty plan and there wasn't any service charge, let alone any charge for parts.  Free!!  And while they were at it, they fixed a few other minor items that were free due to a recall.  Free is nice!  Free is stress reducing.    And the folks at the counter seemed appreciative that I was so happy and soon on my way.  Thanks to the folks there who do a great job and work hard to make their customers happy.  Review #2859

Although this place may not appeal to everyone, it must certainly be a favorite of those who are looking for uniforms and costumes.  I got a chance to chat with the owner who says that some of his pieces are used in plays, events, and even some museums in Chicago because of their condition.  There are some antiques like gramophones and oil lamps, even some antique guns/rifles.  But the mainstay of this place is the availability of clothing and hats that fit specific themes.    Oh, and if this sort of thing interests you, I got a tip that they may only be around another few months before moving (and taking their collection) to Canada.  If you are interested in uniforms and related military items, get here soon!  Review #1937

In preparation for Super Bowl XLVI, the Arts Council of Indianapolis commissioned artists to create a lasting tribute to the celebration and to Indianapolis called "46 for XLVI".  Hoosier artist Pamela Bliss was selected to paint this mural back in 2011 (she did touch up in late 2016).  The mural is officially called "My Affair with Kurt Vonnegut".  Bliss has been a key contributor to the public art scene in Wayne County (Richmond area) by holding a series of annual mural contests which brought public art to every town in the county.  This mural was made from a composite of photographs of the author and faces northwest.    Vonnegut was an author born in 1922 who wrote such famous works as "Slaughterhouse Five", "Cat's Cradle", and "Breakfast of Champions".  Many of his books mention Indianapolis which Vonnegut had a deep connection to.  For more about public art in the Indy metro area, see the Arts Council of Indianapolis Public Art Directory (PAD): https://www.indyartsguide.org/public-art/my-affair-with-kurt-vonnegut/  For more about the artist, see her Facebook page: https://www.facebook.com/pg/PamelaBlissArt/posts/?ref=page_internal  Review #1172

How did I never stop in this place when I lived on the east side?  Walking into this place would make a small child's eyes bulge out of their heads (and probably some adults too) with all the colorful array of pastries and small collectibles/dolls on display.  I wasn't stopping for the non-edibles, but I will admit their collection of items was worth checking out if you are looking for something unique.  But I was there for pastries....I'm not a yeast donut guy.  I like lots of flavors in my morning selection and this place delivers.  Who knew they carried individual pies and cakes?  I picked up an apple pie, a cherry pie, a Pineapple Upside down cake, and the most creative "turtle" I've ever seen.  And there were cream horns, lots of small sugar cookies, and some bismarks.  Frankly, for such a small space for pastries, I was amazed at how many choices they had even at mid-morning.  The woman behind the counter was very friendly and when I saw the turtles, she pointed out the woman who makes them by hand.  If you haven't seen my photos, she forms a chocolate shell around the caramel and uses pecans for the feet to support the shell.  Very cool, but I'm afraid my wife ate it before I got a chance to try it!  It sure looked good though.  Located just east of the 10th and Shadeland intersection, the stand alone building was easy to get in and out of (I went when it wasn't rush hour).  Nice place to stop for something tasty to make your morning special!  Review #2283

Nice variety of cakes, cupcakes, cheesecakes, and mini-pies.  There are even quite a few large cookies!  They have convenient parking in their lot on the east side of the building.  You can even order special event cakes, but I strictly stopped by for something sweet to eat right away!  The cupcakes were running about $3.75 each, while the pies and cheesecakes were a bit higher.  It's not cheap, but it isn't standard grocery store baked good either.  Good and fresh with lots of flavor.  The adage "You get what you pay for" applies here.  The service was friendly and efficient and the store was spotlessly clean.  Review #1705

I was hoping to give this place a little better rating, but there are some problems that customers should be aware of.  First, the bartender/manager is the only one who works days during the week on the front end.  So, she was hustling throughout the lunch period.  Unfortunately, there were customers and the waitress wandering around (even delivering food) without the masks on or in place.  We figured it out before she came over and masked up.  Since there wasn't enough business to hire a waitress, there were waits between phases.  We got our food fairly quickly, but when I was ready to check out, she had stepped out front to smoke and left nobody in place to allow us to pay or to get a to go box.  I had to go outside and ask her to come in.  I understand people need breaks, but she should have checked her customers needs first before disappearing outside.  The sandwiches we ordered were good.  My wife got a pulled pork that had a smoky flavor she liked.  My tenderloin was a classic Hoosier style that greatly exceeded the bun.  Good flavor on both and not overcooked.  They do have a well stocked bar, but I didn't see any sodas listed on the menu and they only seemed to carry the commercial beers that are mass produced elsewhere.  Maybe the regular customers like cheap beer.  I would have liked to seen some local craft beers offered (at least in cans).  So I just ordered an unsweetened ice tea.  Lost sales.  Oh well, it was a filling meal and not bad, but I don't think I would stop again with the lack of covid enforcement and minimal staffing.  Review #3829

I love this first expansion of the Chilly Water Brewing Company.  Same great beers that you find in Fletcher Place, but instead of dealing with a kitchen, they teamed up with Hoagies & Hops (formerly at Flat 12) to handle the food options which allows the bartender to focus on serving you beer!  They have an industrial look with lots of gold and platinum records lining the walls (all with fun beer names instead of songs).    The west end of the bar has glass garage doors that will open up in summer months.  They are planning to give the existing patio a makeover to make it more welcoming to guests and cyclists.  Right now, they have free street parking along both cross streets.  I was able to grab a spot just outside on 42nd.  No problem finding the place either since you can easily get here from 38th and turning onto Boulevard.  And the beer is simply delicious.  They have specials on some days and on Thursday, they featured a Blood Orange IPA (Blood on the Tracks 7.4%) that were going fast to customers, even at lunch time!  I also tried the Dyslexic Heart (Dunkelweiss 4.9%), Good Kisser (German Kolsch 5.6%), and the One Hop Wonder (American IPA 6.9%), all of which were good.  They even have a collaboration called Kiss the Sky (Hazy India Pale Lager 6.4%) that I got a sample of, but my brain fails to recall who they partnered with on this one.  They were all good, so go the flight route ($8 for four 5-oz pours).    The bartender was really friendly and was able to tell me a lot about the company and the plans they have for developing the place.  They also have some merchandise available for those interested.  Great combo of beer and on site food.  The next time you are in the area, give them a try!  Review #2233

Rusted Window is tucked away in the corner of a strip mall a half block east of the roundabout of Rangeline Rd and Carmel Drive.  I had a bit of trouble finding it, but was glad I did.   The shop has a little bit of everything.  Home Decor?  Candles? Just Pop in! popcorn? Women's Clothing?  Floral arrangements? Yes to all!  I will say I was surprised that there wasn't more floor space since it looks rather roomy from the parking lot.  But once inside, there are basically two rooms for shopping while the rest of the space is storage area behind the counter.  The staff was friendly and offered to assist in finding something.  The space was organized and arranged so that it presented the items in groupings that made sense, not cluttered like some spaces.  Review #2098

I hadn't been to Pure Eatery in a few years, so I decided to stop back for lunch during the week.  The interior seemed much brighter than I recalled and that's a good thing.  It seemed more inviting than my previous visit.    So after seating myself, it wasn't long before I was greeted and placed my order for crab cakes.  Note that they have a crab cakes appetizer which you can get for lunch (no side) or a crab cakes entree with a side that is only available after 5 p.m.  The cakes are a mix of crab and tilapia over a bed of greens with pimentos, and a spicy remoulade sauce on top.  The cakes were cooked nicely with a bit of a sear on top, but remaining fork tender.  The size of the three cakes were smaller than I have had elsewhere, but I'm giving them the benefit of the doubt since it was listed as an appetizer.  The pimentos were good also and paired well with the cakes and the sauce.  Just a little heat and a lot of flavor from the sauce.  Good choice!  Service was good though not personable....never caught her name until I read the bill.  She was good at explaining the difference between the two listings of the crab cakes and got my order in and bill processed without any delays.  Overall, it was a fine lunch that was handled quickly which is good for a lunch service.  Review #1154

On May 28, 2016 (Saturday), my wife and I met friends early in the evening to dine at Pioneer.  It was their first time (our second).  Because it was a nice evening, we chose to sit outside in the new beer garden on the south side of the restaurant (Note:  There is some parking to the west of the beer garden if you approach from the west on Morris Street.)  Our server was really helpful in making suggestions and accommodating our seating request.  He was helpful in helping pick out our beverage choices as well as knowledgeable about the individual food items.  My wife ordered the Chicken Liver Mousse - Schmaltz (rendered goose fat), Pickled veg, Amelia's bread which was shared with the table.  There is a LOT of mousse, so we placed a couple more requests for the bread to spread it on.  (Note:  Each additional request for bread had a charge.  It wasn't much, but it should have been pointed out before the order was placed.)  The flavor is really good and it is hard to not finish eating it all.  It is very creamy in texture.  I placed an order for the Gnocchi - porcini cream sauce, speck (smoked pork belly), ramps, morels from the small plates list and for the Salmon - Asparagus, green garlic panisse (the brown cube made with chickpea flour), onions, egg yolk jam from the entree listing.  Both were good, but I would give a slight nod to the Salmon if I had to choose one.  It had a nice crispy crust while the flesh was moist and tender.  We each ordered different items and I have to say that I definitely preferred what I ordered to the other items ordered by our guests.  My wife ordered the pork belly and found it didn't quite measure up to other entrees that featured the pork belly at other restaurants in the area. She probably won't order it again.  We didn't stay for the evening entertainment, so I can't really comment on that.  We like the restaurant, but it isn't one that we are planning on rushing back to.  Review #10

I was surprised at how much I enjoyed Bar Louie.  I don't go to many national franchise/chain restaurants, but I was intrigued by this one.  So, while near the mall in Greenwood, I decided to stop by and check them out.  Although it's November as I write this, I noticed a very nice patio out front that is within viewing distance of the large fountain down the sidewalk.  Looks like a cool place to hang out on weather friendly days.  Inside, there was lots of room, especially surprising was the number of seats at the central bar.  It was enormous!  The bartenders can walk around the center piece and the seating wraps around the walk area.  Since I was dining by myself, I selected a seat at the bar instead of tying up one of the 4-top or booths.  Although the bartender was responsible for getting drink orders out for the other wait staff, she did a good job of getting my order and beverage promptly.    I decided to go with the Voodoo Sandwich, which had a bit of heat, but nothing too strong.  It comes with blackened chicken breast (nice and moist) with andouille sausage, pepper jack cheese, sauteed peppers and onion strips, lettuce, tomato, mayo, and spiced pickles on a brioche bun.  The sandwich was fairly large, so I cut it down the middle and proceeded to eat it that way.  My advice, don't cut it.  Because there was so much piled on top of the real chicken breast (not uniformly sliced piece of meat), I kept loosing the peppers and onions which would dangle from the sandwich, held only in place by the melted cheese.  I ended up needing my fork to get all the dropped pieces since my fingers were getting kind of messy.  Overall, it was a nice flavor but no wow factor.  I think the flavor built the more I ate, but then the heat tended to blot out some of the smaller flavors of the veggies.  I also upgraded my side (an extra $1) to a side salad with a house vinaigrette.  Yum!  The vinaigrette was a little more sweet and creamy than most I have had.  The red onion strips were crisp and not overpowering of the rest of the salad.  I would definitely recommend it.  They have a lot of alcoholic beverages available, particularly cocktails and wines.  I can't comment on those since I passed on the opportunity.  I was surprised at how quickly my order came out and felt the staff did a fine job of taking care of me and my order.  Checkout was easy and timely as well since I had someplace to be after lunch.  I would definitely recommend Bar Louie for grabbing a bite for lunch.  Review #435

I was driving along the interstate around lunch time (4-27-16) and remembered that not too far off I-70 and Rural was one of the Top 25 Restaurants per Indpls Monthly magazine for 2016.  Since the Love Handle is only open for breakfast and lunch, I thought it was a perfect opportunity to stop in.  The area of town is a bit dicey, so I was glad I was able to street park directly in front of the restaurant's picture windows.  The restaurant operates with the day's menu written on a blackboard behind the counter where one of the owners takes your order.  (She will bring it out to you once it is ready, so go ahead and find a seat.)  I ordered the "Julian" based on her recommendation for a first timer.  This sandwich was Beef Shoulder roast, raclette cheese, peach ramp chutney, & crisp kale on a grilled bread with a flavored popcorn side.  I also tried a Sidral Mondet Apple soda which I will have to track down finding some for home!  Let me say this....the sandwich was an absolute delight!  So many complimentary flavors and textures that I am left amazed at how the chef can come up with these ideas.  And this is for a simple roast beef sandwich.  I can't wait to try something more exotic...just trust the chef and try it.  From just this one meal, I can see why this restaurant is receiving such high praise.  They may get a lot of attention for their delicious breakfast options, but their lunch options definitely hold their own.    I definitely plan on returning with friends so that we can try more things (if I can get anyone else to share!)  Review #22

Originally posted 2/4/2018:  I enjoy coming to this park, the largest and best equipped park in Mooresville.  It has 150 acres of land that is home to multiple soccer and baseball fields, a water park, a zip-line, 7 shelters (most with their own playground!), and trails that are great for getting a good workout while you enjoy being surrounded by nature.    I particularly like bringing my dogs and strolling along the paths on the far side of the park (west end).  While on leashes, my dogs can still enjoy all the scents of nature and wildlife that live in the park.  Some of the trails cross the east fork of White Lick Creek.  There are even covered bridges over the waterway making the park seem more rural than being within the city limits.    The park has a large parking lot at the front and fortunately, it has a single paved looping roadway so that a visitor can bypass the cluster of shelters and head back to the wooded area.  There is a single shelter and playground on the west end of the park (permanent restroom is located there too!)     The busiest part of the park tends to be where the ballparks, playgrounds, and seasonal waterpark attract lots of kids.  My favorite playground is at Shelter #2 and is called "Pirate's Cove".  There are ramps and slides and lots of climbing pieces of equipment for kids to burn energy on.  The base for the play area is made of the padded squares that allow for even footing as kids run around.      Overall, there is something for adults and for kids to interact or find some peaceful spot to stroll and enjoy nature.    Review #549

I really like the Talbot Street Art Fair.  It focuses on bringing lots of vendors (around 270 booths) to a central location bearing items that are different from the typical online buying offerings.  Because it is offered on the weekend, there are a number of local businesses that allow their parking lots to be used for only $5, so you don't spend a lot of time just getting to the fair from your car.  Since the fair is free, you can even take a break and haul some of your findings back to your car so you don't have to carry them around with you when the place gets crowded.  I also like that I don't have to pay an admission charge to pay for "entertainment" and food/beverage vendors to come that I may not have any interest in.  That leaves more money to consider using towards an actual purchase.  The fair is arranged between 16th and 20th Streets on Talbot (a half block east of Pennsylvania St.)  I like that you can start at one point and just focus on one side and the flow of the fair will take you to every booth without having to browse both sides at once.  There are a couple "spurs" with food and restrooms and additional vendors.  They even have ATM machines for folks who prefer to use cash instead of their credit cards for purchases.  There are numerous examples of vendors.  The booths consists of eleven categories:  2D art, 2-D mixed Media, 3-D mixed media, Clay, Fiber, Glass, Metal, Jewelry, Photography, Sculpture, and Wood.  The fair is an annual event that is usually the third weekend of June.  Review #322

My wife and I have dined here several times in the past few years, most recently on a Monday for lunch (5-23-16).  Curiously enough, we have never tried the pizza.  Most times, I order the Italian Beef sandwich and have been delighted each time.  Excellent flavor combinations.    But on this day, I wanted something with a little less sodium, so I decided to go for the Grilled Chicken with a small side salad with vinaigrette.  I selected the pepperjack cheese to perk up the flavor and really loved the flavor combination with the lettuce, tomato, mayo, and "honey mustard" that tasted more like a spicy brown mustard to me.  The chicken was grilled perfectly and was probably my favorite chicken sandwich of the year!  (I also recommend the Stanley chicken at Oaken Barrel as a close rival.)  The cheese was melted thoroughly and draped over the meat.    We also took advantage of their onsite parking and the outdoor seating.  Okay, the view of a parking lot isn't that impressive, but the weather was too nice to sit inside a somewhat dark interior during daytime hours.  Attentive service even if there was limited beverage knowledge due to the waiter being a non-drinker. I can't hold that against him! :)  Solid food options at a decent price.  We enjoy having this restaurant in our go to rotation.  Review #15

My wife and I went with another couple to a local gathering of food trucks for lunch.  Because we are retired, we were able to be there before the crowds got too big.  So, we had very little wait in getting our order turned around.  I ordered the Scratch Burger - 1/3# ground beef, bacon marmalade, arugula, & gorgonzola cheese on a toasted bun as my sandwich.  I ordered it medium (cooked correctly to order).  Having read the excellent reviews, I was disappointed with the results.  I took two bites before I tasted the bacon marmalade.  I also noticed the gorgonzola had not melted at all, so the flavor didn't blend as smoothly as I had expected.  Finally, the burger had no sear for browning, so the beef was rather bland as well.  I didn't add any condiments because all the other reviews had cautioned not to.  Just a miss for me.  I also tried the Poutine de Peru Fries with Peruvian yellow pepper sauce, queso fresco cheese, and cilantro.  Unfortunately, this was another miss for me.  I accept this as partly my fault for ordering it since I am not a banana pepper fan, but I am trying to expand my palate to include the wave of world cuisines that have come to Indy.  I own that, but the fries quickly became soggy and flimsy.  Just not worth the upgrade.  I should have just gone with the traditional fries.  I did order a Strawberry Basil Lemonade which was really delicious.  Too bad it was the highlight of my meal.  My wife ordered the Scratch Grilled Cheese - with red wine braised short ribs, caramelized red onion, muenster cheese, arugula, & colby jack cheese on toasted honey white bread.  This sounded fantastic, but was another disappointment.  When described as grilled cheese, she expected the sandwich to have enough cheese so that it would ooze when bit into.  Frankly, there was so little cheese that it appeared spread on with a knife.  It should have been called a short rib sandwich.  That was disappointing enough, but the flavor of the ribs was completely different than what she expected.  They were just bitter!  I took a bite and noticed the odd flavor, but was hard pressed to identify it.  Later on, I tried more since my wife didn't even want the second half of the sandwich.  The only thing I could come up with is that the red wine had reduced to concentrate the tannins bringing the bitterness as the strongest flavor of the sandwich.  I am not sure if we just caught the truck on an off day or if my tastes are that different from those who gave this truck high ratings.   For me, I am not sure that I would give the truck another chance with so much competition out there.  Review #84

One of the best things about trying a new restaurant is when everything exceeds your expectations.  Well, our recent lunch (Sat 6/25/16) at 1911 Grill in Speedway certainly did that!    The best part of the revitalization of Main Street in Speedway is that it is filling with quality places to visit.  I expected the Sarah Fisher "Speedway Indoor Karting" to be top notch, but expected the dining to be an afterthought, and thereby suffer from lack of attention.    But under the direction of GM/Chef Todd Howard, we were treated right from the moment we entered.  Our greeter welcomed us and offered us the choice of indoor or outdoor dining.  Indoors was air conditioned and spacious with multiple televisions and a view of the indoor racing.  Outdoors are two patios on the west side of the building, so we could be outside without the direct heat on this near 90 degree day.    We opted for outdoor dining.  Within moments, our waitress arrived to take our beverage order.  We had a few questions about the menu which she answered.    While waiting, we noticed the two seat Indy Car was giving rides to a group of guests at a private party held upstairs.  We must have seen a dozen laps around the building during our visit.  Very cool!    Our lunches arrived:  My wife ordered the BackFire Shrimp (served over a salad) while I ordered the Pulled Pork Sandwich and fries.    The BackFire sauce is made in house and mixed at the time of the order, so our waitress informed us that the sauce could be made milder or hotter upon request.  My wife isn't a fan of heat, so she was very pleased that she was given that option and totally enjoyed her shrimp and salad.    My pulled pork was cooked perfectly with just enough sauce on top to compliment the flavor of the pork.  The meat was moist and tender.  The fries had a bit of seasoning for flavor which decreased the need for lots of salt.  I appreciated that.    As we sat there enjoying our food and a nice summer breeze, the chef/GM came out to see how we liked our food.  I know a lot of places send a manager around to check, but some come off as being a watchdog.  This visit seemed like it was about genuinely wanting us to have a positive experience.  Mission accomplished!    I hope to bring some friends along with us the next time we visit.  Review #62

I stopped in for lunch on Monday after reading and hearing great reviews of Wildwood Market.  This converted service station has bay doors that open to reveal an eclectic grouping of all the foodstuffs you wish you could find in the big markets.  From sauces to oils, from frozen to fresh, it really is surprising how much variety they have.  The lunch menu is written on a small clipboard above the counter.  What works for this place is offering a single sandwich and a single salad option each day.  This makes for a very efficient behind the counter operation, so wait times were minimal.  I opted for one of each.  My salad was made with a bed of local spring mix greens, topped with curry chicken salad (large pieces of chicken), local apples, onions, and bell pepper, Kefir, scallions, cilantro, golden raisins, and sliced almonds.  As you can tell, this isn't just a boring salad.  Lots of flavor combinations with each bite.  However, the greens are not cut at all, and with only a plastic fork, eating my salad was a bit awkward and messy.  I definitely needed to use my napkins to keep from having yellow curry on my face!  I am not a huge curry fan, so I thought the salad okay.  My sandwich was a Mesquite organic chicken, with Beeler's bacon, Monterey Jack, local tomato, marinated local onion, leaf lettuce, avocado and ranch mayo...on sourdough. The sandwich was much more enjoyable than the salad.  The bacon and mesquite flavors combined with the fresh flavors of the produce made for an enjoyable dish.  I picked up one of their "Lattice & Lard" pies (Strawberry, Peach, Ginger) to go.  This mini sized pie was really tasty, with a nice balance of sweet and tart and savory.  Definitely recommend picking one up!  So, if you are looking for something to eat and are feeling a bit adventurous, stop in.  Or, if you have one of those creative minds that can see something out of the norm on a shelf and say to yourself, "I could make xxxxxxxxx with this!", then make it a destination!  Review #133

My wife and I have dined here twice with friends and we are anxious to return!  This is clearly our favorite restaurant and apparently others think so too (Indpls Monthly Top 25 for 2016).  The first time we went (3-2-16), we were able to catch the last spot in the limited parking behind the restaurant.  We entered from the New York St entrance to take advantage of the visual impact wall of fresh herbs and greens growing on the wall.  When we were shown to our seats next to the indoor/outdoor fireplace, I asked if we might look around and were given a personal tour of the facility.  When other places might be pushing to get you seated and order, the front end folks showed us the bar area on the west end, the private dining area above that, the cooling area where house made charcuterie hangs aging for some future creation.  By the time my friend and I returned, our waiter had already brought out a basket of multiple kinds of fresh breads.    This is the top of the line for the Cunningham Dining Restaurant Group.  The service we had was spot on all night and seemed to know when to arrive without any delays.  I also like that we placed our entire order at the beginning so that the different types of entrees could be timed to arrive at our table at the same time.  I am a big fan of helping the kitchen to plan a perfect dining experience for me.  Finally the food was fantastic.  For our first visit, I ordered the Pork Belly Custard, the Red Oak Salad (pulled from the wall I mentioned earlier), the Chicken with charred romanesco, lobster risotto, butter poached lobster, and enoki mushrooms.  The unexpectedly huge piece of lobster meat in the risotto might as well have made this a Chicken and Lobster entree.  Fantastic!  Oh, and my coffee and chocolate dessert was playfully plated and was rich in multiple coffee and chocolate flavors.  On our second visit (4-6-16), we lucked into a spot right down the street from where the valet parking station sits in front of the restaurant ($6 was the price for Valet service.)  Again, we had a wonderful meal with fantastic service.  We felt like royalty here.  Very knowledgeable wait staff and sommeliers answering our questions and offering suggestions when asked.    This time, I ordered the Crab & Octopus Roll (with sliced avocado, jalapeno, sesame, crispy potato crumbles, mango smear, chili, and white ponzu).  This was the first time I have tried octopus and to be honest, the combination of flavors was so good, I couldn't really identify the individual taste.  My wife, who isn't a seafood enthusiast, saw how beautiful my plate was and tried the dish.  Even she liked it!  We were totally surprised and that added to the fun of the evening.  I also ordered the Whole Grains Salad with meyer lemon cream, feta cheese, lentil falafel, potato chips, and roasted tomato jam.  This was okay, but not my favorite since it is such a change from the usual "salad" course.  Finally, I had the Salmon with pork ragu, asparagus, artichoke, and yellow tomato jam.
