Again, at the risk of sounding like a broken record, it was delicious.    Yes, the experience is expensive.  Yes, the portions aren't a lot for the money.  But if you are a foodie and love trying delicious combinations while being treated to excellent service, I HIGHLY recommend Vida.  Review #55

We headed north to Zionsville for lunch at "Rosie's Place"  (Sun 6-12-16).  We were fortunate to find a spot right in front of the restaurant.  Seemed like a good omen for a good meal.  We had not made reservations, but only waited a few minutes at the entrance which allowed us to look over the menu as well as the large number of pastries located at the check out counter. (The waitress takes your orders and gives you your bill, but you pay at the counter which allows you to add pastries to your bill as well as keep an eye on your credit card the whole time.  Thumbs up on both accounts!)  The interior of the place is not fancy and the tables are packed together somewhat closely, but there was enough room to get around and the noise level never got so loud that our conversation was ever interrupted.  We placed our beverage order.  We noticed that the glasses were hot from coming directly out of the dishwasher.  My wife was first to notice it and was surprised since she ordered iced tea.  I ordered one of the limited number of craft beers and I think my glass could have used one more rinse since there was a noticeable scent of detergent in the first sip.  I took another sip and the taste wasn't as noticeable....not sure it was really that or not, but something that should be watched for.  Aside from the beverage surprises, the food made up for the rough start.  My wife ordered the half soup/half sandwich combo.  She chose a very tasty tomato bisque that was as thick as a ragout....could have been more soup like.  She also ordered the egg salad sandwich and took the waitress' suggestion of toasting the bread.  I ordered the Salmon BLT - blackened salmon with crispy bacon (delicious!), baby spinach, roasted tomatoes, and pesto mayo on grilled ciabatta bread.  This was a delicious sandwich.  It was loaded with baby spinach that made it hard to see the fish, but was well balanced in flavor with the other ingredients.    I ordered the Spinach Salad as my side dish.The spinach salad had very sweet and colorful strawberries and was served with a strawberry vinaigrette.  Excellent choice.  Feeling good and happy about the overall meal, we couldn't help but order a few samples of the baked goods.  We chose the blueberry scone, the toffee cookie, and a gooey butter cookie to go.  The butter cookie barely made it out of the restaurant.  It was delicious!  I am saving the other two for tomorrow morning's breakfast.  If you don't mind a drive, Zionsville's Main Street is worth checking out as it has rebounded from the doldrums it went through a few years ago.  We will be back soon to check out some of the other restaurants too.  Review #11

Another fabulous night of friends and food on an early Thursday evening.  Our group of four had been anticipating our return visit, especially since both couples had earned their Cunningham Dining Group VIP gift card.  Excellent service from Adam and the rest of the staff.  Very knowledgeable about all the items on the menu.  Excellent recommendations and a sense of humor that was easy going, but totally professional.    From the moment we ordered our beverages, we kept experiencing fantastic flavors.  The smoked cherry in the Amaretto sour was so good that our friend asked the waiter if each of us at the table could have one just to taste how delicious it was.  The complimentary amuse bouche of smoked salmon on a house made dill pickle slice had one of our group wishing for a plate of them.  The mushrooms in the Wild Mushroom Croque had another party wishing for a plate of them.  And so on throughout the dinner.  Wonderful combinations as our party tried new flavor components for the first time ever.  This is a place you can trust the chef to know what pairs well, even if you don't know what some of the ingredients are.  (Please note the staff is all too willing to help answer any questions about the menu and the preparation.)  We all had a wonderful evening and look forward to our next visit.    p.s.  The new patio furniture has arrived, but we did not sit outside during dinner.  Rev #1

After lunch on Saturday, my wife and I stopped in Black Acre Brewing.  We took advantage of the free parking in a lot behind the brewery.  We considered sitting on the patio under the table umbrellas, but a couple pesky bees kept buzzing around my wife's soda, so we moved back into the bar.  Our waitress was very cool with the moving around and maintained a great attitude throughout our visit.  I decided I wanted to try a flight of some of the less bitter beers available.  The samples (about 4 oz each) are only $2 each, so I sampled four different styles.  Our waitress arranged them in order that she thought would maximize the appeal.  I started with the Sassy Pants kettle sour farmhouse ale.  (5% ABV, no IBU listed)  This was definitely a sour ale, kind of a lemony taste.  Otherwise, very smooth.  I moved on to the Cucumber Basil Blonde which is a variant of their Lamp Post Blonde (which was sadly not available).  The chilled cucumber flavor was much more pronounced than the basil and reminded me of a refreshing taste of cool water.  No aftertaste, just a clean flavor.  (6% ABV, 18 IBU)  My third selection was noticeably different in appearance.  The Killer Robots was very fruity in taste due to Blackberry and Ginger.  The aftertaste was more of alcohol than any of my other choices.  (5.3% ABV 23 IBU)  My final selection was the Hive Wire Hopped Session Braggot with Mango.  This tasted really bitter like orange rind, but was really low on the IBU scale (5% ABV 28 IBU)  Just goes to show that IBU isn't always a guarantee on personal tasting.    I have tasted other Black Acre brews at restaurants around town like the Flora Flora Flora Blonde Ale (my favorite), Natural Liberty, and Cherry Ol' Fritz (sour).  Of the seven beers I have tried, I would be likely to try five of them again.  I can't comment on the food or the late night vibe, but the service was attentive, the decor was cool, but welcoming, and the overall quality and variety of beer is enough to give this place a solid review.  My only negatives were that two of the beers I was hoping to taste were out of stock.  Review #95

Here's a thought...if you are going to name the place River Heritage Park, you should post some information about the heritage.  I saw unusual rolling mounds with a walkway cutting through them, but no information.  There is a large white silo in the park that seems to be a central feature, but no information.  Why are they there?  The park also is along the White River and unlike the park just about a mile to the north, this one gets flooded.  So, my exploration of the park was limited to the areas immediately by the parking lot which though sandy, was packed down and dry.  The saving grace of the place is the universally accessible playground.  It says for kids from 2 - 12 "where all abilities play".  All the equipment is low rise and ramp accessible.  I am not sure every piece is like that, but at least they have made an effort to be inclusive.  There is also a large shelter but it isn't very close to the parking lot or the playground, so it has some exclusivity if you want it, but otherwise, isn't in the best location.  Overall, it is an okay place, but certainly doesn't have the "wow" factor of some of the other regional parks.  Review #799

I've been meaning to stop in here for awhile, so I finally made a plan to make it a destination one Wednesday(4-6-16) for lunch.  I was able to find street parking reasonably close and the lunch time crowd wasn't too packed, I didn't have to wait in line to place my order at the counter.  I decided to try the Turkey, avocado, bacon, and cheese on a croissant with a side of cole slaw.   Excellent choice.  The croissant was what I had hoped it would be on texture and flavor.  The rest of the ingredients were fresh and generous without being over the top.  Just an all around good sandwich.  I also stopped at the bakery counter to get some bread to go.    It's a shame it takes me nearly an hour to get to Broad Ripple.  This is a sandwich worth stopping back in for!  Review #36

Mad Max Smokehouse is one of those food trucks you wish was around all the time.  They have two locations that are fairly fixed on the schedule:  The LA Fitness at 106th & Michigan Road is where you can find them Mon-Fri from 11-2.  During the summer, they will try being open from 4-6 for the dinner rush there.  I had the good fortune of finding Brad, the operator of Mad Max Smokehouse, while at Traders Brewing at 86th and Zionsville Road.  Basically, whenever Traders is open to sell beer, Mad Max is there to provide food.  So, Thu-Fri for evenings, and Sat and Sunday for late lunch and dinner.  I caught Brad right as they opened on a Saturday.  I ordered the 3/4 pound Mad Max Sandwich with a side of pan fried potatoes.  First note that the brisket is sliced, not shredded, so it is similar to eating a high quality roast beef sandwich with the smoked flavors of bbq and a large amount of sweet Kansas City sauce (Brad says they smother the meat in sauce for traditional).  So, if you want less sauce, be sure to let Brad know!  (Note:  he is developing a vinegar sauce but hasn't begun offering that on the meats yet.)  You also get a couple slices of Texas Toast with your order and you can specify if you want it on the side to mop up the sauce or have the beef on top.  Since the pan fried potatoes were running a little long, Brad whipped up a pesto chicken flatbread that was amazing!  Crispy edges on the flat bread and a nice punch of flavor from the garlic and basil pesto which complemented the chicken and cheese.  Bad news:  It is not on the regular menu...yet!  While eating at the bar, he stopped by and asked if I wanted to try a dessert he was developing that he called the "Apple Thing"!   He makes his own cinnamon bread (no raisins in his bread) and tops it with carmelized apples and cinnamon.  This was also very sweet and had just enough spice to add depth to the sweet and tart combo.  Again, it's not available yet, but hopefully will be soon.  I really liked the tender slices of brisket and the food paired well with the beer at the brewery.  If you want to try something new and enjoy great flavor while doing it, hunt down Mad Max Smokehouse's food truck.  Review #804

Pretty good food at a great price in this hard to spot location.  I was wandering through Fountain Square and after parking in the public lot just north of Virginia, crossed over to the south side of the street to Naisa.  There is no outside signage for Naisa.  They do have a large sign inside the restaurant that is visible through a window, but that's it for calling attention to the restaurant.  (It is in the second building west of the Woodlawn intersection.)  Once I got into the entrance, I had to turn to the right to go through the "enter" door.  Although no sign was posted, I waited to be seated since I was having a late lunch and a number of tables were awaiting being cleared.  One of the staff acknowledged me and when I indicated I was dining alone, he cleared and cleaned a table and brought me back.  The restaurant is long and narrow and is decorated with consignment art work.  Light music seemed to add to the Asian atmosphere.  (Note:  A windowed door in the back is for access to the restrooms though no sign is visible from the dining area that indicates a restroom.)  Service was hustling to catch up with all the diners checking out and clearing the tables.  Even with that, I was pleased with how quickly my order was taken, my food brought out, and with the  regular checking in to see if I was doing okay.  The food itself was pretty tasty!  I really enjoyed the egg drop soup which was served as part of my lunch special.  In addition to the free soup, there was a small plate of fried noodles served with both duck sauce (sweet) and spicy mustard (horseradish).    My entree was the Honey Sesame Chicken with rice (I chose brown), broccoli, and a seafood cheese wonton.  The wonton was delightfully cheesy while staying crisp.  The broccoli pieces were bite sized (Yeah!) but a little over cooked.  The chicken was lightly breaded dark meat with a sweet sauce (kinda sweet, not over the top) and toasted sesame seeds.  The chicken was shaped into "nuggets" just a bit bigger than bite sized, but were pretty easy to cut with my fork.  The flavor was fine, but nothing to make me say "wow".  I was pleased with the overall quality of Naisa.  Glad to see they were able to get back on track an reopen this spring.  Review #359

In a strip mall area surrounded by chain restaurants, it was nice to find an independent cafe that had good food and a nice vibe.  You will notice lots of art on the walls in the dining room.  The noise level, even when busy, is conducive for conversation.  And the food is approachable and tasty.  I ordered the Carolina Mustard Pulled Pork with a side of fries.  The Pork itself was great.  Just enough bark to add that extra bit of flavor to the large pieces of meat.  (This isn't shredded like some other places.)  Although I really liked the sandwich, I didn't thin the sauce was Carolina Mustard...it was dark brown and sweet without the acidity from a typical mustard bbq.  Still, it was good.  My wife opted to try the Chili "Mac Doggie" which is a bed of macaroni, topped with a spicy chili and a 1/4# hot dog.  I was surprised that she liked it since she normally doesn't care for spicy food.  I tasted it and upon first tasting, the bite was rather bland (tasting the mac first), but at the swallow, the heat of the chili ramped up quickly to a noticeable level.  I won't say it was my favorite flavor of chili, but it definitely met the description of spicy.  The servers were attentive, but would sometimes disappear from the floor to pick up their food from the kitchen.  Sometimes, every front end person was missing from the floor.  Although they were very friendly and welcoming, they tended to make a lot of unnecessary trips (like not clearing an empty plate while making a water refill run.)    We did experience a long delay from the time we sat down until our food was delivered (we noticed other tables asking too.)  We arrived right around noon and there was a rush of people at the same time, so I think it was a case of bad timing for the small kitchen.  It's not fast food, so if you go, allow time for dining.  Review #737

I met a friend on Wednesday for lunch at B's Po Boy.  After parking in the lot behind the restaurant, I met him inside.  There were a number of seats available outside under the umbrellas at each table, but since it was getting warm, the a/c seemed better suited to lunch.    After a bit of a wait, our waiter showed up and took our drink and food orders.  I decided to go with a recommended Yelp selection of 1/2 Shrimp (fried) po boy with extra shrimp (upcharge) and remoulade (upcharge).  I also decided to get a side salad with the house red wine vinaigrette.  The sandwiches here are plentiful!  The bread is very tasty and fresh tasting; sturdy enough to hold up to the sandwich, but soft enough to have bite appeal.  My sandwich was loaded with crispy shrimp.  The shrimp were bite-sized and didn't have any shell remnants. Yeah!  The salt was right on the edge of being too strong, but after that first sensation that the shrimp might be too salty, the flavor seemed to balance more as I began to eat the sandwich as intended.  The first bites I took were of the plentiful shrimp that spilled out of the bun in this upgraded version.  But when I tasted the shrimp with the bread, remoulade, lettuce, tomato, mayo and pickle, the saltiness came back into line and complimented the rest of the flavors.  The side salad was just right in size and the wine vinaigrette dressing was flavorful enough to enjoy.  Overall, a pretty good selection  I enjoyed going back to B's.  I had forgotten how much I had liked my previous visits, so it's always nice when the current visit doesn't disappoint.  Review 137

How does this place continue to get better every time?  If you have put off going to Vida waiting for it to get settled beyond the start up phase, then you have been missing out!  This was our fourth time and we brought friends who love this place as much as we do.  This is our absolute favorite place to dine!!  The staff are so welcoming: Just the right balance of friendly and efficient.  Brandon D was our host tonight and answered every question and really seemed to appreciate guests who take an interest in the food.    From the amuse bouche and bread serving through the next three courses, all the food was fantastic.  Brightly displayed with accent sauces that are full of flavor, not just decoration, the food had many layers of taste and texture.  Who knew that so many flavors could be pulled together?  And, to make our evening even more special, Brandon knew we had missed the "Dig In" festival over the weekend, so he brought out Pastry Chef Hattie McDaniels bearing a complimentary serving of the dessert Vida served at "Dig In".  We really enjoyed our chance to talk with her.    Three of our group dined on the "Devour Downtown" menu (three courses for $45) while I went rogue and ordered the scallops, the halibut (with robuchon potatoes!!), followed by the panna cotta with berries.  The evening flew by all too quickly.  I only wish I had something to mop up all the sweet and savory sauces left on my plates.  Rev #12

While visiting a friend in the hospital, I wanted to grab something for an early dinner.  Trader's Mill was just across 86th, so I decided to give it a try.   They share a large parking lot, so finding a spot was easy.  The interior is kept kind of dark even though it was sunny outside.  I was directed to seat myself anywhere I liked, so I grabbed a spot at the bar since I was dining alone.  Service was quick and efficient throughout the meal.  I ordered a breaded tenderloin with the works and upgraded to the onion rings.  The tenderloin was typical Hoosier style..too thin and too large for a bun.  But, it was still moist inside instead of being overcooked.  The breading had little flavor while hot (I got a to go box and noticed the flavor was more noticeable after the sandwich had gotten cold.)  When I finally got to where the bun and other toppings could help, the sandwich definitely tasted better.  The onion rings were thin and crispy on the outside and easy to bite through.  (I hate when old onions with thick membranes between layers don't get cooked through!)  Excellent job on the ring preparation!  The breading was light and golden brown.  Really couldn't ask for better!  Since I wanted to get back over to the hospital, I passed on trying their beer selections and was on my way within 45 minutes.  Review #1210

Note:  My review is based upon ordering take out with my interaction with the staff limited to time while I waited.  I have seen the signs for this place hundreds of times in the six years I have lived in Mooresville.  But for the longest time, I didn't really know where it was.  There's a small corner of Johnson County that crosses SR 37 near the intersection with SR 144.  Those kids go to Center Grove (Greenwood area).  The kids across the street go to Mooresville.  The street address is listed as Martinsville, and the cashier told me the phone number was from Bargersville.  No wonder I was confused!!  So, if you are heading south on SR 37, you can find this place by turning west onto SR 144 and take the first side road that leads to the BP on the corner.  Across the street (behind the parking lot for the Knuckle Sandwich) is a small white building that looks like a single story house.  If you still don't see it, you can call from the parking lot and they will talk you in! (They literally have done this!)  Anyway, I found this restaurant and new from the sign that they had BBQ, so I thought for my first visit, that would be my selection.  I went for the brisket, though they have pork and chicken as well.  I went for the platter which includes two sides from a large selection.  I went with the baked potato and green beans (you also get two halves of a sliced and buttered Texas Toast).  First, let me say that the staff was friendly for the 15 minutes or so I was there.  Very personable and welcoming.    The brisket was thick sliced (about a half inch) and was generously portioned.  It was served dry with a half cup of sweet BBQ sauce on the side.  The brisket was a little dry on it's own and didn't have a deep smokiness to it.  Therefore, the slices broke apart easily when I used my fork to lift it.  Fortunately, the sauce compensated for the drier meat and made it quite tasty.  The potato was an Idaho baked in aluminum foil.  So, the skin didn't get crispy, but the flesh of the potato was thoroughly cooked.  Again, it was a large potato.  The green beans were cut small with many pieces only about a half inch in length.  There was a lot of seasoning (primarily salt and pepper stood out) and benefited from having onion and either bacon bits or ham bits cooked into the mix.  They were excellent and I could have eaten more!!  Overall, quick and friendly service with hearty portions of comfort food make this place worth the effort to find!  Review #812

My wife and I stopped in for a quick bite while on the northwest side.  The sandwiches we ordered were really good.  However, the soups brought the average down.  She ordered a combo 1/2 sandwich and cup of soup which is packaged at the same price as a whole sandwich.  Since it was a "cold" sandwich, she got to select the bread and all the toppings she wished to add.    However, even though the corn chowder had lots of nice sized veggies and had a sweetness that was good, the corn chowder was very "soupy".  We both like our chowder to have a thicker, more hearty consistency.  This looked more like vegetable soup with an extra bit of corn.  The flavor was okay, but it wasn't what she was hoping for.  I went with a whole sandwich from the grill.  The daily special was "The Libby" which was lots of warm turkey (layered to about half an inch thick!) topped with crisp bacon and provolone cheese, with Chipotle mayo on grilled sourdough bread.  The prime ingredients were great.  However, the Chipotle mayo didn't do much other than add a little heat (not significant.)  I am not sure if you can order extras on the grilled sandwich like tomato or lettuce.  They didn't offer to add any sides like they did on my wife's cold sandwich, so I assume that it is served as is (I guess it wouldn't hurt to ask before ordering.)  Anyway, the flavor was a bit on the bland side, but still good.  I also ordered a cup of the chicken chili.  This had nice sized pieces of chicken along with the beans in a chili with a definite chili powder taste.  Nothing bland there!     Overall, I liked how quickly they greeted us and my wife had her sandwich delivered to our table by the time I got done placing my order and paying.  The staff were all friendly as well.  Plenty of parking out front and most options are $7 or $8.  Additional sides and drinks can be more if you don't order one of the specials.  Review #272

At the time of my writing this review, this park is approaching the 50th anniversary of an historic event in Indianapolis' history.  On this site, Senator (a candidate for President) Robert F Kennedy announced to the citizens of Indianapolis that the Reverend Martin Luther King Jr was assassinated.  On a night when our country saw anger unleashed in many cities, the message of love, compassion, and unity delivered by Sen. Kennedy gave comfort to the people gathered here.  Indy was the only major city in the country to escape violence.  One of my favorite art pieces in the city was dedicated by President Clinton in 1995 showing the outreached hands of King and Kennedy stretching across the lighted path beneath them.  The images are cut out of the sweeping curves of bronze signifying that we need to break out of the routine, change course to make the world a better place.  The memorial "Landmark for Peace" is the focus of the southern half of the park.  The northern half is a more traditional children's park containing a playground, basketball court, swimming pool, and a large shelter/pavilion.  There are two parking lots on the northern half.  The park has many paved paths to move around including down to the memorial.  The park has seen improvement due to the upcoming 50th anniversary which will likely have a number of festivities planned around the event.  Review #516

Although not a official city park, the Opti Park (Optimist Club) does have the standard playground features that small kids seem to enjoy.  There is also a parking lot (gravel), a baseball field with a backstop, a small shelter, and some shaded seating.  The best part about the park is that it has a great location that allows you to park here, play and relax, and then if you wish, to stroll over to the Arts Center (on the north end) or along the Monon to some shops and restaurants.  So, as long as you don't mind walking, it's a great place.  Otherwise, the park is what you get just about anywhere in the metro area.  Review #1176

My wife and I stopped in after seeing their colorful decor on the back porch/yard of this shop in Greenwood.  Since it was a fall day, all the unique items fit perfectly with the season.  From rustic to fancy, this place has a bit of everything.  My wife was drawn to the nice selection of clever plaques touting the wonders of being a Grandma!  I liked the varieties of yard flags and pot pourri. Lots of holiday items too!  The staff was very friendly and welcoming.  They shared info about when the open house would be in November for converting their entire store from fall to Christmas items.  They even mentioned to watch their Facebook page for updates on sales and promotions.  Sure, lots of places do that, but I liked that the staff had such enthusiasm for the place.  It was like an invitation to join the fun!  We will definitely be back, and for me, it is a lot closer than driving to Nashville/Brown County.  Review #147

I had heard good things about Santorini, so I met a friend for lunch (3-24-16).  I decided to go with one of the daily specials.  The food was generous in proportion, but frankly, didn't make much of an impression on me.  The dining area is a spacious room and the service was okay.  No complaints...just nothing that makes me desire to return.  Review #39

I don't usually pick donuts.  I like to eat early when I get up, so I am not hungry by the time I get out the door.  But something about the story behind this new franchise from Amish country in northern Indiana made me curious to stop by.  So glad I did!    When I stopped in this small stand alone building along SR 135 (known as Meridian north of the county line), I was surprised to see the "stations" around the lobby.  Over on the left side was a wall with rows of Jellies.  Next to that is a station for beverages.  An island with a full size bicycle on it was loaded with packaged cookies and pies (full size and minis).    There is a limited amount of seating by the door, and a large display counter of freshly baked donut options.  There is also a table of packaged donuts and a small table with samples!  One bite of the best selling "Cinnamon Caramel" donuts and I was hooked!  I can't believe how moist and light the donuts are and the flavors of the donuts were disproportionately "eye buggin'" good!  I bought a box of the donut holes and opted to try one of the mini peach pies as well.    Service was busy but friendly as customers continued to enter even at 11 a.m. while I was there.  Looks like the place is off to a good start and with quality like this, I think they may be around for a long time!  Review #464

My initial review was a five star for when the restaurant first opened.  However, I was informed by someone I trust that the initial chef who opened the restaurant was no longer associated with the place within six months.  Apparently there were issues between management and the chef on how the place should be run, so I was advised to wait awhile and have not been back since the change.  So, please be aware that my review is based upon my experience before the change.  Our group of 3 dined early on Thursday evening and had a genuinely fun evening of sampling food and excellent service.   We especially enjoyed sharing our appetizers, both of which featured Dungeness crab.  The Dungeness Crab Cake came with a Remoulade and herb salad.  The crab was fresh and the taste was prominent even with the light breading...not hidden by strong herbal flavors like some other restaurants.  The Crab Pot was a creamy bowl of Dungeness crab, artichokes, and Parmesan served warm with four slices of artisnal bread.  Delicious!  We did order another batch of bread ($2) because we didn't want to leave any of the dip in the bottom of the bowl!  Note:  Even though the restaurant has only been open a few weeks, there have been a number of changes to the menu that aren't reflected on the website yet.  I was going to try a Prime Filet Tips & Wild Mushroom appetizer, but it is now gone.  Other small changes like the type of crab or the type of cheese or nuts used in a coating have changed.    For my entree, I selected the Pan Roasted Kachemak Bay Halibut Cheeks (5) in a Parmesan crust, served over a bed of risotto and a ring of lemon butter sauce.  Simple flavors, yet excellent results.   Another entree of note was a pieced together meal of Grilled Split Lobster Tail paired with a side of Indiana Sweet Corn Brulee.  The lobster comes with a small bowl of liquid butter for dipping.  The brulee comes out with a somewhat charred appearance, but a flavor that is pleasant roasted corn with the sweetness of a candy glaze.  Definitely would order the brulee again.  Sure, there were a couple things that needed some attention, but level heads and pointing the issues out in a friendly way, led to swift and satisfactory resolution.  The manager came over quickly and let us know what he suspected the cause of the problem was so that we could go on with our fun.  I can only imagine things will continue to improve as the place gains experience.  Our servers, led by Brandon, were all friendly and willing to explain any of the items we didn't understand on the menu.  Food was brought out swiftly from the time we placed our orders.  They had a nice selection of wines, beers, and house cocktails.  Valet service was also available (Thurs through Sat nights) though we found a spot on Michigan Street for $3 for 2 hours.  I look forward to returning again for another great night!  Review #128

I went here in March, so none of the water park was in use, but even without having access to that large portion of the park, I can see this park has a lot to offer.  First the park has a lot of paved parking and instead of making it some giant rectangle, it is separated by outcroppings of natural plantings.  There are also paved paths to a number of the activity centers in the park.  There are quite a few activity centers:  a skate park near the entrance, a full court basketball area, a playground is located right next to a splash park with a shelter (concession stand?) with restrooms within easy range of both.  There are shelters that can be reserved and an expanse of open space that includes a hill which can be a challenging uphill run or a thrilling sled down when there is snow.  It was clean and seemed in fine condition (a park and rec worker was there even in March taking care of the place.)  Overall, it felt like a place I would gladly return to.  Review #644

I had driven by this restaurant a few times and finally made it a point to stop in.  So, one Friday I headed to 16th & Penn to try one of their lunches.  I began looking over the menu, but when the waitress arrived and listed the day's specials, I decided to go with the two Tilapia Tacos and added a side of apple slaw.    The food was good and served with little delay.  I especially enjoyed the twist on slaw with the Granny Smith apples.  Nice creativity in the kitchen!  The atmosphere is elegant and I almost felt under dressed in my casual attire, but I noticed most of the folks seated where somewhat casual as well.  The only thing that I would caution against is sitting in the booths.  There was so little room between seat and table that I could barely get my feet under without some effort.  The good news is that when I went, there was ample seating elsewhere in the restaurant.   Service was efficient and cordial and reminded me of the type of service I would receive at a higher end establishment.    I plan on returning with some friends so that we can sample some of the regular menu items.  Review #43

The park is huge with open prairie and lawns that run from 30th to 38th street on the near east side.  As many other reviews have mentioned, there is room for frisbee golf in addition to the other amenities.  The north end has numerous basketball courts and a small playground by one of the shelters.  There are several shelters scattered throughout the park.  On the south end, a local police check-in spot lies on the southwest corner across the street from the Community Center.  Near the center is a nice playground and a small pond.  The park has history:  The Children's Zoo was here from 1964 to 1987 before transitioning to the full zoo at White River Park in 1988.  If you walk around the playground, you will see a couple pedestals, one with a frog and the other with a chimp sitting on top.  If you find some old photo of the zoo, it is fun to try and see where the attractions were located.  (Some are still identifiable.)  If you like getting outdoors, there is plenty of room to walk or play while leaving your car in the huge lot on the south end of the park.  Review #695

I really enjoyed my visit to this new distillery located on the northeast end of the Circle City Industrial Complex (CCIC).  It is a little challenging to find if you are not familiar with the area and road construction along Brookside doesn't help with a business trying to launch.  But once the street is finished, the distillery should be close to offering more to the customers.  The distillery is run by three guys who have a passion for their product and a vision of how they want to grow the business.  Matt, with his dog, was setting up signs outside to help customers find the place (among other duties).  He and his wife Jaime are part owners.  Mason, Matt's brother (also a part owner) primarily works on the distilling end of the business.  And Dmitri is the bartender/mixologist with a load of personality that makes an excellent Mojito.    The large front room of the business is filled with four top tables and about another dozen bar stools.  From there, you can see the stacks of barrels and the still used for making their liquor.  At the time of my visit, they were only selling rum and gin, but have plans in the near future for adding two more varieties. (They have added a Dancehall Panic Rum which is more Jamaican and sweeter and a Barrel Aged Hopped Gin. 8/31/18)  During my visit, there were four standard drinks offered.  The rum was used in the Mojito and a Daiquiri.  The Gin was offered in a Gin & Tonic and a Circle City Spritz option.  (See photo of menu for more offerings).  While talking with the guys, I learned that they hope to have a tasting room set up so that guests can sample the expanded line soon.  It was still in the planning stages, so I didn't get any cost estimate for the tastings.  (There was a small flight of three 1/2 oz tastes for $8 and single tastings 1/2 oz. for $3 as of 8/31/18.)  There are no plans for adding any hot food.  The current menu offers Broad Ripple Chips by the bag.  Bottles of their gin and rum are sold in the 750 ml bottles.  As the CCIC develops, I think the place will take off as a logical extension off Mass Avenue.  Centerpoint Brewing and Lick Ice Cream are already firmly established there along with a number of artists/galleries who rent space.  I am looking forward to my next visit!  Review #1008

I was in Broad Ripple on a Saturday and decided to try out the brunch menu at Bent Rail Brewery.  There was plenty of parking behind the building.  I walked passed the outdoor patio tables and entered the large warehouse housing the brewery.  From the rear, the bar was on the right and the family dining and stage were on the left.  I grabbed a seat at a small table (per directions on a sign) and waited for the staff to greet me.  Before long, I was acknowledged and given a menu, informed that the brunch menu was the only option until 1 p.m.  That was fine with me, so I ordered a draft while reviewing my munching options.    Note:  They have begun making their own beer!  There were six varieties available, but were not offering flights yet.  (They have ordered pallets for serving them, so stay tuned to reviews!)  I selected the German Hefeweizen with Apricots called the Apricot Illusion (5.2% 15 IBU).  Yum!  The flavor was delicious!   I couldn't help but notice that there were three large groups in addition to a smattering of small groups dining that day.  Fortunately, I arrived before two of the large groups, so I was able to get my order placed for the Grilled Chicken Ranch Wrap.  Unfortunately, there was only the one waitress to serve everyone in the place.  I think she did a great job of staying calm and relatively efficient, but someone from management should have came out to assist (I did see two guys that looked to be employees not doing anything out front.)  Anyway, my wrap was pretty good.  I ordered one of three sauces for my wrap, going with mild (they also have hot and BBQ).  The wrap was short, but thick and sliced to make it easier to handle.  I also selected a fruit cup which was filled with a variety of melon and berries that were ripe and tasty.  Overall, I was pleased with my visit and look forward to returning to try a flight along with my next meal.  Review #400

Having nothing planned for lunch Saturday, I decided to head to the near east side.  I started my journey by stopping in at Love Handle, parking in the lot directly behind the building.  Since I arrived around 11, there wasn't much of a crowd and I was immediately helped at the counter where I placed my order.  I selected another Sodrel Apple Soda to go with my sandwich, the "Enos" (Braised Pork Cheek, Artichoke Crema, & Ramp Fermented Cukes on a locally produced bread.)  Once again, I was thoroughly pleased with the taste, right from the first bite!  In common terms, think of this sandwich most like a pulled pork sandwich with pickles, but with a flavor upgrade.  One of the things I really like about Chef Chris' creations are that they remind me of favorite sandwiches, but he always finds a way to make them extra tasty.  The more I ate, the more I became aware of a hint of "heat" build up (and a bit of saltiness too, but not out of control.)    I enjoyed the sandwich so much that I decided to get another selection "to go" since I didn't know how soon I would be back to try another.  This time, I went with the "Bex" (Smoked Pork Belly, Limburger, Raspberry Jam, & Raw Onion on bread.)  I talked with the chef about the Limburger since I had a negative opinion in my head from watching old cartoons where Limburger was likened to Pepe le Pew! :)  True enough, the salt and raspberry jam in the sandwich offset the pungency of the cheese as Chef told me.  However, I did find the smokiness of the pork belly a bit strong for the rest of the sandwich.  So, this wasn't my favorite of the sandwiches, but I like to push my range of tastes to experience new flavors, so it was worth ordering.  A very friendly staff and bright dining area make this restaurant inviting.  I look forward to trying again in the near future to see what other combinations I may discover.  Rev #6

I stopped in this quirky strip mall coffee shop that has a unique vibe that feels cool and fun.  Lots of consignment art on the walls; an array of seating chairs and couches, and interesting music playing, loud enough to be heard, but not stifle conversation.  I started with a cup of coffee and a Sausage and Egg (w cheese) croissant.  Even the simple cup of black coffee let me choose from five flavors.  The heated cup was handed to me after placing my order at the counter on the rear right side.  I was encouraged to sample the different flavors, settling on the Morning Blend.  While I waited, the croissant was heated and brought out to me at a location I selected.  The croissant was especially light and fluffy.  The sausage patty had a hint of Rosemary which made it take on a slightly different flavor from traditional breakfast sausage.  Overall, a very nice option!  I wasn't finished with my coffee, so I decided to try out one of their many flavors of muffins.  I opted for a blueberry.  Nice size and fresh tasting, I liked that the blueberries were still moist.    They offered to heat the muffin as well, which I recommend as well.  My coffee order was for a single cup.  If I wanted refills, they were an additional 50 cents and were self serve.  The only waiter activities were delivery of heated items and clearing of plates and utensils after you leave.  Still, it was nice to be greeted and to have pleasant exchanges each time I approached the counter.  Review #386

My first time at this event, I wasn't sure where to go, but I eventually found the exhibition hall and saw five long rows of vendors.  The outside rows and the back row were dominated by food products and wine.  The inner rows had more jewelry, pottery, wood craft, and artists.  Once inside, I decided to do a walk through just to see what caught my eye and not regret making a purchase one place just to find something I might like better later.  (Note:  They have an option where you can store your purchases and not have to carry them, since many of the food content comes in glass jars that can become heavy and strain your grip when using a plastic bag.)  Having completed my walk through, I then began doing my tastings and that was my downfall.  So many really good products, that I knew I was going to be spending some bucks!  I ended up getting some apple butter, blueberry lemon jelly, banana butter, two kinds of cheese spreads, a spicy yellow mustard, a ramp kraut, and two dipping sauces:  Caramel with ginger and dark chocolate hot fudge.  Other than just eating out of the jars, I need to figure out meals and desserts that I can take advantage of these flavors.  I went on Sunday morning and the crowds weren't bad.  Some vendors seemed loaded with customers while others with similar products had none....If I had to guess, it was about being outgoing and drawing people in.  All seemed to have samples available.  There were some really beautiful art pieces on hand, but since I wasn't looking to make a purchase, I really only looked at the pieces from outside their booths.  Still, if you are interested in acquiring something, there was a diversity of styles and mediums available.  Note that parking was running $5 in addition to the $10 per person entrance fee.  Review #258

This is a massive store with a wide variety of books, audiobooks, games, cd's, and DVD's.  If you are old school and like the feel of having a book in your hand but hate waiting for the latest read to be available at your library, then this place is a must!  The spacing in the aisles is wide enough to let people pass while you are browsing.  I hate feeling crowded in a lot of smaller stores, but that's not a problem here.  They also seemed to have quite a few folks on staff even on a Monday afternoon.  The only place that seemed like it needed a bit of attention was the south side of the store where the audio (books, dvds, etc) is located and has scanners to prevent theft.  That desk appeared to be unattended, so I heard other folks commenting that they weren't sure if they could leave that area to the main checkouts without setting off alarms.    But overall, I was pleased with the variety of offerings the place has.  I'm not sure how else this place can reinvent itself in the digital age, but I wish them luck.  I still like coming in to see what they have.  Review #1897

I really enjoyed my late lunch visit at Tavern at the Point.  By the time my wife and I arrived, the lunch rush had passed so we were able to find street parking (metered) near by and were able to grab a seat inside.  They have bar seating, counter seating in the room behind the bar, and 2- and 4-top seating inside.  When weather permits, about 40 more spots are available on the patio to overlook the busy intersection of Mass Ave and Vermont.  From the moment we entered, the staff was pleasant and welcoming.  Although we had Miranda as our primary waitress (Great job!), everyone pitched in to make sure our used plates were cleared, our beverages refreshed, and even our bill payment processed.  We especially appreciated that when the manager stopped by to ask our opinions of the meal, he took notes on some suggestions that my wife made.  I was impressed!  The indoor dining was a bit loud because of the numerous hard surfaces, but once they turned down the air conditioning, the volume became much more pleasant and conducive to conversation.  I can see this place getting loud like several other Cunningham restaurants, but at least for us, the sound was okay.  We started off with an appetizer, the Chicken Sticky buns (or Chicky Buns! ha!)  The order comes with three fluffy white buns (think marshmallow texture) filled with shredded chicken, pickled carrot and daikon, "Kayaki" (?), and served with a spicy soy.  The chicken was tender and when dipped, the balance of heat, sweet, savory, and acidity was perfect!  My wife does not care for spicy heat, but this dish had just enough to make the flavor jump without building to a level that was unpleasant for her.  She would gladly order this for a main dish for herself next visit!  I wanted to also try the Spinach salad which is large and features dried pear, brie cubes, pistachio, thin sliced apple, kale, and a choice of dressing.  I went for a vinaigrette (the Champagne vinaigrette is one of three vinaigrette options!)  The flavor here was also wonderful.  If pressed, I would say the dressing, which is added to the salad before bringing it out, was applied a little bit heavily.  Every bit of the the leaves had moisture, but not so much that there was any pooling on the bottom of the plate.  For out entrees, I thought I would go lighter, and ordered the Anne Marie Wrap which uses an herb wrap to hold spinach, cucumber relish, chickpea, apple, bleu cheese, kale, and honey mustard.  As you can see, the ingredients are very similar to my salad choice.  Although I found the flavors good, if I had to do it over, I would have probably selected something else to get a different flavor profile than the second course.  There was a bit of juice that dripped from the wrap, so if you order it, be sure you have your napkin in place.  My wife wanted to give the Big Fontana Burger a try.  This is one of those mile high stacks that often make folks pause to figure out how to get all the flavors in one bite.  The burger (made with the same beef mix as BRU burger across the street) has two 4-oz patties with a couple slices of American Cheese, multiple strips of thick smoky bacon, shaved onion, shaved pickles (these may be house style, not typical store bought dills), and Fontana sauce (I think from Fontina soft cheese).  The ingredients are stacked on a butter bun and served with a side.  Although she liked the flavors (I agree after my sampling), she found it difficult to cut the burger for easier handling.  Instead of using a regular plate, the burger and side arrive in a round cake pan lined with paper.  The juice of the burger makes the paper a bit soggy and when trying to cut through the burger with a knife, the sides of the pan get in the way and the paper lining gets torn and can stick to the bun.  So, if you order the sandwich and want to cut it, get a side plate to make it easier.  (My wife recommended simply changing the serving dish.)  The side she selected was the pimento mac and cheese.  The dish was plentiful and topped with paprika for appearance.  They also add a bit of jalapeno into the cheese sauce for a heat element.  I found it quite good, but as mentioned before, my wife didn't enjoy it as much because of the heat level.  The manager mentioned that if she wants to order the mac and cheese without the heat, they can quickly make some for her that would be more traditional. (Another example of working with the customer to be pleased.)  All in all, I was very impressed with the new look of the place having dined here quite a few times about a dozen years ago under its previous owner.  No more cigarette smells.  No more dingy floors.  Everything looking nice and cool.  Regardless if this was the first day or one after many days of operation, I found the overall experience wonderful and the food delicious.  Review #888

Overall, the food is okay, but I have to say I was a bit disappointed after trying several new BBQ places on the south side.  Compared to those, the food here wasn't on the same level.  For full disclosure, I got my order to go but ate it within five minutes of leaving the parking lot of this restaurant tucked away to the west of the busy Michigan Road and 96th Street intersection.  I ordered two of their most popular items:  The pulled pork and the bacon mac and cheese side.  The order was out in virtually no time at all,  which is generally a plus.  However, I wasn't asked about what type of sauce to go with the pork.  It came fully loaded with a sweet sauce.  The pork was tender and moist, but it makes me wonder if they have any other flavor options.  Good, but not great.  The mac and cheese though, was very disappointing.  You know it's over cooked when it retains the shape of a large scoop.  They use larger noodle than I see in home box mixes and there wasn't much cheese flavor.  In fact, the texture of the cheese seemed like it might have been from a powder mix instead of real.  Seemed like there was no creaminess to the side.  The bacon was visible, but again, didn't add significant flavor.  Overall, I wouldn't order that again.  So, at best, I could give this a 3.5, but because the options seemed limited compared to other BBQ places, I have to round down.  The staff said that they had been open for 2 1/2 years.  Seems like they would have figured out how to make better mac and cheese or offer more sauce options by now.  Review #425

There are so many cool items in this shop that I was surprised!  Not only do they carry greeting cards, but they have collectibles including Disney, Dept 56, and Possible Dreams.  They carry puzzles, stuffed animals, Colts logo items, and lots of gift items.  There is even a women's fashion area called Simply Noelle to the left of the entrance.  On the right is a room dedicated to Dept 56 with several diorama's of village setups including Halloween, a New England Village, and a Dicken's Christmas Carol.  I must have shopped and browsed for ten minutes checking out the store and none of the three people working acknowledged me while I was there.  I liked being able to browse without being hassled, but at the Greenwood Hallmark, I was greeted and told that if I needed any help, to just ask.  That would be nice to hear from this one.  Review #2084

Plain and simple review:  If you want a delicious bundt cake (various sizes and about a dozen flavors available), then this is your 5-star place to go!  However, if you want something else, there isn't much else available to eat.  They do have some birthday candles, coffee mugs, and other little knickknacks you can by, but this is a chain that says let's do the best bundt cakes we can.  And they do.  I liked that they had a sample of the day where you can taste a bite-sized amount of one of their flavors.  I liked the sample (white chocolate raspberry) and bought one of their Bundtlettes of that kind as well as a Lemon.  Both cakes were really moist and have a light and sweet icing ribbing on them.  Very reasonable prices too since each one of the cakes was shareable in size.  Review #1713

Our group of four really enjoyed our dinner at this upscale north side addition to the Cunningham Dining Group.  They have multi-course options for a fixed price, but if you are watching $, you can order individual courses or share with a friend.  But make no mistake, this is a high quality dining experience and charges accordingly.  We went a couple weeks after the grand opening. They have valet parking, but there is also a common lot shared with the new Ironworks Hotel and what will be other businesses as they open on the first floor of the complex. (Rize, a breakfast/lunch restaurant will open in Oct 2017).  Provision is located on the second floor.  They have a separate entrance via their own stairwell, but we chose to enter via the hotel and use the elevator directly north of its entrance.  The hotel is very industrial and the restaurant has a great transitional look, with lots of wood detail, large sized tables, and a mix of browns, grays, and blacks.  An elevated patio is nearly complete and will provide outdoor seating.  An arched Chef's Table will give a close up view of the kitchen and offer a nine course dining menu ($125/ea) with a wine pairing available ($50).  On our night, the table was used for seating for walk-up diners.  The food:  Excellent!  Chef Layton Roberts brings the magic touch from Vida with him to this site.  Starting with a complementary amuse bouche (ours was a smoked salmon with celery on a crisp) through "shares", salads, entrees, and desserts, everything we ordered was excellent.  They have different sizes on many of the "farm" options.  The staff is also willing to bring extra plates if you wish to share different courses.  I am fairly sure that the menu will change frequently using seasonal and special ingredients as they are found/available.  The service:  There is so much staff that you don't have to wait for anything.  New silverware is brought out for each course.  Water (cool, but no ice) is continually topped off.  When your food is brought out, a different staff person carries each plate instead of loading a giant platter and balancing it.  Entire orders are encouraged at the beginning of your dining with the exception of dessert which you may or may not have room for with so many courses available.  Most of the evening was very enjoyable.  As we were finishing our meal, we noticed that the noise level started to spike as the restaurant filled.  Very similar to Mesh in that sense.  So, be aware that if you like conversation with your meal, go early.  They also have a few computer glitches that they are working on when it comes to using the CRG Dining cards, so hopefully, that will become a non-issue soon.    Review #397

While browsing around Zionsville, my wife and I stopped into this boutique on the south side of Pine Street.  The shop is nicely decorated around the perimeter and features free standing racks of women's clothing in the middle.  The target age of the clothing is probably younger woman and from what we could see, targets smaller/athletic fits.  The woman behind the counter was friendly and offered to help find something, but it didn't seem the type of clothing my wife could see herself wearing.  From a neutral observers point of view, I did find the simple racks looking a bit out of place from the rest of the store which was spaced nicely and decorative.  The racks just looked a bit cluttered and not as fine as the rest of the shop.  Review #2212

I took my wife out to lunch and we both really enjoyed our time at The District Tap!  She really thought the interior was warm and inviting.  Even though there is a tv in every booth and on nearly every flat surface, the sports theme didn't interfere with her appreciation of the tastefully decorate interior.  We were greeted in the central lobby and taken to our booth in the main dining area where the bar is centrally located.  They also have a room to the left for private parties (with its own patio when weather is nice) and two more areas, including a game room with darts and shuffleboard that can be rented as semi-private areas.  I wanted to try one of the 60 drafts they have on hand.  I chose the 3 Floyds Space Station Middle Finger (a Golden American Pale Ale 6% 50 IBU) while my wife went with her standby SunKing Sunlight Cream Ale.  I found out they do flights of four beers that have about four ounces each if you are inclined to sample more than one draft at a time. (Note prices on flights varies depending upon the selections.)  In a short while, our lunches arrived.  I got the Breaded Tenderloin with Grilled Asparagus (I didn't realize there was a $1 upcharge for my side selection.)  My wife went with the TDT Cuban.  Both sandwiches were excellent.  The Cuban used shredded pork belly along with the ham and the flavor was very well paired with the other ingredients.  The pressed brioche was quite buttery tasting as well as on the fingers (napkin please!)  I must say my Tenderloin was one of the best I've had.  They didn't pound it paper thin just to get more surface area.  Instead, the lightly seasoned breading was crisped without drying out the pork inside.  Crisp and juicy.  That's a sandwich!!  Although we didn't see our server frequently, she had a knack of showing up when needed.  No waiting was involved.  Our water didn't run out and the bill was processed promptly so we could get on our way.  Oh, be sure to check in before you pay your bill.  Yelpers get a 10% discount on food items on their first visit.  We really enjoyed the food and experience.  It's definitely a place I'd return.  Review #543

This place has friendly staff and a wide variety of tea options, in hot, cold, and latte forms.  They also have some coffees and alcoholic beverages too.  For your munchies, they have bagels, muffins, scones, and several types of cookies.  Catering is also available through this shop.  For those who have been to the shop in Broad Ripple, this is a little different experience.  In BR, it is a tea shop that has merchandise and meals including soups and sandwiches.  It is a place to sit and relax.  The Keystone at the Crossing (KatC) location is a place to get in and go.  It is located in the center of the food court with a circular counter.  One spot you enter the ringed off area and place your order (note that they have paper menus for you to help yourself to so you can decide.)  To the left is a place to pick up your order after paying and giving your name.  In the space between the order and pickup counter is a display of the teas.  I assume you may be able to smell the teas to help you decide, but I didn't.  (I suggest asking the clerk before opening them.)  Because teas require water heated to near boiling and then being allowed to steep for 3 to 5 minutes (dependent upon the type of tea), you will expect a small wait for your order.  Fortunately there are lots of seating spaces near the shop.  I played it safe and simply stood and waited for my Apricot Cream hot tea.  The aroma and taste were really great.  The only problem is that it was served too hot so that I had to wait another five to ten minutes for it to become drinkable.  I make tea at home and watch my temperatures so that by the end of a five minute steep, I can drink it without a scalding risk.  Not so lucky here.  Blowing on an insulated cup which doesn't cool it off much, so I did get a bit of burn on the first sip.  Seriously, if they had managed to keep the tea at more drinkable temp, I would have given five stars.  It's nice to have a hot beverage option inside KatC.  I think I still prefer the BR location because of the wider options and the more relaxing atmosphere.  Review #2188

My wife and I had a really great breakfast at this clean and friendly breakfast franchise.  I had a desire for a large, hearty meal and was very pleased.  We pulled up near the door of this stand alone business conveniently located near the I-70 interchange for Plainfield.  (Note that the crossroad is called Perry Rd on one side and Hadley Rd on the other, so it is easy to miss if you aren't familiar with area.)  We were seated promptly and before long, our exceptionally good waitress (Debbie) brought out the coffee and soda (and additional water for me) before taking our order.  My wife went with the Ham Scrambler meal which is a basic scrambled eggs (2 large) and diced ham with a large side of hashed browns.  Although she didn't rave about the flavor of her basic selection, everything was prepared well and we gladly took a "to go" box for the amount she couldn't finish.  I decided to go with French Toast as my main meal.  I saw a picture on Yelp of a strawberry laden option posted by the owner.  The photo called it the "Honey Bear French Toast with Stuffed Strawberries".  So I ordered the Honey Bear French Toast.  Unfortunately, the photo on Yelp is not a standard option as pictured.  The Honey Bear is basically three slices of French Toast covered with honey, butter, and pecans.  When the food arrived, there weren't any berries, so I asked about them.  Although my waitress was confused because what I ordered didn't list berries and whipped cream on the menu, she took the time to ask why I thought it did.  I showed her the Yelp photo and she insisted that I would be satisfied.  After a minute, I heard her discuss the photo with the chef and that she wanted him to make it.  A couple minutes later, I had a fantastic recreation of the photo on my plate!  Although the combo of berries and honey/pecans was about a dollar more than the basic Honey Bear, it was every bit as delicious as it was visually appealing.  This waitress never lost her cool, didn't waste time acting like it was my mistake, and swiftly found a solution.  She earned a generous tip!  I also wanted a side of hash browns and 2 large eggs over easy.  They don't have those as individual sides, so she suggested one of the menu items that included both and we went with that.  This waitress found solutions!    So, if you are looking for solid, delicious food that is a pain to make at home, but great to treat yourself to when starting your day, I highly recommend this restaurant.  My only negative would be for the owner to fix his photo description on Yelp.    Review #365

I avoided all the drama by simply pulling in to the pumps and filling up with gas.  I liked that they had the squeegee and towels to clean my windows actually in working condition.  However, the pump I chose ran out of paper and directed me inside.  I didn't need a paper receipt and simply used my phone to take a picture of the amount.  No need to go inside.  No drama.  Review #2900

If you like your food with a bit of spicy heat, why not try a Flamme Burger!  I was able to find a spot in the busy parking lot outside the restaurant and once I entered, the hostess/manager (?) suggested I sit wherever I liked and she would follow with a menu and place setting.  I chose the dining area over the bar which was surprisingly full at lunch time.  I was greeted by my waitress and after getting my beverage, she took my order for the Flamme Burger and an upgraded fry option, the Truffle Parmesan Fries.  Although they offer a number of dips and aiolis for the fries, I chose not to add any since I wasn't sure what would go with the upgrade I selected.  While waiting, the servers came around to all the tables and passed out fresh baked chocolate chip cookies!  Not sure why since I didn't see them on the menu, but it was a nice surprise while waiting for my meal.    Before long, the burger came out first and then the fries a couple minutes later. Not that big a deal since I was by myself, but not what I would normally expect at a restaurant.  The burger came on my choice of bun (whole grain for me) and was served with a steak knife to facilitate cutting it in half.  I ordered the burger medium per the recommendation of the hostess.  The burger (I'm guessing 6 oz) was a bit pink in the middle, but did have a good char on the outside from the cooking over flam(m)e, so it was moist/juicy but had that nice grilled flavor.  The burger came with a gruyere cheese and applewood bacon, and also was topped with serrano peppers and "flamme sauce" which is like a siracha mayo (I think).  So, with the multi layered flavor, there was a steady build up of spicy heat.  I didn't think it got too hot, but it was definitely noticeable.  Very tasty!  The fries were very plentiful and served in a paper lined metal basket.  I could see the bits of parmesan sprinkled generously over the fries throughout the mix, not just on the top.  However, the fries were a bit on the wilted/soggy side.  Maybe they didn't let the truffle oil get quite hot enough to give a crispness to the fries, but for some reason, the texture was a bit disappointing.  The flavor was very nice and I didn't think I needed any sauce.  Note that if you eat fries with your fingers, you will probably get parmesan bits on your finger tips, so be aware of that so you don't accidentally touch your clothes.  The service was friendly and thorough, with refreshed water and check processing as well.  Overall, a fine meal that was different from most burger places and tasty enough to warrant the premium burger prices.  I would gladly return if I was in the area.  Review #2185

This large shop has a variety of sections including a canned goods grocery, home decor, and a seasonal holiday section.  The place was crowded with shoppers and the aisles got a little congested, but most were plowing through the Christmas stuff.  The rest of the shop seemed pretty easy to get around.    They don't carry the high end brands, but the items are serviceable.  So, there can be some savings if you are willing to take the time to work your way through.  Review #1932

Good food and friendly service make for an enjoyable meal.  If you are downtown, the easiest way to get here is to head east on New York St and once you go under the I-65/I-70 overpass, cross the railroad tracks and take the first side street (Dorman) north.  Street parking is available along Dorman, but be aware as you step out since there is some rough stone alongside the street.  As you approach, you will see signs for Hoagies and Hops as well as Flat 12 Bierwerks.  They share the common entrance and for first timers, this can be confusing.  As you step inside, the bathrooms are on your left, the bar entrance is on your right, and in front of you are a bunch of people standing around in front of a makeshift counter.  Behind the counter is a list of beers.  It isn't until you walk in a bit further that you see the counter for Hoagies and Hops on the far left.  There are a few items listed on chalk boards, but if you want the full menu, you need to grab a paper menu from the counter.  You eventually realize that the counter at the back of the room is for filling growlers of beer.  The people standing around are either waiting for their turn to get their growlers filled or waiting for the their food order to be prepared.   So, if no one is at the counter, it is okay to step up and wait for the staff to ask you what you want.  They have the same folks make the food as take your order. So, you may have a slight delay while they get a sandwich wrapped or some sides put together before they will approach to take your order.    The staff was very friendly, but very busy when I went on a Saturday for lunch.  Because I ordered a number of side items, they said they would help me carry them to my table.  Understand that there are only two tables in the common area, so I grabbed a spot in the Flat 12 bar.  (There is additional outdoor seating at the bar.)  The sandwiches come in 9 and 18 inch sizes (half size sandwiches are available between 3 and 5 for only $5!)  The bread is delicious, somewhat soft and doughy in texture, but sturdy enough to hold up to the ingredients.  I chose the "Dutch Country" made with Seltzer's Lebanon Bologna, Muenster cheese, a local spicy mustard, lettuce and tomato.  This type of deli meat reminds me of a salami more than generic bologna:  darker color with bits of spice and fat and a strong pepper taste.  The flavors worked well together.    I tried a number of the side dishes as well.  The house slaw was a light and sweet style (about a half cup for $2).  The Peppadew Pepper Shooters (2 per order) are sweet & spicy and stuffed with provolone and prosciutto ($1).  The Red Beet Pickled Eggs (2 per order) are hard boiled eggs that are peeled and soaked in the juice of pickled beets and turn the egg whites to a purplish pink color (the yolks remain bright yellow).  I've been eating these for over 50 years and love the flavor.  (For fun if you are drinking:  Try fitting one whole egg in each cheek without damaging the egg!  You will look like a chipmunk!)  And "Pat's Philly Pretzel" is a chewy pretzel with really good flavor.  It also comes with the choice of a beer cheese or the local spicy mustard.  I went for the mustard option.  Although the flavor was good, the mustard is a bit granular and doesn't coat the pretzel like a cheese would.  Overall, I enjoyed the meal and having the extra seating next door in the bar makes it convenient to grab a brew to go with the food.  I think there could be some improvement made on the communication side, especially for first timers.  A sign could be hung from the ceiling with an arrow pointing towards the deli would help.  A sign with "Take One" or "Menus" would be more noticeable than having them flat on the counter.  A sign "Place food order here" could also be useful and eliminate the negativity of some reviews.  I would definitely try some of their other sandwich options if I was downtown or wanted to host a catered party.  Review #144

What a great time I had at lunch today.  The staff was friendly, the beer was good, and the food was great!  For those who remember the look of the place as its previous business, you won't believe what they've done inside (already) and outside (what is coming this fall!)  After grabbing a spot in the parking lot behind the building, I noticed all kinds of construction taking place just north of the lot.  Seems they are building a beer garden (may be 2 stories tall!) and their own smoke house.  They have the people to manage that part of the menu with a little help from some of the finer local meat producers (Smoking Goose/Turchettis).  I heard they are targeting having both the beer garden and smokehouse ready for Oktoberfest.  Sounds like a reason to visit again!  Inside, what was once drab gray walls and a huge vacant looking space has been partitioned with colorful walls dividing the main dining room from a private party area.  The dining area is open to the bar area which is still in the same place on the west end of the building.  Lots of splashes of color and German images on the shelves and walls.  I grabbed a spot at the bar looked over the menu.  They have a variety of German influenced foods and some beer brewed in house (you can see the equipment through glass walls on the north side of the room.)  Although they don't offer flights yet, they are generous with allowing samples of their house and seasonal beers.  I went for the Kitt, a Hefeweizen (4.8% abv) in a half liter glass mug.  You could get a good workout doing curls of those!  They also have full liter mugs ($11) available which you may want a straw to avoid having to lift! ha!  I started my lunch with a Tomato, Peach, & Cucumber salad that was as tasty as it was to look at.  Bits of chiffonade mint, pickled onion, Feta cheese and a dressing based on the Hefeweizen contribute just the right balance to the taste.  I also went for the Bratwurst which has beer braised onions & sauerkraut, fried shallots, gherkin (diced), and mustard creme fraiche on a pretzel bun.  The brat was bigger in the bun so I was able to taste the brat unadorned.  Very nice!  Then adding all the other flavors was even better.  I got my choice of sides and highly recommend the Spaetzle mac 'n cheese.  Not the typical mac and cheese that is bland or one dimensional.  This had a savory quality as well as the creamy cheese taste.  Best of both worlds.  If you were a fan of The Vanguard, I understand that a lot of that staff has migrated to Liter House.  There was a definite teamwork evident even though this was opening week.  For instance, the bartender was swamped with orders from the staff on the floor, so it would have been easy for those dining at the bar to be neglected.  But, other staff made sure to keep things flowing by bringing out my order, clearing my finished plates, bringing silverware, etc.  Teamwork cannot be ignored in running a great food/beverage place.  They are off to a great start.  I really enjoyed dining and had conversations with a couple other folks at the bar.  Everyone was excited about the place and seemed to enjoy it as much as I did.  Looks like I will be returning for Oktoberfest  Review #1113

If you are looking for:  an elegant restaurant suitable for a special occasion without feeling stuffy; some food that is based on authentic coastal Italian cuisine; desserts that are as delicious as they are masterfully created; then Nesso is the place to go!  For fans of Vida, know that several key staff have come over to Nesso to help launch it off to a good start.  And though they have only been open a week, our group could tell how close to detail the serving staff (Thanks Brandon D!) was focused on making our evening special.  And Chef Hattie's desserts are fantastic!  To be honest, I had little experience with Coastal Italian Cuisine.  No spaghetti and meatballs here!  Instead, the meal is intended to be eaten in several small courses including Pane (Bread), Crudo (raw seafood), Antipasti (salads/veggies), Primi (pasta course), Secondi (entree), and Dolci (dessert.)  You can pick and choose which courses you wish (or all of them like I did!)  They are developing a Chef's Menu, but it was not ready at the time of our visit.  Because there are so many courses available, no single course is expected to be filling.  (This isn't a place to judge a meal by how much it fills you, but by the quality of the flavor.)  One of the standout dishes that our group enjoyed was the Primi  course - Tortelloni which are large pasta stuffed with ricotta and served with pumpkin, amaretti, speck (tasty cubes of meat), apple jam, and spiced mascarpone.    Two of our group ordered the Secondi course - Branzino sea bass, with chile, tomato, olive oil, herb, basil aioli, fennel, and lemon.  The dish comes with potato verdura (a spicy hot side dish).  My wife isn't a fan of spicy heat, but wanted the fish, so they arranged for the broccolini with shallots instead.  Both visitors loved the fish which is served without the head, bones and scales, but comes with the tail and skin on.  The skin gets seared to a crispy and tasty finish which my wife said made the dish!  First time she's eaten the skin on a fish and she raved about it!  We also tried three of the Dolci course and though all were good, our clear favorite was the Tartufo di Cioccolato - dark chocolate mousse, caramel creameux, caramelized hazelnut butter, malted mousseline, and gold leaf.  Check out my photo to see how beautiful this dessert was.  And it tasted even better.  And if you are a fan of Vida's ricotta donuts, Nesso takes them up a notch and makes them into a Tiramisu!  Yum!  The interior of the restaurant is also amazing.  It looks very chic, but comfortable.  The west dining area is separated from the bar and main dining room, so it is great for carrying on conversations.  The seating is comfortable, but because some of the tables are couches or bench style, there is the chance for an occasional bump from a waiter trying to reach the table.  I felt sorry for the guy filling water glasses since he had to avoid spilling it on anyone while trying his best to reach everyone's glass. (We just passed them down to the end to avoid a problem.)  I look forward to trying some of the other dishes and am anxious to see what other dishes eventually rotate in as the cuisine moves around the coast of Italy to highlight different flavors.  (I hear truffles are coming in February!)  If you like trying something new, this is a restaurant to try.  I recommend looking at the menu online before coming so that you can check out the ingredients and look them up if you are uncertain.  Our server was glad to answer any questions about the ingredients as well.  Reservations are recommended since they have had several nights of having to turn away walk ups due to customer volume.  Don't miss out on this experience!  Review #1345

In the outdoor shoppes area of Greenwood Park Mall (northwest side of the building), a spacious restaurant is visible from the south (next to the Cheesecake Factory, but on the opposite side of the spur).  Kumo specializes in both Hibachi style food and sushi.  During my lunch visit, I didn't see any "performances" by the chefs though there were some folks sitting at one of the squared dining areas.  I was dining alone and was simply seated at a standard table (2 small tables nestled together).  At the entrance, there is a hostess stand and a bar area on the left.  The right is the dining area that has a sushi kitchen visible along the wall and additional dining rooms beyond that.    I decided to start with a cup of Miso Soup.  The soup had tofu and seaweed and a little bit of salty taste.  Overall, pretty good for Miso.  My next three items arrived in rapid order so that my table filled fast!  My Beef Negimaki was my favorite of the dishes I ordered.  Sliced beef with scallions served rolled like sushi pieces set in Teriyaki sauce equals YUM!  If you have a friend who isn't a sushi fan, this is something they might enjoy.  Before I got more than one of the rolls eaten, my Nigiri sampler and my Eel Avocado Roll arrived.  The sampler had five different pieces selected by the sushi chef:  shrimp, a white fish, white tuna, a red fish, and salmon.  I was surprised that I wasn't provided a bowl for dipping soy sauce.  I decided not to bother with it because I wanted to taste the fish.  Most were quite good, but the white fish had a bit of a stronger taste that wasn't too appealing.  The shrimp and salmon were my favorites.  The Eel Avocado roll was a six piece roll that was topped with eel sauce.  Nice flavor combo and the avocado was very soft and creamy in texture.  It wasn't as elaborate as some of the Dragon Rolls I have ordered with very similar ingredients, but this was just more than half the cost of the Dragon Roll offered here (and a smaller portion since I was trying all those other items.)  Service was prompt and cheerful.  The kitchens made my order quickly which made my wait time minimal.    It was an expensive lunch ordering all those items, but it gave me a sampling of the different options they offer.  Based upon my visit, I would gladly return and recommend it.  Review #2580
