I've been following this place on social media ever since bookmarking them on Yelp.  But because I live outside Indy, my schedule never had me in the right part of town on the right date.  Fortunately, I had the opportunity to catch up with them at a Milkshake IPA party at Guggman Haus where BBBq was providing the food.  So glad I did!  The folks in the truck were cranking out the sandwiches quickly.  I ordered the Chopped Brisket and the Ric Flair Sandwich.  The sandwiches aren't cheap, but they don't taste cheap either.  The brisket was not shredded, but somehow the large chunks of juicy (with a hint of char) beef mostly stayed inside the bun.  The flavor?  Excellent.  They also have four kinds of BBQ sauce to add (a hot sauce, a sweet, a Carolina mustard, and a mango.)  The meat has a lot of flavor on its own, but dialing it in with the sauces can really take it to another level.  The Ric Flair was a pulled pork sandwich topped with a creamy, yet tangy coleslaw and sliced pickles.  I have to admit that this one is messy.  The thickly loaded sandwich is challenging to keep together and you may end up wearing a bit if you aren't careful.  But the flavor?  Again, it was delicious.  Be sure to grab lots of napkins and possibly a fork because I am certain there will be some tasty bits that spill out onto the paper tray the sandwich is served in.  Excellent food.  Friendly and quick service.  And I found out that they are getting close to opening their brick and mortar store in Washington Square Mall in the Fall of 2019.  They will be on the northwest side of the mall building.  I am glad I finally found a time and location for meeting up with this food truck.  I am looking forward to the new stationary spot to open.  Review #2901

I hadn't been to Canterbury Park for about ten years, but it has been maintained well.  I like that it has restrooms and a water fountain (great place to know about if you are running the Monon Trail next to the park!) There are swings and climbing & sliding equipment for the kids.  There is shade, a volleyball court (no equipment, just a location), and a shelter with picnic tables and a grill.  Considering the size of the place, it has enough to make it useful and fun without feeling crowded.  Review #594

I love that Carmel has set aside so much land on 116th Street, especially on the west side of town, as large parks.  Less than a half mile from the 125 acre Coxhall Gardens, this 121 acre park offers lots of natural habitats in the outlying areas of the park.  Yet near the entrance, there are lots of activities for little ones in the splash park and playground.  One of the eye-catching attributes is the large hill in the middle of the park.  On the south side facing the parking lot, a paved path zigzags across the face of the hill to gradually lead you to the top (It's a nice alternative to having to run up the steep slope!)  Once on top, you can see how the park is divided roughly into quadrants.  The south east is open field which lies beyond the playground and shelter area by the entrance.  The north east side is mostly wooded.  The north west side is a prairie meadow area that is left pretty natural, but does have a trail that goes by it.  The south west side is where the pond and marsh area is located.  Most of the state's natural marsh land has disappeared, so it is great that this area has been designated for that purpose.  To reduce disturbance, an elevated boardwalk allows for nice strolls and some fishing in that section, but far enough from the marsh to avoid problems.  In between the marsh and prairie areas, there are three shelters for those who like to reserve those for events.  They are smaller than the larger shelter by the playground which also has the bathrooms and water fountains.    The park is easy to find and was well maintained.  I can see the park being a destination for sledding on snowy days and the long trail around the park would be great location for exercising yourself or you dog.  With all the demands for prime real estate in the area, I hope the park stays intact for a very long time.  It truly is an asset to the community!  Review #744

My wife has become a fabulous quilter and when she heard about Crimson Tate, I thought it worth a road trip...check out the store and maybe grab lunch from one of the myriad of Mass Ave restaurants!  I've learned a little but am not a quilter myself.  The store, while small and having to deal with the angle shape of the building, was comfortable to get around for the amount of customers.  Note that this place specializes in quilts.  They don't have all the sewing and home decoration accessories of the big franchises.  But they do have a nice collection of quilting supplies including fabrics, bundles of quarters/squares, and some patterns.  Tastefully decorated, they even have some quilts mounted on the walls that you can get all the materials in the store.    The staff was very friendly and knowledgeable about the fabrics, designers, and sources.  For items they did not carry in house, they were able to suggest websites of designers or fabric stores that have high quality to satisfy the customer's needs.  Maybe they didn't have every item my wife was looking for, but she was able to get quite a few items for her next two projects and the positive experience made us both feel welcome.  It's nice when a business gets a good reputation for service!  Review #372

This was my first time at this theater and I had a very pleasant experience.  The lobby and parking lot were clean.  The cashier at the counter was pleasant and knowledgeable about the offerings.  And the theater had good sound and comfy seating.  Not too hot or cold either.  Overall, a pleasant experience for $7.50 matinee.  Review #2908

I stopped by early on a Saturday afternoon during their opening week.  There was some free street parking not too far away available even though there was a street festival going on that kept me from grabbing a spot out front.  The brewery has a pretty small seating area on the left as you enter and the order counter/bar is on the right.  I was carded (even though I'm nearing 60) as was everyone who came in the door.    The brewery had five varieties of house beers to offer:  a Blonde, IPA, Hefeweizen, Pale Ale, and a Brown Porter.  I was curious if they had a flight and they will, but their flight boards hadn't arrived yet.  (They will offer flights of four small beers in another week or two.)  So, I got a sample of the Hefe and the Blonde.  Both were good, but neither had that "Wow" factor...probably because of the type of beer they are.  They offer beers by the pint or growler, so I went with the Hefe.  It had a semi cloudy appearance like a Hefe should, but didn't have as much banana and clove flavor as I've had elsewhere.  I love that flavor combo and always feel a little disappointment when the flavors are a bit muted.  Oh, well, that's just personal preference.  The beer was still enjoyable.  The bartender was one of the owners of another brewery who was friends with the Beech Bank owners and was helping cover the shifts.  Very friendly and informative about hops and beer brewing in general and made the time fly by.  I appreciate learning about the behind the scenes activity from someone who does it for a living.  Overall, a nice brewery, but could use a bit of pizzazz in the seating room.  There was a single television (muted), but otherwise, not much atmosphere.  They do offer some bar snacks like pretzels and chex mix, but otherwise, no food is on the menu.  Review #1336

On a rainy Monday morning, I headed into North End BBQ for lunch.  Fortunately, there is plenty of parking right outside the entrance since this restaurant is located in an out lot of the Target store on 86th in Nora.  I was greeted promptly and given a seat at a table in the nicely decorated bar.  The bartender also came right over and took my beverage order while I looked over the menu.  It wasn't long before I had my beverage and he took my order.    Within a very short time period, a tray lined with brown paper was brought from the kitchen.  Upon it, were my entree and three sides (two normally come with the entree, but due to good reviews, I thought I would go for a third.)  My entree was the Carolina Pulled Pork.  The smoked and partially shredded (plenty of large bites were left intact!) pork came without bread, but did have a small serving plate that was perfect for sampling the four sauces that were also brought out.  Of the four sauces, my personal favorite was the Carolina Gold - a sweet and tangy mustard sauce that was fantastic!  I also sampled the Classic (sweet tomato flavors), KC Style (Very sweet molasses and brown sugar flavors), and Texas Red (combo of sweet and acid/vinegar flavors).  For my sides, I selected the Fries, Collard Greens, and the Mac & Cheese.  As good as the pork was, each of the sides was a near miss for me.  The crispy fries came with smoked bone marrow butter drizzled over them and thinly sliced fresh jalapenos.  I am not a big raw pepper fan, so I didn't really enjoy the combo.  However, when I ate the fries without the pepper, they became a little bland, so I ended up adding some table salt and they were fine.  The Collard Greens were cooked perfectly, but I was two thirds of the way through the serving before I found any bacon.  Frankly, the bacon just lacked the punch of the ham I am used to when ordering collards.  The Mac & Cheese was a creamy combo and had a nice light flavor.  I wasn't a big fan of the rib jam on top.  For my tastes, just a few small tweaks could have made this a five star review.  Review #102

Although I haven't purchased any pianos or instruments here, I have been to their showroom and have attended two concerts in the performance hall.  Such was the case for my most recent visit.  After browsing through their rows of grands and uprights, I entered the large room to listen to the performances of a pair of pianists that were brought in by the business to entertain.  The pair alternated in short sets and really displayed the range of sounds and emotions that an artist can extract from the equipment.  It really makes a difference when someone that talented plays an instrument that you might be considering.  I did notice that for the performance, nobody from the business made a point of introducing the artists.  They had to introduce themselves which seem like an oversight.  If they are going to continue providing concerts, surely someone could be available to do the introductions.  If you are interested in purchasing a piano or guitar, there is a large selection here and the arrangement of them seems conducive to "test driving" them before you purchase.  They also offer lessons and additional accessories to enhance your skill and enjoyment of the purchase.  Review #2498

5 Star as good as it gets...that pretty much describes a perfect evening of dining at Tinker Street with our friend.  This was the fifth time my wife and I have dined here (this time on an early Thursday night).  We brought a friend along for her second visit since she enjoyed it so much the first time we brought her.  Since we arrived just as they opened, we were able to grab one of the parking lot spots on the north side of the building.  Although we thought we might want to sit outside on the patio, it was still too hot and we were able to move to one of the limited number of tables inside the building.  We started off with our complimentary sparkling wine to cleanse our palates.  After bringing our beverages, we placed an order for a couple of the small plates.  The Steam Buns were filled with local mushrooms, hoisin, some zippy kimchi'd pickles (a nice kick of heat!), and sesame.  Very nice texture and flavors.  The second small plate was the Di Stefano Burrata soft cheese with arugula, sweet tomato jam, and EVOO along with several slices of crunchy artisan bread to spread it on.  Anyone who has read my profile knows that burrata and tomatoes are my current crush, so I was savoring every bite.  After a slight delay, my "Botanical" course was served:  Blistered "My Dad's Sweet Corn" had three 4 inch ears of corn skewered and slightly blistered from roasting served on a bed of summer greens with ranch dressing drizzled over the top.  I had fresh cracked pepper added to my portion.  Excellent flavors....the corn was especially sweet which was offset by the savoriness of the dressing and the roasted flavors.  Another perfect dish!  For entrees, my wife and our friend both got the Seared Beef with sweet corn succotash (with zucchini instead of lima beans), cherry tomato, and a house steak sauce.  I was able to get a bite of both the succotash (this was the best I have ever tasted!) and one of the beef.  Because the ladies were raving about the steak sauce, I decided to go ahead and try it even though I prefer my steak without sauce.  I have to admit there was a zing to the sauce when I took my bite which was then followed by the savory beef flavor.  I love combination flavors!  My entree was the Wild Sockeye salmon with haricot verts, marble potatoes, and blueberry BBQ sauce.  I was a bit surprised that the vegetables were cooked, but cooled to room temperature before serving.  I wasn't aware that they would be served cool, so my first reaction was that maybe it was a mistake, but the flavor was still delicious, so I went ahead and finished my plate.    For dessert, the ladies split a wonderful Banana Cream Pie served in a shell of vanilla wafer crumble with whipped cream, fresh banana, and banana brulee.  I didn't get a bite! :(  I did get my own Cornmeal Hoecakes with local fruits, sorghum butter and hickory syrup that was mighty tasty as well.  The service was exceptional throughout the evening.  A real team spirit exists as the army of staff is always watching for empty plates, used silverware, and water glasses that need topping off.  For anyone who has experienced this level of service, it makes the evening special.  The great food and service show why this was rated one of the top 5 restaurants in Indy by Indpls Monthly Magazine.  Bonus:  One of the owners of Tinker Street stopped by and spent about 20 minutes with us as we ate our desserts.  We were able to ask all kinds of questions about the business and the two new restaurants he will be opening within the next year on 16th Street.  It is easy to see why the employees enjoy working here when the owners are committed to providing the best for the customers with the appreciation for all the staff does.  Review #86

I decided to stop by Best Buy since I had been having some audio problems with my computer's sound system.  I was pretty sure it I had a short in my old system, so I started browsing the options inside the computer section of the store.  Before long, one of the "blue shirts" asked if I was doing okay or needed any assistance.    Long story short:  He answered all my questions, even demonstrated the sound quality I could get from the system, and then answered some more questions about another item.  When done, he made sure I knew to ask any of the blue shirts if I had any more questions.    This is the third Best Buy I've been to in a month and each one has done a much better job of being customer friendly than I had remembered from years passed.  Yes, they still offer a "buyer's insurance" warranty on almost everything, but I don't have a problem of saying no on the lower end items that are more disposable.  The new system was easy to install and the sound is really good.  No more short!    Review #3698

What a fun night filled with great service and delicious food!  My wife and I took our frequent dining friends out to dinner early on a Thursday evening.  I had grabbed some street parking near this corner restaurant rather than using the valet service or paying the $8 for 3 hours at the parking garage north of the restaurant on Pennsylvania.  We were greeted by the bartender (Chris) who was very friendly and took us to our seating outside.  We were quickly greeted by our excellent server (Ben T) who treated us like royalty.  Although the restaurant is upscale and has appropriate pricing, the staff was dressed more casually which will probably suit the clientele that start frequenting the place once the Pacers start their season.  Although we got dressed up, there wasn't any indication that all guests should be.  We started off with our beverages.  My friend and I tried the "French 48" cocktail ($6) which was a sparkling (Prosecco) gin and lemon drink.    Before long, we ordered the Aunt Donna's Meatballs (4 pc) since my friend isn't a seafood fan and the Crab Beignets (5 pc).  The meatballs were large, moist, and served in a red sauce.  The beignets were also large, had a light crispy shell filled with Boursin cheese and lump crab with a white remoulade and a five pepper jelly.  Yum!!!  As we started getting chilly, we asked to move inside and were quickly accommodated before our entrees arrived.  The ladies started off with bowls of Clam Chowder.  These were really large (probably 2 cups or more!) and were quite filling.  Lots of clam and potatoes with a hearty soup that had a bit of sweetness.  Both were clean "platers"!  Chower comes with corn bread on the side.  My friend's wife and I both selected the Divers Scallops.  She got them with Oscar Lobster, I went with Oscar Crab.  We both loved our dinners.  We each got four mid-size to large pan seared scallops with truffle risotto and grilled asparagus.  So good!  My wife, who was getting full, ordered the Captain Tso's salmon with white rice and broccoli.  Again, another fine meal.  My non-seafood friend ordered the 12 oz New York Strip rare (though it was probably medium-rare when served.)  It had a deep char that he thought was delicious!  It comes a la carte, so he also ordered grilled asparagus which were huge and numerous.  We finished off the evening sampling three of the desserts:  Kylie's Cheesecake, bread pudding with praline sauce, and Toll House Pie with vanilla ice cream.  We all liked our choices.  (I think my wife actually preferred her friend's bread pudding over her own Toll House Pie.)  At the time of my writing, there have been some really low ratings dragging down the overall average.  We thought Ben brought just the right amount of upbeat spirit to his professional way of attending customers.  If you are concerned at all about the negative reviews, simply make reservations and ask for Ben.  He will make it his mission to make sure you get your money's worth!  Great job!  This isn't a cheap night out, but it can be one that is memorable.  We all left well fed, in good spirits, and thinking we will be back again.  Review #3161

I've been a fan of Vida since my first visit, and even though they have made a few changes to the way the menu works, I still give it five stars after my fifth visit!     My wife and I invited fellow Yelper's Kim G and David G to meet us for dinner recently, their first visit.  Fortunately for us, they like to ask questions and order different items from the menu and are willing to share samples so that we could get an idea of what we might be missing.  I am pretty sure they enjoyed it as much as we did.   The change I mentioned in my opening statement is that instead of offering a preset five course meal for $65 (with an optional wine pairing for an additional $40), they now offer a four-course meal for the same price.  The benefit is that now you can build your own menu, selecting one item from each of the courses listed.  You still have the option to select ala carte menu items if you want slightly larger portions, but I believe most people will find eating from four courses is quite filling enough.   The setting and the service are still at the top of the chart for people who want to be able to carry on conversation while dining.  There is just enough buzz to keep it from feeling stodgy, but the high ceilings, the slatted panels, and the carpeted flooring dampen that noise that makes some upscale restaurants unpleasant.  It also helps that the bar is separated from the main dining hall by the reception area between buildings.   Many of the items on the menu may have components that are unfamiliar to you.  I have found that by simply asking for clarification, the staff is willing to help you understand what to expect.  About the only thing they can't explain is how fantastic the food tastes!  Trust me that this is one of those places that you can't help but feel like you are in for a special evening. Note that I seldom go out in large groups so I can't say how that experience would be, but this place is perfect for couples and small groups who are willing to trust the chefs have designed courses that are deliciously paired.   I am already looking forward to my next visit!  Rev #21

Although there are a few growing pains that are being addressed, this place has the potential to be a five star addition to the neighborhood as well as the Indy beer scene.  I have been to the original Scarlet Lane in McCordsville only once, so having their beverages available only half the distance from my home is a plus!  I usually order flights when I visit breweries (or their extensions) to get a better idea of what they have to offer.  So on this occasion, I went with four 5-ounce pours.  I started with an Australian IPA the Asteria (4.9% 40 IBU).  It was different than I expected due to the type of hops which make it an Australian.  Not bad, but not quite what I was expecting.  I then moved onto the Katrina.  Wow!  This beer was like eating a liquid snickerdoodle cookie!  So much cinnamon and brown sugar that I could see warming this one up and sipping it around a firepit!  (6.6%, 15)  I moved onto the Dorian Espresso Stout (5.5%, 42).  I like beer.  I like coffee.  This was a happy blending of the two!  And I boldly decided to slay the remainder of my thirst with the Eirik Bloodaxe (11%, 100 IBU!)  What a beverage!  I am not normally a hopster, but the perfect blend of hops with all the other robust flavors made this a winner!  I will definitely have more of that one!  Since I went on a Friday just after lunch time, I had time to chat with the manager (who will also be managing the BR extension when it opens in a month or so).  I learned about the brewing industry and how most of the local breweries get along with each other, viewing it not so much as competition, but as a community of folks to help improve each other's product.  It was a fun way to pass the time while I sipped my flight.  The space is currently being finished out.  A new sign for out front was expected soon and the mural artist was still adding some colorful imagery to an otherwise understated atmosphere.  A really tight angle to get into the parking lot will soon be remedied when a nearby dilapidated building will be torn down and converted to a parking lot.  Looks like this bold adventure to bring a high quality beverage to the old southside should be a hit!  Review #1656

Has it really been that long since I last stopped by here?  Man, does time fly.  Anyway, I was downtown and decided to stop in again.  Glad I did!    It was lunch and the tavern was about half full.  It looks like it is still arranged the way I remembered it: main floor as you enter (dining) and the bar a couple steps up on the left.  There wasn't a sign about seating, so I went up into the bar and after a couple minutes, was able to get the bartenders attention.  I headed back to a table in the dining area and was greeted promptly by my waitress who had been busy ringing out some orders.  The service was good the rest of the way (maybe they need a bell or buzzer to let them know customers have arrived.)  I ordered the Chicken Wrap Ranch (I got the grilled chicken, not the crispy) which comes in a flour tortilla with pepperjack, tomato, and lettuce with the ranch on the side.  I also selected cole slaw as my side.  The food was brought out reasonably quick.  The wrap was not oversized...actually it was just right for a lunch size meal.  The chicken was moist and tender and had a nice grilled flavor.  The rest of the ingredients seemed fresh and all worked well together.  The cole slaw was not the creamy kind, so there was plenty of crunch and nice blend of sweet/vinegary taste.  Very good!  Note to self:  Don't wait so long between visits.  Review #577

My wife and I really enjoy dining at Bosphorus Cafe.  For a number of years, Orhan Demirtas has been bringing authentic Turkish food to Indianapolis.  We definitely have favorite items that we like to order.  For me, the Shrimp Mediterranean is my go to dish (Sauteed with tomato sauce, green peppers, tomatoes, onions, and potatoes).  I love the flavor combinations and the sides of a small salad and rice are perfect.  The rice helps to soak up every last bit of flavor on the plate.   For my wife, she loves to order the Shepherd Salad (Tomatoes, parsley, cucumbers, and onions tossed with olive oil).  These aren't your typical lettuce based salads....these are collections of vegetables that are as colorful as they are flavorful.  (Our friend likes to get the Navy Bean Salad and highly recommends it as well.)  Fortunately for us, most of the popular items stay on the menu instead of disappearing.   We also love the decoration of Turkish culture....take time to notice the decorative painting and wall art.  On the negative, the building itself needs some work. The floor sags and could benefit from some floor jacks.  This causes some of the tables to not be quite level. The main floor is also elevated from the street, so access might be restrictive for those wheelchair bound.  Occasionally, I have had the wrong shrimp dinner brought out.  I understand that some of the dishes are very similar in appearance, but feel the staff should be able to keep them straight.  However, there wasn't a long delay in replacing the dish.  If you are new to Mediterranean food, this is a great place to start.  We really enjoy bringing friends here and seeing them become fans of the restaurant too.  Review #48

Now that I'm retired, I don't wear as much high end clothing as I did.  So, I mainly shop here when my wife is looking for something.  I like the direction the stores are taking with emphasis on customer service.  My wife was greeted and ended up making a purchase in record time.  I also like the atmosphere in the store.  During the holidays, the pianist was playing holiday music near the escalator, surrounded by a Christmas tree and lots of decorations.  It seemed more festive than the other stores.  Sure, the pricing is higher than most of the other mall stores, but that is pretty well known by the shoppers who are looking for that something special.  There also seems to be plenty of room to move around in the store and enough staff to handle the daily shopping customers.  Review #1905

Wow!  If you are hungry on Virginia Avenue, here is a place for you!  There is a lunch buffet for $11 that gives you access to the salad bar, a beverage, and the pizza bar that has multiple types of pizza and a baked dish.  The baked dish on my visit was a Mastaccioli Pasta and Sausage mix.  Okay, parking is a challenge as it is for nearly ever spot along Virginia Avenue due to turn restrictions and narrow streets, but if you can find a spot near here, just count yourself lucky.  There is a small parking area behind the building off Stevens Street (one way east bound) around the former Cafe Nonna.  Inside, there is a small dining area in front of the order counter and another larger dining area to the right where the salad bar, beverage dispenser, and pizza buffet are located.    Simply place your order at the counter (I just said "buffet") and pay. Then you help yourself by grabbing one of the plates along the buffet table.  I am not aware how they interact with you if you order a sandwich or special order a pizza.  But they will bring it out to you.  The salad bar has a wide variety of toppings to go with your choice of iceberg lettuce and spinach.  There were five bottled dressings as well.  The buffet had at least five flavor combos for your choice of pizza.  I went with a slice of thin crust with onion, spinach, and fresh tomato that had a real cheesy flavor.  I also grabbed a humongous deep dish sausage and bacon slice that was over an inch thick and the end of the crust nearly two!  The cashier also brought out a marinara and a cheese dipping sauce for the crust.  Yeah!    The pizzas had good flavor, but they do sit under heat lamps, so that does affect the texture a bit.  The thin crust got a little steamed so it lost any crispness it may have had when first brought out.  The thick crust seemed to hold up better under the conditions.  Overall, the flavors were fine and with so many options, including the baked dish along side the pizza, I don't think too many folks would have difficulty finding something tasty to eat.  A solid addition to the neighborhood as an alternative to the fancier restaurants in the area.  Review #1654

Located just to the right once you enter Door 3 of the St Vincent's Hospital in Carmel, this little cafe has a nice variety of lunch and breakfast options.  The menu items are listed behind and above the counter, but printed menus are also available if you prefer reading things closer to your face.  You place your order on the right side and pay at the time you order.  They call out the food item, not your name, so you need to pay attention so that someone who comes after you doesn't grab your smoothie or panini by mistake!  We stopped by for lunch and didn't have to wait to order.  Within minutes, our orders were ready.  It was a little more challenging than when they call out names.  I mean if you miss the first word or two of what is being called, you may not recognize the order.  Fortunately, the place was only about half full and the cashier (very personable!) nodded at me like "Hey, that's yours!"    I ordered a Turkey Cranberry panini which was pretty tasty.  The turkey was served warm and juicy (for turkey).  The Swiss cheese was thick and gooey (yum!) and the cranberry flavor was from cranberry mayo with cranberry bits.  The panini was lightly grilled/pressed and was quite good.  I also ordered the Tropical Oasis smoothie, which is a bunch of fruit juices including strawberry, pineapple, and banana.  It was cold and refreshing, but like a lot of smoothies, you have to wait for the melting to catch up to your thirst.  By the bottom of the smoothie, the flavor was a little monotone compared to the taste at the beginning.  My wife opted for the Carnitas (pork) wrap.  She opted for the flour wrap (four options are available) to hold her marinated carnitas, black beans, corn salsa, avocado, salsa and sour cream.  As you can see, the food tastes on the lighter side, but is sufficient enough in quantity and flavor to satisfy someone on the go for lunch.  Overall, it was easy to figure out the process and the staff were friendly in the limited interaction.  They have a self serve soda fountain, and an accessory counter to the left of the main counter.  Once you finish, you are expected to buss your own table.    Review #458

Don't be fooled by the small storefront.  The mall not only has that space, but the building to the east which also has a basement to browse through.  There a many booths (though some are not clearly defined spaces) of items with a wide variety of items.  I saw a lot of dishes and because it is December, lots of holiday items for sale.  I wouldn't say that it was an antique mall so much as a mix of antiques and lots of collectible items that may have some age, but not the value that bargain hunters may be looking for.  The staff was friendly and helpful.  Review #1936

Whether you are looking for something new, something antique, or are simply thinking of doing something to make your dated furniture look newly antique, this is a place to check out.  The shop is on the southeast corner of Main and Pine on the south end of the Zionsville village.  It occupies two building spaces, so it does have a few steps inside the showroom, but it does have a ramp on the north end of the shop to allow access inside for those who have physical challenges.  There is a lot of space so it is easy to browse through the store and check out the numerous displays.  There are numerous groupings of furniture with accessories to complete the look.   There is also a large supply of milk paint mixes that you can purchase for those do it yourself projects.  They have classes where they teach you (about 3 hours in a block) to mix and prep, then paint your furniture (They give you something to practice on so that you don't have to lug your stuff in for the class.)  The staff was friendly and seemed happy to answer questions from the visitors.  My wife was thinking about signing up for a class once the weather got warmer.  Go to their website for more information.  Review #2210

I returned to Ember Urban Eatery for lunch (6-21-16) with a friend I used to work with.  We like to meet at Ember because it is easy to get to without driving through the downtown traffic and it has parking available in the lot next to the building as well as street parking.  All that is fine and convenient, but what keeps bringing me back is the Brisket Sandwich.  It is my favorite meal on the menu and is the best brisket I have had, bar none!  I don't know how anyone could complain about the quality of the brisket.  It is slow roasted and sliced into small pieces with just enough sauce to keep it moist.  Then add the Dijon mustard and the special BBQ slaw on top and you have a great blending of savory, sweet, and acidity.  It comes on a brioche bun and with your choice of sides.  Today, I opted for the Tomato Bisque.  I also ordered a Sun King Indian's Lager which tasted great with the sandwich.  I know there are some other tasty items on the menu (and I haven't even tried the desserts yet), but I keep getting drawn back to this sandwich.  My friends seem to order it too because I have raved about the flavor and they seem very pleased as well.  Another reason they get high marks is the friendly service.  Richard understood I was meeting a friend and that I wasn't sure if we were going to eat inside or outside in the shade.  He still gave me a menu to look over and brought me a glass of water and was fine with me taking my time.    They also have a rewards program for frequent customers, so if you are someone who can take advantage of the great sandwich, you can earn points toward a freebie!  Review #53

I was on the west side and decided to stop in for lunch at this restaurant, just north of Washington Street  on High School Road.  There is convenient parking in the lot and when I entered, there were plenty of booths and tables to choose from (the waitress directed to seat myself).  The lunch menu was pretty brief (just over a dozen options), but had a $6 offering of entrees with a cup of veggie Thom Yum soup and an egg roll (crispy veggie).  The soup was on the spicy side.  It had good flavor, but if you are sensitive to heat, then you may struggle.  I definitely felt the spice burn on the first sip.  The egg roll was thin and on the small side and didn't come with any dipping sauce.  Still, the flavor was pretty good on its own.  Being my first time at this Thai restaurant, I went with my default Pad Seuw entree, this time with chicken.  The noodles were the large and tender type that I like.  I especially liked that the broccoli was sliced into uniform thickness instead of being chunky.  The broccoli remained crisp and added a nice crunch to the meal to go with the tender noodles.  The chicken was also thin sliced and didn't seem to have any additional seasoning (a little bland).  The kale that was added to the meal became wilted (as expected) from the heat and didn't really add much but color to the overall entree.  I ordered a cup of Jasmine green tea which was served as a cup with a tea bag instead of as a small pot.  There was a slightly higher priced option which may have been that, but I didn't ask.  Silverware comes wrapped in paper napkins already on the tables.  The eating ware included a fork and tablespoon for the soup.  The entire dining area was covered by one waitress who also handled the cash register and carryout orders.  Although there were slight delays waiting on her check ins on me, she did a really good job of managing the floor.  I only hope that they have more help when the dining room gets more patrons.  Rev #380

There is a beautiful little shop on the south end of old town Zionsville that displays the art of (and is operated by) 24 artists, including local talent.  The art covers a wide range of mediums including paintings (all kinds), ceramics, fused glass, woodcraft, stained glass, jewelry, and textiles.  And the quality is amazing.  Sure, the prices will probably be higher than the mass produced stuff you find at the big box stores, but the quality is worth the price and in most cases, the pieces are hand made (there are some smaller prints of paintings in the $10-25 range).  The arrangements are done tastefully allowing each artist to display their works in a manner that you can quickly see what appeals to you.  With up to 24 artists contributing, you may want to allow some time to browse before picking anything up.  My wife was particularly interested in the fused glass of artist Deb Achgill and the ceramics of Chris Davis.  I liked the unique wood carvings of Bob Anderson and the numerous paintings throughout.  What ever your interest in art, you can find something here that is priced so that you may be able to leave with it.  I look forward to returning to see what new items are added.  Review #2208

I love the smell of a barbecue restaurant/catering service.  I get hungry just standing there trying to make up my mind what I want to try.  And when they offered a sample of the moist and tasty ham, I knew I was going to enjoy this.  The restaurant part of the business opened in 2019 after some remodeling to the Walker Egg's store allowed for some seating and the order counters to be approached while you shop.  They open at 11 a.m., so it was enough to draw me back since my first visit to the store was too early to place lunch order.  I went with a sampler which comes with 1/2 pound of meat and two sides for $10 (Brisket add $2).  I ordered the pulled pork and the cheddar mac and cheese and the State Fair green beans.  They have sauces that you help yourself to on the left end of the order counter (lids come with them!)  I picked out a sweet sauce and a Carolina (mustard) sauce.  The pork was shredded and juicy with a nice smoky flavor, but obviously, little seasoning.  So, the sauces really bring out the best.  I also decided to grab a half pound of the ham and of the brisket.  Both are sliced thick (about 1/2") instead of shredded.  I really liked the ham because I got a slice that was from the outside and had all the extra flavor from the exposed area.    The only disappointment was that the brisket was very dry.  It had a nice layer of fat which I thought would keep it more juicy, but by the time I got home (20 min), the meat was dry.  The sauce helped, but I hope they can dial in the roasting time so that I can enjoy the flavor.  Overall, they have a wide variety of meats to choose from and quite a few sides (served warm) to compliment the meal.  I will have to come back to try some of the other offerings.  Review #3322

Reading through the other reviews, it seems pretty clear that people only write reviews when they have had a bad experience.  The thousands of travelers who have no problems, or minimal, don't bother to write about it.  The airline did what it was supposed to do.  What's to write?  My wife made arrangements through American.  We had a connecting flight in Dallas that took us to our final destination.  We had a connecting flight through Phoenix on the way home.  Overall, we had a positive experience.    She had handled shopping around for the best deals that would get us to our hotels and when it was time to go, she used one of the kiosks and soon had our boarding passes.  We checked our luggage quickly too.    I think the only problems we had were due to a problem with the plane in Dallas.  They detected a problem and had to bring another plane instead.  I was fine since the new plane was 10 seats wide, had onboard charging stations, each seat had its own entertainment screen, and since we were flying to the middle of the Pacific Ocean, the plane was working properly.  So glad they didn't take a risk with our safety.  Sure, it costs us two hours in Hawaii, but I would rather be alive for the rest of the vacation than take a chance with an improperly working one.  Sure, the process of charging for every extra like baggage and full meals adds up quickly, it's the price we drove the airlines to by making the no-frills airlines so popular just to save a buck.  It's competition.  No sense complaining about it.  I don't take a lot of trips, so it is hard to say when I would use American next.  But based upon my most recent trip, I would have no trouble flying with them again.  Review #2390

This theater is a real benefit for the folks in Mooresville.  The recent upgrades in the sound systems and seating have made the movie going experience much better.  As a retiree, I really appreciate the low prices during the day.  The staff is courteous and I have rarely had to wait to purchase my tickets.  I also appreciate that they don't show endless trailers (I think they target about 8 minutes instead of 20 or more at other theaters.)  With the internet, I have usually seen most of the trailers before they appear in previews.  My only negative is that the daytime hours are limited to when school is out or when it is the weekend.  (I really appreciate the summer schedule.)  I understand that it isn't cost effective to be open most days, but it is something the "competition" offers.    I would also like to see more independent films shown in the small theater #8.  The southside doesn't have an arts theater, so I have to travel all the way to Keystone at the Crossing or wait until the movie is released to online services/dvd to see some films.    I plan on continuing to go to this local gem.  If you haven't been here recently, then treat yourself to a much improved experience.  Review #59

I saw reviews were starting to be posted for this new coffee house in Fountain Square, so I decided to stop in on a Saturday morning.  I parked in the free public lot just across Woodlawn and entered through the patio entrance.  (The main entrance is actually on Virginia Ave.)  There were about a half dozen customers standing back from the counter and I wasn't sure where the line started.  I asked one of them if she was in line and she directed me to the south end of the counter.  Turns out most of the folks were waiting on their orders to be called out.  The folks behind the counter weren't really directing people to the spot and there wasn't a sign that said "order here", but there was a register.  Still, it would help if the staff would occasionally say that anyone wanting to order should step down to that end.  I didn't see standard drip coffee, but they did have Americano available, so I went with that.  The staff were friendly, but I assumed they were generally quiet due to the constant stream of customers and trying to keep up.  The coffee did have a very nice flavor but was served piping hot.  What fooled me was that the to go cups they use are really well insulated, so it didn't feel that hot until it passed my lips.  Ouch!  So, no perfect score from me since coffee should be drinkable without pain or waiting ten minutes.  Beginning in a few days, they should have some pastry options available for those who want to grab a bite (they had sold out the limited amount they had started the day with.)  There are a few seats/tables in the main room and there is additional seating in the back room that has three steps leading up to it.  Very cool decor.   The patio also had plenty of additional seating and lights were strung overhead for those stopping by in the darker hours.  Overall, it was a good experience with generally friendly and helpful people and a good deal of beverage choices (hot and cold.)  Once they get some feedback, they ought to be able to dial in the experience for future customers.    I wish them good luck and I'll have to swing by to check out their pastries in the near future.  Review #3128

This was my first time at Christmas at the Zoo and came at the end of visiting about a half dozen other Christmas exhibits around Indy earlier in the day.  I really liked the Santa's Village area with so many activities for young and old.  I also liked that everywhere I went in the zoo seemed to have festive lights.  They also had a giant fireplace and fire pits for warming though parents really need to watch their kids around those.  You can expect to pay usual pricing for zoo entrance which also includes a steep parking fee ($8) for non-members.  So, I wasn't surprised by the cost.    The only negative is that if you are going to see the animals, you won't see too many.  Sure, the walrus, the penguins, and a tiger were moving about.  And you could see some of the indoor exhibits like the oceans, dolphins (at a set time based upon when you arrive), and the orangutans, but the Plains area was closed off and many of the animals were not out.  Even the bears were sleeping.  So, five stars for the lighting and festive activities (I really enjoyed the Snowflake Mirror Maze) but a 3 for being able to watch the animals.    Review #3425

I've read a lot of negative comments about this place, but I sat at the bar for lunch and had great food AND great service.  The bartender had a booming voice, so he was easy to understand over the background noise and he got every part of my order right the first time.  I started with a couple samples of wheat drafts (over 50 drafts are on tap!).  I made my choice and was promptly brought my Mashcraft Hefeweizen (5.3% with a nice balance of beer/banana/clove flavors.)  When I was ready to order lunch, he took my order and offered a glass of water to go with the meal in addition to the lunch.  (I accepted!)  There are a variety of appetizers and salads. They also have flat breads and sandwiches.  The French Dip caught my eye and I ordered a side of Jasmine Rice too.  There was a slightly longer than expected wait for the food to come out, but I saw a steady stream of food coming out of the kitchen, so I think it was just a case of bad timing.  The good news is that the food was worth it.  I think the flavor combination of the seasoned ribeye, caramelized onions, Swiss cheese, garlic aioli, and the porter infused au jus sauce was the best I have ever had!  The sandwich wasn't the largest or the cheapest I've had, simply the best flavor.  The toasted hoagie was just the right size, being able to soak up the au jus without falling apart or being so thick as to be unable to get the sandwich in my mouth.  Perfect.  And the flavor?  Think steak dipped in butter with a hint of onion and garlic and just enough gooey cheese to make it delicious!  The jasmine rice was unadorned and had a sticky rice texture.  It was easy to load bite-sized portions on my fork and I didn't drop a single grain.  If you've never tried jasmine rice, treat yourself to this.  Really good flavor.  If I had one knock, it would be that the plate was rather dull in appearance.  A sprig of garnish on the plate would do wonders for making it more appealing.    p.s.  The menu makes beer recommendations (types) to go with the food options.  Review #922

Like a lot of native Hoosiers, I like trying "Asian" restaurants, but don't have a great deal of understanding about authentic dishes.  And when I get to one that is described as Asian Fusion, I give up any pretense of knowing about that sort of thing.  But I know what I like and I like Meet Noodles.  Located just east of Castleton Square in a somewhat neglected shopping plaza, I found this small restaurant on the east side of the parking lot.  I was greeted as I entered and shown to a small table with a bench seat back.  I was brought a glass of ice water and a complementary small plate of marinated (?) peanuts with small diced veggies mixed in.  Nice flavor but mostly nutty.    I decided to order one of the bowls of La-Mian (fresh hand pulled noodles) called Lanzhou (pr. lon-Jo).  This dish contained clear beef bone broth as a base with sliced beef, half a marinated soy egg (hard boiled), cilantro, scallions, and baby bok choy.  It came with a large soup spoon and a pair of chopsticks.    I will be the first to admit that I don't hold the sticks properly, but I somehow make them work.  But I've never been able to grab noodles before.  I should have asked if they have forks (I didn't), but I was determined to conquer this task.  It took a bit of experimentation and a bit more slurping of noodles than I would want anyone to watch or film, but I eventually got the hang of it.  Note that once you master noodles, the rest of the food is easy!    The entree is very warming like a comfort food should be.  All the flavors were mild without any surprises.  Just a good bowl of beef and noodle soup!  One thing I noticed is that nobody was given napkins.  When I first started eating, I realized I didn't have one, but didn't see anyone else with one, so I thought I would be as neat as I could be and I seemed to make it through the entire meal without making a mess or wearing any.  I don't know if they only provide them for people who ask or not, but I watched every other group that came in while I dined and nobody was given one.  (Update Note:  According to my friend Wanda, there is a drawer at each table with napkins and forks.  Thanks buddy!)  I can't say that the meal exceeded my expectations, but it was a hearty and good tasting meal.  They do offer appetizers that I might try on a future visit, but unless I want left overs, I know the bowl dishes are quite a lot and that appetizers would probably need to be shared in my case.  Service cleared dishes promptly and asked if I was ready for the check.  Quick visit overall, so if you have a time crunch, you might consider this if you are in the area.  Review #3177

People who follow me on Yelp know I prefer to support locally owned businesses, but every once in awhile, I venture into the world of chain restaurants just to try something different.  It gives me a point of reference.  So being on the north side of Indy/Carmel area, I took my wife to lunch at this location on 96th, just east of Meridian.  It is a confusing place to find since it doesn't have its own entrance.  It shares one with Drury Plaza Hotel and then has the restaurant entrance facing away from the entrance.  So, we parked and entered through the patio/bar entrance, then saw the hostess table to check in, and were told to sit wherever we liked and someone would find us.  Seems an odd way to run a business and probably contributes to the complaints many have commented on about delays in service.  Anyway, we sat out on the patio and were attended to promptly! Yeah!  My wife had a few questions that were answered and then ordered the Buffalo Shrimp with the sauce on the side (she can't stand things too hot).  I ordered a Strawberry Basil Cooler after having a delicious cocktail the night before with the same flavors.  This was a non-alcoholic version and even though it had free refills, just didn't have the balance right.  Tasted somewhat like soda, but without the fizz.    However, for my entree, I ordered their Salmon and could not have asked for a better dish.  Just the right amount of seasoning for a lightly crusted top while the interior of the salmon stayed moist and flaky.  That seasoning included just a bit of salt which I rarely notice on most salmon and it was a pleasant surprise.  The dish was served with fresh veggies (just a bit past al dente which is the way I prefer), and my choice of Parmesan Mashed Potatoes that were delicious!  Very buttery flavor paired well with both the fish and veggies.  I love that they roast the lemon halves too.  Roasting, or heating in general, loosens up the pulp and makes squeezing the lemon very easy and I'm able to get a lot more juice out to enhance the brightness of the fish and veggies.    I would be remiss if I failed to mention the wonderful wood fire aroma that is in the air.  I smelled it from the parking lot and started to get hungry right away.  Service was good right up until the last fifteen minutes or so.  I think the waitress thought we were finished since it looked like our check in her hand when my wife surprised her by asking for a dessert menu.  That took a couple visits to arrive as well as an additional Ice Tea which took even more visits before it arrived.  We eventually got everything taken care of, but it was a definite drop off in efficiency from earlier in our visit.  Overall, the food and ambiance were delightful.  Service was generally good, but could use more consistency.  And for having the appearance of a high class restaurant, I was pleasantly surprised that our two meals, beverages, and a dessert were under $60 including tax and tip.  Review #2435

Overall, my wife and I enjoyed our carryout from Crustiez.  The Hershey's ice cream is smooth and creamy and delicious.  Highly recommended.  I like that they offer a cracker crisp crust on the Tsunami pizza and that they asked if the thin crust was okay before they placed the order.  My wife really likes the crispy crunch.  She isn't a fan of the soggy fold over pizzas we've had elsewhere, so I think she was very pleased with the texture AND the flavor.  So with great tasting pizza and Ice cream, why only 4 stars?  Well when you have wings listed first in your name, due to a huge rush on wings the day before, as earlier as 4 pm on a Friday, they were completely out of wings.  I think the manager needs to take the hit for not having more on hand.  I was going to get a pound roughly 9 or 10 wings for my dinner, but ended up getting bread sticks to go with the pizza and ice cream we ordered.  The bread sticks don't mention being garlic, but I could definitely smell the garlic when I opened the box.  They offer a marinara and a cheese sauce for dipping.  Both had a hint of spicy heat.  I wasn't expecting that but it wasn't too hot for me, but my wife did not like either.  There is plenty of parking in front of the building just off Southport Road, west of SR 37.  We will return.  Too bad they don't open until 4 pm.  I would probably eat here more frequently if they offered lunch.  They offer (usually) a wide variety of wing flavors, so I hope they restock soon so I can give the place another try.  Review #3914

One of the perks of the holiday season is that you don't have to have a large group to have a meal at the recreated "L S Ayres Tea Room".  After wandering the museum, I stopped in the restaurant and they had plenty of room for me.  (Note that the room can be reserved for private events that could interfere.)   I am old enough to have visited the original restaurant when it was located on the northeast corner of what is now the Circle Centre Mall.  I wasn't a frequent diner, but I think they museum has done a great job of recreating the look of the interior of the original.  They've even put views of Meridian Street in the faux windows to enhance the aesthetic.   What I recommend to visitors here is that they go with the classic menu items that are marked on the menu.  No visit is complete without their Chicken Velvet soup.  Just a bowl is enough.  But it is truly one of the best soups I have ever had.  Just enough chicken.  Such a creamy texture.  Delicious taste.  I also ordered the Classic Club which is a stacked, lightly toasted sandwich that is quartered with spears.  The sandwich contains ham, turkey, bacon, & Swiss.  The small triangular quarters tend to disassemble when you take the spears out, but if you use two hands, you can manage.  The flavor was okay, but just not on the same level as the soup.    I haven't tried the other food items to see how they compare since I only get here infrequently and go for the classics.  The service was dressed to match the fine setting and was friendly and very good though they can be tied up by large groups for short periods.  This is a place you can wear your fine clothing, but casual wear is okay too.  It tends to draw an older crowd who appreciate the history, but don't let that discourage you from taking in a tasty meal while visiting the museum during the holidays.  Review #3422

This location, just north of the the SR 267 exit on I-70, is a convenient spot to pick up a wide variety of beverages and mixes.  I was directed here by the Cardinal Spirits website as a place to find their products.  Although Discount Liquors doesn't carry the full line, they were able to help me find the Bramble Vodka that I was looking for.  I like when local products are available to purchase conveniently.  This location also carries local wines and beers as well.  Of course, they still carry most of the big name options as well, but this store is smaller in size than the big warehouse type liquor stores.  Still, I like supporting the independent and smaller businesses when I can, so I recommend giving this shop a try.  Review #2119

Although this restaurant has been open over a year, this was my first visit to this locally owned Mexican restaurant (they have a spot at 22nd & Delaware too!)  They set a challenge for themselves being a few blocks east of the Fountain when there are several Mexican restaurants already along Virginia Avenue.    Since they took over the former Santorini restaurant, they were fortunate to have their own lot on the east side of the building as well as free street parking out front.  I pulled in and entered into the lobby of the place.  The lobby opens into the bar area and greeter's area.  The dining is off to your right where I was taken to a table.  It was funny to see that I was the first customer right after 11 am, but before long, the place was filling up rapidly.  I was fortunate to get my order in ahead of all the rest and within a few minutes (I hadn't even finished my complementary salsa and chips), I was dining on my Carne Asada tacos.    The three tacos were served in soft double shells topped with cheese and avocado slices.  On the side were Mexican rice, a small dish of taco sauce, and a small bowl of "Churri" bean soup.  Each item had good flavor, but be aware that the heat level was on the low side.  They do have some hot sauces on the tables available.  The meat was chopped small and still tender rather than in strips.  The tacos were stuffed full and I was glad I had my napkin handy since some ingredients fell out while I was trying to get bites.    The service was prompt and friendly and I was easily in and out of the restaurant in a half an hour!  Granted, groups of folks may take longer, but my waitress did a really good job of making sure I was taken care of.  Good food, served with a smile and without a delay at reasonable prices.  Sounds like a winner to me!  Review #3553

Union 50 is a great place to share a dining adventure with friends.  Great service accompanies the creative assemblage of flavors that will surprise those dining.    Our group of four arrived early Sunday evening after parking in the free lot on Walnut Street.  We chose to be seated inside the spacious, high ceiling-ed dining hall, across from the bar.  Our server and a number of supporting staff made sure we had plenty of water, fresh plates and silverware for each course, and were personable, without being intrusive.  We started off with some of the smaller plates and an order of Artisan Bread (not complimentary, but very affordably priced).  The Sticky Chicken Wings had a delightful toasted sesame soy glaze.  Very tasty!  The plate was complimented by cucumber, fresno chili peppers, scallions, and a surprisingly delicious seaweed salad.  Who knew seaweed could be so yummy?  Oh, we also were brought warm moist towelettes with a slice of lemon to wash our hands after eating the wings with our fingers.    We also shared a plate of Medjool Dates.  The dates were stuffed with Tequila spiked chorizo,  and wrapped in bacon, over Peruvian pepper sauce.  I really liked the combination of flavors of sweet, salty, and savory components.   The order of Wood-Fired Wild Mushrooms was larger than expected.  The potato-bacon terrine was nestled atop a tangle of mushrooms, adorned with colorful pea shoots and a trail of romesco sauce.  The bacon was wrapped around a deck of mandolined potatoes and baked to a done, but not crispy finish.  This was another hit with the group.  For our entrees, I ordered the Maple Leaf Farm Duck, one ordered Shrimp & Grits, and the other two ordered the Smoked Gunthorp Farms Pork Chops.  When our friend asked about the heat of the Tasso ham featured in the Shrimp & Grits, our server took time to describe it and even brought out a sample before confirming the order.  She liked the Tasso which was mild heat wise, but had plenty of flavor.  Overall, she liked the shrimp and the heirloom grits with oyster mushrooms and Tasso ham gravy, with house Worchestershire and scallions.  I also liked the flavor of the Maple Leaf Farms Duck.  I think I liked the combination of blackberry sauce, duck leg confit, and the parsnip puree and hickory roasted turnip more than the actual duck breast itself.  The breast was a bit overcooked and slightly dry.  The  rest of the ingredients were wonderful, including the asparagus side.  A near miss on the duck itself, but everything else was 5 star.  The two who ordered the pork chops had differing opinions of their meals.  For our friend who likes spicy heat, he seemed to enjoy the chop which was moist and crowned the creamed sweet corn, serrano potato pave, green tomato chow chow and was topped with peach BBQ.  For my wife, who does not handle heat very well, the serrano seasoning on the potato was too strong and she ended up struggling with the meal.  She ended up giving most of the pave to our friend.  She thought the corn was really good, but noted that the chop itself had little flavor beyond the one note of heat.  (Confirmed by our guest.)  So, if they took a bite of just the chop, it was bland.  Our friend was able to pair the chop with some of the other flavors more successfully, but still thought he would prefer to try something else the next time he dined here.  To wrap up the evening, we ordered two of the dessert options:  a collection of chocolates and a "Decadent" Chocolate Cake that came with vanilla ice cream and a flavored whipped cream.  I am not sure if all the molded chocolates were made in house or acquired, but they had a nice dark chocolate flavor that melted in my mouth.  They contained several flavors of complimentary tastes.  We got nine pieces of chocolate and creamy mousse like scoop for $8.  Good flavors, but lacking a Wow factor.  Same for the Decadent Cake.  Comments were that it was much like a brownie with ice cream.  Pretty standard and relatively small portion for another $8.    So, some of the small plates and the service were Wow, level 5.  However, some of the entrees lacked a bit due to the factors sited above.  Like many of the avant garde restaurants in town, you have to roll the dice (and sometimes use a dictionary) to figure out what to order.  I can't say there is a single plate that could be described as routine.  Union 50 pushes the boundaries of your taste...most of the time, taking you to places that are beyond what you can imagine yourself.  Review #109

Real crab meat paired with a creamy mustard mayo makes for one fantastic lunch!  I parked in the Circle Centre Mall parking garage and shook my head at the lines of people waiting at the fast food places in the mall.  (They must waste half their lunch hours waiting for blah food.)  A short trip outside to the Meridian Street entrance of Oceanaire and I knew I was in for a good meal.    As a seafood restaurant, you can tell a lot by what you smell the second you walk in.  No seafood smell at all, so that was a relief!  Even as I walked by the huge oyster bar to get to the regular bar seating, not a scent!    I was greeted immediately by the bartender and she (Kristin) offered a cocktail menu, chilled veggies, and a bread course to get started.  I passed on the cocktail (they also have wine and some bottled beers available.)    The veggies were served under ice.  There was a nice assortment of items to choose from:  olives, pepper, radish, cucumber, garlic dill pickle, and celery.    The bread was warm and partially sliced, mostly conducive to tearing the remainder of the way.  The whipped butter was cool, but easy to spread.  Very tasty!  I was in the mood for a crab cake.  They had an option under the entrees that had two cakes ($35), but I knew I wanted to save room for a side dish as well, so I got the appetizer version (one cake for $18).  Sure, it may seem like an expensive lunch, but I don't mind when the food lives up to the price.  This crab cake rivals any I have had!  (It may be even better than the one I had a week ago at Salt on Mass under the direction of the previous Oceanaire chef!)  The crab was generally shaped as a cake shape, but the chef was wise to not over process the meat.  There were some flavors added and a bit of celery for a little bit of crunch, but time after time, there were lumps of crab meat that were easy to spear and dip in my dish of creamy mustard mayonnaise.  It also came with a quarter wedge of lemon so that I was able to get multiple layers of flavor.  The slight browning on the outside of the cake (broiled?) brought out a rich flavor as well.  I almost regret not getting the second one!  To go with the crab, I also ordered the grilled asparagus with Parmesan and lemon.  Huge spears of asparagus about 3/4 of an inch thick covered a serving plate.  They were cooked perfectly too!  Tender, but not mushy, they were easy to cut and almost had a sweetness to them when paired with the other flavors.    As I walked back to my car, there were folks still waiting in line for the fast food.   I couldn't help but smile and think it's good to be me! ;)  Full disclosure:  I have not been to Oceanaire for five years.  I had a really bad experience during a Devour Downtown promotion on a night when the wind chill was well below zero.  It took me this long to get over my resentment and now I am kicking myself for not getting back here sooner.    Review #139

Who knew?!  In the small southeast corner of Hendricks County that surrounds Camby across SR 67, there is a wonderland of things to look at (some for sale!) for fans of the long running Doctor Who series.  I have driven by this shop hundreds of times, but it wasn't until the relaunching of the series that caught my attention and I decided to stop in.  I know very little about the stories, but have picked up enough to understand that this sci-fi character has a pantheon of characters and because so many actors have taken turns playing them, it makes for a lot of merchandise for collectors to acquire.  Pulling into this private lot (note the highway is divided, so you will have to pay attention getting in here), I entered into the middle of the shop.  To the right is a museum of past merchandise/memorabilia that the shop owners have accumulated.  It is amazing to see how much they have.  To the left is the merchandise that is for sale.  There are books, magazines, comics, DVD's, audio CD's, T-shirts and other clothing, games, action figures, and just about anything you can imagine...all related to this figure.  And the place hasn't forgotten photo ops:  There are full size cutouts you can pose with (and buy), there is a Dalek near the front door, and a Tardis (blue police box) that are known to all the Whovian followers.  I don't do a lot of collecting now, but I have to admit that if I did, this would be the first place I would go.  If it has to do with Doctor Who, this is a must stop for those interested.  Right here in Central Indiana....Who knew?  Review #3531

There is a little Chinese restaurant outside of I-465 on east Washington St. that had a lot of influence on my culinary journey.  Over 30 years ago, I was living near 10th and Franklin and my wife and I wanted to take our kids to someplace that wasn't fast food.  We stumbled upon this restaurant (remember, there was no Yelp, there wasn't even an internet in those "olden" days!)  The only Chinese food I had eaten was my mom's fried rice which I'll guarantee wasn't made from an authentic recipe.  So, being a picky eater, I decided to go with something with beef 'cause I like meat.  And I realized that I had misjudged an entire cuisine because of one bad, or at least not very tasty experience.  The kids liked the food too, so we would go to Yen Ching once or twice a month.  Great tea!  Tasty crab rangoon and potstickers (Gyoza).  We loved it! And every time, James was running the front end of the house and making sure we were taken care of.  And then we moved...we tried the Yen Ching on Michigan, but found the buffet very blah.  It just wasn't the same.  So today, I was headed to Hancock County and remembered my old favorite restaurant.  Sure enough, it was there in the same location.  I ordered the Broccoli Beef lunch special and it was still the same tender beef (probably the most tender beef I have ever had including at steak houses!) that I remembered.  And behind the register, looking a lot grayer, but with the same warm personality, was James.  I'm sure he didn't recognize me, and he was busy checking things in the back, prepping to go orders, and keeping everything running smoothly.  So, I didn't get to chat with him, but my server mentioned he had been running the place for 37 years.    It may not be 100% authentic Chinese (pot stickers come to mind), but the food simply tastes good....I think of it as Chinese Comfort food.  Sure, some of the employees are somewhat reserved and that may be misinterpreted for being less welcoming, but James always greets the customers.  Sure, the decor looks like it hasn't changed in 30 years either, but that's okay.  It is very small and intimate like any good hole in the wall restaurant should be.  I'm not telling you to go here because you will find something that pushes the frontier of cuisine or because you will have the time of your life.  But I don't know how much longer James will be there.  Treat yourself to a meal at one of the staple restaurants of the east side while you can.  Just look for the guy with the big smile.  That will be James.  Review #778

I stopped in for lunch on Friday.  Great food as usual.  If not for a miscommunication problem, this would have been a 5 star review.  When I was seated, my waiter arrived quickly and I informed him that I was going to order a "dine-in" meal and then get two sandwiches to go.  I then asked him to put all the orders in at the same time so that the sandwiches would be ready when I finished.   The Food:  The dine-in Spinach and Mushroom pizza was delicious!  Crispy crust that almost snapped with each bite easily supported the nicely blended flavors.  The cheese was soft and gooey, but not stringy.  This was quality food and I would definitely recommend it.  The Ham and Cheese sandwich (to go) was saved for dinner.  The ham (Nueske's spiral sliced honey baked ham) was served in quarter inch thick slices, not some measly folded stuff you get at a sub shop or from a prepackaged deli shelf.  This is ham that's good enough for a Christmas feast, but without the wait!  Delicious again!  The Italian Beef sandwich (to go) was also taken home for dinner.  This is my most ordered item since I rarely make Italian Beef at home.  This sandwich is full of flavor with sweet peppers and lots of seasoning.  It even comes with additional balsamic vinaigrette on the side for more flavor.  The bread stayed moist and had a nice flavor on its own.  It has a soft doughy bite but is sturdy enough to hold up to the filling.  Great selection #3!  So, the problem isn't with the food.  Basically, my waiter got my order right, but because he relied upon the support staff to take care of me throughout the meal, he was unaware that my pizza hadn't come out.  I kept thinking that it would be out soon, so I waited, but finally flagged him down to see if he would check the status of my order.  Before coming over, he returned to the pass and brought my sandwiches out.  I explained that I never got my pizza.  He did chase down the problem and got my slice out fairly quickly after that (what he brought may have been a double sized slice since it looked like a quarter pizza.)  Although he said the kitchen took responsibility for the oversight, I think it shows a lack of ownership for a waiter to allow about twenty minutes to pass without personally checking to see if I wanted anything else or had any questions/complaints.  Team spirit on a staff is great, but ultimately, the waiter is the one who gets the majority of the tip and has to be responsible for taking care of the customer.  Rev #14

I like the direction that Conner Prairie is heading.  Sure, they are still a living museum that portrays life in Indiana from our early settlement history and they do that as well as any place I've been.  But they aren't sitting back.  There are areas of the park that don't get as much attention and I visited some of those recently.  On a hot day, I can't tell you how much I appreciated the Visitors Center which is climate controlled and makes for a nice respite.  Inside you can get your tickets for the park and the tethered hot air balloon ride (on fair weather days).  There is also a store for souvenirs and the Makesmith area where kids can work on skills/craftmanship in areas that relate to those before technology.  There is also an animal encounters area which is a place where kids can be around farm animals that they might not otherwise see other than at the fair.  Granted, there are mainly goats and sheep, so it was a little disappointing not to see horses, ponies, or mules.  (Cattle are on site, but in another area and are not for petting.)  The Conner House has been preserved fairly accurately but with a few modern conveniences (heating and cooling) that are out of sight.  Built in 1823, it is a home that offers tours as well as browsing depending upon your time and interest.  An area I hadn't been to before is the Treetop Outpost.  After listening to historic reenactors in some of the other areas of the park, the Treetop Outpost is a place where kids can run wild, beat on things, jump, and play.  The Treehouse is huge and has ramps and stairs and places to lookout through the woods.  Fort Hoosier is also there and has a large slide for kids to go through.  There is a River Outlook over the White River that is close by as well.  There is also a covered bridge that has been moved to the site where you hear voices describe life in 1863 as you walk through.  Not all of the state was pro-Union which seems evident throughout our state's history.  Whether you are a history buff, or want to explore new things, Conner Prairie is evolving to offer more for visitors to experience.  Review #2719

While waiting at the hospital, I decided to a grab some breakfast.  As I was heading to the cafeteria, I happened to notice this restaurant.  Near the entrance, there were several stations with table seating beyond them.  Along the wall was a pastry station and a salad/chilled item cooler at a right angle.  A soup island with several varieties was placed between the pastry wall and a breakfast/sandwich counter.  Cashier stations were to the left with a self serve coffee station beyond that.  I grabbed a cinnamon roll while waiting for my order of "the Good Egg" to be prepared.  I also grabbed a small Hazelnut coffee.  After paying, I enjoyed my meal in house.  The sandwich was really good.  The bun was toasted and the eggs, spinach, tomato, avocado, and aioli were ripe/fresh and tasty.  The cinnamon roll was glazed with icing and had a slight taste of citrus along with the cinnamon.  The center had a slightly doughy texture.  The coffee was full flavored and though served hot, did not scald.  Good food and a smooth system for getting served quickly.  Review #3411

Although I got my order to go, that didn't diminish my appraisal of the food at this restaurant.  I saw that it nearly made the top 10 of Yelp!'s "Top 50" restaurants in Indiana, so I made a point of heading there.    As you drive across Raymond, the restaurant is about 200 yards (?) west of the Sherman intersection (near the grain elevators.)  The restaurant is located on the west side of the building set back from the street.  It shares a sign with a graphics company, so from the street it appears to say "Graphics Peruvian Sandwiches" until you slow down and see that the bottom half of the sign has "Don Juan" in smaller letters.      The restaurant has a very industrial look to it with a few Peruvian items along the walls to give it a bit of identity.  There is plenty of free parking in the lot outside the entrance.  The inside of the restaurant consists of a dining area with a counter straight back from the doors, the kitchen on the left end of the dining area, and an area that was closed off during the day that can be used for overflow seating and entertaining since it has a stage area in the room behind the dining area.    They do offer wait service, but since I was getting my order to go, I headed back to the counter to order, and then grabbed a seat.  The wait was about 15 minutes since all the sandwiches are made to order.      I decided to pick up two sandwiches so that I could sample more and split them with my wife who was at home.  I went with the Lomo Saltado and the Chicharrones.  They have sodas, chips, empanadas, and other items available, but I stayed with just the sandwiches.  The sandwiches were individually packed in styrofoam boxes and kept warm the entire 40 minute drive home!    The Lomo was the first one I tried.  The sandwich was 8-9 inches in length and has a hearty bread which was needed since the sandwich was rather juicy.  It consists of Beef tenderloin strips, sauteed with onions, tomatoes, and cilantro.  The meat was cut into large enough strips that there was a definite chew to the texture.  A couple bites were a little tough, but that could have been from the long drive allowing the meat to overcook.  The flavor was delicious!  The accompanying blend of veggies were seasoned and had a bit of salty taste that complemented the beef flavor.  The sandwich was packed and the ingredients overflowed from the sandwich into the serving box.  So, you may need a fork (or fingers if you don't mind getting a little messy!) to finish off the ingredients.  Trust me...you will want to!    The Chicharrones sandwich is served on the same bread and has thick sliced (between 1/8 and  1/4 inch) deep fried pork, served over fried sweet potatoes and topped with salsa Criolla.  The salsa isn't like Mexican salsa.  It has red onion strips that tasted pickled to me.  The onions are prepared with a variety of other ingredients, but aren't as juicy as the Lomo.
