It made for a much neater sandwich to eat.  And the flavor was once again tremendous!  The pork was mostly tender, but again a couple bites had a bit of chew, possibly from the long wait.  The sweet potato is sliced thin and fried to bring out the sweetness and that really pairs well with the meat and the tart/savory flavors of the salsa.  Again, another sandwich I would recommend.    The sandwiches with tax were just under $20, but considering the prices of beef tenderloin, I found the prices to be market appropriate.  Sure, you can find sandwiches cheaper, but if you want really good flavor and a sandwich that is more like an entire meal, treat yourself to Don Juan!  Review #305

My wife treated me to the newest addition to the Fundae's franchise which just opened in Speedway.  I was pleasantly surprised at how friendly the staff was, encouraging us to sample any flavors of ice cream we had questions about.  There were about two dozen flavors, a wide variety of flavored cones dipped in chocolates, and lots of toppings to add if you were inclined to do so.  I'm probably not their target customer preferring a simple, but creamily delicious, cup of ice cream.  I sampled a tasty lemon poppy seed flavor before settling on a divine Raspberry Rhapsody.  Creamy cold smoothness with raspberry swirls and chocolate coated raspberries to offer a little texture.  My wife went with the Caramel Chaos ice cream that was equally as creamy.  The place was spotlessly clean and though we were not rushed, we were through the line quickly and enjoyed our ice cream in the small dining area.    Parking was free along the street, but there is also a free parking garage nearby (for up to 3 hours).  Once the word gets out, I can see this being a very popular spot this summer.  Review #2848

I stopped by the new Love Handle restaurant on Mass Ave for lunch today and was glad to see they had a great crowd.  I could see Chris working in the kitchen while Ally was taking orders at the counter at the back of the dining area.  They retained the blackboards of menu items to the visitor's left and also had printed copies of the day's items for anyone who finds reading colored chalk difficult to read.  If you haven't been to the new place yet, they have kept the unique sandwich combinations that have won over many customers.  They have the breakfast items like the biscuits and gravy too.  And, since the sandwich options change (daily, I think), you just have to trust Chris' expertise that the sandwiches he lists will not only taste great, but will be colorful and will amaze you with the pairings.  For instance, I ordered a Tipp Scott which is a roast pork belly, with mixed berry jam, pickled red onions, and Blu Chz (their spelling!)  I would never think of putting this combination together on my own, but Wow!  They tasted great!  The cuts of pork belly were tender and had a little bit of salt.  The jam was sweet, the onions added a nice crunch along with the acidity component, and the savory cheese just balanced the flavors.  Served on a fresh hoagie bun sliced for easier handling, I devoured the sandwich faster than I intended.  So good!  The differences from the old place include extended hours Tues-Sat to include the dinner hours, having beer and wine on hand, and having the popcorn side now a separate side (sorry, no more freebies).    The process:  You place your order and pay at the counter in the back.  They give you a numbered card that you put on a stand at your seat of choice and when the food is ready, the staff brings out your order to you.  Silverware and napkins are on the tables.  Flavored water and coffee are found on a blonde side table on the east wall.  Customers are expected to bus their own trash and stack the plates/baskets on top of the disposal bins.  If I had one suggestion to the owners, it would be to add either a small salad or some mixed veggies to the menu as staples.  I didn't see any vegetables on the menu other than the popcorn or as ingredients on the sandwiches.  I enjoyed my lunch and from the size of the crowd, the word is getting out about the new location.    Rev #33

If you are curious by nature, or just like checking out museums, this teeny shop hosts a collection of Lady Liberty memorabilia like I've seen nowhere else.  Most of the times I've driven by, the museum is closed.  But while I stopped by the neighboring Tim & Julie's Another Fine Mess, I asked about the museum and the staff went over and opened it up for me to browse.  Apparently, Tim owns the collection and wanted to share it with anyone who was interested.  So, if you are interested, just go when the store is open and maybe they will let you into the museum.  Once inside, there isn't much room to move around.  There is a counter to sign in and behind it, some wall mounted objects.  The other walls have shelves of collectibles including dolls, mugs, statues (all sizes), photos, clothing, and posters.  There is even one small statue that is about the size of a coin.    They do ask that you not touch the items to help preserve their collection's condition.  Still, it is fun to look at.  I understand that if you go when Tim is around, he can tell you a lot more about the collection.  He wasn't there during my visit, so I was on a "self-guided" tour.  There are only a few steps worth of space, so I didn't need much guiding!    It was a fun diversion to see that someone made an effort to make his private collection available for others.  Most of my collectibles are long gone from downsizing.  I applaud this guy for finding a way to hold onto his items.  Review #3368

I haven't tried their computer service yet, but I did take my phone in for some work.  My battery was just not holding a charge and it seemed I always needed to be on a charger.  Didn't like being out on the road and having the GPS go out, so my wife recommended trying this little shop located within the Meijer in Camby.    When we arrived, we hit the dinger bell to let them know we were at the counter.  We were greeted and were told they didn't have my type of battery in stock.  We were given an estimated time for when it should be available and the price for parts.  They have a standard rate per hour for repairs and were given an estimate for that as well.  Unfortunately, the battery didn't ship on time and we were delayed.  I also didn't notice they are closed on Sundays, so that visit was a "no go", but I simply didn't see the small sign with their hours on the counter.  When the replacement battery came in, we were told they suspected it had a defect because it took a long time to charge.  It seemed to work okay, but they were going to get another battery to replace the replacement and there would be not additional charge.    Finally, I was able to drop it off when we got the notice the new battery was available.  Everything seems to be working okay, though I noticed this new battery still takes a long time to charge.  It does seem to hold the charge though, so I am not 100% sold that everything is working perfectly.    I got the impression that the individual who worked on my phone understood the problem, but wasn't certain why the charging issue had sprung up.  If I have a problem that isn't something I can easily adjust to, then I will take it back for one more try.  I think they are trying their best to be helpful, but I seriously don't know how anyone can keep up with all the technological changes and upgrades.  They are small staffed, so the turn around on repairs may take longer than you would like, but I prefer it to work the first time, not just get it back and then have problems.  Review #3800

I had set up and bookmarked Pomodoro when I first read that it was to become the latest restaurant to make a go of it inside the first floor of the Hampton Inn across from the Circle Centre Mall.  Though I had originally planned on stopping by for dinner, I was glad to see that they have recently added lunch hours.  So, I asked my wife to join me for lunch there.  We parked at the mall and walked over to the restaurant (I noticed a sign for valet but assumed it was for evening guests.)  As we stepped inside, we were greeted at the host counter where an overhead menu let us know what they have to offer (small pamphlet menus are also there.)  While we were deciding, a second staff member let us know they also had lunch specials which include half a pizza (cheese or pepperoni only) with a side salad and a beverage.  My wife ordered the pepperoni special while I decided to go with the Meat Lasagna ($18). I was surprised that it didn't include any sides or appetizers for that price, but I decided to stay with it and pay for a side salad as well.  (Note that all salads come with a house dressing.)  After paying, we were given a number to put on our table and we selected our own seat though we were informed a large party was going to take over the back room of the restaurant, so we decided to stay in the front bar area dining room.  Soon, my wife received a large bowl of salad and her beverage while I got my lasagna and small side.  The same individual from the check in brought out our meal and poured the chilled (no ice) water for me.  I knew that the time lapse was too soon for her pizza to be ready, so we began eating.  The portion sizes of my salad and lasagna were suited to lunch time, though I became even more aware that for the price, there needed to be something more than just a modest serving of lasagna.  There was a lot of cheese (three types) and ground beef and Pomodoro sauce.  So there wasn't a lot of flavor from either the meat or the sauce.  Maybe that is more authentic, but I found it rather bland.    After about 15 minutes, my wife had finished her large bowl of salad and I was nearly finished with my meal when we flagged down the server to ask about the pizza.  He went back to the kitchen and then didn't follow up with us.  Instead, he seemed focused on the large party that had arrived in the back.  We then flagged down the second staff member who we met at the desk and let him know.  Again, he disappeared and didn't get back to us.    Finally, we got the attention of the first server and he went back and got my wife's meal.  Surprisingly, the 4 slices of pizza and another salad arrived on the same plate.  He said that the system had not delivered the food order to the kitchen which had caused the delay.  Seems odd that my order and a large salad got to the kitchen, but hers didn't.  Obviously, by this time, my wife was disappointed by the lack of follow up by the two staff members.  To make up for it, the server did comp her meal and gave her some complementary tickets towards future purchases.  But she was not a fan of the pizza which was a bit greasy from the pepperoni and somewhat limp/floppy in the middle (she prefers a crisper crust.)  And the pepperoni slices were not evenly distributed so that numerous bites were just cheese.    I understand that there can be some glitches in service at a new restaurant, but when a customer has to try three times to get someone to check on a meal, that is a basic mistake that needs to be addressed immediately.  I appreciate that the server tried to make amends but the difference of failing to give us feedback on the first request instead of the third makes it impossible for me to give this place a higher rating.  Hopefully, this review can help the management to be more aware of the orders and to instill a follow up mentality in those serving.  Review #3692

Sunday morning...wife out of town...didn't feel like my usual bowl of fruit and cereal, so after walking my dogs, I hopped in my car and headed downtown to try a restaurant I hadn't been to for brunch (probably over 10 years since my last visit.)    Finding parking is hit or miss downtown for convenience, so I usually park in the mall for $3 and walk the 2 blocks to this location north of the convention center.  Maybe the morning rain kept folks away, but I was able to be seated right away at the food bar where I was told about the self serve coffee bar and given the menu and specials of the day.  Although I usually have a modest and healthy breakfast 5-6 times a week, I LOVE big breakfasts.  So when I drove the 35 minutes to get here, I was committed to indulging in what looked most appetizing.  I decided to start with the Croissant French Toast Patachou.  This comes topped with powdered sugar, chopped pecans with a small pitcher of warmed syrup and a side cup of fresh fruit.  Sounded like a good start to go with my coffee of the day, a tasty Banana Nut drip.  I must say, the flavor was really good on both the dish and the coffee.  Just the right balance of savory and sweet (I only used part of the syrup to not drench it).  I will say though that I was a bit disappointed in the appearance.  I think of croissants as light colored and flaky.  This was just a darker brown flat that didn't have much visual appeal.  And the side of fruit was okay...it was fresh, but maybe a bit under ripe.  Not unusual in April, but I've had better.  Still, if you care more about flavor than appearance, the dish was very tasty.  I had also committed to trying one of their "Broken Yolk" sandwiches (I went with the Pork Sausage).  The manager behind the counter who took my order asked if I was sure because the double meal was a lot to eat.  I figured I could always get a to go box if I didn't finish it, so I said "Thanks, but Yes!"  I really like how they waited until I was finishing my first order before placing the sandwich in the queue. That's confidence in their ability to turn around a sandwich quickly.  Let me say that the kitchen is great at keeping up with orders and if anything, it was the servers who were letting food back up at the pass.  But since I was seated right there, I was given my order as soon as it was set up.  My sandwich came with eggs that were served with soft yolks and white cheddar on my choice of wheat bread and with a side of arugula salad lightly dressed with a vinaigrette (a nice bit of color on the plate too!)  I sliced my sandwich in half and unstacked the two sausage rounds so that it wasn't one of those big mouth sandwiches.  Although the yolks broke a bit with the cutting, I was okay with that.  I love the way warm egg yolks taste with the rest of the ingredients and though a little messy, I didn't have to worry about biting into the yolk and having it pop over my shirt.  I was also able to swab the bread over the yolk that ran to the plate and not lose any of the taste.  An excellent sandwich.  As I looked down at the empty plate, I was glad I hadn't filled on coffee.  The meal(s) were very satisfying and though the price for the double meal was a lot more than I could have made it at home, I appreciated that the service was helpful, very efficient, and friendly throughout.  A nice treat to myself that I didn't mind paying for.   It won't be nearly so long until my next visit.  Review #2470

With the challenge of construction, one way streets, and interstates making this location a difficult space to get to for those who aren't familiar with 11th and College, take solace knowing that the food and service is worth the effort!  Located in the former site of R2Go, there is free street parking along 11th though it does get a little crowded quickly.  Just be sure to look it up on your GPS before you go and you should be okay!  Although there is a door on the southwest corner, they are directing everyone to go through the large double doors on the west side of the building.  Inside, the order counter is straight back (menus mounted on the wall behind the cashier). On the right is the pastry and baked goods counter but you don't order from the staff stationed there.  Just remember what you want and place the order at the cashier along with any beverage you wish and with any sandwiches/other food items you want.  Understand that this isn't some cheap donut shop or fast food place.  If you want sandwiches for lunch, I think the ones we ordered were $10 and $12 apiece.  They serve them sliced and because we ordered some pastries as well as the grain side salad with our sandwiches, neither of us finished our sandwiches at lunch.    We chose to sit outside by the entrance to the building.  I found it a little unusual that they didn't give us a table number, but the staff successfully delivered out pastries and sandwiches to our table.  We carried our beverages with us.  They also bus the tables, though it would be nice if they had a trash can near the outdoor patio so that we could get rid of our trash or could set our used silverware in a tub to make it easier for the staff.  Everything we tasted was uniquely tasty!  I ordered the Roast Beef Chimichurri and the bread was toasted and the sandwich sliced for easier eating.  Lots of yummy ingredients that I would never think of or go to the trouble of preparing at home.  My wife ordered the LVTHNTBA (a turkey, bacon, and avocado sandwich on marbled rye) that she also liked I got a bite and liked it too!  From the pastry side, my wife ordered some almond croissants and a crispy pastry called the Kouign-Amann which she raved about.  I ordered a slice of the Blueberry-Lime coffee cake that has a crumbled top.  Excellent.  When we added drinks, tax and tip, some would complain it was an expensive lunch.  But considering some was taken home for dinner and the pastries (what didn't get devoured immediately) would be nice for breakfast tomorrow!  It's multiple meals unless you are just a beast that stuffs yourself each meal.  Everything we tried was unique (other than the almond croissants), so in a time when I've become bored with my own cooking, it was fun to get out and try some new flavor combinations.  Very pleasant staff and plenty of seating inside as well.  If you want to try something different, make a plan for a day trip to downtown.  Just take College north to 11th and be patient going passed the Bottleworks construction.  Review #3784

Although my wife isn't a big sushi fan, I talked her into trying this quick restaurant because they have egg drop soup and gyoza as well.  So we pulled into the shopping plaza (near the Kroger) and strolled into the space.    The interior starts with a small dining area where customers can grab a table to dine or simply to wait for their "to go" order.  Seems like a lot of customers were getting theirs to go.  So we grabbed a menu from the order counter/sushi bar and took our seats until we had decided.  I then went to the counter and selected an egg drop soup (rich in color and taste, but very hot temp and a little thin), gyoza, edamame, a Tiger roll and some beverages from the cooler.  After paying, we waited a short while as the food came out as it was ready.  The edamame was a nice portion for 2 people and had a medium amount of salt.  My wife would have liked a little more salt, but I think it was fine.  The gyoza was tender and had 6 pieces filled with pork and some onion.  It came with a dipping sauce that seemed to go quite well.    My Tiger Roll was served on a tray (looked like a cutting board with a spiral design on it.)  I agree that it wasn't the biggest I've had, but I thought the portion was just right.  I get frustrated with those giant pieces that are difficult to eat in one bite.  These were just right for me.   And the flavor was exceptional.  Fresh and multilayered, I loved the eel sauce sweet/tangy and the crunch on top of the eel, avocado, cucumber and crab stick.  One of the best I've had around town!  The man running the order counter was friendly and efficient and brought out our meals to us without having to get names or numbers.  I also liked that he printed off an itemized list of our order for us to confirm before we paid.  It seems simple, but it eliminates a mistake in ordering unless you are the one who isn't paying attention.  I hope they keep this plan.  When we finished, we bused our own tables.  I like that the soup is delivered in a to go container since it is a large serving.  Nice lid to keep it from spilling during travel.  Now, if they only would get larger sized spoons than the little plastic teaspoons..that would be appreciated.  Overall, I liked everything I tried.  Good food and pleasant service.  Clean space.  And the option to eat in or take out.  Seems like a nice addition to Brownsburg.  Review #3319

This is one of those reviews where I think if they could get some help, they could quickly raise their rating.  The food I had was quite tasty, but when the sushi chef is having to wait tables as well as make the food, it is too much to have high expectations.    I decided to give this place (along the SR 267 corridor that crosses over I-70 as the first exit to Plainfield) a try.  I pulled in for lunch in front of the restaurant and noticed a "help wanted" sign, which I've learned should immediately lower your expectations.  Fortunately, most places seem to manage in the short run.  When I entered the lobby, a sign directed me to the main dining area by the bar.  I saw a couple of folks dining but they may have been employees since they ended up going back to the kitchen area and exiting a side door.  Anyway, one of them let the waiter/chef know I was there.  He was soft spoken and I wasn't sure if I heard much of what he said the entire meal.  I grabbed a menu off a table since I had decided to sit at the sushi bar.  He brought my water and I ordered a bowl of veggie Tom Yum soup to start.  Later, I ordered a 2pc Nigiri Sake (salmon) and an Eel Avocado roll.  The chef (before I knew he was the chef) began working on some "to go" order before bringing out my soup.  When the soup, which was full of flavor, but not spicy hot like I've had elsewhere, arrived without a napkin for me. I mentioned it and I was given the chopsticks, napkin, and a dish for soy sauce.  The soup was good and piping hot but the shape of the spoon made it hard to get the vegetables, especially the broccoli over the lip of the spoon.  Before I finished the soup, the chef had finished the other order and brought out my entrees on a plate.  Everything looked and tasted really good too!  However, I had to ask for the soy sauce since he had forgotten to bring it as well.  See the pattern?  Again, I enjoyed the food and when I was finished, I was quickly able to check out.  Note that I was the only dine in customer at the time.  What must it be like if a large group or several tables of customers had arrived?  I don't know that I can give this place any higher rating despite the good food until they get someone who can help fix the service issues so that the chef can simply cook.  Review #3592

Inside the Tube Factory, there is a cool new coffee shop.  Basically, there is a counter area where you can order Tinker Coffee beverages and get Amelia's pastries at a fair price and be surrounded by all the cool things in the Tube Factory exhibition/art gallery space.    If you've been around Indy for any time at all, you know the quality of Tinker and Amelia's.  If you haven't been to the Tube Factory for an event or to just look around, bookmark it as something out of the ordinary for you to do.    Inside, there is a voluminous space with lots of windows.  It is quiet with lots of places to sit.  If you need a break from sitting, you can check out the exhibits (free) that are on display.  I stopped by and got a self serve drip coffee (immediately drinkable in a NorMal ceramic mug).  Note that busing your own plates/paper is expected and is collected by the self serve coffee station.  The chocolate pastry was light and flaky and really good!  Outside, there are three notable pieces of public art.  Totally Pencil by the Big Car Collaborative adorns the west side of this bright purple building.  On the east side is Scarab by Jules Muck.  On the south side (on one of the garage doors) is an oversize mural of Marguerite Young (a local novelist) by Jules Muck.  There is also a dedicated parking lot and live chickens on the campus.  If you still aren't convinced you want to make a trip to the near southeast side, plan to swing by neighboring Garfield Park.  In particular, stop by to see the new Blake's Garden by the Conservatory.  Again, it is free and is such a cool place for bringing kids to learn about growing things.  Cool things are happening on South Shelby and the Garfield Park area. Check it out!  Review #3059

Each time I go to Nesso, it seems they outdo the experience they provide my small group.  It's like they keep all the things that are great (food, ambiance, and SERVICE), and then add more.  On our latest visit, we got to check out the new patio (with a cover that opens and a fire pit!), try a new "Red Pop" that is house made and bottled with multiple kinds of booze (nothing else!), and were introduced to Chef Kawika Pieper who brought out a dish of Rabbit Terrine to try as a future item (Oh MY!!!)  Everything is first class and served with a smile.  Of course, we always ask for our favorite waiter in town, Brandon D who greets us at the door when we arrive and seats us on the quieter side of the restaurant because our group likes to talk and be able to hear without shouting.  That is greatly appreciated.  We started off with the Burrata with an extra side of buttered and toasted semolina sourdough.  After patiently waiting for my photos, Brandon then broke down the cheese ball so that it would be easier for us to spoon on to our sharing plates.  This was so delicious!  It comes with a cherry tomato conserva, red wine candied onion, and pesto.  (see photo)  We knew we were in for a special night when it started this good.  We ordered cocktails, my friend ordering a "Balanced Martini" that was excellent and smooth, while I got the Pearbarbaro which was sweet and like a pear juice with a bit of alcohol.  Very nice!  Our wives tried the Red Pop and were surprised at how easily they could sip that like a soda!    We ordered a variety of antipasti dishes which we all enjoyed (see photos), and while waiting for our entrees from the Primi and Secondi, the chef brought out the Rabbit Terrine.  Only two of us had tried rabbit before but nothing like this.  It was served seasoned and deep fried with a light crust along with some prepared radishes (sorry I can't recall the type and procedure), some greens with little white flowers, and a spread of delicious flavor on the plate.  (no menu to look at for the details yet) There were four small pieces maybe two bites in size.  I speared one with my fork and it was so tender, that the terrine fell apart.  It was literally fork tender.  And the flavor?  Wow!  Light and juicy like the best dark meat of chicken you've ever had.  Wow!  The radishes were cold and prepared so tender that I didn't have to chew them.  I could crush them with my tongue!  The meal with the exception of the greens, seemed to melt in my mouth.  I gave a resounding "Yes!" to adding this to the menu soon.    For our entrees, I went out of my comfort zone and ordered the Calamarata (lamb sausage with noodles, Calabrian chile, labneh, pesto, and oil-cured tomato.)  Although I'm not a big fan of lamb, I had no trouble finishing my plate.  The complementary flavors seemed to carry the day as I got further into the dish.    Of course, we had to get some desserts and since we were celebrating both couples' anniversaries and my wife's birthday, we tried a bit of everything.  Chef Hattie and the kitchen once again gave us the perfect ending to a night of delicious exploration.  If you come here, come to enjoy the experience.  We had a group of staff stop by to assist in water or removing used plates, bring out new utensils for every course.  We greeted each and were pleasantly greeted and served in return.  It's hard to say if we like the food or the people more.  Can I just say both?  Rev.  #43

Twenty five months ago, I gave my very first Yelp review: the Loft at Traders Point.  I have been there a few times and usually get dinner and wander around the place, enjoying the experience seeing the cows and the dairy production.  I just realized when I was looking for a place to get ice cream that I had never reviewed the Creamery.  So after crossing the one lane bridge on Moore Rd, I turned into the private parking lot (gravel) and saw the Dairy Bar was open.  This small "shack" sits in front of the first floor entrance into the shop where Traders Point Creamery products are sold as "to go" items.  Inside, there are varieties of cheese and yogurt and just about anything dairy that can be made on the premises.  But today I was just hunting ice cream (also made here).  They don't have  infinite flavors, just some of the most popular.  I went with a single scoop (actually 3 small scoops) of chocolate chip mint ice cream that was delicious and perfect on a hot day.    Review #1115

I can't say how good the food is here since I had just finished eating across the street when I noticed this place.  I decided to try one of their smoothies.  No matter what flavor you order, they give you the option of making it juice or yogurt based.    The staff was prompt on taking my order (at the counter) and my wait was short as they finished someone else order before making mine.  The interior is small and cozy though it didn't get too loud.  Most folks were dining and managing their voice levels so that it seemed like if you found a spot, you could do a little work while consuming your purchase.  Review #3167

The service at the drive thru window (including the speaker system) were good. Even though we went for a quick lunch, there was no wait as we pulled up, placed our order, and pulled around to pay at the window.  There was minimal interaction in handling the food exchange and payment transaction, but I've yet to find a place that is 100% efficient on eliminating some sort of risk.  But this was as good as most places I've tried during the close down.  Although listed with an Indianapolis address, this is right along SR 67 near the southwest corner of I-465.  So, it's closer to Camby.  I had enjoyed KFC in my pre-Yelp days when I wasn't as aware of supporting small and independent businesses.  I was in the mood for some fried chicken and didn't feel like making it myself or going to the other place in my town that is known for their chicken.  So, I talked my wife into taking me to this closest location of KFC.  As I said earlier, the staff were friendly, the lot seemed pretty clean, and I liked that the speaker system worked well enough that we were able to understand our conversation with the staff inside.  We ordered a couple individual meals.  I got an original 2-pc with dark meat.  My wife ordered an extra crispy with light meat.  We both got the biscuits and mashed potatoes as our side.  There was minimal wait after we pulled around to pay.  It took about ten minutes to get home.  By then, my wife's extra crispy had become soggy, though the inside was a little dry.  My original seemed cooked properly with just a bit of crunch and with moist chicken inside.  The only problem is that the breading on the chicken was very bland (my wife's was quite spicy comparatively). We both liked our sides.  Were the mashed potatoes spectacular?  No, but for fast food, they were tasty, had a nice consistency, and the gravy was smooth and didn't overwhelm the potatoes.    I would have liked to give this place a better rating because of the service and sides, but considering this place is supposed to specialize in chicken, I have to say we were both disappointed in the flavor (and for her, the consistency).    I rarely rate fast food restaurants particularly when they are chains.  But this one would have gotten a better rating for the service, but a lower rating based upon the chicken.  I probably won't rush back due to that discrepancy between food and service.  But if you are in a hurry, it's a nice option to consider.  Just be careful pulling out of the parking lot since that is one busy stretch of highway.  Review #3772

Having enjoyed a previous evening meal at Spoke & Steele, my wife and I decided to bring a long-time friend from Northern Illinois to brunch.  We weren't sure what time she would arrive, so it was fortunate that this upscale restaurant was open from early in the morning through late into the evening without any down time!  It turned out to be a perfect choice.  Arriving somewhere around 11 a.m., we got our choice of seats in the dining area near the bar.  We placed our beverage orders and selected a pastry basket to start on while looking over the menu.  The pastries were four small sized options including a cinnamon, a raspberry, an apple, and a pecan variety.  All had good flavor (I didn't get to try the cinnamon one because my wife nabbed that one as soon as we peeled back the cloth covering.)  The main courses or "Large Plates" were a series of familiar breakfast options elevated to the best quality and presented with an eye for whetting the appetite.  I was intentionally hungry going in because I wanted to try a couple of the large plates this Saturday morning.  For my choices, I selected the Amelia's Brioche French Toast - orange butter, strawberry danish dessert cream, bourbon syrup (the toast was light and delicious even before I used the syrup and butter.)  The strawberry cream was perfect for these thick cut slices.  My other choice was the S&S Organic Eggs with applewood bacon, hash browns, & whole grain toast.  I chose my eggs over easy and didn't even use the variety of jellies that accompanied the dish.  I used the bread to mop up the egg yolk that broke over my hash browns and onto the plate.  Excellent choices for me!  My wife went for the Cheese Omelette that came with steckler cheddar, hash browns, and her choice of the rye toast.  She seemed to really enjoy the flavor of the cheddar eggs.  I wasn't as big of a fan as she was on the bite she shared with me, but she really thought they were good, especially with a little extra table salt.  Our friend went with the Pork Belly Benedict with poached egg and citrus hollandaise with hash browns.  She commented that the hollandaise was delicious.  The pork belly portion was generous as well.    Oh, and the coffee was just right.  I like mine black, so I found the taste was robust enough to stand up to the entree flavors but very smooth.  Service was prompt and efficient.  Maybe it could have been a little more inviting since we were the only ones dining at that early lunch hour, but our coffee was kept topped off and my wife's request for salt, ketchup, and a soda to replace the iced tea were handled immediately.  I am looking forward to returning soon when the next Devour Downtown is available for dinner.  Review #77

Sometimes I walk in a store and get this sense of delight just from being there.  In addition to eating at lots of places, I usually do the cooking at my home and so I enjoy going into specialty stores that serve those of us who enjoy cooking and like finding new gadgets and spice combinations to experiment with.  This store is also nicely spaced with a bit more room to move around than their competitor in the Fashion Mall.  And though they don't have as many mixes/sauces/etc as the other, I still felt that the place has a lot to offer (huge selections of knives and cutting boards!).    I also felt this place was more welcoming than the competitor where I sometimes am not acknowledged.    I couldn't help but notice the Cooking Classes room in the back which was well attended while I was browsing.  There seems to something different offered every single day, so if you have an interest in cooking, I encourage checking out their website or stopping by to pick up a schedule.  Classes aren't cheap, but you can target your specific interests to make it more affordable.  I ended up picking up a bottle of white balsamic vinegar to go with my Brussels Sprouts and sesame seeds at home.  I also found a Parmesan mix to go with my acorn squash that I am looking forward to trying.    Review #3670

While in the area, I noticed this bakery on the west end of the strip mall east of the Interstate on 96th.  I had been to and enjoyed my goodies from the original SweeTies near Broad Ripple (by Keystone Ave).    So, why pass up a chance to find something tasty?  I stopped in and was greeted right away.  The long, narrow shop has cases of baked goods on display on the left side of the store and a "menu" behind the counter on the wall.  They had lots of cupcakes piled high with frosting.  They also had a nice collection of brownies too!  I saw they had Turtle Brownies and decided that was what I wanted.  Now, I am sure I could eat this all by myself, but it was about 4x4 and rather thick, so I was a gentleman and shared it as an after dinner dessert with my wife.   It was full of flavors that you expect from a chocolate turtle, and was surprisingly lighter than most brownies (more cake like than brownie).  I am all about not feeling full after sweets, so that was a plus for me!  The ladies working there were friendly and helpful.  I found that this location had only been open a couple years, so everything was in good shape and clean.  I didn't check into their full sized cakes, but from the photos I've seen, they seem to be quite good at making those too!  Review #3724

A new home decor shop opened in Mooresville that has a variety of arrangements, accessories, pottery, knick knacks, and furniture.  They sell oils and narrative plaques.  Just a wide variety of items.  The general character of the shop is rural/comfortable living.  The shop is located in the shopping center where the local cinema can be found. It faces SR67, but you have to enter at the light and then drive to your right to get here.  Once you drive to the storefront, there is plenty of parking.  The shop has a lot of room to grow.  There was space at the back, and even in the middle of the shop, there is plenty of space between the aisles.  There were two people working when I entered and they greeted me even though they were still working on arrangements.    If you are looking for someplace new to get ideas for your home, why not stop by!  Review #2145

My wife and I headed north with a friend for a Monday night early (5 pm) dinner.  We found parking in the large lot near the entrance and went into the restaurant.  Our first impression is that all the walls are black but richly decorated with Italian art work.  Bar on the left, dining on the right.  We were greeted immediately and without reservations, were seated along the front windows (which had the blinds pulled).  The overall atmosphere was elegant and the light Italian music in the background was just loud enough to be heard without blocking conversation.  This was our first time at the restaurant, so Chelsea did an excellent job welcoming us and answering questions about our beverage selection, offering suggestions when asked for recommendations (all were excellent!)  She brought out a bread course (complimentary) to go with the infused olive oil on the table while we reviewed the dinner options.  When it came time to order, we were impressed with the numerous "specials" in addition to the standard menu.  We ordered two of those.  Let me say now that I was very pleased with the flavors of EVERYTHING I sampled.  Between the three of us, here is what we ordered:  Antipasti course:  Gamberi Alla Griglia - Large gulf shrimp wrapped with prosciutto served over field greens tossed with herb-infused olive oil, garlic and tomatoes.  Great flavors of shrimp and crisped prosciutto.  Even the greens were tasty.  Insalate course: Special - Heirloom tomatoes over field greens with a balsamic reduction and burrata cheese.  Sweet tomato flavors blended with the balsamic perfectly...Delicious...and the burrata (think mozzarella with a light creamy inside) was a great addition.  I ordered the special ravioli dish of the evening:  Tortellini with Osso Buco (veal shank) stuffing in a marsala sauce with rosemary.  Again, the pasta could not have been prepared any more perfectly with just enough veal stuffing to match the rosemary and marsala sauce.  My wife ordered the Penne alla Emiliana - penne served with a sauteed Italian Sausage, prosciutto, and caramelized red onions in a tomato and butter sauce.  I loved the different tastes in every bite depending upon the combinations I picked up with each fork full.    Our friend ordered the Spaghetti Fra Diavlo - Spaghetti served with sauteed gulf shrimp in a spicy garlic tomato cream sauce.  This had some heat to it, but was probably more "one note" on flavor than the multi flavored entrees that we ordered.  And to finish off, I ordered the Bomba Spumoni - spumoni ice cream (chocolate, cherry, and pistachio) wrapped in dark chocolate with a white chocolate drizzle.  Delicious.  The gals ordered the Bomba Gelato - raspberry, mango, and passion fruit filling wrapped in white chocolate.  They wouldn't let me have a bite!    A fabulous evening of enjoyable atmosphere, food, service, and friendship.  We spent two hours from the time we arrived until we finished off our beverages, but it seemed like no time at all.  It made it worth the 50 minute drive and facing rush hour traffic!  We will definitely return.  Review #49

I was in the KatC area to catch an afternoon movie, so I decided to stop by a couple independent places to grab a snack and a lunch.  I had seen the high Yelp rating for this place, but honestly, I wasn't sure I "got it".  I can't say that I've ever paired doughnuts and beer before.  I don't play a lot of board games unless the grand kids are spending the night, so playing games and eating donuts is also something I haven't done.  And while playing board games, I haven't really had beer or wine since I'm playing with the kids, so none of the main elements of this place seemed to go together for me.  After parking in the shared lot for this strip mall business, I entered and was surprised at how large it was.  High ceilings, large dining area, and a couple side rooms as well.  But the place was empty at lunch time on a Monday.  There were two staff waiting behind the counter which has the doughnut display on the left, then the coffee, and the alcoholic beverages to the right.  Instead of rows of donuts to trigger your hunger, they had a sample doughnut of each type.  Shy of a dozen varieties too, so the display case looked as empty as the seating area.  It just felt weird like a place going out of business rather than one that was trying to bring people in.  I decided to order a couple bismarks and got them to go.  I ordered the Blueberry filled bismark with lemon basil.  I will say that the place must have read other reviews because my bismark was filled to bursting!  Every single bite had the blueberry filling.  It was a little thin and runny (i.e. messy) so they could work on that.  And the flavor was okay.  Nothing funny tasting, but the blueberry filling tasted more sweet than berry.  I also ordered the Cannoli Bismark.  This was stuffed with a cheesy cream like an Italian cannoli would be.  It was topped with chocolate and a yellow fine grind that may have been lemon zest.  I liked it, but my wife tried it at home and was not a fan.  For me, a decent selection with an apt title, but nothing special to go out of my way for.  I didn't try any of the beer or wine offerings or even the coffee.  I also would say that unless you just want to pick up some donuts to go, plan on coming with a group of friends/family that like playing board games.  Otherwise, there isn't much going on here.  Review #3299

After seeing a banner posted over the patio facing SR 267 (Quaker Blvd), I was curious if this new restaurant was any good.  So, I decided to catch lunch there last Tuesday.  It's a good thing they have a banner/sign on the back.  Otherwise, I might never have been aware of them.  Located between Hadley and Reeves Rd, I turned east on Hartford Avenue and then north on Cambridge Way to pull into the shopping plaza on the left.  There was plenty of parking out front so I made my way into the restaurant.  There are two main sections:  The dining room with table seating in the middle and booth seating on the sides; The bar which is on the north (right as you enter) that is only about half as big as the dining area (the kitchen fills the other part of the space).  A sign at the entrance listed all the lunch specials of the day. Seems like many of the common items were about $8.  I was greeted promptly and seated at one of the booths.    The interior is clean and bright with a bit of a pattern to the table tops, but otherwise, the place could pass for any standard diner.  No wild colors and images plastered on the walls or chairs.  Just tastefully done.  I was greeted by my waitress and she brought complementary salsa (decanter) and chips with my water.  I found the salsa to be quite good with just a hint of heat, but not enough to alienate most diners.  The chips were fresh and the small decanter allowed me to fill the dipping bowl a few times.  Before I finished my chips, my lunch was served.  I had ordered the Burritos Tipicos with beef tips, in two flour tortillas and topped with burrito salsa.  There was also shredded lettuce, chopped tomatoes, and guacamole salad.  The flavor was really good!  The beef was very tender and moist.  The dish also comes with a chicken option as well.  The portion size was huge, so I made the smart choice (for my waistline) and got a to go box for the second burrito.  (My wife grabbed the box out of the frig and said it was still delicious as she was heading out the door, so it makes for good leftovers!)  Friendly service, short wait times, and good food made for a pleasant dining experience.  Not a lot of atmosphere, but I didn't sit in the bar or on the patio either.  Maybe my next visit will allow me to explore.  Review #3109

I really enjoyed my rainy day lunch at Fitzgerald's.  Since I got here late in the lunch hour, there was no line at the counter.  I was greeted as I entered and was directed to the menu on display to the left of the service counter and towards the daily specials written on mini blackboards on the counter.    Once I stepped back to the counter, I was greeted again and placed my order.  They have both dine in and carryout.  I opted for the dine in and after paying for my order, was directed to the drinks (self help water & teas, canned sodas.)  While waiting for my order, I noticed a number of cool & vibrant art pieces hanging around the shop.  Turns out that Kyle Fitzgerald not only works here, but does all the paintings too.  (Most are for sale.)    Before long, my order was brought out to me:  Cubano sandwich with real Cuban bread; potato salad (with red skin potato chunks and spicy brown mustard or maybe horseradish), potato chips, and they tossed in some Mac & Cheese to sample (I think it was because I traveled 50 minutes through the rainstorm to get here! ha!)  Everything was tasty and fresh and worth ordering.  I have had a number of Cuban sandwiches in my day, most not making much effort to be authentic.  But this was prepared with the right ingredients, still warm and moist, with a nice crunch to the outer crust of the bread.  Yum!  The mac and cheese had a solid cheese flavor without being too gooey or too dry.  The potato salad had enough spice to give a quick jab to the taste buds, but not so strong as to grow overwhelming, especially when paired with the sandwich.      I was pleased to see that all the folks behind the counter were pleasant and engaged the customers in what seemed a genuinely positive manner.      They also have four standard salads, 7 sandwiches, soup, and cookies available.  So, a nice variety of options for returning customers.   The dining room is on the small side, but fortunately, in summer months there is additional outdoor dining on the east side of the building that is covered by the roof overhang.  I noticed several of the patrons were dining outside watching the rain fall while staying dry.    For customers dining in, each table has additional napkins and silverware available in a jar. There is a collection spot near the door for dropping off your trash and returning your serving tray and utensils.    If you are not familiar with the area, you can take I-465 to the east side and get off on 56th Street.  Take 56th east to Post and turn north (left on Post).  The first stop sign is Otis (turn right).  About a block and a half east on Otis, you will see Cafe Audrey on the left.  Pull into the parking lot just passed the Cafe and you will see Fitzgerald's.  (There is no sign pointing to the parking lot/restaurant on Otis). It is worth the drive!  Review #340

Note:  Review is for the Palladium Theater only  I had only been to the Palladium Theater once before and that was for a Christmas movie.   So, I was anxious to hear a live concert and found an opportunity to hear Boney James play some new Jazz music from his latest album.  The theater is arranged in five levels with floor seating, box seats up the sides, and more boxes and a gallery of seating at the rear.  Buying tickets is easy, but figuring out exactly where you will be seated is confusing.  I saw a number of people directed to one spot, only to move later because they were in the wrong section.  Don't get me wrong, the volunteers were very helpful and pleasant, but even they were struggling with getting people in the right places.  I will definitely agree that the place is beautiful and climate controlled without having lots of noise from heating and cooling systems.  Very comfortable climate for watching even as the place filled.  The place holds up to 1600 fans if you count the additional seating behind the stage.  They do have elevator service, but if you can take the stairs, especially when the show is over, you will save a lot of time.  They do let you into the venue ahead of time, but you can't get to your seats until a half hour before the show starts.  A chime goes off and that alerts the ushers to let you in.  In the meantime, you can find the coat check or get a cocktail/beverage while waiting.  I had a seat towards the back of the theater in the fifth level boxes....i.e. the cheap seats.  I was impressed by how close I was to the stage and I could see most of the stage while seated, but if the performer went to the nearest end of the stage, I had to lean forward to see him.  If that is a concern, I would suggest getting a lower level seat to have better angles...I guess you get what you pay for.  Parking is free at three parking garages within a couple blocks.  There is also free street parking, but don't count on that unless you are extremely lucky.  The do have valet service available and a separate entrance on the west side if you have accessibility concerns.  Anyway, the whole experience was enjoyable.  I think the only disappointment was that the vocals and when the artist spoke were garbled.  I had trouble hearing what was being said, but I suspect that was the sound engineer's fault, not the facility's.  I am going back in a couple weeks.  If the problem occurs again, then I will adjust my rating.  Review #1755

Fresh, baked to order pizza and garlic bread are available at this Avon branch of Magoo's.  Located on the northwest corner of Ronald Reagan and US 36, it helps to be headed west bound to avoid having to turn across heavy traffic and/or cars backed up waiting for the light to change.  (There is a turn lane in the middle, so take advantage of that if you can.)  The parking lot out front is limited in size and unfortunately, there is no place else to park since there is no side street or street parking available.  I grabbed the last spot (maybe it wasn't actually a spot) and headed into the spacious dining area.  An order counter is at the back of the space and I was greeted promptly.  I wanted to get a pizza to go and also an order of garlic bread (they don't carry traditional bread sticks.)  The wait was only about 15 minutes.  I ordered a medium Supreme Pizza with my choice of sauce.  I went with tomato based, but could have ordered garlic sauce, or half and half.  The pizza was sliced into 10 wedges and were very uniformly dressed.  The crust was sturdy without being tough or brittle.  The restaurant uses only Halal quality products, so you won't find bacon or ham or pork sausage (if I understand it correctly.)  But there was plenty of meat and veggies on the pizza.  Really good!  The garlic bread has two half loaves that are sliced into three pieces each.  Each piece had plenty of cheese and garlic flavor with the bread having a soft texture.  I especially liked that it had a bit of dipping sauce, but it is a bit difficult to fit the bread into the small plastic cup for the sauce.  All in all, the pizza and side were very good and if you can time it when the parking is open, it is worth stopping by.  They do have delivery in the area as well, so maybe that is a better option for you.  Review #2935

It was over seven years since I last dined at PF Chang's, and this latest visit will probably be my last.  The food was okay, though some of the pairings were odd.  It was mainly a management and service issue that made for an unpleasant visit.  I hate going to meals in large groups because it always, ALWAYS brings out the worst in service.  Our group of 13 which had reservations, was assigned a single waiter to serve us on a Sunday afternoon.  (He also had a 6 top and two 4 tops as well.)  No busboys.  No one to help on water glasses.  Just a little help when the food was brought out.  This is bad management to not have anyone help on a large group.    And as much as I wanted to have sympathy for our server, he made a lot of mistakes in his organizational skills that kept putting him farther behind and keeping our table waiting so that our lunch took a full two hours.  We tried telling him at the beginning who was on the same bills.  He didn't want to hear it until the end.  We couldn't even get water until the last couple arrived, so we then had to wait for our beverages.  (I got one replacement glass of water in the entire 2 hours.)  We asked for our bills, he had them in his hands, and without delivering them, went to take another order, then logged it in, then brought out our bills.  Why didn't he drop off our bills, then go take the order while we filled out the tips and payment?  Items like additional drinks or "to go" boxes were just not delivered.  We ended up having to go to the bar for additional drinks and get our own boxes from a service counter.  Just horribly inept service and no clue that things were going bad.   It's sad when you go out to celebrate an occasion and all everyone talks about is how bad the service was.  I never did see anyone from management come by to see how things were going.  We were just glad to get out of there before dinner.  Done...finished...won't be back.  And I think I'll turn down any invitations to large gatherings from now on.  Review #2348

If you like a touch of nostalgia, okay, a lot of nostalgia, with your fine dining, then this is a place to check out!  Geraldine's Supper Club & Lounge was only open about a week before my visit, so I wanted to check it out for myself since there weren't a lot of reviews.  Great steaks!  Solid service & cocktails!  and hearty sides and appetizers that aren't fancy, but are pretty good.  Just north of the fountain in Fountain Square, the restaurant sits on the south east corner of English and Shelby.  In the evenings, there is street parking (free) along both sides of each cross street.  They open the bar at 4 and the restaurant begins taking orders at 5, so I arrived about twenty minutes to 5 to look around inside and order a cocktail.  The interior is somewhat dark and has a lot of unfinished walls in juxtaposition to the elegant black table cloths downstairs (white on the family/reserved room dining upstairs).  The bar has lots of seating and there is a row of 4-top tables downstairs as well.  They have a very large assortment of cocktails to choose from.  They are a bit pricey, but not out of line with the fine steaks that area available to pair with.  I went with a "Hemmingway Daiquiri" which has a bit of lime and grapefruit juice added and I was surprised that there wasn't any sour taste...mostly sweet flavors with a hint of tartness.  I ordered the Blue Crab Cakes as a starter and got two nice sized cakes with a half cup dipping sauce.  The cakes were the kind with shredded crab, sweet corn, and topped with what I would guess to be chopped pimento over a bed of arugula.  Nice flavor though the crab flavor was a little understated with the sauce and other ingredients.  A little on the soft side when served, so easily cut with a fork.  The star of the night was the 8 oz filet (the Oklahoma) which I upgraded to include a dish of sauteed onions on the side.  The steak was extremely tender and had just a bit of char on top.  The onions were sweet and paired excellently with the steak.  I also thought the presentation was enhanced by a pair of cooked cherry tomatoes.  (I hate getting a lonely looking steak on a plate with nothing else.  Nice to see color on the plate!)  The only negative was that the plate was a little messy from the sauce spreading out over the plate, but that wasn't a big deal.    I also ordered the sides of potato au gratin and the sauteed asparagus.  I didn't see the menu mention that these were shareable sizes, but probably should have guessed because of the prices for each.    The au gratin potatoes came in a bowl and had about a 6" square block of potatoes topped with cheese.  They were cooked perfectly and the cheese was soft and warm.  Nothing fancy, just a standard presentation.  I did think the potatoes were a bit under seasoned and for the price, I expected to be blown away.  Good, but not great.  I also thought the asparagus was good.  I got around 15 large spears that were sauteed until tender, not al dente.  I prefer my asparagus cooked to this level.  These, though served unadorned and not having additional seasoning, were cooked right to the point were they were done and not a second longer.  They held their shape yet were tender and warm.    The prices were in line with steak houses and I liked the sense of place.  Loved the vibe and music of the "rat pack" in the background.  Overall, if they can tweak the sides and appetizers to be on the same level as the steaks, they will get a 5-star rating.    Review #1527

This space is located a couple miles from my home, and so when I have a package that is ready to go (return postage guaranteed), I can simply walk in and place the item in a collection box in the lobby and trust that it will get there.   No line, no fuss.  The reason that I don't rate this place higher is because there doesn't seem to be enough help during the rush times and they don't have nearly the supply of inventory that the Greenwood UPS has.  This place has a cluttered/unfinished look to it and I've had difficulty finding shipping supplies that fit my needs.  The Greenwood UPS looks like it was designed with customers in mind and looks like a place that you can get a lot of things done besides simply shipping a package.  As I've said in the Greenwood review, I often drive the 10 miles instead of the 2 if I am going to need to deal with the service counter.    On my most recent visit, I was the only one in the place and I wasn't even greeted when I came in to drop off a prepaid package.  What happened to greeting customers?  It goes a long way if done properly.  Review #1993

New name, but the same great breakfast place as before!  Recently, the former Stacks Pancake House & Grill was purchased by the same owners as the next door Super 8 Hotel.  From what I can tell, no changes were made to the staff or the interior of the place.   Some of the menus still refer to the prior name, but new signs will be coming soon to announce the change of ownership to Star Pancake House & Grill.  I recently went with my wife and another couple to brunch here.  There was plenty of parking surrounding the restaurant and still room inside!  There was a short wait as the hostess who seats new arrivals also takes the payments at the end of the meals.  Before long, we were given our choice of booth or table.  The restaurant has a wide assortment of offerings as both meals and ala carte items.  My wife went with the Star Omelette which comes with hash browns.  I chose the Eggs Benedict and also had the hash browns.  The plates they serve on are huge, so there is plenty of room to mix and mash and sample someone else's food if they let you!  We both enjoyed our meals and my wife needed a to go box for hers.  Our friends even made special orders and the kitchen/waitress managed to do a great job on delivering what was requested.  Nice to know that the food is made to order, not something that was sitting under a heat lamp.    The coffee was fresh and kept coming throughout the meal too.  If they could figure out a way to smooth out the slight delay at the front between checkouts and arrivals, then this place would be even better.  Rev. #41

I love the new place and the potential to become even better!  This place is easier to find than the previous location and I can't wait for the warmer weather to come and allow the garage doors to open up to the patio.  The owner of Hoagies & Hops is the same, but this time, she's partnered with Chilly Water Taproom which shares the space on the other side of the wall.  At H&H, you can still get all the great sandwiches/hoagies/philly steaks and some new sides.  They even have some non-alcoholic beverages and cookies available.    Right now, they only have street parking, but it is free.  I grabbed a spot on 42nd without a problem.  For lunch, I ordered the Pitt Twist sandwich.  I went with the smallest version which is only 7" (they have two larger sizes!) and it was plenty to eat considering I got a side of Nan's Red Skin Potato Salad too.  The Pitt Twist comes with Black Forest ham, Provolone cheese, house slaw, crumbled potato chips, and mayo.  Yum!  The potatoes have nice chunks that spear easily and make for a nice bite.  I would have liked them with a hint more seasoning, but they were still good.  To order, simply checkout the menu board over the counter and let them know what you like.  They give you a number to take with you to your seat (if you are dining in) after you pay.  It doesn't matter if you sit on the restaurant side or the bar side...they can find you!  Great sandwich with high quality and lots of flavor.  Don't let the new location keep you from checking them out.   Rev. #40

On our return visit to 1911 Grill, we stopped in for lunch on a rainy Sunday (July 3).  My wife and I were greeted and shown to a seat in the spacious dining room near the window for viewing the indoor race tracks.    Although upbeat in approach, our service seemed to be a little on the inexperienced side of attention.  Simple things were missing like walking away before giving us a chance to comment or make requests; like bringing the check before asking if there would be anything else.  Nothing really negative transpired, but just not 5 star service.  I ordered something new this time, the Blackened Salmon with Cole Slaw.   I thought both were very good  and would order them on a future visit.  My wife ordered the Backfire Shrimp again.  When she asked for the sauce to be mild, the waitress didn't know that the sauce could be made to order.  (That is what we were told by the staff during our first visit.)  When there are multiple "backfire" items on the menu, it seems like the ability to request the heat level would be taught to all staff.   Fortunately, the request was communicated to the kitchen and my wife's entree came out fine.  Overall, we still enjoyed our visit and will return again.  Rev #4

While exploring the Garfield Park area, I used Yelp to help find this cool and unique boutique filled with old books and re-purposed items turned into note/sketch pads.  Located just across the street from the Garfield Park entrance on Shelby, I was able to street park right in front of the store.  The woman who owns/runs the shop was setting out her daily pink balloons to help customers find the shop.  Inside, the space is very small and has this nostalgic/vintage feeling to it.  There are lots of books that are over 100 years old and quite a few with Indiana ties.  But what really caught my attention was the supply of crafted notepads.  There were some spiral ringed pads that had old book covers.  Others that were larger may be used as sketch pads with old album covers trimmed to fit the pages.  Mini sized notepads were also available.  Some are lined, while others are just blank sheets.  Each had an elastic strap affixed to keep the pad closed.  I found one of the mid-sized ones with a hard cover showing some vintage fashion.  I have a pre-teen granddaughter that loves to design clothes and sew as well as draw/paint.  I thought a fashion covered pad would be a unique gift for Christmas.  Not too expensive, so it could be a stocking stuffer (although it might be just a bit too wide.)    The owner was very welcoming and personable and let me browse without making me feel watched over.  But as soon as I was ready, she stopped her other duties and made sure I didn't have to wait.    Now, I will have to check in from time to time to see if I can find something for my other granddaughter.  The place is small and though they had a nice representation of each sized item, space limits them to being able to have something for everyone.  So, you just have to know what your tastes are and keep an open mind.  I found the place to be quite unique and an enjoyable place to browse.  Review #3306

The worst thing about this place is that they make it so hard to decide what you want.  They are very helpful in answering questions and everyone I talked to was busy, but friendly.  Since I had trouble figuring what was in each display, I simply asked and they let me know.  I decided to go with a lemon blueberry scone which was fresh and tangy (Too many other places have scones that are dry and heavy.)    The star of my visit was the giant cinnamon roll that was as big on flavor as it was in size.  It was so good that I nearly had to arm wrestle it away from my wife just to get a couple bites!  She wanted me to go back downtown to pick up some more and declared it her favorite cinnamon roll ever!  First, the outside was crispy and a bit flaky, while still being light and filled with ample cinnamon flavor inside.  And the icing was light, not overpoweringly sweet like some places.  This was executed to perfection with a great balance that left us delighted with the flavor without feeling like we were suffering from a blood sugar overload.  I encourage you to grab one if they have them available.  Otherwise, my wife and I may come get them all! ;)  Review #2298

Wow!  I knew I was in for good food tonight, but seriously, "Wow!"  I made reservations for the chef's counter and got to watch my food being prepared.  Clockwork precision.  I had a cocktail, four courses and complementary dessert candies in 35 minutes!  I asked my waitress if I could get my courses staggered instead of brought out all at once and I never waited more than a couple minutes between courses.    And the staff kept an eye on me to make sure my water was topped off, my used plates were cleared, and my check processed with efficiency.   Pleasant attitudes from the moment I entered to the moment I left.  Even one of the line chefs asked how I was enjoying my evening during a momentary lull in the action (it was a Monday night, so the crowd was not huge at 6 p.m.)  And Chef Brooks was manning the "pass" to make sure everything that came out was right.   Okay, let's talk food.  I started with an amuse-bouche of Wild California Uni (sea urchin) Spoon.  When it was delivered, my server mentioned I should eat it as one bite and as soon as possible to get the best effect. (It has ice chips on top to keep the bite cool and add a little crunch to the multi flavor and multi textured bite.)  Great depth of flavors that I could eat a plate of those!  I moved on to the Wild Mushroom & Yellow Squash.  This was simply the best mushroom dish I recall ever eating.  Super savory flavors made the mushrooms taste like my steaks at home.  Pair that with the pickled cattails for acidity and a bit of tartness and then add a tarragon buttermilk sauce that added a creamy texture and that hard to describe tarragon flavor (is it sweet or licorice? somewhere in between?)  Anyway, delicious!  I moved onto the Squid Boudin.  The squid was two cross slices of tentacles that sat like cups filled with the squid ink sausage, and surrounded by caramelized sweet corn and sea beans.  The corn was addictive.  The sausage was loose (like a hash instead of compressed like a sausage) and had a brighter flavor than expected.  I finished off with the Pig Skin Pad Thai which is served in a bowl with chopsticks and topped with lots of peanuts (I had to breakdown and use my fork to get them all.)  A bit of heat and each bite was a little different depending upon which ingredients I picked up with my sticks.    Oh, and I also tried the Daydream cocktail made with rum, coconut rum liqueur, banane du Bresil, Sazon syrup, and lime juice.  Very tropical and a blend of sweet and tart.    I had a wonderful meal and nothing I ordered was over $17.  For those who complain about quantity and high prices for the area, I say "get over it".  This isn't typical food you find all over.  It is unique.  The ingredients are top quality.  And if you aren't full when you leave, try drinking more water.  I will gladly return.  Review #1041

My wife noticed this new restaurant on a morning news promotion, so when we were looking for something "new" to try, I suggested this place on SR135 near Main Street.  It occupies the spot of the former Stacked Pickle.  So if you know the spot, it is easy to get to and has plenty of parking.  I was surprised to see such a nice sized outside seating area too.   Although I have read some reviews that cited an odor from the nearby nail salon.  But upon our visit, we had nothing but pleasant aromas of Tex Mex food.  We were seated at one of the small tables in the bar area.  The only non pleasing aroma was when someone in our area ordered seafood and I could smell it as the waiter moved by our table.  To play it safe, I ordered the Steak Fajita and my wife the pork burrito.  She also tried a raspberry margarita that looked delightful.  Unfortunately, it was mostly ice and booze.  Just not enough flavor.  She didn't even finish it. My steak was tender and the fajita comes with lots of fixins to dress it up.  I got 3 five inch flour tortillas.  I also ordered the roasted street corn which was tough & chewy like it was either overcooked or was field corn instead of sweet corn.  The flavor was fine.  Mostly it was a texture thing.  Flavor was not a problem.  Portion size was more than either of us could finish.  With a bit of fine tuning, this place could be really good.  But there is a lot of competition in the category, so hopefully they will adjust quickly.  Review #3909

I had limited time left on my parking meter, so I decided to stop into the City Market for something quick.  I have been to quite a few of the restaurants/cafes inside, but realized I hadn't tried Mambo's yet.  It is located on the main floor of the central building near the southwest corner (near City Soups/City Sweets).  They actually have a rather large space in the Market.  They have a system where you order/pay on the south end and pick up your order when they call your name at the other end.  Your drink is given to you while you wait by the person who takes your order.  In between, the menu is listed over the windows that allow you to watch your order being made.  I went with the "Original" Cheesesteak which comes with beef, onion, and cheese on a bun.  When they called my name, the man working at that end asked which toppings and sauces I wanted added.  For my fries, he asked if I wanted them seasoned.  Napkins and other items are next to the pick up window.  My sandwich was large and sliced in half which made it easier to handle.  Lots of flavor and with so many options for what to add, it really depends upon what you add to dial in the taste.  I found mine to be quite good.  The fries were the shoe string type and when hot, were great!  Note that if you only eat part of your meal and take the rest home as leftovers, the fries get soggy from being in the same box as the sandwich, so I recommend eating the fries all in one sitting.  Friendly and helpful service at the counter.  A handy carrying box that can easily be transported to the upstairs seating or be used for "to go" orders.  Good value for the money, especially for downtown.  Parking is always hit or miss with pay parking along the side streets and a pay garage just north of the Market.  Review #3684

I had a very nice lunch at Manee Thai.  There was plenty of parking in the shared lot and though there was some outdoor seating in the front of the restaurant, I chose indoors.  I was greeted and shown to a table midway through the dining area.  The room was decorated with several paintings reflecting the Thai culture.  The tables each had a decoration beside the condiments.  Although there was a decent sized list of lunch specials, I decided to give the Pud See You (it's spelled differently at every restaurant!)on the main menu a try.  I liked that they asked if I wanted it lunch sized and when I said yes, I found that it still came with the appetizer of the day (egg roll on Wednesday), egg drop soup, and ginger side salad.  Soon, the soup and salad were brought out.  Though there was a LOT of ginger dressing on the salad, it wasn't overpowering and didn't affect the chilled iceberg lettuce.  Nice flavor.  The soup was good too and I was surprised it had a small amount of carrots and peas.  Nice texture on this hearty soup.  (I liked it enough to get a small cup to go for my wife!)  After a short wait, the entree and egg roll were delivered.  I was given the option to select a heat/spice level and went with #2 out of 4.  It was a level where my wife would have thought it too hot, and someone who likes it spicy would have thought it needed more.  I found it just right with a bit of a spicy tingle that added flavor without detracting from my enjoyment.  I will advise that both the entree and the egg roll were extremely hot (temperature wise) when delivered.  Not so much the meat and noodles, but the broccoli of the entree was still steaming and I needed a quick sip of water to take the heat down.  The same happened with my first bite of the egg roll..steam shot out of the veggies inside the crispy shell and I was grabbing the water again!  So, let those set a minute or two to avoid discomfort.  The egg roll was a okay and had a bit of a dipping sauce, but nothing out of the ordinary.  The entree was pretty tasty and I was pleased that the pork (my meat of choice that day) was done without becoming tough.  The only thing I didn't care for in the entree was that even though the menu describes it as having wide noodles (which are usually a bit thicker as well), the meal came with basic thin flat egg noodles.  Those just don't hold the flavor or have the texture that I've had at most of the finer Thai restaurants around town.  Still good, but just not at the same level as my favorite Thai places.  The service was fine, but the waitress didn't ask if I wanted anything else before dropping off the bill.  I had to ask her to add the "to go" small soup.   She took care of the adjustment efficiently and brought out the soup ready to go when she delivered the bill to be signed.   Nice recovery.  Overall, I had an enjoyable meal and thought the pricing very reasonable and the service quick enough that a visitor could easily dine in and still get back to work...if they have to!  Review #1213

My wife and I finally cut "the cable" from our service provider and they paid for shipping back the equipment we had used by using FedEx.  Since we only have places that are other businesses and handle FedEx shipping as a secondary job in our area, we headed to this Greenwood Location just north of the White River Library on SR 135 which is strictly a FedEx office that specializes in printing (not used on this visit but competitively priced) and shipping.  They had a lot of supplies on hand for visitors and lots of self help printers and even some small cubicles that I assume you can use to assemble your projects.  I walked in and was greeted.  I was carrying my returned equipment (didn't even have a box) and let the man behind the counter that I was returning the ATT equipment and had printed off the return label for him to use.  He verified the equipment was the same as what ATT was expecting, and said because they waited to ship the equipment (in bulk) when they had enough equipment to make it worth shipping.  In the meantime, I got a printed receipt that I had dropped off the equipment.  The whole thing took only a few minutes and I was happily on my way.  Because this was the only time I've been to this facility, I can't say how helpful the staff is on shipping without being an automatic return.  I also didn't use any of the printing, so a 4 star rating for the service and ease of returning I experienced.  Review #823

Depending upon the type of bar you like to frequent, your opinion of this place could vary widely.  I like going to places where I can see the labels on the shelves, where the volume is at a level where I can carry on a conversation, and the bartender is knowledgeable of his service and can help me learn more about what is available.  If you like a place that is a hole in the wall and is dark, noisy, and crowded, then this probably shouldn't be your first choice.  The bar is set in the middle of a large market space with a high ceiling, lots of folks strolling by looking for places to eat, and lacks a specific vibe that some bars have.  I found my drink to be very affordable compared to many bars downtown and though not served in a fancy presentation, there was plenty of kick in the cocktail and the flavor was quite tasty.  The bartender was quite knowledgeable about the type of booze I was looking for (gin) and had multiple options at different price points.  Seating was plentiful as it wrapped around the stall/shop.  They not only carried cocktails, but a variety of local brews and wine.  For a location with so many places to eat, I think they will do okay since there aren't many places on site to pick up alcohol.  If you are in the mood, stop on by and check it out!  Review #3949

This store has a bright and cheerful vibe filled with a small but diverse collection of well made items (per my wife's observation.)  It's easy to find if you go to the Coca Cola Bottleworks and see the signs for the Hotel, this store is just north of the hotel on the same side of the street.  Metered parking is available on Mass Ave or there are pay lots across the street and behind the "Garage".  I am not aware of any validating of your parking stub for this store.  You would have to ask.  Once you find it, the store feels fresh and new, is well lit, and seems to mirror the title "Good Neighbor" with quality items and friendly staff.
