Since it was a cold weekday just before lunch, there weren't any other customers, but the young lady who was working didn't hover over us but engaged us in conversation offering to help find anything we were looking for.  Basically, women's clothing is to the left as you enter and men's to the right.  They did have quite a bit of denim clothing, and lots of warm wear for getting us through the winter.  You can shop and then head over to the Garage Food Hall (located north of 9th street only) across Edison.  Or if you are curious, look into the lobby of the new Bottleworks Hotel which preserved much of the art deco facade.  It is a beautiful area to shop with everything clean and new, but paying homage to the past.  Check out Good Neighbor while in the area!  Review #3845

Overall, my wife and I enjoyed our carryout from Crustiez. The Hershey's ice cream is smooth and creamy and delicious. Highly recommended. I like that they offer a cracker crisp crust on the Tsunami pizza and that they asked if the thin crust was okay before they placed the order. My wife really likes the crispy crunch. She isn't a fan of the soggy fold over pizzas we've had elsewhere, so I think she was very pleased with the texture AND the flavor. So with great tasting pizza and Ice cream, why only 4 stars? Well when you have wings listed first in your name, due to a huge rush on wings the day before, as earlier as 4 pm on a Friday, they were completely out of wings. I think the manager needs to take the hit for not having more on hand. I was going to get a pound roughly 9 or 10 wings for my dinner, but ended up getting bread sticks to go with the pizza and ice cream we ordered. The bread sticks don't mention being garlic, but I could definitely smell the garlic when I opened the box. They offer a marinara and a cheese sauce for dipping. Both had a hint of spicy heat. I wasn't expecting that but it wasn't too hot for me, but my wife did not like either. There is plenty of parking in front of the building just off Southport Road, west of SR 37. We will return. When they first opened, they did not offer lunch hours, even for ice cream I will probably eat here more frequently now that they offer lunch hours . They offer (usually) a wide variety of wing flavors, so I hope they restock soon so I can give the place another try.  In the meantime, I can always swing by to grab some ice cream! Review #3914

Okay, if you can find this place, it is well worth the effort to get here and the promise of the new AMP (artisan Market place) that will be convenient for all the new businesses opening in the Tech 16 development.  First, Tech 16 is the west side of downtown's answer to the Bottleworks.  Lots of high tech jobs with lots of creative people will be located in the area north of the river just north of IUPUI.  The development is just west of the Riverside neighborhoods and will bring lots of jobs (within walking/biking distance) for locals.  Since this side of town doesn't have the amenities of food and shopping that downtown, Mass Ave, Ft Sq offer, the developers knew they needed to provide food and shopping to the employees who will fill the high tech jobs in the district.  The AMP (Artisan MarketPlace) is expected to be open before race day, I heard mid-May.  But you don't have to wait to explore.  Circle City Sweets is already open on site.  For now, there is limited free street parking out front, but a new side road will be built to give access to a 1000 space parking garage behind the complex.     The bakery is still run by the same folks who had the shop in City Market, so you know it is so good.  The only negative I had was that they don't sell beverages here.  Good thing Tinker Coffee should be one of their new neighbors in the AMP.   Okay, from downtown, take Indiana Avenue northwest over the River.  Just before you get to 16th Street, turn left (south) at Gent Street and it goes right to AMP and Circle City Sweets.  Go now to avoid the rush and grab one of the free parking spots on Gent.  Just follow the signs into the bakery.  Prices are reasonable for the high quality pastries.  Note that this isn't a donut shop.  There are plenty of those elsewhere, but if you want something really good, stop by here.  Rev #59

I wish I had found this store when I was able to do more hiking and exploring around the state.  When I walked into this spacious shop that had a lot of clothing suitable for hiking and for promoting our state's parks and places to explore, I felt drawn to browse the items which also include handy stuff for taking with on a hike.  Check it out for yourself to see what you always wished you had with you.     The store is spacious so I did not feel crowded by other shoppers.  The checkout is on one end (south) and the woman working didn't greet me or leave the counter the entire time I was browsing.  I wasn't planning on hiking soon, so I ended up leaving without making a purchase, so I can't say how easy that process is.     I liked that the logos on the clothing were promoting local sites and places to visit.  I enjoy wearing that type of clothing, especially while out on an adventure.     If you are still in your adventure seeking years, be sure to check this place out for supplies and clothing to make you look like you know what you're doing!   Review #3873

While downtown, I decided to try something familiar (the former Acupulco Joe's location) but new.  There is still a lot of the familiar Joe's decor.  There is a lot of booth seating so plenty of spacing when we visited during the week for lunch.  The food was quite tasty and since the place was relatively low on customers, our  waitress did a fine job getting our orders taken, delivered and our bill without any long delays.     I ordered a manager's special with steak and found the strips of steaks to be tender but with enough char to bring out the beefy flavor.  My wife ordered a lunch Chimichanga that was large enough for her to ask for a to go box for what she didn't finish.  She really liked that the chicken was cut into strips, not shredded.  Her only problem was that she found it had a bit too much spicy heat for her, (I didn't think it was hot at all) but she said it was a cumulative heat that got to her.   We didn't order anything from the bar, but they do have options available.  We also didn't check out appetizers or other options since the lunch meals seemed plenty.  Mine came with spanish rice and pico de galo that were really good and the veggies fresh.     I know there are lots of Mexican food options around the metro area, but if you are downtown and want some good food at a reasonable price with good service and plenty of room inside.  Parking is limited to metered street parking and just watch out for bus lanes and bicycle lanes which can be confusing for folks not familiar with downtown.  Lots of one way streets to be aware of on your way over here.    I know Joe's had a lot of history, but I think this food is better than what I remember getting at the former establishment.    Review #3889

If you are strictly looking for hardware, I will say that there are numerous big box stores that have more items.  But if you are looking for a place to get Christmas items (trees, lights, outdoor items, and ornaments), then this beats them all!  After pulling into their parking lot along Keystone, I entered the north side of the building and made my way passed the checkout line (you wait your turn in one line and go to the next available counter when it opens.)  Most of the hardware, along with some snack items, are towards the check out counter.   But as you work your way back through the multiple display rooms, you see more and more Christmas items and displays (at least during my visit.)  There were lots of trees at the back of the first main area.  Once I passed through the doors, I found a miniature train display for kids to watch, Sully's Grill for grabbing a snack, and more Christmas stuff along with some outdoor barbecue equipment (Big Green Egg is really popular here.)  Beyond that room, there is more stuff for garden, though it was not stocked during December.  (You also enter the Yellow House for home decor items via the garden area.)  Overall, I encountered friendly folks who actually responded when a customer asked questions.  Review #3438

The food was fine and once we were eventually seated, the wait times on our order wasn't very long considering it was a Sunday brunch and the place was packed.  I expected there to be a wait because of the time we chose to come here.  However, it's like the place has no management paying attention.  They did close some tables down near the entrance because of the backlog of people standing in a crowd at the entrance.  We managed to get through the pack and get our name on the list for people waiting tables.  There was a 15 to 20 minute wait and we knew there would be something similar on a Sunday if we tried someplace else, so since we had our vaccines and it has been 2 weeks and we had our masks on, we waited.  There was no line. Just random people.  Some were waiting to get on the list, while others were waiting for their name to be called and others were trying to pay their bills all at the same spot.  You would think they could have some plan in order.  Someone on their staff could be taking names of guests at one of the empty tables near the entrance and they could have taped lines on the floor for that group.  They could also take cell phone numbers to call people when their table was ready.  The folks could wait in their cars and free up the cluster of people blocking the entrance which would open more tables since they were closed because of the close proximity to the pack standing there. They could also have the waitresses take the bills to a register and someone could ring up the orders while the customers waited at their tables.  Less people crowding the checkout/checkin/waitlist pack. When finished I went to pay my bill and stood off to the right of the cashier and someone walked up right infront of the cashier and handed his card and receipt ahead of me.  He was huge, so I didn't want to start something I couldn't finish, so I waited.  When I was directly in front of the cashier behind the big guy, by the time he tucked his wallet in his pocket and turned around, someone came up from the dining side and without even looking at me, the cashier took the "cutter's" card and bill.  I finally got right in front of the cashier and forced my card as the person behind the cutter tried to ignore my position.  Hey manager...you have a mess at your front door and are no where in sight.  Add to that that some customers were just roaming around without masks.  I don't know what the local rules are here, but being a decent human being should still matter and covering your face and waiting your turn should still matter.  Without some management to 'manage', it was just chaos and a place I'm not likely to return unless I know some changes are made for the better.  There are just too many places that have similar quality brunch offerings to put up with this mess.    It's a shame because our waitress was doing a good job not only covering her tables, but having to cover for a no show (or someone on staff who left early.)  It took a long time for her to circle back to refill my coffee, but she heard me say please bring my check and she did that fairly promptly.    I think if we would have gone on a different day or at a later time, it may not have been as hectic as it was during our visit.  They have a wide selection of food to choose from, but the weird checkin and checkout didn't make a good first OR last impression.  Review #3902

Maybe it was a case of having our expectations too high for a restaurant that has only been open a short while.  This is the newest of the CRG line and we have been fans of most of their line.  For a long time, Vida was our favorite of all restaurants, so if that is a 5, you can understand why this has a lower rating.  I think that when we return in the near future (yes, it has that much potential), they can iron out a few kinks and earn a higher rating.  We made reservations so that we could be assured of seating together with our friends as they celebrated their 54th anniversary and I approach my 1 year anniversary after my brain surgery.  So a big thank you to Modita for honoring both couples with a complementary dessert.  Fortunately, they let us know that so that we saved room for dessert after multiple courses.  Be aware that when you order, they want you to order all your courses except dessert up front so that the kitchen can minimize your wait times between courses and minimize the occurrence of your food growing cold.  Between the two couples, we ordered multiple items from each course and gave them a challenge.  Unfortunately, one of the entrees, the Amish Chicken  Yakitori did arrive cold (not just warm, but our friend said it was cold and my wife confirmed.  To their credit the waitress offered to replace it or comp it.  It was still tasty so she decided to go ahead and eat it (it was cooked, but had just grown cold) so she wouldn't have to make the rest of us wait.  Most of the food was excellent and worth trying.  We did have a few minor issues.  The A5 Wagyu Strip Steak (not upgraded to "Japanese" for another $20) was delicious but more chewy than I expected for Wagyu.  I realize a strip steak isn't going to be as tender as a filet, but I thought it would be more tender.  The group thought the Bao Buns were the best surprise.  I was last to try them from the shared plate and found mine to be way too smoky.  No one else seemed to notice anything but a hint of smoke.  I didn't want to finish it since I am not a fan of smoky flavor.  I prefer grilled taste.  My wife finished mine and commented that it was substantially more smoky than her piece which she found excellent.  I wish I would have enjoyed the dish as much as they did, but something in the kitchen must of caused my meat (pork belly) to become overly smoked.  Hopefully, as the kitchen gets settled, they will keep better balance across the dish.  We also tried the Maine Lobster Rangoon and my first piece smelled and tasted "fishy".  My second one was much better.  My friend let me sample his Bison short rib Bulgogi and it was delicious.  I also ordered the Short Rib Gyoza which was yummy and came with a sauce that was sweet and hot (not too hot for me, but too much for my wife's palate.)  My friend and I both ordered Gin and Tonics with Hendricks gin.  Excellent flavors.  I also tried one of the fruity house cocktails, the "Cuddle Magic" that was delicious.  Pay attention to prices as each couple's bill went up over $100 despite the comped food.  There are so many delicious items to choose from and even the cocktails were $14 each.  Oh well, we were celebrating and having a great time.  Our waitress Cora did a wonderful job of taking care of us throughout the evening though our request to turn the volume down on the music only yielded turning down the lights. ha!  I mentioned we were there to eat and talk, not dance.   I am sure that in a short amount of time the CRG people will iron out the minor issues we encountered.  My wife would also like to request a hand rail be installed for people who don't want to walk to the end of the ramp just to get back to the entrance.    We are definitely going to give Modita another chance soon.  Note that they don't comp your parking like the shops/restaurants in the Garage do.  That would be nice too!  We weren't able to find any available street parking at our visit, but were able to grab a convenient space in the surface lot across the street and north of 9th.  They have automated machines which need fixing because the audio says one thing and the message that you read says something else.  I finally gave my card to my friend and said to read the machine and not listen and it worked.  Not Modita's problem.  Just wanted you to be aware of parking for the restaurant.  Review #3903

Since we live roughly an hour away, I like when a restaurant delivers on taste and service.  This was our first visit to this restaurant and my wife and I enjoyed our lunch.  We were greeted and because there was so much room inside the two indoor dining rooms (one has the bar) we got to pick our own booth.  They offered the scan with your phone menu, but because they have such an extensive menu of ala carte items, we asked if they had printed menus (I carry my own hand sanitizer just in case).  Menus made it easy to check out ingredients as well as names and photos...the phone versions are too small for me to see much.  Thank you for offering the real menu option.  Before long we were able to place our order including my wife's strawberry daquiri.  She likes them frozen and said it was good, but just a little tart (sour in her words) and fairly strong in ABV.  Didn't stop her from enjoying it!  She ordered the lunch Chimichanga with chicken and the tortilla unfried.  Seemed tasty.  I went with the El Lago Bowl with steak.  Nice flavoring on the steak strips and plenty to eat when combined with the rice and avocado and black beans, pico de galo, and sour cream.  The steak strips were just a tiny bit dry on their own, but when mixed with everything else, were pretty good!  There was a decent sized crowd for a lunch, but because there is so much space, we felt comfortable dining inside.    While there, take time to notice the beautiful wall mural by Nekoda Witsken in the dining room (non bar area).    We are not in the Geist area often, but I would gladly return to El Lago (the lake) for lunch or dinner.  Review #3878

The shop is one of those places that is fun to browse and is affordable enough to pick up some items that catch your eye.  If you like vintage items like t-shirts of places you visited when you were younger, or if you like the non-typical sports wear of local teams, both pro and college, The Shop is a good place to start.  It also promotes the points of interest, parks, and festivals of he area too.  I was surprised I had not reviewed the Shop yet because I definitely have been before.  My confusion caused me to not take photos in store or of the store front, so you'll just need to go see for your self.  I picked up several items and they seem to be of good quality.  Although parking is always challenging in BR, I grabbed lunch at Union Jacks next door and then walked over the the Shop.  When I first discovered the Shop, it has been years and they had less competition for this niche market, so I was wowed back then.  Now, with so many online places, the selection isn't quite as unique.  But if you like the actual shopping experience, I highly recommend stopping by.  Service was helpful too.  Note that they have two front doors and if one is locked, try the other if you know the store hours indicate they are supposed to be open.  MY wife noticed and so we were able to enter and browse/purchase.  If you want to get out and do a bit of shopping, it makes sense to give a place called "The Shop" a try.  You may find a nice gift for a friend or for yourself!  Review #3948

What an eclectic mix of offerings for a small independent restaurant (I believe so!) that serves so quickly that we had hardly any wait in the drive through lane.  Amazing!  Though they do have some indoor dining, we decided to get ours to go through the drive up.  We both ordered Greek food, though they have traditional Americana food, and some Mexican items too.  I got the Chicken Gyro plate which has the Chicken gyro AND a small Greek Salad with Tzatziki sauce on the side.  My wife just wanted the sandwich.    We waited until we got home to eat but the sandwiches remained hot.   I forgot how large and filling a gyro can be.  These portions were plenty!  In fact, trying to pick them up and fold them over to eat was a challenge they have so much stuff on them.  I do wish they would cut the green peppers and onions a little smaller.  I like my toppings to compliment, not dominate the meat portion of the sandwich.  So, after removing some of the large pieces, and adding the sauce, we were able to enjoy our meal.  I will admit I settled down with a knife and fork to cut the gyro down to a more manageable size and less mess at the table.  ha!  Good taste and really fast service.    Nice tip:  Although this shop is located on a busy section of East Washington Street, you can cross lanes without worrying about being blocked by a raised median strip by the entrance/exit.  Just watch traffic since it can get busy here!  Nice to know that if you change your mind for what sounds good, they have multiple options to choose from.  Review #3887

A nice place to stop for a cup of coffee and to grab some tasty pastries.  It is so nice to see some of the vacated shops in Irvington have new businesses jump in to keep this mini strip at the intersection of Audubon and Bonna Avenues stay full and doing good business.  This location has its own parking lot in front and used to be home to Tyner Market and The Mug.  Now, along with Heartbreaker and Strange Bird, the space is filled with food and beverage places and has become a destination for the historical area that is vibrant and current!  After some morning business downtown, I suggested to my wife we try something new to us and headed back to our old stomping grounds of the east side in Irvington.  The store doesn't have much signage on the building, but there is a street sign to help you find it.  Inside, the place has a fascinating ceiling that you'll have to check the photos or go in person to believe.  Not your average coffee/pastry shop.  They have a pastry counter and the items are clearly marked so you can maintain social distancing while deciding.  One of the strong plusses for me was that my plain black coffee (my go to for every new coffee place I try) was a nice medium roast and was immediately drinkable.  No burned tongue to throw off my tastebuds.  So glad to find this place.  My wife ordered a chocolate Croissant which was light on the chocolate, but otherwise good.  I also ordered a Blueberry Scone which had nice taste and texture...not all dried out like some bakeries I've been to.  The line moved quickly and checkout was quick and easy too!  Multiple options on how you want your receipts are available too.    My wife commented how she wished we had something like this closer than 45 minutes from our house and she might take up drinking coffee! ha!  Review #3885

What a breath of fresh air for a neighborhood that is steadily becoming a place on the rise.  This house turned bar is located on East Street between Morris and Raymond with free street parking along each side.  I grabbed a spot for an early dinner (lunch hours are being considered soon.)  There are a couple steps up into the entrance and the door is heavy and needs a good pull to open (it also needs a guide on the top to keep it from slamming shut.)  Entering, you step into a lobby area with the family dining area to your left and the bar area straight ahead.  The dining area is mostly four top tables and there is a TV on one wall.  Music is piped in fairly loud, but patrons seemed to be able to talk over it.  The bar area is a bit small with some additional seating at tables.  Unfortunately, several patrons decided to stand right at the bar entrance and made it difficult to approach.  The good news is that the owner is really trying hard to make each visit a positive one for his guests.  He was running the bar and still found time to come out to where I had grabbed a table in the dining area to take my food and beverage orders.    I started with one of the draft beers (they also have bottles, cans, wine, and cocktails).  I then ordered a cup of Chicken Velvet soup which was the SotD.  Excellent.  Plenty of seasoning/salt but without overwhelming the chicken flavor.  The chicken was in chunks which really was appreciated.  Croutons were floated on top of the soup as well, so lots of texture from the bites and creaminess.  I also ordered the Italian Melt sandwich and got the cole slaw side.  The slaw was unsweetened and the non-creamy style, so it was a little surprising, definitely unique to my dining experience, but still quite good.  The star was the sandwich.  It came toasted and sliced on the bias along with two pickled peppers and a dill spear.  I would best describe the taste as that of a meat lover's pizza.  Lots of layers of seasoning and plenty of cheese with a tomato slice inside.  Full of flavor, it is a little greasy to pick up (from the grilling), but the owner brought out extra paper napkins to accommodate for that.  Really good sandwich.  And checkout was timely too.  I had to be somewhere and I appreciate that I didn't have to wait around for a long time to wrap up.  I hope that someone has been hired to help the owners keep up with the crowds that gather later in the evening.  Otherwise, they are going to burn out running back and forth after all the customers.  Good food in an upcoming neighborhood (Three Chicks and a Hammer are renovating many homes around here).  Don't wait until there is a line outside to give this place a try.  Review #3532

Since I underestimated traffic and missed the start of my movie at the Keystone Arts Cinema, I decided to wait until the next show and found Ebar at the northwest entrance of Nordstrom.  Located on the main floor, I noticed the tables spaced around the entrance to Nordstrom and had to look closer to actually see the entrance to the coffee and tea place.    Once inside, I noticed they had a variety of teas and coffee like items, pastries, and some smoothies.  I saw a promotion of the "Chocolate Hazelnut Banana" smoothie and decided to go with that.  Wow! What a great tasting smoothie!  All three flavors were clearly present and the smoothie itself was quite large, well over two cups of cold/frozen smoothie.  I liked that despite it being very cold, I never had the drink freeze and block the straw from functioning.  I was on guard against brain freeze since it tasted so good I wanted to keep on drinking it!  Now that I know it is there, I may start arriving at the theater early and hope there is time to try something else from their menu.  If only they could make one about half that size, I think I would like it even better.  Quite a bit to take in, especially if you want to get back to shopping or to a movie where you can't take the beverage with you.  Review #471

In addition to my enjoyment of trying different restaurants, I have recently added an interest in locally brewed craft beers, so I went to lunch on a Thursday (5-26-16) to Oaken Barrel Brewing Co in Greenwood.  It is easy to get to from the I-65 exit for Greenwood and there was plenty of parking.  The strip mall area looks a little rundown, but the inside of the restaurant was well maintained.  I was seated in the bar area and had good service.  In order to get a better appreciation of the ales available, I ordered the 5 beer flight sampler as my beverage.  Some I liked, some didn't quite make the mark for me.  My favorite was the Indiana Amber (5.3% abv, 28 ibu).  What was a really pleasant surprise was my entree.  I ordered the Stanley Chicken Sandwich with cole slaw and a pickle spear.  This sandwich was perfectly cooked.  The chicken was moist and had really good flavor that was complimented by the other toppings of Swiss cheese, lettuce, tomato and mayo on a grilled bun.  Really, this was one of the best chicken sandwiches I have had this year.  For a Thursday, there was a steady flow of customers, but not too busy for good service.  I saw some other items on the menu that I will be returning for.  Review #13

Behind the town hall in Avon, there is a beautiful park with lots of open space for hiking and disc golf.  To the east of the town hall is a playground, a remote control car course (bring your own), a pair of outdoor ping pong tables, and a twin set of shelters.  Behind the town hall is a large pond that allows fishing and makes for a pleasant view while hiking around it.  The pond also has a couple art pieces along the trail.  "200 Years" was commissioned for the Bicentennial while "Angel of Hope" is a secluded monument area for parents who have lost children.  Behind the pond is a huge disc golf area that has quite a bit of elevation to it.  There is plenty of space on the east and west wings of the park that are great for hiking too.  Overall, it is a well maintained park with plenty of parking at the front and easy access from US 36.  Review #724

I've seen some negative reviews about this restaurant, but let me tell you what I like about it.  My wife and I live close by and this has become our "go to" for nights when we don't feel like cooking and want something that we know is consistently satisfying.  This is the one restaurant where I always order the same thing.    I always order the tacos carne asada.  It comes with 3 small soft shell taco shells wrapped around some delicious small bite pieces of beef that are seared for flavor.  If you like beef flavor, then this is the meal to choose.  I always request that lettuce and cheese be added (there is no extra charge for this).  It also comes with small bowls of pico de galo and of a spicy sauce that adds even more flavor, but not too much heat.  The meal also comes with a side of Mexican rice and refried beans.  It is always enough to fill me up, especially after eating the free salsa and chips.  My wife loves to eat the Chimichanga.  Gets it every time.    Service is always fast.  Even though there isn't much interaction with the staff who mostly speak in Spanish to each other, there is enough understanding of English that we always get our order correctly and quickly.    I can't speak to all the other dishes.  We found something we really like the flavors of and at a price that is reasonable.  And it tastes like real food, not like fast food.  I don't know if it is better or worse or even authentic.  We aren't fans of super hot spices, so the food here is what is consistently expected.  Isn't that what a neighborhood place should provide?  We think so and will continue to return.  Review #12

I stopped in for an early lunch on Wednesday.  I have wanted to go here since seeing several tasty photos on Yelp!  Anyway, since it was early, I decided to grab a lunch special before loading up on sweets.  I'm giving this a 4 overall, but if you ask about just the desserts, it's a 5 all the way!  This shop is very cool.  I thought it might be a little to frilly at first, but the atmosphere is stylish, not stand-offish.  The staff (Kathy) was welcoming and glad to explain about the lunch specials and offer samples of the Graeter's Ice Cream.  Although the cafe was experiencing a computer glitch, she managed to get my order and get my bill processed without any real delay.  The idea here is to order at the counter and then you can either wait for them to bring it to your table or wrap it up if it is "to go".  I opted to beat the heat and stay in the nice air conditioning.  I selected the lunch special of a smaller salad and half a sandwich (a cup of Cheddar Potato soup was also an option).  I went with the Frona Salad with Balsamic Vinaigrette (a bit tart tasting) and the Egg Salad on Whole Wheat with lettuce and a tomato slice.  The sandwich was just okay, no wow factor.  Only five ingredients in the egg salad itself and the bread was a bit dry which held up well under the moisture of the salad, but still detracted from the flavor of the egg salad.  Overall, the sandwich was a bit bland.  But, before I sound too down on this place, I also got to select a free cookie for ordering the lunch special.  This isn't any little commercial sized cookie.  I'm talking about a half inch thick Oatmeal Applesauce Cookie with golden raisins and icing!  Probably a good four inches across too!  To go along with the cookie, I ordered a brownie (huge) and a slice of fruit pie that I think was called "Mountain Berry" or some unusual name because it tastes like a collection of several types of berries into one pie.  I took all three desserts home and shared some with my wife.  Wow!!! Every dessert was delicious!  The Cookie was crisp on the outside, moist in the middle and tasty all over.  The Brownie was a little mushy, almost "molten" inside, but loaded with chocolate flavor.  The pie, well it had a nice crust and the combo of multiple berries was a refreshing change from the chocolate explosion of the brownie.  This is good stuff!  If you haven't tried Frona Mae's, make a point to go there.  The lunch is okay and you have other options like a BLT or a chicken salad sandwich as well as what I ordered.  But the reason to really make a point of going is the dessert.  This is a locally owned business, not another chain store pushing their preservative loaded stuff at you.  Indy has an explosion of new restaurants and breweries, but finding a new bakery is tough to find in parts of the city.  I will return!  p.s.  Wine and Champagne are also available if you are interested.  Review #127

I found free street parking down 49th and strolled in late in the lunch hour.  Since I was dining by myself, I selected the bar/counter dining instead of tying up a table since the room was pretty full.  I liked that the menus were already sitting on the counter for each seat so that I could begin looking over my options while the waitress was finishing up some other tasks.  In the meantime, I was given some water (no straws here) and had my attention directed to the daily specials.  I decided to go with those and was glad I did!  I started off with a Chicken Velvet soup.  If you've never tried it, you have something to look forward to.  If you have, I will suggest this was the richest/deepest flavored soup I've tried.  So good!  And it was steaming hot, so I needed to wait just a minute or two even though I was chilled to the bone from the cold winds blowing outside.  I added an omelette to my meal that was the special:  Asiago, sausage, tomato, and spinach. Wow!  It looked so ordinary because it is served without any topping sauce, though they did offer hot sauce and ketchup if I wanted them.  But the flavor was very good without them.  I can't get over how thick the omelette was without being heavy or over cooked.  Mine never turn out this well at home, so I may have to bribe someone to show me how they make theirs! ;)  They even allowed me to substitute my soup instead of ordering a different side that would normally come with the omelette.  The only mix up was that when they offered toast with the dish, I selected whole wheat, but it came out as cinnamon bread.  They have a sign on one of their machines that says "Don't be afraid to try something different", so I went with the flow and tried it.  I ended up eating both slices.  Very tasty!  Of the Patachou franchises I have tried, this has been my most enjoyable.   Review #719

I enjoyed my lunch at Rosita's.  It is located near the north end of a strip mall on the north side of County Line Road (across the street from the car wash.)  I found a spot in the lot outside the entrance and was greeted as I entered the restaurant.  After being shown to one of the bench seat tables, I decided to go with the Rosita's Chimichanga as my meal.  They have a variety of standard Mexican dining options and daily specials at lunch, but I decided that my first time should be one of the house named specialties.  While I waited, I was brought bowls of salsa and chips.  The salsa was on the thin side, but did have onion, green pepper, and cilantro in with the tomato base. (Nice flavor, no heat.)  The chips, however, while crisp, were room temperature like they were either store bought or made far ahead of time.  I've dined a couple other places lately that bring the chips out hot, crisp, and with a little saltiness which makes these taste rather bland.  Before I finished off the salsa, the Chimi was brought out on a 14" plate.  The Chimi itself was about 7" in length and was stuffed with moist shredded pork and topped with a cheesy white sauce.  The toppings for the Chimi included the standard Guac, lettuce, pico de galo, and sour cream.  The rest of the plate was filled with rice and beans.  The bean and rice sides had unique flavors that gave them a pleasant taste, but just a little different from most of the other Mexican restaurants I have dined.  Overall, very enjoyable and quite filling.  The decor of the place is bright and festive, but still has the broken up feeling of a strip mall store.  The staff was courteous and although there were just two working our side of the business, I never had to wait long throughout the meal.    Review #300

My wife and I were running errands in Greenwood when she asked me where I wanted to go for lunch.  Since she hadn't tried House of Thai yet, I suggested it based upon my first visit.    First, there is plenty of parking out front. (They have fixed their sign too!)  We appreciated the nice surroundings of the interior.    My wife went with the Cashew nut with Chicken lunch special.  I went for the Pad See Ewe with Beef (stir-fried flat noodles with gai lin {Chinese broccoli}, carrot, broccoli, cabbage and egg in homemade sauce).  Both entrees come with a bowl of soup (tasty lemon grass soup with a little bit of heat and a nice vegetable savoriness after the tart initial taste.)  We also each got a mini salad with delicious house dressing, and a deep fried spring roll with sweet dipping sauce.  She generally liked her cashew and chicken entree, but because she ordered it mild, it was a little bit bland.  She would have preferred a little more saltiness, not spicy heat.  I took a bite and thought the mushrooms were delicious.  I thought my Pad See Ewe was also very good.  When it was brought out with the salad and spring roll, I could see the entree was still steaming hot, so I ate the sides first.  Even then, the steam was visible so I ate cautiously.  The flavors of the homemade sauce and the egg really elevated the overall flavors.  The beef had a nice sear on it, but because the veggies were so hot, the beef I had towards the end of my meal got a little bit tougher because it continued to cook while resting.    Overall, a very reasonably priced lunch with a nice setting and attentive service.  Rev #7

Although their grand opening isn't until June 29, I saw the sign they were open as I was leaving the Mooresville Showtime Cinema.  The location looks like it could have been a bank since the south side of the building has a covered area for drive thru customers to get their orders.  On the inside, there are two small rooms with 2-top tables (one on each side of the entrance), and a central seating area filled with 4-top tables and the order counter.  On your right is a rack of packaged pastries like danish, donuts, and blondies.  There is a menu of hot and cold beverage options on the wall next to the order counter.  When you are ready to order, you place your order with the cashier and give your name and then pay.  When your order is ready, they call your name and you pick it up a little farther down the counter.  The place has a large variety of hot beverage options.  Many of them I have never tried before let alone heard of.  I'm sure folks who drink a variety of coffees will be more familiar than I am.  They also have frappes and smoothies in three sizes (16, 24, & 32 oz.) with multiple flavors of each.  I went with the medium Strawberry-Banana Smoothie and answered "yes" to the choice of adding whipped cream.  The smoothie was cold and delicious and I must say that the whipped cream tasted really good too!  Since I usually drink my coffee unsweetened and black, I am glad to see this independent, veteran-owned shop offer an option for me ($2 drip coffee) as well as the smoothies for later in the day.  And for all those folks who love rich and sweet caffeine, why not give this place a try and show your support for a local business instead of that franchised giant.  Review #1011

I guess I underestimated the preparedness this place would put into getting ready to open.  On just their second day, I stopped in for lunch and had a wonderful meal with pleasant service.  Not a single glitch!  After pulling into their small, but attached parking lot, I decided to dine inside the restaurant instead of sitting on the patio.  I grabbed a spot at the bar and started with one of their non-alcoholic drinks:  The Hibiscus Palmer.  A combo of Hibiscus tea and lemonade, the red over yellow drink was quite tasty!  I soon had my appetizer, the Garlic & Parmesan Smashers, delivered.  A fresh take on potato skins, the fingerling potatoes were smashed and roasted so that they took on a crisped texture while staying moist and tender inside.  The potatoes were coated with garlic butter, Parmesan cheese, chopped parsley and I think a little bit of salt which rounded out the flavor.  These were great and arrived in a small bowl that I easily devoured, though I suppose more modest appetites would share. (Hint, grab them quick so that if you are sharing, you won't miss out!)  Within a minute of finishing my appetizer, my sandwich arrived.  I ordered the Merlin's Carolina Pork.  This pulled pork sandwich comes with a light amount of Carolina Mustard BBQ sauce, served over house pickles, and topped with cole slaw and crisped onions.  There was a nice balance of flavors though I was expecting more of a smoked or barbecue flavor than what I tasted.  It was still very good, but not "typical" barbecue.  The sandwich also came with a small salad (with a light lemon dressing or lemon juice) and house chips, which were crisp and lightly seasoned.  All worked together nicely.  The service was swift, friendly, and inquired about my opinion of my meal as I went through the courses.  I was able to order, eat and cash out in well under an hour.    If you are in the area, I definitely recommend giving this place a try!  Review #844

In 2018, I am revisiting restaurants that I haven't been to in awhile in what I call my "Ten Years After" challenge.  So, in July, I selected the downtown pub/restaurant across from the State Capital, Loughmiller's.  I recall when I worked downtown, Loughmiller's (pronounced "Lock-Millers") was known for their Reuben sandwiches.  Back then, I wasn't a big fan of sauerkraut, so I only had moderate interest in the place.  Jump forward to today and my palate has developed to appreciate a wide range of foods.  I have seen a lot of reviews where Yelpers have tried burgers, but I'm telling you that if it's your first visit, you should treat yourself to the Reuben.  It is that good!  The sandwich, sliced diagonally, is served on a grilled swirled rye.  The corned beef is sliced thin (all meat, no fat!) and then folded.  I counted 6 folded slices which made the meat nearly an inch thick!  They also add a layer of sauerkraut about a third of the way between the beef and a slice of Swiss between the next third.  They spread a generous portion of Thousand Island dressing along the crust.  The sandwich is served hot and though the bottom gets a little soggy from the steaming heat of the beef, it is still manageable enough to hand hold.  My waitress even brought an extra napkin just in case.  The sandwiches come with your choice from eleven different sides.  Some of them have an upcharge, but it's cool that they give so many options.  Unfortunately, the Krinkled fries were a disappointment.  Tasting store bought and flavorless, the ketchup and salt couldn't bring the flavor back to life.    Service was good and the waitress dropped off my bill at the time of my food so that I could take care of the bill whenever I wanted (I assume they get a lot of folks who have to return to work.)   Checkout was quick as would be expected.  The big drawback about the location is the limited parking at a reasonable price.  Street parking uses meters and fills fast.  Valet parking at the hotels is expensive.  If you don't mind the walk, I recommend parking in the mall (only $1 at lunch during the week) if the weather is nice.  Overall, a good experience and one I am glad to have made a better impression than a decade before.  Review #1090

I've seen a number of reviews from folks who have held events at the Artsgarden and yes, they do have some legitimate criticisms about restrooms and access to a space suspended above the intersection of Washington and Illinois Streets.  But my review is based upon the main purpose of the the Artsgarden:  To showcase the local artists through a series of public performances and visual art exhibitions.  It also serves as a "cultural Concierge" providing information about that arts and cultural activities in the area, making it possible for visitors to take in the events when time and money allow it.  The Artsgarden is run by the Arts Council of Indianapolis.  There is a lunchtime music series several times each week called "Garden Jams".  Local professional musicians are scheduled to perform for the lunch hour Noon to 1 pm for no charge to the public.  So, whether you are just passing through the facility from one building to another or have grabbed a lunch and decided to take a seat, there is frequently music/entertainment available.  The Arts Council website has a list of performance dates and talent schedule for the month.  Each month, there is also a new visual exhibit, not limited to professionals, so you may find works from emerging artists, students, and  different cultural and social organizations.  And I would be remiss if I didn't mention this amazing physical structure soaring seven stories into the downtown sky.  Lots of glass makes excellent viewing for a birds eye view of downtown.  It's one of my favorite buildings in the area.  Next time you are downtown, especially for lunch, why not check out the Artsgarden for a cool place to check out the arts of Indy!  Review #484

I first heard about this business through a Yelp event, but because there was so much demand (Yelpers got to actually make their own ice cream!), the line was long and I made a decision to come back on my own to give them a try.  So, after lunch, I decided to try the place for myself.  There are basically eleven "starter" flavor mixes to choose from.  Once you make a selection and pay, one of the staff begins making your ice cream on a frozen metal disc.  I missed the start where the basic ingredients are mixed because I was checking out which of the many toppings I was going to add. (You can select three types of toppings which is included in the price.)  I stepped over to watch the process unfold, then refold.  Basically, the ingredients are continuously mixed and spread thin to freeze them over and over.  Then additional flavors are added based upon your selection.  Once all those have been added, the ice cream is shaped like a large square which is then slowly scraped into a roll shape.  There were five rolls about 3 inches across and they were stacked on their ends inside a paper cup.  Then, your toppings are carefully added (the ends of the rolls are taller than the cup, so they don't want the toppings falling off.)    There are self serve napkins and sturdy spoons which are needed.  The ice cream is very cold and until it warms a bit, can require a bit of pressure from the spoon to get through the rolled ice cream.  Fortunately, the spoon was equal to the challenge and I was able to enjoy my treat.  Be aware that these are full cup servings.  I didn't see any options on the menu board for different sizes.  So, either come with an appetite, or bring a friend who likes the same choices you do!  Good flavor, fun to watch, and lots of options to make the ice cream fit your taste.  Review #1186

I stopped in this little shop for lunch and Wow!  What a deal!  It was my first visit, so I had to use the Yelp! map to be sure I found it. (It is one of the few businesses in a long strip mall that is mostly empty on the east side of Michigan Road, a little south of 71st.)    Once inside, they have a nice sized dining room and with a half wall separating the order line from the dining area.  On the west end is where the staff take and fill your orders.  It appeared most were getting their orders to go.  White boards behind the counter show the regular food options, while the small white board on the west wall shows the weekly lunch specials.    From what I could see, most of the food is prepared ahead of time which keeps the line moving quickly.  When it is your turn, one of the staff will ask what you want and then will go back and assemble the items you select before collecting your payment.    I decided to try the "ribs & chicken (dark)" special for only $8.50.  Not only did I get two large ribs (about 9" long by 2" wide), I also got a chicken leg and thigh (chopped with a cleaver to make them fit into the to go box).  In addition to the blackened spiced meat, I got a couple large scoops of beans & rice, some cooked cabbage (served warm), and a plantain (I got three slices of the fried sweet fruit.)  It was a full meal!    What I really liked about the food was that the meats had excellent flavor even before adding my choice of sauce (they have a BBQ or Sweet sauce, a mild, and a hot).  There were places on both meats where the grilling created a fantastic bark that was full of flavor.  Inside the rib meat was still moist and tender.  The chicken was the same.  Different textures, different amounts of seasoning, and then I got to dip into the sauce and added another level of flavor.  Oh, and there is a smoky aftertaste that stayed with me for awhile.  So good!    This is a true gem if you would like a change from the same old thing.  With all the closings of great independent restaurants lately, you can't waste time getting out to try them.  Review #327

This sprawling nature park (188 acres!) has a lot of modern conveniences to make for a fun day at the park.  There is a 2.5 mile paved trail that goes throughout the developed parts of the park.  The winding access road through the park goes by each of the numerous shelters and provides parking so that you don't have to lug your picnic very far.  There are a couple playgrounds located near the shelters as well.  But for those who like to bike and hike, the trail is the reason to come.  And if that isn't enough, there are unpaved trails through the woods for getting back to nature.  The park seems well maintained and attendance seems light compared to some of the other large nature parks around Indy.  Consider this park if you want to explore something new on a staycation.  Review #675

My wife and I tried this delightful new restaurant on Main Street in Carmel.  We found a spot in one of the community lots and had a short walk to the restaurant (a free parking garage is available for the building as well.)   This restaurant has a "build your bowl" concept.  You choose your bowl size and which type of rice (or leaf lettuce) you want as a base.  You then proceed down the line and have the staff add to your bowl.  I selected from the raw, marinated, and cooked seafood and farm proteins, then sauces, veggies, toppings, and more sauces.  I think most items were available at no extra cost, but I did order avocado which was 50 cents more.  My wife, who has a completely different palate preference than I do, was glad she could take as much or as little of the options as she wanted.  They have spicy options, sweet options, and combinations of flavors.  I opted for the marinated tuna and salmon with cooked shrimp.  I paired the sesame soy sauces with the veggies and sweet fruit options.  I then added the toppings to bring a bit of savory flavor and texture to my bowl.  Excellent!  My bowl took on a desired sushi roll flavor.  Very fresh.  Overall, the meal was tasty and quite filling even though we both chose the small bowls (2 cups).  Note:  They do have some beverage options (including Coke products).  There seemed to be plenty of indoor seating and the noise level was quiet to moderate.  Staff was very personable and informative.  Payment is made when you take your food from the counter.  Plastic ware and napkins are available on a side counter.  Customers are supposed to bus their tables when finished.  Review #405

I stopped in for lunch Monday and decided to sit outside because of the warm October weather.  The restaurant had clear plastic in place to allow the sunshine in, but keep any chill from the wind out.  I was seated promptly and greeted by my server.  Service was generally efficient and friendly.  I placed my beverage order and in a short while, placed my order for lunch.  I decided to try out a couple sliders called French Dipsters.  The selection has two petite buns topped with sliced prime rib & provolone cheese.  It comes with a cup of jus, kettle chips, and a dill pickle quarter.  I also ordered a side of grilled asparagus.  The flavor was fine and the meat was still fairly moist.  However, the menu describes the meal as "shaved" prime rib, but this was simply sliced about 1/8 inch thick.  My first impression was that this was going to be tough and chewy.  (I've overcooked plenty of beef cuts to know!)  However, the beef wasn't nearly as tough as I had imagined.  It still had plenty of chew for a prime rib cut, but it was served before it got to the point of being unacceptable.  Since the flavor was still good, I went ahead and completed eating my sandwiches.  The asparagus consisted of the very thin type that cook up quickly.  Even though the flavor was fine, they were served in narrow bottomed china dish which left very little surface area for slicing the stalks.  The table knife was rather dull and made it difficult to draw the blade through on the small surface.  I mostly gave the stalks a semi successful draw and then folded them at the partial cuts to fit them on my fork.   Little things can detract from the enjoyment of a meal.  I can't say there was really anything wrong with the flavor.  The restaurant just needs some work on execution and presentation to take this up to a higher rating.  Review #151

The park is a lot bigger than it seems when you first pull into the parking lot.  From there you can see a large open space with a walking trail that navigates around the perimeter.  There is also a basketball court to the west of the parking lot.  But as I wandered around, I noticed an opening in the woods that led to a bride which then led to the north where another narrower trail takes you back to a pond for fishing!  There is even a deck that lets you get over the pond and avoid snagging your line in an overhead tree branch.  Good thinking!!  After returning to the path around the open greenspace, I passed through another small stretch of trees and emerged on another open space that nearly equaled the first in size.  There was a small rest area on the northeast corner of the park.  Working my way around the east end I got a better view of the shelter and dual playgrounds on that side of the park.  The playground had separate equipment for the toddlers and the bigger kids.  What I really liked was that there was a huge shade tree that had a bench strategically place under it that could watch both playground areas at the same time.  More good thinking!  The park has a portable restroom on site that is rated for being handicap accessible near the parking lot too.  The only negative for me is that there seems to be a lot of under utilized space.  Most of the visible area is open lawn without any attempts to make them ball fields, or horse shoe pits, or anything fun.  Even planting some more trees along the path would break up the big lawn look.  Not much visually to enhance the visitor's experience.  Review #946

Although my latest visit was on a cold winter day, I've been here in the summer when the park is shaded by mature trees and is filled with the sound of the central fountain.  The park is in the center of a roundabout a couple blocks south of Washington Street at the intersection of Audubon and University.  The location is where Butler University used to be located before relocating to its current campus.  The park also features a bust of Washington Irving, a famous American author at the beginning of the 19th century.  Irving is commonly known by his works including "Rip Van Winkle" and "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow".  I didn't find why the author from New York was memorialized here other than the similarity between his last name and the name of the community.  There aren't any other amenities like a playground, shelter, or restrooms due to the lack of space.  But the location is a nice addition to the neighborhood, offering a gathering place for the community as well as a quiet place for individuals.  Review #554

I stopped in this family owned business in a strip mall at 86th and 465 on the west side.  Lots of free lot parking and a double door entrance that keeps the dining room from blasts of outdoor air are great for customers.  The restaurant is one where you place your order at the counter, pay, and then pick a seat to wait for your meal.  They do have a self service beverage dispenser and a place to pick up your silverware, napkins, and if you want, to add extra spices.  I ordered the crabmeat rangoon and my standby Pad See-eiw for first time visits to new Thai places.  After a short wait, my rangoon came out first.  Very light and crisp, there was enough cream cheese and crab for flavor, especially since they were still warm.  The dipping sauce bowl was a bit small to dip the rangoon, so you have a choice of drizzling the sauce over the top, or tearing the rangoon in half which works for dipping.  The sauce wasn't the thick red sweet sauce you find other places, but it was a tasty orange colored liquid that was a nice surprise.  The pad see-eiw (I think it is spelled differently every place I go!) had the wide noodles I like and are stir fried with egg, bite sized broccoli crowns, and chopped cabbage hearts.  Really yummy and decently portioned.    My only negative is that I am used to getting far more for my money at my favorite Thai places on the south side (i.e. Small spring roll, small salad included).  The price and quantity are still reasonable, just not the best in town.  They do bring out your food and buss your table when you are finished, so it is somwhere between full and self serve for dining.    Review #454

Crispy Bird:  Where bright flavors meet chicken.  That's what came to mind when I dined here during opening week.  Even though it was a cold and windy Wednesday, the small restaurant was nearly packed around 6.  I found free street parking a short distance away on 49th.  Since I was by myself, I didn't mind sitting at the bar where about a dozen or so stools form an "L" around the bar and grill.  There are also a number of four tops, some with benches, in the main dining area.  Note that like many of these re-purposed old buildings, the customers are nestled fairly close together.    I started with an order of Chicken Skins that comes with a Meyer Lemon Kosho Aioli Dip.  The portion was huge with maybe a half dozen large curled skins.  I didn't notice the prep, but would guess they are deep fried due to their curliness.  Seriously, some took four big bites just to finish.  When I make them at home, I like to pan fry smaller pieces and use some salt, pepper, and butter.  So, without the aioli, the skins were on the bland side.  Fortunately, the aioli had a bright citrus flavor that saved the day.  Still, cutting them a bit smaller and seasoning them would make them tastier for me.  While I waited on my entree, I sipped on one of the house cocktails, the "Jack Rose" made with apple brandy, grenadine, and lemon.  Again, a very bright flavor with enough brandy to taste without overwhelming the balance.  Nice!  Since I pigged out on the skins, I only ordered a Fried Chicken Sandwich.  I really liked it!  The breaded chicken was large, tasty, and juicy (the juice was still a bit hot since it was served directly.)  The chicken was accompanied by house pickles (nice addition of acidity and crunch), coleslaw, and another aioli, this time, spicy.  Although stacked high, the bread was fresh and could be "smushed" enough to take a good bite.  Lots of flavor and worth ordering again!  The servers and manager did a great job of watching my spot for finished plates and topping off water (note that they left a bottle of water that I could use to help myself.)  Everyone from the host & hostess at the door throughout the dinner was friendly.  So, if you are in the area and don't mind going to a cozy place with a nice buzz in the atmosphere, stop by and give it a try.  You might just feel "brighter"!  Review #469

I stopped in for lunch after finding a paid parking space right out front on Mass Ave.  There is a lot of construction across the street, so I suspect that cuts down on the foot traffic.      At the entrance, the counter has some large "pie" slices available for quick purchase along with some prepackaged salad options (pasta, garden, and Caprese).  The menu is on the wall near the ovens and also on the right end of the entrance in case there is a line.  You place your order and pay up front in exchange for a number.  Note:  You can get a salad right away along with your utensils, napkins, and drink selection.   The selections of meals breaks down into 3 categories:  Specialty "Pies", pizzas of your own selections, and oven baked subs/calzones.  There are also sides (various breads and sauces) and desserts as well.    The specialty pie names reflect the theme of the pizzeria.  "Goodfella", "Wiseguy", & "The Don" represent some of the options.  There are three full pizza sizes available: 12", 16", and 22". All the options are New York style thin crust pizzas.    The make your own pizzas are priced per topping accordingly:  $1.25 for the 12" (for 2 or 3 people); $2 for the the 16" (feeds 4-6); and $3 for the 22" (feeds 6-8).    The subs are named after celebrities such as Robert DeNiro, Al Pacino, The Italian Stallion, Frank Sinatra, and, my selection, the Dean Martin.      I ordered the Caprese salad which is basically diced tomatoes in olive oil and salt topped with ciliegine mozzarella and basil.  It was tasty and refreshing but rather simple.    The Dean Martin sandwich took a little over ten minutes to come out and consisted of a sliced sub bun crisped on the outside, but soft inside.  The toppings included seasoned chicken, artichokes, and fresh mushrooms topped with a creamy alfredo sauce.  The flavor was nice, but nothing exceptional.  I also thought the chicken was rather sparse.  Several bites didn't seem to have any chicken at all.      In fairness, I didn't explore the lounge for the "adult beverages" or sit out on the covered patio overlooking Mass Ave.  Both look like nice options.  I also didn't sample any of the pies, since I didn't want to order a full pie or opt for one of the limited selection of ready to go slices, so maybe my score is a little low.  Still, there are lots of pizza joints around town including competition just a few blocks away.  If this place wants to make it, it needs to have more "wow" factor.  Review #265

Excellent chocolates with as much visual appeal as they have taste.  As much as 98% of the candies are made in house and the variety I sampled were really good!  Lots of varieties coming in milk, dark, and white chocolate flavors.  Chocolates are sold in packages or by the piece.  The only negative is that the pricing is quite a bit higher than house chocolates I've had in Zionsville and Greenwood.  If money is no object, then you can let your tastebuds and imagination go wild!  I recommend the Ganache (Raspberry).  Review #453

Wow!  What great flavor!  I stopped in for lunch at this new restaurant on the northeast corner of 49th and College.  A small parking lot on the south and west sides of the building allowed me to park closely.    Upon entering, I was greeted and allowed to select my own seat on the first floor.  A number of small 4-seat tables and one larger table for groups were available.  The tables have napkin holders, and shakers for parmesan cheese and for pepper flakes.  (After 4, the taproom upstairs opens for the 21+ crowd.)  I quickly received some water and asked for a sample of a couple of the Quaff On! beers on their list.  I went with the Cherry Wheat Ale (excellent!) and placed my order for the Greek's Special pizza (small - 6 slices of a 10 inch pie).  Before long, my pizza arrived and it was fantastic!  The special has a buttery crust where the ends puff and crisp.  It comes with Italian sauce and sausage, Spanish onions, blended cheeses, bell peppers, baked ham, sliced mushrooms, and crispy and generous pepperoni.  The balance of flavors was great, but I could eat a plate full of those pepperoni slices.  They were like spiced bacon disks!  None of the greasiness, just lots of flavor.  Wow!  If this place keeps up the great service and food, it will become a favorite for as long as they want.  Review #335

As of my writing, there is a new manager running the daily operation of this place and she is making some changes in the near future that should please some of the reviewers who were on the negative side.    She has already decided upon making the brewery more family friendly with the bar area for 21+ and the majority of the tables being open.   She will be adding some games to keep kids busy while the adults relax and try the offerings.  She also said that early in October 2018 they will add some street tacos and simple snacks.  They don't have a full sized kitchen, so they have to limit what they can offer, but she heard the requests for food and is trying to bring something to customers.  Grilliant BBQ will provide the shredded pork for the pork tacos, but Noble Order will add their own sauces.  I remember that chicken tacos and one other type will also be offered.  She also has had maintenance done on the coolers to maintain the quality of temperature control on the beverages.  The beer, wine, and mead come from the Richmond parent location, so she is working with the owners to provide better quality control for the products.    Although quite early on a Saturday afternoon, I found the environment friendly and well lighted.  I'm not sure what reviewers experienced when they commented it too quiet/depressing.  It's not a regular bar that has booming music and is a hook up spot.  It's a place to go to sample craft beer and wine from a Hoosier company.  The server/operation manager was friendly and quite good at handling multiple customers.  She really seemed interested in making the place a destination for folks to stop by.  I tried a flight of four beers for $8.  I went with the Furst Bood Orange Sour (American Wheat based 4.8% abv, 25 IBU) that was more orange than sour.  It would be a nice gateway to approaching sours if you aren't a  beer snob that only drinks one kind.  I like exploring tastes and found this one very approachable.  I then had a Free Spirit Kolsch (4.8%, 25) and the Grand Circus IPA (5.8%, 65).  Of the two, I liked the IPA better.  It had a definite hop taste, but not overpowering, so it would also be a nice choice for someone wanting to expand their beer palate.  I ended with the Noktoberfest Lager (5.1%, 25) which had a very pleasant, almost sweet taste after drinking the IPA.  All the beers were good, though there wasn't any single one that I would favor over all the others.  I've already made plans for the next time I am in the Richmond area to stop by parent location to check out the winery and brewery there.  Until then, this seems like a nice option for a shorter trip.  Review #1397

Although I am not an expert when it comes to craft brewing, I do like a high percentage of the brews I have sampled at Sun King.  I really appreciate that they have a continually changing line of specialty and small batch beers.  However, they are smart enough to have three house brews that are available all year round for people like my wife who orders the Sunlight Cream Ale whenever it is available.   I like to be a bit more adventurous, so when I stop by the brewery, I like to order the specialty flight which allows me to sample six drafts of my choosing (the standard flight gives you the three house beers and your choice of only 3 of the other drafts available.)     There is usually a "Small Batch" option available.  The Small Batch is truly that, but means it was brewed at the Fishers location where the brew masters apparently have a lot of fun trying all kinds of combinations.   The lineup of draft options may also have a Nitro option, a Kings Reserve / barrel aged brew, and a variety of ales like IPA's, stouts, and even malt liquor.   If you are there late in the week or on a weekend, you can ask about tours.  I went on one on my last visit and learned about the history of Sun King and of beer sales in Indiana. They also showed me the production process equipment and answered any questions I had.  You don't have to go without a beer on the tour which lasts a little over a half hour.  They only take people around on days that production is halted for safety reasons.   So, if you are looking for something fun to do and want to try some good beer, check on Sun King.  Review #213

I saw a number of great reviews from my Yelp friends, so while in BR, decided to stop by.  Unfortunately, I didn't look at the address and stopped at the new place opening in February 2018 at 64th and Cornell.  Fortunately, the construction worker inside new how to get to the current boutique on Guilford, so I left my car in my free parking spot and walked down to the strip and "popped" in. (pun intended)  The current shop has a small customer area but they manage to pack in a number of varieties of popcorn bagged and ready to go.  There were both individual flavors and gift packages that had four kinds.  Behind the counter, the staff were getting ready to package a new blueberry flavored popcorn which I managed to get a sample of.  (Quite tasty, but it did make  my tongue blue!)  The staff was friendly but I didn't see any varieties set out to sample.  I didn't ask, so I assume you have to trust your judgment about which flavors you might like.    I decided to go with the advice of my Yelp friends and I definitely picked some winners.  I picked up a couple varieties that were "team ups" with other local vendors.  The Dark Chocolate Osiris (Sun King) has a deep flavor of dark chocolate that was quite tasty.  The Caramel Bacon Cheddar (Smoking Goose) was full of spicy, savory, and sweet flavors.  I also picked up a Cheese & Ale pretzel flavor that was loaded with sharp cheddar.  If any of these sound like your kind of flavors, then stop by and pick up a bag or two!  Note that the new place will have a lot more room, will serve beer and wine, and have its own small parking lot behind the shop accessible from the alley.  And for those who may have trouble climbing the numerous stairs on the front, there is a ramp on the parking lot side.  Based on the success I had on my first visit, I can't wait to see what they do with the new place!  Review #480

I had a fun time at this little bit of Chicago sports bar.  Located in the revitalized old town section of Zionsville, I found some free street parking about a block away and was able to navigate the steep stairs to this second story bar.  Lots of Chicago themed sports and skyline images adorn the walls.  There was a variety of comfy chairs & tables of different sizes and also some high top metal bar stools along with communal tables in the +21 section.   Service was pretty quick and friendly.  I knew ahead of time what I wanted, so my wait time in the restaurant was fairly brief.  What I didn't expect was the huge servings!  On the positive side, "da sausage" was a large Italian Sausage served as a sandwich.  I opted for the marinara (free) and Mozzarella ($1) and was very glad I did.  Not only do they put marinara on the sandwich, but provide a small cup of extra sauce.  The sauce itself was thicker and held its own with the spicy Italian flavors.  The negative was that the serving cup was too small for easy dipping of the sandwich, so I made do with using my fork to dab the rich sauce on each bite.  The mozzarella was warm and gooey, and went great with the sandwich.  I would gladly order that again.  I remembered family cookouts on the south side of Chicago while eating.  That was good sausage!  The only negative was the cole slaw side.  While it was generously served (about a cup), the slaw was on the dry side, lacking enough vinegar and sugar to take it from the basic shredded cabbage to a tangy sweet slaw I prefer to even the creamy kind.    Lots of televisions with the sound turned down, so the noise level was modest while still allowing fans to watch the activities of multiple games at once.  Review #414

My wife gets a lot of her sewing supplies through Joann Fabrics.  I usually tag along and so this is the third one I've been in.  While the one in Bloomington has the greatest collection of fabric (by far!), this one has a nice mix of fabric and crafts, with a fair amount of room for seasonal items.    One thing I've learned is that you are going to overpay if you don't have the JOANN app on your phone.  They always, and I mean ALWAYS, have coupons that will save you double digit percents (I've seen 60%) off your purchases.  The staff has been helpful when we've made purchases, but they do get slammed on weekends at the cutting counter.  I always encourage my wife to go during the week to avoid the delay.  Review #1933

I would have loved this place as a kid/teenager, especially if I had any money!  As a fan of comics growing up (and now movies), I would have enjoyed looking through the collectibles (like statues) and t-shirts.  They have a lot of things that I've not seen elsewhere too, so points for that!  The space was a little crowded by the routing of customers around the counter, but once I got passed that, I was able to move about fairly easily.  Prices on some stuff seemed quite reasonable considering the store is located in a mall.  Fun place to browse if your interest runs in this direction.  Review #1908

Embroidery and Cross Stitching supplies are what you will find in this delightful shop.  There is a rainbow of colorful threads that greet you as you enter.  Patterns and supplies are found throughout the two stories of shop.  The woman working was very helpful in explaining the differences and showed a number of completed examples to make it easier to understand.  Upstairs, there are a couple long tables where it looks like you might be able to get some training/guidance on how to do the craft.  Overall, I found the place to be a one stop shop for pursuing your interest in this type of hobby.  Review #2198

I've been to many of the local franchises of B&B, so I thought I would stop by this one in Broad Ripple to see if there was anything new.  (There was!)  Like most of the places, they carry all five of the standard B&B brews.  They also carry some limited edition flavors, a Flat 12 option (B&B recently bought Flat 12 which has been brewing the B&B beers the whole time), and for non-crafters, a PBR.    The place has two menus:  one for beer and beverage options and one for food.  I had previously dined elsewhere, so I only asked for the beer one.  They had a really unusual option that was okay, but maybe a bit too ambitious, "Coffee Augustus Gloop's Secret Stash".  That one is listed as a "Bourbon Barrel-Aged Triple Chocolate Imperial Milk Stout w/ Hubbard & Cravens Coffee".  I knew their brews had names based on book titles, but that description is like an entire book! ha!  It also packed a 13.5% ABV, so this isn't your every day ale.  Instead, I decided to go with the "Old Bitter Ms. Havisham", an oatmeal extra-special Bitter (6.8%, 45 IBU).  It had a nice flavor, a reddish-orange color, and wasn't that bitter.  Nice flavor that I would recommend.  The folks working there were friendly and kept me company since it was early afternoon.  The crowd had dwindled by the time I arrived.  There is some free angled parking across the street if you are lucky enough to grab one of those, and there is some parallel parking (free) along Cornell heading southbound.  Note that there are stairs at the front entrance but there is a ramp on the north side of the building.  Review #2282

I have to admit I was impressed with this place.  Not only is it huge, it has a lot of items that you wouldn't normally think of in a bookstore.  It seems they realize that people who read books might also like board games, of collectibles, or gifts for folks who read, and a cafe for enjoying your newest purchase.  On the day we went, there was an organization providing gift wrapping for the holidays.  Very cool and convenient.  And of course, they have all the latest books and if they don't, they can track it down for you.  The staff we dealt with were helpful and friendly.  Great experience!  Review #1949

I used to eat lunch here fairly often about a dozen years ago, and then things changed and I wasn't in the Broad Ripple area very often.  So, I decided to stop by and see if it was the still familiar.  My wife and I dropped by on a cold Tuesday and fortunately, there was parking right out front on their odd shaped and somewhat difficult to navigate parking lot.  Once inside, we could hear people talking but the lobby wasn't "manned" so we wander in and looked for the staff.  The bar area had the wait staff and when they saw us, we were immediately greeted and seated.  (Maybe some bell or buzzer to let them know guest were arriving could help.)  The inside of the dining room (intended for families and under 21s) was filled with colorful murals on the wall.  After the waitress took our order, she encouraged us to walk around the restaurant to see the different rooms.    To the west of the dining room, Cornerstone Coffee's bar/coffee shop/pastry place is open for M&J's customers who wish a quieter experience with assorted cocktails or coffees available.  Yes, you can order M&J's food in the coffee shop.  To the south of the dining room is the main bar.  At the west end of the bar is additional seating, a pool room, and a gaming room.  Lots of televisions make this a popular spot for watching ball games, especially when Butler is on.  When weather is warmer, there is also outdoor seating available.  Our food arrived and I really enjoyed my Pesto Chicken Sammie.  The bread was fresh and tasty.  The chicken was served hot and it retained its moisture even though it was white meat.  I really liked the basil pesto, provolone cheese, roasted tomato, and spinach combo.  Very nice flavor.  The sandwich came with choice of a side dish, so I opted for the roasted red potatoes.  They were roasted to perfection so that the potato's sweetness came out.  The light seasoning was subtle, but enough to not need salt added.    My wife went with one of the daily specials, a parmesan chicken sandwich.  She didn't care for the sauce flavor and thought the bun was way too big for the amount of chicken.  She did mention her chicken was also cooked properly and was moist.  She really liked the potato chips which were seasoned as her side.  She decided to order the Brownie Sundae since she remembered how good they were long ago.  She was not disappointed!
