The large glass had a warm brownie base with vanilla ice cream and lots of whipped topping with chocolate syrup on top.  Excellent to share.  Overall, we enjoyed our experience.  The food was of good quality and I liked that we had options for the type of dining environment we wanted.  Review #562

Maybe we caught the place on a bad day in the kitchen, but our most recent visit to the Farmers Market Cafe was really disappointing.  We took our granddaughters to the State Museum and decided to eat at the cafe for convenience.  The process was easy:  look at the menu board for the food options and place an order and pay at the counter and take a number for your table so they can bring it out.  Still lots of room and a nice view of the canal (it was raining or it may have been an even greater view.)  After helping ourselves to the beverages, we waited a while for our food to be brought out.  The servings were large and looked appetizing.  The granddaughters enjoyed their kids menu items though the youngest wanted more jelly on the PBJ.  But the good things stopped there.  My wife ordered the Caribbean Cuban Sandwich which comes served on a baguette with chips.  The sandwich comes with a mango chili chutney that simply overwhelmed the meat tastes and was odd.  We have had Cuban Sandwiches elsewhere that we have loved and thought this would be similarly tasty, but the flavor was really disappointing.  She thought the flavor a 2-star, especially for the cost.  The side of chips were thick and crispy but lacked any seasoning.  Okay at best.  I ordered what looked like an appealing (and highly approved on Yelp) sandwich, the Sweet Cherry Walnut Chicken Salad which comes on a toasted croissant roll.  The sandwich was generously laden with the chicken salad, but it looked like it was applied with an ice cream scoop that formed a ball of meat/salad in the middle with nothing on the edges.  I adjusted for that myself and thought the flavor was okay, but nothing outstanding for the lengthy list of ingredients.  The real disappointment was that the croissant was not fresh and light.  It was chewy and tough and the texture really took away from my enjoyment of the sandwich.  I suppose I could have eaten the salad with a fork, but that isn't the point.  I was looking forward to a tasty croissant with the right texture to complement my chicken salad.  Fail.  The restaurant/cafe is basically a minimalist interaction sort of place that relies upon location and views for business.  I guess it is up to each visitor to decide if it is worth eating here or if they should plan to eat before or after visiting the museum...someplace else.  Review #1608

You know a restaurant has something working for it when it can add new franchises faster than I can keep up.  I haven't been to the Public Greens downtown in the Cummins Building yet, but since we were meeting our financial planner near KatC, I finally made plans to take my wife to lunch at this location.  Located in the newly (2018) updated food court at the mall, we stood in front of the large blackboard full of options (beverages are on another one).  While looking, one of the thoughtful employees came over to greet us and explained how the menu worked which was very helpful.    We soon decided and proceeded passed the quick kitchen and salad prep area to the order counter.  We were given a number to put on our table and I helped myself to the station where they keep bottles of water and glasses while she waited for her iced tea.  Before long, our food was delivered.  My wife got a substantial serving of BBQ Pork served in a large bowl.  The pork comes with beans, couscous, coleslaw, Bread & Butter pickles (more spicy heat than I've had elsewhere), and topped with Ranch Dressing.  It was more than she could eat, so I helped her a bit and we still had some leftovers to take home.  Generally, it was a good meal, but there was something about it that just didn't blend flavors as good as I had hoped.  Nothing bad, but I suspect it was the flavor of the B&B pickles overpowered some of the other flavors, so it wasn't our favorite BBQ.  I ordered a smaller Orange Cashew Broccoli salad without any additional protein.  This came with a roasted Hazelnuts instead of cashews (??) and  was topped with a sweet sesame sauce.  I really liked the flavor and though I am curious how it would have tasted with cashews, I must admit I really liked the savory taste of the nuts with the sauce.  The broccoli was cut a bit larger than bite sized (at least my wife thought so).  Of the two dishes, I definitely preferred this one.  When we were finished, we let the staff know and they brought our bill and bused our table after we left.  Service was very good throughout the meal and we generally had a very positive experience with plenty to eat.  Review #2462

After trying out another new restaurant on Mass Avenue, my wife and I stopped in three nearby gift shops.  This was our favorite.  There are small items from around the world that range from jewelry and clothing, to food items, to art projects, and Christmas ornaments.  There were spices and hand made greeting cards.  Each item also tells you which country the crafter was from.    It was mentioned by several of the staff that the artisans are paid a "fair wage" for their goods.  I'm not sure who determines that wage, but it sounds like more than most places do.  Anyway, we saw a number of items that interested us enough to make purchases.  It was fairly busy, but the place didn't seem too crowded, so that was also a plus.  Review #1833

My timing was fortunate, but not optimal as I caught this place just minutes before closing on a Saturday afternoon.  So, they didn't have any black drip coffee available, but suggested an Americano as an alternative.  I also grabbed a twist tie coordinated blueberry muffin (they have a mini chart to help you identify the flavors by twist tie).  The server was friendly and helpful and I was planning to get my coffee to go anyway, so I didn't have a lot of opportunity to check out for ambiance though I will say that the seating area looked inviting.   The American was just a bit too hot to enjoy right away, but had a good taste and was a useful alternative to standard drip coffee.   The muffin, though not huge, was very filling.  I am not sure how long it had been there.  The blueberries had a bit of a raisin texture to them.  It didn't affect the taste, but it was a bit unusual compared to other muffins in my experience.  Good food, service, and setting.  I like it!  Review #2869

Great beers and tasty food were the key to an enjoyable lunch on Wednesday.  Arriving just after opening at 11:30, I selected a barside seat.  I was greeted right away with a menu and a list of beverage options.  Having reviewed the menu ahead of time online, I was able to place my food order right away which then gave me time to go over the beer selections.  I also let the bartender know I was watching my time so that I could catch a movie.    I opted for a flight of four 4 ounce samples of the home brew.  Although one of my choices was currently unavailable, the bartender (Taylor) suggested a substitute that fit nicely with the style of beers I had chosen.  Being relatively new to craft beer, I opted for the Cornerstone Koelsch (5%), Golden Maris Summer Ale (5.2%), Benevolent Belgian Blond (6.2%), and the Sanctuary Saison (5.9%).  Each had a nice clean taste, becoming progressively fuller as I worked through the order.  My favorite was the Maris followed closely by the Koelsch.  Delicious!  Soon, my order of the "Cab" Grilled Chicken Breast Club Sandwich with a side of fruit arrived.  The club was a Full-sized sandwich!  The whole wheat bread was grilled crisp on the outside (I did have to wipe my fingers occassionally on my napkin after holding the sandwich).  A plump, juicy, and very tender chicken breast was nestled in a bed of lettuce and basil aioli, then covered with a flavorful layer of bacon and plenty of Swiss Cheese.  Although the chicken itself lacked seasoning, the other flavors worked well with each other to make the sandwich tasty.  I could have used a tad more aioli or maybe spicy brown mustard, but it was still good.  And my compliments on the side of fruit (about a half cup).  The fruit was diced, not left as some oversized pieces that would need to be speared or cut.  (You have to appreciate a sous chef/staff that takes care of the details!)  And the best part of the assorted melons and berries was that they were all fresh!  These made an excellent compliment to the sandwich.    And to finish off my experience, Taylor asked if I wanted my check  just as I was finishing, commenting that she remembered I had a movie to catch.  Attention to details indicates quality in my book.  I will be glad to bring friends here to sample more.  Review #105

I stopped in this fourth location in the Scarlet Lane Brewing stable while visiting the southeast side (Beech Grove).  The manager of the mother ship (McCordsville) also manages this location and she was tending bar when I stopped by Saturday afternoon.    The bar has convenient free street parking on both sides of Main Street and there are a couple small tables with chairs in front of the building to allow patrons to sip outside.  Inside, the bar is on the left and additional table seating is on the right.  The walls are covered with murals and are similar in theme to the other locations.  I checked out the tap menu on the blackboard behind the middle of the bar (they do have paper listings on the tables), and noticed quite a few beers that I hadn't tried before, so I opted for a flight of four.  And I was pleasantly surprised to enjoy all four of my choices!  The Loiterers is a salty Kolsch (5%) that reminded me of when I was young and would use the old trick of sprinkling a bit of salt on my beer to make it foam.  Apparently the beer reminds the brewer of her Oregon home sea salt.  Not for everyone, but I found it a nice change of pace beer.  I moved on to the Event Horizon (4%) which is a Tart Cherry Pale Ale.  If you like sours, this is the closest I've tried from Scarlet Lane.  Not too sour, but just enough tartness to give the flavor depth.  Moving on, the Ghost 1.1 Hazy Pale Ale (4%) was a completely different taste featuring Cinnamon, Vanilla, and Coconut which made it more like a tropical drink than a beer.  Smooth and easy drinking on this one.  It could easily be one that you could drink a lot of!  I finished off with Eir the Merciful Rye IPA (4.7%) which was the fourth completely different flavor done well.  Something about the rye really lights up the sides of my tongue about half way back.  It's one of the hardest flavors for me to describe, so I will simply say I really enjoy it like I enjoy rye bread.  Clean taste and smooth drinking here too.  Pleasant conversation and really good beers make this place a winner.    Review #2611

Although I am not an aficionado when it comes to bagels, I know when I like something.  I stopped by for a late lunch and tried the Diesel Hasselhoff (Turkey and Bacon w/American Cheese) on Asiago (bagel).  They grill it like a panini and the flavor was really good!  It comes with lettuce & mayo as standard, and is delivered wrapped in foil while served on a reusable plate/bowl.  Nice crunch to the bagel and just enough meat and cheese to balance the flavor.  The mayo and lettuce keep it moist though I would suggest eating it quickly to avoid having the lettuce get steamed.  I also tried a Chocolate Banana smoothie that was delicious and surprisingly brain freeze cold.  I didn't think so, but it snuck up on me and made me slow down on the delicious drink!  The place shares a parking lot and entrance with a salon next to it.  You place your order at the counter, give your name, and wait for them to call it out.  Note that they don't call out names on beverages, just the beverage type, while the names are reserved for sandwiches.  A little confusing, but not too difficult to pick up as long as everything is unique.  The staff was friendly and seemed to be getting the orders out smoothly.  The bagels are large and I saved half for later which made me appreciate the foil wrap even more to preserve its freshness.  Minimal wait during the week just after noon.  Plenty of time for those who need to get going on a time table.  Review #1471

Wow, not only do they have coffee options and a variety of breads, they also serve lunch options during all hours of operation!    My wife and I were on the north side around 10:30 a.m.  You know, right at the end of most places breakfast hours and too early for lunch.  But we decided to try Lulu's and thought we could at least try one of their bakery items while I grabbed a cup of coffee.  The cafe wasn't too busy when we parked in the lot outside their entrance. (Note, they do have a single step up from the lot but do have a wheel chair access about 40 yards to the right.)  Inside, there was a variety of tables near the entrance and several seats along the left side as you went on back.  The right side is where the display and order counter are located, with the kitchen area farther back.  The staff behind the counter was very friendly and helpful.  Although they had the food items posted behind the counter, we were directed to the paper menu on the counter that we could take back to our table to peruse until we were ready to order.    My wife wanted a slice of banana nut bread while I was eyeing a zucchini bread slice.  The staff offered to heat them and then bring them out to us.  Both slices were moist and flavorful, and tasted especially fresh with the warmth of the bread releasing more aroma.  We munched on those slices while we waited on our lunch selections.  My wife went with the egg salad plate which was neatly presented with sliced cucumbers acting as dividers between the scoops of egg salad on a bed of lettuce. She really liked the taste.  (I prefer a little more contrast in flavors, but she was happy.)  My order was the Chicken Bacon Ranch Wrap which, I must say, was probably the best wrap I have had all year!  Not only did the cubed chicken stay moist and tender, but the ingredients inside (lettuce, tomato, cheddar, ranch, and bacon) were fresh and full of flavor too.  What set this wrap apart from all others was that the outsides of wrap were pressed/grilled so that there was a crisp crunch to the sandwich.  No doughy texture or flavor, just warm and yummy wrap.  Both plates came with fresh baby carrots, so the plates looked as colorful as they were tasty.  Overall, I was very pleased with the food and service.  I think we will return soon when we are back in the neighborhood.  Review #384

Reme's is a new addition to Plainfield's growing list of independent restaurants (Yay!)  Located in a strip mall just south of the Pier 1 at Perry Crossing, parking is plentiful and makes it easy to get here.    The interior is simple with a mix of different sized tables and booths.  The cashier stand is near the entrance and a sign indicates to wait to be seated.  I was taken back near the kitchen and seated in a booth.  The menu is very bizarre:  Breakfast all day, American Traditional, Mexican (the Hoosier kind), and after 3 p.m., pizza.  In addition to this diverse collection, there are daily specials.  I opted for one of those which was a Chicken, Avocado Panini with fresh fruit and a cup of soup (Chicken Noodle).  My soup was brought out promptly.  Served at a temp that allowed for immediate consumption, the soup had pulled chicken meat, celery and carrots, and noodles in the broth.  Nice flavor, but nothing remarkable.  Just good quality ingredients.  Then, I waited for close to 30 minutes for my sandwich to arrive.  I was told that "the chicken takes longer to cook"...not once, but twice.  (Since when?  Mine at home doesn't.)  Anyway, after asking for when it would be ready, it showed up in less than five minutes.  Fortunately, the chicken was cooked just right.  It came with sliced avocado and the flavor was fine.  Not a lot of flavor depth, but still good.  The fruit was fresh and diverse.  There were seven varieties on my plate and they went well with the sandwich.    My bill was dropped off at my table with my entree and I paid at the counter near the entrance.  If they could get the delays worked out, I would have enjoyed the meal more.  A bit more seasoning would be nice too.  Review #2767

This is one of my favorite music stores to browse.  They have lots of music on both cd and vinyl.  Not just inventory, but lots of really good records to choose from.  There are listening stations for cd's and a play area if you need to let your kids play while you browse.  The prices for vinyl were running in the $20-40 range for most of the classic albums I was looking at.  I also liked the friendly greeting when I arrived.  Review #2866

My wife and I stopped in during a day trip to explore Broad Ripple.  This shop is located next to "The Corner" at Guilford and Westfield.  It is filled with jewelry, home decor/gifts, and appears to do custom framing too.  The shop is small but is filled with a lot of high quality items.  My wife kept finding many cool things to look at.  The items seemed unique and well made which explains why they are on the pricey side.  If you like looking for a special gift, for either yourself or a friend, check this place out.  Review #2156

In the wedge neighborhood formed by the intersection of Virginia and Shelby Streets in Fountain Square, a small playground was added on a corner lot of Grove and Elm.  The playground is fenced and has a mulch base throughout the entire play area.  Slides and swings are the main source of entertainment/activity for the park.    The park has no dedicated parking and does not have running water or restroom facilities, so plan a visit accordingly.  Review #538

My wife and I enjoyed our lunch.  The parking lot was nearly full, but once we entered the restaurant, we realized there was a lot of room inside and we were quickly seated.  No problems at all with service.  We had our food before much of a wait, including our free chips and salsa, and our beverages.  (A slight delay on getting our bill, but even that wasn't too long.)  The chips were crisp and the salsa had a decent flavor, but was a bit on the watery side, so it was necessary to keep a napkin handy.    I ordered from the Mexican (adjusted to American palates) menu and got a Texas Fajita which was large for a lunch offering.  It came with beef, chicken, and shrimp with a couple flour tortillas and a boat of shredded lettuce, pico, guac, and some sour cream.  There were also some tasty refried beans with cheese on the side.  Back to the fajita, there were loads of onions, bell peppers, and tomato slices in the spiced sauce.  Good flavor, maybe even delicious.  Just that the meats were pretty overcooked, so they got either chewy or rubbery.  Not so bad that it stopped me from enjoying the taste, but enough to mention if that is a big deal to you.  My wife ordered a burrito deluxe which thought pretty good, but the more she ate, the more the red sauce reminded her of spaghetti sauce than anything Mexican.    Overall, a pleasant experience with good service and good flavor.  Not my favorite Mexican spot in town, but a solid showing.  Review #1896

Wild Ginger offers a variety of sushi options for lunch and dinner.  They also have a nice selection of wines to go with your meals.  And, of course, they have a number of appetizers to start your meal off right.  After parking in the shared lot, I was greeted and given the option to dine inside or on the patio.  Since it was a bit warmer than I liked outside, I opted to stay inside.    The interior is only modestly decorated and has a white room with multiple doors that can close off from the rest of the dining room.  There is an impressive origami cluster of birds (in multiple colors) that hangs above the center of the room.  Service was pleasant and efficient.  The food was delivered with minimal delay and my water was topped off.  Check out was timely as well.  I started with the Tempura appetizer.  It comes with three shrimp which are sliced to make them uncurl into a straight stick shape.  The breading was crisp and puffed (very light).  The breaded shrimp was okay on its own, but when I dipped it in the Tempura sauce (more liquid than sauce), the flavor was greatly improved.  Very Good!  The tempura also comes with four kinds of vegetables that are also breaded and fried.  They were also done well and were good when dipped.  Through the breading, I was able to identify asparagus, a sweet potato slice, a flat carrot slice, and some other white/yellow that I wasn't quite sure of.  I also ordered one of the specialty rolls:  Dragon Roll.  They have two kinds, so if you order, you need to specify whether you want the regular or the Flaming kind.  I went with the regular which may sound boring compared to one that is lit on fire, but the presentation of the roll was quite imaginative.  In addition to the bright green (sliced avocado) on the back of the dragon, shrimp was sliced to shape a tail and head for the dragon.  And they even used the suction cups from a small octopus to form the eyes!  It looked great and was tasty as well.    If you are looking for good sushi in the Fishers area, I would recommend stopping in at Wild Ginger.  Review #1289

My wife and I strolled into this house-turned-business on the south side of Old Town Zionsville.  There is a large porch that you climb a few steps to from the free street parking out front.  Once inside, you see the room where they have cookie doughs for visitors to buy.  To the right is a prep room where the guy who waited on us was busy but stopped what he was doing to help us.  A third room around the corner contained a counter with baked cookies that was what we were looking for.    I really liked that they had bite sized samples of several cookie types available.  My wife selected a thick and softer chocolate chip cookie.  I picked a peanut butter cookie and a combo raisin/cranberry cookie that were also very good.  The young man who worked there was friendly and helpful and I appreciate that he was able to attend to us promptly without making us feel rushed.  I think if my wife and I liked eating cookie dough, this place might even get a higher rating, but since we only like our cookies fully baked, we will settle on a 4-star rating with only the limit on the number of options keeping it from being a 5-star.  Review #2641

At a recent Yelp Event, I had a brief conversation with Stacy P and Niki B about vanishing communities that draw people in just for the experience of being there.  Maybe you'll find something that you don't find elsewhere.  With Nashville, IN undergoing a huge property sale, we were trying to think of places that are similar that could carry on.  I think with more shops like the Hero House, Fountain Square could become one of those places.  I know, it's a comic shop and it carries all the current titles as well as having an inventory of graphic novels, clothing, and merchandise.  But, having this clean and organized business right in the heart of Fountain Square gives locals access to this type of entertainment as well as offering visitors something to do during the daytime.  I mean, although I can eat a lot, I want more than just bars and restaurants if I am going to drive 40 minutes into the city to grab lunch or an early dinner.  I feel that getting a wide variety of independent shops to fill in the spaces between the places to eat would make Fountain Square a place to visit and stay awhile (other than just drinking in a bar.)  Between Virginia Avenue, Shelby Street, and Prospect, there are lots of spots that are just a short walk from each other that if business owners wanted to take a chance, there could be a ground swell of visitors to the area.    And Hero House is a great example of what a community needs:  Friendly staff who know their products and have a solid inventory of items available.  I found free street parking out front and around the corner.   Plenty of room inside without feeling like it was overcrowded.  It made for a pleasant shopping experience.  I applaud this small business for fitting in with the bigger picture of what Fountain Square can be.  It looks to be a really nice addition to the area.  Review #3307

Another hidden gem in restaurant offerings of Indy is this standard bearer for Greek food.  It's located between McCarty and I-70 on South Meridian, just a couple blocks from the Wholesale District.  It has a small parking lot behind the building and there is free street parking also available.  I really think that whether you give this restaurant a 4 or 5 depends upon which combination of flavors you pick on your visit.  I've tried their sampler (not listed on the menu, but you can ask for it if you have a huge appetite), and realized there are some items I like, and others that I REALLY like.   On this visit, I wanted to try something new, so I started off with the Avgolemeno, a creamy chicken stock based soup with egg and orzo pasta and a large wedge of lemon on the side which you can squeeze to your own preference level.  My server suggested trying it without the lemon first to get a base level, and then start squeezing the lemon to suit my own preference.  Great suggestion!  I still used all the lemon that was provided, but appreciated the change as the acidity added to the depth of flavor.  And though I stumble when pronouncing it, I was able to point at the menu and select the Spanakotiropita (spinach and cheese pie).  The dish comprises three phyllo hand-rolled triangles stuffed and baked to a crispy golden brown edge.  These were also very good, but I kept looking for some type of sauce to dip them in since they could have benefited from just a little more oomph in seasoning.  The dish also came with a side-salad and two pieces of Pita bread.  My visit was early in the lunch hour and I was in and out in just over a half hour.  The waitress was very cordial and did a good job bringing ice water and clearing the empty plates.  She even left the bill with me and instructions to pay her instead of having to walk up to a cashier (at my convenience.)  I assume she thought I may have to get back to work and wanted to expedite my closing process.  The only fault was she could have asked if I wanted anything else (maybe to go) before placing the bill.  Review #827

Although the food is pretty standard fare for Hoosier Mexican restaurants, the service and space lift it above the mediocre crowd.  First, the space is in a strip mall with plenty of free parking.  The space is also quite large, but because it is sectioned into smaller rooms, the noise level in each colorfully decorated room never got too loud.  The staff who worked here sounded more like Hoosiers than Mexicans, so there was excellent communications;  no wondering if the server understood our orders or requests.  The staff also made sure to check in with us to be sure we had enough of the complementary chips and salsa as well as keeping us supplied with beverages.  The food, as mentioned before, was pretty standard lunch fare.  My wife ordered a chicken chimichanga that came with rice and beans and a guacamole salad.  I ordered a beef (ground) burrito that came with pico de gallo and rice.  I will mention that the rice was more buttery tasting than spicy which was a pleasant surprise/change of pace.  Some might not like its lack of authenticity, and they can write about it in their own reviews.  For me, I just wanted something with good flavor and that was what I got.  Review #3326

The Antique Emporium surprised me with the number of large pieces of furniture that I saw in this double spaced strip mall shop.  Though the shop looks small from the front, having the second area to the west doubles the space making it possible for large pieces to fit in, often as cabinets, with loads of small items.  There are collections of vinyl albums, vintage clothing, dishes, coins, books, and just about anything you can think of.  Not the largest collection, but decent quality pieces.  Review #2019

I decided to pick up something for dinner (take out) while on the north side.  So, I stopped in Yujo to see what they had.  I will state up front that I am not a huge fan of ramen at dine in places.  I struggle with eating noodles with chopsticks and even if given a fork, they often serve large slices of meat (pork in my case) that are too big for one bite.  The broth drips when you lift it and trying to bite through the meat and then returning the remaining part back into the bowl seems awkward if not just odd.  So, I really appreciated that my 'to go' order placed the broth in one bowl and the ramen/meat/other stuff in a separate sealed bowl.  Once home, I was able to place the non-liquid contents on a cutting board, and cut them all to bite sized pieces.  I then divided the pieces between two bowls and added the reheated broth to each.  Ramen bowls are notoriously huge servings for one person.  The flavor of my Yuzu Signature was wonderful!  The broth had a chicken & pork stock base with a bit of lemon zest for brightness of flavor.  The chashu (braised pork belly) was thin, but originally was a large slice (more lean with just a bit of fat).  The rest of the flavors worked really well with the broth and meat for a hearty dish.  I also ordered a half sweet Strawberry Assam (milk tea) but they were out of boba (I wonder if they were going to make any for the evening shift since the place closes at 3 and reopens at 5.)  The flavor was good, but without the boba, was less than expected.  Overall, I found the food quite tasty and the service, though a bit inexperienced due to the newness, was pleasant and helpful.    If you are a fan of ramen, check the place out.  If you are new to ramen, I recommend getting it to go so you can practice at home.  Review #3296

I hadn't been to Datsa Pizza (great name BTW) in a long time and decided to stop by for one of their lunch specials.  The building, just east of the Central Library, is very small but does have some additional patio seating when the weather is more pleasant.  Somehow, they still manage to fit a small stage inside.    If you want to place an order to go, the counter and kitchen is to the right as you enter.  If you wish to dine in, there is limited seating to the left.  I wasn't sure if there was waiter service (there is), so I went to the counter to ask.  They assured me that they normally seat you and take your order, but since I was at the counter, I could go ahead and place my order to speed things up.  I made my choice, paid, and then grabbed a seat by the front window.    I had ordered the lunch pizza special.  For about $10, I got an 8" pizza that came with a drink, and a choice of a side salad or two bread sticks or chips.  The pizza comes with a selection of free ingredients that you can get any or all of (Sweet or Spicy sausage, pepperoni, bell pepper, onion, and Mushroom.)  They also have a variety of other items for a small upcharge (no substitutions for the free items).    Before long, my drink and then my side salad arrived.  The salad was mostly iceberg lettuce, but had red onion, tomato, cheese, and croutons and my choice of dressing.  All the ingredients were fresh and crisp.  Soon, my pizza arrived cut into four slices.  I could see the steam coming from it, so let it sit a little while to avoid the dreaded roof of mouth burn!  The crust had a nice browned crispness which I liked.  The ingredients, seemed to be evenly distributed.  The only negative I found was that there wasn't much seasoning in the sauce.  They do have some hot pepper flakes in a shaker on the tables, but I was more interested in the sauce having a bit more flavor.  Otherwise, the pizza was pretty good.  Just enough to be filling without making me feel stuffed.  I appreciated the staff checking in to see if the pizza was okay.  It seemed like the staff really cared about the quality of their product.    I don't go out for pizza often, but I will keep Datsa Pizza in mind for when I do.    p.s.  They have free parking in their own lot if you need to drive there.  Review #565

When I heard that Flat 12 Brewing had a new restaurant open in their building, I made a point of heading downtown to check it out.  Turn 3 Chicken & Waffles is only in its 3rd week as of the time of my visit, so it has a somewhat limited menu of breakfast items that are served all day during the same hours as the brewery.    Although the restaurant has its own space on the rear left as you enter, you can order food at the Flat 12 bar which has the menu.  Your bartender/server can place the food order for you.  (Note that the food you order is placed on the same bill as your beer orders from Flat 12, so you don't have to worry about fishing out your credit card twice!)  The four food options available are:  Chicken & Waffles, Breakfast Burrito, Breakfast Scramble, and Breakfast Pizza.  Within the last three options, you get your choice of meats:  ham, bacon, or chorizo.  You can also get Sriracha sauce if you need a bit more heat.  I ordered the Breakfast Burrito that comes with sides of tortilla chips, salsa, and cheese sauce.  The burrito was huge and filled with things like diced potatoes, scrambled eggs, pepper and red onion, jalapeno, and cheese.  The burrito is served without any toppings on it, but you could use some of the salsa or cheese sauce.  The chef said he was looking into viable options to offer a "dressed" version of the burrito as opposed to the current hand held version.  (If you need silverware, just let them know and they will bring it for you.)  And the taste? Wonderful!  I'm a breakfast lover anyway, so this option of a hearty breakfast meal really went well with me.  And I liked how it paired with the flight of beer I had as well.  No weird side tastes, just good beer and a tasty burrito.  Hopefully, as more customers start checking out their food, the restaurant will add some of the best suggestions to meet their needs.  For now, they are off to a good start.  Review #2541

This location of BBW is one that contains the White Barn candle section in the back half of the store towards the checkout counter.  There are lots of sales, especially during the holiday season.  My wife also enjoys the foaming soap products while I prefer the candle section.  Plenty of room to move about without feeling crowded too!  Review #1926

I was impressed with Taylor's Bakery.  Not only do they offer a lot of cakes, but there are counters full of pastries, and displays with popcorn, house ice cream, and assorted other snacks.  I didn't show up until nearly noon, and was impressed that there was still a nice selection of pastries to choose from.  I picked up a crispy flat nutty one that I knew my wife would like (I just had to make it home without eating it so that she could enjoy it!)  They also had some really large "alligator" pastries that were more than I wanted on my visit.  But I did find some other items that were sized more for the individual.   I picked out an apple Danish that had a nice balance of chew, sweetness, and tartness to make for a tasty treat.  They also had mini-Danish which are rolled like a cinnamon roll instead of laying flat with a pool of jelly in the center.  I picked up a few of these that only take a couple bites each:  Strawberry and Pecan.  I appreciated the easy parking in the lot in front of the place, though getting out of the lot onto 116th can be challenging.  Hint:  If you want to go west on 116th, use the road south of the business to get to the side street which has a stop light intersection at 116th.  Much easier and faster!  Review #1288

I've been looking forward to the opening of the new Popcorn Cafe at Just Pop In!  Located across the street from Public Greens and diagonally from BRICS, the corner is becoming a great place to stop!  Since it was lunch time, I was fortunate enough to get one of the 8 parking spaces in the lot behind the cafe.  They have a really nice ramp for access from the back of the building that rises along the south wall up into the elevated outdoor dining area.  The whole dining area is covered by a pergola or roof, and the seats are made of rattan.  My wife thought it just needed a little sand out front to remind her of Florida!  Inside, there are two dining areas on the main floor.  One has the bar on the west side and the popcorn counter is across the aisle next to it.  The north dining room has eight 2-top tables with benches on the outside, chairs on the aisle sides.  There is a very cool mural of a carnival with a Ferris Wheel.  The Ferris Wheel is also accented with colorful neon to make it look vibrant like a real one.  Upstairs are two more rooms with large communal seating and some additional comfy chairs.  The rooms can be open to each other or closed off by those large sliding barn doors if a room is reserved.  The menu is what I would suggest to be lighter faire.  There are salads, tomato soup, and "plates" of meat & cheese, crudites, or hummus.  They also have pairings of popcorn with beer or wine.  And there are four choices of desserts too.  There is a wine list, beer list, and sherry cocktails, mimosas, bellinis, and slushes for adult beverages.   There are "services" which are available for the meats (you can also get them a la carte) paired with your choice of bagel (I chose multi grain over plain or onion), choice of cream cheese (I chose herbed over plain), and meat (I chose Tuna Salad instead of Egg Salad, Lox/Smoking Goose, or marinated veggies.)  The service also comes with "service vegetables" like tomato slices, red onion, cucumber, and radish quarters.  Throw in Dill Pickle popcorn to complete the service.  I really enjoyed the tuna salad service.  The flavors of the tuna with the cream cheese and bagel were delicious!  The bagel is toasted which brings out the roasted flavor of the grains and keeps the bagel sturdy when you spread your cream cheese, top with the veggies, and then spoon your tuna salad on top.  I loved the flavors, but the tuna (and my wife's egg salad) seemed a bit too watery, leaving lots of flavor on the plate.  If they can tweak it to be a little more solid, the filling will stay on the bagel better and make it easier to get all the good taste.  The cafe has a two-way liquor license so I think they have done an imaginatively good job of coming up with ideas for cocktails.  The flavor combo of my "Fritz" which uses Fino Sherry, Cappelletti, pineapple juice, lime juice and muddled cucumber was pretty good, but it didn't have the flavor punch of a hard liquor cocktail.  Good, just different.  Just one of those things where your mind thinks one thing while your tongue sends a different message.  Will have to try something different next time like a mimosa or bellini.  And if you don't fill up on the menu items, you can always stop by the popcorn counter (or order from the menu) to pick out some tasty snack.    Beautiful decor, an imaginative menu that would be great for lunch or for those nights you don't feel like eating anything heavy, and pleasant service make the Popcorn Cafe a fun place to check out.  Revised #36

I've never been a "cupcake" guy.  Too many store bought, dried out hockey pucks with some goo stuck on top with a few sprinkles.  Yuck!  But being adventurous in culinary pursuits, I stopped by Confectioneiress after having sampled some of the "bites" offered at a sister store to the east.  Would this be a taste changing experience?  You Betcha!  Located in a strip mall on Brendon Way, I pulled up to the store (plenty of parking) and went in.  I thought that since it was after lunch, the selection might be picked over and not very promising.  True, that the display cases looked about half full, but it looked like they still had items in eah variety, just not as many.    After being greeted, I let them know it was a "to go" order and that I wanted to get three cupcakes.  The server grabbed a box and started placing my order inside.  What is worth mentioning is that a false bottom of the box has rounded openings for the bottom of each cupcake to sit in so that they don't slide around and smash together.  AND there are additional notches in the openings to allow your fingers to get a good hold of each so you can pull the cupcakes out without damaging the icing on top!  Very practical and greatly appreciated! (see photo)  The cupcakes were delicious!  I got a pumpkin pecan, a red velvet, and a salted chocolate caramel.  I ate the red velvet promptly and it was everything I could want in a cupcake:  moist and colorful cake; rich icing that wasn't too sugary but rather, a blend of a savory and sweet (maybe some cream cheese?).  Delicious!  I waited until the next day to try the other two and shared those.  The pumpkin pecan was a hit too!  nice sized pieces of pecan on top that allow for that nutty crunch.  The cake was similar to pumpkin pie in flavor, but with the cake texture.  The icing was creamy and balanced out the flavor.  Another winner!   The salted chocolate caramel was okay, but for me, not on the same level as the other two.  The cake was fine, but the topping was just not as balanced as the others.    There were lots of items to choose from, so even if the ones I described aren't your personal favorites, look around.  They have lots of flavor combos.  I can definitely say these were the best donuts I have had.  Now don't start calling me "cupcake".  ;)  Review #1394

Wow, what a refreshing meal I had at Ali'i Poke!  The serving, though I only ordered a regular, was huge!  And the bonus was that I didn't feel stuffed..rather, I felt content.    Tucked away in a mini stretch of quick restaurants where Indiana Avenue and 10th Street converge, you can enter the restaurant from the street or from the back where there is a parking garage which gives customers the first hour free.  The order counter starts on the right hand side as you face it.  You tell them the size (regular or large), then the base (sushi rice, brown rice, spring mix salad, or tortilla chips).  The next step is your protein:  Ahi Tuna (three ways); Salmon (two ways); Tako (Octopus); Shrimp; or Tofu.  Then you either select one of the "signature bowls" or create your own.  Of the four signature bowls (a house version, a tropical version, a spicy version, and a traditional island version), I ordered the Maui Poke (tropical).  It comes with pineapple, cucumber, pickled ginger, seaweed salad, mango, scallion, sesame seeds, sesame shoyu, and a mango pineapple vinaigrette.  I also added some spicy crabmeat.  They also have sides like Miso soup, seaweed salad, and mango sweet rice.  But since the regular "bowl" was so large, I passed on the sides.  I decided to eat inside the restaurant and grabbed a free glass of lemon cucumber water.  The flavoring was subtle and refreshing.  The bowl itself is a little hard to mix at first since it reached the rim of the container it was served in.  But once I got some bites out of it, I was able to stir the ingredients around more so that I could get a better mix of flavors.  Note that near the water dispenser are plastic utensils and chop sticks.  The flavor of my order was similar to a teriyaki chicken with pineapple.  There was a sweet and savory base to it with the acidity of the pineapple and freshness of the mango adding more depth than I was expecting.  Really a great tasting combo.  I would gladly return for another meal here!  Review #1009

I'm normally a fan of Target.  I used to shop here for goods, and occasionally, groceries when I lived in Greenwood.  The store was generally clean, well stocked and organized.  Sometimes there weren't enough cashiers active, but not so bad that it was a regular problem.  On my latest visit, I was nearby and needed to get some items that I would normally get at my 'go to' Meijer near Camby.  On this visit, I was surprised how small this "supercenter' seemed comparatively.  I only had a few items on my list and wasn't able to get them here.  Total cereal?  Not here.  No brand (affordable) bird seed? Only overpriced smaller bags with a 250% higher price.  My regular frozen pizza wasn't here either.    A trip through the produce section was nice, but didn't have nearly the space and variety.  Was it always like this?  I guess this is a case where you think you've got something great and then you try something else and see the short comings.  It's hard to give this a five when I prefer someplace else.  Still, the store has a pretty good selection and if you are willing to make substitutions, you can make do.  I will still stop by when in need and in town, but 4 star is a more realistic expectation for this place.  Review #2700

Good food and cocktails.  Good service too!  Basically, it is what you would expect from a lounge under the St Elmo's brand.  But like the steak house, it gets too crowded.  (Visit the one in Fishers for comparison.)  They offer a nice variety of cocktails.  I went with the French 75 that is based upon an old recipe from Harry's Bar in Paris.  Nice flavor with a hint of lemon and splash of champagne.  I also tried the Sesame Seared Sashimi Tuna served over a mound of rice.  Excellent flavor when combined with the dipping sauce on the side.  But understand that you have to climb a flight of stairs to get here and the lounge is kept very dark with a bit of a reddish lighting.  It isn't exactly welcoming to older folks who may have trouble seeing the menu or have mobility problems.  (I didn't ask if they have an elevator in St Elmo's, but there wasn't any visible from the lounge.)  And because of the tight quarters, it can get loud.  If those things don't affect your experience, then you may give it a 5 star rating.  Prices are comparable to St Elmo's.  Review #3424

Here's a secret...there is a great place to grab breakfast on Michigan Road.  Apparently, it is a well kept secret because the place was more than half empty on a Saturday morning.    When I first entered, the visual impression was that it was like a lot of family diners; small and cozy, nice music in the background, self serve coffee (5 kinds!) on a side table.  There were a number of small tables to choose from and even a "bar" area which is where I chose since it is a "seat yourself" place.  Even looking at the menu names led me to believe this would be standard fare.  What a difference it makes to read a little closer!  I usually order Eggs Benedict when I go to a new place for breakfast.  If a place can make a delicious Hollandaise sauce AND make a great poached egg (two per order), then I figure they can handle all the standard bacon and eggs and omelet items.  Here, the double Eggs Benedict was picture perfect.  Soft yolks inside the eggs, toasted English muffins underneath, salty Canadian Bacon, and a thick and yummy Hollandaise.  Light as a feather, but full of flavor.  But the sides almost stole the show!  The dish comes with fresh fruit (chopped into bite sized pieces and full of color) and "Rosemary potatoes".  I wasn't sure what to expect with the potatoes, but the bite sized reds were accompanied by sweet potatoes, onions, & red bell pepper.  So good!  Yeah, rosemary isn't for everyone (my wife can't stand it) but I thought it paired well with the veggies and made for a wonderful dish that exceeded my expectations.  The service was friendly and the food came out in minutes.  I also ordered a croissant with strawberry jam to go and didn't have to remind the waitress.  When I saw the croissant, I initially thought there was a mistake.  It looked kind of like two large pieces of toasted bread.  But then I realized the the croissant was sliced horizontally and the sliced sides were either toasted or grilled to add a little crispiness to the bite.  Yum again!  And the strawberry jam was generously provided and the remainder will be used on some toast at home.    Sure, the price is more than a lot of fast food breakfasts, but you get what you pay for.  When's the last time you had a breakfast that made you say "Wow!"?  Bookmark this place while you can.  I have a feeling that the secret may be spreading soon!  Review #455

We stopped in for lunch on a Saturday afternoon.  There was plenty of parking and seating.  We selected a spot on the bar side of the L-shaped dining area.    There wasn't a list of beverages, so I strolled over to the bar where the beer was listed on a blackboard.  The bartender did a fine job in answering my questions and offered samples of the beers to help me make up my mind.  Knowledge in hand, I returned to my seat as the waitress returned with our water.  We then ordered our sandwiches of choice:  I had the Chicken Salad on Croissant while my wife ordered the Tenderloin.  After awhile, our sandwiches arrived with a side of onion rings.  Up to that point, everything was going pretty well.  Unfortunately, the sandwiches were underwhelming.  The tenderloin was a respectable size and the meat was fairly moist, but my wife thought it was too dry.  The coloration was also rather dark as to be either a bit over cooked or maybe the oil was not as fresh as it could be.  There was a nice bit of salt in the breading, but not much flavor other than that.  My croissant arrived with the top laying on the side to show how fully the sandwich was loaded with chicken salad.   Sadly, the top of the croissant was rather flattened and had a bit of an oily taste/finish.  I was expecting the croissant to be more "puffy" and flaky/crispy.  I assembled the sandwich and instead of a buttery flavor complimenting a mix of chicken, celery, and onion flavors, I got a rather bland, one dimensional flavor.  It wasn't bad, but just didn't have much flavor at all.    The onion rings were nicely breaded and had a good flavor, so they were probably the best part of the meal.    The service was friendly, but wasn't as efficient as many other restaurants.  My wife's iced tea ran out and we didn't get our waitresses attention until we were nearly finished dining.  So, if you are in the neighborhood, it may be a decent and reasonably affordable option.  But if you are willing to drive a little further or spend a little more, there are plenty of other places in Greenwood that will be more flavorful.  Review #73

I have taken the guided tour of the stadium and been to events held at the stadium, both on the field and in the conference rooms below.  So, my overall impression is quite favorable.  There seems to be generally comfortable accommodations in the seating for the big events without feeling packed.  Sure, a little more room between rows would make it easier for attendees to get passed each other, but we seemed to manage okay.  Although an effort has been made to make signs to help attendees navigate this huge space, I did find it somewhat confusing when fortune made using the ramps necessary.  There seems to be signs for the ramp system that lead to dead ends or closed doors without electronic opening buttons to push.  That required coordination between the guest in the wheel chair and myself on navigating through the openings.  Seems like it was awkward in general and could be dangerous in an emergency.    I like that the stadium hosts events of many kinds including overflow for the convention system conveniently located next door.  There are some dining options available, but considering the large number of attendees for the events, you need to either eat before arriving or plan on allowing enough time to get through the lines.    Most of all, having the stadium opens the possibility for attending events that would not be possible if the facility were not here.  Accessible from each side of town, the location is perfect for those staying downtown during a convention. For those in the suburbs, traffic quickly disperses from the area, unlike many of the waterfront stadiums which force all the traffic in a single exit route.  As someone who used to be stuck in traffic on Lake Shore Drive in Chicago, this is infinitely better!  The tour that is provided at a low cost during the week is informative and is generally held in groups small enough that allows for attendees to ask lots of questions.  The scale of the stadium is immense, especially when you stand on the field and look at the seating/roof area during the tour.  The engineering necessary for such a facility is mind boggling.  Overall, it is a stadium/facility that serves the community well.  Review #441

Although some of the prepackaged items available after hours have been a little disappointing, I have to say the actual meal I had on Thanksgiving Day was quite good.  I selected the roast turkey with two sides (green beans and dressing) and some delicious cranberry sauce for about $8 (including soda and tax).  Good price and good quality food.  There isn't much direction as you walk into the cafe.  There are multiple stations including salad, pizza, entrees, and desserts.  There are also the prepackaged sandwiches and salads available for someone on the go.  Beverages are self serve and you use trays to load up your selections and carry to a cashier at the entrance of the dining area.  Silver ware, napkins, and condiments are available beyond the cashier, but in three different locations which seemed odd.  The place seemed to have quite a few seats in different groupings and was generally maintained well.  You are expected to buss your own dishes to the trash and dish washing conveyor area.  Although I am not a big fan of places where meats are kept under heat lamps for long periods of time, I think going to an early lunch worked in my favor.  The turkey was moist and tender and generously portioned.  Not much interaction with the staff is needed, especially if you are familiar with the location of all the stations.  Review #452

This block of downtown Indianapolis has undergone several transformations and name changes, but now is a beautiful park with a fountain and obelisk in the center.  Originally plat 5, the block was designed and completed as a plaza in 1930.  A fountain and and obelisk were added in 1929 by Henry Hering.  The park was commonly known as Obelisk Square.  The obelisk rises 100 feet and is topped with gold leaf.  There are depictions of the four "foundations" of our society near the base of the obelisk:  Law, Science, Religion, and Education.  The fountain that surrounds the tower is also 100 feet across.  In 1976 for the nation's bicentennial, the park added the landscaping to convert what was once a concrete place into an actual park like setting.  Trees and lawn soften the appearance tremendously.  Further work was completed in 2004.  On the east and west sides of the fountain can be found (equally divided) the flags of the 50 states.  An American Flag can be found on both sides.  The park lies between the Indiana World War Memorial (to the south) and the American Legion Mall (to the north) which creates a nice expanse of green space and park like locations to stop by.  Review #1861

On south SR135 in that place where Greenwood and Bargersville  addresses get mixed, a brand new restaurant has opened that specializes in Vietnamese cuisine, Sushi, and Pho. (Yea for choices!) Roku (which means Good) Sushi & Pho opened in a strip mall just south of Stones Crossing near Tried and True Ale House.  There is a shared parking lot and as you approach the restaurant, the windows have the shades down for privacy inside, but tends to make it look like they aren't open.  Fortunately, there is a small sign by the door to let you know it's okay to come in.  Inside, the room is spacious.  A hostess desk is on your right when you enter and the mainly square room has the sushi counter at the back (the kitchen is not seen, but located behind that.)  There are a couple large televisions, lots of decorative plates along the north and south walls, and not much else for decoration.  The tables are a polished wood (no tablecloths) with wooden chairs.  Most of the seating is 4 top, while there are some longer communal tables and some booth seating along the walls.  After being seated, I was brought a menu and asked about my beverage.  They carry Coke products, a variety teas (hot and iced), and a few other options.  I don't believe they have a liquor license.  Since it was my first time (opening day), it took a while to read through the multiple page menu.  As stated before, they have a variety of food types, and there are even more options when you add in appetizers, salads, Vegetarian options, soups, and combos.  I came with an appetite, so I started off with an order of Salmon (sake) Nigiri (2 pc).  If you aren't familiar with the terminology, that means the salmon was raw and served over an oblong ball of rice.  The portion was the largest I've had!  Most places, I am able to pop each piece into my mouth all at once.  Not here!  I had to bite each one in half.  The flavor was really good, including the rice.  The salmon did look a little dry on top, not sure why, but it didn't affect the taste.  Oh, and at table side, they only had soy sauce, not the low sodium.  I didn't ask if it was available since I usually don't add it to my nigiri.  I also ordered the Dragon Roll which was large and colorful.  I like that the menu mentions which ingredients are inside the wrapper (Eel, cucumber, and avocado) and which ones are outside (more avocado, eel sauce, and spicy mayo).  Really nice flavor and the sushi held together well when picked up by chopsticks.  I also placed an order for Spring Rolls (listed under appetizers).  They didn't come out at first, but arrived after I finished my sushi roll and nigiri.  The serving (4 pieces, though the menu says 5) was crispy outside and was at a good temperature to bite right in.  (I've been steamed a few other places.)  The veggie mix included carrots, mushrooms, and cellaphane noodles (though the menu has a typo that calls them cellphone noodles. ha!)  The dipping sauce was very liquid and didn't stay on as well as some other restaurants I've been to.  The liquid didn't have that much flavor.  I was expecting it to be somewhat sweet and spicy.  And since I wanted to get as well rounded tasting as I could, I went ahead and ordered the Pad Thai Chicken.  This was the only disappointing dish of the meal.  The dish did have a lot of chicken cut into large strips which makes the lunch size price seem more reasonable.  But the chicken (breast meat) was overcooked and became dry, and in some bites, a bit rubbery.  Add to that they use a sweet tamarind sauce and the flavor just didn't work for me....a bit too sweet and a bit tart (?)...I'm not sure, but it was a house spin on flavor, not the traditional Pad Thai recipe you get elsewhere.    Since it was their first day, there were a few small delays and a slight mixup when a second batch of spring rolls showed up (I wasn't charged and didn't have room to eat them anyway!)  Through it all, the servers kept a good humor and did their best to keep everything moving.  I do have two suggestions for the management though:  Proofread your menus and have them reprinted.  I have found dozens of typos (I am not exaggerating!) and found it distracting when reading through.  The other suggestion is that when the wait staff stop by to see how I am doing or to tell me my order will be ready soon, they should take away the finished plates.  I had to request my used plates be removed after each course so that I had room.  It seems like a simple tweak, but one that will definitely be noticed.  Review #1250

Despite being a Saturday evening, we arrived here around 5 and had no trouble finding a table.  We grabbed a parking spot in the shared lot out front and were greeted as we entered.  We chose to sit in the dining area at one of the booths by the windows instead of the bar or dining room tables.  It took just a couple minutes for our waitress to show up which we used to look over the menu.  So when she arrived to get our beverage order, we knew what we wanted to order for dinner.  My wife ordered the Flashback Shrimp which is served in a paper cone with slaw.  The slaw was a creamy style and tasted fine.  The shrimp were breaded and large and had a mildly spicy taste.  I think there were six in the order.  The order also came with a small plate which made it easier to eat and avoided the paper becoming soggy when the slaw was moved.  I ordered the Flashback Burger which is a BMB (Big Mouth Burger), grilled to order with a charred outside and juicy center.  The bun was stacked high with the burger, bacon, cheddar cheese, and onion strings.  I also had them add lettuce, tomato, red onion, pickles, and mayo.  Really good sandwich but just a tad sloppy.  The only negative was that the fries, though plentiful, were unsalted and dry so that even table salt I added fell off.  They were a bit chewy like they had cooled off before serving.  Service was pretty good throughout the dinner which lasted less than an hour.  The room gets a little loud and if you sit near the entrance, the cold air of winter can be felt as new customers arrive.  Review #3662

I was really glad to see that BitterSweet had decided to reopen as a bakery after closing the doors a couple years ago on the restaurant.  I got a chance to talk with the owner/chef and the bakery is where her true passion lies.  And you can tell.  The sampling of Items I purchased were all delicious.    The zoning in Irvington makes it somewhat difficult to find this place.  There are lots of restrictions that are not "pro-business" which contributes to the high turnover rate of places in the area.  Anyway, the bakery's entrance is perpendicular to Washington Street and you enter from the parking lot that you access from behind the building.  (I told you it was tough.)  Inside, the space is plenty large enough for visitors and for baking.  Be careful as you walk in.  The floors are dark and instead of a step, there is a several inch slope that will challenge you if you aren't paying attention.  There is a sign, but maybe a lighter color flooring would help make the drop/slope more visible when coming in from the bright sunshine.  There is a large antique counter with glass displays of the baked goods that are available.  The owner makes a lot of items to order if you want to request something ahead of time.  Otherwise, you take your chances on what you will find when you arrive.  Fortunately, there are lots of goodies to try.  Maybe you want some cake.  Maybe it's cookies or lemon bars.  Some granola or a cup of coffee (or a bag of coffee beans.)  I had no trouble finding something I liked.  It was tough limiting myself!  Good quality, independent bake shop with a nice selection.  If you are in the area in the later part of the week/weekend, search this place out for something you are bound to enjoy!  Review #3064

For a long time, I've been getting some of my exercise by walking the Monon.  Sometimes it was a stretch in Broad Ripple from 54th up to near 70th.  Sometimes it was hunting public art from 21st down to 10th.  Maybe it was a stroll after dining in Broad Ripple or some place new in Carmel.  It doesn't really matter:  Wherever you are, you can count on there being a wide, paved trail with a center line letting users to know they should be on one side or the other to allow others to pass or be passed.  It's that simple.  There are long stretches where the trail is shaded which offers relief from the heat on summer days.  There also stretches where there isn't much to look at, so it motivates you to push on so that you can find some more cool stuff!  There are times when you will feel it's almost too crowded due to its popularity.  And there are times you might wish to see a friendly face because as twilight sets in and you are surrounded by woods, it can seem a little creepy without adequate lighting.  So know your limits and your comfort level before heading out.  There are some watering stations and restrooms along the way, but unless you are familiar with the area, you might miss them.  Review #1178

Tucked away just outside of downtown Indy is the newly launched/rebranded RAD Brewing.  The location has a history of fine brewing as the site of the former Flat 12 (note that they still make some of the Flat 12 favorites here.)   If you aren't familiar with the location, it is on the first north/south street (Dorman) east of where I-65/I-70 cut through downtown.  So, from downtown, you head east on New York (or Vermont) and turn left on the first street beyond the train tracks.  Street parking (free) is available on both sides of the street.  Inside the main entrance, there is a common area with restrooms, merchandise, and some family friendly seating.  On the left is the kitchen which has been branded RAD Burger.  On the right is the brewery/bar.  I've not tried ordering food directly from the restaurant section.  I've always gone into the bar and had the bartender take my order for food and beverages.  The bar area is open and spacious with even more room for an outdoor patio in nicer weather.  On my first visit on opening weekend, my wife and I grabbed lunch and I ordered a flight of their beer.  Understand that they are growing the number of RAD beers available (only a handful on opening week), but supplement the beers with their Flat 12 line, so you will have a huge variety of beer types available.  As more RAD beers are developed, most of the Flat 12 will go away with the possibility of a few of the large selling Flat 12 beers becoming a "Classic Line".    I tried a diverse line of brews in my flight (highly recommended for first timers).  These guys know good beer and I really enjoyed them.  My wife also ordered the nachos and I ordered one of their burgers "Chill Style".  The food was okay, but the cook made some mistakes in the ingredients and so it was a bit disappointing.  I pointed out the mistakes to the bartender and he adjusted our bill as a kind gesture.  The kitchen should get better with more familiarity of the menu.  They offer burgers, baskets, appetizers, some brunch items (from the former Turn 3 chicken & waffles menu) and desserts.  I stopped by just before Christmas for another flight and found that the RAD Brewing offerings had nearly doubled, so I was able to get another flight of completely different ales than the first time.  They still have a lot of the favorites from before.  On both occasions, the bartenders were friendly and though busy, wait times weren't bad for getting beer, food, or my check.  The bar part of the business is dog friendly since the food prep is done on the other side.  Just be aware of any animals if you choose to eat in the bar.  If the food quality gets up to the level of the beer, I will upgrade my rating.  I've enjoyed all eight of the new beers I've tried.  Review #3465

King Dough has some uniquely tasty pizza options including the Pork & Pine which I tried.  They also have salads, appetizers, and sandwiches along with a full bar.  The first expansion of this Bloomington restaurant is tucked away at the corner of Michigan St (one way west bound) and Highland.  They have some street parking along Michigan Place (side street) and a small lot on site if you are lucky enough to grab one.  The restaurant has a large pergola covered patio that leads into the dining area (but could use some signage letting you know where to enter.)  The dining area is bright and has glass garage doors that will open up to the patio during warmer months.  There is also a separate bar on the east side of the building next to the kitchen.  The staff were friendly and even though I was getting an order to go, offered me a beverage while I waited.  The pizza was ready in a surprisingly short time too!  The flavor of the pizza was really good.  The pork & pine comes with Turchetti's Canadian ham, pickled pineapple, pickled jalapenos, red sauce, and cheese.  The pickling was a great addition to the flavor depth as the acidity balanced the sharp flavors of the peppers and fruit so that when paired with the savory flavors, made for a full flavored bite.  My only real negative was that the pizza was charred on the crust (it bubbles quite a bit) and soggy in the middle which made most of the ingredients fall off or stick to the box in the center.  It didn't detract from the taste, but is a bit of a nuisance when the cardboard box gets soggy.  Maybe they could adjust the amount of baking powder so that it didn't bubble as much which would allow the center to cook just a bit longer.  I would have thought a pizza place could figure that out, but maybe they like soggy centers.  Me, not so much.  Review #2227

There is a really nice wine shop on the west side of Zionsville that features wines from around the world that you won't find elsewhere in the area.  I had the chance to talk with the owner as I was sampling some of the selections and found that this relatively new boutique opened in 2019.  She mentioned that she doesn't carry any wines you can find in a grocery store or any of the widely distributed local wines.  She does have a few local options, mostly seasonal, but prefers to direct customers to the actual wineries when she can.  So, you will find a nice balance of imports as well as California and Michigan wines here.  Although they have events scheduled almost daily, I stopped in right after lunch and the place was quiet.  After the owner took care of some managerial issues on the phone, she let me know that she sold wine by the ounce, the glass, or the bottle.  So, if I wanted to build a tasting flight, I could select an ounce of any wines that were on the multiple page list.  The tastings are priced based upon the specific wines selected, not some blanket price like you might find at a winery.  I had already eaten, and since I was by myself, I chose not to sample any charcuterie or cheese boards but they have a lot of options for the types of meats and cheeses that can be included.  The shop also has small tables for customers, as well as comfy sofa areas which are available.  I chose to sit at the large curved bar to make it easy for the owner to build my flight.  I like that I was able to ask questions about the wines and feel like I learned while there.  And the wines were really good.  Note that many are more expensive than what you will see at your local grocery or liquor store, but that's because these aren't the mass produced options.  But don't let that stop you from stopping by to check out the flavorful options that are here.  Review #3690

If my rating was based on flavor, this would be a 5 star place.  I purchased four different items from the "to go" section of the restaurant (to the right of the entryway) and I really liked every single item.  Not just simple sweetness, but layers of flavor even on the smallest items make them quite tasty.  I tried the Raspberry Rose Marie Antoinette pastry which is nearly five inches of macaron stuffed with cream and fresh raspberries.  Yum!  The chocolate chips have a light sprinkling of salt to cut through the deep rich semi-sweet chocolate taste.  The Magic Bars are thick layered combo cookies with everything but the kitchen sink added in.  And the almond croissant was light and crisp with no skimping on the almond flavor inside.  Know that the space is elegantly beautiful in its decor.  Opulence is seen throughout the restaurant and to go shop.  So, count on the prices here to be higher than your average bake shop.  And maybe, that's a good thing.  It may keep you from over indulging in sweets.  But there are some things that could be improved.  Even at 2 pm on a Wednesday, wait times were over a half hour to get something to go.  Part of the problem is that every piece that is purchased is individually packaged, either in a paper sleeve or in a separate box.  Then those are stacked in a bag.  All that takes time where other shops simply place items in a box with a slightly tacky bottom to keep them from sliding.  And the amount of packaging is really quite wasteful.  Maybe the demand will slow and wait times will be reduced, but considering how crowded the Broad Ripple shop has remained throughout the years, I am not confident that the owners are going to do much to address these delays.    So, if you have lots of time (and readily available credit), stop by for some delicious baked goods.  Review #2810

The ice cream and gelato we ordered were okay.  Pretty standard for homemade ice cream shops.  Although the service was prompt, when they asked if we wanted the homemade waffle cones (which were fresh and crisp), they made no mention that they were $2.50 per cone (without the ice cream!).  My bill (with tax) for two cones (one single, one double) was over $16!  I had seen the photos on Yelp and in those photos, the cones were only $1 or $1.25 extra.  Be advised to look at the prices before you order.    The shop was clean and had a lot of room for visitors.  Parking is limited to the available street parking.  Review #1032

This park is primarily a sports park with numerous baseball fields.  The good news is that there is a lot of paved parking for when there isn't a game on.  There park has a couple shelters and there are playgrounds near each.  Some of the equipment is unique with playground pieces that look like trees, or the stages of a butterfly, or a bee.    The park also has tennis and volleyball courts on the west end of the park.  Perk:  The park is within easy walking distance of Mrs Curls Ice Cream shop!  The park definitely has a lot of features, but doesn't have any "wow" features of some of the more modern parks in central Indiana.  Review #777

I stopped in for lunch on Friday (7/1) right as the restaurant opened.  Parking was easy since this is a strip mall restaurant, especially in appearance from the outside.  But once you step inside, you see that this restaurant was designed to be a permanent fixture.  I was very impressed how completely my expectations changed seeing the decor.    I was greeted immediately and was given a table near the window even though I was by myself.  They have a separate lunch menu which has some a la carte selections but also has some great value "specials" for about $8.  While I looked over the menu, I opted for the ginger tea.  It was brought out quickly in a white ceramic tea pot (enough for three mugs of tea.)  Very tasty.  I am looking forward to sampling some others.  I went with the "Cashew Nut" special and was able to select from a variety of proteins.  I went with chicken.  The special comes with soup, salad, a spring roll, and rice.  I was pleased that I got to select from mild, medium, hot, and very hot seasoning.  I went with medium.  Soon, my soup arrived.  I asked twice what type of soup it was, but I wasn't quite sure my Hoosier ears understood.  I believe I had some "tom yum" soup made with spicy lemongrass.  Whatever it was, it tasted great!  Just a bit of spiced heat to add another layer of taste.  Almost as soon as I finished the soup, out came my entree.  Very colorful and appetizing.  The spring roll was crispy on the outside but not overcooked inside.  There was a small cup on my plate that was unidentified, so I tasted it and realized it was the sweet/sour sauce for the roll.  Excellent flavor enhancement.  The salad was chilled lettuce with some red cabbage and sweet house dressing.  There must have been a full cup of white rice to go along with the entree which included cashew, carrot, mushroom, water chestnut, bell pepper, baby corn, & onion.  Again, the flavor was good and there was enough crunch on the carrots and chestnuts to offset the softer veggies.  A great value for a low price.  Good service and good flavors.  If I had to make a suggestion, I would ask that an entree called "cashew nut" would have a lot more cashews.  I ate about half the entree before I got to my first one.  Seems like a simple fix to me.  And, although the service was quick and polite, there was very little dialogue.  Maybe it was a cultural thing, but I prefer being comfortable enough to ask the wait staff what they recommend, especially when I try a cuisine that I have little experience with.  If you are free for lunch in Greenwood, stop by and give this place a try.   Review #69

It takes confidence in your beer to open on the same day that Sun King opened their new location in Fishers.  It takes confidence in your beer to open a business named "18th Street" (based upon their origin in the "Region") while actually located on 10th Street.  And it takes confidence to expand your business into a neighborhood that is slowly transitioning to being visitor/resident friendly.  But after stopping by on opening day, I now understand why they have so much confidence!  I had only had one of their beers before (Rubicon IPA), so I was looking forward to getting a flight of their beers to go along with one of the daily lunch offerings.  Although there is free street parking on two sides of the building, I found a spot in the lot directly south of the brewery.  If you know where Love Handle used to be, then you know where to find 18th Street Brewery.    I entered on the north east corner and saw a small dining area to the right and the bar/counter seating directly ahead.  They don't offer wait service here, so you need to go to the counter to place your order (including food.)  Fortunately, there are lots of one page menus on the tables if you aren't greeted by one of the staff as you enter.  It's a seat yourself kind of place.  Although I asked about flights, they didn't have their flight boards/glasses ready yet (should be a couple weeks.)  However, because the bartender wanted to make things right, he allowed me to sample four of their beers.  I liked all four so it was a tough decision to select a pint, but I went with the "Temporal Purgatory" Pale Ale (5.9% ABV) which tasted good on its own as well as when paired with my Brisket Panini & side salad.  I also liked the "Lake Street Express" Session IPA (4.7%), the "Best Patio" Pilsner (4.9%), and the "Fox & the Hunted" Porter (5.2%).  The lunch offerings aren't numerous, but they had a few options including vegetarian to choose from.  Not your typical bar food, the flavor was really good!  My panini was toasted to a nice crunch on the outside while the brisket was as tender and flavorful as pot roast.  The grilled onion and melted white cheddar rounded out the flavor, especially with the horseradish dip on the side.  The side salad was also tasty with their Green Goddess dressing and shaved strips of cheese.  And the salad was cut to bite sizes, not large leaves that require cutting.  The staff, though very busy, were friendly and if you have a little patience, you get noticed here.  They also bring your food out to you and clear your space/dishes when you are through.  So glad to see this new addition to the near east side.  They are right across the street from the newly opened Healthy Harvest Market which can use your support too!  Review #3611

Although this place feels a little more cozy than our regular El Rodeo in Mooresville, I can't say I enjoyed it as much.  Sure, we were seated promptly and brought out our beverages and complementary salsa/chips, but even those weren't as good.  My wife likes a margarita and this one was served in a standard beverage glass.  It wasn't as frozen, but did seem stronger in alcohol than she likes.
