The salsa and chips were okay (I can't complain too much since they were free), but the salsa seemed thin and with less flavor.  My wife ordered a taco salad with chicken.  It was fine.  Not much better or worse.  I ordered the Carne Asada tacos that come with beans and rice on the side.  I noticed that the dish was served differently than I am used to.  These were on an open rack already prepared with some small sauces and minced pickled veggies on the side.  Our regular place serves the torillas wrapped in foil while the steak and veggies are served on a searing skillet that brings out the fond in the steak.  This meat was dull in color and lacked flavor and became a bit rubbery from cooking at too low a heat level.  It just wasn't as flavorful as our regular El Rodeo.  The food was okay.  The service from the kitchen was quick and the waitress didn't keep us waiting too long at any point.  But I can't see coming back here when there is another El Rodeo that is closer to my home and that I consider my favorite place for Carne Asada tacos in the metro area.  Review #3661

Back in 2015, this Tex-Mex Barbecue Taqueria made the Indianapolis Monthly list of Best New Restaurants, so while on the north side, I decided it was time to stop by for dinner.  So glad I did!  They have a front entrance which has a hostess stand and seats the family dining half of the restaurant.  They also have a bar entrance around the side which has easy access to the limited on site parking.  The bar area seems to be sunken compared to the dining area and was generally darker in atmosphere than the family room.  The family room is filled with an eclectic collection of skeletal and Mexican themed artwork.    I started with the small order of chips and salsa.  The chips were easily shareable in size and I never did finish them even when the salsa ran out and I used them on my side of guacamole.  The salsa was exceptionally good using smoked tomatoes in the mix.  Very tasty!  The chips were lightly salted and tasted fresh and crisp even without the salsa or guac.  They aren't free, but for $3, I got plenty!  I ordered the Border Quesadilla based upon some recommendations and enjoyed that too!  The chicken option was my choice and I could taste the barbecue flavor even without adding one of the four house barbecue sauces (they have hot sauce too!)  The Quesadilla came with pico de gallo and cilantro sauce on the side.  The only negative was that the serving paper under the meal became a bit soggy and tore when I tried using my knife and fork to cut the quesadillas into bite sized pieces.  (The paper sometimes stuck to the bottom, so keep an eye that you aren't scooping up the paper too!)  I tried a house Margarita served over ice, not frozen.  I paid an extra dollar to add strawberry flavor to it and it was okay, just not my favorite.  I don't drink Margaritas usually, so if you are looking for a recommendation here, you should probably look to someone else's review for the drinks.  I sat in the dining area and the service was great!  Very friendly, with recommendations when asked and a personable manner.  Checked back at reasonable times and got my bill and check out swiftly.  Definitely a great dining experience!  Review #415

Wow!  What a fantastic night of upscale dining.  Great food, great service,  and great atmosphere make it worth every penny!  Look, I know some folks have problems with high end restaurants and want something for nothing.  But when you get what you pay for, it's great to feel like you had a dining experience, not just another night out.  For our first visit to Tony's (this is the third restaurant in this chain out of Cincinnati), we braved the cold weather and parked in the nearby Circle Centre mall ($3 parking for up to 3 hours), walked through the Artsgarden, and down into the Claypool Courts where there is an entrance to Tony's without having to step outside in the cold!  We stepped in and were greeted by the staff and directed to the hostess' desk.  Since we arrived a bit early, we were asked to wait in the bar area until our reservation.  We were brought ice water and a couple of us ordered cocktails.  My friend had a Cucumber Negroni made with Hendricks Gin that he raved about.  I tried the Raspberry Mule served in a metal cup that everyone wanted to taste.  The drinks were $12, but since they were delicious, nobody complained.  Soon, we were seated in the opulent dining room.  The ceiling was lined with curved wooden ribs that were beautiful.  Many of the tables were booth style (note that they did have a step up into the seating area, so be careful and don't forget the step when you leave) though they did have some standard four top tables.  We were greeted by Jordan who had such an amazing voice we couldn't figure out why he wasn't on stage someplace.  Easy to hear and understand, his voice was easy going and welcoming and he took care of us all evening.  We started with a complementary bread course (crispy crust with warm and soft bread in the middle) served with warm whipped butter and bourbon butter that had a hint of cinnamon in it.  My wife wasn't sure she would ever move on to the first course since she loved the bread!  Since we opted for the Devour Indy menu which was $45 per diner, we had a reduced number of options.  But don't think that lessened our dining experience.  The portions were really large and the service didn't suffer because we were keeping our costs down.  Truly professional!  In our party of four, two went with the crab bisque soup with large chunks of crab that got rave reviews.  Again, this was a large bowl, not just a cup.  I went with the Caesar Salad which comes with shredded cheese and an ornate cheese twill.  Not spectacular, but everything was fresh and tasty.  For our second course, we all tried something different.  Jordan brought out extra plates so we could share tastes of the meals.  My wife ordered the Rig-A-Tony pasta dish made with house ground prime steak.  It had a somewhat spicy sauce that grabbed her attention right away, but didn't get too spicy.  My friend ordered the New Zealand Lamb Chops that were served popsicle style.  He went with a medium rare and I must say it was the finest lamb I've had.  Very tender and moist.  It came with a marinated Romaine heart and fingerling potatoes.  His wife ordered the Organic Scottish Salmone that came with an al dente green bean salad and hazelnuts.  I somehow missed getting a sample, but was told it was quite good.  I went with the Tournedos Rossini which are two small rounds of steak topped with Foie Gras Terrines, Madiera sauce, with charred asparagus, mashed potatoes, and small slices of bread underneath.  The steak was cooked to a tender perfection.  My only complaint is that I'm not a fan of foie (ground liver) on my steak, since the texture is somewhat dryer than that of the steak (my brain thinks overcooked steak though it wasn't), so for the second steak, I removed the terrine from the bite and enjoyed the beef more.    For dessert, my wife and friends all were served huge servings of Traditional Bread Pudding (no raisins) with a Bourbon Hard sauce and mixed berries.  Yum!  I went with a Chocolate Mouse that was a recipe from another Cincinnati restaurant that won awards for their dessert.  The cool part was the mouse was served inside an edible semi-sweet chocolate cup with sliced strawberries and a cookie.  It was a little difficult to manage with a spoon, but it was chocolate and I was determined, so I made it work!  Great flavors.  The service and management of the place were fantastic.  From the young man who made sure our water glasses were filled and used plates removed, to the general manager who stopped by to chat, everything was delightful.  The GM found out my friend loves Hendricks Gin and brought out a limited series Hendricks for him to sample.  Very cool!  From start to finish, it was a wonderful evening and with the Devour pricing, we knew how much to expect to pay.  No runaway bill from ordering.  If you want a wonderful night out, stop in at Tony's!  Review #2144

This southeast side park is a gem for youth sports leagues and families.  In 1921, Wilmer and Edna Christian donated about 40 acres of property to the city and when added to the city's additional purchases of land, created this 62 acre park.  The park has a lot of open & wooded greenspace between the north and south drives of E Pleasant Run Parkway.  To the south of that (east of Sherman), the park is filled with numerous team sports fields and courts (baseball, football, basketball, and tennis!)  There are a couple shelters located in the park and some randomly scattered picnic tables.  Grills are on site too for those who want to rent the shelters for a gathering.  Because the park is so large, the hiking is great for those who like mileage without the challenge of elevation.  Large wooded areas exist outside the ball fields.  There is a family center which is free but does have specific hours for pursuing activities.  Near the family center is a large playground and to the west, a splash park is available during summer months.  There are also several parking lots making it easier to access the facilities without having to walk extensive distances.  The park seemed to be in good to great condition.  My only concern is access to restrooms and water fountains for such a large park.  Review #542

I had been to the previous business at this location and decided to give this new Burmese restaurant a try.  They have made a name for their Burma Milk Tea that is served warm, creamy, and delicious.  After parking in the space along the side of the business, I entered a small area before entering into the large dining/cooking space.  There are seats on the one side and a long bar with individual seats on the other.  I didn't see any staff in the room and decided to go sit at the bar and grabbed a menu.  After a few minutes, a waitress showed up and greeted me.  I told her I wanted to try the milk tea and one of the appetizers.  Unfortunately, they have a large menu filled with photos, but only the photos with prices on small labels are available.  So, no appetizer for me.  I decided to order the Beef Curry which comes with about 2 cups of long white rice.  The beef is spiced and the sauce that comes with it is great to mix some rice into.  The beef was generally tender, though I did get one gristly piece that was discarded.  The dish also comes with a broth/soup that when I asked about it, was told "chicken".  The soup had a little heat to it and only had diced green onion, but it was quite pleasant  Once the waitress was in the room, she was there the entire time and my food and bill were delivered promptly.  I didn't have any trouble in communication.  She did check to see how I liked it and even brought me a second bowl of soup when I said that it was very good.  Although I enjoyed my meal, the atmosphere of the restaurant needs a lot of work.  There was an unpleasant aroma when I sat at the bar.  Kind of a stale air smell even though they had the ventilation going.  That smell was there from the previous business (I checked my write up.)  So, I enjoyed the food and the service (even though only one person was working the front of the house), but not the atmosphere.  Note:  The parking that surrounds the building is angled, so I suggest entering on the north side of the building and then driving around to find parking.  (Entrances on both the north and south sides of the building.)  Note 2:  They also share the front part of the building (street side) with an Asian Grocery that has an open door to the restaurant.  Review #3509

I was pleasantly surprised to hear that a new brewery franchise out of Louisville had recently expanded to Indy to give locals a different set of tastes to choose from on their beers and ales.  Located across from Elmo's on Illinois, there is plenty of affordable parking inside the attached parking garage or in the mall parking across the street.  To look at the place, you would still think it is the RAM because much of the signage has not been updated  to reflect the new business.  Even inside the restaurant/brewery, there is still Ram merchandise being sold.     So let me move on to what I like about Goodwood Indy.  First they have good food inside so you don't have to mess with ordering from someplace else.  They also are open on Mondays which is a rarity downtown.  They are also open mid afternoon, so if you are late to lunch or want an early dinner or something to tide you over until later, you can get it here!  My wife and I like dining early since we live in the suburbs and like to avoid rush hour traffic and still be able to get good seating before the restaurants get too crowded or loud.  Mid-afternoon was perfect for us to be able to pick our own seating and carry on a conversation without shouting.   Because they are a brewery, there were lots of new (to me) beers to choose from.  All were on tap and many were barrel aged in various types of woods.  The tie in to Louisville, home of the Louisville slugger bats used in baseball.  I tried a variety of their barrel aged ales and found the aging didn't overwhelm the ales.  However, I was surprised how little I noticed the wood taste on many of the brews, so none of their brews really stood out as a must order again.  Maybe I just need to get used to the flavors.  I will say that the bourbon barrel stout which is used in the chili (along with brisket) was good.    As far as food, I ordered a 6 pc wing which comes with a variety of sauces to choose from (served on the side to reduce sticky fingers.)  I selected a Walnut Brown BBQ sauce which I found really tasty (mild heat at most).    I also recommend the Truffle oil tots for fans of crispy nuggets.  My wife ordered the regular tots, but received the seasoned ones which were way too salty.  She didn't finish them.  She also ordered the Classic Burger which is double pattied and makes it a BMB (Big Mouth Burger) that she needed to slice to be able to eat like a slice of cake.  Thought it had a nice charring on the beef and lots of toppings.    One last negative that took away from the experience was that we had considered dining outside on the patio in the afternoon, but there were homeless people wandering within a couple feet of our seats and made my wife uncomfortable.  A group was standing just down the sidewalk between the seating and the entrance to the parking garage.  Not sure what the restaurant can do other than put up some more barricades between the tables and the sidewalks.  So, I advise dining inside if that makes you uncomfortable.  Review #3945

Did you know you could stop in for lunch without having to make reservations for "high tea"?  I was in the Carmel Art District around lunchtime and decided to stop by to try one of their lunch options.    Most of the interior is laid out with four or more guests per table, but fortunately, they had a single table for one near the entrance.  I gladly accepted it when greeted by the hostess/server.  The interior is filled with English images that go with the elegant table settings.  The menu is filled with options though all are of English origin.  I went with the "Sandwich Selection" option for my meal.    The Sandwich Selection offers five quarter sandwiches from three varieties:  a. Cucumber, cream cheese & dill on white; b. English Cheddar cheese and Grandma's green tomato chutney on white; and c. Coronation chicken salad with mild curry and dried cranberries on wheat.  I also got a side option as part of the meal (side salad for me.)  The sandwiches were all good!  The first was mildly flavored with a nice crunch from the cucumber and just enough dill to keep it interesting.  The second was my favorite as the chutney added a noticeable punch in flavor intensity of the first option.  Delicious!  The third had a nice balance between the chicken, the curry, and the creamy (almost egg like) taste of the dressing.  The salad (I chose balsamic dressing) was mostly field greens with cherry tomatoes and red grapes (both sliced).  I was surprised at the tartness of the thin dressing.  Still good, but different from balsamic dressings I've had elsewhere that were a bit more creamy and deeper, vinegary in flavor than here.  My only negative was that the bread was dry on all the sandwiches.  I'm not sure why, but it was noticeable enough that it affected my enjoyment.  A+ for the flavors, but a C for the bread.    Parking is limited to street parking on adjacent roads or one of the public lots.  Range Line Road has no parking available out front.  Note:  First time Yelpers get a 10% discount on their meal by checking in before checking out!  Review #961

While in the area to photograph a mural sponsored by Chuck's, I decided to stop in and support this fairly new (2018) business.  The traditional Coney Island hot dog is available here, but I suggest trying the "Detroit Dog" for something tasty and new in the area.  It easily bested the traditional in my opinion.  Finding Chuck's is easy, but getting into the parking lot is a bit challenging.  I literally circled the block to figure it out.  There is an alley next to the fire station and if you pull into the alley from 10th St, you can get access into the spacious paved lot next to the building that is home of the restaurant and the barber shop.  The restaurant is long and narrow and is decorated with all things Detroit.  Lots of Lions and Tigers stuff on the walls.  At the back of the dining area is an order counter with a bench for waiting on the right and bar stool seating on the left.  I was greeted and when I asked about the Detroit Dog, I was pleased that the young man working the desk had lots of information that made it clear.  (I just wish I could remember all the details.)  Anyway, it turns out the Detroit Dog is really popular there and offers a different spin than the Coney Island or the Chicago style dogs.  The Detroit Dogs come on a super light and fluffy bun with the dog covered with a Detroit style chili sauce, cheese, and crispy bacon pieces.  Really good!  The Coney Island comes with the same bun and dog, chili, onions, mustard, and if you want it, shredded American Cheese.  It was good, but pretty standard.  The fries I ordered were plentiful and were spiced/seasoned which included a lot of black pepper.  Nice flavor but the fries were just a bit too soggy to be 5 star.  Good flavor, but the seasoning was a bit inconsistently applied.  Some a little bland, others rather spicy.    The meal only took about ten minutes from the time I ordered, so the wait was very reasonable.  If you are looking for something different and want to support another local business while doing it, give Chuck's a try.  And get the Detroit Dog!  Review #2930

For those who prefer their parks to be for hiking and enjoying nature, this is the side of Central park for you!  The densely wooded park has both old and new forest trees and has a variety of trail paths to walk on.  Some are paved, some are mulch, and wherever there is a chance of getting wet feet, they have put in elevated boardwalks.  Several of the trails have information plaques that may contain historical information about the area or botanical information about the trees that grow there.  On the Woodland trail, there is a place on the northwest side of the loop where the trail opens up into a prairie (the trail runs along the edge of the woods.)  There is also a creek that runs through the woodlands and the trail has an overlook to get a nice view of the water.    There is plenty of parking that is generally centralized and a shelter area for those who may want to picnic.  Several picnic tables are scattered along the trails as well.  A restroom that uses ventilated pit latrines for disposal is located near the parking lot.  If you can't stand those, the sign directs you to the community center to the west of the parking lot.  Everything seems to be well maintained and because there is virtually no elevation change, the trails are rated as easy with the longest (Woodland) trail being somewhere around a mile in length.  And that is one of the drawbacks of the park:  There isn't much to see other than trees.  Other parks around the area have elevation changes which can add some challenge for hikers/enthusiasts as well as a chance to see some rock formation or waterfall.  Unless you have great timing and see some small woodland creature running by or see a bird overhead, the trails tend to look the same before long.  Review #943

While in Fishers, my wife wanted something traditional for lunch, not anything new and adventurous like I might try.  So, nothing says traditional in the area like Sahm's!  We pulled into their shared lot in the shopping plaza just south of 116th on the east side of the street.  There is a hostess stand which you wait at to be seated and then you are escorted to either a table or booth.  The interior is quite dark for a restaurant, but I guess they see themselves as a pub, so that is to be expected.    The interior also seems a bit dated.  The fabrics on some of the benches were fading.  Though clean, it just seems to need a bit of life added to the dining room.  That somewhat shows since the average age of the customers was 50+.  It just doesn't have the 'wow' factor that appeals to younger customers.  We placed our orders and noticed that our server was quite busy.  He never stopped moving from table to table.  My wife ordered the Chili Cheese Dog.  It came with some really tasty fries.  Our table's supply of ketchup was empty, so she needed to use one from another table since our waiter didn't deliver the food to our table and didn't get back for awhile.  My wife thought the sandwich was fine, but the hot dog was rather average.  Nothing special about it.  I ordered from the lunch special and got the 1/2 salad and soup option.  I went with the Chicken Velvet which was really good.  Lots of veggies and some shredded chicken.  (Note that a clam chowder was originally brought out and I had to send it back.)    I also got the Balsamic Strawberry Fields salad.  Nice bite sized pieces of lettuce and other ingredients and topped with strips of grilled chicken.  Not sure why everything else was served bite sized and the chicken wasn't.  But before I ate it, I couldn't see any dressing.  I expect balsamic dressing to have a dark color.  There was very little shine to the greens.  So I mentioned it and the second waiter removed it and brought out another.  I could see a dressing was on this one, but it didn't have the dark colored balsamic either.  I was tired of sending things back and ate it.  It was still good, but whatever dressing it was, it lacked the deep savory/acidic taste of balsamic vinegar which is a shame since that usually pairs with fresh strawberries quite well.  And the chicken was completely overcooked.  Good grilled flavor, but dry.    We were able to get our check and that payment process went smoothly and quickly.    But the overall experience, even if they had brought the right foods each time, was just okay.  At least it was traditional.  Review #3312

I stopped in for lunch having found a metered parking spot near the entrance.  The inside of the restaurant is vibrant in rich yellows, reds and black.  I was greeted promptly and got a table just outside the bar area (they have a variety of cocktails as well as some beer and wine.)    Since this was my first visit, I went with Pad See Ewe.  It's a dish I have ordered at other Thai places, so I know it is usually a good bet that I will like it and I will also have an idea of how the restaurant compares to other Thai places I've been.  I also went with pork as my selection of meat and "medium" as my choice for heat level.  While I waited, I was provided a refill of my ice water (yes, not some tepid iceless stuff!)  Before long, a large square plate of my entree arrived.  The noodles were tender and seasoned well.  There were large pieces of broccoli, some cabbage and carrots as well.  I found the silverware was only a fork, so I asked for (and received) a knife since eating broccoli that big can get awkward.    The flavor was really delicious!  I'd say the flavor was as good as any I have had.  The heat level was about what I expected....enough heat to make my sinuses react and my throat tingle, but not hot enough to detract from the flavor.  (Probably too hot for someone who doesn't like heat, but they have a mild level.  Not hot enough for those who want lots of spice..they have a couple levels above medium as well.)  Compared to other places, the portion size was far larger than the lunch portions I have had.  So, that somewhat explains the higher price than the competition.  I had no trouble eating the whole thing, but think my wife may want a "to go" box for this size portion.    As far as negatives, the meal was simply the plate I ordered.  Other places provide a small bowl of soup, a veggie egg roll, and even a small salad along with lunch.  This was a little surprising.  They do offer some sides, but everything has a price.  The other negative was that the pork, while still tasty, was a bit overcooked and was a little on the tough side instead of tender.  (Much like when I try to make it at home.)  Overall, I would gladly return with some friends who wanted to check the place out.  Review #252

On Labor Day, I stopped in for lunch before going to see a movie.  The lot was pretty full as were the side patio and sidewalk seating.  There were even about a half dozen folks waiting to be seated.  I took my chance and was able to have one of the remaining counter seats right away.    Throughout the meal, the service was prompt and efficient even though being next to the "pass" I could see the hectic pace that was managed without incident.    I decided to start with a Yogurt Berry/Banana Smoothie as a starter while I reviewed the options.  The smoothie was chilled, but not cold.  The flavor was a balance between fruity and tart.  I was expecting more sweetness, but was glad that it avoided being too sweet and overwhelming the other flavors.  For lunch, I went with the combo: a cup of Tomato Artichoke Soup and a half Patachou Chicken Salad Sandwich on toasted whole wheat (sourdough was another bread option).  The soup had an orange red color with croutons and cheese topping the liquid.  I am not quite sure what the croutons were made from, but reminded me of a sage taste (like dressing at Thanksgiving).  The flavors worked well.  The sandwich was lightly toasted with little browning, so the wheat flavor was okay but lacked that toasty flavor.  The salad itself was white meat chicken with celery, bacon, and mayo.  The  flavor was good, but the texture was very smooth.  The celery was finely chopped as was the bacon.  The chicken itself was either finely pulled or ground.  I prefer chicken salad with a bit of crunch from either larger celery bits, fresh grapes, or even some kind of nut.  (I wonder if they exclude nuts in their recipe due to so many folks having food allergies?)   My sandwich came with a side of chips which were very crunchy, so that somewhat amended the overall appeal of the dish.    Overall, I would gladly return, but would advise anyone else to come in small groups unless you want a long wait.  Review #125

On a stressful Monday (4-11-16), I needed a break and found this Thai restaurant in a strip mall on 86th.  I appreciated the plentiful free parking as it started to rain, so I hurried in.  Visually, I realized I was still in a strip mall restaurant, but there is almost a visual overload of color trying to create a feel of Thai culture.  So, as I placed my order, there was plenty to look around and take in.  The restaurant was relatively quite and calming.  I started off with a Pia Thos (veggie spring roll) with sweet and sour sauce and Asian Cole Slaw.  This was delicious!  The spring roll was complimented by the sauce perfectly.  The slaw was tasty and helped clear my palate from the sweetness of the sauce.  I next ordered the Tom Ka Gai Soup which I had read was "the National Soup" of Thailand.  Since I didn't know when I would have another chance to try it, I ordered a bowl.  Unfortunately, the coconut milk seemed to dominate the flavors, leaving the chicken rather bland.  Very little seasoning was detectable, so now I am wondering if this was an authentic representation or just a missed mark.  Finally, I ordered the Pud Pug Ruam with Chicken.  This was another delicious dish.  It had considerably more heat and flavor than the soup.  The vegetables were al dente and offered plenty of crunch.  The white rice was good at absorbing some of the juice so I didn't lose much of the flavor that was there.  I can't say how authentic any of these dishes are since I have only a minimal exposure to Thai food.  It was different enough from most of the Americanized Asian food I have had at fast food chains that it was a different dining experience.    I left the restaurant well fed and pleased with the hour of stress free dining.  Review #33

There's a "sweet" little house turned business along Main Street (US 136) that opened early in 2019 that makes delicious cupcakes and cookies!  I usually am in Browsburg in the evenings, so I kept missing my chances to stop by.  But when I saw this place was open on Sunday, I made a detour to specifically swing by.  There is no dedicated parking that I could see, but there is a lot next to the shop and a larger one across Main St.  I grabbed one of those and crossed at the nearby intersection.  After climbing a few steps, I entered into one of the rooms set up as display/dining area.  There were several styles of seating including one small room that looked like it was made up for a Halloween party.  To the right is the order counter and I was greeted pleasantly.  There were about four kinds of cupcakes, some coconut macarons, and some other cookies of which the chocolate chip looked really appealing.  I ordered some macarons, the chocolate chip (loaded with chips!) cookie, and a cherry almond cupcake and a snickerdoodle cupcake.    Everything I had was really good and fresh.  I just wish there was more of a selection.  I didn't ask, but I didn't see any pastries or baked bread.  So be aware if you are looking for one of those items.   It appears they do have cakes available too.  If you have a craving for something sweet, fresh, and delicious, swing by Paige's.  You won't be disappointed.  Review #3176

I don't get to this part of town very often, so I made a point of coming here to try one of their lunches.  The restaurant is located on east bound New York Street (fortunately State Street allows access from the north or south).  As soon as I entered through the double door entry, I was greeted and seated at one of the colorfully decorated boths that fill the dining area.  There was also some single seats at the bar near the entrance.  I was impressed with the service here.  My server, Sonia, was friendly and brought out each item so fast that I wasn't finished with the previous one.  Okay, that can be bad if you are eating a steak, but for Mexican food, it was delightful!   I started with the complementary bowl of salsa and chips.  Pretty standard stuff, but the salsa was topped with fresh chopped onion and cilantro.  Nice touch and it definitely upped the flavor.  Next arrived my Elote (Mexican Street Corn).  Arriving on a stick, the cob was covered with mayo, cotijo cheese, and paprika.  If you haven't tried this, you are missing out.  Layers of flavor and just fun (and a little messy) to eat.  My entree, the chimichanga arrived and I immediately knew I was going to need a to go box.  I chose a seasoned ground beef for my filling and was given sides of beans and rice.  I was a little surprised that there weren't bigger pieces of onion and bell pepper inside, but there were jalapeno slices.  The flavor was delightful.    Checkout was quick and orderly as I paid the waitress.    I don't have the background to comment on authenticity, but I can say that the flavor was good throughout and the friendly service was deserving of a 5 star visit!  Review #2132

It's almost unfair that Mass Avenue gets so many high quality places to eat/shop.  I would have missed this one if not for the keen eye and reviewing of some Yelp friends who let me know.  First benefit is that it is located within Needler's grocery, so you have free parking in their lot for 2 hours.  That's right next to Mass Avenue.  No meters.  No hunting.  No having to back out into oncoming traffic.  This is a great place to take care of business!  Next, it has direct access from Alabama Street with large windows for people watching if you like that sort of thing.  You can step right off the Cultural Trail and refuel right here.  The place has a variety of ready to eat lunch options and lots of beverages to choose from too.  Want some fruit to go with your meal?  There is a full grocery to choose from right there!!  And, if you like all those things, wait until you try the goodies they sell in the central island of the cafe.  A friendly woman was working there and answered my questions, checking to make sure I got the exact item that caught my eye before ringing my order.  They have large muffins, cannolis, beautiful icing works of art that have cupcakes under them, and cookies.    Oh, and they sell coffee too!  What are you waiting for, an invitation?  Okay, you are invited!!  Review #3208

I'd like to say that I have been to the Slapfish in Noblesville twice before, once at a Yelp event.  The owners of that Slapfish have expanded to Mass Ave.  Apparently, Slapfish is a California franchise that offers something different than the standard fish and chips that many local seafood places offer.  At Slapfish, you get a bit of the So Cal flavors as well as some healthier options than just fried food.  If you check out their menu, you will see a street taco with options of grilled or breaded fish.  The lobster taquitos (two per order) have a little bit of kick (heat) in the sauce that is drizzled over the crispy pastry filled with lobster.  My wife went with the Hawaiian bowl that is a large serving of food, so don't let the price tag scare you off.  She had enough to finish off at dinner later that evening!  Since we went during the pandemic, most of Mass Avenue is closed to through traffic so that tables can be set up for outdoor eating.  Here's a tip....If you are downtown, head north on Delaware to Vermont and look for street parking (most are metered.)  Turn right (east) on Vermont and we found that Mass Ave was open from that side of the block and we were able to grab a parking space just a few steps from the Vonnegut Mural (another check-in opportunity).    On the Saturday we went, there weren't a lot of patrons, so we had our choice of dining inside or outside.  You still go inside to order and once you've paid, they give you a number stand to place on your table.  Also note that softdrinks are self serve to the right of the order counter as are paper napkins.  The bar was open, but no seating was allowed at the bar (Xs are across those seats).  Ordering was quick and easy and before long, our food was brought out to us.  I thought my orders were delicious and considering they were two of the lower priced items on the menu, I was especially pleased.  My wife liked the Hawaiian bowl, but the kitchen did not make the change order my wife requested (we heard the cashier ask the kitchen if they could use just iceberg lettuce instead of a mix of greens and the cashier confirmed the change was easy.)  So, my wife's initial impression was disappointed, but the flavors won her over.  When it comes to raw veggies, she likes large slices, but not thickly cut.  Just a bit of crunch, but not so small that she has to chase them around the bowl with her fork.  She said all the veggies were fresh and crisp.  The shrimp were grilled properly and were tasty too.  The pineapple chunks were also grilled which she really liked too.  So, overall, we had a good meal at this newly opened restaurant.  If you feel like something other than a pizza or burger for lunch and aren't on a grade-schooler's budget, stop by for a tasty meal (or two!)  Review #3777

While in the area, I saw this place on Yelp and decided to stop in before lunch (shameful, I know!)  This local shop has been in business going on 25 years and I can see why.  They had friendly servers and a wide variety of flavors of ice cream.  They also offer lots of coffee options too, but I didn't explore those.  The shop is located in a strip mall just east of the intersection of Fall Creek and 79th (it becomes 82 on the other side of the stop light.)  Plenty of parking out front, so I grabbed a spot and wandered in.  There is a dining room at the front and along the right side.  On the left is the order counter where you can see the buckets of creamy ice cream and the wall full of flavoring options for your coffee.  Note that as you face the order counter, your spoon and napkins are behind you towards the door if you need them.  I saw a sign out front that was featuring the key lime pie ice cream, so I got a taste of that before ordering.  I liked the creamy texture and the bits of crust/cookie inside the ice cream rounded out the flavor and helped balance the sweet/tart tastes of the ice cream.  Very good and reasonably priced.  It was nice to be able to grab a seat in the dining area and relax while enjoying my ice cream.  The place was clean and organized.  Review #2952

So, on a day when it struggled to get above zero degrees, I decided to make the trek to 49th and College to try a warm bowl of ramen.  I have been waiting for Ukiyo to open, but since I prefer smaller crowds and less hectic surroundings, I chose a Tuesday lunch period to make my visit.  I know that parking in Broad Ripple can be a challenge, but I grabbed a spot two spaces from the door.  They also have street parking beyond the pull up lane for this strip of buildings.  There is also a frequently used parking lot across College that can handle some of the visitors as well.  The space is set up with a dining area (some tables, some booths) beyond the reception desk as you walk in; a pass through area to the left which serves as a ramen bar area where you can sit on a stool; and a tightly packed dining area beyond the pass through that is narrow enough for just a single row of small tables.  Seating here is quite close with only about 16-18" between tables.  Not bad when the crowd is small, but the area filled quickly and made it a little awkward not to overhear the neighbors conversations.  My server was very personable and helpful since a number of items on the menu were of Japanese origin and were not familiar to me.  He and the rest of the staff kept my chilled tap water topped off, removed my empty dishes, and even turned down the volume of the booming music upon my request.  I was seated by the glass windows at the front of the restaurant and was being bombarded by sound waves up until that point, so the swift adjustment was greatly appreciated as conversation volume had also grown louder.  (Note:  after the volume adjustment, the ambient noise level was normal.)  I was glad I got there just before the noon rush:  I was quickly brought out my side dish of Tsuekmono (3 types of fermented and pickled vegetables for $5).  I am not 100% certain that what was served matched the description on my receipt, but all were quite tasty!  The first small bowl had a finely shredded veggie topped with sesame seeds.  The receipt said it was made from carrots preserved in soy sauce which had a chewy texture which was a little odd, but the flavor was "Wow"!  Great combo of the soy and sesame.  There were also some halved slices of daikon pickled in vinegar and sprinkled with colorful seasoning.  Nice acidity to the crunch.  And finally, it was listed as a Hakurei turnip preserved in salt, but may not have been right.  It definitely had a crunch component like a turnip but there were smaller diced veggies included that added to the overall flavor.  If you are looking for a side to add, make this your go to.  (Note that the veggies will change depending upon availability.)  And I must confess that this was my first "official" tasting of restaurant prepared ramen.  I went with the "Shoyu" ramen option ($15) which consists of a broth made from chicken and Dashi (sea based ingredients), with Chashu (tender pork), menma (a condiment), half a cured egg, diced scallion, and chicken oil.  To this was added a large serving of ramen noodles (they looked and tasted very similar to capellini or angel hair pasta) that were steaming as I lifted them.  Oh, and I added an upgrade for $2.50 for three slices of pork belly which were cut about a 1/4 inch thick and about 3 inches in length.  The bowl was really large for a lunch portion.  The broth, as expected is thin, but has a savory flavor.  I really appreciated that it was served at a temperature that was ready to eat (I can't tell you how many times I've burned my mouth on ridiculously hot soup!)  They give you chopsticks and a Japanese style soup spoon to eat with and a verbal advisory that slurping is perfectly acceptable since the noodles are long and don't twist onto a chopstick as easily as a fork!  So, after a little experimentation, I figured that if I grabbed a bunch of noodles with my sticks and jabbed the top part into my mouth, I could hold them there long enough with my lips to grab any dangling noodles with my sticks and hold them as I took my bite.  No Slurping Here!!      Overall, I was very encouraged by my visit and hope to return sometime in the near future to try the dinner menu.  If the flavor combos are as good as they are at the ramen lunch, this place will be a great success.  Review #494

I had never heard of this place until I was reading some advice from a Yelper about places an out of towner should be sure to try.  Lick has been around for six years and is currently located in an industrial looking building (CCIC) just north east of the downtown tip of Mass Ave.  Parking is available in the lot across the street.  We wandered through several hallways to the back (thank goodness for directional signs in the building!) and came upon a small area in front of the production part of the business.  One of the co-owners (sisters) greeted us and pleasantly let us sample flavors of their made from scratch ice cream.  Wow!  This stuff is delicious.  Sure, some of the combinations may sound kind of "out there", but a lot of time and testing went into getting each flavor right.  I tried the "Sweet Corn", the "Balsamic Dark Chocolate", and settled on the "Peach Caramel Pie" that features bits of crumble instead of pie crust.  Delicious!   One of my friends went with the balsamic dish (also tremendous!), while my wife and my friend's husband each got the classic Root Beer Float.  The floats feature the vanilla ice cream topped with Hansen's Root Beer.    All the ice cream is made completely free of artificial ingredients, even food coloring.  So, not as wide a range of colors, but pure, fresh flavor all the same.    If you are downtown before 5 late in the week, stop by if you are willing to try something new and delicious.  It is worth it.  p.s.  Note that there isn't a place to sit down, but you will probably eat your treat so fast it won't matter.  p.s.s.  They primarily sell to a number of restaurants downtown and on the north side.  So, if you are ordering ice cream, see if they carry Lick brand.  p.s.s.s.  Although the production part of the business is likely to stay put, a new, more accessible store front may go in SoBro.  p.s.s.s.s.  I can't resist throwing in that the business got started when one of the sisters got an ice cream maker for a wedding gift....Now that was a useful gift put to good use!  Review #120

My wife and I decided to take a tour of the Catacombs under the west wing of the City Market.  So we went online to the Indiana Landmarks to sign up for a tour.  The prices run $10 to $12 per person depending upon the date and time.  Tours are available on the first and third Saturdays during the warmer months of May through October.  Half hour tours start at 11 a.m. and start each half hour through the last one which starts at 1 p.m.     Once we signed in and signed a waiver (the flooring of the Catacombs is uneven and could cause someone to trip), we began the tour above ground on the Whistler Plaza (west side of the City Market.)  We listened to a presentation that included photos and illustrations of the buildings and their histories that have occupied this location.   Finally, we went downstairs into the catacombs and saw this cool (literally) place that was sometimes used for cold storage by vendors who were selling in the market area above.  I kept hoping there would be some great photo opportunities and points of interest, but frankly, the catacombs never took on a function of their own.  That was disappointing.   When the plans for Indianapolis were created back in 1821, plat #45 was designated as the location about a quarter mile east of Monument Circle.  So through the years, a city market has been at this location in many forms.  Back in 1886, Tomlinson Hall was built on the west end of the block.  Then, in 1958, the great hall burned and left only remnants of the building:  The arch that free stands on the main level, and the catacombs.     So, if you are into local history or all things "Indy", you may enjoy the tour which is more about the history of the City Market than the catacombs.  If you are expecting something special in the realm of "eerie" or specific stories about the catacombs, you may want to pass.   The tours are conducted by volunteers from the Indiana Landmarks group.  They seemed well informed and personable.  I think they do about as much as they can with the subject matter.  Too bad that this place was never developed into some cool purpose like a bar or nightclub.    Review #320

While exploring the Stafford Crossing Shoppes, I decided to grab a quick lunch at Chicago's Pizza.  It's located on the west end of the businesses and because of the large lot, I was able to grab a spot close to the entrance.  I noticed an patio for fair weather dining to the right.  As I entered, I waited briefly to be seated.  My waitress brought my ice water while I looked over the menu.  I decided to order from the menu instead of selecting one of the "lunch" menus which on most days, includes the salad bar and/or pizza bar.    I didn't see anything about the sizes of the pizza available, so I went with a small, thin/crispy crust of the "Windy City".  This pizza has mild Italian sausage, and chopped white onion and green peppers.  I also ordered a side salad with a creamy balsamic dressing.  The salad arrived promptly (with utensils) and I was pleased to see it had been cut to bite sized pieces (except for the tomato slices).  Yeah!  I appreciate that.  If I have to cut the salad just to eat it, I might as well stay  home and make it myself!  The salad was fresh and though it didn't have a lot of ingredients, it did taste good.  Before long, my pizza also arrived.  The small was about 12" (6 pieces) so I knew I was going to want a to go box since I didn't need to eat that much at one sitting.  As far as the pizza goes, the crust held up pretty well, though I wouldn't say it was crisp.  The ingredients were distributed pretty well across the pizza as well.  I also liked that the small chop on the veggies made it easy to eat.  The only problem was that the pizza had very little flavor.  The mild Italian  had barely any noticeable taste.  I have had Italian sausage where you can taste several spices/herbs, but this sausage was just disappointing.  It did contribute a bit of grease to the pizza, which I had to dab off with a spare paper napkin.  The other issue was that the onion and peppers still tasted pretty raw.  They had a lot of moisture in them and because they were topped with cheese, the quick bake time didn't allow the sweetness to roast into the flavor.  (At home, I usually grill my veggies before baking if I am going to top them with cheese.)  So, although the list of ingredients was promising, the rush to get the food out with an efficient process resulted in pizza that was lacking in flavor.  I even tried using some of the spicy shaker flakes, which helped, but didn't allow for much layering of taste.  So, if you want pizza and feel like getting out to do so, this place is okay.  But don't go expecting lots of real Italian flavor.    Review #3481

After reading some positive reviews from my Yelp friends, I decided to stop by City Market since I was already parked about a block away.  The restaurant/booth was easy to find in the center aisle of the main hall of the Market.  Since it was nearing 1:30, there was only one customer ahead of me, so the wait was really short even though the crepes are made to order.  The owner/operator is very friendly and loves when people mention they were directed to her business by Yelp.  She even gives 1 free item (I selected a bottled water) for Yelpers who check in for the first time while there.    I went with a couple savory selections, the Green Eggs and Ham crepe and the Harvest crepe.  She asked if I was thinking of eating them in the Market or getting them to go.  When I said I was dining in, she thought it might be too much for one sitting and suggested cutting each in half and serving half on a plate and the other half of each in a to go box "just in case".  Good idea!  So, within just a few minutes, I had my two varieties and headed up the stairs of the Market to grab a spot to eat.  (Note:  Even for a day that hung around the freezing mark, the Market was sufficiently warm.  That seems like an improvement over past experiences.)  I started with the Harvest.  The crepes, even half-sized, were indeed large and though I could have used my plastic ware, I simply folded the pizza shape in half which made it easy to eat like a sandwich.  Watch out for any juiciness that may escape from the bottom!  The Harvest was delicious!  Ham and cheese, apples, cranberries, raw spinach, and a tasty dressing to keep it moist.  Wow!  This selection is probably somewhere between savory and sweet.  My second crepe was the Green Eggs and Ham.  Very savory with the egg, ham, Mozzarella, spinach and pesto.  The basil in the pesto turns everything green inside the crepe.  The herb is probably the strongest flavor of the mix but didn't overwhelm the other flavors.  The cheese got nice and gooey with the stretchy strings of cheese if I didn't bite sharply. Very nice!   I can definitely see returning here to try some of the other selections whenever I'm in the neighborhood.  If you haven't tried them, treat yourself to something tasty!  Review #521

This diner/cafe located on the south east side of Indy is a fun place to stop for breakfast or lunch.  There isn't a lot of room inside and the place seems to have a large number of returning customers, but I came in for an early lunch and was seated right away.  The staff is very friendly and did a good job of keeping my coffee and water topped off.  Although I could have gone with a breakfast (everything on the menu is available while the place is open!), I chose to go with the "Poor Boy" and fries.  The sandwich came on an 8" bun (very fresh) with lots of ham, Swiss cheese, sauteed onions and bell peppers, and was topped with a house Thousand Island dressing.  The fries come with a plain or seasoned option (seasoned has an upcharge).  I went with the plain which didn't even have salt.  Fortunately, my table was loaded with condiments, so I didn't even need to ask for ketchup and salt.    The sandwich was really tasty and came with a steak knife to help cut it in half since it was large.  The fries were okay, reminding me of the kind I make at home from store bought packages.    No visit is complete without taking a stroll around the interior of the diner.  Tons of nostalgic memorabilia covers the walls, shelves, and even the ceiling!  If you are old, like me, you may remember some of the items for your youth.  If not, you might just shake your head wondering what the fascination was with these objects.  Review #553

To be honest, before visiting this store with my wife, I had never heard of this store.  I tend to ignore newspaper flyers and commercials on television, so unless someone tells me about a place like this, I really have no thoughts one way or the other.  I have to admit for being a big box store, they were clean and had a wide variety of items to browse through.  During the week, there weren't a lot of staff on hand, but the one who helped us was really good.  My wife had a return to make and one thing keeping this place from getting a higher rating was that there was no signage indicating where customer service/returns were located.  None of the cashier aisles had anyone there when we entered.  We browsed a little and my wife spotted a gal who was stocking inventory (loads of seasonal stuff was filling the shelves).  The employee immediately stopped stocking and directed my wife to the second cashier spot and she opened the spot and processed the returned item with a simple review of the receipt to confirm it was purchased there and the price to be refunded.  In about a minute, my wife was refunded her money.  My wife also asked if they carried some artificial plants and where would she find them.  The clerk pointed in the general directions and then gave some verbal direction to help find the specific items.  Unfortunately, they had similar stuff to what my wife wanted, but not exactly.  But that wasn't the clerk's fault.  Prices seemed reasonable and the quality of the items I picked up seemed good too.    All in all, if you like shopping in person and discovering things you didn't know a place like at home carried, I would recommend stopping on by!  Review #3811

Tucked away in the small strip mall across from the entrance to the Jiffy Lube and Crew Car Wash is a nice place to check for your vinyl needs!  After pulling into the shared lot, I entered the shop with the checkout counter on the right as you enter.  The rest of the shop was filled with rows of albums (and some 45's) arranged by genre.    As I browsed through the rock section, I noticed that all albums seemed to be wrapped in a plastic sleeve with the actual vinyl in the inner paper sleeve removed from the cardboard cover to show that the record was complete.  Many of the covers had "new" labels on them, so I assume that meant they would be scratch free.  The plastic sleeve was folded over and sealed with a bar code label that had the price for each album.  The range for albums I checked out ran from around $5 to into the $20+ range depending upon the demand.  (Some are even higher, but that's to be expected for hard to find or collectible editions.)  There were also other genres and I was pleased to see so many artists, including independent ones, represented.  No, they don't have every album, but that is probably limited by size of the store as much as anything.    Still, you are free to browse and when asked, the owner was helpful.  If you are building (or rebuilding) your vinyl collection, add this shop to your places to explore.  Review #3525

My wife and I were looking for a new dining table and chair set, so we stopped by to see what they had.  We were greeted by one of the salespeople who let us know to come see her if we had any questions.  We browsed for a bit, but didn't really see anything on the floor like we wanted.  Too bad I hadn't read Dylan's review that mentions they have an online catalog available.  Also too bad for the salesperson that she didn't mention it either.    They did have some nice pieces, but nothing jumped out as being a piece we wanted for our home.  I guess we will continue looking.  If we are in the area (it's about a 50 minute drive for us), I wouldn't mind using their online system.  Review #2049

I stopped in for lunch before catching an afternoon movie and the good news is that I got a tasty meal (to go) in just over a half hour after pulling into the shared parking lot.  This first expansion of the Petra Cafe (on Mass Ave) is very similar to the original in that it has a small space with a small, but really good menu.  The food prep area is clearly visible from the dining area.  The dining area is filled with mostly 2-top tables that are close together.  In fact, while waiting in line to place my order, I was very aware that I was really close to other customers who were dining already.  After about 10 minutes or so, I was ready to order from the overhead menu.  I decided to go with the Falafel Sandwich.  They do have combos available that include fries, beverage, and choice of sauce.  They also have platters which come with rice.  There are salads and appetizers as well, but trust me, unless you are sharing, the sandwiches are huge and will fill you up!  I stood off to the side of the counter while I waited the 20 minutes for them to get to my order (I should have called ahead.)  Again, I felt I was a bit in the way as people were either getting their food delivered or as customers came up to the counter when their number was called.  It wasn't clear that either way was dominant.    Part of the problem is that they don't have a table busing area where patrons can clean their own mess before leaving.  So, there were some tables with remains sitting on them that I didn't choose to sit at.  Don't get me wrong; the cashier was busy all the time and he cleared the tables as soon as he got a chance and was always courteous/apologetic for the delay.    And the food?  I got mine to go and it was really good!  Generous portion with a lot of fresh veggies to go with the fried falafel.  The "bread" held together keeping most of the ingredients inside, so I could tell it was fresh too.  I think this is another case of the business is more successful than planned and so seating is limited and waits were a bit longer than someone on a lunch hour may want to do a walk in order.  Pleasant staff and fresh, quality food made for a pleasant meal, but I doubt I would like dining with people standing right next to my table.  Review #3300

Wow!  I was blown away by the antique furniture and architectural pieces available here.  I almost wish I had a giant house that I could just add these pieces too!  Okay, from the highway (96th Street near Zionsville Road), the place doesn't look like much.  In fact, the main building looks like a simple enclosed pole barn while the the side building and the barn look in need of a lot of work.  And since it was my first visit, I found the side building rather cramped and filled with lots of fixtures, hinges, small lighting fixtures, etc.  It did have a few cool pieces (somewhat large for any old home) that caught my eye as statement pieces when I explored the back room.  The barn was unheated and had lots of old doors in various conditions.  But what I wasn't ready for turned out to be the items inside the main building.  The place is huge and I can't think of a single place I've looked at antiques that had as an impressive collection of fireplaces, bars, chandeliers, and more.  I wandered through and saw ornate details everywhere.  This building was still packed, but much easier to get around and find items.  Although they are going to convert to a standard price tag, most of the existing pieces have a paper tag with three numbers on it.  The middle number is the price component of their system, so be advised.    Now I can't say if their prices are the best or competitive, but considering how unique some of the pieces are, I can say I haven't seen anything close to some of the pieces here.    If you are looking for something unique to add to your home, check out this place.  Even if you don't buy something, you may be impressed with the artistic details you will find.  Review #3563

Inside Nordstroms on the second floor of Keystone at the Crossing is the company's dining option.  The restaurant is quiet and arranged with the kitchen, including the brick oven on the south end with bar style seating facing the chef area.  From there, a mixture of booth and chair seating on an arc fills the center, with tables and some additional booth seating along the walls.      The restaurant asks for patrons to wait at the front entrance, but no one greets you there.  You have to go in to the left (after picking up a menu at the entrance) to place your order and pay in advance.  You then pick your seat and wait for your food, tableware, and drinks to be brought to you.    I ordered the Bistro Club sandwich which comes with Bistro French Fries and kalamata olive aioli.  The Sandwich was delicious and huge!  Served on a toasted rustic bread, the sandwich has sliced chicken breast, organic baby greens, crisp and thick bacon, tomato, avocado, French green beans (adds to the crunch!), and garlic aioli.  Very tasty!    My wife ordered the Citrus Turkey sandwich which has Gruyere cheese, tomato, organic baby greens, citrus cranberry chutney, garlic aioli, and slice turkey on a toasted multi-grain ciabatta bread.  It wasn't quite as large as my sandwich, but was plenty to be filling.  She found it quite good as well.    The service was also attentive and courteous and prompt.  Kuddos to them too!    So with sandwiches so good, why not a higher score?  Well, several little things kept us from thoroughly enjoying the experience.  First, the bathrooms are not in the restaurant, but at the northwest end of the Nordstroms.  No sign tells you this at the entrance (at least we didn't see one), so if you want to wash your hands before eating, you have to leave the restaurant again.    The Bistro French Fries have no description on them in the menu.  They are brought out already seasoned with parsley and rosemary.  My wife cannot stand the taste and even the smell of rosemary, so she didn't eat but one.  Since I assume the seasoning is added after the  cooking process, it would be nice to offer "unseasoned" fries as an option.    I was not sure what the kalamata olive aioli was for.  My wife used it to dip her sandwich for additional flavor.  I thought it might be for the fries.  Either way, I am not a fan of the bitterness in kalamata olives, so I passed on this (letting my wife add it to her sandwich).  I would have liked an option to have a simple catsup for my fries, but since they were seasoned, chose not to ask if it was available.  Still, it would have been nice to have that option mentioned by the staff.    Finally, when you pay up front, they keep your receipt until you are ready to leave.  When they bring your receipt, they don't have an option for leaving a tip on your credit card, so we needed to dig for cash to leave a tip.  If they have a plan for tipping (or a no tipping policy), it would be nice if they explained it when the order was placed and paid for.  I think this is one place that could benefit from customer service cards to fine tune the dining experience.    If I return, I will know to ask more questions up front.  Any business that wants to create a payment policy different from the standard owes it to the customers to be forthcoming with the info and not assume everyone knows the "Company Way", especially after we told them front desk it was our first visit.  Review #294

I really enjoyed my visit for lunch.  The staff was friendly and the menu had a wide variety of options, including lunch specials.  I started with a cup of hot tea (yes, by the cup, not a tea pot).  Since I've been eating a lot of sushi lately, I decided to go with the Hibachi Salmon instead.  It comes with a choice of clear soup or side salad (salad for me), about a cup of fried rice, and a generous serving of delicious sauteed veggies.  The salmon had a nice glaze that was quite tasty too.  The serving of salmon was a little small, but considering how expensive salmon can be, it was reasonably portioned.  The dish also comes with small sides of Yum Yum sauce and Ginger sauce.  The place is a little tricky to get to since you cannot pull in directly from Emerson.  There is a stoplight just north of the restaurant that allows you to pull in an make a few right turns behind the shop to get to the parking out front.  The only negative was that the dish took a bit longer than I expected to come out considering the place wasn't that busy when I placed my order.  I can see waiting a half hour causing some problems for folks who have to get back to work.  Review #1927

If you had a grocery store that was dedicated to beer, wine, and liquor, you would call it Total Wine & More!  This place is huge when compared to most liquor stores.  But unlike buying liquor at a grocery, here the staff is knowledgeable and helpful.  The selection as you might guess is huge and the prices very reasonable!      I won't promise they will have everything you need, but this is sure a good place to start.  They even have rewards programs and classes for those who want to learn more about the products offered here.  I live an hour away, otherwise, I would be intrigued by the options!  The store wasn't swamped when we entered, but it was quite busy and they had enough check out stations open to make that process quick too!  Because it is in a shopping center, we found a spot close to the entrance.  And the parking is free too!  Our friends took a little longer since they were going through the aisles of wine.  I was simply looking at liqueurs and though I didn't find the particular flavor of brandy that I was looking for, I grabbed a bottle of sloe gin that was put to use later in the evening.  The staff offered to help me find what I missed, but since I already had one bottle, I decided that was enough for the day.  Friendly staff, good selection and prices made for a pleasant experience.  I forgot to mention they even have shopping carts to help you carry all your items if you decide to browse awhile.  So glad our friend recommended stopping in here after lunch.  It was amazing to see so many options.  Review #3848

At a recent Yelp Event, I was fortunate enough to try one of Danny's ice creams:  Queso.  It wasn't what I expected.  Instead it was a thick and creamy ice cream with a sweet flavor that I couldn't quite identify.  It was delicious, but different.  At that event, we were only allowed to try one flavor, though several were available.  So, I made up my mind to make a trip out to the actual shop and try them for myself!  Although my GPS was throwing me off a bit on finding the place, my wife spotted it in the corner of a strip mall near the road.  Inside, the restaurant is bright green and yellow and is well lit.  Everything is written in English unlike some other places in town that were a bit out of my comfort zone.  Yes, you can get a lot of Mexican specialties, but you can also get some more traditional flavors if you aren't as adventurous.  Just know that whatever flavor you choose, the ice cream will be rich, sweet, and have a creamy texture.  Your spoon won't rush through this ice cream.  And when it hits your tongue, you will be able to let it melt and deliver a lot of flavor before you swallow!  Since it is a Mexican ice cream shop, I wanted to try some of the flavors that I missed at the event.  I sampled the Corn ice cream which was true to the flavor of sweet corn (just no butter).  I've had corn ice cream other places and knew I would like it, but I was intrigued by the Horchata which I had never tried before.  The Horchata looks like vanilla when scooped, but has a taste that I would say reminds me of rice pudding but with a thick and creamy flavor.  Maybe a bit sweeter, but the hint of rice flavor is subtle and gives it some depth.  I didn't notice any cinnamon in the flavor, but I was quite pleased with my selection.    My advice is that there is no reason to skip this shop because it offers something different than you may be used to.  Danny is a young entrepreneur (he is only 21 at the time of this review!) that is following the American Dream.  If you decide to try one of the Mexican flavors, you get a small spoon to sample it before buying.  But know that the flavors are delicious and your hardest decision may be to limit yourself.  Fortunately, they have containers for additional flavors you can take home!   Review #2265

When my wife and I moved to Greenwood, we really used to enjoy shopping here.  Now that we have moved again, I don't get over here nearly as often, but I still find that they have a nice selection of items to choose from.  After parking in their shared lot, I entered through the double sliding doors and emerged into the kitchen supplies area.  I always browse through here since they carry high quality items as well as a few more "unique" items that I had never considered.  Beyond that, they have a candle/fragrance area, a section for wall hangings/mirrors, and on the far side, bedding ideas.  As you walk around the circular path towards the front, there is another section with travel items and quick snacks before entering the lanes for check out.  Note that you have to pass through that area because the doors you came in don't open from the inside normally.  Although I didn't make any purchases on my most recent visit, I noticed that the lines were small with several cash registers open to help minimize wait times.  The store was clean and orderly as well.  A good place to stop by for items for your home.  Review #3522

Let me say that I've been to Prime 47 in downtown and had a wonderful 5 star meal.  So, I had pretty lofty expectations when I took my wife and another couple here to celebrate the Devour Indy promotion.  It wasn't that there was anything bad about the evening, but there were a lot of "just okay" factors for a meal that went for over $70 each.  The restaurant is located in the stylish Clay Terrace shopping area.  We were able to grab one of the restricted parking spots across the street.  Otherwise, they do have valet parking from the front entrance pull up.  Once inside, we noticed the facility is kept very dark and chilly.  One reason we didn't stay longer was simply how cold it was with the air conditioning blowing on us.  Even sitting close to the windows didn't seem to brighten up the space.  I don't know...I like to be able to see the menu and the people I'm dining with without having to use my flashlight on my camera.  The staff (they work in teams) were cordial, but aloof.  Professional?  Certainly.  But there wasn't any connection like I've had from other top end restaurants.    Before ordering from the Devour menu, we did order cocktails and some appetizers.  I thought my Pamatini was quite tasty (raspberry absolute and Pama) and my friend liked his Hendricks Gin & Tonic.  My wife also really liked the crab cake.  Our friends ordered the Caprese Salad which tasted good, but frankly, the tomatoes were a light red color.  If you can't find ripe tomatoes in August, then you need another supplier.  The appetizer course from the Devour menu was a choice of a side salad or the soup of the day which I believe was called Jalapeno Cheese soup.  The salad was fresh and crisp while the soup had a bit of a pinto bean flavor (more than cheesy) and a bit of heat on the back end of the taste.  Both soup and salad were good.  One of my guests ordered the Faroe Salmon and she commented that it was the best salmon she had ever had.  It had a honey horseradish glaze with a nice balance of flavors.  Definitely recommended.  The rest of us ordered the 6 oz filets.  One thing I found odd was that the steakhouse's "doneness" ranking was rarer than that used at other metro area steakhouses.  Normally, I go with a medium-rare which is a warm red center.  At Prime 47, that is medium according to the servers.  So, I went with medium.  Now the last thing I want to do is slice my steak down the middle when it is first served and have the juices run out.  So, I worked my way in from the edge and though I ate fairly quickly, realized that the steak was cooked medium well with just a bit of pink.  I hate sending food back if I've eaten nearly half of it.  The flavor was fine, but just not as succulent as I had hoped.  My wife and friend's turned out okay...mine was the anomaly.    And if you like presentation, then these chain restaurants that serve a 3 inch steak on a full size plate without anything else will disappoint you.  I get that some use super hot ovens which risk burning the guests just to keep the steak searing, but they don't look appetizing.  Transfer the steak to a plate and put the side dish on it for some color.  Look at my photos to see how unbalanced the plates look.  The sides were okay.  Totally forgettable.  My wife thought the cream corn was okay at best.  I had the green beans and they were al dente with fully cooked red bell pepper, but were a bit on the chewy side.  One friend got the sauteed mushrooms and thought they were the best part of the entire meal.  On to dessert and the other three ordered the Half-baked chocolate chip cookie with vanilla bean ice cream and chocolate syrup.  One friend would eat cookie dough raw, so he really enjoyed it.  The other two thought it so sugary (the sugar didn't melt properly and was somewhat grainy) that they didn't finish theirs.  I went with the Pretzel Crusted Brownie which had a slightly salted pretzel bottom to the brownie and I found it to be quite good.  The hint of salt perked up the chocolate in the brownie.  Would definitely order that again.  Oh, and our friend noticed that there was a tear in the table cloth after we had been served our first course.  She pointed it out to the servers, but we opted not to move since it wasn't affecting our meal.  It just shows a lack of attention to detail...and that seemed to be a theme with the restaurant.  I'm sure some of these issues were one time problems, but considering how the evening went compared to other steak houses I've been to, it was just a bit disappointing.  I will probably stick with the ones downtown.  Review #1278

On my way to this location, I actually drove passed the original Rize at Iron Works.  I wondered how this new location, open about a week, would compare.  In my opinion, this one is even better!  The new Rize (a Cunningham Group restaurant) is located in the Fishers District (the "Yard") complex that is east of the interstate at 116th.  Rize is towards the north end and has "nose-in" parking on two sides of the building.  The entrance is on the east wall and is next to a fenced patio area that extends to the northeast.  Inside, the stylish dining area is "L-shaped" which helps keep the noise level down.  There seemed to be plenty of space between the tables offering bench and chair seating options.    We were greeted and seated from the host stand and from our table, we could see the "pass" where food was reviewed before being sent out to the customers.    After getting a cup of tasty and immediately drinkable coffee, I ordered a "Strata" while my wife went with the "Chicken Sandwich".  The Strata is a layered dish consisting of Yukon Gold potatoes, egg custard, milk bread, and roasted mushrooms.  It is cut into servings like a quiche.  The tasty dish was enhanced with a layer of sliced ham on top and pickled onions for a tart/acidic layer of flavor.  There was also hibiscus mustard, tomato jam, and cilantro pesto that added flavor and color to each bite.  Highly recommended.  Note that I also ordered a side of sausage (pork links) to go with the meal.  Those were okay, maybe a little too lean to match the flavor of the main dish.  My wife went with the Chicken Sandwich that comes served on a fantastic croissant (made by Chef Hattie McDaniel) that my wife said was just incredible on its own!  The sauteed chicken comes with bacon, honey mustard, and sliced Gruyere cheese.  It was a large sandwich, but she polished it off faster than I ate my dish!  The sandwich comes with a side salad of mixed greens topped with a honey vinaigrette.  My wife usually doesn't like "weeds", but she ate nearly all of it because of the dressing.  And if you have ever been to the other Rize, you know that this place makes GIANT Cinnamon Rolls.  We ordered one to go just before leaving so that it was still warm when we got home.  We are still eating it the morning after!  Service and staff were friendly and we never felt rushed during our visit.  Coffee refills were timely, though my cup did run out for about a minute.  Our server was very knowledgeable about the menu items.  We were able to have all our questions answered before ordering.  Note that this is a high quality restaurant with multi-layered flavors.  It is NOT a Denny's or Bob Evans-type all you can eat restaurant or buffet for small change.  If you are concerned about affordability, check out the prices online before you go.  But if you love going out to eat for food that you probably don't treat yourself to at home, come visit Rize for exceptionally prepared dishes that are delicious.  Review #3331

There's a new restaurant open in the southwest pocket of Indy:  Chicago Fish Chicken & Gyros.  I'm not sure if it is connected to the one on the far east side, but this spot is located in a small stripmall along SR 67 before you reach Heartland Crossing.  I went in on their opening weekend and found that they have dine in seating but no waiting service, so you need to place your order at the counter at the back of the dining area.  They don't have overhead menus, so you need to find one of their printed menus at the counter or on a side table.  The menu has a large number of options; many would be suitable for family dinners or even tailgaiting.  The menu has categories including Chicago Style Sandwiches, Middle East Style Food, Wings, Tenders, and Fish.  They also plan on having lunch specials (Mon-Fri) for about $7 including fries and drink.  I decided to get a gyro (comes with fries & drink) and an order of 15 pc wings (with fries).  I paid and was told to give them about 15 minutes.  While I waited, I could see that if they want this to be more of a dine-in restaurant, they would benefit from a bit more decoration and fewer large tables so that individuals or couples could find a spot without taking up a large bench.  They could also use some individual chairs for people waiting for their "to go" orders.  When I got home, I tried the gyro first.  Really good sandwich with enough flavor to be enjoyable.  The meat was not dry and had just enough sauce to blend with the spices.  The fries were also freshly made, but I was not offered any ketchup for them.  The fries were seasoned with salt, so I didn't need any additional amount.  The chicken wings (I got full wings, but half wings are also available) were served in an aluminum container along with the fries and topped with foil.  They were still hot when I got home and I could see they were heavily seasoned.  Good flavor, but leaning towards too much salt.  The fries were plentiful too.  But here's the problem:  Packaging a large number of wings and fries together allows their internal heat to continue cooking them.  The chicken can become dry inside while the fries pick up the steam from being enclosed and can become a bit soggy.
