When I got home, I immediately pulled the foil back to and separated the fries to allow the chicken to be spread out.  I quick baked the fries at 400 for a few minutes to restore their crispness.    I would also have liked to see dipping sauce (Ranch Dressing w/celery sticks) offered for the wings.  As is, the salty taste accumulated.  With some sauce, it might not be as noticeable.  Like with the ketchup, it was a problem I solved at home.  But if you are buying and don't have access to  items in your fridge, you might be disappointed.  I hope that the owners will also put their phone number on a banner or in large letters on their window.  If it takes 15 minutes for a meal, letting people know their number so they can call ahead would be really helpful.  Although there were a few minor disappointments, I think they can iron things out and become a nice addition to a well traveled, but sparsely populated area.  Review #3533

Although I have read reviews of the YMCA, none of them talked about the cool park and trail system just north of the facility.  The park has paved trails for hikers and bikers that allow options for one mile and 5K distances.  Inside the northern loop, there are soccer fields, a baseball diamond, and a beach volleyball court.  Along the south side of the loop is a shelter with picnic tables inside.  On the west side of the park is a wooded area that is undeveloped with trails, but not blocked off by fencing.  On the east side is a community garden for locals to plant their own gardens.  There are also loops of trails which run down each side of the campus towards US 36 for the extra hiking distance.    The park looks to be pretty well maintained as well and is free to use without the gym membership.  Parking is available in the lots for the YMCA.  Review #723

1.  This review is for the donut side of the business and does not include eating a meal at the cafe side of the business.  2.  This is CASH ONLY, so if you plan to stop, be sure you have paper, not plastic.  3.  The donuts I tried were really good.  Even the ones I had the next day were still fresh and tasty.  4.  The jelly filled donut I selected had a fair amount of jelly in each bite.  5.  The cinnamon roll I ordered (without the icing) still had a light glaze which allowed the pastry to shine without being smothered in sugary goo.  6.  The cake donut I ordered was light without being doughy or dry.  7.  There is seating, both bar stool and booth, in the donut side of the business.  8.  Employees were efficient and moved the line quickly, though not especially welcoming.  9.  If you hate dodging across traffic on a very busy road like Keystone, you can use the light at 54th street and come up to the parking lot from the side streets to avoid risking an accident trying to get across the multi-lane road.  10.  Overall, good for donuts if you are in a hurry.  Nice selection and very  reasonable prices.  Review #3466

I've been to three different restaurants in the passed month that feature Greek food (gyros and Greek salad) as well as some other traditional American foods, and this is my favorite.    Not only does it have the convenience of a drive through, but it has plenty of space inside to enjoy your meal.  The menu is simple and easy to navigate from the overhead board above the counter.    I stopped by on a Saturday afternoon, ordered when I was ready, and waited for them to call out the order when it was ready a couple minutes later.    The gyro was generously portioned and though I probably could have eaten it all at once, I chose to save part of it for later since I am trying to watch portion sizes.  This is easily a two portion sandwich.  Wrapped in pita, there was a lot gyro meat, tomato, onion, and sauce that make for a wonderful combo.  I also ordered a Greek Salad which was filled with fresh ingredients and comes with the dressing on the side so that you can control how much you use.  The salad comes with olives, tomatoes, onions, and green bell peppers.  There are also cubes of cheese.  (see photo!)  Really tasty food, friendly and efficient service, and convenience.  Sounds like a winner to me!  Review #2054

While in Carmel (Clay Terrace), I decided to grab a bowl of ice cream.  I've only been to one other Cold Stone Creamery before, which I enjoyed, so I thought this would be another good experience.  It was.  I know they offer lots of fancy concoctions and even more mix in items, but I tend to keep ice cream simple:  I want to taste the ice cream as created, not add lots of other sweet items.  They were advertising a couple flavors and I decided to get a little of both:  the Whipped Meyer Lemon sorbet and the Wild Blueberry Muffin Batter ice cream...side by side in the medium bowl.  Wow!  What a combo!  The lightness of the sorbet with that bit of tartness paired really well with the thicker richness of the ice cream.  I felt like a genius!   I have to laugh that so many negative reviews (sadly they are 1 star) are because of the price.  It's Carmel!  It's Clay Terrace!  What do you expect?  It's ice cream.  If you can't afford an occasional splurge on a treat, how can you afford to live here? SMH    I enjoyed the ice cream and even splurged and bought a taffy apple from the other business to go.  Review #2418

I've tried stopping by here several times and always seem too early for their lunch hours  or dinner hours, but I finally arrived later in the day closer to dinner and picked up a large NY style slice of pepperoni that I found to be delicious.  No wonder when the proteins are locally sourced from Turchetti's Salumeria. Delicious!  My only problem was that I didn't want an entire pie, so I settled for a slice which I had no idea how long it had been sitting there.  The flavor was fantastic!, but the crust had become tough and chewier than I prefer.  But that didn't deter me from devouring the slice.  I'll need to return with a group so that we can order an entire pie fresh to see how well this place measures up with other favorites.     I hope they can get enough staff to offer longer & earlier hours.  Pizza for lunch sounds good, but it hast o fit my lunch schedule.  If you like NY Style pizza that is full of flavor, stop by Frankie's.  I t is located along the back wall on he north end of the AMP.  Enjoy!  Review #3950

I'm not sure why restaurants set up in shopping centers where lots of shrubs and trees block a view of the signage and make it easy o miss the entrance.  I get they can't control all the street construction in the area, but for our second lunch in a row, my wife and I struggled finding a restaurant.  Maybe our GPS isn't as accurate, but I had a pretty good idea where Verde was located and through my wife's sharp eyes and her persistence, we pulled up right in front of the restaurant.  After checking in the main entrance, we were able to grab a spot on the patio to enjoy a nice lunch on the patio.     She grabbed a lunch margarita special while I tried my first Paloma.  Not sure why they put the seasoning on the side of a glass that they give you a straw for.  It feels a little weird licking a glass (especially post-covid).   We were provided with some tasty house chips and salsa (the bowl big enough to actually dip!)   My wife ordered the lunch sized Burrito Mexicano with shredded chicken while I got the lunch Chimichanga with the chicken also.  My lunch also came loaded with rice, beans, pico, and sour cream.  no skimping!  My chicken was light and juicy, but my wife's was much dryer, maybe too dry.  The only thing our two chicken orders had in common was that both were woefully underseasoned.  Had they just boiled it?  Good thing I had all the other sides to go with my entree.  There was also a white sauce (Queso) to add which helped a bit too, but the star of the meal should have been the protein, not the sides.   Service was generally good, but at times, the entire patio was devoid of any staff, so my wife offered to head inside to see if she could find someone.  Fortunately, staff appeared before she had to search.  After that, service was better, including getting our bill and checking out.  Overall, it was a decent meal and drink, but with dozens of Mexican restaurants between Verde and my home, I think it will probably be a one and done visit for us.  Review #3930

Disappointing.  That's how I would describe my latest meal at Divvy.  This was the third time my wife and I brought friends to dine with us at Divvy and both prior visits were 5 stars!  But something seemed off as dishes we had tried before weren't as good as we remembered and one of the new ones was just poorly conceived.  I will say that most of the things I ordered tasted pretty good.  Maybe a 4 star.  But when I tried a number of items my tablemates ordered, I found the flavors too one note / bland or slightly inconsistently balanced.  The killer for me was the "Duck Drummies".  They were supposed to have a Thai flavor, so I was expecting something with a bit of heat.  What I got was a soy reduction sauce that concentrated the saltiness to a point that every one at my table agreed that it was too salty.  When I called the waitress  over to see if they were brined because they were extremely salty, her response was that they were supposed to be salty and spicy.  Seemed like she considered the matter closed.  Sure, the drummies were moist and tender, but the sauce was terrible.  We also had some trouble getting our waitress's attention.  I cut her some slack since she was training someone new, but she wouldn't look our way as she passed us, so it was hard to get her attention.  For the price we paid, I expected quality service like I get at other comparably priced places.  Just another disappointment.    I will give them a three because my first two visits were outstanding.  Maybe I just needed to order something different to have a delicious meal and a waitress who was focused  on us instead of training.  Still, I am concerned that one of our favorite northside places may be slipping.  Review #174

As the popularity of malls decreases in central Indiana, the popularity of a different type of experience is stepping into the social vacumn   Instead of lots of stores with a few places to eat, we are now seeing more places to eat and a small grouping of stores being wise enough to locate where people are already gathering.  What makes this food hall different from the others scattered around the metro area is the uniqueness of the Bottleworks development and the effort in preserving the historic details of the former largest coca cola bottling plant in the world.  The Garage is the name given to the food court and you will see the name garage all along Carrollton etched into the building on the west side of the street all the way from Mass Avenue, passed 9th, and up to the north end of the development.  We didn't realize that the south end of the development was NOT the food court and shops.  It is for a separate business.  The food court is strictly north of 9th Street.  There is limited street parking (metered) along Mass Avenue and a few spots along Carrollton, but most of the street is drop off zones only.  Fortunately, there are parking lots that require you to take a ticket when you enter.  The lots are on the west side of the building that contains the food court.  They aren't cheap by Indy standards, running about $5 for 3 hours, with prices for longer periods escalating from there.  The good news is that if you make purchases inside, you may get your parking validated or at least discounted.  I didn't use the lot, so I can't say how much it saves.  Note that you have to take your receipts to a validation station before you attempt to drive off.  Hopefully a future visit or review will make note of where the validation stations are located.    Inside the Garage I found a bunch of food places with mutiple ethnic offerings as well as a burger place, so hopefully, everyone in you group will find something to satisfy their appetite.    The interior of the garage does get a bit loud and my wife thought it a bit austere in appearance.  You get spoiled looking at all the cool detail on the outside of the building and at the hotel, but in here, it seems like any other large space.  Not bad, just not the wow that you see on the approach.  The garage has typical food court seating with mostly smaller tables for social distancing.  So, if you see one retaurant is packed with customers in line, there are usually some tables not too far of a walk down the way.  The place appeared well maintained and seemed like sanitation was in good order too.  Restrooms were unisex and located in the middle of the garage.  You have to keep you eyes open to find them since they don't have large flashing signs calling attention to them.  We found some near the "Lick Ice Cream" shop.  I would gladly return to check out some more of the shops and food places if offered the chance to go.  Review #3844

This review is abased upon my wife's first experience using the large capacity washers and dryers to handle cleaning of new quilts.  Her quilts are simply too large for our home equipment, so she decided to give this modern laundromat a try.  When we arrived, there were plenty of parking spaces near the entrance which made it easy to transport our load of material.  I was impressed by the overall cleanliness and how bright and colorful it was.  I've seen way too many laundries that were dark and dingy, so finding a spacious location with plenty of seating and machines which appeared to be in great working order an eye opening  experience for me.  If you aren't a regular who understands the system, you can ask at the main office (near the entrance for help)  MY wife was told to pick which washers and dryers she wished to use and to go ahead and load the washers.  Each machine is numbered, so remember those numbers for when you are ready to start. (Note you need to bring your own soap and supplies since only some of the machines come loaded with those. Back at the kiosk, you can prepay with coins, currency, or cards.  Once paid, you push another button to start the washing.  I suggest you have all your laundry loaded into the washers before heading to the kiosk so that you don't have to leave the kiosk until you have made all your selections.   We went on a weekday morning and there was no line so my wife got immediate assistance and she found the machines were plenty large enough to easily handle her quilts.  The machines are large and sturdy, so when they went into spin cycle, what would have caused a deafening racket at our home was relatively quiet.     The end result was that my wife's quilt came out clean and dry and didn't take all day to accomplish.    As long as my wife keeps quilting, I can see returning here as a customer.   Review #3946

After several years of being hard to find unless you frequent Farmers Markets or the Circle City Industrial Complex, it's nice to see the sisters behind the delicious ice cream company Lick land a spot in the new Bottleworks Garage.    All the same flavors and all the things you like about the ice cream itself, but now located where you can grab a meal from one of the other vendors in the garage.  All the ice cream is made completely free of artificial ingredients, even food coloring. So, not as wide a range of colors, but pure, fresh flavor all the same.   Although the production part of the business is likely to stay at the previous location at the CCIC,  a new, more accessible store front went into the Bottleworks Garage (Just north of 9th Street).  I ordered a small bowl of champagne cherry ice cream and was thrilled with the flavor!  Make this a must visit place when you visit the Garage.  p.s. I can't resist throwing in that the business got started when one of the sisters got an ice cream maker for a wedding gift....Now that was a useful gift put to good use!  Rev #57

IKEA has its own way of doing things.  It must work for them since the place is very crowded even 3 weeks after opening.  I have never been to one previously and had only scanned a few reviews before trying again on a Monday, late morning to make my first visit.  I was mainly interested in trying the Swedish Meatballs that everyone was praising.  (A full plate of meatballs, potatoes and gravy, lingonberry sauce, and seasonal veggies for only $4.99 is a great deal.)  So after finding a parking spot in the massive lot they have surrounding the store, I entered the east entrance and quickly figured out that I started at location 1.  What I did not realize until I made my way passed the endless meandering shoppers who were blocking the aisles was that there are no straight hallways until you reach location 21 which looks like the inside of a Lowe's or Menards.  That large warehouse area leads to the checkout area (Location 22).    The significance of this winding pathway is that you can't just go to the area you wish to shop directly.  You have to go through the entire store to find what you want and then pay for it on the other end.  Sure, if you look closely enough at signs, there are a few double doors that let you short cut (like through a maze) to save time.  But as I found out that the restaurant was at location 11 (the middle), you have to do a lot of walking to get there.  Oddly, you can see the street from the windows of the restaurant, but there are no doors there.  The restaurant was clean and bright, but only one side was opened as I waited nearly 20 minutes (on a Monday) to get to the order counter.  I noticed that the other side opened after I was well into the winding aisle for my side, so bad timing on my part.    I will say that the food is very affordable and the portions were quite enough for a lunch.  I enjoyed trying the Swedish Meatball plate (see above for details).  The gravy and berry sauce both worked well with the meatball flavors.  I also ordered a small berry cheesecake slice that was again, very affordably priced and tasted very light for a cheesecake.  Admittedly, the cream cheese layer was thinner than most, but it did have a layer of baked in berries and was topped with a sweetened crumble.  (4 stars for the food flavor, 5 stars for value).  After lunch, I decided to look for the Swedish Market after picking up a household item along the way.  They have stations of bright yellow bags for hauling your items around if you don't wish to push a cart throughout the entire store.  The overhead guides/directories count off which location I had reached and I kept seeing the Swedish Market was in location 23.  But since the checkout is in location 22, where was the market?  I doubled back and finally stopped an employee and was told that the Swedish Market (23) and the Bistro (24) were outside the checkout area.   So, I stood in line for one of the 7 open lanes (15 possible) and waited for about 15 minutes before two more aisles opened.  I made like a madman for the counter and was second in line.  I paid and looked at my purchase just sitting there.  I asked and apparently, they don't put your purchases in bags for you.  Some Eco friendly reason, but not very helpful for shoppers.  So, I grabbed my purchase and receipt and wandered over to the Swedish Market.  There I picked up a few items. Again, I wasn't sure what I was supposed to do.  Where was I to pay for them?  I went to the bistro and was able to pay there.  Apparently, someone had gone on lunch break who was supposed to tell people where to pay and to sell them reusable bags for carrying purchases.  Good thing I only got the three things at the market!    Sure, there are lots of items for sale and some even had great prices.  But it was odd having to make purchases at the restaurant, at the checkout, and at the bistro for the market.  Seems like a very inefficient way to run a business.  It apparently works for them, but not for me.    I made my way out with my purchases literally in my hands through the west exit.  Note that if you want to go to the market or bistro, I think you can directly enter the west side and avoid the long walk.  Review #434

I had a bit of a struggle settling on how high of a rating to give this Verde.  I think it depends upon your expectations before you arrive.  If you like a place that has tasty food and drinks, I could easily have bumped his up to a 5 star.  If you want to dine in a clean space that looks like new with good service (Pablo was our guy).  Again, another high rating.  If you want to eat an affordable lunch without alcoholic beverages, well there are lots of other options within the metro area that are far more affordable.  I also thought the dining area was a bit noisy and that even though the restrooms were right off the dining area, there was no signage indicating where to head without asking.  Some outdoor seating is also available if you catch a nice weather day and don't mind nearby traffic sounds.  Let me say hat my meal was delicious!  I ordered a quesadilla with strip steak that was so tender that I didn't need a knife to cut the tortilla or the meat.  Great flavor and texture.  I love that there was plenty of topping for the entire entree incl. pico and sour cream.  Rice and beans weren't overcooked either, so the entire meal was enjoyable.  Didn't have room for dessert, but they do have several options to choose from.  Lots of mixed/frozen drinks to choose from as well.  Just be aware that if you're top concern is pricing, know that the cost will skyrocket quickly.  Most entrees even at lunch were $10 or more.  This isn't like dining on street food or from a food truck.  This is more like dining in a nice restaurant and paying for that experience.   Review #3956 ee

When I am looking for something new for my home, I really like that feeling when I first walk through the door, that the place is filled with lots of options and all seem like they could make my life more interesting.  Now that I am married, an item needs to pass both my criteria AND my  wife's, but even that wasn't a problem at Houseworks!  As we explored the showroom, we were greeted by the staff and offered help if we needed anything, otherwise, we were free to browse.  My wife was simply looking for a table lamp (which she found) and also a floor lamp.  She had in mind what she wanted and while she worked with the salesman to find it, I browsed what seemed like an art museum of wonderful furniture and fixtures and decor.    If I wanted to have the coolest den or man cave, there were tables that used gears for expanding or drop leaves that could save room.  Artistic pieces adorned the walls and side tables too.  My wife tried some of the chairs around the multiple tables set up for dining rooms and if she may start prompting me to go along with getting some.  She liked that they were more than simply functional for eating, but that they could easily adapt to becoming more relaxing allowing the person seated there to lean back.  Honestly, if all shopping was this much fun, I would go more often!  Now understand these aren't mass produced (ie poor quality) pieces.  But if you are shopping for furniture on the north side of town, I assume you already know that it can get expensive.  As long as the quality is there, I don't mind.    I have a feeling that some more shopping is in our near future.  I have a feeling that Houseworks  will be seeing us again soon!  Review #3847

After a morning of hiking, I stopped by Rick's for lunch.  Since I had been outdoors, I passed on sitting outside by the reservoir and chose a spot at the indoor bar.  I was immediately greeted and brought menus and a glass of ice water.    Although I was leaning toward something from the lunch menu, I wanted to try an appetizer which is only listed on the dinner menu.  No problem.  I ordered the crab stuffed mushrooms served with melted mozzarella and a Mornay sauce (a white roux with greyere cheese).  There were six mushrooms in the tray and the flavor was really good.  I'm not sure what other seasoning was added, but the flavor was definitely lifted.  Before long, my lunch salmon roulade arrived.  The salmon was served rolled on its side, stuffed with melted Boursin cheese and warmed spinach.  As might be suspected, the outer ring of salmon was a little overcooked, but the interior rings were cooked just right.  Overall, it could have used more seasoning since none of the components stood out flavor wise.  The entree came with a small salad/slaw and a scoop of Yukon Gold mashed potatoes.  The slaw was okay, but had an unusual texture.  The potatoes were quite tasty even without any additional seasoning.  I was the only person seated at the interior bar since it was so early in the day.  So, I was able to get swift attention from the bartender in between orders from other servers working out in the dining area.  Overall, the staff seemed efficient, but not very personable.  The food was good, but on the bland side.  The prices seemed to match the food, but made for an expensive lunch.  For the quality of ingredients and pricing, I expected something a bit closer to a "wow" factor in flavor.  Review #834

While in Irvington for breakfast Our first,choice-place, was Closed due to a lack of staffing.  Fortunately I remembered that Lincoln square offered complete meals just down the street and had their own lot.  inside had plenty of room though it wasn't as accessible as I had-hoped.  normally I order  Eggs Benedict when out for breakfast,  I changed selection to the Indiana Benedict.   Instead of the light and   and rich Hollanddaisese..the meat was more like a burger patty than Canadian bacon for breakfast   The breakfast wtopped with gravy which was much heavier than the usual Hollanddaise too,I would suggest   The Standard option.  Review#3946  .

A lot of my Yelp friends have been enjoying this place, so I decided to follow their suggestion and stop by on a cool and drizzling afternoon.  They have plenty of free parking during the day, so I waited for the doors to open and went inside.  I immediately noticed the large stone fireplace that took all the chill and dampness out of the air.  Inside was a bit sparse, but was still inviting to customers.  As the first customer of the day, I decided to sit at the small bar area and enjoyed hearing the story behind the founding of the distillery.  I hadn't had a cocktail in 30 years so I decided to stay away from the straight shots and picked one of the selections suggested by the bartender based upon my previous experiences and flavor preferences.  (Very helpful!)  I settled on a house vodka based drink that had a key flavor elements of lemon juice, raspberry, and mint.  The complementary mint leaf and fresh raspberry on top made the beverage as visually appealing as was the taste.  I decided to use the narrow straw since the glass was filled with ice after the beverage had been shaken, not stirred. ;)  It was a little strong at first since my palate wasn't used to the concentrated alcohol, but because the vodka was smooth, I quickly adjusted to the taste and enjoyed the drink.  Very nice flavor balance between the ingredients.    Quite a few of the cocktails they have on their menu are seasonal, so if you aren't a regular here, there are bound to be new flavor combos the next time you visit.  I really enjoyed the conversation and beverage.  Great atmosphere and although they don't have a food menu, there was a popcorn popper on site and food is allowed from other restaurants inside the dining area.  Oh, and it is pet friendly.  Review #408

On a return visit, I brought my wife along to dinner on Thursday night.  The restaurant was about 2/3 full, but we were greeted immediately and shown to a table promptly.  The staff was very friendly throughout the evening as several staff members stopped by to see if we needed anything else throughout the dinner.    My wife ordered a Chimichanga with shredded chicken wrapped in a fried tortilla and served with rice, lettuce, sour cream, guacamole, and Pico de Gallo.  The Chimi also had a cheese sauce with a bit of heat to dress the wrap.  My wife commented that the chicken was moist and was made from real chicken, not some processed, pre cooked pieces like she has had at some other restaurants.  She definitely preferred Don Cuervo's to our regular haunts.  She also had a strawberry margarita rimmed with sugar.  The size was a bit smaller than some monstrous margaritas she has had elsewhere, but the price was significantly less as well, so the price seemed reasonable for the quantity.   I decided to go with something different from my normal and selected the Tacos de Camaron with grilled shrimp, Mexican rice, pinto beans with cheese, cabbage, & cilantro on soft corn tacos.  There were three double shelled tacos that came with a "green" sauce (guacamole based) and tomatillo sauce (spicy with a bit of heat).  I tried my tacos with different combination of sauces and found the combo with both sauces the most tasty.  I also preferred when I only used one of the shells instead of the double shell.  I understand that a single layer can tear and spill the contents, especially when using sauces.  But the taco held together for me and the single shell allowed the flavors of the contents to shine more.    The quality of this restaurant's food and staff made us feel welcome and appreciated (and quite full!)  We are in agreement that it is worth the extra miles to return for our future Mexican food cravings.  p.s.  In the brief time between my visits, new additions have been made to adorn the wall space.  Now I don't have anything to complain about!  Rev 11

I stopped in at lunch today and enjoyed a tasty herbal tea and light lunch.  The restaurant is located on the northeast corner of 22nd and Talbot.  The business has a private lot on the north side of the building (per the employees:  ignore the towing warnings if you are a customer.)  There is also limited street parking out front on 22nd and southbound on Talbot.  The interior has a very cool vibe.  There are paintings by Indy's own Justin Vining on the west wall.  There isn't a lot of seating, so I'm not sure how well it would accommodate a larger group.   The order counter is beyond the dining area.  A couple small chalkboards on the right hand side list the options:  One for all the tea options; one for the sandwiches and sides available. I found it easier to read the small print by going over to the chalkboards first instead of trying to read them from the counter and holding up the line.  I selected one of the combo options:  1/2 sandwich, Caesar salad, and side (for about $8).  I also noticed the teas are grouped into four categories.  They also have ordering "steps" on each board so that you can understand your options before getting in line.  Now here's something to be aware of...let them know if it is for dining in or a to go selection.  Then, if staying in, have your table selected.  My cashier seemed intent on asking these questions which necessitated my stating my order a third time since he was too focused on doing things in order and not listening to what I said.  Not a big deal, but it didn't seem like he was an experienced staffer.  I paid for my order at that time and then went to my table.  In a very brief time, my plate was brought out with a cloth napkin and fork.  The plate looked a little sparse on presentation.  The Ham and Swiss (half) had a nice flavor, but didn't seem to have any condiments or additional ingredients to lift it beyond a somewhat bland flavor.  The spinach salad looked rather underwhelming, but when I tasted it, the salad dressing completely changed my mind about the salad.  It was delicious!  I would definitely order it again.  Oh, and the unadorned potato salad, which looked like it was plated by a half cup ice cream scoop, was one of the best potato salads I have ever had.  I noticed a sweetness that I would guess was from bread and butter pickles being one of the ingredients.  Nice chunks (a large dice) for most of the potatoes as well, so again, it exceeded my initial perception.  If they could work on plating (maybe a little garnish?) and offer condiments for the sandwiches, they could add another star to the rating.  Finally, I ordered one of the herbal teas (Iced and Individual sized).  The staffer was quite helpful about making a recommendation after hearing I was looking for an herbal iced option, even offering me a view and whiff of the aroma before choosing.    Sadly, I only had two bites of my meal left by the time my tea was brought out.  I assume it was delayed due to the glass being individually brewed.  I can't fault them for that, because the taste was delicious instead of tasting like something that had sat around all day.  But be aware that if you want something to drink with your meal, you might want to order a glass of water unless you can hold off eating until the drink is served.   Review #276

Although this theater shows second run films, they have somehow managed to keep the place in good shape and are an affordable option for anyone who wants the big screen experience without going broke.  I recently returned to catch a film I missed during the avalanche of movies released trying to be considered for Oscar nominations.  The check in process was easy and the common areas appeared clean.  The actual theater was huge with two aisles splitting the seating into three areas.  I grabbed a seat closer to the front to get the "big picture" effect and was able to pick any seat I wished.  The picture and sound quality were okay.  Not the best, but good enough to be enjoyed.  The seating was the old fashioned kind that you sit in...not recline/nap in.    They appeared to have a variety of concession items and a few activities in a game room just off the lobby.  My only real negative is that the hallways outside the theater are quite dark.  Even a my noon time viewing, it felt like walking down a darkened city street.  A few simple lighting modifications could make the area much more inviting.  Review #491

I saw a photo of this restaurant on Yelp this morning, and since I was going to be in the neighborhood, I decided to grab an early lunch.  There was plenty of parking since this restaurant is in the same strip mall as the Kroger on SR135 in Greenwood.    I noticed a sign as I entered that informs the customers to place their order at the counter or to help their selves to a menu and place their order when ready.  I decided to go for the Hibachi chicken (with mixed vegetables and brown rice) and the Tiger Sushi Roll - Deep fried shrimp, cucumber, topped with eel, avocado and eel sauce with spicy sauce on the side.    The chicken was okay but a bit overcooked and drab in appearance.  The vegetables were tasty (onion and squash) and the rice was well over a cup.  I appreciated the option of using plastic ware and/or chopsticks.  Maybe some more colorful veggies or some decorative garnish could help make the meal appear more appetizing.  The flavor was fine, just nothing special that you can't get at a fast food franchise.  I was also given a bright yellow bottle that looked like a mustard dispenser.  I had to ask the cashier what it was since the bottle wasn't labeled.  She told me it was Yum Yum sauce and couldn't describe it.  I decided to give it a try on my rice and I can't really describe it either.  It was tasty, but I still can't place a name to the flavor combinations.  Finally, the sushi was on a completely different level (so glad I saved the best for last!)  First, the presentation was on a real plate (not styrofoam).  The sushi segments were colorfully arranged in a serpentine pattern which made it look much more appetizing as well.  And the flavor was delicious!  The shrimp was cooked just right.  The two sauces added a nice layer of flavor along with the soy sauce for dipping.  My only recommendation for the sushi would be to have a lower sodium soy sauce option available. (The plate comes with a small amount of wasabi paste and ginger, as well.)  There are quite a few options for Japanese food which I haven't sampled yet.  But based upon today, I know where I can get a good tasting sushi made to order with very little wait.  Review #61

I have been here three times and have always enjoyed the experience.    I was able to attend the grand opening (5-9-16) and was pleasantly surprised at how good my meal was. I had heard good things about the beer selection from friends who had been to the Nashville franchises, but they had not told me about the food. What caught my eye was the JB Burger....JB as in "James Beard" award winning combination burger with two kinds of mushrooms mixed in with three kinds of beef cuts. Add locally made brie cheese and you have yourself a delicious sandwich. I was also glad that they offered baked potato wedges instead of the traditional fries. This was the best burger I have had this year!  Being a newbie when it comes to craft beers, I was able to get a nice tutorial from the saloon bartender Tabby. She let me sample a variety of the house brands so that I could find a selection that I would be happy with. I ended up buying a 4-pack to have at home.  My second time, I met a retired friend from work for lunch (5-17-16).  Based upon another friend's recommendation, I started with the White Bean Puree (with grilled corn tortillas, cherry tomato, fiesta relish, lime cucumber chips, avocado, and cilantro oil).  Excellent choice.   I also tried the Smoked Brisket (with Tulip Tree Nettle cheese, pickled squash & micro greens on Ciabatta bun with baked potato wedges.)  This was the only item I have tried that I was disappointed with.  There was some gristle in the brisket and the nettle cheese didn't appeal to my palate.  Probably won't try the sandwich again unless they make some changes to the ingredients.  My third visit, I talked my wife into stopping for lunch after she had an appointment on the west side (5-25-16).  We were able to sit out on the east patio in the shade and enjoy the beautiful spring weather while we waited for our shared Primal Pizza (Pepperoni, Sausage, bacon, ham, marinara & mozzarella). Although I could easily have devoured the entire pizza my self, I showed some restraint and got a to go box.  The pizza was still good cold.  As far as service, it was a little slow on opening day, but that was totally expected.  But once I was first greeted, there was plenty of attention, including the beer tutorial.  I have not encountered any of the delays.  Of course, going at "off peak" times seems to reduce the likelihood of those delays.  Finally, I have sampled a number of craft beers and although not all of them have been for me, they do have a wide variety as well as wine and hard liquor options.  I know which of the house beers I like and am looking forward exploring some of the seasonal options.  I already have plans in the works for bringing two more sets of friends out to enjoy the restaurant.  Review #14

It's been awhile since I have been to a BRU Burger, so I was pleasantly surprised by the newest addition to the expanding Cunningham Group.  Located on the eastern end of the central block of Perry Crossing, there is plenty of free parking in the lot to the south of the building as well as a few angled street spaces out front.  The entrance is on the northeast corner of the building (although there are some doors on the east side that could use some signage directing you to the front.)    We were greeted promptly and noticed there are several rooms of tables for dining indoors and an outdoor patio on the north side.  We were taken back into one of the more spacious rooms and were surprised at how full the place was even at 5:30 on a Tuesday evening.  We suspected something good was about to happen.    After a brief wait, our server arrived with menus and silverware and took our drink orders.  We were ready with our selections by the time she returned, so we were able to place our orders ahead of the growing crowd.  I ordered the fantastic Gorgonberry Pecan salad (small size) and the Garlic Three Cheese Burger with a side of Fries.  All were tasty and generously sized.  My wife went for the Patty Melt and a side of onion rings (and a to go box since she couldn't finish it all!)    Notes:  The "small" salad filled most of a square 9-inch plate!  I specifically asked if this was the small and it was confirmed.  Wow!  That was a lot of salad!  Excellent flavor combinations with just enough dressing.  I really liked how the pecans no longer have the red pepper flakes on them like the original BRU Burger downtown had.  The bacon on top was crisp and in large bites so that the flavor wasn't lost in the mix.    Although I like my steaks medium rare, I like my burgers with a nice char on the surface, so if it has to be cooked well or medium-well to get the char, that's fine with me.  (I hate bland fatty burgers!)  So, I was glad that this burger met my specifications and had a nice flavor with the roasted garlic and truffle aioli.  The sandwich came with thin dill pickle slices that I recommend adding into the sandwich.  The salty/vinegar taste added another level to each bite that really made the sandwich.    Instead of ordering appetizers of onion rings or fries, we went with the sides.  The portions here are huge, so unless you are ravenous, the side portions are less than half the price of the appetizers and still have enough for most humans I know!  ($3 for onion rings, $2 for fries).    Service was attentive and made sure that to acknowledge our requests and act upon them promptly.  And if you are going to dine here regularly, you've got to get a dining card to accumulate points.  We are about one dinner away from earning a $100 gift card!      The only negatives I can point out are that the room can get a little loud, but we didn't have any trouble conversing.  Seating was rather close, so it was a little awkward hearing our neighboring diners' conversations in detail.  The "house" ketchup is okay, but something about it tasted different from the downtown location.  I really loved the downtown original ketchup.  Something about this seemed out of balance and made me almost ask if they had a standard ketchup, but it was okay.  Just not my favorite.    I appreciate that there are lots of burger places that want to push the envelope of flavor combinations.  But not all of them work.  Sometimes, keeping it simple tastes the best.  So, I really like that there is a "Classic" section of the menu as well as the "Chef" section.  Just enough tweaks to make them something you probably wouldn't have at home, but close enough so that you still taste the burger.  Review #285

There is a great new brewery that opened on South US31 along the Greenwood/Whiteland boundaries.  Though the address is 6001 N, the actual location is in the 6800 block just south of Pushville Road (CR700N) in the South Greenwood Shoppes.   Since the brewery just opened in early May '18, I was surprised at the number of brews they had on hand (around a dozen).  All the batches are small, so there is a lot of turnover on the listing blackboard (two of those listed were out, but another two were ready to take their place!)  The name of the brewery and some of the ales can be tied to the owners experience with the construction industry.  I decided to go with a pilsner (GFI 5.3%, 22 IBU), a coffee flavored stout (Sledge Hammer 4.5%, 25), a Session (6%, 25) and a Peanut Butter Stout (5.7%, 24) as a flight of five ounce drinks.  The flights can be up to six selections and pricing is affected by the type of beer selected and the quantity of choices you make.  My four were $7.25.    I thought most of the beers had good flavor with the exception of the GFI which was a little weak....probably because my tastes are changing as I move towards stouts, sours, and IPA's.  It wasn't bad, just not what I would order next time.  At the time of my visit, there was a menu of grilled cheese, a panini, and flatbreads.  There are also salads, soups, and some dips and charcuterie. Those foods are available for dinner around 6 or so until the chef goes home for the evening.  When that happens, there is a limited "after hours" menu that has some chips and salsa/dip, pizzas, hot dogs, and pretzels.  The bartender and the owner were both accommodating and easy to talk to.  They have obvious passion for making their business take off and hope they can build a strong business.  Adding local musicians is already in the works for entertainment.  As the business grows, there is hope to add a lunch menu with new hours as soon as they can get the right staff hired.  Plans for expanding to add a distillery next door are also in the works.  For those who are not beer drinkers, there are some wines and a 17% harder liquor available for cocktails, but I have not tried them.  Review #1003

Krannert is another one of the better Indy Parks.  This is one with a very nice pond and shaded shelters/playgrounds.  There is a large family rec center and an aquatic center.  In the outlying areas of the park, there are sports fields/courts for the bigger kids.    For those who like hiking, there are two options with paved pathways.  Although the park & rec center are showing some age, I did see the parks department had workers attending the outdoor swimming pool.  I hope the maintenance continues to keep the park at a high quality.  Review #662

What I like most about this theater is that it carries a wide variety of films.  Living on the southwest side, I am pleased when one of the "art" films plays here, saving me a trip to the other side of town (Keystone Arts theater).    Since there are 18 theaters, they come in a variety of sizes.  I believe all now have reserved seating and have improved comfort, many with the ability to recline.  One thing to be aware of is that there is a single entrance area on the east end of the building.  Because of the building's size, you can have quite a long walk from the lobby to the far end if your movie is showing on the west end.  I am not sure whether it was poorly designed or simply modified to add more theaters at a later date, but most over-sized theaters I have been to have a central lobby for convenience.  Prices vary depending upon the movie and sometimes, upon the day of the week/time of day.  I seldom buy popcorn or snacks, so I assume these are somewhat standard, but most assuredly over priced for value.  The theater is not my favorite, but is one I often turn to for convenience and options.  Review #920

Mofoco is a nice choice if you are near the Monon in Broad Ripple.  They have a variety of taco options, but on my visit, I decided to try the Chicken Club Wrap.  Really solid choice.  The wrap is stuffed with lots of meat and veggies and flavored with smoked gouda and chipotle aioli.  Very nice flavor.  Although the chicken was a little chewy, the other ingredients kept it moist.    I also ordered the seasoned fries as a side and upgraded with the basil aioli for dipping.  Very tasty combo that went well with the wrap.    Service was prompt and courteous.  I appreciated that the check was dropped off while I was still eating which allowed me time to ask for a "to go" box for the other half of my wrap.  Overall, a very pleasant experience.  Review #345

The first time I went to Big Woods was opening week.  5-stars on everything (considering how swamped they were).  Great food and knowledgeable service.  The next three times, the food was okay, but I noticed the place was loud and service was pretty good, but not great.  Last night, I went in a group of four and the drop off was so significant that I could no longer give this a high rating.  The waitress was attentive and did a "good" job, though there was a mix up between our bills that was partially corrected.  The beer was excellent, as usual.  But the food was just not up to standards we saw when the place opened.  Nobody at the table felt the food was that good.  My pizza had a marinara sauce that might have been plain tomato sauce.  No flavor depth even with multiple toppings.  The worst was my wife's fish and chips.  The fish itself was okay, but the breading/batter was soggy.  She tried it and ended up peeling it off because of the texture.  It was like the fish had been cooked and then either reheated or put in a microwave.  I don't know, but it shouldn't have been soggy.  She could have sent it back, but since everyone was already hungry and had started eating, she put up with peeling it.  A great waitress would have noticed the pile of breading on the plate and have asked.    And the cole slaw, which most places have as a cool and refreshing or at least creamy with a crunch, was soggy and topped with hot pepper flakes.  My wife doesn't like heat, so she only ate a bite of the cole slaw.  I sampled it and it was so different from what I expect from a cole slaw that I passed on a second bite.  Who wants hot flakes on cole slaw?  Put heat on entrees or wings, but why ruin cole slaw?  I may continue buying their beer, but Speedway now has plenty of other good places to get a good meal.  Rev.  #24

This neighborhood park has historical significance for Indy as well as providing a nice playground for kids.  Camp Morton was a training ground for soldiers preparing for the civil war on what was once the state fairgrounds.  Later, the site became a Confederate prison from 1862-5.  Now, this raised park (wheel chair accessible) has good drainage and paved walkways with numerous picnic tables and trash bins to help keep the park clean.  Leashed pets are welcome and doggie bags can be obtained from a dispenser on site.  The playground has a central climbing piece with slides.  To the east, a set of swings and a spring animal for riding have been added.  A shelter occupies the south east corner of the park.  There is no designated parking for the location and I did not see any water fountains/restrooms on site.  Still, with a bit of planning, the park looks like a fun place to gather where families can grab a table and watch as the kids have fun.  Review #517

Peterson's is a very good steak house that is changing to a more customer friendly restaurant.  I would like to give them another half point just for that!    I took my wife out to dinner on Wednesday evening as part of the Devour Northside promotion.  Although I misjudged the drive time to Fishers (rush hour traffic is not for the inexperienced!), I called to let the restaurant know we would be late.  The receptionist was understanding and said they would hold our reservations.  (It always pays to be considerate!)     We arrived around 5:30 and found a convenient parking spot just outside the entrance in their private lot.  Note:  The entrance is on Hague Road north of 96th Street and getting across the southbound traffic can be challenging.  Once you make it across the street, you have to drive past the first business and look for a sign that directs you back to the Peterson's lot.    Once seated, it did take about 15 minutes for our waiter to show up, but after that initial wait, service improved significantly.  Still, it would have been nice to have had a more prompt greeting.    Ah, but the food was worth the wait!  After an amuse bouche of ceviched salmon on a crisp cracker, we were brought a bread course of warm pretzel and potato breads.  These came with room temperature butter and cheddar butter.  I appreciate that the butter is spreadable and doesn't lay there like a lump on the bread.  This was so good, we got a second round!    I ordered the Miniature Maryland Lump Crab Cake with stone ground mustard, beurre blanc, red pepper coulis, and Italian parsley aioli.  Excellent!  It had a fresh taste and had nice bits of celery to add a crunch to the tender crab.  Some spices, but nothing too strong to mask the crab flavor.    My wife ordered the Maine lobster bisque which has sherry, herb infused oil, and chives.  In the description, it denotes lump Maine lobster.  Unfortunately, there was very little actual lobster "lumped" into the bowl.  The flavor was good, but if you say there should be lumps of lobster, then you should check your dish before bringing it out.      We both ordered the Grilled 6 oz hand cut midwest beef tenderloin filet with house made veal jus, roasted tomato confit.  Very nicely prepared and served on a plate that didn't come with a burn warning.  They let the steaks rest so that the juice doesn't rush out when you first slice into the meat (which you are asked to do at the time the steak is served to check that it is cooked properly.)    One of the improvements at Peterson's is that they now include side dishes with the steak instead of gouging you for shareable a la carte servings.  As a customer, I find a large white plate of steak without any garnish or sides to be rather boring and unimaginative.  The Peterson plate comes with their signature mashed potatoes (creamy with bits of potato skin and just enough lumps to remind me of home made potatoes) and a side of garden fresh roasted carrots and squash medley.  There is actual color on a plate and to me, that makes the whole meal look more appetizing!  The veggies are sprinkled with tarragon to add an herbal taste to compliment the savory roasted flavors.  Of special note, the mushrooms were buttery and really raised the whole dining level when eaten with the potatoes.    The manager stopped by our table and we discussed the change.  He seemed rather pleased that we noticed the difference and said it wasn't something done just for the promotional period.      For dessert, my wife went with the creme brulee while I opted for the Eli's Cheesecake with blueberry compote and whipped cream.  The desserts were okay, but not the spectacular culmination we hoped for on a nice evening dining out.    So, if you are looking for a special night out, consider Peterson's if you don't mind the adventure getting there.  Review #138

I heard about the southwestern bar Reata a few months after it opened, so I picked a nice Tuesday (3-22-16) to check them out for lunch. I got there right as it opened, so I decided to sit at the bar of this shotgun style bar/restaurant.  Although I am not a fan of country music, it lent a pleasant background vibe. After looking over the menu and placing my order, I asked the bartender if he would mind my looking around while I waited.  I ended up getting a mini tour of the facility which was very much appreciated.  I found a second bar just off the main dining and bar area.  This bar catered primarily to the two sports themed rooms on the east and west of the bar.  One is decorated as a Purdue room, the other as Indiana U.  Apparently, there is enough room for indoor corn hole games to break out!  I also was shown the area in the back with multiple individual restrooms with doors that become more opaque once they are closed.  NOTE:  If you can see out, then you haven't gotten the door properly closed and locked. :)  I also found out that the name "Reata" which means "lariot or lasso" was chosen because it was the name of the ranch in the James Dean movie "Giant".  The bartender was very informative (and I believe one of the owners.)  Even though it was a Taco Tuesday (special), I decided to go with the salsa and chips (large enough quantity to share) and the Southwestern side salad.  What I really liked about the salad was that it had roasted corn in the mix.  The roasted corn flavor made this salad distinctively memorable in a good way.  I will definitely consider ordering it again the next time I stop in.    I have heard good things about the mac and cheese too, but was too full from the chips and salad to try the pasta on this trip.  A steady flow of customers started rolling in as it got closer to noon, so I let the bartender take care of his customers while I enjoyed my lunch.  Review #40

"What's the point of being alive," she said, "if you're not going to communicate?" - Kurt Vonnegut - Bluebeard  Okay, let me state up front that this is based upon my lunch on Monday.  I haven't dined in the evening, and my two previous lunches a few years ago left me disappointed (the first time) and uninspired (the second).  So, why the turnaround now?  Well, I took my wife down Virginia Avenue, and our first choice restaurant was closed.  We saw Amelia's and headed there before finally deciding to stop in next door at Bluebeard.  So, without a chance to plan what I would have, I went with my gut and chose the simple burger.  The menu didn't even identify the "house side".  In the past, I have tried some more "creative" food items and they just weren't for me.   I must say that the burger, although on the high side of price, was excellent.  Cooked a little more than I requested, the chef understood my main message:  The burger has to have a great sear or else it isn't worth eating.  The good news is that the burger was juicy and full of flavor in spite of being cooked until devoid of pink.  There was a salty component that brought out the beef flavor.  When combined with the Dijon bacon aioli, provolone, fresh tomato, romaine, and pickled red onion for the acidity, the burger was delicious.  The bun was a brioche and was fresh and soft, yet sturdy enough to hold up to the juices.  The house side was a pasta salad.  Macaroni noodles with cherry tomato halves, basil, and a few other unidentifiables brought a savory rich flavor to go with the salted beef of the sandwich.  Totally delicious and highly recommended.  My wife opted for the Egg Salad sandwich.  The sandwich was served on crispy toasted country loaf and included capers, pickled red onion, greens, goat cheese chunks, and bagna cauda.  She thought it one of the better tasting egg salad combos she has had.  This one tasted of lemon and salt undertones to the egg.    The service was suited to the setting.  We chose to dine on the front patio under the shade of one of the leafy trees.  I ordered a Gose (sour lemon flavored beer) to sip while we waited for our meals.  Jared was welcoming and although he left the patio at times, seemed to show up at just the right times to bring our food and our bill.  The experience felt more like a picnic than a fancy luncheon.  Overall, my wife seemed to enjoy the break from our routines as much as I did.  Oh, one last thing:  I took my wife into the bar area so that she could see the ultra cool setting.  "Bluebeard", the novel by Hoosier author Kurt Vonnegut, inspired the decor as well as the name of the restaurant.  The walls of the bar dining area are covered in shelves laden with hard covered books and antique typewriters (redundant, I know).  It is somewhat dark like the place a writer might find an escape from the grind of turning out pages.    Review #115

I really liked my lunch at Miracle.  There is a cool ambiance to the restaurant and the friendly staff were quick to greet me and show me where to sit.  I decided to start my meal with the Brussels Sprouts.  They are served halved and tempura style, surrounded by lots of smoky bacon bits.  The dish comes with both spicy mayo and sweet chili sauces for dipping.  I wasn't expecting to find sprouts in an Asian/sushi restaurant, but I was so glad I tried them. Delicious!  I followed up the appetizer with the Crispy Unagi roll.  This 8-piece specialty roll was tasty and had a nice balance of flavors.  I liked that they serve low-sodium soy sauce in a cool mini pitcher and bowl as the default soy.  The roll comes with both wasabi and ginger.  The ginger is white ginger and has a tart flavor instead of the usual floral taste.  It still looks pink in color, but the flavor was a refreshing change of pace.  Service was friendly and prompt.  Parking was convenient with free parallel parking out front and lot parking behind the restaurant (both sides have entrances.)  Prices are on the higher end of the sushi spectrum, but reasonable since the quality is top notch.   Overall, it was a delightful dining experience.  Review # 450

I stopped in one afternoon to try a flight of the house brews.  They offer a trio of your choice for $7 (each sample comes in a "fruit glass" size of 5 or 6 ounces.)  I liked that there was plenty of parking in the lot next to the building and a fair amount of room inside (they have a patio for nice days as well.)  The place was clean and the staff seemed friendly and provided timely service.  It's just that the beers didn't wow me.  I found the three I picked seemed like they didn't have much difference in taste.  That surprised me because I thought there would be significant differences when I ordered a Kolsch, a blackberry wheat, and an Oktoberfest.  When I tried the Kolsch, I wasn't sure I had the right glass.  (Honestly, the bartender may have switched the Oktoberfest and the Kolsch since the Oktoberfest seemed closer to what I expected than the Kolsch did.)  The Kolsch could have been any generic beer...no significant taste of clove or bananas that I get from most local breweries.     The blackberry wheat was my favorite of the three, but even it had only a small amount of blackberry flavor.  It did have a little tartness to it to make it stand out the most of the three choices.  The Octoberfest had a spiced taste, but didn't stand out like some autumnal beverages I have enjoyed elsewhere.  The beers weren't bad...just nothing special.  So, based on my experience, I was disappointed.  Note that I haven't tried any of the food or gone when the business was really busy.  Just one man's thoughts on a sunny autumn afternoon.  Review #410

I went with my son to B Spot one weekday evening.  The restaurant shares parking at the Ironworks with other businesses (including restaurants), so we had to park at the far side of the lot.  So, we were surprised at how few diners were in B Spot.  It was a nice day, so the sides of the restaurant were open to let in the fresh air.  We sat near the opening and placed our orders fairly soon after arriving.  I was considering the "build your own" option, but chose the "award winning" Porky's Burger with pulled pork, cole slaw, and Cleveland sauce.  I also added onion rings and sampled some of my sons rosemary fries.  Frankly, the Pork was a bit dry and I wasn't sure if I should add one of the other sauces in bottles.  I didn't want to screw up the intended flavor by adding something different just to moisten the pork taste.  The burger part was okay, but not memorable.   Considering this restaurant takes so long for me to reach (nearly an hour), I doubt I will return.  There are so many good burgers around town that when an "award winner" fails to wow me, then I think I will choose the other better, and closer, options.  Review #47

There is a lot to like about TwoDeep Brewing.  First, it's downtown and has its own parking lot on the north side of the building.  You have to approach from the north since Capitol Avenue is one way southbound, but any street aiming north can get you to St Clair, and from there, just head south and look on your right.  Second, the building is spacious and has a cool look and vibe to it.  Lots of seating with a lounging area and local art on consignment.  I think there may have even been a fireplace!  Great staff who were attentive and friendly.  Since I went on a Sunday afternoon, there wasn't a large crowd, so I got the inside scoop on the naming process for the brews (mostly movie related) and the intel on upcoming brews and events.  If you come in the front entrance, the door is at street level.  If you come in from the parking lot, be aware there are a few steps and if your eyes don't adjust quickly, you may be surprised.  It appears they do have some food available, but I didn't see (nor ask for) a menu.  Someone had a pizza brought out from the back room and seemed to be doing a pretty good job of finishing it.  Although I wasn't going to eat, it would have been nice to have been offered a menu or at least informed of the options.  I had other plans for dinner, but I didn't see anything food related mentioned on the official website.  Other than the house beers, the specialty brews come and go depending upon the popularity/demand.  During my visit, there was only one IPA and two light options.  All the rest were darker, heavier tasting varieties.  Since I ordered a flight (5 brews samples for $8.50), I was getting a majority of darker ales.  Overall, the flavors were solid and pretty accurately described on the listing.  My favorite was the Jenny Wit (6.2% 15 IBU) which had a really nice flavor without too strong of an aftertaste.  My least favorite was the Dead Rabbits Irish Extra Stout (Dry - 6.6% 35 IBU).  I wasn't able to discern any clear flavor standing out to best describe it.    Review #286

I don't get to this side of town often, so I hadn't been to Marco's in about 15 years.  But the feeling of being welcome and comfortable came rushing in as I stepped in the rear/side entrance for the dining area.  (Note that the front entrance by the patio is the Lounge/bar area.)  The atmosphere is cozy and somewhat darkly lit.  The dining area was sparsely populated by customers so I headed into the lounge area and grabbed a small table.  Lots of silent televisions had news and sports programming on while a radio played funky 70's pop music in the background.  Since it was lunch time, my waitress brought a regular menu as well as a printout of the numerous daily specials/options.  Although she was covering a lot of tables, she did a fine job of keeping my water topped, getting my food out quickly, and processing my check at the end.  I decided to go with a plate of Marco Wings which had ten pieces (half wings) of crispy chicken that had a spicy hot coating.  The wings came with both Ranch dressing and a hot sauce for those who want to suffer.  I thought the wings were plenty hot on their own, so I mainly used the Ranch.  The wings were also piping hot out of the fryer, so I needed to let them cool just a moment and kept my beverage ready.    I had asked for my side salad to be delivered right away and selected a Raspberry Vinaigrette which was fantastic!  The salad used mostly iceberg lettuce as the green, but there were several other greens as well as cucumber, cherry tomato, and super crunchy croutons.  Very nice!  Oh, there was also a complementary serving of two rolls with butter.  The butter patties were a little too chilly for easy spreading, but the bread was warm inside and seemed to soften the butter if I spread it thinly.  Good flavor there too!  Parking is convenient along the side of the building.  Access from 54th street (both in and out) was easy because the stop light at Keystone seemed to allow time for easing across the road if needed.    Overall, good service and tasty food in an old fashioned dining area made for an enjoyable lunch time experience.  Review #485

I've seen this little shop a number of times, so I decided to stop by.  (Note that you have to enter off Stop 11 Road.  The nearby parking lot of Michael's & Hobby Lobby does not connect.)   On the positive side, I got my Chicken tamale with red sauce immediately and for a very reasonable (low) price.  The staff was friendly, and there were plenty of spaces out front to park.  However, the food was simply forgettable.  I was going to order a side of guacamole, but it doesn't come with chips.  (Those have a separate charge.)  So, I just went with the tamale. I have only had a tamale maybe once before, so I wasn't sure what to expect.    I got the wrapped tamale on a plate and when I unwrapped the corn husk, it let off a little steam, so I knew it should be moist and ready to eat.  In fact,it was, but what I saw was a small, colorless "roll" that had so little sauce that I wasn't sure if they forgot to give me a side of sauce or if that is just the way it is supposed to look.  I didn't see any additional sauces at the counter for napkins/plastic ware, and there wasn't anything else on the table.  So, I ate it.  And it tasted liked it looked.  Barely any taste.  I can't imagine people going out of their way to buy tamales if this is the standard.  The chicken was overcooked.  The doughy part of the tamale was bland, and the sauce was unrecognizable (I never did find out what it was supposed to taste like.)  So, I would give this a 2.5 stars, but since I only had the one item and have read reviews that suggested I might have better results with a dessert tamale, I will round up to three stars.  They do have tacos and other Mexican foods available, but a place named for tamales should present tamales that are memorable.  Review #466

My wife and I stopped in for lunch on a Wednesday morning.  We were able to find a spot at the back of the restaurant for parking and made our way inside.  There was a slight wait as there were a couple large groups having reserved some seating, but soon, we were able to share a booth over on the bar side.    In the bar area, it seemed quieter than my other visits. Previously, we had only been here during dinner hours in the large dining area.  Live music starts around 6 each night from within the bar oval where a piano and microphones are set up.  But during lunch, there was no music (live or background).  We shared an appetizer of Lump Crab, Roasted Shrimp & Spinach Stuffed Mushrooms.  This has been updated from the last time we had ordered it.  We still got the same number of stuffed mushrooms, but this time, there was no cheese spread over the top.  However, there was more seasoning on the shrimp to spice up the flavor.  For lunch, I ordered the Blackened Mahi Mahi Tacos - pico de gallo, salsa verde, & cilantro sour cream; and the Sweet Corn Black Bean Salad.  There were three soft shell tacos with two types of sauce.  There was a nice grilled flavor to the tacos that added depth to the flavor.  The salad was sweet and savory.  My wife ordered the Lobster "BLT" Lettuce Wraps - lobster salad, Beefsteak tomato, Applewood bacon in bibb lettuce; and the housemade pickles.  She got two wraps that she thought were very good.  The pickles are the kind that are brined in sugar, onion, and vinegar.    Finally, we ordered one of the mini indulgence desserts:  I had the Mocha Macchiato - mini mocha mousse, vanilla mouse, chocolate cake, caramel sauce, whipped cream.  Excellent! My wife got the new Traverse City Cherry Creme Brulee - mini classic vanilla bean infused custard, intense compote of Traverse City cherries.  Even though my wife isn't a big fan of cherries, she loves creme brulee and this did not disappoint.  Oh, one last note.  We mentioned that we had an appointment that we needed to keep, so that we only had about an hour to dine before we had to leave.  We were not rushed and were still finished in about 45 minutes.  Excellent attention to timing on our server's part.  Sure, all those options were pricey for a lunch menu, but the quality was as good as any dinner menu.  Review #75

What I liked about this place was that they had a wide variety of Asian foods (Vietnamese, Thai, & Chinese) available with quick service in a clean, if somewhat sterile, environment.  The restaurant is in a mini strip mall with a large step to get in from the parking lot.  When you walk in, you will probably see a line backed up near the door, but rest assured, it will move fast.  On the right is a photo wall with pictures of the items available with plenty of labeling to help you decide.  They also have menus on the counter and on the wall behind the counter, so you have plenty of opportunity to make your selection.  Once you get to the counter, they give you a number and bring your order out to you. (They bring your drinks and silverware too.)    What I loved about this place was the appetizers.  I ordered the crab meat rangoon and it was the best I've had!  The rangoon were hot and mostly crisp while the center was piping hot, so be sure to let them cool just a bit before biting in like I did. They have a sweet sauce on each table (the red bottle) that pairs well.  Excellent choice.  My wife also really enjoyed the egg drop soup.  The serving was small (about a half cup) but full of flavor and topped with crunchy strips.      What I was a bit disappointed with was the actual entrees.  My wife's sweet and sour pork was served in a breading and appeared to be deep fried.  Unfortunately, the pork was very tough and chewy.  I ordered the Pad See Yew (Beef) and although the flavor was good and the beef more tender, the noodles appeared to be simple egg noodle...the half inch wide long noodles I can get at the grocery.  The menu indicates that the dish comes with wide noodles, but these were clearly not.  I much prefer the wide noodles that I have tried elsewhere.      I will also admit that I tried the clear wrapped spring rolls which come with a little bit of shrimp and pork visible through the wrap, but not found on the inner portion of the roll which was stuffed with white noodles, a few sprouts, and greens.  The rolls are served with a peanut sauce that has a little heat added on top.  This was my first experience with the cold wrap (I am guessing it is rice paper).  The texture was chewy (reminded me of eating a small gummy bear with a salad).  So, maybe that's the way it is supposed to be, but for me, I would prefer the deep fried/crispy spring rolls.  They looked good and the portion for the three was generous.  Just not my favorite.  So, if you are in the area and want to try a variety of different Asian cuisines, you can stop here and get quick service at a reasonable price.    Review #356

My wife and I stopped by on a warm, sunny day in late September and grabbed a seat out on the rear patio.  They have lots of tables with umbrellas there.  We were greeted after grabbing a table and were brought our beverages in a timely manner.  We had read about the great wings they serve so we each ordered a batch of six.  Since there was a special on wings, they didn't come with the celery and carrots that they do on most other days.  Instead we placed an order for a side of onion rings.  The wings take about 20 minutes and are lightly breaded to a crispy finish.  You can get them plain, or mild (hot sauce mixed with butter), BBQ, Buffalo, or hot sauce.  You can also order the wings with sauce on them or on the side.  We both opted for our sauces on the side and that made it a lot less messy.  Very good chicken and good size for the wings.  The onion rings were really good too.  They were also lightly breaded and crisp with a nice sweetness to the onions.  The breading also stayed on the onion rings, not exploded like some other sports bars I've been to.  Since it was a football Sunday, there was a full crowd around the bar and a fair number under the covered patio watching the television.  Because we were the only ones on the sunny patio, we decided to head into the bar to pay when we were finished since it looked like the staff was really swamped for the number of staff working.  Still, the wait wasn't too long.  I will advise anyone who has mobility issues that I didn't see any ramp or easy access up to the elevated entrance.    Out back, there are several activity areas like horse shoes.  There is also a large space that looks like it may be a driving range for golf, but during our visit, it had been converted to an obstacle course for drone racing.  Several were trying it out for a possible competition.  Quite amazing to watch!  Overall, a pleasant staff and good food, though a limited menu.    Review #1372

Okay, there have been a lot of diverse reviews of this place, mostly by a number of folks who have reviewed very few restaurants.  So, I decided to go myself and see what I could find out.  First, they have a great vibe being located "just off" Mass Avenue north of North Street, around the corner from the sister company Outlier's Brewing.  There is limited street parking near there and a pay lot for $10 a block south.  I was fortunate and found some pay parking on Mass Avenue about a block north of the intersection.  So, a short walk saved me quite a bit of change.  The staff greeted me as I walked up and were cool with letting me walk around the place to see the artwork by FAB Crew and Sophie Gamand before dining.  They answered questions and had my place ready to go when I was done.    I asked about trying a flight of beer since they carry Outlier's, but that wasn't a set option.  However, the waiter offered to let me try samples of any that I was interested in.  I tried several and then asked what my waiter would recommend of my options to go with the food I was planning on ordering.  Done and done!  I went with a German Pilsner called Blau Machen (4.5%, very little bitterness).  I started with an item that was new to me:  Conservas.  Conservas is a European style of food preparation where a seafood is harvested fresh and canned with a variety of herbs and spices allowing the seafood to marinate.  I went with the "Pickled laughing bird shrimp".  The process basically cooks the shrimp through the pickling process and as expected, makes the texture just a little more chewy than raw shrimp.  What was unexpected was the fantastic flavor!  The conservas is served still in the can and after clearing away a bay leaf, I used a cocktail fork to spear the warm shrimp.  The aroma from within the can reminded me of a seafood soup, only you don't drink the liquids in this case.  As part of the meal course, I got my pick of "preparations" = side dishes to pair with the conservas.  I went with the "Romantica" which consisted of thin sliced Spanish Chorizo, aioli, and crouton (four slices of crisp bread cut on the diagonal.)  I alternated between bites of the shrimp and the mini sandwiches I made with the Romantica.  Absolutely delicious!  I could have ordered another with no problem, but I decided to move on to my large plate option:  Pork Schnitzel. (see why I got the German pilsner?)  The Schnitzel is a pounded pork cut that becomes tenderized as it becomes thinner.  (It looks similar to a pork tenderloin.)  Here, the pork is breaded in a pretzel crust and served with grilled asparagus, sugar snap peas, diced potatoes, a sliced boiled egg, and a couple dollops of lemon mayo.  Wow! This was great!  Because the schnitzel looked thicker, the chef sent out a steak knife in case my bread knife wasn't sharp enough.  I never used it.  I was literally using my fork to cut the meat.  I couldn't get over how tender it was and I loved the pretzel coating....very German tasting to my palate.  The asparagus were mild and had just enough grilling to bring out their flavor.  The sugar snap peas (called just peas on the menu) come in the pod and were very sweet.  That was unexpected but a great pairing with the rest of the meal.  The potatoes were cut into small pieces about diced size, but had an unusual shape to them.  They were completely done and took on that great flavor that potatoes get when they have been cooked to completion, not like some half baked giant potato.  The lemon mayo made for good dipping and if anything, I could have used a little more on the side for dipping the veggies.  So, for the things I tried and the service I received, I say 5 stars.  I am already looking for friends who want to tag along with me the next time so I can try something new.  Review #271  Follow up:  My return visit with guests allowed me to sample quite a few items: The Black Mole Skirt Steak - not one you can order to temp.  Served with a full char on the outside which has a great flavor.
