Pairs well with the veggie relish, tomatoes, and cotija cheese  Chicken Thighs - my friend ordered this and though it looks like a salad, the chicken in a wild rice pan sauce is delicious, creamy, and moist.  The stone fruit panzanella covers the chicken when served.  (You never see the brick since it doesn't leave the kitchen)  Conservas:  Octopus in chili tomato paired with Vera Cruz (green olives, capers, oregano, and fried potatoes).  The chili tomato sauce is thicker than in the shrimp conservas.  The octopus is served warm to room temperature and has a nice chew without being rubbery.  Pickled eggs and beets - this is a shareable bar food option with probably three full eggs served sliced over thick, large beets.  These had less pickled sweetness than commercial pickled beets I have tried  Pork belly rillettes - initially, this was disappointing because the pork belly (pate) was fairly bland.  Paired with pickled peppers and mustard = excellent!

I stopped in for a late lunch on Saturday after getting a tip that this new restaurant was really fantastic.  Being open only about six weeks, I wasn't surprised that the spacious dining area was still barely decorated.  And that is the only negative I have!  The food is delicious and the service is efficient and friendly.  This greatly exceeded my expectations for quality.  Don Cuervo's Mexican Cuisine restaurant is a family owned business (their first attempt at running a restaurant.)  Upon entering, I was greeted and given a booth with a view of the soccer game on one of the televisions.    Since they haven't gotten their website up and running yet, it was my first time seeing the menu (I've posted pics of the menu at this time).  So, I placed an order for my beverage and asked them for a few minutes to decide.  In the meantime, I was brought a large basket of complimentary chips and salsa.  Even though it was a very humid day, the chips were crisp and large enough to hold plenty of salsa.  The salsa was a nice blend of smooth tomato based salsa with nice sized pieces of onion and peppers.  Very nice flavor.  The basket was easily shareable.    Soon, I placed my order for the Carne (steak) Asada Burrito.  Within a few minutes, my plate arrived.  The burrito wrapped around the steak, with sauteed onions & shredded cheese.  The wrap was covered with both green and cheese sauces.  The burrito was about 11 inches in length.  The steak and onions were cooked with enough seasoning to highlight the flavors.  The wrap itself was fresh and held together well when I sliced the burrito and lifted the sections with my fork.  The entree came with fresh Mexican rice (moist, not dry like a lot of places), and warm corn and cool black beans served atop shredded lettuce.  I have had the beans heated other places, so I was a little surprised.  When I asked about it, the waiter said that it was intended as a salad item, not a side dish.  The flavor of everything was spot on!  Fortunately, my stomach was able to hold this huge serving plate of food!  And I wasn't finished yet!  I had to try the Fried Ice Cream for dessert.  This was also large enough for normal folks to share, but I had no trouble putting it away too! ha!  The dessert is served in a cinnamon sugar tortilla shell.  The vanilla ice cream is deep fried which creates an outer crust that takes on a coconut texture (but retains a sweet flavor) that added a nice chew to the dessert to go with the creaminess of the ice cream and crispness of the shell.  The ice cream is topped with whipped cream, chocolate syrup, and cherries.  I definitely recommend this as well!  Great food, genuinely friendly service, and a reasonable price are why I highly recommend this restaurant.  I wish this family business great success and plan on bringing guests here to enjoy the experience.  Review #108

I stopped by for lunch on a Friday (4-15-16).  The restaurant was crowded (even though there is a large parking lot, I had to walk quite a distance).  However, since I was dining alone, I was seated in the central dining area quickly.  I took a few moments to look over the menu and then put in my order.  Service was surprisingly quick for being so busy!  I chose the Shrimp Tempura Roll (with avocado) and Sesame Seared Scallops with white rice, spicy cabbage and plum white wine sauce.  The sushi was good, but didn't deliver any wow moments....pretty standard fare.  However, the scallops were delicious.  The sesame seeds covered the scallops pretty thoroughly and may have masked the flavor a bit, but because the flavor was so good, I wasn't disappointed.  I was pleasantly surprised at the spicy cabbage.  Very colorful as well as tasty.  I didn't use very much of the sauce.  It was okay, but I think I preferred the flavors with very little of the sauce.  The white rice was fine as a filler and kept the spice flavors from becoming too intense.  I would definitely recommend this restaurant to any seafood fan that is in the area.  Review #28

On opening day, I expected there might have been a problem, but the only surprise I got was how well the staff handled the customers!  I arrived for lunch without a reservation and since I was dining solo, I accepted a seat at the bar.  There, I was greeted and was shown a menu with food on one side, beverages on the back.  They have a Zero Proof option for someone wanting more than water, but non-alcoholic, so I decided to try a Kitchen Rickey which is a ginger ale based beverage with a lime, and orange bitters.  What a great punch of flavor that had! And the ginger added something close to a heat element that tingled at the back of my throat.  Great palate cleanser too!  I opted for a sandwich and side for my meal.  The Roasted Mushroom sandwich came with gruyere, garlic aioli, and braised greens and was served on square bread sliced diagonally.  Really great mushroom taste and the aioli was a great complement, not too garlic strong, but enough to balance the flavors.  The plate also came with dressed simple greens and fries (I went with garlic type offered by the waiter/bartender).  I also had an order of Carmelized Brussels Sprouts and Turnips on the side.  The sprouts were quartered and still large.  The turnips were pickled before hand and then roasted to bring out a sweet taste.  They were served as chunks.  The dish was topped with a ham hock vinaigrette with pieces of ham that were served close to a jerky texture, but easier to chew.  Great flavor all around!  The two bartenders were conversational and there were two other staff members (?) who asked how I was doing and what I had ordered.  Even on the way out, the folks at the front desk thanked me for coming in.  I hope it lasts, because I like feeling my patronage is appreciated.  Overall, I can't wait to return with a group for dinner to take advantage of the free evening/weekend parking behind the building.  Great start for a new restaurant.  Note:  The menu is on the pricey end for Mass Ave, but the food quality was great.  I didn't mind the prices.  Note 2:  For the grand opening, I was also given some promotional swag to help kickoff their Sunday Brunches that begin on Mother's Day.  Review #773

On Tuesday, I stopped in for lunch at this 54th Street shop.  Although I did not try their pasta, I was impressed with the variety they offered.  As you walk in, there are three counters in front of you:  pasta, cheese, and olives.  There is also a table for more food items for sale like peanut butters and nuts.  On your left wall as you enter, there are some blackboards with the days soups, salads, and sandwich offerings.  I was greeted promptly and I mentioned it was my first time in, the woman behind the counter immediately explained all the lunch combos for me and pointed out her favorites.  She was so enthusiastic, that I decided to take her up on her suggestions.  (Note:  I had looked at the menu a few weeks ago and wrote down some items to try, but the menu had already changed since then.)  After paying for my order, I got to pick a seat in the dining room that is down the hall on the right.  There were a pair of 4 seat tables and a couple communal tables as well.  I selected one of the smaller ones and one of the staff brought out my flatware (wrapped in a napkin and tied with a piece of twine) and a carafe of chilled water.  In a very short time, my lunch combo arrived:  I ordered the Roasted Garlic Tomato Soup (served with large pieces of tomato and piping hot!).  My other half of my lunch was a rather generously sized Giardiniera sandwich pressed like a panini making the bread nice and toasty!  The sandwich had salami, capocollo, provolone, and giardiniera for that extra bit of salt and acid to balance the savory meat/fat/seasonings.  Although the soup could have used a hint more flavor on the garlic side, it was still tasty and would be appreciated even more on a cooler day.  The sandwich nailed it!  And filling enough that I didn't regret passing on the full size. (The half was 5-6 inches long and about 4 wide.)  All in all, I would definitely come back to try some of their salads and pasta dishes.  And maybe bring a cooler to keep some fresh pasta until I can make it home.  Review #146

Just north of the Mile Square between the Central Indianapolis Library and the Veteran's Memorial Plaza is a two block park that is nestled between the American Legion National Headquarters (on the east) and the Indiana American Legion Headquarters (on the west).    Since the Indiana World War Memorial is located two blocks to the south to honor veterans of World War I, additional memorials were set up on this mall to honor World War II, Korean War, and Vietnam War veterans.  These monuments were created between 1996 and 1998 by sculptor Patrick Brunner.  In the center of the north end of the mall is a cenotaph (empty tomb dedicated to veterans) with four columns topped with golden eagles built in 1931.  The middle of the south block is a sunken garden/lawn that raises to street level and is edged by the street level war monuments.  The park is a great location for hosting events downtown or for strolling along when the weather cooperates.  Review #1862

Generally, I am not a mall shopper.  I don't go for big crowds and hate waiting in line.  But now that I am retired and since it is the Christmas season as I write, I was pleasantly surprised at the condition of this place and that I didn't have to deal with the flocks of young people who can sometimes take over a mall.  The mall was clean and in good condition.  The holiday decorations,  including a place for Santa, seemed appropriate, but not over the top.  I saw a number of newer food options, and a number of new stores that I hadn't seen on my last visit.  New is good and can help keep the interest of shoppers.  Review #1900

I enjoyed my first visit to this version of O'Reilly's.  There was plenty of parking outside, plenty of room to grab a seat (they have three sections, two of which are family friendly, the other being the bar), and quite a few options for food and beverages.  I was there for lunch and grabbed a spot at the bar.  Note that there is leg room under the bar that makes it comfortable to sit and dine there!  I went with their specialty Chicken Salad Sandwich with seasoned fries.  The sandwich was really large and used big chunks of chicken instead of shredding it.  I got mine with lettuce and tomato to make it a moist and tasty option.  They even toasted the bread on one side.  The fries were seasoned, but not too strongly.  They offer ketchup and salt, but I passed on both since I thought there was enough flavor without them.  The only negative was that for such a small amount of diners in the early afternoon, I was surprised at the delays coming out of the kitchen.  The bartender apologized for the delay, stating it usually didn't take so long.  At least she was aware of it and did her best to keep an eye on the kitchen to bring the food out as soon as it was ready.  Great job Erica!  Oh, I also mentioned it was my first visit and was given a piece of bread pudding as a first time guest.  I'm not sure if they do that for all first timers or if that was a way of making up for the delay, but I took it!  The flavor was really good (though it was served in a milky bowl that seemed a little bit sloppy.)  Good flavor, nice attitude, and a little bit slow in the kitchen evens out to a 4-star rating.  I'd be glad to go back and try something else on the menu as long as I wasn't in a rush.  Review #1910

While attending an event on the north side/Carmel, I noticed a lone food truck had set up on the south end of the market place.  It was my first time trying El Venezolano and I was pleased.  I don't eat at food trucks often since they tend to have a limited menu compared to brick and mortar restaurants, but the description of the Arepas that were being offered convinced me to give one a try.  I went with the Pollo (Seasoned Shredded Chicken) Arepa which comes with a condiment size cup of sauce.  The arepa is a gluton-free corn cake (about as thick as a pancake) that is folded like a taco and STUFFED with the meat of choice.  The sauce, a creamy mint colored option added some moisture, though I wasn't aware of the change in flavor compared to the rest of the entree.  Plenty to eat; plenty of large pieces of white chicken breast, a mild seasoning and the sauce was enough to be filling.  It might have been nice to have some sides offered, but I didn't see any.  I think if I see them again, I will try one of the beef options that I see are recommended on other reviews.  Review #2656

Having enjoyed my visit to the Greenwood location, I decided to try the one in Avon.  The place is huge and has a fair amount of parking, but they do run out of spaces at peak times.  Fortunately, there are nearby lots across the roads in the shopping center.  Dining by myself, I asked to sit at the bar so that I could sample a flight of their house drafts (four 5 oz choices) with my meal.  At the time of my visit, they had eleven ales and a cider made in house as well as numerous "guest" beverages, including wine and mixed drinks.  I went with the Oasis (amber 4.7%, 19 IBU) that was quite tasty (nice wheat flavor).  I also had the PM (porter 5.5% 25) which is supposed to taste of chocolate, but tasted more like coffee.  I had the Tatonka (stout 8.5% 50) which is supposed to have a dark malt flavor.  Both the PM and Tatonka were prepared with Nitro (not CO2) so they were very smooth, but I still prefer the CO2 style of beverages at this point.  I finished with the Hopstorm (IPA 6.5% 65) which was a nicely balanced ale.    What surprised me was how much I enjoyed the meal.  I've had a lot of ham and cheese sandwiches, including those grilled like they are here.  What makes this sandwich so tasty is that they grill parmesan on the outside of the sourdough bread and use Havarti on the inside with the smoked ham.  Note that the ham is moist, not dried out from the smoking.  There is also a creamy alfredo.  I was supposed to get a dijon mustard on the side, but didn't realize it until I had already finished the sandwich.  This isn't a sandwich for those on diets.  It is listed at 1030 calories which probably doesn't include the delicious fries that come with the meal.    The flavor was simply delicious.  One of the tastiest sandwiches I've had in a long time.  Note:  Although I was seated promptly at the bar, the bartender had to supply all the drinks for the restaurant and so there was a delay in getting a menu and my order placed.  So, you may want to get a table in the dining area instead.  Review #2118

I figured with over 100 check-ins at this place, I ought to say why I come here.  I don't buy a lot of items other than the groceries, but it is nice to know that they have a lot of stuff to choose from when I go.  What I want to focus on is that the store has added some new improvements that really make for a better shopping experience.  First, they bought all new shopping carts this summer.  I find it so much more pleasurable to shop if I don't have to deal with a squeaky wheel or a wheel that won't turn.  I get that taking carts out across the blacktop parking lot can put a lot of wear on the wheels, so for while it lasts, I am enjoying having the new carts.  They also modified the style for the smaller cart which seems to hold more than the previous version.  Second, they have opened an express lane area for shoppers who don't want to buy their groceries that day.  The west end is close to the doors on that end of the building and near the seasonal, toy, and clothing area.  No longer do you have to compete with all the shoppers from the grocery area.  I generally am able to get reasonably priced food items, some hard to find elsewhere, at this location.  My only real negative is that the store doesn't get to select its own items and therefore, complaints that they are out of stock are heard, but "can't be helped".  I buy a particular brand of cereal because it has lots of vitamins and it has been out of stock numerous times.  I have checked with the help desk several times and if it is in stock but not out, they help.  If it is on order, they let me know when it will come in.  But if it isn't on order, they can't begin to tell me when I might be able to find it since the store doesn't have a choice.  That means I have to shop elsewhere to find what I like.  (I have bought other cereal, but it's not what I want.  Lost business and a complaint on Yelp are the cost.)  Review #1767

This park has a very accessible location, lots of parking, and some amenities that aren't as common at the area parks:  a full aquatic center and an ice rink.  There are ball fields, tennis courts, basketball, shelter, playground and plenty of room to hike around.  However, from recent news that persistent ice troubles forced the rink to close during the youth hockey league, the park must do lots of work to have the rink repaired by fall of 2018.  As the last park ice rink in the city, this was very disruptive.  So, I applaud that the park is trying to fix the problem...I just hope it has better luck than with Ellenberger Park.  Review #687

I really enjoyed dining at this new Mexican restaurant.  It is easy to find since it sits directly on Washington Street and has free parking available on the east and south sides of the building.  I took advantage of the $2 taco Tuesday lunch special to make my first visit.  The space itself was clean and is lightly decorated with Mexican imagery.  The main entrance area has a little lounge area by the window which can be used for dining or for guest performers.  At the back is the bar area where they serve beer and wines.  (They do have some mixed drinks available if you ask your server for the options.)  There is dining in the middle and over in the east wing of the building which is where the kitchen is located.  I was presented a basket of chicharrones while I waited for my order.  These were light and crisp and had a little bit of spicy heat for flavor.  Soon, my order of Guacamole and chips arrived.  The guacamole was about a cup size serving and had a nice balance of flavors, probably a little lighter on the lime juice than most places I have had it.  The onion and tomato flavors were more noticeable because of that.  The chips were crisp and were able to hold up to the task of scooping the dip.  As I neared finishing the dip, my two tacos arrived.  Both types were served in double layered corn tortillas (about 5" circles) folded and served on a rack, topped with onions and cilantro.  The pastor (pork) was chopped into small bits and marinated, and served with chiles, spices, and pineapple in addition to the topping.   I also added a medium salsa and lime juice.  The sweetness of the pineapple worked very well with the savory pork and spices.  This could be my favorite pork taco ever!  I am not normally a fan of corn tortillas (the taste is kind of musky to my palate), but these were okay to me.  The carne asada taco was okay, but the steak was cut too small and browned without getting charred and became just a bit chewy.  Not bad enough to ruin my taco, but not good enough to have that "wow" factor like the pork did.  Service was very pleasant and welcoming.  Water came chilled and they use real silverware.  Checkout was also prompt.  Overall, it was a very enjoyable way to spend my lunch.  Review #476

I had been waiting for the grand opening of Macaron Bar, so when I started seeing reviews pop up, I made a trip downtown to check them out.  I grabbed some street parking (metered) along Vermont and walked over to Mass Ave.  I figure if a business makes good enough macarons (and nothing else!) to stay in business, they must be good.  If the business is good enough to franchise (out of Cincy), they must be really good!  And they are!  The shop has a few seats in the window that are great for people watching.  Then there are the display counters with a colorful array of macarons, all kinds of flavors.  Beyond that, there are spotlessly clean tables and ovens for the baking classes they offer.  And the macarons are delicious!  I was first introduced to macarons (do not confuse these with macaroons which have chewy coconut) at Gallery Pastry in Broad Ripple and I thought these just as good.  The macarons here are tasty and with the egg white based cookies, melt in your mouth down to the tasty filling.  They have a variety of regular flavors and add in some seasonal options as well.  I picked up a box of six that I made the selection.  (They sell them individually as well.)  There are flavors like Black Raspberry Chocolate, Pistacho, Caramel Apple, and Spiced Pumpkin.  With flavors like that, who wouldn't want to stop by!  Review #1473

Tip:  If you want to check out Krueger's but don't want the large crowds or the loud noise, do like I did and stop by during the week before 6.  We had an unseasonably warm March evening and the garage doors were open to the front patio of the restaurant.  Nice breeze, but sound was not trapped inside.  And the patio looked great with the pergolas, but I wanted to see the inside while dining.  I was greeted and seated at a small high table near the bar.  Note that these bar stools have a round metal base that I thought made them attached to the ground, but you can move them with a little "umph".  The good news is these were stable and didn't rock like some high stools.  My server was friendly and pointed out items on both sides of the menu.  One side was mostly beverages and the other was food.  I started with a Hoosier celebrity named drink, the "John Daly".  Think Arnold Palmer with a bit of Vodka.  It was served with the lemonade on the bottom and tea on top.  The vodka was present, but didn't overwhelm the flavors.  I decided to go with the place's namesake burger and when prompted, decided to go with the grilled asparagus as a side.  The burger is a double patty with generally about the same amount of total meat you get at the other prestige burger places around town.  They simply cook faster being thinner and so mine were done to where there was no pink.  I would have liked a bit more sear on the surface to bring out the beef flavor, but it was still good.  It also had shredded lettuce (tough to keep on the burger), cheese, and some condiments which helped with the overall flavor.  Good, but not exceptional.  What I did find fantastic was the grilled asparagus.  I discovered that grilled asparagus has a much different taste than steamed, so when I see the grilled offered, I usually jump on board.  No disappointments here!  The grilled flavor was delicious and the grated parmigiano reggiano with lemon juice knocked the dish out of the park.  I made a point of telling the staff how great it was.  I know parking is a concern for a lot of folks when it comes to Mass Ave, but at that time of day, I found pay parking spots all over Vermont Street and there were additional spaces on southbound Pennsylvania another block over.  If you like checking out new places, especially with an industrial vibe, give them a try.  If not, then wait until it's warmer and check out the patio on Delaware.  Review #2342

If you are an adult, this neighborhood park may be more appealing than the Shawn Grove Park.  This park has no playground, just a central fountain and mature trees.  There are several areas that separated by shrubs and distance so that even if someone else is there while you are, you can still relax on one of the benches or in the gazebo.  There is a special section designated for sensory appreciation for visually impaired visitors.  Unfortunately, the sign is written in English only and could have added braille.  I guess they figured someone without eyesight would need to bring them here at least the first time.   The park does have a water fountain but no restroom facilities and no designated parking.  Street parking is free but dependent upon the time of day and occasion for how accessible it can be.  Review #514

Although this '50's style restaurant has been around since that time period (1957), there was no sense of "experience" that I have felt at other themed restaurants.  The place was clean and bright like a fast food chain with some 50's style decor and a juke box (which appeared to be free to anyone who wanted to make a selection by pushing the buttons.) The menu is pretty simple American Traditional, i.e. something you can make at home but prefer they have to clean the kitchen instead of you.  Since it was February, I wanted to dine in and approached an order counter.  It served as a spot for both dine in and to go orders (just like a fast food place.)  Your order ticket has a number and they call it out over a speaker when it is ready for you to pick up.  You pick your own seating location and can grab your beverages and plasticware/napkins on your own.  One thing that I missed was that if you want TLC (Tomato, lettuce, and/or Cheese), they charge $0.29 for each.  Not enough cost to stop me from ordering, but I didn't realize it before paying.  Good customer service would point that out whenever someone is asked what they want on their sandwich.  Why get someone upset over so little of a charge?  I went with the breaded tenderloin and fries.  The food was ready quite quickly (almost fast!) and the ketchup for the fries was in small packets which I find annoying.  More mess than necessary.  The fries were well done to a crispy bite, but were unsalted/unseasoned in any fashion.  Not greasy at all, so the salt didn't stick to them except for when I had ketchup on them.    The tenderloin was not thickly breaded like I've read in other reviews.  I found the ratio quite favorable, though I will agree that the meat was extremely thin compared to a number of places I've had them.  The meat is thoroughly cooked, but wasn't too dry either.  Not much seasoning, but it was fine.  Also, mine was larger than the bun, but there wasn't anything huge about it by Hoosier standards.  And the bun was a plain white bun which suits the era, but does nothing for the flavor.  If you want to support local, grab a quick meal without buying big chain, then this is a nice place to dine (there aren't a lot of options in the area).  However, if you want to feel more like you're at a real greasy spoon or diner, I would encourage you to check out Rock-Cola 50's Cafe (south of Irvington) or the Oasis Diner in Plainfield.  Review #2262

I was in the mood to grab a bite to eat before catching a movie at noon at one of the local theaters, so I decided I wanted something quick.  I hadn't been to Primanti Bros before, but my wife had and liked what she ordered.  I pulled into their private lot and asked the hostess about getting a "to go" order.  She directed me to the bar and said that the staff there would help me.  I was greeted and saw menus by the counter.  I helped myself to one and ordered a Corned Beef and Cheese with Classic tater tots.  I also asked about how long the order would take and was told about 10 minutes.  Sure enough, my order was ready then and I was on my way.  What I will tell you is that even though the sandwiches are pricey and don't include sides other than chips, the total size of the sandwich is huge.  Thick bread, lots of meat, and a tart cabbage/slaw instead of sauerkraut made for a nice meal.  Of course, the meal was enough for two meals, so I saved the second half for later.  The only negative, which was minor, was that I got French Fries (a generous portion) instead of tots in my order.  I am not sure if fries are what they mean by "classic cut", but it wasn't what I was expecting.  I will say that the staff also packed a comprehensive "to go" bag full of condiments for me which also was generous enough to keep.  I can't tell you how many times I've had to go orders that skimped or completely forgot to include condiments.  Overall, a quick and tasty meal with enough leftovers for another one.    Review #3134

I have enjoyed the idea of having Ann Dancing ever since her "sister" Sarah was part of an early downtown public art initiative (The Arts Council commissioned her as part of a series by Julian Opie called "Signs" back in 2005.)  When Sarah was first installed at Washington and Meridian, it was a shock to folks downtown.  You see, folks used to miss all the cool things there: the building details, the statues, the art that folks just took for granted.  And in today's world where so many have their faces glued to their devices, the art is under appreciated/noticed worse than before.  But these moving images forced reactions from a group of people who probably didn't go to art museums or galleries.  She was on the corner and silently got their attention.    In 2008, Sarah was long gone and Ann began dancing at her current spot.  Are there sometimes lights that go out? Sure, but they eventually get repaired.  Has technology advanced over the years so that the light movement could be more sensational? Sure, but is that what the artist had in mind?  And for those who think she is somehow too seductive for kids, well the porn is in your mind, not on a bunch of moving lights.    What I like about the installation is my own interpretation that life is too short to rush from one meeting to another; too precious to waste staring at a phone.  If you hear some music and feel like moving, then do it if you want to.  If not, then don't.  The installation doesn't preach or judge (unlike some self-appointed "gods" of good taste or art critics), it simply exists.  If it brings a smile to someone, then it is a good thing to have.  For those who are disgusted by the light show, you are taking this much too seriously.  Maybe you should listen to Ann.  Review #1182

Now that I am exploring more coffee shops (I usually make mine at home), I thought I'd head to the near east side and try Rabble Coffee.  Located about half way between the CCIC and Rural Ave, the shop has parking in the rear which you can access from the alley on the west side of the shop.    Inside the shop, the order counter is about half way back on the right.  The front seating area is filled with black and white images over newsprint for a retro vibe..very eclectic.  2-tops and larger tables are available.  The order counter has a variety of foodstuffs, mainly pastries and some chips, but I believe sandwiches are available.  As per usual, I ordered a black drip coffee and was pleased to see they had Tinker Coffee available.  I picked an Ethiopian blend that was immediately drinkable (no scald!)    Sadly, the owner decided to remove the cool mural that she had commissioned just a short time before.  I fail to see how the removal of the art makes the world a better place or helps anyone.  To me, it just feels like censorship.  As she is entitled to her opinion without consultation, so am I.  Maybe this is why we don't see local artists taking risks.  Review #2855

Although a bit hard to find (It doesn't face the street, but is set back and faces west), this small new business is worth the hunt!  Just a short distance west of where the Monon Trail crosses Main, take the sidewalk on the side of the building that has KURR and Main Street Treats to find the entrance.  Inside this elegantly decorated shop are glass display cases of shop made chocolates that come in a variety of shapes and flavors.  The rest of the shop has packaged options and even a mural painted by one of the co-owners.   The idea of the shop grew out of a passion for art that led to an interest in creating chocolate designs.  After living in Austria where there was an apprentice like arrangement, the couple came to the US to sell chocolates while perfecting their own.  After years of selling at local farmer's markets, the time was right to open their own shop.  I chose a variety when I visited.  Some were dark chocolate shapes made from molds that look like little robots or building blocks.  Others are simple squares that are washed in an edible 'paint' that looks like an impressionist painting when you see them all together.  Although they do have some milk chocolate options, there seemed to be a larger selection of dark chocolates, many of which were enhanced by flavored centers.  I particularly liked the Chai flavored pieces.    Note:  They are Yelp fans, so if you check in before you order, you get a discount on your first purchase!  Be aware that this isn't mass produced candy.  It requires quality ingredients and is made in small batches by humans.  So, it won't be cheap.  But if you want to taste some divine tasting chocolates that are locally made, give this place a try.    Review #2496

There's an old joke that goes "How do you make a million dollars?"  Response:  "Start with $8 million and open a restaurant!"  It seems the more that I go to restaurants that I've been anxious to try, the more I see the delays with permitting and hiring and the myriad of things small business owners have to deal with that they just didn't expect to delay them.  So, this place opened early in May for what turned out to be a "soft opening".  Turns out there were some permitting issues with the smoker getting licensed which they expect to be resolved any day now, but because of that, they are currently serving a very limited menu of some pulled pork, pulled chicken, and some hot dog/links entrees just to stay open until they get full certification on their smoker.  It's been further complicated because they need both Speedway AND Marion County approval.  Speedway? Check!  Still waiting on the county.    Unfortunately, these limitations haven't been mentioned on Yelp or elsewhere that I've followed, so I have made a couple trips there, turned away once, and ate from the limited menu on the second.  So, you may have a totally different experience once they officially have a Grand Opening.  The place looks very cool; Nicely adorned, without too much, and lots of tv's tuned to sports channels.  We got our menu and though we were surprised there were only five items for entrees, we decided to stay.   I got the pulled pork and Greens, my wife choose the pulled chicken.  What was a bit surprising was that these $10 sandwiches didn't come with anything else than some pickle chips on the sandwich.  No potato chips unless you want to spend an additional $4 a bag.  Really?  Despite my frustration, I will say the the pulled pork sandwich tasted really good.  The bread was fresh, the meat was tender and moist, and the flavor was a bit of sweet and smoke.  My wife enjoyed the chicken as well, though she found some of the chicken wasn't "pulled" very much...large pieces that sometimes fell out of the sandwich.  And the "Greens" were delicious.  Unlike regular collard greens which may have bacon or ham in the mix, there was no meat visible and the dish took on a somewhat sweeter taste than I'm used to.  I asked the waitress about the different textures I noticed (some leafy, some circular/tube shaped) and was told they use kale instead of collards and use the entire above ground portion of the plants, so the tubes were chopped stems.  I appreciate that the owners reached out to me to let me know that they are still in transition (limited menu) for about a week (or so they have been told).  If you are going for the pulled pork or chicken, then stop on by.  They really are good.  But if you are looking for ribs or salmon, or wings, then follow along on their social media to ensure you don't experience the frustration of opening a new place.  Review #2625

Nice smoothie chain based in Dallas with good flavor and service.  I stopped in while shopping for a boost.  After finding some free parking out front, I entered and placed my order and paying at the counter. I left my name for the order and stood to the side.  In just a few minutes, my smoothie was ready.  I got a 20 oz. Banana Boat that was delicious.  I passed on the added peanut butter option which may have been even more tasty.  The staff was friendly and kept busy so I was on my way quickly.  Review #3442

It's a winter wonderland!  While on the northwest side, my wife asked me if there was a McNamara Florist in the area.  (We normally visit the one in Greenwood.)  I Yelped and found this one near Brebeuf on 86th.    They share a parking lot which was nearly full because of the nice mix of shops in the plaza.  But we lucked out and got a space right in front of the store.  As soon as we entered, we were surrounded by colorful Christmas decorations.  All kinds of things we might be looking for, as well as some things we hadn't imagined.  My wife really likes some of the table standing items as well as their lamps.  So we checked out some glass/crystal and acrylic candle stands.  Unfortunately, they only had two sizes since a taller one had been broken earlier in the week by someone's kid.  (This is not a place for kids to touch things or run around!)  But the clerk did call around to see if any of the other stores had a taller one.    We also checked out the live plant room (year around).  Although we didn't buy any, we learned about the care for some of them while there.  There are lots of trees and garlands already decorated, but you can buy the basic trees as well.  Each one displayed in the store has a theme of subject and/or color palette.  It really lets you see what a tastefully decorated tree could be.  As I said, the service was helpful and friendly without hovering.  We were free to browse and then stopped at the counter to get more assistance.  No wait times either!  This is a cool store to check out when you want to start getting in the mood for the Christmas season.  It tends to run a bit on the high side in price, but it isn't the mass produced stuff you find at the big box stores.  And quality tends to last.  Review #3320

What a nice surprise for lunch!  This deli is clean, has its own parking, and was playing a slew of Dean Martin hits while we decided what we wanted.  This is a place you place your order at the counter, and if dining in, take a number so it can be brought to your table.  I liked that the tables already had the napkins and silverware (salt & pepper shakers too) ready for the customers.  The menu items are listed by menu type on a large blackboard behind the counter.  We hadn't looked at the menu online, so when we first arrived, we saw the list of specials and then began navigating through the options.  The owner asked if we were ready and we let him know it was our first visit.  He said to take our time!  Granted, we were the only ones in line that early in the lunch hour, but I appreciated the greeting and the lack of pressure to make a choice.    I went with the Pesto Chicken Wrap which comes with a side.  I went with their fries which are served with blackened seasoning.  The fries were quite tasty and had just a bit of heat that set them apart from standard fries.  The wrap was sliced on the bias and stacked for presentation.  There were lots of fresh and crisp spinach leaves along with diced tomato in the wrap.  The pesto was more of an accent flavor on some of the first bites, probably due to where it was applied during the wrapping process, but as I got down into the wrap farther, the presto became more of a contributor to the full flavor.    My wife's original choice of a fish and chips special wasn't available, so the owner suggested a couple other fish items.  She went with the tilapia without realizing it was served blackened.  She also ordered the fries, but I knew that they came seasoned.  The owner quickly stated he could easily make them regular (salt only), so she went with those.  Considering that she doesn't like spicy (hot) food, she thought the sandwich pretty good, but would have preferred it with less seasoning.  Still, she mentioned that the place exceeded her expectations and thought it was a nice place to catch a meal.  Overall, it was a pleasant trip to a new place for lunch without settling for the same old fast food crap so many places serve.  The ingredients seemed fresh on both plates and when added to the good service, we had a high quality meal.  Review #814

If you liked Papa Roux's food, then chances are you will like Yo Mama Roux too.  The major change to the customer experience is that this place is no longer a dine-in restaurant.  So, even if the line doesn't look very long (or in this case the mob waiting in the small customer area), you may have a bit of a wait due to call-in and online orders.  I made the mistake of being absent-minded and showed up at this cajun restaurant on Mardi Gras.  Yikes!  At noon, I couldn't get inside the place.  I left and came back around 1:30 and though I was able to place an order, I stood for an hour waiting.    Now, I could have been mad at the delay, or mad at myself for not realizing the place was swamped because of the occasion, but instead, I took the opportunity to watch the small crew manage the barrage of orders.  Mama was manning the grill in the far corner.  Several others were assembling orders, putting together the side dishes, keeping the chef alert on what was coming up on future orders.  Seriously, they were hustling the entire time and nobody got a break.    And the customers simply waited patiently.  I've never seen anything like it.  Nobody complained.  When I finally got my order of the Vouxdoux Grilled Shrimp Poboy and a side of Mushroom Etouffee (with a free cole slaw thrown it too!), I tasted it and knew my answer.  The food was worth waiting for.  Now, I wouldn't want to wait an hour every time, but I went with the flow, learned something by watching a kitchen operate, and then enjoyed my meal.  If I could make one suggestion for improvement, I would encourage them to make better use of the customer waiting area that is very small.  They could easily open up part of the dining area (without tables) from the previous version of the place and make it less crowded for the customers.  Having some chairs would at least make the wait more comfortable during the rush times.  Review #2288

Good quality food with huge portions!  My wife ordered the pulled pork sandwich and fries and said that this was even better than she had when this business was at it's previous location in Mooresville.    I ordered the rib tips which also come with fries and a couple slice of white bread for sopping up the extra sauce.  I tried to be neat and use the utensils, but that doesn't work with tips that have bits of bone and cartilage to cut around, so it's best to just pick them up and nibble!  The only negatives were that the fries were a little under cooked and come unsalted.  Fortunately, they have salt and ketchup on the tables.  Still, a little bit crisper fry would be an improvement.  The tips also come in a tangy BBQ sauce while the pulled pork comes with the sauce on the side.  I hope they will expand the types of sauce they have available since I'm a Carolina Mustard fan.  The house sauce is a cross between sweet and tangy.  I don't know if they have anything hotter available.  Nice family run business that lives in Avon.  Support this local place and make a change from all the chain restaurants on the US 36 strip!  Review #2071

Sometimes, good things are worth waiting for.  I had nearly given up on this place ever being finished, but the reward is that there is a cool setting to sit and enjoy delicious beer!  I tried a flight of four and enjoyed every one.    They are located off 16th on Gent Avenue.  If you know where Tinker Coffee is, Gent is one block west, turn north and look for the Green House.  A convenient parking (paved and free) is across the street.  Note the unfinished building to the south of the green house which will eventually become their more spacious and accessible home.  After climbing a few steps to get in, you step into a lounge area with a stairway to the left:  Upstairs is office, downstairs is the brewery and additional seating.  Beyond the lounge area is the dining area and the order counter where they sell the beer and merchandise.  (Note that although they don't have much to eat currently, they are hoping to start offering sandwiches soon.)  Beyond the dining area, is a pet friendly patio that surrounds the house.  Giant games of Jenga and Four Score were available.  And the beer?  Fantastic!  I had a flight that included Wilbur's Prize Pils, a  hoppy American Pilsner (5.2%, 40 ibu) that was fully flavored than most pilsners I've had.  Very tasty!  I then tried the Guggenweizen - Hefe (5.7%, 12) which was a traditional banana and clove flavored beer (one of my favorites!)  I moved onto the Winner's Milk Jug - Stout with lactose (6.2%, 32).  This beer was very coffee flavored forward but after a few sips, it settled into a more balanced milk stout region.  I finished off with the Great Day IPA (6.7%, 70) that was crisp with a bit of citrus and fruity flavor.  Very enjoyable.  If you are a fan of craft beers and like seeing places that are ahead of the curve of hot spots, then this is the place for you.  Tech 16 development will be transforming the area between 16th Street and the river, so lots of big bucks will be making this area a focus of attention, bringing customers to Guggman and other pioneers like Tinker Coffee.  Support local!  Review #2677

After seeing Seoul Fresh on the Hot and New list, I decided to make a trip downtown for lunch.  Located on the third floor at the southwest corner of the mall food court, I approached and saw some folks standing around.  I figured out that you go to the right side of the counter to place your order, let them know if it is for "here or to go" (to go means you get it in a plastic bag and they put the lid on top, instead of the bottom), get a number on your receipt, and then move to your left to receive your order.  They could use signs saying order/pay here and one at the other end saying to pick up your order.  As it was, an odd looking line formed and blocked passage from people wanting to get by.  Service was quite friendly and they make your order when it's placed.    There are basically two food options:  A chicken or a beef.  You do get a choice of a bowl or as three tacos as well.  There is a regular size bowl and a large.  First time customers should go with the regular...I could have eaten it in one sitting, but I was content well before I finished.  Fortunately, the plastic bowl and lid make it ideal for saving for later if you have a place to refrigerate any leftovers.  The bowls also come topped with an over-easy egg.  The flavor was pretty tasty with a variety of spices (a little bit of heat, but not too much) to perk up the meat, rice, and lettuce which make up the majority of the bowl.  Note:  The meats are marinated ahead of time.  When I grabbed a spot at one of the food court tables (the restaurant does not have any designated seating), I realized they didn't give me a plastic knife to go with my plastic fork.  Some of the lettuce was oversized and the edges of the egg had crisped which made it difficult for the fork to cut through with the soft bedding of lettuce and rice below.  I managed with the fork, but think it would be a nice touch if they gave out the knives as well.  Overall, the experience was a positive one.  The food tasted good, the service friendly with just a few minutes of wait time, and the cost was under $10 without a drink.  Considering that some folks might get two meals out of bowl, that's a pretty good price.  Review #1185

Stopped at this cozy little bar after finding metered street parking out front.  We grabbed a 4-top near the entrance, around the corner to avoid the draft on a cold winter's day.  We ordered our drinks and after hearing the day's specials, my wife went with one:  Chicken Adobo Chimichanga.  This huge, tasty dish was a hit with her.  Served on a taco salad shell, the monster sized Chimi was delicious.  Lots of fresh veggies on the outside and plenty of chicken, rice, grilled bell pepper, cheese, and sauce on the inside.  Definitely needed a "to go" box for her to finish it later.  I went with the House Smoked Pulled pork.  The sandwich comes topped with cole slaw and dill pickle chips inside the bun.  The pork has a DEEP smoked flavor.  They have their own BBQ sauce, but I couldn't really see it when I popped the lid of the BBQ.  Mostly, I got smoked flavor.  Maybe I should have asked for more sauce, but for me, I really didn't get much pork taste, just smoke.  My wife tried a couple forks of pork and thought it really good.  I prefer my pork tangy with a Carolina mustard sauce or a hickory/sweet combo.  The only sauce brought to the table was a hot sauce, so I assumed they didn't have anything else.  Anyway, the sandwich was okay, just not my favorite.  However, I upgraded my side to the Roasted Brussels Sprouts for a couple bucks.  YUM!  The sprouts were tender and tasty with sorghum mustard and bacon chunks.  Delicious!!  Overall, we thought the service was fine and friendly.  It took about fifteen minutes for our food to be prepped and served.  Checkout and getting the to go box also was efficient.  Good food and with a patio overlooking the canal, it could be a nice spot to return to in warmer weather.  Review #467

Wow!  Even with high expectations based upon who is behind this restaurant, I am still blown away what I had here.  If you don't know, Croute Baking is the newest addition to the Cunningham Restaurant Group (CRG) family of restaurants.  Executive Pastry/Baking Chef Hattie McDaniel is the master craftsman behind the bakery portion of this carry out restaurant.  Though she is still making the fine desserts for Vida and Nesso, she is now making pastries for visitors who stop by this shop on North Meridian downtown.  (In mid-August, the Cafe at Croute will open a few blocks away inside the Regions Tower.)  Although you can look in the window from Meridian, the entrance to the shop is through the buildings central lobby.  Everything in the bakery is in plain view as you can see Chef and her assistants preparing the pastries which are placed in display cases near the entrance.  There were Danish, Croissants, Bostocks, and cookies.  I ordered the Almond Bostock which was delicious.  Think round sponge cake texture stuffed with an almond frangipane and fruit jam.  Yum!  I also got the Ham & Cheese Croissant which was made with house ham, gruyere, and a bit of dijon for flavor.  Light and crisp with that buttery flavor you expect from a good croissant.  They also serve breakfast sandwiches to including Toast & Avocado, English Muffins, and others.  I had a chance to briefly chat Chef Hattie while there!  But that's not all.  The bakery will also serve as a test kitchen for CRG like Vida was supposed to be.  You can stop by for lunch (after 11) and grab sandwiches, soup, salad, and wraps.  I picked up a Pastrami + Carraway Havarti sandwich that was as delicious as it was huge!  (Note:  this could easily be sliced and be shareable.  Ask to have it sliced if you prefer it that way.)  Chef Carl Chambers (you may have seen him on IndyStyle) was overseeing the prep of the sandwiches to make sure they were perfect.  My sandwich qualified as one of those BMS (Big Mouth Sandwiches) that I needed to scrunch to fit inside my mouth.  The sandwich came on grilled rye with cheese and fontana sauce.  And don't forget the spiced pickles that come with.  I could eat a jar of those!  One last thing.  Late in the year (hopefully in November), the test kitchen part of the shop will host private tasting events with multiple courses (around 10) for those who wish to reserve the table.  I don't know the cost yet, but the reservation will have a set price and you can reserve it for yourself or up to ten people.  I hope my family & friends see this and takes me out for my birthday!!  Great food. Great people.  I was treated like a king when I arrived after a minute or two to look around.  It's worth the hunt for a parking spot to get down here!  (And come hungry!)  Review #2823

I usually don't go out for tacos, but when I realized this franchised taco shop was locally based, I decided to give it a try.  I really liked that they had a variety of tacos available including a chili ground beef soft taco and a chicken soft taco.  I loaded them with what ever toppings they had and selected the 2nd of five heat sauces since I wanted some heat and flavor, but not too much that might override the taste.  The ingredients were fresh and the taco shells were sturdy enough to stay together while loaded.    The amount of chili on the chili taco was minimal and was a bit disappointing.  The chicken version had a lot more meat, but it seemed like standard chicken deli meat, not seasoned like I might find at some other Mexican restaurants.    The staff was friendly and fairly quick on building my meal, but they have very limited interaction other than calling your name when your order is ready.    No tipping or busing of the tables by the staff seemed apparent.  Plenty of parking in the common lot of the strip mall.  Review #1985

I stopped in for lunch with my wife after a fun round of mini-golf at IMA.  One side of the Cafe is fairly simple cafeteria style, while the other half is all windows and overlooks the beautiful Sutphin Fountain.  If you wish to order something from the "cold" side, you simply make a selection from the refrigerated section and pay for it at the counter.  If you wish to order from the "hot" side, you place an order and pay at the counter.  They give you a number to display on your table and will bring your food out to you.    Unfortunately, the wait for hot food can get a bit long depending upon how many orders are ahead of yours.  In our case, my wife had finished her "Collections Club" (Peppered Bacon, ham , turkey, swiss cheese, lettuce, tomato, red onion, dijon aioli on toasted sourdough bread) and was moving on to her Chocolate Chunk cookie by the time my meal arrived.  She liked the flavor of the sandwich, but because all the meat was rolled into a 1.5 to 2 inch diameter log and placed on the sandwich, the sandwich was kind of clumsy to eat.  She ended up cutting the sandwich with her knife and fork and it became more manageable.  I ordered the Peppered Bacon Burger (7 oz Angus beef burger, peppered bacon, provolone cheese, lettuce, tomato, red onion, blue cheese horseradish aioli on brioche roll).  The bacon was crisscrossed over the burger so each corner had a porcine extension.  This was very tasty and the bacon had plenty of cracked pepper.  The burger came with "Food Should Taste Good" whole grain chips (more cracker than chip; tortilla chips made with brown rice, flax, sesame and sunflower seeds, and quinoa).  The chips had a great crunch and were delicious, especially when paired with the burger.  It would be nice if the cafeteria of an art museum could be made over to compliment the settings of the rest of the museum instead of appearing drab.    Although the flavors were good, it was rather awkward having to watch each other eat the cold and hot meals.  Not sure what can be done about that without sacrificing quality, but the folks on the grill really need to be aware that "the heat is on" them to get the food out quickly.  Review #135

I enjoyed my visit to Tacos & Tequila.  First, there is plenty of convenient parking in a public lot across Main St.  Second, there is outdoor seating in front of the building for those sunny days when it is too nice to sit indoors.  Third, the wait service was efficient and friendly.  I was welcomed and told I could pick my own spot (otherwise, they ask you to wait to be seated per a sign by the counter). They checked in regularly and were efficient in bringing my bill when I was finished.  Fourth, the wait for my food was minimal.  I was brought a complementary bowl of chips and a small dish.  The table had a verde salsa and a tomato based salsa with a little bit of heat but rather mild. (They do have hot sauce and a "roja" sauce by request.) The salsa was thin enough to be dispensed through a squirt bottle, so it didn't stick to the chips which were too large to dip into the small bowl provided without breaking the chips.  They use paper towels (located on each table) for napkins and I needed to use a couple extra sheets to clean up my salsa splashes.  My meal choice was the carne asada (steak) burrito which comes with a side of rice and beans.  The burrito was also topped with a white sauce (cheese?).  The burrito was thicker than most places I have been to, but not as long.  The flavor was good, but because the ends of the tortilla were folded so much, some of the bites on the end were mostly tortilla with little meat.    I also ordered a side of guacamole which is less expensive than the appetizer which I assume is shareable size.  It was the perfect size for me and because it had a thicker consistency than the salsa choices, the points of the chips were able to scoop and have the guac stay on.  Although there were a few minor items that kept this from being my favorite Mexican restaurant, I think the quality of the food and service deserves a solid four.  I would gladly go back to try other items.  p.s.  This restaurant is owned by the folks who run Barbecue and Bourbon down the street.  Review #387

This park has a wide variety of activities and plenty of room for enjoying the park.  There was an aquatic center with a splash park, pool, and water slide.  There were basketball and sports fields.  There was a long hiking trail around the park and another that goes to the south around a farmer's field.  There are several shelters with grills and a playground with a nice variety of equipment for sliding, swinging, and climbing.  One of the negatives is that the park doesn't have adequate drainage along the trails, so I noticed several places where water was standing across the paved paths.  I don't appreciate getting my shoes and socks wet while on a long hike and that would discourage me from using the trails unless we had a dry spell.    Otherwise, the park seemed in pretty good shape with plenty of parking.  Review #611

I was surprised when I checked in that Claire's hadn't been reviewed before.  Like almost every mall in Central Indiana, Perry Crossing/Metropolis was no exception to having one of these small accessory shops.  Here you can get your ears pierced, pick up earrings and head bands, a few toys, and holiday novelty items.  During the week, the crowd was small so it was fairly easy to get around.  The only negative was that when my wife was ready to pay for some festive earrings, the only clerk was busy with an indecisive boy about getting his ear pierced.  (He didn't.)  So, depending upon your situation, you may or may not be helped promptly.    Like most malls, parking is limited in front of the store with free lots about a block away from the store front.  Review #3446

Having stopped by the "other Mama" bakery in the neighborhood, I wasn't sure what to expect at this one.  What I found was a smaller display room with custom cakes on a rack on the left, some packaged baked goods on the right, a few tables, and a counter to place my order.  Turns out this place not only does custom cakes, but they offer fully loaded (as well as some Vegan) baked goods.  I didn't realize that they also offer meals throughout the day that include soups, baked potatoes, and BBQ.  They have a few other entrees like chicken salad sandwich and red beans and rice.  Since I had already eaten lunch, I decided to focus on the baked goods and though the display wasn't large, there was a nice variety of items to choose from.  I picked up a package of peanut butter cookies (large, soft, and flat...and quite yummy!), one of brownies (thick, chocolatey, and a little bit gooey), and a square of German Chocolate Cake that was chilled and was really good!  The cake had just enough coconut to give it that chewy texture which paired well with the light, fresh cake.  If the lunch is anywhere as good as the bakery side, then this place is a winner!  Review #2464

I only go to the zoo once every few years.  I like to go when the weather is cooler so that the animals are more active and the crowds are smaller.  Sure, animals sometimes hide and rarely move, but occasionally, I get a really great photo of an animal.  I don't go "to be entertained".  This isn't a circus.  So I get that there will be days when I am a bit disappointed.  But that isn't the purpose of a zoo.  The zoo is there to provide a sanctuary from the ever decreasing space in the wild; where the animals will be given the best care that humans can provide.  Considering that the zoo doesn't get any tax dollars from the city or state, I don't even mind the price.    I remember when the zoo was an embarrassment to the city.  It was some rundown little park on the north side between downtown and Broad Ripple.  Mini goats were one of the big features back then.    To go now and see this planned park with lots of "natural" settings for the animals to live in is a complete change from where it began.  Sure, it would be great if space and finances weren't a problem to add even more varieties like some other regional zoos have.  But I appreciate that the exhibits that we have are done well.  The zoo has had to find a balance between conservation and entertainment.  As we see theme parks add zoos to their attractions, the zoo has had to add rides that are entertaining for children, but not too crazy that they disturb the animals.  It's about balance.  So, I heartily recommend going out and spending a day with the animals.  It may just be a matter of time before some species will only be left thanks to places like this.  Review #270

After reading the review of this place by one of my Yelp friends, I bookmarked it and made plans to give it a try.  It's a small cafe with a motor theme (lots of gears & tools used for decor) that sits tucked away in the former Angie's List campus.  The cafe has limited indoor seating on the first floor, but plenty of patio seating and lots of upstairs seating if you can climb stairs.   First, finding the place is the key.  The address is misleading.  It's actually along Cruze Street, not Washington.  From downtown, head east on Washington under the interstate bridges by College.  Head east to the next light.  Turn left onto Cruze.  Head north slowly and when you see the old metal diner on your right, turn into that parking lot before the diner.  Moto shares that lot.  Inside, the place is industrial with a stairway, one table (yes that is correct) and the order counter that has a salad bar.  The menu is listed on the wall behind the order counter.  I was welcomed and when I asked what the cashier would recommend, she said to "always go with the weekly special".  It was a Cuban sandwich so I went with that.  They also have a variety of sandwiches, some soups, salads, and brownies for dessert.  All beverages are kept chilled in a cooler including water.  After paying, I gave my name so that they could call it out when it was ready.  I headed upstairs to explore that area since I was originally planning on dining in.  The upstairs has a bank of windows facing north and an exterior stairway.  I thought it interesting that a tool storage container was used as a place to get your condiments (packets) and napkins (rolled paper).  I headed back downstairs and noticed the cashier leave.  That left the cook in the back.  I wasn't sure what was going on, but after a few minutes, the cook came out with my sandwich in a to go box and so I just grabbed some napkins and headed out.  It seemed a bit strange that the cashier disappeared without saying anything.  Not sure what new customers would have done with nobody to give an order to.  Despite the oddity, the sandwich was really good with a crispy outside to the bread and a nice blend of flavors inside.  Hopefully, I will be able to try  a cup of soup with my sandwich on my next visit.  Note:  It is easy to return downtown by heading north to Market Street and following that back.  Review #3333

I feel bad for the guys in the kitchen.  I stopped by for lunch and after seeing the sign to seat myself, waited a short period for someone to stop by.  A guy from the kitchen informed me that he was sorry, but there were no waiters working that day.  He would try to do his best if I wanted to stay.  I had traveled over 45 minutes to Irvington, and doubted I would be back anytime soon, so I decided to give it a shot.  I received a menu and some ice water and when I found what I wanted, went up to the order counter and let the guys in the kitchen know that I was ready.    A short while later, the same kitchen guy apologized that neither of the kitchen workers knew how to make a boba tea.  So, I settled for the water.  While waiting, I noticed the continual assault by houseflies buzzing around the window and occasionally annoying me.  I've seen this issue commented on before and it made me wonder why this issue isn't taken seriously by the owners.  I've dined at over 700 restaurants and have never experienced a problem this bad.  The guests sitting on the other side of the room didn't seem to have the problem, so it must have been something about the windows attracting them.  A quick look at the floor let me know that it could use a deep cleaning as well with a buffer.  Very dingy.  I wondered if the kitchen was in better shape and if I should leave.  Fortunately, the banh mi I ordered arrived and was amazing!  Fresh ingredients topped the toasted sandwich.  The crust had a nice crunch and the pork n' shredded pork was delicious!  I would gladly recommend that to someone.  But I would suggest getting the order to go....the inside looks unfinished (abandoned murals, open holes in the air system) and questionable at best.  Sad.  Review #1123

One of Indy's older parks (1909), the park has plenty of room for hiking, two playgrounds, a shelter, swimming pool, and indoor ice rink.  The park is lined with numerous mature trees offering shade to visitors and shelter for lots of neighborhood animals.  The only real negative I'm aware of is the limited availability of the single shelter.  For a park having 42 acres, it seems a shame that there wasn't planning for another shelter to facilitate family gatherings.  The park has had its problems (some are financial based) with the pool and ice rink staying open.  Hopefully, those issues are behind them as the warmer weather approaches.  Review #555

I was on the west side of Indy and decided to trust Yelp to help find a new place to stop for lunch.  So, I got off at the Washington Street exit of I-465 and found this brightly colored building just east of the Morris Street intersection.  They have a small parking lot on the east side of the building.  Once inside, I was greeted from the far end of the dining room and told I could sit anywhere.  The interior was bright green with plenty of tables in a long, narrow room.  At the back was a curtained area where I could see Mexican beer and beverages for sale.  A music system was playing Mariachi-style music, while a single television played a soap opera in Spanish.  I noticed the menu had lots of pictures and the food was grouped into categories with very little description of the meal, and those were in Spanish.  Leafing through the pages, I saw "Quesadilla" and it came in several varieties.  My waitress was very conversant in both English and Spanish, so she let me know what types of meat were available for the dish (I went with the steak).  Just below the listing, there was Sopes which I was unfamiliar with.  She explained it was a corn meal disk topped with frijoles (refried beans), lettuce, cheese, and sour cream and that I could pick a type of meat for the dish as well (I went with chicken.)  She asked if I wanted anything else and I thought the two dishes were enough.  It wasn't until the plates were brought out that I realized the restaurant did not give complementary chips and salsa like most Mexican themed restaurants.  The dishes also did not come with any sides (at least at lunch.)    I liked the flavor of the Sopes as it was served.  The chicken was warm and moist and the dish had enough flavor that I didn't feel the need to add any sauces.  The Quesadilla was served on another plate and appeared a bit naked.  It was basically a folded pocket of a tortilla filled with a decent amount of stock cut into small pieces and a nice melted light cheese.  It was served with two bottles of sauce:  Salsa verde and "Red" sauce.  I especially liked the flavor of the salsa verde with the meal.  The red sauce had a little bit of heat but was relatively mild.  Most of the steak was pretty tender, but there were a couple bites that were a little tough.   One thing I noticed was that between each entree and the plate was a single sheet of serving paper.  I used a table knife to cut my entrees into bite sized pieces and couldn't help but cut the paper.  So, I was concerned the cut paper might stick to the bottom of each bite.  I decided to pull the paper out from under the food and was left with scraps of wadded up paper on my plate.  I wonder why they feel the need to place the paper under the food?  The table knives were not very sharp and required a bit of cutting to get through the food.  Maybe steak knives would be more convenient for customers to use.  The waitress was attentive without being intrusive.  I liked that she offered lime wedges with my water.  She also did a good job of getting my bill taken care of so that I could get on my way.  Overall, the food was good and service was fine.  It was a bit different from the "standard" Mexican experience that I have had at most economical restaurants of this cuisine.  My advice?  Don't be afraid to speak up and ask questions about the food and what may or may not come with it.  Review #374

After a long stressful Monday (4-11-16), I decided to stop into Matt the Miller's Tavern for dinner.  I was fortunate to find a street parking spot just outside the front door.  The crowd was moderate with a constant hum of conversation and sports on the large screen tv's.  Since this was my first time here, I didn't have any real idea of what to try.  So, when my waiter read off the specials, one of those jumped out at me.  I decided to go with the Haddock with Shrimp & tomato lemongrass cream sauce with kale, julienne broccoli, Brussels sprouts, cabbage and chicory.  I also ordered a local craft beer Sun  King Osiris Ale for the first time as well.  Two great choices!  I think I underestimated the quality of food to expect from a "tavern".  It looked and felt like a sports bar, but this seafood dish was top notch....one of the best I have had this year!  When I am paying for a meal, I really appreciate when a chef makes the entree as visually appealing as the taste.  It sets the level of expectation.  This colorful plate looked better than I had hoped for and the taste did not disappoint.  Everything was cooked perfectly.  The tartness and the little bits of crunch worked well with the fish or on its own.  All around a great meal.  My only regret was that I ate it too fast and didn't take more time to savor the flavors.  I definitely plan to return and sample some of the regular fare on the menu.  Review #32

I really enjoyed my lunch and a brew at this B&B.  Although the ridiculous road construction was a bit problematic, I didn't hold that against the brewpub and found my way inside.  Stepping in, the space is very open and bright.  On the east end is where you will find stacks of books and games...a place to unplug from your devices and enjoy the experience of reading from a book or for socializing with a board game.  Sadly, not currently having Wifi is a deterrent for some who think of it as a coffee shop.  The name says it:  BOOKS and Brews...not your phone and Brews.  (Note:  they are pursuing having Wifi at this location, just not yet.)  The west end of the space is where the bar and additional seating is located.  I had one of their Naan lunches called the "Wilbur" which is best described as a personal pizza like meal with pulled pork as the meat.  Very tasty!  Definitely recommend it.  I wanted to try something different from the core 5 house beers, so after sampling a couple interesting choices, I settled for the "Stout of Evermore" which is a Peanut Butter Stout (5.5%, 35 IBU).  The peanut butter they use in the brewing is from Reese's Pieces.  This was a delightful drink and held its own while I ate my lunch.  Another plus!  Hopefully, the construction will end soon and I would like to see the outside get some art work to brighten the dull gray exterior.  After all, you can't judge a book by its cover...but you can catch someone's attention with it!  Review #1754

As much as I like new restaurants that push the envelope of tastes with new combinations, I have to admit that simple food done well still makes for an enjoyable meal.  Such is the case at Dawson's which was packed even on a Thursday lunch.  To avoid a wait, I was able to sit at the bar where the bartender did a great job.  Not only did he manage the folks seated around the counter (it quickly filled), but he took care of all the folks in the room including a large party of 12 that wanted individual checks!  That's is efficiency and impressive.  He let me know all the daily specials and soon had my order in.  I went with a lunch special of the Chicken Salad Sandwich that came with a small side of fresh fruit.  I also ordered a cup of French Onion Soup.  Being so packed, I expected some delay in getting my order, but was a little disappointed that the soup didn't come out first.  Instead, it was served at the same time as my sandwich.  The folks who ordered salads as their sides got them ahead of time, so I was hoping the soup would come so I could occupy some of my wait time.    The soup did taste wonderful and the cheese was soft and stretchy, the kind where you can separate it with just the spoon, but almost always need your fingers to break those few strands that cling to the cup.  Nice flavor with just the right amount of saltiness.  The side of fruit was disappointing.  Some of the fruit was chilled, some looked a little 'soft'.  Some rind was still on the cantelope, but not much.  This could have been much better.  The sandwich came on my choice of wheat bread which was thick and had a chewy crust that was okay, but not great.  There was a large dollop of chicken salad, probably about a cup, in the center of the sandwich like it had been placed by an ice cream scoop.  Would have taken much time to spread it evenly?  I remedied the distribution, but it just made the restaurant seem like it was taking shortcuts.  The flavor of the salad was okay, but I did like that there was lots of chicken and they had sliced grapes which I always appreciate in my salad.  Overall, just an okay sandwich.  So, I would give a 5 for the service, a 4 for the soup, and a 3 for the sandwich & fruit.  They obviously have a good value for the quality of food since the place was packed, so if you want something affordable, then definitely stop by.  Review #1974

I can't say how good this store is throughout the year, but during the holidays, they have a wide variety of accessories that my wife wanted to check out.  Conveniently located near the front of the store, there were loads of colorful earrings and small gifts or stocking stuffers.  She picked out a pair during our visit and had a quick checkout process.  Everything seemed to be working well today!  Review #1901

If you want to try something different from the standard/fast food style tacos that are found all around, check out this new addition to the food scene in Broad Ripple.  Located in the upstairs portion of the corner building, there is limited parking on the south side and steep stairs on both front and back to enter (my wife did say she saw an elevator, but I'm not sure where it was located.)  I loved the flavors that I tried and with the exception of the shrimp being a bit overcooked on my wife's taco, everything was cooked with expertise in bringing out flavor.  I tried the Guadalajara Beef Stew which comes served with house made chips.  The chips are double layered and the layers sometimes split creating extra crunch without being too tough to bite through.  No oily problems on my visit.  The chips were great for loading bites of stew.  The beef comes in longer strips, so I did need to cut them down to bite sized pieces, but that was simple enough and the flavor was phenomenal.  Highly recommended.  My wife tried the salsa and chips.  There is a $3 charge and the chips are the same style as I received on my appetizer.  The salsa was smooth and was so mild that it was borderline bland.  It was okay, but I've had tastier.  Get the stew instead!  We didn't want to get too full, so we each ordered only one taco:  my wife got the Adobo Grilled Shrimp and I got the Baja which is a cod based taco.  Each cost about $4.50 and they were only four or five inches across.  So, not a great price for tacos, but for me, the flavor was worth it.  My taco had a great balance of savory and acidity.  Nice crunch and texture too.  My wife enjoyed hers as well, but the shimp was a bit overcooked and there were only three small shrimp on her taco.  Not a great deal and a little disappointing.  But the flavor was really good.  We didn't try the drinks or desserts this time, but we really enjoyed the food we had.  As others have suggested in their reviews, the service was a bit sporadic so expect some waiting time between seeing the waitress.  The restaurant was only half full at lunch, but the sound level was very loud so that conversation was often repeated.  Both issues can be addressed if management wants to improve the experience.  I don't have a problem with charging for quality ingredients or think that all tacos should be cheap, so I won't knock them on pricing.  After all, if they aren't profitable, they will join a long line of closed businesses at this location.  Review #2155

I had lunch here shortly after the restaurant moved into the new location on Virginia.  I went early and was able to find street parking across the street.  The cuisine was new to my experience, so I decided to go with some of the items that I had seen mentioned in reviews.  I started off with a Korean Fried Chicken Steamed Bun.  This was my first tasting of the steam buns....I am definitely a fan!  The deep fried boneless chicken and the mint were a pleasant surprise.
