I hadn't realized the chicken would be breaded and crispy.  The bun itself had a texture that reminded me of marshmallows, but still had a delicious bread taste.    I also wanted to try the Cuban Banh Mi. This reminded me of a panini style cuban sandwich...with pork and ham.  It was okay, not fantastic.  The plate definitely lacked any color and the sandwich without any side made me think I should have reconsidered and picked up something else instead of another protein dish.  They do have some veggie dishes, but not specifically as sides you can add.  Overall, the dining selection is fairly unique as well as tasty, so I would recommend giving the restaurant a try.  Review #58

I really liked this new ice cream/treats shop in Fountain Square.  The building recently completed renovation next to the new bus stop.  There is free street parking out front, but if that's full, there is a free municipal lot about a half block away.  The interior is a bit dark with high ceilings, but most of the items to choose from like sodas, candies and other treats are near the front where the lighting is a bit brighter.  The ice cream/order counter is about a third of the way back on the left with dining along the right wall.  There is a cool game board wall that brightens the place up a bit as well.  I didn't try anything but the ice cream and I have to say that the Chocolate Raspberry Truffle ice cream was delicious!  Very creamy and it stayed cold with melting all over while I ate it.  They don't have as many flavors as some of the bigger ice cream places (especially the franchises), but they do offer a decent sample and can make shakes and sundaes for you.  They also have some Vegan options for an extra $.50.  I'm not sure how many vegan flavors they have or the taste, but I wanted to point that out.  They also have numerous gluten free options as well.  Prices are about the middle of the pack when compared to small shops around Indy.    My only negative is that they don't open until 2, so stopping by after lunch to grab something is a bit of an inconvenience.  Review #2883

When I write reviews, I try to share the answers to questions first time visitors might like to know.  I also base my ratings on comparable business types.  So, my standards for a steak house are higher than for an ice cream stand.  So when I did a return visit to the Iron Skillet (this time, a to go order), I struggled with finding comparable businesses.  You see, this restaurant has been in business for a long time (1956), even longer than I have been alive.  It is an elegant house that serves "family style" meals.  What that means is that if you order a dinner, you select the protein and then you are given a large number of sides prepared en masse.  So a skillet chicken dinner for one (1) comes with about five pieces of meat, mashed potatoes and gravy, pickled beets, cottage cheese, green beans (with a bit of onion flavor), 2 small biscuits, a wedge of house dressed iceberg lettuce, and corn.  And those servings are generous, so when I placed my order I ordered two helpings since my wife was due back around lunch time.  When I picked up my order (which was ready on time), it nearly filled an entire shopping bag!  A lot of food and served as both lunch and dinner for us.  Note that if you dine in, they charge a bit more and include a dessert option which would be challenging to eat if you eat all your veggies!    The food as served in a to go order, reminded me of the selections I have seen at cafeterias like Gray Brothers in Mooresville.  I will say that the flavor was more appealing here.  Although some of the veggies were over cooked, part of that may have been due to my travel time in waiting to eat them.  The pickled beets were delicious, the gravy and mashed potatoes (served very smooth so I'm not sure if those are from scratch) tasted good too.  I liked the additional flavoring in the beans though they were a bit soft.  And the chicken?  Well it was pretty much like a lot of fried chicken in Indiana:  hard to stop once you start.  Very tasty and not too salty.  As I noted earlier, the interior is elegant.  You could dress up for this place and fit with the table settings.  However, most folks arriving were very casual.  Waiters wear white shirts with black ties and slacks.  The hosts wore a dress and a suit.  Seems like the tradition of treating a meal out as something special has been lost in today's culture.  One of the negatives about the place is the appearance of the outside.  From the private parking lot off of 30th Street, you see a boarded up window on the outside and the whole house looks like it could use a bit of exterior maintenance along with the grounds.  Hopefully, warmer weather will provide an opportunity for those things to be addressed, but they don't make a good first impression.  It should match the interior to be more inviting to customers.  Overall, a hearty meal if you like an abundance of food that is mostly selected for you.  I think there may be some a la carte options, but I didn't pursue those.  It is a lot of food for the price and the convenience of having a full meal with more sides than I normally prepare at home.  Review #2471

I decided to stop for an early dinner while on the north side and found a spot in the private lot next to Friendly Tavern.  Because it was early (just after 4 pm), the dining room was closed, so I sat in the room surrounding the bar.  There wasn't much of a crowd, so I experienced no waiting.  I was greeted promptly by my server after being directed to sit anywhere I liked by the bartender.    I grabbed a two top table near the bar and reviewed the paper menus that also seem to serve as place mats.  Because of the positive Yelp reviews, I opted for the Friendly's Famous Wings and a side order of celery and carrots with Ranch.  While waiting, I ordered wine from a brief, but diversified list of alcoholic beverages.  Before long, my plate of veggies arrived and I was stunned!  The plate had 12 pieces of carrot and celery (divided equally) that were about eight inches long!  The carrots were crisp and sweet and tasted great with the Ranch dressing.  The celery hearts were nearly as long as the carrot strips and were even more crisp and juicy.  Before I could finish my veggies, a huge plate with 20 pieces of battered chicken wings arrived.  I had read there were usually 18 to 20 pieces, but it didn't dawn on me that the drummettes and flats would be that large.  I can eat a lot, but discretion made me come to my senses when my taste buds kept telling me to eat more!  The pieces were crunchy on the outside and tender and moist on the inside.  I got to choose two dipping sauces with my order, so I went with the Honey Apple BBQ and the Ranch.  The chicken was really good without either.  But the sauces added layers to the flavor.    As much as I enjoyed the meal, I asked for a "to go" box and was even brought lids for the sauces without having to ask.  Great anticipation (probably happens frequently there) by the waitress who also kept me in the loop on meal delivery times.  The bar area had several conversations between customers and the bartender leading me to think that they had talked before.  Seems like a great place for the locals who have been in the area for a long time.  Nice to feel welcome as a visitor too!  Review #417

I was downtown and decided to check out this unique Cunningham Dining Group cafe.  Located inside the high rise at 251 N Illinois St, there is a parking garage under the building, but unfortunately there is not a discount or validation option available.  So, you are either limited to street parking (metered) or walking from some other lot you may favor.  (I parked in Circle Centre Mall and walked over here.)  So, most of the customers are folks who are already downtown and are within easy walking distance.  A lot of the customers get their orders to go.  However, there are more tables than I expected available for those who may want to dine in like I did.  The line for placing your order (sorry, no wait staff here) starts on the east side where you grab a tray, napkins, and use the plastic ware dispensers.   There is a conveniently placed menu on the wall.  The line is laid out with "stations" for salads, sandwiches, soups, and for me, ordering a Ham and Cheddar Quesadilla.    At that area, I was able to select the items I wanted to add to the basic ham and cheese.  After adding things like tomatoes, pico de gallo, and onions, I asked for recommendations from my server and he suggested trying the black bean salsa (great choice!)  He folded the oversize shell in half and took it to the grill, telling me that he would bring it out as soon as it was heated.  I grabbed a fruit cup as a side order and was told I could help myself to a sour cream cup and a salsa cup before paying.  They have a self serve beverage counter near the west entrance to the cafe.  Note:  Although this is a Cunningham restaurant, the computer system is not compatible with the Cunningham points system.  But never fear!  If you show your dining card, you get a 10% discount on your order!  That works for me!  After a five to ten minute wait, the server who was making my quesadilla brought it out (he had given me a heads up when it was about 2 minutes out.)  When he delivered the plate, I asked how he kept track of orders since they didn't ask for names or have numbers on the receipts.  He said he had to learn to pay attention to customers when they came through so that he could recognize them.  That could be challenging, but seemed to work.  Finally, the food was really good!  The giant quesadilla shell was cut into four manageable pieces.  I added the sour cream and salsa to mine, so I used the plastics to eat, but could have picked the pieces up by hand since they held together well.  The quality was what you would expect from the Cunningham group.  Fresh ingredients, clean restaurant in front and behind the service lines, and friendly service.  If you are downtown for lunch, check out this place for a nice change of pace!  Review #438

I stopped by for a quick lunch at this Irish Pub/sports bar located on the end of a strip mall on the south east side.  Inside, there's a sign to wait to be seated for the dining room.  Although I was dining by myself, I chose not to sit in the bar that was behind a short wall beyond the dining area.  I was taken to a 2-top table with a bench seat on one side.  Silent sports television was playing on the numerous screens.  I went with the Classic Reuben and fries for my meal.  The Reuben has thick sliced grilled corned beef, a sauerkraut that was a bit more sour than most, Swiss cheese, 1000 Island dressing, and grilled rye.  The fries had a crispy exterior like they were fried in duck fat (not sure what they used.)  Both sandwich and fries were good and I'd recommend them.  My waitress did a good job of keeping my lunch on track in case I had a limited amount of time.  She checked on water refills and processed my check timely.  Overall, a good place to stop for a meal!  Review #2644

Despite all the traffic on east 96th St, I was thrilled with my lunch at this north side edition of Tried & True (the original is in Greenwood.)  After finding easy parking in the lot outside, my wife and I entered the bar entrance (the family entrance is farther to the right).    The interior was spacious with an industrial look and high ceilings.  There is the customary bar seating and a number of small tables inside the area beyond the bar.  There is also a decent sized patio with umbrella covered tables as well.  It was a nice day, so we sat out there.    Our waiter was there promptly and got our beverage orders.  I went with a local craft beer out of Lapel's Pax Verum Brewing called "Smooth Criminal".  It was tasty New England IPA (5.8%, but only 25 IBU).  The beer paired nicely with our appetizer of Crispy Brussels Sprouts served with a house mustard sauce for dipping.  The sprouts were generously portioned and had a nice crispy texture on the outside flakes (that's my favorite way to eat the halved sprouts.)  They could have used a little more seasoning, but the dip was still pretty good on its own.  I also ordered the smallest of the Wing Baskets (8 pc.)  The small size comes with celery sticks and choice of dip (I had sour cream) and the choice of one glaze for the boneless wings.  I asked for the breaded wings to be served "naked" (no glaze) but with the glaze on the side.  I also upgraded for a small fee to get a second glaze so I had Teryaki Sweet and the Parmesan Garlic to dip my wings in.  I really liked both!  The chicken was moist and the breading (light, not doughy) had a bit of seasoning that made the chicken taste good even without any glazes.  I don't order wings often, but these were the best I've had at a restaurant in a long time.  I definitely recommend them.  My wife ordered a taco salad.  She liked the flavor but was a little surprised it wasn't a classic bowl shaped shell, but instead, was made with corn chips.  She got over being surprised and enjoyed her meal.  Our waiter did a good job in checking on us out on the patio.  He brought a couple of beer samples for me before I settled on my choice.  He also brought the check out in a timely fashion so that we were on our way without delay.    I love when a business surprises me and exceeds my expectations.  Good job T&TA!  Review #2989

Great Beer, Good Service, and okay food.  That may be an oversimplification, but it serves for those of you who aren't reading for the details.  My wife and I stopped in on a Friday for lunch and wanted to try some of the food as well as their tasty beverages.  She ordered a basket of the breaded pickles and we got the garlic dip to go with.  There were enough to be shareable and they were quite good.  Not oily, the breading made the slices easy to eat as finger food even while dipping.    I went with a flight and they come as a group of four for $8.  What surprised me was the size of the glasses.  These were much taller than I've had elsewhere and I would say they looked like they were at least 5 oz, but maybe even 7 oz!  I went with the Dirk Dubbelr (Belgian 8.6% 18 IBU) that was good, the IPA (6.4% 70) that had a pleasant hoppy taste without too much bitterness, the Ginger Snap spiced ale (5.2% ?) that was the favorite of both of us, and the Pippi Lager Stocking (5.5%, 25).  I enjoyed them all.  I also asked for a tasting sample of the Alex, a Raspberry Milk Stout (4.2% 21) that had a pleasant flavor, but I wasn't able to taste the raspberry as much as I had hoped.  Still, I would gladly try each of them again!  For lunch, I went with the fish tacos which come with a pair of flour tortillas (each), some pickled cabbage, and a sauce that has a little bit of kick or heat to it.  Nice flavor blend that kept the flavor perked, not flat.  My side of the house kettle chips was really good with a bit of sweet and cinnamon (?) flavor.  Unfortunately, my wife's fish and chips (fries in this case) was the only disappointment.  The breading was a bit soggy/under cooked and definitely under seasoned.  She simply ate the fish without the breading since she is watching her calories intake, so it wasn't a big deal. But we did mention the breading problems to the waitress who listened and was glad that we mentioned it to her so that she could pass it on to the kitchen.  Apparently they are trying some new things and appreciated the real time feed back.  I respect the way our server handled the suggestion.  Overall, a very positive experience and I would gladly come back to try some more beverages and maybe a few of their other items on the food menu too!  Review #2047

I rarely give a 1 star rating but if a place deserves it, that's what they get.  So when I heard about this new discount store opening on the south side of Mooresville, I felt I should check it out even though I am not a fan of discount stores in general.  This place was below my expectations!  The premise here is that each week, a couple semis will unload their items into aisles of bins.  On Friday and Saturday, everything is only $5.  They are closed on Sundays, but on Monday, the prices start decreasing.  So Mondays, everything drops to $3, Tuesday to $2, Wednesday to $1, and for a couple hours on Thursday mornings, everything drops to $0.25.  It sounds like an interesting concept but that is where it ends.  On opening day, photos were posted of people getting 32" televisions and drones for only $5!  However, all sales are final as is.  If there are no instructions, you figure it out.  If it simply doesn't work?  Too bad.  No returns.    I decided to go on Monday after knowing they were closed on Sunday.  What I walked into was a place where shoppers with giant carts (most left them angled in the aisles so it was hard to get by) and bins of random items:  some in boxes, some without markings (but you can't open them to look.) Some items were in plastic bags and others were just loose.  No sense of order.  Even though there was an entire day for the staff to straighten things out or group items.  No effort at all.  I guess when you charge so little, they don't want to pay anyone to actually make it seem better.    When I compare it to a discount place like Ollie's on the other side of town, this place makes Ollie's look like an upscale experience.  There you can find things by type and orderly.  Here, it's just like going to a hoarder's place and wading through it.  Unless you are so desperate to spend a little bit of money, I would suggest staying away and wait for a nice garage sale.  It will be interesting to see if more televisions and expensive electronics continue to show up each week of if that was just a ploy to kick off the business.  By Monday, all the high end items were gone.  I'm curious how long this place will last.  Review #3434

I stopped by while in the area and decided to check out this pet store since I had not heard of it before.  They are located in the strip mall on the north end of the SuperTarget in Greenwood.  So, there was plenty of parking and I headed on in.    I was immediately welcomed to the store by the staff and told that they would gladly answer any questions and gave me a general overview of where to find items.  I decided to browse and got the sense that this place focuses on canines, but does carry some feline products as well.  I didn't see much for more exotic animals or fish/birds.  The products you find here are not the kind you find at the large chain stores/or groceries.  I hadn't heard of any of the items, but could generally  pick up what the purpose of the items were (treats, wet food, dry food, chewies, etc.)  My impression was that most of the items were either less processed products or contained less chemicals and additives than other brands.  I thought they had a wide supply of items to choose from and even had a display of dog bakery items that were decorated like cakes and cookies.  I did pick up a few things to try and see if my dogs would like them and the clerk mentioned that they had a money back guarantee.  She said that even a partially used can could be returned and they would donate the food to a local shelter.  Very cool idea!  The prices are higher than I usually pay, but not so outrageous that it kept me from picking out some items for treats and to try.  Based upon my dogs' reactions, they found the food items to be great!  Review #2180

This 100+ year family business makes authentic German sausages, lunch meats, and other meat cuts using no preservatives and generally, giving you a great start for your meals.  I hadn't been here in a long time, so while driving by on Shelby, I decided to stop in and pick up some Bratwurst for dinner.  Inside, the store is a little dark and the meat counter runs the entire length of the space.  On the left are the meat cuts, with the sausages in the middle and the lunch meats on the right.  Shelves of canned goods like pickles and sauerkraut are located behind the counter and you simply ask for them.  I waited a short time while the butcher helped other customers but soon, I was ready to order.  I went with the bratwurst.  These are real, unsmoked links that are made from pork and veal.  I asked the butcher for recommendations on how to prepare them without a grill and he offered suggestions for cooking as well as sides!  The brats aren't smoked, so they retain their off white color (not brown like in some stores.)  They are so light that even the large links (7-8 inches long) weren't that filling.  They had a puffy texture that is so different from a lot of other sausages.  I suggest that you may want to brush up on what they have by going to their website ahead of time and then looking up what ingredients are in each type of lunch meat.  I had never heard of most of them, so I passed on ordering any of them this visit.  They do look tasty though!  If you want authentic, high quality meats for you dinner or next party, check out this spot!  Feel free to speak in German!  Review #3432

I read the reviews of this bakery opening not too far away from me, so on a Saturday morning, I stopped by.  There was a convenient parking lot across the street and as I approached, I could see the place was already filled with people dining in both sides of the business.  As I entered, there was a menu over the counter and two display cases:  the one on the left featured the cookies, macarons, brownies, etc.; the center one had tower displays of croissants.  Before I had a chance to look through everything, it was my turn to order.  After making the decision to eat in or carry out, I started making my selections.  As it was later in the morning, I went for the savory Ham & Cheese croissant.  So delicious!  nice and flaky outside with a deep buttery taste inside.  The ham was placed all on one end which made my first few bites just croissant with a bit of cheese.  Still, it was good.  And when I got to the ham, it went to another level.  It tasted like the ham was seasoned (maybe a bit of rosemary?)  Very good.  I also picked up a Honey Almond Croissant.  I only got a little of that but my wife assures me that it was really good too!  She thought the almonds were perfectly toasted.  I wanted to pick up some macarons as well, so I went with one Hazelnut and one Lavender.  They were much larger than I've found elsewhere.  They measured nearly 2.5" across and were stuffed with a creamy filling to be about 1.25" deep.  Fresh and packed with flavor, the macaron dissolves as you eat it.  I noted that the Lavender particularly had a floral flavor punch.  I didn't try any of the coffee available.  They do carry Tinker Co brand, so I am sure it is good.  Overall, the service was friendly and efficient.  Note that this is a bakery, not a donut shop.  The pricing reflects the artistry that goes into making each item, so expect to pay more.  If you are okay with that, then you will have a great time tasting the items you purchase.  The hard part is trying to figure out which ones to select.  Review #1149

I normally don't shop in the Kroger shopping center, but my wife let me know there was this pet store and so I made a point of stopping in.  Plenty of parking in the lot and the store was a lot bigger than I imagined.  The first thing I noticed was how large the aisles were.  Stacked from floor to above head height with lots of options.  They also have room for some stands where seasonal toys were for sale.  I couldn't resist a squeaky snowman head that was small enough for my mini pin to pick up easily (she loves it!).  Towards the back is a pet wash station that could be helpful if your dog wasn't too dirty to load into your car in the first place.    They also have aisles for cats, fish, birds, and critters.  The fish tanks were clean and the fish looked healthy.  The snakes and lizards were mostly inactive, but that's expected.  The clerk at the front of the store that manned the cashier's table was pleasant and offered to help me find anything I might be looking for.  He also asked specifically about my pet which was a nice touch.  I liked that they carried a lot of options in a wide band of prices.  I am particularly fond of a specific type of treat which my dog loves and though it is pricey, she is small and the treats last a long time.  Overall, a good place to get that something special for your pet.  Review #3436

Very nice upscale bar/restaurant with pleasant and helpful staff at this new location in Fishers District (the Yard).  Located just east of Ikea Way, we had no trouble seeing the bar or finding parking.  We were greeted at the entrance by several staff at the host desk where we received information about the layout including where the restrooms were located.  After being seated, our waiter Gabriel brought a carafe of chilled water and poured for us.  He then took our beverage orders.  I went with a delicious "The Godfather" cocktail  made with scotch, amaretto, and Luxardo liqueur.  Excellent!  We soon ordered our lunch.  My wife ordered the Wagyu Steakburger and fries.  I went with a lunch combo called "The Director" which has a couple sliders, mac and cheese, and Caesar salad (my choice of option).  While we waited for our meal, I looked around the bar.  There is a private room near the entrance that can be reserved.  To the left of the bar are a couple of alcoves for folks just here for cocktails.  One was very informal.  The other had a long table for a group.  Beyond the bar, a patio was enclosed for the winter but should open up in nicer weather.  There are heaters for cool days.  Although the restaurant was moderately busy, our food seemed to take about a half hour to arrive.  I was hoping that my salad would arrive first, but because it was part of a lunch package, it arrived at the same time as the rest of my meal.  By the time I finished it, the other items had started to cool.    The sliders were quite small with a  piece of unadorned steak inside.  I used a bit of the dressing from my salad to add more flavor.  The mac was tender but the flavor was mild, not much depth.    My wife liked her burger she ordered medium.  It was just a bit dry even though Wagyu has a high fat content.  The fries were disappointingly cool and chewy.  I hope they dial that in soon.  We decided to share a really yummy blueberry bread pudding that comes with whipped cream and vanilla ice cream.  Very good!  Overall, the place has a great look and service was fantastic.  The kitchen just needs to match the same level to justify the prices.    Note that though the place is upscale, many visitors were dressed casually.  Review #3408

I have breakfast before I head out to explore each day, so donuts are more of a treat for me than a meal.  In fact, I rarely eat donuts; but I do know flavor and I really enjoyed each of the ones I bought at Jack's.  Why you may want to go here:  1.  They accept credit cards here so you don't have to stop at a bank machine to have enough cash like at Long's.  2.  Although I didn't use it, they have a drive through lane so you don't have to get out of your car.  3. They have a wide variety of donuts.  Even within categories, they may have some filled with raspberry jelly, Bavarian creme, or sweet white fluffy filling.   4. They offer some powdered, some flaky, some drizzled or spread with chocolate.  5.  The apple fritter I picked up was so good, that I got maybe two bites before my wife finished it off.  She normally likes yeast donuts, but she tore into that one and made it disappear like magic!  6.  They have indoor seating and offer some beverages to go with your order.  7.  They had several folks working behind the counter (one kept restocking the front order counter). Very pleasant and patient with customers.  8.  Very reasonably priced.  I got all four of my selections for under $5.  For anyone who complains about these being too expensive, try making them at home and you will find out that the price is very reasonable.   9.  All the stuffed donuts were filled almost end to end.  I am so tired of other places that put a glob of filling in one end leaving the other end empty.  Not here!    10.  Even if you decide to stop in, there is plenty of free parking outside the shop.  And that's why I liked picking up donuts here!  Review #3704

Every time I enter a record shop, I debate within my mind whether to get back into vinyl or simply stay with cd's or streaming.  It's nice to know that at Luna Music, you don't have to choose between cd's or vinyl...they have both!  And the collection here isn't just the pop stars of the moment.  They had a wide variety of artists here...maybe not every record in the discography, but a solid representation of the artist's work.  Most of the previously unused (I find it hard to call a 40 year old record "New") vinyl that I checked out were running in the mid $20s range.  The used items, which are separated (yea!) are considerably lower.  It looks like this place stays in touch with the local music scene as well, so that's another bonus for stopping by.  Parking is a little hit or miss with reliance upon street parking (south side of 52nd to the west of College is where I found free parking.)  You can turn around on one of the side streets to head the right direction if needed.  Friendly greeting but otherwise, you are free to browse without hovering.  Review #3639

This relatively new coffee shop on east 46th is part of the Patachou Foundation building (a group that is fighting hunger, especially in children in the Indy area.)  There is a small lot and some parking along the driveway on the north side of the building.  The entrance is on the northwest side of the building.  As you step in, the order counter is to your left and limited seating is to your right.  The counter serves as the workstation for the employees to prepare your coffee/beverage as well as a display for a limited number of pastries, salads/fruits, and bottled beverages.    I was greeted and made my selection at the counter.  After ordering, I paid and selected a seat along the wall.  My coffee (house blend) was ready immediately and I was delighted to find I could sip it right away since I had also ordered a slice of pumpkin bread.  The staff offered to heat the bread slice for me and delivered it to my seat.  Something about the combo of hot coffee and pastry makes both seem better!  I will say that the space is really small and though cleanly designed, there are lots of hard surfaces for sound to bounce off.  An occasionally shrieking child hastened my departure so I grabbed my plate/napkin and bused them to an area near the entrance.  Good food, good coffee, and friendly staff made for a positive experience.    Review #3469

Tucked away in a strip mall, this two roomed Mexican restaurant provided a quick and tasty lunch.  Upon entering the restaurant, the lobby has two doors.  The one on the left appears to be more overflow seating while the one on the right, which I chose, allowed me to be greeted and seated upon entering.  Service was good throughout the meal as I was quickly brought my water and utensils and had my order taken.    Complementary salsa and chips were provided.  The bowl of salsa was wide so that the large chips could easily scoop the salsa.  The salsa was smooth in texture but still had a nice flavor.  The chips were fresh and crisp.  After a short wait, my Burrito de Chile Colorado arrived with my choice of rice (beans also available.)  The cubed beef tips were tender and covered in a special sauce and cheese.  Really good!  The rice was also tasty, not dry like some places.  When finished, I was brought my check and paid at the front counter.  Review #3641

If this place tries as hard once they are officially open as they did during today's soft opening, they are bound to have a winner!  I stopped by for lunch right as they were opening.  I had grabbed one of the free street parking spots along Talbott Street, but found that the restaurant/bar has half the parking lot across the street for their customers to use too!    Inside, there is a hostess desk where you check in to be seated.  They have garage doors that open and let you be seated on their partially covered patio.  They also have bar seating and plenty of indoor dining at 4-top tables.  I was seated by the front windows and was greeted by my waitress who let me know that if I had any questions, to be sure to ask.  The place has a 3 way liquor license, so they have a variety of beers, wines, and cocktails available.  They also have milkshakes and Boozy Milkshakes where they pair liquor with the milkshakes.  Just let them know what flavor booze you like and they will help you find the best combo.  As far as the food menu goes, they don't have a huge selection, but they have some signature items as well as a build your burger option, broasted chickens (half and whole) and salads.  I went with the Strut Burger and a side order of fries.  The fries were plentiful and shoestring style.  Hot, with a bit of crispness/crunch.  If they were seasoned, it was very lightly.  They do have shakers and condiments on each table.  You can also get the fries loaded with sauces/toppings for an upcharge.  The Strut burger comes with two smashed thin burger patties, smoked gouda cheese, bacon, dill pickles, mango chutney, and something called "Dazzle Sauce".  In all, it was a nice blend of savory, salt, and sweet.  I also ordered a strawberry milkshake (without booze) and was surprised at first that it wasn't pink.  No artificial coloring added here.  And the flavor?  It was delicious!  I also like that they include a thick straw (like one you would use for boba).  Highly recommended!  This isn't a cheap restaurant that folks will swing by like a fast food place.   They do have a kids menu that runs in the $7-8 range, that includes a burger/chicken/mac 'n cheese, a side of choice, and a beverage.  But keep in mind that they do use quality ingredients.  There is a buzz growing in the neighborhood with Shoefly, Teas Me Cafe, and Loco in proximity.  Maybe this is one of those places that will continue to build in popularity.  Review #3062

I really enjoyed this new concept in dining:  Combine a Hoosier favorite (deep fried chicken and fries) with food that is prepared Halal to create a "gateway" into the world of food that uses tandoori and masala flavors.  I get that some people want "authenticity" and that's fine if you have a built in market for that.  But how do you create a market if it doesn't exist?  Give people something that will take the fear out of trying something new!  Brought to you by the family that runs Chapati (check them out too!) and Shani's Fashion Boutique and Salon, it looks like they have another potential hit with this place.  During my visit (Feb '19), they are in a soft opening with their food set, but the transformation of their space is still in progress.  So, they still don't have a sign up out front which can be confusing.  Simply walk into Chapati and either ask where Shani's is, or go through the door on the right wall that leads into the space.  They currently only have evening hours, but once fully open, will expand to lunch too!    We met the owner who was very enthusiastic and friendly.  He took time to show us around and explain his vision for the place while we waited on our food.  There are a few places to sit during this phase, or you can sit over in Chapati's finished space if you like.    The menu is pretty simple:  You can get individual selections of deep fried chicken legs and thighs, boneless tenders, or a chicken sandwich.  You can specify if you want the "Classic" (regular Hoosier flavor), Tandoori, Spicy, or Faridi which has a family blend of spices.  You can also get Masala Fries (crisper and another family spice blend), Malai Bomb (deep fried potato mozzarella cheese balls), or the Garlic Cheese Naan as sides.  Pretty simple and quick to order and the wait is short.  My wife who is not a fan of food that uses curry or "exotic" spices was talked into trying the food with me, but she is a good sport and ordered the Classic Chicken Sandwich.  It comes served on a naan bun which she thought was a nice touch.  Tasty flavor when combined with the lettuce/pickle/mayo.  Maybe a touch over cooked, but I thought it tasted fine.  We shared the Garlic Cheese Naan which I would say is a MUST TRY!  It looks like a small thin crust cheese pizza (it fills a large 'to go' box), but uses a soft naan bread for the crust and is loaded with gooey (in the best sense of the word) mozzarella cheese.  You get a spicy sweet and sour sauce that packs a bit of heat to dip your naan in.  They slice it in long strips that I would suggest making one more cut across the center to make them more manageable.  The flavor is SOOO good.  My wife, who doesn't like spicy heat even tried it and thought the savory cheese and naan flavors tempered the heat to where she was glad to share the naan with me.  I went with the Tandoori style leg and thigh with the Masala Fries.  At first, I thought I got the wrong order.  It looked just like Classic fried chicken.  But when I bit into it, I could see the outer layer of the chicken under the breading had the expected reddish color where the spices were.  As you might guess, the flavor was somewhere between the two styles so that it would make a good transitional option for folks new to the flavors. The chicken was tender and moist inside, crunchy on the outside...just about as good as you could hope for!  The Masala fries are more crisp than the standard fries you get most places.  They don't offer a plain fry option since they are afraid they will seem tasteless compared to the other food, so they only offer fries with their family blend of spices.  The spices are mild but after you eat all of them, you will become more aware of the flavors.  The only suggestion I would make is that they need to watch temperatures/order size so that all of the fries are cooked uniformly.  Very good!  If you like supporting local and exploring new businesses, make a point to swing by and give this place a try.  You can even bring friends who aren't willing to try new flavors...but they might surprise you when they take a bite of yours!  Review #2224

I had an enjoyable lunch at this strip mall restaurant.   I went in for a late lunch on Sunday and after waiting a short while for the hostess/cashier to ring out some finished customers, I was taken back to a seat in the main dining area.  The room had a number of bench seats with oversize tables in the middle row for larger groups.  A number of televisions were going with the sound down so I was able to catch action and scores on one of them during football season.  The interior is kind of odd...a log cabin style decor on the walls and a rustic old west look to the rest of the interior looked out of place for a Mexican restaurant and with multiple tv's.  However, I was there for the food.  And the food was really good!  I got the complementary salsa (in a small decanter) and chips while waiting for my order of the Quesadilla el Potro.  This huge meal had a 10 inch tortilla filled with steak, chicken, and chorizo, with bell pepper, onion, and tomatoes.  Even folded, it took over half the plate!  On the side was a colorful array of fresh veggies and sour cream.  (Note that cheese is available for a small upcharge.)  The flavor was really delicious and the veggies inside the tortilla were al dente, not mush.  Nice sweetness to the peppers and onions.  The only negative on the food is that the plate was so full, it was hard to slice the tortilla without spilling the veggies off the side.  The veggies themselves could probably have been cut a little smaller, particularly the lettuce, but fortunately, a table knife comes with the dish so I made quick work of making everything bite-sized.  The hostess was pleasant and efficient, but the service once seated was a little on the inattentive side.  Although friendly, I didn't get offered a water refill, I had to wait for him to make his way back to my area of the restaurant to flag him down to get my bill.  Also, the lady who was busing the tables walked by a couple times without removing the finished dishes I had neatly stacked along the side of the table.  Little things, but other restaurants have done a better job of taking care of the service side.  (And they weren't that busy at 2:30 in the afternoon.)  So, if you aren't in a hurry and are looking for some tasty Mexican options other than fast food, give this restaurant a try.  It's easy to find just north of US 40 at Perry Road.  Rev #382

This is one of the newest CVS pharmacies in the city.  Located on the corner of South and Delaware, you can park on the north side of the building (off Delaware) or pull into the drive thru (off South).  Note that current construction on South Street limits you to pulling in from westbound only.  The entrance is on the northeast side of the building.  Inside, the space is clean and filled with rows of pharmacy items as well as some convenience store items where you can pick up seasonal items (yes, both Christmas and Halloween items are on display).  There are grocery items as well including breakfast cereal that I hadn't seen elsewhere.  I didn't use the pharmacy, so I can't really comment on that.  I assume they are comparable to other CVS locations.  One thing of fun to be aware of if you visit is that there are a couple cool murals on the outside of the building (see separate reviews for details).  One is an instagram worthy butterfly wings on the east side while there is a shadowbox of giant butterflies on the south side.  Review #3314

I made my way downtown to this new crepe franchise located on the first block east of Meridian on the north side of Washington Street.  It shares the space with two other places:  Citybytes Cafe which is upstairs and Wei Ramen which occupies the back half of the first floor.  T-Swirl is located at the front of the building with the order counter to the left of the aisle leading back.  The order counter has flyers for seeing all the options which I found easier to look at than the overhead screens.  Once you decide what you wish to order, you pay at the counter and wait for the crepe to be made for you.  They can only make two crepes at a time, so wait times will be dependent upon how many folks are ahead of you in line.  Fortunately, my wait time was minimal since only one order was ahead of mine.  There were 14 types of Sweet Crepes available to select from plus a Brulee option and Chocolate option where you get to select the fruit you wish to add.  There are also 12 Savory Crepes to choose from if you want something more meal than dessert.  They also have salads, teas, and slushes available.  I ordered a Caramel Fuji Apple Crepe (#4) that comes with caramelized apple slices, raisins, custard cream, whipped yogurt, caramel, and granola.  Wow!  It was so good!  You can dine in or choose to get it to go.  They offer tear away sleeves for  the crepes which are rolled into a conical shape.  They also have fitted plastic bags with handy handles for carrying them without spilling the contents.    Parking is always a challenge and requires some fee.  I chose to park in the Circle Centre Mall ($3 for a few hours) and walk over to the location.  Hopefully, folks already downtown will choose to try this (these) shop(s) and enjoy some delicious Japanese crepes for a change to their routine.  Review #3650

Somehow, I missed the opening of this independently owned franchise of an Indiana pizzeria chain.  Let me say I was glad to see it since I have enjoyed every dining experience at the other franchises including 16th street, Broad Ripple, and in Franklin.    I don't know that Mooresville needed or had enough demand for another pizza place with multiple options in the area, including sharing the same parking lot with another independent on the other side of the movie theater.  We called ahead and got a time estimate and while my wife waited outside, I entered (mask on) and let them know I was there.  They were slicing my order in the back and brought out my pizza and my side order of garlic breadsticks in about a minute.  While inside, I noticed a small game room to my left not being used with a few games in fairly close proximity to one another.  Beyond the game room on the left was also the order/payment counter separated by a half wall from the indoor seating.  The place appeared clean and the tables appeared to have plenty of space between them.  Because it was only about 4 p.m., the place was empty until another customer arrived to place an order just before I left.    I asked and at the time of my visit, the man behind the counter said they were seating well over 50% capacity comfortably.  Note that I did not see any wait staff on duty at that early hour, so I can't say they have full service, but since I wasn't sure if we were going to be able to be seated inside, I didn't ask.  We simply placed our order ahead of time and gave them our name when I entered.  The man from the kitchen  brought out my order when it was ready and said my name before I received my order.    The place is set up for indoor dining, but due to being a new place and opening during the pandemic, I am not sure about the availability and any time constraints upon when full service may be available.  I did note that they have a decent amount of local craft beers available on site, but did not order any of those.  (see photo for what they had on hand.)  The food was fine.  It seemed like the pepperoni was spicier (hotter) than I remember having before.  My wife thought it too spicy.  The ingredients were generously portioned, the cheese had my favorite qualities of not being bland and too chewy.  Instead, the cheese had a nice pull to it without being that irritating kind that seems stringing.  I enjoyed the pizza since I don't mind the spicier heat.  I will say we were a bit disappointed with the breadsticks though.  The smaller and crisper breadsticks we received were doused in garlic butter which made it impossible to avoid getting the garlic smell on our fingers when eating.  The breadsticks come with a choice of a marinara dipping sauce or a nacho cheese that had a small amount of heat (but again, my wife wasn't a fan.)  You can get both sauces for an additional $.99.  The service was fine (though napkins would have been nice to have been offered because we wanted to try a breadstick before heading home to eat.)  The overall quality was good, but with so many choices in the area, I'm not sure what will bring me back to this location other than convenience and maybe a beer.  I think I may check them out at another date to try some of their lunch options/sandwiches/strombolis/salads.  Review #3825

The people who work here are welcoming and friendly.  My cocktail was tasty and a really good value.  The sandwich, a PB&J had a delightful mix of flavors that included some items that made my wife question why I ordered it (but I liked it.)  So why not five stars?  It's because I can't quite figure out what this place wants to be.  I've read the reviews and the interviews with the owner, and it just doesn't fit.  The owner wants to be inclusive and affordable and is tired of the "foodie" craze that makes food too unapproachable and too expensive.  Yet who puts pickles and arugula on a PB&J?  Isn't that catering to the foodie?  Surely that isn't for everyone.  It's supposed to be standard pub grub but with an Indian twist.  Isn't that foodie?  Having lived through decades of bland offerings in the city, I am personally glad that there are foodie options for those of us who are tired of chain food and like new flavor combinations.  I enjoyed the ones I had here, too, so I simply don't understand the POV.  And the name of the place is Jailbird (based upon a Kurt Vonnegut novel) and does have a whimsical prison themed mural on the wall, but the rest of the bar is a weird collection of items that make it hard to figure out what they are going for.  There's a flag in one corner, a game lounge with a hand made rug and plants in another (very 70's vibe), and just a bunch of items that don't seem to go together.  It's just stuff.  I don't get what the connection is to the name.  Bottom line is that the food and drinks are affordable.  They don't carry ANY craft beers which is a shame.  The grub food of hot dogs, hamburgers, and some unusual sandwiches may be good, but nothing that would make it a regular food selection.  It will be interesting to see if it draws in the target group it claims to appeal to.  Review #2617

I've been by this place many times but it always seemed to be closed.  I finally noticed it open on a Saturday afternoon and decided to stop by.    The place is smaller than I expected with the space being divided into a front and back room with the purchase counter about midway in the store.  What made an immediate impression was that there was a lot of glassware/ceramics in the front end of the shop.  There were also some ornate furniture, but just a few pieces.  The back half of the store was more of an assortment of items, with pricing seeming a bit high for the condition of the items.  The clerk was engaged in a general conversation with one of the other customers during my visit, so I can't say that there was any interaction during my visit.    Like a lot of antique places, if they have what you are looking for, you will have a higher affinity for the place than if they don't.  I didn't see anything that jumped out at me to consider making a purchase.  Review #3293

When I try to go to my local butcher shop in Mooresville, there are lines of people waiting with nobody looking at the boring and somewhat grimy grocery store.  What a difference when I stopped in at Moody's!  No lines, no waiting, lots of options, and so much cool stuff to browse through even if there was a rush on the butcher/deli counter.  The store is clean and bright.  The displays are orderly and along the wall near the street entrance is a cooler filled with cheeses and packaged sausages/meats.  About half way into the shotgun style shop the order counter is on your left along with the full butcher counter filled with fresh cuts of meat.  In the space on the customer side of the counter, there are displays of sauces and canned goods, a local ground coffee display, and a craft beer section.    My wife saw a pair of thick cut pork chops that she couldn't resist (about 1 pound each!)  We will be enjoying those soon in one of her favorite recipes!  Very helpful staff behind the counters and they seemed very knowledgeable of their products.    I also found there are three Moody's scattered around the metro area, so I will have to check out the Avon shop since it is a lot closer to home.  A very pleasant shopping experience and I'm sure I'm going to enjoy the items we purchased.  Review #2200

The restaurant is a basic breakfast/lunch place with the kind of cooking you can do at home with the convenience of eating out.  Since it is billed as a breakfast place, I ordered my "go to" for breakfast:  Eggs Benedict (Traditional Benny).  Whenever I try a new breakfast place, I usually order this because it has a number of good tasting components, but requires some skill to execute (and is a royal pain to fix at home if you want real Hollandaise sauce!)  So after grabbing a spot in a booth near the window, I placed my order and waited.  Before very long, my plate arrived with the diced potatoes I selected as my side.  Overall, the flavor of the Benny was good, but one of the eggs was a bit overcooked and the yolk, when broken, didn't flow.  The other egg was a bit under cooked with some of the egg white not cooked through.  The Canadian Bacon didn't cover the English muffin bottom so that some bites did not have any meat.  The potatoes were unseasoned, but fortunately, each table had shakers for salt and pepper handy.    The server, while friendly, disappeared from the floor for long periods.  My water was not refilled and she never checked back to see if everything on the plate was okay.  So, not exceptional service on my visit.  If I wanted to have a sit down breakfast or lunch, I would consider coming again, but wouldn't think of this as a destination place for dining.  Review #661

I went to see my first movie at a cinema in a long time as the pandemic is stabilizing.  Our group of 3 got our tickets ahead of time which is good because our ideal time was already sold out (just after lunch on a Friday).  The theater was limited to 50% capacity to allow adequate spacing and so we felt comfortable going.  We didn't order any food having just finished lunch and not feeling certain about how much we wanted to risk contact.  We were able to tell our seating and though my wife thought she had ordered something farther back, we ended up sitting in the 2nd row in those super stuffed lounge chairs.  Two of the three seats we were seated in didn't adjust posture and foot rests like they were supposed to, but one of the attendants immediately helped us and got the chairs to work.  Good service!' This visit, we weren't able to go to the IMAX theater, but got the Dolby which definitely added to the experience.  Though I am prone to afternoon naps, especially in a dark environment, the incredible audio which literally shakes the chairs during the action sequences was clear to understand (my wife didn't need her aides to understand!)  We were able to comfortably spend the time in the theater.  It wasn't too hot or cold, but I did keep my sweatshirt on.     The signs for the exits could use better identification as some led directly outside, while some led back to the lobby.  Since it was my first visit, if they could let you know which ones could get you to the lobby without wandering in the near total darkness.  I didn't miss much of the movie while wandering around, but with steps and people having their legs extended, it is not a place you want to turn around and watch the screen while walking.  I made it okay, but it definitely crossed my mind that an improvement could be made.     My wife bought tickets and thought our seats would be higher up than the 2nd row even though the tickets said row B.  As I searched for the exit, I think I did see a second row B above the midway point.  (Probably where we should have grabbed our seats) but it seems odd that they use the same row name for two different rows.  Maybe could have used a double letter designation if they have too many rows for our alphabet.   Oh, well, we still had an enjoyable afternoon and were glad to be able to enjoy it at the movies.  Review #3899

I was looking for a place to try something new when I found Rayan Restaurant & Bakery on Yelp!  Their website mentions Taste of Yemen which was something I had not tried before, so I stopped in for lunch on a Sunday.  Located in a strip mall on the south side of 38th Street (just west of Georgetown Rd), I found convenient parking out front and stepped inside.  There is a large greeting counter with lots of baked goods for sale located just inside the entrance.  The host was friendly and directed me to select my own table since there were numerous four tops and even private dining rooms available.    I was hungry so I decided to start off with an salad like appetizer, the Fattoush with Lemon (mixed lettuce, tomato, cucumber, scallions, parsley, and special dressing topped with crisp pita bread chips.)  I also ordered the Mendi Chicken & Rice which is one of their most popular dishes and serves a 1/2 chicken seasoned and slow roasted with a ton of Mendi Rice.  I also ordered an Adani tea (with milk) and water from the host/waiter.  My order was soon put in and then the host attended taking "to go" orders and greeting more guests as they arrived.  Unfortunately, my water didn't arrive very promptly.  I sat near the back of the restaurant where I could see my food come out of the kitchen to a staging area.  My salad was set down and before long, by entree came out.  One of the staff directed the guy from the kitchen to bring both the salad and entree to my table.  I finally flagged down the host/waiter and he did bring over my water, and eventually, my tea.  Strange sequence for serving and something that could be improved upon.  Anyway, the portions were huge!  The Fattoush was piled high on an oval plate and at first, didn't seem to have much lemon flavor.  There were some lemon slices adorning the dish, so I did add some for a bit of flavor.  What I liked about the dish was that the ratio of greens to veggies was very balanced with lots of tomato and cucumbers.  The taste of parsley was very pronounced, so I would say order this if you like that herb.  As I worked through the salad towards the bottom, I began to notice a stronger tart taste from the lemon.   Not sure if they use just lemon juice or if there is more to their special dressing, but it could have been applied more evenly for a more balanced flavor.  Still, the salad was good and the abundant pita chip crisps added a nice taste to the overall dish.  The entree was very plentiful.  The chicken was so moist and tender that they don't even provide a knife.  I was able to use my fork to break down the chicken (along with an occasional use of my fingers) which was truly amazing.  I can't remember chicken this tender before.  The spice was colorful, but the taste of the seasoning was on the mild side and easy for a Hoosier to adjust to.  The rice was long grain (Basmati?) and took on an orange color from the seasoning.  There must have been 2 1/2 cups of rice on my plate!  Very tasty, but even I couldn't eat it all.  Oh, and if you desire to try the Adani tea, take the "with milk" option.  The tea is extremely sweet and the milk tends to keep you from flying away on a sugar high.  Very tasty and sweet unlike any tea I have ever tasted.  I have a feeling that your enjoyment at this restaurant will have a lot to do with the choices you make.  If you are new to the cuisine, I suggest you play it safe with your choices like I did.  The food tasted fresh, even though it was obvious that the chicken had to be roasted for quite awhile before my arrival.  The salad was colorful and the ingredients seemed ripe and crisp.  Overall, it was enjoyable experience.  Review #460

I was heading to a movie and didn't have a lot of time, but I had read the reviews of LaSpada's and it sounded like I could pick up a couple slices of pizza fairly quickly.  So glad I did!  The restaurant itself is in a one story renovated shop that doesn't catch your eye right away, but does have a large sign on the exterior of the building.  It is on the north side of Washington/US 40/Main St just west of the intersection for Walmart.  There aren't any lines painted on the blacktop in front of the building, but you can park there, or pull around to the back and use the sidewalk between buildings to come in the front.  There are a couple steps to get into the entrance, so the owner hopes that customers don't block the steps when they park.  Inside, there are a few tables, but I sense that the majority of the customers get their orders to go.  The order counter is on your right as you enter and most of the time, the owners will be there to greet you and take your order.  There are menus on the counter that they encourage you to take with you so that you can order ahead of time when you return.  The front of the menu lists a number of specials, while the back lists the individual items including size/quantity and pricing.  I ordered the "Meal Deal" which is two slices of single topping pizza and a 20 oz. chilled bottle of Pepsi product soda.  You can do as I did and get a different topping for each slice.  The owner asked my name and told me the expected wait time would be around 8 minutes.    While I waited, I got to chat with the owner Duane/Dwayne (?) and learned that the couple is from the Buffalo, NY area and had 30+ years in the pizza business with big franchise places before deciding to go into business on their own.  What they have is a Western New York style pizza which is what makes their pizza unique in the Indy market.  Instead of thin crust or thick crust, the crust is somewhere in between for thickness while remaining feather light.  The bottom and side pieces get a little crusty, but that is my wife's favorite part....the crunch.  Otherwise, the house made dough is very light.  The Meal Deal comes with the traditional sauce, but if you are ordering a pizza, you can select one of three types of sauce.  I heard that the average slice was pretty large, but even though I heard 4" x 6", it didn't sink in how much pizza two slices could be until I saw them.  This isn't a meal you will go hungry from.  Good flavor on both types I selected.  The pepperoni fairly covered the top without overlapping the slices.  The spicy Italian sausage slice definitely had a spicy quality to it without being too hot.  Both were good by themselves, so I look forward to trying a combo pizza to see how all the ingredients work together.  While waiting, I also got to try some of the side items:  the logs.  The logs basically take egg roll wrappers, stuff them with goodies, and then seal them and deep fry them like an egg roll.  Inside, the pizza log had mozzarella and pepperoni, with some traditional sauce.  The ham-n-cheese log has ham and cheddar inside.  Again, the sauces for dipping are available for no extra charge.  The owners are always looking for new items to add to the menu, so I even got to try one of their prospective new flavors that they would be adding soon.  All the logs had that tasty crunch (just like an egg roll) but filled with nice sandwich ingredients.  One last thing....the pizzas here are served rectangular, so they use their own terminology on sizing their options.  A "Full Sheet" pizza is large enough for 32 slices!  1/2 sheet and 1/4 sheet options are available in build your own options or in pre-selected combos.  I highly recommend going into the shop to see the sizes before ordering.  The full sheet has more pizza than two 17" round pizzas according to the owner.  Overall, the pizza and sides were yummy and the owners were very pleasant who encourage customers to use the website or call in orders.  They welcome Yelp customers and pay attention to the feedback so that their shop can be the best it can be.  Give them a try!  Review #378

This is the second of the Rise'n Roll Bakeries I've been to in the Indy Metro area.  I'm not even that much of a donut fan, but I make an exception for their Cinnamon Caramel donuts/donut holes that fans have labeled "Amish Crack" because the donuts are so addictive!  And if this place is like the one in Greenwood, wait for the ice cream filled donuts in warm weather!  Parking is okay now, but as more shops in the Fishers District (the Yard) open, you may have to park and walk or even use one of the parking garages that should be opening soon.  Inside the shop, you will notice it is long and narrow and it can get a bit crowded in the aisles.  Not only do they have fresh baked donuts/pastries baked in Northern Indiana and driven down daily, but there are lots of local artisan food related items like candies, popcorn, and jellies too.    While waiting in line, be sure to notice the cool artwork by local (HSE) artist (Ne)Koda Witsken who painted the murals before the grand opening in 2019.  She painted the geometric patterns by the coffee counter and the "Rise and Shine" mural of a horse drawn buggy in a rainbow of colors. (She also did the Mudsock Spirit mural in downtown Fishers!)  Some high quality products as in Greenwood, just a little smaller space that makes it a bit harder to get around when busy.  Review #3603

This place seems to appeal to some people, and to others, not so much.  They did have some unique items and there seemed to be plenty of room to browse for items as well.    I guess the problem is that I found a number of their items to be crass.  Okay, I get an unexpected comment that is off color can have some humor.  But this place is loaded with items that use sexual references or bathroom "humor" to be funny.  I outgrew that about half a lifetime ago, so I didn't see anything I would want to give as a gift to anyone I wanted to keep as a friend.  What is a shame is that it was scattered throughout the store, so it wasn't like I could avoid it.  There were some nice items that I might have considered buying, but didn't on my visit.    Review #1835

Let me start by letting you know that my review is based upon getting some pastries to go.  I didn't stop for a drink or for a brunch type meal.    Much like the sister business in Broad Ripple, this place has incredibly beautiful and tasty pastries that I know I couldn't make at home or find at a place that didn't specialize in baked goods.  I ordered a tiramisu based cake that was moist and tasty.  So good!  I also got a couple other items that were equally appealing, but I am saving them for this morning.  My wife got an almond croissant and reported that it was delicious (I didn't get to try that one either!)    Note that this business does not have a big presence on Pennsylvania Avenue.  Basically, there is a sign on the entrance to let you know where they are.  Just head south on Pennsylvania (one way street) from Washington or Maryland and look for metered parking on the right hand side.  The entrance is across from the Fieldhouse (formerly Bankers Life) located by the entrance to the new hotel and parking garage on Pennsylvania.    There was minimal outdoor seating.  Once inside, we were checked for temperature with their wand. Unfortunately I had worn a hat to keep the sun off my face but the hat trapped the heat and caused me to have an initially high temperature.  I took the hat off and my temp dropped back to normal.  So, be aware of what you wear, especially on days when the heat index is near or over 100.  You may scan as hot.  Fortunately, we had already eaten, but were there just to peruse the pastry counter.  With masks in place, my wife were able to point out the pastries we wanted and my wife paid for them.  I have read other reviews that were pleased with the loud music and vibe, but I don't want that if I am going for brunch.  Late drinks? Okay, but not for brunch.  The walls were bouncing sound all over so it was way too loud for our comfort level.  There were several long tables and though the tables weren't crammed together, it was obvious that the patrons weren't concerned about social distancing.  Looked like an office party to me.    The service on getting our pastries was prompt and helpful with describing what was inside the colorful items.    Note that if you are familiar with the Broad Ripple location, this doesn't feel like the same place. The BR place has a cool vibe that seems authentic and eclectic.  This seems newly purchased to look eclectic.  It does look good, but just lacks some of the charm of the BR location.  Much easier access to this place though!  If you don't mind splurging on something you can't find elsewhere just to make your day, stop by and give the pastries a try.  I'll have to return another day to review their brunch options.  Review #3778

If you like "buying Indiana" and supporting local businesses, then make a point of visiting A Taste of Indiana.  At the time of my visit, the owners of the shop carried products from 180 vendors from around the state.  You can buy these items individually for yourself, or if you like, package them together and send them as a gift using boxes made in Greenfield!  Although you can see the shop from Binford Avenue, you have to pull into the shopping center from a rather nondescript access road on 62nd street, just west of Binford.  Once you find the street, there is plenty of parking out front in the shared lot.  Inside you will find a wide variety of products.  Lots of sweets and snacks including chocolates, cookies, brownies, and popcorn.  There are books, mugs and shot glasses, greeting cards, jams and salsas.  And if you don't find what you're looking for in the small front of the shop, the owner will encourage you to browse the shelves of the back room where they do the boxing.  They have rows of items that simply don't fit out front.  The owner was very friendly and knowledgeable about the products and encouraged me to pass along to anyone who reads this that if they would like their products carried at this shop, to contact him via the website.    The prices tend to run higher for Indiana products than for the mass produced items you may find in the grocery.  But I found the pricing to be reasonable and affordable.  The hardest thing is trying to keep from picking up too much at one time!    I definitely enjoyed my experience here and though it is a long drive from my house, I will make a point to return (or use their website to order items now that I've seen them first hand.)  Review #2139

After seeing a feature on "Indy Style" showing Charbonos had updated their menu, I took my wife for an early Tuesday night dinner.  After being greeted we asked for a table and were seated promptly.  Our server was friendly, but admitted she was fairly new.  So she made a few "rookie" mistakes, but we were able to keep her from rushing off too quickly.    The atmosphere is still rather dark, and although they got rid of those terribly dated artificial vines (yeah!), it looked like most of the decor had remained in place.  Not worn, but not necessarily current.  Along with our drink order, I placed an order for the Heirloom Tomatoes and Burrata.  I had tried something very similar to this appetizer at Sangiovese, so I decided to give the Charbonos version a try.  Absolutely delicious!  This version had less greens, but made up with them by adding numerous toast crostini.  I was able to scoop some burrata onto each slice and place the sliced yellow and red cherry tomatoes on top with a bit of the arugula.  The reduction was sweet and savory and went perfectly with the other flavors.    Of course, we also got the signature bread and dipping oil that Cunningham Dining Group is known for at their Stone Creek/Boulder Creek restaurants.  My wife worked on that while I gobbled the crostini.  For entrees, I was having a hard time deciding, but ended up going with the Scallops, with Parmesan Risotto, zucchini, and tasso ham beurre blanc.  The risotto was fantastic with enough cheese to add flavor to each bite of the risotto and zucchini.  Definitely worth ordering again.  My wife opted for the 12 oz NY Strip since Charbonos doesn't carry the deep fried shrimp she gets at the Stone Creek locations.  She paired the steak with some delicious green beans (not  too crunchy like some places, but not soft and mushy either.  What I would consider ideal!)  She also ordered the sweet potato fries which were coated with a sweetened cinnamon powder.  (She needed a to go box!)  Finally, we split a creme brulee which was chilled so the crust was nice a brittle while the creme was smooth.    If I could give this a 4 1/2 I would, but since there was a bit of improvement that could be done to update the restaurant and with experience, improvement of the service, I will settle for a 4 star rating.  Review #66

I made my way downtown to this new restaurant that bought one of the buildings along the first block east of Meridian on the north side of Washington Street.  It shares the space with two other places:  Citybytes Cafe which is upstairs and T-Swirl Crepes which is right at the front of the building on the main floor.  Finding Wei Ramen is a little confusing, but you simply walk passed the order counter for T-Swirl and you will be greeted by a host/hostess from Wei Ramen who will help you find some seating.  Wei Ramen has full wait service (the other places you order at their respective counters).  I was greeted by my waitress and brought my beverage before ordering.  I started with a pork bun which was really tasty.  The soft steamed bun was folded over sliced pork and some veggies and had a somewhat sweet taste to me.  I simply ate it like a sandwich.  There isn't a lot of meat in the bun, but considering they have to fold it, they are somewhat limited on how much they can fit inside.  I also ordered a Rice Don entree which came with a side salad that was also quite good.  My waitress asked if I needed silverware in addition to the chopsticks which I decided would make eating the salad much easier for my lack of skills.  The Rice Don I selected was a Tempura Shrimp and Veggie option (others are more like stew).  It had close to 2 cups of white rice as a base with some tempura shrimp and a veggie that reminded me of a fried potato wedge.  There was also some cooked white onion and the meal was topped with a fried egg and a drizzled sauce (Eel sauce).  The menu mentioned Kimchi and a half soft boiled egg, but I didn't notice any spicy kimchi and the egg was definitely hard fried on my dish.  Service was quick and attentive.  I was able to talk with the owner and he filled me in that in the near future, you will be able to order food from his shop even if you are sitting in the coffee shop upstairs.  Note that you will have separate checks for each business you order from, not a consolidated one since each business is separately owned.  Good food and service in a tough location for restaurants historically.    Parking is always a challenge and requires some fee.  I chose to park in the Circle Centre Mall ($3 for a few hours) and walk over to the location.  Hopefully, folks already downtown will choose to try this (these) shop(s) and enjoy some tasty Japanese food.  Review #3648

Of the many Yelp Top 50 restaurants that I have visited, One World Market has one of the most unique environments I've experienced.  Half the business is a market for groceries, mostly boxed, canned, or bottled items from Japan/Pacific Rim Asia.  About a quarter of the space is for in-house dining, and the rest is the actual restaurant/food preparation part.  They have quite a few of their food items chilling in a cooler ready for folks on the go.  You can also use their website to order food for take out, or place your order in person and have it made for you, including a "build your own" sushi roll.  If you are a first time visitor as I was, they have paper menus by the cash registers which you can mark with your selection while you wait in line.  I was fortunate and was able to walk right up to the counter though a line quickly formed behind me even at 1 pm.   The cashier was very helpful and helped me find the items on the list that I selected from the big display of menu items hanging over the cooler.  Once the paper menu was marked, I got to take my 10% Yelp discount for checking in.  She wrote my number on my receipt and I went over to the dining area to find a spot.  Since I didn't call ahead, it took about ten to fifteen minutes for my large lunch to be prepared.  They called my number and I carried my food back to my spot.  Note that they don't have waiters, so you help yourself to water or beverages, plastic ware, and bus your own tray when finished.  They even have a microwave for heating any of the entrees that you might pick from the cooler!  I ordered an extra large lunch since I wanted to get a sample of both the sushi side as well as the entree side of the menu.  For my sushi choice, I went with the "Dragon Roll" which came with a side of Miso soup.  The soup was standard with a bit of tofu and green onion.  But the sushi was jaw-dropping!  The roll was huge and was shaped to look like a dragon!  It even had horns and a neck frill!  What was most amazing was that unlike most sushi I have had elsewhere, this dragon had an eel fillet positioned across the back of the rolled rice/crab stick/ avocado!  The fillet was covered with eel sauce to give it a sweet/salty/savory flavor.  I was impressed by artistry and the flavor.  Note, that if you have any trepidation about eating eel, you might want to try it someplace else where the fish isn't so prominent.  But I give credit to OWM for being bold and giving the roll a generous portion!  The only negative for me was the extra height of the roll due to the layer of fish on top made for a big bite!  Some of the pieces were cut especially thick, as well, and that made me contemplate cutting the roll.  Fortunately, I was dining alone and didn't feel too embarrassed by stuffing the over-sized pieces into my maw.  I also ordered the Tempura Udon. This meal consisted of a large shrimp tempura, a bowl of savory soup with a generous portion of Udon (fat round noodles), and a couple slices of fish cake.  (I wasn't sure what these slices were, but used the menu description and the process of elimination to figure it out.)  The Udon noodles were long and because they were thick, they didn't wrap around my fork very well.  Since the noodles were floating in the broth, I ended up getting a few splatters of broth as I tried lifting the fork to my mouth.  I don't know if there is a proper way to eat them, but I advise having a few extra napkins on your lap if you eat like I did.  The flavor of the noodles and broth (and even the fish cake slices) were really good.  The texture of the Udon was a bit spongy, more than spaghetti, but less than gummy bears.    The tempura shrimp (singular) was light and crisply breaded.  I didn't use any sauce or condiments for dipping.  They do have soy sauce on the tables and additional seasoning at the the self service area for supplies.  Since I bought the Udon meal, I also got a choice of a California roll or a dessert option called Inari.  I opted for the Inari which is a fried tofu pouch filled with sticky rice.  It has a sweet taste and doesn't really need any additional sauces.  It is served hot, but cools rather quickly, so you might want to take a bite early instead of waiting to the end of your meal.  (I was given two Inari on my plate.)  The staff seemed very friendly and helpful, but once I left the counter, there wasn't much interaction.  They realize this, so when I got my bill, there wasn't a place designated for tipping.  Overall, it was a pleasant experience with good food.  Just not the kind of place if you want to be waited upon.  Review #388

I had seen this giant warehouse advertising antiques many times over the years, but it wasn't until my wife was watching a segment of Inside INdiana Business with me and saw Brittany S's segment on Destination Shopping that my wife suggested we go.  After grabbing a bite to eat at Tavern on the Point, we headed over.  Pro tip:  Approach the business from the east and enter the parking lot from Michigan Road.  If you are any other direction, go east on New York, north on Dorman, and then west on Michigan to enter.  Otherwise, lots of one way streets in the area can make it frustrating to find.  Although the building has three stories, only the first two are open to the public (Sep 2019).  We absolutely loved the main floor, but felt the second floor lacked the quality of the first.  So, if time is limited, explore the main floor.  There is no theme for arrangement of items, just a series of booths or display cases.  And there is no pattern to follow to navigate all the shops.  So hopefully, you have a good sense of where you have been and approach the exploration with some sense of order.  Otherwise, you can wander around all the separate rooms and diagonal booths and duplicate or worse, miss out on some places.
