We were surprised at how much quality furniture and fixtures were available.  Most were very reasonably priced.  Kudos to the vendors for making that decision.  I know if I decide to pick out some antiques, this will be on my "must look" places to visit.  There are some original art pieces too.  I found some of them to be quite interesting.  There are also vinyl records, comic books (way over priced for the condition), and prints/posters that were cool if you had a themed room to decorate.  Access is limited since there are stairs to get in and go up to the second floor.  Restrooms are available on the first floor and water fountains are on both floors if you spend a lot of time shopping/browsing.  I enjoyed looking at the items and though I didn't make any purchases, I would return to see what new items had arrived.  Review #2992

Four of us made our first visit to Hyde Park during the Devour Indy promotion.  What we encountered was delicious food, excellent service, and a pleasant dining environment.  What else do you need? (okay, parking would be nice, but they do offer valet service and Circle Centre Mall isn't too far to walk.)    Although we were pretty sure all of us were going to order filet mignon from the Devour Menu, we listened to the specials and recommendations of our waiter.  What was apparent was that if we stuck to the special 3 course meal, we would be saving a lot of money while still getting to experience this 5 star restaurant.    Even though we did stick to our decision, we opted to add a Wagyu Beef Carpaccio starter served with peccorino romano cheese and greens and a couple biscotti.  I ended up making mine into a sandwich while my fellow diners used more gracious table manners eating their appetizer components individually.  Excellent, especially with the flavor from the capers managing to add a bit of saltiness.    When we discussed our likes, we made reference to one of our party not liking seafood which our waiter picked up on.  What we didn't know was that an amuse bouche of carpaccio was planned for the night, so word got back about our order and the kitchen whipped up a unique starter for our table.  Three were a crisp topped with a tuna based bite and a fourth amuse bouche of caprese style tomatoes was put together for the non-seafood guest.  That's service!    A course of bread was next on the list (the staff didn't cut corners just because we were going with the discounted menu options.)  The flavors were good and there was a nice variety, but the soft pretzel was very salty on the top; enough to draw a negative comment from my wife.    We then got our first course.  Two of us went with a lobster bisque which was okay...it had large pieces of lobster, but the flavor of the lobster seemed a little "strong" on the first bite, but seemed milder on subsequent bites.  Maybe the sherry poaching affected the flavor. The others ordered a wedge salad and a Caesar...both got good marks.    All of us decided that the first time to a steak house we should try the steak.  On this occasion, we all went with the filet mignon. One chose to upgrade to a larger size and another went with the crab and asparagus upgrade.  I think everyone ordered medium-rare and enjoyed the tender beef.  The steak came with garlic mashed potatoes and was topped with onion crisps.  We also ordered sharable asparagus and a dish of Brussels Sprouts that were prepared in a bacon marmalade (Wow!  Really great!)  The steaks were very tender and were slightly under seasoned for my taste, but still quite delicious.    For dessert, two of us went with the Cheesecake that had a cherry topping.  The other two went with the flourless chocolate cake that was very dense and rich.  I would recommend sharing one between two people unless you are a complete chocoholic!  Maybe a cup of coffee might help clear the palate between bites of the cake.    The service was excellent throughout the evening.  Besides the waiter checking on us, the manager (who was from Cleveland to train the staff) and the Executive Chef (Braulio Delatorre) stopped by our table during the evening to make sure we were being taken care of.  Their timing was not intrusive on our dining and was appreciated by our group.    Overall, I recommend dining here if you would like a special night out or are independently rich.  They do have a special cut of Wagyu beef that goes for $140 all by itself.  Yikes!  But because the business offered to participate in the Devour Indy promotion, I now know that the food and service are excellent and that quality supports the prices.  Review #217

My wife and I are fans of McNamara since we find many unique items (especially around holidays) in addition to the floral arrangements.  This shop in the Geist area is much smaller than the other McNamaras I have visited.    Though it has a bounty of beautiful bouquets and arrangements, there isn't room to carry as many home decor items that we search for.  But even though the shop is smaller, I can't tell you how much I enjoyed stepping into a room full of color and floral scents...it felt like springtime!  The woman who greeted me was friendly and let me know to take as much time to browse as I wanted and that she would be there to assist if I had any questions.  Nice!  Although smaller, this is still a fine addition to the McNamara name.  Review #3673

On an early summer evening with a nice breeze, we brought our friends with us for their first visit to Mama's.  We opted for seating in the beautiful shaded garden on the south side of the restaurant.  The garden is filled with reddish orange table umbrellas, statues, and a gazebo.  Frank Sinatra music was playing in the background but never interfered with conversation.    After a round of cocktails/wine and a bread course, we decided to try sharing a couple of the appetizers.  The Sicilian Asparagus patties were roughly shaped like hamburgers, but were filled with a wonderful blend of flavors:  grilled diced aspargus, egg, parmesan, and bread crumbs.  These were topped with a lemon aioli and marinated diced tomatoes.    We also ordered the Fried Fresh Mozzarella which is a ball of cheese stuffed prosciutto and crusted with breadcrumbs before frying.  It comes served atop a balsamic glaze and marinated tomatoes.  Not as complex a flavor as the patties, but still very tasty!  Not to be outdone, our entrees were delicious too!  I selected the tilapia with angel hair pasta.  The fish is breaded with chopped walnuts and herbs and drizzled with blackberry basil sauce (asparagus spears on the side.)  The savory combo of nuts and berries are fantastic with the whitefish.  Highly recommended.  My wife opted for the Chicken Picatta with angel hair pasta.  This comes with the standard lemon and olive oil sauce with capers.  She needed a to go box.  Our guests ordered the Clams with mushrooms over linguine sauteed in butter with herbs, parmesan and a splash of Crown Royal.  Veal Marsala with angel hair pasta was sauteed with prosciutto, fontina cheese, and mushrooms and drew great compliments about how generous the cut of veal was as well as the flavor.  For desserts, the guys ordered the Tiramasu (moist and tasty without the harsh alcohol taste) and the ladies went with the creme brulee.  Nice sugar crust with large berries on top also drew favorable comments.  If you plan to go to Mama's, know that there is limited parking in a lot on the south side of the building.  Early is better than later in the evening if you want to reduce your wait times and weekdays are better than weekends.    There is indoor seating as well, but for us, the indoor dining seems a bit darkly lit.  So, we always time our visits to the summer, watching for days when it won't be too hot and with little chance of rain.  If you are flexible in your schedule, you can have an amazing evening of food and conversation.  Review #337

Come for the free water.  Come back for the cool park to the west of the Artesian Well.  Seriously, I didn't know what to expect at this place as I pulled up.  I had seen the small white building with a few benches while driving by, but had not noticed the shelter and the trail that leads into a wooded area where Cool Creek meanders in an ever changing path.  The path is paved until it reaches a bridge that spans the creek where it bends back on itself.  But once you cross the span, the path is natural and not as friendly for anyone who is physically challenged.  The path wanders in a loop around the trees.  Inside the small white building, there is a circular area where a pipe comes up from the ground and distributes the water to four elbow pipes where you can fill your own containers with the water.  The water currently flows at about 15 gallons per minute.  It's a nice park for relaxing and taking a stroll in the shade.  And remember to bring your own jug!  Review #739

Since my favorite gelato place closed in Fletcher Place last year, I have been hoping to find a place that makes delicious Italian Gelato.  I've found it!  I tried the green apple gelato and the texture was creamy, the flavor tart and sweet, and though I got it to go, I barely made it to my car before I devoured it!    They also have pastries and I got the tiramisu.  It made it home, but didn't last too long.  It was probably the lightest tiramisu I've ever had.  Full of flavor, not too soggy on the bottom, and evenly dusted on top.  Delicious!  Pricing was $2 per scoop of gelato and though the scoops were about a third cup size, the 2 scoop bowl I got was sufficient (but is any amount of ice cream or gelato really enough? Ha!)  The tiramisu was $5.50 which may discourage some folks, but is still less expensive than in the restaurants I've had it.  So, I would say you get your money's worth in taste and satisfaction.  Parking wasn't a problem since this shop is in a strip mall with several rows of parking available.  No reason not to stop by the next time you are in Carmel!  Review #1040

It's with mixed feelings that I write this review:  I was pleased to have finally stopped by to sample the wines at Chateau Thomas only to realize that they will soon be out of business.  The owner of the winery passed away recently and the location was sold to a winery our of Fort Wayne looking to get a foothold in the Indy market.  Soon, the place which is already seeing changes to the exterior of the building and landscaping, will be completely rid of the CTW wines and will replace them with a sweeter mix of wines bottled in Fort Wayne by Country Heritage Winery and Vineyard.  As I pulled into the parking lot, I could see that work was already being done to move the main entrance from the east side of the building to the south.  There will also be a space created for outdoor entertainment which the FW company is big on.  But on my visit, I still entered on the east side and made my way to the gift and tasting room.  I was greeted by one of the men behind the counter who let me know about what was going on with the company.  I was told that if I really liked any wine I sampled in the tasting (at least five for $5), that I should buy them since they wouldn't be making any more and once the paper work on the licensing got done, all the inventory of CTW would be removed and no longer available.  No pressure!  Don't misunderstand, the man was simply letting me know facts, not pushing to make a sale.  Several of their wines were already sold out, but I still had an easy time of finding five wines to select.  Based upon the ones I marked on the order sheet, I was offered complementary tastes of some other wines that he thought I might enjoy.  And he was generally right since two of the bottles I purchased were flavors he recommended.    They also have a few sweet wines, some in jugs.  Those were quite fruity and might make for nice change of pace beverage or something to offer folks who really don't drink much wine and might be turned off by the drier selections.  I picked up a peach Chardonnay that was very fragrant as well as peachy...hardly could taste any alcohol, so it could be dangerous! ha!  So, if you have been before and want to pick up a bottle, now is the time to do it.  If you have never been and have simply put it off, now is the time to go.  Just keep in mind that the prices haven't been reduced, they are simply liquidating the inventory.  Since no firm date is set for the transition, I can't say how soon they will run out or will remove the inventory.  They have good wine.  Stop by and try them for yourself.  Review #2522

If you are looking for a taste of the Caribbean, why not try this Jamaican gem.  There are various types of meats available in sandwich or meal forms.  I opted for the bone-in Jerk Chicken (regular size) that comes with beans and rice, chopped vegetables, and fried plantains.  The wait was around ten minutes from the time I placed my order.   The chicken (mine was a breast and wing) was nestled atop the other ingredients.  Although the skin wasn't as crispy as more American style chicken, it was coated with the dark jerk seasoning and loaded with flavor.  The heat, although not overwhelming, does hit hard with the first bite. Even the rice has a bit of heat to it.  Fortunately, the veggies gave a refreshing alternate flavor to cleanse the palate a little so that my taste buds weren't desensitized.  The plantains were plenty sweet.  The veggies and plantains were small portioned, but there was plenty of rice and beans.  This little shop is tucked away in a corner of a strip mall on the northwest corner of Range Line and City Center Drive (126th).  Plenty of parking, a few tables inside, and a large outdoor seating area make this restaurant very convenient.  Review #311

What a delightful surprise!  Although the place is small and it is difficult to pull in the tiny parking area located directly on 38th Street (just a few blocks east of the fairgrounds), it is well worth the effort the next time you are in the area.  I grabbed the last spot and decided to get my order to go since I didn't want to keep other customers from finding a spot.  (The lot is shared with other businesses too, so I hope they can find a more accessible spot someday!)  The inside is clean and has a small dining room set up which seems like it is mainly a place for customers to wait while their order is being made.  The menu is located on the back wall and there is a small counter with beverages next to the cash register.    The woman behind the counter was very friendly and greeted me and was glad to let me browse the menu until I was ready.  I decided to try the Grilled BBQ Salmon that is shredded, coated with honey and BBQ sauce and grilled with peppers.  It comes served on a normal sized wheat bun.  No sides come with it, but the price was under $6 and I felt like it was a bargain!  Excellent flavors that didn't mask the grilled salmon taste.    Although the menu board didn't have the current list of veggie options, I ended up with ordering a grilled broccoli with mult-colored bell peppers and a variety of seasonings.  That was different from anything else I've had (and I've had a lot!) but it was all good.  I would definitely recommend both the side and the sandwich.  I also picked up a sweet tea which comes without ice.  Not sure why it doesn't have any, but it was chilled and tasty without the ice.  Note that this restaurant does have Muslim books and newspapers on display, much like a lot of Christian restaurants do.  I didn't feel any awkwardness due to the store expressing its views quietly.  No pressure or judgment was noticed.  Good food that exceeded my expectations.  Food takes about 10-15 minutes depending upon what you order and how busy they are.  Most of the items are seafood or veggie based.  Review #2707

Although we drove by it a couple times, we finally found this small restaurant on the south side of US40 just a short distance east of Cumberland.  There isn't any sign by the roadside, so it is easy to miss.  But we were glad we stayed hunting and found it.  I ordered a breaded tenderloin with a side of house slaw that had a tangy flavor too.  The sandwich was thick, not pounded flat and tough.  It was some of the most tender pork I've had (reminded me of my wife's pork steaks, but on a bun.  I ordered my version fully loaded and I could barely fit it in my maw which is pretty large!  I like a bit of yellow mustard and mayo on my sandwich, both were already on it.  Dill pickle, fresh tomato slice, and crisp lettuce too. Just enough yellow onion for a wonderful sandwich.  The only negative was that the bun it was served on became a little soggy and fell apart with some handling.   My wife decided to go with a diagonally cut BLT and some tater tots.  She liked them both, but thought the bacon was cut way too thick and it became chewy, not crisp.  The flavor was fine, but the texture became like jerky, not good for a sandwich. If they fine tune these minor negatives, I think they could have gotten a 5th star from us.  Portion sizes were generous and reasonably priced for the metro area.  Good food, good service, and clean well spaced seating indoors and out.  Give them a try!  Review #925

My wife and I decided to take our eldest grandson to lunch to a restaurant near where he lived on the eastern edge of the Broad Ripple area.  The word Margaritas in the name caught my wife's attention and unfortunately, was the main reason this place which was clean and prompt and had good food failed to get a fifth star.  My wife only likes frozen margaritas, not just over ice.  For some reason, our waitress came back to our table promptly after placing our order to let us know that the margarita ice machine was running slow and would take about ten minutes before the drink would be served.  The waitress asked my wife if she would like anything else while waiting and she ordered a pepsi instead.  Not what you expect from a place with Margaritas in the name.  Anyway, while we waited for our lunch, we were brought out a bowl of large house chips that were tasty and plenty for our group.  We were given two small bowls of salsa that were too small to dip the large chips into without breaking the chips into smaller pieces.  Note that there was no mention of any other flavor or heat levels available for the snacks.  I ordered from the lunch menu and got the lunch chimichanga with grilled sirloin that was really tasty.  I probably could have finished it all in one setting, but decided to get a to go box and not feel stuffed the rest of the afternoon.  Our grandson opted for the burrito supremo and ate most but decided the remainder would make for a nice dinner so he wouldn't have to come up with anything to have to fix.  He's not a great chef though he comes from a line of men who enjoy cooking.  My wife got a Chimichanga Margaritas named after the restaurant (no actual Margarita was included.)  Like me, she decided to save a portion to go so we wouldn't have to come up with anything to fix for dinner either! ha!  Service was good throughout though the angles of the interior would block her from view for periods of dining.  But she was good at her job and never disappeared for very long.  The lunch crowd was fairly sparse so spacing was no problem and we had no safety concerns with masks being required for moving about the restaurant.  If you are looking for a Tex Mex place to get some familiar type food offerings at a reasonable price for the portions, give this place a try.  Plenty of free parking on site.  Review #3882

First, thanks to the restaurant for being open on Labor Day.  I was out exploring the northeast side and was getting hungry.  So glad I used the bookmark feature on Yelp to help me find this place!  And it is easy to find.  Located just south of 82nd Street, there is a convenient stop light at their entrance which takes out the worry of being located on such a busy road just west of the interstate.  Plenty of parking outside in their private lot too, so I grabbed a spot and headed in.  The dining room is large and open.  There were booths along the sides and larger tables in the middle.  I was greeted and seated promptly, brought a glass of ice water and my order of Jasmine tea.    I decided to go with a lunch special ($7.99) that included a spring roll with sweet dipping sauce, soup (warm coconut), and side salad (ginger dressing).  As usual for my first time at a Thai place, I go with the Pad See Ewe to be able to compare it to the other Thai places I've been to.    The soup was brought out almost immediately.  The coconut flavor was somewhat sweet and the temperature was between warm/hot which brought out the flavor while not being so hot that I had to wait.  I could eat it right away.  There were a few small veggies bites in the soup as well though I couldn't see them through the opaque white liquid.  I recognized some other Yelpers in the dining room and as soon as I returned to my booth, my entree arrived.  The spring roll was veggie filled and had a really good flavor with just a hint of heat in the sweet sauce.  It was a little less than crisp, but not soggy.  I assume the steaming veggies inside had something to do with it.  The salad was small and because all the dressing is on top, it is hard to get a balance of dressing and veggies in each bite.  The Pad See Ewe comes with meat and tofu options and also five levels of heat.  Medium was listed as the second heat level from the bottom, so I went with chicken and medium.  The noodles were wide and flat and looked house made.  Cooked just right.  The heat level at medium was immediately noticeable (I could see the red pepper flakes) but though I was aware of the heat, it didn't make my sinuses react.  So for me, that was perfect.  I don't eat to challenge my tolerance levels.  I eat to find wonderful taste and this level allowed me to enjoy the sweet and savory flavors paired with the moist chicken and cooked veggies.  The sauce that the dish covers all the items without becoming heavy and thick.  No pooling.  Just another fine meal from this restaurant that also has a sister business in Plainfield.  Water was topped off and my bill was brought out promptly even though my waiter was tied up serving someone on the other side of the room.    Good food and lots of options for dialing in a meal that suits you.  Review #2953

Wow, I was blown away by the "sip-ability" of these tasty liquors even without making them into cocktails.  I've been to quite a few local distilleries and I have to rate this one right at the top of the list for number of liquors tried to number liked.  I ordered the tasting flight and they bring the flight board out with four of their 8 liquors.  You get a half shot (approx.) of each one on your board (about $8 in early 2021).  I usually don't drink liquor straight or even just over ice, mostly in cocktails.  But on my first visit, I decided to bypass the cocktails offered and went with the flight.  I liked all four that I tried and seriously considered buying more than one, but decided to get just one and then have another reason to return to get more on another day/visit.     At the time of this review, I focused on the vodkas and rums which had lower ABV than some of the notorious rums available commercially.  But if you like to taste the liquor flavors, I highly recommend the flight.  I found all four on my flight to be pleasant for sipping.  No.1 Industry Vodka was a huge surprise at how much I liked it.  There was a bit of sweetness on the finish.  I ended up getting a bottle of no. 7 Botanical Rum made with kola nut, vanilla, a bit of pepper to get your attention, and an oaky finish, but not overpowering the rest of the flavors.  Just really well balanced.  They distill on site so you can look through the windows, but if you want a tour of the process and facility, you have to make a reservation for a Sunday to be sure they can fit you into their schedule.     Not really a place to get anything to eat, so I suggest grabbing lunch somewhere local and then head over here to make the most of your trip to Zionsville.  Review #3901

My wife and I decided to try some of the new restaurants inside the AMP for our lunch.  She was leaning towards getting a Philly Cheese steak, but when she got there some of the breakfast sandwiches caught her attention.  But when she tried to order one, she was told they were only doing lunch sandwiches.  None of the signage indicated limited hours on the breakfast foods and she didn't ask the manager even though it wasn't noon yet.  Some of the breakfast options sounded tasty, so she left disappointed.  Not sure how much she missed the cutoff by, but if you are going to have the breakfast foods listed in the middle of your display, there should be some indication of when they are available.    She was still hungry, so instead of a cheese steak, she went with bacon double cheeseburger instead.  She ate about half and I finished it off for her.  She immediately remarked it didn't taste like bacon, but like a burger and a sausage.  I tried my first bite and thought it tasted like a burger and sliced ham.  Not what either of us expected.  Not sure if there was an east coast spin on the flavor or what, but it just didn't taste like a bacon cheeseburger.  The sandwich was double pattied, so there was plenty there and I know there was bacon, but it didn't look like bacon I'm used to seeing.  So another disappointed customer.   Hopefully they will figure out to put times on their menu board if they are going to limit the selections (or better yet, let the customer order what they want!)  I have read good things about their cheesesteaks (even enjoyed one at the City Market location. but our visit to try this location left us filled, but not satisfied.  Review #3935

If you are a fan of BMB (Big Mouth Burgers) with lots of flavor and maybe a beer or adult beverage to go with it, then give this place a try.  The interior is spacious at lunch time and with an enclosed patio under construction (both heated and cooled), there will be even more room.  Sure, there were long waits during opening week, but we had good service during our visit in the second week.  The restaurant has convenient (shared free) parking in a lot behind the building.  There is a rear entrance with a host area to help you with your carryout order or to find seating which was a minimal wait while the tables were being sanitized.     Sure, you can get burgers here, but my wife opted for a BBQ Pork Nacho appetizer (shareable) as her entree.  She said the pork had just bit of heat, but had a sweet BBQ sauce and was juicy.  Some of the best BBQ she has had in the metro area!  And we've tried quite a few places.  I agree it was right up there though I usually don't get the sweet sauce.  But I was limited to one bite as she didn't want to share!  That's good!   I've been to 5 BRU Burgers and have tried quite a few options, but I had never tried an Impossible burger until this visit.  The have a Hawaiian style burger called Hiki'Ole (Hawaiian for Impossible) burger that was surprisingly similar to beef in texture and when combined with all the other flavors, I thought it remarkably similar to beef in taste.  It comes with a Maple-Chipotle glaze, guacamole, Iceberg lettuce, a a relish of cucumber-mango-pineapple.  The sandwich is stacked high when you add tomato and pickles and because of all the ingredients, it can get a bit sloppy.  You may want to ask for an additional paper napkin to go with you black cloth one since you may need to wipe your face and fingers more often than with other burgers.  Finger licking good, but I try to minimize that during the pandemic.     Our server was perceptive in noticing we were struggling to read the menu on the phone app and she brought us a paper copy of the menu and since we were seated near the bar, I could see the beverage list.  My wife got an Arnold Palmer (tea and lemonade) that she thought one of the best she's had.  I got a Terre Haute brewing Wango Tango IPA which is just one of the many local craft beers available.  (If you are one of those unadventurous types who only drinks commercial (cheap) beer, then they have some options of those too.)     Note that they have some simple burgers, but they are priced a lot more than the fast food places.  I mean what's the point of going to a place that has chefs designing the flavor combinations and you order something like you can make at home?  Live a little and give your tastebuds a treat.  You'll get your money's worth!  No estimate for when the outdoor patio will be ready.  But it looks like it will be nice and I look forward to returning.  Review #3897

For anyone who is a fan of history, writing, and/or life in Indiana, this home is a gold mine of information and cultural artifacts.  What makes this home different from so many other museums is that nearly all of the pieces (incl. furniture, carpeting, dishes, etc) are from the original owners of the house, not just period pieces assembled by some curator.  The opulence of the home is obvious and the home was a key player in social affairs in Indy late in the 1800's. The fact that the "Hoosier Poet" from the "Golden Age" of Hoosier literature lived in one place for nearly a quarter century at the height of his fame makes the stories about the place even richer.  The President of the United States (Harrison) dined here.  Mark Twain (Tom Sawyer), Booth Tarkington (Alice Adams & the Magnificent Ambersons), General Lew Wallace (Ben Hur) and numerous authors dined here.  Any given night might be an occasion for celebration.  The woodwork is stunning.  The baseboard is a foot high.  The doorways in the entry are about 12 feet high in rooms with 14 feet ceilings.  Detailed plaster surrounds the chandelier bases and marble fireplaces in nearly every room turn the functional pieces into artwork.  If you are planning on taking a group, make an inquiry to see if you can have a visit from "Mr Riley" who may read some of his more famous poems.  The actor was a former student of one of our group and we were really impressed with the passion and charm that the presentation added to the experience.   Count on starting with a brief film to start the tour and then moving over to the house.  The only negatives of the tour are that no photographs are allowed inside (postcard photos are available at the end) and that you can only step into each room about three feet.  Although that doesn't allow too many folks to view at one time, our group of four managed to shuffle around and take turns without missing very much.  Parking is free on the north side of the street, so approaching from Park Avenue is ideal.  There are quite a few steep stairs to climb, so keep that in mind if you have difficulty climbing.  Review #221

I like to eat and I've become a decent cook on my own.  So when I go out to eat, I love when a restaurant takes ingredients I am familiar with and puts them in combinations that totally exceed my expectations.  That happened at Gregory's!  I went to dinner on a quiet Tuesday evening.  I've had some home made attempts at Russian cuisine, but never been to an authentic Russian restaurant.  So, I wasn't sure what to expect.  What I found was a relatable selection that made me wonder why I had never thought of the flavor combinations before.  Very approachable food and so much was delicious!  I started with a Baltika No 3 Classic Beer (4.8%).  Though on the pricey side since it is imported from Russia, the nearly full pint bottle was chilled and full of flavor.  Before long, my Pierozki appetizer arrived.  This four piece serving of puffed pastry filled with a combination of minced beef, pork, and chicken was light and flaky.  The pastry was so light that bits of pastry stuck to my lips with each bite.  Inside, the flavor was very subtle and reminded me of the tenderest of meat in a Philly steak.  Subtle at first, my taste buds quickly adjusted to the light seasoning that let the meat flavors work with the buttery taste of the pastry.  I was surprised how light the appetizer was.  I didn't feel stuffed even after eating all four pieces.  Before I finished my appetizer, my entree of Sauteed Beef (Zharkoe Goulash) arrived.  I remember my mom's goulash and it was not very good. So when I took my first bite of this slow cooked beef, onions, and mushrooms in a brown gravy, my expectations were greatly exceeded!  If you order this, definitely dip your fork in the sour cream served on the side.  The bit of tartness in the cream added another layer of flavor to the beef mixture.  Fantastic and fork tender!  I got to pick two sides, so I went with the sauteed veggies and the "carrots in milk sauce".  The veggies were cooked through thoroughly and had a great deal of butter on top.  All the flavors were released and though I sometimes like al dente, I have to admit for the combo of veggies served, the taste was spot on.  Oh, and the carrots in milk sauce were the highlights of the plate.  The long slices of carrots were also cooked thoroughly and served in a sauce that reminded me of condensed sweet cream!  So sweet and delicious, paired with the buttery veggies and savory beef dinner made a meal full of flavors that hit on all the taste buds!  I couldn't pass up on one of the house made desserts.  I opted for the Napolean which was chilled and had just enough chocolate sauce to make this dessert shine.  Highly recommended too!  Since it was early on a weeknight, there wasn't any live entertainment, but because the evening was slow, I enjoyed talking with the owner/hostess/waitress and felt very welcomed.  She pointed out how they grind their own meats, make their own desserts, and try to be as authentic as possible.  Very pleasant conversation and she welcomed that I drove an hour from the southwest side just to try the place.  It's a trip I would and mostly likely will do so again soon!  Review #401 p.s.  There is plenty of parking out front since this restaurant is in an outlet of Castleton Square.  They are also "kid friendly" since there isn't a bar taking up space.

I stopped in after reading numerous articles about the shoppe moving from Greenfield.  This shotgun style business on the north side of Shelby has a great location for people exploring the fountain area of Fountain Square.    When you walk in, there is a wall on the right that is where the owner makes all the chocolates in house.  Pretty cool!  Although there hasn't been much effort to decorate the place, we all know that we are here for the chocolate.    The chocolates are on display towards the back of the shoppe.  There are labels for each variety, most of them giving a fairly good idea of what to expect.  There aren't any prices next to the chocolates, so it is a little awkward if you are concerned about the total bill you may run into if your chocolate-mania takes over.    I haven't sampled many of the chocolates yet, but I think I enjoyed the caramels best.  Very soft and easily melt in your mouth under the crisp chocolate outside.  On my occasion, the almond toffee (served hard crack style) was slightly over roasted for my tastes...not burned by right on the edge.    There are also varieties of truffles that are decoratively finished. I picked up the "Black and White" and the Raspberry.    Although I don't eat chocolates often, I enjoyed stopping in and picking out some tasty pieces.  Review #250

If you can find this restaurant (it's on a little side street south of US 36), the first thing you will notice when you walk inside is the festive atmosphere.  Bright colors everywhere, children with their parents grabbing something to eat, and pinatas hanging from the ceiling all made me feel like I was late joining the party.  Fortunately, they have really tasty frozen strawberry margaritas for those so inclined to catch up!  We had efficient service from our waiter throughout the dinner.  The food also came out of the kitchen quickly, and our bill was brought as soon as we asked for it.  (This is a place where you pay at the checkout near the door instead of at your table.)    I appreciated the huge bowl of chips and second bowl of salsa (all complementary) to start off the dinner.  I also really enjoyed my Burritos Tipicos (beef tips) that came with beans on the side and a guacamole salad on top of the burritos.  The first bite I took was flavorful and had a lot more heat than I expected.  But by the time I got towards the middle (where I was picking up salad and guacamole on my fork as well), the heat seemed to fade.    Not sure if it was just the addition of the greens or if the burritos had more heat at the ends than in the middle.  Good taste either way, but a bit inconsistent.  The only negative was my wife's Burrito Supreme.  It was served rather ingloriously as a bald wrap with some cheese sauce in a cup on the side.  The beans and rice were on a separate plate, so the meal had no visual appeal (unlike my Tipicos which was full of colors.)  I think she got over the appearance rather quickly, but the chicken inside the burrito was totally over cooked and dry.  She tried mixing the cheese sauce to perk up the flavor, but was a bit disappointed wondering if it hadn't been pre-cooked and reheated.  I gave it a try and had to admit that the flavor was disappointing.  So, no five star evening, but still, my wife enjoyed her beverage and I enjoyed my entree.  If not for the dry chicken, I think that we would have felt part of the fiesta!  Review #403

I stopped in for dinner on a Saturday afternoon (4-23-16) on my way home from Brownsburg.  I had enjoyed a dinner at the Dawson's on Main a year or two ago, so I thought I would give this extension a try.  The restaurant is part of a strip mall, so there is plenty of parking.  I chose to sit inside and was taken back into the restaurant.  I noticed that there were some art pieces on the wall, but the atmosphere of the restaurant was stark and rather drab.  It didn't feel like an inviting place to dine.  I ordered a craft beer and the Grilled Shrimp Parmesan with a Ciabatta roll.  The shrimp were large and seemed to be prepared well.  The pasta was okay, but forgettable.  So, I doubt if I would go out of my way to return when I can go to the original Dawson's on Main which is much closer for me.  Review #23

The NCAA Hall of Champions (HoC) is a complementary addition to the White River State Park.  Where the State Museum and Eiteljorg (and nearby Historical Society) focus on cultural and political aspects of our history, the NCAA focuses on the world of physical achievement, highlighting each of the activities governed by the NCAA.  The HoC is very affordable, in fact, it is less expensive than the cost of the parking garage shared with the State Museum & Eiteljorg.  Other parking options are limited unless you wish to street park a few blocks away.  The HoC has two levels.  The first level is a showcase of the 22 sports operated under the guidelines of the NCAA.  The second floor is more interactive.  As you walk through the first level, you are greeted by the "Flying Wedge" installation.  This formation was used in the early days of football when padding was scarce and knowledge of concussions and high impact collisions was more scarce).  It was a contributing factor in the formation of the NCAA which sprang from the concerns of a few visionaries who believed sports should be conducted in a way that allowed participants to excel without taking needless risks.  The rest of the floor highlights each of the sports with an installation with quotes, equipment, photos, and in some cases, video and personal stories about the activity.  Depending upon your interest, you may find yourself spending a few minutes at each location or quite a bit longer if you watch all the film.    There is also a Hall of Fame section and a theater show about achieving the required grades necessary to participate in collegiate athletics.  Throughout the HoC, there are reminders that these are "Student" athletes, in that order.  The second level is supposed to be an interactive section and features equipment for the sports with "ghost figures" of athletes overhead.  I found this section to be a bit disappointing.  Some of the equipment was bolted into place and made it difficult to interact.  There is a gym with a regulation height basket ball rim that allows for free throw attempts.  But because there is only limited room, it is conducive to only a small number of participants at one time.  Be aware that the equipment is unsupervised so that if you bring your kids to the HoC, you are responsible for making sure they understand how the equipment is to be used.    Overall, I learned some things about the NCAA and about some of the other sports that don't get the national attention.  Each endeavor requires dedication and challenges the student to work through obstacles, sometimes as part of a team; sometimes as individuals.  Review #204

From the moment I stepped inside, I felt welcome in this new addition to Mass Ave.  The actual entrance is located on the East Street side of this wedge-shaped building.  There appears to be room for outdoor seating when the weather becomes a bit more stable.  Like all Mass Ave area restaurants, parking is hard to find. However, the experience was worth the hassle.    Since I was dining alone, I opted for seating in the bar where Jacob and Jacob did a fine job of highlighting the offerings in each section of the menu.  In addition to the complementary bread course (served with cultured butter and olive oil) and a large bite (this night's was a bread round topped with an olive and pepper construction), there are selections in a variety of appetizers, small and large plates.    From the "bread culture" section, I decided to go with the Crispy Octopus.  I had only sampled octopus once before, so I thought it would be an excellent opportunity to see if I liked it.  The mollusk was cut into small bits and cooked over a fire giving it an extra layering of flavoring from the searing.  It was served over a slice of country bread (the crust is a bit tough to cut through) and nestled in a bed of chicory topped with a white balsamic vinegar.  The vinegar and chicory paired exceedingly well so that each bite had a rounded flavor.  For those who have never tried octopus, the texture is similar to calamari or a large shrimp.    I passed on the crudo, terrine courses and small plates and jumped right to the large plate selection of Bavette steak with fingerling potatoes and pan sauce.  The steak was seared in a cast iron skillet and then transferred to another skillet for serving so that the steak didn't over cook and removed the risk of searing my own skin!  The steak arrived already sliced and topped with a flavorful garnish (I am guessing minced shallots).  The fingerling potatoes were sliced lengthwise but were easily bite size, or at most, could be speared and eaten in two.  The potatoes were a little under seasoned, so I made sure to use every bit of the topping to enhance the flavor.  The meat was very tender and delicious!  (Note:  not much sauce was visible in the skillet.)    To finish off the evening, I liked that they offered several desserts including locally made "Lick" ice cream.  I selected the Gingersnap and Lemon Curd option.  Wow!  Lots of flavor and a great palate cleanser in one.       The service was friendly and welcoming, and even though the place was getting busier, I didn't wait for any of my courses or getting my bill to check out.  A very pleasant experience throughout!  I can see bringing friends here and trying out the outdoor seating on my next visit.  Review #263

Overall, our dining experience was pretty enjoyable.  Service was very courteous and generally efficient.  Flavors were delightful as well.  Just a few minor things that kept it from being a solid 5 stars.  Our group of three had multi courses for the evening.  Miso soup was a side that came out early and had a nice bean flavor.  Unlike what I expected, but very tasty.   The edamame was a generous portion and came salted just right.  The Beef Rolls, sliced Angus ribeye wrapped around scallions and served with a flavorful sauce had good taste, but the meat was just a bit overcooked.  The Gyoza dumplings came with a sauce of their own that was okay, but not as good as a dark sauce I have had elsewhere.  Also, even though the pork filling was done, the outside wrap didn't become even the slightest bit crispy which we have come to expect and prefer.  I also ordered the nigiri salmon.  Although on the pricy side, the flavor was delicious with just a hint of wasabi to go along with the salmon and rice flavors.  For my entree, I chose the seared scallops with mixed vegetables over rice.  The scallops had a drizzled sauce over the top and had really good flavor.  Maybe a hint of chewiness, but acceptable.  The veggies were tender while the rice soaked up any of the remaining remnants of sauce.  My wife also ordered the California Roll for her entree.  She thought it compared well with other venues.    In and out in a relatively quick timespan, we had very little down time between courses.  Overall, it was an enjoyable evening.  Just needs a few tweaks.  Review #182

The feel of this BRU Burger is a little more upscale than the other two around town.  There is plenty of outdoor seating as well as plenty of room in the dining room, the bar area, and what appeared to be a private dining room.  The service was really attentive and friendly, even holding the door for us to enter!    My wife seemed to enjoy her Buttermilk Cobb salad which was rather large, even though she ordered the smaller version.  Lots of tasty ingredients cut down to decent sizes so that she didn't need make additional cuts.  I have been hearing about the Black Bean Burger for awhile now, so I decided to give it a try and upgraded my side to Onion Rings.  The Burger had a nice flavor, somewhat less spicy than I expected from reading the ingredient list.  The "burger" was full sized and moist...maybe a little too moist since chunks of patty dropped out of the bun when I lifted it.  Fortunately, there was a fork handy to pick up the fallen parts.  The onion rings were lightly breaded and the onion inside was very sweet.  The house made ketchup paired well and is highly recommended.  We also decided to share the Peach White Chocolate Bread Pudding with pecans and whipped cream.  Very delicious and just the right size for sharing after a full meal.  Review #385

Although I don't get here often, I have had enough positive experiences to say that the food and service are pretty good.  My wife always orders the Fireside M-80's shrimp and seems to enjoy the large cone of fried shrimp with the sweet chili garlic sauce and side of cole slaw that is served underneath.    I like to try different items here, so on my most recent visit, I started with the Fireside Shrooms.  There were seven mushrooms (about ping pong ball size) topped with mozzarella and a basil pesto sauce.  Nice flavor, a bit on the sweet side.  For my lunch entree, I ordered the Avocado-Ahi salad.  The salad had 4 oz of seared tuna coated with peppercorns and served atop a bed of field greens & spinach, carrots, peppers, onion, wontons and served with sesame seed dressing on the side.  The salad was huge (about a 10" square plate).  Although the flavor was good, the greens were served uncut, so it required both knife and fork to eat it.    The key lime pie dessert was really good.  The lime was tart and the whipped cream sweet.  The graham cracker crust was a little on the thin side, so it didn't have any crunch, but the lime zest sprinkled over the pie was a nice bonus.  The service was pretty good.  Generally friendly, the waiter kept our water topped off and brought a soda refill.  Wait times weren't too long between courses.  My only negative was that the salad came in both full size and lunch size.  I made the mistake of assuming that since it was noon, I would get the lunch size as a default.  Instead there was a huge 10" square plate which I thought large, but because I was engaged in conversation, didn't pay too much attention to.  It was the full size salad ($17) instead of the lunch size ($10).  I wish I had paid more attention and could have saved myself the $7.  It would have been nice if the waiter had asked which size I wanted instead of assuming I wanted the full size.  Review #379

This "not just another steakhouse" has really good food and a casual environment.  Our group visited during the Devour Indy promotion and really enjoyed the flavors.  From the complimentary bread course through the desserts, there were delicious options.    We parked in the Circle Centre Mall garage and crossed the intersection to the restaurant.  I liked that the restaurant built an inner glass wall to keep the cold air from rushing directly into the dining area (it helped, but if you get cold easily, ask to sit farther back in the dining room). We were seated near the front window which was much brighter than the rest of the room.    Our waiter greeted us promptly and got our drink orders and after a while returned to take our dining selections.  We were dining early on a Thursday, so I was a little surprised that the first course didn't come out until about a half hour after we arrived.  Good thing we had a bread course which was excellent.  (Note:  no "amuse booze" cocktail was served as mentioned on the website.)    I went with the Braised Alligator Gumbo as my appetizer.  This is a carryover from the previous incarnation of the restaurant, Georgia Reese's.  If you like peppery flavor with a slow heat build on your palate, then this is a must try.  The flavors remind me of navy bean soup with moist, shredded meat (I know....tastes like chicken!), topped with a dollop of saffron rice and pickled okra (very much like dill pickle flavor, but more texture).  The flavors worked really well together.  My guests tried the wedge salad and the Caesar salad. Both got good reviews.    All three of us ordered the petite filet mignon medium rare.  Note that the chef's version of medium rare was less pink than I have at other fine restaurants, so consider that when you order.  The filet's were served on separate serving plates with a circle of house roasted tomato gastrique surrounding the meat and topped with pepper cress.  I am not a fan of steak sauce, so the flavor wasn't my favorite (think A-1).  The meat was very tender and the slices I had without getting the steak sauce were a little under seasoned but still very pleasant.  (I would prefer they put the sauce on just one side of the plate so that I could choose whether or not to dip the steak.)    The standard sides are sharable and big enough for 2 to 4 guests.  For Devour, the sides were reduced in portion, but still plenty to let us share samples around the table.  (It would have been nice if our small bread plates would have been left, so I had to scoop the samples onto my steak plate and pick up that steak sauce flavor on some of my bites.)    The flavors of the sides were really good!  Between us, we had the Whipped Sweet Potato Souffle (with marshmallow topping!), Cream Greens (a spinach based dish served in a skillet and topped with Parmesan cheese and roasted shallot crumbles), and Smoked Sweet Cream Corn.  My wife really enjoyed her sweet potato dish...very light and airy, not dense like some places.    For dessert, we again ordered different options.  The Cheesecake was excellent...especially the triple berry compote.  I could eat that on just about anything!  The Caramelized Banana Tart got a good review too.  The only dish that was just okay was the Creme Brulee.  It didn't have much flavor and had a tapioca texture....not sure if it set right.  When dining out, my wife usually gets creme brulee as her dessert, so she has had plenty of fine restaurant selections to compare to.      As far as service, we seemed to have a revolving door of servers throughout the evening. Most were attentive and did a good job of making us feel welcome. The water was filled every time I seemed to take a sip which got a little intrusive. Another waiter had a habit of leaning over the table when he spoke and made us feel a little uncomfortable having his face about a foot away.  We all noticed it, so I hope this gets corrected.     So, lots of tasty food, and just enough minor tweaks needed to settle on a four star rating.  Hopefully, as the staff gets more experience (this place opened in November), some of the bugs will be worked out.    Review #220

I stopped in this spacious lower level brewery on the southwest corner of the Biltwell Event Center.  Plenty of parking in the lot outside, but it does have a few see through grated stairs down to the floor from the entry.  That was a bit unexpected!  The brewery opened around October 2016 and was currently offering six selections on draft.  Five were their own brews and the sixth was a collaboration with Sun King.    They have a few snacks, but otherwise you can order food or bring in your own.  Since they don't offer food, they mentioned they are dog friendly in the seating area.  Since it was my first time there, I asked about a flight.  Here, they offer three selections for $7.  The selections are seven ounces each, so it still seems like a good value compared with other craft breweries I've been to.  I opted for some of the less hoppy/bitter options (I heard others who are fans of IPA's commenting about a selection called Kiss that they recommended!)  The Round Town Lager (4.8% 28 IBU) was a nice lager, but didn't stand out.  The Valley Golden Ale (4.8% 19 IBU) was one I liked and the flavor became my favorite the more I drank.  I would definitely order this one again!  My third choice was the collaboration Angle Juice dark mild ale (3.6% 40 IBU).  This had a deeper flavor, but was pretty smooth.  The malty flavor was okay, just not my favorite of the visit.  I forgot to ask how often they rotate flavors/options.  If you are looking for a place near downtown but without the parking issues, stop by here...south on Kentucky Avenue until you get to the I-70 underpass, then turn right.  If you reach Morris St on Kentucky, you've gone too far!  Review #253

Great new restaurant on the near north side!  I found some free street parking next to the building since the parking lot in the back was already full. Be aware that 22nd street is a two-way street while Delaware in only one way north.  As I walked up 22nd, I noticed that they have a separate carry out window for walk up customers.  Once inside the building from the entrance on Delaware, the bar is against the wall in front of you with the kitchen behind it.  The take out window is to the right of the bar.  There was a blend of tables and numerous seats at the bar.  A couple televisions were on the walls, but as of this early review, not much decoration.  I grabbed a seat at the bar and selected one of their local draft brew options.  They also serve wine and cocktails and some additional beer in cans.  To start my dinner, I went with a cup of Bone Broth.  This tasty soup is served in a large bowl that has edamame and bean sprouts on the bottom.  The broth is served in a small tea kettle and is poured over the veggies.  The flavor is deep and savory with a bit of heat on the tale end of the flavor profile.  The sprouts maintained a nice crunch despite the hot broth.  The only negative was that the sprouts, when not herded into a nice bunch, tended to be a little long to eat gracefully, but hopefully, they will give them a nice chop before serving in the future to make it more user friendly.    I also ordered the Egg Rolls.  Unlike any I have had before, these crispy rolls sliced on the bias were filled with large pieces of monkfish and served with ginger scallion dashi for dipping that also adds a bit of saltiness to the flavor combo.  Excellent!  Moist inside, crunchy outside and delicious flavor.  Definitely would order these again!  For my entree, I ordered the Tonkatsu.  This dish consists of Fisher Farms pork tenderloin (about 6 oz) pounded flat and lightly breaded.  The finished piece is then sliced into several strips that are just a bit large to eat gracefully with chopsticks.  (Don't be afraid to ask for silverware if you aren't up for the challenge!)  The tenderloin was thin, but retained its moisture while the breading was crisp!  Some sort of magic must be involved because I have rarely seen meat like this both moist and crispy.  Excellent technique here!  The entree comes in an ornamental dish that has soy sriracha sauce on the bottom with a slice of white bread then the tenderloin and some pickles and onions.  On the side are the condiments:  green chili paste and fish sauce cucumbers.  You can either dip the tenderloin or spread some of the chili paste on top.  Slide your tenderloin around the bottom of the bowl to pick up some of the sriracha, then be sure to add some of the pickles and onions as you take your bite.  Wow!   It's at that moment you realize there are toasted sesame seeds sprinkled across the top of the meat and the flavors are vibrant.  Before you take your next bite, try some of the cucumber to enjoy the acid component of flavor.  It's all good!    Although the menu is fairly limited in quantity, I find myself wanting to come back soon and try some more options.  I didn't ask how often the menu items will change, but I recommend getting here soon so that you can enjoy some great Asian flavors.  p.s.  This is the sister restaurant of Shoefly Public House down the street.  The same husband and wife team are behind both places.  Review #189

Although this side of town has seen a stretch of economic downturn, there seems to be a new energy as the city is focusing on redeveloping the area and entrepreneurs open new businesses near the park.  So, it should come as no surprise that this park should see an upturn in interest as more people discover it.  On the west end of the park, new public art installations are adding visual interest to visitors who stroll along this long and narrow park.  To the east of the artworks, there is a playground and shelter/gazebo portion of the park.  The rest of the park has numerous mature trees that line Pogue's Run as it flows southwest towards the White River.   Review #558

I have always enjoyed the food at Mesh. My only problem has been that it can get very loud inside, so I tend to go when I can dine on the outdoor patio or, as in this case, go for Sunday morning brunch when the crowd is comparatively small.     As part of the Cunningham Restaurant Group, this is one of the older established businesses they have.  Many of their best chefs have passed through the doors of Mesh (asw well as the non-affiliated chef owners of Revery in Greenwood).  So, there is a lot of attention to food and service here.    My wife and I brought one of her lifelong friends with us.  We were able to find free parking on Mass Avenue at this time of day.  They also have limited free parking through the alley next to the building in a private lot behind Mesh.    We started off with the shareable biscuits and jam:  Housemade buttermilk biscuits with butter, apricot jam, honeycomb, and lemon curd as taste options.  All were delcious!    I went for the Chicken & Waffles breakfast.  Crisp, but moist chicken that was lightly breaded and served with a quartered Belgian Waffle with syrup and butter was a plate full, but wasn't so filling as to need a to go box.  It also comes with an apple slaw that had a flavor of what tasted like green onion to me.  It went well with the bites of chicken, not so well with the waffle.    My wife ordered the Benedict with two poached eggs on an English muffin with smoked pork loin, spinach, tabasco hollandaise and a side of country potatoes.  She found the hollandaise to be mildly flavored which is fortunate since she doesn't especially like spicy heat.    Our guest ordered the French Toast which comes with cream cheese, whipped butter, maple syrup, apricot jam, and a side of smoked bacon.  I would have preferred the bacon a little crisper, but she found the bacon to be fine.    As with all CRG restaurants, we earned points on our VIP card.  With 1000 pts, we earn $100 gift card good at any of their restaurants.      There is also a holiday seasonal promotion that for every $50 gift card, an additional $10 gift card is issued.  Note that the regular gift card is good anytime.  The seasonal $10 gift card is good only from Jan 1 through Mar 31 2017.    Overall, we continue to be impressed with the quality of food and service at these restaurants.  We will return to one of their businesses soon!  Review #194

During opening week, I stopped by to pick up a couple items from this new restaurant.  From their menu, you can see they have several Ramen Bowls, Rice Bowls, and Banh Mi sandwiches available.  After placing my order at the counter, I sat by the window bench and waited for my order to be ready.  I really enjoyed the Swedish Meatball Banh Mi.  It featured a couple nice sized meatballs and I selected to dress it with spicy mayo, pickled diakon, sliced cucumbers, and fresh cilantro.  The flavors worked well together with my only negative being that the bread (about an 8 inch bun) is thick and quite filling.    I also tried the "Black Eye Bowl" (Ramen).  Since all meals are to go, I was given a small bowl filled with a very salty iekei broth & spicy Miso (separated for better transport) and a larger bowl for all the other ingredients (ramen, Asian Ground Pork, soft boiled egg, and corn).  Once home, I mixed the two bowls together to let moisture warm the drier ingredients. Although I liked the first bite very much, the saltiness fought the other flavors after awhile and became too dominant.  My wife noticed the saltiness on the first sip and didn't want any more.  Yes, it was that salty!  My favorite part of the bowl was the soft boiled egg.  When I split the egg white, the warm runny yolk flowed into the broth and really tasted wonderful!  So, I would give the sandwich a 4.5 or 5 while the ramen bowl would only get a 2.5 or 3.  If they could cut back the saltiness, the rest of the flavors seemed to be really good and the flavor would definitely jump a star or two.  The staff was very friendly and efficient during my visit.  Sandwiches are made to order and the bowls have to be assembled, so the wait was about five minutes when I visited early on Friday for lunch.  I was able to grab some free street parking on the south side of the street (south bound).    Review #848

I stopped in for lunch on a Wednesday (3-30-16) after parking in a nearby lot.  Upon entering, I saw how spacious this place is and that the bar is on the near left, the grill on the back right.  The walls are decorated with posters and memorabilia that has a heavy metal theme.  I had heard that the music was loud, but at least this lunch time, the music was background and somewhat a non-issue.  (Not sure if they turn it up in the evenings.)  Anyway, I was going to pick a burger that had a great combination, but it wasn't on the lunch menu.  I specifically asked if I could order the type I wanted and got a somewhat muddled "answer" that didn't address my question stating "here are the lunch specials".  I decided to go with the "Kuma Burger".  It was a smaller size burger that was appropriate for lunch time.  It comes with bacon and a sunny side up egg.  (I am not sure why this combo was chosen to be the namesake.)  I liked the pretzel bun, but was disappointed with the bacon and egg on top of an entree.  It just doesn't taste that good to me..rather bland.  (Maybe I should have stripped them off and eaten them separately.)    When I go out in the evening, it is rare that I go out for burgers. Unless I find something better on the lunch menu that catches my interest, I probably won't be back.  Review #37

I stopped by for lunch after hearing good things about this family run cafe.  I was able to find street parking just around the corner and took a seat in the front part of this shotgun style building.    I have heard good things about the soups (I will have to try them on another day), but I was intrigued by the Hawaiian Grill sandwich:  croissant (that's my hook!) with ham and cheddar, pineapple, and honey mustard.  I went with the standard chips (soup and side salad are options for an extra $1.50)  Although all the ingredients were fresh and tasty, the pineapple was a bit too dominant/sweet for the rest of the sandwich....maybe a spicy brown mustard instead of the sweet honey mustard would have been a better match to add flavor depth.    The cafe is eclectic in decor with a comfortable feel.  There is a sense of humor to some of the signs and a definite link to canine appreciation.    I plan on returning to try some soup and investigate their bar options.  Review #45

La Margarita is a nice Mexican restaurant on the corner of Virginia and Woodlawn Avenue.  There is some street parking on Virginia, and a free public lot about a half block north on Woodlawn.    After entering the restaurant through the common building entrance on Virginia, you head straight back to the second door to enter the actual dining room of the restaurant.  A hostess stand is on the left as you enter and that is where you wait to be seated.  They have a large interior dining area with a bar on the far wall.  On the right is the doorway to the patio.    The restaurant has a decent sized patio for outdoor seating that has a small wrought iron fence to keep folks from cutting through the dining area.  There are tables with umbrellas and a few benches to relax on near decorative flower boxes.  While we waited for our entrees to come out, we had our water, beverages, and a basket of fresh and hot tortilla chips with a spicy (some what hot) salsa and a pico de gallo type salsa of nicely diced veggies and herbs.  Note that the pico de gallo can be hot or cool.  I asked the waitress about the difference in our first and our refill bowl and it was simply of luck.  Our original bowl of pico had jalapeno slices and was a bit too spicy for my wife.  Our second had more avocado and we didn't notice any jalapeno, so my wife enjoyed that much more.  Seems like a little more stirring of the source could even out the flavor.  I ordered a really tasty Carnitas en Chile Verde.  It came with three dark steamed tortillas, and sides of refried beans and Spanish rice.  There was also an avocado (guacamole?) spread and more pico de gallo.  I was pleased that the pork was a combo of shredded and chunks.  It all was moist and tender with a bit of spice. I ended up using all the tortillas before the meat was gone, so I had to finish it off with my fork.  Too good to waste! I definitely recommend this.  My wife went with a Burrito de Carnitas en Chile Verde which also had the same sides.  She needed to ask for sour cream since it wasn't brought out with the original plate.  She seemed to enjoy her meal quite a bit, but needed a "to go" box due to the large portion size.    The price was a bit higher than most Mexican restaurants I have sampled, but that's probably due to the location.  Still, it was a reasonable price and would not discourage a return visit.  Good food and a great location for people watching and enjoying a nice summer day.  Review #361

I had lunch on Tuesday at 317 Burger based upon the excellent review by Kim K!  I took advantage of the free parking down the street (Northeast corner of Westfield and Winthrop, north of Brugge Brasserie) and chose to sit inside instead of on the covered front patio.  Inside, they have a dining area to the left and a bar area to the right.  I went with the dining section.  As recommended, I chose the Fried Mac & Cheese as a starter.  Excellent flavor!  I asked how they made the Mac into a ball shape and the server said they make it into a risotto like mixture.  Not sure I fully understood, but it worked.  The sauce for dipping reminds me of the sweet/sour sauce I get for Asian fast food, maybe a little more liquid than the bottled stuff.  The combo of pasta and cheese sauce were fine on their own, but lacked a lot of depth in flavors until I added the dipping sauce.  That sweet and tangy flavor really complimented the appetizer.  I also chose to try the "Strawberry Hill" Burger.  Now this was a stretch for me.  I have dined at a number of burger places and some get so fancy that I lose the flavor of the burger under the mountain of fruits/vegetables, everything but the kitchen sink!  So, when I saw that this burger came with peanut butter and a spicy strawberry compote, I was questioning whether it would work.  And then they had some Goose the Market Bacon (fried crisp) and some Ghost Pepper Cheese for a lot of heat, I knew I was pushing the boundaries of my burger experience!  Although it wasn't my absolute favorite burger, I think it mostly worked.  And the bottom line is this:  I could still taste the burger (8 oz of Black Angus).  It was a little pink in the middle, but had a dark brown char on the outside and was seasoned properly as if it had to stand on its own.  That keeps it a hamburger, not just filler.  Sure, each bite took on its own flavor balance as the various tastes came to the center of my attention.  But underlying the peanut butter, or the super sweet compote, or the throat tingling heat of the ghost pepper was the taste of burger.    To go with the burger, I opted to upgrade from the standard fries to the cole slaw since I thought the fries and fried Mac might be too much fried food for one sitting.  The slaw was nice and creamy which also made the heat from the Ghost Pepper Cheese much easier to manage when I alternated bites of slaw and burger.  It takes me a long time to get to Broad Ripple from the Southwest Side of town, so even though I'll likely not become a regular, I definitely would like to come back on a Thursday to take care of the discounted prices on some of the other selections.    p.s.  Service was quick and friendly.  However, I did need to look for staff when I first arrived and asked for more water before my server noticed I was out.  Little things, but not enough to fret over.  Review #112

I saw this place on a list of new places to look for in Fountain Square this fall/winter, so I decided to give it a try.  Although it has space enough to be available as an event center, I found it comfy enough to be inviting.  As the first customer of the day, I got to choose my seating.  (They have about 10 2-tops and 6 4-top tables in the area surrounding the central counter/wine bar).  Along the north east wall is a large rack of wine bottles.    I wanted to try a wine flight and the charcuterie board on my visit.  The wine flight was priced at $9 for four selections from the red and white wines. (Sparkling wines are available for purchase, but not in the flights).  The wines are selected from domestic and foreign sources.    The charcuterie board has a variety of options, but comes with your choice of three meats, two cheeses, and a spread.  It also comes with a small half loaf of Amelia's bread which is served heated.  I went with the thinly sliced Soppressata, Gentile Seasonal, and Mortadella meats for a nice combination of savory and salty.  For my cheeses, I chose the Aged Cheddar and Naturally Smoked Gouda (both from Fair Oaks).  Both cheeses were thick sliced (about 1/4") and were great when paired with the other board items.  For my spread, I opted for the Fig Jam which is their most popular selection.  It adds a sweet component to go with the other choices I made.  I formed all types of combinations with the sliced bread and jam and the other items.  It was fun discovering the different flavor combos available.  All in all, I thought the food and wines were really good.  I could see meeting friends for a relaxing afternoon, munching on tasty offerings while sipping some fine wines.  Sounds like a plan to me!  Review #432

Yummy food and pleasant service made for an enjoyable Sunday lunch.  My wife wasn't sure about going when I mentioned I wanted to try an Irish restaurant.  We've had some disappointing meals elsewhere, but she was relieved that they carry other food items besides the standard Irish fare.  The place was filled with rich woods and some holiday decorations.  It was a little dark in the room we sat in, but there was some natural lighting that helped.  (Some small lights on the book shelves could help!)  My wife went with a pulled pork nacho (from the appetizer menu) and was surprised at how large the portion was.  It came with large, seasoned chips that stayed pretty crisp and she really enjoyed the flavor of the pulled pork.  Thought it was moist as well.    I also ordered from the appetizer menu.  I started with the Corned Beef and Cabbage rolls which are best described as egg rolls cut on the bias stuffed with the main ingredients, potato, 2 kinds of cheese, and then served with 1000 Island dressing (think Reuben flavors).  Very tasty.  Even my wife ate one of the halves and enjoyed it!  I got an order of Pretzel Bun Sliders (3) which I must admit was getting me full enough that I ended up taking the last one home.  The ground beef was seared nicely, but as often happens with sliders, got a bit overcooked in the middle.  The flavor was good with lettuce, tomato, onion, cheese, and their own slider sauce.  I ended up using some ketchup from the table to add some moisture and that worked well.    Overall, it was a really good meal.  The service was friendly and efficient, getting us in and out in good fashion.  Note:  Phones get practically no bars inside, so ask the staff for their WiFi password since I don't recall seeing it posted.  Review #1952

They have a really nice lunch special.  I ordered the Broccoli Beef and it came with soup (I went with Egg Drop), an egg roll, and steamed rice (about a cup sized serving).  All of this for only $8 plus tax and tip.    There was a private lot and seemed to be a lot of tables available on the inside.      I had a couple waits that seemed awkwardly long during my visit:  No one greeted me when I entered and when I was finished, the two staff members were engaged in a conversation without either watching the dining area.  So, I simply got up and walked over to check out.      I liked my food, but wouldn't say it was any better than a number of other places around town.  I'll give them a pass on the delays, because most reviews seem to praise the service....maybe it was just an off day.  Review #599

I stopped in this new restaurant after seeing it pop up on my phone's "hot & new nearby".  I am not well-versed in Greek food, so it seemed like a nice opportunity to get acquainted.  The restaurant has a small footprint on the west side of Mass Avenue, just north of Stella.  There isn't an outside shingle advertising it, so I actually missed it as I was walking by on the other side of the street.  However, there is a cool sign on the front window.  Anyway, I am glad I found it!    Inside, there is a small dining area with about a dozen or so chairs.  Even around 2 in the afternoon, all the tables were full, so I decided to get my order to go.    The restaurant was a one-man operation during my visit.  There is an order line beyond the dining room where you can see the options on the overhead menus.  The menus have photos of the meals, but don't list the options or ingredients (I looked for, but didn't ask if they had any paper menus that might list ingredients in the sandwiches.)    I placed my order and then waited my turn.  Since he was cook and cashier, I watched as a family of four got their order as it was ready.   I guess we take it for granted at larger restaurants that all our food comes out at the same time.  It is understandable that the food comes out this way when you see this guy hustle.  Even though it came out at different times, the wait was no more than a few minutes apart.    About ten to twelve minutes after I placed my order, my Shawarma combo (drink and fries) was ready.  The fluffy pita bread (I think) looked like a rolled pancake stuffed with chicken, lettuce, tomato, onion, & Tzatziki sauce.  Watch out when you lift it the first time.  I didn't realize the sauce would be so fluid and ended up wearing a nice curry flavored liquid on my shirt and shorts.  Yikes!  Anyway, the Shawarma tasted really good and the curry didn't overwhelm all the other flavors.    The fries had a crisp crunch to them and were generously portioned.  I noticed the potato flavor was the most dominant.  Not sure if they were salted or not, but if they were, it was very lightly.    Counting tax, the whole combo was well under $10.  There was plenty there to eat for the price, so I give it a good value rating for being a downtown restaurant.  Review #334

I have to give this McNamara's the benefit of the doubt because they are trying to move the last of their Christmas items with a big sale, because I imagine in a week or two they will have all kinds of new items to explore in the showroom part of the store.  During my visit, the pieces they still had were classy, just not what I was looking for. The store is laid out nicely and was easy to get around.  Like the other McNamara's, they have a cooled room that they keep their fresh flowers in to prolong their beauty.  I normally shop/browse the Greenwood store and this one seems quite a bit smaller in floor space and shelf space, so they just won't be able to show as many cool items.    As I browsed, both of the staff working this afternoon let me know that they would gladly help me if I needed anything or had any questions.  I like that!  Review #2085

After sampling some of Agave's food at a recent Yelp Event, I made a point of bookmarking the restaurant as a Thank You for the support they gave our event as well as to support a small business.  So when my wife needed to pick up something from a shop in Carmel, I decided to go along and stop by Agave for a late lunch.  Located on Main St on the east end of the Arts District, the shop is fortunate to have some public parking on the south side of the building.  We found our way in and were greeted promptly and because of the time, allowed to pick our own seating (normally you wait to be seated).  We grabbed a spot on the main floor (the upstairs is open when needed) near the windows.  There is a bar on the west side of the dining area.  After selecting our beverages, my wife went with the Chimichanga and I decided to choose the Tacos de Carne Asada which I saw a lot of great reviews of on Yelp (it is also one of my "go to" selections when trying a Mexican Restaurant for the first time.)  In a very brief time, our entrees were delivered (we hadn't even finished the complementary salsa and chips.)  My choice came with two corn tortillas with steak, cilantro and onion with refried beans on the side.  There was also a spicy sauce to add which added dimension to the flavor.  Although I prefer the taste of flour tortillas, the tacos were still pretty tasty.  My wife's chicken Chimi came with Mexican rice, pico de gallo, sour cream, and a bit of guac on the side.  There was also a cheese sauce over the Chimi.  She liked the flavor, but was disappointed that there wasn't any crispness to the shell.  The dough was a bit spongy like it had been either undercooked or reheated or the cheese had softened the crust.  Not sure what happened, but she was expecting the crispy texture and didn't get it.
