She did let the staff know about it in a nice way but went ahead and ate her meal anyway.  Note:  She also was expecting it to be shredded chicken, but instead found a large single piece of chicken (tenderloin or breast meat).  The flavors were on the mild side which normally my wife likes, but even she thought it could use a bit more spice.  I will say that we really liked the taste of the salsa.  It seemed to be more complex than a lot of tomato based salsas....it seemed to have a hint of smoky flavor to me.  Service was friendly and attentive and like the rest of the family, sincerely interested in making the dining experience a positive one.  Overall, I think the 3.5 star rating is pretty accurate based upon my first dining experience here.  No "Wow" factor and the slight disappointment in the Chimi, but I'll round up to 4 because of the friendly service.  Review #2344

This was my third visit to Amelia's, a bakery located next to Bluebeard, along the Cultural Trail on Virginia Avenue in Fletcher Place.  I would probably have stopped by more often if they had more parking, but it is hit or miss finding a spot close by.  Just plan on stopping while in the area for one of the bars, distilleries, or restaurants.  Although this was only my third time, I have been fortunate to have tasted Amelia's bread upon many occasions since they supply breads to quite a few restaurants in Indy. Always tasty.  On this Friday afternoon, I selected a Semolina bread.  The staff was friendly and attentive and offered to slice the bread at no extra charge.  On the wall opposite the counter and bread racks are a number of items that may compliment a sandwich or a picnic dinner.  I have selected tomato jam and rumesca (garlic-y sauce) on prior visits.  Good quality foods!  Review #92

If you like pizza with your beverage of choice, then you will like Pi in Carmel!  The food truck that specialized in pizza in Indy now has a fixed location as well.  Located on the second floor of the new Sun King Distillery along the Monon Trail, you can get your personal sized pizza for dining in or to go.  There are four red sauce options and four white sauce options.  You can also build your own (or rather, let them build it with your requests!)    The pizza are thin crust and though fired to a browning on the bottom, the pizza is a little floppy, so fold the pie to avoid losing your toppings.  The service was friendly and the wait was quite reasonable (I only had about a ten minute wait since I was there right as they opened.)  You place your order at the counter, pay and then give your name so that they can find you when it is ready.  You can look around the rest of the building or browse through the menus which are located on every table around.  They also serve garlic sticks and soft drinks.  Or, you can ask one of the Sun King roving servers to bring you a beverage from the distillery/brewery. (That is billed separately from Pi.)  Don't be discouraged by all the construction.  You can get through it from either east or west and can park free inside the Midtown Parking Garage a half block south of the building.    Good pizza and lots of beverage options.  Wish I lived closer!  Review #1038

This park has a lot of the standard features (shelter, playground, parking lot) of most parks, but also has a great nature trail (about a half mile) through the woods that winds along a creek.  The trails are easy to follow and in most places, stays relatively dry so that you don't have to get muddy just to walk.  There are also some open areas for active sports and additional picnic tables by the east end woods.  There is also a sturdy bridge that spans the creek if you wish to enter the park from the south side of the woods.  Review #769

This Lowes doesn't seem quite as good as it was 10 years ago when I was a more frequent customer.  It also doesn't seem as large as the one I now frequent.  Lots of staff behind the counter, but not many out in the aisles when you need assistance.  This one has most of the seasonal items in a separate area between the yard and the main building.  Review #3407

So glad I gave Kuma another chance!  The service this time was excellent and the food was top notch.  Sure, it was a pricey lunch but it wasn't the same old thing that I could do better at home or some lame thing from a fast food joint.  This was really delicious food and a nice beer selection to go with it!  If you've read other reviews, then you probably know this has a "Heavy Metal" theme of posters and music in the background.  What you may not know is that the more combos of burgers that I tried, the better I liked this place!  I went during Indy Burger Week and for $5, Kuma offered a 3 oz slider called Soilent Green.  This little burger had a patty that was infused with bacon, cheddar, and habanero and then it was topped with more bacon, pepperjack cheese, and green chiles.  It was served on a buttery flavored pretzel bun.  Excellent!  I was a little concerned that it may be too hot, but the flavors worked and the heat was more of an accompanying layer to the flavor.  Too bad this is a promotional item and will be going away soon.  I hope they add it to the full time menu!  I also tried the Led Zeppelin.  It's a full 10 oz burger topped with BBQ pulled pork, cheddar, and dill pickle slices.  Again, the flavors were very complementary and the burger itself was nicely charred without becoming dry.  (I needed a to go box since I had a salad too!)  I got a Whole Lotta Love for the Led Zeppelin burger!  My wife enjoyed her Kuma burger once I cut it down.  These are BIG BURGERS!  Hers came with bacon and an egg served sunny side up.  She really enjoyed the flavor combo.  (She shared my to go box too!)  They have a small lot on the east end of the place for parking, otherwise you can try finding some street parking in the neighborhood or take a chance in the lot across the street.  Not sure how they feel about sharing their spaces.  Note:  to park in the lot you have to come up from the south side of the building since it is on a one-way street and can't turn south from Prospect at the corner.    There is also outdoor seating for nice weather days on the east end by the parking lot.  Inside seating has a divider between the bar and the rest of the dining, so I think it may be okay to bring kids in now.   Rev. #28

Good service and a warm, inviting atmosphere for this restaurant.  We took our granddaughters with us and although it says it is a pub, the pub is in a separate room from the dining.  The portions were generous and the food didn't take long to come out.  Our granddaughters were able to find things to order from the kids' menu (cheese quesadillas and a large hot dog with fries.)  My wife ordered a Taco Salad and the shell was nice and crisp even when stuffed with the salad and meat (she chose the beef).  Pretty tasty!  The only negative was the Blackened Chicken and Shrimp Penne that I ordered.  Although there was plenty of seasoning sprinkled around the large dish, the shrimp and chicken were not blackened, looking rather pale, or in the shrimp's case, white.  I am used to having the seasoning added during the cooking process and actually turning the meats dark/black, so this was disappointing.  Sure, I was able to get a bit of cajun seasoning flavor, but the blackening adds a depth to the flavor.  Lots to eat, just not as enjoyable as I had hoped.  I would probably order something else next time.  Service was attentive and prompt all through the dinner.  They brought a complementary bread course while we waited for our dinners and cleared the table efficiently.  Overall, they did a good job.  Review #352

In August 2016, a new addition joined the growing public art on Mass Ave downtown.  "Mari Evans" is a 30-foot tall image of the 97 year old poet who has lived in Indianapolis since 1947.  Evans is best known for her poetry, children's books, and short stories. She was also quite involved with the "Black Arts Movement" during the 1960's and 1970's.    The art work was created in a very brief time period by Michael "Alkemi" Jordan who has a number of public art murals around Indy.  (Jordan's "The Kiss of Life" was part of the "46 for XLVI" SuperBowl initiative.)    Jordan was requested by Evans to paint her likeness on the side of the Davlan Building at 448 Mass Ave.  Big Car and the Riley Area Development Corp produced the art with funding from the Indiana Arts Commission and the Efroymson Family Fund. (Source material from the Indianpolis Star website)  I Am a Black Woman - Mari Evans "I am a black woman  the music of my song  some sweet arpeggio of tears  is written in a minor key  and I  can be heard humming in the night  Can be heard  humming  in the night  I saw my mate leap screaming to the sea  and I/with these hands/cupped the lifebreath  from my issue in the canebrake  I lost Nat's swinging body in a rain of tears  and heard my son scream all the way from Anzio  for Peace he never knew....I  learned Da Nang and Pork Chop Hill  in anguish  Now my nostrils know the gas  and these trigger tire/d fingers  seek the softness in my warrior's beard   I am a black woman  tall as a cypress  strong  beyond all definition still  defying place  and time  and circumstance  assailed  impervious  indestructible  Look  on me and be  renewed" - 1970  Review #124  FYI: For a more complete list of Public Art in Indianapolis go to the following website:  http://www.indyartsguide.org/public-art/

Simply stated, "Go for the beer, return for the food!"   On my visit, I saw there were only four brews on tap: two IPA's, a stout, and a golden ale.  Well, actually, the golden ale (which I ordered) was a Thai Basil/ginger mix called "One Night in Bangkok" (4.5% 30 IBU).  It was a cloudy gold in appearance and had a slightly odd taste at first, but got better once I got used to the different flavor.  Compared to other breweries, it's hard to give this place a 5 due to the limited selection.  But as far as food goes, both items I ordered were really good!  I started with a deviled egg taco with the tortilla made with beet juice for a bright reddish purple color.  Inside was a deconstructed hard-boiled egg, diced beets (pickled?), beet greens, and salsa verde.  The flavors were delicious!  It was a little tough keeping the ingredients inside the taco, but I managed to scoop up the remnants with my fork and get the most of it!  I also ordered the pepper turkey panini.  The sliced turkey had a hint of pepper flavor that added a fullness to the sandwich when paired with almond butter, and crisp apple slices.  On the side was a fennel-apple salad which was lightly dressed.  The subtle flavors of the salad worked well with the multi-textured panini.  I highly recommend this selection.  The bar has a garage door that opens up to allow fresh air on pleasant days.  The bar itself is a shotgun style building with a long stainless steel counter.  The cooking is done right behind the counter as are the tanks for the brews.  The staff was friendly and service was prompt.  There is limited parking available behind the building, but free street parking is an option as well.  Review #259

Located just across 16th street from Methodist Hospital is the Neuroscience center where I was able to get lots of answers regarding what to expect during my upcoming battle with brain cancer.  I am simply allowing a bit of healing to occur after the removal of a fist sized tumor from my right temple.  Once my body is a little more stable, I will begin undergoing a multi tiered and multi cycle treatment plan to battle the aggressive brain cancer that my lousy genes caused.  I feel that the doctors did a great job of providing information about what to expect and what kind of a commitment it will take to whip this thing.  I am thankful that the staff cared so much for me and allowed my wife to attend the meetings with me so that she could take notes since my brain is a little befuddled still.  (She has been my angel that has kept me on my medicinal schedule and tracked my appointments while providing transportation since I've lost my license due to the seizures.)  The staff has been helpful and I feel a lot of confidence that I will be able to whip this disease with all the options they will pursue to help me win.  Trust these folks know what they are doing.  Review #3761

Fast and friendly place to pick up a slice.  The price is very affordable too.  The single slice looks to be about 1/6th of an 18" pizza (about 9" across and from rim to center) so a single goes a long way.  On the negative, I got a slice to go and when I opened the box, I could see the slice was unevenly cooked.  The crust rises on the rim, so some of it was bordering being burned.  However, the center (point) of the pizza was so under cooked that the ingredients fell off because the dough was so soggy.  I thought about folding the slice across, but because the rim was so thick, it didn't lend itself to being folded.  Even though my slice was a multiple meat option, there really wasn't much flavor other than in the sausage.  The other meats were chopped/sliced small and didn't add much flavor.  There was hardly any sauce and the cheese was underneath the toppings so it didn't add much flavor.  I decided to get an order of Garlic Knots as well.  The knots were twisted bread that were unseasoned and were baked to a light crispy outside with a warm and soft inside.  Not much flavor on their own so I decided to dip the knot in the accompanying tub of garlic butter/sauce. The butter itself was very liquid and I was concerned I would spill it.  If you love garlic, you may love this sauce.  However, if you like your garlic as more of an accent, not a feature, this sauce may be too strong.  I'm still tasting it 3 hours later even after brushing!  One other note:  If you go in and order from the counter, there is no overhead listing of menu items.  I noticed none of the "ready" pizza slices were labeled either.  There is a large selection to choose from, so it can be a little overwhelming to try to figure out what each slice has without taking a lot of browse time.  If there was an overhead menu or labeling, I think it would be a lot easier for first time customers to make choices.  I like that I could get pizza in a hurry, but if I have the time, I would rather have a small pizza baked for me elsewhere.  Review #488

Having had the pleasure of tasting some of the food from this restaurant at a recent Yelp event, I brought my wife here for lunch.  This ornate building includes colorful murals and sculptures that make it unique in its style and appearance.   The dining room is very open with high ceilings.  Although the room looks huge, there is a lot of open space, so fewer tables than I initially thought.  There is also a lot of hard surfaces for noise to bounce off, so it does get a bit loud even when only half full.  After receiving our complementary salsa and chips, we placed our order.  My wife usually goes with a Taco Salad, this time with chicken.  I chose to go with a Torta with beef tenderloin and onions.  Note that the restaurant does not have a liquor license, so you can't get a margarita here.  They do have a collection of beverages though.  The chips were made in house as was the salsa.  I was pleased to note that the salsa was not as cilantro forward as many other Mexican restaurants.  Instead, the taste brought forward the onions and peppers for a nice change of pace.  I also had a "small" Guacamole dip which was very light and creamy in texture.  It was a little under seasoned, but the limes I got with my entree and a little bit of table salt perked it up.  Not quite what I was used to, but again, definitely unique.  My torta was great!  The sandwich started with a very light and tasty bun that held the strips of beef along with the onion, tomato, avocado, etc.  Although a very large serving, it didn't seem heavy and filling.  It also came with the lime wedges (definitely a great addition to the meal) and fresh cucumber on the side.  I would gladly have that again!  My wife's lunch was a disappointment though.  It looked great:  Deep fried bowl with a colorful mix of ingredients.  But a couple of things were fails.  First, the oil temperature must not have been hot enough because instead of being crisped and light, the shell was flexible and we could taste the oil.  If the temp is high enough, it should seal the shell and not take on that taste.  And though the inside was good, there was so much liquid settled in the bottom (a creamy white liquid/sauce) that it became very soggy.  She could hardly transfer the remaining amount to the to go box.  Hopefully they will make some adjustments to the dish so that it rises to the level of my meal.  When we were finished, the waitress gave us our bill and we paid at the cashier/carryout counter near the door.  It is a beautiful space and one I recommend visiting if you are someone who appreciates the setting of your meal.  Review #2542

Although I've seen larger fabric stores and quilt shops, this one has a solid inventory of fabric, quilting machines, threads, patterns, and accessories.    I browsed around noting that most of the fabric and threads were sorted by color palate.  There was a section for holiday quilts/runners including an advent calendar; a section for baby/small kids with whimsical prints; and many types of quilts for everyday interiors or for those quilters who like a challenge.  And that challenge is what made my wife make purchases here.  She wanted to find something beyond the basic squares and triangles.  Not only did they have some finished quilts on display matching her needs, they also had accessories that made it easier to be precise while doing the odd shapes.  The staff was very helpful and even pointed out somethings that my wife might have her sewing group make for fund raising ideas.  Review #3489

I stopped in for a quick lunch and was very pleased with the quality and service.  They have daily lunch specials, so I ordered the Sun King Beer Battered Chicken Strips and chose the homemade coleslaw.  The chicken had a tasty seasoning and was moist and tender inside the crunch of batter.  The coleslaw was crisp and sweet.  I sat at the bar and the bartenders were friendly and efficient at getting my order in.  Ten minutes was all it took from the time I ordered to the time I was eating!  Great local spot to stop by during a lunch hour.    Review #1328

I haven't been here during the warmer months, so I probably haven't been able to appreciate the full beauty of the place.  But even in the winter, I could see the elegance of the design of the park.  There are plenty of picnic tables within a short distance of the ample parking on the north side of the garden.  The small pond has a fountain and koi fish.  The park sits next to the Monon and makes a nice stopping point for travelers to relax.  Review #2017

I really enjoyed my first visit to this Tex Mex chain.  The place is bright and clean and there seemed to be plenty of parking in their own lot, but know that there is a target across the way with lots of additional parking if needed.  Inside is bright and festive, but be sure you look where you're going if you head towards the bar.  There are two small steps down.  They are marked, but if you are looking around instead of where you're going, you may stumble.  (I'm okay, but probably looked awkward.)  Not sure why they didn't just level this room with the rest of the restaurant.  Anyway, I sat at the bar and the bartender/waiter was very pleasant.  I wasn't interested in alcohol, but I did find it odd to not see a list of what beverages they had to offer.  It looks like they have a variety of margarita's chilling in the machines there.  I ordered a steak burrito with the Tex Mex sauce instead of the hot green sauce.  This sauce had a rich, almost bbq flavor that paired really well with the steak and cheese burrito.  They throw a little bit of salsa and lettuce on the side that was good too.  I forgot to mention that the chips are very thin and light, yet crisp.  The salsa is a little watery, so be careful not to drip on your clothing.  I also found the salsa to be hotter than most places.  Not too hot, just a different experience than the red tomato sauce you find a lot of places.  Check out was quick since they leave your bill in a glass for whenever you are ready. (Pay your server.)  Review #2910

When you pull into the lot for this Hallmark store, you climb a few stairs not expecting how much room there is!  They have two stories of collectibles, winter holiday items and ornaments, and greeting cards.  I don't know if the place has always had as much home decor/fun items or if there used to be more space devoted to greeting cards, but either way, the current mix they now have makes it more likely that customers would return more frequently.  The staff was very friendly and even though they were busy converting the store post Christmas, they took time to greet me and let me know they were there to help.    I enjoyed browsing through the items and though they tend to run a bit on the pricey side, I've found that the pieces I've bought in the past have held up really well.  You pay for the quality as well as the name brand.  Note:  There is a lot of traffic on SR 135, so it is much easier to approach from the south and exit north if you are planning your route.  There is a turn lane in the middle of the highway, but the timing of the lights makes it  an adventure if you are crossing traffic!  Review #2052

I am relatively new to Thai food, so when I try a new place, I usually go for something I have enjoyed elsewhere.  Not only does it increase my chance for getting something I should like, but it gives me a point of reference to other Thai places I have dined.  This was one of the best I have had!  The restaurant is located on the north side of county line across from Greenwood Mall, so it can be a bit challenging to get in and out of the parking lot if you don't know exactly where you are going.  Once there, I had no trouble finding parking out front.  I went for a late lunch (around 1) and was greeted and seated immediately.  I must say the service was prompt, courteous, and the food I ordered was brought out swiftly.  I went with one of the lunch specials for under $8 (before tax, drink, & tip).  I selected the Padd Seuw and it comes with a choice of chicken or vegetarian.  I went with the chicken option.  It also can be adjusted for heat (like most good places) and I went with the mild-medium.  Not much heat, but enough to help the flavor.  Excellent!  The noodles were tender and full of flavor.  The chicken was plentiful and thin sliced, but not too overcooked.  Several veggies added some color to the plate as well as flavor and texture.  I highly recommend it.  The lunch special came with vegetarian styled lemon grass soup and spring roll.  Upgrades to include meat options are an extra $1.  These were brought out together right after placing my order.  The soup had very little vegetable matter, but packed a lot more heat than I have had at other Thai places.  It definitely affected the back of my throat and made my sinuses react.  The flavor was good enough not to be lost in the heat.  For people who like heat, this is probably not a big deal, but for my wife and some of our friends, I would need to caution them about the soup to avoid having a negative experience.   The spring roll was served warm and the flavor was once again enjoyable.  The outside was crisp and flaky.  The inside was al dente and had just enough texture to give a good bite while being firm enough to hold together.    The decor is nice featuring a number of paintings and mostly table/chairs on the side of the dining room I was seated in.  I am not sure how authentic the decor was, but it looked clean and generally in good shape.    Overall, I had a very positive experience.  I was in and out in about a half hour.  I would definitely go back when I am in the area.  Review #274

I wasn't sure what to expect other than a variety of breakfast and brunch foods.  What I found was pretty good food, some even really tasty, in a casual diner setting.  There was plenty of parking out front of this strip mall restaurant.  The outside and walls looked nicely decorated/styled though the floor was left as concrete (I'm not a fan of concrete floors in dining facilities that are stained from the previous owners.  Just looks dingy.)    We were quickly seated, had our orders taken and delivered and were given a self pour water bottle (no ice) for our beverages.  The water was chilled.    My wife ordered a Chicken Salad Melt that came with a choice of salad or soup.  She went with the Tomato Bisque.  She thought the sandwich was pretty good noting that the thick cut multi-grain toast was the tastiest part.  The toppings were good with nice portion size too.  She did say the soup was lackluster, tasting like the canned stuff we get at the grocery.    I ordered the special Heirloom Tomato & Burrata toast.  It had the same delicious toast as a base and was topped with marinated heirloom tomatoes, a hefty dollop of burrata cheese and lightly seasoned.  Very good!  I liked that I was given a steak knife which made quick work of the slicing.  The plate also had two sunny side up eggs which paired well with the main item.    I also tried the Millionaire's Bacon and though it did have a lot of tasty ingredients, the overall effect was disappointing.  There were four strips of hardwood smoked bacon laid out on the serving plate.  They seemed thick cut and appeared crisp (Yeah!)  They were coated with brown sugar, black pepper, cayenne, and maple syrup.  The first bite was tremendous!  Lots of depth to the flavor and the trailing heat was good.  However, the more I ate, the more I noticed the bacon seemed to be a bit chewy and soggy possibly due to the moisture in the other ingredients.  The heat definitely continued to build and eventually, for me, overwhelmed the bacon flavor.  Although I applaud the idea of mixing the flavors, I don't want to lose the bacon as the main taste.    Although you can either pay your waitress (which I did) or pay the cashier, I recommend paying up front since our server had just seated two more tables and was attending them when we were ready.  No big deal, but after collecting my card for payment, she handed the card to the cashier who then came back to the table for the signature.  So, to save yourself time and their staff effort, just pay up front.  Review #331

I dropped in for lunch on a Monday around noon to this neighborhood pub.  From the outside, it appears very dark inside and takes a moment for eyes to adjust to the lighting.  The front of the bar is a sports themed area, while the bar and booth seating areas tend to have a nautical theme.  The bar was full of customers engaged in conversations with each other, so I assume they were regulars.  I grabbed a seat across from the bar and waited to be noticed.  After a few minutes, I flagged down one of the two ladies tending to all the customers.  After a bit of time to peruse the menu, I decided to go with a salmon salad.  She suggested that there was a Blackened option  available, so I gladly took her up on the suggestion.  I was nearly floored when I saw the size of the salad.  It was huge!  The salad covered a 12 inch oval plate with an entree size salmon and an entire hard boiled egg on one side.  Lots of veggies in addition to the bed of lettuce.  The salmon was cooked correctly and the blackening lent a decent amount of flavor.  However, the iceberg lettuce and out of season tomatoes were more filler than flavor.  So, overall, decent flavor, but nothing I would be willing to make a special trip back for.  I think this place has great appeal for those who are regulars.  But for me, I can get similar or better flavors a lot closer to home.  Review #19

I happened to find this new business while filling time before a local concert.  This locally owned business grows about 70 percent of its grapes in Montgomery County (near Crawfordsville) and chose this location on Main to open its first tasting room.  Although the patio faces north, there is a south entrance from the convenient parking lot for the retail/housing complex.    I usually do wine tastings on my first visit, but because of my time constraint, opted to go with a chardonnay that is my default wine type.  I was offered a sample of the Yellowstone Creek (2017) and found it to be excellent!  So, with glass in hand, I browsed around a bit.  There are some tables for larger parties on the side opposite the order counter.  There are also some taller tables for folks to stand by in small numbers.  I selected one of those and noticed that the front patio was nearly ready for the season (it was raining and so the chairs were turned down to avoid holding water).  Inside the decor reflects the owner/president of the company's interest in rafting.  In fact, he stopped by to chat with me to see how I liked the place and the wine.  Very personable fellow who seems to really enjoy this new venture.  Interestingly, the wines take on the names of parks/rapids.  As I was wrapping up my visit, a local musician was setting up to provide entertainment for the evening's guests.  Good first taste.  I will have to stop by again to sample more of their offerings, and maybe pick up a bottle or two.  Review #2497

Even though I have driven by this place numerous times, it took a Small Business Saturday event for me to make time to drive here.  So glad I did!  If you are looking for antiques, and I mean just about any kind, it is worth stopping by here.  They have convenient parking in a small lot at the back of the store.  Inside, there are numerous rooms and nooks that are filled with so many different antiques that you may never be sure you've seen them all.    There are collectibles like vinyl, license plates, toys, kitchen ware.  There are numerous pieces of unique furniture and architectural enhancements.  They have an outdoor section (somewhat limited) for yard items.  And you never know what you will find next.    Maybe you are looking for a barnyard animal character to add some whimsy.  Maybe you are a wannabe big game hunter and want some stuffed trophies (there is a full sized crocodile hanging on one wall!)  Or maybe you want to find some items that you remember seeing as a kid, but had no idea where to find them.  Stop in here.  You just might be lucky!  I can't say how their prices compare to other places, but so much is unique, I don't know how I would be able to.  And if you are refinishing an older home and need some architectural items to finish the restoration, you should definitely explore here.  I can't say the pieces are ready to use, but if you know how to restore a piece, you can probably find what you are looking for here.  Friendly staff who were willing to let us browse without being hurried or pushed towards a purchase.  Check it out!  Review #3365

When you pull into the long, narrow parking lot that acts as a buffer between the row of businesses containing Ruth's Cafe and the always busy 86th Street by KatC, you can't help but wonder if you will find a parking space and if it's worth the effort.  It was packed, but the lunch was worth it!  Fortunately, we found one of the few open spots on the east end and had a short walk to the restaurant.  The interior was filled with a cacophony of sounds that mirror the visual bombardment of the walls, tables, and even chairs that walk the fine line of humorous and kitschy.  Every place you looked there was something different.  We were escorted to the second dining area and had a two-top near the front window where we could see a couple of outdoor tables for guests.  Inside, we had friendly and efficient service throughout the meal.  We were in and out in about 35 minutes.  My wife ordered the lunch combo and opted for the half soup/half salad.  She went with the Tomato Basil which was a full bowl portion!  The soup came with a small dish of croutons to add a little texture. She thought the soup out shown the egg salad which was the salad served over a bowl of mixed greens.  The salad was generously portioned as well, but was on the bland side.  Maybe some chopped sweet pickle or celery bits could have perked up the flavor.  I, however, really enjoyed my Bistro sandwich.  Another huge selection (sliced in halves) was basically a grilled chicken and BLT merged together with added Swiss cheese and the house Dijon Bistro sauce over a rosemary crusted Ciabatta roll.  Excellent taste!  The rosemary was on the surface only and was used lightly so as not to overwhelm the other flavors.  Great use of restraint on the baking.  The sandwich also came with a complementary dill pickle spear and my choice of side (I went with the fresh fruit cup).  I really enjoyed my meal.  Overall, I thought the cafe worthy of a stop if you don't mind the volume and are looking for something different from the fast food or food chain options.    Review #391

While looking for someplace new for me to try in the City Market, I remembered enjoying some food at a Yelp Event provided by Duos.  So, I made my way to the center aisle of the ground floor of the food hall and checked out the menu board posted behind the counter.  Although the local chain (3 locations in downtown) specializes in healthy food/vegan/vegetarian, I was glad to know that they do offer both tofu and chicken for some of their bowl entrees.    I opted for the "Balance Bowl" and added the shredded chicken breast to my order.  I paid and had just a short wait (less than five minutes) before my order was ready to go.  I grabbed some plasticware and napkins before leaving the counter.  The bowl had a light bedding of fresh spinach and had a mixture of brown rice, lots of veggies, black beans, and topped with a nice aioli for more flavor.  The chicken paired nicely with the meal.  I found the flavors good but it didn't have any "wow" factor for me.  I like that in a hall filled with items that aren't typically considered the most healthy, that this place offers a viable option for nutrition.  I also appreciate that they are able to produce their meals quickly so those who are on a limited time schedule can enjoy coming here.  Parking is always a challenge downtown, but there are some metered street parking spots in the area and a parking garage nearby if you are planning on staying awhile.  Review #3605

I wasn't sure what to expect on opening day of a new brewery.  Would the beers taste okay?  Would the staff be trained enough to keep up with the crowd while paying attention to the individual customers?  Would the food be any good?  Yes!  YEs!! YES!!!  The old High School of Whitestown was connected to the grade school by a gymnasium.  The gym is now half bar and dining, and half "The 1915 Room" for music and events held at the brewery.  (The HS was built in 1915.)  There is also a patio on the west side for nicer days.  The interior is a mix of industrial and woodsy with all the two tops being irregular shapes made from tree cuttings.  The bar has some high tops and quite a few tables and even some booths.  The dining area by the front entrance has two and four tops available.  The kitchen is located behind the bar but not visible.  I wanted to try a flight of beers since it was my first visit.  They had nine beers on tap and the flights come with the option of sampling 4 or 8 in 5 ounce glasses.  I went with a light lager "King of Troy" (5.5%, 16 IBU), and a German Hefeweizen "Hef-Czkowski" (5.6%, 12) which was good but not as clove dominant as some other Hef's I've tried.  I also enjoyed the Porter "Into the Void" (5.4%, 39) with hints of chocolate and caramel and the Stout "Bright Side of the Moon" (7.2%, 50) with a coffee signature taste and hints of cocoa and maple syrup.  Sorry, I didn't try any IPA's....you'll have to sample those for yourself!  The food was good too!  I ordered one of the flatbreads,  "Porky the Pig" which is served on a crisp, cracker like base with pulled pork, St Adrian sausage, bacon (thick), pickled red onion, mozzarella, and bbq sauce.  Yum!!  I also ordered a half corn on the cob that is smoked and coated with a rub and bbq sauce.  You have to expect smoked corn to be a bit overcooked, so it gets a little chewy, but the flavor was really good.  It reminded me of Mexican Street corn without the cheese.    The staff were friendly, ready to answer questions, suggested walking around to look at the place, and encouraging to those of us on social media.  Note:  The brewery is one block west of Main Street, but you can go through the parking lot on Main and either drive or walk through the lot to the main entrance on Bowers.  Review #708

I was over near St Francis Hospital and Professional buildings and relied upon Yelp to help me find a place to stop for lunch.  The highest rating in the area went to this cafe.  This place is one of many food selections in this strip mall just south of Stop 11 on South Emerson Avenue.  Lots of parking in the shared lot just outside the entrance.  Once inside, the brightly colored decor was playful and welcoming.  The staff was friendly and helpful.  (Note:  As good as the food was, the vibe of this place was as genuinely upbeat and friendly as I have encountered.  It seemed like a haven from all the devisive behavior in the news.)  The music, which was just a bit loud for my tastes, was generally light and upbeat.  After exchanging some light conversation with the staff, I placed my order at the counter, paid, and waited for them to bring my order out.  I started off with the Berry, Berry Good Smoothie.  This large, mind-numbingly cold drink was a blend of raspberries, strawberries, blueberries, blackberries, and banana with 20 g of vanilla whey protein.  If you like fruitty sweets, this is one to try.  I really enjoyed it!  I also ordered the Jamaican Jerk Chicken as a wrap (it can be served as a salad as well.)  I selected the orange colored "Mayo-Basil" wrap for my dish.  It comes with grilled chicken breast, Caribbean jerk seasoning, lettuce, cabbage, onions, rice, and mango salsa.  The serving size was huge!  So, a good value for the money.    So, why not 5 stars?  As good as the vibe and the smoothie were, I didn't have any "wow" moments from the main dish.  I understand that this is meant to be a healthy choice restaurant and I think they met that standard.  But because they are health conscious, I feel they used little salt in their wrap.  When they took away that flavor level, the supporting spices didn't elevate the wrap up to the flavors I have had elsewhere.  Maybe a bit more of the jerk spice could have made up for the reduced salt.  I'm sure they would have to test the seasoning to make sure they found the balance. But when added to the wrap, the greens and salsa, the chicken itself was a bit on the bland side.  Still good, and pretty healthy, just not a wow type sandwich.  Service was pretty quick and as I said, the positive mood and belief in their products went a long way in making this more than just another strip mall cafe.  Good luck to the staff and owners of this place.  I hope you do well!  Review #190

After seeing some good reviews on Yelp, I decided to stop by and give the restaurant a try!  This strip mall restaurant has plenty of parking but is a bit difficult to get to and out of due to being located at the busy intersection of US 31 and County Line Rd.    You basically have to be east bound on county line or south bound on 31 to get into the parking area.  The atmosphere has some color, but is still fairly stark.  So, it's not necessarily a place for meeting a date, but seems just fine for lunch.  I wasn't sure if I was supposed to help myself or grab a seat so I walked back into the restaurant.  I was directed to sit anywhere and was brought a menu.  There is a lot of non-English spoken between the employees, but they always spoke in understandable English with me.  (Some are more conversant than others.)  Since this was my first time at the restaurant, I played it safe and went for something recognizable to me:  Egg Rolls and Sweet and Sour Chicken.  Note that the Sweet and Sour also has beef and pork options, but the beef wasn't available on my visit.  All versions are served with a large helping of white rice.  The egg rolls (3 per order) come with a dipping sauce and are stuffed with carrots, rice noodles, and mushrooms.  They do have meat versions available as well for an upcharge.  To their credit, the egg rolls were brought out first.  They were steaming hot, so I needed to let them cool just a bit to avoid burning my palate.  The flavor was quite tasty and the outer shell was crisped although I did detect a bit of chewiness in the bite.  The dipping sauce was definitely a plus, although I am not certain I know the ingredients.    The star of the meal was the Sweet & Sour.  The chicken pieces were easy to pick up with my chopsticks and small enough to fit into my mouth without having to be cut first.  The white rice was served on a separate plate and came with a fork and table spoon to make transferring the rice much easier.  Unfortunately, the plate used for the chicken and sweet & sour sauce was sized for the entree without the rice, so I had to eat them separately until I got enough room to transfer some rice.  The chicken seemed like it was lightly breaded and worked well with the sauce.  The sauce should be called "3S" for sweet, sour, and SAVORY!  The sauce had a quality that seemed like it had been cooked slowly to allow all the flavors to come out.  Even after I finished my chicken, I kept transferring the rice to soak up as much of the sauce as I could.  I definitely recommend ordering this if you want to give the restaurant a try.  I would definitely return to try some of their soups and noodle dishes now that I know they have nailed the basics.  Glad to have another option on the south side of Indy that isn't another chain!  Review #195

After an afternoon of shopping around the Perry Crossing mall, we decided to stop for a late lunch at the Stacked Pickle.  It's located on the west end of the main strip and is conveniently located near the parking lot.  We stopped in and saw the sign that says to wait to be seated.  However, a second sign mentioned that for those of age, seating at the bar area was immediately available.  We headed on back to the tables there and before long, were greeted.  It took a moment to get menus (I think they could leave those on the tables), but it didn't take long to figure out what we wanted, so our wait times were brief.  My wife went with a tasty Honey BBQ (Chicken) Wrap that was huge!  It came with fries that she said were perfectly crisped but were unseasoned, so a little salt was helpful.  The wrap was sliced in half as presented and my wife immediately knew she would need a to go box.  She thought the flavor of the meal really good.  I decided to go with something different.  I ordered the chicken wings with Jerk (Caribbean) seasoning and Ranch Dressing on the side.   I also added a side of mixed veggies (steamed, not al dente).  The veggies (carrots, broccoli, cauliflower) were fork tender and I liked being able to dip them in the Ranch for a bit more flavor.  The Jerk Chicken (8 pcs) were decent sized with lots of meat.  The seasoning was a dry rub and was generously added (a small mound was left in the center of the plate when I finished.)  The seasoning was very savory and just a tad salty, which paired really well with the chicken.  Note that because they are so liberal with the seasoning, the seasoning can get on your hands and face quite easily.  You may need extra napkins from your table stand.  The bartender/waiter was friendly and did a good job of keeping up with our order.  Wait times were brief between visits.  I was pleasantly surprised at the food quality and was glad I stopped by this local food chain started by one of the former Colts.  Review #3448

After visiting Gallery 924 on Penn, I decided to head a few blocks south to check out the newest addition to neighborhood restaurants.  Located in the former Elbow Room, this new business(es) maintained a lot of the interior architectural details while giving it a thorough cleaning and making it seem less crowded.  They also maintained the outdoor seating that is on the Ft Wayne St side once the weather cooperates.  As you enter from Pennsylvania St, the Point is on your right.  The left side is a small connected building that hosts "The Flatiron" which is an evening/dinner side of the business for food and drinks.  There is also a stairway that leads to the "Upper Room" which can be reserved for private parties and has the wine "cellar".  (Otherwise, the space is not open.)  When you head towards the order counter of the Point, there is a comfy lounge area with four stuffed chairs and a small central table.  I wasn't sure if patrons could dine there or simply wait for their to go orders, or wait to be seated in the small interior dining room.  The dining room consists mainly of a single row 2-top tables with bench seating on one side and a chair on the alternate.  At the actual point of the restaurant, there is a larger table that has an excellent window view of downtown.  The east half of the point has the order counter, then displays of "KK's" pastries, and a food prep area behind another counter where they call out your name once your food is ready so that you can pick it up.  There is also an "extra" station where utensils, sugars, napkins, sauces, etc. are self help.  The staff was very friendly and welcoming.  Service was very prompt too!  But there were some things that can be improved upon.  Their schedule is a bit confusing with KK's opening at 7:30, full breakfast opens at 8, then switching to lunch at 11 (until 3 on their website),  and then closing that side and moving over to the Flatiron for dinner, but the website doesn't say when that side opens and for how late.  They could simplify this.  Do they stop serving breakfast at 11 or can you still get something from that menu?  Why not open the breakfast at the same time as the pastry side to avoid confusion or making someone wait an additional half hour to get something more than a pastry?  They also ran out of steak and avocado by 11 am, so the steak salad was not an option and any of their lunch items that had avocado were also off the available options.  When I reviewed the overhead menu, the hostess/cashier mentioned they had fish and chips as their specialty.  (Though not on the menu board or the website.)  I decided to go with that as my order.  Although I ordered my meal for dining in, it was put in a to go box that had three fish fillets (battered cod) and was loaded with house made, lightly salted potato chips, not traditional English chips that are thicker.  My initial thought was that it was rather expensive for frozen fish and chips, but I realized as I ate that the fish was light and flaky, so much so that I wasn't sure if it was house made or commercially prepared.  It was that good!  And the portion was generous with enough chips left over that I ended up making use of the to go box to take the chips home.  I had a pleasant overall experience and I understand that prices have to be higher to cover the rent (the building owners got too expensive for the Elbow Room to stay), but the food quality was solid and not too pricey for downtown.  I think I would return and try some of their soups and/or sandwiches to get a better idea of the Chef's vision.  It's nice to have options for dining in the area just a bit north of the circle.  Review #2492

If you like finding products that aren't carried at the big box stores, then this is the place to shop!  The store is filled with shelves of all kinds of small items from greeting cards to cosmetics, t-shirts to specialty food items.  I was greeted and asked if I needed any help to find something.  Since it was my first time, I wasn't sure what I was looking for and just spent time browsing to see what they had.  It seems they find small businesses/artisans around the country and group them on shelves beside related items to make the store have a flow to it.  I did notice a large selection of t-shirts and many had clever comments on them.  However, they stack the folded shirts in front of the displayed ones, which makes it hard to stand back and read them all at once.  (The folded ones often didn't reveal the entire message.)  So, if they could put a description of what they carry on a label or clip board, that would make it easier for the customer.  I was enjoying my browsing without giving into impulse buying until I got to the counter near the check out.  There I found a selection of Newfangled Creations' "Frittle" and B. Happy Peanut Butter's "Joy to the World".  I feel bad for folks who have peanut allergies because these two products are so delicious!  I'm grateful that I can eat anything without consequences.    A pleasant, no pressure buying experience with lots of unique items to choose from awaits at Homespun.  Great ideas for gift giving along with the cards too!  Review #2684

In the old town part of Whitestown, there is a friendly cafe on the southwest corner of the traffic stop.  Inside the restaurant, there is a separate room to the left, a bar on the near right, and more dining room seating to the far right.  Above the bar, real motorcycles are displayed which fits the theme of the place.  The dining room is filled with four top tables with white linen tablecloths, topped with large sheets of white paper for easy clean up.  My wife and I were greeted at the hostess desk and shown to our seats.  They have a variety of soups, salads, and sandwiches, including some lunch specials available.  My wife ordered the breaded tenderloin which was good, but a bit over cooked so it was a bit dry.  I went with the Reuben and it was excellent!  It came with the thousand island dressing on the side, so I could adjust the flavor accordingly.  The sauerkraut was almost sweet and blended with the savory taste of the corned beef and the acidity in the dressing for a really great taste.  The bread was a marbled rye that had a little bit of char from the grilling.  I highly recommend.  And the portions were large, so we ended up getting a to go box.    The service was friendly and brought refills on the beverages as well as making checkout quick and easy.    If you like getting out and exploring, make a point to stop by here.  Review #2136

Note:  This review is for their remote site vending at Penrod, not a dining experience at their restaurant.  While wandering around at Penrod, I noticed a new vendor that was serving some delightful smelling sandwiches.  Turns out the business was just open a few months downtown in the Salesforce tower and had eluded my "radar" of new places.  So I hopped in line.    While waiting, I overheard people thinking they were waiting for Portillo's, the Italian chain.  Fortunately they figured it out before getting all the way to the front of the line.  The restaurant was hustling to keep the line moving and the guy working the register was in good spirits.  I wish more businesses recognized how important that first contact is for making a good impression.    The menu here was rather narrow with a list of roasted pork (Porketta was my choice), brisket, or chicken.  (They have some salads too.)  All the meat choices are served on a thick Italian Hoagie bun.  You then let them know what ingredients you want added (they have suggestions for each option.)  They do offer variations of sandwich types at the restaurant, but still focus on the three primary ingredients as bases.  The flavor was really good as I selected the sharp cheddar, a broccoli rabe, and a garlic sauce.  The only negative is that the bread is really thick and though it holds up well to support the sandwich, I found myself not eating all the bun since the meat wasn't "end to end' on the sandwich.  I didn't mind that the sandwich wasn't "full", but that the bread was too thick and made it difficult to eat without squishing it a bit.  I enjoyed the sandwich and service, just hope that they dial in the bread selection to improve the ratio to ingredients.  Review #2991

I don't really feel drawn to diners.  I usually have low expectations and in some cases, have felt uncomfortable as an outsider (especially afterwards if I don't give it a great review.)  But when I heard the Peppy Grill was reopening after having closed last November (2018), I was intrigued.  I had been to most of the restaurants in Fountain Square/Fletcher Place, so I stopped by for lunch at this nearly 70 year old survivor.  Even after going through some upgrades and improvements (adding a covered seating area outside and some new equipment inside), the place still retains a diner feel.  Plush red bench seats in the dining room rest on a classic black and white tile floor.  The bar is on the left towards the back.  They do have wait service, but I chose to sit at the bar.  I was greeted and was given a menu and delivered my beverage promptly.  I ordered the Breaded Tenderloin and a side of fries (sandwiches are a la carte.)  I also spent the extra $0.35 for the deluxe toppings of onion, lettuce, pickles, Mayo, and tomatoes.  (Note they have salt, ketchup and mustard at each table and on the bar counter.)  However, they don't have napkin dispensers and the staff forgot to napkins with the meals.  Hopefully they will remedy that soon.  The tenderloin was large, but not ridiculous and had a tasty breading while staying moist inside.  The deluxe ingredients were stacked in the middle of the bun, so after a little arranging on my part, I got a taste of everything in each bite.    The fries were skin on and cut long.  Served unseasoned, I was glad there was a salt shaker nearby.  Good flavor, but just a little bit under cooked  which left them a bit limp.  Not bad, just not quite dialed in.  Check out was prompt and I was soon on my way.  Looks like they have some umbrella tables outside but I would suggest asking at the bar if you can sit there.  Not sure they have a waitress assigned to watch the outdoor seating.  There is also a patio area, but it wasn't set up for dining at my visit.  It's nice to see an historic diner continue to make it among all the new businesses.  It's a very affordable option that is open around the clock, though it is just a bit higher than fast food.  But it is food made to order.  And that is worth the price.  Fun fact:  The sign out front adverises "Hamburgs", not hamburgers.  Review #3058

Although I've only had limited transactions here, I have to say that service I received was prompt and accurate.  Although my wife bought her computer while we were at the Best Buy on the north side, when we learned having the start up (adding all the software & antivirus) would take several hours (up to 24), we found that we could take the computer to the store closest to us and avoid having to make the long drive again.  So, we dropped off the computer and a few hours later, it was ready.  I went to pick up the computer, and after showing ID, was able to pick up the computer for my wife (who had made the purchase).  It only took a couple minutes for the tech to bring it out, and launch the computer to demonstrate it worked.  No mess, no fuss.  I was soon on my way.  I see some negative reviews, but I honestly can't think of any other store I would take the purchase of a new computer to in the metro area.  Review #3679

I've lost count of the number of times I've driven by Bungalow, so I decided to pull into their convenient parking lot and stop in.  I was greeted by the staff and a friendly pup that welcomed me.  The shop, though somewhat small, had a nice selection of clothing, both serious and whimsical (think fancy socks!), mugs, books, and home decor items.  I didn't really think of this as a furniture place that you might guess by the image of the polka dotted mural on the east side of the building.  But it was a cool gift shop sort of place that I could see finding something unique, often humorous, for someone.  Definitely worth checking out the next time you are near the canal!  Review #2104

I stopped by on Friday for lunch and although there was a nice sized crowd, I could get in the door (unlike the opening week!).  There is a small parking lot in front of the restaurant that is shared with the grocery and coffee shop.  It is a bit of a tight fit, so you may want to choose some street parking on the south side of the lot as a better option.  The restaurant is one that you may place your order at the counter (plastic menus are available to read or you may read from the overhead menu behind the counter.)  Once you pay, you are given a number to take to your table and they bring out your food when it is ready.  They ask you to be patient since it is not "fast food" despite looking like it.  No heat lamps here keeping things kinda hot until you order.  I ordered the Original burger (1/4# of pasture raised beef) with Mug sauce, American Cheese, LTOP, on a plain, soft bun.  I also went with the "Fresh-cut Fries".    The burger was thin and had a nice char without being dry.  I am not sure I can describe the Mug sauce flavor, but it was unique to my burger experience and a pleasant surprise.  I definitely recommend it.  The fries were generously portioned and had a crispy crunch.  The lard used in cooking adds a little flavor, but because the crunch layer is thick compared to the overall thickness of the fries, the potato flavor is muted.  The server asked if I wanted catsup and salt for the fries, but instead of a bottle and shaker, I was given a packet of each.  Sure, I could have grabbed more from a central display inside, but I would definitely prefer have bottles and shakers so that I didn't have to tear open a bunch of packets.  (Am I the only one who finds it odd that the place is promoting natural foods, but using lots of plastic and paper packets?)  Anyway, since I didn't grab any additional salt and catsup, the fries didn't have the flavor that I expected.  Note:  you can add toppings to your fries for more flavor for an upcharge  I noted garlic and pulled pork options while there.  The menu has desserts, beer, and wine available to go with their assorted sandwiches and sides.  The staff seemed positive and efficient.  The only negative is that a number of folks who were getting their food to go or waiting on others to join them tended to congregate in front of the counter.  (Maybe they should make some sort of line to help newcomers.)    So, if you want to grab a decent burger and fries while in Irvington, give this place a try.   Review #159

I've been to a lot of craft and hobby stores, including several other Michaels in the area, and I have to say this is one of my favorites!  Not only did the store have a tidy appearance, but it was well stocked with the types of items I expect.  Sure, there are some other places that are even larger and have items like furniture and faux antiques, but I wouldn't buy those types of things anyway.  Here, they have rows of crafts, florals, accessories, and a few other items like toys.  Basically, they had what we were looking for.  When we had a little trouble finding a specific item in the craft section, one of the employees brought us directly to the item.  And checkout was prompt, even opening another register to help us through.    I wish the Michaels closer to home were as well managed and operated as this one.  Review #3652

After dinner, I noticed an independent bookstore in the shopping center I was in (near Steinmart).  I believe it is owned by the same folks who run the Books for Sale shop in Southern Plaza on the south side of Indy.  What first caught my attention was that this place was huge!  There were all kinds of books, some filed by category on regular shelves, but also tables where some special categories or fan favorites were placed.  They also had vinyl and tapes/cd's as well.  There were comics and graphic novels, lots of kids books, and just about any other category you might think of.  The only problem with used book stores is that they may not have that one item in a series that you are looking for.  But, there is a lot of turnover and if you want the discount prices, you have to be vigilant.  And speaking of discounts, the rule of thumb is that if you pay for three items, you get a 4th and 5th items (the lower cost ones of the bunch) for free.  You don't have to get them all in the same genre or shelf either.  Anywhere in the store that has the signs on the book shelves are eligible. Seemed like a good deal.  I thought the books I was picking up were priced very affordably as it was, but to then get the freebies was like a great deal!  Plenty of parking and there are even a couple comfy spots to sit down inside the store.  Seems like the guy inside was friendly and helpful and he was able to direct me to some items related to what I was looking for.  Check them out!  Review #2286

I stopped in for a quick lunch on Wednesday since I was exploring the near north and the SoBro areas.  Although the interior of the restaurant was quite dark, my eyes finally adjusted enough by the time I was seated.  Having already perused the menu before arriving, I was able to place my order for the Warm Spinach (salad) and the Boar Bolognese (entree) when my waiter arrived.  I really appreciate when a restaurant works with me to cut down wait times, so getting seated through getting my bill paid in less than 35 minutes was fantastic!  The warm spinach was a generous portion of baby spinach greens that were almost large enough to need a knife for cutting, but I found most bites were manageable.  The toppings included tomato, onion, chopped eggs, small mushroom pieces, and a bacon vinaigrette.  There was also a mystery sweet element to the salad that complimented the flavor combos.  The Boar Bolognese listing on the menu didn't address the specific meat used in the pasta dish, but if they follow the online recipes suggestions, would probably be wild boar and bacon/prosciutto.  The pasta was cavatappi (spiral shaped about an inch long and 1/2 inch coil) with Parmesan.  Mixed in with the meat was a spicy essence of carrots, celery, and onions.  All were finely chopped so that no individual flavor dominated.  In fact, the spicy heat tended to build the more I ate, so my only negative would be that the heat masked some of the flavor.  What I had was good, just wish the heat would have been a tad less.     The portion of the pasta dish was rather large and if you are a light eater, I would suggest splitting it with a friend or planning on a "to go" box.  The pasta came with a deliciously buttery length of crisp crostini.  I could munch on that all day!  Overall, a very nice experience, with good service and tasty food.  I definitely recommend giving this place a try for your next fancy meal.  Review #161

I took my wife to brunch on the restaurant's second weekend and had an enjoyable experience.  Although there is indoor seating, we opted to dine outside on the floral patio.  (Note that you have to check in the restaurant through the door on the north end of the hotel.  This requires climbing a couple steps to get in.)  We were able to grab free street parking out front, but there is additional street parking on the southern cross street near the restaurant.  Our service was friendly and attentive even though our server was covering both indoor and outdoor customers.  Fortunately, the crowd was relatively small and between the server and the hostess, we didn't have to wait long.  We were given a carafe of chilled water for the table so that we wouldn't have to wait long if our water glasses were running low.  My wife decided to order from the savory side of the brunch menu.  She opted for the Croque Madame.  This plate had a base of Pain de Mie (bread) with a salty country ham (cut about 1/8 inch thick), Emmantaler (cheese), a sunny side up egg, and a house made mornay sauce (tasted like it had a hint of horseradish.)    I went with a plate from the sweet side of the menu:  Hummingbird Pancakes with a side of Becker Farms Bacon.  The pancakes came with a rum creme anglaise and was topped with fresh bananas and pineapple, as well as walnuts (lightly candied?)  The flavor was good on both our plates.  Although we loved the setting and atmosphere and thought the service was very good, we felt that the execution of the meals was just a little off.  Since there was already a lot of saltiness from the ham, she thought the eggs were salted as well (she tried them separately) and the combination was too salty for her.  I got a sample bite and it was fine on its own, but I could see how eating the entire plate of food could accumulate the saltiness.  She also thought the ham was a little tough to cut through.  On my plate, the pancakes were a little doughy (they were done, but dense) in the middle and the spices used to add to the flavor profile were distributed a little unevenly.  The combos of the fruit and the spices were really good in some bites, but in others, the pineapple, served fresh, overbalanced the other items.  Maybe if they served the pineapple carmelized, it would balance better.  Overall, we enjoyed our experience and plan to return to try the dinner menu.  It's just that if you are going to charge around $12 for a breakfast plate, you really have to nail the execution.  I hope they can find their footing as they are open longer.  Review #354

Normally, I get up early and fix breakfast for myself, so going out for coffee or brunch is more the exception for me.  But as a fan of trying new places, especially small businesses in my home town, I made plans to try out this coffee house.  After parking in the free public lot about a half block west of the coffee house, I strolled into what I thought was a shotgun style building (long and narrow).  The main room has a long counter where you can grab a bar stool to watch the staff as they pull together your order.   There are also a few small tables.  What I didn't expect was that there is also a large dining area on the west side (actually part of the building next door) that has plenty of seating if you decide to bring a group of friends.  When I entered just after 8 a.m., there was a line of customers near the register.  I assumed they were getting orders to go, so I grabbed a seat.  However, when I saw someone who arrived after me place their order, I thought that maybe I should have stayed in line.  But here's the thing:  Everyone was so nice!  A young man who had seen me seated let me get back in line and allowed me to place my order.  I asked the staff about the placement of orders and was told that if you are concerned about going in exact order or are under a time constraint, then it probably is good to get in line.  But otherwise, if you are relaxing, they will get to you.  So, not exactly waitress service, but they do bring out your order if you decide to grab a seat.  (Note:  You pay when you place your order.)  I ordered a standard black coffee, but they do have a variety of flavored coffee options and related hot beverages.  They also have coke products if you aren't a coffee person. There is usually one savory option made fresh each day (they start baking at 4 a.m.)   I ordered a Sausage Salsa Frittata which gets briefly reheated in a microwave to bring out all the flavors.  Very tasty!  I also wanted to try the daily special Orange Glazed Mango Muffin (served at room temp).  This muffin was large, but light and moist.  The orange flavor paired well with the mango and both flavors went well with my coffee.  Excellent!  Since my wife wasn't able to go with me, I decided to pick up a cinnamon roll to go.  They suggested heating it in the microwave for 30 seconds to warm it up.  When I got it home, the icing was not thick and gooey.  It was more liquid in nature and spread out over the sides of the roll as I cut into it.  The icing was lighter and not sickeningly sweet like some other rolls I have had.  I really appreciated that aspect of the icing.  The staff was very friendly and welcoming and seemed to enjoy their work.  They seemed to know quite a few of the patrons and didn't let the rush of people bother them.  When not swamped, they graciously answered a number of questions I had about the business.    FYI:  They do have gluten free options.  They also make all the pastries from scratch, no mixes.  Most items are made fresh daily with the exception of the pies which are made a day ahead so that they can set up properly before serving.  I enjoyed my food and visit at this coffee house and look forward to my return visit to try some of the tasty looking pies!  Review #369

I really enjoy finding places that fit their neighborhood, and in this case, are a gathering place for locals.  Inside, the folks who volunteer here were all welcoming and upbeat.  And the coffee was fresh, tasty, and ready to drink without a long wait to cool.    In addition to the coffee, there are some baked goods to grab if you're hungry.  And did I mention that a small coffee is only $1?  What a deal!  The space is simply decorated with a huge dining area/gathering space that has a pool table, a communal table made from a wooden door, and there's a laundry available (I don't know the specifics of that).    I was also able to buy some fresh ground coffee that is a special blend made just for Lincoln Lane.  If you like what you try and can't get here often, just do like I did and buy a bag to go!  Review #2609

I stopped by on a chilly Tuesday for a late lunch after running errands in Greenwood.  This place shares the building with a Family Video store on the south east corner of the Greenwood Mall property (north west corner of Frye and Madison).    The signs out front and on the side mention sushi, but guess what.  They no longer have sushi on the menu and the waiter confirmed that they don't have it any longer.  So, scratch that from my selections.  I decided to go with a cup of Rangoon Tea/Coffee based on other Yelper suggestions and followed that with a bowl of Steak Noodle Pho.  The tea was served at a drinkable temperature and was surprisingly sweet!  I know I've tasted the underlying flavor before, but I'm unable to determine what it reminded me of.  Whatever it was, it was great.  (Note that a single cup was plenty for me.  I don't believe you get free refills.)  Before long, by large bowl of Pho arrived with a fork and Asian soup spoon (ceramic).  It also had a small plate with sliced pepper (looked like jalapeno), mint sprigs, and raw bean sprouts.  I also received bottles of Hoisin and Sriracha sauces.    I must admit I have had Pho three times previously and was clueless on what was proper.  So I You Tubed it and solved the problem.  I added the individual leaves off the mint, the sprouts, and the pepper slices and stirred them in, letting the hot broth semi-cook the new ingredients and let their flavor spread into the pho.    The broth was tasty even before I added the new ingredients, so I really enjoyed the perked up flavor.  At the bottom of the bowl, the long rice noodles (think white thin spaghetti) and the thin sliced beef nestled.  I think the owners realize that most Hoosiers would struggle using chopsticks to fish out noodles, so the fork was a welcome tool.  And whenever I speared a bit of the steak, I dipped it in the Hoisin sauce I had put on my small serving bowl that the soup spoon had been delivered in.  The steak (and probably all the meat options) don't have a lot of seasoning since they soak in the broth, so dipping the pieces directly in the Hoisin makes for a much tastier bite.  Yes, the meat gets a bit chewy, but because it is sliced thin, it wasn't difficult to get used to.  (I am not sure how the shrimp would hold up since I am not a fan of it when it gets rubbery.)  The dining room was pretty sparse, so the noise level was low even with some classic rock playing softly in the background.  Not much atmosphere inside, but the bright tangerine walls and a few decorative plates kept it from looking too sterile.  Overall, a good meal (huge quantity) and nice service all at an affordable price.   Now, if they would just take down those Sushi signs...  Review #2219

After meeting our son to look at his latest construction project, he suggested coming to Boathouse Grill for lunch.  He had eaten here about ten times during the project and said he really liked everything he tried.    So although I wasn't thrilled on my previous visit, I decided to give it a try.  And I am glad I did!  Although not much has changed in the three years since my last visit, this time I ordered the Italian Beef (served on a hoagie) and it was delicious!  The giardiniera veggies, Provolone cheese, and the au jus made a wonderful combination with the tender sliced beef.  The bread held up well even after dipping it in the sauce.  It was soft and thin enough bread to not make this difficult to get a full bite.  My wife said her taco salad had a crispy shell and the seasoned chicken had a pleasant taste.  Thought the sauce was just a little hot, but other than that, she really enjoyed her meal too.  The place does get full around lunch time and quite noisy.  The waitress got busier as the crowd rolled in, so other than it taking a little longer to get our check and processed out, the service was good.  Seems like a popular spot on 56th just between I-65 and I-465.  Rev. #42

My wife and I stopped in this small, no frills restaurant for lunch.  It's tucked away in a strip mall on the north side of 82nd street near several other restaurants and bars.  When we arrived, we were the only ones in the place.  We were greeted and were able to pick our own seating (booths and tables are available.)    I started with a cup of Green Tea that was quite good. (Note they sell it by the cup, not by the tea pot as other places do.)  Because we ordered entrees, we each were brought a bowl of a chicken broth (with a few veggies) to start the meal.  Well seasoned, though not visually appealing.  My wife ordered the Fried Rice with chicken while I ordered the Sesame Pork which is both sweet and spicy.  She thought her chicken was cooked properly (not too rubbery) and the rice had a fair amount of flavor.    My entree came with about a cup of white rice and a pair of fried cream cheese rangoon that were light and crisp.  The rice was a great side for gathering more of the sauce that had coated the entree.  The heat was moderate but definitely noticeable.  The sweet took on a citrus flavor as well.  The pork was cut in slender strips and were just a hint over cooked, but not enough to detract from the flavor.  Our waitress/manager (?) was really friendly and easy to communicate with.    Fortunately, a number of guests started arriving for both dine in and take out, so it looks like we simply beat the rush.    I do think the only negative for us was that the place could use a good deep cleaning to make sure everything is dust free and the bathrooms could use a good scouring.  But all table tops and dishes were clean, so we weren't concerned.  Review #3678

Nothing like having a good cup of coffee ready to drink when you take your seat in a coffee house.  Throw in some tasty banana nut bread and you are off to an even better start.  And when the staff is friendly when they greet you and seem like they really appreciate your stopping by, that makes for a 5 star rating!  This new coffee shop is in a stand alone building on Southport Road, just west of Madison.  They sit a bit below street level, so be careful driving down the slope and turn to the right if you need to find additional parking in the rear.    Inside, the surfaces shine and the place has lots of wood grain finish on the tables, walls, and counter.  As you walk in, you see their merchandise and ground coffee that you can buy for home.  The order counter is fairly straight back with the pastry selections below.  They don't have a menu mounted on the wall, so I had to wait until it was my turn to order to see what they had.  (They could have the order menus somewhere more visible so that you could decide while you wait.)  When your order is ready, they call your name and pass it along a bit farther down the counter.  Seating was plentiful for mid-morning and most folks seemed to be on their phones and computers.  I simply enjoyed having my black drip coffee served at an appropriate (non-scalding) temperature so that I could enjoy it with my pastry.    Overall, it was a fast and pleasant experience that I recommend checking out!  Review #2737

Although I didn't get a haircut, I did stop by on a chilly autumn afternoon to grab a cup of coffee.  Turns out they still had some tasty looking croissants from Circle City Sweets still available too, so I placed my order for a black coffee and Ham & Cheese Croissant.  The coffee was made to order, so though it took a minute or two, it was served ready to drink!  Anyone who regularly follows my reviews knows that I deduct points for coffee served scalding hot.  This was perfect!  And with the giant croissant (light and flaky, but with just enough chew to make the buttery and savory tastes linger), I really needed for the coffee to be ready to drink so that I could enjoy the croissant.  The barista was very easy going and helpful since this was my first time here.  We chatted about local art and music while he worked.  Not stand offish like some places.  Very welcoming.  Note that the location is below ground level and does require being able to negotiate steps to get to the coffee shop.  (Note you can get to the barber shop via an opening in the wall of the coffee shop.)  Note 2:  Because this shop shares the block with Needlers Fresh Market, you can park in the shared lot for FREE for 2 hours.  Plenty of time to grab a coffee/beverage and a bite to eat.  If you like checking out new places or are looking for one you can stop by and get some work done while enjoying a beverage, give this place a try!  Review #3283

Location! Location! Location!  If you like walking through a wooded space along a river, this place is for you!  This 62 acre mature park has a lot of options for visitors of all ages.  A family center, swimming pool and spray park, a dog park (requires a pass from the family center showing your dog has its shots and fees are associated), large playground, shelters (can be rented, but otherwise are first come/first served), and sports fields are here with plenty of space between them.  There are lots of events held here too, so check out their website for a list.  Fun fact #1:  This park used to be the site of the carousel that is in the Children's Museum during the 1920's.    Fun fact #2:  This park used to have the steam locomotive that is is at the Transportation Museum in Noblesville.  Review #588

This restaurant has figured out how to handle quick service with the benefits of a "sit down" restaurant.  I have dined at several Greek and Mediterranean places around central Indiana and Madd Greeks has found its niche.  The hardest part of going to Madd Greeks is dealing with some of the crazy intersecting traffic and one way streets.  To make it easier, there is a parking garage located right behind the strip of food shops on 10th Street and the parking is FREE for the first 60 minutes.  My advice?
