Look on line to see what interests you so you can save time and avoid paying for parking!  They do have parking metered street parking out front, but that is a matter of luck getting one of those.  (Note:  The parking garage and the street it is on are narrow, so big vehicles may have a little difficulty.  Once you are in the garage, turn right after entering instead of going straight.  Right = up; straight = dead end.)  There is a convenient rear entrance from the back street into Madd Greeks.  Once inside, they have ample seating for you to choose from.  I was greeted within a minute of picking a table.  Since I knew what I wanted, I had my fresh meal brought out to me in less than 10 minutes (maybe closer to 5!)    I ordered one of the pita types, the "Walking" pita with Chicken Shawarma as my meat filling.  (They have quite a few choices or you can go vegetarian if you prefer.)  The Walking pita is a folded pita wrapped around the strips of meat, lettuce, tomato, and onions and topped with fries (yes, inside the wrap).  I got to choose from two types of sauce, going with the Tzatziki for mine.  And the standard chips were anything but!  They were thicker cut and still warm and crisp when served.  They had a little bit of salt/seasoning which made them quite tasty too.  Even though the place was fairly busy, I was in and out in less than a half hour, bill payment included.  Friendly, efficient, and tasty.  That's good enough for me!  Review # 431

I stopped here on a bit of misinformation.  I had put in "CD Stores" in the Yelp search and because Yelp groups DVDs & Music together, I was given this location as the closest spot.  The store is located in the fringe shops by the Walmart on South US 31.  Parking is plentiful, but spaces close by are hit or miss.    When I entered, I saw that the shop was arranged with long rows of organized cases.  There were DVDs, Blu Ray, and Video Games of all kinds.  It appears that most rows were arranged alphabetically, so it took just a bit of quick scanning to get to the titles of interest.  Sadly, no CDs here.  I did notice a few things while I browsed.  Apparently, all the shelf items are empty, presumably to reduce shoplifting.  I assume you take the cases up to the back of the store counter and they get the contents for you when you pay.  I also found that there are discounts listed in the shop so that if you buy five items, you get the sixth one free.  Even during a weekday, the shop was really busy, so it looks like the place has figured out how to make the best of a second hand market in the face of a growing streaming surge.  Review #3701

Review for Pick-up order, not dine in:  After catching an afternoon movie, I didn't feel like fixing dinner or dining out, so I stopped by Chicago's and placed an order for a "Skyline" (supreme) pizza.  I went ahead and paid at the counter and then used one of the seats in the lobby of the restaurant to wait (about 15 minutes) for my thin crust pizza to be ready.  Even though I was waiting, I was asked what name to put on the pizza order.  While waiting, I noticed that the location has a separate room by the entrance that appears to have garage doors that can open in season to create a patio.  Otherwise, the space seems like just additional seating.  I will say that I made sure to check my pizza before leaving and was very pleased.  The ingredients were evenly spaced and even though there was pepperoni, there wasn't any greasy build up on top.  The crust was thin and crisp (my wife's favorite style) and the slices were cut to smaller sections which helped keep the topping on.  Some purists might complain they can't fold this pie, but I don't care about that.  I just wanted to eat something tasty with a nice crunch.    Thanks Chicago's!  Job well done!  Review #3530

My wife and I stopped in for lunch while shopping in Greenwood.  I forgot how huge the portions are...even at lunch time.  We had efficient and pleasant service and enough food for my wife to request a "to go" box.  There is always plenty of parking since the restaurant is in a strip mall next to Old Time Pottery.  We entered and were greeted and seated promptly.  There are over 500 types of beer available, so I opted to try a local draft that was new to me.  I was brought samples (small in plastic cups) that were enough to tell which I liked best. The price was $7 for my draft, $6 for my wife's canned variety  The lunch itself was pretty tasty and the sides are huge!  My wife wanted onion rings, but we made the mistake of ordering the mound the last time, so she asked what her options were.  She could get the half order or a side.  She choose the side and it was still enough to share between the two of us.  It came with a Cajun Ranch for dipping that was good.  The rings are the thin and mostly crispy kind, not the thick sweet battered ones.  Still, there was enough flavor to make them enjoyable.  My wife ordered the taco salad and it came served on a bed of pinto beans.  She went with the "taco meat" selection (instead of chicken strips) and thought it was really good.  I knew when they brought it that she wouldn't be able to finish it in one sitting, especially after the onion rings.  I went with the 5 ounce top sirloin lunch special which comes with a baked potato.  I opted for the side salad for another $2.  The salad came out fairly soon and it covered an 8 inch plate.  The greens are served mostly intact or at least in large pieces, so I ended up needing to cut them down to bite-sized pieces.  I liked that the dressing is delivered on the side allowing me to select how much I wished to add.  The steak was cooked correctly and was quite tender.  It comes with a variety of herbs/spices on top that added a different flavor profile than the steak I serve at home.  It was different, but fine.  I'm just someone who prefers the taste of beef to be dominant, with maybe a bit of buttery flavored shallots, but the flavor was okay.  The steak is dwarfed by the huge baked potato that comes with the meat.  It had to be close to a pound of potato as it took up nearly one half of the plate!  I got the butter and sour cream which looked like a lot when brought out, but the potato was so big that I used most of the butter and cream anyway!  Our server was courteous, efficient, and was visible without being intrusive.  Good job on her part!  If you are looking for a place that is filled with visual interest and a definite antique feel to the decor, then give Shallos a try.  And bring an appetite!  Preview #244

I'm not sure why this place is so popular with the other reviews.  I have been to a lot of furniture and consignment places in the past few months and I found the inventory small, random, and not really anything that grabbed my attention.  I think I spent more time trying to find the place than shopping.  Once you climb the stairs near loading dock 10, the front area looks promising.  It seems coordinated and decorated with cohesive pieces.  But once you enter the warehouse with its concrete floors and walls, you realize that the majority of the space is "employees only" and you can only shop a long single aisle.  Very little as far as wall decor was on display compared to other places.  If I am going to take the time to get out and shop, I think I would go to some other places around the metro area where they have more of a selection.  Review #2090

I enjoyed my visit to Insomnia Cookies.  I saw that they offer something called a Cookiewich:  your choice of two warm cookies with your choice of ice cream in between.  They serve it on a small plate with a plastic spoon.  The flavor was great with the chocolate chip in the cookie being somewhat melted and the Moose Tracks ice cream juxtaposed with its cool crunch.    The only problem is eating it.  The cookiewich was to thick to get a proper bite and the plastic spoons aren't sharp enough to cut through.  I ended up deconstructing the treat eating the cookie by hand (you WILL need napkins) and ice cream by spoon.    Very friendly gal behind the counter who was very helpful and even asked if there was enough ice cream.    Lots of flavors of cookies are available individually or in groups.  Ice cream too!  Or you can make combos by adding ice cream or frosting to your cookies.  Not cheap, but this is more about serving that immediate craving rather than getting full.    Review #2703

This was my first visit to Beasley's Orchards and I must say that I was very pleased with my visit.  Not only do they have an orchard, but there was a decent sized parking area, a play area and corn maze (both require a fee), and a store.  The store has a sampling of apples and garden vegetables, honeys, jellies, apple slushies and cider, and a bakery that makes pies and cobbler.  Outside, pumpkins and mums are for sale too.   All the store and outside purchases use the same checkout line, so the line can get quite long on weekends.  Review #1371

While on the east side of Indy, I decided to stop by for ice cream and ended up getting that AND dinner.  This colorful shop sits on the corner of Sherman and English and has free parking around the building.  Inside, there is an assortment of "to go" chips and ice cream treats, the payment counter, and a bank of ice creams that conveniently have the names written on stickers on the glass above the frozen tubs.  There is also a spot by the ice cream with a full menu available to peruse.    I went ahead and ordered a Coffee (flavored) ice cream and while they made it, the menu caught my eye.  It was primarily in Spanish but fortunately, there were lots of photos.  I am the first to admit my knowledge of foreign languages is poor, but fortunately, the woman behind the counter was able to understand me and communicate pretty well.  I selected from the lunch menu (lonches) and ordered what looked like a sandwich.  The Planchados o Dorado is apparently a sandwich type meal that deep fries the bread to a golden (dorado) color and then pressed or ironed (planchados).  I went with the Cochinita filling which is a shredded pork with a spiced (some heat) seasoning.  I also added tomato and onions to my order.   I ate my ice cream while they made my sandwich to go.  The ice cream was creamy and the waffle cone tasted fresh.  A nice combo, though not really a "Wow" flavor.  The sandwich arrived and I paid at the counter before heading out.  The pressed bread takes on a chewy texture, but in a pleasant way.  The flavor was really good, though the juiciness made it something to watch out for since the juice had an orange color that looked like it could cause one heck of a stain.  Fortunately, they wrapped it in foil and then put it in a small plastic sleeve to catch the drippings.  I simply peeled back the foil and slid the sleeve down as I ate and managed to not spill a drop!  I still needed some napkins, but was relieved that I didn't have to do laundry when I got home!   The folks behind the counter were friendly and made the wait time seem minimal.  I appreciated their willingness to explain some of the terms that I was unfamiliar with.  Seems like it is authentic Mexican food and worth checking out.  Review #2578

I enjoy going into independent gift shops and being able to find items, though familiar, are different from what I find elsewhere.  Such is the case at Onatah.  I pulled up in front of the building (free street parking on both the front and east side of the building) and climbed the few steps into the shop door on the northeast corner.  There are lots of plants here for a small shop, most of them by the north window.  There are also display tables in the middle and some racks/stacks along the walls with check out counter at the back.  There are items like candles, and bath soaps and oils, incense, cards, and chocolates.  There are some clothing items, but somewhat limited there.  The overall sense is that of welcome with lots of small items to peruse.    The woman behind the checkout table was friendly without being nosy.  Upbeat in nature which is always appreciated too!  I purchased one of the chocolate bars and she filled me in on why the store carried that line.  This place is easy to find:  just a couple blocks east of the fountain in Fountain Square in an area that has really turned the corner in development.  I find more and more shops going in to appeal to the residents of the area.    Review #3609

Welcome to Indy! or more specifically, Fishers!  This is the first brick and mortar location of a business out of New Albany, IN that launched less than a year ago down there and has taken southern Indiana and Louisville by storm.  Word of mouth let them know the metro area here wanted to have beautiful party trays on demand and so, they listened and opened this spot just east of I-69 and north of 96th.    I walked in on opening day and they were still stocking their shelves and working on decorating/organizing their space.  I heard they are working on adding wine to their offerings and possibly a place in the back of the shop where customers can drink and dine on a charcuterie boards.  This is how it works:  You go on their website and can select from different size trays or smaller offerings called Graze boxes (for individuals/couples).  The website tells you how many each size is intended to serve.  You can also add more meats or cheeses for a fee as well.  They also need to know about allergies.  They ask for at least 24 hours lead time to prepare.  No size is too large since they once served 1500 people!  While I was there, I noticed they also sell cheeses, jellies, and honey at the counter.  I started chatting with one of the men at the counter and he offered to put together one of the Graze Boxes for me ($20).  I had traveled nearly an hour to check this place out, so I was glad to have a chance to actually try some of their food (I didn't know about the 24 hour rule and can't guarantee they will make a Graze box on demand for all customers.)  In just a short time, my box was ready and came with a honey dipper and  small wooden fork tied to the box.  Inside, the large box included locally sourced meat, three kinds of cheese, lots of berries and grapes, roasted macadamia nuts, small gherkins, chocolate covered nuts, some of the most delicious crackers I've ever had, and a small jar of honey.  I knew this would make for a fun dinner later that evening.  All the ingredients were excellent and just looking at the arrangement made me hungry!  The food was so good that I had to grab a few pieces and leave before I devoured the whole thing on my own. (My wife did get to have some.)  Be aware that the store isn't visible from 96th or even from Fitness Lane since there is another building (Starcrest Cleaners) that blocks the view from the street.  You have to drive around the building to the north end of the parking lot where you will find this shop in the middle of that building.  Plenty of parking was nearby.  Note:  Watch for an Elite Event through Yelp sometime later in the year.  Niki is working out the details with the owners.  Review #3722

The shop is much more than just a bakery for dogs treats.  You can find dog beds, apparel for humans, kerchiefs for the dogs, and assorted dog related items.  There is also a section of wall dedicated to flavored dog biscuits which are kind of ordinary looking.  Then you head toward the counter and see the colorfully displayed hand made dog treats.  Some are big, some are small.  Most have a colorful icing applied for visual appeal.  Some are cut out in shapes like bones, trees, and others.    I picked up a couple large ones which were decorated to celebrate the Indy 500.  I also got some small ones including pastel colors and others with sprinkles!  Most of what I ordered had a peanut butter base.    When I got them home, my dogs were a little skeptical, but once they played with it a bit, they devoured them!    The prices are not cheap, but if you've ever tried making these type of things on your own, then you will appreciate how much time it takes to decorate even something that seems simple.  My dogs enjoyed their treats.  I enjoyed the service and dog friendly space.  Review #2600

Although I don't shop here regularly, I like that the grocery has a nice location that isn't too far off SR 37(eventually to be I-69) along Southport Road.  They carry all the brands you see in the larger Krogers and have a pharmacy on site.  They also have a floral area, a bakery, a produce section, and a deli.  They have a decent sized area for wine, liquor and beer, including a few local craft brews.  I was a little surprised that only half the self serve stations were open.  I get that they don't need all the check out lanes staffed, but why not have the self check lanes open?    The store was clean and seemed like the produce and deli sections were filled with fresh items (no fishy smell like at some groceries.)  Seems like a great place for "one stop shopping" for those in the area.  Review #3619

Having been a fan of the Poke Guru in City Market, I was glad to see either an expansion or relocation to this spot on the north end of the Garage at Bottleworks.  Still the same great flavor of a freshly made bowl of food with great combinations of flavors that I never think of trying at home!  Note that the Garage Food Hall is located inside the Bottleworks on the north side of 9th street and west side of Carrollton.  Poke Guru is on the right side at the end.    The bowls they offer come in different sizes though I will admit that the smaller bowl was plenty for my lunch (and still left a little room for some Lick Ice Cream across the shared seating area from Poke.)  My wife ordered the Kalbi which comes with a choice of sushi rice or brown rice, and is topped with grilled Korean short ribs, seaweed salad, edamame, avocado, and pickled mustard seeds, pickled pear, and crispy onions.  She would have enjoyed it more if the rice were warmed instead of chilled and a bit clumpy.  I opted for the smaller bowl of the Bowl with No Name.  I chose brown rice (it  offers mixed greens instead), tuna tossed in pickled mustard seed (spiced with wasabi), cucumber, edamame, carrot, green onion, pickled daikon, and garlic chips.  Excellent flavor combo, but if you order it, be sure to get a beverage to temper the "heat" unless you are one of those people who loves heat.  You order from a counter and the meal is bagged for easy transport to your table in the common food hall area.    If you choose the Kalbi, you can expect a longer wait time because they have to grill the short ribs while you wait.  Maybe 10 minutes or so, but definitely longer than if you order one of the other bowls.  It isn't a cheap spot to grab a bite, but the quality of ingredients makes it worth the price.  I would gladly go back to Poke Guru for more!  Review #3842

This is our go to pharmacy.  I guess that sums it up in that we use them when needed and generally, have success and good experiences dealing with the pharmacy and the general store staff.  I like that even though they aren't 24/7, they generally are open when I am in need of something.  Their prices are usually okay if you have insurance, but it doesn't hurt to use a price checking app like GoodRx to see if you can get a better deal elsewhere.  But I like the convenience of this place being close and their past service has earned our trust.  One point I want to mention is that for a small store, they have a nice variety of stocking stuffers in the seasonal aisle each Christmas season.  Although it looked a little smaller this year, I always pick up something for the grandkids when I stop by.  Review #1768

I stopped in while in Speedway since I had not been to this location before.  It was my fifth location of this franchised brewery that has its own recipes for beer but doesn't actually produce them (Flat 12 does the brewing for all the Indy area B&B's).  The interior is much like those of the newer franchises, but does have a patio and a separate room (not completed closed off) for private parties.  A kid's birthday party was going on when I arrived.  Oh, and plenty of parking.  The staff was very friendly and after greeting me, offered to let me taste test some varieties before ordering a bigger serving.  (Note that they do offer flights of beers as well for a fee.)  I tasted a very fragrant Flowers for Ale-gernon that was okay, but I thought a full glass might be a little too much floral.  I decided to go with the Toil&Trouble English Brown Ale (4.8% 20 IBU) instead.  I selected a 10 oz pour and that was just right.  Nice flavor with a pleasant balance of flavors.  I can imagine this would be a good one to pair with food as well.  Clean place, not too noisy (even with the kids party), and very open space.  Lots of board games if you come with friends to pass the time while you explore their beer menu.  I believe they also have a small menu of food items, but I didn't try any on this visit.  Review #2056

It had been several years since my last visit to this spot.  We used to be fans of Osteria Pronto but for some reason, hadn't been in awhile.  I saw that they rebranded to OP Italian and were advertising an event each Thursday for lunch for Half Price Pasta.  Sounded like a great opportunity to get reacquainted with the restaurant.  After pulling into the underground parking garage for the Marriott, we took our ticket with us and had the restaurant's hostess validate our parking for up to 90 minutes.  Don't forget...if you don't get it validated, the hotel charges $24 for the first 2 hours, and $10 more if you run longer than that.  So pay attention to when you get your ticket...time starts then.  We were greeted and seated promptly in the main dining room.  After our beverages arrived, my wife chose the Grilled Salmon Salad instead of a pasta dish.  I went with the Spicy Shrimp Spaghetti and ordered a plate of (4) garlic bread.  Note that first time Yelpers can get a 15% discount for checking in, but you can't use that discount if you are getting the half price pasta.  All other times, I would recommend using it!  The bread was very pleasing to me.  One side was grilled to a light crunch while the other stayed mostly soft.  There was a garlic butter on the bread and a light dusting of parmesan (I think).  Some pieces had more than others.  The ones with it were really good.  The others were just okay.  My wife's salad came with a lot of romaine lettuce and a few heirloom tomatoes (sliced).  She was a bit disappointed that the piece of salmon was only one small cube (maybe 2 oz?) and that there were hardly any green olives.  Most of all, she was disappointed that the lemon dressing didn't add much flavor to an already barely seasoned fish.  She didn't finish her meal even after trying to add some table salt.  Just too bland.  I, on the other hand, really enjoyed my dish.  There were a fair number of shrimp (no tail scales on them) and though cooked thoroughly, weren't rubbery.  The pasta had a buttery taste and the spicy red pepper flakes added just a bit of heat, but not too much.  The parmesan dusting and the roasted garlic flavors helped keep my dish well balanced in flavor.  Service was friendly, but a bit irregular.  There were supposed to be two waitresses attending our section, but only one arrived at our table.  She seemed busy and in plain sight, just not available.  We had "help yourself" water jugs, but nobody asked if they could refill my wife's tea until after we had finished dining.  Maybe because my wife didn't eat much of her salad made them think we were still dining.  IDK    We were getting a little antsy toward the end to get going, so the wait for them to process our check may have seemed longer than it was.  The discounted pasta price definitely helped make the meal more affordable.  Still, it is clear for the flavor of the meals, the prices listed are what you would expect from a hotel restaurant that has built in customers.  With tax and tip (and discount) we still spent nearly $50 for lunch.  It was good, just not great.  Review #2512

According to my wife there has been a lot of turnover in the   sewing machine business including in the repair business. We are fortunate to live in the Indy area   and have access to a chain of repair shops that have about a dozen shops in  the Midwest. When my wife found this  location in Greenwood, She found that their specialist on her quilting arm   and getting her existing machine to work properly was located three hours   away. The local repair guy was able to   diagnose the problem but did not have the part and expertise of the other   technician. So he offed free shipping   to the other shop and an estimate of the cost and time it would take. Both   sounded acceptable to my wife. We only needed the sewing machine sent, so   no dismantling of the quilting arm was needed based upon my wife's   description. Turns out this business   is owned by the same person so he is   trying to provide the best customer service and cooperation between locations   so there is enough work for each location to keep his repairmen fully employed and not loose them to a  competitor. The owner has begun expansion into buying fabric stores to become   an even more complete provider to his customers. my wife still wishes there was a shop a   little closer, but is glad that she is  able to keep her machines which are her favorite hobby and pastime and   creative outlet running.      Review #3961

FYI:  My rating is based upon the bakery side of the business.  I had already dined at another place before stopping in on Tuesday afternoon, so I didn't have enough room in my stomach to sit down for a full meal.  But one look in the pastry counters (yes, more than one), and I knew I would be kicking myself if I didn't ask for several items to go!  Sure, I spent a while wandering around the seemingly endless nooks and crannies of this place before coming back to place my order.  It seemed everywhere I looked were collections of anything and everything related to German culture.  I also found numerous little niches where tables were occupied by diners....seemed like a full house when I was there.  Anyway, I selected four items and anxiously made my way home and called my wife over to see what I had selected.  Of course, we had to sample each one before putting them away for tomorrow...you know, just to make sure we got to taste them at their freshest!  :)  Our favorite was the Peach Streusel.  The serving was large and had a great balance of bite sized pieces of peach layered over a dough crust with light, but plentiful streusel topping.  Totally delicious....I could see ordering this for a brunch and wowing all my friends!  Another tasty choice was the Cherry Cream Puff.  (It didn't survive until evening!)  My wife doesn't even like cherries, but she ended up snapping up about 2/3's of it! The puff portion was light and flaky and perfectly balanced the whipped cream and cherries inside.  I also liked the Apple with Toasted Almonds.  This roll up had excellent balance in flavors as well.  My only negative on this was that the almonds seemed a bit raw (not enough toasting) and weren't as good when eaten by themselves.  But with the rest of the flavors, they seemed okay.  Finally, our fourth selection was the Raspberry and Blueberry with Hazelnut Buttercream.  This multi-layered cake and fruit paste dessert was topped with colorful buttercream.  Although the presentation looked beautiful, the cake portion seemed a little bit dry.  Of course, when comparing to the wonderful selections mentioned above, any little thing stands out.   I can't wait until tomorrow when I can sample what remains again with a hot cup of coffee!  Review #98

With lots of restaurants not offering dine in service because of the pandemic, I was happy to find this franchise open with spacious seating areas but only a modest sized crowd during my lunch.  The place has lots of parking and plenty of room inside.  The walls are covered with screens but most have the volume off so that the pleasant sounds from the house video channel can be heard without blasting too loud to block conversation.  We were greeted and seated and had good service throughout our time there.  My wife ordered a small bowl of chili (just a hint of spicy heat) and tater tots which she saved the leftovers for home.  I looked over their beverages and ordered a local craft Lift Off by Daredevil brewing (on tap).  I decided to go with a stacked high Wild Shroomin' Burger (1/2 pound) and got the seasoned shoestring style fries.  So much that I ended up saving some for dinner that night.    We both liked our meals and combined with the pleasant atmosphere inside and good service, we had a solid dining experience.  Minimal wait times during our lunch.  I would recommend it as place to dine if you want to be taken care of in a comparatively safe environment.  Review #3870

'Surprisingly good tasting food served at your car window with prices that compete with fast food joints' is my quick summary.  I have driven by this local drive-in hundreds of times, but I had never stopped in before.  It sits across a steep "up and down" railroad crossing that you don't want to take very quickly and then is along a frontage road that isn't in the best condition.  Let's face it:  Mars Hill doesn't get much support from the city, so I'm usually surprised when I DON'T hit a pot hole.  Pulling in to their lot, you may want to pick a spot at the overhanging roof that allows you to read the menu.  The place looks in need of some maintenance, so it doesn't make a great first impression.  But what I noticed late in the lunch hour was that there were cars sitting there in the January cold with folks eating their meals.  And there was a steady stream of cars rotating in and out for their meals "to go".  In less than a minute of my arrival, a pleasant woman greeted me at my driver side window and asked what I would like.  I ordered the Tenderloin with Fries and an Oreo Shake (small).  The Tenderloin (I chose breaded) is small for Hoosier standards, but for just $.80 more, you get a second one ($3.50 for both!)  I passed on the second, but was impressed.  In just a few minutes, the waitress brought a small tray to hang on my window complete with napkins and condiments (salt, pepper, catsup, and yellow mustard) along with my meal.  I haven't had a dining experience like that since I was a kid!    And though I've read a lot of reviews that refer to this as a "greasy spoon" or with a derogatory cliche, the food wasn't greasy or oily.  It may have been fried, but I've had far worse and paid higher prices.  This is simply good (and affordable) food that is served quickly.  And they take credit cards too!    I didn't drive around the building, so it appeared to me that there wasn't any inside dining, but they do have picnic tables tucked away on the back of the lot that could be used in warmer months.  This was a nostalgic experience for me and I would gladly recommend stopping here for anyone who wants to remember what fast food was like before the drive-thru was invented.  It doesn't have roller skates or lots of neon here, but I did get a good meal and great service.  When I was finished dining, I simply put my basket and trash back on the tray on my window and the waitress (she covered every customer) immediately came over and removed it so I could get on my way.    Review #3607

My wife and I met a friend for lunch on Wednesday.  We were able to park right outside the entrance in one of the dedicated parking spots.  The inside of the restaurant was nice and cool.  The "family" dining and restrooms are located to the left and the bar was located to the right.    Because it wasn't too hot when we arrived, we opted to sit outside the bar area on the patio.  I ordered one of the local craft beers from the lengthy list.  The gals ordered iced teas and the waitress did a great job of bringing "extra" lemon for my wife.  All was going well until road construction started up across the street.  No problem....we flagged down the waitress and she helped us move inside where the road work could not be heard.  (We did sit in the corner of the bar and the volume of the background music was a bit louder than we would have liked for our conversation.  We noticed other people were talking loudly too.)  Although only our guest had an appetizer (the soup du jour Tortilla Soup), the wait for entrees didn't seem too long.  I opted for the "Lake" which is a pan-fried trout sandwich with lettuce, tomato, red onion and chipotle mayonnaise.  It came with a dill pickle spear and I went with the Roasted Vegetable Medley.  The fish sandwich appeared like it was going to be dry but it was cooked properly and I squeezed a lemon wedge over the top of the fish to brighten the flavor.  The roasted vegetables were fantastic!  Such great flavors come out when done properly.  The veggies had the right balance between roasting and being firm (no mushiness detected).   Very nice dish for a very reasonable price (under $10).  My wife enjoyed her burger with bacon and some of the usual burger fair.  The chipotle mayo seemed to go well with the rest of the burger.  The sweet potato fries had crisp edges while staying soft towards the center.  Both the soup and salad got good marks as well.    With parking available, a full beer selection, and good food, I would recommend stopping in here again for a reasonably priced meal.  Review #79

Best fish sandwich I have ever had!  Okay, I have only tried one meal here, so I may not be the most qualified to rate this place, but based upon my fellow Yelpers recommendations, I got the "Caplinger's Special" sandwich with the Collard Greens as a side.  As a lunch special, counting a large drink and tax, it was just under $10.  I wish I didn't live nearly an hour away or else I would be here more often!  I arrived on Tuesday morning around 11, so I was greeted as I entered and offered a menu.  I asked a few questions and then placed my order at the back end of the seafood counter.  They gave me a receipt with a number and a cup to self serve from the soda dispenser.  (Napkins, straws, etc. are located near the dispenser.)  After just a few minutes, my sandwich and greens were ready.  Since the sandwich was a bit too hot, I concentrated on the collard greens.    I had never eaten collards until about a year ago, so this was maybe the third time I have tried them.  These were delicious and easily compare favorably with any I have had.  For what my limited experience is worth, I definitely recommend getting them.  I ordered the sandwich with the works, so the bun had lettuce, tartar sauce, onion, pickles, and, of course, the deep fried Basa.  The fish was several inches longer than the round bun, so there were bites where all I could taste was the fish and breading.  Oh my!  As described in other reviews, the flavor reminded me of tender deep fried chicken!  Excellent flavor with a touch of heat in the spices.  The fish was extremely mild in flavor.  I asked about the type of fish and was shown the whitefish Basa in the display counter before breading.  Cooked perfectly, this fish is a "must try" for first time diners.  I hope to get back to the northeast side soon so that I can pop in for another taste!  p.s.  They have a second location open (opening?) in Noblesville at Gray Road and 150th.  p.s.s.  The Basa is a distant cousin of the catfish, but is not a bottom feeder.  Rather, it eats plants.  This is why the flavor is so mild compared to other catfish I have tried.  Not sure if this was farm raised or shipped from the Mekong or Chao Phraya basins in Indochina.  p.s.s.s.  There are more types of fish and seafood available in the counters that are not listed on the menu (scallops, for example).  Anything in the store is available to purchase on ice or to have cooked by them for you.  No minimum quantity is required.  Note that if the order is for food items over $10/pound, there is no charge for cooking, and only $2 if you order one of the less expensive selections.  Review #96

Pleasant service, lots of information, and light creamy pastries of assorted colors and combinations!  Yum!  I stopped in after lunch to pick up some tasty treats to go.  Since it was my first visit, I stood to the side for awhile and let the hostess behind the pasty bar help several others, explaining as she went.    Since the appearance was somewhat hypnotic, I simply bought a sample of lots of things!  There were large crispy croissants, both plain and almond flavored filled with almond butter.  Macarons were on sale today, so I picked up some of each flavor:  Rose Raspberry and Salted Chocolate Caramel.  These are fresh and dissolved in my mouth when I ate them, not the brick hard kind I find too often at the grocery.  The Chocolate Pillow was a flourless chocolate cake covered with a chocolate mousse glaze and hazelnut crunch (and a touch of gold leaf!) and the Provence is a beautiful half sphere of macaron base topped with lavender and white chocolate mousse.  I also tried the Opera:  an almond sponge layered with coffee buttercream and ganache.   Sure the prices are about the same for each of the specialty items as you would pay for a dessert in a restaurant, but if you have will power, you can get just a few and refrigerate the ones you don't scarf down right away to make the prices seem more affordable! :)  But these aren't tastes and textures you get from a mass produced bakery.  My photos don't do them justice since they got a little knocked around on my 50 minute car ride home.  Trust me, these treats are something special and can help make your day a little nicer!  Review #162

I've only tried Burmese food a couple times before, so I decided to take another adventure in cuisine at Chin Brothers.  This business is located in a strip mall on the north east corner of Stop 11 and Madison.  There is plenty of parking (though there are pot holes to navigate) out front of this combo business:  Grocery on the left, restaurant on the right.  Burma (now Myanmar) is located north of Thailand and east of India and Bangladesh.  So, the restaurant offers some Pan Asian options as well as those native to the country.    I was greeted and taken to a table for lunch and I ordered a pot of tea and some chilled water while I made my selections from a one page menu.  Note that there are photos of many of the items that use a letter/number combo to match the menu to the pics.  I was surprised that the menu didn't list any of the soups that I've seen mentioned in the other reviews, so I asked about them.  Yep! You can get them even though they  aren't on that menu.  So, I started with a Chinese Cruller which is a huge unseasoned pastry that is longer than the dinner plate it was served on.  (Actually, it was halves that were easily torn apart.)  The outside was a bit crispy as if it was deep fried and left just a bit of oil on my fingers.  I could imagine these with sugar/cinnamon or maybe even chocolate and being a real hit.    But since they were plain, they were just okay.  Before long, my huge bowl (8" across and a couple inches deep) of Kyay Oh arrived.  I'm no expert, but if you've had Pho, this seems similar to me.  It has a rich broth, a huge tangle of really skinny noodles (they make angel hair pasta think about going on a diet!), quail eggs, bok choy, cilantro, large slices of dark mushrooms, sliced beef, and some ground meat (I'm guessing pork).  This dish comes with a soup spoon, a fork, and chop sticks.  On the side, they offer chopped chiles.  Beware if you aren't a fan of heat....those chilies are the real deal and just one small piece lit up the back of my throat!  The flavor of the soup bowl was subtle, but hearty as the warmth of the ingredients filled me.  No room for dessert!  The quail eggs were small and their shape made them hard to stab in the bowl, so I used the spoon to catch those.  The noodles were clumped and slippery, so I struggled to get them to stay wrapped around my fork.  The owner suggested using the chop sticks, but I'm sure I wouldn't have ever finished with those!  The beef and ground meat were very tender, but also lacked much flavor since I assume they were cooked in the broth instead of on a skillet or roasted.  The mushroom (unlike any kind I've ever had) had a slight chewy texture but a mild flavor as well.  But despite my struggles to get things speared and in my mouth, I eventually got all the food eaten and the more I ate, the more I noticed the subtle flavors and appreciated them.  The owner/waitress checked on me several times and encouraged me to come back and try some more options.  I paid at the counter when I was done without being delivered a receipt until I got there.  Review #2635

I will echo the reviews of many of the Yelpers who actually stopped in this shop just west of Keystone on 54th.  The place has a wide variety of bird supplies, reasonable prices, and friendly/helpful staff.    After pulling in their lot out front of the building, I entered the shop which has two large rooms, front and back.  I heard a voice of greeting as the employee came forward towards the entrance and asked if I needed any assistance.  It seemed a little odd that the checkout was in the backroom, but wasn't really any inconvenience for me.  As I browsed around, I was pleased to see such variety of offerings.  Even the suet that I purchased for feeding the birds that stay in winter had more than a dozen varieties including some that deter mammals from raiding the feeders.  Not only do they have feeds, but there were lots of feeders and accessories, they also had yard decorations and because of the season I visited in, ornaments that were bird/pet related.  Look, I get it if you don't want to drive across town to shop here, but this is really close to Broad Ripple and you can help support a local business as well as make your home an attractive site for flying creatures.  Overall, a nice place to shop.  Review #3467

I've been to several Bed Bath & Beyond and found this one to have a very similar layout to the one in Greenwood, so I assume they have a general plan for all their franchises.  Basically, you start with kitchen supplies, move to wall decor, then to bedroom supplies, and finish with bath as you work your way clockwise through the store.  I was looking for a new mandoline that could add some uniformity to my slices as well as julienne cuts.  I found several mandolines in different price ranges and sizes, but with varying levels of options (some only sliced).  Fortunately, even the one I purchased was very affordable and looked like it was dishwasher safe.  When I got to the checkout, they didn't have a specific line since only the customer service desk was open.  When the clerk finished the customer she was serving and saw two of us were waiting, she called for support to open another line and someone actually came, opened the line, and let me make my purchase quickly enough to get through before the customer ahead of me got through!    I was pleasantly surprised at the upbeat attitude of both clerks and their willingness to expedite my purchase.  I was really pleased with their effort.  Sometimes, the quality of service is the determining factor for which of the locations I go to when shopping the big box stores.  This location went a long way on getting return business.  Review #3681

Excellent food and service throughout the dinner!  Although on the higher (cost) end of food venues in the greater Broad Ripple area, there is a casual appeal to the food and vibe of the restaurant.  We were fortunate to find a spot on 46th not too far from the restaurant (see parking info later in the review.)  We were greeted as we entered and though a detour on College had furthered our delay, our reservation on a Tuesday night was honored.  I was surprised how busy the restaurant was at 5 p.m. on a weekday.  But service never faltered.  Our waitress Tammye was great at making recommendations for first time visitors and she guided us through the multiple courses we selected.  We started off with a couple small plate items:  Drunken Deviled Eggs and Grandma Daisy's Angel Biscuits.  The eggs arrive as 3 halves with pink egg whites nestled on an ornate plate and topped with herbs and a root chip for a little texture.  I really liked them though my wife isn't a pickled egg fan thought they were just okay.  However, when it came to the biscuits, it was all she could do to keep from just ordering plates of them.  The biscuits are fresh and warm, with a little crunch in the crust and soft & tasty insides.  And the chicken jus dipping sauce (along with sea salt and benne seeds) was something I would buy by the bottle!  Real comfort food flavors.  Highest recommendation here!  We decided to get the two shareable entrees for dinner.  My wife was leaning towards the half rack of Barbecue Bruleed Spare Ribs (served sliced).  They are smoky and lightly burnt with brown sugar, pickled Fresno chili slices, and tangy bbq sauce.  Very tender, though not quite falling off the bone.  Definitely recommend eating this as a finger food.  I was leaning toward the Sweet Tea Brined Fried Chicken which are lemon dusted (just the right amount of spices on the skin) and served with a honey tobasco sauce on the side.  Very moist and tender chicken with crisped skin.  The sauce wasn't very spicy hot but added a layer of flavor to our choosing.  We went with the half chicken which is literal so we got both dark and light meat.    Note:  After eating both entrees with our fingers, we needed a little assistance cleaning up, so we mentioned it to our waitress who brought out a miniature bath tub filled with steaming hot mini hand towels to wash our fingers clean.  They are VERY hot, so be careful if you request and use these.  Our entrees also paired with a side order of collard greens.  The greens were large leaf, not slice/cut.  Though cooked in a pot with ham, I didn't particularly notice any meat in the serving.  But the brothy liquid the leaves were nestled in provided lots of flavor.  Very good!  For dessert, we split a chocolate chip cookie sundae which has a house made cookie sliced in half and served with salted caramel ice cream, roasted peanuts, and chocolate fudge.  The cookie had a chewy texture and had some white bits (I'm guessing macadamia nuts or white chocolate) that added more flavor than just a simple CC cookie.    Overall, I really enjoyed my visit and look forward to returning to try some more interesting options from the menu.  Getting there:  Because of the construction and red line on College, be aware of any detours (College was closed between 38th and 42nd).  Also note that many of the east/west streets don't allow you to cross College because of the raised median.    Parking:  Minimal parking spaces are behind the restaurant.  46th has free street parking on the north side of the street east of College, so approach from the east to use these.  There is also an "unofficial" parking area on the southwest corner of 46th and College with access from 46th or from southbound College.  The lot seems shared with "Next Door".  Reservations:  I went during the week and had no trouble making reservations through their website/open table.  I am not sure if those who wrote that they don't take reservations on weekends were understanding correctly that there were no reservations left.  The website says they take them but the prime dining times were already booked for this coming weekend (early Feb).    Excellent addition to the SoBro dining scene.  Price is not cheap, but the place is definitely a dining experience provided by two Top Chef contestants that chose Indy as their first foray into the midwest.  Review #3622

After fighting rush hour traffic in the morning, I decided to stop in for a quick bite before getting back on the road.  Caffe Buondi made the fight with traffic worth it!  Delightful food, service, and a pleasant surrounding got my morning back on track.    I sat at the coffee bar and Corey got me a menu, a water, and took my beverage order (black drip coffee) promptly.  I loved that the coffee was not only good, but ready to drink temperature.  Yeah!  I went with the Rafa which is a plated dish (think lasagna) made from spinach noodles, with layers of egg, bacon, and covered with bechamel sauce.  I selected the fresh fruit cup to go with it.  Really nice flavor and pleasant change from so many breakfast places.    There was plenty of parking in this strip mall location and I thought the decor was pleasant (they even have a fireplace built in by the dining room.)  Even though it was just after 8 a.m., I didn't find the crowd that noisy.  Overall, I found this place to be well worth returning for a breakfast, brunch, or lunch.  Note:  This is owned by the same folks who run the Convivio restaurants (next door and Zionsville).  Review #2311

Wow!  When I give 5 stars, it's because the business exceeds my expectations.  I stopped by after a Colts victory and was their first customer of the evening.  Since I was dining by myself, I grabbed a spot at their long bar counter and was impressed that this was a bar I could eat from without banging my knees or having to lean forward over some over sized ornamentation on the bar edge.  I like comfort when dining, so this was a great start.  The manager was tending bar and after greeting and asking what I was interested in, gave me both a cocktail menu and a food menu as well as running through the evening's special.  He also directed me to craft beer list on the chalkboard near the entrance.  So, I was glad to have options.  They don't have a huge menu, but it looked like there was plenty for a guy to eat.  But something about the special (a soup and sandwich combo) sounded good, so I went with that.    While waiting, I ordered a "Black Cherry" cocktail made with Cognac, Maraschino Liqueur, and a house spiced cherry (it takes five days to make these).  The cocktail is delicious!  Not too sweet, not too tart, just a nicely balanced pleasant flavor that was great on its own as well as robust enough to stand up to the flavors of the food that soon arrived.  The special was a bowl of Broccoli Cheese soup and a sliced grilled BCT (Bacon, Cheese, & Tomato) sandwich.  The soup was good and had some small florets of broccoli, but a little on the thin side.  Good, but not great.  And then I took a bite of the sandwich and I was impressed!  I think I heard angels sing! ha!  This is the best grilled cheese sandwich I ever had and I've dined at nearly 900 different food and beverage places in the area.  The bread was thick (almost Texas Toast size) and was toasted to a delightful crunch.  Not buttery or oily like a lot of grilled cheese.  I could pick this up and not have residue on my fingers.    Inside, there was just the right amount of American Cheese, thick cut Tyner Farm bacon (pre cooked to crispness, not soggy), and a thin slice of tomato that I didn't realize was there at first, but provided just the right amount of moisture to the sandwich so that it wasn't dry.    I am used to grilled cheese that is gooey and oozing, but often starts to "set" if I take too long to eat it.  But this cheese stayed in its place and stayed creamy smooth.  It was evenly distributed to the edges of the sandwich and was perfectly balanced with the bacon and tomato flavors.   I didn't know I liked grilled cheese this way until I ate it.  I only hope they add this to the full time menu since they nailed this recipe down!  It's a shame it takes me 45 minutes to get to this place, but I was glad I made the trip.  I recommend that you do too!  Review #1991

There are a few choices for breakfast/brunch in Mooresville and this is the newest member of that lineup.  Located just a couple lots north of Grays's Cafeteria on Indiana St, there was plenty of parking when we visited for a brunch around 9:30 during the week.  We didn't go on Senior discount day or on a weekend, so it is possible that there are times when waiting and parking may challenge your enjoyment.  But for us, we were seated right away and parked near the front entrance so we were off to a good start.  We were seated in the room next to the main dining room.  It was near the kitchen, so it wasn't the quietest location, but it wasn't too bad either.  Our server was attentive and did a good job of keeping an eye on us to see if I needed a coffee refill and if we needed our check.  Both came timely.  (Note that you pay at the counter on the way out instead of paying your server.)  I don't go out for breakfast very often, so there may be other folks who can give you better information of how this place compares to some of the established brunch/breakfast houses in the area.  To make up for that lack of familiarity, I tend to order the same foods when I go out for brunch so that I can compare the quality of specific dishes.  I usually choose Eggs Benedict which require some skills to prepare while my wife usually gets a strawberry crepe.  I also drink black coffee to see how that tastes at its most basic level.  As I said, the service was good which is why I rounded up to 4 stars.  I also will admit that the flavor of both my wife's crepe and my eggs benedict and hash browns were quite tasty too!    The main reason this place didn't get a 5 star was that the cooking times were off just a little.  Not bad enough to send the food back, but enough that it was noticeable.  My wife's crepe had an odd color compared to most places I've been.  I think the crepe was a bit undercooked which made it pliable and easy to roll, but left it with a color that wasn't as appealing and a chewiness or maybe sponginess is a better word to describe what she experienced.  Not bad enough to send back, but just not top notch.  The black coffee was strong and bitter.  Maybe a touch burned.  They have a variety of sweeteners and flavored creams which can be added to mask some of the bitter/burned taste, but since I like mine straight, it stood out as being served at a temp that was too hot to drink right away without a bit of tongue scalding.  I find this mistake way too many places, even places that only serve coffee.  You wonder if they ever drink their own product.  The eggs benedict had a wonderful flavor.  One of the best flavors I've had from a local restaurant.  However, where most places I've been leave the egg yolk soft so that it can spill out and run over the hash browns (one of my all time favorite flavor combos), this egg was soft cooked and stayed in place.  The hash browns were done to a crisp on one side, but just warmed on the other so that I suspect they weren't flipped over during cooking to get an evenness to the finish.  The seasoning was done very well, but compared to all the other places I've been for breakfast, this place could just fine tune their cook times.  I understand not everyone likes their eggs and hash browns like I do, but since it was my check and my review, I get to express what my expectations were and how close the restaurant came to meeting the expectations.  Good, but not ideal.  So, four stars for service and flavor, but one star off for lack of execution on the presentation and cook times.  If you aren't as picky as I am about some matters, you may give this place a higher rating.  It wasn't the cheapest place to eat breakfast and did take about 15-20 minutes to get our meal, but I found the wait not unpleasant.  If you are looking for a place to try something for brunch, give this place a try and hopefully they will grow into their routine enough to iron out the imperfections.  Review #3808

While waiting on our candles to set at Penn & Beech, we headed over to this restaurant just a few blocks away on Main Street for a delightful dinner.  I had planned ahead and made reservations for early evening (5:15) during the week so that we got a nice choice of seating location (not too close to the exits) and not too close to the people standing around waiting to be seated.  We had solid service throughout the dinner and very delicious food and cocktails.  I wasn't sure from the website or other reviews just were this was.  They don't have much outdoor signage, so you need to keep your eyes open for the restaurant and available street parking.  Some spaces are reserved for valet parking at Anthony's Chophouse & 3 UP which are in the same building to the east of Savor.  Other spots are limited to less time than dining in would require.  Fortunately, there is a nearby free parking garage south of the restaurant in case you can't nab one of the free street spots.  Just target where the Monon Trail crosses Main Street and you should be able to see the restaurant on the south side of Main Street, on the corner.  (Google maps didn't have the restaurant properly located, so I thought I would include a photo of the exterior with my review to help first time visitors like myself.  Inside, the place is open and spacious.  That can get a little loud when the place gets busy, but we went early in the evening and we were able to engage in conversation while we dined or in between courses.  Service was fine with our server Aaron.  Minimal wait times and he had an easy going demeanor and sense of humor as one of our party likes to joke around.  I appreciate someone who can go with the flow, but keep the process moving without feeling overwhelmed.    The cocktail I chose was called the Spa Day which used Hendricks Gin as a base.  Excellent.  I wish my cocktails at home tasted this good!  Everyone at the table ordered something different for entrees.  I asked each one how they enjoyed their meal and got thumbs up from everyone (I miss the days were we could sample each other's meals.)  Our group ordered the lamb chops, the ahi tuna, side salads (and were able to substitute romaine for the mixed greens normally included.)  My wife ordered the Romano Crusted Chicken which comes in a cheese sauce as well.  It looked like a lot of cheese for one meal, but she found it tasty and balanced.  One friend ordered the Jumbo Prawn with Angel Hair Pasta and artichokes.  Another ordered the Lobster Risotto while I ordered the Scallop Risotto and they were quite tasty too.  Even the Asparagus in the risotto was cut diced on the bias which gave little hints of flavor to each bite.    Overall, the meal and service were excellent and contributed to our nice outing with our friends. Review #3894

This is a pretty good place if you are looking for some fried chicken to go.  Not much atmosphere in the limited dining space they have, but they have an easy to read menu of chicken items on display that helps you get individual amounts or larger family/party sizes.  The chicken breading here is more salty and less peppery than that national brand.  Not too salty, but it is definitely the strongest taste in the coating.    The chicken was nice a crispy on the outside, but just a bit over cooked on the white meat.  The biscuit was a little on the dry side too, but that may be due to the early afternoon timing of my visit.  Pricing was very affordable and I was in and out so fast that I really didn't get much chance to look over what other items they have on their menu.  Review #1913

Delightful food and smoothies to go with the pleasant service!  I've been watching for an opportunity when my wife and I could make it to the far southside (just across the street from Greenwood!) for lunch and it finally arrived.  Although a little hard to find if you don't know specifically where to look, it was well worth the effort.  If you are on County Line between Indy and the Greenwood Mall, you will notice a car wash and Saint Peter is the road on the west side of the carwash that is where you will turn north to find the restaurant.  They do have a large sign on County Line Rd if you know where to look, and once you pull up to the restaurant, there was plenty of free lot parking.  Easy to find once you have a good idea.  Upon entering, we were greeted (masks on everyone) and because they weren't that busy at lunch, we got a nice dining table (4 top) with plenty of spacing between the tables.  We had dined at a Japanese Steakhouse about a week before that had really disappointed us.  So maybe we weren't expecting much, but were hoping for a better experience here.  We loved it!    We started off with the salted Edamame.  (plenty of salt per bean pod.)  I decided to order the Salmon (Sake) Sashimi with 8 slices of fish.  Wow!  I usually order Sake whenever I go for sushi, but I have to say this was right up at or near the top for quality.  No sea smell like the other place.  The texture of the raw salmon was the most succulent I have had.  Only $10 for the whole thing.  I didn't even need the soy sauce because it was so delicious.  But on the pieces I dipped, Just another layer of flavor.  They didn't offer chop sticks but I did use a fork from my wrapped napkin to facilitate my eating.  Note that I understand sushi is "finger food" but having had a bad experience handling raw fish elsewhere, I wasn't sure I wanted to use my fingers and during these times, I made sure I had my hand sanitizer handy to be sure I hadn't touched anything either.  The point being I highly recommend the salmon.  I still can't get my wife to eat salmon raw, but it was my standout choice.  (I will have to go back to get a photo.  Can't believe I didn't have one.)  While waiting, we enjoyed our very affordable smoothies.  I got Strawberry Banana, and my wife got that with Pineapple too.  Just think they need wider straws since the pulp and ice would occasionally block the end of the straw.  Maybe a boba style straw would be better.  Soon, our main dishes arrived.  I went with the excellent Pad Thai with lots of chopped peanuts and an absolutely delicious sweet chili sauce.  I selected beef as my protein and it was fine.  I think most proteins would be secondary in flavor compared to the bright tastes of the rest of the meal.  My wife ordered an appetizer of Pork Gyoza Dumplings.  They were a bit on the small side and were only browned on one side, maybe just a bit too much but no sides were soggy like our experience elsewhere.  She didn't ask to see if they had low sodium soy sauce, so it did get a tad bit salty (especially after sharing the order of edamame.)  I got a small bite and I thought it was really good too.  Portion size left me quite full, but I could have easily asked for a to go box, but I was hungry and enjoyed every last bite.    Yes, you can run up a pricy tab but it all depends upon how much you order.  I don't understand why people complain about lunch saying it should be less expensive.  If you are getting full sized servings and it takes just as long to make as dinner, what difference does it make?  So, I had no problem with the cost.  Everything I ordered I really enjoyed and look forward to return and hope they don't slip on their food quality and service in the mean time.  Review #3881

One thing I value in reviews of bakeries and cake shops is when a review lets me know if I can walk in and buy something to eat without pre-ordering.  I can't tell you how many reviews I've read and they never mention it.  Well, here is a place that you can walk out with treats!  After moving to this shop location in Oct '18, this custom cake baking shop has a simple, relatively unadorned interior.  After entering from their shared parking lot, there is a wall of cake styles they have prepared (they look fantastic!) on the left.  A simple double display counter is in the middle and some additional items are on the right.  I was greeted and chatted with the owner/baker about being able to walk in purchase.  The only hitch is that you don't know exactly what will be available unless you a.  pre-order; or b.  stop in and check it out!  Over on the left side of the counter are several kinds of cake pops (I picked a couple that were really good!).  There were also hard frosted sugar cookies (mine were shaped like "Minion" faces), double coated chocolate oreos (emoji), and other items.  Over on the right side were varieties of frosted cupcakes sold in 2-packs.  I picked the peanut butter cupcakes which have chocolate cake topped and center shaft filled with a peanut butter mousse icing with crumbles on top.  OMG!  I just blew my diet completely, but it was so worth it!  A must for PB lovers!  Friendly staff, very reasonable prices for a bakery, and high quality finishes if you are thinking of ordering something for a special occasion.  I can't say how their order prices are compared to other bakers in the area since I haven't hosted any events in a long time.  But from what I saw and tasted, this is a place to definitely check out the next time you want to order something special...or just drop in.  Review #3350

I first found BHappy Peanut Butter at the annual Yelp Christmas festival at the Central Library a few years ago.  Back in those days, you could get out with other people and get free samples of vendor products.  One of the highlights of that event was discovering BHappy Peanut Butter.  On that night, I discovered my favorite of their offerings, the "Joy to the World" flavor combo.  This is really great around the Christmas season since it brings together a lot of great tastes like peanut butter, cranberries (dried), and both white and dark chocolate bits.  But I don't wait to buy it then.  Not only can you find this in some local groceries Like Target and Fresh Thyme, but at some local shoppes that sell Indiana products and even at some County/city welcome centers that carry local products as well!     Since I have seen these tasty treats all around, I haven't used the online service to order them.  I am strictly giving my rating based upon the end product.  These don't need to be refrigerated and if you have lots of willpower, they will last a long time if you can hide it from your family to make it last longer.     Even if you are successful in keeping your 12 oz. jar hidden, it may have some of the peanut butter oil separate.  But if you simply take a spoon and stir it up, it returns to the wonderful taste and texture that you expect.  Based upon all the nibs and items in my selection, the peanut butter was on the crunchy side, less creamy.  I like it that way, but it doesn't spread on butter as easily, but like most reviewers, I simply use a spoon to get a big bite and nurse it for awhile just to show I have will power!  Review #3884

We decided to head to Broad Ripple for a Sunday lunch and though there is a small lot for customers of Union Jack behind the restaurant, it was full, so my wife alertly spotted a place on Broad Ripple Avenue and pulled in.  Normally, it is metered, but on Sunday, was free parking!  We entered near the bar and were greeted!  Can you  believe it?  A pub/bar that actually welcomes its guests!  After asking if we were eating in or getting it to go, we were directed to the main dining area, but told that if we didn't find anything suitable, we could sit in the other dining area on the west side of the bar.  They normally don't have that area open, but because of the games on the multiple tv's, they had a large crowd.  Fortunately, our server/bartender was high energy and made sure he hustled to get our order  in and our beverages (and tableware) brought out promptly.  Excellent attention which I appreciate someone who realizes that taking care of the customers is important.   Anyway, we ordered the full size fish and chips and asked them to split it which they did.  We each got cole slaw (house made and quite tasty).  He brought out the malt vinegar, but since the tartar sauce was so delicious, I never even tried the malt.  The fish was delightfully breaded and seasoned.  Little bits of crispness, but no oily taste to the breading.  The fish was fork tender and fresh.  Bright white in color so it looked just as appealing as it tasted.  Note the waiter brought out steak knives, but we simply didn't need them.  I looked through the lengthy list of beverages, but since I had tried most of the local options, I went with a Breckinridge  NItro Raspberry Porter.  Maybe not the perfect choice for fish, but a pleasant tasting beverage for sipping while waiting.    I haven't been here during the evening, but I highly recommend stopping in for lunch!  Review #3855

What nice people!  It was my first time at this new restaurant and from the moment I entered, I was greeted and treated like I was a welcome guest.  The restaurant is the third in the metro area for R&R Extreme Wings.  It is located in a line of buildings on the west side of Lafayette Road, about a block south of 38th Street.  There is free parking out front, though it isn't a large lot.  Inside, you enter into the family dining area but you can also see the bar which is separated by a half wall.  The bar has a full liquor license, so some cocktails are available.  But, because I was getting my order to go, I didn't ask to see a beer/wine/cocktail list.  I decided to go with a lunch special which included six (half) wings, choice of topping (they have nearly 20!), choice of Ranch or Bleu Cheese for dipping, crinkle cut fries, and a non-alcoholic beverage (20 oz bottle) for only $6 (plus tax and tip).  When I had entered, the bartender asked me if it was for dining in or carry out and asked me to come over to the bar area to place my order.  I simply hung out there (they have a couple muted TVs going) while my order was prepared.  The wait was really short and I had my order with 10 minutes.    I ordered the Teryaki wings and they were really good.  The wings were roasted to where they had just a little bark to them and the sauce was generously applied, so I was glad they included napkins.  I would normally complain that they didn't include a wet napkin packet, but this was so finger lickin' good that I didn't want to waste any sauce!  The fries were large and crinkle cut with some seasoning already added.  Nice flavor and texture, and definitely didn't taste like they had been sitting under a heat lamp.  These had just a bit of crunch and tasted like they were a fresh batch.  Not oily either!    If you like checking out new restaurants, like trying lots of flavors on your wings, or simply like being around people that are in good moods and enjoy what they do, stop by for some tasty food at this location.  Review #3717

Bangkok offers a variety of lunch specials for about $10 and I decided to give one of those a try while visiting downtown.  The Pad See Ew is what I like to order on my first visit to a Thai restaurant to see how it compares to all the competition.  I went with the pork option at a medium spice level and the pork had an excellent flavor:  very deep and savory.  The noodles they use are the proper wide flat noodles and it is prepared with bits of broccoli, carrot, & celery.  The only negative was that the pork was overcooked and a bit dry.  Not bad though when eaten with the other bites.  The spice level seemed a bit lower than I expected, but that may be due to the surprisingly high spiciness of the Tom Yum soup that comes with the entree.  The entree also comes with a small egg roll (veggie) and side salad with a ginger dressing (it had a more complex flavor like they use more than ginger in their dressing.)  I will say that the service was just okay.  I waited to be seated and when taken to my table, wasn't provided a menu.  The table had been washed off, but wasn't dry (I used my napkin to take care of it.)  I asked for a menu, and after receiving it, the service was pretty routine.  Apparently, there is a lunch buffet available too, but I somehow missed it on the menu I was given.  The website only lists the dinner menu, so if a buffet interests you, you will need to ask about it or be more thorough than I was.  Fun fact:  Bangkok Restaurant is in the location of the once popular Charlie & Barnie's Chili on Ohio Street.  Maybe only old timers remember that place, but it used to be one of the "go to" places for lunch.  Review #1379

After a meeting on the north side, my wife mentioned she wanted to look for a computer (one that I wasn't tying up writing Yelp reviews on).  She was looking for a laptop that was average sized and would do the basics.  She suggested Best Buy which was just a short drive to the out buildings at Castleton Square.  We were greeted as we entered and when we headed over towards the computer, one of the staff named Sarah saw us and asked if we needed any help.  Boy, did we ever!  So, after a few questions about what we thought we wanted and what we needed the machine to do, she showed us four types including the one my wife ended up purchasing.  It was an upgrade from one of the early ones she was shown and this one was on sale for the same price!    While there, she also picked out some software and accessories that would make getting the machine more ready to go.  Since the store is nearly an hour from our home, we were able to take the computer with us to the Avon store to have the Geek Squad set up everything for us.  We simply dropped it off there and asked for a one day turn around to have the machine ready to go.  Overall, I was very pleased that Sarah offered help and walked us through the process from start to finish.  This was so much better than experiences I've had at other electronics stores, including other Best Buys.  Review #3677

I really enjoyed my visit to Vito Provolone's.  The service (Amy) was pleasant and efficient, the food cooked perfectly, and the atmosphere was  comfortable and well suited for Italian dining.  After parking in their lot out front, I was one of the first customers and was greeted and then seated on the right side of the restaurant.  They have a partial brick wall that blocks off the view of the rest of the restaurant unless you are standing.  It also helps reduce the effect of the opening of the door when it is cold out.  After hearing about the day's wine special ($3.50 a glass), I opted for a nice Chardonnay.  I placed my order for stuffed mushrooms (lots of cheese and spinach), and Orange Roughy Florentine which comes with choice of a side salad or a cup of soup.  I chose the salad.  My server then asked if I would like the salad brought out before the mushrooms since they would take a while to prepare.  (Great move!)  I said yes and enjoyed my salad (dressing came on the side...another plus) while waiting.  And before I finished the salad, an entire loaf (8") of sliced garlic bread arrived hot from the oven.  Very tasty and hard to resist eating it all at one time.  The mushrooms (6) were covered with cheese that was melted and stretchy, but not impossible to cut or bite through.  Just about perfect!  Some were bite sized and others I simply cut in half and had no problem finishing them.  Highly recommended.  Note that my server was clearing plates whenever she passed by and kept my water glass filled as well throughout the evening.  A pro!  My entree came out and looked fantastic.  There was a bed of spinach (with roughy bits underneath) and two fillets of fish that appeared to be covered with paprika and two slices of lemon on the side.  It looked great and was cooked perfectly!  Most and flaky.    The only problem was that there just wasn't much flavor.  Not sure what the chef was going for.  The white fish doesn't have a lot of flavor on its own and though I added the lemon and even a little bit of salt, I couldn't get much flavor out of it.  The paprika was not adding much to the flavor, so I was a bit disappointed because it looked so yummy.  There was nothing wrong with it, it was simply less flavorful than I had hoped.  I passed on dessert and was quickly processed after letting my server know I was finished.  A very nice experience for me, but I would probably go back to one of the dishes that comes with a rich sauce.  Review #1771

While out exploring, I remember my wife had mentioned some items that we needed and I figured that Walgreens might carry those items.  This store is located on the northeast corner of Madison and County Line so there are medians to deal with getting here, but the entrances to their parking lot are far enough away from the intersection to not be much of a problem getting in and out (except for rush hour).    The store is a fairly good size, though maybe not as large as the one in my hometown.  As you enter, the checkout counter is on your right with the pharmacy in far left corner, separated from the shopping by a little distance which affords a bit more privacy.  The aisles were clear and well spaced.  A Seasonal aisle is centrally located on the counter side of the store.    Although there was a delay at the counter, another employee saw that I was ready to check out and opened up her register so that I could proceed.  Very nice!  Review #3429

My wife and I were downtown for an appointment but when it was over we decided to grab lunch which is always a challenge on a Monday when so many restaurants are not open. Someone we had met during the meeting asked if we had tried Sauce on the Side which was one of her favorite places to grab a meal.  I hadn't tried it yet and checked Yelp to see if it was open on Mondays, so it sounded like a nice suggestion.  I know it says it is categorized as Salads, Desserts, and Italian, but I figured I would go for the Italian.    Having not read any reviews before going other than seeing it had a good overall rating.  I was a bit surprised that most of the Italian menu items were served as Calzones or "folds".  It is definitely not the kind of Italian restaurant where you find a wide variety of pastas and seafood.   But they do have a lot of flavor combinations in large folded calzones, each served with a small cup of sauce on the side.  I didn't think about it at the time, but since the meals and sauces are separate, I wonder if you can choose different sauces for your calzones than what is "normal" for each order.  I ordered the Meat me in St Louie calzone which came with a meaty tomato sauce.  My wife ordered the Five O which is a spin on Hawaiian that came with a chili sauce that wasn't too spicy for her.     Note that the servings, even folded cover have a dinner plate so we ended up getting to go boxes to save half our meals for dinner.  We didn't try any desserts or sides because the meals are big and filling.  They do carry some beer and cider in cans for customers who don't have restrictions on their lunchtime selections.   The calzones get pretty well toasted, so you may note a bit of browning on the crust (or blackening) and looking through the photos of the food on Yelp as well as our own meals, they aren't the most photogenic /appealing looking meals you can order, but the flavor was fine.  MY wife commented that the ham in her Five O was diced very small and didn't seem to stand up to the other flavors.  Bigger pieces of ham would have made it more appealing to her.     Inside dining was easy.  We ordered at the front counter (although we could have called in an order.)  The hostess said to pick our own table since there weren't many customers when we were there, so no concerns about social distancing for us.  We also were able to get boxes for our remaining food and even small cup lids for our remaining sauces so they didn't spill during transport home.     Parking is available mainly through metered street parking.  There is a garage which can get pricy if you stay very long.
