I think the garage is open to the public but it is connected with a hotel across from the Fieldhouse, so you may want to call ahead before arriving.   It was good food, but with all the options on most days downtown, I don't know that I would drive from my home and pick this place again.  If I worked in the area, I would probably explore more options on their menu.  Review #3888

Since I hadn't been to Yats on Mass Ave since they relocated to the north end, I found a spot along the road on the east/south side of the building and headed inside. The main entrance is on Mass Ave, but there is also an entrance on the east end.   There is a large central dining room compared to the prior location. Beyond a half wall, there is a counter where you place your order based upon the blackboard listings on the wall behind the counter. I noticed that at least one of the recommended items I was looking for was not listed, but fortunately, my Yelp! friends had made several recommendations.   I ended up ordering the half and half special for just a dollar more than a single item option. I went with the Chili Cheese Etouffee with Crawfish and the Maque Choux. Both were served over white rice. Both selections have a rich creamy base that smothers the rice. The first entree comes with chili seasonings, cumin and coriander, and is filled with cheddar cheese and crawfish tail meat. The meat is chopped relatively small, but I could definitely tell when I got a bit. Nice texture and the flavor was quite good.  The second half was a sweet and spicy mix with carmelized corn and chicken. The corn was really sweet and delicious. The chicken was cut into fairly small pieces, so it didn't stand out as much as the crawfish on the other side of the plate.   My friend grabbed a shaker of Cajun Seasoning and recommended trying it on my dishes. Wow! What a great suggestion! Just a few shakes and I could tell the flavor became fuller and was greatly improved. I highly recommend adding this. It added flavor without adding heat.  I also ordered the extra bread which is sliced and seasoned on the inside. Nice crunchy texture and it pairs well with the entrees.  So, the food was really good, but I was disappointed that for a sit down restaurant, there was no customer/staff interaction. I placed my order and asked about the recommended entree....all I got was a response that was blunt and said they only had what was on the blackboard. Sure, the food was served at the next counter within a couple minutes, but the food was set up on a tray along with my friends (even though we had ordered separately) and abandoned. I wasn't expecting to see two dishes on my tray and wasn't sure it was mine since I didn't really know what my meal would look like.   The customers are expected to get their own drinks and plastic ware and then bus their own tables. Okay, but I've had more pleasant staff interaction at a fast food place than here. So, this could have been a five star review if I had been greeted and made welcome. A vending machine shows about the same amount of personality.  Review #296

My wife and I were looking to try some place different for lunch and so we stopped at the AMP.  On the far end near the stage and restrooms, we found this shop.  It was bright and clean and the staff were friendly and attentive. We both ordered 6 Southern BBQ wings, but I also ordered fries which were crisp and lightly seasoned so they were really good.  Flavor was delicious on what we ordered but there were a couple things that could be improved.  First, the wings are coated before you get them, I prefer being able to dip them in the sauce.  This made for a really messy meal and since they don't carry handy wipes, we ended going to the nearby restrooms and soaking some paper towels on our own.  Hopefully they will address the clean up or offer to let the customers dip their own or both.  We didn't try the salads/greens part of the menu, but we both enjoyed the mild, but yummy flavor of the Southern BBQ.  They have a variety of sauces of varying heat levels to appeal to most customers.  They give you a receipt when you order that tells you order # which they call out, so be sure to stay in the area so you can hear when it is called.  There is plenty of seating in the area that is shared with other vendors.  We ended up busing our own table when finished.  I didn't see anyone from the AMP doing it.   Good wings and fries with soft drinks sold by the bottle.  Be sure to grab lots of napkins....you will need them!  Review #3938

What did I like about Upland's newest brewpub?  Let me see:  1. Despite it being opening day, everyone who was working was making sure customers were being looked after.  I was greeted with a smile, and when I sat at the bar, I had a team of folks swing by to see if I needed anything.  Special shout out to Steve who was my main server.  2. The space is huge and even though the parking lot was nearly full at 4:30, I never felt crowded.  3. The Cuban sandwich was delicious!  It's not an authentic version, but it is one of the best I've had.  They use Smoking Goose City Ham (great on its own) and a spiced & smoked pulled pork along with melted swiss cheese and house pickle chips.  Delicious with a bit of heat, just enough to let you know it's there.  4. The Exploration flight which allows you to pick two of the their standard beers and two of the sours/barrel-aged beers to make your flight.  Sure it is more expensive than other places, but if you know about brewing, you know you have to keep your sours away from your regular beers which means having a separate facility for the brewing.  That costs money.  But if you want to try a sour or a barrel-aged sour, you won't find more choices than at Upland.  5.  The patio.  This is going to be a deal changer for the area.  Understand that despite the efforts of a few brave businesses like Kuma and Revolucion, nobody was drawing the crowds that Upland was doing to the east of the fountain.  With the new apartments going in across Prospect, Upland is moving the restaurant/nightlife area across that Shelby Street boundary.  The patio had lots of tables and with the open garage doors to the brewery, felt very much a part of the business, not just stuck out there.    Five reasons = five stars.  Check this place out!  Review #2846

For as many times as I've been in this store with my wife, I can't believe I hadn't written a review yet!  Although there are several Joann Fabrics and Crafts within an hour's drive from our place, this is probably our closest and is definitely my wife's "go to" fabric store.     The plusses include lots of parking, lots of room inside the store, a really nice selection of seasonal items, both fabric and craft, as well.  If you download their app, you can save double digits on the discounts they offer.  They also have some in store coupons for those old-schoolers if you know where to find them.   I've never tried their framing services, so I can't recommend them one way or the other.   They usually have a lot of variety and supply, but not as much fabric as the Bloomington store which is a nice place to just wander.  Unfortunately, during our most recent visit, supplies were lower than usual, but I suppose that is somewhat expected during the pandemic.  Still, my wife was able to find what she needed and the lady at the cutting table even helped her find the correct stabilizer she needed.  The problem with this store is there never seems to be enough staff to help people who can't find an item, to cut the materials, or to open another register to get people through the lines.  It seems people working are answering phones, helping customers find stuff, as well as working a register or cutting fabric.  Just need more knowledgeable help to speed it up.  But overall, the service is good enough to keep us coming back.  Just so you know, they offer sewing machines for sale here too.  My wife is advanced enough that we've never asked about lessons.  Review #3805

I'm a black coffee kinda guy.  No cream or sugar, just a rich tasting cup of joe that I can drink right away without having to burn my tongue and ruin my tastebuds.  Pretty simple.  So, due to a change in my morning "routine", I hadn't had any coffee and while in Greenwood, decided to stop by this place I had been noticing for awhile.  So glad I did!  The exterior is rather nondescript and the inside is a bit industrial, but they do have a fireplace on the right side of the dining area and you can see through a window where the staff work some magic on roasting.  I went to the order line and used the chalkboard menu to help me decide on an "Everything Scone" to go with my medium roast black coffee.  The coffee was handed over right away and I was told they would call out the order when it was up (Not my name or a number, so I can imagine this could be confusing if two people ordered the same thing before the first was delivered.)  As I said, I like my coffee, but served at a temperature I can enjoy it. This met the challenge.  The medium black coffee had a nice aroma and the taste was rich, but not overpowering.  And when I ate the scone, the coffee was strong enough to not loose its taste.  The scone was fantastic!  About four inches long, the scone was a ham and cheese filled pastry that was still moist, though a little crumbly.  They also had some herbs inside the dough to enrich the flavor.  The Everything also has a hard fried egg between the scone slices.  It also came with a choice of bacon or sausage.  I went with the bacon since I am trying to maintain my weight during the holiday season.  Excellent choice.  I definitely recommend this combo.  The shop also has a rewards program for frequent visitors and a mug club where your mug hangs on a wall.  Note:  I bused my on table when done.  Not sure if that is expected or not, but they have a place by the water dispenser on the counter where I saw other used dishes and a trash bin.  Note 2:  The profits from this place are used to provide counseling for people who are in need.  I like that!  If you are a coffee fan and want a comfy place to relax while in Greenwood, make a point of checking this place out!  Review #1957

Like the anchor Books & Brews in Fishers, the Carmel taproom is filled with books and a nice selection of book inspired beers.  They also have a group of local guest taps if you aren't finding one of the house beers to your taste.  That would seem to be a rarity since they have five different house beers that are available year round and at least one other seasonal option.  I have tried all their standards, from the "Cream & Punishment" cream ale to the "Charlie and the Chocolate Stout" (milk stout), and have enjoyed them all.  On this occasion, I went with a pint of the "Your Local Library Lager" (7.6%, 20 IBU) and found it full of flavor and refreshing.  Not some one note beer, the tastebuds seemed to perk up on the first sip.    The guys working behind the counter were friendly and offered samples of both their beer and the guest taps.  That takes confidence in your product to trust yours will be the choice selected.  This franchise is located between Matt the Millers and Divvy restaurants and I had no trouble finding free parking behind the building.  There is a parking garage available too if you go at a more active hour.  Keep your eye on this business.  They have opened in a number of north side cities, and have plans for Colorado, Muncie, Broad Ripple, and even the south side within a few months.    Review #493

My wife and I stopped into this small Thai shop in a strip mall across from the entrance into Keystone at the Crossing.  Parking was pretty crowded due to the surplus of restaurants along this strip, but we found one on the back row along the highway.  Inside, we were greeted and seated at one of the tables in the clean dining area.  Not a lot of seats here, but enough to hold the customers of the day.  Our waitress took our drink orders and we placed our food orders at the same time.  My wife ordered the Fried Rice (with chicken) and selected mild for the heat content.  She thought it good, but should have gotten an upgrade on spiciness level or asked for soy sauce....just needed a little something to make her happy.  I ordered my standard Pad see ew (pork) also with a mild spice level, though I usually go with a medium spice.  I thought the meal had a nicely balanced flavor and the thick noodles were lightly coated.  The veggies could have been cut a little smaller, but otherwise, they were fine.  Each entree came with a cup of soup (fuller flavor than most places I've been), a small gingered salad, and a crisp spring roll with a sweet dipping sauce.  Service was friendly and prompt throughout the meal.  I think the spiciness would have helped my enjoyment of the meal more, but it was still good.  Review #3651

I've been in the shop a few times, but this was my first purchase of clothing.  (Other visits were for small items with the Colts' logo.)  I was greeted and asked if there was anything in particular I was looking for and when I mentioned long sleeve shirts, I was taken to a couple spots where they were located.  Some of the options were high on the wall, so when I pointed to one of them, the salesman grabbed a stick that lifted my size shirt off the rack.  He also mentioned that I could try it on in a concealed dressing room which I appreciated since I wasn't sure if a medium or large would fit best.    There was a small glitch with the receipt printer, but they took care of the problem with minimal delay.  The prices are higher than you would expect from comparable quality clothing, but that is because of the "official" franchise logos.  I knew that before going in, so I wasn't shocked at the prices.  But it was still a lot of money for a single shirt.    Note that they have a lot of non-clothing items with Colts on them as well.  Good service and a nice variety of items to choose from.  Review #3315

I've read the reviews and have to agree...this restaurant is a "must go to place" if you want great flavor.  It's not for picky eaters.  It's not for special diets or people on diets.  It is simply great tasting food that is generously portioned and is loaded with buttery flavor.  The Trap is a "hole in the wall" operation on the side of a liquor store at 34th and Keystone.  It's a one person operation and although there are hours posted on Facebook, the restaurant opens when the chef is ready.  My only complaint has been that I have been there several times at 11 a.m. when I expected the place to be open and there were no signs of anyone inside.  So, be advised to check the FB page for any closings and then wait closer to 11:30 to arrive.    Normally, I would have given up on a place that isn't open on time, especially after a 40 minute drive.  But, I reached out to the chef and she asked me to give it one more try.  Am I glad I did!  I stopped by around 12:30 and there was a relatively short line.  I placed my order and had my food bagged and ready to go in about five minutes.  There is limited seating at a picnic table, so I assume most customers eat in their cars or take it home.  I didn't see any beverages listed on the menu, so I was fortunate to bring my own bottle of water.  Okay, that's enough about the place.  The food is some of the best tasting I have ever had.  I ordered the "Loaded salmon with shrimp" meal.  I ordered it mild and with Parmesan cheese added.  I also selected one of the four "Trap Buttah" options, mine being the OG Garlic Herb Buttah.  The "loaded" selections come with the seafood of choice (mine had 5 large shrimp and about 6 oz or two decks of salmon), an ear of corn on the cob (really sweet!), a hard boiled egg, a sliced new potato, and about a third of a head of brocolli (not bite-sized, but tender enough to spear with my plastic fork.)  All this was smothered in the Garlic Buttah and "sprankled" with a fresh spice seasoning "New Bae" (instead of Old Bay).  After the first bite, I couldn't wait to try the next item on the loaded styrofoam tray to see how the buttery sauce enhanced the taste.  Consider my mind blown!  Okay, I think you get the picture that I liked this place.  Here are some other things I noticed.  - The styrofoam is lined with aluminum foil so you aren't eating off the foam.  - The food is served hot, so if you don't eat it right away, the seafood will continue to cook in the closed styrofoam, so it may get a little overdone.   - There wasn't a plastic knife, but fortunately, the food was tender enough to be speared or separated with the plastic fork.  - A free towelette was included along with several napkins.  You WILL get your fingers messy picking up the shrimp and the corn.  The sauce is loaded on, so you may be wearing some of it by the time you finish.   Now, if there was only a biscuit to sop up some of the remaining buttah...  Review #290

Just west of Allisonville Road on 116th is this pet store located in the same shopping plaza as the Kroger.  There is plenty of parking nearby and the store was generally clean and orderly (though someone left one of those large ladders blocking one of the aisles.)  The franchise out of Michigan isn't the largest pet store, but seems to carry a fair supply of healthy dog and cat foods, supplies for those pets and also sell birds, fish, and a few other critters.  In the back is a dog washing room for those who like self serve, but prefer to not do it at home.  I did notice that when I checked out, the Yelp discount seemed to show up as being expired.  Fortunately, the clerk went ahead and gave me the 10% discount which I appreciated.  Seems like the manager should look into that.  Overall, I had a positive shopping experience and would recommend this place to people who care about their pet's.  Review #3688

Just because there are lots of new restaurants on 116th, don't forget to check out some of the places on 96th!  Chao Vietnamese Street Food is located just east of the Interstate on 96th (near the former Sun King Brewing location).  Great sandwich and a good value when you consider they throw in a bowl of Pho with your lunch special.   Because it's in this stripmall, there is a lot of free parking nearby.  I entered into the dining area and quickly realized that I should place my order at the counter at the back of the shop.  The man behind the counter was friendly and helpful.  When he realized I was ordering a Bahn Mi (Pork), he mentioned it came as a special with the bowl of pho (chicken for me) for about $9.  It sounded like a good deal, so I paid and was given a number stand to put on my table.  After a few minutes (less than 10), my meal was brought out.  The Pho was steaming hot, so I decided to try my sandwich first.  The Banh Mi was colorful with the fresh cilantro and julienned veggies (especially the carrots) topping the grilled pork.  The seasoning of the pork was delicious and the bun was lightly crisped for a little more crunch.  Highly recommend!  The pho was a mildly flavored broth with thin noodles and strips of poached (?) chicken.  The chicken seemed like it had no seasoning, so I can't rave about it.  The bowl was roughly a cup sized serving and came with a soup spoon to help get all the broth.  Each table has chopsticks and forks in a can, so I opted for the fork to get the chicken and noodles since my chopstick skills aren't quite good enough to handle the slippery noodles.  I thought the pho was okay, but would like to try the veggie version for only $1 more.    The dining area was filled with small tables and wasn't too loud.  I think it is due for an update since the walls are marked up by people sliding their chairs against it.  After all, the dining room makes the first impression, so it would help to make it a good one.  Although I saw a place towards the back where dishes could be bused,  I noticed none of the other customers were doing that.  One of the employees was clearing the tables.  Overall, the sandwich was delicious.  The Pho was okay, but could benefit from seasoning.  The service was friendly and prompt.  Review #3725

I am certain that I will need to revise or at least update this review in a month or so once there is a grand opening and more shops have moved into the AMP (Artisan MarketPlace).  Like another review, I think this place has a lot of potential.  It is intended to serve the many new businesses locating in the Tech 16 development as well as serve the neighboring communities providing some job opportunities for locals who may not have high tech degrees that many of the employees of Tech 16 will have.  Nice to see a new development think of benefitting the existing neighborhoods while providing state of the art buildings/research facilities, etc.  When I compare it to other communal areas like "The Garage at Bottleworks", this place is much brighter and at least currently, much quieter.  I noticed that on the east end of the AMP is a raised stage so there may be a time when live music/entertainment may raise the sound levels.  But now with just a few shops open while more construction goes on in the east end of the building, it was easy to carry on a conversation and easy to hear the staff working at the shops.  Note that a new side road will be added from Gent Street on the north side of the AMP building which will provide access to a 1000 car parking facility to accommodate the crowds that will be drawn to this area.  Right now, there is limited free parking along Gent Street.  Hopefully, the construction will catch up with the demand as more people find their way here.  For those who know where Guggman Haus Brewery, The AMP is just a few blocks south on Gent.  As of my last visit, Circle City Sweets and Tinker Coffee Co at the AMP were open.  Prox (from the City Market) is nearly ready with chef crafted salads.  Frankie's Pizza Parlor looks close to being ready on the east end where the construction is currently limiting access.  Review #3908

I stopped at Walgreens in hopes of seeing the new ELF Villain's collection. Sometimes Walgreens gets them before the holidays. Sometimes they don't. This particular one doesn't ever get them according to their cosmetics person. SAD. Really sad. I suppose I'll have to skulk other Walgreens to find them.

I love shopping at Ross Stores. I stop at every one I come across. Yes, much of the merchandise is the same, but once in a while, you find a gem. It really is a treasure hunt.   They carry a selection of "as seen on Tv" stuff, a slew of Jr's clothing, a decent selection of ladies and missy, but they generally fail at plus, men's and petite.  These markets are woefully represented. Sure they have a men's section, but looking through the stuff, it's crappy t shirts and fubu jeans. Hardly anything the men in my life would wear.  This particular store's selection of lingerie/under garments is sad. They don't have a good variety of lingerie other than bras and panties.  Their home goods is very nicely situated as are their bed and bath items ... and their shoes!! My goodnes, their shoes are to die for!  One rhing I've noticed recently is that they are carrying many more high end designers: Michael Kors, Calvin Klein, and others at decent prices. So it does pay to shop at Ross.

Tried a Flat White for the first time on the recommendation of a friend (Thanks Amy P!) The first location I went to said no, I couldn't because they were out of whole milk. This location though, they were more than happy to oblige. The service was quick and efficient. The barista was both bubbly and sweet as she made my drink order.   The drink itself was tasty, not sweet but rich on the tongue. Next time I get this, I'll see if they can add vanilla to it.

It was whispered this was some of the best Ice Cream out there. I can NOT dispute this fact.  I splurged and got myself a single scoop of Mint Chip. The scoop was HUGE. I mean -HUGE- The flavor was delicious and it was so creamy! It was a delight in my mouth!  I also ordered a large cappuccino. While it wasn't the perfect cuppa, it was a decent cup of rich java, and that's just what I wanted with my ice cream. I would reccomend this place to anyone.

It's been a while since I've visited BayWalk... that I call it BayWalk tells you just how long it's been.  Re-branded the Sundial, it city center has undergone an overhaul and is quite lovely! From its open air design, to its stunning sundial sculpture with dolphins surrounding it's base, you can tell that there's been a small fortune sunk into the over haul and its well worth it.   High end shops line the promenade, A lot of restaurants have decided to populate this popular destination and of course Locale Market has finally opened, this means more foot traffic! This it certainly is a good thing for Down Town St. Pete.

Ice creamery outside of the Cobb theatres at Countryside.  I'm giving this a 3 because the girl who tended, Sarah, us was good but she was left to flounder due to poor scheduling. She was in the weeds. I felt bad for her.   The ice cream was good, especially when she blended in the toppings I requested. But there was a line building up and there was only one girl, a new menu and she was new there. She kept her cool and di just fine with us.

This started out GREAT! The place smelled wonderful, and the food, Pretty darn tasty. The price was good, and food was plentiful and hot.   When we arrived there was one table of a mother and daughter, and our table.  After we arrived another couple arrived. There was 1 waitress.  While I can't say it ever got truly busy, I can say that she never checked back with us after the initial "How's everything?" never asked us if we wanted more water. After we were clearly finished with our food, she never came back to see if we needed boxes.   At this point 2 more groups came in, one group of 4 and one group of 5 and they sat at the back of the place, those seemed to take up her time. This was about 6:30. My friend and I were done by now, we were looking at our watches, commenting that it was relatively early. By 7pm, though we were still talking, the waitress still hadn't checked on us, when we would try to get her attention, she never did seem to make eye contact with us, she simply ghosted to the back areas of the eatery.   At 7:15 we had to verbally signal her to get us boxes, and to ask for the check. She then didn't remember them for another spate of time, we finally got out of the establishment at 7:44.  The times are known because I made note.   I would come back for the food, but the service was pitifully slow. Need more help in there.

Had dinner with a friend here, before going out shopping.    The service was quick, efficient and friendly. I ordered a pick two of French Onion Soup and a 1/2 salad.  I asked for extra croutons and dressing on the side. My requests were easily made and cheerfully done.  My friend ordered a special sandwich on white bread.  They did that for her as well. We were quite pleased.

Tasty, tasty, tasty!   For a fast food option, they're relatively healthy. The pulled pork was delicious and moist. The black beans were delightful, but the salad was over dressed. I'll come back when I get the chance, since it's on the way to work, but now I know it's a great choice for protien.

Lunch after a massage is always something that I crave. So since this was in the same plaza as the massage envy I go to, I stopped in for a bite.   The locale is large, it's spacious with nice seating. I was even greeted by the company dog outside.  Once inside, I realised I was the only person there on a Monday Afternoon. Sad really..   I placed an order for water and a small pizza, this way I could take most of it home and eat it later.  I ended up getting the margharita pizza, and it came out rather quickly. The ingredients were fresh, large slices of tomato topping it with lots of basil and some garlic and oil. Tasty. But a touch underdone.   I'd go again.

What a neat little shop! I don't get down to South Tampa to shop, but when my fellow Massage Therapist invited me out for a shopping party, how could I resist.  I made my way down and parked near the little ravioli shop and walked into this warm and inviting little storefront.   She has -everything- you might want. Some great fashion, some very ecclectic styles, but her size range really only goes from Xs to Large.  As a woman who currently fits in 3 size ranges (Yes, I can wear a Jr.s XXL, A Womens XL or a 1x) this can be a bit disconcerting. But I did find a thing or three that I just needed.  I didn't buy them, NO, I bought accessories. She has SO many pretty sparkingling and shiny things, that I couldn't keep my hands off of them!  If you need dangly necklaces, Tassles or shiny stones, this is the place to come. Her prices are just about average and her service is right on the money. The only reason she's not getting 5 stars is the music, It was NOT the choice for me, and it might have just been for that night but hearing the rap and hip hop was off putting to me, so that MIGHT make me not come in on some days. Other wise, Great selection, great accessories and over all an excellent shopping environment.

We saw Jessi at one of the most derelict events I've ever been to. I only say this because I've been to a few and My husbeast and I were the only people who weren't vendors at the Glorifying Women's Expo, that Say's something.   I'd seen Jessi and her Product on Monday at the Moonlight Bazzar at Red Rockstar Bar, but since I don't like hot things, I had avoided her. HOWEVER.. This time I had the Husbeast. and he is an avid consumer of all things HOT and spicy.  This was a good match. Jessi was awesome. She allowed him to sample each sauce, telling him about the components behind them and even offered some to me. Sharing with  me a brownie bite that was decadent and made with her blueberry ginger sauce.   In the end, we liked them So much that we bought all 6 flavors. Yes, You read that right all six bottles now have homes in my kitchen. We will certainly be new customers as long as she's making these delicious condiments.

In a food truck food court, one food truck stood out in stark contrast above the others, it was Twisted Iron. Why? they had a line.  We were at the front of this line and I was happy for that, because it was chilly under the Bridge at Pierce street market.   Both the husbeast and I got Chicken & Waffles. The wait time was short but the food portions were large. 3 juicy pieces of chicken atop a large waffle, a serving of smuckers breakfast syrup and I THINK It was honey Mustard, but since I don't use it, I gave that to the husband.   The chicken was good. VERY VERY GOOD. it had a nice flavour and was perfectly cooked.  THe only thing about the waffle I can say negative is that it wasn't light. it was very heavy and dense, and that's not the way I prefer my waffles. Bt the flavour was spot on and yum to my mouth!   I ate all the chicken and 1/4 the waffle. The husbeastie was a member of the clean plate club!

So I came back to Tin Drum on my own, and I have to say that I'm pretty impressed. I walked in after the lunch rush, so there was plenty of parking, and there was no line!  I ordered one of the main dishes we'd had at our event, which was the Tin Drum Curry. It was the first time I'd had curry, and it set well with me. I did ask that it not be too spicy, and as I made that request, they brought me more rice so I could thin out the sauce.   When it was brought to my table, after very minimal wait, I was pleased. It wasn't terribly spicy at all.   It was incredibly good. There was just enough chicken, sauce and spinach to make me happy.  And a few minutes later, Kaitlyn brought out the bowl of extra rice, apologizing that it didn't come with the meal. I thanked her.   The staff was very proficient about keeping the place clean and neat. The tables were wiped down and dishes - if you were eating in - were never left on the tables long.   My only complaint? No Jasmine tea! It had been there for the event, and wasn't there when I went back. *sad*  Ah well, I will be back, I truly enjoyed my meal!

The husbeast is working from this building for a while, as his new company is setting up shop off of 60.  The lobby is clean, neat and the bathrooms are kept spotless.  The only issue is that their wifi isn't strong. Le Sigh.

I LOVE me some Zaxby's Zalads.  Their House Zalad is fantastic, with cucumber, tomato and crispy onion, it makes for 2 delicious meals. Add to that some zesty fried mushrooms and life is good!   The seasoning on their fries is perhaps the best around - though I've noticed that Universal uses something very similar!

Totally a gorgeous venue, if you're looking for a place to have your wedding or other special event. What is not to love about floor to ceiling windows draped in diaphanous curtains, or marble floors that are originals to the building. The Vault is steeped in History, and will make your event something so very memorable.

I've never seen a "super center" that is this small.  It lacks a cohesive plus size clothing center - heck what used to be their plus wear is mostly clearance now.  They do have a decent electronics department, if you have an Iphone. A fairly OK selection of Health & Beauty.  But this is mostly a Walmart if you need to quick stop. There's a real super center 20 minutes away on SR54 or JUST up the road on Alderman.

Long drive home and I needed sustenance... I don't generally care for fast food, and since Steak 'n shake is a step above most places, I opted to stop there.  Where else can you get a triple patty steak burger and fries for $4 bucks?   In general, the food is good, the burgers are fresh, even if the service is NOT the fastest.

I remember when these apartments were horrid.   Now they're kind of passable. I had to drop a friend off here after she stayed the weekend with me. Gated entry and exits keep this from being the suitcase city of old.  (and yes, way back when, I used to .. well not live here exactly, but spend a LOT of time with my then boyfriend, now ex husband - ahh good ole college days..AHEM)  They've done a lot to clean up the place, given it a complete over haul, even though the apartments still look like boxes on the inside.

The burgers take time to come out because they're made fresh. The fries weren't as hot as tthey could have been, but the food was made to my specs and I didn't have a problem with that.  The diet coke was a good mix and all in all, II'd come back.

If EVER there was a store that had -too- much, Bed, Bath and beyond is the perfect example of that store.  They have floor to rafter and just about every square inch of floor space - save that what you would call isles filled with merchandise.   And given that this is Christmas shopping season, well, it's doubly so! Yes, if you've seen it on TV, you can find it there. Do you want the Veg-o-matic Spaghetti maker? They have it.  Do you want Poo-Pouri?Its there too, and in multiple scents. The sweeping craze of Adult Colouring is big as is STAR WARS. Oh lard, lets talk about Star Wars. If it's got Kylo Ren or the Chrome Storm Trooper on it, its there.   They have pillows and comforters, they have everything you need. It's packed floor to beam with everything and more. I don't enjoy the pace, or the place, but it is what it is, and they will print you out a Gift receipt if you forget to ask for one when they're ringing things up.

Contrary to other reviews, this is NOT the worst Ross out there. Sure it has it's issues, and yes, like any other major discount retailers, the clothing is a bit jumbled and discombobulated. But for the most part it's an OK shopping experience.   The Loss Prevention person hangs out near the door, is more like a Walmart greeter, if you ask me. Yes, their presence is seen, but what do they actually do? Not a lot, really. Nothing they CAN do, honestly.  Since the holiday hours have been extended, they're currently open til 12:30 am or 1:30 am on any given night. This means, no long waiting lines to check out.   Heck! I walked away with 4 new dresses last night, all of them looked great.  I'll continue to shop here when I can!

Stopped here for lunch. It wasn't busy at all, so our food was made very quickly.   This location is not at all like the other location I've visited in Tampa, but it is quite nice. The food came out hot and fresh.

This isn't my first go with a Korean BBQ. I've visited one in Hawai'i, and it was a similar experience.   We had a large group, 10 people. When I say this is both a labor intensive and confusing experience, I mean it.  It could have been our group, or it just could have been the night, but though the food was endless - most of the group ordered the hot pot/bbq all you can eat combination for $30.  The meat for the hotpot came in frozen roll ups and the meat for the BBQ came in slabs of marinated meat, but the seafood and meats were combined and you only got one or two pair of tongs. I was exceedingly concerned about cross contamination.  We had one person allergic to mushrooms and ask that they be separated out, they were not. We made sure to cook his food separately for him since we didn't want him getting sick.   I will say they are concerned about how they are perceived. I ordered the Honey dew water (?) A frothy, almost sweet but very light drink. It was delivered, but shortly after, the waitress came by and delivered another saying she'd given me the wrong one, she'd given me a cucumber, I honestly couldn't tell them apart.  I noticed that the glass was split - broken down the side, but not enough to leak, just enough to shatter if it clinked against another, when I was 1/3rd the way done with my drink. I pointed this out to the waitress on her next pass, she immediately took that away, and brought me a 3rd. All in all, I got an apology from the owner/Manager for the inconvience, and we only paid for one of them. I understand things like that happen, and I didn't ask for a replacement as the drink was already consumed.   We were there 2+ hours, the food was plentiful and they kept coming around filling our pots with broth, and asking if we wanted more meat.  I assure you we got our money worth.  I admit that when I got home, I stripped and put everything in the wash and immediately set to shower, because we smelled like food. Something that you remember from working in the food industry.   While it was an alright experience it was more labor intensive than I want my dinner to be. Would I do it again? Maybe.

I've been meaning to come here since they opened. Today afforded the opportunity.   I've been to Oahu, I've had Mac Nut Pancakes and I've been craving them ever since.. and today, I had them again. they were Ono Grinds! The weather was perfect for sitting outside on the patio deck, listening to the conversations that flowed around me while I ate my food, and sipped my tea.   The service was attentive and the food was fresh. The menu was a bit daunting for a dyed in the wool omnivore like myself, but if you're a vegetarian or are health conscious, visit Ohana Cafe, Give a little Aloha and Mahalo to the wait staff.  I will be back!

Stopped in today after finding out that my favorite Thai place didn't open until 4.  Since Red Robin was close by and I had an errand to run at the mall, the husbeast and I decided why not.   What we first noticed is that they've got advertising up for their new autumn menu, including the Sam Adams Oktoberfest beer and their Pretzel burger.  This piqued the husbeast's interest and me, well, I'm a simple creature, I just wanted MEAT!   We perused the new slick menu layout - instead of being a fold out menu, they've now got newly photographed food offerings in a book style menu- and i chose to have the French dip, as a starter, we chose their pretzel bites. I've had them in the past and they've been delicious, today though, they were a disappointment. The cheese was clumpy and the bites themselves tasted microwaved and over salted.   The way the food is presented is much prettier now. Gone are the plastic baskets, now food comes neatly arranged on plates, fries come served in hammered steel buckets. Everything looks slick and delicious.  They even offer 7 different sauces for your fries that are standard, and a few other sauces that are premium for an up-charge. This is something new.  Our entrees were served quickly and as ordered. They were delicious! The food and the service was excellent.   Since I've been on a restricted diet, I ended up having to take half my meal home. Its days like today that I wish I could order off the kiddie menu!

I'm not a huge fan of Chick-fil-A, but I will say that they are always courteous, quick and the food is always good, if you order one of their value meals. You certianly can't beat the waffle cut fries or their grilled nuggets. Seriously, if you've not tried the grilled nuggets, do so, they're the tastiest thing on the menu!

I went all afternoon without eating. This is a dumb move, so finally after my trip to Kohl's was done, I stopped in at Tijuana Flats fo fill my neglected tummy.   This is a new store, the windows really provide for a very bright, airy feeling to what are usually dark venues. The bright "comic book" style art on the walls always makes me smile. This store's, in particular was crisp and fresh, even the ceiling, which was not yet tiled in painted tiles, had ones that were neatly done.   The Manager, himself waited on me, he was polite and funny and made sure i got just what I wanted, including the Diet coke, topped with cherry coke for sweetness. *grin*  He came out to check on me a few times to make sure that everything was ok, and that I really enjoyed things.  And I did. His competency was excellent. He was really personable and told me about how the training of the stores were done, how quickly the stores are growing and how they manage to keep quality even across the board.

Popped in to Hot Wax but briefly last night. I didn't get a chance to do more than just peruse while my friend was on a call out side.   The store is beautiful, well lit and kept very clean. The staff seems friendly and knowledgable. I love that there's a glass blower right there making pipes right in front of you. That's so neat.

Honestly, I'd normally skip this place because of the way it looks like. But as the adage goes, don't judge a book by the cover. Once inside, I placed the order for a Margarita pizza and took a seat outside with my friend.    Our pizza was delivered shortly, it was topped with fresh tomato, LOTS of fresh basil and garlic, and a white sauce. THe crust was perfection, toasty and tasted wonderful. Everything was just right.   We had discussed knots but in the end decided not to order them, imagine my surprise when an gratis order was delivered to us. You can bet that we will be back here again. Perhaps not to eat in, but certainly for carry out. I really want to try their wings.

I was meeting a friend here because I remembered the last time I was here, they had a coffee shop attached.  It wasn't busy, but lawdy, Clearwater was sure hopping. After fighting for a parking spot, I finally gave up and paid a pretty penny $10, for a spot behind CVS across the street and walked to the destination.  As I said, it wasn't busy and that was good. My friend and I placed our orders, I got the Steakhouse burger - sauces on the side, and He got the All American burger. We upgraded to the combo for $3 more, and got a drink (Soda for me, coffee for him) and a side, rings and fries respectively. I paid the $27 and we got our buzzer and took our seats.   Five minutes later, we were called up and our food was given. They were good sized burgers, however, i took the bun off of mine. They weren't over done, they were cooked just over medium. The toppings were done too. The rings and fries were tasty.   I'd come back.

Crockett's towing was the service that the FHP used when my mom was in her accident. At first, we had no idea where her car was at, so it took a little detective work on my end, but we found it.   The people there were awesome, caring and understanding. There was a hold on our car and the others involved in the multi-car accident so I had to wait to get the important things out of our car.  Those things included the hearing aids that she was wearing when the airbags went off. So for a week she was deaf as a door nail. Ah well.   When we were able to retrieve things, the Crockett's team was there to help me with getting the license plate off, made sure I had what I needed. All in all, they did a great job with helping me.

I have driven past this TBBCW a few times and wondered what it was. Was it just a brewing company, or was it food too? Since the husbeast and I were both out and about, we decided to stop in and check it out.  The evening was absolutely mild, so we opted to sit outside in the bar patio area. With the fire tables and the over head bulb lighting, it was fun and festive. And of course, it was just beautiful at sunset.  Our waitress was perfect, she was quick, friendly and informative, and I especially loved her backward written tattoo. Great message to one's self.   We ordered our drinks and placed our order for Hummus and Lebeneh with naan. It's been AGES since I've had Lebeneh - a tangy goats milk cheese with a yogurt like consistency, that's absolutely decadent to the tongue. I was Thrilled that they had some and even happier that it was well made and came with a really flavorful hummus. The naan was crispy perfection.   The husbeast ordered a steak and bacon chop salad, and I ordered the Rat something shepards pie, with a side salad,  the side salad... I should have stopped there, it was HUGE. A meal in itself.  I couldn't finish it, so it went into a box.  The meals themselves were tasty and good. Both portions were large and yes. VERY VERY yummy.   Will we be back? Sure will!

Stopped here because there was an ETSY craft show.  The only other time I'd ever been to the Coliseum was a Cat show nigh on 20 years ago. Nothing had change except what they were showing. The floors are still lovely wood and highly polished, The accoustics are great and the stage calls to me.   This particular show was set up as any craft show is, with rows and rows of people selling things, the Venue itself was selling hot dogs for a buck and they were tasty.   The only complaint I had was that parking was scarce and hard to use.

During Third Friday I decided I just NEEDED to stop in. They have such great displays that I wanted to see what else they might have. Lo and behold, they had a picnic basket just outisde the door, and it was a whopping $5. I bought that! It will make a fantastic Ren Faire basket.   Inside, its a bit cluttered, there's a lot to look at, a lot to browse, and you can't forget to look up at the walls near the ceiling, as there's stuff up there too! The prices are reasonable, and all in all, its a fun afternoon to poke around.

A friend told me about the Honu last night on FB, given that I adore Hawai'ian inspired food, I made the decision to go today! I'm really glad I did.   It's located right off Main street in Dunedin, in an adorable cottage/bungalo that is very welcoming and bright. Parking might be difficult at first, but Dunedin has plenty of street and public parking so that's that.   Once inside, I was seated and the specials were gone over.  The menu itself was quite extensive too!  I decided I wanted to do things the Hawai'ian way, and went for the plate lunch: Agave Pork, green goddess slaw and potato mac salad.  The table next to me, three wonderful ladies also made the same order, so we shared in the community of the same food and chatted while we waited.   When the food was delivered, it was obviously made fresh, smelled great and tasted even better! The green goddess slaw was unlike anything I'd ever had before! It was light, fresh and tangy, the flavor was bright on the tongue and I really couldn't get enough. The Potato-mac salad was out of this world.  The agave pork was a bit on the sweet side, but I liked it fine.   I actually ate every scrap of food on my plate, the portions were JUST right!  I opted for dessert, because really who can resist? I chose their "that's how the cookie crumbles" Which was immense! warm chocolate chip cookies, fresh whipped cream.. all served sundae style. Honestly it would only be made better if they sold it WITH their macadamia nut ice cream!  Over all, the food and the service were absolutely amazing! I will most certainly be back

A Tampa classic.   I've stopped in here so many times. It's odd that I've never given them a review.  I find them best for late night bites and cups of coffee, when you want to linger with the person you're with, but don't want to deal with Denney's or Village Inn.   Their food is damned good, and the waitresses work hard to get you what you want.

Popped into Glossy 130 Nails & Spa by chance. My nails needed done, but I wasn't keen on making the drive all the way down to Countryside.  On a whim, I turned at Glossy nail and went inside.   Almost immediately I was take to a seat, a gentleman named Deon started to work. He commented on how shiny my current nails were (the other place does great work.) and asked what I was looking for. I want the SNS Dip Polish and was given a display of colors to choose from.   Once I chose what I wanted, he started to work on removing the old nail polish so that the new could be put on.  He really didn't let the nail polish remover sit on long so there was a lot he had to remove via dremmel.   Once the color was off, he set to trimming and shaping my nails. He was very gentle and kind while he was working. He made sure that I was happy with the length and the shape. The last time I left that up to the technician, this time I asked for a specific look.   When he was done, about 45 minutes in total, my fingers shone prettily in the light. A sparkly blue that will look fabulous for my friend's spring wedding.

Came here with a friend of mine before doing a salt float. We chose it because it was close and our original destination was closed because it was a holiday.   Chili's wasn't busy, and we were seated rather quickly. Both of us perused the new menu, neither of us saw what we really wanted but did notice that there was a lunch menu that offered relatively cheap food for a low price.    The server was concientious and quick, but the food was mediocre at best. My friend opted for the fajitas on the lunch menu with the side of rice and beans - Cadillac style, and was disappointed to find out that the rice was hard, as if it was old and had set out and dried.

I found this shop completely by accident! I love spice shops, I love the way they smell, I love the way they have their displays.  This store was special in the way that they will let you taste the blends as well as smell thing. I've never encountered that before.   Service was impeccable. The gentleman running the store too an interest in what I was needing, how It could be used, and showed me some recipes I might be interested in.  He even had a powdered chili pepper that my husband would love.  I will -certainly- be back.

Took a class here, so this is only for the Meeting room.  The staff was friendly enough, and directed me to the large room where the CPR class was being held. The room had one small issue, the AC was either too hot or too cold, there didn't seem to be a happy medium. I would certainly take a class here again.

Date night, Apparently there are 2 locations in Oldsmar and I was at one while the beau was at another. While I waited for him to join me at this location, I ordered my hot chai Tea. Jonah was absolutely wonderful. He was personable and friendly and exceptionally warm. We chatted about how our names are different (my alternate Id) and how we don't often hear them, though mine is growing popular due to Anime.   Once my order was placed, it took only a few minutes to have it in my hands so I could wait for Bruce to join me. I'd come back.

Friday night is a busy night... and when it's cold outside, it's even busier since they can't use their outside seating.   The food is -good-, VERY good.  The husband and I decided to try a little something from every column.  We tried the Caprese salad, two different kind of wings: The fire side and the Garlic/parmesan wings and a small margharita pie.   Everything was delivered relatively quickly, the caprese salad was very fresh with nice big leaves of basil. The wings were tasty, but the garlic/parm wings were missing something.. salt.   And the pizza.. THE PIZZA was delicious! Absolutely tasty. Would certainly come back for that any day.

A friend won tickets to see Gary Valentine at Side Splitters and asked if I wanted to join, and since it was a Thursday night, I said SURE.  I've not been to Side Splitters since the late '90's and thought why not.   The place really hasn't changed. The waiting area is still predictably small, and the seating area is still a bunch of small (VERY) small tables pushed together onto a small floor where the comedian stands on a stage and does his/her schtick. They have a 2 drink minimum, and prices are... well, they're not cheap.   The entertainment we saw, The first, a local fellow from NPR (poor guy - I grew up there, I KNOW all too well the tribulations of Redneckville) was decent.  I liked him, but I think the crowd didn't know how to react to him.  The headliner? He was funny. I'd honestly not heard of him, but recognized him when I saw him. He was on King of Queens, and he had us ROLLING.   Over all, the show was a fun outing.  They did say there would be trivia after the show to win prizes, I waited around.. trivia never happened.  ***EDIT TO ADD***  So a friend of mine just related this to me:  "I had paid by credit card, left "in Cash" on the tip line and left her $3 bucks in cash at the table.  When I checked my statement, I saw that she added a $5 charge for the tip, to a $14 bill?  I don't think so."  This was on Tuesday.  She tried to get a hold of them, but no one answered. Finally she got through and she was supposed to hear back from them on Wednesday. Of course, she never got a call back. Today, she received a message from their Manager stating that a mistake was made and that $5 would be credited back to her card.   I find this slightly shady, honestly. Not everyone checks their bill, and $5 here and $5 there adds up quickly when you're padding your tips.   BE AWARE.

I usually REALLY like Applebee's. But this time, the resturant fell flat.   Mom and I came here for lunch before going to Joanne's fabric and crafts.  We ordered an appetizer of the beercheese bread sticks before our mains.  When it came to the table, I noticed that the cheese was unmelted, so I tried to stir it into the gloop and see if that made any difference. Sadly it did not. The sauce was cold.. like someone didn't even TRY to heat it up.  Mom and I both ate a bread stick while I tried my darnedest to flag down my server, but the server was handling so many different tables. When she finally came to me to see what was going on, I pointed it out and she took it away, letting me know she was going to make it right.  Shortly, our mains came out and those were ok.  A few minutes later the Manager came over and apologized - he said that the appetizer was on him. At least this time the cheeze was crusted and piping hot, even if we didn't get to eat it because our food was with us now.   Over all, it wasn't a great experience, but they made it right.

So when I first visited back in 2013, I gave them a 2 stars. They've improved but not a lot.  I have found the non smoking area, but found that many of the machines there were in need of repair ( a whole bank of wheel of fortune machines was cordoned off with tape and half taken apart) and many were just not up to snuff - by sound not working or just having the blue screen of death.   Quite honestly, the area needs to be larger, as it was the most crowed area of the casino.  I did not appreciate the people who walked towards the bakery STILL SMOKING. That was wholly inconsiderate of the non-smokers.   Also noticed that they are now charging a $10 parking fee for every car.  Your first half hour is free, but "All day" which lets be honest, can be 2 hours or 12 hours, in my opinion the $10 parking rate is ... kind of steep, especially for those who are there frequently (Daily) or those who come only for a little bit of time. Let's also talk about the issue the parking meters have on getting into and out of the parking garage (South), there is inevitably a hold up because they're new, and it takes folks some time to get their ticket and get through the barrier.  I'm not sure I know what they're doing with this fee, but sure, it's a revenue generator. Yet I think it will limit people coming as well.

I had almost given up on this place. I've driven by it, I've stopped on days I thought it would be open - but it must have been closed for a holiday, For what ever reason, I've had a horrible time getting in to the Little Thai Cafe. Tonight, though, we saw that it was open, so after the last push of Christmas shopping, we decided TONIGHT's the NIGHT!  I'm glad we were able to get in, while the decor is not at all like the other Thai places in the area - no rich woods, not many statues, no familiar altar- it was comfortable. The place smelled AMAZING. We were seated almost immediately and offered drinks. I chose my favorite, Jasmine hot tea and it was -the absolute best- hot jasmine tea I've ever drank, it smelled of pikake blossom.   We ordered the fresh spring rolls and chicken satay for starters and they were both the epitome of fresh. The flavours of the herbs and the curry just jumped out on the tongue. Our mains were a Amazing Thai Chicken for me and the husbeast got a Thai Noodle soup with beef - thai hot.  (He always does that, and I always laugh because he ends up crying and sweating, it's SO very funny to watch. ;)   The flavours were both bright with garlic and cilantro, mine was light and crispy, the chicken was especially delicate. It is certainly a place that we will want to visit again.

After going to the Neiman's in San Fran, I was So hoping to find that they too carried a great selection in bras.  Sadly, they do not.  They have a fabulous collection of clothing, great designers and what have you, but their foundation selection is paltry and very slim. I am saddened by this. I mean, really! There were no bras over a DD cup even offered. THIS.. just is not acceptable.

Now here's a concept. Not really a buffet, but certainly it's an "all you can eat" style place.  When I first heard the idea, I was a bit turned off. Who wants to eat sushi that's been sitting out all day, but nope, it's all made to order.   You're sat down, given a menu, and the waitress comes by and takes your order like any other place, the only catch is, this is ONE PRICE for everything you order, but you better eat it all, especially if you plan on eating Sushi or sashimi - they'll charge you for the peices you don't eat.   I tried the Goyza- listed as pan fried, it came out Deep Fried - no pan involved, the General Tso's chicken (helped myself to the husband's plate) it was light and crispy and the sauce wasn't terribly hot. The steak and shrimp hibachi- The shrimp was well cooked, but the steak was over done. and the Green beans, SO GOOD!  The husband had the General Tso's chicken, twice! He liked it so much. And yes, it was really good. He had some sushi, not sure what kind, because I don't usually eat sushi. I did have a piece and it was good, not fishy at all, i really liked the spicy mayo.   And to conclude dessert, we shared a fried banana - yes, you read that right, a Fried Banana- a banana tempura battered and deep fried, then sliced and served with chocolate sauce and whipped cream, and a scoop of vanilla ice cream.  The banana was odd, but not bad. The ice cream was totes delicious!

Not your typical chili.  Don't expect beef & beans, don't expect your typical taste. This is more of a meat sauce than Chili con carne, but it's still flavourful, it still have a good texture, and you can add beans if you so choose.   I like the cinnamon taste to it, It's very Greek to me.   This isn't an everyday place to go to, it's a guilty pleasure, a once in a while kind of location to go to, and since my Father in Law is from Maysville, Indiana, we go here every so often. For me, it's either a chili dog or Dogs in a bowl. For the husbeast it's a burrito, and the father in law gets the Chili 5 ways.     Anyway you serve it, it all tastes like home.

I generally don't rate low, and had the service been better, I would have given this 4 stars, but when the waitress forgets to put your order in, yeah.. it's bad.  The hubs and I went in yesterday, as we were on the way to picking up friends to take them to the airport. We had a half an hour to kill and from his previous experience, this should be enough time to get our food and eat it.   We got there at 1pm on the dot, and while there were a few tables that were full, and the counter had 1 person at it, they were no where near slammed.  Our waitress came to us, told us she'd be with us in a moment and walked past to deliver drinks to another table.  When she did come back we placed our order for drinks and food and thus began our wait.  The counter filled up, and they were served. Food was coming out all over the place, and the minutes kept ticking by. Our waitress didn't come to check on us, when 10 minutes had passed by, I looked at my husband and he shrugged.  At 15 minutes i had almost finished the little oyster crackers in my bowl. When 20 minutes came, the waitress finally came by and checked on us, I asked her if we could just get our food to go.   She blinked a few times and went over to the line cooks and checked on our order, then came over to us. "I'm sorry, I didn't put your order in, I'm going to jump it ahead of everyone and you can eat it in if you like." I then explained what was going on, that we had to pick friends up to go to the airport and she nodded, our food was ready to go in 3 minutes and she apologized profusely.   Everything was bagged up and we were given our drinks to go as well, and sent on our way. Yes, we left her a nice tip too.  When we finally did get to eat it, at a lovely little beach near Tampa International, the food was good. I had a Chili 4 way with beans and the hubs had the Chili 5 way.   For me, I am not a fan of Cincinnati chili, but the flavour was good, you could taste the cinnamon, the beans were good, it had a richness to it. The pasta was tasty too, and there was the cheese! So much CHEESE!!!

I needed to grab food on the way home from a play date. This was just up the street and on the corner. Having never been to a Culvers, I wasn't sure what to expect, however, After a quick read through of the menu, I settled for a combo of their Bacon cheese burger, fries and a dr. Pepper.     When I pulled up to the window, I paid, was given my soda and a number, the kind of number that you'd put on your table to wait for someone to deliver it to me. I sat there. No one told me to pull forward. After a minute, the girl looked out the window and I asked. "So, did you WANT me to pull forward?" she nodded.  Great, be clear. that's the important part, I've never been here before.   I pulled around to the very first (last) parking spot and waited.. less than a full minute for the person to bring me out my sack of food.. I'm sorry to say that i was disgusted when they smiled because they had what you'd say was meth mouth.  It was disconcerting to say the least. But the fries were hot, if over cooked, and the burger was YUMMY.. I might come back.

The chocolate covered strawberries are what called my name, but I didn't end up getting them. Sadly the service was terribly slow and I didn't want to wait. They are always busy!  There's a reason for that though! Godiva chocolate is GOOD chocolate and people want that stuff!

The name is no longer Holiday inn, but rather Tampa Stadium Hotel. I showed up because a friend let me know about an Estate stale that was going on here.   The hotel itself is in need of some repair, and the little out building smelled of mold.  But the sale was decent, I was able to pick up some much needed things. And some wanted things.

I just got back from the new 701 Taphouse and over all had a pleasant experience. I would have given them 5 stars if it weren't for a few small errors with our order, other wise things were pretty damned good.  My party of three arrived at the prime dinner time on a Friday evening, only to see that everyone else had apparently had the same idea, "Try the new place in Tarpon out."  The option of seating was slim, but we were given a side by side place near the bar that suited us fairly well.    It took us a few minutes to order, due to the sheer volume of people, but when we did, our waiter, Dylan was great! He was quick and efficient and made sure that our order was taken and placed all at once.  Our food didn't take too long to arrive.   Our starter was the onion straws, they were crisp and delicious, served with a sauce that had really great flavour, but a LOT of spice. Almost too much for me, but the husbeast loved it.   Our mains, here's where we had a bit of trouble. I ordered the big mouth burger; no raw onion and sweet potato fried. It arrived with the wrong fried and the raw onion.  My husband ordered the Grouper sandwich, Fried, with fries. He got his baked. My mother ordered the Philly cheese steak with the broccoli and her's was absolutely perfect.   All in all, the small mistakes aside, the food was delicious, the service was quick and courteous and the beers - we had a Raspberry/Pear ale - were absolutely incredible.

After a comedy show fund raiser for a friend, I needed to grab a quick bite. But it's Monday, it's after 10 and it's Tampa. Very little is open this Late. What to do, what to do?  We high tailed it to IHOP and got our food on.  The waitress was surley, but the food was tasty. Other than the service being minimal, I really can't complain.

Due to the size of this hotel, the Old Hickory Grill is the only option for food on site, except for the bar, but they get their food from Old Hickory, too.   When I visited the first time, there was only one other couple in the place, so I was sat RIGHT in the middle of the eatery, the 2nd time, pretty much the same.. Always dead center of the room.  My first meal was the Meatball and a wedge salad, an actually reasonably priced meal for $16 total. Filling too since I wasn't sharing it with anyone.    The 2nd time I ate there We had 4 people in our group, so there were several things ordered, nothing complicated, but the Apps didn't come out ahead of time, not that it really mattered, but it's the little things you notice. Our glasses of water were allowed to go empty.   I eventually opted to go out side of the hotel by Lyft driver.

After a -really- long day, the husbeastie and I decided we'd stop for a treat.. We've waited to visit the Twistee Treat because there's -always- a long line.  The line today was not terrible, but it still existed in the drive thru.   Our order was simple, A dish of Strawberry and a medium vanilla dipped in chocolate cone.  We were both surprised at how large the servings were. Sadly the cone had alredy started to melt when they handed it out to me. *le sigh*   The ice cream was delicious, very smooth and creamy. I will certainly have it again, Diet permitting.

I really don't like to shop at WD. Their stores are generally .. dirty in appearance, but I stopped in because they were running this wicked sale on Keurig K Cups. How can you beat -any- variety of KCup for $5.99  but if you bought 4 or more packs, they came down to $4.99. YOU know I ended up buying 8 boxes. A nice variety of diferent flavours!    I won't give up my publix shopping, but if they run sales like that, I'll be back.

Brand new location. They are new and there are growing pains. I will re-evaluate them later, but for now, they're solid at a three. Why? 15 minutes in the drive through with only one car ahead of me.  I placed my order at 2:55 pm and it wasn't handed to me until 3:10, it really should not take that long.   However, the service was polite, the food was good, and the value was pretty ok. I enjoy Zaxby's and am happy to have one closer to Tarpon, than all the way out off of Waters or Hillsboro/Dale Mabry.

I go here one Wednesday a month. I meet with a chapter of friends and hang out with them. We're all of like minds and when we get here, we have the best service, We have a great time.  The food? It's ok. It's not stellar, but it is filling. Their omlettes are good, as long as you get the grits with real butter. :)

it's IHOP. It was late at night on GRAY Thursday/ Early Morning Black Friday. I really did expect it to be busier than it was. But when Mom and I walked in, there were 3 groups. One group of giggling teens, one group of 30 somethings and Us.   The service was amazingly fast, our waitress was very polite and courteous. She knew her menu in and out. Answered any question we had without reservation and delivered our food very quickly.   The food was Ok. Again, it's IHOP ,so it was nothing special, but it was tasty and inexpensive. It's chain food, a little better than fast food.

Stopped here for a lunch date with a friend.   Hadn't been to this particular VI in forever, but the food was all the same.  It wasn't a wednesday so no Free pie for us. *sad*  Our waitress was amazing and she was handling a huge section all alone. How she did it, I don't know, but she did and she did it with a smile. WAY TO GO.   We both ordered off the VIB menu,  I got the cheese omelet, bacon, 1/2 a waffle and coffee. My friend got the same but opted for the pancakes. OMG the food was tasty

I -wish- it was non smoking.  The moment you hit the door you can smell the smoke and the stuff they use to cover up the odor. It was rather.. strong.   Inside though, the light is phased out and the bells and whistles of the machines come up, There is an odd sense of euphoria that seems to weigh over you as you approach and you sit down at the slots.  I played the $0.02 machines (Really more like $0.40 -$0.80 machines based on the bets you have to play) and did fairly ok.   The one thing I can say that I do not like is the inconsideration of the staff when they stand RIGHT behind you, quite literally nearly touching you when they're helping someone out. This happened twice to me. It makes me very nervous and very .. uncomfortable.

Other than the service - which I found  touch lacking. Everything was AMAZING.   After watching a play at the Studio@620, the paramour and I walked down to Cask & Ale, and while they weren't busy, we had to actually place our orders at the bar vs any sort of table service, this was kind of irritating but other than that, what we found out was that we were VERY pleased with what we ordered.   I ordered the spring fling (I think that's what it was called) and the Paramour ordered a Maple old fashioned. To eat we ordered their bacon mac and cheese. When everything came to the table, EVERYTHING was absolutely amazing. My drink was light and fresh, the lover's was sweet and tasty. But the mac & cheese? The Mac & cheese was in-freaking-credible.  I have to say it's probably the best that I've ever had.   I will come back.

All Target stores seem to have an "entrance fee" for me of at least $50 these days.  What I mean by this is that when I enter one, I will not spend less than that before I leave.    This Target has recently renovated and put in a Starbucks!  The scent of coffee fills the air where once there was only go backs and customer service issues.

While checking for new places to eat, I stumbled across Caposey's by sheer accident. No, it's not new by any measure of the scale, heck it's been in New Port Richey for as long as I can remember, but as far as I can recall, I've NEVER been there.   By happy accident, the husbeast and I arrived on the coldest day of our Winter - so far- and we were able to be seated immediately, according to the owner, it had been PACKED but the lunch rush had just ended. Normally she had more seating because of her outside seats, but due to the chill, she couldn't in good consciousness offer that to us, and thankfully she was right. It was COLD.   We were seated right by the door, but that was fine, and our waitress came to get our drink orders, Both of us ordered coffee and ice water, and that was returned to us quickly. When she came back, we placed our order for our meals, I placed an order for the french toast combo based on the recommendations from other yelpers,  and the husbeast got the Chicago sandwich, with the soup of the day - stuffed pepper.   We didn't wait very long, my Scrambled eggs with 4 pcs of bacon and 2 generous slices of french bread dusted with cinnamon and powdered sugar and served with warmed syrup.  The husbeast's sandwich was brought out with his peppers and his soup and a side of au jus. Everything was REALLY tasty. The bacon was perfect, they offered me a side of salsa for my eggs which I happily took and the french toast was divine!  THe husbeast was a member of the clean plate club so I'm guessing he liked everything too!   Will we be back? You betcha! This is the Kind of place you want to become a regular at.

Located at the corner of Us 19 and Tarpon Ave/Main street, you'll find this Subway.  It's a nice, clean store with some of the most complicated parking.  Inside, the employees are friendly, the store is neat and the baking bread smells great.   We arrived at noonish on Friday afternoon. I was quite surprised that it wasn't overly busy, we were able to place our orders for a 6" BLT and a Foot long BMT very quickly. Since we were on our way over to the theme parks I'd thought we were getting them to go, but the husbeast decided to eat in store.   All in all a fine place to eat if you want a quick sandwich either in store or to go.

Came here on a date with my Darkness. We opted because it was nearby where we were staying.  It was close to closing when we walked in, so it was quiet and not at all heavily occupied.    We were seated and our waitress was over almost immediately.  We perused the menu and the chips and salsa were laid down. I have to admit I LOVED the sampler but the best part was the black bean dip, that was my ultimate favorite.   We weren't terribly hungry, so we ordered the Nacho Appetizer, the Guacamole and the steak tacos.  We'd share it. We had NO idea how big the Nachos were.. LAWDY! That was such a huge portion, we didn't finish it. The Guacamole was Delicious, especially topped with the roasted corn.  The only thing we were disappointed with was the steak taco, and that was because of the masa shell. Took that off and the flavor returned.   The service was perfect, the food was great and the company was better than anything else.  We will most certainly return.

For her birthday, Mom got a new mailbox. She needed to have numbers for the side and that's something she was lacking. Sure we could have painted them on the side, but neither one of our handwriting is the greatest.  So what we needed to do was go get those 3" tall sticky letters...  Home Depot had it all, our numbers were hidden on isle 13, buried down near the mail boxes and sundry. A pack of 26 numbers was less than $3.  SCORE!

First visit in, and my impression is pretty good.   I needed a new battery for my cartridges, the one I have wasn't giving me enough of a draw.  Their selection for that wasn't huge but they did have what I needed, even encouraged me to try it to see what the output was. Pretty cool.   They have a guy there who works, who's a glass blower, he's done many of the pipes there, his work is really nice.   They sell tobacco, they sell water pipes and they even say on the door that they sell drug (weed) related products, so if you're offended, don't go in.   Prices are competitive and reasonable.

This BBQ joint is located in the space of the very first eatery I ever ate in when I FIRST came to Florida way back in 1984. Back then it was a Chinese place called Eng's. Now it's a Barbecue place that holds it's own.   Mom and I had driven by this spot earlier in the week and I made a note to come back with my guys. They're open until 10 on Friday, 8 on Sunday, so there's some play in the hours. Check before coming.   It has an "old west Chuck wagon" look to the outside with some theming, a nice inside area and a large, covered outdoor seating area with fans because lawdy it gets hot here!   We got there around 7 on Sunday evening, perused the large menu board and noted the were out of Ribs & Wings per the printed sign on the door and register. That's ok, didn't want either. The Husbeastie chose their fried burrito thing, and my Beau and I both had their brisket platter with Mac & cheese and yellow potato salad  My guys both got unsweetened iced tea to drink and I got one of their special sodas, a bottled Frostie Blue Cream soda. Cream soda, only blue, for nostalgia sake. Our food didn't take too long to come out, and during that time the guys explored their sauce bar.   **Note to patrons** chose your pumped sauce carefully, there is a limit to one side cup of sauce per plate,  and an up charge of $0.50 for each additional one according to the sign.   They have their regular bottled sauces, my favorite is a Carolina mustard sauce and theirs was good! The brisket was thick and tender with a nice smoke and crust on it and the fat was so flavorful. The Mac& cheese was kinda disappointing to me, it tasted like Stouffer's, and that's meh. The potato salad was good.  The Husbeastie thought the burrito was "interesting" but did not finish it. So that says a lot about it. He would have liked th other choices.   While we would not normally travel from Tarpon to eat here, if I was visiting Mom in Port Richey FL, I would.

Typical Wendys.  I used the drive through on my way home, and grabbed their 4 for $4 with the Crispy BLT Chicken Sandwich, nuggets, fries and a drink.  I asked for the crispy chicken BLT to have no mayo. When I got my order, the fries were not hot - not cold, more of a kinda UH.. not tasty and there was Mayo on the chicken. Meh.

I've driven past the Golden Spirit Alpaca Ranch a lot, and I never knew it was an agribusiness. But when my friends returned home from Scotland and wanted to see if we could check in on them, I was game.   We bought our tickets on line for $30, 8:30 am tour on a Saturday morning.  The house is set back from the road amid old oaks. The inside is now a gift shop with a taxidermied Alpaca when you first walk in that is so wonderfully done.  Up stairs is a bathroom with a door that does not lock.    The tour guide (I didn't get her name) was very nice, knowledgable and friendly, she gave us the history of the ranch and info on how to tell a llama and an alpaca apart, as well as the different types they have on the ranch.   We then set out to feed the alpacas.  They each have different personalities and while most were skittish, several were sweet and loved their necks and bonnets pet.  We even got to see Simon up close, though he didn't want to eat from our hands.   It was a lovely way to spend the morning and support agribusiness in Florida.

The ultimate men's playground.   Even for men like my husband who's not truly Home repair inclined.
