We went, looking for some wire so I can make costume wings, and ended up getting a much needed 8' ladder, some window cling film, new sprinkler heads...   What should have been a quick and inexpensive trip, turned into a fun shopping trip that cost a small fortune - and one that the husbeastie actually ENJOYED!

The heart of the Tarpon Springs sponge docks holds Hellas' bakery and Restaurant. It's a great place to dine, to people watch and to grab a cup of coffee and a slab of bakalava. There really isn't anything better to do on a Saturday afternoon, than sit at one of the outside tables, sipping your java and licking honey off your finger tips. The food is fantastic! Opa!

I enjoy banking at FCU's. I find them safer and more friendly than your average National Bank.   GTE FCU is no exception.  This location is always friendly and quick with their service. I'm glad that they're close by!

Stopped at Newks as we needed to get to Target to pick up something I needed for my up coming trip.   We ordered their get two options, I ordered the salad and pizza, teh husbeastie got himself a sandwich and soup.  The pizza was tasty, but the portions were still too much for me.   They were woefully understaffed at my visit. People who were prepping food had to leave their job doing that to handle the register, or were cleaning the eatery after people had eaten. I saw Three people working, possilby four at 2 in the afternoon on a Saturday.

This is a Tampa Icon, and sadly it is soon to be closing it's doors forever!  A comprehensive costume house, Features offers you the ability to rent or buy costumes that run the gamut from your most basic tunic and fabric shoulder piece for your Christmas padgent as a wise man to the most ornate Lady in Waiting to a Queen.  Each costume is marked with a rental/purchase price and all are fair.   There is a HUGE makeup selection, wig and accessories are all available. The customer service is always helpful and friendly.   If you're looking for a good sale, right now absolutely EVERYTHING is 50% off while they liquidate their inventory. I suggest if you're looking for theatrical makeup, you go and invest in some quality Ben Nye product! Their lipsticks DO NOT MOVE, not even through eating fatty pork! I know, I tried it this weekend!

Stopped in to get myself my usual Carmel swirl latte... I was told that the Caramel was on recall. Funny, the next one down the road didn't have that issue. I dislike being lied to. REALLY dislike it. Consider that I won't stop at this particular location.

Not too crowded, the place was designed to look 1950's retro. I have to admit I liked the decor.   Coming to the theater on a Wednesday afternoon had it's perks. There were no kids, no crowds and no lines.  It was the perfect time to see a new release!    The movie itself - Insidious chapter 2 - was almost a private showing, with 2 other small groups of people, who all had the same idea, cluster in the center of the theater for the best seats.    I'd come here again if it were nearby!

Stopped in this new Starbucks for a coffee after visiting my niece. The starbucks is easy in, easy out, and the people that work there are just fine. I ordered a vanilla latte iced, it took about the time I placed the order until I got to the window to pay for my drink to be ready.

I usually attend the Holiday, Fl Location, but since my Beau lives more closely there, we meet here to work out after work.   This gym is well lit, with a large work out area filled with an assortment of machines.  There are areas for Abs, free weights and the 30 minute circuit as well as the Ropes area.   The Lifestyle machines for weights are well kept and everyone wipes them down between their usage.   Depending on your level of membership, you can tan or even get an aquassage (a massage table that uses controlled jets of massage to relax you) or use a massage chair.   It's a really nice facility.

I needed a drink, that's all. The drive through was efficient. I ordered a medium Pepsi. I waited in line for about a minute and forty seconds and paid money, got drink with a smile from a guy covered in tattoos.  All in all a fair exchange.
Friends of mine were hosting a small bazzar to give back to a community of cafts people in developing worlds.  The place allowed them to do so on their patio. That gets big marks from me.

I've driven past here many times but since I was with a friend and we were looking for things to do, I figured why not.   The place is bright and clean, but older. They aren't brand new and have been serving the area for a while, but that's ok. They serve the community with love.   My friend and I walked in and were seated immediately. We had a very friendly waitress, and our order for Coffee and water, as well as a Reuben and a Hamburger club were taken right away.   The food came out quickly as the place wasn't terribly busy at 1:45 pm, and what came out was HOT and delicious. My Hamburger club was delectable, It was tasty and fresh, the bacon really added a lot of flavor.    The only "complaint" I have is that there were too many fries.  How is that even possible? It was, but that's not a complaint, it's really a good thing. Keep up the good work, I'll be back.

Large WalMart, got what I needed and got out.  I dislike this walmart because on Thanksgiving 3 years ago, someone tried to use our "Credit Cards" while we were out of town. We don't know how they got our numbers, but they used them here.  Not the cleanest store.

Needed Gas on the way to my MOM's house before leaving for my trip to Alabama. The price was right at $1.69.  This racetrack is neat on the outside and neat on the inside with quick service and clean pumps.    If you can avoid the Pasco County yahoos who drive through here as a cut through to avoid the light at 19/fox hollow, you'll do just fine. Otherwise, someone might try to take your bumper off.

Wow! This place was fantastic! It was like walking into a Haunters paradise.   From the goat person mannequin out front to the myriad bones, costume bits and books that lay about here, I was in heaven.  What can I say, I like ODD.   If you're looking for pieces for your Gothic decor, this would be a place to look. Do you need bits and bobs for your Mad Scientist display? You'll find it here. Do you need a cage to keep your captive? (only for a scene, not for real, folks) It's out in the back porch.   Be sure to check out the Rope Snake, that's a piece of art.   I especially liked the Christmas Ornaments made with Sage and sea horses, those were being made by the Cashier and quite unique.   There were some "objectionable" pieces near the register, but they are historical. There is a market for them, and thus I must mention them, but not what they are, after all, they do have antiques here.   Also, there's a Gorgeous Jeep out front that was for sale, with AMAZING spider web doors on it. LAWDY! The Haunter in me wanted this for myself.   I'll be back, this is a place that I could see visiting frequently.

Stopped here for breakfast as i was headed out to Spring Hill to go get my Mom's car.    It was a sit anywhere kind of place, and the service was beyond good, it was by far some of the best I've ever had. The waitress was wonderful. I told her I hadn't had any sleep the night before, so she took the small coffee cup off the table and replaced it with a big mug.   She took my order, and within minutes it came out. The food was DELICIOUS. I ordered the ham and cheese omelette, with breakfast potatoes and an English Muffin. I think I age just about every scrap. Ok, so I was hungry.   When I asked for my check, my waitress asked if i needed a coffee to go, I said yes, and she came back with her largest cup to go.  She was AWESOMESAUCE.

New Location to open up in Late Feb, early March according to the people I spoke with today (January 14, 2017)   At first glance, you might be a little wary of this place, but don't let the mismatched tables and chairs scare you off, the food is good as is the service.  We showed up on a Saturday afternoon around 1pm. It wasn't terribly busy but tables were slim pickings inside.  However, We wee able to take a seat at the biggest table in the place - even though we were just 2.   The young waiter - I found out they're all culinary students from Tarpon High - gave us our menus and took our drink order, a few minutes later, he came back and we both placed our orders for the 3 ribs, 1/3 lb pulled pork and 2 sides I chose the Potato salad and the Macaroni & cheese, the husbeast also ordered the same dish, save he got coleslaw instead of the mac & cheese.   Our meals came out at different times, there was a slight mix up in the kitchen, according to the supervisor, but that's ok.   I will say their sauces are a bit sweeter than I like, I'm more of a tangy, savory girl vs sweet in my meat, so I had quite a bit left over.  The ribs though, they were meaty and juicy.  The husbeast ate all his pulled pork, but he had the same thing, he'd prefer more savory over sweet.   I thought that the Mac & cheese was good, but greasy. The Potato salad was excellent, and the garlic bread was ok.    We'll come back when the new place opens.

I drive past this place frequently and finally decided to stop in.  They have La Segunda Bread. That's some damn fine Cuban bread!   Feed the cows! For a small price, they will give you a helping of veggies they've cut up for the bovines out back and you and your littles can go feed them. They will thank you, your kids will thank you and you, might just enjoy the break from being on the computer.   Get some local produce, fruits and veggies, some herbs and meat too.  THey've got hives now, so Honey is there as well.   This is a nice agribusiness!

Located near the up and coming area of Trinity, FL this Goodwill is huge.   I came here specifically for old luggage. There were a few newer pieces but nothing like what I needed, and that's OK. They did have a varied and clean assortment of just about anything you could possibly nwantnor need.  They even had a new section. I've seen this at other locations. I'm not sure when this started, but it's kind of cool.

First Watch opened on Monday and it seems they've been busy since their doors were unlocked.   My Beau lives literally around the corner, so we've been waiting with fascination as we watched the eatery being built from the ground up, so when I stayed over the other night and headed home in the morning, I stopped in for breakfast.   I was seated immediately. Inside is rustic but lovely, with lots of wood and metal decor. Reminiscent of farmhouse, but not quite.  It smells good.   Their menu isn't one I was familiar with, lots of whole grain and other things, but I found what I was looking for and ordered their Old Fashioned breakfast with Eggs, bacon and a belgain waffle, and a pot of coffee.   The coffee was strong, and the table side creamer had seasonal PUMPKIN SPICE creamer in it as well as my prefered half/half.   Breakfast came out in 10 minutes or a little more, the place was busy, after all and it was good. The bacon was well done and crispy, the eggs were as I ordered and the waffle was light and airy, with a side of fruit compote to go on top. I didn't think to ask for maple syrup.   Would I eat here again? Yes.

An adorable little shop on Main street Safety Harbor that calls to you with it's uniqueness.   We came inside while at Third Friday in December 2018. The weather was rotten, but the store was nice and inviting and smelled divine.   Inside the store there is a selection of unique gift items, spa & resort clothing (With the attached price tag - soft pants that were $169 ?? Really?) Hand bags, jewelry and other accessories.  It was a very, perfectly lovely store that you could find that perfect gift for someone in.

My family and I stopped here to see the lights during their annual Christmas display.   We arrived too late for the 8:00pm display but on the center stage they were still entertaining with dancers from a local dance studio. Scenes from A NutCracker seemed to be going on. The kids did a great job. Some very promising young dancers out there!  The Shops is an open air Mall, with some fantastic anchor stores like Barnes & Noble, JcPenney and Nordstroms & Macys.  There are plenty of specialty shops too, so if you're looking for SOMETHING special, you're likely to find it there.   There's plenty of parking, lots of parking lots and even in front of shop parking too, so please be careful when crossing the street and make sure to look both ways.

I was hankering for some charred meat, and I wasn't going to be able to get to my favorite spot, so the husbeast and I compromised and decided to try some place new.  We opted for this quaint little hole in the wall in Safety Harbor.    In side, we were greeted with the scent of roasting pig, and a friendly enough, if quiet atmosphere. It being a late Sunday afternoon, the baseball game was on, but there was only one other soul in the place, a guy drinking wine at the bar.   We sat at a table, and our waiter brought us menus.  It only took a few minutes but we decided to choose a combo plate of spare ribs in a Memphis style rub and pulled pork.  Since we got the combo platter, we got a side, I chose potato salad and the husbeast got coleslaw, and we got a try.. or a small side salad, which I chose dill macaroni salad and the hubby chose potato salad.  When the food came to the table, we were offered three sauces: Spicy, Regular and Mango chutney.  The spicy, I couldn't even be bothered to try. The regular was smoky and just this side of sweet, and the Mango-chutney.. OMG, what a winner they have here! I just could not get enough.   The sides are fairly typical, the potato salad was tasty if leaning to the side of too much mustard.  The dill potato salad was absolutely delicious. The ribs were spectacular and the pulled pork was moist and flavourful.  Everything was tasty and filling. We probably could have ordered one plate and had it been enough for both of us.   Don't expect to find high style though. The seating is picnic benches, the decor is low country chic and the music is straight out of the radio, country tunes to keep your toes tapping. It's comfortable and quaint, with quality food and service.

Publix is my choice for grocery shopping bar none.   You have -everything- you need in one shop. Bakery, deli and one of the best produce selections around outside of a farmer's market.   The staff is always friendly, always asking if you need help and most importantly seem to genuinely like their jobs.

Review #3000  I gave my former CM a choice as to what would be my 3000 review and this is the business he chose (It was waiting in line to be reviewed).  I visited Haslam's Books in early March, before the big worry about Covid struck, so I had a chance to browse the stacks and enjoy the scent of old books and paper.  I'm a HUGE bibliophile!   I looked through the voluminous stacks of old books, through the new books and even the huge children's section because why not! Everything here is pretty special if you ask me.  Haslam's is an institution in St. Pete.  It is the epitome of a bookstore, complete with ghosts and cats.   While I was there, I caught myself in the Metaphysical section and found a book that predicted this whole current situation. I REALLY should have bought it. I'm kind of kicking myself now, I could have seen how everything turned out.   TL/DR  If you're a book fan, if you like reading or just LOVE the smell of books (Because that is a thing) Go to Haslam's (when quarantine is lifted) and give them some of your money, You'll thank me later. This place is the utter bomb!

The husbeast is going to Washington, to make a presentation. He has to look nice! Since he's a large man, buying clothing can be a challenge. It used to be that Men's sizes were easy, now they're leaning towards some vanity sizing as well.    We were able to find the pants and vest, 2 shirts and 2 ties he needed for a 2 night stay in the DC area, and yes, it wasn't cheap. For some reason clothing manufacturers believe that larger clothing needs to be higher priced. It really doesn't. Especially Tees and polos. There isn't that much more fabric.   The store was clean and well maintained, save for the bathroom which had a lack of a working towel dispenser or toilet paper holder, both were just rolls set on top of things. Stay classy Tampa.   The store is necessary. Yes, They carry Big and Tall sizes, Emphasize on the TALL. They seem to have a LOT in that category.

Solid eatery.   Dinner choice of my friend while she visited and we were dapperfied.    I'm sad they got rid of pork nachos, but the food is still good, still fresh. I ordered the cajun chicken nachos. The chips were fresh. There wasn't a lot of chicken on there but the other toppings were plentiful.  The drinks never stopped flowing .

The host hotel for the Legendary Haunt Tour. My room was up on the 5th floor, the quiet floor. It was for the most part.  The bed was comfortable, the shower was nice, but there were a few housekeeping issues, such as: a few stray hairs on the tile of the shower floor.  Odd things on the carpet that were missed by the vacuum - like food or something. Not sure what they were. One coffee mug was NOT clean, but had been "Wiped out and put back."

HUGE. This facility is one of the newer Goodwill stores recently built within the last 5 years. Their floor plans are open and they even have new merchandise, not everything is donated. During Halloween they have a full zone of new merchandise that has never been opened or used. I suspect it is previous years overstock from the "big halloween stores".    There is the usual merchandise as well, the stuff people have donated and it's kind of hard to find things by size since it all gets jumbled when things get put back. Sadly the plus sized stuff is almost non-existant, and hard to find.   Shoes at this particular location were amazing. I have a feeling a Drag queen off loaded her heels because I found MANY amazing pair of heels in size 13. They were So PHENOMENAL! I wished I could wear them, ALMOST, but then again I can't wear heels any more.

Since haunt season is in full swing I needed to get my scare on . I decided to bring my Niece and her best friend with me and we had a great time.   We arrived round 7:30 so at that time the only house open was the 3D house. They do it right, with a couple of good distortion areas.  Some of the actors were lacking passion but I'm sure on busy nights, they bring it.   The 2nd thing we did was the hayride. I'm generally not a fan of hay rides as I don't think they fit Florida as a theme. Especially when themed as Old West. Over all it was fun, though the zip liner scare actors weren't up and running. I missed that element, but I was very grateful that we weren't packed like sardines on the flatbed   The third house we did was one of the two interactive houses. I chose to wear the necklace that gave permission, while my niece and her friend chose not to.   I really didn't get bothered by the folks in this maze. A few of them touched my shoulders, but I wasn't pulled into any small rooms, no one tried to cut my hair or anything like that. Those are thing I saw happening.   The fourth maze we did was Black pool Prison. Again, I wore the interactive necklace. Here the actors were all engaged, all playful and very on point. I had a great time with these fellas. Especially #PrettyRicky.    The final maze was the out door path, lit by tiny lights and of course your camp light.  It is not my favorite path, but it wasn't a bad one. I don't like  it mostly because the ground is uneven and one of my party had a sprained ankle and the uneven terrain caused her some difficulty, that combined with the darkness made it hard to see, not scary.   Over all, a very strong showing from one of the newest Haunts to Tampa.

Chick-Fil-A, I love the food, but hate the politics.    That being said, when I want something that can be ALMOST healthy (The naked nuggets and the grilled chicken breast sandwich are the best on the menu) and those waffle cut fries, this is where I head to.   They are always friendly at the drive through and I've yet to get the wrong order unlike at other drive thru services.

Fellow Yelper, Stacy Z recommended that I stop in and check this place out. She wasn't wrong.   First thing out of the box is this store is clean, it smells good and they have a huge selection of merchandise.   They have all the tobacco for all your smoking needs. There's a respectable sized humidor with a good selection of varied sizes/style and quality of cigars.   They have all your assorted smoking parephenalia, from rolling papers to lighters to the occasional (or more frequent) water pipe.  Their selection is quite nice.   They also carry CDB and Kratom at this time.   Join the VIP program and get 10% off your purchases each time you come in  -simply mention it.

We were driving down to Sarasota and since we didn't nosh before we left the house we really needed to pick up something to eat on the way.  The idea was to grab food before we crossed the Skyway, so we stopped in Pinellas Park.   There were a lot of selections, but seeing I'd never had a Jersey Mike's sub We opted for it.  I perused their menu and saw they offered Cheese steaks and that made me happy. I chose the BIG Kahuna! So a cheese steak with extra onions, mushrooms and cheese. It was delicious, I got a size regular, with chips and a soda.   Everything was delicious, the service was quick and friendly.   I'd come back again.

After trying out a disappointing cupcakery in Orlando, I was happy to find this little shop in the strip mall near where I was eating lunch.  The cup cakes were fresh and lovely in her display case, each one marked with a Heart, noted a filled one. All cup cakes were $1.50 save for the canolli cup cake and that was $1.75 because it was real canolli filling and a bit more expensive to make.   The shop smells wonderful upon entering. It is a bit no frills but over all, that's fine. It's the product that you're looking for. The cup cakes are small, but GOOD. Moist cake, good icing, not too sweet but very tasty. The husbeast had the blueberry filled one, and he said it was amazing, I opted for the Salted Caramel cupcake and it was DELICIOUS.   I will come back when I'm by this way again. This is the kind of place that needs to be heard about. They're a little off the beaten path, but well worth the journey.

The crown jewel of Tarpon Springs.   If you're coming to the sponge docks, make time to visit Hellas too. The food and service are genuinely impeccable. The gyro's are flavourful, the souvlaki is tender and the flaming cheese is, well, in a word  HOT!  You can get all your Greek cuisine favorites like: Skordilla, stuffed grape leaves, Avgolemono soup, spanokipita,Horiatiki Salad, Greek Salad, a broiled octopus and even a whole fish that is then deboned at your table side.   And while you're there, don't forget to visit the bakery for even more absolutely decadent treats, the bakalava is some of the very best you'll ever eat.   OPA!

A town and country institution. I've driven by this place a thousand times and never once gone in.  So one Sunday morning, after staying at the Beau's home, we opted to go here for breakfast.  He apparently used to go here when he was a kid.   Opening the door was like stepping back in time. It is most certainly a greasy spoon, but that's fine.  The place hasn't been updated in 30 years but the food is good and the service is amazing.   We both had breakfast food, I ordered their skillet and ate nearly every bite of it except for the potatoes, the man ordered eggs, bacon and french toast.  Mind you, it said 3 pieces of french toast. Most places that'd get you three triangles, right? Nope here, it was 3 whole pieces of french toast and that stuff was amazing.   The coffee was kept full and hot.   Will I be back? You know I will.

If you are looking for something COMPLETELY different than your ordinary Halloween Experience, The Vault of Souls is it.   This is -not- your daughter's theme park experience, this is an Upscale experience that you won't find anywhere else. An elegant night of fear.  Don't come with the expectation of lines, of others body to body with you as you're herded though some chintzy maze, because that is not here.   What IS here?  It is a lush party in the arrival, where you will be given your number. While you wait, you can enjoy ghostly music and dancers as they float through the room. Have your aura cleansed and be read by the resident ghost hunter.  Enjoy hand passed appetizers or a drink from the bar as you wait for your time to come.   When your number is called, you will be brought down to the Vault, here you will be given a choice of which path to choose, and that choice is WHOLLY up to you. This is a nonlinear event. There is no ONE way to go. 12,000 sq feet of space for you to look through. You are encouraged to open drawers, read everything and touch.. just not the spirits, though they MAY touch you.   Each vignette is special, there are spirits in each room that will speak with you or not. They will interact with you in a different way. Your goal, to find the way out. They are just happy to see you.   It may take you as little as 20 minutes to get out, if you just briefly look things over, but it can take 90 if you thoroughly investigate and immerse yourself, and this is something you DO want to immerse yourself in. The scenes are beautiful, the Spirits are engaging and it is a world that has been masterfully crafted by a Storyteller who is beyond comparison.   When you do find your way out, you can wind down a bit in the Gin joint, enjoy the music and dancers that perform for you, and of course the delectable libations. Or have your tarot read as well as desserts and gelato up stairs in the reader's clearing.   A couple of things to note: the event starts at $100.00 per ticket, and goes up to $400.00 Each ticket tier has it's benefits, and it is reservation only.   HOWEVER Each ticket comes with valet parking - in downtown Tampa, this benefit alone is amazing.  There is a dress code, Please don't come dressed in sneaks and a Tee, Come dressed to be immersed in the event, as if you were going out to the theater, Just, Please Ladies, no High Heels. The vault contains uneven floors, so spike heels are not suggested. The event is for 18+ and up, no children will be allowed.   -YOU- will be wearing the masks and asked to not speak while in the vault, this is so that the spirits do not follow you home.   Come enjoy a night of paranormal fun, a night of elegant fear with a sinister twist. The spirits are expecting you.

The name caught my attention, more than the color of the building, so I knew I had to go check it out.    It makes me REALLY happy to see that this is a great thrift shop that supports the LGBTQ community and offers FREE HIV testing.   Inside is well laid out, lots of clothing to choose from, lots of bric-a-brac and furniture too.  They had a great selection! But honestly, what I liked best was their imagnative window displays. Their manequins were well done.

I've driven past this Marshall's a few times in the recent past, so I decided to pop in on the way home. The asiles were wide and clean, and yes, it's filled with Christmas merchandise already, but what a fabulous collection.   I found KT Tape - something I didn't think I'd find there. I found Hawaiian Black & red salt, a cool journal that will make a neat gift for a friend, and a few other things. Over all a productive trip shopping.

I'll admit, I've not stopped in here before because I wasn't sure how it would be. I was skeptical, because it looked sketchy to me.  But the beau was craving BBQ and we agreed, it sounded good and was pretty close to home.   We arrived around noon on Saturday, we sat and our waitress was there quickly. She was friendly and welcoming.  We took a few minutes to look over the menu and when we were ready, we placed our order - All of us getting the brisket and each of us choosing a different 2nd meat: I got the chicken quarter, there was pulled pork and sausage.  Sides ranged from Okra to cole slaw, Mac and cheese to green beans.   When we were done, there wasn't Anything left. We consumed it like locusts. It was THAT good. Everything had so much flavor, good texture and the sauces were really good too.    Now that we've tried it, we'll certainly come back. The guys didn't get to try the amberjack spread, and they're really wanting to.

I thought this would be like another eatery that I've been to. They're an AYCE type place with a menu, so you choose what you want, and the wait staff brings it to you. This includes items from a sushi menu, a hibachi menu and what have you. It is not a buffet.   The service was decent, and the food was edible, but it was not what I was expecting for the price.  My neice and I started with clear soup and goyza. The soup was good, but the Goyza was like the kind you get from the super market. All dried out and obviously had sat around for a bit.  The sauce was nil.  The ginger salad was pretty gross, the dressing was mayo based and I haven't had that before at any Asian eatery, it wasn't good at all.   Our mains, Chicken Hibachi and Steak hibachi were from completely different worlds.  My neice got hers as I finished my soup.  But my steak took a very long time to come out. When it did, it was cold and some of the beef tasted old. That taste of being a day from totally going bad.  That alone made sure I wont be coming back.   My niece has been here before and she absolutely LOVES the place, but said that this was a bad experience.

Largest of the Ollies I've been too. Product repeats in different sections of the store says there's too much space, not enough product for the location, but I suppose that means they can always get more stuff in.   We went before Phase 3 opened, so they were still social distancing, they were still wearing masks (And should be still). Their book section was HUGE and well spaced out. They have lots of coloring books and reader glasses, if you're the type who doesn't want the stigma of always wearing specs.   Toys were prevalent, we saw they had the teenage mutant ninja turtles, a whole set, but one of them was boxed wrong so it looked like you'd have gotten 2 Raphaels, but you would have actually gotten them all. A collectors gaffe. We didn't buy it.   The store was disorganize but fun.

I've been wanting to try Canes for some while and with friends in from out of town, this was our chance.   We're still in the world of Covid, so we socially distanced when we placed our orders: A raspberry tea, a frappe and an italian soda, 2 bacon, cheese and steak pies and a cuban sandwich.  We took a seat outside and waited for the order to come.   The drinks, all made to order, took a few moments to come out, but they were deliciously refreshing.  The food, because it's baked to order, came out about 20 minutes later.  The cuban sandwich was good, one of the top cuban's I've had in a long time.  The steak pie? I felt like I was back in Scotland (although these are Aussie style). They were DELICIOUS. My friend and I were over the moon with these fresh baked delacies.  They were so good, that I decided to bring home some for the family for dinner.   We even ordered Sausage rolls for breakfast the next day.  Totally not unhappy with anything we got, including the PRIDE rainbow socks from their General store portion.    The service was awesome, friendly and warm. I can certainly tell you that I'll be back!

I honestly thought this was a new shop, but according to the owner, Miss Merrie, they've been in that location for 13 years! Huh. You'd think I'd pay attention to my home town a bit more. *chuckles*  I wandered in because it reminded me of Rocket Fizz, only with a better more cohesive selection.  What I noticed is that they had more imported candies, like licorice from Norway (including these awesome licorice pipes) and a whole LOT of Gummy bears from Harribo. There were turkish taffies and all manner of different candies from all over the world.   If you're looking for something unique, stop in this quaint and clean shop. You won't be upset.  THe prices are fair and much less than the $12.99 a pound shops you find in the mall.
I stopped to fill my tank and get a slurpee. I sent my guy inside to get me the frozen concocotion, while I pumped the gas at a clean pump.

After my most recent doctor's visit,  I needed to come down stairs and get a mammogram.  My doctor said that I could just go in, and they'd take me with no wait.  She was right.   The ladies at intake were very friendly, they took my information, scanned my palm and I sat for a very short handful of minutes before I was taken behind the scenes and into a softly lit waiting room.   While in the waiting room, one of the techs asked me if I was cold, offered me blankets or coffee. I was fine, but the room does get a bit chilly so if you're prone to temperatures, bring a jacket.   When the room was available, I was taken in and asked to undress from the waist up, and put on one of the most comfortable, thick gowns.  I wanted to take it home.   The technician explained the process and we went to it.   A mammogram today is not like it was back in the early 90's. I remember those rooms being stark lighting, and the machines being cold.  The Technicians then didn't seem too concerned with how it felt for you to get your girls smashed between glass.  My tech this day was VERY kind, very friendly and took care to position me and my girls very carefully. There was no discomfort, there was no awkwardness, I was in and out in 10 minutes. Now we wait for the results.

Typical walgreens. Had to stop here on the way home from the shopping extravaganza with mom to pick up some pain reliever for the niece. Poor thing couldn't figure out the dosage on the kids ibuprophen all because "she wasn't 11" I did explain that being over 11 meant that was the "adult" dosage. *chuckles*  Clean and fair priced. I'd stop here again.

I can't tell you how many times I've driven by this place but I've never stopped in. Well that changed when the husbeastie and I decided we needed a change of pace.   We stopped in and were seated immediately.  It has a nice ambience for a former Burger King.  It was busy and there was one waitress for the entire dining room, so wait time was a bit high but not unacceptable.  We perused the menu which was quite extensive but settled on the Sushi Dinner and the Shrimp Tempura to get an idea of what they made the best.   Their miso soup and salad were delicious, I especially love the ginger dressing, it's so good.  Infact that's what I opt to have as the dipping sauce for my shrimp tempura.   The meals came out and the sushi dinner looked and smelled fresh. The husbeastie devoured it, so I assume it was good.  My meal had plump, juicy shrimp and several different veggies and a side of sushi rice.  I ate the proteins but split the veggies with the husbeastie.    All in all, a very pleasant experience.

I'd heard some good things about this place.  They had a Huge selection of goth and steam punk wear, and I was thoroughly impressed with what I saw.    That is until I saw on their re-sale rack an Alter-ego Corset.  Alter Ego Corsets are lovely pieces of leather that are now available under a different name.  What bothered me about this is that the price was tagged at $150.00. NOT a bad price for a leather, steel boned corset, until you realize that when they sold this item on Ebay (their main sales option back in the early 2000's) They sold for new between $100-130.   This left a really bad taste in my mouth.   Otherwise, they've got a great selection of clothing, in a variety of sizes, from a variety of manufacturers: Hellbunny, leg avenue, Tripp, the whole gamut is offered up. Go check them out, you won't be disappointed.
As of this writing, the new location on Main St in Tarpon has closed. It is sad to see this happen.

This review is for the gift shop. I've not yet had the pleasure for the actual tea room, but that will come soon.   My love and I had decided our "One tank trip" Would take us to Down Town NPR and all that it had to offer, which is surprisingly a lot compared to when I was a kid. The down town area has shifted and changed and now offers Up Scale and fun things to do.   We saw the White Heron, and I was familiar because I'm on their facebook, the gift shop was absolutely lovely, with lots of little Halloween things in the window, and so I just had to stop in. It smelled absolutely delightful with the tea and fresh baked Items.  As I looked at the Gift ware, I found a perfect shirt for a friend, an early Christmas present, and I found a Batty scarf for myself. Needless to say, I know where I'll come if I'm looking for something one of a kind.   I got to talk to the owner and found out they carry the delicious William and Dean chocolates (Get you some!) and that they're opening a new business, soon. It all sounds amazing.  The lady who owns this place has her fingers on the pulse of the city, she's been here since birth and is really proud of her place, and it's well deserved. She's got a great establishment.   I look forward to returning.

Came here to work on one or two of the artists as a massage therapist and then got some ink for myself. My artist was Matt.  Matt was extremely professional. We consulted over what I wanted, and he drew it up, presented it and got to work.   It'd been a decade since I've had any ink done so I was a little apprehensive, but I didn't have to be. He was gentle and made sure I knew exactly what he was doing, what needle he was using and everything else.   He made sure to check in with me, to see how I was handling things and when it was done, I was incredibly pleased. I now have the Lotus I wanted! It's delicate and the ink work is incredibly fine. I can't wait to get more ink soon!

My guy and I were looking for a place to eat last Saturday night, and we wound up in Dunedin. We were going to do Mexican, but our usual spot seemed too crowded in the age of Covid, so we saw the D-Town and stopped in.   It's very nicely decorated, the staff is really friendly and they do adhere to social distancing and masks.   We placed an order for an appetizer (rare for us) of stuffed potato skins, thinking they be like the yukon gold potatoes, small. Boy howdy we were wrong. These were idaho russets, large and stuffed with bacon, cheese & chives. They were delicious.   For our mains, my guy got the steak special and I ordered wings. The steak was nicely cooked, with a good seat to it. It came with a salad and a baked potato.   The parmesan garlic wings were a savory delight. I wish we'd had room for dessert, but alas, a cream puff was not to be.   We'll be visiting again.

Nice looking gift shop in the new condos on Main Street.  Absolutely adorable shop with gifts for every age range.   I LOVED the Turtle pillows and mermaid items which were right out in the front of the store.    There was a large selection of toys and childs clothing as well. And while I was there, I found out it has a new owner too! Apparently a woman came in to buy something and wound up buying the store.   In any case, the store is well kept and the people are friendly. Stop in and see if there's something you want.

McDonalds that butts up against Fivay High School, it's in nice condition, the store is clean and the double drive thrus are extremely efficient and friendly.   I placed a special order (Fish Fillet without cheese, extra tarter) med fry & med coke, and was pleased that the order was right, the fries were hot and my coke was upsized (Thanks!)  Service was quick and they even gave me a shout out on Twitter when I checked in.   Will be back when I'm in the Hudson area.

This joanne's is located in NPR, and is usually a disorganized mess. They're always getting ready for one holiday while the other one is in the middle of a clearance or still in full swing. Honestly i've seen Halloween, Thanksgiving, Christmas and Valentines day up all together. Talk about a mish mosh.   But when you come in looking for fabric or jewelry findings, they have it. They'll ahve what you need and it's easy to locate. Their associates are easy to deal with and friendly too.

This is actually for the "old Fashioned Christmas"  I had wanted to go shopping in Dunedin, but when I arrived I noticed that there were cars EVERYWHERE. Oh NO.. Something was going on. When we started walking down the street.. well what do you know, there's a parade going on! I stood there and watched a good 50 floats/groups going by, and that was just up to #73, with more to come.    It was staring to get cold so I wandered away, but I can tell you that they were planing on having an excellent event with snow and vendors, it looked like it was going to be a heck of a time.

With the Covid-19 outbreak many stores have decreased their hours, so I was stuck going here instead of Publix.  I was NOT disappointed.   I sent my boyfriend in to the store to pick up a few essentials, and he said the store was fairly well stocked, even a half hour before closing. That the fruits and vegetables appeared fresh and that the store staff was friendly, right up until 5 minutes before closing when they stationed an employee at the door to dissuade any further people from coming in.   We were able to get the milk, bread and other sundry items we came for at cheaper than I expected.  If I had to,I'd certainly shop there again.

A quaint, little park near the street car line's last stop that serves as a place to hold the Saturday market, Free Pt, and a few other things.   Lovely chickens roam through the area at their will and there is often parking available around the area if one is inclined to make their way to the park.
My mom's 2nd home, or so it feels like.   I can't tell you how often I've brought a sewing machine here to be repaired or just serviced. They're always nice folks.

Had a lovely lunch here with my friend Amy.   We had not seen each other in some while and were looking for a place that would allow her and I to both eat happily. She's a pescatarian and I'm an omnivore.   Poblano's menu was very flexible and customizable with what proteins you wanted. The service was good, friendly and prompt. Our glasses never went empty.    The Portion sizes were quite large as both of us had take home boxes. We were quite happy and both would recommend the place to others.

I popped into Clothes Mentor after getting a massage just down the way. I've been in once before, but it'd been a while so I thought I'd check to see what was going on now.   They carry all sizes, including Plus, but their selection for anything over a large isn't huge. I looked through the racks and shrugged, I found a few things but it wasn't until I found the back wall that I was happy.   On the back wall they had Lularoe items. Many of them were Unworn and new. I helped myself to 2 pair of new leggings at $10 a pair (vs $25 new) and a necklace which was marked $0.99 but came up $6.95, they corrected it, but that was still annoying.   Over all, I'd come here again, but I wasn't terribly impressed.

My 1000th Review!  I waited too long to eat. I'd been sitting in my stylist's chair and my tummy was getting angry with me, so that when I finally was able to get food I was grumbly and moody. I opted to head to the international mall and decided to try The Earl.   I'm sad they don't have combos, so everything turns out to be really expensive, but the food is very good. I had a bowl of soup and a buffalo chicken wrap, of which I ended up only eating half - see if there was a combo that allowed 1/2 a sandwich and a cup of soup, it would have been better and I wouldn't have wasted money!  Though I did end up getting a better deal on a drink, since they were out of small cups, they had to give me the big cup for the price of a small.   Service was quick, the food was good, I'd give them another chance.

Tonight, after a hideous day, I just needed some comfort food, and Orchid's was on the menu.  The maternal unit, the husbeast and myself headed the handful of blocks from Mom's place to their store front, only to find them packed!  We only waited a little bit of time as they cleaned up a table and sat us.  Our waitress was amazing, she took our order, looking rather shocked when my husband ordered his meal Thai Hot.  Seriously, he means it. He wants to cry and sweat when he eats his soup. Me, i can't handle it... but I digress, she put the order in and brought out the pepper tray too.   I ordered the Chicken Sateh, Mom ordered the Sampler platter and the Husbeast ordered the Noodle soup with beef and meatballs, we had an order of fried rice for the table. Everything was absolutely fresh and delicious. The food came out quick and hot and nothing was left on our plates in the end.  If you like Thai desserts, I suggest you try the Mango Sticky Rice. It's Delicious!

We dropped by after attending a Spooky themed night at the Cuban club.  The decor is the perfect cross between Addams Family Lush and Goth Library plush. It's perfect.    My guy helped himself the the Kavatender's knowledge and ended up with a drink that made him happy and mellow and kept him awake all night long. That was some really good stuff there.

Stopped because gas was 2.88 for regular unleaded, 11 cents cheaper than surrounding locations.   Pumps were clean, but the trash cans needed emptying. There were windshield buckets missing and although they request that you use towels to dispense your gas, none were provided and no hand sanitizer.

I'm a massage therapist. So what do I do when I need a rub down and can't do a trade with a friend? I utilize my membership at Massage Envy at the Fountains.   In truth, I've been coming here since just before I got my license. They have some damn fine therapists that work there! My favorites are Tony, Karen and Diane. Each of these therapists are going to listen to what you need, do what they know your body needs and leave you feeling rejuvinated.  There are some draw backs, though: It's a membership place. Some people don't like that.  They up charge $10 for Bio-Freeze (WHY? it's $16 a bottle retail), $10 for Aroma therapy (most oils, even special blended oils don't cost that much) and $16 for a foot scrub... yeah.   There are some pluses: They're open from 9 am to 9 pm, they have a lot of locations and a lot of different therapists to suit your needs, weather you like it gentle or are like me and need a little tough love.    Either way, I'll be back at least once a month, because I work hard, and I deserve some touch therapy. SO DO YOU!

Totally my go to when I don't have anything in the house or am feeling lazy.  It's SO easy to place an order on line, and in a few minutes, I get a hot, fresh and tasty pizza delivered to my door.   Are there hiccups? Occasionally, but they have Pizza insurance. So if there's a problem you just call and they fix the problem.

We'd been in Tampa proper and needed to eat. Out of Nostalgia, because ABC Pizza's were once everywhere, we stopped in. It was like stepping back in time. We loved it.   We were seated and our waitress was wonderfully fast. We ordered a large Cheese pie and a salad, and I swear our food was out in record time.  The cheese pie was perfect! I wish the one by me was still an ABC at times.

Daniel from Fluent in NPR recommended this and another dispensary as his favorites.  Since I'd been down south, and this was on the way home I opted to make the stop.   A former bank, this Dispensary has a drive through, and a lovely, lofty interior with polished concrete floors. When you arrive, you give them your ID and sit in the waiting area until you're called back.    Once in the back, they have their product on display and nice screens that tell you what they have in stock. At the time of my visit, I was looking for vape cartridges, and they had some pretty good things in stock. The bud tender Tyler (I think, His handwriting of his name was difficult for me to read)was really helpful. He explained how to use concentrates and was happy to answer any questions I asked.   I really enjoyed the location, their product is pretty good. I did buy some green and the bud I got "99 problems" and that's pretty good stuff. I'll make the drive here on occasion.

Stopped in on a Sunday afternoon, the place was hopping. Got myself a berry smoothy and the beau got himself one with kale and ginger.  It took a few minutes, cost us a little over $20 but we were both happy with what we got .   We would totally come back again.

I must have driven by this place daily for the last 7 years. Tonight, after the gym the beau and I decided that we should grab some grub and I decided that Angelo's pizza would be where we'd get our food.   Walking in, it wasn't busy, but it sure smelled delicious. The eatery was sporting 3 different families eating, including the kids of one of the cooks, and boy!They were cute.   We were able to sit where we wanted, and our waitress was there in a flash to take our drink orders.  I ran to the rest room (It was clean and even had a few current ladies magazines.)while the beau placed our order for a Mozzarella Caprese salad, and Chicken Parmagana, with a salad.   The Caprese was delightful, the Chicken Parmigana was great! The order was large enough to split between the two of us, with it's side of linguini. We left happily full.
if you're a fan of the TV program, then you'll love the outlet. Much of what you see ends up on the outlet floor. When people return items they come back here, and you get them for a great price.

I have driven past this place a million times in the past, but today I had the chance to stop.  We'd been visiting the local alpaca ranch just around the corner so this was a logical stop for lunch.   Inside it's dark but clean, the folks behind the counter are friendly, the sandwiches are made to order, and the cubans are hot pressed, and delicious.  I had myself a medium cuban with a small side of Greek potato salad and a ginger ale.  The total was $10.85. The meal was substantial, but I was not hungry when I left.   The tables are outside, under a covered porch with fans to cool you off.  If you sit too close to the building you do risk catching smoke from the workers when they step out to catch a smoke break, but it's not terribad.   Over all, I'm sad I waited so long to try this place. I'll be back for sure.

Big Lots is either hit or miss.   This store has undergone a recent renovation and is much easier to sort though now. It tends to be cleaner than a lot of the other big lots locations and that's a huge plus in my book.  I like that they're not always busy, so you don't have to fight with other people over things you might want to buy.

This store is large, neat and quite well stocked, but they ddin't have what I was looking for. I an an owner of the Pixel XL and was looking for a specific case. Sadly they didn't have what I was looking for in stock.  The person helping us did check to see if it was locally available, but sadly it was not. I'll just have to order on line.

My first time back since visiting with the Yelp group back in October, and I'm glad I came! I had lunch with a friend of mine today and I just couldn't wait to try their Salad and pasta again.   The salad I remembered had lovely greens, some walnuts, apples and cranberries, what I ended up getting had huge hunks of apples, big pieces of bleu cheese, fresh tomatoes, bell pepper and chicken all through it. It was DELICIOUS!  It came with bread and I ordered a side of the pasta salad too, I wasn't able to finish it though. S'ok, I'll eat it as a snack later. :)   My friend ordered a turkey and cheese sandwich, she said it was pretty amazing. Her coleslaw was damned good.  The one thing I didn't get, because I didn't Yelp before I got there, was my free coffee. It's ok, I'll get it next time.   The place is clean, neat and orderly, you can bet I'll become a regular!

Late at night, Before leaving for a trip and I'm hungry. What am I going to do? I'm going to go to one of the fast food outlets near by.  This particular KFC is a KFC/Taco Bell.  They were 25 minutes to closing, and the service was just fine. I was happy with how quickly everything came through.

The pharmacy staff is always very efficient. I'm quite amused/excited by the selection that this particular CVS has collected in the Family planning/prevention area. They've got a better selection of Condoms & lubes than most adult stores. I'm truly impressed.

I always like what Yummy House puts out. And this location is no different.  A few of the friends got together for an Unofficial event and met here on a Weeknight, at 7:00 pm there was NO parking, and the line, quite literally, was out the door.   Thankfully, one of us arrived early and procured a table! Once we started filing in, the conversation flowed and the catching up began and a lot of that had to do with the food.  We all are familiar with the food, so we ordered our favorite dishes and shared amongst ourselves.  I personally love the Salt & Pepper Calamari, I've never been disappointed with it. Their Hong Kong Style Won Ton soup was absolutely magnificent with the baby bok choy as the garnish.  Other entree's I tried were the Salt & Pepper tofu - which was very tasty as well.   The service, while not 5 star due to how busy they were, was good, attentive when the other large tables weren't calling him away.   I would certainly come back to this location.

I was not impressed. It really was nothing more than a bit more fancy Moe's. All the plain metal and wood. The menu didn't interest me in the slightest. The biggest thing it has going for it is that it's 50' from the husband's work place. So that makes it a plus in my book. It's not bad at all, don't get me wrong, it's just not my idea of a good time.

I just needed an diet coke after spending an hour shopping. The drive through took entirely too long to purchase just this item. Normally I get the #17, but this was just for a large diet. *shrug* At least they got the order right.

I've lived all my life in Tampa. This is the first time i've been to the Gasparilla Festival of the Arts. I was impressed.  Held down at the Curtis Hixon park, along the water front and just at the Tampa Museum as well as the new Glasier Children's Museum, the festival is filled with new as sell as established artists from all over, as well as the local area.   There was even a kids area where the kids could make an art project and purchase their own art project! A great way to keep the kids involved.    It was a great way to spend the afternoon since the weather was absolutely wonderful. A bit warm, but the grounds were perfect. Nothing like watching the UT rowers out on the canal as you stroll and look at the artistic offerings.

Came here for the husbeast's birthday. They have the hot wing challenge, and if there's one thing the Husbeast likes,it's HOT food. He'll do Thai, but it has to be -real- Thai hot.   Anyway, he ordered the wing challenge, and ate them with no problem. He even said they weren't terribly hot. He didn't need any milk or anything sweet to kill the heat as they went down. The rest of us ordered different things. I ordered the Garlic Parm wings, supposedly with a bit of heat, but they were tasty. We had a plethora of food and the service was decent.   Over all I'd eat here again, but I could do without all the sports stuff ephemera.

First things first. Have you looked at the building? At first glance, I see a prison. The central tower, with other small towers, and the complex. It's kind of scary.  Other than that, there's ample parking, there's even a bus loading and unloading area... I guess they're expecting tours.   It has all the stores you expect and places for more to come in.  I noticed a plethora of clothing, shoes and luggage stores. Frankly only one or two seemed to catch my eyes. I wasn't overly impressed with what's going on.

At the end of Main street, take a right and you'll find the Safety harbor Peir, it's right near the Spa and Resort. it's actually a lovely little spot to sit and reflect, as you watch the waves lap at the shore line.    They throw some lovely festivals down along the edge, and occasionally you'll get to hear live music or even catch some of the native wild life as it swims in the water.  It's a little piece of Florida you don't want to miss.

Books, books & more books!  I love books. I don't want a kindle, I don't want a nook. I want to turn my pages, I want to get lost in them.  B&N is the last of the large, comfortable book stores to remain. It's clean, well lit and has a large selection to choose from.   Today, there was a great selection of gadetry to choose from, a lovely selection of gifts to browse, and even some wonderful bargains on some recent releases! $100 bucks later and I've filled a Christmas list, gotten a new series to read and bought 2 books for under privlidged kids.

I LOVE make up. I love that the Mall at Gulfview has an Ulta store, and it's one of my favorite playgrounds.   I will say that the service can be spotty. Like today. When I walked in 2 ladies, one of them was the General Manager were holding a conversation that was far too busy to give up in lieu of customers coming into the store.  After about 5 minutes they walked over to see if they could be any help.   It's service like this that makes stores like Ulta and sephora seem unapproachable, but if you know what you're looking for, you'll find it.  What I was truly happy about was that I found that Urban Decay lipsticks were 50% off due to them being discontinued for re-boxing. New packaging means a great bargain. So instead of being $22, I got 4 gorgeous lippies for $11 each. I also picked up 3 new Nyx lipsticks too.   Yeah, makeup shopping is hard on my pocketbook. WOE is ME.

While looking for a brunch to attend, I came across this one. It is by the same company that owns Island Way in Clearwater, so I didn't think it could be too bad. It runs from 10-2 on Sundays and is $19.90, which is an easy price to swallow.  When we arrived, what used to be a Melting Pot is now a very open seating place, comfortable with plenty of tables. The food was laid out on different tables, and while the selections were decent, they were kind of picked over by the time we got there at 1pm. There were an assortment of breakfast foods: Eggs, bacon, sausage, pancakes, blintzes and even hand made omelettes. There were stir fried items, beef and chicken and there were oysters and shrimp on ice.   The buffet also includes 2 drinks in the price, either a Mimosa, screwdriver or a do it yourself bloodymary. It's a pretty good deal.

After a busy Sunday of giving massages, I decided I wanted to meet with a friend for some Girl Time.  Since she's starting down the road of veganism and Me, I'm a meat eater, we decided that Thai food was the best middle ground.   And since I was working in Dunedin and she was coming from St. Pete, she spun the urban spoon and this is where it landed.   The outside of the place is fine, looking a little brash with it's neon lights, but inside, there is a soft glow of serenity.  The floors were all neat and clean and the table set up, while tight was comfortable.  We were sat in the first alcove and waited for our waiter.    Here is where things took a not so pleasant turn, when he came to the table, it was from the outside, as if he was called in from his smoke break, and took our orders; for Jasmine tea and Thai Coffee with ice water.  It was returned quickly enough but he forgot the ice water.  Any question we asked was answered almost snappishly, and almost unintelligibly.   Our orders were placed, mine is what I always order, Chicken Sateh & Combo fried rice, she placed an order for curry puffs and some vegetable dish.  As if to prove that he wasn't listening, he had to come back out and get my order a second time. This did not fill me with confidence.  And when our starters came out, I did not get the chicken sateh, but rather, beef.  I did not complain, but ate it. I'd never had beef sateh, and it was OK, but it was NOT chicken, which is by far a more lovely dish.   When our mains were served, I noticed that my combo fried rice was served, not with the traditional beef, chicken and pork, but with scungili and shrimp. Apparently the seafood that he'd told her would be in her vegi dish, wound up in my rice. It was terribly confusing.  I don't eat seafood, but I ate around it, because I didn't clarify what was in their fried rice, this was on me.   Now, their food is fresh, it is tasty and it comes out fast. My only fault with this place was our waiter's inattentive attitude and the fact that he really didn't pay attention to what he was doing. It was clear he would have been any other place than serving us at our table, and it showed.   The high point of our meal? The Thai custard and sticky rice with coconut sauce, it truly was delicious and we thanked him for recommending it to us to try. It brought both of us back to Hawaii.

Came to Miller's Ale house to wish a friend off to better pastures. We've been here once and had a good time. So I am glad that we got to go here again.  We hung out in the Bar area, sipping on Martini's and passing stories back and forth.   The service was good, but for some reason my $2.00 vodka martini was actually $5. *shrug* not that it's terrible, but I didn't quite understand the explanation.

Tax Day. Yep, I had to mail my amended return out. Nope, I had already filed, but the husband had gotten something ELSE in the mail and we had to get it sent off because, well.. the IRS needed MORE money.   This is the closest location to the husband's work place, and though it's the hardest post office to ever get into, has the least parking spaces I've ever encountered, the employees actually seemed to give a damn. In fact, when I came in, 2 patrons were arguing. One of the employees told them to shut it. I'm glad she did. No one has time for that crap.   They worked through a line of 15 people in 15 minutes or less. Efficient and friendly? You all get my vote!

I was not happy with this visit to Dunkin.  I was on my way to the Airport when the husbeast and I stopped.   I get it, they were busy, but they messed EVERYTHING up. I ordered a combo, and while I got a combo, it wasn't the one I wanted. I wanted a Bacon/egg/cheese on bagel, but I got a sausage/egg/cheese on a croissant. Not that it wasn't tasty, but if I'd wanted that, I would have ordered it.  The combo comes with hash rounds, and I can never eat them, because frankly they never feel/taste cooked through.  And my coffee.. *sigh*  No, just no. I'm not sure if it's because the ratio of their caramel to coffee was off or something else was, but it just wasn't satisfying.   They missed my husband's order for a large coffee but at LEAST they got his order for his sandwich right.  He didn't want to waste any more time there, else we would have said something to the window.

I was really impressed!  I went here with a friend to celebrate my new employment status, and on her urging, we went here.  We ordered the Farmer's pizza, with light sauce on the whole grain crust.  What we got was a delicious pie, heavy on flavour, light on the red.  It was filling, and we even had enough to take home.   Will certainly come back!

In dire need of food, and no where else to turn before my Chiro visit, I stopped into KFC and got myself one of their $5 boxes. For $5 I got 3 chicken strips, a Mashed potatoes and gravy, a cookie and a drink. That's a pretty decent deal, if you ask me.  Unfortunately I wasn't terribly hungry, ate 1 of the strips, a few spoonfuls of the taters and threw the rest of it away.

Stopped at the Gwazi Park for the final night of Kenetix.  Let me just say that when Busch Gardens puts on a party, they REALLY put a party on.  There was a packed audience, there were top 40 songs, singing, dancing and a little girl balancing on a man's forehead -HOLY CRAP!    The singers were amazing, FRANK has an awesome, soulful voice! I liked this year's version better than last, but each year just keeps improving.  Thanks for the wonderful Summer Night's Programing, Busch Gardens! Keep up the good work!

I haven't been here in months, but seeing that I was in Ybor during the day, I needed to stop in and see what they were offering.    Though today I only got an espresso, I remember their delicious crepes. My favorite is the Tampa with Nutella and strawberries with real whipped cream. It is So absolutely delightful on the lips.  Their savory crepes are delightful as well. I can't remember the ones I've eaten, but I have to admit, that they're all damned tasty.

Stopped here to join my friends for a cast reunion from our last year Haunt. It was nice to play shuffle board with them as well as drink an apple flavoured lambic and enjoy a bun-less burger with both tomatoes and pickles. Sadly they were out of the wings.   Our service was fine, our waitress was checking on us frequently.  all in all a damn fine visit.

I didn't come to this location for the jazz house format. I came here because it was the host of a Burlesque show I wanted to see.  Due to the rain earlier in the day, we were a little worried about what it was going to be like, but it turned out to be a beautiful, if humid night.   The stage was well placed and the burlesque performers (Especially Tila Topaz) were amazing. It was the first time I got to share a dance with my special guy. Something about that I just won't ever forget.

Decided to go here today with a friend. Now I'm kind of sorry we did.  The food was OK. At least they got our -special- orders right.  So why the 2 stars?  Our waiter was S-L-O-W.  And I don't mean slow.. I mean, he took our beverage order and then disappeared for the next 10 minutes.  He didn't come back to take our order for a long while. It was quite frustrating. Here we were, ready to order, but we had to wait... and wait.. and wait.   When we did order, the food came out fast enough, and it was just how we ordered it, but the service just took away from everything.

Out of season Haunt opened for Hauntcon,  Thank you SO much for opening your doors on a Chilly January Evening.  Loved the concept of your event, pretty stark for the bible belt! (in other words KUDOS!  The distortion room- that was by far one of the best rooms, especially when you add the double flash strobe, and the varied terrain of the floors. Man, I left that room feeling ill, which, is exactly what we wanted!  The black out room! Great idea. Most people took too long, thankfully I've been through one of these before, and knew the trick.   Your actors were fun, I loved their interaction with their fellow haunters (Us), not sure they'd do that with everyone else, but HELL we all had a blast.  The hemi-peni'd satan at the front was a fun detail too.  I look forward to seeing what more you add to this in the future.

Came mid week with a dear friend who is working down at the base.  Parking is a nightmare, but the atmosphere is amazing inside.  The soaring ceilings, the art on the walls and just about everything else will make you glad you stopped in.   Our service was awesome, we were sat at the inside wall, and we couldn't have been happier. I ordered the meat loaf, and my friend ordered a crab dish, both were perfection, and the drinks we had, I had a pineapple beer and she had wine, were both excellent.  This is a place that is very Hip, very trendy.

Drive thru ATM... this was the 2nd location I visited this evening, because the first was down. Apparently it was sytstem wide, because YEP.. the lady before me had the same issue as the one in Palm Harbor. You could enter your card, key in your pin and even enter what you wanted to do. If you wanted to get cash out though.... You weren't getting it. So Sorry.. The ATM was timing out on you.
Quick, efficient and tasty. This was just what I wanted after my weigh in.  I was able to sub out the fries for extra veggies and get my non-sweet tea.  Life is good when lunch is under $10.

Dillards was always my go to when I was heavier, because they always had a great selection in clothing. What I never knew was what they carried in bras!  I am HAPPy to report that they carry La Mysterie! this brand is fantastic for us larger than DD cup girls. They are comfortable, supportive and yes, while expensive, they're not going to break the bank.   The girls who work the registers are friendly, but not overbearing.

I stopped in to get my eyebrows waxed. Granted the experience was good from the beginning until mid way through the waxing, when my waxing professional stated she'd been sick not but the day before "REALLY SICK" and that her 3 year old daughter was still ill. Here she was, in my face, sniffling every few seconds and doing my brows.  This isn't acceptable. I was going to be traveling in a few days - not to mention it was just before the final weekend of the Halloween Season for the Vault, and I am immuno compromized, and she was not wearing a mask.  I left, and looked at the makeup she'd done on my brows, without my glasses it seemed ok. Once my glasses were on, I had two big red commas on my face. Again, not so good. I do a better job on my own.  I'm glad I didn't pay for the service, because they have the first service free offering. I can't say I'll be back.

Earlier this year, the husbeast hurt his low back. He was not healing quickly and it was starting to hurt to move.  I drove him to the Florida Hospital ER in Palm Harbor.   It's a great looking place, the waiting room is neat and clean, The intake went quickly and smoothly and once we were brought back into the room the Nurse saw us quickly. He asked what was going on and the husbeast explained his pain.   It didn't take too long to get diagnosed with his issue, be given some exercises and some pain relievers.  He's since seen our PCP and is working on taking care of it.

I'll state up front, I don't agree with Chick-fil-a's poitics. That being said, I love their waffle fries.  It's been well over three years since I've eaten at one, and with no lunch, I pulled in there on Wednesday.   The drive through was quick, efficient and when I placed my order, it always creeps me a bit out when the people say it was "My pleasure to serve you." it sounds wrong for fast food.   i'm only giving three stars because the people inside the drive through window were futzing around with the whipped cream canister, playing around infront of customers and in general flirting with each other. There's a time and place, work really isn't it. *shrug*   Foood was tasty, wish they'd had the dressing I wanted (Ceaser) but I got stuck with ranch.

What do you do when you've not seen your friends in ages, and you're careful about what you eat.. You go to a deli.   My friends and I meandered through I-Mall to TooJays to enjoy a lovely dinner together, two of us opting for salads and the other for one of the sandwiches offered. The service was very good, quick and friendly. The food was typical fare, nothing that stood out, really. My fried chicken salad was Ok, served on a bed of meh iceburg lettuce. The steak salad that my companion got was literally ringed with a plethora of chopped black olives.   The sandwich? It looked yummy, but it's been so long since I've tasted bread, i'm afraid I might break if I did.

So it's the first time that we've eaten here, and I'm impressed. More so than the other people who've reviewed this place.   We were looking for something to nosh on before we hit the stores for the Tax Free weekend. And since Bealls was on our list, we opted for the Green Market Cafe.  Apparently a lot of other folks chose to eat here too, since finding a seat was a like finding buried treasure. If you found one inside it was GOLDEN.  The husband ordered one of their wasabi wraps, it said on the menu that it was -hot- but he said that there was a hint of heat, but a LOT of flavour. The chicken was creamy and their addition of peas added an Asian flare.    I ordered the pick 2 combo, which included a 1/2 salad and a cup of soup. I chose the classic Ceaser salad and a cup of their tomato bisque soup. Both were fresh and delicious. Though if that was a half a salad... it was HUGE, 2 people could have dined off of it. My goodness.   And both of us received a small froyo as a dessert!  They had 4 flavors to choose from including cocovanilla and taro, both of us made the easy decision of the CocoVanilla and received a delicious lightly coconutty vanilla froyo treat that satisfied our sweet tooth!    We will eat here again now that we know what to expect!

This is the most unorganized, erratic and least staffed Burlington I've had the displeasure to be in.  The floor was... disorganized, it was hard to tell what clothing sizes were where. When looking at dresses they were quite litterally all over the place.   The wallets and gift sets were strewn about, many were missing pieces. I know that this isn't the store's fault, that this is LOSS, but the associates should at least cull those that have been rifled through and remove them from the floor for mark downs.   This is not a place I will be visiting again.

Here it is... I have found a piece of heaven!  I saw this store while driving home one night. The window display caught my eye: A formal dress made out of business cards, that alone was enough to make me stop in.  I wasn't sure what to expect, given that it is tucked amid all the antique shoppes along the avenue.    When I entered, i was impressed with their selection. They had just about anything you could want that was considered Geekery: Dr.Who Salt Shakers, a disappearing Bill of Rights coffee Mug, hand crafted leather bound journals - as well as hand crafted paper inserts for said journals.   There were clothes for belly dancing, steam punk dresses and corseted umbrellas (which I bought). Victorian riding hats and top hats. Antique goggles in cases and a whole bunch of neat stuff to explore.   I could have spent all day inside this singular shop, and likely I will the next time I go back. I was especially enamoured with their key-hole mirror!  This place is the tops!

Made a reservation because it was our 8th anniversary earlier in the week but due to work and what have you, we decided to celebrate on the weekend.  The reservation process on line, was very simple, and got an immediate confirmation.   When we arrived, we were advised that we would have to wait 10-15 minutes, even though we had reservations. No worries, it wasn't terribly busy, and there were seats available.  When we were called, they called by the first name, and didn't ring the buzzers they gave us, which I thought was odd, and it turned out badly too, since there were two groups with my first name. We had been there longer, and we were obviously the first folks that needed to be seated, so the reception folks were a bit confused as to how to handle what was going on. *shrug* they did end up taking us and seating us in that hand of people.  Once seated, the service was excellent. Our drinks and appetizer waiter was exceedingly friendly, very warm and gregarious as he took our orders and made sure our drinks were gotten to us on time.   He made sure that he had who ever had celebrations take care of ahead of time too.   Our chef.. while pleasant enough.. didn't do much of a "Show" at all, even though we had 2 young children at the table. The only "trick" that he did was the volcano, there was no Choo-Choo train, nothing else that entertained or engaged the rest of the table.    But over all, the food was well done and tasted great.

The last time I visited a JR's it was in Orlando and the review wasn't that good. This time it was much better.   Our waitress was quite friendly, very refreshing from some of the servers as of late. We placed our orders for our drinks and looked at the menu, as I chose my food, I popped a quarter in the table side juke box, made my 6 selections, but sadly it apparently didn't work. That's ok, it's only $0.25.  When the food came, it both looked good and was delivered with a smile. LITERALLY! The little ketchup plates are always filled with smiles of the condiment. Since I don't like ketchup, I asked for Ranch and it was delivered without an issue.    My chili dog was delicious and the fries were Ok, not fryer fresh, but still fine. The husbeasts burger was delicious, but so juciy that he needed to eat it with a fork, since the bun fell apart.   Since I don't get to Citrus Park mall all that often any more, I don't know how frequently I'd be back, but I certainly would be.

Due to being Ill, I had to have tests done. I had to stop by Labcorp to get the necessary supplies.   Everyone I encountered was fast and efficient, polite too. Once I was able to provide the samples I had to take them back to Labcorp and turn them in.  It's nice to know just what the problem is.. now I just want to be cured.

Mom, bless her soul, wanted to find a yard stake, something to decorate her yard with. And since we were at Cracker Barrell,  I figured why not. I'd not been there since they opened. It would be neat to see what they had.  I'm not sure what I thought I was going to find, but everything was there. From sheets and bedding, albeit low end items, to artwork,  dinosaurs and floating god heads. If you could think of it, they likely had it. Quite freaky, really.  Though mom didn't buy anything, I found a Kiss a Geek coffee mug for the husbeast,  2 grow a pepper in a can and some led light kits for relatively cheap. I was pleased to find the lighting!

First: Thanks for the tickets! I've never been to one of these events, so the fact that I got to bring my husband and 2 of our friends, well, that was a really nice treat!  We arrived around 7pm, while the event was in full swing. I popped over to the ticketing tent (clearly missing the sign on the back side that said WILL CALL, and just gave the woman there my name. She pulled up my tickets and asked if I had anyone with me who'd be drinking. Oh yeah.. so I called my friends all over to me and we showed our ID's, got banded and then headed into the fray.   There were a lot of choices, and my tummy isn't that big these days, but MAN oh MAN where do you start. I have to admit I was impressed with the offerings from James Joyce Irish pub, their Buffalo Chicken burger and their Jamison Burger were delicious.   The waffle fry and oil infused burger from Wicked Wiches was so tender and flavourful, but Nothing, and I do mean NOTHING beat what EATS! put out. Their burger was served hot, fresh from the grill and super juicy. Every time that someone voted for them, their whole team cheered! Seriously good eats from Eats.   By the time that the rest of my compatriots finished up - i'd wussed out early on, I got us all Ice Pops from the only place offering cool sweet treats, and they were absolutely scrumptious.   A round of applause to the folks that both participated in the event, attended and ran it. I lost my phone. I apparently dropped it while taking a photo, and someone actually turned it in. Man, that 20 minute period of my life was.. dark. Looking back, I know it's not the worlds end, but Jeez, that left me scared. So thanks to EVERYONE there, for being good people!
