I don't usually go to chic-fil-a for many reasons, but I needed food, and they were close. The service was exceedingly polite. They were prompt and most of all, the fries were hot and fresh.. OMG the FRIES!! People can say they love McD's fries, but I love me some waffle fries!!! They really are the best!  Again, always service with a smile, friendly people who don't cop an attitude when you have a special request an they always count your change back, unlike most other places.

While exploring my home city, I stumbled upon Eat Greek Kouzina. I gave a shrug and took a chance, an BOY am I glad I did.  This place was fabulous.  Inside it's small, intimate and cozy.  There's a section that you access by a staircase, and seating beneath, along with seating along the window and seating along the wall. That's it.. Small.   The owner is the chef and it's clear that he love his food. The first thing that we were introduced to was an olive and pepper tepenade, spicy yet so tasty.  We ordered an appetizer of cheese and spinach, not your typical spanokipita, but in any case it was absolutely delicious.   Our main courses were brought out quickly: I ordered the pork chops and french fries, my friend ordered a Gyro, both were amazing, and the fries were seasoned very well, with a dill and feta sauce.   Would I come back? You're damned straight I would.

I'm sad that they've got such a low rating but I understand why. They did get off to a rocky start. This is my 2nd visit, I really thought I'd put my first one down, but I guess I forgot.  *Shrug* That's ok, it wouldn't have been great.   This visit though, we were pleasantly surprised. The place is all decked out for Christmas, in blue and silver, very Greek in decor and very nice - if you can over look that it used to be a Bob Evans.  Our server was exceedinly polite and very thorough. She made sure we had our bread and fresh coffee when we were seated. She covered the specials which included a fish that they served whole and surf and turf, neither were what we wanted.   We did place our orders - Mine was the Fried Jumbo Shrimp with fries and a salad, and the husband went with Mousakka - a Greek tradition with the soup of the day, Cream of Mushroom.   The salad was crisp and delicious and she even put on two large slices of fresh feta for me.  The soup was YUMMY!  Our food came quick and the portions sizes were huge. We even left with left overs. Will we be back? Of course we will, they're right down the street and we like the customer service.

New, this Chipotle location has a clean, industrial and edgy vibe to it. The staff was friendly,  the service was fast, and the food appeared to be fresh  I got myself a bowl, made with the barbocoa beef, rice and beans, I added guacamole and sour cream, got chips and a drink and paid a total of $13.13 (the guacamole was $1.95 add on)   It tasted good, I won't lie, I enjoyed it,  but hated that the music was blaring at above conversation level. Wit their open air atmosphere,  no carpeting, nothing at all to absorb sound, it was very uncomfortable to the ear. And the food left my stomach sour all evening, perhaps it was an ingredient in the meat or something was off, but I was unsettled until the next morning.

This is the first time I've been to the new location since they moved down to Largo.  I'll be honest, I wasn't completely impressed. They do have quite the selection of things, but it's a jumble. There are a lot of things that are of good or decent quality, and then there are things that are kind of questionable.   I saw retractable power cords, like the one I was using at that very moment to charge my phone. Theirs was $14.99. I'd bought mine in Georgia at Fry's for $6.99, that's not a deal.  They'd had argyle socks for $3.00. This is about the price I'd pay at Target. Speaking of Target. They had a Mossimo purse from Target, black leather, for $25.00.  Doesn't sound bad, until you know that the price tag from Target was still on it, and it was originally $26.99. *SMH*  I did buy an ergonomic stool from them for $40 - with 20%off. Currently the same model is being sold on Amazon for $79.00.  I also got a pair of knee high boots for $20. They usually run about double that. So it is really hit or miss with what you find. If you know what you're buying, if you know the average of prices, then you know what you're in for. It is all Buyer beware.   My biggest complaint though: The movie section. There is no rhyme or reason to it. There is a HUGE selection but it is all thrown together. Frankly that's too much work even for $2.00 a pop.
Stopped in before 3rd Friday so I wouldn't be tempted by all the goodies offered by vendors.  I'm glad I did too! I had a magnificent flat bread and a bowl of soup. Their tomatoe soup was amazing!

I can't say I've ever been to a theater like this before! We walked in and at first we were confused. We didn't see where to buy the tickets, but you buy your tickets and your concessions TOGETHER. That's pretty novel.  Their Movie times tend to go by rather quickly, so pay attention, but other than that it's pretty good.   Their manager was pretty awesome, he was very helpful. He signed us up for the Carmike Cinema card which is also good with Muvico! We have a Muvico in Tampa. Apparently the points I earn there will count at any Carmike place. COOL!   Very comfortable cinema. Very New and very nice. I wish one of these would come near Tampa.

After such a delightful lunch, we needed to go someplace to walk it all off. Since we were going to be in NPR, I suggested we go to the Mall.   I used live in NPR, and I was in the city when it was built. It has fallen -so far- down the rabbit hole from what it used to be in it's prime.  Gone are stores that used to be stellar (Jc Penneys, Maas Brothers, Burdines) and now you have stores that I just don't even understand  (On Point fashion, Dollar Town, Rue 21)   I miss the book store, I miss Sabaros, I'm glad that there are stores like the comic book store down near Dillards, and that there's now an Ulta, because that Ulta is fantastic. But it makes me sad to see that the mall is barely surviving. It's holding on by it's fingertips and someone seems to be stomping on them.

Tampa's Curtis Hixon Waterfont park is the perfect place to hold community events. The event that I attended was "Take back the Night " #tbtntb or #turntampateal, an event that helps promote awareness about the resources available to those who've been victims of domestic or sexual abuse.   There were plenty of tables but more than 1/2 of the community tables were available, they'd been assigned, but no one was at them. Wether this is because the event wasn't promoted or because those who'd committed to the tables didn't want to chance the weather (There'd been a chance of rain), it was disheartening.   The event compromised of music, of a pledge to stop or intervene in abuse, the processional and the candelite vigil and then the stories. It was a telling and emotional evening, but a necessary one.  Given my profession, I hear a lot of stories and in my circle I am the one people come to, so now I have the resources to help my friends and chosen family..   You are not alone, there is help, Take back the night.

It was another game of Spin the Yelp to see what would come up when I was getting out of dance class and the husbeast was getting out of work late. When it landed on this one.. I liked the concept and so.. a decision was made.   Finding it was ..tricky. I ended up at Charlie's Cafe, but apparently the GPS was off of our location by about 100 feet, the pub is next to Domino's so we just had to move our cars.  *shrug* Parking for 1933 Pub & grill can be tight, as it was, i took the last space and there didn't seem to be a lot of people there, I think everone must have taken there own vehicles!  We walked in, it was dimly lit. There was NO hostess, the waitstaff was all behind the bar, so we sat down and waited. Minutes ticked by until one of the people finally came out and asked us why we didn't flag them down, their regulars would have been screaming by then (five or so minutes had passed).   When we did get the menu, we perused it for a few minutes and finally placed our orders, we started with their Slim Pickings - Basically Chili Cheese fries. And they were very good, The only thing I can say about them is that the chili was on the WAY mild side, even for me, and that it lacked salt.   The husband had one of their burgers, and chips with cajun flavoring. The chips were some of the crispiest I've ever had and his burger was both thick and juicy! I opted to have some wings and cole slaw, the slaw was DAMNED good! And the wings were right tasty as well. Their medium sauce wasn't too spicy, and had a good bite on the tongue.   Personally, I found it too dark inside, I had to use my cell phone to order by, and the minimal light offered by the tea-light on the table was barely enough to light my pictures. Other than that, it was a good place to catch a meal and conversation!

New coffee shop, nice play on name that really doesn't deliver... YET.   We came in on a Sunday afternoon during a spring/summer rainstorm.  The shop had quite a few patrons, but we were served right away, with no wait at all.   The service was friendly and quick. I got a vanilla latte, my boyfriend got himself a coffee and chatted with the owner.  Admittedly, it's bland on the inside, the green walls are a bit boring, but with time I'm sure that you'll see the place come alive with art.   The coffee was well made and delicious.

I'd heard that one of the designers from Project Runway had put a line out of Ready to Wear for plus sized women at JCP and I wanted to see what they had.  Indeed! They were carrying ms. Ashley's line and I found it right up front in the section I was looking for.   The store was organzied well, and i was able to quickly buy what I was looking for.

Color me surprised to walk into the food court of Brandon Mall on Sunday (father's day) and see a Pho Shop in the Mall!  I had a choice of something other than fast food and fried? You betcha I'm gonna take that any day of the week.  Service was quick, food was fast and fresh, and the girls, although it was about an hour from closing were cheerful and happy to help. For "Mall Food" It was quite good. I will be certain to come back again when I'm in Brandon!

I needed food after being out all day, and so I stopped in thru the drive-thru. I picked up three items, A med. frosty, a small chili and a small fry. All came to about $5.75. The fries were lukewarm, the chili was spicier than usual and the frosty was good.   I had no problem with the service, just sad that everything wasn't as good as it could have been.

My friends have all talked up Aldi, and this evening, I thought we could check it out.  It may just be this location, but WOW, It was not at all what I was expecting.   This store was a MESS. There was seemingly no rhyme or reason to the way it was laid out and the way the stock was arranged. It looked and felt very chaotic.  It also felt very much like a Sams/BJ's on the inside, cold and impersonal.   The prices were fine, the products look good. And the location was fine too. Though one cashier at 7pm probably was a bad call. There was a decent line the entire time I was there.  I don't think I'd return.

I needed a new pool brush. Mine is a bit sun damaged and when I last scrubbed the pool, I noticed that the brush ends were breaking off.. So after visiting mom, I popped into Lowes, and asked where the pool supplies were. I was told they were "Out Side".    I wandered out side, It took a few minutes, but I found the pool things... Man, I had NO idea that there were SO many kinds of pool brushes available. Since I'm not sure what the best one is, I buy three. Well, I can, so i do, now I have a choice. LOL the husbeast can't be mad.. it's for -cleaning-!!!

Recently opened in the old Barnhill's location on SR 54, My husband and I decided to check it out. Truth be told, I was hankering for some Peanut Chicken and didn't want to drive down to Chopsticks.  We were surprised when we walked in. They have gutted the old building, taken out about 60% of the seating and put in a LOT of buffet tables. The food variety is there, Hot and cold, including a hibachi and sushi. However, the turn over that I've seen at other places like Chopstics & Super Buffet isn't there. The greenbeans were wilted and cold, with about 5 in the pan. So when things were running out they weren't being re-stocked.  They had a mystery meat-type loaf that scared me. THEY called it a pork loin, but it was simply pressed meat. I didn't try it.  The husband said the sushi was fresh and tasty. Their chicken on a stick was delicious and their desserts were copious, but  overall, I wasn't terribly impressed. Prices were decent, $6.99 for lunch 11-4pm on M-Sat. Drinks at $1.49 seems to be a bargain.

My first impression on walking into Besa was.. Wow this place is SWANKY! The lounge music playing was classy, the interior is full of dark woods, rich upholstery and little bits of crystal dripping from the ceiling, and pretty purple accents.  All in all the place is very visually appealing.   The second thing I notice is why is it not at all crowded? There aer 2 tables of 8, both full of swinging silver foxes from what I can tel, a group of Sixties and a group of Eighties, but other than these two tables, the place is empty.  My friend and I are kind of concerned, but the hostess seats us at a quiet booth (which is totally adorable, by the way - with its black and silver rose upholstery and purple pillows) and we wait for our waitress.   The waitress is pleasant, warm and friendly but she really doesn't know the menu, and I can't fault her for that, it seems to be something that might change. However the items all appear to be fresh and the place smells wonderful, so my friend and I peruse the items and make our selections, he chooses the Turkey, avacado club and I choose the Besa Bistro Burger both came with fries.   The Turkey Avacado Club was everything you'd think it should be, crisp and light, served on toasted white bread and a healthy side of fries.  The Bistro Burger though. WOW! The Burger was done medium, topped with grilled portobello Mushrooms, goat cheese, fresh guaa, arugala, roasted red peppers and served on Chibata bread.  Me, I asked for the red peppers on the side and they were happy to accomodate my request.  The flavors all popped together nicely, the sharpness of the cheese and guac mixed beautifully and the meat was tender, it really was a damned tasty burger!  Their fries had a good seasoning on them as well.  It was so juicy that I had to separate the bun from the burger and eat the meat aside.   However it was a very large portion and I left much of it behind, in favour of ordering dessert! I wanted to try their churros. Yummy fried dough sticks sprinkled with cinnamon sugar served with caramel and fudge sauce. You really can't go wrong, right? There are 4 of these, they are cut in half and so you're given 8. They are stacked log cabin style and brought to you on a plate. The first thing I said when I saw it was.. I'm going to need a box.  With a cappucino - served with a rock sugar stick, this was the perfect way to end a meal.   Good company, a good meal and nice atmosphere, I admit though I had my reservations, I will be back!

Stopped in with the beau after a lovely date night.   I'm familiar with the older location and found the new location charming.  Though the waitstaff didn't seem ..I don't know.. enthuiastiac(?) to be there.  We were seated and a waitress was there immediately.   Our orders were taken, I opted for one of the skillets while my beau chose his usual, with a side of bacon.    The coffee was hot and fresh, and as always delicious.  When the food came out, it was as described, everything was perfect. My skillet had the right amount of egg, meat and potatoes.  My beau was quite happy with his food too.   We left happy

Sign on the speaker said "If we don't answer in 2 minutes, drive around" they didn't so I drove around.  WHen I got to the window, the girl asked me "Why did you drive around?" She was very confused. So I placed an order at the window for a chili cheese dog and tots.   The food was good, edible, I just wish they were closer.

Just off the Courtney Campbell causeway is the Best Western Bay Harbor Hotel. It's tucked in an alcove off the road and houses Hogan's Beach. I was there because I was obtaining my CEU's for Massage, so we used their conference rooms. They were large but noisy since they were tucked up against the kitchen.  I can honestly say this was a huge distraction when you're trying to do some energy work.   Over all, it's got some nice features, but a big drawback is the way their bathroom in the public area isn't kept up.

Eggstyle is one of my favorite places to eat Brunch. The food is always good, always a feast for the senses and always delicious. Sure the service might be slow, but in the end the quality is decadent.    My favorite thing is the Sandwich surprise. Basically french toast, with Ham, Egg and swiss grilled between it. Smothered in a sweet sauce and fruit. It is absolutely HEAVEN! It's pricy, yes, but it is worth every cent!

I needed to get cash, and since I prefer to use my bank for that task, I simply keyed in the name and BINGO.. Yelp directed me to the closest location.  No drive up ATM for this location *sad* but covered parking when the weather was turning bad and a covered atm made the trip easy peasy.

Beautifully maintained, well kept and well appointed, this park was a surprise.  I love finding out that I can rent a canoe here and spend a few hours out on the bay!  The learning center here is great! It's a useful and necessary way to learn about our local eco system.   If you've not had the chance, come and visit the Upper Tampa Bay regional park.

I watched this business start as an idea, begin to grow as they owners, a Mother and Daughter - with the husband working tirelessly beside them, began to renovate an old coffee shop next to where I work.  Every day, I wondered about their progress, and every time I'd work, we'd ask them to make sure that from X - X could they not use the power tools as there was a massage going on, they were very agreeable.   Over the past few months, they've worked day and night, it seems and now the business has opened, inside it's neat and clean and very picturesque. They've got a lovely cold case with pretty cupcakes, delicious looking rice krispy treats and other decadent treasures waiting for me to try. They sell artisan breads and they make sandwiches and coffee too. It appears they're going to be a full service shop in no time.   I didn't have much time, but I did want to stop in and patronize the shop, so I purchased a lovely little cupcake, a yellow one with vanilla icing and sprinkles, It was almost too pretty to eat.. ALMOST~ But that first bite sealed the cupcake's doom! It was ruthlessly devoured. Although I admit, some of the icing survived. There was just a touch too much for me!   Would I go back? Yes. Why? Because it's next door to where I work, because the service was excellent and the people seem like first class folks!

This Target has the best Pharmacy! Barbie is awesome!!! I come in every two weeks to pick up my RX and they know me by sight. You can't beat that for service.   Like every other Target, they too have an "Admission fee", and by that I mean, i can't leave any target without paying my "ticket" price.. I always find way more than I originally came in for. If I went in for toilet paper, I walk out with that, plus a new video, some books and $100 worth of merchandise. I just love shopping at Target!

Had a date with a dear friend. Neither of us had been to Cappy's so we took a chance, rolled the dice and arrived.  The atmosphere is pretty cool, Soaring ceilings, High booths and trivia on the tables.   We ordered the cheesy bread as an appetizer, and I can guarantee you that our drinks never went empty, as my friend JP and I chatted over many different topics, and quizzed each other on the Trivial Pursuit cards on hand (for the record, we both suck)   We ordered a Chicago Deep Dish style pizza as our main dish, and we were NOT disappointed.   The crust was thick and buttery, the toppings were cheesy and plentiful and amazingly Tasty.  Our service was great too! As I said the cups never went dry, and we never wanted for anything. Even the sub out from mushrooms to bacon was accommodated without any issue.   Will I be back? You betcha!

How did I not know this place has been here for 35 years? Granted I knew it'd been here a while, but why has it taken me so long to eat here? The answer is that it's just not in my usual path. But it will be now!  My paramour and I decided we needed a nice, romantic dinner.  Ok, we needed to eat, The romantic part was added by the dimly lit interior of the eatery.  We were a party of two, it was around 8:30 when we were sat and our waiter was prompt and courteous.  Since it was our first time, we opted to sample a lot of things.   We ordered Garlic knots, Caprese salad, and a large Calamari to share.  The three came out and I'm not gonna lie, I kinda wondered why we ordered entrees.  The food was SO good. The calamari came with a side of red sauce that was delicious.  The Caprese salad was so fresh and tasty and the garlic knots were out of this world.   Our mains were Sausage and peppers for him and I got the Chicken Parmigana, both came with sides of pasta, he got a side of Alfredo which was a $4.50 up charge and I got rigatoni in red sauce.  EVERYTHING was amazing, it was seriously some of the very best alfredo sauce I've ever had.    We ate about 1/3 of everything and had it packaged up to go home.  They're meticulous about wrapping everything up in plastic wrap over the take out containers so they don't leak which is fantastic! The left overs were heated up for my sick husbeastie at home and a meal the next day.   I will certainly be coming back to this place, over and over again.

The last time that I was at this ROSS, it was a hot mess. They've since cleaned up their act.  The Ross was neat and clean, well stocked and in general a very pleasant experience for shopping.   I was able to find a few items that I'd not seen in any of the other Ross' I frequent. And if you follow me, I frequent them ALL.

Gulfview Square Mall is not what it used to be and this Anchor Store is... while nice, not an amazing experience.  I went mainly to go to the semi-annual sale, to see what bras they had available in their 65% off area.  There were a few that were available in my size, but not nearly as many as there were at International plaza.  I suppose that is par for the course, given the area.  The store was neat and clean, there were plenty of items for sale, plenty of high end merchandise on display, but not many folks shopping.    The Lingerie department was neat, well stocked and carried a majority of the same stock as the larger format stores, so I can't complain. All in all it was a solid experience.

This shop used to be up near me in Tarpon, but they've since relocated to Dunedin.   It's a lovely little used bookstore that has an amazing selection.  There are some new books too, along with autographed first editions and other things of interest.   it's a great stop in you're eating in a place near by, or just walking the town.

I -FINALLY- got around to using the gift card I won at our big party.  Since I was out in Brandon tonight i decided to invite a friend out with me to sample the food, and see if it was as good as I remembered it.   We arrived at 7ish,  and Tony was our waiter, Apparently he worked our Yelpie's event at Carne! He was a very gracious waiter and made sure that all our needs were met.  We started our meals with drinks, chips & salsa. The chips were hand made and the salsa was fresh - if made with a touch too much cilantro - but that's to my taste, someone else might not agree.   We asked suggestions on meals as we'd never been there before and he suggest the Carne (pork) and a few other dishes. I took him up on the pork as it's one of my favorite dishes and my friend went for the enchiladas. In the mean while, our chips were re-filled and we were given a dish of some of the tastiest guacamole I've ever had the pleasure of eating - SO DAMN GOOD!  The meals came out and LAWDY... I have no idea how I was supposed to eat all this food. After all, I'd already nommed on the tasty chips and salsa. But the meals were there and eat we did. Mine came with hand made tortillas and a huge helping of Carne, rice and beans and a salad. It was So good. The plate with the enchiladas came with 4 - yes that's 4 enchiladas, the choice was either Chicken or cheese & onion, and could be either rojo sauce or salsa verde. His plate was just as full as mine and looked JUST as good.   We ate about 1/3rd of what we were given before calling it quits.. we wanted to make sure that we got to sample the desserts: Tony rattled off a list of things which included Churros, Flan, a Choco Taco (not the ice cream treat) and tres leche cake.. It was hard to make a decision. But I wanted flan and my friend went for the tres leche cake.. Both were delicious, I did end up taking 1/2 of mine home.    I quite literally have a meal for tomorrow with the left overs.   YES!! I will be back and I will recommend this place to people  in Brandon. It's THAT good.

Tampa Theatre is a gorgeous old venue, it's on the register of Historic places and is even rumored to be haunted. (Screw the rumors, I've seen things, so I know there's at least a few presences that are active). She's a stately old Dame with beautiful trappings. Soaring marble stair cases, a stunning lobby and a wonderfully set stage. This is what theaters used to look like, back when they had personality!  The stage itself is set for plays, for musical acts and can be set up for feature films, of which they show plenty. But what brought me here this night was a chance to see two wonderful people on stage, Neil Gamin (Author) and Amanda Palmer (Author & Musician - the Dresden Dolls) in a talk called "Heartbreak Hotel" Or an informal talk on Heartbreak and Valentine's day.  It was a promising evening.   When I got tickets, I was happy, these things apparently went very quickly. I ended up in the nose bleed seats up in the far back of the balcony, however they were almost dead center of the stage, so our view was excellent. The only thing I can complain about is the size of these seats. The theater, as I've mentioned before is older. It is in dire need of a seat renovation. They are narrow, (And I mean about 17 inches wide) They are uncomfortable, and the isles are narrow too, so if you're tall, there is NO leg room. Those of us with the blessing (or curse) of height had our knees shoved up under our chins.   I was sandwiched between my husband, who's not small, and two wonderful women who were plus sized. Mind, I'm not small myself, but I fit comfortably into my seat. These two lovelies were markedly uncomfortable and vocal about it. They left within the first 30 minutes of the show, it was that bad.   Will I return? YES! They're offering quite the line up in the near future, including the internet sensation Miranda Sings, and it's already sold out.

I wasn't sure what to expect. The place has been there forever, but I was hungry and they were the first breakfast stop I found.  I walked in and was able to seat myself, being as it was almost noon, they were serving breakfast and lunch(breakfast is served all day).  The service was very quick and friendly! The waitress was very happy to answer any questions I might have.   It didn't take long for my order of a classic skillet (Eggs served over a skillet with potatoes and breakfast meats - in this case ham, bacon and sausage, with cheese) to arrive. There was A LOT of food. I only made a dent and it came with toast too!  The coffee was hot and dark, and never went empty. I'd likely come here again.

If you're visiting from out of country and you want to avoid the theme parks, where do you take them? Local celebrations! Enter the Strawberry Festival!  I took the Scot to our bachanalia of strawberries and whipped cream, of fried foods and carnival rides. It's been a long time since I've been here myself, so it was fun to see it with both his and my eyes.   We checked out the live stock - gotta love cow a,  bunnies and fluffy chickens!  Then we made our way to the midway in search of funnel cake covered bacon, which we didn't find. We opted for corn dogs the size of our arms - the Scots first ever, we walked the expo hall and decided the rain coming was making the air too chilly, so we decided to head out, but not before the Scot grabbed an ice cream to go! SILLY!!  8 years stong, and the traffic gets worse each year. Ugh!

I don't get to SteinMart all that often, but I was killing time so I wandered in and looked around.  I found a few items of interest, like a dress that was very Pucci-esque, a great idea for a 1960's style costume $14.95. I found a pair of shorts for the husband for under $20.00.  The prices were fair, these were clearance items after all.. and I was happy with the quality of the items.  The one thing I really liked is the boyfriend jacket i purchased, a black and white striped affair that fits perfectly for just $10.00

Beautiful, state of the art facility.    I had the pleasure of having Ashley Ann as my este for my Hydrofacial, she as extremely pleasant and friendly. She walked me through each step of the process and answered every question I might have.   The process was quite relaxing and very soothing for the 50 or so minutes it took. The table was comfortable and at no time was I ever uncomfortable.    They took before photos so they'd have an idea of what my skin looked before the procedure, so that in the future they'd have something to go off of.  Of course my skin would be in a flare from rosacea and being in Perimenopause, but hey, it's what they have to work with.   I would certainly come back in the future.

Friendly staff, great selection and lots of delightful shiny things! I was very happy to see that they hae so many new 1940-50's inspired designs.    I haven't had much luck here in the past, but today.. today I was blessed to find a new costume skirt for my corsets, a L/Xl from Burleska for under $100. The seaming and everything looked fantastic.  Pricey? somewhat, but it's good to know that I'm no longer too big to wear their fabulous fashions!

Hole in the wall, but the service was great.    Went with a group of 6 folks, found the music to be a touch loud and the offerings on the cold bar to be a bit meager, even if my diet doesn't allow me to have much. But please, bring on the meats.   The sword bearers brought out their offerings every 4-5 minutes, and there was everything from sausage to bacon wrapped filet, there was an amazing sirloin with the most delicious crust on the meat. Honestly it was so good that was what we really wanted more of.  $24.99 per person wasn't a bad cost at all!

I just want to extend my heartfelt thanks to the crew at Animal Emergency & Urgent care. My elderly feline had been failing and a week ago, he let us know it was time.   I gave them a call and made sure they were open. They were, they're 24/7. We arrived and were taken back to a room and seen by a tech who took our Kit'en's vitals and got the Doctor to see us.   I'm not going to write out the long story here, suffice to say it was our feline's time and the clinic's staff was sweet and caring and very compassionate towards our needs.  When the time came, they gave us all the time we needed to say good by before the end came.   We will be forever thankful for their care.

I stopped in today after seeing the sign on the side of the road, and I'm honestly glad I did. The first thing I noticed about this little tucked away boutique was how tasteful it is. How clean and beautifully decorated it was.  Everything is neat, there are sparklies everywhere.   Top of the line products are her specialty from Escante Lingerie for the plus sized gal to Lelo vibrators, Penny does not skimp on anything.  She's personable and her parrot, Valentine is an adorable flirt to be sure.  This store carries corsets, silk boxers, hosiery, accessories and even a few mild fetish items. If you want it, or want to explore it, Intimate Desires seems to have it.  Check the store out, you won't be disappointed, I know I wasn't!

I was really happy to see Pho Queen open. The only reputable Pho place is in Countryside mall, and now we have another!  The husbeast and I were seated, our orders placed and we ended up getting our starters - Fresh spring rolls - in less than 3 minutes. They were absolutely fresh! The peanut sauce was a tiny bit sweet but over all, they were very good.  My husband ordered combination pho and I ordered one of their Bun bowls, with pork and shrimp. These came to our table in about 7 minutes. The food was amazing! It too was fresh, quick and oh so damned tasty!  The only reason I've given them a 4 was that it's OBVIOUS this used to be a steak house, they've done nothing to change it at all. And the music.. Adele's greatest hits played only on piano. It just lacked something. I would much rather have heard standard "Oriental" or "Asian" music for atmosphere.    We WILL be back!

We stayed here in early November, while the place was undergoing a bit of a renovation. The room we were given, 302 faced the road and was very large with an AC unit that could not handle the size (Or rather the set up of the room, had the AC unit been placed on the wall vs under the window, the room would have cooled the room, vs the small section of the room it did.)  The hotel itself was really nice, the bed was comfortable, the shower was large and the linen was clean.  The service from the ladies down stairs was always friendly and fast.  We would certainly stay here again if we were in the area.

Talk about your hidden gem.  I vaguely had remembered seeing the sign for this Pho eatery in the shopping plaza when driving by, so I looked it up and took my husbeast there for his 2nd birthday dinner.   When we arrived, they were not busy at all. One gentleman was waiting on a to-go order, and us.  We were seated immediately and our server got our drinks. I got hot tea and ice water, the hubby got iced tea. They were at our table in a flash.   We placed our orders for fresh spring rolls, the hubby got a deconstructed salad with cucumber, rice noodles, pork, eggroll and shrimp.  It was delicious.  I had roast pork over rice with cucumber and tomato on the side.  It too was fresh and tasty.   The husbeast declared that this is his new favorite Vietnamese eatery.

I can't believe I waited 3 years to go inside. They're LITERALLY right around the corner from me.    The other night the boyfriend and I went inside because I needed something new, and BOY! Did I find it.    This store has quite the collection of EVERYTHING. If you need a new water pipe, a new hand pipe, papers or what have you, they've got it. Need incense? sure!  A lighter? Its there.. CBD? yep, Kratom? they have it.   Everything is competitively priced and high quality.  The shopping center isn't inviting but the store really is. Stop in, you won't be disappointed.

Local ice cream parlor located off Hudson Avenue in Hudson, right down the street from one of the busiest beaches.   We stopped in on a Wednesday afternoon, you would have thought it was a Saturday, with how busy the line was.  We had one person scooping, one person ringing, and the line was 10 deep.  Yes, it was busy, but no one was complaining   Mom got the Elvis Sundae, a fun mix of Chocolate ice cream, bananas, marshmallow and peanut butter.  I got myself a single scoop of Espresso chip ice cream.  The sundae was large and only cost $5.50 for the size of it, and it was loaded with whipped cream. Mom really loved it.  Personally I found the ice cream I chose too sweet and cloying, but that's personal taste. I did not finish mine.   We would come back. This place is hopping.

I've been to Ohio and seen this concept before, I'm GLAD it's here in Tampa now. This is such a great idea. A place where you can choose what you want to eat, find a place to share your meals and enjoy. It's pretty awesome.   There's so many different types of places to eat too!

Not at all what I expected.  I expected an over lit, jam packed store filled with batteries, juice and god knows what else. What I encountered was a store in subdued lighting, a long bar with seating where you can get your Kava and Kratom tea, Different vape juices and a pit area for video games.   Over all, the vibe was cool and chill. No one was loud, there was a soft dull murmur that was comfortable to the ear. The attendant at the bar was very helpful.

We were looking for Chinese one night when the Husbeast was working late and I was home sick.  This used to be our go to place, so I rang them up and placed an order for 2 General Tso combos, much to the husbeast's consternation.   The meals were tasty, both had fried rice and an egg roll and a helping of General Tso's chicken that was MORE than enough for me, and the husband was a member of the almost clean plate club.  It was Good, but not phenomenal.

Smoky, so smoky that you can smell it out side. Dark, but lit by black light. The bar however is good, the drinks are cheap, yet potent. A dive bar that is king of dive bars.  It's one of those places that you go to and if you're a regular, they know you by name.   Parking is.. well.. tight, but it's ok.  I was there on this particular night for a concert offered by Goth's own VOLTAIRE, the man is a legend in some circles. He was opened by VampHelsing. THe music was horribly loud, I couldn't understand the words, but hey, what are you going to do, it's Gothmetal. So I endured. Ah the plight of the elder goth.   For Voltaire, well that's what we all came for. The sound was perfect, he was engaging and I really hope he comes back as he said he would and make this a yearly thing. Gracious and engaging, warm and generous with his time, he sang a few songs never heard before and regaled us with a few stories of his time on the road.  Yeah, this is what I came to the Pegasus for, even if it felt like I had to burn my clothing after wards due to the smoke.

Such a small location. Seating is hard to come by, either inside or out.    My beau and I stopped here to see about breakfast after a sleep over at his place. We waited in a short line, we placed our orders for their cheesy hash brown bagel,  or at least the same thing, with an Everything bagel instead since they were out of those hash brown bagels.   We bussed our own table, got our coffee and sat and waited for our food to be ready. The food was tasty and made well. The service was fine.

Nice new age store on Central ave.  The stones were great, they have oils and crystals, tarot and what have you. Their prices were pretty decent.  While I was there, there was a live reading going on.  It seemed like a pretty cool place.

A wonderful femme positive store. It has a little bit of fashion, makeup, jewelry and art. It truly is an ecclectic mix and a store I could spend hours in and not see it all.  Loved it and wish there was one in Tampa that I could support.

This is the original 1983 location of Hooter, and I can't believe that I'm writing the first review.   A recent renovation has updated the location and made it look sharp and clean on the inside.  I especially like the bricks with quotes on the floor.   Our service was prompt and efficient, and the food was tasty. it's a wing place so that's what we got, along with a side of mediocre fries.   It's full of kitsch and nostalgia, but it's not a place you really go to for the food.

Down in the Tyrone area, not usually a place I venture, but it was our Geekly bi-weekly dinner.    They have an AYCE offer for $22.99 that offers a slew of sushi, apps and hibachi alternatives that turns out to be a pretty decent offer if you like what they're serving, and our table sure as heck did.   I'm not a sushi fan, so I stayed on the Hibachi side. I started my plate with the Edamame, Spring rolls and Tempura veg.  All were perfectly done, and I should have stopped there. That was more than enough food for me.  People all around me were talking about the New York Roll and the Miso Soup being delicious.   My second course was 3 of the tempura shrimp. I wish I'd known that you get 2 shrimp with every order, so I ended up with 6 tempura shrimp, which was too much for me, so I panned that out to others at my table.  (You're not supposed to share, but everyone at the table was doing the AYCE, so we didn't see the problem and neither did our waiter)  The peppered tuna was ABSOLUTELY to die for. It's the best thing sushi style I've ever put in my mouth. Very steak-y, very yummmm.   My last thing I ate was their Hibachi steak. This was perfect. The meat was not over done, it was well seasoned and perfectly tender.  Often hibachi meat is over done and dry. Not here. This I would have again and again.   If it weren't so far away  ( and I see they have a closer location) I would go agan.

The husbeastie and I stopped in today to have lunch on his birthday.  I've been here before, when the eatery was a different name.   It's cute, and quaint with dark wood and wrought iron. The heavenly smells of pizza and greek food from the kitchen all serve to make us hungry.  We were seated quite quickly and our waitress was with us right away.   We placed an order for an iced tea and a pepsi, which were delivered straight away, the Pepsi in a can.   We placed our order for a STARTER of the zuchini chips, and our mains would be the pork gyro platter and the pork souvlaki platter no onions.  We waited and people came in, the eatery filled, our waitress told us it wouldn't be much longer. The people who came in after us, got their appetizer, and we still hadn't gotten anything.  A minute later, our mains came out.  I asked about our starter and our waitress apologized and said that it would be right out, about 3 minutes later it came out.   The Pork Gyro, while tasty wasn't as gyro as my husband would have liked. It lacked the juiciness of the lamb and the spices the blended meat gyro would have.  The Pork souvlaki tasted good, the fries and pita were all tasty.   Over all, the food was good, the service was ok.

New to the Tarpon Scene, Papa T's Steak House is a really nice addition and something that's been missing.   Last night was date night with the beau, and since Covid started, there have been precious few of those as of late, so we took advantage of it being midweek and a new place to try it out.  It was just after the 5 pm hour, so they were not busy at all. We sat along the far wall, just beneath the stained glass from the former incarnation of this building. Still, really lovely windows.   The host asked us our drinks and advised us our waiter, Dareon, would be out soon.  I ordered a Pepsi and my beau an Unsweetened Iced tea.  Both were delivered in a minute or two with dinner rolls by the aformentioned Dareon.  The drinks were good, but the bread was very chemically tasting. I took one bite and let it sit. The beau was hungry, so though he too, said it tasted blerg, he ate it anyway.    We placed our orders, I got the Keto plate: 2 chicken breasts, served with sauteed Mushrooms and onions, and smothered with ooey gooey american, swiss and provolone cheeses.  My guy got the 12 ounce NY Strip.  We got sides of Chicken Tortilla soup, Pinto Beans and Green Beans.   The Chicken Tortilla Soup was good, really had a lot of flavour. It was topped with crispy onions vs Tortilla strips, but ok.  The pinto beans and green beans had a lot of down home, deep cooked flavor. Very tasty. The steak was cooked to perfection, though at first, my guy wasn't sure because he thought something smelled off.   My plate came and I admit I was somewhat confused. It was 2 chicken breasts, it was smothered in cheese, though I couldn't tell you the specific cheeses, they all melted together, but I didn't see any yellow american plastic cheese, Onions and peppers.  And the following raw foods arranged above, carrot strips, celery strips, Pickle wedges and the best tomato I've eaten in AGES.  It was odd, and there was a lot of food, so it mostly came home with me.   We'll be back, when they've settled on theme. They seem to be sort of aiming at something right now, but haven't really landed on it yet.  The food is good, the service was excellent. The only spot on this was that chem tasting bread.

Apparently we entered the wrong side, because we saw a sign that said "Don't seat yourself on the patio, go to the tiki bar to be seated" to find the tiki bar was fun, we were led through the kitchen by whom I assume is the manager, maybe even the owner and to the host station. A young man sat us in the dining room as I asked NOT to be sat where they were playing the live music (It's good, but too dang loud for my ears)  The weather outside was gorgeous, and we were sat on what amounts to be an old time Florida sun porch. We can hear the music and the breeze is coming in through opened windows, it was lovely. Our waiter was slow, but friendly and affable.  We ordered our drinks, Iced tea and a shock top for the husbeast and it seemed to take an inordinate amount of time to get drinks (7 minutes - yes, I time these things occasionally)  It turned out our waiter had a very big area alone, so I really can't fault him.   When we placed our order, I opted for the grouper nuggets with fries and coleslaw, and the hubby got a fisherman's platter which was a combo of fish, shrimp and other seafood.  with fries and coleslaw as well. It didn't take very long for these to come out, both platters were large, I will say that the grouper was listed Market Price, we asked, our waiter thought a moment and said $12.98, it was actually $9.98 and I'm not sure it was actually grouper. Some of it tasted right, some did not.  I don't eat fish often because it tastes "FISHY", these grouper nuggets usually don't and most didn't, but 2 did, and turned me off.   The husband ate every scrap of his food, so i can safely assume he liked every last bit of his.  We ordered dessert because they made a Fried Banana pudding, I'd never experienced that, and really needed to try it. It was Ok, it was nothing to write home about, but I would try it again, with a minor modification.

This was my second visit to the Fort De Soto park in my (mumble)something years in Florida.  I'm sorry I've not visited more frequently and that the visit today was for somber reasons.   We were in a shelter (#14) and it was very easy to get to, parking was ample and the shelter was HUGE with a domed roof, so if there was inclement weather, unless the rain is horizontal, we'd be safe and sound.  There were restrooms located adjacent to our location and provided both toilets and showers.  The beach even has ramp access for those in wheel chairs.   The beach is large and pristine with a gorgeous view of the Skyway at the east beach and the historic grounds of Fort Desoto on West beach, where the waves lap at the shore.    Things to know $5.00 all day parking, and access is by the toll road only, so be prepared for that.

We used this location for my dance studio's monthly recital. The space is easy to navigate and comfortable, but there were some issues with the lighting and sound cues. Over all, It appears that for this kind of venue, I think they'd be better off in other places. (But this is MY opinion)

I'm not a huge best buy fan. Yes they have a niche, but they're over priced on their tech. They are pretty much run of the mill every where you go.   Their staff is generally friendly, welcoming and all that, but today, not once was I approached, offered help or what not.  I also found it odd that the registers closest to the mall's entrance were closed. I suppose that they have the ability to stop people who are shop lifting, but this.. just doesn't seem smart to me.

The husband and I decided we wanted something new tonight. We were going to go to one of our old stand-bys, but opted for "The Brown Boxer Pub and Grille when the name popped out at me from across the street.    We got there, and it wasn't crowded. It was Open seating, which I think is a novel concept. You can sit anywhere you want, no hostess to seat you.  I've only been to one other place that does that.   We opted to sit in the -almost- patio section. Almost patio because its inside, but it's still out doors since the patio is right there and the windows are all open.    Our Waitress was very friendly, Somewhat knowledgeable and over all, helpful.   As we perused the menu we noticed one item that jumped out at us.. Boxer Balls. O....Kay. Being who we are, we just had to try them, so for an appetizer, we opted for those and the grouper nuggets.  When those were delivered, we tried them both.  The serving of the Grouper nuggets was HUGE. The fish was light and tasty, but I'm not sure if it was truly grouper. You can't be too sure these days.   As for the 'Boxer Balls" - they're apparently all the goodness in a Reuben inside fried balls.  All but the sauerkraut/cabbage, which I didn't notice much in there.   THey were tasty, but I'd probably not get them again.  Our mains were pretty simple faire: I got the French dip with a side of tator tots, and the husbeastie got the Napa Salad, which was full of fresh veg and a delicious raspberry walnut dressing.  All in all both were tasty, but I wasn't keen on the tots, they probably needed another 10-30 seconds in the oil.   We'd certainly come back, if only to try one of their fantastic after dinner drinks..

Beautiful hospital.   We were visiting a friend who was in the hospital after having surgery the night before.  The lobby is giant, the gift shop is run by some lovely ladies there. I bought a candy bar and light up kitty ears.   The ICU nurses are kind and patient, and the rooms there seemed large and comfortable, if you need that specialty care.

Stopped to use the drive through ATM.  The place was clean and neat. The ATM was in working order. It was easy to use and provided me the much needed cash I asked it for. Nothing spectacular or special.

I stopped by Home Depot after visiting my Mom because I needed to get some Fireplace Logs due to a cold snap in Florida.  I didn't find them inside, but I did find 2 associates in the aisle so I asked them where they were. I was lead to them, and the older gentleman helping me even picked them up (heavy) and put them in my cart.  The young black man who was working with him was really helpful in letting me know where I'd find the Green Gobbler for my sink.  I was able to get a gift for the husbeastie's birthday and a bunch of disposable masks as they had a great supply of PPE.

I've been a member of Suncoast for .. ever it seems.   I've not been to this location in a minute, at least since they did the remodel and took out the living tellers and set in the automated systems.  I'm not a fan.   Today I went in with the bi-anual collection of my piggy bank as I'm heading out of town this weekend and this will be my present budget.  I used their coin counter and then got in line for the next available teller.   It took two cycles and one reminder to a gentleman that "It's all one line.. " Not that he could just walk up to one of the cubbies and wait. When it was my turn, I followed the directions and ... waited again. Another wait of 5 minutes. I'm not even exaggerating. Meh.   While they were quick with the service when it actually happened, to me, this was akin to being called up to the next teller, only to watch her balance her drawer, and then do paperwork all while you stand their awkwardly waiting for her to acknowledge you.  It certainly hasn't streamlined anything, but I guess it's good for the fact no one is getting robbed.

Brand new WaWa just opened in Trinity area. We stopped here for gas so that we could fill up on our trip home from Georgia.  The pumps were clean and neat, well swept. They worked quite well.   We didn't go inside, but from the outside, the store looked clean and in good repair.

I stopped here to have lunch here with friends before heading over to Busch to ride Cobra's Curse.  This is the 2nd Little Greek place I've been in. Sadly it was not as clean as the last one I was in, however the food was Just as nice.   I opted for the Gyro platter, with fries and a soda, they gave me a little plate with pita and taziki sauce as well.  The food was fresh and tasty, and since I ordered it with out onions, it was just like I liked it.  I'd come back if I was in the area.

My guy and I stopped in because we took a one tank trip to New Port Richey and we needed a nice place to eat. I'd eaten here once before, and knew it was good food.    Today, we opted to sit on the porch, since it was a lovely autumn afternoon and it was the perfect weather to be out doors. The patio is covered and has lots of vines that protect you from people, but you can still see the street if you're interested.   We sat ourselves, but let the waitress knew we were there. She let us know she had a couple of people ahead of us, and we were cool with that, another girl came out and took our drink orders in the mean time.  When she finally came out, our waitress was extremely pleasant and friendly, she wore her mask the whole time. (Yes, they're still masked, which is awesome, they expect you to wear your mask on the inside as well.)  We placed our orders, I got their Chicken Quesidilla with black beans and rice, with homemade pico de gallo and my beau got steak and eggs. The food was fantastic, he ate everything on his plate, I couldn't finish mine, but It was really good.  I certainly recommend them if you're in town. Parking is right across the street and is free.

I was looking for a specific gift for friends who got married.  As it turned out they were unveiling the Christmas ornaments this particular week (Yes this review is being written late, sorry). The store was busy, but the ornaments were absolutely gorgeous.   I'm not one who decorates for Christmas but a little bit of my heart yearned to do so as I saw what was going to be previewed.   I did happen to find the perfect gift and they were on sale, that made me very happy. I also found some funny signs for my husband's desk. Now if only he'd employ them to keep the stress away instead of letting people walk all over him. heh.   Great store, Clean and neat and the people are really top notch.

I needed my nails done. I didn't want to go to my usual location, so I opted to go here, where I'd seen some of their work on the Hostess at Long horn's hands.  There was no wait, And they did do the dip polish like I enjoy.   The technician asked me what color I wanted, because apparently they don't have a wheel with the colors of their dip polish. I said a shiny, glittery red. They didn't have that (?) they did have all shades of neon pink but in the end I opted for a clear, but dark base with multi flash glitter within.  She took her time, and though she didn't do it the way the other location does it, my nails turned out well.   I give them a three because the walls, the floor and the stations were not spic and span. The place was kind of run down looking. But the people were friendly.

This theater is state of the art. The seats are large and comfortable, they even rock ever so lightly! The sound is pretty amazing, and the screens are still in great condition.  There's even a "cafe" in the concession area that serves coffee and sandwiches. Far better than your standard fare - though that too is offered.

Talk about your stereo typical hole in the wall bar! I'd never been inside, but we were hosting a going away party for a friend, and this was one of three locations of the night (My only stop, though).   The place was fairly large with a few pool tables, some dart boards and a few video games in the back, Other wise there was a large bar with plenty of seating, and some tables off to the wallside.   Service was really good, as were the drinks. For the inexpensive price, the drink was pretty high on the octane.  Other than the constant stink of cigarettes and some of the patron's questionable music choices, I'll probably go back.

The Castle is an Ybor City institution for all things Goth, punk and New Wave.  I went here in my 20's and well, I'm in my 40's so... yeah its been here forever.  It's an imposing structure filled with loud music. Dark moody lighting and bars that help you get into the feel of things.   The Castle consists of 5 rooms, on two floors: The Saloon, the Tower, the Courtyard, the Main hall and the Dungeon. Each has it's own look and feel, each providing it's own.. take on the place.  And there's the grand staircase, because that's how you traverse between the two floors.   Themed entertainment can be found on certain nights. The night I recently visited was the "Steampunk Ball". Normally I wouldn't go out to the Castle on a Saturday, but one of my friends, and Steampunk Royalty was in town, and he asked me to show my face, so dutifully I went. And so did a lot of other people, including Makers and crafters alike. There were so many creative souls in the place, that had tragedy struck, Tampa might well have been left a barren wasteland bereft of any beauty because it would have all been left in the rubble of the castle.   You can find their regular night list - their current theme nights on their website, thecastle.com. A couple of nights to look forward to would be StarWars night where you can bring out your inner Jedi or maybe your inner Jawa (I think that would be awesome to see)  and of course the Half way to Halloween party on May 14, which has become a Tampa ritual for those of us in the Halloween industry as a benchmark because we don't get to play with everyone else, so we claim this day.

"It's like a cleaner, fresher Mo*'s." Said the Husbeastie when we entered the establishment. And he wasn't wrong. The menu is smaller, but the items are essentially the same. The burritos, burrito bowls, taco salads, tacos and other Mexican items are variants of the same dishes available on both menus.   Fresh food is prepared and available after you tell them what you want. Once you've made your decision of item, then you add either beans or rice, the meat, and all the veggie toppings, sour cream and Guac (available for a surcharge).   It's all tasty and delicious, and VERY reasonable.

Formerly Riverwalk, the Sparkman wharf is now a lovely idea that I've seen executed very well up in New Port, Kentucky.  They have something almost identical atatched to their aquarium and walk over bridge to Cincy,Oh.  Its a nice concept and I got to be there because I was heading to the Ship for a friends and family night. I will say the parking lot is tiny, so many folks will not be happy with that. Otherwise, the offerings are pretty cool, sadly, it appears that after 8 pm they aren't open. Such is the curse of Tampa.

A stressful week needs a stressless weekend.  My beau decided we needed to have a little mindless fun so he took me to this retro arcade for adults.  It was kinda awesome if I don't say so.   Vector hasn't been open very long, but it's a nice addition for Downtown Clearwater.    There are plenty of arcade games and a nice selection of pinball games as well.  He's got a big screen set up so you can play off of another system too.   They serve beer from some local brewers and have a cold case for other drinks like Cider and wine as well as a menu for Tea and coffee, for those of us who don't often partake. The owner told me they blend their own tea. That's pretty fantastic if you ask me.   That night, they were playing some 80's music, and it was almost a trip back in time to my teens, watching my beau play and hit high score, myself, I'm ok at video games, just not that fabulous.  It was a nice evening to be sure.   I hope they continue to make a name for them selves, perhaps add a few more titles or more seats.  This business could expand and that'd be great for Down Town.

Taco Thursday has become a regular date afternoon for a good friend and I. It's pretty much the best menu out there. No, it's not $1.00 tacos, but they have a varied price, $2, $2.50 ,$3.00 + is just fine.   Regularly we'll arrive and sit inside, where the ceiling is decorated with surfboards and other beach paraphernalia. Our table is greeted by enthusiastic wait staff, and fresh chips & salsa is brought out.  My order is the pork belly tacos without onion and cilantro, it REALLY is so succulent and delicious.   My date gets the surf and turf tacos, which while not my favorite is damn tasty. I have yet to be disappointed, and I don't see THAT happening any time soon.

WOW!  We were looking for a new place to try, so I spun the yelp roulette wheel and landed on San Miguel, and I am NOT sorry.   The first thing I noticed upon walking in is how HAPPY the place feels. It's bright, warm and inviting. And then the food smells hit you and it smells good enough to make your tummy rumble.  The hostess is friendly and we were seated right away. You can make reservations, but we were late enough in the evening that we did not need to.   Our waitress was friendly, very quick to make sure nothing ran out. We ordered our drinks, which she had on the table very quickly along with some fresh chips and salsa which was delicious and fresh.  We placed our orders for the Guacamole San Miguel which is A lot of Guacamole, and our mains which were the Chicken Taco Salad and the Fajitas.    The Guacamole was Delicious, some of the best I've had that wasn't made table side. It had the perfect amount of lime. The food was fresh and tasty, and I now know where I will turn to for Mexican when the craving hits. THIS is our new favorite spot.  I knew I was in a good place when I saw the Jack-O-Lantern.

Found this place totally by accident. My friend and I decided that this was a good idea to try for both of us.   She got one of the Acai bowls with all sorts of yummy fresh fruit. It was beautiful! The colors were amazing and since we all know that we eat with our eyes, my eyes first said HUBBA!!  I had one of the savory dishes, a chicken one, it came with pineapple, carrots, seaweed salads and peppers, which I had them hold back.  WOW! It had such great flavor. I also had one of their Lattes, which was really really tasty.

CVS is central to everything and I needed to grab something quickly. I was able to run in and get just what I needed! The staff was friendly and warm, they answered the question that I had and even told me that it was on sale - all I had to do was sign up for their CVS loyalty card (already a member) and I could get a buck or two off.

Currently under renovation so the place smelled of adhesive, that made me uncomfortable in the lobby, but other than that, the theatre we were in was fine.    We saw Maleficent, Mistress of Evil, and loved it. The restrooms could use a bit better attention, but they handeled someone getting sick and throwing up very well and tended to cleaning up the mess quite quickly, once it was reported. (I hope the girl felt better.)  If i'm in the area, I will certainly visit again.

I needed a quick dinner while waiting to hear from a friend to see if it was OK to stop by. Since this was close to their location, I popped in and ordered my usual, the crispy chicken salad add almonds, with ranch on the side, and a drink.  It was ready in mere moments and I ate it at the counter.   I love watching folks as they work and this team seems to work like a well oiled machine. I like PDQ and hope they branch out to my neighborhood soon.

This is the husbeast's FAVORITE sushi place -bar none. So because we were in town, we stopped in. Me, I'm not deep into sushi, but In the past, I knew I could get something else.  Their menu is extensive, the food is beautifully presented.   We started with Goyza and Vegetable tempura, both were INCREDIBLE.  I know I shouldn't have ordered both starters, but They're both my absolute favorite, and I wasn't disappointed at all. The sauce with the goyza was just perfect. The right amount of sour to make the taste buds sing.  The Vegie tempura was light and flavourful.   The husbeast ordered A LOT of sushi, and I tried their mexican roll.  It was Alright, but again, I'm not a huge fan of the stuff, but I ate my roll.  The Chicken Teriaki was beautifully presented, bright and colorful, but a touch sweet. In the future, I probably won't order anything but starters and small plates, while the husbeast orders his sushi.  ;)

On the land that used to be the Rennaissance Festival grounds sits that Largo Cultural center.   It's a large play house with a beautiful stage, and a lovely back stage area for participants to get ready.  This was my thrid visit to the LCC, and normally I'd be the one up there preforming, but due to being sick, i was unable to be in the spotlight. Instead, i was in the very comfortable seats, directly in the middle with an excellent view of the performers putting on Ms Linda's annual production of "Steppin' Out!"  I was very pleased with the will call booth and with the restroom facilities. Everything was neat and clean.

Met up here with fellow Yelper Tiffany H at her suggestion, and I was impressed, Other than the live music (which was REALLY LOUD - and OUT Side) this place was really nice.  The coffees were delicious and the desserts looked amazingly yummy.  When I get the chance you can bet that I will be back to Everything Dolce.

We stopped here because on line it said they had wings.   We decided to empty our tanks before filling them up once more.. However the guy that was playing out in the main room... was louder in the bathrooms and actually clearer in there, than he was out in the public space.. WHAT?  Anyway, we sat down, looked at the scant menu, and then opted to leave.

There is nothing like a lazy weekend morning brunch with someone you care about, and Einstein Brother's Bagels is quickly becoming the place my beloved and I like to start those special days.   The selection, the level of service and the freshness is always fantastic, and the coffee is always hot and fresh.   We tend to go for the bagel sandwiches, but they have a bakers dozen bagel option that's out of this world. They have a fantastic selection of cream cheese and other schmears.   I look forward to the next time I can spend a leisurely visit here.

It used to be if you needed clothing of a vintage nature you went to thrift stores. Sadly that was not what I found when I went to look for pieces for a 70's costume for my husband. Oh, I'm sure they have pieces from the era, don't get me wrong, they just didn't have them in his size. in fact their men's selection seemed a little thin.  I didn't think to look at prices. One thing I did notice is that they have a large jr's section up front and a large selection of Women's Wedding Dresses that gave off a lot of sparkle and shine. So if you're looking for a discounted dress, that might be a place to check out. Happy bargain hunting!

This was probably the -worst- day to come and check them out, so I will have to come back again. Why was it the worst day? Their gas was being fixed. We stuck around anyway. I ordered one of the quiches and mom got the chicken salad.   I have to say that the chicken salad was tasty - she let me have a bite. It was served with a luscious piece of cantaloupe and some seedless watermelon. I had the ham and cheese quiche. Honestly, I wasn't impressed, I know it was re-heated with a microwave and due to the heat being out, it wasn't the best it could have been.   Like I said, I'll come back when I can give this a better review.

Clean and well organized, I used to think the "Florida Store" was for old folks.  That's simply not the case. It's an old school "department store" on one floor. They have all the essentials, including gifts and gourmet foods. Their section of accessories is bar none.  In fact today I saw something there that I've never seen before.. Metal done in the fashion of lace. It was exquisite.   There are some great seasonal sales going right now, so if you can, stop by and earn some Beall's Bucks of your own.

For the most part, Southwest is a decent enough airline. I dislike the practice of un-assigned seats. Where you have to check-in at 24 hours -on the dot- to get somewhere in a decent spot, and even then you might end up at mid B or even C row, and that guarantees you'll be sandwiched between people in the middle seats.   There's a little disclaimer on the website that spots A1-15 might still be available, if you check at the desk... FOR A PRICE. $40.00 upgrade to get those first 15 positions, but in honesty, it's worth it if you're not stuck wedged between people.   I will say this: My last flight with SWA was on Sunday (3:45 from Las Vegas - delayed due to weather from an inbound flight)  One of the flight attendants acted as though she were the Queen of the air. She snapped at at people, she acted as though it were her right to be out right RUDE, when no offense had been committed.  My offense? I didn't see her there, and she gave my coffee to someone else, when I noticed her "Well you weren't paying attention so I gave it to someone who -WAS- paying attention." in the rudest tone I think I've ever heard. She made no attempt to get my attention at all, no "Excuse me" nothing. Just an imperious attitude and a look down her nose.   The others on the flight were awesome, only this Jamiacan woman (as per her accent) was obviously having a bad day and we were all her whipping boys & girls. It's sad really, because if it weren't for her, this might have been a higher review.

I popped into Maggiano's to visit a friend, unfortunately, and unknown to me, he wasn't working today. Oh well.. it was lunch time, so I ordered my stand by meal of Chicken Parm and waited.    My waiter, Daniel, was very nice, he made sure that everything was just how I wanted it. When my food came out, it was piping hot and absolutely delicious. My entree was huge. 2 large fillets of chicken, lightly breaded and fried with provolone and sauce, and a side of spaghetti with red sauce.   It was SO good too! I have only been to Maggiano's once before and only remember it being family style, so this was a nice change!

We had to stop. The husband saw a 3 wheeled Indian vehicle out front so we stopped.   If you're looking for doors, for windows, for old wrought iron, you will find it here. If you're looking for brass hinges, for impact pieces that are from old homes and previously distressed, it's probably here. I saw the fuselage of a plane, some old piece of a wheel that got my mind spinning. There were banquettes made out of car parts. Indeed this i most certainly an awesome place to shop and dream

I'm familiar with another location, so when my date suggested this location for our date night,  I agreed. After all, Its right across the street from B&N. What could be better?  We arrived and walked in, after a few minutes to look at the paper menu, we placed our orders: He got the Bacon cheese burger, I got the Black & Blue wedge salad and we shared an order of fries.   The one thing that we noticed is that He ordered his burger med. Well, and what he got was a burger that was unevenly cooked. One half was cooked appropriately, the other half was more med. rare.  And this is.. while not fine, it was ok. We figured that the burger must have been on the edge of the grill.   My salad was quite tasty, three small blackend slider patties served in a bowl, atop a large serving of lettuce, diced tomato, bacon and bleu cheese, drizzled with ranch dressing. THe portion was large and very filling.   The tables hadn't been bussed in some time, so finding a clean table was hard, but finally someone came out and cleaned off the ones that were filled with dirty plates and what have you, opening up tables for people to sit at.   The employees who work there, Especiall Jason (Tall blonde guy who was at register and bussing tables) Were especially friendly.

Saturday, 11:15 and we're waiting for a table? Not because they're busy, but because their hostess isn't behind the stand, she's in the back, behind the bar, doing other things, not doing -her- job.  It wasn't just us, it was two other groups too.    When we were sat, we had an excellent waiter. Seymour (yes, the "little Shop Of Horrors" jokes were not lost on us either) made sure our orders were taken and our food was gotten to us quickly. After all, we had a movie to catch.   Since the menu change, Ruby Tuesday really is nothing more than mediocre. The food was tasty but nothing to write home about.

Why was I here? It's not a store I'd usually go to. Sports stores hold no allure for me... but I had to go here because they alone held my T-shirt and my number for the Foam Glow 5k. So  .... I did what I had to do: Fight wicked traffic from my home city all the way to Brandon, during Rush Hour (oh god!) and followed the purple arrows on the floor all the way to the back. The sign in procedure was quick and easy and so was the getting of the exttras. That was all fine and good...   What disappointed me was.. Looking through the racks and noticing that much of the yoga clothing ended at size Lg. Granted I can wear this now, but Very few XL and not a single XXL. So I'm guessing that you're not allowed to wear stylish clothing if you're larger and want to exercise. I find this an annoying thing that stores do.

This place is an institution in St. Pete. I've known about it for over 40 years. I've passed by it at least 100 times. But I've never had that chance to stop in until recently.   We stopped in on a Friday evening, it was just before the car show, so parking was a premium. We sat near the bar, under the fans to help alleviate some of the summer heat.  Our waitress was friendly and efficient, so I was confused when our meals came out at different times.   We ordered an Ap of cheese curds, the Prime rib special (a 14 oz ((more like 24 oz)) cut, veg of the day, baked potato and bread for $15.99) and 2 chili cheese dogs with tater tots.   The cheese curds came out with cold marinara. They were good.  But almost immediately the prime rib came out with the waitress saying that it was good it came up so fast because they'd been behind all day.  We waited another 15 minutes for two chili cheese dogs. Those were just OK. I kind of get squicked if my hamburger in my chili isn't all nearly uniform pieces - and in this case I got a HUGE chunk of meat. It put me off the food.   All in all, it was Ok. My friend eating the prime rib said it was delicious and the cut of meat was gigantic. more than the 14 oz they claimed.

What a neat little place. No it's not 4 star dining, but it's not meant to be. This little diner, tucked along alternate 19 is a sleeper, a place where you go because you've been going for 25 years. Where the regulars are known and the waitstaff automatically bring their drinks to the table. Where when it's their birthday, the chef makes special pancakes for them!  The food was simple, but good! I had a bacon/egg/cheese wrap, which was far larger than I expected. The husband had a double bacon cheese burger with fries. Also far larger than we expected. No, not fresh ground beef, probably those patties that they get from SYSCO, but still tasty.   The staff was very friendly, very attentive. We weren't even sure they were open today, but they were, until 2pm. Since we arrived at 1:15, they were more than accommodating to us. Our cups never went empty and the food came out -very- quickly. It certainly was fresh and delicious.  I know that I'll come back and try them for another meal.

I -LOVE- bookstores! It comes from the fact that I used to work in one. Now I just can't keep away from them.  B&N is one of the last Large Brick and Mortar stores and they manage to carry so many good things..   They have a large selection of gifts and gadgetry too! I especially like their bargain section and the journals that they carry. Finding a hand tooled (at least it looks that way) leather bound journal is just the perfect gift for an aspiring writer.   Today I came in to find something for my newest passion, and find it I did. Adult coloring books are all the rage, and they had them in spades. I managed to pick up three of them, along with the newest release from Laurell K. Hamilton. YAY, I'm a happy me!

What better way to end the day than with ice cream.   Personally I think $11.75 (ish, going by memory) is a bit expensive for 2 ice creams, but I paid it.   We were offered samples, and the gentleman behind the counter was polite and friendly.  Our ice cream was tasty and quickly provided to us.

CHAI!!!  I swear sometimes that's my battle cry.  This day it was. After all, I was meeting a friend to pick up some clothing I'd left with her at the Ren Faire.   We met up at this starbucks and the ordering process was quick, efficient and quite friendly. The prices were absolutely like they were everywhere else.. and of course, the quality was just fine.  This location is easily accessable right off of Dale Mabry.

A former Home Haunt, they had too many people coming to their house that the City of Tampa made them move to a bigger location.  Fair enough.   They bill themselves as the "Most Extreme Haunted House in Tampa", and as a veteran haunter, I don't think I can say that's accurate. They're good, don't get me wrong. They've obviously put a lot of work into the venue. They've got a lot of money invested, but they've got a lot of work to do, to become "EXTREME".  What is EXTREME, anyway?  To me, extreme is something that pushes boundaries. Nothing in this house pushed boundaries. You had all your typical haunt effects. You had a LOT of things hanging from the ceilings, you had your expanding walls and you had your pop scares.  You even had a child. But.. no one touched you, there was no re-direction, there was nothing of an extreme element except maybe the volume of the music and sound effects.   Overall, they get a B for effort.  Their costuming and makeup was on point and I LOVED that they gave the history up front. Kudos. Keep on bringing the game and you will get there.  The $10 admission fee was a bit steep for the 5 minute walk through, but with no line, it was Ok.

Dude, seriously... you'd think that the State Fair would hire people who know what they're doing. Obviously it's lowest bidder time.  I just had the pleasure of attending the Funshine Music Festival on opening day.  Getting parked, no big deal.  Getting in the gate? HOLY MOTHER OF MOSES! And worse? Getting OUT of the place.  I nearly got hit twice because of the doofus "directing" traffic, didn't have a clue what he was doing. He'd guided me, and then guided another car almost directly INTO me.   It's not just for this event stuff like this happens, it's every time I come to the Fairgrounds. Even the vendors who were running the booths out on the midway couldn't decide what the price of water was. In one booth on center line it was $4.00 and the next one beside it it was $2.00, both run by the same company. *face Palm*
