After having been treated to SPY by Yelp, I returned here to see Poltergiest, the re-boot with my old friend and his partner. I was pleased with the movie, and happy to see that the theater was large and comfortable. The snacks were well provided for and they even use the new coke machines.

Become a member of the club, you'll get money off gas for your first 30 days. Plus with every fill up you'll get a special offer, You really can't beat that.  The representitives inside are pretty awesome, very friendly and they have almost every soda known to god at their soda bar in the back.   The gas pumps are clean and shiny, very comfortable to use.

We arrived with a large party on a Friday night. Yes, we took up the center table and it seemed like a lot of the patrons didn't like us there. Why? 8 people, talking, sharing boxed wine (What? Don't judge, it's apparently pretty good.. I didn't have any) and enjoying each others company.   The food and service was alright, well.. the service was a bit slow, but the food was damned fine.

New fast food place in Port Richey, I decided to give it a try on my way home from Atlanta.   The drive through was quick, I placed my order and though it was later on a Sunday evening, the girl at the menu box was both professional and polite. I special ordered my burger with no condiments but pickles and knew if they got that right (most don't) it would be good.   Once I paid, I was given a number to put on my mirror and pulled up just past the trashbin to wait.  The wait wasn't that long, and my food came out. Yes, it was right. The only reason they're not getting a 5 is that the fries were old and hard. Not really that tasty. But the burger was good.

Dinner on Third Friday and everyplace was packed. We made our way to Marker 39 and were pleased that there was no wait and we were seated immediately.   The ambiance is lovely, a cross between beachy and artsy, with a lovely outdoor porch if you're into that sort of thing. (misquitos and I don't get along, so we sat inside)  We both ordered a Cider and perused the menu. The service was awesome as we decided on a shrimp appetizer - which was tasty, but for $11 I expected a bit more than 5 shrimp.   Our dinner salads were very petite, and by very petite I mean surprisingly small.  Dinner was delicious though. I ordered the Pulled pork over rice and my husband had a salad with some form of fish. Each plate had unique flavors that were exceptionally combined. Even the Kimchee slaw..   We would certainly come again.

After stopping at Tribecca to get my hair done, I was hungry - three hours in the stylist chair will do that to you, so I drove down Kennedy, and popped into Ducky's. I didn't know what to expect, but what I was met with, was wall to wall tv's, blaring sports at me.  (YAWN)  I was seated immediately, and within moments, my waitress came over, she was quite pleasant and told me the specials (Their burgers were $6.00) and offered me a beverage. I ordered their all american burger and added on fried onion rings and fried pickles ( $1.00 each)  It didn't take long but when it arrived, it looked really good, and was cooked to perfection. I'm sad to say I got 2 fried onion rings and 1 fried pickle for a buck each.. That's over priced for that small amount of add on.   However there was a generous portion of Fries, and the burger was simply amazing. For my Fries and burger, my drink ,it cost me less than $10.00 Not bad for a really good meal.

I've been tyring to get to Green Springs Bistro for a while now, and finally had a chance to go there with a couple of my dance girls after class.   On a Thursday evening, we were happy that we were sat immediately, no reservation required. The tables and walls are covered with art. Our table had "The Lion Sleeps Tonight" lyrics painted on it. Clearly this place is very cheery.   As we perused the menu (and it's kinda pricy) the waitress/hostess brought around samples of the Mushroom bisque for us all to try, compliments of the chef. I thought that was nice. We placed our orders, each of us opting to do a tapas style meal, Crab Cakes, Flat Bread or in my case the Mushroom caps with goat cheese.  The food was good, but I will admit, it was priced too high. 2 portabella mushroom caps with goat cheese, red peppers and a bit of olive were $10.00. I can see that for 4 of them, but not 2.   The flavours though, combined delightfully though.

Decided to try Ford's Garage on a whim with my Beau. We'd tossed a coin to choose our destination for dinner.  There was no wait and we were seated immediately.   The decor was whimsical and fun and we enjoyed the way the horn at the bar would go off when someone tipped the tenders well.  We perused the menu and placed our drink orders, I chose a Strawberry Lime cider from Sweden, that when delivered Mr. P said smelled like a jolly Rancher, and it was TASTY.   We also ordered coffee and water. The coffee was lukewarm and the water was perfect.   We started our meal with their version of fried pickles, because some how, while living in the south, Mr. P has never had them.  Theirs were lightly fried like Japanese Tempura, and so tasty with the two dipping sauces.  We ate them slowly because they were so hot, but they were so good. My Beau is now convinced that Fried Pickles are delicious.   Our burgers were placed, I don't remember the names of our burgers, since they were named after local celebs, but I chose the black N' bleu burger and he got the one topped with the fried onions and puled pork..  Both of them were done to perfect medium well, juicy and messy  Each was dressed with tomato and lettuce of course and served on their own specific type of bun.  Mine was on a pretzel bun with grilled onions and a lot of bleu cheese crumbles. What an explosion of taste in the mouth.   The serving of fries on the side was good, they could have been crispier, but they were ok.   Over all, we're looking forward to making this place a spot where we go over and over. We liked it a lot.

Stopped at Cheddar's with the paramour. The food was.. what I expected, it was nothing fantastic, but it was adequate. I will say this for them, they only have 2 settings on their ac. It is either ice cold or really warm there is apparently no comfortable setting.

I needed breakfast before I flew home. O'Charley's looked like a nice spot. It wasn't far from my gate and wasn't terribly busy either.  I was escorted to a table and chair and offered a menu. After placing my drink order- I opted for one of their hand crafted strawberry Lemonades (tasty!) I placed my order for their over load: 6oz grilled steak, Eggs, bacon, sausage, potatoes and toast. I ordered this even though I knew I wouldn't eat half.   It arrived at my table, and though the state was just a touch over done, It was tasty. The eggs were perfection and the potatoes were SO good. The bacon.. It didn't look or taste right. It really reminded me of beggin' strips. So i don't think it was Real Pork apple wood smoked bacon. It was just off. And thier sausage was SO SPICY. but tasty.   As I expected, I didn't eat hardly a 1/3 of it but I ate the steak, some of the eggs, some of the sausage and all the potatoes. THe service was wonderful and I was even given a cup of the strawberry lemonade to go.

I came looking for something to eat, I'd been here in the past and was hoping for something GOOD. What I got was Ok.   I decided I didn;t want breakfast fare, but opted for Coffee to drink anyway. No less than 3 people touched my table in some way or another.  First, I watied more than 5 minutes to be seated. Not because they were busy, I came at 1:30 pm. I waited because there was no one on the floor. The waitstaff was doing end of day work, the one lady bussing tables was busy and finally the Manager sat me. He asked me what I wanted to drink, I told him coffee..   A few minutes later, a waitress comes to my table and asks what I wanted to drink.. I told her coffee too. *shrug* Ok. Anyway, the coffee was delivered, and it smelled and tasted rich and decadent.   When I ordered my food, I opted for an open faced chicken salad sandwich (Topped with mozz cheese and tomato slices) and a bowl of tomato/basil soup.   The food came quickly and was delivered by the third person, a gentleman, who I asked for a glass of water from. That came quickly too, but no in the standard milk bottle, he just brought me a glass.   The food was tasty. The Basil tomato soup was good, but lacked depth. What could have made it better would have been croutons and parmesan cheese. I asked for some, and the waitress said she didn't have any parmesan cheese in the place - this despite their menu having one or more dishes offering that cheese as an ingredient.  The sandwich was tasty, nothing to write home about.   All in all, the food is Ok. I might try again, i might not.

I only come to this hotel one weekend a month for an event that a group that I come to hosts. They hotel staff is very friendly and accommodating towards us. I'm happy to say that I will attend the event as long as it's here.

Newly opened, and much needed, Lowe's Home Improvement is right off of us 19 in Tarpon, close to Main Street.   What brought me in? I needed a chain saw to tame my back yard, it's truly become a jungle and only a chainsaw is going to tame the trees as they've begun to close in on the house.  The agents are friendly, the stock is immense and the store is clean. What more could you ask for??

I attended the Riverside Grille for a Halfa - a bellydance community event.   While the space was quite nice, the food options were quite limited.  There was a buffet that was lukewarm,  which consisted of a salad with 3 dressing options. 3 potato choices, a seafood w/salmon option, 2 chicken options and bread. Dessert was brought to your table, a choice of 2 options of cheese cake and a chocolate item.  It wasn't bad, nor was it over priced, but it was.. just -ok-.  The service was alright, the waitresses were overwhelmed and so it was a bit slow, but the view was incredible. We were able to see the lovely ladies dance, and look out as the sun set over the waters at Tarpon Springs.   It is sad that the venue is closing. Otherwise this could really be a great place.

My friend Corrin - a new Yeper had had a bad day,and since  our husbands work together and were doing a presentation tonight and that left us either alone, or we could hang together, we opted for the later. So because she had a bad day, I wanted to take her someplace neither of us had been.   I asked my dentist for a suggestion since I didn't know the area past Sunset point road all that well, and he suggested Johnny's. He warned me about all the garlic and told me that I'd become addicted to the Johnny bread. MAN was he right.   We arrived a little before 6:30 and the parking lot was FULL. I'm serious, there were very few places to park, but we both found spots out back and met inside. Our waitress resembled Elsa with a bit too much eyeliner, but other than that, she was phenomenal! She was always on point, never let our drinks go dry and checked on us, even with her huge section that was full of people.   We started out with the Johnny bread, of course and their famous "Sauce" which they make in house, daily - the dipping sauce is an amalgam of olive oil, spices and cheeses, which is deliciously thick and tasty. They also make all their own pasta sauces there in house too! Quite a feat in today's day and age.   We ordered a Caprese salad to start, thick slices of beefsteak tomato with mozzerella cheese, bits of basil and of course basalmic reduction for us to ad at will. it was fresh and tasty. They also brought us out our Pasta Fajolie (sp) soup, and it was killer. Now, mind you, most of the PF soup's I've had in the past have meat of some sort in them, this one did not, but I don't think it was missing anything.   Our main courses were (Corrin) Chicken tetrazini, in a wine butter sauce, served with fettucinni alfredo. - the chicken looked delicious and she gave me a bit to taste, it was tender and flavorful. Myself, i got the chicken parm. and it was good, the only thing I wasn't particularly fond of was the side of linguini. I don't reallyt eat pasta, so that sat on the side of my plate untouched.   When we were done eating, and our left overs were waiting to be boxed up, I perused the menu for desserts, Corrin asked if there was anything made of chocolate, Well, yes there was, a flourless chocolate cake, so we ordered one to share. It was a decadent treat. To cut through the cloying sweetness, we ordered espresso. Since they were out of demitasse cups, she gave us an extra half shot of espresso since the cups were so large and the coffee amount looked silly in the cup.   I would happily return. This place is busy!!

I was craving MEAT, roasted meat.. and this was half way between mom & I so I took her here for lunch.   We both ordered a pulled pork plate, 2 sides and the endless salad bar.   The service was good, if a bit slow. I'd blame it being on Sunday, but the place wasn't busy.   When we did get out plates for the salad bar, I kinda wish we didn't. First, the salad mix was Ice burg lettuce, and there was a side bowl - the size of a soup bowl- that was of another mix and it was almost empty. I took those mixed greens. I added a bit of the cucumbers, some egg, some black olives, and when I went to get the corn, it was.. Goopy. Yes goopy, like it had gel in it. It was.. Gross. The other offerings from the salad bar were equally disappointing, the Tuna salad - lumped together and discolored, the potato salad, not even going to try it. Only the macaroni salad.. it seemed edible.   The rest of the food came quickly, it was tasty and fresh, but the Salad bar was disgusting.

Small, but very nice, happy making airport. Music City indeed. The gates are neat, but close to each other, there are a lot of choices when it comes to eating, and drinking. They have more than a few little gift shops and boutiques.  I loved hearing the live music everywhere, and found that their baggage claim area was neat and easy to get your baggage from. I hope to visit this airport again soon.

I'm glad I found this place! I never knew this place existed, and with Features closing/closed, finding a costume shop that caters to just about everything is kind of hard to find.   What drew me in was a costume sale, up to 50% off older costumes. Sadly much of what they had wasn't my style, but I did look around. I was pleased to find that they had a WHOLE lot of stockings, Ben Nye Make up, Facial appliances and the like.   They carried the standard "Sexy ____" costumes, as well as more elaborate set ups, Lots of varied styles and quality. From the cheap to the expensive you'll find it there. And it seems they carry a great selection of things for Gasparilla too! Lots of pirate tack up at the front to the store.   From Steam Punk to Super heroes, Freddy Kreuger to Woodland Fairy they carry just about everything you could imagine. Boas, Stockings, and all the accessories in between. Stop by, they're just off Park Blvd, the Purple building kind of stands out.   OH! And if you like a surprise, they have grab bags! For a buck, you could get some trinkets like vampire teeth, a mardi-gras coin or a bendy-alien or you might win a $25 gift certificate. I just LOVE grab bags!

After picking up my brother at the tuckstop on his Birthday, I wanted to take him for Lunch. Since he'd never been to PDQ, it was my choice to go there.  We ordered the 4 strip basket and my usual salad with bacon and almonds added.   The food was up quickly and tasted as fresh and delicious as usual.  I LOVE PDQ. I really wish there was a location closer to Tarpon Springs. I hate that I have to go to Tampa or Clearwater to enjoy this place.

The South Tampa location is where I first became aware of Fit Life foods. Their behind the scenes tour was pretty amazing.  It was interesting to see how things like Alfredo sauce is made - since it's not "cheesy".  I liked finding out how the meat was taken care of, and being able to taste a few of the entrees fresh.   If you've never tried Fit Life foods, I suggest you do, you will NOT be disappointed!

I'm glad there's a 2nd location. This one is closer to me!  We like the newly renovated place, it's got that great rustic feel with the Edison lights and the slightly Steampunk feel, but when it comes down to it, none of that matters. What maters is the food and the service and they've got that covered!  Our waitress was awesome, Always smiling and right on the ball with our drinks. We never went below half full.   We started with our usual app of the buffalo cauliflower which is hands down delicious. I really need to learn how to make this.  We devoured it with gusto.   Next we had our mains.  The husbeast had his salad and I had a french dip sandwich. Both of these are not what we usually go with, but with the new location, we opted for something different. We were not disappointed.  And since we were at the new location, we decided to do dessert too! Their Peanutbutter chocolate pie was amazeballs.   Will I be back? That's a hell ot the yes.

Most certainly a newer location for a TJ Maxx, still shiny and chrome!  Lots of high end purses, designer labels along the walls and by far more luggage than I've EVER seen in any of the TJ Maxx or Marshall locations, quite the selection.   Still well organized, they had the best selection of makeup and clothing I've seen in a very long time. If this were closer I'd be a frequent shopper.

I'm in the south, I want GOOD BBQ, I'm going to go where the locals go. This apparently ranks high!  We walked in after taking a Lyft here, and were not disappointed! The scent alone made my tummy rumble.  We walked right in and looked at the menu, both of us placing an order for the 1/2 rack of ribs with 2 sides : potato salad and green beans.   The dry rub on the meat with a bit of their mild sauce made my day. OH MAN the meat was fall off the bone tender. The flavour of the beans and potato salad was SO good.  Yep. Another favorite in a city. I'll be back!

Ok, the ONLY reason I stopped at Burger King was to get a Diet Coke.   First things first: A medium diet coke was $2.63??!!!  Holy cow.  Secondly: When I paid, I asked for a receipt. I don't know why, I just did. I'm glad I did. When I got to the expedition window the girl, Mariah handed me a COKE. I asked, "Diet"?  and the conversation went like this? "No, Coke, you didn't order Diet." I looked at my receipt, it said DIET.  I showed it to her. "What number is that?" "15" "Huh.. " she speaks indistinctly to the manager in the background.. "What else did you order." "Nothing, Just the medium diet coke, lite ice." She looks confused. Clearly they have both paper and monitor to look at the order, I' not sure where the issue is coming into play.. but there was an issue.   FINALLY I'm handed a Medium Diet Coke, that I paid $2.63 for and GOOD God, it has lots of ice in it.. *eye roll* for the love of all things holy...

I first visited Iavarone's over 13 years ago when the husbeastie and I were dating.  Seeing that it is now our 10th wedding anniversary, we figured that it was about time to go back.  We stopped in before 5 pm on 5/12 and were asked if we had a reservation. We did not, so we were sat in the bar area, which is fine with us, the tables there were just perfect.   We looked over the menu, made a decision to have drinks, an appetizer and our mains. When the waitress came around, I placed an order for a Chocolate Martini, the husbeastie had Unsweet Iced tea. While we waited for the drinks to come, we were served bread with olive oil and olive paste with herbs. This was delicious.   The Chocolate Martini was decadent! Delicious indeed.   We then placed our orders for the Bruschette , the NY Strip and the Lasagne. Both came with a salad, I ordered the house salad and the husbeast got the lasagne.  There wasn't much time to wait before out salads were delivered. The ceaser was light and delightful the croutons were huge and crispy. The house was light and tasty and not much different from the ceaser save the huge wedge of tomato and the green olives.   When the appetizer of bruschette came out, we were pleased, large crostini heaped with fresh tomato, garlic and onion. The flavors were bright and danced on the palate. So good!  When the mains were delivered I had gone to the restroom (very nice there too),but I passed the Waitress by on the way back and she let me know she'd just delivered the food to our table.  Imagine my surprise when I saw that the husbeast had already eaten 1/4 of his lasagne.   The red sauce was a bit spicy but so good. The steak was cooked to a perfect medium and the potato was excellent, topped with bacon bits, cheese, chives, butter and sour cream. It was out of this world.   A great dinner, with tip came to under $100.   And at the end of it, another Chocolate martini was delivered, apparently the original ticket didn't get removed, so instead of wasting it, they gave it to us for free!   We'll not let another decade pass before we return.

Ok, When I think of a place called a "Mexican Grille" This is not what I think of.  To me, a grille is a place where you have table service and you sit down and eat. This however is more like Moe's, where you order your tacos or burritos and have them fill it with the toppings you want.   The food was tasty, the servings were huge.  My mom and I did have to wait because the cashier was chatting with a customer and the other person up front was milling around behind, listening to her, we, however were clueless as to what to do as it's not intuitive.   Their guacamole is delicious.

I wanted wings tonight! I was going to drive all the way to Hooters in Clearwater, but the husbeast didn't want to do that at all, so we debated where to go and opted to BWW over Ker's.  Parking was a pain in the ass, but when we finally found a spot, it was relatively close.  We walked in and waited to be seated. The lady before us wanted a seat for 25, and our host said he'd get someone on that, he went ahead and seated us, a more manageable party of 2.  We were sat near a party of VERY LOUD teens, and just beneath a HUGE TV.  The tv didn't bother me, the teens though? No one had ever apparently taught them ANYTHING about being out in a group. Or maybe they had and they jsut tossed everything out the window. What ever it was, I tried to ignore them and their behaviour. I was good, I didn't yell at them, but I wanted to. LORD how I wanted to.   We ordered fried pickles - the last time I was at a BWW, they were pretty rancid, not crispy and just pathetic. This time, they were pretty good.  THough we did ask the waitress for regular ranch, it never came.   We ordered Mild wings for me and the new GHOST PEPPER Wings for the husbeast. They came quickly and they were both very good. He managed to devour his, I ended up taking half of mine home.

I came in looking for a 24K gold plated Curling Iron by Paul Mitchel. Yes I know that sounds like a terribly frivilous purchase, but so far, that's the only thing that has made my hair curl and keep a curl.  Sadly the store does not carry Paul Mitchel, but they do carry other brands.   The 1" curling iron by the "top selling brand" as stated on the packaging was on sale for $29.99 so I picked it up. That's actually a fairly good deal, so I'll give it a 30 day tril and see what I think.   The store was well stocked, clean and the employees were courteous as well as funny, after I caught one dancing to a popular tune on the radio. "I always get caught by the customers" Indeed you do, and you're good natured about it too! Nice to share a laugh sith some one!

While it was convieinent to have everything I needed neatly in the store, and easily accessed off the road at a lighted intersection, I found it incredibly disheartening to hear the cashier say - out loud and NOT terribly under her breath "Well I THOUGHT I'd get some shopping done." as if my being in the store and needing to check out was ruining her day.

Brand new location of the Twistee Treat franchise.  It took them, what seems like, forever to put this in, but now that it's here, it's a great addition to the plaza.   The service was quick, when my beau ordered us both twists dipped in chocolate. We opted to sit out in the chairs and enjoy a late afternoon snack in the summer sun.   We watched one of the employees set up corn hole and hula hoops for the kids that were around.   Over all, a nice place to visit, wether you have kids or not.

Do not stay here... ever. Not all RRI's are bad, but this one is disgusting.  If I could give less than 1 star, I would.  This place was a hell hole.  Let me begin by saying that when I checked in, the person behind the desk was OK. She was very nice.  The first room I checked into was absolutely DISGUSTING. The wet, heavy scent of mold permeated the air. There were stains on one of the bed covers. They weren't small stains either, they were the size of a dinner plates.  There was also a blood stain on one of the bed covers the size of a dime.  Yes, a blood stain.   The bathroom was equally disgusting. The cover was off the fan unit on the wall, and the innards of the fan were exposed, everything covered in a thick layer of dust and who knows what.  Inside the bathtub there was a wad of hair and god knows what else.  I was skeeved.  This was intolerable, especially when they say that these are "All New Rooms". Clearly the NEW only means the paint on the walls.   I went up to the front desk and let the clerk know of the situation at hand. She moved me towards another room. This room also smelled of mold, but not as badly. The beds were at least clean, but the big issue with this room was... ABSOLUTELY no towels. How did this happen? All I had was a single washcloth.  So once more I had to walk up front and speak to the clerk. I realize that it's not her fault, but she didn't have any towels to give me, save a small stack that had been sitting up front.  I ended up getting 2 towels and 3 floor mats.   This was such a disastasterous experience that I ended up putting the chair before the door and hoping that I wouldn't end up dead, and this is where we ended up getting our final surprise: there were a pair of panties on the floor. They didn't belong to me or my room mate, so apparently they'd been left beneath the chair, along with the dog kibble.  Clearly, Housekeeping has failed to do their job here.     I will not be staying at another Red Roof Inn again.

LUSH!!  This is by far my personal splurge! I love their bath stuff. Their bombs and fizzies and everything in between. Anything and everything that can go in water to make it smell nice and make my skin soft that's hand made and not tested on animals? Yep, that's Lush and I buy it.   I just picked up 3 of the new, but limited ones for the spring season, and I'll be sad when their gone. *sad face* but I'll have fun using them.    So if you're a bath fanatic, come try Lush.

i need to get out of the Fitness Rut I'm in, so after seeing a friend's commentary on their gym, I stopped into Planet Fitness, since they're 5 miles from my home.  They have a lot of contemporary equipment. But they also have different areas, they have an AB concentrated area, they have a stretching concentration area, and an area that's similar to Curves.  As well as all your Cardio and free weights. I like that. I went for the premium membership so $19 a month.. (and I get the aqua-massage and tanning) isn't a bad investment in my self.

Opened 7 months ago, and they're slowly accruing quite a clientele.  Mostly serving breakfast and lunch they offer a special every day. So far, I've stopped in for breakfast on the way to Ren Faire, and I can tell you that you will NOT find any better home fries ANYWHERE. They were delicious.  I've also stopped in for Lunch on their $5 burger Monday's.  They're not kidding, those burgers are HUGE. One caveat, tell them if you want the burger more done than medium. I was fine but my mom likes things a touch more well done.  The onion rings are to die for!     The service is always friendly & they're pet kind too, so bring your pups and let them enjoy the atmosphere too. OH! and they have a poker club that meets on Thursday nights, if that's something you're into, by all means, check them out!

I've got to admit, it was the name that caught our attention! The husbeast and I had a snicker over it but we decided to go ahead and give it a try.   We arrived at prime dining time on Friday evening, and though the place was hopping, we were seated in what appeared to be their 2nd dining room, not the room with the little nooks and private booths, but the open tables, and this was all well and good.  We were given our menus and given a chance to peruse what was available.   Some time passed, I'd estimate more than 5 minutes before the waitress came over and took our order, but when she did, she got everything; drinks, starters and mains.  I was impressed, she didn't write anything down.  A few minutes passed and she brought out our drinks - Jasmine tea for me and unsweet iced tea for the hubster.  Our starters came out a few minutes later, mine was Chicken Sat-eh and his was Tom Yum Ka soup. Both were pleasant enough, but the chicken was under seasoned and the soup was sort of bland.  When the waitress was walking by, I noticed she had a drink on her tray, a Thai Coffee, and I asked about it, she brought one by for me on her next round, it was heavenly! The service here was by far some of the fastest and best I've had in a long time.  Our mains arrived, mine was the House Combination Fried Rice (Notice a trend when I go to Thai places?) and my guy got Spicy Fried Rice - Thai Hot. Both were presented prettily with carrots and cabbage as a garnish. While the portions weren't as large as other local places, they were generous, and the food was delicious. There was a silkyness to the rice that was sublime.  And according to the husbeast, the thai hot was right on.   Would we go back? Certainly. With food that good, and service to die for, you can bet they've got a couple of new regulars.

I've always loved 5 guys, but after last night they really get my vote.   I went there with my visiting Scot, and he has a peanut allergy, but we didn't think anything of it even though 5 guys has Peanuts all around.  It was only after looking around that we realized that perhaps the fries were cooked in the oil. Much to our chagrin, they are.  Not only does my friend not get to eat those delicious fries, they could kill him.   I explain the dilemma, and the cooks understood. They explained that his current burger, wrapped in the foils, was covered by the fries, but they would go ahead and re-make his burger for him.  He was able to have one of their delicious burgers after all.

Near Citrus Park Mall, it's on the way home from Howl-O-Scream so I stop on occasion.  They are slower than most fast food places, but that's because they're getting the food made to order.   The only thing that usually disapppoints me is that they almost always give me cool fries. I HATE cold fries. YUCK@

Mall food. But it was quick and reasonable. I ordered the bourbon chicken plate, with two sides. What I ordered was supposed to be "Mixed Vegs" but it turned out to be cabbage, green beans and the bourbon chicken. The green beans seasoned with garlic but there was no actual flavor. The Chicken was tasty and the cabbage was.. it was cabbage.   I would not eat there again.

Once in a while I get a wild hair... today was that day.   The last time I was there, I had remember that there was a shop that had tiara's and I wanted to share it with a friend of mine.  The shop was still there, but alas, they didn't have many tiaras this time.   There were, however, trips back in time. In one particular shop, as we perused the goods, we came across things that we each had had in our youths.  I personally remember the Nescafe globe coffee cups - Mom still has them. There were Disney Glasses and even boxed drink glasses from the now defunct (world famous) Lous Pappas Resturaunt at the Tarpon Springs Sponge Docks.   We found boxed sets of VHS tapes of the Highlander. Juke Boxes and a lot of ... well there's no way to say it.. CRAP.  And of course there is the import store: the cheap stuff imported from China, they take up several areas and are filled with well... EVERYTHING. I actually found metal decorated claw clips for $1, so I bought 10 of them. They look pretty in my hair!  I also learned what I could do with my used CD's  - make a religious icon!  On the way out, They had a delicious selection of local strawberries - YES! it's almost strawberry season, and I bought a half flat!

I saw a friend of mine visit this the other day, so I just had to go here.  When I walked in I thought that I had walked into Egg Harbor, a cafe in Atlanta. I even asked the hostess if they were partners, because the coffee cups and the decor are identical, the logo is only slightly different.   We were seated, and the table was sticky, I had to ask that it be wiped down.  The hostess and our waitress (One in the same) Took care of that immediately, and then she wandered away. It took a little bit of time for her to come back, but when she did, she took our orders, asking if we wanted an appetizer (With breakfast?) We said no and then we placed our order for: The Hawaiian French Toast platter and the Laffitte Tortilla.   When the Hawaiian French Toast came I was kind of disappointed, I expected it to be .. different. I mean it was simply Kings Hawaiian Bread sliced and made into french bread - tastes the same as Challah bread. I was kind of expecting a macadamia nut sauce or even pineapple but no go. Otherwise it was good. The husbeastie's tortilla was good, he said it was thick and full.  The price was a bit pricey, but the flavours were good. We'd come back.

Recently I received a notice in the mail stating that my card was to be suspended due to the activities of some unscrupulous lout on Black Friday.  But I shouldn't fear! No!  I would get a new card in the mail by 2/18, and until then my compromised card would still work.  Here we are on 2/18 and I've still not received my card.  So I did the dutiful thing and called the bank. According to them, I have an OLD ADDRESS on file.    How can this be? I changed my address IN PERSON at the local branch when my last card expired 8 months ago and I'd not received the replacement.  I know that it was changed because not only did I receive the NEW card then, but the POS Verification for Zip code now works with the proper one.     After explaining this to the girl on the phone she had no answer.  She will send me a new card, shipped via Fed Ex to the Proper Address. It should be here by Friday morning and someone will have to sign for it. I'm OK with that.  I just don't get how their systems aren't communicating with each other.   The address was changed, I did it in person. I know that I've received a replacement card at my current address before... so... the issue is on their end. They need to work harder at making things seamless for their customers. I don't like having to wait now for my card to come in.

Why oh why did I wait until the last minute to go to Target?  I needed something for my Christmas dinner tomorrow, Target was on my way home from Tampa so I stopped in. For a Super Target, this place is well organized and unusually clean for tonight's date. I was impressed.

A friend of mine told me that this TJ Maxx location was one that you could find things at, that you could find no where else. Since it was the ONE location in the Tampa Bay area i didn't hit before Christmas, I decided to put her information to the test.   The store is neat and clean, and given that this is the week after Christmas, that's a feat. Especially when there's a storewide clearance going on.  But my friend didn't exaggerate at all. I found things there that I didn't find at any of the other locations. Like La Vanilla perfume roller balls, gorgeous leather shoes and a few other odds and ends.  I ended up buying the shoes, the La Vanilla Roller ball perfume as well as some gold under eye treatment and a lip treatment with Wine in it.  There were some small containers for sauces that I found that I couldn't live with out. All in all, I ended up sending a fair chunk of change, but I'm not upset, I found a new shopping oasis for 2015!

First thing - This place is kept FREEZING COLD. Bring a jacket.   I visited twice in a week: The first visit was kind of wonky.  They received a surprise visit from their GM, and that threw off the service as they only had one waiter on at the time.  However that's not terrible.  I get that things like that happen.    My mom got a sandwich and soup, I got the BLT Salad.    The soup - Chicken noodle soup - tasted like Campbells. The sandwich, the grown up BLT was good. The bread was tasty looking.  The salad for me was MOSTLY good, except there were a few pieces of lettuce that SHOULD never have made it into the salad. Both were nearly black, slimy and just gross.    When I pointed this out the the server, the manager took the whole salad off my bill, even though I ate the rest of the salad. They get good points for service.   On my 2nd visit, I ordered the Bacon, chicken ranch sandwich, comes with cheese,tomato & lettuce, fries as a side.   I don't know what went wrong, but my sandwich had no lettuce or tomato, the bacon was nearly burnt and the ranch was on the side.  The fries... they were meh.   However that 2nd visit was on Wednesday so .. FREE PIE!  I ordered the Coconut cream pie, I was told that would be $1.00 more, but it wasn't.

So after a HUGE meal at the Yelp CYME event, I decided I wanted to walk things of. Walking it off meant SHOPPING!  So shopping brought me to Forever 21. I don't get to get there often, and when I do, I can now shop in either department! Today I looked through the (SHRINKING) plus department. I note that it's shrinking because when the Forever 21 in Countryside opened it was large, now it's rather tiny and unkempt. This always upsets me to see.   ANYWAY...  I pawed through the paltry selection and chose a few items to try on, A couple of body conscious dresses and a crop top and skirt set.  In the dressing room, I was pleased, all the pieces fit, but I wasn't thrilled with they way they did. Their XL is probably equal to a10/12 size wise.     I did end up with a gorgeous 3/4 sleeve royal blue burn out velvet dress that is to die for. It was relatively inexpensive. I'll find a reason to wear it, because it really flatters my skintone and my figure.

What a sweet little spot in Down Town St Pete! I was happy to find this on the way to the car after the Yelp event.  Sweet gelato that has many different flavours. I was excited to them! I ended up getting the Chocolate Peanutbutter and the Dulce De Leche.. One was delicious, but the Dulce De Leche... It tasted very chemically. I wasn't impressed.   Prices are decent, and with a small or Picolo size you can try 3 flavours for less than 4.50.  I reccomend this highly!

I really wanted to like this place. A new seafood place that isn't your usual run of the mill? It would be great to have it not be Red Lobster. When we walked in, I liked the decor, but honestly, beyond that, I was hard pressed to be impressed.  We were there for my boyfriend's birthday, so this is doubly sad that it wasn't a better experience.  Our waitress was extremely attentive and when we placed our orders, she cautioned the BF to not order the crab sandwich that he was wanting as she'd said she'd gotten several complaints on it in the past. It is apparently what they serve as their crab dip and per her words it is better as a dip than as a sandwich.   Taking her at her word, He ordered the fish & chips, with coleslaw and a bowl of their clam Chowder. I got a burger with fries and garlic green beans.   The clam chowder was delivered first and the BF said it tasted pretty good. He's from Boston so that's a high compliment coming from him. It had good clam flavour and a nice body.  But this is where the experience started to go down hill.  When the rest of our food came out, we both looked at each other. His fish didn't look done. Well the -fish- was, but it wasn't golden, the breading on the outside was barely browned at all.. the fries well they are hand cut and cooked to order, so those were.. ok, but they were limp, not crispy, and the coleslaw was flavourless.   My burger, I'd ordered it medium, and it was most certainly over cooked. Far past Medium and much closer to well. The burger itself was pre-made and probably a bubba burger or some such, but it tasted ok. The Fries were the same as my boyfriends, they were limp and soggy with oil. And the garlic green beans .. well.. there was very little garlic on them.   The reason I'm giving this a 3 and not the 2 I feel it truly deserves is the Service. When the waitress came by and asked how it was, we answered Ok. She must have told the Manager, because suddenly the Manager was over at the table asking if there was anything she could do for us. There wasn't we didn't want anything.  They treated the Boyfriend to a slice of Keylie pie for his birthday and they took 10% off the total bill, even though we didn't ask for anything to be done, so they are very concerned about how they are perceived. Which I totally appreciate.   I have to believe these are growing pains as this is a new chain in our area.  I'd try them again.

The new overhaul looks pretty good, and the food was tasty, I had their new steak dish with roma tomatoes. The flavour damned tasty!  What I didn't like was the overwhelming scent of animal dung. It smelled like I was back stage at Busch Gardens near the elephants.   I'm guessing the stink is from the new wood, varnish or some combination of the two, but it is a touch off putting, to say the least.   Still 1/2 price apps after 10 can't be beat.

This was a spur of the moment decision to go to by friends. We'd been out all afternoon and they were heading over there, and said "We're going, ask the hubby if he wants to join." So I did. He'd join us there in about 30.  IN the mean while, the three of us (Plus infant in carrier) waited in the bar.    In the bar, the bartender was .. OVER ATTENTIVE. She had baby lust. The woman didn't allow us to have conversation because she was all over us like white on rice (pardon the pun) She didn't know how to stay away from our little grouping. We were engaged in a quiet conversation at the bar, and every few moments she was interjecting her opinion about SOMETHING about the baby. How she wanted a baby - never mind that it would be a miracle for her to have one at her age - her words.  She fawned over the little one overly much, and her hovering was bothersome.  The adults were -trying- to have a sort of intimate conversation, but it was hard to do so with this woman lingering in our space.     When we were called for our seating, we informed the hostess that we were still waiting on our 4th person, and the bartender shot her mouth off with "Don't you hate it when someone is late, that is So rude."  My friend and I both looked at her a bit incredulous, "He's not late, this wasn't planned." we explained. But there was no apology from this woman. I personally found her behavior invasive, excessive and overtly offensive.  For Dinner, we were taken to a corner area, where the seats were chairs that the legs had been sawed off, and placed on a table riser, we were sat here because they don't have a baby chair or table sling for a baby seat - they used to but they're all broken. (um, it would be time to replace such things, don't you think?) The table was hard to get in and out of, but we managed. We were joined by another family celebrating a birthday and sat down to enjoy a nice meal and conversation.   The meal, it's nothing to write home about. The show, what little there was of it, wasn't impressive. I'm sorry to say, that like other reviews, they seem to be going through the motions. There was little passion in the way he did things.The table cook was understandably flustered, we had a few picky eaters at our table. *chuckles* But the food was well cooked, tasty and we all brought home extra in our to go boxes.

I know it's a fast food place, but seriously, how many times must I -repeat- my order to the 2nd window, while I'm sitting there waiting for pick up? You've already handed me my drink, why are you trying to hand me -another- drink? I don't have kids, I didn't order a kids meal.  I'm waiting on the Mc Nuggets for the 4th time. Perhaps you forgot your AdHd Medication? Or you're just not paying attention? Either way, Look at the screen, See the one with the Iced Tea and the Mc Nuggets? Yeah? that's me. *facepalm*

I like steak N Shake because I can usually trust their burgers to be fresh.   What I I found utterly ridiculous about this particular location was that I waited 12 minutes in the drive through after placing my order. When I got to the window, and I was ready to pay, The girl there, handed me my bag and said "Thanks, have a good day."   Nope, she didn't take payment. "I haven't paid yet." So the girl behind her told her to collect the money. She did, gave me the correct change and all that. then wished me another good day. "Can I have my drink?" She looked behind her. "Is this your drink?" Honestly, how am I supposed to know? I'm not inside the location.  "is it a large diet? Then it's mine." I'm polite, but seriously, make sure that your folks are trained before you put them on the window.

I came here to see a friend perform a Magic show. I wasn't quite sure how far out it was, but for me, it was quite a drive. Well worth it though.. The ambiance was quite nice and the drinks were delicious.   I sat in the bar area and was pleased with the level of service that I had.  I ordered the French dip sandwich and it came with fries. When I got the fries though, they were cold. I let the waitstaff know and they put down another order for me without one complaint.   Seriously good food and alcoholic drinks here. And the entertainment was AWESOME.

I enjoy Zaxbys. I love their flavours. I like the idea that they have seasoned fries and the offer specials on certain days.. but I wish the person at the register paid attention to what they actually told you waht the total was. I was told $x.Xx so that's what I had ready. When I got to the window, they told me another price. *facepalm* I corrected them."Oh yeah.. it's wednesday* Oy..

First review of 2015!  The husband has lost a nose pad from his glasses. He has very light weight archetectural frames. They're a specialty style that not everyone carries, but we thought that perhaps, just maybe Accu-vision Optical might carry the replacement pad for them.  Going inside. the place was neat, but small. They seemed to be doing a fairly busy trade for 2:30 in the afternoon, so when we got to speak with someone, she said that they used to carry the glasses, but currently they don't. She did look around to see if she could find the nose pieces, but being that they are a specialty style piece, she didn't think they had them.  Sure enough, a few minutes later, she came back empty handed.   No worries, we were determined to find what we needed, this place just didn't have them. No harm, no foul.

I get my car's oil changed every three months or so, so when the little wrench popped up, I knew I had to make a call and get an appointment.   I called on Thursday afternoon, about 4:30.  When the service department answered, I asked about Saturday times. Unless I was leaving my car with them, they didn't have anything available until 3pm. I was fine with that.   When I arrived at 3pm, I was told that they'd get my car in as soon as possible. I'm fine with waiting a bit, I'm a patient soul.   While waiting, they played a movie on the DVR, but it's nearly impossible to watch a movie in their waiting room with all the ambient noise. The volume is either too much, or not enough, there is no happy medium.   It was almost exactly 1 hour to the dot, and my car was finished. She runs beautifully now. Thank you, Courtesy Palm Harbor Honda for doing an excellent job on a tire rotation and oil change. You always do good work.

I popped on up to TPS to catch a showing of RHPS. I have heard tales of their shadow cast and wanted to see for myself, as 2 of my friends are in it.  I was not dissappointed. Not in the show and not in the venue.  I will say that our table seemed to be the only one that didn't get service for the longest while, but I understand, we had a table in front of us with a horde of annoying birthday celebrants, and a table to the left filled with a tonne of folks. No harm, no foul.   The cast was good, the show was fun and I made new friends too! Bonus!

For 2013, the theme for the Radley Haunted house is "The Orphanage". Taken from their Facebook page: The Radley Paranormal Research Team is on the verge of giving up on the Radley Orphanage case. One of our own has taken his life after days of lost sleep. He claimed "she" would not stop haunting his every thought. We're all seeing her now. We need new recruit researchers, our fans to pick up the remaining clues. Under enormous pressure and scrutiny we open the reconstructed orphanage.  The sets are amazing. Be sure to pay attention to the black light painted walls, some scares are subtle, some are more .. pronounced. But either way, this is one hell of a haunt!  You'll want to go through again and again.   The haunt is "free" but a suggested donation is $4.00 per head. I would suggest a bit more.  They do -that- good of a job.

I've been here once before, when they used to do their farmer's market, but this evening I was down here because my beau and I went for a nice stroll in the evening after having a date up the street.  It's a nice walk from the eateries and shops up on Cleveland St and the scenery is lovely.  It has a lovely park with several sculptures and nice areas to either sit or walk your dog, and the Clearwater/Tampa ferry lets off right here.   We chose to walk out onto the tiny pier and watch the boats for a bit, watching the evening storm roll in and enjoyed the breeze.  This is truly an asset for Clearwater.

Since we'd been given Come Back coupons after seeing SPY, the husband and I decided we'd go see Mad Max. Veterans 24 had the best time for us.   We arrived and there was no problem using the ticket. The ticket taker was very excited that we'd be seeing Mad Max. He gave a personal reccomendation that the movie was REALLY GOOD.  Our theatre was #2, one of the smaller side theatres. It wasn't terribly small but there were 8 whole people in the place so it was quite comfortable and everyone had good seats. Concessions are as they are in every place, expensive. Since this is where movie theatres make their profits, but 2 waters, Nibs and sour gummies and we ended up seeing a great flick in comfort.   We used to come here all the time, sadly it's too far away now.

Every month, Third Friday does a different theme. This month was Victorian Holiday and Christmas shopping. As usual, the streets were blocked off from 5th to the Phillippe parkway and vendors of all sorts were out, selling their products.   I arrived late, since it goes from 6pm to 10, I figured that showing up around 8:45 I would be ok. Sadly that's not quite the case.  Several of the shops vendors were already packing up. I think this was in part due to the cold front that was coming in. The temperatures were falling and the wind was pretty chilly.   I LOVE Safety Harbor though! It's got a great Main Street, A wonderful chamber of commerce and they're so pet friendly that you can't help but love that they host these kind of events to get everyone out of the house and milling about, listening to great music, from buskers to carolers and everything in between.

This was the third house I got to see on my visit with the Legendary Haunt Tour.    We started out with a Haunted Hay ride. Again, I'm from Florida, we don't do these things, but In the north east I guess they're a THING.  Bates puts a lot of heart and soul into the scenes pacing them well and their actors seem to really get into it as well.   The Bates Motel was so well done! Makeup, costuming and actual haunt were all so very excellent. Timing of the actors, the variety of scares and not just relying on the BOO! factor. I especially liked the mossy creeper in the garden. He's got a lot of fun and range to play in. And I know it was cold when we visited, so Kudos to him.  The bloody Mary was also particularly memorable in the fact that she gave me WAY too much dialogue, but she was a delight when chatting with her after.   The corn maze/trail.. I LOVED the Vampire Nest, though threatening to choke me with my scarf? Now now, don't play into kinks. ;) Really though here was a lot of fun. I loved the circling of the scarecrows who played with you and the bubba's out in the middle of nowhere who wanted to eat us.  All in all, everyone embraced their character and gave us 110% on such a chilly night. The fire afterwards was perhaps the all-star though!

The bi-weekly geekly dinner chose this bbq joint because one of ours wanted to get messy with dinner.  He really wanted wings, but settled for bbq.   Jazzy's is a hole in the wall joint, off of Water's ave in Tampa, right off of the Veteran's expressway. Upon walking in, it smells absolutely amazing, You look over the menu, then you place our order, then you sit down and they bring it out to you.   My husband & I both ordered their 2 meat combos, I got the ribs and pork and he got the ribs and the beef, the portions were large and filling, the ribs were fall off the bone tender and the sides of Potato salad, french fries and Mac N' Cheese were all very satisfying.   We really enjoyed our meal and will come back again in the future.

My husbeast and I went to dinner recently at Ballyhoo Grill in Tarpon. The renovations to the location have it looking better than it was before, the more powerful air conditioner was MUCH better. ;)   However the food.. We ordered the Grouper appetizer $10.90 for 4 pieces of fish - while tasty, was seriously over priced.  We ordered the seafood platter for two, which included enough food for four people, but in the end, we left more food behind than we actually ate, simply because we didn't like the oysters.    We probably won't go back.

A recent addition to our Tarpon Springs line up and I'm happy to have it here. I'll admit, I didn't have high hopes, but they've surpassed their first 6 months and they've FINALLY put up their permanant sign! (we were there when it was being painted)   The food is good.  We had a lovely dinner of their Shrimp Scampi pasta and the Anduii Sausage pasta, both of us started with their soup, my hubby had the crab bisque and I had their cheeseburger soup and we were happily surprised they were tasty.   The meals themselves were both large and delish!    Since we're so close we know that we'll be back again.

I like Culvers. I find that their food, cooked to order is always top quality. Their service too, is always on point. This largo location is no different. The store was clean and neat, the employees are friendly and the food was hot and fresh, served directly to our table.

Came here with a group of six people, a rather large group for our Bi-Weekly geekly dinner.  They were able to accommodate us easily! We were seated at a long table at the back of the dining room, and our waitress was with us in just a minute.   Our group was accommodated fairly easy, we're 2 couples and 2 singles, so the breaking up of the check can be sometimes annoying, but the waitress didn't complain. We ordered our appetizers and our meals and then chatted until the food came out.   My husbeast and I ordered the Wild West shrimp, which is always delightful and tasty, it came out done to perfection and with an extra side of ranch that we didn't ask for but certainly needed.    We also ordered a Delmonico and the New York Strip, both came out cooked to our liking with our preferred side of Baked Potato and veg.   The meal was delicious and it's a great place to hang out and chat with our friends.   For the two of us, with our tea, appetizers and the expensive steaks I think with tip (Our party of six didn't get gratuity included, which surprized me) came out to $85.  So not terrible.  We'd come back.

Lovely facility with caring people who work inside.  I was a patient LONG ago, so when it came time to get our eyes checked for new glasses, I made our appointments here. It has a good reputation and is really only 5 minutes from my door.    We didn't wait long once we checked in, our appointments only 15 minutes apart.  It was one of the most thorough eye exams I have ever had.  By the time it was over, I realized that yes, I needed new glasses, and ones far stronger than the readers I'd been wearing. It was time for the dreaded... Progressive lenses.  Ah well, I'm older now, and I will like them muchly.

Tried this spot because WHY NOT! It's a place we'd not yet been to, and I'm looking for those right now.   The first half of the eatery was packed, but the 2nd half, where we were seated was empty, and as the hubby said "Kinda spooky" the lights went out.  That was corrected a few minutes later when the waitress we had turned the lights back on.   We were seated, looked the menu over, and placed our orders for a lg everything pizza and garlic herb wings.   Since the wings were taking a bit of time to get to us, the waitress brought us an order of garlic bread, That was awesome of her.  After that, the food came out quickly.  The pizza is deep dish, but we were told we could ask for it thin crust in the future. It was tasty though, so it doesn't matter to me. The toppings were good and the sauce wasn't too much, a bit on the sweet side if you ask me.   The wings were good, they could have had a bit more garlic herb sauce but other than that, they were big and tasty.   We'd come back again.

On the way to an event in Largo, an area im none to familiar with and I needed to nosh. Lucky for me, this was in the same plaza as my intended destination.  I noticed they had a painted window that offered any 2 slices and a drink for $5.00. Thats a damn fine deal. So thats exactly what i ordered. 2 slices, 1 white, 1 roni. The counter girl took them to the back to heat upand my friend and I waited.  The TV inside was terribly loud for such a small location and they only serve pizza... So rjose are draw backs, but the pizza was good, the crust was light and crispy and the toppings were flavourful.

I needed to run a quick errand, and I -knew- there was a Walgreens just up the street from where I was.. and i was right. So I got in the turn lane and turned in.  Upon arriving, I was greeted with a friendly "Welcome to Walgreens!" (Seriously has everyone adopted MOE's slogan? It's kind of annoying.) I looked up at the isle headers and found what I needed.  When I looked at the price of the item, I kind of kicked myself, it would have been nearly half the price at Walmart or Target, but what can you do? I was at a convenience store.. ah well, my bad.    At the check out, I had to wait behind an elderly woman who was, quite literally counting out her coppers. That took quite a few minutes, but once that was done, the checkout process was quite seamless. I entered my loyalty number to get points (For what, I'm not sure) and was told to "Be Well" (something else I hate.. it's both annoying and stirs bad memories or makes me want to respond  "BE F*cked" as a quote from a movie)

Went here because of the Ads on TV. Very effective. I'd have thought that because it was Xmas Eve, it would have been slammed, however it was really slow. That was a plus for us.  We ordered the Loaded Fries, French Dip and the Mushroom Cheese burger.   The food came out quick, it was hot and DELICIOUS! Prices were really reasonable, and I admit it, I'm a perv. I peeked, and got a button for it!

With so many GOOD reviews, I'm sad to give it such a bad one, but I must.   Last night, after attending the aerial event, my Scottsman and I needed to eat, using the YELP spinner, I came across Lat 28, it sounded fantastic, so we decided to head on over.  We arrived at the same time another couple did, however once we entered, the music was -SO LOUD- and the 6 people at the bar were so drunk/obnoxiously loud that the other couple turned around and left, we however sat down at a table and gave it a chance.  The music was the wrong kind of music for this establishment. What is essentially a dive bar with pizza, You'd think they'd have something less ... hip hop, but no, blaring through a sound system in a room the size of 2 average bedrooms with half the furniture, you have (c)Rapp Music - of the worst possible kind.   There was no getting away from it either, People were shouting over it to be heard in their personal conversations. It was kind of pathetic.  Our waitress came over and we noticed that she was either /REALLY/ friendly or she'd been imbibing with the other patrons a bit, because she was very.. VERY friendly. Almost a little TOOO friendly. After she gave us her names she asked for ours. Not something I'm used to with waitresses.    We placed our orders for our drinks - I found it odd they didn't have Iced tea, only bottled coke, diet and 7-up, or the alcohol, but hey, not my circus/not my monkeys. And when they came out, they weren't even the full sized bottles but the squat bottles carrying only 8 0unces each. o.O.  We ordered the Blanca pizza and sat back to look at our phones because conversation was impossible.   While this was going on, I took some time to observe the Regulars, since this was going to be the entertainment for the evening. There was a trio at the bar consisting of 2 guys and a girl, two of which were perfectly fine, the other, was well into his cups and scrappy. At one point he piped up "What's the matter with you two, you think you're better than us? You're sitting so far away.." I looked at my date, and he at me, as we weren't sure who he was slurring his words at. It turned out he was speaking to the bar tender and the cook. This guy was just spoiling for a fight.   The other folks at the bar seemed to consist of a man and woman, two older guys and a woman drinking wine The two guys , the guy with the woman and the woman drinking wine would occasionally get up and go out side to smoke at one of the tables outside of the door for such purposes and come back in. One of the couples at the bar apparently was an off duty waitress, as per the commentary over heard in a small spat about "Which one of my friends came in and dined & dashed?"  Needless to say, this didn't set the tone for a good experience. The crowd was rowdy, was .. rather obnoxious over all. And the waitress appeared to be under the influence of something, or in her cups as well, as she danced and swayed to music that she only heard, because lord knows it wasn't the rap music that was being played overly loud through the speakers.   When the pizza was delivered, I had to ask for utensils from the cook, since the waitress hadn't brought them to the table.  The pizza itself was absolutely delicious. It was garlickly, well cooked and cheesy to the max. When we were done, there was but one slice left, we asked for a box, having to repeat the request 3 times to the waitress because either she didn't comprehend what we were asking or she couldn't hear us over the loud music. She even made the snide remark that there was only one slice left, what's the use of taking it home.   Once we paid and left, we over heard the woman who'd been at the bar commenting that a party of 8 had ordered and then left before the food had come out because the music was inappropriate and way to damn loud for the place.  Hrm, perhaps they were onto something... ? I could be wrong, but .. maybe not.

I stopped in here this afternoon for a quick cuppa.    Since it's at the end of a shopping center, it's an odd place for a drive-thru, but once you realize that you just go through the light and enter at the very last drive way, you're good to go.   When I approached the speaker, a cheery voice asked me if I wanted to participate in the Happy Hour, sure, why not, even though I wasn't sure what the deal was. She explained and I accepted, for $1.09 for a med. Iced coffee, it was awesome. I also got myself a chocolate glazed donut.  There was no issue with service, it was quick and polite. All in all a good visit.

Had to stop to get gas before crossing over the Skyway bridge. This location is at the corner of Us19 and just before you get on the stretch of 275 that goes over it. The gas was inexpensive and inside they were busy. It was neat and clean, but someone was very eager to get into the toilet while I was using it. Apparently telling them "OCCUPIED" wasn't enough. *shrug*

A beautifully laid out Publix in the Fishhawk Ranch area of Lithia. It is large and neat, well lit with a large parking lot.   We popped in to do some grocery shopping for my brother in law who is currently laid up due to an injury.  While things weren't in the usual places, like they are at our local Publix, but we were able to locate everything we needed, or ask an associate and find out where things were, with an offer to take us to them, which we declined.   My brother in law did well this week, nearly everything on his shopping list was bogo, which Publix does quite frequently, making shopping at publix truly a pleasure.

Let me start by saying the food was delicious. I had absolutely no problem at all with that. I've been several times to the Lagerhaus in the past and I've always enjoyed my dining experience, however tonight was ... different?  I came in alone, the husbeast was busy with preparation for our Vegas trip, so I got to catch dinner on the fly. I spun Yelp and came up with this as a destination, and since I hadn't done a review, I was especially happy!  When I entered, I was greeted by the hostess and let her know there would be just me "We can do that." and she drew me back to a table with a singular seat - it happened to be at a corner of the wall, just in front of a LARGE party table. She told the waitress serving that table that she had me as well. The waitress looked... -thrilled- (sarcasm).  I was greeted with no eye contact, no smile. Asked what I wanted to drink, and when it contained no alcohol, the contempt was clearly there. Unsweet Iced tea was ordered and brought to my table, and I was asked if I wanted to place my order. Weinerschnitzel, with a Caeser Salad & Grilled Vegetables.  With a nod she went and took it to the chef.  My menu was never taken away. It stayed on my table until the very end of my meal.   At some point before my food came to the table, I managed to get her attention, I asked for some Sweet & Low. Rather than tell me they didn't carry that and offer me splenda (I'm allergic to it) she reached behind me, to another table - one that had a full set up - something mine lacked (No salt/pepper, etc) and plopped it down in front of me, no words, nothing. Color me unimpressed.   The food was run out by other waitstaff. And mind you, I got my salad with the Entree and side. Something that hasn't happened with my service in the past. I'm used to getting the salad before I get the main course.  When the food was delivered, I needed salt. Rather than flag her down -again- I turned around, and I saw it. She was kabitzing with the table behind me, Has been the entire time. They are a large party of 8. I see that she is enjoying their food with them, sharing in their conversation and everything. And that's FINE, if you don't have other people to attend.   I made eye contact when I got the salt briefly before sitting down.  She came back over about 10 minutes later, and with a lifeless voice -told me- "Evertyings good." And before I could answer, she walked away. It was about then that I was mostly done. Half of my dinner remained, I was sitting with my back against the wall, my phone in my hands, avidly NOT paying attention to my food, and trying to catch her eye as she passed by me 3 or 4 times. She had to pass me, because the Computer to input orders was right around the corner.   Finally another waitress saw the posture and asked if I needed a box, and I said yes, "And my check." The box was given as was my check, handed to me by "my" waitress. When I received it, I did something I don't ever do, You see, I work in the service industry, Tips are important, but they have to be earned. I tipped, but ultra low. Clearly she didn't care about her service level to me, so I didn't care about my tip level to her, and noted it on the bill as well.   I hate that I had to drop the review by a star because of this kind of service, because the food was Delicious! Their schnitzel was great, the vegi's were tasty and the salad... well it was salad! But poor service is poor service and attitude is everytihing. I'm sorry if she was having a bad day, and if a singular person who isn't going to be a burden to you is the final straw... but it pays to pay attention.

A great bridge to get stuck on during the height of spring break.  It's better than getting stuck on the one to Clearwater beach as it's shorter, and faster, and not as many people use it.    While this may seam facetious, I assure you it's not. The road way offers spectacular views, There are pull offs where you can launch boats. A walk way so you can walk the causeway and places to fish from.   You'll hardly find a better bridge in Pinellas.

I played Spin the Yelp with my mom to find a place to eat.   Elizabeth's is the one that popped up first.  After reading the reviews I was sold.   We made the drive and went inside, the place wasn't quite busy, but we came after the lunch rush so that was keen. Mom and I perused the menu and both of us ordered the Potato Leek soup and a sandwich along with two coffees   Be warned, they're not cheap, but the food is hand made in shop and absolutely DELICIOUS. Lunch for the 2 of us came out to about $40 and it's money well spent.  We will be back.  The soup was some of the best I've ever had.

Ate here with friends after helping them move.  I'd not been here in a dogs age so it was really nice.   The food was good, I had the weinerschnitzel, a perogie and side salad with mine, friends had other things, and we all had cider.  All of us chatted and ate, as the atmosphere is conducive for that.  The place is surrounded with cold cases and merchandise.

Got the notice this company is closing on Mother's day 2019, which is sad because I just found out about them the previous weekend.  I decided I needed to try them out before they closed shop.  It's an hour from home, but I'm not upset that I mad the drive.   The husbeast came with me, and though we had a bit of a wait (About 30 minutes at 6:30 pm on Tuesday) we were seated and offered bread before we placed our orders. I ordered their special a 1lb Sirloin with a salad and side. The husbeast ordered wings and their french onion soup.   The salad was tasty, their ranch dressing is GOOD.   The French Onion soup appeared to be chicken stock based, but still had very tasty flavor.  The steak was good, could have used a bit more seasoning, but I ate 1/3 of it and all of my baked zuchinni side, which was with redsauce and tasty.    The wings! The wings were the stand out of the meal. We chose unbreaded, cajun style with hotsauce on the side. OMG those were SO good. It's sad we cant get those any more.    Best to the owners on their retirement!
Stopped at this 711 because I absolutely had to use the restroom.    Restroom was clean, store was clean. Nothing out of the ordinary.

My car went into the shop after I had a fender bender.    They were able to get the car fixed in about three days, and return it to me before I left for a trip on that Saturday afternoon. It was nice to be able to drive my own vehicle.   The work looks amazing!

After a gym date night, we opted for a high protien, low carb, not so fancy dinner.  Why? Because its sometimes fun just to hang out together and just be and enjoy ourselves. And let's be honest, the foood at the awful waffle isn't so bad at all.   The service was quick and friendly, our coffee cups were kept full and the cream was cold.   I'd ordered your typical breakfast meal of scrambled eggs (dry, with cheese) bacon, hash browns  and toast. My beau had similar but with tomatoes instead of potatoes.   The food was made quickly and served hot, we ate and talked as you're want to do in places like this. Our waitress was friendly and warm, and my beau and I chatted a bit with her.    We'd come back (and we have since this date took place back in late April/early May)

I don't often go to CFA but I was taking my niece to get her tattoo, both of us were hungry and this was literally the 2nd fast food eatery on the way, the first being a McDonalds near Dunedin and Meh.   We noticed a short line, and 2 people were taking orders, One walked up to us, we placed our order, said we were paying cash, and they said they'd get us at the window. Indeed, it was then that the heavens opened up with a storm.  We paid at the window, by the time we got to the 2nd window our food was ready, the fries were steaming hot, the cokes were iced and the chicken sandwiches were in their aluminum lined baggies.  Lunch was ready.   Everything was tasty.

History is one of the neatest things you can learn, and Tarpon is full of it. Did you know that the guy who named St. Petersburg was from Russia and brought the Rail Road through Pinellas County all the way there?   Tarpon was once a flourishing area filled with high end houses, hotels that proudly promoted the Florida film industry and held Stars of the era.  The volunteers that spend the hours there are a colorful bunch, they are enamoured with the History and they are happy to share their knowledge with you.   Built in 1909, this building replaced the original structure that served the Atlantic Coast Line Railway and burned down in 1908. The rail service continued until the mid 1970's for passengers and ended service for Freight in the 80's, what was the rail line is now part of the upper pinellas trail.   The museum is a lovely addition to the shining gem that is Tarpon Springs.

As of today, I've found out that the doors to this eatery will be closing for good on 5/12. It makes me sad to hear this.  Wishing them all the best in the future    The husbeastie looked up the new restaurants in the area and pulled the trigger, I told him what this used to be and how they'd under gone a Bar Rescue, he was surprised and wanted to check it out.   We were not upset!  The place still looks much the same, except when you go inside. Thanks to the deep burgundy drapes, and the rock wall treatments gave it a dark feeling. To alleviate this, they added bare Edison bulb lamps to the booths along the back.  While this shouldn't be a problem, those bulbs are TOO bright, and very uncomfortable to the eye. We ended up turning ours off, the one behind us on either side to alleviate the issue.  Before we left, the whole row of lights had been turned off.   **this should say something to the owners, Shade the lights they're far FAR too bright to be unshaded**    That was really the only issue. The food is good, solid.   The husbeast had a Brat on a roll, I had their Jagerschnitzel, with their onion creme sauce on the side. Both of us had the German potato salad as our side.   It took a bit of time to get our food, that turned out because they originally put my sauce on top and had to remake.   The husbeast found that the sauces and stuff on his roll made it fall apart. Suggest a heartier roll to handle the grainy mustard and what not.  My Jagerschnitzel wasn't a thin pounded pork cutlet, but that was fine, It was quite well seasoned and VERY VERY Tasty.  The sauce on the side was also damn good, almost like a soup. VERY glad I got it on the side though, else I feel it would have broken down the crispy crust.   Service was fine, but I noticed there was only one server for about 7 tables inside and 4 outside, and one bartender for 5 bar patrons. Busy and perhaps a bit understaffed.  Over all, I will certainly come back.

I don't like airline travel so much these days, but If I have to, I'll fly. I was lucky enough to use the newer gate at Tampa, and was there for the grand opening of the new stores. They've done a lot of work.   United is fine, The price was fair for my needs. I was not impressed, but It is what it is.

Walked in with only one thing on my mind today, GET THE FINAL CHRISTMAS PRESENT!  And that's what I did.  I walked into the Whisky isle and was confronted with far too many choices. Lucky for me, Chris was there. He's their Spirits Manager (As well as Store manager). He was more than happy to help me out and give me a few suggestions as to options and choices, showing me a few different varieties of whisky that my recipient might enjoy. I was -sold-.  I took a few minutes to get acquainted with the store, found the Cider section and was happy to see just how large a selection they have. I'm not limited to Redd's and Angry orchard any more!  While at the check out, I noticed a Cordovan Leather case, the price was $459.99, I asked about it. Apparently it was Patron Tequilla. I was aghast. The clerk chuckled, apparently they had sold an 80+ year old bottle of brandy yesterday that was $2500. WOW!   Needless to say, the selection is HUGE, The people are great! They're friendly and experienced. It's great to have them in town.

Came here to see my Orthapedist. No surgery for me just yet, but perhaps in the near future.   The staff was very friendly, quite professional. Their Xray machine was down at the time so a full exam was not available at the exact moment but when I come back, they'll do it then.   Over all, very pleased with the way everything was handled.

First Friday of 2019, we didn't have a reservation (Recommended) but they sat us right away.  Our waitress, Nataly B, was bubbly and friendly and just about as perfect as you could ask for came right over and asked us for our drink order, we ordered tea which she brought right away, along with fresh, hot bread with oil dipping sauce and marinara, which was delish!  We asked a few things about the menu, she didn't hesitate to answer any questions, and gave a few suggestions of her own. In the end, we skipped the appetizer and just ordered mains: I got the Chicken Parmesan and the hubby got the Lasagne.   They were busy, but not terribad, but given that it was Epiphany weekend, It was a good crowd. The volume was loud but not too loud given the high ceilings.  The salads came first and they were good, the home made Italian Dressing was delicious, very flavorful.  The salads were large and fresh.   Our meals came out next. I generally judge an Italian place on it's Chicken Parm, if I do this, they won't get high marks.  It was just Ok. The  fillets weren't crispy, they were not HOT, they were sort of luke warm, not quite crunchy, but the Marinara was tasty and the linguini was REALLY good.  The serving size was large and I took half home.   The lasagne was more brown than red, and there was some spice in it that neither the husband nor I could identify. It didn't taste like any Lasagne we had had before. It wasn't bad, but it was different. He cleaned his plate, so it must have been good.
