The spice decor along the edge of the plate was almost smoky, but the sauce that the food had wasn't smoky. I don;t know how to describe it.  Its not what I would have ordered.   Once we were done with our mains, we said we wanted dessert. It turns out that our waitress is also the Pastry Chef, so we asked what she'd recommend, she ran through her menu and we opted for the Chocolate Caramel cake, it was a good choice, it was rich and tasty, and split between the two of us.   We'll come back because this is a local spot and I support local businesses.

Ok. I'm surprised. I haven't been in a Winn Dixie for years, because the last time I was, they were crappy.    This Winn Dixie is a former Kash N'Karry so they're large, with a good lay out. A huge produce section and bakery all at the front of the store. Since it was my first time in, I wasn't used to the lay out but I found exactly what I wanted pretty easily.   Check out was a breeze and the cashier was really very friendly.  I did notice that their prices were higher than Publix on MANY items. And honestly, that surprised me.

Stopped here for brunch on our way down to Sarasota.   We ordered soup, Million dollar bacon and avocado toast, thinking we'd get the soup or bacon ahead of the entree.  Unfortunately everything was brought out at one time so a lot of food went wasted. If we'd been able to stagger the delivery time, we'd have been able to eat more of what we'd ordered.  Eh, Oh well.

I drive by this place so often, that last night when the beau decided that we needed to get out of the house, as my mood was going south, when he proposed coffee, I suggested this place.  I'm REALLY glad I did.   Copenhagen Cafe is so warm and friendly, the interior may seem stark at first, but when you're inside you feel like you belong.   The food cases are clean and neat, and the display looks very appealing. I was Happy to see traditional pastries as well as meringues in all their light, airy glory.   The beau noticed the gelato case too, so we had a hard time making choices of what our snack would be.  He chose Chocolate rum truffles and I chose one of the Belgain Chocolate Meringues, we were both happy.   He also got a cappuccino and I got a vanilla latte, the coffees were made to perfection, and the pastries were absolutely delicious. I will most assuredly be back.

Flipping amazing food!  I decided that I didn't want to have my usual Hellas tonight so the family opted for a new (to us) place, Mykonos.   It didn't look busy, but we were greeted with smiles and very helpful service.  We sat right next to the window so we could look out at the street, and took a few minutes to look over the menu.  Our dinner started off with spanokipita, or Spinach pie.  They make theirs from scratch, but it's worth the wait. Not heavy of the feta, it is heavy on flavor. Lots and lots of spinach, fresh onions and feta fill the phylo dough shell, and it's baked crispy. Absolutely some of the best I've ever eaten.  Our dinners came shortly after.  Mom had the shish-ka-bob, just pork, onions, tomatoes and green peppers, on a skewer. Nothing fancy, but the seasonings were delightful.  The husbeastie had the Pastichio, a pasta dish with hamburger and potatoes, with a Greek salad. He said it was good!  Mine, It was one of the Chef/Owner's specialties, Mini meat loaves filled with feta cheese, covered in a red sauce. The red sauce was SO GOOD! I  swear it was better than any red I've ever eaten, and the meatloaf was OMG delicious!  The owner even came over to speak with us on our way out. That was a nice touch! Since we live in the neighborhood, I know where we'll be eating from now on.

2nd location of LeRoux bodyarts and Piercings.   This place is STUNNING. Wait until you visit in person! Each room is gorgeous, each station is simply put together with a beautiful, vintage goth aestetic. The artists love what they do, and it shows.

I stopped in on a Wednesday Afternoon. It was myself and another couple in the place. Very quiet. For an Italian eatery, it doesn't look like one on the inside. None of the dark woods or reds and whites you expect to see, it is all Yellow and white, very light and airy  - almost seaside looking.   The bread and oil you're served is tasty, I ordered Chicken Parmigan for my meal and found that when it came to the table, it was burnt. They tried to hide that it was, but underneath, the bottom side was black. It didn't taste terrible, but it was certainly black.  The pasta sauce was tasty.   Would I come back? no.

I had been excited to try Texas de Brazil, and my first chance was going to be with my friends at a birthday celebration.  We were a party of 5 and seated near the salad bar. Our server was polite, and the bread that was dropped at the table was interesting.   Our meat cowboys didn't seem to pay any attention to the red or green signs that our table displayed AT ALL. They simply were there, Ready to serve you meat. Some of which was very tasty, some.. eh. it was ok.   The salad bar was good, I enjoyed the selections there in, and my friends love the bisque.  We had trouble getting the friends birthday discount applied to our checque.

My Kitties needed a check up since we were bringing a new boy into the house.   The staff was friendly and warm when meeting my elderly 17 year old cat and just as delightful when meeting my younger 2, 3 year old boys.  They all seemed to like the staff as well. No one had a bad reaction.

We ordered 2 pizzas and a dozen cinnamon sugar knots and picked it up. The pizzas were huge (XL) and the knots were fresh. Let me tell you, the pizzas were so good. The pepperoni pizza was delicious and the margarita pizza was light and tasty.  I ate the cinnamon knots the next morning with coffee.

Popped in here to take mom to lunch for Mother's day (if belated), I noticed immediately that the place was nearly dead, only two other groups were inside, which is a shame, this building is rather large and is formerly a Hops. (How I miss them!)  We were sat near another group of women and given our menus, which we perused quickly and placed our orders. Mom and I both ordered off their special insert for lunch, I got the chicken Parm sub and mom got something else, I don't remember which at this point, I just know that they were delivered with HEAPS of fresh french fries.   The servings were large and the hearty portions, the chicken parm sub was delicious, the fries were fresh and I'd asked for bleu cheese to dip my fries in, and it was provided (and tasty too!)  When we were done, we stopped at the bakery counter out front and ordered pastries to go.  Each of those were delicious and delicate.

My friend is a teacher and only gets to come back to town when she's on breaks.  We like to dress up for each other and meet for drinks and dinner. Repeal 18 was our choice of libation stops because of what we hoped would be the ambiance.   Their drinks are fantastic, The service was wonderful. But what really, REALLY knocks my review down is the damned TV's.  I get personal preference, and bars get people to sit there and mindlessly drink when the game is on. But it really ruins the experience for me when I want to is there with my gals and catch up and there's this monstrosity in the background. I don't expect this to be popular.  I know I'm not a sports bar fan, but we are whisky fans.   Try the Aphrodite, it's amazing, does this color change trick. You'll thank me.
Drive thru was really quick and efficient with the order I placed. The cashier was very pleasant as was the food expiditer, who handed out the food.

I came here to see a play tonight,  CellMate Confessions. A friend of ours was performing and I wasn't sure what to expect.  The PLAY was amazing, great talent.   The space? It's nice. The art on the walls is pleasing to look at, they offer it at little to no cost to different types of artists, and that's fantastic. I think every community needs this kind of space.    There were 2 major detractors to the space though: Parking. If you park next to the building You WILL BE TOWED. They do not own the space. So parking is either confusing or on the street  -especially if you're not from the area.  And Risers are needed. I was in the 2nd to the back row. I'm nearly 6' tall, but I still had to bob and weave to watch the people on the "stage" and by stage I mean the floor. So either make a stage or give risers to your people in chairs.

We've been to Grill One Nine so often that one particular waiter knows our order by heart. I could have sworn that I've written them up before.  Today though, They disappointed us.  The food is normally very good, and today was no exception.   For the summer they have a few new options, and instead of my usual NY Strip and grilled vegetables I opted for the Chicken Tempura and vegetables.  My Husband got the Udon soup with tempura.  We also ordered three different sushi rolls. Since I don't eat sushi, this is a big deal. The husband has a ravenous sushi appetite, but me.. No thanks, i'll pass!  But they do it well! I always get their Hawaii five-o roll and it's always good. Tonight, our meals came out, we ate, and at the end, they FINALLY brought out our sushi. Apparently they were down one Sushi chef, and one of guys was new, so the service was beyond SLOW.  Though it makes me wonder if they weren't serving the larger orders out first, since I saw a table get served their sushi before us, and they came in well after us. *shrug*

Since we live in the area, seriously close, we decided to forgo the usual Greek fare and try out Rusty Bellies.  We've seen the ads on tv, and tonight we put them to the test.  Walking in, it was damned cold, so we asked for a patio seat, and we almost regretted the decision, with the overwhelming scent of sea side.  Low tide will do that to you, but with the fan blowing, the scent was quickly forgotten.   Our waiter, Nathan, was quick to serve us, and his attitude was infectious and fun. He was quick to bring our drinks and hush puppies, and let us watch the dolphins that were playing in the water way. We got to see two calves and one adult as they swam about in the shallows.    When we did place our order, the husbeast chose a fried scallop plate,with cole slaw and black beans & yellow rice. I chose the steak which came with vegetables and rice pilaf. Both were well seasoned, the portions very generous and everything tasted fresh and delicious. One caveat, I ordered my steak medium rare, and it was most certainly rare. I didn't mind though, it was quite tasty.  When it was time for dessert, we ordered the homemade peanut butter pie. If you get the chance to order this, don't pass it up. The piece was large enough for the two of us and I still took some of it home. I'll enjoy it in the morning with some hot coffee. It really is that good.   I will return later in the summer so I can see the dolphins play again and enjoy an alcoholic beverage out on their tiki deck. It looks like the best place to watch the sunset over Tarpon Bay.
I love the City of Tarpon. It's my home base!   They are always doing something fun, whether it be a street fair down on Tarpon ave or one on Dodecanese, you'll find something that will amuse you.

Drive thru only. The hubs and I went thru their double drive thru after Xmas shopping. We needed a little pick me up.  The order taking process was efficient and quick.    And the line was short. Once we were.paid, we didn't wait long forour food, which was a happy meal and a 10 pc nugget meal, fries were not hot but edible   Food was good. Nothing extra special.

Stopped in here to get out of traffic on a busy Friday afternoon.   This was a different format of a Target than my local Target, but that's fine, I could easily find what I needed, or what wasn't really needed and what was really just an impulse buy.   I spent about an hour here, looking and eventually buying the black yoga pants I came in for. I'm always happy to find exactly what I came in for. Target is good for that.

I had heard about Blaze in other locations, but THRILLED we have one in our area now.  I didn't know what to expect, or how quick it would be, but a line of 10 people deep went very fast, and soon it was my turn to order.   I had perused their menu and opted to get their white pizza, adding mushrooms and garlic with salt and pepper. I swear it was done in 90 seconds in the oven.   I was happy to find out that they offer both Keto and cauliflower crusts for those with gluten intolerances, those have a $3 or $3.50 price upcharge, I didn't try them, but one of the people I'd spoken to, did and they really liked it.   I was impressed. I'll be back.

My Mom was signed up for the Covid-19 vaccine  and when we arrived we found it very disorganized.   While the staff was nice, competent and friendly, there was absolutely NO organization at all. It was basically every man for themselves. There needed to be some kind of set up.

Large, recently opened Hobby lobby that had everything I needed right before Christmas and much of it was 60% off. That was a pretty sweet deal.   We found a few last minute gifts, wrap and tape, as well as a few drawing implements that I needed for my budding rock business.   All in all I was quite pleased with the experience I had at Hobby Lobby

My paramour and I went here for our Datenight, because he wanted something light and healthy. This was a place neither of us have ever been to, so it was a nice change of pace.   The atmosphere inside was nice, the booths have a private feel as you slide into them.  That was especially nice for a date night.  We both started with green tea ad water.   We ordered for appetizers a seared tuna app and tempura veg, we ordered the terryakai chicken and Pork Katsu.   Soup and salad that came with the meals came first and were good.  The tempura veg was tasty, crisp and hot. The seared tuna ... I didn't like it, my beau ate it but to me it didn't taste the freshest.     Just after that was delivered came our main meals, The chicken was cool and bland, it didn't have much flavor at all. The pork was covered in the usual dipping sauce and was not hot, as it should have been since it's a fried dish.  It tasted Ok but I don't like sauces, I'd have preferred to have the option of dipping not being forced to have it on my food.  The service was impeccable, but the food was just ok. I'll try it again.

Nice, large Publix located near Earth Origins and Sonny's Barbecue.  It's not the easiest complex to get into, but it's still quite nice.   Stopped here on the way home after eating at Sonnys. Grabbed ourselves some essential things.  The store is no longer requiring that you follow one way arrows on the ground, which is fine, but most people are still wearing masks (Good).   Clean and efficient, Like most Publix stores, it's easy to shop at.

I did it, I took the plunge to see what all the hubub was about.   Make no mistake, I've been to a TJ's before, in LA, in GA & In Va, but here in FLA, I wasn't sure what to expect. I mean.. we've got Whole Paycheck, did we Really need a TJ's?  We did, and this one is very nice! The parking? It's a problem, it could have been better, but the produce, the fresh flowers, and the specialty items are WONDERFUL!  Those are the things that I like to have "nearish".   I like that TJ's employes friendly people, that the offer some very interesting products that you're not going to find in Publix or Winn Dixie, that they're going to be worth the trip when I make it down to South Tampa. Over all, I'm glad there's one close by!

There was a Maker's Fair advertised so the Husbeastie drove to New Port Richey, we stopped inside and had a Drink.  The husband likes sour beers, so he got their version of one while I shopped the Makers that had come to attend.  He said it was "Different" and I had a small taste and did not like it.    That's not to say their product is bad, I just didn't like that one.  I'm sure everything is wonderful. Their building was cool and had a nice atmosphere to it, it was very comfortable. We will be back.

When we arrived on Saturday afternoon, the line was out the door. It surprised us, to be honest, because the place has a solid 3 star review.   Like the others say, it's a hole in the wall shop, there are booths on the inside that probably haven't been updated since the place opened in the mid 80's, the menu is relatively extensive and the food is prepared to order.  It's about as Working Man's place as you can get.   That being said, we placed our orders: I got the Philly Cheese Steak combo and the husbeastie got himself and Italian combo add Jalapenos.   The place was hopping so we got a booth by luck, someone was leaving. We waited about 10 minutes and finally our order came. The food was delicious! My sub was hot and fresh and super tasty. The husbeastie said his was so good too!   We both got 12" sandwiches, and while the hubby devoured his, mine I took 1/2 home and ate the other half later.   All in all, I'd come back.

Off Bailey's Bluff road, You'll find Key Vista Nature Park. Ever since I've lived in Tarpon Springs, Ive meant to stop in, finally my guys and I stopped by over the weekend when we had absolutely perfect weather.   There's plenty to do here, lots of hiking, bird watching, picnicking or even playing in the water off the coast.  The park is filled with a lot of dead fall from the last few hurricane seasons which make it a bit of a fire hazard.  Down on the coast, there's a board walk that connects down to Anclote Gulf Park, there's a 3 story tower that is kind of rickety at the top, but it's a beautiful view.   We spent a good 2 hours here just wandering around and exploring. We met lots of folks and their doggos, which is great since the park is fully dog friendly.

Drive through, we aren't sure why, but we were asked to wait on an order for 2 large diet cokes. I suppose it could be that they were changing the Co2 but that wasn't communicated. We were told to wait. We waited 12 minutes.  We had asked that one be without ice, and one to have lemons. They both had no ice, and neither had lemons.
Stopped in here to get a diet soda after shopping with a friend.  It was uneventful. I placed an order through the drive though. There was nothing more than that. A fine transaction.

Clean gas station.   Sign up for their perks and get $0.03 to $0.05 cents off a gallon of gas when you enter the phone number.   They have great coffee on the inside and the chewy ice if you're so inclinded.

A newly remodeled McDonalds with twin drive-thrus for fast service, I fully approve.  We stopped here to get drinks after driving across the bay. The store appeared clean and neat from the outside, and most certainly could tell that though it was a busy store from the location, it was kept up on the outside.   Service was quick, and polite. I like when I encounter that at a MickeyD's

It's starbucks, Home of over priced, over roasted coffee.  And apparently when You ask for a chai with 2 xtra pumps you get a Chai with 2 shots of espresso. That is not a good thing. Oh well, live and learn.. *chuckles*

This is just down the street from my house, I'm serious, about a mile down Alt 19, and I can be there in 5 minutes flat.  Tonight the husbeast and I decided to make a go of it on the way home from our respective work places so we met there and went inside.  This is a come as you are kind of place, with open seating and a friendly staff, that seem more like family than a wait staff.  We were seated immediately and only waited a few seconds for our waiter to come over and take our orders, since we know the menu, it was easy to place our order (Souvlaki platter for me, Gyro & onion rings for the husbeast & pita w/tziki sauce for starters) and sat there talking.  Our starter came out in mere minutes, their Taziki sauce is amazing! Just the right amount of garlic and onion with the cucumber turns into perfection.  Our mains were delicious as well. Remember, if you're ordering a platter, you get a lot of food. With the Souvlaki, I got a Side Salad, rice, pita & 10 chunks of meat. I ended up taking more than half of it home.  My husband's only complaint is that the order of onion rings was $3.95 and he got seven rings.  Yep.. SEVEN.  All in all, the food is quality, though I should warn you, if you're doing take out, ALWAYS check your food. we've learned this the hard way.

I took mom out to dinner at Chili's in New Port Richey. It's been some time since I've been to this particular location and they've done a complete renovation to the inside. It looks nice.   The service was quick and efficient and mom and I enjoyed our dinners. Mom had just had dental surgery so she was stuck eating their chili, which she said was tasty and warm. Myself, I had their chicken quesedilla salad, one of my stand bys and it seemed to be missing something, but I couldn't put my finger one it.   All in all, it's a solid place.

I didn't actually go into the cafe side of the store, but into the bookshop side, and I was pleased. They had a little bit of everything for the ecclectic soul. One thing that I was disappointed in though, was their selection of music.  Other than that, it is a one stop shop for sage, crystals, incense and tarot cards as well as live psychic readings on the appropriate day.   I'll certainly be back!

I LOVE Dunedin!   This little town is filled with Charm, filled with shops and of course, it's the gateway to Clearwater Beach.   If you're looking for an art or street festival, Dunedin is one of the Cities in Florida that really seems to thrive on them. Almost every weekend of the year, it seems, you can find something to do. Whether it's a parade, art or craft fair or even a Farmer's Market in the town square.   If you're into great dining, you'll find it here too! Lots of delicious but unique eateries await your taste bud's pleasure. Along with craft brews like the Dunedin Brew House and 7th Son Brewery.   Come out and enjoy this great little city, The Sister city Stirling, Scotland and embrace your inner Scotsman today!

I usually love Makeup stores. Ulta is usually one of my favorites because they carry both high end and drug store brands.  What I had no clue about, until today was just how much they mark up the drug store brands.  I know this, because the brands I just bought at Target & Wal-Mart, were purchase-able here but they were a good 2 dollars more. RIDICULOUS.  They do carry many of the brands that Sephora carries, and that's cool, but yeah.. they need to clean up their act. Their displays -the ones for their own brand and that of the high end polishes were really nasty looking, their testers all broken and smeared, the nail polishes all spread out over the plastic. This is not the visual I want when shopping at a store.   Needless to say, I bought nothing.

Visited this hotel, where a friend was staying.   The room was large and well appointed. This is not a top of the line hotel but a comfortable business traveler class hotel. It has what you need, it have a breakfast buffet and it has comfortable beds. The rooms all have in room coffee and a nice TV.

I had time to kill, I was craving Italian, so what's a girl to do? She stops into a place she's never eaten. First, the place is immaculately clean. Second, it had very few people inside, but I did see people carrying things out, so at least there's people visiting it.    I thought I should place my order at the counter, but it turns out they have sit down service as well. I opted for a ham & cheese calzone and a soda. Seated my self in a booth and was given two piping hot parmasean & Garlic bread sticks with red sauce. That was delicious.  When the actual food came out, it was HUGE, stuffed with cheese & ham and tasted so good.   Service was a little slow, given how slow it was on the inside, but otherwise, I will probably be back.

Tonight I got to meet a friend for the first time in a Decade of knowing them on line, I wanted a nice place to enjoy a meal and their companionship, so knowing the reputation of Bonefish, I opted for this to be our meeting place. I was not disappointed.  For a Wednesday night, the place was hoppin'! Parking was at a premium, but the parking fairy was with me and I got a spot right up front! Our wait time was quoted as 25 minutes, but we were seated in less than 15.   At our seat, our waiter, Joe was prompt with our drink orders and to our starters, we opted for the bacon wrapped scallops with the mango salsa.  These were delivered quite quickly and were exquisitely delicious.   We were asked if we wanted bread and pesto, which we agreed to, and I have to admit the pesto was the best bread dip I've had in -ages- so flavourful and yummy! When our mains came, Lily's chicken with augratin potatoes and asparagus, my friend had the fillet with double garlic mashed, both were served quickly and absolutely perfect. The chicken was seasoned to perfection and cooked so that it was both juicy and tasty. The steak was asked for as medium rare and we could find no fault.   As a treat, we chose dessert too, the Chocolate Creme Brulee. There was certainly enough in this dish for two people! It was so tasty! My friend had never had creme brulee before and now he's a fan!  I can guarantee you that I'll try another location of Bonefish in the future!

While driving through down town Palm Harbor, the Husbeast and I decided to go out to dinner at Peggy O'Neills.  Now I'd read some pretty negative press about it on 4square, about how the service was lacking, but our experience wasn't bad at all.   Our Waitress, Alex was very quick, and when asked what was good, since it was our first visit, she was quick to point out the fish and chips, the meat loaf and the mac and cheese.  Taking a cue from the suggestions we decided to order the fish and chips and the meatloaf, both were fresh and tasty, the meatloaf came with a gravy (I got mine on the side) that was made with Guiness and was absolutely decadent.  My husbeast found himself dipping his fries into it as a treat.  We actually started the meal with fried pickle spears - YUM! and ended it with something that looked like a mushroom, but really was a chocolate cupcake with espresso ice cream in the center. it was truly a meal-ender. Even with the two of us, it was far too much to eat.  The service, while not exactly first class, was good. It could have been quicker, but it was a busy Friday night at a hopping bar. The live music though, was worth mentioning.
This drive through is fast and efficient, I love that they're right off the fork in the road! Sure they're next to a Panera's but it's STARBUCKS! Id' rather use the drive through than park anyway!

We called ahead and reserved a table for 6.  It's our typical Friday night out with our friends, so we wanted to make sure that our little group was going to be able to get seats at this prime dining time of 6:30 Pm.   I was the first to arrive and though seating wasn't a problem, Parking was. I had to use the Valet service, and while free, I just don't like someone else using my car.  Anyway, I digress. The rest of our party arrived, and we were seated outside. It was a lovely evening, so that wasn't bad. A few flies and mosquitos were annoying but this is Florida, you survive it.   The food was good, My husband ordered the coconut shrimp and I ordered the Rumba Platter, which was a Fillet kabob, a Grouper cake & a few of the coconut shirmp, everything arrived quickly and hot, The food was tasty and the service was good.  We'd come back again.

I needed something to do after dinner and I just found a TJ Maxx location I hadn't visited. They have a fairly decent sized accessory and hair/make up selection, but none of it is.. what I'm used to. I'm used to name brand makeup (Something other than ELF or Max-something) Their Haircare was up to snuff though.   Their clothing was .. limited to say the least, but I did notice that they had a decent selection of NYDJ, some of the best fitting jeans made. THey had a neat selection of gift wear and house wares, which made things interesting when shopping. All in all, this store is a bit picked over, but clean.

The place came up in conversation last night, a friend was going to go there today to celebrate New Year's day.  I have to say, I've driven past so many times, and I've always giggled at the name, but when someone brings up a place, I listen.  She spoke highly of the Salt & Pepper Calamari, and so I considered it.  Then I read Facebook today and other friends of mine had gone here today for lunch, that sealed the deal..    We arrived around 6 pm, the place was HOPPING!  We had to park around back - as the lot is very small.   When we got inside, we waited a few minutes to be seated, and our mouths were watering, the place smelled -so- good!   We ordered the Salt & Pepper calamari, Cashew chicken & Yummy Chicken.  Though the place was busy, the service was very quick.  They got the appetizer out to us within minutes, and OMG it lived up to the hype! It was perhaps the best calamari I've ever eaten.  There was just something about it. I really can't place my finger on it, but it was ... fantastic!  Our mains too.. both were flavourful and rich, the right amount of vegetable and meat with sauce, and of course a big bowl of white rice to go with it.  We ended up taking much of the Cashew Chicken home, which is good because that means I get to have it for lunch tomorrow.   With drinks and all three dishes, the total with tax was $30.  Not bad for an evening out.  You can bet that we will come back to this place, and we will be telling all our friends.    Yummy house certainly lives up to it's name!

Stopped here on the way home from Orlando. My car told me it needed gas and I was only happy to get off I4 and out of the traffic that was nearly at a standstill.   The pumps are clean and neat, the gas on the day that I pumped was $2.59 a gallon for regular and I was able to fill up without any issue or wait.  All in all, the TA Travel Center was fine. No issues, nothing spectacular or out of the ordinary. Just a great place to get gas.

Met a friend here for a beer after giving a friend a massage.   How did I not know this was in Tampa? This place is awesome. The food, the cider, the atmosphere, all of it was top notch.   The celtic eggs and the Guiness gravy fries are amazing snacks.   The live music, while not the Black Velvet Band, the night I was there, was excellent. I have to admit I loved hearing "The Rattlin Log" Haven't heard that since my bardic circle days.  *raises a pint*   I will be back!

I used to think of BEALLS as an old person's store. And sometimes it is, but lately they've had some decent buys and bargains.  They've almost always got a sale running, and if you sign up for their credit card, you can earn Bealls bucks to earn money off of things.  I did just that, earned 20% off my purchase and when the bill came, I ended up with an addtional $20 off my next purchase. Pretty sweet deal.

A friend of mine directed me to this location because I needed a half wig.  I neeeded something that would give me Long hair and match my current color, I was fiarly hard to match, but lucky enough they had something that worked.   The prices ranged from realtively inexpensive to .. HOLY COW.  I found one for about $60 and it was the perfect color match. I am VERY happy to have it.  You can bet I'll be going back to silkies any time I need to.

This is a great place to go with friends.  A nice place to create your own menu and watch it be cooked before your eyes.  I like the idea that you can be totally creative with your food, add as little or as much as you want and then make it taste different with the addition of sauces. It's usually a win/win for me.

I wasn't terribly impressed with this location.   The mall is a nice place for BJ's but with all the TV's and all the noise, it's terribly loud and terribly overwhelming.   Their menu, is like all other BJ's, so it's HUGE.  Both the husband and I decided to enjoy an appetizer of Calamari, which was tasty. I ordered the steak - this is not a steak house,  I know to order something different in the future.  The side of green beans was -meh- and the soup was absolutely decadent.   My husband's dinner of the Indian inspired Salmon. There were a lot of curry flavours blended in, and he said it was really tasty.   However it took over 15 minutes after we were done to get our check, and yes, we could check out "at the table" with their ap, but this is not my idea of secure, so we waited for our check... I was not happy.

Formerly Peach-mac, now Simply Mac, they are a quick stop to picking up something that I needed for my older Mac computer. It was really an IN and out stop. $10 out of pocket and we were done. The service was fine. No complaints at all.

I was asked what my 2150th review would be about, and I think this is about the best one I could settle on.   Every other week, our geek social group decides on an eatery to go to, this one has come up pretty regularly, and due to the fact that they are in St. Petersburg, the husbeast and I usually opt out. However after seeing the reviews and hearing our friends rave about their steaks, we decided we'd join in this time.    We over estimated our travel time (Even with it being Friday Drive time and a Ray's game night) and got there with plenty of time to spare. We also got Rockstar parking, which can't be beat.  Since we were the first, we entered and were greeted by Mo, Thinking we were just a couple she was really warm and polite, but once I explained our reservations, she immediately led us to our reserved table and chatted a bit. Love that personal touch.   The place is decorated in such a nice style, with the rich red walls, and dark woods. It really makes you comfortable. One detractor was that the canned music was a touch too loud.  Our waiter, Greg of the wonderful beard, was very attentive and happy to answer any questions we had. He was there when we needed him, and not when we didn't. Our glasses never went dry and our plates were cleared when they were done. The service was spot on.   As the menu specials were read, party members were thrilled to hear there was some Waygu beef being offered, while others loved the Delmonico, and yet the husbeast and I were thrilled with the idea of a Tomahawk steak to share.  So that's how it fell down. One couple each ordered the Delmonico steaks, The single males ordered the Waygu Beef, and my husband and I opted for their dinner for two which came with sides of Spaghetti in wine and garlic, veg of the day, something called Shrimp DiJoghne, bread, salad and dessert all for the price of $99.   The meal started with the crispy bread and a blended butter with garlic and chives - seriously great bread and butter, Yes, ask for seconds. The salad was on the small side, but I'm not complaining at all. We took ours with the regular vinagrette dressing, One of our table mates got the creamy garlic dressing (+$2.00 according to the menu) and it was amazing. So much flavour.  When the meals came out  - and they all came out together, we were impressed. The food looked amazing. The Tomahawk was HUGE. I am not exaggerating when I say that the bone on that thing was 20+ inches. It was perfectly done! The seasoning was excellent.  The veg of the day was tender crisp Italian green beans (my favorite!) and the Shrimp DiJoghne was so GOOD! Whole peeled shrimp blanketed in soft garlicky, sherry laced bread crumbs.  There were 4 peices of shrimp in the serving and if there'd been more I'd have eaten it. Really so very delicious.  We accidentally ate one of our friend's sides, because it was set down near our plate and we thought it came with ours - Parmesan Mashed Potatoes They are DAMNED GOOD. The spaghetti was also decadent !  This meal rivals Bern's in quality.   No, we didn't eat the the whole Tomahawk ,I have no idea how big it is/was, but we did end up taking about 1/2 to 1/3rd home. We cut it from the bone so that my Mom's dog can have a nice treat tomorrow. Since we were so full, we were unable to eat our dessert, and opted to take it home with us, A slice of boxed red velvet cake. If I had any disappointments it would be that this dessert wasn't made in house. But short of that, this was as close to a perfect meal as there ever was.   I will be back!

Date night with the new paramour, after a dance recital. We opted to go to Clearwater Beach on Saturday Night, and we weren't sure what was open.. A quick game of Yelp Roulette, and we landed on The Reef Steak and Seafood.   It was open air designed, and normally, I'm sure the view is GORGEOUS! But there's some construction going on across the street so the view of the intercoastal is obstructed. No worries, with the Large doors open, it was a lovely evening, and it wasn't busy at all.    We started out evening with short rib potato skins - which were AMAZING. These should be on EVERY menu. Seriously, they were a meal in their own right.  We then ordered our mains, The paramour ordered his - a braised short rib sandwich with fries and I opted for a pulled pork grilled cheese.  He got more of those short ribs and their deliciousness and I got some tasty pulled pork which was a touch on the sweet side, the pickles were the right counter balance for it all.   Neither one of us could finish our meals, we ended up talking half home. ;)

I got there mid afternoon, around 2pm. No one was in the store, no one seemed to be behind the counter, at least until I hit the register and then a single guy popped out the back and greeted me.  I remember when this place hopping, when it first opened. I guess they have an afternoon slump between the Lunch Rush and the Dinner Rush.  Anyway, I placed my order for a Little Burger with A1, Grilled onions & Mushrooms and a small order of fries.  I asked for the fries to be extra crispy with Mustard.  I know I'm odd. *shrug*  The burger and fries came up quite quickly and were done to perfection. They have made their fries smaller in size than they used to, but they still over fill the serving size so you do get more than you order.   I can say that I am not fond of that 100 flavour coke machine. I get that it's totally customizable, but Meh.. just MEH. The flavours are all off somehow. It tastes powdery to my delicate tastebuds.

Though my friends have been coming here for years, this was the first time I had a chance to visit the Boba house.    THe atmosphere was really relaxed, comfortable and I absolutely LOVED the musical selections.  what I didn't like were the prices. For a brewed loose leaf tea, no boba.. NOTHING. it was $4.65. Thats even more than Starbucks!  Will I go back? Yes, I will , but I probably won't get anything, I'd just go back to enjoy the vibe.

I don't know, but for the longest time the name of the place held me back. "Cookhouse" just didn't seem appealing. But today, the husbeast and I decided to stay local to lunch and went inside.   What we found was a Mom & Pop style diner that was neat and clean on the inside. The counter top was filled with in house baked pastries and cookies, and the cold case near the register had cakes, pies and napoleons. All looked delectable.   The place was hopping, and right away we could tell why, the place smelled absolutely divine.  We were sat near the window and handed the menu that was extensive. They cover breakfast, lunch and dinner, as well as a lot of desserts.   As we perused, we noted that they had -everything- from Greek, Italian and even peruvian items on their menu, even a good, old fashioned thick American burger graced the page.  There was a typed up page of "Specials" for the day tucked inside.   In the end, I opted for their Own recipe fried chicken and the husbeast ordered the fried seafood platter... yes, it was just one of those days.   We both got a salad, a form of starch and veg, and little did we know the plate also included our dessert. Trust me, this is a LOT of food.   The salads are large, crisp and fresh! With pepporcini peppers, klamata olive, onion, tomato, cucumber and 2 kinds of lettuce, all brought in every other day and chopped in house. You can tell, it's REALLY fresh and tasty.  The blue cheese dressing was REAL blue cheese. I had a hunk of cheese that was literally 1" large in mine.   The meals themselves were generously portioned too. My chicken was 1/2  a small chicken, dipped and golden fried. It was slightly sweet and very crunchy. The potatoes I chose were the oven roasted and Oh so tasty. The green beans were flat style and they were ok.   The husbeast's plate had Large, juicy shrimp, breaded scallops - so large I thought they were hush puppies and a very large cod fillet. He got fries and cole slaw with his meal and he liked it all.   The end of the meal came with our desserts: Really good vanilla ice cream and Rice Pudding - what? I'm in Tarpon, sue me.   The service was REALLY good, very attentive. You can be certain I will come back, and soon!

Michaels  stores are always a fun store to browse through. You can find virtually -any- craft item (Save fabric) in them. If you need ribbon, they have it, you need crystals? Got it. Do you need cake decroating supplies? They are here too!  I purchased bits and bobs to decorate my new bellydance bra, and I'm sure the 50% ticket really helped with my selection!  I really enjoyed that they had a huge selection of things on sale, but even with that, I spent $100.00.

I'll admit, I dropped the ball. It's Mother's Day weekend, and I didn't have a place to take Mom for Brunch.  I hopped onto Open Table and saw I could get a reservation to the Texas Cattle Company and decided to roll the dice. What could go wrong, it's a steakhouse...  I've driven by numerous times, It always smells great from the road, and from the inside, it was even better.  We arrived a half hour before our stated time and just like that, we were taken to a table and seated in Greg's station.  I have to admit, I really didn't know what to expect when I saw our waiter in all black and wearing a cow boy hat, but the decor is very "Texas" and the mural on the wall is very "Texas" So I might as well be served by a Paniolo.   Taking a look at the menu, I was not surprised, there's really not a lot of diversity, it's meat, meat and more meat. I could learn to love it there quickly.  My husbeast decided he would chow down upon the chicken friend bacon and we opted for the southern staple of fried green tomatoes for starters. Both were good, but the bacon? Who decided to do this? I have to know! Lightly battering & then deep frying thick cuts of bacon and then dipping them in a side of country gravy? Simply something close to heaven!    They include a house salad with every meal, and it's not a small thing, with their bread, which was AMAZING on it's own, this could easily be a meal.  But once they brought out the mains... Mom got the 18oz CowGirl T-bone, I had the 22oz New York Strip and the husbeast got himself the pork chops.. we knew immediately that we'd have to have a box for the left overs. There was NO WAY any of us was going to finish a single thing. Especially when each had an accompaniment.    Everything that was brought out was cooked perfectly, The steaks rivaled Bern's in quality. The taste and texture of the meat was absolutely decadent. There was absolutely NOTHING I could find wrong except maybe there as too much?   And since this was Mother's Day, we opted to stop eating early so that we could make sure that Mom got to end the day on a sweet note. We got one of their desserts - a dense vanilla cake, layered with strawberry & pineapple, with a rich buttercream icing. Three people and we STILL couldn't finish it.     Will I be back? You betcha. The prices were steep, but nothing that you couldn't handle if you either shared or went here for a special occasion. Make reservations on busy nights, else you might have a long wait.  And remember they do give you a free Cow Girl Steak on your birthday. So I'll be back EVERY march!

What a beautiful Gem in Safety Harbor! I hadn't ever walked through the place, until I had lunch with a friend. We decided we wanted to go through the library and see what they "Friends of the Library" had to offer.  We were there on the day the Deaf Students were getting their graduation pictures taken, and I got to communicate with them, since my sign language skills are .. nil and rusty as they are.   I did end up picking up a few new additions to my personal library, new-ish books for less than $5 total. You can't beat that deal!

Really impressed with the Sacred Pepper. Came here mid week, a Wednesday evening I believe, with no reservation. The place wasn't busy, yet, but it was beginning to build.    This place is STUNNING. From the inspired lighting, to the gemstone reception desk to the artwork on the wall, they really feed your eyes. And then, what they put on your plate feeds YOU as well.    We tried their Sacred Pepper salad and the Sacred heart salads - both were delicious. I have to admit I was concerned when I read about the coconut vinegrette, but it was so tasty. Light but only a hint of sweet.   We both had the chicken burrata, with Brussel Sprouts. The roasted sprouts were amazing, and the chicken was perfectly cooked.  And we certainly can't forget the bread service, can we? The olive bread and the sun dried tomato bread were both to die for.   However the best thing we put in our mouths that night was the Carrot Cake. It had to have been the best carrot cake either of us had ever eaten. It was perfectly moist, not too sweet, large chunks of nuts and raisins. Just a delight on the palate.   Will I come here again? 5 stars = YES YES YES!

Took a girlfriend to dinner so we could chat.   It's an Olive Garden, so chain italian. The place was super clean, the service was very good, if solictious, but over all, it was a good experience.   The only small complaint I had was the calamari was... fishy.  It was not the best I'd ever tasted.  Otherwise. I'd go back for their Soup/Salad/Breadsticks.

Like all Chain places, they have their reasons to go, this particular place is because of the lunch time soup/salad/breadstick deal for $6.99. It really can't be beat.   I was sat in a section that had 2 wait persons. One was running his butt off with about 4 or 5 tables, one table was particularly needy, needy to the point that I wanted to tell them that he was not their personal waiter, that he had other tables to attend to. I really wanted to say this to them when I over heard them say that "Well, I don't see him running around" That's because you're ahead of his section, and we're all behind you, and behind a half wall, you dolt! However I was civil and kept my tongue.   The other waitress was a young woman, handling my table and another, She wasn't moving quite as fast, but she was doing ok. My food was served all together, I don't think she checked on me once, but that's allright, I wasn't needing anything in particular, and I certainly wasn't in the need of refills on anything which seemed to surprise her when I asked for my check after 1/2 a bowl of soup and 1 serving of salad.   I come back time to time to visit with my mom.

It's McDonalds. What can you say? I stop in most every day to grab myself an Iced Tea before work. I get one of two cashiers. One is great, warm and friendly, the other acts as if she's doing me a favour by being there. *shrug* I get it, I did my time too, but c'mon. Enthusiasm for the job, even if it's fake makes the day go by faster.

I like Grillsmith, really I do. But tonight I was kind of disappointed.   The husbeast and I went here after a long, hard day after work.   To say that the service was slow, is an understatement.  I get that they want you to enjoy the ambiance, that's all well and good, but it shouldn't take the waitstaff 7 minutes to come to us, and another 5 to get us our drinks.  We ordered our starter of calamari, and while it was good, it was overly chewy, so it was over cooked. Our mains were quite tasty, i recommend anyone try the mixed grill. We even treated ourselves to the rare dessert, a slice of Key Lime Pie; the crust was to die for.

Spent 4 nights here as part of a Haunter's Convention. yes, you read that right HAUNTERs. You know, people who run haunted houses.  The hotel is large, it actually wraps around itself and so getting lost is possible, but you will find your way back, eventually.   The lobby is spacious and quite pretty, the elevators are at the oddest angles but stately and proud.  I was on the 2nd floor, which happens to be the club floor - We'll talk about the club lounge in a moment.   While I was not in a Club Room, I had a friend who had one, so I was able to see the differences.  My room was 2 beds, with a lot of extra room, but the view, well, there wasn't much of one, except of the air handling units. Still I had a balcony.. *shrug*  My friend had a club room, King sized bed LOTs of excess room and a balcony that over looked the pool - Winter, so no one was out in it. And it was in need of a cleaning, but still, a better view than I had.  Because he had the club room, he invited me to the club lounge, the first thing I noticed in there was the overwhelming stink of the garbage can.  It needed to be attended to both times I visited.  Other wise, they provided a nice breakfast, with pastries, hot entrees and drinks as well as coffee and lattes for those at the club level.   The hotel handled the convention very well.

This is my home base Publix.   I'm comfortable in it's isles. I know where -everything- is, and generally what the prices are.  Publix runs a lot of BoGo's every week and their stores are fantastically clean, which is what keeps me coming back. I really enjoy their bakery too. Nothing like their 7 grain bread of one of their whipped cream birthday cakes when you need one.   The associates are usually really friendly and willing to help you, they'll take you to the location of where the item is, not just tell you random isle numbers. Something you don't get other locations in the city.

There is nothing like checking out a haunt off season.  How'd I get to do this? Well i was with HauntCon! So their house opened up to us as part of the tours.    An old theatre has opened up to us and with an (almost) full staff, we were able to explore their event.  The inside standing queue can be small and cramped but if you sing and talk with your fellow haunters it makes the time pass easier.    Their attention to detail is good, I especially liked the clown maze, and the slider clown and the ramps up and down which made it fun to keep your balance. Over all a solid house, except for the overpowering stench fo Slaughter House scent. UGH, I had to let my clothes air out before I expected to get on a plane the next day.  That stuff is NASTY.

Went looking for a place I've never visited, and the Beau and I stumbled upon this spot.    The biggest challenge was finding parking that wouldn't tow us, but we found it at the back, it was crowded and a bit difficult, but we were able to fit into a spot.   Once inside, we noticed how packed they were. We waited just a moment before we were seated, and our waiter came over and took our order.  I placed an order for the French Dip and the Beau got the reuben, both came with fries, and a soup or salad. We chose soups.   We didn't wait very long for the starter, Greek Wedding Soup to come to the table, it was very good, but it was SUCH a big bowl that I knew better than to finish it.  When the actual meals came to the table they were LARGE.   My sandwich was too big for me, I managed to take home 1/2 the sandwich and most of the fries because it was so big.  The taste was alright, but the provolone cheese wasn't melted and didn't really add anything to the sandwich, it was just OK.     The beau really did love his, and ate it all.

New location of an existing store, and I'm glad they're in the neighborhood!  This cute little cupcakery has come distinct flavors like: Holy wow, chocolate lava and twix. everything is made fresh there in the store and served in their sweet shoppe.   I will certainly come back.

I was referred here b Florida Hospital North Pinellas, due to popping a ligament in my foot. Nothing -broken- on the xray so they opted to send me to an Orthopedic doctor.  Dutifully I made my appointment and showed up.   I arrived, filled out my 7 pages of medical history, gave my license and insurance card and then waited about 5 minutes before I was escorted back by a very surly Pa or Ma (not sure which) who did nothing more than grunt hello at me, before walking me back to a room to take more history.  He asked me what I did, I told him  " I was walking back to my car at the beach, in the parking lot, and I felt, and internally heard something in the ball of my foot pop"  a minute or so later he asked. "So you were in your drive way, and you felt the top of your foot crack?"  Seriously were you even paying attention?  I had little hope for the doctor.   Dr. Williams came in, wearing a NASCAR shirt and his hair in a short ponytail, ok, I see they cater to some sports enthusiasts here, I can give him this.  He looked at my X-rays, then asked me about the issue. I explained again. He asked if this has ever happened before, "Yes, on the other foot, I dance, and have PF." He nodded.  He told me his Diagnosis. That what I'm already doing is what he would do, that it wouldn't be beneficial to come back. Ok.   1. Their staff that I met other than the doctor wasn't welcoming.  2. they don't want to run your insurance up.  3. No unnecessary wait time for me.  So it was an alright visit.

I came to attend a Japanese Summer Celebration that was held at this church today. The church lacks somewhat in parking, but the grounds were beautiful. The church allowed the event to be held under the large awning that they use for their school yard events. All in all it's a beautiful place.

I couldn't get to my favorite Target, so to pick up necessities and not so.. I had to go to walmart. At least this one is clean and semi organized.   They were apparently having some sort of clearance, and I was able to pick up a couple of bras for my niece for $3 a piece, so.. GOOD deal there!  Service, what there was of it, was polite & efficient, even if it was completely in Spanish and not really directed at me. *shrug*

Big Lots is ALWAYS an adventure. They have a lot of GOOD items and they have some iffy items. There's always something fun to find amid the stuff you'd NEVER buy.  I've gotten lucky and found some top notch hair care items, some pretty high end make up too. But most of the time, I go to big lots when I'm looking for a Cheap Barbie as a gift or just want to shop and have NO particular goal in mind.

I remember when this place opened, oh so many years ago. I can't believe it took me so long to visit!  I've got a friend staying with me this week and since we didn't have anything planned for today, I asked if she wanted to check out this hot spot on the water.  She had worked there in the past, so we opted to see what had changed in the years since she had been employment.   Upon arriving, we found out that parking was going to cost $6.00, it wasn't something I planned for, but it's less than the cost of parking at any of the theme parks.  The walk from the lot to the actual building can be quite a hike if you've got kidlets, so be sure you're wearing comfy clothes and keep them on the inside of the side walk. The trolly cars pass very close to where you're walking.   I was surprised to find that they'd moved the "Chicken" from off of Kennedy to the center traffic circle right in front of the Aquarium. Not that I should be, but I had been wondering where the piece of modern art had gone, now I have my answer.  Admission was $21.00 for each adult. There had JUST been a Groupon for 2 for one, but I missed out on the deal.  So it's good to check to see if there are any specials for getting in.  I hadn't thought about it, but it's mid-week, any other time of year it probably wouldn't have been so busy, but it's summer vacation. Every summer camp that has a camp in session had a group of loud, unruly kids there. I was pushed, shoved and yelled at by more 8 year old's today, than any other day in my previous history.  Thankfully they thinned out after 3:30 pm.  The place is well themed, I loved seeing birds in "natural" habitat, being able to see fish up close, seeing how large some of our fish are that inhabit our mangrove swamps can get. And of course I love the rays!   I also had no idea they had PENGUINS! OMG! Now these were African black footed penguins and they were absolutely the most darling things ever. I really wanted to take one home, but I don't think my cats would like it.   The 3' wide Manta Rays were beautiful to watch as they glided through the water, and seeing their under bellies with their human-esque lips always makes me smile. Flip, the sea turtle is a beauty to behold as well.   The only "complaint" I have is about the dive show.  Jessica- the announcer was a delight. She was articulate and interacted with the audience well. She truly represented the aquarium to it's fullest. But the diver, Lillian, I could not understand a word she was saying. It may simply be a bad sound system, or it may be that she does not speak clearly. I would have liked to have understood the program though interaction.

Stopped in on a Monday, We had seen this particular shop on the way home from the beach and wanted to check it out.   First things first, the parking areas are tiny, but other than that, this place does not disappoint! The service and the food are top notch. The atmosphere out side as well as inside is very sweet, very comfortable.   While there, the beau and I ordered mozzerella cheese sticks. These were kinda disappointing becasue they were pretty much your standard freezer fare.  Our mains though: He ordered the Meatball Grinder and it was both huge and delicious. I ordered their hand made ravioli, it was AMAZING. Their red sauce was to die for.   At the end of the meal, our waiter brought out little sample spoons for us to try of their gellato, it was so convincing that we had to order a small straberry and nutella to share. OH SO GOOD!   Will we be back? You betcha. I need to try their pizza.

We had been looking for a place to eat, and while my friend was suggesting chains, I wanted something different. I saw that Bubbaque's had quite a few cars outside, so I suggested it. I'm glad I did.  Inside, the place is full of kitsch decor, very 'down home', Redneck, and hill billy. It was cute.  I opted for a Combo platter of 2 items with 2 sides or a Side and a sweet ending, (which is what I got) I got pulled pork and fried shrimp with steamed broccoli and banana pudding. My friend got the Sunday Special, a half rack of ribs, with fries and a drink.   The girl who took our order was also our wait person, she brought us our drinks (Unsweet tea and ice water) and our meals followed shortly after.  My meal was delicious. 8 large fried shrimp, a generous portion of pulled pork and some tasty steamed broccoli.  My friend's ribs were a bit dry and tough, but his fries were good, as was the home made ranch dressing he opted for.    The banana pudding though? OUT OF THIS WORLD!  The service was good too. Very efficient and very friendly. I'd certainly come back any time I'm in Brandon.

This location is just in front of the Husband's new work place, so I met him down here before my dance class and enjoyed a lovely dinner alfresco one evening.   We dined on the patio, as the night started to fall and realized the lighting was quite poor. The service was a bit slow as well, but we figured that was probably because our waiter had inside tables too.  Over all, the food was very good, and the location is quite nice.

Halloween supplies are out!  I really love when they have everything out for my favorite season. They have SUCH an incredible selection. As of 10/1 they had all Halloween merchandise on sale for 50% off! I couldn't believe that, but I took advantage of it!

Eliza Steak and Seafood opened up in what used to be Ballyhoo off of Alt 19 near Dodecanese blvd in Tarpon Springs.  The whole place has been given a make over on the inside. New paint has been done in a lovely color of dark teal to a pretty mid tone to white at the top of the walls.    There's an oyster bar to one side, a bar in the front of the establishment and a gorgeous wine lounge in reds and whites that really stands out amid the blues of everything else.   Yes, the walls are bare, but that's ok. There's no need to be "Fun" as another reviewer said, if you're going for a more Upscale vibe, which is what I got.   On this particular afternoon, It wasn't terribly busy, with a few people at the bar, another quad of diners and my husbeast and myself being the only folks in attendance, so our service was impeccable.  We ordered the Calamari Fries, I ordered the fish and chips and the husbeast got the bacon Cheese burger.  Our drinks NEVER went dry, the calamari fries were unique and tasty, with ranch (over their signature thai sauce) was made even better.  They serve toasted bread with an olive dip which is unique. And our mains were good. The fish and chips were different in a cornmeal batter and an aioli that was not tartar sauce, but something a touch spicy-er.  The rockfish was meaty and reminded me of grouper. In any case it was flavourful and good.   Since it's only been open for a little while they still don't have a lot of folks visiting yet, but give them some time and they will. I see people complaining about service, and I imagine that there are some folks with issues however this can all be surpassed with a little kindness on your part as a diner. It really is nothing personal.

It's Starbucks, home of overpriced coffee in Tarpon Springs.  The staff is genial enough, the service is good and the inside is clean and tidy.   Outside, you can expect the Greek men to be congregated around the tables, chattering. Young couples outside sipping on their frappes and watching the traffic go by.   It's Starbucks, people, not rocket science.

This is an older Joann's crafts. It was nice to be able to walk in and find what I was looking for and amusingly enough, most of it was on sale. I didn't find that at the others I've gone to! 9.99 coin trim for $0.97? You can bet I bought every last roll. Ah the life of a bellydancer!

Haven't been to a Five Guys in ages so we opted to stop here in the way to pick up the beau.   The place was spick and span, almost gleaming when we walked in on a moderately busy Sunday afternoon.     We placed orders for a Bacon burger and a Bacon Cheese burger, a small order of fries and two drinks.  We would eat in.  We were given our drinks and we filled them at the drink stations and took our seats.  We waited about 5 minutes and our food was ready.   Everything was hot and well made. The small fry was the perfect size for the two of us.

This is a little hole in the wall cafe, with plenty of seating, wonderful warmth and generous portions.   I had the privlidge of eating here with fellow Yelper Tiffany H. today after we participated in a "Church", on her suggestion and the food was AMAZING. She had vegetarian fare, and I had their version of Meat pie.  Everything was made to order and absolutely fresh.   I have to admit that the only thing that was disappointing about it was that the CD/music player kept cutting out, so that the ambient music would leave us hanging.  it's hard when you get 2 dancers together and the music just -stops- le sigh.   Excellent service, excellent food and by all means make sure you try the fresh made bakalava! Its so damn good!

Fast food is not something I usually do but it'd been all day and I needed -something- so I stopped to use their drive thru. The ordering unit was out of order so you had to drive around and speak to the person.  I ordered one Arby Sandwich - that's it, and it came up quickly. They aren't cheap but they are tasty when hot. I was on my way within 3 minutes.

Lovely venue, the place was all decked out for the Holiday season, as well it should be with the Rockettes in town, among the other shows on stage.   I was situated in Ferguson Hall to see 50 Shades!The Musical, an Original Parody.  I wasn't sure what to expect, but I'm glad I went. The theater was one of the smaller ones, seating about 1000 folks, and though I couldn't order my tickets on line 24 hours in advance, I was able to get through and still get decent seats for the 5:30 showing.   My seat was pretty good too, slightly off center in the Orchestra seating area, about 15 rows back. No obstructions, the acoustics were very good and the leg room in the rows was plentiful.  The seats were comfortable too, so all in all, quite a nice experience.  In the lobby, the restrooms for Ferguson hall are located to the right, tucked up near the elevators. There is a bar to the right as well, near the windows, the prices were a bit expensive, and the wine didn't smell all that appetizing.  The merchandise for the show was offered openly, including a pink riding crop and a lipstick vibrator, along with the usual t-shirts, cheeky and fun!

First time gassing up the rental Jeep. Since I'm not sure how big the tank really is, I didn't wait until I was empty, I filled up at 1/4 of a tank.   I stopped at WaWa because they had the best price for gas, they were clean and of course, I enjoy their store - even if I didn't go in today.   I'm happy to report the Jeep, while it doesn't get the gas mileage I'm used to.. Doesn't completely suck my wallet dry.

As of now Lagerheadz is FOREVER CLOSED.  It appears that their landlord no longer wished to lease the land to them. It was either buy the place outright or move on. Since they're not operating now, the choice was clear. Looking on their Facebook page, there was no indication this was coming.

So a friend of mine posted about Cupcake Heaven on facebook doing something nice for her son - totally cheering him up on a bad day.  This really makes me want to check a place out. So what do I do? I hop in my car, grab my mom, and we made our way up to Spring hill to check this place out.   The owner Diane, is wonderful, She has a lot of fantastic options, and if she sells out of one that you want, she will go back into the kitchen and make it for you, right then, right there.  The cup cakes are large, they are delicious and the icing is to DIE for.   When she found out where we had made the trek from, she gave us ice packs to keep the cakes cool for the journey home and didn't even charge us for that. She's got the customer service down pat!  While there, I ordered a half dozen mixed cups... My favorite was the Kaluah- OMG.. truly it was OMG. The elvis and peanut butter cup went over very well with friends and the chocolate raspberry was said to be dense and decadent, intense. So if you're looking for a very friendly, warm hearted person who really does right by her customers, go check out cupcake heaven and see Diane.  Tell her Liam,Robin and Dianna sent ya. You may just make her cry tears of joy.

This was the first mall I went to back in the late 70's and early 80's and it's still around.   They've made some major improvements, they have some REALLY awesome stores, even if the parking sucks.  And coming early next year, there's going to be a whole paycheck.. I mean Whole Foods beneath Sears.    I have to admit, I like shopping here! Charming Charlies just opened to compete with Forever 21!

Walmart, The 'Murican Church of the Deal. I needed to stop in and pick up a few things. we always find more than we need, and I suppose that it's a good thing, but it's probably not. Heh.   I picked up my cat litter, the hair conditioner and lipstick I needed and was able to get on my way with out too much fuss.

Tarpon Springs' local USPS is usually quite busy, today was the exception, not the rule. There were 4 clerks, one was occupied with someone who was irate, one was on her cell phone, texting - and being told by another one "Are you Crazy? There's a camera RIGHT THERE!", still another was busy taking a package to the back and then there was Peggy. Peggy was bright and warm, she was both efficient and caring.   I needed to mail off a priority letter - to Georgia with Signature request. I could have sent it through the APC, but i Really just wanted to deal with a person versus a machine,  I was glad I got to deal with this clerk as she left me with a smile on my face.

Went here for a birthday lunch with a friend. (Happy Birthday, Frank)  I've been here on a few occasions, and during the month of October, they invite you to eat a pink taco to help raise funds for Breast Cancer Research.. I'm sorry, I just can't order one, let alone eat one with a straight face. AHEM!  We ordered at the counter, the staff was quick and efficient. We sat at the tables outside because it was a flippin' fabulous day. Our food came out fast and it was tasty. I love that they have the sauce bar for folks who need it, but me, I'm not one of them fancy folks. :)

I'm not the biggest Moe's fan, but the husbeast likes all things Spicy and Mexican, so we went to his choice of eateries.  They offer meal deals and plenty of options if you're a vegetarian, so that's good.

Not my favorite DD location.  I stopped here on the way to my HOS orientation. The hope was to get myself an iced caramel swirl latte. No such luck, it seemed that the latte machine (?) was broken. I think the woman meant the espresso machine, but I could be wrong.    In any case, I asked then for a brewed coffee with caramel and cream, which would replicate the drink I was looking for. What I ended up getting was -not- that, but it was "almost' drinkable.    The new coffee-creme donut is delectable though. I recommend that.

This is my kind of toy store!    I stopped in to pick up a new Bare Mineral's Foundation, and while there, I got to look through the new trends out there! I love seeing what the color trends are and what new shades and styles will be.  They have one of the best nail bars out there.   Service is always tops!

The newest of the Wal Mart Super centers in the area, it is by far one of the larger format stores.    Clean, it's not had a chance to get mucked up yet. The store is well stocked. It's on the corner of Us41 and Bearss avenue making it a good location for the slightly rural area of Tampa that it's in.   I hope that they'll maintain it to some degree, else it will turninto a ghetto fabulous walmart in no time.

This is my Go-To Publix. It's 3 miles from home, and smaller format than some of the stores in the area.  It's got everything I need , everything I want.  I love their fresh fruit and veg section and of course I LOVE their bakery!    The employees are always polite, willing to help out when you need them.

As residents of Tarpon Springs, My husband and I have been trying to get out to the local places and see what they have to offer. Tonight, it was Laggerheadz. We walked in from the cold outside and were immediately assaulted by the sounds of cheering. Well, I guess my reputation preceded me, only kidding, it was NFL Sunday and a game between SanDiego & Baltimore was on the TV and the fans were rabid.    We were advised to sit where ever we wanted, and our waitress would be over in a moment. Menus were presented, including an impressive beer menu listing things on tap and bottles. I'm not a beer drinker, but they did have some fancy schmancy ones in their list that my husband took a shine to, Such as the Pumpkin Ale (Sold Out) and the Florida Blueberry (also sold out) but the house recommended the Salty Dog Blue Ale, a light crisp blueberry beer that was so light and fragrant that you smell the blue berries in it's heady aroma. He was very pleased!  We ordered our starter of grouper nuggets and our mains of Fish & Chips (the husbeast) and Mojo Pork over Black beans and Rice.  When the grouper nuggets arrived, they were light and crispy with a flavourful tartar sauce that enhanced the light battering that was over the tasty fish bites.   My husbands dish was golden brown and large, he said the fish was really light, flaky and had a delicate taste, someone like me, who doesn't really eat fish would find it not only edible but quite delicious.  For my meal, the meat was tender and moist, the beans were great, but the rice, it was a travesty. Hard and dried out, there wasn't a single forkful that I could eat that would have been edible. I brought this to the waitress' attention and let her know that, while I didn't want a replacement, I did want to bring it to someone's attention. She said she let the cook in the back know.   We would certainly eat here again.

My nails were growing out and I was in desperate need for a manicure.  Since I had to be at the plaza I decided to check out Got Nails.   My tech, Lisa, didn't seem to speak much English, but that's ok, she communicated in other ways. She was polite, friendly and quite talented.  She was efficient and neat, always keeping her work space clean and neat.   I was happy with the way my Dip manicure came out. I will likely come back.

I decided I wanted pancakes for breakfast. Well considering that it was 1:30 in the afternoon, I suppose it was more brunch, so we needed a place to go that served all day breakfast  - the first place that came to mind was IHOP.   I don't know what I was thinking? I had hoped they still had their deliciously deviant pancakes they had earlier this year, but sadly no, No Bueno. I ended up ordering one of their new dishes though, an All American Bacon Scramble. It was OK. The cheese they used seemed a bit sweet for me, so.. I didn't eat it all. The hash browns were ok, and the pancakes, I upgraded to chocolate chip ones were a lovely treat.. I could only eat about half though.   The husband opted for a spicy omelette that had everything but the kitchen sink in it and came with a hot pepper on the side. He devoured it as if he hadn't eaten in a week. He got himself a triple stack of blueberry pancakes.. he said it was YUMMY!  I think the only thing bad about the visit was when we were being sat, one of the waitresses mouthed "Dont sit me", and I called her on it, playfully. I get it, but still, make sure the patrons don't see you do that. Tsk tsk.

I came to see the Banned Books Burlesque in the CL space. While the show was absolutely delightful, the space was warm. Almost uncomfortably so, but it was large and well kept, with a large kitchen and neat bathrooms.   If I had need to rent something I might consider renting a place like this one.

Since we were visiting the FIL out in Mango, we decided to take him to the HRC for a belated Father's day brunch.  Now the last time I was there, I remember the prices being MUCH steeper, like $35.00 each, so imagine my surprise when it was $20 a head, and if we presented our Player's club cards, we got an additional $5 off! SCORE!!!  My FIL really enjoys the oysters - but me, I was more in the mood for the Fried Chicken or even the omlette station since it was brunch.. I helped myself to a little bit of everything that I wanted, including dessert and left there satisfied.  Both the husband and the FIL were saited too!   it's a nice, and clean place where the food is tasty and the price isn't too steep!

There was a challenge issued to us, we surpassed it. The reward? Our stage manager would get a tattoo.  When the time came, he opted to get his tattoo done at Ybor City Tattoo company, partly because they were open on Sunday, and partly because of their ratings on Yelp.   When I arrived, half my cast was already there, and we were waiting for the artist to finish her adjustments to the artwork that would soon adorn "Mother's" arm.  After a tweak or two, he took to the chair.   She was exceedingly kind, very understanding and very explanatory to him when it came time as to what was going to happen.   All in all, the tattoo process took about 45 minutes. When it was done, it looked fantastic. All of us were pleased. Most especially Mother, because it is adorning his body forever. I'm almost certain that I'll come back and get it done here.

I enjoyed my visit to Brick House tonight.   On a friends reccomendation, I tried the Greek Meatballs as an appetizer.  I was impressed, they were quite tasty. I liked the croistini that they were served on, the sauce and the salad that came with. Everything had great flavour.   For our mains, the husbeast had a chopped chicken salad and I had Chicken and waffles.  While the salad was your usual fare, albeit, he felt that there should have been more egg, since he couldn't find much in the salad.   For me, I found that the waffles were a bit cold, but they had good flavour. The chicken tenders - 6 in total, were crispy and light, with good flavour. I just didn't know how I'm supposed to eat it. Do you eat it like a sandwich? Do you eat them all together? Or do you eat them separately? Either way, ate what I could and ended up taking more than half home!   The food and service were very very good! We will certainly be back!

It's nice to not have to order from a catalogue. It's great to be able to test the slip and drag of lotions, it's great to be able to see the product up close, to smell and feel the texture. That's probably the best thing about having Sunset park Massage Supplies close at hand.   Their service is amazing, they always have the most attentive staff, ones who are most willing to show you what they have to offer, ones who are happy to go over the oil's, gels & lotions at hand. If there's not a sample, they'll find you one.   I don't get down here as often as i like, but when I do, I always leave happy!

First time in FOREVER that I've been PHL.  I think the last time I was here was when I was 14.  Anyway it's changed a lot in the ensuing time. The airport is HUGE, I flew into Gate E and was confused for a bit until I got my bearings. I followed the signage and ended up down at the baggage belt.    The baggage claim area is cavernous but seems to be relatively neat and clean, efficient. Once my bag was claimed, I placed my txt for a lyft. The only thing that I found confusing is the signage for the ride services. But that worked itself out when I spoke to someone with a hang tag.   Overall not a bad airport experience.

The Newest Ross in the local area, it tends to be the best kept. They have a good selection of shoes, of hair acxessories, of purses and dresses. Their tech selection is ..ok, but of course it's Ross, not best buy or tiger direct.  They have a nice selection of dresses, Wether it be for everyday use or special occasion. Give them a look see.

I was CRAVING pizza.. I've been to Pinocchio's before, so I thought I'd take the Scot there... we walked in and wow, the place sure had changed. Apparently,  they're under new ownership!  Pizza still is yummy, still tastes amazing. The Caprese salad is fresh and delicious,  a hearty portion for the price, and the garlic knots are to die for!   It seemed like they were in the process of ironing out small details, but I know I'll be back!

I'd received an invitation from Anna to Join her at Cheese Please before she made it an UYE, and after looking it over and checking my social calendar (because you know, we all have one) I agreed to come along.   I made the hour journey from Tarpon out to South Tampa amid the heavy pre-3 day weekend traffic and found the location tucked into a strip mall on MacDill.
