It's outside is unassuming, Inside though, it's both quaint and alluring. The hosts are warm and charming.   After taking my seat, (I was not the last of our party to arrive, although I was 3 minutes late) I was poured the first of the three wines of the night, a light crisp white, which, for me wasn't bad (I'm notoriously NOT a wine girl). I chatted with my table mates and got to feel out what was going to be happening. There was a sheet of paper in front of me with a listing of cheeses that would be served, with and without complement.   Each course was different, no cheese was repeated, and each left a different taste on the palate. Some were rich and creamy, some were decadent and some were.. um.. well, not as pleasant as others. But there was something for everyone. For me, I found I really REALLY enjoyed the Thompson Tom, it had a Buttery, sharpy, salty taste. I liked the Wasabi Goat cheese, and The No Woman cheese - A jerk seasoned cheese that was so flavourful!   The wines were all right. We were served two reds. One didn't sit well with me at all, and I gave that one to Anna. The other, a Spanish one, was nice on the tongue. The white was crisp on the tongue and sweet.   Because we attended the event, we received $2.00 off our first glass of wine in the wine bar, and 10% off our purchases in the cheese shop.  This is a great way to expand our tastes away from the general American, Cheddar, Swill and provolone.

With a name like Brick House Tavern, I honestly expected to walk in and be visually assaulted by busty waitresses in short skirts, I wasn't, so I was pleased.   What I did walk into was -the ULTIMATE- sports bar, or so it appears, what with the 40 or so screens I saw hanging from the open beam ceiling, it seems pretty impressive.  We only waited a few moments to be seated. For a Monday night the appeared to be hopping.   We were led to our couches that surrounded our table, and they were impressively comfortable. We were given the menus to look over, including their disposable drink menu, which they roll off of a butcher block roll of paper - pretty cool idea.  Their Beer/wine list includes 21 different drafts.   Their food menu includes a pretty wide selection of foods to choose from and I noted that someone likes siracha.   We placed an order for pretzel sticks, their Drunken pork, black and bleu burger with the house specialty mac & cheese, which our waiter Joel told us about.  I can say that Joel didn't lie when he said that everything we ordered was going to be really good.   The pretzel sticks came with three dipping sauces: Mustard, Siracha Ranch and a Jalapeno Cheese sauce. Each had it's own merit, but I loved the cheese sauce the best. :)   The pork chops and the burger were very good, the portion sizes were so big that we both went home with half our meals tucked away.   I should address too, their drinks. The husbeast had one of their Ciders, it was simply the stuff we buy from Publix, Wood Chuck Cider. and Me, I got a Zombie, They say on the menu that they limit you to two. i can see why, i was quite tipsy after only drinking 2/3rds of mine!  Good stuff too.  The service was quick and very friendly. Joel was knowledgable of the menu, he pointed out things he thought we might enjoy and when I ordered the drunken pork chops, he let me know that the day's special was a different pork chop and I could save some money. But the sides that came with it weren't attractive to me, so I wasn't interested.    If you're a big beer drinker, check out their Beer Bongs.. 100 oz of your favorite brew brought to your table with a spigot.  It was very popular.  We'll be back and hope to get Joel again!

WOW, it is finally open! Took them a while but they're here and they're pretty tasty.  We tried to stop by last weekend on a Saturday, but there was NO way that was going to happen. I'm thinking the fire hooping out in the courtyard might have something to do with that.   Given that I was dealing with a migraine headache, I didn't want to sit inside where the noise was magnified, we opted to sit outside where the air was fresh from rain, and there were tables that were covered and along the wall. We sat under a large fan, in an area lit by edison light bulbs and surrounded by topiary. It was lovely. Our table had been carved from a single log and during a busy night, I'm guessing that it would seat up to  12.   The Menu is impressive. It's HUGE with a lot of selections, a lot of plays on words, a few double entendre and such. Playful, I like that.   I was pleased to see they have my ABSOLUTE favorite starter on the planet... Buffalo Cauliflower. ZOMG.  for $8.95 you get what seems to be a whole head of Cauliflower, with bleu cheese and celery. - I found it odd that we were charged for our dipping sauce, but our waitress was new/training, so I didn't say anything, and it was only $0.50.    We perused the alcohol selection, I opted for diet soda, while the husbeast chose a sour beer. I honestly don't remember which it was, but he seemed to like it. It was a local ale/cider blend.  Our mains.. I chose the Chicken Caprese entree, it came with a side and a salad. The husband ordered a sandwich, named after a movie, it was a buffalo chicken sandwich and it was HUGE.  My meal was sized well, a split chicken breast, with mozz cheese, tomato slices and basil drizzled with vinegar, the side I chose was "garlic green beans." the only slight issue I had was that the green beans were bacon green beans, and that is NO real issue for me. ;)  the husbeast decided to get his side as chips. LAWDY the amount of chips was obscene!   I will mention that there was a table with 4 people outside near us. The waitress serving them.. wasn't exactly the most professional. At one point,she went off into the darkness with the male of the group. I'm guessing it was her boyfriend, and another waitress came out looking for her. She was gone 10-15 minutes. They went behind the building, or onto the side, it looked a bit sketchy. *shrug*

Came here for a congratulatory party for a friend of mine on a new job. It was WAY out of the way, but Hell, why not?  Karaoke was the theme of the night and the KJ sang a few and the regulars did as well. The sound was good and the drinks were fair priced. Over all, I was quite happy. I just wished it were closer instead of hell and gone from my normal location.

For dessert after Datz.. what more can I say other than Om nom nom!    The Chai Latte was made absolutely deliciously, just the way i liked it, with steamed milk. My friend opted for a sweetened latte and she loved it too.   She'd had an older check in offer and received a free scoop of gellato - which she graciously offered to me, so I got myself one of their custom flavours, the Lady Finger Toffee.. SO GOOD.   Our girl, Melissa, was absolutely wonderful *kiss kiss* Thank you for your help!

Dinner brought the husbeast and I out to Zhills to console a friend who's going through a break up.  Feeling in the mood for Thai, we asked our friend for a good recommendation and this is where she said to go.  It's a little hole in the wall in a nearly empty strip mall on SR 54, but when we pulled in the parking lot was pretty full, and all the patrons were for this place.  The eatery itself is clean, tidy and very efficiently run. The staff is pleasant and quick when it comes to serving you.  We each ordered a starter and an entree, the starters were fresh spring rolls and chicken satay, which came to the table very quickly. The spring rolls were delicious, the sauce even had a faint note of licorice which brought out the flavours in the roll more distinctly. The chicken satay was exceptionally tasty. Our entrees were yellow curry, which was mildy spicy, but had a delicious, rich texture and complex flavor. Cashew pork which was sultry to the tongue and of course, the husbeast ordered super noodle soup, thai hot. They're the only place to have ever gotten it hot enough to make him hiccup!  Our meals were good, the serving sizes were very generous and the prices were really reasonable for what we got. All in all, we were pretty stoked to find such a place so out of the way.    If you like sushi, I'd recommend that you visit this place, their sushi menu was EXTENSIVE. So many options and each of them were well described. It made ME want to eat sushi and I don't eat fish.   We'll certainly be back the next time we're out this way.

Oh man... Where were you in my teen years when i was traveling to Largo all the time?  This is the epitome of independent coffee shops. Local artist's works hang on the wall. They have people in to perform A Hula Hooper is in residence by the name of - Brutal Hoops - and she's phenomenal! (Tanya Pistillio - Brutal Hooping, check her out!)  They sell your typical coffee faire, including tea lattes. I'm told to try their green tea matcha latte-Tiffany style, apparently it is tasty.  They also sell sandwiches, soups and a variety of breads, cakes and cookies.. Some that are gluten free. They also have a decent wine selection.

We've driven past this place so often, but usually after 3 pm so we were never sure they were open.  I opted to go here so we'd have brunch on Saturday.   The parking lot was full, so we expected the diner to be full as well. I was greatly pleased to see that we were seated right away.  Our waitress, while a bit surly, was quite prompt and accommodating. We both opted for coffee and water as our drinks.   When she came back, we placed our orders, I opted for a bacon omlette and the husbeast opted for the Mexican burrito.  Our food took 15-20 minutes to come to us, and that's fine, the coffee was heated up a few times in that span.  When delivered, the food was hot and tasty. I'd asked for grilled onions to be added to my home fries (adds a tonne of flavour) and they were added and they made the potatoes were 100% better.  The omlette was perfectly done as was my husband's burrito. He liked it so much that he was a member of the clean plate club.

I really expect that when the times on your door say 11 that you're open till 11. So when I show up at 10:30 you should still be open. Not be closing, not have your grill be closed. Not only be serving only alcohol. I was not happy.

What a flipping horrid Ross.   1 ... yes 1 row of plus sized clothes. That's two sides to one rack, less than just about anywhere else in the area. Totally unorganized, the store was dirty, and in general, for as large as it is, it has very little merchandise to hold. It feels like a werehouse.

The company Christmas party was held here and I was excited since I've never been to it before.   There was a storm rolling in, so instead of putting the party out under the stars, they brought us inside. THat was a bit warm and crowded and I could smell the fog juice/ fog scent they used during the haunt, but that didn't seem to bother others.   The ship itself is awesome. We had a docent give us some pointers on the guns on the deck, and show us the quarters for the sailors.  I really do look forward to come back here. It isn't the easiest place to find, but it's a great place to visit!  I'm coming back for sure!

Are you Goth and on a budget? Are you in need of a nice pair of boots or a great pair of heels?  Perhaps you need a costume and you don't know where to go.  Check out the Anarchist's Closet in Tampa off 56th street.   Part thrift store, part costume shop, you'll find what you need to put together your latest Castle Ensemble, your Gasparilla pirate wear or even something for a costume soiree, right down to the make up and eyelashes.   She has sizes Xs to 3x so just about anyone can find something, and the prices are very reasonable.

I don't like having to rent a car, but with my car in the shop and the repairs expected to take all day, I opted to rent one vs having the dealership take me home for the day and then pick me up.  They took me down to Enterprise where I was put into a Chrysler, a car that was big with blind spot, and a flex fuel vehicle -something not explained.  When I was given the car, I was explained the rate, and I, at first, waived the additional insurances, because the rate went from $20 - $78 for the day, but when I refused the agent went all high pressure on me. Frankly I didn't want to have to put up with the bs, so I said FINE.   When I got back to the dealership, they told me that the car would have to be kept over night so the rental would be on them. I explained that I'd taken the full coverage, and they said that'd be fine.  When I brought the car back to the dealership - NOT the Enterprise location, as the dealership said to do, I reiterated that I'd paid full amount, and they said that'd be OK.   That evening, I received a call from the rental agent, asking me what time I turned in the car, and if I'd done it at the dealership. I knew the dealership called, I was there when she did it.  He then asked me what card I wanted the $78 charged to. I explained, Rather patiently, that the car dealership was taking care of it. "Oh, they'll cover the base rental, but you took out.." I stopped him. "They assured me they'd cover it all."  The agent got quiet and spoke again saying "I'll call them tomorrow (Thursday) and speak with them, I'll get in touch with you. Likely you'll have to pay the difference."  I didn't hear back from him.   This is my 2nd dealing with Enterprise I've had, 2 different offices and both have had shoddy customer service. I'm not a fan.

Long lines, off putting agents.. being told to hold out my hands  as something is rubbed over them, but not being told what it is. This does not make me comfortable. I will ask questions. I appreciate that the one TSA agent I spoke with DID answer politely, others have not been quite as understanding.

The husbeast had wanted to try Fords so I found a different location than the other one I'd visited and took him there.  There wasn't a large crowd for our late afternoon Sunday lunch, the afternoon rain had already come so we opted to sit inside in the AC.   Our waiter was friendly, our service was quick, and our drinks were on the table within 4 minutes of being seated.  That's always a good thing.   We ordered an appetizer, the buffalo chicken dip, which we were told was their number one seller. To be honest, I liked their fried pickles better. The dip is really runny, not a lot of chicken to make it substantial, but the flavour is good.  We did have to get a refill of their house made chips.   My husbeastie ordered a burger, the signature one and he got it in the angus beef, he said it was delicious. I got the Chicken Henry, which is an awful lot like the Chicken Bryan from Carrabas.  Either way, it was damned delicious.

For a newer Ross - this particular store opened in October, it sure is ... well, Meh.  Yes, it's bright, but that's where the niceness ends. The stock is minimal, they have one cashier on duty - and according to her, that's pretty much status quo.    Accessories and make up were NIL, the absolute minimun that I've seen. The fashions were pretty pathetic too. About 3 racks of regular, 1.5 of plus & petite combined and too many of Juniors.  The Dress racks were all discombobulated with the sizes all jumbled together. It makes me wonder if people spend time doing this on purpose or if it's just something that the staff doesn't pay attention to when they're putting clothing back.  Meh, I'd hoped to find somthing exciting. Alas, I did not.

It has been a few weeks, but due to prior engagements, I haven't been able to go out on weekends and enjoy a leisurely lunch. Now that Howl-O-Scream is over, it's time to get back on track!  Today I ventured a WHOLE mile from home and went to Mama Maria's Greek Cuisine for lunch today, We were greeted by one of the owners, and promptly told to sit where ever we felt like, and chose a window seat. The place smelled REALLY good and my mouth set to watering almost immediately.    After a quick look at the menu we selected our starters, tatiziki dip and some Greek Meat balls, both were good, though I'm used to my tatiziki having either a bit more garlic or cucumber, I'm not sure which was off. Our food was the baked chicken special for me, and the Gyro platter for my husband.  Both came with soup or salad, and since there was a chill in the air, we chose the soup, a traditional lemon chicken soup that was absolutely to die for.   The entrees came and they were HUGE. The chicken was aromatic and moist, the green been side was extra generous, but the spice on it was a bit odd. It was still very tasty.  The husband's Gyro was large as well, very tasty too, a bit heavy on the lamb over beef.    Service was quick and friendly, I'd certainly come back!

The newest ride to be added to Busch Gardens, Cobra's Curse is completely new concept to the park, it is a SPIN coaster. You don't go upside down, but you do spin like you're in one of the mad hatter's tea cups if you're situated properly!    When I rode the ride the other day, the wait time was 70 minutes, however the wait was made longer by several malfunctions.  People wanted to leave and they were made to go through the entire line backwards, not allowed to go through the emergency exits or allowed to exit through the front. I think that needs to be fixed.    The interactive portions of the ride are pretty fun. The projection Snake king is awesome. I loved the 2x I saw it, the rain and the fire aspects were nicely done. It's clear that they put quite a bit of effort into the themeing and lay out in the queue line.  The new snake fountain and artifacts are gorgeous.   While it's sad to see Tut's tomb gone (And the Experiment..so sad) this is a nice addition to the park.

Its never a good day when you have to go to the ER, but should you have to go, and you're in the area, I recommend St. Joe's North.  Granted, I came in on a Tuesday evening around 7, I was pretty much the only person in the waiting room. Once I sat down, I was called back almost immediately.   From Triage, everything was smooth, except the one nurse who was efficient if not friendly, and didn't give me her name, everyone else was friendly, warm and caring. Much nicer than most of the other hospitals I've been too. Usually ER's are harried and horrid places, where the Nursing staff is running 4 ways to Sunday and don't have time to really think about what they're doing.  These Nurses, Especially Nate, the RN and Former Marine who had my room were caring and friendly. I liked them all.   After a urine test, a blood draw, and a bag of fluids, I was seen by the doctor and her consensus was the same as Mine was, my previous medication wasn't working and while I didn't have a full blown kidney infection yet, it was working that way. So new RX, and I was out the door in less than 3 hours. All in all a fairly nice experience.

I'd driven into the complex just by chance, and after speaking to Penny @ Intimate Desires, she recommended that I use Jessica, her new stylist.  I was in dire need of a new cut after having the same look for the past couple of years.  When I went in on Tuesday, Jessica didn't have any appointments available right then, but she was able to give me a consult, and decided that she knew what she wanted to do with my hair. We made an appointment for today and I'd just come back.  Fast forward to today, I came in about a half hour early and was received quickly, I was taken back to the shampoo and received a great wash & condition.  Jessica then took me to her chair and we chatted again about what she had in mind, what I had in mind and she set to work.  I noticed that all over the salon there some really great stylists doing a bang up job. People seemed really satisfied, and the stylists seemed happy too. THAT'S really important in my book.  When Jessica was done with my cut, I couldn't have been more happy. She trimmed up my ends, gave me some great layers in the front and gave me a lot of body. I'm thrilled with the way it came out. You can bet that I'll be returning!

I like to shop for bargains, I love when I can get good things for decent prices.  And TJ Maxx is usually one of those stores.   This particular store is clean, well organized, but their fashions are lacking. Why this world seems to focus on Juniors versus those who can actually pay for their clothes boggles me.  It also amuses me to no end.  I did manage to find some nice vanilla massage oil, a pair of flips and some chipolte salt for the husbeaste all at a good price though, so that saves the day.

THis is for the location at the airport, located at Gate C, near Shulas.  Around 11, before my flight I stopped in to get a coffee. The service was mediocre, and I watched as a woman, unhappy with her morning sandwich - because As she said, it was half cold, but she ate half so she wanted a "certificiate for a free sandwich on her next visit" Clearly she's played the game before. Clearly she knew what she was doing, but the folks at Starbux weren't playing.  The did re-heat the sandwich for her, The 'Supervisor' did explain that they don't do the coupons there, that they aren't the same as a regular unit. But the lady wasn't taking that for an answer. She made the supervisor write out something on paper, not that this would be valid anywhere..   I bring this up because it slowed down all the service, It showed a lack of concern for the customers in general. Do I think companies should bend over backwards for customers who are running game? No. And it was clear that this lady knew the policy. She was taking advantage of things.

I was in a car accident, Geico sent me to West Coast Collision Center for my Repairs.  The location was clean and the people there were friendly.   Every one that I encountered was professional, willing to answer questions and very approachable.    When I brought my car in, it was after closing time, so I called the number on the door and the owner came over, opened the gate and drove my car though, so that it was protected.  I was originally quoted a 10 day turn around for my car, and that would have been great if the world was perfect. Sadly it was 30 days before my car was ready.   I have a lifetime warranty on the repairs they've done. I've had the car back for a few days now, and I'm OK with what they've done. We'll see how my car fares over time.

Used the dual drive thru to get McNugget meal and a happy meal The wait was normal for this time of day (3pm), the guy at the register was wearing his nose out of his mask.   At the window I was given what I ordered. No mistakes.

Since the place we'd chosen for dinner appeared closed, we opted to slip across the street and eat at Bonefish grill.   After we were sat, it took a long handful of minutes before our waiter came over to get drinks and appetizers, actually he did drinks, disappeared, came back, got apps.. disappeared. Normally I like to give my order at one time. After all, I had the time to get it all ready.   Our app, the bang bang shrimp, it was Ok, sadly because it's become such a well known starter, it's now being done better by other locations. Still, it's a tasty shrimp dish and I do enjoy it.   Our mains, The husbeast had a wedge salad and the spicy tuna bowl, I had the fontina porkchop. Everything was tasty, but for me, there was too much going on with the pork chop and the sides, the green beans and the garlic mashed actually over shadowed the main dish.   Over all, it was a fine, if expensive meal and probably not something I'd rush back to repeat.

For mall food, this place is tops in my book!   If you've never eaten pho, start here with the beef or veg pho, hand rolled spring rolls and a boba tea to round out your meal, and I guarantee you will go away satisfied and content.  Always fresh, I've not yet had a bad experience with the food. They are always quick, efficient and courteous, and that makes me want to come back for more.

I may just have a new hot dog place!  The hubs suggested getting a chilidog since I'd craved one the night before my little procedure yesterday.  I suggested we try this new place today, and so we were off for a little special early week encounter.   When we arrived a bit after the noon hour it was quiet, but that's understandable with covid and all, there was one other guest, and the staff, who were busy keeping the place spotless.  A note on the door let us know to wear masks (Good) and to Socially distance (Also good).  In the eatery, the tables were spaced so that you sat at every other one. Yes, I felt safe to eat inside.   They had a special for $4.99 I could have a special chili-dog with fries or slaw and a drink. For an extra $2.00 I could add an extra chili dog. Honestly that's a great deal! They use Vienna dogs, Import their potatoes from Belgium because the owner doesn't like to use preservatives and make all their chili in house.   You have your choice of Cincinnati chili, a rich, unctuous, slightly sweet with cinnamon chili or you can have the Detroit chili which isn't terribly spicy but has a more nuanced flavor and nutmeg.  The difference is delectable, but both are delicious.  I opted for the Cincinnatti since I'm more familiar with it, and the hubs got the Detroit, we both added the extra dog, and the hubs subbed out a sausage for one of his.    The food was made to order, it took 10 minutes tops and all the while the staff was doing their duties, I was listening to their awesome radio tunes, singing along, I just can't help it.  When we were served I was floored by the size of the crinkle cut fries. The size they gave us was huge. I certainly could NOT finish and neither could the hubs. It's the size we'd share at our normal hotdog place.   The food was good, the chilis were fantastic. The lady behind the register even came out to give me a sample of the detroit chili and suggested that I dip my fries in it. I totally would order those fries SMOTHERED in Chili and Cheese.   This place opened in November of last year and Covid has really impacted them. They're delicious, and it's centrally located, across from South Gate Shopping center, Near Our Lady Queen Of Peace.  Stop in, Say hi! Get good Dogs!

I was going to give this place a higher rating until the last few minutes inside.    We arrived, there was very little wait, my husbeast was drawn right back to see an older hairstylist who really did a great job taming his long pony tail and the new growth of baby curls at his nape. He was quite pleased.   The establishment was clean, looked neat, etc. But ... BUT, it was at the end, maybe about 5 minutes before we were going to leave that one of the stylist's (Her name is Chelsee btw, and she's apparently pregnant, not that this matters, but she was yelling about it) friend's came in.  The moment this woman walked in the door. Chelsee's voice went to RANTING level, filling the salon with it's acrid sound.  She was unhappy about something. A lot of "I KNOW YOU DIDN'T COME HERE FOR A HAIR CUT." and "I JUST NEED MY BREAKLIGHT CHANGED." among other things.  There was some sexual inuendo by the friend, but it completely went over the other's head.   Frankly it was this level of unprofessionalism that made me very uncomfortable.  Chelsee's friend even made a comment about why was she Yelling? And the stylist went out of her way to pooh pooh it, to explain away her behaviour. I'm Sorry, Your shop is full of folks you don't know. You've just managed to turn off paying clientele. GOOD JOB! (only not so much.)

Came here after getting a massage from a friend, and we were a bit more than a half hour before they closed.  We were worried because a lot of places don't give you good service when you come in that late, but we got AMAZING service from Ashley. She was perfection.   Our food was delicious from the bang bang shrimp to the scallops and shrimp that my friend had. My pork was also tender and tasty.  This location is a bit hidden, but it's certainly worth visiting.

I generally don't eat mall food, but I know that here, I can at least get some decent chicken and veggies for a reasonable price.  I don't think they're very cajun, but they're quite friendly. They always have someone standing out and offering samples of their Burbon chicken, I never take them but I always walk to the counter and take the #7, two meats and one side. It's actually cheaper than the 2 sides and one meat.. I don't know how that works, but hey.

I was wanting some Mexican. We'd stopped in here once before and were impressed, so we opted to try it again.   The service is hit or miss, but the food. The food is the star of this place.  My husband had the enchiladas and I opted for the fajitas. Lets talk about portion size. The amount of meat I got with my fajitas was AMAZING. It would have fed 2 people, and I'm not even exaggerating, the sides they served it with Rice, beans, lettuce, pico, guac and sour cream were all top notch, but they skimped on the guac and the sour cream.   Everything was hot, fresh and made to order. SO DAMN GOOD!

I really wanted to love this place. I mean I did when we had the Yelpies, but they fell short on this night.  We arrived before the Kevin Smith show and since we were early, we opted to pick up a quick dinner.  We waited.. and waited to be acknowledged for a seat. When we were seated... we waited again. 7 minutes passed before someone saw us waiting and asked if anyone had been over. When we said no, he found our waiter and then came back over to us and told us that he'd picked up a table outside and he'd be right with us.   From then on out, the service was acceptable, but that really left a bad taste in our mouths.  The food though, it was good. We ordered the deviled egg appetizer and it was so tasty. And both of us got the classic wedge salad. Both of these items were quick and delicious. We just had to wait again for the bill. Once we paid that, we were out on our way to see our show.  I can see where this could be a problem for folks in a hurry.

Totally non-descript from the outside, but on the inside it's really airy and nice.  It isn't like other places that have a lobby up front, but rather the door opens and counters are right there.   One Caveat, please follow the arrows on the floor.   We are in the season of Covid right now, so before you even enter, Mask up.  Follow the lines on the floor. If there are too many people inside, you'll be asked to wait in your car.  These are precautions for your and their safety and it's a fine policy. Be patient, your turn is coming.   Inside, they take your ID and either set up or pull up your profile, They have what you are allowed at their fingertips, which is great, if you're not currently aware of your limits or where you're at.   They have some screens behind their heads touting their merchandise, as well as counters that have displays. The bud tenders are happy to answer questions you have, tell you about any current promotions and sign you up for their loyalty program (I highly recommend this). OH! And on your first visit you get $75 off $150, which is an awesome deal. You get a pretty fantastic deal.   Overall, I was pretty impressed with what I saw and experienced. I've heard some good and bad about LHS but all I saw was good. I'll certainly be coming back soon.

Locally made, New York, water style bagels that are delicious.   The store is open 6-2 daily and they have a wonderful selection of Fresh baked bagels, spreads and coffee.   These are not your corporate style bagels, no sir! These are handmade and absolutely delicious.

I like culver's burgers, I especially love that I don't have to get fries but can get either onion rings or the cheese curds as a choice (Cheese curds all the time please)   The hamburgers are made to order, so they're always fresh and hot. The service is always polite and friendly.

We made a call a few days ago to make an Appointment for the oil change and tire rotation. They were able to get us in when we wanted.   The husband dropped the car off and all was good. They called before the movie started to let him know he needed 2 tires. That's allright, he has tires for life! So he got those put on, the oil changed and everything set up to par.    When we got back from the movie, I checked out the restrooms, they were clean and tidy, and the car was ready to be picked up. All in all, not bad!

Typical CVS store. Neat and organized with helpful employees.   I came in while I was waiting for a friend and saw that their Christmas was in clearance for a great price.   I was able to pick up a bottle of water, use my CVS card and save a little money.

Finally got a chance to visit the Enchanted Spirits Gift shop in Dunedin. It's got a great energy, and if you're looking for crystals, it might be a place for you to stop in.   The paintings on the walls really draw my eye, I love the attention to detail.    They carry a lot of products, from crystals to incense to tarot decks and so much more. Over all, this is a great new age shop. I'm glad to have found it.

Bright, clean and Airy are the first things that pop into my mind when I walked into the lobby of the Hospital to see my newest niece.   We checked in with the reception, having to give our ID's because we'd never been there. I get the precaution and I'm happy for it, since we're going to the neonatal and these days you can't be too sure.   Their gift shop has a nice selection of flowers and presents to give to the new parents and pleasant people working there. Their volunteers were very friendly and took us upstairs and showed us how to get thru the doors at the Maternity ward.   Inside, the rooms are large and airy, and well appointed. The nurses seem to really want to be there around the families and babies.  I was really impressed with this place.

I was low on my Espresso Steak rub, something I usually pick up in Tarpon, but since I was in Dunedin, I opted to get it there.    The store is a bit smaller, but still smells absolutely delicious, and I knew right where what I needed was. The lovely lady behind the counter helped me get a few more items - Mostly hot pepper blends for the husbeast.   I walked out, paying $40 for 4 things and was quite happy.   I signed up for their affinity program, which is different than the one in Tarpon, make sure you sign up too.

Dinner time on Sunday had the Husbeast and I wandering down through Clearwater looking for a place to eat. Normally, I'm not one for seafood, but there was that certain itch I had, and so.. I caved and we went to Frenchy's to catch not only some grouper but also the bleeding edge of the sunset.  I've eaten here before, once, when a freak storm blew a cabana across the beach like a tumbling wheel of death across the sand, but tonight it was fairly calm. When we checked in, we were offered a wait list to sit on the porch or immediate seating on the inside, Hungry, we chose immediate seating and had a lovely view of the water.  Our waitress was so GOOD! She was there almost immediately taking our drink and starter's while we chatted about our day.  The appetizers were delivered very quickly and we dove into our Grouper Nuggets and cheesy garlic bread much to our delight.  As I might have mentioned before, I don't eat seafood often, but I will eat these Grouper nuggets any time, they are the YUM!  We ordered our mains, a Buffalo grouper sandwich for the husbeast and a shrimp basket for me, those too came out very quickly, and I was VERY impressed with the quality of the food. My shrimp were huge and juicy, the coleslaw was so flavourful and the fries crisp. The husbands sandwich was spicy, just the way he likes it, and that is very important.   Our glasses NEVER went empty, which with my husband, is something of a feat, he drinks like a fish and the fact that the waitress kept up with his Iced Tea habit! Kudos to her. She really impressed us with her level of service.  In the end, we even opted for dessert, something called the Baked Smores.  This was wholly decadent: Marshmallows, caramel, peanut butter and a chocolate ganache all on a hand made graham cracker crust, it was SO good.   There was one small problem, and this is something I notice with a lot of eateries these days. Not only was there a tv on in every main room (Ok, there was a Buc's game on, so.. ) but there was also music on at an almost intolerable level. All this distraction rachets up the conversation levels so that it seems every one has to yell. Why not ditch the tv, or save it for the bar area alone. I didn't think this was a sports bar, but hey, I could be wrong.

The last time I was here, it was an ABC location, Now it's Foodys ,and it's GOOD.   My Beau and I decided after a day out just looking around the neighborhood that we would go ahead and try them for lunch, so we stopped by.     In this day of Covid awareness, every server was wearing gloves and masks, and everything was brought out to us, including salt, pepper, sugar  all in single serve packets, so as to reduce cross contamination. Well done!   I ordered the taco salad w/o jalepeño peppers and he ordered the chicken and waffles with a side of bacon. He got coffee and I got a soda.  We didn't have to wait long, as our waitress and the whole staff was very efficient and friendly.  When our food came out, it was beautifully presented and smelled great.   I did have to take off white onions from my salad, but that's because I didn't ask for no onion. It's ok, I'm a big girl, I can remove them. The manager saw that and I explained the same, I wasn't mad at all, no biggie, it was my error.  The Beau was happily enjoying the fresh, crisp waffle and the thick chicken tenders.   Neither one of us had anything left over, except the carcass of my taco shell.  I'd say we were really happy and will come back.

Had the pleasure of a little weekend date night with my guy tonight, so we tried the new Italian spot in Tarpon Springs, Jojo's.  I'd heard a bit of buzz about it on my Facebook groups so I knew it was time to check it out.   6:30 on Sunday, and it's a slow evening, which is fine. We were sat quickly, our waitress Larissa was an absolute delight. She was friendly and engaging, explaining the menu's highlights and specials. She had me sold.   We ordered: the stuffed mushrooms, the caprese salad, the Chicken parmesan alfredo, with idea salad, and ended the meal with cappuccino and italian tiramisu.   The food was amazing! Very fresh, very flavorful. The alfredo sauce was delicious and buttery. I will never order chicken parmesan the old way again. This changed me!   We really liked the presentation of the caprese salad and the taste of the mushroom caps. Everything was so good.   The only complaint is the lighting. We chatted with the owner, Really great guy, and I can tell.you that we'll certainly be regulars here.

I was hoping to be impressed. I was there for a birthday party for a friend. Sadly I was not.   The place is laid out rather well but it looks old and run down. My friends who rented the room had to change rooms because of an unknown stain beneath the bed and to the side and living & dead cockroaches. SO there's there.   The rooms we were mostly in were the party room and the lounge.  The party room was small but adequate. Our party was nice and worked for the three circles of friends who seemed to all be there.   The smoking patio was right outside the door, near the pool and that made it kind of gross if you're not a smoker to get through to the pool.   Over all, not a place I'd be visiting often. But I will come back to support my friends and their activities.

I don't usually go into used sporting equipment stores, but the beau let me know that that would be the best place to look for a teeter hangup without having to pay full price. So we looked.   We found exactly what we were looking for. We found one that looked like it had been assembled and never used. The assembly stickers were still on the frame.  Given that these things sell for $450 new, the $250 price tag was a bargain.   They even disassembled it and put it in my trunk. I've now got a nice Teeter Hang up  and my back feels wonderful. I'll be back!

I was really surprised when I walked in, I wasn't sure what to expect.  I do a lot of shoppping at Ross, but I might switch over to Marshalls, after all, where else can you find Coach & other HIGH END name brand items at really low prices. I'm talking about Coach shoes for $49 & wristlets for $25.    I ended up buying a pair of Bright pink sneakers, a pair of Famous maker wedges and a few other odds and ends, I was happy to come out of there with what I bought for well under $150.00.

I love this local place!   Just on Alt 19, on the corner of Main, across from the Orthodox Church, you'll find Madeline's. It's an absolute Gem of Down Town. They have some of the best Falafel I've ever had, and their Shwarma is oh so good too!  I've stopped in a couple of times, ordered to go as well and I've never been unhappy. Their prices are amazing and their portion sizes are larger than average in my opinion.    Their veggies are always crisp and tasty and the pickeled ones are really good too. Dang, writing this makes me think I'm gonna have to go pick up something for lunch now.

Walked down from Bon Apetite, where we had lunch, and enjoyed the afternoon light. When we got inside it was crowded. Not because people were buying ice cream, but because they were using all the inside seats.  The place is small, but it works.   There are over 40 flavors and yesterday, we got a single scoop of Moose Tracks, which was the No Sugar Added flavor for the Husbeast.  The ice Cream is all local and quite tasty.  The service was quick and easy and the price was incredible.    I would come here rather than going to the "other" creamery across the street.

Publix is always my go to for necessities in grocery shopping. Today, we were on our way to a house party/get together and needed to pick up a "covered dish Item" since I didn't have time to make anything, I asked the husbeast what he thought about Publix Fried chicken, he was A-OK with that.   The store was neat and clean, the staff members were courteous, and even reminded us that since we'd basically picked up the fried chicken meals, we could get a pack of Kings hawaiian rolls to go with it. I went back and picked those up too.

We are brand new regulars.   I've drive past this place for /YEARS/ and it was only frequently that my beau and I stopped in. We were heading to Crystal River, and needed lunch, so we stopped in at Route 66.   The first thing we noticed was the Kitsch decor and the absolute wonderful attitude of the waitstaff.   The tator tots with chili and cheese are amazing, But don't order more than one order per table. The serving is huge. This goes for their fries too! HUGE. Their Cheeseburgers are DELICIOUS! They are something of legend.   There hasn't been anything that we've ordered that hasn't been incredible. I recently ordered their Mediteranen Chicken, and it was delectable.  I encourage you to visit. I know I'll be there with my guys frequently.

We visited this location to celebrate two friends deciding to join their lives together before the SCOTUS determines that marriage equality is not the right path for our country.   The grounds of the Botanical Gardens are lush. Though we did not go past the butterfly area, we were most impressed. I loved the musical Instruments that encourage participating together.   We were told that there's been a large gator seen that morning in the lake! I love Gators!   I do hope the kindness rocks folks in pinellas county lace this place with their smiles, as it seems to be the perfect outlet, with wonderful paths and lots of shady nook's

Upon arriving I feared they weren't open, as the place has no real OPEN signs beside hand printed ones that say they are 'JOYFULLY OPEN' until 8pm each evening.  I was happy to know they were still open at 6:30 pm.   We were greeted with a cheery Aloha, and ushered to a seat. The aroma in the place was absolutely mouthwatering. Our Waitress was both friendly and warm, she offered us the menus and the new alcohol menu, which we declined, but placed orders for water and tea.   Once our drinks were delivered, we ordered our mains: I got the Kaluah Chicken with cabbage and rice, which came with either a bowl of soup or a salad. I opted for the Coconut Lime Veggie soup - SO GOOD! All that would make it better would have been some fresh lime for a garnish.   My friend ordered the sunshine burger, with sides of pop chips, black beans and avocado.  Everything came out quickly, the serving sizes were impressively large, and the service was incredibly friendly.  I'd certainly come back.

Drive thru service, Why is there no Chili combo? Ah well.  I always get the same order, A Large chili, small fry and a drink, that is my Hub's favorite meal, but there's no combo. MEH.   I love their asiago chicken ranch combo too. The food is usually good, but the drive through can be a bit slow, especially at lunch, so know your timing.

It's covid season, so things are a bit different right now. The store is set up so one door is entrance, one is exit, people seem to be following the instructions for the most part.  They are Following the lines that they've put on the ground.  They are wearing masks, both associates and patrons alike. That's good.   The store was large, bright and clean, well stocked too! The only thing I didn't like was we'd passed one of the deli/meat department folks outside on a smoke break, and they were the ones who got us our meat, but we didn't see them wash their hands. I'm sure they did, but we didn't see it so ... meh?   Their selection of meat was good, their selection of produce was spectacular but the BEST thing about this store is their selection of health and beauty aids. Their vitamin and natural products is really above the bar and the quality is excellent. While the rest of the store may seem expensive to some, the prices in this area are amazing and impressive selection too!  Overall we're happy visiting over and over.

Saw this place while out exploring, so we drove on in. It was too hot to truly explore, but what we did see, while taking our sunday drive showed us that Walsinghamp park is HUGE. The lake in the center is lovely, with a public boat launch so it can truly be enjoyed.   Hiking trails and paved bike paths make it a wonderful park for everyone in the whole family to enjoy.

Able to walk right in, put my name in the queue and was seen within 20 minutes.   During these pandemic times, all the agents are wearing masks, gloves and other form of PPE.  They were courteous and friendly, even to the guy who got angry because I got to go before him, because HE stepped out and missed when they called his name.   The draw went quickly, the Phlebotomist was quick and efficient and i felt no pain. I'd come back easily.

Literal hole in the wall breakfast shop in holiday.   We stopped in because it was a place we'd never been in before.   Seeing their menu board, I opted for a Sloppy joe & the husbeastie got a burger. When the food was delivered it was exactly what we expected, He loved the burger, it was as if they did it on their charcoal grill out side, a nice sized hand formed patty cooked to perfection.  A sie of fries and coleslaw.   For me, the Sloppy Joe was good, but the bread was too soggy. It was as though they'd steamed the bun, put it down on a mildly wet plate and let it desintegrate, so by the time it was served, the bun was mush but the meat was delicious.   Over all, the impression wasn't top notch, but it was decent.

Had a chance to go to dinner with the usual suspects tonight at Bascom's Chop House. I've never been and I was happy for the chance.  We had reservations under our usual name for 7 for a party of 8. When we arrived at just before 7, we were told the name was DIFFERENT and the party was for 9 and it was actually 7:30... Uh.. Ok? I'm not sure how they got all of that wrong, but hey.. They are over achievers in that respect.  It turned out that only 6 of our usual party were able to show up so once we were all assembled we were actually seated at 7:10.  Our waiter, Phil introduced himself and explained about Bascom's Chophouse, what their specialties were and a little about their wine list - which looked usual, until you opened the leather cover to see an Ipad beneath. Pretty Cool.   We all took a few moments, while bread and water was delivered.  One thing that I can say about this is when I'm at a  "high end" place, I expect real butter not a margarine mix, sadly that is what we got. ICK, the bread though, was hot, crispy and tasty.   While others placed their orders, the husbeast and I placed ours for starters of a French Onion Soup and the Fried Shirmp, we decided to split the 24 oz Porter house cooked Med Rare, and sides of a Caeser salad and asparagus. I disliked that everything for the meal - the usual sides, when ordered with a steak or chops were ala carte, but when ordered with seafood, were included. The prices for the steak were high enough for those things to be included.   The soup: it was GOOD. I mean really, REALLY good. The broth was pretty amazing, the cheesy topping was crispy and a mix of cheeses and of course the carmelized onions were perfection.   The fried shrimp: It was a serving of 4 split shrimp lightly battered and well seasoned. They tasted delicious, but for $11.95 that's $3 a shrimp. I would NOT order that again. I figured for the price, you'd get maybe 6, I was wrong.   The salad: It was served with 2 anchovies atop, with a parmesan frico on the side, atop a pile of some good, some off tasting romaine lettuce. What saddened me was that our waiter didn't offer fresh ground pepper, which would have brought this salad up quite a bit.   The asparagus: 10 spears for $5.95. A bit expensive, but absolutely delicious. When I took my portion and placed it on my plate, it got covered with the meat juices and that just made it SO much better.   The Steak: Our Porterhouse was perfectly cooked, a nice char on the edges, with just the right amount of fat. I cut the meat off the small side (the fillet) and the tip off the other side and kept that for me, giving the husbeast the bone and the rest.  My meat was absolute perfection, buttery and melt in your mouth good.  $34.95 and I would certainly order it again.   The service was fabulous. Phil was attentive and made sure our drinks got filled and refilled as needed. When it was time for desserts, some of our party chose the flourless chocolate cake and some chose cheesecake, while others simply chose coffee.  The coffee was divine,and the flourless torte was OMG So good.   I will come back. The food was Delish!!!

I'm Very happy to have a Trulieve location near by my home.  It's newly opened, about a week old, and bright, shiny and clean. The staff (mostly) is following their masking rules and social distancing is enforced. The lobby is comfortably situated with seats 6 feet apart, about 10 people would be comfortably able to wait before being called back to the actual dispensary.   The dispensary itself is warmly lit, the wood is light and the cases hold product nicely.  The soundsystem is a bit too loud for the space, and since there is absolutely nothing like carpeting, the sound just bounces around and doesn't get absorbed. Combine that with 6-10 people talking  all at once, makes it very difficult to hear your bud tender.   Over all, it was a good experience. I'm glad they're in my town and will be expanding to Palm Harbor in the very near future.

I'm super excited about my up coming trip to the UK. I had a few questions about currency and honestly, I didn't know where to get the answers, so I headed up to AAA And asked. In the past, they were the ones I used to get Amex Travelers Checks from, but they no longer handle them, instead, they offer a pre-paid credit Card, so I selected that option. Now I'm ready to hit the UK running and see what there is to see.

My family and I went here for dinner to try a local Indian place, rather than driving down to Oldsmar.   While small, the food is OH SO GOOD!   Their naan is fresh made, so allow a little time for it to come out. I really liked their Butter chicken, it was rich and flavourful.   My guys both had the chicken Tikka masala, hot. They had tears in their eyes and very happy bellies.   We will be coming back.

I'M SO HAPPY THEY OPENED UP!  I've been waiting for YEARS for PDQ to come to my area, and now they're here! I love their food, their service and everything about the company. Everything is so good and tasty!  I took the Husbeast there, and we both got the chicken salad, I added almonds, We ordered an order of three chicken tenders and a side of their parmesan and garlic broccoli.  The wait was hardly any time and everything we got was piping hot (Except the salads) and extra tasty. I like that they have a sauce bar, that makes getting extra dressing - THE RANCH IS TO DIE FOR - easier and you don't have to go up to the counter.   It does seem smaller than those in Tampa or St. Pete, but I'm ok with that.  I'll be a regular patron anyway.  Infact, I'll probably go there for lunch today!

Generally,on Tuesday, the husband and I go into town and eat Greek.  Tonight was no different, but we changed our usual location. We went across the street and dined at Dimitri's on the Water.  It's owned by the same family, but it's quite different. Where the original place is very FAMILY, Dimitri's tries for upscale. I say tries, because when you first walk in, you notice a lot of clutter, a lot of disorganized things that really don't belong in an upscale dining establishment.   There are boxes of fruit & veg, there were folding chairs. Basically it looked as if the foyer was being used as storage.   The dining room, though, was a different story.  The ambiance was lovely. With great big windows that looked out over the water and the sponging boats on the canal. Strings of lights, swathed in panels of pale fabric casting an almost romantic ambient light across the tables, each with their own salt rock candle holder.  It really was quite lovely.     We were seated with a view of the canal, where darkness had descended, but we could see the boats that bobbed on the surface creating an idyllic scene.  The Service was delightful, our waiter was a handsome man who was very friendly and efficient, making sure to take our drink orders and getting our starter order quickly.  We ordered the zuchinni & eggplant with sauce, it was tasty but heavy.  They serve complimentary bread to the table with a dish of olive oil and spices with baslamic vinegar, a wonderful taste on the tongue.   When we ordered our mains, I ordered the souvlaki platter (pork) with veggies and a side salad. My husband ordered the Moussaka with soup and veggies.  These came out quickly and while my portion was huge - 2 large skewers of meat, tomato, onion, pita and a large serving of Veggies; the Husband's serving of Moussaka wasn't as large as he'd hoped.  But the taste was very good. Everything was hot and well cooked.  Sadly, both of us were already full - damn diet!, and we ended up taking more than 80% of our meals home.   The reason this is a 3 and not a 5 star rating is not only the lobby mess, but the fact that although they don't close until 10, at 9pm, while we were the only diners in the room, they were already doing full closing procedures.  Completely undressing tables, pulling up chairs off the porch, taking condiments up.  The language the kitchen staff was using was easily heard in the main dining area - most of it with their co-workers- was profane and unprofessional. It does not reflect well on the image of the place.    We will come back from time to time, but our home is truly across the street.

I didn't even know that this one existed, but the husbeastie and I were driving by so we stopped in.   The first thing we noticed was how spic and span it was, how clean it appeared to be. How everything it shined. The waitress was extremely warm and friendly and the food came up really quickly. We both ordered ourselves Chili 4 & 5 way respectively - the husbeastie even opted for their new spicy cheese because for him, anything hot is good.   We liked out dining experience. If we're in the area we'll stop in.

Fantastic Actual Mexican food.   Small and hidden in a strip mall in Pinellas park, we spun Yelp and found it by accident. I'm so glad we stopped in though. The food was fresh and amazing. Especially the Aquafresca!   The place was absolutely tiny, six tables and everyone of them was filled with hungry patrons.  I got their fajitas and the food was tasty as heck! My Guy got their tacos, and ate every bite.

Stopped with my niece because both of us were Hangry.  Clueless register person who didn't know if she'd given me my change, even though the $1.14 was right there on the counter, just at her finger tips.  We ordered a Mexican Pizza and a Nacho Bell Grande and 2 $1.00 sodas during their "Happier" hour.  Total was under $10.   Food was edible, service was slow, but it's "Fast food" So I can't complain terribly much.

Literally right down the street from my house, it was formally known as the Tarpon bar and grill.   They start the service off with little pastries - which are quite tasty. The service can be hit or miss. When they first opened they had nice, fresh flowers. Now they have cheap looking silk flowers on the tables.   I've seen service be spot on, and I've had the service go t*ts up.  Usually it's just fine.  The place is ALWAYS busy. Take today, we stopped in, but just as we arrived, the kitchen told the waitstaff that the people ordering then would be waiting AT LEAST a half hour due to how many folks had recently arrived.   My favorite is their fried chicken salad. The chicken breast is light and crispy, the greens are always fresh and tasty. my husband likes the Meatloaf, for me it has a slightly sweet taste and I don't like sweet meat.

Sprouts Farmer's Market in the old Books a Million building is brand new! And the parking lot shows that its HOT!  What is Sprouts? Think of WholePaycheck, only a smaller foot print. You have all your "all natural" beauty products. Your gluten free stuff and your grass fed meats. There's a great big produce section and a bulk foods area, a seafood/sushi department (Yes, fresh sushi is mae on premisis) a bakery and I'm sure I'm missing things.   The staff is super efficient and friendly. Case in point, I wheeled past 2 when they heard my NEW cart squeaking. The manager immediately went out and obtained a new cart for me, he unloaded my cart and re-loaded it for me. Turns out the small gate at the bottom had gotten bent so that with every push it swung and squealed.  Really super service and wonderful attitudes.   Some of the produce though.... The peaches were very small and the Pineapples didn't smell ripe.   However their bulk gummy bears are To die for as are the dark chocolate covered pepitas (Pumpkin seeds)

At the gate, waiting for my plane and I'm hungry. I decided to see what options there were.  I saw a few names I was familiar with and then saw this one, one I wasn't familiar with.   I stood in line, placed my order for a Hyde Park, no onions.  I waited, and then got my soda and headed to sit over at my gate.  By the time I opened my burger on the plane, I realized, too late, that there were onions on my burger. *sigh*  I do this because I don't eat raw onions. They do something to my digestion that isn't very friendly at all.   I had to scrape much of the condiments off, eating only 1/2 the bun none of the toppings except the pickles.  I was not happy. They couldn't get the no onions right.   I did fill out their survey. They responded that they would speak with their  people, and I'm sure they will. I'm also to let them know the next time I'm there and they'll comp me a meal.  Honestly I won't eat there again, because I can't trust them to get it right.

Can't believe I've not reviewed this location before.   Nice, neat smaller format Target. Needed to stop here to see what new stuff they had out for Christmas. I was overwhelmed. But the store was clean and presentable for just before Black Friday.  Was even lucky enough to run into a very dear friend of mine.   Parking lot is "Fun" to drive in, as people ignore signs, but it is what it is.

What a lovely park on the Bayou.    Gorgeous, old growth oaks, plenty of benches in shady spots or up close to the river so you can see the Manatees when they come in.  The Mermaid statue is absolutely stunning.   The Children's playground, the Little Free Library, The Band Shell, the restrooms, The dog park, picnic area, veteran's memorial, The Tarpon Springs Heritage Museum, tennis courts, shuffle board courts, boat launch and other amenities that I am no doubt forgetting are all here for the public to use in a lovely, picturesque setting.    Some of the most photographable homes in Tarpon surround the park.  Craig park is walkable to Main Street Shops and eatery or the Shoppes at the Sponge Docks if you're a little more adventerous.   Craig Park is where they hold Epiphany each January 6th, and the Art in the Park each year (Pre-Covid).  It's a beautiful centerpiece to the town of Tarpon Springs.

First review of 2020, 2974 (for personal accounting).   We came to Tibby's as a suggestion by my sister in law, and after looking over the menu, I was excited to go. They have all the stuff you'd find in New Orleans and EVERYTHING sounded amazing.   We were a larger group of 8, 5 adults and 3 kids under 12.  The wait time was minimal, and we were seated at a large table outside of the bar, but close enough that we could see the game on and hear the cheers as NOLA took on another team.   The service was great, our waitress was attentive and friendly, and our drinks never went dry.  We got drinks, trying a hurricane and a milk punch, both were delightful and delicious.   The food! Starting with the fried pickles and the beef tip eggrolls, both were amazing and delicious.  I personally had the Muffeletta sandwich, 1/2 and it was large enough that I took home 1/2 of it as well.   We had more than enough food to go around and all of us left content with promise to return happily.

Our original destination turned out to be closed, so the Husbeast asked if I remembered where we ate in Palm Harbor before. I did, but now it was Catcher and the Rye. I was surprised but not upset.   This new place is rather amazing. The dark wood, the collection of Bourbon and Whisky along with other libations were quite impressive and then there's the menu, that too was tops.   Since it was a lovely spring afternoon in Florida, and I'm not sure how many more of those we have before the temps soar, we opted to sit out side on the seashell encrusted patio.  Our seats were comfortable and the tables were emblazoned with the eatery's name, a nice touch. We looked over the menu and opted to start with the 'Sizzling Pickle Backs' - their twist on fried pickles. Very well done, not as tart as others but their dipping sauce was on point.   For my Main I had the Adult Grilled cheese: Smoked Gouda, Sharp cheddar, Chive cream cheese and Whisky bacon book ended by Texas toast, served with house made chips.  This is a HUGE sandwich. It seems they take one of the slices of bread and slice it in half, the other is between the meat and cheese. It's LARGE and in charge and absolutely delicious. I honestly could not finish it. The bacon was top notch.   The Husbeast went with the "Grouben" AFlash fried local Grouper in a ruben style sandwich, with house pickled beerkraut, swiss chese and a unique flamingo sauce.  Served on Marbled rye and with tator tots. It was all you'd expect and more.  He loved it.   The service was amazing and Everything was delicious.  If you're a Whisky drinker I'd recommend you visit this place when you get the chance.

I haven't been in a Denny's in FOREVER. The last time I was in one, it wasn't a good experience. This Denney's... This was a nice experience.  The diner was clean, the staff was friendly and they were either down someone or maybe they were just short staffed that day, what ever the reason, the waitresses were working as Hostess, cashier and waitress and they were busy.   We were seated, our drink order of coffee and water was placed and retrieved for us quite quickly, even though the server was the only one on duty.  She came back to us in a few minutes after seeing to her other tables and took our orders, we kept it simple, just a few of the pancake puppies and 2 All American Slams.    Once more, the food came out promptly, the eggs were perfect, the hash browns were crispy and the bacon was well done. Everything was absolutely wonderful. My beau and I got to enjoy our meal and occasionally chat with our waitress about her tattoos.   We will come back as the Bayonet Pointe location rocks.

We stopped in just after the eateries re-opened for Covid, when they could go to 25%. This place had tables marked off, they had tables made into Celebrations for people graduating this year, which I thought was a pretty damn good idea!   Most of the folks serving seemed to be wearing masks, but the lady who sat us, wasn't and that was kind of unnerving. Our waitress, though, she was fully masked and gloved.   We started our meal with their fried cheese and it was tasty and a fun shape.  The meal its self was burgers for both of us. I had a bacon cheese burger and my guy had a double burger with some spicy fries.   The food came out quickly, I needed a knife and fork to eat mine, but It was REALLY tasty.  The service was excellent, efficient and friendly. I'm pretty sure if they were closer, we'd be back.

Came to BB's dance for the 80's Circus event. I have friends who teach and who take classes, so it was nice to touch base with everyone there.   The folks who did their routines, who worked the trapeeze, the silks and the hoops were amazing! I am jealous of their talents and can see  myself getting involved in something like this in the near future. Aerial silk and hoop work call to my soul.

This was awesome. The Carrollwood Players held a yard sale and I found out about it. I love costumes and I wanted to check out what I might find...  What I found was pretty amazing. I got a tuxedo for my husband, it was the perfect fit, I got a cutaway tuxedo jacket for me, because when I do my Ring Master work, I need this. I got several eccumenical robes, some wigs and some Ren Faire garb, and the best part of this.. I paid $2.00 for all of it. Yep a whole sum of $2.00

Located in Port Richey, not far from Gulf View Square Mall, Linsey Eye care offers a great selection of frames to choose from. Excellent customer care and even licensed optomitrists to assist you with all your eye care needs.   They do accept insurance, so stop by and see what they can help YOU with.

Normally I'm a Red Robin Fan, but this time I really couldn't bring myself to find the good.  My friend and I ate here and while the service was good, the place wasn't clean as I'm used to. I'm used to seeing the staff sweeping up between patrons, but here there was food on the floor for my entire stay.   Coupled with there being some melmine/broken plate in my food really turned me off of my dish. THe manager was cool, he gave me half off my meal and gave me a coupon for something off my next but it really left me with the thought of how did a broken plate piece get into my meal??/

Met a friend here for dessert.   Neither of us had been here before so we were on even footing. I was happy to find this place as I love crepes, and this place has a lot of potential.  They make awesometacular espresso and mixed coffee drinks. The crepes we're tasty but would have been better if they were fresh strawberries vs frozen. Given we're getting ready for strawberry season I don't see that being a problem.  The proprietor was friendly, the service was excellent and warm. If you speak Greek you'll find it more so.

I've been with TMobil for over 10 years, I'll remain with them until I feel the need to change, but that's not happening any time soon.  They have some awesome associates and some not so good ones. Ones that REALLY know their stuff and others that want to rush you out the door, prefering ot just get the sale.   Today we went in for the father's day sale, the free tablet, we got that, but we had a question about the bill. In other instances, They've called up customer service and helped out, but today we were told to Call Customer Service.   Over all, i'm happy that this location is near the house, I can get my new phones every six months (Yay jump plan) and keep getting what I need from them.

I stumbled across this little hole in the wall today on the way to get my hair cut.  I'm always looking out for sushi places to take the husbeast.  So when I got home, I told the Husband where we were going for dinner and he perked up. I just hoped that they had something I could eat.    We arrived and they weren't too busy, but the first thing I noted was that the place was CLEAN.  Nothing was out of order, everything was spic and span, and there was absolutely NO fishy odor. This was a huge plus for me.  We were told to sit where ever we wanted, so we chose a place across from the sushi bar, and watched the Sushi master at work, rolling for the other patrons.  The waitress came over and asked us what we wanted, I opted for one of the nonfish options, which actually even comes with Sushi.. The Teriyaki beef dinner (comes with House salad, rice, fruit, goyza and half a California roll) and The husband chose a Wabi Sabi Deal (pick 3 rolls and a soup) plus an additional Dragon Roll.  We also ordered edamame & drinks. All of this came out to be about $40.   The food was absolutely fantastic. My dinner, in particular, was very tasty. I've never had teriyaki that tasted so tender and good. The goyza (think pot sticker) was tasty, and the california roll was actually really good!  The husbeast said he loved his sushi. I even ate part of his! Well, truth be told, he made me eat some, one of them, the Tampa roll, was made with chicken.   This little place is a gem. They're new in town and they're gonna be hopping. Get in now while they're not packed to the walls. Once the bar down the plaza opens, he plans on staying open late so that he can fulfill hungry bar goers needs.  The owner also said he was thinking about making Sunday a $1 sushi roll day and plans on having a happy hour from 4-7 or 4-6 very shortly. These changes will be very welcome!   We plan on being very regular customers there!

Love, Love, LOVE this store.    Most of you know that I'm not a big thrifter. Yes, I like bargain shopping but I'm not a huge shopper of thrift stores, so when someone told me about a Thrift Store that caters to the plus size woman, I was interested. I do like clothes, I have - quite literally - 3 closets full and several rolling racks.   When I arrived, I was greeted by the very lovely and extremely knowledgeable Janise, who was wonderfully polite and warm. She told me how it works, how the store is set up and offered to start a dressing room for me when I found a few items.    The sales floor is very well organized by size, garment type and color within the actual items. They carry sizes 14-30, shoes, purses and accessories. There's even a great selection of bras and lingerie. Most of the items are gently used but if you look, you'll find some items that are new and still tagged from the places they were bought. (I see there are other shoppers like me out there.)  The items are offered on consignment and they take clothes 3 times a week, you're offered a percentage in store credit that is available immediately and available for a full year.  But please understand that they don't accept everything, they are choosy.  Sizes vary from manufacturer to manufacture so things bought from on line sellers may or may not be taken.   When I was there, I saw a lot of familiar labels: Torried, Just My Size, Vera by Vera Wang, Assets, Lane Bryant, and many others. You can bet that I'll be bringing in my gently used clothing to the Clearwater or Tampa location soon.

The store is full of so much stuff. So many fashions in bright colors! They have a good range of sizes and styles at awesome prices. This isn't Ross, so unless it's on clearance you're not going to walk out with something super low priced, but you will find things for a great value.

We came to Tom Yum Thai because friends invited us. I don't think we even knew it existed before.  It's in an unassuming strip mall, and with the weather being bad, well... we probably would have missed it.   Upon getting out of the car, we saw a lovely water turtle trying to make tracks to a pond.. well his pond was a puddle so we tried to turn him around, since we didn't want him becoming a speedbump.   Inside, the place smelled delicious.  It wasn't terribly busy, but it took a few minutes for us to be seated, and then a few minutes more for us to be served. Once the waitress came over, we placed our orders for our appetizers and for our meals.  The appetizers: Spring rolls, soups and Chicken Satay. Everything was served quickly and tasted absolutely delicious.   2 of our party like their food Thai hot... and they actually achieved this after much cajoling. Many places don't want to do this for middle aged white folks, but when you convince them, they do give in.   Our meals came and the food was incredibly flavourful. The ingredients were very freshly made and everything had such pizzaz. From the garlic and black pepper pork to the other dishes that I can't remember. Everything was perfect!  Even the dessert was so good.. mango and sticky rice! My absolutely favorite dessert in a thai place!  I would certainly come back.

After watching Alton Brown create pizza on a HUGE mini bake oven, Anna M and I needed Pizza. It wasn't a want, it was a NEED, so with our handy dandy spinner, we found the 8th avenue pub!   This is located just off Main Street in Safety Harbor, Parking can be tricky if you're not good at paralel parking, but Main street has a lot of open spots. The place is nice, the music is ecclectic and fun. When we arrived, it seemed as though the tender might give us a bit of attitude, but once we were seated, she warmed up and took care of us well.   We ordered a pizza to share and I got a salad, the salad was delicious, crisp lettuce with cherry tomatoes, craisns and cucumbers and cheese. The dressing was on the side and quite tasty.   The pizza was equally tasty. The toppings were generous on this Pub Pie: Pepperoni, Mushrooms, Onions, sausage and garlic. While I didn't find it under done, Anna seemed to think it was.  The location is set up to have live music and it appears they have a lovely outside area as well. Neither was active this night.   Lots of local beers are available on tap! So if you're a beer drinker, this might be the pub for you!

Needed something to stave off the headache I felt coming on after visiting mom in the hospital.   I pulled into the drive through, placed my order for one of the seasonal hot chocolates (Peppermint, thank you, very much) and then pulled around to pick up my order.   The wait was not terrible, but it seemed a little slow. May not have been,I have no idea what the people before me ordered.  When I got to the window, I paid my $4.02 and was handed a wonderful, delicious hot chocolate.   it was made perfectly, it was actually a drinkable temp, which is unusual, but oh so very welcome. Delicious to the last drop.

It wasn't my choice to eat here, I'll be honest. I was there because I was at a conference.  The location wasn't particularly busy and it was raining outside so it was the natural choice. Inside, it was loud. I don't mean music, I mean visually. With a disco ball, gigantic fans and garish colors that are the signature colors for the man the place is named after, Former Champion Wrestler Hulk Hogan.   The staff was pleasant. I had Mr. Wright as my waiter. I remember this because of his tattoo. He was awesome! He was personable and very happily made my request for a salad vs fries and made sure my salad didn't have onions. When he THOUGHT it did, he double checked for me. That's AWESOME service. A+ for him.  I ordered the Philly cheese steak, and it was very tasty. Excellent in quality and even though I didn't eat the bread, the cheese, the meat and the veggies were all well cooked and the flavours all blended together so well.   All in all, it was a good meal. I'll be eating there tomorrow too.

I like a mall with a lot of choices.   What I don't like is a mall that offers teeth whiting near a starbucks.. Kinda creepy!  I wish this mall offered more in the way for women who are plus sized, there's not a single store that caters exclusively to them. No Lane Bryant, no Avenue (though an Avenue is across the street). They do have plenty of lingerie stores: Victoria Secret, Fredericks & Soma, all nestled together. There are accessory stores galore and even a plethora of "hipster" clothing stores.   There really is something for everyone and it's pretty centrally located to the upper Tampa area.
Taco bell, where else can you get yourself a quick meal, at a reasonable price. This location is fast and friendly and usually clean.

Great little New Age Book store tucked in historic Palm Harbor.  I've been here before, and had almost forgotten about it, but I'm glad I took the time to stop in. There's just something about the energy that manifests inside one of these places. and this store is no different. It's inside an older home, with a cafe attached to it.   It's calming, smells delightful and I really could get lost just browsing and looking at all the bits and bobs that are around.  Because it was Small Business Saturday, i was doing my part, and picked up a few items that I personally wanted, including a new tarot deck. I can't wait to see what the cards have in store for my friends.

Lenny's is an institution in the Tampa Bay area. I can't believe it's taken me this long to visit.   My husband works down the street, so I had the chance to visit him at his new office, once the visit was over, we made our way here for Brunch.   Though they close at 3pm every day, and we arrived at 2:30, there was no issue with us being there. Our waitress was friendly, and we were sat immediately. The menus have a lot of things to select from so we took a few minutes and then placed our orders.   We had friends with us, and they both ordered some kind of eggs benedict. I ordered an omelette and my husbeast ordered a salad and sandwich combo. The food arrived fast and was quite tasty! It even came with a pastry basket!   My omlette was light and fluffy, filled with all the meats and flavour, cooked to perfection. The grits I ordered were .. well they were a bit thick, but adding enough butter and they were ok too. My friends all loved their foods, except the one who ordered the portabello mushroom Benedict. She said it had too much sauce and - she'd never had grits before, didn't like them, but they replaced it with fruit so no problem. We'll most certainly be back!

They've remodeled since the last time I was here. The store is easier to navigate.  Today, I just had to run in to get a bow tie.  Yes, a bow tie!  Anyway, I knew where they'd be in general since I'd been at a large format super walmart last week. I'm happy to report that it was in the -exact- same place at this location.
