At 10:00pm however, checking out is a challenge. THey had quite a few registers open, but all the lines were moving slow, even when there were only 2 or three people in them, with very few items.   One thing I didn't like, the guy pushing the carts inside. I tried to pass him, and he just didn't give 2 whits. I'd speed up, he would too, I tried to get around him and he didn't even look at me, nearly running me over, when he did "See" me, he gave me a look filled with attitude. Oy.  Happy Holidays to you too.

I brought my Scotsman home from the airport and the first thing I wanted for him was food. The 13 hour trip is a long one and fast food wasn't going to cut it.  Since I know he has food allergies (Peanut), a steakhouse was the easiest option for dining.    We popped into Outback because they're generally quick and tasty and today was no different. Instead of steak though, we both ended up ordering fish entrees. I got the Mahi with artichoke and sun dried tomato toppers.  He ended up getting the steamed salmon. Both were delicious and that's saying a lot coming from a person who doesn't really like seafood!

We stopped in here on the way home from Tampa. I'd been wanting to see what they had to offer and yesterday we were not to be disappointed.   We pulled in late in the afternoon, shortly before 4pm.  My husband wanted BBQ and I wanted Hot Dogs, since this is what Qdogs offers, we were happy to be able to be acomodated. I ordered 2 dogs with chili and cheese. The chili was very mild and no beans, and yummy sharp cheddar.    The husband ordered pulled pork with sides of coleslaw and chili with beans.  His meal was hugely portioned, the sides came in clear plastic containers, with lids, no styrofoam here! I think they took the advice from PenelopeT .  My dogs were large 1/4 pound dogs, the toppings were generous and my side, Potato salad was delicious and also very generous. The only drawback was that the hot dog roll got soggy very quickly. It's a good thing that I am on a low carb diet and didn't plan on eating it anyway.  Some things to know: Over 30 toppings can be found for your hot dogs!  Look for specials on the chalk boards, they're quite helpful! They serve coke products! Always a plus.  And ALWAYS be careful of traffic on Alt 19.

Stopping in for "Lunner", The husbeast and I got to try out this quaint little family diner in down town Safety Harbor.  I saw that they had advertised specials on their place mats and opted for their pot roast over noodles. I was expecting brown gravy but what I got was something all together different. A luscious tomato, pepper and onion gravy over tender roast beef and pasta.  The meal also came with soup or salad (I chose the Lemon chicken soup) and a dessert of rice pudding. All was served quick and fresh, it was quite tasty, and for under $10.00.  My husband opted for the other special of a "Cheeseburger in Paradise" which was just what it was, a cheeseburger with all the trimmings and big steak fries. The fries were done to perfection and the burger, though pre-formed, was tasty as well.  We rounded out our meal with unlimited iced tea.  The service was excellent and we would certainly come back again!

WaWa gas stations are all alike in one way, They're super clean and super efficient.   Pumped my gas, and had my friend go in and get us each a cuppa joe for the road. The coffee was good and the gas was reasonable.

HOLY CRAP! This store is HUGE!  I wasn't sure what to expect, but I'd heard on the radio that they were doing some special things for the 'Holiday Season' (Shouldn't start until after Thanksgiving, but I digress)   There was a large area set aside for children to met Santa, with remote controlled vehicles, a talking reindeer as well as other things to keep the little ones occupied.   If you need something for hunting, fishing or guns, you will find it here. Including a neat live fish area.  However the taxidermy area really made my skin crawl.  Its not my thing.   I DID like the selection of Hot Sauces and gift items, and will probably visit again just to pick up some christmas hot sauces.

It's Cracker Barrel, a country staple. Sweet tea,rocking chairs on the porch and quick service.  While my Mother doesn't like them, I have no issue with this place and will eat at them when ever I go on a trip.  Now they've built them in town and I try to eat at a CB every so often.  The service is friendly and fast. The food is down home and the tea is always "just right".

Stopped in today to pick up a few essentials after doing a long spate of massages. I remember why I don't like going into convience stores.. They may be convienient, but their prices are 2x what I'd find at Target or Walmart. Needless to say I didn't buy the tiger balm I wanted. I did however, find that Spin Pins ( a hair accessory) were on sale for $2.99 with their card. That's a deal!

Brunch after a doctor's visit is always nice. This little spot is kind of tucked away off the road in a business park. I've been here before, but Apparently forgotten to check in.  It's Diner food with decent prices.   It's a sit where you like - but don't sit at a dirty table, please, kind of place.  The menu is simple but sturdy and the service and the waitresses are friendly.  On this visit, I ordered a Ham and provolone omlette, with home fries (with onions) and white toast.  The omelette was made with 3 eggs and was cooked to perfection, the cheese and ham really made it taste good, but to me, the centerpiece of this meal was the Homefries, the onions REALLY brought out the flavours, and I ate every last bit of them, leaving half the eggs on my plate.   All in all, check this place out when you've got the time. THey're open til 3 most days and now serve dinner on Friday and Saturdays.

Stopped for Gas.   The pumps were clean and neat. No debris and it appeared that the garbage cans had recently been emptied. The washing fluid and squeegies were all filled and in operating order.   Though I didn't go in the store directly, through the main window, I did not see an Employee manning the desk, so I assume they were busy doing stock work.

After a private tour of the Dali museum, I really needed some coffee, so I paused at the Cafe for a moment. Three people behind the bar, and it took 2 of them to make an Cafe con Leche (A Cappuccino).  At first the woman said she'd make it, and then the guy took over. He made it perfectly dry, and it was absolutely delicious! I really appreciated the rock candy stirrer.   I made the mistake of giving the cup to the husbeast to watch... he drank most of it, and so he went out to get me another.. he came back with both an espresso and cappuccino. This time the cappuccino was wet - the difference being foam and no foam. I LOVE foam.  Still tasty.

Sears was one of my first jobs back when I was a teen. It's kind of interesting to visit a store some 30 years later to see if the tenets of the Customer service you learned are still the same.  The store was well stocked with clothing, their usual brands and some I've never heard of. They had their tools as well, I don't think those will EVER go away.   I was able to find the husbeast a wallet here. He prefers a wallet where the card slots are pointed towards the inside of the wallet, and they actually had them. So  Yes, I purchased him a new leather wallet for under $20. Nice that it was on sale!   The one thing that I found peculiar is that there was a heat lamp on over the particular register (or cash wrap) that I was at. (Located near Mens & Ladie's Plus) It is nearly 85* outside in December and there is a Heat lamp on. It made it uncomfortable for me, I can only imagine how the associates felt as they worked beneath it. I was told it is on EVERY day of the year.

I debated with the stars for this one, but in the end, the 2 won out.   THe place is hopping, so they must be doing a brisk business, but I'm not sure how. The first thing I noticed when we walked in was the sour, garbage like smell. It was unpleasant to say the least.  I'm not sure where it was coming from but we stomached it.  We were lead to our seat by a friendly (perhaps overly so) waitress. The banquet style benches were old, and by old, I mean ripped and holy, not the kind that you'd really want to be seated in.   The menus are ancient, with hand written inserts - well hand-written on lined paper, and then photo copied, with sticky notes over a certain section in the menu saying they're OUT of that item (Waffles).  Now the food, we placed our orders and the food was delivered quickly, it was quite tasty and not at all bad. The pancakes were actually VERY good, a sweet base that was very pleasant to the tongue. My eggs, I'd asked for them well done - scrambled, dry. Someone actually got it right. And this is why I debated on the 2 or 3 stars.    Over all, I won't be back. I hate saying that, but ... it's true. The stink of the place resonated on my skin and I can't tolerate that at all.

I wasn't sure what to expect, but the parking lot was full so that's got to be a good sign, right?  When we stepped in, we found out you put your order in first, before you sit down. Given that they were so busy, and it was an hour before closing, their ordering board said they were out of a few things. That's ok. We could work around that.   We placed our orders, I got a pulled pork combo, and my husband ordered a ribs combo, both of us would get our meat plus 2 sides for $11 or $13 with cornbread.  Not a bad price really, just a bit over average.  Once our order was placed, we walked into the small seating area and waited.  .. And waited.. And waited. As I mentioned it was packed in the parking lot, and so it was packed inside.  When we sat, they were calling #96, our ticket was #107 so we knew we'd be waiting for a while.   Time passed slowly, the husband and I chatting quietly, taking a look at the people around us plates, when I noticed one lady had just gotten her hush puppies, she must have had about 10 on her plate. I told her how good they looked and she offered me one. I politely declined, but I really thought that was nice.     As we were waiting, the woman who took our order came around to several of the waiting orders and told them that they were out of ribs.  She finally came to us and told the husband that they were out of ribs and would he rather a different meat. He chose brisket, he was fine with that.   When it was time to pick up our plate we were doubly surprised! The serving size of the sides were huge (Unless you got the onion rings, you only get 4) and he got Ribs. Apparently they found the last order of them.  This kind of made the lady who was sitting near us upset as she too, had ordered ribs and ended up getting prime rib. She was not a happy camper.   The food itself was good. There were 3 different sauces offered. One was very sweet, with a hint of Maple. The next one was kind of sweet but much more smoky and the last was smoky with a lot of heat. I liked the smoky one and the Hubby prefers the hot one.  The pulled pork was well smoked and very flavourful, the potato salad had a *special ingredient* that added some zip to it and made it unforgettable. While the fried okra that the husband had was very tasty as was the coleslaw.    What I was really surprised to see was that you couldn't get either Coke Or Pepsi there, but rather Kodiak soda, I've never heard of this brand but people seemed to like it. They also had unsweetened flavoured teas to try.   We will certainly try this place again when there isn't a groupon out, and have a better chance of trying everything we really want to.  I guess you can't fault a place for being popular, and having to turn customers away by telling them "I'm sorry, we've run out of food!"

If you've been following me for -any- length of time, you know I love to shop.   Man, this store was a deplorable experience. Granted, it's less than a week out from Christmas, but there is NO excuse for a store to be this disorganized, this picked over, and this utterly disgusting. The merchandise was scattered willy-nilly over different departments, the employees that I encountered, all three of them didn't appear to want to be there, and there appears to be a high rate of theft.   In the accessory/jewelry/makeup & gift department department I found more open products, more missing items and more slippage (Aka THEFT of items) than I have ever seen in one location.   The only good thing was that they had MY size bra in the lingerie department. They've been the only location to do so.   I will -not- be coming back.

I've lived in Central Florida for .. well most of my life.  And I had never been to The State Florida, but when my friends rented it out for their wedding I finally got my chance.   It is a lovely venue. Since they had live music at their wedding, I got a chance to witness several concerts playing, the accoustics were wonderful. The stage is at the perfect height for just about anyone to see everything, since the wedding was a great view and I was dead center at the sound booth.   The restrooms, though small were functioning and well kept, a plus for any music venue if you ask me.    Over all, the State Theatre gets a big 5 from me for service and functionality since my friends Ajax and Norval will forever linger in love there, they're part of the tapestry of that place. As much as any musical act will ever be.

Last day of Howl, and I needed a place to eat lunch with the husbeast. Grill Smith was on the way. They didn't have a lot of people in the parking lot so we weren't sure they were open, but they were.   Entering, we were seated, we placed our orders for our drinks and Apps, and then our mains. The apps was the Spicy Thai Shrimp, which is -always- Delicious.  Our mains were the Grill Smith burgers. They were good, and my special order was accommodated, the only thing wrong was the wedge salad we ordered never came to the table until after our bill was paid. We declined it, of course.  :)

I popped down to Graphi-Ko because a friend of mine was involved in the Art Show that was going on, and I wanted to support him. I was not ready for what I was going to find.  This place has a myriad of Art, jewlery and gemstones. They have men's and women's items as well as some of the most interesting manequin's you'll ever see.
New Race Trac on Hillsborough ave, it's clean and competitvly priced with the others in the area. The inside is well lit and the pumps are all nice and neat.  Inside they have all you could need.
Stopped in after a night with the ladies - simply because nature called.  Their restrooms are neat, clean and well supplied. Not a single drop of urine on the seats or a scrap of paper on the floor.

So, I've been on a weight loss journey for the last 18 or so months and have lost 100+ pounds. I can now wear a size L or XL depending on the cut.  I decided to see what this particular store had in stock, since the display manequins were adorable.   Inside, it's all junior clothes, and as such, typically cheaply made and priced at a low price point. One thing I noticed is that there wasn't anything over a size large, so I was hesitant. Still,I meandered through the racks and pulled a few things. Some crop tops  (i'd use them as Choli's for belly dance) a sweater dress, and a cropped sweat shirt.   When I had my things, I went to the dressing room. The attendant kind of gave me an incredulous look, but let me into a room. (Most juniors aren't Busty like me, nor are they 6' tall) I tried everything on, and they ALL fit.  The choli tops are perfect for what I need them for, so I picked up a black, a royal and a print at $5.99 each, and the sweater dress, well for someone of junior proportions, it'd be a dress, for me, it was a tunic, so I passed on it. But needless to say, I was happy that it fit and was flattering.   I even picked up a lovely necklace that I can wear in the future.   They had an -interesting- return policy: Apparently for Christmas, anything purchased from November 26th until now, could be returned until 1/6/15, but it must be returned with tags intact, and only for store credit.  The necklace is not at ALL returnable. Odd that, but I didn't inquire why.

I really enjoy stopping at the newest addition to Gas Station/Convenience stores in the area. Wawa's are always clean, well lit and fully stocked. They've got some of the neatest options for snacking. I picked up pepperoni/cheese/crackers for under $3.00 from their cold case.   Though sometimes the items in the cold case can be expensive! 4 strawberries, with a tablespoon of chocolate chips and a dollop of whipped cream? Over $4.00.  (It was still tasty though!) Their crew keeps the place spotless and their gas is always a few cents cheaper than down the road.

Nice home town brewer. Intimate etting on the inside with an outdoor patio.    The folks inside are super friendly, they offer you a sample of their beers if you're not sure what you want, and I have to say, being a beer novice that was truly helpful.  I tried their chocolate stout and found it very yum, but ended up going with the Ocean Tropical Pale as I'm told it's their best. It was light and refreshing.   This venue often has performances - I'm lucky because those people are people I know and love. Can't wait to see one of the burly shows here.

Do you like BBQ? Are you in South Tampa? Then come to Jimbo's. Centrally located right off of Kennedy, you'll be able to get there in no time.   Walking in, it's like walking into your father's den from 1970. It's ALL wood. Dark wood at that. Sitting down on hard wood benches or in the booths it's comfy and cozy. Taking a look around you'll see the old advertisements and the waitress will be right with you.    To the back of the place is a pickle and pepper bar, try some, they're really good. Homemade if I'm not mistaken.   The food! We had a party of 7 last night, so everyone seemed to order something different. Myself, I got the pig ribs (1/3rd rack) with double green beans. The husbeast got a salad with pulled chicken and the brother next to me got brisket with beans and coleslaw. I couldn't see what everyone else got, but I can tell you that nearly everyone cleaned their plate.  My ribs were delicious, tender, very flavourful and just the right amount of fatty. The pulled chicken was juicy and smoky and oh so good. The salad beneath was chock full of good leafy greens.   And of course, lets not forget about the hush puppies. I'm not supposed to eat them right now, but I did eat one.. ok Two. And they were SO good.   The kids - 2 of them ages 7 and 3 both had dessert. One just had ice cream, the other had a brownie sundae. I swear, hand to god, that the ice cream on the sundae was nearly a foot high. And ZOMG.. it looked so tasty, the soft serve looked creamy.   For 7 people, the bill was under $100.

I was happy to find this Sephora because Every other Sephora in the local area was sold out of the Divergent limited edition kit!  On line at Sephora.com, it said the Citrus Park location had it.   So I trekked over to the mall, through JC Penney, because THAT's where I thought Sephora was. Imagine my surprise when I found out that it wasn't yet built.   Instead I had to wander through the mall to find the location! And find it I did. The moment i walked in, the girls were very happy to help me. I picked up the -very last- Divergent Limited Edition kit in the area and a nude lip liner. I am happy!

Formerly Hess, now Speedway (Why did this happen, anyway? What's going to happen to the Hess Truck at Christmas Time?? ) is clean and tidy. The gas pumps have their safety seal across the printer box to tell you it hasn't been tampered with. The pumps run well. Over all, it's a nice gas station. I have not been inside in a long time.

Dollar Tree.. the meca for cheap stuff made in China. But where else can you still find bobby pins priced right? I swear, when I walk into Target and find them at $3.59 for 90 of them, I get angry.   $1.00 for 70 is a decent price. I also picked up a pack of cheap combs and 2 sets of ear phones. GREAT things to give to a niece who keeps losing hers.

Tonight, although I brought home dinner from another place, the Husbeast and I decided we wanted to try a new place, so.. Bring on Seadog Brewpub.    The first thing I can tell you is that parking is a nightmare! We ended up parking about 3/4 the way out to Red Lobster. According to our greeter, the employees are told to park out there anyway, since close up parking is hard to get.    There was live music out on the patio, but we were inside in the dining room, and that was ok with me.  We started our night with a Raspberry Pale ale and the Sea Dog Bluepaw wild blueberry pale ale, which had blueberries in it and was absolutely delicious. Our appetizer was pretzel bread sticks with beercheese sauce, this was absolutely divine!  Our main courses were a little less thrilling. I ordered the Fish and chips, and while they came out hot, and the fish was nice and plump, the batter on the fish was soggy and not at all crunchy, and rather bland. The coleslaw was abundant and the fries were plentiful.  The husbeast got the pulled pork sandwich with fries. He said he liked the flavour of it, but it just didn't look appetizing to me. Something about cheese on pulled pork...   The server, Cicily, was warm and friendly and quite efficient. I thought she was going to break out in the Time Warp any moment because she reminded me so much of Columbia from the Rocky Horror Picture Show. She was a delight.   Would we go back? Probably not. It wasn't the best I've ever had and though the atmosphere was nice and modern, it was very loud on the inside.  The metal and wood furniture doesn't allow for any sound dampening at all. And I really detest so many tv screens and sports programs in my dining.

Beautiful location, It's clean with an outdoor section for the smokers. However there's this disconnect from there. When you walk inside there's a greeter's desk, or so you think, but no one mans it. You're left to wonder wtf are you supposed to do.  The two servers were busy in the back, doing something, I observed them at the back, but they weren't helping anyone when we arrived, they were interacting with each other. The husbeast and I seated ourselves.   When we sat, we waited and finally were approached by our waitress. She was scattered, very.. distracted acting.  We placed our order for our Spin dip and our drinks.  It took 5 minutes to get our drinks and they were served with lots of apologies.  When the spin dip came out it was good, the chips were hot and fresh.   When we placed the order for our mains, the Husband ordered the bacon cheese burger, this is when the waitress said she wasn't Muslim, because she didn't eat pork or bacon. That really made me uncomfortable. Obviously if she were Muslim she'd be wearing more than booty shorts and a tank top, but that's not here nor there, We didn't care, her personal politics is of no matter to us, we're there to eat.  I understand her comment might have been said to diffuse some chuckle head, but with us, it didn't matter.   Our food came out a long while later, apparently it was shift change. as she brought out the food she put down napkins to "hide the dirty" the tables were streaky but we didn't think they were dirty. She said they needed new towels to clean the tables with.   We ate, the food was tasty and hot, and then we were done, and we waited. She got a few more guests and we waited. Finally the husbeast got up to use the facilities. And we waited.. Finally I caught her eye and asked for a box and the check. She'd forgotten about us. *SMH*  So the food was good but the service was Meh.

I came here with a great group of people tonight, as our weekly "Coffee Time Gathering". Since there were 40+ of us, we had the place pretty much to our selves, and that was a good thing.  I won't say we're demanding, but some of us can be.    That being said, for all the people we had, the wait staff was efficient and sweet, they were running quick and got the orders right. I ordered a ham calzone and breaded mushrooms as my dinner and I was really impressed. The calzone was really large, stuffed with ricotta cheese, Mozarella cheese and ham, the red sauce tasted so fresh that I thought it might have just been crushed tomatoes and a bit of seasoning, it was -that- good.  The mushrooms were delicate and tasty.  Over all, I think this is a hidden gem of a place, tucked away in a strip mall next to a pack n' ship and new age bookstore. Go check it out!

Coming home from spending time at the nudist resort, I was hungry. I didn't want fast food, and it was KINDA late. So I saw that there was an Outback, it wasn't quite 9:00, my wheels turned and I pulled into their parking lot.   This is out in Trinity, so they're a bit .. trendy in this area. I'm a single woman alone, I got the hairy eyeball from the host, but was sat in one of the booths near the bar, and the waitress came over very quickly.    Using the menus provided, my choice was quick. I chose one of their Wednesday specials, where I'd get a starter (Soup or salad), my main and my dessert for $11.99.  All in all, with a drink the meal (including veg and bread) came out to just over $15.  Not a bad deal for Outback. If they keep this up, theyll likely see more of me.

I only visited here for a few hours, because I went to the Mashables meet up for social media. The grounds were gorgeous, the pool area especially. The staff was certainly friendly and helpful - willing to answer any questions you might have.   If I was going to be staying someplace on St. Pete beach, I might choose here, I like their retro-chic vibe.

I'm certainly familiar with this post office. I've been going here since 1974! It's undergone several renovations and has been in it's current incarnation for a long while.  It's large and roomy, with all the bells and whistles you'd expect, including the APC, which wasn't working at the time.  (I honestly prefer to use the APC vs humans)  There was a short line to get through, and the it was quickly meted through, with only a couple of people who were holding up the line. One having the audacity to hold the line up and then complain that she was indeed in a hurry. Ah well, such is life in the service to the public.   The workers here are friendly, caring and over all, well mannered. I come here when I'm visiting mom.

it's a dirty, gritty place, but I wouldn't change it for the world!  The only reason I come to the Crowbar is because they're where WIT Improv performs. And hence the reason I was just there. They hosted WIT IMPROV reacently for a reunion show featuring Alex Crow.    As usual the drink prices were great, the comedy show was fantastic and getting to see my friends was a huge bonus!

I -REALLY- Thought I'd done a review of this place before. Guess not.   We don't come here often. Honestly the place is HUGE, it's not much to look at, and when you come in, it doesn't smell very good. There's no hostess, and you kinda ... wait a while before someone sees you're there.   HOWEVER, once they seat you in the normal seating area, the service is pretty decent. It's never very busy so you're given your drink orders and chips & salsa fairly quickly. The chips are hot and the salsa is tasty.   We generally order the Fajita for 2 no shrimp. They give you a whole salad plate, not like you get anywhere else. No chintzy cheese, salsa and sour creme. NO! You get refried beans, sour cream, guacamole, rice, lettuce and pico de gallo, and it all tastes good.   The fajitas are HUGE too. When they say it's for 2 it really could feed three, and it's not terribly expensive either, lots of meat, onions and peppers all seasoned so well.

Panera as a general fact is decent food. Their selections are good, I love their TWOFER's, where you can get a bowl of soup and half a sandwich/salad for a low price.  I like making my own combinations.   I just wish that you could actually look at a menu in hand vs the menu board. Sometimes I miss details of what's on the sandwich vs what I get and I get confused. I don't like a lot of toppings and hate that they might have to be re-made.     Their pasta selections are good, but I'm finding that they're starting to rely on their microwaves far too much. The other day, I ordered soup combo for both me and the husbeast and both our soups were microwaved. The tell tale beep went off for both of us. And sadly my soup was only just luke warm. *sad*   And only half my panini was toasty.. That never makes me happy.

Got to say I'm hooked. I've been back nearly every other day this week. I end up picking up a breakfast, lunch and dinner for both the husband any myself.    Beyond the food being really healthy and great tasting, it's easy too! Most entrees take one to two minutes to heat up in the microwave (Flavourbox) and come out perfect!   There is an amazing variety of things to choose from. Something for every taste. Right now, my favorite things are the Greek Meatballs and the Mama's Homemade meat loaf. Both are absolutely delicious and the accompaniments really do make the meal.   Also! Every time I check in here on Yelp! I get a free bar or granola, that's a $3.85 value.

Sally's is a beauty supply store. They carry things used by salons and beauticians and nail techs. Sometimes they carry things for Massage therapists too, but not often.   Today I had to go in for a teasing comb, i was shown a fine tooth comb for $0.99, but it didn't have the serrated teeth to help lift the hair, or the fork at the end.  The clerk was a bit .. terse? When I asked for color depositing conditioner, She looked at me as if I had two heads, "No, we don't carry -that-." her tone was condescending. Well, sadly I buy mine at a high end salon, so I figured they might carry it at a salon supply store. *shrug*  All in all, not a bad visit, but not a 5 star.

After the wrap party for Yelp's Fall Break, a few of us headed over to the Hyppo to get some ice pops. All creative flavours and all made fresh.   I tried a Blueberry Clove one, and sadly It didn't taste at all like those flavours, but the camaraderie and the service was above par, so the flavour didn't matter so much. I enjoyed myself with every passing moment.

My husband and I went here for lunch. We weren't especially dressed up, but I figured since we were close to the beach, this wasn't going to be an issue, I was right. I'm glad that we didn't hesitate going.  First, our view was spectacular. The lighting inside was gorgeous, from the airy atrium effect to the light spilling inside through the windows that face the inlet, there was nothing short of a spectacularly soothing feeling.   Our waitress Mary was efficient and personable with her reccomendations towards food and that this, being September is community harvest month, she explained that 5% of our total would be going to one of a list of charities, we chose which.  Lunch was a decadent affair of the beefsteak tomato salad, Roast pork ala cubana and finished off with Flan.  The food was seasoned and cooked to absolute perfection.    As we were watching the people out on the water, I spied another waitress making sangria, I asked Mary about this, and she was happy to make this for us. It was an experience I would recommend for anyone. The white sangria is lively and delicious, made with fresh fruit and champagne, it is utterly mouthwatering.  Though not cheap by any means, give this place a chance, you won't regret it.

Drive thru service on the way to the doctor's office. I needed coffee. I NEEDED coffee like whoa! The drive through wasn't terribly backed up, and there was a young man being trained on the register. I saw the trainer being very patient with him. That made me happy.   The coffee was made to the right temperature. Often you'll find that the coffee is made too hot, and the steamed milk is scorched, luckily this was just right.  I'm happy with what I got, but there is always room for improvement.

SLOW service. When we were seated, it took 10 minutes for the girl to come back to take our orders.  Prices are decent, the provide a reasonable menu, but it's not a stellar place, it's only marginally clean. It really is a come as you are kind of hole in the wall.

After our trip to Cheese Please, it was suggested that we head over to Pane Rustica vs other locations since this was in the same strip mall.  This was fine, it admittedly smelled DELICIOUS! The heavenly scent of garlic perfumed the air from the outside.   .....  Once inside though.. as a group of 10, we were given a table for 6, and made to fit around it. That was fine, we were a close group, we made it work, except we were bereft of one chair. We let them know that we needed one more, and were assured that they would get it. And we waited.. and waited, after 5 or so minutes, one of our part stood up, walked over to another table, and politely took an empty chair. Problem solved.   Our table was lit by a singular tea light candle. This place is DARK at night. So even though the table was up by the front, and there are only sheers on the windows it was hard to see the menus - the -4- menus we were given. So several of us took out our cell phones and used our flash light options.   I had a tree molesting my hair and shoulders every time I shifted even slightly, and I realise that was MY problem because I chose to sit where I sat, with my back against the Window, and not facing the rest of the populace, call it paranoia, but I like to see people.   I took a walk through the rest of the location, looking at the art, taking in the couples, the groups and enjoying what I saw. It was clear that people were enjoying themselves. And that was great, but when I got to the restroom, and saw that the toilet paper had been "changed" but not.. the new roll was just sitting on top of the spent roll. It annoyed me that I had to change the toilet paper roll in this "upscale' place.  Yes, I know it was likely a patron who'd done this previous to my visit, but they should have someone checking on that occasionally.   The service was Ok. I wouldn't say it was top notch, because when I order dressing on the side, that's what I expect, instead my salad was drenched in dressing. And the $7.00 salad I got, was what I would get for $4.00 at any other location, but the flavours were good even if the portions were small.   I might consider coming back at say Lunch, but this would not be a dinner destination for me in the future.

Pretty decent Marshall's. They're clean, have a large selection of Housewares and gifts. And they had exactly what I was looking for, which is the Kat Von D mini lip sticks.   I love finding the high end make up that I don't expect at these discount stores! It's a treat! These lipsticks ran $60 last year at Christmas, and I picked them up for $9.99.  If you're looking for OPI nail polish, this is the place to come!

A crafting heaven, This is where I go when I need to pick up something that is specifically for a project. They're one of the few places that still has fabric, and a fine selection too!  Late in the evenings, there aren't many folks on staff, so you may end up waiting for a while when it comes to measuring and obtaining fabrics.   There are also different departments - Yarn, Floral, kids crafts, beading among others. It really is a place to go if you want to find a craft place that does it all.

Wandered into Buckle with a friend of mine who was shopping for jeans. The store wasn't busy but not a single associate approached or asked if we needed help.  The jeans we were looking at were priced at $150 a pair. (WOW)  When they didn't have what my friend was looking for, we looked at other styles that they would look good in. Sadly they didn't have what their usual location has so we opted not to buy anything and wandered over to Dillards.

Normally, I'd give Publix a high rating, but ... this one was opting to have their parking lot re-surfaced. This made a difficult parking lot even harder to park in.   They had a lovely bakery and a nice wine selection - the two things I came in for, but their card selection wasn't impressive and their gift wrap left a lot to be desired.   The cashier and bagging girl were AWESOME though.

I've driven past here before and not noticed that a new place had popped up after the Pizza joint moved out.  The husbeast and I had one thing on our minds, a new eatery to try. So here's where we stopped.   We entered and due to the set up, stood in line for a bit.  When we got up to the register, we placed our order for : 2 drinks, 1 Elote, 1 Queso & Chips, 1 buritto and 1 tostada.  We took a seat after I filled our drinks, and didn't wait more than 5-7 minutes for our food.   Though we ordered appetizers, everything cam out at one time.  The chips & cheese were excellent as was the Elote. I'd never had that before and now I'm in love.  The burito was huge, and filled with everything - as that's what the husbeast ordered, and I got the marinated pork. The tostadas were crisp and thin, the meat was a bit on the smoky side, but once I added some queso to them, they were a bit more palitable.   Over all, $30 for our meal was a decent price. We'd come back.

It really saddens me to write an update like this. I went in this evening because I've been having trouble with my phone ever since there was an Android update 2 days ago. Since it went into effect, my phone fights powering on. If it DOES power on, it doesn't stay on for long. Essentially it's become absolutely useless.   I looked up on line how to do a hard re-boot, but the phone wouldn't get to the code screen. It was being obstinate and simply refused. It would come up to the actual usage screen, but then in a short matter of time.. go away once more.  It was frustrating to say the least.  In the past, I've been able to go to the stores and one of the people working there either knew of a fix or knew someone who could help me. NOT TONIGHT.  I walked in at 8pm, an hour before closing, and got Shae, a bespectacled, pinup banged young lady with a very blasè attitude. "How may I help you" she asked as we looked around.  So I came over to where she was.  As I settled into what was wrong, I explained the situation, that I -COULD NOT- get to the hard re-boot screen, and I needed help because of the issue with the recent update. She was NOT actively listening.   She took the phone, turned it over in her hand, looked at it as if it were a piece of offal and then set it on the counter, she asked my name, asked for my phone number and ID to make sure that it cleared and then she scanned my account. "Well You don't have insurance on the phone." Ok.. what?  I've had insurance on the phones - all of them since I've been with T-mobile. I also had just been here recently to check on something and KNEW that I had insurance, so when I was told this, I took exception. "I pay for it." So she looked deeper. "You have it on XXXX, But not this number." Uh huh.. My husband came over to find out what she was saying. He got a touch heated, "So what your saying is that We don't have insurance on the phone, even though I know we pay for it?" She looked at him and said, "That's not what I said." (Actually it is just what you said.) And so she looked a little deeper and Guess what? We have insurance on ALL THREE LINES!    "Well, your choice is you can Pay off the phone or you can invoke the insurance but your deductible is $175."  Wait, wait wait.. You're expecting me to pay off a phone that's busted due to NO FAULT Of my own, due to a softwear push?  "Well, there's nothing that I can do, I'm not allowed to take back phones that aren't in working order."  I didn't ask once to have the phone taken back. I had asked for HELP. To see if they could get the phone back to the hard reset screen.  This is when she told me what she "thought" she heard. Clearly the girl didn't care, didn't want to know how she could truly help.   She simply wanted us out of there. She had the flat, monotone tone of boredom. We weren't buying anything and all we were doing was taking up her time now, and clearly, she'd screwed up, and she wasn't going to take any responsibility for it. There was no apology for the misinformation. No, "I'm sorry, I read that wrong." Only an "I'm just reading what I see on your profile." Really? I suggest a remedial reading course.     So now, I have a conundrum: I have a phone, with a $400.00 balance. I can pay it off. I can invoke my insurance (Though I'm not sure why, since NOTHING I DID effected the phone) and get a new one. OR I can call the customer service in the morning  and talk with them to see what will happen. Since frankly, I'm a little underwhelmed by the level of non "Customer service" I've received.  Do I want to continue this 10 year+ relationship? In the past they've done right, but this one employee has put a dark coloration over my eyes. I know that this branch won't see much of me from now on. I don't trust the competency of their employees.

Late night, needed a bite to eat before going home and after seeing The Hunger, so we stopped. The rain and the cold made the night miserable and the homeless man on the inside reeked of urine, but what can you do? He needed safe harbor too.   Shawna, our waitress was exceedingly helpful, We ordered our food as we talked.. and talked.. and had our food. An omlette for him and red velvet pancakes for me. All was well done and tasty. And shawna made sure I got the extra whipped cream for my cakes. She deserved the extra tip I left.

Visited this place with a party of 8 on a Friday night. Thank goodness we'd called ahead and made reservations as it was hopping. Our table was towards the back and so it was in a busy thoroughfare but our service was excellent.   The food was Ok, it wasn't anything spectacular, but everyone was eating it at a break neck pace. One thing I specifically liked was that they bring out mild salsa, with extra peppers so you can kick up the heat if you so choose.  Would I go back? Probably. I would try something other than the ground meat tacos though. They needed spice or something.

Since we were in Dunedin, we needed to grab ourselves some kind of food for the first meal of the day  - I know, I know, we should have eaten earlier, but oh well.   We've tried to eat here a few times, but parking has -always- been a nightmare. Today was almost no exception, except someone was pulling out from one of the front spaces.  The parking around the building is tight, not a lot of spaces for a place that has plenty of room indoors and out, I'm guessing that they park in the municipal lot across the street. And YES, Survey, there is BIKE parking.   Once we were sat, outside, since the day was nice, our server came right away. I was kind of worried because most of the complaints were about the service. Our girl, I don't remember her name, was on point. The husband was looking for a "sour beer or Lambec" but sadly they had neither. He ended up getting a cider. I opted for a tea.  We began our meal with their Horsey Deviled Eggs and they were absolutely delicious. A touch on the salty side, but a good note to start the meal on.   For our Mains, I had the Pulled pork on Texas toast with a side of Mac & Cheese, and the husband had their Heart attack on brioche. Both of us were surprised at the size of the servings. My meat was over flowing off the toast! It was a generous portion, sauced nicely, with a side of sauce.  The Mac and cheese, while tasty was barely warm. That was kind of a disappointment.   The Heart Attack on brioche looked incredible: 2 huge slabs of good beef, topped with 2 different cheeses, and some brisket that was nice and smoky with a side of cole slaw with mango. The husband said that the brisket added a really rich flavor to the food, but was almost on the edge of over powering. The slaw was -good-. You might think the mango might be TOO sweet, but no, it was perfect.   And we indulged in dessert: The Banana bread pudding. It was a delightful concoction of Fried banana, bread pudding with cinnamon and chocolate chips - such a good addition - with Caramel and Chocolate sauce.  This came arranged on a plate with strawberries, whipped cream and both sauces. Dear god, this was amazing on the tongue, and one dessert was surely enough for 2 people.   I'll be back, that's for sure. We really enjoyed our experience.

I needed my nails done and didn't feel like making the drive to my usual place, so I drove up to the farther reaches of Tarpon and found Best Nails. They were able to take me on a moment's notice.    I started out with one woman, but she ended up getting an appointment and was transfered to Mia, who is one of the owners.  Once my old Gel polish was removed, I chose a lovely teal green color, and she started to do the trim and shape of my nails.   She did a great job. She really took her time with the paint and shape and I'm very happy with how they look. I can certainly say I'll be back.

The husbeast and I were looking for someplace new to try, and stumbled upon Iron Oak New American BBQ and decided to give it a go.   I can't say they're like EVERY other BBQ joint I've ever been to, but they're very good. I liked the outside porch that we sat on, they had misters so that the area wouldn't get too hot, and they had a nice back area that was "grass" and you could play games on, which added to the ambience of the area.   The food was good. I ordered the small brisket with 2 sides, coleslaw and their Ranch tater tots. The husbeast got a burger and fries.    The brisket is slow smoked and tender, really does melt in the mouth and taste delicious.  The slaw was tasty, but the ranch tots were too oily. They didn't taste very good to me at all.   The husbeast really loved their burger. It was juicy and loaded with toppings. Their regular fries were very good.   We even ordered dessert, the S'mores Tempura, this would be delicious State Fair food, but not something I'd order in a resturaunt again.

Great local haunt!   A little hard to find, but if you look for the signs, you'll be in like flynn.    Staffed by volunteers, and smack dab in a residential neighborhood, you'll find that this little haunt is right up your alley.  The greeter is more than gracious, the scareactors are good with their timing and over all, it's a haunt with heart.  Why heart? Well all your donations go to St. Jude's children's hospital!  That's right, a free haunt. Don't be cheap though. They do this on their own dime, everything coming out of the home owner's pocket, so make sure that when you give, you give from the heart so that they can give back to St. Jude.   Come spend some time with the folks at Hellview Cemetery, you're sure to have a scream!

I hadn't been to Richey Suncoast theater in ages, but my friends were in a production of Legally Blonde so I decided to support them.   The theater is quaint and older, but still quite lovely. It isn't fancy but it doe the job. Their concession stand is minimal, but very reasonably priced with water and sodas as well as pre-packaged snacks.   Support the arts in NPR and come out to the Richey Suncoast Theatre.

Stopped for gas and for a soda. The store was clean, the gas pumps were full and kept clean.  We were literally in and out in less than 5 minutes.

I'm a huge fan of shave ice, smoothies and all things that resemble sno-cones, so when I saw Bahama Buck's I knew I had to go in.   It's located in the corner of a dying (Be hones, it is) Strip mall on Alternate 19 in Tarpon Springs. The location is marked by a ton of paper umbrellas put into the trunks of 2 palm trees and that decor looks so summertime festive!  On the inside, it's painted brightly, with pictures of beaches, surf boards and an LCD screen of waves.  It's quite nice.  After perusing the board, my beau and I chose smoothies, he opted for one that tasted like a Piña Colada and I chose one that was almost like an Orange Julias, both of them were delicious.   They weren't busy when we arrived, but there were 2 large groups of people who came in while we were there.   There are a lot of items on their menu to order from, a lot of options to add to your ice, a plethora of flavors and even ice cream or a protein shot, so it can be "healthy".   When we were there, they were having an issue with bees on the outside near one of their garbage cans. I hope that those were taken care of properly and not simply killed.

Christmas eve, 6:30 pm, people want to head to their homes to be with their families to celebrate.  This Wendy's was open, there were about 8 cars in the drive through, and only one table on the inside that was busy.    We pulled in and hoped for the best.  We knew they were going to be stressed and very busy due to the holiday, but when I walked in, there was one woman waiting on her order, and 8 people behind the counter, being very discombobulated.  I stood there for 5 minutes until the person handling the front counter turned around and noticed he had people.  I didn't speak up because the line in the drive through needed expiditing.   My order was taken without any fanfare, I waited a very short time, and by short, I mean I was only able to grab my handful of napkins and fill my soda at the fountain before it was up and ready on the counter.   It's a fine location, our orders were fine, the fries were hot and the chicken nuggets had been sitting around for a while. Other than that, it was unremarkable.

I was hungry, I didn't know what I wanted but knew that I wanted something new.  As we got to Sr54, I saw the sign for Rocky's and decided that is what it would be.     When we came in, there was one other couple inside eating, so we sat down and they brought us the menu, which the beau and I perused.  After a few minutes we placed our order for a small sandwich with onions and mushrooms, an order of fried mushrooms and a diet coke.  Both of us got the same thing.    It didn't take long for the fried mushrooms to show up, a REALLY large order for 2 people to share and they were amazing. Their ranch dip is SO GOOD.  And when the sandwiches came out, You'd have thought we were starving, we inhaled them, they were that dang tasty.  The food is good, made to order and fresh.   This place is now on my radar and you know i'll be back.   Be aware, if you eat in, they do not do cups of anything. No cups of ice or water, it's all bottled. Saves on cost.

Stopped here at 7:30 on a Friday night, as we were traveling to Georgia.  We put our names on the list and waited. The weather was coolish as a storm had come through, so it was quite nice out on the porch.   While we waited, we perused the menus so that we would know what we wanted and cut our wait time down greatly.  We waited abut 30 minutes until we were called to be seated.  Once seated, our waitress was awesome. Our drinks and our food came out fast.  We ordered the Buffalo Chicken dip to start and it was tasty. Both of us ordered the brisket burger and we ate until we burst.   Everything was delicious and came out quickly. For a place that was busy, everyone was so sweet and kind.

On our bi-weekly dinner with our Geekly crew, this was the destination that was chosen.  They're currently under construction, so we had to enter through the Kokopelli bar, kind of nice, though, because I wouldn't have seen this side if we hadn't have done that.  The Kokopelli bar was dimly lit, the music there was low and intimate.  There was also a patio seating area, which probably doubled their space and allowed for dogs to visit with their owners, a win for everyone   We were a group of 7 not so small people, we were sat in the very first rounded booth in the room, 4 were to sit in the booth and 3 at chairs around the perimeter of the table. My chair was quite literally against the wall. Once I was seated, I was not moving without disturbing 3 other people dining. This is the reason that I had to give one less star, the accommodations for this size of a group were barely adequate.   We placed our orders for drinks, a Beer, a bottle of wine, which was first brought out incorrectly and then corrected) a mixed drink, two margaritas and an iced tea.  The tea actually took the longest to get in relation to time ordered.   Most of us ordered some version of steak. My own personal order was the Delmonico, done medium with baked potato, fully dressed. The steak came out perfect.  One of the couples at the table ordered 2 different steaks, one cooked rare, the other cooked medium.  The Medium came out rare, and had to be re-fired, and the rare came out well done, having to be replaced. This caused the couple to have to wait on dinner, finishing well after everyone else.  It was a small inconvenience.   The food was delicious, the atmosphere was nice.  The service was impeccable. Our waiter, other than the drink issue and the steak issue, which was NOT his fault, was quick, efficient and on point.   I will most certainly come back again and again.

We've been waiting for this to open, and so when we saw that the "Grand Opening" banner was up, we decided that's where dinner would be.    It's a different concept than other Pho eateries in the area, so you place your order at the counter. The menu is small, but my husbeast ordered the three meat pho and I had the pork + egg roll salad.  We also ordered the Vitanemese coffee and an Iced tea.    There is a sign at the register that says "Help yourself to water and toppings for the pho" that seemed a bit confusing, but there, at the windows is a self help bar with cucumber water, basil, jalepeno peppers, limes and bean sprouts. There are complementary shrimp crackers, as well as all your doggie bag needs. No need to pester the people behind the counter.   Our food came to the table after about 10 minutes, but we still hadn't gotten our drinks. I asked about them "Oh yeah, they're coming right up." and then "Um, what did you order again?" we reminded the Runner what we'd ordered and in a few minutes she came back with my Husbeast's Ice tea, and an iced coffee that was 2/3rds full, and most of that was ice. This drink cost $3.75.  I didn't say anything at the time because it already took this long to get.   The food was good, exceedingly fresh, tasty.  They are new, there will be growing pains.  I will give them time to settle and train their staff a bit more. I think there's a lot of potential.

Thanks for being so great! I would have never been there, save that we were filming part of the 48hour film festival and this was one of our locations. The employees were awesome and they actually became part of our cast for a brief moment.   I know I appreciated the brief respite from the heat in your air conditioned haven, and your polite demeanor as we shot inside your store. Thanks so much!  Oh! And from what I could tell, the customers were really happy with the grooming! Every pup I saw was super cute!

The Beau chose this, because one his work mates told him about it. I was excited to try it because who doesn't love chicken & waffles?  It's located in a non-descript strip mall about 3 blocks from the back side of Busch Gardens and it's TOTALLY worth finding.    Upon entering, there's a warning on the door, letting you know that if you don't like Urban music with adult lyrics, you might not enjoy this place. They don't make apologies or excuses.  What they make is REALLY good food.   Their menu is pretty simple and straight forward, they offer chicken and waffles, wings and a few other things. You can get them topped or plain, with hot sauces or not.   I actually opted for their Southern Fried chicken tenders with a bacon topped waffle, it wasn't what I expected, but it was EVERYTHING I wanted.  When it came to the table, the chicken was perhaps a bit darker than I imagined, I suspect they either needed more oil or it was time to change, but it didn't affect the flavor, it just made it a bit dark.   The spices were a great combo, a touch spicy but SO good.  I really didn't expect the bacon to be INSIDE the tender Belgain waffle, but it was there, and it was good. The maple syrup was of good quality too!  My guys both ordered the #4, the pecan crusted waffle and they said it was spectacular too.    To get a taste of something different, they ordered boneless wings as well, in Korean and Jamacian flavors and they looked and smelled delicious, but sadly too hot for me to try.   I will most CERTAINLy come back.

I can't believe I've never written a review about our local pool supply store. We've been coming here since we started renting this place. They keep us in the know about what we need to put in our pool, how our pool is doing and when we need something new. They do our chemical analysis for us and everything is good.  They do not try to over sell us and they don't try to do anything that isn't necessary.

Really nice local brewing Company.   We met our friends here to support their partner on Open mic night.  They offer quite a few different community events on the different nights of the week so make sure you check their calendar to see what's going on.   The husbeastie ordered one of their beers, a Sour, which is what he likes it was an Apple Pie, and while good, he didn't get those notes. No biggie. I had a coke in a bottle and that was cool. They don't serve food, but there was a food truck out side so that's here I got my dinner from.   Will most certainly visit this place time and again.

When craving a quick order and reasonable pizza the husbeastie and I place orders on line and we are usually able to pick up things within 15 to 30 minutes.  This is down the street and very convenient for us.

Stopped here on the way to Orlando so I could catch my flight to Scotland.   The place wasn't yet busy on this Sunday afternoon, the church crowds weren't there quite yet, so there was no wait to put in our order for our Pick Twos.   It's a small format Panera, but neat and clean. They had order stations and a cashier so I guess that helps with rapid ordering at busy times, but I'm not a fan of electronic ordering, and prefer to keep people employed, so I ordered with the human being.   We both ordered our usual, For me that's broccoli cheddar soup and the grilled cheese sandwich. The husbeast tried something new, one of their soba bowls with a salad.  Both came up very fast, and both were just as they should have been, hot, fresh and tasty. The broth of the Soba bowl was very tasty, i think I'll try that some time.    One thing I noticed is that the seating in this location is very limited. And on a rainy day, it's even more so.

Typical fast food pizza joint. Super Bowl Sunday, I thought they'd be slammed, however when I placed my order, it would only take 15-25 minutes for it to be ready. Since i live in a gated community and the gate codes are a PITA, I decided to go pick it up.   It was ready when I got there, and it was just what I ordered, their wings are tasty, their stuffed cheesy bread wasn't anything special. Why only 3 stars? Because their customer service was nil. Sure they handled the order quickly, but it wasn't friendly, it was simply done. And as I left, before I was even out the door, One of the men was cursing about something. He could have waited until I was out for sure. I did hear his compatriot admonish him for that.

Took my niece to Lucky You for a tattoo. She'd worked with the artist at her former place of employment and had previously given the woman a deposit, 1/2 the cost of the session and given her an idea of what she wanted.   Time and a few changes later and finally my niece was able to get her tattoo done, She'd not yet seen the idea, a Frog, and given that she's afraid of them, she didn't know what to expect. The sketch she got was nothing short of adorable and amazing.   The actual tattoo room is clean, smells good and is well lit. Their tables are nicely padded and it didn't take long at all for the ink to be laid into her skin. My niece has a beautiful, one of a kind froggy on her forearm that she totally loves.

Here's a little gem of a Movie Theater, nestled in the heart of Palm Harbor.  It's half way between home and the new Cobb at the Mall, so since we wanted to catch Iron Man Three, the Husbeast and I decided to check it out.  After all, they just renovated!  WOW! Talk about a change! The last time I was here, it was dark and dank, with old seats that were pretty gross and stained. NOW they've got Dbox and state of the art sound. And in the big theatre they've even got stadium seating.   While we got there first thing for the first showing on Sunday, we weren't able to get the d-box seats for the show, we now know to get them on line. What we thought was neat, was that they assign seats! I've not seen another theater do this for regular seating. I LIKED that.   Prices were still a bit high, $8 for matinee + $3 for 3D + $8 for Dbox. So you could be looking at a very PRICEY afternoon ticket, but this is typical for every movie theater across the city.   The only draw back I saw was that the arms don't lift up between the seats. That would make all the differences in the world.

Ok, this is new, this is different. I get they did a refurbishment,but they removed ALL the people, except the greeter.  WHY? This is NOT how I want banking to be.  Ok, I get it, you want to do virtual banking, but this was almost creepy.   You step up to an ATM looking thing, put your Driver's license down, and key in your account or ssn, and a person with a head set pops up in the viewer. Its VERY impersonal. Sure it's neat but damn, I really do prefer personal service. NO BUENO.

One of my favorite coasters in all the world! It's most especially fun at night when the only thing you can really see are the tracks and the soft lighting and hear the screams of those around you due to it being Howl-o-Scream.

I was invited out by my long time friend, to an evening of karaoke and some camaraderie. It's been too long so I accepted..   The bridge is most assuredly a local's bar.  There is a regular rotation of soulful singers who share their voices with the crowd. And skill, or lack of  doesn't even matter, every one is encouraged and applauded.   The drinks are good, but the parking lot can be a bit hazardous when crossing across Alt 19.  Over all, I had a good time and I'd go back.

On the way home from Brandon, this was our first stop so the car would not over heat.  Because they closed at 6pm, we were an hour before they closed.  We still received excellent service, the food was delicious and very quickly delivered to our table.   I ordered the chicken breast dinner and the Husbeast ordered a burger, both were hot and tasty. I have to say that I ordered their yummy mac & cheese. It wasn't swanson and it was VERY tasty! I'd come back.

This is right down on the quaint Main street of the town where I live, Tarpon Springs, and it's a fantastic addition to the neighborhood. I know it's been here a while, and I've actually stopped in once, with my mom, but she wasn't interested in sticking around and playing vidya games. BAH!  Last night, my beau and I got the chance to stop in. It was a little before closing, there weren't many people inside beside the receptionist, and we came in to play a few rounds of pinball.  I saw a few really vintage games and some awesome new school games as well.   My beau was more about Synestar, Galaga and other old school games.  I think we played for about 30 minutes before they closed up before it was time to close, but I can tell you this, it left a great impression for me, I'll be coming back so that I can shake off some stress.

New Chipolte, but wow, not a good one.   The husbeastie and I went here for lunch and we were surprised at how poorly it went.  First was the couple in front of us, can't fault the store that the family in front was too lazy to order all together, that the Mom had to leave to go back and get the dad's order and leave the kids in line.  The 2nd part was when I ordered my bowl, the person behind the glass gave me apparently "Extra" and when I went to pay for it, the cashier told me that it was "Double meat"  I told her I didn't ask for that and I wasn't paying for it.  RIGHT THERE, she went and dressed down the girl scopping out the meat about her portion sizes, as if to shame us both.   They were out of napkins and though there was no line when they were told, it still took them 10 minutes to fill the napkin dispensers up.  They didn't bus the tables and seats at clean spaces were sparse.   All in all, it was not a pleasant experience, and the food wasn't that good to begin with. We won't be back.

Love this park. On the day we visited they were busy, someone had a blow up bouncy house for a party and the shelters were all full, so my love and I went across the street to the sunset pier and watched the weather and a whole onslaught of little horseshoe crabs come through. It was a lovely evening.

Arrived after 7:30 on a Friday and still had a long wait.  We started our meal with the wings, and while they were tasty, they were very salty.    The husbeastie and I both ordered steak, the renegade medium with broccoli and both were over seasoned but not to the point of being unedible but I wouldn't want much more.   The service was excellent, our drinks never went dry and we were offered 2nds on bread as the kitchen was a bit slow that evening.

I drove by this spot and thought to myself, I have to come back, So I did, with one of my fellas.  We ordered 24 wings, in Garlic Parm and Lemon Pepper, We also got the Cheeseburger Baked potatoes.   Trust me when I say that we now have a new wing place.  These wings were big beautiful and JUICY. They were so damn good.   And if you think that a baked potato dressed like a cheeseburger is odd, it's not, It's AHMAZING.  It was so good and SO BIG that i had to take half home.    The lovely lady also let us try her delicious baked potato soup, which is a gift from the gods themselves, especially when topped with bacon and cheese.    This food is made with love and with a lot of heart.   Go there for breakfast too, I did, and the waffles are amazing, as well as the wings that top them.   I AM A HUGE FAN.

Dinner last night was at Saki. We'd been to the Clearwater location but never to the one here in Tarpon Springs/Palm Harbor so we decided to try it out.  The strip mall is pretty non-descript, but inside it's a really nice looking eatery.   We were seated into a booth, and a few minutes later our waitress came by and asked what we wanted to drink. We opted for unsweet iced tea, and then perused the menu.  The concept is fairly simply for one price ($20.99 for dinner on a regular night, less for lunch and for Sundays)  you get all you care to eat, but be aware, if you don't eat all the sushi, they'll charge you PER PIECE between $0.50 or $0.85 depending on the roll.   I ordered appetizers of Salt & Pepper Shrimp and Gyoza and the husbeastie went right away to the good stuff.  The thing about getting aps? They come right away. The Gyoza was 3 peices and the S&P Shrimp came out a great big serving.  The shrimp was a bit over done, but tasty none the less. I shared some with my guy and we waited until he got his, which was beautifully plated.   We were happy with what came out, sated with what we had and then I ordered the 2nd course for me: I got Hibachi green beans (My favorite) Hibachi Steak with veg, no rice and more gyoza - its so tasty.  The green beans were delicious, served with other veg too, the Steak was PERFECTION. I mean seriously, that was some perfectly cooked and seasoned steak. I could eat that all day!  The husbeastie ordered himself some S&P shrimp to finish his meal.    All in all we were satisfied, and we capped our meal off with ice cream, Green Tea and Mint Chocolate Chip.   Service was better than most of these style places, being relatively quick and pleasant. We enjoyed our trip and will certainly be back.

I visited the Paul Mitchell School as a demo dolly for a friend who was doing makeup certification.  I got to experience the class room atmosphere and see how the instructors conduct a class.   It was fun to have my makeup applied, the Smoky eye in a non-traditional color, mine was a rich burgundy with a metallic overly and let me tell you, it was a look! I know just when and where I'd have worn it.

Stopped in for a party and got to see how the school runs.  I love the way the place is set up, and what they offer. It's pretty exciting when you see it all broken down.    Movement is pretty exciting: From American Ninja to Lyra to general movement classes you're able to find it here at the Shinobi School. Its my understanding they'll be adding new and exciting things in the next few months.

I'm not sure just what I was expecting,but what I found was Ross, only with a higher dollar point.  Granted, they had high end makeup - Laura Geller, Nyx and Smashbox, they had famous maker lingerie and clothing, but it really was set up like a Ross.   I found a Michael Korrs dress for $78, I found NYDJ for $36 (That's a GREAT buy, as those are Fantastic jeans) and I found other designer wear for decent prices, but they are off season if you want a REALLY good deal.   One thing I can give them kudos for, They do carry G & H cup bras. This is GOOD news if you're of the Full bust club.

Our oldest kitty passed away a month ago, and our other cat was showing signs of being lonely. My husband, who's baby it was, was also ready to start looking at new companions. So this past Sunday, I took him down to the Humane Society (the area's largest No Kill shelter) and we set about looking at cats to fill the hole in our house.   The staff was friendly, they gave us a tour, showed us the habitat and told us the areas where the cats were housed. They advised us to be gentle and to use the alcohol gel between animals - This can be a challenge as many of the little containers are out and you have to hunt it down. I carry it on my purse (thanks Yelp!) so I was good to go.   We looked in every cage, fell in love a few times, but this one fellow, Cosmo, he stole our hearts. Our old boy, Spooky was a shy fella, and cosmo was hiding when we came in but he peeked his head out and trilled at us. He was a little lovebug and let us pick him up. He was easily handled.  We looked at others but came back up and made the decision that he'd be ours   We met with the adoption counselor and talked about mutual expectations, and what both needed, we were a good match and Cosmo was ours.    I am happy to say that every one there treated the animals with the utmost kindness and respect. You could tell that they were truly loved.  Cosmo is currently adjusting to his new home and big brother, Itty. It is actually going very smoothly because his big brother is such a sook.

Used the drive through to get Chicken Mc Nuggets and coke. Placed our order and got through without any issue.  The nuggets though had apparently been sitting as they weren't oil fresh and tasted MEH.

Stopped here in hopes to pay the bill on my Boyfriend's phone. However this store apparently does not accept in-store payments or so we were told.  No reason to come back if the service needed is not provided.

I usually use the NPR location of Quest, but this time I tried the Tarpon location.  It's honestly about the same distance, but that doesn't matter.   I was able to make an easy appointment on line, I was able to check in on line and go inside (other options include waiting outside or in your car) in their waiting room. My name was 2nd on the waiting list.    The waiting area is comfortable. Seats are currently staggered for COVID seating and Masks are still required (That's cool. I'm vaccinated but I do still mask for the benefit of others.)  I waited about 3 minutes, before I was called back to Room 2, which was large and comfortable. My Tech was knowledgable and I gave her a choice of arms as I'm blessed with "pipelines". She chose the left and she was able to take all she needed without any issues.  I was in and out in 15 minutes.   The only issue with the location is it literally looks like an abandoned place. Outside the parking lot is over grown, not well kept and the lot is strewn with debris. It needs a little love.

I'm spoiled, I admit it.   But these days when I go to an AMC theatre, I kind of expect the leather recliners, the nicely set up theatres, the either staffed ticketing windows or the computer kiosks that work.  This theatre had none of these.   There was one fella, who had to work 2 lines, the unwashed and the Stubb's preferred. And it was slow going. Especially when you had to pick your seat, since it's out doors and the glare was horrible.   Inside the seat I'd chosen was WAY too close to the screen, apparently I chose poorly or didn't understand the set up, but thankfully it was an underwhelming attendance so we had our pick of seats.   The seats, not recliners, not comfortable and not even truly stadium seating. Clearly this theatre is showing it's age. I hope that it gets is much needed upgrade soon.

Stopped here after getting my most recent Covid-19 test (As of writing, I'm still negative) They are all wearing masks, there is MOSTLY socially distant seating (Hard to take into count when the glass separator is the separator between you and someone else, but I digress). People arriving were also wearing their masks.   Our waitress didn't realize we were seated and apologized profusely for our few minute wait.  That was fine, we placed our order for coffee and our breakfasts of eggs, hash browns and french toast.    When the food came out, it was delivered quickly and with a smile behind the mask. The food was delicious and tasty, neither of us could finish the french toast we were given.   The french toast though... it wasn't really toasted but rather scared by the flame and almost heated. There as none of that rich caramelization you expect.   Over all it was a good visit. We'd come back.

This is a compounding pharmacy, it's tucked away next to a funeral home and several other medical offices. Honestly if you didn't know it was there, you'd never see it.   The people there are polite and friendly. Quite efficient and my order was ready within 48 hours of it being submitted. I was happy.

I came in to have my knee looked at. They weren't particularly busy,  but the doctor seemed to rush through his exam. He did a basic palpation of the area, asks me if I could bend it, but didn't really engage me at all, didn't ask me what I was doing to help relieve my own pain. He saw me for about 2 minutes. In that time, he speed talked, he asked if I had a primary care physician, and that I should really see her.   He said I should probably see an Ortheapeadist, and I should, but all he wanted to do was get me the hell out of there.   I'm glad that I didn't have a huge co-pay on this visit or I'd be highly upset by the lack of care I received.  The last time I was here they at least took an Xray and checked to make sure nothing was wrong.  This guy didn't even compare the swelling to the other knee.  Like others before me, it seeems like this might just be a mill. Especially when it comes to prescribing RX's. I had to remind the Physician about my own drug interactions based on what I take and that he can not prescribe anything with ibuprofen. He seemed put off by that. Oh well, at least I know what I'm OK to have.    WOULD NOT RETURN.

What a great local tea shop.   I showed up because I saw an Instagram post about a Rock and stone show and since it was near by and my beau and I were looking for something to do that afternoon, we opted to see what was up.   We were VERY happy we went. We found a nice community place that sells great beverages, has an awesome community spirit and supports everyone. Talk about inclusivity.   While there, I entered the raffle, and WON! I got myself 3 bags of Ayurvedic Teas, A Tigers eye mala necklace, a lapis point and a mushroom that is black light reactive. Talk about making my weekend.   They have 2 new customers in us!

Little Greek does Greek Right, and that's high praise coming from me.  I've tried both their Souvlaki and their Greek salad and neither disappointed.   From the moment you walk in and see the rainbow of fresh veg getting ready to be made into salads or put onto sandwiches, Everything looks so very inviting and delicious.   And when it's delivered to your table, you can't help but eat every last bite!  Don't skip the bakalava either. You're gonna love it!

We stopped here after my guy got some tattoo work done.  The atmosphere was lovely, very intimate, and it smelled delicious.  We got a panini for him and a small pizza for me.    It was a Friday afternoon, the service was a bit slow, but that's ok. My paramour and I enjoyed ourselves and talked quietly while listening to some good music.    The food was super fresh and tasty. We'd certainly come back.

I'm making it a point to visit parks I've never known existed. So I spun Yelp and landed on Sawgrass lake park. I loaded up my rocks and headed out.   The park is beautiful, it's hard to pinpoint my favorite "ecosystem" or area of it. Is it the Manicured area that you can picnic on or sit near the river and watch the water birds and dragon flies? Is it the boardwalk through the swamp during the golden hours that highlights the gossamer webs of spiders, capturing rays of sunlight making the depths of the swamp look magical. Maybe it's the Mangrove area with it's sandy walking path and stage area... It's got such diversity of areas. I love it all.   Its certainly going to be a place I come back to.

Life in a pandemic world: They are practicing social distancing.  Please wear your masks to protect others. All staff is wearing them.  Selection of merchandise is good. I love coming to 5 below to do shopping for art supplies and gifts for my niece who just moved into her new apartment. She's thankful and the items are trendy. They're not made to last forever, but just long enough.   The store has a vast selection of things! From toys and gifts to housewares and electronics. Its so much fun to shop at!

On the way home from the Airport, I took the Beau here for Lunch. We both opted for Hot tea and water for the drink, and then ordered lunch from their menu. It was nice that they brought us soup and eggrolls as starters - so we didn't have to order them!  Our food was good, Chicken pad thai and Chicken with mixed veggies. I found the brown sauce was a bit sweeter than I'm used to from other places and I could really smell the fish sauce in the pad thai, but the food was quick and tasty and filled us both up.

Took my guy to one of my old favorites from a life time ago.   The place is a hole in the wall, but the food is absolutely delicious. I had the Ropa Vieja with yellow rice and cuban bread. The portion was large enough that I could take home my lunch for the next day.

First visit and I'm happily impressed. It's really cute on the inside and the food smells great.   I was seated in one of the tall, teal blue booths and perused the menu for a moment before settling on the steak fajitas.  The waiter brought my drink and complementary salsa and chips.  The salsa has a rich smoky flavor that's delicious, not just a watery tomato salsa, it's got depth. YUM.    Anyway, the fajitas came out with all the fixings, a plate with refried beans, Mexican rice, lettuce, pico and sour cream.  I couldn't do the pico due to the large chunks of jalepeno pepper, but if you like that, it's fresh!   Nice sized portion, price was a little steep, but the service was friendly and attentive.
